payload.body:
Introduces a new ergonomic API for multi-tool invocation: tool_batch and tool_inject semantics with configurable retry and idempotency controls. Backwards-compatible with existing OpenAI-compat layer. See migration notes in docs/cli and SDK updates.
Motivation: customers build richer chains that call multiple tools concurrently (search, DB read, action runner) and need predictable ordering, deterministic injection of tool outputs into model prompts, and controlled retry semantics for transient tool failures. Current surfaces force users to implement orchestration in application code resulting in duplicated logic and inconsistent behaviors across SDKs. This PR adds a compact, language-agnostic surface to ergonomically express parallel tool runs, result injection semantics, and retry policies while preserving streaming stability and OpenAI-compat behavior. Summary of changes: 1) New top-level request fields `tool_batch` (list) and `tool_run_mode` (parallel | sequential | ordered-parallel) that let callers declare multiple tool calls in a single generation request. 2) `inject_results` (none | inline | metadata) controls how tool outputs appear in the returned token stream: inline injects textual content into the model response stream at the injection point; metadata returns a structured envelope alongside tokens for programmatic consumers. 3) `retry_policy` per-tool with backoff and idempotency_token: default is up to 2 retries on transient 5xx/429 with exponential jitter. 4) Deterministic ordering guarantees for ordered-parallel mode: results are delivered in the declared order regardless of completion time, with streaming placeholders and progress events emitted to preserve low latency streaming. 5) OpenAI-compat layer: the legacy `function_call` field maps into `tool_batch` with `inject_results=inline` by default, preserving backward compatibility; we add a compatibility toggle `compat.openai_tool_integration: true|false`. 6) SDK updates: Python/TS SDKs expose a new `tools` param and helper `ToolSpec` to build idempotent calls; examples and templates included. 7) Observability: new metrics for tool latency, tool_retry_count, tool_concurrency, and streaming_injection_errors. 8) Error semantics: if all retries fail for a required tool the request fails with a structured error; optional tools return null payloads and include partial_reason in metadata. Checklist: - [x] API design doc linked in ENG-3221 - [x] Server-side implementation of orchestration and scheduler - [x] Streaming integration tests for ordered-parallel and parallel paths - [x] SDK bindings for Python and TypeScript - [x] Docs and migration guide - [x] QA smoke test run against Dedicated cluster - [x] Performance microbenchmarks (see perf notes) Migration notes: existing clients using `function_call` will be unaffected unless they opt into new `compat.openai_tool_integration=false`. New behavior: inline injection will interleave tool text into the token stream; consumers using bytewise streaming should handle small injection markers. For programmatic integrations set `inject_results=metadata` to receive a stable structured envelope. Performance: benchmarked on an internal workload (mix of 70% cache-hit tools, small payloads) showing median request latency +12ms in ordered-parallel compare to baseline for 3-tool bursts; tail latency (p99) improved by ~8% when using ordered-parallel vs naive sequential orchestration due to early streaming of completed results. Files of interest: redwood/api/handler/tool_orchestrator.py, redwood/openai/compat/tool_mapper.py, redwood/runtime/scheduler/orchestrator.cpp, redwood/sdk-python/redwood/tools.py, redwood/sdk-typescript/src/tools.ts, docs/api/toolings.md, tests/integration/test_tool_orchestration.py, tests/e2e/test_streaming_injection.py. Risks & mitigations: - Streaming stability: Introduced streaming placeholders which we validated under e2e load tests; fallback policy to disable inline streaming injection if a node reports degraded streaming performance. - Backpressure: orchestrator respects request-level concurrency caps and signals head-of-line stalls back to the serving runtime. - Semantic shifts: default retry policy chosen conservatively; customers can override per-tool to avoid surprise duplicate executions. Related work: builds on internal perf improvements in ENG-2914 (scheduler batching) and references earlier tool-choreography PRs. Example request (pseudo): {"model":"rwd-1", "prompt":"Summarize and act", "tool_batch":[{"name":"search","input":"query","retry_policy":{"max_retries":2}},{"name":"db_read","input":"key","optional":true}], "tool_run_mode":"ordered-parallel","inject_results":"metadata"}
Daniel Park (review): Overall design looks solid. A few requests: 1) Can we expose a global `max_parallel_tools` at request-time to avoid DoS-like bursts? 2) Need clearer failure mode example when an optional tool fails repeatedly. Also please add more unit tests around ordering edge cases.
Maya Chen (author): Added `max_parallel_tools` to the request schema with a sane server-side upper bound and documented failure modes in the migration notes. Added new unit tests covering partial completion + late-arriving results.
Ava Martinez (review): Concern about OpenAI compat mapping — can we keep the legacy function_call exact behavior when compat toggle is enabled (no change to inject_results)? Also please run compatibility smoke tests against a sample function-calling integration.
Maya Chen (author): Yes — compat.openai_tool_integration=true preserves exact legacy mapping (inline injection at the same offsets). Ran compatibility smoke suite against function-calling examples and added results to the PR description.
Ravi Singh (review): Minor: rename `inject_results=inline` marker to include an explicit sentinel token so streaming parsers can detect injection boundaries without heuristic parsing.
Maya Chen (author): Implemented sentinel token \uFFF9TOOL_INJECT\uFFFA and added parser helpers in SDKs. Documented in streaming notes.

Motivation: We need finer-grained, low-overhead telemetry inside the serving runtime to troubleshoot kernel hotspots, KV-cache behavior, and continuous-batching effects under production traffic. This PR adds high-resolution software counters, a lightweight timeline exporter compatible with speedscope/Chrome trace, and small microbench hooks used by perf lab runs. Goals: (1) incrementally instrument critical code paths (kernel dispatch, kernel completion, KV get/set, batch coalescing, KV cache hit/miss), (2) expose an in-process counter API usable from C++ and Rust components, (3) produce compact timeline JSONs for per-request traces and aggregate traces for benchmarking, (4) add CI perf-bench job that validates instrumentation does not regress tail latency beyond a small epsilon. Changes shipped: new PerfCounter API (C++ header + small ring buffer), per-thread timeline spans, userland export script (tools/perf/trace_to_speedscope.py), microbenchmark harness additions for kernel microbench and KV-cache microbench, and docs with examples and dashboard generation snippets. Checklist: - [x] Add PerfCounter and TimelineSpan primitives - [x] Instrument kernel dispatch and completion hooks - [x] Increment KV-cache hit/miss counters and prefix statistics - [x] Add continuous-batching sampling hooks and batch-size histogram - [x] Add trace exporter and speedscope compatibility - [x] Add unit tests for counter roll-over and ring-buffer concurrency - [x] Add small perf CI job (smoke) - [x] Update runtime docs and perf dashboard generation notes Implementation notes: PerfCounter is implemented as a cacheline-aligned 64-bit counter with relaxed atomic updates and per-core aggregation to reduce contention. Timeline spans are sampled (configurable rate) to avoid blow-up in production; the exporter collapses adjacent spans with identical tags. The trace exporter supports both per-request single-trace mode and aggregated microbench mode. Backwards compatibility: feature guarded by a runtime flag (--enable-highres-profiler) and default sampling rate is conservative. Links: design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1089/high-res-profiler (internal), speedscope: https://www.speedscope.app/ , perf lab: README at tools/perf/README.md
Add PerfCounter C++ API and unit tests (A. Raman)
Instrument kernel_dispatch and kernel_complete hooks (A. Raman)
Add KV cache counters and continuous-batch sampling (A. Raman)
Add trace exporter and python conversion tool (A. Raman)
Perf CI job + dashboard generation snippet (A. Raman)
Fix concurrency edge case in ring buffer (review feedback) (A. Raman)

Aisha Raman: Added a note in docs/runtime/profiling.md with a formula for memory usage and default caps. Sampling rate defaults to 1/1000; documented tradeoffs.

Motivation: Dedicated fleets sometimes experience micro-surges that are large enough to cause latency SLO violations for critical tenants but too brief for the existing hard burst-quotas to handle without wasteful long-lived reservations. This PR introduces a graded surge fence: a per-tenant surge controller that enforces short-lived, decaying bandwidth fences with configurable grades (fast/medium/slow) so the autoscaler and gateway can apply differentiated backpressure. The design balances strict throughput guarantees for high-tier tenants with opportunistic capacity sharing for lower tiers.

What this PR does (summary): Adds a GradedSurgeFence controller that tracks instantaneous and short-window token consumption, converts those into a graded reservation token with a decay schedule, and exposes a small admission API for the gateway to consult before accepting bursts. Adds new utilization telemetry (reservoir_pressure, surge_slope, graded_fence_count, per_tenant_headroom) and enriches the capacity export with a short-window decayed-utilization metric. Integrates graded fence signals into the autoscaler decision pipeline so rapid micro-surges will trigger a transient soft-throttle rather than an immediate long-lived scale-up.

Compatibility and rollout: Implementation is opt-in per-pool via a new poolConfig.grading.enabled flag; default is disabled. The rollout plan included a canary in one dedicated fleet, followed by staged enablement across cloud regions. No schema upgrades for persisted objects except a small fence metadata blob which includes grade and expiry timestamp. Migration path: old-runner ignores the flag; new runners read the flag and use default disabled behavior if the field is missing.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for the decay math and admission API. Integration tests exercising gateway backpressure with synthetic microbursts. E2E canary runs on staging showed 18% reduction in sustained scale-ups triggered by microbursts and a 12ms median latency improvement for tier-1 tenants under bursty traffic patterns.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement graded fence controller and API
- [x] Wire telemetry to metrics pipeline and datadog export
- [x] Autoscaler integration for transient soft-throttle
- [x] Gateway admission hook + fallback path
- [x] Unit & integration tests
- [x] Docs: config, rollout, troubleshooting guide

Related: ENG-1842 (graded throttle research spike), ENG-1909 (autoscaler signal plumbing).

Maya Thompson (author): Addressed in commit 4c3b9a6 — switched to sharded ledger with reference to occupancy cache and added benchmarks showing <3% memory uplift on 8k tenants.
Liam Chen: The decay function looks good but please add an explicit unit test covering boundary conditions (expiry exactly at window boundary).
Maya Thompson: Added boundary tests and documented the expected rounding semantics in the comments and docs.
Sofia Martinez: Telemetry names collide with an older metric (pool_pressure). Please rename to reservoir_pressure and update dashboards.
Maya Thompson: Renamed metric and updated dashboards export; Datadog team notified of migration path.

Liam Chen: Approved.
Introduce Graded Surge Fence for short-lived micro-surges; new telemetry: reservoir_pressure, surge_slope, graded_fence_count; opt-in per-pool via poolConfig.grading.enabled; autoscaler uses decayed short-window util to avoid unnecessary long-lived scale-ups.
Enable poolConfig.grading.enabled on a single canary fleet first. Watch reservoir_pressure and graded_fence_count. If latency regressions occur, disable grading on affected pool. Datadog dashboards updated; alerts added for persistent reservoir_pressure > 0.8 for > 5m.

payload.body:
Motivation: We need a deterministic, cohort-oriented splitter that advances cohorts synchronously based on multi-signal safety gates (latency P95, error rate, quality regressions) and that enforces a time-to-live (TTL) for stalled stages to prevent indefinite partial rollouts. This PR adds an orchestrator component (CohortSynchronousSplitter) which complements existing canary and shadow controllers by: 1) allowing cohort-bound grouping for traffic slices (e.g., by tenant, region, or user segment); 2) implementing an adaptive funnel controller that widens or narrows cohort exposure based on observed metrics; 3) enforcing a safety TTL that automatically rolls back or promotes cohorts after configured time windows to avoid human drift.
Design summary:
- New control plane API: rollout.strategy = "cohort-sync" with parameters: cohort_keys, initial_fraction, funnel_step, metrics_gates (latency_p95_threshold, error_rate_threshold, quality_regression_delta), stage_ttl_seconds, max_cohorts, deterministic_sampling_seed.
- Runtime behavior: Splitter deterministically assigns requests to cohorts using stable hashing on cohort_keys; the funnel controller monitors aggregated metrics per-cohort and applies a decision graph each evaluation interval. If a stalled stage exceeds stage_ttl_seconds without either meeting promotion criteria or receiving manual intervention, the safety TTL triggers an automated rollback to the last known-good cohort and emits an incident event.
- Observability: emits new metrics (rollout.cohort.exposure, rollout.cohort.p95_latency, rollout.cohort.quality_delta, rollout.cohort.ttl_expiry) and tracing spans for decisions. Console adds a cohort timeline with TTL indicators.
- Backwards compatibility: Default rollout strategy remains unchanged; the new strategy is opt-in. Migration path documented.
Checklist (implemented):
- [x] API surface for cohort-synchronous splitters
- [x] Runtime deterministic cohort assignment
- [x] Adaptive funnel controller with multi-signal gates
- [x] Safety TTL enforcement and automatic rollback action
- [x] Unit tests for assignment, promotion, rollback logic
- [x] Integration test with simulated traffic generator and metrics sink
- [x] Console timeline UI + docs example
- [x] End-to-end perf benchmark for 1k qps workload
- [x] Feature flag gate for gradual enablement
Detailed description (single paragraph): This change introduces a cohesive rollout primitive designed for multi-tenant, production-grade deployments where fairness and safety are required. Unlike regular canaries that phase based on percentage only, the cohort-synchronous splitter lets operators group users into cohorts and advance them in lockstep while the funnel controller adaptively tunes exposure based on real-time signals. A TTL prevents partial rollouts from lingering when automated gating conditions are noisy or when SREs are occupied, by rolling back to a safe cohort after expiry and creating a traceable incident that records the decision path.
Implementation notes:
- Control plane: new controller implementation under redwood/controller/rollouts/cohort_sync_controller.go.
- Serving runtime: lightweight assignment layer inside redwood/serving/splitter/hash_assigner.go, respects existing batching and KV cache semantics.
- Metrics & alerts: new prometheus metrics + alert templates in redwood/observability/alerts/cohort_rollouts.rules.yml.
- Console: cohort timeline component redwood-console/src/components/RolloutCohortTimeline.tsx and API wiring redwood-console/src/api/rollouts.ts.
Safety considerations:
- Rollback action is idempotent and uses existing fallback policies (route to pinned-version) to avoid double-failures.
- Deterministic sampling seed can be set per-rollout to ensure reproducible splits for debugging.
- TTL default is conservative (24h) and can be overridden per-rollout.
Related work: builds on ENG-7244 adaptive canary gates and is intended to work alongside shadow mirroring features implemented in ENG-8410.
Linear tickets: ENG-9241 (cohort-sync design), PM-1130 (product acceptance criteria).
Lydia Park: Nice concept. Two asks before approve: add/update unit tests for TTL expiry path and ensure deterministic seed is present in serialized rollout object.
Arjun Patel: Addressed — added TTL unit test and serialized seed in the API. See commit b7c8d9e and assigner_test updates.
Evan Martinez: CI flaked on integration test (timeout) — please retry with increased test harness timeout. Also suggest a small perf test for 5k qps path.
Arjun Patel: Increased harness timeout and added a bench config for 5k qps in benchmarks. Integration test rerun passed.
Priya Singh: Security review: ensure incident payload does not contain PII. Confirmed redwood/security/policy_review.md documents this restraint.
Lydia Park: Approved after changes. Marking ready to merge.
Release Manager (automated): merge-safety-check passed; no overlapping migrations detected.
Adds 'cohort-sync' rollout strategy: deterministic cohort splitting, adaptive funnel gating, and TTL-driven automated rollback to reduce stale partial rollouts. Opt-in feature behind feature flag. Console timeline and alerts included.
Feature gated. To enable: set rollout.strategy=cohort-sync and provide cohort_keys and stage_ttl_seconds. Recommend starting with stage_ttl_seconds >= 86400 and monitoring rollout.cohort.p95_latency and rollout.cohort.quality_delta. If TTL expiries occur frequently, increase gate tolerances or investigate metric noise sources.
This change provides safer progression for multi-tenant rollouts and reduces manual intervention by automatically reverting stalled stages. Performance overhead is minimal (deterministic hashing and a small control loop).

payload.body:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets currently allocate reservation credits to tenants based on static commitments + a simple burst pool. This leads to two problems: (1) long-lived underutilized reservations that waste capacity during pressure windows, and (2) brittle low-latency guarantees when many tenants simultaneously consume burst tokens. This PR introduces a reservation watermarking and safety allocator that dynamically adjusts effective reservations, reclaims idle headroom, and enforces safety caps during overload.

High-level design: We add two concepts to the fleet allocator: a low watermark (committed floor) and a reclaim watermark (soft cap above committed). When tenant utilization falls below the reclaim watermark for a configurable idle window, the allocator tags the reservation as reclaimable and moves that capacity into an ephemeral pool. Conversely, during load surges the allocator will respect a safety cap per-tenant (configurable percentage of total fleet) to avoid noisy-neighbor collapse. The allocator integrates with the autoscaler and the burst pool — reclaimed capacity is visible to the burst pool and prioritized by fairness score.

Behavioral changes: - Reservations are no longer binary; they carry dynamic effective_reservation values computed from watermarks and recent utilization histograms. - Ephemeral pool uses LRU-style aging and per-tenant priority buckets (production, critical, standard) to decide assignment. - Safety caps prevent any single tenant from consuming more than X% of cluster capacity; X is a runtime knob that can be tuned per-fleet. - Preemption: when safety caps are hit, lower-priority ephemeral allocations are preempted before cutting into committed floors.

Files changed (high-level): allocation/allocator.go (new watermark logic), allocation/ephemeral_pool.go (LRU aging + priority queues), autoscaler/integrations.go (hook for reclaimed capacity), api/v1/reservation.proto (expose watermarks and effective_reservation), telemetry/metrics.yaml (new metrics), observability/dashboards/reservation-overview.json, e2e/tests/reservation_reclaim_test.go, pkg/config/fleet_defaults.yaml, docs/allocator.md (design doc + knobs), small client changes in sdk-go and sdk-python to surface new reservation fields.

Commits (summary): - introduce reservation watermark structs and histogram-based utilization tracker - implement reclaimable tagging and ephemeral pool assignment - safety cap enforcement and preemption path - autoscaler integration to treat reclaimed capacity as available headroom - add metrics/tracing and dashboard wiring - unit + e2e tests + docs + SDK surface fields

Testing and results: Unit tests cover watermark transitions and preemption paths. E2E benchmark on a 50-GPU staging fleet reproduces a 7-day mixed-tenant workload: compared to baseline, median request latency at 95th percentile improved 8-12% for standard tenants under bursty arrival patterns, and overall cluster utilization increased from 64% to 78% during daytime peaks. Tail regressions under a simulated hot-tenant were prevented by safety caps; we observed negligible SLA violations in the runs.

Rollout plan: Feature gate behind fleet.experimental.reservation_watermarks (off by default). Canary rollout to 2 fleets (dev and staging) for 48 hours with telemetry alerting on reclamation_rate and preempt_count. If stable, enable on low-risk production fleets for 72 hours, then full roll once autoscaler equilibrium metrics are stable.

Related: ENG-7684 implements the reclamation telemetry; ENG-7710 tracks dashboard and alerting changes. SUP-2102 was an incident prompting earlier manual reclamation of idle reservations.

Notes: This PR intentionally avoids changing the committed billing model or customer-visible reservation guarantees; effective_reservation is an internal serving-time construct and is surfaced in telemetry and SDK only for observability.
Marcus Li (reviewer): Can you clarify the durability semantics when a reclaimed allocation is preempted? Would that trigger immediate cancellation of in-flight requests?
Author (Aisha): Good question. We only preempt ephemeral allocations, which are never guaranteed for in-flight requests. In-flight requests under ephemeral allocation are given a 300ms drain window communicated via the runtime; if they exceed that, the request will be rejected with a 429 and logged under preempt_count. Committed floors are never preempted.
Diego Ramos (reviewer): I ran the stress job and saw a spike in scheduler CPU with the histogram computations. Can we cache the bucket summaries and only recompute every 500ms?
Author (Aisha): Implemented a lightweight sliding-window summary cache and moved the histogram crunch to the allocator worker thread. CPU overhead dropped ~40% in my microbenchmarks; pushed a follow-up commit
Sofia Nguyen (reviewer): We need an ops kill-switch in case reclaiming causes instability in a fleet. Suggest a runtime flag to set reclaim_rate to 0 and a dashboard panel to flip it.
Author (Aisha): Added fleet.experimental.reclaim_rate (float, default 0.2) and an Ops runbook entry in docs/allocator.md. Also added an unsafe_disable_reclaim boolean for emergency toggles.
Marcus Li: Approval after the CPU cache change and runbook additions. 
- approved by Marcus Li
Sofia Nguyen: Approved. 
- approved by Sofia Nguyen
Diego Ramos: Approved after addressing the histogram recompute scheduling. 
- approved by Diego Ramos
payload.title: Tenant reservation watermarking and safety allocator

payload.body:
Motivation: We observed intermittent correctness regressions and KV-cache divergence when nodes opportunistically switched to lower-precision kernels under load. These issues were most pronounced during warm-up phases and when continuous-batching mixed short warm-up sequences with steady-state traffic. The goal of this PR is to make the low-precision fast path reliable in production by adding conservative checks and an automatic, observable annealing mechanism that trades small amounts of peak throughput for deterministic correctness.

Summary of changes: add a light-weight per-node kernel stability probe that runs microbenchmarks on model startup and periodically during low-utilization windows; expose a configurable 'kernel_stability_threshold' that gates transitions to low-precision kernels; implement a precision-annealing state machine that steps precision down gradually (fp32 -> fp16 -> int8) only when stability and latency criteria are met; add a kv-sync-guard which attaches short-lived checksums to KV cache snapshots and prevents applying a cache state if checksum mismatch or stale-timestamp detected; update continuous-batching heuristics to avoid batching sequences observed during the warm-up probe and to prefer homogeneous-decoded sequences to reduce cache churn.

Configuration and defaults: default kernel_stability_threshold=0.92 (fraction of microbench runs that must pass), anneal_step_interval=30s, min_stable_window=2m. Operators can override in runtime config or via console per-cluster. Canary rollout automatically enables annealing on 10% of nodes by default.

Design notes: stability probe is intentionally lightweight (per-model token-limited runs) and runs on a background worker with a low scheduling priority. We capture simple metrics: decode latency variance, kernel success/failure, and checksum of produced KV updates. The precision-annealing state machine records a rollback count and will automatically revert to the last-known-good precision if a regression is detected for two consecutive evaluation windows. KV-sync-guard uses a small 64-bit checksum and timestamp to detect divergent updates; it prevents a stale or corrupt cache from being applied and triggers a re-fetch path that is more conservative (sequential KV application with verification).

Performance and correctness: measured on internal perf-lab with a mix of 1k short-chat and 200 long-generation traces: baseline (optimistic fp16 fastpath without probes) showed +12.3% token/sec vs safe fp32 but a 2.8% rare correctness/regression signal on our eval set and occasional KV-invalidation incidents during canary. With this PR enabled (default canary), we observe +9.1% token/sec, p95 token latency improved by 6ms relative to safe fp32, and correctness regressions dropped to 0.12% (within noise). CPU/GPU telemetry indicates a ~7% reduction in wasted kernel restarts during warm-up.

Commits (summary):
- feat(kernel): add kernel stability probe, probe scheduler, and probe metrics (maya/commit/1)
- feat(anneal): implement precision-annealing state machine and runtime flags (maya/commit/2)
- fix(kv): implement kv-sync-guard with checksum verification and fallback path (alex/commit/3)
- perf(scheduler): adjust continuous-batching heuristic to avoid warm-up mixing (noah/commit/4)
- test(perf): new perf harness scenarios and canary harness (sofia/commit/5)
- docs: ops notes and runtime configuration docs (maya/commit/6)

Files touched (high level):
- src/runtime/kernel_probe.cpp (new)
- src/runtime/kernel_selector.cpp (modify)
- src/runtime/precision_annealer.cpp (new)
- src/cache/kv_manager.rs (modify)
- src/scheduler/batcher.rs (modify)
- tests/perf/annealing_scenarios.py (new)
- ops/docs/fastpath-ops.md (new)
- scripts/canary_rollout.py (modify)

Testing: unit tests added for state machine transitions and kv-sync checksum logic; integration canary runs in perf-lab for 48h; additional chaos test where random kernel failure is injected to validate rollback behavior. CI initially failed on a flaky kv-manager apply test (race in test harness); I fixed the test harness timing and re-ran. Final CI: all checks passed (build, unit, integration-smoke, perf-canary sim).

Review conversation (high level):
- Andre Patel: "This looks promising — my main concern is metric noise causing oscillation. Can we add hysteresis?"
- Maya Chen: "Added rollback_count and min_stable_window config to prevent oscillation; updated tests to exercise noisy conditions."
- Sofia Lopez: "KV checksum is a good safety net. Can we make checksum optional for extremely latency-sensitive clusters?"
- Maya Chen: "Yes — checksum can be disabled per-cluster; documented tradeoffs in ops doc and console UI will show expected risk increase."
- Noah Kim: "Please ensure the annealer doesn't increase tail latency under multimodal traffic."
- Maya Chen: "Batcher heuristic update ensures warm-up sequences are isolated, avoiding mixed-batch tail effects; added perf tests that mimic multimodal traffic."
- Andre Patel: approved after minor doc nits.
- Sofia Lopez: approved.

CI and canary: initial canary run on 10% nodes for 72h showed stability; we increased to 30% and then full rollout. Post-rollout monitoring showed one transient kv-stall on a highly loaded node which was auto-rolled back by annealing and later resolved by a kernel patch (follow-up PR scheduled).

Backward compatibility and migration: all flags default to conservative values; clusters not opting into canary see no behavior change. Ops doc includes a migration checklist to enable annealing and KV checksum on dedicated clusters.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-2493: extend probe to multi-model ensembles (planned)
- SRE-619: dashboard and alerting on kernel stability score
- Hotfix PR planned to backport small kv-sync optimization to 2026.02 release branch if customers request earlier rollout.

Merge: squashed and merged to main on 2026-02-18 after approvals and green CI.

Notes for maintainers: keep an eye on SLO dashboards for the first 2 weeks after rollout; if automated rollback rates exceed 0.5% consider increasing min_stable_window or disabling annealing during peak traffic windows.
Adds kernel stability probes, a precision-annealing state machine, and a kv-sync guard to reduce correctness regressions when switching to low-precision fast paths; safe defaults and canary rollout enabled.

payload.body:
Motivation: customers using the OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat.completions endpoint reported mismatches in behavior vs public OpenAI: stop sequences passed as arrays were ignored in some paths, roles from third-party SDKs (e.g. 'user_message', 'assistant-v2') were treated as free-form tokens causing downstream routing bugs, and streamed deltas did not reliably surface logprobs or tool-call boundaries. This PR brings parity for common OpenAI shapes and stabilizes streaming for tool/function calling.

What this PR does: 1) Accepts `stop` as either a string or an array of strings for both non-streaming and streaming requests; arrays are checked before string fallback. 2) Introduces a canonicalizer for incoming message.role values (mapping known aliases to system|user|assistant|tool). 3) Adds consistent inclusion of token-level `logprobs` in streaming deltas when the client requests `logprobs` in the completion params, guaranteeing that final streamed event and non-streaming response match. 4) Implements a lightweight framing shim for tool/function calls during streaming: we emit explicit `tool_call.start` and `tool_call.end` events (internal event type in streaming payloads) so clients can reliably reconstruct tool invocations without waiting for finalization. 5) Tests and updates the OpenAI compat middleware and SDK adapters to exercise these changes.

Compatibility notes: default behavior preserves existing Redwood semantics for clients that do not enable strict OpenAI compatibility mode. The new canonical role mappings are idempotent for standard roles; collisions only arise for exotic aliases and are logged at INFO. Stop-array handling is enabled for all users because it is safe and consistent with real-world usage. Streaming framing is additive and does not change final text outputs.

Testing and verification: unit tests for the canonicalizer, stop-array parsing, and streaming event generator; integration tests that compare /v1/chat.completions (compat) vs the native API for the same prompts; an E2E smoke run against the TypeScript SDK and a small canary in staging with real traffic for 48h.

Rollout plan: feature gates exist behind `OPENAI_COMPAT_STRICT` environment flag. Default rollout: enable stop-array & role canonicalization cluster-wide on day 0; enable streaming framing behind the flag, flip for 10% traffic after CI green, expand to 50% then 100% if no regressions.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration tests added (compat matrix)
- [x] SDK adapter updates (ts + py)
- [x] Canary plan documented

Links: Linear ENG-1764 (compat parity), ENG-1899 (streaming reliability), SUPPORT ticket SUP-742.

- Add full support for stop as an array (matches OpenAI /v1/chat.completions semantics)
- Normalize message.role values coming from clients to canonical set: system/user/assistant/tool
- Ensure streamed delta events include consistent logprobs when requested
- Introduce streaming framing shim to keep function/tool-call boundaries in partial responses
- Backwards-compatible by default; opt-in flag to enable strict OpenAI-mode for legacy clients
Cameron Li: Overall looks good. Can you add one more test that mixes stop arrays with streaming and ensures earlier termination?
Asha Patel: Added streaming stop-array termination test and updated integration script to simulate high-latency token tails.
Sofia Martinez: The role canonicalization map needs a comment about future collisions and a metric; request adding a metric count for 'role_alias_mapped'.
Asha Patel: Added role_alias_mapped counter and a short note in openai_compat.md explaining mapping policy.
Ethan Boyd: CI flake on linux/arm build in first run; reran CI and fixed a tiny concurrency bug in stream_generator.go related to token buffer reuse.
Cameron Li: Approved after the concurrency fix and added tests.

payload.body:
Motivation: Client integrations expect /v1/chat.completions parity for streaming envelopes, stop semantics, and tool/function-calling metadata. We observed two classes of mismatches in production: (1) clients that prefer framed JSON chunks lost continuity when the runtime emitted line-delimited fragments; (2) stop sequences could trigger early termination during KV-cache fragmentation or backpressure, especially with short stop tokens and interleaved tool calls. Additionally, tool_call metadata was not consistently propagated across internal fallback paths, leading to broken tool orchestration in multi-model fallbacks.

This PR implements a small negotiation layer and runtime safeguards to achieve parity while maintaining our internal streaming optimizations. Changes are backward compatible (negotiation defaults to current behavior) and covered by unit/integration tests and a compatibility test targeting popular OpenAI client behaviors.

What I changed (summary): 1) Add a lightweight framing_mode negotiation header so clients can opt-in to "framed-json" envelopes or remain on "ldjson"/line-delimited streams; server selects the most restrictive framing supported by both sides to preserve compatibility. 2) Implement a stop-sequence backoff heuristic: when short stop tokens are detected within the last N tokens and a flush would otherwise close the stream, the runtime waits up to a small jittered window to confirm termination (reduces false-positive stops under KV/cache fragmentation and bursty batching). 3) Ensure tool_call metadata (origin, tool_id, correlation_id) is serialized into the stream envelope and preserved through fallback/model-swap paths; this required changes to the coordinator and the fallback merge logic. 4) Normalized the logprobs envelope key to match OpenAI's naming for downstream tooling and added a transform for legacy clients. 5) Added docs, a compatibility test harness, and JS + Python SDK adapters for the framing negotiation header.

Checklist: - [x] API: framing negotiation header + default behaviors - [x] Runtime: backoff and safe-termination guard - [x] Tooling: persist tool_call metadata across fallbacks - [x] SDK: opt-in header in JS/Python compat adapters - [x] Tests: unit + integration + compatibility matrix - [x] Docs: compatibility note and migration guide

Commits (high-level): - c1b3d9f: negotiate framing_mode header and unit tests - 3a0f11e: runtime: stop backoff heuristic and jitter window - f9d2a0b: coordinator: preserve tool_call metadata during fallback - 7b4c621: adapt JS/Python compat layers to expose framing header - 2d8ea12: normalize logprobs envelope and update docs - 0a6f9e7: compatibility test harness and matrix results in CI

Files touched (high level): - api/openai_compat/v1/chat_adapter.py - runtime/stream/coordinator.go - runtime/stream/framing_policy.go - runtime/kv/cache_manager.cc - runtime/fallback/merge_policy.go - sdk/js/openai_compat.ts - sdk/python/redwood/openai_compat.py - docs/openai-v1-framing.md - tests/compat/test_stop_backoff.py - tests/compat/test_framing_matrix.js - examples/compat/framed-json-example.md

Review notes and discussion (abridged): - Anika Shah: "Can we keep the default unchanged for existing clients and gate the framed-json behavior behind an explicit header?" -> Response: default is unchanged; header is opt-in. - Liam O'Connor: "Backoff window looks fine but we should ensure it doesn't violate strict latency SLAs for paid tiers." -> Response: backoff is bounded and only applies when stop tokens are ambiguous; added a config knob per-customer and a runtime SLO guard that aborts backoff past a hard cap. - Priya Nair: "Tool metadata serialization looks good, but add a test for multi-tool call interleaving." -> Response: added test case in tests/compat/test_tool_interleave.py.

CI: initial run failed on a flaky test in tests/compat/test_framing_matrix.js (timeout). I re-ran the job, fixed a race in the test harness (use deterministic port allocation) and CI passed all checks.

Merge: squashed and merged to main after approvals. Linear references updated: ENG-4621 moved to "Done".

Notes for operators: rollout is safe-by-default. To enable framed-json universally, ops can set framing_mode: framed-json at the customer routing policy; otherwise clients can request it via the X-Redwood-Framing header. Backoff defaults are conservative; manifest keys allow disabled behavior per-customer for low-latency SLAs.
Stabilizes OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: introduces framing negotiation, improves stop-sequence backoff to reduce premature stream termination, and ensures tool_call metadata survives fallbacks and model switches.
Anika Shah: please ensure default is unchanged -> Sofia: default unchanged, header opt-in
Liam O'Connor: note latency SLO impact -> Sofia: added per-customer knob and hard cap for backoff
Priya Nair: add multi-tool interleaving test -> Sofia: added tests/compat/test_tool_interleave.py

Context and motivation: Production customers hit a class of errors where brief client disconnects (mobile network flaps, browser tab swaps) caused long-running streaming requests that invoked tools to either get duplicated or be lost after client reconnect. Existing resume tokens preserved raw streaming offsets but did not maintain function-call intent or partial outputs, making resuming tool invocations unsafe. This PR introduces a small set of changes to make streaming resumes predictable and safe for function/tool calls and structured output in the OpenAI compatibility layer.

What this change does (single continuous description): Adds a server-side "reconnect quarantine" (default 20s) during which a session can reconnect and claim in-flight stream state; introduces a server-enforced soft-cancel TTL for tool/function calls that allows the runtime to decide whether to allow the tool to finish or abort early when a client disconnects; augments resume tokens with a per-invocation idempotency key and partial-result checkpoint so a resumed session can continue or safely re-run a tool without duplicating side effects; updates the OpenAI-compat adapter to carry function_call metadata across resume and to map resumed partial payloads into the structured output contract; updates JS/Python SDKs to surface resume semantics, honor reconnect hints, and provide explicit opt-out flags for aggressive hard-cancel; adds end-to-end harness tests that simulate flaky disconnects and targeted regression coverage for previously observed duplicate-tool invocation failures.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc and linear: ENG-3881 - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] E2E reconnect harness with simulated network flakiness - [x] Backwards-compatible adapter changes with feature flag (compat.resume_v2) - [x] Docs and SDK changelog entries - [x] Perf regression bench run (no regression in p50 latency observed)

Commits (high-level): - "session: introduce reconnect_quarantine manager with TTL and reclaim logic" - "runtime: soft-cancel policy and invocation idempotency keys" - "openai_adapter: preserve function_call and partial_args across resume" - "sdk-js: expose resumeToken behavior & reconnectHints to clients" - "sdk-py: resume client + test harness" - "tests: e2e flaky disconnect harness and regression cases" - "docs: streaming resume semantics and migration guidance"

Changed areas (high level): service/streaming/session_manager.go - new reconnect quarantine manager; runtime/invocation/soft_cancel.go - soft-cancel/safe-retry logic; adapters/openai/compat.go - carry function_call metadata and partial-result checkpointing; sdk/js/streaming.ts - resumeToken handling, reconnect hints; sdk/python/stream_client.py - same for python SDK; tests/e2e/stream_reconnect_spec.py - new harness; docs/api/streaming_resume.md - documentation and migration notes; console/observability/alerts.yaml - tuned alert thresholds for streaming disconnect spikes.

Review conversation (highlights): - Priya: "Can you clarify how the idempotency key is generated and where it is stored? If it's ephemeral only in memory we risk losing it on a node failover." 
Author (Ava): "Good call — idempotency key is now stored in the session metadata (persisted to our session store with eventual expiration aligned to the quarantine TTL). Updated commit adds migration to ensure older sessions get a generated key on first touch."
- Lucas: "The soft-cancel branch looks reasonable, but we need a clear operator knob to lower the quarantine in high-load scenarios to avoid resource hoarding." 
Author: "Added server config 'stream.reconnect_quarantine_ms' and admit policy to the Dedicated config; also threw in metrics (stream.quarantine_claims, stream.quarantine_evictions) for SLO tracing."
- Zoe: "SDK behaviour: when a client receives a resume token and then immediately reconnects, do we double-ack function calls? We should document recommended client-side backoff." 
Author: "Added SDK helpers and docs recommending an exponential jittered reconnect up to the quarantine window; SDK also exposes 'resumeMode' with explicit 'resume' | 'restart' choices."

CI & testing summary: - CI pipeline initially failed one flaky e2e test (tests/e2e/stream_reconnect_spec.py::test_multiple_disconnects) on first run; root cause was non-deterministic test harness timing. Adjusted harness timing and reran. - All unit tests: pass - Integration: pass - E2E (re-run): pass - Benchmarks: p50 latency unchanged, p95 +3% under pathological reconnect storm (acceptable; documented and configuration knob added).

Migration & backward compatibility: The OpenAI adapter changes are behind a feature flag (compat.resume_v2). Existing sessions continue to use the legacy resume behavior until customers opt-in or until we flip the default after the deprecation window. SDKs will default to presenting the new behavior but will not force servers to adopt it.

Operational notes: Added two new metrics and one alert: stream.quarantine_claims (counter), stream.quarantine_evictions (counter), alert "HighStreamingQuarantineUtilization" (fires when >80% of streaming pool has claimed quarantine slots for >5min). Documentation includes mitigation (reduce quarantine_ms, increase pool capacity, or enable fast-hard-cancel).

Merge notes: squash-merged after approvals; no migration scripts required for customer data beyond session metadata backfill which is handled lazily on first resume touch.

If you want to exercise the new flow locally: see docs/api/streaming_resume.md and the e2e harness under tests/e2e/ for guidance on toggling the feature flag and simulating reconnects.
Adds server-side reconnect quarantine window (default 20s) and configurable server-enforced soft-cancel timeouts; improves resume semantics for function/tool calls so partial tool results are preserved and retried idempotently; public SDKs updated to surface resume token behavior and retry guidance.
Priya Nair: Can you clarify how the idempotency key is generated and where it is stored? If it's ephemeral only in memory we risk losing it on a node failover.
Ava Chen: Added persistence to session store with TTL aligned to quarantine window; updated migration and tests.
Lucas Meyer: Need operator knob to lower quarantine in high load to avoid resource hoarding.
Ava Chen: Added config 'stream.reconnect_quarantine_ms' and metrics: stream.quarantine_claims/evictions.
Zoe Patel: SDK behaviour edge case: potential double-ack on immediate reconnect; recommend client-side backoff.
Ava Chen: Added SDK helper for jittered reconnect and explicit resumeMode to avoid accidental double-runs.

payload.body:
Motivation: users building complex tool chains requested clearer ergonomics for multi-tool and parallel tool calls (particularly when mixing streaming LLM output and tool result injection), more predictable retry semantics for transient tool runner failures, and a path toward OpenAI-compat structured output envelopes. This PR refactors the tool execution API surface to: 1) introduce a high-level ToolExecutionPlan that expresses ordered or parallel tool groups (supports per-tool concurrency hints), 2) add explicit injection_points that let the runtime insert structured tool result envelopes into the streamed token sequence with stable delimiter tokens, and 3) add idempotency keys + exponential jittered retry helpers for tool runners plus a coordinator-level retry policy that avoids double-execution for side-effectful tools. Changes are backward-compatible by default: the previous single-tool call path remains supported. Key behaviors: - Parallel groups: the planner can execute non-dependent tools in parallel and stream their results as interleaved structured envelopes; ordering is preserved inside each tool. - Injection points: callers can specify where tool outputs should appear relative to assistant messages (before/after/specific-token anchors). Runtime emits a consistent JSONL envelope ("__tool_result__" token marker) that SDKs can hydrate into structured_output items. - Retries: each tool execution gets an idempotency_key; coordinator will not retry tools marked non-idempotent. Retries use configurable backoff with randomized jitter and a max_attempts cap. - OpenAI-compat: compatibility layer extended with new fields (tool_concurrency, injection_points, structured_output_v1) and translation helpers for older client requests. Implementation summary: - Core: refactor tool_orchestrator (pkg/runtime/orchestrator) to a planner/executor split. - Protocol: introduce tool_execution_plan.proto and structured_result.proto for wire-stable envelopes. - Streaming: update streaming multiplexer to recognize tool envelope markers and avoid buffering assistant tokens while waiting for parallel tool results (reduces stalls). - SDK: client-side helpers in redwood-sdk-typescript to build plans and to parse injected structured_output envelopes; updated examples. - Tests: unit coverage for parallel scheduling, injection ordering, and idempotency logic; integration test that replays a previously flaky golden stream (reproduced in perf-canary). Risks and mitigations: - Streaming order complexity: added end-to-end integration test and a new stream fuzzer that exercises interleaving; watchdog will force fallback to sequential group execution on detection of malformed envelopes. - Backwards compatibility: compatibility translators inserted early in request pipeline; maintained default behavior. Checklist: - [x] planner/executor split implemented - [x] structured envelopes defined and stable - [x] SDK helpers in TS added - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs + migration notes drafted - [x] perf canary run (green) Related: ENG-3421 (tooling ergonomics), ENG-3560 (streaming stability).
Luis Moreno (review): This is a large surface change — can we ensure we have a clear migration path for existing single-tool callers? Suggest adding a compatibility translator unit test.
Priya Kaur (author): Added compat_translator.go and unit test; kept old single-tool handler on by default. See added test: test/unit/compat/single_tool_compat.test.go.
Asha Patel (review): Concern about streaming: if two parallel tools emit many small chunks, will we interleave them in a way that breaks existing streaming parsers? Recommend a distinct token marker and an opt-in flag for early rollout.
Priya Kaur (author): Implemented __tool_result__ JSONL envelope token and added opt-in header X-Redwood-Tool-Injection to gate injection until SDKs can be rolled out. Also added stream fuzzer and an integration test that simulates many small chunks.
Tom Bernard (review): Please add metrics for dropped/invalid envelopes and a canary run. Also double-check telemetry does not leak tool outputs in non-PII-safe logs.
Priya Kaur (author): Added tool_execution_metrics and masked tool payloads in observability layer; triggered a perf-canary run (see CI comments).
Introduce ToolExecutionPlan to express parallel/ordered tool groups, injection_points for deterministic streamed tool result insertion (JSONL __tool_result__ envelopes), coordinator-level retry policy with idempotency keys, and OpenAI-compatibility translations for tool_concurrency and structured_output_v1. Backwards-compatible by default; SDK updates available in typescript package.
This PR touches runtime, protocol, SDK and docs. We intentionally kept the default behavior unchanged and gated injection behind an opt-in header to reduce risk during rollout. Perf canary showed median latency unchanged and tail latency improved for mixed tool/LLM workloads.
payload.title: refactor(tool-exec): ergonomic multi-tool orchestration, result injection, and retry semantics

payload.body:
Motivation: production workloads increasingly issue multiple tool calls per response (lookups, enrichment, external actions) and clients expect predictable injection semantics, low-latency parallelism, and transparent retry behavior when external tools fail. This PR introduces a lightweight multiplexer for tool execution that: 1) executes independent tool calls in parallel when safe, 2) exposes an explicit idempotency token + retry middleware for transient tool failures, 3) provides an ergonomic result-injection API surface for handlers (deterministic injection points with ordering hints), and 4) keeps OpenAI-compatibility behaviors (function-calling fallback and structured outputs) intact.

Summary of changes: commits implement a runtime-level ToolMultiplexer that accepts a list of ToolCall requests and returns deterministic ToolResults with stable ids and insertion points. We added a RetryMiddleware that respects per-tool idempotency tokens and exponential backoff policies, and a backpressure-aware worker pool that bounds concurrency based on route config. The compatibility shim for openai->redwood function calling was updated to translate function return values into the new ToolResult shape. Documentation and SDK ergonomics were updated (Python and TS examples) and end-to-end tests were added for mixed success/failure scenarios.
Ava Chen: High-level looks good. Two API questions: (1) should we make ordering_hint mandatory on ToolCall or optional? make it optional with clear docs. (2) How do we communicate partial failure to the caller (status + per-tool error) — ensure structured output maps to OpenAI function semantics.
Diego Morales: Reply: ordering_hint is optional; multiplexer will preserve provided order when present and otherwise use deterministic sort by tool_id. Partial failures are surfaced as per-tool result objects (status: success|error) and we map that to function-calling content for openai shim (see compat_layer translation).
Priya Natarajan: Is idempotency enforced only by user-provided token? What about non-idempotent tools invoked in parallel — risk of duplicate side effects. Recommend a warning in docs and a safe-mode flag at route level.
Diego Morales: Added route config 'tool_safe_mode' that forces serial execution for non-idempotent tools and emits warning log + telemetry. Updated docs and SDK helper to accept idempotency_token.
- Add ToolMultiplexer to execute multiple tool calls in parallel when safe; supports ordering hints and deterministic injection points.
- Introduce per-tool idempotency tokens and RetryMiddleware with exponential backoff.
- OpenAI compatibility shim updated to translate function calling into multiplexer-friendly ToolCalls and map results into structured outputs.
- New observability metrics: tool.count, tool.latency.p95, tool.retry.count.
- Route config 'tool_safe_mode' to force serial execution for non-idempotent workflows.
When rolling out to Dedicated clusters, monitor tool.retry.count and tool.latency.p95. Default workerpool size reduced to 16 (was 32) to limit memory pressure on small nodes. If customers rely on side-effecting tools without idempotency tokens, recommend enabling tool_safe_mode on the route.
Merged via squash after approvals and rerun of flaky e2e. No migrations required.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: We observed periodic micro-stalls in the continuous batching scheduler under mixed KV-heavy and short-lived inference workloads. Root cause analysis pointed to: (1) tight deterministic deadline windows causing synchronized probe storms when many requests reach the same soft timeout boundary, and (2) KV-pinned requests monopolizing head-of-queue positions leading to starvation of small, latency-sensitive requests. This PR introduces two cooperative mechanisms: (A) soft-timeout probes with randomized jitter and exponential backoff to avoid synchronized probe storms, and (B) deadline-steering that biases scheduling decisions away from long-KV pins during probe windows so short requests have a better chance to complete. Both are runtime-only scheduler changes with no public API surface.

Summary of changes: - New probe subsystem (internal/serving/batcher/probe.go) implements soft probes: instead of hard preemption at N ms, a soft probe flags requests for lightweight admission checks. Probes are jittered +/- up to 25% and use an adaptive backoff per origin to reduce re-probing frequency for offenders. - Scheduler modifications (internal/serving/batcher/scheduler.go): when a soft-probed request is present, scheduler evaluates a deadline-steering score that temporarily reduces priority of requests with active KV pins and high predicted token cost. The steering is proportional to probe urgency and decays over a configurable grace window. - KV awareness (internal/serving/kv/cache_manager.go): probes annotate requests with kv_pin_estimate and attach a short-lived lease so the scheduler can reason about potential blocking. - Observability (pkg/observe/metrics/batcher_metrics.go): new metrics added: batcher_probe_count, probe_backoff_rate, deadline_steer_evictions, kv_pin_lease_count; histograms for probe-to-exec latency. - Tests and documentation: deterministic integration tests (tests/integration/batcher_stall_test.go) that simulate mixed workloads and assert tail-latency and throughput; runbook guidance for tuning the new knobs (docs/runbooks/batcher-tuning.md).

Design rationale: - Soft probes instead of hard timeouts: allow scheduler to make better packing decisions rather than preempting work. - Jitter reduces global synchronization under load spikes. - Steering uses lightweight heuristics (kv_pin_estimate + token_cost) to avoid complex global optimization loops; we prefer predictable, auditable behavior. - Backoff state is kept per-origin and capped to avoid state explosion.

Performance summary (internal CI/bench): - Baseline: mixed workload (60% KV-pin heavy long requests, 40% short chat-like requests) tail P95 token latency = 420ms over 30m window. - After change (default knobs): P95 = 320ms (-23%), P99 = 640ms (-14%), median unchanged. - CPU/GPU utilization: slight increase in scheduler CPU (~3%) but overall token throughput steady. - Under synthetic probe storms, observed probe storms reduced by ~78% due to jitter+backoff.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation + unit tests - [x] Integration test reproducing previous stall - [x] Metrics + dashboards updated - [x] Runbook draft - [x] Benchmarks and resource budget sanity - [x] Security review (no user data exfiltration risk)

Files changed (high level): - internal/serving/batcher/scheduler.go: add steering score, hook into admission path, unit tests for decay logic - internal/serving/batcher/probe.go: new file implementing probe lifecycle, jitter/backoff policy, probe metrics - internal/serving/kv/cache_manager.go: expose kv_pin_estimate and short leases for scheduler; small refactor to avoid locking hotspots - pkg/observe/metrics/batcher_metrics.go: new metrics and tags - tests/integration/batcher_stall_test.go: synthetic workload harness, asserts on tail-latency and fairness - docs/runbooks/batcher-tuning.md: knobs explanation and suggested defaults

Review conversation (excerpt): - Marco Liu (review): "Nice isolation of probe lifecycle. One concern: the per-origin backoff map could grow unbounded in high-tenant systems. Can we auto-evict or TTL entries?" - Author (Aisha): "Good catch — added TTL+LRU cap (configurable) and a cleanup tick; updated tests to validate eviction behavior." - Riley Thompson (review): "Can we avoid any mem alloc on the hot path for the steering score?" - Author: "We changed steering to use a preallocated scoring buffer and removed allocations in hot path; benchmark shows <1% extra allocs." - Priya Desai (approver): "Verified metrics and runbook; approved after a small nit on doc wording." - Additional comments: one infra CI failure (flake in tests/integration/flake_x) was rerun and passed.

CI and stability notes: - CI run: unit (pass), integration (pass after one rerun), benchmark jobs (internal perf cluster) completed and attached. - Notable flaky test fixed in this branch: tests/integration/flake_x — flake existed due to timing assumptions; made test robust to small timing variance.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan: - No API changes. - Feature gated behind runtime flag batcher.enable_soft_probes=false by default in main; rollout plan: enable for 10% rollout on Dedicated and Hosted canary pools for two weeks, monitor probe metrics + tail latency; then ramp to 50/100. - If regressions observed, automatic fallback policy in console will flip the flag and route to non-probed variant.

Operational guidance: - Default knobs are tuned for mixed production traffic; for KV-heavy enterprise workloads, increase kv_pin_lease_ms and reduce probe_jitter_pct. - Runbook (docs/runbooks/batcher-tuning.md) includes alert thresholds: probe_backoff_rate > 0.1 sustained and deadline_steer_evictions > 5/min should trigger investigation.

Merge notes: Squash-merged into main on 2025-12-02 after approvals. Merge commit: "squash: introduce soft probes + deadline steering (ENG-4012)".

payload.body:
Motivation: Dequantization work is a material token-level cost in quantized inference (INT8/FP8). Existing dequant+matmul+requant sequences introduce extra memory traffic and duplicate per-token scaling that becomes significant for long contexts and continuous-batching workloads. This PR implements a set of complementary changes: (1) a fused attention microkernel that accepts quantized inputs with packed per-head scaling metadata and emits quantized outputs without a separate dequant/requant roundtrip; (2) a temporal dequant amortization layer that caches and reuses per-head/per-key scale factors across contiguous KV windows; and (3) KV cache alignment logic so cached keys/values and their scale metadata remain coherent across prefix-shared requests and continuous batching. The goal is to reduce token-level dequant overhead while preserving numerical fidelity for INT8/FP8 models.
Arjun: Can you explain how per_head_scale is stored in the request blob? Risk: making blob larger could regress small-payload throughput — author: per_head_scale is optional and only present for quantized models; it's delta-compressed and only attached to first token in a KV window.
Evelyn: Numeric drift on FP8 models was visible in the initial microkernel; author: adjusted accumulation path and added 16-bit accumulation for attention softmax (see fused_attn_int8.cu lines ~220-260), reduced max delta to 1e-3 relative to baseline in our eval set.
Miguel: How do you ensure cache entries don't leak across tenants? author: scale_cache respects tenant IDs and uses the existing KV cache eviction + namespace keys; migration tool converts old caches to namespaced entries during rollout.
Arjun (follow-up): Please add telemetry for amortization hit-rate — author: added metrics runtime.kv.scale_cache.hits and .misses and a continuous-batcher tag for amortized requests.
There was a short red on the bench-suite due to an incorrect vectorized path for 1-token sequences; fixed in commit e52b730. After rerun, the bench-suite shows consistent improvements on INT8 and parity on FP8 numerical fidelity targets.
Microbenchmarks on A100 (p4d-style hardware) with batch sizes 1..64 and sequences up to 8192 tokens: INT8 end-to-end token latency reduced by 9-15% median and p99 improved by up to 18% on long sequences (>=2048). Throughput for sustained streaming workloads increased 12-22% depending on sequence length and batching configuration. FP8 variants show 4-7% improvements (mostly from reduced memory traffic) with <0.2% absolute change on per-token perplexity in our eval set. Amortization hit rate in canary traffic averaged 78% (higher on chat-like workloads).
Canary on non-production tenant group (10% traffic) for 72h with telemetry checks: kv.scale_cache.hits, p99 latency, and numeric regression alerts. Gradual ramp to 50% over 48h if no alerts; full rollout behind a runtime flag. Migration tool will be run as part of the controller rollout to convert existing KV cache entries; fallbacks available to disable temporal amortization per-tenant.
Included a migration tool (serving/runtime/integration/kv_migration_tool.py) that can convert existing cached KV blobs to include per_head_scale entries. Runtime supports both old and new cache formats; if new format not present the fused kernel falls back to the legacy dequant path. This ensures safe rollback.
Added unit tests for scale_cache eviction semantics and TTL; added integration tests that replay recorded chat sessions to validate scale reuse; extended bench harness to compare fused kernel vs baseline in identical scheduling conditions.
Performance: Reduced dequantization overhead for quantized models via fused attention microkernel and temporal amortization. Observable improvements in INT8 throughput & latency for streaming/continuous-batching workloads. Safe rollout with runtime flag and migration tool.

payload.body:
Summary: Introduces a hybrid scheduling path that allows requests to start on the fast, lower-precision kernel chain and transparently fall back to a conservative (safe-mode) kernel when numerical consistency checks fail or when upstream correctness policies are triggered. This change targets tail-latency and cost while preserving correctness guarantees for production workloads.
Motivation and context: We've seen intermittent regression cases where aggressive fast-path kernels (quantized/mixed-precision attention) provide large median improvements but occasionally diverge on corner conditions for long sequences or very large batch re-ordering. Existing fastpath gating is binary and heavily conservative, causing either too many misses (performance lost) or too few (correctness risk). This PR implements a gradual fallback strategy, per-request precision toggles, and a non-blocking correctness validator that reduces unnecessary escalations.
What changed (high level):
- New hybrid_scheduler module that tracks per-request health and assigns a decay score; requests with low confidence are staged onto safe-mode without global blocking.
- Introduced "precision_toggles": a lightweight per-layer hint metadata carried on requests so we can switch specific kernels from int8->fp16 or fp16->fp32 at layer granularity.
- Added an asynchronous correctness validator that performs lightweight checksum/consistency probes on a sampled subset of tokens; violations trigger targeted fallbacks rather than global disable.
- KV cache eviction integration: cache_manager now exposes a fast eviction hint for requests on fallback to reduce memory pressure and avoid cache thrash during degen sequences.
- Continuous batcher: added an adaptive window that short-circuits batching for requests flagged with high fallback probability to maintain tail latency.
- New unit and perf tests plus a small demo notebook exercising progressive fallback and toggles.
Performance notes: On our TPU and A100 perf lab runs with llama-variant workloads (seq=1024, mix of short/long prompts):
- Median latency (P50) improved by ~9% across the board due to opportunistic fast-path use.
- P95 improvements vary: up to 12% for conversation loads with moderate concurrency.
- P99 improved by 6-8% in scenarios where adaptive batching prevented harmful queueing.
- Cost: token compute cost reduced by ~7% in synthetic traces with 70% of requests eligible for fast-path.
Correctness/regression mitigation:
- The async validator samples ~1% of requests by default; when a mismatch is seen it records a fingerprint and triggers targeted re-execution on fp32 for that request only.
- Added metrics and tracing (fallback.reason, fallback.scope, fallback.count) to Redwood Console to make any degradation visible immediately.
Backwards compatibility and rollout:
- Feature gated behind config runtime.hybrid_fallback.enabled (off by default).
- Safe default: the scheduler starts in observation mode where it logs but does not alter routes; opt-in rollout via Dedicated flags and console toggles.
Aisha: Requested clearer invariants around when per-layer toggles are allowed; asked for explicit bounds on sampling rate and rationale. Miguel: Found a race in cache_manager eviction hints when requests downgrade mid-flight; asked for a small mutex or epoch check. Samir: Wanted a perf-run showing memory overhead for the async validator and suggested lowering default sample rate to 0.5% in prod. Author replies: Added committed fixes — replaced a naive atomic with epoch-based guard for cache hints, tightened toggle scope to attention+ffn only, and added an opt-out tag for latency-sensitive routes. Follow-ups: Add a dashboard panel for fallback fingerprints and a small incident runbook. Final: approved by all reviewers after 2 rounds of review.
Introduced Hybrid Scheduler with gradual fallback and per-layer precision toggles. Default disabled; opt-in via runtime.hybrid_fallback.enabled. Improves median latency and cost by opportunistically using lower-precision kernels while providing targeted fallbacks to maintain correctness. See docs/notes/hybrid_fallback.md for rollout steps and runbook.

payload.body:
This PR adds a CI-first pipeline to produce deterministic delta upgrade packages and stamp SBOM/provenance metadata into the private-installer release artifacts. Motivation: customers running Private (VPC/on-prem) need compact upgrade bundles and a verifiable upgrade graph so operators can perform safe roll-forwards and rollbacks without re-pulling full images. The output of the pipeline is a signed delta-index (delta-index.json) that expresses available upgrade paths between installer versions and references per-artifact SBOMs, Helm chart lockfiles, and Terraform module plan snapshots. Changes include: 1) new pipeline job (private-installer:delta-pack) that builds compact tarballs containing only changed manifests and image digests; 2) delta-indexer tool (tools/release/delta-indexer.go) which computes graph edges and emits SBOM references; 3) SBOM stamping step using syft and a lightweight metadata envelope; 4) cosign/cosign-wrapper integration to attach OCI signatures and timestamped provenance to each delta bundle; 5) Helm chart lockfile generator (charts/lockfiles/) and Terraform module plan snapshotter (terraform/modules/plan-snapshots/); 6) makefile and CI matrix additions to validate deltas with a staging smoke deploy and terraform plan dry-run. Checklist: - [x] implement delta-index format and generator - [x] wire up CI job and pipeline config - [x] add SBOM generation and envelope signing - [x] add unit tests for indexer and SBOM parsing - [x] add e2e smoke test in staging workflow - [x] document format and CLI usage in docs/release/delta-index.md Backwards compatibility: existing full-installer artifacts and release flow are unchanged; the delta-index is additive and consumed by the private-installer CLI/upgrade controller. Note on security: SBOMs are generated with syft v0.83.0 and emitted alongside artifacts; cosign keys are stored in the CI KMS and rotated per release cadence. See linked Linear tickets for rollout plan and gating criteria.
Alice Nguyen (reviewer): Left a few nits on error messages in delta-indexer.go; please check multi-arch image digest handling.
Ethan Park (author): addressed nits and added explicit tests for amd64/arm64 digest selection in commit b7c8d9.
Marco Ruiz (reviewer): requested CI job to publish unsigned staging artifacts for manual validation before cosign step -- added a conditional publish step.
Priya Shah (security): asked for SBOM tool version pin and signature envelope format verifier. Added syft v0.83.0 pin and envelope verification unit test.
Ben Cohen (approver): Verified staging smoke deploy on us-west-2; approved after 2 successful CI runs.
Zoe Kim (approver): Approved — suggested follow-up to add a delta retention policy for old bundle GC (tracked in ENG-5923).
Introduce delta-index (delta-index.json) for private-installer releases: smaller upgrade bundles, SBOMs per delta, signed provenance, Helm/Terraform lockfiles. Operators can use the index to compute safe upgrade paths and perform rollbacks more quickly.
Unit tests added for delta graph computation and SBOM envelope parsing. CI runs: 2x matrix builds (linux/amd64 linux/arm64), staging smoke deploy succeeded, terraform dry-run validated. Flaky test (e2e network teardown) was re-run and passed on the second attempt.
Risk: consumers may accidentally apply a partial delta for mismatched base versions. Mitigation: delta-index includes base-version constraint checks and the installer will refuse mismatched deltas. CI includes a gating smoke deploy and signature verification to prevent unsigned deltas from reaching stable. Added audit log events for delta apply/rollback.
To consume deltas, upgrade private-installer CLI >= v0.23 which understands delta-index.json. CI publishes both full and delta artifacts; by default the installer will prefer delta bundles when ancestry is available. For emergency rollback, use --force-apply with a specific delta bundle digest from the index.
ENG-5923: implement delta bundle GC and retention policy
ENG-6001: integrate delta-index consumption into private-installer operator
PM-1234: add delta visualization to Console release page
Merged after CI green and approvals. Deployment: no immediate rollout to production; release manager will tag the first delta-enabled release after coordinated customer communications.

Motivation: Customers expect exact parity with OpenAI's /v1/chat.completions for role handling, stop sequences, and logprobs output shape. We also have recurring streaming edgecases where role tokens arrive as separate SSE events leading to downstream SDKs mis-attributing first assistant delta. This PR harmonizes the OpenAI-compat layer to produce: 1) canonical role deltas where the initial assistant role is coalesced into the first token event; 2) explicit mapping for 'stop' as either string or array and consistent enforcement across server- and client-side truncation; 3) support for returning token-level logprobs and top_k entries when logprobs>0 is requested; 4) a structured-output framing option that injects a stable JSON wrapper event and schema hint to help SDKs auto-parse structured responses. Changes are backward-compatible by default: legacy clients keep previous behavior unless the compatibility flag openai_compat.enable_new_role_delta is enabled in config; the structured-output framing is opt-in via parameter structured_output=true. Risk/compatibility notes: the logprobs payload can be large and is gated behind both the request param and a per-tenant quota to avoid accidental cost spikes. Streaming changes required subtle buffering to coalesce role tokens; buffer size is capped and falls back to previous behavior on overflow to avoid head-of-line blocking. What this PR does: -- Introduces openai_compat role coalescing logic and deterministic SSE event order. -- Adds parsing and normalization for stop param (string|array) and validates server truncation semantics. -- Implements token-level logprobs serialization matching OpenAI shape: tokens, token_logprobs, top_logprobs (top-k as objects). -- Adds structured-output framing: emits an initial "structured_schema" SSE event with user-provided schema hint, then emits 'delta' events with content_parts tagged. -- Adds comprehensive unit and integration tests, plus an e2e replay harness against a testrpc model to validate SSE order. Testing: new unit tests in pkg/openai_compat/*, integration tests in tests/integration/openai_compat_streaming_test.go, and end-to-end recorded replay scenarios added to benchmark-lab. CI: initial flaky test in sse_emitter was fixed by adding a small deterministic backoff in the emitter; all checks green on final run. Docs: updated docs/openai_compat.md and examples with structured-output example. Rollout plan: feature gated, enabled for staged tenants during canary week; monitoring added to detect a 5xx or SSE reorder regression. Checklist: [x] role coalescing logic implemented [x] stop param normalization [x] logprobs serialization [x] structured-output framing (opt-in) [x] unit/integration/e2e tests added [x] docs updated [x] feature flag and monitoring added
Ava Chen: Please confirm that the coalescing avoids adding latency for small responses. Samaira Patel: We limit coalescing window to 10ms by default and fall back on overflow; latency regression tested <0.5ms p50 in microbenchmarks.
Diego Martinez: The logprobs schema looks good but clarify top_k ordering. Samaira Patel: top_logprobs is now emitted as objects mapping token->score and we added docs to clarify ordering is not guaranteed; SDKs should sort if necessary.
Priya Singh: Can we gate structured-output behind a feature flag? Samaira Patel: Yes, structured_output=true param plus a tenant-level feature flag; added monitoring for parse failures.
Oliver K. Baker: CI failed once on sse_emitter concurrency flake; resolved by deterministic backoff and a retry on non-fatal EPIPE. Samaira Patel: added tests to reproduce and fixed emitter accordingly.
Ava Chen: Approving after the docs update. (approved)
Diego Martinez: Approving. (approved)
Priya Singh: Approved after a small nits patch to examples. (approved)
