Motivation: We have multiple inconsistent streaming iterator semantics, token-refresh handshakes, and backoff defaults across the Python, TypeScript and Go SDKs. This has caused developer confusion and subtle production bugs (lost partial messages on reconnect, token race during refresh) across customer integrations. This PR unifies the behaviour by introducing a common "StreamCursor"/iterator abstraction and standardizing the auth handshake lifecycle and retry/backoff defaults across the three SDKs.

What this PR does (high level): - Adds a StreamCursor abstraction in each SDK that provides: next()/has_next() style iteration, resume tokens for safe reconnects, and deterministic finalization to drain KV caches. - Implements a two-step auth handshake: (1) token pinning at stream open to avoid mid-stream rotation races, (2) transparent refresh callback with optimistic retry on auth failure. - Replaces per-language ad-hoc backoff constants with a shared policy: jittered exponential backoff starting at 200ms, max 8s, max retries 6 for transient stream errors. - Surfaces ergonomic helpers for common patterns: stream.to_async_iterator() in Python, stream.asyncIterable() in TS, and StreamCursor.Iter() in Go. - Updates examples, tests, and bump package versions in each SDK.

Files changed (high level): see changed_files for exact paths.

Migration notes: - Existing streaming loops that relied on the old per-chunk callback shape should switch to the StreamCursor API. Migration helpers are provided and are backwards-compatible wrappers for the most common patterns. - If you have custom token rotation, review the new refresh callback hook; handlers that mutate tokens should be idempotent and accept a context param in Go / cancellation token in TS / timeout in Python. - The default backoff is more aggressive than some client-customized configs; customers can override via the SDK config object (see examples).

Testing and QA: - Added cross-language unit and integration tests that validate partial message resume across disconnects and token rotation scenarios. - Ran full e2e matrix on linux/arm and linux/x86, and verified memory profiles for long-running streams. - Security scan: no new secrets; auth handshake code reviewed by security.

Checklist: - [x] Python implementation + tests + docs - [x] TypeScript implementation + tests + docs - [x] Go implementation + tests + docs - [x] Migration guides updated - [x] Bumped package versions and changelogs - [x] CI green (see ci_checks)

Related: ENG-3412 (stream reliability), ENG-3571 (sdk ergonomics), SUP-9182 (customer incident tied to token rotation).
Unified stream cursor API across Python/TS/Go, consistent auth handshake and exponential backoff defaults; ergonomics improvements for streaming loops; bumped SDK versions: python 2.8.0, typescript 1.12.0, go 0.9.0. No runtime-breaking changes expected; minor API surface tweaks documented in migration notes.
Daniel Park: This looks great overall. Two asks: 1) can we make the default backoff configurable from the top-level client config? 2) add a short benchmark (latency/throughput) for the new cursor to confirm no perf regression.
Leah Martinez: +1 on making backoff configurable. Added ClientConfig.streamBackoff and documented override in migration guide. Benchmarks added under benchmark-lab/examples/stream-cursor. See commit f6ea4b2.

Motivation: customers and internal teams reported opaque retry behavior in streaming SDKs and duplicated token refreshes under high load. This PR introduces a cross-language (Python/TypeScript/Go) retry-inspector hook for low-cardinality telemetry and a session-snapshot checkpoint primitive that lets generator/pull-stream consumers resume after auth refresh or transient failures. Key changes: 1) retry-inspector API and default emitter (py/ts/go) that emits sampled retry lifecycle events and tags (opt-in sampling, low-cardinality flag documented); 2) session-snapshot checkpoints for async generators/iterables and pull-stream adapters with a simple serialization proto and pluggable persistence (file/memory/kv); 3) legacy token callback compat adapter that maps old providers to the new credential profile shape; 4) deprecation notes and migration helpers for callback-based streaming surfaces, with code examples; 5) minor ergonomic tweaks to stream constructors and backpressure hints; 6) package version bumps (python 2.5.0, typescript 1.28.0, go 1.9.0) and changelog updates; 7) integration tests and docs examples. Backwards compatibility: provided via the compat adapter; default behavior unchanged unless the retry-inspector or snapshot persistence is enabled. Checklist: - Implement retry-inspector hooks and samplers in py/ts/go; - Add session snapshot serialization + persistence adapters; - Provide legacy token provider shim; - Add unit and integration tests (resume, retry telemetry); - Update docs and changelogs; - Add CI harness knobs for memory-backed snapshot store. Planned follow-ups: expand Dedicated deployment examples and add alerting rules for retry flux.
Adds cross-SDK retry inspector for observability; introduces session snapshot checkpoints for resumable streaming; minor API ergonomics and version bumps for py/ts/go; compatibility shim for legacy token providers.

Asha Patel: Reply: Added an explicit 'low-cardinality' flag and defaulted retry-inspector to sample=0.01 in the integration test harness. Documented the opt-in behaviour in docs/sdk/retry-inspector.md.
Maya Chen: The Go snapshot persistence uses local temp files in tests; can we add a memory-backed stub for CI to speed up runs?
Asha Patel: Reply: Added memory-backed store implementation and made it the default in CI; kept file-backed for local dev via env var.

Motivation: parity gaps between TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs surfaced in customer work and internal examples. Specifically: (1) token refresh behavior differs under transient 401s which causes duplicated requests in streaming/long-poll client code; (2) retry semantics for idempotent vs non-idempotent calls were inconsistently documented and implemented; (3) streaming client lacked a programmable backpressure hook useful for browser/edge usage. This PR harmonizes policies and provides ergonomic helpers across the TS SDK surface to match behavior implemented earlier in Python/Go, adds tests, and bumps package.json minor version. Changes include: consolidated TokenManager with pluggable refresh strategy, new RetryPolicy enum (standard/strict/no-retry) with explicit idempotent flag on request helpers, StreamingClient.onBackpressure(callback) and an automatic low-water/high-water buffer that pauses the underlying network-readable stream when backpressure is signalled, clearer error classes (AuthError, RetryLimitError), and small ergonomic helpers: client.withDefaults() and client.streamLines() convenience. Checklist: - [x] design doc reviewed (ENG-4123) - [x] TypeScript implementation and unit tests - [x] e2e against local proxy that simulates 401 refresh races - [x] docs updated in README and changelog - [x] version bump to 0.8.2 - [x] reviewers sign-off The description below summarizes commits, changed files at a high level, CI results, and the review thread.

Motivation: customers with strict data residency and compliance requirements have requested stronger guarantees that KMS keys and audit trails are region-scoped and that RBAC bindings prevent accidental cross-region access. This PR implements three coordinated changes: 1) KMS key policy scoping and an enforcement check to ensure created keys are annotated and ACL'd to a single allowed region for a tenant; 2) Audit pipeline enrichment so every audit record emitted from the control plane includes resolved region, kms_key_id (redacted for public logs), and an explicit residency_tag; 3) RBAC v2 binding templates and a migration helper that tightens previously open bindings for role principals that include 'data-residency' constraints. This is a focused compliance change that reduces blast radius for keys and makes post-hoc incident analysis much easier. What I changed (high level): - Add kms/policy/scoped_key_manager.go: enforces region annotation and rejects cross-region key reuse. - Add audit/enrich/region_enricher.go and schema v2 bump with a backwards-compatible field (residency_tag) and migration guidance. - Add rbac/v2/templates/data_residency_bindings.yaml and generator script rbac/tools/generate_residency_bindings.go to produce tightened bindings from existing role manifests. - Integration tests under infra/tests/kms_region_scope_integration_test.go that run in CI with simulated tenant metadata. - Add migration script tools/migrations/20260222_migrate_residency_bindings.sh and docs/compliance/kms-region-scoping.md. Rollout plan: staged feature flag rollout per-tenant (feature.flag.kms_region_scoping) with safety switch to opt-out for SE-assisted migrations. Also included a small admin console notice for affected tenants. Checklist: - [x] KMS enforcement code and unit tests - [x] Audit enrichment + schema bump + compatibility note - [x] RBAC generator + tests - [x] Migration script and manual rollback steps - [x] CI green on linux/amd64 integration suite - [x] Documentation updates and release notes Notes: this PR intentionally does not auto-block existing keys; instead we emit a warning and provide a migration helper that rotates or re-creates keys in-region. The audit schema bump is additive and backwards compatible; downstream consumers should start consuming residency_tag when available. Related: Linear ENG-2987 (data residency enforcement), SEC-412 (kms scoping threat model), SUP-1023 (customer support case about cross-region key leak).
Ethan Cole: Can you clarify whether the scoped_key_manager rejects keys missing the region tag or only flags them? Right now behavior looks like 'reject' in code but docs say 'warn'.
Priya Raman (author): Good catch — updated with explicit preflight: newly created keys are rejected if no region tag is present; existing keys are only warned and flagged for migration. Added comment and test to assert this behavior.
Rui Zhang: Audit schema bump looks additive which is great. Please ensure consumer teams are pinged; added a TODO to the release checklist to send a migration email to the observability consumers.

Motivation: production SREs and platform engineers frequently need highly targeted per-invocation signals (token-level cost, phase latency, kv-cache warm/ miss markers) without ingesting full traces for every request. This PR introduces two complementary features: 1) Invocation Microtelescope: a lightweight per-invocation micro-telemetry packet that captures a compact token-phase breakdown, kernel warmup hint, and a small set of trace anchors. Microtelescope is designed to be emitted at configurable sampling rates and can be routed independently of full traces. 2) Cost Signal Router: a pipeline-level router that classifies cost-related telemetry (microtelescope, token-cost rollups, and coarse traces) and directs them to different retention/alerting destinations (short-retention hot-index, long-retention cost-store, SLO-alerting queue) based on configurable policies (tenant tier, route, cost-per-invocation thresholds). What changed: - New binary protobuf for microtelescope packet and serializer with a shipper shim (redwood/telemetry/microtelescope.go, redwood/telemetry/microtelescope.proto). - Router and policy implementation (redwood/observability/cost_router.py) with unit tests and fixtures. - SDK change: Python client now emits an optional microtelescope hint header to reduce parsing work on server side (redwood-sdk-python/redwood/transport.py). - Dashboard: Grafana panels for microtelescope-derived token-phase sparklines and per-route cost-router metrics (redwood-observability/dashboards/cost-router.json). - Alerts: tuned SLO alert rule that uses routed signals to reduce noisy alerts for low-value tenants (infra/alerts/slo-cost-routing.yaml). Rollout plan: feature gated by runtime flag (telemetry.microtelescope.enabled) and default-sampled at 0.1% for hosted tier; can be increased for Dedicated customers. Backwards compatibility: router accepts older packets and falls back to legacy routing path. Performance/backpressure: microtelescope serializer is ~400 bytes compressed and the router has flow-control hooks to drop low-priority packets under memory pressure. Testing: local unit tests, integration tests with mini-router, and a staged rollout to beta tenants. Related: ENG-1987 tracks signal retention product work; SUP-4123 triggered a hotfix request during an incident that motivated lower-noise routing. Checklist: - [x] Proto and serializers implemented - [x] Router policies + unit tests - [x] SDK hint header update - [x] Grafana panels and alert tuning - [x] Add e2e integration test harness - [x] Document rollout gates and RBAC controls
Samir Patel (2026-02-11): Can we quantify memory and CPU overhead at 1% sample? Please add microbenchmarks for serializer and router hot path.
Anika Rao (2026-02-12): Added a microbench in tests/bench/test_microtelescope_bench.go and included numbers in the PR description. At 1% sample on a c5.4xlarge-equivalent, CPU overhead < 0.6% and mean serialization latency is 80µs.
Jordan Liu (2026-02-13): Router policy looks good. Request: make default policy explicitly deny routing to long-retention index for dev tenants. Also add a feature flag to disable token-level enrichment for regulated tenants.
Anika Rao (2026-02-14): Added tenant checks and a config toggle telemetry.router.allow_long_retention in policies.py and documented smoke tests.
Introduces Invocation Microtelescope (compact per-invocation telemetry) and a Cost Signal Router to separate high-volume token-level signals from long-retention cost stores. Feature gated and off by default; see rollout docs for increasing sampling for Dedicated customers.

Motivation: Reduce duplicated auth lifecycle logic across the Python/TS/Go SDKs and make streaming consumer ergonomics simpler for common patterns. This change introduces a compact AuthFacade that centralizes fallback and token refresh semantics, a lightweight RetryProfile helper shared by all SDKs, and a small consumer-friendly StreamConsumer surface that wraps common async-iterable/pullstream patterns. Goals: 1) cut cognitive load for application engineers integrating streaming and token rotation; 2) eliminate a recurring class of races observed in long-lived streams under intermittent 401s; 3) align retry semantics so hosted and dedicated deployments observe consistent behavior. What changed: - New compact AuthFacade API added to redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-typescript, and redwood-sdk-go. It exposes a minimal credential lookup + fallback chain and a single refresh hook that SDKs call when 401s occur. The facade is intentionally tiny (3 methods) to encourage composition rather than inheritance. - Shared RetryProfile presets added (fast-fail, balanced, durable) with documented defaults and tuned backoffs for streaming vs unary calls. SDKs accept RetryProfile by name or config object. - StreamConsumer utility: a thin wrapper that normalizes chunked server streaming into an ergonomic async iterator with built-in reauth-on-401 wiring and opt-in checkpointing. - Small refactor to internal session code to let SDKs plug the AuthFacade without changing public client constructors. - Migration helpers and deprecation notices: old TokenProvider.swap_to and SessionManager.startWarmup are deprecated but remain functional with console warnings; migration guide added. Backwards compatibility: No breaking behavior for existing call sites by default. New APIs are additive; a few internal helper signatures were changed but kept private. We added deprecation warnings where required and documented explicit upgrade steps for users who want to opt into the new stream reauth behavior. Testing and rollout: All unit and integration tests updated across tri-sdk matrix. We added an integration test that simulates mid-stream 401 and validates graceful reauth and resume logic. CI initially flagged a flaky streaming test on Linux; the failure was due to a timing assumption corrected by a small sleep + event ordering fix and retry on test harness. Performance: Slight reduction in allocations for streaming hot path in Python and Go (microbenchmarks show ~6-8% CPU improvement for steady-state multi-connection throughput). Also small improvement in TypeScript memory churn under high-concurrency streaming. Docs and version bumps: docs/migration/compact-auth-facade.md and examples/streaming/reauth-example added. SDK versions bumped: python 1.9.0, typescript 2.4.1, go v1.6.0. Rollout plan: feature flagged server-side for canary customers first, then broad release after one week of warm traffic. Rollback path: revert the facade registration inside SDK constructors if unexpected regressions occur. See linked Linear tasks for rollout ownership and telemetry additions.
Jared Lowe: Nice consolidation. Two asks: (1) can we rename RetryProfile 'durable' -> 'throughput_safe' for clarity? (2) add an explicit example showing how to opt out of checkpointing in TS and PY
Priya Nambiar: Renamed durable->throughput_safe and added opt-out snippet in Python/TS examples; pushed a follow-up commit. The goal with short names was to balance discoverability and brevity; we can adjust further if you prefer more verbose labels.
Marta Ivanov: Found a small race when stream resumed immediately after refresh; suggested a mutex around the session swap and an integration test. I added the mutex and integration test in the last commit.
Chen Li: CI green on final run, approved. Left one stylistic nit on facade.ts (prefer explicit return types). I applied the change as part of the squash.

feat(retry): add RetryProfile presets (fast-fail, balanced, durable)
feat(stream): add StreamConsumer wrapper with reauth-on-401 checkpointing
refactor(session): make session adapter pluggable for facade injection
docs: migration guide for compact auth facade and stream examples
test(integration): flaky stream 401 reauth test and harness timing fix
Added a compact AuthFacade and StreamConsumer utilities across Python/TS/Go. New RetryProfile presets (fast-fail, balanced, throughput_safe). Migration guide added. SDK bumps: python 1.9.0, typescript 2.4.1, go v1.6.0. No breaking changes by default; see migration doc for opt-in behavior.

Context and motivation: customer support traces and internal canaries revealed intermittent auth failures for streaming tool-calls when requests cross tenant/org boundaries (hosted -> dedicated routing, or reverse proxied plugin gateways). Failures were caused by brittle header heuristics (we previously prioritized X-Project-Token prefixes only) and a mismatch between the OpenAI-compat streaming handshake and our session-anchored signed-nonce path. This PR unifies header heuristics and introduces a streaming handshake adapter to map legacy OpenAI compat frames to Redwood's tolerant auth checks.

Summary of changes: - Header normalizer: introduce x-rw-tenant and tenant discovery heuristics that try (in order) explicit x-rw-tenant, project-scoped token prefix, org-key fallback, and a safe header-mapping table populated for proxied requests. This is a best-effort discovery that does not change auth decision semantics (we still validate token scope/TTL) but reduces false negatives during routing. - Streaming handshake adapter: a small adapter layer that inspects the initial connect frame (OpenAI style "openai-session", or Redwood "rw-session-nonce") and normalizes fields into a canonical session object used by the runtime. Adapter tolerates both signed-nonce formats (v1 HMAC header and v2 structured signature) to maintain compatibility with older SDKs. - Signature parsing: make request-signature verification tolerant to 2 formats (X-RW-Signature: hmac={sig};v=1 and X-Signature: sig_v2={b64};alg=ed25519) and log a single metric for signature format fallbacks. - CORS: relax preflight mapping for streaming upgrade endpoints; the adapter now echoes project-origin hints in Access-Control-Allow-Headers if the request includes X-Project-Origin to avoid some browser preflight failures when proxying through third-party hubs. - Tool/function calling stability: preserve tool-call context across reconnects by applying a lightweight reconnect token derived from the original signed nonce (TTL 60s). If reconnect presents the reconnect token, adapter rehydrates the call context and hints to the tools-layer to resume safely. - Observability: add tenant_auth_attempts, tenant_auth_fallbacks, and stream_handshake_format metrics; wire them to the console dashboards.

Commits (high-level): - 4c2d9a2: header_normalizer: new package and heuristics implementation - b7f1e3d: stream handshake adapter and format toleration - d5a7b99: signature parsing helpers + metric emission - a2e8f12: unit + integration tests for streaming auth + reconnects - f9c4b01: docs and upgrade notes

Files changed (high-level): - internal/auth/header_normalizer.go: main heuristics + a small mapping table for proxied hosts - runtime/stream/handshake_adapter.go: adapter that canonicalizes session frames - api/openai_compat/stream_bridge.go: glue code for OpenAI compat clients - tests/integration/stream-auth-suite.test.js: end-to-end scenarios for reconnect and cross-tenant routing - docs/api/auth-header-mapping.md: explain the ordering and migration guidance - observability/metrics/tenant_auth_metrics.prom: metric names and labels - cmd/installer/upgrade-notes.md: operator guidance for private deployments

Small illustrative snippet (adapter canonicalization):

  // pseudo Go excerpt from handshake_adapter.go
  // prefer explicit tenant header, then token prefix, then org fallback
  tenant := header.Get("x-rw-tenant")
  if tenant == "" {
    tenant = headerNormalzer.MatchProjectPrefix(token)
  }

Review conversation (selected): - Liam Chen (reviewer): "Please ensure the tenant discovery ordering is documented and that falling back to org keys cannot grant higher privileges than the presented token scope." - Maya (author): "Documented ordering in docs/api/auth-header-mapping.md and enforced scope check in header_normalizer.MatchProjectPrefix; added unit tests to assert no privilege escalation." - Nora Gómez (reviewer): "The reconnect token TTL 60s seems short for some flaky networks; can we make it configurable via runtime flag?" - Maya: "Added runtime config flag stream.reconnect_token_ttl (default 60s) and an env override for Dedicated/Private installs; note in upgrade notes." - Evan Brooks (reviewer): "CI flaked on the integration suite once, but logs looked unrelated; please add a retry hook to the flaky external-hub test to reduce CI noise." - Maya: "Added a single-retry wrapper for the external-hub scenario and re-ran CI." - QA (comment): "Found an NPE on adapter when initial frame omitted an authorization header entirely; handling added and covered by tests."

CI summary: initial run (run #1) reported 1 failing test in tests/integration/stream-auth-suite.test.js (external-hub flake). After adding retry and handling empty auth-frame, rerun (run #2) passed all checks: unit, integration, lint, e2e-nightly. Metrics smoke test included.

Backward compatibility and migration notes: - This change is backward compatible: we accept both legacy and new signature formats and both openai-style and rw-style handshake frames. - Operators upgrading Dedicated/Private should review cmd/installer/upgrade-notes.md to optionally enable extended tenant-mapping lists for proxy gateways. - No breaking changes to public SDKs; we added a reconnect token path that SDKs can opt-into to improve resume behavior.

Why this is different from prior PRs: prior work focused on signed-nonce normalization and CORS mapping in isolation; this PR explicitly centralizes tenant discovery heuristics (to reduce cross-tenant false rejects) and introduces a streaming handshake adapter that acts as a single compatibility surface for both auth headers and streaming frame formats. It reduces duplication and clarifies where compatibility decisions live.

Testing performed: unit tests for header heuristics, property-based token-prefix parsing tests, integration suite exercising hosted->dedicated routing via a test proxy, manual canary on perf-canary with a small traffic slice verifying no latency regression, observability smoke tests verifying metric emission.

Merge details: squash merged by Maya Patel after approvals from Liam and Nora. Merge method: squash. Changelog: included in release notes for the next patch release.

Follow-ups / future work: - ENG-2145: expand tenant mapping ingestion from control plane for multi-tenant proxies - ENG-2212: plumb reconnect-token usage to TS/Go SDKs as an opt-in resume API - Add tracing spans to show which heuristic matched for easier debugging in the console
Normalize tenant discovery headers across streaming handshakes; add tolerant request-signature parsing to support legacy OpenAI-compat clients; improve streaming reconnect heuristics to preserve tool-call contexts.
payload.title: Align tenant header heuristics and stream handshake adapter

Motivation: customers and regulators require cryptographic operations to be bounded to a tenant's configured region and for audit trails to include the resolved key location. Existing KMS scoping enforced at request time but allowed cross-region alias resolution for legacy keys; RBAC v1 lacks concise group inheritance semantics needed to model delegated tenant chains (service-account -> platform-broker -> tenant). This PR implements region-aware key wrapping, a tenant-scoped key alias migration path, and RBAC v2 hierarchical group checks to enable safe tenant chaining.
Design summary:
- KMS region-aware wrapper: a thin platform-level component that resolves key aliases with tenant and region constraints, validates the key's location against the request's effective tenant region, and performs wrap/unwrap via the region-local KMS endpoint. For private deployments a configurable kms_region_map is respected. Errors contain auditable fields but do not leak sensitive key material.
- RBAC v2 hierarchical groups: policy evaluator extended to support group inheritance and explicit delegation chains. Policies may include a 'delegate_chain' clause that asserts which identity principals are allowed to perform operations on behalf of a tenant. This supports service accounts that act through platform brokers.
- Audit translation: audit exporter now enriches events with kms_key_region, key_alias_resolved, and tenant_chain if delegation occurred. These fields are surfaced in both internal logs and the tenant-facing audit bundles (redacted where necessary).
- Migration/tooling: migration tool (scripts/migrate-kms-aliases) to rewrite legacy global aliases into tenant-scoped aliases (format: tenant/<tenant-id>/key/<alias>) with safe fallback meta. The migration is idempotent and emits a report used by Governance teams.
- Feature flag & rollout: all runtime checks guarded by rbac_v2_tenant_chain and kms_region_enforce feature flags. We roll out in three phases: dry-run audit (collect only), soft-enforce for low-traffic tenants, and full enforce after 2 weeks with metrics stable.
Implementation notes:
- Changes touched: auth/policy/evaluator.go, kms/wrapper/region_wrapped_client.go, audit/exporter/translate.go, deploy/helm/values.yaml (private KMS maps), scripts/migrate-kms-aliases.py, docs/security/kms-region-and-delegation.md, tests/integration/kms_region_enforce_test.go.
- Performance: added a single network call for alias resolution when no cached mapping exists; integrated a short-lived platform cache with TTL=30s to remove observable p99 latency regressions. Benchmarks run in perf-canary show <1% token-latency impact for typical generation flows.
- Backwards compatibility: legacy aliases continue to work via the migration shim (reads prefer tenant-scoped alias if present), and the feature flag allows staged enforcement.
Testing and CI:
- Unit tests: policy evaluator inheritance tests (x8), kms wrapper happy/error paths (x12), audit enrichment cases (x6).
- Integration: e2e in staging exercise tenant-chained request path with private deployment (KMS emulator).
- Canary: canary rollout engaged for 5% of incoming requests with monitoring dashboards for fail rates and latency regressions.
Rollout & Monitoring:
- Dashboards: new panels for kms_key_region rejects, delegate_chain denials, migration report failures.
- Alerts: PagerDuty on >0.1% KMS-region-enforce rejects or sudden spike in delegate_chain errors.
- Rollback: flip off rbac_v2_tenant_chain and kms_region_enforce flags to revert runtime behavior; migration tool produces a reversal mapping to revert alias rewrites if needed.
Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: mis-migration could orphan keys — mitigated by idempotent migration with dry-run and multi-signer confirmation for write-phase.
- Risk: latency regression — mitigated with platform-side caching and canary limits.
Docs and compliance:
- Added docs/security/kms-region-and-delegation.md with example alias formats, operator migration steps, and FAQ for compliance teams.
- Updated privacy/audit-guidelines.md to describe new audit fields and retention considerations.
Morgan Li: Please add a diagram for the delegate_chain flow and clarify the fallbacks when alias resolution fails.
Avery Chen: Added diagram to docs and clarified fallback semantics: if tenant-scoped alias unresolved we fall back to legacy alias only in dry-run; full-enforce mode rejects.
Diego Alvarez: Why introduce an in-memory TTL cache instead of leaning on existing runtime cache? Concern about duplication and consistency.
Avery Chen: TTL cache is a small platform-local cache to avoid cross-process coordination; we use existing distributed cache for long-lived mappings. Added comments and a helper to centralize cache instrumentation.
Priya Sharma: Tests look good, but add an integration test for private installer KMS map override.
Avery Chen: Added private-installer test and updated README with operator steps.
Introduce region-aware KMS wrapping and RBAC v2 hierarchical group support for tenant chaining. Adds audit translation to surface KMS location and tenant aliasing. Backwards-compatible rollout behind feature flag rbac_v2_tenant_chain.
Migration steps: 1) run scripts/migrate-kms-aliases.py --dry-run and review report; 2) schedule migration window and run without --dry-run; 3) enable rbac_v2_tenant_chain in dry-run audit mode for 48 hours; 4) enable soft-enforce for low-traffic tenants; 5) full-enforce after metrics stable. Governance must sign-off on final enforce step.
Flip feature flags rbac_v2_tenant_chain and kms_region_enforce to false. Use migration tool report to map tenant aliases back to original global aliases if full revert necessary. Re-deploy previous helm values for private KMS map.
Unit and integration coverage added. Canary at 5% for 72h, then ramped to 20% before full rollout. No production rejects observed during canary; 2 migration warnings fixed pre-rollout.
Security: enforce tenant-region KMS wrapping and add RBAC v2 delegation chains (feature-flagged).

Context: customers observed fast repeated short bursts from tenants that depleted reservation budgets too quickly and produced noisy utilization spikes which confused autoscalers and billing. This PR introduces a slotted burst quota scheme and an SLA smoothing window to make dedicated fleet burst behavior predictable and billable without sacrificing tail latency. Goals: 1) bound instantaneous burst allocation with fixed-size time slots per tenant, 2) amortize burst consumption across a configurable smoothing window to avoid autoscaler thrash, 3) emit new telemetry for billing and SLO tracking, 4) remain backward-compatible with existing reservation/percentile contracts. Approach: add a slot allocator that carves each tenant's burst budget into M fixed slots per minute and enforces one-slot consumption per indexed request until slot refill; implement SLA smoothing that computes a weighted moving average of per-tenant throughput and uses that smoothed value in the scale-decision path and the reservation safety checks; add amortized billing tags so burst usage can be reported in both instantaneous and smoothed billing views; expose two new runtime flags: --burst-slots-per-minute and --smoothing-window-seconds. Implementation notes: controller changes in pkg/allocator manage slot reservation and soft-preemption; autoscaler consults smoothing metrics instead of raw instantaneous RPS for headroom decisions; metrics exported: tenant_burst_slot_usage, tenant_burst_amortized_rps, sla_smoothing_ratio; added integration tests and a small migration path that defaults slots to 0 (no-op) unless explicitly enabled by fleet config. Rollout plan: feature-gated behind fleet config flag; staged rollout to Canary then to Dedicated fleets with monitoring dashboards and an alert on smoothing anomaly. Related: touches SUP-7643 (support report), ENG-1842 (autoscaler stability work), ENG-1910 (billing telemetry). Checklist: [x] core slot allocator and API, [x] autoscaler integration, [x] metrics & tags, [x] docs/design note, [x] integration tests, [x] e2e smoke in perf canary. 
Ben Collins: Left a few comments on concurrency and the refill goroutine; suggested using a leaky-bucket variant for refill to smooth jitter. Requested unit tests for the time-edge case when smoothing window < slot period.
Aisha Patel: Addressed Ben's comments by making refill idempotent and adding an integration test that simulates fast slot cycles; added comments explaining tradeoffs vs leaky-bucket. Pushed fix in commit 'Fix: race in slot refill worker'.
Lena Huang: Asked for a clear fallback when the flag is disabled and to ensure metrics don't produce high-cardinality labels. Confirmed that tenant id is a coarse-grain label and per-slot emission is aggregated. Approved after CI green.

Motivation: current shadow/canary primitives at Redwood route mirrored traffic with simple fixed sampling rates and immediate aggregation windows. This causes two operational problems in real product traffic: (1) bursty feature flags or short-lived user sessions produce noisy signals that trigger premature rollbacks, and (2) high-cardinality signals (e.g., per-customer QA tests) overwhelm the telemetry pipeline when mirrored at 100% for short windows.

This PR introduces a stage-aware shadow rollout mode with two cooperating mechanisms: a configurable grace window and loss-aware sampling. The grace window delays hard rollback decisions until a minimum sustained observation period has elapsed for the canary stage; during the window, transient anomalies are throttled by a hysteresis policy. Loss-aware sampling lets the orchestrator automatically lower mirror sampling on high-traffic routes or when a sampling budget is reached, while preserving representative coverage across customer segments via stratified reservoir sampling.

Changes include: deployment API additions for staged rollouts, runtime routing changes to support delayed decision timers, telemetry tags to mark grace-window samples, a lightweight reservoir sampler implemented in the routing layer, and aggregation logic in the rollout controller to compute sustained regressions (statistically significant degradations) rather than per-minute spikes. The description below includes a checklist, high-level commits, files changed, and review summary.

Checklist:
- [x] Add stage field to rollout spec (staged, shadow, canary, promoted)
- [x] Implement grace-window timer and hysteresis policy in rollout controller
- [x] Implement reservoir-based lossy mirror sampler in router (configurable by route and customer segment)
- [x] Tag mirror traces/metrics originating from grace window for downstream filtering
- [x] Add aggregation queries and alerting rule updates for sustained-regression detection
- [x] Unit + integration tests for sampler + controller interactions
- [x] Documentation updates (API + operations guide)

Context and risk: this is framework-level work for rollout safety. The sampler is intentionally conservative (defaults to 5% mirror) and off by default for managed-hosted tiers; Dedicated/Private customers can enable with explicit config. The aim is to reduce false-positive rollbacks while keeping observability signals useful.

Kenji: Can you justify the default 5% mirror? Aisha: 5% is conservative and chosen to keep telemetry cost low; customers can opt up. Marta: How do we avoid biasing segment coverage when dynamic sampling reduces rate? Aisha: sampler is stratified by customer_segment and request_path and uses reservoir sampling to keep representation. Samir: Is the grace window tunable per rollout? Aisha: Yes, rollout.spec.grace_window_sec is per-rollout with org-level defaults. Kenji: CI flake on integration tests after the first push; looks like a race in sampler warmup. Aisha: Fixed by adding a deterministic seed and warmup hook in the second commit. Marta: Please add an ops playbook; approving after docs update. Final: approved by Kenji and Marta, Samir requested small telemetry naming fix which was addressed.
Add stage-aware shadow rollouts: grace window prevents premature rollback on transient anomalies
Introduce reservoir-based lossy mirror sampling to control telemetry costs for mirrored traffic
Operator notes: defaults conservative; Dedicated/Private users can tune sampling and grace windows via rollout spec
payload.title: stage-aware-shadow-rollouts-with-grace-window-and-lossy-sampling

Summary: Introduces Runway Guardian, a lightweight tenant-level agent (CLI + small runtime hooks) that synthesizes conservative prefill defaults, emits compact quantization profiles for downstream inference, and forwards cost/latency telemetry to Redwood Optimize. Motivation: customers frequently ask for conservative, turn-key defaults to avoid surprise overages during ramp or traffic spikes. Existing autotuners are powerful but require telemetry plumbing and orchestration; this change delivers a compact, opinionated CLI and telemetry adapter to plug into private or dedicated environments so teams can run safe prefill policies without heavy ops work.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a new CLI (runway-guardian) that can: generate tenant prefill templates (batch/caching targets and KV cache sizes), simulate runway (estimated unit-econ over 30/90/180 day horizons), and emit compact quant profiles (fp16/int8 suggestions with safety thresholds). 2) Adds a telemetry adapter service that ingests existing serving metrics and forwards normalized cost/latency signals to the Optimize pipeline for automated recommendations and alerting. 3) Ships a small policy-as-code library (YAML templates + validation) so security and platform teams can codify guardrails. 4) Adds end-to-end tests, docs, and Helm chart pieces for private installs.

Design notes and constraints: - Conservative defaults: generated profiles bias toward lower ms/token and higher fail-safe batch limits to prioritize user experience during ramp. - Compact quant profiles: output is intentionally small (JSON with <= 8 keys) so it can be embedded in tenant metadata and pushed with model manifests. - Simulation model: a simple stochastic runway estimator that consumes sample qps+dist and returns expected cost curves; not intended to replace full econ tooling but to give a conservative operational runway estimate.

Files changed (high-level): see files_changed field below for a concise list.

Checklist: - [x] CLI implemented and unit-tested - [x] Telemetry adapter implemented and integration-tested against Optimize staging - [x] Policy templates and validator - [x] Docs and examples - [x] Helm bits for private deploy - [x] Security review (KMS usage for small secrets)

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: overly aggressive quant suggestions could degrade quality. Mitigation: profiles include a quality-safety floor and require an explicit opt-in flag to apply to live model manifests. - Risk: telemetry flooding. Mitigation: adapter performs sampling and pre-aggregation and uses the existing Redact/PII path for sensitive fields.

Related work: builds on ENG-4301 (prefill policy schemas) and reuses portions of the econ-simulator in /tools/sim. Linear references: ENG-4352 (Runway Guardian roadmap), PM-1218 (product acceptance criteria).
Diego Morales: Nice end-to-end shape. Please add a short rationale comment in the sim about why we bias toward lower batch sizes for ramping tenants.
Priya Nair: Telemetry adapter looks good but add a flag to toggle sampling rate per-tenant; we don't want one-size-for-all sampling. Also add an opentracing span around normalization.
Alex Kim: Can we make the compact profile tie to model semantic version so downstream can detect incompatible profiles? Otherwise lgtm.
SRE oncall (comment): Helm fragment needs resource requests to avoid OOMs during install; suggest 200m/256Mi baseline.
Security review (Kiran): KMS usage looks fine; ensure the docker image doesn't leak build secrets. Add a pipeline step to scan image for credentials.
QA: e2e_runway smoke failed intermittently due to flakiness in the e2e harness - added retry in the script and extended wait for deployment readiness.
Eloise Chen: Added the sim rationale comment and a conservative default batch bias. Added --sampling-rate and per-tenant override flag; opentracing spans inserted. Compact profile now includes model_semver. Helm resources added. Thanks for the reviews!
Squash-merged after approvals from Diego, Priya, and Alex; CI green. 1 review iteration for telemetry sampling and helm resources.
Adds Runway Guardian CLI and telemetry adapter for tenant prefill policies; introduces compact quant profile generator and new default prefill templates. Backwards-compatible.
Introduce Runway Guardian (CLI + telemetry adapter + compact quant generator). Admins should review default templates in docs/runway-guardian.md before enabling in production. CLI is opt-in and safe by default; compact quant profiles require explicit apply to model manifests.

payload.body:
Motivation: We observed intermittent auth failures for multiplexed streaming clients (browser SDK using SSE/WS multiplexing and server-side HTTP/2 multiplexers) during reconnects and when edge proxies split preflight and streaming connections. Root causes: (1) ephemeral per-connection signed headers (X-Redwood-Signed, X-Redwood-Nonce) were not reliably propagated across reconnection flows and multiplexed substreams, and (2) CORS preflight behavior on some enterprise proxies stripped or rewrote nonce-prefetch headers used by the OpenAI-compat layer. This PR stabilizes the auth surface by: - Introducing persist-signed-session middleware that binds a short-lived signature token to a reconnectable session-id (X-Redwood-Session) and ensures the runtime accepts either the original per-request signed header or the session-bound token during a reconnect window. - Splitting the preflight nonce semantics into two headers: X-Redwood-Prefetch-Nonce (for preflight/signed-session bootstrap) and X-Redwood-Stream-Nonce (for in-band stream frames). This makes proxies less likely to remove the bootstrap header while preserving in-stream integrity checks. - Adding compatibility shim for OpenAI-compat streaming where existing clients send Authorization: Bearer project:... or org:... tokens; the shim will translate project-scoped bearer tokens into session-bound signatures when the request indicates a long-lived streaming intent (stream=true or transports: ["sse","ws"]). - Ensuring function/tool-calling metadata (toolcall-signer headers and prefetched function manifests) are replay-safe across reconnects by including a checksum header X-Redwood-Toolcall-Checksum and validating it on reconnect. Key implementation details: - runtime/server: new middleware in runtime/auth/session_store.go that issues and validates session tokens and enforces a configurable reconnect_window_ms (default 15000ms). - streaming layer: changes in streaming/stream_muxer.go to attach session-id to substreams and to accept either per-request signature or session token on reconnect. - http proxy adapter: change in adapters/proxy_cors.go to preserve X-Redwood-Prefetch-Nonce across preflight responses and to echo a small probe header (X-Redwood-Proxy-Probe) used by client-side checks. - openai-compat: compat/openai_stream_bridge.go updated to detect project-scoped bearer tokens and issue a temporary session token pair. - tests: new e2e for reconnect behavior (tests/e2e/stream_reconnect_auth_test.go), and unit tests for nonce-splitting logic. Checklist: - [x] Add session-store and token lifecycle (runtime + tests) - [x] Update streaming muxer and client probes - [x] Implement header split and proxy adapter changes - [x] Add openai-compat shim and docs note - [x] Add e2e reconnect tests that run in CI - [x] Document migration notes in docs/streaming-auth.md Migration notes and operator action: - Default behavior is backward compatible: existing per-request signatures continue to work. The new session-id flow is additive and opt-in via client flags or when the client sends a streaming intent field. - Operators who deploy custom proxies should ensure adapters/proxy_cors.go changes are applied or that their proxies are configured to forward X-Redwood-Prefetch-Nonce and not strip small unrecognized headers. Rollback plan: revert the feature flag for session-bound tokens (feature.session_auth=false) which disables the session-store acceptance and restores strict per-request signature validation. Related: ENG-4218 touches reconnect heuristics and ENG-4321 documents enterprise proxy behavior. Links: RFC: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4218/multiplexed-stream-auth-rfc Docs: https://redwood.example/docs/streaming-auth.html
Liam Chen: Nice approach. Two concerns: 1) the reconnect window default seems long for high-rotation tokens (15s). Can we make this configurable via env and add an integration test that asserts both short and long windows?
Aisha Kapoor: Good call — made the reconnect_window_ms configurable with env REDWOOD_SESSION_RECONNECT_MS and added test vectors for 2500ms and 15000ms in tests/e2e.
Sofia Ortega: The proxy probe header is clever. Would we be able to make the probe optional? Some proxies log unknown headers. Suggest exposing it behind feature.probe_header flag.
Aisha Kapoor: Probe header is now behind feature.probe_header, default on for browsers but off for server-to-server flows. Updated docs.
Devon Park: Approving after CI pass and one minor nit about variable naming in session_store.go (sessionToken -> session_token to match style).
Aisha Kapoor: Renamed the variable and pushed fixup commit. Thanks!
Stabilized streaming auth for multiplexed connections: session-bound signatures and split preflight/stream nonces. Backward compatible; operators may need to ensure proxies forward X-Redwood-Prefetch-Nonce. See docs/streaming-auth.md for migration steps.
This PR was merged after a short staged rollout to Dedicated clusters and monitoring for parity metrics (auth_failure_rate, stream_reconnect_latency). Observed a 78% reduction in auth failures during reconnects in canary.

payload.body:
Motivation: We observe duplicated tool/function calls and flapping state when clients disconnect abruptly and immediately reconnect with a new connection that races with in-flight server-side commits. This is particularly visible for OpenAI-compatible clients that expect the same abort semantics but do not always close cleanly. This PR adds a graceful 'soft drain' window on server-side connection close plus a periodic client-cancel sweep that reconciles lingering in-flight operations so downstream tool invocations are not executed twice. Scope: 1) soft drain: on receipt of a client disconnect or abort event we transition the server stream into DRAINING for a configurable window (default 250ms) during which we continue to stream buffered tokens but suppress duplicate tool invocation deliveries and allow short-lived reconnects to reattach. 2) client-cancel sweep: a background reconciler periodically queries active session leases and issues idempotent cancel confirmations for sessions with ambiguous finalization to prevent orphaned toolcalls. 3) structured-output fences: we tighten fences for partial-structured outputs so the adapter will only emit toolcall events when a complete fence sequence is closed, reducing partial-toolcall noise. 4) OpenAI-compat handshake: add a compatibility handshake flag that keeps legacy abort semantics unless the client opts into 'soft_drain_v1' to preserve behavior for older clients. Checklist: - [x] Design docs and protocol notes (lease_handshake.md) - [x] Implementation of drain and sweep logic - [x] Unit tests for idempotency and fence handling - [x] Integration test for reconnects and short lived disconnects - [x] Metrics and observability (streaming_metrics.prom) - [x] Example in SDK python for users to opt into new behavior Commits summary: initial spike: add soft drain state machine and handshake flag; add drain policy and reconciliation loop; add structured-output fence guard; tests and flaky-test fixes; docs and changelog. The changes are intentionally conservative and behind config flags with defaults set to maintain existing production behavior. Related work: addresses regression described in ENG-3124 and follows up on discussion in ENG-3180. Implementation notes: soft drain is implemented as a state transition with an adjustable deadline; during DRAINING we mark any newly-observed toolcall candidates as "suppressed-pending" and buffer an idempotency token. If the client reconnects and reattaches with the same session token within the window we clear suppression and deliver only the first delivery. The client-cancel sweep reconciler uses a bounded parallel worker pool and respects existing rate limits. A new metric streaming.soft_drain_suppressed_total was added to help evaluate impact. Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves prior semantics; opt-in via openai.compat.soft_stream_drain_v1=true flips to the new behavior. Testing notes: added soft_cancel_test.go with deterministic fake clocks to validate timing edge cases. Integration pipeline initially failed due to flaky stream_integration_test (seed-dependent); fixed by stabilizing test seeding and reducing timeouts. CI: all checks passed on final run. Merge strategy: squash and merge. Merge notes: no migration required, behavior behind flags, no changes to API contracts beyond documented flags.
Introduce a soft stream drain and periodic client-cancel sweep to reduce duplicate tool/function calls during abrupt disconnects. Backwards compatible with existing OpenAI-compatible abort semantics. Config flags introduced: openai.compat.soft_stream_drain_ms, openai.compat.client_cancel_sweep_ms.
Evan Lewis: Please add a unit test that simulates second connection racing in with delayed backend commit. The new state machine looks good but we need explicit coverage.
Maya Chen (author): Added determinisitc race test and a fake commit hook to validate suppression semantics. See soft_cancel_test.go commit.
Priya Nair: We should ensure metrics have tags for tenant and model to help analysis in multi-tenant clusters. Also note potential perf impact of sweep; please add a token bucket limiter.
Maya Chen (author): Added tenant/model labels to streaming.soft_drain_suppressed_total and a configurable sweep_rate_limit in drain_policy.go. Benchmarks show <2% CPU for default settings.
Lukas Müller: Docs look good. One nit: callout in changelog should advise users how to opt-out, otherwise they may be surprised. Approving after the changelog entry is clarified.
Maya Chen (author): Clarified changelog and added an example snippet in docs/openai_compat/streaming-behavior.md. CI green, ready to merge.

payload.body:
Motivation: the OpenAI Responses API v3 introduces a seed/determinism flag and richer per-response metadata fields. Customers expecting parity through our OpenAI compatibility layer were hitting two classes of issues: 1) requests with deterministic seeds sometimes routed to fallback model variants causing non-deterministic behavior, and 2) streaming reassembly and function/tool-calling events lost user-supplied metadata (e.g., trace ids) on intermediate fragments. This PR: - Propagates the new 'seed' and 'determinism' fields from OpenAI-style Requests through our compatibility translation layer so upstream callers can control RNG determinism when we map to compatible model variants. - Adds per-request metadata passthrough: preserves and forwards top-level metadata and nested response-level metadata (user supplied) through streaming frames and the final assembled Response object. - Stabilizes streaming reassembly for mixed partials (text chunks, tool call fragments, structured JSON outputs) by introducing a sequence/frame id and last-frame markers in the compat layer; this avoids interleaving when a single call fan-outs to auxiliary model variants. - Ensures function/tool-calling events are emitted with the original 'metadata' and 'seed' fields intact so SDKs relying on tool traceability continue to work. - Adds exhaustive integration tests against the Responses v3 contract and extends streaming unit tests to emulate packet reorder and intermittent delivery. Implementation notes: - New compatibility translator: redwood/openai_compat/responses_v3_translator.py maps OpenAI fields to internal inference request flags (seed->rng_seed, determinism->sampling_profile). Translator is intentionally minimal: we preserve unknown fields in a passthrough map under compat_metadata for future extensions. - Streaming layer changes: redwood/api/streaming.py: implement frame_sequence_id and final_fragment bool. Reassembly uses (request_id, frame_sequence_id) ordering plus a small re-sequencing buffer gated by latency_slo to avoid head-of-line blocking. - Routing: routing/policy.py updated to prefer exact-architecture variants when determinism is requested; fallback still allowed if pinned variant unavailable. - Tests: tests/integration/test_responses_v3_compat.py includes deterministic-seed repeatability checks, metadata round-trip assertions, and simulated packet reordering scenarios. - Docs: docs/openai_compat.md updated with Responses v3 mapping and guidance for determinism semantics. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged if seed/determinism not provided. We intentionally do not make determinism true by default because it impacts throughput. Checklist: - [x] Translator for seed/determinism fields - [x] Metadata passthrough in streaming frames - [x] Stable reassembly and ordering buffer - [x] Routing preference when determinism requested - [x] Integration + unit tests - [x] Docs update - [x] CI passing on rerun Rollout/rollback notes: feature gated behind a compatibility flag (OPENAI_COMPAT_V3=true) and an experiment toggle for routing. If customer issues are observed around tail latency with deterministic requests, the routing policy can be relaxed to fallback earlier while preserving seed values in logs for replay/diagnosis.
Amit Patel: The translator looks good overall. One open question: if the requested seed exceeds 64 bits, how should we normalize? Suggest we hash down with siphash and record the original in compat_metadata. Can you add a test for large seeds?
Marisol Vega: Responding to Amit: added normalization using siphash64 in translator and test case in tests/integration/test_responses_v3_compat.py line ~120. Original seed preserved in compat_metadata.seed_raw for auditability.
Claire Nguyen: Reassembly buffer hardens well but we should be conservative with the latency_slo default. Recommend 20ms default or tie it to per-customer SLO config. Also noted minor lint issues in streaming.py.
Marisol Vega: Reduced default re-sequence buffer to 20ms and moved config to per-customer tunables. Fixed lint comments and added comments describing tradeoffs.
Benji Rosen: Verified end-to-end locally including tool call round-trips; approved after Marisol pushed the siphash change and the docs clarification.
CI Bot: Build #2245: lint failed on first run; second run passed (all checks green).

payload.body:
Background: Customers running latency-sensitive LLM endpoints often over-provision small batch sizes to meet 99th percentile SLOs which increases per-token cost. Separately, cold KV cache misses for multi-turn chat impose a tail-latency penalty that pushes teams to keep higher headroom or run less aggressive quantization. This PR introduces an end-to-end feature: (1) adaptive microbatch presets exposed as route defaults, (2) a lightweight KV-warmup heuristic that uses request-side prefix probing to prefill caches for hot sessions, and (3) a non-invasive Unit-Econ Prober service that injects low-rate synthetic probes to estimate per-route cost/latency curves used to pick microbatch and warmup presets.

Summary of changes: Adds a new runtime hook + controller and a Console UI flag to enable adaptive-presets per-route. Implements the Unit-Econ Prober as a standalone internal controller that schedules probes based on traffic heatmaps and returns JSON summaries consumed by the heuristics engine. Updates serving runtime to accept microbatch-presets and a cache-prefill window parameter. Adds telemetry (per-probe token cost, p50/p95 latency, KV-prefill hit-rate). Includes a migration tool to backfill presets from historical per-route traces.

Motivation: Prior work (frugal batching and autotuners) optimizes at global or per-model granularity; teams asked for safer route-level defaults that are cheap to compute and can be toggled without full traffic experiments. The prober lets us measure realistic unit economics in-cluster without affecting customer payloads, while the KV-warmup materially reduces tail latency on multi-turn sessions where conversational state is reused.

Design highlights:
- Microbatch presets: a small enum (none, conservative, balanced, aggressive) plus per-route numeric override. The presets translate to target batch size, max latency window, and max async in-flight requests. The runtime schedules a microbatch delta scheduler that tries to reach the preset without violating latency SLOs.
- KV-warmup heuristic: samples incoming request prefixes for active sessions and issues low-priority prefill requests using the same model variant. Prefill concurrency is capped per-route and backpressure-aware (won't prefill if CPU/GPU utilization > threshold).
- Unit-Econ Prober: generates 1–5 probe requests per minute per hot route (configurable) with synthetic but realistic prefixes (derived from anonymized recent traffic). Prober returns a compact profile: p50/p95 tokens/sec, cost-per-token, inferred break-even batch size. These profiles are stored as route annotations consumed by the presets controller.

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/scheduler/microbatch.go (scheduler + presets implementation)
- runtime/caching/kv_warmup.go (prefill client + heuristics)
- controllers/unit_econ/prober_controller.go (prober logic + metrics collector)
- api/routes/types.go (route presets schema + validation)
- console/src/routes/RouteSettings.tsx (toggle and summary UI)
- telemetry/metrics/unit_econ.prom (new meters)
- migrations/20260215_backfill_presets.go (backfill job)
- tests/e2e/prober_integration_test.go
- docs/operational/route-presets.md

Small code excerpt (microbatch policy application):
```
// targetWindowMillis derived from preset
scheduler.SetTargetWindow(routeID, targetWindowMillis)
// runtime will attempt to form batches within target window up to maxBatchSize
```

Testing and benchmarks: Unit and integration tests added. Benchmarked on the perf-lab using a 4-model mix (chat, completion, rerank, embedding) across 8 GPU backends. Key numbers from canary cluster: conservative preset reduced cost by 6.2% vs default while holding p95 latency within 1.1x; aggressive preset reduced cost by 17.8% but increased p95 by 1.45x on tail-heavy workloads. KV-warmup decreased session tail p95 by 18% for multi-turn chat flows with average session length >6 turns.

CI: initial run failed lint due to a naming inconsistency in proto; lint-only commit was pushed and CI passed on rerun. End-to-end test showed a flaky case in prefill backpressure—added a retry/backoff and fixed.

Migration and rollout plan: feature default off. Deploy prober controller and metrics in canary region, enable presets UI for internal teams only, run the backfill migration to seed sensible defaults. After 2 weeks of monitoring (unit-econ signals + console charts) we will flip the defaults to "balanced" for routes tagged with 'autotune-eligible'. Rollout is reversible: presets are per-route overrides and can be disabled immediately.

Rollback: remove route annotations and revert controller feature flag. Migration is idempotent and a reverse job exists to clear seeded presets.

Security and privacy: Probes use anonymized prefixes derived from sampled tokens and conform to the data retention policy; probes do not include user-identifiable metadata. Prober runs with restricted IAM roles and KMS usage consistent with Private deployment rules.

Open items and follow-ups:
- Add automatic quantization recommendation integration (next PR) to suggest int8 profiles when latencies allow.
- Expand probe synthesis logic to better model long-tail conversation styles.
- Expose detailed cost/latency curve plotting in Console (UX ticket PM-329).

Related work: refs ENG-8473 (microbatch scheduling improvements), PM-312 (route-level defaults), and prior perf canaries PRs for KV cache improvements.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration tests
- [x] Perf numbers from lab
- [x] Console UI with toggle
- [x] Migration/backfill job

Merge notes: squash + reword. See migration job schedule in release notes.
Miguel: Can we ensure prober rate cannot amplify and become a DoS? Author: prober uses leaky-bucket and route caps, added in code.
Lena: Why not use historical traces instead of synthetic probes? Author: historical traces are used for synthesis seeds but probes are needed to measure live unit-econ under current infra.
Rajesh: Will prefill increase GPU usage? Author: capped by route and global thresholds; scheduler respects util metrics and will disable prefill under high utilization.
- Add adaptive microbatch presets (route-level)
- Add KV-warmup prefill heuristic to reduce tail latency on multi-turn sessions
- Add Unit-Econ Prober to estimate per-route cost/latency tradeoffs and seed presets
- Backfill migration to seed presets from historical traces
payload.title: Adaptive microbatch presets and KV-warmup heuristics with unit-econ prober

payload.body:
Adds PMU-backed cycle counters and a continuous-batching simulator/harness for reproducing live request distributions. Exposes per-core ring buffer export for timeline analysis and integrates NVTX markers for scheduler windows.
Context and motivation: We frequently need a low-overhead, system-level signal for per-token cycles to attribute runtime overhead between kernel execution, scheduling, and blocking I/O. Existing high-res counters (nvtx and software timers) are useful but insufficient to correlate CPU-side stalls and kernel timings at the per-core level under high-concurrency continuous batching.

Summary of changes: Adds a PMU-backed sampler (runtime/telemetry/pmu_sampler.*) that uses perf_event_open to record core cycle and instructions-retired counters with a lightweight sampling loop and per-core ring buffers. The sampler is opt-in (enabled via PERF_BUILD and runtime flag) and drains into an in-memory ring buffer exposed to user-space exporter hooks. We added a small, single-file continuous-batch simulator (tools/batch_sim/continuous_sim.cpp) that can replay recorded request arrival traces and exercise scheduler policies and batching heuristics deterministically. An exporter (perf/exporters/timeline_csv_exporter.py) converts ring buffer samples + NVTX annotations into a timeline CSV compatible with existing perf dashboards and a simple post-processing script to drive Speedscope/Perfetto. NVTX annotations were added around scheduler windows to make the scheduler batching lifecycle visible in traces.

Design notes: The PMU sampler aims for minimal overhead by: 1) sampling at a coarse frequency tuned per workload, 2) using mmap'd ring buffers to avoid syscalls on record-forward path, and 3) compressing sample payloads to 16 bytes (timestamp, core, sample-type bits, value). The ring buffer API is intentionally small (push/poll/drain) so it can be reused by other telemetry producers in the runtime. The continuous-batch simulator supports trace replay with adjustable QPS, jitter models, and per-request sequence length distributions to approximate production traffic during perf runs.

Performance impact: On a representative generator (concurrent clients=64, mean seq=256, model=redwood-7b-quant), enabling the sampler at a 1ms sample interval added ~0.6% median per-token CPU overhead and produced stable cycle attribution samples. Using the simulator we reproduced a 7-12% median per-token latency regression in a scheduler path when a misconfigured batching window caused frequent micro-batching; the NVTX + PMU trace made the root cause (frequent wakeups + context-switch stalls) obvious.

Tests and CI: Added an integration test (tests/perf/pmu_sampler_integration_test.cpp) that runs the sampler in a controlled environment and validates ring-buffer exports and exporter parsing. CI: perf-pipeline job added to infra/ci/perf-pipeline.yml that runs the simulator with a small trace and validates timeline export. The initial CI run failed due to missing CAP_SYS_ADMIN in container; we updated the perf CI image and reran — final CI status: pass.

Files/areas touched: runtime telemetry and scheduler, a new tooling harness under tools/batch_sim, a small Python exporter, docs and example traces, and CI perf job. Changes are mostly additive; scheduler NVTX annotations are guarded by a preprocessor define so runtime behavior is unchanged when PERF_BUILD is off.

Review conversation (high-level):

- Maya (author): "Sampler uses per-core buffers and mmap'd ring semantics; hot path avoids locks. Added a bounded drain and a configuration option (max-buffer-events) with a reasonable default."
- Samuel Park: "Simulator is great — minor nit: make the default trace rate conservative in CI to avoid flaky runs."

Motivation: customers relying on OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility have increasingly complex tool/function outputs and varied role labels from legacy clients. The streaming path was producing verbose, repeated JSON fragments for tool responses and leaking low-confidence token-level logprobs during long streams. This PR introduces an 'output coordinator' layer in the v1 chat adapter and a conservative 'role-pruner' to normalize incoming roles and emit a compact structured mode for tool/function outputs.

Summary of changes: added an adapter-level coordinator that: 1) recognizes and collapses repeated tool JSON fragments into a single compact structure when clients request compact output (new query param compact_output=true), 2) supplies a configurable stop_hint_priority so that explicit stop sequences sent by the API call are respected ahead of model-internal heuristics when desired, and 3) filters streaming logprob deltas below a configurable threshold to reduce bandwidth and surface only meaningful token confidence changes. The role-pruner maps unknown or noisy role labels (e.g. "assistant_bot", "system_user") into canonical roles (system, user, assistant) while preserving an optional role_metadata bag in streaming envelopes. The default mapping is conservative to avoid breaking customers who depend on custom roles.

API surface: new v1/chat query params (all optional, backward compatible): compact_output (boolean) - when true, server collapses repeated tool JSON fragments and returns a single 'tool_result' object per tool invocation; compact_mode (string) - "compact"|"verbose" controls how much ancillary metadata is included; stop_hint_weight (float 0-1) - higher values prefer explicit stop param over model-internal stops; logprob_filter_threshold (float 0-1) - tokens with probability below threshold will have logprobs suppressed in streaming deltas to reduce bandwidth. The existing 'function_call' behavior is unchanged unless compact_output is enabled.

Runtime changes: introduced runtime/stream/coordinator.py to manage stream fragment coalescing with backpressure awareness, integrated compacting logic into the v1 adapter to avoid double-encoding, and added a small heuristic to avoid coalescing across user-turn boundaries. Implemented a lightweight role-pruner in server/adapter/openai_compat/v1_chat_adapter.py that consults a normalization table and emits a role_hints field on the streaming envelope to surface pruned-original-role for observability.

Compatibility and safety: defaults preserve current behavior (compact_output=false, stop_hint_weight=0.5, logprob_filter_threshold=0.01). Role-pruner requires an opt-in flag (role_prune=true) for strict normalization; otherwise we only emit role_hints. The change intentionally avoids rewriting function signatures or existing response envelopes to prevent breaking existing integrations.

Testing and benchmarks: added integration tests under tests/integration/test_toolflow_streaming.py and unit tests for coordinator heuristics. Benchmarks run on perf-canary showed ~9-12% reduction in outbound streaming tokens for workloads with verbose tool JSONs (internal benchmark workload 'toolsuite-large-2025'), and ~3-6% average reduction in end-to-end latency due to fewer serialization events.

Docs and migration: updated docs/openai_compat.md with example calls, recommended migration path, and a sample shim for SDKs to opt-in to compact_output gradually. Release notes include guidance on when to enable compact_output and how to tune logprob_filter_threshold for telemetry vs fidelity.

Checklist: - [x] Runtime coordinator implementation + unit tests - [x] Role-pruner with opt-in flag - [x] SDK sample snippet and doc update - [x] Perf benchmark and canary run - [x] Security review for envelope changes

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the compact representation as an opt-in addition. We observed a handful of legacy clients that relied on repeated fragments for incremental parsing; for those customers we recommend gradual migration with compact_output=false while testing SDK helpers that reconstruct streamed fragments into a compact object on the client side.

Maya Singh: Good catch — updated the normalization table and added an 'allow_prefixes' config that preserves roles with configured prefixes. Default includes 'x-'.
Diego Rivera: The compact_output handshake looks fine but I worry about partial JSON fragments being dropped during reconnects.
Maya Singh: Coordinator now emits a sentinel event on stream disconnect that lists in-flight tool ids; client-side SDKs can use that to resume reassembly. Added integration test for reconnect scenario.
Priya Nair: Can we add an opt-out to keep full token logprobs for auditors?
Maya Singh: Added logprob_preserve_for_roles list in config and documented how SSO teams can request full logprobs; default remains filtered.
Ethan Park: CI flakes on arm64 linting job initially.
Maya Singh: Fixed lint in .github/workflows and bumped a pinned dependency; reran CI and all checks passed.
Introduce optional compact_output for v1/chat to collapse repetitive tool JSON fragments and reduce streaming bandwidth. Add role_prune opt-in to normalize noisy role labels while preserving original role metadata. New tuning params: stop_hint_weight and logprob_filter_threshold. Backward compatible by default; opt-in for compacting behavior.

Summary: Adds a new opt-in structured per-token metrics exporter and OTEL log enrichment to attach token-level fields to traces and logs. Motivation: token-level visibility is necessary to diagnose long-tail latency/cost regressions (esp. when batching and KV cache interactions differ by request priority). Existing token cost/latency buckets cover aggregated cases but do not preserve per-token attributes (model, priority_tier, cache_hit, prompt_hash). This PR provides a low-overhead, sampled event stream and a Prometheus bridge for aggregated consumption.

What changed (high level): 1) telemetry.proto: new TokenEvent proto describing timestamp, model, token_index, token_type (prompt/response), priority_tier, cache_hit, sequence_len, approximate_cost_micros, hashed_prompt_id, and sample_reason. 2) token_exporter: an exporter that accepts TokenEvent and can push to OTLP collector or aggregate counters/gauges via a Prometheus bridge. Exporter supports sampling policies (always, head-only, uniform n/sample, priority-weighted) configured in config/flags. 3) runtime instrumentation: generation emits TokenEvent at token finalization; emission path is non-blocking and uses a ring buffer + background flusher to avoid adding tail latency. 4) OTEL log enrichment: log_enricher attaches token-related attributes to the existing request-scoped OTEL logs and spans when sampling is enabled. To avoid PII risks we only include hashed_prompt_id; raw prompt text is never emitted. 5) Dashboards & alerts: new Grafana panels and an alert bundle that surface per-model token latency histograms, stream of sample reasons, and cardinality metrics. 6) Tests & docs: unit/integration tests added; docs describe feature flag, retention guidance, and cost implications.

Backward/compatibility notes: feature is behind the config flag telemetry.token_events.enabled=false by default. Exporter uses OTLP protocol; when disabled the codepath is no-op. No breaking API changes. Migration: operators who enable the exporter should size their telemetry collector for event rate; we include example sampling configs in docs.

Checklist: - [x] proto and exporter implementation - [x] runtime emit + non-blocking flusher - [x] OTEL log enrichment (opt-in) - [x] dashboards and example alert rules - [x] unit and integration tests - [x] docs and config entries - [x] performance validation: microbenchmark on p99 tail showed <0.25ms median additional latency in sampled mode

Commit summary: see commits list. Files changed: see files_changed list above. Small snippets: - telemetry.proto adds TokenEvent message and TokenSampleReason enum. - emitter writes events to telemetry/token_exporter.go via EmitTokenEvent(ctx, event).

Testing performed: unit tests for exporter serialization and prom-bridge aggregation; integration test that spins up a mock OTLP collector and asserts receipt for sampled events; CI e2e telemetry job that ran against a small serve binary and validated enriched OTEL logs and metrics; load microbenchmark (scripts/telemetry/load_test) at 10k rps with 1% sampling to validate CPU and memory overhead.

Security & privacy: raw prompt text is explicitly excluded; only hashed_prompt_id (HMAC-SHA256 with instance key) is emitted. The feature will appear in the privacy review checklist (ENG-8791). Operator docs include guidance for rotating keys and retention limits.

Open follow-ups: - Add adaptive sampling policy based on queue depth (ENG-8820) - Integrate exporter with billing pipeline to derive token-level cost telemetry (follow-up PR) - Add per-tenant rolloff in Dedicated deployments to avoid noisy tenants

Merge: Squash-merged by Priya Nair on 2026-03-04 after two approvals and successful CI.

Lina Wu: Added exporter_test.go with hashed id test and a table for sampling variants (see commit 3)
Omar Elbaz: Can we avoid creating a goroutine per request for the emitter? Concerned about contention under heavy concurrency.
Lina Wu: switched to a shared ring buffer + worker pool in token_exporter.go and added a benchmark in emitter_test.go
Priya Nair: LGTM overall; left a few nits on naming and comments, and an alert threshold question on token latency SLOs
Lina Wu: Addressed nits and lowered the critical alert from 95th token latency > 1.2s to 95th > 1.4s for now; added follow-up ticket ENG-8821 to refine thresholds
Opt-in structured per-token telemetry: operators can enable telemetry.token_events to export sampled per-token events to OTLP or aggregate them via the Prometheus bridge. This enables detailed token-level diagnostics (latency, cache_hit, priority tier) and enriched OTEL logs. Defaults off. See docs/observability/token-metrics.md for config and sizing guidance.

Motivation: customers repeatedly request safer, production-ready defaults that reduce per-token costs without regressing latency. This PR introduces the Adaptive Cost Gatekeeper, a small runtime component that synthesizes workload signals (median seq-len, request hotness, p95 latency budget) and emits recommended batching, prefix-caching, and quantization tier defaults per route. It also includes a unit-economics estimator used by the console to show projected cost delta for suggested changes. What this PR does: 1) adds gatekeeper daemon that watches RPS/sequence distributions and proposes defaults, 2) implements a conservative batching policy (max_batch_size and preferred_batch_timeout heuristics), 3) adds prefix/KV cache suggestion logic and cache key fingerprinting to avoid over-caching low-cardinality routes, 4) adds quantization recommendation hooks (FP16/INT8 preference hints) tied to observed quality deltas from eval harness, 5) surfaces estimator events to observability and console telemetry, 6) feature flags and rollout plan. Checklist: [x] gatekeeper core daemon and gRPC API; [x] conservative heuristics for production safety; [x] unit-economics estimator and telemetry events; [x] integration tests for batching/caching toggles; [x] console wiring (backend) for preview; [ ] console UI polish (follow-up). Related: Linear ENG-1294, ENG-1321; incident reference SUP-887 for cost spike patterns. Deployment notes: flag-guarded; start in opt-in mode for Dedicated customers and opt-out canary for hosted accounts. No breaking API changes. Merge method: squash.

Marta Silva (2026-02-20): The cache-fingerprint logic looks good but we should add a guard for low-cardinality keys (e.g., user_id absent). Author reply: Added a low-cardinality threshold and unit test in suggester_test.

Release Manager (2026-02-25): Approved for merge behind feature flag and with canary plan.
Start rollout in 'suggestion' mode for hosted small tenants, enable enforcement for Dedicated 1-week canaries only after metrics show stable p95 and no increase in 5xx. Watch metrics: gatekeeper.suggestions.applied, unit_econ.estimated_delta, runtime.batch.size.p95. If errors spike, rollback gatekeeper.enforce -> false.

Motivation: recent production incidents showed pathological tail latency when short-lived high-priority traffic interleaved with KV-heavy long-context requests. The continuous batcher could become congested by probe/burst requests that pin KV slots and prevent fairness tokens from progressing, causing latency spikes. This PR introduces a queue-horizon throttling policy and an exponential backoff for KV probe requests to reduce transient pin contention while preserving throughput.

b3a1e77 - kv_cache: probe backoff controller with exponential + jitter
d2f6c18 - scheduler: integrate horizon checks into admit path and fairness tokens
