Introduced redwood.openai.compat.strict_parity (default true) to toggle exact OpenAI parity. See docs/openai-compat.md for migration guidance.

Context: Customers building agent-style flows requested clearer, deterministic semantics for multi-tool calls, improved streaming stability when tool calls interleave with model tokens, and a minimal API surface compatible with OpenAI function-calling semantics. This PR introduces a 'tool-call bridge' and an injection shim that centralizes tool result routing, deterministic ordering, and per-tool idempotency for retries. Motivation: prior behavior allowed non-deterministic ordering for parallel tool invocations and ambiguous retry semantics which caused occasional output corruption during streaming and brittle client integrations. Goals: 1) Provide an ergonomic parameterized surface so callers can choose parallel vs ordered invocation without duplicating orchestration logic. 2) Maintain OpenAI-compatibility for function call metadata while offering richer structured-output hooks for Redwood-specific optimizations. 3) Make streaming stable when tools produce tokens mid-stream and during retry/fallback events. Design summary: - API: new optional request fields: "tool_concurrency" ("ordered" | "parallel" | numeric), "injection_policy" ("first-available" | "wait-for-all" | "per-tool"), and "tool_idempotency_key" (string, optional) to let SDKs and customers control retries. Backward-compatible defaults preserve previous behavior (ordered, per-tool). - Bridge: a new lightweight server-side component (runtime/tool_invoke/bridge.go) mediates tool invocation lifecycle. It receives tool call intents, issues concurrent invocations to the tool runner, collects results, applies injection policy, and forwards structured payloads to the streaming output path. The bridge also annotates calls with idempotency tokens and tracks transient failures. - Injection shim: converts tool outputs into structured "tool_result" frames that can be injected inline into a streaming delta stream or emitted as side-channel events. Each frame includes stable ordering metadata and an ordinal to enable deterministic replay for clients. - Retry semantics: automatic safe retries are implemented for idempotent tool calls when an error is transient (e.g., network timeouts). For non-idempotent tools, retries require explicit tool_idempotency_key or SDK-level opt-in. - OpenAI compatibility: we preserve the functions-compatible shape in the response ("function_call" and "function_result" fields) while adding a lightweight "redwood" envelope for ordering and diagnostic metadata. SDKs (python/typescript) map the redwood envelope to higher-level concurrency helpers. - Streaming stability: the bridge batches short-lived tool results into atomic injection frames to avoid mid-token interleaving. For long-lived streaming tool outputs (e.g., logs), the shim provides a "stream_chunk" frame type and backpressure signals to the runtime. - Observability: new metrics (tool_call.latency, tool_call.retries, tool_call.injection_lag) and tracing spans are emitted; Console dashboards updated. - Docs & examples: updated API spec and a new multi-tool example demonstrating parallel invocation with deterministic merge and fallback to ordered mode when concurrency budget is exceeded. Rollout strategy: feature gated behind runtime flag and a short beta period. Default behavior unchanged. SDKs include opt-in helpers in a minor release. Tests and CI: unit tests for bridge logic, integration tests against the tool runner and OpenAI-compat shim, and streaming e2e tests were added. See test notes below. Backwards compatibility: callers that do not set new fields will see preserved ordering and existing streaming behavior. Migration notes and examples are included in the docs.
Diego Ramos: Request changes — please make retry behavior explicit in the API section and add a note about non-idempotent tool safety. Also flag potential perf regression in high-concurrency workloads.
Asha Menon: Reply — added explicit 'tool_idempotency_key' field and documented non-idempotent fallback. Benchmarked concurrency overhead and optimized buffer path; numbers in PR description.
Samir Patel: Nitpick — prefer 'wait-for-all' vs 'collect-all' naming; otherwise LGTM after tests pass.
Laura Chen: Approve — tested with docs examples and python SDK; streaming e2e flakiness fixed by increasing small timeout.

Backwards compatible by default; SDK helpers available in minor SDK releases. Observability metrics and docs included.
Feature gated behind runtime flag 'tool_call_bridge_v1'. Recommend beta rollout to a subset of hosted customers and Dedicated tenants. Update SDKs in lockstep. Monitor tool_call.injection_lag and e2e-streaming errors for 48h post-rollout.

Motivation: Improve ergonomics and reliability for tool/function-calling in the OpenAI-compat layer and native Redwood API. Customers asked for easy multi-tool invocations, deterministic injection of tool results into continuations, safe parallel tool execution, and more robust retry/backoff for transient tool failures. This PR introduces a small, backwards-compatible API extension plus a new parallel tool-runner implementation and runtime wiring for result injection and structured output hints. Summary of changes: 1) API: add `tools` invocation signature that supports multiple tool calls in a single step and an optional `parallel` flag. 2) Runtime: implement ParallelToolRunner with optimistic concurrency, coordinated token streaming, and ordered result injection points. 3) Retry semantics: add configurable retry/backoff policies per-tool with circuit-breaking thresholds and idempotency markers. 4) Structured output: expand function-calling schema to include `injection_point` and `merge_strategy` hints for deterministic consolidation of parallel results. 5) OpenAI compatibility: surface the new multi-tool signature through the OpenAI-compat endpoint with feature gating and compatibility warning headers. 6) SDK: Python and TS client updates for ergonomics and typed helpers. 7) Tests & docs: unit + integration tests for parallel tool execution, backpressure scenarios, and streaming stability; docs and migration guide. Implementation notes and tradeoffs: - Parallel execution is best-effort: by default the runner executes tools concurrently and injects results in the order of `injection_point` when present. If tools have cross-dependencies, callers should use explicit sequential mode or `depends_on` fields. - Streaming: we added a coordinator that merges streaming outputs from active tools into a single response stream while preserving token interleaving semantics. This required a small amount of additional buffering (configurable via runtime flags) to avoid head-of-line blocking. - Retries: only idempotent-marked tools will be automatically retried; non-idempotent tools can opt into safe-retry wrappers. Retries use exponential backoff with jitter and a per-tool max attempt limit. - Backwards compatibility: existing function-calling calls remain unchanged. The new fields are optional and gated behind an SDK flag and an OpenAI-compat header for the next release window. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed by runtime and API teams (ENG-8341) - [x] Prototype validated in perf-canary with small synthetic workload - [x] Unit tests for ParallelToolRunner and retry policies - [x] Integration tests for streaming merge and structured injection - [x] Python + TS SDK helpers + docs snippets - [x] Compatibility guard and migration notes in docs - [x] Load test showing <5% median latency regression on typical chat workloads Known limitations: - Result consolidation for very large tool outputs can increase memory usage; we recommend streaming-friendly tool outputs or chunking. - Deterministic ordering across parallel calls is only guaranteed when callers provide explicit injection points. Related: ENG-8341 (tool ergonomics), PM-412 (product requirements), SUP-2023 (support case that drove retries). See inline changed files for details.
Diego Alvarez (review): Can we guarantee streaming ordering when a tool streams partial results? Concerned about race conditions between the runtime coordinator and long-running tool streams.
Maya Chen (author): The coordinator preserves per-tool stream order and exposes an ordering hint. For full determinism callers should specify injection_point; otherwise we guarantee causal ordering but not deterministic interleaving across tools.
Priya Natarajan (review): Suggest adding a circuit-breaker metric so SRE can alert on retries spiking for a given tool.
Maya Chen (author): Added per-tool circuit breaker hooks and metrics (runtime/tool_retry_policies.py); updated observability docs.
Samir Patel (review): SDK ergonomics look good for TS; Python helper should include an async context manager example.
Maya Chen (author): Added async context manager sample to python examples and an nb viewer-friendly notebook in the SDK examples.
Diego Alvarez (approval): Approved after addressing ordering doc and adding integration test for streaming merge. CI passed on final run.
Release-Manager (note): Merged via squash; compatibility header will be enabled by default two releases from now.
Add multi-tool invocation API and ParallelToolRunner: clients can invoke multiple tools in one call with optional parallel execution. Improvements include result injection points, merge strategies for structured output, and per-tool retry/backoff. Backwards compatible; gated behind feature flag for OpenAI-compat clients.

Motivation: make private-installer release delivery reproducible, auditable, and fast to rollback by switching pointers rather than rewriting channel manifests. This PR introduces a content-addressable (CA) blob index for release artifacts, KMS-backed signing of blob indexes, and an "immutable upgrader" Helm sidecar/Job that upgrades clusters by installing releases referenced by CA blob digests rather than mutable URLs. The CA index is an append-only manifest of artifacts with stable digests, upload timestamps, and cosign signatures. The upgrade flow moves from channel-based mutable manifests to digest-pinned artifacts while preserving compatibility with existing on-prem workflows via a migration shim. Changes include: 1) a new CA indexer micro-binary that enumerates built release blobs, computes digests, and emits a signed index; 2) Helm packaging adjustments so chart tarballs are uploaded with digest-based object names and the upgrader resolves artifacts by digest; 3) Terraform module additions that introduce a 'release_pointer' resource (a single transactional S3 object/key) and a 'rollback_trigger' boolean that forces the installer to switch pointers atomically for emergency rollbacks; 4) CI pipeline updates to sign indexes with KMS/cosign and publish delta shards for faster client pulls; 5) e2e tests that exercise upgrade and rollback using a local minio test fixture. Backwards compatibility: a migration controller reads the existing channel manifests and generates an initial CA index mapping; customers may opt-in to the CA mode. Security: all indexes are signed with customer KMS keys (private deployments) or with the org key for hosted CI; cosign verification is performed as part of the upgrader pre-flight. Rollback model: to roll back, the ops flow flips the release_pointer to the previous digest and notifies the upgrader; the upgrader will perform a reconcile based on the pointer change. Migration steps and rollback playbook are included in docs. Testing: unit coverage for indexer and Terraform module, integration job in CI that runs a full upgrade+rollback scenario, and staged canary validation. See linked Linear tickets for rollout staging and rollout gating. Breaking change: false. Merge rationale: reduces blast radius for upgrades and enables atomic rollbacks across environments.

Introduces a queue-latency-aware autoscaler that allocates tokenized burst credits to dedicated tenants and a Utilization Gap Reporter that surfaces sustained under/over-utilization. Backwards-compatible config flags; rollout gated behind feature flag and 2-step canary.
Context and motivation: customers on Dedicated have asked for better fairness when bursts co-exist with steady throughput tenants. Existing burst pools and reservations ensure throughput but can starve latency-sensitive tenants during microbursts. This PR implements a tokenized fairness scaler: a lightweight token accounting layer that mints per-tenant 'burst tokens' proportional to committed throughput and dynamically redistributes spare tokens based on queue-latency buckets.

Design summary: the scaler observes per-tenant request queue latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and token consumption rate. When a tenant's p95 exceeds its latency target and tokens are available in the cluster pool, the allocator grants ephemeral tokens that raise the tenant's concurrency cap for short windows (configurable TTL). Tokens are reclaimed proactively when latency recovers or when they expire. Token minting respects tenant share weights and a soft floor so smaller tenants cannot be starved.

Utilization Gap Reporter: a new telemetry pipeline sampler that computes 'util-gap' = committed_capacity - observed_effective_throughput over rolling windows. Significant positive gap (>X%) indicates underutilized reserved capacity; negative gap suggests chronic oversubscription and triggers alerts. The reporter aggregates per-tenant and per-cluster signals and emits events to the Console and to the autoscaler's feedback loop.

Key behaviors and safety: - Autoscaler only grants tokens if cluster headroom >= headroom_threshold config. - Tokens are time-limited (default 30s) and double-checked before increasing concurrency to avoid drift. - Manual overrides: operators can pin token budgets per-tenant via the Dedicated Console. - Feature gated: flag 'tokenized_fair_scaler_v1' controls rollout.

Files of note: see changed files list below for implementation and tests.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for token accounting, TTL expiry, and reclaim logic. - Integration tests with synthetic traffic generator that simulates bursty and steady tenants and validates latency SLOs improve without increasing aggregate CPU/Tensor utilization. - Canary plan: deploy to a single Dedicated cluster with low-risk tenants (internal sandbox), monitor util-gap and latency deltas for 48h, then expand to two clusters before full rollout.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-1842 tokenized-fairness-scaler) - [x] Unit & integration tests - [x] Telemetry for util-gap metrics - [x] Console toggles and tenant budget API - [x] Feature flag behind canary - [x] Safety tests and chaos run

Related: references existing autoscaler work (ENG-1532) but intentionally keeps runtime changes minimal to reduce risk.

Priya Kaur: @Ethan added a 5s jittered debounce for headroom flips and a revocation hook that consults reservation credits before granting. See allocator.go lines ~210-245. Added unit tests that exercise the interaction.
María López: Please add observability to show token churn rate (tokens/sec) and per-tenant average grant duration. Also suggest a lower default TTL (15s) for initial canary.

Motivation: Debugging long-tail latency/cost incidents is currently hard because traces often drop context for large requests and we have no compact way to reconstruct the original request token stream tied to the sampled spans. This PR introduces a lightweight, per-model-instance tail-span sampler plus a request-reconstructor that stores compressed, TTL-backed request snapshots (token offsets + prompt metadata) in object storage for post-mortem. The system is conservative by default (sample rate 0.01% for normal traffic) and exposes policy knobs for SLO-driven sampling (e.g. sample all requests that exceed p99 latency or cross a cost threshold). The change set includes: 1) a tail-span sampler in the serving runtime that marks traces with a tail_reason tag (latency/cost/cache_miss), 2) a request snapshotter that deduplicates and compresses payloads (LZ4 + shared-prefix dedupe on repeated system prompts), 3) a reconstructor service that can rehydrate a sampled request for local replay and full-token timing breakdowns, 4) new Grafana dashboard panels and an alert rule showing reconstructed-request cluster counts and the most common tail reasons per model instance, and 5) an automated retention/cleanup workflow to limit storage and PII exposure. Backwards compatibility: tracing spans keep the existing service/name conventions; the sampler only adds an opt-in config block in the cluster spec. Migration notes: enabling the feature requires an object-store bucket and the telemetry-agent sidecar to have write access. Security/privacy: snapshots are redaction-aware (PII scrub hooks) and default to 7-day TTL. Config defaults remain conservative. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-1245) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] e2e rehearsal in canary - [x] dashboard and alert JSON - [x] docs: observability/tail-debugging.md

Context: Our Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs diverged in how long-lived streaming connections handle token refresh, transient errors, and ergonomic iteration patterns. This caused intermittent stream resets, duplicate token refreshes under expiry storms, and developer confusion when porting examples between languages. Motivation: provide a single mental model and operational behavior across SDKs so product teams can rely on predictable streaming semantics and SLO-friendly retry/backoff defaults. What this PR does: centralizes token refresh logic behind a shared AuthRefresher interface (Python/TS) and a token watcher goroutine (Go), serializes refreshes per-connection to eliminate race conditions, introduces a uniform exponential-with-jitter backoff policy for streaming retries (special-cased to honor streaming idempotency), exposes a StreamIterator in TypeScript with parity to Python's iterator/async-iterator ergonomics, and adds an opt-in connection pooling toggle in the Go SDK to reduce TCP churn for high-connection-count clients. Compatibility: Default behavior is backward compatible; new behaviors opt-in via client option flags or environment toggles. Checklist: - implement AuthRefresher adapters in each SDK - wire backoff policy into streaming loop with metrics hooks - add TS StreamIterator wrapper and docs examples - add Go pool as opt-in with sane defaults and metrics - augment e2e and perf tests; update changelogs and bump SDK versions. Migration notes: existing usages continue to work. To opt in: Python/TS: pass auth_refresher or use SDK default; Go: set REDWOOD_GO_CONN_POOL=true or pass ClientOptions.UseConnPool=true. Tradeoffs: serialized refresh reduces redundant token calls but can add small latency when many connections refresh simultaneously; connection pooling reduces connection setup cost at the expense of shared connection lifecycle semantics (documented). Rollout plan: canary on internal integration clusters, gated release with perf lab smoke tests, immediate revert patch available if regression detected. Testing summary: unit tests, integration streaming tests, and perf microbenchmarks were added; CI run passed after a single flaky streaming test re-run.

Motivation: Improve streaming resilience for mobile/unreliable clients and make client-initiated cancel behavior idempotent while preserving OpenAI compatibility. This PR introduces a 'streaming session snapshot' model and explicit client ACK semantics so disconnected clients can reconnect and resume without inconsistent tool calls or duplicate function invocations. Includes small API surface additions (resume_token, session_id, seq) exposed in the OpenAI-compatible streaming adapter.

Summary of changes: 1) Protocol: add optional query/header parameters: X-Redwood-Session-Id (UUID), X-Redwood-Resume-Token (opaque token), and X-Redwood-Seq (monotonic integer). Server will emit a resume_token event at checkpoint boundaries (full structured object flush points) to allow resumption. 2) Client ACK semantics: streaming responses now include an ACK event type ("ack") that clients can send to confirm they received the last checkpoint; server holds tool-call/side-effect commits until ACK or until server soft-timeout expires. 3) Idempotent cancel: client-initiated cancel now accepts a cancel-with-reason payload and returns an idempotency token; repeating cancel requests with the same idempotency token is a no-op. 4) Server-side grace window: implement a configurable soft grace period (default 30s) after disconnect where session state and pending tool call fences are retained to allow resume. After grace window expiration the session is garbage collected. 5) Function-calling/structured output: ensure structured JSON blocks are flushed at checkpoint boundaries; add deterministic boundaries to avoid partial structured chunks on reconnect. 6) OpenAI compatibility layer: expose resume_token as a top-level SSE event named "resume_token" and support incoming resume headers for existing SDKs; keep the text/event-stream framing compatible with existing clients.

Why this is different from previous proposals: previous work focused on reconnect/retry-backoff and teardown safety. This PR couples explicit checkpoint metadata and client ACKs to avoid duplicate function calls and to provide a concrete resume point that is safe across network blips. It is optimized for tool calling workloads where side effects must be constrained to once semantics.

Commits (high-level): [1] protocol: add session id and resume token headers and wire through adapter; [2] runtime: checkpoint serializer and resume token generation; [3] runtime: hold-and-commit mechanism gated by client ACK and grace window; [4] api: idempotent cancel endpoint and cancel idempotency token; [5] openai-adapter: SSE event renames and backward-compatible parsing; [6] tests: end-to-end resume and duplicate-cancel tests; [7] docs: streaming lifecycle migration guide and SDK hints.

Files changed (high-level): api/streaming_adapter.py (protocol parsing and headers), runtime/checkpoint_manager.rs (checkpoint persistence and GC), runtime/tool_fence.rs (hold/commit logic), openai_compat/sse_adapter.go (resume_token event), stdlib/net/ack_client.py (SDK helper), tests/integration/test_resume.py, docs/streaming-lifecycle.md.

Small illustrative snippets: - in SSE stream: event: resume_token

  data: {"token":"<opaque>","seq":42,"session_id":"..."}

- cancel endpoint: POST /v1/streams/:id/cancel {"reason":"user_abort","idempotency_token":"abc123"} -> 202 {"cancelled":true,"token":"abc123"}

Testing: added deterministic unit tests for checkpoint boundaries and a flaky-network harness that simulates TCP drops and validates resume semantics across reconnects. End-to-end tests ensure that function-calling side-effects execute exactly once when clients follow ACK/resume contract. Performance: microbenchmark shows ~3% p99 overhead for sessions with frequent checkpoints (configurable), negligible for typical chat flows.

Migration notes: - Backwards compatible: clients that do not send session headers keep existing behavior. Resume support is opt-in (server issues resume_token only when session_id provided). - SDKs: quick helper added in python/ts/go SDKs (std ack helper) and docs updated with example reconnect flow. - Operators: new config runtime.streaming.grace_window_seconds (default 30) and runtime.streaming.max_session_persist (default 10m).

We will later add signed tokens for cross-region resume. - Tool-call fences add memory pressure while session is in grace window; follow-up to add spill-to-disk for very large pending calls (ENG-2210).

Checklist: [x] design doc linked, [x] unit tests, [x] e2e tests, [x] docs updated, [x] SDK helpers, [x] load test run, [x] security review (RBAC/headers sanitized).

Aisha Gomez: Edge-case: what happens if client ACK is lost and resume_token used? Proposed server-side re-emit on reconnect if session still valid. Implemented and covered by e2e tests.

payload.body:
Context: We continue to see noisy long-tail latency alerts where aggregated percentiles obscure per-segment (prefix / KV-cache warmness / batch-size) behavior. This PR introduces a lightweight per-segment 'latency trellis' rollup plus a log entropy-based filter to suppress low-signal alerts from high-cardinality noisy routes. Motivation: reduce alert fatigue, surface actionable regressions, and provide a compact dashboard for investigating tail behavior at the segment level. Summary of changes: 1) telemetry/rollups: add TrellisBuilder that buckets requests by segment keys (prefix_hash, kv_hit, batch_bin) and emits downsampled reservoir histograms keyed by segment_id; 2) tracing/span-enrichment: attach segment_id and entropy_score to sampling spans to enable correlation between logs and trellis buckets; 3) logging/filter: implement LogEntropyFilter which computes a rolling entropy score per route and suppresses low-information log flaps from surfacing as incidents; 4) dashboards: add dashboards/latency-trellis.jsonnet with segment heatmap, top-entropy routes, and quick drilldowns to traces; 5) alerts: introduce tuned alert rule 'trellis_long_tail_anomaly' that uses segment-level anomaly score and an entropy gate to reduce false positives; 6) tests: unit and integration tests for trellis aggregation and entropy filter, plus a synthetic SLO replay in perf-canary. Implementation details: TrellisBuilder operates as an incremental aggregator inside the telemetry ingestion pipeline and emits compact rollups every 30s; reservoir histograms are bounded to 256 samples to control cardinality. segment_id is a deterministic 64-bit hash of the tuple (route, prefix_bucket, kv_hit, batch_bin) so it is stable across rollouts. Entropy is approximated with a small fixed-window counting sketch (64 counters) to keep memory bounded per route. Rollout plan: 1) deploy trellis rollups in staging for 48h; 2) enable dashboard in read-only for SRE and product; 3) enable alert gating at 10% of traffic and monitor false-positive rate for 72h; 4) full rollout on success. Backwards compatibility: recorded metrics are namespace-prefixed with telemetry.trellis.v1 so older dashboards remain unchanged. Testing and CI: added unit tests and an integration test that replays synthetic sessions to validate segment-level percentiles; one flaky histogram serialization test was rerun in CI and passed on second attempt (CI status: pass). Review notes and trade-offs: reservoir histograms trade exactness for bounded storage; entropy gate reduces signal for very low-traffic noisy routes which risks missing rare regressions — we tuned thresholds conservatively and included an override label to force bypass per-route in the console. Observability additions: new metrics telemetry.trellis.segment_latency_p50/p95/p99, telemetry.trellis.segment_count, telemetry.trellis.segment_entropy; tracing enrichment fields segment_id and entropy_score; dashboard and alert definitions included. Related work: complements ENG-1173 (kv-cache profiler) and PM-442 (long-tail alerting improvements). Checklist: ; [x] unit tests added; [x] integration test added; [x] dashboard JSONnet included; [x] alert rule added with gradual rollout; [x] migration notes and docs updated. Please see commits summary and file list below.
4 commits: 1) Add TrellisBuilder core aggregation and reservoir histograms; 2) Attach segment_id and entropy_score to sampled spans; 3) Implement LogEntropyFilter and add unit tests; 4) Add dashboards and alert rules + docs and perf replay test.
Reviewer Marta: 'Can you clarify memory profile at 1M routes?'; Author Linh: 'We bound per-route sketch to 64 counters and shard state; memory projection added to docs and is ~120MB for 1M active routes in worst case; see docs/observability/memory_projection.md'; Reviewer Lucas: 'Prefer metric names without deep nesting' -> Author: 'Kept telemetry.trellis.v1 to allow future schema changes; provided compatibility shim'; Reviewer Priya: 'Alert threshold looks aggressive for low-volume routes' -> Author: 'Added entropy gate and per-route override label; added canary at 10% traffic.'; Final: Approved by Marta and Lucas, Priya requested one small rename in alert docs which was applied.
Introduce per-segment latency trellis rollups and log-entropy filter to reduce long-tail alert noise and provide segment-level latency insights. New metrics and dashboard added. Configurable entropy gate for alerts.
Run perf-canary replay with provided synthetic sessions; verify trellis segment buckets appear in telemetry backend; validate that entropy filter suppresses noise on designated noisy-route fixture; check dashboard heatmap and trace drilldowns.
payload.title: Introduce per-segment latency trellis and log entropy filter for long-tail reduction

payload.body:
Motivation: We observed that burst credits and reserved quotas sometimes sit idle on underloaded tenants while other tenants temporarily hit SLA throttles. This PR implements a fleet-level quota rebalancer that (1) proactively redistributes short-term burst budget across compatible tenants within a reservation class, and (2) accounts for slippage and debt so that rebalancing does not cause sudden regressions for donors or recipients.

What this PR does (high-level):
- Introduces a new "quota rebalancer" background controller that computes transferable credit windows and issues grace-limited transfers at configurable intervals.
- Adds slippage accounting: when credits are transferred, both donor and recipient receive an amortized slippage ledger entry to smooth the impact across subsequent allocation windows.
- Implements graceful-debit behavior for recipients: if downstream load drops, the rebalancer drains amortized credits over a configurable decay period instead of immediate revocation.
- Extends utilization reporting with amortized-credit-aware metrics: reported util% now includes an "effective utilization" value that factors in temporarily borrowed budget and shows donor/recipient deltas.
- Exposes new autoscaler knobs: min_headroom_ratio, slippage_tolerance_pct, transfer_window_secs, debt_decay_secs, and max_concurrent_transfers.
- Adds a new telemetry export for "transfer events" (transfer_start, transfer_commit, transfer_revert) with contextual tags for reservation_class, donor_tenant, recipient_tenant, and reason.
- Regression and integration tests for stability under bursty traffic and during rolling upgrades.

Why it's safe: Transfers are conservative by default (slippage_tolerance_pct=3, transfer_window_secs=300, max_concurrent_transfers=2). All transfers are reversible by policy within the debt_decay_secs window and emit audit entries so operators can trace state changes. The rebalancer only operates within the same reservation class and respects tenant-level hard caps.

Files/areas changed (summary):
- runtime/fleet/rebalancer.go: new controller and reconciliation logic.
- runtime/fleet/ledger.go: amortized slippage ledger and decay logic.
- runtime/autoscaler/config.go: new knobs and validation.
- telemetry/metrics/exports.go: transfer events and effective_utilization gauge.
- api/v1/reservations.proto: added TransferEvent proto and new fields on ReservationStatus.
- docs/ops/rebalancer.md: operator guide and recommended alerts/dashboards.
- test/integration/rebalancer_burst_test.go: load scenarios and assertions.

Testing and results:
- Unit test coverage added for ledger math and decay (ledger coverage ~92%).
- Integration load test (100 tenants, stochastic burst model) shows 18% reduction in SLA throttles for high-demand tenants during 15m peak windows, with median donor impact <1.5% latency regression.
- CI: initial perf benchmark flagged a small race in ledger expiry; fixed in second commit and all checks passed on final run.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature gated off by default.
2) Enable in canary fleet for 48h with transfer_window_secs=600 and slippage_tolerance_pct=1.
3) Observe effective_utilization and transfer_* telemetry; ensure donor_loss_p50 < 2% and no transfer_revert spikes.
4) Gradual ramp to 30% of fleet then full rollout.

Monitoring and alerts to add (docs/ops/rebalancer.md):
- Alert if transfer_revert_rate > 0.5% over 5m.
- Alert if average debt_per_tenant > reserved_capacity * 0.2 for > 10m.
- Dashboard panels: transfer event timeline, donor/recipient latency delta, amortized debt heatmap.

Related work: ENG-1187 (fleet headroom adjustments), ENG-1199 (utilization telemetry revamp).

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration tests
- [x] Perf bench (rerun after fix)
- [x] Docs and operator guide
- [x] Feature gate and default off

Notes: This design intentionally avoids cross-reservation-class transfers to reduce blast radius. We plan a follow-up PR to add a soft-scheduling hint so the admission layer can prefer donors with lower p95 latency for transfers.
Diego Lopez: Can we add a per-tenant safety cap so a donor can't go below its hard cap? (addressed: ledger enforces hard caps, see ledger.go commit)
Sonia Kaur: Requesting a stronger perf test matrix for p99 latency under donor churn. Suggested adding synthetic slow donors. (addressed in integration tests, added slow donor scenario)
Evan Brooks: Found a racing condition around expiry timers on the ledger; pushed a fix and added deterministic timer tests.
Maya Patel (author): Replied - added safety cap checks, expanded perf tests, and included audit events for every transfer. Leaving feature gated by default until ops rollout complete.
SRE Bot: CI perf bench initially failed (race); rerun passed after e7c3b9d fix.
Introduce fleet quota rebalancer (feature-gated). Adds slippage accounting and amortized debt to allow short-term credit transfers across tenants within the same reservation class; exposes telemetry and autoscaler knobs for operator control.

Context: Customers are starting to adopt the OpenAI Responses v4 style endpoint and expect parity with existing v3/v2 behavior for determinism controls and metadata propagation. Prior attempts preserved basic streaming compatibility but lost deterministic seed hints and user metadata when routed through the OpenAI compatibility layer. This caused flaky repros for customers relying on 'client_seed' and made audit logs incomplete.

This PR implements three coordinated changes to the compat bridge and runtime: 1) deterministic seed propagation: accept an optional client_seed|seed_hint field on the mapped Responses v4 request and reliably propagate it through the bridge into the internal InferenceRequest seed field (used by deterministic sampling kernels). Seed is stored on the canonical ResponseRecord so downstream logs/keys include it. 2) metadata forwarding: user-supplied metadata blob (freeform JSON) is attached to the ResponseRecord and surfaced in internal telemetry and audit exporters, with size-limits and sanitization. The compat shim no longer strips top-level user_metadata fields. 3) streaming stability + reassembly: streaming packets are now annotated with a stream_chunk_index and seed_affinity flag to ensure reassembly logic groups tokens emitted under the same seed context, preventing cross-chunk reseeding that caused non-deterministic outputs during stream reconnects. 

Checklist: 
- [x] API mapping and translation layer implementation (pkg/bridge)
- [x] Kernel/runtime plumbing to accept propagated seed (internal/runtime)
- [x] Streaming reassembly changes and tests
- [x] SDK helpers in python/ts to expose seed and metadata on client side
- [x] E2E tests and CI matrix updates
- [x] Docs (api-mapping/responses-v4.md)

Compatibility notes: This change preserves the existing default behavior when no seed/client_seed is provided. When a seed is supplied, it acts as a deterministic hint for sampling kernels; we do NOT guarantee bit-exact outputs across hardware variants. The seed is honored deterministically within a single runtime configuration. For customers using Dedicated or Private deployments, the seed propagation is a no-op unless the underlying runtime is configured to enable deterministic sampling.

Security and privacy: forwarded user_metadata is rate- and size-limited (4KB) and scrubbed of known sensitive keys (password, ssn, credit_card) with a best-effort redaction. Audit-exporter tests updated to include user_metadata.

Migration: No breaking changes to public Redwood API. OpenAI-compat clients can start attaching 'client_seed' and 'user_metadata' in Requests v4 body; SDK helpers added to python/ts to make this ergonomic.

Related: ENG-1347 (compat), ENG-1412 (streaming-reassembly), SUP-9021 (customer case).
Diego Marquez: Please add one-line docs for behavior when seeds are absent. Added in docs, resolved.
Priya Nair: Will the seed_affinity mechanism increase latency for small requests? I couldn't find a perf regression on benchlab but please add notes. Reply: microbench shows <0.5ms median, included a note in CHANGELOG.
Tomoko Sato: Found a race in reassembly when client reconnects mid-chunk. Fixed with atomic chunk-id and added test.
Add client_seed and user_metadata passthrough for OpenAI Responses v4 on the compatibility bridge; streaming reassembly updated to preserve seed affinity and improve reproducibility. SDK helpers and docs included.
payload.title: OpenAI-bridge v4: seed propagation and metadata forwarding for Responses

payload.body:
Context: Certain customer workloads with short-lived contexts (conversation turns, search rerank slices) are sensitive to per-request dequant overhead. Existing dequant fusion paths for INT8/FP8 reduce operator count but still incur per-token memory traffic when invoked indiscriminately across batches.

Motivation: Reduce tail latency and average per-token cost by making the dequantization decision token-adaptive and by introducing a blockwise sparsification pass that lets kernels skip dense dequant work on low-importance token blocks. This PR implements a runtime policy and accompanying kernel-side fastpath that cooperates with KV-cache-aware continuous batching and scheduler heuristics.

Summary of changes: 1) Token-adaptive dequantization policy: a lightweight scoring function (based on token position, attention weight variance, and runtime quality heuristics collected at warmup) that marks token ranges as "hot" or "cold" for full dequantization. Hot ranges follow the existing fused dequant+matmul path; cold ranges use a reduced-precision in-place cast with deferred requant/rescale downstream. 2) Blockwise kernel sparsifier: new block-skipping annotations in the fused attention and FFN kernels to bypass dequant memory copies on contiguous low-importance blocks, implemented as an inline conditional in CUDA/TVM kernels to avoid extra dispatch overhead. 3) KV-cache integration: extend KV cache metadata to carry per-key block importance vectors; continuous batching aggregator uses these vectors to coalesce requests with similar block profiles to increase coalescing efficiency. 4) Scheduler hints: add "dequant_cost" and "block_sparsity" hints to the request router so the policy can prefer lanes that minimize latency SLO impact (e.g., route cold-block-heavy requests to high-throughput nodes). 5) Perf harness & benchmarks: new microbenchmarks and a production-style benchmark harness that simulates mixed-turn chat workloads to measure latency P50/P95 and token throughput under realistic batching.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4128)
- [x] Unit tests for policy and KV-metadata
- [x] Kernel microbenchmarks added
- [x] SLO regression tests run
- [x] Backwards-compatible KV metadata encoding
- [x] Documentation (runtime flags, tuning knobs)

Commits summary:
- feat(runtime): add token-adaptive-dequant policy and scoring utils
- feat(kernels): add blockwise sparsifier primitive and CUDA kernel patch
- perf(tests): add mixed-turn benchmark harness and scripts
- ci: add perf job to run harness on push
- docs: note new flags and recommended tuning in ops guide

Changed areas/files (high-level):
- runtime/dequant_policy.py (new): main scoring logic and runtime config hooks
- runtime/scheduler/hints.py: add dequant_cost/block_sparsity hint plumbing
- serving/kv/metadata.proto: extend KV metadata with block importance vector (backwards-compatible optional field)
- kernels/attn/block_sparsifier.cu: block-skip implementation with inline fastpath
- kernels/ffn/block_sparsifier.cu: mirrored logic for FFN path
- kernels/fuse/dequant_fuse_pass.cc: tie-in for fused vs deferred path selection
- benchmarks/mixed_turn/README.md and harness scripts
- tests/unit/test_dequant_policy.py: coverage for scoring edge cases
- docs/ops/dequant_tuning.md: operator-level tuning knobs

Illustrative snippet (kernel guard): "if (unlikely(block_importance[i] < sparsity_threshold)) { // fast-skip dequant path; operate in-place with reduced copy } else { // full fused dequant+matmul }"

Review conversation:
- Siddharth Rao (reviewer): "Overall good direction; two concerns: 1) scoring should avoid oscillation across batches (we need hysteresis), 2) ensure metrics emitted for block-level quality so we can detect regressions."
- Marisol (author): "Added a 3-step exponential smoothing for scoring in dequant_policy.py and emitted block_quality metrics (histogram + tag by model/version)."
- Linnea Olsson: "Kernel looks solid but please add a fallback that disables skipping when debug flags enabled; also add comments explaining the alignment assumptions for block boundaries."
- Marisol: "Added debug flag and comments; updated unit tests to cover misaligned blocks."
- Ethan Brooks: "Bench numbers look promising but CI perf job failed on first run (OOM on small runner). Reran on bigger runner and results stable."

CI checks and timeline:
- Linux unit tests: pass
- Linter: pass
- CUDA kernel compile: pass
- Perf harness (initial): fail (OOM on small runner) -> rerun: pass (on large runner)
- Integration: pass

Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2024-11-18 by Marisol after approvals from Siddharth and Linnea. Rationale: performance gains without functional changes; opt-in runtime flag allows gradual rollout.

Measured results (benchmark harness, mixed-turn chat profile):
- Latency: P50 reduced by ~9% and P95 reduced by ~14% on INT8 fused models with typical chat-turn length of 16 tokens
- Throughput: token/sec increased by ~7% at 99th percentile under steady batching
- Cost: estimated per-token memory bandwidth reduced ~11% for workloads with ≥20% cold-block density

Release notes: "Introduce token-adaptive dequantization and blockwise kernel sparsifier to reduce latency and memory bandwidth for quantized (INT8/FP8) inference. Opt-in via runtime flag 'runtime.dequant.token_adaptive=true'. Backwards-compatible KV metadata extension; no model changes required."

Operational notes and rollout plan:
- Feature disabled by default; enable behind a feature flag for a subset of customers/runtimes
- Start with A/B canary (5% traffic) and monitor block_quality, token_latency P95, and error-rate regressions
- If regressions detected, scheduler hint can route problematic requests to fallback lanes that always use the fused dequant path
- Add a smoothing threshold config and a per-tenant override to tune sensitivity to block sparsity

Additional remarks:
- This PR intentionally keeps the policy heuristics pluggable; next steps include an ML-based classifier in ENG-4210 that can replace the heuristic scorer, and a follow-up kernel patch that supports mixed precision within a block for further gains.
- No breaking API changes; KV metadata addition is optional and server-side-only, older nodes ignore the optional field.
Siddharth Rao: scoring hysteresis + metrics required
Linnea Olsson: add debug fallback and alignment comments
Ethan Brooks: perf job failed on small runner; rerun on larger runner
Marisol Vega: addressed comments, added smoothing and metrics, updated tests
Squash merged by author. PR approved by two reviewers. Feature behind runtime flag for staged rollout.
Introduce token-adaptive dequantization and blockwise kernel sparsifier to reduce latency and memory bandwidth for quantized (INT8/FP8) inference. Opt-in via runtime flag 'runtime.dequant.token_adaptive=true'.
Follow-up items: add telemetry dashboard for block_quality; iterate on ML-based scorer (ENG-4210); evaluate mixed-precision within-blocks in next kernel patch.
payload.title: Token-adaptive dequantization policy and blockwise kernel sparsifier for low-latency quantized paths

payload.body:
Context: Customers reported inconsistent behavior between Redwood's /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer and upstream OpenAI semantics when (1) multiple stop sequences overlap with token boundaries, (2) logprobs are requested together with function/tool calling metadata, and (3) framed streaming envelopes interleave toolcall boundary tokens. Motivation: Align Redwood's OpenAI compatibility surface with expected client behavior so that integrations relying on stop precedence, logprob provenance, and function-call boundaries do not observe regressions during streaming or when using fallback model variants. This PR implements three coordinated changes: 1) Stop reconciliation: Introduce a deterministic priority policy for overlapping stop sequences (longest-match first, then earliest-occurring) and ensure the stream terminates with a stop fragment that preserves the exact byte offsets clients expect. 2) Logprob annotations: When clients request logprobs alongside function/tool calls, annotate returned logprobs with provenance tags ("response", "toolcall-prefix", "toolcall-output") so downstream scorers can attribute token probabilities properly. Keep the extra metadata compact to avoid adding per-token payload overhead for clients that do not request logprobs. 3) Toolcall delimiter stabilization: Add an explicit framed delimiter event in the streaming envelope to mark toolcall handoff points; this reduces race conditions where partial tool outputs would be emitted inline with model tokens. Changes in this PR: - server/api/openai_compat/chat_adapter.py: Adds stop reconciliation module and config flag to enable longest-match policy; wire-up for streaming envelope delimiter. - server/stream/framer.py: New envelope type "TOOL_DELIM" and deterministic emission ordering to avoid interleaved fragments. - runtime/proto/logprob.proto: Extend logprob message with a provenance field (enum) and compact bitflags. - runtime/handlers/chat_stream_handler.go: Integrate provenance wiring so logprob requests flow end-to-end during streaming. - docs/openai_compat.md: Expanded compatibility notes and a migration section explaining the stop priority semantics and the new logprob provenance field. - tests/test_chat_stream.py: Add integration tests covering overlapping stops, logprob+toolcall scenarios, and streaming boundary events. Summary of commits: - 1a2b3c4: initial implementation of stop reconciliation logic and unit tests - 2b3c4d5: add streaming envelope TOOL_DELIM and framer changes - 3c4d5e6: wire logprob provenance through proto and handler path - 4d5e6f7: docs, test harness updates, and CI flake fixes Testing and CI: The first CI run showed a flaky streaming test (test_toolcall_boundary) on macOS runners; I adjusted test timing and rewrote the harness to use deterministic pseudo-clock. After two reruns all checks passed (build, unit, integration, linters). Rollout plan: Feature is gated behind feature flag "compat.stream_graft_v1" default-on for canary clusters. We'll monitor the per-route regression dashboard for 72 hours, focusing on end-to-end test sets (Linear ENG-8421) and customer reports. Backwards compatibility: The new stop priority is opt-in via config for older Dedicated/Private installations — the hosted API will use the new behavior to match upstream expectations. Release notes: "OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: deterministic stop matching, logprob provenance, and stable toolcall streaming delimiter (backward-compatible opt-in for self-hosted)."
Diego Ramos: Please add a comment in chat_adapter explaining why longest-match was chosen (not earliest).
Evelyn Morgan: Added comment and rationale referencing OpenAI compatibility notes in docs/openai_compat.md
Priya Khanna: The provenance enum names look fine; can we keep the numeric values stable for wire compatibility?
Evelyn Morgan: Confirmed numeric values are explicitly set in proto with inline comments — added a unit test asserting enum values.
Liam O'Connor: Integration test failed once in CI due to a nondeterministic clock in test harness — please replace with pseudo-clock. /approved after fix
Diego Ramos: Verified end-to-end against a small regression prompt set (ENG-8421) — LGTM
Release Manager (automated): Merged via squash commit
Deterministic stop matching (longest-match priority), compact logprob provenance tagging for mixed toolcall+logprob workflows, and a stable streaming TOOL_DELIM event to reduce interleaving of partial tool outputs. Opt-in for Dedicated/Private; hosted API enabled by default.
Monitor per-route mismatch rates for chat.v1->openai_compat over next 72h. Add an alert if stop-truncation regressions exceed 0.1% or if streaming TOOL_DELIM reordering observed.

payload.body: Summary: Adds per-model metadata and API filtering hints to the model catalog to help clients select models that support tool/function calling, have strong streaming stability characteristics, and expose recommended rate/price limits. Motivation: Customers building production-grade chat experiences need a single model listing that surfaces not just capabilities but operational hints (streaming robustness, function-calling fidelity, concurrency guidance, and pricing bounds) so they can safely route requests and set fallbacks without trial-and-error. This change is intended to reduce integration surprises for SDK users and make the hosted catalog more useful for Dedicated/Private routing policies. What changed (high level): 1) Catalog schema: added fields streaming_stability_score (float 0.0-1.0), streaming_profiles (list of short ids), tool_calling_compat (enum: none/partial/full), structured_output_profiles (list), recommended_concurrency (int hint), pricing_tier (string), per_token_price_usd_hint (decimal string), and region_rate_limits (map-style string encoded per-region hint). 2) List API: new query params supports_tool_calling, min_streaming_score, pricing_tier, max_per_token_price_usd and region to filter results server-side. Also added response hints in the model object to suggest default streaming configuration and recommended backoff. 3) OpenAI-compat shim: updated compatibility flags to include function_calling_policy and structured_output_profile names so the shim can map OpenAI-style function calling to our tool_calling_compat enum. 4) Docs & examples: extended model_catalog.md with new filter examples and SDK snippets (TS + Python) showing how to pick models for stable streaming and safe function calls. 5) Tests & migrations: DB migration to add columns, unit tests for filters and serialization, e2e streaming stability check in CI. Backwards compatibility: All new catalog fields are optional and default to conservative values (tool_calling_compat=none, streaming_stability_score=0.0). Clients that ignore unknown fields will continue to work. Checklist: - [x] Schema migration and defaults - [x] API changes and parameter validation - [x] SDK examples updated - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Docs updated - [x] Release notes drafted Commits (summary): - catalog: add streaming_stability_score and tool_calling_compat to model schema - api: add list-models filters and param parsing + validation - db: migration 20251112_add_catalog_hints.sql - docs: update model_catalog.md and examples - tests: add streaming filter unit tests and e2e streaming scenario Review convo (summary): - Evan: requested stronger validation on min_streaming_score and asked for examples of how scores are computed. Aisha: added score computation note to docs and clamped query param server-side. - Jia: asked to surface concurrency hint only as advisory (not enforced by routing); updated handler and docs accordingly. - Samir: flagged that per_token_price_usd_hint needs a currency string to avoid ambiguity; we switched to decimal string with USD suffix in docs and validation. CI and stability notes: The streaming e2e matrix initially produced a flaky test against the older runtime image; we reproduced locally, adjusted the test harness timing, and reran CI which passed. Load tests for listing endpoints at 50 concurrent requests passed with the new indexes. Merge and rollout plan: Merged to main via squash on 2025-11-18. Feature gate enabled by default but catalog consumers can opt out by filtering only models without the new flags. Rollout steps: - DB migration run in staging -> monitor catalog list latency and index usage for 24h - enable new query params in staging SDKs samples -> validate downstream callers - schedule a gradual rollout to canary Dedicated tenants before global rollout Breaking change? false. Rollback plan: revert migration + roll back service, or keep fields optional and disable new query parsing if immediate rollback needed. Release notes: Added advisory metadata in model catalog: streaming stability score, tool-calling compatibility flags, structured output profiles, and per-model recommended concurrency and token-price hints. This enables safer client-side model selection for streaming/function-calling workflows. Merge method: squash. Additional context: This PR is intended as an intermediate step before exposing richer streaming configuration profiles (follow-up ENG-2308) and before adding server-enforced rate limits per-model (planned feature ENG-2401).
payload.title: Add model-catalog hints: tool-calling support, streaming-stability score, and rate/price limits

payload.body:
Motivation: production services experience intermittent client disconnects (mobile flaps, network handovers). Existing streaming behavior loses in-flight toolcall/state and forces full retry which causes duplicate side-effects and poor UX. This PR introduces a lightweight reconnection handshake with explicit handoff semantics, a short-lived server lease for inflight sessions, and a soft-lease refresh path so reconnecting clients can resume streaming without replaying side-effectful tool calls. It also updates the OpenAI compatibility adapter to surface reconnection metadata for clients and adds idempotency enforcement hooks for tool/function calls.

Design summary: 1) handshake: when a client reconnects within a configured grace window it provides prior_session_id + reconnect_token. Server validates token and either returns a resume_ack (session reattached) or a replay_hint (client should replay prompt but mark toolcalls idempotent). 2) server lease: newly-created streaming sessions allocate a short-lived lease (default 45s) that preserves in-memory KV for quick reconnects; background TTL refresh can extend leases for healthy sessions. 3) handoff semantics: if a reconnecting client attaches while a worker is mid-toolcall, the server sets a toolcall-escrow flag and returns a toolcall-status block in the resume_ack so the client can safely decide to wait, replay with idempotency token, or soft-abort (no-op). 4) OpenAI-compat adapter exposes X-Redwood-Reconnect-Token and Reconnect-Window headers and maps resume_ack -> delta events for streaming consumers. 5) Structured output integrity: partial JSON chunks are repaired by the runtime on resume by replaying remaining tokens from the point-of-truth (server-side reconstruction), avoiding malformed outputs on client reconnect.

Checklist (completed): - [x] runtime: reconnection handler, lease manager, token validation - [x] API: header + body compatibility changes, resume_ack schema - [x] sdk-python: reconnect helper + examples - [x] openai-adapter: header mapping and migration tests - [x] e2e: integration test with simulated disconnects and mid-toolcall reconnection - [x] docs: short migration note and example flow in console docs

Risk/rollout notes: default behavior is backward compatible: clients that do not send reconnect metadata get existing semantics. Feature gated by runtime flag stream.reconnect.enabled=false for canary rollout. Idempotency tokens for toolcalls are required only when toolcall is marked side-effectful; we added a runtime check and a developer warning in logs for missing tokens.

Related: ENG-3187 (reconnect product spec), ENG-3201 (toolcall idempotency), incident INT-442 (customer outage reproducer).
Liam Patel: Can we keep the default lease shorter (30s) for GA? Longer leases increase memory pressure; suggest configurable default.
Maya Chen: Answered: made default 45s after load testing; added runtime flag stream.reconnect.default_lease_secs and explained memory/throughput tradeoffs in PR description.
Sofia Rodriguez: Are there any client backwards-compat issues if headers are missing? Please add regeneration path for reconnect_token collisions.
Maya Chen: Added collision guard and fallback to replay_hint; updated adapter tests to cover header-absent flows.
Arjun Mehta: Unit tests for toolcall escrow look good. Request: add metric for escrowed_toolcalls_count.
Maya Chen: Added reconnect_metrics.prom + increment where escrow is set.
Added optional streaming reconnect handshake and short server-side leases to improve resume reliability for intermittent client disconnects. OpenAI-compat adapter now exposes reconnect headers; SDKs include reconnect helpers. Backwards compatible by default.
Canary rollout started on dedicated clusters; monitor reconnect_success_ratio and escrowed_toolcalls_count.
payload.title: Reconnect handshake handoff and server lease refresh for resilient streaming

Context & motivation: Several production workloads (ENG-1984) showed that the majority of per-token CPU/GPU overhead for quantized models comes from frequent small dequant/requant transitions and scattered KV cache misses when sequences have high prefix reuse. This PR consolidates the fast path by introducing a 'hotpath attenuator' that folds adjacent dequant/requant operations for INT8/FP8 fused kernels and pairs it with a windowed KV prefetcher that materializes likely KV ranges ahead of time for continuous-batching traffic. The goal is a measurable throughput improvement for mixed-precision models and steadier p95 latency under bursty arrival patterns.

What this change does (summary): - Adds a hotpath attenuation pass in the execution planner that detects foldable dequant/requant pairs and rewrites them into a single composite op with an optimized kernel hook. The composite op carries per-channel scale LUT references so we avoid repeated host-side scale transforms. - Implements windowed KV prefetcher in the scheduler: per-request predictions (small LRU-weighted histogram) select a KV window to prefetch into the local KV cache, reducing remote reads for repeated prefixes. The prefetcher is tunable per model via config flags (window_size, prefetch_threshold). - Adjusts continuous-batching heuristics: the batcher will now favor requests with high KV-affinity to improve kernel utilization while keeping latency SLOs via an adaptive deadline parameter. - Low-level kernel changes: new fused kernel path for INT8->accum->FP8 output that uses vectorized per-channel requant LUTs and a microkernel register tiling to reduce memory pressure. - Safety & compatibility: when foldability is ambiguous, we fall back to the original separate ops. Deprecated runtime flags are preserved, and model version pinning keeps behavior stable for previously pinned model configs.

Benchmark highlights (internal lab): - GPT-style 1B test: sustained throughput +22% (tokens/sec) when using INT8 fast path consolidated vs baseline dequant/requant pipeline. p50 latency: +1ms, p95: +2.8ms (within SLO for most customers). - Mixed precision FP8/INT8 workload: throughput +18% averaged across sequence lengths [64,512]. - KV-heavy conversational trace replay: median remote KV miss reduced by 63% with window_size=32 and prefetch_threshold=0.6. - Microbenchmarks: fused kernel shows 1.6x reduction in per-token memory traffic on representative layers.

Commits (high-level): - 1a2b3c4: add hotpath attenuator pass to planner and unit tests for fold detection - 2b3c4d5: implement windowed KV prefetcher + scheduler integration and config flags - 3c4d5e6: fused INT8->FP8 requant kernel and microkernel optimizations + benchmarks + docs - 4d5e6f7: end-to-end integration tests, CI fixes, and perf test harness updates

Files changed (high level): - src/runtime/planner/hotpath_attenuator.cc/.h - src/runtime/scheduler/windowed_prefetcher.cc/.h - src/runtime/kernel/fused_quant_kernels.cc - src/runtime/kernel/pc_lut_requant_microkernel.S - src/runtime/batcher/continuous_batcher.cc - integration_tests/perf/quant_hotpath_replay.yaml - docs/ops/quant_hotpath.md - tools/perf/bench_scripts/kv_prefetch_runner.py - ci/flake/adjust_timeouts.yml

Testing & CI: - Unit tests: new fold detection unit tests and negative cases added. - Integration tests: replay harness with representative conv traces. - Bench CI: added a synthetic bench that runs on the benchmark-lab infra and posts summary numbers to the PR. - CI result here initially failed one flaky test (quant_hotpath_unit::fold_detect_negative) on 2026-02-20; root cause was an edge-case when scale LUT has near-zero channels — added a guard and re-ran. Final CI status: pass.

Review conversation (high-level, chronological): - Marco Diaz (reviewer): "Nice consolidation. Two asks: (1) ensure the prefetcher respects VPC/zone-affinity to avoid cross-region prefetch costs, (2) add a small fuzz test to catch false-positive fold decisions." - Priya (author): "Added zone-affinity check and a new fuzz harness under integration_tests/ (commit 2b3c4d5). The fuzz will run in bench CI jobs and is feature-guarded behind PERF_DEBUG flag." - Ellen Park (reviewer): "Kernel looks good; microkernel naming and ABI change needs a changelog entry because downstream on-prem packaging uses symbol checks." - Priya: "Added symbol compatibility wrapper and a docs note in ops changelog." - Jordan Liu (reviewer): "Observed p95 regressions on a low-memory GPU profile in the perf runner. Can we add a fallback to the old path for devices with <8GB available?" - Priya: "Added runtime check to avoid fused path on devices with <8GB memory; the build includes that guard and tests pass. See commit 3c4d5e6." - Marco Diaz: "Approving after the device guard and VPC-affinity check. Verified bench numbers on benchmark-lab (run 2026-02-23)." - Ellen Park: "Approved. Left a docs nit which was addressed by author." - Merge: squash/merge performed after approvals and green CI.

Compatibility & rollout plan: - Feature is behind a runtime flag: quant_hotpath.enabled (default true on hosted for now). - Canary rollout: enable for 10% of requests for two weeks, with auto-rollback if p95 regression >5ms or token-error-rate increases. - Dedicated/Private: flag defaults to off; customers can opt-in via console or config. - Metrics to watch: quant.hotpath.fold_rate, kv.prefetch.hit_rate, batcher.affinity_score, p50/p95 latency per model, and token error rate.

Follow-ups & future work: - Expand fold detection to include weight-dropout cases (ENG-2021 follow-up). - Tune prefetcher machine-learned predictor (currently a lightweight histogram); plan an offline experiment to replace with a small predictor if stable. - Explore packing fused kernels for multi-layer fusion in next sprint.
Redesigned quantized hotpath: merges dequant/requant stages, adds windowed KV prefetcher, and scheduling heuristics for continuous batching. Improves throughput for INT8/FP8 mixed workloads with minimal p95 latency impact. Backwards-compatible with existing quantized model profiles.
benchmarks/gpt1b: +22% tokens/sec; mixed-precision: +18%; KV miss rate on conv traces: -63% with window_size=32; fused kernel reduces per-token memory traffic by ~1.6x

Motivation: We need a lightweight, centralized way to run staged model rollouts (canary/A-B/shadow) that supports: weighted traffic-splitting, programmable health gates (latency, error-rate, regressed quality), synthetic traffic injection for validation, and deterministic automated rollback hooks. This PR implements a server-side traffic-splitting plugin and a generic rollback hook framework so rollout policies can declare health gates that trigger an automated rollback and post-mortem ticket creation.

What this changes (high level):
- New runtime plugin: pkg/rollout/plugin/traffic_split.go (weighted routing at request-proxy layer, supports fractional weights, priority fallbacks)
- Health gating infra: pkg/rollout/health/gates.go (pluggable gate types: latency_p95, error_rate, eval-regression)
- Rollback hooks: pkg/rollout/hooks/rollback.go + integrations with notifications and Linear (minimal adapter)
- Synthetic traffic generator: tools/trafficgen/canary_driver.go (replay and synthetic workload profiles for SLA validation)
- Console: console/src/routes/rollouts/preview.tsx to show split ratios and real-time gate metrics
- Tests and CI: integration tests for canary path, unit tests for plugin and hooks, e2e smoke for Console view

Checklist: 
- [x] Traffic-splitting plugin implementation + unit tests
- [x] Health gate API and a latency/error_rate gate impl
- [x] Rollback hook framework + Linear adapter (no credentials shipped)
- [x] Synthetic traffic generator and CI integration test
- [x] Console display for rollouts and gate metrics
- [x] Docs: docs/runbooks/rollouts.md with new failure scenarios and runbook steps

Backward compatibility: The traffic-splitting plugin registers as an optional runtime plugin. Existing rollout policies that do not opt-in retain current behavior. No wire-level API changes to the public Redwood API; rollout configuration is an internal service-level extension.

Performance notes: The routing path is optimized for the common fast-path: when weight=100% it compiles to a direct forward (no additional allocations). Fractional traffic uses a consistent-hash + token-bucket approach to maintain session stickiness without per-request storage. Benchmarks in benchmark-lab show median additional latency <0.6ms on our internal perf-canary for 128-byte payloads.

Testing summary (CI):
- unit-tests: pass
- lint: pass
- integration/canary: initially failed due to a race in synthetic driver; fixed by introducing deterministic seeding and re-run -> pass
- e2e/console: pass on first run

Rollout and merge plan: After review and sign-off we merged via squash. The feature is gated behind a feature flag (rollout.traffic_split.enabled) and a default policy that is off for existing customers. We will enable only for internal canaries in the next week and progressively for beta tenants.

Related work: ENG-4921 (unified rollout requirements), PM-128 (product acceptance criteria), previous experiments in perf-canary for staged traffic (see pr refs in runbook).

Notes for reviewers: Pay attention to the gates.go API boundary — it's intentionally minimal to avoid coupling eval infra. The rollback hook intentionally emits a compact JSON payload to the Linear adapter; teams wanting richer context should extend the adapter (small example in docs/runbooks/rollouts.md).

Merge outcome: merged to main via squash on 2026-02-15 after approvals from Ethan and Sofia and a green CI run.

Ethan Rivera: Can the traffic-split logic guarantee per-session stickiness across autoscaling events?
Priya Nair: Yes — we use consistent-hash by session id and include node affinity token; when nodes are rescheduled we fall back to weighted reassign which is rare and documented. Added comments and a test for deterministic reassign.
Sofia Martinez: Are gate thresholds configurable per-tenant?
Priya Nair: Yes, gates are per-rollout config and we expose them in the console; the default system policy used by internal canaries is conservative.
Benji Kline: The Linear adapter includes only a summary — will we ever need full request traces?
Priya Nair: We decided to keep the adapter small to avoid leaking PII in tickets. There is an opt-in trace dump hook for support-driven escalations (disabled by default).
Sofia Martinez: Approved after addressing CI flake and adding docs.
Ethan Rivera: Approved after minor comments and bench numbers added to the PR description.

payload.body:
Motivation: high tail-latency investigation showed disproportionate CPU time spent in request path serialization, repeated allocations, and frequent epoll/syscall handoffs from per-socket queues. This PR consolidates socket IO queue management into a small number of shared, per-NUMA event loops and replaces the heavy ad-hoc serializer with a lightweight span-based serializer to minimize copying and allocations. Approach: 1) Introduce io/event_loop_shard.{h,cc} that groups sockets by a fast hash (socket id -> shard) and processes batched readiness events using a batched epoll/poll loop. This reduces syscall frequency by coalescing readiness handling and amortizing lock acquisition across batches. 2) Replace the prior RequestMarshaller with SpanSerializer, a zero-allocation view-based serializer that composes IO frames by referencing buffer slices and only materializes a single contiguous frame when the network path requires it. SpanSerializer supports in-place KV-cache witness pointers so cached prefixes can be forwarded without copy. 3) Move blocking disk/metrics flushing out of the event loop into a bounded async worker pool with backpressure hooks; event loops now only run non-blocking tasks and lightweight admission control for continuous batching. 4) Scheduler changes: reduced size of the global CPU worker pool and enable local work-stealing between per-socket shards to reduce cross-thread wakeups; removed most explicit thread pinning in favor of shard affinity hints that let the OS schedule while preserving NUMA locality. 5) Compatibility: kept public API and RPC wire formats unchanged; added feature-flag to toggle SpanSerializer at runtime for staged rollout. Testing and validation: microbenchmarks show 18-28% reduction in median CPU cycles/request on our standard chat workload and 22% improvement in 95th percentile latency under synthetic burst traffic. End-to-end canary on staging for 72h with production-like queries (including embeddings and streaming) showed no increase in error rate and a 6% reduction in token-cost due to fewer retries. Rollout plan: enable feature-flag in dedicated clusters for low-traffic customers, monitor per-route latency/cpu and KV-cache hit metrics in Console dashboards, then progressively enable for higher throughput pools. Caveats: the new event loop sharding introduces a small (<1%) CPU overhead for very low-concurrency single-connection scenarios due to batching window; also some kernel versions show different epoll semantics so we included a fallback to existing per-socket loop. Related work: builds on continuous-batching changes from ENG-3890 and addresses follow-ups from PRs that attempted to decouple serialization from affinity (see linked PRs). Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for SpanSerializer and event loop shards - [x] Integration tests with KV cache and streaming enabled - [x] Performance regression tests added to benchmark-lab - [x] Feature-flag + rollout doc added in docs/ops/feature-flags.md
Miguel Torres: Nice end-to-end numbers. Two things: can we avoid the extra memcpy when network driver already accepts scatter-gather? Consider adding an iovec path.
Aisha Patel: Good point — added an iovec fast-path in SpanSerializer and a test to verify zero-copy to sendmsg. See span_serializer.cc + tests.
Liang Chen: The worker_pool reduction looked risky for high core counts. Did you test with colocated workloads? I want to see results with mixed short/long sequences.
Aisha Patel: Ran mixed-load perf on perf-canary (2x cpu and 4x small/large sequences); results included in bench outputs show stable throughput and improved tail latency. Added notes to benchmark output directory.
Sofia Martinez: Please make sure the feature flag can be toggled per-cluster. Also add guard rails for kernel versions with known epoll behavioral differences.
Aisha Patel: Feature-flag is per-deployment and we added a kernel-version check with a documented fallback to the previous per-socket loop in event_loop_shard.cc.
4 commits: initial io shard scaffolding and tests; span serializer prototype; integrate span serializer into request path; cleanup, tests, and feature-flag wiring. Commits are small and focused with test coverage and perf harness additions.
Merged via squash-merge after approvals from Miguel and Liang and green CI. No conflicts with main. Deployed to staging as feature-flag off; feature toggled on for canary clusters immediately after merge.
Reduce CPU copies in request path by introducing SpanSerializer and consolidating socket IO into NUMA-aware event loop shards. Improves median CPU per request and tail latency for bursty traffic. Rollout behind a feature flag. See ENG-4121 for benchmarks and canary results.
If increased request timeouts are observed after enabling the flag, check event_loop_shard metrics (batch_size, epoll_syscalls) and kv_cache prefix forwarding counters. Fallback: toggle feature-flag off to revert to previous marshaller and per-socket loops.
payload.title: Consolidate socket IO queues and introduce lightweight span serializer to reduce CPU path copies

Context: Long-tail token/sequence shapes cause disproportionate cost and SLO churn but are rare, so sampling needs to be both precise and cheap. This PR implements a lightweight 'needle' sampler that: 1) continuously scores incoming invocations by sequence-shape rarity and observed per-token cost, 2) escalates sampling probability for invocations with anomalous kernel latency patterns, and 3) records a compact backchain representation (kernel-ID -> queued-duration -> phase-breakdown) to a new trace index. Goal: improve signal-to-noise for operators and SREs while keeping telemetry egress and query costs low.

What this PR does (single-pass summary): Adds a new sampling pipeline (redwood/observability/needle_sampler.rs) with a pluggable scoring function, a compact on-disk backchain indexer (redwood/observability/trace_index/compact_indexer.py) that stores backchains as deduplicated shards, a token-cost correlator service (redwood/telemetry/token_cost_correlator.py) that joins sampled traces with token-cost rollups, and dashboard panels (telemetry/dashboards/needle_sampling.panel.json) to visualize sequence-shape index, sampled backchains, and top-correlated kernels. Also updates the Python SDK telemetry hooks (sdk/python/redwood/telemetry.py) to expose the lightweight sampling header and a feature-flag gating mechanism.

Design notes: - Needle sampler design chooses ~0.1% baseline sampling and applies multiplicative boosts for rare sequence-shapes (low-frequency n-gram fingerprint) and multi-phase kernel stalls. The scoring function is configurable via runtime flags and tuned to avoid skewing production SLOs. - Backchain index is intentionally compact: we store a shingled lineage of kernel IDs + phase durations (at 1ms resolution) instead of full spans to reduce storage and query costs. Reconstruction code can hydrate the full span when needed. - Correlator computes Spearman correlations between per-token cost vectors and kernel-phase latencies across sampled population and produces ranked kernel suspects for pull-through investigation.

Rollout plan: Feature-flagged under telemetry.experimental.needle_sampling. Start in staging for 48h synthetic replay, then opt-in to 5% production traffic for 72h with perf counters monitored. If CPU/ingest cost exceeds budget, the default sampling rate will be cut in half. Full rollout requires a follow-up migration doc to add long-term retention policy for the compact index.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for the score function and indexer included; an integration test (tests/integration/test_needle_sampling.py) replays historical traces and validates backchain reconstruction fidelity. Load test in perf-lab shows sampling adds <0.6% p99 latency and ~3% telemetry ingest increase at 5% traffic. CI: one flaky e2e in SDK telemetry hook was fixed in an additional commit.

Operational impacts and runbook: - New telemetry metric: telemetry.needle.sampled_invocations (counter) and telemetry.needle.correlator_jobs (gauge). - Add an alert: needle-sampler-ingest-surge if sampled_invocations > expected_rate * 1.8 for 30m. - Dashboard includes an "Investigate" link that opens a compact backchain viewer and pre-populates a kernel suspect list.

Related work: ENG-2984 (observability long-tail projects), SUP-1123 (customer incident pointing to kernel phase stalls).
Marco Li: Nice direction — can we make the sampling caps configurable per-tenant? I'm worried about multitenant hotspots.
Anika Rao (author): Good point; added tenant_cap argument and a default 10x cap in the config. See compact_indexer.py config block.
Priya Singh: Please add a feature-flag kill switch in the feature rollout section and ensure the dashboard panels gracefully handle zero data.
Anika Rao (author): Added telemetry.experimental.needle_sampling.disable flag and panel fallbacks. Also added unit test for empty-index rendering.
James O'Neill: The correlator's Spearman computation could be expensive at scale; suggest a streaming approximate quantile join instead of full-sort grouping.
Anika Rao (author): Swapped to an incremental rank-approximation with reservoir sketching for large cohorts (see token_cost_correlator.py commit). Reduced memory by ~40% in perf tests.
QA (Sophie Tan): Integration tests passed in staging; ran a 48h synthetic replay, no SLO violations observed.
Ops (Ravi Patel): Approved rollout. Added runbook snippet under docs/observability/needle_sampling.md.
Adds a low-overhead "needle" sampling mode that prioritizes rare token sequences and long-tail kernel backtraces; introduces a compact trace backchain index and dashboard panels for correlating token-level cost with kernel execution paths; rollout behind feature flag; non-breaking.
