payload.body:
Motivation: customer integrations observed intermittent incompatibilities when using Redwood's OpenAI-compat endpoint for /v1/chat.completions. Problems included (1) callers sending stop as a single string vs array, (2) streaming chunks that split token-level logprobs causing consumers to miss logprob metadata, and (3) inconsistent placement/framing of function/tool-call payloads in the stream. This PR converges the compatibility surface so integrations get deterministic envelopes for tooling and logprobs, and normalizes params for easier client code.

Scope and approach: - Normalize incoming `stop` to an ordered array early in request validation and propagate canonical stop semantics into runtime routing. - Introduce a compact "stream-envelope" framing for ephemeral streaming events: {type, data, meta} where type in [delta, logprob, function_call_start, function_call_end, done]. Implementation keeps human readable JSON per-chunk but adds a single-char prefix for alignment detection to help clients resync on partial TCP chunks. - Ensure token-level logprobs are emitted as discrete logprob events whenever a KV-cache flush or chunk boundary would otherwise split values; this avoids partial-token loss. - Formalize function/tool call handshake: emit function_call_start with provisional metadata, stream tool outputs as delta events, then emit function_call_end with final structured payload. - Maintain backward compatibility for simple consumers: if client requests legacy framing (compat_mode: legacy), the server will still emit plain-delta chunks for text only responses.

Checklist: - [x] normalize stop param and add unit tests - [x] add streaming envelope encoder/decoder - [x] add e2e tests simulating chunk boundary splits - [x] add SDK parser update (TS) and docs - [x] perf smoke test on dedicated pool - [x] audit and update observability traces/metrics

Related work: ENG-1189 (streaming resilience), ENG-1212 (openai-compat parity), incident SUP-8721 referenced a customer outage.

Implementation notes: commits implement a small deterministic prefix ("~\n") per payload to help the client locate JSON boundaries after network partial reads; we debated binary framing but decided on a minimal ASCII prefix to preserve existing text-streaming client simplicity. The canonical stop normalization is applied in packages/redwood-api/src/inputValidation.ts and packages/openai-compat/src/paramNormalizer.ts. The streaming envelope lives in packages/openai-compat/src/streamingEnvelope.ts and the runtime emitter uses runtime/stream-router to decide when to break and emit logprob events.

Tests: unit tests cover normalizations and envelope conformance; e2e covers canary rollout using a dedicated test pool with artificially delayed TCP chunks to reproduce splits.

Rollout plan: merged to main, canary on dedicated cluster (10% traffic) for 48h, metrics to watch: stream-fragment-recover-rate, function-call-missing, avg-latency-95.

Backwards compatibility: legacy consumers unaffected; new behavior is opt-out via compat_mode=legacy if downstream parsing cannot be upgraded.

Documentation: updated docs/openai-compat.md with examples for new envelope and SDK change notes.

CI notes: initial CI run failed a flaky e2e test (chat-stream.spec.ts) which was fixed by increasing the TCP chunk jitter simulation timeout; final run passed.
Stabilizes OpenAI /v1/chat.completions streaming behavior: normalizes stop to an array, guarantees logprob envelope is emitted consistently during partial streaming, and wraps function/tool call metadata in a stable event envelope. Backwards-compatible: legacy single-string stop values accepted and normalized. Fixes several edge cases where streaming chunks split token logprobs or omitted final function call payload.
Marco Alvarez: Left a couple nits on naming and suggested a smaller prefix token ("~") to reduce parser overhead.
Leah Park: replied that we chose a two-char prefix ("~\n") to improve cross-language line-oriented readers; added comment in streamingEnvelope.ts
Jinsoo Kim: requested stronger unit tests around an edge case where stop=[] and user-provided model adds EOS tokens; asked for explicit regression test
Leah Park: added regression unit test and noted it in the commits, addressed comment
Renee Castillo: ran canary on staging and reported no increase in 95th latency; approved
Marco Alvarez: approved with minor comments
payload.title: chat-compat: resilient streaming chunking, stop-array normalization, and tool-call metadata envelope

Motivation: Product teams need a single, efficient query surface to discover model capabilities and runtime hints that drive API behavior (streaming vs non-streaming, structured-output templates, function-calling profiles and per-model pricing/limits). This PR adds a new endpoint /v1/model_catalog/capabilities_query that returns a normalized capability document for each model and expands the model index with structured-output and function_calling profiles plus optional per-route pricing hints. The change is designed to be backward-compatible with the existing /v1/models listing and the OpenAI compatibility shim.

What this PR does: Adds a query-focused catalog endpoint that accepts flexible filters (capability flags, max_sequence, supports_streaming, openai_compat_level) and returns a compact capability payload. Introduces two first-class capability families: structured_output_profiles (named templates + JSONSchema hints + stability score) and function_calling_profiles (preferred calling semantics, argument mapping, and failure_fallback policies). Adds a pricing_limits field (per-1000-token cost_hint and soft_rate_limit) to model entries to aid routing/costing decisions at the gateway. Updates the OpenAI shim to map compatibility_level -> openai_deprecation_hints so older clients get migration guidance. Includes tests, docs, and console list adjustments to surface the new query filters.

Compatibility and migration: Existing consumers of /v1/models are unaffected. The new endpoint is additive. The OpenAI shim will continue to expose the current compatibility flags but now emits an additional deprecation hint if a model's openai_compat_level is below the requested threshold. Operators should review release notes for telemetry changes: new metrics were added (catalog.query.latency, catalog.query.result_size, catalog.query.filtered_count).

Checklist:
- [x] API endpoint implementation server-side (HTTP + SDK bindings)
- [x] OpenAPI/SDK docs updated
- [x] Unit and integration tests for filtering and profile shapes
- [x] Console UI: add capability filter and pricing column
- [x] Migration notes and telemetry added

Rollout plan: Feature-gated via feature_flag:capabilities_query. Default off for Dedicated customers in the initial rollout window; enabled in hosted after 72-hour dark-traffic validation.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps profile schemas minimal (string identifiers + lightweight JSONSchema references) to avoid inflating catalog payloads; future work (ENG-2089) will add a cached profile store for richer profiles.
Camila Ortiz: Can you clarify the expected payload size for the structured_output_profiles array? We need to ensure gateway caching remains reasonable.
Jordan Lee: We only include profile identifiers and a tiny stability_score by default. Full schema references are stored as URIs; payloads are intentionally compact. Added note in docs.
Evan Zhang: The OpenAI shim change seems fine, but please add an explicit unit test that validates the deprecation_hint is present when compat_level < requested.
Jordan Lee: Added test_openai_shim.py::test_deprecation_hint_for_legacy_compat.
Maya Thompson: Lint flagged a missing type annotation in catalog.go; please fix before merge.
Jordan Lee: Fixed and pushed. CI green.
Added a new /v1/model_catalog/capabilities_query endpoint to fetch compact capability documents. Models now enumerate structured_output_profiles and function_calling_profiles and expose pricing_limits hints to help routing and cost estimation. OpenAI compatibility shim now emits deprecation hints for low compatibility models. This is an additive change and is feature-flagged.
Add capability-focused query API and enrich model entries with structured output/function profiles plus pricing hints to improve routing, OpenAI compatibility guidance, and UI discoverability.

Motivation: customers building on the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions surface reported subtle incompatibilities around parameter aliases (role hints, presence/temperature mappings), inconsistent stop-array handling in streaming mode, and missing logprob fallbacks when models were served by variant kernels. This PR implements a lightweight compatibility shim that (1) translates incoming v1 parameters into Redwood's internal serving config deterministically, (2) normalizes role aliases and enforces role ordering preservation, (3) coalesces stop token arrays and applies a deterministic stop prioritization for stream fragments, (4) provides a graceful logprob fallback path for quantized/approx kernels, and (5) hardens the stream coordinator's backpressure and resume handshake for tool/function call fragments to reduce dropped fncall payloads.

What this changes (high level): translated-params: a small param-mapping layer that accepts OpenAI-style fields (temperature, top_p, presence_penalty aliases, role hints) and emits a canonical Redwood inference config; role normalization: map common role aliases (assistant/bot/system => standardized role tags) while preserving user-provided metadata fields; stop handling: merge duplicate/overlapping stop arrays and attach a compact stop index to fragments so the stream reconciler deterministically decides cutpoints; logprob path: when the fast kernel cannot produce token-level logprobs we synthesize a lightweight fallback by using the approximate scorer and mark the token with a provenance field so downstream tooling can opt out; stream coordinator: introduce a small datagram ACK and a resume token for fncall fragments so tool outputs spanning multiple stream chunks are reassembled without duplication on transient reconnects; structured output shaping: add a permissive JSON-sanitizer that attempts to coerce obvious single-object responses into valid JSON while preserving raw-text fallthrough.

Commits (summary): - 7b3f2a1 add param-mapping layer and unit tests for alias permutations - f9c4d27 implement stop-array coalescer and deterministic stop indexer - a11e0d3 add logprob fallback shim and provenance tagging - c3d9ee5 stream coordinator: backpressure ACK/resume token and integration tests - d7b44bf structured-output sanitizer and docs examples - e2f6a5c update python/ts SDK proxied examples and compatibility note

Files changed (high level): src/compat/v1_chat_shim.py (new): param translation, role normalization, stop coalescer; runtime/stream/coordinator.go (mod): ACK/resume token, backpressure tuning; runtime/inference/logprob_fallback.go (new): approximate scorer fallback path; sdk/python/openai_proxy.py (mod): proxy entrypoint and examples; docs/openai_compat.md (mod): compatibility guide and migration notes; tests/integration/test_v1_chat_compat.py (new): end-to-end scenarios including toolcall fragmentation; webui/playground/compat_demo.json (new): example prompts for QA.

Testing and CI: local unit and integration test suite expanded. CI status: build: pass, unit: pass, integration: flaky@first-run (tests/integration/test_v1_chat_compat.py retried once and passed), lint: pass, e2e-demo-deploy: pass. We exercised the shim against a small matrix of model variants (fp16, int8-approx, kv-cache-optimized) and confirmed behavior parity for the canonical prompts in docs/openai_compat.md.

Review thread (high level): Priya Kapoor requested clearer guarantees around stop priority and asked for an explicit note about non-deterministic stop resolution when model tokenization boundaries overlap. Author reply: added deterministic stop indexer and documented the caveat in docs/openai_compat.md. Priya approved after documentation update. Ethan Brooks raised perf concerns about added branching in hot path (param mapping per-request). Author reply: moved the hot mapping into a lightweight fast-path (frozen mapping table) and added microbenchmarks showing <1% p99 latency delta at 128 concurrency. Ethan requested a benchmark artifact; artifact uploaded and linked. Ethan approved. Sofia Martinez asked for more robust resume semantics for tool fragments (edge cases with reconnects and partial writes). Author reply: added resume token, ACK semantics, and an integration test that simulates reconnects; Sofia approved with one minor nit fix (renamed resume_token -> stream_resume_token) which is included.

Risk and rollout plan: This PR is behind a feature flag (compat.v1_chat_shim) enabled for internal staging and opt-in for early access customers. Gradual rollout: stage -> canary -> 10% prod -> 100% over 7 days with close monitoring (latency, error-rate, mismatch-rate against golden responses). We added metrics for: compat.param_map_rate, compat.stop_coalesce_count, compat.logprob_fallback_rate, stream.resume_retries. No breaking changes expected; default behavior remains unchanged unless the feature flag is enabled.

Notes and follow-ups: Add an opt-out header for customers who prefer strict legacy behavior; follow-up ticket ENG-8523 created to add RBAC guard for the shim in Private deployments. Also plan a small docs addendum showing how to interpret provenance-tagged logprobs in the Console.

Merge: squashed and merged to main after approvals and green CI. Merge commit references the Linear tasks ENG-8421 and ENG-8437.
Backfills OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity for params, roles, stop arrays, and logprob fallback; improves stream backpressure handling and toolcall handshake resiliency; no user-facing breaking changes expected.
Priya: Please clarify stop prioritization and document tokenizer overlap caveat.
Diego: Added deterministic stop indexer and docs note; PTAL.
Ethan: Concern about hot-path perf; can we keep mapping fast?
Sofia: Please add reconnect simulation to integration tests; thanks.

Motivation: long-tail SLO incidents are often caused by correlated micro-patterns across invocation phases and noisy long-lived logs; debugging requires quick aggregation of signal fragments plus compact log summaries. This PR introduces a signal-mosaic aggregator that coalesces per-invocation phase metrics (queue, kernel, kv-cache, token-emit) into a compact multi-dimensional histogram plus an anchored log-summary component that extracts representative log snippets tied to signal spikes. Changes include: 1) signal_mosaic engine that computes per-invocation phase histograms and an outlier fingerprint; 2) anchored-log-summaries module that uses reservoir sampling combined with entropy scoring to pick representative logs for an invocation cohort; 3) new Grafana dashboard panels (mosaic sparkline + log-anchors panel) and a lightweight alert rule that triggers a short-lived debug collection; 4) unit and integration tests plus docs and examples. Checklist: - Implement core aggregator and summarizer; - Add dashboard JSON and display config; - Add alerting rule and feature flag (obs.signal_mosaic.enabled); - Add tests and CI validation; - Add runbook snippet in docs. Links: Linear ENG-2743 for design notes; support ticket SUP-588 for an incident that motivated this work. Backwards compatibility: feature gated; default off for all customers. Rollout plan: enable behind feature flag, canary to internal tenants, monitor cost and storage impact for 48h, then broad enable if no regression.
Lena Huang: overall looks good, please add a short privacy/security blurb about log anchoring persistence; consider truncating PII in anchored logs.
Asha Patel: added a redaction step in anchored_log_summaries and added tests to validate anonymization.
Omar Aziz: can we add a metric for sample-reservoir-evictions so we can track memory churn? consider exposing as a gauge.
Asha Patel: added reservoir_evictions_total gauge and increment at eviction site; included in dashboard as small counter.
Priya Nair: alert rule looks noisy by default; suggest adding a debounce window and requiring two consecutive windows before runbook triggers.
Asha Patel: updated alert rule to require 2/3 windows and added a feature flag for debug-collection to be enabled only for canary tenants.
Lena Huang: approving after minor docs tweak.
Add invocation signal mosaic aggregator and anchored log summaries behind a feature flag. Includes new Grafana panels and a debug alert that collects short-lived traces and log anchors for SLO investigation. Default off; rollout to internal canary tenants for 48h before wider enablement.
If the new alert floods, flip feature flag obs.signal_mosaic.enabled=false and disable alerting rule alerting/rules/signal_mosaic_debug.yaml. Watch for reservoir_evictions_total spikes indicating memory pressure; if observed, reduce reservoir size via config telemetry.signal_mosaic.reservoir_size.
payload.title: Introduce invocation-signal mosaic and anchored log summaries for long-tail SLO debugging

payload.body:
Motivation: reduce tail latency and peak memory pressure for high-concurrency, small-batch serving scenarios by (1) fusing QKV interleave + concat followed by a single reduction kernel to avoid extra device memory transposes, (2) applying rotary/rope positional transforms as an inline fused op (preapply) to remove an extra KV write/read, and (3) introducing a light-weight KV-prefetch policy in the continuous-batching scheduler to warm slab cache for hot prefixes. This PR implements a new CUDA kernel suite (attn_interleave_fused_reduction.cu/h), runtime hooks, and scheduler policy flags.

Changes included: checklist: - [x] new interleaved QKV concat + fused reduction kernel with half-float/INT8-friendly paths - [x] fused rotary/rope preapply (optional per-model flag) to avoid a separate rotary kernel pass - [x] KV-prefetch scheduler strategy that issues async prefetches for hot route prefixes when batch size < target but concurrency high - [x] unit tests for kernel correctness (QK normalization, softmax numerics, gradient parity in training-mode builds) - [x] integration tests in the runtime CPU/GPU CI matrix - [x] perf harness and microbenchmarks committed under benchmark-lab/attn-prefetch/ - [x] documented runtime config flags and migration notes in CHANGELOG and docs snippet - [x] rollout plan with canary percentage and automatic rollback on p95 latency regression > 10%

Design notes: We observed two key overheads in microbenchmarks for 1-4 token sequences at batch sizes 1-8 and high concurrency: (A) extra global memory transposes between Q,K,V layouts; (B) repeated rotary application that materializes KV and causes eviction pressure. The new interleaved kernel accepts packed QKV (interleaved along head dim) and computes attention reductions in-place producing output without an intermediate full shuffle. The fused rotary preapply accepts rotary parameters and applies them to Q/K lanes in the same kernel launch; this is gated by model metadata so models without rotary/rope skip the path. Kernel implements numerically-stable scaled softmax and supports autoregressive KV-caching via an optional stream that writes into the slab cache with write-combining hints.

Scheduler change: introduce scheduler flag continuous_batcher.prefetch_policy with options [off, heuristic, aggressive]. Heuristic mode issues prefetches when observed reuse heatmap for prefix route > 0.6 and concurrency > 16; aggressive warms if p50 latency > target SLO and memory headroom available. Prefetches are issued with a low-priority CUDA stream to avoid head-of-line contention. Backpressure: prefetch is canceled if runtime memory estimator signals > 85% reserved.

Benchmarks: microbench harness (bench/attn_small_seq.py) results on p4d-like instance: - baseline (main): p50=10.8ms, p95=34.2ms, tokens/sec=5.6k - this PR (heuristic prefetch, fused kernels): p50=7.1ms (-34%), p95=20.9ms (-39%), tokens/sec=7.8k (+39%) for 1-4 token sequences, batch sizes 1-4. For larger sequences (>256) and large batch sizes, difference is neutral (+/-2%) indicating no regression on standard throughput paths. Memory: peak device allocation decreased ~18% on average for small-batch workloads.

Compatibility and flags: The new kernels are feature-gated. Default rollout: feature disabled by default; enabled via runtime config attn_fusion.enabled=true and per-model catalog flag model_config.attn.fusion=auto. We provide two modes: fast-path (fused rotary preapply + fused reduction) and compatibility-path (concat interleave only). Models can be pinned to either. No change to public API.

Testing and validation: added unit tests for numerical parity against baseline single-head reference, long-run stability test (24h concurrency emulation), and a memory-leak smoke test. CI initially failed due to a missing device sync in the prefetch cancellation path; fixed and re-ran. Load-test canary at 5% traffic for three hours showed stable p95 improvements and no error spike.

Rollout plan: 1) merge to main behind feature flag, 2) enable on staging for dominated low-latency routes (messaging/chat), 3) 5% canary production for 3h, 4) 25% if metrics stable, 5) global if no regression after 24h. Automatic rollback rule: if p95 increases >10% or error-rate increases >0.1% relative.

Notes: This PR focuses on serving runtime; training kernels are untouched. Added comments in attn_interleave_fused_reduction.cu about vectorization choices and fallback heuristics for non-contiguous QKV layouts. Potential follow-ups: integrate per-head quantization-aware reduction, extend prefetch heatmap to persistent ML model predictions of prefix reuse, and explore fused dispatch for multi-query attention in transformer-decoder-lite variants.
Marco Chen: Nice work on the kernel. A few nitpicks on register pressure and unrolling. Please add a fallback for non-native layout; see inline.
Eleanor Briggs: Added layout fallback path and comments explaining tradeoffs; kept fast-path register allocation after microbenching.
Priya Raman: Scheduler looks good but the 0.6 heatmap threshold should be configurable via runtime flag. Also add telemetry for canceled prefetches.
Eleanor Briggs: Exposed heatmap threshold as continuous_batcher.heatmap_threshold and added telemetry event prefetch.canceled + reason tags.
Samir Patel: CI failure reproduced locally; good catch on missing device synchronize. Approving after fix.
Samir Patel: APPROVED
Introduce interleaved QKV fused-reduction kernel and optional fused rotary preapply to improve small-batch latency and reduce memory pressure; add KV-prefetch scheduler policy to warm slab cache for hot prefixes. Feature gated; off by default. See docs/perf/attn_fusion.md for configuration and rollout guidance.
payload.title: add interleaved-qkv concat + fused-reduction kernel with rotary preapply and kv-prefetch scheduler

payload.body:
Motivation: production workloads saw uneven gains from the INT8/FP8 serving paths due to two related problems: 1) dequantization happening as a separate op after KV cache materialization created memory traffic and prevented kernel fusion, and 2) scheduling decisions did not account for quantization alignment in the KV cache which caused small but frequent parity fallbacks to FP16 that kill tail latency.

This PR introduces a new vectorized dequant-fusion operator and scheduler hints to: (a) consume quantized KV cache entries in-place, apply per-head smoothing/scale adjustments (smoothquant-inspired), and emit requantized activations fused with the attention microkernel; (b) align continuous batching decisions to prefer grouping requests with compatible quant metadata (scale/zero point/signature) so kernels can be reused across microbatches; (c) add a conservative FP8 compatibility check and graceful fallback threshold to avoid correctness regressions.

High level changes: new native kernels (C++/CUDA) for fused vectorized dequant+requant, scheduler heuristics in the runtime planner, KV cache metadata extension (small 16B signature per cache entry), continuous-batcher grouping changes, benchmark harness updates, and unit+integration tests.

Checklist:
- [x] microkernel implementation and CPU fallback
- [x] runtime scheduler integration and policy flag (runtime.quant_kv_alignment=true)
- [x] perf benches (see commits)
- [x] unit + integration tests
- [x] canary perf rollout config
- [x] docs note in optimization guide

Related: ENG-14234 (quant roadmap), SUP-7321 (customer incident describing FP16 fallbacks)
Marco: Can you share numbers for seq_len=1024 and batch sizes 1/4/8 on A100? Also how does this behave for causal vs non-causal attention?
Aisha: Benchmarks attached; see ci artifact perf/quant-bench-20250212.csv. For causal attention we reuse the same fused path; non-causal saw ~3% extra memory traffic due to padding but still benefits.
Samantha: Is the KV signature guaranteed stable across model sharding and checkpoint loading? Potential mismatch could cause silent correctness issues.
Aisha: KV signature is derived from the model-scale vector and quant config saved into the checkpoint header; added tests to validate reload and mismatch triggers conservative FP16 fallback.
Ethan: CI regression on nightly showed a nondeterministic failure in test_quant_kv_alignment on CPU fallback; reproducer?
Aisha: Found a race in the cache GC path exposed by the new metadata access, fixed with a lightweight RCU guard and added deterministic ordering in test. Follow-up commit added.

Context: We have several compatibility edge cases when bridging OpenAI-style function/tool-calling into Redwood's native invoke pipeline. Two concrete problems surfaced in customer integrations: 1) clients sending tool schemas with inconsistent property annotations (e.g., nested 'required' declared both on object and individual properties) which causes downstream schema resolution to fail, and 2) long-running fragment coalescing during streaming function/tool handoffs can cause client-side timeouts. This PR introduces: 1) a tool schema normalization pass (v3) that canonicalizes required/nullable/enum annotations, flattens aliasing for common types, and preserves vendor extensions in a provenance header; 2) a runtime-safe streaming "heartbeat" envelope injected between fragments when coalescing is delayed beyond the configured fragment window, keeping HTTP/WS clients alive without leaking semantic tokens; 3) an opt-in OpenAI compatibility header OpenAI-Compat: tool-schema=v3 that triggers the normalization shim; 4) telemetry tags on tool_choice decisions to measure how often schema normalization changes selection order. Migration plan: default remains v2; we enable v3 behind the header and a feature flag controlled by Canary routing. Rollback: toggle the feature flag or remove the header for callers. Tests: unit schema normalization tests, integration test that simulates slow fragments and validates heartbeat frames, and an e2e compatibility test with the openai-compat adapter. Implementation notes: normalization is conservative (no aggressive coercion), we add a stable mapping table for common aliases (int -> integer, str -> string, date-time -> string(format=date-time)), and a deterministic tool_choice tie-breaker that leverages schema specificity score + provenance weight. See related Linear items ENG-2981, ENG-3034. Checklist: [x] normalization pass implemented [x] streaming heartbeat implemented [x] unit + integration tests [x] docs updated [x] canary rollout configured
Ethan Cole: Nit - can we rename 'heartbeat' -> 'ping-envelope' in code to avoid confusion with internal health checks? Priya: replied that heartbeat is already used in public docs for streaming keepalive and changing would be a bigger docs surgery; left as-is.
Maya Thompson: Request changes - normalization should not strip vendor extensions (x-*) from schema. Priya: updated implementation to copy vendor extensions into a provenance.header and added tests to assert they are preserved.
Luca Rinaldi: Concern about adding load under high QPS for the normalization pass. Priya: added micro-benchmarks (2x 1k req/s baseline) and an optional cache layer keyed by schema fingerprint; cache hits are expected to cover 70% of production traffic.
CI bot: integration pipeline flake on first run (timeout on test_stream_heartbeat). Priya: increased test timeout and added deterministic timing injection for the coalescer; CI passed on re-run.
Adds OpenAI-Compat tool-schema v3 normalization and streaming heartbeat to avoid client timeouts during fragment coalescing. Opt-in via header OpenAI-Compat: tool-schema=v3. Improves tool_choice determinism and preserves vendor schema extensions in provenance metadata.
Performance: normalization introduces ~0.6ms median overhead on cold schema paths before caching. Telemetry: new tags openai_compat_schema_version and tool_choice_provenance added to choice metrics. Observability: dashboards updated under Observability > OpenAI-Compat.

Summary: Implement a selective fallback policy plus a dynamic precision toggle and scheduler heuristics that route only high-risk requests to conservative kernels while keeping the fast kernels for the common case. This reduces 99th percentile latency for interactive routes without broadly sacrificing throughput or eviction correctness.

Motivation: The existing fallback-on-every-error approach is too conservative for many interactive workloads. We observed that a small fraction of sequences trigger correctness guards and force slow kernels for all concurrent work on the same worker, causing tail latency amplification. This PR introduces heuristics that: 1) identify high-risk requests at admission time, 2) apply safe-mode kernels only to those requests, and 3) allow other requests to continue on fast paths with a dynamic precision toggle that can temporarily relax precision for short-lived tokens. The goal is to balance correctness guarantees for vulnerable inputs with overall latency and throughput improvements.

Design: - admission classifier: lightweight checks based on sequence length, token-entropy hints from tokenizer, and presence of structured output constraints. Tunable thresholds are stored in configs/fallback_policy.yaml. - request tagging: requests that fail conservative checks are tagged as safe_mode=true and routed to conservative kernels. Others are allowed to take fast kernels; if a downstream kernel returns an invalidation, only that request is elevated and its KV entries are quarantined to avoid polluting shared caches. - dynamic precision toggle: the kernel_selector can change precision (fp32->fp16/quantized) for non-critical tokens for a bounded prefix window; toggles are logged and decay after N tokens. - KV cache isolation: kv_cache_manager adds lightweight per-request quarantine buckets and probabilistic re-insertion after validation. - scheduler changes: admission is integrated into the continuous batcher so that mixed batches are split gracefully rather than forcing entire batch to safe-mode.

Implementation notes: commits touch runtime and rust components: - src/runtime/scheduler.cc: split batch paths and gating hooks added. - src/runtime/kernel_selector.cc: new precision_toggle API and telemetry. - services/kv/kv_cache_manager.rs: quarantine and reinsertion logic with eviction-safe guards. - configs/fallback_policy.yaml: default thresholds and tuning knobs. - tests/perf/fallback_latency_test.py: benchmark harness that runs synthetic and real prompts. - docs/design/fallback_isolation.md: design doc describing correctness properties and rollout guidance.

Commits: - Add selective fallback admission classifier and default config (Aisha) - 2026-02-18 - Add precision toggle API to kernel selector and unit tests (Aisha) - 2026-02-19 - Implement KV quarantine and reinsertion policy (Aisha) - 2026-02-20 - Integrate admission into continuous batcher, split mixed batches (Aisha) - 2026-02-21 - Add perf harness and perf benches, tune thresholds (Aisha) - 2026-02-23

Changed files summary: - src/runtime/scheduler.cc: add split_batch_for_safe_mode and metrics hooks - src/runtime/kernel_selector.cc/h: add set_dynamic_precision and query_precision_hint - services/kv/kv_cache_manager.rs: add quarantine buckets, probabilistic reinsertion - configs/fallback_policy.yaml: new default config - tests/perf/fallback_latency_test.py: new benchmark harness - docs/design/fallback_isolation.md: new design doc

Small snippet (admission classifier pseudocode):

if (seq_len > config.max_fast_seq) or (token_entropy > config.entropy_threshold) or (requires_strict_output) then
  tag request safe_mode=true
else
  tag request safe_mode=false
end

Testing and results: - Unit tests added for kernel_selector API and KV quarantine logic. - Perf run on staging cluster (p3.2xlarge equivalent) with rw-mix workload: baseline main branch 99p = 320ms; this branch 99p = 220ms (approx 31% improvement) while 50p saw a negligible 2% regression in throughput when dynamic precision was disabled and a 5% improvement when enabled. - KV correctness: synthetic fuzz tests against real models showed no regression in output equality for requests flagged as safe_mode; quarantined requests were validated before reinsertion.

CI and iteration: - Initial CI run failed two unit tests related to deterministic seed ordering in kv_cache_manager; fixed by making reinsertion order deterministic under test mode. - Re-ran CI, all checks passed including linux build, unit tests, integration tests, perf harness smoke. CI timeline: fail -> fix -> pass.

Review conversation (high-level): - Connor Li: asked for explicit invariants on KV reinsertion to ensure we never leak stale kv entries across tenants. Action: added per-tenant namespace enforcement and tests. - Marta Ruiz: requested telemetry for how often dynamic precision flips to enable future cost accounting. Action: added kernel_selector telemetry counters and a console dashboard tile planned in ENG-915. - Devon Patel: suggested a simpler-safe fallback for extremely short sequences to avoid classification overhead. Action: special-case short sequences and added microbenchmarks. - Final approvals from Connor and Marta after fixes.

Rollout plan: - feature flags behind configs.fallback_policy.enable_selective (off by default for enterprise private deployments). - Ramp on hosted: enable 5% traffic -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% while monitoring p99, errors, and kv eviction metrics. - If kv reinsertion rate or mismatches exceed threshold, auto-disable and open rollback alert.

Documentation: design doc included and a short runbook added to docs/ops/fallback_runbook.md describing metrics, alerts, and manual rollback steps.

Notes for on-call: watch eviction_rate, kv_quarantine_size, precision_toggle_rate, and p99 for the top 10 routes. There is an emergency env var REDWOOD_FALLBACK_SAFE_MODE=on to force conservative behavior cluster-wide.

Merge: squash and merge after CI green and approvals. Merge method: squash.

payload.body: Motivation: customers and billing need a single source-of-truth that ties token costs to traces so we can attribute spend to tenants, models and rollout variants and detect regressions early. This PR adds trace-tag propagation for tenant_id/model_variant/batch_size/cold_start, exposes tenant-scoped token-latency histograms, and ships a synthetic SLO replay harness that replays representative prompts to validate per-tenant alerting and SLOs before rolling to prod. Design summary: 1) Trace correlation: add deterministic propagation of tenant_id and model_variant as top-level trace attributes (tag keys: tenant.id, model.variant, batch.size, runtime.cold_start) and emit them on span creation points in the serving hot path. 2) Metrics: new Prometheus histograms: redwood_token_latency_seconds_bucket{tenant_id,model_variant} and redwood_token_size_total{tenant_id,model_variant}; a derived counter redwood_token_cost_cents_total{tenant_id} computed in the metrics pipeline to support near-real-time billing dashboards. 3) Synthetic SLO replay: a Kubernetes CronJob (synthetic-replay) that replays tenant-specific prompt sets at configurable qps and records golden-trace fingerprints to detect quality/latency regressions. 4) Dashboard & runbook: Grafana dashboard 'Tenant Billing & Trace Correlation' with per-tenant tabs, scatter of token-cost vs 99.9p latency, a reconciliation panel that compares expected token cost (from usage) to derived billing. Also added a short runbook section to handle false-positive spikes and rollback steps. Commits summary: - init: add tenant trace tags and metric hooks to serving/runtime entry points - metrics: introduce histograms, expose labels to scrape - pipeline: small adjustment in ingestion mapping to compute derived cost counter - synthetic: add synthetic-replay job and sample prompt sets for two internal tenants - dashboard: add Grafana json, panels and templating variables - tests: unit tests for tag propagation and an integration harness for synthetic job - docs: quickstart for using tenant replay and interpreting reconciliation panels Files changed (high-level): - redwood/serving/src/trace/tags.rs (propagate tenant/model tags and cold_start flag) - redwood/serving/src/hotpath/emit_metrics.rs (emit tenant-scoped histograms; minimal allocations) - redwood/metrics/pipeline/mappings.yml (derive token cost counter) - redwood/infra/k8s/synthetic-replay.yaml (CronJob + image + configmaps) - redwood/observability/dashboards/tenant_billing.json (Grafana JSON dashboard) - redwood/docs/observability/tenant_replay.md (how-to and runbook) - redwood/tests/integration/synthetic_replay_test.py (replay smoke tests) - redwood/tests/unit/trace_tag_tests.rs (unit tests) - redwood/ci/workflows/observability.yml (add synthetic job in e2e matrix) - redwood/console/src/components/CostAttributionPanel.tsx (UI panel wiring) - go/metrics-exporter/README.md (how to pull derived counters) - infra/alerts/tenant_slo_rules.yml (per-tenant 99.9p alert with synthetic verification hook) Review timeline and conversation: - 2026-02-23 Jared Bloom: "Nice direction. Please ensure tag propagation is zero-copy on the hot path and add benchmarks. Also prefer tenant_id as opaque string not numeric casted everywhere." Author (Aisha): "Addressed: switched to Cow<'static, str> storage for tags and added micro-bench harness. Updated tests accordingly." - 2026-02-24 Samir Gupta: "Synthetic job looks promising. We should gate high-qps tenants behind a feature flag to avoid billing surprises during rollout." Author: "Added feature flag synthetic.replay.enabled and defaults off for prod in k8s manifest. Added docs." - 2026-02-25 Marta Chen: "Alerting: aggregation over tenant cardinality may blow up. Add rate-limited alerting and a sliding window for 99.9p." Author: "Implemented slidingWindow(10m) + dynamic thresholding and a secondary alert that triggers only if synthetic replay also shows regression." - 2026-02-27 CI: initial run failed (lint errors in dashboard json and a formatting issue in metrics mapping). Author fixed formatting and re-ran. - 2026-02-28 CI: tests: small flake in synthetic-replay integration due to timeouts; increased retry in harness. - 2026-03-02 Review approvals: Jared: approved after benchmarks added; Samir: approves after feature-flag gating; Marta: approved pending small doc tweak which was pushed. Rollout plan & safety: - Rollout will be staged: feature flag off in production by default. Enable for internal-account sandbox and two low-traffic tenants for 48h, monitor token-cost vs expected and 99.9 latency. - If synthetic job shows divergence or reconciliation panel shows >5% mismatch for a tenant for 2 consecutive windows, automatic rollback to previous model_variant via rollout policy will be triggered (documented in runbook). Backcompat & migrations: - New metric labels add cardinality. To protect TSDB we: 1) shard tenant label cardinality by default to active tenants only via metrics sampling rules; 2) recommend on-prem customers enable sampling. See metrics/pipeline/mappings.yml for limits. Testing & performance: - Added microbench harness for tag propagation (no measurable increase in p50 token latency on small runs). - Unit + integration tests added and synthetic replay smoke tests included in CI e2e matrix. Observability & alert tuning: - New alerts: tenant_token_latency_high (99.9p sliding window with synthetic verification) and tenant_billing_reconciliation_mismatch (percentage delta between expected vs derived cost). - Dashboards: templated per-tenant view and a global reconciliation heatmap. - Added short-runbook: steps to mute false positives, inspect traces, re-run synthetic replay, and rollback rollout policies. CI status: final green on 2026-03-03 after fixing lint and increasing replay retries. Merge: squashed and merged by Marta Chen 2026-03-03. Notes and caveats: - We intentionally kept metric emission inlined in hotpath with careful allocation avoidance; maintainers should avoid heavy allocations when modifying emit_metrics.rs. - Cardinality controls are conservative; ops can tune sampling for large enterprise customers. - Synthetic prompt sets are not exhaustive — intended to catch regressions, not replace full evals. Related: ENG-4721 (billing attribution epic), ENG-4830 (slo automation).

Motivation: We need a conservative way to introduce alternate execution routes (new kernels, quantization modes, scheduling heuristics) into production without risking correctness regressions or SLO violations. Prior approaches toggled whole-worker fast/slow modes which caused occasional bit-rot and tail regressions. This change introduces a route-sampler and a numeric-stepdown helper that together allow safe, measurable rollouts.
This PR implements a staged verification and slow ramp for alternate execution routes. Key ideas: 1) Route sampler: a runtime component that probabilistically routes a small percentage of requests to candidate execution routes and records per-request end-to-end correctness signals (hash of deterministic outputs where applicable, divergence heuristics for non-deterministic outputs) and latency distributions. 2) Staged verification: metrics are evaluated on rolling windows; routes that maintain correctness thresholds and meet latency/regression budgets advance through stages (probe -> warmed -> promoted). 3) Numeric stepdown: a lightweight numeric width stepping library that lets us progressively reduce numeric fidelity (e.g., layer-wise reduced-precision warmup) instead of an immediate snap to a lower precision. This reduces catastrophic degradations and provides meaningful intermediate telemetry. 4) Scheduler integration: the scheduler selector consults verified-route metadata to prefer promoted routes for low-latency classes while keeping fallback routes as a safety net. 5) Rollout tooling: runbook and CI benchmark to validate behavior in canary before global promotion.
- [x] Route sampler implementation with opt-in sampling rate config
- [x] Staged verification state machine and metrics exporter
- [x] Numeric stepdown primitives with deterministic fallback
- [x] Scheduler hook and priority logic
- [x] Integration + unit tests
- [x] Benchmark job and runbook
Canary perf runs (internal runner) comparing baseline vs candidate route (with numeric stepdown): median token latency +2%, p95 +6% at 1% sample rate; after warmed promotion median +0.5%, p95 +1.8%. CPU/GPU utilization improved 7% under heavy batching for candidate kernels. No deterministic mismatches observed on deterministic test corpus (15k samples).
Correctness signal: deterministic-hash match or divergence score for stochastic outputs. Promoted only when mismatch rate < 0.01% and p95 regression < 5% over a 30m rolling window. Automatic demotion if error budget or latency budget is exceeded. All promotion events are recorded and surfaced via console. Default sampling rate is 0.5% (configurable per-tenant).
Unit tests cover state transitions and numeric stepdown math paths; integration test simulates scheduler behavior under mixed routes; perf benchmark job runs in CI with synthetic load. Manual canary: staged rollout using the runbook in docs/ops/runbooks/route-sampler.md deployed to a small subset of Dedicated capacity.
Risk: underpowered sampling may miss rare correctness regressions. Mitigation: pipeline to run offline corpus replays against candidate routes and stricter thresholds for deterministic-only workloads. Risk: added complexity in scheduler decisions. Mitigation: fallback routes remain default for high-risk workloads and promotion metadata can be reset via API.
1) Enable sampler at 0.5% on canary fleet. 2) Observe metrics for 24h; if thresholds met, ramp to 5% and enable numeric stepdown warming. 3) After 72h stable, promote to 25% then global. Each step can be reverted automatically if thresholds exceeded.
Ethan Moore: Can we expose the sampling weight at per-model granularity? Suggest adding a model label selector. Response: Added label selector and default model whitelist in runtime/route_sampler/manager.py.
Lina Gómez: Numeric stepdown looks promising; how deterministic is the fallback path for mixed-precision layers? Response: Stepdown library records deterministic checkpoints per layer; fallback swaps back to exact kernels per-request if divergence exceeds layer threshold.
Samuel Park: CI perf seems noisy in earlier runs. Suggest running multi-seed benches and storing artifacts. Response: Added bench matrix in benchmarks/ci/route_sampler_benchmark.yml and artifact upload step.
Ethan Moore: Approve after small nits (naming + a doc line). Lina Gómez: Approve. Samuel Park: Approve.
CI: unit-tests (pass), integration (pass), perf-bench (pass on matrix 3 seeds). Flaky test: none in this run. Benchmark artifacts uploaded to internal blob storage.
Introduce a conservative route-sampler and numeric stepdown mechanism to safely validate and roll out alternate kernels and scheduling heuristics. Enables staged promotion based on correctness and latency budgets; configurable sampling and per-model selectors. No behavioral changes to default routes until promoted.
This is intentionally conservative: all promoted changes require both correctness and latency budgets to be satisfied. Follow-on work: expand deterministic offline replay CLI and refine divergence scoring for chats/multi-turn workloads.

Summary: Introduces the Helix attention accelerator kernel and scheduler integration: a fused rope/rotary path plus a continuous-KV batcher and lightweight prefetcher. This change aims to reduce tail latency for mixed-sequence workloads and decrease per-token compute by improving locality and reducing memory traffic.

Motivation: Production traffic shows increased variance in small/medium sequence mixes (<=1024) where kernel dispatch and KV cache thrashing drive 95th percentile latency spikes. Existing fused kernels were efficient for long homogeneous sequences but did not optimize the small-batch, mixed-length SLOs we primarily serve. Helix focuses on three axes: 1) a compact fused kernel that applies rotary/rope transforms in-register and coalesces QKV writes to reduce memory bandwidth; 2) a continuous-KV batcher that keeps warm KV lanes resident and opportunistically batches across requests while honoring latency SLOs; 3) a predictive KV prefetcher that leverages a lightweight LRU+freq table to warm likely upcoming KV segments.

Changeset highlights:
- runtime/kernels/helix_attn.cu: new CUDA kernel with interleaved QKV fusion, in-place rotary application, and warp-aware tiling. Micro-optimizations: fused GEMM+softmax path for small heads, reduced shared memory copies, and 16-bit accumulation option for fp16 models.
- runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.cpp: scheduler integration that implements continuous batching with SLO-aware delay windows and per-model batching policies.
- runtime/kv/prefetcher.cpp: predictive prefetcher with LRU+freq heuristics and metrics hooks.
- runtime/kv/kv_cache.h/.cpp: API additions to pin/unpin KV lanes and expose temperature metrics.
- tools/bench/helix_microbench.py: microbench harness and a simple latency histogram reporter.
- docs/perf/helix_design.md: architecture notes and configuration knobs (ENV_HELIX_*).

Benchmarks: Microbench on p4d.24xlarge-equivalent machines using a mixed workload (30% tokens <=128, 50% tokens 128-512, 20% tokens 512-1024):
- median latency: -12% vs baseline fused kernel
- p50: 9.8ms -> 8.6ms
- p95 latency: -28% vs baseline fused kernel
- p95: 42ms -> 30.2ms
- throughput (tokens/sec): +6% at 99% SLO compliance

Notes: results vary by model size and head count; improvements are strongest for models with <=32 heads and batch sizes 4-16.

Compatibility and fallbacks: Helix registers as a capability and is automatically selected when model config meets quantization/attention shape constraints. If kernel selection fails, runtime falls back to the prior fused kernel path. The prefetcher is enabled per-model via config; default conservative heuristics are used to avoid regressing memory pressure.

Testing and validation:
- Added unit tests for KV pin/unpin and prefetch heuristics.
- Added end-to-end smoke tests in perf CI.
- Ran a 72-hour canary on Dedicated slice d-helix-01 with production traffic shaping; no regressions observed, observed consistent reduction in retries.

Review and discussion (high-level):
- Initial implementation landed as draft after microbench showed promising median improvements but had outliers in p99 under adversarial request patterns.
- Reviewer requests: Sana asked for hard SLO guards in the scheduler (implemented: per-route max delay window and immediate fallback). Luis requested more telemetry around KV lane temperature and eviction counters (added metrics and console dashboard link in PR body). Julee requested a memory safety audit and we added bounds checks and a small fuzz harness for the prefetcher.

CI and iteration:
- First CI run (linux-gcc-ubuntu/build+unit) failed due to a static initialization order issue in the prefetcher; fixed in second commit.
- perf CI initially showed a 2% regression in throughput for a single large-model synthetic test; root cause was aggressive prefetching on large sequences; added model-size-based heuristic and re-ran.
- Final CI status: all checks passed, microbench and e2e smoke green.

Commits (summary):

- feat(scheduler): continuous KV batcher SLO-aware windowing
- feat(kv): prefetcher with LRU+freq and KV pin/unpin API
- test: helix microbench and kv unit tests
- fix: init order and prefetch heuristic tuning

payload.body:
Motivation: During recent production incidents we observed sharp tenant throughput drops when warm pools exhausted and immediate backfill paths were unavailable. This PR implements a lightweight runtime proxy that provides two capabilities: 1) Transparent capacity fallback to degraded-but-compatible model variants or lower-concurrency paths when the preferred pool is constrained; 2) Emergency credit borrowing (short-lived, safety-capped) from a cross-tenant emergency ledger that lets critical requests complete while preserving global SLA budgets. Design summary: the proxy sits in the serving request router and evaluates a candidate request's priority, estimated token cost, and current pool headroom. If headroom < threshold and request is high-priority, the proxy first attempts a local fallback (compatible model variant, quantized path, reduced max_tokens). If local fallback insufficient, it will attempt to borrow emergency credit from the reservation ledger via a bounded API: borrow_credit(tenant_id, amount, ttl, reason). Borrowed credit is tracked and reclaimed by subtracting from the tenant's next commit or through an automatic compensation factor applied over N windows. Safety: credits are strictly capped per-tenant and per-cluster, borrow attempts can be rate-limited and audited. Important configuration knobs live in /configs/fleet/fallback-proxy.yaml and are feature-gated under rollout flag rollout.fallback_proxy.enabled. Implementation notes: - Router changes (router/proxy/fallback_proxy.go): new decision path and lightweight state machine. - Ledger client (ledger/emergency_client.go): borrow/release RPC, local cache with optimistic concurrency. - Metrics and tracing: added metrics fallback_proxy.attempts, fallback_proxy.success, fallback_proxy.credit_borrowed, fallback_proxy.credit_repaid, and traces for decision span. - Policy engine (policy/fallback_policy.json): serialized rules for compatible fallbacks keyed by model_family, sequence_length_profile, and tenant_tier. Backwards compatibility: when rollout flag disabled, router behavior unchanged. Rollout plan: staged rollout to canary fleet -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 7 days with synthetic load tests during each step. Migration: adds a ledger table emergency_credits but maintains existing reservation flows. Testing: unit tests for policy matching and ledger semantics; integration tests in perf-canary that simulate pool exhaustion; chaos tests that kill warm-pool nodes and verify fallback latency and no loss of critical requests. Performance summary (canary results): - median latency for fallback-eligible requests: +12ms (p95 +35ms) vs baseline; - success rate for prioritized requests in exhaustion scenarios improved from 63% to 94%; - emergency-credit utilization peaked at 8% of safety cap during simulated storm. Observability: dashboards added in observability-pack/fallback-proxy.json; alerts: FallbackProxy:HighBorrowRate and FallbackProxy:UnrepaidCredit. Risks and mitigations: - Overuse of emergency credit: capped and auto-repay; alerts created. - Incompatibility with strict tenant isolation: option to disable borrowing per-tenant via tenant config. - Complexity in billing: billing signals are emitted (billing.emergency_credit.used) and will be reconciled in billing pipeline. Related work items: Linear ENG-1538 (fallback routing RFC), ENG-1689 (ledger sharding), PM-4021 (priority tiers).

Ava Martinez: Reduced default cap to 5% cluster-wide in configs and added tenant override to zero it out.
Priya Nair: Ledger client needs a fallback when the ledger master is partitioned to avoid blocking requests.
Ava Martinez: Added optimistic local cache with bounded staleness and a fast-fail path that refuses borrow when ledger unreachable; documented behavior.
Samir Patel: Add a smoke test that asserts no billing events are emitted for transient borrow-and-repay flows.
Ava Martinez: Added smoke test and billing event deduplication for rapid borrow/release sequences.
Introduce a fallback proxy that transparently routes requests to degraded-compatible paths and a bounded emergency credit mechanism for critical request preservation during warm-pool exhaustion. Configurable via rollout.fallback_proxy.enabled and fleet fallback config. Observability and billing hooks included.

payload.body:
Summary: This PR introduces a probabilistic flush scheduler and microbatch prioritization in the serving runtime to reduce streaming first-byte latency for small, latency-sensitive requests while retaining batching efficiency for throughput workloads.

Motivation: recent production traces (ENG-4821) showed a consistent 40-120ms tail on first-byte for short responses when continuous batching held tokens waiting for batch fullness. We need a low-risk change that improves p50/p95 for small messages without regressing cost/throughput for bulk workloads.

Design: 1) ProbabilisticFlushScheduler: a scheduler that, for a microbatch below a configurable size threshold, decides to flush immediately with probability p(t) where p increases with queued duration. The stochastic decision reduces tail waiting by opportunistically releasing ready tokens while keeping some batching benefits. The function p(t) is configurable and defaults to a conservative curve tuned from production traces. 2) MicrobatchPriorityQueue: small requests are assigned elevated scheduling weight so that KV prefetch and kernel allocation favor them for the next scheduling slot. This prevents tiny microbatches from being starved by a stream of large batched requests. 3) KV prefetch window tuning: prefetch window is shortened for prioritized microbatches, and an inline optimistic prefetch path was added to reduce KV cache miss latency on first token. 4) Kernel scheduling hints: added light-weight kernel pinning hints so prioritized microbatches attempt to reuse a warm kernel when available.

Implementation details: - runtime/streaming/probabilistic_flush_scheduler.cc: new scheduler implementation and configuration knobs. - runtime/scheduler/microbatch_priority_queue.h/.cc: new priority queue, lightweight comparator based on size, age, and priority class. - runtime/kv/prefetcher.rs: added optimistic inline prefetch path with a fast-path check to avoid allocations on hits. - runtime/kernel/hints.h: small hint enum and runtime sampling counters. - dispatch tests and integration harness updates under e2e/streaming to validate p50/p95.

High-level commits: - Add probabilistic flush scheduler and config defaults - Add microbatch priority queue and wire into stream dispatcher - Add KV optimistic prefetch path and adjust prefetch window tuning - Add kernel hinting and counters - Tests: unit, integration, and scaled canary harness

Changes at a glance (high-level file list): - runtime/streaming/probabilistic_flush_scheduler.cc - runtime/scheduler/microbatch_priority_queue.h - runtime/scheduler/microbatch_priority_queue.cc - runtime/kv/prefetcher.rs - runtime/kernel/hints.h - e2e/streaming/canary_runner.py - tests/streaming/test_flush_behaviour.cc - docs/ops/flush_tuning.md - examples/streaming/flush-config.yaml

Behavioural knobs (configurable): - streaming.flush.prob_curve: base/progression curve (default conservative) - streaming.flush.size_threshold: microbatch size threshold for eligibility - streaming.priority.size_cutoff: what counts as small request - streaming.kv.prefetch_window_ms: target prefetch window for prioritized microbatches

Performance results (canary): - Canary run on a mixed workload (50% small prompt < 32 tokens, 50% large throughput batches) shows: p50 first-byte improved from 38ms to 19ms, p95 improved from 126ms to 68ms for small prompts. Overall token throughput decreased by ~1.8% in the synthetic mix, within tolerance for our Dedicated customers. Cost impact is expected to be neutral at scale because probabilistic flush preserves batching for most requests.

Safety and rollout plan: - Default conservative probability curve and size thresholds to avoid aggressive flushes. - Feature gate: streaming.enable_probabilistic_flush (off by default for private deployments). - Gradual rollout: canary -> regional rollout -> global.

Observability: added new metrics: streaming.flushes.probabilistic, streaming.microbatch.priority_skipped, kv.prefetch.optimistic_hit_rate, kernel.hint_reuse_rate. Added corresponding dashboards and alerts (ops doc referenced below).

Tests: - Unit tests for scheduler determinism with mocked time. - Integration test in e2e harness emulating mixed latency/throughput workloads. - Stress test for KV optimistic prefetch path to validate stable memory behavior.

Review conversation (selected): Reviewer Aisha Patel: "High level: solid approach, but can you justify the probabilistic curve shape? Concerned about oscillation under bursty arrival patterns." Author reply (Priya Rao): "Added a doc with empirical curve fit from production traces and a safety backoff when host CPU or kernel contention is detected. Will include adaptive backoff in follow-up if needed." Reviewer Marco Li: "Please add observability for flush decisions and make sure the metric cardinality is bounded." Author reply: "Added streaming.flush.decisions.count with labels limited to {probabilistic, forced, scheduled}. Kept label cardinality to 3." Reviewer Evan Hart: "Stress tests look good, but add a test that simulates many small requests interleaved with huge batches to ensure no starvation." Author reply: "Added tests/streaming/test_priority_starvation.cc and validated locally."

Requested changes and resolution: - Reduce default base probability by 20% (addressed). - Expose configuration via runtime flags and console UI (console change tracked in ENG-4893; small docs stub included). - Add canary gating flag for Dedicated (added).

CI and checks: - CI initially failed one flaky test in tests/streaming/test_flush_behaviour.cc (timing sensitive). - I fixed the test by using an event barrier and re-ran CI. Final CI: build: pass, unit: pass, integration: pass, e2e-canary: pass.

Merge notes: - Squash-merged after approvals from Aisha and Marco and green CI. - No database or API contract changes.

Ops notes and release_notes: "Improves streaming first-byte latency for small prompts via probabilistic flush and microbatch prioritization. Default settings conservative; operators can tune via streaming.* flags. See docs/ops/flush_tuning.md for details."

Backcompat: This is a non-breaking runtime improvement behind gates; behavior is opt-in for Private by default and conservative for Hosted.

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: slight throughput degradation in mixed workloads; mitigated by conservative defaults and canary rollout. - Risk: metric noise; mitigated by bounded metric labels.

Follow-ups: - Add adaptive probability adjustment based on observed queue length and kernel contention (planned ENG-4992). - Surface a per-customer tuning preset for Dedicated customers.

Example config (examples/streaming/flush-config.yaml): "streaming:\n  enable_probabilistic_flush: true\n  flush:\n    size_threshold: 8\n    prob_curve: \"0.01,0.05,0.15,0.4\"\n    kv_prefetch_window_ms: 10"

Acknowledgements: thanks to Marco for kernel hint guidance and Evan for stress harness improvements.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: We have several customer patterns that combine multiple tool calls inside a single chat turn: parallel lookups (user profile + permissions), speculative enrichment (NER + web search), and chained transforms (summarize -> format). In some of these cases, the runtime previously returned non-deterministic injection ordering and duplicate re-injections after retries, which caused frontend flakiness and made downstream structured-output validation brittle. This PR introduces a cohesive ergonomics layer for multi-tool flows that focuses on three goals: 1) deterministic injection semantics (order and idempotency keys), 2) a reconciliation strategy for parallel tool results that constrains fanout and attaches provenance metadata, and 3) an explicit developer-facing retry surface that avoids duplicate payloads and maintains streaming stability.

What this changes (high-level): - Adds a deterministic injection protocol: tools are assigned stable invocation IDs, and the runtime tracks insertion points so that on resume/retry the same logical positions are used. This prevents content shuffling when partial streaming responses are resumed. - Parallel reconciliation operator: a new executor that accepts multiple tool futures, applies configurable merge policies (first-wins, priority-map, merge-by-field), and emits a single canonical injection block with provenance headers. - Retry surface: explicit retry annotations on tool descriptors (max_retries, backoff_policy, idempotency_hint) and centralized retry coordinator that deduplicates in-flight retries using the invocation ID and at-most-once commit semantics for side-effecting tools. - Compatibility shim: small OpenAI-compat layer change to preserve function_call ordering when tools are returned as an array; structured output helpers expanded to attach tool provenance (tool_id, invocation_id, latency_ms) so downstream evals can assert stability.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc: ENG-1892 linked - [x] Unit tests for injection semantics - [x] Integration test for parallel reconciliation (includes edge cases for duplicate tool results) - [x] E2E streaming test to ensure resume doesn't reorder injections - [x] Backcompat tests for OpenAI compatibility layer - [x] Docs: console docs + SDK surface notes

Commits (summary): - 9f1c2b0: introduce invocation-id allocation and tracking - 4b3a7de: parallel-reconciler executor and merge policies - a6d4f11: retry coordinator and idempotency dedupe table - 2c7e9b4: openai-compat: preserve function_call array order + add provenance fields - e5d2a90: tests + fixtures for multi-tool flows - 1b7d033: docs and examples for TypeScript/CLI quickstarts

Files/areas touched (high-level): - runtime/executor/reconciler.py (new) - runtime/invocation/id_allocator.py (new) - runtime/retry/coordinator.go (new) - api/openai_compat/handler.ts - sdk/typescript/src/tools.ts (small surface additions) - tests/integration/multi_tool_reconcile.test.ts - docs/console/toolflows.md

Review conversation (highlights): - Jason Lee (reviewer): "Overall design looks solid. Concern about memory growth in the dedupe table for long-lived flows; suggest LRU or TTL eviction. Also please add a metric for 'injection_reorders' so we can detect regressions in canary." - Priya (author): "Added TTL-based eviction (configurable per deployment) and an internal metric injection.reorder.count. See retry/coordinator.go lines ~120-160. Will surface to Console dashboard in a follow-up if we want a default chart." - Marina Kovács: "Merge policy set is flexible — can we expose 'merge-by-key' in the SDK with a small helper? Frontends need to prefer first-wins for some use cases." - Priya: "Added merge helper in sdk/typescript/tools.ts export mergeByKey and updated quickstart example." - Owen Park: "One nit: OpenAI compat preserves order but we introduced an additional provenance wrapper; make sure it doesn't break existing parser libs that expect raw function_call objects." - Priya: "Compat shim emits an optional _provenance field; existing SDKs ignore unknown keys. Added an extra opt-in flag in openai_compat handler to disable provenance for strict parity." - CI flakiness: initial CI run failed two flaky streaming tests; rerun fixed it and logs included an added 50ms sleep in the test harness to stabilize race windows.

CI summary: - unit: pass - integration: pass (with retry flakiness fixed) - lint: pass - e2e streaming: pass - security scan: pass

Performance notes: Local benchmarks on a small canary (r4 nodes) show median tail latency increase of ~1.8% for single-tool calls (due to id allocation overhead) and a 12-18% improvement in aggregate latency for common parallel-lookup patterns because reconciliation reduces duplicate downstream processing. Cost tradeoffs documented in ENG-2034.

Rollout plan: - Canary on Dedicated for a small set of customers with multi-tool usage for 2 weeks - Monitor injection.reorder.count, tool.invocation.latency, and retry.dedupe.rate - Gradual rollout to hosted API with a feature flag controlling provenance and reconciliation behavior - SDK release (TS) coordinated: minor bump with helper and example changes

Merge: squashed and merged by Priya Narang via squash-merge. Merge commit: "squash: convergent toolflow ergonomics — deterministic injection + reconciliation + retry surface".

Notes and follow-ups: - Add a dashboard tile in Console for injection stability (ENG-2140) - Optional opt-out API for provenance for strict OpenAI parity - Explore bounded memory advisory to surface to customers with very long-lived sessions
Improves tool-calling ergonomics: deterministic result injection for multi-tool pipelines, parallel reconciliation with bounded fanout, and a developer-facing retry surface. No breaking API changes. Recommended rollout to canary before full production.
Author ensured backcompat path: provenance opt-out and no change to existing function_call payload shape unless opt-in. Key metric injection.reorder.count introduced for monitoring.
Deterministic tool injection, parallel reconciliation operator, retry coordinator with idempotency dedupe; added provenance metadata on tool results (opt-in).

Motivation: observed end-to-end tail latency spikes when heavy KV cache churn interacts with continuous batching and the scheduler's single evaluation path. This addresses a class of regressions where the eager fast-path evaluator would return slightly out-of-spec logits under low-precision kernel fallbacks during GC-like KV churn. Design: split the scheduler's evaluation phase into two distinct evaluators: fastpath_evaluator (aggressive kernels, lower overhead) and safe_evaluator (conservative kernels, strict correctness). The scheduler now assigns requests to the fastpath by default using a runtime gating heuristic; on repeated soft failures (accuracy-check mismatches, KV lookup misses that cause cache rebuilds, or precision toggle events) requests are demoted to the safepath and a per-session KV heuristic updates to avoid oscillation. Added a KV cache heuristic module that tracks per-key miss-rate and recent rebuild windows and suppresses aggressive cache eviction when continuous batching is high. Implemented an opt-in environment flag REDWOOD_FASTPATH_SAFEGATES with three modes: off | permissive | strict. Default is permissive so we gain perf without surprising correctness regressions. Includes metrics, tracing, and a canary rollout plan. Compatibility: preserves API and config surface; no schema changes. Tests: unit tests for evaluator selection logic, integration test that replays a recorded workload with induced KV churn and asserts token-level similarity thresholds, e2e perf test results included below.

c4d5e6f: kv: add heuristic tracker for per-key miss-rate and rebuild windows

e0f1a2b: config: add REDWOOD_FASTPATH_SAFEGATES flag and documentation
f3a4b5c: tests: add recorded workload replay with KV churn and similarity assertions
Marco Chen: Great separation. Please add a comment explaining why the fastpath does not check kv->validity synchronously; I want to avoid future regressions where callers assume strong consistency.
Aisha Patel: Added inline docs and a unit test that ensures the fastpath observes KV validity before returning tokens. The fastpath only skips a heavyweight KV-lock in permissive mode.
Lina Ortega: Can we get perf numbers for both permissive and strict modes and a regression window? I want to see the cost of demotion under heavy load.
Aisha Patel: Attached canary run stats to the PR and summarized below. Demotion costs ~6-10% P50 token latency on a pathological trace but reduces mispredictions to zero.
Daniel Kim: Security note: ensure the safe_evaluator always uses deterministic kernels for audited deployments. Marking as requested change to add an explicit policy flag.
Aisha Patel: Added runtime/flags check and documented the default to be enabled only for enterprise compliance profiles. Updated release notes accordingly.
Lina Ortega: Approving after the perf dashboard link and CI is green.
Marco Chen: Approved. Squash merge recommended to keep history focused.

Baseline (main): P50 token latency 22ms, P95 78ms, tokens/sec 540
Fastpath (permissive): P50 18ms (-18%), P95 68ms (-13%), tokens/sec 630 (+16%)
Strict mode (safe-heavy): P50 20ms (-9%), P95 70ms (-10%), tokens/sec 600 (+11%)
Worst-case demotion trace: demotion increased P50 by 6-10% for affected sessions but eliminated 100% of small-output-drift regressions observed previously

Stage 2: Permissive mode to 10% of traffic for 72h with similarity monitoring
Stage 3: Ramp to 50% if no regressions, strict mode available via config for sensitive customers
Rollback: instant toggle via REDWOOD_FASTPATH_SAFEGATES=off and rollback automation that reassigns in-flight batches to safe_evaluator
Introduces scheduler split (fastpath/safe) and KV cache heuristics. Default gating mode is permissive. Improves token throughput and reduces tail latency while providing a conservative safepath for correctness-sensitive workloads. Operators can set REDWOOD_FASTPATH_SAFEGATES to control behavior. See docs/flags/fastpath_safegates.md for details.

payload.body:
Motivation: newer OpenAI Responses-style clients are starting to pass lightweight RNG/determinism hints and inline annotations in requests; when we bridge those requests into Redwood's runtime we must preserve the client's intent across streaming reassembly, tool/function-call handoffs, and into response metadata. This PR implements a compatibility layer that: 1) recognizes common client-side RNG/determinism fields (rng_seed, client_seed_hint, deterministic_hint) and forwards a normalized header (X-Redwood-Client-RNG) into the serving path so the runtime can apply a deterministic sampling policy when requested; 2) captures client annotations (annotations, client_metadata, x_annotations) and forwards them as structured headers (X-Redwood-Annotations) and also injects them into the Responses-style response envelope under response.metadata.annotations so downstream consumers (SDKs, loggers) can observe them consistently; 3) ensures that streaming chunks carry sequence and rng context so that streamed partial chunks and final tool_call events are stitched with the same RNG context and annotation set; 4) adds a translation shim so older OpenAI-compat calls that used "seed" boolean or numeric flags still map into the new header scheme.

What changed (high level): added an adapter module that normalizes incoming OpenAI-compatible fields into a small set of internal headers, extended the streaming reassembly path to keep a per-request rng_context object through partial-chunk buffering and toolcall handoffs, and updated the tool-calling plumbing so tool invocation events receive the X-Redwood-Annotations and X-Redwood-Client-RNG headers as part of the call payload. Also added unit + integration tests, docs updates, and CI checks for streaming stability under chunk loss.

Checklist:
- [x] Normalize and forward client RNG/determinism hints
- [x] Preserve annotations through streaming and tool calls
- [x] Add translation for legacy seed flag formats
- [x] Unit tests for header translation and streaming reassembly
- [x] Integration simulating chunk reorder/loss
- [x] Docs note for SDKs about new header semantics

Compatibility notes: This is additive for most callers. Default behavior is unchanged unless a client sends determinism/rng hints or annotations. For customers relying on previous implicit RNG behavior, the runtime still falls back to random sampling when X-Redwood-Client-RNG is absent. The header values are advisory; enforcement requires opt-in via route config (see notes in docs/openai-compat.md). Linear: ENG-4129.

Sofia Martinez: Requested a test that simulates tool-call failure mid-stream to ensure rng_context is cleaned up; added integration test and ensured no leak
Akash Reddy: Looks good overall; suggested clarifying docs about advisory nature of rng hints
