payload.body:
Background & motivation: We see recurring false-positive canary alerts when traffic composition shifts (prompt length, cohort mix, or feature flags). Existing baseline estimators assume stationary traffic; this PR adds a covariate-matched baseline estimator that conditions expected latency/throughput on a small set of traffic covariates (input length bucket, api_route, traffic_cohort, and quantized model cache hit rate). The goal is to reduce sensitivity to benign traffic shifts and improve true-positive precision for regressions.

What this PR does: 1) Introduces a new estimator (canary/detectors/covariate_baseline.py) that builds stratified baselines with shrinkage priors and an online embedding of recent covariate histograms. The estimator computes an expected percentile distribution (p50,p90,p99) for the current traffic slice and reports a covariate-adjusted delta compared to historical matched windows. 2) Adds a soft-fallback rollout policy (canary/policies/soft_fallback.py) that, when a marginal regression is detected (alpha < threshold but above noise floor), will route a small steady fraction (configurable, default 5%) to a fallback variant and activate higher-frequency probes for 10 minutes before closing the decision loop. 3) Wires the estimator into the canary evaluator and dashboard annotations; new metrics are emitted with the covariate dimension tags (cov_input_length, cov_route, cov_cohort, cov_cache_bin). 4) Adds unit and integration tests plus an offline simulator scenario that replays 30 days of production slices to validate improved alert precision.

Design notes & tradeoffs: - The estimator intentionally keeps the covariate set small to avoid sparsity; we use grouped shrinkage (Bayesian or empirical-Bayes style) to borrow strength across groups. - The soft-fallback policy is conservative: by default it only activates when the covariate-matched delta is significant AND the absolute regression magnitude exceeds a configurable token-cost impact threshold. - This PR does not change existing hard-rollback policies; it augments the middle of the decision funnel to reduce unnecessary rollbacks.

Testing & validation: - Offline replay: ran the new estimator against a 30-day production replay and measured a 42% reduction in false-positive alerts for latency regressions tied to input-length shifts (detailed numbers in docs/canary/covariate-baseline.md). - Unit/integration: added deterministic unit tests for the estimator edge cases and an integration test that steps through the soft-fallback lifecycle. - Staging canary: staged rollout in perf-canary/staging with synthetic probe bursts; observed expected metrics emission and fallback traffic shaping.

Rollout plan: (1) merge behind feature flag (canary.covariate_baseline.enabled=false by default), (2) enable in staging for 48h, (3) gradually opt-in signal groups (start with chat-api, then embeddings), (4) monitor precision/recall of alerts and adjust shrinkage priors if underfitting.

Related: ENG-2345 (reduce canary churn), ENG-2389 (add adaptive fallback patterns), SUP-8912 (incidents tied to traffic composition changes).

Checklist: - [x] implementation of estimator and policy - [x] unit tests - [x] integration test and replay harness - [x] docs and runbook snippets - [x] metrics and dashboard annotations

Notes: This is intended as an iterative improvement; future work includes automated covariate selection and per-customer baselines for high-volume tenants.
Miguel Santos: Can we reduce cardinality of covariates? Suggest quantizing lengths to 4 buckets and collapsing low-volume routes. Also asked for metric name prefixes to match the existing convention.
Asha Patel: Addressed in second commit; length quantization added and metric prefix changed to perf_canary.
Claire Huang: Please add an explicit cooldown to the soft-fallback policy to avoid oscillation; requested an integration test that simulates repeated small regressions.
Asha Patel: Added cooldown and extended the replay test to include repeated spikes; updated docs with expected behavior.
Devon Brooks: Lint failure on first CI run (flake) — re-ran CI and it passed. Small nits fixed in final commit.

payload.body:
Motivation: Existing threshold and percentile-based canary checks miss gradual or context-dependent regressions that manifest as subtle distributional shifts. This PR introduces a probabilistic change-point (PCP) canary gate that detects distributional changes in latency and throughput by estimating recent and baseline densities with kernel density estimation (KDE), applying context weights (traffic shape, request size, model variant), and deriving a probabilistic change score used by the rollout controller. Design/changes: 1) New detector module canary/detectors/pcp_detector.py implemented in Python; it exposes a Detector interface compatible with the canary runner. 2) Lightweight Go adapter in canary/orchestrator/runner.go wires the detector into the existing canary evaluation flow and emits structured telemetry. 3) New default_canary_profiles.yaml contains an opt-in profile: pcp-sensitive with tunable window sizes, kernel bandwidth scheduler, and alpha thresholds for automated soft/hard rollback. 4) Telemetry: metrics/labels added to metrics_registry.yaml and dashboards/pcp_canary_overview.json for visual inspection. 5) Tests: deterministic unit tests for KDE behavior, synthetic integration tests that inject controlled shifts (e2e-tests/pcp_canary_integration.test), and bench scripts for profiling. 6) Docs and runbook: docs/pcp_canary.md and runbooks/perf_canary_pcp.md outline tuning guidance and incident playbook. Implementation notes: The detector computes two KDEs (baseline and probe) using Gaussian kernels with an adaptive bandwidth based on Silverman's rule scaled by traffic variance per-context. Context weights come from a routing key (model_id, request_size_bucket, priority) and are applied to reweight samples before density estimation; this reduces false positives when traffic composition changes. A Bayesian change probability is computed by comparing log-likelihoods and calibrated using historical false-positive windows. The detector emits a change_score [0..1], a p_value, and a representative fingerprint sample. Integration and rollback policy: The canary controller now supports a three-tier response: monitor-only (log/metric), soft-rollback (throttle new traffic routes to control plane fallback), and hard-rollback (immediate traffic switch and alert). The profile configuration maps change_score thresholds to actions and cooldowns. Performance and safety: Microbenchmarks on a 64-node testbed with synthetic load show median detector CPU of ~12ms/sample and <2% added end-to-end canary latency for typical 5s evaluation windows. We added a sampling rate cap and a batched estimator path for high-throughput customers to limit overhead. Backwards compatibility: Detector registers behind the existing abstraction with the new profile disabled by default; existing linear and percentile checks are unchanged. How to test locally: run perf-canary/Makefile targets test-pcp and bench-pcp; e2e test harness can simulate controlled drift using scripts/bench/poc_latency_profile.py. Rollout plan: feature behind opt-in profile for 2 weeks in canary orgs, then gradually enable as default for internal smoke accounts if FPR < 0.5% over 14 days. Observability/alerts: New alerts perf_canary_pcp_high_probable_change and perf_canary_pcp_consistent_shift for sustained changes; dashboards added. Security/privacy: detector only uses aggregated latencies and metadata keys; no PII. Documentation: detailed tuning guidance and example Linear tasks are included. Related work: complements percentile-decay and traffic-shape guards by capturing distributional shifts. Summary: Adds a robust probabilistic change-point detector with context weighting, integrated into canary orchestration with safe rollout controls and observability.
Add new probabilistic change-point (PCP) detector as an optional rollout guard. Improves detection of subtle latency/throughput regressions by combining kernel density estimation with contextual weighting and temporal smoothing. Backward compatible with existing canary pipelines. Default off for customers; opt-in via canary profile.
Sofia: Suggest reducing default sensitivity; can we expose bandwidth multiplier per-customer? Author(Aisha): Added bandwidth_multiplier config and docs note about tuning. Marco: Can the detector be vectorized in the Go path to avoid cross-language overhead? Author: Added a batched estimator path and microbench numbers; follow-up work ENG-4821 to add pure-Go estimator. Jordan: Add test covering traffic composition change to avoid false positives. Author: Added synthetic composition test and verified CI. Approvals: Marco and Sofia approved after iteration; Jordan approved with comment to monitor false-positive rate. Merge: squash-merged after all CI passed.
Ops: New alerts added; to quiet noisy signals during initial rollout set profile.pcp.sensitivity=low. For high-throughput orgs enable batched_estimator and sample_rate<=0.1; verify metrics perf_canary.pcp_change_probability and perf_canary.pcp_fingerprint_count in dashboards.

payload.title: Probabilistic change-point canary gate with context-weighted KDE

payload.body:
Context: Our current canary detector can be hypersensitive to transient spikes (short-lived latency blips, bursty traffic drops) which led to a handful of noisy rollbacks during aggressive rollouts. This PR implements two complementary techniques to reduce false positives while preserving sensitivity to real regressions: (1) probabilistic smoothing (an uncertainty-aware EMA) per metric to avoid overreacting to single-sample spikes, and (2) a weighted-metric fusion layer that combines latency percentiles, throughput drop, error rate, and queue depth into a single 'fused canary score' with configurable weights derived from historical feature importance.

Summary of changes: 1) core detection library (perf_canary/detector) now exposes SmoothingWindow and ConfidenceEstimators and computes per-metric posterior distributions instead of single-point samples; 2) fusion module (perf_canary/fusion.py) implements a logistic-weighted aggregator with normalization and historical-weight calibration; 3) canary policy schema extended with "min_confidence" and "fusion_weights" and wiring in the orchestration layer (orchestrator/canary_policy.go); 4) offline simulator and backfill (tools/canary_simulator) to validate detection precision/recall and re-calibrate thresholds using historical traces; 5) dashboards and runbook updates (docs/observability/canary-metrics.md).

Why this design: Probabilistic smoothing lets the detector express uncertainty (wide posterior during cold starts/bursts) so the rollout guard can require a minimum confidence when deciding to fail. Weighted fusion keeps the system flexible: teams can tune which signals matter most for their workload (e.g., latency-heavy vs throughput-sensitive). The offline simulator helps pick weight priors and fusion thresholds from historical false-positive/false-negative tradeoffs.

Commits (high-level): - feat(detector): add probabilistic EMA and confidence estimator - feat(fusion): implement logistic-weighted metric aggregator and calibration routines - feat(sim): add offline canary simulator and backfill script - perf(tests): add unit and integration tests for fusion/detector - docs: canary policy schema, migration guide, observability dashboard panels

Files changed (high level): perf_canary/detector.py, perf_canary/fusion.py, orchestrator/canary_policy.go, tools/canary_simulator/main.go, docs/observability/canary-metrics.md, tests/test_fusion.py, tests/test_detector_confidence.py, charts/canary-values.yaml, scripts/backfill/recalibrate_baselines.py

Small illustrative snippet (fusion scoring pseudocode):

  score = 0.0
  for metric in metrics:
    norm = (metric.value - metric.baseline_mean) / metric.baseline_std
    contribution = sigmoid(alpha * norm) * weight[metric.name]
    score += contribution
  fused_score = score / sum(weights)

Rollout guard change: the canary policy now evaluates fused_score and a confidence estimate. The policy fails a canary if fused_score > threshold AND confidence >= min_confidence for stable_window seconds (configurable). This reduces flips on transient spikes while keeping sensitivity to sustained regressions.

Testing and validation: unit tests cover calibration and edge cases (zero-variance baselines, missing signals). The offline simulator ran historical replay over the last 90 days of production traces (sampled) to evaluate precision/recall for a range of thresholds and weight priors; simulator results are included in tools/canary_simulator/output/ and summarized in the PR artifacts. CI includes a perf-regression check which compares detection latency/false-positive rate against the current baseline; this PR passes the check.

Migration & rollout plan: feature gated behind "perf_fusion_v1" flag. Plan: 1) Stage rollout to 10% of clusters for 48h with elevated telemetry retention, 2) run simulator-based calibration and adjust default weights, 3) expand to 50% for 24h, 4) full rollout with automatic fallback to previous detector if false-positive rate exceeds 1% over 6h. We rolled this sequence out in staging and observed a 62% reduction in noisy rollbacks for the test cohort.

Risks & mitigation: the main risk is mis-calibrated weights causing reduced sensitivity. Mitigations: conservative default weights, feature-flagged rollout, and an automatic rollback trigger at the canary controller level if false-positive or missed-regression metrics degrade beyond threshold.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the fusion layer model-agnostic (no ML model dependencies) to avoid infra complexity; however the calibration module emits CSVs suitable for later ML-based weight tuning if we opt in.

Related: Linear ENG-6821 (canary stability work), ENG-6903 (canary simulator enhancements).

- Add probabilistic exponential smoothing for noisy latency/throughput signals
- Add weighted metric fusion layer that computes a single canary score from multiple signals
- Backfill baseline recalibration script and offline simulator for validation
- Canary policy updated to require confidence threshold and minimum stable window (non-breaking)
Alden Park: Can we get more detail on the confidence estimator math and edge behavior?
Author (Maya): Added detailed comments and a reference test (test_detector_confidence.py) that validates behavior at low-sample counts and zero-variance baselines. Confidence is computed from posterior std via a normalized inverse-variance transform.
Riley Gomez: Simulator looks good — did you try different weight priors?
Author: Yes — simulator run artifacts include 5 priors (uniform, latency-heavy, throughput-heavy, error-weighted, learned-from-history). Default uses the history-based prior but teams can override in policy.
Samira Patel (LGTM): Please add a short runbook entry to docs/observability and ensure the charts expose per-signal contributions (now included).
Author: Addressed — added dashboard panels and runbook section; CI passed on re-run.
Merge: Approved by all reviewers and merged via squash.

payload.body:
Motivation: existing canary detectors focus on post-hoc latency/throughput regressions and percentile shifts; they have limited visibility into upstream changes in request composition and concurrency (load profile) that can silently drive apparent regressions or mask true regressions. This PR implements a context-aware load-profile drift detector that tracks multivariate request-shape features (input token length distribution, concurrency histogram, model route mix, and batch size distribution) and raises structured alerts when the running distribution deviates from baseline beyond an adaptive threshold. Design: 1) lightweight feature extractor executed at the per-route aggregator to emit compact sketches (q-digests and histograms) for token-length and latency-by-context; 2) drift scorer combines KL-like divergence for categorical route mix with Wasserstein-like distance for numeric features, weighted by recent token cost and route importance; 3) integrate a new "autoscaler_guard" rollout policy: when drift is detected concurrently with increased autoscaler activity, the platform will temporarily widen canary thresholds and attach a deterministic health tag to decisions to avoid cascading rollbacks due to load shaping; 4) add backfill mode for historical baseline recompute and an explainability payload that surfaces the top contributing features for triage. Implementation notes: detector implemented in perf-canary service (Go) and provides a protobuf-compatible alert payload consumed by canary-orchestrator; storage of compact sketches uses existing windowed metrics backend (Prometheus histograms + a small Redis index for sketches) to avoid new stateful services. Testing & validation: synthetic workload generator added to perf-canary/test/ with controlled shifts in token length and route mix; unit tests for scorer functions and end-to-end smoke harness runs against local canary-orchestrator. Rollout plan: feature gated behind config flag perf_canary.load_profile_drift.enabled=false by default; staged rollout to dev -> staging -> prod with canary windows of 5m/15m/1h; ops playbook included for interpreting explainability payload. Checklist: Closes ENG-4210; add unit/integration tests; add documentation and playbook; verify CI green; coordinate with infra for minor Redis index. Related: complements percentile-based detectors by offering early detection of input-shape-driven regressions and prevents unnecessary rollbacks during autoscaler transients.
Asha Patel: Great direction. Can you clarify the expected cardinality and retention of the Redis index? Ops will want limits hard-coded.
Leah Kim: Index stores O(routes * windows) sketches; default retention 6 hours; added caps and eviction policy + config knobs in new commit b4c2d09.
Marcus Liu: How sensitive is the scorer to short-lived spikes? Could we add a minimum sample count or debounce?
Leah Kim: Yes—added an adaptive debounce that increases window length when sample count < 200 and added a tunable min_samples config; see scorer.go changes.
Samir Nair: We should make the autoscaler guard opt-in per-namespace. Otherwise we risk hiding real regressions.
Leah Kim: Done: autoscaler_guard has namespace allowlist and global override; documented in playbook.
Asha Patel: CI flaky on first run due to test_e2e_drift timing; re-run fixed it. Approved after fixes.
Marcus Liu: LGTM, please squash and merge with release note entry.
Add context-aware load-profile drift detector (perf-canary). Detects shifts in token length distribution, route mix, concurrency; includes autoscaler_guard to avoid false rollbacks during scaling activity; gated behind feature flag; docs and ops playbook included.
Default config keeps detector disabled in prod. When enabled start in dev and staging; monitor "drift_alerts_total" and "drift_top_features" dashboards; if autoscaler_guard expands thresholds excessively, revert namespace allowlist or disable autoscaler integration; Redis index is capped and will evict oldest sketches under pressure.

payload.body:
Motivation: Canary detectors today are sensitive to short-lived traffic bursts and noisy tail samples across shards. This leads to false positives during ephemeral load spikes and excessive rollbacks. This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: (1) Temporal Burst Mitigator (TBM) — a lightweight traffic-smoothing preprocessor that normalizes short-term burstiness before metrics are fed into detectors; (2) Quantile Consensus Guard (QCG) — a guard that fuses quantile estimates from multiple execution shards/nodes using a robust consensus algorithm to reduce false alarms from localized tail noise.

What this change does: Implements TBM as a pluggable preprocessing stage in the canary ingestion pipeline; TBM computes an exponential moving average of arrival rates and applies a short sliding-window dampening factor to limit spiky contributions to latency percentiles. QCG computes a consensus range for a configured set of quantiles (p50, p95, p99) using median-of-means and an outlier-trim step; the canary evaluator only triggers if the consensus indicates a regression across a quorum of shards.

Design highlights: - TBM parameters (window_ms, smoothing_alpha, burst_threshold) are configurable per canary config; defaults chosen to be conservative for general traffic patterns. - QCG exposes quorum_size and trim_fraction; defaults: quorum = 0.66 of reporting shards, trim_fraction = 0.15. - Integrates with existing canary backoff/rollback logic: QCG is a precondition check to prevent noisy single-shard regressions from failing a rollout. - Adds telemetry: tbm.bursts_suppressed, qcg.quorum_failures, qcg.consensus_width, and per-quantile consensus values.

Compatibility and rollout strategy: Both features are opt-in behind canary config flags. Default config enables QCG for any canary with >3 shards and TBM for canaries with 1k+ qps by default; these defaults can be overridden via canary policy. We will gate full platform rollout for 2 weeks in the staging/perf ring and ingest metrics into a new observability dashboard.

Testing: - Unit tests for TBM smoothing math and boundary conditions (zero traffic, constant load, burst windows). - Unit tests for QCG consensus logic with synthetic shard samples (including adversarial shards). - Integration test: end-to-end canary run in perf-sim harness under simulated burst traffic shows TBM prevents false-positive rollback in 94/100 runs. - Canary lab run against production traffic shape (shadowed) for 48h.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation of TBM and QCG algorithms - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests in perf-sim harness - [x] New metrics emitted and documented - [x] Documentation changes for canary config (values.yaml defaults updated) - [x] Feature gated and staged rollout plan

Commits summary:  - feat(tbm): add temporal burst mitigator preprocessing stage and API hooks  - feat(qcg): add quantile consensus guard and quorum logic  - test: add unit/integration tests and perf-sim scenarios  - docs: document configuration and metrics  - ci: add small perf job to CI that runs TBM/QCG sanity checks

Files changed (high level): src/detectors/temporal_burst_mitigator.py, src/rollout/quantile_consensus_guard.go, src/canary/config.go, charts/perf-canary/values.yaml, tests/perf/tbm_qcg_integration_test.py, docs/canary/guards.md, .github/workflows/perf-check.yml

Notes: The body text contains choices (median-of-means, trim fraction, smoothing) with brief rationale; these hyperparameters are set conservatively and exposed for tuning.

Aisha Khan: Please add a short section in docs explaining how smoothing interacts with request batching and KV cache—could smoothing mask real latency regressions for bursty but valid workload patterns?
Priya Menon: Good point — added docs note and a unit test that asserts no suppression for uniformly higher latency across the window.
Diego Rivera: The quorum threshold default (0.66) seems arbitrary; can we justify with empirical results? Also include fallback if only 2 shards are reporting.
Priya Menon: Added a small experiment summary in docs (see tests/perf/consensus_experiment.md) and fallback logic to require simple majority if shards <4.
Benji Lee: CI showed a flaky integration test in the first run (random seed causing one failure). Can we make the test deterministic or retry in CI?
Priya Menon: Made tests deterministic by fixing RNG seeds and added a retry wrapper for the perf-check job; reran CI and all checks passed.
Added Temporal Burst Mitigator to smooth short-lived arrival spikes before detection, and Quantile Consensus Guard to reduce false positives from shard-local tail noise; opt-in via canary config with conservative defaults. Expect reduced noisy rollbacks for bursty traffic patterns.

payload.body:
Context: We observed recurring subtle regressions that escaped percentile-based detectors when traffic composition shifted across correlated slices (region+model+route). This PR introduces a traffic-convolution drift sensor that measures spatiotemporal cross-correlation between traffic slices and latency/throughput features, plus an adaptive rollback governor that uses the sensor score to modulate canary rollback thresholds. Motivation: Improve sensitivity to multi-slice correlated regressions while reducing false positives from benign shifts (e.g., planned traffic migrations). Goals: detect correlated degradations earlier, avoid unnecessary rollbacks for single-slice noise, and provide tunable conservatism per-customer or per-rollout. High level changes: 1) New inference pipeline stage 'traffic_conv_sensor' that computes a sliding-window convolution over slice-time matrices, outputting a normalized drift score. 2) Sensor exposes a low-cost streaming implementation suitable for the canary worker (C++) and a Python reference implementation used by local evaluators. 3) Adaptive rollback governor that converts sensor score + traditional canary signals (latency percentiles, error rate) into a dynamic rollback probability and threshold. 4) Unit and integration tests for sensor stability under traffic reshapes, synthetic correlated regressions, and bursty noise. 5) Docs and architecture notes in perf-canary/README describing config knobs and recommended guardrails. Commits (summary): - feat(sensor): add traffic_conv sensor core and streaming C++ implementation - feat(governor): implement adaptive rollback governor and policy config - test: add synthetic correlated regression generator and integration tests - docs: document config parameters, tuning guidance, and failure modes - ci: add new test job and benchmark harness for sensor perf Files changed (high level): - perf-canary/sensors/traffic_conv_sensor.cc (core streaming implementation) - perf-canary/sensors/traffic_conv_sensor.h - perf-canary/governor/adaptive_rollback.go - perf-canary/tests/synthetic_correlated_regression.py - perf-canary/benchmarks/sensor_latency_bench.py - perf-canary/configs/default_rollout_guard.toml - perf-canary/README.md Rollout config snippet added: sensor_window_seconds=300 convolution_stride=60 normalization=median-absolute-dev governor_base_threshold=0.95 governor_sensitivity=0.6 governor_decay_seconds=600 Design notes and tradeoffs: The convolutional approach treats traffic slices (region, model, route) as a sparse 2D grid and applies lightweight temporal kernels to surface correlated shifts. We bias toward explainability: sensor outputs include top-3 contributing slices for the score so SREs can triage. We experimented with ML-based detectors (autoencoders) but chose convolutional heuristics for determinism and observational cost reasons. Performance and cost: streaming C++ implementation adds ~0.7ms p50 compute to the canary worker on a loaded host in our benchmark; sensor runs are disabled by default in small deployments and enabled by default for Dedicated/Private with sampling. Tests and CI: New unit tests (C++ + Go) and an integration test that replays a synthetic correlated regression trace and verifies that the adaptive governor triggers rollback with >90% probability for high-severity regressions and <10% for benign traffic shifts. CI: all checks passed on first run except a flake in linters which was fixed by a follow-up commit. Review conversation summary: - Ava asked for more clarity on slice cardinality explosion and a memory bound; author added an LRU slice pruning heuristic and documented it. - Ravi requested a safety cap on governor sensitivity; author added governor_sensitivity_max and unit tests. - Leah suggested exposing the top contributing slices for alerting; author added the explanatory metadata and docs. - QA flagged an edge-case where evenly distributed small regressions across many slices could inflate the score; mitigated via median-based normalization. Security and privacy: sensor only uses aggregated metrics (latency, throughput counts) by slice keys; no raw request payloads are used. Configuration: sensor is off by default for orgs with <100k monthly requests; rollout plan: staged rollout to perf-canary cluster followed by canary rollouts in Dedicated customers who opt-in. Migration notes: backward-compatible configs; default behavior unchanged until sensor enabled via config. Impact: expected to reduce time-to-detect correlated regressions, improve median false positive rate for rollouts by ~18% in internal canary replay tests. Merge and follow-ups: merged via squash merge. Follow-up work tracked in ENG-3499 to add a dashboard and alerting playbooks. Checklist: [x] design proposal linked [x] unit tests added [x] integration tests added [x] perf bench added [x] docs updated [x] reviewed and approved by 3 reviewers Merge method: squash
Adds a new spatiotemporal drift sensor (traffic-conv) that detects correlated latency/throughput shifts across traffic slices and an adaptive rollback governor to tune rollback thresholds based on payload heterogeneity and recent stability
Ava Martinez: Please add memory/cost bounds for slice explosion — suggested LRU pruning — resolved in commit 3.
Ravi Shah: Add hard cap for governor_sensitivity and tests — addressed in commit 5.
Leah Ortega: Expose contributing slices for triage and alerting — added explanatory metadata and docs.

payload.body:
Context: Recent rollouts exposed a pattern where a small subset of tenants with bursty traffic exhausted replica headroom and caused noisy tail latency regressions that standard canaries missed (because aggregate signals were dominated by stable tenants). This PR introduces a tenant-aware headroom sentinel that synthesizes low-sample microburst probes, maintains per-tenant capacity fingerprints, and computes an adaptive rollback quantum so rollouts can fail fast for affected tenants while continuing elsewhere. Motivation: reduce blast radius of perf regressions caused by tenant-specific workload modes and improve sensitivity for sparse high-impact tenants without increasing false positives for the majority. Summary of changes: - Add headroom estimator + fingerprint store with eviction and time-decay (canary/orchestrator/headroom_sentinel.py) - Implement microburst synthetic probe that targets short-window concurrency saturation (canary/probes/microburst_probe.go) - Integrate sentinel with rollout controller to emit per-tenant "quanta" decisions (canary/orchestrator/rollback_quanta.go) - Small TS/JS bindings for Console visualization of tenant heatmap (redwood-console/plugins/canary-tenant-heatmap.ts) - Unit and integration tests that simulate heterogeneous tenant mixes (tests/test_headroom.py, tests/integration/test_tenant_quanta.yaml) - Docs and runbook describing tuning knobs and migration steps (docs/canaries/headroom.md) Design notes: - Headroom estimator uses a Bayesian low-sample smoothing prior tuned for burst detection; it intentionally weights very recent microburst probes higher so transient saturation is visible within 30s windows. - Fingerprints are lightweight histograms (log-buckets) of observed concurrency/latency pairs with TTL-based decay to avoid stale isolation after cutovers. - Rollback quanta are fractional percentages (eg 5% -> 50% of rollout traffic for affected tenants) computed from estimated probability of tail degradation; they are conservative by default and increase only after repeated correlated probes. - Integration with rollout controller allows per-tenant canary gating: if tenant headroom score exceeds threshold, traffic for that tenant is diverted to stable model variant or previous release. Migration and rollout: - This is opt-in behind a feature flag and off by default. - Suggested pilot: enable for 5 high-variance tenants for one week, observe Console heatmap and canary alerts, then widen. Checklist: - [x] Headroom estimator implementation - [x] Microburst probe and probe scheduler - [x] Rollout controller integration and quanta computation - [x] Tests: unit + integration - [x] Docs and runbook - [x] Console visualization work Notes on safety: defaults are intentionally conservative; sentinel will not trigger account-wide rollbacks without two corroborating probe cycles and a cross-signal agreement (latency tail and concurrency spike). Related: ENG-4590 (tenant isolation perf initiative), SUP-1287 (customer incident with tenant burst).
Lena Park: Really like the per-tenant fingerprinting. One question: how large can the in-memory fingerprint store grow under heavy tenancy? Can we add a hard cap?
Aisha Khanna: Added eviction + approximate LRU with TTL; typical memory footprint is ~80 bytes per tenant histogram, capped via charts/canary-values.yaml. Included benchmarks in tests showing 10k tenants within 64MB budget.
Devon Harris: The Bayesian prior parameters look aggressive — might produce false positives for noisy short-lived spikes. Can we back off sensitivity and prefer repeated confirmation?
Aisha Khanna: Adjusted initial prior scale and added requirement for two corroborating probe cycles before increasing quanta beyond 10%. Kept single-cycle alert path for on-call visibility but not automated rollback.
Marcus Li: Integration with rollout controller looks clean. Please ensure feature flag gating and a clear kill-switch for emergency rollback (ideally via existing release controller API).
Aisha Khanna: Feature flag added (ff/perf/tenant_headroom) and rollout controller exposes an immediate emergency-disable endpoint; documented in runbook.
Lena Park: CI flaked on integration job initially, reran and all green. Approving for merge.
Devon Harris: Approved.
Add tenant headroom sentinel: per-tenant microburst probes and adaptive rollback quanta to limit rollout blast radius for bursty tenants. Opt-in behind feature flag ff/perf/tenant_headroom. See docs/canaries/headroom.md for tuning and runbook.

payload.body:
Motivation: We have seen multiple customer incidents where clients retried aggressively after stream-level failures (partial stream disconnects, intermittent 502/503) or mis-parsed Retry-After (HTTP-date vs seconds). Tool/function calling flows add complexity: who owns idempotency (client vs server) across stream reconnects was ambiguous, leading to duplicate tool side-effects for some customers. This PR standardizes semantics across OpenAI-compatible endpoints and makes retry decisions deterministic for clients.

Summary of changes and behavior: - Normalize Retry-After header parsing to accept both integer seconds and HTTP-date; we expose a canonical `retry_after_seconds` field in the OpenAI-compatible error envelope for clients that prefer structured values. - Introduce a top-level `retryable` boolean in the OpenAI error object (same envelope used for streaming and non-streaming) to indicate whether a safe automated retry is recommended by the server. This decouples transport-level heuristics from client policy. - Define idempotency ownership rules for tool/function calls: the client-provided idempotency key (Idempotency-Key header or `idempotency_key` field) remains the canonical owner for deduplication across retries and reconnects; the server will reject ambiguous reconnects when ownership cannot be established. - Stream reconnection contract: when a streaming connection drops mid-response and the server returns an error with `retryable: true`, clients SHOULD resume by issuing a new request with the same idempotency key and start_position token (if server supports prefix resumption); otherwise they MUST treat the call as opaque and follow normal idempotency semantics. - Error mapping: map transient infra errors (502/503, connection reset, server overload) to OpenAI-style 500/429/503 error objects consistently and set `retryable` appropriately. - Backwards compatibility: existing clients that ignore `retryable` will continue to operate; new structured fields are additive.

Checklist: - [x] Normalize Retry-After parsing and add structured field - [x] Add `retryable` flag to error envelope - [x] Implement idempotency ownership checks in call routing - [x] Update OpenAI adapter tests for streaming reconnection scenarios - [x] Add docs and migration notes in docs/openai_compat/error_handling.md

Commits (high level): - a12b9c7: add structured retry_after_seconds and retryable boolean to openai error envelope - f3d4e1a: normalize Retry-After parsing across proxy + sdk shims - 9f7c4d5: enforce idempotency-key ownership for function/tool calls in router - 2b5a8f2: streaming reconnection support and tests for prefix resumption - 4e90d2b: docs and example client snippet + changelog entry

Changed areas (high level): - src/proxy/openai_adapter/error_envelope.go: add `RetryAfterSeconds` and `Retryable` fields and mapping helpers - src/proxy/openai_adapter/handlers.go: map transport errors to envelope consistently - src/runtime/streaming/resume.go: add prefix resumption hooks and ownership checks - src/runtime/idempotency/store.go: add strict ownership checks and TTL semantics - docs/openai_compat/error_handling.md: document the new contract and migration guidance - tests/openai_compat/stream_reconnect_test.go: new integration tests for reconnection + idempotency - examples/openai_compat/client_retry_example.md: example showing how to use the fields - ci/config: update integration matrix to include streaming reconnect tests

Small snippet (illustrative, single-line for copy/paste): `{"error": {"message": "server overloaded", "type": "rate_limit_exceeded", "retryable": true, "retry_after_seconds": 30}}`

Notes for reviewers: - The primary behavioral change is exposing `retryable` and the canonical `retry_after_seconds`. We intentionally keep HTTP Retry-After intact to preserve proxies and intermediate cache behavior; the structured field is for clients that want deterministic parsing. - Idempotency ownership is conservative: if a reconnect cannot be tied to the original idempotency key (missing header or mismatch), we return 409/422 with guidance rather than guessing. This reduces accidental duplicate tool invocation. - This surfaced a race in a small subset of routing tests; I fixed the router locks and added a dedicated integration test for concurrent reconnects.

Migration guidance (single-paragraph): Clients should start reading the `retryable` boolean and `retry_after_seconds` on OpenAI-compatible error payloads. For streaming function/tool calls, clients that want automatic transparent retries should supply a stable idempotency key for the lifetime of the logical operation and support prefix resumption tokens if they want to avoid restarting from scratch. Existing clients will continue to function but may be less deterministic in retry behavior.

CI and performance: Integration tests exercise high-concurrency streaming reconnection patterns. Local benchmarks show <2% regression in median latency for streaming start (the path touched a small lock in the router which I optimized).

Merge notes: Squash-merged to main after CI green and final approval from Maya and Liam.
- Normalize Retry-After parsing (seconds or HTTP-date) for OpenAI-compatible endpoints
- Add `retryable` boolean to error payload to make retry behavior deterministic for clients
- Clarify idempotency ownership rules for tool/function calls in streaming sessions
- Improve error mapping so 429/503/502 are consistently classified across streaming and unary APIs
Maya Chen (2026-02-20): Love the structured retry field. Please add an explicit example for HTTP-date parsing in the docs (done in latest commit).
Liam O'Connor (2026-02-22): +1 overall but raised a concern about the router lock causing a latency regression; you addressed with a second commit that switches to a read-mostly pattern (verified in benchmarks).
Priya Rangan (2026-02-25): Request clarification: what happens when a client reuses an idempotency key for a different operation? I added a 4xx guidance error and doc note rather than silently deduping.
Ava Thompson (author) (2026-02-26): replied to Priya and updated docs with explicit 'ownership' section and error examples.

payload.body:
Motivation: production p99 CPU consumption spikes traced to eager request deserialization and heavy thread-pin churn in the fast path. On busy hosts the userland work (JSON/proto decode + route lookup + KV cache checks) dominated latency even when the model run time was small. This change reduces CPU overhead by deferring full decode until a handler actually needs structured fields, replacing per-request OS-thread pinning with a cooperative single-threaded event loop for light-weight request dispatch, and reworking the KV cache to per-shard read-mostly paths to avoid a global lock handoff. Summary of changes: 1) Add runtime/serialize/lazy_decoder.rs: a shallow header parse that extracts only routing keys and request sizes, and a thin accessor that decodes fields on first access. 2) Introduce runtime/dispatch/event_loop.rs: a cooperative event loop that handles socket read, shallow parse, routing, and small-scope scheduling decisions; long-running or kernel-intensive work is submitted to a short-lived worker pool via a lock-free handoff queue. 3) Rework KV cache in runtime/kv/cache_shard.rs to use epoch-based fast reads and an update path that copies-on-write for rare mutations to keep fast path lockless. 4) Continuous batching change in runtime/batching/coalesce.rs: cancel-less deadline batching that opportunistically coalesces requests without blocking the event loop and uses a soft backpressure signal to avoid head-of-line blocking. 5) Add microbench and e2e perf tests: tests/perf/lazy_decode_bench.py and tests/e2e/dispatch_smoke_test.go. Results: internal perf runs show median CPU user-time per request reduced by ~28%, 95th latency improved by ~18% and p99 improved by ~34% on our small-sequence LLM workload (same hardware and traffic replay). Checklist: [x] perf benchmarks added and scripted for CI replay, [x] unit tests for lazy decoder and KV shard, [x] integration smoke test for dispatch/event loop, [x] canary rollout plan included in docs/perf/notes.md. Backwards compatibility: runtime API and public wire formats unchanged; lazy decode is strictly internal and transparent. Risks & mitigations: deferring decode could change when decoding errors surface—decoder is now hermetic and always raises a typed decode error during handler evaluation; added metric runtime.request.decode_late_count to monitor. The event loop reduces OS thread migrations but requires careful yield points; added watchdogs and a cooperative-yield metric to ensure fairness. Rollout plan: staged canary (5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100%) with a short hold after each step for perf/regressions. Related: ENG-1423 (CPU hotpath profiling), ENG-1498 (KV cache contention investigation).
Miguel Santos (Reviewer): Overall this looks like the right direction. A few concerns: the epoch sequence for KV reads needs comments about memory growth and the backpressure signal may under-react on tail-CPU bursts. Please add a small explanation and one more test for GC of epochs.
Anika Rao (Author): Thanks Miguel, added comments in cache_shard.rs and a unit test 'epoch_gc_test' that forces churn; documented memory bounds in docs/perf/notes.md.
Eleanor Kim (Reviewer): I ran the perf replay on my m-class hosts. P99 improvement matches your numbers but I saw a small increase in 50ms allocations from the worker handoff path. Can we reduce allocations on the queue path?
Anika Rao (Author): Reworked the handoff queue to reuse a pooled node and removed an extra boxed closure — new commit 'Perf tweaks: reduce allocation churn' addresses this. Reran the replay and allocations at 50ms bucket are down.
Jared Bloom (Approver): Tested canary stage and verified no increase in error rates and improved tail latency. Approving to merge.
CI Bot: linux-build passed, unit-tests passed, perf-replay passed (baseline comparison attached).

Motivation: CI-driven prompt-set regression gates have high sensitivity to rare prompt failures and can generate noisy alerts when transient latency spikes or skewed sampling amplify low-impact differences. This PR introduces an importance-weighted cohort smoother plus a latency-tempered CI hook that reduces spurious failures by downweighting historic low-importance samples and attenuating the effect of high-latency outliers in quality gates. Design summary: 1) importance_weights module computes per-prompt weights using a configurable recency window, exposure frequency, and an inverse-latency factor; 2) cohort_smoother aggregates eval metrics (accuracy, BLEU-like similarity, and semantic similarity) using the IW estimator with bootstrap confidence intervals; 3) latency_tempered_hook plugs into the existing CI eval runner and applies a sliding-temporal dampening factor to the gate decision when latency variance exceeds threshold; 4) a fallback soft-fail path is provided to create a triage ticket instead of failing main pipelines for marginal regressions. Changes include implementation, unit and integration tests, docs, and a small CI adapter. Testing & rollout: unit tests and deterministic sim harness added; staged rollout enabled via feature flag eval.iw_smoother.enabled:false by default; nightly CI will opt-in on a 10% canary for 48 hours before global enablement. Local test instructions: pytest tests/test_iw_smoother.py::TestIWWeighting::test_bootstrap_estimator --runslow and run scripts/ci_eval_runner --hook latency_tempered_hook --sample-size 200. Backwards compatibility: the hook is opt-in and defaults to no-op when importance weights are unset; it does not change stored eval artifacts format. Related work: builds on ENG-3429 (cohort sampling refactor) and ENG-3498 (CI gate abstractions). Release notes: Add importance-weighted cohort smoother and latency-tempered CI hook to reduce CI noise from transient latency spikes and rare prompt samples.

Maya Chen: Updated default to 7 days and added config override in ci/hooks/iw_cohort_smoother.yml

Maya Chen: Added deterministic sim and test that asserts dampening behavior under synthetic latency variance

Context and motivation:
Traffic and latency regressions can be subtle and localized to particular traffic shapes (e.g., long-sequence prompts, low-frequency endpoints). Existing canary detectors operate on coarse aggregate percentiles and often miss progressive degradations that first appear as steady slope changes across small cohorts. This PR introduces a 'gradient-sliced' approach: we split traffic into many lightweight slices, compute per-slice latency gradients over multiple window sizes, and then fuse slice-level signals into a traffic-weighted slope anomaly score that is robust to noisy outliers and transient bursts.

What this implements:
- A new probe module (perf_canary.probes.gradient_sliced) that maintains N hash slices per route and computes exponential-weighted linear regression slopes for each slice across short/medium/long windows.
- Slice-weighted fusion: weights slices by request-volume stability and SLO impact to produce a single slope anomaly score per-route.
- Adaptive threshold calibration: baseline drift is estimated using exponential percentile deciles per-slice; thresholds auto-scale with traffic so low-volume slices don't dominate.
- Synthetic microburst injection harness (optional) to exercise slope detectors in CI and on-demand smoke runs.
- Automated rollback controller that plugs into rollout orchestration: if slope anomaly score exceeds configurable severity and sustained_duration, the controller first throttles new canary traffic, then issues a rollback when budget/hysteresis rules are met. Controller exposes: holdoff, grace_period, rollback_budget, per-slice quarantine list.
- Metrics and tracing: new metrics (gc_latency_slope, gc_slice_violation_count, gc_fused_score) and distributed trace spans for degenerate slices to enable fast debugging in Console.

- [x] Add integration tests with perf-canary harness (synthetic traffic)

- [x] Add dashboard tile and alert rules for slope anomalies

Motivation: We observe short-lived high-frequency traffic pulses from a subset of clients that produce transient tail-latency spikes which the existing canary detectors either ignore (too short) or treat as regressions (too sensitive). This PR introduces a "traffic pulse fader" probe and a small-state "degraded-mode automaton" that together: 1) detect high-frequency short-duration pulses using a sliding-event pulse detector tuned for burstiness, 2) apply a temporary smoothing window (fader) on aggregated latency percentiles to prevent premature canary-triggered rollbacks for pulses that self-resolve, and 3) transition the rollout guard into a degraded mode where stricter quorum and sanity checks are enforced before auto-rollbacks. The goal is to reduce noisy false positives while preserving fast response to sustained regressions. Design summary: - pulse detector: lightweight CWT-inspired heuristic that flags pulse candidates based on short-window throughput derivative and inter-arrival entropy (src/probers/pulse_fader.go) - fader: exponentially-weighted decay applied to percentile deltas that reduces short-lived spikes' impact on the canary score (evaluator/fader.py) - degraded-mode automaton: finite-state machine with states {NORMAL, SOFT_DEGRADED, HARD_DEGRADED} that escalates based on persistent signal across cohorts and enforces additional cross-slice consensus checks before rollback (config/canary_policy.yaml, src/automata/degraded_mode.py) Compatibility and safety: - New detector is opt-in via canary_policy flags; default config keeps existing behavior. - Observability: added dedicated metrics (canary.pulse.detected, canary.fader.decay_applied, canary.degraded_mode.state) and debug logs behind debug-level gating (docs/observability.md). Testing: - Unit tests for pulse detection edge cases and fader decay (tests/test_pulse_fader.py). - Integration harness run against replayed production traces including three known pulse incidents; added synthetic pulse generator in benchmark-lab/fixtures/pulse_traces.json. - CI run: initial lint/test failed due to race in snapshot test; fixed by adding controlled clock in tests. Rollout plan: - Deploy to staging Canary group A for 24h with metrics dashboard and alert thresholds adjusted; if no sustained regressions and reduced false positives seen, roll to global. - If degraded-mode engages in staging, ops will get a notification and human-in-the-loop will operate rollback controls; automatic rollbacks are disabled for SOFT_DEGRADED in first rollout. Checklist: - [x] Implementation for detector, fader, automaton - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Observability metrics and dashboards (draft) - [x] Config gating and feature flag - [x] Linear ticket ENG-4217 attached Related: mentions SUP-9021 where a customer reported frequent short spikes during traffic bursts, and links to prior canary work on burst handling. For reviewers: main behavioral change is the fader math and the automaton transitions; please focus on the escalation thresholds and the observability coverage.
Sophie Barnes: Nice work — can you document the expected memory and CPU overhead of the pulse detector? Concerned about additional per-prober allocations.
Diego Alvarez: Added a microbenchmark in the PR description and included a note in docs. Detector uses fixed-size ring buffers; cost measured ~0.4% CPU at 10k rps in staging sim.
Marcus Kim: The decay constant choice is critical. Can we expose it as a per-canary override? Also please add more unit tests for corner-case decays.
Diego Alvarez: Made decay_k configurable in policy and added tests covering nil/edge values.
Leah Chen: CI flaked on snapshot diff; looks like timing-based nondeterminism. Suggest using a fake clock in tests (see comment).
Diego Alvarez: Switched tests to monotonic fake clock; pushed fix. CI green after rerun.

Motivation: We've observed production tail events that only emerge when heterogeneous models are exercised together (e.g., a heavy LLM rerank paired with a small chat model). Existing single-model workload runners miss cross-model interference on shared GPU resources and scheduling-induced cliff edges. This PR adds a Multi-Model Hotpath Simulator (MMHS) and a Cliff-Edge Reporter pipeline to capture those behaviors and produce deterministic, analyzable artifacts.

What this PR contains: 
- MMHS: a workload runner that can orchestrate concurrent request streams across multiple model types with configurable sequence distributions, KV primer policies, and controlled priming overlap windows. It supports both synchronous and streaming patterns to reproduce mixed RPC behavior.
- PULSE smoothing: latency post-processor that applies phase-aware smoothing (PULSE algorithm) to reduce noise while preserving transient cliff events for detection.
- Cliff-Edge Reporter: a reporting pipeline that identifies stepwise throughput/latency cliffs, annotates affected kernels, and emits an HTML+JSON artifact for triage.
- Integration hooks: small adapters to the existing bench harness to allow scheduling MMHS runs in nightly pipelines and to attach tapes for deterministic replays.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implement multi-model runner and orchestration primitives
- [x] Add PULSE smoothing component and CLI flag to toggle smoothing
- [x] Add reporter pipeline + artifact writer (HTML summary + compact JSON)
- [x] Unit tests for scheduler, primer, and reporter edge-cases
- [x] End-to-end smoke run in CI with a 3-model mix

How to run locally: 
- python -m benchlab.runner --config examples/multi_model_mix.yaml --out artifacts/run-<timestamp>
- artifacts contain run.trace (binary), run-summary.json, and report.html generated by the Cliff-Edge Reporter.

Expected outcomes and measured results from internal CI run: 
- 3-model nightly mix (chat-small, rerank-medium, large-gen) reproduced a 2.8x p99 latency spike when KV primer overlap was 30-50ms.
- PULSE smoothing retained the cliff event while reducing per-minute noise by ~22% enabling more stable cliff detection thresholds.

Related items: Linear ENG-4721 (benchmark design), ENG-4882 (reporting UX). References to prior investigations: incident INT-1024 spike analysis.

Notes on safety and reproducibility: The runner supports a deterministic 'tape' mode that records request timing jitter and can replay with recorded seeds to reproduce cliffs. The artifacts include provenance fields for exact binary hashes and kernel versions.

Evelyn Park: Added scheduler.memory_cap_bytes per-model and documented behavior in examples. Also added unit test to cover memory cap enforcement.

Evelyn Park: Reporter now embeds optional flamepoint URLs when provided by CI artifacts; skips gracefully otherwise.
Harish Menon: CI run showed a flakey test on primer timing; please add a deterministic tape mode (requested change)
Evelyn Park: Implemented tape mode and updated tests to use recorded seeds; reran CI.
Marco Ruiz: Approving after CI green and documentation updates.
Nina Sokolov: Approved

payload.body:
Context and motivation: We've seen recurring short-lived regressions that are not well-captured by time-domain percentile comparisons alone. Some regressions manifest as subtle periodicity or harmonic energy shifts in tail latency/throughput time series that correlate weakly across cohorts, which cause noisy canary signals and frequent false-positive rollbacks. This PR introduces the 'spectral-congruence' detector: a frequency-domain ensemble that measures cross-cohort congruence of spectral fingerprints and a cutover-stabilizer that enforces temporal hysteresis and consensus before triggering automated rollback or throttling.

Key changes (high level):
- New detector service: perf-canary/spectral_congruence.py (core algorithm and scheduler).
- Cross-correlation pipeline: transforms cohort time-series to power spectral density (PSD), computes banded cosine similarity, and aggregates per-SLO weights.
- Cutover stabilizer: state machine in perf-canary/stabilizer.py implementing staged thresholds (observe -> warn -> safe-cutover -> block) with exponential backoff and cooldown windows.
- Metrics and alerts: new prometheus metrics (spectral_congruence_score, spectral_band_alerts, stabilizer_state) and Grafana dashboard JSON under observability/dashboards/spectral-congruence.json.
- E2E integration: a new canary-e2e test harness scenario that injects harmonic noise into tail latency streams to verify detection and non-flapping behavior.
- Docs: architecture note and runbook in docs/canaries/spectral-congruence.md and runbooks/spectral-cutover-playbook.md.

Checklist: 
- [x] Algorithm implementation and unit tests
- [x] Integration tests added (canary-e2e with simulated noise)
- [x] Metrics exported and dashboard draft
- [x] Runbook and expected operator actions
- [x] Performance: detector runs in <200ms per cohort on sampling window, memory within target envelope

- 7f2a5b9: Implement banded similarity aggregation and SLO weighting

Review conversation summary (selected highlights):
- Marco Chen (reviewer): "Nice work isolating the spectral signal — can you add a short doc string about the resampling assumptions? Also we should be careful about using PSD window sizes that conflict with existing sampling cadence."
- Lena Ortiz (author): "Responded: added resampling explanation to spectral_congruence.py and used the platform's canonical sample window (30s) by default; made window size configurable via environment flag."
- Priya Singh (reviewer): "Can we quantify the false-positive reduction vs. current percentile-only detector? A small A/B shown in tests would help."
- Lena Ortiz: "Added an A/B folder under perf-canary/tests/ab_experiments with a synthetic trial showing ~3.6x reduction in false-positive rollbacks on injected harmonic noise while keeping true-positive detection comparable."
- Omar Williams (reviewer): "Operational question: what is the CPU/memory cost of running this per-tenancy? Could be expensive when we have hundreds of tenants."
- Lena Ortiz: "Benchmark results appended to docs/ops-bench-spectral.md: average 160ms CPU time and ~6MB RSS per cohort on our standard probe host; we gate the detector to run only for cohorts with >=100 rps by default to limit cost."

CI and rollout:
- Initial CI run (2026-01-20): unit tests passed, integration canary-e2e failed intermittently due to a flaky network timing in harness. Failure: canary-e2e/test_harmonic_injection timed out.
- Rerun CI after fix (2026-01-22): adjusted harness timeouts and added retry in test harness; all checks passed (lint, unit, integration, terraform validate).
- Staging rollout: rolled to staging for 48h on Canary tenants group B; observed stabilized rollouts with fewer spuriously blocked cutovers. Metrics recorded in perf-canary: spectral_congruence_score reduced noisy alerts by ~62% during the window.

Operational guidance (summary):
- Default thresholds tuned conservatively: require spectral_congruence_score > 0.72 for 3 consecutive windows and a minimum cohort traffic of 100 rps before warn state.
- Cutover stabilizer enforces a 15-minute cooldown after a forced block and uses exponential backoff (1m -> 2m -> 4m -> 8m) between state promotions to prevent thrashing.
- Runbook: see runbooks/spectral-cutover-playbook.md for triage steps, metrics to inspect, and rollback instructions.

Compatibility and limitations:
- This detector complements existing percentile/fingerprint detectors; it does not replace them — it provides an orthogonal signal that helps identify periodic or oscillatory regressions.
- Not recommended for cohorts with extremely irregular traffic (<10 rps) due to poor PSD fidelity. We gate detection based on minimum traffic.

Related work and links: ENG-5123 (Linear): initial spec and operator story; architecture note in docs/canaries/spectral-congruence.md.

If there are follow-ups: add an adaptive band-selection mode (learned band weighting per-cohort) and a tenant-cost-gating flag for high-volume customers.

Add a spectral-congruence canary detector that compares frequency-domain fingerprints across cohorts; add a cutover stabilizer to reduce flapping during noisy rollouts.

payload.body:
Background: we see recurring noisy tail regressions that only surface when traffic composition shifts (short-text vs long-context, embedding vs generation), which the current percentile canaries either under-react to or produce excessive false positives. Goal: introduce a detector that measures variance across percentiles (a percentile-variance heatmap) and an adaptive replay system that replays stratified micro-bursts from live traces to stress candidate variants deterministically. This PR implements the detector, a lightweight replayer service, integration hooks into the rollout controller, and observability artifacts.

What this PR does: adds a percentile-variance heatmap detector (sliding-window, decay-weighted), exposes heatmap-score and contribution breakdown metrics, implements an adaptive stratified-probe replayer that reconstructs representative bursts by traffic slice, hooks a new evaluation step into the canary pipeline that runs replay probes against new variants, introduces a new rollout guard that combines heatmap thresholds + replay pass/fail signals, exposes a Grafana heatmap dashboard and alert that uses a composite signal, and wires the feature behind a feature flag (perf.heatmap_canary).

Why it matters: the heatmap captures dispersion across percentiles (e.g., simultaneous shift at p50 and p99) which is hard to detect with single-metric detectors; the replayer enables deterministic validation of suspected regressions so we can avoid noisy automated rollbacks while still failing fast on real degradations.

Implementation notes: detector implemented in perf-canary/src/heatmap_detector.go using an incremental KD-style binning for percentiles to keep memory bounded; replayer implemented as an independent process (perf-canary/replayer/) that pulls hashed request signatures and sampled KV caches from the probe broker, reconstructs sequences with preserved inter-arrival times for micro-bursts, and emits structured replay results (latency distributions, token-level error rates). Rollout controller integration: new canary step `heatmap_replay_evaluation` added to pipeline DSL; policy supports soft-hold (pause weight increase) and auto-throttle (reduce concurrency) to allow graceful mitigation during marginal failures.

Backward compatibility and safety: default thresholds are conservative; feature is opt-in via feature flag and Linear ticket triggers for production enable. Replayer does not store raw payloads — only hashed request signatures and anonymized length buckets.

Testing done: unit tests for detector math and decay windowing, integration tests that run replayer against synthetic traffic shapes in perf-lab (short-text long-text mixed, spike/decay patterns), staging end-to-end smoke (canary run at 5% traffic against mock variant), and load-run against dedicated GPU nodes to validate performance overhead (observed <1.5% extra CPU and negligible GPU impact). Added replay fixtures and golden files in tests.

Rollout plan: behind feature flag in main; enable in perf-canary staging for 48h, then gradual enable on canary rollouts (5% -> 25% -> 50%) with automated hold if heatmap_score > 0.18 or replay_failures > 2 in the sample window. Operational runbook added to docs/canaries/percentile_variance.md.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement detector algorithm and metrics emission
- [x] Implement stratified probe replayer and local harness
- [x] Integrate evaluation step into canary pipeline DSL
- [x] Add dashboard and alert panels
- [x] Unit & integration tests
- [x] Run staging canary + smoke tests
- [x] Add rollout runbook and feature flag

Limitations & TODO:
- Thresholds are currently tuned on internal lab traces; we will run an adaptive calibration job (follow-up) to tailor thresholds per-customer traffic profiles.
- Replayer currently supports a limited set of request shapes; adding multimodal fixtures (image/audio) is tracked in ENG-8139.

Related linear/jira: ENG-8124, ENG-8139, PM-341.
Arjun Rao (2026-02-20): Could you add more detail on how the heatmap thresholds are derived and whether they'll be per-customer? Requested: add a calibration job and document defaults.
Maya Chen (2026-02-21): Added calibration follow-up ENG-8139 and documented default conservative thresholds. The detector emits per-customer baseline stats to support later auto-calibration.
Sofia Martinez (2026-02-24): Replayer looks good but we need a privacy review sign-off for trace materials. Please confirm only hashed signatures are stored.
Maya Chen (2026-02-24): Confirmed in description and replayer code comments: raw payloads never persisted, only hashed request signatures and anonymized length buckets. Added a unit test asserting hashing pipeline.
Noah Klein (2026-02-26): CI flake on replayer integration; reran jobs and inspected logs. Approve after green CI.
CI Bot (2026-03-02): Integration job retried and passed. All checks green.

payload.body:
Motivation: perf-canary must never emit or persist customer data. While the canary uses synthetic prompts, we still had a few sharp edges where (a) debug logging could print request bodies on errors and (b) some error/reporting paths would include raw prompt text / user-provided identifiers if they ever slipped through config. This PR adds explicit redaction + hard assertions so we fail-closed and keep logs/metrics safe. Summary of changes: (1) Introduce a centralized redaction helper for log fields and error payloads; (2) Add runtime assertions that enforce "synthetic-only" prompt sources (no external prompt injection), with an opt-out only for local dev; (3) Ensure we never log request bodies, prompt strings, or headers that may contain identifiers; (4) Add "safe fields" allowlist for alert webhook payloads so incident-bot never receives prompt content; (5) Add tests that simulate error paths (HTTP 4xx/5xx, timeouts, JSON decode errors) and verify log output + alert payload are redacted; (6) Add lightweight "no_pii" static checks on structured logging calls in canary request loop. Operational notes: if assertions trip in prod, the canary request will be dropped and counted under canary_safety_dropped_requests_total with reason=no_pii_guard; the process stays healthy and continues other model targets. Checklist: [x] No prompt strings in logs on success/error paths [x] No customer identifiers in metrics labels [x] Alert payload contains only model/region/version/baseline/observed deltas + links [x] Unit tests for redaction + guardrails [x] Docs note in README about dev-only override. Risk: low/medium; touches error handling and logging. Rollout: safe to deploy alongside existing canary; no config change required. Follow-ups: add a prometheus metric for redaction_invocations_total to track unexpected surfaces; consider moving dev-only override behind a build tag.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: Continuous perf canaries detect regressions early, but noisy production signals (traffic bursts, distribution shifts) lead to false positives and noisy alerts. This PR introduces a replay-driven canary orchestrator that captures stratified, anonymized production traces and replays them deterministically against candidate binaries in an isolated harness. The approach reduces false positives by comparing matched workloads, provides deterministic tail latency and throughput deltas, and produces a calibrated confidence score that feeds existing rollout guards. Design summary: - New service 'replay-orchestrator' responsible for trace sampling, anonymization, storage, and scheduling replays. - New probe type 'replay-probe' that runs recorded traces concurrently against baseline (deployed) and candidate (head) environments and aggregates latency/throughput distributions. - Stratified slicing by traffic signature (route, payload size, user cohort) to surface targeted regressions. - Confidence model: bootstrap-based comparison on high-percentile latencies with false-discovery-rate controls. - Integrations: rollout guard API, perf-canary dashboard, tracing/metrics pipeline (prometheus + jaeger), RBAC. Key changes in this PR: - services/replay-orchestrator: new service, scheduler, worker pool (Go). - perf-canary/agents/replay_probe.go: probe implementation and orchestration API. - perf-canary/harness: deterministic replay harness with KV-cache warmup and sequence-control. - observability: dashboards, new metrics (replay_runtime_ms, delta_p95, replay_confidence). - infra: k8s job templates, S3-compatible artifact storage for traces. Testing and validation: - Unit tests for scheduler, probe logic, and confidence model. - Deterministic replay integration tests using recorded synthetic traffic. - Small-scale production shadow run (stage->prod shadow) for two weeks, followed by a staged rollout. - Load tests to verify harness isolation and resource accounting. Rollout plan and safety: - Initial rollout to canary tier only with max 5 concurrent replay probes per cluster. - Auto-pause and open rollback if delta_p95 > 15% with confidence > 0.95 OR throughput drop > 10% and confidence > 0.9. - Manual review gates for high-impact routes. Checklist: - [x] Scheduler + workers implemented - [x] Replay harness deterministic (seeded RNG, KV warmup) - [x] Metrics + dashboards created - [x] CI integration tests added - [x] Security review for trace anonymization - [x] Staged rollout plan documented Related work: builds on ENG-4821 (canary framework refactor) and ENG-5020 (rollout guard API). Known limitations: does not yet support streaming-replay for long-lived sessions; replay storage retention defaults to 7 days configurable per-team.
Adds a replay-driven canary orchestration service that replays sampled production traces against candidate builds to improve regression signal-to-noise. Integrates with rollout guard to pause and rollback on high-confidence regressions.

Aisha Patel (author): We added stratified sampling by route and user cohort to address representativeness. Throttling is implemented at the scheduler (max concurrent per-cluster) and we added cost-based backoff in scheduler.go.
Lina Zhang: Please add telemetry to track how often replays change rollout decisions. Also request an opt-out flag for PII-sensitive teams.

Marcus O'Neill: Minor nit on exponential backoff constants and a request to surface confidence threshold as a runtime config.

payload.body:
Motivation: transient spikes and throughput-coupled latency bumps are already handled by our existing canary detectors, but we observed production incidents where small sustained (minutes-long) latency elevations evaded windowed detectors and caused customer-visible degradation after cutover. This PR introduces the 'eddy' sustained-latency detector: a rate-decoupled, windowed detector that detects persistent latency elevation while resisting short bursts and throughput-driven noise. The detector implements: 1) rate-decoupling by normalizing latency fingerprints against a throughput-derived baseline per shard; 2) temporal persistence requirement (configurable consecutive windows) to avoid one-off spikes; 3) autocorrelation-aware smoothing to reduce sensitivity to periodic jitter; 4) configurable sensitivity knobs (window_ms, consecutive_windows, alpha smoothing). To prevent overreaction during a detected sustained regression, the PR also adds a 'rollback leash' controller that enforces gradual traffic rollback with a budget and cooldown (config knobs rollback_percent_per_minute, rollback_budget_tokens, cooldown_minutes). Implementation summary: added a new detector module perf_canary/detectors/eddy_detector.py (core algorithm + unit tests), integrated detector into the canary evaluator framework with feature flags, added leash control logic in perf_canary/leash_controller.go, plumbing for detector telemetry and traces (metrics names: perf.eddy.p50_delta, perf.eddy.sustained_windows, perf.rollback.leash_progress), and a Helm values flag to enable in clusters deploy/helm/perf-canary-values.yaml. Rollout plan: feature-flagged on staging for 48h with synthetic sustained-latency injection scenarios, canary on 1% traffic for 2h, then 10% for 4h, observe p95/p99 and rollback events. Test plan: unit tests for detector math, integration tests in tests/integration/test_eddy_probe.py that exercise rate-decoupling under varying throughput, and an end-to-end canary simulation harness run in perf-canary CI. Performance impact: detector is O(1) per shard per window; measured CPU delta on a staging prober ~0.15% and memory <10MB. Backwards compatibility: disabled by default; no breaking config changes. Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4821/eddy-detector-design, Linear ENG-4821 is referenced in the PR. Checklist: [x] design doc linked [x] unit tests added [x] integration tests added [x] CI green after re-run [x] docs (design + knobs) added.
Camila Ortega: Request changes - tighten default consecutive_windows from 4->3 and add unit test that simulates throughput ramp to validate rate-decoupling. Also ask for clearer metric naming to avoid collisions.
Jordan Park: Addressed - updated default consecutive_windows to 3, added test case test_rate_decouple_ramp in tests/integration/test_eddy_probe.py, and prefixed eddy metrics with perf.eddy.*
Noah Patel: Approved - sanity-checked the leash backoff math and the cooldown behavior. Asked to add a short comment about budget exhaustion semantics; Jordan added the comment.
Leah Kim: Comment - recommend adding a dashboard slice for cross-shard aggregation. Added dashboards as follow-up work in ENG-4821.
CI: initial run had a flaky test test_canary_runner_timing, rerun succeeded
Jordan Park: Merged via squash after approvals and green CI
Adds a new sustained-latency 'eddy' detector that finds minute-scale latency regressions while ignoring short bursts; introduces a rollback leash to perform budgeted, gradual traffic rollback when sustained regressions are detected; feature-flagged and disabled by default.

payload.body:
Motivation: previous canary fingerprinting treated subscribers independently which produced false positives when short-lived cross-subscriber latency bursts occurred concurrently. This PR adds a correlation-aware fingerprint that factors cross-subscriber covariation and a lightweight peeking buffer so detectors can align windows across moving subscriber streams. Goals: reduce false positives for multi-tenant workloads, surface correlated degradations, and provide a gradual rollout path with safe fallback. Design summary: 1) subscriber window peeking: a bounded in-memory sliding window per logical subscriber that exposes aligned windows to aggregators; peeking is read-only to avoid changing request ordering. 2) correlation fingerprint: compute pairwise Pearson covariances on aggregated latency summaries and compress into a fixed-length correlation fingerprint used by the canary classifier. 3) scoring: detector now combines single-subscriber anomaly score and correlation anomaly score with a tunable weight canary.detectors.correlation_weight. 4) safety: feature gated behind canary.detectors.correlation_enabled default false, with fast fallback to legacy fingerprint when correlation module is disabled or OOM is detected. Implementation notes: added a new stream stage subscriber_peek_buffer, implemented correlation_fingerprint module with single-pass incremental covariance estimator to keep memory bounded, added config schema bump v1.13 for the two new properties, added short-circuit paths to ensure sub-ms added latency for normal traffic. Tests and verification: unit tests for covariance estimator and peeking buffer, integration test that injects synchronized latency spikes across three subscribers and asserts reduction in false positive rate compared to legacy detector, e2e perf bench that measures overhead across 1000 concurrent subscribers. Observability and alerts: new metrics canary.correlation_coeff_avg, canary.cross_subscriber_cov_max, canary.correlation_faults_total; dashboard tile added to perf-canary Grafana (grafana/dashboards/correlation.json) and alert rule canary-high-correlation that triggers at correlation_coeff_avg > 0.6 during canaries. Rollout plan: gated behind feature flag and config default false, stage 1 deploy to canary cluster with smoke tests, stage 2 limited traffic rollout to 10% customers with auto rollback if perf-regression-check fails, stage 3 enable by default with monitoring for one week. Related: ENG-4820 covers detector design, ENG-4901 tracks rollout telemetry requirements, SUP-9821 motivated by a customer incident where co-located subscribers caused noisy canary spikes. Backwards compatibility: config bump is additive and safe. Performance impact: negligible steady-state memory and CPU overhead; worst-case when correlation window length is large can cause extra work but bounded by configured window_ms and max_pairs. Why unique: instead of just changing thresholds or window sizes this PR adds cross-subscriber signal awareness which reduces correlated false positives that previous PRs did not address.
Diego Morales: Overall looks good. Please confirm worst-case memory growth and add a defensive cap on pair tracking. Also suggest lowering default correlation_weight to 0.2 until we have more field data.
Asha Patel: Added pair cap of 250 pairs and set default correlation_weight to 0.2, documented rationale in docs/perf-canary/correlation.md. Measured memory bump at 250 pairs is ~1.2MB per detector instance in our test harness.
Ellen Park: Integration test is valuable but flaked once on CI due to timing assumptions. Can we make the injector deterministic or add retry logic?
Asha Patel: Updated integration test to use simulated clock and added retry-based assert to reduce flakiness. Also annotated test with @flaky to assist CI triage if it still flakes.
Add optional correlation-aware canary fingerprint to reduce false positives from synchronized subscriber spikes. Feature is disabled by default and can be enabled via canary.detectors.correlation_enabled. Configurable window and weight parameters added. Safe fallback to legacy fingerprint provided.
