payload.body:
Context and motivation: Recent canary incidents (tracked ENG-3421) showed that upward shifts in request mix during staged traffic ramps and transient downstream slowdowns produced false-positive canary alerts and caused unnecessary rollbacks. This PR adds two related protections: a windowed traffic-shift detector that detects and discounts significant traffic-shape changes during evaluation windows, and a successive-degradation rollout guard that requires regressions to persist across multiple consecutive windows before triggering automatic rollback. Summary of changes: 1) New detector module perf_canary/detectors/traffic_shift_detector.py implementing a sliding-window KL-divergence and chi-squared test on binned request signatures; 2) New guard perf_canary/guards/successive_degradation_guard.py that maintains a short-lived state machine across N windows and only escalates when threshold-crossing occurs K times in a row; 3) Canary config schema extended (canary_schema.yaml) with traffic_shift_window_ms, traffic_shift_threshold, consecutive_failure_count; 4) Instrumentation and tagging updates to emit traffic-shape fingerprints (request_path_buckets, model_size_bucket, token_length_bucket) alongside existing latency/throughput metrics; 5) Integration of guard into canary-runner pipeline: detectors are evaluated after metric aggregation but before final verdict; 6) Unit and integration tests added plus a new e2e scenario simulating staged rollouts with synthetic traffic shifts; 7) Dashboard and alert playbook additions (grafana/dashboards/canary-traffic-shift.json, docs/playbooks/traffic-shift.md). Commits (high-level): - Implement traffic shift detector and unit tests - Add successive-degradation guard and state persistence util - Extend canary config and validation - Hook detectors into canary-runner decision path - Add e2e scenario and flaky-run mitigation - Docs and dashboards update - Address review comments and threshold tuning Changed areas (high level): - perf_canary/detectors/traffic_shift_detector.py (new) - perf_canary/guards/successive_degradation_guard.py (new) - perf_canary/canary_runner.py (modified) - perf_canary/schema/canary_schema.yaml (modified) - tests/unit/test_traffic_shift.py (new) - tests/integration/test_successive_degradation.py (new) - grafana/dashboards/canary-traffic-shift.json (new) - docs/playbooks/traffic-shift.md (new) Tests and CI: Initial CI run: lint/static-analysis passed, unit tests passed, integration tests passed, e2e suite failed (timing-sensitive scenario) with two flaky assertions related to sampler timing. After adding a short jitter and increasing the synthetic load ramp tolerance the e2e suite passed on a rerun. Patch notes in CI: mark two e2e cases as flaky and added a follow-up linear ticket ENG-3490 to harden the harness. Review conversation (summary): - Anika: Asked for rationale behind KL vs simple percentile-based divergence; requested a justification in comments and an example showing noisy upstream vs real traffic-shift. - Author (Maya): Added bench script results in tests and inline docstring explaining why KL plus chi-squared gating reduces sensitivity to tail noise. - Liam: Questioned state persistence window for successive_degradation_guard and suggested bounded memory model; requested max-state TTL. - Author: Implemented TTL of 5 minutes and added a bounded deque with explicit eviction to prevent unbounded memory. - Ravi: Requested explicit rollout annotation when detector suppresses an alert (so ops knows why automatic rollback was skipped). - Author: Added an annotation path and updated the playbook. Approvals and merge: After two rounds of minor changes and one follow-up commit to stabilize e2e timing, Anika and Liam approved. CI green on final run. Merged via squash on 2026-02-22. Backwards compatibility and config: Default behavior is opt-in via canary config flags; detectors are disabled unless traffic_shift_window_ms > 0. This makes the change non-breaking. Follow-ups: ENG-3490 (harden e2e harness), ENG-3515 (tune defaults after 2 weeks of canary telemetry). Operational notes: - New metrics emitted: canary.traffic_shape.kld, canary.traffic_shape.pvalue, canary.guard.successive_degradation.count - Dashboards include a 5/15/60s breakdown and an example playbook for noisy downstreams. - Rollout gating semantics: the guard only triggers an automated rollback when consecutive_failure_count >= configured value; otherwise the canary is marked for manual review. Implementation details for reviewers: - Traffic fingerprinting uses 8 coarse buckets by path, 4 by model size, 6 by token length; these were chosen to balance cardinality vs signal. - Detector computes KL over fingerprints with an adaptive floor to avoid divide-by-zero on rare buckets; chi-squared test is used as a secondary gate for small sample sizes. - Successive-degradation guard persists minimal state keyed by canary_run_id in the ephemeral store used by canary-runner (same store as existing short-lived counters). - Unit tests include parameterized scenarios that simulate noisy tails and true traffic-shifts. - Integration tests include an A/B style rollback simulation. Rollout: This was first enabled for internal perf-canary experiments, then enabled for a subset of customer-facing rollouts behind a feature flag. Observability and alerting: Added annotations and an alert rule that fires an informational alert when a traffic-shift is detected but suppressed (so SRE can triage).
Add traffic-shift-aware canary detector to suppress false positives during staged rollouts; add successive-degradation guard to detect progressive regressions across multiple windows; new config knobs for window duration and required consecutive failures.
Anika: Please add rationale for KL divergence vs percentile approach and an example that demonstrates noise vs real shift.
Maya: Added benchmark script and docstring; included small bench results in unit tests.
Liam: How is state bounded for successive_degradation_guard? Could this grow unbounded?
Maya: Implemented TTL (5m) and bounded deque eviction; included in unit tests.
Ravi: When detector suppresses an alert annotate the canary so ops knows what happened.
Maya: Added rollout annotations and updated playbook accordingly.
Anika: LGTM after threshold tuning.
Liam: Approved after TTL and eviction changes.

payload.body:
Context: As part of the hardware tuning profiles pack rollout (H100/L40S first, B200 gated), we need perf-canary to catch regressions that only show up when `hardware_profile_pack` is enabled and the runtime selects SKU-specific presets (scheduler/kernels/KV-cache budgets). Existing canary jobs compare runtime builds against a baseline, but they don’t segment by “profile-enabled” vs “profile-disabled”, and alerts are currently too noisy (especially on L40S runners per INT-8832). This PR adds explicit gates for profile-enabled builds, tightens/loosens thresholds where appropriate, and updates alert routing so actionable regressions page the right rotation.

What’s in this PR: (1) New gate group `hardware_profiles_rollout` that runs paired experiments (A/B) with `RUNTIME_ENABLE_HARDWARE_PROFILE_PACK=1` (treatment) vs `=0` (control) for the same build SHA where possible, and evaluates deltas relative to the control; (2) Separate thresholds per GPU SKU (H100 vs L40S) and per workload class (short context, long context, streaming) using the workload matrix runner outputs; (3) Guardrails for tail latency: p95 and p99 decode latency deltas are gated more strictly than p50, and we add an explicit gate on “prefill/decode fairness regression” proxy metrics to catch the class of issues we saw in early H100 validation; (4) Throughput gates: tokens/sec must not regress beyond allowed deltas per workload bucket; (5) Reduced-noise evaluation: bootstrap confidence intervals + minimum sample size, and an “unstable runner” annotation path to avoid failing the PR on known infra flake while still emitting a warning; (6) Alert routing: hardware-profile gate failures route to `#eng-runtime` + `#eng-sre` Slack, and only page `runtime-perf-oncall` when (a) p95/p99 latency gate fails or (b) throughput regression exceeds the “page threshold” for two consecutive intervals.

Thresholds (initial defaults): H100: p50 latency delta <= +3%, p95 <= +5% (streaming: +6%), tokens/sec delta >= -2% (short/medium) and >= -3% (long context). L40S: p50 <= +4%, p95 <= +7% (streaming: +8%), tokens/sec delta >= -3% (short/medium) and >= -5% (long context). Note: L40S long-context has higher allowed variance while we address runner stability (INT-8832) and KV-cache fragmentation variance. B200: gates added but are warning-only unless `ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_B200_PROFILE_GATES=1` is set (this matches the experimental gating strategy for early B200 bring-up).

Operator notes: The alert payload now includes `profile_pack_version`, `selected_profile_name` (if available), SKU, workload bucket, and the exact threshold that triggered. This is intended to speed up triage during staged pool/region rollouts.

Test plan: Updated unit tests for gate evaluation logic; ran `./canary run hardware_profiles_rollout --dry-run` against last 7 days of artifacts; validated alert routing changes in staging Alertmanager; re-ran on L40S runners to confirm we no longer hard-fail on infra flake without a confidence interval.

Rollout: Merge + monitor canary dashboards for 24h; if false positive rate is still high on L40S, we’ll adjust sample sizes and/or widen only the long-context p95 gate while keeping H100 gates strict.
Allison Grant (review): The paging criteria looks right, but can we ensure we don’t page on single-interval blips? Also, please include the threshold values in the alert annotations so oncall doesn’t have to cross-reference the gate file.
Aisha Bello (author): Updated paging to require 2 consecutive failing intervals for throughput paging, and added `threshold`, `measured_delta`, and `workload_bucket` to alert annotations. Pushed commit 4f9c2b1.
Kira Volkov (review): For L40S, the long-context variance is still huge. I’m +1 on warning-only for “unstable runner” but we should avoid masking real regressions. Can we make the flake path require evidence of runner instability (missing GPU perf counters / node reboot) instead of a generic flag?
Aisha Bello (author): Done. The “unstable runner” downgrade now triggers only when the runner emits one of the known instability markers (missing NVML counters, reboot during run, or artifact gaps). Otherwise it fails normally. Added tests + fixture coverage.
Sean Gallagher (SRE review): Routing: please route to #eng-sre (not just #eng-sre-alerts) during rollout week, and add a label for `gate_group=hardware_profiles_rollout` so we can filter dashboards quickly.
Aisha Bello (author): Adjusted routes to include #eng-sre and added `gate_group` label to all emitted alerts for this group.
Sofia Ivanova (runtime scheduling): The “prefill/decode fairness regression” proxy metric name is ambiguous. Can we link to the metric definition and ensure the label includes `mode=streaming|non_streaming`? Tail latency differs a lot for streaming.
Aisha Bello (author): Added a doc link in the gate doc and included `mode` in the emitted series + alert label set. Also split thresholds slightly for streaming vs non-streaming as described in the PR body.
Allison Grant (final): Approved after changes.
Kira Volkov (final): Approved.
Sean Gallagher (final): Approved, please monitor paging volume after merge.
Added profile-enabled rollout gates for latency and throughput with SKU/workload-specific thresholds.
Reduced noisy failures by using bootstrap confidence intervals + minimum sample size and constrained flake downgrade conditions.
Updated alert routing/paging rules for hardware profile rollouts; alerts include threshold + measured deltas for faster triage.

Motivation: We've observed hard 'latency cliff' failure modes where p95/p99 jump sharply within a short window even though rolling averages look stable; these events bypass percentile-based canaries and lead to partial outages. This PR implements a latency-cliff detector that detects rapid percentile deltas across short windows and wires an adaptive-concurrency rollout guard that temporarily reduces per-replica concurrency and pauses rollouts when a cliff is detected. Changes include detector algorithm, integration with the canary evaluation pipeline, a lightweight local load harness for reproducible cliffs, dashboards, and unit/integration tests. Checklist: [x] detector algorithm and unit tests, [x] canary integration and gating, [x] adaptive-concurrency policy and actuator, [x] dashboards and runbook, [x] CI flake fixes. Rollout plan: rollout as a guarded feature flag for 2 weeks, enable in perf-canary staging, monitor metrics and KB/alerts, then enable for canary->prod rollouts. Backwards compatibility: no public API changes; the guard is opt-in via canary config; defaults are off. Performance cost: detector is O(1) per incoming metric update and uses bounded memory. Related: ENG-1428, ENG-1534. Test plan: unit tests cover algorithm edge cases; integration test injects synthetic cliff using examples/load-profiles/stepped-cliff.yaml; manual verification with dashboard in charts/perf-canary-dashboard.json.
Priya: Nice direction; can you limit the detector memory footprint and add a micro-benchmark?
Miguel: Added a sliding-window packed sketch and micro-benchmarks under perf-canary/tests/benchmarks; memory per-detector capped at 48KB - measurement attached.
Ethan: Request to rename metric labels to follow prometheus naming conventions (perf_canary_cliff_delta -> perf_canary_lat_cliff_delta).
Miguel: Renamed metric and updated dashboards, also added a compatibility shim for older dashboards.
Sana: Integration test is flaky on CI (timing); suggested increasing timeout and using deterministic seed. Miguel: increased timeout and added deterministic seed; CI rerun passed.
Priya: Approving after test stability confirmed. 
Adds a latency-cliff detector that flags sudden percentile spikes and an adaptive concurrency rollout guard that reduces per-replica concurrency when cliffs are detected; includes dashboards, runbook, and a load profile example for reproducible tests. Opt-in guard; no breaking API changes.

payload.body:
Motivation: Existing evaluation gates rely heavily on bootstrap intervals and cohort-level aggregates which can mask paired differences on small prompt-sets and make root-cause triage noisy. This PR introduces a paired-permutation significance gate that operates on per-example paired deltas between baseline and candidate, combined with an FDR-controlled per-prompt fault localizer that surfaces which prompts drive the regression signal. The gate is lightweight, deterministic (seeded permutation), and designed to be cheap for CI (default 2000 permutations with early stopping).

What this change does (summary):
- Adds a new CI hook `permutation_paired_gate` that computes a paired-permutation p-value for the mean delta and fails the CI when p < alpha (alpha default 0.01). The gate supports one-sided and two-sided tests and a configurable effect-size guard (Cohen's d).
- Implements a per-prompt fault localizer that ranks prompts by their paired contribution and reports the top-K problematic prompts with summary stats and small example diffs to aid reviewers. Localizer applies Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across prompts to control false positives.
- Integrates the gate into the existing eval orchestration pipeline and adds a lightweight CLI `evalctl gate-run` option to run only the permutation gate locally for debugging.
- Adds unit and integration tests, and a short docs page describing usage, configuration knobs, and rollout guidance.

Checklist: 
- [x] API for paired-permutation test and effect-size guard
- [x] CI hook and config template for repo-level inclusion
- [x] Fault localizer reporter + JSON artifact output for triage UI
- [x] Tests: unit (permutation math), e2e (small synthetic prompt set), CLI smoke
- [x] Docs + migration notes

Implementation notes (details):
- New core routines live in `eval_harness/stat_tests/permutation.py`. We implemented a vectorized permutation routine with early stopping when running mean-of-deltas crosses the critical threshold in more than (1-alpha) fraction of permutations. The implementation uses numpy for speed and explicitly avoids resampling with replacement (we do label-swapping of paired differences).
- The gate wraps the core test in `ci/hooks/permutation_gate.py` and emits two artifacts on failure: (1) `permutation_summary.json` with p-value, observed_mean_delta, effect_size, permutation_trace (sampled quantiles) and (2) `prompt_localizer.json` listing top-20 prompts and per-prompt p-values and corrected flags. The artifacts are intentionally compact to keep CI upload costs low.
- The localizer ranks prompts by absolute paired-delta and computes a per-prompt paired sign test; we then apply Benjamini-Hochberg across all prompts in the set. For small prompt-sets (<30) we fall back to an exact sign test.
- Default permutation count is 2000; for heavy workloads CI config allows lowering to 500 for faster feedback. There is an env var `EVAL_PERM_SEED` to ensure reproducible runs in CI.

Testing and validation: 
- Unit tests cover the permutation engine with deterministic seeds and edge cases (zero-variance prompts, constant deltas).
- e2e integration uses a synthetic prompt-set where we inject known per-prompt regressions; the gate triggers and the localizer lists the injected prompts in the top-3 ranking in 97/100 runs.
- Performance: a 500-prompt paired run with 2000 permutations completes in ~18s on CI's standard runner; we added a micro-benchmark in `tests/bench/test_permutation_bench.py`.

Rollout plan: 
- Stage 1 (canary): enable gate as non-blocking in `eval-harness` repo for two weeks with notifications to #eval-alerts; collect artifacts for false-positive analysis.
- Stage 2: after tuning thresholds and verifying low false-positive rate, flip gate to blocking for PRs that touch `models/` or `infra/` changes.

Migration notes: existing regression gates are unaffected. To opt-in to the permutation gate add a small config snippet to `eval_config.yaml` (example in docs). The gate emits artifacts compatible with the triage UI; product infra already supports the artifact schema.

Related: ENG-2134 (evaluate alternative paired tests), ENG-2178 (CI gating roadmap).
Ravi Singh: Can we reduce default permutations for CI to 1000 and enable an early-exit threshold? (comment)
Asha Patel: I added early stopping and made default 2000 but added note about 500/1000 in CI config; we can adjust after canary (reply)
Elena Morales: Localizer output looks useful—please ensure PII is scrubbed before artifact upload. (request change)
Asha Patel: Added scrubber to reporter and an opt-out flag for example payloads (reply)
Tom Baker: Tests look good; approve pending minor doc wording nits (approve)
Add paired-permutation CI gate and per-prompt fault localizer: new eval gate for paired-significance testing with FDR-controlled prompt localization. Opt-in via eval_config.yaml; artifacts `permutation_summary.json` and `prompt_localizer.json` are produced on failure.
Focus review on statistical assumptions, artifact schema compatibility, and CI runtime. Pay attention to the scrubbing logic in the localizer to avoid leaking prompt contents in public CI runs.

payload.body:
Summary: This PR adds first-pass metric emission for perf-canary runs: end-to-end latency histograms and tokens/sec (plus supporting counters) with per-model attribution. Metrics are emitted from the canary process (not the runtime) so we can alert even when runtime telemetry pipelines are delayed. Motivation: We need low-noise, per-model signals for p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput (tokens/sec) before we can wire dashboards/alerting. This also sets the label policy up front to avoid a repeat of past cardinality blowups (e.g., per-prompt identifiers or unconstrained model strings). Metrics added (Prometheus/OpenTelemetry bridge): perf_canary_request_e2e_latency_ms (histogram; attributes: model_id, model_version, region, tier, hardware_sku, outcome); perf_canary_request_tokens_per_second (histogram; computed from generated_tokens / decode_time; same attributes); perf_canary_generated_tokens_total (counter; same attributes); perf_canary_requests_total (counter; same attributes); perf_canary_metric_dropped_total (counter; attributes: metric_name, drop_reason) to make guardrail drops visible. Cardinality guardrails: model_id + model_version are sourced from control-plane config and validated against an allowlist at startup; we reject/replace unknown model identifiers with model_id="unknown" and increment perf_canary_metric_dropped_total (drop_reason=unknown_model). We also hard-cap unique label sets per process (default 500) to fail closed (drop + log) if someone accidentally adds a high-card dimension. Explicitly not emitted: prompt text, prompt hashes, request ids, customer ids, raw error strings. outcome is normalized to a small enum (ok | timeout | http_error | inference_error | cancelled). Notes: tokens/sec is computed as generated_tokens / max(decode_wall_ms, 1ms) and emitted only for successful runs; for failures we still emit latency + counters to avoid survivorship bias in alerting. Follow-ups: This PR does not include baseline comparison logic (see PR-19218) or region/SKU fanout config (PR-19226).
Logan Wright (review): Please confirm we’re not emitting any free-form strings (errors) as labels; we’ve been burned by this in the past. Also, do we have a way to know if we’re dropping metrics due to guardrails? Omar El-Sayed (author): Good call. outcome is now normalized to a small enum and we explicitly do not include error strings. Added perf_canary_metric_dropped_total with (metric_name, drop_reason) so drops show up on dashboards and can page us if it happens. Nadia Rahman (review): Model label source worries me: if someone configures model_id inconsistently (e.g., alias), we’ll fragment baselines. Can we enforce canonical ids? Omar El-Sayed (author): Updated to pull canonical model_id/model_version from the control-plane config schema; runner rejects values not in the validated canary target list. Anything else becomes model_id="unknown" and increments drop counter (we also warn once per minute to avoid log spam). Allison Grant (review): +1 on the series cap. What’s the default, and can it be overridden without code changes? Also please add a short metrics doc for Grafana/PromQL examples. Omar El-Sayed (author): Default is 500 unique label sets per process; override via PERF_CANARY_MAX_SERIES env var (documented). Added docs/metrics.md with example queries for p95 latency and tokens/sec. Noah Patel (review): tokens/sec computed from decode time only makes sense, but it can be noisy if decode_wall_ms is ~0 for short runs. Make sure you clamp/divide safely and only emit on success. Omar El-Sayed (author): Implemented clamp max(decode_wall_ms, 1ms) and only emit tokens/sec when outcome=ok. We still emit latency for all outcomes. Rina Kobayashi (review): Can we add a test that confirms prompt text never reaches metrics/log fields? Omar El-Sayed (author): Added a guard test around label builder; prompts never enter the metrics package. We also assert that request context does not pass prompt content to emitter APIs.
perf-canary now emits per-model end-to-end latency histograms and tokens/sec metrics with strict label cardinality guardrails and drop counters for visibility.

payload.body:
Introduce Sweep-and-Stitch rollout adapter: a telemetry-first, cohort-handover mechanism for low-risk promotions and automated rollback triggers.
p95 latency +2-5ms in worst-case during handover windows; net cost neutral due to reduced failed-promote rework and improved cache reuse
Summary: Adds a new 'Sweep-and-Stitch' rollout adapter to the rollout orchestrator that performs a lightweight telemetry sweep on shadowed traffic and then stitches cohorts into live traffic with consistency latches. The adapter coordinates short-lived cohort handoffs, session fencing and a small staged drain window to avoid mid-session model swaps. Motivation: Existing promote/pause workflows rely on fixed step timers or simple metric gates which can either delay safe promotions or allow brittle promotes when signals are noisy. Sweep-and-Stitch treats promotion as a two-phase operation: 1) Sweep: send mirrored/shadow traffic slices to the candidate, collect rich telemetry (latency tail, token-level error proxies, structured output diffs, log-level warnings, and eval-set regressions), and compute cohort-specific risk scores. 2) Stitch: for cohorts that pass risk thresholds, perform an atomic cohort handover using a short consistency latch that maintains session affinity and drains session-bound KV caches before full cutover. Design highlights: - Cohort selection: configurable cohort selectors (percent-based, geo, header-pinned, experiment IDs). - Telemetry aggregation: new streaming aggregator produces rolling risk scores per cohort combining latency P50/P95/P99 deltas, error-rate deltas, structured-output drift (via lightweight token-diff heuristics), and eval-set probe results. - Handover latches: latch tokens tied to session IDs ensure in-flight sessions complete on the original model until a drain-window completes; new 'stitch' call in the service API acts as the atomic handoff point. - Safety gates: multi-signal gating with hysteresis, optional manual holdpoints, automatic rollback triggers on expedited regression patterns. - Observability: per-cohort dashboards and a 'handover timeline' trace in the Console showing sweep metrics, pass/fail reasons and KV-cache drain durations. Backwards compatibility: Adapter plugs into the existing rollout runtime via a new adapter interface; if disabled, orchestrator falls back to legacy phased promotion. Tests & validation: - Unit tests for risk-score math and latch semantics. - Integration tests with the shadow bridge harness to validate mirrored traffic sweep and stitch sequence. - Load test in perf-canary that simulates 5000 RPS mixed cohorts verifying p95 latency and drain correctness. - End-to-end dry-run against a staging model using synthetic eval probes. Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind "sweep_stitch_adapter" feature flag and config defaults disabled. - Phased canary: start with 1 customer org on dedicated staging, then 10 internal orgs, then broader. - Monitoring playbook added: alert on stitch failures, reversion events, or prolonged latch durations (>30s). Related work: builds on earlier shadow-verifier and cohort-handshake work (ENG-6121) and ties to the telemetry aggregation pieces in ENG-6932. Motivation ticket: SUP-3321. Implementation notes: - Runtime changes in runtime/service: introduce StitchCoordinator and lightweight in-memory cohort state cache. - Observability in console: new timeline visualization component and per-cohort panel. - API: small addition to rollout API: POST /rollouts/{id}/stitch to trigger the final handover (internal use only). - Security: stitch operations require rollout.write permission; audit events emitted for every stitch and rollback. Operational considerations: - Handover latch increases short-term memory usage to maintain session mappings for the drain window; configured default latch TTL is 60s. - To minimize cost, the sweep phase samples mirrored traffic with adaptive sampling driven by request diversity heuristics.
Amit Varma: Strong idea. Please add more detail on how risk-score weights are tuned and whether they can be overridden per-customer. Also add a fallback path if the latency signal is noisy.
Riley Chen (author): Added per-customer overrides and a default noise-resistant rolling-mean for latency; documented fallback behavior (legacy phased promote) in the design doc.
Sofia Patel: Concern about latch TTL causing memory retention on busy hosts. Can we make latch TTL adaptive based on session length percentiles?
Riley Chen (author): Implemented adaptive TTL tied to 95th percentile session duration with a max cap; added config knobs and tests.
Jun Park: Tests look good; observed a flaky test in the shadow bridge harness under high concurrency. Please stabilize before merge.
Riley Chen (author): Fixed harness race by introducing deterministic request ordering in the test; re-ran perf canary.
Amit Varma: Approved after fixes. Sofia Patel: Approved. Jun Park: Approved.
Added Playbook: On stitch failures check aggregator signals (latency, error spikes, structured diff), examine latch drain durations, if automated rollback triggered inspect snapshot logs and optionally re-run sweep with increased sampling. Contact oncall: #sre-rollouts.
payload.title: Sweep-and-Stitch rollout adapter with telemetry-driven cohort handover

payload.body:
Motivation: We continue to see spurious canary failures when traffic composition shifts sharply (cold start bursts, client-side A/B traffic shaping) even though core latency distribution for steady-state users remains stable. This PR implements a traffic-shape-aware regression fusion detector that reduces false positives by weighting metric signals by concurrent traffic percentile buckets and by fusing orthogonal detectors (latency percentile drift, request-rate-aware tail risk, and service-time quantile drift) with a probabilistic voting model. Summary of changes: 1) New fusion detector module src/detectors/traffic_fusion_detector.go — computes weighted quantile deltas per traffic-percentile slice, applies exponential smoothing, and outputs a composite regression score; 2) Rollout guard integration internal/guards/traffic_fusion_guard.go — ties detector output to canary policies with configurable thresholds, cooldowns, and auto-rollback windows; 3) Canary simulator test harness tests/canary_sim/traffic_shape_sim.go to reproduce bursty-shape scenarios and validate false-positive rate reduction; 4) Metrics and dashboards dashboards/perf/traffic-fusion.jsonnet and observability hooks in internal/metrics/exports.go; 5) CI/perf job adjustments .github/workflows/perf-canary.yml to include the new sim; 6) Documentation: docs/perf/canary-detectors.md updated with configuration knobs and recommended thresholds. Design notes: the detector buckets traffic by request size, client region, and user cohort signals when available, then computes per-bucket latency quantiles (p50/p95/p99) and derives a weighted aggregate delta using traffic-weighted importance and recency decay. The fusion layer combines evidence from three independent heuristics and produces a calibrated p-value-like score that maps to guard action levels (monitor, warn, fail). Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for detector internals - [x] Integration tests for guard + pipeline - [x] Canary sim scenarios covering skewed traffic shapes - [x] Dashboard + alerting wiring - [x] Performance budget: detector CPU < 3% of canary service on standard instance - [x] Backwards compatible config defaults Rollout and operational notes: default behavior is opt-in via canary config, recommended initial threshold is score>=0.85 to trigger a soft-fail with automated alerting and a 30m cooldown, we expect to tune based on canary traffic in first two weeks after rollout. Migration: no data migrations required, default configs preserve existing detection behavior until enabled. Risks and mitigations: false negatives for extremely low-volume cohorts — mitigated by a minimum-sample guard and an aggregated fallback detector; increased CPU consumption under extreme cardinality — mitigated by a cardinality cap with sampling. Testing and validation: local unit coverage 92%, CI integration job initially failed on a race in metrics exporter causing a flake, fixed by introducing a metrics export mutex and re-ran perf-e2e where the canary sim showed false-positive rate drop from ~6.4% to ~1.1% on historical noisy traces. Related work: follows up on ENG-2319 where per-percentile routing was proposed, and PERF-402 which prototyped multivariate detector fusion. Notes for reviewers: focus on detector calibration math in traffic_fusion_detector.go and the guard thresholds; new sim is intentionally deterministic and includes seeded randomness to make CI reproducible. Manual QA: ran canary against a synthetic service with injected 10% tail latency perturbation and verified guard escalations and rollbacks behave as documented.
Diego Alvarez: please add a short note about how we choose decay constants; suggest exposing as a knob in config and defaulting to 3 minutes — responded and added decay constants to defaults.go
Priya Nair: observed a potential O(N^2) in the bucketing step for high-cardinality client ids, requested a ceiling and sampling strategy — implemented a cardinality cap and added unit tests — author reply: added cap with graceful sampling and documented behavior
Liam O'Connor: can we measure detector CPU under high load? suggested a microbenchmark — added tools/bench/traffic_fusion_bench.go and included results in PR description; CI perf job shows CPU at ~2.2% of canary service under test
Introduce a traffic-shape-aware regression fusion detector and an opt-in rollout guard. Reduces false-positive canary failures during skewed traffic patterns; opt-in via canary config. No breaking changes.
payload.title: Add traffic-shape-aware regression-fusion detector and rollout guard

payload.body:
Summary: This PR adds a new set of synthetic probes that continuously validate cross-region reachability and request latency between Redwood regions (e.g., us-east -> eu-west). Results are published as (1) Prometheus metrics for dashboards/alerts and (2) a compact, low-cardinality event stream intended for Region Health Service ingestion.

Motivation / context: As part of the Regional Failover Automation Upgrade, Region Health needs an authoritative reachability signal that is independent of application-level error rates (which can be noisy) and provides faster detection of hard network / DNS / control-plane reachability issues. These probes are designed to answer: “Can region A establish a connection to the public/edge endpoint of region B, complete TLS, and receive a minimal response within a fixed budget?” This is intended to be a top-priority corroboration signal in the failover trigger hierarchy (ADR-042).

What this does:
- Adds a probe runner that executes a matrix of source_region -> target_region checks on a fixed cadence with jitter.
- Implements two probe types:
  1) tls_handshake: raw TCP connect + TLS handshake to the region’s edge endpoint.
  2) http_healthz: HTTPS GET to a minimal endpoint ("/healthz" on the regional edge) with an internal token, expecting 200.
- Exports metrics:
  - perf_canary_reachability_success_ratio{source_region,target_region,probe_type}
  - perf_canary_reachability_latency_ms_bucket{source_region,target_region,probe_type}
  - perf_canary_reachability_error_total{source_region,target_region,probe_type,error_class}
- Publishes events to an internal topic for Region Health ingestion (no customer payloads). Event payload is intentionally minimal and stable:
  - timestamp, source_region, target_region, probe_type, ok (bool), latency_ms, error_class
  - NOTE: error_class is an enum (dns, connect, tls, timeout, http_4xx, http_5xx, other) to avoid exploding label cardinality.

Design notes / guardrails:
- Cadence: 10s base with ±2s jitter per source/target/probe_type.
- Timeouts: connect 800ms, tls 1200ms, http total 2000ms (configurable).
- Retry policy: no immediate retries (to avoid amplifying brownouts); next scheduled run only.
- Cardinality: labels limited to (source_region,target_region,probe_type,error_class). No per-host / per-IP labels.
- Auth: uses an internal canary token scoped to the health endpoint only (no access to customer traffic). Token is loaded from the perf-canary secret store; no plaintext in config.
- Failure handling: runner is resilient to partial config; missing target list logs a warning and continues.

How to consume:
- Region Health Service should ingest events (preferred) or scrape metrics (fallback). The event stream is intended to be treated as “reachability evidence” and combined with other signals (5xx burn, tail latency burn, capacity). For initial rollout, SRE will use this to power the reachability panels in the failover signal dashboards and as a corroboration requirement for automated failover decisions.

Testing:
- Added unit tests for:
  - region matrix expansion (including exclusion rules)
  - timeout classification -> error_class mapping
  - event schema serialization and backward-compatibility guard (golden test)
- Manual staging validation:
  - Deployed to perf-canary-staging in us-east + eu-west
  - Verified metrics appear in Prometheus and events appear on topic perf-canary.reachability.v1
  - Induced a controlled DNS failure for one target; confirmed error_class=dns and that latency histograms do not get polluted with sentinel values

Rollout plan:
- Merge to main and deploy to staging first.
- Production enablement behind feature flag PERF_CANARY_CROSS_REGION_PROBES (default off).
- After 24h stable in staging, enable in prod for (us-east, eu-west) only.
- Expand to remaining regions after Region Health Service confirms ingestion stability.

Notes / follow-ups:
- Follow-up PR planned to add a small “quorum evaluator” helper (e.g., 3-of-5 OK) for downstream consumers; keeping this PR focused on producing clean signals.
- We should align final timeout budgets with DNS TTL changes (see infra risk thread) once those land.

Links:
- Linear: ENG-2417 (perf canary probes), ENG-2413 (region health service), ENG-2418 (metrics/alerts)
- Related: Regional Failover Automation Upgrade umbrella (ENG-2411)
Victor Alvarez (review): Can we distinguish DNS failures vs connect timeouts? We’ve seen provider incidents where DNS is fine but connect stalls. Also please confirm we’re not hitting any customer-facing handler that could be rate limited.
Emily Zhao (author): Added explicit classification for dns/connect/tls/timeout and verified the endpoint is edge /healthz with a dedicated canary auth scope. No customer handler and no per-tenant routing involved.
Allison Grant (review): Metric label cardinality: please do not include error_message or target_host. Also histograms should not include ok=false latencies unless we’re careful with sentinel values.
Emily Zhao (author): Removed error_message label, switched to error_class enum. For failed probes we increment error_total only; latency histogram is observed only when ok=true.
Miles Thornton (review): For downstream failover decisions, we need stable event schema + versioning. Can we add a golden test and pin the topic name/version?
Emily Zhao (author): Added schema_v1 with golden test and set topic to perf-canary.reachability.v1. Documented fields and versioning contract in schema_v1.go.
Ravi Menon (review): Timeouts seem tight for eu-west during load. Do we have config overrides per region pair? Also ensure we’re not retrying aggressively.
Emily Zhao (author): Timeouts are config-driven and can be overridden by pair. No immediate retries; only next scheduled interval. Added jitter to spread load.
CI (bot): flaky test detected in schema_v1_golden_test (ordering) on first run.
Emily Zhao (author): Fixed nondeterministic map iteration by sorting fields before serialization; reran CI.
Victor Alvarez (approval): Approved. Please coordinate with Region Health ingestion owner before enabling prod flag.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved after label/cardinality fixes.
Miles Thornton (approval): Approved. Schema versioning looks good.
payload.title: Add cross-region reachability probes + publish results for region health ingestion

payload.body:
Adds a compact telemetry format and a canonical invocation signal catalog. Improves ingestion throughput and reduces high-cardinality payloads; adds console toolbar to inspect sampled invocation signals and stagewise alert tuning defaults.
Motivation and summary: We have several duplicated ad-hoc invocation signals across services (e.g. kernel_queue_time_ms, kvcache_miss, token_phase_time) and expensive, wide telemetry payloads that increase ingestion cost and slow down aggregation. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: 1) a compactifier module that compresses telemetry at ingest time into a normalized, compact wire format (binary protobuf variant + tokenized key table) to reduce size and parsing overhead; 2) an Invocation Signal Catalog (docs + registry) that defines canonical signal names, standardized units, and recommended aggregation semantics so downstream dashboards/alerts can consume consistent inputs. The change also adds a small Debug Toolbar in the Console to surface sampled invocation signals for a request (helps engineers correlate token-level cost/latency breakdowns with logs/traces) and a set of stagewise alert tuning presets that use the new canonical signals for long-tail SLO detection.

What this contains: compactifier implementation (src/telemetry/compactifier.go) with pluggable codecs and a migration shim; a registry and YAML-backed catalog (internal/observability/signal_catalog.go and docs/observability/signal-catalog.md); Console UI components and a DebugToolbar that fetches sample signals for a given invocation (console/ui/components/TelemetryToolbar.tsx, console/api/telemetry.ts); helm chart additions for optional telemetry-sidecar and feature flag to enable compacted ingestion (helm/telemetry-sidecar.yaml); telemetry ingestion pipeline unit and integration tests (tests/telemetry/compactifier_test.go, tests/ingest/compact-integration.yml); alert rule updates and examples (observability/alerts/stagewise-slo-presets.json).

Backward compatibility and rollout: The compactifier exposes a migration header; older consumers will still see an expanded JSON representation until we flip the feature flag cluster-by-cluster. The catalog registers friendly aliases so existing metric names are mapped to canonical signals incrementally. Rollout plan: enable compactifier in telemetry-ingest staging for 48h, validate size reduction and pipeline latency (expected ~40% payload size reduction), then enable in canary, then global. Feature flags and migration CLI included.

Performance and cost: Local benchmarking on a 10k message sample reduced ingestion bytes by 38-45% (median), CPU cost for parsing in the aggregator reduced ~12% due to smaller allocations and simpler schemas. We measured no regression in 99th percentile ingest latency after sharding and enabling async decode workers.

Testing and validation: unit tests for compactifier codecs and catalog validation; integration test that runs full ingest + decode path; Console e2e test that opens toolbar and asserts sampled fields render. Also smoke tests for alerts to ensure stagewise presets do not fire excessively.

Checklist:
- [x] Compactifier implementation with codecs and migration headers
- [x] Signal catalog with canonical names, units, recommended aggregations
- [x] Console Debug Toolbar to inspect sampled invocation signals
- [x] Helm / sidecar and feature flags for staged rollout
- [x] Tests: unit, integration, console e2e
- [x] Docs: signal-catalog.md and rollout runbook

Risks and mitigations: Main risk is cardinality creep if services add arbitrary keys into the compacted payload. Mitigation: compactifier enforces an allowlist and token table rotation policy; new keys are rejected by default and require a catalog update. We added sampling to prevent heavy traffic from overwhelming the toolbar queries. Another risk is alert regression; stagewise presets are conservative by default and tied to existing SLO baselines.

Related work: follows ENG-1219 (telemetry normalization) and ENG-1402 (console sampled-context UI). Jira SUP-887 tracks a customer case where large telemetry payloads caused delayed alert evaluation.

Migration notes for operators: Use the provided helm/values.telemetry.yaml feature flag (enableCompactifier: true) to opt-in. Monitor consumption.bytes and ingest.decode_latency during the staging window. If the compacted payloads are rejected by old aggregators, toggle decodeFallback=true to let ingest emit expanded JSON alongside compact blob for one window.

Contact: Asha Veer (author) and Miguel Torres (runtime), Priya Nair (console).
Miguel Torres: Left a few nits on compactifier.go – prefer context-aware worker pools and expose metrics for decode queue length.
Jonah Kim: Can we add a sampling guard for toolbar queries? Also please ensure signal unit conventions are explicit in the catalog doc.
Priya Nair: Console styles are fine; please add accessibility labels on the signal table and a toggle to limit fields to canonical list.
Asha Veer: Addressed Miguel's pool comment by adding a bounded worker pool and expose telemetry.compactifier.decode_queue_length histogram (see latest commit).
Merged after approvals and green CI. Toggle plan executed across staging and canary clusters; migration shim left enabled for two days. Observability team to monitor ingest.bytes and alert noise; initial confirmation shows ~40% median payload reduction and no alert regressions.
payload.title: Introduce telemetry compactifier and invocation signal catalog

payload.body:
Context: we observed short-lived latency regressions during staggered canary rollouts that correlate with replica warm-up timing and sporadic KV-cache invalidation. Motivation: current canary detectors can be sensitive to transient phase shifts when a subset of replicas are in different readiness phases, which generates false positives or noisy alerts and can trigger unnecessary rollbacks. This PR introduces two pieces: (1) a phase-aware replica synchronizer that annotates probe traffic with replica phase metadata and enforces a short coordination window to align probe sampling across replicas, and (2) a regression fanout guard that aggregates per-replica canary signals with tunable quorum and temporal smoothing to suppress spurious rollbacks while preserving sensitivity to sustained regressions. Design summary: the synchronizer runs as a lightweight sidecar in the probe runner and tracks replica lifecycle hooks (initialization, warm-up, steady) emitted by the serving runtime; probes in the warm-up phase are tagged and routed into a weighted sampling bucket rather than being directly included in canary statistics. The fanout guard consumes per-replica metric streams and applies a three-stage filter: per-replica anomaly detector (quantile shift with bootstrapped confidence), cross-replica consensus (weighted quorum with phase weights), and temporal dampening (exponential smoothing with configurable half-life). Config knobs: early_quorum_threshold, phase_weight_map, smoothing_half_life_seconds, max-coordinated-delay. Operational impacts: default settings are conservative to avoid masking real regressions; deployment flips are gated by Linear ENG-21345 and require a canary rollout with the sentinel probe enabled. Backwards compatibility: if the sidecar is absent, the synchronizer falls back to legacy behavior (no annotation); the fanout guard has a passthrough mode. Testing & validation: unit tests for phase transitions and weighted quorum logic included; end-to-end perf harness runs show 48% reduction in false-positive rollback triggers during synthetic staggered-rollout scenarios and a <3% increase in probe latency. Rollout plan: enable in opt-in canaries for 2 weeks, monitor false-positive rate and SLO breach delta, then flip global default with a 24-hour canary ramp. Related: builds on prior work in ENG-19702 (canary aggregation) and complements the traffic-shape-aware detector in PRs around staggered rollouts.
Arjun Patel: Nice approach to reduce noise from warm-up replicas. Two requests: 1) add an opt-out flag at runtime in case we need to disable across a region quickly, and 2) add a short doc about how this changes the interpretation of per-replica metrics.
Marta Liu (reply): Added runtime opt-out via --synchronizer-enabled boolean and documented impact in docs/phase_synchronizer.md; left default on for opt-in canaries only.
Diego Ramirez: Fanout quorum looks good. Can you justify the default phase weights (steady=1.0, warm-up=0.2, init=0.0)? Might want to make them relative to observed latency variance.
Marta Liu (reply): Default weights chosen from A/B grid over historical rollouts; added adjustable phase_weight_map and a note in the schema for teams to tune based on measured variance.
Add phase-aware replica synchronizer and regression fanout guard to reduce spurious canary rollbacks during staggered rollouts. Default opt-in for canaries; tunable quorum and smoothing parameters. See perf-canary/docs/phase_synchronizer.md.
When enabling globally, monitor 'canary.false_positive_rate' and 'canary.quorum_disagreements' dashboards for first 72 hours. If you see sustained suppression of genuine regressions, decrease smoothing_half_life_seconds or lower early_quorum_threshold.
Enable feature via canary policy: 'phase_synchronizer: enabled: true' on target canary
Run a staggered-rollout synthetic job (harness/staggered_rollout_test.py) against the canary to validate behavior
Observe dashboards: observability/dashboards/canary_phase_overview.json
payload.title: Add phase-aware replica synchronizer and regression fanout guard

payload.body:
Adds segmented traffic reservoir and staggered rollout guard to reduce false-positive regressions caused by noisy neighbor traffic slices. Backwards compatible; default policy enabled but configurable per-canary.
Motivation: We've seen an uptick in false-positive canary failures when small, high-latency traffic slices (noisy neighbors, churned tenants, spikey integration tests) distort global latency signals. Existing detectors treat traffic as a single stream which amplifies low-volume noise during gradual rollouts. This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: (1) a segmented-traffic-reservoir that preserves per-slice baselines and provides representative sampling for low-volume segments, and (2) a staggered-rollout guard that phases weight increases across segments to avoid correlated blowups.
Design summary: 1) Segmented reservoir: maintains an independent reservoir sampler per traffic slice (routing key: tenant_id / route / region). Each reservoir tracks lightweight quantile sketch state (t-digest) and an EWMA of the 95th/99th percentiles. Reservoir sizes are proportional to slice entropy and capped to bound memory. 2) Adaptive threshold fabric: thresholds are computed per-slice using an EWMA of historical quantiles plus a multiplicative safety margin that shrinks as slice volume grows. 3) Staggered rollout guard: when a canary increases traffic weight, weight ramping is applied per-segment with jittered start times and configurable hold windows. The guard uses slice-level verdicts to compute a global canary decision via a weighted aggregation that downweights low-volume but highly-volatile slices.
- New package perf_canary/reservoir adds SegmentReservoir and SegmentSampler (Rust -> native bindings). - Threshold fabric is implemented as policy nodes under perf_canary/detectors/fabric.rs. - Rollout guard implemented in perf_canary/guards/staggered_guard.{rs,py} and wired into the canary controller. - Console integration: exposes `canary.slice.*` metrics and a `per-segment breakdown` toggle in the Canaries dashboard. - Policy DSL: small additions to canary policy YAML: segment_reservoir:{enabled:true, base_size:512, volume_scale: 0.1}, staggered_ramp:{window_s:120, jitter_s:30, hold_s:300}
segment_reservoir:
  enabled: true
  base_size: 512
  volume_scale: 0.1
staggered_ramp:
  window_s: 120
  jitter_s: 30
  hold_s: 300

Testing: added unit tests for reservoir edge-cases (empty slices, single-sample slices), integration tests that simulate tenant noise and synthetic microbursts, and an e2e scenario that verifies gradual canary wins/rollbacks when a noisy slice spikes. Rollout: enabled behind feature flag perf.segmented_reservoir; staged rollout to 10% of clusters for 48h, monitor canary slice eviction and alerting. Monitoring: new metrics canary.slice.count, canary.slice.evictions, canary.slice.p95_ewma, and guard.staggered.*. Alerts suppressed for slices with volume < 50 req/min by default.
Risk: new per-slice state could increase memory usage and introduce bookkeeping CPU. Mitigations: conservative defaults (base_size 512, max_segments 50k), LRU eviction, and a telemetry-driven kill-switch. We added a circuit-breaker that disables per-slice aggregation under controller memory pressure and falls back to legacy global detector.
Arjun Patel: Nice separation of concerns. Two questions: how do we bound worst-case memory if there are millions of slices? Is there a global eviction policy?
Maya Chen (reply): We cap reservoirs by configurable max_segments and use LRU eviction with a compacted sketch flush to long-term store. The default max_segments is conservative (50k) and we included telemetry to monitor evictions.
Sofia Martinez: The staggered ramp windows look right, but can we make hold_s configurable per-canary? Some customers want longer holds during large deploys.
Maya Chen (reply): Exposed hold_s in the policy DSL and added validation in the controller. Updated docs with example per-canary override.
Diego Alvarez: CI flaked on e2e due to clock skew in the test harness. Please add a clock tolerance in tests.
Maya Chen (reply): Added test harness tolerance and retried CI; included note in test file.
Arjun Patel: Approved after second pass. Marking for squash-merge.
Create dashboard tile: Canaries -> Per-slice breakdown
Add runbook section: noisy-slice-investigation
Monitor evictions metric for 72h after rollout
Announce in #perf-canary with opt-in notes
payload.title: Introduce segmented-traffic-reservoir and staggered-rollout guard for noisy-neighbor mitigation

payload.body:
Adds a probe arbiter service and a probe priority index to improve probe allocation under constrained budgets; introduces a shortfall escrow that stores rollback credits for under-sampled cohorts. Includes new metrics and dashboards; safe rollout by default.
Context: Canary probes are our primary signal for detecting regressions, but high-cardinality and bursty traffic cause probe starvation in some cohorts while others are oversampled. Motivation: reduce missed regressions and noisy false positives caused by uneven probe distribution, without increasing overall probe budget. Design: introduce a lightweight 'probe arbiter' that centralizes short-lived probe decisions. The arbiter maintains a priority index per cohort that combines recent drift score, historic coverage, and probe shortfall debt. When global probe budget is constrained the arbiter favors cohorts with high drift and high shortfall debt. A shortfall escrow mechanism allocates rollback-credit tokens to cohorts that missed probes; tokens can be spent to temporarily elevate priority on subsequent windows, ensuring cohorts eventually catch up. Changes in this PR: 1) new service: perf/canary/arbiter (golang) - core allocation logic and metrics exporter; 2) controller changes to query arbiter before scheduling probes; 3) probe scheduler update to respect escrow tokens and priority index; 4) new Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboards (canary/arbiter-overview, canary/shortfall-heatmap); 5) tests: unit + integration harness that simulates bursty traffic and sparse cohorts. Rollout plan: feature gated behind canary.allocator.v2; gradual ramp (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated monitoring checks for probe availability and false positive rate. If the false positive rate rises by >2x or coverage drops for critical cohorts, automatic rollback triggers. Backwards compatibility: arbiter serves as advisory; existing scheduler can be fallback if arbiter becomes unreachable. Testing: unit tests cover allocation heuristics and token accounting; integration test runs a 24h synthetic traffic replay validating allocation fairness and regression detection F1 score improvement. Motivation: existing canary probes rely on fixed synthetic inputs or direct traffic shadowing which can either overfit to synthetic patterns or perturb production routing. This PR implements a 'stochastic probe multiplexer' (SPM) as a lightweight probe layer that interleaves randomized virtual probes with low-impact production-shaped sampling to isolate rare tail regressions and reduce probe-to-prod mismatch. Goals: 1) improve sensitivity to tail latency/throughput regressions without raising false positives from synthetic-only probes, 2) avoid meaningful interference with production traffic and SLOs, 3) produce richer feature vectors for the canary evaluator to support quorum-based rollback decisions. What this change does (summary): - Adds a new probe coordination service (perf/canary/probe_mux.py) that defines virtual probe streams, randomized offsets, and multiplexing policies. - Implements sampling kernels that shape virtual probe payloads to observed traffic histograms (perf/canary/sampler.py). - Integrates multiplexed probe signals with the canary evaluator (perf/canary/evaluator.rs bindings updated) so that probe-origin metadata is preserved end-to-end. - Adds permutation-test based anomaly scoring and a quorum gate to the canary decision logic (perf/canary/quorum_gate.py). - Dashboard and alerting updates (dashboards/canary_probe_mux.yaml) and lightweight synthetic fixtures for CI (tests/probe_mux_test.py). Backwards compatibility & safety: SPM runs disabled by default. When enabled for a canary rollout, it respects per-customer rate caps and can be configured in the rollout policy (default: <0.1% of requests as virtual probes, randomized across zones). The module supports 'dry-run' mode to surface signals to observability without affecting routing. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed with SRE and evaluator team (ENG-1879) - [x] Unit + integration tests added and passing - [x] Feature flag gated and opt-in via rollout policy - [x] Dashboard and alerting updated - [x] Load safety checks (per-zone rate caps) implemented Performance notes: Initial lab runs on a 48-GPU perf bench with mixed short/long sequences show 2-4% improvement in detection time for injected tail regressions at equivalent false positive rates versus the existing synthetic-probe baseline. See perf results in the commits. Rollout plan: start as opt-in on internal canary clusters for 2 weeks, then gradually enable on canaries with high variance workloads. Related: references SUP-4421 incident postmortem where single-shot synthetic probes missed a multi-modal tail shift. Risks & mitigations: randomization increases complexity in debug — all probes include canonical trace ids and probe descriptors; dry-run mode avoids routing changes; quorum gate favors conservative rollback thresholds by default.
Arun: overall design looks good; please add a short section describing how probe payloads are sampled from production histograms. Maya: added sampler module and inline docs; see sampler.py. Leah: CI flakes on macos_py37; please pin the fixture timestamps to avoid clock skew. Maya: fixed test to use monotonic timers and added a second integration run. Jonas: minor nit — prefer quorum gate default to 3-of-5 rather than 2-of-3 for noisy workloads. Maya: bumped quorum to 3-of-5 and added rollout flag to override. Arun: approving after test flake fix and quorum change. Leah: approving. Jonas: approving. Automated CI: perf-check passed, unit tests passed, lint passes. Merge: squash and merge performed by Maya after approvals.
Introduce stochastic probe multiplexer (opt-in) to improve detection of rare tail regressions with minimal production impact. Configurable via canary rollout policy; dashboard and gates included.

Motivation: improve canary probe efficiency and reduce probe-induced noise during rollouts by composing sequential probes and allocating cutover budgets adaptively based on recent telemetry. This change introduces a Sequential Probe Compositor that stitches short-window synthetic probes into prioritized sequences to better surface phase-aligned regressions, and an Adaptive Cutover Allocator that computes per-rollout cutover budgets using traffic-conditioned stability scores and SLO-weighted credits. Key goals: lower false positives from probe collisions, preserve signal fidelity for tail latency, and enable safer gradual cutovers for large traffic shifts. Adds a new entropy-based degradation fence to detect distributional degradation during canary rollouts; no behavioral changes to existing APIs. Ops: new alert and dashboard created.
Summary: Introduces a Rolling Entropy Degradation Fence for canary rollouts. Motivation: percentile-based checks (p50/p95/p99) miss subtle distributional shifts where tails shift gradually or mass moves between latency modes. This PR implements an adaptive entropy-based detector that measures changes in the latency/throughput histogram distribution over a rolling window and fences rollouts when sustained distributional degradation is detected.

Design and behavior: The detector bins observed latency samples into an adaptive histogram (dynamic bucket sizing based on observed percentiles) and computes a rolling Shannon entropy plus a KL-divergence/JS-distance to a baseline histogram. We combine three signals: (1) instantaneous entropy change, (2) KL divergence to baseline, and (3) a sustained drift score computed with exponential decay. A canary fence is tripped only when the composite score exceeds the configured threshold for a configurable duration (default 5 minutes) and when traffic-weighted significance passes a minimal-sample check. The fence triggers: (a) pause rollout (canary traffic frozen), (b) escalate to oncall via alert channel, (c) automatically snapshot recent traces for post-mortem.

Implementation notes: - New module perf_canary/entropy_fence.py implements histogram maintenance, entropy/KL computation, smoothing and scoring. - A lightweight online estimator avoids storing raw samples; uses reservoir sampling for rare-event amplification in tail buckets. - Exposes config knobs via canon canary config: window_seconds, bucket_count, min_samples, entropy_threshold, kl_threshold, sustained_seconds. - Integration with existing rollout-control API: rollout_guard.plug('entropy_fence') returns decisions with reason codes and signal payload for observability. - Dashboard: dashboards/entropy_fence.json added with example panels (entropy timeseries, KL, composite score, sample counts). - Tests: unit + small integration tests under tests/test_entropy_fence.py and a synthetic load test script scripts/load/entropy_sims.py.

Compatibility & ops: Defaults are conservative (low false-positive rate). Gate-added to default canary guard chain but disabled for legacy customers via config flag. No schema changes to persisted canary objects. New IAM role not required.

Risks & mitigations: Entropy can be noisy on low-sample traffic; we added min_samples gating and sample-weighted smoothing. We also include a backoff and auto-unfreeze after manual-confirmation window if team marks event as false-positive.

Testing & validation: Local unit tests + simulated traffic scenarios included. We ran a two-week shadow run on internal staging (release/2026-02 staging) and verified zero false positives on normal traffic, detected 3 injected drift scenarios (gradual tail shift, bimodal shift, traffic-mode flip) and produced actionable signal.

Notes: This approach is complementary to existing percentile and trajectory detectors; recommended to use together for improved sensitivity to silent shifts.
Owen Patel (reviewer): The histogram bucket sizing looks good, but can we explain why we chose JS vs KL in the code comments? Requested a short rationale and a small refactor to make distance function pluggable.
Maya Chen (author): Added doc comment and made distance computation pluggable with default to JS for symmetry; pushed commit b4c22e7.
Liang Wu (reviewer): Please add a gating check for low-sample windows; entropy can spike on sparse traffic and we'd get noise in small tenants. Left a TODO that became a test request.
Maya Chen (author): Implemented min_samples gating, added unit test, and documented the default conservative thresholds. Pushed c91f5d4.
Priya Natarajan (reviewer): Integration with rollout-control API looks clean. One suggestion: expose the composite score in telemetry with reason codes for easier alert triage. Added a small nits list.
Maya Chen (author): Exposed composite_score and reason_code in telemetry events, updated dashboard panels, pushed f2a7d58.
CI system: integration-tests rerun required after test flake; reran and all checks passed.
Priya Natarajan (reviewer): Approve after CI green. Approved.

Summary: Introduces an adaptive spline-based baseline estimator for temporal nonstationarity and a lightweight hedged-fallback sentinel that automatically stages fallback traffic and graceful backpressure when small-but-persistent regressions are detected.
Motivation: existing canary detectors are brittle against slow drifts in traffic shape (diurnal load, request size shifts) which inflate false positives. The spline baseline models the smooth trend at multiple time-scales so the detector focuses on short-term deviations rather than long-running baselines. The hedged fallback sentinel provides a low-latency mitigation path: when the detector signals a soft regression, we simultaneously route a small hedged fraction of traffic to a fallback model/replica pool while continuing evaluation; if the hedge shows stable improvement we widen failover, otherwise we gracefully revert and record diagnostics.
Design highlights:
- Adaptive spline baseline: multiscale B-spline smoother with automatic knot density adaptation driven by traffic curvature; uses online incremental updates and O(1) amortized per-sample cost. Configurable windows: short (1m), mid (15m), long (3h).
- Residual whitening: residuals are normalized by a dynamic variance estimate to avoid spike sensitivity.
- Probabilistic drift detector: gaussian-mixture residual model with temporal decay; outputs a continuous anomaly score and calibrated p-value.
- Hedged fallback sentinel: traffic hedging controller that maintains a target hedge-rate (default 5%), runs A/B style evaluation on hedged traffic, collects latency/qps/quality metrics and computes an expected-value score for progressive failover.
- Graceful backpressure: when backend capacity is constrained, hedged controller enforces soft throttles and signals autoscaler hints.
- Observability: new dashboards and span tags: canary.spline_baseline.*, sentinel.hedge.*. Alerts for persistent hedges and high rollback churn.
Checklist:
- [x] Algorithm implementation
- [x] Unit tests for spline updater and detector
- [x] Integration test against synthetic diurnal traffic generator
- [x] Canary dashboard panels and alert rules
- [x] Docs: design doc and operator runbook
- [x] Performance microbench (latency overhead < 2%)
- [x] Safety: default-off hedging for mainline until opt-in
Deployment plan: landed feature behind feature flag perf.spline_baseline.enabled=false by default; canary rollout to perf-canary stage cluster for 48 hours using gradual ramp policy.
Related: builds on theory in ENG-9876; incident SUP-4321 motivated hedging fallback after 2026-01-28 degradation.
Commits:
- a1b2c3d: initial implementation of adaptive spline baseline, unit tests
- b4c5d6e: add drift detector + variance normalization, CI tests
- c7d8e9f: hedged fallback controller, dashboards, runbook docs
Changed files (high-level):
- perf-canary/src/baseline/spline_estimator.py
- perf-canary/src/detectors/probabilistic_drift.py

- perf-canary/integration/tests/diurnal_integration_test.py

Notes on code: spline_estimator.py contains an incremental knot-adjustment routine, with a small bounded in-memory ring buffer per time-scale. Detector uses an exponential-decay window for moments and fits a two-component gaussian mixture online. Hedged controller exposes an HTTP control endpoint for dynamic hedge-rate tuning and emits prometheus metrics: perf_canary_hedge_rate, perf_canary_hedge_latency_ratio, perf_canary_hedge_quality_delta.
Testing & CI:

Review thread (chronological):

- Marina (author): "Answered inline; added unit test knot_density_test.py and microbench; worst-case mem ~120KB per worker per time-scale, CPU 4% at 2k qps in our microbench."

Summary: This PR adds tier-aware SLO gating to perf-canary for the Workload-aware Batching Defaults launch. We now fail the perf-canary run if: (1) FAST tier p99 latency regresses beyond threshold (tail-latency protection gate), or (2) STANDARD tier p95 latency regresses beyond threshold (steady-state gate). The intent is to stop merges that silently violate the published tier SLOs while still allowing legitimate improvements to land with a controlled baseline refresh process. Motivation: As we move batching config from ad-hoc per-route knobs to three customer-facing tiers (fast / standard / cost-efficient), we need CI guardrails that match what we’ll ship. Previously, canary gating was based on a single aggregate p95 and a single scenario per model. That missed fast-tier tail regressions (p99) and could overreact to noise in standard tier when concurrency ramps changed. What changed (high level): (1) Adds a tier_slo_gates.yaml config describing which percentile to gate on per tier, thresholds, and the scenario → tier mapping. (2) Extends the results parser to ingest tier labels from benchmark-lab output (scenario metadata), and compute per-tier regression deltas against the stored baseline. (3) Adds a baseline refresh workflow with explicit approvals, including a short “baseline justification” note that is stored next to the refreshed baseline file. (4) Adds a regression triage runbook tailored for tiered batching: how to distinguish scheduler regressions vs workload-mix drift, and what artifacts to attach to the Linear issue. Details: Gating rules: FAST tier: gate on p99 end-to-end latency, primary metric = request_latency_ms (includes queue + prefill + decode), scenario group = mixed_workload_streaming_shortprefill + mixed_workload_nonstreaming_shortprefill. Threshold default = +6% relative regression OR +25ms absolute (whichever triggers first) with a minimum sample size requirement. STANDARD tier: gate on p95 end-to-end latency, scenario group = mixed_workload_balanced + summarization_mediumprefill. Threshold default = +5% relative regression OR +35ms absolute. Note: COST-EFFICIENT tier is intentionally not a merge-blocking gate in this PR; we still compute and report it, but it only posts a warning annotation. This matches the staged rollout plan and avoids blocking on known variance for aggressive batching experiments. Noise controls: (a) sample-size gate: if we have < N requests for a tier/scenario, the gate is “insufficient data” and does not fail the run (but posts a warning). (b) warm-up exclusion: ignore first K requests in each scenario to reduce cold-start variance. (c) optional “max allowed stddev” heuristic (disabled by default) included behind a flag for future tuning. Baseline refresh process (new): We now store baselines under baselines/<model_family>/<hardware_class>/baseline.json and include a matching baselines/<...>/baseline.meta.txt with: timestamp, perf-canary run URL, benchmark-lab revision, and a one-paragraph human summary of why the refresh is safe (e.g., “intentional latency improvement due to scheduler tweak”). To refresh: run ./scripts/refresh_baseline.sh --model-family llama --hw h100 --scenario-set tiers --run-id <canary-run> then open a PR containing only baseline files + meta. That PR must have approvals from one Runtime reviewer and one SRE reviewer. Regression triage notes (new docs): Added docs/regression_triage_tiered_slo.md. Key guidance: verify the tier label in the artifact, check queue depth & batch-size distribution in the attached benchmark-lab plots, compare streaming vs non-streaming deltas (fast-tier p99 is usually driven by admission/wait budget), and tag the resulting Linear issue with runtime+slo-gate. Also includes “when to refresh baseline” vs “when to block merge and fix” decision table. Changed areas/files (high level): - config/tier_slo_gates.yaml: new canonical gating config - src/gating/tier_slo_gate.py: new tier-aware gate implementation - src/results/parser.py: scenario metadata → tier mapping + percentile extraction - src/cli.py: new flags for tier gating, warm-up exclusion - scripts/refresh_baseline.sh: baseline refresh helper + guardrails - docs/baseline_refresh.md: refresh procedure + required approvals - docs/regression_triage_tiered_slo.md: triage playbook - .github/workflows/perf-canary.yml: upload tier gate summary, annotate PRs Commit summary: 1) parser: ingest scenario metadata and emit tier breakdown 2) gating: implement fast p99 + standard p95 gates w/ thresholds 3) scripts/docs: add baseline refresh + triage docs 4) workflow: upload artifacts + PR annotations Validation: - Ran on 6 recent canary runs for top model families; no false failures after warm-up exclusion and sample-size checks - Verified that a known fast-tier p99 regression (synthetic +12% added wait budget) fails the gate - Verified that a known standard-tier improvement (scheduler prefill/decode split change) passes and baseline can be refreshed cleanly Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Add an optional gate for COST-EFFICIENT tier once variance is reduced (likely after we stabilize queue backpressure heuristics) - Integrate “reason codes” (profile selection telemetry) into the canary report when available from runtime 1.22 - Expand coverage to additional regions/hardware classes once Dedicated fleet baselines exist
Review notes: Sean Gallagher (SRE): Can we ensure this won’t page people for noise? I’m worried about p99 being unstable on low-volume scenarios. Also, can we make sure insufficient-data doesn’t fail merges. Sahana Iyer (author): Yes — insufficient-data is a warning only; the gate only fails if we have >= min_samples. I also added warm-up exclusion and kept absolute+relative thresholds to reduce sensitivity. Rafael Mendes: Baseline refresh needs an explicit paper trail. Can we require a meta note and link to the canary run? Sahana: Added baseline.meta.txt and made the refresh script fail if run URL / benchmark-lab rev is missing. Also documented required approvals (Runtime + SRE). Marcus Reed: Scenario→tier mapping: where is it defined? I don’t want it diverging from benchmark-lab. Sahana: Mapping lives in config/tier_slo_gates.yaml but keys are scenario names produced by benchmark-lab. Added a small unit test to fail if unknown scenario appears without a mapping (forces update). Allison Grant: Please keep metric names consistent with observability-pack; also ensure we don’t explode labels in annotations. Sahana: Annotations only include tier + percentile + delta; no model×region fanout in the GitHub comment. CI failures during review: - 2026-03-12: lint failed (shellcheck on refresh_baseline.sh) → fixed quoting + set -euo pipefail - 2026-03-14: unit test flake on parser test due to unordered dict → normalized sort - 2026-03-16: workflow permissions issue uploading artifact → updated permissions: actions:read, contents:read, checks:write Final approvals: Sean Gallagher, Marcus Reed, Rafael Mendes. Merge: Squash merged to main after green canary run 2026-03-18 (run id: pc-20260318-1127).
