Context: During an incident on 2026-02-02 we observed tenants being effectively starved when a transient regional control-plane hiccup triggered an ephemeral 'region bypass' flow. The bypass path was designed to let healthy regions accept traffic while a small set of nodes in the affected region drained, but a race and an over-aggressive weighted-shed calculation amplified shedding for medium-priority tenants. This PR fixes the race and restores the intended fairness guard.

Motivation: Prevent tenant starvation and improve survivability of hosted inference for partial-region outages. Avoid cascading degraded quality (higher latency + dropped requests) caused by incorrect weight normalization and incorrect bypass window semantics.

What I changed (summary):
- runtime/election/region_bypass.go: tighten ephemeral bypass window semantics and add deterministic tagging so a region bypass has a clear open/close lifecycle (avoid lingering bypass tags that caused double-shedding).
- runtime/shedder/weighted_shedder.go: clamp intermediate scores, normalize per-tenant weight contributions, and reintroduce a minimum-fairness floor that prevents cumulative shed probability from exceeding expected bounds for mid-tier tenants.
- Added comprehensive unit tests and an integration test that simulates a two-region failover with staggered reinstate to reproduce and validate fix.
- observability: emit bypass_count, bypass_window_ms, per_tenant_shed_rate metrics and structured bypass events for post-incident analysis.
- controllers/failover: ensure orchestrator acknowledges 'bypass closed' signals only after KV sync completes to prevent premature traffic re-routing.
- docs/ops/regional-failover-playbook.md: updated playbook with a new troubleshooting section for ephemeral bypass misfires and recommended query statements for telemetry.

Why this is safe: Changes are scoped to the runtime and controllers that orchestrate failover and shedding. No external API changes. Default configurations were tightened but kept conservative (backwards-compatible). The fairness floor guards against regression that previously surfaced in production.

Checklist: 
- [x] Reproduced the issue with a deterministic integration test that failed prior to changes.
- [x] Added unit tests for weighted_shedder edgecases.
- [x] Telemetry added and registered in registry YAML.
- [x] Updated ops playbook and logging docs.
- [x] Ran full CI + integration with simulated regions (see CI run #128).
- [x] Smoke-tested in a staging cluster with synthetic traffic and tenant mixes.

Tests & CI: Initial CI run failed (flake) due to an unrelated integration timeout in orchestrator_integration_test (flaky heartbeat). I pushed a retry fix to the test harness and re-ran. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, lint, integration, e2e-sim). See CI summary: unit=pass, lint=pass, integration=pass, e2e-sim=pass.

Review notes and highlights: 
- The fairness floor is tunable via pkg/config/defaults.json under shedder.min_fairness (default 0.05). The value was chosen conservatively after simulation runs described in ENG-1724.
- Telemetry tags include region_id, bypass_tag, tenant_tier, and shed_reason to support rapid post-incident triage.

Small code snippets (illustrative):
- region_bypass.go (new close confirmation):
  if kvSync.CompletedFor(region) && bypassWindow.Expired() {
      tag.Close("ephemeral-bypass")
  }
- weighted_shedder.go (clamp logic):
  score := clamp(rawScore, 0.0, 0.85) // prevent full probability under burst
  score = max(score, cfg.MinFairnessFloor)

Migration notes: No migration scripts required. Ops should watch telemetry: bypass_count and per_tenant_shed_rate for the first 24 hours after rollout. If you observe persistent high bypass_count, follow the updated playbook section to force-close stale bypass windows and inspect KV sync latencies.

Related work and timeline: This is a targeted hotfix branched from main after the incident on 2026-02-02. Follow-ups planned (ENG-1731) include a broader audit of shedder normalization across other admission paths and a small perf optimization to avoid extra allocations when computing per-tenant scores.

Merge outcome: Approved by Diego Morales and Lena Fischer after tech discussion on fairness floor and telemetry. Final approval from SRE (Owen Park) for operational readiness. Merged to main via squash on 2026-02-20.

Notes for on-call: If customers report sudden QoS regression for mid-tier tenants after the merge, check per_tenant_shed_rate and tenant_scoring_breakdown metrics. Revert plan: revert commit b3c9a8f..a9e1b55 as a single revert (squash) and roll back in the same release window.

Fixes a race in ephemeral region bypass and corrects weighted load-shed calculations to avoid tenant starvation during regional partial outages. Not user-facing API change; operational impact only.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: We observed a recurring class of false-positive canary regressions when probe traffic arrives in short bursts or when client-side concurrency spikes align with canary probe windows. These cases amplify tail latency and create high variance in the canary signal, causing unnecessary rollbacks and developer churn. This PR implements two complementary mitigations: a stochastic concurrency fence (probabilistic admission control) to smooth bursty concurrent requests and a staggered probe scheduler to desynchronize probe timing across hosts.

What this changes (high level):
- Add perf-canary detector that computes `concurrency_entropy` per host and enables a probabilistic cap when entropy exceeds threshold.
- Replace existing probe dispatcher with a staggered scheduler that shards probe time windows to hosts and backfills missed probes without amplifying traffic.
- Export new prometheus metrics and tracing spans for debugging (see docs/designs/stochastic_fence.md).

Checklist: [x] design doc (perf-canary/docs/designs/stochastic_fence.md) [x] unit tests for fence and scheduler [x] integration stress test (tests/integ/canary_stress.sh) [x] backward-compatible config defaults [x] feature-flagged rollout in console

Implementation notes: The stochastic fence uses a lightweight token counter per runtime worker plus a small RNG-based drop decision to probabilistically reject new speculative requests once the measured concurrency distribution entropy rises above a configured baseline. The fence is parameterized by window_ms, entropy_threshold, and drop_p_max; drop probability grows with measured excess entropy to avoid hard cuts. The staggered probe scheduler assigns a deterministic offset per host based on host-id hashing and a jitter seed; it cooperates with the fence so probes don't get entirely rejected.

Safety and rollout: The feature is behind `perf.canary.stochastic_fence` flag and defaults to disabled in release builds. The canary pipeline now evaluates `perf_canary.concurrency_entropy` during pre-rollout shoulders and will auto-abort rollouts if entropy increases > 2x baseline and tail-p95 latency deviates > 20ms. We added a soft-fallback that disables the fence automatically if overall throughput drops > 5% relative to baseline.

Testing and benchmarks: Microbenchmarks show a 40% drop in variance for p99 under synthetic burst traffic and no measurable throughput regression (<1% difference) with default params. Integration stress runs ran for 2 hours across multiple hosts; one flaky e2e test failed initially due to an off-by-one in the offset calculation (fixed in commit 3) and CI was rerun.

Related: ENG-8421 (noise-reduction effort), ENG-8502 (canary signal stability). Design doc: perf-canary/docs/designs/stochastic_fence.md.

Please focus reviews on: correctness of entropy calc, safety of the fallback heuristics, and Prometheus naming/labels.

Summary of changes and commits below.
- Introduces a probabilistic concurrency fence that caps request concurrency with tunable drop probability to prevent burst amplification of tail latency.
- Adds a staggered probe scheduler that spreads canary probe traffic to reduce synchronization noise.
- New metric: perf_canary.concurrency_entropy (used by rollout guard).
- Backwards-compatible knobs; feature gated behind `perf.canary.stochastic_fence` flag.
Priya Natarajan: 'Entropy calc looks reasonable, can you add a short comment describing numeric stability assumptions around log2? Also add a small unit test for empty-window behavior.'
Evan Cho (author): 'Addressed: added numeric-stability comment and an empty-window unit test in commit d2b7a10.'
Marcus Li: 'What happens to canary latency SLOs if we enable the fence with very aggressive drop_p_max? We should ensure the fallback disables fence before operator intervention.'
Evan Cho: 'Added soft-fallback thresholds (throughput delta check) and documented them in the config docs. See defaults.toml and design doc.'

Evan Cho: 'Added panel suggestion to the design doc; dashboards will be included in a follow-up PR to avoid coupling the dashboard change to runtime.'

Summary: This PR implements a stratified throughput-delta detector plus a backpressure gate for rollout guards. The detector segments incoming traffic by configurable attributes (model_variant, route, client_tier) and computes per-stratum throughput deltas and confidence intervals. When one or more strata exhibit statistically significant negative throughput deltas (adjusted for expected diurnal/batch patterns), the backpressure gate reduces canary weight and triggers a pause + notification. Motivation: Current canary detectors aggregate traffic and can miss regressions that only affect a subset of users (e.g., large-batch enterprise clients) or raise false positives during traffic-shape shifts. Stratification improves signal isolation and our backpressure gate enables graceful slowdown instead of immediate rollback, reducing churn and unnecessary rollbacks for transient noise. Design and behavior: - Stratification: users can supply 1..N keys to split traffic (default: ["route", "model_variant"]). Each stratum maintains a rolling throughput time series and a sample count. - Delta computation: per-stratum delta = relative change over baseline window (median-smoothed) with bootstrap-derived confidence bounds. Deltas are normalized by stratum weight so small but high-impact strata can surface. - Aggregation policy: detector computes both per-stratum alerts and a weighted global score (L1 of significant negative deltas). The gate triggers if (A) at least one stratum crosses its per-stratum threshold AND (B) the weighted global score > configured threshold. - Backpressure gate: on trigger, canary weight is decreased in a staged manner using exponential backoff and a cooldown window. Gate exposes actions: PAUSE_CANARY, REDUCE_BY_PERCENT, and NOTIFY_ONCE. CLR (canary lifecycle) is updated to respect gate decisions and to surface rationale in the rollout timeline. - Adaptive calibration: uses historical traffic shape profiles to avoid flagging routine shifts (e.g., nightly large-batch jobs). There is a permissive mode for safe rollout into unfamiliar regions. Configuration knobs: - stratify_keys (list, default ["route","model_variant"]) - min_samples_per_stratum (int, default 50) - baseline_window and probe_window (seconds) - per_stratum_threshold (relative delta e.g., -0.15) - global_score_threshold (float) - backpressure_reduction_step (percent) - cooldown_seconds - permissive_mode (bool) Implementation notes: - New detector: perf_canary/detectors/stratified_throughput_detector.py (Python, 420 loc). - Gate: perf_canary/gates/backpressure_gate.go (Go) integrated with canary scheduler. Gate exposes a small RPC to the controller for decisioning. - Metrics ingestion: added per-stratum keys to throughput pipeline (observability/ingest) and an index in the time-series store for efficient per-stratum queries. - Tests: unit tests for delta statistics, integration test that runs a synthetic workload with a noisy large-batch stratum, and an e2e smoke test in the perf-canary harness that exercises staged weight reductions. Commits (high-level): - c1a9f2b: initial stratified detector prototype, bootstrap CI tests - d04b7e1: wire detector into canary evaluation loop, add config schema - f7e33c: implement bootstrap confidence intervals and weight-normalization - a8b21ff: implement backpressure gate in Go; add RPC + controller wiring - b3c9d10: add metrics ingestion changes and index migration script - e11c4a2: add unit/integration tests and docs - f0d5b6a: address reviewer feedback, tune thresholds, add permissive mode Changes (high level list of files changed): - perf_canary/detectors/stratified_throughput_detector.py - perf_canary/gates/backpressure_gate.go - perf_canary/controller/canary_scheduler.go - observability/ingest/ingest_pipeline.py - observability/tsdb/migrations/20251112_add_stratum_index.sql - perf_canary/tests/test_stratified_detector.py - perf_canary/tests/e2e/test_backpressure_gate.py - docs/canary/stratified-detectors.md - examples/perf/stratified-canary.yml - ci/flake_checks.yaml - Makefile (add new test targets) Small illustrative snippet (detector delta logic): "delta = (probe_median - baseline_median) / max(1.0, baseline_median); if bootstrap.pvalue(delta_samples) < alpha: mark_significant()" Review thread (high level): - Maya Chen (reviewer): "Nice isolation layer; two asks: 1) please add a safety valve so we don't continuously throttle low-volume strata, 2) justify the bootstrap sample size — it's currently 1k in tests." - Author (Samir): "Added min_samples_per_stratum guard (default 50) and doc comments explaining bootstrap sample size tradeoffs; reduced default sample size in CI to 200 to keep runtime reasonable." - Jordan Alvarez: "Can we expose the global_score as a metric and expose per-stratum deltas to the console?" - Author: "Exposed global_score and per_stratum.delta as metrics with label keys; updated docs and dashboards in a follow-up doc-only PR planned." - Priya Nandakumar: "Concern about running index migration in-prod — what's the rollout plan?" - Author: "Migration is backwards compatible: the ingest path writes an additional index but queries fall back to legacy scan during migration; step migration + monitor over 48h. Added migration runbook in docs." CI notes: - Unit tests: pass - Integration tests (local harness): one flaky e2e initially failed on timing; increased probe_window + added retries; rerun green - Static analysis/lint: pass - Benchmark: lightweight perf regression harness shows 3% CPU increase in ingest path at peak for tagging; within acceptable envelope. QA and rollout: - Canary stage: enabled for non-critical routes first (canary default weight 1%) with permissive_mode=true for 24h. - Observability: dashboards added to show per-stratum deltas, global_score, and gate state history. - Monitoring: Alert if gate reduces canary weight >50% within 10 minutes or if >3 distinct strata trigger in 1h. Follow-ups planned: - docs PR to expand operational runbook and add example Grafana panels (WIP) - add UI controls in Console to configure stratify_keys and backpressure thresholds - long-term: explore combining stratified detection with the entropy-based detector for richer signal fusion Merge and rollout: - PR merged via squash on 2025-11-20 by Maya Chen after CI green and stakeholder approval. - Post-merge, feature flagged behind perf.stratified_detector and rolled to beta accounts over one week. Notes on uniqueness and risk: This approach biases toward early detection for heterogeneous workloads and provides a softer remediation (backpressure) compared to immediate rollback—intended to reduce noisy rollbacks and allow operators to investigate. Risk area is the added index/migration and potential ingest CPU increase; mitigation is staged migration, throttled indexing, and an opt-out flag. Related work: builds on ENG-3421 (stratified-metrics proposal) and ENG-4570 (canary lifecycle hooks), and is intentionally orthogonal to the percentile-decay detectors (not a replacement).
Adds a stratified throughput regression detector that segments traffic, computes per-segment deltas, and gates canary traffic using a backpressure policy. Improves detection sensitivity for heterogeneous traffic patterns and reduces false positives during load shifts.

payload.body:
## Summary This PR adds first-class configuration for running perf-canary across multiple **regions** and **hardware SKUs**, while ensuring we don’t accidentally fan out to every region/SKU combination (and burn the overhead budget). The canary runner now supports: (1) Target selection by `region` and `hardware_sku` (optional), (2) A hard fanout guard that defaults to conservative behavior, and (3) Safer defaults for Helm/Env-based deployments. This is needed for Phase 1 rollout where we want to start in `us-east` on a single SKU, then expand gradually to `eu-west` and additional SKUs once baselines/thresholds are tuned.

## Motivation / Context Today the canary targets are effectively “global” (implicitly whatever the control plane routes to). That makes it hard to: - Attribute regressions to fleet changes (SKU-specific) vs runtime changes - Set region-specific baselines (telemetry variance differs per region) - Control cost/overhead during rollout (avoid accidental wide fanout)

This change is intentionally scoped to **config + selection + safety rails**. Baselines/threshold wiring is handled by baseline fetch logic in a separate PR.

## Design - **Target dimensions:** `region`, `hardware_sku` are added as *optional* dimensions to the canary target config. If `hardware_sku` is omitted, the canary runs “per region” and relies on the inference tier routing for SKU; if provided, we force requests to that SKU via the internal routing hint header (same mechanism used by benchmark-lab).
- **Fanout safeguards:** - New config key: `fanout_max_targets` (default: `3`) - New config key: `fanout_allowlist` (optional explicit list of `<region>:<sku>` tuples). If set, only those tuples run. - New startup-time safety check: if computed target count exceeds `fanout_max_targets`, the process exits non-zero unless `--allow-fanout-over-max` is explicitly set (intended only for controlled manual runs). - New “blast radius” log line on startup prints the exact computed targets and the derived capacity budget per target.
- **Metric labels / cardinality:** Region is now a standard label on canary-emitted metrics. Hardware SKU is only emitted when explicitly configured (to avoid accidental cardinality growth); when omitted, we emit `hardware_sku="unknown"` for aggregator stability.
- **Alert payload:** Alert webhook payload includes `region` + `hardware_sku` in the `scope` section so incident-bot threads are dedupe-able per tuple.

## Config changes - New config schema fields (YAML): - `targets.regions` (list) - `targets.hardware_skus` (list, optional) - `targets.matrix_mode` (one of: `region_only`, `region_x_sku`) - `safety.fanout_max_targets` (int) - `safety.fanout_allowlist` (list of strings `region:sku` or `region:*`) - `safety.require_explicit_region` (bool, default true)

Example (Phase 1): ```yaml targets:   regions: ["us-east-1"]   matrix_mode: "region_only" safety:   fanout_max_targets: 2   require_explicit_region: true ```

Example (Phase 2 w/ SKU): ```yaml targets:   regions: ["us-east-1", "eu-west-1"]   hardware_skus: ["h100-sxm", "a100-80gb"]   matrix_mode: "region_x_sku" safety:   fanout_allowlist: ["us-east-1:h100-sxm", "eu-west-1:h100-sxm"]   fanout_max_targets: 3 ```

## Implementation notes - Added `TargetMatrix` helper to compute the final run list. This keeps selection logic out of the request loop and makes it unit-testable. - Added request routing hints: `X-Redwood-Region` and `X-Redwood-Hardware-Sku` (only when configured). These are already supported server-side for internal callers; the perf-canary service account is restricted to internal endpoints. - Extended the runner loop to include `target_scope` in logs and metric tags.

## Tests - Unit tests for matrix expansion, allowlist filtering, max-target guard, and stable ordering (so rollouts are deterministic). - Updated config loader tests to validate schema errors (e.g., `region_x_sku` with missing `hardware_skus`). - Added a small “dry-run” mode test that prints computed targets and exits.

## Rollout plan - Merge behind conservative defaults: `require_explicit_region=true`, `fanout_max_targets=3`, `matrix_mode=region_only`. - Phase 1 (ENG-4880): enable `us-east-1` only, no SKU dimension. - Phase 2: introduce SKU dimension for `h100-sxm` only, validate baseline alignment, then expand.

## Risks / Mitigations - Risk: accidental fanout increases load/cost. Mitigation: hard guard + allowlist option + explicit override flag. - Risk: metrics cardinality blowup. Mitigation: hardware_sku label only when explicitly configured; region label is bounded and already present in most dashboards.

## Screenshots / Output (dry-run) - `--dry-run` output example: `computed_targets=[us-east-1:*] target_count=1 fanout_max_targets=3` - `region_x_sku` example: `computed_targets=[us-east-1:h100-sxm, eu-west-1:h100-sxm] target_count=2 fanout_allowlist=2`

## Follow-ups - Baseline store needs to key off (model, runtime_version, sku, region) once we enable SKU dimension broadly. - Confirm incident-bot dedupe keys include region+sku (separate PR in incident-bot repo).
Vanessa Ortiz (review): Can we make sure there’s no way to deploy this to all regions by accident? The default config path is Helm values, and people will copy/paste. Noah Patel (author): Yep. Added `require_explicit_region=true` default. If regions are empty we fail fast with a clear error. Also added `fanout_max_targets` guard; default 3. Logan Wright (review): Region label is fine, but hardware SKU label worries me for cardinality. How are we controlling this? Noah Patel (author): SKU label is only emitted if `targets.hardware_skus` is set OR an explicit `matrix_mode=region_x_sku`. Otherwise we emit `hardware_sku="unknown"` to keep queries stable without blowing up. Nadia Rahman (review): For baselines, does the target selection order stay stable? We don’t want baseline fetch churn. Noah Patel (author): Yes—matrix expansion is stable-sorted, and allowlist filtering preserves order. Added tests to enforce it. Rafael Mendes (review): For on-call, can the alert payload include region+sku so incident-bot can dedupe correctly? Noah Patel (author): Added `scope.region` and `scope.hardware_sku` to the webhook payload. Incident-bot PR will pick it up, but this is backwards compatible. Vanessa Ortiz (requested changes): Please add a startup log line that prints computed targets + derived per-target QPS budget so we can sanity check rollouts. Noah Patel (author): Done in 8a2f4c1; log line prints `computed_targets`, `target_count`, `capacity_budget_qps_total`, `capacity_budget_qps_per_target`. Vanessa Ortiz (approval): Looks good. Thanks for the guardrails. Logan Wright (approval): OK with conditional SKU label + `unknown` fallback. Nadia Rahman (approval): Good to merge. Tests cover matrix/safety behavior.
payload.title: Add region + hardware SKU dimension config (with fanout safeguards)

payload.body:
Motivation: existing canary detectors are sensitive to short traffic bursts and correlated infra noise which leads to noisy rollbacks during expected traffic-shape changes (jobs, migration windows, marketing spikes). This PR introduces a traffic-pattern-aware "failover sentinel" and a lightweight "regression isolator" that fuse traffic-shape signals with performance metrics to reduce false-positive rollbacks while preserving rapid recovery for real regressions.

What this PR adds: 1) Traffic-shape ingestion: a new input pipeline that classifies incoming traffic into shapes (steady, spike, ramp, batch) using a configurable window and simple clustering heuristics. 2) Multi-signal fusion: a scorer that combines latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), tail latency slope, throughput saturation, error-rate delta, and infra saturation (CPU/GPU util) into a single anomaly likelihood score. 3) Context-aware thresholds: the anomaly thresholds are adjusted by observed traffic shape and recent baseline variance; spikes reduce sensitivity to p50 swings while emphasizing p99 and error-rate. 4) Regression isolator: when a signal crosses threshold, the isolator runs a short adaptive probe (synthetic vs production-sampled traffic) to determine if degradation is systemic or limited to a traffic slice. 5) Failover policies: new rollout guard policies that recommend automated partial failovers (region/model-variant-level) with an explicit rollback window and manual-approve fallback. 6) Observability: dashboards, per-canary timeline traces, and a compact alert format for automated incident responders. 7) Tests and pipeline integration: unit tests for scorer and classifier, e2e smoke harness against the perf-sim runner, and GitHub Actions CI changes to run the canary smoke suite.

Compatibility and opt-in: the sentinel is disabled by default; teams can opt-in via canary profile YAML (examples included). Default heuristics are conservative to avoid impacting existing rollouts. Migration docs and config examples are included.

Risks and mitigations: classifier mislabeling could reduce sensitivity; mitigated by fallback to legacy detector after 10 minutes of ambiguous labels. The isolator issues synthetic probes with throttled rate to avoid user impact.

Summary: improves reliability of automated rollouts in variable-traffic environments while adding guarded automation for fast failure containment.
Luca: This looks promising. A couple of questions: how do you prevent probe amplification when many canaries detect anomalies simultaneously? Maya: probes are rate-limited at the tenant and global level; isolator will jitter and back off if global probe budget is near exhausted. Priya: can we get a brief on the classifier false positive rate? Maya: added unit tests and an offline evaluation (results in docs) showing <2% FPR on historical traces after conservative tuning. Owen: please add a canary profile example for high-burst latency workloads. Maya: added examples and a migration note. Luca: LGTM after addressing the probe budgeting comment. Priya: approving after docs update. CI passed on final run and I verified dashboard panels.
- Add traffic-pattern-aware failover sentinel: reduces false-positive rollbacks during traffic spikes.
- Introduce regression isolator with adaptive probes for deterministic rollback decisions.
- Opt-in canary profile and example configs.
- New observability dashboards and alert templates.
Feature gated behind canary profile opt-in. Rollout recommended to a subset of non-critical services for 2 weeks before full adoption.
Enable sentinel on a test canary via config YAML
Run perf-sim smoke harness and verify no spurious rollbacks under synthetic spike traffic
Trigger an intentional p99 regression and confirm isolator recommends partial failover

payload.body:
Motivation: reduce noisy CI cycles and catch prompt-set regressions earlier by maintaining a rolling historical baseline and exposing a lightweight priority-smoke CI hook that runs in pull requests. This PR introduces a rollforward-able baseline snapshot format, a prioritized sampling algorithm for producing tiny smoke cohorts, an integration in the eval-runner to compute stabilized delta metrics (win-rate with bootstrap intervals and length-normalized perplexity proxy), and a CI adapter that fails fast on statistically significant regression signals while allowing configurable escalation. Key behaviors: 1) Baseline snapshots are stored as anchored JSONL with metadata (model version, commit, timestamp, aggregated metrics); 2) Rollforward workflow: when a PR updates a prompt set or model scoring, the CI compares the PR run to the latest baseline and if changes are benign the snapshot is rollforwarded automatically with a short TTL; 3) Priority-smoke sampler selects N=150 high-impact prompts using a combination of recent-failure weight, user-frequency weight, and semantic diversity hashing to maximize early-detection power; 4) Metrics: primary signal is weighted pairwise win-rate with bootstrap CI and actionable effect-size thresholds, secondary signals include response-length-normalized score and top-k token-shift; 5) CI hook modes: fast-smoke (PR-level, ~3-5m), expanded-smoke (pre-merge gated run, ~15-20m), and backfill (nightly full baseline recompute). Backfill triggers remedial guidance and automatic rollback candidates when large historical drift is detected. Compatibility: integrates with existing eval-runner, supports existing cohort/spec yaml, and can be toggled per-repo via eval-harness config. Migration notes: existing baseline format is supported as read-only; operators must run `scripts/baseline-upgrade` once per workspace to enable rollforward metadata. Rationale: many regressions in our deployment pipeline are surfaced only after full-house evals; a statistically-driven tiny-smoke approach yields much faster feedback with low cost and higher signal-to-noise. This PR bundles implementation, docs, and CI wiring so reviewers can test end-to-end in feature branches.
Sanjay: Can we make the default priority-smoke cohort size configurable via project config instead of hardcoding N=150? I want to use 50 for some low-cost repos. Author response: added config path `eval.priority_smoke.size` and doc example.
Ruth: The bootstrap CI sometimes produced wide intervals on small cohorts; can we include a fallback deterministic delta (median difference) to avoid flapping? Author response: implemented median-delta fallback and added a unit test and a flag `--deterministic-fallback`.
Jonas: Suggest to gate rollforward by a manual approval for high-impact prompt sets flagged in metadata. Author response: added `impact_level` metadata and default requires approval for impact_level >= high.
CI: first run failed on lint in snapshot.py, autorun fixed by commit d2b8f22 which tightened whitespace and imports, subsequent rerun passed.
Adds historical baseline snapshot format and lightweight priority-smoke CI hook for rapid prompt-set regression detection. Includes sampler, metrics, CI action, operator docs, and migration script. Configurable cohort size and impact gating.

Context: As part of the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint, we’re enabling quantized kernel modes behind flags and rolling out via perf canary. The existing canary gating uses a single threshold policy that was tuned on baseline (FP16/BF16) runs and has been noisy for quantized modes (especially when sample sizes are small or when the scheduler mix shifts TTFT/TPOT differently). This PR introduces explicit threshold profiles for quantized kernels and per-SKU baselines so we can gate safely and reduce false positives while still catching real regressions. Summary of changes: (1) Add threshold profiles keyed by kernel_mode (baseline|fp8|int8) and sku (h100|a100|l4) with separate TTFT/TPOT constraints and minimum sample requirements. (2) Add noise suppression: a small-sample guardrail, robust aggregation using trimmed mean for p95 deltas, and an EWMA-based stability check that prevents flip-flopping when the signal is borderline. (3) Add a per-SKU baseline registry: baseline references are pinned by (model, sku, region, traffic_profile) so the canary compares fp8/int8 vs the correct baseline cohort rather than a global default. (4) Add explicit “capacity/variance” classification: if GPU clocks are not locked or if variance exceeds the configured bound, canary emits a WARN and does not auto-rollback (still pages on-call if error rate spikes). Default policies included (initial cut): H100 fp8 is allowed tighter TPOT deltas but slightly looser TTFT due to known launch/scheduler interactions in mixed workloads; A100 int8 is looser on TPOT until we finish shape guardrails coverage; L4 has stricter min-sample and longer evaluation window to smooth bursty workloads. Config format: new YAML profiles under config/threshold_profiles/ with schema validation in CI. Example snippet (illustrative only): profile: quantized_h100_fp8; ttft_p95_delta_pct_max: 6; tpot_p95_delta_pct_max: 3; min_requests: 2000; ewma_alpha: 0.2; trimmed_mean_pct: 10. Operational notes: This PR does NOT change any runtime flags. It only changes how perf-canary evaluates telemetry deltas when kernel_mode is fp8/int8. Rollback behavior: auto-rollback triggers remain enabled only when (a) min_requests met, (b) stability check passes (not high variance), and (c) delta breaches the configured bound for 2 consecutive windows. Otherwise we emit a blocking canary failure (no rollout progression) but do not auto-flip flags. Follow-ups: (a) once ENG-7428 matrix runs are complete we should tighten H100 fp8 TTFT; (b) add model-family overrides for known long-context TTFT sensitivity; (c) wire in the new metrics dimensions (model/gpu/kernel_mode) after runtime PR lands (tracked in ENG-7427/PR-19934 in monorepo).
Rafael Mendes: The auto-rollback guardrails look good. Two questions: (1) what’s the behavior when sample size is met but variance is high? (2) can we ensure this doesn’t block non-quantized rollouts? I don’t want a global gating change that surprises us.
Allison Grant (author): (1) If variance > variance_max (computed from baseline window + current window), we classify the result as UNSTABLE and do not auto-rollback; we still stop progression and mark the canary as failed so on-call looks. (2) Non-quantized uses the existing default profile; the new profiles are selected only when kernel_mode tag matches fp8|int8. I added a unit test to ensure baseline profile remains the default when kernel_mode missing.
Noah Patel: The EWMA stability check is a good addition, but I’m concerned about the trimmed mean on p95 deltas — are we trimming across shards or across time windows? Also: can you link to the rationale from the sprint plan/variance investigation?
Allison Grant (author): Trim happens across time windows within the evaluation interval (we keep N windows, compute delta per window, then trim top/bottom 10% before aggregating). We don’t trim across shards; shards are already aggregated upstream. I added a comment + doc section and linked the approach to ENG-7429 notes in Linear.
Irene Choi: Please include explicit SKUs as they appear in fleet labels. Our H100 label is "h100-sxm" and "h100-pcie" in some regions. Can the profile system map both to "h100" without copy/pasting config?
Allison Grant (author): Added sku_aliases: [h100-sxm, h100-pcie] support in schema and mapped both to canonical "h100". Same for a100-80gb vs a100-40gb (canonical "a100"). Tests included.
Marcus Reed: For TTFT vs TPOT, the profile has TTFT looser than TPOT. That matches what we saw, but we should cap absolute TTFT delta in ms too; percent deltas can blow up on low-latency regions. Can we add an optional absolute bound?
Allison Grant (author): Added optional ttft_p95_delta_ms_max and tpot_p95_delta_ms_max fields. Set defaults only for L4 (since percent was too sensitive in our synthetic runs). Left H100/A100 on percent-only for now.
Rafael Mendes: Approved once the sku alias mapping lands.
Rafael Mendes: Looks good now. Approved.
Perf-canary: Added quantized-kernel threshold profiles (FP8/INT8) with per-SKU baselines and noise suppression. Improves canary signal quality and reduces false-positive rollbacks during quantized rollouts.
payload.title: Add TTFT/TPOT threshold profiles for FP8/INT8 kernel canaries (per-SKU baselines + noise suppression)

Motivation: Canary detectors currently trigger on aggregate percentile shifts which are brittle under localized traffic shape changes (small high-volume routes or short-lived hotspots). This PR introduces a compact sketch-based latency fingerprint (per-route latency hash) that captures the distributional signature of latency across request slices and a cross-slice gate that requires correlated drift across multiple independent slices before triggering an automated rollback. Design: 1) Sketch fingerprint: a streaming quantile sketch per slice that emits a stable 128-bit hash summarizing percentile layout (p50/p90/p95/p99 buckets + weighted entropy). The hash is intentionally small to keep memory pressure low on embedders. 2) Cross-slice gate: policy layer that observes the set of active slice hashes over a sliding window and computes a correlation score; only if N independent slices exceed configured correlation & severity thresholds does the canary evaluator escalate to a hard-fail rollback. 3) Config: new canary policy fields idle_slices_threshold, correlation_window_secs, correlation_threshold, severity_threshold. Implementation summary: - lib/canary/fingerprint/sketch_hash.go: Golang streaming sketch + stable hash function + deterministic serialization. - pkg/alerts/cross_slice_gate.py: policy evaluation used by the canary evaluator (keeps a lightweight LRU of recent hashes). - charts/perf-canary/values.yaml: new defaults for gate config under canary.policies.cross_slice_gate. - tests/integration/test_latency_hash.py & tests/unit/test_cross_slice_gate.py: deterministic tests for hash stability and policy behavior. - docs/perf-canary/operational-notes.md: rollout guidance, tuning knobs, and failure modes. Compatibility and tradeoffs: the fingerprint is designed to be collision-resistant for realistic production traffic signatures but not cryptographically secure. It favors determinism across language runtimes and quantization settings. The cross-slice gate reduces sensitivity to single-slice outliers but can delay detection of real regressions that are localized; defaults bias toward safety but are tunable per team. Rollout plan: 1) Feature flag gated behind perf.canary.latency_hash (off by default). 2) Canary rollout: enable in staging canaries for 48h, run shadow canary decisions for 7d in production (decision path exercised but not enforced), then promote to enforced gate if no regressions detected. 3) Observe correlation metrics and false-positive rate for two weeks before making default-on. Checklist: - [x] Sketch algorithm implemented and unit-tested - [x] Policy evaluator + integration tests - [x] Helm chart config and feature flag - [x] Docs and ops guidance - [x] Manual canary run in staging completed - [x] CI green after reruns Related work: builds on earlier multivariate and ensemble detectors (see ENG-6123) and aims to address noisy regressions observed in SUP-7812 incident. Links: Linear ENG-2319 (design doc), incident SUP-7812 (postmortem).
Adds a low-memory sketch-based latency fingerprint component and a configurable cross-slice gating rule to reduce noisy false-positive canary rollbacks. Backwards-compatible; configurable via canary policies.
Added sketch_hash.go (~220 LOC) implementing a CompactTDigest-like sketch, cross_slice_gate.py (~120 LOC) policy, small changes to evaluator.go to call gate, helm values additions, and tests. No changes to runtime C++ kernels.
Asha: Could you add an integration test that simulates route churn? We should ensure the LRU doesn't evict too aggressively.
Author (Diego): Added test that exercises route churn and increased default LRU size to 1024.
Riley: LGTM overall. Can you document how the hash behaves across quantization modes?
Author: Added note in operational-notes.md clarifying determinism guarantees and known caveats with 8-bit quantized models.
Maya: One nit on variable naming in sketch_hash.go; requested a small refactor.
Author: Refactored per request and responded to inline comment. Ran CI again.
Asha: Approved after CI green.
Riley: Approved.

payload.body:
Motivation: Canary detectors focused on latency fingerprints struggle to surface throughput regressions when traffic mixes multiple user cohorts with different request sizing and arrival patterns. This PR adds a near-real-time throughput fingerprint prober and a traffic-cohort gating policy that reduces false positives by conditioning alerts on cohort-aligned baselines. Changes include a new prober module that computes compact per-window throughput fingerprints, a cohorting service that assigns traffic using stable hashing and feature hints, and a gating controller that enforces cohort-aware thresholds during canary analysis. The description below outlines design, implementation, testing, and rollout plan.
Design: - Throughput fingerprint: multi-resolution histogram of inter-arrival deltas and per-request token counts computed with reservoir sampling; outputs are hashed and quantized into a small footprint vector (64 bytes) to allow efficient differential comparison across time windows.
- Cohorting: traffic is grouped by stable prefix-hash of routing key + optional meta-features (client_type, token_distribution_bucket). Cohorts are dynamic; a light-weight drift detector will retire cohorts inactive for >1h.
- Gate policy: when evaluating canaries, the detector computes per-cohort delta in throughput fingerprint distance (Jensen-Shannon on smoothed histograms). If any cohort crosses configured delta or experiences simultaneous throughput drop >X% and p99 tail shift, the rollout is paused and an automated investigation probe is triggered.
Implementation highlights: - perf_canary/prober/throughput_fingerprint.py: implements reservoir sampling, multi-res histograms, compact hash output, incremental delta update hooks.
- perf_canary/cohort/assigner.py: stable hashing + rules engine to attach request to cohort.
- perf_canary/gates/cohort_gate.py: gating logic, threshold tuning knobs, integration with existing canary orchestrator.
- integrations: telemetry -> metrics export via openmetrics; stored as compressed fingerprint series in the canary TTL store for 48h.
Compatibility and safety: - Fingerprint generation is opt-in for existing canaries (config flag canary.use_throughput_fingerprints). Default thresholds are conservative to avoid noisy pauses.
- Memory/CPU: prober uses bounded buffers and async IO; local CPU < 2% on production canaries in our internal trials.
Tests and validation: - Unit tests for sampling and fingerprint stability (perf_canary/tests/test_throughput_fingerprint.py).
- Golden regression tests comparing controlled synthetic workloads (burst, steady, bimodal) against baseline detectors.
- Canary lab: deployed to canary cluster with synthetic mixed cohorts for 72h. Observations: improved signal-to-noise for throughput regressions; minor tuning required for very sparse cohorts (handled by automatic cohort retirement).
Rollout plan: 1) Feature flag behind canary.use_throughput_fingerprints = off by default. 2) Stage to small subset of internal tenants (10%) for 1 week. 3) Increase to 50% with monitoring dashboards and alert set to notify SRE on first automated pause. 4) Full release once thresholds stabilize.
Links: design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-5123/throughput-fingerprinting-canary-gates; dashboard prototype: https://grafana.internal.redwood/c/throughput-fingerprint.
Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests in perf-lab - [x] Backwards compatible (opt-in) - [x] Telemetry integration - [x] Safety knobs and default conservative thresholds
Commits summary: "initial throughput fingerprint prober implementation (wip)", "add cohort assigner and gating policy", "tests for reservoir sampling and fingerprint delta", "telemetry export and TTL store integration", "docs: prober config and rollout guide", "tune default thresholds after lab run", "fix race condition in assigner with concurrent retires".
Files changed (high level): - perf_canary/prober/throughput_fingerprint.py (core implementation) - perf_canary/cohort/assigner.py (stable hashing and rules) - perf_canary/gates/cohort_gate.py (canary gating controller) - perf_canary/tests/test_throughput_fingerprint.py (unit/golden tests) - docs/canary/throughput-fingerprint.md (runbook and config) - perf_canary/integrations/metrics_exporter.py (compressed series export) - perf_canary/helm/canary-values.yaml (feature flag and knobs)
Review conversation and resolution (high-level): - Marcus Nguyen (reviewer): "Can we avoid cohort explosion? how does retirement work?" Author reply: "we cap active cohorts per canary to 128 and retire cohorts inactive >1h; added tests for cap behavior and metrics to alert if cap reached." - Marcus: "add more observability for cohort churn" Author: "added metrics perf_canary.cohort.churn and dashboard panel" - Lena Ortega: "threshold defaults look permissive; prefer conservative for initial rollout" Author: "lowered default delta threshold and added opt-in flag; updated rollout plan to 10%" - Evan Chen: "any cost impact on telemetry retention?" Author: "fingerprints are 64 bytes per window and TTL is 48h by default; at 1k canaries this is ~3GB/day compressed — added cost note in docs and helm defaults to throttle sampling windows for low-tier tenants" - Marcus: "CI flaky on integration test, re-run"
CI history: - Unit tests: pass - Integration (perf-lab): flaky initially (timeout on synthetic burst test), fixed by increasing synthetic driver timeout and adding retry; subsequent runs all pass - Lint: pass - Security scan: pass
Merge outcome: merged via squash and merge after approvals from Marcus and Lena and green CI. Post-merge notes: - Feature flag remains off by default; ops will enable for internal tenants first. - Follow-up tasks: ENG-5289 (dashboard panel consolidation), ENG-5337 (add anomaly attribution hints to probe).
Add a lightweight throughput fingerprint prober and introduce a cohort-aware gating policy for canary rollouts; improves detection of throughput regressions in mixed-traffic environments and adds a graceful pause for cohorts that diverge significantly.

payload.body:
Background: Current canary routing uses deterministic thresholds on percentile metrics (p50/p95/p99) which can miss signal when variance grows or when tail instability is intermittent. This PR introduces a probabilistic degradation guard that reasons about the probability that a canary is degrading relative to baseline rather than relying on single-point thresholds. Motivation: Provide safer traffic ramp decisions by estimating the likelihood of true degradation and enabling risk-aware traffic shaping and automatic rollback. What this change does: 1) Adds a lightweight heteroscedastic regression-based risk estimator that models mean and variance of latency/throughput metrics and outputs P(degradation > delta) for configurable deltas. 2) Integrates the estimator into the canary controller so traffic ramps are gated by a configurable risk budget (e.g., only ramp if P(degradation>delta) < 0.05). 3) Implements a traffic-shaper policy that can do partial-rollbacks based on continuous risk estimates (gradual rollback rather than binary). 4) Exposes new metrics and tracing spans: canary.risk.probability, canary.risk.confidence, canary.risk.model_version, and a canary_decision.reason tag to the existing observability pipeline. 5) Adds calibration harness and eval notebooks for offline verification against historical canaries. Backwards compatibility: Guard is opt-in via canary.policy.type = "probabilistic" and has sane defaults. Performance: estimator runs incrementally using streaming summaries; typical latency impact on controller is <2ms per decision loop. Testing: unit tests, integration tests against perf-sim local harness, and a historical-snapshot calibration run included. Rollout plan: default off; enable for internal perf-canaries for 2 weeks, then offer to customers as beta. Related: ENG-4128, ENG-4199. Changeset summary and rationale included in commits.
Benji Liu (2026-02-22): Nice approach. Two asks before approving: (1) add a small section in the design doc on choice of delta and how operators should pick it, (2) include a short description of estimator warmup and cold-start behavior in the controller comments.
Diego Marquez (2026-02-23): Question: how does this interact with the existing percentile-based canary? We should ensure both can run in parallel during migration. Also flagged a potential race in traffic_shaper.go when controller cancels a pending ramp.
Samantha Ortiz (2026-02-24): UX: operator needs visibility into the risk budget; please add a console widget showing remaining budget and a link to calibration results. Also request e2e test covering partial rollback path.
CI Bot (2026-02-25): unit-tests failed: TestEstimateVariance flaky on arm builders (timeout). See failure log: variance estimator timed out on a single outlier sample.
Benji Liu (2026-02-27): after addressing Diego's race fix please re-request review; also add a comment with the mathematical reference used for heteroscedastic modeling.
Aisha Kapoor (2026-02-23): Added design doc section for delta selection and operator guidance. Added controller comments describing warmup: estimator requires N=50 samples by default and uses an exponential decay for older samples. Will make warmup configurable.
Aisha Kapoor (2026-02-26): Fixed race by switching to controller.workQueue rate-limited reconciliation and using compare-and-swap on the pendingRamp state. Added integration test to cover the cancel path.
Aisha Kapoor (2026-02-27): Added console widget JSON and a short e2e test that runs a synthetic partial-rollback scenario in the perf-sim harness. CI retry scheduled for flaky test.

payload.body:
Motivation and context:
Customers running Redwood Private reported two recurring problems during upgrades: (1) concurrent terraform applies against per-tenant state caused transient double-allocation of (small) subnets and IAM race conditions; (2) rollbacks after partial failures frequently exposed IAM role drift which made re-apply brittle. This PR introduces a lightweight tf-orchestrator module plus two supporting modules/patterns to mitigate these classes of failures for GPU-backed private deployments.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds modules/tf-orchestrator: a small coordinator that sequences terraform operations per-tenant and provides a pluggable lock/fencing backend (DynamoDB-style lease by default, noop for air-gapped installs). It exposes pre-apply and post-apply hooks for canary tasks (helm chart preflight, kube-object reconciliation).
- Introduces modules/subnet-claim-fence: a claim interface and terraform helper that atomically allocates subnet IDs with a fencing token. Prevents two controllers from claiming the same /28-/24 in racey upgrade scenarios.
- Adds modules/immutable-iam-profile: a pattern that creates immutable role ARN prefixes and rotation-safe attachment objects so rollbacks do not re-use rotated names and cause dangling grants.
- Updates modules/gpu-nodepool to emit tenant-scoped node pool names and to accept an external "fence_token" output to bind with claim flow.
- Migration tool: scripts/migrate-orchestrator.sh and a step-by-step doc to move existing per-tenant state into orchestrator-managed apply order.

Why this design:
- Minimize blast radius: orchestrator sequences changes per-tenant while keeping terraform state boundaries intact (we do not collapse state files).
- Compatible with air-gapped installs: fencing backend is pluggable; default uses a small DynamoDB table but the module supports filesystem- or consul-backed implementations for on-prem.
- Safe rollbacks: immutable IAM profile naming reduces identity churn when a prior release rolls back and later re-applies.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add tf-orchestrator module and interface docs
- [x] Implement subnet-claim-fence terraform helpers and tests
- [x] Update gpu-nodepool module to accept fence_token and tenant labels
- [x] Add migration scripts and operator runbook
- [x] Integration test: simulated concurrent applies across 3 tenants
- [x] Confirm CI and e2e pass on staged infra

Commits (summary):
- feat(tf-orchestrator): new module + README + example usage (Juniper)
- feat(subnet-claim-fence): atomic claim resource + tests (Diego)
- chore(gpu-nodepool): expose fence_token and tenant-affinity labels (Marcus)
- feat(immutable-iam-profile): stable ARN prefix + attachment helpers (Evelyn)
- docs(migrations): add migrate-orchestrator.sh and runbook (Juniper)
- tests(integration): add concurrent-apply simulation harness (SRE test infra)

Files changed (high level):
- modules/tf-orchestrator/main.tf, outputs.tf, README.md
- modules/subnet-claim-fence/claim.tf, data.tf, examples/simple-claim.md, tests/claim_test.go
- modules/immutable-iam-profile/main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf
- modules/gpu-nodepool/variables.tf (new fence_token), outputs.tf, examples/tenant-affinity.md
- scripts/migrate-orchestrator.sh (idempotent migration helper)
- docs/private/migrations/orchestrator-runbook.md
- tests/integration/concurrent_apply_test.go
- CI: .github/workflows/terraform-orchestrator.yml (new workflow)

Review conversation (condensed):
- Marcus Chen: "This looks good overall. Two asks: (1) make fence backend pluggable in examples; (2) include a conservative default lock TTL so long-running applies don't leak."
- Juniper Lee: "Addressed: added backend variable with example consul fs implementation + default ttl of 15m and an explicit renew script for long applies. Pushed commit cf8b2e7."
- Evelyn Park: "Immutable ARN pattern is helpful. Please ensure IAM policies referencing dynamic ARNs are computed via outputs so external infra doesn't rely on ephemeral names."
- Juniper Lee: "Updated outputs to include stable_role_arn and stable_role_id; documented migration caveat for existing policies in runbook."
- Diego Morales: "Integration tests flaked once due to timing. Added jitter and retry to claim helper; re-ran CI."
- Evelyn Park: "Approved after smoke on staging."

CI / checks summary:
- terraform validate (modules) : pass
- unit tests (claim tests) : pass
- integration (concurrent apply harness) : pass after one retry
- linters (tflint, tfsec) : pass (one minor tfsec suppression for allowed broad assume-role for control-plane bootstrapping)

Migration and rollout notes:
- The orchestrator is opt-in. To adopt, teams run scripts/migrate-orchestrator.sh which takes current per-tenant state buckets and registers them with the orchestrator control table. The runbook includes a dry-run mode and a checklist to run canary applies on a single tenant before full conversion.
- Backwards compatibility: existing Terraform state layout is preserved; orchestrator only sequences applies. If the orchestrator is removed, state remains untouched.

Operational considerations and follow-ups:
- We should add a Prometheus exporter for claim-fence metrics (allocations, conflicts) in a follow-up PR (tracked ENG-5527).
- Add a Helm chart preflight hook that validates fence-token reachability during preflight (follow-up).

Merge outcome:
- PR merged via squash on 2025-12-01 after full approvals and green CI. Post-merge: created a short-lived feature-flagged rollout to enable orchestrator in staging, validated four rolling upgrades using the new flows and confirmed no subnet collisions and stable IAM roles across rollbacks.

If you want to run this locally: see modules/tf-orchestrator/README.md for quickstart and scripts/migrate-orchestrator.sh for migration steps.

Add `tf-orchestrator` to coordinate atomic applies across tenant state backends; introduce subnet-claim fencing to avoid double-allocation of subnets during parallel upgrades; add immutable IAM profiles for tenant-scoped roles to reduce drift during rollbacks. Backwards-compatible rollout with feature flag and migration tool included.
This PR is intentionally conservative: it sequences applies rather than consolidating state files, reducing risk for customers with complex per-tenant TF state. The fencing and immutable name patterns were co-designed with SRE to reduce incident recurrence during private upgrades.

payload.body:
## Context
Incident-bot v2 relies on the telemetry query service to render saturation/context cards in the first ~60–90s of an incident thread. We’ve seen query latency spikes during incidents (bursty usage + upstream timeouts) that cause empty/partial cards and slow responder workflows. This PR adds a dedicated perf canary to continuously validate telemetry query latency and error behavior under a representative diagnostic workload.

Related:
- INT-3341 (telemetry query timeouts from incident-bot)
- ENG-5427 (telemetry query cache/coalescing)
- ENG-5429 (bot degraded-mode + load shedding)

## What this adds
1) New canary: `telemetry-query-latency`
- Runs every 60s (configurable) from 3 regions: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1
- Executes a fixed set of low-cardinality queries that mirror incident-bot cards:
  - GPU utilization (pool-level, region scoped)
  - Queue depth / scheduler backpressure (service + region)
  - KV cache pressure (cluster + region)
  - Error budget burn link generator preflight query (metadata only)
- Includes a small amount of concurrency (default 4) to catch p95 regressions without introducing significant load

2) Success criteria + SLO-style thresholds
- Records latency histograms for each query family + overall request
- Enforces guardrails:
  - p95 < 2.0s for `telemetry_query_total`
  - p99 < 5.0s for `telemetry_query_total`
  - timeout rate < 1% over 10m
  - non-2xx rate < 0.5% over 10m
- Canary marks a run as failed if any threshold is violated; emits a structured failure reason to make debugging actionable (e.g., `upstream_timeout`, `rate_limited`, `bad_gateway`, `query_budget_exceeded`).

3) Metrics + dashboard wiring
Emits the following (Prom-style) metrics:
- `perf_canary_telemetry_query_latency_ms{region,query_family,tenant_scope}` (histogram)
- `perf_canary_telemetry_query_success_total{region,query_family}`
- `perf_canary_telemetry_query_failure_total{region,query_family,reason}`
- `perf_canary_telemetry_query_payload_bytes{region,query_family}` (to detect accidental query expansion)

Adds a lightweight dashboard panel set (documented in the runbook) and a deep-link format compatible with incident-bot cards.

4) Alert
Adds an alert intended for SRE + telemetry oncall:
- Fires when p95 or p99 breaches for 10m OR when timeout rate breaches for 10m
- Includes annotations for top failing query_family and region
- Routes to `#eng-sre` and `#telemetry-oncall` (same routing as other perf canaries)

## Implementation details
- Canary uses the same auth mechanism as other perf canaries, but is scoped to a synthetic service identity with read-only access to the telemetry query endpoint. No tenant/customer identifiers are used.
- Query parameters are explicitly bounded (time window 5m, region scoped, no per-tenant grouping) to avoid creating cardinality pressure.
- Adds backoff + jitter when a run fails (prevents thundering herd if telemetry service is unhealthy).
- Adds an allowlist of query templates to prevent accidental addition of ad-hoc expensive queries.

## Changed areas
- `canaries/telemetry_query_latency_canary.ts`: new canary implementation + query families
- `canaries/index.ts`: registry wiring
- `config/canaries.yaml`: scheduling + regions + thresholds
- `alerts/telemetry_query_latency.rules.yaml`: alert definitions
- `runbooks/telemetry-query-latency-canary.md`: triage steps and escalation pointers
- `dashboards/telemetry_query_latency_canary.json`: panels for latency/errors by region and query family

## Testing
- Unit tests for:
  - threshold evaluation and failure reason mapping
  - query template rendering and hard bounds (time window, grouping)
  - retry/backoff behavior
- Local dry-run: `yarn canary telemetry-query-latency --once --region us-east-1`

## Rollout plan
- Merge behind `canary.telemetryQueryLatency.enabled` (default off)
- Enable in staging for 24h, then prod in us-east-1 only for 24h
- Expand to remaining regions after confirming alert noise and baseline distributions

## Notes
This canary is intentionally conservative: it aims to detect when incident-bot context gathering is at risk, not to load test the telemetry query service. If we want load-based validation, we should add a separate stress canary with an explicit budget and ownership.

---
### Commits
- canary: add telemetry query latency canary scaffold
- canary: implement bounded query families (gpu/queue/kv/error-budget)
- metrics: add histograms + failure reason labels
- alerts: add telemetry query latency SLO alert
- docs: add runbook + dashboard references

### CI
- build (node 20): pass
- lint: pass
- unit tests: pass
- canary dry-run (staging): pass

### Merge
Squash merged into `main`.

---
### Review conversation highlights
Logan Wright: "Please double-check that the canary can’t accidentally introduce high-cardinality tags (tenant_id, model, route). We’ve been burned here." 
Nadia Rahman (author): "Added a hard allowlist for group-by keys and a unit test that fails if `tenant_id|model|route` appear in the rendered query. Also capped time window to 5m."

Allison Grant: "Alert will be noisy if we page on single-region transient spikes. Can we require 2/3 regions OR a 10m window?" 
Nadia Rahman (author): "Updated rule to 10m and added annotations for top region/query_family; kept per-region firing but with a 10m window and higher p99 threshold to reduce flaps."

Miles Thornton: "Can we include a hint in the alert on what incident-bot symptom this maps to?" 
Nadia Rahman (author): "Added alert annotation: 'Incident-bot diagnostics may degrade (empty/slow context cards). Consider enabling degraded-mode (links-only) if widespread.'"

Caleb Johnson: "Any risk that this canary masks real issues because it uses cache?" 
Nadia Rahman (author): "We explicitly set `cache_bypass=false` to match incident-bot behavior; the goal is end-user perceived latency. Added metric for payload_bytes + noted in runbook how to check uncached latency if debugging."
- Adds a perf canary that continuously measures telemetry query service latency for the incident-bot diagnostics workload.
- Emits p50/p95/p99 + error/timeout rates and opens an alert when SLO is violated.
- Provides a runbook and dashboard links for quick triage during incidents.

payload.body:
Context: As part of ENG-4821/ENG-4828 (TP stability fixes), we need a repeatable long-context workload in perf-canary that exercises the failure modes we’ve seen under sustained mixed prefill/decode. Current TP coverage mostly targets short/medium contexts and does not reliably surface the “prefill spike -> decode starvation -> collective stall” class of issues.

What this PR does:
- Adds two new TP stress scenarios focused on long-context prefill + sustained decode:
  - tp_longctx_a100_80gb_tp4: long-context (32k) prefill, streaming decode, concurrency ramp
  - tp_longctx_h100_tp8: long-context (64k) prefill, streaming decode, higher steady-state concurrency
- Defines pass/fail thresholds that are explicitly stability-first (hang/timeout detection) and perf-aware (p50/p99 and throughput deltas vs baseline).
- Wires the scenarios into CI (GitHub Actions) as a gated workflow for PRs that opt-in via label (ci/gate-perf) and as a nightly on main for drift detection.
- Adds documentation on scenario intent, runtime flags, and how to interpret failures.

Scenario details (high level):
- Workload shape:
  - Prompts: weighted distribution with a heavy long-context bucket (>= 28k tokens) plus a smaller short bucket to keep scheduling pressure realistic.
  - Decode: streaming on, 256–512 tokens per request, mixed stop reasons.
  - Concurrency: ramp 1 -> 8 (A100) and 2 -> 16 (H100) with a steady-state hold to catch slow stalls.
  - Duration: ~12–15 min per scenario (kept under our runner window).
- Stability thresholds:
  - No run-level hang: scenario must complete within max_wall_clock (hard cap).
  - No “silent stall”: fails if progress heartbeat is absent for > 30s (client-side) OR if step-level throughput drops below min_tokens_per_sec for > 90s.
  - Request timeout rate <= 0.1% (timeouts are treated as hard failures unless explicitly annotated as infra).
- Perf thresholds:
  - Throughput regression > 5% vs baseline on the same runner type fails.
  - p99 end-to-end latency regression > 10% vs baseline fails.

CI/Gating:
- New workflow: tp-longctx-stress.yml
  - Runs on pull_request if label ci/gate-perf is present (keeps PR loop fast by default).
  - Runs nightly on main for both A100 and H100 runner pools.
- Artifacts:
  - Uploads run summary JSON + CSV timeseries (tokens/sec, p50/p99 latency, timeout counters) and the rendered report.
  - Includes runner metadata (GPU type, driver, NCCL, CUDA) to simplify correlations during triage.

Why label-gated instead of always-on:
- These are intentionally heavier than our smoke perf runs and require GPU runners. The label approach lets runtime PRs opt-in when touching TP scheduling/kernels while still giving us nightly signal for drift.

How to run locally (dev):
- ./bin/canary run scenarios/tp/tp_longctx_a100_80gb_tp4.yaml --set runtime.tp.enabled=true
- ./bin/canary report --input out/latest --format html

Docs:
- Adds a new section under docs/scenarios/tensor-parallel.md describing the long-context workloads, thresholds, and common failure patterns (scheduler starvation vs comms stall vs infra runner issues).

Notes / follow-ups:
- We intentionally kept the thresholds conservative to catch stalls/hangs first. Once ENG-4824/4825 land broadly, we can tighten perf budgets and add a mixed prefill/decode cancellation subtest.

Checklist:
- [x] Scenario configs added + validated on bench-lab A100/H100
- [x] Thresholds tuned against 3 baseline runs
- [x] CI workflow added + artifact upload verified
- [x] Docs updated

References:
- ENG-4828 (perf-canary TP stress scenarios)
- ENG-4821 (initiative umbrella)
- Related runtime work: tp watchdog + heartbeat metrics (see redwood PRs in ENG-4823/4826)
Marcus Reed (review): The stability thresholds look good, but I’m worried about false positives from transient runner hiccups. Can we distinguish “no progress” from “low throughput” and add a short grace window after ramp changes?
Rina Kobayashi (author): Yep. I split the detector into (a) heartbeat absence (hard fail after 30s) and (b) sustained low throughput (fail after 90s). I also added a 20s grace period after each concurrency step to avoid tripping while the system re-stabilizes. Pushed in 8c1a2f4.
Kira Volkov (review): Baseline comparison: are we pinning by runner type + CUDA/NCCL versions? Otherwise baseline drift will be noisy.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Baselines are keyed on (scenario_id, runner_pool, gpu_name, driver, cuda, nccl). Nightly updates the baseline only on green runs. Added that metadata to the artifact summary as well. See commit 2f9b7d1.
Aisha Bello (review): For alertability later, can we ensure the summary includes timeout_rate and a single “stall_reason” field when failing? Helps with dashboards if we mirror this logic.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Added timeout_rate to the top-level summary and introduced stall_reason enum: HEARTBEAT_GAP / LOW_TOKENS_PER_SEC / MAX_WALL_CLOCK / PERF_REGRESSION. See 41d0c6a.
Sahana Iyer (review): CI wiring: label-gated is fine, but please ensure the workflow is not required for all PRs. Also double check secrets usage on fork PRs.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Confirmed: workflow only runs on pull_request when label ci/gate-perf exists and uses internal self-hosted runners + repo-scoped secrets, so it won’t execute on forks. Updated docs/ci/perf-gating.md to spell this out.
Marcus Reed (approval): Ran on bench-lab (A100) and it caught the expected long-prefill throughput dip without failing. CI green. LGTM.
payload.title: Add TP long-context stress scenarios + thresholds (A100/H100) and wire into CI gating

Motivation: Long-tail incidents often require a compact, queryable snapshot of an invocation (tokens, top-level spans, prompt shape, cost estimate) to triage without pulling full traces. This PR adds a lightweight observability snapshot exporter that periodically writes compact invocation snapshots to the telemetry store, and introduces an alert-mixdown mechanism that reduces noisy alerting by weighting route-level signals and optionally attaching sampled snapshots to alerts.

What this PR does (summary): Adds a snapshotter service that emits compact invocation documents (invocation_id, timestamp, route, prompt_shape_hash, token_counts, estimated_token_cost, top_n_error_spans, pre/post-kv-warm flags). Adds a minimal sidecar exporter to the telemetry pipeline for fast writes. Adds alert-mixdown rules that: (1) apply per-route weight and quiet window; (2) attach one sampled snapshot per alert group when severity >= warning; (3) allow per-tenant opt-out. Adds a Grafana dashboard and a focused playbook for oncall. Updates docs with configuration knobs and upgrade notes.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implement snapshotter runtime and config schema
- [x] Export compact snapshot docs to telemetry index with bounded retention
- [x] Hook snapshot attachment into alerting pipeline with rate limits
- [x] Add unit + integration tests for sample selection
- [x] Add dashboard + runbook pages
- [x] Add Linear links for rollout and opt-out controls

Backward compatibility & safety: Snapshots are opt-in per-tenant by default off; when enabled snapshots are written to the existing telemetry index under a new type (invocation_snapshot_v1) with TTL. The alert-mixdown is configurable and disabled by default for existing alerts. No breaking public API changes.

Related: ENG-5732 (observability long-tail), ENG-5778 (alerting noise reduction).
- 0a1b2c3: initial snapshotter and schema + config
- 1b2c3d4: sidecar exporter and telemetry client integration
- 2c3d4e5: alert-mixdown rules and attachment plumbing
- 3d4e5f6: dashboard JSON and playbook draft
- 4e5f6g7: unit/integration tests and flakiness fixes
- 5f6g7h8: docs, changelog, and small lint fixes
Miguel: overall great direction — can we bound the snapshot size? Please ensure we trim user-provided context.
Author (Priya): trimmed user context and added max_snapshot_bytes with telemetry-sidecap enforcement.
Hannah: request to add per-tenant opt-out and explicit retention TTL in the mapping.
Author: added opt-out flag in tenant config and mapping TTL; added documentation.
Arjun: CI flake on integration test (race on sample selector) — please fix.
Author: fixed selector race by moving selection to a single-threaded sampler loop and added stress test.
Miguel: approve after verify retention and opt-out behaviour in staging.
Hannah: approve.
Merge: squashed and merged by Priya after green CI.
Adds a new optional invocation snapshot exporter (invocation_snapshot_v1) that teams can enable per-tenant to speed long-tail debugging; introduces alert-mixdown to reduce noisy alerts by route weighting and optional snapshot attachment. Config knobs: max_snapshot_bytes, snapshot_ttl_days, alert_mixdown_weights. Disabled by default; see docs/observability/snapshots.md for upgrade steps.

payload.body:
Motivation: We observed recurring noisy short-lived latency regressions that pass single-slice detectors but cause user-visible blips under specific traffic blends. This PR introduces a cross-slice quantile-trend fusion detector that combines quantile deltas across stratified traffic slices and uses an entropy-based gate to reduce false positives from low-information slices. The approach fuses short-term and medium-term quantile trends per slice, weights them by traffic fraction and slice stability, and aggregates a probabilistic confidence score. An entropy gate suppresses alerts when per-slice signal entropy is below threshold, preventing overreaction to low-variance or single-outlier dominated slices. Key outcomes: improved precision at 95% recall on historical regressions, reduced false positive rate by ~32% in replay tests, and integration into the rollout guard pipeline as an optional check for staged rollouts. Implementation notes: Added a new fusion runtime component that accepts per-slice histograms, computes trend vectors, and emits a fused quantile delta with confidence metadata. The entropy gate computes normalized slice entropy over a sliding window and sets an adaptive suppression factor. This PR includes deterministic offline replay tests and a lightweight in-cluster canary emulator for smoke testing. Rollout plan: feature flagged behind canary.experimental.cross_slice_quantile_fusion, enabled in canary-runner for internal perf-canary and gradually rolled to production canaries after one week of green metrics and manual signoff. Related work: complements the temporal-cohort consensus detector and the multiscale fingerprint quarantiner; references ENG-2207 for evaluation harness and ENG-2215 for entropy heuristics. Breaking changes: none. Commits summary: feat(fusion): add cross-slice quantile trend fusion engine; feat(gates): add entropy gate and adaptive suppression; test: add unit and replay tests with historical regression fixtures; ci: add integration job and update canary-runner config; docs: runbook and onboarding notes. Changed areas: core fusion algorithm in src/canary/fusion/quantile_fusion.py; entropy gate implementation in src/canary/gates/entropy_gate.py; new cross-slice aggregation API at src/canary/api/aggregation.py; canary-runner wiring in deployments/canary-runner/config.yml; replay harness updates in tools/replay/harness.py; unit and replay tests in tests/canary/; documentation in docs/runbooks/canary-quantile-fusion.md. Testing: local unit tests and deterministic replays on a 30-day window of production traffic including 12 known regressions were used to calibrate thresholds. Integration CI runs include a canary-emulator that simulates slice-level traffic and validated that the fusion detector preserves latency SLOs under injected regressions. Observability: new metrics (fusion.confidence, fusion.fused_delta_q90, fusion.suppress_reason) and dashboards added to perf-canary team Grafana. Backwards compatibility: aggregation API accepts legacy per-slice histogram payloads; when feature flag is off the system falls back to existing single-slice detectors. Merge and deployment: PR merged via squash after approvals, feature behind flag, gradual rollout with telemetry-based gating. Runbook: docs/runbooks/canary-quantile-fusion.md contains remediation steps and guidance for threshold tuning.
Luca Perez: Nice design. Can you clarify the complexity of the fusion step at 1k slices? We need an upper bound for scheduling.
Maya Thompson: The fusion step is O(n*logk) where k is quantile bins; added a note and a benchmark in tests to show 1.2ms median on 1k slices on c5.xlarge-equivalent. See tests/canary/bench_fusion.py.
Anya Kline: Entropy gate looks reasonable but we should avoid too aggressive suppression during low traffic windows. Can you add adaptive scaling?
Maya Thompson: Added adaptive scaling that lowers suppression during windows where total throughput < 200 qps; rationale documented in runbook.
Samir Rao: Integration CI flaked once on canary-emulator, reran and passed. Approving.
QA Bot: Integration jobs passed in second run. All checks green.
payload.title: Introduce cross-slice quantile-trend fusion canary with entropy gating

payload.body:
Context: we’ve had at least one production regression where streaming responses under-counted output tokens in metering, which then cascaded into Unit Economics dashboards (blended $/1M output tokens) and reconciliation views. This PR adds an automated canary that detects output-token metering regressions before a gateway/runtime change is widely rolled out.

What this adds:
- New canary suite `metering_output_token_parity` that runs against a small allowlisted canary tenant in prod.
- Exercises BOTH streaming and non-streaming generation paths (including tool-call shaped outputs) and validates:
  1) output_tokens reported by the API response metadata
  2) output_tokens recorded by metering events (usage pipeline)
  3) that the delta between (1) and (2) is within a configured tolerance after accounting for ingestion latency
- Adds guardrails for ingestion lag: the canary polls the metering lookup API for up to 6 minutes (configurable) before declaring missing events.
- Emits a single structured result event per run (pass/fail + diagnostics) and wires alert routing:
  - warning to #eng-platform when parity drift > 0.5% for a single run
  - page oncall (telemetry) when drift > 1.0% for 3 consecutive runs OR when missing metering events exceed 2% of requests

Key implementation details:
- Request set: 18 requests per run (9 streaming, 9 non-streaming) with fixed prompt fixtures to keep variance low.
- Models: uses `rw-llama-3.1-8b-instruct` (cheap + stable) pinned to a specific model version for determinism.
- Tokenization alignment: uses the server-side token counts only (we do NOT attempt client-side tokenization); the canary is specifically checking parity between two server-side sources of truth.
- Correlation: uses `x-request-id` and `metering_correlation_id` to look up metering records; falls back to time window + route + model + canary tenant ID when correlation ID missing.
- Flake reduction: retries on 429/503 with exponential backoff; run is considered inconclusive (non-paging) if infra is degraded and error rate > 30%.

Rollout:
- Enabled in dry-run mode for 24h (records metrics but does not page).
- After 24h, flip `CANARY_METERING_PARITY_PAGING_ENABLED=true` in the perf-canary prod deployment.

Notes / limitations:
- This is not a billing reconciliation test. It only checks output token counts parity between API-side accounting and metering events.
- Known source of noise: very rare duplicate metering events; the canary de-dupes by (correlation_id, sequence).

Operational links:
- Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/unit-econ-output-token-parity (will be finalized alongside ENG-8435)

Why now:
- The internal Unit Economics dashboard (v1) depends on reliable output token counts (especially streaming); this canary is intended to catch regressions like the one fixed in `redwood` PR-19355 before they impact exec/finance reporting.
Allison Grant: Tolerance looks tight. Are we sure we won’t page due to metering lag?
Nadia Rahman (author): The canary waits up to 6 minutes for events and only pages on 3 consecutive runs >1% drift. Single-run drift posts to #eng-platform only. Also added an inconclusive mode when prod error rate is high.

Sean Gallagher: Please add an explicit guard for partial streaming truncation (client disconnect) so we don’t attribute it to metering.
Nadia Rahman (author): Good call. Added a fixture where we intentionally cancel a stream and assert that both API metadata + metering record the same truncated output_tokens; also tags those requests separately and excludes them from drift paging thresholds.

Logan Wright: Correlation fallback via time window scares me. Can we require correlation_id for the paging path?
Nadia Rahman (author): Updated: paging calculations only include requests with correlation_id present. Fallback lookup remains for debugging output in the log payload (non-paging).

Caleb Johnson: Add more structured diagnostics in the failure payload (model, route, streaming flag, expected vs observed tokens).
Nadia Rahman (author): Done. Failure includes per-request rows and summarizes top deltas; also includes metering record timestamps to see lag.

Allison Grant: Approved.
Sean Gallagher: Approved.
Logan Wright: Approved after correlation_id-only change.

Merged via squash.
Internal: Adds production canary to detect output-token metering parity regressions (streaming/non-streaming) and alert Telemetry/SRE before broad rollout.
