Motivation: production private upgrades exposed a class of failures where partial schema migrations combined with controller restarts left clusters in a nonrecoverable state. This PR introduces a snapshot-first upgrade flow and an explicit downgrade guard that prevents accidental rollbacks unless a verified restore snapshot exists. High level changes: 1) rpictl snapshot create/restore commands (CLI + install hooks) that create a consistent data snapshot (Postgres logical dump + object storage of blobstore pointers) prior to any upgrade; 2) Helm hooks to trigger pre-upgrade snapshot job and a post-upgrade health-check job that auto-rolls back on detectable data drift; 3) a migration-runner job that validates schema diffs in dry-run mode and fails the upgrade if forward-only migrations would be irreversible; 4) Terraform module updates to provision a dedicated snapshot bucket (S3-compatible) with lifecycle + encryption, plus state-lock improvements to avoid concurrent upgrades; 5) an explicit downgrade-blocker controller that checks release semver and snapshot provenance and rejects a lower-version apply unless --force-downgrade is passed with validated snapshot id. Backwards compatibility: installer still works without snapshot bucket (legacy mode) but the new guardrails are enabled by default for new deployments. Checklist: - [x] rpictl CLI + docs - [x] Helm charts and hooks - [x] migration-runner image and manifests - [x] Terraform module + tests - [x] e2e upgrade test using KIND + local S3 emulator - [x] security review (KMS + bucket policy) Rollout plan: feature flag gated for existing clusters; default-on for new installs. Related: Linear ENG-9821 (upgrade resilience), ENG-9902 (terraform snapshot infra). Links: internal runbook https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-9821/upgrade-resilience, design doc https://redwood.internal/docs/installer-snapshots.
Added snapshot-first upgrade flow and automatic downgrade guardrails for private installer: rpictl snapshot commands, Helm pre/post upgrade hooks, migration-runner dry-run validation, Terraform snapshot bucket module, and an admission webhook to block accidental downgrades. These changes are opt-in for existing clusters and enabled by default for new installs.
Unit: CLI + controller unit tests run locally (go test) and on CI
Integration: e2e upgrade test using KIND + minio passed in CI (integration-e2e), validates snapshot creation and restore flow
Load: simulated snapshot on 200GB logical workload tested in staging, average upload 12m with multipart enabled
Security: KMS envelope encryption validated, bucket policy restricts access to installer service account
If a release fails post-upgrade health checks the post-upgrade hook triggers a Helm rollback automatically; manual rollback steps: 1) rpictl snapshot restore --id <snapshot-id> --wait to restore DB and blob pointers, 2) helm rollback <release> <revision> via the console, 3) monitor health-checks and open INCIDENT if state mismatch persists. For emergency downgrades, use --force-downgrade with a verified snapshot id and coordinate with on-call; audit-log entries are required.
Snapshot uploads require S3-compatible storage with server-side encryption and KMS key access limited to installer/service-account. The admission webhook enforces provenance checks; no plaintext credentials are added to manifests. Terraform changes ensure ACME of bucket policies; security-scan in CI passes. See docs for KMS key rotation guidance.

Aisha Patel: Addressed; multipart enabled behind feature flag and prometheus metrics exported as rpi_snapshot_duration_seconds in commit b4c1a9f.
Sofia Chen: The downgrade-blocker needs an override for emergency on-call. Can we gate with a CC-list and an audit log entry?
Aisha Patel: Added --force-downgrade along with a required snapshot-id and an audit-log event; webhook rejects plain --force without a valid snapshot reference (see e1f4b67).

Aisha Patel: Added an opt-in terraform apply target and documented the migration steps in docs/installer/upgrade-with-snapshots.md

Motivation: private deployments frequently require an initial, idempotent enrollment flow for customer HSMs and a safe upgrade path for KMS-backed secrets. This PR implements a bootstrap enrollment controller, Helm pre-upgrade hooks to reconcile sealed secrets to a new envelope key, Terraform idempotency fixes for kms modules, and an explicit rollback-safe secret staging flow. Changes are focused on automation so operator work during upgrades is minimal and recoverable. Scope: (1) A new 'kms-enroller' component that runs once per cluster to generate an envelope key in Vault Transit or directly provision a HSM-wrapped key via PKCS#11 attestation; (2) Helm chart hooks: pre-upgrade job that validates cluster keys and moves sealedsecret payloads to a staging namespace while writing reconciliation records to a ConfigMap; post-upgrade job to switch active key and re-seal payloads; (3) Terraform module tweaks to make kms resources fully idempotent across apply/destroy cycles and expose new outputs for enrollment tokens; (4) A rollback-aware operator hook that keeps previous envelope key active for 72 hours and automatically reverts if checks fail. Security model: enrollment uses short-lived enrollment tokens (rotating via Terraform state), attestation to HSM via PKCS#11 and TPM endorsement where available, and Vault policies scoped to transit:encrypt/decrypt only. Migration path: - dry-run mode available on the enroller to simulate re-seal operations; - operators can opt into the automatic migration or run manual reconcile via the installer CLI; - automatic fallbacks to previous key ensure zero-downtime during partial failures. Testing and verification: integration tests added under test/integration/kms-enroll that mock HSM via SoftHSM and an end-to-end using a temporarily provisioned Vault instance. Canary rollout notes: default behavior is off behind a feature flag RELEASE_KMS_BOOTSTRAP; when enabled the installer performs a dry-run and creates a /bootstrap-ready ConfigMap before any mutation. Checklist: - [x] implement kms-enroller controller and CLI hooks - [x] pre/post-upgrade Helm hooks and job templates - [x] Terraform idempotency fixes and module outputs - [x] integration tests and CI pipeline updates - [x] documentation and upgrade notes. Risks: HSM attestation failure modes are explicitly caught and reported; fallback preserves previous envelope key to avoid irrecoverable secret loss. See linked linear items for rollout schedule and stakeholder sign-offs.
Marco Li: Overall direction looks good, please add metrics around enrollment latency and count so SRE can alert on stuck enrollments.
Asha Patel (author): Added prometheus metrics to controller and exported histogram 'kms_enrollment_duration_seconds' and counter 'kms_enrollments_total'.
Riley Nguyen: Terraform change looks correct, but please ensure state locking docs mention Crossplane and remote state edge cases.
Asha Patel: Expanded terraform/README with remote state and crossplane notes and added an acceptance test that creates/destroys the module twice.
Eva Korner: Need clearer failure messages on PKCS#11 failures, and ensure we don't leak the PKCS#11 token/slot in logs.
Asha Patel: Sanitized logs and added retryable error classification for attestation failures.
Marco Li: CI initially failed on SoftHSM version mismatch; re-ran pipeline after bumping test container image and CI passed.
Added an idempotent KMS enrollment flow for private deployments with Helm pre/post-upgrade hooks, Terraform idempotency fixes, and a rollback-safe staging path for secrets. Feature gated behind RELEASE_KMS_BOOTSTRAP. Operators should read docs/private-deployments/kms-enrollment.md before enabling.
Hotfix consideration: if customers run a 3rd-party HSM that doesn't support PKCS#11, the enroller will fall back to a manual enrollment path documented in the README.
Operational runbook added to docs with 'force-rollback' CLI and detection thresholds for automated revert.
Backwards compatibility: sealed secrets encrypted with previous envelope keys remain readable until TTL expires; controller keeps previous key active for 72 hours by default.

Motivation: reduce air-gapped bundle size and improve first-boot experience for on-prem installs across diverse Linux distros by shipping minimal, deterministic kernel-module helpers, a small CRI compatibility shim (auto-detects containerd/crio/cri-o), and a seeded OCI index for faster bootstrap. This PR introduces a new 'slim' airgap bundle layout intended for constrained environments and regulatory sites where image size and deterministic install ordering are critical. The change also adds a Terraform helper module to pre-seed a local registry with OCI index manifests and introduces upgrade/rollback metadata hooks to avoid kernel module drift during in-place upgrades.

What changed (summary): single-line install wrappers for kmod packages, kmod-install-helpers that detect distro/package manager (deb/rpm/apk) and try to apply out-of-tree module stubs when kernel headers are unavailable; a tiny CRI-compat shim binary and systemd unit that normalizes container runtime socket locations; helm chart patch to allow offline-only imagePullSecrets and explicit hostPort mappings used by the installer; terraform/modules/oci-seed module to push OCI index manifests and layer-lists to an airgapped registry; upgrade-preflight and rollback-postflight hooks that validate loaded kernel modules and reconcile the sealed vendor-lockfile.

Backwards compatibility: this is additive. Existing full bundles are unchanged; the slim bundle is opt-in via a new --bundle-profile=slim flag in installer bootstrap scripts and a new `bundleProfile: slim` value in the airgap bundle manifest. The kmod helpers are no-op when the runtime reports full bundle capabilities.

Testing and validation: unit tests for the kmod helper logic (bash/shim/test harness) and integration tests in perf-canary that validate install on CentOS 7/8, Rocky 8/9, Ubuntu 18.04/20.04/22.04, and RancherOS derivatives. Manual validation performed in an internal airgapped lab: seeded registry, install, upgrade, rollback.

Checklist:
- [x] New slim bundle layout and manifest schema changes (+ docs)
- [x] kmod install helpers and distro detection script (+ tests)
- [x] CRI shim binary (C minimal) and systemd unit (+ tests)
- [x] Terraform OCI seeder module and example usage
- [x] Helm chart opt-in values for offline-only mode
- [x] Upgrade/rollback hooks and migration test cases
- [x] Release notes and migration guidance

Commits: commit 1: add slim bundle manifest schema and generator templates; commit 2: add kmod helper scripts and unit tests; commit 3: add CRI shim and packaging; commit 4: terraform module for oci-seed and example; commit 5: helm chart values and install templates; commit 6: upgrade/rollback hooks and tests; commit 7: docs and release notes.

Files changed (high level): list below highlights modified paths and representative snippets where helpful. Most files are small scripts, module glue code, or helm value files.

Risks and mitigations: the kmod helpers attempt to operatively load or place out-of-tree module stubs; on systems where kernel headers are available the helpers defer to distro packaging. We run conservative heuristics and fail-safe markers so the installer can fall back to full bundle behaviour. The CRI shim only normalizes socket locations and will exit with a clear error if it cannot proxy; we include clear logs and healthchecks used by the console.

Operator notes: to build a slim bundle run `make airgap-profile BUNDLE_PROFILE=slim` in the private-installer directory. The terraform module `terraform/modules/oci-seed` contains a --dry-run flag to generate index manifests without pushing images for validation.

Migration notes: customers using existing on-prem bundles are unaffected. If teams adopt slim bundles they should run preflight checks included in the repo to ensure kernel module compatibility prior to production rollout.

Maya Thompson (author): Added build-dir check and fallback path in kmod-helper.sh. Also added a verbose flag for debugging.
Priya Shah: Terraform module needs idempotency checks for stale manifests in the local registry; what happens on partial push?
Maya Thompson (author): oci-seed now writes a .seeded marker with manifest hash and supports --force to re-seed; documented behavior in README.
Anders Müller: CI failed once on Alpine test due to musl edge-case in cri-shim; is this accounted for?
Maya Thompson (author): cri-shim rebuilt with musl-friendly flags and small test harness added; reran CI and green.

feat: kmod-install-helpers with distro detection (installer/scripts/kmod-helper.sh)
feat: small CRI-compat shim and systemd unit (installer/bin/cri-shim.c, packaging/)
chore: terraform oci-seed module and example usage (terraform/modules/oci-seed)
fix: helm chart values for offline mode and hostPort mapping (charts/redwood-private/values-slim.yaml)
test: add integration tests for slim profile (test/integration/airgap-slim)
docs: slim bundle migration guide and release notes (docs/installer/slim-bundles.md)
Added slim airgap bundle profile with kernel module helpers and a CRI compatibility shim; terraform oci-seed module for local registry seeding; helm chart opts for offline-only install. Guidance for adopting slim bundles included.

Motivation: private installs currently require multiple manual steps to stand up monitoring: a Terraform step to provision Kubernetes infra and persistent volumes, followed by ad-hoc Helm chart installs for Prometheus, Grafana, and a separate log shipping layer (Fluent Bit / Promtail + Loki). Operators reported drift between installs and painful manual upgrades. This PR delivers a single declarative Terraform module that orchestrates Helm Operator-driven installs for the monitoring stack (Prometheus Operator + kube-prometheus, Grafana with a resilient provisioning sidecar, and Loki + Promtail) and includes automated dashboard import, alert rules packaging, versioned migration hooks, and rollback-safe Grafana provisioning.
Initial module scaffold: terraform/modules/monitoring with variables and outputs
Add helmreleases for prometheus-operator, grafana-sidecar, loki, promtail
Implement grafana-provisioner: idempotent dashboard import and retry semantics
Add migration hooks for statefulset PV expansion and grafana provisioning rollbacks
Integration test harness + sample install overlays for on-prem and vpc profiles
Fix: upgrade path for existing installs that used legacy helm values (preserve secrets)

Motivation: Private control plane installations require predictable address allocation, repeatable security group policies, and correct cross-account DNS resolution. Current installs leave a lot of address space decisions to operators which causes drift and complex peering rules when we bring up multiple regional control planes. This PR implements: 1) a deterministic subnet allocator that splits a customer-provided VPC CIDR into named controlplane/worker/egress subnets anchored by AZ index so identical cluster manifests produce identical subnet ranges; 2) a set of security-group templates (controlplane, worker-api, egress-proxy, inter-region-peering) exposed as variables so operators can opt in/out to additional stateful ports; 3) conditional Route53 Resolver rules and endpoint automation to forward redwood-internal names (controlplane.redwood.local, datastore.internal.redwood) to customer DNS/IPs or to the VPC endpoints depending on install mode, with clear fallbacks for cross-account peering. The description below is a single continuous string but has logical sections separated by headings and checklists. Changes summary: - Terraform: added modules/network/subnet_allocator.tf, modules/network/sg_templates.tf, modules/dns/route53_resolver_rules.tf, modules/network/az_indexing.tf - Installer: bin/installer/allocate_subnets.py (deterministic allocator used during plan), bin/installer/validate_networking.sh - Helm: charts/redwood-private/values.schema.yaml updated to expose sg template flags - Docs: docs/private-installer/subnets.md, docs/private-installer/dns-forwarding.md - Tests: test/terraform/unit/test_subnet_allocator.go, test/e2e/dns_forwarding_test.sh Commits (high-level): - 1a2b3c4: initial deterministic allocator + unit tests - 2b3c4d5: wire allocator into installer; add CLI flag --seed-for-allocation - 3c4d5e6: SG templates, default port lists and deny-by-default rules - 4d5e6f7: Route53 resolver rule module with cross-account role assumptions - 5e6f7g8: docs and migration notes Why deterministic allocation: When multiple installs are created from the same manifest (e.g. single tenant per region), operators expect deterministic IP placement for firewall rules and peering. The allocator uses the provided VPC CIDR, target number of AZs, and per-AZ index to carve /28-/20 subnets with a stable mapping (algorithm described in docs). Security group templates: Templates are parameterized lists keyed by role. We default to deny-all-ingress/egress and open only the minimal ports needed, with explicit variables to allow wider ranges for legacy customer requirements. Route53 resolver automation: The module creates inbound/outbound endpoints on demand, and conditionally creates resolver rules that forward controlplane.* to 10.0.1.2 (customer DNS) when customer-provided-dns is set, or forwards to aws-vpc-endpoints when private-endpoints-mode is selected. It also adds tags used by the TransitGateway peering automation so resolver rules are discovered across accounts. Backwards compatibility/migration: - Existing installs without the new flag keep current allocations. - A migration tool (bin/installer/migrate_subnets.py) is included to compute and optionally apply the new deterministic allocation; it emits a dry-run report showing differences. Checklist: - [x] deterministic allocator implementation and unit tests - [x] SG templates with examples for common customer profiles - [x] Route53 resolver rules + cross-account role assumption docs - [x] Installer integration + end-to-end e2e test - [x] Docs and upgrade notes Testing notes and reproduction: - Unit tests for allocator cover /16 -> /24 splits and multi-AZ stable mapping. - e2e test spins up a minimal VPC in test-account, creates outbound resolver endpoints, and verifies controlplane.<install>.redwood.local resolves to configured target. - Manual validation steps included in docs/private-installer/dns-forwarding.md What changed in Terraform (illustrative snippets): - modules/network/subnet_allocator.tf: added resource "local_file" "allocation_map" { content = var.allocation_map } - modules/dns/route53_resolver_rules.tf: added aws_route53_resolver_rule "controlplane_forward" { domain_name = "controlplane.redwood.local" rule_type = "FORWARD" resolver_endpoint_id = aws_vpc_endpoint.this.id target_ip { ip = var.customer_dns_ip } } Limitations and open items: - IPv6 deterministic allocation deferred (tracked in ENG-3899) - Resolver rules across non-AWS clouds require additional adapters (future work) Review summary and conversation: - Diego: "Can we ensure the allocator never produces subnets that overlap reserved AWS /100 ranges for AWS-managed services?" Author reply: "Added a reservedRanges variable and pre-flight check; installer will fail early with actionable message." - Maya: "SG defaults look tight; add example allowing existing monitoring ranges." Author: "Added three example profiles (monitoring, pci-legacy, permissive) and documented risks." - Liam: "CI flaked on e2e. Confirmed rerun succeeded and recorded artifact link." CI and checks: - terraform fmt/lint: pass - unit tests: pass - e2e (integration): initial run failed due to quota in sandbox account, rerun after quota increase passed - security scan: pass - package build: pass Merge: Squash-merged into main after approvals (Diego + Maya), release-note entry included in docs/internal/release_notes.md Release notes (short): - deterministic subnet allocation for private installs - new SG templates for control-plane and egress profiles - conditional Route53 resolver automation for cross-account DNS forwarding Migration note (short): run bin/installer/migrate_subnets.py --dry-run to preview changes. Summary: Introduce a sealed-OCI-registry connector component that enables an ephemeral local registry sidecar to serve signed, content-addressable runtime bundles in fully offline sites, plus a small Terraform module (airgap-egress) to provision minimal egress rules/NAT for controlled registry seeding. Motivation: many customers deploy Redwood Private in heavily restricted networks where a full persistent registry is undesirable. The connector provides a deterministic, GPG-signed index and lockfile so site operators can seed an ephemeral registry from a single sealed bundle and safely update it with delta snapshots. This PR also adds explicit RHEL8 slim runtime bundles with sha512 manifests, and lightweight k0s bootstrap shims to broaden supported kube distros. What changed (checklist): [x] sealed OCI registry connector service and operator; [x] terraform/modules/airgap-egress with security-group/NAT template and examples; [x] bundles/rhel8/signed-index and manifest generator; [x] installer/bootstrap/k0s shim and preflight checks; [x] helm chart updates for airgap-registry (values to enable sealed mode); [x] e2e harness for offline seeding smoke test. Design notes: The connector runs as a short-lived job+sidecar pair that validates the sealed bundle's GPG signature, materializes blobs to a local registry, writes an immutable lockfile (content-addressed), and exposes a /prometheus metrics endpoint for seeding progress. The Terraform module creates a minimal 'airgap-egress' security group plus an optional NAT gateway and a route table that can be used in on-prem clouds or private VPC-like environments; the defaults are conservative and require explicit enablement. Backwards compatibility: All features are opt-in. Existing installs will not change behavior unless users enable the new helm value 'airgap.registry.sealed.enabled=true' or apply the terraform module. Testing: Unit tests for manifest/signature verification; integration test that seeds a k0s cluster with the ephemeral registry in an isolated container network; manual verification on RHEL8 VM for package index and systemd unit templates. Operators guide (short): 1) Create sealed bundle using tools/bundle/seal.sh; 2) Apply terraform module to create egress ACLs if you need SRC NAT for registry seeding; 3) Install helm chart with sealed mode enabled and point to the sealed bundle local path or HTTP artifact; 4) Run installer bootstrap (k0s or kubeadm) which invokes preflight that checks lockfile hashes. Links: Linear ENG-2981 (offline registry UX), ENG-3050 (rhel bundles), SUP-1219 (customer request). Related: RFC#2026 (airgap-sealed-bundles). Notes for operators: signed-index uses GPG key rotation via keys stored in the sealed bundle; connector enforces a strict key whitelist. Security: no persistent credentials left on disk, registry blobs are stored under a per-job ephemeral directory and pruned after the seed completes unless 'persist=true' is set in Helm values. Migration plan: None required; opt-in feature. Rollback: Helm value toggle and Terraform destroy for egress module. Known limitations: does not yet support policy-driven delta merges across multiple sealed bundles; larger installs (>10GB) will need longer seeding window and may choose a persistent mirror. Checklist before merge: [x] design review approved; [x] tests green in CI; [x] e2e smoke on k0s green; [x] documentation updated in docs/airgap/sealed-connector.md; [x] security review completed.
Adds sealed OCI registry connector and terraform 'airgap-egress' module; RHEL8 signed runtime index; k0s bootstrap support. Opt-in, non-breaking improvements to on-prem installer.

Context: With signed offline bundles, Support/SEs frequently need to answer "did verification run" and "what exactly was verified" from a support bundle alone (esp. in air-gapped environments where customers share a tarball via offline transport). Today the support bundle includes installer logs and config, but it does not summarize the offline bundle’s manifest/signature state, leading to longer back-and-forth (SUP-31844) and mis-triage when transport corrupts artifacts (SUP-31892). This PR adds a structured summary file and a small amount of diagnostic output so that a support bundle can stand alone for first-pass triage without exposing sensitive customer data. What this changes: (1) Adds a new support bundle attachment: support/bundle-verification.json containing the last-known offline bundle verification result, plus key metadata pulled from the signed manifest and verifier. (2) Includes the raw verification error code + remediation hint (not the full stack trace) to align with the installer’s verification error taxonomy. (3) Captures bundle identity fields needed to correlate to release artifacts: bundle_build_id, bundle_version, manifest_digest_sha256, signature_digest_sha256, signer_key_id, trust_store_version, and installer_version. (4) Adds a "verification_context" block that records whether verification ran during preflight, whether break-glass override was used, and any detected time-skew handling path (without recording the host clock). Safety/redaction: no file paths outside the bundle root are recorded; no customer tokens/URLs are included; the trust store content is not dumped, only the configured trust store version/id and the selected key id. Implementation notes: the support bundle generator now consumes the same in-memory VerificationReport object returned by preflight (or loads the persisted report if present) and writes a stable JSON file using canonical key ordering for diffs. If verification has never been run, the support bundle records status=unknown and includes next steps. Testing: unit tests cover "success", "hash mismatch", "unknown key", "not yet valid" and "break-glass" cases; integration test verifies support bundle output is produced in air-gapped mode. Release note: none (internal supportability improvement), but docs/runbook owners have been notified to reference the new file in triage steps.
Dev Patel (review): Can we make sure Support has a single place to look without parsing logs? Suggest a top-level "status" plus "reason_code" and a short "next_steps" string.
Ethan Park (author): Added top-level status + reason_code + next_steps. Mapped next_steps from existing error taxonomy so it stays consistent with CLI output.
Logan Wright (review): Please confirm we’re not emitting anything that could be considered customer environment PII (hostnames, internal mount paths). Also avoid including the entire trust store.
Ethan Park (author): Confirmed: no hostnames, no absolute paths, no trust store dump. Only trust_store_version + selected signer_key_id. Added a unit test asserting no "path:" keys and no "trusted_keys" array is emitted.
Marcus Lin (review): From a security perspective, include manifest digest + signature digest so we can detect replay/tamper from the support bundle. Also ensure the file is clearly marked as derived from verification, not a new source of truth.
Ethan Park (author): Added manifest_digest_sha256 + signature_digest_sha256. File header comment is not possible in JSON, but added "generated_by" and "source" fields (e.g., source=preflight_verification_report) and documented in SUPPORT.md.
Owen Phillips (review): In SUP-31892 we saw customers using zip/unzip that altered files. Can we surface "bundle_path_transport_warning" when we detect common corruption patterns?
Ethan Park (author): I didn’t add heuristics here (risk of false positives), but I did include the normalized error mapping and next_steps that explicitly calls out "re-transfer bundle, avoid tools that modify permissions/line endings" for hash mismatch cases.
Dev Patel (approval): This will materially reduce first-response time. Approved once CI is green.
Logan Wright (approval): Looks good; thanks for keeping the redaction tight.
Marcus Lin (approval): Approved; security requirements met.
Ethan Park (author): Re-ran integration tests after addressing a flaky temp-dir assertion; all green.

Motivation: Private installs occasionally encountered mid-upgrade TF state contention across controller processes and racey GPU nodepool rollbacks when an upgrade fails partway through. This PR introduces a light-weight TFState Coordinator service and a GPU Rollback Handler Terraform module to make state locks explicit, enable safe coordinated upgrades, and provide a deterministic rollback path for GPU nodepools. Changes: 1) modules/tfstate-coordinator: new module that provisions a small, policy-driven locking table (DynamoDB-compatible) plus a controller deployment (k8s) that exposes a minimal REST API for acquire/release/heartbeat of logical state locks; 2) modules/gpu-nodepool-rollback: idempotent rollback module that captures nodepool configuration snapshots (labels, taints, autoscaling settings, subnet attachment) in an immutable S3 prefix and exposes a plan-only path for dry-run rollbacks; 3) installer/upgrade: wiring in the coordinator to the upgrade controller so the controller acquires a cluster-scoped lock before mutating tfstate-backed resources; 4) docs and examples: upgrade-playbook.md and example-migrations/ showing step-by-step for existing customers; 5) CI and tests: add terraform unit tests, integration harness that simulates concurrent runs and a failure injection test for GPU pool delete+recreate scenario. Backwards compatibility: the coordinator is optional; by default installer continues to use existing remote state locking (backend locks) if the coordinator is not enabled. Migration path and rollout plan included in the README. Testing performed: local terraform plan/apply against a small fixture cluster, integration pipeline run that simulates two concurrent upgrade controllers (conflict expected then resolved via coordinator), and manual verification on staging where we triggered a synthetic failure in nodepool upgrade and tested automatic rollback to snapshot. Rollout plan: feature-flag defaulted to off -> enable in staging -> bake for 3 days -> enable in early adopter private installs -> enable by default. Checklist: [x] module implemented [x] e2e tests added [x] docs and playbook [x] migration notes [x] canary rollout plan
Diego: Can we avoid adding another datastore by relying on existing backend locks? Aisha: Backend locks are not sufficient for the installer controller because multiple controllers (operator + bootstrapper) race; coordinator makes semantics explicit and allows cross-account coordination. Priya: Confirm IAM least-privilege for the snapshot writer lambda. Aisha: tightened IAM policy in commit d4e5f6g and documented required KMS key usage. Liam: Request add a dry-run path to rollback module so SREs can preview changes. Aisha: added plan-only mode and test coverage. Diego: Approve after CI green. Priya: Approve. Comments addressed and small formatting nit fixed in a follow-up commit.
Private installer: optional TFState Coordinator for coordinated upgrades; GPU Nodepool Rollback module providing snapshot-based safe rollback; upgrade-playbook and migration notes added; feature-flagged rollout; no default behavioral breaking changes
1) Read docs/private-installer/migration-notes.md for feature-flag usage; 2) Deploy modules/tfstate-coordinator to shared infra (apply Terraform with coordinator_enabled=true); 3) Enable coordinator feature flag in installer config for staging; 4) Run a dry-run upgrade and validate plan-only rollback snapshots; 5) Promote to production cohorts per rollout plan; 6) Decommission old heuristics after 4 weeks
This PR intentionally keeps the coordinator optional to allow gradual adoption. The snapshot writer uses customer-managed KMS keys; SREs must ensure IAM principal for the lambda has kms:Decrypt and s3:Get/Put for the snapshot bucket. We intentionally scoped snapshots to a per-tenant prefix to make restores deterministic.

Motivation: Customers running air-gapped Private deployments want smaller, incremental OCI bundles that support multiple CPU architectures (x86_64, arm64) and per-distro overlays (kubeadm, rke2, k3s) so upgrades and node replacements can consume only the layers required for their platform. This PR introduces a layered multi-arch bundle format + a lightweight overlay system that applies runtime distro-specific patches during installation. Key changes: 1) new layered OCI index generator that produces per-arch index manifests and a top-level umbrella index; 2) delta snapshot metadata that allows clients to fetch only changed layers for incremental updates; 3) distro overlay manifests (kubeadm-1.26, rke2-1.23, k3s-1.28) with small systemd unit drop-ins and CRI shim config fixes; 4) installer changes to resolve and validate the layered index, apply overlays atomically, and provide an explicit rollback path. Checklist: - [x] implement layered OCI index generator - [x] add per-arch delta metadata and verifier - [x] add distro overlays and examples - [x] wire installer to apply overlays in airgap mode - [x] tests: unit + e2e airgap multi-arch smoke - [x] document format and migration steps Docs: docs/airgap/multi-arch-bundle.md includes format, migration strategy, and example commands. Migration notes: existing single-index bundles remain supported; migrate by generating layered index with --umbrella flag and distributing the umbrella index plus arch-specific OCI blobs. Rollback: installer writes a snapshot manifest before apply and will attempt to restore previous manifest + layers if any overlay post-apply check fails. Security: signed index support enforced in CI and verified at install time (cosign v2). Related: complements ENG-7891 (airgap distribution improvements) and OPS-402 (onboarding requirements for arm64 fleets).
Marco Nguyen: Nice work. Two questions: (1) can we avoid shipping duplicate layers between x86/arm if the blob checksum matches? (2) overlay_applier needs clearer failure semantics so we don't leave half-applied state.
Anya Patel: For (1) the layered index deduplicates by digest and only references shared blobs from multiple arch entries; generator uses content-addressing so duplicates are avoided. For (2) installer now writes a pre-apply snapshot and uses atomic rename for active-manifest; failure will trigger rollback and we added verification checks post-apply.
Liam O'Connor: Please add unit tests covering signature verification path; I saw CI flake on cosign verification once.
Anya Patel: Added signature verification test and extended CI job to run cosign verify using offline keyring in test harness.
Rina Shah: Approving the approach, but please include a short note in release notes about the new umbrella index format and migration command.
Anya Patel: Added release notes and a migration example in docs/multi-arch-bundle.md
Added layered multi-arch airgap bundle format and distro-specific overlay support. Customers can generate an umbrella index to serve both x86_64 and arm64 with deduplicated layers. Installer applies overlays atomically and will rollback on failure. See docs/airgap/multi-arch-bundle.md for migration steps and examples.

Motivation: Customers with multi-AZ private control planes saw elevated egress cost and transient routing flips when NAT pools or PrivateLink endpoints were rebalanced. This change introduces an AZ-aware egress gateway allocator and a conditional PrivateLink routing mode that creates PrivateLink endpoints only for subnets tagged as "redwood:privatelink=true". The allocator pins egress assignments to AZ-local gateway instances where capacity permits, falls back gracefully to cross-AZ gateways when required, and exposes a deterministic allocation table so rollout and troubleshooting are reproducible.

What this PR does (single-string description): Adds a controller (egress_allocator) that reconciles EgressGateway CRs, selects AZ-local gateway resources, and writes assignment annotations. Adds a privatelink_router controller that can create/delete PrivateLink endpoints based on subnet tags and route table annotations. Adds Terraform module changes to support named egress pools, EIP rotation policies, and per-AZ affinity tags. Updates Helm templates to expose allocator feature-flag and health/readiness metrics. Adds integration tests that simulate AZ failover and verify allocator stability and minimal route churn. Adds docs with a step-by-step migration and an upgrade/rollback playbook.

Migration and rollout notes: Default behavior is backward compatible — allocator is disabled unless featureFlag. To enable: update charts/values-private.yaml to set allocator.enabled=true, apply Terraform to provision per-AZ named pools, and upgrade installer controller. Migration steps included in docs/private/egress-migration.md and a canary plan for small clusters. Rollback is handled by controller draining and releasing assignments; Terraform module preserves existing NAT gateways unless explicitly replaced.

Commits (high level):
- 7c1a2d2: add egress allocator controller scaffolding and API types
- 2d9f4a1: implement deterministic AZ affinity algorithm and assignment reconciliation
- a117b8c: terraform: add egress-gateway module with named pool support and EIP rotation policy
- b3f4e22: helm: expose allocator flags, probe endpoints, and metrics
- 49c12f0: privatelink_router controller with tag-driven endpoint lifecycle
- 8d7a901: integration tests for AZ failover and route stability
- 0f4b8c3: docs and migration playbook

Files changed (high-level): Terraform module adds new variables for az_affinity_weight and eip_pool_policy; Helm chart gains allocator.enabled, allocator.metricsPort, and privatelink.routingMode flags; controller adds two new CRDs (EgressGateway, EgressAssignment) and two controllers. Tests include simulated AZ outage harness and assertions on route-table modifications.

Examples and snippets: allocator computes a weighted score for candidate gateways and pins assignments via annotation: "redwood.io/egress-assignment: gateway-az-a-0001". PrivateLink creation is gated by subnet tag and only proceeds if the subnet's route table has the 'egress://managed' tag.

CI and testing: CI ran integration pipeline (ci/pipeline/egress-integration.yml) with creation of 3 simulated AZs; one flaky test (route-flap-detect) initially failed and was retried, subsequent runs passed. Unit tests cover allocator algorithm edge-cases.

Review summary and decisions: After feedback on deterministic tie-breakers and API naming we settled on deterministic assignment tables and kept EgressAssignment as a namespaced CRD rather than cluster-scoped to simplify RBAC. We also chose to make PrivateLink routing opt-in via a subnet tag to avoid surprising customers who manage endpoints externally.

Related work: builds on ENG-7123 (egress cost stabilization) and SRE-314 (private control plane routing hardening).

Merge notes: Squash merge after green pipelines; Terraform module bump requires a follow-on apply in infra to create named pools. Manual verification checklist is included in docs/private/egress-migration.md.
Introduces AZ-aware egress gateway allocator and optional PrivateLink routing per-subnet tag. Backwards compatible defaults; rollout requires terraform plan and operator upgrade. Improves cross-AZ failover stability and reduces NAT cost churn.
Elliot Chen: Please ensure allocator is idempotent across controller restarts; observed a race when multiple controllers reconcile same EgressGateway.
Maya Patel (reply): Added optimistic locking via annotation version and test that tears down/restarts controller; included in allocator_test.go.
Rina Kaur: Can we gate PrivateLink creation behind a feature flag and subnet tag? I don't want implicit endpoint creation.
Maya Patel (reply): PrivateLink creation is gated by both charts.values and 'redwood:privatelink=true' subnet tag per review; updated docs to call this out.
Samir Patel: Terraform change will create named EIP pools — add migration plan so existing NATs are preserved.
Maya Patel (reply): Included migration steps and a non-destructive default that preserves untagged NATs; added a migration playbook in docs.
Elliot Chen (approval): Approving pending one small linter nit fix (done).

Motivation: private control-plane endpoints for on-prem/VPC customers must remain reachable during partial AZ failures and UX should avoid per-customer manual route-table surgery. This PR introduces an AZ-aware PrivateLink proxy (daemon + small control-plane component) and a route-mapper terraform module that automates deterministic ENI/interface-endpoint placement, per-AZ fallback, and safe DNS alias migration. The change touches three areas: terraform modules (new module vpc/controlplane-proxy), Helm chart (installer chart: add control-plane-proxy subchart and RBAC), and the installer migration script (idempotent migration path to convert existing interface endpoints to be fronted by the proxy and switch DNS aliases with TTL-drain). Key goals: 1) Provide graceful AZ failover without modifying customer application routing. 2) Keep endpoint ENI allocation deterministic so security groups can be applied predictably. 3) Enable staged rollout using feature flags and a safe rollback path. Design summary: the proxy runs in each AZ on a small EC2 or light-weight instancegroup and creates a single ENI per AZ that registers behind the interface endpoint via PrivateLink. The route-mapper terraform module ensures one subnet per AZ is used and claims the same ENI IP via a deterministic naming/tagging scheme. Health checks are performed by the proxy and the control plane updates Route53 private DNS aliases to point to healthy AZs with low TTL during migration windows. Compatibility: works with transit gateway and peered VPCs; includes explicit opt-out for customers that prefer direct interface endpoints. Rollout plan: 1) dry-run terraform apply that creates proxy infra but leaves DNS untouched; 2) enable proxy in a canary customer; 3) run migration script to atomically update Route53 aliases during low-traffic window; 4) monitor metrics (latency, 5xxs, endpoint accept-rate) and revert if needed. Rollback: migration script includes a --rollback token that reverts DNS aliases and tears down proxy ENIs created by the module. Security considerations: minimal IAM needed for the proxy to update Route53 aliases within the customer's zone (least privilege policy included), SG hardening template ensures control-plane ports are limited to known mgmt subnets. Testing: unit tests for terraform modules (plan assertions), helm unit tests (chart rendering), end-to-end canary in perf-lab with simulated AZ flaps. Backwards compatibility: existing customers not opting into the new module experience no changes. Documentation: installer README updated with migration steps, and an operator playbook added under docs/migrations/controlplane-proxy.md. Related work: replaces earlier manual endpoint failover runbooks and complements the egress allocator and conditional privatelink work.
Liam Chen: Can we avoid making Route53 changes by default? Suggest dry-run-only behavior unless --apply is passed. (resolved)
Noah Patel: The IAM policy had broader permissions than necessary; reduced to 'route53:ChangeResourceRecordSets' scoped to zone ARN. (updated)
Elena Ruiz: helm values schema needs a 'podDisruptionBudget' entry for the proxy; added and validated. (addressed)
SRE Bot: ci/terraform-plan-assertions failed on first run due to naming collisions in TF state; add explicit name_prefix based on stack and rand suffix. (fixed)
QA: Request to add a smoketest that simulates endpoint failure and asserts client-side reconnects; added perf-lab canary.

Motivation: customers deploying Redwood Private in fully air-gapped datacenters requested a more deterministic bootstrap flow for registries and OS images. Current airgap bundles are large and monolithic which makes incremental updates and signature verification awkward during upgrades. This PR introduces a compact OCI image index format for runtime bundles, and a Terraform module to provision a local mirror + registry-signing step in offline environments. Changes include: 1) a new 'oci-index' manifest generator that emits per-arch component descriptors (runtime images, charts, kernel modules) and an LRU-aware delta manifest pointer for efficient staged upgrades; 2) a Terraform module redwood-terraform/registry-mirror which wires up a local registry, preloads index manifests, and produces a signed admission config used by the installer; 3) Helm chart hooks to verify image signatures using cosign during pre-install, and a lightweight pre-pull controller that validates manifests against the pinned index; 4) installer upgrade/rollback flow updates: atomic manifest pinning with symlinked index bundles and a fast rollback hook that swaps pointer files and triggers a controlled reconcile. This description includes implementation notes, test plan, and rollout strategy. Implementation notes: the oci-index generator is written in Go and produces index.json alongside OCI blobs; each entry includes a semantic component tag (eg runtime:v1.42.0) and a digest pin. The Terraform module supports grabbing index artifacts from an offline bundle, uploading to a local registry, and producing a signed keypair bundle (KMS compatible) for the installer to verify at runtime. The Helm hook runs as a pre-install Job that verifies signatures and pre-pulls images into node-local cache. Testing: unit tests added for index generator, integration tests for the Terraform module using localbin (kind + registry) in CI, and an optional e2e nightly airgapped pipeline that exercises upgrade/rollback. Rollout: feature gated behind installer flag --offline-oci-index and disabled by default; will be exposed to customers as experimental for two releases. Checklist: - [x] OCI index generator (Go) - [x] Terraform registry-mirror module - [x] Helm pre-install signature verification hook - [x] Installer manifest pin/rollback hooks - [x] Unit/integration tests - [x] Docs and upgrade notes Backwards compatibility: existing monolithic bundles are still supported by the installer; when --offline-oci-index is not enabled, bootstrapping behaves exactly as before. Security: cosign is used to verify images; private key material is expected to live in customer KMS and is never uploaded to Redwood systems. Related: Linear ENG-3942 (airgap registry UX), ENG-4037 (upgrade safety).
1) Add oci-index generator and unit tests (A. Chen)
2) Add terraform/registry-mirror module and docs (A. Chen)
3) Add helm pre-install cosign hook and pre-pull controller (D. Martinez)
4) Installer: atomic manifest pointer + rollback strategy (R. Singh)
5) CI: add integration job for registry-mirror (CI Bot)
Unit tests: ./cmd/oci-index tests cover manifest generation and digest pinning.
Integration: terraform apply against local registry (kind) in CI; cosign verification end-to-end in an ephemeral cluster.
E2E: nightly pipeline (optional) performs full bootstrap from oci-index bundle and simulates upgrade + rollback.
Diego Martinez: Nice work on the index format — can we include a small TTL field per component to help garbage collection?
Ava Chen: Added ttl_seconds to descriptors and documented GC behavior in docs/airgap/oci-index.md.
Riya Patel: CI flaked on the integration job the first run (registry timing). Added retries and a wait-for-registry helper to the test harness.
Owen Walker: Suggest adding a document describing key rotation for signed indexes.
Ava Chen: Added a key rotation subsection and example scripts.
Reviewers approved after two iterations.
Ship as experimental in v1.17. Customers opt-in via installer flag. First release will include migration docs for maintainers who want to convert monolithic bundles to OCI index bundles using provided tooling. After stable signal (2 releases, positive customer feedback) flip default to enabled and deprecate monolithic path with a 6-month warning.
Private keys are KMS-managed and only referenced during offline signing; cosign public keys are bundled with the index but validator code verifies trust chain. Installer refuses to boot when signature verification fails. All network touches are local to the customer's network during bootstrap.
Added metrics: installer.offline.index_verification_duration_ms, installer.offline.prepull_images_count, registry_mirror.upload_size_bytes. Dashboards updated in docs/dashboards/offline-index.md.
Introduce experimental OCI index based offline bundles and a Terraform registry-mirror module to streamline air-gapped bootstrapping and staged upgrades. Disabled by default behind --offline-oci-index flag.
This is intentionally conservative in behavioral changes: existing customers are unaffected unless they opt-in. The design aims to reduce bundle churn and to allow small delta updates in highly regulated offline environments.

Motivation: private control plane installs in multi-AZ accounts were intermittently failing during cutover when multiple regions attempted simultaneous subnet handoff and Private Hosted Zone (PHZ) propagation. This PR implements an ordered subnet handshake plus a deterministic private DNS stitching path to avoid race conditions during peering and route propagation. In addition it introduces a small cross-account role-sync helper so peering acceptance and Route53 resolver rules are created in a reproducible order. Design summary: 1) Subnet lifecycle hooks: add a 'handover_sequence' attribute to controlplane_subnet module and a transient lock via DynamoDB to serialize AZ handoff if multiple controlplanes run in parallel. 2) Peering acceptance: add iam role bootstrap and a short-lived S3-backed token to prevent race acceptance across accounts. 3) Private DNS stitching: create explicit resolver rule promotion steps (forwarding -> inbound resolver rule -> conditional PHZ association) with polling and exponential backoff instead of blind parallel associations. 4) Security groups: create an explicit egress-firewall SG that is attached as a managed dependency, and tighten management CIDR on peering ACLs. 5) Helm: small values.yaml change and template to surface the controlplane subnet annotations so downstream installer hooks can observe 'handover_sequence'. Backwards compatibility: all new fields are optional and default to previous semantics (parallel handoff). Existing customers unaffected unless they opt-in. Rollout plan: merge to main, ship as a minor private-installer release, enable ordered handoff via feature flag in 2 pilot customers, monitor resolver association latencies and peering acceptance errors. Rollback: feature flag toggle and reapply old module defaults; explicit cleanup steps included for DynamoDB locks and resolver rules. Testing: unit terraform plan snapshots, integration run in staging with two concurrent installs, end-to-end test asserting no PHZ overlap and route propagation within 3 minutes. Checklist: [x] terraform fmt and validate [x] added unit tests for module logic [x] integration test in staging [x] documented new variables and upgrade notes [x] rollout playbook included
Ethan Liu: Please add a note on IAM key rotation for the short-lived token and ensure it is logged for audit — also include a retrofit guide for existing installs. Author: Added rotation note and included CloudTrail logging for token actions.
Sophie Müller: The DynamoDB table could become a single point of contention; can we multiplex by controlplane_id and add a TTL? Author: multiplexing implemented and TTL set to 1 hour; updated tests.
Jamal Carter: Tighten security group egress to only necessary ports between controlplane and nodes, and add integration test asserting SG rules. Author: tightened rules and added SG assertion to integration test.
Ethan Liu: CI terraform fmt failed on first run. Author: fixed formatting and pushed commit a1d3f6c.
Sophie Müller: Request to add an option to disable ordered handshake for low-latency internal installs. Author: added feature_flag.enabled boolean defaulting to true.
Jamal Carter: Approve after change requests addressed. (Approved)
Ordered subnet handoff and deterministic private DNS stitching to prevent race conditions during controlplane provisioning; optional feature flag 'ordered_handover' (default true); new DynamoDB lock table and short-lived peering token for cross-account acceptance; tighter SG defaults; helm exposes subnet handover annotation; upgrade playbook included.

Context: Private installer deployments have multiple ad-hoc TF modules for GPU nodepool leases, IAM roles and VPC peering created during early iterations. This fragmented layout makes cross-account peering and tfstate operations brittle during upgrades.

Motivation: Consolidate the GPU-lease semantics into a single, tenant-scoped module, centralize IAM scoping rules, and introduce an idempotent VPC peering module plus a tfstate migrator to safely move existing state to the new layout without downtime.

What this PR does: 1) Introduces modules/gpu-reservation (replaces legacy gpu-lease and gpu-subnet-claim modules). The new module exposes an immutable reservation object and a lightweight lease-to-reservation shim for backward compatibility. 2) Adds modules/vpc-peering-idempotent which performs peer creation with edge-case retry handling for cloud API eventual consistency and exposes explicit peering IDs for rollback. 3) Adds tooling/migrator/tfstate-migrator-v2 which: - Performs a dry-run mapping of old resources to new module addresses - Creates a deterministic state rewrite plan (no resource re-creates) - Applies state move operations against a locked remote backend with verification checksums and post-migration validation hooks 4) Tightens IAM role scoping: new roles use tenant-scoped path prefixes and least-privilege polices for nodepool role and peering management. 5) Adds migration docs and a staged rollout checklist.

Rollout plan (short): - Stage 0: Run migrator dry-run in staging and validate resource counts and checksums - Stage 1: Run migrator against staging state, apply new TF, smoke test nodepool creation and GC - Stage 2: Coordinate a rolling migration window for production with customer ops, snapshot state, run migrator, apply TF, monitor.

Backout plan: - If post-migration checks fail, use the migrator snapshot to revert state, or restore backend snapshot and re-apply old TF.

Checklist: - [x] Module refactor and new module tests - [x] Migrator implementation with dry-run - [x] Integration smoke tests (local k8s + mocked cloud) - [x] Docs and runbook - [x] IAM least-privilege validation - [x] Reviewer approvals

Testing notes: ran migrator dry-run on an internal staging tenant (tenant-e2e-03) and validated mapping (10 nodepools -> reservations) and cross-account peering reconciliation.

Observability: added telemetry counters for migrator: dry_run_map_count, moved_resources_count, validation_fail_count.

Risks and mitigation: - Risk: state move mistakes — mitigated by deterministic mapping and checksum/verifier hooks - Risk: peer acceptance race — mitigated by idempotent peering retries and explicit peering-id outputs - Risk: IAM scope regression — mitigated by separate IAM role testing in staging
Consolidates GPU lease/reservation TF module, introduces idempotent VPC peering module and state migrator v2. Updates IAM scoping for tenant-bound GPU roles. Migration tool included for safe in-place tfstate transformation; no runtime API changes expected.
Aditi Mehra: Please add explicit post-migration verification steps for existing node labels — otherwise LGTM.
Evan Chen: Added verification script and assertion in migrator that checks nodecount and label checksum. See tooling/tfstate-migrator-v2/README.md for invocation.
Lena Ortiz: Concern about peering id collision during concurrent migrations. Recommend backoff jitter in peering module.
Evan Chen: Added deterministic collision-resistant ID derivation and exponential backoff; pushed new commit.
Marcus Liu: Ran the staging migrator dry-run and validated output. Approving for merge after CI is green. :+1:
CI: All checks passed. Maintainer (Aditi Mehra) approved and merged via squash.

Motivation: air-gapped on-prem installs for large clusters were taking 60-120+ minutes due to monolithic OCI bundles and registry seeding ordering. This PR introduces a shard-aware bundle layout, a preseed planner Terraform module, and a small controller/cli that performs delta-friendly, parallelized registry seeding and atomic workload apply. Goals: reduce initial bootstrap wall time, make upgrades/rollbacks resilient in flaky networks, and expose per-customer shard selection in Terraform for smaller storage footprints.
1) Add sharded-bundle manifest schema and packer (shard index + component manifests)
2) Implement registry preseed planner Terraform module (modules/registry-preseed) + docs
3) Add rbw-bootstrap CLI (Go) to orchestrate parallel shard sync, verify checksums, and apply Helm charts atomically
4) Helm: make charts idempotent for partial component apply and add readiness probes for staged apply
5) Add e2e harness updates to test slow networks and partial seeds
6) Migrations: update airgap docs and upgrade/rollback playbook
(Each commit atomic and documented in changelog)
Sharded airgap bundles (v1): significantly faster initial registry seeding via parallel shard sync; new Terraform module `registry-preseed` for generating shard manifests and bucket planning; rbw-bootstrap CLI to orchestrate verified, delta-friendly applies and staged Helm deploys. See docs/airgap/sharded-bootstrap.md for migration steps.
Local validation: packed three sample clusters (small/medium/large) and measured bootstrap time improvements: small (35% faster), medium (48% faster), large (62% faster) on simulated 100Mbps constrained link. Performed upgrade dance: partial shard rollback succeeded without cluster-wide downtime in test harness. Added e2e scenario for interrupted preseed and resume behavior.
1) For customers using monolithic bundles: use `rbw-bootstrap pack --convert /path/to/old-bundle` to produce sharded bundles. 2) Run Terraform registry-preseed plan to estimate preseed storage and set `shard_policy` (per-component or balanced). 3) Use `rbw-bootstrap sync --manifest shards/manifest-v1.yaml --parallelism N` to seed registry. 4) Apply helm/airgap with `rbw-bootstrap apply-helm` to ensure staged readiness checks. 5) For upgrades, rely on `--rollback-grace` to keep previous shard images until cutover. Refer to docs/airgap/sharded-bootstrap.md for full playbook.
Signed manifest support added: pack.go emits SHA256 checksums and an optional GPG-signed manifest. rbw-bootstrap verifies signatures before any write operations. Terraform module includes recommended IAM/bucket ACL minimal privileges in README. Added unit tests for signature verification in internal/oci/indexer.
Added metrics to rbw-bootstrap: registry_sync.duration_seconds, registry_sync.shards_total, registry_sync.failed_shards and exported prometheus-friendly labels (cluster_id, shard_id). Helm templates now emit job completion annotations for Console to pick up and display staged apply duration.
v1 sharding assumes components can be separated into independent OCI image sets; some legacy operators that depend on colocated images may need a conversion wrapper. The packer currently targets GCR/OCI registries; ACR/Artifactory tested but requires minor registry URL mapping (documented).
Samir Patel (review): The shard manifest schema looks promising — can we guarantee deterministic ordering for the packer to avoid different index hashes?
Elena (author): Packer now emits a stable component sort (name, then tag) before indexing; added tests in internal/oci/indexer to validate deterministic hashes.
Jiawei (review): Terraform module needs clearer variable names and a way to export planned preseed size for budgeting.
Elena: Added outputs.preseed_bytes and documented the var names; added example tfvars in examples/terraform.
Ruth (requested): e2e flaky under simulated packet loss; please retry CI with longer timeouts.
Elena: Increased timeouts and added jitter to registry sync backoff; CI rerun green.
Post-merge note from release manager (Ruth): remember to bump bundle version in release pipeline and notify SRE to validate customer onprem upgrade window.

Motivation: On large private deployments customers asked for safer, tenant-scoped upgrade and rollback tooling that minimizes blast radius and supports partial rollforward when a single tenant needs a schema correction. This PR introduces a staged backup residency model, tenant-scoped snapshot tagging, a 'dry-apply' schema migration runner, and a pluggable rollforward hook system so operators can apply fixes to a single tenant without a full cluster rollback.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a new backup residency controller to the installer operator. Backups are now marked as 'staged' and optionally kept in a short-term residency store to enable rapid partial restores.
- Adds tenant-scoped snapshot tagging (annotations on S3/GCS/MinIO objects + Terraform state tags) so snapshots can be discovered and restored per-tenant.
- Implements a dry-run path for SQL schema migrations that records the proposed DDL/DDL-order without changing production state. Dry-runs are stored alongside snapshots.
- Introduces rollforward hooks: a lifecycle hook type operators can write to run corrective statements or replay logic against a single-tenant snapshot after restore. Hooks are namespaced per-tenant and executed in a sandboxed transaction by default.
- Helm chart and Terraform updates to expose residency TTL, snapshot retention policies, and enable per-tenant annotations during install/upgrade.

Checklist: 
- [x] Backup residency controller + CRD and controller unit tests
- [x] Snapshot tagging + Terraform state patch and tests
- [x] Dry-run migration runner and storage format compatibility tests
- [x] Rollforward hook API + executor and e2e test harness
- [x] Helm chart values and example override for on-prem installs
- [x] Documentation draft included in installer README and examples

Related Linear/Jira: ENG-2314, ENG-2387, PM-402

Commit summary: 
- 1f4b3e0 add CRD stagedbackup, controller scaffolding and basic reconcile loop
- 2b9d12a implement residency store interface and minio adapter + unit tests
- 3c7a9d1 tenant-tagging: annotate snapshots and terraform state outputs
- 4d5a2f4 add migration dry-run runner and record writer for dry manifests
- 5e6b7c2 rollforward hook API + executor + sandbox transaction wrapper
- 6a8f0b1 helm: expose residency.ttl, snapshotRetention and tenantAnnotation values
- 7c3d9e4 examples: add tenant-restore-playbook and a sample dry-run manifest

Files changed (high level):
- installer/operator/api/v1/stagedbackup_types.go
- installer/operator/controllers/stagedbackup_controller.go
- installer/operator/controllers/residencystore/minio_adapter.go
- installer/terraform/modules/state/output_tags.tf
- installer/migrations/dryrunner/runner.go
- installer/migrations/dryrunner/record_writer.go
- installer/rollforward/executor.go
- helm-charts/redwood-private/values.yaml
- helm-charts/redwood-private/templates/backup-residency.yaml
- examples/private/tenant-restore-playbook.md

Testing notes: 
- Unit test coverage added for controller reconcile paths and minio adapter.
- Integration job in CI spins up a local MinIO + Postgres and runs an end-to-end tenant restore + rollforward using the example playbook. The e2e runs are marked as long and gated behind the 'e2e-long' job.

CI status: Initial run: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, e2e-long: fail (flaky network in MinIO container); rerun: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, e2e-long: pass. Lint warnings addressed in follow-up commit.

Deployment/upgrade notes: The stagedbackup CRD is opt-in by default; existing installs will not change behavior unless residency is enabled via helm values or Terraform parameter. There is a migration path that converts existing snapshot archives to tagged snapshots using a migration job (included). Operators should plan for a short maintenance window when enabling residency for the first time for large archives.

Security considerations: Rollforward hooks execute SQL against tenant schemas. Hooks run in a sandboxed transaction and are limited by role-based DB access granted by the operator. The hook executor also signs manifests to avoid replay attacks. See docs section for recommended RBAC and KMS key policies.

Why this is different from prior work: Existing PRs added generic backup/restore and rollback guards; this PR focuses on minimizing blast radius by enabling tenant-level restores, keeping short-term staged snapshots for rapid recovery, and providing a controlled rollforward mechanism so fixes can be applied without cluster-wide downgrades or full rewinds.

Notes for reviewer: The residency store interface is intentionally minimal so it can be implemented for different object stores; prefer reviewing the interface contract and the minio adapter unit tests first. The dry-run migration format must be compatible with our eval tooling; double-check the JSON manifest schema in installer/migrations/dryrunner/record_writer.go.

Reviewer: Diego Morales: 'Would prefer the default TTL to be conservative (7d) and require explicit override for shorter retention; otherwise we risk S3 costs.'
Author: Aisha Patel: 'Agreed; default TTL set to 7d in values.yaml. We added helm chart comment to call out cost tradeoffs.'
Reviewer: Claire Hsu: 'Can we ensure rollforward hooks never run outside a transaction? We shouldn't allow partial commits.'
Author: Aisha Patel: 'Hook executor now wraps hooks in a sandboxed transaction; added unit test to validate rollback on error.'
Reviewer: Jonah Klein: 'Dry-run format looks good but ensure compat with eval harness schema v2.'
Author: Aisha Patel: 'Updated record_writer to include schemaVersion and added conversion helper.

payload.body:
Motivation: Private control plane provisioning often requires tight CIDR coordination between multiple tenants and existing customer VPCs. Manual allocation leads to collisions and slowdowns during onboarding. We need an idempotent, deterministic allocation strategy and safer lifecycle for endpoint credentials that works in air-gapped / VPC-only environments.

What this PR does: Implements a hash-based subnet reservation allocator and an automated endpoint credential rotation controller for private control plane endpoints. Adds preflight validation, DNS priming with split-horizon awareness, and an operational runbook for safe rollout and rollback. Targets Terraform/Helm paths used by the private installer.

Key features: * Deterministic subnet allocator: computes a stable CIDR block per tenant+AZ using a configurable hash seed. Allocations are idempotent and representable in Terraform state so they can be reconciled without drift. * Overlap safety: optional "existing_cidrs" input causes plan to fail-fast if computed block collides with customer ranges. * Reservation record: allocator writes a reservation tag/record into a designated DynamoDB/Terraform state key so multiple runs converge. * Endpoint credential rotation: a Helm cronjob controller rotates TLS/credential secrets for private controlplane endpoints; integrates with KMS for customer-provided or installer-managed keys. * DNS priming: before publishing endpoints, performs Route53 ownership checks, split-horizon detection, TTL tuning and exponential retry backoff. * Preflight checks: network adjacency, cross-account peering readiness, and IAM/KMS permissions verification. * Runbook and rollback: explicit steps to revert allocations, revoke rotated credentials, and re-prime DNS.

Checklist (high level):
- [x] Terraform allocator module with unit tests
- [x] Helm chart changes (endpoint rotation) and chart tests
- [x] Installer controller wiring and preflight checks
- [x] DNS priming logic with split-horizon handling
- [x] Documentation: ops runbook and playbook
- [x] End-to-end integration test against a minimal AWS account

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature flag (enabled=false)
2) Deploy to canary with feature flag on for a single tenant in staging; observe allocations and DNS priming logs for 48h
3) Enable endpoint rotation for non-prod clusters and validate credential TTLs and KMS usage
4) Gradually enable for additional tenants and environments

Rollback plan:
- Disable feature flag; the allocator will no longer claim new blocks. Existing allocations remain in state and can be rotated back by running the provided revert script.
- The endpoint rotation controller supports a one-shot rollback where last valid credentials are re-inserted; instructions in docs/ops/endpoint_rotation_playbook.md.

Testing: Unit tests for allocator permutations and overlap detection included. Integration test runs against a sandbox account that exercises the DynamoDB reservation record, Route53 priming, and a bare-metal-like private control plane (no public endpoints). CI: terraform fmt/lint, helm lint, unit tests, and an integration matrix on staging were green.

Security considerations: Rotation uses KMS; pattern allows either customer-provided KMS key ARN (recommended for enterprise) or installer-managed key with a 90-day rotation window. Secrets are stored in the cluster secret store and only exposed to the controlplane pods. IAM policies required are documented and gated by preflight.

Related work: Builds on ENG-4821 (subnet reconciliation) and ENG-5042 (endpoint lifecycle).

Notes for reviewers: focus on allocator idempotency and Terraform state interaction, and on the worst-case rollback for endpoint rotations. Logs for DNS priming are verbose by design (helps investigate split-horizon), but we can reduce level after validation.
Arjun Patel: Can we guarantee no CIDR overlap across existing non-redwood subnets? Please add a safety check in allocator.tf.
Maya Singh: Allocator includes an optional existing_cidrs input and will fail-fast with explicit message. Added unit tests to cover overlap scenarios.
Leah McCarthy: Endpoint rotation looks good; ensure the KMS key ARN can be provided by private installer users.
Maya Singh: Exposed kms_key_arn in values.yaml and added fallback to installer-managed key with rotation window.
Sofia Rios: DNS priming needs to handle split-horizon where private zones exist; add TTL tuning and retry backoff.
Maya Singh: Added exponential backoff and a fast-path when Route53 zone already delegated. Updated docs with troubleshooting steps.
Introduces a deterministic hash-based subnet reservation mechanism to minimize manual CIDR coordination, adds an automated endpoint credential rotation controller (KMS-integrated) for private control plane endpoints, and improves DNS priming with split-horizon awareness. Includes preflight checks and rollback/runbook.

Context: Private control plane upgrades previously applied endpoint and security-group changes in-place, which caused transient connectivity issues during canary rollouts. This PR introduces an upgrade-safe endpoint reconciler that performs staged changes and a preflight runner that provisions ephemeral security groups and validates connectivity/policy before any destructive changes are applied.
Motivation: reduce blast radius during Private installer upgrades; give operators a fast, deterministic preflight that mirrors production routing and DNS behavior.
Summary of changes: 1) Terraform: add 'ephemeral_sg' optional resource set and a deterministic 'subnet_affinity' module flag that, when enabled, allocates az-subnet claims the same way during plan and apply to avoid drift. 2) Installer controller: add EndpointReconciler v2 (idempotent, adopts existing endpoints, supports staged replace + fallback) and an EphemeralPreflightRunner that creates ephemeral SGs and test endpoints in a temp namespace. 3) Helm chart: expose new values (preflight.enabled, preflight.timeout, reconciler.stage_window_ms) and add RBAC rules for the preflight runner. 4) DNS: introduce a 'preflight-ttl' path for Route53/Consul tests and a conditional 'dns-stitcher' fallback used only during staging to avoid full-record flips. 5) Tests & tooling: e2e test harness that runs the preflight flow in CI (k8s-integration job), plus a small CLI helper (installer ctl preflight run) to trigger the same flow locally.
Design notes: - Reconciler is optimistic: it attempts server-side minimal PATCH, then if it detects incompatible changes (CIDR or service owner diff) it creates replacement endpoints and keeps the old ones until traffic drain completes. - Preflight runner uses ephemeral security groups that are tagged with installer:preflight=<run-id>; those SGs are short-lived and automatically garbage-collected on success/failure. - Rollback plan: if preflight fails, the reconciler aborts the staged rollout and annotates the control-plane resource with the failure reason; operator can run 'installer ctl preflight report <run-id>' to inspect logs and decisions. - Safety: all ephemeral resources are created in a customer-owned, nonce-scoped namespace and require a new IAM permission (ec2:CreateTags + ec2:DeleteSecurityGroup) documented in README.
Checklist: - [x] Terraform resources and variables added and documented - [x] Helm values and RBAC updates - [x] EndpointReconciler implementation and unit tests - [x] EphemeralPreflightRunner + e2e tests - [x] CLI hook for local preflight runs - [x] Docs and upgrade notes - [x] Linear ticket(s) updated
Testing done: - Unit tests for reconciler state machine and preflight runner (local) - Integration tests in CI (k8s-integration) exercising preflight against a mini-cluster (mocked Route53/Consul) - Manual canary run against an internal staging VPC (screenshot logs attached in PR comment)
Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag 'reconciler_v2_enabled' on the installer; default false for 1 week, flip for internal accounts, monitor SLOs and route53 delta metrics. Related: builds on work in ENG-6882 (subnet affinity) and addresses incidents flagged by SUP-2241.
Release notes: "Introduce an upgrade-safe EndpointReconciler and a preflight runner that uses ephemeral security groups to validate endpoint and DNS changes before they are applied to production. Operators should enable reconciler_v2_enabled behind a staged rollout."
CI notes: k8s-integration job uses an experimental cluster with mocked DNS; full-cloud integration was run manually and validated in staging.
Arjun Patel: Overall this looks good. A few safety questions: how do we ensure the ephemeral SGs cannot be used as a backdoor? Please show tag scoping and a TTL GC mechanism.
Sylvia Cho: Added tag scoping (installer:preflight=<run-id>, customer-id) and a GC controller that deletes SGs older than preflight.gc_ttl (default 2h). Tests added in runner_integration_test.go.
Marta Ruiz: Tests are solid, but I want a clearer error path for 'partial failure' (some AZs succeed, others fail). Can we make reconciler annotate per-az and surface that in the CLI?
Sylvia Cho: Reconciler now writes annotations reconciler.preflight.az.<az>=<ok|fail> and CLI report shows per-az statuses. Updated tests and docs.
Liam O'Connor: Security review: IAM change acceptable but needs a note in upgrade docs for enterprises without ec2:DeleteSecurityGroup — added fallback instructions to use maintain_existing_sg flag.
Arjun Patel: Approving after small nits fixed (typo in docs).
Marta Ruiz: Approved.
Introduce an upgrade-safe EndpointReconciler (v2) that stages endpoint replacements to avoid downtime during Private installer upgrades. Adds an Ephemeral Preflight Runner that provisions ephemeral security groups and validates endpoint + DNS changes before production application. Feature is behind reconciler_v2_enabled and requires additional IAM tags/permissions. See docs/private-installer/upgrade-safety.md for migration and rollback steps.
