payload.body:
Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private on constrained on-prem clusters frequently use lightweight Kubernetes distributions such as k3s and RKE2. These distros have different defaults for container runtimes (containerd, crio) and simplified kubelet/systemd layouts that can break the existing online-first installer and airgap bundle. This PR produces a minimal, vendored airgap bundle targeted at k3s/rke2 and updates the installer logic to detect distro quirks and apply compatible manifests.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds an airgap bundle variant: bundles/k3s-rke2-v1.26.tar.gz containing pre-pulled OCI image tarballs (controller, runtime, sidecars, cri-tools), curated Helm charts, and a manifest overlay directory with distro-specific tweaks.
- New helper: installer/scripts/generate-airgap-bundle.sh to build the tarball from a lockfile (images.lock) and output sha256 checksums for offline verification.
- Installer changes: installer/airgap/install.sh gained a --distro hint (k3s|rke2|generic) and automatic container runtime detection; it will load OCI tarballs into containerd and adjust systemd service overrides for k3s/rke2 where necessary.
- Helm chart patches: charts/redwood/values-airgap.yaml and small template conditionals to defer certain initContainers that assume Docker or cloud metadata.
- Terraform module tweak: terraform/modules/private_network/main.tf adds an optional nat_gateway boolean used when doing hub-and-spoke airgapped bootstrapping (helps in staging-by-proxy flows).
- Upgrade/rollback: installer/airgap/upgrade-hook.yaml adds a preflight hook that snapshots current manifests and a rollback.sh script that can be run locally to re-apply saved manifests and image states.
- Docs: docs/airgap-k3s-rke2.md with step-by-step airgapped install and verification checks.

Checklist: 
- [x] Bundle generation script + lockfile support
- [x] Container runtime loading and verification
- [x] Helm conditional compatible with k3s/rke2
- [x] Upgrade snapshot + rollback helper
- [x] Basic e2e on k3s (v1.26) and RKE2 (v1.26) clusters
- [x] Documentation and example commands

Testing performed:
- Local k3s (v1.26) lab: generated bundle, transferred to an airgapped node, ran install.sh --airgap --distro k3s. Verified all pods came up and KV cache backend connected.
- RKE2 cluster in isolated VLAN: exercised image import (ctr images import), systemd override applied for container runtime, performed an in-place upgrade of the controller and used rollback.sh to revert to previous manifest set.
- CI: installer unit tests + shellcheck + minimal integration job; initial pipeline had a transient network flake when pushing a test artifact to internal registry and was re-run manually. Final state: passing.

Backward compatibility and upgrade notes:
- Default airgap bundle is opt-in. Existing online installer behavior is unchanged unless --airgap is provided.
- The installer will fallback to "generic" mode when distro detection is ambiguous; generic behavior preserves current semantics.
- Rollback is not automatic for every failure; the preflight snapshot is required for rollback.sh to succeed. We document limitations in the new docs page.

Known limitations / follow-ups:
- We only vendor images for the minimal runtime set; some optional addons are still downloaded at install time if not present in the bundle. Plan: add an optional full-bundle in ENG-1902.
- RKE2 with CRI-O variants were tested in smoke only; additional CI coverage planned.
- We currently support k3s/rke2 for v1.26 only; future PR will expand matrix.

Context & links: Linear ENG-1847 (airgap experience), ENG-1902 (bundle sizing), support ticket SUP-322 documenting a customer incident where k3s nodes failed to load images.

Example commands (illustrative):
- Generate bundle: ./installer/scripts/generate-airgap-bundle.sh --lock images.lock --output bundles/k3s-rke2-v1.26.tar.gz
- Install in airgap: scp bundles/k3s-rke2-v1.26.tar.gz installer-node:/tmp && sudo ./installer/airgap/install.sh --bundle /tmp/k3s-rke2-v1.26.tar.gz --distro k3s
- Rollback: sudo ./installer/airgap/rollback.sh --snapshot /var/lib/redwood/snapshots/2025-11-26

Please read docs/airgap-k3s-rke2.md for full operational guidance and troubleshooting steps.
Adds a focused airgap bundle and installer adjustments to support k3s and RKE2 clusters in on-prem/air-gapped environments. Includes vendored OCI image tarballs, distro-specific systemd overrides, Helm chart tweaks, and a rollback hook for upgrades.
Diego Ramos: Left a couple of nit comments about error messages; also suggested a more robust retry around ctr image import (handled by adding exponential backoff).
Priya Nair: Asked to document how to verify image checksum after loading; updated generate-airgap-bundle.sh to output checksums and added verification section to docs.
Ben Holloway: Approved after confirming the rollback snapshot flow on his local RKE2 cluster; noted an idea to add a dry-run --verify flag in a follow-up (ENG-1902).
Avery Cho (author): Responded to comments and pushed a follow-up commit that adds retry/backoff and checksum output. Thanks for the reviews — addressed all nits and confirmed CI green.
This is intentionally conservative: the bundle is targeted and small to keep customer transfer times reasonable. Operations requested we keep checksum and provenance info next to bundles for audit. We plan to follow up with an automated package signer (ENG-1975).

payload.body:
Motivation: past upgrades surfaced brittle imperative init jobs and tightly coupled Helm hooks that made tenant bootstrap ordering difficult to reason about in air-gapped/on-prem installs. This change introduces a lightweight declarative InitPhase operator CRD plus Helm template helpers and a values shim that produce tenant-scoped connector seed manifests and sequenced hook resources. The goal is to decouple sequencing intent from imperative job orchestration so installs and upgrades are more auditable and resumable.

What this PR does (single-line narrative): adds an InitPhase CRD and controller-friendly annotation conventions, extends helm templates with 'initPhase' helper functions, supplies a values translation shim (values.v1beta->values.v1alpha) for backwards compatibility, and wires the installer charts to emit phase-scoped seed manifests instead of inlined init Jobs for connectors.

Key changes and rationale: - InitPhase CRD: a small CRD that declares ordered phases, optional timeout, and capacity hints. Operators or the private-installer can act on these phases rather than relying on Helm hook ordering. This reduces failure modes during partial upgrades and allows external controllers to resume work when Helm aborts. - Helm helper templates: new templates/chart_helpers/init_phase.tpl and templates/tenant-seed-phase.yaml.tpl that render Phase objects and connector seed manifests scoped to a tenant. These helpers accept values.* v2-style phase definitions and retain compatibility with legacy initJobs via the shim. - Values shim: values/translate_v1beta_to_v1alpha.go (generator) and a helm values example values/tenant-init-phases.example.yaml. The shim converts common legacy initJobs blocks into the declarative phases at chart render time for existing customers. - Templating changes avoid large inline job manifests; seed manifests are generated as separate files under templates/seed-manifests/ so we can apply them via the InitPhase operator or keep older behaviour when the feature flag is disabled. - Canary rollout support: a feature gate values.privateInstaller.enableInitOperator (false by default). When enabled, chart emits InitPhase objects; when disabled it falls back to legacy init Jobs. This allows staged rollouts per-tenant.

Checklist: - [x] CRD schema and OpenAPI v3 validation added - [x] Helm helpers with unit tests - [x] Values shim CLI check (generator tested locally) - [x] E2E in k3s harness for 2 tenants (canary + default) - [x] Migration docs and upgrade notes included - [x] CI green after fixups

Motivation: Private upgrades suffer from restore mismatches, interrupted applies, and schema regressions that surface only after roll-forward. This PR adds a small, opt-in orchestration layer (migration-orchestrator) to reduce human error and make rollbacks observable. It combines three core mitigations: immutable backup manifest headers stored with snapshots, Linear ticket annotations on every migration step for traceability, and a rollback dry-run shim that simulates revert paths (terraform plan + Helm dry-run with preflight hooks) to detect blockers before executing a real rollback.

What changed: Introduces a CLI binary (installer/bin/migrator) and operator controller hooks that sequence: backup verification, schema compatibility checks, staged terraform apply, canary quiesce, and optionally a rollback simulation. Key features: (1) Immutable manifest headers (backup-id, source-cluster, schema-version, sha256) are written alongside snapshot objects in S3/GCS and validated prior to restore to avoid cross-cluster restores. (2) Linear-trace: each migration step embeds a Linear key in logs and migration records so audits and support can correlate run artifacts to the originating ticket. (3) Rollback dry-run shim: new command runs terraform plan against the target rollback state using the last-known manifest and executes Helm dry-run with our migration hooks to reveal ordering, schema, and hook failures that would otherwise be discovered only while mutating live state. The shim also enforces a downgrade guard: automated downgrades are blocked when schema_compat reports regressions unless explicitly acknowledged with a flag.

Compatibility and safety: Migrator is gated by an operator feature flag; default installer behavior is unchanged. Backups created by older installers remain visible but restore will be blocked if the manifest header is absent unless the operator passes --force-legacy with an explicit reason. The rollback guard defaults to on for private deployments to prioritize safety.

Testing: Added e2e tests under test/e2e/migrator that run a staged migration and a simulated rollback using localkind clusters and mocked storage providers. CI added an integration matrix that runs: bootstrap, backup/verify, terraform-plan (rollback shim), and helm-dryrun stages.

Operational: New telemetry metrics introduced: migrator_run_total, migrator_failures_by_stage, backup_manifest_mismatch_count. Documentation: docs/upgrade-playbook.md updated with an enablement checklist, runbook steps, and examples for staged restores and rollback rehearsals.

Related linear tickets: ENG-4721 (migration auditability), ENG-4875 (rollback dry-run automation).
Diego Alvarez: Nice work — I like the manifest headers. A few questions: how do we rotate manifests for long retention buckets?
Maya Thompson: We add a generation timestamp and rely on lifecycle rules; migrator ignores manifests older than max_generation_age to avoid accidental restores from stale snapshots.
Priya Kapoor: Schema validator looks solid. Can the downgrade guard be default-on? We should err on the side of safety for private installs.
Maya Thompson: Agreed. Switched the guard to default-on and added a --allow-downgrade advanced flag. Tests updated.
Samir Choudhury: CI flagged a hook naming collision with existing Helm hooks; please rename to quiesce-migrator-prehook.
Maya Thompson: Renamed the hook, pushed fix, and reran CI. Lint and helm tests now pass.
Diego Alvarez: Approve after green CI.
- Adds migration-orchestrator CLI to sequence backup verification, schema checks, staged applies, and rollback dry-run.
- Writes immutable backup manifest headers (backup-id, sha256, schema-version) with snapshots to reduce restore mistakes.
- Adds rollback dry-run shim using terraform plan + helm dry-run to surface rollback blockers.
- Adds Linear trace annotations for auditability and new migrator telemetry metrics.
This change is intentionally conservative: migrator is opt-in and does not change existing restore semantics unless enabled. Operators should rehearse rollback-dry-run in staging with representative snapshots before enabling in production. Enterprise customers get an enablement checklist in the docs.

Motivation: Private deployments require repeated, safe onboarding of tenant control-plane components without exposing long-lived credentials. This PR adds a credentialless tenant bootstrap operator that performs ephemeral workload identity exchanges (K8s ServiceAccount token + short-lived bootstrap grants) and an accompanying Helm preflight policy-check step that verifies RBAC templates, policy bundles, and required KMS secrets before applying charts. The goal is to reduce manual steps for customers using the private installer (VPC/on-prem) and to make automated upgrades and rollback safer. Summary of changes (high level): - New controller: installer/boot/credentialless-operator (scaffold, controllers, admission helpers) - Helm preflight check: helm/preflight/policy-checker (validates policy bundles, checks required KMS/HSM keys, and cross-checks tenant isolation constraints) - Terraform: modules/tenant_bootstrap enhancements to support bootstrap tokens and conditional outputs for air-gapped flows - Helm charts: charts/private/values.schema.yaml and charts/private/templates/rbac-helpers.yaml updated to consume ephemeral grants - Rollback playbook: playbooks/rollback/tenant-rbac-rollback.md with stepwise rollback & verification steps - Docs: docs/private/bootstrapping.md and quickstart snippets added - Tests: tests/integration/bootstrap_e2e.sh and unit tests for operator reconciliation Why this approach: Using a short-lived bootstrap grant mitigates the need to ship secrets in configmaps or store long-lived service principal keys in TF state. The preflight policy checks prevent failed installs due to missing KMS keys or mis-scoped RBAC templates. Checklist: - [x] Operator scaffold and controller reconciliation loop - [x] Helm preflight checker and schema validation - [x] Terraform module changes and backward-compatible outputs - [x] Playbook and docs updated - [x] Integration tests and smoke tests - [x] Security review and threat model notes Related work: ENG-4213 (tenant bootstrap redesign), ENG-4298 (helm preflight architecture), SUP-214 (support case: failed private installs due to missing KMS keys). Migration notes: Existing installs will continue to work; new installs can opt into credentialless mode via values.privateInstaller.bootstrap.mode=credentialless. There is an optional migration helper that emits a one-time ephemeral grant and updates TF outputs; it is documented in docs/private/bootstrapping.md.
Adds credentialless tenant bootstrap operator + Helm preflight policy checks to improve private installer idempotency and reduce manual RBAC steps for air-gapped/private deployments. Includes Terraform module updates and a rollback playbook.

Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private in stateful, multi-AZ datacenters asked for an automated, testable, and reversible failover path that preserves KV cache and data-plane state during evacuations and region-level maintenance. This PR introduces the "stateful-failover-orchestrator": an orchestration layer plus playbooks-as-code that coordinate safe evacuations, snapshot-and-drain steps, and an automated rollback path for failed switchovers.

Summary of changes: adds a lightweight controller and a set of opinionated runbooks implemented as Ansible playbooks and Terraform/Helm orchestration glue. The design favors explicit, idempotent steps: quiesce inbound traffic, snapshot PVs and object-store checkpoints, drain inference nodes while preserving KV cache checkpoints, promote standby replicas, validate model checksum and runtime state, then flip traffic via the load-balancer with a staged canary. If any validation fails we run the safe-rollback sequence that replays checkpoints to the original cluster and resumes traffic.

Key features: automated snapshot hooks (PVC and object-store), drain with KV-cache flush and delta snapshots, staged canary traffic switch, health gating (latency/cost/quality metrics), rollback-as-code (replay checkpoints + rehydrate caches), and integrated runbook templates for on-call. All runbooks are parametric (region, cluster, model-tag) to support private VPC and on-prem variants.

Why this is different: existing DR assets were manual runbooks and scattered scripts. This PR consolidates them into executable playbooks and tight Helm/Terraform semantics so rehearsals and audits are reproducible, and post-mortem traces map cleanly to the automation steps.

Testing performed: unit tests for the orchestrator controller and helm templates; terraform validate on all modules; a 3-node multi-AZ rehearsal in our lab (simulated AZ failure) exercising snapshot, drain, promote, and rollback flows; integration tests exercised the canary gating logic and verified KV-cache rehydration within latency SLOs.

Operational notes: adds a new ServiceAccount with restricted RBAC for the orchestrator, and a new optional helm value family (orchestrator.enabled, orchestrator.runbookPath, orchestrator.canary.percent). The terraform module exposes variables for snapshot retention and snapshot-schedule. There is a migration helper script to convert existing manual runbooks into the parametric playbook format.

Rollback plan: the PR includes a documented, automated rollback step that is invoked by the orchestrator on failed validations. Human approval gates are optional by default but can be required via a helm value for stricter escalation paths.

Docs & runbooks: added a /docs/dr-automation.md guide and an operational playbook at installer/ansible/dr-runbooks/stateful-failover.yml. Also updated the README and the upgrade checklist for Private deployments.

Checklist: [x] Terraform modules added/validated [x] Helm templates linted [x] Ansible playbooks written and tested [x] Integration rehearsal completed [x] Runbook documentation committed

Related: ENG-4821 (DR orchestration prototype) and OPS-327 (on-call failover runbook).

Sofia Nguyen: Moved canary.timeout to top-level and added docs note.

Sofia Nguyen: Added pre-warm hook and made it opt-in via orchestrator.prewarm.enabled=false by default.
Introduces 'Stateful Failover Orchestrator' for Private deployments: executable runbooks, snapshot & drain automation, canary traffic gating, and rollback-as-code. Operators should review RBAC changes and the new helm values under charts/private-installer. No breaking changes to existing installs unless orchestrator.enabled is turned on.

Motivation: Upgrades for private deployments (VPC/on-prem) require predictable, auditable state transitions and a low-risk path to roll back when migrations touch DB schemas or object-store layouts. This PR adds two orthogonal safety primitives: 1) migration-preview mode — a dry-run path that validates planned migration actions (DB DDL/DML, helm chart template diffs, terraform plan artifacts, and file-store transforms) against a snapshot of the cluster and returns a deterministic report; 2) safe-commit hook — an idempotent final-state checkpoint written at the end of a successful install/upgrade that records applied migrations, checksumed manifests, and a compact failure-containment plan so rollbacks can pick up cleanly. Summary of changes: - installer/cli: new `--migration-preview` flag; preview writes a human-readable report and machine-friendly artifact to <artifacts>/migration-preview/<run-id>. - installer/hooks: implement `safe-commit` hook executed only when `--safe-commit=true` and the run completed successfully. The hook writes final-state.json and a signed lockfile to the configured artifacts backend (S3/GCS/MinIO). - helm/redwood-core: chart hook annotations to gate post-upgrade finalization, avoid Helm completing release until safe-commit artifact persisted. - terraform/modules: add `migration_plan_output` optional output and a `plan_checksum` export; wiring plumbed to the installer so preview compares planned vs applied. - db/migrations: add schema-compatibility checker (non-destructive compatibility ruleset) that runs during preview and actual run; it prevents downgrade-only-unsafe operations unless explicitly allowed by `--allow-destructive`. - upgrade-playbooks: document a rollback sequence that uses final-state.json to produce a restore playbook and automated sanity checks. Design details: - Preview semantics: preview runs all code paths except executing destructive DDL/DML and object-store movers; instead it simulates them using a mutable snapshot in a temp namespace or a locally mounted copy. It records the exact set of files/SQL statements/k8s manifests that would be applied and computes a deterministic checksum for each artefact. - Safe-commit semantics: safe-commit writes {run_id, timestamp, base_branch, head_commit, migration_checksums[], terraform_plan_checksum, helm_chart_checksum, validation_summary, rollback_hint} plus a cryptographic HMAC when KMS key present. The hook is resilient: retries with backoff, and on repeated failure marks release as `finalization_failed` with instructions for manual salvage. - Rollback/restore: a new script `installer/bin/restore-from-final-state` reconstructs a minimal cluster snapshot and runs the inverse actions for non-destructive rollbacks; for destructive changes it emits a guided manual path. Testing performed: - Unit tests for schema checker rules (db/migrations/test_schema_checker.py). - Integration tests using KIND + MinIO to exercise preview and commit (test_migration_preview_e2e.sh). - Manual dry-runs against customer-like manifests (two internal lab clusters). - CI: added a matrix job (preview, safe-commit) that runs the simulated path and validates artifacts are produced. Backwards/compatibility notes: - Default behavior is unchanged; both migration-preview and safe-commit are opt-in flags. - Safe-commit artifacts are compact JSON + gzip; we provide a migration tool to import legacy backups when present. Rollout plan: - Stage feature behind feature-flag in release channel A for 2 weeks; invite early-adopter customers for Private channel testing. - After no critical issues, flip to default-available (not enabled) in the console and add to upgrade checklist. Related: Linear ENG-4123 (migration preview), ENG-4199 (safe commit hooks). Links: internal design doc: /docs/private/upgrade-safety/migration-preview.md. Full implementation here includes small Helm chart updates and Terraform outputs to carry checksums. See changed_files for specifics.

Summary: This PR adds a first-class backup orchestration phase to the Private upgrade workflow. The installer now runs a pre-upgrade backup step that can (a) create volume snapshots via pluggable snapshotters (initial support: Kubernetes CSI VolumeSnapshot and AWS EBS snapshots via CSI annotations) and/or (b) perform an optional logical DB backup (pg_dump) when snapshots are unavailable or when operators request an additional safety net. The orchestrator emits structured progress events (for CLI + future UI) and persists backup metadata into the upgrade state store so rollback and support bundles can reference what happened. Motivation: We’ve had multiple upgrade incidents/near-misses where rollback was risky because there was no deterministic backup step or because snapshot behaviors differed across environments. This change makes upgrades safe-by-default and reduces operator guesswork, aligning with ENG-4838 and the broader “Private upgrade + rollback mechanism” project. Design/behavior: 1) New phase in plan execution: pre_upgrade_backup runs after prechecks and before any control-plane schema migrations or chart changes. 2) Backup strategies: SnapshotBackup (preferred) creates snapshots for PVCs selected by label/allowlist (db, control-plane state, queue/cache if configured). Uses CSI VolumeSnapshot API if supported; falls back to an AWS EBS snapshot flow when running on EKS with the EBS CSI driver (detected via StorageClass provisioner + PV topology). LogicalBackup (optional) runs a job in-cluster to produce a compressed pg_dump stored to a configured object store endpoint or a local path in on-prem mode. The logical backup is explicitly opt-in (--backup.logical.enabled) and requires credentials/target to be present. 3) Encryption and access: The orchestrator enforces encryption expectations when possible (e.g., checks StorageClass parameters / snapshot class annotations). For logical backup targets, it validates that the destination is configured for server-side encryption when supported (S3 SSE-S3/SSE-KMS) and warns otherwise (non-blocking). 4) Progress reporting: Standardized events are emitted for start/progress/complete/failure with stable step IDs. CLI prints a compact progress view; verbose mode includes per-volume timing and snapshot IDs. 5) Failure handling: Backup failures are blocking by default (upgrade aborts before any mutations). Partial snapshot creation is treated as failure; the output includes the created snapshot IDs to help cleanup. A --backup.continue-on-failure flag exists for break-glass situations (hidden; requires confirmation prompt). 6) Auditability: The upgrade state store now records backup artifacts (snapshot IDs, VolumeSnapshot names, logical backup URI, timestamps, duration, and validation status). This is used by future rollback commands and included in support bundles (ENG-4899 follow-up will wire the bundle). Operator UX: New installer flags: --backup.enabled (default true for upgrade), --backup.strategy=snapshot|logical|snapshot+logical, --backup.snapshot.pvcSelector (label selector), --backup.logical.enabled, --backup.logical.destination (s3://… or file:///…), --backup.timeout, --backup.continue-on-failure (hidden). New commands: redwood-private upgrade plan now includes a Backup stage when enabled; redwood-private upgrade run prints a Backup section with progress. Notably, this PR does not implement restore; restore/rollback hooks will consume the recorded artifacts (ENG-4844 / PR-4862). Testing: Adds unit tests for snapshot selection, CSI capability detection, and state persistence. Adds an integration test job in CI that runs a mocked snapshotter and verifies that upgrade plan execution halts on backup failure. Limitations: On-prem snapshot support depends on the cluster’s CSI driver exposing VolumeSnapshot. If VolumeSnapshot CRDs are missing, snapshot backups will fail with a clear remediation message (install snapshot-controller + CRDs) and operators can choose logical backups instead. Logical backup currently supports Postgres only (our control-plane DB). Follow-ups: (1) Add restore hooks + verification checks for snapshots and logical backups (ENG-4838). (2) Support additional snapshot backends and explicit SnapshotClass selection (requested by design partners). (3) Wire backup metadata into support bundle and audit log events (ENG-4899 + redwood monorepo PR for audit logging).
Adds installer-managed backups for Private upgrades: pre-upgrade snapshot hooks (CSI/EBS) and optional logical DB backups with progress reporting. Persists backup metadata into upgrade state for auditability and rollback workflows. Improves failure handling with clear remediation output and a safe abort path when backups fail.
Sean Gallagher: Can we make backup failure blocking by default? We should not mutate anything without a backup artifact recorded. Irene Choi: Yes—default is blocking; added explicit abort semantics and a hidden continue-on-failure flag with confirmation. Connor O'Brien: How does this behave for air-gapped/on-prem where S3 isn’t available? Irene Choi: Snapshot is the preferred path; logical backups can write to file:/// mounted paths. Added validation + remediation text if VolumeSnapshot CRDs are missing. Hanae Suzuki: Please confirm that state persistence doesn’t store credentials. Irene Choi: Backup destinations/credentials are read from existing secret refs; upgrade state stores only redacted URIs and snapshot IDs; added tests for redaction. Vanessa Ortiz: Snapshot selection needs to be explicit; we can’t snapshot everything by default. Irene Choi: Added allowlist labels + pvcSelector flag; default matches only control-plane DB + state PVC labels. Rafael Mendes: Add timeouts and surface duration in output so on-call can reason about stuck backups. Irene Choi: Added per-step timeout and duration metrics in progress events and state.
payload.title: Private upgrades: backup orchestrator + snapshot hooks (CSI/EBS) + optional logical backup

Motivation: private deployments running in multi-AZ and on-prem clusters were observing uneven init job placement, occasional head-of-line blocking when tenant bootstrap jobs became heavy, and fragile upgrade windows when all init jobs retried simultaneously. This PR adds a focused set of Helm values and template changes to make init orchestration zone-aware, priority-safe, and more resilient via jittered backoff and optional leader-election for cross-namespace coordination. Key user-visible changes: 1) values.init.priorityClassName: allow operators to pin init jobs to a provided PriorityClass so critical migrations run ahead of low-priority tenants; 2) values.init.zoneSpread.enabled and values.init.zoneSpread.constraints: basic affinity/nodeSelector helpers so customers in multi-AZ environments can prefer spreading boot jobs across zones to avoid resource churn in a single AZ; 3) values.init.backoff: tunable backoff.initialSeconds, multiplier, and jitterPercent to avoid synchronized retry storms during cluster upgrades; 4) values.init.leaderElection.enable (default false) and values.init.leaderElection.namespace to optionally use a namespaced ConfigMap lock for sequencing cross-namespace init waves in air-gapped environments where API-server watch latencies are variable; 5) transitional defaults and migration notes so existing installs are opt-in and safe for rolling upgrades. This PR also updates the terraform module reference docs to demonstrate how to pass these new values from top-level installs, and adds unit tests for the Helm templates plus a small e2e job that simulates staggered init waves. Backwards compatibility: all fields are opt-in with sensible defaults; existing installs will continue to use previous behavior unless values are provided. See Linear tickets ENG-4821 and ENG-4990 for the broader rollout plan and gating alongside the runtime batching feature. Checklist: - [x] Helm values schema additions and comments - [x] Template changes for init Job/cronjob - [x] Add priorityClassName to init Job spec - [x] Add optional nodeAffinity/zone spread helpers - [x] Implement jittered backoff calculation in template helpers - [x] Add leader-election ConfigMap lock templating and RBAC snippets - [x] Unit tests for template rendering (helm unittest) - [x] Terraform docs example updated - [x] Manual QA: staged upgrade on dev cluster with 3 zones - [x] Release notes entry drafted
Diego Martinez: Can we ensure the default backoff.jitterPercent is conservative (15%)? Observed larger jitter can postpone critical migrations during recovery. Author reply: Set default to 15% in values.schema.json and added note in docs about tradeoffs.
Priya Raman: Leader election across namespaces is tricky for airgapped clusters because the operator's service account may not have cluster-scoped permissions. Suggest we make it explicit that leaderElection default is false and include RBAC snippets. Author reply: Done — added namespaced ConfigMap lock and RBAC via charts/private-installer/templates/rbac-init.yaml; leaderElection.enable defaults to false.
Liam O'Connor: Template helper complexity looks fine but add a unit test that asserts backoff seconds never exceed a configured cap. Author reply: Added a helm-unittest case that validates maxBackoffSeconds <= 3600 when multiplier and initialSeconds are high.
Security review (automated): noted that the leader lock uses ConfigMap writes; ensure audit logging and KMS keys are not referenced here. Author reply: This PR keeps leader lock ConfigMap scoped and documents that audit logging is provided by cluster logging — no secrets written.
QA (manual): Verified staged upgrade on dev cluster across 3 AZs; init jobs spread across AZs when zoneSpread.enabled=true; observed expected reduction in retry storms after jitter enabled.
Merge-resolver bot: lint fixes applied to templates via a small follow-up commit to address Helm lint warning about missing metadata. Author reply: incorporated fixes and re-ran unit tests.

Motivation: customers and internal auditors need deterministic ways to validate that RBAC v2 decisions, KMS region scoping, and audit events remain consistent across installer upgrades and multi-region mirrors. This PR introduces a first-class compliance probe toolchain packaged with the private installer that performs sampled audit consistency checks, surfaces KMS region telemetry, and provides an operator consent reporter for post-deploy review. Summary of changes: 1) new runtime subcommand 'redwood-installer probe compliance' which can be run in dry-run or enforce mode; 2) audit-consistency-checker: samples audit streams (Kafka/S3 hooks) and validates event ordering, immutable fields, and KMS region headers against the policy decision logs; 3) kms-region-telemetry: collects per-request KMS region hints, region pin violations, and latency histograms, emitting a compact telemetry envelope to the observability service; 4) consent-reporter: aggregates operator approvals and timed attestation envelopes signed with tenant-scoped CMKs for traceability; 5) RBACv2 linter integration: new lint rule set to catch attribute scoping and region-anchored role templates during installer render; 6) docs and runbook: step-by-step compliance-runbook and upgrade notes. Backwards compatibility: feature is opt-in and disabled by default; probes run locally or as a separate job in the installer control-plane; nothing mutating by default. Migration and rollout: operator can enable via values.yaml flag 'complianceProbe.enabled: true' or CLI '--enable-compliance-probe'; recommend dry-run for 72 hours before switching to enforced checks; the consent-reporter requires KMS CMK permissions (see docs) and will no-op if unconfigured. Security considerations: probe signs telemetry envelopes with a installer-attest key; KMS usage is limited to region metadata and attestation signing; we added strict scope checks to avoid key exposure. Testing: unit tests for checker rules, integration tests against a mini-Kafka audit fixture, e2e run for installer with a two-region mirror. Observability: new metrics 'compliance.probe.sample_rate', 'compliance.kms.region_mismatch', 'compliance.audit.stability_score'. Implementation notes and rationale: the checker uses a timed-window replayer strategy to avoid stateful long-lived compares across tenants; instead it computes stable hashes for event prefixes and compares proof windows across mirrors. Motivation: Private deployments require an auditable, least-privilege RBAC bootstrap that can be automatically generated from the actual infrastructure plan and Helm values used for install. This PR adds a tenant-scoped 'privilege bundler' that synthesizes minimal Role/ClusterRole and RoleBinding sets from live Terraform plans and chart values, plus a Terraform drift detector that fails bootstrap when plan drift would grant more privileges than intended.

What this change does (single string): adds a new cmd/installer subcommand (rbac-bundle) that ingests terraform plan JSON and Helm value snapshots, emits a policy bundle (k8s YAMLs) and a compact capability matrix (JSON) per-tenant; integrates a pre-apply drift check that compares generated policies against a stored allowlist and rejects bootstraps that expand capabilities unexpectedly; wires the bundler into the Private Installer post-apply hook so generated bundles are applied idempotently; provides a rollback runbook and a safe-retry mode which can automatically create a limited "bootstrap-sandbox" namespace for dry-run validation.

Key user-facing behavior: when operator runs private-installer with --rbac-auto, the installer will: 1) run terraform plan --out and convert tfplan to JSON, 2) compute minimal bindings per-tenant based on resource ownership annotations and Helm chart role templates, 3) run the drift detector against cluster state and stored allowlist, 4) apply generated bundle to a tenant-scoped namespace or fail fast with a clear remediation hint.

Implementation notes: the bundler uses a capability scoring heuristic (resource_kind, verbs, resource_name patterns) to compress allowed actions; policies are grouped into a bundle.yaml with deterministic ordering to keep diffs small; the drift detector uses a predicate engine that tolerates benign refactors (label changes) but flags verb/verb+resource expansions. The change adds unit/integration tests for the generator and drift detector and an operator E2E that validates idempotent apply/rollback.

Security and ops: KMS-wrapped signing was added so bundles are signed before applying (installer verifies signature). The PR also adds RBAC validation hooks so the installer will not bind a cluster-scoped role to a tenant namespace service account (prevents accidental cross-tenant escalation).

Checklist:
- [x] rbac-bundle generator CLI and Go library
- [x] terraform plan JSON adapter
- [x] drift detector and allowlist config format
- [x] post-apply hook integration and idempotent apply
- [x] bundle signing + verification (KMS integration in private builds)
- [x] runbook for rollback and safe-retry
- [x] unit + integration tests

Related: builds on design doc ENG-2481 (rbac bootstrap lifecycle) and the tenant-isolation audit in ENG-2623. Not intended to change defaults for existing installs unless operator opts into --rbac-auto.

Merge strategy: squash+merge to keep the bundler change as a single logical commit and simplify backporting.
Marco Li: Overall approach looks solid. Two concerns: (1) capability compression heuristic might under-approx in edge cases where wildcard patterns are used; we should provide an escape hatch. (2) need stronger unit tests for KMS signer error handling.
Aisha K. Raman: Added an explicit `--policy-escape` flag and documented it in the runbook; also added extra unit tests that simulate KMS failures (signing retry + clear error messages).
Priya Desai: Please ensure the installer does not ever auto-apply cluster-level bindings without explicit --allow-cluster-bindings. Also suggest we log the exact plan diff that's causing rejection to aid operators.
Aisha K. Raman: Added --allow-cluster-bindings flag gated behind an env var in private builds; drift detector now emits a compact plan diff artifact (stored in /var/log/redwood/rbac-diffs) and surfaces a truncated diff in CLI output.
Evan Thompson (security): What threat model did we use for signing? Do we rotate keys? How do we revoke a bundle?
Aisha K. Raman: Signed bundles include key id and timestamp; installer checks KMS key policy TTL. Revocation is via a denylist controller (separate follow-up ENG-2690) and the runbook includes steps to revoke and rollback an applied bundle. Added a TODO to link ENG-2690.
CI: initial run failed (lint error on pkg/rbac/bundler/heuristics.go: exported function without comment).
Aisha K. Raman: Fixed lint and re-ran CI; all checks green.
Adds automated tenant-scoped RBAC bundle generator and terraform plan drift detector for Private installs. Operator opt-in via --rbac-auto. Includes bundle signing, idempotent apply, and rollback runbook.

Motivation: Private control plane migrations to new PrivateLink endpoints often require careful, per-AZ cutovers to avoid control plane disruptions. Existing tooling performs route table swaps in-place which can cause transient connection loss for the control plane and user workloads. This PR introduces a subnet-shadowing pattern and a staged Privatelink switchover operator to enable non-destructive endpoint adoption with safe rollbacks.

Summary of changes: added Terraform modules to create 'shadow' subnets that mirror control-plane subnets but target new Privatelink endpoints; extended the installer Helm chart with a new 'switchover-operator' deployment implementing a staged switchover finite-state-machine (drain, probe, swap-routes, update-dns, rotate-sgs); added preflight and postflight checks, canary rollout hooks, and a rollback path that restores previous route tables and DNS records. Also added IAM least-privilege policies for the operator and integration tests for staged swap behavior.

Implementation details: 1) Terraform: new modules/network/shadow_subnet.tf creates duplicate subnets with descriptive tags (redwood:shadow-of=<subnet-id>), a dedicated route table (rtb-shadow-<subnet>) and conditional Privatelink ENI attachments. The module is opt-in via installer values: "enable_subnet_shadowing". 2) Helm: new chart component "switchover-operator" (controllers, rbac, deployment, hpa) with configurable concurrency and probe thresholds. 3) Operator: implements stages (PREPARE -> DRAIN_ROUTES -> PROBE -> SWAP_ROUTES -> UPDATE_DNS -> ROTATE_SGS -> VERIFY -> COMPLETE). Operator uses a leader-elected controller; state stored in a CRD (SwitchoverPlan) scoped to the install namespace. 4) DNS: staged TTL reduction and atomic CNAME swaps for control plane zone to minimize cache inconsistencies. The operator writes DNS intent records during PROBE so monitoring can verify consistency before final swap. 5) Security: new IAM policy documents added to terraform/iam/privatelink_operator_policy.json with only ec2:CreateNetworkInterface, ec2:DescribeRouteTables, route53:ChangeResourceRecordSets (narrowed to control plane hosted zone), and iam:PassRole to a dedicated operator role. 6) Observability: added metrics (switchover_attempts_total, switchover_stage_duration_seconds, switchover_failures_total) and logs annotated with plan_id and subnet_shadow_id.

Rollout and migration plan: create shadow subnets for a single region and AZ, attach test control-plane nodes to shadow route table, enable operator in canary mode (max_concurrent_plans=1) and run a single SwitchoverPlan with dry_run=false and probe_threshold=5 successful probes. After 48 hours of metrics and smoke-testing (control-plane latencies, hello-checks), increase to 50% AZs and finally full cutover. Operator supports pause/resume and immediate rollback which swaps back original RTs and restores DNS and SG attachments.

Testing: unit tests for operator state transitions added under operator/pkg/*; integration tests in infra/tests/switchover/ exercise per-AZ swap and rollback using a local k8s kind cluster with a mocked AWS API (moto-based harness). Added end-to-end acceptance that validates DNS TTL behavior and confirms no dropped control-plane requests during probe thresholds. CI: full workflow includes lint, unit, integration (mocked), and a lightweight k8s smoke test. One flaky network test was stabilized by adding retry backoff (see commits).

Backward compatibility and safety: feature is opt-in and default off. Existing clusters are unaffected unless enable_subnet_shadowing is set. The operator verifies sanity (route table tags, ENI attachment health, DNS ownership) before performing modifying actions. Rollback is idempotent and safe to run multiple times.

Related work: follows patterns in ENG-2124 (safe egress transition) and Infra ticket INF-398 (Privatelink orchestration). This PR is intended to reduce blast radius when migrating endpoints and to give SREs an automated, observable path for rolling upgrades.

Files touched and high-level diffs included in the commits. See changed_files for specifics.

Jordan Patel: Request changes - tighten IAM permissions for route53 to exact hosted zone ARN and add unit tests for missing error path in ReplaceRoutes().
Maya Thompson (author): Addressed - narrowed route53 permission and added ReplaceRoutes error path test, pushed new commit c9d2a1b.
Evan Li: LGTM after nits - please add an observability dashboard link in the runbook and include the plan_id in all logs.
Maya Thompson: Added dashboard JSON and plan_id annotation to logs in operator, updated docs.
Sanjay Rao: Approve - verified mocked integration runs locally and rollback path succeeds repeatedly. Marking ready to merge.
Add opt-in subnet shadowing feature to enable non-destructive Privatelink migrations.
New switchover-operator Helm chart for staged per-AZ cutovers with safe rollback.
New observability metrics and runbook for Privatelink endpoint migration.

Motivation: Upgrading the observability stack in private installs (Prometheus + Grafana + log-shippers) has been causing alert storms and noisy pager traffic when dashboards and recording rules change out-of-band. This PR implements a safe, rolling upgrade path that suppresses tenant-scoped alerts during the critical window, provisions dashboards atomically, and provides an automated rollback playbook for fast recovery.

What I changed (high level): Added a small Kubernetes controller (helm-hooked) that sequences Grafana dashboard provisioning and PrometheusRule application with tenant-scoped suppression annotations; added a Terraform variable alert_silence_window (seconds) to the observability module; updated Helm charts to include pre-upgrade hooks that create Silence objects and a post-upgrade verifier; introduced an immutable-folder import mode for Grafana provisioning to avoid transient duplicate dashboards; added e2e test harness which exercises upgrades across 3 tenant namespaces and validates no firing alerts during silence window.

Commits: 1) controller: implement rolling upgrade sequencer and tenant label propagation; 2) helm: pre/post hooks + grafana immutable-folder mode; 3) terraform: expose alert_silence_window and canary_namespace for staged upgrades; 4) tests: integration harness and playbook docs; 5) docs: upgrade/rollback runbook.

Files changed (selected): charts/grafana/templates/pre-upgrade-hook.yaml (new), charts/grafana/templates/post-upgrade-check.yaml (modified), modules/observability/main.tf (var+outputs), modules/observability/README.md (docs), pkg/controllers/upgrade/sequencer.go (new, ~420 LOC), test/e2e/upgrade_safety_test.go (new), docs/upgrade_playbook.md (new).

Testing: Local kind cluster + Prometheus/Grafana chart pinned to test fixtures. Ran CI integration suite (observability-e2e) which reproduces tenant alerting workload; CI passed after fixing race in sequencer reconciler (addressed by commit 3). Manual dry-run performed on internal staging private-installer with two tenants; observed no alert firing during the configured silence window and dashboards landed in immutable folders as expected.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag 'obs_rolling_upgrades' in installer config; 2) Enable in canary region with alert_silence_window=180s and canary_namespace set; 3) Monitor token-level and per-tenant alert counts on Redwood Console dashboards for 24 hours; 4) Gradually increase rollout to all private installs.

Rollback playbook (high level): - If post-upgrade verifications fail, controller triggers a Helm rollback of the Grafana release and removes Silence objects; - Run 'installer rollback-playbook --snapshot <pre-upgrade-snapshot>' to restore PrometheusRule and dashboard state; - Run validation harness from test/e2e to confirm alerts have returned to baseline. Detailed steps live in docs/upgrade_playbook.md.

Review thread (summary): - Liam: requested explicit tenant label propagation and unit tests for sequencer; added two unit tests and clarified label handling in sequencer.go. - Sofia: asked for an audit log entry when silences are created; added controller emit of Kubernetes Events and a short note in README. - Ethan: asked for terraform variable naming clarity; renamed alert_window_seconds -> alert_silence_window and updated module README. All reviewers approved.

CI status: GitHub Actions matrix ran unit, lint, helm template, terraform validate, and observability-e2e. Observability-e2e initially failed due to race; fixed in commit 3 and all checks passed on re-run.

Backward compatibility: No breaking API changes for customers. Optional feature flag controls behavior. The terraform variable defaults to 0 (no silence) to preserve existing installs unless explicitly configured.

Notes and follow-ups: - Proposed follow-up: autoscale silence window based on number of tenants and rule churn (ENG-2027) - Consider adding a dry-run mode to sequencer for dry verification before committing to production.

Merge: Squash-merged after approvals and green CI.
Introduces tenant-aware alert suppression window during observability upgrades; adds a rolling upgrade controller for Prometheus/Grafana Helm releases; Terraform flag for controlled dashboard provisioning; rollback playbook and test harness for on-prem private installs.

Motivation: Private control planes in multi-AZ customer environments require deterministic failover when subnets are degraded, cross-account egress role provisioning for outbound NAT/privatelink use, and an idempotent DNS priming step to ensure resolvers observe freshly created control-plane endpoints. This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) a 'subnet-set' allocator that groups AZ subnets into primary/failover sets with deterministic selection and graceful draining hooks; 2) cross-account egress IAM role templates and an installer flow to provision and rotate those roles when customers request egress via a partner account; 3) a DNS priming orchestrator that performs staged Route53/forwarding priming and health probes to reduce DNS convergence time during control-plane switchover. The changes touch Terraform modules, Helm values for the installer operator, and the control-plane state reconciliation code.

What this PR does (summary): - Adds terraform/modules/subnetset allocator module with idempotent plan/apply behavior and tagging scheme for ownership and lifecycle. - Adds terraform/modules/egress-role to create cross-account IAM roles and managed policy attachments with a minimal trust boundary and rotation hook. - Adds installer helm chart values and a small controller (cmd/controlplane-reconciler) that orchestrates subnet-set failover and invokes DNS priming using a new controller job. - Introduces a DNS priming job image and k8s Job template with exponential backoff probe logic to avoid thundering herds. - Adds unit and integration tests for the allocator and end-to-end smoke test in the perf-canary harness.

Checklist: - [x] Terraform module + documentation - [x] Helm chart values + migration notes - [x] Controller + e2e smoke test - [x] Security review for cross-account role trust policy - [x] Linear tickets linked (ENG-2231, ENG-2278)

Operational notes: The subnet-set allocator uses a deterministic hash of VPC ID + AZ + cluster-id to pick primary/failover sets and writes subnet tags used by the control plane reconciler to pick the correct subnets. The egress role module emits outputs consumed by the installer to populate ExternalAccountPrincipal fields. DNS priming is opt-in via helm value installer.dnsPriming.enabled (default false) to avoid surprise behavior for existing customers. The PR includes migration documentation under docs/installer/migrations/subnetset-2025-11.md.

Asha Menon (author): Added probe jitter and increased probe timeout in the helm job template; noted TODO to surface histogram metrics for probe durations.

Motivation: customers in regulated environments require an HSM-backed auto-unseal for Vault and automated service certificate rotation tied to cert-manager. The private installer lacked a consolidated flow to (1) provision/unwrap an HSM-wrapped master key (PKCS#11 keywrap pattern), (2) configure Vault auto-unseal against a managed HSM/KMS, and (3) rotate cluster-facing TLS certificates with cert-manager while preserving in-place upgrades and safe rollbacks.

This PR adds: consolidated Terraform modules and installer hooks that wire Vault auto-unseal to an HSM/KMS keywrap (PKCS#11 compatible), Helm chart values and templates to consume the auto-unseal config, a cert-manager-based certificate rotation controller hook that updates Service/Ingress SANs during node/region changes, and an upgrade hook that ensures Vault unseal keys are rewrapped atomically so rollbacks do not leave Vault un-unsealable.

Key design points: single continuous installer flow that: 1) provisions or references an existing HSM key (supports AWS CloudHSM, on-prem PKCS#11 HSMs, and KMS-wrapped key material via keywrap); 2) performs an operator-managed keywrap (wrap/unwind) transaction logged to audit; 3) configures Vault's seal stanza dynamically and rolls Vault pods with a deterministic sequence to avoid split-brain; 4) uses cert-manager ClusterIssuer with ACME or internal CA to manage short-lived certs and a controller hook to reconcile SAN changes across Services/Ingresses; 5) exposes explicit terraform module inputs for key lifecycle policies and rotation windows.

Backward compatibility: installer defaults remain unchanged unless the new installer flag vault.auto_unseal.enabled is set. Existing deployments will be unaffected. For upgrades, the hook performs a reversible keywrap step and stores a wrapped copy in the sealed-secret store (or user-managed Vault transit) to allow rollback.

Security considerations: private keys are never written to plain kube secrets. Wrapped key blobs are stored only in sealed-secrets or HSM/KMS. Audit entries are added for wrap/unwrap. The Terraform module requires RBAC gating and forces explicit operator consent for automatic rewraps.

Testing and validation: included unit tests for Terraform templates, Helm template rendering snapshots, an e2e policy test in perf-canary that exercises auto-unseal lifecycle, and an e2e tls-e2e that simulates SAN changes and validates zero-downtime cert rollouts. CI flagged a flaky tls-e2e which was retried and passed; we added a follow-up ticket to harden timings.

Docs: upgrade notes and an operator runbook added to docs/private-installer/vault-hsm-rotation.md describing operators steps, rollback instructions, and manual unseal steps in edge cases.

Rollout plan: gated behind a feature flag in installer config. Recommend staged rollouts to one tenant cluster, then to Dedicated pilot customers before general availability.

payload.body:
Motivation: Private deployments run into dangerous rollback windows during multi-tenant upgrades where partial schema changes leave some tenants in a non-backwards-compatible state. This PR introduces a tenant-scoped epoching mechanism plus a rollback-seal that prevents restoring to an older epoch once critical migration steps have been recorded. It pairs that with a Terraform plan gate which validates presence of verified backups and compatible migration artifacts before allowing infrastructure changes that could trigger an upgrade.

What this PR changes (high level):
- Database: add tenant_epoch table + helper functions (set_epoch, read_epoch, seal_epoch). The seal is a one-way marker (idempotent) that prevents recovery to epochs < sealed_epoch without operator override.
- Installer operator: new pre-upgrade hook that quiesces tenant workers, records the current epoch, runs migrations in a transactional sandbox, and seals the epoch when migrations reach a designated safepoint.
- Helm charts: add lifecycle hooks for pre-upgrade-quiesce and post-rollback-validation; add values to configure epoch seal TTL and operator override policy.
- Terraform module: introduce a tf plan checker script (bin/tf_plan_gate.sh) which calls the new operator API to confirm backups and epoch compatibility; the module's apply is gated by an external data source that runs the checker.
- Tooling: add `rwi migrate preview --tenant <id>` command that shows a migration timeline and indicates whether the tenant will cross a seal boundary.
- Tests and docs: integration tests for epoch monotonicity, helm hooks smoke tests, and documentation in docs/private/upgrade-safety.md.

Description and rationale:
- Epoching: Each tenant now has a monotonically-increasing integer epoch representing the tenant's DB schema/runtime compatibility level. Migrations increment epochs in a controlled, transactional way. This allows operators to reason about how far a tenant has advanced and prevents accidental rollbacks that would violate schema constraints.
- Rollback seal: Once an operator marks a migration safepoint (seal), the system rejects restoration into an older epoch unless an explicit operator override is performed with an audit reason. The override path requires a multi-party approval recorded in the operator audit log.
- Terraform plan gate: Many customer outages stem from infra changes that trigger upgrades without verifying backups and migrations. The tf plan gate performs three checks before apply: (1) verified S3/MinIO backup exists with matching prefix and timestamp, (2) operator API reports no unsealed migrations that would be lost by a restore, (3) Helm chart version compatibility check against the operator-managed model. If any check fails, the plan gate exits non-zero and the apply is blocked.

How to test locally:
1) Start the private operator in dev mode: `make run-operator-dev`
2) Create two tenants and run `rwi migrate preview` to observe epoch changes.
3) Run the helm pre-upgrade hook: `helm upgrade --install --dry-run` and confirm the quiesce hook runs and creates a preflight snapshot in `/tmp/preflight-<ts>`
4) Run `bin/tf_plan_gate.sh` against a sample terraform plan (instructions in README).
5) Integration test: `make test-integration-upgrade` spins up a lightweight pg instance, applies migrations, seals epoch, then attempts a restore to an older epoch and asserts operator reject.

Checklist:
- [x] Add tenant_epoch table and DB helpers (idempotent migrations)
- [x] Operator pre-upgrade quiesce + seal API
- [x] Helm hooks + values for epoch settings
- [x] Terraform plan gate + example integration
- [x] CLI preview command and docs
- [x] Integration tests and CI workflow updates

Commits (summary):
- add: tenant_epoch migration, SQL helpers, and tests
- feat: operator API + quiesce/seal implementation
- chore: helm chart lifecycle hooks and new values.yaml entries
- feat: terraform module external data source for plan gating and bin/tf_plan_gate.sh
- feat: rwi cli migrate preview implementation and docs
- test: integration suite + github actions workflow for upgrade tests

Files changed (high level):
- installer/operator/pkg/epoch/handler.go
- installer/operator/api/openapi.yaml (exposes /operator/tenants/:id/epoch)
- installer/migrations/2025_01_17_add_tenant_epoch.sql
- charts/private/values.yaml (new epoch settings)
- charts/private/templates/hooks/pre-upgrade-quiesce.yaml
- charts/private/templates/hooks/post-rollback-validate.yaml
- terraform/modules/private/plan_gate/main.tf (external data source)
- terraform/modules/private/scripts/bin/tf_plan_gate.sh
- cli/rwi/cmd/migrate_preview.go
- docs/private/upgrade-safety.md
- test/integration/upgrade_epoch_test.go

Review notes and decisions:
- We intentionally make the seal a one-way operation to reduce operator error: sealing requires explicit intent and is rate-limited. Approval flow is plumbed into operator audit logs.
- The tf plan gate is conservative by default; teams can opt-out with an explicit flag in their terraform module but must accept a documented risk waiver.
- The migration preview CLI is read-only and will never mutate tenant state.

CI and tests:
- GitHub Actions matrix: unit (go/test), lint, helm-template, tf-plan-check (runs tf_plan_gate.sh in CI with mock backups), integration-upgrade (runs on schedule and on PR label apply).
- First CI run exposed a flaky race in operator shutdown; I added a shutdown-wait in operator/pkg/manager to wait for in-flight quiesce tasks before exiting. Subsequent runs passed.

Backward compatibility and rollback story:
- New schema additions are additive-first, with guard rails to ensure older operators can still read tenant_epoch until migrations that require epoch changes are rolled out.
- If an operator attempts to restore a backup whose tenant_epoch < sealed_epoch, the operator will refuse the restore and require an explicit override documented in the audit log. This prevents silent data corruption across tenants.

Migration plan for customers:
1) Upgrade operator to a release with epoching enabled (non-sealing mode by default) to collect epoch telemetry for 1–2 weeks.
2) Run `rwi migrate preview --all` to identify tenants likely to cross seal boundaries.
3) Schedule maintenance window to run pre-upgrade quiesce + migrations; once verified, seal epochs per-tenant with approvals.
4) Enable terraform plan gate in CI for added safety.

Release notes: "Introduce tenant epoching and a rollback-seal mechanism to prevent unsafe restores; add Terraform plan gating to require verified backups and migration compatibility before infra apply. Includes Helm hooks and operator API for safe upgrades."

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on operator audit logging correctness, idempotence of SQL migration, and terraform plan gate failure modes.
- I left TODOs in the operator audit docs for multi-party approval UI (ENG-4920), which will come in a follow-up.

Ethan Zhao: please ensure the seal has a reversible admin override path with audit logging — we need that for enterprise customers. Author reply: implemented override with approver list and audit entry (see operator/api).
Lena Fischer: the tf_plan_gate dependency on S3 prefix could block air-gapped installs. Author reply: added a MinIO-compatible path and a configurable 'gate_method' value to support airgap (documented).
Marcus Green: integration test failed on first run due to operator race — can you add a wait/timeout? Author reply: added shutdown wait and re-ran CI; tests are stable now.

Motivation: Customer private deployments running in constrained multi-AZ VPCs observed asymmetric egress after NAT failover and inconsistent DNS ownership when controlplane endpoints cross-account. This PR introduces a policy-driven NAT failover mechanism and a deterministic DNS handoff that ties service endpoints to an explicit ownership tag so that route propagation and resolver forwarding remain consistent during upgrades and AZ failover.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a controlplane egress policy layer (Terraform + Helm) that can pin egress traffic by service tag, prefer specified NAT gateways per-AZ, and fail over using prioritized policies instead of simple health-check rotation.
- Introduces a service_ownership tag on AWS endpoints and corresponding Route53 resolver conditional-forwarding entries to ensure DNS queries for controlplane subdomains resolve to the correct account/endpoint in cross-account setups.
- Adds idempotent reconcilers in the installer that detect mismatched endpoint tags and reconcile resolver rules without disrupting active sockets.
- Back-compat: existing clusters without the tag keep the current behavior; the installer can opt-in via `controlplane.egress.policy.enabled=true`.

Files and components affected (summary):
- terraform/modules/vpc/egress_policy.tf: new module that declares prioritized NAT groups and IAM to rotate ownership safely.
- helm/controlplane/templates/egress-policy-configmap.yaml: runtime config consumed by the controlplane agent.
- installer/hooks/reconcile_endpoint_tags.go: controller that ensures endpoint and resolver state converge.
- installer/upgrade/rollback.sh: quick rollback helper that re-applies prior resolver rules and drains affected instances.
- docs/operators/egress-and-dns.md: operator-facing docs describing parameters and troubleshooting.

Testing and validation steps performed:
- Unit tests for Terraform module logic + plan diffs for edge cases around multiple NATs (see commits).
- Integration test in staging VPC with a simulated cross-account endpoint and Route53 inbound/outbound rules verified.
- Blue/green upgrade in a dedicated test cluster to exercise the reconciler and rollback helper without request loss.

Upgrade notes / operator guidance:
- To enable: set `controlplane.egress.policy.enabled=true` and provide `controlplane.egress.policy.preferred_nats` list in values or Terraform var.
- For cross-account setups, ensure the installer principal has bless permissions to create or tag endpoints in the target account; see docs/operators/egress-and-dns.md for role assumption example.
- Rollback: run `installer/upgrade/rollback.sh <cluster>` which will re-apply previous resolver rules and fail back NAT weights safely.

Checklist: 
- [x] Terraform module + unit tests
- [x] Helm chart + helm lint
- [x] Installer reconciler implementation + e2e integration test
- [x] Docs and operator playbook
- [x] CI green and manual staging validation

Related: Linear ENG-3421 (egress policy workstream), INF-1188 (dns handoff design).

Notes: This PR intentionally avoids forcing a migration for existing clusters. The tag-based ownership allows a gradual rollout per-tenant. Follow-up PRs will add observability counters for failover events to the Redwood Console and an automated Linear task creator when resolver mismatches are observed.
Rafael Ortiz: Can the reconciler tolerate partial IAM permission failures (tagging in a subset of accounts)? Please add graceful degradation and metrics.
Maya Chen (author): Yes — added explicit retries and a metric (installer.egress.tag_reconcile_failures) and documented behavior in the operator guide.
Lina Patel: Helm values.schema.json needs the new fields documented and validated; please add schema validation to prevent runtime misconfig.
Maya Chen (author): Added values.schema.json entries and a unit test for missing required list when policy.enabled=true.
Operator-facing: Add opt-in controlplane egress policy with prioritized NAT failover and deterministic DNS handoff via service_ownership tagging. See docs/operators/egress-and-dns.md for rollout and rollback steps.

payload.body:
Motivation and summary: We observed a class of private-deployment failures where control-plane egress relied on centralized NAT instances that created single points of failure and noisy neighbor egress behavior during upgrades. This PR introduces an AZ-aware ENI-based egress proxy pattern that attaches ephemeral ENIs into customer subnets, plus a DNS cascade fallback mechanism (primary resolver set in-region, secondary cross-region) and explicit upgrade rollback hooks to restore prior routing and ENI state when healthchecks fail during a control-plane upgrade.

What this changes (single continuous description): Implements a new Terraform module (terraform/modules/az-eni-egress) that allocates per-AZ ENI proxy appliances (small EC2 instances or AMI-based proxies) with associated security groups, IAM role, and per-subnet route table entries. The installer will create route-table hooks that can be atomically swapped during rollout: new-route -> healthcheck -> confirm -> commit. If healthchecks fail, the rollback hook removes ENI routes and restores previous route attachments. Adds opt-in configuration in the installer values (helm/controlplane/values.yaml) to enable AZ_ENI_EGRESS true/false, with sensible defaults enabled for Dedicated/Private tier.

DNS cascade fallback: Adds a resolver set abstraction and two resolver groups: local (primary) and global-fallback (secondary). The control-plane resolver configuration will prefer local resolvers and fall back to the global set when local lookups timeout or NXDOMAIN patterns match (configurable TTL and retry thresholds). Implements resolver chaining in the installer templates and a small sidecar agent (controlplane/dns-fallback-agent) which monitors resolver health and atomically updates /etc/resolv.conf inside the control-plane container group when a failover is required.

Upgrade/rollback tooling: Adds a small orchestration script (hack/upgrade-rollback.sh) used by the installer to perform staged route swaps and ENI promotions during rolling upgrades. The script executes: (1) create new ENI proxies in target AZs, (2) add temporary route entries with lower priority, (3) run healthcheck suite (connectivity, latency, DNS resolution), (4) commit by switching route priority, (5) clean up old ENIs. If any step fails the script triggers rollback: revert route table to previous state, de-assign new ENIs, and emit alerts with a runbook link. The Helm chart includes a post-upgrade hook to call this script when using the helm-based installer.

Terraform and helm changes: - terraform/modules/az-eni-egress/*: new module with main.tf, security group templates, outputs for route IDs and ENI IDs. - installer/helmcharts/controlplane/templates/eni-proxy.yaml: DaemonSet/Deployment template for proxy installation. - installer/helmcharts/controlplane/values.yaml: new config flags and resolver groups. - hack/upgrade-rollback.sh: orchestration script (bash). - docs/privatedeploy/az-eni-egress.md: operator doc with config knobs and troubleshooting. - tests/integration/test-eni-rollback.py: small pytest integration test simulating failed healthcheck and asserting routes restored.

Commits (summary): [1/5] terraform: add az-eni-egress module and README - scaffolds resources and outputs. [2/5] helm: add eni-proxy chart fragment and values for resolver groups. [3/5] installer: wire module outputs into controlplane module and add route-swap hooks. [4/5] tooling: add hack/upgrade-rollback.sh and unit tests for rollback logic. [5/5] docs + integration tests: operator guide and pytest for failure case.

Files changed (high-level): terraform/modules/az-eni-egress/main.tf; terraform/modules/az-eni-egress/outputs.tf; installer/helmcharts/controlplane/templates/eni-proxy.yaml; installer/helmcharts/controlplane/values.yaml; installer/controls/route-swap-hook.yaml; hack/upgrade-rollback.sh; docs/privatedeploy/az-eni-egress.md; tests/integration/test-eni-rollback.py; charts/values.schema.json (bumped schema).

Testing and CI: Local integration suite was run against a minimal VPC in CI using a small instance type for proxy appliances. CI initially failed in the first run due to a race in route propagation; fix applied in commit 3 and CI re-run. Final CI status: pass (build, terraform-plan, helm-lint, integration-tests).

Review conversation (high-level, single continuous narrative): Ravi: "Can you clarify how the ENI proxies authenticate to AWS APIs and whether we leak IAM credentials under scale?" — Leah: "ENI proxies use an instance-profile IAM role with least privilege; we rotate role association using the installer's role-assignment workflow. Added README section and automated test to validate no long-lived credentials are written to disk." Ana: "We need to ensure rollback doesn't leave dangling route table associations in multi-AZ tests." — Leah: "Added atomic route-swap steps and an explicit finalizer that re-checks route table state; integration test covers this." Marcus: "How does DNS cascade affect latency-sensitive control-plane calls?" — Leah: "Default thresholds are conservative (50ms timeout, 3 retries) and can be disabled; documented trade-offs. Also the agent prefers in-AZ resolvers so long tail is minimized." Several smaller comments addressed (nits on naming, extra logs) and approvals granted by all reviewers.

Security review: Security reviewed IAM policy and SG rules; no high-severity issues found. Added extra egress filtering rules to the proxy SG and documented the minimum port set.

Merge outcome: Merged via squash-merge after approvals and green CI. Release plan: staged rollout to Dedicated customers during next maintenance window; changelog entry added.

Operator notes & runbook pointers: docs/privatedeploy/az-eni-egress.md includes a troubleshooting section that covers ENI cleanup, route reconciliation, and how to manually trigger rollback hooks. The hack script emits structured logs for the console and integrates with our alerting topic for automatic paging when rollback activates.
Adds AZ-aware ephemeral ENI egress proxies for control plane, DNS cascade fallback between resolver sets, and automated rollback hooks for failed control-plane upgrades; Terraform modules and Helm charts updated. No user API changes.
Ravi: Can you clarify how the ENI proxies authenticate to AWS APIs?
Leah: ENI proxies use instance-profile IAM role with least privilege; README updated.
Ana: Ensure rollback doesn't leave dangling route table associations in multi-AZ.
Leah: Added atomic route-swap + finalizer and integration test to validate.
Marcus: How does DNS cascade affect latency-sensitive calls?
Leah: Defaults are conservative, agent prefers in-AZ resolvers; documented.
Ravi: please add SG egress whitelist to reduce blast radius
Leah: added SG rules and re-ran security checks

Summary: Adds a new terraform module (tfstate-lease-transactor) and an operator-style helper (gpu-topology-mapper) to better separate tfstate ownership for tenant GPU leases from nodepool lifecycle, and to map GPU topology to tenant-level network slices. Motivation: Private installs have increasing drift and outage surface from tightly-coupled tfstate files that contain both network and ephemeral GPU lease state. This causes rollbacks and upgrades to be risky in multi-tenant private deployments. The new transactor introduces a small stateful orchestration layer that serializes lease handoff, provides a compact lease index for fast reconcilers, and enables a safer migration path (non-destructive) for existing tfstate layouts. The topology mapper improves scheduling affinity by emitting consistent nodeclass -> tenant network annotations and a small mapping CRD for the installer to consume. What changed (high level): - New terraform module: modules/tfstate-lease-transactor (handles separate backend configs, locking semantics, lease index object schema, and migration helpers). - New helm chart patch and k8s manifests: charts/private-installer/templates/gpu-topology-mapper-deployment.yaml and CRD for gpu.topology.redwood.ai/v1alpha1. - Migration tooling: tools/tfstate/lease-migrate.sh and a Go helper cli that performs dry-run and apply paths. - Minor refactors: modules/gpu-nodepool updated to emit nodeclass labels compatible with the mapper; IAM role module additions to allow transactor service account to assume lease owner role. - CI infra: added e2e test spec in test/e2e/gpu-lease-migration.spec and a lightweight local runner for CI. Commits summary: "initial transactor module scaffolding"; "implement lease index and locking primitives"; "add migration dry-run; unit tests"; "gpu-topology-mapper controller and CRD"; "helm chart integration and docs"; "fix IAM role scoping and unit tests"; "ci: add e2e gating and retry on flaky migration test" Files changed (representative): - modules/tfstate-lease-transactor/{main.tf,outputs.tf,variables.tf,README.md} - charts/private-installer/templates/gpu-topology-mapper-deployment.yaml - charts/private-installer/templates/gpu-topology-mapper-crd.yaml - modules/gpu-nodepool/variables.tf - modules/iam/roles.tf - tools/tfstate/lease-migrate.sh - pkg/installer/topology/mapper/controller.go - test/e2e/gpu-lease-migration.spec - docs/private-deploy/lease-transactor-migration.md Testing: Local unit tests for the transactor module (terraform validate + terratest style), controller unit tests in Go, and an e2e scenario in a k3d cluster that exercises migration dry-run/apply and verifies node labels/annotations are consistent post-migrate. CI: initial run showed a single flaky e2e failure (migration test timeout) which was addressed by adding an exponential backoff and increased timeout; final CI status is green. Backwards compatibility and migration plan: - Migration is opt-in. By default installs continue to use current tfstate layout. - operators can run tools/tfstate/lease-migrate.sh --dry-run to produce a report of proposed state moves and a safe apply plan. - The transactor only takes over leases when the apply completes and a consensus lock is acquired. - Rollback path is provided: migration produces a state snapshot and a revert plan; the transactor will honor the snapshot to restore prior ownership. Rollout plan and risk mitigation: - Canary on internal staging clusters for 2 weeks; then opt-in beta with customer success for 3 tenant installs; observe for lease-granularity regressions. - Keep previous nodepool lifecycle path as fallback by setting a feature flag in values.yaml. - Monitor metrics introduced: transactor.leases_acquired_total, transactor.acquire_latency_ms, mapper.mapped_nodes, and migration.dry_run_reports. Review highlights (single string timeline): Reviewer Marco Liang: "High-level: nice separation. Please clarify lock semantics for cross-region installs and add an integration test that simulates concurrent lease requests." Author reply (Aisha): "Added a locking section in the module README and added a simulated concurrent request test to e2e; lock uses per-lease index with sequenced tokens and Terraform state locker as a last-resort guard." Reviewer Riley Thompson: "IAM scoping looks broad; can we tighten the assumeRole policy and require a pointer to customer KMS for rotation?" Author reply: "Tightened assumeRole to sts:AssumeRole for only transactor SA + explicit resource ARNs; KMS pointer added to module variables with a note in README for enterprise installs." Reviewer Samira Gomez: "Please add migration dry-run to changelog and ensure non-root users can execute the CLI." Author: "Fixed - CLI now supports delegated users via kubeconfig contexts and we added non-root install docs." Merge notes: squash merge after green CI; release note entry added. Related Linear tickets: ENG-4529 (tfstate split for private installs), ENG-4580 (gpu topology mapping and affinity). Related Jira: SUP-7891 (customer-reported private upgrade drift). Known limitations and follow-ups: - Cross-account tfstate replication is not implemented (follow-up ENG-4692). - Mapper currently supports only Nvidia A100 and H100 profiles; adding other GPU families planned. - Need to add RBAC audit hooks for transactor operations. Documentation: docs/private-deploy/lease-transactor-migration.md contains operator-facing steps, sample terraform var blocks, and rollback instructions. Merge outcome: merged to main via squash on 2026-02-24.
Adds opt-in TFState Lease Transactor to decouple GPU lease ownership from nodepool lifecycle; introduces GPU Topology Mapper and migration tooling; includes IAM scoping and rollback plans.
