payload.body:
Motivation: Private control-plane provisioning in multi-AZ customers exposed two operational challenges: (1) unpredictable ENI IP assignment across AZs that caused route-table overlap and late-stage kube control-plane failures during upgrades, and (2) inadequate security group attachment semantics for egress proxies where tenants need zone-anchored egress policies without changing core control-plane SGs. This PR introduces a zonal control-plane IP allocator and an egress-security-group adaptor to address both problems in an idempotent, Terraform-first way. Summary of changes: - New Terraform module: zonal_controlplane_ip_allocator (modules/network/zonal_ip_allocator) that reserves stable /32 IPs per control-plane instance per AZ using an idempotent tag-based allocation and a namespaced state key so customers can re-run provisioning without collisions. The module supports a migration path from the legacy ip-pool by optionally claiming existing ENIs. - Egress SG adaptor: a small controller and Helm chart values (charts/private-installer/templates/egress-sg-adaptor.yaml) that maps logical egress profiles to per-AZ security groups and attaches them to control-plane ENIs via instance-tag lookup. The adaptor is deployed as a sidecar-capable DaemonSet in on-prem flows and as a Deployment for VPC-based private control planes. - Installer changes: private-installer Terraform plan now wires the allocator module outputs into control-plane ENI resources and adds conditional outputs for cross-account peering routes. Added smoke checks and a migration toggle (feature_flag.migrate_zonal_ips) to convert existing clusters safely. - Helm/values: new values.private.controlPlane.zonalIP.enabled and values.egress.adaptor.enable for toggling in upgrades. Existing defaults remain off to preserve backward compatibility. - Tests & CI: terraform validate, fmt, unit tests, and a new integration harness (tests/integration/zonal_ip_simulator) that simulates AZ failure and verifies allocator idempotency. A constrained e2e run was executed against the staging VPC to validate SG attachments and DNS resolution across peering. Approach and rationale: - Deterministic allocation: We allocate per-AZ deterministic IPs by deriving an allocation index from the VPC CIDR and AZ hash to avoid centralized counters in state that cause contention in large fleets. The allocator stores a small set of tags on the allocated ENI and a TF-managed tag entry so subsequent runs can reconcile in-place. - Safeguarded rollouts: The default is off. The migration toggle performs a dry-run reservation, emits warnings for conflicts, and requires explicit manual approval in the Console or CLI to execute the migration. - Minimal blast radius: The egress SG adaptor attaches ephemeral per-AZ SGs instead of mutating core control-plane SGs. This lets tenants test egress policy changes per-AZ and roll back quickly. Rollout plan: - Stage 1: Feature merged behind flags; enable in a single non-prod region and run the migration tool in dry-run mode. - Stage 2: Canary: enable migrate_zonal_ips=true in one customer region with automated cutover window and on-call monitoring. - Stage 3: Gradual enablement: Open opt-in for customers via Console and then broad enablement after two weeks of canary stability. Testing performed: - Local integration: ran tests/integration/zonal_ip_simulator with 3 AZs simulated; allocator was idempotent across repeated apply/destroy cycles. - Staging VPC: Terraform apply used the allocator; DNS/peering smoke passed; adaptor attached per-AZ SGs and traffic shaping validated using iperf. - CI: terraform validate, terraform plan, helm lint, unit tests, and integration smoke passed. Known limitations and follow-ups: - Windows on-prem flows still use legacy ENI binding; follow-up ticket ENG-4240 will add Windows support. - Edge-case overlap in extremely small CIDRs (/28) will surface a validation error; added preflight check to block allocation in those cases. - Observability: added allocator metrics (alloc_attempts, reconcile_duration) to the installer metrics bundle but we need dashboarding; tracking INF-1001. Related work: references to prior PRs that handled control-plane subnet handoff and conditional DNS (see SUP-3312). This PR also introduces a small migration helper CLI (bin/migrate_zonal_ips) that is gated by RBAC. Security review notes: adaptor performs least-privilege AWS calls (DescribeNetworkInterfaces, ModifyNetworkInterfaceAttribute, CreateTags) and we added an IAM policy template with minimal actions and a short expiry token recommendation for on-prem automation.
Evan Granger: Please add a migration dry-run flag and surface conflict counts in the log — we don't want surprises during customer rollouts.
Maya Patel: Added migrate_zonal_ips.dry_run and log summary with conflict_count and sample conflicted ENIs. PTAL.
Lena Ortiz: Can you scope the IAM policy tighter? Suggest removing CreateTags from the broad role and instead use a separate short-lived tagger role.
Maya Patel: Narrowed IAM policy and added a documented recommendation for a short-lived tagging role; included example in README.
Noah Kim: Integration harness looks good, but add a test for CIDR /28 validation to prevent runtime errors.
Maya Patel: Added preflight validation for minimum CIDR size and unit test in tests/unit/cidr_validation_test.go. Ready for final review.
Evan Granger: Approving after verifying that terraform plan shows no destructive changes when migrate_zonal_ips=false.
Lena Ortiz: Approved.

payload.body:
Motivation: Private control plane installs in highly restricted networks require tighter egress controls and predictable DNS resolution for service endpoints (Privatelink, resolver endpoints, and partner APIs). Customers frequently ask for a minimal, auditable egress path that enforces mTLS from control plane nodes and rewrites external FQDNs to private endpoints without wide-open SGs or brittle manual Route53 changes.

This PR introduces a small, opt-in egress assembly composed of a lightweight mTLS proxy (Envoy-based) provisioned behind an NLB and a DNS translation hook that manages Route53 Resolver rules and internal CNAME mappings for control-plane-facing hostnames. Key goals: minimize blast radius, provide clear upgrade/rollback semantics, and make the feature configurable from the installer (Terraform + Helm) with automated tests.

What changed (high level):
- Terraform: added vpc/modules/egress_proxy and updates to vpc/modules/endpoints to create an NLB, target group, IAM role for endpoint acceptance, and security group templates that lock down controlplane -> proxy and proxy -> privatelink flows. Module exposes `enable_mtls_proxy`, `allowed_external_cidrs`, and `resolver_outbound_ids` variables.
- Helm: new values under charts/controlplane/values-egress.yaml and a conditional sidecar injection template so control plane deployments can route outbound through the cluster-local proxy service. The proxy image is pinned and Health/Readiness probes are included.
- Installer orchestration: installer/terraform/upgrade-hooks/egress-dns-translation.sh (atomic upgrade hook) and installer/terraform/rollback-hooks/egress-dns-cleanup.sh. Hooks perform staged Route53Resolver rule creation, then validate by resolving a small set of canonical hostnames against the resolver outbound endpoints. Rollback reverses rule attachment if validation fails.
- Security: tightened SG rules and documented least-privilege IAM for cross-account endpoint acceptance; introduced an optional KMS envelope encryption key for proxy TLS materials.
- Tests: added integration terraform smoke harness under test/integration/egress-proxy that exercises provisioning in a sandbox account (mocked resolver + privatelink stubs). Also unit tests for the Helm template additions.

Files changed (high level): a small number of new modules + values + hooks; no changes to control plane internal APIs. See changed_files for specifics.

Checklist (PR owner):
- [x] Terraform module with sensible defaults and clear opt-in flag (`enable_mtls_proxy`)
- [x] Helm values + conditional templates for sidecar/proxy routing
- [x] Upgrade/rollback hooks with idempotent behavior and validation step
- [x] Security doc + least-privilege IAM snippets in docs/installer/security/egress-proxy.md
- [x] Integration smoke tests added and passing in CI
- [x] Reviewed and approved by SRE and Security

Rollout plan: Feature is behind opt-in flags; default installer does not enable the proxy. Recommend staged rollout: enable in a single non-prod region, run DNS validation (hook automates this), migrate control-plane components to route outbound through the proxy via Helm value change, then progressively enable in additional regions. Upgrades will run the upgrade hook which will create resolver rules and run the validation; rollback hook will revert rules on failure.

Backward compatibility and migration notes: If customers previously used broad 0.0.0.0/0 egress SGs, they must create the `allowed_external_cidrs` list or set `enable_mtls_proxy` to true and allow control plane nodes to reach the proxy NLB. The Helm injection is opt-in; without enabling the proxy, existing installs are unaffected.

Security considerations: TLS certificates for mTLS are generated per-install and optionally encrypted with customer KMS. Proxy enforces client cert verification for all outbound flows. IAM for endpoint acceptance is scoped to the installer account and documented.

Operational notes: Logs from the proxy are routed to the existing control plane log sink with a dedicated `egress-proxy` tag. Metrics exposed: connection_success, connection_errors, resolver_validation_success, resolver_validation_failures. Alerting guidance added to docs.

Why this is different from previous egress work: prior PRs focused on route allocation and NAT actors; this change provides an application-layer, auditable proxy plus an automated DNS translation/validation hook that reduces manual DNS surgery and supports strict mTLS controls required by regulated customers.

Adds an optional mTLS egress proxy and DNS translation hook for private control plane installs. Enables secure, auditable outbound connections from control plane nodes to vendor services without requiring broad SG egress. Includes Terraform modules, Helm chart values and an upgrade/rollback hook. Backwards compatible; enable via installer flags.
Arjun: Can we avoid a hard dependency on Route53 resolver so the hook can run in air-gapped installs?
Maya: The hook is split — resolver rule creation is conditional. If `resolver_outbound_ids` is empty, we skip resolver operations and rely on Helm CNAME rewrites; documented in the security doc.
Lena: IAM permissions look broad for endpoint acceptance. Please scope and add an example role trust policy.
Maya: Updated the TF module to create a role with a policy limited to `ec2:AcceptVpcEndpointConnections` on the specific endpoint ARNs; added example trust policy and tests.
Diego: Integration tests failed on the first runner due to timing on resolver propagation.
Maya: Added retry + validation step that polls resolver endpoints for 120s and included a forced sleep parameter for flaky sandboxes. Retested; CI green.
Arjun: Approving — left one nits re: variable naming in TF, addressed in follow-up commit.

Unit tests for Helm templates + integration terraform smoke test run in sandbox account. CI runs the terraform plan/apply in a short-lived sandbox and validates: (1) NLB health, (2) Envoy healthcheck, (3) resolver rules attached and DNS answers rewritten, (4) TLS handshakes succeed (mTLS). All checks pass in CI. Manual validation steps documented in docs/installer/security/egress-proxy.md.
Opt-in feature; no customer-facing breaking changes. Operational cost: small additional NLB per-region when enabled. Security posture improved for locked-down installs. Installer maintainers should add the new IAM role and KMS policy if the feature is enabled.
Follow-up work: (1) add support for OnPrem installs where customers provide an HTTP(S) outbound proxy instead of NLB, (2) automated migration helper that analyzes existing SGs and recommends minimal `allowed_external_cidrs`.

payload.body:
Problem: Private deployments run schema migrations during upgrades and customers have reported hard-to-reproduce downtime when migrations make irreversible changes. Existing tooling supports full migrations and snapshot-based rollbacks, but we lack a lightweight, repeatable dry-run and audit trail that operators can run against an isolated tenant snapshot or a simulated topology.

This PR introduces a migration dry-run harness and a federated migration plan that can be executed without touching live write paths, plus immutable migration-record objects for audit and safe rollback planning. Key goals: 1) let operators validate migration effects (row counts, FK integrity, index usage) against exported snapshots, 2) run plans in parallel across federated components (operator, control-plane DB, tenant DBs) and aggregate results, 3) provide an immutable record of what a migration DID or WOULD do so rollbacks and postmortems have a single source of truth.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds a migration-simulator sidecar container image and Kubernetes Job template (k8s/migration-dryrun-job.yaml) that runs migrations against a read-only, mounted snapshot volume or a Postgres logical replica. The simulator runs in a no-op mode that records SQL plan effects instead of applying destructive DDL when `DRY_RUN=true`.
- Introduces a new CRD `MigrationRecord` (api/v1alpha1/migrationrecord.yaml) that is immutable after creation. The operator writes a MigrationRecord for every dry-run and every real migration; records include a checksum of the migration artifact, the computed diff summary, and an operator-signed attestation blob.
- Adds a federated planner implementation (pkg/planner/federated_plan.go) that composes per-tenant and control-plane steps into an ordered execution graph, allowing dry-run execution to run in parallel where safe and to fail fast on schema drift. The planner emits a deterministic plan ID used to tie MigrationRecords together.
- Extends the installer CLI (`ri-installer migrate --dry-run`) to produce an exportable JSON report (artifacts/migration-reports/<plan-id>.json) and to optionally push the MigrationRecord into the cluster. The CLI includes a `--terraform-check` mode that runs `terraform plan` against generated infra diffs to detect resource drift that migrations might rely on.
Diego Alvarez: Nice separation of concerns; can we ensure MigrationRecord attestation is KMS-backed? Suggest adding optional KMS keyref in values.yaml.
Maya Chen (author): Added optional kmsKeyRef to helm values and the record controller now signs with the cluster KMS when present.
Priya Raman: Planner looks solid but add a stronger check for FK cascade semantics in the dry-run so we don't underestimate row-level effects.
Maya Chen (author): Added FK cascade check and an integration test that runs a simulated cascade on a 3-table fixture.
Ellen Park: CI flake on test TestPlannerParallelBranches; rerun fixed it, all green. Approving after tests pass.
Added migration dry-run harness, federated planning for upgrades, immutable MigrationRecord CRD, helm pre-upgrade dry-run hook, and optional terraform drift-check from the installer CLI.

payload.body:
Problem
Support/SE and on-prem operators currently have to run a full preflight (or hand-parse the bundle) to answer basic questions like: “What version is this bundle?”, “Is the manifest present?”, “Which signing key signed it?”, and “Did the offline transfer corrupt anything?”. For air-gapped environments, we need an offline-first diagnostic command that can be run on a laptop/jump host without starting an install.

What this PR does
Adds a new CLI subcommand: `redwood-private-installer bundle inspect <bundle-path>`.
The command is designed to be safe to run on a customer machine and produces a concise report that can be pasted into a Support ticket.

Capabilities
- Locate and load the bundle manifest (current: `bundle.manifest.json`; supports the existing legacy name `manifest.json` for pilot bundles).
- Validate manifest schema (required fields present; version fields parse; artifact entries have name/path/hash).
- Print versions/build identifiers (bundle version, build ID, chart appVersions, runtime/model artifact versions when present).
- Verify signature when present (reads signature sidecar `bundle.manifest.sig` when available; otherwise reports “unsigned” with guidance).
- Verify trust chain using the installer trust store by default; optionally allow `--trust-store <path>` for air-gapped key rollouts.
- Compute and compare sha256 for each artifact entry (streaming) to catch corruption after transfer.

CLI usage
- `redwood-private-installer bundle inspect ./redwood-private-bundle-2026.01.0.tgz`
- `redwood-private-installer bundle inspect ./bundle/ --json`
- `redwood-private-installer bundle inspect ./bundle/ --no-hash` (fast path for very large bundles)
- `redwood-private-installer bundle inspect ./bundle/ --trust-store ./trust-store.pem`

Example output (text)
Bundle: ./redwood-private-bundle-2026.01.0.tgz
Manifest: OK (schema v1)
Bundle version: 2026.01.0  Build ID: priv-2026.01.0+build.4121
Signer: key_id=RWDSIGN-2025Q4-01  status=TRUSTED  signature=VALID
Artifacts: 37 verified (sha256)
Charts: redwood-core=2026.01.0 redwood-observability=2026.01.0
Notes: No network access required. For tamper/corruption failures, re-transfer bundle and re-run with `--json` for Support.

Output format
- Default: human-readable, stable labels intended for copy/paste into tickets.
- `--json`: machine-readable output (intended for future “support bundle” integration), includes error_code and failure_reason when verification fails.

Failure modes / error taxonomy
The inspect command intentionally mirrors the preflight error taxonomy where possible.
- Missing manifest: exits non-zero with `BUNDLE_MANIFEST_MISSING`
- Manifest parse/validation error: `BUNDLE_MANIFEST_INVALID`
- Signature missing: exit code remains 0 (informational) unless `--require-signature` is set
- Signature invalid/untrusted: non-zero with `BUNDLE_SIGNATURE_INVALID` or `BUNDLE_SIGNING_KEY_UNTRUSTED`
- Hash mismatch: non-zero with `BUNDLE_ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH` and the offending path(s)

Security / privacy considerations
- No file contents are printed; only paths, sizes (optional), hashes, and version metadata.
- JSON output redacts absolute paths by default when the bundle is a directory (uses relative paths from bundle root).
- Does not attempt any outbound network calls (explicitly enforced by using only local filesystem readers).

Tests
- Golden tests for: valid signed bundle, unsigned bundle, missing manifest, invalid JSON, hash mismatch.
- Regression test for Windows path separators and spaces (pilot environments).

Docs
Adds a short CLI reference section under installer docs with troubleshooting examples for Support/SE.

Rollout
This is additive and safe. Support can start recommending `bundle inspect` immediately for air-gapped cases; preflight behavior is unchanged.

Related
- ENG-4826 (support tooling)
- PR #24844 (preflight signature verification)
- PR #24831 (manifest introduced)

Screenshots/logs
Included in comments below: sample output for both text and `--json`.

Checklist
- [x] Help text + examples
- [x] Unit tests + fixtures
- [x] Lint/format
- [x] Docs snippet
Ethan Park (review): The default behavior hashes all artifacts. For the larger pilot bundles this could be slow. Can we add a fast path / guardrails so Support doesn’t accidentally spend 20 minutes hashing a 200GB image tar?
Devon Price (author): Good call. Added `--no-hash` and also added a progress line every N files. Default remains hashing because it’s the most common failure after offline transfer, but I capped per-file read buffer and made hashing streaming.
Sean Gallagher (review): For on-call, please ensure error codes are stable and map cleanly to the preflight taxonomy. Also, print where the trust store was loaded from (embedded vs flag) so we can spot rotation issues.
Devon Price (author): Updated JSON output to include `trust_store_source` and `trust_store_key_ids`. Text output now includes a short “Trust store: embedded (2 keys)” line.
Marcus Lin (review): When signature is missing, should we exit non-zero? From a security posture perspective, I’d rather have this command make it obvious that “unsigned is not OK” going forward.
Devon Price (author): Added `--require-signature` to force non-zero on missing signature. Default remains informational to avoid breaking current pilot workflows and to keep inspect usable for debugging legacy bundles. We can flip default once migration is complete.
Dev Patel (review): Please add a copy/paste-friendly single-line summary for Support, plus a `--json` example in docs.
Devon Price (author): Done. Added “Summary:” line and expanded docs with both modes + troubleshooting guidance.
Ethan Park (approval): Looks good now. Thanks for the guardrails + `--require-signature` option.
Marcus Lin (approval): Approved with the condition that we track flipping defaults post-migration (filed follow-up in ENG).
Dev Patel (approval): Approved. This will materially reduce back-and-forth on SUP-31892-style cases.
Private installer CLI: add `bundle inspect` for offline bundle diagnostics (manifest, signature, versions, artifact hash verification).

Context: Private deployments require unambiguous artifact traceability across air-gapped and VPC installs. Current private-installer release objects contain multiple ad-hoc provenance links (SBOM, cosine signatures, bucket paths) that are hard to reconcile during upgrades and complicate automated rollback decisions. This PR introduces a release-metadata-generator service and a deterministic stamp that consolidates build provenance, signing metadata, and environment-specific deployment hints into a single release-metadata.json artifact for every private-installer CI build. Motivation: 1) Enable deterministic upgrade planning (compute a deterministic delta between released bundles). 2) Make rollback decisions machine-readable (contain fallback candidates, gating windows, KMS key IDs). 3) Reduce manual forensics after failed upgrades by surfacing canonical provenance at release time. What this PR does: - Add a release-metadata-generator binary invoked by the CI pipeline that:   * collects SBOM pointers, cosign/TUF attestations, and builder provenance (git ref, build image digest)   * computes a content-addressable stamp for the release bundle using SHA256 over a canonical manifest ordering   * emits release-metadata.json and an index.yaml entry that includes a canonical provenance URL and verifier hints - Injects release-metadata.json into the Helm chart packaging step and the terraform artifact index so private installer upgrades and the on-prem operator can reconcile artifacts atomically - Adds a lightweight validator (release-metadata-verify) used by preflight to verify signatures, KMS key IDs, and deterministic stamp before a staged upgrade - Updates the release CI to upload the release-metadata.json to the artifact registry and attach provenance links to the release Git tag Checklist: - [x] release-metadata-generator binary + unit tests - [x] CI integration (new job: publish-release-metadata) - [x] Helm chart packaging change to include metadata - [x] Terraform module index entry updated - [x] preflight verification hook - [x] docs: README for release metadata and verification usage Compatibility & security notes: - The stamp algorithm is versioned (v1) and documented in docs/release-metadata/README.md so future stamp formats can be introduced without breaking older installers. - Key IDs are recorded but no private keys or secrets are embedded in metadata. KMS/HSM key references are echoed as identifiers only. - Default CI behaviour is opt-in until the next scheduled release window to allow a canary rollout on a small set of clusters Migration plan: - New CI jobs will produce release-metadata.json alongside existing artifacts. - Private installer versions prior to the metadata-aware operator will ignore the extra file. - When the operator (v1.42) is rolled out, it will prefer releases with release-metadata.json for deterministic upgrades. Related: SUP-3142 (customer rollback debug), ENG-4291 (upgrade planner), SEC-92 (provenance policy).
1) 9f3a2b2 add release-metadata-generator binary and CI job
2) c1b4d5e integrate metadata into helm packaging and terraform index
3) 7a8f913 add release-metadata-verify preflight command and tests
4) 2b4c6fa docs: release metadata README and usage examples
+++ cmd/release-metadata-generator/main.go: added generator and canonicalizer (see computeStamp function)
@@ helm/redwood-private/templates/_release_metadata.tpl +++
{{- if .Values.release.metadata }}
  releaseMetadata: {{ .Files.Get "release-metadata.json" | quote }}
{{- end }}
+++ tools/ci/pipelines/publish-release-metadata.yaml: new CI job uploading release-metadata.json to artifact registry
Liam: Asked to make the stamp algorithm stable across available go versions; suggested using a stable JSON canonicalizer and adding explicit field ordering. Marisol: Flagged a potential race when multiple artifact uploaders tag the same release; requested idempotent upload semantics and a retry backoff. Evan: Asked for more unit tests around invalid or missing KMS key IDs; requested clearer error messages from release-metadata-verify. Author replies: implemented canonical JSON ordering, added a mutex to the upload step in CI, added 4 more unit tests and clearer errors. Final approval from Liam and Marisol after CI green.
Introduces release-metadata.json (v1) for private-installer releases. Adds CI job publish-release-metadata and preflight verification. Improves artifact traceability for deterministic upgrades and rollbacks. No behavioral changes for existing installers until operator v1.42 is deployed.
If a rollout shows mismatched stamps in preflight, check artifacts in the registry for missing release-metadata.json and confirm the CI publish-release-metadata job completed for the release tag. Use release-metadata-verify locally to validate stamp and KMS references.

Motivation: private installations need a way to integrate external KMS (cloud or on-prem HSM gateways) without forcing Vault-as-first-class and to keep TLS artifacts synchronized across namespaces during key rotation. This PR introduces two coordinated changes: 1) an optional installer hook that deploys a lightweight external-kms-plugin sidecar and Terraform snippets to register external KMS endpoints (KMS plugin config + policy templates); 2) a cert-sync-controller (Kubernetes controller) that watches KMS-backed key metadata and existing TLS secrets (including sealed-secrets-wrapped secrets) to perform automated, atomic certificate replacements across the cluster during rotation. Goals: reduce manual rotation steps for Private deployments, support customer-managed KMS/HSM, and provide a safe upgrade path with canaries and rollbacks. The description below outlines implementation details, migration plan, and risk mitigations. Implementation summary: - Installer/terraform: new optional module `external_kms` in terraform/ modules that wires up provider endpoints, validates TLS with provided CA bundle, and outputs Kubernetes Secret manifests for connector config. - Helm: chart changes add `externalKms.enabled` flag, sidecar container image references, RBAC rules for the cert-sync-controller, and a new `preupgrade` hook to validate existing TLS assets before applying new certs. - Controller: `cert-sync-controller` (Go) runs as a Deployment; it subscribes to a KMSConfig CRD and Secret events, uses signed key fingerprints to detect rotation candidates, generates CSR via local signer when allowed, and rotates target Secrets (supports sealed-secrets encrypted payloads by unlocking via the installer-provided sealing key). - Backwards compatibility: all changes are gated behind `externalKms.enabled=false` by default; controller is opt-in. - Rollout: default canary to 5% of nodes via nodeSelector + label-based canary, automated healthchecks (liveness/readiness + smoke requests) and automatic rollback on certificate validation failures. - Testing: unit tests for controller logic, integration e2e in the benchmark-lab that exercises a simulated KMS gateway, and manual on-prem validation (steps included in docs). See release notes + upgrade instructions below. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module with input/output docs - [x] Helm chart templates and hook - [x] CRD + controller implementation - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Operator RBAC and PSP/PodSecurity verification - [x] Docs and upgrade guide - [x] Canary rollout strategy and rollback hooks Related: builds on work in ENG-4000 (vault auto-unseal) and complements sealed-secrets automation (does not replace Vault). Security: we require KMS endpoints to authenticate via mTLS or a signed token; the installer will validate CA bundles and refuses to enable the controller if authentication tests fail. For sealed-secrets, controller will only decrypt using cluster sealing key provided explicitly by the admin during install (no implicit key retrieval). Migration notes: - Upgrading from 2.3 -> 2.4: operator will detect existing TLS secrets and run a dry-run validation; admin must approve the first rotation via the console or CLI. - Rollback: chart includes helm hooks which will restore previous Secret manifests (helm rollback) and controller will stop rotating if `externalKms.enabled=false`. Observability: new metrics (redwood_cert_sync_rotations_total, redwood_cert_sync_errors, redwood_kms_plugin_sync_latency) and tracing spans (controller reconcile) added to console dashboards. Rollout plan: stage to Dedicated beta clusters for 2 weeks, then enable canary for 5% of customer on-prem clusters with customer opt-in, gather telemetry, then full release. See release_notes for more details.
Ava Chen: Can the controller operate read-only (monitoring) mode? We should allow dry-run so customers can evaluate. -- Author: implemented a --dry-run flag and KMSConfig.dryRun boolean.
Diego Martinez: Ensure we don't leak secrets to logs during rotation. -- Author: scrubbed logs and added structured logging for event IDs only.
Priya Kapoor: How do we validate external KMS TLS bundles? Add a preflight check. -- Author: added terraform validation script and helm preupgrade hook that curls the endpoint with provided CA bundle.
Ava Chen: CI flake on e2e against mock-kms, please stabilize. -- Author: retried, added timeouts and deterministic mock responses; e2e now passes in CI.
Security review (Liam O'Neill): Verified mTLS config and sealed-secrets handling; recommended rotating the sealing key weekly for high-risk tenants. -- Author: documented recommendation in security notes.
- opt-in external KMS integration for Private installs (terraform + helm)
- cert-sync-controller to automate TLS secret rotation across namespaces (supports sealed-secrets)
- new metrics and dashboard panels for rotation observability
- upgrade notes and dry-run mode to validate before rotating

Motivation: Private installs need stronger tenant isolation for GPU node pools, predictable network allocation, and a safer tfstate migration path when moving from a single cluster tfstate to tenant-scoped state shards. This PR introduces two Terraform modules and a lightweight state-mapping helper: 1) gpu_nodepool_fence: opinionated GPU nodepool module that emits node pool resources with tenant-scoped IAM bindings, explicit taint/toleration templates, kubelet flags for node fencing, and optional preflight driver hooks. 2) iam_scoped_subnet_resolver: subnet allocator that resolves non-overlapping /24+/26 CIDR slices per tenant via claims and emits subnet attachment records and cross-account route table associations. 3) tfstate_mapper helper (input-only minimal module): generates a mapping file and migration plan to atomically split cluster-level TF state into tenant-sharded state buckets and produces an advisory plan for state move operations. Key design goals: tenant isolation (IAM least privilege), deterministic subnet assignment to avoid AZ-affinity drift, safe rollback surface (tfstate_mapper produces reversible plan), and minimal disruption to existing nodepool naming. Backwards compatibility: existing installs remain unchanged until operator applies the tfstate_mapper plan; the new modules are opt-in. This PR contains a migration README, example usage, unit tests for CIDR calculation, and e2e validation scripts that run terraform plan against a mock backend. See commits for details.
Liam Chen: Can we guarantee that the deterministic CIDR allocator will not produce collisions across parallel runs? Please add a collision-resilient check and retry policy.
Asha Raman: Added a simple reservation lease and a fast-forward check. The allocator now computes a hashed offset from tenant-id and probes for existing allocations before committing. Included unit tests that simulate parallel claims.
Marta Silva: Concerned about the tfstate migration being disruptive. We need a step-by-step plan and a reversible path if a move partially fails.
Asha Raman: Added tfstate_mapper README with a three-phase plan: dry-run (plan-only), staged copy to tenant bucket with state lock detection, and final state move with verified drift checks. Also included rollback commands and verification scripts.
Diego Alvarez: IAM roles look fine but we should scope the instance-profile role to a narrower permission set for node registration and kubelet bootstrap only.
Asha Raman: Tightened the IAM policy, removed broad ec2:Describe* calls, and documented required extra privileges for optional driver hooks.
Marta Silva: Please add an explicit opt-in flag in the private-installer chart values to switch to tenant-scoped subnets and nodepool fencing.
Asha Raman: Added values.yaml entry and updated the example in charts/private/values.yaml. Default remains disabled to avoid accidental flips during upgrades.
Introduces gpu_nodepool_fence and iam_scoped_subnet_resolver Terraform modules and a tfstate_mapper helper for tenant-sharded state. Opt-in migration path documented. Security: tighter IAM for node bootstrap. Note: Requires operator-driven migration; no automatic state moves.

Motivation: customers deploying Redwood Private with strict key custody requirements asked for an operator to manage HSM-backed key lifecycles (rotate asymmetric keys, publish certificate updates, reconcile PKCS#11 slots) without manual operator intervention. This PR delivers an opt-in controller (HSMRotationOperator), a Terraform provider wrapper to provision HSM objects and helper scripts, and Helm chart toggles + migration path for customers currently using KMS or Vault-wrapped keys.

What this change contains: consolidated changes across the installer, Helm chart and Terraform modules so users can provision keys (or point to existing PKCS#11 objects) and enable automatic rotation and certificate re-issuance. Key pieces: 1) controller/hsm-operator: a lightweight reconcile loop that watches HSMKey custom resources, triggers rotation within configured TTL, performs CRC checks on the public key material, and triggers a rolling secret update for components consuming the key. Operator supports PKCS#11 backends (SoftHSM for tests) and an HSM plugin interface for cloud HSMs and on-prem devices (YubiHSM2, Luna, Thales). 2) terraform/modules/hsm-pkcs11: module to create PKCS#11 objects via vendor-provider and to emit a redwood_hsm_key resource that the private installer can consume. 3) helm/redwood-private: new values.enableHsmOperator, values.hsm.providerConfig (base64 PKCS11 config or reference to sealed secret), and a new chart hook to create necessary CRDs. 4) migration helper scripts under tools/hsm-migration that translate existing KMS/Vault keys into HSMKey CRs with validation and dry-run mode.

Upgrade/migration path: default behavior is no-op; operator is disabled by default. To opt in: update Helm values to enable the operator, install the Terraform module (or point to existing PKCS#11 config), and run tools/hsm-migration migrate --dry-run to validate resources. For clusters using Vault-wrapped keys, the migration script supports a key-wrap-to-pkcs11 flow where it exports wrapped key material into an intermediate sealed secret, then asks operator to unwrap into HSM via vendor provider. We include a recommended canary rollout: enable operator in a single control-plane node pool, run key sync for one service, and watch telemetry for signing errors for 48h.

Security considerations: operator runs with least privilege RBAC only to HSMKey CRs and secrets in the installer namespace. Terraform provider credentials should be stored as sealed-secrets; Helm supports specifying sealedSecrets.enabled=true to keep provider credentials encrypted. HSM access uses PKCS#11 and requires explicit mounting of device sockets (documented). All networked HSM traffic is recommended to be routed inside a private VPC.

Testing & verification: adds unit tests for operator reconciliation, integration tests using SoftHSM in GitHub CI, and an e2e which deploys a tiny TLS-terminating demo service that rotates its certs every 24h (simulated). CI was flaky on first run due to SoftHSM image pull; fixed in commit that pins test image to retry policy.

Operational notes: operator writes rotation events to the new metric redwood_hsm_rotate_total and emits a span with tags hsm.vendor and hsm.key_id for tracing. We also add an alert template in observability/alerts to catch failed rotations >3 tries. Rollback: operator has a safe-backoff and a 'revert-to-old-key' flag on the HSMKey CR which will copy previous key version back to the consuming secret. See notes_on_rollback for more details.

Files of interest and examples are listed below; small config snippet to show Helm values usage: 
values.yaml snippet: 
  enableHsmOperator: true
  hsm:
    provider: pkcs11
    providerConfig: "base64:LS0tUEtDUyMxMS1jb25maWcn..."

Related: ENG-1342 for operator design, SEC-241 for threat model review.
Adds a new HSM rotation operator (optional) and Terraform PKCS#11 provider module. Backwards compatible; opt-in via Helm value enableHsmOperator=true. See upgrade notes for migration steps.
Diego: Can we support existing Vault-wrapped keys without exposing raw material?
Amina: Yes — the migration script supports wrapped export and storing as sealed-secret; operator unwraps into HSM using vendor agent.
Priya: Please add unit tests for revert-to-old-key logic and ensure RBAC scope is minimal.
Amina: Added unit tests and tightened RBAC to only watch HSMKey and secrets in the redwood-operator namespace.
Marcus: CI failed on first run (SoftHSM image pull). Marcus: Approve after CI green.
Amina: Rebased and fixed image pinning; CI passed.
Diego: Approved.
Merge: squash
Operator supports revert-to-old-key boolean on HSMKey CR. For full rollback, set revert-to-old-key=true and operator will copy previous key version to the consuming secret and trigger rolling restart of dependent deployments. Terraform changes are additive; to rollback provider-managed PKCS#11 objects use terraform state rollback. If Helm upgrade fails, run helm rollback release --namespace redwood-private <revision>. Manual steps for emergency rollback are documented in docs/private/hsm-operator.md.
Added HSMRotationOperator (opt-in), Terraform pkcs11 module, Helm flags to enable HSM support, and migration tooling. Backwards compatible and disabled by default.

Motivation: Private deployments need low-risk upgrade paths for multi-tenant clusters. Existing tooling focuses on global dry-runs and snapshot-based rollbacks; this PR adds a lightweight tenant-canary migrator that runs a staged schema/apply workflow against a small tenant slice, a downgrade-simulation harness to validate backwards compatibility of migrations, and a Terraform preflight state-consistency checker that prevents plan application if remote state drift is detected.

Summary of changes: Adds a new operator component (tenant-canary-migrator) that can be configured via Helm to select tenant namespaces by label and execute a two-phase migration: (1) apply compatibility shims and non-breaking changes; (2) run a canary migration job with validation probes; only after canary success will the controller promote to bulk rollout. Introduces downgrade-sim.sh (e2e harness) that replays migration steps against a snapshot of production data in a fenced test namespace to verify downgrade safety. Adds terraform/state-checker module to fail early on unexpected remote state modifications (useful for airgapped installs where state drift is a common source of failed upgrades). Includes docs/upgrade-playbook.md describing runbooks and operator flags.

Design notes: - Tenant canary selection: controller supports two selectors: label-based inclusion and percentage fence. The operator patches the HelmRelease CR (or equivalent) to deploy a migration JobTemplate and waits for user-defined validation probes (HTTP, DB smoke tests, and Redwood-specific evals). - Two-phase apply: compatibility shims (feature flags + compatibility-configmap) are applied first so runtime can tolerate partial schema changes. - Downgrade sim: the harness spins up a quarantined namespace, restores a compressed snapshot, runs the migration forward, then attempts an instrumented downgrade and checks for data integrity and invariant violations. Output is a standardized report consumed by the console. - Terraform preflight: checks provider versions, last-apply commit id in state metadata, and detects suspicious manual resource changes; it fails with actionable messages.

Rollout plan: shipped behind Helm flag values.migration.canary.enabled=false by default. Staged rollout: enable canary on a single cluster in canary region -> 48h observation -> enable on 10% tenant slices -> bulk. Operators default to dry-run for first 24h per cluster to gather telemetry.

Testing: unit tests for controller reconciliation (operator/migrator_test.go), integration that runs downgrade-sim in CI (makes use of mock snapshots), and terraform module tests using tfenv in CI matrix. e2e uses a new lightweight snapshot fixture.

Checklist:
- [x] Add operator and controller logic with reconciliation loop
- [x] Helm values and templating for optional activation and RBAC scopes
- [x] Terraform preflight module and docs
- [x] Downgrade simulation harness and e2e test
- [x] Console report schema and a simple JSON consumer

Commits summary: - "operator: add tenant canary controller with two-phase flow" (migrator.go, reconciler) - "helm: values and templates for canary migrator and job templates" (helm/templates/migration-job.yaml, values.yaml) - "terraform: add state-consistency preflight module" (terraform/modules/state-checker/main.tf) - "e2e: add downgrade-sim harness and fixtures" (test/e2e/downgrade-sim.sh) - "docs: publish upgrade-playbook and troubleshooting notes" (docs/upgrade-playbook.md)

Changed files (high level): - operator/migrator.go - operator/migrator_test.go - helm/values.yaml - helm/templates/migration-job.yaml - terraform/modules/state-checker/main.tf - terraform/modules/state-checker/README.md - test/e2e/downgrade-sim.sh - docs/upgrade-playbook.md - console/reporting/migration-report-schema.json

Small illustrative snippet (helm/templates/migration-job.yaml): "apiVersion: batch/v1\nkind: Job\nmetadata:\n  name: {{ include \"fullname\" . }}-migration-canary\nspec:\n  template:\n    spec:\n      containers:\n      - name: migrator\n        image: {{ .Values.migration.image }}\n        args: [\"--run-canary\", \"--validation-probes={{ .Values.migration.probes }}\"]"

Backwards compatibility: operator gracefully no-ops if migration CRs are absent and all new resources are behind feature flags. Terraform module is additive and returns non-zero exit codes only when inconsistencies are found.

Release notes: "Add tenant canary migrator, downgrade simulation harness, and terraform preflight state checks to reduce upgrade blast radius for private deployments."
Connor Blake (reviewer): Can we make the canary selector deterministic across controller restarts? The label+percentage approach may flip tenants if the controller is rescheduled. Suggested: derive a stable hash from tenant namespace and a cluster salt.
Leila Mendoza (author): Thanks, Connor. Implemented stable-hash selection (see operator/migrator.go commit a1f4b2c). Added a cluster-salt Helm value and unit tests that exercise restart scenarios.
Sofia Ramesh (reviewer): Terraform state-checker is very helpful. Two asks: clearer error codes for API retries, and a short circuit mode that only emits warnings in dry-run clusters.
Leila Mendoza (author): Added retry classification and --warn-only flag to the module per Sofia's suggestion. Documented behavior in terraform/modules/state-checker/README.md.
Ethan Wu (reviewer): Downgrade simulation is great. We should gate execution in CI to a separate workflow because it needs snapshot fixtures and can be flaky in shared runners.
Leila Mendoza (author): Split the e2e into a dedicated workflow (migration-downgrade-sim.yml). CI now toggles using an image-based fixture to reduce flakiness.
payload.title: Introduce tenant canary migrator, downgrade-sim harness, and preflight state-checker

Add a new egress firewall operator for control plane subnets and an idempotent subnet migration operator. Backwards compatible toggle via helm values; includes Terraform module updates and an automated staged rollback path.
Context: Customers deploying Redwood Private at scale have run into intermittent egress path mismatches during control plane upgrades and subnet reclaim operations. This causes transient API reachability problems (control plane -> control plane egress) when route tables or NAT attachments are changed during upgrades. Motivation: provide a safe, observable, and reversible path to (1) install an egress firewall for control plane subnets, (2) migrate control plane workloads between subnets with minimal blast radius, and (3) automate rollback when reachability or health checks fail. This PR contains three coordinated deliverables: 1) an operator (installer/controllers/egress_firewall_controller.go) that reconciles host-route-based firewall rules and controls per-subnet egress ACLs with safe staging, 2) a subnet-migration operator (installer/controllers/subnet_migrator.go) that performs drain/attach/validation cycles when moving control plane instances between subnets, and 3) Terraform/Helm surface to enable the features and a staged rollout plan documented in installer/README.md. Design notes: - Staging model: feature is disabled by default. Enabling requires helm value private.egress.enabled=true and terraform var enable_egress_operator=true. - Safety: operators implement a two-phase commit for route updates (prepare -> switch -> validate -> finalize). If any validation probe fails, operator reverts to previous route and signals rollback. Validation probes include HTTPS /health checks to each control plane IP, route-table consistency checks, and synthetic traffic through the egress path. - Observability: emits metrics (controlplane.egress.switch_count, controlplane.egress.rollback_count, controlplane.subnet_migration.duration_ms) and structured audit logs with pre/post diffs for route/NACL/ENI changes. - Rollback: a /rollback job can be triggered via CR annotation or CLI; operator will run deterministic revert steps and post an incident annotation. - Upgrade choreography: includes a small upgrade hook that sequences the operator rollout with Terraform apply and Helm upgrade to avoid TOCTOU issues. Checklist: - [x] Operator core reconcile loop + unit tests - installer/controllers/*_test.go - [x] Terraform module update: terraform/modules/controlplane/egress.tf - [x] Helm chart templates + values: helm/redwood-private/templates/egress-firewall.yaml and values.yaml default=false - [x] Integration test harness exercises staged switch and rollback in perf-canary cluster - [x] Docs: installer/README.md with rollout/rollback steps and risk matrix - [x] Observability: metrics + opentracing spans - [x] Security review: minimal IAM surface for operator (assume role to modify route tables, ENIs) Known limitations / future work: - Does not yet support cross-account route table ownership (follow-up ENG-4012). - BGP-based on-prem egress is out of scope for this PR. Related: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3921/control-plane-egress-operator, terraform module family update ENG-3958.
Diego: Overall looks good; please make the prepare phase idempotent and add a safety timeout.
Aisha: Added idempotency checks and a configurable timeout (5m default) in egress_firewall_controller.go.
Riley: Can the validator include an application-layer GET to /health instead of TCP-only? Risk of false-positive.
Aisha: Added HTTPS health probe with retry policy and documented probe time cost in README.
Priya: Add a test that simulates a route-table propagation delay and ensure rollback triggers.
Aisha: Added integration test 'egress_rollback_on_route_delay' in ci/integration and mocked propagation delay in harness.
Diego: Approved after fixes. Riley: Approved. Priya: Approved.
Merge choreography: squashed into a single commit, merged on main after green CI and a short wait window for engineering on-call to observe metrics.

Add a GPU tiling Terraform module that provides tenant-scoped GPU subpools and a complementary ephemeral IAM profile for node bootstrap, and replace the existing subnet-claim controller wiring with a v2 interface. Motivation: current monolithic GPU pool modules made tenant isolation and incremental rollout brittle for large private deployments. This change splits nodepool topology into a tiling primitive (gpu_tiling) that composes AZ/instance-type tiles, introduces ephemeral IAM profiles to limit long-lived credentials attached to GPU nodes, and upgrades the subnet claim integration to an explicit v2 contract (claim lifecycle hooks, status field schema). The PR includes migration helpers and a rollback path. Migration notes: operators should run the included plan-generator to produce an ordered apply sequence per-tenant; ephemeral IAM requires a short-lived credential issuer (documented in deploy/ephemeral-iam/README) and a one-time KMS policy update. Rollout strategy: canary apply to a single tenant and AZ, validate scheduling and node bootstrap for 24h, then progressively apply remaining tiles. Rollback: revert to legacy module by running the reverse plan from migration helper; ephemeral roles are guarded by a feature flag. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-4719) - [x] module unit tests and terratest harness - [x] backwards-compatible variable defaults for legacy stacks - [x] migration helper script included - [x] e2e on k3s and GKE staging. Related tickets: Linear ENG-4719, ENG-4890. This description is a single continuous string per repo conventions.

Motivation: Private control plane peering and endpoint automation must fail-safe when customer VPCs have overlapping CIDRs or when peering would expose sensitive subnets. This PR introduces a plan-time and apply-time CIDR overlap detector and a configurable safety policy that prevents automatic peering attachments when a risky overlap is detected. The change adds: 1) a terraform pre-apply validation module that runs CIDR intersection checks and emits structured diagnostics; 2) installer controller logic to switch to a 'safe-attach' mode which will mark peering for manual review rather than auto-create attachments when the detector flags overlap; 3) a Helm flag enableCidrSafety=false/true to toggle strict enforcement for upgrades; 4) a dry-run output mode that surfaces the actionable diff (affected subnets, overlapping ranges, suggested prefix remaps) without making changes; 5) audit log entries and an explanatory message that surfaces in the console when a control plane rollouts fails due to safety checks. Migration notes: default behavior for existing installs is a non-blocking warning unless helm value enableCidrSafety is set to true in the chart override. For customers who want strict enforcement we document the downstream steps to reconcile overlaps (subnet renaming, prefixlist remapping, or transit gateway fallback). Implementation highlights: terraform/modules/vpc/overlap_check.tf implements the plan hook using a new null_resource local-exec step and returns structured output via tf output; installer/controllers/peering_controller.go now evaluates the detector outcome and atomically annotates controlplane objects with safety.status and safety.reason; helm/values/controlplane.yaml adds enableCidrSafety and dryRunSafetyMode flags; tests/integration/overlap_integration_test.go covers plan-time and controller rejection paths with mocked remote accounts; examples/upgrade-notes.md documents the step-by-step rollback if an upgrade flips enforcement on. Testing and rollout: ran tf validate and plan against three customer-like fixtures and a staging account, added unit coverage for the overlap algorithm including IPv4/IPv6 mixed ranges, added e2e smoke that verifies the annotated reason appears in the console. Rollout strategy: feature gate off by default; enable in a canary subset of internal customers for 2 weeks then flip for GA. Edge cases and fallbacks: when overlap is flagged and strict mode is on the controller will not create peering attachments, but will propose a fallback route via transit gateway or leave the existing peering intact and mark the new request for human review; the CLI offers --force-unsafe to bypass checks with an audited justification appended to the audit log. Security and compliance: Intersection checks reduce accidental exposure across customer boundaries and generate evidence for audits. Performance: plan-time check adds negligible overhead (ms-scale for typical VPC ranges). See linked Linear ENG-4231 for the design doc. Checklist: [x] design doc attached [x] tf module tests [x] controller unit tests [x] integration smoke tests [x] helm values and docs updated [x] security review requested. See release_notes for operator-facing details and migration guidance.
Diego Chen: Please add a short-circuit for the common case where the peer VPC is explicitly whitelisted; otherwise we risk unnecessary manual reviews.
Ava Martinez (author): Added a whitelist override (helm value peerWhitelist) and documented auditing implications; updated tests to include whitelist path.
Priya Nair: Can we ensure the controller emits a single canonical reason string for alerts so SLO alerts can filter reliably?
Ava Martinez: Normalized reason codes to safety_reason_{OVERLAP|PRIVATE_RANGE|MIXED_IP_VERSION} and added unit tests asserting canonical reasons.
Samir Patel: Terraform plan-time check currently uses local-exec which won't run in remote plan contexts in some CI. Can we add a pure-Terraform validation path?
Ava Martinez: Added a fallback pure-Terraform math check using cidrhost/cidrsubnet where possible; retained local-exec for richer diagnostic output in local dev environments.
Hannah Li: Security review: request log redaction of account IDs in console messages. Also confirm no secrets are written to logs.
Ava Martinez: Redaction implemented; logs now use account masks and we explicitly avoid writing KMS or token material. Security review OKayed the change.
Priya Nair: Approved on behalf of infra team; please squash and merge once CI passes.
Operator-facing: Add helm flag controlplane.enableCidrSafety (default: false). When enabled, control plane provisioning will block automatic peering attachments on detected CIDR overlaps and require manual review. Use examples/upgrade-notes.md to reconcile overlaps prior to enabling. CLI: new command 'redwoodctl controlplane plan-safety-check' produces a dry-run report. Backwards compatible when flag is unset.
During upgrade that flips enableCidrSafety from false to true, run redwoodctl controlplane plan-safety-check against each customer account to detect and remediate overlaps before enabling. If overlaps are found, follow docs/operator/migration-cidr-safety.md. The helm chart ships with a one-time postinstall hook that can run the check in dry-run mode; do not enable the hook in mass upgrades without a planned remediation window.
Unit tests added for 4 overlap scenarios, integration test simulates cross-account peering with overlap and verifies controller annotates and does not create attachments, e2e smoke ensures audit logs are emitted with redacted account IDs. Manual verification: run terraform apply with TF_VAR_dry_run=true and confirm diagnostics file is produced.

Context: customers running Redwood Private in complex VPC topologies have asked for a way to route control-plane egress through short-lived, auditable nexthops (ENIs/ephemeral NAT targets) to reduce blast radius during upgrades and to provide deterministic routing for IAM/Route53 forwarding. This PR introduces an ephemeral nexthop orchestrator in the installer and a companion Route53 "DNS safelist" mechanism that stages DNS outbound endpoints and limits TTL exposure during controlled switchover.
Motivation: (1) enable safe, staged control plane egress migration across AZs/accounts, (2) provide a fast rollback path that avoids long DNS TTL propagation, (3) improve security by narrowing SG scopes to ephemeral nexthops and recording ephemeral credentials in audit logs.
Summary of changes:
- Terraform: new module network/ephemeral-nexthop that provisions an ENI-backed nexthop, EIP attachment, IAM role for the installer agent, and tags used for lifecycle reconciliation.
- Installer operator (Go): added a reconciler that creates nexthop resources, assigns SGs based on policy templates, and emits provenance events to the control-plane audit sink. The reconciler supports a "staged" lifecycle (provision -> drain -> swap -> cleanup).
- Helm charts: added values.controlplane.nexthop and an optional preflight job chart to validate egress path and DNS behavior.
- Route53 tooling: implement a DNS safelist controller that creates temporary outbound endpoints and manages a small Route53 record-set swap (low TTL priming, atomic CNAME flip).
- Tests & CI: integration tests in perf-canary that simulate switchover, unit tests for the reconciler, and a Terraform plan check in CI.
Checklist:
- [x] Add Terraform module and docs
- [x] Implement reconciler + helm values
- [x] Add unit and integration tests
- [x] Manual QA in staging (AZ failover + peering teardown scenario)
- [x] Security review for IAM/SG changes
Rollout plan:
1) Deploy module with Helm values disabled (no-op) to ensure no drift.
2) Enable module in a single staging region and run the preflight job.
3) Execute staged switchover with traffic mirroring and monitor console metrics/traces.
4) If safe, enable in production with canary subset of control-plane nodes.
Rollback notes: reconcilers keep ownership tags and will revert to previous nexthop if swap fails; DNS safelist controller reverts CNAMEs and shortens TTL to accelerate rollback. See notes_on_rollback below for details.
CI: initial run failed on plan due to missing IAM trust for the installer agent; fixed by adding a narrowly scoped assume-role policy and re-ran CI.
Merge outcome: squash merge after security and infra approvals.
Related Linear items: ENG-3187 (nexthop orchestration), ENG-3219 (DNS safelist), ENG-3223 (release rollouts).
Ravi Patel: Please narrow the installer-agent assume-role policy to only List/Attach/Describe for the ENI resources. Also add a unit test for tag collision handling.
Author (Alexandra Chen): Addressed — policy trimmed, added TestTagCollision to reconciler_test.go and documented the expected ownership tag format.
Maria Gomez: The DNS safelist controller should default to TTL=30s for priming records to reduce propagation risk. Can we make TTL configurable?
Author (Alexandra Chen): TTL is now configurable via values.controlplane.nexthop.dnsPrimeTTLSeconds with default 30. Updated docs and Helm values.
Jordan Kim: Can we add a metric for the number of active ephemeral nexthops and expose it in the console?
Author (Alexandra Chen): Added prometheus gauge installer_nexthop_active_count and wired chart to expose metric in Redwood Console.

Motivation: Private installer customers asked for a safer, auditable way to rotate signing keys stored in HSMs and to automate certificate refreshes without application downtime. This PR implements an auxkey rotation controller that orchestrates staged HSM key rollovers, integrates with Vault transit (or PKCS11 plugins), and provides Helm + Terraform primitives and upgrade hooks so operators can adopt automated rotations with rollback safety.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds `signing-auxkey-controller` binary (k8s controller) that: performs staged key generation, publishes new public material to a configurable endpoint, triggers certificate reissue via the cert-proxy sidecar, and performs a coordinated switchover once signatures verify.
- Helm chart changes: a new `cert-proxy` sidecar template, pre/postupgrade hooks for key-sync and cache-warm, and a `postrender` helper to inject PKCS11 configuration for air-gapped installs.
- Terraform module `tf/kms/grantset` to create policy bindings between tenant service accounts and KMS/HSM roles (works with both cloud KMS and on-prem HSM gateways).
- Migration tool `sealed-to-vault` (lightweight CLI) to convert existing sealed-secrets blobs to Vault-wrapped keys, with a dry-run flag.
- Upgrade/rollback tooling: preflight checks, staged canary policy, and a rollback path that reverts to the previous auxkey and triggers a certificate reissue.
- End-to-end tests: small e2e harness that runs against the `mini-hsm` simulator used in CI and a manual test plan included for on-prem customers.

Checklist:
- [x] Controller core logic + unit tests
- [x] Helm templates and hooks
- [x] Terraform module and examples
- [x] Migration helper CLI + docs
- [x] E2E tests against mini-hsm simulator
- [x] Security review and threat model notes attached (ENG-6128)

Commits summary:
- feat(controller): initial auxkey rotation controller scaffold and reconciliation loop
- feat(helm): add cert-proxy sidecar, hooks, and values schema updates
- feat(tf): add kms grantset module and example binding for installer cluster role
- feat(migration): sealed-to-vault CLI with --dry-run and --apply
- test(e2e): add mini-hsm e2e job and CI workflow integration
- docs: key-ceremony plan, operator guide, rollback steps

Files changed (high level):
- cmd/signing-auxkey-controller/main.go (new)
- internal/rotations/* (controller reconciliation + helpers)
- charts/installer/templates/_cert-proxy.tpl (new), templates/hooks/pre-upgrade-key-sync.yaml (new), values.schema.json (updated)
- terraform/kms/grantset/main.tf (new), examples/grantset/README.md (new)
- tools/sealed-to-vault/main.go (new)
- test/e2e/mini-hsm/* (new harness and fixtures)
- docs/operator/key-ceremony.md (new), docs/operator/rollback-guide.md (updated)

Review thread summary: 
- Diego Alvarez: asked for stronger idempotency guarantees around the controller's switchover path and requested an explicit leader-election backstop to avoid dual-active signing. Noted this was critical for multi-AZ installs.
- Maya Chen (author): responded with design note and added leader-election via existing controller-runtime leader election; added a `switchoverLock` sanity check to ensure only one controller instance performs final cutover.
- Priya Natarajan: requested test coverage for the migration CLI and that the CLI refuse to apply conversions when the Vault config is incomplete. Author added dry-run and validation checks plus unit tests.
- Elliot Brooks: security review asked to document audit events emitted and to ensure that private key material never leaves the HSM path in logs. Author added structured events (no key material) and sanitized logging.
- CI: initial run showed flaky e2e due to mini-hsm timing; adjusted probe timings and re-ran, which passed. One lint failure for helm schema was fixed in a follow-up commit.
- Review outcome: Diego approved after leader-election change, Priya approved after tests added, Elliot gave final security approval.

CI summary: initial failure (flaky e2e) -> fix timing -> rerun -> all checks passed (unit, lint, helm-chart-lint, e2e-mini-hsm). Integration tests passed with a note about increasing the default probe timeout for air-gapped environments.

Operational notes / runbook extract: 
- Default rotation interval: off by default. Operator can enable via values: rotations.enabled=true and configure `rotationWindow` and `canaryPercentage`.
- Rollback: controller stores previous auxkey fingerprint in a k8s secret `rotation-history/<name>` and will attempt automated rebind; if automated rollback fails, run `sealed-to-vault --rollback --name <release>` to restore envelopes.
- Audit: controller emits events to k8s audit sink and writes structured entries to the installer log (no private material).

Migration guidance: run `sealed-to-vault --dry-run` and inspect output; apply only after Vault transit path and KMS grants are verified. Example Terraform snippet included in examples/grantset.

Security considerations: the controller supports two KMS backends: Vault transit and PKCS11 HSM gateway. PKCS11 requires a secure mount and the Helm `postrender` hook ensures the node-level PKCS11 config is injected only when `values.hsm.enabled=true`. The controller enforces a maximum age for auxkeys and requires operator acknowledgement for rotations that cross account boundaries.

Why this is different from previous rotation work: existing PRs focused on rotating primary signer keys or automating unseal. This change introduces a short-lived auxiliary signing key pattern (auxkey) to make rollovers less risky, plus a cert-proxy sidecar to decouple certificate issuance from application lifecycle and explicit Terraform grantsets to bridge cloud and on-prem KMS semantics.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-6135: expand e2e matrix to test hardware-backed HSMs in CI lab (next sprint)
- Add Prometheus metrics for rotation state transitions (PR follow-up planned)

Merge: Squash-merged into main on 2026-02-26 after final approvals.
Introduce a new controller to automate staggered auxiliary key (auxkey) rotations against PKCS#11-backed HSMs and Vault transit. Adds Helm chart changes to deploy a cert-proxy sidecar and Terraform module to bind KMS policies + grant sets. Includes rolling upgrade/rollback hooks and migration helpers for sealed secrets to Vault-backed envelopes.

Context and motivation: Private deployments need consistent, deterministic allocation of GPU nodepools across tenants while preserving immutability in IAM role configuration for auditability. Current tenant lease allocation can drift when nodes are recreated or TF state is sharded, causing tenant-to-node affinity regressions and noisy autoscaler behavior. This PR introduces a new Terraform module that provides a deterministic `lease_index` allocator for GPU nodepools and an IAM role templating system that creates immutable role versions with automated rotation hooks.

What this PR does: 1) Adds module `tfmodules/gpu_lease_index` implementing a lease-index allocation strategy that: computes a stable index for tenant leases based on tenant-id hashing + ordered subnet slices; emits outputs consumed by the nodepool provisioning module to ensure stable assignment even during partial applies and state sharding. 2) Adds module `tfmodules/iam_role_template` which renders IAM role artifacts as immutable-versioned resources (role_v1, role_v2) and wires a controlled rotation mechanism via a small controller job (K8s Job manifest + preflight plan) that can be driven by `private-installer upgrade`. 3) Provides a migration tool `scripts/tfstate-lease-index-migrate` (dry-run + apply modes) to compute and persist lease_index mappings into a new state namespace, with safety checks and a --rollback snapshot option. 4) Adds tagging for GPU nodepool instances to surface lease_index and role_version for drift detection and reconciler diagnostics. 5) Updates Helm hooks in `charts/private-installer` to add post-upgrade validation for IAM rotations and nodepool tag presence.

Design notes: - Lease index derivation uses a stable HMAC(nonce=deployment-id, key=infra-hash) truncated to the pool size to ensure stable ordering across applies. The TF module exposes both `lease_index` and `lease_salt` so downstream modules can detect mismatches and trigger safe rebinds. - IAM role templating intentionally creates new role resources instead of in-place edits; the rotation controller sequences traffic to roles by annotating service accounts, running preflight checks, then promoting a new version, and finally deleting the old role only when safe. - The migration tool does not alter live node labels; it only writes the lease_index mapping into the TF state file and produces a reconciliation plan for the installer to apply.

Commits: ["a1b9f7c add gpu_lease_index module and unit tests", "b4d3e82 add iam_role_template module and rotation job manifest", "f7c2a10 add tfstate-lease-index-migrate script with dry-run", "e3f9b5a update helm chart hooks for post-upgrade validation", "c9d0aa4 add nodepool tagging and reconciler metrics", "d2f8f4b docs: migration and rollout notes"]

Files changed (high level): ["tfmodules/gpu_lease_index/main.tf", "tfmodules/gpu_lease_index/outputs.tf", "tfmodules/gpu_lease_index/README.md", "tfmodules/iam_role_template/main.tf", "tfmodules/iam_role_template/rotation-job.yaml", "scripts/tfstate-lease-index-migrate", "charts/private-installer/templates/post-upgrade-validation.yaml", "charts/private-installer/values.schema.json", "modules/nodepool/attach_tags.tf", "modules/nodepool/README.md", "docs/private-deploy/migration-lease-index.md", "tests/lease_index/unit_tests.go"]

Testing and CI: - Unit tests for lease-index math (Go) and TF unit-style checks included; added integration test to create a two-tenant private deployment and assert stable assignment across repeated applies with shuffled state shards. - CI initially failed due to a lint rule on HCL variable naming; fixed and re-ran. Final CI run: all checks passed (plan acceptance, fmt, terratest, unit).

Review thread summary: - Arun: requested explicit docs on operator runbook for manual rotation fallback; added `docs/private-deploy/iam-rotation-runbook.md` and a small CLI helper. - Sophie: asked to add a preflight check that verifies service account annotation propagation; added contract test and Helm hook. - Mateo: flagged potential permission escalation during rotation; updated IAM policies to require `iam:PassRole` only scoped to role_version resource names and added audit logging. - Reviewer approvals: Arun approved after runbook added, Sophie approved after tests; Mateo requested one follow-up (see TODO).

Migration plan and rollout: 1) Run `scripts/tfstate-lease-index-migrate --dry-run` in staging to preview mappings. 2) Apply mapping with `--apply` to write to a new state namespace (non-destructive) and run `private-installer upgrade --validate`. 3) Observe reconciler metrics: if any tenant reports lease mismatch, the reconciler will temporarily create a shadow nodepool and migrate workloads before deleting the old nodepool (safe by default). 4) IAM rotation: default is manual and gated; operator can run `private-installer iam rotate --role <template> --promote` which triggers the rotation job. A fully-automated rollout is behind a feature flag.

Rollback: - The migration tool produces a snapshot file that can be used to revert state; the `--rollback` flag re-applies the snapshot into TF backend. - IAM rotation includes a rollback path: the controller keeps the previous role until operator confirms traffic has drained.

Risk and mitigation: - Risk: mismatch between lease_index and live node labels during partial apply. Mitigation: tagging + reconciler detection; migration initially run in dry-run and then staged apply; daily reconciliation window during first week. - Risk: accidental role deletion. Mitigation: immutable role versions retained for 7 days by default and deletion requires explicit operator approval recorded in the runbook.

Follow-ups and TODO: - ENG-7460: automated promotion pipeline for IAM rotation (epic). - Add metrics for lease_index churn to SLO dashboards. - Lightweight UI in Console for lease mapping visualization (product ticket).

Merge outcome: merged via squash after approvals and CI green.

Motivation: private/on‑prem installs sometimes fail during the tenant seed/migration phase due to transient DB contention or network flakiness (airgapped pulls, registry bursts). This PR introduces two complementary changes to make installs and upgrades more resilient without changing defaults: 1) a layered values overlay mechanism that lets the installer apply environment-specific overrides (airgap, restricted-network, high-concurrency) on top of chart values; 2) a backoff-aware, idempotent seed/init job implementation with controlled retries and install-phase markers so a failed run can be resumed safely.

What this change does (single-string body): - Adds chart/values.schema.json additions for `seed` and `overlay` namespaces (seed.retryPolicy, seed.maxRetries, seed.backoffSeconds, overlay.profiles). The overlay system supports a simple precedence model: base values <- profile overlay <- installer-supplied patch. - Introduces templates/chart/templates/seed-job.yaml: a job which consults a small init container `seed-runner` that writes a status marker to a ConfigMap and respects backoff policy and jitter. The job uses a non-default backoffLimit derived from values and emits structured logs for monitoring and rollback decisions. - Adds templates/_overlay_helpers.tpl helper used to render (1) profile merge annotation, (2) safe defaulting for retry/backoff, and (3) a `seedResumeKey` annotation used by the private-operator to detect resumable seed state. - Adds scripts/seed-runner.sh: small POSIX script used by the init container to perform idempotent seeding (uses SQL idempotency tokens / k8s object existence checks so repeated runs are safe). Script supports dry-run and verbose logging. - Adds templates/preflight-cron.yaml to optionally schedule a lightweight preflight check that can gate whether the seed job should run immediately or be deferred (useful for slow registries). - Updates README and installer docs with examples for overlay profiles and recommended policies for large clusters.

Checklist: - [x] values.schema entries added and validated by helm schema test - [x] seed job template covers resume and annotation - [x] seed-runner script includes idempotency token and is POSIX-compatible for minimal base image - [x] integration test that simulates transient DB failure and verifies resume semantics - [x] docs updated with example overlays and roll-forward instructions

Compatibility notes: defaults are conservative (maxRetries: 3, backoffSeconds: 30). Overlay profiles are additive and opt-in; existing installs that do not set `overlay.profiles` will behave exactly as before. The new seed annotations are optional and ignored by older operators; the private-operator will be patched in a follow-up change to honor `seedResumeKey` for automated resume/cleanup. See ENG-1142 for follow-up operator work.
Diego Ruiz: Can we make the seed job idempotency marker namespace-scoped? If so we should include a TTL for stale markers. (requested changes)
Maya Chen: Reply: marker is namespace-scoped already; added `markerTTLSeconds` and documented caveats for cross-namespace installs.
Aditi Rao: Please add a unit test for the Helm helper that computes merged overlay precedence. (requested changes)
Maya Chen: Added helm unit test and fixed nil-buttoning for absent overlay list. (resolved)
Tom Fletcher: Lint failed on one template due to trailing whitespace; re-ran CI after fix. (approval)
Tom Fletcher: Approved after CI green and small docs tweak.

Motivation: Private installs require tenant onboarding to be safe and repeatable across upgrades. Current RBAC seeding is brittle during Helm upgrades and terraform-driven infra changes; operators frequently need to hand-run fixes. This PR introduces a tenant-onboard policy generator that emits parameterized tenant-scoped Role/RoleBinding and ServiceAccount templates, plus Helm pre-upgrade guardrails that detect destructive RBAC drift and block upgrades unless an explicit operator-approved drift token is provided. Design summary: - Add a small generator CLI (installer/policygen) that produces idempotent YAML (Roles, RoleBindings, Namespaces, Saa templates) from tenant metadata and operator config. Templates are parameterized (labels, tenant-id, isolation-mode) so the same generator is used for initial bootstrap and for later reconciliation. - Introduce a Helm pre-upgrade hook (charts/preflight/policy-check) which runs a dry-run policy lint and a simulated apply against a sandbox namespace using the generated templates. If the lint or simulation would remove required bootstrap permissions, the hook exits non-zero and the upgrade is blocked. - Add a terraform module output mapping so infra automation can consume the generated SA names/ARNs/IDs without parsing YAML. - Provide a safe-rollback playbook: when upgrades are blocked, operators can run "installer policygen --snapshot" to create a snapshot of current bindings, submit to the ops ticket, and the rollout can be retried with a deliberate --allow-policy-drift flag after manual review. Checklist: - [x] policy generator binary + unit tests - [x] Helm pre-upgrade hook + simulated apply runner - [x] terraform outputs + examples in examples/terraform-rbac - [x] idempotency tests for repeated generator runs - [x] integration e2e harness for preflight (flaky fixed) - [x] docs update in docs/private/onboarding.md Migration notes: On deploy, operators should run `installer policygen --tenant <id> --isolation-mode strict` and commit generated YAML to the tenant manifests repo or feed into terraform via the new outputs. Rollback: if an upgrade is blocked, follow the playbook at docs/private/upgrade-playbook.md which includes snapshot-and-restore steps. Security considerations: templates avoid embedding plaintext credentials; ServiceAccounts are referenced by name only and KMS/HSM integration is documented for any secrets. Two asks before merge: (1) ensure generated RoleBindings include an annotation with a stable generator fingerprint so we can detect external mutation, (2) add a CI step that runs the generator with --tenant dummy and diffs against a golden file to catch regressions.

Right now the chart blocks upgrades which is correct for strict isolation, but we should have a per-release override.
