Motivation: Private-installer releases need a single canonical manifest index that the CI can attest and gate on before publishing to customers. This PR implements a manifest rollup transformer that ingests per-arch/per-release artifact metadata, computes a deterministic canonical index (content-addressed ordering + delta graph), emits an attestable bundle, and wires an optional CI gating check that rejects a release if attestations are missing or provenance fails verification.

This is intended to reduce the number of manual steps in private-installer release runs, make rollbacks deterministic (by publishing a signed index snapshot), and give SREs/Customers cryptographic proof of the exact artifacts applied by an upgrade. Related Linear: ENG-4379 (manifest rollup) and ENG-4391 (attestation policy).

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds manifest-rollup binary and library used in the release pipeline to compose a single canonical manifest index from per-artifact metadata.
- Produces a deterministic index file (index.json.sha256) plus an attestable bundle (index.tar.gz.sig + provenance.json) suitable for cosign/canonical verification.
- Integrates a new CI gating job (release-index-verify) in .github/workflows/release.yml that verifies signatures, provenance chains, and KMS references before allowing the release job to proceed.
- Adds a backfill migration script to regenerate canonical indexes for a small subset of historical releases (used in the migration smoke tests).
- Documents the attestation policy and failure modes in docs/installer/release-attest.md.

Checklist: [x] unit + integration tests for rollup logic, [x] end-to-end CI check wired, [x] docs updated, [x] security review acknowledged.

Notes: The design favors deterministic ordering over human-readable diffs (index is content-addressed). The attestation policy is configurable per-env (see installer/release-attest.md). If the KMS path is unavailable the gate fails closed; we ship a temporary bypass keyed to a Linear ticket for emergency rollouts but it is disabled by default.
Ethan Park: Can we please avoid depending on a single KMS path? Suggested adding a fallback verify-only mode — responded that verify-only exists but the gate fails closed by default.
Sofia Martinez: Tests look good; request small refactor to separate signing from upload side-effects — author split attest.go into attest_sign.go and attest_upload.go in a follow-up commit.
Daniel Kim: Question about index size and memory use for very large releases; added streaming writer + chunked processing to indexer and added integration test that simulates 10k artifact entries.
Merged by squash on 2025-02-02 after CI green and two approvals. Merge commit message lists ENG-4379 and SUP-1284 and includes a short migration plan. Post-merge: CI kickstarted a backfill job for 5 historical release candidates against a staging bucket; no regressions observed. Documented emergency bypass procedure in ATTENTION.md.
Private-installer: canonical release index and attestation gating added; release CI now rejects un-attested indexes by default.
Operators: new migration script to backfill canonical indexes for selected historic releases.
Security: index bundles are signed (cosign) and provenance.json is published alongside the index for downstream verification.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: Private deployments require strong isolation of network and GPU resources per tenant while keeping Terraform state manageable for multi-tenant customers. Existing TF modules relied on coarse VPC-level subnet allocation which caused contention during concurrent tenant onboarding and complicated rollback paths when network claims failed. This PR implements a tenant-scoped BGP subnet allocator and a GPU nodeclass orchestrator to reduce allocation conflicts, enable safer upgrades, and support tenant-prefixed TFstate layouts for easier recovery.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces terraform/modules/tenant-subnet-allocator: a declarative TF module that exposes a 'lease' API for requesting contiguous /24 subnets from a BGP-able address pool. The allocator writes an immutable lease record into a prefixed TFstate key (configurable prefix per-tenant) to prevent double-allocations across apply retries.
- Adds terraform/modules/gpu-nodeclass-orchestrator: decouples tenant leases from nodeclass definitions so GPU nodepools are created once and bound via node affinity policies at tenant claim time. This reduces duplicate nodepool churn and speeds onboarding.
- Implements terraform/modules/iam-shard: a pattern for scoping IAM roles and KMS grants per-tenant using a stable hash-derived namespace to avoid cross-tenant collisions and to make rotation predictable.
- Adds terraform/modules/state-prefix-migrator: a small CLI wrapper + script (migrate.sh) to perform safe TFstate prefixing/migration when customers opt into tenant-prefixed states. Migration performs a dry-run, copies state objects to the new prefix, and leaves tombstone markers to allow rollback.
- Installer changes: helm chart values.yaml gains new knobs for allocator settings and rollout strategy; upgrade-hooks/plan-fence.sh and rollback/rollback-checker.go add fences to block simultaneous plan+apply workflows for overlapped tenants.
- Tests: integration tests added under tests/integration verifying concurrent tenant claims (simulated BGP pool exhaustion), and nodeclass binding behavior.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Lease model: the allocator uses an optimistic lock in TFstate (lease record + index) to avoid introducing an external database dependency. This keeps the change self-contained in Terraform but requires careful rollback semantics (handled by the state-prefix-migrator and plan-fence hooks).
- BGP behavior: module exposes hook points for route-programmers; default behavior emits route objects compatible with the on-prem router shim used by the installer. Customers with external routing systems can provide a 'route_operator' null provider.
- IAM sharding: we intentionally use a deterministic hash to allow stable role lookup by operator tooling; the module also emits a role rotation helper for scheduled key rotation.

Summary of commits in this PR:
- commit 1: scaffold tenant-subnet-allocator module, basic variables & outputs
- commit 2: add allocator core: lease resource, address arithmetic helpers, and acceptance tests
- commit 3: gpu-nodeclass-orchestrator module and example usage in private-installer chart
- commit 4: iam-shard templates and rotation helper script
- commit 5: state-prefix-migrator CLI + docs and migration plan templates
- commit 6: integration tests, CI pipeline updates, lint fixes

Changed areas / notable diffs:
- terraform/modules/tenant-subnet-allocator/main.tf: primary new logic (lease resource + allocation math).
- terraform/modules/gpu-nodeclass-orchestrator/*: new module coordinating nodeclass lifecycle and tenant binding CRs.
- terraform/modules/state-prefix-migrator/migrate.sh: posix script to perform safe state copy and tombstone writes.
- helm/charts/private-installer/values.yaml: new 'allocator' and 'nodeclass' sections and rollout knobs.
- installer/upgrade-hooks: plan-fence.sh was added to enforce sequential plans for overlapping tenant ranges.
- tests/integration: new concurrency tests flagged as flaky in CI until resource limits were adjusted.

Review conversation (high level):
- Maya Chen (reviewer): asked for clearer invariants on lease immutability and requested that the migrator perform a checksum validation post-copy. Response: added a post-copy checksum step and documented the failure modes.
- Omar Reyes (reviewer): raised concern about optimistic locking in TFstate leading to possible orphaned leases. Response: added tombstone markers and an idempotent reclaim path in migrate.sh and the plan-fence hook to mitigate overlapping applies.
- Priya Patel (reviewer): requested IAM role scoping examples for customers with STS federation. Response: added examples and a rotation helper that integrates with KMS.
- Threaded comments: small follow-ups included renaming variables for clarity and reducing the default pool size in CI to avoid flaky test failures. All requested code changes were addressed in follow-up commits.

CI and validation:
- Initial CI run: lint and unit tests failed due to shellcheck errors in migrate.sh and a missing test fixture. Fixed in commits 5 and 6.
- Rerun CI: all checks passed (unit, integration smoke, terraform validate). The integration pipeline includes a simulated BGP pool exhaustion scenario.

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Ship modules behind a feature flag in helm values; no behavior change for existing deployments by default.
2) For customers opting in, run state-prefix-migrator in dry-run mode and validate checksums.
3) Apply tenant-subnet-allocator for the tenant while plan-fence is enabled to ensure no concurrent claims.
4) Promote GPU nodeclass binding by updating tenant binding manifests; orchestrator will reconcile node affinity without destroying existing pools.
5) Once validated, flip the feature flag and remove the migration guard after a scheduled maintenance window.

Risk & rollback:
- Risk: partial migration leaving tombstone markers that would block reclaims. Mitigation: migrator can revert tombstones and plan-fence prevents concurrent operations during migration window.
- Rollback: rollback/rollback-checker.go detects partially-applied migrations and prevents a destructive apply until an operator clears the migration marker or runs the migrator revert path.

Why this is different from previous work: Existing PRs introduced TFstate sharding and lease concepts but were focused on subnet tagging and GPU pool labeling. This change couples a BGP-aware allocator with explicit tenant-prefixed TFstate migration tooling and a dedicated GPU nodeclass orchestrator to reduce churn and simplify tenant onboarding semantics.

Merge outcome: After addressing reviewer feedback and fixing CI shellcheck/test fixture failures, the branch was squashed and merged to main on 2025-11-10. Release notes were prepared and a rollout runbook was added to docs/private-deployments/tenant-networking.md.

Follow-ups (tracked):
- ENG-3478: Add observability hooks (metrics & traces) to allocator for allocation latency and failures.
- ENG-3499: Expand integration tests to cover cross-region allocations for multi-AZ private installs.
- PM-128: Evaluate UX knobs for self-serve tenant onboarding using the allocator API.
Adds tenant-scoped BGP subnet allocator TF module, GPU nodeclass orchestrator module, tenant-scoped IAM sharding templates, and a state-prefix migrator to enable per-tenant TFstate layout. Includes upgrade/rollback fences and integration tests. No breaking changes expected for existing deployments.
payload.title: Introduce tenant-scoped BGP subnet allocator and GPU nodeclass orchestrator

Motivation: private installs need reusable, testable Helm library components for tenant-scoped init jobs and a safer rollback orchestration path that minimizes partial-bootstrap states. This PR introduces a small Helm library (templates/_init_library.tpl, templates/init-wave-helpers.yaml) that centralizes common init job patterns (credential seeding, migration dry-run, cert bootstrap) and a config-driven rollback-orchestrator hook that coordinates safe quiesce and compensating actions when upgrades fail.

What changed (summary): consolidated init templates into a library with explicit values contracts; added values.schema.json for the library and the rollback orchestrator; introduced a new hook template (templates/rollback-orchestrator.yaml) that emits a Job responsible for staged quiesce + reversible steps; wired library into redwood-private-installer umbrella chart via chart dependencies example; added unit tests for the library templates and a simple k8s manifest smoke test to validate hook ordering.

Checklist:
- [x] library templates and helpers
- [x] values.schema.json and examples/values-tenant.yaml
- [x] rollback orchestrator hook with backoff and idempotency markers
- [x] integration smoke test in charts/test/verify-init-rollout.sh
- [x] release notes entry

Compatibility/Upgrade notes: the library is additive; existing consumers continue to work. Default behavior preserves current init job timing. To opt into the orchestrator, set rollback.orchestrator.enabled=true in your values. The values.schema includes explicit deprecation notes for legacy hooks (legacyInit.enabled) to ease migration.

Testing: local helm template against k8s v1.26 and v1.27, CI runs template-lint, go-template unit tests, and the smoke shell verifier. Stage rollout was validated on an internal QA cluster with tenant-sliced installs and simulated migration failures to ensure rollback orchestrator executes compensating actions in order.

Follow-ups: add HelmChart CRD-driven gating for air-gapped image pre-warm (separate PR), and a small operator to surface init-job state in tenant CR status (tracking ENG-4201).
Diego Rivera: This looks good overall but can we avoid creating clusterrolebindings in the library by taking an RBAC template from the installer? Creating cluster-scoped RBAC in a library can surprise consumers.
Asha Menon (author): Adjusted to include a namespaced-only RBAC option and documented the trade-off. Kept a clear note in values.schema.json about the namespace-scoped mode being the safer default.
Sofia Khan: Can the rollback orchestrator be made conservative by default (no automatic delete of resources)? We should prefer quiesce + pin + manual finalizer unless opt-in.
Asha Menon (author): Orchestrator default changed to 'observe-only' for the first wave; documented opt-in steps to enable automated compensating deletes. Added test to ensure observe-only path leaves resources intact.
Liam O'Connor: Minor nit around templating style and helper naming (use 'initWave' consistently). LGTM after small rename.
Asha Menon (author): Renamed helper to initWave* and pushed fixups. CI green.
Add Helm library providing tenant-aware init templates and an optional rollback orchestrator hook. New values.schema.json and example values included. Defaults are conservative and non-breaking. To opt into automated rollback actions, set rollback.orchestrator.enabled=true.

Motivation: customers deploying the Private installer in multi-jurisdiction environments reported two classes of operational surprises: (1) operator/service tokens occasionally routed to a KMS provider outside the declared jurisdiction when primary providers were under heavy load, and (2) audit payloads from edge nodes caused sustained disk pressure and S3 ingress charges due to verbose event emission. This PR introduces three coordinated controls: 1) a jurisdictional operator fallback middleware that enforces operator-claim-to-kms affinity with configurable soft/hard fallback modes; 2) a KMS cost allocator that annotates KMS usage with cost-tokens and emits compact, per-tenant cost summaries to the control-plane to enable chargeback without revealing plaintext envelopes; 3) an audit-size optimizer that applies sampling, event coalescing, and lightweight compression to audit streams for non-critical event types. Changes are implemented as opt-in feature flags in the installer config with sane defaults (soft-fallback=true, cost-allocator=enabled, audit-optimizer=enabled). The description below lists design decisions, rollout plan, and compatibility notes. Design: the operator fallback uses a two-stage resolver: preferred-providers list -> in-region fallback -> geo-fence denylist. In soft mode a cross-region provider is selected but annotated with an operator-affinity header and blocked for tenants with residency enforcement. In hard mode the operation fails fast and surfaces a clear remediation message to the installer UX. KMS cost allocator instruments the kms-proxy to attach a per-tenant cost-hash header and emits a compact telemetry metric (kms.charge.tokens) to the control plane; it never alters encrypted payloads and integrates with existing KMS provider adapters. Audit-size optimizer introduces a pluggable pipeline step in the audit-forwarder to: 1) classify events (critical, neutral, telemetry); 2) compress neutral/telemetry buckets with LZ4-lite and apply adaptive sampling windows; 3) emit size-delta metrics for alerting. Rollout: feature flags gated behind installer v0.44 opt-in, staged canary across three pilot customers, follow-on cluster-wide rollout with 2-week monitoring window. Backwards compatibility: behavior is opt-in and the default soft-fallback preserves existing routing when providers are healthy. KMS adapters must implement new cost-metadata hooks (shimbed for AWS/GCP/Azure in this PR). Security review summary: design reviewed with security and compliance; audit-optimizer preserves cryptographic integrity and never removes signed audit envelopes; cost allocator exposes only hashed telemetry and cannot be used to exfiltrate plaintext. See related Linear items ENG-4182 and SEC-702 for acceptance criteria and audit checklist. Checklist: [x] design doc updated [x] e2e smoke tests added [x] unit tests for fallback resolver [x] compatibility shims for AWS/GCP/Azure KMS adapters [x] installer config samples updated [x] migration notes and release-notes drafted.
Diego Morales: Nit: resolver.go has a 200ms hardcoded probe timeout; recommend making it configurable per-deployment. Also can we add an observability tag for 'fallback_reason' to help post-mortems?
Asha Patel: Good catch. Exposed probe_timeout in config with default 200ms and added fallback_reason tag on the resolver path. Updated tests to assert tags are present.
Lena Fischer: Security question: how do we guarantee the cost-hash header cannot be used to correlate across tenants? We should document collision resistance expectations.
Asha Patel: The allocator uses HMAC-SHA256 with a deployment-scoped salt and truncates to 128 bits; added note in docs and a unit test that ensures same tenant->same token across requests but different deployments produce different tokens.
Marcus Chen: Audit compression looks good; please add a metric for 'audit.payload.post-compress.size' and an alert if average compression ratio falls below 1.05 over 30m.
Asha Patel: Added the metric and alert rule to docs/operations with threshold guidance.
Added optional jurisdictional operator fallback middleware to control KMS affinity, a KMS cost allocator for per-tenant cost telemetry, and an audit-size optimizer that compresses/coalesces non-critical audit events. Opt-in behind installer flags; see docs/operations/jurisdictional-rollout.md for migration and rollout guidance.
After upgrade: validate installer config 'jurisdictional' block; confirm KMS adapters are at least v1.2.0 or fallback will use shim mode. Monitor metric kms.charge.tokens and audit.payload.post-compress.size for the first 48 hours.

Context: Private installs are increasingly hitting scale limits and operational friction when a single tfstate file, broad IAM roles, and undifferentiated GPU node pools are used across multiple tenants and AZ boundaries. This PR introduces two complementary Terraform modules and an orchestration helper to partition tfstate into "state silos" while providing a 'nodeclass-broker' that binds GPU nodeclass definitions, scoped IAM roles, and network attachment policies per tenant or workload class. Motivation: reduce blast radius for tfstate operations, enable smaller reconciliation units (faster applies), and support finer-grained IAM/egress controls for regulated workloads. What this PR does (high level): 1) new module terraform/modules/state-silo: implements a state partitioner pattern and remote state configuration helper that can be wired by tenant, region, or cluster-role. It includes lock/backup hooks and an opt-in 'drift-protector' workspace that snapshots resources before critical changes. 2) new module terraform/modules/nodeclass-broker: exposes a small Terraform interface to declare GPU nodeclasses (profile, taints/affinity, allowed instance types) and synthesizes tenant-scoped IAM roles, node pool labels, and subnet claim bindings. 3) small network templates terraform/modules/network-attachments to express per-nodeclass egress policies and cross-tenant VPC peering constraints. 4) a migration helper scripts/tfstate-partitioner/partitioner.go used offline to generate state mapping plans and run retries with exponential backoff; this is a declarative tool (not executed during apply) to aid operators. 5) updates to helm/values/private.yaml to expose nodeclass and state-silo settings that the installer consumes during chart render. 6) lightweight docs and examples in examples/tenant-silos/ that demonstrate a tenant-scoped rollout and rollback path. Migration story: a safe, staged migration is provided. The partitioner produces an ordered list of state moves, verifies resource counts post-move, and annotates the installer helm release with the new state-silo tag. There is a reversible path: every partition step also creates a 'shadow' tfstate snapshot in the configured artifacts bucket and a reconciler job that validates the new state before traffic cutover. Security: IAM roles generated by nodeclass-broker are intentionally narrow: they only grant kubelet-level permissions and specific KMS/encryption access for the tenant's nodeclass. We add KMS key policy examples and recommend using HSM-backed keys in the docs. Backwards compatibility: default behaviour is a single 'global' state silo and a single nodeclass to match existing installs; migration must be opt-in. Tests and CI: added unit tests for partitioner plan validation, Terraform fmt/validate checks, and end-to-end smoke run on a small test workspace in CI. Rollout plan: staged rollout to Private installs via a feature-flag gated helm/installer variable. Why different from prior work: instead of monolithic tfstate migrations or ad-hoc scripts, this PR formalizes a reusable module pattern, provides an operator tool to plan and verify moves, and couples nodeclass configuration to IAM and network policies so node lifecycle operations are lower risk. Related: ENG-4821 (state-silo initiative), ENG-4890 (gpu-nodeclass lifecycle).
Marco Ruiz (reviewer) commented on 2025-11-04: "Nice separation. Please clarify failure modes for partial state moves — what happens if snapshot creation succeeds but move fails?"
Asha Patel (author) replied on 2025-11-04: "Good question — the partitioner performs snapshot->plan->copy->verify sequence; if copy fails we retry with exponential backoff, and if repeated failures occur we leave a 'blocked' annotation and retain the shadow snapshot for rollback. Documented in README."
Zoe Lin requested changes on 2025-11-05: "IAM templates look permissive for service accounts we create — can we scope role names and resource ARNs to the tenant prefix and add least-privilege policy examples?"
Asha Patel replied on 2025-11-06: "Addressed: updated iam.tpl to interpolate tenant prefix and added an example policy for encrypted EBS and KMS use in the module README. Added tests to validate ARN patterns."
Daniel Ortega approved on 2025-11-09: "Approvals pending CI green — verified partition plan dry-run locally. Clean design."
Introduce state-silos and nodeclass-broker Terraform modules for private installs. Operators can partition tfstate per-tenant/region, create tenant-scoped GPU nodeclasses with scoped IAM, and use the partitioner tool to plan safe migrations. Backwards compatible by default; migration opt-in. See examples/tenant-silos/README.md for migration steps.
Operators should stage migrations on non-production tenants first. Ensure artifacts bucket retention is at least 30 days for shadow snapshots. Feature flag helm.installer.stateSilos.enabled must be set to true to opt-in. Rolling back is supported by restoring shadow snapshots and re-annotating helm releases.
IAM roles generated are tenant-scoped; recommend KMS HSM-backed keys. Audit logs are emitted during partition moves to the central audit bucket and should be monitored for repeated failures.
1) terraform init + terraform plan in examples/tenant-silos/test-workspace (local backend) 2) run scripts/tfstate-partitioner/partitioner --dry-run to inspect proposed moves 3) enable helm.installer.stateSilos.enabled in a staging cluster and deploy the installer with nodeclass definitions 4) verify node pools are created with expected labels and IAM role binding 5) run partitioner plan and then apply steps against a disposable workspace to validate snapshot/verify flow.

payload.body:
Motivation: air-gapped installs increasingly require stronger supply-chain verification and smaller upgrade windows. Existing installer bundles pull full OCI images for every upgrade which is expensive for large on-prem fleets. This PR implements an SBOM-driven delta-sync path and a verified extraction flow so offline bundles are applied only for layers that changed and only after provenance checks. Summary: 1) Generate and consume CycloneDX SBOMs per bundle artifact and ship a compact index in the sealed bundle; 2) A delta-sync engine that compares local registry state (layer digest set) against bundle SBOM and fetches only missing/changed layers; 3) Verified extraction: signature (cosign) verification + SBOM checksum validation before writing runtime artifacts; 4) Terraform module update to support 'sbom_index' seeding to local registries during bootstrap; 5) Helm chart hook for installer that blocks apply until verification succeeds; 6) New installer CLI flags (--sbom-verify, --delta-sync-only, --sbom-cache-dir) and preflight checks for KMS key presence. Design notes: - SBOM format chosen: CycloneDX v1.4 with additional vendor extension carrying OCI layer digests to avoid full image manifests. This keeps the on-device index compact (~10-100KB per bundle). - Delta algorithm: compute symmetric difference of layer digest sets, fetch in parallel with backoff and resume on failure. - Security: cosign signatures are validated against configured root certificates (support for KMS/HSM signing is in separate PR but the verification hook supports PKIX chains). - Backwards compat: if no SBOM present or --sbom-verify disabled, installer falls back to existing full-extract path. - Rollback: installer records applied delta IDs in /var/lib/redwood-installer/applied-deltas.json and supports the existing rollback hook. Usage: Examples included in README change: redwood-installer apply --bundle sealed-bundle.tar.gz --sbom-verify --sbom-cache-dir /var/cache/rwi/sbom --delta-sync-only To seed a local registry during bootstrap (Terraform): module "registry_seed" { source = "github.com/redwood/private-installer//terraform/registry-seed" bundle_sbom_index = "path/to/index.json" } Testing: unit tests for SBOM parsing and delta set diff (coverage added in pkg/sbom/*), integration tests run in CI smoke job using a small sealed bundle with three images. CI: initial run hit a flaky e2e related to partial pull timeouts; added retry logic and extended network mock timeouts, all checks now pass. Migration: existing sealed bundles without SBOM continue to work. We recommend re-publishing bundles with SBOM when teams are preparing upgrades to reduce bandwidth. Limitations: current SBOM index is per-bundle; federated index across many bundles is future work. Implementation details: - New packages: pkg/sbom (parsing/validation), pkg/deltasync (delta calculation + fetcher), cmd/installer (new flags + verified extraction orchestrator). - Helm: charts/installer/templates/hooks/verify-preinstall.yaml blocks install until the installer sidecar reports verification success. - Terraform: terraform/registry-seed adds a small helper that reads an index.json and pushes missing blobs to a local registry using skopeo/oras. - Docs: docs/airgap/sbom-index.md with examples, and upgrade notes.
Introduce SBOM-driven delta sync for sealed bundles; add verified extraction path that enforces SBOM and signature checks; Terraform helper to seed local registry with SBOM-index; Helm pre-install hook that validates bundle provenance; rollout is backwards-compatible with existing offline bundles (no forced upgrade).
Luca Ortega (review): Nice approach — can you clarify failure modes when cosign roots are missing? We should fail fast in the preflight instead of halfway through extraction.
Maya Chen (author): Good point — added a preflight KMS/cosign root check and made verified extraction a blocking step in the helm hook. See installer preflight changes in cmd/installer/main.go.
Priya Iyer (review): Terraform module looks good but please add an option to skip skopeo and use a preseeded tarball for air-gapped environments with stricter egress policies.
Maya Chen (author): Added 'use_local_tarball' boolean and updated README with tarball usage and examples.
Evan Park (approval): Integration tests exercise the delta path and rollback; satisfied with retry/backoff changes. APPROVED
CI Bot: initial pipeline failed on e2e:timeout (network mock). Rerun triggered.
CI Bot: pipeline passed on rerun. All checks green.

payload.body:
Motivation: customers with strict air-gapped installs ran into nondeterministic vendor bundles when we deduplicated images and packages across distro overlays. This caused cache misses during local registry seeding and made atomic promotes brittle. This PR implements a vendor-lock graph generator (content-addressed), plus a distro policy hook that selects the minimal overlay set per target distro and kernel variant. The generator emits a stable lockfile and a compact delta manifest used by the offline bundler and the terraform seeder. Changes are backward-compatible: existing bundle formats are supported and the new CLI toggles are opt-in. What changed: 1) build/airgap/vendor-graph: new generator that computes content-addressed artifact nodes, canonicalizes package order, and produces a vendor-lock.json with checksums; 2) installer/preflight: verify vendor-lock checksums, support quick-fail when local registry lacks promoted layers; 3) charts/overlays/distro-selectors: small policy DSL (YAML) + selector runtime used by the bundler to pick only necessary overlays for k3s/rke2/kubeadm; 4) terraform/registry-seed: hook to ingest vendor-lock and apply atomic promote semantics to multi-repo mirrors; 5) docs and examples: updated airgap quickstart and migration notes. Testing: unit tests for graph canonicalization, e2e on small k3s image set using local registry mirror, manual validation of delta promotion on a seeded mirror. Backwards compat: when the flags are not set the bundler falls back to previous behavior. Rollout: feature gated by CLI --vendor-lock and controlled in Private Console for initial customers. Migration notes: existing customers should regenerate bundles to benefit from dedupe and smaller deltas. See linked linear tasks for rollout plan and telemetry collection.
Adds a deterministic vendor-lock graph generator, kube-distro policy hooks for distro-specific overlay selection, and a small backward-compatible CLI flag for airgap bundle generation. Improves bundle size stability and preflight validation for on-prem installs.
Asha: Can we include a short-lived compatibility shim so older registry seeders ignore the new fields? Author: added a minimal shim and unit test in terraform module.
Diego: Please add a warning in the console when bundles are generated without --vendor-lock. Author: added banner and tests.
Samir: How do we ensure we don't regress delta promote latency? Please add a microbenchmark. Author: added a small local-promote benchmark and measured ~3% overhead with better dedupe gains.
Merged via squash on 2026-03-01 after CI green. Merge included a short changelog entry and a follow-up linear task to add telemetry for vendor-lock adoption. No breaking changes introduced; consumers are encouraged to regenerate bundles but existing bundles remain supported.

payload.body:
Motivation: In several recent customer upgrade exercises we observed instability caused by operator images floating between upgrades and by silent chart metadata drift that allowed incompatible post-rollback states. This PR introduces three complementary safeguards: (1) operator image pinning via digest lockfiles surfaced in both the installer manifests and Terraform module outputs; (2) a chart sub-release stamping mechanism so the installer can detect and refuse upgrades that change sub-release semantics without an explicit migration plan; (3) a Helm post-rollback validation hook that runs lightweight data-plane health checks and fails the rollback (leaving operator in quarantined mode) if core invariants are violated.

What I changed (summary): Added an image lockfile generator and validation flow to the installer CLI; extended terraform/modules/installer to accept and export image_digest values and refuse plan/apply when the lockfile is stale; modified Helm charts to include a chartSubRelease annotation and collector logic in the operator bootstrap; added a post-rollback Helm hook that executes a small job which runs sanity checks (DB schema version, KV cache presence, background worker connectivity). Added docs: upgrade-runbook and operator-image-lockfile guide. Added e2e upgrade job to CI that runs a staged upgrade -> rollback -> validation flow to exercise the new hooks. Implemented a small migration guard in the installer that annotates resources with schemaVersion markers and will block a downgrade if the on-disk schema version is greater than the target release.

Commit highlights (high level): - add: installer/cmd/lockfile: generator + validator - add: terraform/modules/installer/image-lock.tf + outputs - add: helm/templates/hooks/post-rollback-validate.yaml - change: helm/Chart.yaml (new chartSubRelease field and annotation processing) - change: installer/upgrade/guard: schema-version preflight checks - add: docs/upgrade-runbook.md and docs/operator-image-lockfile.md - add: ci/e2e/upgrade-rollback-flow.yaml - tests: integration/upgrade_rollback_test.go and unit tests for lockfile validation

Files changed (high level): helm/Chart.yaml, helm/values.schema.json, helm/templates/hooks/post-rollback-validate.yaml, installer/cmd/lockfile/*.go, installer/upgrade/guard.go, terraform/modules/installer/image-lock.tf, docs/upgrade-runbook.md, docs/operator-image-lockfile.md, ci/e2e/upgrade-rollback-flow.yaml, integration/upgrade_rollback_test.go, tests/fixtures/*, scripts/bin/lockfile-generator.sh

Implementation notes: - Image pinning: the installer generates a lockfile mapping component -> image@sha256:digest. The terraform module consumes a lockfile path and exposes image_digest outputs so upgrades pin the operator/controller image. During a dry-run the installer will fail if current cluster images differ from lockfile (opt-in override supported for emergency operations). - Chart sub-release stamping: Chart.yaml gains a new optional field chartSubRelease. The operator bootstraps will compare stored sub-release (in ConfigMap metadata) with the incoming chartSubRelease and require an explicit migration when the stamp increases in a way that implies structural change. - Post-rollback validation: Implemented as a Helm post-rollback hook that triggers a short-lived pod which runs a small binary (included in operator image) to validate DB schema, consumer queue health, and cached KV consistency. If validation fails the hook marks the release with label rollbackValidation=failed and operator enters quarantine mode and emits a high-severity event. - Downgrade guard: Installer upgrade path now sets a schemaVersion marker on the cluster; the preflight will fail if targetVersion < schemaVersion and the user has not supplied --allow-downgrade with an explicit migration plan.

Testing & CI: Unit tests for lockfile parsing/validation (installer tests), integration harness that runs a create-upgrade-rollback scenario (integration/upgrade_rollback_test.go), and a new e2e pipeline job runs a small cluster in KinD that exercises the lockfile + post-rollback hook path. CI summary: initial run failed due to flaky timing in the hook job; fixed by adding a 30s readiness probe and retry loop. Final CI: all checks pass.

Migration plan & rollout: This PR is safe to merge to main but requires a coordinated rollout: - Step 1 (canary): merge and enable image lockfile generation for internal staging only; do not enforce failure on stale lockfile (log-only). - Step 2: enable enforcement for beta clusters with a migration-runbook run. - Step 3: enable enforcement by default and surface upgrade failures via Console. For private deployments customers can opt-in to enforcement by supplying the lockfile to the terraform module.

Backwards compatibility: default behavior is non-breaking (lockfile generation and chartSubRelease are optional). Enabling enforcement is opt-in until Step 3 described above. Downgrade guard is conservative and requires explicit --allow-downgrade to proceed.

Risks & mitigations: - Risk: operator image digests drift causing unexpected failures for customers who rely on image tags. Mitigation: we provide an automated lockfile generator and the installer supports a staged rollout with an opt-in enforcement flag. - Risk: post-rollback hook could cause longer rollback times. Mitigation: validation is intentionally lightweight (<60s typical) and can be disabled per-release via annotation for emergency rollbacks.

Related work: previous PRs added manifest hashes and version lockfiles; this complements them by publishing digest pins, adding chart sub-release semantics, and automating validation after rollback. See related Linear items: ENG-5124 (upgrade safety), ENG-5178 (helm rollback validation).

Notes for reviewers: focus on the lockfile format, terraform consumption surface, and the failure semantics of the post-rollback hook. The hook uses the operator image binary (validate-bridge) which already exists in the image; integration tests exercise failure and success paths.

Merge outcome: squash-merged into main after approvals and CI green.
Diego Alvarez (reviewer): Please add a test for the terraform module that asserts image_digest output is populated when a lockfile is provided.
Maya Chen (author): Added terraform unit test and a small fixture; pushed patch to generator to expose the imageDigest output.
Priya Natarajan (reviewer): The post-rollback job looked flaky in the first CI run; can we add a retry loop and a readiness probe?
Maya Chen (author): Added a 30s readiness probe and a 3-retry loop in the hook job; updated integration test to account for backoff.
Samir Patel (reviewer): We should avoid failing customer rollbacks by default. Ensure enforcement is opt-in and documented.
Maya Chen (author): Enforcement is opt-in until the staged rollout completes; clarified in docs and added --enforce-lockfile flag to the installer.
This PR intentionally keeps enforcement opt-in to avoid surprise failures in customer environments. Operations runbook and console messaging will be published in a follow-up that adds UI toggles for enforcement state.

Installer preflight now emits actionable verification failures (error codes, likely cause, remediation, log paths). No change to verification semantics; still fails closed by default.
Context: With signed offline bundles, verification failures are expected to be one of the top support drivers during pilot. Today, failures often surface as generic crypto/library errors with no guidance on what to do next, and logs are not consistently referenced in the CLI output. This PR keeps fail-closed behavior unchanged, but makes the UX/support story significantly better.

What this changes: - Introduces a structured error taxonomy for bundle verification with stable error codes (RV-VERIFY-0xxx). - Maps common failure modes to a short 'what happened' + 'what to do next' remediation block, including where to find logs. - Adds a single-line summary suitable for copy/paste into tickets, plus a verbose output behind --verbose. - Normalizes log locations across Linux packages and containerized installer runs, and prints the resolved log path in the error footer. - Adds a 'transport integrity' remediation hint for hash mismatches seen in SUP-31892 (zip/unzip tooling, line-ending conversions, partial copies). - Adds time-skew specific messaging (not-yet-valid / expired) including suggested checks for air-gapped time sources.

Non-goals: - No change to verification policy (still blocks install on invalid/untrusted signatures). - No change to signature format / manifest schema (handled in other PRs). - No break-glass flag in this PR (tracked separately).

Testing: - Added unit tests for error mapping and formatting. - Updated integration tests to assert error codes + presence of remediation hints. - Manually validated output on Ubuntu 22.04 and RHEL 8 with tampered manifest + unknown key cases.

Docs: This PR updates the in-repo installer help text for the new error codes and log path footer. The full customer-facing docs update is tracked in ENG-4850.

Related PRs: - pr-24844-verify-bundle-signature-during-preflight - pr-24859-add-trust-store-and-key-rollover-support
Marcus Lin (review): The mapping from x509 errors to our codes looks good. Please make sure we never print raw certificate subjects/serials by default (avoid leaking customer environment details into screenshots/tickets). Also, suggest adding an explicit note that verification failures are non-retriable unless the bundle/trust store changes.

Ethan Park (author): Good call. I moved cert detail printing behind --verbose and redacted serial/subject in the default path. Also added a 'Retry only after…' line to the remediation templates (bundle re-copy, trust store update, clock fix).

Dev Patel (review): Love the copy/paste line. Can we standardize the last line so Support can grep it in support bundles? Something like 'redwood-private-installer: RV-VERIFY-0012'. Also include the log file path *and* the support bundle path if generated.

Ethan Park (author): Added a stable footer: 'redwood-private-installer: <CODE> (see <log path>)'. For support bundle path, we only have it after bundle generation; I added a hint: 'If you generated a support bundle, include support-bundle.tgz'. PR-25011 will wire verification status into the bundle automatically.

Owen Phillips (review): For hash mismatch remediation, please explicitly warn about 'text mode' FTP / CRLF conversion and using 'unzip -aa'. We saw exactly that in SUP-31892.

Ethan Park (author): Updated the RV-VERIFY-0021 remediation block with concrete do/don't examples and added a link target to docs/troubleshooting.md section.

Kira Thompson (review): Can we keep wording consistent with docs ("offline bundle", "manifest", "detached signature")? Also suggest changing 'signature invalid' to 'signature verification failed' (more precise).

Ethan Park (author): Updated terminology to match our docs draft and made the message text more precise.

Sahana Iyer (review): CI looks fine. One nit: error code ordering in errors.go is out of sequence and will be painful to maintain. Please sort by numeric code and add a brief comment on stability guarantees.

Ethan Park (author): Done. Sorted codes, added comment: codes are stable across minor versions and should not be reused.

Marcus Lin (final approval): Approved after redaction changes + code stability comment. Please ensure we track adding these codes to the external docs FAQ (ENG-4850).

Dev Patel (final approval): Approved. This will reduce back-and-forth on pilot tickets.

payload.body:
Motivation: In large on-prem/private installs we saw race conditions during parallel tenant provisioning. Multiple bootstrap workers could attempt to create identical tenant-scoped IAM roles and run overlapping terraform apply operations against the same remote state, causing apply conflicts and intermittent install failures. This PR introduces a safer, idempotent bootstrap flow: 1) the installer requests a short-lived (24h by default) bootstrap role per-tenant which is created with a unique suffix; 2) terraform modules are updated to use a central locking backend (S3+Dynamo/Consul/Postgres supported) and expose a lock namespace per-tenant; 3) helm charts add pre-install hooks that gate CRD/namespace creation and requeue if lock unavailable; 4) a reconciler process runs after successful provision to revoke/delete ephemeral roles and emit a permanent tenant role binding (if configured). The change set covers terraform modules, helm hooks, policy bundle generation templates, and the installer orchestration with a migration path. What changed: - Terraform: new module tenant-bootstrap now accepts bootstrap_role_name, lock_backend, lock_namespace and can run in a dry-run idempotent mode. Added state locking examples and a small migration script to move state with minimal downtime. - Helm: charts/private/templates/hooks.yaml adds a pre-install hook that obtains a lock before applying tenant-scoped resources and retries transient lock failures. Added values for lock config. - Policy bundle generator: emit per-tenant temporary role templates and include ttl metadata so the reconciler can identify and rotate them. - Installer: bootstrap coordinator creates ephemeral roles using the policy generator, records bootstrap metadata to installer-state, calls terraform with lock namespace, waits for success then triggers post-provision reconciler to convert ephemeral role to long-lived bindings where required and revoke leftover permissions. - Scripts: tools/migrate-bootstrap-roles.sh to migrate existing installs that used the old global bootstrap role into the new per-tenant ephemeral model. - Docs: docs/upgrade-rollback.md updated with explicit rollback steps in case terraform apply cannot acquire a lock. Checklist: - [x] Design reviewed (ENG-1024) - [x] Terraform module unit tests - [x] Helm lint + integration k8s smoke tests - [x] Policy bundle template unit tests - [x] Migration script tested on internal staging cluster - [x] Rollback playbook documented Rollout plan: staged rollout. 1) Merge to main and tag canary release. 2) Enable new flow behind feature flag in private-installer. 3) Run migration script for customers that opted in. 4) Monitor metrics/alerts for provisioning failures and excessive role creation. 5) Flip feature flag once stable. Backwards compatibility: existing installs that don't opt into the new flow keep using the global bootstrap role. The migration script automates switching an install to the new model. Security considerations: ephemeral roles have a limited TTL and minimal scope; reconciler ensures revoke on success/failure; audit events are emitted to installer audit log. Performance: small additional latency while acquiring locks under high contention; perf mitigation includes exponential backoff and configurable lock timeouts. Testing: unit tests for terraform templates, CI e2e canary against staging, and manual smoke on a 50-tenant parallel create scenario where we validated no conflicts in 50 concurrent runs. Known limitations: If the lock backend is misconfigured, installs may block rather than fail; docs call out supported backends and troubleshooting steps. Merge notes: squash and merge, bumped module versions and added migration script to tools/.
Adds ephemeral bootstrap roles for tenant provisioning, central TF state locking options, helm hook updates to ensure idempotent tenant CRD creation, and a post-provision reconciler that removes temporary privileges. No user-facing API changes.
Diego Morales: Can we parameterize TTL by cluster config rather than hard-coding 24h? Suggest values.yaml + installer flag. - PR author: Agreed, added TTL override via installer flag and helm values.
Priya Kapoor: The migration script should do a dry-run mode and output affected resources before mutating. - PR author: Added --dry-run and a confirmation prompt. Also added a small safety check for active consistency markers.
Sam Thompson: Wanted stronger tests for lock contention; can you add a synthetic concurrency test? - PR author: Added tests/helm_integration/lock_retry_test.yaml that simulates 30 concurrent lock requests in CI canary.
Diego Morales: Needs Terraform plan output in CI; saw a missing provider pin in module. - PR author: Fixed provider blocks and added terraform plan CI job.
Priya Kapoor: Approve after small nits addressed: log level and clearer error messages for lock failures. - PR author: nits addressed.

Motivation: Customers running private, air-gapped installs need cryptographically verifiable, reproducible installer bundles they can mirror into immutable registries and audit. This PR introduces deterministic bundling and an opinionated signing flow so operators can verify artifacts offline. Summary of changes: 1) New OCI index generator that produces content-addressable indexes with stable ordering and reproducible manifest digests. 2) Bundle signing tool that emits detached GPG + SHA256 manifest files alongside OCI tarballs; verification CLI is included for offline validation. 3) Deterministic bootstrap scripts for kubelet and runtime preloads (RHCOS/Flatcar/Ubuntu) that remove timestamps and non-deterministic tar ordering to make delta bundles reproducible. 4) Terraform module tweaks to registry-mirror to accept signed-bundle metadata and expose artifact ACLs for mirror automation. 5) Chart and values additions for private-installer to surface verification flags and signature public-key config. Backwards compatibility: unsigned bundles are still supported but installer now warns and logs mismatch severity. Migration notes: a migration utility is included to re-index existing local vendor caches into the new reproducible layout. Testing: unit tests for indexer and verifier, integration runs against k3s and kubeadm single-node air-gapped clusters in CI mirror job, and manual validation in an internal staging rack with a private registry. Security review: signing key handling documented and KMS/HSM integration recommended for production keys. Rollback plan: installer falls back to previous unsigned behavior if verification fails and operator provides --force-allow-unsigned; this is logged and emitted as an alert to the console. Checklist: [x] Design doc linked [x] Unit tests added [x] Integration e2e added [x] Docs updated [x] Security review notes applied.

Motivation: Customers deploying Redwood Private in highly restricted on-prem sites ran into two recurring pain points during air-gapped installation: 1) brittle vendor image set management across multiple distro variants (Ubuntu/RHEL/Alma/Rocky), and 2) long manual steps for pre-warming kubelets and local registry mirrors so nodes can join with minimal network access. This PR introduces a focused set of changes to improve offline bundle vendoring and automate kubelet bootstrapping for isolated sites.

What this PR does: 1) Add an OCI lockfile producer that emits a compact per-distro OCI index (images + digest pins + minimal platform hints) making vendored bundles smaller and easier to validate during apply. The index supports delta snapshots so airgap bundles can be shipped as incremental updates. 2) Add a small, idempotent kubelet-bootstrap script (systemd + unit template) which preloads CRI images from the local registry mirror and precreates required /var/lib/kubelet paths to reduce node bootstrap time in networks with high packet loss or proxy gateways. 3) Terraform module tweaks to the registry-mirror module: support for OCI-staging bucket configuration, atomic apply toggle (disable optimistic apply in strict-airgap), and improved IAM policy docs for on-prem object stores. 4) Helm chart change to allow imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent and to accept an ociIndex URL so charts can validate image digests before rendering. 5) Documentation and an example playbook for composing a minimal delta bundle and applying it to an offline cluster.

Backwards compatibility: Existing installer flows that use the previous monolithic lockfile continue to work; the new oci-index path is additive. If the installer finds an oci-index.json next to the bundle, it prefers the smaller delta-aware index.

Testing performed: Unit tests for the oci lockfile generator, integration test of delta snapshot apply using k3s in an isolated VM, manual bootstrap validation against Ubuntu 24 and Rocky 9 nodes, and terraform plan/apply smoke tests with a local minio backend. CI initially failed on lint (helm chart yamls); fixed chart values and re-ran.

Rollout plan: Release as part of the next private-installer minor (v0.46.x). Recommend early adoption in staging environments and a canary airgap rollout to two customer sites before recommending as default in docs.

Related: ENG-20248 (airgap bundle size reduction), ENG-21011 (kubelet bootstrap workstream).

payload.body:
Motivation: We observed multiple upgrade incidents where subtle schema changes (nullable -> not-null, removed columns, implicit type narrowing) caused partial upgrades and difficult rollbacks. This PR introduces an automated pre-upgrade compatibility check and a post-restore validation step to make private installer upgrades safer and more auditable.

What this PR does: Adds a schema compatibility checker that runs as part of the Helm pre-upgrade hook and the Terraform upgrade plan job. The checker compares the target release's migration manifest with a database introspection snapshot to detect incompatible operations (destructive drops, narrowing type changes, non-null constraints without defaults). If an incompatibility is detected, the hook fails the upgrade and emits diagnostic artifacts (schema-diff.json, sample rows) into the release-namespace PVC.

Backup/restore automation: Introduces a pre-upgrade backup job (helm hook) that triggers an atomic snapshot export of Postgres WAL and a compressed dump for on-prem environments; the job uploads artifacts to the configured artifacts bucket or local NFS. A new post-restore verification job validates critical invariants (row counts for "tenants" and "deployments" tables, checksum of configuration blob, presence of required indexes). The verification job returns non-zero on mismatch and writes a short report to the same artifacts location.

Schema compatibility rules: Basic rules implemented: (1) dropping columns is flagged as unsafe; (2) removing NOT NULL without default is flagged as a breaking change; (3) narrowing integer types or reducing varchar length is flagged; (4) adding columns with default/nullable is allowed. The rules are configurable via values.yaml: upgradeSanity.rules.allowUnsafe and upgradeSanity.rules.customWhitelist. Teams can opt-in to allow-unsafe for emergency upgrades using a documented flag and an explicit override token.

Installer changes: Helm charts: added pre-upgrade and post-restore hook jobs, new templates for schema-diff uploads, and values knobs. Terraform: added state-lock verification before terraform apply and an optional module input to enable remote snapshot validation in IaC pipelines. Installer CLI: new subcommand redwood-installer verify-upgrade --target-version that runs the same checks locally against kubeconfig for offline validation.

Observability: Emits Prometheus metrics upgrade_sanity_check_total, upgrade_sanity_check_failures, backup_hook_duration_seconds, restore_validation_failures; logs include a structured reason code (SCHEMA_DROP, TYPE_NARROW, NOT_NULL_ADD) to assist incident triage.

Testing: Unit tests for compatibility rules and integration tests covering helm pre-upgrade hook execution on KinD: we added a CI matrix job e2e/restore-canary which runs a simulated backup+restore against a seeded dataset. The first CI run showed a flaky timeout in restore verification which was fixed by raising the default restore timeout and adding retries for eventual index creation.

Operational notes: The default behavior blocks upgrades that are potentially unsafe. For existing large customers, we ship a migration report generator (redwood-installer migration-report) that operators can run to get a human-readable plan and the list of incompatible actions.

Docs and rollout: Added docs/private-upgrades.md and upgraded the upgrade checklist in docs/operational-playbooks/upgrade-checklist.md to include running verify-upgrade and saving the backup artifact manifest.

Rollback plan: On failure, the pre-upgrade hook prevents the release from being applied. If an operator performed an emergency override and later needs to rollback, the post-upgrade artifacts include an automatic restore script and a validation report to verify the rollback restored invariants.

CI/QA: See tests_run for details. This change does not modify runtime code paths for serving; it is focused on installer and orchestration.
Adds a pre-upgrade schema compatibility validator, automated pre-upgrade backup hooks, and post-restore verification to reduce upgrade/downgrade risk.

Jordan Wells (2026-02-14): Yes — added upgradeSanity.rules.customWhitelist and plugin hook in compat_checker.go (see commits).
Miguel Torres (2026-02-17): CI e2e/restore-canary failed on first run with restore timeout; please add retry and increase default timeout for on-prem restores.
Jordan Wells (2026-02-18): Increased timeout and added 3 retries for restore verification. Re-ran CI, green.
Priya Nair (2026-02-21): Approving after test coverage numbers look reasonable and docs updated.
Merged via squash. CI green after restore timeout fix. Merge commit recorded in main.
Unit coverage + compatibility rule permutations added. e2e restore canary validates backup/restore end-to-end against seeded dataset. First CI run failed due to timeout fixed by retry/backoff; subsequent runs green.

Motivation: reduce blast radius from failed schema migrations and terraform drift during private upgrades. This PR implements a multi-layer safety net: 1) a preflight 'schema rollback safety' controller that captures migration intent, computes a reversible migration plan and produces an idempotent rollback script; 2) an automated restore-rehearsal harness that runs synthetic restores against a sandbox cluster using the existing snapshot catalog; 3) a Terraform Plan Canary module that applies plans to an isolated canary namespace and verifies resource diffs before allowing cluster-wide apply; and 4) helm post-upgrade verification hooks that validate CRD compatibility and seatbelt short-circuit (quiesce operator, verify websocket KV replay). The description below lists what changed, test/CI outcomes, and rollback instructions. This PR targets release/v1.12 as a safety-first patch for upcoming private upgrades.
1) add rollback safety controller and reversible-plan library; 2) add terraform/plan-canary module and example pipeline; 3) add restore-rehearsal script + sandbox job; 4) helm: post-upgrade-verifier job and chart values; 5) docs: upgrade playbook additions and runbook snippets; 6) tests: e2e rehearsals and unit coverage for reversible-plan
Maya: Can the reversible-plan library handle non-transactional DDLs (ALTER TYPE, drop column)? Please document limitations.
Author (Asha): The current implementation annotates non-reversible steps and will block canary promotion; added a docs section that enumerates limitations and manual remediation steps.
Liam: Terraform canary job looks good but we should ensure state locking is never targeted at prod statefile. Add explicit backend overrides.
Author (Asha): Added backend override and isolated S3 bucket configuration for canary pipeline; test artifact shows no writes to prod state.
Jian: CI flake on e2e rehearsal initial run — looks like timing assumptions in operator quiesce. Requested a retries/backoff fix.
Author (Asha): Updated quiesce logic with exponential backoff and added idempotent timeouts. Re-ran rehearsals and CI passed.
Maya: Approve on safety grounds after confirming docs and runbook additions.
Adds reversible migration plans, automated restore rehearsals, Terraform plan canary pipeline, and Helm post-upgrade verifications to reduce upgrade blast radius. Operators should read docs/upgrade_playbook.md before scheduling tenant upgrades.

payload.body:
Summary: This PR introduces a control-plane endpoint lifecycle manager for the private installer along with an optional namespace-level DNS mirroring mode that keeps customer-private control-plane DNS names resolvable across shared and delegated zones.

Motivation: Customers deploying Redwood Private in VPCs across accounts and AZs ran into two recurring issues: (1) transient endpoint drift during rolling upgrades / node replacement that left stale ENIs and SG attachments; (2) split-horizon DNS complexity for cross-account privatelink setups where control-plane services live in different route domains. The goal is to make endpoint lifecycle deterministic, idempotent, and auditable, and to provide a low-risk DNS mirroring option to avoid manual route53 delegation edits.

Design:
- endpoint-lifecycle-manager: a reconciler (installer controller) that performs create/refresh/revoke cycles for control-plane privatelink endpoints. It tracks resource intent via tags and a small controlplane-state SSM parameter for cross-run coordination. The reconciler enforces graceful drain: a handshake that verifies active connections and KV cache warmup before swap.
- ephemeral-auth-tokens: short-lived IAM policies attached during endpoint creation to allow cross-account accept/attach without giving permanent rights. Tokens are rotated on every successful reconciliation.
- namespace DNS mirroring: an opt-in installer flag (values.controlplane.dnsMirrorNamespaces) that causes the installer to maintain CNAME records in a mirror zone (customer-controlled) and create conditional forwarding entries in the control-plane VPC resolver. Mirror entries are updated in a staged fashion to avoid TTL cliffs.
- Rollout semantics: canary by namespace; can be executed per-region. Reconciler supports a dry-run mode and a staged commit strategy that lists planned changes before applying them.

Implementation highlights:
- Terraform: new module modules/controlplane/endpoint_lifecycle with idempotent create/update hooks, prereq checks for IAM roles and route53 permissions. Added outputs for mirror zone name and change-batch id.
- Helm: charts/controlplane/templates/endpoint-reconciler-deployment.yaml and values.yaml flags for dnsMirrorNamespaces, reconcilerConcurrency, and dryRun.
- Installer: pkg/installer/reconciler/endpoint_manager.go implements the state machine (intent -> provision -> attach -> verify -> publish-dns -> finalize) and exposes metrics for reconciliation duration and transient failures.
- Scripts: scripts/upgrade/rollback-ephemeral-endpoints.sh to assist migration during emergency rollbacks.
- Tests: tests/e2e/controlplane/dns_mirroring_test.go added to validate TTL-safe updates, and tests/integration/endpoint_reconcile_test uses a mocked AWS API with recorded fixtures.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature-flag disabled by default.
2) Enable reconciler in a staging account with dnsMirrorNamespaces set for a single namespace and run dry-run for 24h.
3) Flip to commit mode and monitor reconciliation metrics & Route53 change-batches.
4) Canary to one production account/region for 48h.
5) Full enable across accounts.

Rollback: reconciler supports revert-to-previous-state which re-applies last-change-batch for DNS and reattaches previous ENI for 10m window; scripts/upgrade/rollback-ephemeral-endpoints.sh provides an operator workflow.

Observability:
- New metrics: controlplane_endpoint_reconcile_duration_ms, controlplane_endpoint_reconcile_errors_total, controlplane_dns_mirror_change_batches_total.
- Audit logs: reconciler writes audit entries to a reconciler-audit S3 prefix with JSON debug for every decision to aid postmortems.

Migration notes:
- Operators must grant route53:ChangeResourceRecordSets and route53:ListHostedZones to the installer role if dns mirroring is enabled.
- Cross-account acceptance still requires delegated IAM trust; ephemeral tokens avoid long-lived roles but require sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity in some setups.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for the state machine with simulated transient AWS errors.
- Integration tests with localstack recording of route53 and ec2.
- CI: terraform-validate, helm-lint, unit, integration.

Security review: scoped ephemeral tokens reviewed by security; recorded in SUP-9812. No plaintext secrets introduced.

Compatibility: The feature is opt-in and behind a Helm flag; existing installs are unaffected.

Files changed (high level): modules/controlplane/endpoint_lifecycle/main.tf, modules/controlplane/iam_roles.tf, charts/controlplane/values.yaml, charts/controlplane/templates/endpoint-reconciler-deployment.yaml, pkg/installer/reconciler/endpoint_manager.go, pkg/installer/reconciler/state_machine_test.go, scripts/upgrade/rollback-ephemeral-endpoints.sh, tests/e2e/controlplane/dns_mirroring_test.go, docs/privatelink-dns-mirroring.md, examples/controlplane/dns-mirror-example.yaml, ci/terraform-validate.yml

Commits: - "init: add endpoint lifecycle terraform module and basic plan" - "feat(reconciler): implement endpoint lifecycle state machine" - "chore(helm): add reconciler deployment + values" - "test: add e2e dns mirroring tests" - "docs: add privatelink DNS mirroring operator guide" - "ci: add terraform and helm validation steps"

Review conversation: ["Marco Li: Overall this looks good; can we make the dry-run output machine-readable (JSON) so automation can detect planned changes?","Priya Menon: Added a --output=json option and included it in the reconciler CLI; updated docs.","Ana Rodriguez: We need explicit retries for Route53 throttling errors; add exponential backoff with jitter.","Priya Menon: Implemented retry wrapper and added recorded integration tests for 429 handling.","Samir Patel: Confirmed no long-lived IAM policies created; can you add an audit event for token issuance?","Priya Menon: Added reconciler-audit S3 write for every ephemeral token issuance and rotation.","Ana Rodriguez: Please add a brief runbook for operator rollback.","Priya Menon: Included rollback script and runbook section in docs/privatelink-dns-mirroring.md"]

CI checks summary: ["unit: pass (34s)", "lint: pass (12s)", "terraform-validate: pass", "helm-lint: pass", "integration: pass (retries: 1)", "e2e: pass (flaky: rerun succeeded)"]

Changed files (detailed list): ["modules/controlplane/endpoint_lifecycle/main.tf", "modules/controlplane/endpoint_lifecycle/outputs.tf", "modules/controlplane/iam_roles.tf", "charts/controlplane/values.yaml", "charts/controlplane/templates/endpoint-reconciler-deployment.yaml", "pkg/installer/reconciler/endpoint_manager.go", "pkg/installer/reconciler/state_machine_test.go", "scripts/upgrade/rollback-ephemeral-endpoints.sh", "tests/e2e/controlplane/dns_mirroring_test.go", "docs/privatelink-dns-mirroring.md", "examples/controlplane/dns-mirror-example.yaml", "ci/terraform-validate.yml"]

Notes on idempotency and safety:
- The Terraform module is written with lifecycle ignore_changes on ephemeral metadata tags to avoid churn when reconciler rotates tokens.
- Reconciler will not perform destructive detach operations unless the verify step confirms no active connections OR the operator explicitly sets force=true.
- DNS mirror changes are applied in a two-phase commit: prepare (create new entries with suffix .staging), verify resolution, swap CNAMEs, then garbage collect staging entries.

Merge outcome: merged to main via squash on 2025-11-12 after approvals from Marco, Ana, and Samir.

Next steps: monitor new metrics for 2 weeks, collect feedback from on-call, and prepare a short postmortem template to capture any reconciliation incidents.
Introduce endpoint lifecycle reconciler for private control plane and enable optional per-namespace DNS mirroring for cross-account Privatelink setups. No user-facing API changes; operator-facing config knobs added.
Marco Li: Overall this looks good; can we make the dry-run output machine-readable (JSON) so automation can detect planned changes?
Priya Menon: Added a --output=json option and included it in the reconciler CLI; updated docs.
Ana Rodriguez: We need explicit retries for Route53 throttling errors; add exponential backoff with jitter.
Priya Menon: Implemented retry wrapper and added recorded integration tests for 429 handling.
Samir Patel: Confirmed no long-lived IAM policies created; can you add an audit event for token issuance?
Priya Menon: Added reconciler-audit S3 write for every ephemeral token issuance and rotation.
Ana Rodriguez: Please add a brief runbook for operator rollback.
Priya Menon: Included rollback script and runbook section in docs/privatelink-dns-mirroring.md

Motivation: On private deployments we observed long reconciliation loops and spiky Vault API traffic when the SealedSecret controller attempted to re-encrypt many DB credential secrets during rotation windows. This PR decouples the SealedSecret poller into a lightweight controller and introduces a KMS-envelope wrapping hook that uses the HSM-backed KMS plugin to wrap/unwrap database credentials during backup and rotation workflows. Goals: 1) reduce Vault/API thundering during cert/key rotations, 2) ensure DB credentials stored in SealedSecrets are additionally envelope-wrapped with the customer KMS key as an extra-at-rest protection, 3) provide a safe upgrade path with a reversible migration and automated rollback on failure. What changed: - Introduced sealedsecret-poller-shim controller (separate deployment) that watches only the SealedSecret status, performs low-cost diffs, and enqueues targeted re-encrypt tasks rather than full-list reconciliation. - Added kms-envelope-hook binary and Helm pre-upgrade/post-upgrade hook templates. The hook calls the HSM KMS plugin to create an envelope key, performs an extra layer of AES-GCM wrapping for secret.Value, and stores metadata in sealed-secret annotations (k8s.redwood.com/kms-envelope-v1). - Terraform: new module redwood_private_kms_hooks with IAM role and KMS policy templates for on-prem KMS proxies, plus outputs to inject into Helm values. - Helm chart: values options for enableSealedSecretShim, kmsEnvelope.enabled, hook concurrency and backoff controls. - Migration: a two-stage rollout. Stage A (dry-run): annotate existing SealedSecrets with kms-envelope=dry-run and run the hook in validation mode to verify unwrap via HSM without writing changes. Stage B (gradual apply): patch a percentage of namespaces via the rollout controller until success criteria met. Rollback: Helm hook supports safe revert by removing annotations and re-running original SealedSecret controller on failed migration nodes. Backwards compatibility: shim is opt-in and disabled by default; existing clusters are unaffected unless the operator toggles the values. Testing: integration test harness simulates 5k SealedSecrets and runs a rotation window; end-to-end used a local HSM emulator (SoftHSM v2) and a pre-prod HSM plugin binary. Performance: in our bench runs the average reconciliation loop CPU dropped by 62% and peak Vault API calls during rotation reduced by 88%. Security review: crypto review performed, envelope metadata includes keyID, nonce, and CSROVER (opaque mac). Docs: migration guide and troubleshooting section added to the installer docs under operations/secrets. Checklist: linear ENG-2041 tracks rollout, add e2e test to perf-canary, update runbook. References: Linear ENG-2041, Jira SUP-4729 for a customer incident that motivated this change.
Liam Roberts: overall looks good; can you add a short-circuit if the HSM plugin is unreachable so post-upgrade hooks don't block helm?
Priya Patel: added connectivity timeout and non-blocking failure mode in hook (defaults to dry-run); updated docs with expectations
Maya Chen: pls add metrics for shim queue length and hook failures so SRE can alert if migration stalls
Priya Patel: added prometheus.metrics for sealedsecret_shim_queue_length and kms_hook_failures (already exposed via existing metrics endpoint)
Derrick O'Neill: verified softHSM integration and ran the perf harness; approving pending minor terraform doc tweak
Derrick O'Neill: APPROVED

Adds a fast-sync local registry seeder and snapshot-backed rollback mechanism for on-prem/offline installs. Includes a Terraform module, Helm chart hooks, e2e tests, and operator guide updates.
Motivation: Private on-prem installs frequently hit long bootstrap windows when seeding large OCI registries over slow links. This PR introduces a delta-aware fast-sync engine plus snapshot-based rollback anchors so customers can perform atomic upgrades and quickly revert to a known registry state in air-gapped or VPC environments. What changed: 1) new Terraform module redwood.local_registry that orchestrates an initial seeding plan and creates a signed snapshot manifest, 2) a sync agent (installer/bin/registry-sync) that performs checksum-driven delta pulls, resumes interrupted transfers, and applies layer-level parallelism tuned for low-latency paper networks, 3) snapshot manifest format and a lightweight anchor scheme (snap-<epoch>-<seq>) stored in the registry under a signed tag, 4) Helm chart additions: registry-mirror-init sidecar, offline-values configmap templating and a preflight hook to validate snapshot compatibility, 5) upgrade/rollback tools: installer/bin/rollback-to-snapshot that verifies chain integrity before promoting a snapshot atomically, 6) docs and runbooks under docs/installer/reg-sync.md and runbooks/rollback-playbook.md, 7) tests: e2e against a local OCI mirror and unit tests for manifest signing/verify. Rollback approach: snapshots are created before any upgrade step, indexed by monotonically increasing sequence and a signed digest. Rollback validates that the registry contains all referenced layers and performs an atomic tag swap using a temporary tag promotion flow to avoid partial reads. Backwards compatibility: the manifest schema v1 is backward compatible with our existing sealed bundle indexer; the Terraform module offers both a 'seed' and 'resume' mode. Testing and validation: ran offline e2e in a simulated 10Mbps link with large model blobs; median bootstrap time reduced 4.2x versus baseline, resume tests passed on network interruption, and rollback exercise completed within expected latency budget. Security considerations: manifests are signed with customer KMS keys when available; sidecar runs as non-root. Migration notes: existing install workflows that rely on the previous registry seeding script can opt-in to 'fast_sync=true' in the installer config. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module + docs - [x] sync agent binary + unit tests - [x] Helm chart hooks and templates - [x] rollback tool + runbook - [x] e2e validation and CI integration - [x] docs and example values How to validate locally: follow docs/installer/local-fast-sync.md to bring up a miniregistry, run terraform apply in examples/registry-seed, then run installer/bin/registry-sync --plan examples/plan.json. Related: follows discussions in INFRA-234 and reuses part of the delta-indexing code introduced in ENG-42099.
Riley Chen: Nice approach; two quick asks: please add a small integration test that simulates an interrupted transfer and also document KMS key rotation implications.
Samira Patel: Added an e2e interrupt test and a KMS rotation section in reg-sync.md, clarified how signed manifests are reissued during rotation.
Mateo Alvarez: The Terraform module looks good but can we avoid setting default wide-open ACLs on the bootstrap bucket? Suggest making ACL explicit and documenting least-privilege pattern.
Samira Patel: Updated module to require an explicit 'bootstrap_bucket_acl' variable and added an example policy in examples/terraform/README.md.
Priya Nandan: Verified helm templates with chart lint and dry-run; minor nit about indentation in preflight-hook, added LGTM after patch.
Samira Patel: Fixed indentation, addressed comment; requesting squash-merge when CI green.
