Motivation: Private installs currently lack a standardized, rollback-safe path for introducing external log sinks (Splunk HEC) and corresponding observability stack changes. This PR adds a configurable Splunk HEC forwarder integration, upgrades our observability Helm chart to be rollback-atomic, and introduces a lightweight Rollback Operator that coordinates pre/post-helm hooks for state snapshot/restore of Prometheus and Grafana. The change set spans Helm, Terraform, and the installer operator so tenants can enable Splunk forwarding without risking dashboard or metrics loss on failed upgrades. Key design points: 1) Splunk forwarder implemented as an optional Vector-based sidecar DaemonSet that can be toggled via values.observability.splunk.enabled and configured with sealed secret + KMS-backed secret rotation. 2) Terraform module observability now exposes observability_namespace and splunk_hec_endpoint variables and conditionally provisions RBAC and network policy rules for VPC-restricted HEC endpoints. 3) Helm chart changes introduce an observability-prebackup Job and observability-postrestore Job triggered via Helm hooks; the Rollback Operator watches HelmRelease annotations (installed by the installer) and, on failed upgrades, runs the postrestore with a locked operation to restore Prometheus TSDB snapshots and Grafana provisioning state, then reconciles the log-forwarder state. 4) Dashboard promotion flow: dashboards added to charts/dashboards/promoted are pushed to a tenant-specific Grafana folder via the sidecar; promotion includes a dry-run flag and semantic versioned metadata to avoid unintentional overwrites. 5) Alerts: We add a templated PrometheusRule which defaults to a conservative alert evaluation window and includes tenant tagging for routed alertmanager grouping. Security: Splunk HEC credentials are stored as sealed-secrets; installer wiring adds optional KMS key reference for cloud KMS or a path for HSM-backed secrets in air-gapped installs. Migration plan: This PR includes an upgrade playbook that runs preflight checks (disk enough for snapshot, available replicas) and an automated verification step that queries Prometheus for target scrape health and runs a dashboard checksum compare. Testing: Unit tests for helm templates, an e2e in the private CI that validates a simulated failed upgrade path and verifies rollback restores Prometheus targets and dashboard folder contents. Checklist: - [x] Helm templates and hooks implemented - [x] Terraform variables and docs updated - [x] Rollback Operator prototype + CRD + controller tests - [x] Sealed-secret + KMS wiring documented - [x] Upgrade playbook and runbook added - [x] e2e verification job in CI
Evan Kim: Can we avoid DaemonSet in air-gapped environments by making the forwarder a sidecar on the log-aggregator? Also add a note about HEC endpoint cert validation.
Maya Patel (author): We added values.observability.splunk.deploymentMode with options [daemonset, sidecar] and documented cert validation. For air-gapped installs the default will be sidecar attached to the existing log-aggregator deployment.
Lina Gomez: Rollback Operator looks promising. Please add a leader-election and annotation-based semaphore so two controllers don't run concurrently in HA setups.
Maya Patel (author): Added a lease-based leader election and annotation lock. Tests updated to simulate concurrent reconcile loops.
Theo Rains: CI flaky test in private e2e: 'prometheus snapshot restore step' times out occasionally. Recommend increasing timeout and surface a retry metric.
Maya Patel (author): Increased snapshot restore timeout from 5m to 15m and added a retriable job wrapper. CI rerun is green.
Add optional Splunk HEC forwarder (Vector) with sealed-secret + KMS support; introduce Rollback Operator to ensure safe rollback of Prometheus TSDB and Grafana provisioning state; new Terraform observability variables (observability_namespace, splunk_hec_endpoint); see docs/private-installer/observability-splunk-hec.md for upgrade playbook and runbook.

Motivation: on large on-prem installs the full airgap bundle push and mirror updates take too long and make upgrades brittle. This PR introduces an incremental vendor snapshot format and associated registry delta application logic so mirror appliances can fetch/apply only changed asset groups, plus a kubelet-preload hook that pre-warms kernel modules and large runtime libraries on hosts that lack fast network access. Design summary: (1) snapshot format v1.1: top-level manifest points to named asset groups (images, charts, artifacts) with per-group content hashes and an optional parent-snapshot reference enabling incremental diffs; (2) registry-sync delta applier: server-side component that computes minimal push set and a client-side apply step that validates checksums and performs atomic swap; (3) GC-aware index: keep last N snapshots with a thin-refcounted index to avoid re-pushing unchanged blobs; (4) kubelet-preload hook: a small init container and a systemd-friendly unit that pulls and extracts preflight artifacts (kernel modules, containerd prefetch layers, nvidia drivers) into a host staging path before kubelet starts to avoid expensive runtime pulls. This PR contains installer UX (airgap index generation CLI), registry indexer, helm chart changes to expose preloadDaemonSet and a loader Job, terraform module additions for mirror lifecycle, and documentation/upgrade notes. Testing: local integration harness simulated slow links (100ms RTT, 10Mbps) and applied 10 incremental snapshots with a synthetic 8% asset churn to validate delta sizes and resume behavior; CI includes airgap-e2e matrix with k3s and rke2. Migration and upgrade notes: new snapshot format is backwards-compatible; the indexer emits a parent reference and a compatibility flag; older mirror-appliances ignore parent and perform full apply. Operators performing upgrades should run `rwi airgap inspect --dry-run` to preview delta size before applying. Rollback: snapshots are applied atomically using swap-and-validate; the apply step creates a timestamped symlink and performs a post-apply health check; on failure the previous symlink is retained and the apply aborts. Security: manifests are signed with cosign; registry-sync validates signatures and rejects unsigned snapshots when the "require_signed_snapshots" flag is true. Checklist: [x] Snapshot format and generator CLI implemented, [x] Server-side delta computation implemented, [x] Client apply + atomic swap implemented, [x] Kubelet preload hook unit and Helm values added, [x] Terraform module for mirror lifecycle added, [x] Integration tests with slow-link simulation included, [x] Docs and upgrade notes updated. Related: ENG-2179, INF-903, SUP-489. Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2179/airgap-incremental-snapshots; cosign verification reference https://github.com/sigstore/cosign. Manual steps and troubleshooting are in docs/airgap/incremental-snapshots.md
Daniel Cho (2024-11-08): This is a strong iteration. Two questions: 1) how does the GC avoid accidentally dropping blobs referenced by older snapshots used by existing clusters? 2) can we expose a dry-run that reports OCI blob diff sizes without downloading?
Sofia Patel (2024-11-08): Answered: GC uses refcounts computed from the indexer across the last N snapshots configurable via mirror.retention_count; the dry-run mode for registry-sync computes and reports blob deltas using remote manifest queries only, no downloads.
Priya Nair (2024-11-10): Please add an option to require cosign signing for applies in the helm chart values and document the operator workflow when signature checks fail.
Sofia Patel (2024-11-10): Added require_signed_snapshots value with default=false and documented failure modes and remediation steps in docs.
Ethan McBride (2024-11-12): CI reported intermittent failure in kubelet-preload e2e when host disk is slow (ext4 with heavy journal). Suggest adding configurable timeouts and a preflight disk-check to the Job.
Sofia Patel (2024-11-12): Implemented disk-check and made timeouts configurable via values.preload.timeouts. Re-ran e2e matrix and green.
Marta Ruiz (2024-11-13): Security scan flags cosign-wrapper as shipping an unpinned cosign version; please pin the cosign release in packaging and add a CI step to validate checksum. Also request a short security blurb in release notes.
Sofia Patel (2024-11-13): Pinned cosign to v1.12.0 and added CI checksum check. Added security note to release notes.
airgap: add incremental snapshot format (v1.1) and delta apply to reduce mirror sync time
installer: kubelet-preload hook to pre-warm kernel modules and runtime layers on air-gapped hosts
packaging: mirror lifecycle terraform module and GC-aware indexer
security: cosign-based snapshot signing support and optional enforcement
Preview delta size: rwi airgap inspect --snapshot new.snap.tar.gz --dry-run
Enable signature enforcement: set values.require_signed_snapshots=true in charts/airgap/values.yaml
Rollbacks are atomic: the apply step creates a symlink swap; inspect /var/lib/redwood/mirror/current for active snapshot
Retention: default mirror.retention_count is 3, increase for longer rollbacks

Motivation: private control plane installs in cross-account environments require automated DNS forwarding, secure ENI-based interface endpoints, and least-privilege security group peering rules. This PR adds Terraform modules and installer orchestration hooks to provision cross-account Route53 forwarding, create interface VPC endpoints with ENI attachments for the control plane, and a small Helm chart tweak to surface the controlPlane.vpcEndpointId setting. Summary: 1) New Terraform module terraform/modules/vpc-crossaccount-dns-forwarding that creates a Route53 outbound/inbound resolver association, IAM role for cross-account zone delegation, and conditional resource creation for hosted zones or delegated subzones. 2) VPC peering and security group automation in terraform/modules/vpc-peering-secgrp including explicit ephemeral rule creation, deny-by-default security group templates, and automated route table propagation for peering connections. 3) Installer orchestration changes in installer/upgrade to run a preflight DNS/peering validator and to annotate created endpoints for safe rollback. 4) Helm change to redwood-private/control-plane values to accept vpcEndpointId and configure internal service discovery via DNS suffix forwarding. Migration notes and rollbacks are included as outputs to the installer run. Backwards compatibility: module uses feature flags so existing single-account installs are unaffected. Testing: unit plan tests for Terraform modules, integration test that deploys two VPCs in the CI AWS account with delegated hosted zone, and manual validation steps in CONTRIBUTING docs.

Maya Chen: IAM role limited to route53:AssociateHostedZone and route53:DisassociateHostedZone and sts:AssumeRole. Added TTL note to installer/README.md.

Maya Chen: Added opt_out_for_route_propagation variable and default selection logic to choose route tables tagged with redwood:control-plane=true. Documented behavior in module README.

This PR introduces a policy-driven failover automation stack for private deployments: a lightweight Helm operator that surfaces 'runbooks-as-code' as Kubernetes CRs and executes them safely (prechecks, dry-run, gated step progression), plus a Terraform module and Helm chart changes to support cross-AZ load-balancer failover and restore hooks. Motivation: customers running Redwood Private in VPC/on-prem clusters asked for an automated, auditable failover workflow that can be triggered manually or by alerting playbooks and that can be rehearsed as code. What changed: 1) new component 'runbook-operator' Helm chart (charts/runbook-operator) and CRD + controller to run templated runbooks as Jobs, capture step outputs to S3-compatible store, and emit events/metrics; 2) new terraform module 'tf-modules/dr-network' that creates cross-AZ LB configs, health-checks, and an optional floating VIP via metalLB or cloud provider API; 3) installer hooks: pre-upgrade and post-upgrade DR validation jobs wired into the private-installer Helm umbrella charts; 4) runbooks/ directory with canonical DR playbooks (failover, failback, partial-az-evacuation, etc.) expressed as YAML with parameter schemas and test fixtures; 5) upgrade/rollback tool improvements: 'installer rollback --dr-validate' flag that runs the operator's post-checks and can auto-open a rollback ticket; 6) E2E canary job and chaos script used in CI to validate failover paths. Backwards compatibility: operator is optional and gated by values.runbookOperator.enabled=false by default. Testing: unit+integration for controller logic, e2e on a 3-AZ kine cluster, and a smoke terraform plan/apply in CI. Checklist: - [x] Helm chart and CRD design reviewed - [x] Terraform module interfaces documented - [x] Migration guide added to docs/private-dr.md - [x] Smoke e2e and CI jobs added - [x] Security review for S3 credential handling completed Rollout plan: staged canary in Dedicated -> Private trial customers -> general availability. Related: ENG-4821 (DR runbook operator), ENG-4897 (installer failover hooks), SUP-9112 (customer incident that motivated automated failover).
Liam Chen: Can the operator run steps in parallel? Concern about locking when multiple playbooks reference same resources.
Priya Nair: Operator supports step-level locking via a lightweight ConfigMap mutex; parallelism is opt-in per-runbook. Added tests for concurrent runs.
Marisol Ortega: Terraform module needs clearer inputs for cloud vs metal deployments.
Priya Nair: Added variable 'provider_mode' and example files for aws/gcp/onprem; documented in README.
Noah Patel: CI flaked once on e2e when chaos injected network partition too early; recommend adding a readiness wait.
Priya Nair: Added readiness probe and extended wait in chaos script; re-ran canary and CI is green.

- Introduce terraform module 'dr-network' for cross-AZ LB and optional VIP.

Motivation and summary: This PR introduces two cooperating automation pieces for private installs: (1) a dashboard-seed CronJob + provisioning sidecar pattern to ensure Grafana tenant folders are populated deterministically on first install and after upgrades, and (2) an alert-promotion Kubernetes operator that can safely move PrometheusRule alerts from a cluster-wide 'staging' namespace into tenant-scoped folders with optional canary promotion semantics. The goal is to reduce manual dashboard and alert bootstrap steps for air-gapped/private customers and to make rolling upgrades/rollbacks of alert rules safe and auditable.

What changed (high level):
- New k8s controller: observability/alert-promotion-operator (small controller in Go) - watches PrometheusRule staging namespace and creates/updates tenant-scoped PrometheusRule objects + creates a corresponding Grafana provisioning manifest to surface the alerts in tenant folders. Promotion is opt-in via annotation and supports a 'promote-once' safe guard.
- Dashboard seeding: chart/grafana/templates/cronjob-dashboard-seed.yaml - CronJob uses the grafana-provisioning sidecar approach and a one-shot seeding container to upload JSON dashboards on initial creation. It is idempotent and uses a ConfigMap-backed list of seeds.
- Prometheus state migration helper: tools/prom-migrate/ - small idempotent helper to rename legacy label keys used in older private installs (cluster_id -> tenant_id) and to copy over recording rule names safely when customers upgrade from older versions. This helper is invoked as part of the Helm post-upgrade hook when migration_needed=true.
- Terraform: modules/private-installer/main.tf - adds optional input enable_observability_seed (default false) and a toggle for Grafana provisioning RBAC and storage class for dashboard artifacts.
- Helm: values.yaml and chart defaults updated with feature toggles, RBAC roles for the operator, and reasonable resource requests/limits.
- E2E: e2e/observability/ - added smoke tests that validate seeding runs on a fresh cluster and that promotion operator correctly creates tenant PrometheusRule + Grafana provisioning entry.

Commits (summary):
- 7f3a1c9: initial operator scaffold + CRD wiring
- b1d4f7e: implement promotion logic + annotation handling and locking
- c2e8a2a: add dashboard seed cronjob, provisioning templates, and example seeding manifests
- 1a9f4bb: terraform input and docs for enabling feature in private installs
- 4c5d9ea: add prom-migrate helper and helm hook integration
- 9b7e2d3: tests, CI fixes, and RBAC adjustments after review

Files changed (high level):
- charts/grafana/templates/cronjob-dashboard-seed.yaml
- charts/grafana/values.yaml (seed list, sidecar toggles)
Adds an idempotent dashboard seeding job plus a small operator that automates safe promotion of alert rules and dashboard provisioning across tenant folders. Includes Terraform variable for enabling the feature and Helm value defaults. No user-facing breaking changes.
Evelyn Park (reviewer): Are we sure the seeding approach works in air-gapped installs without external internet access? Please document the required bundle layout.
Author (Priya): The seed job uses bundled JSONs supplied via the installer tarball; I've added docs and an example tar layout under docs/private-installer/observability-seed.md.
Tomás Silva (reviewer): RBAC looks permissive for the operator - can you narrow permissions to just configmaps, prometheusrules, and provisionings? Also add tests for operator restart resilience.
Author: Reduced RBAC to a tight set (ConfigMaps, PrometheusRule, Secrets for grafana credentials, and a custom provisioning ConfigMap). Added controller unit test for leader election and restart recovery.
Aisha Khan (reviewer): Add exponential backoff for API errors when creating Grafana provisioning manifests (we've seen 429s during large installs).
Author: Added retry with jitter and added note in release docs recommending controller CPU/Memory defaults for contention scenarios.
Tomás (approver): Verified on local airgapped cluster and example tenant; approving now.
Local integration tests + e2e observability smoke tests run in CI. Verified airgapped install flow manually on customer-sim cluster. Added unit tests for controller and helm hook scenarios.
Operator and cronjob are designed to be safe on rollback: seeding is idempotent and promotion operator marks promoted rules with an annotation so the Helm rollback can detect and preserve vs delete. Prom-migrate writes no-destructive operations unless --apply is passed.
RBAC scoped to minimal resources; grafana credentials are always pulled from customer-managed Secret. No new external network access is required for default behavior; seeding bundles are delivered with the installer artifact.

Motivation: customers running Redwood Private reported two correlated issues during multi-stage upgrades: (1) intermittent restore failures when bringing up an older control plane from a newer DB state, and (2) upgrades that included non-reversible schema migrations accidentally allowing downgrades to proceed. This PR adds a pragmatic, operator-friendly restore bootstrapping flow for Postgres backups, a lightweight schema-drift preflight validator, and a downgrade gate that blocks non-reversible downgrade attempts.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds an idempotent restore bootstrap script (installer/scripts/pg_restore_bootstrap.sh) that performs ordered steps: restore base snapshot -> apply reversible shim migrations -> populate migration_metadata table -> run post-restore consistency checks. The script is safe to re-run and publishes a restore-token to S3 to avoid concurrent restores.
- Introduces a schema-drift preflight check in the installer (installer/preflight/schema_drift_check.go) used by both the Helm pre-upgrade hook and the rwictl CLI. The check compares current DB schema fingerprint against the expected release fingerprint and fails fast if incompatible, with clear operator-facing remediation hints.
- Adds a downgrade gate to the private installer that inspects the release's migration manifest. If the manifest contains migrations marked "non-reversible", the gate prevents applying a release with an older version unless an explicit --force-downgrade WITH operator confirmation is supplied. This is enforced in the Helm pre-upgrade hook and Terraform plan validation.
- Helm: add pre-upgrade and post-restore hooks to perform safe snapshot creation and to run the schema preflight before live traffic is switched (helm/templates/pre-upgrade-snapshot-hook.yaml, helm/templates/post-restore-hook.yaml).
- Terraform: add restore verification resources and data sources (terraform/modules/backup/restore.tf) that can be used in automated restore pipelines to assert restore-token and checksum match.
- CLI: extend rwictl restore workflow with a --bootstrap flag and progress output (installer/cli/rwictl/restore.go).
- Docs: add an operator playbook with step-by-step restore and downgrade guidance (docs/ops/restore-playbook.md).

Why this is different from previous work: prior PRs focused on atomic migration rollbacks and snapshot preservation; this one focuses on making restores idempotent and safe when control plane versions and DB schemas diverge, plus an explicit downgrade safety gate tied to migration metadata.

Testing and validation: unit tests for schema fingerprinting and migration manifest parsing were added (tests/unit/schema_drift_test.go). An e2e roundtrip test was added that runs a restore -> bootstrap -> upgrade -> downgrade cycle (tests/e2e/restore_roundtrip_test.go). During CI we observed a flaky e2e that required an extra retry boundary; the test harness was hardened.

Upgrade notes for operators: follow docs/ops/restore-playbook.md. For automated restores use the terraform data source to verify restore-token before promoting traffic. To bypass the downgrade gate you must run rwictl restore --from-s3 <snapshot> --bootstrap --allow-unsafe-downgrade and acknowledge the risk; this flag is intentionally noisy in logs.

Security notes: restore tokens are short-lived and stored encrypted in S3 with KMS. The bootstrap script enforces least-privilege assumptions (separate restore role) and writes audit entries to the installer audit log.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add bootstrap script and CLI plumbing
- [x] Add Helm hooks and Terraform verify resources
- [x] Add schema-drift preflight and tests
- [x] Update operator docs and playbook
- [x] Run and stabilize e2e restore roundtrip

Rollout plan: ship in v1.8.4 as part of the private-installer patch release. Operators should schedule a backup snapshot before applying the new installer and run a restore dry-run using the terraform verify data source.

Samir Patel (2026-02-16): Please add explicit unit tests for the restore-token expiry path — I saw a flake locally when token rotation occurs.
Asha Nair (2026-02-16): Added token expiry unit tests and updated the bootstrap to early-exit on expiry; PTAL.
Evelyn Chen (2026-02-17): The schema fingerprint algorithm needs to tolerate comment-only changes; added suggestion to canonicalize by ignoring COMMENT statements.
Asha Nair (2026-02-17): Implemented canonicalization and added a test vector. Also updated docs to mention comment-only drift is ignored.
Liam O'Connor (2026-02-18): Can we make the Helm pre-upgrade hook idempotent across failed hook runs? Observed helm retry causing double snapshot creation.
Response: converted snapshot creation to a create-if-not-exists flow keyed by release name.
Samir Patel (2026-02-19): e2e started failing on CI due to timing around primary promotion; added a retry with exponential backoff in the test harness. Rerun CI.
3 commits:
- Add pg_restore_bootstrap.sh and idempotency token handling (Asha Nair)
- Implement schema drift preflight and CLI integration (Evelyn Chen)
- Helm hooks, terraform verify data source, docs and tests (Samir Patel)
Operator-facing: add idempotent Postgres restore bootstrap, schema-drift preflight, Helm pre-upgrade snapshot hooks, and a downgrade safety gate. See docs/ops/restore-playbook.md for runbook.

## Summary
This PR adds customer-facing documentation for the Runtime LTS channel: what it is, who it’s for, how long it’s supported, what changes qualify for backport, and how to read the “slower-change” LTS release notes. It also adds Private deployment upgrade/rollback guidance links and clarifies version pinning semantics.

## Why
Enterprise Dedicated/Private customers have been asking for (a) a stable runtime baseline for 6–12+ months, (b) a predictable patch cadence, and (c) an explicit backport policy with a clear risk rubric. Support and Sales also need canonical language for “what LTS covers / doesn’t cover.”

This is the docs counterpart to the Runtime LTS branch work happening in the runtime repo and the first pilot preparations.

## What’s included
- New docs page: Runtime LTS channel overview
  - Definition: stability-focused runtime track intended for Dedicated + Private
  - Support window: 12 months standard, optional extension for contracted customers (wording aligned with Product)
  - Patch cadence: monthly patch releases; out-of-band security patches as needed
  - What’s not included: feature parity with mainline; experimental heuristics; non-critical refactors
- New docs page: Backport policy
  - Eligibility buckets: Security, Sev1 correctness/crash, Sev2 major degradation
  - Risk rubric: minimal diff preference, test requirements, perf validation gates
  - Approvals: Runtime + Release Eng + SRE; expedited path for security
  - Expectations: no “best effort” for feature requests; follow-on fixes may be deferred
- New docs page: Interpreting LTS release notes
  - Taxonomy used in LTS notes (Security, Reliability/Correctness, Performance/Latency, Ops/Packaging)
  - Required metadata: affected versions, known issues, mitigations, compatibility matrix pointers
  - Guidance on when to upgrade: mandatory vs recommended vs optional patches
- Upgrade/rollback guidance pointers
  - Links to Private installer pinning + checksum verification section
  - Rollback checklist + “validate after upgrade” steps
- Glossary and FAQ updates
  - “LTS vs latest” selection guidance
  - “How do I request a backport?” (routes to Support intake + required info)

## Customer-facing wording highlights
- LTS is a stability track. New features land on mainline first and may not be backported.
- Backports prioritize correctness, security, and high-severity reliability issues.
- LTS release notes are “slower-change” and include explicit known issues + mitigations.

## Files / structure
- docs/runtime/lts/overview.md (new)
- docs/runtime/lts/backport-policy.md (new)
- docs/runtime/lts/release-notes-guide.md (new)
- docs/private/upgrade/runtime-lts.md (new)
- docs/support/backport-requests.md (updated)
- docs/release-notes/lts-format.md (new)
- docs/_includes/compatibility-matrix-links.md (new)
- docs/glossary.md (updated)
- docs/faq/runtime-lts.md (new)
- mkdocs.yml (nav wiring)
- redirects.yml (new redirects for older “release channels” page)

Motivation: we've observed short-lived egress oversubscriptions in eu-west and us-central during large batch replays and cross-region failover exercises. Those spikes cause transient SLO risk (95p latency violations) and aggressive circuit flips that cascade to downstream dependent services. This change introduces 'Steadyhand', an anticipatory egress gate that coordinates SLO enforcement, a region-aware circulator (soft circuit), and a graded load-shedding path to avoid abrupt failovers. Key goals: 1) reduce SLO violation risk during brief egress congestion windows; 2) avoid hard cuts (hard circuit opens) where a gentle throttled window preserves connectivity; 3) provide clear telemetry and a rollbackable rollout for on-call to revert quickly. Design summary: Steadyhand runs as a small control-plane daemon co-located with the regional router. It subscribes to existing capacity signals (egress_capacity_pressure, kv_pressure) and SLO-derived risk score from the global SLO enforcer. When pressure crosses a calibrated threshold it begins a two-phase response: (A) anticipatory throttle: progressively reduce burst allowance for non-critical tenants and mark requests with X-Egress-Mode:soft-throttle so downstream logging can correlate; (B) soft-quarantine window: place high-risk tenants into a timed probation with exponentially increasing backoff but still allow low-rate traffic to flow (avoids complete KV eviction). The mechanism integrates with circuit broker via a new 'softOpen' state which records a lease token and emits audit events to chronicle service decisions. Rollout plan: feature gate off by default; small canary in us-east-1 -> expanded to eu-west as metrics validate (SLO delta < 0.5pps). Emergency rollback: scripts/hotfix-rollout.sh toggles steadyhand=false and respawns router. Checklist: - [x] design doc and runbook written (docs/steadyhand.md) - [x] unit + integration tests (test/integration/egress_gate_test.go) - [x] telemetry and dashboards (observability: steadyhand/egress_pressure, steadyhand/slo_risk) - [x] API contract: X-Egress-Mode header and softOpen lease events - [x] rollout script and ops runbook commits summary: 1) initial control-plane and gate state machine 2) SLO enforcer hooks + risk scoring 3) circuit broker softOpen support 4) telemetry streams and dashboard definitions 5) integration tests and canary config changed areas/files: - cmd/steadyhand/main.go: new control-plane binary that drives the gate - pkg/slo/enforcer.go: add RiskScore API and minor refactor to expose windowed risk - pkg/circuit/broker.go: add softOpen/softClose transitions and lease metadata - pkg/egress/gate.go: throttle policy and tenant probation map - charts/steadyhand/values.yaml: canary/default config knobs - docs/steadyhand.md: runbook and dashboard links - test/integration/egress_gate_test.go: deterministic congestion simulator - scripts/hotfix-rollout.sh: emergency toggle and fast rollback samples Testing and CI: unit tests cover state machine transitions, deterministic TTL expiry, and header emission. Integration test simulates egress pressure and validates SLO delta and no hard-open circuit within the probation window. CI checks: lint (pass), unit (pass), integration (flaky -> fixed second run), e2e (pass on canary), bundle-sbom (pass). Observability: add steadyhand.egress_pressure gauge, steadyhand.slo_risk histogram, steadyhand.softquarantine_events counter. Backwards compatibility: the header X-Egress-Mode is opt-in; tenants not aware of the header observe no behavioral changes. Release notes: Steadyhand introduces an opt-in egress gate that provides smoother degradation under transient egress overloads and reduces the chance of hard failover. Ops runbook included in docs. Risks: mis-calibrated thresholds could cause unnecessary throttling — mitigated by conservative defaults and canary rollout. Long term: consider automatic learning of thresholds per tenant based on p99 tail latencies and usage patterns.
Diego Muñoz: Nice incremental approach. Please add a metric for 'soft_throttle_active_tenants' and ensure we tag by tenant cohort for postmortem aggregation.
Aisha Raman (author): Added soft_throttle_active_tenants counter and tenant_cohort label in telemetry commit c3d4e5f.
Priya Shah: Integration test looked flaky initially — can you make the simulated jitter deterministic? Also, add a comment in enforcer.go about the window sizing rationale.

Liam O'Connor: Approving pending the hotfix rollback script includes a safety check that prevents toggling steadyhand off during region maint windows.

Motivation: Customers running Private deployments reported long apply times and frequent terraform lock contention when multiple tenant teams concurrently change infra (GPU pools, network attachments). A single monolithic tfstate also makes targeted rollbacks and per-tenant upgrades risky. This PR introduces a tenant-isolated state layout plus a lease-based locking option tailored for on-prem/private installs, and extends the GPU nodepool module to support explicit subnet affinity mapping so GPU pools can be co-located with customer-provided subnets. The change includes: 1) New backend conventions: per-tenant state workspaces (backend template + naming), optional MinIO/GCS backend examples, and an on-prem Consul-session lease mechanism for state locks (fallback to S3/DynamoDB in cloud). 2) A migration helper (state-splitter) that generates per-tenant state snapshots and a dry-run plan for operator review. 3) Enhancements to modules/gpu-nodepool: subnet_affinity_map variable (az->subnet-id), preferred_host_pools flag, and ephemeral-ip allocation policy for burst pools. 4) Console/operator-facing docs (docs/migrations/tenant-state-split.md) and an upgrade checklist. 5) Tests and CI: terraform validate/fmt, unit tests for the migrator, and an e2e private-installer test that exercises nodepool creation with subnet affinity. Rollout plan: feature gate in values.yaml defaults to off; operators can enable per-cluster; run state-splitter in dry-run mode, review generated plans, then flip over. Rollback: state-splitter also emits rejoin plan to remerge per-tenant states back into the consolidated state in case of rollback. Impact: No forced downtime for runtime workloads; terraform apply ordering will change for operators who opt-in (see migration doc). Checklist: - [x] Implement per-tenant backend templates - [x] Consul lease-based locking implementation (on-prem) - [x] GPU nodepool subnet affinity variables and tests - [x] state-splitter tool + dry-run validation - [x] Docs + upgrade checklist - [x] CI green (after rerun)
Ethan Morales: Can we avoid adding another mandatory backend type? Suggest default is opt-in (enabled=false) and document both Consul and DynamoDB options.
Priya Nair (author): Agreed — made it opt-in. Consul lease is only used when operator flips enable_consul_lease=true. Added cloud-backed DynamoDB example in backends/README.
Lina Chen: The subnet_affinity_map looks good, but how does it interact with autoscaler labels? We should ensure node labels are set consistently so the operator can target pools.
Priya Nair: Added preferred_host_pools and label propagation in nodepool module. Updated examples and tests to verify labels are present after apply.

Ethan Morales: Approve with minor doc suggestions.

GPU nodepool module gains subnet_affinity_map and preferred_host_pools to colocate GPU node pools with operator subnets. Migration tool emits dry-run and rejoin plans. Motivation: customers running Redwood Private in multi-AZ/on-prem topologies requested an automated, auditable 'switchback' path that performs controlled failover and then a validated failback (switchback) when primary capacity is restored. This PR introduces the Switchback Operator (controller+CRD), idempotent Terraform rollback hooks, Helm lifecycle evacuation hooks, and a runbook-as-code integration for drill automation. Changes include a lightweight controller that orchestrates: preflight validations (consistency/kv-cache sync check), staged evacuations (pod/VM cordon->drain->kv checkpoint), model routing updates via our private control-plane API, and a reversible switchback plan with automatic canary verification. Checklist: - [x] Implement Switchback CRD and controller with leader-election and rate-limited reconciliation - [x] Add helm/templates/evacuate-hook.yaml with post-install/upgrade hooks and pre-delete draining hooks - [x] Provide terraform/modules/hadr/rollback_hook.tf (idempotent, pessimistic locks, state checks) - [x] Add runbooks/hadr/switchback-playbook.yaml as executable playbook for drills - [x] Add e2e-hadr test harness and new unit tests - [x] Add Linear links in code and server logs for observability Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-5123/switchback-operator-design, runbook template https://confluence.redwood.ai/hadr/switchback-runbook. Commits: ["a3f4bd1 Add Switchback CRD and controller scaffolding","b9cde88 Implement idempotent terraform rollback hook","d2f0a7e Helm evacuate hooks and templates","e6f98b1 Runbook-as-code and test harness","f1aa554 Fix flakey e2e assertions and improve lock handling"]. Small illustrative snippet: helm/templates/evacuate-hook.yaml (excerpt) "apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: ""{{ include "redwood.fullname" . }}-evacuate""
spec:
  template:

      containers:

Rollback semantics: terraform rollback hook is designed to be idempotent and declarative; it acquires a named lock, checks live routing table and kv cache hashes, performs partial rollbacks in stages, and exposes a dry-run mode. Motivation: Private installs have been drifting from the upstream observability configuration over time (dashboard edits, alert fingerprint changes, and Helm values drift). This PR adds automated drift detection for Prometheus/Grafana manifests and an opinionated dashboard versioning and rollback path integrated into the installer tooling. Goals: 1) Detect when cluster-side observability resources differ from the last-applied installer state; 2) Capture and version dashboards and alert rules as part of release artifacts; 3) Provide a safe rollback path that can reapply the last-known-good dashboard set without disrupting metrics ingestion; 4) Make Helm/Terraform provisioning idempotent and upgrade/rollback-friendly for constrained on-prem environments. What changed (summary): - New Terraform module: terraform/modules/observability-diff - exposes an object-bucket (S3/GCS/MinIO) backing store and a small state artifact to record last-applied manifests. - Helm chart updates: charts/grafana/templates/versioned-dashboard-crd.yaml and charts/prometheus/templates/alertgroup-annotation.yaml to include metadata for installer-managed versions. - Installer CLI: bin/installer observability sync --dry-run/--apply which runs a k8s dry-run diff, uploads changed manifests to the artifacts bucket, and creates a versioned manifest pointer. - Upgrade/rollback helper: scripts/obs-rollback.sh that can rehydrate the last-known-good dashboards and reapply via Helm with a controlled canary (N pod subset) and wait-for-stable. - Drift detector controller: k8s/controller/observability-drift-controller (lightweight Go binary) that periodically scans managed namespaces and emits DriftDetected events to the console and an internal metrics endpoint. - CI pipeline: added terraform validate, helm lint, and an e2e scenario (minikube) exercising sync->apply->rollback. - Docs and runbooks: docs/observability/drift-detection.md and runbooks/observability-reconcile.md. Compatibility and safety notes: - The state bucket can be configured to use customer-provided MinIO for on-prem installations; the module supports KMS key id strings for encrypted objects. - The rollback path performs Helm upgrade with --reuse-values and a controlled maxSurge=0 canary so running services aren't restarted en masse. - Dashboard JSONs are scrubbed for cluster-specific IDs and timestamp fields prior to versioning to reduce false positives. - For GDPR/audit customers we optionalize dashboard uploads (opt-in via main installer variables). Testing and validation: - Unit: Go controller unit tests and Terraform module unit checks added. - Integration: e2e test simulates a manual dashboard edit in-cluster, runs installer observability sync --dry-run to surface drift, then sync --apply to record and push, and finally scripts/obs-rollback.sh to validate reapplication. - CI: terraform validate, helm lint, go test, and a flaky-tolerant e2e job that runs on a separate runner with minikube 1.30. Backwards-compat: Defaults maintain current behavior (installer does not upload dashboards unless observability.versioning.enabled = true). Migration: An opt-in migration step is provided (bin/installer observability migrate --from-manual) that will snapshot current dashboards on first run. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module with bucket + IAM instructions - [x] Helm chart changes for dashboard CRD versioning - [x] Controller binary + unit tests - [x] Installer CLI commands and docs - [x] Rollback script and canary logic - [x] E2E tests and CI integration Related: builds on discussion in ENG-4421 and the SRE runbook from SRE-208. Not included: SIEM forwarding (separate follow-up to wire syslog/CEF).

Lina: The rollback script should validate that the backup manifest is for the same prometheus/grafana chart versions; added chart-version metadata to the artifact (added).
Ravi: Please add Terraform state locking guidance for on-prem MinIO to avoid concurrent writes (added doc section and module notes).
Maya: Responded - added unit tests and clarified opt-in behavior in docs.
Arjun: CI e2e flake: minikube networking occasionally breaks; added retry and moved to a separate runner.

Motivation: Production control planes deployed into customer VPCs (Private) sometimes observe intermittent egress path failure when primary privatelink proxies are overloaded or when subnet affinity causes cross-AZ transient connectivity issues. This PR introduces a composable 'egress service chain' abstraction plus Route53-based DNS failover stitching to provide deterministic fallback paths, safer upgrades, and clearer observability for controlplane outbound traffic.

What this implements: a) Terraform: a new module 'egress_service_chain' that models an ordered list of egress targets (Privatelink endpoint -> zonal proxy NLB -> regional egress proxy -> S3/VPC endpoint) with conditional route table attachments and cross-account IAM roles required for peering/bind operations; b) Helm values & templates: new chart values for the installer and controlplane charts (private-controlplane.egress.serviceChain) allowing operators to declare the chain at install/upgrade time and opt into staged rollout; c) DNS failover: Route53 health checks + failover/weighted records wired to alias records for NLBs and privatelink endpoints to ensure sub-30s automatic switchover when a target becomes unhealthy; d) Security: SG templates and least-privilege IAM role bindings for the chain components and a new egress-sg preflight validator; e) Rollout tooling: a CLI hook in the installer that performs a canary swap and verifies healthchecks before applying route changes.

Files changed (high level): updated terraform modules (modules/egress_service_chain/*), hooks in installer/terraform/live/bootstrap.tf, helm charts (charts/private-controlplane/values.schema.yaml, templates/egress-chain-configmap.yaml), add e2e smoke test (test/egress_chain_smoke.sh), and docs (docs/private-deploy/egress-service-chain.md).

Migration and rollout: default behavior is backwards-compatible: service chain is opt-in via helm values. Existing deployments are unaffected until operator explicitly updates values or runs the installer hook. For customers who enable the module, the installer performs a preflight check that validates route table ownership, CIDR non-overlap, and presence of required privatelink endpoints. The canary procedure updates a per-az route attachment for 5% of controlplane traffic (via routing weight/target group attachment), monitors latency/error budgets for 15 minutes, and automatically rolls back if healthchecks trip.

Testing and verification: ran full terraform plan/apply in staging (account-stg-3), smoke tests against NLB failover scenarios (simulate target failure by deregistering target), Route53 failover verification, and added new unit tests for the terraform module's input validation. Integration pipeline initially failed on a flaky import test (terraform import of existing endpoint) — fixed by adding an import helper and retry logic; CI was re-run and passed.

Security considerations: tightened egress SGs to only allow outbound to specific privatelink and NLB ranges, added IAM role with scoped AssumeRole for cross-account peering operations, and added audit log entries for route modifications. No secrets were added; all new infra accepts existing KMS keys and follows account-bound policies.

Performance and cost: the default chain adds an NLB per-az when enabled which increases hourly infra cost moderately; however the chain enables more efficient local failover and reduces expensive cross-AZ proxy hop latencies in failure scenarios. See perf_impact below for numbers from staging.

Release notes: Adds opt-in controlplane egress service chaining with automated DNS failover and safe canary rollout. Operators must opt-in and may need to grant cross-account role for peering automation.

Related: ENG-3248 (egress stability), ENG-3301 (installer hooks), SUP-2124 (customer incident that motivated deterministic failover).
Ethan Cole: Please tighten the security group egress CIDR to the minimum set of privatelink/NLB ranges and add comments explaining the sources; also add an explicit deny for 0.0.0.0/0 where not required.
Aisha Patel: Addressed — updated modules/networking/sg-templates/egress-sg.tf with narrower egress ranges, added inline comments and a configurable extra_allowed_cidrs parameter (default empty).
Priya Narang: Request changes — add terraform import tests and make the module idempotent against pre-existing endpoints; integration pipelines failed on this previously.
Aisha Patel: Added ci/integration/terraform-import-helper.sh and retry logic; updated module to use data sources when endpoints exist. Pushed commit f9c8e12 to address flakiness.
Lena Schmidt: Approved after verification on staging and confirming preflight checks — left a 👍
Ethan Cole: Approved — I re-ran the integration suite and confirmed no regressions in installer bootstrapping.
Opt-in egress service chaining for private controlplane deployments: deterministic failover via Route53 health checks, installer canary hook, new Terraform module, tightened egress SGs. Operators must opt in and may need to grant a cross-account role for peering automation.
Default: no change. To enable, add 'privateControlPlane: { egress: { serviceChain: enabled } }' to your installer values.yaml and provide cross-account role ARN via 'egress.serviceChain.crossAccountRoleArn'. Run 'installer apply --canary' to perform a staged rollout. See docs/private-deploy/egress-service-chain.md for full checklist.
Staging (account-stg-3): terraform plan/apply, smoke test (simulate NLB target failure), Route53 failover observed <25s to fallback target. Integration pipeline initially failed due to terraform import flake; fixed and re-run. Unit tests for input validation added and passing.
Staging numbers: median egress latency during failover reduced from 420ms to 110ms when chain is enabled (local zonal NLB fallback) at cost of ~0.09 USD/hr per additional NLB per AZ. Exact numbers depend on topology.
SRE and Security reviewed SG tightening and IAM scope; added audit events for route modifications and require operator-managed KMS for any NLB certificates. No PII exfiltration risk introduced by this change.
1) publish docs site update (done); 2) notify customers via private-deploy changelog about opt-in behavior; 3) schedule rollout runbook review with SRE; 4) add observability dashboard tile for egress-chain health (follow-up PR ENG-3377).

Motivation: add a hardened zero-trust egress path for control plane VPCs that (1) provides an auditable, tenant-isolated bastion bridge for outbound control-plane management traffic, (2) implements cross-account delegated DNS stitching for control-plane endpoints, and (3) exposes an operator-safe toggle for progressive rollouts and immediate rollback. This PR bundles Terraform module changes (networking and iam), Helm chart hooks for the installer control-plane agent, and an upgrade/rollback hook for the private-installer operator. Implementation summary: - Terraform: introduce module vpc/egress_bastion_bridge. Creates a pair of AZ-aware bastion ENIs in a dedicated egress subnet with sg rules restricted to control-plane CIDRs and a proxy IAM role for signed egress requests. Adds route table association and optional Transit Gateway/Peering attachment ACLs. Adds a cross-account Route53 delegation resource (hosted zone delegation + glue) with conditional IAM assume-role to allow control plane to provision endpoint records in customer-owned zones. - Helm: add pre-upgrade/post-upgrade hooks to install a small controlplane-egress-agent DaemonSet that performs signed TLS-forwarding to the bastion bridge, emits metrics to the console (egress.latency, egress.errors), and can be disabled via values.egress.enabled=false. - Installer operator: adds a reconcile step and feature-flag to orchestrate staged promotion of DNS delegation and egress-bastion creation; supports a canary rollout using tag-based subnet selectors. - Tests and validation: end-to-end terraform plan/apply smoke in the lab (benchmark-lab), integration test that the installer can create a delegated record and validate DNS resolution from a control plane pod, and unit tests for the IAM policy templating. Rollout plan: 1) Enable feature-flag in staging clusters, 2) Create cross-account delegation in a single region and monitor DNS propagation metrics and egress latency for 48h, 3) Promote to all regions with automated remediation steps. Revert plan: operator exposes 'egress.disable' annotation to short-circuit agent; terraform destroy plan created as part of the PR for emergency teardown. Security notes: minimal IAM permissions are requested and documented in SECURITY.md; bastion ENIs are locked down to the control plane CIDR and central ops role. Backwards compatibility: default flags are off; customers must opt-in to enable delegation and bastion bridge. This description includes implementation details, testing notes, rollout and rollback instructions, and security rationale.
Marco Chen: Can we scope the bastion SG to a short-lived CIDR list instead of wide control-plane CIDR? Suggest adding ipset-based automation.
Aisha Patel: Addressed - updated module to accept allowed_ipset_id and added automation note to docs. Kept default conservative to existing control-plane CIDR for compatibility.
Devon Li: IAM policy looks tight but please add explicit deny for s3:DeleteBucket on the assume role - safety belt.
Aisha Patel: Added explicit deny for destructive S3 actions in iam/egress_assume_role.tf and added unit tests for policy generation.
Ravi Kapoor: CI flake on integration test in eu-west-1; rerun after test timeout bump. Also request a helm value to disable metrics emission when customers route metrics externally.
Aisha Patel: Increased test timeout and added values.egress.metrics.enabled flag (default true).
Introduce opt-in zero-trust egress bastion bridge and Route53 cross-account delegation for private control plane. Includes Terraform module, Helm agent, operator rollout hooks, and rollback scripts. (opt-in feature, disabled by default)

Context: This PR is primarily a requirements/alignment thread captured in the PR description + review comments to unblock implementation of Runtime LTS pinning in the Redwood Private installer. Dedicated/Private enterprise customers want: (1) the ability to pin a specific runtime patch (e.g., 1.18.1-lts) for 6–12+ months, (2) verifiable artifacts (checksums/signatures/provenance) that can be audited, and (3) a predictable rollback path when a patch introduces regressions. This PR documents and finalizes the installer-facing requirements so Release Eng can publish the right metadata and Runtime can keep semantics stable across the LTS line.

Requirements agreed in this thread:
- Pin semantics (must be explicit):
  - Installer MUST support pinning to an exact LTS patch version string (e.g., runtime=1.18.1-lts) and MUST NOT silently upgrade within the LTS line.
  - Installer SHOULD optionally support pinning by immutable image digest (sha256:...) to satisfy strict change control.
  - If both version and digest are provided, digest wins and the installer records both for audit.
- Artifact verification (enterprise default):
  - Installer MUST download a release manifest for the selected patch containing: image tag, image digest, per-arch digests, sha256 checksums for auxiliary tarballs, provenance pointer, and release notes URL.
  - Installer MUST verify sha256 checksums of downloaded tarballs (air-gapped flow) and MUST verify the runtime image digest matches the manifest when pulling from registry.
  - Signature verification: in this phase we capture requirement + interface; implementation may be gated behind availability of signing keys/verification tooling (tracked in ENG-4832). The installer will accept a --verify-signatures flag (default on when signatures exist; fallback to checksum-only with a loud warning).
- Rollback (operator safe):
  - Installer MUST support rollback to the previously installed runtime patch (one-step rollback) and MUST preserve the previous runtime image reference (tag + digest) and manifest in state.
  - Rollback MUST be supported for both online registry pulls and air-gapped artifact bundles.
  - Rollback MUST not require re-running full cluster bootstrap; it should be a targeted runtime component rollback.
- Observability + audit:
  - Installer MUST write an install record capturing: selected channel, requested version, resolved version, resolved digests, manifest checksum, and timestamps.
  - Installer MUST surface a single command to print the current pinned version + digests for audit (used in SOC2/ISO evidence requests).
- UX + defaults:
  - Default behavior for Private is unchanged (track recommended stable), but when customers opt into LTS they should see an explicit prompt/flag path that makes the “no auto-upgrades” property clear.
  - For regulated customers, we expect most to use exact version pinning, with digest pinning as a stricter option.

Non-requirements explicitly called out:
- Not promising that Private installer can automatically select “the newest patch in the LTS line” (that conflicts with change control expectations).
- Not implementing full signature verification unless Release Eng artifacts are signed consistently; however, we are locking the installer interface now.

Implementation notes included here to keep scope tight:
- New config knobs will be added under runtime: channel (stable|lts), version, digest, verify_checksums, verify_signatures.
- Installer will fetch a small JSON manifest published alongside LTS releases (owned by Release Eng). For air-gapped, customers can supply the manifest file path.
- We record state in the existing installer state directory and store the previous runtime reference for rollback.

Why a PR for requirements: This was the fastest way to converge across Release Eng, Security, and Private packaging while we already had PR-663 open for the pinning feature work. The conversation below is the canonical alignment and is referenced in the follow-up implementation commits.
Thread: clarifying requirements for Private installer pinning, checksums, and rollback for LTS artifacts

[2025-02-24] Bruno Silva (author): Pulling the requirements conversation into this PR so we can lock semantics before I land more code. The key question: do we pin by tag (1.18.1-lts) or digest, and what verification is mandatory for regulated Private?

[2025-02-24] Vivek Kulkarni: For regulated Private, tag pinning is necessary but not sufficient. Procurement wants a change ticket that points to immutable artifacts. We should support digest pinning (optional) but must at least record resolved digest even when user pins by tag. Also: no “auto-latest patch” behavior; customers explicitly approve upgrades.

[2025-02-24] Connor O'Brien: +1. Release Eng will publish an LTS manifest per patch. Proposal: installer takes runtime_version=1.18.1-lts, resolves to a manifest that includes runtime image digest(s) and checksums. If digest is supplied, skip resolution and just verify digest matches manifest when available. We’ll wire the manifest format into the LTS release pipeline.

[2025-02-25] Sahana Iyer: From CI/build standpoint, checksum verification is the minimum bar. Signature verification depends on getting key management + verification tooling into the installer runtime. Let’s add the flags now and make verify-signatures a no-op with a warning until artifacts are signed end-to-end.

[2025-02-25] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Please make the failure modes explicit: (1) missing manifest should be a hard error when channel=lts unless --allow-unverified is set; (2) checksum mismatch must hard fail; (3) signature missing should warn (for now) but be designed to become a hard fail later. We need an audit record for compliance.

[2025-02-26] Sean Gallagher: Rollback is critical. We need a one-step rollback that Support can walk customers through at 2am. Keep it targeted to runtime components and don’t touch unrelated services. Also include a “print current pinned version+digest” command so SRE can quickly confirm what’s running.

[2025-02-26] Bruno Silva: Updated the plan accordingly: explicit version pin, optional digest pin, always record resolved digest, manifest required for LTS, checksum verification hard fail. Added design for rollback to previous runtime ref.

[2025-02-27] Connor O'Brien: Confirmed: manifest will include release notes URL and SBOM pointer (if present). For first LTS patches we may have SBOM stub; that’s OK as long as we’re explicit.

[2025-02-28] Vivek Kulkarni: One more requirement: the installer should not change the pinned version on reruns unless the operator explicitly changes config. No surprise drift.

[2025-03-01] Bruno Silva: Implemented. State file stores requested + resolved refs; rerun compares and is a no-op unless config changes.

[2025-03-03] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Approved with comment: please ensure the audit record includes manifest checksum and timestamp; that’s needed for audit trails.

[2025-03-03] Connor O'Brien: Approved. We’ll align the manifest format with ENG-4832 and update Release Eng docs accordingly.

[2025-03-03] Vivek Kulkarni: Approved. This matches customer expectations from SUP-18506.
payload.title: Private installer: pinning requirements for Runtime LTS artifacts (checksums, digests, rollback)

Motivation: Private installs running in regulated environments require predictable certificate and key promotion procedures that tolerate HSM-backed KMS constraints and support fast, safe rollback. This PR introduces a small controller (expiring-cert-promoter) plus Helm/Terraform integration to pre-provision replacement TLS certs and KMS key labels, stage rolling rekey operations, and expose explicit rollout/rollback hooks to the installer. The goal is zero-downtime certificate replacement with an audited handoff and automatic safe fallback when HSM bindings or Vault sync lag.

What this changes: adds a new operator that monitors cert expiry windows and pre-stages a candidate certificate + key-wrapping metadata (labels/annotations) into Vault/SealedSecrets; introduces a KMS-labeling extension in the Terraform KMS module to declare promoted keys and HSM-operator compatible labels; updates the private-installer Helm chart with pre-upgrade/post-upgrade hooks that perform dry-run promotion and a staged traffic drain; includes a rollback-safe reencrypt plan that reverts pointers without destroying promoted keys for a grace period.

Key constraints considered: HSM-backed keys cannot be rewrapped in-place on some vendors (requires create-new + promote). Vault replication latency across zones can be multi-second; hooks include idempotent reconciliation and an explicit 'promote-confirm' gate. The controller keeps promotion metadata in annotations to allow operators to inspect staged candidates and abort promotions before final cutover.

Security notes: promotion operations mark promoted keys with a revocation-delay tag and write an audit entry to the installer audit log; we avoid exposing raw private key material outside Vault/HSM. The chart changes add RBAC rules scoped to the promoter service account and document least-privilege IAM bindings for the Terraform module.

This description contains implementation details, upgrade guidance, and manual rollback steps to help SRE and platform teams run the promotion in low-trust environments.
Samir Patel: Nice direction — can you clarify the failure mode if Vault replication lags >30s? Is there a cleanup path for half-promoted keys?
Clara Mendes: Answered: the controller marks candidate keys with 'promote:pending' and a TTL; an automatic cleanup job demotes candidates older than the TTL unless 'promote-confirm' was set. Added TTL config and docs.
Lina Zhou: Request change: tighten RBAC in the Helm chart; don't grant promoter SA cluster-admin. Also add unit tests for label canonicalization.
Clara Mendes: Addressed: promoter only gets namespaced secret access and specific KMS/Cloud HSM policy bindings. Added tests and updated chart.
1) Ensure Terraform KMS module 'promote_labels' is set for HSM providers. 2) Install chart with enablePromoter=true. 3) Run helm hook 'pre-promote' to dry-run. 4) Verify candidate cert in Vault and set 'promote-confirm' annotation when ready. 5) Post-promote job performs pointer swap; if failure, run rollback script in docs to restore pointers within grace period.
Added expiring-cert-promoter operator to pre-stage certificate/key promotions for private installs. Included Helm hooks and Terraform KMS labels to enable staged, rollback-safe certificate rotations with HSM compatibility. See docs/operations/promote-playbook.md for runbook and rollback steps.
This PR intentionally avoids auto-destruct of old keys to preserve forensic capability and to support forced rollback. Coordinate with HSM admin for providers that require offline approvals.

Background: Private installs historically used a single global tfstate for networking and GPU nodepools. That has been a scaling and blast-radius problem: a single tfstate edit can impact multiple tenants and complicates network isolation rollouts. This PR introduces a tenant-scoped tfstate sharding approach plus a runtime GPU affinity adapter that binds GPU nodepools to tenant subnets with stronger isolation guarantees. Motivation: 1) limit blast radius when changing subnet/GPU allocations; 2) enable per-tenant lifecycle (apply/rollback) for network and GPU resources; 3) simplify cross-tenant IAM scoping by isolating role bindings.

What this PR changes (summary): - terraform/modules/tfstate-sharder: new module that provides state backend mapping utilities and outputs a shard mapping manifest used by the installer. Supports S3/GCS backends with prefix-based shard keys. Includes README and usage examples. - installer bootstrap: bootstrapping code (cmd/installer/bootstrap/shard-mapper.go) now reads a shard mapping file and wires Terraform runs to the appropriate backend per-tenant. - GPU affinity adapter: a small controller deployed via Helm (helm/charts/installer/templates/gpu-affinity-adapter-deployment.yaml) that watches TenantSubnetClaim CRDs and ensures GPU nodepool labels/taints and subnet annotations reflect affinity rules. The controller is intentionally permissive by default; an operator flag enforces strict AZ-local affinity. - Migration helper: install-scripts/tfstate-migrator/migrate_shards.py provides a safe migration path from monolithic state to tenant shards. It performs a dry-run validation, writes a checkpoint file, copies state objects, validates resource IDs, and flips the mapping only after all checks pass. - IAM adjustments: modules/iam/tenant-roles.tf adds aliasing support to allow tenant-scoped roles to reference shared infra without granting global privileges.

Migration plan (high level): 1) run migration helper in dry-run mode against a snapshot; 2) run migration helper with --checkpoint-dir to create per-tenant state files and a checkpoint; 3) run installer in "drain-and-verify" mode (added flag) that verifies the shard mapping and performs a canary apply for 2 tenants; 4) if canary passes, flip the global mapping in the installer config and allow gradual rollout. Rollback: the migrator creates snapshot checkpoints and a manifest of moved resources so the installer can rebind original state if needed. See docs/private/tfstate-sharding.md for runbook.

Testing done: - unit tests for tfstate-sharder module validation and variable handling. - local e2e that spins up a 3-node cluster, provisions two tenant subnets, runs migrator, and exercises GPU affinity adapter (tests/e2e/gpu-affinity-migration.test.js). - CI: lint/format on terraform and helm, unit tests, and a smoke e2e harness (first run failed on helm lint; fixed and re-run).

Risk and mitigations: - Partial migration could result in split references: mitigated by checkpointing, pre-validation, and a reversible flip step. - Scheduler / cross-AZ traffic: adapter prefers same-AZ and can be toggled via values.yaml. - IAM regressions: IAM changes are additive; roles are created per-tenant and aliased rather than replacing global roles.

Operational notes: - Installer must be upgraded to >= v0.12.0 to honor shard mapping. - New Helm chart values: installer.gpuAffinity.strictAZ (default: false), installer.sharding.mappingPath. - Terraform state backends supported: S3 (recommended), GCS. - Rolling upgrade sequence is documented in docs/private/tfstate-sharding.md.

Checklist: - [x] Add tfstate-sharder module and docs - [x] Implement gpu-affinity-adapter and Helm hooks - [x] Add migration helper and checkpointing - [x] Unit and e2e tests - [x] Update installer bootstrap to read shard mapping - [x] Update docs and runbook

Related: Linear ENG-1423 (state partitioning), ENG-1487 (gpu affinity), SUP-621 (customer incident that spurred this work).
Add tenant-scoped tfstate shards and a GPU affinity adapter controller to isolate state and improve subnet/GPU binding. Includes a migration helper and Helm hooks. No breaking API changes; operator upgrade required.
Marcus Lee (request changes): Rollback safety is my main concern. If migration partially succeeds we could end up with half the tenant pointing at a new shard and the installer still referencing the old one. Suggest a checkpointing file and an idempotent rollback. -- Alyssa: added checkpointing to migrate_shards.py, introduced a validation pass before switch-over, and documented the rollback steps in tfstate-sharding.md.
Priya Shah (comment): Can the affinity adapter handle multi-AZ clusters with mixed GPU types? Please ensure scheduling doesn't cause cross-AZ traffic for low-latency workloads. -- Alyssa: adapter now prefers same-AZ subnets and falls back to compatible GPU types only when allowed by a new "relax_affinity" flag. Documented behaviour in README.
Diego Alvarez (approve): Verified e2e tests in the canary cluster and checked IAM role creation. Small nit: rename shard_key -> shard_id in variables for clarity. -- Alyssa: renamed the variable and updated all references.
CI Bot (status): First pipeline failed (lint) on helm chart indentation. Re-run fixed after chart tweak. All checks green on final run.

payload.body:
## Why
During design partner pilots we keep losing time to “is this VPC wired correctly?” ambiguity. We now have an alpha set of Terraform VPC modules in `redwood-terraform`, but the installer docs do not explain:
- what outputs the installer expects / how to map module outputs to installer config
- which VPC endpoints + DNS settings are required for private-only installs
- how to interpret common failure modes (image pull failures, intermittent DNS)

This PR adds an explicit integration doc page in the installer repo, links out to the Terraform module suite, and tightens up a couple of preflight error messages so that support/SE can triage faster.

## What changed
### Docs
- Added a new guide: `docs/terraform-vpc-modules-integration.md`
  - Minimal “happy path” example wiring Terraform outputs into the installer config
  - Required endpoints list for fully-private installs (no public egress): ECR (api + dkr), S3 (gateway), STS, CloudWatch Logs (if log shipping), EC2 (for some bootstrap flows), KMS (if using CMKs), and optional endpoints called out
  - DNS notes: Private DNS behavior for interface endpoints, VPC resolver settings, and the most common pitfall (endpoint exists but private DNS disabled)
  - Connectivity notes: placeholders for VPN/DX; explicitly out-of-scope for alpha to auto-configure
- Updated `README.md` and `docs/troubleshooting.md` to link to the new guide and call out the alpha status + version pinning recommendation for modules.

### Installer messaging
- Updated the missing-endpoint preflight error copy to include:
  - the exact AWS endpoint(s) we detected as missing
  - the common remediation (“enable interface endpoint + enable Private DNS”)
  - a link to the new docs page
- Added a troubleshooting hint for intermittent DNS resolution that points to VPC resolver / DHCP options + CoreDNS forwarders.

## How to test
1) `make docs-lint` (markdown + link checker)
2) Run installer preflight against a VPC with ECR endpoints intentionally missing:
   - Expect: preflight fails with actionable error + docs link
3) Run preflight against a VPC with ECR endpoints present but Private DNS disabled:
   - Expect: preflight warns/fails with “endpoint present but Private DNS disabled” guidance (best-effort detection).

## Notes / scope
- This does not change the underlying endpoint detection logic (that’s in #19110); this PR focuses on documentation and making the failure text actionable.
- We intentionally do not prescribe a single subnet topology beyond “private subnets with route to NAT or endpoints”; the reference Terraform modules are the opinionated path.

## References
- SUP-28411 (installer fails pulling images due to missing ECR endpoints / Private DNS)
- SUP-28458 (intermittent DNS in private subnets during pilot)
- Linear ENG-4869 (align installer preflight checks with VPC module defaults)

## Checklist
- [x] Docs labeled as alpha and link to module repo + release notes
- [x] Added troubleshooting section for endpoints + DNS
- [x] Ran docs lint/link check in CI
- [x] Reviewed by Infra/Networking + Security
Victor Alvarez (review): The endpoint list looks right, but can we call out that S3 should be gateway endpoint for most customers? Also specify ECR requires both api + dkr. We’ve had confusion here.
Kira Thompson (author): Good call. Updated the required list to explicitly list ECR (api + dkr) and noted S3 gateway endpoint as the default recommendation. Also added a short note about interface endpoints vs gateway endpoints and why S3 is special.
Nina Petrova (review): The guide mentions “private subnets only” but doesn’t state that the installer needs outbound access to AWS services either via endpoints or NAT. Can we add a statement up top that *some* form of egress is required, and that fully-private requires endpoints + private DNS?
Kira Thompson (author): Added a “Connectivity requirements” section at the top clarifying: (a) installer/cluster needs access to AWS APIs + registries; (b) either NAT or endpoints; (c) for no-internet environments you must configure endpoints + Private DNS. Also linked to troubleshooting.
Sean Gallagher (review): For the preflight error copy: please include the service name(s) and a copy/paste-friendly example (e.g., `com.amazonaws.<region>.ecr.api`). Even if we don’t create endpoints, naming them helps support.
Kira Thompson (author): Done. Error now prints the missing endpoint DNS names and points to the docs section with the full list. I kept it short to avoid noisy output, but included the exact identifiers.
Marcus Lin (security review): Doc currently suggests CloudWatch Logs endpoint “if log shipping”. Can we also mention that customers may route flow logs to S3 and that logs should remain in customer-owned accounts/buckets by default? Otherwise it reads like we require CWL.
Kira Thompson (author): Updated wording: CloudWatch Logs endpoint is optional and only needed if the customer chooses that sink; also added a note that logging destinations are customer-owned by default and that S3 is common for regulated setups.
Markus Klein (SE): +1. Please add a quick “If you see image pull failures” callout that directly ties to missing ECR endpoints + private DNS. That’s the #1 POC derailment.
Kira Thompson (author): Added a boxed callout at the top of troubleshooting with the image pull symptom + what to check first (ECR endpoints, Private DNS, resolver).
CI Bot: Tests failed: docs-link-check (2 broken links).
Kira Thompson (author): Fixed the broken links (wrong relative path in nav + typo in heading anchor). Re-ran CI.
CI Bot: All checks passed (unit, lint, docs-link-check).
Sean Gallagher (approval): Looks good. Messaging improvements will save us time in support.
Victor Alvarez (approval): Ship it. Endpoint/DNS guidance matches what we’ve been telling pilots.
Marcus Lin (approval): Approved with the logging wording updates.

Context: Customers deploying Redwood Private into strict air-gapped and heterogeneous on-prem fleets have asked for a single, verifiable operator bundle that carries OS-specific shims and a machine-readable dependency graph so site admins can pre-seed registries deterministically. This PR introduces an "offline operator bundle" artifact plus supporting installer changes.

Motivation: reduce manual steps when installing in regulated environments, make preflight verification deterministic, and provide safe rollback hooks for operator-driven components.

Changes in this PR include:
1) packaging: add 'bundles/offline-operator' containing:
 - operator-manifests.yaml (CRDs + controller manifests, rendered for non-rootless installs)
 - distro-shims/{ubuntu20.04,ubuntu22.04,almalinux9,rocky8}.yaml that patch nodeSelector/tolerations and initContainers required for kernel-module preload or real-time variants
 - dependency-graph.yaml (simple DAG mapping images -> checksums -> seed-order)
 - checksums.txt and image-list.csv for registry seeding automation
2) installer: installer/airgap/verify_bundle.go and a lightweight verifier script installer/airgap/bin/verify-bundle that validates checksums, ensures distro shim compatibility, and emits a seed order for registries
3) helm: charts/private/Chart.yaml and templates updated to support an optional OperatorDeployment that will be deployed from the offline bundle and is annotated for safe-rollbacks
4) terraform: modules/registry-seed added support for the explicit seed order and an atomic 'seed-plan' input consumed by the registry sync job
5) upgrade/rollback: installer/airgap/rollback-metadata.json is emitted by the installer to allow deterministic reversal to the previous operator bundle.

Checklist:
 - [x] bundle produced by CI artifact pipeline
 - [x] verify-bundle tool + unit tests
 - [x] terraform module consumed by local e2e seed runner
 - [x] helm templates include canary labels and rollback annotations
 - [x] docs updated (quickstart airgap section)

Commits summary:
 - add offline bundle layout and assets
 - implement verify-bundle CLI and unit tests
 - wire verify step into installer preflight
 - helm chart: operator deployment and rollback annotations
 - terraform: seed-plan ingestion and example
 - docs: airgap quickstart and operator bundle explanation

Files changed (high level):
 - bundles/offline-operator/operator-manifests.yaml
 - bundles/offline-operator/distro-shims/ubuntu22.04.yaml
 - bundles/offline-operator/dependency-graph.yaml
 - installer/airgap/verify_bundle.go
 - installer/airgap/bin/verify-bundle
 - installer/airgap/rollback-metadata.json
 - charts/private/templates/operator-deployment.yaml
 - terraform/modules/registry-seed/main.tf
 - terraform/examples/seed-plan/seed-plan.yaml
 - docs/airgap/operator-bundle.md
 - Makefile (CI targets)
 - ci/publish-bundle.yml

Testing performed: unit tests for verifier (checksum and DAG validation), integration run against a local registry seeded by terraform example (seed-plan), cluster smoke test deploying operator from bundle to K3s 1.26 and RKE2 1.22, manual validation on AlmaLinux and Ubuntu 22.04 nodes for shim behavior.

Backwards compatibility notes: the bundle format is additive; older installers ignore the new dependency-graph.yaml and distro-shims, so legacy installs are unaffected.

Migration: for existing airgap customers, recommended flow is to run verify-bundle --generate-seed-plan and feed the resulting seed-plan to the terraform registry-seed module; the installer will then apply the operator as an optional step.

Rollback story: the installer writes rollback-metadata.json before switching operator versions; running installer/airgap/rollback --from-file rollback-metadata.json will atomically revert operator deployment and return registry seeds to previous checksums where possible.

CI: some flakiness observed on the integration job that pulls from a transient local registry; reran twice and green on second attempt.

Security/Signoff: added checksum verification to prevent accidental divergent images; reviewers audited shims to avoid escalation vectors in initContainers.

Docs: docs/airgap/operator-bundle.md describes the bundle layout and step-by-step seed-plan generation.

Operational notes:
 - seed-plan is intentionally explicit to enable customers to copy seed order to offline registries that do not support dependency graphs
 - distro-shims are lightweight and only patch nodeAffinity/tolerations and an optional initContainer; they do not introduce privileged mounts by default

Rollout plan: merge into main, tag v0.11.0-bundle, publish bundle artifact to CI storage, send migration guide to customers who opted in to operator-managed installs.

Related work: ENG-2147 (airgap improvements), ENG-2203 (installer rollback metadata).
Added an air-gapped operator bundle that includes distro-specific shims and an explicit dependency graph for deterministic offline installs. No breaking changes. Backwards compatible with existing seed registry layouts.

Evan Patel: Confirmed terraform module accepts seed-plan as list(string) and added example usage.
