Add a drift-resistant Grafana sync agent and accompanying installer automation to reliably provision dashboards in airgapped / intermittently-connected private installs. The core is a lightweight daemonset 'grafana-syncd' that supports two input modes: mounted versioned bundles (e.g. from an object-storage mirror) and an on-cluster git mirror. The agent does idempotent apply of dashboard JSON, supports template variable expansion using tenant-scoped values, and exposes a 'preflight drift-check' operation that can run as a Helm post-upgrade hook to detect conflicting manual edits before upgrades proceed. To make operations robust we implemented exponential backoff and jitter for Grafana API usage, incremental writes for large dashboard sets to avoid rate-limits, and a checksum-based short-circuit that avoids re-applying unchanged dashboards. This change also includes: 1) Helm chart: new 'grafana-sync' chart under charts/private-observability with values for mirror providers, rbac, and probe windows; 2) Terraform: mirror-storage module enhancements to provision optional S3/GCS-compatible buckets for private mirrors and IAM bindings; 3) Installer hooks: declarative Helm hook that triggers a preflight dry-run and blocks rollouts if drift is detected (opt-out via values); 4) Tests/Fixtures: an offline-e2e scenario that simulates latency/intermittent control-plane connectivity; 5) Docs & Playbook: upgrade/rollback playbook describing safe canary rollouts, force-sync procedures, and emergency rollback steps. Motivation: several customer incidents where dashboards drifted after upgrades in private installs and a recent support ticket (SUP-9482) where an airgapped tenant could not receive pushed dashboard updates. This PR aims to make dashboard provisioning pull-friendly and resilient to partial connectivity, reduce human-error during upgrades, and provide an auditable sync path for compliance.
Avery Chen: Please add Prometheus metrics for apply_success and apply_latency (helpful for alerting).
Marta Lopez: Added metrics exporter and instrumented apply path in internal/sync/apply.go; updated unit tests.
Ravi Patel: The backoff defaults look aggressive for very large tenant dashboards; can we make them tunable via values.yaml?
Marta Lopez: Backoff and batch-size are exposed in values.yaml with sensible defaults; documented in module README.
Sofia Nguyen: Can you add a short circuit for dashboards marked 'managed=false' so customers can opt out for particular folders?
Marta Lopez: Added support for a 'managed' metadata flag and updated preflight to report such dashboards as ignored rather than drifted.
Ravi Patel: CI flakes on the e2e offline fixture; looks like timing assumptions.
Avery Chen: Increased probe windows and added retries to e2e harness; reran CI and all checks passed.
New: grafana-syncd daemonset for private installs to enable pull-based dashboard sync in airgapped environments. Improved: Terraform mirror-storage module to provision S3/GCS-compatible mirror buckets. Added preflight drift-check Helm hook and upgrade/rollback playbook. Impact: opt-in via values.yaml; safe defaults applied.

Context: customer installs running Redwood Private in regulated VPCs required a safer TLS rekey path that avoids broad sealedsecret replacements and supports gradual cutover with an HSM-backed envelope key fallback. Motivation: previous bulk-rotation workflows caused transient downtime and increased ops toil when controllers re-applied long-lived sealed secrets across namespaces. This PR implements a staged promotion workflow plus an envelope-key fallback that reduces blast radius, supports dry-run promotion, and enables safe rollback. Design summary: 1) Add a new 'staged-seal' Helm subchart that creates promotion artifacts in a dedicated namespace (redwood-seal-staging) and ties to a new Kubernetes Job pre-upgrade hook that validates the promotion on a small sample of workloads; 2) Extend the terraform 'kms_key_binding' module to v2 which emits an envelope-key ARN and a promotion flag; 3) Introduce a vault migration helper (cli script) that migrates existing sealed secrets into the staged namespace by re-encrypting with the envelope key while leaving original secrets intact; 4) Implement controller-side gating so the private-installer controller only flips production references after an explicit 'promote' annotation applied to the staging object; 5) Add metrics (staging.promotions_total, staging.failures_total) and tracing spans for each promotion step. Migration plan: - Default deploys create staging artifacts but do not promote; operators run the included dry-run job which validates decryption and TLS chain rotation for one ingress per namespace; - After SMT validation, operator annotates the 'staged-seal' resource to trigger canary promotion across a subset of namespaces; - Full promotion requires two successful canaries spaced 30 minutes apart. Rollback plan: annotated reversal flips references back to original sealed secrets; envelope key remains available for decrypting any promoted items until an operator executes a safe purge command. Helm/Terraform changes: - Helm: new subchart 'staged-seal' with templates/sealed-promote-job.yaml (pre-upgrade hook), templates/secret-proxy.yaml, and Chart.yaml bump; add hookweight/annotations to ensure deterministic ordering during upgrades; - Terraform: module kms_key_binding v2 with new output envelope_key_arn, input enable_promotion boolean and migration helpers; state migration script included as scripts/tf-state-backcompat.sh; - Installer: add CLI flags --enable-staged-seal and --promotion-timeout to private-installer bootstrap command. Testing and validation: unit tests for helm templates, integration harness test that runs the dry-run job in kind with a mocked KMS (local kms emulator), e2e (gke) smoke test that performs a canary promotion then rollback. Security considerations: envelope-key usage is audited via new audit log entries and requires KMS Decrypt permission scoped to service account; promotion annotation is RBAC gated to cluster-admin by default; migration helper logs sensitive operations and can be run with --audit-only for planning. CI: add parallel pipeline stage 'staged-seal-smoke' that runs the kind-based dry-run. Observability: dashboards added in redwood-console-config (prometheus queries and alert rules for promotion failures).
Introduce staged promotion of sealed secrets and envelope-key fallback for zero-downtime TLS rekeying; Terraform module bump for kms_key_binding_v2; Helm hooks to ensure idempotent pre-upgrade secret staging; rollback path documented.
Miguel Alvarez: Please ensure the envelope_key_arn output is backward compatible; we should not require immediate TF state rewrite.
Author (Aisha Khan): Addressed by adding tf-state-backcompat.sh and keeping the original output name as legacy_kms_key when enable_promotion=false.
Priya Nandakumar: Can we gate the pre-upgrade job behind a feature flag so air-gapped installs don't accidentally attempt live KMS calls?
Author: Added --enable-staged-seal false by default and added a --dry-run-only mode for the migration helper.
Ethan Brooks: CI flakey on Kind test; saw a timing issue during job cleanup on low-resource nodes.

Adds automated provisioning and upgrade paths for an opinionated observability stack in Private deployments. Motivation: private customers repeatedly request a reproducible, secure observability bundle (Prometheus + Alertmanager, Grafana with preloaded dashboards, and Fluent Bit log shipping) that can be toggled during installer runs and upgraded/rolled back reliably. This PR implements: (1) a new Helm umbrella chart 'redwood-observability-private' that installs Prometheus Operator service monitors, Alertmanager with routing rules, Grafana provisioning (dashboards + datasources), and Fluent Bit DaemonSet with pluggable outputs (S3/Elasticsearch/HTTP). Charts respect podSecurityContext and run-as-user constraints for hardened clusters; values allow disabling any subchart. (2) A Terraform module 'monitoring/monitoring-network' that seeds required infra for on-prem/VPC installs: optional VPC peering resources, S3 buckets (for log archive), IAM roles/policies for pushers when cloud endpoints are used, and a managed Alertmanager webhook endpoint. Module is idempotent and supports plan-only runs during dry-run install. (3) Installer CLI flags and config schema changes: --enable-observability, observability.mode (managed/local), observability.outputs (s3,elastic,none), and rollout.strategy. (4) Safe upgrade and rollback toolkit: helm pre-upgrade hooks snapshot Prometheus PVCs, Terraform state locking integrated via remote backend, and a new installer subcommand 'redwood-installer observability rollback --to-revision N' that coordinates helm rollback plus terraform state revert. (5) Observability CI: unit tests for Helm chart templating, an integration harness that boots a 3-node private cluster in CI's k8s-in-docker job and validates serviceMonitor metrics and a sample Grafana dashboard render. Compatibility notes: default installation is opt-in; existing private installs are unaffected unless operator flips flag. Secrets: S3/Elastic credentials are injected via the existing installer secrets mechanism and never stored in chart values; RBAC manifests are minimal and documented. Checklist: manual review of dashboards; docs for operators; e2e smoke pass; alert routing reviewed with SRE. Known limitations: fluent bit output plugins require customer's endpoint to accept lines in the configured format; large-scale Prometheus retention must be tuned per-customer. See files_changed for code pointers and the review thread for decisions.
Automates provisioning and lifecycle (install/upgrade/rollback) of an opinionated observability stack for Private deployments, with Terraform infra module and Helm umbrella chart; opt-in and backwards compatible.
Added opt-in observability bundle for Private installs: helm umbrella chart (Prometheus/Grafana/Fluent Bit), Terraform module for infra dependencies, installer CLI flags to enable/disable, and safe upgrade/rollback tooling; RBAC and secrets handling hardened; documentation and example configs included.
- New Helm umbrella chart 'redwood-observability-private'

- Installer CLI flags and rollback command
- Preloaded Grafana dashboards and provisioning templates
Unit helm template tests pass; integration e2e smoke runs in k8s-in-docker succeeded after retry fixes; manual validation performed against a customer-like VPC on prem environment; added CI job to run smoke on protected branch.
To enable observability during install: add observability.enabled: true and observability.mode: local|managed to your config, or run 'redwood-installer apply --enable-observability --tf-backend <backend>'. To rollback: 'redwood-installer observability rollback --to-revision <rev>' which coordinates helm rollback and terraform state revert.
Prometheus retention defaults are conservative; for high-cardinality workloads customers must tune retention and remote-write. Fluent Bit has limited built-in parsers; customers with custom syslog formats should supply custom filter configs.
Support teams: when customers report missing metrics, check serviceMonitor selection labels and namespace scoping; for logs, verify fluent-bit output configuration and S3 policy permissions. Use the included troubleshooting section in docs/private/observability.md.

payload.body:
Motivation: Customers deploying Redwood Private need stronger guarantees that customer workloads use jurisdictionally-appropriate KMS providers and that audit records produced at install-time and runtime are tamper-evident. This PR introduces a perimeter KMS policy enforcer in the installer runtime and an immutable audit envelope writer that signs/salting audit payloads before sending to the central aggregator.

What this changes (single-string description): Adds an installer middleware that validates configured KMS provider bindings against a per-tenant jurisdiction policy template (templates/kms-residency/*.yaml). The enforcer runs during both: (a) initial install validation and (b) runtime operator credential handoff when the private control plane boots. When a KMS binding violates residency rules the installer fails fast and emits a descriptive remediation hint. In parallel we introduce audit-envelopes: audit payloads are wrapped with a canonicalized header, timestamp, and an HMAC over the payload using a rotation-capable signing key stored in the local keystore. Envelopes are marked immutable; the edge forwarder will reject any audit record that does not verify.

Design notes: The enforcer uses OPA-style policy templates but ships a tiny policy engine (policy/engine.go) that evaluates residency predicates offline so the installer is self-contained for air-gapped customers. KMS selection supports multi-provider rules (aws:kms, gcp:cloudkms, hsm:local) and a fallback preference list when multi-provider consent is enabled. There is also a compatibility shim to opt-out (environment variable REDWOOD_PERIMETER_KMS=disabled) for older installs; default for new installer releases is enabled.

Security considerations: The audit envelope signing includes a nonce and provenance metadata (installer-version, host-fingerprint, tenant-id) to reduce replay risk. Signing keys are seeded from the installer keystore and can be rotated via the new subcommand installer key rotate. The enforcer logs minimal information on policy failures (policy id, reason) and only emits tenant-level identifiers to support incident triage.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests for policy engine and envelope verification included. Added integration tests that exercise a three-node private control plane in acceptance harness (ci/integration/kms-perimeter). Rollout plan: default feature-flag = enabled for new images; staged canary via the installer channel and a 2-week telemetry check before global enable.

How to review: scan policy templates under templates/kms-residency, read policy engine (policy/engine.go), and inspect installer hooks (installer/hook/kms_enforcer.go) and audit envelope code (audit/envelope.go). Important: the e2e harness files under ci/integration were expanded to include an offline KMS mock.

Checklist:
- [x] Policy engine implementation and unit tests
- [x] Immutable audit envelope writer and verification tests
- [x] Integration tests with KMS mock harness
- [x] Docs and upgrade notes (docs/private-installer/kms-perimeter.md)

Notes: This is purposely conservative in scope (installer + forwarder + local policy engine). Future follow-ups: (1) central policy management UI sync, (2) runtime enforcement inside private control plane long-running process, (3) hardened HSM integration for signing keys.
Add perimeter KMS enforcement and immutable audit envelopes for private installs; opt-in via --enable-perimeter-kms flag; rolling upgrade instructions included.
1) Run installer --validate to surface residency violations. 2) Resolve or add consent entries in templates/kms-residency. 3) Re-run installer with --enable-perimeter-kms. For air-gapped installs, ensure templates are present in the bundle. See docs/private-installer/kms-perimeter.md for examples.
Upgrade path: run installer --validate on existing manifests to detect any policy violations; use installer key rotate to pre-seed signing keys for audit envelopes. To temporarily disable enforcement set REDWOOD_PERIMETER_KMS=disabled until policies are reconciled.
Security reviewed by SecOps (Rohit Patel). Key outcomes: signing key lifecycle added, canonicalization hardened, limited PII in failure logs. No unresolved findings.
Diego Marquez: +1 on the design; please add a small debug log when a binding is auto-rewritten by the fallback rule so operators can see the change. — Author: added ephemeral.debug log and note in upgrade docs (commit 4)
Rohit Patel: Concern about diffing canonicalization causing false negatives on envelope verification. — Author: canonicalization is now strict JSON canonical form with sorted keys; added roundtrip test to envelope_test.go
Marta Ivanova: Please enumerate possible false positives for residency templates (e.g., overlapping regions). — Author: updated templates and added validation routine to templates/validate.go

Motivation: Private installs exhibit brittle init ordering across cloud/onprem clusters when tenant-scoped seed jobs, cert provisioning and secret reconciliation run concurrently. Existing hook templating duplicates logic in values and templates which makes safe incremental upgrades error prone. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) a Helm template transformer library (templates/_value_transformer.tpl) that allows environment-aware value morphing and lightweight lookups at render-time, and (2) a declarative initGraph structure surfaced in values.yaml which renders as sequenced Helm hook Jobs and a compact init-graph controller helper that enforces inter-job ordering, per-phase concurrency, and idempotent requeues.  Summary of changes: added values.schema.json for the new valueTransformers and initGraph contract; new helper templates (templates/_value_transformer.tpl, templates/_init_graph_helpers.tpl); an optional preflight dry-run job (templates/preflight-dryrun-job.yaml) that validates transformed values; template overlays for safe rollback (annotations on hook jobs to fence rollback windows); example values at examples/private-values-initgraph.yaml; README updates documenting the new contract and recommended upgrade path.  Checklist: 1) implement transformer helpers and unit tests (done) 2) add values.schema.json and examples (done) 3) update chart README and migration notes (done) 4) run full private-installer e2e with onprem and AWS VPC profiles (green) 5) coordinate rollout with platform team for roll-forward window and feature-flag (deployed behind values.enabled.initGraph).  Backwards compatibility: default values preserve existing behavior when values.enabled.initGraph is false. The transformer DSL is opt-in per-section (valueTransformers.*) so older values continue to render unchanged.  Upgrade notes: Operators should set values.enabled.initGraph=true in a canary tenant first and run preflightDryRun.enabled=true to validate the transformed manifests in-cluster without side effects; the preflight job runs as a non-mutating validation that checks RBAC, CRDs, and image availability. After validation and one successful tenant boot, set the initGraph concurrency to a safe default (1) and ramp up.  Rollback strategy: hook jobs include a rollback-fence annotation and the transformer writes an explicit release-version label; if a rollback is required the hooks will refuse to run against mismatched release-version and an operator can safely revert values.  Testing performed: local helm template checks, values.schema.json validation, integration with private-installer CLI smoke tests, and full e2e in staging using the AWS VPC profile and an on-prem lab cluster.  Risks and mitigations: transformer DSL introduces another templating layer; to limit blast radius it is disabled by default and scope-limited by transformer profiles.  Contact: @devon for rollout coordination and @aisha for operator playbook updates.
Aisha Nambiar: Nice separation between transformer and initGraph; please add explicit schema examples for 'lookupProfile' and a short table of supported transform functions (merge, redact, envLookup).
Devon Patel (author): Added a more detailed schema fragment to values.schema.json and expanded examples/private-values-initgraph.yaml to show merge and envLookup. Left notes in README about security considerations for redact.
Ramon Ortega: Two nits on templates: use 'include' instead of 'tpl' for the small helpers to be more testable, and add a 60s backoff retry block for transient image pull errors in the hook job. Also request to add an e2e step that toggles preflightDryRun.enabled to true.
Devon Patel (author): Addressed both nits — split large tpl into include helpers and added configurable retry/backoff annotation; added a staging e2e job to the pipeline that exercises preflightDryRun.
Claire Zhou: Approve after confirming schema validation passes in CI and after adding an ops playbook snippet for rollback steps.
Devon Patel (author): Added ops playbook to README and linked to Linear ENG-1729 for rollout coordination.
charts(redwood-private-installer): add opt-in initGraph declarative sequencing and a Helm value transformer DSL. Operators can enable initGraph for safer, ordered tenant bootstrap and use preflightDryRun to validate changes before rollout.
Migration steps: 1) deploy chart with values.enabled.initGraph=false to main; 2) pick a canary tenant and set enabled.initGraph=true and preflightDryRun.enabled=true; 3) inspect preflight job logs for transform output and validation errors; 4) if green, set initGraph.phaseConcurrency=1 and continue canary tenants; 5) once stable, ramp phaseConcurrency. Important: ensure all nodes have the required init-image pre-pulled or set images.prepull=true to avoid head-of-line delays. For rollback, use helm rollback and ensure release-version labels match; the init hooks will not run for mismatched release-version, preventing partial double-run.
Feature is opt-in. Preflight dry-run validates but does not mutate resources. Transformer functions that touch secrets must be gated by 'redact' profiles and are documented in README.

Motivation: Upgrades for private deployments must have a low blast radius and the ability to verify a rollback without touching production state. This PR implements two complementary safety mechanisms: a rollback dry-run emulator (emulator) that simulates an in-place rollback sequence against an ephemeral clone of cluster state, and a Helm constraint enforcer that gates Helm value sets and chart versions during upgrade/rollback orchestration. Summary of changes: 1) installer/upgrade: add 'upgrade-dryrun-emulator' binary and operator API hooks. The emulator performs an automated sequence: snapshot export, ephemeral namespace restore, execute rollback steps (helm release rollback, CRD reduction/restore, DB migration reversal using migration runner in read-only mode), and post-run verification that checks service account bindings, KV cache compatibility, and storage layout. 2) operator: add UpgradePlan validation webhook that runs Helm constraint checks and consults chart version pinlist to block unsupported downgrades. 3) terraform: add plan-lock hook that fails concurrent apply attempts for clusters with an active UpgradePlan. 4) helm: add values schema and enforced constraints (persistence.enabled must be true for replicas > 1, image.tag pinning, pdb minimum available thresholds). 5) docs/tests: add detailed dry-run playbook and new e2e test which performs a synthetic rollback against a cloned Postgres dataset. Design notes: - The emulator is intentionally non-destructive: it uses snapshot/restore to a namespaced clone so no production DB, manifests, or PVs are modified. - Constraint enforcer exposes a 'strict' and 'permissive' mode; default is 'strict' for release channels tagged 'enterprise'. - Terraform plan-lock integrates with the existing state backend and writes an UpgradeLock object to the installer operator; this avoids split-brain upgrades. - All changes are configurable via operator Helm values under 'upgradeSafety'. How to test locally: - make dev-upgrade-emulator: runs integration-dryrun using testdata snapshots. - rictl upgrade dry-run --cluster <test-cluster> --plan <plan-id> will run the emulator and upload artifacts to the specified workspace. Backwards compatibility: the operator will reject UpgradePlans that request downgrades unless 'allowDowngrade' is explicitly set and an approved bypass token is provided. Rollout plan: merged to main, feature flagged off by default. Gradual enable for staging clusters, then opt-in for customers. Related: ENG-9321 (upgrade safety), ENG-9410 (helm gating), SUP-5482 (customer incident followup).
Added a non-destructive rollback dry-run emulator and a Helm constraint enforcer to reduce upgrade/rollback risk for private deployments. New operator UpgradePlan validation and terraform plan-lock guard help prevent concurrent or unsupported upgrades. Includes CLI support (rictl upgrade dry-run) and e2e test coverage.
Unit tests added for webhook logic and emulator orchestration; integration-dryrun verifies end-to-end rollback simulation against an ephemeral Postgres clone; manual staging run performed on staging cluster 'stg-us-west-2' and results validated by SRE; promoted to canary after 48h with no regressions.
Feature disabled by default. To enable: set charts.private-installer.upgradeSafety.enabled=true and configure chartVersionPinlist and planLock.backend. If enabling in production, schedule a maintenance window and run rictl upgrade dry-run for each target cluster to collect artifacts before performing real upgrades.
Diego Morales: Can the emulator be run without a full DB snapshot? Author: yes; emulator supports logical pg_dump-based dry-run for smaller testcases
Ava Chen: Helm constraint enforcer should surface which specific constraint failed with a link to remediation steps. Action: added detailed error payloads and remediation links
Samir Patel: add metric for 'dryrun_success_rate' for monitoring. Action: added Prometheus metric and Grafana dashboard panel
QA: observed intermittent failure in e2e when underlying storage class reclaim policy is Delete; added additional cleanup and wait logic
Most checks green. Integration dry-run initially flaked due to timing; fixed by adding wait for PV binding. Terraform plan step now emits a warning when plan-lock is present; CI runs in warn mode to allow merge after manual review.
Implement rollback dry-run emulator and Helm constraint enforcement to reduce upgrade blast radius; add terraform plan-lock integration; add rictl dry-run command and docs.
Low-medium: emulator performs non-destructive operations; however, added operator webhooks and terraform hooks change upgrade gating behavior and must be carefully configured. Default keeps safety checks off for self-hosted until explicitly turned on.

Context: Customers deploying Private control planes in strict environments asked for stronger network-level guarantees: (1) control-plane ENIs must be provisioned encrypted at boot and bound to predictable IP allocations so firewall rules and egress policies can be pre-provisioned, and (2) DNS mirroring used during control-plane upgrades must support a safe rollback path that avoids left-behind stub zones or split-horizon drift. This PR implements an encrypted ENI bootstrapping flow in the Terraform installer, adds a deterministic IP assignment mode for controlplane subnets, introduces a lightweight Helm chart hook to seed a DNS mirror with signed zone metadata, and wires an automated rollback hook that re-scopes stub zone records and removes ephemeral mirror records on failed upgrades. Scope: terraform/modules/network/controlplane/* - new encrypted_eni module and deterministic_ip submodule; helm/controlplane/templates/dns-mirror-hook.yaml - pre-upgrade job to snapshot signed-records and post-failure job to reconcile; installer/upgrade/rollback.sh - idempotent rollback logic and a dry-run verifier; docs/installer/networking.md - operational notes and migration steps; test/terraform/controlplane_integ.tf - added integration fixture for encrypted ENI with mock KMS. Design notes: ENI encryption leverages customer KMS keys passed through the private-installer values and uses an immutable tag pattern (redwood:eni:hash) to detect re-attachment vs replacement during upgrades. Deterministic IP mode exposes a small allocator that maps a CIDR chunk + index -> stable IP and records the mapping in a tfstate-backed lock file so re-applies are stable across operators. DNS mirror hook writes signed RRsets into a namespace-backed ConfigMap and uses TTL pinning to avoid cache stomping; the rollback job reverses TTL pinning and prunes records only when lock metadata indicates the mirror was created by this release. Backwards compatibility: existing installs remain unchanged unless operators enable encrypted_eni or deterministic_ip via the new installer variables. Testing: added unit tests for allocator, a Helm integration run in CI that exercises pre-upgrade snapshot and a staged rollback scenario. Risks & mitigations: key rotation - the module refuses to re-encrypt existing ENIs without an explicit force flag; network policy mismatch - included a preflight verifier that checks security group rules against expected controlplane rule set. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module and unit tests - [x] Helm hook and rollback job - [x] Installer orchestration script - [x] Docs and migration guide - [x] CI integration run Summary of changes, commits and tests below.
Ethan Park: Left a few nits on variable naming and suggested extracting the KMS key validation to the preflight checks instead of the module. Please add a unit test for the allocator edge-case when the CIDR has an odd-sized range.
Maya Patel: Addressed the variable renames and moved KMS validation to scripts/preflight/checks.sh. Added allocator unit test and a guard for odd-sized CIDRs.
Leah Morgan: Approved after confirming Helm hook obeys helm.sh/hook-weight ordering and that rollback job tolerates API transient failures. Commented about adding metrics for rollback-run counts.
Carlos Ruiz: Noted a concern about state-lock expiry causing duplicate IP allocations during long operations. Recommended a lock TTL bump and detection to avoid overlapping allocations. Maya responded with a small retry backoff and a detection heuristic that refuses allocation if a recent allocation timestamp is present.
CI Bot: Initial pipeline failed on 'helm template' due to missing Chart.yaml dependency; fixed by adding Chart.yaml and re-running. Second run passed all integration gates.
Ops: Please add a migration note for customers with pre-existing ENIs — the module will not replace ENIs by default. Added to docs.
Leah Morgan: Post-merge request to follow up with a dashboard for rollback metrics (ENG-4821 follow-up).

Enable features by setting installer values: encrypted_eni.kms_key and deterministic_ip.enabled. Run installer preflight to verify SGs, KMS access, and CIDR suitability. Rolling back a failed upgrade should be invoked via installer/upgrade/rollback.sh --run, or CI will execute a dry-run on failures.
Added allocator unit tests, terraform integration fixture, and a helm integration run. CI initially failed on helm lint due to a missing Chart.yaml dependency, rerun passed all checks. Post-merge nightly integ will run full e2e against a mock VPC.
Low for existing clusters; enabling deterministic_ip or encrypted_eni will introduce new resources and require KMS permissions. Rollback hook reduces risk of lingering DNS mirror records after failed upgrades.
ENG-4821: add rollback metrics dashboard and alerting; ENG-4902: investigate providing automatic KMS key rotation helper; PM-121: add UI toggle to Console for deterministic IP mode.

Motivation: Provide a deterministic, low-ops path for cross-AZ / cross-region DR activation that does not rely on a long-lived Kubernetes operator. Some customers run in constrained environments where background operators are undesirable; this PR introduces an operatorless switchover flow that uses Terraform to orchestrate infra-level failover and a lightweight helm hook + one-shot scripts to perform application-level state transitions. Key goals: deterministic activation ordering, safe read-only probes before cutover, reversible staged traffic siphon, and clear runbooks-as-code for drills and audits. Changes include a new terraform module (dr/activation-orchestrator) for region fencing and DNS cutover, a helm chart sub-template (charts/private-installer/templates/dr-switchover-job.yaml) for one-shot application migration steps, and a small set of idempotent shell helpers (installer/scripts/dr-heartbeat.sh, installer/scripts/siphon-traffic.sh) for heartbeating and staged connection draining.
Miguel Santos (requested changes): The terraform work looks solid but we need stronger idempotency on the DNS update step; if the control-plane retries during propagation we must avoid flip-flopping. Suggest adding a stable marker record and TTL guard.
Anya Patel (author reply): Added marker-record logic and TTL guard in the latest commit; expanded unit test for dns marker behavior.
Elena Korsakov (approval): Verified the staged-siphon smoke flow in a 3-AZ dev cluster. Observed expected transient read-only window and successful rollback path. Approving with small nits in docs.
Priya Narayanan (comment): Please ensure the heartbeat script logs to stdout-only for compatibility with telemetry collection in Private installs.
Introduce operatorless DR activation workflow: terraform module + helm one-shot jobs + scripts
Add runbooks-as-code for staged traffic siphon and reversible cutover
New integration test for DNS TTL-safe cutover

Motivation: private deployments that use SealedSecrets + Vault/KMS face a race during TLS/KMS key rotations where consumers may receive partially-rotated secrets. This PR implements a safe 'swap' flow to allow staged SealedSecret rotation with an automated compatibility probe and a documented rollback/recovery path. Goals: 1) perform TLS/KMS-based rotation with zero-secret-latency windows for runtime; 2) detect keywrap/unwrap incompatibilities prior to cutover; 3) provide easy rollback and audit telemetry for operators. Changes are split across Helm templates, Helm hooks, a small controller-ish job for probing previously-rotated entries, Terraform variables for the installer, and runbooks/playbooks for operators. Checklist: - [x] Helm chart: new values for sealedsecret.swap.enabled, probeJob config, and pre-upgrade hook annotations - [x] Helm templates: introduce sealedsecret-safe-swap Job and associated RBAC - [x] Terraform: optional var enable_sealedsecret_safe_swap and minimal IAM/KMS policy docs - [x] Installer hooks: pre-upgrade probe step and post-failback cleanup - [x] Recovery playbooks: operator runbook for canary, rollback, and forced rewrap - [x] E2E smoke test added to ci/upgrade-tests that exercises probe job against a simulated KMS mismatch - [x] CI: new pipeline step added to run the probe job in the chart verification job Rationale/flow: 1) Deploy new chart with sealedsecret.swap.enabled=true; the chart installs a probe Job (disabled by default) and adds annotations to SealedSecrets managed by the installer to include a rotation metadata label. 2) Operator triggers rotation; the system creates rewrapped SealedSecret objects under a staging suffix and the probe Job attempts to unwrap them using the target KMS key material. 3) If all probe unwrappings succeed, a safe-swap controller (lightweight K8s Job run by Helm hook) performs an atomic replace of the live secrets; otherwise the probe returns detailed failure reasons and the installer can either rollback or continue to manual remediation. 4) If a failure occurs after partial cutover, recovery playbooks provide steps to: rewrap to prior key, promote canary nodes to traffic, and audit the event using the new telemetry labels. Telemetry: chart adds labels and emits events to the installer operator (via the probe Job logs) with structured messages that the Console can pick up (rotation.id=<uuid>, stage=probe|commit|rollback, failures=...). Security considerations: the probe Job has least-privilege IAM/KMS usage documented; secrets are never written to disk unencrypted and logs redact key material. Implementation notes: - The probe job is implemented as a small Go binary (probe-wrap-check) compiled into an image referenced in values.yaml. It performs KMS Unwrap in a dry-run mode and returns deterministic status codes. - Helm templates add a pre-upgrade hook that can be toggled off (useful for low-trust air-gapped upgrades). - Terraform variables add optional IAM role binding for probe job when enable_sealedsecret_safe_swap=true. Migration notes: existing installations must opt-in by setting values.sealedsecret.swap.enabled=true; default remains off to avoid surprising behavior. See docs/private-deployments/sealedsecret-safe-swap.md for operator guidance and playbooks.
Introduce a staged SealedSecret rotation flow with automatic fallback to KMS-wrapped values, pre-upgrade probes and documented recovery playbooks. No user-visible API changes.
Arielle Gomez: Left a few nits on the probe job RBAC scope; prefer a dedicated KMS role instead of cluster-admin-flavored bindings.
Priya Natarajan: replied: updated role to kms-sealedsecret-probe-role and tightened serviceAccount binding per feedback.
Liam O'Connor: request_changes: add a failure-mode that clearly signals partial cutover and include a deterministic remediation command.
Priya Natarajan: pushed a follow-up commit that includes remediation cli 'installer sealedsecret rollback --rotation <id>' and explicit partial-cutover event reasons.
Hiroshi Tanaka: approval: Verified chart renders in CI and probe job exits 0 against mock KMS; LGTM after one small logging tweak.
CI Bot: build passed; integration tests for terraform module ran in ephemeral env and passed.
Docs reviewer (A. Mendes): small doc suggestion to include an example of rewrap TTL—addressed in latest doc commit.
Operators: to enable the safe-swap flow, set charts.private-installer.sealedsecret.swap.enabled=true and ensure the installer has a kms:Decrypt IAM role bound to the probe SA. Use the included playbook 'sealedsecret-safe-swap.md' before scheduling a rotation. If the probe reports 'unwrap-failure: key-version-mismatch', run 'installer sealedsecret rewrap --from <old-key> --to <new-key> --rotation <id>' to reconcile, then re-run the probe. Audit: rotation events include rotation.id label for correlation.
Risk: misconfigured KMS IAM could cause probe to fail and block automated cutover. Mitigation: probe is opt-in and chart will not alter live secrets until probe passes; there is a documented operator rollback path and automated cleanup hook.

payload.body:
Motivation: On private deployments customers run HSM-backed KMS with periodic key rotations. Past rotations that involved immediate primary key swaps caused brief failures during leader election and sealed-secrets unseal handoffs in air-gapped clusters. This PR implements an "atomic key promotion" flow plus a configurable grace period and automated rollback hooks to ensure safe cutover without downtime.
Add atomic KMS key promotion orchestration, Helm chart hooks for staged promotion, Terraform module updates for key metadata, and rollback hooks that revert promotion state and re-issue lightweight certificates when cutover fails.
Design highlights: 1) Introduce a small KMSPromotion CRD that records desired_key, fallback_key, state, and promotion_window. 2) Controller coordinates: pre-validate HSM key status, run promote job as Helm pre-upgrade hook, wait for verification, atomically swap primary keystore symlink, mark promotion complete. 3) On failure, controller triggers a rollback hook that restores prior symlink, re-issues short-lived certificates for workloads that request re-enrollment, and emits detailed audit events. 4) Terraform exposes promotion_window and fallback_key to ops teams to set conservative defaults for on-prem clusters.
Defaults preserve prior behavior: if promotion_enabled is not set, nothing changes. The CRD is optional and controller is no-op until a KMSPromotion resource is applied.
Phase 1: Canary in staging with one dedicated region (72h observation). Phase 2: Opt-in customers via Terraform flag 'promotion_enabled'. Phase 3: Gradual enablement with telemetry-based rollback thresholds. Ops runbook included in docs.
Added integration e2e that simulates HSM transient failures, verifies promotion_window semantics, and asserts rollback hooks restore cluster to healthy state. Manual verification script included (scripts/tools/promote-check.sh).
When upgrading installer: new controller will be installed side-by-side. Operators should create KMSPromotion resources only after ensuring node agents are at vX+1. Terraform module bump required for promotion flags. No forced schema migrations.
If a promotion fails in production the controller will automatically invoke rollback; manual rollback steps: 1) kubectl annotate kms-promotion <name> --override=rollback=true 2) run ./scripts/tools/promote-check.sh --force-rollback 3) monitor logs (controller logs include 'rollback-complete' event)
- Added atomic KMS key promotion orchestration and controller
- Helm hooks to coordinate pre/post promotion jobs
- Terraform variables to configure promotion window and fallback keys
- Automatic rollback hooks and documented runbook for on-prem clusters
Avery Chen (reviewer): Can you clarify the invariants the controller expects from the HSM when promoting? If the HSM can return transient errors we should not mark promotion complete.
Elena Ruiz (author): The controller treats HSM transient errors as retryable for the duration of the promotion_window. Only persistent failures (>= 3 consecutive failures over promotion_window) trigger the rollback hook. I added comments and unit tests around retry behavior.
Priya Natarajan (reviewer): Helm hooks look good but make sure the promote-posthook is idempotent in case the job is retried by Tiller or Helm3. Also include a final 'verify-pp' probe before switching primary symlink.
Elena Ruiz (author): Updated promote-posthook to use a compare-and-swap flag stored in a Kubernetes annotation; added verify-pp probe script and tests.
This PR originated from a support case (SUP-8301) where a customer experienced a failed HSM promotion that took several minutes of manual intervention. The automation reduces human error and latency during cutover.

Background: customer private control planes require strict egress policies but also need DNS resolution to Redwood control-plane endpoints and private model registries in cross-account deployments. This PR adds a least-privilege egress security group for control-plane subnets, provisions Route53 Resolver endpoints (outbound+inbound where requested) via Terraform modules, and wires resolver rules so private DNS for *.redwood.internal resolves to the vendor VPC resolver. It also updates the private-installer Helm chart to support configuring resolver endpoint IDs and exposes a safe rollout path with a dry-run mode. Summary of changes: 1) Terraform: new module redwood_vpc_dns_resolver that creates Route53 Resolver outbound endpoints, resolver rules, and conditional inbound endpoints (for on-prem VPN/Direct Connect scenarios); supports tagging, secondary-secondary-subnet placement for HA, and explicit security group attachment. 2) Security: new controlplane_egress_sg with explicit allow-list egress for: - Route53 Resolver IPs (port 53 UDP/TCP) - TLS egress to platform endpoints (443) to specific prefix-lists supplied by the control plane account - NTP (123/UDP) to customer-provided NTP CIDRs (configurable) All other egress is denied by default. 3) Helm: chart values.schema updated with resolver.enabled, resolver.outbound_endpoint_id, resolver.inbound_endpoint_id, resolver.rule_name, and installer.dryRun to support preflight validation without applying route changes. 4) Installer orchestration: adds a two-phase rollout; phase A creates outbound endpoint and resolver rules and attaches the egress SG in a permissive verification mode, phase B flips the SG to enforce deny-by-default and tears down permissive verification hooks. 5) Docs and upgrade: added upgrade notes and rollback steps for both Terraform and Helm paths and a script to back out resolver rules in 1 command. Motivation: several customers hit operational surprises when egress was wide-open and DNS leaked to public resolvers; this reduces blast radius while preserving resolution for platform-hosted edges. Testing and validation performed: - Unit/integration Terraform plan and apply in a dedicated test AWS account using the new module - Helm template rendering across supported chart versions and dry-run mode validation - End-to-end validation that control-plane pods can resolve and reach *.control.redwood.internal and model-registry.private.redwood.internal after outbound endpoints are provisioned - Failover test: simulated subnet failure by draining one AZ and ensuring resolver HA works - Security audit: manual review of SG rules to enforce least privilege and avoid 0.0.0.0/0 egress. Rollout plan: 1) Deploy module in staging with resolver.enabled=true and installer.dryRun=true 2) Verify DNS via the staging control plane and metrics for DNS latency/error 3) Flip dryRun to false and apply SG enforcement in a maintenance window 4) Monitor for 48 hours and use rollback script if anomalous resolution or app connectivity occurs. Rollback: instructions added to docs/installer/rollback-resolver.md and implemented as a terraform destroy target plus Helm values revert. Related: builds on ENG-4872 (subnet isolation work) and closes ENG-5127. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module implemented and unit-tested - [x] Helm values/schema updated - [x] E2E validation in staging account - [x] Security review completed - [x] Upgrade and rollback docs added - [x] CI passes (lint/terraform fmt/helm lint) See also: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-5127/control-plane-egress-and-dns-resolver-design and internal runbook https://redwood-internal.example.com/runbooks/controlplane-dns-egress.
Ethan Cole: Can we avoid creating inbound resolver endpoints by default? Suggest making inbound endpoints opt-in via variable resolver.create_inbound (response: PR author: made inbound endpoint opt-in with resolver.create_inbound default=false)
Marta Lopez: Needs a note about resolver rules priority and how they interact with existing customer rules (response: added rule_name and priority docs and validation) 
Jun Park: Please add unit tests that assert the SG does not contain 0.0.0.0/0 egress after apply (response: added terraform test and manual audit note)
Security Bot (automated scan): flagged potential NTP wide-open rule in initial patch (response: restricted NTP to customer NTP CIDR and documented requirement)

Motivation: Customers deploying Redwood Private in air-gapped/on-prem environments require a single reproducible offline bundle that includes vendored container images, Helm charts, CRD artifacts and distro-specific runtime manifests. Previous installer iterations relied on customers mirroring public registries or running an external proxy, which is error-prone for regulated environments. This PR implements an end-to-end offline bundle generation workflow, vendorizes key runtime dependencies, and introduces config overlays for multiple kube distros (kubeadm, RKE2, k0s) so installs are resilient to distro-specific networking and CRI differences.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a new CLI command: "installer bundle create-offline --output <dir> --kube-distro <distro> --images-list <file>". This command downloads and packs: container images (tarred), Helm chart tgz, vendor/operator manifests, CRDs, and a distro overlay. The command supports a --verify-checksum mode to produce SHA256 manifest.
- Vendors runtime dependencies into /bundles/<version>/vendor: nginx-ingress (forked minimal manifest), cert-manager v1.12.0, redis-operator, and the redwood-runtime Helm chart tarball. All vendored artifacts are stored with provenance files (SOURCE, CHECKSUM).
- Helm chart changes: chart/templates now include a distro-overlay conditional path so values can toggle kube-distro specific defaults (service type, hostNetwork/hostPort handling, init container CRI adjustments). Added a new values.kubeDistro map with supported keys: kubeadm, rke2, k0s.
- Installer manifests: Introduces a small distro runtime shim that patches ServiceAccount annotations and PodSecurityPolicy alternatives for distros that lack PSP (k0s).
- Terraform module updates: terraform/modules/private-installer now exposes bundle_source (local archive path) and pre-seeded_registry config used by on-prem mirror bootstrap. Added a helper script terraform/bootstrap-mirror.sh to load images into a registry.
- Upgrade/rollback: bundle metadata contains a bundle.manifest.json (packaged as string in the bundle) that the installer uses to detect bundle mismatch and offer an automated just-in-time partial rollback of Helm release values when upgrading between vendored runtime sets.

Testing and validation:
- Added unit tests for the CLI arg parsing and checksum verification.
- Integration test harness (perf-lab simulated air-gapped cluster) exercised bundle create-offline -> bootstrap-mirror -> installer apply on kubeadm and k0s. Test logs attached in CI artifact.
- Manual verification run with a customer-provided RKE2 lab cluster uncovered and fixed a DNS kube-dns readiness race (handled via a preflight wait step and configurable timeout).

Backward compatibility and migration notes:
- The installer still supports the existing online install flow; offline bundle support is opt-in and gated behind --bundle.
- Existing Terraform deployments can set bundle_source to null to keep previous behavior.

Security and compliance:
- All vendored images are signed using our internal Cosign key and signatures are included in /vendor/signatures. The CLI emits a human-readable provenance log for audit.
- No runtime secrets are introduced into the bundle. KMS/HSM integrations remain unchanged.

Follow-ups (future work):
- Automate periodic vendor refresh job to rotate bundled third-party components.
- Add RKE2-specific systemd tweak presets and more exhaustive distro conformance tests.

References: Linear ENG-2319, ENG-2494 (upgrade tooling), customer ticket SUP-9042 (air-gapped install requests).
Diego Morales (reviewer): Nice work. A few asks: please split the big vendor tarball creation into a streamable path (memory bounds) and add a health-check for the mirror bootstrap script.
Aisha Kumar (author): Thanks — split the tar streaming logic into streamTarWriter() and added a --buffer-size flag. mirror bootstrap now retries with exponential backoff and reports per-image errors.
Lin Chen (reviewer): Helm template change looks good but we should avoid introducing hostNetwork by default. Please ensure kubeDistro defaults are conservative.
Aisha Kumar (author): Updated values.yaml to set hostNetwork: false for all distros by default and added an explicit example in docs for when hostNetwork is required.
QA (reviewer): Integration tests failed on RKE2 due to kube-dns readiness. Reproduced locally. Suggested adding a preflight wait for DNS with configurable timeout.
Aisha Kumar (author): Added preflight wait step and a new flag --preflight-timeout with default 5m; re-ran integration tests and they pass in CI artifacts.

Motivation: Private installer deployments were occasionally failing during tenant bootstrap when parallel installs applied overlapping RBAC manifests; rollbacks could leave partially-applied roles that broke subsequent upgrades. This PR introduces a manifest fingerprinting mechanism, a sealed-bootstrap orchestration mode (no external credentials required during in-cluster seeding), and a rollback guard to detect and safely revert only fully-applied policy bundles. Scope: adds a deterministic fingerprint to each generated RBAC/policy bundle, consolidates bootstrap permissions into a single ephemeral controller role, implements a staged-apply planner that validates idempotence via plan-diff and fingerprint checks, and adds a preflight network+policy scan to the Helm preinstall hook to ensure tenant isolation constraints. Checklist: - [x] Design doc and architecture review complete - [x] End-to-end integration tests for bootstrap and rollback - [x] Terraform module backwards compatibility tests - [x] Helm chart bump and values schema update - [x] Security review for reduced-privilege bootstrap flow Implementation summary: - Manifest fingerprinting: a SHA256 of normalized YAML (sorted keys, stripped timestamps) is appended as annotations/redwood.io/manifest-fingerprint to all generated Role, RoleBinding, ClusterRole, and ClusterRoleBinding manifests. This enables deterministic detection of whether a bundle was applied unchanged. - Sealed-bootstrap mode: bootstrap-controller runs with a sealed-serviceaccount token pattern; it fetches encrypted secrets from the installer step (local disk or cloud KMS) and performs tenant-scoped seeding without long-lived elevated credentials. - Staged-apply planner: computes plan-diff against live cluster and refuses to apply if non-fingerprint changes are detected unless explicitly forced with --force-unmanaged. - Rollback guard: on upgrade failure, the operator will only revert bundles whose fingerprints match the last successful apply; bundles with divergent fingerprints are marked for manual investigation and left intact to prevent accidental privilege escalation or data loss. - Preflight policy scan: Helm preinstall hook now runs a lightweight admission-style check that verifies VPC networkPolicy templates and namespace-affinity rules to catch tenant isolation regressions before apply. Migrations and compatibility: - Terraform module change: outputs now include bundle_fingerprint and sealed_bootstrap_enabled flags. Existing installs will continue to run in legacy bootstrap mode unless the new sealed flag is set. - Helm values: added .sealedBootstrap.enabled (false default), .rbac.bundleFingerprintPolicy (hash|none), and preflight.enabled (true default for private deployments). Testing: - Unit tests for fingerprint normalization and deterministic ordering - Integration CI job added (private-installer/e2e-bootstrap) exercising sealed-bootstrap with KMS mock - Manual validation documented in docs/installer/README-sealed-bootstrap.md Rollout plan: - Canary deploy on low-load private tenants for 48h with staged-apply logs enabled - Monitor SLOs and audit logs for any unexpected role bindings - If any plan-diff mismatches occur, abort rollout and open ENG-PRIV-ISSUE for manual triage Security considerations: - Sealed-bootstrap reduces blast radius by using ephemeral controller credentials and KMS-sealed payloads - Fingerprint annotations are non-sensitive and only used for idempotence checks - Audit trail inclusion: installer records fingerprint and plan hash to the tenant audit log Files changed (high level): - installer/pkg/bootstrap/controller.go (new sealed bootstrap controller and rollback guard) - installer/templates/rbac/*.yaml (added fingerprint annotations and normalization) - helm/redwood-private/values.schema.json (new fields) - terraform/modules/private-bootstrap/outputs.tf (fingerprint outputs) - docs/installer/README-sealed-bootstrap.md (new doc) - ci/jobs/e2e-bootstrap.yaml (added integration job) Example normalized snippet used for fingerprinting (normalized YAML one-liner): "apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1;kind:Role;metadata:{name:tenant-admin,namespace:tenant-123,annotations:{'redwood.io/manifest-fingerprint':"<sha256>"}};rules:[{apiGroups:[''],resources:['pods'],verbs:['get','list']}]" Commits summary: - add: sealed-bootstrap controller and manifest fingerprinting || - feat: staged-apply planner and rollback guard || - chore: helm values schema and terraform outputs || - test: e2e private-installer job and unit tests || - docs: sealed-bootstrap usage and migration guide
Ethan Z: Please ensure fingerprinting normalization is stable across Go YAML serializers; prefer canonical JSON pathing if possible.
Maya L: We need a clear admin recovery path documented in case preflight blocks valid customer network setups.
Ibrahim K: CI flaked on e2e with KMS mock, re-run after fix to mock logic.
Sofia P (author): Addressed serializer stability by switching to canonical JSON marshalling; added recovery steps to docs and tightened KMS mock in CI.

Motivation: customers deploying Redwood Private in constrained VPCs reported intermittent egress failures when control-plane outbound traffic was routed through shared NAT or proxy appliances. This PR introduces a controlled VPC PrivateLink-based egress proxy for control-plane components plus an AZ-aware subnet handoff that keeps control-plane ENIs in the same AZ as worker subnets to reduce cross-AZ data charges and improve latency. Changes are implemented primarily in Terraform modules and the controlplane Helm chart, with an idempotent upgrade/rollback script and docs. Scope: terraform modules: new privatelink egress module, security-group least-privilege rules, route table propagation guards; ansible/subnet-handoff playbook for on-prem installers; helm: controlplane values to enable headless egress service + readiness for TLS over privatelink; scripts: upgrade/rollback-controlplane.sh which runs a dry-run then applies changes with health checks; docs: detailed migration steps and Rollback playbook. Checklist: [x] implement privatelink egress module and tests (unit + plan) [x] add AZ-aware subnet handoff playbook [x] update controlplane Helm chart values with feature flag [x] add CI smoke test for control-plane egress [x] add documentation and upgrade playbook [x] validate route propagation and SG audit. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is unchanged unless operators opt into the new privatelink_egress=true flag; upgrade script is safe by default (dry-run + canary). Related: Linear ENG-10234 (private control-plane resiliency), ENG-10577 (egress cost regression). See internal design doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/privatelink-egress (internal).
Arjun Patel: Please tighten SG egress rules - I see a 0.0.0.0/0 fallback in the initial module. We should only allow AWS-managed prefix lists + the proxy ENI range.
Maya Chen: Updated sg-controlplane.tf to reference aws_managed_prefix_list for S3 and ECR and added explicit privatelink ENI CIDR set. Pushed a follow-up commit (c2381b2).
Lina Gomez: Can we add a safety guard to avoid automatic TGW route propagation? If the customer has multiple TGWs this can leak routes between control-plane and data-plane VPCs.
Maya Chen: Added route_propagation_lock variable and explicit aws_ec2_transit_gateway_route_table_association resources only when enable_tgw_propagation=true. Also documented the risk in the migration guide.
Samir Rao: Upgrade script looks good, but add a --no-reboot-mode for on-prem where reboots are disruptive.
Maya Chen: Added --no-reboot flag and an explicit health-check wait loop that gates completion. Also added CI smoke test to validate no-reboot path.
Arjun Patel: Approved after SG tightening and tests green.
Lina Gomez: Approved.
Introduce optional PrivateLink-based control-plane egress proxy and AZ-aware subnet handoff. Operators can opt-in with privatelink_egress=true; includes upgrade/rollback script and migration docs. Reduces cross-AZ egress and provides least-privilege SGs for control-plane outbound traffic.
To enable in an existing deployment: 1) run installer/scripts/upgrade/rollback-controlplane.sh --dry-run and review plan; 2) set privatelink_egress=true in controlplane values and apply; 3) validate control-plane pods have ENIs in target AZs and that Route53 Resolver rules are configured for cross-account DNS forwarding if applicable. Rollback: rerun script with --rollback flag. See installer/docs/privatelink-egress.md for troubleshooting.
Low-medium: default behavior unchanged. Enabling feature modifies VPC routing and SGs; improper configuration can disrupt egress. Migration includes dry-run and health gates. Customers with complex TGW setups should coordinate with network teams.
Unit terraform plan tests added, helm smoke tests added, ansible idempotence validated. Manual canary applied to two internal staging VPCs and observed no regressions in control-plane health metrics over 48h.
1) publish migration doc to customer-facing KB 2) bump module version in registry 3) monitor control-plane egress metrics and alert on >2x baseline egress after rollout

Motivation: Private installs running high-cardinality workloads (customer embeddings, per-tenant metrics) hit Prometheus remote_write/ingestion bottlenecks and cause alert storms during upgrades. This PR implements three operational features to make observability upgrades and high-throughput installs safer: 1) exporter rotation orchestration that drains and replaces metrics exporters (node-exporter/prometheus-exporter sidecars) during upgrades to avoid double-scrape spikes and gaps; 2) remote_write sharding support in the Terraform module + Prometheus Helm values so high-cardinality telemetry can be sharded across multiple remote_write receivers/backends; 3) alert autoscale policy and Alertmanager replica rotation to prevent alert floods from bringing down control plane components. Summary of changes and approach: - Helm: add values.exporterRotation.{enabled,drainTimeout,preStopHookScript} controlling a preStop lifecycle script that signals exporter sidecars to stop emitting for a short window and waits for Prometheus to complete pending scrapes. Also add prometheus.remoteWrite.shards and prometheus.remoteWrite.shardKey settings and templates to render multiple remote_write targets. - Terraform: extend modules/observability with variable remote_write_shards (default 1), remote_write_targets (list of endpoints) and create a lightweight sharding plan that generates k8s Secret + Service resources for each shard when shards>1. Also add upgrade-safe lifecycle for Grafana deployments to rotate pods with a configurable maxUnavailable and annotation-based rotation marker. - Installer orchestration: add a new hook (scripts/rotate_exporters.sh) used by Helm hooks and by the installer upgrade pipeline to perform a coordinated rotation: mark exporters read-only, wait for KV cache flushes and Prometheus scrape windows, then scale down old exporters and scale up new ones. Hook is idempotent and logs to /var/log/redwood-observability-rotate.log. - Alerting: add a horizontal-pod-autoscaler template for Alertmanager that uses a custom metric (alerts_per_min) collected by a tiny exporter; include default thresholds and a fallback to fixed replicas when metrics are absent. Also include a rate-limiting rule and default grouping/routing templates to cut alert storms during rollout windows. Backwards compatibility and upgrade notes: the changes are opt-in via new installer flags (observability.exporterRotation.enabled and observability.remoteWrite.shards) so existing customers won't see behavior changes unless they enable them. The Terraform module supports a migration path: with remote_write_shards set to >1 the installer will create additional k8s Services and Secrets; a one-time run of 'terraform apply' will materialize shards. Rollback plan: helm rollback will disable rotation hooks via a release annotation the hook checks; Terraform changes are additive (create-only) and removed on shard count=1. Tests and validation: - Unit tests for terraform templates and helm templating added. - Integration e2e run in the private-installer CI staging cluster validated exporter rotation with a synthetic 50k series workload and confirmed no more than 2% scrape loss during rotation. - Manual runbook added to docs/upgrade-observability-rotation.md. Monitoring and observability: added metrics for rotation progress (rotation_in_progress, exporters_drained_count), Prometheus recording rules for alert autoscale triggers, and Grafana dashboard panels to visualize shard distribution and rotation state. Why this is different from previous provisioning work: earlier PRs focused on bootstrapping stacks and provisioning dashboards; this PR focuses on operational safety and runtime scaling for high-cardinality customers and upgrade windows, providing automated, reversible operations for on-prem and VPC private installs.
Sofia Chen (2026-01-30): This approach looks good; can you make the rotation script tolerant of network partitions?
Jordan Patel (2026-01-30): Updated rotate_exporters.sh to retry on transient failures and to log per-step status; added idempotency checks
Marcus Liu (2026-02-02): Suggest lowering default drainTimeout from 120s to 60s for smaller clusters; also asked for a fallback when remote_write receiver returns 503s
Jordan Patel (2026-02-03): Lowered default to 60s and added exponential backoff for remote_write target retries; added circuit-breaker annotation
Priya Nair (2026-02-08): Verified terraform plan output and helm templates in staging; requested one more e2e run against 50k-series workload
Jordan Patel (2026-02-09): Re-ran e2e, attached logs and confirmed metrics; CI had a flaky integration test which I reran and it passed
Sofia Chen (2026-02-10): Approved and marked for merge
Added exporter rotation orchestration for safe upgrades, support for sharded Prometheus remote_write via Terraform and Helm, Alertmanager autoscaling with alert-throttling templates, and runbook for enabling these features in private installs.
Operators enabling sharding must provide remote_write endpoints in installer config and ensure downstream storage can accept shard-specific keys. For upgrades, run the rotation in a maintenance window and monitor rotation_in_progress metric. The rotation script writes detailed logs to /var/log/redwood-observability-rotate.log.
payload.title: observability: exporter rotation, remote_write sharding, and alert autoscale for private installs

Problem: release application for private-installer can partially apply manifests when concurrent pipelines overlap (e.g. two builds push near-simultaneously). This has caused transient mismatches between the published release manifest and the in-cluster helm state, forcing manual rollbacks. Goal: make release manifest publishing and cluster apply transactional and idempotent so that either the entire manifest set is applied (and published) or nothing changes, with a short, observable staging window and an automatic rollback marker if something fails.

What this PR does (single string): Adds a TUF-backed transactional lock and a manifest staging area to the private-installer release pipeline. The new flow stages a release bundle under a provisional manifest name (manifest:vN-staging), obtains a transactional advisory lock via the TUF metadata store (using conditional metadata updates and an ephemeral lock role), performs preflight validation (diff checks, schema/helm lint, and cluster dry-run against the target kubeconfig), attempts a staged helm apply using --wait and a short timeout, and upon success atomically promotes the staged manifest to the canonical manifest name (manifest:vN) using a signed metadata rotation step. If promotion fails or preflight fails, we write a rollback marker file (manifest:vN-rollback) and garbage collect the staged artifacts after a TTL. The implementation is intentionally conservative: timeouts and retries are tunable via pipeline variables and default to conservative values to reduce false positives.

Changes included: 1) CI pipeline: new release-transactional job (gitlab/worker) that stages artifacts and orchestrates TUF metadata updates; 2) TUF tooling: add tuf-lock CLI and small library helpers for conditional role updates and ephemeral lock roles; 3) Installer: manifest staging path support and rollback marker handling in the private-installer repo; 4) Helm: chart hooks updated to treat staged annotations specially and to emit structured apply result records; 5) Terraform: adds a data source that can query the canonical manifest state for automation hooks; 6) Tests: end-to-end CI integration test simulating concurrent publishes, and unit tests around lock edge-cases.

Why this approach: We considered a pure datastore advisory lock but chose to build on top of our existing TUF metadata store to ensure provenance and signed atomicity of promotion steps. This gives auditability (signed metadata changes) and prevents race conditions across regions that rely on the same artifact index. The staged manifest approach also preserves a traceable artifact lineage for rollbacks and postmortem.

Checklist: - [x] Add staged manifest path and promotion API - [x] Implement tuf-lock CLI + library - [x] Hook promotion to signed metadata rotation - [x] Add rollback marker and GC policy - [x] Integration tests for concurrent publish - [x] Update release docs and runbook snippets - [x] CI job and RBAC for pipeline to sign/push metadata

Notes and migration: Existing release consumers that read manifest:vN remain unchanged. New consumers can query manifest:vN-staging when they want to validate in a staging environment. The pipeline introduces two new environment variables (RELEASE_LOCK_TTL and STAGING_TTL) with reasonable defaults. We also rotate one ephemeral TUF key used for lock leases; the rotation step is included and gated behind a feature flag for the first rollout.
Diego Morales: We should be careful about TUF metadata size growth with staging metadata — can we compact signed history after promotion? (answered: we add a compaction GC that keeps N historical signed promotions and tombstones older ones)
Anya Patel: The helm --wait timeout default seems long for CI. Suggest adding a short default and exposing config. (fixed: exposed STAGING_TIMEOUT and reduced default to 3m)
Owen Park: Race scenario where promotion completes but a downstream CDN hasn't pulled new blob; how do consumers handle eventual consistency? (reply: producers must write promotion + published index; consumers can use a small backoff or detect 404s and retry; added doc section)
Security review (Emily Zhao): Ensure pipeline signing keys are in KMS and not present in CI image; verify — switched to KMS sign flow and added an allowlist for signing service accounts
Adds transactional release apply for private-installer: staged manifests, TUF-backed advisory locks, promotion and rollback markers, and CI job to orchestrate atomic publishes. Improves reliability for concurrent releases and provides stronger provenance for promotion steps.
payload.title: transactional-release-apply: add TUF-backed transactional locks and manifest staging

Context: Private control plane installations in multi-region accounts occasionally experience cross-account DNS resolution failures during regional failover. This PR introduces a deterministic regional-fallback peering mechanism that creates ephemeral route targets and orchestrates conditional Route53 Resolver rule promotion for the control plane's private hosted zones. Motivation: reduce downtime during regional control plane migrations and simplify cross-account endpoint routing without permanently enlarging peering footprints. Design summary: (1) Terraform module `controlplane-peering` creates scoped peering connections with tags and a lifecycle policy that ensures peering attachments are ephemeral and self-reconciling; (2) Helm hooks for the private controlplane operator to trigger staged DNS promotion and graceful KV-cache flushing when peering target changes; (3) Add a resolver-guard Lambda (optional) that validates resolver rules and applies TTL-aware promotion to preserve DNS cache correctness; (4) Security: security group templates restrict controlplane peering to specific ports and use egress-only prefix lists for data plane egress; (5) Rollout: a canary rollout that first provisions peering and resolver rules in the staging account, then promotes to two additional regions with automatic rollback on health/trace regressions. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module and example usage - [x] Helm chart templates and hook implementations - [x] IAM least-privilege for peering orchestration - [x] E2E canary test in staging - [x] Observability: metrics + alerts for resolver promotion failures - [x] Upgrade and rollback documentation included in the chart notes. Testing and validation: unit tests for Terraform plan diffs added under modules/controlplane-peering/tests; integration harness run against the staging org with three accounts verified resolver promotion under 95th percentile latency. Manual runbooks for forced rollback are added: `docs/rollback-controlplane-peering.md`. Deployment notes: Use the new chart values `controlplane.peering.enabled=true` and `controlplane.peering.fallbackRegions=["us-west-2","us-east-1"]`. When enabling in production, first run the terraform module with `plan-only` in a non-prod account to inspect proposed peering attachments. If the optional resolver-guard Lambda is enabled, ensure the IAM role is granted cross-account Route53Resolver permissions. Related: ENG-6372 for rollout automation, OPS-129 for incident follow-ups.
Marco Li: This looks good overall. Two asks: 1) Can we make the resolver-guard optional by default? 2) Add a smoke test that verifies SRV/TXT records are preserved during promotion.
Priya N. Iyer: Agree; made resolver-guard opt-in via chart value `resolverGuard.enabled=false` by default and added an integration smoke test validating TXT preservation.
Hannah Ortiz: Security review: tighten the SG egress to only allow AWS-managed prefix lists for ECR and S3. Also request a short threat model note in the docs.
Priya N. Iyer: Applied SG change and added threat model section to docs/rollback-controlplane-peering.md.
Connor Blake: CI flaky on first run due to parallel Terraform apply in tests. Reran and all checks returned green.
CI Bot: unit-tests passed; terraform-plan checks passed; helm-lint passed; integration-canary passed (staging).
Add optional regional-failover peering for private control planes. Includes terraform module, helm chart hooks, resolver promotion tooling, and rollback runbook. Opt-in via chart values. No breaking changes by default.
To enable: run terraform apply in a non-prod account first. Ensure cross-account IAM roles exist before enabling resolver guard. Canary duration defaults to 30 minutes; extend if you have long TTL caches.
Unit tests for module diffs, helm-lint, and staging canary integration. Manual rollback tested end-to-end using the provided runbook. Observability: added metric resolver_promotion.success and resolver_promotion.latency.
This PR addresses repeated incidents of controlplane DNS mismatch during region failover (see SUP-4412).
