Context: Cross-SDK parity work to reduce cognitive load for integrators and to harden streaming auth behavior that caused rare token handoff races in high-concurrency workloads. This PR implements a \"sessionless\" stream bridge for the Go SDK that decouples streaming client state from long-lived session objects, adds a typed error surface, harmonizes retry/backoff presets with TypeScript and Python, and bumps the Go SDK to v1.2.0. Motivation: Several production customers observed rare stalls during credential rotation when the stream consumer held onto a session object while a background reauth replaced tokens (race between send and rebind paths). The previous model also required the consumer to manage explicit session lifecycles, which is a common source of misuse across languages.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces sessionless.StreamBridge which maintains ephemeral per-stream credentials and performs in-line credential refresh with a single goroutine per bridge instead of per-session. This reduces goroutine proliferation and removes a hard-to-observe race where a session replace could outlive inflight requests.
- Adds a typed error package (errors/typed.go) that surfaces enumerated failure kinds (ErrTransient, ErrAuthExpired, ErrBackoffExceeded, ErrProtocolMismatch). Consumers can switch on concrete error kinds instead of string matching.
- Harmonizes retry presets with TS/Py: introduced RetryProfileLight, RetryProfileDefault and RetryProfileConservative and a lightweight adapter that maps SDK retry hints to the platform's centralized retry router. This aligns with ENG-1193/ENG-1195 and companion SDK PRs (TS: PR #670213, Py: PR #381207).
- UX/ergonomics: single-call consumer API StreamBridge.Start(ctx, opts) returns a typed iterator that supports ctx cancellation, .Pause()/.Resume() hints, and backpressure-friendly ReadFrame(ctx) semantics. The old SessionHandle API remains but is deprecated in favor of the sessionless flow.
- Version bump: updates go/sdk/version/version.go to 1.2.0 and a short migration guide in docs/upgrade/sessionless.md.

Commit summary (short):
- 9a1b3d: add sessionless StreamBridge implementation and core runtime loop
- d7c0f1: add typed error enums and conversion helpers
- f2e7aa: retry profile adapter and mapping table; add tests
- b3c9e5: add examples and migration docs
- 7f21d4: wire CI cross-checks and update changelog; bump version to v1.2.0

Files changed (high level):
- go/sdk/stream/bridge.go (new): core sessionless bridge loop and lifecycle
- go/sdk/stream/iterator.go (updated): typed iterator with context-aware ReadFrame
- go/sdk/auth/refresh.go (updated): inline refresh helper + jittered backoff
- go/sdk/errors/typed.go (new): typed error surface and constructors
- go/sdk/version/version.go (updated): bump to 1.2.0
- docs/upgrade/sessionless.md (new): migration steps and example
- examples/streaming/sessionless_example.go (new): end-to-end snippet
- tests/stream/sessionless_test.go (new): concurrency and rotation tests
- ci/integration/stream-check.yml (updated): run matrix across Go/TS/Py crosschecks
- python/sdk/sessionless_adapter.py (cherry-picked doc change): API note for migration (kept deliberately small to aid parity checks)

Testing and CI: All unit and integration suites were run in CI. Notable checks: go test (race) passed, integration-stream matrix passed against a local platform runtime fixture, TS and Py parity smoke checks ran in the job and passed. One intermittent flaky test (tests/stream/rebind_race_test) was quarantined and converted to deterministic harness; original flaky behavior reproduced locally prior to the fix which validated the change.

Review summary and conversation:
- Diego Marquez: \"This reduces goroutine churn and looks much cleaner. Concern: how does this interact with Dedicated slow-start? Please add a metrics hook for bridge_count and refresh_latency.\" (requested changes)
- Marina Ortega (author): \"Added bridge_count and refresh_latency histogram; pushed an extra commit to expose metrics via the Console shim.\" (resolved)
- Aisha Kapoor: \"Typed errors are very helpful — please ensure we keep conversion helpers for older consumers who still compare strings.\" (requested minor change)
- Marina Ortega: \"Added As() helpers and updated migration docs with examples using errors.Is/As.\" (resolved)
- Linus Park: \"Please add a migration note about deprecated SessionHandle and a short snippet showing equivalence.\" (approved after docs update)
- Final reviewers approved and CI green; PR was squash-merged to main on 2026-02-20.

Backwards compatibility and rollout guidance: The change is backwards-compatible but the SessionHandle API is deprecated (not removed). Recommend bumping application dependencies to v1.2.0 within a 2-week window for customers who previously managed session lifecycles. For high-throughput tenants, enable the new bridge behind an opt-in flag in Console; we plan to flip by default in 2 minor releases after additional telemetry collection.

Release notes: See release_notes field for structured bullets. Migration doc added at docs/upgrade/sessionless.md.
Diego Marquez: Concern about Dedicated slow-start; requested metrics hooks (bridge_count, refresh_latency).
Author: Added metrics and exposed via Console shim; pushed commit d7c0f1.
Aisha Kapoor: Asked for As()/Is() helpers for typed errors; requested doc sample.
Author: Added helpers and updated migration docs; tests added.
Linus Park: Asked for migration snippet comparing SessionHandle -> StreamBridge; docs added and approved.
SDK: Go SDK bumped to v1.2.0 — introduces sessionless StreamBridge (recommended) and deprecates SessionHandle.
UX: New typed errors (ErrTransient, ErrAuthExpired, ErrBackoffExceeded, ErrProtocolMismatch) for programmatic handling.
Reliability: inline credential refresh with single-goroutine bridge reduces goroutine pressure and fixes rare rebind races.
Interoperability: retry profile presets aligned across Go/TS/Py (RetryProfileLight/Default/Conservative).
Added sessionless StreamBridge and typed errors; deprecated SessionHandle; bumped version to 1.2.0; migration guide added.

Context: As part of the streaming/tool-calling examples refresh, we need a runnable Go example that matches the canonical event model and a small set of fixtures to keep behavior stable across releases. We’ve also had customer confusion around tool-call args looking “truncated” mid-stream (SUP-18421). This PR adds an example + tests that explicitly demonstrate how to assemble tool-call arguments across deltas.

What’s included: 1) New example: cmd/examples/tool_calling_streaming/main.go (and README) demonstrating: - Defining tools with JSON schema-ish parameters (kept small and copy/paste friendly) - Streaming loop that handles: message deltas, tool_call deltas, and final assembly - Correct handling of partial tool-call arguments: accumulate string fragments until the final tool_call message is complete before json.Unmarshal - Executing multiple tool calls sequentially (example shows 2 calls) and sending tool results back as tool-result messages

2) Golden fixtures + tests: - Added fixtures under internal/testdata/golden/tool_calls/*.jsonl capturing a few “representative” transcripts: a) tool-call args split across multiple events b) tool-call args split at UTF-8 boundary (defensive) c) parallel-ish tool calls emitted back-to-back (model emits multiple tool_call entries before final)
- Added TestStreamingToolCallsGolden that replays event JSONL into the assembler and asserts stable output (final assistant message + tool call list).

Notes / caveats documented in the example: - During streaming, tool_call.arguments may be partial; do not parse until you see the final tool_call completion event / finish_reason. - Do not assume each chunk is valid JSON. Treat args as an opaque string buffer until complete. - Fixtures strip request_id/timestamps to avoid flake.

Why fixtures in Go repo: we want a language-local guardrail so the example doesn’t drift when we touch the stream consumer loop (ENG-4825). This is meant to be small/fast (runs in <1s) and does not hit the network.

Checklist: - [x] Example is runnable end-to-end with REDWOOD_API_KEY - [x] Example output is deterministic given fixtures - [x] Tests added + run in CI - [x] Comments call out partial args pitfall + reference SUP-18421

Follow-ups: We may later expand to show true parallel tool execution (goroutines) once we finalize the recommended pattern; for now the example keeps execution serial to be easiest to copy/paste.
Ibrahim Khan (review): This is the right direction. Two nits: (1) please make it explicit in the example that args buffers can be invalid JSON mid-stream; (2) the golden fixtures should not include request_id-like fields or timestamps. Also, can we add a small comment referencing the support ticket about “truncated args” so folks understand why we buffer?

Mateusz Zielinski (author): Good call. Updated README + inline comments to say args are opaque until completion; added a section “Why args look truncated” and referenced SUP-18421. Also added a fixture normalizer that strips request_id/created_at-ish fields before committing the JSONL.

Brian Murphy (review): The assembler currently attempts json.Unmarshal on every delta if the buffer ends with '}'. That’s not safe (nested braces, strings, etc.). We should only parse once we know the tool_call is complete (finish_reason or explicit final event).

Mateusz Zielinski (author): Agreed. Removed the 'endsWith' heuristic. Now we parse only when we receive a completed tool_call entry (event indicates tool_call is finalized). Added a test case where args buffer contains braces inside a string.

Sahana Iyer (review): CI note: golden tests are great but can flake if ordering differs. Please ensure deterministic ordering for tool calls in the assembled output, or assert as a set with stable sort.

Mateusz Zielinski (author): Sorted tool calls by (tool_call_id, index) in the assembler output before asserting. Updated tests accordingly.

Sabrina James (review): Example reads well. Minor: rename variables from tc to toolCall for readability; and please ensure the tool result message uses the exact role/name field expected in other language examples.

Mateusz Zielinski (author): Renamed variables, and aligned the tool-result message shape to match the parity guidelines (role=tool, tool_call_id set, content is the tool output).
Ibrahim Khan (approval): Looks solid now. The README callout on partial args + the fixtures make this much safer for copy/paste. Approved.
Brian Murphy (approval): Thanks for removing the heuristic parsing. Approved.
Sahana Iyer (approval): CI is clean; fixture linter is a nice touch. Approved.

Context: Our Go examples still used the old “print whatever arrives” approach for streaming. That breaks down once you include tool-call deltas, content deltas, and the final assembled message (and it’s a common source of support pings when customers try to copy/paste).

This PR refreshes the Go streaming example consumer loop to match the canonical event conventions we’re aligning across Python/TS/Go:
- Treat the stream as an event sequence (content deltas, tool-call deltas, final message, and errors)
- Assemble the final assistant message deterministically (instead of assuming the last chunk is the full message)
- Log/handle partial tool arguments safely (don’t attempt JSON decode mid-stream)
- Add concise retry/disconnect notes so the example doesn’t imply “just reconnect and continue” semantics we don’t guarantee

What changed:
- New helper: AssembleFinalMessage(events) that merges content deltas + tool-call deltas into a final assistant message shape for printing/returning.
- Updated example loop to switch on event.Type and call the helper at the end.
- Improved comments around known footguns: partial args, premature JSON parsing, disconnect/retry.
- Small output changes so the example prints a stable “final” block at the end (useful for docs and smoke tests).

Why now:
- Needed for cross-SDK parity work (ENG-4821/ENG-4825) and the docs refresh.
- Addresses recurring confusion in SUP-18421: customers were parsing tool-call args on every chunk and seeing truncated JSON.

Notes/Non-goals:
- No API/protocol changes. This is example-level code + small helper in the examples package only.
- We intentionally do not add any “resume stream from last event id” sample because we don’t have a stable server-side resume guarantee.

Test plan:
- go test ./... (unit + compilation)
- Ran examples/streaming_chat locally against hosted API (manual) and verified:
  - content prints incrementally
  - tool call args are only parsed after final assembly
  - final message prints once, deterministically

Release notes:
- Go examples: updated streaming consumer loop to robustly assemble final responses; includes guidance for partial tool args and safe retry behavior.
```go
for evt := range stream.Events() {
    switch evt.Type {
    case redwood.EventContentDelta:
        fmt.Print(evt.Delta)
        events = append(events, evt)
    case redwood.EventToolCallDelta:
        // Tool args may be partial mid-stream; defer JSON parsing until final.
        events = append(events, evt)
    case redwood.EventError:
        return fmt.Errorf("stream error: %w", evt.Err)
    case redwood.EventDone:
        final, err := stream_assemble.AssembleFinalMessage(events)
        if err != nil { return err }
        fmt.Printf("\n\n--- final ---\n%s\n", final.Content)
        return nil
    }
}
```
Ibrahim Khan: Can we make it explicit in the example that tool-call args are not guaranteed to be valid JSON until the end? A lot of customers try to Unmarshal on every delta.

Mateusz Zielinski (author): Yep — added a comment in the tool delta case and moved all JSON parsing to after AssembleFinalMessage.

Brian Murphy: The helper currently concatenates args strings; do we need to handle “multiple tool calls” within the same response?

Mateusz Zielinski: Good catch. Updated AssembleFinalMessage to key by tool_call_id and merge args per call. Added a test with two calls in one stream.

Wei Chen: Please add a short retry note. Docs keep getting questions about reconnect semantics.

Mateusz Zielinski: Added a retry/disconnect section: we recommend retrying the *request* idempotently, not resuming mid-stream. Also added a link placeholder to the canonical streaming conventions page (docs will wire it up).

Monica Patel: Any chance this changes public SDK APIs?

Mateusz Zielinski: No public API changes; helper is under examples/internal. Streaming API usage is unchanged.

Ibrahim Khan: Approved after the multi-tool merge fix + tests.

Brian Murphy: Approved.

Monica Patel: Approved.
Merged via squash after adding multi-tool merge handling in AssembleFinalMessage and clarifying retry/disconnect semantics in example comments.

Context: This PR is part of the cross-language SDK parity work for streaming semantics and error taxonomy. We’ve had multiple reports (SUP-29505) of streaming disconnects behind proxies/load balancers where the Go SDK returned opaque io.EOF / net errors without request_id, making Support/oncall triage slow (INT-1182). Also, customers asked for clearer guidance on whether they should retry streaming calls, and under what conditions (avoid duplicated completions / side effects). What this PR does: (1) Introduces typed streaming error surfaces so callers can distinguish server-side HTTP failures (pre-stream) vs transport disconnects (mid-stream) vs user cancellation/timeouts. (2) Propagates request_id and status_code onto those error types whenever we can infer them from headers/initial response. (3) Adds docs + examples for safe retry patterns and reconnect guidance, with explicit idempotency considerations. Details: - New error types (package redwood): StreamDisconnectError (raised when the HTTP connection drops after streaming has started), StreamResponseError (raised when we receive a non-2xx before streaming begins; wraps the existing APIError shape and includes request_id/status_code/error_code), and StreamCancelledError (wrapping context.Canceled / deadline exceeded so users can distinguish client-driven aborts from server disconnects). - request_id sourcing: for pre-stream errors, request_id comes from the JSON error payload when present, falling back to the X-Request-Id response header; for mid-stream disconnects, we attach request_id from the initial response headers captured at stream start (if we got that far), otherwise request_id is empty and callers should log their own correlation ID as well. - status_code behavior: StreamResponseError always has status_code; StreamDisconnectError sets status_code to 200 when we successfully established the stream and later disconnected (since the HTTP status was OK) and includes a reason string populated from the underlying error (EOF, read: connection reset, unexpected FIN, etc.). - Retry guidance (docs): We intentionally do NOT auto-retry mid-stream because replaying a generation can duplicate user-visible output and can duplicate side effects when tool/function calls are involved. The docs now recommend: (a) retries are safe only when the request failed before any tokens/events were delivered (StreamResponseError) and only for retryable status codes (429/5xx) using the shared retry policy; (b) for mid-stream disconnects (StreamDisconnectError) treat it as a partial result; if you must resume, restart a new request using application-level state (messages so far, partial text) and ensure your downstream side effects are idempotent; (c) for any retried request that could cause side effects, set an Idempotency-Key header and persist it per user action so retries dedupe on the server where supported. - Examples: Added a small snippet showing how to log request_id and differentiate disconnect vs retryable HTTP error. - Tests: Added unit tests that simulate: non-2xx error payload with X-Request-Id header; mid-stream disconnect after N events; and cancellation via context.WithCancel. Tests assert error types and fields (request_id/status_code) and verify we don’t leak API key in error strings. Why now: This was a top gap in the parity matrix (streaming edge cases + request_id propagation) and blocked docs updates and support macros. Follow-ups: - Conformance suite: we should add a fixture that forces a streaming disconnect and asserts the error surface matches other SDKs (tracked in ENG-5127). - Platform: ensure request_id is always present on initial streaming response headers even for proxy-buffered clients (see platform PR redwood/pr-28426). Checklist: - [x] Typed errors exposed for streaming paths - [x] request_id surfaced consistently and redaction-safe - [x] Docs updated w/ retry + idempotency guidance - [x] Unit tests for disconnect + cancellation - [x] CI green
- Go SDK: streaming errors now include request_id + status_code when available, and expose a specific StreamDisconnectError for mid-stream disconnects. - Docs: added guidance on safe retry/reconnect patterns for streaming (idempotency + avoiding duplicate side effects).
Allison Grant (review): Can we make sure the disconnect error includes enough info to distinguish a 200-established stream vs a pre-stream failure? Also please avoid suggesting automatic retries for mid-stream disconnects—SRE is worried about duplicate billing concerns and replay storms. Mateusz (author): Yep—StreamDisconnectError will set status_code=200 if the stream was established and will include the underlying error cause; docs updated to explicitly say no auto-retry mid-stream and to treat it as partial output. Marcus Lin (review): Please confirm we never include the API key/token in error strings and the docs don’t encourage logging headers wholesale. Mateusz: Added redaction checks in tests and the example only logs request_id/status_code and the error type. Ibrahim Khan (review): Looks good for parity; can you also mention Idempotency-Key usage and that it must be stable per user action? Mateusz: Added a dedicated section in docs and a small code snippet. Sabrina James (review): Minor: can we align the field naming in docs with Python/TS (request_id, status_code) and call out that request_id can be missing if disconnect happens before headers? Mateusz: Updated wording and added the caveat. Approvals: Allison ✅, Marcus ✅, Ibrahim ✅, Sabrina ✅

Summary: This PR introduces a compact credential cascade (credential fallback chain) for the Go SDK and refactors the PullStream iterator into a slimmer, ergonomics-focused iterator surface. The goal is parity with newer TS/Python ergonomics while keeping the Go footprint small and allocation-friendly.

Motivation: Customers reported friction when their token provider rotated unexpectedly during long-lived streaming sessions; we observed repeated token refresh retries and duplicated reconnect attempts. At the same time, the current PullStream iterator surface in go-sdk had a few ergonomic rough edges (blocking Read semantics, inconsistent context propagation, and heavy per-chunk allocations) compared to TS/Python counterparts.

Changes: - Add credential cascade: an ordered chain of credential providers (env -> file -> delegated provider -> runtime refresh hook). The cascade is pluggable and preserves existing default behavior but makes it trivial to add a short-circuit fallback provider for dedicated/private deployments. - Introduce CredentialProvider interface with GetToken(ctx) and optional Prewarm(ctx) hooks. - Implement DelegatedProvider shim used by redwood Private customers that need short-lived delegated tokens; the shim includes jittered warmup and transparent refresh. - Slim PullIterator: replaced old PullStream.ReadRaw with PullIterator.Next(ctx) returning a typed Result and an Error sentinel. The iterator is non-blocking-friendly and reduces allocations by reusing a small buffer pool for streaming chunk assembly. - Per-stream retry window: expose a StreamRetryWindow config that constrains automatic reauth/retry attempts for individual stream sessions (useful for low-latency flows that prefer fast failover to fallback models). - Session pinning opt: a small API to pin a stream to a session lease when callers want session-affinity across reconnects. - Backwards-compat: adapter shim for old ReadRaw callers included; deprecation notice added to comments. - Tests: end-to-end integration harness added that simulates token expiry mid-stream and verifies single reconnect and resume.

Commits (high-level): - 8d21c4f: introduce credential cascade types and default chain - b3f2a90: add DelegatedProvider shim and warmup logic - c7a7d85: refactor PullStream into PullIterator with buffer pool - 4f9e303: add StreamRetryWindow and session pinning API - 91a4b55: add integration test harness and CI job - 2b7c1d2: docs and examples, deprecation adapters, changelog

Files changed (high level): - internal/auth/credential_cascade.go (new) - internal/auth/delegated_provider.go (new) - public/cred_provider.go (new interface + docs) - public/stream/iterator.go (refactor: new PullIterator) - public/stream/adapter_compat.go (adapter for ReadRaw) - examples/streaming/cred_fallback_example.go (new) - tests/integration/stream_token_rotate_test.go (new) - docs/sdk-go/streaming.md (updates) - ci/jobs/stream-integration.yaml (adds new job)

Design notes: - The credential cascade is intentionally minimal: providers return a token and TTL; the cascade respects TTL and defers to a fast-path provider when tokens are fresh. - DelegatedProvider implements an exponential jittered Prewarm to avoid thundering herd during churn. - PullIterator.Next(ctx) returns (Result, bool) style internally but surface returns a small struct with EventType/Bytes/Meta to make downstream switch handling obvious. - Reuse of a sync.Pool for chunk buffers cut allocations in local benchmarks by ~35% for 8k average chunk size.

Backwards compatibility: - The adapter_compat preserves old ReadRaw semantics by delegating to the new iterator; it logs a single-level deprecation warning and will be removed in a future major version.

Testing & CI: - New integration job (ci/jobs/stream-integration.yaml) runs against a local test harness that can inject token expiry and network stalls. - Unit tests for credential cascade, DelegatedProvider, and iterator behavior. - CI initially flaked on a timing-sensitive integration test (first run failed due to race in test harness); I bumped a test timeout and added deterministic jitter control. Subsequent runs passed.

Performance: - Microbenchmarks included: iterator allocation profile, buffer reuse, and token-provider latency. - On a small benchmark (simulated 100 concurrent streams, 8k chunks), median p90 CPU went down ~9% and total GC pause decreased.

Migration notes: - Consumers using the older PullStream.ReadRaw API should either migrate to PullIterator.Next or keep using the adapter shim. - If you rely on custom credential providers, implement the CredentialProvider interface and register it in the SDK's Chain. - The default chain is unchanged; opt-in required to enable DelegatedProvider.

Security considerations: - DelegatedProvider is opt-in and requires callers to supply a trusted short-lived token endpoint. - Token values are held only in memory and never logged.

Review conversation: - Claire Thompson (2026-02-13): "Nice cleanup — can we make the Prewarm backoff configurable via a small struct so Private deployments can tune aggressively? Also, please add an example showing DelegatedProvider error handling." - Diego Alvarez reply (2026-02-13): "Good call — added PrewarmConfig and example in examples/streaming/cred_fallback_example.go. DelegatedProvider already returns typed errors; updated docs with usage pattern." - Ethan Liu (2026-02-14): "Iterator looks good; one nit on naming: Next returns StreamEvent vs Result — prefer StreamEvent for clarity." - Diego Alvarez reply (2026-02-14): "Renamed Result -> StreamEvent in public surface and adjusted adapters; updated tests." - Maya Patel (2026-02-15): "Integration test flaky on first run; we should ensure deterministic jitter in CI. Also, add a small comment about buffer pool sizing." - Diego Alvarez reply (2026-02-15): "Added deterministic jitter flag in CI harness and documented pool sizing heuristics in streaming.md." - Claire Thompson approval (2026-02-16): "LGTM after small nit fixes addressed."

CI summary: - Unit: pass - Integration (stream-integration): pass (after one rerun) - Lint: pass - Vet/govet: pass

Merge outcome: Squash and merge to main.

Post-merge followups: - ENG-3498: add a telemetry metric for 'credential_fallback_used' to Console dashboards (tracked). - ENG-3520: propose a TS/Python parity doc to ensure DelegatedProvider behavior matches across SDKs.

Motivation: customer teams saw divergent retry behavior and credential fallback semantics between Go and the other SDKs which created intermittent auth failures under heavy streaming load. This PR harmonizes credential fallback ordering, surfaces a lightweight typed stream handle for cancel/drain ergonomics, and updates the Go SDK to v1.6.0 to match Python/TS parity work.

What this PR does (single-string body): Adds a CredOrchestrator that composes primary token source + delegated fallback providers with deterministic priority and backoff hints; introduces StreamHandle (typed, context-aware) that exposes Cancel/Drain/Closed semantics and emits structured stream lifecycle events; surfaces declarative RetryProfile presets (hedged, latency-sensitive, throughput) and plumbs them into the client transport; fixes several race conditions in session renewal (session.go) discovered in integration tests; updates examples and changelog; bumps module versions and tags v1.6.0. Checklist: [x] unit + integration tests updated, [x] cross-sdk spec docs referenced, [x] minimal migration notes in CHANGELOG, [x] version bump and release notes prepared. Migration notes: existing code using RawStream() can swap to StreamHandle via client.Stream(ctx, opts) which returns an idiomatic interface with Cancel() and WaitClosed(ctx). Backwards compatibility shim provided for one release.

Context and motivation: We observed repeated tenant-facing errors during regional egress congestion where the existing regional circuit opened aggressively and tenants with bursty but otherwise healthy traffic were evicted disproportionately. This PR provides a 'soft-fallback bridge' that (1) applies an SLO-aware grace credit to tenants during transient regional stress, (2) runs a proportional backpressure token pool to ensure fairness when shedding, and (3) smooths circuit-breaker reopen/reclose decisions using a short sliding window to prevent thrash. The change addresses three pain points from ENG-1890 and the incident on 2026-02-03: noisy reopen flips, unfair eviction of mid-tier tenants, and inability to quickly admit warm KV-cache lanes after failover. Work items: - implement soft_fallback_bridge service behind /internal/fallback API - add tenant_grace_credit allocator (configurable per-tier) - introduce backpressure_token_pool with weighted fairness - replace binary circuit reopen with smoothed reopen_score over a 30s window - add telemetry: fallback_decision{tenant,region,reason}, grace_credit_usage, token_pool_utilization - add unit/integration tests and e2e canary config Checklist: - [x] design doc reviewed by runtime and product (ENG-2025) - [x] unit tests added - [x] integration tests on perf-canary - [x] telemetry wired into console dashboards - [x] canary baked and monitored for 48h - [x] hotfix patch included for nil-pointer cold path Migration and rollout: Default config off for stable release channel; enabled on dedicated canaries and a controlled percentage (5%) of hosted traffic via rollout flags. Ops knobs: per-tenant credit cap, token pool size, smoothing window length. Backwards compatibility: All API changes are internal; no public API breaking changes. Related: touches regional failover path and KV cache admission logic.
Diego Romero (reviewer): Overall approach LGTM. Two requests: make the grace credit uncapped only for enterprise tiers and add instrumentation for per-tenant denied-counts. Also please add a small backpressure unit-test that simulates multi-tenant contention.
Evelyn Zhang (author): Addressed: grace credit is capped via config and defaulted to 0 for free tier. Added denied_count metric and a new test backpressure/fairness_test.go that reproduces contention. See commit d4b68a1.
Priya Nair (reviewer): Concern about smoothing window hiding real regressions. Suggest exposing reopen_score percentile to console and alert on sustained low reopen_score. Also confirm that smoothing window doesn't delay detection beyond SLO window.
Evelyn Zhang (author): Exposed reopen_score p50/p95; added SLO-window gating so detection still respects tenant SLO windows. Updated dashboards and alerts.
Liam O'Connor (approver): Verified local and canary runs. Observed more even eviction and faster warm-KV readmits during a controlled spike. Approving pending CI.

payload.body:
Context
We’re standardizing timeout behavior across Python/TS/Go. The Go SDK currently mixes (a) http.Client.Timeout, (b) ad-hoc context.WithTimeout usage, and (c) streaming loops that can keep blocking reads even after ctx cancellation. The result is inconsistent behavior across request types and, in a few cases, goroutine leaks + hung streaming reads when callers cancel.

This PR aligns the Go SDK with the timeout ADR direction (overall + granular connect/read) and makes ctx cancellation reliably abort:
- non-streaming requests (request/response)
- streaming requests (SSE/event-stream) including when blocked in io.Read / bufio reads

What changed
1) New unified timeout configuration
- Introduce sdk.Timeouts:
  - Overall: total wall-clock time for the request (0 = no overall timeout)
  - Connect: max time to establish connection + receive response headers
  - Read: max idle time waiting for the next byte on the response body (0 = no read timeout)
- Client now accepts WithTimeouts(Timeouts) and applies defaults consistently.
- Deprecate the old client option Timeout (single duration) but keep it working (maps to Overall) with a deprecation notice in docs/comments.

2) Transport-level mapping (net/http)
- We no longer use http.Client.Timeout for streaming calls by default (it can terminate long-lived streams unexpectedly).
- For all requests:
  - Connect maps to Transport.ResponseHeaderTimeout (covers time-to-first-byte / headers)
  - Overall is enforced by context deadline on the request (ctx.WithTimeout)
- For non-streaming calls:
  - Read is enforced by our response body reader wrapper (idle timer) and by ensuring ctx cancellation closes the body.
- For streaming calls:
  - We enforce cancellation by closing the response body as soon as ctx.Done() fires; this unblocks the streaming read loop immediately.
  - Read timeout (idle) is opt-in; default is 0 for streaming to avoid surprising disconnects on slow token streams. (Docs updated with guidance.)

3) Context cancellation that actually interrupts streaming reads
- Streaming previously used a buffered reader loop that could remain blocked in Read even after ctx was cancelled.
- Now, when a stream is started, we wire a cancellation watcher:
  - go routine waits on ctx.Done() and calls resp.Body.Close()
  - stream loop exits with context.Canceled / context.DeadlineExceeded mapped to a typed SDK error
- Added safeguards to avoid goroutine leaks:
  - watcher exits when stream finishes normally
  - we use a done channel to signal termination

4) Tests
- Add regression tests for:
  - ctx cancellation interrupts an in-flight non-streaming request (server blocks)
  - ctx cancellation interrupts a streaming read (server writes headers then stalls)
  - Overall timeout triggers deadline exceeded for non-streaming
  - streaming does NOT apply Overall by default (unless explicitly configured)

5) Docs + migration notes (in-repo)
- Update README + godoc for ClientOptions / WithTimeouts.
- Add a short note in CHANGELOG.md about the new timeout semantics + deprecation of Timeout.

Defaults (proposed standard for Go SDK)
- Connect: 10s
- Overall (non-streaming): 120s
- Read (non-streaming): 60s idle
- Streaming:
  - Connect: 10s
  - Overall: 0 (no overall)
  - Read: 0 (no idle read timeout)

Why these defaults
- Avoid retry storms / cascading failures from overly aggressive timeouts, while still preventing hung non-streaming requests.
- Streaming is long-lived and should be caller-controlled via ctx and/or explicit timeouts.

Notes on backward compatibility
- This is a behavioral change for a subset of customers who previously relied on the legacy Timeout applying to streams. That behavior was inconsistent anyway (some streams ignored it, some were terminated by http.Client.Timeout). The new behavior is explicit: to limit stream duration, pass a context deadline or set Overall for streaming via WithTimeouts.

Checklist
- [x] Conforms to timeout ADR direction (overall + granular)
- [x] Cancellation consistently aborts streaming reads
- [x] Unit tests for cancellation and timeouts
- [x] Docs/godoc updated

Follow-ups
- Conformance suite fixture for streaming cancellation (shared across SDKs) will land in ENG-5127.
- After TS/Python land similar changes, we should align wording for streaming guidance across all docs.
Allison Grant (review): Can we avoid http.Client.Timeout entirely? It’s a footgun for streaming. Also please document the default differences between streaming vs non-streaming.

Mateusz Zielinski (author): Agreed. Removed http.Client.Timeout usage for streams and clarified defaults + guidance in README/godoc. For non-streaming we rely on ctx overall + idle read timeout wrapper (and Connect via ResponseHeaderTimeout).
Sean Gallagher (review): Concern: the ctx.Done() watcher goroutine could leak if the caller never drains/closes the stream iterator. How do we guarantee cleanup?

Mateusz Zielinski (author): Added done channel that is closed when stream loop exits; watcher selects on done OR ctx.Done(). Also ensured Close() on the stream iterator closes the body and signals done. Added a unit test that cancels early and checks stream goroutine count via leaktest helper.
Ibrahim Khan (review): Can we make the API shape match the parity doc? (Overall/Connect/Read). Also please ensure context.Canceled maps to a typed error with request_id (when present).

Mateusz Zielinski (author): Renamed fields to Overall/Connect/Read. Updated error wrapping: request_id is captured from response headers (when available) and included in TimeoutError/RequestCanceledError. Added tests for both code paths.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): Minor: ensure we don’t log the configured timeouts alongside auth headers in debug logs.

Mateusz Zielinski (author): Debug logging already redacts auth headers; this PR does not change logging behavior, but I added a test asserting Authorization is never printed in error strings. Timeouts are safe to log; auth remains redacted.
CI: go test ./... initially failed (data race in stream cancel test) -> fixed by serializing cancellation and waiting on done channel; rerun passed.

Final approvals: Allison Grant, Sean Gallagher, Ibrahim Khan.
Merged via squash.
payload.title: Align timeout model + ensure context cancellation aborts HTTP and streaming reads

Summary: Adds a compact credential hub plus stream decorator helpers to the Go SDK to unify auth retry behavior, provide per-stream retry presets, and improve ergonomics for long-lived streaming consumers. This PR converges parity with the TypeScript and Python SDKs' recent credential middleware work while remaining idiomatic for Go.

Motivation and context: Several customers and internal SDK teams requested a clearer path for multi-credential flows, prefetching, and per-stream retry tuning. Existing code duplicated token lookup logic across connectors and made stream cancellation/heartbeat coordination awkward. This change centralizes credential lookup/rotation into a small credential hub abstraction and adds lightweight stream decorators that wire retry, heartbeat, and graceful shutdown correctly.

What this changes: - Introduces credentials/hub.go (CredentialHub interface + concrete LRU-backed hub)
- Adds stream/decorators.go with Decorator chain primitives: WithRetryPreset, WithHeartbeat, WithCancelOnError
- Exposes a new ClientOption: WithCredentialHub(...) for DI
- Adds a RetryPreset type and a small registry; default presets match py/ts semantics (fast-retry, balanced, conservative)
- Tests: unit tests for hub eviction, token refresh race, decorator interaction; integration smoke that validates streaming reconnects under simulated token rotation
- Docs: sdk/go/README.md updated with migration guide and examples
- Version bumped to v1.8.0 with changelog entry

Checklist: - [x] CredentialHub abstraction implemented and tested
- [x] Stream decorators implemented and documented
- [x] Cross-SDK parity verified against TS/Py reference PRs
- [x] Benchmarked: ~0.8% median latency regression on cold-start removed; 3-5% throughput gain for hot reuse in curl-style workloads
- [x] Added release notes and migration guide

Migration notes: Consumers that previously provided custom token lookups to individual stream constructors should switch to creating a shared CredentialHub and pass it via WithCredentialHub. Backwards compatibility: Client constructors still accept the previous TokenProvider func; if both are present, the CredentialHub takes priority and falls back to provider for legacy paths.
Priya Nair: Nice consolidation. Can we avoid global state in the LRU cache? Suggest passing a context-based eviction hook.
Evan Matthews: Good call — switched the LRU to be attached to the hub instance and added an OnEvict callback that accepts context. Tests updated.
Miguel Santos: CI noticed a data race in TestStreamDecorator_Order when run with -race. Root cause was shared timer in tests; please isolate timers.
Evan Matthews: Fixed — tests now use fakeclock.New and are hermetic under -race.
Jordan Lee: Approve after nits: docs example shows WithCredentialHub before WithRetryPreset; prefer a paragraph explaining ordering semantics.
Go SDK v1.8.0: Introduces CredentialHub for centralized token rotation + stream decorators for per-stream retry/heartbeat behavior. API ergonomic improvements (WithCredentialHub, RetryPreset registry). Backwards compatible; see migration guide in sdk/go/README.md.
Example: hub := credentials.NewHub(credentials.WithCapacity(64), credentials.WithPrefetch(true)); client := redwood.NewClient(redwood.WithCredentialHub(hub)) — then use stream := client.Stream(ctx, opts...)

Motivation: long-tail token cost and tail latency often correlate with particular callsites in user code (prompt patterns, tool calls). Current sampling is either coarse (per-invocation) or heavy (full-trace capture) which increases cost and makes dashboarding noisy. This PR introduces a lightweight callsite-aware sampling layer that attaches compact 'trace profile' anchors to representative invocations and a new cost-decomposition dashboard widget that surfaces per-callsite token/latency contribution across recent windows.

What this implements: 1) backend sampling engine (observability/sampling/callsite_sampler.go) that computes and persists small trace anchors (callsite signature, token count, phase timings) using reservoir sampling per-route and per-tenant. Sampling heuristics balance token-cost-weighted and entropy-guided selection so we capture both high-cost and high-variance callsites. 2) compact RPC and storage schema (telemetry/schema/callsite_profile_v1.yaml) and migration logic to retain backwards compatibility with existing invocation rollups. 3) frontend dashboard widget (ui/dashboard/widgets/cost_decomp_widget.tsx) that queries aggregated callsite profiles and renders an interactive stacked decomposition by token-phase (encode/attend/decode) and latency phase, with drilldowns into representative trace anchors. 4) alert tuning helpers: a new metric (observability/metrics/callsite_suspect_count) and an alert rule template (alerts/observability/callsite_alert_templates.yaml) that can be used to attach callsite-level suppression windows and quieting. 5) docs and runbook (docs/observability/callsite_profiles.md) describing how to interpret the widget and how to onboard routes to higher-fidelity sampling.

Backward compatibility and migration: the schema and query layer fall back to the existing invocation rollups when callsite profiles are not available. We added a short migration tool that backfills top-K callsite anchors from recent heavy invocations (runs as a low-priority job) — it is opt-in via an admin flag.

Tests and validation: unit tests for sampler selection logic and reservoir correctness; end-to-end integration test that simulates synthetic traffic shapes and validates widget aggregation. Performance: sampling layer adds ~0.7% CPU overhead at 95th percentile on our perf-canary (measured on p3-type nodes) and reduces full-trace capture volume by ~63% for large tenants in the replay bench. Dashboard query latency (90th) for the new widget is ~120ms for a 30m window after adding targeted indexes.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind 'callsite_profiles' per-tenant flag. Start with opt-in on redwood internal tenant and two beta customers for 2 weeks, then expand to early-access customers with communication and dashboard training.

Risks & mitigation: potential increase in cardinality due to callsite signature explosion — mitigated by shingle-based normalization and a top-K eviction policy per-route. Storage overhead is controlled by compact anchor format and TTL. Alerts can be noisy initially; included templates add auto-quiet windows and decay to avoid alert storms.

See related Linear tickets: ENG-1429 (callsite sampling design), ENG-1452 (dashboard widget), and support ticket SUP-8212 for early customer request.
Daniel Kim: Requested adding a unit test covering deterministic eviction when reservoir is full — added tests in tests/unit/callsite_sampler_test.go and addressed flakiness by switching RNG seed approach.
Priya Nair: Asked for clarification on schema TTLs and index choices; clarified in telemetry/schema/callsite_profile_v1.yaml and added comments to the migration; approved after verifying query latency on canary.
Liam O'Connor: Noted potential double-counting in per-route aggregations — fixed aggregator query and added guard in callsite_aggregator.sql; ran e2e to validate.
SRE oncall (in thread): Observed an initial spike in write QPS on the telemetry cluster during canary; we throttled backfill and added batching to serializer (compact_anchor_serializer.go) to smooth load.
4 commits:

- 6b2f4d0 Add callsite profile schema and migration/backfill job
- a3e8b56 Add frontend cost decomposition widget and client query helpers
- 1f4b2e9 Add alert templates, docs, and e2e test for sampled profiles
Introduced callsite sampling and a new cost decomposition dashboard widget. Feature is behind tenant flag 'callsite_profiles'. See docs/observability/callsite_profiles.md for onboarding steps and runbook.

Context & motivation: Our polyglot SDKs have drift in how they interpret server session TTLs and surface lease windows to callers. That leads to subtle token rotation races and duplicated retry logic in higher-level apps. This PR harmonizes the Go SDK behavior with the Python/TypeScript SDKs (lease-window semantics), introduces a small, ergonomically-friendly StreamAdapter for pull/push streaming patterns, and bumps the Go SDK minor version.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Introduce pkg/session/ttl.go which provides a SessionLease wrapper that converts server TTL (expires_at) into a client lease window and exposes deterministic RefreshNeeded() semantics; add stream/adapter.go implementing lightweight PullStream and PushStream facades with a small BufferHint API to let callers opt into zero-copy/pass-through for low-latency flows; centralize retry presets in internal/retry/presets.go to match the default profiles used in py/ts SDKs (fast-warmup, conservative, realtime); add integration tests tests/integration/session_ttl_test.go and tests/stream/adapter_e2e_test.go; update examples/streaming/credential-ttl.md with a migration note; bump go.mod to v1.6.0 and update CHANGELOG.md. The description below summarizes commits, changed files, review discussion, CI checks and merge details.

Commits (high-level): - 7c1f9a2: initial session-lease implementation and unit tests; - 2e4bff1: add StreamAdapter facades and BufferHint; - 9a712d4: centralize retry presets and wire into client.New(); - 4b8a0d6: docs and examples for streaming TTL usage; - 82d3ab7: fix linting and adjust naming per review; - d1f5a33: test flake fixes and CI config tweaks.

Files changed (high level): - pkg/session/ttl.go (new) - stream/adapter.go (new) - internal/retry/presets.go (modified) - client/client.go (wired TTL + retry presets) - tests/integration/session_ttl_test.go (new) - tests/stream/adapter_e2e_test.go (new) - examples/streaming/credential-ttl.md (doc) - go.mod, go.sum, CHANGELOG.md (version bump / release notes)

Testing & CI: CI initially failed on golangci-lint (unused var and naming complaints) and a flaky adapter e2e that relies on a mocked backend timing. I pushed two follow-ups: rename utils and add a small sleep+retry in the e2e harness. Final CI matrix: unit-tests (pass), integration-tests (pass), linters (pass), race (pass), e2e (pass). Test coverage: added focused unit tests for TTL math and adapter buffer boundary behavior.

Review conversation (summary): - Arjun Patel (review): "Nice consolidation. One concern: RefreshNeeded() vs LeaseRefreshDue() naming — prefer something that reads as a clock/threshold. Also can we avoid exposing time.Time in the public helper?" - Author (Maya): "Addressed: renamed to LeaseRefreshDue() and switched public API to return window.Duration rather than raw time.Time; added docstring and example in examples/streaming/credential-ttl.md." - Evelyn Ross (review): "StreamAdapter is ergonomic but I worry about the BufferHint on default behavior; can we make zero-copy opt-in?" - Author (Maya): "Made BufferHint opt-in (default is safe copy). Updated README and added test for zero-copy path." - Diego Marquez (review): "CI flaked on e2e; tests look stable now. Approving pending small linter fixes." - Arjun Patel: "Approved".

Requested changes & fixes made: - Renamed API per reviewer feedback; - made zero-copy opt-in and documented tradeoffs; - folded retry presets into central internal/retry to avoid duplicating constants; - resolved golangci-lint warnings and tightened variable names; - added explicit integration test to capture token-rotation race scenario.

Compatibility & migration notes: Consumers relying on the old Session TTL helpers should migrate to the new SessionLease.{LeaseRefreshDue,RefreshNeededGrace} helpers; the migration is a small surface area change (rename + type change from time.Time to time.Duration for the refresh indicator). Examples and changelog were updated to walk through the migration. No breaking runtime behavior expected when consumers switch to new helpers; default semantics remain backward-compatible for typical usage.

Version & merge: This PR bumps the Go SDK to v1.6.0 in go.mod and CHANGELOG. After reviews and CI green, PR was merged via squash/merge on 2026-02-24.

Rollout and follow-ups: - Monitor sessions and token-rotation pager (SUP-3192) for 48h after release; - plan companion small patches in py/ts SDK repos to align naming (ENG-8479 already tracks parity housekeeping); - follow-up perf microbenchmark to ensure adapter adds negligible latency for the default (safe-copy) path.

TL;DR: Harmonizes session TTL semantics across SDKs, adds a small ergonomic StreamAdapter in Go, consolidates retry presets, bumps version to v1.6.0, and includes tests/docs to smooth migration.
Go SDK v1.6.0: harmonized session TTL handling with Py/TS, added lightweight streaming adapter facades, improved retry presets, and multiple test/regression fixes.

Motivation: Long-running investigations frequently require iterating through hundreds of large spans and full invocation traces. This PR introduces an invocation snapshot compactifier, a span paginator API for the Observability UI, and an "alert sedimentation" mechanism that reduces alert noise by consolidating repeated token-cost/latency signals into a single actionable event. The goal is to reduce UI load, lower storage amplification for sampled traces, and make alerting more interpretable for SREs and product owners.

Summary of changes (high-level):
- Add a compact indexer service (telemetry/snapshot-compactifier) that consumes sampled invocation payloads, extracts a compact keyset (heatmap anchors, token-count signature, route fingerprint), and writes small snapshot blobs to the indexed store. The compact blobs are ~80-150 bytes per invocation vs 5-20 KB previously for sampled traces.
- Implement a span paginator endpoint (observability/api/paginator) that returns ordered span slices for a given invocation snapshot id. The paginator supports cursor-based forward/backward paging and a streaming mode for UI progressive rendering.
- Add "alert sedimentation" (observability/alerts/sediment) policy that groups successive token-cost or latency alerts from the same route+fingerprint into one escalated alert with a summarized runbook link. Sedimentation windows are configurable per-team.
- UI: dashboard tweaks to invocation list and a new compact snapshot preview card (webapp/dashboards/CompactSnapshotCard.tsx) that renders metadata and a short timeline without pulling full spans. Pager integrated into the invocation detail view.
- Migration: a background job to bootstrap compact index entries from last 7 days of sampled traces.
- Tests: unit tests for indexer logic, integration tests for paginator cursor behavior, e2e preview smoke tests for the CompactSnapshotCard.

Commits:
- 3f8b2c9: initial compactifier service scaffolding and proto for compact snapshot blobs
- a7d9f11: add paginator API and cursor implementation; add integration tests
- b5e6a2d: alert sedimentation policy, UI preview card, alerting docs and migration job

Files changed (representative list, not exhaustive):
- telemetry/snapshot-compactifier/README.md
- telemetry/snapshot-compactifier/indexer.go
- telemetry/snapshot-compactifier/proto/compact_snapshot.proto
- observability/api/paginator/handler.go
- observability/alerts/sediment/policy.go
- webapp/dashboards/CompactSnapshotCard.tsx
- webapp/routes/invocationDetail.tsx (paginator integration)
- terraform/observability-alerting.tf (new sedmentation config variables)
- tests/integration/paginator_test.go
- scripts/migrations/bootstrap_compact_index.sh

Behavioral notes and constraints:
- The indexer runs in best-effort mode; snapshots are additive. We do not delete original spans or sampled traces as part of this PR. The compact blobs are intended to be a low-cost, quick-preview path for most investigations.
- Paginator returns stable cursors tied to compact snapshot generation timestamp; cursors expire after 48 hours. This avoids unbounded retention on paginated cursors and simplifies garbage collection.
- Alert sedimentation uses a sliding decay: repeated alerts within window are collapsed; after stable recurrence above escalation threshold we produce a single parent alert with a summarized evidence payload (compact snapshot reference).

Testing and rollout strategy:
- Canary: roll indexer to observability-canary with a 1% sample of sampled traces for 48h. Monitor compact index hit-rate and UI render latencies.
- If compact index write error rates exceed 0.5% in canary, automatically scale back to 0% via feature flag.
- Gradual rollout to prod over 2 weeks with telemetry on: compact_index_write_success, paginator_latency_p95, alert_sedimentation_rate.

Impact on cost: Compact snapshots reduce per-invocation storage for sampled traces by ~95% in the traced sample pipeline; initial estimates show 12-18% reduction in observability storage TCO for teams with high sampling. There is minor added CPU for the indexer (profiled on n2-standard equivalent, ~5% CPU on canary).

Backward compatibility: Paginator API is additive. Existing trace consumers and alerting rules continue to function unchanged unless teams opt into sedimentation. Feature flag "obs.compact_snapshot_v1" gated.

CI summary: initial CI run failed lint on webapp formatting and a race in paginator_test. Fixes included in second commit. Final CI: build/pass, unit/pass, integration/pass, e2e/pass. See CI details below.

Review conversation (abbreviated, single continuous narrative):
- Arjun Rao (reviewer): "High-level this looks great; can you justify the 48h cursor TTL? Is that long enough for cross-team handoffs?"
- Maya Patel (author): "We picked 48h to limit GC complexity and disk pointers; teams needing longer handoffs can pin the invocation or export full trace. We can extend TTL per-team if necessary — added a config flag in terraform."
- Lena Thomason (reviewer): "alert sedimentation is promising but risk of masking flakey incidents. How do we ensure we don't hide a real regression?"
- Maya Patel: "Sedimentation keeps an evidence link and increments an internal recurrence counter. If recurrence crosses escalation thresholds we escalate with a richer payload. Also added an operator opt-out label to disable sedimentation for critical routes."
- QA (reviewer): "paginator test flake reproduced locally; suggest deterministic clock usage in cursor encoding."
- Maya Patel: "Addressed: cursor encodes a trimmed timestamp and monotonic sequence; used test clock in tests. Re-ran CI and integration tests now stable."
- SRE (approver): "Approving for canary. Please add a runbook snippet for what to do when compact index lag > 5 minutes."
- Maya Patel: "Added runbook snippet into telemetry/snapshot-compactifier/README.md and linked from observability runbooks."

CI details (single line summary): "CI: build/pass; lint/pass; unit/pass; integration/pass (one rerun due to paginator_test flake); e2e/pass; security-scan/pass; deploy/canary/pass"

Merge outcome: Merged via squash-and-merge after approvals from SRE and two reviewers. Release notes entry added.

Release notes: "Add compact invocation snapshot indexer, UI preview card, paginator API, and alert sedimentation policy — reduces observability storage for sampled traces and improves investigation latency. Feature gated and rolled out to canary."

Related Linear items and tickets: "ENG-1498, ENG-2301"

Notes for oncall and pager teams: "If you see sudden drop in sampled-trace render rate or compact_index_write_failures > 0.5% for 30m, run the diagnostic in README and disable obs.compact_snapshot_v1 via the feature flag. For sedimentation mis-grouping, use team label 'sediment:disabled' on route config to bypass."

Context: Several customers observed credential stampedes and inefficient reauth churn for long-lived streaming sessions. Motivation: provide a Go-native facility that coordinates credential refreshes across concurrent stream handles, prefetches rotation windows, and exposes simple presets so application teams can get safe defaults without custom retry wiring. This PR implements two related pieces: 1) Session Scheduler: a light-weight scheduler that groups imminent token refreshes (TTL windows) and serializes refreshes to a single upstream token provider when safe, with configurable jitter and fanout limits to avoid leader election overhead; 2) Token Curator: a prefetching/validation layer that tracks upcoming rotation windows and primes a hot-swappable cached token to reduce first-byte latency on reauth. Design notes: - Scheduler binds to the SDK's SessionFactory and can be enabled per-client or globally via SessionSchedulerOptions. - Token Curator exposes a minimal interface (Curator.Start, Curator.Stop, Curator.Get) and hooks into the existing CredentialProvider interface for seamless compatibility. - Provides a new RetryPreset: "session-friendly" that adjusts hedged retry bounds for long-lived streams and prefers graceful backoff on auth-failures. - Backwards compatible: default behavior is disabled; existing consumers continue to use the prior credential cache. Checklist: - [x] Implement scheduler and curator in go/sdk/cred - [x] Add unit + integration tests that simulate concurrent stream churn - [x] Add e2e perf harness measuring reauth QPS and tail latency - [x] Add docs and examples demonstrating enabling via client opts - [x] Version bump to v1.9.0 Implementation summary and notes: The scheduler uses a small, sharded token map keyed by session id and TTL bucket. It performs coordinated refresh by electing a local refresh leader per bucket using an atomic compare-and-swap and falling back to queued refresh so only one outbound token call is made per bucket in the rotation window. The Token Curator keeps a ring of prefetched tokens per identity and validates tokens asynchronously; stale tokens are evicted promptly. Observability: added span annotations and metrics: cred.curator.prefetches, cred.scheduler.leaders, cred.refresh.latency, and a lightweight gauge for cached token age. Compatibility: The PR keeps the public CredentialProvider surface unchanged; new constructs are optional and documented. Migration: recommend enabling the session-friendly preset for services with >100 concurrent streams to reduce auth QPS. Performance: in the perf harness we observed ~3.8x reduction in outbound token calls under a simulated 1k-conn churn pattern and 14% P99 tail latency improvement for stream connect times after enabling curator+scheduler.
Add Session Scheduler and Token Curator to Go SDK; exposes lightweight ergonomic APIs for coordinated token warmup and retry presets; bump go SDK to v1.9.0. No user-facing breaking changes.
Liam O'Connor: Nice design — can we avoid a global lock for leader election? Suggest sharded CAS per TTL bucket (resolved in implementation).
Asha Menon: switched to sharded CAS based on TTL bucketing; added comments and microbenchmarks (see commit).
Marta Ruiz: Add a safety TTL guard to ensure we never serve expired token from curator (requested extra test).
Asha Menon: added validation test and a fallback path that forces synchronous refresh when token age ambiguous.
Sanjay Patel: Request to expose metric tags for tenant_id and region for aggregator dashboards; also confirm low-cardinality for default metrics.
Asha Menon: added tenant_id as optional tag and documented cardinality guidance in metrics.md.
QA (automated): Flaky test noticed on first CI run (TestCuratorEviction) — reran, passed after increasing eviction tolerance to 50ms in test harness.
payload.title: Introduce Session Scheduler and Token Curator for Go SDK (parity + ergonomic retry presets)

Context: Go SDK stream ergonomics have diverged on fallback behavior and retry surface between platforms, causing product teams to implement fragile ad-hoc logic. This PR introduces a compact fallback connector that centralizes credential fallback, a pluggable retry profile system tuned for streaming vs RPC use-cases, and a small ergonomic API surface to make stream consumers simpler to adopt. Changes include: 1) CompactStreamConnector: a thin adapter that unifies token-warmup, heartbeat, and transparent credential failover with a single constructor and minimal caller lifecycle. 2) Retry profiles: streaming and rpc profiles (fast-bail, steady-window, and conservative) implemented as strategy objects and registered via WithRetryProfile(...). 3) Consumer ergonomics: StreamHandle iterators now expose ResumeAfter(token) and WithContext(ctx) helpers to reduce boilerplate. 4) Backwards compatible fallbacks: default behavior preserved (no breaking change) but advanced behaviors opt-in via new options. 5) Tests & docs: added integration and unit tests exercising credential swap while streaming and updated SDK README+migration notes. Motivation: reduce duplicated token/fallback logic customers are implementing, improve parity with TS/Python ergonomics, and provide safer default retry suitable for long-lived chunked streams. Migration notes: existing users can continue with current constructors; to opt in call NewCompactStream(conn, WithRetryProfile("streaming")) and use StreamHandle.ResumeAfter to resume partial reads. Performance: bench shows ~3% CPU reduction on steady-state streaming due to lightweight connector path; memory impact negligible. Rollout plan: gated behind feature flag in production; rollout to canaries for 48h, then full. See release_notes for actionable items.
Elena Park: Can we ensure the default profile keeps current semantics? Suggest adding an explicit test for zero-downtime token swap.
Ravi Menon: Added integration test 'TestTokenSwapDuringStream' that simulates rotating credentials and asserts seamless continuation; kept default profile identical to previous behavior.
Samir Gupta: The WithRetryProfile API is sensible, but prefer naming 'RegisterRetryProfile' for discoverability. Small nit: comment on profiles.go about window sizing.
Ravi Menon: Kept API as WithRetryProfile to follow existing option-builder conventions used across SDK. Expanded comment and added a TODO to evaluate renaming in next minor release.
Marta Novak: Bench numbers look good. Please add a brief note in release notes about expected CPU regression when using conservative profile.
Ravi Menon: Added release note entry and clarified the cost/latency tradeoffs in docs.
AutoCI: integration suite initially failed (timeout on TestRetryBackoff) — re-run fixed it; added a 2s buffer to the test harness to reduce flakiness.
- Go SDK v0.34.0: Add CompactStreamConnector for unified token fallback and heartbeat handling. - Introduce pluggable retry profiles: 'streaming', 'rpc-fast', 'conservative' (opt-in). - StreamHandle helpers: ResumeAfter(token) and WithContext(ctx) for ergonomic consumption. - No breaking changes: defaults preserved. - Performance: ~3% CPU improvement in steady streaming when using CompactStreamConnector. - Migration: existing constructors still work; opt-in with WithRetryProfile("streaming").

payload.body:
Title: Align auth env vars + Authorization header formatting; redact secrets in debug logs

Context
This is part of the cross-language SDK parity initiative. Go was slightly out of sync with Python/TS on:
- which environment variables are recognized
- precedence rules when multiple auth sources are provided
- header formatting (API key vs bearer token)
- debug logging: some code paths could print full Authorization or X-API-Key values when RW_DEBUG=true

This PR aligns Go with the standard (Security-reviewed) behavior so customers don’t see "works in TS but not in Go" auth issues and so we avoid accidental secret exposure in logs.

What changed (behavior)
1) Auth resolution order (standardized)
- Explicit option on client always wins: redwood.WithAPIKey(...) / redwood.WithBearerToken(...)
- Otherwise resolve from environment variables in this order:
  a) REDWOOD_API_KEY
  b) REDWOOD_BEARER_TOKEN
- If both env vars are set, prefer REDWOOD_BEARER_TOKEN (matches Python/TS and our guidance for fine-grained tokens).
- Backwards-compat: still recognizes legacy env vars for one release window:
  - LEGACY: REDWOOD_APIKEY, REDWOOD_TOKEN
  - If a legacy var is used, we emit a debug-level log message indicating the preferred name (without printing the secret).

2) Header formatting
- API key auth now sets: X-API-Key: <value>
- Bearer token auth now sets: Authorization: Bearer <value>
- Ensures we never send both headers; if both are configured via options (misconfiguration), we return an error at client init: ErrAmbiguousAuth

3) Secret redaction in logs
- Introduced a small header redaction helper used by debug logging and HTTP tracing hooks.
- Any header key matching (case-insensitive): authorization, x-api-key, cookie is redacted.
- Debug logs now show a safe shape: e.g. Authorization: [REDACTED], X-API-Key: [REDACTED]
- Also redacts query params for common keys (api_key, token) if present in URLs that are logged.

4) Typed errors
- When auth is missing, errors are now consistent and do not include hints that echo env values. Error message is intentionally generic:
  "missing credentials: set REDWOOD_API_KEY or REDWOOD_BEARER_TOKEN, or pass WithAPIKey/WithBearerToken"
- Errors include request_id when available (ties to INT-1182; request_id propagation is handled in other PRs, but this PR avoids dropping it in auth failures).

Files / areas changed
- internal/auth/resolve.go: env var normalization + precedence
- client/options.go: validation to prevent ambiguous auth
- transport/headers.go: centralized header construction
- internal/logging/redact.go: header + url redaction helpers
- transport/debug_roundtripper.go: safe header logging
- tests/auth_resolution_test.go: precedence + legacy fallback
- tests/log_redaction_test.go: ensures we never print secrets under RW_DEBUG

Commits
- sdk-go: resolve auth from standardized env vars + legacy fallback
- sdk-go: centralize header formatting for api key vs bearer token
- sdk-go: redact Authorization/X-API-Key in debug logs and tracing
- sdk-go: add tests for auth precedence + safe logging

Verification
- Unit tests cover:
  - explicit option overrides env
  - env precedence when both new vars exist
  - legacy env vars still work
  - debug logging never contains raw token/key
- Manual:
  - ran examples/chat with REDWOOD_BEARER_TOKEN
  - confirmed Authorization header is "Bearer ..." (not "Token" / missing space)

Related
- Python: pr-842-align-auth-env-vars-and-precedence
- TypeScript: pr-1316-sdk-auth-env-vars-alignment
- Security guidance: SDK auth resolution and secret handling (Confluence)

Risk / rollout notes
- Not intended as a breaking change; legacy env vars remain supported.
- The only stricter behavior is when both API key and bearer token are provided explicitly; we now fail fast with ErrAmbiguousAuth rather than sending inconsistent headers.

Review conversation
Kaitlyn Nguyen (platform/auth) - Requested changes:
"Can we match the exact env var names from the security guidance (REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_BEARER_TOKEN) and keep legacy aliases separate so we can deprecate cleanly? Also please confirm header name for API key should be X-API-Key (not Authorization)."

Mateusz Zielinski (author):
"Yep. Updated to treat new vars as canonical, legacy vars as aliases only if canonical absent. API key header now consistently uses X-API-Key. Added tests for the alias behavior." 

Marcus Lin (security) - Requested changes:
"The debug roundtripper currently logs headers after request construction; ensure Authorization and X-API-Key are always redacted, and that we don’t log env var values in errors. Also please redact common token query params if URL logging is enabled." 

Mateusz Zielinski:
"Added internal/logging/redact.go and applied to both headers and URL logging. Updated error strings to avoid echoing values. Added log_redaction_test to assert secrets never appear." 

Allison Grant (SRE/observability):
"Can we include a stable field for which auth source was used (explicit vs env) without leaking which env var was set? Useful for support." 

Mateusz Zielinski:
"Added debug-only log: auth_source=explicit|env|legacy_env (no var name, no value)." 

Ibrahim Khan (SDK parity TL) - Comment:
"Please ensure this matches the parity matrix: explicit > env; bearer token preferred if both present; no retries on auth failure." 

Mateusz Zielinski:
"Aligned + added unit tests. No retry changes in this PR." 

Approvals
- Kaitlyn Nguyen: Approved
- Marcus Lin: Approved
- Ibrahim Khan: Approved

CI
- go test ./...: PASS
- golangci-lint: PASS
- examples build: PASS

Merge
- Merged via squash into main.
- Go SDK auth now resolves credentials using the standardized env var names and precedence. Authorization headers are formatted consistently; debug logging redacts secrets by default.
payload.title: Align auth env vars + Authorization header formatting; redact secrets in debug logs

payload.body:
## Summary
This PR implements the SDK parity retry standard for the Go SDK: retryable status codes + network errors, exponential backoff with jitter, and Retry-After parsing/precedence. It also adds a public configuration surface so users can tune or disable retries consistently across languages.

Motivation:
- Fixes customer-reported behavior where the Go SDK ignored Retry-After and retried too aggressively during rate limiting (SUP-29477).
- Aligns with the cross-language standard for predictable behavior and easier support/debugging.

## What changed
### Defaults (v1)
- **Retryable HTTP status codes:** 408, 409, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504
- **Retryable network errors:** connection reset, EOF mid-response before headers, temporary errors, and timeouts from the underlying net/http stack
- **Not retried:** context cancellation/deadline exceeded initiated by the caller, and any 4xx other than 408/409/429
- **Max attempts:** 4 total (1 initial + up to 3 retries)
- **Backoff:** exponential (base 250ms) capped to 8s, with full jitter
- **Retry-After:** respected when present on 429 (and generally for 503 when present), parsed from either delta-seconds or HTTP-date; capped by MaxBackoff; takes precedence over computed backoff

### Public API
New options on client construction:
- `RetryOptions{ MaxAttempts, InitialBackoff, MaxBackoff, Jitter, RetryableStatusCodes, RespectRetryAfter, OnRetry }`
- `WithRetryOptions(RetryOptions)`
- `DisableRetries()` convenience

`OnRetry` is a hook invoked for observability/debugging (no secrets): attempt number, wait duration, status code (if any), and Redwood request id (if available).

### Implementation details
- Centralized retry policy in `internal/retry/policy.go` and wired through the default HTTP transport wrapper.
- Retry classifier uses:
  - HTTP status code classification
  - net.Error temporary/timeout checks
  - explicit exclusions for `context.Canceled` / `context.DeadlineExceeded` caused by caller context
- Retry delay selection:
  1) Retry-After (if enabled and parseable)
  2) computed exponential backoff with jitter

### Streaming behavior
Streaming requests are **not automatically retried**. This matches the standard and avoids duplicate side effects / duplicated output. The SDK surfaces a typed error with the last known `request_id` (when available) and guidance to retry only when the user can safely do so with idempotency.

## Tests
- Unit tests for retry classifier: status codes, context cancellation, common net/http error types.
- Unit tests for Retry-After parsing (seconds + date) including max-backoff capping.
- Integration-style tests using `httptest.Server` to simulate:
  - 429 with Retry-After and verifying sleep duration is derived from header
  - 503 bursts and verifying attempts count and jittered wait range
  - network failure on first attempt then success

## Files / areas touched
- `client/client.go`: plumb retry options into HTTP client creation
- `client/options.go`: new `RetryOptions` and `WithRetryOptions`
- `internal/retry/*`: retry policy + backoff/jitter helpers + Retry-After parser
- `internal/transport/retry_round_tripper.go`: transport wrapper implementing retry loop
- `internal/errors/*`: propagate request_id into retry errors (ties to INT-1182)
- `docs/retries.md`: updated to match parity language and defaults

## Backwards compatibility
This is a behavioral change (retries will now happen in more cases, and will slow down appropriately under Retry-After). To minimize surprises:
- Defaults remain conservative (4 total attempts, capped backoff).
- Users can disable or tune retries via `DisableRetries()` / `WithRetryOptions`.

## Follow-ups
- Conformance suite wiring to shared fixtures (tracked in ENG-5127).
- Ensure gateway always emits Retry-After on 429 (platform work; tracked separately).

---

## Review conversation (highlights)
**Allison Grant:** Can we confirm we don’t retry when the caller’s context is canceled? This was a common source of “SDK ignored cancellation” complaints.

**Mateusz Zielinski (author):** Yes. The classifier checks `errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)` / `context.DeadlineExceeded` and treats those as terminal. Added a unit test covering both cases.

**Sean Gallagher:** Please cap Retry-After to MaxBackoff to avoid long sleeps on misconfigured proxies.

**Mateusz Zielinski (author):** Done. `retryAfterDelay()` now clamps to `MaxBackoff` and logs (via `OnRetry`) that clamp occurred.

**Ibrahim Khan:** Default attempt count should match the standard (4 total). Also ensure Retry-After takes precedence over computed backoff.

**Mateusz Zielinski (author):** Updated defaults to 4 total attempts and reordered delay selection to prefer Retry-After.

**Kaitlyn Nguyen:** Ensure `OnRetry` never includes the API key in errors/logs. Also no request/response bodies.

**Mateusz Zielinski (author):** Confirmed. Hook receives only attempt/wait/status/request_id + error type.

Approvals:
- Allison Grant ✅
- Sean Gallagher ✅
- Ibrahim Khan ✅
- Kaitlyn Nguyen ✅

## CI
- go test ./...: pass
- golangci-lint: pass
- docs build: pass

## Merge
Merged via squash into `main` on 2026-01-28.
Go SDK now uses standardized retries: retries on 429/5xx + network errors with exponential backoff + jitter; respects Retry-After; exposes RetryOptions to configure/disable retries. Streaming requests are not automatically retried.
payload.title: sdk(go): standardize retry policy (429/5xx/network), Retry-After, jittered backoff + options

payload.body:
Motivation: Several production incidents showed that under bursty clients + aggressive backpressure, SSE fragments could be emitted in very small chunks that broke partial JSON spans and interleaved function/tool call sentinels. This caused: 1) downstream JSON parse errors, 2) tool/function-call sentinel reordering, and 3) opaque partial outputs that the OpenAI-compat layer could not reconcile.

This PR introduces a lightweight cork/uncork headroom replay mechanism and canonical delimiter/escape sequencing to make SSE chunking resilient without increasing latency for normal traffic. Key ideas: cork headroom buffers small low-entropy fragments for up to N ms (configurable) and attempts an ordered replay when the next chunk arrives; span anchors (span_id + seq) are stamped on outbound SSE events to allow deterministic reassembly; delimiter and escape tokens are normalized at the framing layer ("data: " prefix handling and trailing newline normalization) so we avoid split-escape sequences (e.g., a backslash split across frames). We avoid full message coalescing to retain streaming semantics — corking is optimistically short and abandons replay if headroom exceeds threshold.

Compatibility: The OpenAI-compat shim maps the old "tool_call" sentinel to the canonical "function_call" tag and honors span anchors when reassembling. Integration tests emulate TCP split and delayed segments to verify reassembly and correct function/toolcall ordering.

What changed (high level): commit list below. Tests added: unit tests for escape normalization, e2e for bursty-client reassembly, and fuzz harness for random delimiter splits. Metrics: added sse.reassembly.attempts and sse.reassembly.success_rate; added logging note when cork is abandoned.

Risk and rollout: This touches the streaming framing layer and the OpenAI compat adapter. Feature guarded behind feature flag "sse_cork_headroom_v1"; rollout to canary, then full main. No customer-facing API changes.

Developer notes: headroom defaults to 8ms and max replay size 4KB. Operators can tune via runtime config. The approach minimizes cost and latency impact while removing a class of partial-JSON and sentinel-order bugs.
feat(sse): introduce cork headroom buffer and replay path
fix(sse): canonicalize delimiter/escape sequencing in framing layer
chore(openai-compat): map tool_call->function_call and respect span anchors
test(sse): add e2e bursty-client reassembly test
perf: micro-optimizations to avoid extra copies during replay
docs: document sse_cork_headroom_v1 flag and tuning knobs
Ethan Park: Can you explain how corking interacts with existing prefix KV cache? Concern about duplicate-capture of partial KV cache entries.
Priya Shah: Cork only operates at framing layer; it does not retain semantic KV cache entries. We added a separation boundary (framer -> runtime API) and unit tests that assert no duplicate cache insertions.
Marta López: Lint flagged a formatting nit in compat_adapter.go; please run gofmt (fixed in second commit).
Samir Ahmed: e2e failed on first run due to timing flakiness; added retry and tuned default headroom to 8ms (was 12ms). Verified green on rerun and approved.
- Fixes partial-JSON parse failures caused by micro-fragmented SSE chunks under bursty backpressure.
- Stabilizes function/tool-call sentinel ordering across split frames.
- Adds feature flag sse_cork_headroom_v1 and new metrics: sse.reassembly.attempts and sse.reassembly.success_rate.
