Motivation: Our existing CI eval gates are brittle when individual metrics jitter independently (semantic similarity, token-overlap, calibration). This PR introduces a robustness signal fusion layer that combines orthogonal eval metrics into a single, tunable gate signal and integrates it into the CI pipeline. The fused signal reduces false positives from single-metric noise and enables per-prompt-set sensitivity controls. What this PR implements: 1) robustness/signal_fusion module: implements a configurable aggregator that ingests multiple metric streams (semantic-similarity, length-stability, calibration-gap, perplexity-delta, token-overlap) and outputs a composite z-scored signal with tunable weights and smoothing window. 2) ci/gates/robustness_gate: a CI hook that evaluates the composite signal against cohort-level thresholds and emits a deterministic pass/fail with diagnostic score breakdown. 3) backfill runner: ability to backfill historical eval results and recompute fused signals (used for threshold calibration and retrospective triage). 4) adapters: shims to convert existing eval outputs into the fusion input format (JSON lines schema) so this gate can be dropped into current pipelines with minimal changes. 5) dashboard metadata and trace tags for per-prompt-set explanations and top-contributing metrics. Checklist: - [x] core aggregation algorithm and unit tests - [x] CI hook and integration tests - [x] backfill runner and sample backfill job - [x] docs (README + gating configuration examples) - [x] metrics/tracing tags added - [x] reviewer feedback addressed Breaking notes: non-breaking for consumers that don't enable the gate; opt-in via repo ci config. Rollout plan: land on main behind a feature flag, run backfill on the last 90 days, propose thresholds based on 95% historical percentile, then flip gate to warn-only for 2 weeks before hard-failing PRs. Related: builds on prior eval work around cohort sampling and stability anchors (references: ENG-2742, DEV:cohort-prioritizer).

Motivation: Large prompt-set backfills are expensive and risk noisy regressions when ground-truth labels are sparse. This PR adds a pseudo-ground-truth (pseudo-GT) fusion step that combines a small curated human label set with high-confidence model-derived annotations to create a richer reference for regression checks. It also introduces a staged backfill executor that runs in prioritized waves and a CI soft-fail policy so teams can detect degradations early without hard-blocking merges. Key design points: 1) Pseudo-GT fusion algorithm that weights human labels and model annotations by calibrated confidence; 2) Staged backfill orchestration with configurable wave sizes, sampling heuristics, and conservative promotion criteria; 3) CI soft-fail adapter that surfaces regression score deltas as a "soft-fail" status and integrates with the existing eval CI dashboard to track exposure and recovery; 4) runtime telemetry hooks to emit per-prompt scoring, cohort-level deltas, and fusion provenance to Redwood Console. Rollout plan: feature gated behind eval.feature.pseudo_gt (off by default); run canary backfills on 5k prompt subset then 50k then full set; enable soft-fail in CI for 2 weeks before considering hard enforcement. Checklist: - [x] Add pseudo-GT fusion module and unit tests; - [x] Add staged backfill executor and scheduling; - [x] Add CI adapter for soft-fail signaling; - [x] Add telemetry and Console wiring; - [x] Docs and runbook. See related items: ENG-1942 (fusion research), SUP-4812 (customer incident that motivated progressive recovery strategy).

Summary: Add a new CI hook that enforces deterministic evaluation seeds and performs cohort-resampling when a prompt-set is unstable across runs. Motivation: We observed intermittent flakiness in prompt regression checks driven by non-deterministic sampling and small cohorts; teams were getting noisy failures for legitimate model changes. This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: (1) deterministic seeding at the harness level with a reproducible RNG seed that is recorded per run, and (2) a cohort-resampling strategy that expands failing cohorts and re-evaluates to distinguish statistical noise from real regressions. Implementation: - New CI hook `eval-harness/ci/hooks/stable_cohort_check.py` that wraps existing eval jobs. The hook pins RNG seeds for sampling, logs seed metadata to the run artifact, and when a cohort fails the configured threshold, triggers an automated resample up to a configurable max-resamples (default 3x) with the same seed family to produce a confidence estimate. - A light-weight resampling scheduler that runs within the CI container; it calls into existing `eval-harness` entrypoints so no duplicate eval logic is added. - Integration with CI metadata: the hook annotates the GitHub Check with deterministic-seed:<seed> and a confidence score (pass/confident, pass/uncertain, fail/confident). - Config: repo-level YAML under `eval-harness/ci/configs/stable-cohort.yaml` with tunables: seed-entropy, max-resamples, cohort-size-multiplier, significance-threshold. Testing & CI: - Unit tests for seed propagation and resampling logic (tests/ci/test_stable_cohort.py). - Integration test that simulates flakey prompt responses via a mocked sampler and verifies the hook escalates only on consistent failures. - E2E in a staging runner that executed against a small suite of real prompt-sets; artifact logs include recorded seeds and resample traces. - CI matrix runs: python unit, integration, eval-smoke, lint. All checks passed after one re-run of flaky integration. Rollout & Next steps: - Default behavior is opt-in via repo config; we'll enable for core prompt-sets after two weeks of monitoring. - Follow-up PR to add a dashboard in Console showing seed heatmaps and resample confidence over time. Related: closes ENG-2119, links to PM-423 for rollout plan.

Motivation: Flaky prompt-set regressions often surface only under small interventions (token edits, paraphrase anchors, or inserted context). Context and motivation: We observed intermittent CI failures where small syntactic perturbations to prompts caused outsized quality regressions that were brittle across seeds and model minor-version bumps. This PR introduces a neighborhood perturbation prober that generates controlled, semantically-aware perturbations around each prompt in a prompt-set and a hysteresis-style SLO adapter for CI that uses perturbation stability to decide hard vs soft failures. Goals: 1) Surface regressions that are robust to small semantic-preserving changes (true regressions) vs brittle flakiness, 2) Reduce noisy CI failures by adding a perturbation-stability threshold and a short rolling window (hysteresis) before hard-failing, 3) Produce compact minimal-patch suggestions when degradations are reproducible across perturbation modes.
Summary of changes: - New prober: harness/probers/neighborhood_prober.py implements perturbation modes (duplicate-synonym, punctuation-shift, clause-reorder, paraphasing-proxy) with configurable intensity and a seed-safe stochastic mode. - CI adapter: ci/hooks/hysteresis_slo_adapter.py adds a multi-window decision layer that classifies failures as soft, review-needed, or hard-fail based on perturbation consensus and historical drift budget. - Result reporter: harness/reporters/perturbation_diff_reporter.py produces per-prompt per-mode deltas (precision/recall-style metrics and token-level saliency delta) and exports a compact minimal-patch suggestion when a high-consensus regression is found. - Tests: tests/probers/test_neighborhood_prober.py and tests/ci/test_hysteresis_adapter.py with deterministic fixtures and a small end-to-end smoke test harness/tests/e2e/prompt_neighborhood_smoke.yaml. - Docs: docs/eval/neighborhood-prober.md and a short guidance section in docs/ci/hysteresis-slo.md describing thresholds, recommended defaults, and how to interpret patch suggestions.
Implementation notes: - Perturbation modes are implemented as composable transformers and are intentionally conservative by default; intensity is adjustable per prompt-set via config. - The hysteresis adapter maintains a short in-memory rolling buffer (configurable TTL) of recent soft failures and only escalates to hard-fail when persistent across windows or when perturbation consensus is above the configured threshold. This reduces noisy breakages seen during model rollouts while still surfacing reproducible regressions. - Reporter produces an annotated CSV + JSONL export; the CSV is intended for quick triage, JSONL contains per-example inference traces and token-level saliency diffs for deeper debugging. Backwards compatibility: No test fixtures or existing adapters were removed; default behavior for existing CI pipelines is unchanged unless teams opt into the new adapter via .eval-ci.yaml.

Add a CI gate that enforces context-consistency for multi-turn queries with hysteresis smoothing and a CI-side signal broker; exposes Prometheus metrics and a lightweight reporter to the existing eval pipeline.
Motivation: Flapping regressions observed in multi-turn prompt sets where small context shuffles or appended system notes produced outsized score deltas. This change introduces a Query-Context Consistency Gate (QCC Gate) plus a CI signal broker that aggregates multiple eval signals (semantic fidelity, paraphrase invariance, turnwise coherence) and applies temporal hysteresis to avoid noisy failures. Scope: gate implemented as an opt-in CI hook for eval-harness that can be attached to the GitHub CI pipeline; includes a broker service used only during CI to normalize and fuse signals, a lightweight smoothing policy with configurable window and thresholds, Prometheus-compatible metrics, unit and integration tests, and documentation for usage. Checklist: [x] implement core gate logic and hysteresis policy; [x] add CI broker and REST shim; [x] expose metrics and CI reporter; [x] add smoke and integration tests; [x] update docs and quickstart. Backwards compat: non-default behavior; no runtime behavioral changes unless gate enabled in CI config. How it works: the CI run posts batched eval traces to the broker; the broker computes per-cohort aggregated statistics, applies a rolling-window hysteresis (min-streak, cool-down), and returns a pass/soft-fail/hard-fail assessment. Soft-fail maps to a non-blocking annotation and automated issue template; hard-fail blocks the merge. The gate consumes multiple signal inputs and supports weighting overrides per-prompt-set. Related: ENG-2109 (flapping multi-turn regressions), ENG-2147 (eval signal normalizer).
Priya Nair: Nice approach. A couple of questions: 1) how do we pick default weights for the three signals? 2) can the hysteresis window be overridden per-linear key?
Marisol Chen: Default weights are conservative (fidelity:0.5, paraphrase:0.3, turn_consistency:0.2) and documented; added config override per-linked_linear in defaults.yaml and noted in docs.
Diego Alvarez: Tests look good; can we add a synthetic flapping prompt set to the smoke suite so the gate exercise is deterministic?
Marisol Chen: Added synthetic_flap cohort and deterministic seed in test_qcc_gate.py; included explanation in the test header.
Ethan Moore: Lint flagged some style issues in broker; resolved and pushed; requested a run of integration-evals again.

payload.body:
Context: Shadow traffic duplicates a sample of prod requests to candidate variants and scores the outputs asynchronously. This PR adds a thin adapter layer in eval-harness to consume the shadow output payload shape (control vs shadow, plus minimal request metadata) and run the same eval-harness rubric templates we use for prompt-set evaluations, with explicit rubric version pinning so results are comparable over time and across runs.

What’s included: (1) ShadowOutputAdapter that normalizes shadow artifacts into eval-harness JobSpec inputs (request text + response text + optional structured fields like tool_calls / json_output) without requiring the full original request object; (2) RubricRunner that loads templates by rubric_id + rubric_version, executes the configured metric bundle (heuristics + model-graded prompts), and emits a single ScoredShadowResult with per-metric scores plus an overall bundle summary; (3) Rubric version pinning semantics: the caller must provide rubric_version, and the runner will fail-fast if the version is unknown unless allow_fallback=true (used only for local dev); (4) Test fixtures for representative shadow artifacts including: streaming partial capture (truncated output), tool-calling payloads, and “redacted prompt” variants; (5) Golden tests that assert scoring output structure is stable (field names, types, required keys) so Console ingestion doesn’t break.

Design notes: The adapter intentionally does not depend on Redwood telemetry schemas; it only expects the minimal shadow scoring envelope produced by the shadow pipeline worker. This keeps eval-harness reusable for offline replay and reduces churn when telemetry evolves. Rubric templates are versioned via the existing template registry; this PR adds explicit version resolution and a clear error message with suggestions when a requested version is missing.

Rollout plan: This is intended to be consumed by the shadow scoring worker (ENG-5405) in Redwood. The worker will pin rubric_version per experiment at creation time and pass it through with each scoring job. We can add a follow-up PR to document recommended pinning behavior for long-running experiments.

Testing: unit tests for adapter normalization; integration-style tests that run a small rubric bundle against fixtures; lint/typecheck. CI runs both CPU-only heuristic metrics and a mocked model-graded scorer (no network).

Notes for reviewers: Please focus on the rubric version behavior, schema stability for ScoredShadowResult, and fixture coverage for streaming/tool-calling edge cases.
Jonas Weber: Can we guarantee the output schema is stable enough for Console ingestion? In particular, metrics[] ordering and presence of a top-level summary. Olivia Grant (author): Yes—added golden tests asserting stable keys and deterministic metric ordering (sorted by metric_id). Also added summary with pass_rate + mean_score computed over numeric metrics only; non-numeric metrics are excluded and recorded in metrics[].meta. Karthik Iyer: For model-graded rubrics, do we store the grader prompt version too? Otherwise comparisons get messy. Olivia: The resolved template includes grader_prompt_version and it’s emitted in metrics[].meta for model-graded metrics. We’re not making it top-level because not all metrics have it, but it’s present for any grader-driven metric. Selene Huang: Re: rubric_version pinning—should we ever fallback automatically? I’d prefer hard fail to avoid silent drift. Olivia: Agree. Default behavior is hard fail; allow_fallback is only wired for local runs and is not used by the shadow worker. I also added a log warning when allow_fallback is enabled. Sana Farid: The summary’s mean_score could be misleading if different rubrics have different scoring ranges. Maybe keep it but make it explicit. Olivia: Updated summary fields to include score_scale per metric in metrics[].meta and renamed mean_score -> mean_normalized_score, where normalization uses each metric’s declared [min,max] when available; otherwise metric is excluded from mean. Nadia Rahman: Fixture naming—can we include one that simulates the partial-capture case we saw in SUP-28477? Olivia: Added fixture shadow_streaming_partial_truncated.json and asserts that truncated=true propagates into metrics[].meta so downstream can filter.

Requested changes: (1) Make resolve_rubric error include available_versions; (2) Document allow_fallback as dev-only; (3) Add fixture for tool-calls; (4) Ensure deterministic metric ordering. All addressed in latest push.

Approvals: Jonas Weber approved. Karthik Iyer approved. Selene Huang approved. Sana Farid approved (with note to keep summary fields conservative).
payload.title: Shadow scoring: add shadow output adapter + rubric runner with rubric version pinning

payload.body:
Adds a runtime-agnostic orchestrator that fuses multiple eval signals (accuracy, calibration drift, latency regressions, tokenization instability) and escalates with a progressive CI fallback plan to avoid noisy hard failures.
Summary: This PR implements a multi-signal eval orchestrator and a progressive CI fallback policy for our eval-harness. Motivation: we've seen sporadic CI failures where a single brittle metric (e.g. a high-variance prompt cohort) caused full CI hard-fails and blocked rollouts. The orchestrator fuses orthogonal signals (cohort-level regression score, semantic-change distance, tokenization mismatch rate, and latency tail events) into a unified severity score and drives a graded CI response: soft-fail annotations -> targeted replay -> staggered quarantine -> hard-fail only if multiple independent signals cross thresholds.

What changed (high-level):
- New orchestrator core (eval_orchestrator.py) with plugin hooks for signal adapters and pluggable fusion strategies (median + rank aggregation, weighted voting).
- Signal adapters for: cohort_regression, semantic_embedding_delta, tokenization_jitter, latency_p99_delta. Each adapter emits a normalized severity float plus provenance metadata.
- CI hook (ci/fallback-scheduler.yaml + scripts/ci_fallback_runner.sh) that queries latest orchestrator decision and applies the progressive response (annotate, queue replay job, quarantine subset, escalate).
- Targeted replay runner that can execute a lightweight replay on a single model shard / seed set to reduce noise before failing the whole job.
- Telemetry: new metrics (eval.orchestrator.severity, eval.signal.*.score, eval.ci.fallback.action) and logging to the existing influx exporter with tags for model, prompt_set, cohort_id, and seed.
- Tests: unit coverage for fusion logic, adapters, and an integration smokeflow that simulates a flaky cohort and verifies the fallback ladder behavior.

Commits (summary):
- c1a3d9e: implement orchestrator core and plugin registry
- 7b2f90a: add cohort_regression and semantic_embedding_delta adapters
- d4f1a76: tokenization_jitter and latency adapters + normalization utils
- a9b8c12: CI fallback scheduler + runner scripts
- f3e5b21: telemetry hooks and metrics mapping
- 2c7b4d0: add unit and integration tests + test fixtures

Files touched (representative):
- eval_harness/orchestrator/eval_orchestrator.py
- eval_harness/adapters/cohort_regression.py
- eval_harness/adapters/semantic_delta.py
- eval_harness/adapters/tokenization_jitter.py
- eval_harness/adapters/latency_p99.py
- ci/fallback-scheduler.yaml
- scripts/ci_fallback_runner.sh
- tests/orchestrator/test_fusion.py
- tests/integration/test_progressive_fallback_sim.py

Testing & CI: Initial CI run hit a flaky integration smoke test (simulated cohort with nondeterministic seed replay) causing the job to show a partial failure. I added deterministic seeds and narrower time windows in the replay runner, retriggered CI, and the final run passed all checks: unit, lint, smoke-integration, e2e-replay. Coverage summary: new modules ~82% unit coverage; overall repo coverage unchanged.

Review thread (high level):
- Jonas Klein: asked for clearer separation between signal normalization and fusion weighting; requested an explicit docstring explaining the semantics of "severity". Author response: clarified normalization contract, and added a small doc in eval_orchestrator.py explaining assumptions and a recommended default weight matrix.
- Priya Menon: requested a low-risk default in CI (soft-fail/annotate) and an opt-in flag for stricter behavior. Author response: added `EVAL_CI_MODE` env var (soft|staggered|strict) with default "soft" and updated ci/fallback-scheduler.yaml.
- Luca Rossi: requested telemetry tags to include model_revision and cohort_anchor. Author response: added tags and a short migration note for dashboards.
- Code owner review: minor nits on logging levels fixed in subsequent commit. Final approvals by Jonas and Priya on 2026-02-02.

Backwards compatibility: Default behavior is non-breaking and conservative: CI defaults to annotate + queue replay. Operators can opt into stricter fallback via env flags. No public API changes to existing eval result schemas (adapter provenance is an additive field).

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind a boolean flag (EVAL_ORCHESTRATOR_ENABLED) in infra; we plan a staged rollout: 1) enable in canary CI pool for repo owners, 2) enable for internal teams (redwood-wide), 3) enable by default. Observability dashboards added to the Eval Overview board for the canary stage.

Related tickets: ENG-1428 (design doc), PM-337 (acceptance criteria), SUP-9082 (customer incident that motivated progressive fallback).

Merge: squash-and-merge after approvals and CI green.

Notes: This PR aims to reduce noisy CI churn while preserving early detection of substantive regressions. The fusion strategy is intentionally conservative; future work includes adaptive weighting based on historical signal reliability and an automated quarantine shrink/expand policy based on false-positive rates.

Motivation: Our monolithic lint executor was the source of frequent CI re-runs and slow premerge feedback. It loaded language-specific plugins for every changed package and made the presubmit runner sensitive to unrelated workspace files. This PR separates lint plugins into workspace-scoped plugin bundles so that each presubmit only loads the minimum plugin set required for changed files.

What this PR does (summary):
- Introduces a workspace-plugin registry (plugins/workspace-manifest.yaml) and a thin loader used by the presubmit runner.
- Moves existing lint adapters into workspace-scoped packages (tools/lint/plugins/*) and converts the TypeScript/Node bootstrap for release hooks into a small Go-based release adapter (tools/release/adapter) for reliability in CI images.
- Adds deterministic plugin activation: changed-file patterns are used to compute the minimal plugin set. This reduces cold-start work in the lint runner and avoids pulling unrelated toolchains into the job container.
- Replaces fragile bash-based release hooks with a Go binary that uses our internal release library (releasekit) to perform signing, changelog stamping, and artifact promotion. The adapter is idempotent and exposes clearer exit codes for the CI orchestrator.
- Adds unit tests and integration smoke tests for the workspace manifest resolver and release adapter.

Implementation notes and tradeoffs:
- The workspace manifest is intentionally small and declarative to avoid coupling the presubmit runner with repo-specific heuristics. A future PR will add a caching layer for monorepo hot paths.
- The Go release adapter reduces flakiness seen on alpine-based CI images where the Node runtime occasionally timed out on large payloads. However, this increases the binary build step in CI; the adapter is cross-compiled and cached in the build matrix.

Checklist:
- [x] Add workspace manifest and plugin bundles
- [x] Wire presubmit runner to compute minimal plugin set
- [x] Implement Go release adapter with tests
- [x] Update devcontainer and CONTRIBUTING.md notes
- [x] Run full CI and fix lint/test fallout

Related work: ENG-3241 (presubmit feedback speed), ENG-3308 (release automation reliability). See internal RFC: https://linear.redwood.ai/ENG-3241 for perf numbers and design notes.

Maya Thompson: Good point — added default excludes for build/, dist/, and third_party/ in the manifest generator (see plugins/workspace-manifest.yaml). Added tests to cover generated dirs.
Leah Park: Can you add an integration-run that exercises the cross-compiled adapter in the same image we use in release pipelines? We had subtle env issues earlier.
Maya Thompson: Added a smoke job to ci/ci-matrix.yml that uses the release adapter image and runs a dry-run promotion. Marked it opt-in to avoid long presubmit runs.
Carlos Mendes: Two nits: document the CLI exit codes and add a small e2e that asserts idempotency on repeated runs.
Maya Thompson: Addressed both nits. exit codes documented in tools/release/adapter/README and e2e added as adapter_test.go::TestAdapterIdempotent

payload.body:
Context and motivation: We intermittently see noisy CI failures from the eval suite caused by over-representation of small anchor prompt subsets and brittle hard-fail gating for non-deterministic probes. This PR introduces two complementary runtime/CI mechanisms to reduce false positives while preserving signal: (1) a randomized Anchor Rebalancer that detects cohort/anchor imbalance and reweights CI sampling in real-time to better reflect production request distributions; (2) a Soft-Fail Multiplexer (soft-fail-mux) that allows low-severity regressions to be demoted to a soft-fail state with automated escalation windows and telemetry hooks.

High level changes: Added eval_harness/anchor_rebalancer.py implementing a lightweight reservoir sampling + importance reweighting engine; added eval_harness/softfail_mux.py which decorates existing CI gate logic and implements configurable demotion windows, TTL-based escalations, and metadata tagging for downstream incident correlation. The CI pipeline gains a new job eval-shadow-prob-sampler that runs a small randomized shadow evaluation on each push/merge with a probabilistic seed to capture rare failure modes without flapping main gates. Configuration: eval_config.yaml gains an anchor_rebalance section (sample_ratio, max_reweight, seed_ttl) and a soft_fail section (thresholds, window_minutes, escalator_endpoint).

Design notes: Anchor rebalancer uses per-cohort counters and a decay window to compute skew; it applies multiplicative weights to the CI sampler to ensure underrepresented cohorts are sampled up to a max_reweight. This keeps CI cost bounded. The soft-fail mux exposes three policies: hard, soft, and auto. Auto demotes to soft on transient low-severity regressions and will automatically re-evaluate after the configured window; repeated occurrences within the window escalate to hard fail. Both components emit structured telemetry (eval.anchor.rebalance.event, eval.softfail.decision) sent to the existing metrics pipeline and linked in the rollback playbooks.

Test plan and checklist: - Unit tests for reservoir and weight math (anchor_rebalancer_test.py) - Integration tests that run the new CI job locally with deterministic seeds (ci/local_shadow_runner) - Added end-to-end smoke scenario that simulates cohort drift and verifies the rebalancer restores sampling mix within two windows - Added regression tests for demotion/escalation logic and TTL expiration - Updated changelog and docs/ci/anchor_rebalance.md with usage examples - Verified Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboards show new series and created an alert template for repeated soft-fail escalations.

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind eval_config.flags.anchor_rebalance and eval_config.flags.soft_fail_mux. Default to off for 48 hours, then enable in canary CI (runner pool: eval-canary). Monitor eval.alerts.softfail_escalation and token-level false-positive rate. If escalation rate exceeds 1% of merged-evals for 12 hours, automatically revert.

Related: Builds on prior work for cohort-aware samplers (ENG-1710) and the transient-rollforward gating RFC. References SUP-7291 for customer-reported noisy regression incidents.

Notes to reviewers: Focus review on the reweight math and the escalation window semantics. The rebalancer deliberately limits max_reweight to avoid overfitting to tiny cohorts; if product wants a more aggressive policy we can expose that via flags.

Miguel Santos: Please add a short e2e smoke that runs the pipeline with a deterministic seed so we can reproduce the weighting behaviour in CI. Also call out the cost impact of the shadow sampler (expected +3% token budget).
Asha Kapoor: Added a deterministic smoke test and documented the expected +3% token budget in the docs. The rebalancer caps max_reweight at 5x by default to bound cost.
Olivia Chen: Can we make the soft-fail window configurable per-cohort? Some product cohorts are more sensitive.
Asha Kapoor: Done — softfail_mux now accepts an optional per-cohort override and falls back to a global default. Added tests for override behaviour.
Samir Patel: Lint caught an edge case in reservoir sampling when the cohort is empty; addressed in last commit. Approving once CI passes.
payload.title: Add randomized anchor rebalancer and soft-fail multiplexer for CI-stable evals

payload.body:
Motivation: We frequently see regressions that only surface when prompts are slightly altered (typos, spacing, casing, small synonym swaps). These brittle prompts lead to production quality regressions that escape standard semantic checks. This PR adds a Lexical Variance Prober (LVP) CI adapter that runs a configurable suite of lightweight textual perturbations against existing prompt sets during CI smokechecks and reports sensitivity scores per-prompt and per-cohort. Design: LVP is implemented as a CI adapter that can be enabled per-eval-config and integrated into existing smoke gate pipelines. It generates a small set of perturbed inputs for each prompt using deterministic RNG seeds, runs model evaluations in parallel with budgeted sampling, computes a normalized sensitivity score (0-1) using token-level edit distances and semantic drift metrics, and annotates failing prompts when sensitivity exceeds configured thresholds. The adapter stores concise artifact summaries (CSV/JSON) and uploads a lightweight HTML report to the CI job artifacts for human triage. Compatibility and safety: The prober only uses non-invasive perturbations and avoids semantic rephrases that alter instruction intent by more than a configurable semantic-similarity threshold. It's disabled by default for older eval configs and can be opted-in via eval_config.enable_lexical_prober=true. CI integration: Adds a new job eval-lexical-prober in the smoke pipeline that runs under a :memory: budget with timeout guardrails and retries. The job is soft-fail by default for the first rollout and can be promoted to hard-gate by project teams. Metrics and outputs: The adapter emits per-prompt sensitivity, cohort-aggregated percentile, and a small failure set of highest-sensitivity prompts. These are tagged into existing CI telemetry so dashboards can trend sensitivity over time. Tests and validation: Unit tests cover perturbation generators and scoring functions, end-to-end integration runs against a synthetic prompt corpus in CI, and a canary run was executed against the 'paraphrase' and 'instructions' prompt cohorts. Performance: The prober adds ~12s median overhead to a smoke pipeline run for a typical 50-prompt smoke set due to parallelized execution and bounded sampling. Configs and docs: Added config schema docs, a short README with recommended thresholds, and a migration note for teams that want to adopt the prober. Rollout plan: Start as opt-in for two weeks while collecting telemetry, then recommend opt-in for all non-experimental eval configs. Related: ENG-1459 tracking rollout, ENG-1464 follows up to add automated triage labels in the console.
Arjun Patel (reviewer): Can we avoid semantic rephrases that change instruction intent? Add a similarity guard.
Maria Chen (author): Added a semantic-similarity check (Cosine with configurable threshold) and documented the default value. See commit f3a4b5c.
Lena Ortiz (reviewer): CI job timing looks fine but ensure artifacts are small. Request trimming raw model outputs and only storing diffs and summary metrics.
Maria Chen (author): Switched artifact format to compressed summary + top-10 diffs to keep storage low.
Diego Morales (approver): Verified E2E canary against two prompt cohorts. Approve to merge once CI green.
CI Bot: lint failed on first run (line-length) then passed after formatting fix. All checks green on latest run.

payload.body:
Motivation: Flaky prompt-set failures often surface as noisy, undiagnosed regressions. This PR adds a semantic failure attributor that groups failing outputs by semantic equivalence (embedding + cluster heuristics) and attaches a compact explanation blob. In parallel it introduces a soft-fail sentinel CI hook that will let teams mark transient regressions as soft failures for a configurable backoff window while still surfacing them in dashboards. The goal is to reduce alert fatigue and give engineers richer failure context to triage root causes quickly. Changes include: new attributor service, CLI matcher for historic failure lookups, CI hook that can soft-fail with TTL/backoff, telemetry events, and dashboard links. Checklist: 1) Implement semantic clustering with cosine threshold + token-match heuristics; 2) Add exporter for compact failure blobs and anchor examples; 3) Integrate soft-fail sentinel into existing CI pipeline with opt-in label support; 4) Add unit tests and end-to-end smoke job; 5) Update docs and rollout playbook. Related work: this complements ENG-3980 (prompt-set bank) and follows patterns from recent drift-detection services. Linear: ENG-4123. Jira: SUP-786 for customer incident that motivated the emergency hold behavior.
4 commits: initial semantic attributor implementation; add CI soft-fail hook and TTL policy; add telemetry and dashboard link attachments; tests and docs. Commits include focused refactors to the eval runner to expose failure hooks and a small shim to serialize failure blobs for downstream debugging.
+ def compute_semantic_signature(text):
+     	sig = embed(text)[:128]  # truncated vector for grouping
+     return sha1(sig.tobytes()).hexdigest()
+ class SoftFailSentinel(Hook):
+     	def on_eval_complete(self, result):
+     		if is_transient(result):
+     			mark_soft_fail(result, ttl_seconds=86400)  # default 1 day

- removed obsolete flaky_gate flag from eval runner configuration
Andre Dupont: Nice direction. A few concerns: we should ensure the embedding model is pinned for deterministic grouping and add a feature-flag for rollout.
Sophie Martinez: Added a pin to the embedding model in config and feature-flagged soft-fail via env var; included tests that run with local deterministic embedder.
Maya Chen: Telemetry looks good. Can we include a sampling rate for failure blob exports to avoid storage blowup?
Sophie Martinez: Added sampling config and a cap on daily exported blobs per-team. Also included a compact gzip path for larger payloads.
Liam O'Connor: Approving with minor nits on doc wording. Recommend a 2-week canary before org-wide enablement.
Sophie Martinez: Will run canary in 'eval-team' and 'platform' orgs; added rollout notes in docs.
Local unit tests added for clustering logic, sampling logic validated with synthetic failure corpus. Ran a staged canary on 'eval-team' with 48h observation window; soft-fail rate reduced alert noise by ~38% on sampled prompts.
Add semantic failure attribution and configurable soft-fail sentinel to CI. Enables grouping of semantically equivalent failures and optional soft-fail behavior to reduce noisy regression alerts. Backwards compatible; opt-in via feature flag.
Stage 1: enable in eval-team canary (2 days). Stage 2: enable for platform team and monitor failure export volume (1 week). Stage 3: org-wide enablement with default soft-fail TTL 24h and sampling rate 0.1. Rollback: flip feature flag off and purge soft-fail queue.
Failure blobs may contain PII or user content. Exporter defaults to scrub mode: remove email addresses, phone numbers, and long personal identifiers. Teams must opt-in via an enterprise policy for full payload exports and enable KMS encryption. KMS tag: redwood-eval-failure-exports.
Keep an eye on daily exported blob count; sampling defaults can be tuned per-organization. The clustering threshold is conservative by default (cosine >= 0.86). If the embedding provider changes, re-run baseline to recalibrate thresholds.
Add feature flag to infra for org rollout
Schedule dashboard panels to show soft-fail vs hard-fail rates
Follow-up PR to add retention policy for exported failure blobs
This merged change reduces noisy CI alerts by grouping semantically similar failures and letting teams mark certain regressions as soft failures for a configurable window while providing richer context to triage. Authored by Sophie Martinez and approved after canary testing.

payload.body:
- Go SDK: add StreamReconnect helper for chat/completions streaming with retry/backoff and resume-from-last-event behavior where possible. - Add example demonstrating production-safe streaming defaults (timeouts, cancellation, structured logging).
Context: We’ve seen a recurring onboarding/first-prod issue where customers try streaming in a quickstart-like environment and interpret transient disconnects (mobile networks, reverse proxies, idle timeouts) as SDK instability. Support ticket SUP-18488 captures a representative failure mode. This PR adds a small, opinionated helper for resilient streaming consumption in the Go SDK and a runnable example to show recommended patterns.

What’s included: (1) A new streaming reconnect helper in package streamx that wraps our existing streaming client and provides controlled reconnect behavior. It retries on network/transport errors and selected HTTP statuses (408/429/5xx) with exponential backoff + jitter, respects Retry-After, and uses a bounded max elapsed time / max attempts. (2) A lightweight event cursor that lets callers preserve progress (last received event ID / last chunk index) to avoid double-processing when reconnecting. For providers/paths where we can’t resume server-side, we still guarantee client-side idempotency hooks (OnChunk) are invoked with a monotonic cursor and the helper can be configured to drop duplicates by cursor. (3) A new example (examples/streaming_reconnect_chat) showing how to wire context cancellation, timeouts, structured logging, and a simple health endpoint that validates outbound connectivity.

Non-goals: This does not change default retry policy for non-streaming requests. It also does not attempt to fully replay the same server-side stream after partial completion; in most cases the correct app-level behavior is to re-issue the request with conversation state and handle duplicates defensively. The helper is intentionally explicit and opt-in.

API shape:
- streamx.ReconnectConfig { MaxAttempts, MaxElapsed, BaseDelay, MaxDelay, RetryOnStatuses, RespectRetryAfter, Logger, CursorStore }
- streamx.StreamWithReconnect(ctx, cfg, func(ctx) (Stream, error), handler)
Where handler receives chunks/events and returns (continue bool, err error). The handler is invoked sequentially.

Why now: This maps directly to the onboarding checklist “Streaming: handle disconnects/timeouts” step and unblocks the DevEx team from pointing to a single canonical Go snippet.

Testing: Unit tests cover backoff behavior, Retry-After parsing, max elapsed cutoff, duplicate suppression via cursor, and handler error propagation. Integration-ish tests run against the existing mock streaming server used elsewhere in the SDK.

Docs: Adds GoDoc comments + a README in the example directory with copy/paste instructions.

Rollout: Safe additive change. No behavior changes unless consumers adopt streamx.StreamWithReconnect or copy the example patterns.

Screenshots/log output: Example prints connection attempts, retry reasons, and final outcome; see examples/streaming_reconnect_chat/README.md.

Follow-ups: Align naming with TypeScript SDK helper once that lands (ENG-5820 umbrella). Consider adding a small section in docs site linking to this example from the Console checklist deep link.
Example usage (abridged):

cfg := streamx.ReconnectConfig{
  MaxAttempts: 6,
  MaxElapsed:  2 * time.Minute,
  BaseDelay:   250 * time.Millisecond,
  MaxDelay:    5 * time.Second,
  RespectRetryAfter: true,
  RetryOnStatuses: []int{408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504},
  CursorStore: streamx.NewInMemoryCursorStore(),
  Logger:      log.Default(),
}

err := streamx.StreamWithReconnect(ctx, cfg, func(ctx context.Context) (streamx.Stream, error) {
  // create a fresh stream each attempt
  return client.ChatCompletionsStream(ctx, req)
}, func(ev streamx.Event) (bool, error) {
  // idempotent processing recommended
  fmt.Print(ev.Delta)
  return true, nil
})
Ibrahim Khan: API looks good. Two concerns: (1) We need to be careful not to imply we can resume server-side streams universally. Please adjust docs/comments to call this “reconnect + duplicate suppression” not “resume”. (2) Ensure we never retry on 4xx except 408/429. Also verify we respect ctx cancellation immediately between attempts.
Mateusz Zielinski: Updated terminology in GoDoc + README (removed “resume” language). Retryable statuses now default to {408,429,5xx} and we explicitly reject other 4xx. Added ctx checks before sleeping and before establishing a new stream.
Sean Gallagher: From SRE perspective, please cap backoff and add jitter (avoid thundering herd on regional blips). Also, can we surface metrics hooks in the helper? Even just callbacks would help.
Mateusz Zielinski: Added MaxDelay and full jitter. Added optional callbacks OnAttempt / OnRetry / OnGiveUp in config (kept lightweight, no dependency on metrics libs). Example demonstrates logging these callbacks.
Monica Patel: This will be linked from onboarding checklist. Please ensure the example sets timeouts (dial + overall) and shows how to set User-Agent tagging if supported.
Mateusz Zielinski: Example now sets http.Client timeouts via SDK client options and uses the existing UserAgent option. Added a README section mapping to “streaming disconnects” troubleshooting.
Ibrahim Khan: Final nit: move CursorStore interface to its own file and add a test for Retry-After with multiple header values.
Mateusz Zielinski: Done. Added test cases for Retry-After parsing across formats and multiple headers. Ready for re-review.
Ibrahim Khan: Approved.
Monica Patel: Approved.
Sean Gallagher: Approved (thanks for jitter + hooks).

payload.body:
Context and motivation: Some regressions manifest as shifts in the model's probability mass over semantically equivalent answers rather than hard label changes. Existing binary pass/fail gates can be too brittle (false positives) or miss subtle quality drift. This PR adds a 'soft-label prober' and a calibrated-expectation CI hook that (a) probes prompt cohorts with synthetic soft labels (probability distributions over acceptable outputs), (b) compares aggregate likelihood mass assigned to expected semantic clusters, and (c) uses a noise-aware historical model to set dynamic tolerances so teams get fewer spurious CI failures while retaining sensitivity to true regressions.

Goals: 1) detect semantic drift that doesn't appear as single-answer mismatches; 2) reduce noisy CI failures by modeling historical variance per-cohort; 3) provide clear remediation artifacts (example worst-case prompts, delta distributions, suggested rollback windows).

Implementation summary:
- Core: eval_harness.probers.soft_label_prober.py implements probing loop, clustering helper (semantic buckets via embed+kmeans), and soft-label matcher that accepts distribution-level comparisons (KL, Earth Mover Distance).

payload.body:
Motivation: our long-running prompt suites produce large numbers of noisy failures that drown signal and cause frequent engineer interrupt loops. This PR implements two complementary pieces: 1) a shard prioritizer that assigns probe shards (cohorts/prompt-sets) priority scores based on recent instability, historical importance, and latency impact; priority influences sampling frequency and scheduling so that high-risk prompt shards get probed earlier in CI windows; 2) a failure-compressor that groups identical or near-identical failures into envelope signatures (text-normalized message, canonical stack, metric deltas) and emits a single canonical incident summary to the CI reporter. Together these reduce noisy duplicates and improve the signal-to-noise ratio for regression alerts. The PR also wires a new reliability_score metric used by the CI bridge to make retry/attenuation decisions and introduces a small CI adapter that performs rate-limited retries for transient failures and suppresses repeated signatures for a configurable cooldown window. Backwards compatibility: existing probe configs continue to work; the new prioritizer is opt-in via eval_config.prioritization.enabled. Changes include: scheduler refactor to add shard metadata, a lightweight LRU signature cache for compression, metric emitter for reliability_score, a CLI flag (--shard-prioritizer-debug) for local dry runs, and docs + examples. Testing: unit tests for prioritizer heuristics, integration smoke that runs on a sampled suite, and a synthetic replay to validate compressor grouping heuristics. Related work: ENG-4123 (probe noise reduction), ENG-4189 (ci alert throttling).
Adds shard-based probe prioritization and a failure-compression layer to reduce noisy CI alerts. New metric (reliability_score) and CI adapter to rate-limit retriggers. Backwards-compatible with existing probe configs.
opt-in prioritizer available via eval_config.prioritization.enabled; new reliability_score metric emitted under eval.reliability_score; default compressor cooldown is 1h and is configurable via eval_config.compressor.cooldown
Manual QA steps: run `evalctl probe --shard sample --prioritizer` on a 1k prompt set to verify prioritization order, trigger repeated synthetic failures to observe single compressed incident in CI output, and validate reliability_score trend on metrics dashboard.
Low risk: feature is opt-in and safe by default. Compressor only aggregates and annotates failures; it does not drop raw traces. Memory usage scoped with LRU cap and metrics exported.
Diego Ramos: Left a few nits on the scoring weights and asked for a short benchmark that shows reduced time-to-detect for high-risk shards. Also asked to ensure the LRU cache is bounded by memory and exposes a clear eviction metric.
Asha Patel: Responded with a microbenchmark (see commits) and added eviction gauges for the compressor. Clarified the default weights in docs and made them configurable via eval_config.prioritizer.weights.
Marta Lee: Requested an integration test that simulates heavy duplicate failures to validate suppression behavior. Noted a small race in scheduler ordering — requested a fix.
Asha Patel: Added deterministic ordering fallback and integration test; CI initially flagged a flaky test in the smoke suite, reran and passed.
Connor Nguyen: Approved after confirming metrics are emitted with stable labels and that the CI adapter does not alter exit codes for non-transient failures.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: We observed a class of spurious CI failures where late-arriving contextual drift or transient model nondeterminism caused the primary smoke cohorts to surface regression alerts, triggering interrupts and engineer investigation. This PR introduces a lightweight "reverse-probing" cohort and a fidelity rollback adapter that works as a CI-layer soft-fallback: when a regression is detected, the reverse-probing cohort re-evaluates the failing prompt subset with inverse perturbations and seed-variance traces to detect instability vs. true quality degradation. If the reverse probe indicates high instability (configurable threshold), the fidelity rollback adapter will mark the CI gate as 'soft-fail' and trigger a prioritized re-run and targeted replay rather than a full blocking failure. This reduces noise and gives a fast path for automated triage.

What this PR includes (single-line summary): implement reverse-probe cohort sampling, probe scheduler, rollback adapter, CI hook, unit and integration tests, docs and lightweight telemetry.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement reverse-probe sampling strategy and scheduler
- [x] Implement fidelity rollback adapter and CI hook integration
- [x] Add unit tests for probe behaviors and adapter decision logic
- [x] Add integration test that simulates nondeterministic churn and ensures soft-fail semantics
- [x] Add docs: rationale and runbook for ops teams
- [x] Add telemetry hooks: probe outcome, rollback.reason, replay.job_id

Design notes: The reverse-probe cohort uses a complementary perturbation set (token-suffix shuffles, paraphrase templates, and inverse temperature sweep) to exercise orthogonal failure modes compared to standard anchors. The adapter uses a two-step decision function: (1) compute instability score = weighted combination of cross-seed divergence and paraphrase disagreement, (2) if instability_score > instability_threshold and absolute regression delta < small_delta_threshold, mark as soft-fail and schedule targeted replay with higher sample concentration. Thresholds are configurable via ci.config.replay.

Commit summary:
- 10f4a6c: introduce reverse_prober module and sampling primitives
- 2b9c4de: add fidelity_rollback adapter and CI hook glue
- a3d2f71: tests: unit tests for instability scoring and adapter pathing
- f4e1b58: integration test for nondeterministic churn and soft-fail behavior
- 9c8b41d: docs: add runbook and configuration example

Testing and CI: The PR wired up a staged CI job: unit -> integration(replay-mock) -> e2e(smoke). Flaky network on first integration run caused a single rerun; final CI status is green. The integration includes a mocked replay service so this can run in CI without requiring cluster access. Add a prompt-heterogeneity sensitivity latch to the eval harness and integrate a smoke CI hook that soft-fails when prompt-group behavioral dispersion exceeds calibrated thresholds. Adds telemetry and quarantine markers for failing prompt subsets.
Motivation: Some regression failures we see in CI are driven by increased variability across heterogeneous prompts (different intents/labels) rather than a global model degradation. This PR introduces a prompt heterogeneity sensitivity latch — a lightweight statistical guard that detects when the per-prompt-group dispersion (e.g., variance in composite quality score) exceeds an adaptive threshold and surfaces a soft-fail in CI with explanations and candidate quarantines. Goals: reduce noisy, non-actionable CI failures, provide clearer signals for prompt-set issues, and add tooling to quarantine subsets for focused debugging. What this changes: - New analysis module: eval/heterogeneity_latch.py implements bootstrap-calibrated dispersion thresholds, cohort weighting, and an explain API for top contributing prompts. - CI smoke hook: ci/hooks/heterogeneity_smokehook.py integrates the latch into the eval CI job; the hook reports structured reasons and can mark failing prompts with a quarantine tag in the eval artifact ledger. - Telemetry: metrics/tracing additions emit "eval.heterogeneity.score" and top-k prompt fingerprints for downstream dashboards. - Tests: unit and integration tests under tests/cover to validate sensitivity, bootstrap stability, and integration with existing eval reporter. - Docs/design: docs/decisions/heterogeneity_latch.md and a short how-to in docs/ci-ops/README.md. Backwards compatibility: default configuration keeps the latch in "monitor-only" mode (it annotates results but does not block merges) unless a repo-scale Linear flag is set. Checklist: - [x] Implement core latch algorithm with bootstrap calibration - [x] Add CI hook and wire into .github/workflows/eval-ci.yml (disabled by default in repo config) - [x] Add unit tests with synthetic prompt sets and a small real-world regression example - [x] Add telemetry tags and simple Grafana dashboard stub (not included in this PR) - [x] Update docs and add a troubleshooting section - [x] Add migration note for teams that enable strict gating in their config Known limitations and future work: We intentionally keep the latch conservative to avoid false positives on very small prompt cohorts; next work items include a cohort-size-aware smoothing policy and a human-in-the-loop quarantine approval flow. Related: ENG-4539 (design), PM-1180 (product ask), SUP-2231 (customer report about noisy CI failures). Links: design doc: docs/decisions/heterogeneity_latch.md; example run: ci/runs/heterogeneity-smoke/2026-02-18 (internal).

Asha Patel (author): Added a conservative sample-size floor (defaults to 30) and bootstrap smoothing; documented the behavior in the design doc. See tests/test_heterogeneity_latch.py:TestSmallCohortCoverage
Diego Ramirez: Please emit a distinct metric name and tag the evaluation run id so we can filter occurrences in dashboards. Also requested top-5 fingerprint emission for triage.

Motivation: CI has historically caught mean-regression but misses flaky or highvariance regressions introduced by model changes, quantization, or runtime scheduling. This PR adds a cross-run stability CI hook that runs a compact prompt-set across multiple randomized seeds and uses a denoising resampling step to detect changes in both central tendency and output variance. The hook introduces a new stability_score metric (combines bootstrap mean delta, inter-run variance ratio, and token-level agreement) and a noise-aware gate that fails CI when the expected mean delta exceeds threshold and stability_score < threshold. Implementation summary: 1) core hook at eval_harness/hooks/cross_run_stability.py that orchestrates N independent runs (default 5) with configurable random seeds, computes per-example bootstrap CIs, and aggregates cohort-level stability_score; 2) denoise resampler module that runs lightweight label-free reruns and builds a consensus output to reduce single-run noise impact; 3) CLI flag --stability-hook in eval-runner to enable locally; 4) unit tests and integration tests under tests/ that simulate synthetic drift and flaky outputs; 5) CI pipeline additions in .github/workflows/eval-ci.yml to run the stability hook on PRs that touch eval-related directories and when a new model is promoted. Operational notes: thresholds are conservative by default (mean delta 1.5% and stability_score 0.7) and live behind a feature flag eval.stability_gate so we can rollout progressively to the repo and to selected projects; there is an opt-out decorator for long-running golden test suites. Backwards compatibility: the hook is additive and not enabled by default for existing repos unless the feature flag is set. Checklist: - [x] Core orchestration and denoising algorithm implemented - [x] Unit tests for resampler and score aggregation - [x] Integration test that fails on synthetic high-variance regression - [x] CI workflow entry and gating rule - [x] Documentation: README for the hook and runbook for triage - [x] Linear tickets linked for rollout and dashboarding How to run locally: pip install -e . then python -m eval_harness.runner --stability-hook --stability-runs 5 --stability-seed-base 1000 Examples and expected output are in tests/fixtures/ and the run prints a short summary table with stability_score, bootstrap mean delta, CI decision and links to artifact logs. Rollout plan: enable behind feature flag for internal e2e job, run in monitoring mode (logs only) for 2 weeks, then enable soft-fail (mark as warning) for 1 week, then gate on merge if no signal drift. Related work: ENG-2031 (prompt regression monitoring), ENG-2089 (eval CI orchestration improvements), SUP-445 was the support ticket that surfaced noisy failure patterns in customer tests. No breaking changes to public APIs. Merge: squash and merge after final reviewer approvals and CI green.
Arjun Patel: This looks solid overall, one question on the stability_score composition — can we make the weights configurable via config with sensible defaults?
Maya Chen: Good point, added config.default.stability_weights and documented the defaults in docs/hooks/stability_hook.md
Sofia Martinez: The denoising rerun adds infra cost for CI, please add a fallback path that uses a lightweight token-agreement heuristic when budget is constrained.
Maya Chen: Added a budget-aware path in denoise_resampler that switches to token-agreement mode when ci.budget_estimate < threshold; included tests for both paths.
Ben Liu: Minor: the integration test is flaky on mac builders due to random tmp file ordering, please switch to tempfile.TemporaryDirectory to avoid ordering assumptions.

payload.body:
Motivation: We frequently see regressions that are concentrated on small prompt sets or particular intents. Existing CI gates trigger on snapshot-level metric regressions but lack the ability to attribute early-stage degradation to stewarded prompt groups or to suggest targeted mitigation. This PR adds a lightweight 'prompt stewardship' CI gate that tracks temporal degradation signals per prompt cohort and surfaces automated remediation suggestions.

What this PR does: implements a CI hook and evaluation adaptor that computes a temporal degradation score (TDS) per prompt cohort, produces a severity-weighted alert, and integrates with the existing CI gating layer to fail builds when the aggregated risk exceeds team-configured thresholds. The gate includes: (1) prompt stewardship metadata (steward_id, intent_tag, owner_contact) ingestion, (2) a sliding-window AUC-of-degradation metric (default 7 days) and short/long term slope comparison, (3) a quarantine suggestion engine that maps signal patterns to recommended actions (quarantine, pin-model, add-smoke-eval, lower-temp fallback), and (4) telemetry to the console for per-prompt traces and remediation history.

Design notes: the TDS combines three components: delta-normalized metric drop (relative to historical baseline), volatility multiplier (higher weight for low-variance cohorts), and exposure factor (traffic share estimate). Score = AUC_drop * (1 + volatility_norm) * exposure_score. We experimented with a few normalizers; chosen formulation balances sensitivity to small, high-impact cohorts. The gate is configurable via eval-config.yaml under gates.prompt_stewardship: threshold, window_days, min_examples, steward_whitelist.

Why unique: unlike past approaches that only look at cohort-level average changes, this gate reasons about prompt ownership and operational workflows: suggestions are actionable (contact steward, schedule canary, auto-quarantine) and the gate emits structured remediation suggestions to downstream tools (Slack/Linear webhook adapter). The gate is intentionally conservative by default (min_examples=50, threshold tuned to ~3% short-term AUC drop for high-exposure cohorts) to reduce false positives.

Files & tests touched: Adds unit tests for scoring logic and synthetic cohort simulations; adds a lightweight integration test that runs the gate against archived eval-replay data; adds docs with rollout steps and config examples.

How to review: focus on the scoring function (eval_harness/gates/prompt_stewardship/score.py), the CI hook adapter (eval_harness/hooks/prompt_stewardship_hook.py), and the webhook adapter for remediation (integrations/linear_and_slack/prompt_stewardship_notifier.py). The bulk of additions are test fixtures and documentation.

Checklist:
- [x] implement scoring and gate integration
- [x] unit tests for scoring edge cases (zero-variance cohorts, sparse cohorts)
- [x] integration smoke against eval replay pipeline
- [x] docs and config example
- [x] register Linear hooks for remediation suggestions

Rollout plan: feature flag gated on eval-config, opt-in for 2 weeks (monitor noise rate), then enable soft-fail (raise warnings but not block merges) for core models, then hard-fail for stewarded high-exposure cohorts after tuning window.

Notes & future work: planned follow-ups include an on-call routing integration (pager for critical stewards), richer remediation suggestions (automated rollback playbooks), and a UI in the console to triage stewarded prompts.

Related: Linear ENG-1427 (prompt-level regression tooling), PM-308 (product rollout plan).

payload.body:
Motivation: We need a targeted, explainable signal for regressions where the model fails to preserve key referenced facts present in prompts (citations, referenced tools, explicit constraints). Current eval gates focus on overall accuracy/quality but miss cases where the model omits or rewrites referenced content. This PR introduces a Prompt Recall Fidelity (PRF) scorer and a granular CI thresholder that can be applied per-prompt-cohort with a soft-halt behavior to avoid blocking unrelated rollouts.

What this PR contains: 1) An efficient PRF scorer (eval_harness/metrics/prompt_recall_scorer.py) that computes a recall-style score combining token-level alignments, embedding overlap for paraphrase-tolerant matching, and a lightweight referent-extraction verifier for structured references (URLs, DOIs, code identifiers). 2) A CI adapter (ci/hooks/recall_thresholder.yml + eval_harness/ci/recall_thresholder.py) that takes cohort-level distributions and applies adaptive thresholds: per-cohort baseline + delta, with configurable soft-halt (mark PR as "soft-fail" and annotate with per-prompt evidence) and hard-fail escalation options. 3) Test coverage (tests/test_prompt_recall_scorer.py, tests/test_recall_thresholder_integration.py) with deterministic fixtures and a small synthetic suite that simulates hallucinated omission, paraphrase-preservation, and truncated output cases. 4) Docs and example (docs/eval/prompt_recall_fidelity.md) that explain metric semantics, recommended cohorts, and suggested thresholds for common families of workloads (FAQ/chat, citation-anchored QA, instruction-following).

Algorithmic notes: - Token alignment uses a fuzzy longest-common-subsequence weighted by wordpiece lengths to penalize dropped referents. - Embedding overlap uses precomputed sentence embeddings (cosine) with a simple calibration against positive/negative examples to be robust to paraphrase. - Structured referent verifier extracts deterministic tokens (URLs, hex ids, package names) and applies exact-match and prefix-match heuristics. - Final PRF score is a weighted combination: exact structured-match first, embedding overlap second, token alignment third; weights are configurable via YAML.

CI behavior and operator UX: - By default the CI hook runs as an optional check that reports mean/median PRF by cohort. Teams can enable strict mode (hard-fail) or soft-fail mode. Soft-fail annotates the PR with the lowest-scoring prompts (top K per cohort) and a suggested remediation: add a focused prompt-set or a targeted model variant test. - The thresholder supports time-windowed baselines (7/30/90d) and will automatically fall back to global baselines when cohort history is sparse. - When the check triggers, the CI comment includes inline evidence: prompt id, expected references, model output excerpt, PRF score, and nearest-match embedding snippets.

Commit summary: - commit 1: initial PRF scorer implementation and unit tests - commit 2: integrate structured referent extractor and embedding calibration - commit 3: CI adapter + thresholder operational config and GitHub check reporter - commit 4: docs, example cohorts, and cli wrapper for local run - commit 5: test hardening and threshold defaults tuning after review feedback

Changed files (high level): ["eval_harness/metrics/prompt_recall_scorer.py", "eval_harness/metrics/_helpers/structured_referent_extractor.py", "eval_harness/ci/recall_thresholder.py", "ci/hooks/recall_thresholder.yml", "tests/test_prompt_recall_scorer.py", "tests/test_recall_thresholder_integration.py", "docs/eval/prompt_recall_fidelity.md", "examples/recall_cohorts/example_cohorts.yml", "eval_harness/cli/run_recall_check.py", "eval_harness/metrics/embeddings_calibrator.py", "eval_harness/ci/reporting/recall_reporter.py", "pyproject.toml"]

Selected snippets: - recall_thresholder.yml declares thresholds per-cohort and maps to Linear keys for escalation - prompt_recall_scorer.py exposes a score() function that accepts (prompt_text, model_output, reference_tokens) and returns {"prf": float, "evidence": [..]} (See docs for schema).

Review conversation (high-level thread): - Maya Chen (reviewer): "Nice focused metric. Please add a unit test for structured referent extractor when multiple referents share token prefixes (e.g., pkg-1 and pkg-10). Also we should avoid expensive embedding computations in the fast path." - Evan Park (author): "Added targeted unit for prefix collisions and moved embedding calibrator to an async background cache with TTL; cheap fingerprinting allows early-exit for exact matches." - Jordan Liu (reviewer): "Can we expose a debug mode that dumps per-prompt alignment traces to help SRE triage failures?" - Evan Park: "Added debug flag to CLI and a retention param for CI artifact upload; default off to avoid large artifacts." - Priya Raman (approver): "Tests and docs look good. Suggest default soft-fail for non-enterprise orgs." - Maya Chen: "Left one minor comment about logging levels, addressed in follow-up commit."

payload.body:
Motivation: regression monitoring today focuses on scalar metrics (accuracy, F1) and cohort drift, but we lack a lightweight, automated probe that detects subtle increases in hallucination rates for prompt-sets used by production routes. This PR adds a hallucination prober that runs in CI (and optionally as a scheduled backfill) and a hit-rate quality gate which fails CI when the fraction of outputs containing required factual anchors (hit-rate) degrades beyond a configurable tolerance compared to a rolling baseline.

What this PR does (summary): adds a new prober implementation (model-agnostic), an entailment-based lightweight verifier for anchor detection, a hit-rate gate that integrates with existing CI gate infrastructure, unit and integration tests, docs and runbook, and a small backfill worker to compute baselines for historical prompt-sets.

Key behaviors: - Sample-based prober: selects representative examples from a prompt-set (stratified by length and expected output type) and issues multiple perturbations (paraphrase + distractor injection) to stress hallucination modes. - Anchor extraction: prompt-set owners can declare one or more "anchors" (short canonical facts or ground-truth snippets). The prober checks presence and semantic entailment of anchors in model outputs rather than exact substring matches. - Hit-rate calculation: counts prompts where at least one anchor is validated, normalized over the probe sample. - Gate policy: compares current hit-rate to an exponential moving baseline and fails if the drop exceeds the configured absolute or relative threshold. Gate supports soft-fail (comment + label) and hard-fail (CI fail). - Backfill: a batch job to compute baseline hit-rates from historical runs and seed the baseline store for new prompt-sets.

Why this approach: purely lexical checks are brittle; entailment gives robustness and reduces false positives while remaining computationally lightweight compared to full human review. The gate is designed to be conservative by default (small tolerance, soft-fail) and to escalate only after repeatable regressions.

Checklist:
- [x] Prober implementation (eval_harness/probers/hallucination_prober.py)
- [x] Hit-rate gate (eval_harness/ci/gates/hit_rate_gate.py)
- [x] Unit tests and integration smoke (tests/probers/test_hallucination_prober.py, tests/ci/test_hit_rate_gate.py)
- [x] Backfill worker and baseline store adapter (tools/backfill/hit_rate_backfill.py)
- [x] Docs and runbook (docs/ci-gates/hit-rate.md)
- [x] Add CI hooks and GitHub action config snippet (ci/actions/hit_rate_gate.yml)

Backwards compat & config: the gate is opt-in for existing prompt-sets. New prompt-sets created via the prompt registry will default to a soft-fail policy and a 2% absolute tolerance relative to historical hit-rate. Ops can flip to hard-fail via project config.

Risks & mitigations: - False positives from noisy entailment: mitigated by threshold tuning, paraphrase ensemble, and a configurable minimum confidence. - Cost overhead: prober sample sizes are small (default 100) and entailment runs cache embeddings; backfill is rate-limited to off-peak windows.

Next steps: add Prometheus metrics (probe_latency_ms, hit_rate, gate_failures) and a dashboard to make regressions visible; add a Canary runner that runs the prober against a small live shadow traffic slice.

Notes on run: the initial runs were executed against three models (redwood/base-1, redwood/qa-2, open/llama-3) to validate behavior and to seed baselines for a subset of internal prompt-sets.
Priya Shah: Good overall shape. Two asks: make the entailment confidence threshold configurable per-prompt-set, and add a test for paraphrase perturbations failing to flip anchors incorrectly.
Diego Montes (author): addressed config and added paraphrase test; moved default threshold to 0.82 and added comments on rationale.
Ethan Liu: Can we avoid calling the large entailment model for every sample? Suggest caching embedding for anchors and running a cheap cosine check as a pre-filter.
Diego Montes (author): added embedding prefilter and benchmark numbers in comments; cache TTL set to 12h and invalidated on anchor update. See eval_harness/utils/entailment_adapter.py for implementation.
Marcelina Gomez: integration tests look flaky on CI (intermittent network timeouts to the verifier). Recommend adding retry with exponential backoff and marking the gate runner as tolerant to transient verifier failures (soft-fail).
Diego Montes (author): added retries and circuit-breaker; updated gate to fall back to previous baseline on verifier outage and emit alert metric.
- Add hallucination prober: lightweight probe that validates presence of declared anchors via entailment-based checks.
- Add hit-rate CI gate: fails CI when validated anchor hit-rate drops beyond configured tolerance.
- Backfill job to seed historical baselines and adapter for baseline store.
- Opt-in by default (soft-fail) for existing prompt-sets; project-level config to enable hard-fail.

Motivation: We need a repeatable way to track prompt-set level regressions across time windows (epochs) and a compact CI guard that prevents merges that materially degrade end-to-end quality for high-priority cohorts. This PR introduces an "epochal prompt-versioning" model for prompt sets plus a semantic-parity SLO gate that runs in pre-merge CI. What changed: 1) prompt_epoch manifest and tooling: a lightweight epoch manifest (manifest.py) and migration helper (migrate_epoch_tags.py) to tag and snapshot prompt-sets as epochs; supports automatic epoch creation via tag_current_prompts.sh. 2) semantic-parity metric: metrics/semantic_parity.py implements a hybrid score combining embedding cosine agreement, normalized token-level agreement, and a calibrated penalty for hallucination-like divergences. Score is cohort-aware and returns confidence intervals using bootstrap resampling. 3) CI pre-merge SLO gate: ci/premerge_slo_gate.yml runs a compact smoke eval that samples representative items from high_priority_cohorts.json, computes semantic-parity vs the pinned baseline epoch, and fails the job when the 3-day rolling mean parity drop for any high-priority cohort exceeds 2.5% (configurable). 4) Backfill & orchestration: orchestrator/backfill_runner.py can backfill historical epochs to compute trend signals for the first run and seed baselines; runner modifications wire the new scorer into the standard eval pipeline. 5) Tests & fixtures: new unit tests and synthetic regression fixtures to exercise boundary conditions (minor wording drift, paraphrase-preserving changes, and tokenization-induced mismatches). 6) Docs: docs/prompt_epoching.md documents processes for creating epochs, rollback guidance, and governance for pinned baselines. How it works: The semantic-parity scorer uses a two-stage pipeline: cheap embedding similarity to filter likely-paraphrase matches, then token-aligned normalized agreement with an edit-distance-derived gap penalty; results are bootstrapped to produce CI-level bounds per cohort. The pre-merge CI runs the smoke eval with a 50-example stratified sample per high-priority cohort (configurable), computes the cohort-wise parity delta, and applies a configurable smoothing window before gating. Backfill can be run in a longer job to populate historical baselines. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind a feature flag: start with 'dry-run' CI behavior (warnings only) for one week, then promote to soft-fail (block merge but auto-create incident draft) for the next week, and finally enforce hard-fail gating for the high-priority cohort set. Migration: a migration helper tags the current prompt set as epoch v1; operators can run migrate_epoch_tags.py --backfill to populate historic baselines. Testing notes: unit tests added and a local smoke harness included; run ./scripts/run_local_smoke.sh --cohort high_priority to reproduce. Related tickets: ENG-3421 implemented the epoch model; PM-118 defines the SLO thresholds; SUP-9442 requested a pre-merge guard after a recent prompt regression incident. Backwards compatibility: existing eval APIs unchanged; new epoch manifest lives under eval-harness/prompt_epoch and is opt-in. Security/privacy: no training data are exported; embeddings are computed transiently with caching disabled in CI. CI: initial runs caught a flaky bootstrap seed; tests fixed by seeding and a 5-retry test harness. This PR is intentionally conservative in its gating thresholds and ships with an operator override to bypass gating during urgent rollouts.
Liam Carter (reviewer): This looks good overall. Two requests: make the cohort sample size configurable from defaults.yaml and add a short-circuit when the cohort sample returns fewer than N items so CI doesn't randomly fail.
Aisha Roy (author): Good catch — added cohort sample config to defaults.yaml and short-circuit logic in bench/cohort_sample_selector.py. Updated tests to cover small-cohort fallback.
Mariana Ortiz (reviewer): The hybrid metric is clever but I'd like a short doc blurb on calibration methodology and an example where embedding similarity disagrees with token agreement. Please add to metrics/README.md.
Aisha Roy (author): Added calibration notes and an example in metrics/README.md. Also included a small diagnostic plot generator for offline inspection.
Ethan Blake (reviewer): CI job is heavier than typical pre-merge checks. Can we ensure it reuses cached embeddings and times out gracefully?
Aisha Roy (author): CI uses a small no-cache mode by default to avoid stale results, but premerge_slo_gate.yml will run in ephemeral mode with a 90s timeout per cohort; backfill uses cache-enabled longer runs. Added explicit timeouts and retry logic.
Mariana Ortiz: Approved after docs and sample-size fix.
Liam Carter: Approved. Minor nit resolved in a follow-up patch.

Add a stratified semantic baseline comparator and a lightweight CI hook that computes per-stratum delta with adaptive slack scaling. Motivation: existing regression gates operate on coarse aggregates and miss regressions that are localized to semantic strata (e.g., intent clusters and domain slices). This PR introduces a semantic clustering step, an importance-weighted delta comparator, and a CI hook that can be configured to quarantine prompt-sets that exceed stratified thresholds. The implementation is intended to be low-latency and safe to run on CI workers. Key behaviors: (1) builds semantic clusters using an ensemble embedding/UMAP downsample strategy, (2) computes per-cluster baseline distributions and a weighted composite delta, (3) applies a progressive quarantine policy that escalates from WARN -> QUARANTINE -> FAIL based on delta magnitude and sample size, (4) emits structured annotations consumed by the eval dashboard for follow-up triage. This PR also includes a small test harness for synthetic strata and guidance docs for adding new strata definitions in repo. Checklist: add unit tests, integration smoke in CI, docs, add Linear ticket reference, update changelog. Related Linear: ENG-12044. This description is intentionally consolidated into a single continuous field for the PR artifact.
--- a/eval_harness/hooks/stratified_semantic_comparator.py
+++ b/eval_harness/hooks/stratified_semantic_comparator.py
@@ def compute_delta(baseline, current):
-    # previous coarse comparator
-    return simple_mean_diff(baseline, current)
+    # stratified comparator: compute per-cluster deltas and weight by cluster mass
+    deltas = [cluster_delta(b, c) for b, c in zip(baseline.clusters, current.clusters)]
+    weights = [max(1, c.count) for c in current.clusters]
+    return weighted_sum(deltas, weights)
--- a/ci/pipeline/eval_comparator_stage.yml
+++ b/ci/pipeline/eval_comparator_stage.yml
@@
-  - name: run-eval-gates
-    script: run_eval_gates.sh
+  - name: run-stratified-semantic-comparator
+    script: python -m eval_harness.ci.hooks.stratified_comparator_runner --config ci/configs/stratified_comparator.yml
Unit tests cover semantic clustering determinism with fixed seed, cluster persistence, and weighted delta logic. Integration smoke verifies the CI stage runs under 90s on standard runner with default downsample. Synthetic E2E validates quarantine escalation path using a seeded failure injection.
Added stratified semantic comparator CI hook: enables per-stratum regression detection and progressive quarantine policy. Configurable downsample and minimum sample safeguards. Requires dashboard annotation consumer to be available to fully leverage quarantine workflow.
When enabling this hook in org CI, start with 'warn-only' mode for 2 weeks and monitor quarantine annotations in the eval dashboard. Recommended defaults: n_sample=500, min_sample=50, warn_delta=0.08, quarantine_delta=0.18. If running on limited CI machines, set downsample=200 to reduce memory footprint.
Arjun Patel: Positive overall; asked for clarification on cluster stability across seed changes and recommended persisting cluster prototypes to avoid noisy reassignments.
Sofia Martinez: Replied with plan to persist cluster centroids and added an "anchor snapshot" step before CI runs; bumped tests to assert centroid persistence semantics.
Maya Chen: Flagged potential cost implications for running UMAP on large prompt-sets in CI and suggested an opt-in downsample parameter; requested explicit gating when sample size < 30 to avoid unreliable statistics.
Sofia Martinez: Added downsample and minimum-sample safeguards; updated docs with recommended default settings for CI (n_sample=500, min_sample=50).
Diego Ramirez: Approved after seeing improved test coverage and smoke-run results; left a note to follow up with dashboard integration for triage annotations.
CI Bot: 2/5 checks failed on first run (unit tests flaky). After rerun, all checks passed.
