Motivation: Large prompt sets often hide concentrated regressions that are diluted by overall aggregate metrics. This PR adds a CI hook that clusters queries by semantic similarity, computes cluster-level regression signals, and applies an adaptive-anchor reweighting policy so noisy or overly-large clusters cannot mask meaningful failures. Design summary: 1) query_clusterer module computes embedding-based clusters using existing embedder + configurable clustering algorithm (kmeans or agglomerative with dynamic cluster count), 2) cluster_anchor_store keeps deterministic anchor examples per cluster and maintains historical baselines, 3) cluster_shield_hook runs as part of the eval CI stage, comparing current cluster metrics (accuracy/semantic-f1/custom scores) to historical baselines with an outlier-aware p-value test, 4) when a cluster exceeds thresholds the hook triggers a targeted rerun on that cluster with cross-seed sampling, and 5) an adaptive-anchor reweighter adjusts cluster contributions to the global SLO to avoid dominance by large low-variance clusters. Integration: adds a new GitHub Actions job eval/clustered-regression that runs after the baseline eval job, exposes config via eval_harness.yaml under "cluster_shield" with parameters: cluster_algo, min_cluster_size, baseline_window_days, pvalue_threshold, rerun_backoff. The hook is backward-compatible: disabled by default and can be enabled per-repo or per-prompt-set. Implementation notes: - Uses existing lightweight embedding cache to avoid recomputing embeddings for large prompt-sets. - Deterministic seeding for clustering to ensure reproducible CI behavior. - Adds a small synthetic benchmark (benchmarks/cluster-demo.jsonl) used by unit tests to exercise edge clusters. - Provides metrics: cluster_count, clusters_flagged, reruns_triggered, per-cluster-delta. Risk & mitigation: additional CPU/embedding cost on CI (~+1.2s per 1000 queries for small datasets) but clustering is limited to a configurable sample size and cached artifacts are uploaded between CI steps. The rerun path uses exponential backoff and rate-limits to avoid CI storms. Backwards compatibility: no breaking changes; default disabled. Documentation: added docs/ci/clustering_regression.md and updated README with configuration examples. Testing: unit tests and an integration smoke test added. See files_changed for specifics and conversation thread for review notes, fixes, and final approval.
Marco Liu (reviewer): Strong design; two asks: 1) make clustering seed deterministic across runs and 2) add a small-cpu fallback when embeddings are disabled in private deploys.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Addressed. Added deterministic seeding and a 'lightweight' lexical-cluster fallback when the embedder is unavailable; documented in clustering_regression.md.
Evan Park (reviewer): CI cost looks ok but please cap the default sample size and ensure logs are redact-safe (no raw user data).
Aisha Kapoor (author): Default sample capped at 2k queries; anchor store only keeps hashed indices, logs sanitized. Added test to assert no PII in uploaded artifacts.
Sofia Rinaldi (reviewer): Request a backoff on reruns to avoid repeated failures from flakiness. Also suggest exposing pvalue_threshold as env override.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Implemented exponential backoff with jitter and added env var override; added test for backoff behavior.
CI: initial run - lint failed (flake8 E231), unit tests passed. Author pushed fix. CI: rerun - all checks passed.
Marco Liu (reviewer): Approved after fixes. Evan approved. Sofia requested one final minor doc tweak which was applied. Maintainer merged with squash.

Add query-clustering CI hook that finds cluster-level regressions and triggers targeted reruns; introduces adaptive-anchor reweighting to improve failure localization. Disabled by default; opt-in via eval_harness.yaml. Includes docs and tests.

Motivation: intermittent, non-deterministic prompt-set regressions have been difficult to triage because changing request traffic mix amplifies or suppresses regressions. This PR introduces a seed-anchored baseline reconciler that pins a stable RNG seed and a compact canonical snapshot for each prompt-set cohort, plus a traffic-aware smoke sentinel that weights smoke-eval signals by recent production traffic distribution. The reconciler writes compact baseline artifacts to the artifact-store and exposes a reconcile command used by CI to produce a stable delta summary. The smoke sentinel is a CI hook that mirrors a small, weighted sample of recent traffic into the eval harness and gates PRs when traffic-weighted degradation exceeds configured thresholds. Key goals: 1) make regression signals reproducible across reruns, 2) reduce noise from rare-traffic outliers, 3) provide compact, actionable delta reports suitable for code reviewers. This change is opt-in via eval config flags and defaults to disabled for existing pipelines to avoid accidental gate flips. Implementation notes: light-weight reconciliation algorithm, deterministic seeding for batching and sampling, traffic-weighted scoring that normalizes by cohort frequency, and a compact delta report generator with per-prompt examples and token-level attribution hints. Related work: builds on ideas from ENG-7261 (stable-seed utilities) and complements existing anchor/replay features but focuses on traffic-weighted gating rather than strict anchor mirroring. Checklist: - [x] baseline snapshot API and serializer - [x] reconciler CLI with --artifact-path support - [x] CI hook and GitHub Actions workflow for traffic-weighted mirroring - [x] unit and integration tests - [x] documentation and runbook - [x] performance sanity checks to keep per-eval cost low Backwards compatibility: configuration is additive and disabled by default, no runtime changes to existing production instrumentation. Rollout: start with shadow runs on release branch, then enable gate for low-risk repos.
Leah Moreno (reviewer): This is a great direction for reducing noisy regressions. A couple of asks: (1) Can we ensure the baseline serializer is compact and contains checksums to detect drift? (2) Please add a short note about privacy for mirrored traffic.
Amir Navarro (author): Added checksum metadata and truncated example contexts to the serializer, and added an explicit privacy note in docs to redact PII before mirroring. See reconciler/stable_baseline.py changes.
Jasper Liu (reviewer): Tests look good but the traffic-weighting formula feels brittle for highly-skewed cohorts. Suggest adding a floor and cap to cohort weights and document the rationale. Also saw a lint error in uploader.py on the first CI run.
Amir Navarro (author): Implemented cap/floor at 0.01/0.5 in the weighting code and fixed linting issues. Added a short appendix in reconciliation.md explaining the tradeoffs.
Nina Patel (approver): Verified integration against a mirrored snapshot and the delta reporting was actionable. Approving pending green CI.

Adds a coordinator that runs multiple evaluation windows in parallel and surfaces epochal regressions with configurable grace windows; no breaking changes to public APIs; opt-in via config.
Motivation: Current CI evals treat a single sliding window which can make transient regressions or bursty noise trigger unnecessary rollbacks. This PR introduces a multi-window epochal eval coordinator that runs multiple overlapping evaluation windows (short, medium, long) in parallel and aggregates signals with a configurable epoch and grace policy to reduce false positives while preserving sensitivity to sustained regressions. Summary of changes: add coordinator orchestration layer, new multi-window aggregator algorithm, per-prompt epochal state store, a lightweight decision rule DSL for progressive gating, a CI hook that emits structured `epochal_signal` events, and tests + docs. Design notes: windows run concurrently and report weighted signals; short window has high sensitivity but low persistence, long window has low sensitivity but high persistence; coordinator exposes thresholds, decay, and quarantine timers via config; a grace window parameter defers automatic fail actions until a minimum epoch count is observed. Migration: existing single-window jobs remain unchanged until projects opt-in by setting `EVAL_COORDINATOR_MODE=multi-window` or adding the new `coordination` block to eval.yml. Backwards compatibility preserved for existing CI hooks. Testing: unit tests for aggregation math, integration test that runs seeded synthetic regressions across windows, end-to-end smoke in CI. Checklist: - implement aggregator and coordinator code; - add unit/integration tests; - add CI hook and event schema; - update docs and quickstart; - verify perf and tune default thresholds. Related: ENG-1287 (reduce false-positive rollbacks), ENG-1320 (epochal alerting UX).

Sonia Alvarez: Please add a migration step for teams that use custom CI hooks. Maya Chen: Added opt-in env flag and an example eval.yml with coordination block.
Liam O'Connor: Unit tests look good, but integration test flaked once in my run. Can we add deterministic seeding for the synthetic regression generator? Maya Chen: Added deterministic seed and re-ran; CI green.

Adds a sparse error annotator to reduce false-positive prompt-set regressions and a CI autorepair hook that attempts lightweight canonicalization on low-confidence failures. Improves gating stability and reduces noisy interrupts to rollouts.
Summary: This PR introduces a lightweight 'sparse error annotator' and an accompanying CI autorepair hook aimed at reducing noisy, low-density failures in prompt-set regression checks. The annotator detects when a regression signal is concentrated in very few prompts or is likely caused by brittle input formatting; the autorepair hook runs a set of deterministic canonicalizers on flagged examples and re-executes the failing tests in CI. If the example passes post-repair the check is quarantined as a probable flake instead of failing the entire job. Motivation: We saw recurring alerts in canary / smoke evals where 1-2 prompts per prompt-set caused CI failures that were later determined to be formatting or tokenization edge-cases. These false positives interrupt rollouts and cause unnecessary investigations. This change reduces noisiness while preserving sensitivity to real regressions.
Behavioral note: Autorepair runs only on low-confidence, low-density failures. High-density regressions still fail the gate.
Operational note: Quarantined prompt-sets are surfaced in the console under 'Eval -> Quarantines' and will be re-evaluated by scheduled backfills.
Risk: Over-aggressive canonicalization could hide real regressions; we intentionally kept repairs minimal (trim/normalize whitespace, punctuation normalization, simple date normalization) and require low annotator confidence before applying.
Mitigation: A monitoring alert triggers if repaired_pass_count / quarantine_count > 0.8 within a 24h window (indicates possible overfitting by repairs).
Added unit tests that exercise: high-density regression (should fail), single-example formatting flake (should be quarantined after autorepair), and confidence threshold boundaries.
Integration test in CI simulates a flake-class failure and validates quarantine + metric emission.
Ran a canary on internal prompt-sets for 48 hours — observed a 42% reduction in noisy CI failures for affected suites with no missed high-density regressions.
Manual review: product-quality team spot-checked 50 quarantined prompts; 44 were legitimate flakes (formatting/tokenization), 6 required human follow-up.
docs/eval-runbooks/quarantine-and-autorepair.md added with operational steps for triage and unquarantine flow.
Console UI: new lightweight note on quarantined prompt-sets and auto-suggested canonicalization applied (visible to SRE/product reviewers).

Motivation: We need a metrics surface that captures end-to-end sequence fidelity for prompt sets where small token-level perturbations lead to disproportionately large semantic regressions. Current prompt-level scalar checks (accuracy/EM/ROUGE) miss cases where sequence order, repeated subphrases, or token-insertion errors degrade downstream behavior. This PR adds a sequence-level fidelity evaluator plus a CI decision-layer that gates merges when fidelity regressions exceed statistically-derived thresholds.

What this change does: introduces a fidelity evaluator that computes an alignment-aware sequence similarity score (sequence-F1) combining Levenshtein alignment, soft-token embeddings similarity, and a novel penalty for out-of-order subsequence occurrences. The evaluator is implemented as a new module eval_harness.metrics.sequence_fidelity with a lightweight Cython-accelerated alignment util for large prompt sets. It ships with: 1) an offline baseline snapshot store and retention policy for historical score distributions; 2) a CI adapter that consumes nightly baselines and produces pass/fail decisions using a bootstrapped confidence interval and an adaptive tolerance calibrated per-prompt-cohort; 3) a small CLI to produce HTML diff reports for failed prompts to speed triage.

Backward compatibility: The default evaluator is opt-in (not replacing existing metrics) and can be enabled in project-level smoke/eval configs via a new key "sequence_fidelity". For organizations already gating on existing eval metrics, the CI adapter supports combined decision rules (AND/OR) so teams can adopt it incrementally.

Performance: The Cython alignment core improves throughput ~6x versus pure Python on typical prompt sets (5000 sequences, average length 80 tokens). Memory overhead is modest; the module streams batches and keeps a compact histogram of baselines.

Why this is important: We saw an internal incident where a model patch introduced an infrequent token-repeat pattern that created downstream hallucinations despite unchanged accuracy. Sequence-Fidelity surfaced the issue and would have prevented the rollout. The CI decision-layer allows enforcement of historical-stability SLOs without causing noise-driven blocking (bootstrap smoothing + cohort reweighting are used).

Rollout plan: Feature merged behind a feature-flag. Default CI behavior is opt-out; teams receive a summary report in nightly eval runs. We'll run 2 weeks of shadow-mode across key prompt sets, then recommend enabling hard gating for critical flows.

Notes and follow-ups: add a Prometheus-compatible export for the new histogram buckets (ENG-4790), and a docs page with interpretation guidelines and suggested thresholds for common product flows (ENG-4721).

Jonah: Add more unit tests for boundary cases (empty sequence, large repeat blocks). Eleni: Added tests for those cases and extended fixtures. Marco: Approving after tests pass. Context: As part of efforts to detect subtle quality regressions we observed in prompt cohorts that correlate with demographic and style axes, we need both a stable debiasing-aware signal and a way to flag sharp metric gradient changes that precede behavioral regressions. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) an eval-debiasing-oracle that computes cohort-aware adjusted scores and returns a single normalized 'debiased_delta' used by CI gates, and (2) a gradient-stability-adapter CI hook that computes per-metric gradient variance across prompt partitions and allows progressive soft-fail -> hard-block policies. Motivation: existing per-prompt SLOs can be noisy for small cohorts; debiasing oracle reduces noise by combining a lightweight reweight + calibration step while preserving sensitivity to meaningful shifts. The gradient-stability adapter helps catch brittle regressions where mean metric change is small but gradient variance increases (indicating divergent failure modes). This is a production-oriented change: added a fast smoke profile to keep CI latency low while preserving signal fidelity for main gates. Changes: - New module eval_harness/oracles/debiasing_oracle.py implementing reweighting, stratified bootstrap calibration, and an exported scoring shim compatible with existing eval orchestration. - New CI hook eval_harness/ci_hooks/gradient_stability_adapter.py that integrates into existing eval CI pipeline. The adapter supports config options: window_size, variance_threshold, soft_fail_ratio, quarantine_ttl. - Integration tests under tests/eval_oracles/test_debiasing_oracle.py and tests/ci_hooks/test_gradient_stability_adapter.py - New smoke profile: config/smoke_profiles/debiased-smoke.yaml - Docs: docs/eval/oracles/debiasing-oracle.md and docs/ci/gradient-stability-adapter.md - Example alert mapping and Linear automation in scripts/ci/linear_autoresponder.py Checklist: - [x] Implementation and unit tests - [x] Smoke profile added to CI matrix - [x] Docs and examples added - [x] Reviewed and addressed feedback from reviewers Risk: low-to-medium; new thresholds are conservative by default and require opt-in via project configuration. Rollout plan: merged behind feature flag in CI config; ops will enable for a subset of repositories for 2 weeks and monitor false positive rate. Related: Linear ENG-2345 (cohort regression guard), ENG-2399 (eval infra observability), SUP-1182 (customer-reported cohort drift).
- Add 'eval-debiasing-oracle' metric shim that computes per-cohort debiased scores and exposes a normalized delta for CI gating.
- Add 'gradient-stability-adapter' CI hook that tracks metric gradient variance between baseline and candidate and escalates regressions when instability exceeds thresholds.
- New smoke-eval profile 'debiased-smoke' for faster pre-merge checks.
- Docs: evaluation/ oracles and ci adapters documentation and config examples.
Evan Park: High level: I like the idea of reducing cohort noise, but can you clarify the assumptions of the reweighting? Is there a chance of masking a real regression if cohort sizes change dramatically?
Marta Kline: Reply: Good point — the oracle logs cohort cardinalities and exposes an 'effective_sample_factor' in telemetry; we also abort reweighting when any cohort has < 50 examples and fall back to raw scoring. Added tests for that case.

Motivation: Our existing CI smokechecks treat every prompt in a prompt-set equally which leads to noisy failures when a small subset of high-variance prompts trigger alerts. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) Adaptive Fidelity Curator: a CI hook that assigns per-prompt fidelity weights using an exponential-moving-average of recent evaluation scores and token-level stability signals, and exposes a soft-fail gating policy that scales alert severity by weighted SLO violations; (2) Compact Failure Summarizer: a post-failure analyzer that clusters failing examples by semantic/diff similarity, extracts exemplars, and produces a one-page failure summary with suggested roll-back scope (prompt IDs or prompt-cohort) for on-call triage. Changes in this PR are intended to reduce noisy alerts, prioritize high-impact regressions, and provide engineers with an immediate, digestible failure digest. Checklist: - [x] Implement Adaptive Fidelity Curator hook with EWMA weighting and cohort windowing - [x] Implement Compact Failure Summarizer using hierarchical clustering + diff compression - [x] Unit tests for weighting, gating, and summarizer outputs - [x] Add e2e smoke CI job wiring + sample prompt-set - [x] Update docs/ci_hooks.md and examples - [x] Add backfill job to compute initial fidelity baselines for existing prompt-sets - [x] Performance benchmarks for hook overhead (avg + p95 latency) Design notes: The curator maintains a sliding window of the last N CI runs per prompt (configurable; default N=30). For each prompt we compute a fidelity score f in [0,1] combining: normalized metric delta (metric-specific, e.g., exact-match/ROUGE) and token-stability score (1 - normalized edit distance across model outputs). We then compute an EWMA: w_t = alpha * f_t + (1-alpha) * w_{t-1}, alpha configurable per workspace. Per-prompt weights are normalized across the prompt-set and used to compute a weighted SLO breach score. Gate policy supports: hard-fail on weighted breach > T_hard, soft-fail (notify but don't block) on T_soft < weighted breach < T_hard, and auto-escalation if breach persists for M consecutive runs. Compact Failure Summarizer works after a CI failure: it vectorizes failing outputs using the eval-harness sentence-embedder (existing infra), clusters with average-linkage, selects top-k exemplars per cluster (k configurable), and produces a markdown summary with cluster descriptions, representative diffs, frequency, and a suggested scope for rollback. Small on-disk summarizer sample (embedded in tests) compresses diffs with a 3-line context window to keep summaries brief. Backfill: a job to run the curator against historical eval traces to seed initial weights. It runs as a separate scheduled job and writes fidelity baselines to the prompt-set metadata store. Safety and opt-outs: hooks are opt-in per-repo/prompt-set and respect existing ignore-lists and label overrides. Notably this PR does not change any default hard-blocking behavior unless the workspace enables weighted gating. Related work: ENG-4219 (fidelity-weighting design doc), ENG-4302 (CI alert noise audit). Commits summary: - 9a3b2c1 implement adaptive fidelity curator core with ewma and windowing - f4d2a10 add compact failure summarizer and clustering util - b7e5c33 wire hook into ci-pipeline and add e2e smoke job - c1f0a9d add backfill job + migration to write baseline weights - 2e8b5f7 tests: unit + integration + perf harness - 3d4c2b1 docs: ci_hooks.md + examples + config reference - a7c9e88 linting and minor refactors Files changed (high-level): - src/hooks/adaptive_fidelity.py - src/hooks/compact_failure_summarizer.py - src/ci/pipelines/weighted_eval_pipeline.yaml - scripts/backfill/seed_fidelity_baselines.py - tests/unit/test_adaptive_fidelity.py - tests/integration/test_weighted_gate_e2e.py - docs/ci_hooks.md Notes on implementation: adaptive_fidelity.py is ~420 lines; core algorithm is implemented with a small in-memory ring buffer and a pluggable metric adapter so new metrics can be added per-prompt-set. The weighted gate adds ~20ms p95 overhead to the existing smokecheck run (measured in perf harness) and is configurable to run in a 'dry-run' mode which computes weights and logs decisions without affecting CI outcomes. Example gating config snippet included in docs (simplified): "gate: { mode: weighted, alpha: 0.15, window: 30, thresholds: { soft: 0.08, hard: 0.18 }, escalation_runs: 3 }" Tests and CI: Unit tests added for EWMA math, normalization, and cluster exemplar selection. Integration test simulates a prompt-set with a mix of flaky/high-variance prompts and validates that the weighted gate reduces false-positive hard-fails by ~42% in the simulated workload. Performance test asserts the hook adds <50ms median overhead under default config. Logging and telemetry: curator emits per-run aggregated metrics (fidelity_weight_distribution, weighted_breach_score, gate_decision) to the existing metric namespace eval.harness.curator. Summarizer logs cluster counts and exemplar IDs to the event store for postmortem linking. Docs: docs/ci_hooks.md updated with configuration, opt-in instructions, and examples for rollout. Migration/backfill: seed_fidelity_baselines.py will be run once by infra after merging; it includes a dry-run mode to preview changes. Rollout plan: - Week 0: merge to main, feature flag off - Week 1: enable dry-run for all workspaces to gather baselines - Week 2: opt-in pilot on two high-volume prompt-sets - Week 4: measure alert noise reduction and toggle weighted gating on by default for pilot repos if results are positive Rollout risks and mitigations: risk: underweighted rare but critical prompts may be deprioritized. mitigation: we add an override list that marks prompts as critical and pins their weight above a floor. risk: clustering could group distinct failure modes together. mitigation: summarizer exposes cluster isolation metrics and a human-in-the-loop re-cluster button in the failure UI. Response: "Added escalation test and added prompt_set_id tag to emitted metrics (commit 2e8b5f7)." - Liam O'Connor: "CI flake: integration job timed out once; please ensure smoke job has retry=2." Response: "Increased job retries and added stronger timeouts to the e2e harness (commit b7e5c33)." Motivation: Some prompt-sets show non-deterministic score variance across interleaved few-shot orderings and sampling seeds which can cause flaky CI failures or missed regressions. This PR introduces an interleaved-shot consistency validator plus a fuzzy-threshold CI hook that smooths tiny, non-actionable deltas while still surfacing meaningful regressions. Design summary: 1) interleaved-shot validator runs configurable permutations of k-shot examples (interleaved ordering) and computes a pairwise consistency score distribution for each prompt in a set; 2) fuzzy-threshold hook aggregates prompt-level distributions into cohort-level statistics and applies a tunable soft-threshold with an exponential smoothing window so transient noise does not fail CI; 3) exposes knobs for sample count, permutation strategy, alpha for smoothing, and minimum effect size. Implementation details: added a new validator module eval_harness/validators/interleaved_shot.py that implements permutation sampling and consistency metrics, added a compact consistency metric to eval_harness/metrics/consistency_metric.py, and added a CI adapter ci/hooks/fuzzy_threshold_adapter.py that integrates with existing eval-orchestration state machine. Tests and docs: unit tests and a smoke suite were added under eval_harness/tests, and docs/quality_gates.md updated with usage examples and rollout guidance. Rollout plan: default hook disabled; enable as an opt-in gate for canary branches and then roll to baseline projects after two weeks of stability. Why this is different: instead of hard binary thresholds this approach models intra-prompt ordering variance explicitly and uses a probabilistic smoothing gate to reduce noisy CI churn while preserving signal fidelity. Backward compatibility: config defaults are conservative to avoid changing existing gate behavior. Checklist: [x] validator implemented, [x] CI adapter wired into pipeline, [x] unit + smoke tests, [x] docs updated, [x] Linear ticket linked. Motivation: We intermittently see downstream regressions when models change but our prompt sets are brittle to surface-level paraphrases. This PR introduces a lightweight synthetic paraphrase prober and a consistency SLO enforcer that runs as a CI hook. The prober generates paraphrase variants for targeted prompt sets, scores the model's outputs for semantic and ranking stability, and raises a quality gate if a defined per-prompt consistency threshold is violated. Summary of changes: - New module hooks/paraphrase_prober.py: generates paraphrases (back-translation + template perturbations), deduplicates variants, and produces a canonical probe bundle. - New module hooks/consistency_slo.py: scoring and threshold enforcement logic; supports token-edit-distance, embedding-cosine stability, and top-k rank-stability. - CI hook integration .github/workflows/probe-ci.yml that runs fast probes for PRs touching prompt sets or evaluation code. - Tests: tests/test_paraprobe.py, tests/test_consistency_slo.py with deterministic seeds and mocked model API. - Small infra: scripts/probe_cache.py (local caching of generated paraphrases to keep CI cost low) and docs/PROBES.md describing the SLO contract. Design highlights: - Probes are parameterized: sample_size, paraphrase_engine (back-translate or synonym-swap), similarity_metric, and slo_thresholds per cohort. - Scoring: an aggregated consistency score is computed by combining normalized rank-stability (50%), embedding similarity (30%), and normalized token-edit stability (20%). Thresholds are configurable per-prompt-set in eval-configs/consistency-policies.yaml. - Fast-path CI: The workflow does a single-shot cached probe run (default 50 paraphrases across a small representative sample) to keep runtime under 5 minutes for most PRs. - Fallback: On borderline failures the hook posts a diagnostic artifact (HTML with examples) and opens an internal issue template for triage. Checklist: - [x] Prober core implementation - [x] CI workflow and caching - [x] Unit tests and synthetic model mocks - [x] Docs and runbook - [x] Backwards-compatible configs Rollout plan: Feature gated behind eval.probes.enabled; gradual opt-in for critical prompt-sets first (search, summarization, billing messages). If the hook rejects a PR, logs include sample failures and a direct link to re-run with relaxed thresholds locally. Tests and CI: Unit tests cover scoring math, sampling determinism, and caching. Integration smoke in CI uses a lightweight mocked model that returns deterministic paraphrase-preserving outputs; full model-run is gated to nightly runs to avoid quota consumption. Risk and mitigation: False positives from paraphrase generator noise — mitigated by caching, deterministic seeds, and requiring >1 metric to fall below threshold before gating. Performance: Adds ~2-5 minutes to affected PRs; caching reduces repeated cost. Commit summary: - 1a2b3c: add paraphrase prober and paraphrase cache - 2b3c4d: add consistency SLO enforcer and policy config - 3c4d5e: CI workflow and probe artifact publishing - 4d5e6f: unit tests and mocks - 5e6f7g: docs and runbook Examples of changed files (high-level): - hooks/paraphrase_prober.py: new class ParaphraseProber(gen_engine, dedupe=True) with generate(), batch_apply() - hooks/consistency_slo.py: new function evaluate_consistency(bundle, model_client, policy) - .github/workflows/probe-ci.yml: adds conditional probe job triggered on paths: 'eval-configs/**', 'prompts/**', 'hooks/**' - eval-configs/consistency-policies.yaml: policy schema and default thresholds - tests/test_paraprobe.py: unit tests and fixtures - scripts/probe_cache.py: local cache helper - docs/PROBES.md: user-facing guidance How to review: Focus on the scoring math in consistency_slo.py, the policy schema, and the CI performance characteristics. The paraphrase generator is intentionally shallow (back-translate via a small translation model or synonym-swap) to keep noise low. Related work: This complements existing perturbation and fuzz probes but emphasizes paraphrase invariance and per-prompt SLO enforcement. Links: Linear ENG-2145, internal runbook link in docs.

Hannah Li: 'Edge case: paraphrase generator may introduce lexical drift that creates false negatives. Recommend a minimum embedding similarity check.' payload.body:
Context and motivation:
We observed intermittent regressions where single-turn metrics (e.g. per-turn BLEU/EM) passed, but multi-turn sequence coherence dropped for a small subset of prompt-sets used in chat flows. These failures are often noisy and surface only at scale, leading to slow rollbacks or undetected user-impacting regressions. ENG-8124 asked for a narrow, low-friction mechanism to: 1) detect sequence-level coherence regressions, 2) surface those in CI with an actionable signal, and 3) avoid noisy hard-blocks during early detection.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a new scorer pipeline module: seq_coherence_delta. The scorer computes a cohesion score by aggregating turn-level semantic similarity and discourse-level entailment signals across multi-turn prompt samples. The output is a normalized delta vs baseline and a per-cohort severity tag.
- Adds CI hook: traffic-shepherd. The hook runs lightweight shadowed evaluation on a sampled traffic window and, on repeated flagging, reduces promotion rate for the head branch (canary-style traffic cap) rather than outright failing the pipeline.
- Plumbs the scorer into the eval orchestration: a new evaluation task type (seq-coherence-check) and an optional config flag in eval-configs to opt a prompt-set into sequence-aware checks.
- Adds test coverage and a small synthetic prompt-set generator for deterministic unit tests.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- The seq_coherence_delta scorer is intentionally conservative: it prioritizes precision over recall to keep false positives low. Score thresholds are configurable per-cohort and stored as metadata in the prompt-set manifest.
- The traffic-shepherd hook implements a 3-run grace window: only after 3 consecutive CI runs with severity >= medium does it escalate to a hard-fail block. This reduces churn from flakey signals.
- We avoided adding heavy external dependencies; the discourse entailment model is a distilled transformer baked into the eval-harness artifacts and quantized to keep CI runtime modest.

Commits (high level):
- initial: add seq_coherence_delta scorer and unit tests
- add: traffic-shepherd CI hook + config surface
- fix: tune thresholds and address flake in synthetic generator
- docs: update eval-config and CONTRIBUTING with opt-in instructions

Backward compatibility and opt-in path:

payload.body:
Motivation: We've had recurring incidents where a small prompt tweak in a PR produced outsized regressions for a narrow but critical slice of prompt-sets. Existing CI smokechecks flag macro regressions but provide little signal about which prompts, tokens, or candidate edits are most influential. This PR adds an 'influence matrix' eval hook that attributes per-prompt and per-perturbation influence on aggregate metrics, and a lightweight rollback scorer that suggests the smallest prompt change(s) that would return metrics to baseline.

What this does: Implements an eval hook that runs alongside existing regression checks. For each prompt-set it computes an influence score per prompt and per change vector using a randomized leave-k-out approximation (bounded sampling plus importance-weighting) and aggregates into an influence matrix (prompt x perturbation). The CI adapter consumes aggregated scores and will soft-block PRs that exceed a configurable impact threshold, surface a ranked list of top-k harmful prompts in the PR UI, and attach a rollback_scorer report with candidate minimal edits (text span revert or constraint relaxations) with estimated delta impact.

Design notes: The algorithm favors speed and interpretability over exact Shapley values; we approximate contribution via stratified sampling and an anchored baseline. Influence values are normalized per-metric and can be weighted by metric severity (e.g., hallucination > BLEU-like). The rollback scorer uses greedy local search over candidate revert spans and prompt parameter toggles (system message, temperature hints) to propose edits with confidence bands.

Backward compatibility: Hook is opt-in per-eval-job via job config and defaults to disabled for long-running production backfills. When enabled it adds a bounded extra eval cost (~10-30% depending on cohort size). The hook exposes tunables: sample_budget, top_k_reports, soft_block_threshold, metric_weights.

Files changed: See files_changed field for a concise list.

Related: ENG-2319 (detect high-impact prompt regressions ahead of rollout), PM-412 (UI work to display ranked prompt influence in PR).
Asha: "This is a great direction—two questions: can we bound worst-case CI time, and do we risk noisy hints for low-traffic prompts?" Elena: "Bounded sampling with sample_budget defaults to 200 per-cohort; we've added an early-exit if variance is under threshold to save cycles. Low-traffic prompts are de-emphasized via metric_weights and an exposure floor so they don't dominate."
Marco: "Can the rollback_scorer propose edits that violate safety policies?" Elena: "Rollback candidates are restricted to reverting changes present in the PR diff or toggling non-content parameters; we also run the existing safety linter over proposed edits and drop any candidate that fails."
Priya: "Will this integrate with the console UI for 'top harmful prompts'?" Elena: "Yes, report schema was coordinated with PM-412; each entry includes score, sample context, and suggested edit."
Changes after review: adjusted default sample_budget to 200, added integration test that runs on small real-world cohort, added an explicit opt-in flag and improved report schema versioning.
Checks run: python unit tests (pytest), lint (ruff + mypy), small integration eval (runs influence hook on trimmed cohort), docker build of eval image, GH Action artifact upload. Observations: initial run failed due to nondeterministic sampling seed in tests; fixed by seeding sampler in tests and adding variance-tolerant assertions. Final status: all checks passed on rerun (2026-02-24).
Merged via squash by Asha Singh on 2026-02-24. Merge commit includes concise changelog: introduce influence-matrix eval hook + rollback scorer + CI action + docs. Changelog entry added to release-notes draft for 0.54.0. No hotfixes required post-merge.
- New eval hook: Influence Matrix (opt-in) — attributes per-prompt/per-perturbation impact on eval metrics and surfaces top harmful prompts.
- Rollback Scorer — suggests minimal prompt edits to recover baseline metrics and emits candidate patches for review.
- CI Action: influence_evaluator — integrates with PR checks and uploads JSON reports for Console UI.
Notes: Hook is opt-in and has tunables to control cost and sensitivity.
Ops: when enabling for larger backfills set sample_budget conservatively and monitor eval runtime. New metrics exported: eval.influence.samples, eval.influence.top_prompt_score, eval.rollback.candidate_count. Add alert for eval.influence.top_prompt_score > 0.6 on canaries.

payload.body:
Motivation: Current prompt-set regression checks sample uniformly from test pools and often underrepresent semantically rare but important cohorts. This PR introduces a semantically-balanced probe that samples prompts proportional to cluster rarity (via embedding clusters) and a CI-side suppressor that reduces noisy flakiness alerts from low-confidence cohorts. The goal is to improve signal-to-noise in CI alerts while preserving sensitivity to real regressions.

What this PR does: Adds a new probe (sem_balance_probe) and a CI adapter hook (noise_suppressor) that together provide: 1) embedding-based clustering of prompt sets with configurable cluster granularity; 2) stratified sampling so each CI run includes a fixed quota from each cluster, with oversampling of rare clusters; 3) a dynamic quorum scoring mechanism that requires multiple independent failure modes (semantic cluster-level Delta + per-prompt regression) before raising a hard CI failure; 4) an adaptive suppressor that converts low-confidence cluster blips into soft alerts with an explanatory tag and a suggested backfill command for escalation; 5) telemetry hooks to surface cohort-level metrics in Redwood Console.

Implementation notes: The probe uses existing sentence-transformer embeddings from eval-harness, then applies mini-batch k-means with an autoscale option keyed to prompt-set size. The cluster IDs are cached and pinned per test run via a small metadata blob stored alongside the prompt-set snapshot to ensure determinism across reruns. Quorum scoring is computed as a weighted sum of (cluster-level mean delta, proportion of prompts in cluster failing threshold, historical volatility) with tunable thresholds via config. The suppressor includes a whitelist for high-priority prompt tags and an opt-out label for teams that want strict fail-fast behavior.

Testing and verification: Unit tests for clustering edge cases and deterministic caching. Integration smoke runs against three internal prompt-sets (chat-assistant, summarization, rerank) with synthetic regressions injected to validate quorum behavior. CI matrix includes python 3.10 and 3.11 runners. Performance: end-to-end probe adds ~1.2s overhead per 1000 prompt-set entries when embeddings are cached; initial runs show a 38% reduction in flaky CI failures (measured on historical CI flake corpus).

Things to watch / follow-ups: 1) Backfill job to recompute clusters for large historical prompt archives (tracked in linked_linear ENG-9412). 2) UX: expose cluster breakdown and suppressor decisions in the eval report UI (follow-up PR planned). 3) Investigate replacing k-means with hierarchical clustering for very long-tail prompt distributions.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration smoke runs - [x] Metrics emitted to telemetry - [x] Docs snippet in ci-hooks.md - [x] Reviewed and approved by reviewers

Related: This complements existing cohort and drift detectors but focuses on sampling strategy and suppressing transient noise rather than detecting trend drift.
Alex Chen: Can you add a regression test where cluster assignments change slightly between runs? Concern about non-deterministic k-means affecting flakiness.
Author (Priya): Added deterministic seeding and a small cache blob to pin cluster IDs per prompt-set snapshot; see cluster_cache.py commit.
Morgan Lee: The quorum weights look sensible, but please expose them as runtime flags to make tuning easier in staging.
Author (Priya): Exposed weights in sem_balance_config.yaml and added docs describing default values and guidance.
Diego Alvarez: Suggest we add an opt-out label at the test-suite level for strict teams; otherwise this might hide real regressions for safety-critical flows.
Author (Priya): Added opt-out label mechanism and unit tests covering label behavior.

payload.body:
Adds a CI hook that estimates semantic impact of prompt set changes and optionally gates merges when high-risk drift is detected. Backwards compatible; opt-in via eval-hooks config.
Context and motivation: Recently several prompt-set updates caused subtle regressions in downstream tasks even when token-level metrics barely moved. This PR introduces a semantically-weighted change-impact estimator CI hook that approximates the downstream risk of prompt changes by scoring semantic shifts across a prioritized probe set and mapping those shifts to historical regression likelihoods. Design summary: the hook computes embeddings for before/after prompt variants, clusters semantically-similar changes, weighs clusters by historical sensitivity (learned from a small labeled corpus of past regressions), and outputs a single impact score plus per-cohort explanations. The hook can be configured to soft-fail (annotate & block merge with warning) or hard-gate (fail CI) based on thresholds stored in eval-hooks.yaml. This behavior is opt-in per-repo via the ci/configs/eval-hooks.yaml toggles. Checklist and acceptance criteria: - Add deterministic unit tests for embedding diffs and cluster weighting - Add lightweight integration test that runs the hook against a small synthetic prompt delta - Document configuration knobs and recommended thresholds in docs/ci/semantic-impact.md - Include a fallback path that degrades to token-delta heuristic if embedding service is unreachable Commits (summary): - c1f9a2c: initial estimator implementation with clustering and weighting logic - 2b4e7d1: add CI hook shim and entrypoint, config parsing - e3d5b8f: tests for cluster stability and sensitivity-mapping - 7a2f1b0: docs and threshold guidance, update eval-hooks.yaml example - 9d8c0a4: fix flaky test by seeding random generator and add telemetry events Changed areas (high level): - eval_harness/hooks/semantic_impact_estimator.py: core estimator and CI entrypoint - eval_harness/tests/test_semantic_impact_estimator.py: unit + integration tests - ci/configs/eval-hooks.yaml: example config and default thresholds - docs/ci/semantic-impact.md: design notes, tuning guide, operational runbook - eval_harness/telemetry/emitters.py: add lightweight event hooks for impact telemetry - scripts/benchmarks/semantic-impact-smoke.py: local smoke runner Review conversation (high level timeline): - Diego Ramos (reviewer): "Nice shape. Can you clarify how the sensitivity weights are computed and persisted?" - Asha (author): "Added a detailed section in docs/ci/semantic-impact.md and included a small serialized baseline mapping under eval_harness/testdata/; weight computation is a simple logistic regression trained on historical diffs, re-trainable via make targets." - Linus Zhang (reviewer): "Concern: embedding calls could add CI flakiness. Suggest a deterministic fallback and caching of embeddings for identical prompts." - Asha: "Agree; implemented a cache layer with TTL and a fallback to token-delta heuristic; added tests to prove determinism when the embedding client returns repeated results." - Sofia Patel (approver): "Integration tests look solid, and the gating is opt-in which reduces risk. Approved after CI fix." CI history and outcome: - Initial run: lint failed (unused import) - Second run: lint/pass, unit tests flaky (timeout on external embedding mock) - Third run: added mock timeout handling, all tests passed; full CI green. Merge details: merged via squash on 2026-02-24 by Asha Menon. Post-merge notes: telemetry events emitted to team-dashboard under metric name eval.semantic_impact. Follow-up actions: - (ENG-3421) schedule a short experiment to calibrate thresholds on three prod prompt sets - Add a periodic backfill job to compute sensitivity weights from later regression labels
Diego Ramos: Nice shape. Can you clarify how the sensitivity weights are computed and persisted?
Asha Menon: Added docs and a small serialized baseline mapping under eval_harness/testdata/; weight computation is a logistic regression trained on historical diffs.
Linus Zhang: Suggest deterministic fallback and caching of embeddings to avoid CI flakiness.
Asha Menon: Implemented cache layer with TTL and token-delta fallback; added tests.

payload.body:
Motivation: Some prompt-set regressions we observe are intermittent and tied to recent temporal shifts in training data or model weights. Existing cohort/anchor approaches flag regressions but often require manual baseline selection or suffer from noise when the underlying distribution evolves. This PR adds a Per-Prompt Temporal Baseline (PTB) probe that maintains short- and long-window baselines per prompt, a drift-aware CI gate that reasons about recent baseline movement before failing a job, and a lightweight counterfactual replayer used to prioritize regressions for human review.

Design summary: The PTB probe (eval_harness.probes.ptb_probe) computes exponentially weighted aggregates (EWMA) of configured metrics per prompt across two windows: short (default 1d) and long (default 30d). The probe exposes three signals: absolute delta (short vs long), variance ratio, and a stability score combining token-level variance and aggregated metric delta. The CI gate (ci/hooks/ptb_gate.py) uses these signals to decide fail/soft-fail behavior: if absolute delta exceeds the hard threshold we fail; if delta is between soft and hard thresholds we emit a soft-fail with attached diagnoses and optionally enqueue counterfactual replays.

Counterfactual replayer: A new lightweight replayer (eval_harness.tools.counterfactual_replayer) can replay a small, latency-bounded subset of sampled historical inputs against the PR head model variant and against a pinned stable model to produce a prioritized list of likely regressions. The replayer is intentionally cheap (bounded tokens and sample size) so it can run in CI without blowing budgets. It includes deterministic seeding options for reproducibility.

APIs and config: Introduces a new probe registration entry in probes/registry.yaml with tunable params (short_window, long_window, ewma_alpha, soft_threshold, hard_threshold, replay_budget). CI integration exposes these flags via .github/workflows/eval.yml as optional job inputs. Default gate behavior is non-blocking (soft-fail) for self-serve runs; for release branches the gate is enabled as hard-fail.

Testing and verification: Added unit tests covering EWMA convergence, signal thresholds, and replayer determinism (tests/test_ptb_probe.py). Added an integration smoke job in ci/integration/ptb_smoke.yml that runs the probe on a synthetic prompt set and validates gating behavior. Local benchmarks show the replayer adds ~8% CI runtime under the default replay_budget=50 samples.

Rollout plan: Start with opt-in on main via a feature flag (env PTB_GATE_MODE=soft). After two weeks of telemetry (false-positive rate, queue depth, latency) we plan to flip the default to hard for release branches only and surface auto-created prioritized tickets in Linear for prompts with persistent hard-fail signals.

Migration notes: No breaking changes to existing probe interfaces. Existing registries will pick up the PTB probe by default but the gate remains opt-in. See docs/eval/ptb.md for configuration and troubleshooting.

Related: Linear ENG-1984 (per-prompt stability monitoring), PM-422 (release gate automation). Support ticket SUP-6123 provided customer repro prompting this work.
Ethan Park: Looks good overall. Can you justify the default EWMA alpha choices and where the numbers came from?
Maya Chen: Added comment and unit test demonstrating sensitivity scan; defaults tuned from 7-day synthetic replay experiments (see docs/ptb.md#tuning).
Sofia Martinez: The CI runtime increase worries me for queued PRs. Can we gate the replayer to run only on nightly for large repos?
Maya Chen: Replayer scope is configurable via replay_budget. For large repos we set replay_budget=0 in the shared CI config; added guidance to docs.
Priya Nair: Suggest adding a small metric to console: ptb_alert_rate per-run so SRE can monitor early.
Add: Per-Prompt Temporal Baseline (PTB) probe and a CI gate with optional counterfactual replayer to help triage intermittent prompt regressions. Opt-in by default; configurable thresholds and replay_budget. See docs/eval/ptb.md for details.

payload.body:
Motivation: We intermittently see prompts that are stable per-seed but vary significantly across evaluation runs (inter-run variance). These cases bypass current per-run gates and later cause customer-facing regressions. This PR adds a new inter-run variance heatmap reporter and a paired CI hook that can (optionally) auto-suggest repairs (paraphrases) for prompts that exhibit unstable semantics across runs.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a variance aggregation stage that collects per-prompt metrics across multiple evaluation runs (default: 5 runs, configurable). 2) Produces a compact heatmap visualization (text and JSON) keyed by prompt_id x metric, highlighting regressions and divergence patterns. 3) Adds a CI hook (ci-eval-variance) which fails the gated check when more than N prompts cross a configurable variance threshold for a given metric (default: 5 prompts / metric). 4) Implements an optional auto-suggest flow that generates candidate paraphrases via a small paraphrase model (redwood/paraphrase-small-v1) and scores them for reduced inter-run variance — suggestions are surfaced in the CI failure payload and in the Console alert for triage.

Design notes: - The variance calculation uses a bootstrap-of-seeds approach to estimate inter-run standard deviation while attenuating single-run outliers. - Heatmap buckets metrics (e.g., exact-match, semantic-similarity, BLEU-like scoring) into categorical severity bands (info/warn/critical). - Auto-suggest is intentionally conservative: it only proposes paraphrases when the top candidate reduces the measured variance by >= 30% and preserves the original expected label fidelity. Generated suggestions are marked as draft and must be reviewed before being applied to upstream prompt sets.

Backward-compatibility and safety: - The CI hook defaults to soft-fail on nightly branches and hard-fail on release/* branches. Teams can opt out per-prompt via a new prompt metadata flag (metadata: {"variance_allowlist": true}). - The engine that calls the paraphrase model uses rate-limited async calls and does not block the main evaluation pipeline; suggestions are computed post-run and attached to the CI artifact.

Operational impact: - Adds ~12% overhead to full cross-run smoke suites when running with default 5-run aggregation. We profiled this on our perf-canary cluster and observed stable memory behavior. - Telemetry: new metrics eval.variance.runs, eval.variance.per_prompt, and eval.variance.suggest_count (exposed in Console).

Testing and rollout: - Unit tests added for variance calculator and thresholding logic. - Integration test in tests/integration/ensure_variance_reporter.sh that runs a 3-run mock harness. - Nightly canary enabled first week (soft-fail). After 2 weeks of tuning, hard-fail turned on for release branches.

Docs: Added docs/eval/variance-heatmap.md with usage examples and configuration knobs.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation of variance aggregator and heatmap reporter - [x] CI hook and infra wiring (ci/ci-eval-hooks.yml) - [x] Auto-suggest generator with safety checks - [x] Unit & integration tests - [x] Docs and canary rollout plan

Related: builds on ideas from ENG-1984 (prompt stability study) and complements the anchor-based replay hooks we've used previously.

Marcus Liu: please add an allowlist bypass for prompts that intentionally vary (e.g., A/B content) — addressed in commit d4e5f6a and documented.
Sophie Ortega: can we limit paraphrase cost? suggest adding rate limits and an opt-in flag — added rate-limit and opt-in 'enable_autorepair' config, confirmed in tests.
Diego Fernandez: CI failure modes need clear instructions for on-call. Added Console alert payload example and playbook link in docs.
Aisha Patel (author): responded to comments, tuned default thresholds to reduce noisy failures after running canary for 3 days.

payload.body:
Motivation: During the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint we’re moving quickly on kernel dispatch + quantization profile defaults. We need a fast “tripwire” to catch obvious quality regressions (e.g., broken JSON/tool call formatting, language drift, refusal spikes, or summarization truncation) before we flip defaults or broaden canary cohorts. This PR adds a lightweight quantization quality sanity suite built around a small set of golden prompts + deterministic decoding and cheap scoring. Scope: (1) Add `quant_sanity` runner that executes a fixed prompt set and compares against stored goldens, (2) Add scoring utilities focused on obvious failures (structure + similarity), (3) Provide CLI + CI wiring to run on PRs that touch quantization/kernels/profiles (opt-in label for now), and (4) Document update workflow for goldens (manual, reviewed). What this is / isn’t: This is not meant to replace the full benchmark suite v3 or Applied ML eval sign-off. It is intentionally small and cheap (minutes) and optimized for catching “something is clearly wrong” changes. Prompt set: 52 prompts (balanced) across summarization, extraction to JSON, tool-calling style responses, short QA, and long-context sanity (truncated to keep runtime low). The prompts are derived from existing internal prompt sets but reduced and scrubbed for CI; no customer data. Determinism + decoding: temperature=0, top_p=1, max_tokens fixed per case; seed pinned where supported; normalization handles whitespace + minor punctuation drift. Scoring: (a) JSON/schema parse success for structured cases, (b) key presence + type checks for extraction cases, (c) normalized edit distance / token overlap score for freeform cases (thresholded), (d) “refusal” and “empty output” heuristics, (e) length / truncation guardrails for summaries. Output + artifacts: runner writes a single JSONL results file + a summary table; on failure includes top diffs and the exact command line used. Goldens: stored in-repo under `eval_harness/goldens/quant_sanity/` with a `GOLDENS.md` explaining update procedure. Updates require `--update-goldens` and are blocked in CI (only allowed locally), intended to be reviewed by Applied ML (Jonas/Olivia) when thresholds move. Usage: `python -m eval_harness.quant_sanity --model <model_id> --mode {baseline|fp8|int8} --endpoint $REDWOOD_ENDPOINT --api-key $REDWOOD_API_KEY --out results.jsonl` and `python -m eval_harness.quant_sanity --compare results.jsonl --goldens eval_harness/goldens/quant_sanity/goldens.jsonl`. CI: Adds `quant-sanity-smoke` job that runs the compare step (no network) + validates the prompt set and scorer; optional GPU run is behind `run-gpu-evals` label for now (we can flip to required once runtime team is happy with capacity/noise). Notes: This was requested after SUP-31852 (INT8 quality concerns) and to support the runtime sprint’s faster iteration loop. It should also help interpret perf canary anomalies where output degradation shows up as “success” but customers report issues.
Jonas Weber: Can we make sure this doesn’t become a de-facto approval gate? Also, what’s the failure mode if a model legitimately changes phrasing but is still fine?
Priyanka Bose: Agreed. I added explicit language in README + workflow comments: this is a regression tripwire only. For phrasing drift we’re using tolerant similarity thresholds for freeform cases + hard structural checks only where we must. Also added a summary of which cases are “hard” vs “soft” scored.
Claire Dubois: Determinism worries me. Even with temp=0 we’ve seen small nondeterminism on GPU. Can we avoid flaky CI? Also: please pin max_tokens per test and ensure the scorer handles whitespace/newlines consistently.
Priyanka Bose: Updated: CI default job is compare-only + prompt/scorer validation (no model call). The GPU run is label-gated. Also pinned per-case max_tokens and added `normalize_text()` that collapses whitespace + normalizes common punctuation.
Arjun Desai: For INT8, common regressions are malformed JSON and numeric field drift. Can we add type checks and allow small numeric tolerance?
Priyanka Bose: Added schema/type checks for the extraction prompts and a numeric tolerance for known numeric fields (relative tolerance 2% unless overridden in the case metadata). Also added explicit counters for json_parse_fail / schema_fail so we can track improvements over time.
Olivia Grant: Can we add a refusal detector? We’ve had cases where quant changes increase refusals without tripping similarity metrics.
Priyanka Bose: Added refusal/empty-output heuristics (keyword + length + leading phrases) and made them hard-fail for the affected prompt subset. The summary now includes refusal_rate and empty_rate.
Rina Kobayashi: Please align naming with runtime sprint docs: we use “baseline/fp8/int8” consistently. Also, can this output a single-line summary that can be pasted into Slack triage threads?
Priyanka Bose: Renamed modes to baseline/fp8/int8. Added `--slack-summary` which prints a compact line: pass/fail + counts + worst offenders and a path to artifacts.
Jonas Weber: Final nit: goldens update should be noisy by design. Please make sure `--update-goldens` is blocked in CI and documented as “requires Applied ML review.”
Priyanka Bose: Done. CI refuses `--update-goldens` (explicit guard). GOLDENS.md now includes “reviewers: Applied ML/Evals” and a checklist.

payload.body:
Background and motivation: We observed a recurring class of regressions where prompt translations (either human-translated prompt sets or machine back-translated probes) surface quality drops that are not caught by monolingual SLOs. These regressions are subtle because tokenization and punctuation differences can mask semantic drift. This PR introduces a multilingual prompt parity checker as a CI hook to detect regressions that affect parity between language variants of the same prompt set. Design summary: 1) Pair generation: for each canonical prompt set (usually English), the hook pairs it with one or more translated variants (human or machine) and optional back-translated English as a control. 2) Normalization: outputs run through a language-aware normalizer (strip diacritics optionally, unify punctuation, normalize whitespace, unify numbers/dates using locale-aware rules). 3) Metrics: compute semantic-parity score using a symmetric embedding-based similarity (cosine) + token-level fuzzy diff for structural regressions (missing clauses, hallucinated lists). 4) Thresholding and cohorting: per-language baseline means and stddev are stored in the eval registry; checks fail only when the delta exceeds the configured z-score threshold or absolute similarity floor. 5) CI behaviour: the hook runs as an optional evaluation job (eval:multilingual-parity) and can be configured to soft-fail (annotate but not block) or hard-fail depending on linear ticket flags. Implementation notes: - New hook entrypoint eval/hooks/multilingual_parity.py implements pairing, normalization, scoring, and reporting. - A lightweight back-translation adapter lives in eval/adapters/backtranslate_adapter.py used only for generating control pairs in smoke mode. - Baseline storage: eval/registry/multilingual_baselines.csv (small CSV; seeded with en->es,en->fr baseline entries). - Config + opt-in: eval/configs/multilingual_parity.yaml exposes languages, thresholds, and whether to run backtranslate probes. - Tests: unit tests cover normalization edge cases, and an integration smoke test runs on a small curated bilingual prompt set. Backwards compatibility: all changes are behind an opt-in hook; default CI job is gated behind a feature flag so there is zero default test time regression. Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag; 2) Enable soft-fail in nightly pipeline for two weeks, collect baseline deviations and false positive counts; 3) Flip to hard-fail for critical products after validation. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of hook logic - [x] Unit tests for normalizer and similarity scorer - [x] Integration smoke test with curated bilingual set - [x] Registry CSV seeded with initial baselines - [x] Docs stub and example config snippet - [x] Linear ticket linked for rollout coordination Testing and results: On the seeded en->es and en->fr sample sets, the semantic-parity metric reproduces existing known-good baselines (mean cosine 0.92 en->es, 0.90 en->fr); the hook triggered one intentional regression injected during development and produced a clear z-score > 4 signal. Observability: the hook emits per-prompt metrics to the eval-metrics namespace (parity.cosine, parity.token_diff_ratio) and summary alerts when > 5% of prompts exceed the configured tolerance. Known limitations: - Back-translation quality depends on the adapter; noisy backtranslations can increase false positives. - Language-specific tokenizers may behave differently between model families; baselines are model-variant-aware but initial CSV is coarse. Documentation: Added README section at docs/eval-hooks/multilingual_parity.md with configuration examples and troubleshooting suggestions.
Marco Li: Nice pattern. Two asks: (1) can we make normalization pipeline pluggable so new locales can add rules without changing code? (2) add a short circuit for tiny prompts (<8 tokens) to avoid noisy diffs.
Author (Aisha Rahman): Implemented a NormalizerRegistry that loads rules from eval/configs/normalizers/*.yaml; added token-length short-circuit and updated tests.
Priya Kothari: Can we ensure thresholds are model-variant aware? Suggest adding a model_tag field to baseline CSV.
Author: Added model_tag column to multilingual_baselines.csv and updated parser to match on model_tag when present; falls back to generic baseline when missing.
Jonah Peters: CI time concern: backtranslation added ~20s per prompt for the smoke set. Recommend making backtranslation optional in pipeline and default off in PR runs.
Author: Backtranslation is now opt-in via multilingual_parity.yaml (backtranslate: false by default).
Add a CI hook that detects regressions in multilingual prompt parity by comparing normalized outputs across translations; configurable per-language baselines and tolerance thresholds; opt-in via eval-config; no behavioral changes to production runtime; improves detection of translation-induced regressions.
This hook targets a gap in multilingual regression detection and is intentionally opt-in for early rollout; follow-up work ENG-2056 will extend baselines and add model-family calibration.

payload.body:
Motivation: We frequently see transient regressions in prompt-set smoke checks that only reproduce after replaying historical traffic. The goal of this change is to provide a deterministic, configurable shadow-eval fanout that can (1) route representative live traffic to multiple eval runners with weights, (2) run phased backfills of historical prompts in cost-aware waves, and (3) apply staged soft-gates that escalate alerts only after multi-stage consensus failures. This reduces alert noise while still catching regressions that only appear under specific sample distributions.

What this PR does (overview): Adds a new eval fanout orchestrator module (layered_shadow_fanout) that fans incoming evaluation requests to a configurable set of shadow runners (local, remote, and cached). Introduces a phased backfill controller (phased_backfill.yaml + backfill_worker) that replays historical prompt snapshots in waves with exponential decay on sampling rate. Implements a staged soft-gate adapter for CI: the gate first records divergence signals (weighted-consensus metric), then triggers a soft-alert if threshold X is exceeded for window T1, and finally escalates to a hard fail only if a secondary confidence metric is below Y for T2.

Design notes: - Fanout is layered: the primary live runner gets the request, shadow layers receive the same input with independent timeouts and isolation. Each shadow returns a score object; the orchestrator computes a weighted-consensus score and a consensus-variance signal. - Phased backfill consumes archived prompt snapshots and replays them in bounded batches. Backfill waves are parameterized: initial sample pct, decay factor, max-cost-per-hour and cohort prioritization (semantic-coverage first). - Staged soft-gates are configured via CI hooks: the first stage produces a GitHub neutral check with annotations; the second creates an annotated report and opens a quiet Linear ticket if persistent; the third marks the PR red (hard-fail) only when confirmed by consensus across at least two runners.

Checklist: - [x] Orchestrator implementation and unit tests - [x] Backfill controller with safety knobs - [x] CI hook adapter and GitHub check integration - [x] Docs: how to configure layered fanout and backfill cadence - [x] Local integration test using small snapshot - [x] Load test: 5k shadow evals/hour simulated

Backward compatibility: All APIs are additive. Existing CI hooks remain unchanged unless teams opt in to the staged gate in pipeline configs.

Rollout plan: Feature is behind a feature-flag (eval.layered_shadow_fanout). Enable in staging for 48h with a small cohort, run a 6-hour phased backfill on a 50k prompt snapshot, evaluate weighted-consensus stability and adjust thresholds before gradually enabling soft-gates for critical repos.
Diego: Could the weighted-consensus metric be gamed if one shadow is consistently stale? Reply (Maya): Good catch — fanout applies a staleness penalty on out-of-window responses; implementation and tests added.

Priya: We should limit backfill cost per hour at org level as well as repo level. Reply (Maya): Added max-cost-per-hour global knob and per-cohort override in phased_backfill.yaml.

Arjun: CI hook annotations are a lot — can we surface a concise summary first? Reply (Maya): Reduced GH check summary to two lines and added a collapsible details section with full diffs. Diego approved, Priya approved with one doc nit. Final approval by Arjun after addressing documentation examples.
Checks: unit (pass, 14s), integration (pass, 2m 22s), lint (pass), flake-detect (pass). Backfill-sim load test run as a synthetic job (pass) with 95th p95 latency for shadow path at 120ms. No intermittent failures observed; flakiness threshold under 0.5% across runs.
Adds a configurable layered shadow eval fanout and phased backfill controller. New staged soft-gate CI adapter reduces false positive alerting while preserving detection of distribution-specific regressions. Opt-in via eval.layered_shadow_fanout feature flag.

Motivation: Some regressions only surface when the model is evaluated against ground-truth examples that share contextual attributes with production requests (e.g., system prompt fragments, domain tokens, metadata flags). This PR adds a Contextualized Ground-Truth Sampling Gate: a lightweight CI hook that draws small, context-conditioned ground-truth samples and runs a fast suite of evals to detect regressions tied to context drift. The change includes: 1) a sampling component (ContextualSampler) that matches production-like context fingerprints (sequence length, instruction tokens, metadata tags) and constructs a stratified mini-batch; 2) a gating policy (GateEvaluator) that computes composite signals (exact-match recall, token-level likelihood delta, and a contextual rank metric) and applies a thresholded policy with hysteresis and burn-in; 3) a CI adapter for GitHub Actions that runs the gate on PRs touching model-serving/adapter code and fails early on statistically significant degradations; 4) an automatic rollback / guidance path that posts a triage checklist to the PR when the gate fails, with links to debugging tips and a small replay harness. Design notes: - The sampler uses lightweight fingerprint vectors extracted from a historical request ledger and proactively samples k=50 examples across three strata: short-instruction, long-dialogue, and metadata-heavy. Sampling is randomized but seeded by the PR head SHA to keep runs reproducible. - Gate evaluator computes a composite score: score = 0.5*EM_normalized + 0.3*(-KL_token_delta) + 0.2*contextual_rank. We include a short bootstrap baseline derived from the last green main run. - Hysteresis: the gate will soft-fail on first detection (comment + set status=neutral) and hard-fail on repeated failures over two successive runs to reduce flakiness. - Runtime constraints: the gate aims for <5m wall time by default; longer runs are allowed for release/* branches. Testing and validation: - Local unit tests for ContextualSampler + GateEvaluator (coverage added) - Integration smoke that runs with a minimal model stub (fast) in CI - Stress experiment: ran on 120 sample PRs from the last 6 months; the gate caught 7 context-conditioned regressions that were missed by aggregate metrics and had zero false positives in a manually-reviewed subset. Backwards compatibility: the adapter is opt-in via a repo-level eval.yml toggle. The PR includes sensible defaults so teams can enable it conservatively. Operational hooks: - A dashboard metric (eval_gates.contextual_gt.score) was added to allow SRE to monitor gate stability. - A small alert flavor is included if gate flaps more than 3 times in a 24h window. Usage: To enable, add eval: contextual_gt: enabled: true to .github/eval.yml or flip the repo toggle in the console. The PR body includes examples of the minimal config and the sample output format. Related work: inspired by production incident SUP-4421 where a prompt-anchored regression went undetected by global evals. Related Linear ENG-2021 tracks the broader CI gating roadmap. Summary: this change materially improves sensitivity to context-conditioned regressions while balancing runtime and flakiness via hysteresis and burn-in.
Diego Alvarez (reviewer): Can we avoid touching the historical ledger directly in the CI container? Suggested extracting a small summarized fingerprint store as an artifact.
Maya Chen (author): Good point — changed sampler to read compressed fingerprint snapshots (see ci/actions/contextual-gt.yml).
Priya Singh (reviewer): The composite weighting looks reasonable but please add an easy knob for teams to prefer EM or likelihood-based signals.
Maya Chen (author): Added per-repo config overrides and documented them in docs/eval_gates.md.
Owen Patel (reviewer): CI time budget needs to be explicit. Ensure default is 3 minutes for PRs and 10m for release branches.
Maya Chen (author): Adjusted GH action timeout and added comments in the workflow file.
QA (automated): integration smoke passed against model stub on first run, second run validated baseline recalibration.

Motivation: Existing eval CI gates operate on global delta thresholds (avg accuracy or aggregate score) which miss signal from small-but-critical prompt regressions and cause noisy failures from flaky prompts. This PR introduces a delta-driven CI hook that evaluates per-prompt metric deltas against configurable SLOs and makes gated decisions with two outcomes: 1) fail CI for systemic regressions (aggregated SLO breach), and 2) open actionable alerts for targeted prompt regressions without failing the whole pipeline (soft alerts). This reduces noisy red builds while ensuring high‑priority prompt regressions are surfaced.

Design summary: single new CI hook binary (prompt_delta_gate) that ingests baseline eval artifacts (previous successful run) and current run results (JSONL prompt-level metrics). It computes for each prompt: delta = current_score - baseline_score, normalizes by baseline variance, and compares against per-prompt SLO definitions. The hook returns a non-zero exit only if the aggregated SLO breach score exceeds the pipeline threshold. Otherwise it emits structured diagnostics, uploads a condensed regression manifest to the artifacts bucket, and posts summarized findings to the configured alert sink (Slack/Sentry/Linear).

Key features:
- Per-prompt SLO config (yaml): allow per-prompt thresholds and severity tags.
- Baseline selection: supports select-by-tag (last-stable), specific run id, or time window.
- Aggregation policy: weighted-sum of violations, with weights driven by prompt importance and volume.
- Flakiness suppression: automatic jitter/flip detection to avoid alerting on single-run noise.
- Metrics integration: emits Prometheus metrics (eval_prompt_regressions_total, eval_regression_weighted_score) for dashboards and long-term trending.
- CI behavior: two modes - strict (fail on aggregate breach) and permissive (fail only when high-severity regressions are detected).

Sample per-prompt SLO config (illustrative):

slo_version: v1
global_threshold: 0.25 # weighted breach threshold to fail CI
prompts:
  - id: intent/confirm_email
    importance: 3
    delta_threshold: -0.05
    severity: high
  - id: info/faq_shipping_time
    importance: 1
    delta_threshold: -0.12
    severity: medium

CLI usage (examples):
- Run in CI comparing last-stable baseline: ./tools/prompt_delta_gate --baseline-tag last-stable --current results/2026-02-11.jsonl --config .ci/prompt_slos.yaml --mode strict
- Generate artifact only (do not fail): ./tools/prompt_delta_gate --baseline-id run-2026-02-10 --current results.jsonl --emit-artifact only

Backward compatibility: We keep the existing aggregate-score gate as a fallback and add the new hook to the eval CI workflow; teams can opt-in by adding a small config entry in their eval job template.

Security: The hook only reads eval artifact blobs and writes a small regression manifest to the configured artifacts bucket. No secrets are embedded; auth uses CI runner credentials.

Testing: Unit coverage for delta math and aggregation; integration test against synthetic eval artifacts (in tests/integration/test_delta_ci.py). Load-tested locally on 10k prompt runs to validate performance (median run < 6s for 10k prompts with simple metrics).

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Docs (ci/prompt-slo-gates.md)
- [x] Prometheus metric emitters
- [x] Add to .github workflow (eval-ci)

References: Linear ENG-4821 (prompt regression detection), ENG-5032 (ci gate UX), prior discussion: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4821/prompt-regression-detection
Liam O'Connor (review): Overall design looks solid. A few asks: (1) show how we pick baseline when there are flaky past runs, (2) include a CLI flag to produce a machine-readable regression manifest for automation, (3) default to permissive mode for repo-level opt-in.
Author (Asha): Addressed - baseline selection added (tag/time-window). Added --emit-manifest flag and made permissive default when config not provided. PTAL.
Priya Nair (review): Prom metrics look good; suggest adding a label for 'prompt_category' to make dashboarding easier.
Author (Asha): Added prompt_category label and updated exporter. Also added tests verifying label presence.
Gabe Reynolds (approval): Tests + docs are sufficient. Approving for merge pending CI green.
Adds a delta-driven prompt-regression CI hook that enables per-prompt SLO gating and targeted alerting. Default behavior is permissive; teams can opt into strict failure mode. Emits Prometheus metrics for monitoring and uploads a regression manifest artifact for triage.
