Motivation: We keep seeing transient prompt-set regressions that are localized to small input spans or to particular provenance buckets (derived from data ingestion/annotation pipelines). Existing CI gates flag failures but provide little automated remediation guidance, which slows on-call and release engineering. This PR introduces two coordinated capabilities: 1) a Span-Aware Gate CI hook that computes span-level divergence scores (token-range / semantic span) and escalates failures only when divergence is broad or repeated across anchors; 2) an Anchored Repair Orchestrator that runs staged repair actions (replay with alternative prompts, selective re-ranking, contextual anchoring) against failing prompt sets and produces an ordered repair plan for human review or automated patching.

What this changes (high level): adds a CI hook that (a) attaches span metadata to eval traces, (b) computes per-span divergence and hit-counts across anchors; integrates with the existing smoke / regression pipeline to produce a contextual fail reason tag (SPAN_WIDE, SPAN_NARROW, PROVENANCE_SKINNY). Adds an orchestrator service within eval-harness that: - selects anchor examples (stable sentinel prompts) and fuzzed variants; - runs staged repairs (replay with prefix-anchoring, candidate prompting, lightweight reranker, and conservative output masking); - records repair summaries and suggested patch artifacts (prompt diffs, config deltas); - emits a suggested rollback or canary plan when repairs fail or introduce new regressions. The orchestrator is opt-in per-promptset via a new yml config (eval_harness/configs/promptset_repair.yml).

Implementation notes: - Python 3.11-compatible module eval_harness/orchestrator/anchored_repair.py (actor + runner + simple state machine) - CI hook implemented as ci/hooks/span_gate.yaml and ci/hooks/span_gate_runner.py (invoked by the existing eval-ci entrypoint) - Telemetry tags added to all eval traces: span_id, anchor_id, provenance_bucket - New compact export format for repair proposals: /exports/repair_proposals/<pr-number>.ndjson - Unit + integration tests in tests/test_anchored_repair.py and smoke tests under tests/ci_span_gate_smoke.py - Docs: docs/anchored_repair.md and examples/repair_playbook.md

Checklist: [x] design doc linked in Linear ENG-4829 [x] unit tests [x] integration smoke tests [x] telemetry + tags emitted [x] docs updated [x] e2e run in staging (passed) [x] performance benching for hook latency included

Risk and mitigation: The span computations add a second pass over tokens; we implemented early-exit heuristics and thresholded sampling to keep median CI hook latency within 1.2x baseline. The orchestrator runs in a sandboxed job with bounded retries to avoid accidental mass replays. Config opt-in prevents accidental activation for all prompt sets.
Arjun Patel (reviewer): The span scoring looks sensible but the metric names collide with existing 'divergence_score' in the registry. Please namespace them (span_divergence / anchor_hit_count) and add a short migration note.
Maya Chen (author): Updated metric names and added a compatibility shim in telemetry/exporter to populate old names for dashboards. Added migration note to docs.
Benji Park (reviewer): Tests look good. Concern: orchestrator might produce many suggested patches for large promptsets. Can we cap proposals per-run and add a priority heuristic?
Maya Chen (author): Added cap (default 5 proposals/run) and a priority heuristic (anchor_hit_count * span_width) used to rank proposals. Documented the tunable in config file.
Sofia Alvarez (reviewer): Can we avoid flakiness on CI by making the smoke-test seeds deterministic and lowering non-deterministic timeouts?
Maya Chen (author): Set deterministic seeds in smoke tests and added a retry for an occasional network flake in the backfill script. Reran pipeline and all green.
Sofia Alvarez (reviewer): Approving after the fixes; verified the CI run in staging and the metrics emitted properly.
Arjun Patel (reviewer): Approved.
- Add Span-Aware Gate CI hook that computes span-level divergence and reduces noisy false positives.
- Introduce Anchored Repair Orchestrator that stages automated repair attempts and outputs patch proposals for failing prompt sets.
- Telemetry: new tags span_id, anchor_id, provenance_bucket for easier triage.
- Opt-in config promptset_repair.yml to control rollout and proposal caps.
Span gate may increase CI runtime slightly; configured default sampling and an early-exit threshold to bound latency. If staging shows elevated failure noise for a promptset, disable the orchestrator for that promptset via eval_harness/configs/promptset_repair.yml -> enabled: false and re-run the CI. Repair proposals are idempotent ndjson lines and can be replayed against staging without affecting production.

Context: Some production prompt-sets show temporal drift and intermittent regressions that standard anchor replay misses because anchors age out or are not representatively sampled. This PR adds two related pieces: a temporal-weighted exemplar replay hook for CI and an adaptive prefetch/prober that warms the eval cache with time-representative examples before heavy smoke runs. Motivation: reduce noisy regression alerts and improve early detection of degradations tied to temporal distribution shifts. What I changed: implemented a replay strategy that assigns higher sampling weight to recent examples while preserving long-tail anchors, added a prefetch scheduler that monitors recent traffic distributions and seeds the eval runner cache, and exposed lightweight knobs in configs for half-life and prefetch window. Tests and validation: unit tests for scheduler and weighting, integration smoke harness runs against three production prompt cohorts, and a controlled A/B run showing an 18% reduction in spurious regression alerts and a 12% increase in early-detection hits during the last 7-day window. Performance: prefetch adds approximately 1.8s median to CI job startup but reduces total rerun time downstream by about 22% in failing cases. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve existing sampling behavior unless the feature is enabled in config. Checklist: ensure Linear ticket ENG-1913 referenced, add docs entry, add integration test coverage, verify Docker build. Related: follow-up will add a visual dashboard for temporal coverage. Commits summary: see commits list. Files touched: see changed_files list. Merge notes: validated by reviewers, CI green, merged via squash.
Add a temporal-weighted exemplar replay CI hook and an adaptive prefetch scheduler to reduce false positive regressions for time-sensitive prompt sets; no API changes.

Author: The temporal weighting keeps long-tail anchors via a floor weight while improving sensitivity to recent regressions; stratified sampling was noisy in recent A/B tests. Sofia: Add a safety threshold for very small recent windows. Author: added a minimum-sample floor and updated tests. Marcus: CI runtime looks slightly higher, any ways to mitigate? Motivation: We currently run per-model calibration checks, but when we roll new model variants (quantized, distill, or different checkpoints) we lack a CI-level guard that compares calibration performance across variants. This PR adds a "cross_model_calibration_score" metric and a CI adapter that enforces a configurable SLO for cross-model calibration parity so we can detect regressions caused by model swaps or quantization changes.

What this PR does: 1) Adds an evaluation metric implementation that computes calibration parity across a set of anchored model variants (eval_harness/metrics/cross_model_calibration.py). 2) Adds a CI hook (ci/hooks/cross_model_calibration_hook.py) that can be plugged into the existing eval CI pipeline and will FAIL the gate when the aggregated calibration shift exceeds the threshold. 3) Provides a backfill script (scripts/backfill_cross_model_calibration.py) to compute historical baselines for selected prompt sets. 4) Adds dashboard metadata and a short docs page (docs/metrics/cross_model_calibration.md) explaining interpretation and recommended thresholds. 5) Adds unit and integration tests and an example prompt anchor set.

Design note: the adapter computes Brier-based calibration per variant and then reports RMS difference across variants as the cross_model_calibration_score. We intentionally report a single scalar for CI gating and emit per-variant breakdowns for dashboards. We considered a KL approach but opted for Brier parity for interpretability and boundedness. Performance: typical CI runs add ~3s for a 1k-sample prompt-set on a standard runner. Backfill is IO-bound and can be parallelized in the future.

Motivation: A recurring pattern in our prompt-set regressions is short-lived entropy spikes from synthetic probes that trigger immediate CI escalations. This PR adds a new entropy-stabilized synthetic prober plus a failure-rate debouncer gate to reduce noise-driven flakiness while preserving sensitivity to true regressions.

Summary of changes: Added a pluggable synthetic prober that emits probe sets with controlled entropy perturbations across random seeds and context shuffles; introduced a debounced failure-rate metric and gate which requires sustained elevation for N windows before failing a CI job; wired the new signals into the smoke and regression gates and added telemetry (probe_entropy_score, debounced_failure_rate) to the eval console. The prober supports per-prompt-set policies and an opt-in config so teams can enable conservative probing for high-sensitivity prompts.

Design notes: The prober generates 4 probe modes: prefix-noise, suffix-noise, paraphrase-anchor, and context-swap. Each probe run collects multiple seeds (default 5) and computes an entropy-normalized agreement score. Entropy stabilization normalizes per-seed variance with a shrinkage estimator so rare-but-high-variance probes don't dominate the failure signal. The debouncer computes a rolling-window failure rate with exponential backoff and requires M consecutive windows over threshold to escalate (configurable; default windows=3, stride=1).

CI integration: The gate exposes two CI hooks: a pre-merge smoke hook (fast mode, 2 seeds, small sample) and a full regression hook (policy-controlled, backs off to soft-fail & ticket when triggered). Default behavior on hosted CI is soft-fail + create ENG ticket; on release branches it escalates after debouncer windows.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for entropy estimator, sampling scheduler, and debouncer logic added. End-to-end smoke tests included in ci/smoke/prober_smoke_test.py. We ran a 2-week canary across three teams (lexicon, search, docs) and observed reduced transient CI failures by ~68% with a 2.5% median increase in eval CPU time for full regression suites.

Migration and rollout: Feature-flagged behind eval.feature_flags.entropy_prober (off by default). Documentation added to docs/ci/probes.md with usage examples and opt-in guide. Operators can backfill historical probe metrics via the provided CLI command evalctl probe backfill --range.

Summary: Adds a targeted synthetic negation test suite and a lightweight deferred-fix queue CI hook to reduce noisy blocking failures while preserving visibility into prompt-set regressions.

Motivation: We frequently see regressions around negation, double-negation, and polarity flips that are under-covered by existing prompt sets. Those failures can be brittle and noisy, leading to frequent CI blocks and alert fatigue. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) a synthetic negation suite that programmatically generates diverse negation/contradiction variants across prompt templates, and (2) a deferred-fix queue CI hook that surfaces failing prompt-set checks into a non-blocking queue for triage while still allowing fast-path merges for low-risk changes.

Design:
- Synthetic generator implements a hierarchy of perturbations (single negation, scoped negation, lexical inversion, prefix vs. sentence-level negation) and records deterministic fingerprints for reproducibility.
- Tests include a curated baseline of high-salience prompt templates and a stochastic sampling mode for nightly stress runs.
- CI hook evaluates the negation suite as a separate check. Failures are recorded in the deferred fix queue (backed by a lightweight ledger file checked into artifacts and an optional webhook to the QA Linear project).
- The deferred queue exposes metadata: failing prompts, example model outputs, failure severity (high/medium/low) heuristics based on prior flakiness and semantic distance.

Implementation notes:
- New file eval/harness/suites/synthetic_negation.py contains generator, canonical perturbation pipeline, and deterministic seed handling.
- Deferred queue in eval/harness/ci_hooks/deferred_fix_queue.py implements a pluggable policy: default is 'non-blocking-notify' but maintainers can opt into 'block-on-critical' by label.
- Added unit tests in eval/harness/tests/test_negation_suite.py with fixed seeds to keep CI stable.
- docs/eval/negation-suite.md documents usage, how to add templates, and how to opt a library into stricter gating.

Checklist:
- [x] Synthetic generator with deterministic fingerprinting
- [x] Unit tests and CI integration
- [x] Deferred queue implementation with metadata capture
- [x] Documentation and usage examples
- [x] Linear linkage for triage (QA-4452)

Review summary:
- Ethan: requested that the deferred queue include a short-term retention policy to avoid unbounded ledger growth; implemented via a 90-day TTL and pruning routine (see commit f2e3a44).
- Sophia: asked for tighter test fixtures to avoid flakiness on GPUs with different tokenizers; added tokenizer-agnostic assertions and cross-tokenizer smoke checks.
- Marcus: suggested a severity heuristic threshold to keep the queue actionable; added a simple semantic-distance rule that downgrades micro-diffs to low severity.

CI behavior:
- Unit tests and lint pass on main (all checks green).
- Negation suite runs as a separate check named "negation-suite" and reports results to the CI summary.
- Failing checks create an artifact JSON and append a record to artifacts/deferred_fix_ledger.json (CI only) for maintainers to inspect.

Example changed areas (high-level):
- added new harness module and tests
- wired CI config to run in both PR and nightly modes
- added docs and an example guide for partner teams

Migration/opt-in notes:
- By default the deferred queue is non-blocking; teams can opt into blocking mode by adding the label `eval-blocking` to a PR.
- To add custom templates, drop YAML files under eval/harness/templates/ and register them in the suite manifest.

Related work: This PR complements existing cohort and anchor-based evals by providing targeted perturbation coverage for logical operators and polarity flips.

Linked Linear tickets: ENG-11234 (negation coverage initiative), QA-4452 (deferred triage workflow).

Merge: Squash merge to main after approvals.

Post-merge steps:

- Monitor the deferred_fix_ledger artifact and create QA tasks for high-severity entries.

Priya Anand: Added TTL and pruning routine; ledger rotates daily and prunes >90d entries in maintenance job.
Sophia Chen: Tests were flaky on macOS + HF tokenizers; switched to tokenizer-agnostic evaluation and added a smoke check.
Marcus Park: Suggest adding a semantic-distance fallback for severity - implemented and tuned to avoid noise.
Add: Synthetic negation perturbation suite (targeted tests for negation & polarity flips); Add: Deferred-fix queue CI hook to capture non-blocking prompt-set failures; Docs: usage guide and opt-in instructions.

Motivation:
Client disconnects and slow clients were contributing to two classes of production issues: 1) sessions left open on the server (KV-cache and state) that consumed GPU memory until evicted, and 2) sudden resource pressure when many slowed clients resumed and pushed large request windows, causing transient tail-latency spikes. This PR introduces a coordinated connection orchestration layer for our OpenAI compatibility streaming surface to address both problems.

What this change does (single-pass summary):
- Adds a configurable client grace window on cancel/disconnect events (default 45s) where the server keeps ephemeral state but disables expensive prefetching and applies rate caps.
- Implements a server-side idle timeout with an active probe/ping before final teardown to avoid noisy double-teardowns and give clients a chance to reattach.
- Introduces a lightweight backpressure token bucket per-session to slow incoming token production from resumed clients and protect KV-cache growth.
- Propagates cancel semantics to in-flight function/tool calls while preserving idempotency metadata so downstream tool providers can safely retry or noop.

Design notes and rationale:
- We prefer a grace window vs immediate teardown to support intermittent mobile networks and short client restarts (common in SDK telemetry). The 45s default is based on routing team traces showing a median reconnect < 30s for mobile clients with occasional spikes.
- To prevent resource leakage, during the grace window we mark sessions as "drained" for background prefetch and large optimizer tasks; serving runtime keeps only minimal KV-cache checkpoint pages in pinned memory.
- Server idle timeout (configurable per deployment tier) uses a two-step sequence: (1) on reaching idle threshold, send a probe frame to the client and wait probe_timeout (default 10s); (2) if no ack, proceed to final teardown. This reduces race conditions when clients are closing and servers concurrently decide to evict.
- Backpressure is implemented as a token-bucket applied to the incoming token stream for resumed sessions. Bucket refill rate is derived from the session's SLO class (hosted/dedicated/private) and current GPU sched pressure. This prevents pathological bursts from causing preemption.

API and compatibility considerations:
- All behavior is gated behind the OpenAI-compat streaming layer flag; host customers keep the same wire protocol. SDKs will surface a new connection_lifecycle option to tweak grace_window_ms and enable_probe.
- Function/tool call cancellation: we now attach a per-call idempotency_token and a cancellation intent header so external tool adapters can decide to continue or abort. This is opt-in for adapters lacking idempotency guarantees.

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests: connection state transitions, token-bucket refill logic, and probe flow were covered.
- Integration: stress tests against the bench-lab with 10k simulated mobile clients with randomized disconnects, verifying that retained memory per-session is within expected bounds and tail-latency stays under SLO when resume storms happen.
- Canary: rolled to perf-canary (10% of traffic) for 48 hours; observed 38% reduction in leaked-session memory and 22% reduction in 99.9th token latency during reconnect floods.

Rollback plan:

Summary: Adds a CI hook that measures per-cohort sensitivity to controlled prompt perturbations and surfaces unstable cohorts as gating failures. The new "cohort sensitivity calibrator" complements existing drift and variance detectors by focusing on whether small, realistic prompt edits cause disproportionate metric swings (e.g., accuracy, F1, embedding similarity). Motivation: During a recent canary we observed acceptable mean metrics while several important cohorts (non-native English, short prompts, and instruction-prefix variants) flipped labels under minimal rephrasing. Existing variance detectors surface high volatility but do not explicitly quantify directional sensitivity to realistic prompt perturbations. This hook provides a repeatable calibration test to catch regressions that are brittle to prompt-formatting and phrasing changes.

What changed:
- New CI hook: ci/hooks/sensitivity-ci.yml wires the calibrator into the eval pipeline as an opt-in gate for PRs touching evaluation code or models.

Summary: Add a new CI adapter and supporting annealer that adapt the baseline for prompt-set regression checks over time. Motivation: we observe frequent transient CI failures when prompt-set baseline metrics shift slowly (seasonal traffic, tokenizer changes, minor model patching). The adapter implements a controlled annealing schedule and a soft-threshold mode that initially flags degradations as warnings and only escalates to hard failures if the signal persists across a configurable window. This reduces noisy interrupts while preserving regression detection.

Motivation: We observed a recurring class of transient failures in prompt-set regression CI caused by seed-sensitive outputs and high-variance cohorts. This PR implements a cross-seed stability gate that aggregates per-prompt signals across multiple RNG seeds, applies an attenuation function to reduce the impact of single-seed outliers, and quarantines prompts with reproducible regressions for progressive manual review.

What this PR does: - Adds a new CI hook (cross_seed_stability_gate) that computes a noise-aware p-value and stability score per prompt by running N independent seeds and combining results with an attenuation curve. - Implements a quarantine flow: prompts that fail the attenuated threshold are moved to a quarantine artifact (CSV + JSONL) and an automatic backfill job is suggested to collect historical performance for context. - Introduces a new metric aggregator (stability_index) that reports cohort-level percentiles, inter-seed variance, and an explainable failure reason tag (e.g., length-sensitive, sampling-noise, model-drift). - Adds a lightweight retrospective mode: when run in "retrospect" mode the hook replays the last successful baseline snapshot and produces a diffed report for SRE/ML owners. - Improves CI ergonomics: junit-style annotations for quarantined prompts, a small console summary for fast failures, and GitHub check annotations linking directly to quarantine artifacts.

Summary: This PR hardens the OpenAI-compat SSE path against a class of partial-JSON and delimiter-splitting regressions observed in tail-drop and retransmit scenarios.
The change introduces two cooperating mechanisms: 1) a lightweight heartbeat-fence marker that preserves event epoch boundaries under bursty backpressure and 2) a delimiter-normalizer that canonicalizes and emits a stable delimiter table for multi-byte/escaped sequences so downstream parsers can resynchronize without losing function-call or structured-output boundaries.

Motivation: We saw multiple incidents where streaming consumers reconstructed broken JSON objects because an escaped quote or multi-byte UTF-8 sequence was split across fragments and combined with delayed heartbeats, causing downstream reconstructor heuristics to misinterpret the sequence as an event boundary. This surfaced most often with function-call tokens and nested JSON outputs.

Design:
- Heartbeat fence: emit an idempotent fence event (":fence:epoch=<N>\n") when the runtime detects a sequence of N small fragments or after a retransmit/replay window. Consumers treat it as a non-JSON sentinel that indicates the boundary between two reliable reassembly epochs. The fence is optional for OpenAI-compat only and is ignored when the connection is native Redwood binary.
- Delimiter normalizer: when a fragment boundary splits an escape or multibyte sequence, the normalizer rewrites the emitted bytes into a canonical, resumable form and appends a small checksum tag for the tail of the fragment. This improves detector confidence when performing mid-stream resync.
- Backoff integration: fences are rate-limited and can be disabled per-client via a header to avoid adding latency when not needed.
- Tool-call handoff: ensure function-call sentinel ordering is preserved by flushing the current fence before emitting a tool-call sentinel so the consumer can deterministically apply the tool invocation.

- [x] Implement heartbeat-fence emitter in sse_emitter.go
- [x] Add delimiter-normalizer in stream_sanitizer.go
- [x] Update OpenAI-compat parser to skip fence events and use checksum hints

- [x] Add unit tests for split-UTF8 and split-escape cases
- [x] Add integration test that simulates retransmit + burst and validates JSON reassembly
- [x] Documentation note in docs/openai_streaming.md

payload.body:
Motivation: flakiness in prompt-set regression checks arises when cohort-level summary statistics miss localized instabilities tied to input distribution shift. This PR introduces a transductive anchored prober: an anchor-driven sampling strategy that builds a small, per-prompt neighborhood using model-inferred similarity at evaluation time and runs focused consistency checks. The prober is designed to detect regressions that only surface under model-side distribution drift and to produce a compact signal that can be gated in CI.

What this PR does (single continuous description): - Adds a transductive anchor sampler and probing harness that constructs neighborhood examples around human-curated anchors and computes consistency metrics (agreement, rank-stability, and entropy-delta) for each prompt. - Integrates a lightweight CI hook (ci/hooks/anchor_gate.py) that runs the prober in parallel with existing smoke-evals and can fail the build when per-anchor inconsistency exceeds a configurable threshold. - Wires the gate into ci/workflows/eval-gates.yml behind a feature flag (EVAL_ANCHOR_GATE) so we can opt-in per-branch. - Adds instrumentation: per-anchor telemetry (latency, consistency_score, sample_size) and an example dashboard config. - Includes unit and integration tests, a small example notebook for debugging anchors, and docs describing best practices and threshold selection.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation of transductive anchor prober and sampler - [x] Unit tests covering edge cases (empty anchors, tiny neighborhoods) - [x] CI hook + workflow integration behind flag - [x] Docs and example notebook - [x] Alertable metric emitted to eval-metrics namespace for downstream dashboards

Rollout plan: Enable EVAL_ANCHOR_GATE=false for main for one week while we backfill historical runs using scripts/anchor-backfill.sh and inspect signal quality. On successful calibration, flip the flag for release branches and enable soft-fail mode (metric-only) before hard-failing CI. Related Linear: ENG-4621.

Notes: Thresholds default to conservative values (consistency_score < 0.85 triggers soft-fail). Config lives in eval-harness/config/anchor_gate.yaml (see docs).
Jun Ho Park: Nice design—two asks: add more unit coverage around empty-anchor fallback and include a simple microbenchmark for per-anchor latency (we query many neighbors).
Maya Patel: Added microbenchmark and tightened fallback handling in commit c2e6f4b; benchmark results included in docs (sub-120ms/anchor on average).
Elena Garcia: Can we gate this behind a feature flag and soft-fail mode? I want metric-only for two weeks before hard-fail. (requested changes)
Maya Patel: Gate added as EVAL_ANCHOR_GATE and soft-fail mode implemented; docs updated with rollout plan.
Samir Desai: Approve after CI green and a smoke run against latest main history. (approved)
CI Bot: integration-smoke ran against 30 days of historical prompts via scripts/anchor-backfill.sh; summary attached to the run.

payload.body:
Motivation: We frequently see noisy regression failures that are actually seed/ensemble variance or transient distribution shifts in prompt cohorts. This PR implements a lightweight 'probe-ensemble anchoring' CI hook and a soft-revert mechanism that reduces noisy alerting and gives teams a controlled rollback path when a prompt-set regression is likely real.

What this PR does: Implements a new CI hook (eval/ci/hooks/probe_ensemble_anchor.py) that runs short probabilistic ensembles across multiple RNG seeds and aggregates a calibrated anchor score per prompt-cohort. Anchoring blends historical snapshot agreement with current ensemble consensus using an exponential decay so recent stable behavior has higher weight. A separate 'soft-revert' policy (eval/ci/soft_revert.py) uses the anchor score plus a smoothed regression metric to decide whether to: 1) file an actionable regression, 2) mute/soft-fail (mark as flaky) and schedule follow-up probes, or 3) trigger an automated snapshot rollback for the prompt-set with a human review tag.

Key features: - Probabilistic ensemble runner with configurable sample budget and per-cohort stratified sampling. - Anchor score that fuses historical agreement, current consensus, and seed entropy to reduce false-positives. - Adaptive thresholds: thresholds are percentile-based and adjust with empirical variance, avoiding brittle fixed cutoffs. - Soft-revert flow: when confidence is high that a regression is due to a bad rollout, the CI creates a rollback candidate, attaches diagnostics (diffs, failing examples, anchor trace), and leaves the final revert to a human-approved workflow. - Metrics: new telemetry (eval.anchor_score, eval.anchor_entropy, eval.soft_revert_candidates) and debug traces emitted to the eval telemetry pipeline.

Implementation notes: - New files added under eval/ci/hooks/, eval/metrics/, and tests/mini_probes/. - No changes to production serving code; all logic lives in eval-harness and CI. - Introduces a small deterministic state file format (jsonl) for anchor snapshots; migration script included to backfill anchor history from recent smoke-eval runs. - Performance: probe runs are short (default 5 seeds, 3 samples per prompt) and gated behind a configurable 'probe budget' to avoid CI cost blowup.

Testing: - Unit tests for anchor math and thresholding (tests/test_anchor.py). - Integration smoke test that runs a staged probe against a small prompt set and asserts soft-revert candidate generation only for targeted failures (tests/test_soft_revert_flow.py). - Added CI job eval-probe-quick that runs the new hook on PRs labeled with 'eval-probe'.

Files changed (high level): - eval/ci/hooks/probe_ensemble_anchor.py - eval/ci/soft_revert.py - eval/metrics/anchor_metrics.py - eval/cli/commands.py (hook registration) - tests/test_anchor.py - tests/test_soft_revert_flow.py - scripts/backfill_anchor_history.py - docs/eval/anchor-probe.md - examples/anchor-demo/{small_prompt_set.json,run_probe.sh}

Related work: This complements ENG-3922 (prompt snapshotting) and ENG-4100 (cohort stratified sampling). It is intentionally conservative: default configuration mutes automated reverts unless a confidence threshold and human-approved policy are both satisfied.

Risks and mitigation: - Risk: new logic could hide real regressions. Mitigation: soft-revert defaults to opt-in autosnap/revert and always surfaces human-reviewable artifacts; thresholds are conservative and telemetry visible in the eval dashboard. - Risk: CI cost increase. Mitigation: probe budget and quick-probe job keep incremental cost small.

Request: Please review the anchor math, threshold defaults, and the soft-revert human-approval flow. I added detailed commentary in the hook file and tests for clarity.
Arun Patel: Overall looks good. A couple of nitpicks on the anchor decay math — can you add a short proof-of-concept note explaining why we favor exponential decay over sliding windows?
Marta Klein: Added comments and a short appendix in docs/anchor-probe.md with empirical plots and rationale for exponential decay (see commit c3d9f44).
Sofia Marin: For the soft-revert flow, can we ensure the create-rollback action is logged as an audit event?
Marta Klein: Added audit log calls and a small integration test to assert an audit entry is written when a revert candidate is created (commit e5f0b8c).
Diego Ramos: CI job looks fine but please gate the default probe budget with an env var to avoid surprises in staging runs.
Marta Klein: Done — probe budget is configurable via EVAL_PROBE_BUDGET and documented in the README.
SRE Bot: flake detected in test_soft_revert_flow on Py3.8 during first run; reran and passed.
Arun Patel: Approved pending squashing of minor commits.

payload.body:
This PR introduces a new evaluation gate — the Contextual Anchoring Consistency (CAC) gate — and a progressive rollback CI hook that triggers automated mitigations when anchor-consistency regressions are detected. Motivation: existing prompt-set regression checks focus on output-level metrics (accuracy, BLEU-like scores, token-level divergence) but do not isolate whether regressions are due to context-dependent brittleness (prompt-length/context-ordering) vs semantic model degradation. CAC computes a per-prompt anchor-consistency score by replaying a small set of "contextual anchors" (minimal context variants, paraphrases, truncated/extended contexts) and measuring stability of structured outputs and key-field extraction. The gate runs as part of the CI eval stage for PRs touching prompt sets, transforms, or scoring logic and will: 1) fail the CI when the weighted anchor-consistency delta exceeds a configurable threshold, 2) attach a prioritized list of failing anchors with deterministic rerun seeds, and 3) optionally trigger the progressive rollback hook which attempts a staged mitigation: re-run on identical compute with expanded sampling, then run the auto-replay augmentation (adds paraphrase/augmentation shots) and finally produce a suggested patch (prompt tweak or anchor whitelist) to reduce false-positives. The PR contains: - a new module eval_harness/gates/contextual_anchor_gate.py implementing CAC metric and gate interface - a lightweight anchor-sampler eval_harness/anchors/sampler.py that generates anchor variants and records canonicalization diffs - a CI hook integration scripts/ci/hooks/progressive_rollback.py that orchestrates reruns and artifacts upload - updates to CI pipeline config .github/workflows/eval-ci.yml to insert the gate into the eval stage - dashboard instrumentation hooks in observability/eval_metrics.ts to emit anchor_consistency.delta and anchor_failures.top_k - unit+integration tests under tests/eval/gates/test_contextual_anchor.py and smoke tests in tests/ci/test_progressive_rollback.py The description below documents design decisions, expected failure modes, and operational runbook for on-call teams. Design notes: CAC is intentionally conservative — it uses median-based aggregation across anchors, confidence normalization for low-token outputs, and a short-circuit to mark prompts as "non-anchorable" if anchors are semantically ambiguous. The progressive rollback hook is opt-in per-repo and scoped to eval-harness; when enabled it will not auto-merge patches but will open a suggested-changes PR with annotations and run a second eval pass on the suggested patch. Operational runbook: - When CI fails due to CAC, the failing anchors will be listed in the CI artifact and triage panel. - Triage: run the provided rerun command (scripts/ci/hooks/progressive_rollback.py --replay-id=<id>) to reproduce locally. - If anchors exhibit acceptable variance (human judgement), add them to anchor-whitelist.yaml in the prompt-set; if not, follow the suggested patch or escalate to ENG-5834. Backwards compatibility: gate is additive and off by default; enabling requires a single flag in repo_eval_config.yaml. This PR also includes docs and a shortguide at docs/eval/contextual_anchors.md.
High-level changed files: eval_harness/gates/contextual_anchor_gate.py (new) - implements CAC scoring, config knobs; eval_harness/anchors/sampler.py (new) - generates paraphrase/truncate/extend anchors with deterministic seeds; scripts/ci/hooks/progressive_rollback.py (new) - orchestrates reruns, uploads artifacts to eval-artifacts; .github/workflows/eval-ci.yml (modified) - insert contextual-anchor gate as 'eval-anchor-check' step; observability/eval_metrics.ts (modified) - new metrics anchor_consistency.delta and anchor_failures.top_k; tests/eval/gates/test_contextual_anchor.py (new) - unit tests for score invariants; tests/ci/test_progressive_rollback.py (new) - smoke test for rerun flow; docs/eval/contextual_anchors.md (new) - design + triage examples; repo_eval_config.yaml (modified) - gate enable flag and thresholds. Illustrative snippet from contextual_anchor_gate.py: "def compute_anchor_consistency(reference, anchors):\n    scores = [score_fn(reference, a) for a in anchors]\n    return median_normalized(scores)". CI workflow change snippet: "- name: Eval anchor check\n  run: python -m eval_harness.gates.contextual_anchor_gate --config ${{ env.REPO_EVAL_CONFIG }}".

2024-11-13 Maya Chen (author): Added synthetic test in tests/eval/gates/test_contextual_anchor.py covering semantic vs context regressions. Updated repo_eval_config.yaml to allow per-prompt-set overrides. PTAL.

payload.body:
Context: Optimize quality gates run offline eval suites to decide whether a proposed batching/caching/quantization config diff is safe to apply. In beta we’ve been seeing occasional noisy regressions driven by nondeterminism (model sampling variance, evaluator jitter, infra blips) and prompt-set sensitivity. This PR introduces (1) a formal flakiness score computed per suite/run, (2) an automatic rerun policy with bounded cost and clear exit conditions, and (3) deterministic aggregation of multiple attempts into a single GateRunResult that downstream services can consume. Key behaviors: - Each gate run attempt produces AttemptResult (raw metrics, rubric outputs, infra metadata, error codes). - Flake score (0.0–1.0) is computed from cross-attempt dispersion on primary metrics + attempt-level failure signals (timeouts, evaluator exceptions), normalized by metric type and minimum sample size. - Rerun policy triggers up to max_attempts (default 3) when results are inconclusive (near-threshold deltas) or high flake score; policy does not rerun when a clear regression is detected beyond the hard-fail margin. - Aggregation uses median-of-attempts for scalar metrics and majority vote for boolean success metrics; confidence bounds are derived from attempt dispersion and sample size, and included in the response. - API response gains: flake_score, attempts, rerun_reason (if any), aggregated_confidence, and a stable decision field: passed | failed | inconclusive. Inconclusive is explicitly treated as fail-by-default for enforcement, but allows a targeted override workflow upstream. This change is backwards compatible: existing callers that only read decision + deltas continue to work; new fields are additive. Follow-ups: wiring quarantine tooling and surfacing flake signals in dashboards is tracked in ENG-3926/ENG-3929; Optimize service integration is tracked in ENG-3922.
Flake score details: For each primary metric m, compute delta-to-baseline per attempt. Let MAD be median absolute deviation across attempts (robust to outliers). Normalize dispersion by an expected-variance term derived from sample size (n) and metric type. Add penalty terms for attempt errors (timeout, evaluator error) and high retry rate. Final flake_score = clamp01(w_dispersion * norm_dispersion + w_error * error_rate + w_near * near_threshold_rate). Defaults (configurable per suite): w_dispersion=0.65, w_error=0.25, w_near=0.10; near-threshold window defaults to 0.5x the regression threshold. Rerun policy details: attempt 1 always runs; attempt 2 runs if (flake_score >= 0.35) OR (abs(delta) within near-threshold window) OR transient error code; attempt 3 runs if after 2 attempts decision is inconclusive OR flake_score >= 0.55, bounded by max_attempts. Early exit occurs if hard-fail is exceeded (delta worse than threshold + margin) or hard-pass is exceeded (delta better than -margin) with low flake score. Aggregation details: scalar metrics use median; confidence is reported as an interval derived from MAD (scaled) + sample size floor; boolean success uses majority vote with tie -> inconclusive; any attempt marked non-transient infra failure increments error penalties but does not automatically fail unless all attempts fail. All attempts and their artifact pointers are included in the response for audit/debug.
Sana Farid (review): How are we normalizing dispersion across different metric scales? Also, we should avoid treating “near threshold” as synonymous with “flaky” unless we can separate signal vs noise. Olivia Grant (author): Added per-metric normalization (expected variance term) and split near-threshold penalty to a small independent weight. Flake score primarily comes from cross-attempt dispersion and error rate; near-threshold only influences rerun triggers and contributes 0.10 by default. Jonas Weber (review): Please ensure we don’t rerun when it’s clearly failed; cost will blow up on big suites. Also want the decision to be stable for Optimize enforcement. Olivia Grant (author): Implemented hard-fail early exit (threshold + margin) and hard-pass early exit; decision field is now passed/failed/inconclusive and aggregation is deterministic via median/majority. Selene Huang (review): Inconclusive must be explicit and visible; do not collapse into failed silently. Also add artifacts for each attempt so we can debug evaluator drift. Olivia Grant (author): Done. API response includes attempts[] with artifact URIs and rerun_reason. Connor O'Brien (review): CI: add a contract test to ensure additive schema change won’t break callers; also ensure migrations are safe for rollbacks. Olivia Grant (author): Added schema test and made persistence change additive (nullable attempts field). Migration is backward compatible; rollback keeps reading the old fields. Allison Grant (review): Please add structured logs/tags for rerun cause and flake_score so dashboards can break down by suite and region. Olivia Grant (author): Added log keys: gate_run_id, suite_id, flake_score, rerun_reason, attempt_idx, error_code; also propagates region and runner_pool labels.
Eval-harness gate runs now support flake scoring and bounded automatic reruns; responses include attempt-level artifacts plus aggregated confidence and an explicit inconclusive state to prevent noisy pass/fail flips.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: Production prompt sets occasionally regress not because a single model fails but due to growing disagreement across an ensemble of models or model variants. Existing eval gates report regressions but do not capture persistent cross-model divergence or provide actionable remediation suggestions.
What this PR does: 1) Ledger: adds a compact ledger schema (sharded by prompt fingerprint) to store timestamped model outputs, tokenized similarity metrics, and a normalized disagreement score. The ledger supports incremental writes and a TTL-based compaction policy. 2) Aggregator: implements a rolling-window disagreement aggregator that produces smoothed "semantic-slope" and spike detectors, with tunable sensitivity and cohort bucketing. 3) CI adapter: integrates a new ci/adapter that consumes ledger snapshots at CI time, computes per-prompt escalation level, and annotates PR checks with inline prompt-level diagnostics. 4) Auto-suggest repair: when disagreement passes the soft threshold, the hook computes minimal localized perturbations (paraphrase narrowing, guard tokens, or explicit instruction anchors) and posts suggested prompt edits as a machine-authored comment and as structured suggestions embedded in the CI artifact. Suggested fixes include paraphrase examples and a confidence score derived from ensemble consensus. 5) Soft-fail strategy: default CI behavior is to mark the check as 'soft-fail' (annotation-only) and include an auto-suggest badge; maintainers can opt into hard-fail escalation after N consecutive CI runs where suggestions were not applied. 6) Tests & docs: adds unit/integration tests and an ops doc describing config knobs and rollout plan.
Commits summary: ["Add ledger schema and durable writer (ledger/ledger_v1.py)", "Implement rolling-window disagreement aggregator and scoring (aggregator/*)", "CI adapter and formatter with auto-suggest plumbing (ci/adapter_ensemble_disagree.py)", "Auto-suggest generation module with heuristics and scoring (suggest/suggestor.py)", "Unit tests, integration smoke tests, and docs (tests/*, docs/ensemble-disagreement.md)" ]
Changed files (high level): ["eval-harness/ledger/ledger_v1.py", "eval-harness/aggregator/rolling_aggregator.py", "eval-harness/ci/adapter_ensemble_disagree.py", "eval-harness/suggest/suggestor.py", "eval-harness/tests/test_disagreement_ledger.py", "eval-harness/docs/ensemble-disagreement.md", "eval-harness/utils/fingerprint.py", "eval-harness/ci/templates/disagreement_report.j2"]
Test and CI behavior: The first CI run tripped an integration flake in the smoke runner (timing-sensitive compaction test). The flaky test was quarantined and retried, second run passed. Full CI matrix: unit-tests: pass, integration-smoke: pass (after rerun), lint: pass, security-scan: pass, eval-comparison: pass.
Migration and rollout notes: Ledger is backward compatible; new ledger_v1 sits behind a feature flag (env EVAL_LEDGER=enabled). Migration script included for optional backfill; TTL default set to 90 days. Config knobs include soft_fail_threshold (default 0.65 disagreement), escalation_runs (default 3), and suggested_patch_max (default 3).
Review conversation highlights: - Ravi Kapoor (reviewer) asked for clarifications on shard compaction safety and cross-region writes; response: added safe-write fence (ledger_v1.write_safe()) and a small compatibility test (test_cross_region_compaction). - Aisha Martinez requested clearer metrics and dashboard hooks; response: added reconciliation metrics (disagreement_window_mean, disagreement_spike_rate) and a Grafana dashboard template. - Tom Barlow requested limits on auto-suggest generation to avoid noisy suggestions; response: limited suggestions to top-K highest-confidence candidates and added a rate limiter on the suggestion generator.
Code style and architecture notes: The suggestor uses a lightweight constrained paraphrase sampler and a pairwise scoring model to rank repairs; it is intentionally conservative (prefers guard tokens and instruction anchors over aggressive rewriting).
Observability: CI annotations include per-prompt timeline sparklines, consensus delta, and suggested edit diffs.
Security and privacy: all stored outputs are configurable to be hashed or redacted; default ledger stores tokenized fingerprints rather than raw outputs.
Edge cases & limitations: will not attempt repair for prompts marked immutable by owners; suggestions are heuristics and should be reviewed by humans before broad rollout.
Manual QA: performed a small canary across three internal prompt sets and validated that suggested edits reduced ensemble disagreement by median 28% on the canary.
Merge details: merged via squash and merge after final approval from reviewers. Merge method: squash and merge. Links and references: Linear ENG-4123 outlines milestone, SUP-9801 is related support ticket for a customer-facing regression this surfaced.
Next steps: add a feedback loop to capture which suggested edits were applied and incorporate that signal into future suggestion ranking.
Adds an ensemble disagreement ledger with a new CI adapter that surfaces per-prompt disagreement trends and auto-suggests minimal prompt repairs in CI reports. Soft-fail default with optional escalation to hard-fail. Backwards compatible with existing eval schemas.
Ravi: Please add a safe-write fence for compaction edgecases when a shard is moved. Maya: Added write_safe() and compatibility tests.
Aisha: We need dashboard hooks for alerting on disagreement spike rate. Maya: Added metrics and a Grafana dashboard template under docs/.
Tom: Limit suggestion volume and ensure rate limiting. Maya: Added top-K gating and suggestor_rate_limit config.
Ravi: Approve after adding cross-region test and documenting TTL behavior. Ravi: Approved.

payload.body:
Summary: Add a new token-level saliency smokecheck that detects sudden shifts in token attribution patterns for prompt sets, plus a CI soft-fail adapter that lets teams ship the check gated as a warning for the first rollout window. Motivation: high-sensitivity prompt regressions can be noisy in early adoption; teams want early detection of quality regressions (token attribution drift) without failing pipelines for harmless distribution shifts. This PR implements a conservative detector and a CI adapter that records findings as annotations and optionally converts failures to warnings for a configurable grace period.

What changed (high-level):
- eval_harness/smokechecks/token_saliency.py: new smokecheck implementing token-level attribution fingerprints, baseline snapshot loader, and drift score computation. The algorithm computes per-token average saliency vectors across a prompt cohort and reports Jensen-Shannon divergence aggregated to prompt-level and cohort-level signals. Includes configurable sampling and smoothing to avoid noisy single-run spikes.
- eval_harness/ci/soft_fail_adapter.py: CI adapter that integrates with the existing eval CI pipeline; it inspects smokecheck outputs and, if the check is in 'soft' mode, converts non-critical failures to annotations and a non-blocking status. Soft mode is time-bounded and respects team-level whitelists.
- tests/test_token_saliency.py: unit tests for saliency computation, small synthetic prompts with deterministic saliency maps, edge cases (zero-length token sequences), and missing attribution entries.
- ci/workflows/eval-smokechecks.yml: add step to run the token saliency smokecheck and conditionally trigger soft-fail behavior based on repo config file.
- docs/smokechecks/token-saliency.md: short design doc and migration notes for teams enabling the check.
- examples/prompt_sets/saliency-demo.jsonl: small prompt cohort used in integration test and demo runbook.

Commits (summary):
- c1b3f8d: initial token_saliency module with core saliency fingerprint logic and tests
- a2d4f9b: add CI adapter + workflow integration and configuration parsing
- f7e9b2a: tighten vector normalization, add smoothing kernel and sampling harness
- be4d2ca: docs, examples, and fix edge-case tests; update changelog

Design notes / algorithm:
- We treat attribution maps as token-anchored score vectors; for each prompt in a cohort we normalize token scores by L1 and compute a distribution over token positions. The detector computes an empirical distribution over positions aggregated across the cohort and compares current-run distribution to the saved baseline via JS divergence.
- To avoid spurious alerts from short runs, the smokecheck requires minimum cohort size and a median-token-length threshold. Low-signal cohorts are skipped and annotated with a reason.
- The detector exposes tunables: cohort_window, sample_fraction, smoothing_alpha, and js_threshold. Default values are conservative (higher threshold, stronger smoothing) to prioritize precision over recall on first rollout.

Testing and QA:
- Unit tests cover normalization, divergence calc, and guard rails for missing/zero attributions.
- Integration test runs the workflow against examples/prompt_sets/saliency-demo.jsonl in CI matrix (small/medium cohorts).
- Local manual runs validated behavior across three baseline snapshots (stable, drifted, and adversarial). Results recorded in the PR artifacts.

CI behavior and incidents:
- Initial CI run (2024-11-16) showed one flaky test in tests/test_token_saliency.py on macOS runner (timing-dependent). Flake traced to async RNG seeding; added deterministic seeding in f7e9b2a and retried.
- Soft-fail adapter enabled in repo config for the first two weeks of rollout; by default it annotates failures and does not block merges. A follow-up job (ENG-1210) will flip enforcement after verification.

Review thread (highlights):
- Diego Marques: "Thanks — solid design. A few asks: add explicit overflow protections in JS divergence impl and ensure the adapter respects override flags from repo config." (addressed in a2d4f9b and be4d2ca)
- Asha Raman: "Can we expose a debug-mode to emit per-prompt token heatmaps to artifacts? That would be useful for triage." (added optional debug artifact; gated by env var)
- Samir Patel: "We should not rely on attribution format being dense arrays; added a comment to normalize sparse inputs." (handled in normalization helper)
- Author (Priya): replied inline to each comment and pushed fixes. Final approval from Diego and Asha.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main with soft-fail adapter turned on for the org default config (non-blocking).
2) Monitor annotated findings via the eval console dashboard for 14 days (metric: percent cohorts flagged, median JS divergence).
3) Triage top 20 flagged prompts/week, tune js_threshold and smoothing_alpha accordingly.
4) Flip adapter to blocking after ENG-1210 verifies signal quality or extend soft window if noisy.

Backward compatibility and impact:
- No breaking changes to public SDKs or API surfaces. The smokecheck is opt-in via repo config. Teams not opting-in will see no changes.

Notes for release notes:
- Introduces a conservative token-level saliency smokecheck to detect attribution drift across prompt cohorts. Includes a CI soft-fail adapter to reduce noise during initial rollout.

Additional pointers:
- Linear: ENG-1182 (detector prototype), ENG-1210 (rollout & enforcement runbook)
- Design doc: docs/smokechecks/token-saliency.md

Merge: Squash merged by Diego Marques on 2024-11-21 after CI green and approvals.
Add token-level saliency smokecheck and a CI adapter that soft-fails noisy regressions to reduce noise during rollout. No user-facing API changes.

payload.body:
Context and motivation:
Small, targeted prompt-set changes have produced outsized regressions on a few high-risk cohorts in production. Existing CI gates surface aggregate regression signals but frequently miss concentrated susceptibility where a low-volume cohort experiences large quality drops. This PR implements a Cohort Susceptibility Index (CSI) plus a CI soft-blocker hook that integrates with the existing eval runner to flag merges that are likely to cause concentrated regressions.

What this PR does (single-string summary):
- Adds a new metric (CSI) that quantifies cohort-level sensitivity by combining effect size, variance amplification, and token-entropy-weighted failure concentration.
- Adds a CI hook (soft-blocker) that computes CSI + configured quality deltas and returns a soft-fail decision (block for manual review or auto-suggest rollback) rather than a hard pipeline failure by default.
- Wires CSI into the decision layer so team-specific thresholds and hysteresis (entropy hysteresis to reduce flapping) are respected.
- Adds telemetry events and an ops runbook to triage flagged cohorts.

Checklist:
- [x] Metric implementation (eval/metrics/chi.py)
- [x] CI hook and decision layer (eval/ci/hooks/soft_blocker.py)
- [x] Unit tests (tests/test_chi.py)
- [x] Integration test with a small synthetic cohort (tests/integration/test_soft_blocker_integration.py)
- [x] Docs and runbook (docs/ci/soft_blocker.md)
- [x] Benchmarks and lightweight perf test (benchmarks/chi-bench.toml)

Commits (summary):
- feat(eval): add cohort susceptibility index implementation and helpers
- feat(ci): add soft-blocker CI hook with hysteresis and threshold config
- test: add unit + integration tests for CSI and CI hook behavior
- docs: runbook and example configs for teams + CI YAML snippet
- perf: add microbench harness and baseline numbers for common prompt lengths

Files changed (high level):
- eval/metrics/chi.py (new)  -- CSI core algorithm, normalization, docstrings, small utility functions for cohort aggregation
- eval/ci/hooks/soft_blocker.py (new) -- CI hook that calls eval runner, computes CSI, compares against per-team thresholds, emits telemetry, and returns soft-block decision payload
- tests/test_chi.py (new) -- unit coverage for edge cases (zero-variance, small-cohort smoothing, entropy weighting)
- tests/integration/test_soft_blocker_integration.py (new) -- lightweight end-to-end exercise with synthetic cohorts and mock telemetry sink
- docs/ci/soft_blocker.md (updated) -- runbook, signal explanation, troubleshooting steps, and example Linear/Jira escalation templates
- examples/ci-config.yaml (updated) -- example threshold config and hysteresis settings for teams
- benchmarks/chi-bench.toml (new) -- bench cases and target SLOs for CSI compute time

Design notes and algorithm summary:
CSI is intentionally conservative: it amplifies effect-size signals for cohorts with high per-example variance and high token-entropy (common failure modes are more critical when model is confident on wrong outputs). The score is a bounded scalar in [0,1] where higher means more susceptible. We use a clamped winsorization on extreme outliers and a sample-size-aware smoothing term so small cohorts do not spike the CSI unless the effect size is large and consistent. Hysteresis: CI stores the last N CSI values per cohort (configurable) and reduces flip-flopping by requiring sustained elevation above threshold for auto-block escalation.

Telemetry and observability:
- Emits chi_evaluation.start / chi_evaluation.end for each CI run with CSI, cohort id, sample size, and contributing metric breakdowns.
- Adds a CSI breakdown panel to existing eval dashboards (instructions in docs).

Review conversation (abridged):
- Arjun Patel (reviewer): "Nice approach. Two asks: (1) clamp the entropy weight so adversarially long open-ended prompts don't dominate; (2) add an opt-out flag per repo/team."
- Maya Chen (author): "Addressed both: added entropy cap in chi.py (entropy_cap config) and added team_opt_out flag in CI hook; updated examples/ci-config.yaml and tests to cover opt-out path."
- Lina Morales (reviewer): "Integration test flaky on CI runner initially, likely due to timeout. Can we reduce synthetic payload size?"
- Maya Chen: "Reduced synthetic cohort size and added retry/rerun in test harness. CI rerun passed."
- Samir Gupta (reviewer): "Please ensure runbook includes first responder checklist and Linear template."
- Maya Chen: "Docs updated with Linear template and three-step triage."

CI and validation:
- Initial CI: unit tests passed, integration job failed once due to timeouts on the macstadium runner.
- Rerun: all checks green.
- Performance baseline: CSI compute ~18ms per 1k examples on our CI runner (benchmarks/chi-bench.toml).

Backward compatibility and rollout plan:
- Default is soft-fail; teams must opt-in to hard blocking in examples/ci-config.yaml. This prevents accidental pipeline hard failures.
- Rollout: enable telemetry for 1 week for a pilot team, collect flagged cohorts, iterate on thresholds.

Merge outcome:
- Merged via squash on 2025-02-20 after reviewers approved. Merge commit: "squash: add cohort susceptibility index + CI soft-blocker (ENG-2431)"

Follow-ups and TODOs:
- Add cross-model calibration to CSI (follow-up ticket ENG-2478).
- Add UI drilldown in the dashboard for flagged cohorts (PM-118).
- Add a small canary on Dedicated instances to exercise heavy prompt-length distributions before wider rollout.

If you want to test locally: see docs/ci/soft_blocker.md for a step-by-step, or run `pytest tests/integration/test_soft_blocker_integration.py -k local` to exercise the synthetic scenario.

References: ENG-2431 (Linear), internal runbook link (docs/ci/soft_blocker.md).
- Add Cohort Susceptibility Index (CSI) to score prompt cohorts for regression sensitivity.
- Add CI soft-blocker hook that gates merges when CSI + quality delta exceed thresholds (soft-fail with automated rollback suggestion).
- New unit and integration tests; updated docs and runbook for ops response.

payload.body:
Adds a timeline sensitivity reporter and a non-blocking CI hook that reduces false-positive regressions using a noisy-prompt bloom filter. No public API changes.
Motivation: We repeatedly see short-lived spikes in per-prompt regression signals that trigger noisy CI failures or noisy alerts. This PR introduces a timeline-based sensitivity reporter that aggregates per-prompt metric deltas over sliding time windows and applies robust smoothing + outlier suppression so transient blips do not immediately escalate.

Design summary: The reporter computes a per-prompt sensitivity series (delta in metric vs baseline) on each eval run and maintains a short-term timeline of snapshots (default 7 recent evaluations spanning multiple CI runs). The series is processed with an EMA (alpha configurable) followed by a Hampel-style outlier detector to identify single-point spikes. Prompts flagged as "noisy" are tracked in a per-window Bloom filter so the CI hook can suppress gating for prompts that have historically shown intermittent volatility. The CI hook is non-blocking by default and emits advisory regression tickets; teams can opt-in to fail-on-regressions via a label or per-linear policy.

Implementation: - New module eval_harness.reporting.timeline_sensitivity.py: implements timeline state, EMA smoothing, Hampel detector, and Bloom filter windowing (4 hash functions, 1024-bit per-window by default). - CI adapter eval_harness.ci.timeline_hook: wraps existing smoke-eval runner, merges timeline snapshots from the run artifacts, and posts a structured advisory to the CI UI. - Persistence: timeline snapshots stored as small JSON blobs in the existing artifacts bucket under artifacts/eval/timeline/ to avoid introducing a new DB. - Config: feature toggles + thresholds via eval-config.yaml (new section 'timeline_sensitivity').

Testing and validation: added unit tests for smoothing/outlier logic and Bloom filter ops; added an integration smoke test that replays three synthetic eval runs to validate suppression behavior. Locally ran the end-to-end smoke suite and a short perf benchmark.

Rollout plan: feature behind config flag off by default. Ship as advisory for 2 weeks, monitor advisory-to-action ratio. Post-rollout, we will expose an opt-in gating mode for teams that want automatic quarantine of severe regressions.

Notes: This is intentionally non-invasive: no changes to existing metric schemas, downstream dashboards, or alerting. Intended to reduce noise in CI/regression pipelines and speed triage.
Unit tests for smoothing and bloom filter; integration replay with synthetic volatility; manual end-to-end run on staging pipeline to verify advisory payload and artifact persistence. Added CI smoke run that simulates a noisy prompt spike and verifies suppression behavior.
Maya Chen: Nice work on the Hampel integration — can you add a short justification for the chosen window sizes in the config docs?
Diego Alvarez: Added rationale and links to our historical variance analysis in the runbook (docs/ops/timeline-sensitivity-runbook.md).
Liam O'Connor: Concern: artifacts bucket writes may race when parallel CI jobs run for the same PR. Suggest using per-run temp filenames and an idempotent merge.
Diego Alvarez: Addressed with per-run temporary snapshot + atomic rename and a merge routine that is commutative; added tests to exercise parallel merge.
Priya Kapoor: Tests look good; can we add a small performance note in release notes about expected overhead?
Diego Alvarez: Added perf note: overhead ~+30–50ms on typical smoke eval run; no measurable token processing impact.

payload.body:
Motivation: our current eval CI treats model quality and latency as independent signals. In practice, increased tail latency (p95/p99) often correlates with degraded quality for production prompts, and teams have been forced to choose between passing quality gates at the cost of unacceptable latency or failing fast on latency regressions while ignoring subtle quality changes.

What this PR does: introduces a latency-aware quality-weighting mechanism and a CI SLO enforcer that folds latency penalties into the quality score used by CI gates. The evaluator computes per-prompt quality metrics (accuracy/f1/semantic-similarity) as before, then applies a latency penalty function across configured latency buckets to produce a single weighted_quality metric. The CI hook compares weighted_quality against a per-project threshold and an allowable latency SLO.

Key design points: 1) Latency penalty is configurable via an exponential decay: penalty = exp(alpha * (latency_ms - bucket_center)/bucket_center) clipped to [0,1]. 2) Buckets are derived from historical percentiles (p50,p95,p99) by default; teams can override buckets in eval_config.yaml. 3) Weighted quality preserves interpretability by reporting breakdowns: raw_quality, latency_penalty, weighted_quality. 4) CI enforcer supports soft-fail mode (annotate + do not block) and hard-fail mode. Soft-fail is default for new projects. 5) Provides a backfill tool to recompute historical weighted_quality for dashboards and alert thresholds.

Files changed: adds core scorer at eval_harness/metrics/latency_weighted.py, a CI hook at ci/hooks/latency_quality_gate.py, integration test harness and unit tests under tests/, a docs page describing config and SLO semantics at docs/ci/latency-quality-slo.md, a dashboard SQL snippet, the CI workflow to run the new gate, and a short changelog entry.

Testing and validation: unit tests cover penalty math, bucket derivation, and config overrides. Integration tests run a synthetic prompt set with injected latency distributions to validate gate behavior across soft/hard modes and different thresholds. Benchmarks show median extra runtime of ~3ms per eval run (mostly from percentile aggregation); we ship a caching layer for historical percentiles to mitigate CI cost.

Backward compatibility: defaults to soft-fail and no penalty if latency history is unavailable. No mandatory changes required for existing eval configs.

Follow-ups: 1) Add a UI control in the Console for toggling soft/hard mode and tuning alpha per project (ENG-1107). 2) Explore per-cohort alpha tuning in a later PR.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation (scorer + CI hook)
- [x] Unit & integration tests
- [x] Benchmarks & micro-optimizations (cache for percentiles)
- [x] Docs and changelog
- [x] Telemetry/dashboard query

Links: Linear: ENG-1024, related eval infra work ENG-980.
Anika Shah (reviewer): Questioned the default alpha value and asked for a short guideline on how teams should pick alpha; requested a small table in docs with example alphas for typical latency profiles.
Maya (author): Added a guideline section and example table in docs; default alpha set conservatively to 0.002 with note to tune per-cohort.
Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Noted concern about noisy latency percentiles in small test sets causing flakiness; suggested adding a minimum-sample check and a cached historical baseline.
Maya (author): Implemented a sample_size threshold and cache for historical percentiles; integration tests updated to simulate cache warm/cold paths.
Priya Nair (reviewer): Asked for clarity on how the gate interacts with existing regression locks and whether it will block release automation.
Maya (author): Documented interaction and set soft-fail default; hard-fail requires explicit opt-in via eval_config.yaml.
Anika Shah (reviewer): Ran the new CI workflow on a noisy internal prompt set and requested an opt-out flag per-prompt-cohort.
Maya (author): Added cohort-level opt-out in the config and corresponding tests.

payload.body:
Summary: Adds a lightweight execution-verification smoke hook to the eval-harness that runs generated code snippets from execution-targeted prompt sets inside a constrained sandbox. The goal is to detect regressions that cause runtime failures or semantic breaks (exceptions, wrong exit codes, or deterministic output mismatches for small, executable examples) rather than purely surface-level text metrics. Motivation: Several recent regressions in code-generation workloads were only detectable via execution. Relying solely on token/semantic similarity increased false negatives for obvious runtime regressions. This PR introduces a first-class CI hook that can be attached to prompt cohorts annotated for execution testing and integrated into existing CI gates.

What this change does (high level):
- New module eval_harness/hooks/execution_smoke.py implements: 1) a runner interface that supports Python and NodeJS snippets, 2) per-example execution expectations (exit code, stdout matcher, time budget), 3) a scoring function that converts observed failures into a weighted regression score used by CI gating logic.
- Provides a small sandbox image (tools/sandbox/dockerfile.exec-runner) used by CI for deterministic, isolated runs. Sandbox enforces CPU, memory, ephemeral FS limits and disables network by default.
- Adds a CI job (eval_harness/ci_jobs/execution_smoke.yml) that runs the hook on changed prompt-sets or on-demand when the PR touches exec-tagged examples.
- Example prompt set (examples/prompt_sets/executable_examples.jsonl) demonstrating expected metadata per example: language, run_command, expected_stdout_pattern, timeout_ms.
- Tests (eval_harness/tests/test_execution_smoke.py) covering runner timeouts, pattern matching, sandbox invocation mocking, and scoring thresholds.
- Documentation (docs/eval/hooks.md) describes how to annotate prompt sets, configure timeouts, and interpret gate scores.

Design notes and safety: The sandbox has strict resource caps and explicit opt-in for network. The execution hook only runs examples explicitly marked with "exec": true in the prompt set metadata; arbitrary prompts are not executed. We run examples under a minimal unprivileged user inside a container and mount a transient tmpfs. Timeouts are enforced both at the container level and in Python harness logic to avoid stuck jobs.

Scoring and gate behavior: Each example maps to one of three outcome categories: PASS, SOFT_FAIL (non-deterministic mismatch or flaky runtime), HARD_FAIL (exception, crash, or timeout). Gate calculates a weighted failure rate: HARD_FAIL weight=1.0, SOFT_FAIL weight=0.4. If weighted failure rate > 0.05 for a prompt cohort, CI fails the eval gate. Gate is configurable via job parameters and can be set to warning-only in ephemeral branches.

Rollout plan: Start as optional CI job on main for exec-annotated prompt sets (1 week shadow runs), then flip to a required eval gate for repos with high code-generation traffic based on ENG-2479 signals. We will monitor false positive rate and adjust SOFT_FAIL weights and sample size.

Commit summary: - 8c1a2b: initial exec hook module and runner interface - 3f4d7e: add dockerfile and CI job definition - b6d9aa: add example promptset and basic tests - 1a2bb3: tighten timeouts and sanitize inputs - d4e5f6: add docs and CI parameterization

Files changed (high level): eval_harness/hooks/execution_smoke.py — core logic (~430 LOC), tests — unit cases for semantics (~120 LOC), ci job YAML — integration wiring, docs — guidance for annotating prompt sets, sandbox dockerfile.

Review conversation (high level, condensed):
- Evan McCormick (2025-09-04): "Nice end-to-end design. Two asks: (1) ensure we have an allowlist for language runtimes and avoid enabling arbitrary interpreters, (2) can the runner produce structured telemetry (exit_code, runtime_ms, mem_kb) for downstream dashboards?"
- Maya Patel (author) reply (2025-09-04): "Agree on allowlist; initial implementation supports python3.11 and node16 only; added explicit checks. Added structured telemetry output (json lines) to the runner and tests."
- Sofia Liang (2025-09-05): "Concern about flakiness — will this gate be overly sensitive for non-deterministic outputs?"
- Maya Patel reply (2025-09-05): "We added SOFT_FAIL category and sampling-rate parameter to escalate only on sustained regressions. Also safe default sample size is small (20 examples) to limit noise."
- Ravi Kapoor (2025-09-06): "Security question: make sure container image is rebuilt regularly and signed. Also, add an optional dry-run mode that doesn't run containers in PR comments."
- Maya Patel reply (2025-09-06): "Added CI step to pull signed images and a dry-run flag. Documented recommended image rebuild cadence."
- Evan McCormick (2025-09-07): Approved, "Looks good; tests cover core paths and gate tuning is configurable."

CI Summary: The execution_smoke job runs on a self-hosted runner with the sandbox image. The pipeline runs the hook on 20 sampled examples from exec-tagged prompt-sets. Initial run reported 1 SOFT_FAIL and 0 HARD_FAILs; final CI run after fixes passed. Lint, unit tests, and integration job all passed on re-run. ci_status: pass.

Merge outcome: Merged via squash on 2025-09-08 after all approvals and CI green. Merge method: squash. Release notes: "Add execution-verifier ci hook for executable prompt-sets; enables early detection of runtime regressions in code-generation workloads. Configurable thresholds and sandboxed runner included."

Backward compatibility and next steps: The feature is opt-in via prompt metadata. Next PR will add a Grafana dashboard to visualize execution failure trends and wire up alerts when weighted failure rate exceeds configured thresholds. We will also add additional language runtimes after security review.

payload.body:
Motivation: Current prompt-set regression gates treat all failing prompts equally, which makes canary rollouts brittle when a small fraction of high-severity prompts dominate the failure signal. This PR introduces a quantile-based prompt severity estimator and a staggered canary CI adapter that weights failures by estimated severity and stages rollbacks progressively based on quantiles instead of absolute counts.

What this change does (single-string overview): Adds a lightweight severity scorer that integrates model confidence, token-level divergence, and historical impact (how often a prompt failure correlated with downstream user-facing regressions). The scorer emits a 0..1 severity score per prompt. We then compute quantile buckets (p50/p75/p90/p95) over the failure-weighted severity distribution for a given CI run. The new CI gate triggers progressive actions: for p50/p75 it annotates and stalls the PR for human triage; p90 triggers a canary hold and notifies on-call; p95 triggers an automatic rollback of the canary and opens an incident candidate. The staggered behavior reduces noisy rollbacks while surfacing high-impact regressions rapidly.

Implementation notes: - New module eval_harness/metrics/severity_estimator.py implements the ensemble scoring pipeline with pluggable features (confidence_gap, token_entropy_delta, historical-impact-score). The estimator is deterministic given a seed and includes a per-project calibration file under eval_harness/config/severity_profiles/*.yaml. - CI adapter added under ci/adapters/staggered_quantile_gate.py which subscribes to evaluation run artifacts, computes quantiles, and maps quantile thresholds to actions via a small policy DSL. - Unit and integration tests under tests/quantile_gate/* validate quantile calculation, deterministic bucketing across seeds, and policy triggers in synthetic runs. - Console & alerts: adds a new per-PR annotation that shows the severity distribution sparkline and links to top-k high-severity prompts. - Backwards compat: feature is behind feature flag eval.enable_quantile_severity_gate (defaults to off).

Migration and rollout: Start in dev CI (off by default). We enabled the gate in a staging workspace for 2 weeks to compare with existing count-based gate. Staging showed 35% fewer automatic rollbacks while detecting the same high-severity incidents earlier in the canary window. Rollout plan in Linear ENG-2145 covers a 4-week ramp with opt-in by repo owners.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement severity estimator and quantile calculation
- [x] Add CI adapter and policy mapping
- [x] Tests: unit, integration, and smoke tests
- [x] Docs: brief runbook and config examples in docs/eval/quantile-severity-gate.md
- [x] Feature flag and migration plan

Risks and mitigations: Severity profiles may need per-team tuning; profiles are stored per-workspace and can be tuned without code changes. Determinism across runs is ensured by seeding and canonical sorting; we added a reproducibility test to catch non-deterministic aggregations.

Related work: contrasts with count-based and weighted-count gates (see ENG-1802). This approach prioritizes impact and reduces sensitivity to noisy low-impact failures.
Marco Ruiz: Overall this looks promising. One concern: historical-impact-score may bias towards older incidents. Can we decay history exponentially?
Priya Desai: Good call — implemented time-decay with a configurable half-life (default 30 days) in severity_estimator; added unit tests to validate decay behavior.
Jordan Li: I saw a small nondeterminism in quantile boundaries on Python 3.8 vs 3.10 in CI. We need canonical sorting before bucketing.
Priya Desai: Fixed by sorting (prompt_id, seed) before aggregation; added reproducibility test across interpreters.
Samantha Ng: Docs look good; can you add a short troubleshooting section for 'sudden p95 spikes' and what to check?
Priya Desai: Added a troubleshooting section with recommended checks: recent model rollouts, prompt set size changes, spikes in token-entropy delta, and calibration profile mismatches.
Marco Ruiz: Approving after one nit (rename variable `q_cutoff` -> `quantile_thresholds` for clarity).
Priya Desai: Renamed and pushed squash commit. Thanks!
CI Bot: flaky-test-suite/test_streaming_quantiles failed on first run (timeout). Reran and passed. Final CI: all checks green.
