payload.body:
Summary: Adds a CI hook and orchestration component that computes a differential linguistic coverage score between new and baseline prompt-sets and enforces a soft-fail gate when coverage delta exceeds thresholds. Motivation: Some recent regressions were triggered by distributional shifts in token-level morphology and named-entity coverage across prompt cohorts; numerical metrics missed these because they aggregated at a semantic level. This PR introduces a reconciler that: (1) computes n-gram and morphological span coverage over prompt-sets, (2) aligns tokenization-robust shards between runs, (3) produces a compact coverage diff and an explainable report with top divergent spans, and (4) plugs into CI to fail builds when the differential coverage exceeds configurable sensitivity tiers. Checklist: - [x] Implement reconciler core and exporter - [x] Add unit tests for tokenization aligner and diff heuristics - [x] Add CI hook integration + smoke test in eval pipeline - [x] Add documentation and runbook entry - [x] Add Linear links and changelog entry Changes in this PR: commits: see commit_summaries field; major files changed listed in changed_files. How it works: The reconciler ingests two serialized prompt-set snapshots (baseline and candidate), canonicalizes tokenization using a configurable token normalizer (handles whitespace/punctuation variants, Unicode normalization, and optional subword collapse), extracts span-level identifiers (n-grams up to 4, morphological lemma signatures, named-entity markers), and computes coverage histograms. We then compute a differential coverage vector and summary metrics: overall coverage delta, uncovered-top-k, and span-frequency-shift. The CI hook executes on PRs that touch prompt-sets or eval configs; it runs a small sampled evaluation (configurable sample size) and rejects the PR if the sensitivity tier is triggered. Sensitivity tiers: - low: informational, annotate PR - medium: soft-fail with reviewer override - high: hard-fail (CI blocks merge) Backwards compatibility: The reconciler is opt-in via eval_config coverage_reconciler block; default behaviour is off to avoid unexpected CI failures for legacy repos. Docs and runbook: Added docs/eval/linguistic_reconciler.md and runbooks/coverage_reconciler.md with examples and remediation suggestions (e.g., tokenization aliases, cohort splitting). Runtime characteristics: The reconciler is optimized for incremental snapshots and runs in ~30-90s on typical prompt-set sizes (1k-5k examples) when sampling tier is medium. We included a caching layer keyed on prompt-set fingerprint to avoid repeated full recomputes. Runtime tests included cache hit/miss scenarios and a stress run against a 50k prompt-set sample. Rollout plan: - Merge to main behind feature flag - Enable low sensitivity on nightly smoke runs for 2 weeks - Enable medium sensitivity for PRs touching eval configs for a month and gather false positives - Consider default medium sensitivity after stabilization Related work and references: ENG-1428 (coverage regressions post-tokenizer-update), ENG-1439 (prompt-set drift detection design).
Evan Chen: Can we avoid false positives for tokenization-only diffs? Suggest adding a normalization preview output in the CI artifact so reviewers can see canonical forms.
Author(Aisha Malik): Added normalization preview artifact under artifacts/coverage_normalization_preview.json and updated the CI hook to upload it.
Priya Nambiar: The medium sensitivity tier sounds useful but we should have an auto-annotator that suggests fixes (token aliases) to reduce reviewer load.
Author(Aisha Malik): Added a prototype annotator that recommends alias rules for high-frequency divergent spans; moved to follow-up ticket ENG-1502.
Diego Morales: Tests look good but add a deterministic seed for the sampling runner to reduce flaky CI runs.
Author(Aisha Malik): Added deterministic seeding and test harness param; reran CI to confirm stability.
payload.title: Introduce differential linguistic-coverage reconciler and CI guard for prompt-sets

payload.body:
Motivation: Large regressions in eval metrics are frequently localized to a subset of prompts (e.g., a single new prompt seed or a topical cohort). Today our gates are binary and can cause noisy global rollbacks. This PR implements a diff-aware throttle that computes semantic-weighted distribution shifts and enforces a progressive quarantine/throttle policy. It also adds a semantic-SLA reporter that translates evaluation metrics into per-cohort SLOs (error-rate, latency-percentile and semantic-degradation) so on-call and product teams can reason about impact at the right granularity.

What this PR does (summary):
- New CI hook: hooks/ci/diff_aware_throttle.py — computes a semantically-weighted KS-style delta across prompt cohorts and outputs a throttle score used by the CI decision buffer.
- New reporter: reporters/semantic_sla/reporter.py — converts eval outputs into time-series SLOs and an approximation of how far an observed run is from SLA thresholds; publishes a compact JSON artifact used by the console.
- Metrics and traces: metrics/sem_sla_metrics.md + tracing hooks so each throttle decision and SLA delta is captured for post-mortem.
- Tests: unit tests for the weighting and throttle heuristic, an integration-style smoke harness that runs a small model against seeded prompt cohorts.
- Docs: docs/ci/diff-throttle.md with configuration knobs and rollout guidance.

Design notes:
- Semantically-weighted delta: prompts are embedded via the eval-harness embedding pipeline; cohort-level histograms are compared using a weighted Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) that prioritizes semantic mass rather than raw counts. This reduces noisy enforcement when the absolute count is small but semantics matter.
- Progressive quarantine: the throttle outputs a score in [0,1] which the CI decision buffer maps to actions: 0 -> allow merge, 0.1-0.4 -> gated canary (require canary run), 0.4-0.8 -> partial quarantine (block merge for flagged cohorts, allow non-impacted cohorts), 0.8+ -> full block. The mapping is configurable via ci/config.toml.
- Semantic SLA reporter: a small rule engine maps metric deltas to SLA signals (example: if semantic-degradation>0.05 for a cohort and latency-95 increases by 20ms, mark SLA as degraded). The reporter emits both human-readable summaries and structured JSON for the console ingestion pipeline.

Compatibility and rollout:
- Backwards compatible: if embeddings are not available the throttle falls back to a count-based delta (current behavior); the reporter will emit warnings but not fail.
- Gradual enablement: default off. Ship as an opt-in CI hook and a console ingestion endpoint. Suggested rollout: enable on non-blocking tier for two weeks, then move to gated canary, then to quarantine mapping.

Testing and validation: included unit tests (tests/unit/test_throttle.py), integration smoke (tests/integration/smoke_sem_sla.py) and a synthetic replay harness (tools/replay/synthetic_cohort_replay.py) to reproduce regression patterns. Run locally via `tox -e smoke` and CI runs evaluate against a tiny model to validate semantics and performance.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc and sync with SRE and console teams
- [x] Implementation of throttle algorithm + reporter
- [x] Unit tests and smoke integration tests
- [x] Docs and rollout guidance
- [x] Metrics/tracing hooks added

Notes for reviewers: pay particular attention to the weighting heuristic in diff_aware_throttle.py (function: compute_semantic_delta) and edge-case handling when cohorts are sparse. I wired a debug flag to store intermediate embeddings for one-off investigation.

Observability: new metrics emitted: eval.throttle.score, eval.throttle.action, eval.semantic_sla.delta_{cohort}, eval.semantic_sla.slo_status. Traces include the throttle decision tree and top-K prompts that contributed to the score.

Security: no secrets or credentials are introduced. The reporter output is sanitized to avoid exposing raw prompts; it only publishes cohort ids and anonymized exemplar hashes when configured.

Follow-ups:
- Hook into console UX for cohort-level visualization (ENG-4891)
- Auto-suggest rollback patches for quarantined cohorts based on exemplar diffs

Summary: This PR reduces noisy, global regression rollbacks by making the CI gate semantics-aware and provides an SLA-oriented reporting artifact to make regression impact tangible to downstream teams.
Jonah Blake: Nice approach. Two asks: 1) can you add a small sensitivity test for embedding noise? 2) make the mapping table for throttle->action also configurable via feature flags?
Author (Aisha Kapoor): Thanks Jonah — added sensitivity unit (tests/unit/test_throttle.py::test_embedding_noise_sensitivity) and moved the mapping into ci/config.toml with defaults. See commit d4f5a6b.
Rui Chen: I worry about EMD cost at scale. Can we cap to sampled exemplars and fall back to approximate hashing?

Motivation: some prompt-sets yield concentrated but high-impact regression failures in a small subset of queries. Current CI gates surface aggregate metrics (e.g., overall accuracy delta) but do not prioritize which failures matter most for product experience or operational cost. Both are exposed as a CI adapter so quality gates can optionally fail merges when high-PIS (Prompt Importance Score) queries regress by severity thresholds.

Motivation: CI early-warning gates were generating a high volume of noisy failures for long prompt-sets where failures clustered around overlapping semantic fragments. This PR introduces a 'semantic shingle' prober that extracts embedding-based shingles (semantic n-grams) from prompt sets, runs focused mini-evals across those shingles, and computes a precision-weighted failure score. The goal is twofold: 1) increase the signal-to-noise of regression detections by isolating semantic hotspots, and 2) provide a graduated rollback orchestration that applies replay backpressure instead of immediate full-suite rollbacks to avoid thrashing on intermittent instability.

What this changes (high level): Add a new prober module that performs shingle extraction using existing embeddings, an orchestration hook that schedules targeted mini-evals and aggregates a precision-weighted signal, and a CI-side rollback orchestrator that can: delay full replays, queue progressive mini-eval replays, and escalate to a full rollback only when aggregated severity passes configured thresholds.

Benchmarks: On a 1.2k-prompt internal SLO set, precision of flagged regressions improved from 0.62 -> 0.81 (fewer false positives), and the number of full-suite replays triggered by the CI gate dropped by ~47% in our simulated backlog run. Median additional CI latency introduced by the orchestrator was +3s (the orchestrator runs async and applies backpressure before expensive replays).

Commits summary: 1) Initialize semantic shingle prober and sampling api (semantics: cosine similarity cutoff, shingle size heuristics). 2) Add targeted mini-eval runner and deterministic replay wrapper. 3) Implement rollback_orchestrator with backpressure queue and escalation policy. 4) Integrate with ci/hooks and add config knobs (shingle_size, similarity_threshold, escalation_window). 5) Tests + docs + small refactors based on review feedback.

Small refactors: moved embedding cache helper into eval_harness/utils/embedding_cache.py to avoid duplication.

for prompt in prompt_set:
  tokens = tokenize(prompt)
  for window in sliding_windows(tokens, size=shingle_size):
    emb = embed(window)
    assign_to_cluster(closest_centroid, threshold=similarity_threshold)
"""

Motivation: Current eval CI gates are binary and sensitive to noisy prompt-level volatility. Teams have asked for a way to distinguish transient/flaky prompt regressions from systemic quality regressions and to tune gate sensitivity without creating a flood of hard failures. This PR introduces two components: (1) a resilience_score metric that summarizes historical volatility and recovery behavior per prompt cohort, and (2) a soft-fail tuner that converts hard CI gate failures into graduated outcomes (soft-fail / warn / hard-fail) based on resilience_score and run-level variance.

What this changes: Adds a new resilience index calculation to the eval metrics pipeline, updates the CI gate decision logic to consult resilience thresholds, and introduces a lightweight standalone CLI (evalctl resilience simulate) for teams to test gate sensitivity locally. The soft-fail tuner also hooks into the existing alerting pipeline so that low-severity regressions create slack/webhook warnings instead of PagerDuty pages by default.

Files and surface area: - metrics/resilience_index.py: implements resilience_score calculation and smoothing; includes configurable half-life and volatility window. - ci/gates/soft_fail_tuner.py: gate policy that maps metric delta + resilience to outcome. - evalctl/commands.py: adds 'resilience simulate' command to produce synthetic historical traces and run decisions. - tests/*: unit and integration tests for scoring, gating, and CLI. - docs/ops/resilience-guide.md: operational guidance and recommended thresholds.

Design notes: resilience_score is a bounded 0..1 score; low values indicate historically unstable prompts (high volatility), high values indicate stable prompts. The score combines: (a) smoothed historical variance of the prompt metric, (b) the median time-to-recover after previous regressions, and (c) prompt-level coverage (sample count). We use a rank-based normalization to make the score robust across metrics and models.

Backward compatibility: Default thresholds produce the previous behavior (hard-fail on threshold breach). Teams can opt-in to soft-fail via per-repo CI config, or run the CLI to preview effects. The metric calculation uses existing stored eval traces; rolling back is safe (no data schema changes).

- [x] soft-fail gate integration in CI

Motivation: production prompt sets can become brittle when anchors are treated as static baselines. This PR implements a shadow-eval pipeline that runs candidate prompt/model combinations against a sampled mirror of production traffic and introduces a decay-weighted regression gate for CI. The decay-weighted gate reduces false-positive regression signals from stale anchors by applying a time-decay to historical anchor scores and combining them using an ensemble weighting scheme. Key goals: 1) Surface true regressions earlier with fewer noisy alerts, 2) allow continuous shadow validation against recent traffic without blocking canary rollouts, 3) provide actionable attribution for prompt- or model-driven regressions. What changed: - New shadow evaluation worker that consumes a sampled, privacy-safe traffic stream and records per-prompt metrics (latency, semantic-match, tokenization failures, hallucination score) in the eval DB. - Decay-weighted regression gate implemented as a CI hook that computes a weighted baseline from historical anchors using exponential decay (configurable half-life per cohort). - Introduced an aggregator that fuses live shadow metrics with scheduled cohort evals to produce a stability score and an optional soft-fail that annotates PRs instead of hard-blocking when sensitivity is low. - New telemetry (meter, tracer spans) and dashboards for shadow load, decay factor distribution, and gate firings. - Config knobs: half_life_days, min_anchor_samples, shadow_sample_rate, soft_fail_threshold. Implementation notes: - The decay logic is implemented in eval-harness/src/hook/decay_gate.py and is covered by unit and integration tests. - The shadow worker is a new process entrypoint in eval-harness/src/shadow/worker.py and supports dry-run vs active modes. - To avoid noisy alerts for low-volume cohorts, the gate includes a minimum-sample check and a stability damping term. Testing and rollout: - Unit tests added for decay math, weighting, and fusion logic. - Integration test simulating anchor drift and verifying gate behavior across half-life configurations. - Shadow pipeline tested end-to-end on synthetic traffic; initial rollout plan is opt-in for the top-20 prompt sets by traffic volume for two weeks. Caveats: - Shadow sampling adds modest extra cost; default sample_rate is 0.1% and can be tuned per org. - This PR does not change existing blocking gates; decay-gate is introduced as an opt-in CI hook until monitored for 2 weeks. Related work: ENG-4309 (anchor-serializer improvements), ENG-4610 (cohort telemetry standardization).

Add an episodic prompt snapshot sweeper and a gradual holdback CI hook to reduce transient noise in prompt-set regression signals and provide a controlled soft-fail path for short-lived spikes. Motivation: recent regression alerts showed high sensitivity to ephemeral prompt bursts that later self-corrected; this change introduces time-windowed snapshotting, decay-weighted anchoring, and an automated holdback policy that escalates failures progressively instead of failing CI immediately. The implementation includes a new Sweeper hook that folds prompt snapshots into short-lived episodes, a Holdback controller that gates CI failures into soft-warnings for the first N minutes/hours and then promotes to hard-fail if persistent, and a small companion tool to backfill historical episodes for retrospective analysis. This PR contains code, tests, docs, CI integration, and a short migration plan for existing prompt sets.

Motivation: We frequently see CI noise from changes that affect response length (verbosity) rather than core correctness. Motivation: We need a gate that can phase-in stricter regression checks across multiple prompt-set variants and weight them by production traffic mix. Existing gates are either binary or treat variants equally, which causes noisy failures from low-impact variants and slow rollouts when a single high-volume variant changes. This PR implements a phased "variant-weighted" quality gate plus an explainable failure reporter that surfaces per-variant contribution and suggested mitigations.

Summary of changes: added a PhaseGate orchestration that accepts variant weights and stage thresholds, a scoring adapter that produces per-variant metrics (accuracy, token-loss, semantic-distance), and an explainability module that generates a short failure report with example prompts, model outputs, and a concise mitigation recommendation. The gate supports three phases (shadow, canary, enforce) and automatically escalates or rolls back based on weighted aggregate score and high-impact-variant signals.

Why this is different: unlike our ensemble or cohort gates this approach natively models traffic-weighted importance, reduces alert fatigue from rare variants, and provides human-readable remediation suggestions to speed incident response. It also integrates with the CI decision buffer to allow staged rollouts during merge checks.

Motivation: Our smoke CI runs are dominated by stable cohorts and waste budget repeating low-signal prompts. This PR adds an adaptive priority sampler and a lightweight CI hook that biases selection toward cohorts with recent regression signal or high variance. Goals: 1) improve early detection of prompt-set regressions by increasing sampling density on fragile cohorts; 2) reduce average cost of smoke runs while maintaining coverage; 3) provide observability for why a cohort was sampled.

What this PR does: Adds an AdaptivePrioritySampler that uses a simple score = alpha * recent_regression_score + beta * variance_score + gamma * recency_boost, where weights are configurable. Integrates sampler as a CI hook (smoke_priority_sampler) that can be inserted into existing smoke pipelines; provides a replay-friendly seed for deterministic runs in CI. Includes: - sampler implementation and unit tests - CI adapter that emits selection telemetry and decision reasons to the smoke run trace - a small migration to add "priority_score" metadata to cohort manifests - docs for enabling and tuning the hook in the smoke CI job config (example included).

Checklist: [x] unit tests added for sampler logic and config parsing; [x] integration test for CI adapter simulating skewed cohort scores; [x] docs for ops + example smoke job snippet; [ ] e2e in staging smoke pipeline (follow-up, tracked ENG-4310).

Usage (short): Add smoke_priority_sampler to the smoke job's hooks list and set sampler.config.weights to tune. Default config is conservative (alpha=0.6, beta=0.3, gamma=0.1) and the hook is opt-in.

Related: ENG-4281 (smoke CI cost reduction), SUP-3421 (support ticket requesting more targeted regression checks).

Commits (summary): - 8f3c2b1: initial sampler and basic config parsing - b2d4ae5: hook adapter + telemetry emission - c14f7a0: tests for edge cases, deterministic seed handling - d9a8b21: docs and example pipeline snippet - e6f3c93: tweak default weights after perf review

Changed areas (high level): - eval_harness/samplers/priority_sampler.py (core logic, ~220 LOC) - eval_harness/ci/hooks/smoke_priority_hook.py (adapter) - eval_harness/tests/test_priority_sampler.py (unit tests) - docs/ci/smoke_priority_sampler.md (usage) - eval_harness/manifests/cohorts_v2.yaml (added optional priority metadata) - internal/tools/ci_templates/smoke_job.yaml (example insertion)

Small illustrative snippet (sampler scoring):
score = (alpha * regression_score) + (beta * variance_score) + (gamma * recency_boost)
# deterministic seed: seed = hash(run_id + job_name) % (2**32)

Why unique: Prior approaches (cohort reweighting) adjusted post-hoc; this sampler makes selection bias explicit and reproducible, plus it outputs a reason string per sampled cohort which helps triage blips in eval dashboards.

Risks & mitigations: Over-biasing could starve cold cohorts — mitigated by a floor probability per cohort and a configurable entropy cap. Performance: sampler is O(N) on cohort list and runs in <20ms for typical smoke sizes.

Motivation: Route-level A/B testing in Console needs a quality signal per {route, experiment_id, variant_id}. Today, eval-harness produces per-run artifacts (full JSON + HTML reports) but those are not consistently attributable to a routing experiment variant, and they’re too heavy for Console ingestion. This PR (1) propagates experiment attribution fields into eval execution and output artifacts, and (2) publishes a compact score stream suitable for near-real-time aggregation and dashboarding.

What’s included: (A) Variant tagging: add optional experiment context to eval runs, including experiment_id, variant_id, route_id, and a stable stickiness_key_hash (when provided), and persist these tags into (i) run metadata.json, (ii) per-prompt result rows, and (iii) summary.json. (B) Compact score stream: emit one record per {run_id, prompt_set_id, scorer_name} with normalized score, raw score, and minimal dimensions. This is designed to be ingested by Telemetry/Analytics and joined with experiment guardrails results without pulling full eval artifacts.

Schema (score stream v1): Each record is JSONL with fields: event_type=eval_score_v1, emitted_at, run_id, eval_suite_id, prompt_set_id, scorer_name, score_value, score_value_normalized, normalization_version, sample_n, model_id, model_revision, region (if applicable), route_id (optional), experiment_id (optional), variant_id (optional), attribution_source (router|manual|unknown), and trace_id (optional). Notes: (1) experiment_id/variant_id are omitted (not null) when not available to reduce payload size and simplify downstream cardinality controls; (2) scorer_name is restricted to an allowlist configured in eval-harness to prevent uncontrolled dimensionality.

Integration points: (1) CLI: new flags --experiment-id, --variant-id, --route-id, --attribution-source. (2) Runner API: EvalRunContext gains optional ExperimentAttribution. (3) Publishers: new ScoreStreamPublisher (default off) that can write to stdout (dev), file (integration tests), or the internal bus topic eval-score-stream-v1 (prod). The publisher is behind a config gate (EVAL_SCORE_STREAM_ENABLED) and can be enabled per environment.

Safety/rollout: Backward compatible. Existing artifact formats remain valid; we only add new keys. The score stream publisher is disabled by default. Added guardrails to avoid emitting records when scorer output is missing/NaN. Added sampling controls for very large prompt sets: emit summary scores always; per-prompt scores remain only in artifacts, not in the stream.

Testing: Added unit tests for attribution propagation, JSON schema validation tests for stream records, and an end-to-end fixture that runs a tiny suite and asserts that emitted JSONL contains correct experiment_id/variant_id. Also added a compatibility test to ensure older consumers parsing metadata.json don’t break.

Follow-ups (not in this PR): (1) finalize Console-facing ‘quality’ metric mapping and thresholds (Applied ML + Product); (2) telemetry aggregation jobs (ENG-9027) to roll up score stream by {experiment_id, variant_id}; (3) documentation updates for customers/internal operators on how evals attach to experiments.

Risk notes: Cardinality is controlled by keeping the stream to a small dimension set; do not add raw prompt text or user identifiers. stickiness_key_hash is salted and truncated to prevent correlation across customers while allowing debugging for a single run.
Example emitted record (JSONL): {"event_type":"eval_score_v1","emitted_at":"2025-03-14T22:18:07Z","run_id":"run_01HQ...","eval_suite_id":"suite_chat_safety_v3","prompt_set_id":"ps_legal_summaries_20","scorer_name":"rubric_helpfulness","score_value":0.78,"score_value_normalized":0.78,"normalization_version":"helpfulness_v2","sample_n":200,"model_id":"llama-3.1-70b-instruct","model_revision":"2025-03-01","route_id":"rt_8f2d...","experiment_id":"exp_2c1a...","variant_id":"var_b","attribution_source":"router"}
Dr. Maya Srinivasan: Can we confirm that scorer_name is stable and not user-controlled? We can’t let this explode dimensionally.
Jonas Weber (author): Yes—added an allowlist in config (scorers.allowlisted_for_stream). Non-allowlisted scorers still appear in full artifacts but are skipped for the stream with a warning counter.
Logan Wright: Please avoid emitting nulls for optional dimensions; our ingestion treats null vs missing differently and it can double series count.
Jonas Weber (author): Updated serializer to omit experiment_id/variant_id/route_id when not present. Added a test asserting key omission.
Caleb Johnson: We should include a schema_version field for forward compatibility (even if it’s v1).
Jonas Weber (author): Added schema_version: "1" to each record and updated schema + tests.
Selene Huang: For quality regression alerts we’ll need normalized score + normalization_version. Also need sample_n to interpret noise.
Jonas Weber (author): Both included. Added doc comment on normalization_version semantics and how to bump it.
Olivia Grant: Small nit: route_id should be the normalized route template, not raw path. Where does this come from?
Jonas Weber (author): The harness takes route_id from the caller (router integration). Added a note in README: route_id must be normalized upstream per platform conventions; harness will not accept raw paths.
Requested changes addressed: (1) scorer allowlist to limit dimensionality; (2) omit optional keys rather than emitting null; (3) add schema_version; (4) add README with producer contract + enablement; (5) add E2E test fixture.
Internal: eval-harness can now tag eval outputs with experiment attribution and (optionally) emit a compact eval score stream (eval_score_v1) for Console quality-by-variant dashboards. Publisher is disabled by default and requires EVAL_SCORE_STREAM_ENABLED.
1) Merge behind config gate (this PR). 2) Enable in staging for route experiments beta suites only (Applied ML). 3) Verify ingestion + aggregation with Telemetry (watch for cardinality + drop rate). 4) Enable in prod for selected suites; expand once Console results view consumes score stream.
No prompt text, user identifiers, or customer content emitted in the stream. stickiness_key_hash (if provided) is salted per env and truncated. experiment_id/variant_id are Redwood-internal identifiers; downstream access controlled by existing analytics RBAC.

Motivation: Several intermittent CI failures were traced to non-reproducible snapshot replay runs caused by clock skew in temporal bucketing and inconsistent seeding for prompt replay. This PR stabilizes the snapshot replay path and introduces a per-prompt failure classifier that tags common regression patterns (tokenization drift, context truncation, seed-induced variance) and emits a compact remediation hint in CI output. Changes include: deterministic seeding for replay runs, normalized timestamp bucketing (UTC-aligned, explicit windowing), a replay dry-run mode to detect drift before full CI, a small Bayesian failure classifier with human-readable labels and remediation suggestions, and a CI hook that attaches a replay artifact + classifier summary to failing runs. Checklist: - [x] deterministic seeding implemented and covered by unit tests - [x] timestamp bucketing refactor with backward compatibility shim - [x] classifier model + mapping table added and documented - [x] CI hook emits structured JSON artifact and human summary - [x] added runbook stub at docs/runbooks/replay_runbook.md - [x] integration smoke tests passing - [ ] add long-running flaky-test benchmarks (follow-up ENG-1482). See Linear tasks ENG-1420 and ENG-1482 for context. Links: linear/ENG-1420, SUP-384 for customer incident notes. Impact: should reduce transient CI noise for prompt-set regression checks and make triage faster by surfacing likely root causes in CI output.
Fixes nondeterministic behavior in snapshot replay and adds a lightweight failure classifier that maps regression signals to suggested remediation steps for CI engineers.
Non-breaking fix. Adds a new CI artifact type 'prompt-replay-summary.json' which can be consumed by dashboarding tools. Recommend release note: 'Improve CI reproducibility for prompt-set regression checks and add automatic failure hints to speed triage.'

Adds a CI hook that probes for prospective outliers in prompt sets and exposes retry-metered backoff suggestions. Non-breaking: opt-in via eval-config and feature flag.
Context: We see intermittent regressions caused by small subpopulations of prompt variants that trigger cascading failures in downstream routing and evaluation. Existing smoke checks surface aggregate regressions but often miss low-rate outliers that later amplify under load (e.g., when mini-batches align). This PR introduces a lightweight prospective outlier prober and a granular retry-metering hook for CI that helps quantify how brittle a prompt subset is under randomized perturbations. Motivation: detect low-frequency but high-severity prompt regressions early and provide automated, actionable telemetry (retry budget suggestions) so ops/engineers can tune canary/rollback policies. Summary of changes (single-line commits):
- Add prospective outlier prober orchestration and scheduler (adds probe harness, sampling strategy, and summary report).
- Implement perturbation mutations (token-level suffix/prefix noise, paraphrase via lightweight backtranslation shim).
- Introduce retry-metering adapter that simulates exponential backoff scenarios and reports a retry budget recommendation per prompt cohort.
- CI hook: integrate prober into pipeline as an optional staged job that can soft-fail (annotates PR) or hard-fail based on team-configured thresholds.
- Tests: deterministic seed tests for sampler, integration smoke for retry metrics, and e2e example run in GH Actions.
Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (link: https://linear.app/rw/issue/ENG-7812/prospective-outlier-prober) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration job added to .github/workflows/eval-ci.yaml (opt-in) - [x] Feature-flag gating and config added - [x] Docs entry in docs/probes.md (lightweight) Commits (high level):
* 3bb7fa2  add prober orchestration and sampling core (A. Patel)
* 8cdf6b1  implement perturbation shims and paraphrase adapter (A. Patel)
* d4f9a73  add retry-metering adapter and reporting schema (A. Patel)
* e1a5c2b  integrate CI job and feature flag (A. Patel)
* f38b9d0  tests and docs (A. Patel) Files touched (high level):
- eval_harness/probers/prospective_outlier.py (new): scheduler, sampler, report writer
- eval_harness/probers/mutations.py (new): suffix/prefix noise, paraphrase stub
- eval_harness/ci/hooks/retry_meter_hook.py (new): CI adapter and threshold evaluator

- eval_harness/config/sample_eval_config.yaml (modified): feature flag + thresholds Example config snippet included in docs: eval_probe: enabled: false thresholds: outlier_rate: 0.5% retry_budget_suggestion: auto
Review conversation (high-level):
- Miguel Santos (Nov 05): "Can the sampler be deterministic for CI runs? random seeds should be plumbed from env."
  - Aisha: "Yes — added deterministic seed plumbing and unit tests to assert reproducibility. See tests/unit/test_prospective_outlier.py"

Hook supports a "dry-run" and a "report-only" mode to avoid blocking pipelines during rollout. Backwards compatibility: default opt-out, config flag required to enable the CI job. Observability: outputs a compact JSON summary with per-cohort outlier_rate, median_retry_budget, p95_latency-increase (for mutated prompts). Merge rationale: provides a low-cost, opt-in safety net to find rare prompt regressions before they hit canaries. Merge method: squash and merge. Merged at 2025-11-11.

payload.body:
Motivation: We've seen intermittent metric oscillations across repeated eval runs (same prompt set, different seeds / sampling windows) that cause nondeterministic gate failures and noisy postdeploy regressions. This PR introduces a Historical Variance Detector (HVD) to detect when a prompt-set or cohort exhibits unstable score distributions over a sliding window of previous eval runs and optionally block merges.

What I changed (high level):
- Add a new module eval_harness/variance_detector.py that computes per-prompt and cohort-level variance, runs a two-sample KS test against the historical distribution, and produces a compact variance report.
- Add an opt-in GH Action workflow .github/workflows/variance-gate.yml that invokes the harness check with the new --variance-check flag on PRs targeting main and release/*.
- Extend the CLI: `harness check --suite <suite> --variance-check --lookback 8 --alpha 0.01 --delta-threshold 0.12` (defaults chosen to be conservative). The CLI returns non-zero if any cohort/prompt exceeds thresholds.
- Integrate an experimental `rollback_scorer` that surfaces the top-N prompts/cohorts contributing to variance; this hooks into the existing rollout recommendations UI (backend only) so SRE/Platform can inspect before rolling forward.
- Tests: add unit tests for distribution comparisons and an integration test that runs against a synthetic history store. Also add a small compatibility shim for older historical-run artifacts.

Commits (summary):
- c1f8b2e: initial variance-detector implementation + docs
- 7a2d9f4: add KS test and sliding-window logic; expose lookback/alpha flags
- e3b4a01: GH Action workflow for variance gate + small CI adapter
- 9f0a5c7: integrate rollback_scorer and add API surface for console
- f1d3b6a: tests and flaky-seed fix (see review notes)

Files changed (high level):
- eval_harness/variance_detector.py (+320 additions)
- eval_harness/cli.py (+18 additions) — new flags and wiring
- integration_tests/test_variance_gate.py (+42 additions)
- .github/workflows/variance-gate.yml (+45 additions)
- docs/variance.md (+30 additions)
- eval_harness/history/shim_compat.py (+20 additions)
- eval_harness/rollback_scorer.py (+35 additions)

Design notes and rationale: HVD is deliberately conservative: it only gates when both the normalized variance and a KS-test p-value indicate distributional shift beyond the delta threshold. This reduces false positives from isolated outliers. The sliding window defaults to 8 most recent eval runs (empirically chosen from internal history), but is configurable per-suite. We log compact histograms and top-contributors to make triage actionable.

Review conversation (abridged, chronological):
- Ethan Cole: "Can the detector be made resilient to differing sample sizes? If historical runs have different numbers of completions we should normalize or bootstrap." PRIYA: "Implemented sample-size-aware bootstrapped CIs in the latest commit; added integration test to cover uneven sizes." (commit 7a2d9f4)
- Maya Chen: "Please parameterize lookback and alpha at the suite level in addition to CLI flags; also document expected run cadence." PRIYA: "Added suite-level defaults in suite_config and updated docs/variance.md with recommended cadences." (commit e3b4a01)
- Luca Bianchi: "Flaky integration test: failing intermittently on CI due to RNG. Can we seed or use deterministic sampling?" PRIYA: "Fixed by seeding the synthetic generator and switching from random.gauss to numpy's Generator with PCG64 for deterministic draws in tests." (commit f1d3b6a)
- Maya Chen: "Approving — please squash on merge; would like a follow-up to wire alerts into Slack ops channel." (approval)
- Ethan Cole: "LGTM after one nit about log verbosity; not blocking." (approval)

CI & gating behavior observed on this PR:
- First run: variance-gate workflow failed due to the flaky integration test (intermittent rng). See job variance-integration (failed).
- Fix applied (seed deterministic RNG) and tests updated; second run: all checks passed (unit, integration, lint).
- ci_status: pass

Edge cases & limitations called out in review: historical store retention matters — if history is sparse the detector will gracefully degrade to a per-run warning mode rather than hard-failure. The KS test assumes continuous distributions; for very small sample sizes the detector falls back to a median-delta check (documented in docs/variance.md).

Compatibility & rollout plan: The variance gate is opt-in by default. We enabled it for the eval-harness repo in team CI to evaluate noise levels for 2 weeks. After that, teams can opt their suites into enforce=true to block merges automatically. The rollback_scorer is experimental and surfaced only as a backend API for now; Console integration will follow as a separate PR (ENG-4302).

Merge: Squash merge after approvals. Merged at 2025-11-05. Follow-ups: ENG-4302 (console UI), ENG-4311 (Slack alerts), and a cross-repo checklist to enable enforcement for prioritized suites.

Notes for QA/Oncall: If adopters see increased gate failures, check eval-harness history retention and per-suite lookback config. For urgent rollbacks, use the rollback_scorer API to identify candidate prompts to revert or to create targeted prompt filters.
Adds a historical variance detector to the eval harness and a new CI gating hook that fails PRs when prompt-set metric variance exceeds configurable thresholds; includes new tests and a small CLI flag for local evaluations.
This PR is intentionally conservative about gating and includes an opt-in path.
Follow-on work tracked in ENG-4302 and ENG-4311.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: We observed subtle regressions in scenarios where prompts compose multiple abstractions (e.g., nested template substitution, chained instructions, and role-switching). Existing prompt-set checks focus on surface metrics (accuracy, token-level delta) and miss compositional failure modes that only surface under suffix perturbations and multi-shot ordering changes. This PR introduces a compositional stress prober and a CI adapter to (1) systematically generate targeted perturbations, (2) score compositional fidelity, and (3) surface risky regressions to triage workflows.

What this change includes: implemented a new prober that synthesizes perturbations across three axes (suffix permutations, instruction chaining, and placeholder composition), a scoring function based on structural match + semantic similarity, a small smoke-suite of representative prompt-sets, and a CI adapter that integrates with the existing eval-gate architecture to raise a non-blocking 'compositional-risk' alert. Also added docs and a migration guide for teams who want to opt in.

Behavior and gating policy: By default the CI adapter emits a soft-fail (annotation + Slack/Linear notification) so teams are alerted without blocking merges. Projects can opt-in to a hard-fail by configuring a risk-threshold in eval-config. The adapter supports backfill runs and stores score deltas in the existing eval snapshots for longitudinal tracking.

Performance and cost: The prober is tuned to run as a low-cost smoke pass (sampled perturbations, capped shots, and early-exit rules). Empirically the added latency for the CI smoke step is ~14s on our dedicated smoke runners and cost is ~0.6% of standard eval budget in our sample workloads.

Backfill and rollout plan: Initial rollout is behind a feature flag. We'll run a 2-week backfill across high-priority prompt sets (ENG-4219 target list) to collect baselines and calibrate thresholds. After backfill we'll enable soft-fail by default and provide guidance for converting to hard gates.

Checklist: - [x] Prober implementation and unit tests - [x] CI adapter + integration tests - [x] Docs and examples - [x] Backfill harness and metrics collection - [x] Config knobs for opt-in/hard-fail

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the scoring heuristic conservative to reduce false positives. Follow-up work (ENG-4320) will add a learned calibrated regressor for risk scoring if teams opt into labeled regression data.
Adds a lightweight compositional stress prober plus a CI adapter that flags compositional regressions (soft-fail with triage). Includes docs and a smoke suite for prompt-set coverage.

Maya Hernandez (reply): Made the embedding provider pluggable via eval_defaults.yaml and added a note in docs on recommended provider pinning. Also added tests that exercise provider swap.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: We observed intermittent CI failures caused by high-variance, low-volume cohorts in our prompt sets. These failures frequently required manual triage and slowed rollouts. This change introduces 'Eval Shepherd', a lightweight probabilistic prober and adaptive-threshold adapter intended to stabilize CI gating while preserving sensitivity to real regressions.

What this PR does: Implements a cohort prober that samples prompts probabilistically across defined cohort strata, computes a per-cohort stability score (variance-aware fidelity metric), and uses a small Bayesian bootstrap autotuner to adjust CI gate thresholds per run. Adds a pressure-aware latch for CI (defer hard fail until variance and effective-sample-size criteria are met), a local CLI for devs to run sanity probes, and a webhook reporter that surfaces cohort-level anomalies to the eval dashboard.

Design notes: The probe intentionally favors stratified stochastic sampling rather than exhaustive replay so CI remains fast. The autotuner computes posterior credible intervals for the metric delta and only tightens the failure threshold when posterior mass exceeds caller-configured risk tolerance. The pressure latch implements a backoff that increases sampling budget when transient noise is detected.

Files and surface area changed: core shepherd runtime, a CI hook, a small CLI, unit/integration tests, docs, and an example probe config. No runtime-serving changes.

How it was tested: Unit tests for Bayesian estimator and latch (deterministic seeds), integration smoke runs against a three-model matrix (tiny/local mocks), and a staged run on the canary CI agent against a representative prompt snapshot.

Checklist:
- [x] Core probe implementation with deterministic unit tests
- [x] CI hook + config for pressure-aware latch
- [x] CLI for local repro and example config
- [x] Integration test with mocked eval backends
- [x] Documentation and rollout notes

Operational considerations: Default autotune parameters are conservative; rollout will start as a soft-fail (warning) in CI before promoting to hard-fail after two weeks. The webhook includes cohort fingerprints for triage and links to the snapshot used for the probe.

Migration path and rollout plan: Feature gated behind experiment flag in ci/configs/sentinel.yml. Enable soft-fail for two weeks, monitor cohort flood events and manual triage latency, then flip to hard-fail when pilot metrics show >30% reduction in false-positive CI incidents.

Related work: INGESTED from previous regressions analysis (ENG-1029); complements the context-length-aware regression gate (separate PR).

Notes for reviewers: Pay attention to the Bayesian credible-interval defaults and the effective-sample-size (ESS) calculations in shepherd/core/estimator.py. The autotuner is intentionally small (no external deps beyond numpy/scipy) to keep CI startup light.
Julian Meyer: Nice approach. Two asks: (1) add a short appendix in docs that explains the credible-interval math for non-stat folks, (2) make ESS calc more robust for zero-variance cohorts.
Anika Rao: Addressed both: added section 'Statistical appendix' to docs and added floor epsilon in ESS calc; updated tests to cover edge case.
Lina Chen: Can you add an e2e smoke script exit codes map so infra can ignore soft-fail presently?
Anika Rao: Added an exit-code flag and documented in CLI help; CI config keeps soft-fail mapping in sentinel.yml.
Marco Santoro: LGTM after nits (doc wording + one log level change).
Julian Meyer: Approved and performed merge.

payload.body:
Context: We need a lightweight, fast smoke evaluation that can run in CI and short-circuit regressions at a prompt-set level without waiting for full-scale evals. Motivation: recent incidents showed slow detection of prompt-specific regressions causing downstream rollback delays. This PR introduces a drift-anchored smoke-eval framework which anchors prompt severity to historical embeddings and scalar metrics, runs a compact probe suite in CI, and wires automatic failback policies that can recommend a fallback model variant or trigger a canary rollback if thresholds are exceeded. What this change does: 1) Adds a new smoke runner module eval_harness.runners.drift_anchor_smoke which computes per-prompt anchor scores using embedding-distance baselines plus a lightweight categorical-quality metric. 2) Introduces a CI hook eval_harness.ci.hooks.DriftAnchorSmokeHook that runs on PRs touching prompt sets or model adapters and produces a single pass/fail signal plus an HTML summary artifact. 3) Implements a per-prompt severity taxonomy and configurable thresholds (low/medium/high) backed by historical percentiles (90/95/99) so small noisy regressions are attenuated. 4) Adds an automated failback shim that suggests fallback model variants (fallbacks derived from model catalog metadata) and can mark PRs with suggested action labels (ci/failback-suggested). 5) Instrumentation: new telemetry metrics eval.smoke.anchor_score.*, eval.smoke.failed_prompts, and eval.smoke.recommended_fallback stored via the existing metrics client. 6) Tests: unit tests for anchor scoring logic, integration test for the hook, and a smoke e2e that runs against the local simulator. 7) Docs: quickstart snippets and troubleshooting runbook under docs/smoke-evals/drift-anchored.md. Rollout plan: merge into main behind a feature flag smoke_evals.drift_anchor.enabled=false by default, enable for canary projects via Linear ENG-2431 and then broader rollout after 2 weeks of telemetry. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of anchor scoring and thresholds. - [x] CI hook producing artifact and non-blocking default behavior. - [x] Unit and integration tests. - [x] Telemetry emission. - [x] Docs and runbook. - [x] Linked Linear tasks created. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is non-blocking; repositories not opting in will see no change. Known limitations: the initial anchor method uses off-the-shelf embeddings and can be sensitive to tokenizer changes; future work includes embedding-stable hashing and cohort-aware baselines. Related: ENG-2431 (drift detection platform), ENG-2507 (ci gating UX).
Rosa Almeida: Nice work, this addresses the slow detection issue we saw in the incident. Two asks before approving: add a metric tag for prompt_set_id and ensure the hook is opt-in by default.
Maya Patel: Thanks! Added prompt_set_id tag to the telemetry and wrapped the hook behind smoke_evals.drift_anchor.enabled=false in defaults.yaml. Also added notes about opting in in the docs.

payload.body:
Adds a lightweight "regression primer" workflow and a probabilistic flaky-prompt filter CI adapter to the eval-harness. Motivation: CI noise from transient prompt flakiness has been increasing (see ENG-5423) and leads to false-positive regressions; teams need a reproducible primer run and a statistical filter to avoid blocking merges for low-confidence failures. This PR implements three coordinated pieces: (1) regression primer: a fast pre-eval sampler that runs a deterministic, stratified subset of prompt anchors to produce a baseline expectation before full evals are scheduled; (2) probabilistic flaky filter: a small statistical layer that consumes per-prompt pass/fail histories and flags low-confidence failures (based on Bayesian posterior of failure rate) as soft-fails, emitting structured metadata so downstream automation can decide quarantine/retry policy; (3) CI adapter: GitHub Check integration and a CLI flag (--primer-mode) to run primer-only checks and annotate PRs with primer delta summaries. The description below documents config knobs, safety considerations, and operational expectations.

Config and behaviour: primer runs are limited to a configurable budget (default 200 prompts or ~5% of prompt set, whichever is smaller), use stratified sampling over cohorts and prompt difficulty bins, and always use a fixed seed and deterministic environment to maximize reproducibility. The flaky filter maintains an in-repo lightweight ledger (TTL-backed JSON) storing recent per-prompt outcome counts; on each run the filter computes a Beta posterior and a one-sided credible interval for the true failure rate. Failures with posterior probability > 0.9 of exceeding the configured threshold (default 15%) are marked hard-fail, while failures with medium probability (0.5-0.9) are labeled soft-fail and annotated with the posterior and suggested actions (retry, quarantine, human review).

Operational notes: the ledger is bounded (N latest entries per prompt) and the filter can operate in two modes: local-only (no external storage) and central ledger (optional S3/GCS). Latency overhead on CI is < 8% in practice (benchmarked on our smoke CI runners). The adapter emits structured JSON annotations and a human-readable primer delta summary inserted into the PR body. We intentionally keep the primer small so it is cheap to run on every PR; teams can opt into larger primer budgets in repo-level config.

Security and data: no model outputs are stored in the ledger, only pass/fail booleans and prompt identifiers; prompt ids can be hashed in high-security repos. We added config options to disable ledger persistence in private/on-prem installs.

Compatibility: integrates with existing eval-harness CLI and the GH Checks plugin; no change required to eval pipelines for baseline runs. Backwards-compatible default behaviour is unchanged: unless --primer-mode or the flaky filter is enabled in config, runs behave as today.

Related work: ENG-5423 (primer proposal), ENG-5499 (flaky-filter spec). This PR includes unit tests, deterministic smoke runs, and a migration script to generate an initial ledger from historical CI results (optional).

Nina: what happens for very small prompt sets (<100)? Are priors calibrated?

Riley: risk of masking real regressions if teams over-tune soft-fail threshold

Motivation: regression noise from few-shot / context variability can mask real model regressions. Teams have requested a lightweight CI-friendly tool that compares compact snapshots of output distributions across heterogeneous shot configurations (0-shot, 1-shot, random-k-shot) and raises percentile-aware quality gates. This PR implements a stability metric and on-pipeline snapshot comparator to detect prompt-set regressions that are driven by sensitivity to example selection or seed variability.

What this change does: introduces a HeterogeneousShotStabilityChecker that: 1) executes a prompt-set against a configurable set of shot-variation strategies (none, fixed exemplar, random sampled exemplars, stratified exemplar sampling) and random seeds; 2) computes per-query fingerprints (tokenized-response hash, normalized length, token saliency sketch) and aggregate distribution metrics (pairwise KL on token n-gram distributions, median pairwise edit distance, percentile stability score); 3) emits a compact snapshot (.hssnap) containing the sample-level fingerprints and telemetry suitable for CI delta comparisons. Adds a snapshot-compare CI hook that diffs two .hssnap artifacts and computes an SLO-aware stability delta (configurable thresholds per-cohort). If the stability delta exceeds thresholds the CI check fails with a concise failure report and suggested remediation hints (reduce exemplar variance, widen SLOs, run expanded shadow eval).

Files changed: lists include the core implementation under src/eval/hetero_shot_stability.py, the CI hook at ci/hooks/snapshot_compare.py, small CLI wrapper bin/hssnap (create/compare), schema additions in schema/snapshot_v1.yaml, unit tests in tests/test_hetero_stability.py, and docs in docs/eval/heterogeneous_shots.md.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of stability checker and comparator
- [x] Unit tests covering fingerprint generation and compare logic
- [x] CI hook integration and smoke test
- [x] Documentation and example prompt-set 
- [x] Backwards-compatible snapshot format with clear versioning

Rollout plan: the new CI hook is opt-in via .hssnap artifacts stored as build artifacts. Default thresholds are conservative (median stability delta > 0.15 triggers a soft fail in the dashboard but hard fail in CI only when explicitly opted-in via repo CI config). We will run this in shadow mode for 2 weeks on redwood/examples and opt-in repositories before recommending wider enabling.

Related: addresses ENG-1452 (reduce noise in prompt regression alerts) and complements existing cohort-based eval gates by focusing on sample-wise shot sensitivity.

Notes for reviewers: the snapshot format is intentionally compact (fingerprints + small skew sketches) to keep CI transfer sizes small and avoid full response diffs. Performance: default run uses sampled subset (configurable) to limit cost on CI; we include an optional longer-run mode for nightly jobs.

Maya Chen: Added test_cross_seed_long_context in tests/test_hetero_stability.py - it uses a sampled long-context template and asserts stability_score < 0.12 for baseline.
Priya Nandakumar: The snapshot format looks good; prefer explicit versioning in the filename rather than only schema inside. Please add v1 to created snapshots.

Priya Nandakumar: Approving after tests and docs; recommend running shadow test on redwood/examples for 1 week.
Diego Rivera: Approved - nice incremental approach and clear remediation hints.
Release Manager Bot: merged via squash — congratulations!

payload.body:
Motivation: We need automatic, fast feedback when prompt-set regressions or metric drifts occur. This PR adds a lightweight CI quality gate that runs a subset of the evaluation harness on PRs touching prompts, eval configs, or model-adapters. Gate decisions are based on configurable metric thresholds and on per-prompt regression checks.

What this does (single continuous description): Adds a new GitHub Actions workflow (/.github/workflows/eval-gate.yml) that runs a staged evaluation: 1) quick-run of the canonical regression prompt-sets with a strict timeout and sampled inputs; 2) compute core eval metrics (exact-match, F1, BLEU-lite, response-latency median) via the new eval-harness/metrics/adapter so integrations are consistent with downstream dashboards; 3) apply quality gate checks defined in eval-harness/quality_gates.yaml which include per-prompt allowable delta, global metric floors, and an opt-in strict mode for sensitive repositories; 4) if the gate fails, the workflow posts an annotated comment with a short summary and a link to the full artifacts; 5) if the gate passes, the PR can proceed and a green check is emitted.

Additional features: - New CLI flag eval-run --ci-sample to run a fast sampled evaluation in CI. - A light-weight cache for prompt outputs to speed reruns (used only in the workflow runner). - A documented fallback: maintainers can re-run the full eval job manually from the console with --ci-sample=false.

Why this is safe: The CI step defaults to a small sample size and strict wall-clock timeouts to keep run-time under the existing CI budget. The added files are isolated to the eval-harness repository and do not alter runtime model-serving code.

Rollout plan: - Initially gate only PRs that change prompt-sets, eval configs, or the eval-harness code paths (filtering is implemented in the workflow). - After two weeks of monitoring and tuning thresholds (ENG-4123), enable gates for SDK docs and examples.

Related: ENG-4123, ENG-4271. See the new docs at eval-harness/docs/quality-gate.md for operator guidance.

Maya Patel: Good call — added a deterministic seed derived from PR number when --ci-sample is used.
Priya Menon: Thresholds look aggressive for a first pass; recommend widening tolerances for BLEU-lite by +0.05.
Maya Patel: Relaxed BLEU-lite thresholds and added a 'strict' opt-in field in quality_gates.yaml so teams can opt into tighter checks.
Omar Haddad: CI artifacts are large — please upload only the JSON summary and the failing example set.
Maya Patel: Adjusted artifact upload to include summary.json, failing_examples.json, and a compressed tarball of raw outputs (max 10MB).

payload.body:
Context and motivation: Our prompt-set regression CI has been producing frequent noisy failures tied to small, cohort-specific regressions and run-to-run variance. Root causes include unbalanced replay (over-sampling small cohorts), single-metric gating that amplifies false positives, and lack of cross-seed replay. This PR implements two orthogonal features to address these problems: (1) a proportional replay orchestrator that constructs replay batches by weighting prompt cohorts proportionally to failure severity and sample variance across recent baselines; (2) a blended-quality CI gate that computes a composite score from multiple evaluators (task accuracy, per-prompt calibration, latency percentiles) and applies an adaptive threshold calibrated using historical variance. Both pieces are integrated into the CI pipeline with feature-flagged rollout and telemetry.

Summary of changes: commits below implement the orchestrator, the gate logic, metric exporters, tests, docs, and CI wiring. Key behaviors: proportional replay avoids overemphasizing tiny cohorts; cross-seed replay reduces seed-specific flakiness; blended-quality gate reduces single-metric sensitivity and supports configurable weights; adaptive thresholds use exponential smoothing over a 14-day baseline to stabilize gating decisions. Backwards-compatible defaults are provided so existing CI setups do not change until the feature flag is enabled.

Commits (high-level):
- feat(replay): add proportional_replay.Orchestrator, sampling strategy and unit tests
- feat(ci): add blended_quality_gate adapter and CI hook integration
- feat(metrics): add blend_score exporter and histogram tagging for cohort/seed
- test: add e2e smoke and deterministic replay tests with synthetic cohorts
- docs: add README and runbook describing tuning knobs and rollback steps
- ci: wire new gate into smoke and nightly pipelines behind feature flag

Changed files (high-level):
- orchestrators/proportional_replay.py
- orchestrators/__init__.py
- ci/hooks/blended_quality_gate.py
- metrics/exporters/blend_score_exporter.py
- tests/unit/test_proportional_replay.py
- tests/e2e/test_replay_orchestrator.py
- docs/eval/README-proportional-replay.md
- scripts/ci/update-gates.yml
- examples/prompt-sets/regen-weighted-sample.yaml

Testing and CI: Local unit tests added for sampling invariants and edge cases (zero-count cohorts, extreme variance). E2E tests run a deterministic replay against a synthetic model stub to assert stability improvements. On CI this ran in two iterations: initial run failed due to a flaky test in tests/e2e/test_replay_orchestrator.py; flaky test was stabilized by switching to a seeded RNG and adding a short wait for background metrics flush. Final CI status: all checks passed. Full CI matrix: lint (pass), unit (pass), e2e (pass after rerun), metrics smoke (pass), integration (pass).

Review thread (highlights):
- Ethan Ross: "Can the orchestrator be configured to prefer recency over severity for some customers?" — response: "Yes — we added 'recency_weight' in the config and documented tradeoffs in the README; default remains severity-first." (resolved)
- Priya Kapoor: "Blended score uses simple weighted average today; can we add a robust aggregator (trimmed mean) to reduce outlier influence?" — response: "Added an optional 'robust_mode' flag that applies trimmed mean; default is legacy weighted avg for reproducibility." (resolved)
- Lena Park: "Concern: cost impact of cross-seed replay on nightly runs." — response: "We added proportional caps and an adaptive budgeter that limits total replay tokens per run; documented cost implications and added a metric to track replay token consumption." (resolved)
- QA note (Raghu): "I hit a timing issue with metrics flush on slow CI agents." — action: "Added flush-wait and telemetry backoff; CI rerun green." (resolved)

Rollout and rollback plan: The feature is behind 'eval/proportional_replay' feature flag. Default is off for all orgs. Enable initially for internal/QA orgs, run 3 nights, monitor blend_score trends and noisy_failure_rate. Rollback by disabling the flag (CI gate reverts to previous simple-metric gate) or by reverting the merge if critical.

Telemetry and observability: New metrics: replay.batch_size, replay.token_consumed, blend_score.value (per-cohort), blend_gate.decision (pass/fail), blend_gate.threshold. Dashboards and an alert are included in the docs runbook; the alert triggers on sustained increase of noisy_failure_rate > 2x historical baseline for 24h.

Notes and related links: Linked Linear: ENG-8421. See docs/eval/README-proportional-replay.md for configuration guide and tuning advice. This PR is intended to reduce noisy regressions and improve developer signal confidence in CI gating.
Introduce a proportional replay orchestrator that replays failing prompt cohorts across recent baselines and a blended-quality CI gate that fuses multiple signals (accuracy, calibration drift, latency regression) with adaptive thresholds. Improves signal-to-noise for prompt-set regressions and reduces noisy CI failures.
Ethan Ross: Please add a config option to prefer recency over severity — addressed with 'recency_weight'.
Priya Kapoor: Consider robust aggregator to reduce outlier influence — added optional 'robust_mode'.
Lena Park: Watch cost of cross-seed replay — added token budgeter and metrics to monitor consumption.
Raghu (QA): Observed metrics flush race on slow CI agents — added flush-wait and backoff; rerun green.
Enable feature flag in a staging org, run nightly pipeline for 3 nights, verify blend_score distribution and noisy_failure_rate in dashboards, run e2e deterministic replay test locally: pytest tests/e2e/test_replay_orchestrator.py -k deterministic --seed 42.
If you need to revert quickly, disable the 'eval/proportional_replay' feature flag; the gate handler will fall back to the previous 'single-metric' gate with no schema changes required.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: We frequently see brittle regressions on prompt sets that only surface when multiple small perturbations are applied in sequence (e.g., punctuation->case->synonym). Existing single-perturbation probes miss these cascading failure modes. This PR adds a sequential perturbation runner and a configurable CI gate with a grace-window to reduce flapping for transient noise.

What this changes: 1) A new harness (eval-harness/hooks/sequential_perturbation.py) that composes perturbation passes into ordered schedules. Schedules are declarative (examples in examples/perturbation-configs/) and support weighted sampling, early-exit on divergence, and deterministic seeding for reproducibility. 2) A new gate (eval-harness/gates/grace_window_gate.py) which evaluates metric streams over a configurable time window and only triggers hard failures when a signal persists beyond the grace period. 3) Two new metrics: compression-aware divergence (captures structural compression differences that indicate paraphrase collapse) and token-level saliency delta (helps pinpoint where the model changed token importance after perturbations). 4) CI integration: a backfill/smoke job (ci/pipelines/eval-smokebackfill.yml) that runs the sequential schedule against recent canary snapshots and reports to the existing eval-dashboard. 5) Docs and examples for configuring schedules and gate thresholds (docs/eval/seq-perturbation.md).

Design notes: The sequential runner supports three modes: replay (deterministic order), stochastic-schedule (sampled sequences with fixed seed), and adversarial-grid (exhaustive short sequences for narrow prompt cohorts). The gate computes a rolling severity score combining metric z-scores, cohort weight, and historical stability; the grace window is expressed as x runs / y minutes threshold (configurable per-linear key). We intentionally keep the gate soft-fail by default with an optional policy to escalate to hard-fail after an extended grace period.

Testing and validation: Unit tests added (tests/test_seq_perturb.py) for schedule parsing, deterministic replay, and early-exit behavior. End-to-end smoke runs were executed against three internal canaries (conversational, summarization, code-completion) — CI artifacts show no notable latency regression (+~1.2% token processing time in worst case due to extra perturbation instrumentation). Metric-level thresholds were tuned on historical rolling windows (30d anchor) and validated against known regressions to ensure recall.

Rollout and risk mitigation: Rollout is staged. Step 1: enable pipeline in nightly smoke for opt-in teams and collect telemetry for 7 days. Step 2: enable soft gating in PR-level CI for top-10 prompt sets by volume. Step 3: enable default soft gating org-wide and add escalation policy for persistent signals. We add backfill tooling so new schedules can be re-run over last 14 days to build baselines.

Operational notes: The gate emits structured events to the eval-dashboard and attaches sample failing prompts + perturbation trace (via eval-harness/utils/trace_exporter.py). We also add a debug flag to export token-saliency diffs for investigator workflows. Compression-aware divergence uses lightweight LZ-based sketching to avoid large payloads.

Related work and references: This PR complements ENG-3421 (cohort prioritizer) by adding a failure-mode-aware probe and links to ENG-3499 (alert fusion) for escalation behavior. It is intentionally model-agnostic and works with both hosted and private eval runners.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add sequential perturbation runner + schedules
- [x] Implement grace-window gate with configurable policy
- [x] Add metric implementations and unit tests
- [x] Wire up CI smoke/backfill pipeline
- [x] Add docs and example configs
- [x] Run canary E2E smoke and tune thresholds

Notes on performance/security: No new credentials or secrets required. The runner adds modest CPU overhead during CI (increasing runtime of some eval jobs); batching and caching are preserved. All exported traces are scrubbed of PII by existing trace exporter filters.

Summary: Introduces a new class of sequential perturbation probes and a pragmatic gate for reducing noisy CI failures while surfacing cascade-sensitive regressions. This fills a gap in our eval coverage and provides actionable signals to triage teams.

Lars Håkansson (reviewer): Please add a short circuit for schedules that produce identical outputs after two steps to avoid wasted cycles.

Context: Optimize needs a first-class way to run offline evals against a proposed serving config change (batching/caching/quantization profile) before allowing apply/rollout. This PR adds a new API endpoint and job plumbing in eval-harness to accept a config diff + baseline reference, execute the requested gate tier against selected prompt sets, and return structured metrics plus artifact pointers suitable for Console/Optimize consumption. Endpoint: POST /api/v1/gates/trigger (auth: service-to-service token; scoped to optimize-gating). Request (JSON): gate_tier ("smoke"|"full"), model_id, baseline (baseline_model_version + baseline_runtime_config_ref), proposed (runtime_config_diff, optional proposed_model_version), prompt_sets (ids), sample_count (optional; defaults per tier), run_metadata (route_id, account_id, region, commit_sha, idempotency_key). Validation: limits request payload size, rejects unknown diff keys, enforces that baseline ref is immutable (no "latest"), and checks prompt set ids exist and are enabled for gating. Execution: enqueues a GateRun job to the existing eval runner queue, pins model + runtime settings for the duration of the run, and writes an immutable run record with normalized inputs for audit/debug. Response: 202 Accepted with gate_run_id + status_url + estimated_duration_s; once complete, GET /api/v1/gates/runs/{id} returns status, summary metrics (per prompt set and overall), and artifact pointers (artifact_store_uri + optional signed_url when allowed), including: raw per-example outputs, rubric/score breakdowns, and a compact "comparison.json" (baseline vs proposed deltas). Artifacts: stored under artifact_store_uri prefix gates/{gate_run_id}/..., with retention aligned to existing eval artifact policy; Optimize can deep-link using gate_run_id. Observability: emits gate_trigger_requests_total and gate_run_enqueue_latency_ms (tags: gate_tier, model_id, region, caller=optimize) and attaches trace/span attributes for correlation from Optimize -> eval-harness. Tests: adds contract tests for request validation + schema stability, a fake runner integration test that asserts correct pinning of baseline/proposed configs, and golden JSON snapshots for the run detail response. Notes: This PR does not implement flake scoring/rerun aggregation (tracked in pr-418); response schema includes an optional flake_score field but it is not populated yet. Rollout: endpoint is behind feature flag OPTIMIZE_GATING_TRIGGER_API and requires allowlisted client identity; we can safely deploy without enabling any callers.

Selene Huang: Please include per-prompt-set summary in the run detail response; Optimize needs to surface which suite failed, not just overall.

Motivation: noisy prompt-set regressions frequently trigger coarse rollbacks or noisy alerts that hide actionable example-level failures. This PR implements a quarantine mitigator that isolates minimal failing example subsets and a conservative 'stitch' reintroduction workflow. It also adds a progressive rollback CI adapter to pause or reverse staged rollouts when quality signals degrade. Design: quarantine markings are added as optional metadata on eval result protos (additive, idempotent). The mitigator computes a minimal failure frontier using a greedy set-cover heuristic to produce a compact quarantine set. The stitch worker samples quarantined examples, runs targeted A/B smoke checks between candidate and baseline, and computes per-example recovery deltas. Stitch reintroduction rate is configurable (default 2%/hour) and guarded by a token-bucket rate limiter. The CI adapter watches sliding windows of quality signals (default window=3) and applies rollout fraction patches via the CI decision API with configurable tolerance and max rollback step. Checklist: - Implement quarantine mitigator core logic (greedy frontier selector) - Add stitch reintroduction worker and prioritized sampler - Add progressive rollback CI adapter and CI hook - Emit telemetry: eval.quarantine.count, eval.quarantine.ratio, eval.stitch.reintro.rate, eval.stitch.success.rate - Unit tests for mitigator and stitch worker - E2E smoke test in CI matrix - Operator docs and runbook - Feature-gate behind "quarantine_stitch_v1" and additive proto change
Testing: local unit tests tests/test_quarantine.py and tests/test_stitch_worker.py cover edge cases (empty sets, identical scores, concurrent quarantines). E2E smoke added to CI matrix using a synthetic prompt set to exercise quarantine->stitch->reintro loop. Performance: mitigator greedy pass benchmarks to <2s on 100k synthetic prompts in CI. Rollout: feature-flagged, staged rollout to internal staging, then opt-in for beta customers. Observability: new metrics and logs to correlate rollback actions with regression signals. Related: complements cohort-based gating and semantic anchors (see ENG-1972). The change is conservative and opt-in; the stitch worker is intentionally cautious and requires explicit opt-in in release pipelines.
Adds quarantine-and-stitch flow for isolating failing prompt subsets and a progressive rollback CI adapter to automate safe rollbacks during staged releases.

payload.body:
Motivation: We frequently see subtle regressions where a model's relative ranking between semantically equivalent positive/negative contrastive pairs drifts (e.g., preferred vs. not-preferred completions) even when absolute metrics look stable. This PR introduces an automated CI hook that computes an odds-ratio style stability metric on contrastive prompt pairs and a complementary randomized-suffix prober to detect suffix sensitivity regressions.

What this PR adds: a) contrastive_odds_gate: a CI hook that runs a batch of labeled contrastive pairs (A/B style) and computes an aggregated odds ratio and confidence interval using bootstrap resampling; the gate fails if the odds ratio drops below a configurable threshold or if the lower bootstrap CI crosses 1.0. b) randomized_suffix_prober: a small probe harness that appends randomized suffix tokens (common punctuation, short phrases, user-like trailing tokens) to prompts to measure sensitivity; outputs a stability score per prompt-set. c) an eval-gate config so teams can opt-in specific prompt sets and thresholds for their repo/route. d) smoke tests and integration test vectors to validate the hook behavior in CI.

Implementation notes: The odds ratio gate treats each contrastive example as a binary win/loss (model selects preferred completion). The gate aggregates across the prompt set to compute odds = (wins + 0.5) / (losses + 0.5) with small-sample smoothing and performs 1k stratified bootstrap resamples to estimate a 95% CI. Randomized suffix probing generates 10 perturbations per prompt by sampling from a curated suffix pool (commonly observed trailing tokens in production traces) and measures maximum relative rank shift across perturbations. Both components are implemented as lightweight Python modules that call the existing eval harness runner API; they do not change model-serving code.

Config and rollout: New CI config file ci/configs/eval_gate.yaml demonstrates two gate profiles: conservative (odds_ratio_threshold=0.9, min_examples=200) and permissive (0.7, min_examples=50). Default behavior is opt-in; the gate is included in the eval-harness CI matrix but disabled for repos that don't list the profile. Why this is different: Instead of only tracking absolute metric deltas, the odds-ratio gate explicitly captures relative preference shifts between paired examples and complements per-prompt suffix robustness checks. This helps catch regressions where overall BLEU/EM remains stable while model behavior flips on important decision points.

Motivation: A growing class of regressions only surface in multi-turn scenarios (turn-to-turn contradiction, context leakage, or degeneration across turns). Existing single-turn smokechecks miss these. This PR adds a multi-turn coherence smokehook and a turnwise replay adapter to detect and gate regressions that manifest across conversational turns.

What this PR introduces: 1) A coherence metric that combines (a) cross-turn semantic consistency (embedding-based similarity between prior assistant turns and subsequent responses) and (b) next-turn prediction stability (model likelihoods / token-level divergence when conditioned on different plausible prior paraphrases). 2) A smokehook that runs a compact multi-turn golden set on every canary and nightly CI run; the hook returns softfail/quarantine when drift exceeds thresholds. 3) A turnwise replay adapter which can: (i) expand failing examples into targeted replay samples (randomized paraphrases and alternate turn orders), (ii) tag failures with per-turn blame hints for faster triage. 4) Minimal UX: a small docs page and a local runner for debug.

Key goals: - catch regressions that affect conversation-level quality early - provide per-turn explanations so engineers can triage which turn(s) caused coherence loss - integrate with existing CI gating so teams can opt into hard vs soft failures

Checklist: - [x] Implement coherence metric and scoring shim - [x] Add multi-turn golden promptset (20 diverse dialogs across styles) - [x] Smokehook + CI job + YAML config - [x] Unit + lightweight integration tests - [x] Docs and runbook section - [x] Add telemetry tags for failure categories

Testing notes: The golden set is intentionally compact (~20 dialogs, 2-6 turns each) to keep runtime small in CI while retaining signal for common regression modes. Local runner supports --paraphrase N to exercise stability under input variation.

Rollout plan: Enable as soft-fail for 2 weeks on main branch runs; if signal is actionable reduce false positives then promote to hard gate for critical release branches. Linked Linear tickets contain follow-ups for threshold tuning and additional golden dialogs.
