Motivation: CI has been noisy for prompt-set regressions where output instability (non-deterministic variation across sampling seeds/temps/minibatches) causes spurious failures. This PR adds a cohort-level stability assertion and a lightweight flake-detection CI hook that (1) computes per-prompt-cohort stability scores during eval runs, (2) compares stability against a stored baseline, and (3) applies a configurable flake policy to reduce noise while still surfacing real regressions. The feature integrates into the existing eval-harness pipeline and GitHub checks: - New metric: stability_score (0..1) defined as 1 - normalized median token-level divergence across N replayed seeds; lower = less stable. - Cohort rules: thresholds by cohort tag (e.g., "conversational", "qa", "api-sample") can be configured in eval_config.yaml. - CI behavior: failures above the regression threshold fail the eval-check job; when instability is detected but under the 'flake_tolerance' threshold the job marks a warning and triggers an automatic single rerun of the eval job to confirm flakiness before failing. - Baseline handling: artifacts/baselines/stability.json stores historical cohort baselines; the check includes a 'record-baseline' subcommand used during baseline rollouts. - Reporting: GitHub check annotations include per-cohort summary and top-3 most unstable prompts (with anonymized IDs). - Telemetry: emits events to eval-telemetry (stability_score, rerun_count, cohort_id) as artifacts for later dashboards. Changes included: hook implementation, metric computation, CI workflow update, unit/integration tests, docs, and an example prompt-set. Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves existing eval pass/fail semantics unless a repo config opts into stability assertions (eval_config.yaml flag: enable_stability_assertions). See docs/eval/ci-hooks.md for usage instructions and samples. Rationale: we saw ~6% of CI eval failures in the last month attributable to non-deterministic output; this reduces developer churn while keeping regression sensitivity for true model quality degradation.

Motivation: Some regressions only manifest when examples/shot counts change (0-shot vs 1-shot vs 4-shot). Existing cohort and drift gates catch overall quality shifts but miss conditional failures tied to prompting style. This PR adds an adaptive shot-sensitivity CI gate that tests a compact set of prompt-sets across multiple shot contexts and flags regressions that are differential by shot count.

What this does (high level):
- Adds a new CI hook (shot-sensitivity-gate) that runs a lightweight, prioritized matrix of prompt-sets x shot-counts during PR gating. The gate compares a rolling baseline snapshot and reports differential regressions where delta_by_shot exceeds calibrated thresholds.
- Introduces a contrastive-replay utility which stores the minimal repro payload (prompt, shot configuration, seed, model hash) to reproduce the failure deterministically in local or CI replay lanes. This aids debugging by producing counterfactual side-by-side outputs for the baseline and candidate commits.
- Adds an adaptive weighting scheme: small, high-priority prompt-sets are weighted more aggressively; low-signal sets use decaying failure penalties to reduce noise from sporadic flakiness. Weight decay parameters are configurable in the CI config file.
- Integrates with our existing eval reporting: failed shot-sensitive entries surface as a new failure type in the existing regression dashboard with per-shot deltas and replay links.

Why it's different: Instead of a broad end-to-end smoke rerun, this gate focuses on prompt-context sensitivity (number-of-examples) and provides deterministic replay artifacts for faster root-cause. It is intentionally lightweight and tuned for PR feedback loops rather than long-running post-merge sweeps.

Implementation notes (single-string body):
- New files added: hooks/shot_sensitivity_gate.py (implements sampling, matrix run, comparison logic), tools/replay/contrastive_replay.py (repro harness, deterministic runner), ci/configs/shot-gate.yml (gate configuration and weights), docs/gates/shot-sensitivity.md (user guide and tuning instructions), tests/test_shot_gate.py (unit + integration smoke tests), eval/fixtures/shot-priority-list.json (prioritized prompt-sets), dashboards/migrations/add_shot_delta_fields.sql (dashboard schema).
- Sampling strategy: top-N prioritized prompts pulled from the master priority list; each prompt is executed at 0-shot, 1-shot, and 4-shot by default. The gate computes per-prompt per-shot metric deltas (e.g. exact-match, semantic-similarity) and then aggregates with the configured weights.
- Thresholding: supports both fixed thresholds and a historical z-score mode against a rolling baseline. Default is z-score backed with a minimum absolute-delta floor to avoid tiny numerical noise.

Testing and CI:
- Local unit tests added for the comparison engine and replay serialization.
- CI matrix includes: lint, unit, smoke-eval (small matrix run), and replay-integration (replays a stored failing case).
- First CI run surfaced a nondeterministic ordering bug in the priority sampler; fixed in second commit by adding stable sort on priority+id.

Operational considerations:
- The default gate is enabled on the preview CI lane (non-blocking) for two weeks to collect signal, then will be flipped to optional failure-on-high-confidence regressions.
- Replay artifacts are stored in the same S3 bucket as other eval artifacts; retention 30 days by default. Keys are small (prompt + shot config + seed), so storage cost is minimal.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: opt-in preview on all eval-harness PRs (reports only).
- Week 2: escalate to soft-fail for high-confidence regressions (requires one approver override to merge).
- Week 4: evaluate false-positive rate and adjust decay/weighting; promote to hard-fail if <1% FP on two consecutive weeks.

Related: Links to ENG-2981 (prompt-set hygiene) and ENG-2999 (eval-dashboard enhancements) in Linear.

Context and motivation: We observed several recent false-positive regressions where syntactically small but semantically important prompts triggered noisy failures in CI. This PR introduces a semantic-prioritized regression gate that weights prompt-set regressions by an embedding-based semantic distance and prompt metadata priors, and pairs it with a cohort scheduler that makes replay/rollback work budget-aware and less bursty.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Implements a new gate module eval_harness.gates.semantic_priority_gate that computes a per-prompt priority score combining semantic drift (cosine distance of anchor embeddings), historical volatility (per-prompt stability index), and metadata priors (owner, sensitivity). High-priority prompts will cause stricter thresholds and faster escalation; low-priority prompts are subject to progressive attenuation (delayed alerts, larger tolerances). Adds a cohort scheduler service eval_harness.orchestration.cohort_scheduler which: (a) staggers replay execution windows to avoid thundering replays against shared models, (b) enforces a configurable daily budget per-linear-ticket/owner, (c) respects dynamic drift signals (samples more aggressively when drift magnitude > threshold). Integrates the gate into CI via ci/hooks/semantic_priority_gate.yml and exposes detailed metrics to observability via eval_harness.metrics.semantic_gate.* (priority_histogram, triggered_alerts_total, replay_budget_utilization). Includes a small opt-in web UI patch for console devs at docs/snippets/semantic-gate-usage.md showing how to configure per-team priors.

Checklist:

- [x] Scheduler implementation and integration tests (local mode)
- [x] CI hook config and example Linear ticket mapping
- [x] Observability metrics and dashboards (Grafana snippets)

Design notes and rationale: The primary signal is embedding-based cosine distance against a stabilized anchor per-prompt; we use a rolling median of recent embeddings to reduce noise. Priority score = alpha * normalized_cosine + beta * volatility + gamma * prior_score; coefficients are configurable via env or console. The scheduler deliberately biases toward avoiding overlapping heavy replays on the same model region to keep token spikes under SLA. We calibrated the default budget to 5% of daily smoke evaluation capacity for non-critical teams.

Adds a Prompt Lifecycle Sentinel prober and a lag-adaptive holdback gate for CI that detects regressions related to delayed prompt rollouts and temporal drift. Emits new metrics and a lightweight dashboard to help triage prompt-set stability issues.
Motivation: We see recurring incidents where prompt-set regressions surface only after a delayed customer rollout or after a time-lag (e.g., versioned prompts combined with partial rollouts). Existing CI smokechecks are good for immediate regressions but insufficient for detecting instability that emerges due to temporal ordering or stale anchor snapshots. This PR introduces a Prompt Lifecycle Sentinel prober and a lag-adaptive holdback gate for CI that together detect and mitigate temporal/regression modes before they reach production.

What this change does: Adds a new prober (eval-harness/probers/prompt_lifecycle_sentinel.py) that captures lightweight anchor snapshots (prompt version, rollout_id, sample seeds), replays a synthesized user-feedback stream using a replay client, and emits time-windowed stability metrics (windowed delta, cohort variance, slowness score). Introduces a CI hook (eval-harness/ci/hooks/lag_adaptive_gate.yaml) that integrates with the eval orchestration to run the sentinel as part of pre-merge checks or nightly regression sweeps. The gate implements progressive quarantine: on the first failure we mark the PR with a soft-hold that requires triage and a follow-up comparative run; repeated failures within a short window escalate to a hard holdback. The gate uses configurable thresholds and min-volume guards to avoid noisy false positives.

Implementation notes: - Snapshot format is intentionally compact and stored in the artifact cache; snapshots include prompt_set id, compacted prompt fingerprint, rollout_id, and a monotonic timestamp. - Replay client is best-effort and rate-limited to avoid burdening serving; tests include a local in-memory stub. - Metrics are emitted via prompt_metrics emitter with tags [prompt_set, rollout_id, seed] and coarse timestamping. - The orchestration wiring adds a non-blocking shadow run path so the sentinel can run during long CI windows and still surface results in PRs without blocking unrelated work. - Added an integration smoke test that simulates a staggered rollout and asserts the gate's holdback transition logic.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests added under tests/probers/*. Integration smoke runs executed in the eval staging environment. CI required one rerun due to a flaky tokenization edge-case in an unrelated test; rerun succeeded. We plan a canary rollout of the gate for the next two weeks: run as soft-hold on main CI, emit dashboards and annotate regression incidents. After monitoring for false positives we will flip to hard-enforce for high-impact prompt_set tags.

Related work: EN G-2134 tracks the prompt rollouts and visibility work; ENG-2207 requested more deterministic replay behavior and was used to justify the replay client changes. Links: internal/linear/ENG-2134, internal/linear/ENG-2207.
Arjun: Can you explain how the sentinel differs from our existing anchor probes? Maya: The sentinel focuses on temporal alignment and rollout lag: it snapshots prompt versions (anchor ids), replays a small synthetic user-feedback stream against the current model, and computes time-lagged stability metrics (delta over sliding windows). It also reports TTLs for anchors so ops can see stale snapshots. Sofia: I want stronger guardrails around false positives from low-volume cohorts. Maya: Added an exponential backoff and progressive quarantine policy so small cohorts require higher confidence before gating; updated tests to cover low-volume thresholds. Tomás: Metrics tag cardinality looks high — will that blow out our storage? Maya: We limit tags to prompt_set, rollout_id and seed; the emitter batches and coarse-grains timestamps to minute buckets. After fixes, reviewers ran the integration smoke test; one flaky tokenization test triggered a rerun but CI passed. Final approvals: Arjun approved, Sofia approved after threshold tuning, Tomás approved after tag limits update.

Motivation: when a primary prompt-set check trips, we often need to run a set of targeted probes (e.g. hallucination prober, paraphrase-stability, token-saliency) to determine failure mode before blocking rollouts. This PR adds a conditional eval fanout layer and a weighted signal aggregator so CI can produce a single composite gating decision that reflects both severity and breadth of regressions. Design summary: - New runtime component eval_fanout orchestrates conditional parallel probes with a budget cap and backpressure to avoid blowing smoke-test windows. - WeightedSignalAggregator implements decay-weighted aggregation across cohorts and probes; weights are configurable per-linear-task and default to severity-first then coverage. - CiHook composite_slo_check integrates into existing eval CI: primary prompt-set runs as usual; on fail, fanout triggers configured probes; aggregator emits a human-readable breakdown and a single pass/fail decision. - Added JSON schema for fanout plan (configs/ : fanout-plans/*.json) and migration docs. Motivation: Flaky or locally scoped prompt regressions generate high-noise CI alerts. This PR implements a contextual anchor lifecycle and a progression gate that moves candidate failures through staged verification before failing the main CI. Design summary: 1) Anchors are short representative prompt subsets (per-cohort) stored with a light fingerprint and baseline metrics. 2) When a CI eval sees a failure on a full prompt-set, the hook emits a candidate and triggers a staged progression: -- Stage 0: Quick smoke re-run with tighter sampling of the same seed. -- Stage 1: Anchored replay (deterministic) that replays the exact examples against the new model/variant and compares composite metrics (semantic-similarity, token-level match, and domain-specific scorer) against stored anchor baseline with configurable tolerances. -- Stage 2: Progressive escalation runs the candidate across a wider randomized cohort and collects metric distributions; failure only bubbles if composite severity > configured progression_threshold. Key properties: contextual thresholds per-cohort, time-windowed backfill (to avoid regressions from transient infra flakiness), and automatic soft-fail tagging to avoid pager storms. CI integration: new hook eval-harness/hooks/progression_gate.py registers in the CI pipeline (e2e/ci/pipelines/progression-gate.yaml) and talks to eval-metrics-service via a Prometheus-compatible adapter for retrieving historical anchor baselines. Opt-in config: anchors.workflows in eval_config.yaml; default gate is disabled for existing projects to maintain backwards compatibility. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of progression gate hook and lifecycle manager - [x] Prometheus adapter for anchor baseline lookup - [x] Deterministic anchored replay test harness - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs and examples for anchor config - [x] CI pipeline wiring and flake mitigation (retries) Commits summary: three logical commits: 1) initial progression gate prototype and lifecycle model (progression_gate.py + helpers) 2) metrics adapter + tests (prometheus_adapter.py) 3) docs, examples, CI pipeline + test fixes (docs/anchors.md, sample_anchor.yaml, pipeline yaml). Files changed (high level): eval-harness/hooks/progression_gate.py; eval-harness/lifecycle/anchor_manager.py; eval-harness/metrics/prometheus_adapter.py; eval-harness/tests/test_progression_gate.py; e2e/ci/pipelines/progression-gate.yaml; docs/anchors.md; examples/anchor_configs/sample_anchor.yaml Testing: local unit tests added to cover anchor state transitions and composite scoring; integration CI runs simulate a seeded regression and validate that only Stage 2 escalates to a fail when severity passes the threshold. Rollout plan: merged behind feature flag; enable for one service (search-rewrites) for one week as canary, monitor alert volume and false positives, then expand. Backout plan: config toggle to disable anchors.workflows; CI will revert to legacy immediate-fail behavior and a short hotfix script provided in ci/scripts/run_anchor_replay.sh. Related: ENG-2578 (anchor lifecycle), ENG-2749 (CI gating UX).

Motivation: existing smoke/eval runners surface brittle regressions but often overload incident channels for transient drift. Add new cascade fidelity CI hook that stages lightweight smoke checks before heavier fidelity runs and introduces a probabilistic soft-stop to reduce noisy hard failures in PR contexts. No breaking API changes.
Context and motivation: multiple recent PRs revealed intermittent prompt-set regressions that only show up under heavy, long-tail evals and cause noisy CI hard-fails. This change introduces an orchestrated 'cascade fidelity checker' CI hook that runs a sequence of checks (fast syntactic/embedding parity -> medium-weight semantic probes -> heavy lineage replay) and applies an explainable failure score to surface offending examples. To reduce developer friction we add a probabilistic soft-stop policy: a PR is only blocked (hard fail) when multiple tiers concur or a high-confidence explainable score crosses threshold; otherwise the CI marks a gated warning and opens an auto-created Linear task for follow-up. Introduce a lightweight statistical cohort drift detector and a one-off backfill pipeline, plus a CI gate integration that fails builds when an immediate, high-confidence drift is detected for critical prompt cohorts. Motivation: teams have seen occasional sudden regressions tied to prompt-set composition changes; this change provides an automated early-warning and a reproducible backfill path to diagnose root cause. The detector computes cohort-level distributions for generation-quality signals (token_precision, completion_coverage, and a normalized score) and evaluates divergence using both symmetric KL and a rank-based Mann-Whitney U p-value. We add configurable thresholds and minimum-sample safeguards; the default config uses cohort_kl > 0.12 OR mwu_pvalue < 0.01 with min_samples=200 to trigger a warning and an elevated threshold to fail CI (used only for protected prompt sets). The backfill pipeline can be invoked ad-hoc or scheduled; it uses batched inference with cache rehydration and writes cohort summaries to a new analytics table. The PR includes tooling to re-run historic evals against pinned model versions, a SQL migration to store cohort drift history, and docs for interpreting outputs and tuning thresholds. CI integration runs a fast sample-level check on pull requests for changed prompt sets and fails only when failure-mode thresholds are reached. Fallbacks: CI gate is opt-in per repo via eval-gates.yml and defaults to warn-only for most prompt sets to avoid blocking developer velocity. Performance: the detector adds negligible runtime to full evals (~+2% CPU) and backfill job processes 150k prompt-examples in ~7 minutes on the standard runner. This change is covered by unit, integration, and perf tests and includes examples and troubleshooting notes.
Initial implementation posted as a draft; reviewers asked for reproducible seeds and clearer minimum-sample behavior. Miguel requested that the fail gate be opt-in and warned about false positives on low-volume prompt cohorts; author updated config to be opt-in per repo and added warn-only default. Priya asked for performance numbers and an integration test that runs a mocked backfill; those were added. Evan requested a concrete troubleshooting doc; a new architecture page and FAQ were added. After two rounds of small fixes (deterministic seeding, error handling for empty cohorts), reviewers approved and marked as ready. Final merge performed via squash with conventional commit summary.
Added cohort drift detection with configurable CI gating and a backfill pipeline for historic evaluation. New metrics (cohort_kl, mwu_pvalue) and a persisted drift history table enable trending and alerting. CI gate is opt-in and defaults to warn-only for non-protected prompt sets.
Unit tests for detector math and edge cases added; integration test simulates a backfill run against a small dataset using a mocked runtime, CI fast-sample check exercised in workflow; perf benchmark verified 150k samples processed in ~7 minutes on standard runner. All tests pass locally and on CI.
Start as opt-in for a subset of protected prompt sets (10% of repositories) for 2 weeks, then expand to 30% and monitor false positive rate and signal-to-noise; full rollout gated on false-positive rate < 0.5% over a 14-day window. Backfill jobs run during off-peak hours by default (02:00 UTC).
Detector adds ~2% CPU overhead to full evals; storage for drift history table estimated at 8KB per cohort per day; backfill job processed 150k prompts in 7 minutes on the standard runner in our benchmarks.
This PR targets improving early detection of prompt-set regressions and provides reproducible tooling to investigate and mitigate. Teams should opt in protected prompt sets into eval-gates.yml and tune thresholds based on historical variance.

Context: Several prompt-set regression investigations in the last quarter (see ENG-2309) traced failures to brittle token anchors and sharp binary gating in CI. Hard-failing CI on single-anchor regressions causes noisy rollbacks and blocks teams even when signal is transient. This PR introduces two cooperating changes: (1) a provisional-anchor-smoothing adapter for eval scoring that probabilistically reweights prompt anchors to reduce single-anchor volatility, and (2) a deferred fail-fast CI hook that performs soft-fail quarantining and escalation windows before treating a regression as blocking.

What it does (high level):
- provisional anchor smoothing: adds eval pipeline logic to compute a smoothed-anchor weight for each anchor in a prompt set, implemented as a temperature-controlled softmax over anchor influence scores with optional per-cohort priors. This is pluggable via the existing eval adapter registry and can be toggled per-prompt-set.
- deferred fail-fast hook: a CI-side adapter that receives eval run outcomes and applies a short quarantine/backoff policy (configurable window in minutes and replay count). The hook will mark a run as soft-failed and schedule targeted replay sampling; only after N corroborating soft-fails within the window does it convert to a hard fail and surface to the blocking gate.

Why: Reduces false-positive regressions from single-anchor noise, improves developer signal-to-noise, and gives on-call and triage automation time to collect corroborating evidence or clear noisy anomalies without immediately blocking mainline merges.

Design notes / how it integrates:
- The smoothing algorithm exposes parameters: smoothing_temperature, anchor_prior_decay, min_effect_size. Defaults chosen after backtesting on historical prompt-sets (see docs/rfc/provisional-anchor-smoothing.md in this PR).
- The hook is written to integrate with existing CI adapter interface (ci/hooks/registry). It emits structured telemetry (soft_fail_count, quarantine_window, replay_job_id) to the eval orchestration logs so the Console can visualize soft-fail timelines.
- Backwards compatible: smoothing is opt-in at prompt-set metadata level; hook has a default non-blocking mode during a gradual rollout.

Testing:
- Unit tests: test_anchor_smoother covers temperature extremes, decay behavior, and edge cases for single-anchor prompt-sets.
- Integration tests: added an emulated CI run pipeline test that exercises quarantine and escalation logic with deterministic time acceleration.
- Backtest: included a small backtest harness and results under docs/backtests showing a 38% reduction in one-off anchor-triggered hard failures across sampled historical prompt-sets.

Changes included (summary of files):
- eval_harness/hooks/provisional_anchor_smoother.py (core algorithm + registry adapter)
- eval_harness/ci_hooks/deferred_fail_fast.py (CI adapter implementing quarantine and replay scheduling)

payload.body:
Why: We see subtle regressions where model outputs are sensitive to the ordering of prompts in a prompt set (e.g., system + instruction + few-shot examples). This PR introduces an automated CI assertion that measures ordering robustness by permuting prompt components/samples and computing a stability score. The goal is to catch regressions where small reorderings cause material differences in model ranking/quality for a prompt-set used in downstream checks.

What:
- New metric: Permutation Stability Score (PSS) — median pairwise Kendall Tau over N random permutations (normalized to [0,1]). Lower values indicate order-sensitive outputs.
- CI check: ci/checks/prompt-order-robustness.yml runs a sampled stability job for changed prompt-sets and fails if PSS < 0.85 or disagreement_rate > 0.05.
- Lightweight sampling harness with adaptive sample size: starts with 10 permutations and increases up to 60 only when variance is high to bound runtime.
- Deterministic reseeding and memoized model-call cache during CI to reduce flakiness and wall time.
- Unit tests for the metric, plus an integration smoke test that validates behavior against a mocked model.
- Docs: guidance for engineers on interpreting PSS failures and recommended mitigations (reformatting prompts, anchor examples, or targeted evals).

Risk/Scope: This adds a new CI check in eval pipelines only (does not affect serving). The default thresholds are conservative so we minimize false positives. The adaptive sampling and caching are tuned to keep CI latency under the existing eval budget.

How to review: Focus on correctness of the PSS implementation (perm_stability_metric.py), determinism under seeding fixtures (tests), and the CI workflow memory/timeout parameters. The implementation is intentionally modular so teams can enable the check per-prompt-set via metadata in defaults.yaml.

Related: ENG-3219 tracks rollout / opt-in across monorepo eval suites. PM-78 is the product ticket for adding prompt-robustness signals to the quality dashboard.

Backstory: This PR emerged from an incident where a canary failed sporadically when a front-end change re-ordered example blocks; a follow-up audit showed sensitive ranking deltas tied to order. We need a smoke/assertion to prevent regressions that are invisible to token-level metrics.

Notes: The description and docs include examples illustrating a failing prompt-set and suggested fixes. The CI job will run only for changed prompt-set directories (opt-in by adding metadata in defaults.yaml).

Liam Brooks: Initially flagged flaky test in test_prompt_order_stability — failed intermittently on CI.
Sofia Tran: Investigated; root cause was nondeterministic fixture seeding and redundant network calls. Added deterministic seed propagation and memoized model call cache — reran CI.
Anika Desai: Asked for adaptive sampling to avoid 60-permutation worst case on every run.
Sofia Tran: Implemented adaptive sample size, added comments explaining tradeoffs, and added a small benchmark in tests to show median runtime at ~45s on build agents.
Priya Nair: Approved after minor doc edits.
Liam Brooks: Approved and left a note that threshold/alpha should be configurable per-team.
Merge: squash and merge after green CI.

- CI workflow: prompt-order-robustness.yml (opt-in per prompt-set).

payload.body:
Motivation: CI flakiness from prompt-set regressions is often correlated with low-confidence outputs and concentrated replay bursts. This PR implements a confidence-normalized regression gate and a replay rate-limiter (replay throttle) to reduce noisy failures and protect downstream infra during automated backfills. The two pieces work together: the gate reduces false-positive failures by normalizing metric thresholds against the model's confidence distribution; the replay limiter spaces out automated replays and applies progressive quarantine for consistently flaky prompts.

What this changes: introduced a new gate type `confidence_normalized_threshold` that computes an adjusted pass threshold per-cohort using a running calibration of model confidence (softmax entropy + median logit gap). The gate can be enabled per-prompt-set and configured with a normalization window and minimum-sample floor to avoid over-calibration on small cohorts. Added a replay controller `replay_rate_limiter` used by the checkpoint replay system and the CI smoke-runner to rate-limit replays by cohort, with backoff and quarantine semantics for repeatedly failing examples.

Design summary (high-level):
- Confidence normalization: compute cohort-level confidence_factor = clamp(1.0 + alpha * (baseline_entropy - observed_entropy), 0.6, 1.4). Adjust raw metric threshold = base_threshold * confidence_factor. This reduces spurious failures when models are broadly uncertain and tightens thresholds when model confidence increases.
- Replay rate-limiter: token-bucket per-cohort with configurable burst and sustained rates, plus an exponential backoff for examples that fail 2+ consecutive replays. After N_quarantine_failures an example is marked as `quarantined` and excluded from automated replay until a manual triage or a TTL expires.
- Flaky suppression: aggregated flaky score stored alongside evaluation metadata to drive downstream triage dashboards and reduce pager noise.

Config example (single string YAML blob included in one field below in the changed files):
```
evaluation_gates:
  - name: confidence_normalized_threshold
    type: confidence_normalized
    params:
      base_threshold: 0.88
      alpha: 0.25
      normalization_window_days: 14
      min_samples: 50
      clamp_min: 0.6
      clamp_max: 1.4
replay_controller:
  type: replay_rate_limiter
  params:
    burst_per_minute: 10
    sustain_per_minute: 2
    backoff_multiplier: 2.0
    quarantine_after: 3
    quarantine_ttl_hours: 48
```

Files changed (high-level): added gate implementation, replay controller, unit tests, integration test harness, docs and a small console-dashboard hook for flaky counts. See `files_changed` for specifics.

Testing and validation: local unit tests (coverage added around gate math and throttle behavior), integration run against a real nightly model profile (ran with `smoke-run --profile nightly-2024-11-01 --dry-run=false`) and a staged CI on `staging-evals` that exercised backoff/quarantine paths. Observed reduction in false-positive failures on a 2-week retrospective run: failing PRs attributable to low-confidence prompts down 42% and total replay volume during backfills reduced by ~63% with default limits.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged gate + controller. Default off for existing prompt-sets; opt-in via prompt-set metadata. Gradual enablement for high-volume cohorts first, then all cohorts after 2 weeks of monitoring. Dashboard shows quarantined counts and replay volume.

Related: references ENG-1984 (rollout stability), ENG-2009 (replay orchestration improvements) and SUP-1132 (support ticket highlighting noisy regressions).

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests for gate math and edge cases
- [x] Integration smoke runs against nightly profile
- [x] Dashboard metric for quarantined prompt count
- [x] Docs: short-runbook and config examples
- [x] Feature-flag gating and rollout notes

--- a/eval-harness/gates/confidence_normalized_gate.py
+++ b/eval-harness/gates/confidence_normalized_gate.py
@@ def adjusted_threshold(base_threshold, alpha, observed_entropy, baseline_entropy):
-    return base_threshold
+    factor = 1.0 + alpha * (baseline_entropy - observed_entropy)
+    factor = max(min(factor, 1.4), 0.6)
+    return base_threshold * factor

--- a/eval-harness/replay/replay_rate_limiter.py
+++ b/eval-harness/replay/replay_rate_limiter.py
@@ class ReplayRateLimiter:
-    def allow(self, cohort):
-        # naive always-allow for initial implementation
-        return True
+    def allow(self, cohort):
+        # token-bucket per-cohort: burst + sustained enforcement
+        self._refill_tokens(cohort)
+        if self._tokens[cohort] > 0:
+            self._tokens[cohort] -= 1
+            return True
+        return False

Marcus Green (2024-11-09): requested changes — please add min_samples floor and explicit clamp to avoid runaway thresholds in small cohorts.
Aisha Patel (2024-11-10): responded — added min_samples config and clamp, added unit tests for small cohorts.
Priya Rao (2024-11-12): approved after minor docs nits fixed.
Liam O'Neill (2024-11-14): requested change — add telemetry for replay backoff events. Aisha replied that telemetry was added and integration smoke validated the counters.
Decision to normalize against cohort entropy rather than raw confidence per-example to reduce sensitivity to single-example noise.
Telemetry added for: adjusted_threshold_applied, replay_throttle_hit, example_quarantined. These appear in the console flaky widget.
Rollout will use feature-flag and two-week monitoring window; default off for existing prompt-sets to avoid surprises.
Add confidence-normalized evaluation gate and replay rate-limiter to reduce false-positive regression failures and control replay load. Feature-flagged; opt-in per prompt-set. Adds telemetry for throttles and quarantines.
If large cohorts start hitting quarantines unexpectedly, increase min_samples or disable the gate; replay rate limits are configurable via eval-harness config and can be relaxed per-cohort. Dashboards: evals.replay.throttle.hits and evals.quarantine.count show impact.
Monitor evals.quarantine.count and evals.replay.throttle.hits for first 2 weeks
Enable gate for two low-volume cohorts as canary after merge
Schedule follow-up (ENG-2009) to autosuggest per-cohort params based on historical traffic

payload.body:
Motivation: some regressions surface only in high-volume contexts or in narrow prompt cohorts; existing eval gates treat each failing example equally which underweights production impact. This PR introduces a proportional failure heatmap and a context-coverage metric that (1) weights failures by frequency and severity, (2) surfaces top-left hotspots in a time-decayed heatmap, and (3) produces a single coverage score used by the CI hook. Design: we cluster prompts into contextual cohorts using the existing prompt fingerprinting + semantic shingle embedding. For each cohort we compute a weighted failure score = sum_{examples in cohort}(failure_weight * recency_decay * frequency_factor). Frequency comes from the sampled traffic histogram (or sample proxy during CI). Severity is derived from configured eval metrics (exact-match, BLEU drop, hallucination flag), mapped to a 1-5 weight. We render a heatmap matrix: rows = cohorts, cols = failure types/buckets, cell = normalized proportional score. The context-coverage score is a normalized aggregate that penalizes under-tested or high-impact cohorts. CI behavior: runs as a post-eval hook. Default is soft-fail (annotate PR and open an advisory alert) and will fail the CI only when coverage < 0.6 AND proportional failure mass > threshold for two consecutive runs. There is an opt-in strict mode in repo eval.yaml to convert soft-fails into hard blocks. Implementation summary: - New hook entry point: eval_harness/hooks/proportional_failure_heatmap.py - Cohort sampler & cache adaptor: eval_harness/samplers/contextual_cohort_sampler.py - Heatmap renderer + export: eval_harness/reporting/coverage_heatmap_v1.py - CLI/backfill helper: tools/heatmap_backfill.py - Dashboard defs: infra/dashboards/coverage-heatmap.json - Unit + integration tests: tests/hooks/test_proportional_heatmap.py + tests/samplers/test_contextual_cohort.py Backwards compatibility: hook uses existing eval outputs; no changes required to model outputs or existing prompt sets. Rollout plan: 1) Merge in soft-fail mode, enable on canary branch for 48 hours (automated job), 2) run backfill for last 30 days using tools/heatmap_backfill.py to populate dashboards, 3) after observing false positive rate < 4% and stable signal for 1 week, flip opt-in projects to strict gating. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration test (CI job) - [x] Dashboard JSON added - [x] Documentation snippet added to docs/hooks.md - [x] Linear tickets linked (ENG-2345) - [x] Backfill tool included
Add a new CI hook that computes a proportional failure heatmap and context-coverage score per prompt cohort. Soft-fail mode by default; opt-in hard gating available via project config. Adds dashboard panels and backfill script.
Maya Gupta: Nice proposal. Can you clarify how frequency_factor is estimated during CI when we don't have live traffic?
Ethan Park: Good question — CI uses a sample-proxy histogram: we synthesize frequency from historical sample rates (last 7 days) stored in the eval cache. If unavailable, a conservative uniform prior is applied and flagged in the report.
Lina Sørensen: The severity mapping table looks arbitrary; please add tests that show sensitivity when weights change.
Ethan Park: Added parameterized tests and a short section in docs explaining how to tune weights per org. Tests cover weight ranges 0.5-3.0 and the coverage score stability.
Rafael Ortega: One nit — avoid expensive tensor ops in the hook path; move heavy compute to background/backfill where possible.
Ethan Park: Moved the full embedding-based clustering to the backfill tool; CI uses cached cluster ids and a cheap hash + shingle fallback. Updated implementation accordingly.
Maya Gupta: Approved after the cache optimization and tests. 👍
Run pytests: pytest tests/hooks/test_proportional_heatmap.py::test_heatmap_aggregation and pytest tests/samplers/test_contextual_cohort.py. To simulate CI behavior locally: python -m eval_harness.hooks.proportional_failure_heatmap --input tests/fixtures/sample_eval_output.json --mode dry-run
Heatmap normalization uses a per-cohort z-score with outlier trimming (winsorize 99th perc). Time decay uses exponential half-life parameter set to 7 days by default. All thresholds are configurable in eval.yaml under hooks.proportional_heatmap.

payload.body:
Motivation: prompt-set regressions sometimes manifest as subtle shifts in semantic fingerprint distribution rather than simple metric drops (precision/recall). This PR adds a Contextual Fingerprint Sentry that fingerprints prompt outputs, computes cohort-level distribution drift, and attaches a soft gate to CI that attenuates noisy, biased sample sets before a hard fail.

What this does: implements a lightweight fingerprinting pipeline (embedding + locality-preserving sketch), a cohort drift detector with exponential decay baseline, and a biased-sample attenuator that reduces the influence of over-represented anchors when computing regression scores. The CI hook integrates with existing eval orchestration to produce a single quality signal (sentry_score) which can be configured as soft (warning) or hard (block).

Changes include: new eval hook code, unit + integration tests, CI configs for gated behavior, and docs for on-call triage and tuning knobs.

Design notes: the fingerprint is intentionally compact (64-byte sketch) to keep storage and comparison cheap. We use cosine-stable bucketing and a simple KS-like test augmented with time-decay to be robust to gradual drifts. The attenuator uses inverse-frequency weighting based on prompt fingerprint clusters.

Rollout plan: feature gated off by default. Roll to staged canary cohorts using the eval harness canary flag; monitor \"sentry_score\" and cohort-coverage metrics in the dashboard. If false positives appear, tune decay window and cluster granularity documented below.

Backward compatibility: existing eval hooks are unchanged unless the gate is enabled via CI config. No model artifacts changed.

Checklist:
- [x] core detection algorithm implementation
- [x] unit + integration tests
- [x] CI hook wiring and example config
- [x] docs + runbook stub
- [x] reviewer sign-offs

Related: ENG-2219 tracks follow-ups for replacing the sketch with an L2-consistent fingerprint store and for adding cross-run attribution.
Ravi Singh (reviewer): Nice approach. Two requests: 1) add telemetry counters for fingerprint cluster sizes, 2) please comment the decay constant choices so SRE can tune later.
Maya Chen (author): Added telemetry counters and expanded comments on decay constants; left knobs in config with defaults. See amended commit.
Eve Hart (reviewer): Integration test looks flaky on the first run (timeout at 55s). Can we reduce the dependence on network timing in the integration harness?
Maya Chen (author): Reworked the test to use deterministic local data with a small mocked timer; CI reran and passed.
Add configurable Contextual Fingerprint Sentry + biased-sample attenuator for prompt-set regression gating; opt-in CI hook to reduce noisy false positives and provide semantically-aware change signals.
No migration required. To enable the gate, add 'contextual_fingerprint_sentry: enabled: true' to ci/config/eval_gates.yaml and tune 'decay_window' and 'cluster_granularity' under the same section. See docs/ci_hooks/contextual_fingerprint_sentry.md for examples.
payload.title: Contextual fingerprint sentry and biased-sample attenuator for prompt-set regression gating

Context: We see a recurring class of SLO regressions driven by inefficient prefetch behavior: infrequent high-cost prefetched invocations that inflate token cost and create noisy alerting during trading-hour spikes. This PR introduces two coordinated deliverables: 1) a prefetch census sampler (runtime sampling component) that records compact, pseudonymized census buckets for prefetched invocations to make long-tail prefetched cost observable at low cardinality; and 2) an operator-oriented "invocation scrub" playbook and dashboard that surfaces prefetched cohorts, entropy signals, and suggested alert dampening. Motivation: enable low-overhead, privacy-preserving visibility into prefetch efficacy and failure modes so SRE and runtime teams can tune prefetch parameters without turning on high-cardinality traces or full payload capture. Summary of changes: - runtime/sampler/prefetch_census.py: new lightweight sampler with reservoir-like buckets, entropy-weighted selection, and K-anon pseudonymization for prompt fingerprints. Emits metrics: prefetch.census.bucket_count, prefetch.census.bucket_latency_p50/p95, prefetch.census.cost_estimate_sum and prefetch.census.sample_rate. - runtime/telemetry/emitters.go: added compact protobuf schema and emitter helper to send census rollups to observability pipeline. - observability/dashboards/prefetch_census_dash.json: operator dashboard with: census sparkline, cohort cost heatmap, prefetch hit/miss ratio, and suggested alert score. - observability/runbooks/invocation_scrub.md: playbook with triage steps, recommended alert thresholds, and rollback instructions. - metrics/alerts/prefetch_alerts.yaml: tuned alert rules (quiet-window gating + cohort-based suppressor) and annotation links to playbook. - tests/sampler/test_census_sampler.py: unit and microbench tests validating reservoir behavior and pseudonymization. - e2e/replay/prefetch_replay_workflow.yaml: replay harness for backfilling census across a tenant window. Commits (summary): ["7b2c9d3: initial sampler implementation and unit tests", "a4f8e11: add protobuf emitter and telemetry integration", "c9d2fac: dashboard + runbook + alert rules", "d0aa3b2: fix sampling edge-case (zero-prefetch) and add additional tests", "e44f1f5: CI & lint fixes; update docs"]. Files changed (high level): ["runtime/sampler/prefetch_census.py", "runtime/telemetry/emitters.go", "observability/dashboards/prefetch_census_dash.json", "observability/runbooks/invocation_scrub.md", "metrics/alerts/prefetch_alerts.yaml", "tests/sampler/test_census_sampler.py", "e2e/replay/prefetch_replay_workflow.yaml", "docs/notes/prefetch-census.md"]. Testing and validation: - Unit tests: added coverage for reservoir boundary conditions and pseudonymization; all unit tests pass locally. - Integration: local-dev emitter forwards compact rollups to staging observability pipeline; dashboards render expected sparklines for synthesized replay data. - Replay: used e2e/replay harness to replay a 24h tenant window with prefetched invocations to validate heatmap shapes and alert clustering. Performance impact: sampler is micro-optimized and runs inline in the prefetch path with a configurable sample_rate (default 1/1000). Benchmarks on an r5-like instance show <0.15ms p99 added latency per prefetch call at default settings. Config & rollout: guarded by feature flag runtime.feature_flags.prefetch_census_v1 and a gating config in runtime/config/prefetch.yaml. Rollout plan: enable in staging for 48h -> 10% of traffic in main -> 100% after 7 days and signal stability. Rollback: flip feature flag off (no schema changes); emitter buffers can be drained and pipeline ignores unknown bucket ids. Security & privacy: pseudonymization is one-way hash with salt stored in KMS; no raw prompt text included in rollups. Compliance signoff: security reviewed (Jonah Kim) for data minimization. CI: unit/integration/lint passed in CI; e2e replay was run manually and results attached. Related work: follows ENG-3012 (prefetch observability spike investigation) and complements ENG-3099 (cohort-based alerting). Ask reviewers: please focus review on reservoir algorithm correctness, protobuf schema compatibility, and the alert gating logic. After merge: operator rotation: mark runbook with oncall owners and schedule a 30m knowledge share.
Ravi Patel: Can you walk through guarantees for the reservoir under sustained bursty prefetched traffic? Looks like edge-case fixed in d0aa3b2 helps — please add a comment describing the complexity and amortized cost.
Marta Alvarez (author): Added inline comments in prefetch_census.py and a paragraph in docs/notes/prefetch-census.md explaining amortized cost. Also included microbench numbers in the commit message.
Elena Park: Alert rule change looks reasonable; please ensure quiet-window gating defaults to tenant-level suppression to avoid cross-tenant bleed. Also request adding a synthetic SLO dashboard tile for prefetch-induced cost.
Marta Alvarez: Updated metrics/alerts/prefetch_alerts.yaml to include tenant-scoped labels and added the SLO tile to the dashboard JSON. Verified rendering in staging.
Jonah Kim: Security review OK — pseudonymization approach acceptable, salt rotation documented. Approved.
Adds a lightweight prefetch census sampler to improve cache warmup telemetry and a runbook (invocation scrub playbook) for operators to triage prefetched invocation anomalies. No customer-visible API changes.

Motivation: Private deployments have accumulated ad-hoc tfstate boundaries and heterogeneous GPU node pool configs which complicate upgrades and cross-tenant networking. This PR rationalizes state layout, adds a safe migrator workflow, and standardizes GPU taints/affinities and IAM templates. Goals: 1) Move from multiple overlapping tfstate backends to a clear per-vpc + shared-infra split while preserving rollback ability; 2) Introduce a migration tool that creates a plan-only preview and a reversible apply path; 3) Standardize GPU node pool profiles (scheduling, taints, labels) and expose those as stable variables; 4) Split IAM role module into workload-scoped templates (serving, admin, metrics) to reduce cross-scope privileges; 5) Add compact networking module for peered-private-slices used by on-prem clusters. Checklist: [x] design doc linked, [x] automated migrator implemented, [x] terraform validate & fmt passing, [x] staged upgrade documented, [ ] e2e migration run in staging (scheduled). Migration notes: the migrator uses temporary workspaces and creates a guard record in state to allow automated rollback. Customers with custom state layouts are supported via an opt-in mapping file (examples/legacy-mapping.tfvars).
Jonah: Can we make the migrator idempotent if it is re-run against a partially migrated state? Suggest adding a guard file and an explicit --resume flag.
Author (Maya): Migrator now creates migration.lock in the target backend and supports --resume; added tests covering interrupted runs.
Priya: IAM split looks good, but please ensure default policy size stays under the provider limit. Consider creating a minimal service role for metrics ingestion.
Author (Maya): Pulled common policy fragments into iam/_fragments.tf and added a minimal metrics role with reduced privileges.
Evelyn: Tests failed in CI on first run (terraform fmt diff). I see a follow-up commit fixed formatting and the CI run passed.
Ops (manual comment): During staging migration, we observed elevated control-plane API calls; added rate-limit throttle to migrator and documented backoff behavior.
Consolidated tfstate layout for Private deployments (per-vpc + shared-infra), added a reversible tfstate migrator, standardized GPU node pool scheduling and taint profiles, split IAM templates by workload type, and introduced a peered-slices networking module for on-prem VPC peering. Migration tool and guide included at docs/private-deploy-upgrade.md.
Staged rollout recommended: 1) Run migrator in preview mode against a copy of backend in staging; 2) Apply to one non-prod VPC and validate runtime (GPU scheduling, IAM role bindings); 3) Run migrator in target VPCs during a maintenance window with --throttle; 4) If issues, run migrator --rollback which restores state snapshot and removes lock. Detailed steps in docs/private-deploy-upgrade.md
Unit tests for migrator and module-level tf validate added. Integration staging migration run scheduled; initial smoke tests pass on nodepool creation/scale, IAM binding assertions, and peering connectivity using our perf-canary harness.
The migrator writes migration.lock to the backend and stores a timestamped snapshot (S3/GCS) before making changes. Ensure long-term backend credentials are scoped correctly; rolling back requires access to snapshot buckets. If using custom backend paths, supply examples/legacy-mapping.tfvars to map old state segments.
- E2E migration run in staging (blocked by infra window)
- Add telemetry to migrator for progress reporting
- Consider supporting partial resource move to avoid short windows of reduced capacity
This PR is intentionally conservative: no automatic re-tagging of existing nodepools, only new profile variables and an explicit migrator path. Customers with highly-customized tfstate should coordinate with SRE before running migrator.

payload.body:
## Summary
This adds an opinionated `vpc-endpoints` Terraform module for the Redwood Private VPC footprint (alpha). The module creates a baseline set of Gateway + Interface endpoints commonly required in fully-private subnets (no public egress) and exposes explicit inputs for private DNS behavior.

Primary motivation: reduce pilot failures related to image pulls / registry access / AWS API access in private subnets by making endpoints part of our reference modules, while staying compatible with customer DNS strategies (Route 53 Resolver, custom forwarders, split-horizon, etc.).

## What’s included
### New module: `modules/vpc-endpoints`
Creates endpoints in the provided VPC + subnets:
- **Gateway endpoint**: S3 (`com.amazonaws.<region>.s3`) with route table association(s)
- **Interface endpoints** (baseline):
  - ECR API (`com.amazonaws.<region>.ecr.api`)
  - ECR DKR (`com.amazonaws.<region>.ecr.dkr`)
  - STS (`com.amazonaws.<region>.sts`)
  - CloudWatch Logs (`com.amazonaws.<region>.logs`)
  - CloudWatch Monitoring (`com.amazonaws.<region>.monitoring`)
  - EC2 (`com.amazonaws.<region>.ec2`) (needed for some node lifecycle flows depending on cluster config)

Also provides a shared security group for endpoint ENIs (default: allow 443 from private subnet CIDRs + any additional CIDRs passed via inputs).

### Private DNS controls
We’ve had multiple pilot/customer environments where enabling Private DNS on interface endpoints causes unexpected resolution changes due to existing Route 53 Resolver rules / custom DNS forwarders.

Inputs:
- `interface_private_dns_enabled` (bool, default **true**): global default for interface endpoints
- `interface_private_dns_overrides` (map(string)=bool): per-service override keyed by short name (e.g. `ecr_api`, `ecr_dkr`, `sts`, `logs`, `monitoring`, `ec2`)
- `enable_*` toggles per endpoint (e.g. `enable_ecr`, `enable_sts`, `enable_logs`) to support environments that have a subset already provisioned by central networking teams

Behavior:
- If an endpoint is enabled and its private DNS is enabled, we set `private_dns_enabled = true` for that endpoint.
- If disabled, we still provision the endpoint but do not flip private DNS; customers can manage DNS explicitly (and the installer can use endpoint-specific DNS names if needed).

### Outputs
- `gateway_endpoint_id_s3`
- `interface_endpoint_ids` (map)
- `interface_endpoint_dns_entries` (map of lists; useful for troubleshooting)
- `endpoints_security_group_id`

## Changes in examples
- `examples/alpha/private-vpc/` now wires in the endpoints module and passes the private subnets + route tables.
- Added a short README section explaining the trade-offs of private DNS and how to debug resolution (dig against VPC resolver, check resolver rules, confirm endpoint private hosted zone association).

## CI updates
- GitHub Actions now runs `terraform fmt -check` and `terraform validate` for:
  - `modules/vpc-endpoints`
  - `examples/alpha/private-vpc` (init with `-backend=false`)
- This is intentionally lightweight; integration tests come later in ENG-4860.

## Notes / constraints
- This module assumes AWS provider >= 5.x and Terraform >= 1.5 (consistent with repo baseline).
- Subnets passed to interface endpoints should be private subnets with appropriate NACLs allowing 443 to the endpoint ENIs.
- We avoid hardcoding endpoint policies by default. Policy can be passed via `interface_endpoint_policy_json` / `s3_gateway_endpoint_policy_json` if security teams require explicit allowlists.

## Testing
- `terraform validate` across module + example
- Manual: applied in sandbox (single region) and verified:
  - ECR endpoints resolve to private IPs when private DNS enabled
  - `aws ecr get-login-password` succeeds from an instance in a private subnet without NAT
  - CloudWatch Logs PutLogEvents succeeds from private subnet

## Checklist
- [x] Module docs added
- [x] Example updated
- [x] CI validation updated
- [x] Security review requested

## Screenshots / logs
N/A

---

### Reviewer discussion highlights
**Marcus Lin (Security):** “Please avoid implicit broad access via endpoint policies; can we default to a restrictive policy?”

**Bruno Silva (Author):** “AWS default endpoint policy is effectively full access within account context; we can’t safely infer customer allowlists. Added optional policy JSON inputs and documented recommended patterns (limit actions + principals, and restrict to required ARNs).”

**Hanae Suzuki (Security):** “Private DNS defaults to true will surprise some enterprises with existing resolver rules. Please add a global flag and per-service overrides, and call out the risk in README.”

**Bruno Silva (Author):** “Implemented `interface_private_dns_enabled` + `interface_private_dns_overrides` and added ‘DNS gotchas’ section to module README + example.”

**Victor Alvarez (Networking):** “S3 should be gateway endpoint by default. For route table associations: accept list to support shared route tables across private subnets.”

**Bruno Silva (Author):** “Done—`s3_route_table_ids` is a list; example passes private route tables.”

**Nina Petrova (Private Deployments):** “Make sure ECR includes both ecr.api and ecr.dkr; we’ve seen partial setups fail during image pulls.”

**Bruno Silva (Author):** “Both included under `enable_ecr` (creates both endpoints), with per-endpoint private DNS overrides supported.”

**Sahana Iyer (CI):** “CI should validate the example too; module-only validate won’t catch wiring issues.”

**Bruno Silva (Author):** “Added `examples/alpha/private-vpc` init/validate step with backend disabled.”

---

## Merge notes
Squash merged after final security + networking approvals. Follow-ups tracked in ENG-4869 (installer preflight) to ensure we warn clearly when endpoints are missing or private DNS is off and the environment expects it.
New `modules/vpc-endpoints` for Gateway + Interface endpoints used by Redwood Private on AWS.
Adds private DNS controls to avoid breaking customer DNS/resolvers while still enabling endpoint usage.
Example environment now provisions endpoints + security group for endpoint ENIs.
payload.title: Add VPC endpoints module + private DNS options for Redwood Private (alpha)

payload.body:
This PR introduces an opinionated set of Security Group (SG) modules/patterns for Redwood Private AWS deployments (alpha). The intent is to reduce pilot variability and common discovery churn by shipping Redwood-validated defaults for: (1) EKS worker/node SG behavior (private nodes), (2) load balancer SGs for internal ingress (ALB/NLB) and controlled cross-subnet traffic, and (3) egress policy that works in a mostly-private VPC with VPC endpoints (ECR/S3/STS/CloudWatch Logs, etc.). Key goals: keep the default posture secure (no accidental broad public egress), but avoid breaking real-world installs where customers still need proxy/NAT-based egress or have non-standard endpoint/DNS setups. The modules are designed to be composable and to expose controlled extension points (additional egress CIDRs, additional destination SGs, and an explicit opt-in for “wide egress”). Summary of changes: Added new module `modules/security-groups` with submodules `eks_nodes`, `internal_lb`, and `egress`. Added a shared `rules` helper to centralize common TCP/UDP rules and keep diffs readable. Default node SG: ingress from cluster SG (EKS-managed), ingress from internal LB SG on app ports (configurable list, default 443), and egress constrained to VPC endpoints (via prefix lists and endpoint ENI SGs) + DNS + NTP (optional). Default internal LB SG: ingress from allowlisted CIDRs / SGs (supports customer VPN/DX CIDRs) and egress only to node SG on configured target ports. Default egress SG pattern: supports two modes: (a) “endpoint-only” (default) where 443 egress is restricted to endpoint prefix lists and/or endpoint SG IDs, and (b) “wide” where 0.0.0.0/0 egress on 443 is allowed for customers who require NAT/proxy access during bring-up (explicit input `enable_wide_egress = true`, default false). Outputs: `node_security_group_id`, `internal_lb_security_group_id`, `egress_security_group_id`, plus lists for per-rule debugging to make installer preflight messages actionable. Example usage added to `examples/alpha/private-eks-vpc/` and referenced in README. Notes: This PR does not attempt to model every enterprise firewall topology; instead, it standardizes the baseline and provides extension points. In particular, customers with explicit proxy egress can attach the egress SG to proxy ENIs or override via `additional_egress_*` inputs. Checklist: [x] Terraform fmt/validate; [x] tflint; [x] checkov (with documented suppressions where appropriate); [x] example plan applies in sandbox; [x] docs updated for supported extension points; [x] aligns with installer expectations for private image pulls (ECR/S3/STSv2).
Victor Alvarez (review): The module shape looks good, but we need to be careful about the semantic meaning of “egress SG” in AWS. If customers attach multiple SGs to nodes, AWS unions the rules—so the secure default can be defeated by attaching a permissive SG elsewhere. Can we make the default still safe while not pretending it’s enforced? Also, can we prefer endpoint ENI SG IDs over prefix lists where possible? Bruno Silva (author): Agree. I added language to the module README: ‘This module provides a secure baseline but cannot prevent additional SG attachments.’ For endpoints, the module now supports both `endpoint_prefix_list_ids` and `endpoint_security_group_ids` and encourages endpoint SGs when customers own them. Marcus Lin (security review): Strong request: default must not allow 0.0.0.0/0 egress. We’ve seen pilots where “temporary” wide egress becomes permanent. If we need a break-glass option, it must be explicit and loud. Also, do not allow all VPC CIDR by default unless justified. Bruno Silva (author): Updated defaults: `enable_wide_egress` is false and guarded; when true we tag the SG with `redwood.io/wide-egress=true` and print a warning in README + example. Removed default allow-to-vpc-cidr egress; it’s now `additional_egress_cidrs` (empty by default). Nina Petrova (private deployments): For EKS private control plane, ensure nodes can reach the cluster endpoint and CoreDNS resolution works consistently. Some customers use VPC resolver endpoints; others rely on the default AmazonProvidedDNS. We should avoid overfitting. Bruno Silva (author): Node SG egress includes UDP/TCP 53 to the VPC resolver address range via `dns_egress_cidrs` input (defaults to the VPC CIDR, with clear guidance to set it to resolver endpoint IPs when used). Control plane connectivity remains governed by EKS-managed cluster SG rules; our module expects `cluster_security_group_id` as input and adds required ingress from that SG. Irene Choi (infra): The initial version had separate SGs per endpoint. That’s too many moving pieces for alpha. Please keep it to three SGs max and make the extension points straightforward. Bruno Silva (author): Simplified: three SGs as described (nodes/internal-lb/egress). Endpoints are referenced as destinations rather than modeled as their own SGs (optional input if customer provides endpoint SG IDs). Sean Gallagher (SRE): Concern about operability: in practice, debugging broken installs is easier when there’s a quick ‘make it work’ path. Can we support a temporary egress mode without rewriting code? Bruno Silva (author): Added `enable_wide_egress` + `wide_egress_ports` (default [443]) and documented a recommended rollback plan: start endpoint-only, only enable wide egress for initial bring-up if required, then revert once endpoints/proxy are validated. Hanae Suzuki (security templates): checkov is flagging ingress rules that depend on user-provided CIDRs. That’s fine, but we need strong validation and examples. Bruno Silva (author): Added variable validation: CIDRs must be valid and non-empty; added example showing allowlisting a VPN CIDR and a customer bastion SG; added checkov suppressions only for the module that intentionally supports customer-provided allowlists, with justification text. Final outcome: approvals from Victor + Marcus after tightening defaults and documenting the break-glass path; merged after CI green.
Alpha: Added opinionated security group modules for Redwood Private AWS VPC deployments (EKS nodes, internal load balancers, and endpoint-first egress). Default posture avoids broad public egress; provides explicit opt-in for temporary wide egress when required during bring-up.
payload.title: Add security group patterns for private ingress/egress (EKS + installer-friendly outputs)

Summary:
This PR introduces a release ledger service and CI pipeline changes to harden private installer releases: deterministic release ledger files (ledger.json), RFC3161 timestamping for release bundles, cosign key rotation automation, and Terraform+Helm client checks to validate ledger entries during install/upgrade. Motivation: we observed confusion during incident SUP-502 where unsigned or un-timestamped artifacts complicated rollback and verification across air-gapped installs. The ledger provides an immutable index with checksums, cross-signatures, and a rollback token that ties to a Merkle root for quick verification.

What this changes (high level):
- CI: release pipeline (ci/pipelines/release.yaml) now builds artifacts, computes SHA512 checksums, requests RFC3161 time-stamp signed timestamps, and invokes cosign to sign artifacts. A cosign rotation job (ci/scripts/rotate-cosign-keys.sh) can be run on a schedule to rotate ephemeral keys and re-sign ledger roots.
- Ledger: tools/release-ledger/generate_ledger.go creates ledger.json containing ordered entries: artifact name, version, checksum, cosignSig, timestampToken, provenance link, and merkle_path. The ledger is output to release-bundles/<version>/ledger.json and uploaded to mirrors (S3/GCS).
- Installer: redwood-private-installer/helm chart gains pre-install hook that validates the fetched ledger.json against the embedded public cosign keys (from terraform module); the helm hook will fail the install if ledger validation fails.
- Terraform: redwood-terraform/modules/installer now exposes a data source installer_release_ledger which fetches and verifies ledger.json prior to rendering values; new optional parameter validate_ledger = true.
- Docs: docs/private-deploy/releases.md documents operator steps for key rotation, emergency rollback procedure using rollback tokens, and how to mirror ledgers to air-gapped environments.

Checklist:
- [x] Build + sign artifacts in CI
- [x] Generate ledger.json with merkle root and timestamp token
- [x] Integrate ledger validation into Helm pre-install hook
- [x] Add Terraform data source for ledger fetch/verify
- [x] Add docs for rotation and rollback
- [x] E2E tests for installer validation

Commits (summary):
- 7a9d2c1: ci(release): add RFC3161 timestamping step and checksum collection
- d3f1b6e: tools(ledger): initial ledger generator with merkle tree implementation and JSON schema v1
- e8c0a4b: helm(private-installer): add pre-install hook and ledger validator sidecar script
- b1f5a77: terraform(installer): data source installer_release_ledger + module flag validate_ledger
- 2d4f9aa: docs: release rotation and emergency rollback runbook

Files changed (high level):
- ci/pipelines/release.yaml (update: adds timestamp & cosign steps)
- ci/scripts/rotate-cosign-keys.sh (new)
- tools/release-ledger/generate_ledger.go (new)
- tools/release-ledger/README.md (new)
- redwood-private-installer/helm/templates/hooks/ledger-validate-job.yaml (new)
- redwood-private-installer/helm/templates/_helpers.tpl (modified to include ledger config)
- redwood-terraform/modules/installer/data_source_installer_ledger.tf (new)
- redwood-terraform/modules/installer/README.md (updated)
- docs/private-deploy/releases.md (updated)
- tests/e2e/private-installer/ledger_validation_test.go (new)
- scripts/mirror_ledgers_to_airgap.sh (new)

Testing and CI notes:
- Local unit tests for ledger generator and merkle tree implemented and passing.
- Integration: ran private-installer helm chart against kind cluster with mocked S3 ledger endpoint; initial run failed because cosign key in test environment was expired. Fixed by adding key rotation stub and re-ran.
- CI flakiness: the first pipeline run flagged an intermittent failure in tests/e2e/private-installer/ledger_validation_test.go due to clock skew in CI runner which caused RFC3161 token validation to fail. Added clock skew tolerance (+/- 5s) in validation logic and re-ran. Final CI status: all checks passed.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Marcus Chen: "High level looks good. Please call out the rotation cadence and the operator UX — we should avoid forcing frequent re-downloads for air-gapped customers."
- Author reply: "Added rotation guidance in docs (recommended 90-day rotation for root keys, 30-day for signing keys; ledger roots re-signed on rotation). For air-gapped installs we publish mirrored ledgers and provide offline signing tokens."
- Priya Nair: "Nit: move the merkle path into a dedicated field in schema v1 and add an example in README. Also ensure terraform data source uses backoff when fetching mirrors."
- Author reply: "Addressed: schema updated and README includes example. Terraform data source now retries with exponential backoff up to 5 attempts."
- Ethan Park: "CI: can we gate rotation job behind an env var and only enable in release pipeline? I don't want scheduled rotations in dev clusters."
- Author reply: "Rotation job requires CI_ROTATE_COSIGN=true and a KMS endpoint; added guard in pipeline and detailed parameters in docs."
- Marcus Chen: "Approve after resolving minor terraform lint failures."
- PR status: approvals received from Marcus Chen and Priya Nair; Ethan provided an approving comment after CI guard was added.

Post-merge actions and rollout plan:
- Deploy rotation cron job to production CI (ops) with CI_ROTATE_COSIGN enabled and monitor for unexpected re-sign events.
- Notify customers running private-installer to upgrade terraform module to >= v1.3.0 (module version bumped in this PR).
- Run a manual ledger mirror to major cloud mirrors and verify checksums at 3rd-party registries.
- Schedule follow-up to add a subscription webhook that alerts operators on ledger changes (ENG-1145).

Security considerations:
- Keys: cosign keys stored in KMS and rotated via CI script that uses short-lived keys where possible.
- Verification: Helm pre-install validation runs inside the cluster as a Job that fetches ledger.json and validates signatures; for air-gapped installs operators should use the provided mirror and offline verification tool.
- Auditing: ledger entries include provenance links to CI build artifacts and pipeline run IDs to ease root-cause lookup.

Notes on uniqueness and divergence from prior work:
This PR differs from previous signed-manifest work in that it: 1) introduces a ledger + merkle-root approach (tamper-evident index of releases), 2) integrates RFC3161 timestamp tokens alongside cosign signatures for external time proof, 3) couples terraform/helm client-side verification (pre-install) rather than only CI/offline signing, and 4) automates cosign key rotation as part of the release pipeline (guarded).

If you want to run locally: see tools/release-ledger/README.md for build/run instructions; sample command: go run tools/release-ledger/generate_ledger.go --input release-bundles/v1.10.0 --output ledger.json --signer cosign://ci-team

Adds a tamper-evident release ledger and automated cosign key rotation for private installer artifacts; CI pipeline now stamps and cross-signs signed manifests and provides rollback tokens. Backwards compatible for existing private-installer clients that fetch release.yaml. Operators should run the rotation job per the new docs and update terraform module versions.
Marcus Chen: High level looks good. Please call out the rotation cadence and the operator UX — we should avoid forcing frequent re-downloads for air-gapped customers.
Priya Nair: Nit: move the merkle path into a dedicated field in schema v1 and add an example in README. Also ensure terraform data source uses backoff when fetching mirrors.
Ethan Park: CI: can we gate rotation job behind an env var and only enable in release pipeline? I don't want scheduled rotations in dev clusters.

Motivation: Private installs currently store a monolithic tfstate per VPC which prevents fine-grained tenant-region lifecycle operations, complicates GPU nodepool leases and IAM role scoping, and makes safe rollbacks cumbersome. This PR introduces a set of composable Terraform modules and a coordinated migration path to slice tfstate by tenant+region, add IAM-scoped profile modules, and provide explicit lifecycle/lease primitives for GPU node pools. Key changes: 1) New module tfmodules/tenant_state_slicer - encapsulates state partitioning and remote state backend wiring for tenant+region shards; supports optional state stitching for cross-tenant shared resources. 2) New module tfmodules/iam_profile_scoped - generates tenant-scoped IAM roles, service accounts, and minimal cross-account policies using a templated role factory (supports KMS/HSM bindings via variables). 3) New module tfmodules/gpu_lease_profile - declares lease resources, ephemeral pool annotation schema, and lifecycle hooks for graceful eviction and drain; integrates with private-installer's allocator via documented outputs. 4) Migration tooling under tools/tfstate_splitter.py and tools/plan-apply-orchestrator.sh - allow dry-run splits, state copies with validation (checksums + drift detection), and automated rollback hooks that create a tfstate-anchor file to allow atomic revert if downstream apply fails. 5) Backwards compatibility: existing monolithic stacks continue to work; the new modules are opt-in via workspace var enable_state_slicing=false by default. 6) Tests and CI: added e2e plan-only runs in staging CI for three sample tenant-region shards, unit tests for IAM role templates, and a chaos test verifying lease eviction path. Migration and rollout plan: - Phase 1: opt-in in a single non-prod tenant-region, run tfstate_splitter dry-run and manual validation. - Phase 2: automated split + apply with monitoring and canary traffic routing; rollback uses tfstate-anchor and the orchestrator script. - Phase 3: gradual rollout to other regions and tenants. Operational notes included in README with step-by-step commands, required IAM permissions for the migrator, and SRE runbook for emergency revert. This PR is intended to reduce blast radius of state changes, enable tenant-scoped IAM least-privilege, and improve the safety of GPU pool lifecycle operations. Related Linear/Jira references included.

Motivation: Private deployments currently keep GPU node pools, IAM roles, and TF state anchored to the same monolithic state file. This makes tenant onboarding, credential rotation, and network reassignments risky and slow. This PR introduces two opinionated Terraform modules (tenant-gpu-fanout and iam-credential-rotator), a light migration helper, and a documented rollout/rollback path to gradually decouple GPU pools and IAM credentials per-tenant while maintaining an auditable state migration path.

Summary of changes: added a new module terraform/modules/tenant-gpu-fanout that creates tenant-scoped GPU node subpools, tenant-local subnet attachments, and lease metadata outputs; added terraform/modules/iam-credential-rotator to manage short-lived IAM service account keys with optional KMS/HSM wrapping; introduced a migration helper script tools/tf-migrate-fanout (bash + minimal Go helper) that creates new per-tenant state shards and migrates resources with state-lock safety checks; updated top-level environments to consume the new modules via optional for_each maps to allow phased rollout; added unit/integration test harness for the modules under tests/terraform/tenant-fanout; and updated docs/terraform/private/gpu-fanout.md with rollout steps and rollback playbook.

Why this is different: existing TF work covers TF state shard boundaries and GPU allocation operators, but this PR focuses on a gradual fanout pattern (one tenant -> many small nodepools) plus an automated credential rotation primitive tailored for Private installations where KMS/HSM integration and air-gapped rollout are common requirements. It also ships a migration helper rather than an immediate state rewrite to reduce blast radius.

Implementation details: the tenant-gpu-fanout module exposes the following inputs (high-level): tenant_id, preferred_zones (list), gpu_profile, min/max_pool_size, node_taints, network_attachment (object), state_prefix. Outputs: list of nodepool ids, per-pool subnet ids, lease_metadata (string JSON), and state_shard_key. The module implements a provider aliasing pattern so each tenant's nodepool resources can be targeted to a different GCP/AWS project or account if the environment map is provided. The iam-credential-rotator module creates a short-lived service account key (rotated by TTL), an optional KMS-wrapped secret version, and a rotation trigger hook compatible with our private-installer webhook contract. Rotations produce a new secret path and increment the rotation_index output to enable consumers to do atomic config swap.

Migration strategy (high level): 1) Enable tenant-gpu-fanout in a single non-prod environment with for_each limited to a test-tenant map; 2) Run tools/tf-migrate-fanout --preview to validate state changes; 3) Apply in canary mode to migrate nodepool resources to per-tenant shards; 4) Switch private-installer to read lease_metadata outputs and create tenant leases from the new nodepools; 5) Once stable, run rotate mode for IAM credentials (iam-credential-rotator) and switch workload identities over to new key material. The migration helper includes pre-apply validation (state lock check, resource diff summary), a timed backoff loop for API rate errors, and an idempotent rollback marker in state to allow safe reversal.

Testing and CI: added three new Terraform integration scenarios (smoke, canary, and regression) that run in our existing CI but in a sandboxed AWS/GCP test account. CI initially failed on static analysis (terraform fmt) and the IAM policies lint; fixes were pushed and CI reran. New tests assert that nodepools created by fanout include expected taints, that network attachments maintain existing CIDR allocations, and that rotation creates a new wrapped secret and increments rotation_index.

Security considerations: rotation module defaults to short TTLs and requires explicit kms_key input for wrapping in Private installs. The module has an allowlist for principals that can request rotations and emits audit events via our audit-log exporter hook. The PR includes updated SLO/alert suggestions in the docs for increased IAM key churn.

Rollback plan: the migration helper writes a migration marker into the source state and creates a copy of the prior state under state-prefix/backup/<migration-id>. The rollback playbook (docs/.../gpu-fanout.md) provides commands to revert private-installer to the previous lease source and to re-run tf-migrate-fanout --rollback which re-anchors resources back into the original state file. We validated rollback in integration by migrating a canary tenant and then rolling back under simulated API latency.

Related: touches private-installer and private-helm charts (annotations to consume rotation webhooks), and the change is coordinated with ENG-4201 (tenant onboarding) and ENG-4132 (credential hardening).

Checklist: [x] module code + examples [x] migration helper + preview mode [x] docs + rollout/rollback playbook [x] CI integration tests [x] reviewer feedback addressed

Commits (high level): see commits list below for granular messages.

Merge outcome: merged by Asha Patel (squash) after addressing reviewers' comments and two CI green runs.

Asha: Can we gate the KMS wrapping behind a variable and default it off for cloud evals? (resolved)
Miguel: Be explicit about provider aliasing in the module docs and show example for cross-project nodepools. (addressed)
Liang: Ensure rotation hook has retry/backoff to handle intermittent 500s from the vault endpoint. (added exponential backoff in migrate.go)
Rachel: Please add an explicit test that validates taints are preserved during migration. (added to tests)
Asha (final): Approved after CI green and small policy tightenings
- Added tenant-gpu-fanout Terraform module to create per-tenant GPU nodepools and subnet attachments.
- Added iam-credential-rotator module for short-lived service account keys with optional KMS wrapping.
- Migration helper (tf-migrate-fanout) to preview/apply/rollback per-tenant state splits.
- Docs and rollback playbook for staged rollout.
