Summary: This PR adds/updates Grafana dashboards to support the tiered batching defaults launch (fast/standard/cost-efficient). The goal is to make it easy to answer: (1) which tier is active and why, (2) whether latency SLOs are being met per tier, (3) whether we are building unsafe queue depth / wait time under load, and (4) whether batch formation is behaving as expected (size and wait budget). Dashboards added: (A) Tiered Batching — Overview: high-level latency (p50/p95/p99), request rate, error rate, and saturation widgets with tier selector; includes a ‘canary vs control’ comparison row (for staged rollout) keyed off rollout cohort label when present. (B) Tiered Batching — Latency & Streaming: end-to-end latency and time-to-first-token panels, split by tier; includes separate panels for streaming vs non-streaming routes to avoid blending distributions. (C) Tiered Batching — Queue & Backpressure: queue depth, queue wait time, admission control rejects, shed/load-shed counts, and scheduler overload mode indicator (when enabled). (D) Tiered Batching — Batch Formation: batch_size_tokens histogram heatmap, batch_size_requests distribution, max_wait_ms utilization, and prefill/decode occupancy (when exported). (E) Tiered Batching — Regression Triage: side-by-side ‘current vs baseline’ p95/p99 deltas for top models, plus a panel for top offenders by (tier, model_family, region). Metrics and tags: This PR assumes runtime emits a tier label and reason codes per ENG-18426 / PR-28473; dashboards are built to work even when reason codes are missing (panels gracefully hide that row). Cardinality constraints are enforced by default: panels use model_family and route_group where possible; model is a template var with a safe allowlist and defaults to ‘top 10 by traffic’. Region is a template var but panels aggregate to region_group when high-cardinality environments are detected. Also adds guidance text within dashboards: “If you need per-route debugging, switch to the Route Debug dashboard and pin a single route to avoid unbounded series.” Alert readiness: No paging alerts are added in this PR (those live in alert-rules repo), but queries were shaped to be portable to PromQL recording rules. Includes draft threshold guidance in dashboard annotations (e.g., fast tier p99 regression > 10% for 15m at constant QPS) aligned with the SRE rollout checklist. Notable changes since first draft: (1) removed direct breakdown by tenant_id and full model name from the default view after review; (2) added a ‘series count’ panel to quickly spot label explosions; (3) renamed panels to match the SLO tier naming in the customer-facing docs (fast/standard/cost-efficient). Testing/validation: Exported dashboards loaded into staging Grafana; verified query performance under typical prod cardinality by replaying a 30m window in the metrics sandbox. Confirmed that all panels render with only tier labels enabled (no reason codes) and do not error when streaming labels are absent. Related: runtime metrics tier labels (redwood PR-28492), reason codes (redwood PR-28473), rollout flagging (redwood PR-28480), internal ticket INT-33012 (missing tier breakdown labels) resolved by aligning label keys used in dashboards with the runtime’s final taxonomy.
Adds tier-aware batching dashboards for runtime-1.22: latency (p50/p95/p99) by tier/model/region, queue depth + admission/backpressure signals, and batch size distribution with cardinality controls. Includes regression panels and alert-ready queries.
Allison Grant (requested changes): Please remove tenant_id and full model breakdown from default panels; this will blow up series. Also add a panel/annotation that helps operators notice cardinality spikes early.
Aisha Bello (author): Done — default breakdown is now tier x model_family x region_group. Added a ‘Series count (approx)’ panel and annotations with debugging guidance for per-route drilldowns.
Caleb Johnson (comment): TTFT panels should be streaming-only; otherwise they’ll confuse non-streaming E2E latency. Also confirm the label is `batching_tier` and not `tier` to match runtime taxonomy.
Aisha Bello (author): Split TTFT to streaming-only and renamed vars to match `batching_tier` (with backward-compat fallback to `tier` for older staging builds).
Sean Gallagher (comment): Add a row that maps to rollout cohort / feature flag state so on-call can compare canary vs control quickly during staged rollout. Doesn’t need to be perfect, but make it obvious.
Aisha Bello (author): Added a comparison row using `rollout_cohort` when present; it hides automatically if the label isn’t in the time range.
Logan Wright (approval): Query shapes look sane; thanks for adding allowlists and dropping tenant_id defaults. Approving once CI is green.
Allison Grant (approval): Looks good after cardinality changes. Please keep the note about pinning a single route for debugging — operators will miss this otherwise.
Aisha Bello (author): Kept the note + added a short ‘How to triage’ text panel at top of each dashboard.
payload.title: Add tiered batching dashboards (latency/queue/batch size) with cardinality-safe dimensions

Motivation: on-call workflows today are tightly coupled to long-lived runbook attachments and heavy telemetry dumps; responders often need a lightweight, ephemeral context that follows an incident lifecycle without creating long-lived artifacts. This PR introduces two cooperating pieces: (1) an Ephemeral Oncall Workflow Bridge that attaches a short-lived 'workflow context' to incidents and automatically expires after a TTL, and (2) a Telemetry Sampler CLI + server-side sampler that captures compact diagnostic envelopes (trace spans, sampled logs, key metrics) at controlled sample rates for fast triage.

What changed: added a small bridge microservice that can be triggered by the incident-bot or SLO alert pipelines to create/update a workflow context object (metadata + ephemeral note stream + short-lived temporary links). The bridge exposes a REST endpoint and a lightweight proto for clients. The telemetry sampler implements rate-limited sampling, field redaction hooks, and an opt-out header to ensure we never capture PII or sensitive headers. A new command-line tool (slo-sampler) allows on-call to request an immediate sample from a target service/trace id and attach the compact envelope to the workflow context.

Design notes: workflow contexts are stored in Redis with signed tokens for short-lived access; full historical artifacts remain in the long-term diagnostics bucket only if explicitly promoted by an engineer. Sampler uses deterministic hashing on trace id + incident id to allow reproducible sampling policies. Default sample rate is conservative (0.02) and can be overridden by policy. The bridge is intentionally minimal: no external UI changes were made in this PR; integration points are via incident-bot annotations and a small webhook that the Console can consume later.

Security & privacy: added KMS-backed signing for ephemeral tokens; sampling has a strict redaction pipeline configurable in environment variables. Default redaction removes headers matching Authorization/Cookie and scrubs email-like tokens. A short security review checklist is included in tests.

Tests & rollout: unit tests for sampler logic and bridge handlers included, e2e smoke harness that runs against a local dockerized Redis and sample backend. Rollout plan is staged: enable bridge in dev, opt-in beta in staging via feature flag, then roll to production with gradually increasing sample rates. Rollback is a feature-flag disable.

Why it matters: responders get fast, contextual diagnostic snapshots without creating large long-lived dumps; platform teams can tune costs via sample rate and promote only important captures to longer retention.

Notes: this description is intentionally compact; see changed_files for code pointers and the commits list for granular changes.
Luca Marin: Can we bound the total size of the compact envelope? If a sampled trace contains many logs it could still be huge.
Asha Patel: Good point — added streaming envelope builder and a max-envelope-size check; if exceeded we attach a size-metadata stub and a promotion hint instead.
Priya Nair: Please ensure default sample rate is documented and cannot be set higher than 0.1 by non-admins.
Asha Patel: Added config validation and a server-side max rate enforced by RBAC; updated ops doc with defaults.
Samir Gupta: CI failed initially on lint and flake8 in the CLI; I see you fixed that in f5c1d88 — can you squash the lint fix into the CLI commit?
Asha Patel: Squashed and rebased before merging; kept a separate test commit for auditability. CI re-ran and is passing.
- Introduced Ephemeral Oncall Workflow Bridge: short-lived context objects for incidents.
- Added Telemetry Sampler and slo-sampler CLI: controlled, redacted diagnostic envelopes for faster triage.

Motivation: On-call playbooks are frequently copied/edited per-service; we want parameterized, audit-friendly runbooks that can be rendered from alert context to reduce human error and speed MTTR. This PR adds a safe templating layer for SLO Toolkit playbooks and a lightweight incident-correlation hinter that surfaces nearby incidents likely related to the current alert. High-level changes: 1) playbooks/schema v2 with templating placeholders and conditional steps; 2) a sandboxed renderer using a limited templating DSL (subset of Jinja-like syntax, no arbitrary code); 3) an incident-correlation hints engine that computes three candidate correlated incidents per alert based on service/trace overlap, metric fingerprint similarity, and time-window heuristics; 4) CLI and web UI preview commands for rendered playbooks; 5) a migration helper (slo playbook migrate) to convert v1 playbooks to v2 automatically where possible. Backwards compatibility: v1 playbooks still supported; new renderer only activates for playbooks with "template_version: 2". Feature gated behind 'playbook_templates' flag and rollout plan described below. Implementation notes: - Template engine implemented in slo_toolkit/playbooks/renderer.py with a strict AST parser and whitelist for filter functions (date, truncate, split, join, lower, upper). No eval or import allowed. - Context keys: alert (metadata), telemetry (topN metrics snapshot), traces (sparse trace ids), recent_incidents (IDs and metadata). - Correlation hints implemented in slo_toolkit/correlation/hinter.py using a small ensemble: service overlap weight, metric fingerprint cosine similarity, and temporal proximity score. Candidates returned with explanation snippets for the UI. - Web UI: added preview pane and correlation hint panel to alert details (webui/alert_preview/*). - CLI: "slo playbook render --alert-id <id>" and "slo playbook migrate --dry-run" added. - Migration: slo_toolkit/migrations/migrate_v1_to_v2.py attempts safe substitution with warnings for manual review. Tests and validation: extensive unit tests for renderer and hinter; an integration test harness simulates incident-bot alerts and validates rendered output contains expected substitutions and no disallowed constructs. Security: initial security scan detected a potential template-injection vector in early impl; replaced the engine with the AST whitelisting approach and added fuzz tests. Rollout and operational plan: - Feature gate by default OFF. - Canary to 3 small teams for 2 weeks with manual opt-in. - Monitor renderer latency (p95 < 50ms) and correlation hint recall/precision via labelled incidents. - Auto-rollback if error-rate for alert pages increases by >1% or if rendering latency crosses 200ms for more than 5 minutes. Checklist: - [x] Renderer implementation and unit tests - [x] Correlation hinter and unit tests - [x] CLI + web UI changes + e2e tests - [x] Migration helper and docs - [x] Security review and fuzzing - [x] Feature gate and rollout plan Commits (high-level): - Add templating AST renderer and basic filters, add unit tests - Implement correlation hinter and scoring, add example fixtures - Add web UI preview pane, CLI commands, and migration helper - Fix security issues flagged by scan (sanitize filters, tighten whitelist) - Add integration tests against incident-bot simulation harness - Update docs: docs/playbooks/templating.md and migration guide Related work: builds on earlier runbook suggestion efforts (see ENG-4219) and integrates with incident-bot's alert context contract (PRs in incident-bot will follow to consume rendered playbooks).
Ethan Moore: Nice direction. Please ensure the templating DSL cannot access filesystem or call arbitrary methods. Add unit tests for malicious payloads.
Priya Shah (author): Added AST-only parser and explicit whitelist; added fuzz tests in tests/unit/test_renderer.py to assert runtime errors for banned constructs.
Lena Ortiz: Correlation hints look useful but could be noisy. Can we attach an explanation string so oncall sees why a candidate was suggested?
Priya Shah: Added explanation snippets and scoring breakdown to correlation response; UI displays top-3 with reasons.
Samir Patel: Performance concern for large alerts. Have we measured render latency under heavy load? Consider caching rendered playbooks per alert fingerprint.
Priya Shah: Added in-memory LRU cache for rendered results keyed by alert fingerprint; cache TTL 10m and configurable via env var SLO_PLAYBOOK_CACHE_TTL.
Ethan Moore: Security scan initially flagged template injection; confirm fix applied.
Priya Shah: Replaced safe_substitute approach with AST whitelist and removed use of python 'format' on untrusted inputs. Re-ran security scan (clean).
Adds v2 playbook templates (parameterized, conditional steps), a safe AST-based renderer, incident-correlation hints (top-3 candidates) and CLI/web preview tools. Feature gated and off by default; migration helper provided.

Context
We’ve had recurring issues where metering tables are “up” but not trustworthy: late-arriving events, duplicates due to retry/backfill paths, and dimensional nulls (e.g., region) causing downstream drift vs billing ledger. Finance/RevRec needs a consistent, auditable definition for: (1) how fresh billing datasets must be to be used for invoice preview / month-end close and (2) what correctness signals we monitor to catch billing-impacting issues early.

This PR adds a reusable SLO template focused on metering data quality, intended to be imported by services/pipelines that publish billing-critical tables (usage events, reconciliation exports, and ledger join views). The template standardizes:
- Freshness SLIs/SLOs (time since last complete partition; late event window)
- Correctness signals (drift vs ledger, duplicate event rate, null/missing dimension rate)
- Example alert rules with paging vs ticket thresholds
- Required runbook annotations and ownership metadata

What’s included
1) New template: metering_data_quality.yaml
- Freshness SLI: max(data_lag_minutes) over required partitions
- Drift SLI: abs(usage_events_cost - billing_ledger_cost) / billing_ledger_cost (aggregated by day + account + model + region)
- Duplicate-rate SLI: duplicate_event_count / total_event_count
- Null-dimension SLI: null_region_count / total_event_count (pattern supports other dimensions)

2) Alert policy defaults
- Freshness paging: > 90 minutes lag for “invoice-preview” tables (business hours), > 180 minutes otherwise
- Drift paging: > 0.75% for >= 2 consecutive evaluation periods OR > 2.0% once (guarded by min volume)
- Duplicate-rate paging: > 0.30% for >= 30m
- Null-rate paging: > 0.10% for >= 30m

3) Example service config + docs
- examples/redwood-metering/usage-events-quality-slo.yaml shows a concrete instantiation with common dimensions, min-volume guards, and runbook links
- docs/metering-data-quality-slo.md documents how to wire the template into Grafana/Prometheus, and how to tune thresholds for pipeline-specific characteristics

Non-goals
- This does not attempt to define the canonical meter spec (token counting, retries semantics, etc.). That remains in Confluence + Redwood app code.
- This does not ship the actual drift queries for every table; it provides a standard interface and example patterns.

Operational notes
- The defaults aim to reduce alert noise via min-volume thresholds and “consecutive periods” gating.
- Runbook link convention: runbook_url must point to the owning team’s doc with triage + mitigation + escalation (Finance sign-off where applicable).

Testing
- Unit tests validate template rendering and schema validation.
- Example config is validated in CI as a fixture.

Rollout plan
- Land template in slo-toolkit.
- Redwood monorepo will adopt in the metering sanity check job + Grafana dashboards (tracked in ENG-4421/PM-1872).
- After adoption, tune thresholds per region/model volume once we have 2 weeks of baseline.

Security/Access
- No customer data included; examples use placeholder metrics and sample names.
- Intended consumers should ensure the underlying metrics/queries respect billing-data access controls.

References
- Linear: PM-1842 (define meter sanity KPIs), PM-1872 (metering change control), ENG-4421 (alert on meter drift vs ledger)
- Related PRs in redwood: pr-27450 (sanity check job), pr-27510 (recon export), pr-27574 (runbook links)
- Adds a reusable SLO template for metering data quality (freshness + correctness signals).
- Adds example alerting rules and runbook link conventions for billing-impacting drift.
- Includes a sample service config for “usage_events -> billing_ledger” pipelines.
Mei Lin (review): Love the standardization. Two questions: (1) drift SLI definition uses cost—can we also allow token-count drift for endpoints where price tables change? (2) how do we avoid paging on tiny denominators?

Aisha Bello (author): Good call. I added a note in docs that drift can be configured on cost or units depending on what’s stable for the pipeline. For tiny denominators, I added min_volume guards in the example config and documented recommended min thresholds (e.g., ledger_cost >= $50/day or >= 1M tokens/day).

Logan Wright (review): Thresholds seem aggressive. Duplicate-rate paging at 0.30% might fire during planned backfills. Can we include a “maintenance window” / annotation mechanism?

Aisha Bello (author): Added required annotation fields: maintenance_silence_tag and runbook_url. Also updated docs to recommend silencing during planned backfills and logging an incident note when silences are used for billing-critical paths.

Allison Grant (review): Template should enforce ownership metadata. We’ve had orphaned alerts.

Aisha Bello (author): Added schema requirement for owner_team, slack_channel, and escalation_policy. CI now fails if missing.

Nadia Rahman (review): For drift, can we add an option to compute per-dimension drift (region/model) and roll up a worst-of? That’s typically how we catch missing dimensions.

Aisha Bello (author): Added a config pattern in docs: group_by_dimensions + worst_of aggregation. Kept the default rollup simple, but example shows region/model breakdown and a top-K panel.

Mei Lin (follow-up): Please add a short section on Finance sign-off expectations for changing SLO definitions.

Aisha Bello (author): Added “Change control” section referencing PM-1872 and recommended capturing pre/post comparisons in the runbook.

Approved-by: Mei Lin, Logan Wright, Allison Grant, Nadia Rahman

payload.body:
Context: As part of Safe apply + rollback for Optimization Configs, we need a consistent way to evaluate rollout gates across services/environments. Prior implementations hard-coded thresholds and metric queries per rollout controller, which made it difficult to tune defaults, apply consistent tagging requirements (tenant/model/region/config_version), and explain gate decisions in the Console/runbooks.

This PR adds a small, reusable “gate rule library” to slo-toolkit with two initial rules used by the canary rollout controller:
- Error rate (5xx) gate
- p95 latency gate

Key points:
- Sane defaults aimed at Hosted/Dedicated canaries, with explicit override hooks for Dedicated/private installs.
- A single evaluation result object that includes a user-facing explanation string, the metric query/selector used, the time window, and the exact threshold evaluated.
- Strict tag requirements (tenant, model, region, config_version) with a “fail closed” option for production rollouts (default), and “warn only” for staging.
- Guardrails to reduce false positives: minimum request volume check + burn-in period support.

The rollout controller (redwood repo) will consume these rules in a follow-up PR; this PR is scoped to slo-toolkit only.

Testing:
- Added unit tests covering: threshold parsing, minimum sample gating, tag validation, override precedence, and explanation formatting.
- Added golden tests for rendered queries to make refactors safer.

Rollout:
- No behavior change until the rollout controller switches to these rules.

Refs:
- Linear: ENG-4827 (SLO gates: latency and 5xx), ENG-4824 (canary rollout controller)
- Related: perf-canary gate signals and dashboard tagging work (config_version annotations).
Example (p95 latency):
- Default threshold: +15% over baseline OR absolute > 900ms (whichever is stricter), evaluated over 10m window after 3m burn-in.
- Minimum volume: 2,000 requests per scope.
- Required tags: tenant, model, region, config_version.

Returned evaluation (abridged):
status=FAIL
reason="p95 latency 1.14s > 900ms (window=10m, scope=tenant=acme model=llama-3-70b region=us-east-1 config_version=ocv_1736)"
Allison Grant (review): "Love the explanation string in the result — will help Console. Two asks: (1) ensure we always include the rendered selector with all required tags, and (2) add a distinct status for 'INSUFFICIENT_DATA' so controllers can pause rather than auto-fail in staging."
Aisha Bello (author): "Good call. I added `rendered_selector` to the result and introduced `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` with env policy (prod=fail-closed, staging=warn/pause). Added tests."
Sean Gallagher (review): "Can we make min-volume configurable per rule? Dedicated customers in low-traffic regions will otherwise get stuck."
Aisha Bello (author): "Yep — `min_samples` is now part of the override schema per gate. Default stays 2000 for Hosted canaries. README updated."
Benji Okafor (review): "From control plane side: please keep override precedence deterministic. We’ll likely pass overrides at rollout creation time and also have an env-level default."
Aisha Bello (author): "Implemented precedence: request_override > scope_override > env_default > rule_default. Added a unit test for precedence and documented it."
Allison Grant (approve): "Looks good now. The golden tests for query rendering are a nice touch."
Sean Gallagher (approve): "Ship it. Please follow up with a short runbook note on how to choose min volume for Dedicated."
Aisha Bello (author): "Ack — will add to the change-management policy/runbook in redwood docs."
New: reusable SLO gate rule library with standard result/explanation format.
New: built-in error-rate (5xx) and p95 latency gates with safe defaults and override schema.
New: required metrics tags enforcement (tenant/model/region/config_version) with configurable fail-closed policy.

## Context
This PR adds burn-rate alerting presets to `slo-toolkit` for Redwood Hosted API enterprise protected routes as part of the Hot-route capacity protection initiative. The intent is to page on *fast* error-budget consumption for enterprise SLOs (e.g., /v1/chat/completions, embeddings, rerank) without generating paging noise during expected best-effort shedding.

Motivation:
- Prior incident and game-day findings showed we need early, reliable paging on *enterprise* SLO risk rather than generic fleet-wide latency/5xx signals.
- With tier-aware throttling/admission control rolling out, we expect 429s on best-effort; burn alerts should focus on enterprise SLI outcomes.

Links:
- Linear: ENG-4926 (Dashboards/alerts for protected routes), PM-882 (Enterprise SLO policy)
- Related PRs (for context): redwood/pr-27441 (429 reason codes), observability-pack/pr-1832 (dashboards)

## What this changes
### 1) New alert presets: enterprise protected routes
Adds new SLO alert rule templates for enterprise route SLOs using multi-window, multi-burn-rate (MWMB) patterns.

Implemented presets:
- `enterprise_protected_route_availability_burn` (availability SLOs)
- `enterprise_protected_route_latency_burn` (latency SLOs)

Windows/burn multipliers (defaults; can be overridden per SLO):
- Page (critical): 5m @ 14x AND 1h @ 14x (fast burn), plus 30m @ 6x AND 6h @ 6x (sustained burn)
- Ticket (warning): 2h @ 3x AND 1d @ 3x

Rationale for numbers:
- Mirrors common SRE MWMB guidance while being tuned for Redwood’s “protected routes” where a small amount of budget burn is meaningful.
- Avoids paging on short spikes that do not materially threaten monthly budget.

### 2) Labeling + routing guidance to keep cardinality bounded
Adds explicit guidance and guardrails in rule generation:
- Requires `route_group` rather than raw `path` labels for alert grouping.
- Allows `model_family` only where it’s a small bounded set; discourages `tenant_id`/`api_key` labels.

### 3) Per-route overrides without copy/paste
Introduces a small override mechanism:
- Defaults live in one place (enterprise protected route presets)
- Individual SLO definitions may override thresholds/windows via `alerting.overrides.*` fields in the SLO spec

### 4) Documentation updates
Adds a short doc page describing:
- When to use enterprise protected route burn alerts
- Recommended paging policy and ownership (SRE vs Platform on-call)
- Example config for chat/embeddings/rerank

## Example
Added an example SLO snippet:
- `route_group: chat_completions`
- `tier: enterprise`
- Applies the new burn presets and routes to `pagerduty_service: hosted-api-enterprise`

## Testing
- Unit tests for rule rendering (ensures correct PromQL shape, annotation fields, and routing labels)
- Golden tests updated for newly generated alert rules
- Lint (yaml/json schema) + CI pass

## Rollout / operational notes
- This PR does not enable alerts by itself; it updates toolkit templates consumed by the Observability Pack.
- Rollout should be coordinated with observability-pack/pr-1832 and the hosted API SLO definitions doc so we don’t page on incomplete SLI wiring.

## Checklist
- [x] Added presets + unit tests
- [x] Added docs and example SLO definition
- [x] Ensured label guidance avoids high-cardinality tags
- [x] Confirmed alert naming aligns with observability standards

---
## Changes (high-level)
- Add new enterprise protected-route burn-rate presets (availability + latency)
- Add override mechanism for windows/thresholds
- Add docs + example
- Update golden test fixtures

## Commits
1) slo-toolkit: add enterprise protected route burn presets
2) slo-toolkit: add override plumbing and schema validation
3) slo-toolkit: docs + examples
4) tests: update golden fixtures and add render tests

## Review notes / discussion summary
- Sergio: Requested that the 5m/1h critical windows be gated by a sustained pair to reduce paging on short-lived deploy blips. Implemented MWMB pairs and added runbook link placeholder in annotations.
- Allison: Flagged risk of `path` label cardinality. Updated templates to require `route_group` and added validation that rejects raw `path` for this preset.
- Logan: Asked to ensure we don’t treat 429s as failures for enterprise SLOs unless explicitly configured. Added doc note: enterprise SLI should count successful responses; 429s should be separated via reason codes and not mixed into error budget unless the SLO definition chooses to.
- Rafael: Confirmed thresholds match game-day outcomes; requested annotation fields include route_group/tier to make incident-bot messages readable. Added annotations and standardized labels.

## CI
Checks:
- build: pass
- unit-tests: pass
- golden-tests: pass
- lint/schema: pass

Merge:
- Squash merged into `main` after approvals and green CI.
Sergio Costa (review): The 5m@14x is fine, but can we gate it with a longer window pair to avoid paging on brief deploy blips? Also please include runbook link in annotations if possible.
Aisha Bello (author): Updated to MWMB pairs: (5m,1h) and (30m,6h) for critical; added annotations for `route_group`, `tier`, and `runbook` (left as placeholder string consumed by downstream pack). Pushed commit 9c3f2a1.
Allison Grant (review): Please do not allow raw `path` as a grouping label for this preset. We’ll regret the cardinality. Route group only + bounded model family if needed.
Aisha Bello (author): Agreed. Added validation: enterprise protected-route presets require `route_group`; schema rejects `path` for this preset. Updated docs with label guidance. Pushed commit 2b71d5e.
Logan Wright (review): Make sure 429s don’t accidentally count as SLO failures for enterprise. We expect best-effort shedding; enterprise should be protected, but if enterprise sees 429-overload we’ll track separately.
Aisha Bello (author): Added doc note + example SLI query guidance (exclude 429 by default; track via separate overload metrics). No changes to SLI here since this toolkit only renders alerts from SLO spec, but clarified recommended setup.
Rafael Mendes (review): Looks good. Please ensure naming matches dashboard spec and that annotations include tier/route group for incident-bot readability.
Aisha Bello (author): Done; standardized alert name prefix `EnterpriseProtectedRoute` and added labels/annotations. Ready for re-review.
Sergio Costa (approve): Approved. MWMB approach + label restrictions are what we need.
Allison Grant (approve): Approved after schema validation change.
Rafael Mendes (approve): Approved. Let’s coordinate enablement with observability-pack.

Motivation: On-call responders repeatedly ask for a concise, actionable summary at incident start (what changed, likely blast radius, probable remediation steps). This PR adds an incident-brief generator plus an auto-checklist feature that synthesizes telemetry, recent deploys, and runbook fragments into a 1-3 bullet brief and a prioritized checklist.

What this does (high level):
- Adds a lightweight briefing service that consumes alert metadata, recent traces, and deployment notes to produce a short incident brief and a suggested checklist.
- Integrates with incident-bot to post a brief into the incident channel and attach a checklist that can be ticked off during triage.
- Provides an operator-facing preview UI in the SLO Toolkit console to review and edit the generated brief before posting.

Checklist for reviewers:
- [ ] validate telemetry parsers for alerts and traces
- [ ] confirm no PII leaks in brief generation
- [ ] run the oncall e2e harness locally and in CI
- [ ] sanity check suggestion ordering heuristics

Implementation notes:
- Briefing service is implemented in Go under internal/briefing for low-latency extraction; heavy heuristic scoring runs in a separate worker using Python to reuse existing NLP helpers.
- Uses existing policy tags from alert metadata to prioritize checklist items (e.g., database, auth, network).
- Includes simple rate limiting and backoff to avoid noisy-post loops when alerts flood.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature behind flag (slo.briefing.enabled) on staging for 48h and sampling at 10% on prod.
2) Monitor posting rate, average brief length, and oncall feedback metric (emoji reaction) for two weeks.
3) Increase sampling to 50% then global enable if no regressions.

Testing:
- Unit tests for parser, scoring, and checklist generation included.
- Added e2e scenarios that simulate deploy-caused incidents and noise floods.

Security and compliance:
- Brief generator redacts potential secret patterns and strips long stack traces by default.
- No new IAM surfaces; service runs under existing slo-toolkit service account.

Docs:
- Adds a console doc page with screenshots and config knobs, plus an operations runbook for when the briefing service fails to generate summaries.

Notes:
- This is intentionally conservative: the first iteration focuses on high precision (don't suggest noisy or incorrect checklist items) over recall. Future work will add feedback loops to improve suggestions.

References: Linear ENG-4021, SUP-1123, past postmortem INT-2025-DB-failures.
Marco Liu (2026-02-16): Nice direction. Two asks: (1) can we cap the brief length to 2 sentences by default? (2) please add a privacy test to ensure no lambda ARN or DB creds get exposed.
Asha Patel (2026-02-16): Responded - added length cap config + redaction test. See commit b2c3d4e.
Priya Nair (2026-02-17): Suggestion: make checklist rank stable across reruns (deterministic tie-breaker). Also prefer smaller set of high-confidence items vs long lists.
Asha Patel (2026-02-18): Implemented deterministic tie-breaker by hashing alert id + rule id; limit checklist to top 5. Updated docs.
Samir Gomez (2026-02-19): CI flake in python worker (async queue) caused intermittent failure. Re-ran CI after backoff fix.
Marco Liu (2026-02-20): Approved after reading latest e2e results. Marking as ready to merge.
Priya Nair (2026-02-20): Approved. Small nit in docs but can be follow-up.
Merge Bot (2026-02-21): Auto-squash-merge completed by integration bot.

Motivation: reduce on-call cognitive load and storage costs by sending compact, deterministic bundles of sampled telemetry for long-tail incidents and by compiling short-form runbooks (mini-runbooks) that only include the actionable steps and repro primitives. This PR adds a sampled telemetry bundler that implements configurable reservoir and time-decay sampling rules, a compact binary envelope for efficient transport and storage, and a mini-runbook compiler that extracts and compresses runbook deltas suitable for pager flows. The combined approach enables fast on-call context loads (sub-200ms deserialisation), smaller artifact footprints for postmortems, and fewer noisy notifications. Changes include a new sampling policy DSL, a telemetry bundler library (Go) with CLI, a mini-runbook compiler (Python) that consumes runbook templates and produces a concise execution plan, integration glue for the slo-toolkit agent to attach bundles to alerts, and end-to-end e2e tests. Backwards compatibility: full-size telemetry and full runbooks are still supported; sampling and mini-runbook generation are opt-in via a feature flag per-service. Rollout plan: alpha on internal infra teams for 2 weeks, canary to 10% of customers via SLO config UI, then gradual ramp; metrics to monitor: bundle size, bundle generation latency, deserialization time on mobile/web clients, oncall resolution time, and false-negative rate for missing context. Security: bundles are signed with the existing KMS adapter; no PII is added by default and redaction rules are applied during bundling. See linked linear items for UX and rollout details.
Diego Rivera: Can we ensure deterministic sampling across restarts? Please add seed derivation tied to alert_id and service_id.
Aisha Menon: Added deterministic-seed logic derived from alert_id/service_id/epoch and included a unit test. Also documented edge cases where alerts are re-issued.
Lena Hofstad: Concerned about bundle size growth when many spans are attached; suggest a hard cap and tombstone marker for omitted traces.
Aisha Menon: Implemented configurable hard cap (default 512KB) and a tombstone marker field. Also added metrics for clipped_count.
Rahul Kapoor: Add lint and type checks for the Python compiler and validate roundtrip of mini-runbook -> full runbook replay in the harness.
Aisha Menon: Added mypy/ruff and a replay validation test that runs the generated mini-runbook in the sandboxed runner. All CI checks green after fixes.

payload.body:
Motivation: We need a single canonical evaluator for Dedicated throughput compliance that (a) computes SLI over sliding windows, (b) applies the Dedicated-specific exclusions consistently, and (c) exports a small, stable summary that the dashboard + incident tooling can consume. Today we have ad-hoc queries in Grafana and a one-off notebook used during SLO metric exploration; they disagree on windowing and don’t encode exclusions (throttling/backpressure) consistently.

What this PR does: Adds a new evaluator implementation `DedicatedThroughputEvaluator` that computes per-deployment throughput SLI and SLO compliance over sliding windows and exports summaries to the toolkit’s standard outputs (Prometheus gauge + JSON summary artifact + optional BigQuery row format). The evaluator consumes the canonical per-deployment throughput time series emitted by the serving stack (deployment_id/model/region labels) and produces: (1) `slo:dedicated_throughput:compliance` (0/1) by deployment_id + tier, (2) `slo:dedicated_throughput:budget_remaining` in [0,1], (3) `slo:dedicated_throughput:window_achieved_tps` and `:window_floor_tps` for debugging, and (4) a compact summary payload used by the burn-rate alert generator.

SLO semantics (encoded here): SLI = achieved_tokens_per_second / committed_floor_tokens_per_second, evaluated over a 30-minute rolling window with 1-minute step. Achieved TPS is computed from `tokens_streamed_total` and `request_latency_seconds_count/sum` only for eligible requests. Exclusions applied: requests rejected due to customer-configured concurrency/quotas (e.g., 429 with `reason=customer_throttle`) are excluded from both numerator and denominator; requests routed to an explicitly unsupported model/version (per catalog metadata) are excluded and surfaced as `eligibility=unsupported_model` in diagnostics; the first 10 minutes after a deployment transitions to READY are excluded (warmup), tracked as `eligibility=warmup_grace`. Server-side admission control rejections (e.g., `reason=redwood_overload_shed`) are NOT excluded (these should count as SLO impact). Window alignment is left-closed/right-open and uses server timestamps to avoid client clock skew.

Exports: Adds `--export-format prometheus,json,bq` to `slo-toolkit evaluate` and a new default JSON artifact `dedicated_throughput_slo_summary.json` containing per-deployment status, budget remaining, primary failure reason (if any), and the top 3 diagnostic dimensions (model, region, rejection reason) for the window.

Tests: Adds unit tests for windowing math (step alignment, gaps), warmup exclusion, customer throttling exclusion, and regression coverage for streaming token accounting (ensures we use the post-fix counter semantics; see note below). Adds a small golden test for JSON summary stability to protect the dashboard consumer.

Notes / dependencies: This evaluator assumes streaming token accounting is not double-counted. If you’re running it against pre-fix metrics you may see inflated achieved TPS. The serving-stack fix is tracked separately; evaluator includes a guardrail metric `slo:dedicated_throughput:token_counter_suspect` when it detects impossible TPS given shape caps.

Rollout: Ship behind `SLO_EVAL_DEDICATED_THROUGHPUT=1` in the toolkit runner. Initial consumers will be the Dedicated SLO dashboard and the burn-rate alert generator (PR #329).
Sean Gallagher (review): Can you clarify why customer throttling is excluded but Redwood admission control is not? Also, do we treat warm pool as the same as READY transition?

Aisha Bello (author): Yes—this matches the SLO doc semantics: customer-side throttling (their configured limit) should not count against Redwood’s ability to serve. Redwood admission control is explicitly intended to protect floors and is considered a Redwood-side miss if it sheds when the customer is within their committed floor. On warm pool: we key off deployment state transition to READY in control plane events; warm pool time before READY is not counted because we only start evaluation once READY is true.

Rafael Mendes (review): Windowing alignment looks right, but the step size being 60s means we can miss short sharp dips. Is that acceptable for the burn-rate alerts?

Aisha Bello (author): Burn-rate is computed over the same rolling windows; with 1m step we still capture dips that persist for more than one step. The intent is to avoid overreacting to single-sample noise. The raw achieved TPS metric is still available at higher resolution for incident triage.

Allison Grant (review): Please keep exported summary stable. Can we add a golden test and document schema fields so dashboards don’t break?

Aisha Bello (author): Added `tests/golden/dedicated_throughput_slo_summary.json` and documented the schema in `docs/evaluators/dedicated_throughput.md#summary-schema`.

Sergio Costa (review): For dashboard drilldowns we need model and region in the summary. Also can you include a `primary_failure_reason` so we can group panels?

Aisha Bello (author): Done. Summary now includes `dimensions` list (model, region, reject_reason) and `primary_failure_reason` enum (below_floor, warmup_grace, unsupported_model, insufficient_data).

Sean Gallagher (follow-up): The guardrail `token_counter_suspect` heuristic—what’s the cap reference?

Aisha Bello (author): Uses shape-level caps from config (conservative) keyed by `shape_class` label when present; otherwise falls back to a default max derived from historical H100/L40S envelopes. This is only a diagnostic signal and does not change compliance.

Resolution: Approved after adding summary schema docs + golden test and renaming `exclude_customer_throttle` -> `exclude_customer_config_throttle` for clarity.
payload.title: Add throughput SLO evaluator for Dedicated (sliding window + summary export)

Motivation: Intermittent client disconnects (mobile, flaky networks) were leaving server-side streaming sessions in a 'limbo' state for the full session TTL. That increased memory/KV-cache pressure and made reconnection semantics brittle when clients tried to resume. This PR introduces an explicit abandon-detection path plus a resume-token reconciliation step in the OpenAI compatibility layer to make reconnects robust and resource-efficient. Overview of changes: 1) server-side abandon detector: heuristics to mark sessions as abandoned after N consecutive failed keepalive windows (configurable), with a fast-path reclamation for short-lived 'ghost' sessions; 2) resume-token reconciliation: when a client reconnects with a resume token, we now validate continuity (prefix match of last committed token sequence), fall back to synthetic soft-cancel if mismatch, and accept partial resumes when the token window is older than retention but alignment is possible; 3) metrics/observability: added abandon_count, resume_reconcile_hits/misses, and a debug trace emitted on mismatch for postmortem; 4) API & docs: small extension to the OpenAI-compat streaming handshake to expose a Resume-Accepted header and doc updates describing the semantics and recommended client retry behavior. This PR intentionally avoids changing token formats or client protocol fields except for the optional header (backwards compatible). Testing notes: unit tests cover heuristic edge cases, an integration test simulates flapping clients and validates cache reclamation, and e2e tests verify resume acceptance scenarios. Related issues: linear ENG-5421.
--- a/services/streaming/session_manager.go
+++ b/services/streaming/session_manager.go
@@ -180,6 +180,22 @@ func (sm *SessionManager) StartKeepaliveLoop() {
+    // detect consecutive keepalive failures and mark session abandoned
+    if sm.abandonDetector.IsAbandoned(session.ID) {
+        sm.reclaim(session.ID)
+        metrics.Inc("stream.abandon_count")
+        continue
+    }
 }
--- a/api/openai_compat/streaming_handler.go
+++ b/api/openai_compat/streaming_handler.go
@@ -78,6 +78,14 @@ func HandleStream(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+    // reconcile resume token if present
+    if token := r.Header.Get("X-Resume-Token"); token != "" {
+        ok, reason := reconcileResumeToken(token, session)
+        if !ok {
+            log.Debugf("resume reconcile failed: %s", reason)
+            // soft-cancel path to allow client graceful fallback
+            session.SoftCancel()
+        } else {
+            w.Header().Set("Resume-Accepted", "true")
+        }
+    }
 }
--- a/docs/openai-compat/stream-resume.md
+++ b/docs/openai-compat/stream-resume.md
@@ -1,3 +1,12 @@
+Resume semantics: Clients may present a resume token after reconnecting. Servers will attempt a prefix match against the last committed token sequence. On mismatch, the server will perform a synthetic soft-cancel and surface Resume-Accepted=false. Clients should re-issue the request from the last confirmed token or start a fresh session.
+Configuration: runtime.abandon.window=3 (default)
+Metrics: stream.resume_reconcile_hits/misses, stream.abandon_count
+Best practices: exponential backoff + jitter on reconnects.
Ethan Bloom: The abandon detector heuristics look good, but can we make the default window shorter for mobile-heavy tenants? Suggested to make default 2 windows instead of 3.
Maya Ortiz: I pushed a config flag and added a note in docs. Default remains 3 to be conservative, but tenant override is now available via runtime config.
Sofia Li: The resume-token reconciliation is clever. Two nit requests: 1) add an explicit debug log when we fall back to synthetic soft-cancel, 2) add a unit test for token prefix mismatch with same suffix length.
Maya Ortiz: Added the debug log and the additional unit. Also added a metric for reconciliation misses.
Arjun Patel: Integration test flake observed locally; CI shows a transient failure in TestFlap_Graceful then passed on rerun. Approving after CI green.
Ethan Bloom: Approving. Please squash merge and include a short release note about the header (Resume-Accepted) and config knobs.
Maya Ortiz: Addressed review comments and rebased on main to pick up the recent lint rule change. Ready to merge.
payload.title: streaming: add abandon-detection and resume-token reconciliation for client disconnects (openai-compat)

Motivation: on-call teams need a lightweight way to validate that playbooks and escalation policies behave under realistic multi-service cascades without standing up heavy simulation infra. This PR introduces two complementary tools: (1) an escalation scenario simulator (CLI + scheduler) that can synthesize alert cascades, inject controlled flakiness, and exercise escalation paths; and (2) a compact sanity annotator that produces one-page annotated reports intended for pager handoffs and quick triage. The simulator supports pluggable probes, probabilistic failure models, and integrates with incident-bot to post simulated cards into test channels. The annotator collates traces/metrics/log snippets and applies heuristics to highlight likely root-cause signals and confidence scores so responders get a prioritized short checklist. What changed: new CLI under src/cli/escalation_sim, scheduler job manifests under infra/schedules, a small web-adapter for incident-bot integration under integrations/incident-bot-adapter, the annotator library under src/annotator with a compact JSON report format and human-readable rendering, docs updated with usage examples and a safety section, and unit+integration tests. Safety and rollout: all simulated runs default to a sandbox channel and a dry-run mode; incident-bot adapter requires an explicit test-token and a config flag to allow posting. The rollout plan is staged: enable nightly smoke runs for a small set of synthetic scenarios, validate with oncall rotation for two weeks, then expose the scenario authoring UI to SREs. Follow-ups: expand probe library, add RBAC for scenario execution, and wire results into the console metrics dashboard. Related: ENG-4921 for simulator design and SRE-88 for handoff UX improvements.

Adds a lightweight RAG authoring sandbox that replays stepwise sessions, captures streamed telemetry probes, and includes a devcontainer for local onboarding. Recommended for teams building iterated retrieval/agent workflows.
Motivation: Authoring RAG workflows interactively is hard to debug when steps are non-deterministic or tools return partial/streamed outputs. This quickstart provides a small, local-first sandbox that can record and replay stepwise RAG sessions, attach streamed probes (telemetry events, intermediate embeddings, tool call traces), and surface them in a compact trace viewer. The goal is to help prompt/contract authors iterate on step boundaries, tool contracts, and retrieval strategies without running full end-to-end infra.

What this PR does (single-string description): Adds a new quickstart under quickstarts/step-replayer that contains: a README with step-by-step authoring guidance, a devcontainer for one-click onboarding, a minimal local replayer binary (node script) that can ingest recorded sessions and replay them with configurable time dilation, a probes YAML schema plus sample probes emitter, a small set of example prompt/step fixtures, and an instrumentation shim that emits compact telemetry to stdout or to an optional local HTTP sink. Also updates docs/quickstarts/index.yml to surface the new quickstart in the docs site navigation.

Why now: Several internal experiments (ENG-4832) surfaced the need for deterministic replay when evaluating prompt variants across retrieval configurations. This quickstart encapsulates those patterns and makes it easier to add step-level assertions for regressions.

Checklist (author):
- [x] Quickstart scaffolding and README with walkthrough and expected outcomes
- [x] Devcontainer and small Dockerfile for reproducible local runs
- [x] Telemetry probes schema and emitter examples
- [x] Step replayer script and replay fixtures
- [x] Docs index entry and short landing copy
- [x] Basic smoke tests in CI (local run path)

Usage notes: The replayer supports two modes: record (wraps a live session and emits a compact JSONL trace) and replay (replays a trace and optionally emits the same stream of probes to a test harness). The README documents how to wire the emitter to a local HTTP probe-sink and how to assert on intermediate embeddings or tool-call payloads. There is also a sample 'contract-checks.json' that demonstrates how to fail a replay run if certain tool call outputs deviate.

Security/Privacy: The quickstart defaults to local-only storage and provides guidance in README for sanitizing PII before recording. There are no remote telemetry endpoints enabled by default.

Backward compatibility: The replayer uses a compact trace schema with an explicit version key (trace_schema_v: "1.0"). Future schema changes will be opt-in.

Related work: Builds on patterns from recent authoring labs and tool-contract proposals. References: ENG-4832, PM-221.

CI/Testing instructions: CI includes a lightweight smoke job that spins up the devcontainer, runs the replayer against a recorded fixture in replay mode and verifies a set of assertion hooks. E2E is intentionally excluded from main CI to keep runtime small.

Merge notes: Squash-merged after approvals and a successful CI run.
Liam Chen (2024-11-10): Nice, this solves a real pain. Two asks: 1) Can the replayer optionally stub out external network calls so CI runs remain hermetic? 2) Add an explicit example of asserting on embeddings.
Maya Thompson (2024-11-10): Addressed. Added a --stub-network flag to the replayer and included 'contract-checks.json' showing embedding assertions. Updated README with examples.
Priya Patel (2024-11-12): Please add a short section documenting PII sanitization before recording — we don't want accidental secrets in traces.
Maya Thompson (2024-11-12): Added a 'sanitize.sh' helper and a short subsection in the README with guidance. The helper is intentionally opinionated and must be run manually before recording.
Anders Holm (2024-11-13): CI smoke failed on first run due to missing permissions in the devcontainer's package install step. Suggest pinning node image and moving 'npm ci' earlier. Also requested a small test to validate the probes schema.

Maya Thompson (2024-11-13): Fixed devcontainer to use 'mcr.microsoft.com/vscode/devcontainers/javascript-node:0-18' and added a probes-schema-smoke test that validates sample-emitter output against schema. Re-ran CI.
Liam Chen (2024-11-14): Approved after checking the replay output locally and verifying contract assertion example.

Maintainer note (release engineer): Merged via squash on main with quickstart tag + docs landing update.
1) Open repo in the provided devcontainer. 2) Run npm ci in quickstarts/step-replayer. 3) Start sample emitter: node probes/sample-emitter.js --sink stdout. 4) Run replayer in replay mode: node replayer/index.js --replay fixtures/sample-trace.jsonl --assert contract-checks.json --stub-network. 5) Observe probes printed to stdout or forwarded to local HTTP sink. 6) See README for advanced assertions and CI integration.

Motivation: on-call responders routinely surface the same investigative steps for a set of noisy but high-impact signals. This PR introduces two coordinated features: (1) a 'Sleuth Playbook' generator that emits graded runbooks based on a compact telemetry diff, and (2) a 'Telemetry Needle Detector' - a lightweight heuristic that surfaces unusual signal combinations (needles) which can drive playbook selection. The goal is to reduce cognitive load and time-to-action for first responders while preserving human-in-the-loop safety for mitigation steps.

Scope and user-facing behavior: the Sleuth Playbook is presented as a 3-tier action card (Inspect, Mitigate, Escalate) with suggested query snippets, required checks, and an estimated confidence score. The Needle Detector runs as a post-alert hook (configurable per-service) and annotates alerts with 'needle' tags and a short rationale. Playbook generation prioritizes non-destructive guidance; automatic mitigations are gated behind a staged 'canary execute' flow which requires both an explicit operator approval and two positive health checks.

Implementation highlights: a new micro-package incident-bot/sleuth/ contains the core heuristics, a compact fuzzy-diff algorithm for telemetry rollups, and a deterministic playbook templating engine. The detector runs in-process with the alert enrichment pipeline but offloads scoring to a bounded worker pool to protect alert throughput. A new runbook executor in slo-toolkit/runner adds a dry-run mode and a graded-execute API that opens a 30-minute operator window for canary runs. We also extended the Slack/Console cards to show the confidence band, needle provenance, and one-click dry-run.

Checklist:
- [x] Sleuth heuristics and templating engine with unit tests
- [x] Needle detector integration and sampling to avoid alert amplification
- [x] Dry-run and graded execution APIs with audit logs
- [x] UI card updates (Slack + Console) and telemetry for explainability
- [x] Safety gates (approval flow, health-check hooks) and policy config
- [x] End-to-end smoke tests and e2e harness updates

Backwards compatibility: the needle tag is an optional annotation and does not change existing alert routing. Playbook suggestions are additive and default to 'suggest-only' mode for the first 30 days in beta.

Operational notes: default sampling is 5% of alerts for needle detection on production; teams can opt-in to higher rates via project config. The worker pool uses a token bucket to avoid contention with high-throughput services. Rolling back: feature flags are behind feature/sleuth-playbook and can be disabled from the console or via the feature flags api.

Related tickets: ENG-2198 (playbook generator), ENG-2201 (runbook executor), SUP-4412 (customer request: faster triage for replication loop incidents).
Omar Singh: This looks promising. Before we can allow graded-exec at scale we need a hard guardrail preventing auto-exec on services with external side-effects (billing, customer emails). Can you add a policy check?
Author (Marina Kozlov): Added a policy layer in graded_executor that checks service tags against an allowlist. Updated docs to show opt-in steps. See new tests in test_graded_executor_policy.py
Leah Thompson: E2E flake on the canary health-check timing observed in CI. Suggest increasing the test harness tolerance instead of changing prod timeouts.
Author: Increased harness tolerance and added a jitter cap; left prod health-check timeouts unchanged.
Diego Alvarez: Approve after minor nits (doc wording).
SRE WG (comment): Please monitor the needle-tag prevalence metric in the first week; default sampling is low but we want early telemetry.
Adds Sleuth Playbook generation and a Telemetry Needle Detector that suggests graded runbooks and dry-run mitigations. Default suggest-only mode; auto-exec gated by policy and operator approval. Configurable sampling; see docs/oncall/sleuth_playbooks.md for rollout steps and opt-in instructions.
payload.title: Automated sleuth playbook and telemetry needle detector

Context: On-call teams maintain many playbooks; some are expensive to execute (multiple API calls, large artifact fetches, or cross-service writes). We need tooling to estimate the operational cost of running a playbook and to guard automatic or semi-automatic runners from executing high-cost operations without explicit approval. This PR introduces a playbook execution cost scorer (heuristic + lightweight model) and a configurable safety-gates layer that prevents automatic remediation or scheduled runs when estimated cost or blast radius exceeds team thresholds.

What this PR does (high level): Adds a cost scoring pipeline that inspects playbook steps and produces a cost_estimate (tokens: estimate of API/compute units, external_io: bytes, blast_score: heuristic for domain impact). Integrates the score into the playbook preview UI/CLI and the runbook-executor path. Adds safety gate checks with three enforcement modes: warn, require-ack, block. Adds telemetry (playbook.cost_estimate.histogram, playbook.safety_gate.blocked_count) and a small data-driven configuration for cost weightings stored in internal/cost_model.json. Ships docs and a CLI preview flag (--preview-cost) so oncall can get an approximate cost before running.

Motivation: Reduce surprise operational spend, avoid automated remediation that causes large downstream effects, and give SREs a lightweight signal to prioritize lightweight vs heavy playbooks. This is intended to be conservative (overestimate rather than undercount) and extensible to more accurate models later.

Checklist:
- [x] cost scorer core implementation (pkg/playbook/scorer.go)
- [x] safety gate enforcement and modes (pkg/playbook/safety_gates.go)
- [x] CLI preview and UI integration (cmd/ptool, docs)
- [x] unit + integration tests (tests/playbook/*)
- [x] telemetry + dashboard notes (docs/observability.md)
- [x] defaults and config schema (internal/cost_model.json, charts values)
- [x] migration note for teams that rely on automatic-approved runs

Backward compatibility: New fields are additive (playbook metadata now includes cost_estimate). Default enforcement mode is "warn" so behavior is opt-in. No breaking changes expected for existing playbooks.

Risk & mitigations: The scorer is intentionally conservative; misestimates could be noisy. We ship with a metrics dashboard to monitor false positives and tune internal/cost_model.json. Safety gate config default prevents accidental blocking.

Related: ENG-1289 (playbook hygiene), SRE-342 (remediation safety posture).
Liam O'Connor: Nice incremental approach. Please add a short comment on why the default weights overestimate (we should be explicit). Also add unit tests for a playbook with mixed IO + compute steps.
Author (Asha Patel): Added tests for blended playbooks and documented conservative defaults in internal/cost_model.json (see commit d12ef7b).
Priya Rao: For safety_gates, ensure configuration can be overridden per-team via the helm values file. Can we also expose an opt-out annotation on playbooks?
Author: Added support for playbook.annotations['slo-toolkit/safety-gate'] = 'off' and document it. Helm values updated to allow per-namespace defaults.
Mateo Silva: CI flaked on the integration test once (network timeout). Re-ran and everything passed. Suggest we add a short note about expected variance in metrics for the first week after rollout.
Liam O'Connor (approve): Tests look solid and UX is reasonable. Approving with a request to monitor telemetry for tuning in the first release window.
Adds a conservative playbook execution cost estimator and configurable safety-gates to prevent automatic or scheduled playbook runs above team-defined cost/blast thresholds. Includes CLI preview (--preview-cost), telemetry, docs, and a migration note. Default enforcement mode is 'warn'.
Follow-up work planned: (1) add a lighter-weight approximate model for offline scoring of hundreds of archived playbooks (ENG-1350), (2) add a per-team dashboard to tune cost weights, (3) prototype ML-based cost estimator using historical run data.
payload.title: Playbook execution cost scorer and safety gates

Add a deterministic runbook regression harness and annotator for validating playbook steps against representative traces; integrates into CI as a gated job. No user-facing breaking changes.
Title: Causal runbook regression tester and auto-annotator

Summary: This PR introduces a lightweight, deterministic regression testing harness for runbooks (slo-toolkit/regression) that replays representative telemetry traces, applies controlled causal perturbations, and verifies that runbook remediation steps map to the expected state transitions. It also adds an auto-annotator that enriches runbook steps with confidence scores, likely subsystem tags, and remediation heuristics derived from past incident traces. Goal is to detect regressions in runbook effectiveness and reduce manual review overhead when playbooks are updated.

Why: We've observed subtle regressions where runbook edits (text or commands) stop being effective against live-like telemetry patterns. Manual testing is slow and brittle. A reproducible harness that can be run locally and in CI will catch regressions early and produce actionable annotations to help authors improve steps.

What changed (high level): - New regression harness package: slo_toolkit/regression/causal_runner.py (deterministic replay engine, seeding, perturbation API) - A set of canonical trace fixtures in examples/trace-fixtures/ (kafka-lag, db-conn-spike, cache-thrash) - Auto-annotator module: slo_toolkit/annotations/auto_annotator.py (step scoring, subsystem classification, remediation hints) - CLI entrypoint: bin/slo-regtest (local run, matrix options, --seed, --replay-window) - CI: .github/workflows/runbook-regression.yml added (matrix over traces + python versions) - Docs: docs/runbooks/regression-testing.md (how to write testable runbook steps, acceptance criteria) - Tests: tests/regression/* (unit tests for runner, end-to-end smoke test)

Checklist: - [x] Add deterministic replay engine with seed control - [x] Provide representative trace fixtures and tooling to pare traces to shorter windows - [x] Integrate harness into CI as gated job (non-blocking for now, will gate next quarter) - [x] Unit and e2e tests for core functionality - [x] Documentation for authors and SREs

Commits (summary): - Initial harness scaffold and data model for trace fragments - Implement deterministic causal replayer with perturbation hooks - Add fixture traces and canonical examples - Implement auto-annotator and confidence heuristics - Add CLI and CI workflow - Address review comments: deterministic seeding, sampling size control, improved logging

Files changed (high level list): - slo_toolkit/regression/causal_runner.py - slo_toolkit/regression/runner_cli.py - slo_toolkit/annotations/auto_annotator.py - examples/trace-fixtures/kafka_lag.json, db_conn_spike.json, cache_thrash.json - tests/regression/test_runner.py, test_annotator.py - docs/runbooks/regression-testing.md - .github/workflows/runbook-regression.yml - bin/slo-regtest (executable)

Small illustrative snippets included in the diff: - deterministic seed usage: runner = CausalRunner(seed=seed, perturbations=perturbations) - annotator output example (CSV/JSON): [{"step_id":"restart-cache","confidence":0.82,"subsystem":"cache","remediation_hint":"increase-ttl-or-restart"}]

Review thread (high level): - Daniel Park (review): "Nicely scoped. Two concerns: 1) sampling may hide flaky failures — we should add a 'stress' mode that increases perturbation intensity; 2) logs need correlation ids so CI artifacts map back to traces." - Aisha (author): "Added --stress and --seed params and included correlation id header in runner logs. Also added sample_size control to CLI and documented mapping to CI artifacts." - Sofia Martinez (review): "Annotator heuristics look useful, but can we avoid leaking internal service names? Suggest mapping to public-facing subsystem tags and adding a redact option." - Aisha: "Added mapping layer and --redact option; updated docs to show anonymized outputs for public artifacts." - Liam O'Connor (approval): "Nothing blocking from SRE side; CI passed locally for matrix runs."

CI summary: - New workflow runbook-regression.yml executes matrix: traces=[kafka_lag,db_conn_spike,cache_thrash], python=[3.10,3.11] - Steps: install deps, run unit tests, run e2e smoke using --seed=42, upload artifacts (replay logs, annotator-json) - Initial CI run failed (timeout on long DB fixture), author trimmed replay window and added --max-duration flag - Final CI run: all checks pass; artifacts uploaded to PR (replay-logs.zip, annotator-results.json)

Backward compatibility and safety: - No changes to runtime behavior of on-call tooling; all new modules are opt-in via CLI and CI job - Annotator outputs include redact option and default to anonymized subsystem tags in CI uploads to avoid leaking internal mappings

Next steps (follow-ups tracked in Linear): - Gate the CI job in next milestone once we have 50+ runbook fixtures and a maintenance policy (ENG-2041) - Add a dashboard in Console to surface annotator confidence trends per runbook - Expand fixture corpus with customer-derived traces and privacy-preserving sampling

Merge: Squash merged to main after approvals and successful CI run.

Add a lightweight telemetry-guided sanity checker and a pretriage CLI hook to reduce oncall noise; opt-in by default for slo-toolkit deployments; includes docs and telemetry metrics for tuning.
Motivation: on-call teams spend time investigating noisy alerts that are detectable as instrumentation anomalies (missing series, stale exporters, or thin traffic windows) before starting a full incident triage. This PR adds a lightweight 'pretriage sanity checker' that runs a small set of telemetry probes when an alert is received and surfaces a short human-readable verdict and artifacts to the responder. Design summary: implement a probe runner (timeout-first, non-blocking) that evaluates a configurable probe set against Prometheus and tracing backends, computes a compact fingerprint, and emits a JSON snapshot + human summary. Ship a CLI hook and a webhook payload for incident-bot/slo-toolkit to call as part of pretriage. Safety and opt-in: default checks are safe read-only Prometheus queries and a trace existence probe; probes and timeouts are configurable per-team via runtime config. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout to 10% of responses for two weeks, converge on rule tweaks, then enable org-wide. Checklist: 1) implement probe runner and schema; 2) add incident-bot hook + webhook contract; 3) surface results in oncall brief (summary line + artifact link); 4) add docs and runbook snippets; 5) add metrics and dashboard for false-positive rate. Testing: unit tests for probe parsing and mock Prom queries; integration test that exercises the webhook path using a local Prometheus test server; end-to-end smoke in canary environment. Related work: builds on prior compact-snapshot work and the 'telemetry-sanity-prober' spike (ENG-1982) and coordinates with incident-bot runbook suggestions. Backwards compatibility: webhook payloads are additive; incident-bot falls back if pretriage fails or times out. Motivation: handoffs are a frequent source of incident friction when telemetry context is lost or ownership is ambiguous. This PR introduces a lightweight handshake/assertion protocol plus a short-term snapshot persistence layer so the outgoing oncall can assert intent (sticky ownership) and ensure the next responder receives a deterministic snapshot of relevant telemetry. Design: 1) Handoff assertions: a new handoff API that records an assertion object (owner, intent, TTL, safe-rollback hints, topical tags) to the oncall metadata store. Assertions are signed by the oncall's service identity to avoid accidental overrides. 2) Snapshot preserver: capture a compact telemetry bundle (traces, top-5 recent logs, sampled spans, alert deltas, feature flag state) into an immutable, encrypted snapshot referenced by the assertion. Snapshots are small by default (<250KB) with configurable included artifacts. 3) Read-after-handoff semantics: the receiving oncall client reads the assertion and snapshot atomically and gets a suggested checklist and sensitivity mask. 4) Safety: PII redaction and retention policy (default 72 hours) with automatic garbage collection and audit logging. 5) Feature gating and opt-out: organizations can disable persistent snapshots or reduce retention via config. Rollout: feature-gated behind slo-toolkit.handoff_handshake flag, staged rollout to 10% of teams for 2 weeks before org-wide roll. Backwards compatibility: clients that do not understand assertions ignore them; no blocking changes to runbooks. GC) - [x] docs + migration notes - [x] privacy review and retention defaults Commit summary and code touches: see commits. Testing: CI passed after a flaky telemetry-parser test was retried; added integration test that simulates a handoff and verifies snapshot integrity across process restart. Migration notes: existing handoff flow is untouched; when enabled, outgoing oncall will attach an assertion automatically during manual handoffs and during incident archive transitions. payload.body:
Context: Users continue to see rare streaming corruption and malformed function-call framing when using combined constraint backends (CFG + regex) with aggressive tokenizers (BPE/bytepair variants). Root causes we identified: 1) constraints chosen by the muxer sometimes fail mid-subtoken boundary when a cached prefix crosses constraint transitions, 2) sampling fallbacks to lower-priority backends are opaque to the streaming layer and can produce partial token emissions, and 3) the OpenAI-compat tool/function-call framing assumes whole-token boundaries that our tokenizer sometimes splits across bytes.

What this PR does: Adds two coordinated subsystems and supporting fixes: 
- Fallback Prober: a light-weight runtime probe that validates candidate fallback backends before permitting an immediate streaming switch. The probe runs a short deterministic prefix evaluation (<=8 tokens) through the target backend with the current KV cache snapshot to ensure it will not emit token fragments that violate the active framing policy. If the probe fails, the muxer uses the next candidate or raises a controlled degrade-to-synchronous mode.
- Token Stitcher: a tokenizer-aware streaming post-processor that detects subtoken splits at constraint boundaries and stitches byte/subtoken fragments into emission-safe units. This avoids partial tool-call markers and broken JSON fragments when model tokenizers slice across punctuation or escape sequences.
- OpenAI-compat streaming adapter updates: preserve function-call sentinel token grouping by deferring emission until the stitcher confirms boundary integrity; extended compatibility tests for toolcall framing in both UTF-8 multi-byte and mixed-encoding prompts.
- Constraint backend changes: small CFG sampler change to expose deterministic-probe mode, regex backend guard to reject matches that would split an ongoing subtoken prefix.
- Observability: new metrics (constraint.probe.success, constraint.probe.latency_ms, stitcher.rate, stitcher.stitched_tokens) and a Console dashboard tab to inspect probe rejections and stitch operations in-flight.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc in PR thread and docs/constraints/architecture.md updated
- [x] Unit tests for probe and stitcher modules
- [x] Integration e2e test with streaming + toolcall in CI (flaky cases reproduced locally)
- [x] Benchmarked perf impact: median token latency +0.8ms, p95 +3.2ms under high batching load; cost-neutral when probe bypasses via short-circuit hits
- [x] Added metrics and console wiring
- [x] Backwards-compatible by default; feature gated behind runtime flags (constraint.probe.enabled=true, stitcher.enabled=true)

Testing: 
Single-node unit tests for edge tokenizers (tests/unit/token_stitcher_test.py) cover multi-byte UTF-8, zero-width joiners, and bytepair split cases. Integration tests (tests/integration/constraint_backends_test.py) exercise fallback paths between CFG -> regex -> null-backend with streaming on/off. Ran the system against our internal benchmark lab and reproduced the original corruption case on a small prompt set (attached example in discussion). CI includes a new e2e streaming job (ci/e2e/streaming-constraint) that was green on the final run.

Rollout plan: feature gated with flags. Start with dedicated/alpha customers with sampling telemetry enabled, monitor constraint.probe.success and stitcher.rate, then flip on for broader clusters after 2 weeks of stable metrics. Emergency rollback: set runtime flag constraint.probe.enabled=false OR stitcher.enabled=false to revert behavior without redeploying runtime.

Related: ENG-1123 (design), ENG-2100 (observability), SUP-4217 (customer-reported corruption incident).

Notes: This is intentionally conservative: the probe avoids invoking heavyweight decoding and uses a deterministic low-branch sampling mode to keep latency bounded. The stitcher is written defensively to avoid altering legitimate token sequences; it only coalesces fragments when it detects a violation of framing invariants (e.g., unclosed JSON braces inside a function-call envelope).

Change summary (high level): updated constraint muxer and backends, added runtime probe and stitcher modules, wired console metrics and dashboard, added unit/integration/e2e tests, small docs update.
Ava: Can the probe ever slow tail latency for p50? How do we ensure it doesn't add extra decoding in the fast path?
Author (Marcos): Probe runs deterministically up to 8 tokens and short-circuits on a successful confidence check. We added a muxer optimization to bypass probing when the candidate backend has an identical tokenizer and KV-shape; added perf numbers in PR description and bench results in benchmarks/streaming/constraint_probe_latency.sql.
Lars: Token stitcher looks good; please add more comments around the heuristic thresholds and a safety clamp to avoid infinite buffer growth.
Author: Added safety clamp and comments; included unit test that simulates long-fragment streams to assert bounded memory usage.
Priya: Are there any corner cases where composing stitcher+probe could mask genuine model regressions? We want to be sure we're not hiding quality drops.
Author: Good point — stitcher only modifies emission when framing invariants are violated; we also added quality-metric alerts (console) for stitcher activity spikes so we can surface regressions.
Ava: Approved after verifying CI e2e job passed and perf impact is acceptable.
Lars: Approved.
Merging: Ethan Zhao performed squash-merge after approvals and green CI.
- Added runtime fallback prober to validate backend switches for constrained decoding (opt-in via flags).
- Added tokenizer-aware Token Stitcher to prevent partial-token emissions across constraint boundaries, reducing streaming corruption for tool/function calls.
- New metrics and console dashboard for probe/stitcher activity.
- Backwards compatible and disabled by default; enable via runtime flags for gradual rollout.
Feature gated. To disable quickly: set constraint.probe.enabled=false and stitcher.enabled=false in runtime flags; monitor constraint.probe.success and stitcher.rate metrics after toggling. If customers report toolcall corruptions after enabling, roll back flags immediately and capture traces using scripts/trace_examples/reproduce_corruption.sh
No secret/material change. Probe runs deterministic short decodes on existing KV snapshots; does not introduce new network calls. Token stitcher observes emitted bytes but does not alter request payloads; instrumentation added to metrics is aggregated and does not include PII.
