Adds a compact on-call minimap widget and an opt-in conditional telemetry sampler to reduce noise and speed handoffs. No breaking changes.
Summary: Adds a compact on-call 'minimap' UI component for quick situational awareness during handoffs, and a conditional telemetry sampler that selectively captures higher-fidelity traces/metrics when the on-call context suggests meaningful deviation. Both pieces are opt-in and designed to reduce cognitive load and storage costs for long-running rotation transfers.

Motivation: During handoffs we repeatedly see pages where responders have to hunt through long alert lists and dense traces. The minimap surfaces a condensed timeline of recent alert clusters, top affected services, and outstanding runbook tasks. The conditional sampler aims to cut noise by only elevating telemetry sampling for sessions that show anomalous signal (error spikes, latency drift, or failing healthchecks) or when the minimap is actively inspected by a responder. This reduces the volume of full-fidelity traces and helps SREs focus on actionable incidents.

Design: - On-call minimap: a compact horizontal timeline widget rendered in the oncall hub (slo-toolkit UI). Shows last 6 hours by default, clustered events, colored by alert priority and service. Click-to-expand opens a contextual query view paired with a preloaded runbook snippet. Persisted per-rotation with ephemeral links for sharing. Implemented as a small React component (minimap/) with corresponding API endpoints to synthesize cluster metadata.
- Conditional telemetry sampler: server-side sampler implemented in the telemetry-proxy module. Default mode is conservative (sample 2% of traces). When the minimap is opened or when an anomaly detector flags a cluster, sampler temporarily activates higher sampling (up to 40%) for the matching service/trace families for a sliding 10-minute window. Sampling rules are stored as short-lived tokens in Redis and are automatically revoked. The sampler accepts white/blacklists per-customer and respects privacy flags (no PII capture).

Implementation notes and tradeoffs: - Sampling decisions are lightweight, evaluated at the ingress of telemetry-proxy; added ~0.4ms median overhead in local perf runs. - Minimap data is aggregated from existing event stores; synthetic cluster keys are computed with a small heuristic: time-window coalescing + service affinity + shared error signature. This is intentionally conservative to avoid false-positive sampling bursts. - Storage: increased short-term ingest (~15% during ramped sampling in e2e tests) but long-term storage decreased because fewer full-fidelity traces are kept for low-signal periods.

Checklist (PR-level): - [x] Minimap UI component and tests (unit + snapshot) - [x] Telemetry sampling logic and integration tests - [x] Redis short-lived tokens for sampling rules - [x] RBAC checks so only oncall roles can promote sampling from the UI - [x] Docs: operational guide and runbook snippets for minimap workflows - [x] Feature flag gating (slo.minimap.enabled, telemetry.conditional_sampler.enabled) - [x] e2e smoke with a synthetic alert storm

Commits (summary): - 3fd4b2b: scaffold minimap React component, styles, and unit tests - b1a9e88: add API endpoint /minimap/summary and clusterer logic - 9c2a0f7: telemetry-proxy: hook sampler hookpoints and token store - 5a7d9c1: add RBAC enforcement + feature flags and toggle checks - 2e4f33b: docs and runbook snippets + migration note for feature flags - 8f1cde4: perf tuning for sampler and added throttling logic

Files changed (high level): - src/minimap/ (React, CSS, tests) - server/minimap_handler.py (summary endpoint + clusterer) - server/telemetry_proxy.py (conditional sampling path) - infra/redis_tokens.py (short-lived token helpers) - docs/oncall/minimap.md (walkthrough + runbook templates) - docs/telemetry/conditional-sampler.md - tests/e2e/minimap_sampler_smoke.test.ts

Review conversation (highlights): - Evan Park (reviewer): "Nice ergonomic improvement. Two asks: 1) make the minimap keyboard accessible, 2) ensure sampling respects customer opt-outs."
  - Author reply: "Added keyboard focus states and aria labels in 3fd4b2b; sampler respects opt-out flags and there's an integration test SUP-8121 that covers this."
- Riley Chen: "Concerned about inadvertent sampling bursts during alert storms; suggest a global token rate limiter."
  - Author reply: "Added token-based throttling with exponential backoff and a global reservoir (8f1cde4). Saw <2% tail increase in stress tests."
- Sofia Martinez: "Docs look good. Can we add a short playbook snippet for handoff checks?"
  - Author reply: "Added a compact handoff checklist to docs/oncall/minimap.md and a copyable runbook seed."

CI and validation: - CI run 1: unit + lint: pass (flake8/tslint warnings fixed) - CI run 2: integration tests (minimap <-> telemetry): pass after adding mock token store - CI run 3: e2e smoke: pass with synthetic alert-storm generator - Perf: internal perf benching shows sampler adds 0.4ms median, p95 +1.6ms; acceptable for SLOs.

Rollout plan: - Behind feature flags by default off. - Canary to internal SRE rotations for 72 hours. - After canary: enable for 10% of accounts for 2 weeks with monitoring (ingest rate, sampled trace volume, feedback). - Full rollout contingent on no regressions in ingest cost and oncall satisfaction survey.

Merge details: Squash-merged by Evan Park after approvals from Riley and Sofia. Post-merge tasks: update internal runbook link in the oncall rotation template (done in follow-up PR), monitor telemetry ingest dashboard for sampling spikes.

Notes / follow-ups: - ENG-3348 to add ML-based cluster detection in a follow-up PR (marked experimental). - SUP-8121: added a customer opt-out test matrix and a remediation workflow for accidental sampling.

This PR focuses on operational ergonomics: faster handoffs, reduced noise, and cost-conscious elevated telemetry only when it meaningfully helps responders.

Motivation: on-call handoffs and first-responder triage often spend several minutes fetching relevant telemetry and assembling playbooks. This PR introduces an "oncall prefetch hub" (hublet) plus a mechanism to produce small, annotated autotriage bundles that can be cached per-service and attached to incidents automatically. The goal is to reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to mitigate (MTTM) by delivering compact, precomputed diagnostic snapshots and ranked playbook steps to responders immediately when an alert fires.

What this change does: adds a lightweight hublet service in slo-toolkit that: (1) continuously seeds telemetry snapshots for high-risk routes using rationalized sampling policies, (2) compiles annotated autotriage bundles (sanitized logs, top traces, relevant kpi deltas, suggested runbook steps with quick commands), and (3) exposes a small API used by incident-bot to attach a bundle to a new incident or to provide a suggested-playbook link in Slack/PagerDuty messages. Bundles are intentionally compact (<= 256KB) and include provenance metadata and an integrity hash.

Design highlights: sampling policies are policy-driven (configurable per-service via YAML), with decay windows to avoid repeated heavy capture during ongoing incidents; sanitization hooks remove PII/keys using existing sanitizers; caching TTLs are conservative (default 5m) and can be overridden by service tier. Attachments are only created for alerts that match selectors to avoid noise. The hublet exposes a CLI (sloctl bundle generate) for on-demand bundle creation and a background worker that runs captures and bundle builds.

Backward compatibility and rollout: incident-bot integration is opt-in via a feature flag `incident_prefetch` in the incident-bot config. Rollout plan: enable for small set of non-sensitive services for 48-hour dogfood, monitor bundle-attached frequency and initial responder feedback, then expand by service. The feature is reversible: disabling the flag stops attachments; bundles remain in cache until TTL expires.

Testing and validation: added unit tests for sampler logic and sanitizers, integration test that simulates an alert -> bundle attach flow, and an end-to-end smoke test that exercises Slack message rendering with bundle link. Load test: lightweight capture path was run at 200 rps against simulated traces (no real customer data).

Observability: added metrics: slo_prefetch.bundle_build_duration_seconds, slo_prefetch.bundles_attached_total, slo_prefetch.sanitizer_dropped_fields_total and a dashboard dashboard/slo-prefetch-bundles. New alerts to watch for rollout: high bundle_build_duration > 5s (P2), sanitizer_error_rate > 1% (P3), unexpected_attach_rate spike.

Security/Privacy: bundles are sanitized; sensitive payloads are dropped or redacted. Access is limited to incident-bot service account via RBAC. We worked with security to ensure KMS keys are not captured in bundles.

Notes: this is intentionally small-scope: hublet is not a full long-term retention store. Future work (separate PRs) will add persistent bundle indexing, ML-based playbook ranking, and richer ephemeral workspace handoff flows.

Motivation: On-call teams have a high volume of low-signal alert noise (e.g., repeated retries, background job churn) that reduces attention for real regressions. This PR introduces an intent-aware notification filter subsystem in slo-toolkit to reduce pager noise by classifying alert intent and applying a configurable sampling policy. Design: intent-classifier is a small inference pipeline (lightweight TF/onnx model) that tags alert events with intent labels (user-impact, background, transient, informational). A configurable rule engine maps intents + alert metadata (service, severity, recent-alert-rate) to a delivery decision: deliver, hold-and-sample, or suppress-with-explanation. The subsystem exposes a simple SDK hook that incident-bot and other consumers can call synchronously before creating an incident or sending a page. Backwards compatibility: default policy is passthrough (no suppression). Admins can opt-in per-service via slo-toolkit config. Rollout plan: staged canary in three services, 7-day ramp with metrics guarded alert-volume, pager-rate, and missed-severity-1s. Implementation notes: added a classifier wrapper, rule engine, CLI tools to preview how a rule would behave against a window of historical alerts, and a small bridge in the incident-bot integration to annotate suppressed alerts with reasoning. Testing: unit tests for rule resolution, integration test with a small synthetic alert generator, load test to ensure classifier adds <5ms p50 latency. Security & privacy: classifier runs on alert metadata only (no full trace payloads) and respects KMS keys for model artifacts. See linked Linear items for evaluation dataset and model-retraining plan.

Summary: This PR introduces `shift-brief`, a lightweight CLI and library for creating compact on-call handoff digests, plus a companion `stratified-probe-sampler` that schedules small, targeted telemetry probes during shift boundaries.

Motivation: long handoff notes and oversized telemetry bundles increase cognitive load for responders and slow down triage during rotations. The goal here is to reduce the reading time and bandwidth for on-call handoffs while retaining actionable context and safe, opt-in telemetry links.

Implementation highlights:
- New CLI command `shift-brief generate` (flags: --window, --severity-threshold, --sanitize-level) that emits a 3–5 sentence summary, prioritized list of active incidents (id, severity, 1-line status), and 1–2 sanitized example traces. Summaries are generated by heuristics tuned for recent incident activity and enriched with SLO drift metadata.
- Stratified probe sampler service: a background worker that picks candidate probes stratified by rotation role, recent failure modes, and historical mean-time-to-detect. Probes are intentionally lightweight (synthetic request pings, targeted trace captures limited to 5 spans, metric delta checks) and attached as ephemeral URLs (signed, 24-hour) into the brief.
- Privacy & safety: automatic redaction/sanitization pipeline runs on candidate attachments (removes PII, secrets, IP addresses) and an opt-out flag per-team. We publish the sanitization audit log as part of the brief for transparency.
- Integrations: hooks for incident-bot to surface brief links on handoff, and slo-toolkit dashboards to display brief health metrics (probe success rate, average digest size).
- UX defaults: by default the brief targets a 300–800 byte plaintext summary + up to 3 attachments. Users can configure verbosity per rotation via team config.

Checklist:

- [x] Probe sampler worker and sampling policy
- [x] Sanitization pipeline with audit log
- [x] Integration tests with incident-bot minimal flow
- [x] Docs and example team config
- [x] Backwards-compatible defaults and opt-out path

Review thread (selected):

Motivation: Teams operating across multiple time zones (and frequent DST transitions) receive ambiguous on-call snippets in dashboards and pager messages. This makes handoffs error-prone and increases cognitive load. This PR introduces a lightweight timezone-aware shift annotator that canonicalizes shift boundaries to the viewer's timezone, annotates DST-awareness, and exposes a compact rotations export (CSV and ICS) to allow sharing concise schedules with external calendar systems.

What this PR does: Implements a tz-aware rule engine in the slo-toolkit library that: 1) attaches normalized start/end timestamps with timezone metadata; 2) computes human-friendly labels (local time with DST flag) and a compact one-line summary for each shift; 3) exposes a new CLI command `rotations export --compact --tz <zone>` that writes either CSV or ICS entries optimized for large rotation sets. The change is feature-gated behind `tzShiftAnnotator` and default-off for existing customers.

Technical details: The annotator lives at src/annotators/tz_shift_annotator.py and uses python-dateutil + zoneinfo fallback for older environments. It avoids modifying canonical rotation records; instead it emits decorated views used by the exporter, pager templates, and the web preview. Exporter serializes minimal ICS VEVENTs (no alarms) to reduce size and a compact CSV with columns [rotation_id, local_date, start_local, end_local, tz, brief_label]. The CLI and library include explicit DST regression tests.

Compatibility and safety: No data migrations. Storage layout unchanged; all annotated fields are derived at read-time. Feature flag `tzShiftAnnotator` controlled via scripts/feature_toggle.yaml for staged rollout. Unit and integration tests cover canonical fallbacks when zone information is missing.

Testing and CI: Added tests/tests/test_tz_dst.py to validate common DST edge-cases (US, EU, Australia, and Antarctic zones used in CI matrix). Added lightweight e2e that runs the CLI export on a synthetic 200-rotation fixture to validate size and parseability by downstream calendar parsers.

Rollout plan: Merge to main with feature flag off. Enable in a 5% canary (internal infra) for 48 hours, validate telemetry for increases in exported size and error rates, then ramp to 100% region-by-region. If unexpected formatting errors occur, gate off and patch.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of annotator and exporter
- [x] Unit tests for DST and timezone edge cases
- [x] CLI help and docs (docs/rotations.md)
- [x] Feature-flag gating and toggle script
- [x] Telemetry hooks for export failures

Notes: This PR intentionally avoids adding calendar alarms or mutating customer calendars. Exported ICS entries are meant to be imported as read-only references. Related work: ENG-1975 (oncall UX improvements), PM-845 (rotation export product request).
Marco Liu (2026-02-12): Nice incremental design. Please ensure the annotator never writes to the DB and confirm fallback semantics when rotation records lack a tz field.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-12): Reply: annotator is read-only by design; added explicit fallback to UTC in code and tests to document behavior.
Sofia Romero (2026-02-13): Request changes: add tests for DST gaps (spring forward) where local times are skipped and for ambiguous times (fall back). Also we should cap ICS export size per-file to avoid giant calendar blobs.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-14): Reply: added tests for gap/ambiguous cases and chunking for ICS exports (max 500 events/file). Noted in docs.
Adds a timezone-aware on-call shift annotator and a compact rotations exporter (CSV/ICS). Feature gated, opt-in via tzShiftAnnotator flag; no breaking changes to existing rotation storage or APIs.

payload.body:
Introduce a signal condenser in slo-toolkit that aggregates noisy telemetry into compact, prioritized oncall summaries; includes CLI, incident-bot hook, tests, and docs.
Add signal condenser utility to produce compact oncall summaries with priority stitching and latency hint recommendations; opt-in via slo-toolkit config and incident-bot mapping. Includes CLI and docs.
Context & motivation: On-call noise from noisy alerts, repetitive traces, and noisy threshold breaches makes initial triage slow. This change introduces a standalone 'signal condenser' component in slo-toolkit that aggregates telemetry (alerts, SLO anomalies, sampled traces, and log fingerprints) into compact, prioritized on-call summaries and surface latency/throughput hints to guide responders. The condenser is tuned for high-noise services and supports TTL windows, dynamic priority stitching, and safe anonymization so teams can adopt it without exposing PII.

What this PR does (high level):
- Add condensed summary generator (src/condenser/signal_condenser.py) with a pluggable priority scoring pipeline (anomaly score, alert footprint, deployment impact, recent-change signal).
- Introduce sampling layer (cmd/slo_sampler) to emit representative telemetry bundles for downstream analysis and reduced-bandwidth oncall mailers.
- Integrate a new optional incident-bot hook (incident-bot/handlers/condenser_hook.py) to attach condensed snapshots to page events.
- Add a small CLI (bin/slo-condenser) for ops to run ad-hoc sampling and to produce JSON summaries for postmortems.
- Docs and quickstart (docs/oncall/signal-condenser.md) and runbook snippet templates used by incident-bot.

Commits (summary):
- Initial implementation of priority pipeline and condenser core (commit 1 of 4).
- Sampling CLI and incident-bot integration; feature flags and config (commit 2 of 4).
- Tests and fixtures for high-noise scenarios; add docs and examples (commit 3 of 4).
- Fix race in KV cache access, lint, and add ergonomics to CLI (commit 4 of 4).

Files changed (illustrative):
- src/condenser/signal_condenser.py (core algorithm + scoring pipeline)
- cmd/slo_sampler/__init__.py + cmd/slo_sampler/cli.py (sampling CLI)
- incident-bot/handlers/condenser_hook.py (optional hook to attach summaries to page events)
- docs/oncall/signal-condenser.md (how-to, config knobs, rollout guidance)
- tests/test_condenser.py (unit + integration tests with synthetic telemetry)
- charts/slo-toolkit/values.yaml (flag to enable hook in Helm deployments)

Behavioral notes & rollout plan:
- Default is opt-out: Helm values and runtime config must enable the incident-bot hook. The CLI and condenser can be used standalone by platform teams for postmortem sampling.
- Priority stitching can be customized per-service by injecting a small YAML mapping (docs includes example).
- The condenser respects a configurable TTL window (default 15m) and max bundle size to limit token/byte cost when summaries are attached to notifications.

Testing & CI:
- Unit tests cover priority scoring permutations and anonymization; integration tests simulate bursty alert storms with synthetic traces.
- CI: lint -> unit -> integration -> acceptance. One flaky e2e (telemetry-sampler-acceptance) failed on first run due to test ordering; rerun passed. All checks green at merge.

Review thread (high-level):
- Omar Khanna (review): "Love the priority stitching idea. Two requests: make the default TTL configurable via env var and ensure the anonymizer is pluggable for regulated teams."
- Maya (author): "Done — added SLO_CONDENSER_TTL env var and an anonymizer interface with a noop adapter for teams that handle PII externally."
- Priya Patel (security review): "Please document threat model and data retention; confirm KMS usage for any persisted bundles."
- Maya: "Added docs section on data retention and confirmed condenser stores only hashed identifiers; no plaintext PII persisted. Helm values expose retention window; note added for KMS requirement when enabling persistent storage."
- Eliot Turner (ops review): "Minor: make CLI exit codes stable for automation and add a dry-run flag."
- Maya: "Added --dry-run and exit codes; updated tests. Thanks!"

Performance & safety:
- The scoring pipeline is intentionally cheap (O(n) across events in window) and limits memory by early eviction. Benchmarks: on a simulated noisy service (2k events/min) condenser CPU < 5% of a single c5.large equivalent and median end-to-end condensation latency ~120ms for a 15m window.
- Security: anonymization in the pipeline, optional KMS encryption for persisted bundles, and strict RBAC on incident-bot attachments. Docs include operational runbook for rollback and disabling the hook.

Migration & compatibility:
- No breaking API changes. The incident-bot hook is behind a feature flag. Existing oncall mailers will see no change unless enabled.

Follow-ups (tracked in ENG-4981):
- Telemetry-driven threshold tuning (adaptive thresholds)
- UI integration in Redwood Console to preview condensed snapshots in alerts
- Export to downstream analysis pipelines and evaluation harness

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main on 2026-02-14 after approvals from Omar, Priya, and Eliot. All CI green.

Notes for reviewers backporting: small config key added in charts/slo-toolkit/values.yaml (enableCondenser: false) — include in release branch if enabling feature flags for customers.

Contact: Maya R. Chen (author) for follow-ups and rollout assistance.
payload.title: Signal condenser for noise-reduced oncall summaries and latency hinting

payload.body:
Summary: This adds first-class support in slo-toolkit for querying burn-rate scoped to a rollout slice (route + model_version + region + optional customer_tier). The rollout controller needs to evaluate fast/slow burn windows against the exact scope of the rollout step; previously we only supported coarse service-level burn-rate and a handful of static labels, which caused both false positives (baseline traffic in other regions) and false negatives (rollout-only regression diluted by global volume). This PR introduces (1) a new endpoint that accepts rollout scope and returns multi-window burn rate + sample sizes, (2) a query-planning layer to avoid N+1 PromQL fanout, and (3) an in-process cache + singleflight to reduce backend load and smooth bursty controller polling.

API changes: - New endpoint: GET /v1/burn-rate/rollout?service=<svc>&route=<route>&slo=<slo_name>&model_version=<ver>&region=<region>&customer_tier=<tier>&windows=5m,30m (customer_tier optional; windows optional, default 5m,30m). - Existing endpoint /v1/burn-rate remains unchanged. - Response includes: burn_rate_by_window, error_budget_remaining, request_count_by_window, evaluation_timestamp, data_freshness_seconds, and query_fingerprint. Note: response schema is still JSON but this PR keeps it backward compatible by only adding fields to the rollout endpoint.

Implementation details: - Scope normalization: route/model_version/region/customer_tier are normalized and validated against an allowlist to avoid unbounded label injection. We reject scopes that contain regex meta characters, wildcard operators, or exceed length limits (route 128, model_version 64, region 32, tier 32). - Query planning: we build a single PromQL expression per window that computes both burn rate and request volume for the same scope, rather than issuing separate queries. This reduces total remote_read calls from 4->2 per evaluation (two windows). - Cache: adds an LRU+TTL cache keyed by (service, route, slo, model_version, region, tier, windows, time_bucket). TTL defaults to 15s; time_bucket floors to 10s to improve hit rate during controller polling. Uses singleflight to coalesce concurrent identical queries (common during step transitions). Cache entries store both result and remote error to prevent thundering herds during backend partial outages (short negative caching, 5s). - Staleness handling: surfaces data_freshness_seconds computed from the newest sample timestamp returned by the query; if freshness > 120s we return 200 but mark stale=true in headers (X-SLO-Data-Stale: true) and include freshness in the payload so the controller can treat it as “monitor stale” and suppress auto-actions per policy.

Performance impact: On staging load tests simulating 1k rollout evaluations/min across 50 scopes, remote query QPS dropped ~62% due to caching + singleflight. p95 endpoint latency improved from 420ms -> 180ms with the same backend.

Security/abuse considerations: Added strict input validation, label allowlist, max windows count=4, and max time range=1h. Also added basic rate-limit hooks (existing middleware) specifically for the rollout endpoint to avoid accidental runaway loops.

Testing: - Unit tests for scope validation, key normalization, and cache behavior (positive + negative caching). - Integration test with the fake prom backend ensures query composition stays stable and returns expected sample counts. - Added benchmark for cache hit/miss path and singleflight concurrency.

Rollout plan: - This is gated behind feature flag in the rollout controller (tracked in redwood PR-28458 / PR-28463). - Observability-pack dashboards/alerts will use the same query fingerprint to correlate evaluation events with backend queries.

Refs: Linear ENG-4826; depends on rollout controller wiring in redwood; aligns with ADR-0127 (dual-window burn-rate + min-sample gating) by returning both fast/slow windows and request volume in one response.
Allison Grant: Can we be explicit about cardinality guardrails here? Adding model_version/route in queries can explode quickly. Aisha Bello: Yep—added allowlist + max length + disallow regex operators. Also capping windows and range. Pushed commit 9f3c2b1.

Logan Wright: Cache TTL at 30s might mask regressions during fast rollouts. Can we tighten? Aisha Bello: Agree. Dropped TTL to 15s and added 10s time bucketing for hit rate; controller will still poll every ~10s. Also added data freshness surfacing.

Jordan Lee: Need request_count_by_window in response for min-sample gating (controller side). Aisha Bello: Added request_count_by_window and query_fingerprint so controller can log/trace evaluation decisions to the backend query.

Rafael Mendes: What do we do if backend is partially down? Should we fail closed? Aisha Bello: Endpoint returns 502 on remote query failure (same as existing), but we add short negative caching to prevent stampede. Controller policy decides suppress vs pause on monitor missing/stale; staleness is returned as freshness seconds.

Approved-by: Allison Grant, Logan Wright. Final note: Please ensure we emit cache hit/miss metrics. Aisha Bello: Added slo_toolkit_cache_hits_total{cache="burn_rate_rollout"} and misses_total with status labels.
- slo-toolkit: new rollout-scoped burn-rate endpoint for route/model_version/region queries
- Includes in-process caching + singleflight to reduce backend query load
- Returns request volume + freshness to support debounce/min-sample logic in rollout controller
payload.title: Add rollout-scoped burn-rate endpoint (route/model_version/region) with query caching

payload.body:
Motivation: Pager thrash and noisy handoffs are a recurring source of toil. This PR implements an adaptive "tempo controller" that smooths incident routing and an ephemeral playbook hooks surface to let runbooks execute short-lived diagnostics in a sandboxed environment. The controller applies a time-decay weighting to recent alert activity, uses configurable cooldown windows per service/route, and exposes a small policy DSL for schedule-aware routing (e.g. prefer on-call A during business hours, fallback to rotation B with exponential backoff at night). The playbook sample harness enables CI validation for playbook snippets and short-lived diagnostic scripts: it spins up ephemeral containers, verifies required telemetry access, and validates that remediation steps are idempotent and time-bounded. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of tempo controller core scheduler and policy engine - [x] Ephemeral playbook hook API and sandbox runner - [x] Unit tests for scheduling heuristics and playbook harness - [x] Integration tests simulating alert bursts and handoffs - [x] Docs (ops runbook + examples) - [x] Benchmarks showing reduced handoff churn in synthetic workload Summary of risk: this changes on-call routing logic; default policies are conservative and off by default. We ship the controller disabled on main; ops can opt-in per-service via config. Related: builds on prior incident-bot alert normalization work (ENG-3320) and complements the runbook serialiser in incident-bot (ENG-4102).
Diego Ramos: Nice direction — can we add an explicit test for sequential bursts that cross the cooldown boundary? I saw one flake in CI that looks related.
Maya Liu: Added a targeted test (test_tempo_controller::test_burst_crossing_cooldown) and fixed a cancellation race that could leave a timer firing after a handler was removed.
Samir Khan: Sandbox runner looks good, but we need to ensure secrets are never mounted into ephemeral containers. Please document the secret access pattern.
Maya Liu: Updated docs to clarify the minimal telemetry role required and added a hard check that prevents accidental host-mounted /etc/credentials into the sandbox.
Ava Patel: Verified bench runs; the synthetic scenario reduces visible handoffs across rotations by ~8%. Approving after addressing Samir's docs note.
Diego Ramos: Approving — small nit on a doc wording changed in a followup commit.
Maya Liu: Squashed and rebased; addressed nits. Ready to merge.
- Introduces an opt-in "tempo controller" to smooth on-call routing and reduce handoff churn.\n- Adds ephemeral playbook hooks and a CI harness to validate short-lived diagnostic runbooks.\n- Default OFF on main; operators must opt-in per-service.\n- Includes unit/integration tests and docs with example policies.
Operational impact: enable behind feature flag: slo.tempo_controller.enabled. Recommend gradual rollout: enable for non-critical services first and monitor handoff-count metric (slo.oncall.handoffs_per_hour).

Motivation: On-call responders frequently need a compact, prioritized snapshot of telemetry together with likely failure hypotheses rather than raw logs. This PR adds a lightweight 'Telemetry Concierge' service that prepares a deterministic, bounded-size package of prioritized metrics/traces/log snippets and pairs it with a probabilistic hypothesis harness that ranks candidate root causes and runbook suggestions. Goals: (1) reduce cognitive load for first responders, (2) enable fast canaryable rollout (opt-in per service/rotation), (3) keep sampling and storage minimal to avoid SLO regressions and cost spikes. Key features: - Telemetry Concierge engine: collects stable, privacy-aware snapshot containing top-N anomalies, delta histograms for critical metrics, representative traces (sampled by anomaly window), and a small context index. Snapshots are versioned and can be requested via CLI/webhook. - Probabilistic Hypothesis Harness: a lightweight scorer that consumes the snapshot and uses feature-weight heuristics + historical hit-rates to produce a ranked list of 3–5 hypotheses, each anchored to evidence snippets and suggested next probes. - Shift-aware deferred sampler: when on-call is busy, the concierge can schedule low-impact deferred sampling (long-tail heap dumps, low-frequency trace captures) that are stored encrypted and linked to the snapshot. - Runbook curator integration: for top hypotheses, we surface runbook fragments with confidence bands and a recommended quick-check sequence. - Safety and opt-in: sampling is opt-in per-service and respects scrubbing and retention policies. Feature flags allow rollout, and sampling budgets are enforced at the agent and server. Implementation notes: Service scoped inside slo-toolkit as pkg/concierge with agent shim for instrumentation; snapshot format is stable JSON schema v1 (compact, delta-encoded), storage by default keeps last 30 snapshots per service with TTLs configurable. Rollout plan: Stage 1 (beta): internal teams only, flag off for customer accounts. Stage 2: opt-in per-customer. Stage 3: broader default with aggressive budget enforcement. Checklist: - [x] Core engine + scorer implemented - [x] CLI and webhook endpoints added - [x] Basic unit and integration tests - [x] Docs: oncall quickstart and runbook mapping - [x] Feature flags + budgets wired - [x] Security review notes added in PR comments - [x] Perf validation on staging (latency < 3ms added on snapshot path) Backwards compatibility: Snapshot schema v1 additive; agents continue to function when concierge endpoint is disabled. Performance: measured under staging workloads; typical snapshot creation adds ~2–4ms median CPU work on agents, server indexing uses bounded queues. Operational concerns: Ensure sampling budgets are tuned for high-cardinality services; recommend default budget = 5 snapshots/hour/service for first rollout.
Marco Ruiz: Looks good overall. Please add a brief note on retention and scrubbing in the public docs; security review flagged potential PII in trace snippets.
Aisha Patel: Added scrubbing notes and TTL defaults in docs; hypothesis harness explicitly excludes raw payloads and only includes indexed trace anchors.
Jenna Lowe: Performance numbers look reasonable, can we add a stress test for a 10k/s agent churn?
Aisha Patel: Added a lightweight stress run to staging and included results in the PR comment (no queue backs up at budget=5 snapshots/h).
Ravi Deshpande: Minor nit: rename 'priority_score' to 'evidence_score' in hypothesis output for clarity.
Aisha Patel: Renamed field and updated CLI/output examples.
Introduce Telemetry Concierge (beta): prioritized snapshot packages for on-call, probabilistic hypothesis ranking, and shift-aware deferred sampling. Opt-in per-service; feature-flagged rollout. See docs/oncall/telemetry-concierge-quickstart.md for get-started steps.
payload.title: Telemetry Concierge and Probabilistic Hypothesis Harness

payload.body:
Context: As part of Dedicated throughput guarantees, we need consistent burn-rate alerting across regions/customers that matches the SLO semantics defined in the throughput SLO evaluator (PR #311). Today each service/team has been hand-rolling rule expressions and thresholds (with mismatched windows and inconsistent annotations), which is creating alert noise and complicating incident triage.

This PR adds burn-rate alert generation helpers specifically for the Dedicated Throughput SLO signal ("throughput floor met" / "below floor"), plus recommended default thresholds and alert templates (labels/annotations/runbook links). The goal is to make it trivial for downstream repos (observability-pack, infra-config) to generate standard multi-window burn-rate alerts and keep them aligned with SLO semantics.

What’s included: (1) New helper: generate_burnrate_alerts_for_throughput_slo(...) that wraps the generic burn-rate generator with Dedicated-specific defaults (page/ticket thresholds, window pairs, labels). (2) Recommended thresholds tuned for Dedicated throughput SLO: Paging on fast burn (e.g., 2h budget consumed in ~1h) and ticket on slow burn (e.g., 2d budget consumed in ~1d), using the standard multi-window approach. (3) Alert rule templates with consistent annotations: deployment_id/customer/tier/model/region, dashboard URL, and runbook URL. (4) Documentation and examples showing how to wire the helper into rule generation pipelines.

Notes/assumptions: The helper expects an SLO record exported by the throughput SLO evaluator with a boolean-like compliance signal over time and/or an error_ratio series (below-floor time / total time), keyed by {deployment_id, region, model, tier}. This PR does not change the underlying SLO computation; it only standardizes alert generation. The default windows are chosen to balance detection speed vs noise for throughput variability (streaming + batching) and match the oncall policy agreed in ENG-19288.

Out of scope: (a) owning the downstream rollout of these alerts into prod rule groups (that will happen in observability-pack / infra repos), (b) changing the Dedicated throughput SLO definition, and (c) credit/remedy logic.

Testing: Unit tests cover rule rendering, label propagation, and threshold/window configuration. Added a golden-file style snapshot test to avoid drift in template strings.

Follow-ups: (1) Wire these helpers into observability-pack rule groups for Dedicated and run a 1-week shadow period to measure noise before paging. (2) Add optional per-tier override knobs (Premium stricter paging) once tier taxonomy stabilizes.
Sean Gallagher (review): The direction is right. Two questions: (1) can we make the window pairs match our standard burn-rate policy (short=30m/2h, long=6h/1d), and (2) please ensure the annotations include the SLO name/id so we can correlate in reports.
Aisha Bello (author): Updated defaults to use the standard multi-window pairs we discussed in ENG-19288 (30m/2h for page, 6h/1d for ticket), and added slo_id + slo_name into annotations. Also ensured labels include service="dedicated" for routing.
Rafael Mendes (review): Please make sure the helper doesn’t assume PromQL-specific syntax in the string templates since some consumers render to Mimir rule groups and others to Grafana-managed alerts. Keep the expressions separate from the annotations. Also: add runbook_url as a first-class field, not embedded in description.
Aisha Bello (author): Good call—refactored so the helper returns a structured AlertRule object (expression + labels + annotations) but still serializes cleanly for Prometheus/Mimir. runbook_url is now a dedicated annotation key with a stable path.
Allison Grant (review): Can we include a canonical dashboard link format and ensure it’s URL-safe (deployment_id can have dashes/UUIDs)? Also, I’d like the templates to include tier to make it easier for CS/SRE triage.
Aisha Bello (author): Added URL encoding for variables in the dashboard URL, and included tier in both labels + annotations. Dashboard URL matches the dedicated-throughput-slo dashboard spec format (region, deployment_id, model, tier).
Sergio Costa (review): Snapshot test is great. One tweak: please add an example snippet in docs showing how to override thresholds for a specific deployment (we’ll need this during beta).
Aisha Bello (author): Added a short override example in docs/alerts/throughput_slo_burnrate.md (per-deployment config block).
Sean Gallagher (approval): Approved. Defaults and templates now match SRE guidance. Please file a follow-up for tier-specific paging policy once Premium semantics are locked.
Rafael Mendes (approval): Approved. Thanks for keeping expressions/tooling-agnostic.
payload.title: Burn-rate alerts for Dedicated throughput SLO (recommended thresholds + templates)

payload.body:
Summary: This PR adds a first-class template for measuring multi-region availability and associated error budget burn, intended for Redwood’s Regional Failover Automation Upgrade. It includes: (1) a reusable SLO definition for multi-region availability, (2) calculators/helpers for computing burn rates over multiple windows (e.g., 5m/1h, 30m/6h), and (3) documentation + examples showing how to classify region-level events vs partial degradation.

Motivation: We currently have per-region availability SLOs and ad-hoc dashboards, but no consistent way to answer: “Are we meeting the multi-region availability SLO as experienced by customers?” During regional impairment, traffic shifts can make per-region SLOs look worse while customer-visible availability remains acceptable (or the reverse if routing is unhealthy). This template standardizes measurement so we can (a) drive alerting off the right numerator/denominator, (b) compare failover controller changes against a stable baseline, and (c) report error budget burn consistently.

Design notes: The template is intentionally opinionated about inputs and aggregation: (a) uses a customer-visible request success metric (2xx/3xx) as the primary signal, with explicit handling for controlled load shedding (e.g., 429/503 with Retry-After) via an allowlist; (b) aggregates across “serving regions” for a route/tier, so the SLO reflects the experience of the routing system rather than any single region; (c) supports tagging/annotation of “region-level event” windows to avoid mixing planned failover tests with organic incidents in retros.

What’s included: - Template: `multi_region_availability` SLO definition with parameters for `service` (hosted-api, dedicated-gateway), `route`, `tenant_tier`, and `region_group` (e.g., us/eu) so we can respect residency constraints in downstream configs. - Calculators: helpers to compute availability ratio, error budget remaining, and burn rates over multiple windows; includes a small library of guardrails (min request volume, missing-data policy) to reduce false positives. - Examples: sample configs and queries for dashboards/alerts used by SRE during failover game days.

What’s NOT included: - No automatic wiring into alert manager/paging routes in this PR (that stays in observability-pack). - No changes to production SLO targets or contract language; this is a toolkit building block.

Validation: - Added unit tests for burn-rate math and missing-data behavior. - Added golden tests for query generation for both Hosted API and Dedicated flavors. - Ran `slo-toolkit validate` against a staging metric snapshot and confirmed outputs match existing dashboard calculations within rounding error.

Follow-ups: - Observability-pack PR will consume the template and roll it into the failover dashboards + burn alerts bundle. - We should align the allowlist semantics for Retry-After responses with the API gateway overload changes (see ENG-2419) so availability measurement matches customer guidance.
- New SLO template for multi-region availability (Hosted API + Dedicated).
- New burn-rate calculators that support region-level impairment classification and multi-window alerting.
- Example queries and config snippets for Redwood’s failover dashboards/alerts.
Allison Grant (review): Can we be explicit about what HTTP codes count as “good” for availability? Specifically: where do we land on 429/503 w/ Retry-After during overload? I don’t want the SLO to incentivize returning 200s on unhealthy systems, but we also shouldn’t page for intentional shedding when we’re within failover guardrails.
Aisha Bello (author): Agree. I added `success_status_classes` + `allowed_shed_statuses` as separate knobs with documented defaults. Defaults: 2xx/3xx good; 429/503 are excluded from “good” but can be optionally excluded from “bad” if `shed_is_not_customer_visible=true` AND `retry_after_present=true`. Docs call out that this should match gateway guidance and be used sparingly.
Miles Thornton (review): The event classification section is good, but we need deterministic language: what makes something a “region-level event” vs partial? Also, can you ensure the template can represent a region-group (e.g., EU-only) so we don’t accidentally normalize away residency constraints?
Aisha Bello (author): Updated docs with explicit classification guidance: region-level event is when routing for a region_group fails to serve within policy (reachability + error burn corroboration), and multi-region SLO is evaluated within that region_group. Added `region_group` parameter and made it required in the template; examples show `region_group=eu` vs `region_group=global` for hosted routes that can spill globally.
Sergio Costa (review): Nit: renderers should cap label cardinality in generated queries. If `route` is unbounded we’ll regret it. Can we add a note or safeguard?
Aisha Bello (author): Added a `dimension_allowlist` option + docs recommending routing-level aggregation for alerts (route_group) and using high-cardinality route only for dashboards. Also added a validation warning when the template is configured with >4 dimensions for alerting use-cases.
Paula Mendes (review): Please add an example that matches what PM-513 wants: a monthly rollup view (error budget remaining) and the standard burn windows for paging.
Aisha Bello (author): Added examples for (a) monthly rollup via 30d window query, (b) burn windows 5m/1h and 30m/6h with recommended thresholds. Also updated README section “Multi-window burn alerts”.
CI Bot: Checks passed: lint, unit-tests, golden-tests, build, docs-link-check.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved. Thanks for tightening the shed semantics and validation warnings.
Miles Thornton (approval): Approved. Region-group requirement is the right call.
Maintainer (merge): Squash merged into main.
payload.title: Add multi-region availability SLO template + error budget burn calculators

Motivation: On-call teams need a lightweight, low-risk way to validate playbook changes across a spectrum of temporal constraints (fast recovery vs slow remediation) and environmental conditions. This PR introduces a staging matrix runner that exercises a playbook against a configurable set of temporal windows and synthetic probes to surface regressions in timing, ordering, and side-effect detection before a playbook reaches production.

What this does (single string): Adds a new 'staging matrix' mode to the playbook rehearsal framework that: 1) accepts a matrix definition (timeboxes, probe profiles, injected-failure rates), 2) runs playbook steps deterministically in a sandboxed runner with injectable probe responses, 3) evaluates safety gates (side-effect detection, external API call thresholds, tenant-impact heuristics), and 4) emits compact rollup reports and actionable remediation hints. Includes a CLI entrypoint (slo-stg) and a Console toggle to schedule matrix runs against a branch or a playbook version.

Checklist:
- [x] core runner implementation (worker + scheduler)
- [x] synthetic probe harness and five probe templates (http-latency, db-timeout, partial-ack, metric-dip, permission-deny)
- [x] safety gate framework with abort/retry policies
- [x] opt-in Console UI hook and CLI flag --staging-matrix
- [x] end-to-end tests with deterministic seeds
- [x] docs and migration notes

Compatibility: The staging runner uses the existing playbook step interface and sandbox adapter; no changes required to user playbooks. A new opt-in annotation stanza is available for playbooks that want to declare external side-effects to improve safety gate accuracy.

Motivation: We have recurring friction and edge-case failures around credential refresh windows combined with bursty streaming workloads. This PR introduces a small runtime-side 'credential thermostat' that smooths reauth attempts across SDKs, plus an ergonomic compact streaming iterator abstraction to make retry/resume behavior consistent across Python/TS/Go. These changes aim to reduce token churn, avoid simultaneous reauth storms during capacity pressure, and make SDK consumer code simpler for common streaming patterns. Summary of changes: - Introduce a lightweight credential thermostat (in-memory, process-local) that staggers refresh attempts using a jittered cooldown window and a priority hint from the connector. Implemented in SDK core and wired into all three language adapters. - Add CompactStreamIterator abstraction (Python: CompactAsyncIterator, TS: CompactAsyncIterable, Go: CompactStreamReader) that exposes a single resume() method, backpressure-safe chunk iteration, and a small state machine to cleanly reconcile reauth & transient reconnects. - Harmonize auth retry profiles: new defaults reduce aggressive immediate retries and favor exponential backoff with capped jitter. - Update examples and docs and bump package versions. - Add unit and integration tests that simulate credential rotation and mid-stream reauth scenarios. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed by SRE and Runtime teams - [x] API ergonomics reviewed by SDK leads - [x] Unit tests for python/typescript/go - [x] Integration test against local canary runtime - [x] Changelog and version bumps included Commits (high level):  - 0b1c3fa: introduce thermostat scheduler and tests  - 47a9b21: add CompactStreamIterator interface and TS implementation  - fad7e33: wire thermostat into python SDK session manager  - 9c2e4f0: implement Go CompactStreamReader + backoff adapter  - a7f5d12: update examples, changelog, and bump versions  - 12d3b88: fix flaky test by adjusting thermostat jitter seed Changed files (high level): ["sdk/python/redwood/session/thermostat.py", "sdk/python/redwood/stream/compact_iterator.py", "sdk/python/setup.py", "sdk/typescript/src/auth/thermostat.ts", "sdk/typescript/src/stream/compactIterable.ts", "sdk/typescript/package.json", "sdk/go/cred/thermostat.go", "sdk/go/stream/compact_reader.go", "examples/streaming/thermostat-demo.py", "docs/sdk/streaming.md", "docs/sdk/auth.md", "CHANGELOG.md", "integration-tests/streaming/thermostat_rotations.test"] Review conversation (condensed): - Priya: "Nice to see a controlled approach to reauth storms. Can we ensure thermostat state is process-local only and does not create cross-container coupling?" - Sofia: "Yes — thermostat is explicitly process-local and not persisted. We discussed a global leader election but rejected it due to complexity; added a comment in code and doc note." - Liam: "TS ergonomics look good, but rename resumeTo(token) -> resumeWith(cursor) for parity with Python; also update deprecation note." - Sofia: "Renamed in TS and added a small compatibility shim for old callers. Updated CHANGELOG." - Ethan: "Integration test failed once on CI (intermittent) — suspect RNG seeding for jitter." - Sofia: "Fixed by seeding jitter deterministically in tests and expanding timeouts for CI environment; re-ran suite." CI & validation: - Initial CI run failed due to an intermittent integration test (flaky jitter seed). - Updated tests to deterministically seed jitter in CI; all tests green on second run. - Lint/format checks required a minor rename and were auto-fixed by pre-commit hook. Backwards compatibility and ergonomics notes: - Public surface maintained: changes are additive and default retry profiles are conservative; consumers may opt back into previous aggressive retry strategy via new config flag (auth.retry.profile=legacy_immediate). - CompactStreamIterator intentionally keeps resume() signature consistent across languages; we added lightweight shims for older API shapes to ease migration. Version bumps: - python sdk -> 2.3.0 - typescript sdk -> 1.12.0 - go sdk -> v0.8.2 Observability and telemetry: - New metrics: sdk.auth.thermostat.cooldowns, sdk.stream.resume.count, sdk.stream.resume.latency. - Tracing: thermostat decisions annotated on session traces to help debug correlated reauth events. Follow-ups: - ENG-3860: consider a cluster-aware thermostat for Dedicated deployments (future work) - Add a canary against dedicated capacity to validate cross-container behavior (security reviewed) Merge notes: - Squash-merged after approvals from Priya and Liam. No database or customer-facing breaking changes. Rollout: - Enabled by default; SDK releases planned to coordinate with hosted runtime to avoid surprises.
Python 2.3.0, TypeScript 1.12.0, Go v0.8.2: introduce credential thermostat backoff, ergonomic streaming iterator polish, cross-SDK parity for stream resume semantics.

Problem: On-call handoffs and post-incident triage routinely require re-running slices of telemetry and attachments to reconstruct the state that triggered alerts. Existing replay tooling either replays too little context (misses correlated signals) or replays everything (expensive, privacy-risky). Motivation: provide a compact, privacy-aware, configurable replayer that can stage evidence by confidence and freshness and a lightweight heuristic scorer to surface the most actionable evidence for responders. This PR introduces two coordinated features: (1) an adaptive triage replayer CLI/service that replays telemetry windows with deterministic sampling and staged output tiers (hot/warm/cold), and (2) a staged evidence scorer that ranks replayed artifacts using freshness, responder-latency proxies, signal entropy, and provenance quality. Key design points: deterministic sampling ensures replays are reproducible across runs; staged tiers let responders fetch hot tier synchronously and pull warm/cold tiers lazily; a privacy sanitizer strips PII from attachments and replaces sensitive fields with deterministic tokens so locally reproducible diffs are possible; scoring is rule-based with pluggable weights and a simple ML calibration hook for future work. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (linear/ENG-6483) [x] CLI + API surface implemented [x] unit & integration tests added [x] privacy sanitizer included with config toggle [x] docs and examples updated [x] migration notes and rollout plan prepared Rollout plan: feature is behind a feature flag (triage.replay.v2). Default behaviour unchanged. Staged rollout to internal SRE then limited customer alpha. Monitoring: add metrics triage.replay.requests, triage.replay.latency_p50/p95, evidence.scorer.score_distribution, privacy.sanitizer.rate. How to test locally: use the included sample bundle (tools/replay/sample-bundle.tar.gz), run `tools/replay/cli --bundle sample-bundle.tar.gz --window 00:05:00 --mode staged`, validate hot tier returns within 500ms in local mode. Security considerations: privacy sanitizer is opt-in by default for replay across account boundaries; local replays retain full fidelity. See SUP-4821 for compliance questions. Related work: builds on incident-bot replaying primitives (incident-bot/handlers/replay) and extends the slo-toolkit playback harness (slo-toolkit/playback). Notes: this is a medium-risk infra change because of new long-running replay workers; autoscaling rules were added to avoid resource exhaustion.
Ethan Chen: Overall this looks solid. A couple of requests: (1) please add a guard in the worker for very large bundles so we fail fast instead of OOMing; (2) expand the scorer doc to show example score ranges and how weights interact.
Priya Kumar (author): Added bundle-size guard (config triage.replay.max_bundle_mb) and expanded scorer docs with examples. See commit d4f9a90 and docs update.
Marisol Vega: Can we reduce the default warm-tier retention to 24h instead of 72h for the first rollout? That will limit storage blowup while we observe access patterns.
Priya Kumar (author): Agreed; changed default in helm values and documented the rationale in rollout notes.
Devon Park: integration tests looked flaky on CI due to timing assumptions in the sampler; recommend switching to clock-mocking for tests.
Priya Kumar (author): Switched tests to frozen time fixture and added retries in the replay e2e harness. The flake was resolved in f1a2b6c.
Add adaptive triage replay and staged evidence scoring: reusable CLI/service for deterministic, staged telemetry replay; privacy sanitizer for cross-account replays; heuristic evidence scorer to surface hot artifacts. Feature gated behind triage.replay.v2. See docs/triage/replay.md for usage and rollout instructions.
Feature gated; no automatic migration required. Operators should set triage.replay.max_bundle_mb and warm_tier_retention before enabling for production. Helm values example included in deploy/helm/values.replay.yaml.
Local: tools/replay/cli --bundle sample-bundle.tar.gz --window 00:05:00 --mode staged. CI runs included mocked clock fixtures. Manual: run small alpha against internal SRE project and sample bundles before wider rollout.
New metrics: triage.replay.requests, triage.replay.latency_p50, triage.replay.latency_p95, evidence.scorer.score_distribution. Alert: triage.replay.error_rate > 1% sustained for 5m and avg hot-tier latency > 1s.
Performance: initial perf bench showed p50 hot-tier latency increase of ~5% under a synthetic load; added autoscaling policy in deploy/helm to add worker replicas under burst load. Privacy: cross-account replay remains opt-in with sanitizer enabled by default for external replays.

payload.body:
Summary: This PR introduces a canonical SLO configuration schema for Redwood’s tiered SLO program (Hosted vs Dedicated) and a runtime loader that validates configs, enforces guardrails, and supports a safe rollout path (dry-run + soft-fail + hard-fail modes). The schema is per tier/region/endpoint class, designed to keep metric cardinality controlled while still enabling multi-window burn-rate alerting and tier-aware dashboards.

Motivation / Context: We need a single source of truth for SLO definitions that can be consumed by: (1) SLO budget computation job, (2) recording rules + burn-rate alerts, (3) Console dashboards, and (4) deploy gate policy checks. Prior work has SLI queries evolving in multiple places and drift between Hosted and Dedicated. This PR implements the config substrate and validation so later PRs can rely on consistent naming and semantics.

Scope: In-scope SLOs in this schema: request success rate (non-5xx), end-to-end latency percentiles, streaming reliability (disconnect/error events). In-scope tiers: hosted, dedicated. Private is not modeled yet (explicitly rejected by validator).

Design highlights:
- Config format: YAML (checked into repo) with a JSON-schema definition (for editor tooling + CI validation).
- Primary keys: tier, region, endpoint_class, window (rolling), and objective.
- Endpoint classes: chat_completions, completions, embeddings, rerank, streaming_chat (streamed responses).
- Regions: enumerated set (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1) to avoid exploding config fanout.
- Objectives supported:
  - availability: target (e.g., 99.9) and error_classification (what counts as bad)
  - latency: percentile (p95/p99) and threshold_ms
  - streaming: metric key for disconnect/error accounting (server-side only)
- Exclusions: encoded as allowlist of SLI filters (invalid_request, auth_error, rate_limited, customer_client_abort) so we don’t vary exclusions ad-hoc across tiers.
- Safe rollout flags:
  - loader.mode = off | dry_run | soft_fail | hard_fail
  - allow_partial = true/false (whether to load configs even when a subset fails validation)
  - required_coverage_min = 0.95 (guardrail for coverage validation; blocks hard-fail if we’re missing too much)
- Coverage validation: optional (enabled in CI by default, soft-fail in runtime) checks that the referenced metric names/labels exist in our telemetry catalog (via telemetry service API stub + cached manifest). This prevents shipping configs that can’t ever compute.

Implementation details:
- New package: internal/slo_config
  - Schema model structs + parsing
  - Validation passes:
    - schema validation (JSON schema)
    - semantic validation (tier/region/endpoint enums, duplicates, window sanity, objective ranges)
    - policy validation (Hosted/Dedicated constraints; e.g. dedicated must specify region explicitly; hosted can default to ‘global’ rollup entries but those are expanded deterministically)
    - metric reference validation (optional)
  - Loader:
    - loads from repo path config/slo/tiered/*.yaml
    - supports hot reload in control-plane (behind feature flag) but currently only wired into CLI + CI
- New CLI: tools/slo-config validate
  - validates all configs
  - prints normalized expanded config and validation summary
  - exit codes aligned with loader.mode
- CI integration:
  - adds a job slo-config-validate to required checks
  - ‘dry_run’ behavior in CI is disallowed; CI always uses hard-fail unless explicitly overridden in emergency (requires CODEOWNERS approval)

Files / areas changed (high level):
- config/slo/tiered/hosted.yaml (initial Hosted targets placeholders; will be updated in PM approval step)
- config/slo/tiered/dedicated.yaml (initial Dedicated targets placeholders; includes stricter latency defaults)
- internal/slo_config/* (schema, parser, validator, loader)
- tools/slo-config/* (CLI command)
- .github/workflows/ci.yaml (adds slo-config-validate step)
- docs/internal/sre/tiered-slo-config.md (dev notes + examples)

Example config snippet (illustrative):
- tier: dedicated
  region: eu-west-1
  endpoint_class: chat_completions
  window: 28d
  objectives:
    - type: availability
      target_percent: 99.9
      bad_events: ["5xx", "gateway_timeout", "stream_server_disconnect"]
      exclusions: ["invalid_request", "auth_error", "rate_limited", "client_abort"]
    - type: latency
      percentile: p95
      threshold_ms: 900

Notes / Non-goals:
- This PR does not create Prometheus recording rules or burn-rate alert definitions. It provides the typed/validated inputs those PRs will use.
- This PR does not wire deploy gates to the new config yet.
- This PR does not define final SLO targets; current values are marked as provisional and will be updated once PM-812 is approved.

Testing:
- Unit tests for parsing/validation (good configs, duplicate keys, invalid windows, out-of-range targets, disallowed tiers)
- Golden tests for normalization/expansion (hosted global entries expand into per-region set)
- CI added: slo-config-validate

Rollout plan:
1) Land schema + loader (this PR)
2) Switch alerting PR to consume normalized config (PR-28492)
3) Switch budget computation job to consume normalized config (ENG-4934)
4) Switch deploy gate policy checks to reference budget state keyed by (tier, region, endpoint_class)

Review notes requested:
- Please focus on semantic validation constraints and the expansion logic (hosted global -> per-region).
- Confirm that metric reference validation approach won’t cause fragile CI failures due to telemetry catalog lag.

Linked: ENG-4926 (build SLO config schema and validation), ENG-4921 (define tiered SLIs and exclusions)

---
Commits:
1) slo_config: add schema model + YAML parsing
2) slo_config: semantic validator + normalization/expansion
3) tools: add slo-config validate CLI
4) ci: add slo-config-validate required check
5) config: add initial hosted/dedicated tiered SLO config skeletons

---
Review conversation (abridged):
- Allison Grant: Can we lock down label enums to prevent future drift (e.g., endpoint_class names)? Also please document where latency is measured (gateway vs serving).
  - Aisha Bello: Added enums + explicit endpoint_class list; updated docs to state latency SLI is measured at API gateway e2e for this program.
- Thomas Baird: Concern on hosted ‘global’ expansion creating silent duplicates when region list changes. Need deterministic expansion + test.
  - Aisha Bello: Implemented deterministic expansion from a single region enum source; added golden test asserting expanded keys.
- Logan Wright: Metric reference validation calling telemetry service could be flaky in CI; can we use a cached manifest with pinned version?
  - Aisha Bello: Updated to use repo-pinned manifest by default; live catalog only in manual mode; CI uses pinned manifest.
- Jordan Lee: We need loader.mode to be controllable for future deploy-gate integration; suggest off/dry_run/soft_fail/hard_fail and log structured events.
  - Aisha Bello: Added loader.mode and structured log events (slo_config_validation_failed with reason codes).

Approvals:
- Allison Grant: Approved
- Thomas Baird: Approved
- Logan Wright: Approved
- Jordan Lee: Approved

CI:
- build-and-test: pass
- lint: pass
- slo-config-validate: pass

Merge: Squash merged into main on 2026-02-07.

This PR introduces first-class SLO Toolkit templates for per-model performance signals that we can reuse across regions/tier pools and plug into perf-canary alerting + rollout gates. We currently have ad-hoc Grafana + PromQL alerts in observability-pack that are hard to keep consistent, and they don't encode our recommended dampening/min-samples patterns. These templates are intended to standardize how we express and reason about performance regressions (latency and throughput) without turning performance into a classical "error budget" SLO. Scope: (1) Add new template families: ModelLatencyRegression and ModelThroughputRegression. (2) Provide guidance in-template for threshold selection (per model + SKU + region), minimum sample size, and dampening windows. (3) Add a small helper to keep label cardinality safe (standard label allowlist + enforced aggregation). (4) Add example configs for perf-canary Phase 1 (us-east) so SRE + Runtime can validate before enabling paging. Definitions: Latency regression signal = observed p95 end-to-end latency compared to a stored baseline p95 for the same model_id + model_version + runtime_build + hw_sku (+ optional region) for the same prompt-shape profile; regression computed as percent change and gated by minimum sample size over a rolling evaluation window. Throughput regression signal = observed tokens/sec (decode-dominant) compared to baseline tokens/sec for same dimensions; computed similarly. Templates intentionally avoid customer prompt data by only consuming perf-canary synthetic traffic metrics and baseline artifacts. Guidance included (docs) covers: recommended initial thresholds (warn at +10% p95 latency or -10% toks/sec; page at +20% or -20% sustained), how to tune per model based on variance, when to split thresholds by region/SKU, and how to avoid alert storms due to baseline drift or label explosions. Follow-ups: observability-pack PRs will consume these templates and remove duplicated alert rules. This does not change any existing production alerts by itself; it only adds templates and examples.
Allison Grant: Please make sure we’re not encouraging region + model_version + prompt_shape + customer_id style labels. Can we explicitly document an allowlist and have validation fail if unknown labels are used?
Aisha Bello (author): Done. Added a strict label allowlist in pkg/render/labels.go and wired it into validate. Docs now call out that region/SKU are optional and should be enabled only when variance requires it.
Sean Gallagher: I like the min-sample + dampening defaults, but paging should require sustained regression (e.g., 30m) and ideally two consecutive windows. Do we have that pattern captured?
Aisha Bello (author): Added guidance + defaults: warn uses 10m eval window, page uses 30m with a 2-of-2 consecutive evaluation requirement (implemented as two sub-conditions with offset). Also updated docs with rationale (anti-flap).
Logan Wright: Tokens/sec query needs to be explicit about which metric we expect perf-canary to emit. Please reference the canonical metric name and include an aggregation example that won’t blow up cardinality.
Aisha Bello (author): Updated to use redwood_canary_tokens_per_sec (gaugehist summary) and included aggregation examples. Also added an explicit "required metrics" block in docs with links to ENG-4873.
Noah Patel: For latency regression, can we split runtime-only vs e2e? Scheduler queueing can dominate; having both will help triage.
Aisha Bello (author): Template now supports latency_scope = {e2e,runtime_only} via a required parameter; examples use e2e. Added note that runtime_only is recommended for kernel regressions and e2e for user impact and rollout gates.
Allison Grant: Looks good. Please add a CHANGELOG entry and ensure the examples pass in CI.
Aisha Bello (author): Added CHANGELOG.md entry; examples render in CI now.
Sean Gallagher: Approved once we confirm these templates are "not enabled" by default anywhere in prod.
Aisha Bello (author): Confirmed. No deployment wiring changes; only templates + docs + examples. Observability-pack will opt-in in a separate PR.
Allison Grant: Approved.
Sean Gallagher: Approved.
New SLO Toolkit templates for per-model performance regressions (p95 latency and tokens/sec) intended for perf-canary alerting and rollout gates.
Adds docs and validated examples, plus guardrails to prevent unsafe metric label cardinality.

Summary: Introduces an "oncall_momentum" metric that quantifies recent alert activity velocity and a probabilistic 'pager decay' scheduler that recommends temporary, short-duration quiet windows when on-call momentum indicates alert noise rather than actionable incidents. Motivation: recurring noisy alerts during low-impact degradations disrupt responders and increase toil; we need a conservative, observable mechanism to reduce unnecessary wake-ups while preserving SLO-driven escalation for real incidents.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Adds a lightweight streaming metric (oncall_momentum) computed from alert ingestion rates, signal half-life, and responder acknowledgements; implements a pager-decay policy that produces probabilistic suppressions (throttle decisions) with auditability; exposes an HTTP suggestion endpoint (/v1/oncall/suggestions) and a CLI command (sloctl suggest-quiet) for engineers to preview recommended quiet windows; wires metric and decision traces into the existing tracing and audit logs.

Checklist: - [x] Metric computation implementation and tests - [x] Pager-decay decision engine and deterministic mode for tests - [x] API surface and auth (token-scoped) - [x] CLI help and basic e2e smoke test - [x] Docs: behavior, tuning guide, and safe-fallbacks - [x] Safety gates: auto-disable when critical alert patterns detected - [x] Telemetry: expose histograms and sampled decision logs

Commits (high level): * feat(metrics): oncall_momentum stream with exponential decay window * feat(scheduler): probabilistic pager_decay engine and deterministic mode * api: suggestion endpoint + OpenAPI docs + auth scope checks * cli: sloctl suggest-quiet implementation and output formatting * docs: quiet-windows.md with tuning examples * tests: unit + integration fixtures for simulated alert bursts * ci: add new lint/test jobs to matrix

Files changed (high level): src/metrics/momentum.py - core metric logic and streaming window helpers src/scheduler/pager_decay.py - decision engine, probabilistic sampler, and safety checks api/routes/oncall_suggestions.py - new route and request validation cli/sloctl/suggest.py - CLI shim and formatting lib/probability/utils.py - small helpers for reproducible sampling docs/quiet-windows.md - behavior, examples, and pitfalls tests/test_momentum.py tests/test_pager_decay.py tests/e2e/suggest_smoke.sh .github/workflows/ci.yaml - add matrix entry for suggestion smoke test

Design notes and safety: The scheduler operates in "observe" mode by default for the hosted service (no automatic suppression). Customers using the private installer can opt-in to execute suppressions via an operator-approved toggle. The decision logic is conservative: it requires (a) momentum above a tunable threshold, (b) absence of high-severity alerts matching incident rules, and (c) a minimum observation window of 2 minutes. Sampled decisions are logged to audit with input vectors to enable post-hoc analysis and regression tests.

Backward compatibility: API additions are additive. The suggestion endpoint requires a new OAuth scope (oncall:suggest) — calling without scope returns 403. CLI defaults favor dry-run output.

Review conversation (compact transcript): Lena Ortiz (reviewer, 2026-02-16): "Nice direction. Two asks: (1) make the half-life configurable via runtime config (not compile-time), and (2) add an explicit opt-out for customers that rely on exact PagerDuty semantics." Maya Chen (author reply, 2026-02-16): "Agree on both; added runtime config and opted to make the opt-out flag sticky in customer prefs. See momentum.py lines 42-68 and api route for pref check." Samir Gupta (reviewer, 2026-02-17): "Can we avoid non-determinism in tests? The probabilistic sampler should be seedable." Maya Chen (author reply, 2026-02-17): "Added deterministic mode and injected RNG seed in tests; included test harness in test_pager_decay.py." Priya Nambiar (reviewer, 2026-02-18): "Docs are great. One small UX nit: CLI output should show rationale for suggestion (dominant signal)." Maya Chen (author reply, 2026-02-18): "Added explanation block to CLI output that lists top-2 contributing signals and their weights."

CI and iteration: Initial CI run showed a flaky e2e that relied on wall-clock timing (2026-02-17); fixed by switching to simulated clock in e2e harness and re-ran CI. Final CI status: pass on all checks (unit, lint, integration, e2e smoke).

Testing and observability: Unit tests cover core math (edge cases for zero alerts), integration tests run simulated alert streams against local scheduler, and e2e smoke runs the suggestion endpoint and verifies JSON schema. Added tracing spans for metric ingestion and decision evaluation and a sampling hook to write sampled decisions to the audit log for 0.1% of decisions by default.

Operational runbook excerpt (included in docs): If customers observe more missed critical alerts after enabling suppressions, toggle the feature off and collect sampled decision logs (sloctl collect-samples) and open a support ticket with SUP-9876.

Related: ENG-4821 implements long-term oncall analytics; PM-119 tracks the user research on on-call noise thresholds.

Merge notes: Squash and merge after approvals; forward-port note for release branch v1.28.1.

payload.body:
Motivation: Repeatedly during incident retros and oncall interviews we see the same root causes related to responder fatigue: short recovery windows between high-alert periods, uneven distribution of noisy alerts across rotations, and opaque health signals for oncallers. This PR introduces an opt-in "On-call Fatigue Index" (OFI) and an automated rotation-suggester service that proposes gentle rota adjustments to reduce fatigue spikes.

What this change includes (high level):
- core/ofa: a small library that computes a normalized fatigue score per person per rolling window using three signals: alert_density (alerts/hour adjusted by severity), disruption_penalty (non-working-hours/overnight page factor), and recovery_deficit (minutes since last high-severity mitigation). Model is configurable via tuning constants and feature-flagged.
- cli/rotas_suggester: a command-line tool and lightweight HTTP endpoint that reads rotation configs and historical oncall telemetry and emits suggested shifts with confidence scores and expected reduction in peak OFI. Suggestions are conservative by default (minimize churn).
- dashboards/fatigue_dashboard.json: an initial Grafana dashboard (panel templates + example queries) to visualize per-rotation OFI heatmaps, rolling exposures, and top contributors.
- incident-bot integration hooks: optional webhook that surfaces high OFI alerts into incident-bot channels with recommended recovery windows and a "suggest rota" quick action.
