Context
We have an internal Confluence page describing the SLO→customer impact tier classifier and the remediation workflow. That page is being referenced during incidents, but the operational details have drifted since the enrichment pipeline shipped score weighting changes (v2) and CS escalation timing was tightened after SUP-19344.

This PR adds the canonical doc to the slo-toolkit repo so it can be versioned alongside the classifier code and reviewed via normal PR workflows. The majority of the content mirrors the Confluence page, but includes the v2 scoring thresholds and updated templates.

What changed (summary)
- Keep: tier definitions (1–4), overall workflow (alert→enrich→score→tier→remediate), evidence retention requirements, and post-incident/error budget reconciliation flow.
- Update: score mapping thresholds (v2), add confidence gating and a human-review fallback, update Tier 1 comms SLA (10 min), and reduce Tier 4 auto-escalation window (4 hours).
- Update: SLO catalog excerpt targets to match current baselines; add explicit note that targets are examples and owners must use the live SLO registry as source of truth.
- Update: capacity knobs table to reflect current CLI commands and pool naming.

Doc content (added under docs/incident-response/)

Title: SLO to Customer Impact Classifier and Remediation Workflow

Overview
This document defines a reproducible classifier that maps SLO signals to a customer-impact tier and a prescriptive remediation workflow. It is intended to: align SRE, Product, and Customer Success during SLO degradations; minimize time-to-customer-remediation; and create consistent inputs for post-incident reviews and error-budget decisions.

Audience
- On-call SREs
- SRE leads and managers
- Incident commanders (ICs)
- Customer Success (CS) and Support for high-impact incidents

Principles
1) Tie every SLO alert to an explicit customer-impact tier (1–4).
2) Automate low-friction routing and remediation for common degradations.
3) Escalate proactively for any Tier 1/2 customer impact.
4) Preserve evidence for postmortems and error-budget reconciliations.

Definitions
- SLO: Service Level Objective (e.g., request_latency_p95 <= 250ms).
- Error budget: 1 - SLO target over the defined rolling window.
- Customer-impact tier: a 1–4 classification used to route and prioritize incident response.

Customer-impact tiers (quick guide)
| Tier | User-visible symptoms | Business effect | Escalation urgency | Owner to notify |
|------|----------------------|-----------------|-------------------|----------------|
| 1 | Multi-region outage OR widespread request failures OR sustained elevated error rate affecting a large portion of traffic | Severe revenue/customer retention impact | Immediate (page) | SRE lead + Product PM + CS Director |
| 2 | Single-region outage, or large subset of customers impacted (major tenants) or major feature down | Significant business disruption for key customers | High (page + slack) | SRE oncall + Product owner + CS manager |
| 3 | Localized errors, degraded latency for non-critical endpoints | Minor customer annoyance, limited support tickets | Medium (slack alert) | On-call SRE + Feature owner |
| 4 | Minor latency increase or transient errors with no customer tickets | No immediate business impact | Low (ticket) | On-call SRE |

SLO catalog excerpt (example mapping; owners must confirm in live SLO registry)
| SLO name | Metric | Target | Error-budget window | Default customer-impact tier |
|----------|--------|--------|--------------------|--------------------------|
| request_latency_p95_public | request_latency_p95{route=~"/v1/.*"} | <= 250ms | 30d | 2 |
| api_error_rate_5m | sum(rate(api_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(api_requests_total[5m])) | <= 0.5% | 7d | 1 |
| embedding_throughput_tail | embedding_infer_latency_p99 | < 1.4s | 14d | 3 |
| console_ui_availability | synthetic_check(console_login) | 99.7% monthly | 30d | 3 |

Classification algorithm (operational)
1) Alert receives telemetry: detector alerts on SLI breach or error-budget burn (alerting config).
2) Metrics enrichment: pull impact signals (affected tenant count, region distribution, top N tenants by RPS, open support tickets matching pattern).
3) Heuristics engine evaluates scores (0–100): failure-scope, severity, customer-exposure.
4) Confidence gating (v2): compute confidence (0–100) based on completeness/consistency of enrichment inputs. If confidence < 50, do not auto-upgrade beyond Tier 3; route to on-call for manual triage and re-run enrichment after 5 minutes.
5) Combined score maps to Tier (v2 thresholds): Score >= 85 -> Tier 1; 70–84 -> Tier 2; 35–69 -> Tier 3; < 35 -> Tier 4.
6) Attach classification + confidence to incident and follow the tiered remediation workflow below.

Heuristics inputs (examples)
- affected_tenant_ratio: percent of total tenant RPS impacted.
- p95_latency_delta: percent change vs baseline.
- error_rate_delta: absolute change in error rate vs baseline (preferred over p99_error_spike for API).
- active_cs_tickets: number of open tickets tagged /inference or /api.
- region_blast_radius: number of regions with concurrent impact.

Operational remediations by tier
Tier 1 (Immediate response)
- Page the SRE oncall and SRE lead (PagerDuty service: customer-impact).
- Open an incident in the incident-management system using template tag=CUSTOMER_IMPACT_TIER_1 (auto-created if classifier confidence >= 70).
- Run mitigation playbook: fallback-to-compatible-model-variant.
- If capacity-related: trigger immediate capacity burst policy (see CLI below).
- Notify CS and Product leadership within 10 minutes with templated Slack/Jira.

Tier 2 (High-priority)
- Page on-call (high urgency) and post to #incidents.
- Execute targeted throttles or tenant fair-share configuration.
- Begin canary rollback of recent model or config changes (if correlated).

Tier 3 (Operational handling)
- Create ticket and schedule on-call investigation within 30–60 minutes.
- Apply mitigations from the runbook: restart worker pool, clear KV cache, or disable newly-deployed feature flag.

Tier 4 (Monitoring)
- Monitor metrics and let automated remediation run. If unresolved after SLA window (4 hours), escalate to Tier 3.

Sample alert rule (Prometheus-style YAML)
alert: HighAPIErrorRate
expr: sum(rate(api_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(api_requests_total[5m])) > 0.005
for: 2m
labels: severity: page impact: "possible-customer-impact"
annotations: summary: "API error rate >0.5% over 5m" runbook: "https://confluence.internal/s/reliability/runbooks/api-error-rate-mitigation"

Enrichment query examples (pseudo-SQL / analytics)
- Tenants affected in last 10m: SELECT tenant_id, count(*) FROM requests WHERE status >= 500 AND timestamp > now() - interval '10 minutes' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 50;
- Support ticket correlation: count tickets where created_at >= now()-10m AND tags IN ('api','inference')

Capacity escalation knobs (examples)
| Trigger | Condition | Automated action | Escalation threshold |
|---------|-----------|------------------|----------------------|
| headroom_exhausted | available_gpu_slots < 7% | trigger-burst-alloc --pool=shared-burst-v2 | immediate (Tier1) |
| model_warm_pool_empty | warm_pool_size < configured_min | scale warm pool by +2 nodes | Tier2 |
| p95_latency_spike | p95 > baseline*1.6 for 10m | enable-prefetch-kv-cache=true | Tier2 |

CLI examples
- Trigger burst capacity (operators only): rcmd infra capacity burst apply --pool shared-burst-v2 --reason "Tier1 SLO breach" --expires 30m
- Re-route traffic to fallback models: rcmd infra routing promote --from model-xyz-v2 --to model-xyz-v1 --weight 100

Communication templates
Slack template (Tier1)
- Channel: #incidents
- Message: [Tier 1 SLO breach] api_error_rate_5m at 1.2% impacting ~32% of tenant RPS across 2 regions. IC: @oncall. Mitigation in progress: promoting fallback routing. Please notify CS lead @renee.zhao. Incident: <INCIDENT_URL>

Jira template fields
- Priority: P0 for Tier1, P1 for Tier2, P2 for Tier3/4
- Components: runtime, routing, capacity, product-feature
- Labels: slo-breach, customer-impact-tier-<n>, automated-enrichment, classifier-v2

Post-incident / Error-budget reconciliation
1) Add classification evidence (metrics, tenant list, tickets) to the incident story.
2) Compute error-budget consumption attributable to the incident window.
3) For Tier1/Tier2 incidents: schedule a joint SRE/Product/CS triage within 72 hours. The triage determines whether to take a governance action (e.g., customer credits, temporary throttle, emergency capacity commit).
4) Document remediation plan and assign owners with due dates.

Postmortem checklist (to include in incident review)
- Summary of classifier result (tier + confidence) and whether the initial tier matched customer reports.
- Timeline of detection -> mitigation -> recovery.
- Root cause and contributing factors including capacity and SLO misconfigurations.
- Action items (owner + due date) and follow-up on error-budget policy.
- Evidence attachments: metrics, logs, enrichment query results.

Automation and operational tooling notes
- The classifier runs in the telemetry enrichment pipeline (owner: telemetry-team). Inputs are Prometheus alerts, request traces, and support ticket API.
- All automated classification decisions must be auditable: store computed scores, confidence, and input summaries in incident metadata.
- Confidence gating exists to prevent false Tier 1/2 upgrades when enrichment is degraded (e.g., ticket API latency, tenant-mapping lag).

Ownership and governance
- SLO owner: Each SLO must list a primary owner (SRE or Product) and a secondary owner. Owners are responsible for maintaining mapping in the SLO registry and ensuring this doc stays consistent.
- Classification engine owner: telemetry-team@redwood.com.
- Incident review owner for Tier1/Tier2: SRE lead on rotation.

Runbook links (examples)
- API error mitigation: https://confluence.internal/s/reliability/runbooks/api-error-rate-mitigation
- Fallback routing: https://confluence.internal/s/reliability/runbooks/fallback-routing-and-rollbacks
- Capacity burst playbook: https://confluence.internal/s/reliability/runbooks/capacity-burst-and-burst-rollback

Change log
- 2026-01-15 — Initial draft published (Priya Natarajan).
- 2026-02-20 — Added capacity knobs and CLI examples (review: Liam O'Connor).
- 2026-03-01 — Finalized communication templates and post-incident checklist (review: Renee Zhao).
- 2026-03-16 — Updated classifier thresholds to v2, added confidence gating, tightened Tier1 notification SLA to 10 min, and reduced Tier4 escalation window to 4 hours (review: Sasha Kim).

Appendix: sample incident evidence payload (illustrative)
- incident_id=INC-2026-0316-014 slo=api_error_rate_5m failure_scope=81 severity=88 customer_exposure=63 confidence=77 mapped_tier=1 top_affected_tenants=[tenant-acme,tenant-vela] evidence_queries=[tenant_impact_query_2026-03-16-10m]

Operator note
If you are an on-call SRE and this workflow appears to misclassify an incident, create a ticket in the SRE backlog and tag telemetry-team for review. Include the incident link and the classifier scores/confidence from incident metadata.

Contact
- Document owner: Priya Natarajan (pri@redwood.com)
- Telemetry owner: telemetry-team@redwood.com
- Incident management: incidents@redwood.com

Testing
- N/A (documentation only).

Rollout
- Once merged, we will link this doc from the internal runbook index and update the Confluence page to point at this repo copy as the source of truth.
Liam O'Connor (review): Please make the v2 threshold change explicit (old vs new) so oncall knows why behavior differs from the Confluence screenshot floating around.
Priya Natarajan (author): Added v2 thresholds in-step (Score >= 85 Tier1 etc) and added confidence gating paragraph. I avoided pasting old thresholds to prevent copy/paste drift, but can add a one-liner callout if you want.
Liam O'Connor (review): One-liner callout is enough. Also the capacity pool is shared-burst-v2 now, right?
Priya Natarajan (author): Updated the capacity table + CLI examples to shared-burst-v2 and added a changelog entry dated 2026-03-16.
Renee Zhao (review): Please change Tier1 CS notification window to 10 minutes (per SUP-19344). Also remove the emoji from the Slack template; our incident tooling strips it and it looks messy.
Priya Natarajan (author): Done: Tier1 comms within 10 minutes; Slack template now uses a bracketed prefix instead of emoji.
Mateo Alvarez (review): Appendix evidence payload: earlier doc showed JSON object with nested computed_scores. This repo doc should avoid implying a strict JSON schema unless we link to the actual schema file.
Priya Natarajan (author): Adjusted appendix to an illustrative key=value format and clarified it's illustrative. The actual schema lives in telemetry-pipeline and will be referenced separately.
Sasha Kim (review): Add a note that if confidence < 50 we should not auto-upgrade beyond Tier3; that’s the key operational change we made after ticket API outages.
Priya Natarajan (author): Added confidence gating rule in the algorithm steps and in automation notes.
Liam O'Connor (final): Approved.
Renee Zhao (final): Approved.

Motivation: On-call responders frequently get paged with terse callouts; understanding which sections of a playbook are actually actionable during a responder's shift boundary is a recurring source of friction. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) a lightweight callout annotator that enriches incoming alerts/pager callouts with contextual runbook fragments and signal-level hints, and (2) a shift-boundary playbook coverage mapper that computes which playbook playlets have owners for upcoming shifts and surfaces coverage gaps to the on-call UI and CLI.

What this changes (summary):
- New service `callout-annotator` (go) that subscribes to alert stream (Kafka topic `alerts.enriched`) and attaches: runbook fragment IDs, confidence hints, quick remediation snippets, and suggested escalation paths. It stores annotations to the existing `telemetry_annotations` table (nullable columns so non-breaking).
- New mapper job `playbook-coverage-mapper` (python) that scans playbook metadata, on-call rotation schedules (PagerDuty/SCIM import), and computes per-shift coverage vectors. Mapper writes a compact coverage manifest (S3 prefix) consumed by console and CLI.
- CLI command: `slo-toolkit playbook-coverage --shift YYYY-MM-DDTHH` that prints coverage heatmap and open responsibilities.
- Console integration: a new badge in the on-call incident panel that links to the coverage manifest and shows missing owners for recommended playlets. (Frontend change limited to a small badge and link).
- Backfill: one-off job to generate coverage manifests for the last 30 days (included as `scripts/coverage_backfill.py`).

Checklist: 
- [x] API and storage schema changes are additive and backward compatible (new nullable fields).
- [x] Unit tests for annotator matching heuristics and mapper logic (coverage thresholds, owner lookup).
- [x] E2E smoke: local runner that replays sample alerts and verifies annotation writes + coverage manifest output.
- [x] Load test: annotator processed 2k alerts/s in bench harness with 50ms median per-message processing.
- [x] Docs: developer notes, CLI usage, and an ops runbook for rollout and rollback.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- We intentionally keep annotation payloads small (IDs + short strings) to avoid duplicating large runbook content across the telemetry store. The annotator references canonical playlet IDs which the console expands lazily.
- Coverage mapping happens at shift granularity (4 hour windows by default) to keep manifest size bounded; we can later add per-minute slices if needed.
- The annotator uses a heuristic matcher (name + regex + entropy-based fingerprint) rather than a heavy ML model to keep runtime and infra cost down; accuracy is ~84% on internal eval set.

Commits summary: 
- Initial annotator service and message consumer (go): callout-annotator/main.go + matching logic + unit tests.
- Playbook coverage mapper (python): mapper, serializer to S3, and backfill script.
- CLI: add `playbook-coverage` subcommand and small output formatter.
- Console: add coverage badge and fetcher client.
- infra: IAM role for mapper S3 writes, new k8s cronjob, helm chart additions.

Changed areas (high level list):
- services/callout-annotator/* (new)
- tools/playbook-coverage/* (new)
- web/console/src/components/OncallBadge.tsx (small change)
- cli/slo-toolkit/coverage.py (new)
- infra/helm/templates/callout-annotator.yaml (new)
- infra/iam/roles.yaml (small addition)
- scripts/coverage_backfill.py (new)

CI and test summary: 
- CI run 1: unit tests (go/python), linter, build: PASS.
- CI run 2: integration smoke against staging cluster: PASS (annotator wrote to telemetry_annotations staging table).
- Bench job: local bench harness measured 2k alerts/s peak; median processing time 50ms.

Rollout plan: 
1) Deploy annotator to staging, monitor latency and annotation correctness for 24 hours (staging flag enabled).
2) Deploy coverage-mapper as cronjob in staging; generate manifests and validate UI/CLI consumption.
3) Canary deploy annotator in production to 10% of alert traffic (routing rule feature flag).
4) If stable after 48 hours, increase to 50% then full.
5) Run backfill after full rollout to populate historical manifests.

Migration notes: DB changes are additive; scripts included to backfill existing alerts with annotation keys. To rollback remove feature flag to stop traffic and remove k8s deployment; S3 manifests are idempotent and can be deleted if needed.

Security considerations: annotations do not include PII or full alert payloads. We run a sanitizer step to scrub any user-provided text before saving. IAM policy scope is minimized to specific S3 prefix and telemetry_annotations table.

Related work: builds on ENG-1289 (playbook metadata normalization) and SRE-447 (oncall rotation importer).

Note: the description is intentionally compact; unit and integration tests are in the PR for reviewers to run locally.
Adds a callout annotation pipeline and a playbook coverage mapper. New CLI: `slo-toolkit playbook-coverage`. Backfill job included. No breaking changes.
Maya Chen (2024-11-21): Nice direction — can we add a small TTL on annotations to avoid stale content if runbook IDs change?
Lucas Ramirez (2024-11-21): Added ttl_seconds column and migration script; annotations are now annotated_at + ttl_seconds (default 30 days).
Priya Desai (2024-11-22): Mapper looks good. I suggest we avoid writing manifests for windows with zero coverage to reduce S3 churn.
Lucas Ramirez (2024-11-22): Mapper now skips zero-coverage windows and emits a compact index file for fast lookup.
Owen Kline (2024-11-24): A couple of nit comments on CLI output formatting and error messages — see inline. Also can we add a short healthcheck endpoint for the annotator?
Lucas Ramirez (2024-11-25): Addressed formatting nits and added /healthz returning 200 and metrics. Updated tests accordingly.
Priya Desai (2024-11-27): Verified staging runner, ran backfill; tagging approval.
Maya Chen (2024-11-28): Approved — small follow-ups captured as issues.

payload.body:
Motivation: oncall responders frequently need a compact, high-signal telemetry snapshot at shift start or during early triage. Large, ad-hoc queries are slow, expensive, and often leak sensitive fields into chat channels. This PR introduces a timeboxed 'telemetry primer' utility that prefetches an annotated, minimal snapshot of critical signals and an ephemeral, read-only debug shell for safe interactive diagnostics. The primer is designed to be low-cost, privacy-aware, and attachable to incident threads via incident-bot.

What this PR does (single-string sectioned summary):
- Adds a lightweight CLI/service that collects a curated telemetry bundle (error rates, latency p50/p95 trends, recent sampled traces, active alerts, recent deploy markers, and a compact list of top 10 callers). The fetch window is configurable but defaults to the last 30 minutes (timeboxed).
- Introduces an ephemeral debug shell (read-only) that runs within a tightly sandboxed Lambda container: provides safe query primitives (schema-aware metrics, trace drilling by id, sampled logs) with rate limits, mandatory redaction rules, and an audit log per session.
- Integrates with incident-bot to publish a sanitized primer card to the incident channel and optionally attach a downloadable artifact. The incident-bot integration uses a feature flag and respects RBAC scopes.
- Adds CI tests, unit tests for sampling logic, property tests for redaction, and an end-to-end smoke test that runs against a local telemetry fixture.

Design choices and safety gates:
- Timeboxed default window (30m) with explicit override required for >2h fetchs; large-window fetches are blocked unless the user has the 'debug:extended' flag.
- Sampling-first approach: traces and logs are downsampled deterministically using a seed derived from incident id so multiple responders see consistent samples.
- Redaction pipeline: field-level allowlist/denylist implemented; PII-like fields are always stripped. The redaction rules are pluggable and live in docs/runbooks/telemetry-primer.md.
- Audit & retention: every primer run emits an audit record to the audit-log-exporter topic with a TTL. The actual artifacts are ephemeral and auto-delete after configurable TTL (default 24h).

Files and surface area changed (high level):
- cmd/telemetry_primer/cli.py: new CLI that produces the primer artifact.
- slo_toolkit/ephemeral_shell/shell.py: sandboxed interactive runner with read-only query primitives and guardrails.
- slo_toolkit/redaction/policies.py: declarative allowlist/denylist rules and unit tests.
- docs/runbooks/telemetry-primer.md: runbook and operational guidance for oncall.
- deploy/featureflags/primer-rollout.yaml: feature flag config for gradual rollout.
- dashboards/primer-summary.json: small Grafana template for primer summary panel.
- tests/test_primer_e2e.py: local fixture smoke test.

Checklist (completed):
- [x] Unit tests for sampling and redaction
- [x] E2E smoke test against fixture
- [x] Docs runbook with operator guidance and rollback steps
- [x] Feature flag gating and rollout plan
- [x] RBAC checks and audit records

How to use (short):
- Run `telemetry-primer fetch --incident-id INC-12345 --window 30m` to get a sanitized artifact.
- Run `telemetry-shell start --artifact ./primer-INC-12345.tgz` to open a read-only shell that exposes `metrics`, `trace`, and `logs` primitives.
- If enabled, post to incident channel with `--post-to-inc-bot`.

Related work: links to the incident-bot integration RFC (internal) and ENG-5124 which requested built-in pre-triage snapshots.

Security notes: all network calls use instance-identity or KMS-backed credentials; the shell has no write APIs and runs with IAM role scoped to read-only telemetry. We added additional lint rules to prevent accidental removal of redaction steps.

Migration and rollout: feature flag start at 0.0.0 for beta, 10% rollout for engineering oncall, then wide. Default behavior is off for customers and on for Redwood internal oncall only.

Ava Martinez: This looks useful. Two concerns: ensure the sampler is deterministic across responders and make the default window short to avoid cost. Can we add an override guard?
Sofia Nguyen: Reply: sampler is deterministic based on incident id seed; default window is 30m and there is an explicit guard that blocks >2h unless the user has debug:extended scope. Added tests for determinism.
Noah Kaplan: Please add an explicit audit record that includes the redaction policy version used. Also add a quick smoke dashboard so oncall can see primer health.
Sofia Nguyen: Reply: audit records now include redaction_policy_version and dashboard panel added (dashboards/primer-summary.json).
Priya Shah: Security review: verify that shell cannot access S3 write APIs and that credentials are ephemeral. Also request an approval from Security before wide rollout.
Sofia Nguyen: Reply: shell runs with read-only role, uses short-lived STS creds; added security checklist in docs. Marked rollout as internal only until Security approval.
Ava Martinez: Approving after seeing tests and docs.

(Approval: ava.martinez — 2026-03-04)
Add telemetry primer for quick triage: timeboxed snapshot, ephemeral read-only debug shell, redaction pipeline, incident-bot integration. Feature-flagged; internal beta only.

payload.body:
Summary: Adds a compact runbook snapshot sampler and a temporal alert resynthesis pipeline to the slo-toolkit to reduce time-to-triage and enable deterministic rehearsal of noisy incidents. The snapshot sampler captures an ordered, token-limited representation of the runbook steps, key telemetry pointers, and contextual breadcrumbs at the moment an alert fires. The resynthesis component takes a window of raw alerts and produces a de-duplicated, temporally-consistent timeline optimized for human review and automated replay. Motivation: On-call responders frequently reconstruct incident timelines from disparate logs and alerts; this PR produces pre-assembled artifacts and synthetic replays so responders can make faster decisions and teams can rehearse previous incidents reliably. What changed: - New service: cmd/snapshot-sampler (Go) with a lightweight HTTP ingestion endpoint and an internal ring-buffer for short-lived samples. - New library: telemetry/snapshot (Go) - protobuf schema for RunbookSnapshot + compact pointers. - New CLI: rw-runbook sample [--rate=] [--ttl=] to produce and upload sample artifacts to S3-compatible storage or local store for on-prem installs. - Temporal resynthesis: telemetry/resynth (Go) implementing fingerprinting, temporal condensation, and probabilistic summarization; supports a deterministic mode for tests/replays. - Integrations: hooks to incident-bot (compact artifact links in PagerDuty/Slack messages) and a small adapter in slo-toolkit observability to surface sample coverage metrics. - Tests: unit tests for fingerprinting and condensation, integration test that runs a synthetic noisy alert stream through resynth and asserts condensed timeline matches golden fixture. - Docs: new runbook describing sampling guarantees, privacy considerations, and storage TTL semantics. Adds compact call-tree capture on incident start and a seeder that populates the on-call primer with suggested next steps and probable mitigations.
Motivation: On-call responders frequently need a quick top-down view of what the service process looked like at incident start (goroutine/thread hotspots, recent exec path, open network sockets) and a focused, action-oriented primer tailored to the observed signals. This PR introduces a lightweight call-tree collector and an on-call primer seeder that bundles captured artifacts with heuristic remediation hints so first responders can act faster without full trace access.

What this does: 1) Introduces a compact call-tree capture agent (golang) that samples active goroutines+stack traces, condenses them into a weighted call-tree (hot path aggregation), and attaches minor environment fingerprints (listening ports, recent open files, binary version). 2) Adds a seeder component (python) that consumes the compact capture and generates a short on-call primer: probable root causes, 3 next diagnostic commands, safe mitigations, and suggested runbook links. 3) Adds Slack and CLI integration so the collector+seeder output can be pushed to the incident channel or downloaded as a .zip. 4) Feature-flagged and opt-in by default for Private/Dedicated clusters (configurable via SLO_TOOLKIT_CAPTURE=true).

Design notes: - Compact format: top 50 call frames aggregated into a tree with counts and a simple entropy score for nondeterministic noise. Designed to be <= 100KB for standard services. - Privacy: the collector strips string literals and environment variables unless an explicit allowlist is set; binaries/paths are hashed when sent to central seeder. - Extensibility: seeder uses a small rule engine (yaml-driven) to map call-tree fingerprints to runbook templates; initial rule-set covers HTTP worker exhaustion, DB connection leaks, event-loop stalls, and native OOM patterns.

Checklist: - [x] Collector implementation (golang) with sampling + aggregation - [x] Seeder implementation (python) + rule engine - [x] Slack + CLI delivery hooks - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Documentation page and runbook templates - [x] Feature flag and opt-in defaults - [x] Sanitization and size guarding

Backward/compatibility: Opt-in; does not change default telemetry or network flows unless enabled. No breaking change to existing APIs.

Security and privacy: Strings are redacted by default. The seeder runs in the control plane (or optionally local) and never expands compressed attachments without explicit operator acknowledgment.

How to review: Focus on the collector's sampling window and aggregation correctness, and on the rule engine mappings for false-positive risk. The seeder's sample outputs are included in tests/fixtures for quick review.

Related work: ENG-4821 (incident triage speedups), SRE-119 (runbook seeding), OPS-337 (private deployment opt-in requirements).
Local end-to-end: 1) build collector: go build ./src/calltree && ./calltree --emit=local --out=./tmp/capture.zip 2) run seeder locally: python3 pkg/seeder/seeder.py --input ./tmp/capture.zip --out ./tmp/primer.json 3) run integration: pytest tests/integration/test_end_to_end.py --capture=tee-sys. Feature flag: export SLO_TOOLKIT_CAPTURE=true to enable CLI delivery. Slack integration requires SLACK_TEST_TOKEN set to a test workspace and will post to #slo-toolkit-test.

Automated tests: pytest -k "collector or seeder" covers unit+integration fixtures. CI pipeline includes lint, unit, integration (containerized), and e2e smoke (simulated).

Motivation: Alerts in the token-cost/latency space spike frequently during transient prompt-shape changes and model rollout warmups. This PR introduces a lightweight token stability scorer that summarizes per-invocation token-level variance and a retroactive alert pause (deadzone) that temporarily suppresses alerts for routes showing coherent short-term instability patterns. The goal is to reduce alert noise while preserving signal for true regressions.

What this PR includes: checklist:
- Implement TokenStabilityScorer service that computes a bounded stability score per invocation (range 0..1) based on token latency variance, KV-cache hit patterns, and prefix warmup indicators.
- Add retrospective alert pause controller: when a route's aggregated stability score crosses the instability threshold for a configurable lookback window, the controller adds a short-lived alert mute annotation (retroactive) and emits an explanatory event.
- Dashboard: observability/playgrounds/token-stability-playground.json — a small, interactive panel to visualize scores, token breakdown, and retrospective pauses.
- Telemetry: new metrics token_stability_score (gauge), token_stability_window_pct_unstable (counter), alert_pause_events_total (counter). Metrics include tags: route, model, tenant, region.
- Backfill/compat: safe defaults for previously instrumented paths; scoring is opt-in via alert policy flag.
- Tests: unit tests for scorer heuristics, integration tests exercising simulated warmups via synthetic-replay bench.

Design notes: The scorer is intentionally conservative — it favors precision over recall to avoid masking hard regressions. Score computation is a linear combination of normalized per-token latency variance, kv-cache miss ratio for the invocation, and prefix-change entropy (from existing prompt-shape histograms). Scores are produced at ingestion time and attached to invocation spans and metrics. Retroactive alert pause is applied as an annotation on the alert decision with TTL and audit trail.

Rollout plan: canary 10% of traffic for 48h, watch: alert rate per-route, mean latency, false-suppression metric computed as alerts suppressed but with downstream error increase. Gradual increase to 50% then 100% if synthetic-replay and canary metrics are stable.

Related linear items: ENG-8421 (scorer), ENG-8422 (alert pause), PM-391 (playground). Related investigation: SUP-2345 (customer noise spike from model v12 warmup).

Notes: The description below lists high-level commits, changed areas, and the review conversation. CI flakiness was observed once (integration e2e-observability) and rerun successfully.

Aisha K: Can the scorer be configured to ignore synthetic replay traffic? Request: add tag-based opt-out (answered).
Author (Nikhil): Added opt-out flag and unit test for synthetic tag. See commit feat: allow-synthetic-opt-out.
Liam C: Concern: retroactive pause could hide an infra regression if applied globally. Suggest scope to route+model. (updated) 
Author (Nikhil): Scope tightened to route+model+tenant; controller rejects pause if global anomaly signals are present.
Sara M: Request adding an audit log line and a metric for suppressed_alert_count. (requested changes)
Author (Nikhil): added alert_pause_events_total and suppressed_alert_count metric; added audit event with owner metadata.
Unit tests for core heuristics (coverage ~88%), integration tests with replaybench simulated warmups, and a 6h synthetic shadow run against staging with 50k invocations showing 62% reduction in route-level noise and no increase in true error rate. e2e-observability showed transient failure once due to test env flakiness and succeeded on rerun.
Introduce token stability scoring and retroactive alert pause. This reduces noisy alerting for short-lived prompt-shape instability; opt-in via alert policy flag. Metrics: token_stability_score, alert_pause_events_total.
Canary rollout: 10% traffic x 48h -> evaluate alert reduction and suppression-safety signals -> 50% x 72h -> 100% if stable. Automated rollback if suppressed_alert_count > 0.5% of baseline or mean latency increase > 5%.

Context and motivation: On-call drills and runbook validation are currently manual and brittle. Teams need a lightweight way to exercise runbooks and on-call playbooks against realistic dependency failure modes (partial flaps, slow degradation, intermittent 5xxs) without incurring cloud costs or affecting production. This change introduces a local 'shift-resilience' simulator and a set of lightweight HTTP/gRPC mock services that can reproduce external-dependency behaviors used in SLO breach drills.

What this PR does: Adds a CLI-driven simulator (sloctl shift-sim) that can drive: deterministic failure patterns, probabilistic degradation curves, delayed responses with long-tail latency distributions, and cascading failure scenarios. Adds a small library of mock endpoints (http-mocks/) that expose configurable fault profiles and a harness to wire them into existing runbook tests. Includes example runbook scenarios that show how responders and escalation paths would behave under simulated conditions.

Files added/changed at a glance: a new binary (cmd/sloctl/shift_sim.go), a simulations package (internal/sim/), a mock service set (tools/http-mocks/), three example runbooks (examples/runbooks/resilience-*) and CI integration in .github/workflows/sim-check.yml.

Checklist: - [x] Simulator CLI implemented and documented - [x] Mock dependency service with configurable profiles - [x] Unit tests for simulation scheduler and profile parser - [x] End-to-end integration test that runs a scenario and asserts runbook triggers - [x] CI workflow that runs quick sim smoke tests on PRs - [x] Basic docs and ’how to run a drill’ example committed

Commit summary: 1) initial simulator skeleton + CLI wiring 2) scheduler and deterministic profile engine 3) http/gRPC mock service with YAML profiles 4) example runbooks and integration tests 5) CI workflow and docs 6) address review feedback (test flakiness fixes, harden profile parsing).

Usage notes: To run a quick local drill: 1) make build && bin/sloctl shift-sim --scenario examples/runbooks/resilience-minor.yaml --mocks tools/http-mocks/config.yaml 2) Observe simulated alerts in the dev Slack webhook and see how runbook steps are executed in dry-run mode. The CLI supports --time-scale to speed up long-running degradation.

Backward compatibility and risk: This is opt-in tooling (no runtime changes to production services). The mocks are in tools/ and the CLI is install-time; nothing modifies production routing. Risk is low; primary risk was flaky tests which were remedied by deterministic RNG seeding in tests.

Related: Linear ENG-8472 (drill automation), SUP-678 (customer ask for repeatable runbook validation).

Notes for reviewers: Focus on the scheduler semantics (internal/sim/scheduler.go), the profile DSL (tools/http-mocks/profiles.md) and the integration test harness (test/e2e/shift_sim_test.go). CI pipeline runs a quick 10s scenario; longer stress scenarios are intentionally excluded from PR CI to keep runs fast.

Release notes: Added a local shift-resilience simulator and mock dependency harness to help teams validate runbooks and on-call procedures without touching production.

Rosa Kim: Tests flaked on CI due to RNG; please seed or inject clock — author reply: seeded RNG and added deterministic clock abstraction; CI green now.
Devon O'Leary: Profile DSL parsing looks permissive; can we tighten validation and add schema examples? — addressed: added stricter validation, schema doc and unit tests.
Marco Jensen: +1 for approach, minor nits in docs (typo fixed)

Motivation: On-call teams have reported recurrent blindspots during planned low-traffic windows (maintenance, regional holidays, cron quiet periods) where existing alert rules either flood with noisy infra signals or produce no coverage for regressions in background telemetry. This PR adds a lightweight 'silent window detector' that analyzes time-series metadata and alert history to (1) surface candidate windows with unusually low alert signal but nontrivial metric drift and (2) recommend focused diagnostic payloads an operator can collect with a single CLI command.

What this PR contains: checklist: - add silent-window-detector module with heuristics based on alert event rate, metric variance, and scheduled maintenance calendar - add operator hint CLI (slo-toolkit hint-collect) that bundles traces, recent metric snapshots, and a minimal sanitized logs sample - telemetry-lint rules that warn about missing synthetic probes or missing alert coverage during identified windows - integration tests and e2e harness for a simulated quiet window - docs and a short runbook template for on-call responders to use when a silent window is flagged

Design notes: The detector runs as an offline job (daily or ad-hoc) using existing metric and alert event APIs; it emits a compact JSON signal that can be consumed by the Console or by automation. Heuristics are tunable via a config map (defaults handle hourly/day-of-week patterns). The operator CLI uses the same credentials as existing oncall tooling and produces a tarball with a deterministic filename and a checksum for easy upload to postmortem artifacts. No hot path change to the production alerting runtime.

Commits summary: - Add detector core + config and unit tests (A. Patel) - Implement hint-collect CLI and unit test harness (A. Patel) - Add telemetry-lint rules and examples (R. Gupta) - Add docs + runbook templates (T. Rivera) - Fix: sanitize sensitive keys in bundled logs (security follow-up)

Files of interest (high level): - pkg/detector/silent_window_detector.go - pkg/detector/config.go - cmd/hint-collect/main.go - tooling/telemetry-lint/rules/silent_window_rules.yaml - docs/ops/silent-windows-runbook.md - test/e2e/silent_window_simulation_test.go - Makefile entries to wire daily job

Testing performed: Unit tests for heuristics covering edge cases (holiday days, maintenance windows, high variance microbursts). E2E simulated replay of 30 days with deterministic random seed to validate detection precision/recall thresholds. Manual smoke-run of hint-collect against staging cluster with sanitized artifact upload to S3. CI initially failed on lint (line-length and vet issues) and on a flaky test; fixed and retriggered, final CI green.

Review conversation: Reviewer Diego Morales: "Can you clarify how the detector differentiates a true quiet window from a transient alert suppression? Concerned about false positives during autoscaler events." Author reply: "Detector uses both alert event rate and metric variance over a rolling 72h window and ignores windows that overlap scheduled autoscaler maintenance (we already read cluster-schedule metadata). Added a unit test for autoscaler overlap." Reviewer Rina Gupta: "Please ensure the CLI does not include any PII tokens; what credential paths are used?" Author reply: "CLI explicitly strips known headers and secrets from logs and only reads K8s service account token via in-cluster recommended path; documented in the CLI README. Added a sanitizer step that removes Authorization and Cookie headers." Reviewer Tomás Rivera: "Docs look good; can we add a sample Linear ticket template for followup?" Author reply: "Added a template and integrated it into docs/silent-windows-runbook.md." Approvals: Diego Morales approved after autoscaler test fix; Rina approved after sanitization step; Tomás approved docs.

Risk and rollout: Low-risk. Detector runs offline as an opt-in job to start; the default config will only surface candidates above a conservative confidence threshold. Rollout plan: feature gated (config flag off by default) -> enable for two internal namespaces -> enable for internal SRE teams -> gradual expose in Console UI. No data migrations required.

Migration notes: Operators can opt-in by adding a configmap entry; hint-collect CLI is backwards compatible and does not change existing artifact formats beyond adding a single metadata file (silent_window_summary.json).

CI history: initial pipeline (linux/unit, linux/e2e, lint) failed on lint and a flaky e2e test; author fixed issues in two follow-ups and re-ran CI. Final status: all checks passing.

Merge: Squash merge after approvals and green CI.

Related: references ENG-4921 for scheduling metadata support and SRE-233 for on-call fatigue interviews.

Notes for release: include runbook in internal docs site and announce on #sre; add a short demo in the weekly oncall sync.
Add a detector that identifies low-activity windows ('silent windows') where alerting coverage should be evaluated; provides an operator CLI to collect minimal diagnostic bundles and suggested playbook hints. Backwards-compatible, no runtime changes to consumers.
This PR purposefully targets tooling that augments human on-call workflows rather than automated auto-remediation to reduce risk; follow-up planned to wire detector signals into the Console as an opt-in alerting 'insight' card.

Motivation: on-call handoffs are noisy and repetitive: large alert lists and dense telemetry windows make readable handoffs hard to write and validate. This PR introduces two companion features: a lightweight 'Handoff Sentinel' that watches for incomplete handoff messages and suggests an enriched summary, and a 'Shift-Boundary Telemetry Compressor' that aggregates high-frequency signals across the shift boundary into a compact, human- and machine-friendly bundle. The goal is to reduce handoff friction, lower oncall cognitive load, and provide a deterministic, audit-friendly bundle that incident-bot and downstream tools can consume. Features: 1) CLI: `slo-toolkit handoff summarize --window 30m --compress-level medium` produces a compressed bundle plus suggested handoff notes. 2) Sentinel: a background check that validates handoff messages (presence of incident summary, pending actions, blockers) and attaches suggested content with recent alerts, top traces, and anomaly highlights. 3) Compressor: a configurable summarizer that turns dense metric/trace histograms into delta summaries, spike fingerprints, and compact traces (head-only snippets + links). 4) Integration hook: gRPC endpoint for incident-bot to request the compressed bundle when producing runbook drafts. 5) Config: runtime flags and Helm chart knobs for retention and compression level. Implementation notes: compressor uses a streaming reservoir + top-k spike detector tuned for 1s-1h signals, configurable by workload; sentinel is non-blocking and returns an enrichment suggestion object rather than mutating handoff text. Checklist: - [x] Implementation for CLI + library (pkg/handoff) - [x] Unit tests and benchmarks for compressor - [x] Integration test that simulates shift boundary handoff - [x] Docs and handbook page under docs/handbook/oncall/handoff.md - [x] Helm chart defaults and feature flag - [x] Performance review and memory cap (see review thread) Compatibility and risk: default compressor settings are conservative; feature is opt-in via helm flag `handoff.enabled` and CLI flag for summarize. No breaking changes to public APIs. Related: ENG-3421 (handoff UX improvement), ENG-4110 (telemetry budget savings).

Maya Chen: Added `compressor.memory_cap_mb` and a fallback path to reservoir sketches. Benchmarks added (see compressor_test). The cap is 256MB by default for hosted use and configurable via helm.

Summary: This PR introduces a shift imbalance detector and an "autoworkflow" hinting system for on-call planners. The detector analyzes rotation history, alert load, incident severity, and response latency to compute a per-rotator fairness score and an overall imbalance metric. When imbalance exceeds configurable thresholds the system surfaces automated hints (suggested swap candidates, temporary lightening of pager duty, and a prefilled Linear task with recommended actions).

Motivation: teams have asked for measurable, actionable signals to reduce responder burnout and uneven duty distribution (ENG-1987). Current dashboards show raw counts but give no prescriptive guidance. This work aims to: 1) surface when imbalance is material, 2) explain which contributors and shifts cause the signal, and 3) recommend safe, low-friction remediation steps that ops owners can apply.

Design highlights:
- Fairness scoring: combines normalized incident counts, weighted severity, average response time, and recent on-call hours. We apply exponential recency weighting to prioritize recent load and cap individual incident contribution to prevent outliers from skewing scoring.
- Privacy/opt-in: per-org setting. By default the detector runs in "suggestions-only" mode (no emails, no automated reassignment). Teams can enable a "planner-assist" toggle to get prefilled Linear tasks and calendar invites.
- Autoworkflow hints: generated hints include (a) swap suggestions with minimal overlap in on-call availability, (b) suggested temporary relief windows (paired with reduced routing rules), and (c) canned Linear tasks with summary, risk assessment, and next steps. Hints include a confidence score and the top three data points driving the suggestion.
- UX surface: small overlay in the on-call roster view with imbalance badge, a detail flyout that explains the score and a one-click "Create assist task" button that opens a prefilled Linear draft. Also added a CLI for infra and SRE teams to run scans and export CSVs for audits.

Implementation details:
- New modules: src/analysis/imbalance/ (detector, scoring, tests), src/ui/overlays/imbalance_badge.* (React overlay + styles), cli/imbalance_scan (small Go CLI wrapper), integrations/linear/prefill (templating layer), telemetry/metrics (new imbalance.histogram and hint_generated counters).
- Data sources: alert ingestion (slo-toolkit-alerts), rotation logs, PagerDuty webhook samples (sanitized), and response time traces (from tracing-store). We added a limited, cached view for raw events to avoid heavy queries on large orgs.
- Algorithms: implemented a tunable scoring pipeline with configurable weights; default weights chosen after running the detector on historical data from 8 pilot teams.

Ship plan: staged rollout. Feature is behind a feature flag (feature.imbalance_detector). Pilot enabled for three internal teams for two weeks, then opt-in beta for customers.

Backwards compatibility: UI additions are additive. CLI and telemetry are opt-in. No schema changes to existing rotation or alert tables.

Testing: unit tests covering scoring heuristics and edge cases, integration tests simulating a rotation with synthetic incidents, e2e smoke test for the overlay.

Performance: detector run (full org, 5k people, 90 day window) completes in ~11s on staging batch job (within target <20s).

Safety and audit: all generated hints are stored as audit artifacts; we added a redact pipeline for any personally-identifying text included in prefilled tasks.

Rollout checklist included in the PR body.

Related: builds on prior alert fingerprinting work (ENG-1204) to reduce double-counting similar incidents.

Known limitations and future work:
- Current scoring does not fully account for multi-team on-call overlaps; we'll add cross-rotation normalization in a follow-up (ENG-2042).
- We do not auto-apply swaps; that remains manual to prevent accidental coverage gaps.
- The initial UI is intentionally lightweight; more advanced scheduling suggestions will follow.
Daniel Kim (2026-02-21): Good direction. Please add a short note describing how exponential recency weighting is parametrized so operators can tune it. Also request a perf test for 10k people orgs.
Priya Kapoor (2026-02-21): Added tuning doc and added a perf job in CI that runs a reduced synthetic load for 10k people. See commit b2d4e6f.
Nina Flores (2026-02-22): Minor UX nit — the badge color should respect high-contrast mode and not rely solely on color. Please add an icon fallback.
Priya Kapoor (2026-02-22): Addressed; added icon and persisted color token. See commit c3f5a7b.
Marcus Li (2026-02-23): Suggest we add a maximum per-rotator cap and document the rationale in scoring docs to prevent aggressive rebalancing in small teams.
Priya Kapoor (2026-02-23): Implemented cap of 4 incidents/month contribution and updated docs. Tests added to assert cap behavior.
Daniel Kim (2026-02-24): CI passed on rerun, approving for canary.
Approval: LGTM (ready to merge after canary monitoring).
Merged by squash on 2026-02-25 by Priya Kapoor. Commit message consolidated the detector, CLI, UI, and integration work. Merge method: squash and merge. Post-merge actions: feature flag disabled by default; pilot toggles enabled for three internal teams; rollout notes posted to #oncall-ops.

Introduce probabilistic handoff scorer (opt-in) and a compact telemetry snapshot format (TSF) for faster on-call context loads; add handoff-eval CLI for simulating shift transitions; compatibility glue for incident-bot runbook suggestions; canary rollout and metrics to track triage latency and false-positive handoffs.
Context and motivation: Oncall handoffs are a repeated source of cognitive load; responders often lack a compact, prioritized signal summarizing the last-decade (recent) activity and what changed during a shift. This PR adds two coordinated features: a probabilistic handoff scorer that ranks recent signals by likely relevance to the incoming responder, and a compact Telemetry Snapshot Format (TSF) to make handoff payloads small and fast to fetch.

High level changes and motivation: The scorer combines signal-level features (alert frequency, recent error rate deltas, SLO breach proximity, owner activity, recent playbook attachments) with a lightweight probabilistic model that outputs an ordered list of handoff candidates and a calibrated confidence score. TSF is a newline-delimited, gzip-friendly binary-compatible format that stores pre-aggregated counters, short traces and a tiny call-tree summary so the UI and incident-bot can present prioritized context in <150ms for typical accounts.

Commits (summary):
- initial: add scorer prototype and model weight schema (hand_off/scorer.py, hand_off/weights_v1.yaml)
- add: TSF serializer + deserializer (tsf/serializers.py, tsf/spec.md)
- add: CLI 'handoff-eval' and benchmark harness (cli/handoff-eval.py, benches/handshake_bench.py)
- tests: unit and integration tests for scorer and TSF (tests/test_scorer.py, tests/test_tsf_integration.py)
- docs: oncall handbook and rollout notes (docs/oncall/handoff.md)
- infra: helm values for feature flag and canary (charts/slo-toolkit-values.yaml)

Changed areas (high level):
- slo_toolkit/hand_off/scorer.py  -- core algorithm, probability calibration and mode toggles
- slo_toolkit/tsf/serializers.py  -- TSF writer/reader and size heuristics
- cli/handoff-eval.py  -- local simulation tool for shift transitions and A/B comparisons
- docs/oncall/handoff.md  -- operator guide and emergency rollback instructions
- tests/*  -- new unit and integration tests to validate edge cases
- charts/slo-toolkit-values.yaml  -- feature flag and canary rollout parameters

Backward compatibility and rollout: The scorer is behind a feature flag (slo.handoff.scorer.enabled) and TSF is opt-in for clients; incident-bot will negotiate TSF support during handshake. Default remains the existing JSON snapshot to avoid breaking older clients. Canary rollout plan included: 5% -> 25% -> 100% in three stages with automatic rollback on triage-latency regression >10% or increase in manual handoffs.

Performance and bench numbers: Microbenchmarks on staging telemetry (mixed prod traces sampled) show: median handoff snapshot deserialize time 18ms (vs 72ms with current JSON), end-to-end handoff load for UI reduced from 160ms to 48ms, and simulated triage time (closed-loop with handoff-eval) improved by ~3.6x for low-signal incidents where context fetch was previously dominant. Memory and CPU overhead are within acceptable limits: scorer inference ~0.6ms/request on a small worker; TSF serialization adds ~4KB per snapshot on median workloads.

Review conversation (abridged, chronological):
- Liam O'Connor (reviewer): "Great direction. Two asks before approving: (1) show reproducibility steps for the weight schema and how weights are updated in prod, (2) add an explicit privacy doc: what PII could be included in TSF and how it's sanitized/encrypted."
- Maya Chen (author): "Added weights_v1.yaml and a small 'weights-repro' script in benches/ that deterministically replays the training seed; added TSF privacy section in docs/oncall/handoff.md and enforced PII scrub in tsf/serializers.py. PTAL."
- Sofia Martinez (reviewer): "Please add unit test for empty-signal edge case and a test where owner metadata is missing — we had a flake in a similar PR previously." 
- Maya Chen: "Added tests/test_scorer.py::test_empty_and_missing_owner. Fixed a bug where missing owner caused NPE in the ranker; updated changelog." 
- Priya Nair (security reviewer): "Confirming encryption-at-rest for TSF when stored in object store and that the serializer doesn't leak raw traces. Let's add a runtime assertion in CI smoke that validates no trace payload >64KB escapes the TSF writer." 
- Maya Chen: "Added integration test to assert size and added S3 upload wrapper that sets SSE-KMS header when the feature flag is enabled. CI smoke added as a fast gating check."
- Liam O'Connor: "LGTM after CI passes; approving."

CI and gating: First CI run failed (unit test flake around missing-owner) — fixed in subsequent commit. Lint/format passed on second run; integration tests (synthetic telemetry) initially showed a size regression for a pathological trace; added a size-trimming heuristic to the serializer and re-ran integration tests. Final CI: all checks green (unit, integration, lint, bench smoke). ci_status: pass.

Security and safety checks: - TSF is opt-in; default snapshot unchanged. - PII scrub enforced with configurable scrub rules per-org. - Feature flag gating and canary rollout included; automated rollback hooks configured on SLO regressions.

Usage notes for operators: - To try locally: pip install -e . && python cli/handoff-eval.py --sample-size 100 --canary 0.05
- To enable for org: flip slo.handoff.scorer.enabled in chart values (see charts/slo-toolkit-values.yaml). - On incident-bot side, add 'supports_tsf' to client capabilities; handshake code added in incident-bot compat layer (separate PR to incident-bot will reference this one).

Open questions and follow-ups: - Weights lifecycle: plan to introduce auto-tuning in a follow-up PR (ENG-8421). - Incident-bot integration PR to add TSF compatibility is tracked separately and will be canaried alongside this change.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after approvals and all CI green. Canaries will run over the next 4 weeks as defined in rollout notes.

payload.body:
Context: As part of the status page transparency upgrades, we need component-level signals that are (a) consistent with our public component taxonomy and (b) actionable for on-call. This PR adds multi-window, multi-burn burn-rate alerts keyed by status component labels (component_id, region, capability) and routes pages to SRE on-call with direct links to the status page update runbook + per-component dashboards. Motivation: Recent incidents showed we were slow to declare partial impact (e.g., Streaming only, or us-east only) because our paging was still too service-oriented (gateway/scheduler) and didn’t map cleanly to the customer-facing component list. These alerts are intended to improve time-to-detection + reduce comms ambiguity by making the component/region impacted explicit from the first page. What’s included: 1) New alert rule groups for the public status components (Hosted API, Streaming, Embeddings, Reranking, Console) with region scoping for us-east, us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast where metrics exist today; 2) Standard labels on alerts: component_id, region, capability, severity, and runbook; 3) Pager routing: page SRE on-call for Sev1/Sev0 burn (fast burn), and ticket/notify for slower burns; 4) Runbook links and dashboard annotations embedded into alert annotations, pointing to the status-page update runbook and component health dashboards; 5) Guardrails: basic anti-noise defaults (minimum traffic / request volume gate) to avoid paging on low-QPS components and staging. Thresholds: Uses standard multi-window burn-rate approach; initial defaults are tuned to mirror existing product SLO burn semantics but applied per-component. Fast burn: 5m/1h window, page. Slow burn: 30m/6h window, notify. Notes/assumptions: This PR assumes upstream instrumentation is (or will soon be) labeling request metrics with component_id/region/capability; where labels are missing today, the alert rules are present but disabled behind a feature flag until the observability pack lands. Rollout: Start with Hosted API + Streaming for us-east/us-west enabled; keep other components/regions disabled pending label coverage audit. Validation: Ran rules against last 7d in prod Prometheus; verified we would have paged correctly for the 2025-11-07 us-east streaming degradation without increasing page volume on normal days. Screenshots/links are in the internal thread referenced below.
Example rule (simplified): alert: StatusComponentBurnRateFast expr: (burn_rate_5m{component_id!="", env="prod"} > 14.4) and (burn_rate_1h{component_id!="", env="prod"} > 6) and (requests_5m{env="prod"} > 500) for: 2m labels: severity: "page" team: "sre" component_id: "{{ $labels.component_id }}" region: "{{ $labels.region }}" capability: "{{ $labels.capability }}" annotations: summary: "High error budget burn for {{ $labels.component_id }} ({{ $labels.region }})" runbook: "https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/.../status-page-update-runbook" dashboard: "https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/..." statuspage_guidance: "If customer impact is confirmed, update the matching public component + region."
Rafael Mendes (SRE) - 2025-11-19: Can we ensure these don’t page when traffic is low (esp. ap-southeast overnight)? Also please confirm the annotation includes component_id/region so comms lead can copy/paste quickly.
Aisha Bello - 2025-11-19: Added request volume gate (requests_5m > 500) and restricted enablement to us-east/us-west initially. Annotations now include component_id + region + capability and direct links to the status page runbook + dashboard.
Allison Grant (Observability) - 2025-11-20: The label names need to match the taxonomy/schema work (component_id, region, capability). Also: can we avoid using internal service names in the alert name/summary?
Aisha Bello - 2025-11-20: Updated to component_id/region/capability everywhere; removed gateway/scheduler references from summaries. Alert names are now StatusComponentBurnRateFast/Slow and the summary is strictly customer-facing component naming.
Christine Wong - 2025-11-20: For the runbook link, please point to the status-page update runbook and add a sentence reminding folks to validate impact before marking degraded. Also: where do we flip enablement flags?
Aisha Bello - 2025-11-20: Done. Flags live in alerts/config/status_components_rollout.yaml; documented in README. Added guidance annotation: 'Validate impact using dashboard link before posting public update.'
Miles Thornton - 2025-11-21: +1. One more request: add a distinct route for 'severity: page' to ensure it hits SRE on-call and doesn’t go to the generic observability channel.
Aisha Bello - 2025-11-21: Added routing policy status_component_paging.yaml mapping severity=page -> PagerDuty service 'sre-oncall' with dedup key including component_id+region.
Enablement is gated per component/region in alerts/config/status_components_rollout.yaml. Initial default in this PR: enable Hosted API + Streaming for us-east/us-west only; all other components/regions disabled pending label coverage audit. After merge, SRE will flip flags via a follow-up config-only PR once metrics label coverage reaches >95% for that component/region.
Internal: Added component/region burn-rate alerts aligned to public status components; pages SRE on-call for fast-burn conditions and includes status page runbook + dashboard links in alert annotations.

payload.body:
Motivation: during on-call handoffs and service restarts we observe noisy, low-signal telemetry and frequent failed snapshot uploads because collectors are still warming. This causes alert noise and gaps in post-incident diagnostics. This PR introduces a lightweight deferred telemetry proxy and coldstart guard for on-call snapshotting to reduce noise and ensure reliable diagnostics. Key behaviors: 1) a telemetry proxy component that temporarily buffers non-critical telemetry exports and replays them after instrument warm-up thresholds are met; 2) on-call coldstart guard for incident snapshotting that defers snapshot attachments for a configurable TTL while periodically probing collectors and sanitizers; 3) idempotent snapshot reattach flow with exponential backoff and metadata-based deduplication to avoid duplicate artifacts; 4) safety and RBAC checks so only authorized on-call roles can request forced immediate snapshots; 5) a small SDK helper (slo-toolkit/collector/warmup) used by incident-bot to signal readiness; 6) docs and migration notes. Implementation notes: the proxy is a process-level sidecar with a tiny in-memory ring buffer and optional persistent queue backing (filesystem) for environments with longer warmups. The warm-up heuristic uses event rate, successful export percentage, and collector health pings. The snapshot deferral workflow attaches a short-lived placeholder to incidents and attempts up to N retry cycles to attach the full artifact. Placeholders are sanitized and marked with provenance. Rollout plan: default behavior off; opt-in via config flag in console and env var SLO_TOOLKIT_DEFERRED_PROXY=1 for private deployments. Includes feature gating, telemetry metrics to monitor deferred message counts and replay success rate, and an emergency bypass for PagerDuty-triggered forced snapshots. Why this is different from previous work: existing PRs suggest auto-runbook and snapshot exporters focused on enrichment; this one specifically targets the coldstart window and failed snapshot attachment surface area with a deferred-retry-first design to reduce noise and increase diagnostic fidelity. Migration & compatibility: backward compatible with current incident attachments and incident-bot hooks; integration tests added to the sim harness to validate failover and reattach scenarios. Rollout recommendation: enable in a small set of teams for 2 weeks and watch deferred_replay_success_rate and oncall_noise_rate. Links: linear ENG-3345 (collector warmup heuristics), ENG-3441 (incident artifact reliability).
Aisha Patel: Overall this looks useful for reducing noise. Two asks: add a metric to count placeholder attachments and ensure the placeholder metadata includes a warmup snapshot ID so we can trace reattach attempts.||Tara Chen: Added placeholder metadata and metric 'deferred_placeholder_count'. Also updated docs with guidance on interpreting the metric.
Marco Nguyen: The persistent queue option is necessary for some private deployments; can we make the backlog path configurable and document retention? Also add a health endpoint for the sidecar.||Tara Chen: Made backlog path configurable via TELEMETRY_PROXY_BACKLOG_PATH; added /healthz and exported backlog_size gauge.
Ben Holt: Tests flaky on CI: attach retry test failed once due to timing. Please move to deterministic mocks for probe success and extend default timeout.||Tara Chen: Switched tests to use deterministic probe stubs and extended the harness timeout by 30s; CI run passed.
Add deferred telemetry proxy with coldstart guard to reduce on-call noise and improve reliability of incident snapshot attachments. Feature is off by default; enable via config. Includes metrics 'deferred_replay_success_rate' and 'deferred_placeholder_count' and RBAC for forced snapshot bypass.
payload.title: deferred telemetry proxy and on-call coldstart guard
