payload.body:
Context
We’re standardizing audit event schema v1 across Hosted/Dedicated/Private and expanding supported SIEM export targets. This PR adds an Azure Sentinel / Log Analytics sink to audit-log-exporter using the Azure Monitor Logs Ingestion API (DCE + DCR) and includes configuration examples for Private deployments.

Why
- Multiple enterprise/security reviews (and SUP-18477) requested first-class Sentinel support.
- Private customers want a supported path that doesn’t rely on “roll your own” forwarders.
- We need consistent payload validation + schema_version tagging before exporting to third-party systems (ties to ENG-4827).

What’s in this PR
1) New sink: azure_sentinel
- Adds a new output target: type=azure_sentinel
- Uses Azure AD OAuth2 client credentials to obtain an access token.
- Posts batches to Azure Monitor Logs Ingestion endpoint (DCE) for a configured Data Collection Rule (DCR) + stream.
- Defaults to emitting JSON as-is (after v1 normalization) and relies on DCR transformation to map into a custom table, with guidance on recommended column mapping.

2) Request shaping + delivery semantics
- Batching:
  - Max events per request: configurable (default 500)
  - Max payload bytes: configurable (default 900KB to stay under typical proxy limits; Azure supports larger, but we keep headroom)
- Retries:
  - Retry on 429/5xx and network errors
  - Exponential backoff with jitter
  - Honors Retry-After when present
- Idempotency guidance:
  - Azure ingestion API doesn’t provide a built-in idempotency key.
  - We include event_id and recommend downstream de-dupe by (event_id, tenant_id) (ties to SUP-18510).

3) Validation + redaction
- Reuses existing schema_version tagging and v1 normalization pipeline.
- Ensures we do not log exporter secrets (client_secret, shared keys) and masks token values in debug logs.
- Adds a small allow-list for high-cardinality fields in exporter metrics to avoid cardinality explosions.

4) Private deployment documentation/examples
- Adds docs snippets for:
  - Helm values.yaml configuration
  - Environment variable configuration
  - Example Kubernetes Secret manifest
  - Troubleshooting checklist (401/403, 429 throttling, DCR mismatch)
- Notes on Azure prerequisites:
  - DCE endpoint URL
  - DCR immutable ID
  - Stream name
  - Service principal credentials (tenant_id, client_id, client_secret)
  - Required permissions (scope to the DCR/DCE resource per Azure guidance)

Example configuration (Helm values)
exporter:
  sinks:
    - type: azure_sentinel
      name: sentinel-prod
      enabled: true
      azure:
        tenant_id: ${AZURE_TENANT_ID}
        client_id: ${AZURE_CLIENT_ID}
        client_secret: ${AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET}
        dce_endpoint: https://<dce-name>.<region>.ingest.monitor.azure.com
        dcr_immutable_id: dcr-00000000000000000000000000000000
        stream_name: Custom-RedwoodAuditV1
      batching:
        max_events: 500
        max_bytes: 900000
        flush_interval_ms: 1000
      retry:
        max_attempts: 12
        base_backoff_ms: 250
        max_backoff_ms: 30000

Implementation notes
- New package: sinks/azure_sentinel
  - token provider with caching (refreshes before expiry)
  - ingestion client with typed errors and retry classification
- Adds exporter metrics:
  - exporter_sink_requests_total{sink="azure_sentinel",status="success|fail"}
  - exporter_sink_request_latency_ms_bucket{sink="azure_sentinel"}
  - exporter_sink_dropped_events_total{sink="azure_sentinel",reason="oversize|validation|permanent_error"}
- Adds unit tests:
  - token caching + refresh logic
  - Retry-After handling
  - payload size capping behavior
  - redaction/masking in logs
- Adds an opt-in integration test (skipped by default) that can be run in CI with Azure credentials (documented in CONTRIBUTING).

Files/areas changed (high level)
- src/sinks/azure_sentinel/* (new)
- src/config/* (new sink config schema + validation)
- src/pipeline/* (wiring sink into existing normalization/validation flow)
- docs/sinks/azure_sentinel.md (new)
- deploy/private/examples/azure-sentinel-values.yaml (new)
- deploy/private/examples/azure-sentinel-secret.yaml (new)
- CONTRIBUTING.md (integration test instructions)

Review discussion highlights
- Hanae: requested explicit masking of client_secret and access tokens in logs; added logger scrubber + tests.
- Allison: asked to keep metrics labels low-cardinality; removed per-stream labels and kept sink-level only.
- Sean: requested clearer behavior when Azure endpoint is down; updated sink to classify failures and avoid hot loops; added runbook notes in docs.
- Nadia: asked to confirm schema_version is included and that we don’t mutate reserved fields; confirmed normalization happens before sink and added a regression test verifying schema_version propagation.
- Amina: requested Private examples include Kubernetes Secret + note on rotating credentials; added both.

CI
- build: pass
- unit tests: pass
- lint: pass
- gosec/staticcheck: pass
- integration tests: skipped (requires Azure creds)

Rollout plan
- Ship behind config (new sink type only becomes active when configured).
- Early validation with one Private customer environment via Solutions Eng (tracked in ENG-4836).
- Follow-up: add Terraform snippet for DCR/DCE provisioning in docs (separate PR to keep this focused).

Merge
Squash merged to main.
- New exporter sink: Azure Sentinel / Log Analytics (Azure Monitor Logs Ingestion API)
- Supports OAuth2 client credentials auth, DCR/DCE configuration, batching and retries
- Adds Private deployment configuration examples (Helm values + env vars) and troubleshooting notes
Allison Grant (review): Can we avoid putting stream_name into metrics labels? It’ll be high-cardinality across tenants.
Kevin Osei (author): Good catch — removed stream_name label and kept sink name only. Added a guard in metrics helper to prevent accidental label additions.
Hanae Suzuki (review): Please ensure client_secret and access tokens never appear in logs, including debug. Also check error wrapping doesn’t include headers.
Kevin Osei (author): Added explicit scrubbing for known secret fields and ensured auth headers aren’t logged. Added unit test that asserts log output doesn’t contain token substrings.
Sean Gallagher (review): What happens during a sustained 429? Make sure we honor Retry-After and don’t build unbounded memory.
Kevin Osei (author): Implemented Retry-After support, capped in-memory queue by max_pending_events (default 50k), and will drop with metric + warn once per minute if exceeded.
Amina Yusuf (review): The Private example should include a Secret manifest and a note on rotation.
Kevin Osei (author): Added deploy/private/examples/azure-sentinel-secret.yaml and documented rotation procedure + recommended secret store integration.

payload.body:
Motivation: Production incidents showed repeated reopen flapping when a regional circuit briefly recovered; this caused rapid request spill and destabilized downstream nodes. We need a short-term stabilizer that dampens reopen events by applying a windowed reopen allowance and an aggressive short-term load-trim to prevent overshoot while preserving SLOs for high-priority routes.

Summary: Implement a preventive fallback stabilizer that: 1) tracks per-region reopen events in a sliding window and prevents reopen attempts if reopen rate exceeds a threshold; 2) introduces a temporary, rapidly-decaying load-trim that reduces admitted requests for non-critical tenants/routes for the first 30s after a reopen; 3) emits detailed metrics and audit logs for each suppressed reopen and trimmed route to aid post-incident analysis; 4) exposes two knobs in the runtime config (window_size_secs, reopen_rate_threshold_pct) and a feature flag for staged rollout.

What changed (high level): added stabilizer component to runtime/circuit, integrated with the SLO enforcer to coordinate prioritized trimming, added region probe hysteresis to avoid premature reopen signals, surfaced metrics and traces to observability, and added unit + integration tests covering edge cases.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4132)
- [x] Feature flag gated and defaulted off in config
- [x] Unit tests for reopen window logic
- [x] Integration test simulating rapid reopen cycles
- [x] Metrics dashboards updated (temporary)
- [x] Rollout plan included in PR description

Rollout plan: feature flag disabled by default. Canary rollout to a single low-risk region for 24h with increased sampling. If metrics show reduced reopen churn and stable high-priority SLOs, progressively enable for additional regions in 6-hour increments. If regressions appear, flip feature flag off and failover to previous behavior.

Testing: CI runs unit + integration suites. Manual chaos test performed on staging by inducing rapid circuit toggles; observed reduced reopen attempts, and trimmed load prevented downstream saturation. Load-trim decay verified (linear decay from 60% trim at t=0 to 0% at t=30s).

Rollback: revert flag and configuration; code instrumentation includes a short-circuit that restores previous behavior without a restart when feature flag is toggled.

Notes: This is intentionally conservative and focused on behavior stabilization, not permanent policy changes. Follow-up PR will evaluate longer-term heuristics and telemetry-driven automatic thresholds (ENG-4150).
Diego Morales: The reopen window default of 60s might be too long for low-latency services. Can we make the window configurable per tier?
Anika Patel: Responded: Good point — added tiered override support in the config (per-priority overrides) and updated tests to exercise the overrides.
Jin Park: Suggest adding a metric that records when the load-trim prevented an Admit to correlate with downstream saturation incidents.
Anika Patel: Responded: Added trimmed_route_count and included trace ids in the audit log so operators can reconstruct the decision path.
Lena Fischer: Integration test looks good but flaky on first run; observed a race in the probe hysteresis timer. Please add a deterministic clock in tests.
Anika Patel: Responded: Switched the integration test to use a fake clock and reran — flake resolved. CI rerun confirmed stability.
Diego Morales: Approving after the tiered config change and adding a short note in the runbook about destructive testing limits.
Jin Park: Approved — good safeguards and observability.
- Hotfix: add a preventive fallback stabilizer to reduce reopen flapping and prevent downstream saturation
- New runtime knobs: window_size_secs, reopen_rate_threshold_pct, per-priority overrides
- New metrics: reopen_suppressed_count, trimmed_route_count
- Feature is feature-flagged and disabled by default; follow the canary checklist in docs/operational/reopen-stabilizer.md
payload.title: Preventive fallback stabilizer: windowed reopen and load trim hotfix

payload.body:
Motivation: On-call queues accumulate runbooks and playbooks with varying usefulness over time. When multiple responders act concurrently, noisy low-value runbooks surface first and important but less-frequent playbooks are delayed. This change introduces a prioritized runbook queue that ranks candidate runbooks by a decaying relevance score, supports per-responder snooze windows, and exposes metrics and config for safe rollout.

What this PR does: 1) Implements a RunbookScorer service that computes a composite score from incident signal (severity, error-class frequency), recent successful mitigations, runbook age, and team-defined priority tags. Scores decay over time using an exponential half-life configurable per team. 2) Adds a prioritized queue layer to the incident-bot dispatcher that returns top-N runbooks for a responder instead of FIFO. 3) Adds responder-level snooze: when a responder marks a runbook as "snoozed" it is hidden for that user for a configurable backoff (defaults: 30m/2h/24h tiers). 4) Safe requeueing: runbooks that are requeued by agents get a temporary suppression boost if they repeatedly trigger for the same incident to avoid flapping. 5) Observability: Prometheus metrics (runbook_queue_size, avg_top_score, snooze_events_total, rescore_latency_seconds) and an OpenTelemetry trace span around scoring and dispatch. 6) Admin UI flags and feature-gates for gradual rollout (global, team-level, and user opt-out).

Checklist: - [x] Core scorer implementation and unit tests - [x] Prioritized queue integration and E2E smoke test against local emulated dispatcher - [x] Responder snooze UI endpoint + backend handling - [x] Metrics and tracing hooks - [x] Linear links and config knobs - [x] Feature gate + rollout plan - [x] Docs PR (linked)

Rollout plan: Stage 1 (canary): enable for internal oncall with runbook sampling, observe top-score distribution and alert on sudden queue-length regressions. Stage 2: enable team-by-team via console flag for teams that opt-in. Stage 3: wide rollout with 7-day monitoring window and automatic rollback on SLO regressions.

Compatibility and fallback: If RunbookScorer fails or times out (>=250ms default), dispatcher reverts to FIFO and emits a metric runbook_score_failures_total. Feature is entirely opt-in via flags.

Notes: Tuning guidance included in the README. Linear tasks ENG-3121 and ENG-3178 capture follow-ups: telemetry dashboards and an A/B test to measure mean time to mitigation (MTTM) with prioritized ordering.
Marcus Nguyen (reviewer): Please add a unit test for the half-life decay math and a deterministic clock so results are stable in CI.

Aria Patel (author): Added scorer_test.go with mocked clock and parameterized half-life cases.

Evelyn Carter (reviewer): Two nits: 1) the default snooze tiers should be documented in config defaults; 2) prefer metrics namespace 'incidentbot_' for Prometheus to align with existing collectors.

Aria Patel: Updated values.incident-bot.yaml to include the snooze tier defaults and renamed metrics to incidentbot_runbook_* . Also added a short section in docs/runbook-priority.md.

Diego Ramos (reviewer): Suggest adding a safe guard so a maliciously crafted runbook cannot starve others by returning extremely high static score. Could we clamp scores per-runbook?

Aria Patel: Implemented a clamp in scorer.go (min 0, max 10000) and added a unit test. Also added a warning log when an outlier is detected to aid future debugging.

CI: First run had a flaky e2e failure on the smoke test due to timing; test hardened with retry. Final CI run: all checks green.

Merge: Squash-merged after approvals from Marcus and Evelyn. Post-merge: feature flagged off by default in main values.

Follow-ups recorded in ENG-3121 and ENG-3178 for dashboard and A/B test instrumentation.
Add prioritized runbook dispatch with configurable decay scoring and responder snooze. Feature gated; metrics and tracing included. Admins can enable per-team via feature flag. See docs/runbook-priority.md for tuning guidance.
Default config keeps feature disabled. If enabling, monitor runbook_queue_size and mean top-score. Roll back by disabling the feature flag if queue length or MTTM regresses beyond configured thresholds.
payload.title: prioritized-runbook-queue-with-decay-and-responder-snooze

payload.body:
Context: As part of the tiered SLO + error budget program, we’re standardizing burn-rate alerting and enforcement. Today the burn-rate alerts page the on-call, but triage is still slow because the initial signal doesn’t include (a) how fast we’re burning, (b) what’s driving it (latency vs errors vs streaming disconnects), or (c) where to go next (dashboards/runbooks). This PR updates incident-bot to listen for burn-rate alert notifications and post a structured “burn summary” message into #eng-sre (and thread replies for updates), including deep links to the tiered SLO dashboards and the active mitigation runbook.

What this does: 1) Adds a new alert type handler for error budget burn-rate alerts (Prometheus Alertmanager payloads via our existing webhook). 2) Builds a canonical Slack message format: header with SLO name + tier + region, a short diagnosis (burn rate + window + budget remaining), and a set of links (Grafana dashboard, logs/traces, runbook). 3) Adds a lightweight “top contributors” section when the alert includes a `route` or `endpoint_class` label (to avoid cardinality explosion we only surface what’s already in the alert labels). 4) Dedupe/ratelimit: repeated firings for the same SLO/tier/region within 15 minutes update an existing thread instead of spamming the channel. 5) Safety: scrub potentially sensitive labels (customer/account identifiers) and only allow a safe-label allowlist to render in Slack.

Message contents (example): - Title: “Error budget burning: hosted / us-east-1 / chat.completions (p95 latency)” - Summary line: “Burn rate: 6.2x (2h window), budget remaining (30d): 62% → projected exhaustion in ~4.8d if sustained.” - Links: “Tiered SLO dashboard”, “Regional comparison”, “Runbook: error budget breach mitigation”, “Incident process (when to declare)”. - Footer: build/version and alert fingerprint.

Config: - Adds `BURN_SUMMARY_CHANNEL` (default #eng-sre in prod) and `BURN_SUMMARY_ENABLED` feature flag (default false). - Adds `GRAFANA_BASE_URL` and `GRAFANA_DASHBOARD_UID_TIERED_SLO` for generating direct links with pre-filled variables (tier/region/endpoint_class). - Adds `RUNBOOK_URL_ERROR_BUDGET_BREACH` to keep the link stable as Confluence pages move.

Rollout plan: - Stage: enable in warn-only mode (`BURN_SUMMARY_ENABLED=true`, channel #eng-sre-sandbox) for 1 week; validate formatting + dedupe behavior. - Prod: enable to #eng-sre after signoff from SRE on-call and CS escalation owners. - Follow-up: once stable, add an @-mention for the correct rotation based on tier (Dedicated vs Hosted) and severity mapping.

Out of scope: - Computing burn-rate itself (handled by recording rules + alerts in redwood/observability-pack). - Any new per-customer metrics; we explicitly avoid printing customer/account identifiers.

Refs: - Related alerting work: redwood/pr-28492-add-burn-rate-alerting-queries-and-recording-rules.json - Related dashboards: observability-pack/pr-6312-tiered-slo-dashboards-and-annotations.json - Runbook: confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/error-budget-breach-mitigation-runbook.json
Aisha Bello (review): Love the direction. Please make sure we don’t surface any customer identifiers in the Slack message. Some alerts include `account_id`/`customer` labels from downstream exporters; we should scrub by default and only allowlist known-safe labels (tier, region, endpoint_class, slo, window).
Sergio Costa (author): Agreed. Added `internal/sanitize/labels.go` with an explicit allowlist and a denylist of common sensitive keys. Message builder now renders only allowlisted labels; everything else is dropped. Added tests for `account_id`, `customer`, and `org` variants.
Rafael Mendes (review): Can we ensure dedupe doesn’t hide state transitions? If the alert goes from warning → critical, we should post an update (thread reply) with the new severity + updated burn rate.
Sergio Costa (author): Yep. Dedupe key includes `(slo, tier, region, indicator)` but we treat severity change as an update condition and post a thread reply even within the 15m TTL. Added test coverage for severity transition.
Logan Wright (review): Link generation: please use dashboard variables rather than hard-coded query params that might change. Also avoid putting raw route names into URLs if they can be high-cardinality.
Sergio Costa (author): Updated to use Grafana dashboard variables only (`var-tier`, `var-region`, `var-endpoint_class`). Dropped `route` from URL generation entirely; if route exists we only show it in the message when it’s already in the alert labels and passes allowlist (currently it does not).
Aisha Bello (review): One more thing: the runbook link should be a config value, not hard-coded. Confluence URLs tend to move.
Sergio Costa (author): Done: `RUNBOOK_URL_ERROR_BUDGET_BREACH`. README updated with expected values for stage/prod.
Rafael Mendes (approval): Looks good. This should materially speed up triage. Approving with staged rollout per plan.
Logan Wright (approval): Approved. Thanks for keeping the label hygiene tight.
payload.title: Post error budget burn summaries to #eng-sre on burn-rate alerts (dashboards + runbook links)

Motivation: In production serving workloads we observe periodic spillover storms and long-tail latencies caused by uneven slot occupancy and synchronous global compaction. This PR implements a shard-aware "shard stabilizer" that performs targeted slab compaction inside noisy cache shards, a responsive spillback controller that applies backpressure to upstream schedulers to avoid simultaneous tenant-wide spills, and an eviction pacing mechanism that smooths reclamation to reduce allocation churn. Design summary: 1) Shard scoring: per-shard fragmentation and occupancy metrics are collected with low overhead and scored using an occupancy-entropy heuristic. 2) Targeted compaction: compaction operates on a bounded window per-shard and uses a cooperative yield model so it never blocks runtime threads. 3) Spillback controller: a token-bucket style controller with hysteresis signals upstream request routers; when a shard approaches its reservation threshold the controller issues graded spillback triggers with a cooldown. 4) Eviction pacing: eviction requests are rate-limited per-shard based on recent latency and spillback state to avoid heavy tail latency spikes. Migration plan and rollout: feature guarded behind runtime flag "kv_shard_stabilizer" defaulting to off. Rollout strategy: canary on Dedicated, enable for a small tenant cohort, monitor surface metrics, then flip cluster-wide. Tests and validation: unit tests for scoring and state transitions, integration stress tests with synthetic hotspot workloads, perf harness runs showing reduced tail latency and lower page churn. Observability: added per-shard metrics: shard_frag_score, shard_compactions_done, shard_eviction_rate, spillback_signal_rate. Runtime knobs: compaction_budget_ms, spillback_threshold_pct, eviction_pace_qps. Backwards compatibility: no changes to public APIs or on-disk formats. Related work: references ENG-4127 for long-tail investigation and ENG-4199 for spillback design doc. Checklist: ensure feature flag, add docs, add SLO dashboards, run canary baseline. CI: all checks green except an initial flaky integration job that was re-run and passed. Everything green before merge.
Improves KV cache fragmentation resilience by introducing shard-aware compaction, and reduces spillover storms via a spillback controller. No API changes. Performance: 12-28% reduction in tail latency under mixed workloads and 18% lower memory churn.
Ethan Morales (reviewer): Looks good overall. Two concerns: 1) compaction_worker uses sleeping loops; can we use the runtime's cooperative scheduler to avoid dedicated sleeps? 2) Need clearer invariants for spillback cooldown to avoid oscillation.
Author (Priya): Addressed both. Reworked compaction worker to yield to the runtime scheduler and replaced fixed sleeps with backoff-based yields. Added explicit cooldown windows in spillback_controller and a unit test to assert no oscillation under synthetic load.
Sara Kim (reviewer): Can we get a perf run comparing before/after under mixed LLM tokenization workloads? Requesting numbers in PR body.
Author: Added results from perf harness: 95th latency reduced by 12%-28% across three workload profiles; memory churn (allocation/deallocation ops) down 18% on average. Figures added to release_notes.
Luca Romano (approver): Verified metrics on canary cluster. Observed fewer simultaneous spills and smoother eviction rates. Approved.
CI Bot: integration-tests flaky on first run, re-run succeeded.
Release lead (comment): Set feature flag off by default. Will coordinate canary on Dedicated on 2026-03-03.
payload.title: shard stabilizer: targeted slab compaction, responsive spillback controller, and eviction pacing

Context and motivation: On-call handoffs at Redwood often require manual status announcements and temporary muting of noisy alerts. This PR introduces a lightweight handoff timer (reminders at preconfigured intervals) and a "silence windows" feature that allows the on-call engineer to quickly suppress non-actionable alerts for a bounded period. The silence windows are SLO-aware: the bot consults SLO slackness from slo-toolkit and prevents auto-mute if doing so would risk violating tight SLO guardrails. Goal: reduce cognitive load during handoffs, make temporary alert muting explicit and auditable, and reduce pager fatigue while preserving SLO safety.

What this PR does (summary): - Adds a /hand-off command that starts a configurable timer and posts scheduled reminders (e.g., "handoff begins in 5m, 1m, now") to the incident channel. - Adds a /silence-window <duration> [reason] command to create a short-lived suppression for non-critical alerts; records metadata to audit log and emits an event to the observability channel. - Integrates with slo-toolkit to query current breach risk: if an SLO is within a configurable threshold (<5% error budget remaining), the bot will either block the silence or require an explicit override with a justification. - Persists silences in Redis with TTL and stores an audit entry in the incident-bot audit index. - Adds unit and integration tests around timing edge cases and SLO query failures (fallback: conservative deny).

Checklist: - [x] Design doc referenced (Linear ENG-7812) - [x] New commands implemented and documented in /help - [x] Basic RBAC: only users in oncall-role or SRE team can start handoff or silence - [x] Audit log entries for all creates/extends/cancels - [x] Tests added (unit + integration) - [x] E2E manual verification in staging done 2026-02-22

Commits: - 9 commits total (squashed for merge) - f3b7e8c: initial command handlers, argument parsing and permission check - 2a9d1b2: Redis persistence + TTL handling and cleanup - 7c8a4ff: slo-toolkit integration client + conservative fallback - 15d3a6e: audit index writer + schema migration - 3b1e9a0: tests for timer edgecases and race conditions - 4f0d2aa: UI message templates, localization keys - 9b6c4d1: docs and /help updates - a1f4b22: CI flake fixes - squash merge prepared commit: merge/final-89432

Files changed (high level): - cmd/handlers/handoff.go: new handler, timer scheduler and reminder helper - cmd/handlers/silence.go: command to create/extend/cancel silence windows - internal/slo/client.go: small wrapper around slo-toolkit HTTP API with basic caching - internal/audit/indexer.go: append-only audit entries with metadata - internal/persistence/redis_store.go: storage helpers for TTLed silences - web/docs/commands.md: help text and examples (added) - tests/*: unit and integration tests (new)

Small snippets included inside changed files to illustrate intent: - silence window audit entry shape (stored as redis JSON string): {"id":"...","created_by":"...","duration":"10m","reason":"handoff","slo_check":"ok"} - handoff reminder template: "Handoff timer: %s remaining. Please finalize commit messages, update runbook link."

Review conversation (high level): - Arjun Patel (reviewer): "I like the SLO-aware default. Two concerns: 1) what happens if slo-toolkit is unavailable? 2) can we tighten RBAC so only 'primary-oncall' can muting by default?" - Author reply (Maya): "Fallback path implemented: if slo-toolkit fails or times out we conservatively deny silence unless override flag is present and requires a justification that is stored in audit. RBAC updated to check primary-oncall or SRE role; added tests." - Fiona Gallagher: "nit: message text is a bit verbose in the channel; prefer single-line summary with a link to details." - Author reply: "Reworked templates to single-line with expand/collapse link to details (see web/docs/commands.md)." - Diego Ramos: "approve after test coverage for TTL expiry and race with extend/cancel." - Author: "Added integration tests for concurrent extend/cancel; CI passing locally."

CI/status: - Unit tests: pass - Integration tests: pass (postgres/redis staging emulators in pipeline) - Lint/format: pass - E2E smoke in staging: manual pass noted in PR body - Final CI run: pass

Merge strategy and outcome: - Requested rebase to keep history clean; final merge performed with squash merge by Arjun Patel on 2026-02-24. Merge commit: 0c9a8e2 - Release notes: "Added incident handoff timer and SLO-aware silence windows. Admins can configure thresholds and enable/disable the feature via incident-bot settings. See ENG-7812 for behavioral details."

Backward compatibility and safety: - Default behavior is off for orgs who haven't opted in; feature flag added: INCIDENT_HANDOFF_ENABLED=false by default. - Existing alerting and muting APIs remain unchanged. - Breaking change: none.

Operational notes and follow-ups: - Follow-up ticket ENG-7900: add telemetry counters for mute attempts vs allowed vs denied (to track misuse) - Follow-up ticket ENG-7901: dashboard for active silence windows and audit search - Ops runbook: short section added to runbooks/oncall.md describing how to override a blocked mute and where audit entries are stored.

If you want to test: 1) enable feature flag in staging 2) run /hand-off 10m 3) run /silence-window 15m "handoff" and observe audit index and SLO check logs.

Arjun: what if slo-toolkit times out?
Maya: fallback denies and allows explicit override with audit
Fiona: shorten bot messages; done
Diego: add TTL concurrency tests; added tests
Added incident handoff timer and SLO-aware silence windows. Feature disabled by default; admins can opt-in and configure SLO thresholds. Audit logs recorded for all muting actions.

Adds an opt-in CLI and internal API to export compact, anonymized ‘retrospective snippets’ for each oncall shift. Useful for quick postmortems, handoffs, and retrospective-summaries. Backwards compatible behind feature flag 'retrospective_snippets_v1'.
Motivation: Oncall handoffs and postmortems often need a compact, privacy-safe snapshot of what happened during a shift: key incidents, actions taken, outstanding items, and suggested follow-ups. Existing incident-bot artifacts are rich but large and require manual sanitization for broader sharing. This PR adds a new export path and lightweight CLI that produces anonymized, context-aware 'retrospective snippets' suitable for internal retros, incident timelines, or automated follow-up generators.

What this change does: Implements a compact export pipeline and CLI 'ibctl retrospective export' that: (1) aggregates incident references, alert summaries, and responder notes for a single shift window; (2) applies deterministic de-identification (email/domain redaction, tokenized user handles, IP truncation) and a configurable PII-safe whitelist; (3) ranks and trims entries by relevance using a simple TF-IDF score over a short context window so the export remains < 200KB by default; (4) emits exports as newline-delimited JSON (jsonl) and an optional markdown digest; (5) supports gzip compression and an S3-compatible upload target. The feature is gated behind the feature flag 'retrospective_snippets_v1' and respects RBAC (only users with 'oncall:export' scope can run it).

Design notes: Export format is intentionally minimal: each snippet entry contains shift_id, incident_refs, timestamp, snippet_text (redacted), tags, and a list of 'followups' synthesized from action items. We maintain a compact provenance header with request_id, tool_version, and anonymization rules applied. Redaction is tuned to err on the side of privacy: unrecognized tokens are replaced with stable pseudonyms (user_####) instead of heuristically trying to guess names.

CLI examples:
- Export a single shift to local file: ibctl retrospective export --shift 2026-02-08T18:00Z --out ./snippets.jsonl
- Upload and compress: ibctl retrospective export --shift 2026-02-08T18:00Z --out s3://company-oncall/snippets/shift-20260208.jsonl.gz --compress gzip --upload
- Dry run (no upload, show top 5 snippets): ibctl retrospective export --shift 2026-02-08T18:00Z --dry-run --limit 5

Privacy & safety: The export pipeline contains a deterministic redaction step plus a layered PII-checker that flags high-confidence PII for manual review instead of auto-including it. There's an admin toggle to include verbatim (unredacted) output for compliance/audit customers but that path requires additional KMS-backed approval. The default behavior for hosted runs is strict redaction.

Implementation summary: Changes touch the export pipeline, a new 'retrospect' subcommand, sanitization library additions, unit + e2e tests, and a short doc in the oncall guide. Key files added/modified are listed below. The core anonymizer lives in pkg/anonymize with a deterministic pseudonymizer and a rule-set that maps to config/retrospective.yml. We added a lightweight ranker in pkg/snippet/ranker.go (TF-IDF over short fields) to keep exported size predictable.
Noah Chen: Overall nice and focused; two asks: make the default limit 100 snippets (instead of 200) and add a unit test for IP redaction edge-case.
Ava Morales: Made the default 100 and added the test for 10.0.0.0/8 redaction edge-case; pushed fix.
Priya Singh: Security thumbs-up on redaction approach; asked for explicit docs on pseudonymization determinism.
Ava Morales: Added a short section in docs/retrospective-threatmodel.md describing the stable salt per-org and rotation policy.
Jordan Kim: Found a race in test harness on CI; requested adding retry-window.
Ava Morales: Added retry and re-ran CI — all green.
Approvals: Noah Chen approved, Priya Singh approved, Jordan Kim approved. Merge method: squash and merge.
payload.title: add compact retrospective-snippet export and anonymized oncall notes CLI

Adds adaptive signal-attenuator (rate/entropy-based suppression) + stepwise-playbook-generator (templated, telemetry-aware playbooks). CLI commands: oncallctl attenuate, oncallctl compose-playbook. Integrates with snapshot composer to attach a minimal telemetry bundle when playbooks are created.
Motivation: On-call noise and low-signal alerts keep interrupting responders and dilute attention away from high-impact incidents. This PR introduces two complementary features: (1) an adaptive signal attenuator that temporarily mutes or down-prioritizes low-signal alert bursts based on multivariate heuristics (entity cardinality, recent noise history, error-rate delta), and (2) a stepwise playbook generator that converts canonical runbook templates into prioritized, step-by-step remediation checklists with embedded conditional telemetry checks. Both are exposed via the incident-bot core and a new CLI surface (oncallctl) and are designed for safe gradual rollout with canary attenuation and an explicit override flow.
Ethan Li: Nice approach. Two requests: (1) add a CLI --dry-run that prints predicted attenuation decisions, (2) make sure the attenuator exposes a reason code for UI display so responders understand suppression rationale.
Samira Alvarez: Added --dry-run and reason_code on the API response; updated UI hint in incident_viewer.js to surface the reason. See commit 8c7b412 and web change.
Priya Natarajan: Can we ensure the default attenuation policy is conservative (95% allow for new alert types) and document the rollback steps? Also please add telemetry that counts false-suppression incidents.
Samira Alvarez: Default policy set to conservative in stepwise_template.yaml and docs include rollback + metric 'attenuator.false_suppression_count'. Added e2e that simulates false suppression and counts metric emission.
Jonah Becker: Integration tests flaky on CI once; reran and passed. Approving once green.
Jonah Becker: approved
Local test harness included (e2e/attenuator_e2e_test.sh). QA should validate: (1) attenuation dry-run output matches live decision, (2) UI displays reason_code and provides an immediate 'unmute' button, (3) false_suppression_count increments on suppressed alerts that later escalate, (4) playbook steps created by compose-playbook contain conditional telemetry checks and a top-level priority score.
Feature gated by flag 'feature.attenuator_v1'. Default off for orgs with < 24h paging SLA. We rollout in three phases: dev, 10% canary, org-wide. Canary can be disabled via admin console or oncallctl attenuate --disable-canary.
No DB migrations. New metrics (attenuator.*) and small schema add to incident metadata: 'suppression' block added to alert documents. Backwards-compatible: absent block => treated as not suppressed.
Attenuator runs within existing incident-bot service boundary and honors RBAC. 'unmute' is an action gated by oncall role. No external network calls introduced besides snapshot composer which calls existing telemetry ingest endpoint.
Introduce adaptive signal attenuator (opt-in) to reduce low-signal paging noise and a stepwise playbook generator to create prioritized remediation steps. CLI: oncallctl attenuate, oncallctl compose-playbook. Feature-gated and rolled out canary-first.
Monitor attenuator.false_suppression_count and alert if > 0.5% over baseline for 2h. Add a dashboard tile in SRE views to track suppression rate, allowed_rate, and median time-to-action on suppressed incidents.
This PR was requested as part of SRE noise-reduction initiative in ENG-7821. The design prioritizes explainability for responders and explicit quick-unmute controls to avoid blind suppression. Consider follow-up work: ML-based classification model for suppression instead of heuristics, and a 'learned' policy that adapts thresholds per service over time.
payload.title: adaptive-signal-attenuator-and-stepwise-playbook-generator

payload.body:
Adds a lightweight recon CLI to run ephemeral telemetry probes and a serializer that emits compact, annotated runbook fragments for faster on-call triage. Backwards-compatible; includes docs and integration tests.
Context and motivation:
This PR introduces a small, safe-to-run CLI (rapid-recon) and an annotated playbook serializer designed to speed first-response during incidents. The goal is to make it trivial for an on-call engineer to run a constrained set of probes, collect a compact diagnostic bundle, and generate a condensed runbook snippet that captures the hypothesis, suggested checks, and quick remediation steps.

Why this is different: existing runbook generation required heavy telemetry exports and manual summarization; this adds a low-friction path that (1) runs ephemeral, sandboxed probes, (2) captures minimal telemetry and metadata, (3) serializes the result as an annotated runbook fragment that can be pasted into the incident timeline or Slack. The serializer emits a compact JSON+markdown hybrid for human readability and machine parsing.

High-level changes (summary of commits):
- Add cmd/rapid-recon CLI (go) that coordinates probes with timeouts and safe-mode sandboxing.
- Implement internal/telemetry/sampler service to capture high-precision short-lived spans and a delta sampler to avoid noise.
- Add pkg/playbook/serializer (python) that converts probe outputs into annotated runbook fragments and supports templates with variable interpolation.
- Add webhooks to post a _quick recon card_ to the on-call Slack channel (opt-in feature behind feature flag).
- Unit and integration tests for the sampler and serializer; e2e using the local sandbox harness.

Commits (high-level):
- 1a2b3c4: initial rapid-recon CLI and probe runner loop
- 2b3c4d5: add delta sampler and probe adapters (http, tcp, redis)
- 3c4d5e6: playbook serializer + compact template definitions
- 4d5e6f7: tests, docs, and demo script

Changed files (high level):
- cmd/rapid-recon/main.go
- internal/telemetry/sampler.go
- internal/telemetry/probes/http_probe.go
- pkg/playbook/serializer.py
- pkg/playbook/templates/compact.yaml
- integrations/slack/quick_recon_poster.py
- docs/oncall/rapid-recon.md
- tests/unit/test_serializer.py
- tests/integration/test_recon_e2e.sh

Example of generated runbook fragment (serialized output snippet):
{"summary":"Validate ingress latency and upstream error rates","checks":[{"id":"http-200-check","cmd":"rapid-recon probe http --url https://service.internal/health --timeout 3s","expected":"200","notes":"Runs cached ping against the service; safe-mode disables writes."}],"annotations":"observed spike at 2026-01-29T03:14:12Z, upstream redis RPO high"}

Small code excerpt (serializer output formatting):
playbook_fragment = f"---\nSummary: {summary}\nChecks:\n{checks_markdown}\nAnnotations:\n{annotations}\n---"

Review conversation (high-level):
- Arjun: "Nice concise API for probes. Please ensure probe adapters have strict CPU/memory limits and do not open long-lived connections."
- Maya: "Added timeouts and context cancellation, moved adapters into a worker pool with hard limits. See internal/telemetry/worker_pool.go"
- Evelyn: "Serializer looks solid; can we reduce noise in templates by removing stack traces by default?"
- Maya: "Removed full stack traces, added a `--include-traces` flag for deep debugging."
- Noah: "Minor nit: rename `compact.yaml` -> `condensed.yaml` for clarity."
- Maya: "Applied rename and updated docs."
- Evelyn: "Approved pending CI."
- Arjun: "Approved."

CI summary and iteration: 
- ci/build: pass on first run.
- ci/unit-tests: two failing tests initially (serializer edge-cases) — fixed in 3c4d5e6, rerun -> pass.
- ci/e2e-repro: flaky in sandboxed environment (network bind race); added a retry and explicit ephemeral port selection, rerun -> pass.
- ci/lint: warnings (line-length in generated docs) — fixed in follow-up commit.
- Final status: all checks green and branch protection satisfied.

Safety and rollout notes:
- Feature is behind an opt-in feature flag: `rapid_recon.enabled` (defaults to false in production).
- CLI defaults to read-only probe adapters; any write-capable probes require `--allow-writes` and explicit opt-in via environment variable.
- Telemetry retention is short-lived (48h) for recon bundles; serializer fragments do not include PII by default.

Testing and docs:
- Added a tutorial in docs/oncall/rapid-recon.md with examples for common failure classes (ingress latency, downstream timeouts, auth failures).
- Included a demo script tests/integration/test_recon_e2e.sh for local validation.

Merge outcome:
- Squash-merged to main (merge commit f3b9c2a).
- Backported the safe-mode timeout fixes to release/2026-01-legacy in a follow-up hotfix PR.

Future follow-ups (not in this PR):
- Add a lightweight UI to inspect recent recon fragments in the console.
- Add a compatibility layer so the serializer fragments can be consumed by the SLO toolkit for automated alert replays.

If you'd like to run a quick demo locally: 
1) make -C cmd/rapid-recon build
2) ./bin/rapid-recon --template=compact.yaml --timeout=10s --output=./sample-runbook.json
3) cat ./sample-runbook.json

Notes for reviewers: this bundle focused on minimal, well-scoped primitives so it can be iterated independently of the larger incident workflow.
payload.title: Rapid recon CLI and annotated playbook serializer

Motivation: on-call responders frequently need full incident context when incidents are bridged across multiple chat channels and paging systems; manual copy/paste is error-prone and slows TTR. This PR introduces a compact, serializable "bridged context" snapshot that travels with the incident across channels and an opinionated library of parameterized escalation templates that the bot can surface or send automatically. Changes include: 1) context capture: snapshot of current runbook pointer, top-3 alerts, recent error rates, and active mitigations; 2) context propagation: add signed metadata token to bridged messages so downstream responders receive identical context; 3) template library: YAML-driven templates with conditional rendering, throttling and dedupe keys; 4) escalation rules: configurable selectors that map alert signals + SLO breach state to template choices and escalation targets; 5) telemetry and auditing: new metrics and audit entries for every template render/send; 6) feature gating: rollout via feature flag per-org with safe defaults. Backwards compatibility: if a downstream bot doesn't understand the token, it ignores it and nothing breaks; templates are opt-in per-oncall rotation. Testing: unit and integration harness simulating bridged Slack<->PagerDuty flows, contract tests for token validity, and an e2e smoke in staging. Rollout: enable for internal SRE rotation (10% of incidents) for 48h, monitor metrics, then expand to all teams. See ENG-4021 for design notes and SUP-912 for support runbook updates. Checklist: [x] design doc linked [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] telemetry added [x] security review requested [x] staged rollout planned.
Ethan Park (requested changes): We should avoid sending full stack traces in context tokens; please confirm we sanitize sensitive fields. Author: sanitized top-level message and excluded traces; also added contract test to assert no secrets are present.
Priya Desai (comment): Template throttling looks good, but what happens when multiple rules match? Author: added deterministic priority ordering and a tiebreaker based on rotation id; documented in templates YAML schema.
Marcus Liu (approved): Verified e2e staging run, metrics look stable and no duplicate escalations observed.
CI Bot: initial integration failed on flaky external-call; author reran pipeline and all checks passed.
Security Review (comment): token signing is acceptable but rotate keys quarterly; author: added key-rotation stub and notes to ops playbook.
Adds bridged on-call context propagation and automated escalation templates; feature-gated and opt-in; metrics: bridged_oncall.escalation_sent_total, bridged_oncall.duplicate_dedupe_blocked_total; see docs/runbooks/bridged-context.md for usage.
Unit tests for snapshot and template rendering; integration tests for Slack<->PagerDuty bridging; staging smoke against a snapshot of production data; contract tests to ensure token ABI stability.
Canary: enable for internal SRE rotation (10% incidents) for 48h -> monitor errors, duplicate escalations, and latency -> 50% teams for 72h -> GA. Feature flag per-org with emergency kill-switch.
low-medium: risk of duplicate escalations if dedupe id generation fails; mitigations: deterministic dedupe keys, rate limits, and audit alerts; security review required before GA.
When enabled, human responders will see a 'bridged context' card with runbook pointer and recent alerts; if auto-escalation triggers, the incident will include the template message and metadata; to opt-out add 'bridged_context: false' to the rotation config.
payload.title: Add bridged on-call context and automated escalation templates

Motivation: In high-concurrency streaming scenarios we observed rare but customer-visible cases where SSE fragments that split JSON payloads or function-call sentinels could be reordered by upstream buffering layers, resulting in malformed partial JSON or tool/function-call ordering anomalies. This PR introduces a fragment sequencer and a conservative JSON rollup guard to make streaming reconstruction deterministic and resilient to reordering, partial-deliveries, and delimiter corruption.

What this changes: Adds a lightweight per-stream fragment sequencer that stamps outbound SSE fragments with a monotonic fragment_seq and epoch header (SSE-Seq-Version:2). The server-side assembler uses the sequencer to: 1) reorder late-arriving fragments within a bounded window; 2) detect missing fragments and trigger a rollup-rescue path instead of emitting a partial JSON event; 3) normalize and collapse duplicate trailing delimiters before handing events to the structured-output pipeline. To preserve strict function/tool-call ordering we also attach an ordered-toolcall-ordinal to fncall sentinel frames so downstream tool invocations see a deterministic ordinal even under retransmit/replay.

Design notes: Sequencer is intentionally small: fragments carry probe metadata (frag_seq, epoch, frag_len). The assembler keeps a bounded reorder buffer (configurable via sse.max_reseq_window) and exposes two outcomes: ASSEMBLED (complete, in-order) and ROLLUP (best-effort rescue that concatenates fragments, validates JSON, and emits a trimmed structured event plus diagnostics). The rollup guard performs UTF-8 safety checks, trailing comma fixes for common serializer truncations, and adds a metadata field sse.rollup_hint to downstream structured-output events for traceability.

Compatibility: The change is backward-compatible for clients that ignore SSE-Seq-Version headers; existing plain-fragment flows remain supported. New behavior is opt-in for Dedicated/Private customers via a runtime flag (sse.enable_sequencer) during initial rollout; hosted API will enable rollouts progressively after Canary.

Testing: Unit tests for sequencer edge cases, fuzz tests for mid-json truncation, and integration tests that simulate interleaved fragments, delayed retransmits, and toolcall replays were added. Load tests show sequencing adds <1% p99 latency at typical token sizes and reduces partial-JSON error rate by ~98% in synthetic reorder workloads. New metrics: sse.fragment_reseqs, sse.rollup_rescues, sse.toolcall_ord_mismatches.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to canary region with sse.enable_sequencer=false by default and run synthetic repros; 2) Enable sequencing for 5% of traffic with auto-fallback to previous emitter if rollup_rescues exceed threshold; 3) Gradual ramp and post-deploy monitoring via new dashboards.

Notes for reviewers: Look at the reassembly invariants in pkg/stream/sse/sequencer.go and the rescue heuristics in pkg/stream/sse/rollup_guard.go. The change includes small API surface additions to the streaming handshake header only (no public SDK breaking changes).
Jun Park: 'Can you explain the choice of window size and how it affects memory under pathological reordering?' — Aisha: 'Default window is 64 fragments, we've observed it's sufficient for typical network reorder; made it configurable to 256 for extreme tests and added backpressure to drop oldest entries with metrics.'; Lina Gomez: 'Need clearer signal on when rollup_rescue happens for customer debugging' — Aisha: 'Added sse.rollup_hint and structured diagnostic payloads; updated docs with examples.'; Tomás Rivera: 'Race in reorder buffer removal noted in initial run' — Aisha: 'Fixed in a0b1c2d, added a deterministic integration test.'; Approval: Lina and Tomás approved after fixes; Jun gave LGTM after CI rerun.
Add fragment sequencing and JSON rollup guards to improve SSE streaming resilience: reduces partial-JSON emissions, preserves tool/function-call ordering, adds sse.fragment_reseqs and sse.rollup_rescues metrics. Opt-in via sse.enable_sequencer; rollout will be gradual.
payload.title: add-fragment-sequencer-json-rollup-and-ordered-toolcall-handoff

Motivation: On-call handoffs and post-incident briefs often require a compact, machine-readable timeline that combines alerts, key traces, and remediation steps. Previously responders manually assembled timelines from disparate sources. This PR introduces two complementary capabilities: 1) a Structured Incident Timeline Exporter that composes a normalized, JSONL timeline from incident metadata, alert events, and selected telemetry snapshots; and 2) a Brief Template Factory that consumes a template catalog and instantiates a concise incident brief (markdown + attachments) populated with timeline snippets, top-ranked traces, and suggested playbook steps. Goals: reduce manual handoff time, make brief contents reproducible, and enable downstream automation (notebook replay, RCA scaffolding).
- Add structured incident timeline exporter (JSONL) for reproducible handoffs.
- Add brief template factory and example templates for quick on-call briefs.
- New CLI: rbx export-timeline and rbx render-brief.
- Telemetry snapshots constrained by default budget (256KB) with override flag.
- No breaking changes to existing incident APIs.
Feature guarded behind feature-flag incident_briefing_v2. Rolling out to 10% of oncall channels for 48h, then 100% after metrics validation. Observability: new metrics exported incident_brief.templates_rendered and timeline.export.size_bytes. Alert if median export time > 750ms or median size > 400KB.
Unit and integration test suites added. Local smoke steps: 1) rbx export-timeline --incident=INC-1234 --out=sample.jsonl 2) rbx render-brief --template=pager-handoff --timeline=sample.jsonl --out=brief.md 3) open brief.md in briefViewer component sample. CI added deterministic fixtures to avoid flakiness.

Introduce runbook suggester and playbook scoring engine for on-call workflows; safe default policy and feature flag; metrics and tracing added; no config migration required; rolls out to beta by default.
Motivation: on-call triage is noisy: runbooks drift, noisy pages lack clear playbooks, and on-call juniors often pick inappropriate remediation steps. This PR adds a lightweight scoring engine that ranks runbooks by a compound signal (recent pager frequency, SLO breach correlation, MTTA/MTTR history, and operator feedback) and a runbook suggester that surfaces candidate playbooks in Slack when an alert is paged. The goal is to reduce time-to-first-action and provide actionable, readable playbooks in the incident channel.

What this PR does (single string): - Add playbook scorer module (incident_bot.runbooks.scorer) implementing a weighted scoring model and small calibration table; weights are configurable via feature flags and defaults tuned on last-90-days incidents. - Add runbook suggester integration for Slack async actions: suggests 2–3 candidate runbooks with confidence score; supports 'apply' to populate incident template. - Add CLI tool incident-bot oncall-check to detect rotation conflicts and missing overrides; returns machine-readable JSON for infra pipelines. - Add SLO toolkit helpers used by scorer: burn-rate heuristics and incident-to-SLO attribution helpers. - Wire metrics (incident.runbook_suggestions, incident.playbook_score.{bucket}) and tracing spans for end-to-end latency. - Tests: unit tests for scorer, integration tests for Slack suggestion flow, e2e harness against test SLO store. - Docs: README and playbook guidance doc plus runbook-quality examples.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added and green - [x] Integration tests for Slack flow - [x] E2E harness run locally - [x] Feature-flag gated rollout implemented - [x] Docs updated with usage and tuning guidance

Backward compatibility and rollout: default policy is conservative (low-sensitivity) and disabled in orgs without SLO metadata. Feature gate: ff.runbook_suggester.v2. Rollout plan: beta -> opt-in on 2 pilot teams -> org-wide after 2 weeks and monitoring checks.

Monitoring and safety: suggestion acceptance rate, false-suggestion rate (manual rejection), and MTTA delta are instrumented. We added auto-fallback to a safe template when confidence < 0.15.

Notes: this PR intentionally keeps scoring simple (linear weights) to make tuning auditable; follow-ups will add a lightweight ML ranker in the slo-toolkit repo once we have stable labels.
Aisha Patel: Please add more context on how the weight defaults were derived. Nina Zhao: We derived weights from a simple grid search over the last 90 days and validated on 3 pilot services; added a note in docs/runbook-suggester.md with calibration results. Luca Moreno: Can suggester handle channels that have suppressed bot messages? Nina Zhao: Yes, we fallback to a direct-thread DM to the on-call and record an event. Priya Singh: Add a toggle to disable suggestions for orgs without SLO metadata? Nina Zhao: Done, ff.runbook_suggester.v2 gates the whole flow and we explicitly check for SLO tags. Daniel Park (SRE): I saw flakiness in the integration test on CI the first run. Nina Zhao: CI retry fixed it; added tighter timeouts and mock for Slack API. Aisha: Approved after docs update. Luca: Approved. Priya: Requested minor change to CLI exit codes; addressed. Daniel: Approved and marked for merge once CI passes.
CI: initial run failed due to flaky Slack integration test (timeout). Rerun with mocked responses and added timeouts; subsequent runs passed. Summary: unit tests 128 passed, 2 skipped; integration tests 24 passed; e2e harness simulated 10 incidents. Lint: minor style fixes applied. Coverage: scorer module coverage 92%.
New metrics: incident.runbook_suggestions.count (tags: team, alert_type), incident.runbook_suggestions.accept_rate, incident.playbook_score.bucket (0-0.1,0.1-0.3,0.3-0.6,0.6-1.0), incident.suggester.latency_ms; Tracing spans: runbook.scorer.score, runbook.suggester.dispatch. Dashboards: added a new panel in Oncall Overview -> Runbook Suggestions.
Operator steps to roll out: 1) Enable ff.runbook_suggester.v2 for pilot team in feature flag dashboard. 2) Monitor incident.runbook_suggestions.accept_rate and MTTA delta. 3) If accept_rate < 0.25 after 48h, revert flag and open ENG-XXXX for tuning. 4) Rotation conflicts flagged by cli/oncall_check.py should be resolved before enabling suggester for that team.
ENG-2601 - add automatic feedback loop to retrain weights from accepted/rejected suggestions
SRE-147 - pilot rollout observations and tuning
ENG-2610 - add optional ML ranker in slo-toolkit

payload.body:
Problem: incident-bot’s Statuspage integration currently performs best-effort POST/PATCH calls with minimal retry handling. During Sev0/Sev1s we’ve seen transient 5xx/timeout/429 responses (plus occasional network blips) leading to (a) failed publishes that require manual retry and (b) duplicate updates when a human re-triggers a step while the original request is still in flight. This PR introduces a small Statuspage API client wrapper with standardized retry/backoff, idempotency keys, and structured audit log entries for every attempted publish/update. Scope: add an HTTP client with (1) bounded retries for retryable failures (429, 5xx, network timeouts), (2) exponential backoff with jitter and respect for Retry-After where present, (3) deterministic idempotency keys so retries and replays don’t create duplicate incidents/updates, and (4) audit logging to our internal incident-bot audit sink so we can answer “what did we publish, when, and who/what triggered it?” without scraping Slack. Non-goals: changing the copy/templates (handled in PR-19344) or expanding component taxonomy fields (handled in PR-19321). Implementation details: The new StatuspageClient wraps fetch with a retry policy: max_attempts=5 (1 initial + 4 retries), base_delay_ms=250, max_delay_ms=5000, full jitter. We retry on: HTTP 429, HTTP 500/502/503/504, and network errors/timeouts. We do NOT retry on other 4xx. For 429 we honor Retry-After (seconds) if present, otherwise use computed backoff. Idempotency: we add an Idempotency-Key header on requests that create resources (incident create, incident update create). Key format is stable and derived from: statuspage_page_id, incident_id (our internal incident GUID), operation (create_incident | post_update | set_component_status), component_ids (sorted), and a normalized “update_fingerprint” (state + message hash + impact window start rounded to minute). This keeps keys stable across retries but different across meaningfully different updates. Audit log: every call to StatuspageClient emits an AuditEvent with request_id, operation, page_id, statuspage_incident_id (if known), idempotency_key, http_status, attempt_count, elapsed_ms, and redacted payload summary (we keep message length + sha256, not the full message). Audit events go to the existing incident-bot audit stream (and show up in the internal dashboard), and we also log a one-line summary to #incidents-bot-debug on failures after max attempts. Testing: added unit tests for retry classification, backoff calculations (including Retry-After), idempotency key stability, and audit event emission; added one integration-ish test that stubs the Statuspage API with a 429 then a 200 to validate behavior. Ops notes: config defaults live in statuspage_client.yaml but can be overridden via env vars for emergency tuning (MAX_ATTEMPTS, MAX_DELAY_MS).
Miles Thornton (review): Retry logic looks good. Please confirm we do not retry 400/401/403/404, and ensure we only retry 429 + 5xx + network/timeouts. Also, can we cap total time spent retrying so we don’t stall incident workflows indefinitely?
Devon Price (author): Yep — only 429/5xx/timeouts. I’ll add an explicit predicate + tests for non-retryable 4xx and add a max elapsed cap (default 30s) in addition to max attempts.
Christine Wong (review): Idempotency key includes message hash + state which is great. One concern: impact window rounding to minute could cause collisions if we post multiple distinct updates within a minute with the same template message. Can we include the incident-bot timeline event id (or workflow step id) instead?
Devon Price (author): Good catch. I switched to include our internal incident_event_id when available (workflow has it); if missing, we fall back to the minute-rounded timestamp. Added a test that consecutive updates in same minute generate distinct keys when event ids differ.
Rafael Mendes (review): For audit logs, please confirm we never store the full customer-facing message. Legal asked us to avoid retaining incident copy beyond what’s already public unless needed. Message sha + length is fine. Also add page_id + statuspage_incident_id to the audit record so we can correlate quickly.
Devon Price (author): Confirmed — we only store sha256 + length, plus operation metadata. Added page_id and statuspage_incident_id fields (nullable until we get it back from create).
Allison Grant (review): Can we emit a metric for retry count / final failure so we can alert on Statuspage integration degradation? Even just a counter tagged by operation + http_status.
Devon Price (author): Added counters: statuspage_client_requests_total and statuspage_client_retries_total, plus statuspage_client_failures_total. Tags: operation, final_status (or network_error), page_id. Wired into existing metrics sink.
Miles Thornton (review): Looks solid now. Approving once the max elapsed cap lands.
Devon Price (author): Pushed follow-up commit adding max_elapsed_ms=30000 default + env override + tests. Please take another look.
Miles Thornton (review): Approved.
Christine Wong (review): Approved.
Rafael Mendes (review): Approved.
Allison Grant (review): Approved.
payload.title: Statuspage API client: retry/backoff + idempotency keys + audit log entries

Context: We see intermittent long-tail latencies that spike under bursty admission patterns. Existing per-invocation metrics are useful but noisy: they surface total latency without splitting where time is spent (queueing, batching, execution, streaming). This PR adds a lightweight runtime instrument and downstream observability pipeline that decomposes per-invocation latency into token-bucket based phases and wires that decomposition into dashboards and an alert fallback orchestrator. Motivation: enable precise SLO attribution (which phase caused the tail) and automated alert attenuation + optional model fallback to preserve availability at acceptable cost.
feat(obs): add token-bucket latency decomposer component; feat(metrics): expose phase-specific histograms and sparklines; feat(dashboards): add decomposed-per-invocation dashboard and tenant breakdown; feat(alerts): orchestrator to suppress noisy alerts and trigger fallback policy; fix(tests): coverage for decomposer edge cases; chore: docs and runbook updates

observability/pipeline/decomposer_consumer.py
telemetry/metrics/registry.yaml
dashboards/observability/decomposed_latency.json
alerting/policies/fallback_orchestrator.yaml
sdk/python/redwood/metrics_adapter.py
docs/runbooks/observability/decomposed-latency.md
tests/metric_integration/test_decomposer_integration.py
ci/observability-checks.yml
Liam Chen (review): Overall nice separation of concern. Please ensure the decomposer doesn't spike cardinality: the proposal to hash callsite+route and emit a fixed-bucket label is good — prefer a 12-bit hash to avoid label explosion.
Author (Aparna): Switched to 12-bit route hash and added a sampling gate for low-volume tenants. See runtime/instrumentation/token_bucket_decomposer.rs + telemetry/metrics/registry.yaml for the sample config.
Sofia Mendes (review): The fallback orchestrator is powerful — need clear guardrails. Add a cooldown window and a maximum fallback rate per tenant to avoid oscillation.
Author (Aparna): Added cooldown and per-tenant rate limit (defaults in alerting/policies/fallback_orchestrator.yaml). Documented in runbook with recommended thresholds.
Noah Patel (approval): Verified metrics ingestion in staging and validated dashboard panels with synthetic replays. Approving pending CI green.
Checks: unit (pass), integration (pass on staging replay), lint (pass), observability-checks (pass after flakiness guard). One flaky test was fixed by adding deterministic timestamps to test fixtures.
Local unit tests + staging replay validated: 1) phase histograms align with synthetic stage (admission->batch->exec->stream) 2) KV-cache miss heat spikes map to execution phase 3) decomposed sparklines render with low overhead. Load test at 500 rps showed ~0.8% metric ingestion overhead and negligible path latency impact.
New dashboard 'Decomposed Invocation Latency' added with: per-route phase stacked histogram, per-tenant tail table (p95/p99 per-phase), sparklines for individual invocation cohorts, and cost-attribution panel correlating token counts with phase durations. Panel file: dashboards/observability/decomposed_latency.json
New orchestrator implements two behaviors: 1) alert attenuation: when noisy low-signal tenants cause frequent p99 flips, suppress alerts for a configurable quiet window and emit an advisory metric; 2) fallback activation: when execution-phase p99 exceeds threshold and queueing is not dominant, trigger model-fallback to a compatible lower-latency variant (rate-limited per tenant). All actions emit audit events and can be disabled per-tenant via policy.
1) Feature gated by runtime flag (off by default) 2) Canary: enable for internal org + 3 beta tenants for 48h with synthetic replay 3) Gradual ramp to 10% tenants over 72h while monitoring decomposition drift and alert noise 4) Full rollout after 1 week of stable metrics.
docs/runbooks/observability/decomposed-latency.md
Added token-bucket latency decomposition to give phase-level visibility (admission, batching, execution, streaming) and a new alert fallback orchestrator that can suppress noisy alerts and optionally trigger model fallbacks for high execution-phase tail. Configurable per-tenant. Backwards compatible; disabled by default.
- Deploy metrics consumer to staging pipeline - Flip runtime feature flag for canary tenants - Schedule 4h post-deploy health checks and an A/C triage session - Follow up with a telemetry review (ENG-2245) to tune thresholds
Related Linear: ENG-2245 (SLO attribution), ENG-3102 (alert reduction). See also: ENG-3301 for future per-kernel energy attribution.
If you see repeated fallback activations for many tenants, first check the 'admission vs exec' phase distribution in the decomposed dashboard. If execution dominates and fallback rate limit is exhausted, rollback the orchestrator flag and open an incident for runtime performance. Audit logs are emitted under observability.audit.fallback.*
payload.title: Introduce token-bucket latency decomposer and fallback alert orchestrator

payload.body:
Motivation:
We frequently get alerts that lack immediate operational context (recent deploys, relevant traces, recent error-rate spikes), which slows on-call TTR. This PR adds two complementary capabilities to incident-bot: proactive alert enrichment (pulls and aggregates quick context from traces/metrics/logs and SLO burn-rate) and responder scripting (small, auditable action templates that on-call can run from the incident thread). The goal is to reduce median investigation time and standardize initial recovery steps while preserving safety controls.

What this change does (single-string summary):
- Adds an enrichment pipeline that runs for new alerts and attaches a compact context summary: last 5 deploys, top traces (sampled spans), recent error-rate/time-series sparkline, and SLO burn-rate across the last 5/15/60m windows.
- Introduces a responder script registry: vetted, parameterizable scripts (bash/python) stored in the incident-bot service with metadata (required_roles, dry_run_supported, idempotency_hint).
- UI/Slack integration: enriched preview posted to the alert thread; scripts rendered as collapsible actions with a one-click "dry-run" or "execute" that performs RBAC checks and records audit logs.
- SLO-toolkit integration: enrichment tags alerts with a severity_hint computed from SLO burn-rate thresholds defined in the SLO toolkit config (consistent with SLO-alarms).
- Privacy & safety: automatic PII redaction rules for enrichment text and script parameter sanitizers; scripts run in a constrained execution sandbox via the existing runbook-executor shim (same sandbox used by canary jobs).

Files changed (high-level):
- cmd/incident-bot/main.go (wire new services, config flags)
- internal/enrichment/enricher.py (new enrichment pipeline core)
- internal/enrichment/redaction.py (PII heuristics + allowlist)
- internal/responder/registry.go (script metadata store + API)
- internal/responder/executor_shim.py (sandbox wrapper and audit hooks)
- web/ui/components/AlertEnrichedPreview.tsx (render sparkline and actions)
- integrations/slo_toolkit/client.rs (small adapter for burn-rate lookups)
- migrations/20260218_add_responder_registry.sql (DB schema)
- e2e/incident-bot/enrichment_flow.test.ts (integration tests)

Commits (summary):
- b12f4d3: wire enrichment service and config flags
- c7d9a9f: implement enrichment core, initial SLO burn-rate heuristics
- d4a1b2e: responder registry API + DB migration
- e8f7c44: responder executor shim and sandbox integration
- f01b3c2: UI pieces & Slack rendering

Migration notes:
- Adds a new DB table `responder_registry`. Migration is idempotent and backward-compatible; if migration is not applied, responder endpoints return 412 with guidance.
- New config flags (incident.enrichment.enabled, incident.enrichment.max_latency_ms, responder.sandbox.max_runtime_s) documented in deploy/CONFIG.md.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests added for redaction rules and burn-rate calculator.
- e2e tests run in CI against a local mock SLO service and a tiny sandbox image.
- Initial CI run failed due to timeouts in sandbox integration; fixed by adjusting test harness timeout and ensuring the sandbox image is pulled in the test step. Final CI status: pass.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy feature gated off by default.
2) Enable enrichment for internal prod only and monitor overhead metrics: enrichment.latency_percentile_p95 and enrichment.cpu_seconds_per_alert.
3) Gradually enable responder actions for trusted SRE group (RBAC gate).
4) After 2 weeks of internal canary, open to broader org.

Telemetry & observability:
- New metrics: enrichment.latency_ms{p50,p95,p99}, enrichment.lookup_failures_total, responder.exec_attempts_total, responder.exec_success_total, responder.exec_audit_events_total.
- Traces: enrichment pipeline emits a root span and attaches trace IDs to alert notes so downstream systems can link traces to alerts.
- Dashboards: added a short-lived panel in SRE dashboard for the rollout phase.

Security & privacy considerations:
- Redaction: default redaction removes tokens, emails, auth headers, and long UUIDs; teams can extend allowlists in config.
- RBAC: only users in roles listed on a script's required_roles can execute; audit events recorded to the existing audit-log-exporter pipeline.
- Scripts are stored encrypted at rest and validated by a vetting webhook that checks for forbidden syscalls/patterns.

Limitations & follow-ups:
- Enrichment currently queries only the tracing and SLO services; logs aggregation will be added in a follow-up (ENG-1331).
- Script sandbox is conservative and does not support long-running interactive jobs; we'll add a job-queue integration later.

References: ENG-1294 (linear), SRE-203 (on-call efficiency spike), internal doc: /docs/incident-bot/enrichment.md

If anything: this PR is intentionally split into a small core feature and a follow-up for broader logging and script templates. Reviewers: please focus on redaction heuristics and the RBAC enforcement path.

Diego Morales (2026-02-19): Nice end-to-end. A couple of safety questions: 1) How do we prevent scripts from exfiltrating secrets if someone passes a leaked token as a parameter? 2) Can we ensure that the audit event includes the pre-exec scrubbed parameters?
Author (Nora Patel) reply (2026-02-19): Good points. We added parameter sanitizers (internal/enrichment/redaction.py) and the executor records both raw and scrubbed parameter fingerprints — raw params are never sent to the audit stream, only hashes and redacted previews. See executor_shim.py lines 120-165.
Anya Chen (2026-02-20): minor nit: the SLO burn-rate thresholds are hardcoded in the initial implementation. Can we plumb these from the SLO-toolkit config?
Author reply (2026-02-20): Done — added integrations/slo_toolkit/client.rs adapter and plumbed thresholds through incident.enrichment.slo_config_ref. Tests added.
Samir Banerjee (2026-02-22): e2e flake observed in CI previously — the sandbox image pull timed out. Looks like you increased test timeout; can we instead make the test pull the image in a setup step to avoid flakiness?
Author reply (2026-02-22): Addressed — test harness now invokes scripts/ci/pull_sandbox_image.sh in the workflow pre-step. CI rerun passed.
Adds proactive alert enrichment (traces, SLO burn-rate, recent deploys) and a responder scripting registry; feature gated and rolled out to internal SRE first. Includes privacy redaction and RBAC controls.

Motivation: We continue to see tail latency spikes on CPU-heavy boxes caused by request marshalling, ephemeral allocations, and the worker-pool being blocked by network IO. This PR attacks the problem on three fronts: 1) Replace per-request serialization copy path with a zero-copy marshalling pipeline that keeps request buffers on the incoming IO arena and hands only lightweight descriptors to CPU workers; 2) Move socket read/write operations off of the worker thread pool to dedicated IO threads with a compact SPSC ring buffer interface, avoiding accidental thread preemption and expensive thread pinning ops on the hot CPU path; 3) Reduce KV cache contention by introducing a fast-path, lockless read using seqlock-style epoch checks, falling back to shared_mutex only on hash-collisions or write cases. Additionally we tweak continuous batching heuristics to pre-reserve batch slots and to prefer same-core batch coalescing when available.
Reduced CPU-side latency by eliminating per-request copies on the hot path; improved throughput under bursty load; KV cache lookups switched to lockless fast-path for common case; no public API changes.
Aisha Khan: This looks great; main concern is the lifetime model for arena-backed buffers crossing async boundaries. Can we add a debug-only sanitizer that tracks arena frees?
Leah Park: Added arena debug tracking under build flag ARENA_SANITIZER and a test exercising cross-thread handoff; left comments in request_marshalling.h about ownership semantics.
Tom Becker: The seqlock approach on kv cache is clever, but we need to ensure we don't spin forever under pathological update patterns. Please add a bounded retry and fallback to shared_mutex.
Leah Park: Added bounded retry (8 spins) and immediate fallback and documented the tradeoff. Also added microbench comparing fallback rate.
Riley Chen: CI flake in tests/integration/zero_copy_marshalling_test initially failed on Linux/amd64 with a race. After the fix the integration runs stable locally and on CI.
Tom Becker: Approved after the bounded-retry change and perf numbers look good.
Aisha Khan: Approved — nit: add a small blurb in ops docs about tuning io thread count relative to NIC queues.
a8c9f1e: introduce zero-copy RequestDescriptor and IOArena, initial plumbing
b4d3e72: implement SPSC ring buffer between IO threads and worker scheduler, tests
c6f1b9a: add lockless kvcache fast-path with epoch checks and fast-path microbench
d9e3aa4: batch-reservation API and scheduler hint for core-local coalescing
e1b7c21: add metrics for dropped-descriptors and io-to-worker enqueue latency
f3c2d11: fix test race on shutdown, adjust lifetime semantics for arena-backed buffers
1a2b3c4: docs: describe marshalling guarantees and developer ergonomics
