Motivation: On-call training and realistic incident rehearsals are time consuming to setup and often unreproducible. This PR introduces a compact 'simulation deck' format and a controlled HTTP failure injector that together let SREs and on-call engineers replay real-world failure scenarios deterministically against a sandboxed environment.

What this adds: a) simctl CLI (incident-bot/cmd/simctl) to compose and run simulation decks; b) a deck manifest format (YAML) that encodes alert traces, latency distributions, downstream-5xx profiles, and deterministic RNG seeds for reproducible runs; c) an HTTP failure injector implemented as a Kubernetes Job and lightweight Envoy filter snippets (applied to a temporary simulation sidecar) to create controlled 4xx/5xx and latency-injection traffic shaping; d) integration hooks that emit simulation traces/metrics tagged with sim_id for SLO impact calculations in slo-toolkit; e) safety guardrails: dry-run mode, namespace isolation, quota checks, a conservative circuit-breaker (max 5 concurrent sim jobs), and an automatic cleanup/finalizer to revert Envoy filters and remove the job.

Safety and scope: The injector runs only in a namespaced simulation sandbox by default (--namespace=oncall-sim-<id>), refuses to target production namespaces, and requires the operator to pass an allowlist file for clusters where simulations are permitted. The default behavior is a no-op dry-run until an explicit --confirm flag is provided. All injected metrics use a "sim." prefix and an exported sim_id label so telemetry is segregated.

Usage (short): simctl init-deck --from-trace trace-2026-01-12.json 
then simctl run --deck example-deck.yaml --confirm --namespace oncall-sim-42 --seed 12345

Test plan: unit tests for deck parsing and RNG deterministic behaviour, e2e integration tests in the canary sandbox cluster (runs as part of integration CI), and a staged runbook exercised during dogfood week that validated cleanup and observability tagging.

Risks and mitigations: initial integration test flakiness was due to job cleanup races; added exponential backoff and a finalizer to ensure Envoy filter removal. Destructive failure injection prevented by explicit allowlist and require-confirm semantics.

Why now: reproducible, fast on-call exercises help reduce MTTR; this gives teams a low-effort way to rehearse specific customer-impacting traces and verify SLO alerting and runbooks end-to-end.
Leah Kim: This is a great start — can we please add an explicit no-target-production check that fails fast? (I raised a small inline suggestion on k8s_job.go)
Priya Narang: Added an allowlist check and updated README; the injector now refuses to run if the target namespace is in the production list. pushed b4e2c19 -> c7b9a0f
Ethan Hall: e2e flake observed when cleanup raced with job failure; we should backoff before re-applying the envoy patch removal.
Priya Narang: Added exponential backoff and finalizer to ensure filter removal (see d2f11b6). Also added deterministic seeds to make replay reproducible.
Hiroshi Tanaka: Please add a smoke test to CI that runs a dry-run deck to exercise parsing and basic flow — low cost, high value.
Priya Narang: Added sandbox dry-run CI job and a short example deck under docs; tests added to integration pipeline.

b4e2c19: feat(injector): add k8s job + envoy snippet runner and safety checks
c7b9a0f: feat(metrics): emit sim_id labels and sim.* metric prefix for slo-toolkit
d2f11b6: fix(ci): stabilize e2e cleanup with finalizer and exponential backoff
e9d0a77: docs: add simulation-deck.md, examples and quickstart
Added simctl + simulation-deck format and a controlled HTTP failure injector for on-call rehearsals. Includes sandbox e2e tests and observability hooks for SLO impact analysis.
This PR is intentionally conservative: injector defaults to dry-run and an allowlist; teams should run simulations in the designated sandbox cluster. Followup PRs will add a web UI and a library of curated decks derived from past incidents.

Adds a guided diagnostic CLI and automated handoff cards for responders; opt-in by default for new installations.
Motivation: First-response time for junior on-call engineers often stalls while they assemble context, meanwhile evidence is lost during handoff. This PR introduces a guided diagnostic "journey" feature that scaffolds stepwise probes, telemetry snapshots and prefilled runbook hints, and ties it to an automated handoff card generator that packages sanitized context for the next responder.

Goals: reduce time-to-first-action, improve handoff signal-to-noise, and provide safe automation with explicit opt-in and redaction policies.

Summary of changes:
- new CLI command `ib diag start|resume|share` to run guided journeys locally or from Slack/web actions
- handoff manager that composes a compact card (2–3 sections) with prioritized hypotheses, key traces, and suggested remediation steps
- privacy engine that redacts secrets/PII via regex + allowlist heuristics before sharing
- web UI: ephemeral handoff card preview and accept/reject flow
- telemetry: new metrics for journey completion, handoff-accepted-rate, and oncall-time-saved
- integration tests and demo runbook templates

rollout checklist:
- [x] CLI surface implemented and feature-flagged
- [x] Hand-off card JSON schema and UI components
- [x] Privacy redaction integration with existing sanitizer
- [x] Unit and e2e tests for happy path and redaction cases
- [x] Docs draft (internal runbooks)

Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1217/guided-diagnostic-journeys and demo video (internal)

NOTE: The description is intentionally compact; implementation details and configuration knobs are in the changed files.
feat(cli): add `diag` subcommand with start/resume/share actions
feat(handoff): new handoff manager to assemble compact cards and push to Slack/email hooks
feat(ui): preview and accept/reject flow for handoff cards (web)
refactor(redaction): unify sanitizer pipeline and add allowlist/denylist patterns
test: add e2e scenario for multi-shift handoff and redaction verification
chore: docs for operators and feature-flag toggles
Samir: This looks great overall — can we add a rate limit on share to avoid noisy handoffs during noisy alerts?
Alyssa: Added a short-circuit debounce (30s) in manager.go and documented behavior in the runbook.
Joanna: Suggest tightening the default redaction allowlist; current allowlist may expose hostnames in some environments.
Alyssa: Adjusted allowlist patterns and added integration tests that include obfuscated hostnames. Thanks.
Marcus: E2E flake on CI on the first run; it fails when the mock telemetry store returns partial traces. Can we add a retry?
Alyssa: Added a retry with exponential backoff (3 attempts) and a deterministic seed for the mock; re-ran CI locally.
Feature is feature-flagged (guided_diag=false by default). Operators should enable in staging and validate sanitizer policies before enabling in prod. Watch metrics: incident_bot.journey_completion_ratio and incident_bot.handoff_accepted_rate.

Motivation:
We observed frequent noisy handoffs where the on-call engineer lacked a compact, privacy-safe telemetry snapshot at assignment time. That leads to context churn and slow escalations. This PR adds an opt-in enrichment pipeline that captures a lightweight, redacted telemetry bundle at triage assignment and attaches it to the incident-bot handoff card. The goal is to improve mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for first responders and reduce chase-back requests for logs and traces.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a new 'handoff-card' enrichment flow that runs when a triage card is created or reassigned.
- Captures a minimal telemetry snapshot: top-3 relevant logs, a 1s top-span trace summary, recent error-rate deltas, and a small metric rollup. Payload size capped and redacted by default.
- Implements configurable retention TTL and opt-in policy per team (feature flag + team-level annotation).
- Exposes a CLI flag to trigger manual snapshot refresh for a card (incident-bot snapshot refresh).
- Adds observability: metrics for enrichment success/failure, snapshot size histogram, and a handoff-quality signal (hand_off_with_snapshot / handoff_total).
- Adds unit and integration tests + an e2e harness run in CI that exercises the enrichment flow against the test telemetry sandbox.

Design notes and safety: 
- Privacy: snapshots are passed through the existing sanitizer pipeline. The sanitizer now applies an additional TTL-based redaction for attachments that contain stacktraces or PII-like tokens. Teams can opt out via a team annotation.
- Performance: enrichment runs asynchronously with bounded concurrency; worker pool size defaults to 4. We added backpressure logic to avoid amplification of alert storms (cards older than 5 minutes skip enrichment when system load > 80%).
- Fail-open: if enrichment fails, the handoff card still posts; failures are recorded in metrics and retried with exponential backoff.

Files changed (high level):
- cmd/incident-bot/main.go: add CLI switch --refresh-snapshot and feature-flag wiring.
- service/handoff/enricher.go: new module implementing capture + sanitize + attach.
- service/handoff/worker_pool.go: bounded async worker implementation and backpressure heuristics.
- web/ui/handoff_card.tsx: UI for showing snapshot summary with 'view details' and 'request-redaction' actions.
- infra/feature_flags.yaml: new flag triage.snapshot_enrichment (default: false).
- telemetry/metrics.yaml: new metrics and dashboards definitions.
- tests/integration/handoff_enrichment_test.go: integration harness against telemetry sandbox.
- docs/handbook/handoff_enrichment.md: operational runbook for teams to opt-in/out.

Commits (summary):
- 2f9b2c9 feature: initial enricher scaffolding and worker pool
- 7a0d1f3 sanitizer: add TTL redaction rule and safer token regex
- c44b3a1 ui: display compact snapshot and add manual-refresh button
- 9d3e8a7 ci: integration harness and retry tests
- e6f12b0 docs: handbook entry and runbook

Testing and CI:
- Added unit tests covering sanitizer logic and worker backpressure.
- Integration test spins up the telemetry sandbox (mock traces/logs) and asserts that snapshots are attached and redacted.
- CI initially failed on a flaky test (TestHandoffEnrichment_Retries) due to timing; increased timeouts and added deterministic retry backoff in test harness. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, lint, integration, e2e mock).

Review conversation (abridged):
- Maya Patel: "Love the safety-first approach. Please call out the retention policy UI surface and make sure the default is conservative."

Motivation: production tenants with mixed traffic patterns (chatty low-latency requests + occasional long-context completions) are paying for overly aggressive prefill and conservative quant profiles. This PR introduces a new runtime component, 'workload-concierge', that (1) prioritizes prefill/cache population for requests most likely to improve unit economics and latency, and (2) runs a lightweight quant annealer that gradually relaxes quantization aggressiveness for stable cohorts while keeping a rollback path when quality signals degrade.

What this implements: workload-concierge has two logical modules: prefill-prioritizer (Go, integrated into the serving runtime scheduler) and quant-annealer (Python controller that emits profile recommendations). The prioritizer uses a small moving-window estimate of per-request marginal token cost and expected latency benefit (based on KV hit-rate impact) to decide which inflight requests should prefill KV or skip prefill under heavy contention. The quant-annealer consumes sampling telemetry and evaluation deltas and produces tenant-scoped quant profiles using a conservative hill-climb with backpressure thresholds.

High-level config example added to defaults.yaml (single-line form): "prefill_prioritizer: {enabled: true, score_window_s: 30, econ_threshold: 0.02}". The annealer exposes a dry-run mode and a safe-apply mode tied to Linear tickets.

Why this is safe: default behavior is opt-in per-tenant; conservative thresholds and an automatic rollback timeout are in place. We added end-to-end invariants for throughput and sample-eval false-positive rate. Rollout plan: staged canary on dedicated pool -> gradual tenant opt-in via console flags -> wide rollout in 2 weeks if metrics hold.

Related: ENG-3642 (tenant warmstart economics), ENG-3701 (quant rollback automation), SUP-1123 (customer report of cold-prefill cost spikes).
3 commits: 1) runtime: add prefill prioritizer hook and scoring API; 2) tooling: introduce quant-annealer controller, CLI and dry-run; 3) defaults & tests: config defaults, unit/e2e tests and telemetry dashboards. Includes small helper refactors in scheduler to accept prioritizer callbacks.
Diego Morales (reviewer): Can you add a guard to ensure we don't prefill for requests below 16 tokens? Small requests got worse in quick local tests.
Asha Patel (author): Good catch — added token-length guard and unit tests (see prefill_scoring_test.go). Also added an override flag for edge cases.
Lena Fischer (reviewer): The annealer looks promising but we need an explicit signal for QA regressions (metric name and threshold). Please add a runbook-based alarm and do not auto-apply if eval-sample-size < 200.
Asha Patel: Added eval-sample-size check and a playbook stub in docs/ops/prefill-and-quant-guidance.md. The annealer now refuses safe-apply when sample size is insufficient.
Jordan Kim (approver): Verified end-to-end on canary pool; recorded latency/unit-econ delta. Approving with one follow-up to validate behavior under extreme write pressure.
CI bot: initial CI run failed (flake in e2e prefill smoke test). Reran job; all checks passed on rerun.
Canary results (10 tenants over 48h): median p95 latency +2ms, KV hit-rate improvement 7% for targeted cohorts, estimated average token cost reduction 3.4% for workloads with >10% cacheable context. One tenant showed quality-regression at extreme quantization; annealer rolled back profile automatically per policy.
Introduce workload-concierge with prefill prioritizer and quant annealer. Opt-in per-tenant. Reduces unit token cost for cacheable workloads and provides safe automated quant profile relaxation with automatic rollback. See docs/ops/prefill-and-quant-guidance.md for rollout steps.
Monitor prefiller_econ_{tenant} dashboards for 72h
Run canary smoke test nightly for 5 nights
Create Linear task ENG-3750 to add tenant-level opt-out via API
Enable feature gate 'workload_concierge' for canary pool only. Ensure telemetry retention 30d for prefiller_econ.* metrics before wide rollout. Annealer requires eval-sample-size >= 200 to safe-apply; enforce in operator config.

payload.body:
Context
As part of the Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding program (ENG-4821), we need a low-latency, human-visible signal when breakers start shedding (OPEN) and when they recover (HALF_OPEN/CLOSED). The current workflow relies on dashboards/alerts only; during incidents this increases time-to-diagnosis and contributes to duplicate triage.

This PR teaches incident-bot to announce breaker state transitions into Slack (#incidents and #eng-oncall) with:
- Transition summary (CLOSED → OPEN, OPEN → HALF_OPEN, HALF_OPEN → CLOSED)
- Scope (region, route, model selector, tenant/tier when available)
- Top contributing signal(s) (queue depth, token/sec saturation, dependency health)
- Links to dashboards and the oncall runbook
- A short “recommended actions” block aligned with the runbook

Behavior
- Posts OPEN transitions to both #incidents and #eng-oncall.
- Posts recovery transitions (OPEN→HALF_OPEN, HALF_OPEN→CLOSED) to #eng-oncall only by default to reduce noise.
- Dedupes repeated OPEN transitions for the same breaker_key within a configurable window (default 10m).
- If event payload does not include route/model details, message still posts with breaker_key + region and a note about missing dimensions.

Implementation details
- Adds a new event consumer for `overload.breaker_state_changed` from the internal event bus (same transport as alert notifications).
- Introduces `BreakerKey` normalization to keep dedupe stable (region + route_group + model_selector + tier + policy_id).
- Adds Slack message formatting using Block Kit, including:
  - severity coloring (OPEN = danger, HALF_OPEN = warning, CLOSED = good)
  - buttons: “Open dashboard”, “Open runbook”, “Search logs”
- Uses `dashboards.redwood.ai` and `runbooks.redwood.ai` deep links with query params prefilled (region, time range last 30m, breaker_key).

Recommended actions (message content)
- OPEN: Verify whether this is capacity saturation vs downstream brownout; check shed-rate + runtime queue depth; confirm Retry-After is being set; page routing owner if fallback loops suspected.
- HALF_OPEN: Watch error budget burn + shed rate; do not raise caps until p95 stabilizes.
- CLOSED: Capture incident timestamp window; confirm alerts cleared; annotate postmortem with breaker_key and top signals.

Safety/guardrails
- Hard cap of 1 Slack message per breaker_key per channel per 10 minutes (configurable).
- Suppresses messages for canary-only breakers unless `announce_canary=true` is set (default false).
- Sanitizes tenant IDs: only posts tenant slug if explicitly marked as `shareable=true` in the event payload.

Testing
- Unit tests for normalization, dedupe window, channel routing, and link generation.
- Integration-style test with a mocked Slack client to validate Block Kit payload.

Rollout
- Deploy behind flag `INCIDENT_BOT_BREAKER_ANNOUNCEMENTS=enabled`.
- Start enabled in staging; prod enablement to follow canary rollout go/no-go email thread.

Screenshots (example Slack message)
[OPEN] Hosted breaker opened: us-east / chat.completions / model=rw-llama-3-70b (tier=self-serve)
Signals: runtime.queue_depth_p95=182, token_saturation=0.93
Shed rate: 14% (last 5m)
Actions: Check Overload Protection dashboard; consider temporary max_tokens cap policy; verify Retry-After present; evaluate fallback policy health
Buttons: Open dashboard | Open runbook | Search logs

Notes
- This PR does not change alerting rules; it is a complementary “human paging context” path.
- Follow-up: thread-safe in-memory dedupe should move to Redis if we run multiple incident-bot replicas (tracked in ENG-4869).
Rafael Mendes: Can we avoid posting recoveries to #incidents? That channel gets very noisy during multi-signal events.
Christine Wong (author): Yep — switched default so only OPEN goes to #incidents; recoveries stay in #eng-oncall unless `announce_recoveries_to_incidents=true` is set.
Aisha Bello: Links should land on the new overload dashboard, not the generic runtime overview. Also time range should be 30m aligned with our oncall doc.
Christine Wong (author): Updated `dashboards.go` to point at Overload Protection dashboard uid=overload-protection and default range=now-30m..now. Added a test to assert query params.
Logan Wright: Dedupe currently uses process memory; incident-bot is single replica today but we’ve talked about scaling it. Add a comment + follow-up issue so we don’t forget.
Christine Wong (author): Added a TODO in `dedupe.go` and filed ENG-4869 for Redis-backed dedupe if/when we go multi-replica.
Peter Holtz: Please ensure we don’t leak enterprise tenant identifiers into Slack. What’s the source of `tenant_slug`?
Christine Wong (author): Event payload now includes `tenant.shareable` boolean from control plane; we only include slug if shareable=true. Otherwise the message shows `tenant=redacted`. Added test coverage.
Rafael Mendes: One more thing: for OPEN transitions, include a single-line hint about Retry-After to prevent retry storms.
Christine Wong (author): Added to the recommended actions block and linked to the runbook section anchor `#retry-after-and-client-behavior`.
- incident-bot posts circuit breaker OPEN/HALF_OPEN/CLOSED transitions with dashboard/runbook links
- messages include recommended actions and suppression to reduce alert spam
payload.title: Announce circuit breaker state transitions to #incidents and #eng-oncall

Motivation: We observed a class of in-production incidents where SSE fragment splits inside escaped JSON strings or multi-byte UTF-8 sequences could cause downstream consumers to see re-ordered function/tool call boundaries or emit malformed partial JSON. This PR introduces a lightweight runtime 'reconstruction guard' that assigns per-fragment fidelity credits and a deterministic handback protocol to ensure toolcall boundaries remain ordered across retransmit/replay and partial-frame repair. Summary of changes: 1) runtime/streaming: add FragmentFidelityLedger and a reconstruction guard that tracks credit windows and stalls handback until a safe boundary is observed or the ledger times out; 2) sse/parser: introduce escape-aware tail rewriter to avoid splitting inside escapes and normalize trailing delimiters before emission; 3) compat/openai: emit X-Redwood-Handback-Fidelity header and annotate stream events with handback_id so OpenAI-compat clients can prefer resumable handoff points; 4) protocol: deterministic toolcall handoff algorithm that converts ephemeral function-call tokens into ordered handback checkpoints to prevent interleaving when fragments arrive out-of-order; 5) tests: large suite of synthetic fragment replays and property tests that simulate jittered, coalesced, and reordered chunks. Implementation notes: The reconstruction guard uses a small in-memory ledger per connection (bounded to 32 entries) and a sliding credit window to avoid unbounded buffering. When ledger credit is insufficient, the connection flushes an escape-normalized delimiter and advances a handback checkpoint; this behavior preserves low-latency in common cases while preventing rare misorders. The OpenAI-compat annotations are backward compatible: older clients ignore handback_id and continue to operate normally. Checklist: - [x] Core runtime changes implemented and covered by unit tests - [x] End-to-end tests with python and ts SDKs - [x] Backwards compatibility validated against existing OpenAI-compat integration tests - [x] Performance microbenchmarks show <0.6% median latency regression on p4d for synthetic workloads - [x] Feature flagged behind runtime.feature.streaming_reconstruct_guard rollout plan: feature off in production initial cut; enable for 10% traffic with canary instrumentation and latency/error dashboards; expand to 100% after 48h with no regressions. Related: ENG-2407 describes incident notes and replay corpus. This description includes small illustrative pseudo-patch: "if (fragment.endsWith('\\') || insideEscape(fragment)) normalizeEscapeTail(fragment)" which is implemented in sse/parser/tail_rewrite.go.
Fix partial-JSON reconstruction when SSE fragments split inside escaped sequences
Introduce reconstruction guard that prevents tool/function-call reorderings during stream replay
Improve OpenAI-compat layer to surface handback-fidelity metadata for client heuristics
Unit tests: 98 new cases covering escape tails, multi-byte utf8 splits, and toolcall order; Integration: SDK e2e verifies end-to-end ordered function calls under chunk jitter; Perf: microbench suite on p4d and p3 shows negligible median impact and tail P95 within 2%
Feature gated behind runtime.feature.streaming_reconstruct_guard. To roll back disable the flag in the feature service and restart stream-workers in a staged fashion. If misordering symptoms appear, enable compat/openai.vet_handback_checks and consult the fragment replay logs (tag: fragment-replay).
Mateo Ruiz: Please explain how the ledger bound interacts with long-running streams; are we at risk of dropping fidelity for very chatty sessions? Ava Chen: Ledger is per-connection and bounded to 32 entries by default; for chatty sessions we prefer more frequent handbacks so credit churn is lower rather than unbounded buffering. Janelle Park: Can you show the perf delta on p3/p4? Ava Chen: Microbenchmarks included, median latency regressions are <0.6% on p4d and tail changes are within noise. Samuel Becker: Add a unit test for splitting inside a 4-byte UTF8 codepoint. Ava Chen: Added property test that injects multibyte boundary splits and verifies JSON reassembly and call order. Mateo Ruiz: Approved. Janelle Park: Approved. Samuel Becker: Approved after requested test added.

payload.body: Motivation: Oncall sessions often need deterministic replays of a narrow telemetry window but doing so risks leaking secrets and overwhelms responders with noisy signals. This PR adds a lightweight, local replay CLI that produces sandboxed, sanitized replay bundles and a signal attenuation layer to reduce noise and surface probable root signals without changing production telemetry. Key points: 1) sanitized replayer CLI (cmd/replay) that consumes a sampled bundle and replays events into a local sandbox process, applying redaction rules and rate attenuation; 2) redactor module with configurable field filters, regex scrubbing, canonicalization hooks and a safety whitelist to prevent accidental exposure of PII/KV payloads; 3) attenuation scheduler that downweights repetitive noisy signals (heartbeats, verbose debug logs) using a tunable decay and per-source weights; 4) playbook hinter that emits suggested runbook steps based on the top-attenuated signals detected; 5) sandbox manifest and e2e harness that runs the replay in an isolated container for postmortem workflows. Checklist: - [x] core replay engine and CLI - [x] redaction schema and safety whitelist - [x] attenuation heuristics + config - [x] docs and usage guide - [x] unit tests for redaction/attenuation - [x] sandbox e2e - [x] security review signoff Design notes: The redactor applies three passes (schema strip, regex scrub, canonical token masking). Attenuation is a probabilistic decayer that assigns a priority score per signal; signals below threshold are throttled in replay but kept in the bundle for auditability. The CLI exposes --attenuation-profile, --whitelist, --dry-run, and --sanitized-output flags. Commits summary: see commits field. Files touched: high-level list provided; changes are intentionally modular to keep runtime surface small. Testing: Added unit tests covering corner cases for nested JSON redaction and attenuation with synthetic traces. Added e2e sandbox that spins a containerized mock service and verifies end-to-end that sanitized replays do not leak raw tokens and that attenuation reduces noise by >=60% on synthetic traces. Review conversation: Amit: "Nice separation of concerns; can we avoid global state in attenuation scheduler?" Maya: "Refactored scheduler to take an explicit context object and made state per-run; PTAL." Jules: "Redaction rules look comprehensive but add example of a false-positive case where service IDs could be masked; also add a defensive fallback if whitelist misconfigured." Maya: "Added examples and a validation step that fails fast if whitelist would redact all identifiers in a bundle." Kai: "CI e2e flaked once for docker startup timeout; add retry." Maya: "Added 2s backoff and CI job retry wrapper; re-ran." CI summary: Initial run failed due to a flaky e2e container start (timeout). Flaky test tolerance added in scripts/ci/sandbox-e2e.yml and tests adjusted to wait-for-ready; rerun completed and all checks passed (unit, linters, sandbox-e2e). Security review: security@sre signed off on redaction heuristics and whitelist fallback. Merge: Squash-merged to main after approvals (Amit, Jules). Notes for operators: attenuation profiles live in incidents/attenuation_profiles.yaml; default profile tuned for oncall short-replays. Usage example: "replay bundle.jsonl --sanitized-output sanitized.jsonl --attenuation-profile quick-oncall". Rollout plan: feature gated behind incident-bot feature flag "replay.sanitized.v1"; soft launch to internal SRE for two weeks, then enable by request for customers. Backout: no production runtime change; removing feature simply deletes CLI binary. Mentioned Linear tickets: ENG-1428 implements core engine; SRE-73 defines attenuation profiles and validation. Merge metadata: merge_method: squash; merged_at: 2025-11-02; merge_commit: "squash: telemetry sanitized replayer + attenuation (Maya Chen)"
payload.title: Telemetry Sanitized Replayer and Signal Attenuation Tooling

Motivation: oncall handoffs are noisy and fragile—important context gets lost when responders paste ad-hoc notes or attachments. This PR introduces an interactive, compact handoff card UI and server-side representation that attaches a tamper-evident provenance token, an elapsed-timer anchored to the incident start time, and an optional severity-delta field to communicate how the oncall perceives trend since the last handoff. Goals: reduce cognitive load during handoff, make provenance auditable, and provide a small, copyable payload for downstream automation (pager bridges, runbook runners).

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a new handoff-card server model (handoff/cards.go) that stores summary, anchored_provenance_token, incident_start_ts, timer_offset_sec, severity_delta, and sanitized_attachments metadata. Tokens are HMAC-SHA256 over canonical handoff fields with key rotation hooks.
- Exposes a small REST endpoint POST /api/v1/incidents/:id/hands that accepts compact JSON and returns a canonical card payload and short-lived attachment URLs.
- Implements interactive web component src/ui/handoff-card.tsx which renders the compact card, starts a live elapsed timer calculated from incident_start_ts + timer_offset_sec, and provides copy-to-clipboard (compact JSON) and 'attach sanitized snippet' flows.
- Adds CLI helper cli/handoffctl (subcommand 'card create') for engineers to create cards from terminals and include sanitized logs via --snip.
- Adds audit logging and wire-level TTL: cards are immutable once created and tokens expire after default 30 days; attachments default to 72 hours.
- Adds unit + e2e tests and docs for runbook integration.

Implementation notes:
- Security: anchored_provenance_token uses a server-side HMAC key stored in KMS; the code includes rotate_provenance_key() with a migration path so old tokens remain verifiable. Tokens do not expose secrets and are small (base64).
- Performance: payloads are intentionally compact; the UI requests only metadata for the last 25 handoffs on the incident list to avoid heavy payloads. Attachments are stored in the existing ephemeral-bucket service; we reuse the signed-url pattern.
- Rollout plan: feature gate off by default. Console feature flag `handoff_cards_v1` added. We will enable for 10% of incidents, monitor oncall latency and card-create errors.

Checklist:
- [x] server model + migration
- [x] REST endpoint + validation
- [x] UI component + accessibility labels
- [x] CLI helper + docs snippet
- [x] audit logging and tests
- [x] feature flag and rollout notes

Commits (summary):
- 1) introduce handoff card model + migration
- 2) add provenance token generation and verification utilities
- 3) REST endpoint + controller + validation
- 4) UI component + client-side timer and copy helper
- 5) CLI helper and integration tests
- 6) docs and release-notes entry

Files changed (high level):
- server/handoff/cards.go (new): model + HMAC helpers
- server/handoff/handlers.go: controller wiring and validation
- migrations/20260210_add_handoff_card_table.sql: DB migration
- src/ui/handoff-card.tsx: new interactive component + styles
- cli/handoffctl/main.go: new CLI command path
- ephemeral-bucket/integration.go: TTL handling for signed URLs (small refactor)
- test/e2e/handoff_card_flow.test.ts: end-to-end coverage for create/list/copy
- docs/handbook/handoff-cards.md: usage, security notes, rollout checklist

Review thread (selected):
- Diego Alvarez (review): "Nice ergonomics. Two asks: 1) can we keep the card payload <1KB by default (avoid embedding snippets)? 2) ensure the timer is timezone-agnostic and always anchored to server incident_start_ts to avoid client clock skew issues."
- Maya (author): "Agree on size constraint—attachments are only metadata + signed URL, snippets are uploaded separately. Timer uses server timestamp and client uses local monotonic timer after initial delta. Added unit tests to validate clock-drift tolerance (see commit 4)."
- Nina Shah (security): "Provenance token looks fine but we need KMS key rotation docs and audit linkage. Also add an explicit expiration claim to the token to prevent reuse."
- Maya: "Added rotate_provenance_key() and documented the verification fallback for previous key IDs. Token now encodes expiry (exp) and a key_id. Updated docs and added audit log entries in handlers."
- Roberto Kim (qa): "e2e was flaky around signed URL expiry in test environment; tests assume 72h TTL and CI mock used 1h. Please parameterize TTL in test fixtures."
- Maya: "Fixed tests to parametrize TTL via test config; CI uses short TTL to exercise refresh logic."

CI summary: initial run had a lint failure (UI styling variable); second run failed one flaky e2e related to signed-url mocking; third run passed all checks. Checks run: unit tests (server), ui-tests (lint + jest), e2e (playwright), security-scan. All green on final run.

Migration & compatibility: The migration adds a new table handoff_cards and backfills nothing. Existing oncall flows are unchanged. Feature is behind flag so no runtime impact until enabled. There is a small DB index added on incident_id + created_at to keep list queries fast.

Telemetry / observability: New metrics exposed: handoff.card.create.count, handoff.card.create.latency_ms, handoff.card.copy.count, handoff.card.attach.upload_errors. Alerts: handoff-card-create-error-rate > 0.5% for 5m triggers paging to infra. Dashboard: added compact handoff card panel to oncall console (per-incident).

Release notes (short): "Add interactive handoff cards with anchored provenance tokens and elapsed-timer to improve oncall handoffs; feature is feature-flagged and off by default."

Merge details: merged via squash on 2026-02-15 after final approval from Diego and Nina. Post-merge: feature flag created, doc entry added to runbook, and a 10% rollout scheduled for 2026-02-22.

payload.body:
Context: On-call teams often create temporary ad-hoc playbooks or tweak runbooks during incidents. These transient playbooks are valuable for fast mitigation but are hard to audit and can be a vector for accidental or malicious misconfiguration. Motivation: provide an auditable, short-lived playbook signing mechanism plus a suppression ledger that records alert suppression windows and their provenance. Goals: 1) Allow engineers to create ephemeral playbooks that are cryptographically signed and automatically expire; 2) Record every suppression (manual or API) in a ledger that preserves who requested it, the reason, link to signed playbook (if applicable), and automatic expiry; 3) Surface ledger entries in the incident timeline and export to audit logs; 4) Offer CLI helpers and a small UI surface to create/surface signed playbooks and suppression entries. High-level change summary: - New signing service (playbook-signer) that integrates with customer or Redwood KMS (pluggable) and issues short-lived signatures embedded in playbook metadata. Signed playbooks can be verified by the incident-bot runtime before execution. - Suppression ledger API + storage: append-only ledger (Postgres-backed using existing eventstore pattern) with strict write paths: api, cli, and authorized webhook. Ledger entries include origin, signer id (if playbook-signed), suppression window, and optional runbook_id. - Feature-flag guarded rollout: incident_bot.features.ephemeral_signing and .suppression_ledger. Defaults off in main, enabled for beta orgs. - CLI: rb-sign and rb-suppress commands to create signed playbooks and ledger entries; output includes signed manifest and human-readable audit line. - UI: small addition to incident detail pane showing active suppressions and a link to download the signed playbook manifest. - Migration: adds a new table suppression_ledger_v1 and a compact index for query by active window. Migration script included. - Tests: unit coverage for signer, ledger append and verification; integration test exercising end-to-end: create signed playbook -> verify -> execute guarded run -> ledger entry created and surfaced to timeline. - Security: signing keys go through KMS abstraction; private key material never stored by incident-bot. Signing operations are performed by a short-lived token service; audit events emitted to the existing audit pipeline. - Backwards compatibility: unsigned playbooks still accepted if feature flag off; when on, unverified playbooks are rejected for orgs that opted into enforcement. - Docs: commands, API endpoints, feature flag instructions, and rollback steps included in docs/operations/ephemeral-playbooks.md. Rollout plan: staged across beta orgs for 2 weeks, gather telemetry on acceptance rates and any failed verifications, then widen. Migration note: migration creates table and index and backfills no data; suppression ledger relies on append-only writes and uses existing housekeeping for TTL on expired entries. Risks and mitigations: potential false positives if clocks drift (mitigated by allowing 30s skew and validating at KMS layer); extra latency on playbook execution when signature verification runs (measured ~12ms in p99 on staging, acceptable).
add: playbook signer service + KMS adapter (playbook_signer.py, kms_adapter.py)
feat: suppression ledger DB model, API, and append-only writer (ledger/model.py, ledger/api.py)
chore: migration SQL for suppression_ledger_v1 and index
feat(cli): rb-sign and rb-suppress commands and integration with auth/cli
tests: unit + integration tests for signer and ledger; add e2e fixture
docs: add operational guide and rollout checklist
fix: tighten permission checks on ledger write path after reviewer feedback
ci: add new matrix entry for signer KMS mock to integration pipeline
Daniel Cho: LGTM overall. Please add an audit event for failed signature verifications (security wants visibility).
Author(Ava Patel): Added emit_audit_event.go call on failed verify and unit test for failure path.
Priya Nandakumar: Can we avoid blocking urgent mitigations when KMS is temporarily unavailable? Suggest a degraded mode that allows human-approved unsigned runs with an extra ledger entry.
Author(Ava Patel): Implemented a 'degraded_run' flag gated by org policy; CLI will refuse degraded runs unless user provides justification, which is written to ledger. Documented the policy in ops guide.
Ethan Brooks: Minor nit: expand integration test to include clock skew case; tests currently mock perfect time.
Author(Ava Patel): Added a 30s skew test case and CI matrix entry using timewarp fixture.
Priya Nandakumar: Approving after the degraded-run note and audit event change.
Daniel Cho: Approved and merged.
CI Bot: All checks passed on rerun.
Added ephemeral playbook signing and an append-only suppression ledger. Operators can create signed, time-limited playbooks and record suppressions with provenance. Feature behind flags: incident_bot.features.ephemeral_signing and incident_bot.features.suppression_ledger. CLI tools (rb-sign/rb-suppress) and a small UI card are included. Backwards-compatible by default. See docs/operations/ephemeral-playbooks.md for rollout and rollback steps.

Summary: Add an ephemeral attachment store for incident-bundles (minidumps, short trace slices, sanitized log excerpts) plus a playbook pre-seeder that runs lightweight telemetry queries in the background when an alert is routed to a responder. Motivation: On-call reaction time is dominated by two things: locating relevant traces/log snippets and picking a first-action playbook. This PR implements a small, opt-in attachment cache with TTL and a separate pre-seeder that enqueues a set of curated queries for the alert context so responders see prepopulated results and playbook suggestions within seconds. Design: - Ephemeral attachment store: small S3-like bucket abstraction backed by Redis metadata and object storage in the private bucket; attachments have a 1h default TTL, automatic sanitizers to remove PII, and a signed short-lived URL exposed in the incident-bundle. - Playbook pre-seeder: ruleset-based query templates (per-service + alert-signature) that execute asynchronously at low priority; results are stored in the attachment store as JSON blobs and referenced by the incident summary. - Opt-in controls: per-team toggles in oncall settings, and a lightweight rate limiter per-project to avoid heavy query storms. - Safety and compliance: sanitizer runs on upload, we emit audit events for every attachment and query execution. Implementation notes: - New modules: src/attachments/ (store, sanitizer, signer), src/preseed/ (rules engine, scheduler), api handlers: src/handlers/attachment_routes.py and src/handlers/preseed_hooks.py - DB: metadata persisted in existing incidents Postgres table with small addition (ephemeral_attachments jsonb, preseed_jobs jsonb). Migration included. - Telemetry: add metrics: incidentbot.attachment.uploads, .sanitizer.errors, .preseed.jobs.started, .preseed.jobs.latency, .preseed.cache.hit. - Backward compatibility: incident payloads without preseed metadata behave unchanged; attachments are optional. Testing & CI: - Unit tests for sanitizer, signer, preseed rule matching (tests/test_attachments.py, tests/test_preseed.py). - Integration test that simulates an alert and verifies preseeded results are visible in the incident summary within 3s. - Load smoke that verifies preseed queries are scheduled at low priority (ci job preseed-smoke). Checklist: - [x] Core store + signer + sanitizer implemented - [x] Playbook rules engine + scheduler implemented - [x] DB migration + simple rollback script - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Docs for feature and admin toggle - [x] Added metrics and dashboards link - [x] Feature gated behind per-team opt-in - [x] Manual verification on staging with synthetic alerts Backwards compatibility and rollout: Feature is behind a per-org feature flag (off by default). Ops can enable per-team; default TTL 1h can be configured. Rollout plan: opt-in to a pilot org, monitor metrics, then enable gradually. Risks & mitigations: - Query storm: preseed scheduler uses priority queues and rate-limits per-project; immediate mitigation is to reduce per-team concurrency. - PII leakage: sanitizer covers common patterns and we added an allowlist/denylist; we run additional audits during pilot. Release notes: Adds an opt-in ephemeral attachment store and playbook pre-seeding for faster on-call triage. Admins can control via oncall settings. See docs link in changed files. Related: ENG-7891 (pilot), SUP-312 (customer request).
Erik Tan: Please add a metric for preseed cache hits and a counter for sanitizer rejections. We need these for pilot dashboards.
Priya Menon: Added incidentbot.preseed.cache.hit and incidentbot.sanitizer.rejections in latest commit. Also added Grafana panel JSON to docs.
Maya Brooks: The default TTL of 1h seems long for some teams; can we make it configurable per-team and add an env var to cap max TTL?
Priya Menon: TTL made configurable via team settings UI and .env REDWOOD_EPHEMERAL_MAX_TTL default 3600 - documented and unit-tested.
Luca Rossi: Security review: ensure signed URLs expire in <5m and sanitizer covers stacktrace PII patterns.
Priya Menon: Signed URLs now default to 4m and sanitizer ruleset extended to scrub common stacktrace paths and token-like strings. Added integration test asserting no raw tokens in stored attachments.
Opt-in ephemeral attachment caching and playbook pre-seeding for faster triage. Configurable TTL, per-team opt-in, sanitizer and audit events. Pilot with ENG-7891.
To enable for a team: - Toggle feature flag in Admin > Oncall > Ephemeral Attachments - Monitor metrics: incidentbot.preseed.jobs.started, incidentbot.preseed.cache.hit, incidentbot.attachment.uploads - If preseed job latency rises, reduce REDWOOD_PRESEED_CONCURRENCY or lower per-team concurrency via Admin UI - Rollback: toggle feature flag off; migration includes a rollback SQL to clear ephemeral metadata.
payload.title: Ephemeral diagnostic attachment store and playbook pre-seeder to speed on-call triage

payload.body:
## Summary
Adds a dedicated incident template + lightweight playbook for Provision-to-Ready / Dedicated fleet bring-up failures (nodes stuck in Provisioning/Validating, mass quarantine, image/driver mismatch, join failures, NCCL smoke flakes).

This is intended to standardize the minimum info we capture in #incidents and in the incident doc so SRE/Infra/Platform can triage quickly and we can compute time-to-ready and failure-rate impacts without back-and-forth.

## Why
During the staged rollout we saw a few common patterns:
- Missing pool metadata (region/GPU type/image channel), which slowed down correlating failures to a specific rollout.
- Unclear ownership handoff (Infra vs Platform vs SRE) depending on whether the failure is “can’t join cluster” vs “validation gate failing” vs “readiness service/API regressions”.
- Links to dashboards/runbooks living in different places and being pasted inconsistently.

This PR adds:
1) A new incident template “Provision-to-Ready / Fleet Readiness failure” in incident-bot.
2) Required fields (bot enforces) for the most important scoping + debugging info.
3) One-page playbook section (first 10 minutes) with quick links and suggested owner rotations.

## Template: required fields
- Incident start time (UTC) + detection source (alert name / human report)
- Customer impact statement (Dedicated pools impacted? capacity shortfall? time-to-ready regression?)
- Affected region(s)
- Pool ID(s) / cluster(s)
- GPU type(s) (A100/H100/etc)
- Image channel + version (candidate/stable + build id)
- Current readiness states distribution (Allocated/Provisioning/Validating/Ready/Quarantined)
- Failing step(s) + top failure reason(s) (e.g., kubelet join, driver parity, NCCL smoke, perf canary)
- Rollout flags enabled? (region/pool constraints)
- Immediate mitigation chosen (pause rollout, reimage, drain/quarantine override, rollback image channel)

## Playbook: first 10 minutes
- Confirm scope using the readiness summary endpoint (counts by state + top failures)
- Check Provision-to-Ready dashboards (step latency + failure rate heatmap)
- Determine whether failure is:
  A) image bake / driver parity (Infra/Release Eng)
  B) cluster join / node config baseline (Infra)
  C) readiness service / state machine / API issues (Platform)
  D) alerting/metrics/cardinality issues (SRE/Observability)
- Apply “safe” mitigations first:
  - Pause staged rollout flag(s)
  - Stop auto-promotion (candidate->stable)
  - Quarantine only if repeatable hardware/validation failure; avoid mass quarantine until capacity impact is understood
  - Reimage a small sample and re-run validation to confirm whether image rollback is warranted

## Suggested owner rotations
- Incident Commander (IC): SRE oncall
- Primary Responder: Infra/Fleet oncall
- Secondary: Platform Control Plane oncall (readiness service)
- Consult: Release Engineering (image channel/promotion), Security (if image hardening or access control suspected)

## Notes
- Links are intentionally internal and stable (dashboards + runbook + readiness service doc). If any of these URLs change we should update the template rather than relying on manual pastes.

## Screenshots
N/A (template-only change).

## Rollout
Once merged, incident-bot will pick up the new template on next deploy (no config changes required in prod).
Vanessa Ortiz: Can we make sure pool identifiers are required? We lost time last week because we only had “us-east” and no pool id, and the failure mode differed between pools. Also please include “image channel + version” as required (candidate vs stable).

Aisha Bello (author): Yep — updated required fields to include pool_id(s) and image_channel + image_version/build_id. Also added a note to include rollout flags for that region/pool.

Miles Thornton: Love this. Two asks: (1) include the SLO/SLI name in required fields so we can immediately tell if this is burning error budget, and (2) add a reminder about cardinality-safe logging (don’t paste per-node IDs into alert annotations).

Aisha Bello (author): Added “Related SLO/alert name(s)” required field and a playbook bullet re: metrics/cardinality (avoid per-node ids in incident doc; use readiness summary/top failures instead).

Connor O'Brien: Can we add a checkbox for “rollout paused / kill switch enabled” and “image promotion paused” so it’s explicit in the timeline? Also, please align terminology with the staged rollout doc (candidate->stable) rather than “beta/prod”.

Aisha Bello (author): Added checkboxes for rollout pause + promotion pause. Renamed beta/prod to candidate/stable throughout.

Rafael Mendes: +1. Please add a short section on when to open a customer support escalation (if Dedicated pool is impacted) and what info Support needs.

Aisha Bello (author): Added a final section “If customer-facing” with the minimum details for Support (pool id, timestamps, impact summary, mitigation/ETA).

payload.body:
Motivation: On-call handoffs and postmortems often require curating a small set of diagnostic artifacts (logs, span snippets, config lines, short runbook links) and sharing them with a responder or another team. Current workflows involve manual copy/paste or creating large zip bundles; both are error-prone and leak too much context. This change introduces a lightweight 'Clipboard' concept in incident-bot: an ephemeral, scrubbed artifact collector that responders can build interactively (CLI or Slack modal) and then share as a single short link or attach to an incident. The Clipboard is intentionally compact (metadata + pointers + small text snippets) and enforces automated PII scrubbing and retention/audit rules.

What this PR does: Adds a new Clipboard service (API + DB model), a small frontend in the Slack modal flow, a CLI helper rbx clip to create and share clipboards, and a hand-off clipper command that attaches a Clipboard reference to an incident or creates a one-time share link. Key properties: 1) automated scrubbing pipeline using the existing sanitizer library with additional redaction rules for secrets/tokens; 2) manifest.json describing included artifacts and provenance; 3) configurable retention (default 7 days) and audit logging entries for every create/share action; 4) feature-flag gated rollout and RBAC check to prevent cross-tenant exposure.

Design notes: The Clipboard stores short text blobs (max 64KB each) and pointer references to existing storage artifacts (log slices in telemetry, trace IDs). We chose not to allow arbitrary file uploads to keep the surface area small. The share link is a short, opaque token that maps to the Clipboard ID plus an expiry timestamp. All share actions record an audit entry (user, target incident, timestamp) to support later review. Scrubber runs synchronously on small text blobs and asynchronously validates referenced pointers.

Testing & rollout: Unit tests added for sanitizer rules, manifest generation, and DB model. End-to-end test simulates Slack flow + CLI create + attach to incident. The feature is behind feature flag "oncall_clipboard" and will be enabled for internal SRE org first. We also added a migration to introduce clipboard_table with backward-compatible defaults. The migration is small and reversible.

Operational considerations: retention policy is configurable via env var CLIPBOARD_RETENTION_DAYS. Audit logs are shipped to the existing audit stream so SOC teams already ingest them. We added rate limits to the create endpoint to avoid abuse. A small metrics set was added (clip.create, clip.share, clip.scrub_failures). Rollback plan: turn off feature flag and run cleanup job to expire outstanding clips earlier if necessary.
Samir Patel: Nice, this looks useful. A couple of questions: (1) how do we ensure no large logs leak in pointers? (2) will the scrubber handle stack traces with tokens embedded?
Ava Chang: Replying: (1) pointer references are to internal log slice IDs and we enforce a maximum pointer size and an allowlist of sources; the UI warns users if a pointer refers to a large archive. (2) scrubber has a regex/entropy-based rule we added; see sanitizer/rules/clipboard_rules.py — unit tests cover common stack-trace patterns.
Leah Gomez: Please add an explicit opt-out for copying raw environment variables into a clip (security).
Ava Chang: Added a UI checkbox and server-side check to block env var patterns; updated tests to assert rejection.
Ravi Menon: Can we log the full diff of the manifest on attach for audit? Might increase audit volume but helpful.
Ava Chang: We log a compact manifest summary (counts + hashes) and store the full manifest in the audit S3 bucket; added a note to ops-runbook about retention.
Samir Patel: CI flake in e2e; re-run tests after addressing timing (fixed by adding retry/backoff).
CI Bot: Tests passed after re-run. Approved by Samir and Leah.
Add an on-call Clipboard feature: small, scrubbed, shareable collections of diagnostic artifacts; CLI helper rbx clip; Slack modal integration; retention and audit controls. Feature behind 'oncall_clipboard' feature flag; enabled for internal SRE first.
Feature flag: oncall_clipboard=false by default. Env: CLIPBOARD_RETENTION_DAYS (default 7). Audit stream: clipboard.audit.* metrics. If disabling, run cleanup job: scripts/cleanup/expire_clipboards.py

payload.body:
Motivation: On-call responders often need a terse, actionable summary of an incident plus a tiny set of telemetry "anchors" (small, replayable traces/log slices and metric snapshots) that let them triage fast without chasing large exports. This PR introduces a compact on-call cheatsheet generator and an anchored diagnostics collector integrated into incident-bot.

What it does: Generates a one-screen cheatsheet for an alert containing: incident summary (one-line), top-3 correlated signals, likely impacted services, recent deploys, suggested immediate mitigations, and up to three "anchors" — small, time-bounded telemetry bundles (tracelets, metric windows, and sanitized log excerpts) with stable anchor IDs. Anchors are small (<= 200KB each) and designed to be fetched or replayed by debuggers.

Design notes: Cheatsheet generation is deterministic: we run a ranking heuristic over tags and signal deltas, then format a markdown blob for chat posting and a compact JSON for the Console. Anchors are assembled from short queries against the telemetry store (traces and logs) and passed through the redaction filter pipeline before packaging. Anchors reference immutable anchor IDs so responders can request fresh fetches or cached copies. Anchors expire by default after 24 hours and are auto-pruned.

Security & privacy: All anchors pass the standard sanitizers (PII redaction, credential scrubber). Anchor storage is ephemeral and encrypted at rest (uses existing KMS key alias incident-bot/anchors). We added rate limits and size limits to prevent accidental data exfiltration. Customer-configurable policies allow turning off log anchors for privacy-sensitive deployments.

Implementation summary: Adds a new service command cheatsheet.generate (server-side), an incident-bot plugin that posts the cheatsheet to the incident channel and attaches anchor IDs, and a small CLI tool to fetch or replay an anchor locally for responders. The generator reuses existing ranking libs and the telemetry sampler but introduces a lightweight anchor packager and an anchor metadata registry.

Testing & rollout: Unit tests cover ranking, formatting and redaction. Integration tests exercise end-to-end generation with a sandboxed telemetry store. We validated size/latency: cheatsheet generation < 200ms on average; anchor assembly 350-500ms depending on trace depth. Rollout plan: feature-flagged by default off; enable for SRE on-call team in canary (2 weeks), then broader opt-in for oncall rotation.

Ops notes: Anchor pruning is a periodic job; added metrics for cheatsheet generation latency, anchor creation count, and redaction failures. Defaults are conservative (max 3 anchors, 200KB each, 24h TTL).

Related: Builds on ENG-1242 (cheatsheet ranking work) and SRE-998 (telemetry sampler improvements).

Files changed and diffs are intentionally small and focused on plumbing, UX text, and safety checks.
Arun Patel (2025-11-08): Overall nice. Two asks: (1) please document TTL + opt-out in ops/README, (2) can we cap total anchor count per incident?
Maya Chen (2025-11-08): Responding - added TTL config and per-incident cap default=3, documented in ops/README and featureflags.yaml
Sofia Martinez (2025-11-09): Minor - prefer anchor IDs be UUIDv7-style for monotonicity. Also suggest exposing redaction failure metric.
Maya Chen (2025-11-09): Switched to UUIDv7, added metric telemetry.anchor.redaction.failures with unit tests
Evelyn Park (2025-11-11): Verified e2e in staging, some flaky test around trace sampler; requested flake fix before merge.
Maya Chen (2025-11-12): Flake fixed by debouncing sampler calls + added CI retry, all green now.
Adds an opt-in compact on-call cheatsheet generator that posts a short summary and up to three ephemeral, redacted telemetry anchors (tracelets/log excerpts/metric windows) to incident channels. Feature is behind a feature flag and disabled by default. Admins can configure TTL, max anchors per-incident, and opt-out for logs.
Reduce time-to-first-action for oncall responders by providing high-signal, low-noise context and tiny replayable telemetry bundles without requiring large exports.
Unit + integration tests added. E2E run in staging against a snapshot telemetry store. Observed median generation latency <200ms; anchor assembly median ~420ms. CI matrix includes a mac job to catch OS-specific build issues.
Feature-flagged: 1) enable for SRE rotation (canary) for 2 weeks, 2) open opt-in to all oncall teams, 3) enable org-wide after 6 weeks if no major issues. Rollback: flip flag off to stop further anchor creation; pruning job will continue until anchors expire or pruning is disabled.
Low-medium: primary risks are accidental data leakage (mitigated by mandatory redaction + size limits) and transient CPU/memory spikes during anchor packaging (mitigated with batching and memory caps).
This is intended to be a conservative, ergonomics-first addition. The implementation is intentionally small to make reviews easy and to allow fast rollback if needed.
payload.title: Compact on-call cheatsheet generator and anchored diagnostics

Context: On-call teams repeatedly create minimal playbooks manually to triage noisy alerts. Small, well-scoped automations (scale up, circuit restart, cache flush) are useful but risky without staged approvals. This PR adds two cooperating pieces: (1) a Skeletal Playbook Prototyper that synthesizes a compact, human-friendly playbook skeleton from alert metadata and recent telemetry snippets; (2) a Gradual Remediator operator that can propose low-risk, staged remediation steps with safety gates (preflight checks, dry-run estimations, and timed incremental ramp) and rollback hints.

What it does (high level):
- Adds a CLI subcommand (incident-bot proto-playbook) and a UI quick-action to generate a minimal .playbook.yaml from alert context. The skeleton contains: intent summary, priority, minimum diagnostic commands, suggested next-action steps, and suggested observability assertions to validate each step.
- Implements a Gradual Remediator engine that models "safe ramps" for a small set of actions (replica_scale, pod_restart, cache_invalidate). Each action is expressed as a staged plan: pre-check → take small step → observe metrics → escalate/continue/rollback. Plans are advisory by default and require explicit approval to execute; a new flag --auto-lease allows limited auto-apply in low-risk environments.
- Adds heuristics to avoid fragility: action-risk scoring (based on service SLAs, historical variance), circuit-breaker to prevent repeated retries, and an emergency abort hook.
- Exposes telemetry hooks so the SLO dashboards can consume stage-level metrics for audit and postmortem.

Why: Reduce toil for on-call while keeping human-in-the-loop safeguards. Synthesis of a focused playbook speeds triage; staged remediations let responders do incremental, measurable actions with clear rollbacks.

Backward compatibility and safety: Default behavior is non-destructive (generate-only). Gradual Remediator requires a separate RBAC permission and an opt-in config value in the control plane. No runtime behavior changes happen unless an operator flips the enablement flag.

Related: ENG-5942 (prototyper feature), PM-881 (oncall flow improvements).

Files touched (summary): added new CLI handlers, new remediator core, small UI quick-action, docs and examples, and unit+integration tests.

Testing: unit test coverage for remediator planner and risk scorer; integration tests simulate a slow-surge alert and assert staged steps and abort behavior. Load tests show minimal CPU impact (~0.6% at 1000 simulated alerts/minute) when prototyper is enabled.

Release notes: New on-call tools: generate skeletal playbooks from alerts and an opt-in gradual remediator for safe, staged low-risk fixes.

Migration notes: Operators should review the new RBAC role: incident-bot.remediator.apply. To enable auto-apply in non-prod, set enable_gradual_remediator=true in the control plane config.
Liam O'Connor: Nice incremental approach — can we make the default generated skeleton even smaller (3 lines max) for pager-first views?
Priya Shah: Agreed; reduced the inspector output and added a condensed CLI flag --condensed.
Marisol Vega: The risk model needs a deterministic test for flapping services. I suggest adding a synthetic flapping benchmark.
Priya Shah: Added test/integration/flapping_svc_sim.go and tuned the suppression window; test added in commit d1b6c55.
Ethan Zhou: We should be explicit about audit traces for each staged action. Add a stage_id and correlation id to telemetry.
Priya Shah: Implemented stage IDs and wired to tracing. CI initially failed on lint (TSX formatting) — fixed in 9ac4f2e.
Marisol Vega: Approving after confirming RBAC gating exists and docs updated. (approved)
Liam O'Connor: Manual smoke-tested generate -> approve -> execute flow in staging, observed intended staged scaling and rollback on negative metric. Looks good. (approved)
Merge assistant: squash-merged by Priya Shah. Tagging release notes and adding RBAC entry to prod rollout checklist.
Add skeletal playbook prototyper (CLI + UI quick-action) and an opt-in Gradual Remediator for staged low-risk fixes. Default behavior is generate-only; remediator requires RBAC and explicit enablement. Includes examples and tests.

payload.body:
Motivation: On incoming alerts responders often need small, safe diagnostic commands and a short prioritized list of telemetry keys to inspect. This PR introduces two complementary features: (1) executable diagnostic snippets attached to contextual alert summaries (one-click copy/run code blocks tuned per service), and (2) a lightweight priority telemetry scorer that ranks traces, metrics, and logs keys by likely causal relevance using heuristics + a small trained logistic model.

Summary of changes: add a new embeddings-backed snippet index, a snippet authoring UI + templating engine, telemetry-scoring service with REST endpoint, alert enrichment pipeline updates to attach top-5 telemetry keys and top-3 snippets, and keyboard-friendly Slack actions to run or copy snippets.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc: ENG-1209 reviewed and linked
- [x] Add snippet schema, validation and safe-run sandbox gating
- [x] Implement telemetry scorer service and config flags
- [x] Wire alert enrichment to attach results to incident threads
- [x] End-to-end tests for snippet safety and scorer stability
- [x] E2E manual verification on staging with SLO-team
- [x] Docs + example snippet templates committed

Commits (high level):
- feat(snippets): initial schema, templating and indexer
- feat(telemetry-scorer): model training helpers and REST endpoint
- feat(enrichment): attach scorer output and snippet refs to alert payload
- feat(ui): add snippet authoring modal and run/copy actions
- test: add unit + integration tests for sandbox gating and scorer
- ci: update pipeline to run scorer unit tests and integration smoke tests

Files changed (high level):
- incident-bot/services/snippets/*: schema, indexer, templates, validation hooks
- incident-bot/services/telemetry_scorer/*: trainer, REST API, feature transforms
- incident-bot/enrichment/pipeline.py: attach telemetry keys and snippet refs
- incident-bot/ui/modals/snippet_authoring.jsx: new authoring modal and example templates
- incident-bot/slack/actions.py: run/copy actions, permission gating
- tests/*: unit + integration tests
- docs/oncall/snippets.md: example usage and safety guidelines

Review conversation (high level):
- Liam Chen: "Nice work. Two high-level asks: tighten sandbox execution limits (timeout/memory) and make scoring feature set configurable per org."
- Ava Martinez: "Agreed — tightened sandbox limits to 2s/64MB and added org-level flags in config; updated tests to assert limits."
- Priya Kapoor: "Can we ensure snippets never include destructive flags by default? Suggest adding denylist patterns."
- Ava Martinez: "Added denylist patterns to validator and a post-approval manual override flow for SREs; documented in docs/oncall/snippets.md."
- Diego Alvarez: "Score distribution looks noisy on low-volume services. Recommend a fallback to heuristic-only scoring if model confidence < 0.6."
- Ava Martinez: "Implemented confidence gating and a heuristic fallback; added telemetry to monitor model confidence over time."

CI summary:
- unit tests: pass
- integration smoke: pass
- lint: pass with minor autofixes applied
- security scan: pass (no new high/critical findings)

Deployment notes:
- feature gate: incident.runbook_executable_snippets (disabled by default)
- rollout: staged rollout to 10% of teams for 2 weeks, then further rollout after metrics validation
- rollback: feature flag and quick revert deploy available if unsafe patterns observed

Monitoring and telemetry added:
- scorer.confidence histogram, snippet-run count, snippet-run errors, per-service heuristic-fallback-rate
- alert: scorer-confidence-drop (>10% drop in week-over-week median)

Release notes for SREs: "Introduces executable, non-destructive diagnostic snippets and a telemetry scoring service that surfaces likely causal keys in incident threads. Disabled by default; enable via incident.runbook_executable_snippets. Review snippet templates before enabling in production."

Related work: builds on ENG-1012 (alert enrichment refactor) and complements recent playbook-ranking efforts.

Backwards compatibility: alert payloads now include optional fields snippets:[] and telemetry_priority:[]; consumers should ignore these if absent.

Manual testing performed: ran synthetic alerts for payment-service and storage-proxy on staging and validated snippet execution sandboxing and fallback scoring.

Known limitations:
- Model was trained on historically instrumented services; cold-start behavior for new services may favor heuristics
- Snippet authoring UI currently requires SRE role; future: allow product engineers to propose snippets with SRE review

Line items for follow-up (not in this PR):
- dataset expansion for low-volume services (ENG-1217)
- admin UI to manage denylist and org-level scoring policies
- export of snippet usage for cost analysis
Adds executable diagnostic snippets in the incident Slack thread and a scoring model that ranks telemetry keys by likely causal relevance. Improves on-call turnaround for triage by surfacing runnable checks and prioritized traces.
Liam Chen: tighten sandbox execution limits and make scoring feature set configurable per org
Ava Martinez: tightened sandbox to 2s/64MB, added org flags and tests
Priya Kapoor: ensure snippets never include destructive flags by default
Ava Martinez: added denylist patterns and manual SRE override flow
Diego Alvarez: fallback to heuristics when confidence low
Ava Martinez: implemented confidence gating and fallback; added monitoring
Merged after approvals from reviewers and green CI. Squash merge applied. Feature is behind a feature flag for staged rollout.
If enabled, on-call should review snippet templates for their services before enabling. Emergency rollback: disable incident.runbook_executable_snippets and redeploy the enrichment service. Watch scorer.confidence histogram and snippet-run-error-rate for anomalies.
payload.title: Executable diagnostic snippets and priority telemetry scorer

payload.body:
Motivation: On-call responders frequently need a compact contextual snapshot of recent telemetry and a starting runbook draft tied to an alert fingerprint. Today responders copy links and manually assemble runbook skeletons; this PR introduces a compact, queryable incident snapshot format and a runbook-stub generator that pre-fills playbook sections based on the snapshot and alert metadata. The feature is behind the feature flag 'rb-snapshot-index' and is fully backward compatible with existing runbook templates.

What this PR does (single-line summary): Adds a snapshot indexer/store, a CLI endpoint to retrieve/redact snapshots, the runbook-stub generator, safety redaction, tests, docs, and a small migration helper for previous snapshot exports.

Checklist:
- [x] Snapshot index schema and store (compact gzipped JSON + minimal index).
- [x] CLI command: `incident-bot snapshot get <fingerprint>` with `--redact` option.
- [x] Runbook stub generator that emits sections: overview, impact assessment, immediate mitigations, triage steps, rollback hints.
- [x] Redaction sanitizer (KMS-backed PII/secret redaction interface).
- [x] Unit tests for indexer, store, and stub generator.
- [x] E2E fixture validating the quick-query => stub flow.
- [x] Docs and example usage in docs/runbook-snapshots.md and examples.
- [x] Feature flag gating and migration script for v1 exports.

Design notes: Snapshots are stored as compressed payloads keyed by an alert fingerprint (sha1 of normalized alert + timeframe). The index stores metadata (timestamp, alert id, top-5 hosts, metric fingerprints, traces sampled) to enable fast listing and recall without full payload expansion. The runbook-stub generator uses a ruleset mapping (rules derived from SRE-332) to pre-populate headings. Redaction runs as a last step and supports pluggable scrubbers; we provide a simple KMS token check and pattern-based scrubber in pkg/redaction/sanitizer.go.

CI / checks:
- Unit: pass (snapshots_test.go covers indexer edge cases).
- Integration: initially failed on flaky e2e that relied on external telemetry emulator; fixed by adding a deterministic fixture and retry in e2e workflow.
- Lint: pass.
- Security scan: pass after adding kube secret avoidance in store logic.

Review conversation (high-level):
- Diego Ramos: Requested stronger guarantees that snapshots never contain plaintext secrets and suggested KMS-backed envelope encryption for the store.
  - Author: Added redaction sanitizers and a KMS-token check before storing; also documented encryption recommendations.
- Lena Park: Asked for test coverage around large snapshot sizes and index read path under high cardinality.

payload.body:
## Summary
This PR adds a new incident-bot event handler for Hot-route Capacity Protection activation events emitted by routing/gateway. When protection enters an active state (or exits), incident-bot posts a structured Slack message to `#incidents` with:
- route_group + route (when available), region, tier class, and activation type
- primary reason code(s) (quota vs overload) and protection mode (admission control vs shedding)
- current/peak metrics snapshot (shed_rate, 429_rate, p95 latency, queue depth where present)
- links to the SRE dashboard + runbook section
- a dedupe key to avoid paging storms during flappy thresholds

This is intended to reduce time-to-diagnosis during overload events and make it obvious when best-effort is being throttled to preserve enterprise SLOs.

## Context
Hot-route capacity protection is rolling out behind flags (see ENG-4927). During the us-east canary we observed multiple on-call threads asking “are we currently shedding?” and “which runbook section applies?”. A lightweight, deterministic bot post was the fastest way to improve shared situational awareness.

## Behavior
### When we post
- On transition into ACTIVE (per region + route_group + tier_class)
- On transition out of ACTIVE (recovery)
- Optional periodic reminder every 20 minutes while ACTIVE if shed_rate remains above threshold (disabled by default; behind `INCIDENT_BOT_OVERLOAD_REMINDER_ENABLED`)

### Dedupe / rate limiting
- Dedupe key: `(region, route_group, tier_class, mode)`
- Minimum repeat interval: 10 minutes (configurable)
- If the source emits frequent toggles, we collapse and post an update message (thread reply) instead of new top-level posts.

### Message format (example)
Top-level post:
- Title: `Overload protection ACTIVE: us-east / chat_completions / enterprise` 
- Fields:
  - Mode: `admission_control + shedding`
  - Reason: `OVERLOAD_QUEUE_DEPTH` (plus any secondary reason codes)
  - Shed rate (best-effort): `12.4% (5m)`
  - 429 rate (enterprise): `0.3% (5m)`
  - p95 latency (enterprise): `820ms (5m)`
- Links:
  - Dashboard: `Hot Route Protection / us-east / chat_completions`
  - Runbook: `Runbook: Overload protection and admission control (Diagnose)`
  - Debug endpoint (internal): `Admission decision inspector` (only shown if `INCIDENT_BOT_SHOW_DEBUG_LINK=true`)

Recovery post:
- Title: `Overload protection RECOVERED: us-east / chat_completions / enterprise`
- Includes duration in active state and a small “before/after” snapshot.

## Implementation notes
- New event type: `overload_protection.activation.v1`
- Source payload is treated as untrusted input; all fields are schema-validated and truncated to keep Slack payload small.
- We intentionally avoid embedding high-cardinality identifiers (tenant_id, request_id) in the Slack message. The dashboard link includes filters but not tenant scoping.
- Confluence + dashboard links are generated from a simple mapping keyed by `route_group` and `region`.

## Config
- `INCIDENT_BOT_OVERLOAD_POSTS_ENABLED` (default: false)
- `INCIDENT_BOT_OVERLOAD_CHANNEL` (default: #incidents)
- `INCIDENT_BOT_OVERLOAD_DEDUPE_MINUTES` (default: 10)
- `INCIDENT_BOT_OVERLOAD_REMINDER_ENABLED` (default: false)
- `INCIDENT_BOT_SHOW_DEBUG_LINK` (default: false)

## Testing
- Unit tests for:
  - schema validation + truncation
  - dedupe + threading behavior
  - link generation
  - ACTIVE -> ACTIVE updates vs ACTIVE -> RECOVERED transitions
- Manual test against Slack sandbox workspace using the replay CLI.

## Rollout plan
1) Merge behind flag (this PR)
2) Enable only in staging for 48h; validate dedupe + message formatting
3) Canary enable in us-east for protected routes only; verify no spam during expected best-effort shedding
4) Expand to other regions post GA enablement window

## Links
- Linear: ENG-4927
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGSRE/Runbook%3A+Overload+protection+and+admission+control
- Dashboard spec: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGPLAT/Dashboard+spec%3A+Hot-route+protection
- Related PRs:
  - redwood/pr-27441-add-overload-reason-codes-to-429-responses
  - observability-pack/pr-1832-add-hot-route-protection-dashboards

Checklist:
- [x] Includes feature flag default-off
- [x] Includes dedupe protections
- [x] Includes tests
- [x] No high-cardinality fields in message text
- [x] Docs link points to correct runbook section
Allison Grant (review): Please confirm we’re not including tenant identifiers anywhere; dashboard filters are OK but make sure the URL doesn’t carry tenant_id. Also, add a note about cardinality in the code comment so this doesn’t regress later.
Rafael Mendes (author): Confirmed. No tenant_id/request_id in text or URL. Dashboard link is route_group + region only. Added an inline comment in `overloadProtectionBlocks.ts` and a unit test asserting disallowed keys are dropped.
Logan Wright (review): Can we include queue depth/scheduler lag only if present and keep field names consistent with our metrics standard? I worry about people comparing apples to oranges.
Rafael Mendes (author): Good call. I’m now mapping payload fields to our standard display names and only showing queue depth when payload declares `source=runtime_metrics`. Otherwise we omit it and keep the message to shed/429/latency snapshot.
Benji Okafor (review): Dedupe interval set to 10 minutes—does that risk hiding quick flaps that matter? Also, ensure we post recovery even if it’s within the dedupe window.
Rafael Mendes (author): Recovery posts bypass dedupe (always post). For flaps, we thread updates rather than posting new top-level messages; added a small “state changed” indicator + timestamp in thread replies.
Dev Patel (review): Support will use these posts during escalations. Can we include the 429 reason code legend link or at least hint ‘quota vs overload’ explicitly in the message?
Rafael Mendes (author): Added a ‘Reason’ field that distinguishes QUOTA vs OVERLOAD and included a link to the 429 reason code docs in the message footer (internal docs link for now).
CI (status): Initially failed on lint due to unused import in replay CLI; fixed in follow-up commit. All checks green after rerun.
Allison Grant (final): Approved. Please keep `INCIDENT_BOT_SHOW_DEBUG_LINK` default false; we should only surface that after INT-3302 access controls land.
Rafael Mendes (author): Kept default false and gated link rendering behind flag. Merging.
