payload.body:
Motivation: On large incidents operators need compact, self-contained diagnostic bundles that include prioritized traces, contextual runbook fragments, and minimal artifacts suitable for ephemeral snapshot handoffs. Currently the incident-bot attaches raw artifacts which are large and noisy. This PR adds a bundler that heuristically selects high-value artifacts, compresses them, and serializes runbook steps into a compact, human-readable + machine-parsable artifact for handoff and archival. Summary of changes: - New autodiag bundler (incident_bot/diag/bundler.py) implementing artifact scoring and retention tiers - Runbook serializer (incident_bot/runbook/serializer.py) that emits compressed JSONL+gzip blobs and a small index for fast preview - Sanitizer hooks and redaction profiles configurable per-team (incident_bot/sanitizers/*) - CLI & API endpoints to request ephemeral snapshot generation and download (api/handlers/snapshot.py, cli/snapshot.py) - Small additions to tests and fixtures (tests/diag/test_bundler.py, tests/runbook/test_serializer.py) Design notes: The bundler scores artifacts using weighted heuristics: recency, error frequency, stack depth, trace span count, and correlation with alert fingerprints. We keep a small top-K by weight and include a deterministic fallback algorithm so artifacts are reproducible. The serializer produces a compact runbook fragment where each step is scored and can include an optional single-line compressed snippet of logs encoded with gzip+base64. Redaction: sanitizer profiles are implemented as a pipeline of token/regex and KMS-backed secret masking rules; default profile strips known PII patterns but preserves operational context. Summary:
Add a weighted on-call simulation harness and pluggable, safety-first auto-remediation hooks for incident-bot. This PR provides: a simulator that replays historical alert streams with configurable weighting and stochastic responder availability; a policy layer that scores simulated on-call load against team rotas and SLOs; and an opt-in auto-remediation hook framework with guardrails (dry-run mode, rate limits, circuit breaker, and audit logging).

Motivation:
On-call fatigue and poorly calibrated automatic remediation have caused slow MTTR and a handful of bad rollbacks in Q2/Q3. We need an offline way for teams to: 1) model the effect of changing schedules or escalation policies, 2) surface dangerous remediation rules before they run in production, and 3) provide a safe runtime path for low-risk automated mitigations during incidents.

Design highlights:
- Simulator: accepts historical alert slices, supports weighting strategies (by service, severity, origin region), and simulates responder availability windows; outputs metrics aligned with our SLO definitions.
- Policy layer: pluggable scoring functions for responder load, fatigue, and correlated failures; can run bulk experiments to find escalation thresholds that minimize MTTR without increasing false auto-remediations.
- Auto-remediation hooks: new hook interface (OncallAutoRemediate) with enforced contracts: requires a pre-approve dry-run result, a rate limiter token bucket per-hook, a team-level circuit breaker that trips on anomalous rollback counts, signed audit events to the audit-log-exporter sink, and an opt-in label in team config.
- Safety-first defaults: all hooks default to dry-run; enabling requires an explicit team-level flag and a two-person approval for production enablement.

What changed (high-level files):
- internal/oncall/sim/driver.go (new): core simulator loop and weighting strategies.
- internal/oncall/weighting.go (new): weighting strategies and config parsing.
- cmd/oncall-sim/main.go (new): CLI to run local/backfill simulations and export summaries.
- internal/hooks/autoremediate.go (new): hook interface, safeties, and wrappers for dry-run and token bucket.
- webhooks/autoremediate-adapter.go (modified): adapter to call hook implementations and persist audit records.
- docs/oncall-sim.md (new): usage and example experiments.
- tests/sim/sim_integration_test.go (new): deterministic simulation golden tests and load scenarios.
- tests/hooks/autoremediate_safety_test.go (new): tests for rate limiting, circuit breaking, and audit emission.

Commits (summary):
- feat(sim): initial simulator skeleton and replay harness
- feat(sim): add weighting strategies and responder model
- feat(hooks): define OncallAutoRemediate interface and dry-run wrapper
- fix(tests): stabilize flaky timing in sim integration test (use fake clock)
- ci: add pipeline job `sim-integration` to run golden sim tests

Testing & CI:
- Added unit and integration tests covering the main safety properties.
- New pipeline job `sim-integration` runs golden scenario replay and compares output metrics.
- Initial CI run failed on timing-sensitive sim test (flake); I switched the sim internals to use a fake clock and re-ran. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, lint, sim-integration, e2e-mocks).

Rollout plan:
- Merge to main in squash mode.
- Feature is behind config:teams.<team>.enable_autoremediate (default: false).
- Enable dry-run experiments for a handful of SRE teams on staging for 2 weeks, run simulations against last 30 days of alerts.
- After validation, enable limited production opt-ins with telemetry and a manual approval gate.

Backward compatibility and migrations:
- No schema migrations required.
- New audit events are additive and consumed by audit-log-exporter; consumers must be tolerant of new event types.

Related:
- ENG-1292 (on-call tooling roadmap), SUP-4421 (customer report about unsafe automated rollbacks), ENG-1338 (observability for remediation actions).

- We intentionally overload the simulator to be deterministic when given a seed for reproducible experiments.

Motivation: On several recent incidents automated mitigations triggered by the incident-bot caused partial service disruption because there was no pre-run simulation of stateful actions and limited safety gating. This PR introduces a lightweight simulation harness that executes mitigation steps against a sandboxed state model and a set of declarative safety gates that must pass before the bot can apply real-world actions.

What this PR does (single-string description): Adds a mitigation simulation harness, a safety-gate DSL for playbooks, a test suite with representative incident scenarios, and small plumbing to record simulation traces in S3 for post-run analysis. Includes documentation, a canary rollout path, CLI helpers (incubate mode) and a feature flag to opt-in per-team.

Checklist: 
- [x] Simulation harness core runtime (deterministic, time-boxed) 
- [x] Safety-gate DSL and evaluator (thresholds, whitelists, dry-run-only exceptions) 
- [x] Unit and integration tests (coverage for 7 common mitigations) 
- [x] CI job adding simulation acceptance tests 
- [x] Documentation and README for playbook authors 
- [x] Opt-in feature flag and incremental rollout plan

Design notes: The harness runs a simulated environment that models key downstream state transitions: service replica counts, leader elections, routing-table updates, and external API rate limits. Mitigation steps implement a small SimulationAdapter interface (simulate(), apply()). Step authors implement simulate() to return a discrete list of state deltas; the harness composes deltas and checks safety gates before returning PASS/FAIL. Safety gates are declarative JSON with rules like max_service_down_time_seconds, max_restarts, and allowed_targets; the evaluator produces a human-readable report.

Backward compatibility: All existing playbooks will continue to work. By default the simulation runs in dry-run and does not block automated mitigations until the feature flag is enabled for a team. Safety gates default to permissive on opt-in, but the admin console will suggest recommended gate values based on historical incident telemetry.

Testing and verification: Added unit tests for gate evaluator and simulation engine. Added integration acceptance tests that run three synthetic incidents: noisy-restart-loop, partial-network-partition, and degraded-cache-eviction. CI runs the acceptance suite under the new workflow. Local repro: ./scripts/run-mitigation-sim.sh --scenario noisy-restart-loop --write-trace ./tmp/trace.json

Commits summary: See commits list below. High level: implement harness, implement gates DSL, wire feature flag, tests, docs, CI.

Changed files (high level): sources: incident-bot/sim/, incident-bot/playbooks/gates/, incident-bot/cli/, docs/playbooks/simulation.md, ci/workflows/sim-acceptance.yml, tests/fixtures/scenarios/*.json.

Rollout plan: Enable feature flag in staging for 2 weeks with trace collection. Run simulated mitigations on nightly canary incidents and review traces. After signoff enable opt-in in production for teams, then progressively require safety gates for fully automated mitigations.

Merge: squash-and-merge after 2 approvals and CI green.

Why this is different: Instead of only gating on simple dry-run checks, the harness executes a compact deterministic simulation of state transitions which catches class of races and mis-ordered steps that previously caused regressions. The design intentionally keeps the simulator conservative (no heavy modeling) to avoid flakiness and keep runs fast (~200–500ms per step in tests).
Ravi Patel: Strong design. Please add one more unit test covering leader election churn. (requested changes)
Ava Chen: Added leader-election test and updated schema validators. Reply: PTAL
Sofia Morales: Can you add an example of a safety gate recommended value from historical data? (comment)
Ava Chen: Added guidance and script to compute suggested gates from telemetry. Reply: added in docs/playbooks/simulation.md
Jordan Kim: Verified CI acceptance run locally, approving. (approved)

Context: On-call teams often waste critical minutes assembling the same diagnostic surface (pod logs, recent deploys, graph snapshots, SLO deltas) before they can follow runbooks. This PR adds an automated diagnostics gatherer plus a lightweight runbook-suggestion engine to incident-bot so on-call responders get an actionable triage checklist and templated next steps in Slack/PagerDuty threads. Motivation: reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to resolution (MTTR) by surfacing high-value signals automatically and recommending runbook steps tailored to the observed signals. Summary of changes: 1) diagnostics worker: new background worker that gathers a bounded set of artifacts (pod logs tails, pod event summaries, recent deploy metadata, SLO deltas from slo-toolkit, topology hints) with configurable TTL and size limits; 2) suggestion engine: rule-based scorer + template library that maps diagnostic signatures to ranked runbook suggestions and immediate mitigation commands; 3) on-call commands: /incident-diagnose which triggers a diagnostics snapshot and posts a suggested runbook checklist back into Slack; 4) triage UI: compact summary card and links to full artifacts (pre-signed URLs) plus confidence score; 5) observability and audit: metrics for diagnoses-per-hour, avg suggestion confidence, and feature flags to enable/disable production use. Compatibility: integrates with existing Slack and PagerDuty hooks, and fetches SLOs using the slo-toolkit API. Security: diagnostics snapshots include redaction hooks and respect KMS-backed secrets; we add an opt-out setting per team. Rollout: feature-gated behind the config flag incident_bot.autorunbook.enabled (default off). Rollout plan includes staged enablement for internal SRE team, canary on a small Slack workspace, and full rollout after 2 weeks of monitoring. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for scorer heuristics - [x] Integration tests against a local slo-toolkit stub - [x] e2e test that posts to a test Slack workspace - [x] Docs + runbook templates added - [x] Feature flag covered and telemetry emitted Testing notes: use the provided test harness under test/harness/diagnostics to simulate cluster events and SLO regressions. See linear ENG-942 for acceptance criteria and the linked design doc (internal link) for decision rationale. Backwards compatibility: when the feature flag is off, no runtime change; the commands are hidden. Rollback: disable feature flag and revoke pre-signed artifact URLs if necessary.

payload.body:
Motivation and summary: On largerincidents the on-call UI was repeatedly doing multi-step DB queries to assemble escalation cards (team membership, current rota, playbook pointer, recent runbook snapshots). That work was a measurable contributor to pager-attention latency spikes and flapping UI components reported by SRE. This PR adds a lightweight, cacheable KV index alongside the existing playbook store that pre-joins the small, hot subset of playbook metadata we need for immediate escalation; it also introduces a 'smart escalation card' transformer in incident-bot that fetches from that index first, with a deterministic fallback to the canonical store if keys are missing. This reduces the 95th percentile card render time and removes a number of anti-patterns where the UI retried slow joins. What this PR does (high level): 1) Introduces a new playbook_kv_index service and schema migration that stores {playbook_id -> abbreviated metadata: title, severity_hint, primary_contact_ids, last_updated, compact_tokenized_triggers}. 2) Implements an index writer that runs as part of the existing playbook write path (sync+async write modes). 3) Adds a card rendering path in incident-bot that queries the KV index (read-through) and falls back to the canonical store on miss. 4) Adds telemetry: per-key hit/miss counters, miss latency histogram, and a small gauge for index staleness. 5) Adds an optional rollout flag and a two-step canary plan to limit impact. Checklist: - [x] Schema migration designed and backward compatible (no forced downtime). - [x] Writer uses best-effort async retry with backoff; synchronous write enabled behind feature flag for customers who require atomicity. - [x] Read path implements deterministic fallback when index miss or degraded. - [x] Telemetry and dashboards added (SLO-focused). - [x] Unit and integration tests included; e2e smoke test against local playbook store included. - [x] Documentation: README and rollout instructions added to docs/oncall/kv-index.md. Rollout plan: Stage 1 (canary) enable index reads for 5% of requests in staging and production; Stage 2 enable writes (async) for 100% while keeping fallback; Stage 3 enable sync writes behind customer opt-in. Monitoring and rollback: watch the new telemetry dashboards (index_hit_rate, index_miss_latency) and oncall-card-error-rate; rollback involves flipping the rollout flag which reverts reads to canonical store immediately. Backwards compatibility notes: index is purely additive; absence of a key triggers fallback. Database migration: a small table and an LRU cleanup TTL; migration has been performance-tested on a copy of the production sample. Links and references: Linear ENG-7482 tracks the index lifecycle; SUP-331 is a support ticket referencing customer-facing latency reports. For reviewers: look at writer durability trade-offs (sync vs async) and the telemetry labels used for downstream dashboards.
3 commits: initial schema+migration + index writer + smart card read-path and telemetry. Commit 1: add migration and table definition with docs. Commit 2: implement playbook index writer and feature flags, tests for writer durability. Motivation: During incidents engineers frequently run ad-hoc queries (k8s describe, recent-error-tail, quick-sli checks) to validate hypotheses. This PR adds two coordinated features: 1) a lightweight live-query probe subsystem that can execute predefined, parameterized queries against supported backends (k8s API, metrics API, log tail) and return sanitized short-form results; 2) an interactive guided-mitigation CLI that surfaces curated playbook steps, runs optional probes, and can optionally execute safe remediation steps via the existing playbook-runner. Goals: reduce cognitive overhead for first responders, speed up hypothesis validation, and centralize audit/sanitization for ad-hoc diagnostics. Key design points: - Probes are declarative YAML snippets stored in config and validated at startup. Each probe declares required permissions, estimated cost (timeout/IO), and a sanitizer pipeline. - Live probes run in constrained sandboxes with concurrency/rate limits and per-incident quotas to avoid causing load during high traffic. - The guided CLI is a TUI (fallback to non-interactive mode) that recommends next steps based on incident tags and probe outputs; it supports dry-run and a single-step auto-apply mode gated by RBAC and an explicit approve token. - All probe outputs are scrubbed by a pluggable sanitizer chain and emit only short summaries to the chat/pager context; full sanitized artefacts are attached to the incident record and stored in the audit-log with retention controls. Changes in this PR: - New subsystem: internal/probes with probe executor, validators, and sanitizer registry. - CLI entry: cmd/ibctl/guided_mitigation.go implements interactive flow and non-interactive flags. - Incident adapter: incident/plugins/live_probe_adapter.go to wire probes into incident runbooks and responder actions. - Config: config/probes.yaml.example and feature flag gating (feature.live_probes.enabled). - Docs: docs/diagnostics/live-probes.md and runbook examples in docs/templates/guided-mitigation.md. - Tests: unit tests for sanitizers and integration tests exercising k8s-mock probe runner. Backwards compatibility and safety: feature gated by default, requires explicit operator opt-in for production. Probes that can modify state are opt-in and require a secondary approval token. Checklist: - [x] Implement probe executor and sanitizer registry - [x] CLI flow + dry-run support - [x] Integration tests (mock backends) - [x] Docs and example probes - [x] RBAC and quota checks - [x] Feature gate behind config flag Usage notes: ibctl guided-mitigation --incident=INC-1234 --run-probes --auto-apply=false will launch the TUI, run safe probes, and present ranked playbook steps. See docs/diagnostics/live-probes.md for authoring probes and sanitizer examples. Related: ENG-8123 (reduce MTTI for first-response), SRE-204 (runbook library schema).
Ethan Morris (requested changes, 2026-02-20): Please add a hard timeout around any k8s describe probe and document failure modes; also ensure the sanitizer chain defaults to removing pod names in public incidents.
Priya Raman (author reply, 2026-02-21): Added a default 15s timeout and explicit sanitizer config with pod-name redaction. Also added unit tests for timeout behavior.
Sofia Patel (comment, 2026-02-24): We should gate any state-changing probes behind a separate operator-enabled allowlist. Will we auto-escalate if a probe indicates service is degraded?
Priya Raman (author reply, 2026-02-25): State-changing probes are opt-in and require the --approve-token flag; for degradation signals the runbook step suggests opening a pager with auto-populated summary but does not auto-escalate by default.
Liam Chen (approved, 2026-03-01): Tests look solid; security checklist satisfied, approving for merge subject to CI green.

Summary: This PR introduces a small, portable telemetry snapshot format called a 'tracelet' and a bulk sanitizer pipeline to scrub PII and high-entropy secrets before attachments are uploaded or shared. Motivation: on-call engineers frequently paste long traces or logs into tickets or Slack which contain sensitive material; we need a first-class, low-friction way to extract the minimum diagnostic context and safely share it with support partners and security. 

What changed: checklist: - [x] implement tracelet generator (tracelet.py) with time-bounded spans and metric rollups - [x] add bulk sanitizer (sanitizers/bulk_sanitize.py) with regex rules, entropy detection, and allowlist hooks - [x] wire incident-bot attachment pipeline to run sanitizer before external uploads - [x] CLI flag incident-bot collect --tracelet to create portable JSONL artifacts - [x] unit + integration tests + sample dashboard link - [x] docs update and on-call playbook snippet

Commits (high level): - feat(tracelet): add scoped Tracelet class and serializer - feat(sanitize): implement modular rule engine and entropy detector - chore(ci): add integration test matrix for sanitizer rules - fix(test): address flakiness by adding deterministic timestamping - docs: add playbook and examples

Files touched (high level): - incident-bot/handlers/tracelet.py: core generator and sampling policy - incident-bot/cli/collect.py: new --tracelet flag and upload flow - incident-bot/sanitizers/bulk_sanitize.py: rule engine, entropy heuristics, allowlist hooks - incident-bot/tests/test_tracelet.py and test_sanitize.py - docs/oncall/tracelet-sharing.md - manifests/rbac-sample.yaml (opt-in role for external-share)

Design notes: Tracelets are intentionally minimal — 30s max window by default, aggregated latency buckets, stack sample pointers (no full stack dumps), and embedded sample hashes to detect repetition. The sanitizer pipeline runs rule modules in a configurable order: allowlist -> regex scrub -> entropy mask -> context-aware redaction. Customers can add enterprise allowlists via KMS-backed rule bundles.

Privacy & Security: This PR purposely avoids exporting raw request bodies and long-form user identifiers. All sanitizer rules are reversible only for internal teams (via audit logs) and external uploads remove reversible metadata. RBAC gating ensures only roles with 'external-share' can trigger uploads. The manifests/rbac-sample.yaml provides an example role to grant the capability.

Testing & CI: Initial CI run surfaced two flaky tests in the integration matrix; added deterministic timestamps and fixed race in the collector which resolved failures. CI summary: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration: pass after rerun, lint: pass, e2e (optional): skipped on fork.

Review thread (abridged): - Ethan Liu (reviewer): "Nice shape. Please add explicit unit tests for entropy thresholds and add a short doc on how to extend allowlists." - Sofia Patel (author): "Added test_sanitize_entropy and docs at docs/oncall/tracelet-sharing.md; updated README with extension points." - Priya Nair (security): "Can we ensure masking is not reversible when artifacts are shared externally? Add a short note in the playbook." - Sofia Patel: "Confirmed: external path strips reversible fields and writes an audit event to a protected log; noted in docs." - Aaron Chen (sre): "Can we make the default window shorter (15s) for high-traffic services?" - Sofia Patel: "Added an env var TRACELET_DEFAULT_WINDOW with fallback to 30s; callers can override per-service." 

Backward compatibility: Non-breaking. Old attachment paths still work; sanitizer is enabled for 'share:external' flows only by default. Admins can enable sanitizer for all attachments via config.

Merge: Squash-merged after approvals from Ethan, Priya, and Aaron. Followups planned: ENG-2042 to add telemetry to Redwood Console UI for tracelet visualization and ENG-1987 for server-side allowlist distribution.

How to use: example: incident-bot collect --incident 12345 --tracelet --sanitize --upload-external=true This produces a tracelet JSONL artifact, runs sanitizer rules, and (if allowed) uploads to the configured external bucket/store with audit logging.

Notes: Kept the implementation small and modular to encourage adoption by other tools (slo-toolkit will consume tracelets in a follow-up). This is intentionally not a full signal export; it's a pragmatic compromise to speed investigations while reducing data exposure.
Adds a compact tracelet generator and a configurable bulk sanitizer to allow on-call engineers to share minimal, privacy-safe telemetry snippets with external teams and support. Opt-in via incident labels; RBAC-aware. Improves triage speed while reducing PII exposure.

Adds a new 'diagnostic walker' feature that automatically runs a scoped series of safe telemetry probes and assembles an evidence bundle for on-call handoff. Motivation: reduce time-to-first-action during incidents by providing a bounded, auditable diagnostic sweep that collects traces, logs, and lightweight health checks without granting broad runbook privileges. Key behavior: 1) user triggers a walker with an incident id; 2) walker consults a per-service probe catalog and a safety policy to select non-invasive probes; 3) probes run in sandboxed worker pods with time/IO caps; 4) results are deduplicated, scored, and packaged into a compressed evidence bundle with a short human summary and machine-readable diagnostics for playbook tools. Checklist: - [x] probe catalog schema and examples - [x] worker sandbox and timeout enforcement - [x] evidence bundle serializer + checksum - [x] on-call summary generator with templated hints - [x] CLI command and HTTP endpoint w/ RBAC checks - [x] unit + integration tests with CI profiles - [x] docs and runbook snippets. Security notes: probes are constrained (no write shell access, network egress restricted to telemetry ingest), and all collected data is marked for retention policy enforcement. This change is intentionally conservative: default probe sets are small and require an incident-scoped opt-in. Related linear: ENG-7480, ENG-7599.

Motivation: On-call responders need fast, targeted diagnostics for noisy alerts without triggering unsafe automated mitigations. This PR adds a Contextual Autodiag Prober that runs a prioritized, low-impact set of probes (metric queries, tail-sampled logs, short traces, and a lightweight synthetic request) based on alert fingerprints and SLO burn signals. It also introduces a Safety-Guarded Runbook Suggestor that ranks playbook actions and prevents high-impact automated remediations unless explicit conditions are met (confidence threshold, canary confirmation, and human approval for critical mitigations).

What this changes (high level): Adds a new prober subsystem in incident-bot that queries SLO burn-rates (via slo-toolkit adapter), selects probes by cost/impact score, and assembles an evidence bundle for the runbook suggester. The runbook suggester computes an action score and suppresses automated mitigation when the safety guard detects high blast-radius or insufficient telemetry coverage. A small CLI command (incidentctl prefetch) lets responders pre-warm the prober before a shift or during a postmortem.

Key behaviors: - Prioritization heuristic: weight by alert severity, recent error velocity, and correlation with high-cardinality dimensions. - Safe mitigation gating: mitigations are only eligible for automated execution when (1) runbook_score >= 0.8 AND (2) canary_probe passes OR human ack present. - Ephemeral collection: all probe artifacts are TTLed after 72 hours and sanitized for PII. - Telemetry: new metrics and traces exported for probe counts, action blocks, and evidence build time.

Checklist: - [x] Core prober implementation and unit tests - [x] Safety guard + policy engine - [x] slo-toolkit adapter for burn-rate queries - [x] CLI prefetch command and docs - [x] E2E smoke in staging - [x] Security sign-off for data retention and KMS usage

Testing & rollout: Unit and integration tests exercised locally and in CI; staging run executed against a canary stack for 48h with synthetic alerts. Rollout will be staged behind a feature flag (incident.autodiag.enabled) and safety_guard defaults to conservative mode (no auto-mitigations) until product sign-off.

Notes on scope: This PR intentionally avoids adding new automated mitigation implementations (e.g., restart services). Instead it focuses on decisioning and safe gating; future PRs will wire approved mitigations through the existing action runner.

Security/privacy: Probe artifacts are encrypted at rest using existing KMS keys; the sanitizer removes user-identifying fields from logs. Audit events emitted for every suggestion and blocked action.

Related items: ENG-1257 (autodiag roadmap), SRE-423 (safety policies), SUP-987 (support case that motivated live probe abstractions).

Summary: Adds a first-class handler in incident-bot for perf-canary regression alerts. The handler formats alerts into a consistent Slack thread, de-dupes repeated firings, and attaches deep links (Grafana dashboard + Confluence runbook + relevant traces) to speed triage.

Context: The perf-canary service will emit alerts as a webhook payload (model + region + tier + metric + observed vs baseline + confidence + baseline version/runtime tags). Before this PR, incident-bot treated canary payloads as generic webhooks which led to noisy, non-threaded posts and no reliable dedupe key, making it hard to triage during regressions and especially during baseline drift/threshold tuning.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a new webhook route + handler for source=perf-canary (Content-Type: application/json). 2) Builds a stable dedupe key and thread key so repeat evaluations (same model/metric/region/severity) update the same Slack thread instead of spamming the channel. 3) Produces a compact Slack message with: top-line regression summary; baseline vs observed; min-samples/confidence; tags (model_version/runtime_build/kernel_tag/hw_sku); and quick links. 4) Adds a lightweight state store interface for dedupe/threads (Redis-backed in prod; in-memory fake for tests). 5) Adds guardrails: drop oversized payload fields, strip unknown labels, and redact any prompt-like fields (defense-in-depth even though canary is synthetic).

Dedupe/threading behavior: - Dedupe key: perf_canary|<env>|<model_id>|<model_version>|<region>|<tier>|<metric>|<severity>|<baseline_id>|<runtime_build>|<hw_sku>. - Thread key: perf_canary|<env>|<model_id>|<region>|<tier>|<metric>|<severity>. - If a new alert matches an existing thread key within the configured TTL (default 6h), we post a reply in-thread and update the thread header (Slack message update) with the most recent observed values. - If severity escalates (warning -> page), we start/attach to the paging thread and include an explicit "Escalated" note with timestamps.

Links: - Runbook: sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/runbook-perf-regression-canary-alert (hardcoded base + slug; environment-aware). - Grafana: deep link to per-model dashboard with prefilled variables (model, region, tier, hw_sku) and time range anchored around first_seen. - Traces/logs: link templates for Tempo/Loki queries using request_route=perf-canary and model_id.

Testing: - Unit tests cover dedupe key generation, Slack block rendering, and TTL behavior. - Integration test covers "first alert creates thread" + "repeat alert updates thread" + "escalation".

Rollout: - Disabled by default behind flag incident_bot.perf_canary.enabled (default false). - Staging enabled for #eng-runtime-canary; prod enablement tracked in ENG-4878.

Checklist: - [x] Adds handler behind feature flag - [x] Slack formatting aligned with SRE paging hygiene - [x] Dedupe TTL configurable - [x] Runbook + dashboard links included - [x] Tests added - [x] Backward compatible with existing generic webhook handler
Allison Grant (review): Dedupe key includes baseline_id + runtime_build + hw_sku which is good, but the thread key currently also includes model_version. If model_version changes during rollout, we'll start a new thread and lose continuity. Can we keep thread key at model_id+region+tier+metric+severity and treat model_version as context in the message?
Rafael Mendes (author): Good catch. I’ll adjust: thread key will not include model_version; we’ll still include model_version in the dedupe key to prevent accidental suppression across versions. Also adding a line in the header showing current model_version.
Sean Gallagher (review): Paging channel selection: for Sev2+ we must route to #eng-oncall and @oncall-runtime (per policy). Right now it’s posting to #eng-runtime for both. Please wire severity routing + ensure the message includes a runbook link at the top.
Rafael Mendes (author): Updated routing logic: warn -> #eng-runtime, page -> #eng-oncall + mention group (configurable). Also moved runbook link into the first block and added "ACK / next steps" bullets.
Logan Wright (review): Telemetry links: please make sure Grafana link variables are URL-escaped; also include env in the link. We had broken links previously when model_id contained "/".
Rafael Mendes (author): Fixed by using url.QueryEscape on all vars and adding env as a required variable. Added tests for IDs with slashes and spaces.
Allison Grant (review): Slack formatting: the blocks are a bit long. Can we collapse the attribution tags (runtime_build/kernel_tag/hw_sku) into a single "Attribution" line and avoid a full JSON dump in the thread?
Rafael Mendes (author): Done. Tags are now a single line and we no longer print raw payload; only a compact summary + link to the stored payload in logs (request_id).

Adds compact on-call shift brief generation and optional redaction pipeline for sensitive snippets in attachments; backward compatible with existing incident snapshot format.
Motivation: On lengthy incidents engineers asked for a short machine-generated shift brief that distills important actions, outstanding tasks, entropy signals, and a scrubbed list of potentially sensitive snippets from pasted logs/attachments. This PR implements a compactifier service plus a sensitive-snippet-redactor step that runs as an opt-in transform in the incident-bundles pipeline. Key goals: produce a one-page shift brief per shift that is under 500 words, safely redact short sensitive artifacts (e.g., keys, IP+token combos, customer identifiers) using conservative heuristics and allow on-call to review before export. Implementation summary: 1) incident-bundle/compactifier: new module that ingests existing snapshots and produces a structured brief (summary, timeline highlights, action items, outstanding blockers, suggested follow-ups). 2) incident-bundle/redactor: regex + heuristic-based redaction with a small allowlist/blocklist, plus a review flag that surfaces redacted excerpts to reviewers. 3) CLI: adds `incident-bot brief generate --bundle <id> --redact [--dry-run]` for local ops. 4) retention/config: feature flag controls automatic brief creation and redact defaults are conservative. 5) tests & docs: unit tests for redaction heuristics, snapshot fixtures, end-to-end e2e job, and docs for operators. Checklist: || - [x] Design reviewed with SRE and Security (ENG-2314) || - [x] Unit tests added for redactor edge cases || - [x] e2e smoke validated on staging bundle samples || - [x] Docs and CLI help updated || - [x] Rollout plan with feature flag and telemetry events described || Migration notes: existing snapshot schema unchanged; compactifier is additive and stored under bundle.briefs.v1. Toggle is off by default for existing customers. Monitoring: added brief_generation.count, brief_generation.duration_ms, redaction.count, redaction.false_positive_alert to observability. Backwards compatibility: brief consumers will ignore bundle.briefs if absent. Rollout plan: enable flag for internal orgs for 48h, gather FP stats, then enable opt-in for customers.

Aisha Kline: Added telemetry names and a review flag; review/undo is implemented by storing redaction candidates in bundle.briefs.v1.review_candidates. Operator can 'incident-bot brief review <id> --approve <candidate-id>' to un-redact.

Summary: Introduces the 'Telemetry Telescope' — a compact, multiresolution telemetry preview generator for playbooks and on-call cards — and a new quiet-hours-aware escalation scorer that downranks non-critical alerts during configured quiet windows while preserving SLO-impacting escalations. Motivation: Oncall fatigue remains a top source of operational toil. We needed a lightweight way to present high-fidelity evidence to responders without forcing them into noisy context switches, and a principled scorer that respects customer-configured quiet-hours policies plus business-impact overrides. This PR bundles the backend scorer, a small React preview component used inside the incident-bot Slack card, a CLI dry-run mode for SREs, and a safe rollback path.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-3241)
- [x] End-to-end integration tests for scorer
- [x] UX review for compact telemetry preview
- [x] Slack workflow and permissions audit
- [x] Feature flagged behind incident.telemetry_telescope and incident.quiet_escalation

What changed (high level):
- scoring/quiet_escalation.py: new scorer that computes escalation_priority = base_score * quiet_window_factor * business_override. Quiet window factor decays non-critical scores by configurable exponent; business_override elevates alerts matching SLO or customer-impact rules.
- telemetry/telescope_generator.py: multiresolution time-series summarizer and compact evidence pack serializer (protobuf). Produces 3 levels (1m, 5m, 1h) plus anomaly annotations.
- slack/cards/telescope_card.tsx: new Slack Block kit compatible compact preview; relies on a hosted thumbnail URL for the mini heatmap.
- cli/incidentctl preview --telescope: CLI flag that returns summary JSON and a dry-run escalation decision for a given alert id.
- migrations/0007_add_quiet_policies.sql: DB schema for per-service quiet-hours windows and override rules.
- tests/*: unit tests for scorer edge cases, integration test that runs the CLI against fixture telemetry and asserts consistent decisions.

Commits (summary):
- 7d9b3f2 Add quiet escalation scorer + unit tests
- a3c1e88 Telescope generator prototype and serialization
- ff12aa0 Slack card + thumbnail renderer and UX polish
- b7d4c1e Hook up CLI preview flag and e2e test
- e8a9d4c Schema migration and feature flag gating

Review conversation (highlights):
- Evan McCarthy: "Nice, this addresses the mid-night noise problem we've been seeing. A couple asks: (1) can quiet window decay be tuned per-service? (2) please add a fallback when thumbnail generation fails so cards still render."
- Author (Priya): "Answered — decay already per-service, it's in the migration as quiet_policies.decay_exponent. Added thumbnail fallback to render a text-only summary if the image endpoint returns 4xx/5xx."
- Lina Rodríguez: "We should be conservative with defaults, especially for business_override. Recommend we default to false and require explicit rules to elevate."
- Author: "Changed default so business_override requires an allowlist; added a Linear task to document the allowlist governance."

CI and testing: Build and unit tests passed on first run. Integration e2e failed intermittently on thumbnail generator in CI due to a flaky image renderer; replaced reference with a stubbed renderer in tests and reran — green. All checks passed: unit, lint, typecheck, integration (flaky case stubbed), security-scan.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind two feature flags (incident.telemetry_telescope and incident.quiet_escalation).
2) Enable CLI dry-run for SREs to evaluate decisions across recent incidents for two weeks.
3) Default quiet-hours policy is disabled; encourage teams to opt-in with per-service decay_exponent and allowlist business overrides.
4) After one week of opt-in trials and no regression in critical escalations (monitored via regression eval), flip the default on for low-noise non-prod services.

Backout and safety: The whole behavior is gated behind feature flags and scoped by DB policies; scorer is deterministic and has a safe-mode that preserves escalation if telemetry indicates SLO breach. We've included a fast rollback by toggling incident.quiet_escalation to false. Migration is additive (new table) and tested in downgrade path in migration tests.

Notes on privacy and size: Telescope evidence packs are redacted of PII by the summarizer (removes string traces and replaces sampled IDs with stable hashes). Packs are capped at 128KB; if exceeded, the generator will return a manifest that instructs the card to render a link to a secure evidence bundle rather than inlining content.

Related work: ENG-3241 design doc, ENG-3309 follow-up for governance UI, SUP-9876 customer request for quiet-hours control.

Merge: Squash and merge after approvals. Commit message standardized to include Linear refs and migration tag.

Adds a multiresolution telemetry preview (Telemetry Telescope) and a quiet-hours-aware escalation scoring function used by incident-bot to reduce noisy wakeups. Includes CLI dry-run and Slack workflow integration.

Why: We keep losing time (and occasionally accuracy) in the first 10–15 minutes of an incident because the intake form doesn’t capture the info required to pick the right public status page component(s). This led to coarse updates ("API") even when the impact was limited to Streaming or Embeddings in a single region. This PR updates the incident intake workflow to require three customer-facing classification fields (component, region, capability) and adds validation + reminders so Comms Lead can publish component-accurate updates quickly.

Motivation: Our runbooks/playbooks corpus has accumulated duplicated or near-duplicate remediation steps and fractured guidance across teams. This makes on-call work slower and increases drift in documented response. This PR introduces a Playbook Consolidator service and a duplicate-step clusterer that discovers semantically similar steps across the corpus and produces safe, reviewable consolidation suggestions. Approach: 1) Offline analysis uses sentence- and step-level embeddings (existing incident-bot embedding pipeline) with a two-stage clustering: approximate nearest neighbor kNN to collect candidates, then agglomerative clustering with a configurable similarity threshold. 2) Step normalization and canonicalization heuristics reduce noise (strip timestamps, redact instance IDs, normalize common command variants). 3) A preview-only consolidation patch generator emits a suggested merged playbook diff and a migration plan (backlinks from removed steps to canonical step ids). 4) Safety-first rollout: the consolidator runs as an opt-in job in the console and only produces suggestions; an operator can apply a dry-run patch or accept full migration. 5) UI: added a consolidation-preview page that surfaces clustering rationale, representative step samples, confidence scores, and links to related metrics (run count, last-used). Implementation highlights: - New package incident-bot/pkg/playbook/consolidator.go implementing the clustering pipeline and patch generator. - CLI: cmd/consolidate/main.go to run local analyses and produce JSON suggestions for manual review or automation. - Console: web/ui/playbooks/consolidation-preview.tsx adds an interactive diff + accept/reject flow (feature gated). - Telemetry: breath metrics (consolidation_runs_total, suggestions_generated, clusters_confirmed) and annotation of applied migrations for audit trails. Tests & validation: - Added unit tests for normalization rules and cluster scoring. - Small integration harness that runs on a 200-playbook sample (testdata/playbooks/dup_examples.yaml) to validate no-destructive merges. - Performance: approximate pipeline runs end-to-end on 200 playbooks in ~12s on CI runner with embedded caching; production job will be batched and rate-limited. Related work: references ENG-2134 (playbook hygiene initiative) and ENG-2199 (embedding infra stability). Rollout plan: feature-gated behind "consolidation" flag in console; initial run limited to internal sandboxes and docs teams, followed by opt-in org-level preview. Backout: generated patches are reversible; migration records are persisted for audit. Why different from earlier work: many previous PRs focused on incident snapshots, runbook generation, or triage helpers; this PR specifically targets long-term playbook corpus quality by recommending consolidation rather than auto-deleting content. Security & safety: redaction is conservative (requires manual review before applying), and all applied migrations are logged with user attribution. Docs: docs/playbook-consolidation.md explains the algorithm, UI flows, and suggested governance. Request: reviewers please validate clustering thresholds and canonicalization heuristics; UX reviewers please sanity-check the preview page.

Maya Chen: Added namespace-aware weighting and an opt-out tag; clustering keeps team-scoped clusters separate unless operator explicitly chooses cross-team consolidation.

Motivation: On-call teams have reported high pager churn caused by short-lived metric spikes and flapping alerts from third-party services. This PR introduces a per-service dampener and a transient-suppressor policy in incident-bot to reduce noisy pages while preserving actionable incidents.

Summary of changes: adds a new ServiceDampener policy engine which tracks recent alert emissions per service and suppresses repeat pages inside a configurable quiet window; implements a TransientSuppressor stage that defers notifications for rules with low-confidence signals for a short evaluation window; exposes service-level configuration via the incident-bot config store and Console feature flag for canary rollout; includes unit and e2e tests and a migration to populate default dampening profiles for existing services.

Key design points: default behavior is conservative — no incidents are auto-closed; only notification emissions are suppressed. Dampener is keyed by (service_id, alert_signature) and supports exponential backoff for repeated noise. TransientSuppressor stores a short-lived hypothesis for an alert (TTL ~30s by default) and will only escalate if the condition persists or additional corroborating signals arrive. Operators can override per-service thresholds and exempt critical services.

Configuration knobs added: service_config[dampener.enabled:boolean], service_config[dampener.quiet_window_seconds:int], service_config[dampener.max_backoff_seconds:int], service_config[transient.enable:boolean], service_config[transient.eval_window_seconds:int], global.feature_flags[service_dampener_canary].

Testing and rollout: unit tests included for backoff maths, suppression TTL and signature collisions. e2e test harness simulates a noisy external service to verify reduced pager counts. Rollout plan: enable canary flag for 5% of services for 48 hours, review PagerDuty incident rate delta and customer-facing SLOs, then ramp to 100% if no regression.

Security and compliance: no secrets change, audit log events added for suppressed notifications to ensure traceability.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-78910)
- [x] Feature gated behind Console flag and service config
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Migration script for default profiles
- [x] Canary rollout plan documented

High-level commits: see `commits` field.

References: Linear ENG-78910, incident postmortem SUP-3241 where this pattern was requested.
Amina Patel: Nice approach, but we need to ensure suppressed notifications still generate audit events that are searchable — can we add an indexable annotation?
Morgan Chen: Added suppressed.notification telemetry and a search tag; updated migration to populate initial annotations.
Diego Ramos: Can we make the default evaluation window for TransientSuppressor configurable per-rule as well? Some anomaly rules are inherently bursty.
Morgan Chen: Added per-rule override (transient.eval_window_seconds) with fallback to service-level setting; updated docs.

Summary: Introduces a new 'oncall contextualizer' feature that collects compact, privacy-safe diagnostic snapshots for incidents triggered via the incident-bot flow. The snapshot is intentionally size-limited (~<20KB by default) and encoded for inclusion in Slack notification attachments and incident threads. Motivation: paging and early triage today require toggling into dashboards and long trace views. This PR surfaces a condensed, structured view (top spans, latency histogram, recent error classes, small log window and metric deltas) to reduce time-to-action for first responders.

What changed (high level):
- New service component `contextualizer` in incident-bot that orchestrates lightweight collection and assembly of diagnostic artifacts (trace headers, top-5 spans, 60s metric deltas, 10 recent log lines sampled).
- Compact snapshot format: a binary-friendly base64 envelope with an accompanying JSON summary used by Slack attachments and the web runbook view.
- Redaction pipeline to strip PII-like tokens (emails, keys, IP addresses) using existing redact util and new heuristics for file paths and long UUIDs.
- CLI helper `incbot snapshot preview` for engineers to locally generate and inspect compact snapshots for a given trace id.
- Tests: unit coverage for assembly/redaction, integration test that runs the snapshot collector against a small synthetic trace and asserts size, schema, and redaction.
- Docs: short addition to README and a new section in docs/oncall-context.md describing opt-in config and privacy guarantees.

- 3c4d5e: redaction heuristics and tests for suspicious tokens

- pkg/contextualizer/snapshot_schema.md (new): compact snapshot schema documentation

- docs/oncall-context.md (new): opt-in configuration and privacy guarantees
- build/ci/incbot-integration.yml: adds an integration job to validate snapshot size and redaction
- pkg/contextualizer/integration_test.go: synthetic trace + assertions

Code snippets (illustrative):
- Example compact summary JSON (included in tests):
  {"incident_id":"INC-2026-42", "top_spans":[{"name":"db.query","p50_ms":12}], "metric_deltas":{"req_s":"+120%"}, "logs_sample": ["error connecting to ledger"], "size_bytes": 10832}

Testing & CI:
- Initial CI run (first push) showed a flaky timing assertion in integration_test.go (assert size < 20KB) on Github Actions macOS runner. I relaxed the timing window and made the synthetic trace deterministic.
- Re-run CI: all checks passed. CI jobs: unit, linters, integration (snapshot-size-validation), fmt, vulnerability-scan.

Review thread (selected):
- Jordan Kim (reviewer): "Love the idea. Please ensure redaction is irreversible and document the heuristics used. Also call out the default size limit and whether size is configurable."
- Aisha (author): "Good call — added docs/oncall-context.md and a 'redaction_rules.md' subsection. Default size is 20KB, configurable via INCIDENT_SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES. Redaction uses redact util + additional regexes; tests included."
- Tomás Rivera (reviewer): "Can we avoid pulling full traces from production on every incident? Add sampling policy or TTL cache."
- Aisha: "Added a strict sampling policy: only retrieve full trace when request rate > threshold AND when trace has error spans. Otherwise assemble from lightweight trace headers. Sampling config: INCIDENT_SNAPSHOT_SAMPLING=error-50pct. Also added a small in-memory TTL cache keyed by trace id to avoid duplicate fetches in traffic spikes."
- Maya Singh (security reviewer): "Please ensure S3 upload of envelopes excludes sensitive customer IDs and mark retention 7d by default. Also add KMS encryption for stored blobs."
- Aisha: "Snapshots are not persisted by default; when enabled they go to the ephemeral bucket with server-side encryption. I added the retention default to 7d and a config flag INCIDENT_SNAPSHOT_PERSIST=true to opt in. docs/oncall-context.md documents this."

Backward compatibility & rollout plan:
- Feature is behind feature flag INCIDENT_CONTEXT_COMPACT (off by default). Rolling deploy plan: enable for internal SRE team first (1 day), expand to a subset of customer incidents (canary via alert tags) for 72h, then global if no privacy or performance regressions. Rollback toggle added in Console feature flags.

Privacy & security notes:
- Redaction + sampling minimize PII exposure; snapshots are size-limited and default to non-persistent. We explicitly avoid including full request/response bodies unless opt-in.
- KMS encryption and S3 retention are documented and require a dedicated enterprise opt-in for Private installs.

Performance considerations:
- Collector uses bounded goroutines with backpressure and a TTL cache to cap calls to the trace service during alert storms. Local synthetic bench shows average assembly latency ~35ms under normal load and 120ms under high contention (within oncall SLO target).

Follow-ups / TODOs (tracked in Linear):
- ENG-2135: Add UI expansion to view full trace from the compact snapshot (deferred).
- ENG-2137: Add opt-out per-customer setting for private deployments.
- SRE-449: Hardening for high-cardinality error types in the sampler.

Merge: Squash-merged to main after approvals (Jordan, Tomás, Maya) and green CI.

Notes for maintainers: If you see size flakiness in the integration job, increase synthetic determinism in integration_test.go by setting env TEST_SYNTHETIC_SEED=42.
Adds an on-call contextualizer that captures compact trace snapshots, recent logs and metric deltas for faster first-response triage. Backwards-compatible; opt-in via config flag INCIDENT_CONTEXT_COMPACT=true.

Context: As part of the Private Day-2 backup/restore toolkit, we need an opinionated observability pack that SRE/Solutions can deploy into customer VPC/on-prem environments to answer two questions quickly: (1) are backups happening and completing successfully on schedule, and (2) are restore drills passing and meeting RTO targets in staging. This PR adds a set of dashboards and alert rules designed to work across hosted VPC installs and constrained on-prem/air-gapped setups (where available metrics are limited and log shipping may be disabled). Scope: (A) dashboards for backup job success rate, last_success_ts, duration, bytes, and error categories; (B) dashboards for restore drill outcomes (pass/fail, duration, validation phase breakdown) and drill cadence; (C) alert rules with conservative defaults plus documented tuning for noisy environments (slow object storage, intermittent KMS throttling, planned maintenance). Metrics assumed: redwood_private_backup_job_success_total, redwood_private_backup_job_duration_seconds, redwood_private_backup_bytes_total, redwood_private_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds, redwood_private_restore_drill_success_total, redwood_private_restore_drill_duration_seconds, redwood_private_restore_validation_phase_duration_seconds, and redwood_private_backup_error_total{category=...} (emitted by control-plane + installer hooks in related PRs). Dashboards/alerts are grouped under a new folder 'Redwood Private / Backup & DR'. Tuning notes: alert thresholds use per-install labels (deployment_id, environment, cluster) and are designed to avoid paging during planned maintenance by supporting a maintenance label/recording rule override; duration alerts are based on p95 over a 6h window to reduce sensitivity to occasional NFS/S3 jitter; stale backup alert uses last_success_ts with configurable expected_interval (default 24h) and grace window (default +6h). Out of scope: defining the core metrics emission (handled in redwood monorepo), paging policy selection (SRE runbook), and customer-specific routing/notification integrations. Validation: Tested in staging with a simulated failing backup job and an intentionally broken restore drill; ensured alerts fire and resolve; verified dashboard variables work when some metric series are absent (air-gapped mode without bytes_total). Screenshots are attached in the PR comments (not committed).
- Adds Grafana dashboards for Redwood Private backup jobs + restore drills (success, duration, bytes, last success). - Adds Prometheus alert rules for stale backups and failing restore drills with tuning knobs + maintenance-window guidance.

dashboards(private): add Restore Drill dashboard (outcomes, duration, phase breakdown)
alerts(private): add stale backup + backup failure rate rules with labels + annotations
alerts(private): add restore drill failing + restore drill stale rules (staging-focused defaults)
docs: add tuning notes for noisy storage/KMS + maintenance window suppression guidance
chore: normalize dashboard UIDs + folder structure; update jsonnet lint

Alert rule (stale backup): alert: RedwoodPrivateBackupStale expr: (time() - redwood_private_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds) > (redwood_private_backup_expected_interval_seconds + redwood_private_backup_grace_seconds) for: 30m labels: severity: page annotations: summary: "Backup stale for {{ $labels.cluster }}" description: "No successful backup within expected interval (+grace). Check backup CronJob, storage backend, KMS availability, and permissions."
Duration panel query: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, cluster, environment) (rate(redwood_private_backup_job_duration_seconds_bucket[6h])))
CI: jsonnet-lint, grafana-dashboard-schema, promtool check rules (PASS). Manual: staged alert firing via metric injection + disabled restore drill runner to confirm stale alert. Verified dashboards render with missing optional series.
Allison Grant (review): The dashboard layout looks good. Two requests: (1) please avoid alerting on raw 'increase(failures[5m]) > 0' because it’ll be noisy for KMS hiccups; prefer error rate over a longer window + add a severity split. (2) make sure all panels have consistent label keys (cluster/environment/deployment_id) and default variables work if deployment_id is missing (older installs).
Sergio Costa (author): Updated alerts to use a 30m window for failure-rate plus a 'warning' tier, and added a fallback variable mapping when deployment_id is absent. Also standardized label joins in queries so panels don’t drop series.
Sean Gallagher (review): Please add explicit guidance on maintenance windows. We keep getting paged during upgrade windows in staging. Can we support a suppression label or a recording rule that on-call can flip?
Sergio Costa (author): Added docs section 'Maintenance windows / planned downtime' with two options: Alertmanager silence + optional recording rule redwood_private_maintenance_window{cluster=...}=1 to gate paging alerts. Also added alert expr guard 'unless on(cluster) redwood_private_maintenance_window == 1' when the series exists.
Neha Kapoor (review): Restore drill alert defaults should be non-paging by default outside staging. Can we set severity=warn unless environment=staging, and add annotation to point to the DR runbook?
Sergio Costa (author): Done. Restore drill failing is warn by default and upgrades to page only for environment=staging (or when redwood_private_restore_drill_paging_enabled==1). Added runbook link annotation and consistent 'next steps' text.
Rafael Mendes (review): One more thing: add a panel showing drill cadence (days since last successful drill) and include it on the overview dashboard. We use that in game day readiness reviews.
Sergio Costa (author): Added 'Days since last successful restore drill' stat + timeseries; also included it on Backup Overview as a secondary row.
Allison Grant (approve): LGTM after the alert tuning changes and label normalization. Thanks for including the maintenance window guidance.
Sean Gallagher (approve): Approved. This matches what on-call needs; please ensure release notes call out the new severity behavior for restore drill alerts.

Summary: Adds a lightweight on-call 'breadcrumbs' capture and a small rollback-hint proxy that surfaces likely revert actions when automated mitigations are suggested. Motivation: during incidents engineers wanted a compact, privacy-safe timeline that highlights key actions (deploys, autoscale events, mitigation commands) without pulling full traces or huge logs. This PR implements a compact breadcrumb store, a UI card to surface breadcrumbs in the incident view, and a small proxy that annotates runbook suggestions with a 'rollback hint' when the recent breadcrumb pattern matches known deploy-caused incidents. Design notes: - Breadcrumbs are sampled, encrypted at rest, and kept for 7 days by default. Each breadcrumb is a small structured event (type, short message, actor, timestamp, optional anchor token) limited to 256 bytes to avoid PII. - Rollback-hint proxy is a ruleset-based annotator that consults recent breadcrumbs and the incident's signal taxonomy to append a hint like: "recent deploy from service-x at 03:14 may be a root cause — consider revert or pin previous image". Rules are conservative and require two corroborating signals to avoid noisy suggestions. - Privacy sanitization: breadcrumb messages go through a sanitizer that strips emails, long stack traces, and API keys. The UI shows a blurred preview with an expand action that requires an extra click and an audit log entry. - Backwards compatibility: feature guarded behind a config flag incident_bot.features.breadcrumbs and an RBAC toggle (role: incident_reader or higher). No API changes for existing webhooks. Checklist: - [x] Implement breadcrumb collector and in-memory sharded store - [x] Persist compact snapshots to object store with TTL - [x] Add sanitizer and redact pipeline - [x] Rollback-hint proxy with 3 simple rules + unit tests - [x] UI card component with blur/expand and audit hook - [x] Helm values and upgrade docs - [x] End-to-end smoke test in CI (local emulation) What changed (high level): commits: see commits list; files changed: internal oncall capture, sanitizer, annotator, small web UI component, helm values, docs. Testing: unit tests for capture rules and rollback proxy rules; an integration smoke harness that simulates a deploy->latency spike pattern and verifies hint shows up. CI notes: initial CI run had a flaky snapshot test (tests/oncall/breadcrumbs_test.go TestSanitizerRace) that failed on race on macOS runners; I reproduced locally, added a short mutex around the test harness and re-ran — CI passed on rerun. Rollout: behind config flag; we'll flip in a controlled canary group (10% of orgs) for 48 hours then widen. If we see more than 3 false-positive hints per 100 incidents, we will rollback the flag. Related work: ENG-2184 (compact incident artifacts), ENG-3301 (runbook hinting RFC). Docs: docs/runbooks/breadcrumbs.md explains storage, retention, and administrator controls. Links: design RFC: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2184/compact-breadcrumbs, deploy checklist: https://wiki.redwood.internal/oncall/breadcrumbs-deploy. Release notes: Adds optional breadcrumbs capture and rollback hinting to incident-bot behind feature flag. No breaking changes. Security: breadcrumbs sanitized and encrypted; KMS-integration for object store snapshots documented. 
Evan Torres (2026-02-06): Nice, this will reduce time-to-context. Please add a short note on how breadcrumbs differ from full trace captures in the docs.
Maya Chen (2026-02-06): Added a paragraph in docs/runbooks/breadcrumbs.md clarifying size, retention and sanitization tradeoffs.
Priya Nair (2026-02-08): Request changes: make sanitizer rulechain pluggable (we may add more scrubbers), and add metrics for breadcrumb drop rate when sanitizer rejects payloads.
Maya Chen (2026-02-09): Addressed: exposed sanitizer hook and added oncall.breadcrumbs.sanitizer_rejects metric (count). Added unit tests for rejection path.
Jonah Reed (2026-02-10): Found a race in breadcrumbs_test (CI repro). Suggest moving the shared harness to a test-only helper and adding a small mutex; also point the helm chart default TTL to 7d vs 30d default in values.
Maya Chen (2026-02-10): Fixed test harness and updated helm default to 7d in incident-bot-values.yaml. Re-ran CI — snapshot flake reproduced on macOS, added a guarding sleep in harness and converted a global counter to atomic ops.
Evan Torres (2026-02-11): Approved after verifying sanitizer metrics and test fixes. Priya approved as well. Merging once CI green.
Initial CI run: unit tests 152 passed, 1 flaky failure (sanitizer race) on macOS runner; re-run succeeded. Integration smoke passed in emulation. Lint and security scans pass.
Adds opt-in lightweight breadcrumbs capture for incidents and a conservative rollback-hint annotator. Feature is disabled by default; ops can enable via incident_bot.features.breadcrumbs in helm values. Sanitization and audit controls included.
After upgrade: set incident_bot.features.breadcrumbs=true and tune incident_bot.breadcrumbs.ttl_days to desired retention. Monitor metric oncall.breadcrumbs.sanitizer_rejects and oncall.breadcrumbs.hints_true_positives/false_positives.
Canary enable for 10% orgs for 48h, monitor false-positive rate and sanitizer reject counts; rollback by setting flag to false and deleting recent compact snapshots if privacy concerns arise.

Context: We've been seeing noisy SLO alerts caused by multi-stage invocation patterns where kernel queueing and KV-cache warmup dominate tail latency and token cost. This PR introduces a lightweight "invocation mesh fidelity" signal that correlates per-invocation phase coverage (prefetch/warmup/steady/evict) with token-level cost and a new oriented alert slicer that can produce candidate quieting rules for oncall and alerting pipelines. Motivation: Reduce alert churn and enable SREs/product engineers to debug long-tail cost regressions by slicing alerts along invocation-phase fidelity and kernel-queue-pressure dimensions. Goals: (1) Surface a compact set of per-invocation fidelity histograms (phase coverage, warmup hit rates), (2) Add an alert-slice builder that suggests suppression candidates when a majority of high-cost samples are warmup-dominated, (3) Add a dashboard and runbook links for triage. Checklist: - [x] Collector: add fidelity fields to the invocation protobuf and exporter (observability-pack/collectors/mesh_fidelity/collector.go) - [x] Metrics: implement phase_coverage, warmup_hit_ratio, kernel_queue_pressure gauges and token_cost_by_phase histogram - [x] Tracing: enrich spans with fidelity tags and add a compact span summary for drilldown - [x] Alerting: oriented-alert-slicer service that ingests sampled traces and emits suggested alert filters - [x] Dashboard: new 'Invocation Mesh' dashboard with sparkline panels and phased cost stack - [x] Tests: unit tests for exporter and e2e replay with synthetic tracebench - [x] Docs: short runbook + API notes in observability-pack/docs/invocation-mesh.md What changed (high level): - Introduced a mesh_fidelity exporter that attaches phase annotations to invocations; the exporter is conservative (defaults to "unknown") and is opt-in via config. - Added three primary metrics: invocation_phase_coverage{phase}, invocation_warmup_hit_ratio, kernel_queue_pressure_samples and a histogram token_cost_phase_bucketed to allow per-phase cost attribution. - Added a lightweight oriented-alert-slicer binary that analyzes a recent window of sampled spans and returns a ranked list of alert-suppression candidates (e.g., "suppress if warmup_hit_ratio < 0.3 AND kernel_queue_pressure > 0.8"). - New Grafana dashboard (observability-pack/dashboards/invocation-mesh.json) with panels for phase coverage, per-phase token-cost waterfall, and an alert suggestion panel that links to the slicer UI. - Small updates to the trace sampler to ensure we include fidelity headers for span rehydration in logs for the synthetic replay. Backwards compatibility: exporter emits new tags but preserves existing fields; older collectors ignore the extra tags. Operational notes: the slicer runs as a best-effort periodic job; suggested filters are not applied automatically. See runbook for recommended thresholds and how to adopt suggestions. Risks/Mitigations: - Incorrect phase classification could lead to bad suggestions; mitigated by conservative defaults and a "confidence" field included with each suggestion. - Additional metric cardinality: phase is low-cardinality (prefetch/warmup/steady/evict/unknown) and we aggregate before export. Testing: included unit tests for classification heuristics and a small replaybench that validates token-cost attribution on synthetic warmup-heavy traces. Rollout: feature gated behind observability.enable_mesh_fidelity (false by default) and an opt-in dashboard import. Related: ENG-983 (alert quieting), ENG-1142 (kernel queue tracing), SUP-4021 (customer-reported warmup alerts).
Diego Rivera: Can we ensure the phase tag is indexed at export time? indexing would blow up cardinality if we aren't careful.
Maya Patel: We only expose phase as a low-cardinality label (5 values) and aggregate by tenant before export; added note in collector README.
Alex Chen: Slicer output looks promising but please add a confidence percentile and a sample reference ID for triage.
Maya Patel: Added confidence field and sample_ref to each suggestion; updated tests to assert presence.
Priya Nair: CI was flaky on the replaybench; saw a timeout on the synthetic runner.
Maya Patel: Increased the replay timeout and mocked the disk IO in test to avoid CI flakiness.
Added invocation mesh fidelity metrics (phase coverage, warmup hit ratio, kernel queue pressure), a new invocation-mesh dashboard, and an oriented alert slicer to suggest alert-suppression rules for warmup-dominated noise. Feature is opt-in and disabled by default.
If you receive an alert with suggested suppression from the slicer, validate against sample_ref footprints in the dashboard and only apply suggestions that have confidence >= 0.85. The slicer suggestions are only hints; do not auto-apply.

Motivation: Teams building retrieval-augmented agents often need to integrate event streams (webhooks, change-feed) and GraphQL backends into tool-calling workflows. This PR adds a compact, opinionated example that demonstrates: an event-sourced RAG pattern (incremental index updates via webhooks), a lightweight GraphQL tool adapter for function-style tool calls, and a telemetry preset tuned for low-overhead dev tracing.
Summary of changes: added an examples/rag/event-sourced-graphql sample with runnable playground config, a GraphQL adapter (TS), webhook indexer stubs, a small smoke test suite, docs snippets for the devsite, and a telemetry preset JSON.
Checklist: - [x] Sample code and README - [x] Local playground config and Dockerfile for quick smoke runs - [x] Compact telemetry preset and docs snippet - [x] CI smoke workflow - [x] Internal design doc link in README (Linear ENG-9123)
What the sample demonstrates: - Event-sourced retrieval: documents are added/updated via an inbound webhook emulator and incrementally applied to a tiny in-memory index + optional persisted SQLite indexer. - GraphQL tool adapter: exposes a typesafe tool wrapper (graphqlTool) that performs queries/mutations against a GraphQL service and returns structured results usable by the agent. The adapter includes simple retry/backoff and schema-respecting output shaping. - Tool calling contract: minimal contract examples (input schema, expected output) and a contract linter config so authors can experiment with structured-tool workflows. - Telemetry: a compact telemetry preset (telemetry/presets/event-sourced-compact.json) that emits token-level cost and per-tool timing only at debug/dev level to avoid signal noise and billing delta in dev clusters.
How to run locally: 1) cd examples/rag/event-sourced-graphql 2) yarn install && yarn build 3) docker-compose up (the playground spins up a tiny GraphQL mock, webhook emulator, and the sample agent) 4) open http://localhost:3000/playground to run the example scenarios
Notes on testing and CI: - Added .github/workflows/smoke.yml that runs the smoke harness (build + smoke tests). The first CI run failed due to flaky GraphQL mock startup; fixed by adding a healthcheck and small startup delay in the docker-compose shim. - Smoke tests cover: index ingestion via webhook, a GraphQL-backed tool call, and a full end-to-end generation that asserts a structured JSON tool response.
Commits (high level): - 1a2b3c4: scaffold event-sourced-graphql example and initial README - 2b3c4d5: add graphql adapter + contract examples - 3c4d5e6: telemetry preset + docs snippet - 4d5e6f7: add smoke tests and github workflow - 5e6f7g8: CI flakiness fix (healthcheck)
Files changed (high level): - examples/rag/event-sourced-graphql/README.md: new walkthrough and developer notes - examples/rag/event-sourced-graphql/src/graphql_adapter.ts: GraphQL tool adapter + small retry layer - examples/rag/event-sourced-graphql/src/webhook_indexer.ts: webhook emulator + indexer glue - examples/rag/event-sourced-graphql/playground/docker-compose.yml: local playground config - examples/rag/event-sourced-graphql/tests/smoke.test.ts: compact smoke tests - telemetry/presets/event-sourced-compact.json: telemetry preset for dev runs - docs/snippets/rag-event-sourced-graphql.md: docsite snippet used by new RN and examples gallery - .github/workflows/smoke.yml: CI smoke job - examples/rag/event-sourced-graphql/Dockerfile: build for playground
Review conversation (summary): - Ethan Liu (reviewer): "Nice focused example — can we add a short note about access control for GraphQL endpoints and masking sensitive fields in the telemetry preset?" Author reply (Maya): "Good catch — added a security note in the README and removed user-identifying fields from the telemetry preset (we mark them as redacted by default)." - Priya Kapoor (reviewer): "Adapter looks good; please add a tiny unit test for the adapter's retry path and explicitly surface retry config in README." Author reply (Maya): "Added retry unit and documented config in README. Kept defaults low so examples don't stall." - Jordan Miles (reviewer): "CI flake observed on first run; looks resolved after healthcheck change. Approving once CI passes." Author reply (Maya): "Re-ran CI, verified green — pushed the healthcheck fix."
Rationale and design notes: - We intentionally keep the example small (single-file adapter + short README) to lower maintenance and to act as a pattern for teams that need to stitch event-driven sources into RAG agents without adopting our full ingestion pipeline. - Telemetry preset demonstrates a conservative default for dev usage: it captures per-tool latency and token counts at debug level only, and redacts PII fields before emission. - The GraphQL adapter is intentionally minimal: it returns structured JSON matching tool contracts rather than a free-text answer, showing how to use the agent's structured output tooling.
Related work: references ENG-9123 (design doc), examples/rag/edge-graphql (older adapter) is intentionally not duplicated; this PR focuses on event-sourced index updates.
Migration notes: no breaking changes. No runtime flags changed.
Docs update: docs/snippets/rag-event-sourced-graphql.md added and will be referenced from the examples gallery.
Follow-ups (TBD): - Add a variant showing persisted indexer backed by SQLite + WAL for larger demos - Add an enterprise note for webhook signature verification (linked linear PM-412)
Add an event-sourced RAG example demonstrating GraphQL-backed tool adapters, webhook-driven index updates, and compact telemetry presets for low-cost dev tracing.

Maya Singh: Added security note and redaction to preset
Priya Kapoor: Add retry unit test and doc
Maya Singh: Added retry unit and documented config

Context: During the route experiments beta we saw a subset of streaming requests (SSE) lose experiment attribution after a retry, which caused (a) undercounted per-variant traffic, (b) misleading guardrail charts, and (c) confusing traces where the initial attempt was tagged but the retry attempt was not. This was escalated via SUP-24877 and corroborated by staging attribution-drop dashboards. Root cause: Our streaming retry path reconstructs a new RequestContext / SpanContext for the retry attempt. The base routing decision (including experiment assignment) was persisted on the first attempt, but the retry code path re-evaluated portions of the request pipeline and did not copy experiment dimensions into the retry context. In some cases we also emitted the streaming response headers from the retry attempt before experiment tags were re-attached, so x-redwood-experiment-id / x-redwood-experiment-variant were missing even though the route was in an active experiment. Changes: (1) Persist experiment assignment (experiment_id, variant_id, config_version) into the per-request RetryState and rehydrate it into the retry RequestContext before any OTel spans/metrics are emitted. (2) Ensure the streaming response header writer reads attribution from RequestContext (not transient span tags) so retries remain consistent. (3) Add a guard to prevent re-bucketing on retry unless the original assignment is absent (maintains determinism and prevents variant flipping mid-stream). (4) Add coverage: integration test exercising streaming + injected mid-stream network failure + retry, asserting that experiment dimensions remain stable across attempts and are present on emitted spans/metrics and response debug headers. Safety/rollout: This is behind the existing route experiments feature flag; behavior only changes when retries occur. Added a metric counter for attribution_rehydrated_on_retry to validate impact in canary. Linked work: ADR-048 (attribution schema), PR-28470 (request context plumbing).
Fixes a bug where experiment_id/variant_id attribution could be dropped on server-side streaming retry paths, improving correctness of per-variant metrics and traces in Console.
Logan Wright (Telemetry): The approach makes sense. Can we confirm we’re not increasing cardinality by adding per-attempt tags? Also please ensure we don’t re-bucket on retry; variant flipping would be a nightmare for attribution.
Caleb Johnson (author): Good call. This keeps the same attribution tags per attempt; no new dimensions. Also added a hard guard: if RetryState has assignment, we skip bucketing entirely and just rehydrate. Added assertions in the integration test to prevent variant changes across attempts.
Jordan Lee (Policy Engine): Why not always re-evaluate bucketing for correctness if config changed mid-request?
Caleb Johnson (author): For streaming, we prioritize per-request determinism. Re-bucketing mid-stream can cause headers/metrics mismatch and violate stickiness expectations. If config changes after the first attempt, the next request will pick it up; this keeps a single request consistent.
Vikram Singh (Data plane): Can you add a log/debug field showing config_version used for the rehydrated path? Helps oncall debugging.
Caleb Johnson (author): Added experiment_config_version to the internal debug log line on retry and exposed it in the internal assignment explain endpoint payload (when present).
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Please add a metric so we can validate the fix during beta without digging through logs. Also ensure it doesn’t spam on high retry rates.
Caleb Johnson (author): Added attribution_rehydrated_on_retry counter and it’s only emitted once per retry attempt. No labels beyond route_id (already present elsewhere) and experiment_id/variant_id (existing dims).
payload.title: Fix missing experiment attribution on streaming retries
