Context: As part of the Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding reliability program, we need first-class visibility into (a) when we are shedding traffic vs failing implicitly, and (b) when breakers are opening/half-opening/closing across regions/models/tiers. This PR adds Grafana dashboards and initial Prometheus alert rules for overload protection signals. Scope: (1) Dashboards: Add "Hosted API • Overload Protection" dashboard group with panels for shed rate, breaker open rate, admission decisions, runtime saturation proxies (queue depth / token saturation / memory pressure proxy), and top shed reasons. Includes recommended drilldowns by region and route family, and a safe set of labels (bounded cardinality). (2) Alerts: Add first-pass paging + ticket alerts for (i) sustained breaker-open rate, (ii) elevated shed rate for paid tiers, (iii) Retry-After header missing on overload responses (via gateway metric), and (iv) mismatch between shed and runtime saturation (possible false positive / bad thresholds). Each alert includes runbook links and suggested next actions. (3) Runbook links: Links to oncall runbook and runtime mitigation guide; includes incident-bot channel references. Notes/guardrails: We intentionally avoid tenant_id and request_id as dimensions. Model is aggregated to a small allowlist via label mapping in the gateway metrics exporter. Dashboards default to last 1h and show p95/p99 lat overlay to correlate shedding with tail latency improvements. Follow-ups: (a) tighten alert thresholds after canary (false positives), (b) add per-tier SLO burn overlays once SLO toolkit classification is rolled out everywhere, (c) add a "top fallback attempts" panel after routing PR-18458 is fully deployed. Screenshots: See internal preview link in the Grafana folder (can be rendered in CI). Runbooks: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ONCALL/Hosted+Overload+Circuit+Breaker+Runbook and https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SERVING/Runtime+Overload+Mitigation. Testing: `make lint`, `make test`, `make dashboards-validate`, `make prom-rules-test`.
Rafael Mendes (review): Dashboard looks good. Two asks: (1) can we add an explicit panel for breaker state transitions (open->half-open->closed) rather than just open_rate? (2) alert thresholds: shed_rate > 2% for 10m might be noisy during canary; can we gate paging to enterprise tiers only and create a ticket-level alert for everyone else?
Aisha Bello (author): Added a "Breaker state transitions" panel using `increase(breaker_state_changes_total{to_state!="closed"}[5m])` and split alerts: paging only when `tier in ("enterprise_hosted","dedicated")` and 10m sustained; ticket-level for self-serve at a higher threshold. Also added annotations for recommended mitigation toggles + links to the runbook section anchors.
Allison Grant (review): Thanks. Please ensure we are not accidentally querying on high-cardinality labels. I see `model` in a few panels—can we switch to `model_family` everywhere and add a note in the README about why?
Aisha Bello (author): Updated queries to use `model_family` + `route_family` only. Added a README note and a small helper in `overload.libsonnet` so future panels inherit the same grouping.
Logan Wright (review): Alert 3 (Retry-After missing) is great, but what's the source metric? If it depends on a new gateway metric, can we include a fallback so the rule doesn't flap in regions where the metric isn't deployed yet?
Aisha Bello (author): Good call. Added `absent()` guard + `for: 30m` and scoped it to regions where `gateway_overload_retry_after_total` is present. Also added a note that this becomes authoritative after gateway PR-18472 reaches 100%.
Christine Wong (review): Can we add a panel that overlays p99 latency and shed_rate so oncall can see if shedding is actually helping? Also please link to the incident-bot breaker announcements in the runbook section.
Aisha Bello (author): Added overlay panel (p99 latency + shed_rate) and included incident-bot channel references in README + alert annotations (`#incidents` / `#eng-oncall`).
Peter Holtz (review): One minor: recording rule name prefix should match existing `hosted_api:` convention. Also the alert group should be `hosted-api-overload` (hyphenated) per standards.

Rafael Mendes (final): Approved. Please coordinate rollout with Connor on canary gating; otherwise LGTM.
Aisha Bello (author): Coordinated with Connor; we’ll enable the dashboards immediately and keep paging alerts disabled by default behind the standard alert routing flag until canary week.
New Grafana dashboards for Hosted API overload protection (shed + breaker visibility) and initial alert rules with runbook links. Paging alerts default to disabled in routing until canary gates are met.

Adds a non-destructive 'autopsy' replay mode for incident playbooks that can step through historical executions in a sandboxed view and safely rewind simulated actions. Includes CLI + Slack blocks and DB proxy for safety.
Motivation: On-call engineers need a safe way to rehearse and investigate historical incident playbooks without risking writes or accidental reruns. Autopsy mode provides a step-through replay of a past execution, attaching the original telemetry snapshots and allowing operators to mark hypotheses, annotate steps, and 'rewind' a simulated action chain for deeper diagnostic drilling.

What this PR does: Implements a non-destructive replay controller (autopsy mode) that replays recorded playbook steps against an isolated sandbox environment. Key features: 1) CLI: incident-bot replay <incident-id> --autopsy opens a guided step-through flow with confirm prompts; 2) API: new /replay/{id}?mode=autopsy endpoint that streams step events; 3) DB proxy: a read-only proxy used during replay to prevent write effects and record attempted side-effects as simulated outcomes; 4) Slack blocks and ephemeral actions for safe operator annotations and hypothesis capture; 5) Playback timeline UI payloads for the on-call console (attachments only).

Migrations: Adds replay_snapshots table (lightweight metadata + S3 pointer) and a small schema migration (20251021_replay_snapshots.sql). Migration includes backfill of latest 7 days for systems with telemetry archives; backfill optional via bin/incident-bot backfill-replay-snapshots.

Backward compatibility: Default behaviour unchanged for normal playbook runs. Autopsy mode is opt-in and gated behind the incident-bot.replay.autopsy feature flag and the incident:replay permission. Existing playbook recordings are compatible; this PR preserves the original payload format and adds a replay_metadata envelope.

Testing and QA: Unit tests for controller logic and DB proxy, integration tests exercising CLI replay and Slack flows in the e2e harness, and a manual checklist used during rollout (see docs/replay/autopsy-checklist.md). CI showed a flaky e2e that required a rerun (flaky: tests/e2e/slack_block_interaction_test).

Usage notes: To run locally: 1) ENABLE_FEATURE=incident-bot.replay.autopsy make dev-run 2) ./bin/incident-bot replay --autopsy <incident-id> 3) Use --sandbox-store to point to a test S3 prefix. See docs for recommended retention and privacy considerations.

Security and safety: The DB proxy enforces a denylist of write methods (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE are simulated and recorded rather than executed). KMS-scoped keys ensure snapshot blobs are encrypted. The UI surfaces a prominent warning banner when the mode is active.
4 commits:
- feat(replay): add autopsy controller and stepper (server/replay_controller.py)
- feat(cli): add replay CLI, confirmation flow and --autopsy flag (cli/replay.py)
- feat(sandbox): read-only DB proxy and simulated side-effect recorder (sandbox/db_proxy.py)
- docs: autopsy mode guide and rollout checklist (docs/replay/autopsy-guide.md)
- test: integration + e2e harness updates and fixtures (tests/integration/replay_*)
Aisha Romero: 'Great idea — can we make sure any side-effect attempts are never sent to external systems? Request we add explicit tests that simulate webhooks and outgoing api calls.'

Priya Shah: 'Acknowledged. The DB proxy now records side-effect attempts and we've added a network egress guard that replaces external HTTP calls with recorded responses when in autopsy mode. Added tests for webhook simulation (tests/integration/test_autopsy_webhook_simulation.py).'

Luca Moretti: 'Minor: please surface the feature-flag check earlier and add a log entry when someone starts autopsy replay (for audit).'

Priya Shah: 'Added audit log entry and feature flag gating; moved telemetry emit to start of controller flow.'

Samir Patel: 'e2e flaky on CI — reran and passed. Approving after CI green.'

Approvals: Aisha Romero approved, Luca Moretti approved, Samir Patel approved.
payload.title: Introduce Playbook Autopsy Mode with Sandboxed Rewind

Context: As part of the status page transparency upgrades, on-call needs a fast, consistent path from a page to (a) the correct status-page component taxonomy and (b) the exact runbook steps for posting/updating component statuses. This PR updates alert annotations across component-level SLO burn alerts in this repo to include: (1) a status page update runbook link, and (2) a status page component taxonomy link. It also standardizes annotation keys so incident-bot and human responders can reliably surface the right links in Slack. Scope: alert rule annotations + lint/test updates only; no threshold or routing changes. Notes: we intentionally keep the links to high-level canonical docs rather than incident-specific pages, and we avoid language that implies an SLA/guarantee. Rollout: safe to merge; annotations-only; validated in staging alertmanager and via jsonnet render output. Follow-ups: once merged, we can have incident-bot surface these fields automatically in the intake + reminders (tracked elsewhere).

Adds an orchestrated, policy-driven log sampler and conditional trace collector to reduce noise and collect targeted diagnostic bundles during incidents. Includes responder CLI, privacy redaction hooks, and opt-in ephemeral debug jobs. Backwards-compatible; feature gated and off by default.
Motivation: During high-volume incidents we either collect too much telemetry (cost, noise) or miss the narrow correlated traces that reveal causal chains. This PR introduces an orchestrated log sampler and a conditional trace collector that lets responders capture small, high-fidelity diagnostic bundles without blasting the system with full sampling.

What this PR does: implements a policy engine that drives adaptive sampling decisions, correlation-aware trace lookups, and a safe, pre-authorized ephemeral debug job runner. Key capabilities: adaptive prefix-and-field sampling, correlation-context propagation (trace/log span keys), conditional trace fetching (only collect spans when correlation score exceeds threshold), responder-initiated snapshot CLI (with RBAC checks), automatic PII redaction hooks configurable per-team, retention and upload policy controls, and a canary rollout for customer tenants.

Checklist: [x] policy engine implementation (pkg/sampler), [x] trace collector (pkg/tracer), [x] responder CLI + auth checks (cmd/oncall-sampler), [x] unit + integration tests (test/unit/*, test/integration/*), [x] docs and runbook update (docs/runbooks/orchestrated-sampling.md), [x] privacy redactors plumbed and tested.

Usage notes: Feature is behind the feature-flag "orchestrated_sample_v1" and off in default config. Operators can enable sampling policies via the console or Helm values (deploy/helm/values.yaml). Responders can call: redwood-incident-sampler collect --incident-id INC12345 --policy fast-path --dry-run to preview.

Security & privacy: Collection requires an on-call role scope; the CLI checks the session token against the RBAC service. PII redactors are applied by default with a team-configurable allowlist; we run an additional scrub pass before any upload/export. Audit events are emitted for every collection.

Rollout plan: Canary on internal SRE org (2 weeks), + gradual tenant ramp. Rollback is a flip of the feature flag and Helm value.

Related: linear/ENG-1284 implements the policy DSL; ENG-1299 is the follow-up for sampling telemetry dashboards. SUP-4321 is the support ticket that motivated the responder CLI.

Notes: This description is intentionally a single continuous string to match PR storage format.
Ethan Cooper: Please add an explicit privacy review sign-off in the PR before merging; also add a small e2e that validates scrubbed vs unscreened payloads.
Maya Thompson: Added privacy sign-off and an additional scrub unit test (see commit a5f7b2c). The CLI will log an audit event for every collection attempt.
Rhea Patel: Found a race in sampler cache under high concurrency (repro in CI). Suggested using RWMutex around cache map.
Maya Thompson: Fixed race, added test that simulates concurrent sample decisions (commit 99bde33). Re-ran unit tests locally and CI.
Liam O'Connor: I'd still like a short note in the runbook about cost controls and expected SLO impact when enabling wide policies.
Maya Thompson: Added cost note and staged rollout guidance to docs/runbooks/orchestrated-sampling.md

Context: Route-level experiments rely on control-plane config propagation into the routing/policy layer. During beta we observed occasional propagation lag and a few classes of attribution anomalies (missing experiment_id/variant_id tags, variant receiving ~0 traffic due to config/eligibility issues, and split skew early in rollout). This PR adds Prometheus/Alertmanager rules and annotations for the standard route experiments dashboards, with SRE-reviewed runbook links and recommended severities. Scope: (1) propagation lag/staleness alerts tied to the new propagation lag metric emitted by the redwood monorepo, (2) attribution drop-rate and missing-dimension alerts for experiment metrics/traces aggregation, (3) “variant 0 traffic” detection to catch misconfigured allocations or eligibility rules. Notes: rules are written to avoid cardinality blow-ups (no per-route fanout by default); high-cardinality drilldowns remain in Grafana dashboards. Related: redwood PR-28631 (adds config propagation lag metric), redwood PR-28734 (runbook URLs in alert payloads), observability-pack PR-1934 (dashboards). Threads: slack/eng-sre/1736455521-alert-thresholds-experiment-propagation-lag.json and slack/eng-sre/1738362044-attribution-drop-rate-alert-noise.json informed thresholds/windows. Rollout: enable in staging immediately; prod enabled behind the existing observability-pack release gate (see release notes section).
Sean Gallagher (review): Thresholds look reasonable, but please ensure paging severity only fires when we have evidence of user-impact. For propagation lag: can we differentiate config push stalled vs read-side staleness? Also please include runbook links as full URLs (not relative) and confirm the runbook has a clear “disable experiments feature flag / soft-stop” mitigation. Allison Grant (author): Updated severities: propagation lag is page only for >10m sustained + >X% of regions impacted; otherwise ticket. Added separate warning for read-side staleness vs publish-side lag based on the two metrics exposed in redwood PR-28631. Runbook link updated to full Confluence URL and added a ‘Mitigation: set experiments evaluator to safe-default + disable auto-stop kill switch’ section reference. Rafael Mendes (review): Attribution drop-rate alert window was too short; in previous incident it flapped on deploys. Suggest 15m window and a higher threshold for warning, plus a distinct alert for “attribution missing on streaming retries” if we can approximate it. Also please add an annotation pointing to the assignment debugging endpoint docs. Allison Grant (author): Adjusted to 15m window; warning at 2.5% sustained, critical at 7% sustained (per staging baselines). Added annotation to internal debug endpoint docs and the assignment debugging runbook. We can’t reliably isolate streaming retries here without new labels; added TODO + linked ENG-9026 follow-up. Logan Wright (review): Please confirm recording rule names align with metrics taxonomy notes and do not include route_id by default. Allison Grant (author): Confirmed: recording rules aggregate by {experiment_id, variant_id, region} and optionally by route_id only in dashboard queries. Also added comment blocks warning against expanding label sets in alerts. Final: Sean + Rafael approved after a quick live review of runbook steps and alert routing.
Added alert groups: RouteExperimentsControlPlane and RouteExperimentsAttribution. New alerts: (1) RouteExperimentsConfigPropagationLagHigh (warning) and RouteExperimentsConfigPropagationLagCritical (page) based on propagation_lag_seconds p95 and percentiles across regions; (2) RouteExperimentsConfigStalenessHigh (warning) when evaluator uses stale config versions beyond SLO; (3) RouteExperimentsAttributionDropRateHigh (warning/critical) when attribution_drop_rate > thresholds; (4) RouteExperimentsVariantZeroTraffic (warning) when a variant receives <0.5% traffic for >20m while allocation is >=5%; (5) RouteExperimentsSplitSkewSuspected (ticket) when observed vs expected allocation diverges beyond a tolerance band for >30m (best-effort heuristic). All alerts include annotations: runbook_url, owner, and console_experiment_link template.
Observability: Added standard Alertmanager rules for route experiments propagation lag and attribution anomalies, with tuned thresholds and runbook links (beta readiness).

Title: Add provision-to-ready dashboards and alert rules

Summary
This PR adds the first cut of Grafana dashboards + Prometheus alert rules for the Provision-to-Ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management). The goal is to make time-to-ready (TTR) and failure modes visible by region/GPU type/step, and to establish initial paging/ticketing thresholds that we can tune during staged rollout.

What’s included
- Dashboards (Grafana)
  - Provision-to-Ready / Overview: P50/P95 time-to-ready, success rate, in-flight counts by readiness state, and top failure reasons
  - Step breakdown: per-step durations (P50/P95), retries, and "stuck" detection views for Provisioning vs Validating
  - Failure heatmap: failure rate by region x gpu_type, and failures by step (GPU health, driver parity, kubelet join, NCCL smoke, perf canary)
  - Quarantine & flakes: quarantine counts over time, validation flake rate, and "recovered after retry" vs "quarantined" split
- Alerts + recording rules (Prometheus)
  - SLI-oriented alerting for time-to-ready and success rate (windowed)
  - Early rollout guardrails to avoid paging for known flakes; pages only on sustained SLO breaches
  - Recording rules to standardize TTR percentiles and keep dashboard queries cheap
- Runbook link stubs
  - Each alert includes an annotation with the runbook doc location and a "next steps" snippet (what to check first: step breakdown panel, failure reason panel, quarantine panel)

Metric assumptions / dependencies
- Assumes control-plane is emitting the canonical metrics (names match the latest proposal in ENG-4821). This PR does not add application metrics; it consumes them.
- Expected series dimensions:
  - region (low cardinality)
  - gpu_type (A100/H100/L40S/etc.)
  - pool_type (dedicated/shared)
  - step (bounded set)
  - result (success/failure)
- Explicitly NOT using node_id/instance_id labels in any alerting expression or dashboard variables. (We learned this the hard way in prior fleet dashboards; node-level drill-down should be via logs/traces, not Prom labels.)

Dashboards (panels / key queries)
- Time-to-ready (TTR)
  - Uses histogram_quantile over fleet_provision_time_to_ready_seconds_bucket, grouped by (region, gpu_type, pool_type)
  - Panels show P50/P95 and a stacked breakdown of step duration share (based on fleet_provision_step_duration_seconds_bucket)
- Success rate
  - 1 - (sum(rate(fleet_provision_result_total{result="failure"}[30m])) / sum(rate(fleet_provision_result_total[30m])))
  - Secondary panel: failure reasons via fleet_provision_failure_total{reason=...} topk(10)
- Quarantine
  - fleet_readiness_state_total{state="Quarantined"} and rate of transitions into Quarantined (if transition metric present)

Alerts (initial thresholds)
NOTE: These are intentionally conservative. We expect to tune after the us-east A100-only staged rollout, once we have a week of data.
- Page: ProvisionToReadyTTRElevatedP95
  - Condition: P95 time-to-ready > 75m for 2h (per region+gpu_type, limited to dedicated pools)
  - Rationale: Catch systemic provisioning regressions (image bake issues, cluster join failures) without paging on small sample spikes.
- Ticket: ProvisionToReadyTTRElevatedP50
  - Condition: P50 time-to-ready > 35m for 6h
  - Rationale: Tracks gradual drift / capacity pressure; not an immediate incident.
- Page: ProvisionToReadySuccessRateLow
  - Condition: success rate < 97% over 1h AND total attempts > 30
  - Rationale: Prevents paging on low volume; aligns with early error budget policy.
- Ticket: ProvisionToReadyValidationFlakeRateHigh
  - Condition: retries per attempt > 1.5 over 6h OR NCCL smoke test failures exceed threshold
  - Rationale: Flake signal for follow-ups (timeouts/backoff, perf canary thresholds).
- Page: ProvisionToReadyQuarantineSpike
  - Condition: quarantined nodes added > 5 in 30m in a single region+gpu_type
  - Rationale: Potential fabric/driver/image issue; can translate directly to capacity shortfall.

Runbook annotations
All alerts include:
- dashboard: link placeholder (Grafana UID + path)
- runbook: runbook-links.md anchor (to be replaced with Confluence URL by Infra/SRE)
- owner: "infra-fleet" for provisioning issues; "sre" for alert delivery; "platform" when readiness service appears unhealthy

Screenshots
- (omitted) Grafana panels render in CI via dashboard lint; screenshots will be added once we have stable UIDs in the shared Grafana folder.

Testing / validation
- promtool check rules: pass
- grafana-dashboard-validator: pass
- jsonnet formatting: pass

Rollout plan
- Merge to main, then import dashboards to the shared Grafana folder (SRE-owned) during the us-east A100 staged rollout.
- Alerts will be deployed disabled-by-default (severity=none) for 48 hours; SRE will enable paging after confirming noise levels.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Confirm final SLO numbers after baseline metrics review (ENG-4821); these thresholds are based on initial baseline distributions and may shift.
- Confirm which metric is authoritative for "attempt" count (orchestrator vs readiness service).
- Replace runbook placeholders with the final Confluence runbook + dashboard URLs once those are finalized.

Links
- Linear: ENG-4827 (dashboards), ENG-4821 (SLOs/metrics)
- Related implementation PRs (metrics emission): redwood/pr-18441 (step breakdown metrics), redwood/pr-18475 (cardinality follow-up)

Commits
1) feat(dashboards): add provision-to-ready overview + step breakdown dashboards
2) feat(alerts): add initial ttr/success/quarantine alerts + recording rules
3) chore(ci): add grafana dashboard validation and promtool checks
4) docs: add runbook link stubs and dashboard import notes

Reviewer conversation (highlights)
- Allison Grant: Please ensure no per-node label usage, and keep dashboard variables bounded; can we add a hard note in the README about cardinality? Also, prefer recording rules for the percentile queries.
  - Sergio Costa: Updated dashboards to remove the node_id template var; added recording rules for ttr_p50/ttr_p95 by region/gpu_type/pool_type and added README note.
- Aisha Bello: The paging thresholds look aggressive for week 1; can we gate paging on attempt volume and require sustained breach? Also, please split ticket vs page for P50 vs P95.
  - Sergio Costa: Added attempt-volume guard (>30 attempts), changed P95 to 2h sustained, and added a separate P50 ticket with 6h window.
- Miles Thornton: Make sure the success rate calculation doesn’t double-count retries as failures; do we have a metric that represents final attempt outcome only?
  - Sergio Costa: Using fleet_provision_result_total emitted on terminal state only (success/failure). Added a comment in recording-rules.yaml to document this assumption.
- Vanessa Ortiz: Can we get a panel for "Validating stuck" specifically and a quarantine trend line? That’s what on-call needs when expansions stall.
  - Sergio Costa: Added "Validating age" panel (based on state gauge + time in state, where available) and quarantine trend line on Quarantine & flakes dashboard.

CI timeline
- 2025-10-11: promtool failed (unknown field `forEach` in rule group) -> fixed YAML schema, reran
- 2025-10-12: grafana validator failed (panel datasource UID unset) -> set datasource to ${DS_PROMETHEUS} and added CI default
- 2025-10-16: all checks green

Merge
Merged via squash on 2025-10-16.

Release notes
- Internal: Added initial Grafana dashboards + alert rules for Provision-to-Ready automation (time-to-ready, success rate, quarantine spike). Alerts ship disabled-by-default pending tuning during staged rollout.
payload.title: Add provision-to-ready dashboards and alert rules

Context: During the 2025-11-07 us-east streaming degradation we struggled to quickly answer “is this a streaming-only issue or broader Hosted API impact?” and we ended up hesitating on which public status components to mark impacted. This PR adds a small set of focused, region-aware panels for Streaming in us-east that on-call can use to validate streaming-specific degradations before posting status page updates. What’s included: (1) a new “Streaming (us-east)” section in the Hosted API component dashboard with panels for streaming disconnect rate, stream error rate (gateway 5xx + upstream), first-token latency p95/p99, and active stream concurrency; (2) a side-by-side comparison row (Streaming vs Non-streaming chat completions) to help confirm capability-scoped impact; (3) dashboard annotations that link to the status page update runbook and specify the “post-update confidence check” items (verify error + disconnect + first-token latency). Notes: Panels intentionally avoid customer identifiers and aggregate at component_id/region/capability. Thresholds are NOT alerting thresholds in this PR; they’re visualization defaults only (alert tuning happens in ENG-4841 / slo-toolkit). Testing/validation: Replayed a slice of the 2025-11-07 incident window against staging metrics and verified the panels light up as expected; also sanity-checked that non-streaming endpoints remain flat in the comparison row. Follow-ups: replicate panels for eu-west and ap-southeast once the region-aware streaming counters land in the redwood repo; we can also add a “status component tag” filter once pr-19211 label standardization is fully rolled out.
Allison Grant (review): Can we make sure these queries are capability-scoped and don’t accidentally include websocket auth failures that are not customer-impacting? Also would be helpful to add an explicit “comparison” panel so on-call can quickly confirm it’s streaming-only. Aisha Bello (author): Updated streaming_error_rate to use gateway route tags for streaming-only endpoints and excluded authn/authz error classes. Added a comparison row: streaming first-token p95 vs non-streaming chat p95 in the same time window and a paired 5xx rate panel. Christine Wong (review): Please add a link/annotation to the status page runbook from the dashboard. The goal is that Comms Lead can use this dashboard as part of the verification step. Aisha Bello (author): Added dashboard annotations and a short panel description block with “confidence check” steps + runbook link. Caleb Johnson (review): These queries are a bit heavy; do we need the p99 and p95 both? And can we pin the timegrain? Aisha Bello (author): Dropped one redundant panel (kept p95 + p99 only for first-token latency), pinned to 1m rollups, and added $__interval overrides to reduce query fanout. Allison Grant (final): Looks good. Please ensure the titles use the same casing as the public component labels (Streaming, us-east). Approved.
payload.title: Add us-east Streaming health panels (disconnects, first-token latency, 5xx) for status validation

Context: Support + CS escalations (notably around audit log delivery latency) highlighted that we lacked a first-class, Support/CS-friendly view of end-to-end audit log pipeline lag and an alert that aligns to enterprise expectations. This PR adds a dedicated dashboard and alerting rules for audit log lag, and ensures panels/alerts link to a canonical runbook. It is intended to reduce time-to-triage during tickets like SUP-1846 and to support the known-issues sprint playbook work by providing an authoritative signal.

What’s included: (1) New Grafana dashboard: "Audit Logs — Delivery Lag" with panels for ingestion → transform → delivery stages, p50/p95/p99 lag, backlog depth (where available), per-region breakdown, and a quick "is this customer-impacting" section (current lag vs expected SLO). (2) New Prometheus alerts: audit-log-lag warning + critical, scoped to production namespaces and grouped by region, with annotations that link directly to the runbook and dashboard. (3) Runbook updates: new section for audit log lag triage, plus explicit "Support-facing guidance" (what we can safely confirm, what data we should avoid sharing, and what mitigation knobs exist). (4) Routing/ownership: alerts are routed to SRE on-call; annotations include escalation guidance for Platform ownership boundaries.

Alert thresholds (aligned to enterprise expectations): - Warning: p95 delivery lag > 10m for 10m (per region) - Critical: p95 delivery lag > 30m for 10m (per region) Notes: These thresholds intentionally do not page on transient spikes; they aim to catch sustained backlog that will breach enterprise expectations. Runbook describes how to validate whether this is isolated to a subset of tenants vs global/regional.

Key design choices: - Use p95 as the primary paging signal to avoid single-tenant tail behavior dominating. Summary: Introduce an 'Invocation Thermograph' metric and dashboard along with a light-weight log-cohort correlation layer and KV-trace anchoring sampler to improve detection and triage of long-tail latency/cost regressions.
Motivation: Existing alert signals surface percentile spikes but miss gradual slope-driven regressions and correlated log patterns that indicate workload shifts (e.g., prompt length or repeated reruns). The thermograph visualizes invocation density across token-cost vs latency slices over time, enabling SREs/product teams to see heating/cooling patterns and isolate cohorts.
Design:
- New metric pipeline that emits invocation_thermograph_bucket{tenant,model,segment} representing counts in 2D microbins (token-cost, latency) aggregated per minute; bins are compact (64 bins) and encoded as base64 for transport.
- KV-trace anchoring sampler: sampled traces attach compact KV-hitmap for first-10-kv-keys to help link cache miss patterns to thermograph hot bins.
- Log-cohort correlation: a lightweight offline join that correlates thermograph hot bins with log cohort signatures (e.g., prompt templates, feature flags) to produce 'cohort tags' for follow-up traces.
- Dashboard: new 'Invocation Thermograph' tile, cohort scatter, and a slope-alert tuning panel.
- Alerting: new SLO rule 'thermograph-slope' that triggers when a bin's occupancy increases with a sustained positive slope over N windows; alerts are debounced by cohort density and paired with a recommended follow-up query.
Rollout: feature-flag rollout over 3 weeks: 10% tenants -> 50% -> all.
Defaults: sampling weight 0.02, thermograph retention 30d for hot bins rollups.
Commits: ["init: thermograph metric encoder and ingest contract","feat: kv-anchor sampler + small proto for kv-hitmap","ui: invocation-thermograph dashboard and cohort scatter panel","tests: thermograph unit + e2e ingestion smoke","docs: observability/thermograph.md and runbook","perf: batch encoding optimization to reduce CPU impact"]
Changed areas/files: ["observability/metrics/thermograph_encoder.go","tracing/kv_anchor_sampler.py","console/dashboards/invocation-thermograph.json","console/panels/cohort-scatter.json","docs/observability/thermograph.md","pkg/ingest/encoder/encoder_test.go","sdk/python/redwood/observability.py","scripts/rollout/flag_toggle.sh","tests/e2e/test_thermograph_ingest.py","ci/workflows/thermograph-smoke.yml","infra/monitoring/alerts/thermograph-slope.yaml","benchmarks/thermograph/encode_bench.go"]

Observed perf: microbench reduces allocation churn by ~40% and keeps CPU p99 within 1% of baseline in our sandbox.

Motivation: We need a lightweight way to validate prefetch and KV warmup strategies against real traffic shapes without provisioning large-scale dedicated runs. This change adds a sampled prefetch simulation runner (prefetch-sim) that replays a bounded sample of real invocations through a lightweight simulator to measure warmup effectiveness, token-level latency delta, and downstream cost impact. In addition, we introduce a "cost thermostat" component that consumes the sim output to propose safe gating thresholds for aggressive prefetching and quantization profiles, and emits threshold-change proposals as telemetry rather than performing any automatic action.

What this PR does: 1) Adds prefetched-sample collection hooks (server-side sampling at the request router) which annotate invocations with warmup candidates and minimal KV access traces. 2) Implements a simulation runner service (telemetry/prefetch_sim) that consumes historic samples, replays the token access pattern against cached/stubbed KV state, and produces metrics: prefetch_hit_rate, prefetch_latency_delta_ms, simulated_token_cost_delta_usd. 3) Introduces the cost-thermostat service that aggregates sim runs across tenants, computes a cost/latency frontier, and publishes recommended prefetch intensity per tenant as telemetry (no auto-enforcement). 4) Dashboard + alerting: a new Grafana panel (observability/dashboards/prefetch_thermostat.json) surfaces per-tenant frontier curves, 95/99 latency deltas, and expected cost delta; an alert rule suggests review when recommended intensity changes by >20% week-over-week.

Why this is different: Existing tooling measures token cost and rollups after-the-fact. The sim-runner produces an actionable, forward-looking signal that lets us explore tradeoffs offline and tune alerts and rollout policies with better fidelity. The cost thermostat is intentionally advisory to keep operational control with SRE/product teams.

Testing & results: Unit tests for sampler and runner (mocks for KV behavior) were added; integration smoke runs against a 2k-sample corpus show median prefetch_hit_rate 68% and median latency reduction 12ms at an estimated 3.8% token cost increase for one high-throughput tenant. On a separate tenant with cold-prefix-heavy traffic, thermostat recommended intensity 0.35 (from 0.7), avoiding a projected 14% cost increase with only 3ms latency gain.

Rollout plan: feature is behind feature-flag (telemetry.prefetch_sim.enabled). Initial rollout to Canary orgs for 2 weeks, then to low-volume production tenants for an additional 3 weeks. Alerts are advisory initially (no PagerDuty) until SRE signs off.

Related: ENG-1429 (prefetch instrumentation), ENG-1590 (alert tuning experiment).
Ethan Chen: Can you add a comment clarifying that thermostat recommendations are advisory and not applied automatically? Also please include unit tests for aggregator edge cases.
Maya Patel: clarified in description and added aggregator edge-case tests (empty cohorts / single-tenant).
Rahul Kapoor: nit: prefer context-aware timeouts in runner.go to avoid long locks during replay; left an inline suggestion.
Maya Patel: addressed timeout suggestion and added adjustable replay batch size via config; pushed follow-up commit.
Sofia Li: ran the canary smoke run; results look reasonable. Approve once CI is green and docs link updated.
CI: integration flaky on first run (saw transient network error); reran and all checks passed.
Added sampled prefetch simulation runner and advisory cost thermostat telemetry. New dashboard and alert rule for evaluating prefetch intensity. Feature gated behind telemetry.prefetch_sim.enabled; no automatic enforcement.

payload.body:
Motivation: recurring token-level alert noise and slow postmortems for long-tail latency/cost incidents. Investigations frequently required stitching sparse traces with infra events and model-fallbacks. This PR adds two composable observability primitives to reduce toil: 1) a synthetic invocation replay harness that can generate structured, replayable invocation traces (including span-level timing, kv-cache hit/miss markers, and model-variant events) so teams can reproduce and profile long-tail shapes without hitting prod customers; and 2) a causal incident dashboard that surfaces cross-source correlations (token-phase waterfall, kv-cache heatmap, model-variant swaps, recent routing/fallback events, and nearest infra events) and an alert prioritizer that ranks noisy alerts by expected customer impact (cost-weighted SLO breach probability).

Implementation summary: server-side: services/observability/synth_replay.go implements a seeded, deterministic replay generator that emits spans with attribute synthetic=true and seed metadata. Ingest pipeline: added enrichment module observability/ingest/enrichment/synthetic_enricher.go to tag and annotate synthetic traces and compute causal_link_score using a lightweight Bayesian co-occur scorer. Metric exports: new counters/gauges exported via Prometheus-compatible /metrics with names invocation_synthetic_replays_total, invocation_causal_link_score_gauge, kv_cache_synth_hit_ratio. Dashboard: grafana/dashboards/causal-incident-dashboard.json contains panels: synthetic-replay-timeline, token-phase-waterfall, kv-cache-heatmap, model-variant-event-stream, alert-prioritizer. Alerts: monitoring/alerts/alert-prioritizer.yaml adds a suppression and priority-weighting step which reduces noise for low-impact long-tail token spikes by 70% in our staging runs.

Privacy and safety: synthetic replays are deterministic and derived from anonymized prompt-shapes; we enforce PII-filtering in docs/runbooks/synthetic-replay-playbook.md and added a unit that rejects replays with >5% token overlap against a protected-strings set.

Testing: unit tests for generator logic and enrichment (tests/unit/synth_*), an integration test that runs a deterministic replay through the ingestion pipeline (tests/integration/synthetic_replay_test.go), and a Grafana dashboard snapshot test. Initial CI: integration test was flaky due to an RNG seed race; fixed by deterministic seeding and timing fences.

Backwards compatibility and rollout: feature gated behind observability.feature.synthetic_replay (off by default). Dashboard added to the default observability folder but hidden until the feature flag is enabled in prod accounts.

Related: ENG-4927 (investigation automation), SRE-210 (alert noise reduction).
Liam O'Connor: Requested more detail on how causal_link_score is calculated and CPU/latency cost of scoring at ingest. Asked for an opt-out for low-tier tenants.
Marcel Chen: Replied with math summary (Bayesian co-occurrence with time-decay window) and added batched scorer path to avoid per-span p99 impact; added tenant opt-out flag and documented config.
Evelyn Park: Raised privacy concerns — asked about PII leakage in synthetic generator and for a guardrail. Marcel: added protected-strings filter, unit tests and a short runbook for reviewers to validate before enabling in production.
Diego Morales: Suggested a UI affordance to show synthetic vs real traces in the dashboard; implemented a clear synthetic badge and legend in the Grafana panels.
Evelyn Park: Approved after one follow-up about alert thresholds and a small lint fix. Liam: Approved after verifying ingest perf numbers in staging.
- Add synthetic invocation replay harness for deterministic, anonymized invocation generation.
- Add causal incident dashboard correlating token-phase waterfall, kv-cache heatmap, model-variant events, and infra signals.
- Introduce alert-prioritizer to reduce noise by ranking alerts by cost-weighted SLO breach probability.
- Feature gated off by default; see runbook for enablement steps.
Staging rollout metrics: alert volume down ~68% on noisy token spikes; median triage time on sampled incidents improved by ~40%. Follow-ups: add an async exporter for replay artifacts (ENG-4992) and a lightweight sampling API for downstream access (ENG-4993).

payload.body:
Title: Add alert rules + routing for Dedicated max-bound saturation and sustained queue buildup

Context
Dedicated autoscaling bounds are rolling out to pilot customers. During pilot we’ve seen two recurring failure/impact modes that are easy to miss without dedicated alerting:
1) Deployment hits max bound for an extended period while demand continues increasing (customers see queueing / p95 latency regressions; support tickets like SUP-28411).
2) Sustained queue buildup (even if not max-bound) indicating a scaling issue, forecast signal outage, or model-level throughput regression.

This PR adds:
- Prometheus alert rules for max-bound saturation and sustained queue buildup.
- Alertmanager routing to Dedicated on-call (page) vs #eng-infra (ticket/notify) depending on severity and duration.
- Rule annotations/runbook links aligned with the Dedicated autoscaler troubleshooting runbook.

What’s included
- New alerts (names follow metric naming standards and keep labels low-cardinality):
  - DedicatedMaxBoundSustained (page): bounded at max AND queue depth elevated for >= 10m.
  - DedicatedMaxBoundHitRateHigh (notify): high ratio of bounded_desired == max over a rolling window, even if queue is not yet elevated.
  - DedicatedQueueDepthSustained (page): queue depth above threshold for >= 15m (guarded by traffic floor to avoid noise).
  - DedicatedMinBoundUnmet (notify): min bound cannot be met (region capacity shortage / provisioning failure), intended as early warning to SRE + capacity planning.
- Routing:
  - Severity=page routes to PagerDuty service "dedicated-oncall" with grouping by (deployment_id, region).
  - Severity=notify routes to Slack #eng-infra and creates a ticket via existing webhook (no new integration).
- Documentation pointers:
  - Annotations include dashboard links (from pr-1934) and runbook section anchors.

Thresholds (initial)
- Queue depth signal uses dedicated_autoscaler_queue_depth (already emitted by fleet telemetry) with a traffic floor via req_rate to avoid paging on low-volume deployments.
- Max-bound saturation uses dedicated_autoscaler_bounded_desired_replicas == dedicated_autoscaler_max_replicas AND queue depth above a small baseline (to avoid false positives when customers intentionally cap above demand).
- All thresholds were chosen to match pilot expectations and can be tuned post-canary; see inline comments in rules.

Files / areas changed
- alerts/dedicated/autoscaling_bounds_alerts.yaml: new rule group(s) for bounds + queueing.
- alertmanager/routes/dedicated.yaml: new routes + grouping rules.
- alertmanager/receivers/pagerduty.yaml: ensure dedicated-oncall receiver exists and has correct service key reference.
- dashboards/links.yaml: adds canonical URLs used by alert annotations.
- tests/promtool_rules_test.yaml: rule unit tests covering basic firing/non-firing cases.

Rollout plan
- Landing behind existing Dedicated bounds rollout (feature is opt-in per account), but alerting is safe to enable globally since it only evaluates when metrics exist.
- We will initially enable paging routes only for pilot accounts (via matcher on customer_tier=pilot) for 1 week, then broaden to all Dedicated once noise is acceptable.

Checklist
- [x] promtool check passes
- [x] alert rule tests added
- [x] annotations include runbook + dashboard
- [x] routing reviewed by SRE

Notes / follow-ups
- We should consider adding a separate alert for "predictive signal stale" once the predictor staleness metric is stable (tracked in ENG-22142).
- The min-bound unmet alert is notify-only by design; paging policy should be revisited after we collect baseline rate.

Screenshots
N/A (rule changes only).
Allison Grant (review): Can we avoid grouping by customer_id in paging routes? It will explode groups on large enterprise accounts. Suggest grouping by deployment_id + region only, and keep customer_id as an annotation.
Sergio Costa (author): Good call. Updated group_by to (deployment_id, region). Kept customer_id in annotations/labels for search but not grouping.
Rafael Mendes (review): For DedicatedMaxBoundSustained, please ensure we only page when queue depth is elevated too; max-bound alone can be normal if they cap high above demand. Also include runbook link to the "Max bound saturation" section.
Sergio Costa (author): Updated expression to require queue_depth > baseline AND req_rate > floor. Added runbook anchor and dashboard link in annotations.
Aisha Bello (review): Queue depth sustained: do we have a consistent unit/scale across models? If not, consider a relative threshold or use queue wait time if available.
Sergio Costa (author): Queue wait time isn’t consistently emitted yet. For now I added a traffic floor and a longer for=15m to reduce noise. Added TODO comment to revisit once queue_wait_seconds is rolled out.
Miles Thornton (review): promtool test coverage looks good. One nit: please use severity=notify (not warning) to match our routing conventions. Also ensure labels are restricted to {deployment_id, region, environment}.
Sergio Costa (author): Renamed severities to page/notify and removed a stray model_name label matcher. promtool + unit tests updated accordingly.
Allison Grant (approval): LGTM after the grouping fix + severity convention update. Let’s monitor noise during pilot week.

Context and motivation: onboarding at scale requires prioritizing model intake and release notes based on real usage signals. This PR adds a telemetry-weighted ingest catalog that merges intake manifests with sampled telemetry to surface high-impact variants during onboarding, plus an autosummary generator that drafts concise release micro-digests for the model registry UI and release pipeline. The feature aims to reduce curation time and improve changelog relevance by ranking changes using measured signal (latency, error-rate, token-cost delta, and usage share). What this changes: 1) catalog indexer that annotates model intake with sampled telemetry fingerprints and impact score; 2) autosummary module that synthesizes short release snippets and suggested human review bullets; 3) lightweight provenance ledger entries for each intake that record sampler seed and telemetry snapshot; 4) small docs and onboarding checklist to guide SME reviewers. Summary: Introduces two coordinated observability features: (1) an 'invocation fidelity fence' — a lightweight rule-based sampler that gates high-fidelity logs and full-span captures based on a composite score (token-cost, phase-latency anomaly, and recent error density) to reduce storage and processing costs while preserving interesting signals; and (2) a new Grafana dashboard 'Cost Tilt Visualizer' that shows per-route/model tilt (skew) in token-cost vs latency and highlights candidates for batching or model-quantization tuning. Motivation: We have increasing log volume and downstream index costs from capturing full traces for many low-value invocations. Existing sampling is mostly random or cost-only which misses subtle high-latency, low-cost tails and high-cost silent failures. The fidelity fence aims to be cheap to evaluate at the edge, adaptive to recent anomaly signals, and transparent to SREs via metrics. The dashboard fills an ops gap — product teams need to quickly identify routes where cost is concentrated in narrow user cohorts or specific prompt shapes (tilt), so they can prioritize batching, cache rules, or model variant routing. Design: - Fidelity fence: a short-circuit policy evaluated at request admission with inputs: token_estimate, route_id, model_variant, rolling 5m anomaly_score (from runtime detector), recent error_rate_1h, and tenant_tier. The policy computes a composite score S = w1*normalized_token + w2*anomaly_score + w3*error_rate and compares to a tiered threshold (config per base_branch/release channel). When S >= threshold, invocation is marked for full fidelity: full-span, full request/response body capture (scrubbed), and enriched log context. Otherwise, invocation gets compact telemetry (metric-only + sampled span id). The implementation is conservative by default (low w1, higher weight on anomaly_score) and is opt-out via a per-tenant flag. - Cost Tilt Visualizer: a Grafana dashboard with three coordinated views: (A) tilt scatter: per-route/model points where x=median latency, y=median per-invocation token-cost, point size=invocations, color=slope of cost vs latency; (B) cohort drilldown heatmap: prompt-shape buckets x sequence-length, y token-cost quantile; (C) timeline sparklines per-route of tilt-score and fidelity-sampled fraction. Also includes a small synthetic replay panel to run query-band replays on a sample. Implementation details: - Edge policy: implemented in observability-sidecar (edge capture hook). Added a small policy engine module (fidelity_fence.py) with a deterministic scoring function, unit tests, and feature flags. - Telemetry: new metrics emitted: fidelity_fence_eval_total, fidelity_fence_allowed_total, fidelity_fence_blocked_total, fidelity_fence_score_histogram (labels: route, model, tenant_tier). - Traces: When a request is marked full-fidelity we attach tag fidelity=high and add enrichment_key referencing the anomaly window. - Dashboard: added JSON dashboard file under dashboards/cost-tilt-visualizer.json with templating vars for env and model families. - Config: new default policy config in observability-pack/configs/fidelity-defaults.yaml; tenant-level override via tenant-config service supported. Testing and rollout: - Unit tests added for policy thresholds and score normalization. - e2e synthetic replay against staging with 10k synthetic invocations showing 63% reduction in full-trace volume while retaining 91% of anomaly captures. - Canary rollout: started on staging tenants -> canary tenants -> all non-enterprise tenants over a 2-week window. Rollback path: feature flag to disable fence globally; metric alarms on fidelity_fence_allowed_total drop trigger automatic disable. Observability and alerts: - New alerts: fidelity-fence-sampling-drop (if allowed fraction drops > 20% unexpectedly), fidelity-fence-error-rate-increase (if per-tenant error rate rises by >15% after fence enablement). - Dashboard includes an 'impact estimator' panel that estimates monthly storage delta given current allowed fraction. Commits (high-level): ["fidelity: add policy engine and unit tests", "telemetry: emit fidelity_fence metrics and tags", "dashboards: add cost-tilt visualizer + template vars", "configs: default fidelity fence policy and tenant override plumbing", "docs: runbook and rollout notes"] Changed files (high-level): ["observability-sidecar/fidelity_fence.py", "observability-sidecar/tests/test_fidelity_fence.py", "telemetry/metrics_registry.py (adds metrics)", "dashboards/cost-tilt-visualizer.json", "configs/fidelity-defaults.yaml", "docs/observability/fidelity-runbook.md", "deploy/featureflags/fidelity_fence.yaml"] Review conversation (summary): - Aditi Rao (reviewer): "Like the direction. Two asks: add CI unit test for normalization edge-case (zero-variance token estimates) and add a short privacy note in the runbook about scrub patterns." - Author (Priya): "Added unit test and clarified scrub rules in runbook (redaction of PII, maintain compatibility with tenant scrubbing policies)." - Marcus Lee: "Can we reduce weight on token_estimate to avoid biasing toward long prompts? Also request a small perf benchmark showing policy eval latency." - Priya: "Lowered w1 default from 0.6 to 0.2, added a microbench (avg eval time 180ns; p99 520ns) to the PR description and test harness." - Sofia Turner: "Dashboard looks good; consider adding a per-model family aggregator to help sales/CS." - Priya: "Added model_family aggregation and enabled templating." CI: - Unit: pass - Lint: pass (fixed a minor flake8 complaint) - Integration: pass (staging harness) - Load smoke: pass (canary load tests within acceptable bounds) Metrics observed in staging: - Full-trace capture volume: down ~61% - Anomaly recall (sampled): 91% retained - Edge policy eval latency: mean 0.18us, p99 0.52us - Grafana dashboard: tilt scores computed via a 5m aggregation job; query cost is within budget Rollout notes: - Default policy applied to non-enterprise tenants after merge; enterprise tenants remain opt-in until product approval. - Feature flags and tenant overrides available in tenant-config API. - Runbook contains steps to disable fence and to force full-fidelity for a tenant for diagnostic reasons Known limitations and future work: - Current scoring is rule-based; next step is a lightweight ML model to predict signal value per invocation. - Prompt-shape bucketing is coarse; once we deploy more prompt fingerprinting we will refine cohorting. - Cost-tilt visualizer relies on periodic aggregations; adding a streaming tilt estimator is planned. Backwards compatibility: no breaking API changes. All changes guarded behind feature flags and tenant opt-in for enterprise. Related: ENG-7421 (linked linear): ties into the storage cost reduction OKR. Related PRs and references: observability-pack/pr-272222 (privacy-safe summarizers), redwood/pr-118903 (adaptive alert smoothing). Merge: squash merge performed by Aditi Rao. Post-merge actions: - Tag dashboards for release pipeline - Schedule a follow-up in 2 weeks to review impact metrics and adjust thresholds - Notify solutions engineering and platform docs to prepare customer-facing notes

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration/staging run
- [x] Runbook and privacy notes
- [x] Dashboard + templates
- [x] Rollout plan and feature flags

CI summary: all green. Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2026-02-18 by reviewer Aditi Rao.
Add adaptive fidelity fence sampler to reduce noisy log volume, and a Cost Tilt visualizer dashboard to surface skewed cost distributions across routes and models.

Context
We’re standardizing a metering data-quality view so Finance/RevOps + Eng can quickly answer: (a) are usage events in sync with the billing ledger, (b) is data arriving on time for close/invoice previews, and (c) are we seeing duplicate usage events consistent with idempotency regressions/backfills.

This PR adds a Grafana dashboard (and initial alerting rules) for metering drift, freshness, and duplicate rates. It is intended to pair with the in-product Console sanity dashboard work (ENG-4415) and the scheduled drift job in the redwood monorepo (ENG-4421).

What’s included
- Dashboard: "Metering Sanity: Drift + Freshness" (folder: Billing/Metering)
  - Drift panels (usage_events vs billing_ledger aggregates)
    - Drift % by day (global)
    - Top-N accounts by absolute drift ($ and tokens) over last 24h / 7d
    - Drift by dimension: region, model, endpoint (chat/completions/embeddings)
    - Breakdown of drift causes when available (late_events, missing_dims, duplicates) from the drift job’s tagged metrics
  - Freshness panels
    - p50/p95 ingestion lag for usage_events (event_time -> available_in_warehouse)
    - Latest partition timestamps for key tables/exports (usage_events, usage_rollups, ledger_export)
    - "Freeze window" annotations (month-end close) based on the Finance agreed schedule
  - Duplicate rate panels
    - Duplicate usage_event_id rate (raw)
    - Duplicate dedupe_key collision rate (post-dedupe)
    - Retries/fallback signal overlays (when emitted) to correlate spikes

- Alerts (initial thresholds; tuned to avoid paging on small-account noise)
  - MeterDriftHigh (page): 24h drift % > 0.50% AND absolute drift > $2,000 OR > 5M billed_tokens, scoped per (region, endpoint)
  - MeterDriftModerate (ticket): 24h drift % > 0.25% AND absolute drift > $500
  - MeterFreshnessSLOBreach (page): p95 ingestion lag > 90 minutes for 30 minutes
  - MeterDuplicateRateHigh (page): duplicates > 0.10% of events for 20 minutes OR sustained > 0.05% for 2 hours
  - All alerts include runbook links + "known incident" annotation guidance

Metrics / data sources
- Prometheus series produced by drift job (redwood):
  - metering_drift_ratio{dimension=..., region=..., endpoint=...}
  - metering_drift_absolute_usd{...}
  - metering_drift_absolute_tokens{...}
  - metering_usage_ingestion_lag_seconds{quantile="0.95"}
  - metering_duplicate_rate{type="event_id"|"dedupe_key"}

Notes:
- This PR does not change metering logic. It only wires dashboard panels and rules to existing signals emitted by the job/export pipeline.
- For accounts with very small spend, percentage drift is noisy. Alerts gate on both % and absolute magnitude.

Rollout plan
1) Merge with alerts disabled by default (rule groups present; routing muted in prod for 48h).
2) Observe baseline noise during ongoing shadow billing compare.
3) Enable Moderate alerts to ticket first; then enable paging on DriftHigh + Freshness after threshold tuning.

Follow-ups
- Add a dedicated "embeddings batch" panel once ENG-4412 backfill completes (missing cache-hit/attribution fields).
- Add alert label for "meter_version" once shadow-billing compare exports meter_version consistently.

Screenshots
- Not included in PR (dashboards are generated from jsonnet). Use the rendered preview link in CI artifacts.

Refs
- Linear: ENG-4421 (alert on meter drift), ENG-4415 (Console dashboard)
- Slack threads: meter drift alert tuning, freshness SLO discussion
- Runbooks: Confluence runbook will be linked once published (placeholder link included).
Caleb Johnson: Drift panels look good. Can we add a variable for warehouse (prod vs staging) to make debugging easier?
Aisha Bello: Added datasource/cluster variable in targets.libsonnet; defaults to prod but supports staging.
Mei Lin: For Freshness, can we show both p95 lag and "latest partition timestamp" for the ledger export table? That’s what Finance checks during close.
Aisha Bello: Added a stat panel for latest_export_partition_ts and a small table panel for the three key tables (usage_events, rollups, ledger_export).
Logan Wright: Alert thresholds: 0.5% seems okay, but can we gate on absolute USD/tokens to prevent paging on tiny tenants? Also please route duplicates as ticket first.
Aisha Bello: Implemented % + absolute gating (usd OR tokens) and set Moderate/Ticket vs High/Page. Duplicate alert stays page only for high sustained rate; added ticket-level condition for moderate duplicates.
Allison Grant: Please include runbook links in annotations and make sure rule labels include owner/team for on-call routing.
Aisha Bello: Added runbook_url annotation and labels: team=eng-sre, service=metering, owner=Aisha. The runbook URL is a placeholder until Confluence page is published.
Add metering sanity dashboard jsonnet + folder wiring
Add recording rules for ingestion lag percentiles + top-N drift queries
Add alert rule group for drift/freshness/duplicates with severity gating
Document dashboard variables and drilldowns
payload.title: Add metering drift Grafana dashboard + alert rules (drift, freshness, duplicates)

payload.body:
Motivation: Some prompt-set regressions are only exposed when small counterfactual perturbations interact with model calibration. This PR adds a counterfactual anchor prober and a companion confidence-decay soft-fail CI gate to detect subtle, distribution-sensitive regressions early. Design summary: 1) counterfactual_anchor_prober: Generates controlled counterfactual variants for each prompt anchor using lightweight perturbation operators (lexical swap, entity obfuscation, tense-shift) and computes an ensemble disagreement + calibration-adjusted robustness score per anchor. 2) confidence_decay_gate CI hook: Aggregates anchor scores across a prompt-set and applies a decaying confidence budget so transient outliers do not block merges but sustained decay triggers a soft-fail (annotated CI failure) and opens an automated investigation ticket. 3) Integrations: Wire prober output into the existing eval-report JSON schema, add telemetry for per-anchor failure modes, and add a remediation suggestions block that lists candidate prompt fixes or recommended model rollout throttles. Implementation notes: - New module eval_harness/probers/counterfactual_anchor.py implements generator and scoring pipeline with pluggable perturbation registry. - CI hook implemented at ci/hooks/confidence_decay_gate.py and registered in .github/workflows/eval-ci.yml as a post-eval step. - Small helper in eval_harness/utils/calibration.py adds confidence-adjusted scoring utilities used by other gates. - Tests: unit tests for perturbation operators and end-to-end smokecases in tests/probers/test_counterfactual_anchor.py. - Docs: docs/eval/counterfactual-anchor.md explains configuration knobs and migration notes. Testing and validation: ran the new prober across three canonical prompt-sets (chatbot-support, email-compose, code-generation) and used historical snapshots to verify that the gate triggers only for sustained degradations (simulated via injected perturbation noise). CI run initially failed due to a nondeterministic tokenization edge-case in one perturbation operator; fixed by normalizing whitespace in the generator and reran. Backwards compatibility and rollout: default configuration is disabled for global CI and enabled in an opt-in eval policy named "counterfactual-guard-v1". We will enable it on the nightlies for two weeks before lifting to PR gating. Security and perf: perturbations run in-process and are lightweight; added an execution timeout and caps on variant count to prevent runaway cost. Checklist: - [x] Prober implementation and unit tests - [x] CI hook + workflow registration - [x] Integration into eval-report schema - [x] Docs and migration notes - [x] Telemetry counters and tracing annotations - [x] Manual smoke runs and historical backtests Related work: builds on prior anchor/replay ideas (see ENG-1176) but focuses on counterfactual perturbations and calibration-driven confidence decay to reduce false-positive gating. Linear/Jira: ENG-1289 epic for regression-detection features, ENG-1292 task for CI gate integration, SUP-4421 customer incident that motivated counterfactual checks. Rollout plan: opt-in -> nightlies -> staged PR gating for 10% org -> full PR gating if noise < 2% over 14 days. Notes: the prober registry is intentionally extensible so other teams can add domain-specific perturbations (e.g., API param shuffling for developer-facing prompt-sets).
Ravi Patel: Nice design. Two asks: (1) can we limit total variants per anchor by default to 20 and (2) add a short-circuit so high-confidence anchors skip heavy perturbations?
Author (Claire Nguyen): Implemented variant cap and short-circuit; updated docs to surface these knobs.
Marta Lopez: CI hook looks good, but pls add an allowlist for sensitive prompt-sets that should never have perturbations run in CI.
Author: Added allowlist support and a fallback opt-out via environment variable EVAL_ANCHOR_ALLOWLIST.
Evan Chen: Telemetry looks fine. One nit: use exponential decay with half-life config instead of linear decay to better match observed regression patterns.
Author: Switched to configurable exponential decay and added tests for decay behavior.
GitHub Actions eval-ci: initial run failed (test: test_perturbation_whitespace) -> tokenization nondeterminism; fix tokenization normalization -> rerun
Secondary checks: lint (pass), mypy (pass), integration-run (pass), perf-smoke (pass), nightly-backtest (pass)
Introduce a pluggable counterfactual anchor prober and a confidence-decay soft-fail CI gate to detect sustained, subtle prompt-set regressions. Opt-in by default and can be enabled via eval policy 'counterfactual-guard-v1'. Adds telemetry, docs, and remediation suggestions.
Enable 'counterfactual-guard-v1' in eval policy to opt into PR gating. See docs/eval/counterfactual-anchor.md for config fields, allowlist usage, and rollback steps.
Run pytest tests/probers and scripts/backtest/counterfactual_backtest.py against historical snapshots. To simulate a sustained regression, increase perturbation intensity in examples/anchor-configs/counterfactual-guard.yaml and run nightlies.
payload.title: Introduce counterfactual anchor prober with confidence-decay soft-fail CI gate

payload.body:
Context and motivation: First responders frequently lose ephemeral UI context (open traces, selected log ranges, pinned screenshots) when a browser reloads or when they switch devices during an alert. That transient loss costs time and forces redundant searches. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: a context resumer that persists minimal on-call state in an encrypted short-lived store, and a sliding telemetry window collector that lets responders attach a bounded recent telemetry slice to an incident for instant replay.

What this PR does (single-string narrative): - Adds a context-resumer service (incident-bot/context-resumer) that snapshots selected UI state (selected span id, time range, pinned logs, active runbook step) into an ephemeral store (encrypted, per-incident, TTL=20m). The store is implemented as a lightweight redis-backed shard with HMAC-signed tokens; by default the feature is gated off and enabled via the INCIDENT_RESUMER flag. - Implements a sliding-telemetry-window collector (observability/telemetry-window) which can capture a time-bounded set of traces, logs, and metrics samples around the time an on-call session is initiated. The window is configurable (default 2m pre-alert, 1m post-attach) and stored as an indexed tarball for quick download. - Wire-up in the UI: resume prompt on reconnect, 'attach recent telemetry' button in the incident sidebar, and a small status indicator showing retention TTL. - Security and privacy: snapshots exclude user inputs and secrets by default; there is a sanitize pipeline for logs that strips IPs and kube IDs. Admins can configure retention and disable storage. - Operational: adds metrics (resumer.hits, resumer.misses, telemetry.window.size_samples) and dashboard panels for hit-rate and storage churn.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-9102) - [x] Unit tests for resumer serializer and TTL enforcement - [x] Integration test for restore flow (happy path + expired token) - [x] End-to-end UI smoke tests (resume flow + attach window) - [x] Security review: sanitize pipeline + threat model notes added - [x] Feature gated behind flag for gradual rollout

Commits summary: - 8f3b2cc: start(context-resumer): service scaffold + redis-backed ephemeral store - c4d2b7a: feat(telemetry-window): collector + archive writer and index - 9d1f5e4: ui(resume): add resume prompt and attach telemetry action - 3b6a2f1: test: integration tests for restore and telemetry attach - a7e9c33: ci: add e2e smoke stage and new metric assertions

Files touched (high-level): - incident-bot/pkg/resumer/* (service, handlers, serializer) - observability/telemetry/window_collector.go (collector + archiver) - webapp/src/components/ResumePrompt.tsx (resume UI) - scripts/e2e/resume_flow.spec.ts (e2e) - infra/redis/values.yaml (optional chart knobs) - docs/oncall/context-resumer.md (how-to and admin settings) - dashboards/resumer_panel.json (grafana panel)

Review conversation (highlights as single string): "Maya Chen (reviewer): Can we avoid storing full stack traces in the snapshot? We should only include trace IDs and a sampling of spans.
Elliot (author): Good catch — implemented a sanitize pass to store only IDs and up to 3 span summaries per trace. Added test to prove sensitive fields are dropped.
Ravi Singh (reviewer): The redis shard may grow if users trigger many snapshots quickly. What's the eviction plan?
Elliot: TTLs are enforced at write and we added a periodic GC job; also added a metric for eviction rate and a dashboard alert if total ephemeral keys exceed threshold.
Ana Torres (security): Ensure we have explicit opt-out for EU customers due to retention rules.
Elliot: Added a per-organization flag and documented the compliance controls in docs/oncall/context-resumer.md.

CI and merge notes: - Initial CI run failed intermittently on e2e (flaky start-up), tests rerun after increasing test timeouts. - All checks passed on second run (unit, lint, e2e-smoke). - Merge method: squash and merge. Release will enable feature in staged tenants via feature flag; ops will monitor resumer.hits and telemetry.window.size_samples during rollout.

Backward compatibility and migration: This is fully backward-compatible when feature flag is off. The telemetry archive format includes a version header and supports a migration path for future index changes.

Operational runbook excerpt (single-line friendly): If resumer.hits is low but resumer.errors is high, check redis auth and eviction logs; if telemetry.window.count spikes, temporarily tighten default duration or enable sampling.

Why this is unique / impact: Restoring UI context reduces time-to-first-action for responders by removing repetitive filtering and trace hunting. Combined with an attachable, bounded telemetry window, this feature turns the first responder session into an immediately actionable view of recent system state, lowering MTTR for transient incidents.

Follow-ups / TODOs: - Add per-incident manual deletion API for compliance - Add automatic anonymization plugins for additional PII types - Consider an on-disk fallback when redis quota is reached (feature gated)

Merge result: merged via squash (maintainer: Maya Chen)."
payload.title: On-call context resumer and sliding telemetry window collector
