Context: As part of the model metadata schema + changelog generator rollout, we now emit structured model change events (promotions, rollbacks, metadata edits) and rollout phase transitions. Support and oncall repeatedly asked for a fast way to answer: “did this latency/regression coincide with a model version promotion or rollout phase change?” This PR adds Grafana panels + recording rules to correlate: (1) model version change rate, (2) rollout phase transitions (canary/A-B/GA/rollback), and (3) incident/regression signals (5xx, timeouts, p95/p99 latency, eval-guardrail failures when present). What’s included: - New dashboard: “Model Rollout Correlation” with panels for change rate over time, rollout phase annotations, and ‘before/after’ latency + error overlays. - Update existing “LLM Serving Overview” dashboard with a compact panel showing model version change rate by deployment_mode and model_name (top 10) plus a click-through to the correlation dashboard. - Prometheus recording rules to normalize and de-cardinalize model change counters for dashboards (avoid high-cardinality labels from raw events). - Standard annotations schema for rollout phase changes (Grafana annotations sourced from Loki logs) to visualize canary/A-B boundaries. Notes/assumptions: - This depends on control-plane emitting model_change and rollout_phase_change events (redwood PR #18435 / #18458). In environments where those logs/metrics aren’t present yet, panels will render ‘No data’ but won’t break dashboards. - We intentionally do not include per-customer/account identifiers in any metric labelset; correlation for account-specific cases should use trace IDs / audit tooling, not dashboards. - Private deployments: these dashboards assume the “control-plane-events” log stream is configured; otherwise skip the annotations panel per docs added here.
Metrics inputs: - counter: redwood_control_plane_model_change_events_total{action="promote"|"rollback"|"metadata_update", deployment_mode, model_name, model_version} (raw; high-cardinality due to version) - counter: redwood_control_plane_rollout_phase_events_total{phase, deployment_mode, model_name, rollout_id} (raw; rollout_id high-cardinality) This PR adds recording rules to collapse labels for dashboards: - redwood:model_change_events:rate5m{action, deployment_mode, model_name} = sum without(model_version,region,cluster) (rate(redwood_control_plane_model_change_events_total[5m])) - redwood:rollout_phase_transitions:rate5m{phase, deployment_mode, model_name} = sum without(rollout_id,region,cluster) (rate(redwood_control_plane_rollout_phase_events_total[5m])) Correlation dashboard panels: - “Model version change rate (promote/rollback)” time series, stacked by action - “Rollout phase transition rate” time series (canary/ab/ga) - “Errors & latency overlay” showing requests_error_rate and p95 latency for the same model_name + deployment_mode, with the above series as overlays - “Regression signals” panel: guardrail_fail_rate (if present) and ‘quality_regression_flag’ (0/1) when eval harness emits it (optional) Grafana annotations: - Source: Loki stream {app="control-plane", component="eventing"} | json | event_type in ("rollout_phase_change") - Annotation text includes: model_name, phase, rollout_id (NOT used as a metric label; only shown in the annotation tooltip).
Local: jsonnet render + grafana-dashboard-linter, promtool check rules. Staging: validated dashboard renders against staging metrics (rollouts dogfood environment). Verified panels show ‘No data’ gracefully when model change metrics absent by toggling datasource to a sandbox Prometheus. Verified that label cardinality does not grow with model_version or rollout_id by inspecting series count for redwood:model_change_events:rate5m and redwood:rollout_phase_transitions:rate5m.
Jada Williams (requested changes): The change-rate panel is useful, but please ensure the recording rules strip model_version; otherwise dashboards will explode in cardinality for frequent promotions. Also can we align naming with the schema doc: ‘promote’ vs ‘promotion’? Logan Wright (author): Good catch. Updated rules to sum without(model_version, rollout_id) and standardized action values to promote/rollback/metadata_update in the rule expression + legend. Michael Nguyen (requested changes): For rollbacks, we should be able to distinguish “auto-fallback” vs “manual rollback” eventually. Not blocking, but can you at least leave a TODO in the dashboard and avoid encoding that as a label now. Logan Wright: Added a dashboard note + TODO in docs; no label added. Leila Farouk (QA): Can you add a snapshot test (jsonnet render diff) to prevent accidental dashboard churn? Logan Wright: Added a CI step that renders jsonnet and checks in the rendered output hash; also tightened formatting so diffs are stable. Dylan Brooks (approve): This unblocks the Console + Support story; thanks. Please link the runbook from the oncall handbook in a follow-up. Logan Wright: Ack; will file a follow-up PR in docs repo.
Follow-ups: (1) add oncall handbook link to docs/runbooks/model-rollout-correlation.md, (2) once rollout_phase_change events are fully deployed, switch annotations to the dedicated events index instead of parsing control-plane logs, (3) evaluate adding a lightweight ‘incident overlay’ annotation feed (PagerDuty) for tighter correlation.
payload.title: Dashboards: correlate model version change rate with rollout phases and incident/regression signals

payload.body:
## Summary
Adds internal Grafana dashboards and alert rules for the Unit Economics pipeline (hourly aggregation + warehouse views) so we can detect missing hours, freshness lag, and dimension coverage regressions before Finance/Product consume the Console dashboard.

This PR lives in `observability-pack` and only ships dashboards/alerts (no runtime or pipeline code changes). It assumes the aggregator and DQ checks emit the metrics introduced in the Redwood monorepo work (ENG-8426/ENG-8429).

## Motivation
During dogfood we repeatedly saw "looks like a cost spike" that was actually missing output tokens or delayed aggregation. The Console page is not the right place to diagnose pipeline health, and SRE asked for a standard set of panels + alerts aligned to the proposed SLO.

## What’s included
- Grafana dashboard: **Unit Economics — Pipeline Health**
  - Freshness lag (now - last successful hourly partition) by environment
  - Ingestion completeness (% expected hourly partitions present in last 24h)
  - Aggregation job runtime and failure rate
  - Warehouse view query latency (p95/p99) for the dashboard endpoints
  - Backfill activity (rows written/hour + throttling indicators)
- Grafana dashboard: **Unit Economics — Coverage & Drift**
  - Output token totals by hour with 7d baseline band (detect sudden drops)
  - Dimension coverage panels:
    - % rows missing `region`
    - % rows missing `customer_tier`
    - % rows missing `model_id` / `model_version`
    - `quantization_profile` cardinality + unknown/other bucket rate
  - Top offenders tables (regions with high null mapping, tiers with zero coverage)
- Alert rules (Prometheus-style via Jsonnet)
  - `unit_econ_pipeline_freshness_lag_hours > 2` (page)
  - `unit_econ_pipeline_missing_partitions_24h > 1` (page)
  - `unit_econ_output_tokens_drop_ratio < 0.6` vs trailing 7d median (page; 2 consecutive evals)
  - `unit_econ_dimension_null_rate{dim=region} > 0.5%` (ticket)
  - `unit_econ_dimension_null_rate{dim=customer_tier} > 0.5%` (ticket)
  - `unit_econ_quant_profile_unknown_rate > 0.2%` (ticket)
  - `unit_econ_warehouse_view_latency_p99_ms > 2500` (ticket)
- Alert routing + runbook links
  - Pages route to `#eng-sre` and `#eng-platform` with oncall mention
  - Tickets route to `#eng-platform` with a lower-noise policy
  - Runbook URL is included in annotations and points to the unit economics oncall guide (ENG-8435)

## Notes on thresholds / noise
- Freshness/page thresholds mirror the proposed SLO: "hourly data available within 90 minutes" with a buffer for warehouse maintenance windows.
- Token-drop alert uses a ratio vs trailing 7d median per environment, because absolute tokens vary substantially by weekday and launches.
- Dimension null-rate thresholds are set to 0.5% for now to catch mapping regressions without paging on small blips. We can tighten after 2 weeks of baseline.

## Files / areas changed (high level)
- `dashboards/unit-economics/pipeline-health.jsonnet` (new)
- `dashboards/unit-economics/coverage-and-drift.jsonnet` (new)
- `alerts/unit-economics/pipeline-alerts.jsonnet` (new)
- `alerts/unit-economics/README.md` (new; runbook + alert intent)
- `lib/panels/unit-economics.libsonnet` (new; shared panels + variable definitions)
- `team-ownership/oncall-rotations.libsonnet` (updated routing for econ pipeline)

## Example rule (illustrative)
The freshness alert is keyed off the "last successful hourly partition" metric exported by the aggregator job:
- expr: `time() - unit_econ_agg_last_success_timestamp_seconds > 2 * 3600`
- for: `10m`
- severity: page
- annotations include runbook and a "first checks" list.

## Testing / verification
- Rendered dashboards locally with `make grafana-render` and verified variable wiring (env/cluster/warehouse).
- Loaded into staging Grafana and confirmed panels populate for the last 24h.
- Dry-ran alerts in staging with lowered thresholds to confirm routing + annotations.

## Rollout plan
1) Merge and deploy observability-pack.
2) Enable alerts in staging for 24h.
3) Enable production alerts with `ticket` severities only for 48h (collect baseline).
4) Promote freshness + missing partitions + token-drop to `page`.

## Open questions
- Do we want a separate Finance-friendly "health badge" summary panel embedded in the Console dashboard? (out of scope here)
- Should `unit_econ_warehouse_view_latency_*` alerts be owned by Console oncall instead of Platform? Current routing goes to Platform due to materialization/partitioning dependencies.

## PR conversation highlights
- Allison Grant: Requested that paging alerts include direct runbook links and a short decision tree. Updated annotations to include: verify ingestion lag, check latest partitions table, run backfill if needed.
- Sean Gallagher: Asked to avoid paging on single-hour drops during scheduled warehouse maintenance. Added `for: 10m` and excluded known maintenance window label where present.
- Caleb Johnson: Flagged that `quantization_profile` could become high-cardinality; requested a dedicated panel + alert on unknown/other bucket rate rather than raw cardinality alone. Added both.
- Mei Lin: Noted the p99 latency threshold should be environment-specific. Added separate thresholds: staging 4000ms ticket, prod 2500ms ticket.

## CI
- lint/jsonnet: pass
- dashboards render: pass
- unit tests (alerts schema validation): pass

Merged via squash.

Refs: ENG-8429 (data quality checks/anomaly alerts), ENG-8435 (oncall runbook/playbook docs).
Internal-only: Adds Grafana dashboards and alert rules for the Unit Economics pipeline (freshness/completeness/dimension coverage) with runbook links and tuned severities.
payload.title: Add Unit Economics pipeline Grafana dashboards + freshness/completeness alerts

payload.body:
Motivation: Running full-traffic canaries for every rollout is costly and slow. For a subset of rollouts (model minor bumps, scheduler tweaks) we want a small, representative traffic 'coreset' that preserves signal for latency/throughput/SLO regressions while reducing test volume and compute cost. This PR implements a traffic coreset sampler plus a slice-stability rollout guard that protects against selection drift and ensures the coreset remains predictive over time.

What this PR adds (summary): 1) coreset_sampler: a lightweight stratified weighted sampler that maintains a bounded-size sample while preserving distribution over key axes (tenant, endpoint, request size, model variant). 2) impact-weighting: requests are weighted by estimated per-request resource cost so the coreset prioritizes high-cost/high-impact traffic slices. 3) slice-stability-guard: a canary guard that computes divergence metrics (Wasserstein distance on request-size, KL on endpoint distribution, p95 delta on latency) between historical reference traffic and live slice; when divergence > threshold it pauses or expands the slice. 4) dashboard and alerting tiles for slice fidelity and slice drift. 5) e2e harness and deterministic replay tests for reproducibility.

Config knobs: sample_size (default 10k requests/min), stratify_keys (default [tenant, endpoint, prompt_len_bucket]), impact_weight_alpha (0.7 default), stability_thresholds (per-metric tunables), auto_expand_on_drift (boolean, default false).

Rollout plan: staged rollout: dev->staging (2 days) with synthetic replay -> canary ring (5% traffic) using coreset slice -> gradual enable across rings with automated monitoring gating. We ran a controlled live traffic dry-run on staging that shows the coreset preserved p90/p99 deltas within 3% of full-traffic canary for a 12.5% sample.

Backward compatibility: No user-facing API changes. Canary controller gains optional flags to enable coreset-based evaluation. Default behavior remains full-traffic canaries until enabled via config.

Related work: complements the existing canary detectors (percentile-decay and correlation canary) by reducing the evaluation surface; references: ENG-10234, perf-canary PRs for percentile-decay.

Limitations: coreset effectiveness depends on good stratification keys; large distributional shifts where unseen endpoints appear require guard intervention. This PR intentionally runs slice-stability checks and defaults to fail-open (pause canary) until manual review if severe drift is detected.
Introduce traffic coreset sampler and slice stability guard for more efficient, targeted canary evaluation; enables shorter canary windows and lower cost while preserving signal fidelity.
Unit tests added for sampling invariants (stratification, weighting). Replay harness deterministic: 10 runs identical across CI nodes. Staging dry-run: compared full-traffic vs coreset canary across 7 model variants and 3 endpoints; p90/p99 deltas within 3% for samples >= 10k/min. Live canary (5% ring, synthetic traffic): no regressions observed; slice drift alert fired once due to synthetic skew and auto-expanded slice to remediate. Post-merge: enabled in staging for 48h with monitoring alerts configured.
Risk: slice may miss rare but critical request types leading to false negatives in canary detection. Mitigations: 1) stability guard monitors distributional drift and pauses/expands slice; 2) per-tenant override to include user-provided critical endpoints; 3) fallback to full-traffic canary on manual inspection or if slice fails validation.
Operational dashboard tiles added: coreset_fidelity_{p90,p99}, slice_wasserstein, slice_kl_endpoint, estimated_cost_savings. Runbook located at docs/perf-canary/coreset.md with rollback steps. To disable coreset mode set canary.controller.use_coreset=false in config.
Marcus Varela (reviewer): The sampler looks sound but can we add a deterministic seed and a way to snapshot the coreset for postmortem replays?
Author (Sophie Park): Added deterministic seeding and snapshot API in the latest commit; updated tests to cover replay equality.
Anita Kumar (reviewer): The stability thresholds are conservative; recommend per-tenant overrides and a metric for resource-cost drift. Also, please ensure the guard prefers auto-expansion before pause for low-severity drift.
Author (Sophie Park): Added per-tenant threshold map and included resource-cost p95 delta as a metric. Default behavior changed to auto-expand by 2x on low-severity drift and pause only on high-severity drift (>2x thresholds).
Diego Salazar (reviewer): CI integration spike: the perf-e2e flaked once in staging but rerun passed. Can you add a retry stanza in the pipeline?
Author (Sophie Park): Added a single-retry to the e2e job and a short jitter to prevent thundering replays.
payload.title: introduce-coreset-traffic-slicing-for-targeted-canary-evals

Context: This PR introduces the baseline alerting + recording rules for the Redwood Private observability minimum pack, focused on the highest-impact failure modes for inference availability and latency regressions. These are intended to be safe-by-default in customer clusters (bounded cardinality, conservative paging) and to map cleanly to the SLO guidance we’ve been using in staging.

What’s included (v1):
- Recording rules (namespace: redwood_private:*) used by dashboards + alerts so queries are consistent and cheaper.
- Latency SLO burn alerts (multi-window, multi-burn) for the API gateway and runtime request path.
- Availability alerts (5xx rate + blackbox reachability) for API ingress and control plane critical services.
- Alert annotations include runbook + first steps links and a canonical dashboard deep link placeholder.
- promtool tests for rule syntax + basic evaluation fixtures.

Alert philosophy / thresholds (rationale):
- We page only on issues that are likely customer-visible and sustained.
- Latency: burn-rate alerts use a 2-window strategy (fast burn for rapid regressions, slow burn for creeping issues). This matches Aisha’s guidance for Private: prefer burn rates over raw p95 spikes to avoid noise in heterogeneous customer traffic.
- Availability: default is request-based (5xx ratio) rather than absolute error count; includes a minimum request rate gate to avoid low-traffic false positives.
- We intentionally avoid high-cardinality labels in alerts (no tenant_id, no raw model name, no full route). Where route-level is needed, we aggregate to route_group and/or service.

Defaults (tuned for min pack):
- Page (Sev2): sustained burn likely to exhaust error budget within 1h OR API is unreachable.
- Ticket (Sev3): slower burn / partial degradation / early warning.
- Warning alerts are created but set to disabled-by-default in values; the helm wiring PR will decide final toggles.

Runbooks:
- Latency burn: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGPRIV/Runbook+-+Private+Latency+SLO+Burn
- Availability / 5xx: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGPRIV/Runbook+-+Private+Availability+and+5xx
- Prometheus scrape health (support): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGINFRA/Prometheus+and+Grafana+for+Private+Installations

Notes / follow-ups:
- GPU saturation, OOM, and restart-loop alerts are tracked separately (ENG-19148).
- This PR does not wire rules into helm values; that is handled in redwood-helm-charts PR-18405.
- We should revisit the latency objective (currently defaults to 800ms p95 for chat endpoints) after we have 2–3 customer baselines from validation.

Checklist:
- [x] Recording rules included for RPS, error ratio, latency quantiles, and SLI measurements
- [x] Alerts include runbook URLs and concise "what to do first" steps
- [x] promtool rule tests added
- [x] Label cardinality bounded (no per-tenant or per-model alert dimension)
- [x] Reviewed against Private metrics/alerting standards

Screenshots/Examples:
- Included in the conversation: example firing of LatencySLOBurnFast after injected delay; and non-firing for low traffic due to request rate gate.
Allison Grant (review): Can we align naming with the standards doc? Prefer redwood_private:sli_error_ratio:rate5m rather than redwood_private_error_ratio_5m.
Sergio Costa (author): Updated to match the `redwood_private:<thing>:<agg>` convention and added a short note in README-private-min-pack.md.
Aisha Bello (review): For burn rates, please use a multi-window multi-burn pattern and avoid a single p95 threshold alert. Also add a minimum traffic gate.
Sergio Costa (author): Switched to 2-window burn (5m/1h + 30m/6h), added `> 1 rps` gate for the SLI streams, and kept a disabled-by-default "p95 spike" warning only for debugging.
Neha Kapoor (review): We need actionable annotations. Include the 3 first steps in the alert description, not only the runbook link.
Sergio Costa (author): Added annotations: (1) check scrape health, (2) check gateway saturation panels, (3) confirm recent deploys/rollouts. Also added placeholders for the Grafana dashboard deep links.
Tomáš Novák (review): Severity labels need to map to paging policy: page-worthy should be `severity=sev2` and ticket should be `sev3`. Please avoid `critical`/`warning` since Support tooling keys off sev2/sev3.
Sergio Costa (author): Updated severities and added `pager=oncall|none` routing hint label per our standard. Confirmed with Rafael this matches staging routing.
Rafael Mendes (review): I replayed the staging incident from last week (gateway auth misconfig causing 401s + 5xx spikes). The 5xx ratio alert fired correctly; can we add a small note that 401/403 are excluded by design?
Sergio Costa (author): Added note in README + kept alert expression scoped to 5xx. Also added a comment in the rule file to prevent future changes that page on auth failures (Support handles separately).
Neha Kapoor (follow-up): promtool tests are great; can we add at least one test to ensure low-traffic clusters don’t fire availability alerts?
Sergio Costa (author): Added fixture `private_availability_5xx_low_traffic.yaml` and a non-firing assertion.
payload.title: Add Private minimum pack Prometheus alert rules: latency + availability (with SLO burn recording rules)

payload.body:
Motivation: long-tail occupancy and cross-request primer interference are hard to reproduce with single-session runners. This PR introduces a Concurrent Primer Sandwich workload runner (concurrent pairs of short primer + target sequences) that stresses KV cache churn, packing/steady-state transitions, and small-microburst coalescing. It also ships a lightweight sparse-kernel telemetry sink that records per-kernel occupancy samples and a compact events stream for offline attribution.

What changed (summary): added a new runner binary (bench/primer_sandwich_runner) that can orchestrate N concurrent primer+target sessions with configurable primer overlap, interleaving patterns, and sequence-length distributions. Added instrumentation hooks that emit sparse kernel occupancy samples to telemetry/sinks/sparse_kernel_sink.go, and a small exporter that writes a compact NDJSON events stream for downstream profilers.

Checklist:
- [x] New runner with deterministic RNG seed and replay mode
- [x] Sparse telemetry sink + unit tests
- [x] CI bench workflow integration (bench/ci/benchmarks.yml)
- [x] Documentation + example configs (docs/bench/primer-sandwich.md)
- [x] Manual verification on a small GPU cluster

How to run locally (examples):
- warmup + single run: ./bin/primer_sandwich_runner --concurrency=16 --primer-len-mean=64 --target-len-mean=128 --seed=42 --telemetry=sparse:./out/events.ndjson
- replay: ./bin/primer_sandwich_runner --replay=out/trace-20241112.json

Design notes: the "sandwich" term refers to each actor executing a short primer, then a target request, then optionally a primer again to simulate inter-request priming. The concurrent mode interleaves many such actors with configurable offsets; this reproduces spent KV slots and eviction churn patterns observed in production traces. The sparse telemetry sink intentionally samples kernel occupancy rather than streaming full traces to keep storage and CI bandwidth low. Sample format is an NDJSON event per sample: {"ts":..., "gpu":0, "kernel":"matmul_fp16", "occupancy":0.43, "active_warps":128}

Commits (high-level):
- 1st commit: add runner skeleton, deterministic session scheduler, CLI flags
- 2nd commit: implement primer/target orchestrator, seed-based replay, and examples
- 3rd commit: add sparse kernel telemetry sink, NDJSON exporter, and unit tests
- 4th commit: CI integration and docs

Changed files (high-level):
- bench/cmd/primer_sandwich_runner/main.go
- bench/internal/scheduler/concurrent_scheduler.go
- bench/internal/session/primer_session.go
- telemetry/sinks/sparse_kernel_sink.go
- telemetry/sinks/sparse_kernel_sink_test.go
- docs/bench/primer-sandwich.md
- bench/ci/benchmarks.yml
- examples/bench/primer-sandwich/example-config.yaml
- Makefile (bench target)

Small illustrative snippet (from concurrent_scheduler.go):
"""
// scheduleLoop advances actor ticks and emits start/stop events deterministically
for tick := 0; tick < cfg.Steps; tick++ {
    for _, actor := range actors {
        actor.Advance(tick)
        if actor.ShouldRunNow(tick) {
            dispatch(actor.Step())
        }
    }
}
"""

Testing and CI: The bench CI workflow runs a small-scale smoke run on a single GPU VM and validates NDJSON telemetry format with the unit tests. An earlier run failed flakily due to a goroutine leak reported by Linnea; fixed in commit 3 by adding context cancellation and a bounded worker pool. Final CI run: all checks green; bench smoke + unit tests + linters passed.

Performance notes: On a 4-GPU test cluster with concurrency=128 and primer-target overlap=0.6 we observed a 12% increase in tail p99 latency compared to uniform sequence runners, and a 7% uplift in kernel occupancy variance. Those numbers are captured in artifacts/out/bench-20241112-summary.json linked in the Linear ticket.

Backward compatibility: runner defaults are non-invasive (single-actor mode matches prior single-runner behavior). Telemetry sink is pluggable behind the existing telemetry registry and disabled by default. No breaking API changes.

Related: Linear ENG-1021 (investigate primer interference), ENG-1087 (sparse telemetry spec). References to prior bench artifacts and a small sample trace are included in the docs.
Marco Delgado: Overall direction LGTM. Please add a small e2e smoke script for CI artifacts and ensure the exporter rotates output files when size > 100MB.
Aisha Khatri (author): Added e2e smoke script and rotation in sparse_kernel_sink (commit 3) — PTAL.
Linnea Sørensen: Found a goroutine leak when controller ctx was canceled; added suggested cancellation handling. Re-run CI.
Devon Park: Verified NDJSON schema and added a small parser to bench/tools/validate_ndjson.go in a follow-up commit.
Marco Delgado: Approved — merging with squash.
payload.title: concurrent-primer-sandwich-runner and lightweight sparse-kernel telemetry sink

payload.body:
This adds a first-pass Grafana dashboard suite for Dedicated autoscaling bounds + predictive mode. The goal is to make it obvious when (a) the autoscaler wants to scale but is clamped by customer max/min bounds, (b) queue depth/latency is building because we are at max, (c) the predictor is under/over-shooting, and (d) scale events are firing too frequently (oscillation). Dashboards are designed to be usable by SRE/on-call and CS/TAMs during pilots with per-customer + per-deployment drilldowns, while keeping label cardinality bounded (deployment_id is supported; request_id is not). Panels rely on new metrics being emitted by the monorepo PRs (desired vs bounded replicas, bound-hit counters, prediction error series, scale-event reasons). This PR intentionally does not add alerting rules (that’s pr-1941) but includes dashboard annotations and templating aligned to the metric naming standard. Rollout: dashboards are under the Dedicated folder and gated by our standard dashboard provisioning; once merged, they’ll be available in staging immediately and prod after the next observability-pack sync.
Dashboards added: (1) Dedicated > Autoscaling Bounds > Overview: per-deployment desired_replicas vs bounded_replicas, min/max bound hit rates (5m + 1h), bounded state % time, queue depth, p95 latency, GPU utilization/saturation. (2) Predictive Mode: forecast_qps vs observed_qps, prediction_error_abs/pct, forecast staleness, fallback_to_reactive counters, and lead-time distribution (when available). (3) Scale Events: timeline of scale up/down events with reason labels (reactive_queue, reactive_saturation, predictive_bias, cooldown_blocked, bounded_max, bounded_min), step size histogram, and oscillation score (event rate + direction flips). (4) Queueing & Latency: queue depth with overlays for bounded_max periods and p95 latency, plus request rate and token throughput. (5) Drilldown: a templated view keyed by customer_id + deployment_id + region with a narrow time window and annotations for config changes + incident markers (manual annotation stream). Key metrics referenced (names expected from monorepo): redwood_dedicated_autoscaler_desired_replicas, redwood_dedicated_autoscaler_bounded_replicas, redwood_dedicated_autoscaler_bound_hit_total{bound="max|min"}, redwood_dedicated_queue_depth, redwood_dedicated_request_latency_ms_bucket, redwood_dedicated_predictor_forecast_qps, redwood_dedicated_observed_qps, redwood_dedicated_prediction_error_abs, redwood_dedicated_scale_event_total{direction="up|down",reason="..."}, redwood_dedicated_predictor_stale_total, redwood_dedicated_predictive_fallback_total.
Validated rendering in Grafana staging against synthetic series and a replayed pilot dataset snapshot. Verified templates: customer_id, deployment_id, region, model (optional). Ensured panels do not require high-cardinality labels beyond deployment_id (no request/session labels). Checked thresholds/units: queue depth as gauge, bound hit rates as per-second and per-interval %, prediction error as both absolute QPS and percent. Confirmed time ranges: Overview defaults to last 6h; Scale Events defaults to last 2h. Confirmed annotations show scale events via Loki stream when available; otherwise panels still render without annotations.
Allison Grant (review): Panels look right, but we should avoid showing both customer_id and deployment_id in every legend; legends are too noisy. Also please align variable names to our standard ($customer, $deployment, $region). Sergio Costa (author): Ack. Updated legend formats to prefer deployment_id by default and moved customer_id into panel description/tooltips; standardized variables across dashboards. Aisha Bello (review): Can we add a panel that directly answers “are we bounded-max and building queue?” for on-call triage? Also make sure p95 latency uses the Dedicated SLO histogram, not generic gateway latency. Sergio Costa (author): Added a ‘Bounded Max + Queue Buildup’ stat panel (30m window) with thresholds and a linked drilldown. Switched latency queries to redwood_dedicated_request_latency_ms_bucket. Rafael Mendes (review): Please add links to the runbook and mention what to do when min bound can’t be met due to region shortage. Also can we annotate config changes? Sergio Costa (author): Added runbook links in dashboard header and a note about ‘min unmet’ degraded state; added optional annotation query for scaling-policy audit events (falls back gracefully if stream isn’t present). Vanessa Ortiz (review): Prediction error panel: can we show forecast staleness explicitly and highlight when predictive fallback triggers? That’s been our pilot pain point. Sergio Costa (author): Added forecast staleness gauge and fallback counter with a 15m rolling sum; updated Predictive dashboard to show both series next to error metrics. Allison Grant (final): Approved after the legend cleanup and variable standardization. Rafael Mendes (final): Approved; please ensure prod folder naming matches our provisioning rules. Confirmed.
payload.title: Add Dedicated autoscaling bounds dashboards (desired vs bounded, queue depth, prediction error, scale events)

payload.body:
## Summary
Adds a packaged Grafana dashboard + alert rules for the Guided Onboarding / First Production Launch initiative.

This is intended to be imported via the standard `observability-pack` rollout (same mechanism as the latency/cost packs), and targets the onboarding telemetry datasets produced by the gateway/control plane eventing work + derived milestone tables.

## What’s included
Dashboard: **Onboarding KPIs (Hosted API)**
- TTFS (signup → first successful 2xx request) trend
  - Median / p90 / p95 by signup cohort
  - Breakdown by `sdk_language` (via user-agent tags), `region`, and `plan_tier`
- TTFP (signup → first production traffic) trend
  - Median / p90 by signup cohort
  - Includes optional filter for "prod_traffic" classifier (see notes below)
- Step completion funnel
  - % of tenants completing each checklist step (ordered)
  - Step-to-next-step conversion + time-in-step
  - Top drop-off steps (ranked)
- Drop-off reasons / first failure signals
  - First auth failure (401/403) rate by cohort
  - First 429 rate by cohort
  - First streaming disconnect signal rate (from gateway termination reasons)
- Data quality tiles
  - Event ingest freshness (minutes behind)
  - Missing required dimensions rate (null/unknown sdk_language/region)

Alerts (recommended; shipped disabled-by-default)
- **Onboarding KPI dataset freshness**
  - Triggers when `onboarding_events_v1` ingestion is > 30m behind for 2 consecutive evaluation windows
  - Also triggers when derived `tenant_onboarding_milestones` hasn’t updated in > 60m
- **Step drop-off spike**
  - Triggers when a step’s completion rate drops > 20% vs trailing 7d baseline (configurable)
  - Default scope is Hosted API + self-serve cohorts; enterprise/dedicated cohorts can be configured separately

## Data sources and metric definitions
This pack assumes the following tables/views exist in the central analytics workspace (names match the platform telemetry spec as of March 2025):
- `analytics.onboarding_events_v1` (raw / lightly normalized events)
- `analytics.tenant_onboarding_milestones_v1` (derived; 1 row per tenant with timestamps per step)

Metric definitions are aligned to PM-751:
- TTFS: `first_success_at - signup_at`
  - `first_success_at` is the first gateway 2xx for the canonical generate/chat endpoints, excluding health checks
- TTFP: `first_prod_traffic_at - signup_at`
  - `first_prod_traffic_at` is computed by downstream classifier (>= N requests over M minutes OR explicit "prod" tag). The dashboard supports both modes via a variable.

Important: the dashboard does **not** join to billing for these KPIs (to avoid the known usage dashboard lag issue). We only use billing-derived fields when available as optional breakdown dimensions.

## How to install
- `obs-pack apply onboarding-kpis`
- or import the JSON from `packs/onboarding-kpis/dashboards/onboarding_kpis_grafana.json`

After import, set variables:
- `environment` (prod/staging)
- `cohort_window` (default: last 8 weeks)
- `deployment_mode` (default: hosted)

## Screenshots
Attached in internal PR UI (Grafana panels: funnel + TTFS/TTFP timeseries + alert preview).

## Notes / limitations
- Step drop-off alerting uses a simple baseline comparison. This is intentionally conservative for MVP; we can add seasonality-aware detection once we see stable weekly traffic.
- `sdk_language` depends on OpenAI-compat user-agent tagging (redwood-openai-compat#265). If not present, values show as `unknown`.
- This PR ships Hosted API defaults; Dedicated/Private filters are stubbed but not surfaced in the default dashboard nav.

## Testing
- Validated queries against staging analytics (last 14d) and ensured panels render with empty-state handling.
- Dry-run the alert rules with `alerts.test_mode=true` to confirm routing/labels.
- Checked for cardinality regressions (no per-tenant series in alerts; tenant-level only in dashboard table panels).

## Rollout plan
- Merge behind pack version bump only (no automatic enablement).
- SRE/Telemetry will enable alerts for internal dogfood cohorts first (see ENG-5815).

## Checklist
- [x] Dashboard uses standard variable names and folder layout
- [x] Alerts are disabled by default and include runbook links
- [x] No PII fields referenced (tenant_id is only used in table panels and not emitted in alert labels)
- [x] Added docs for metric definitions and known caveats

Logan Wright: The drop-off alert query is grouping by `step_name` only, but the dashboard query includes `deployment_mode`. Can we make sure we don't page on Dedicated/Private noise before those cohorts are stable?
Allison Grant (author): Good call. I scoped the alert rules to `deployment_mode=hosted` by default and left deployment_mode as a dashboard variable only. Added a comment + override example in the alert YAML.
Mei Lin: TTFS definition should exclude `/v1/health` and internal console probes. Also, the time window for "first success" needs to be consistent with PM-751.
Allison Grant (author): Updated `ttfs_ttfp.sql` to filter to canonical generate/chat routes and `source != internal_probe`. Added a note referencing PM-751 and the exclusion list in the pack README.
Aisha Bello: Freshness threshold at 30m might be too tight given batch loads. Can we use 45m and require 2 eval windows?
Allison Grant (author): Adjusted to 30m but requiring 2 consecutive windows, and added a 60m guardrail for the derived milestones table. Also added guidance in the runbook for tuning in low-traffic regions.
Chris Osei: Please ensure alert labels don’t include tenant_id (cardinality + privacy). Dashboard table is fine, but alerts must not carry it.
Allison Grant (author): Confirmed: tenant_id only appears in dashboard table panels, and alert labels are limited to environment + step_name + deployment_mode. Added an explicit unit check in `packs/onboarding-kpis/alerts/` comments.
payload.title: Add onboarding KPIs dashboard (TTFS/TTFP + checklist funnel) and recommended alerts

payload.body:
Motivation: Usage Insights is going into beta with interactive console queries backed by hourly/day partitions and reconciliation checks against billing. We need a standard dashboard + alert bundle in observability-pack so SRE/on-call can quickly answer: (1) is data fresh, (2) are we dropping/late-ingesting events by route/model, (3) are we drifting vs billing totals beyond tolerance, and (4) are query endpoints timing out for common ranges.

This PR adds a Grafana dashboard and alert rule templates for freshness lag, late event rate, reconciliation drift, and query p95 latency. The dashboard is designed to be imported into customer-facing/internal stacks with minimal per-cluster edits (templated variables for env/region/deployment_mode/workspace_id).

What’s included: 1) Dashboard: “Usage Insights — Data Freshness & Quality” (Grafana JSON) Panels: Aggregation lag (p50/p95) by dataset (route_model_hourly, route_model_daily) and by region; Ingestion late-event ratio (late_events / total_events) by region + streaming endpoint flag; Missing route_tag rate (events where route_template = "unknown" or null); Reconciliation drift (%) between insights totals and billing hook totals, per workspace and overall; Top offenders table: workspaces with highest drift and highest lag; Query API p95 latency + error rate (v1/usage-insights/* endpoints) with annotations for deploys.

2) Alerts (PrometheusRule templates): - UsageInsightsAggregationLagHigh: fires when p95 aggregation lag > 20m for 15m (warn) and > 60m for 10m (page). - UsageInsightsLateEventRatioHigh: fires when late_event_ratio > 2% for 30m (warn), with a separate page threshold at 5% for 15m. - UsageInsightsRouteTagMissing: fires when missing_route_tag_rate > 1% for 30m (warn) and > 3% for 15m (page). - UsageInsightsReconciliationDriftHigh: fires when abs(drift_pct) > 0.5% for 2h (warn) and > 1.0% for 1h (page), excluding small totals (< $50/day) to reduce noise. - UsageInsightsQueryP95Degraded: fires when p95 > 2500ms for 15m (warn) and > 5000ms for 10m (page), scoped to the insights query service.

3) Runbook stub: Adds a runbook page with investigation steps and links to relevant services/datasets (warehouse partitions, ingestion pipeline, billing hook job).

Metric assumptions (coordinated with Telemetry/Analytics): This PR uses the metric names already in-flight on redwood (see ENG-3824/ENG-3817): usage_insights_aggregation_lag_seconds{dataset,region,deployment_mode}; usage_insights_late_event_ratio{region,streaming}; usage_insights_missing_route_tag_rate{region}; usage_insights_reconciliation_drift_pct{workspace_id}; usage_insights_query_request_duration_ms_bucket{route,status}; usage_insights_query_errors_total{route,status}. If any naming changes land before beta, we can follow up with a patch release of observability-pack.

Noise/guardrails: The drift alert includes a minimum spend floor and a 2h lookback to avoid paging on transient rounding/timing skew (e.g., hourly partitions catching up). The lag alert pages only on sustained lag > 60m.

Testing/validation: Imported dashboard into staging Grafana; validated queries on canary metrics in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Used replayed lag/drift fixtures from staging to verify alert routing and labels.

Rollout notes: This is safe to ship ahead of beta. SREs should import the dashboard to the internal "Console & Tooling" folder and ensure Alertmanager routes page severity=page to #eng-sre, and warn severity=warn to #eng-platform.

Screenshots: (not included in PR; Grafana JSON is the source of truth).
Allison Grant (review): Dashboard looks good. Can we add a panel for missing route tags specifically for streaming endpoints? We’ve seen region-specific gaps there.
Caleb Johnson (author): Added "Missing route_tag rate (streaming=true)" panel and tied it to the same variable set. Also added an alert that pages only above 3% missing tags to avoid noise.
Logan Wright (review): Drift alert should exclude low-volume workspaces; otherwise small rounding errors will trigger. Also please document tolerance assumptions.
Caleb Johnson (author): Added min_total_usd_per_day floor and documented drift tolerance + lookback in runbook. Alert now uses abs(drift_pct) with a 2h avg.
Cole Summers (review): For reconciliation, make sure the query uses the same rounding semantics (currency minor units) as billing hooks. Otherwise we’ll chase false positives.
Caleb Johnson (author): Updated description in runbook to call out minor-unit rounding and timing skew; dashboard panel now includes both raw drift and drift after rounding-to-cents (if metric exists).
Thomas Baird (review): Aggregation lag panel should show p95 and max; also group by dataset so we can tell hourly vs daily partitions at a glance.
Caleb Johnson (author): Done. Added p95 + max and grouped by dataset with a legend that includes region/deployment_mode.
Marcus Lin (review): Any sensitive labels? workspace_id in drift metrics can be sensitive depending on export path. For alerts, can we include workspace_id only on warn, not on page?
Caleb Johnson (author): Adjusted page-level drift alert to aggregate by env/region only (no workspace_id). Warn alert still includes workspace_id for triage. Added note in runbook about label hygiene.
payload.title: Add Usage Insights freshness/quality dashboard + alerts (lag + reconciliation drift)

payload.body:
Problem: Customers and SREs frequently need fast, contextual recommendations for query refinements and an operational playbook when an alert fires. Investigating token-level latency/cost spikes currently requires manual querying across traces, metrics, and slow ad-hoc runbooks.

Goal: Add a small, low-latency service that produces query hints (time/range filters, high-value labels, suggested aggregation windows) for common telemetry queries and synthesize a short, actionable alert playbook when a route/tenant crosses cost or latency thresholds. The service should be non-blocking, cached, and pluggable into the observability UI and CLI.

This PR implements: 1) telemetry/query-hint service that inspects recent metrics/traces and returns ranked hints for faster investigation; 2) alert-playbook-generator that maps common SLO breach patterns to a short checklist and recommended dashboard links; 3) UI panel and API endpoints to surface hints and playbooks; 4) small automation that attaches playbook snippets to newly created PagerDuty incidents.

Design notes: - Query-hint is heuristic-first (entropy and recent variance detectors) and uses a short rolling window (5m / 1h) to avoid stale suggestions. - Playbook rules are YAML-driven (configs under observability/playbooks/) so on-call can iterate without code changes. - All outputs include a provenance token to correlate hint->trace origin for audit/debugging.

Testing and rollout: - Feature gated behind observability.experimental.query_hints (off by default). - Integration tests run against the observability e2e harness. - Step rollout: internal canary -> beta tenants -> GA.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of hint engine and playbook generator
- [x] API + lightweight HTTP handler with auth checks
- [x] UI panel JSON and client wiring in observability console
- [x] Unit + integration tests (e2e)
- [x] Documentation: docs/observability/query-hints.md and playbook author guide
- [x] CI green and manual canary validation

Related: Linear ENG-2389 (query-hint engine), ENG-2390 (alert playbooks), internal runbook RFC: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2350/observability-playbook-rfc
1) Add query-hint core (telemetry/hint/engine.go + heuristics)
2) Playbook generator and YAML schemas (observability/playbooks/*.yml)
3) API handlers + tests (telemetry/api/hints_handler.go, telemetry/api/playbook_handler.go)
4) UI panel & wiring (ui/dashboards/query_hint_panel.json, ui/src/hooks/useQueryHints.ts)
5) Incident attachment automation (integrations/pagerduty/playbook_attacher.go)
6) Docs and tests
Diego Ramos (2025-08-20): 'Nice separation of heuristics vs rules. Can we add a short TTL for cached hints per tenant? I worry about stale suggestions.'
Nora Liu (reply 2025-08-21): 'Added per-tenant TTL (default 10m) and made it configurable via flags. See telemetry/hints/store.go changes.'
Priya Kothari (2025-08-24): 'Playbook YAML is great — can we add a sample for prefetched-warmup oscillation? Also feels like some of the rules might be noisy for low-volume tenants.'
Nora Liu (2025-08-25): 'Added prefeth-warmup sample and introduced a volume threshold config so playbooks only surface above X invocations in the last window.'
Ellen Moore (2025-08-28): 'Integration tests flaky in CI on the first run — looks like a race in mock trace ingestion.'
Nora Liu (2025-08-29): 'Fixed race by adding a retry-backed ingestion step in the test harness. CI re-run passing.'
Diego Ramos (approval 2025-09-01): 'Approving — tested canary, hints were actionable and the playbook linked to the right dashboards.'
Added telemetry query-hints service and alert-playbook-generator. Feature off-by-default behind experimental flag. Provides ranked query suggestions and one-page playbooks for common SLO breach patterns. See docs/observability/query-hints.md for usage and playbook authoring.
If an alert surfaces a generated playbook, the playbook will include a provenance token. Use /observability/query-hints?provenance=<token> to get the originating hints and traces. If hints appear noisy, disable observability.experimental.query_hints for the tenant and file ENG-2390.
Playbooks and hints may contain tenant identifiers; outputs are scrubbed to PII policy and the endpoint enforces tenant-scoped auth. PagerDuty attachments only include playbook snippets (no raw traces).
Toggle observability.experimental.query_hints=false to disable hint generation immediately. Revert deployment if PagerDuty attachments are misbehaving. Archived playbook configs are preserved in observability/playbooks/disabled/.
1) Enable feature flag for a test tenant. 2) Trigger synthetic SLO breach (use telemetry/test-harness). 3) Confirm hint panel shows 3 ranked suggestions and playbook link in console. 4) Verify PagerDuty incident includes playbook snippet. 5) Run e2e test suite: make target e2e-query-hints.

Context: This is part of the Lifecycle Growth Experiments sprint (Hosted API activation + early retention). We need a standardized, self-serve dashboard that answers: (1) where do new signups drop in the funnel, (2) which experiment cohorts/variants moved the needle, and (3) how do we catch regressions quickly after email/nudge/retargeting launches.

What’s included in this PR: Adds a set of activation funnel panels to the existing Growth/PLG dashboard pack and wires in suggested (disabled-by-default) alert rules. The dashboard focuses on signup -> API key created -> first successful request -> first 100k tokens within 7d, plus TTFT distributions.

Dashboard updates: - New row: “Activation funnel (new signups)” with conversion panels per step (absolute counts + rates), and a time series of overall activation_rate_7d (first_request within 7d of signup). - Breakdown panels: conversion by region, SDK (ts/python/rest), and experiment cohort (feature flag holdout vs treatment). - Variant drilldowns: email_variant_id, nudge_id, and utm_campaign (for retargeting) as optional breakdown dimensions (these are behind dashboard variables to avoid exploding cardinality by default). - Latency: p50/p95 TTFT for first successful request (filtered to first_request events only) with a note about sampling and outlier handling. - Data quality: panel that tracks event ingestion gaps (% missing region, % missing sdk) and a warning annotation if the dedupe-fix version hasn’t fully rolled out.

Suggested alerts (added as templates, not auto-enabled): - Activation regression: activation_rate_7d drops >15% vs 28d baseline for 2h (with minimum N guardrail). - Funnel step regression: api_key_created_rate and first_request_rate drops separately, to help localize which step is broken. - TTFT regression: p95 TTFT for first request increases >25% vs baseline (suppressed if volume is low).

Notes/assumptions: - Queries expect the standardized event taxonomy from ENG-10492 (signup/api_key_created/first_request/first_100k_tokens) and will be most accurate once the duplicate-event emission fix is fully deployed (see redwood hotfix PR referenced in ENG-10492 notes). - All breakdowns default to low-cardinality dimensions; high-cardinality drilldowns are opt-in via variables.

Testing: - jsonnet render + schema validation via `make dashboards` - alert rule linting via `make alerts-lint` - manual spot-check in Grafana: panels load under 2s for last 7d; breakdowns under 5s with variables enabled.

Rollout: No runtime impact. Once merged, dashboards ship with the next observability-pack sync. Alert templates require explicit enablement per env (stage/prod) and per oncall ownership.

Screenshots: included in the PR conversation (Grafana panel previews + variable dropdowns).
Allison Grant (review): Can we make it explicit that these alert rules are templates and not enabled by default? Also please rename “Activation (7d)” to “First request within 7d (activation)” to match the KPI doc.

Sergio Costa (author): Yep — updated alert README to call out disabled-by-default + added “enablement checklist” section. Renamed the panel + variable description to match KPI naming.

Logan Wright (review): The cohort breakdown should use `experiment_cohort` from the flag service, not inferred from timestamps. Otherwise holdouts drift when we re-run assignment.

Sergio Costa (author): Good catch. Switched cohort breakdown to `experiment_cohort` and added a fallback note (panel shows “unknown” if not present) so we notice if event properties are missing.

Mei Lin (review): Query perf: the `utm_campaign` breakdown can get heavy. Can we default it off and require enabling via variable?

Sergio Costa (author): Done — it’s now an opt-in variable, and the default breakdown panel uses region/sdk only.

Paula Mendes (review): Add a minimum-volume threshold for the regression alert, otherwise we’ll page on low-traffic hours.

Sergio Costa (author): Added `min_requests >= 200` guardrail and a note in the alert template.

Allison Grant (final): Approving. Please make sure the data quality panel includes % missing sdk + region (those are the two most common issues we’ve seen).

Sergio Costa (author): Added both; merged after green CI.

Summary: Adds first-pass dashboard panels for prefix/KV cache efficiency and supporting signals (eviction pressure + wasted prefill), and introduces conservative alert rules intended as guardrails during rollout. Motivation: With runtime instrumentation landing in the monorepo (cache hit/miss counters, eviction/pressure metrics, wasted prefill), SRE needs a standard triage surface to answer: (1) did hit-rate actually drop, (2) why, and (3) is it eviction/pressure vs config/policy vs workload mix. This PR is intentionally conservative on paging; most alerts are ticket-level until we tune against real workload patterns. What’s included (Dashboards): 1) Cache Efficiency Overview (new row): KV cache hit-rate (time series) with filters: deployment_mode, region, model_family, route_group; prefix cache reuse effectiveness (reused_tokens / prefill_tokens) as both time series and heatmap by prompt_length_bucket; cache miss reason breakdown (stacked area) using miss_reason allowlist (capacity, ttl_expired, policy_disabled, hash_mismatch, version_mismatch, unknown); wasted prefill ratio (wasted_prefill_tokens / prefill_tokens) with request-volume gating annotation. 2) Eviction & Pressure (new row): KV cache eviction rate (evictions/s) with eviction_reason breakdown where available; memory pressure gauges for KV/prefix caches (normalized 0..1) and “time in pressure” indicator; “top contributors” table by route_group and model_family for high wasted prefill (kept to aggregated dimensions to avoid cardinality blowups). What’s included (Alerts): - cache_hit_rate_drop_guardrail: fires when KV hit-rate drops below 0.35 for 30m AND req_count > 5000 in the same window; severity=ticket; includes label set limited to {deployment_mode, region, model_family}. - cache_eviction_pressure_high: fires when pressure > 0.90 for 15m with eviction_rate > 10/s; severity=ticket; intended to flag memory pressure events that correlate with latency and cache churn. - wasted_prefill_spike: fires when wasted_prefill_ratio > 0.55 for 30m AND prefill_tokens_total > 5e6; severity=ticket; this is a noisy metric early on, so threshold is intentionally high. Notes on cardinality and joinability: This PR only slices on stable/low-cardinality dimensions (deployment_mode, region, model_family, route_group) and does not include per-tenant identifiers. Route-level is represented as route_group (gateway-level grouping) until ingestion-side cardinality guards (PR #613) are fully rolled out. Dependencies / Links: - Runtime metrics: redwood PRs #18421/#18422/#18423/#18424/#18430/#18431 (naming alignment) - Sampling/rate limits: redwood PR #18425 - Context propagation: redwood PR #18426 - Cardinality guards: observability-pack PR #613 (follow-up) - Linear: ENG-4824 (dashboards/alerts), ENG-4821 (metric definitions/tags) Testing: - jsonnetfmt + dashboard compilation (CI) - promtool rule validation (CI) - Local render against staging datasource config to verify queries return series (manual) Rollout plan: - Merge behind existing folder structure; dashboards disabled by default in prod until the runtime flag is enabled. - Once runtime telemetry is on in canary, SRE will validate panels for 48h and then enable global dashboard navigation link. - Alerts remain ticket-level until Aisha/Allison tune based on diurnal patterns and workload mix; paging policy explicitly out of scope for this PR.
Allison Grant (review): Queries look good, but we need to ensure we’re not slicing by raw route_id anywhere. Please use route_group only and add a comment in the dashboard var definition about the allowlist.
Sergio Costa (author): Updated templating to route_group only; added comment + removed route_id var from the WIP panel.

Aisha Bello (review): The hit-rate alert will flap if traffic is low. Can we gate on request volume and use a longer window?
Sergio Costa (author): Added req_count > 5k for 30m; window now 30m. Also set severity=ticket.

Sean Gallagher (review): Please avoid paging. Confirm these go to ticket routing only and don’t map to oncall pager.
Sergio Costa (author): Confirmed; alert labels include severity=ticket and routed to #eng-sre-triage in Alertmanager config (no pager).

Logan Wright (review): Miss reason breakdown should match the runtime miss_reason enum. Add unknown bucket and don’t assume version_mismatch exists everywhere yet.
Sergio Costa (author): Added unknown bucket and query uses label_replace to coerce missing miss_reason to unknown.

Allison Grant (final): Approved with note: once PR #613 lands we can safely add a limited route_group top-k table panel. For now keep it behind an “experimental” row.
Sergio Costa (author): Marked the table row as experimental + added note in alerts/cache/README.md.
New: Cache Efficiency dashboard panels (KV hit-rate, prefix reuse, wasted prefill, miss reasons).
New: Eviction & Pressure dashboard panels for cache pressure and eviction rate.
New: Ticket-level guardrail alerts for cache hit-rate drops, high eviction pressure, and wasted prefill spikes.

## Summary Adds an integration test that drives repeated prompts through the real prefill/decode request path and asserts that cache metrics move in the expected direction (miss on first request, hit/partial hit on subsequent requests). This is meant to be a guardrail against regressions in hit attribution (especially around continuous batching and request retries) and to validate the metric wiring end-to-end (runtime -> metrics recorder).  ## Motivation Unit tests validate individual counters/histograms, but we’ve already hit a few integration-level failure modes during implementation (metrics not tagged due to missing context, counters double-counted across retries, test-only metric registry not isolated). This adds a single “golden path” integration test that is deterministic and cheap to run in CI.  ## What the test does - Spins up the runtime integration harness with cache enabled and telemetry sampling forced to 1.0 for the test process. - Uses a fixed model fixture (small, deterministic) and a fixed prompt seed so tokenization is stable. - Executes a sequence: (1) request A (baseline miss), (2) identical request A (expected hit), (3) request A with a small suffix (expected partial hit / reuse), (4) request B (new prefix, expected miss). - Captures metrics from the in-process metrics sink and asserts:   - `cache.kv.requests_total{result="miss"}` increments on the first request, then `result="hit"` increments on the second identical request.   - Miss reason taxonomy is populated (for the baseline miss we assert `reason="cold"` or `reason="not_found"` depending on build flags; see notes below).   - Prefix reuse histogram has non-zero count on the suffix case (we don’t assert exact bucket, only that a reuse observation was recorded and reused_tokens > 0).   - No double counting on the retry path: the test can optionally enable one forced retry; we assert counters only increment once per logical request when `x-redwood-retry-attempt` is present.  ## Implementation notes - Introduces a `TestMetricsRecorder` that plugs into the existing metrics facade and exports a snapshot for assertions. This avoids scraping Prometheus in CI and avoids high-cardinality label assertions. - Test explicitly disables background flush timers and uses a synchronous flush hook before reading the snapshot to remove timing flakiness. - Uses coarse assertions (delta-based) and avoids asserting on model/route labels to keep the test stable while tag allowlists evolve.  ## CI/Perf - Adds ~0.8s to the runtime integration test suite on my laptop, ~1.4s in CI (cold). - No production code path changes beyond a small test-only constructor wiring under `#[cfg(test)]`.  ## Checklist - [x] Deterministic (no wall-clock sleeps; explicit flush) - [x] No raw prompt logging in test output (only prompt id and token counts) - [x] Validates both hit/miss and at least one “reuse depth” signal - [x] Works with continuous batching enabled in CI config  ## Follow-ups - We should add a second test case for batched prefill hit attribution once PR-18433 lands; this test is intentionally single-threaded to be deterministic. - Once metric names are finalized via naming standards, we can tighten the assertions to match the final names (right now we reference the runtime facade constants to avoid brittle string matches).
Omar El-Sayed (review): This is the right shape. Two asks: (1) please avoid asserting specific miss reason values until the taxonomy stabilizes; we’ve got ongoing debate in #eng-runtime. (2) make sure this doesn’t rely on background export intervals — we’ve been burned by flakes.
Samir Qureshi (author): Good call. Updated to assert only that exactly one miss reason label is present (non-empty) and that total miss count increments by 1. Also added `flush_metrics_for_test()` and removed the `sleep(200ms)` I originally had.
Nadia Rahman (review): Can you ensure the test doesn’t introduce per-request labels in the snapshot (prompt hash, request id, etc.)? We’ve got cardinality guards coming on the ingestion side; we shouldn’t normalize on those labels in runtime tests either.
Samir Qureshi (author): Confirmed we only read the aggregate counters emitted by the runtime facade (no request id labels). The `TestMetricsRecorder` drops unknown labels by default and will fail the test if a forbidden label key shows up.
Noah Patel (review): One more thing: the second identical request may still miss if the harness tears down the model between calls. I think your harness resets state on each request right now. Please double check it’s reusing the same runtime instance and cache.
Samir Qureshi (author): Great catch — the harness was creating a fresh engine per request in this test. Fixed to keep a single runtime instance for the whole test and added a comment explaining why.
Sofia Ivanova (review): This is fine from scheduling’s perspective. Thanks for keeping it single-threaded. Approving as long as we don’t pin exact bucket indices for reuse depth (those change as we tune buckets).
Omar El-Sayed (approval): LGTM after the flush + harness reuse fix. This should protect us against the retry/double-counting class of bugs.

Summary: This PR adds the first version of the retention/compliance dashboards and alerting rules needed for the “Retention controls + compliance reporting pack” program. It introduces (1) Retention Enforcement Verification dashboards (TTL lag, purge throughput/failures, backlog) and (2) Compliance Report Pack Generation SLIs (success rate + latency) with corresponding alerts. It also updates the repo README to document metric prerequisites and rollout guidance.

Context / why: We’ve had multiple incidents/tickets where enforcement was “working” but not observable at the right level (e.g., policy applied but TTL lag growing in a single region; purge jobs silently throttling after maintenance). Security/GRC also needs a customer-ready way to evidence enforcement (at least internally) and to demonstrate the compliance pack generator’s reliability as we start using it for enterprise security reviews.

What’s included:
- Dashboards:
  - “Retention Controls: Verification (Overview)”
    - TTL lag (p50/p90/p99) by store + region
    - Purge throughput (rows deleted / min) and runtime
    - Purge failures (rate + top error reasons when exported)
    - Backlog / lag trend line for the last 7d
  - “Retention Controls: Purge Jobs (Deep Dive)”
    - Per-job panels (request-logs, audit-logs, traces, metrics, artifacts where applicable)
    - Retry volume + idempotent re-run indicators (based on job outcome labels)
  - “Compliance Pack: Generation SLI/SLO”
    - SLI: report_pack_generation_success_rate (derived)
    - Latency: report_pack_generation_duration_seconds (p50/p90/p99)
    - Queue/backlog (if enabled) and saturation signals
- Alerts (Prometheus rules):
  - RetentionTTLTooHigh (warning/page)
    - Warning: ttl_lag_seconds{store=~"request_logs|audit_logs"} p99 > 6h for 30m
    - Page: p99 > 24h for 15m (per region) OR backlog increasing for 60m
  - RetentionPurgeFailuresHigh (page)
    - purge_failures_total increase > 10 in 15m per job_type/region
  - RetentionPurgeNoProgress (warning)
    - purge_rows_deleted_total no increase for 2h while ttl_lag_seconds p90 > 2h
  - CompliancePackGenerationSLOViolation (warning/page)
    - Warning: success rate < 99.5% over 1h
    - Page: success rate < 98% over 30m OR p90 duration > 15m over 1h
- README updates:
  - Documents required metrics + labels (store, region, job_type, tenant_tier)
  - Notes on cardinality: alerts intentionally avoid tenant_id; dashboards allow optional filtering but default views are store/region only
  - Rollout instructions: enable dashboards first, then alerts at warning-only for 1 week before paging

Metric dependencies (expected to exist from the product/runtime PRs):
- ttl_lag_seconds{store,region}
- purge_rows_deleted_total{store,region,job_type}
- purge_failures_total{store,region,job_type,reason?}
- purge_job_duration_seconds{store,region,job_type}
- report_pack_generation_duration_seconds{region,outcome}
- report_pack_generation_total{region,outcome}

Implementation notes:
- Alert thresholds were chosen to match SRE guidance in the retention purge runbook: lag > 24h is a customer-impacting condition (policy drift / failure to meet retention), while shorter lags are warning signals that typically correlate with DB throttling or a stuck worker.
- We added a small “debug” row in the deep-dive dashboard for correlating lag spikes to purge job runtime, failures, and DB maintenance windows (annotation placeholder; actual annotation source is separate).
- Dashboards follow the existing Jsonnet conventions in this repo; panel UIDs are stable and include ‘retention-*’ prefixes for easy lookup.

Testing:
- Rendered dashboards locally (make dashboards) and validated against a staging Prometheus snapshot.
- promtool rule checks pass.
- Verified that rule expressions don’t use tenant_id and don’t blow up cardinality with region x store x job_type only.

Rollout plan:
- Ship dashboards immediately (safe).
- Enable alerts in warning-only in staging for 1 week; then promote to production warning-only for 1 week; then turn on paging routes.

References:
- Linear: ENG-18452 (verification dashboards/alerts), PM-842 (initiative), ENG-18441 (report pack generator)
- Related product metrics PRs: redwood/pr-28540-add-retention-verification-metrics, audit-log-exporter/pr-612-add-time-windowed-exports-and-filters

Screenshots: Added to the README section “Retention & Compliance Dashboards” (rendered preview images) and attached in the PR for review.
Sean Gallagher (SRE): The dashboard looks good, but we should avoid any alert dimensions that could explode cardinality. Please confirm no tenant_id usage anywhere in rule expressions. Also, can we add a “no progress” alert? That would have caught the post-maintenance backlog we saw last week.

Allison Grant (author): Confirmed: no tenant_id in any rule. Dashboards have tenant_tier as an optional filter but rules are strictly store/region/job_type. Added RetentionPurgeNoProgress (warning) based on ‘rows deleted’ not increasing while lag is elevated.

Logan Wright (Telemetry): For ttl_lag_seconds, some stores won’t emit p99 depending on scrape interval; please use histogram_quantile on the bucket metric where available, or fall back to max over time. Right now it looks like you’re assuming precomputed p99.

Allison Grant: Good catch. Updated rules to use histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le,store,region)(rate(ttl_lag_seconds_bucket[5m]))) where the bucket exists; added a compatibility path guarded by recording rules in lib/metrics/retention.libsonnet. README updated to note both options.

Nadia Rahman (Observability): Can we standardize the panel naming to match the rest of the pack (“Overview / Deep Dive / SLO”) and add tags so they show up in search?

Allison Grant: Renamed dashboards and added tags: [retention, compliance, security, verification].

Kevin Osei (Retention/Audit exports): For compliance pack, I’d like an explicit panel for ‘percent generated within 15m’ since that’s what we’ll be quoting to GRC. Also, please keep the alert window >= 30m to avoid paging during deploys.

Allison Grant: Added “<=15m” SLI panel and kept paging criteria at 30m/1h windows.

Sean Gallagher: Approved once you flip the initial paging severity to warning-only (we’ll route to #oncall-retention for the first week).

Allison Grant: Done. Paging labels are present but default route config is warning-only; README includes staged enablement steps.

Approvals:
- Sean Gallagher: Approved
- Logan Wright: Approved
- Nadia Rahman: Approved
Observability-pack now includes Grafana dashboards and Prometheus alert rules for retention enforcement verification and compliance report pack generation SLIs; README documents prerequisites and rollout guidance.
