Context: As part of the cross-language SDK parity rollout (standard retries/backoff, timeout model, and streaming disconnect handling), SRE requested first-class dashboards and conservative alerts to monitor load impact and customer-facing failure rates during beta/stable releases. This PR adds (1) new panels to the existing "SDK Client Health" Grafana dashboard for retry rate, timeout rate, and streaming disconnect reasons, (2) companion alert rules with rollout-friendly thresholds and burn-rate style paging, and (3) a small set of recording rules to make the queries cheaper/consistent across environments.

What’s included: - Dashboard panels: Retry rate (by sdk_language, endpoint, model, status_code), Retry attempts distribution (p50/p95 of retry_count per request), Timeout rate (by sdk_language, timeout_scope=overall|connect|read), Timeout duration (histogram heatmap where available), Streaming disconnect rate (by sdk_language, endpoint, reason), Top streaming disconnect reasons (table), and a rollout view grouped by sdk_version (when the label is present). - Alerts (disabled-by-default in prod, enabled in beta + dogfood): (A) High SDK retry rate (warn), (B) High SDK timeout rate (warn), (C) Streaming disconnect spike (warn), (D) Potential retry storm indicator (page) using (retry_total / request_total) + 429 rate + concurrency as gates. - Recording rules: pre-aggregate sdk_client_request_total, sdk_client_retry_total, sdk_client_timeout_total, sdk_client_stream_disconnect_total into 5m rate series with a bounded label set.

Metrics used (existing / recently standardized fields): - sdk_client_request_total{sdk_language, sdk_version?, endpoint, model, status_code} - sdk_client_retry_total{sdk_language, endpoint, reason} - sdk_client_timeout_total{sdk_language, endpoint, timeout_scope} - sdk_client_stream_disconnect_total{sdk_language, endpoint, reason} - sdk_client_request_duration_seconds_bucket (optional; used when emitted)

Notes / assumptions: - Streaming disconnect reasons follow the parity taxonomy being rolled out in SDKs (e.g., server_fin, read_timeout, client_cancel, proxy_reset, tls_error, unknown). Panels will still render if reason is missing (falls into reason="unknown" in the dashboards). - To avoid alert noise from a small number of clients, alerts include a minimum volume gate (requests_per_min) and are scoped to the rollout dashboards folder. - This PR intentionally does NOT add new instrumentation; it only consumes the standardized fields being added in the SDK repos. If a given SDK release doesn’t yet include sdk_version label, the dashboard will still work (the sdk_version view will simply be empty).

Rollout plan: - Merge now; ship to dogfood + beta monitoring stacks. - Enable alerts in beta immediately; keep prod alerts muted until stable releases are out (target: after ENG-5131 go/no-go). - During the first week of stable: watch retry_rate, timeout_rate, and disconnect_reason mix for proxy_reset/read_timeout regressions; use request_id sampling from SDK logs to correlate.

Testing: - Rendered dashboards via jsonnet/grafonnet compile locally; validated queries against staging Prometheus with synthetic load. - Ran alert rule unit tests (promtool) with fixtures covering 429 spikes and elevated read timeouts.

Screenshots: Included in the PR conversation (Grafana panels: Retry rate by language, Streaming disconnect reasons table).

Follow-ups: - Add a dedicated panel for Retry-After compliance once the gateway header adoption is >90% (separate PR). - Consider a dashboard annotation hook for SDK release cut times (Connor coordinating in ENG-RELEASES).

2026-02-04 Allison Grant: Query feedback: "For retry rate, can we normalize by request volume and avoid status_code label on the top-level chart to reduce cardinality? Also suggest splitting timeouts by timeout_scope and keeping endpoint grouping to a short allowlist." 
2026-02-04 Nadia Rahman: Ack. Updated panels to: (1) default view aggregates status_code, with a drilldown panel for status_code, (2) timeout_scope split panels, (3) endpoint variable defaults to top 20 by traffic.

2026-02-06 Nadia Rahman: Confirmed we’re consuming sdk_client_retry_total (not retry_count) and that retry_count is derived as a per-request distribution only when the histogram is available; added README note about label hygiene + no secrets.

Summary: This PR adds the first versioned "Failover Signals & Outcomes" observability bundle to observability-pack. The bundle includes (1) Grafana dashboards (JSON) for diagnosing region-level impairment vs. local/service-level issues, and (2) Prometheus/Alertmanager rule groups for fast-detection burn-rate paging + non-paging early-warning signals. The intent is to support the Regional Failover Automation Upgrade (ENG-2411) by giving on-call deterministic visibility into the trigger hierarchy signals and the automation controller’s behavior (recommendations, executions, rollbacks).

What’s included: Dashboards: failover-signals-overview.json (top-level entry): reachability probe success rate and p95/p99 latency by region pair; 5xx and timeout burn (fast/slow windows); tail latency burn for key API routes; capacity headroom (fleet available vs. target) and "capacity gating" state; automation controller action rate (recommend/execute/rollback) and per-tenant safety limit hits; policy flip history with dashboard annotations (from audit events) to correlate with spikes; API gateway overload responses (429/503 w/ Retry-After) to validate graceful degradation behavior. hosted-api-failover-drilldown.json: route/model slice panels (kept intentionally low-cardinality) plus request volume shifts during failover. dedicated-drain-progress.json: drain state, queued in-flight requests, and drain completion percent (hooked to new drain progress metrics emitted in redwood PR-19842).

Alert rules: rules/failover_burn_rate.yaml: Multi-window, multi-burn alerts for region impairment (fast: 2m/10m, slow: 30m/2h) across 5xx+timeouts, aligned to the multi-region availability SLO measurement approach. The goal is quick detection without noisy flaps; each alert includes runbook_url and dashboard_url annotations. rules/failover_reachability.yaml: Pages only when synthetic cross-region probes fail AND error/latency corroboration indicates likely regional impact (prevents false positives from probe-only issues). rules/failover_controller_health.yaml: Non-paging warning for missing signal streams / stale region health ingestion, plus paging on controller crashloop or sustained decision evaluation errors.

Important implementation notes: Label/cardinality constraints: Dashboards and rules assume the reduced failover_reason/trigger_source label set from redwood PR-19829. This PR intentionally does NOT add any new high-cardinality dimensions. Where we need per-tenant visibility, we use (a) sampled logs links and (b) controller audit events with tenant identifiers in the event payload (not as metric labels). Annotations: Adds an annotation datasource/query template that reads failover audit events (recommend/execute/rollback) so timelines are visible on signal charts. This addresses INT-1149 (missing annotations during rehearsal) and makes postmortems easier to write.

Rollout/versioning: Version tag: failover-pack v2026.01.0 (directory naming + dashboard UID prefixes). Staging rollout: enable in staging first; confirm panels populate for us-east <-> eu-west, validate burn alerts in "recording" mode (no paging) for 24h. Production rollout: enable dashboards immediately; keep the two fastest burn alerts in paging mode only after go/no-go checklist confirms (a) region health ingestion stable and (b) probe data present. A toggle is provided via alert routing labels to direct to #oncall-sre-nopage during initial bake. Backward compatibility: If audit event stream is unavailable, dashboards degrade gracefully (annotations empty). If dedicated drain metrics are not present, the Dedicated dashboard panels show "no data" without errors.

Files/areas changed (high level): dashboards/failover/failover-signals-overview.json; dashboards/failover/hosted-api-failover-drilldown.json; dashboards/failover/dedicated-drain-progress.json; alerts/failover/rules/failover_burn_rate.yaml; alerts/failover/rules/failover_reachability.yaml; alerts/failover/rules/failover_controller_health.yaml; docs/rollout-notes/failover-pack-v2026.01.0.md; dashboards/_shared/annotation-templates/failover-audit-events.json.

Validation: Imported dashboards into staging Grafana and verified queries against staging metrics for the region health service + perf canary probe series. Ran promtool check for rule syntax; simulated burn alerts by replaying a short window of elevated 5xx in a test environment. CI: lint + jsonnet formatting + promtool passed.

Related: ENG-2418 (Add failover metrics and SLO burn alerts), ENG-2421 (Game day 1), redwood PR-19816 (SLO-friendly aggregations), redwood PR-19824 (audit events), perf-canary PR-188 (cross-region reachability probes), redwood PR-19829 (metric label cardinality reduction).

Review notes: Allison requested we split paging vs. non-paging signals; done by separating rule groups and adding routing labels + explicit severity guidance. Aisha requested we align burn windows with SLO reporting; updated to match the standard fast/slow burn approach and added recording rules for regional availability burn. Miles requested the trigger hierarchy be readable from the dashboard top row; added a "signal stack" row with reachability -> 5xx -> latency -> capacity, plus links to the runbook. Tomáš requested clearer runbook ownership and a single canonical dashboard link; added runbook_url and dashboard_url to all alerts.

Changelog (squash): 1) Add initial dashboards (signals overview, hosted drilldown) 2) Add burn-rate rules + annotations 3) Add dedicated drain progress dashboard 4) Tune queries + thresholds; add rollout notes; promtool + uid fixes.

Outcome: Merged. Ready to deploy to staging immediately; production enablement pending go/no-go approval for the controlled failover window.
Adds versioned dashboard pack and alert rules for regional failover automation: signal panels (reachability, 5xx burn, tail latency burn, capacity headroom, policy flips/rollbacks) and outcome panels (failover time-to-mitigate, request shedding, Dedicated drain progress). Introduces multi-window burn-rate alerts for region impairment detection with annotations tuned for on-call triage. Includes rollout notes for staging -> prod enablement ahead of Q1 controlled failover game day.

Context: Redwood rollouts now evaluate SLO signals (latency/error burn-rate + staleness) and can auto-pause/auto-rollback. We need first-class operator visibility and sane alerts before enabling this broadly in production. This PR adds Grafana dashboards and Prometheus alert rules for auto-rollback outcomes (triggered/paused/suppressed), monitor coverage & staleness, and a per-service rollout health view. Dashboards: (1) Rollout Safety — Overview: shows decision volume and rate, breakdown by service/route/model_version/region/tier, and top suppress reasons; includes a panel for “monitor missing/stale” to catch the most common gap from game day/postmortems. (2) Rollout Safety — Rollout Detail: scoped to rollout_id; shows decision timeline + links to rollout controller logs and SLO monitor ids (via labels). (3) Rollout Safety — Service Health: operators pick service + route; shows request volume, p95/p99, error rate, burn-rate status (fast/slow windows), and decision outcomes overlaid. Alerts: (A) RedwoodAutoRollbackTriggered (severity=page) fires when rollback is executed for a production tier and not suppressed; pages SRE and notifies service channel (routing via labels: service/team). (B) RedwoodAutoRollbackPaused (severity=notify) for auto-pause outcomes (default notify only, per PM MVP). (C) RedwoodAutoRollbackSuppressed (severity=notify) for suppress actions (admin override / suppression window) so oncall can validate intent and duration. (D) RolloutSLOMonitorStale (severity=notify) when the monitor adapter reports stale data for the rollout scope beyond threshold (default 10m) OR the evaluation pipeline hasn’t produced fresh samples; includes staleness reason label (telemetry_lag|adapter_error|no_samples). (E) RolloutSLOMonitorMissing (severity=notify) when a rollout is configured for SLO-driven actions but no eligible monitor exists for the scope (route/model_version/region/tier) for >15m. Notes/guardrails: uses low-cardinality labels only; rollout_id is only used in dashboards (templated via ad-hoc filters) and is NOT used in alert grouping keys to avoid paging storms. Alerts group by service, route, region, customer_tier. Also adds a short README section describing routing + how to validate monitors before enabling auto-rollback (ties to release gating work). Follow-ups: once PR-477 in incident-bot is live everywhere, we can switch the notify-only alerts to Slack-only with deep links; for now we keep Prometheus alerts as the primary signal for oncall and use Slack notifications as secondary.
Allison Grant: Dashboard variables look good, but please avoid alerting on rollout_id directly; we can’t page on high-cardinality labels. Also align naming with the rollouts SLO metrics standard (decision outcome labels).
Aisha Bello (author): Ack. I removed rollout_id from all alert grouping/labels and kept it dashboard-only (ad-hoc filter). Also updated panels to use outcome={rollback|pause|suppress} and suppression_reason per the standard; pushed 3f2b7e1.
Sean Gallagher: Severity: I’m OK paging for actual rollback execution in prod tiers, but auto-pause should be notify-only. Also add an annotation with the suggested first steps + link to the new runbook section (Confluence path is fine).
Aisha Bello (author): Done. Paused is notify-only, triggered rollback is page only when customer_tier!=dev and suppressed!=true. Added annotations with triage steps and links to sources/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/auto-rollback-on-slo-breach-runbook.json and the incident playbook section; pushed 8a9c0d4.
Logan Wright: For staleness, can we distinguish “no samples” from adapter failing? That helps oncall decide whether to treat as rollout risk vs telemetry outage. Also prefer a longer stale threshold (10m) to avoid noise during brief telemetry delays.
Aisha Bello (author): Added staleness_reason label (telemetry_lag|adapter_error|no_samples) and tuned default threshold to 10m. Also added a separate low-severity alert for adapter_error spikes that routes to #eng-platform-telemetry; pushed 0c1f6aa.
Caleb Johnson: Recording rules should pre-aggregate by service/route/region/tier; avoid model_version unless needed. Some panels were grouping on model_version by default which can get noisy. Suggest making model_version optional via a dashboard toggle.
Aisha Bello (author): Updated recording rules to aggregate without model_version by default; model_version breakdown is now a panel-level optional query and off by default. Also added a dashboard note about cardinality; pushed 5e77b12.
Rafael Mendes: Please include alert routing labels (team/service) so paging goes to the right oncall rotation, and add a “Top affected services (last 24h)” panel to the overview for game day.
Aisha Bello (author): Added routing labels (team, service) to the alerts (team sourced from existing service metadata map in observability-pack), plus Top affected services panel. Also added a short section in docs on how to update service->team mapping; pushed 2db3a3e.
Allison Grant: Approved after last push. This is consistent with the standards and won’t explode cardinality.
Sean Gallagher: Approved. Let’s monitor alert noise closely during staged enablement and adjust if needed.
Adds Rollout Safety dashboards and alerting for auto-rollback/pause/suppress outcomes and monitor staleness/missing coverage. Paging only for executed rollbacks in production tiers; others notify-only.

Adds tiered SLO dashboards (Hosted + Dedicated) with a comparison view, plus deploy/incident annotations for faster correlation during budget burn.
Summary: This PR adds a tiered SLO dashboard set to the observability-pack, including (1) Hosted SLO overview, (2) Dedicated SLO overview (tier-wide; no customer-level by default), and (3) a Dedicated vs Hosted comparison view. It also adds Grafana annotations for deploys and incidents so we can correlate latency spikes / streaming disconnects / 5xx bursts with changes and incident timelines. Motivation: Part of the Q1 reliability milestone to formalize tiered SLOs + error budgets, we need canonical, tier-aware views that match the new SLI tagging at ingress and avoid metric cardinality blowups. This PR is intended to be the “default” internal dashboard surface linked from burn-rate alerts and runbooks. Out of scope: customer-facing Dedicated per-account dashboards and access control (tracked in ENG-4946 follow-ups) and any changes to SLI definitions/recording rules (those land in the monorepo + telemetry repos). Dependencies/assumptions: Requires tier/deployment mode labels to be present on the primary request/latency/streaming metrics (see redwood PR-28411) and burn-rate recording rules to exist (redwood PR-28492). Key changes: (A) New dashboards: 1) SLO Overview — Hosted (tier=hosted, region filter, endpoint_class filter; panels for availability/success rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, streaming disconnect rate, and top contributors by endpoint_class + region). 2) SLO Overview — Dedicated (tier=dedicated; same core panels; includes headroom hints panel that links to fleet dashboards but does not embed per-customer dimensions). 3) SLO Compare — Hosted vs Dedicated (side-by-side availability, latency percentiles, and streaming reliability; uses a shared time range + shared region selection; intended for incident review and target negotiation with PM). (B) Annotation tracks: “Deploys” annotation fed by deploy event series (redwood_deploy_events_total + build SHA label, aggregated to avoid per-service noise), “Incidents” annotation fed by incident-bot exported events (incident_events_total) with severity and incident_id, and a “Budget burn state” annotation derived from burn-rate alert firing series for quick visual overlay. (C) Dashboard conventions: standard variables (region, endpoint_class, tier), consistent SLO links in panel descriptions, and a top-of-dashboard note on SLI exclusions (invalid requests, explicit rate limits, client aborts) to reduce confusion when support/PM teams compare dashboards with raw logs. (D) Cardinality guardrails: no per-model and no per-account breakdowns in the default dashboard; top contributors are capped to N=10 and use endpoint_class + route_group only (route_group is derived/normalized by recording rules). A hidden “__debug” toggle exists for SRE-only use to reveal model breakdown if the underlying metrics are safe; default is off. Validation: ran grafana-lint + jsonnet compilation; loaded dashboards into staging Grafana and verified variables resolve for us-east-1/eu-west-1; spot-checked that streaming disconnect panel does not include client aborts per current metric taxonomy. Screenshots: included in the PR conversation (staging links). Rollout: once merged, this pack is picked up by the weekly observability-pack sync job; SRE will pin alert runbook links to the new dashboard UIDs after deploy.
Allison Grant (review): Can we avoid any dependency on per-route raw labels? I’m worried about cardinality if folks start adding route=… panels ad hoc. Also, please add a short note in the dashboard about SLI exclusions (rate limited, invalid, client abort) so Support doesn’t misinterpret the gap vs access logs.
Sergio Costa (author): Good call. I switched all “top contributors” panels to use route_group (normalized) and added the SLI exclusions note + links to the SLI spec. Also added a hard cap topk(10) and set the default to endpoint_class only.
Thomas Baird (review): The deploy annotation query is grouping by service + sha; that can still get noisy in multi-service rollouts. Can we aggregate to a single event per environment and show sha in the annotation text instead?
Sergio Costa (author): Updated: deploy annotations now reduce to env+sha (and include service list as truncated text). Also added a 15m dedupe window so repeated deploy events don’t spam.
Aisha Bello (review): The streaming disconnect panel should explicitly exclude client aborts (we’ve had confusion on SUP-28501). Do we have a metric split we can rely on, or do we need to call that out as a known limitation?
Sergio Costa (author): The panel now uses stream_disconnects_total{reason!="client_abort"} and includes a tooltip note. If the reason label is missing, it will show as “unknown” and still count; that’s consistent with current SLI guidance. Added a link to the runbook section on classifying disconnects.
Felix Schneider (review): Comparison dashboard looks good, but can we align the time series colors across Hosted/Dedicated so screenshots don’t get confusing? Also add an explicit “Tier” legend label.
Sergio Costa (author): Done: hosted is always blue, dedicated always green, and legend labels are prefixed with the tier string.
Logan Wright (review): Please ensure the dashboards still render if burn-rate recording rules aren’t present (some regions lag during rollout).
Sergio Costa (author): Added “or vector(0)” fallback for burn panels and a banner panel that warns when the recording rule series is absent in the selected region/time range.

payload.body:
Context: recent incidents (SUP-4021) highlighted that prefetch/warmup heuristics sometimes increase tail cost without meaningful latency improvement for some prompt shapes.

This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: 1) the prefetch-impact-radar — an observability pipeline + dashboard that correlates prefetch delta signals (prefetch hits/false-warms, KV warm counts) against per-invocation token cost and per-stage latency spectra; and 2) an SLO prognostics simulator that projects SLO hit-rate under alternative prefetch/autotune policies so oncall and SRE can reason about tradeoffs before changing policies.

What changed (high level):
- trace-processor: add PrefetchDeltaAggregator that tags spans with prefetch_outcome and warm_affinity scores and emits new metrics (prefetch.delta.count, prefetch.false_warm_ratio, prefetch.warm_affinity_p90)
- metrics: add Prometheus rules and histograms for token_cost_prefetch_bucket and stage_latency_prefetch_split
- dashboards: new "Prefetch Impact Radar" panel group showing cross-correlation heatmaps, per-tenant drift glyphs, and a prognostics control to run scenario simulations
- alerts/playbook: add a playbook entry and a tuned alert (prefetch-impact-high-cost) that uses the simulator to veto noisy alerts and suggests mitigation steps
- sampling: introduce a lightweight prefetched-trace sampler that biases retention towards traces with prefetch delta > 0 to reduce noise and retain signal for evaluation

Motivation: give platform teams a way to quantify whether prefetch warms are actually reducing application-level latency per token (and where they are harmful), and to simulate SLO outcomes before flipping runtime prefetch/autotune knobs. This reduces alert churn and prevents blind policy rollouts.

User-visible changes:
- new dashboard at Observability > Prefetch Impact Radar
- new alert: observability/prefetch-impact-high-cost (default: warning after sustained 10%+ increase in token cost among prefetched invocations for 30m)
- new sampler config: observability.prefetchSampler.enabled (default: true)

Implementation notes / tradeoffs:
- PrefetchDeltaAggregator stitches span edges and uses a lightweight heuristic to compute warm_affinity; there is a small CPU cost at the trace-processor; metric cardinality is bounded by bucketing token_cost_prefetch_bucket into 8 broad buckets.
- Simulator is intentionally conservative: it replays sampled historical traces and applies candidate policy transforms (e.g., reduce prefetch probability, raise warm threshold) to estimate SLO impact; accuracy depends on sample fidelity.

Checklist:
- [x] PrefetchDeltaAggregator impl + unit tests
- [x] Prometheus histograms & recording rules
- [x] Grafana dashboard JSON + panel descriptions
- [x] Alert + runbook entry
- [x] E2E smoke run with sample replay
- [x] Docs: observability/prefetch-impact.md

Links: Linear ENG-2314, incident SUP-4021, design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2314/prefetch-impact-radar

Notes on testing and rollout:
- Feature guarded by observability.prefetchImpactFeatureFlag for 24h ramp in prod
- Sampling defaults on for orgs with >1k monthly invocations to keep downstream costs manageable
- CI: an initial flaky test (trace-processor unit TestTracePrefetchAffinity) failed on first CI run; updated the test harness and retried. See CI summary below.
Adds a new observability module (prefetch-impact-radar) that correlates prefetch/warmup effectiveness with token-level cost/latency and a companion SLO prognostics simulation playbook; dashboards and runbook included.
Liam Chen (review): Could we tighten the histogram buckets for token_cost_prefetch_bucket? Broad buckets hide small regressions. Requested a follow-up to add a diagnostic finer bucket set behind a debug flag.
Aisha Patel (reply): Agreed — added a debug finer_bucket_histogram that is gated by observability.debugFineBuckets. Kept the main recording rule to 8 buckets to protect cardinality.
Diego Marquez (review): Simulator is promising. Request: ensure simulator runs do not read full tenant secrets or PII; mask any prompt content used in replay.
Aisha Patel (reply): Simulator operates on anonymized, sampled traces; added explicit masking and retention checks in the simulator harness (see prefetch-impact.md).
Priya Nair (review): Alert threshold looks noisy for small tenants. Suggested alert rate limiter or tenant weighting. 
Aisha Patel (reply): Implemented tenant-weighted alerting by scaling the anomaly score with tenant monthly invocation percentile; added notes to runbook.
CI run #1: unit-tests failed: TestTracePrefetchAffinity (race in mock time)
Action: fixed test harness timing and added retry in test; updated mocks
CI run #2: all checks green (lint/pass/unit/integration smoke)
Rolled out under feature flag; first canary ran in us-west-2 for 6 hours. Observed 0.8% overall token-cost uplift but 6% tail improvement for a large customer that has aggressive prefetch settings. Playbook suggests avoiding blanket increases and tuning per-model warm thresholds.
Monitor prefetched token-cost delta for 72h and tune alert sensitivity
Schedule follow-up to add optional finer histograms behind debug flag
Coordinate with runtime team to expose warm thresholds via runtime API

payload.body:
Motivation: production rollouts showed brittle promotions when cohorts with skewed traffic characteristics got promoted out-of-phase, causing transient SLO violations and noisy telemetry that obscured regressions. This PR introduces the Cohort Orbit Synchronizer: a controller that enforces temporal alignment windows (orbits) across related cohorts, a lightweight "telemetry sheriff" process that computes drift signals and issues promotion throttles, and a rollback orchestrator that captures compact checkpoints for fast, deterministic rewind. Goals: 1) reduce cross-cohort interference during staged promotes; 2) make telemetry-driven throttles auditable and debuggable; 3) enable low-latency, safe rollback that preserves session affinity.

Summary of changes: added a new coordinator component (pkg/orbit) with a temporal scheduler that aligns cohort promotions into discrete slots, implemented a telemetry-sheriff service (observability/sheriff) that subscribes to per-cohort metrics, surface-level policy DSL for defining orbit windows and throttle thresholds (config/orbit_policy.yaml), and a rollback orchestrator that persists minimal state snapshots to the rollout ledger for deterministic rewind. The runtime integrates with existing promote/fallback hooks and exposes a small Prometheus surface for sheriff decisions.

Checklist: - [x] design doc reviewed (ENG-1429) - [x] unit tests for scheduler and sheriff - [x] integration test using replay harness (benchmark-lab/canary-replay) - [x] e2e smoke in staging - [x] migration tool to convert existing cohort annotations to orbit windows - [x] runbook updated and placed under docs/runbooks/orbit-sync.md

Testing notes: local unit/integration passed. Ran canary-replay with synthetic cohorts and verified orbit enforcement prevented a 10% traffic burst from bypassing guardrails. In staging we ran a 4-hour soak with three linked cohorts; sheriff injected synthetic drifts to verify throttles; rollback orchestrator executed a rewind sequence (squash-commit style) and restored sessions within expected bounds.

Deployment notes: feature is guarded behind feature flag rollout.orbit_synchronizer; default off for existing customers. Rolling upgrade plan: deploy controller -> enable flag in staging -> monitor sheriff metrics -> enable in limited accounts -> gradually flip global flag. Backout: disable flag then apply a quick rollback of controller to  previous stable image.

Related: coordinates with ENG-1438 (canary-replay extension) and SUP-4422 (incident follow-up on cross-cohort flapping).
Ravi Singh: Nice approach; ask for clarity on how orbit windows interact with rate limiting. Please add a small diagram and a unit test for overlapping windows.
Author (Maya): Added diagram to docs/runbooks/orbit-sync.md and introduced TestOverlappingWindows in scheduler_test.go. Also clarified semantics in orbit_policy.yaml comments.
Elena Gomez: Telemetry sheriff looks good. Two nits: 1) rename 'driftScore' to 'deltaScore' to avoid confusion with drift detection library; 2) make the metrics label set stable across restarts.
Author (Maya): Renamed field and stabilized label set; updated unit tests. Marked for another pass.
Tom Wright: Please add integration smoke to the canary-replay harness and confirm e2e flakiness baseline. Approving once CI green.
CI Bot: integration tests passed (reran failed flake once).

payload.body:
Adds Grafana dashboards and Prometheus alert templates for Dedicated staged rollouts. Includes per-stage latency/error/saturation panels, region breakdowns, and rollout promotion/abort annotations. Adds initial SRE-tuned alert thresholds aligned with Dedicated rollout gates (v1).
Summary: This PR adds a first cut of dashboard + alert templates for the Dedicated staged rollout system. The dashboards are stage-aware (stage_id / stage_name) and are designed to support the rollout gate model in the policy engine (latency, errors, saturation/headroom, GPU health proxies). It also adds annotations for stage promotion/abort/hold events so operators can correlate metric shifts with rollout actions.

Context / dependencies: This is intended to ship alongside the redwood monorepo changes that (a) emit stage tags in metrics/traces and (b) provide audit events for promote/abort/hold. Dashboards assume the following labels are present on the relevant metrics: dedicated_pool_id, rollout_plan_id, stage_id, stage_name, region. For cardinality safety, the dashboards intentionally avoid any per-request labels and only group-by the allowlisted stage identifiers.

What’s included:
- Grafana dashboards (templated) for Dedicated staged rollouts:
  1) "Dedicated Rollouts: Stage Overview" (default landing)
     - Stage timeline annotations (promote/abort/hold)
     - p95/p99 latency per stage (overall + per region)
     - request rate + error rate (5xx + 429 separately)
     - saturation/headroom proxy panels (GPU utilization, queue depth)
     - OOM / throttling proxy panels (where available)
  2) "Dedicated Rollouts: Stage Drilldown" (single stage focus)
     - gating window panels (5m + 15m, side-by-side)
     - sample size panel (req/min, tokens/sec) to reduce false confidence
     - region comparison table with pass/fail indicator driven by threshold variables
  3) "Dedicated Rollouts: Fleet Signals" (operator/SRE)
     - node/GPU health summary by pool + region
     - ECC error rate proxy + throttling counters (when present)
- Alert templates (Prometheus rules) aligned to v1 gates:
  - GateCandidateHighErrorRate (per stage)
  - GateCandidateP99LatencyRegression (per stage)
  - GateCandidateHigh429Rate (per stage; motivated by early canary starving capacity)
  - GateCandidateGPUSaturation (per stage + per region)
  - GateCandidateQueueDepthSpike (per stage)
  - TelemetryStaleForStage (marks "unknown" gate evidence scenarios; ticket-level)
- Annotations:
  - Adds Grafana annotation queries backed by the audit event stream (via Loki index) for: rollout.plan.created, rollout.stage.promoted, rollout.stage.aborted, rollout.stage.held, rollout.stage.force_promoted.
  - Annotation text includes actor + reason (if provided) and links back to the Console rollout page (URL templated).

Notes on thresholds (v1):
- Thresholds are intentionally conservative and are parameterized as Grafana variables where possible so we can tune by tier without re-cutting dashboards.
- We split 429 from 5xx because 429 is the most common early-stage failure signature when partition sizing is too small.
- Missing data: dashboards show "no data" explicitly; alerts include a separate TelemetryStaleForStage rule instead of failing other rules open/closed.

Validation:
- Tested with staging data using synthetic stage tags and replayed a known canary incident window from SUP-28522 to confirm panels highlight 429 + queue depth.
- Verified annotations render correctly with sample audit events and do not explode cardinality.

Rollout plan:
- Land dashboards behind the dedicated_rollouts folder; do not set as default home.
- SRE to enable alert rules for staging first, then production after one week of tuning.

Follow-ups (not in this PR):
- Add a customer-facing pared-down dashboard variant (hides infra-only signals).
- Add quality regression panels (eval scores) once the stage-tagged eval pipeline is finalized.
- Tighten region impairment visualization (heatmap) after we confirm multi-region rollout behavior in beta.

Screenshots (staging):
- https://grafana.staging.redwood.example/d/dedicated-rollouts-stage-overview
- https://grafana.staging.redwood.example/d/dedicated-rollouts-stage-drilldown

References:
- Linear: ENG-5966 (stage-tagged metrics), PM-827 (default thresholds)
- Support: SUP-28522 (canary 429s), SUP-28605 (missing gate evidence)
- Related code: redwood PRs for stage tags + audit events (see internal rollout doc for exact SHAs).
Allison Grant (review): Can you confirm we’re not grouping by any high-cardinality labels? I’m worried stage_id + rollout_plan_id could explode on large customers. Also, please add explicit guidance in the README about the allowlist and expected label set.

Sergio Costa (author): Confirmed. All queries only group by {dedicated_pool_id, stage_id, region} and use rollout_plan_id only for annotations (log search), not metrics. Added README section "Cardinality guardrails" and removed an accidental by (rollout_plan_id) on the error panel.

Logan Wright (review): Telemetry staleness rule: please make it ticket-level (not page) and ensure it keys off ingest lag rather than absolute absence (some stages truly have low traffic). Also, can we add a min sample size hint panel? We’ve seen false positives when canary stage is quiet.

Sergio Costa (author): Updated staleness rule to require both (a) metrics missing and (b) ingest lag > 3m from the pipeline heartbeat metric. Set severity=ticket. Added "Requests/min" and "Tokens/sec" panels and a note: 'Gate results unreliable under low sample size'.

Peter Holtz (review): The 429 alert threshold seems low for spiky workloads. Can we either use burn-rate style logic or a longer window so we don’t flap? We don’t want rollout alerts paging every time a customer load test starts.

Sergio Costa (author): Switched 429 rule to two-window approach (5m + 30m) and added a 'sustained' requirement. Also changed severity to page only when 429 coincides with queue depth spike + saturation (otherwise ticket).

Rafael Mendes (review): Please align the p99 regression logic with SLO gate windows (5m and 15m) and add a panel that shows 'baseline stage' vs 'candidate stage'. Otherwise it’s hard for oncall to reason about regression.

Sergio Costa (author): Added baseline-vs-candidate comparison panel using variables baseline_stage_name and candidate_stage_name (defaults baseline=previous stage). Alerts use 15m window for p99 regression; dashboards show both 5m and 15m.

CI: First run failed due to jsonnetfmt mismatch; reran after formatting. Final checks: lint, jsonnet build, promtool check rules, dashboard render tests.

Outcome: Approved by Allison/Logan/Peter/Rafael and merged (squash).

payload.body:
## Summary
This PR adds a first-cut set of Grafana dashboards to visualize Shadow Traffic quality deltas (control vs shadow variants) and scoring pipeline lag/health. The dashboards are designed for Hosted/Dedicated/Private and intentionally avoid high-cardinality breakdowns (no prompt_id, request_fingerprint, raw route_id, customer_id).

This is intended to support beta oncall readiness and help triage the two main failure classes seen during dogfood/beta:
1) quality deltas missing/stale due to scoring lag or ingestion lag
2) metrics backend pressure due to accidental high-cardinality dimensions

## What’s included
- New "Shadow Traffic / Quality Deltas" dashboard:
  - Δ quality score (shadow - control) over time with confidence bands (when emitted)
  - refusal rate delta, format adherence delta
  - sample size panels (n_control, n_shadow) + effective sample rate
  - breakdowns limited to:
    - deployment_mode (hosted|dedicated|private)
    - model_family (e.g., llama3, qwen2, mistral)
    - route_group (sanitized bucket: "core_chat", "embeddings", "tools", etc.)
    - rubric_version (pinned)
    - experiment_id (capped / top-k only)

- New "Shadow Traffic / Scoring Lag & Worker Health" dashboard:
  - scoring queue lag (p50/p95/p99) + oldest message age
  - worker throughput, retry rate, DLQ count
  - ingestion lag for shadow_pair events
  - circuit breaker open rate + dropped shadow attempts (fail-open)

- Alert rule proposals (NOT enabled by default):
  - scoring pipeline lag SLO breach (ticket -> page escalation guidance in annotations)
  - missing scoring signal (no scored pairs for X minutes while shadow attempts > 0)
  - quality regression advisory alert (requires minimum sample size + CI)

## Cardinality / safety notes
This PR follows the cardinality constraints discussed in SUP-28510 and the Shadow Metrics ADR:
- No dashboards query by prompt_id/request_fingerprint.
- experiment_id panels use a top-k query and default to aggregate view.
- route_id is replaced with route_group generated upstream (low-cardinality mapping maintained by telemetry).
- model_id is avoided; we use model_family + (optional) variant_role (control|shadow).

## Files changed (high level)
- dashboards/shadow_traffic_quality_deltas.jsonnet
- dashboards/shadow_scoring_lag_and_health.jsonnet
- dashboards/_library/shadow_traffic_panels.libsonnet
- alerts/shadow_scoring_lag_rules.yml (proposed)
- alerts/shadow_quality_regression_rules.yml (proposed)
- dashboards/README.md (usage + label guidance)

## Example panel queries (illustrative)
- Quality delta (aggregate):
  sum(rate(redwood_shadow_quality_score_sum{deployment_mode=~"$deployment_mode", rubric_version=~"$rubric_version"}[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_shadow_quality_score_count{deployment_mode=~"$deployment_mode", rubric_version=~"$rubric_version"}[5m]))
  -
  sum(rate(redwood_control_quality_score_sum{deployment_mode=~"$deployment_mode", rubric_version=~"$rubric_version"}[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_control_quality_score_count{deployment_mode=~"$deployment_mode", rubric_version=~"$rubric_version"}[5m]))

- Scoring lag (p95):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, deployment_mode) (rate(redwood_shadow_scoring_lag_seconds_bucket{deployment_mode=~"$deployment_mode"}[5m])))

## Rollout plan
- Merge to observability-pack, dashboards deployed to internal Grafana first (dogfood tenants)
- Enable for Dedicated beta tenants once telemetry labels are confirmed stable (route_group + model_family present)
- Alert rules remain "proposed" until SRE signs off on thresholds and paging policy

## Screenshots
Not included in PR description (dashboards are generated in CI and reviewed via preview JSON in artifacts). See CI artifact: grafana-dashboards-preview.zip

## Checklist
- [x] Panels avoid high-cardinality dimensions
- [x] Default views are aggregate-first; breakdowns are opt-in
- [x] Added dashboard annotations linking to runbook sections (shadow scoring lag / missing data)
- [x] CI renders jsonnet and validates Grafana schema

## Notes / follow-ups
- Follow-up: add a small "label sanitizer" doc with examples of safe/unsafe breakdowns (Logan/Nadia request)
- Follow-up: once confidence interval emission is standardized, switch CI panel to render CI bands instead of placeholder series

Related:
- ENG-5409 (alerting quality regression detection)
- ENG-5410 (cardinality guardrails for shadow metrics)
- SUP-28477 (missing quality dashboard data for Dedicated tenant)
- SUP-28510 (cardinality alerts after enabling shadow traffic)
Logan Wright: Please confirm we’re not using route_id anywhere in template vars. We had a cardinality spike last week when someone added it to a dropdown.
Allison Grant: Confirmed. Only route_group is exposed (and it’s limited to a fixed allowlist upstream). I added a comment in the template vars block and a README note.
Nadia Rahman: For experiment_id breakdown, can we force top-k and show an annotation when the series is truncated?
Allison Grant: Implemented top-k via query + added a dashboard note ("limited to top 10 by sample_count"). Grafana doesn’t give a perfect truncation signal, but we add a stat panel showing total experiments active vs displayed.
Sean Gallagher: Alert rules: can we keep them out of paging until we’ve validated thresholds? Also add runbook links in annotations.
Allison Grant: Kept in alerts/ as proposed; they’re not wired into the deployment bundle yet. Added runbook URLs in rule annotations and dashboard links section.
Selene Huang: For quality regression, ensure minimum sample size gating and avoid triggering on tiny deltas.
Allison Grant: Rule requires n_shadow >= 500 and n_control >= 500 over 30m, plus delta threshold. Also added a panel showing sample sizes next to the delta chart.
Caleb Johnson: CI artifact preview is helpful. Can you add schema validation for Grafana v10 to avoid runtime errors?
Allison Grant: Added grafana-dashboard-validator step (v10) to dashboards/render.

Context: As part of the Quickstart Templates rollout, we want a default local-dev observability path that (a) works out of the box, (b) matches Redwood tracing conventions, and (c) does not accidentally leak secrets/PII via spans/logs/attributes. This PR adds two concrete OpenTelemetry Collector configuration examples that template repos can reference and that we can point users to from docs/troubleshooting. What’s in this PR: 1) New collector configs: - collector/config.local-dev.yaml: default OTLP receiver (grpc/http), batch + memory limiter, resource attribution, and a conservative redaction/allowlist policy appropriate for developer laptops. - collector/config.production.example.yaml: production-oriented example (still generic) showing how to wire redaction + attribute allowlisting and keep cardinality under control. 2) New docker-compose example: - docker-compose.otel.local.yaml to run otelcol-contrib with the local-dev config and expose 4317/4318. 3) README updates: - docs snippet describing how template apps should point OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT at the local collector; notes on when to prefer http vs grpc; and guidance on verifying traces are flowing. Redaction / safety details: - We explicitly drop or redact sensitive attributes commonly observed in HTTP/gateway environments (Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, X-Api-Key, and template telemetry tags when misconfigured). - We include an allowlist pattern for redwood.* attributes and select http.* attributes; everything else remains opt-in (to avoid high-cardinality surprises). - We document how to extend the allowlist safely for custom app attributes. Example snippet (local-dev): processors: attributes/redaction: actions: - key: http.request.header.authorization action: delete - key: http.request.header.cookie action: delete - key: http.request.header.x-api-key action: delete - key: redwood.api_key action: delete - key: enduser.id action: delete (templates shouldn’t set this; defensive) transform/sanitize: trace_statements: - context: span statements: - replace_pattern(attributes["http.target"], "\\?.*", "") Notes: - We intentionally do not add any exporter credentials guidance beyond standard env vars; users should use their platform’s secret manager. - The production example includes comments on enabling a filelog receiver only when needed and how to avoid logging request/response bodies. Testing: - Adds a small CI validation step that runs otelcol-contrib config validation against both configs (caught a typo in an earlier revision). - Local smoke: ran docker-compose.otel.local.yaml and verified traces from the Python template show up in Grafana Tempo with expected resource attributes and without header leakage. Follow-ups (not blocking): - Align exact attribute allowlist with the final docs page under redwood-docs/pr-844 once that lands; we may want to keep one canonical source of truth. - Consider adding an optional ‘debug exporter’ block for local troubleshooting, but default should stay safe (no payload dumps).
Allison Grant: Can we be explicit that headers should not be captured by default? Even with redaction, it’s easy to miss a key. Also, please avoid encouraging high-cardinality attributes in examples (e.g., full URLs with query strings).
Sergio Costa (author): Updated both configs to (1) delete common header keys defensively, (2) strip query strings from http.target, and (3) add comments that header capture should remain off unless explicitly needed for debugging.
Christine Wong: For production example, can we add guidance about memory_limiter + batch sizing? We’ve seen template apps overwhelm collectors in dev clusters when batching is too aggressive.
Sergio Costa (author): Added recommended defaults and comments (memory_limiter check_interval, limit_mib, spike_limit_mib) and kept batch settings conservative. Also clarified that production example is a starting point and should be load-tested.
Monica Patel: Templates need a dead-simple local path. Are we okay with both 4317 and 4318 exposed and documenting the one we prefer?
Sergio Costa (author): Yes—local config exposes both; docs recommend HTTP (4318) for easier proxy compatibility, but note gRPC is fine if users prefer it. This matches the template default env var blocks we’ve been using.
Caleb Johnson: Minor: processors order—redaction should run before batching; also, can we avoid adding any user identifiers (enduser.id) to examples to prevent people copy/pasting?
Sergio Costa (author): Re-ordered processors; removed any mention of setting enduser.id and kept a defensive delete rule only (commented).
Allison Grant: Looks good now. Approving once CI is green.
CI: validate otelcol configs failed (unknown processor name) on config.production.example.yaml.
Sergio Costa (author): Fixed processor name + reran; CI now green.
Allison Grant: Approved.
Christine Wong: Approved.

payload.body:
## Summary This PR adds a standard Grafana dashboard for Route-level Experiments guardrails and data quality signals. The dashboard is intended to be deployed alongside the route experiments beta/GA so on-call and customers (where applicable) can quickly answer: (1) Is any variant regressing on latency, error rate, or cost? (2) Are we missing experiment attribution (drop rate) such that results are untrustworthy? (3) Is traffic split behaving as expected (e.g., variant getting ~0% traffic)?

This dashboard complements the control-plane/Console views by providing a fast, infrastructure-centric view over raw telemetry, and is designed to work with the canonical attribution dimensions from ADR-048 (route_id, experiment_id, variant_id, region, model_id) while limiting cardinality blast-radius.

## What’s included ### Dashboard: "Route Experiments / Guardrails" Panels (high-level): - Overview row: total RPS, total requests, error rate (5xx + 429 separately), and attribution coverage.
- Latency guardrails: p50/p95/p99 request latency by variant (timeseries + stat) with a "% delta vs control" table.
- Error guardrails: error rate by variant (5xx and 429 broken out), plus "top error codes" if available.
- Cost guardrails: $/1K output tokens and $/request by variant (based on Redwood cost attribution metrics).
- Throughput: tokens/sec and requests/sec by variant (useful for distinguishing capacity issues from model behavior).
- Traffic split sanity: % of traffic per variant; includes a "variant ~0 traffic" panel to catch allocation/eligibility mistakes.
- Data quality: experiment attribution drop rate (requests missing experiment_id/variant_id when they should be present), plus a "streaming retry attribution" hint panel (links to runbook section).

### Template variables - env (prod/staging) - region - route_id (normalized route template id; NOT raw path) - experiment_id - variant_id - model_id (optional; default All)

### Data sources / metric expectations This dashboard assumes the router/runtime emits experiment dimensions on key metrics and/or spans, as implemented in the core monorepo (see redwood PRs: request context plumbing + OTel tagging). The queries here are written to tolerate partial rollout by falling back to "All variants" if variant tags are absent.

Primary metrics used (names reflect current conventions in the pack; see README changes for exact mapping): - redwood_request_latency_ms_bucket{route_id, experiment_id, variant_id, region} - redwood_requests_total{route_id, experiment_id, variant_id, region, status_class} - redwood_tokens_output_total{route_id, experiment_id, variant_id, region} - redwood_cost_usd_total{route_id, experiment_id, variant_id, region} - redwood_experiment_attribution_missing_total{route_id, region, reason} and redwood_requests_total (used as denominator)

## Why / context - We’ve had multiple beta issues where Console results were confusing or appeared stale, and on-call needed a quick way to validate (a) attribution integrity and (b) whether a regression was real vs. a data artifact (ref: SUP-24910).
- SRE asked for a standardized dashboard that can be installed for every region/environment with consistent panels and variable naming so runbooks/alerts can deep-link reliably.
- The attribution drop rate panels are explicitly included because missing experiment_id/variant_id has been a recurring failure mode (streaming retries, async spans, and header/sticky-key issues).

## Implementation notes - Cardinality: the dashboard does NOT group by raw request path. It uses normalized route_id (template) and requires users to select an experiment_id for most by-variant panels. We avoid “group by {route_id, experiment_id, variant_id, model_id, region}” in single queries unless the user is already scoped down.
- Cost metrics: panels use $/1K output tokens and $/request. This avoids misleading comparisons for variants with different output length distributions.
- Control variant: the “delta vs control” table assumes variant_id="control" when present; otherwise it picks the lowest-sorted variant_id as a fallback. This is called out in the panel description so it doesn’t silently mislead.

## Changed files - grafana/dashboards/route-experiments/route-experiments-guardrails.jsonnet: new dashboard definition - grafana/dashboards/route-experiments/route-experiments-guardrails.dashboard.json: rendered dashboard - grafana/dashboards/route-experiments/README.md: usage notes, required labels, variable conventions - grafana/library-panels/latency-percentiles-by-variant.jsonnet: extracted reusable panel - grafana/library-panels/attribution-drop-rate.jsonnet: extracted reusable panel - CHANGELOG.md: entry for the new dashboard

## Screenshots (described) - "Latency (p95/p99) by variant" timeseries: color-coded variants, with control highlighted - "Attribution drop rate" stat: shows % missing attribution + reason breakdown in a table

## Test plan - Rendered dashboards via jsonnet build (make dashboards) - Validated PromQL in staging against synthetic traffic + a known experiment_id (confirmed series appear with expected labels) - Verified variable dropdowns do not time out when unscoped (route_id and experiment_id are optional until selecting per-variant panels)

## Follow-ups (not in this PR) - Alerts live in a separate PR (pr-1942) to keep review surface smaller and allow independent tuning.
- Add runbook deep links once URLs are finalized (placeholder links included as annotations for now).

## Checklist - [x] Dashboard renders (jsonnet + rendered json committed) - [x] Variables align with attribution schema (route_id/experiment_id/variant_id/region) - [x] Panel descriptions call out assumptions (control selection, partial rollout behavior) - [x] Changelog entry added
Logan Wright (Telemetry): PromQL looks good, but can we avoid grouping by model_id by default? That dimension is optional and can explode in some tenants.
Allison Grant (Author): Good call. I updated the dashboard so model_id is a variable defaulting to All, and the by-variant panels do not group by model_id unless explicitly selected.
Rafael Mendes (SRE): Please add an explicit panel for “variant 0 traffic” / “unexpected split” so we catch misconfig + eligibility issues quickly.
Allison Grant (Author): Added a Traffic Split row with % per variant and a "near-zero traffic" stat that flags any variant below 0.5% (configurable via dashboard constant).
Aisha Bello (SRE): For attribution drop rate, can we show both absolute missing req/s and %? Percent alone hides volume spikes.
Allison Grant (Author): Done. Added a small timeseries for missing req/s and kept the % stat as the headline.
Caleb Johnson (Ingestion): Please document the expected metric names/labels in README and note that some panels will be empty until router tagging is fully rolled out.
Allison Grant (Author): Added a "Required metrics" section + a "Partial rollout" note in README and panel descriptions.
Logan Wright (Telemetry): Approved.
Rafael Mendes (SRE): Approved after latest push.
Aisha Bello (SRE): Approved.

Summary: Adds a Grafana folder + dashboards for the Cost Model API so Console/Optimize rollouts have a single place to monitor health, adoption, and correctness drift. Includes panels for request volume, p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate by code, schema version distribution, request-bounds rejections, cache hit/miss (client-side + service memoization), and a first pass of drift metrics (predicted vs observed) sourced from the scheduled drift job. Motivation: During early Console integration testing we saw two recurring issues: (1) latency spikes due to cardinality blowups on hot paths and (2) drift alerts firing due to telemetry lag vs genuine mismatch. This PR standardizes the dashboards and bakes in guardrail signals (telemetry freshness, missing inputs) so oncall can quickly triage. Related: redwood/pr-28457 (service endpoints), redwood/pr-28490 (drift monitoring job), redwood/pr-28495 (what-if guardrails), SUP-31905 (latency spike report). What’s included (dashboards): 1) "Cost Model API / Overview" (high-level SLO views): RPS, concurrency, saturation, p50/p95/p99 latency, error budget burn (5m/1h/6h), top tenants (bounded), and a "schema negotiation" panel showing unknown/unsupported versions returned to clients. 2) "Cost Model API / Errors & Bounds" (debug): error rate split by status, error_code, and stage; panels for bound rejections (e.g., breakdown_group_by too high-cardinality), request payload size buckets, and timeouts by caller (console-backend vs optimize-service). 3) "Cost Model API / Schema Version Adoption": distribution of requested schema_version vs served schema_version (incl. fallback), percent of clients sending optional fields for cache/batching/quantization; includes a heatmap of version by environment. 4) "Cost Model / Drift": predicted_cost_usd vs observed_cost_usd (daily + hourly), drift pct, confidence bands where available, and triage panels: telemetry lag (ingestion watermark age), missing-runtime-input rate, and "prefill/decode split present" ratio. Alerts: Adds two alert rules (behind the existing oncall routing policy): (a) p95 latency > 300ms for 10m (scoped to prod + excluding canary envs), (b) drift_pct > 5% for 6h AND telemetry_lag < 15m (to reduce false positives during pipeline delays). Notes: Drift is expected to be noisy early; the dashboard intentionally surfaces "telemetry freshness" next to drift so oncall can distinguish pipeline lag from real regression. Implementation details: Dashboards live under grafana/dashboards/cost-model-api/*.jsonnet and are rendered to JSON in CI. Metrics consumed assume the cost-model service exports: cost_model_api_request_duration_seconds (histogram), cost_model_api_requests_total (by status, error_code, caller, env), cost_model_api_schema_version_served_total, and drift job exports: cost_model_drift_ratio, cost_model_drift_pct, cost_model_observed_cost_usd, cost_model_predicted_cost_usd, telemetry_watermark_age_seconds. payload.body: Context/Motivation: We need per-invocation token cost visibility without retaining plaintext prompt or response tokens in observability backends. This PR introduces a privacy-first pipeline: (1) deterministic, salted token-hash bucketing at the edge; (2) a compact per-invocation cost summarizer that attributes per-bucket token counts and tokenized-costs; (3) a bridge service that joins hashed token buckets with model cost profiles for rollups and dashboards. Goals: provide accurate cost attribution for SLOs and billing heuristics while ensuring PII/PHI is never logged or exported. Changes are designed to be reversible (config toggles) and auditable. Main changes: - collector: add pseudonymization middleware that applies a per-tenant salt and BLAKE3-based chunked hashing to token fragments, exposing only bucket_id and hash_prefix_size metadata (no token text). - summarizer: a streaming aggregator that emits per-invocation compact summaries: total_tokens, generation_tokens, prompt_token_buckets (list of bucket_id:count), and model_cost_approx_usd (aggregated using model profile). - bridge service: lightweight joiner that maps bucket-level aggregates to model cost model to compute per-route and per-tenant cost metrics used by dashboards/alerts. - dashboards: add a new Observability Pack dashboard panel group 'Pseudonymous Cost Explorer' with per-route aggregated cost and a new 'quiet-surge' alert rule that triggers only when cost growth is sustained across at least 3 hours and >75th percentile of bucket skew. - telemetry: add metrics and labels for pseudonymization_version, salt_id, and summarizer_latency_ms; tracing spans annotated with sample_rate and anonymized_bucket_count. Backwards compatibility: collector can run in dual-mode emitting both legacy plaintext token telemetry (for fast migration) and pseudonymized summaries behind a feature flag. Checklist: [x] design review (ENG-4321), [x] privacy review with security, [x] unit tests for hashing and summarizer, [x] integration test with bridge, [x] dashboard screens, [x] docs draft. Migrations/deploy: - rollout plan: enable pseudonymization off-by-default; stage enable on a small subset of tenants (canary 1%), monitor summarizer latency and cost deltas for 48h, then ramp to 100% over 5 days. - rollback plan: flip feature flag to legacy mode (no schema migration required). - data retention: summarized rows kept 90d; raw hashed metadata kept 7d and then rotated. Security/privacy notes: salts are tenant-scoped and stored in KMS-backed vault; hashing performed in-process so unhashed tokens never leave the collector process. Commit summary: 1) add privacy middleware and deterministic token hashing; 2) streaming summarizer service and proto changes for compact summary; 3) bridge joiner service and query adapters for dashboards; 4) observability pack dashboard panels and alert rule; 5) e2e tests and runbook. Key files changed: observability-pack/pkg/collector/pseudonymizer.go, observability-pack/pkg/summarizer/stream_aggregator.go, observability-pack/services/bridge/joiner.go, observability-pack/dashboards/pseudonymous_cost_explorer.jsonnet, observability-pack/alerts/quiet_surge.yaml, docs/observability/privacy-token-summarizer.md, test/e2e/pseudonymizer_integration_test.go, scripts/bench/summarizer_bench.go, go.mod, go.sum. Tests: added unit tests for hash stability and collision resistance, integration test that validates summarizer output vs synthetic tokenized inputs, benchmark for 99th-pctl summarizer latency. Observability/Alerting: - New metric: pseudonymizer.tokens_hashed_total{tenant,salt_id} - New histogram: summarizer.latency_ms - New alert: observability.quiet_surge_high_cost (suppresses noisy short spikes; logic included in alert yaml) Release notes (short): Adds a privacy-preserving token-cost summarizer that allows cost attribution without storing token text; dashboards and alerts submitted with observability pack. Rollout and monitoring instructions included. Rationale and alternatives considered: we evaluated full differential privacy vs deterministic hashing; deterministic salted hashing was chosen for lower operational complexity and deterministic joins. We added salt rotation support as a safety mechanism. Open questions: - how to present per-bucket explanations to end-users without leaking token content? We opted for statistical bucket descriptors (e.g., average token length, token_type_entropy) rather than examples. - future: consider integrating cryptographic PPE techniques for smaller tenants. Observability runbook excerpt: On spike after enabling, check summarizer.latency_ms, look for high anonymized_bucket_count, and if latency > 200ms for 5m trigger rollback. Compliance: privacy review approved; KMS usage logged.
payload.title: Add pseudonymous token-cost summarizer and privacy-hash bridge

payload.body:
Motivation: Dedicated burst capacity requires routing to consult the Burst Admission Controller before borrowing from shared burst pools, and to behave safely when burst is denied (protecting non-burst tenants + preserving determinism). This PR wires the routing/gateway path into the admission controller, adds deterministic policy evaluation inputs, and defines the fallback/backpressure behaviors for denied/timeout cases. Summary of behavior: For Dedicated tenants with burst enabled, routing computes a BurstContext (tenant_id, region, hw_class, baseline allocation id, requested_concurrency/requested_tokens estimate, priority tier) and calls the Burst Admission Controller synchronously at request admission time. If admitted, routing tags the request with the admission grant_id and burst_pool_id and routes to the burst pool endpoint group; if denied, routing falls back to baseline dedicated capacity when available (no pool borrowing) and otherwise applies backpressure (HTTP 429 with structured denial reason + Retry-After) rather than retrying across neighbors. Determinism: The admission request includes a stable request_key (derived from gateway request_id + model_route + tenant_id) and a policy_snapshot_hash from the control-plane config cache. Routing does not “shop around” across pools/regions/hardware classes. For the initial release, burst is strictly within-region and within hardware class. Failure modes: If the admission controller call times out or returns 5xx, routing treats it as a deny with reason=admission_unavailable and routes only to baseline dedicated capacity; if baseline is saturated, we backpressure with 503 (no burst) to avoid accidental neighbor impact. Observability: Adds routing-side counters and latency histograms for admission calls, denials by reason, and fallback usage, and propagates denial reason codes to the client error surface (aligned with pr-23795). Notes: This PR intentionally does not implement queueing-on-deny; the chosen semantics for v1 are immediate decision + client-driven retry using Retry-After guidance. Queueing can be revisited once we have stronger end-to-end SLO evidence and per-tenant buffering policies.
Decision flow: 1) If tenant.burst.enabled=false => unchanged routing behavior. 2) If enabled and request fits baseline capacity => route baseline (no admission call). 3) If enabled and baseline indicates saturation risk => call admission controller with BurstContext. 4a) ADMIT => route to burst pool, attach grant_id, emit admitted metric. 4b) DENY (pool_saturated | tenant_cap_reached | cooldown_active | fleet_safety_cap | policy_disabled | admission_unavailable) => attempt baseline route if capacity signal says safe; otherwise return backpressure. Backpressure mapping: When deny reason is capacity-related we return HTTP 429 and include x-redwood-burst-denial-reason plus a Retry-After (seconds) when provided by the admission controller; for non-retriable denials (policy_disabled) we return 403. Timeout budget: admission controller call is capped at 35ms p99 target; routing uses 50ms hard timeout and does not retry. This is to prevent tail amplification. Safety: If routing detects inconsistent config (missing hw_class / region mapping) it disables burst path for the request and logs an error with tenant_id + config version, then routes baseline only.
Mina Haddad: Can we guarantee we won’t bounce between baseline and burst across retries and create nondeterministic user experience? Please clarify request_key / idempotency strategy.
Elena Popov (author): Added request_key based on gateway request_id + route + tenant_id, and ensured routing never tries multiple pools. Also added note that client retries should reuse Idempotency-Key; gateway already does this for streaming reconnects. Updated docs/internal/burst/routing-integration-notes.md.
Ravi Menon: I’m concerned about calling admission for every request. Can we skip when baseline has headroom? Also please ensure this doesn’t regress hosted routing path.
Elena Popov (author): Added fast-path: only call admission when baseline capacity signal indicates saturation risk (or when request explicitly opts into burst via header set by internal batch jobs). Hosted path is untouched; dedicated-only code paths are gated by tenant plan + deployment mode checks. Added unit tests to assert hosted route selector does not import burst client.
Ethan Park: Please align deny reason handling with the reason codes from pr-23795 and avoid introducing new strings here. Also what’s the behavior when policy snapshot is stale?
Elena Popov (author): Updated mapping to use the shared enum + string constants from pkg/burst/denial_reasons.go. For stale snapshot, routing includes policy_snapshot_hash; admission controller returns deny reason=config_mismatch with retry_after=0 and we fall back to baseline only. Added metric burst_config_mismatch_total.
Peter Holtz: 503 vs 429 semantics matter for paging and client retry storms. Suggest 429 for capacity denial; 503 only for internal unavailability. Also add a circuit-breaker on admission timeouts to avoid cascading.
Elena Popov (author): Updated as suggested: 429 for capacity/cooldown/caps; 503 only when admission is unavailable AND baseline also cannot serve. Added a simple local circuit breaker: if admission timeouts > 5% over 1m window, skip admission calls for 2m and route baseline-only (emit burst_admission_cb_open).
Unit: dedicated_route_selector tests cover (a) baseline headroom => no admission call, (b) admit => burst route selected + grant_id propagated, (c) deny tenant_cap_reached => baseline fallback when safe, (d) deny pool_saturated + baseline saturated => 429 w/ reason and Retry-After, (e) admission timeout => baseline-only; if baseline saturated => 503. Integration: added fake admission controller to routing integration harness to validate end-to-end header propagation and error mapping in gateway. Manual: replayed staging traffic sample with burst disabled and verified routing decisions identical (hash compare of route targets).
Behind feature flags: routing.burst_admission.enabled (default off) and routing.burst_admission.region_allowlist. Enable in staging for 1 tenant, then dogfood in us-east/h100. SRE to monitor burst_admission_latency_ms p95 and denial-rate dashboards before expanding allowlist. Rollback: flip flag to disable admission calls; routing returns to baseline-only behavior.
Dedicated: Burst-enabled tenants now consult burst admission before borrowing capacity. When burst is denied, routing falls back to baseline when possible or returns structured backpressure (429) with denial reasons and retry hints.
