payload.body:
Context: During staging rehearsals we observed oscillation risk in the failover controller when region health inputs get noisy (partial reachability loss, intermittent 5xx spikes, and delayed capacity signals). While ADR-043 + the anti-flap timers in PR-19815 reduce flip/flop behavior, we still had two failure modes: (1) the controller repeatedly re-attempts the same action (e.g., re-apply a policy flip) when the policy engine or routing API is degraded, and (2) the controller makes too many distinct automation actions across tenants/routes in a short window, amplifying load and making rollback reasoning harder.

This PR introduces explicit rate limiting for automation actions and retries, with metrics + structured logs so on-call can see when guardrails are gating behavior.

What changed (high level): - Added an in-controller rate limiter for action execution and for retry loops. - Enforced per-scope limits (global, per-region pair, per-tenant) with token-bucket semantics and jittered refill. - Converted "retry until success" paths into bounded retries with exponential backoff and a clear terminal state (ActionDeferred vs ActionFailed). - Ensured dry-run mode is not rate-limited (we still emit the same recommendation/audit payloads), but we annotate recommendations with the expected earliest execution time if rate limits were applied. - Added audit event fields for rate-limit gating (rate_limited=true, limiter_scope, next_allowed_at) so we can reconstruct why automation did/did not act.

Key guardrails/config: - controller.rate_limits.global_actions_per_minute (default: 12) - controller.rate_limits.per_regionpair_actions_per_minute (default: 6) - controller.rate_limits.per_tenant_actions_per_hour (default: 4; enforced only when tenant_id is present) - controller.rate_limits.max_retries_per_action (default: 3) - controller.rate_limits.retry_backoff_base_ms (default: 500) - controller.rate_limits.retry_backoff_max_ms (default: 8000) - controller.rate_limits.idempotency_window_s (default: 120) to collapse duplicate "apply same desired state" attempts.

Why this is safe: - Limits are conservative and designed to prevent thundering-herd behavior when the controller is the one experiencing errors (routing API 429/5xx) or when signals flap around thresholds. - We fail "closed" for safety: when rate-limited, we do not execute policy flips; we emit an audit event and set the automation decision outcome to deferred. - We keep rollback semantics unchanged; this PR only adds gating around execution/attempt frequency.

Observability: - New metrics: failover_controller_action_rate_limited_total{scope,reason}, failover_controller_retry_scheduled_total{action_type}, failover_controller_action_next_allowed_seconds{scope}, failover_controller_action_attempts_total{result}. - Added structured log fields: limiter_scope, limiter_key, tokens_before, tokens_after, retry_attempt, retry_delay_ms.

Test plan: - Unit tests for limiter accounting, per-scope precedence (global > regionpair > tenant), and deterministic jitter bounds. - Integration-style tests with a fake routing API that returns intermittent 5xx and verifies bounded retries + correct audit emissions. - Ran controller in staging with replayed signal traces from the rehearsal window; verified we cap flips and retries and do not spam routing.

Rollout: - Behind feature flag failover_controller_rate_limits_enabled (default off). - Staging default on via the game-day config pack; prod enablement will follow the go/no-go checklist with monitoring of rate_limited_total and action latency.

Notes: This complements (not replaces) ADR-043 rollback/hold-down logic. Anti-flap timers control state transitions; rate limiting controls how aggressively we attempt execution and retry under controller-side or downstream instability.
2026-01-12 Miles Thornton: Can you clarify precedence if both regionpair and global limiters are exceeded? Also, do we risk delaying a real failover?

2026-01-12 Benji Okafor (author): Precedence is strict: global first (protects downstream routing/control-plane), then regionpair (prevents flip storms localized to a pair), then tenant. On delaying real failover: dry-run still computes instantly; execution only delayed if we’re already acting too frequently. Default global limit (12/min) still allows initial failover + follow-up actions quickly; the main gating is on repeated attempts.

2026-01-13 Ravi Menon: Please ensure idempotency is keyed on (policy_id, desired_state) not just action_type, otherwise we might suppress a necessary change.

2026-01-13 Benji Okafor (author): Good catch. Updated idempotency window key to include policy_id + desired_hash (routes/models/weights). Added test coverage.

2026-01-14 Peter Holtz: Retry backoff should respect request budgets; avoid synchronized retry across controller replicas.

2026-01-14 Benji Okafor (author): Added jitter to backoff (+/-20%) and wired through controller instance ID salt. Also added a hard cap on retry queue depth to avoid runaway memory usage.

2026-01-15 Allison Grant: Metric label cardinality: limiter_key looks like it could explode if it includes tenant IDs.

2026-01-15 Benji Okafor (author): Adjusted: limiter_key is not emitted as a label. We only label by scope and a bounded reason enum; tenant-level gating is counted without tenant_id in labels. Detailed keys are in structured logs/audit events (with existing privacy controls).

2026-01-16 Rafael Mendes: Looks good. Please add runbook note: if we’re rate limited during an incident, on-call needs to know how to temporarily raise limits.

2026-01-16 Benji Okafor (author): Added docs/internal/failover-controller/guardrails.md and a config snippet for temporary overrides + a reminder to revert after the event.

2026-01-16 Miles Thornton: Approved after changes. Merge once CI is green.

2026-01-16 System: All checks passed.

2026-01-16 Ravi Menon: Approved.

2026-01-16 Benji Okafor (author): Squashing + merging.
Failover automation: add rate limiting and bounded retries for the failover controller to prevent oscillation and excessive action retries under noisy signals; includes new metrics and audit annotations to improve on-call visibility.
payload.title: Failover controller: rate-limit automation actions + retries to prevent oscillation under noisy signals

payload.body:
Introduces tenant-aware age histograms for KV cache and a Spill-Horizon controller that reduces unnecessary spill traffic under moderate pressure; improves tail latency and reduces write amplification during compaction.
Motivation: We observed recurring tail latency spikes and excess spill I/O on multi-tenant hosts during short-lived memory pressure bursts. The current eviction logic is primarily LRU-like with coarse tenant quotas and lacks temporal fragmentation signal, which drives premature page spills and frequent small compactions. This PR introduces two complementary subsystems: (1) fine-grained per-tenant age histograms (AgeBuckets) that produce a compact fragmentation/temperature fingerprint for each tenant, and (2) a Spill-Horizon controller that uses age distributions, recent spill latency, and global reservation headroom to delay or coalesce spill actions until an adaptive horizon is crossed. Together they reduce unnecessary spill churn and make eviction decisions more locality- and age-aware.
Local stress ran with 64 tenants (mix of 90% cold / 10% hot distributions) for 30 minutes. Compared to baseline main: - p50 eviction latency unchanged (~1.2ms), - p95 spill latency reduced 28%, - p99 spill rate (spills/sec) reduced 3.6x, - write amplification during compaction decreased 22%. Memory overhead for AgeBuckets averaged +0.7% of heap on a 512GB node and stays bounded via sampling and caps.
Includes unit tests for histogram updates and spill-horizon backoff; integration test exercising deferred spills under fluctuating pressure; stress harness script to reproduce multi-tenant bursty workload. Ran full test matrix (linux/cgo) and the new stress scenario in CI; e2e run in staging for 48h before merge.
Feature gated behind kv.experimental.age_histograms and kv.spill_horizon_enabled flags. Default rollout is off for Dedicated until 2024-06-15, gradually enabled for 10% of hosted clusters, monitor spill_horizon_defer_total and compaction_write_bytes metrics before wider rollout. If regression detected, toggle flags to revert quickly.
- kv.age_buckets.num_buckets (default 8)
- kv.age_buckets.hotset_sampling_threshold (default 0.01)
- kv.spill_horizon.base_window_ms (default 150)
- kv.spill_horizon.backoff_multiplier (default 2.0)
- kv.spill_horizon.max_delay_ms (default 2000)
Risk: deferred spills could temporarily increase memory pressure and cause larger tail spikes if misconfigured. Mitigation: controller monitors reservation headroom and forces immediate spill if headroom < 5% or free pages below a safe threshold; operator flags enable immediate rollback.
Ethan Zhang (2024-05-15): Nice approach. Two questions: (1) How do we bound the memory cost of AgeBuckets for high-cardinality tenants? (2) Can you show a before/after p99 spill rate for the synthetic tenant workload?
Author (Anika) (2024-05-16): Answered inline. AgeBuckets are compact (8 fixed buckets + overflow counter) and cached in a contiguous slab per-tenant; we also cap tracking to heavy tenants behind a hotset sampling flag. Attached results in the description show p99 spill rate reduced ~3.6x on our emulator for mixed small/large requests.
Luis Martinez (2024-05-18): Request change: make the horizon backoff multiplier configurable and add a unit test for the backoff path when spill latency is high. Also add a metric that exposes how often Spill-Horizon deferred a spill.
Author (Anika) (2024-05-19): Added config and metric spill_horizon_defer_total; added unit test spill_horizon_backoff_test. PTAL.
Priya Patel (2024-05-20): Small nit: please prefer steady_clock for horizon timers to avoid system clock jumps. Also please add a short ops note for ops to tune the hist bucket thresholds.
Author (Anika) (2024-05-21): Switched timers to steady_clock and added ops section in docs. Thanks for the review; addressed all comments.
CI Bot (2024-05-22): Build failed on macOS: missing include in runtime/batcher.h. (automated)
Author (Anika) (2024-05-23): Fixed include and force-pushed. CI rerun.
CI Bot (2024-05-24): All checks passed.
payload.title: kv: fine-grained age histograms and spill-horizon controller for low-fragmentation eviction

payload.body:
Context and motivation: customers and internal platform teams need a way to express reusable, claim-scoped RBAC profiles (for operator/service partitions) while enforcing per-request KMS usage boundaries and improving audit provenance without shipping full-fidelity logs to downstream systems. This PR adds a compact role-templating DSL, enforces KMS 'fencing' at the policy-evaluation layer, and introduces a lightweight audit veneer that stamps and forwards provenance metadata with deterministic redaction rules. Changes: - Role templating DSL and compiler (pkg/rbac/templates.go, pkg/rbac/template_compiler_test.go): small expressive language to generate RBAC bindings by templating on request claims (tenant, data_class, geozone, operator_scope). Templates are validated at CI and at runtime; invalid templates are rejected with clear diagnostics. - KMS usage fencing (pkg/kms/fence/*): middleware that validates that KMS key decisions for a request match the policy-decisions derived from role templates and tenancy claims. On mismatch, request is rejected with 403 and a structured audit entry. Fencing emits metrics (internal/telemetry/metrics_kms_usage.go) for per-tenant KMS hits and fallback events. - Audit veneer (pkg/audit/veneer/*): lightweight forwarder that attaches canonical provenance headers (kms_key_id, residence_assertion, template_id) and applies a configurable redaction policy before forwarding to external sinks. The veneer is intended for cross-zone observability where full logs are not allowed. - Feature gating & rollout (cmd/console/feature_flags.go, pkg/config/feature_gates.go): all behavior gated behind 'rbac-templating' and 'kms-fencing' feature flags; default off for existing customers. - CI & validation (scripts/ci/validate-rbac-templates.sh): lint/validate DSL in CI, unit/integration tests added. - Docs and examples under docs/security/*. Motivation section also lists threat model: accidental cross-region key usage, operator overreach via role proliferation, and audit proof lacking KMS attribution. Migration plan and rollout: feature-gated rollout starting in Canary then Reserved clusters; cross-team migration doc at docs/security/rbac-templating.md. Backwards compatibility: templates compile to existing RBAC bindings; no change to API surfaces. Audit veneer is opt-in per sink. Tests and validation: unit tests for template compiler, integration tests for KMS fencing (including simulated multi-region KMS responses), e2e smoke that validates veneer redaction. CI: initial run had 2 flaky tests; fixed by making the template compiler deterministic in edge-case ordering (see commit 9c3b7a). Security review notes: asked SRE and Security to review the middleware and veneer; added additional defensive checks to avoid leaking tenant identifiers when redaction is enabled. Performance: KMS fencing adds a lightweight policy cache and per-request lookup; benchmark on canary shows median request tail increased by ~2ms with cache warm and 15% throughput reduction in worst-case cold-cache pathological templates. Observability: introduced metrics for KMS decision latencies, fencing rejections, and veneer-forward rates. Review conversation (high-level): - Ethan Martinez: requested stronger error messages for template compilation failures and recommended telemetry tags for operator_scope. Author response: added error codes and appended template_id where available. - Lena Ortiz: requested explicit deny semantics when KMS decisions mismatch (rather than soft-fallback). Author response: implemented strict deny with configurable emergency-fallback mode behind enterprise feature flag. - Kai Nakamura: asked for integration tests that simulate multi-provider KMS failovers. Author response: added integration_test.go and test harness to stub provider responses. - Security review (Margaret Huang): requested proof that veneer redaction rules cover PII edge-cases; added additional unit tests and example redaction configs. CI history: initial run: lint/pass, unit tests/fail(2 flaky), integration/pending. Rerun: all checks pass. Files changed and impact: 18 files, primarily small/new modules and docs. No database schema migrations aside from an index migration to support template lookup (pkg/migrations/20260215_rbac_template_index.sql). Rollout steps included: enable flags in Canary, monitor metrics for fencing rejections and KMS error surface, if >0.5% rejection for production-critical routes roll back. Merge decision: after reviewer sign-offs, security sign-off and green CI, PR merged via squash on 2026-02-18. Follow-ups tracked in ENG-2031 (add more conservative default redaction sets) and SUP-7123 (customer support request to migrate tenant templates). Additional notes: - This PR intentionally keeps the audit veneer separate from heavy audit-shipper code so teams can adopt provenance stamping in regulated regions without changing retention. - Administrators can opt-in to 'emergency-fallback' to automatically route to a backup KMS provider when fencing rejects requests; this is off by default and gated under an enterprise flag. - Documented operator templates example in examples/ops/role-templates.example.yaml. If issues arise after rollout, revert path is to disable 'rbac-templating' feature flag and redeploy the veneer config.
Introduce claim-scoped role templates, KMS usage fencing policy and a lightweight audit veneer that improves provenance stamping for cross-region requests. No customer-facing API changes.
Ethan Martinez: Please include clearer template compilation errors; we hit opaque failures during onboarding.
Priya Kaur: Added error codes and template_id annotations for diagnostics (see commit f7d3b2a).
Lena Ortiz: Require deterministic ordering for compiled bindings to make audits reproducible.
Priya Kaur: Compiler now sorts generated bindings and we added reproducibility tests.
Kai Nakamura: Add integration tests for cross-provider KMS failover scenarios.
Priya Kaur: Added integration harness and stubs; tests added.
Margaret Huang (Security): Validate veneer redaction covers tenant and user identifiers.
Priya Kaur: Expanded unit tests and provided example redaction policy in docs.
CI: lint passed, unit tests passed, integration tests passed. Final green check before merge.
Merge: Squash merged by Priya Kaur on 2026-02-18 after approvals.

payload.body:
Summary: This PR adds a lightweight invocation-harvest aggregator that consumes sampled invocation fragments (traces + logs) and produces compact token-level cost and latency rollups, plus a configurable alert-entropy governor that dynamically suppresses alerts driven by low-information noisy signals.

Motivation: We continue to see high alert churn from long-tail invocations that exhibit high variance but low actionable signal. Instead of raising the bar on detection thresholds globally, the aggregator+governor give us a per-cohort mechanism to: 1) retain fidelity for high-value invocations, 2) compress sampled telemetry for cheaper retention and query, and 3) dampen alert noise where entropy indicates low SNR.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3245/harvest-aggregator-design
- [x] Unit tests for aggregation and governor logic
- [x] End-to-end integration test in replaybench
- [x] Grafana dashboard JSON + panel/alert updates
- [x] Runbook stub and rollout plan
- [x] Backwards-compatible config (toggle per-tenant)

What changed (high level commits):
- commit 1: add pkg/observability/harvest/aggregator.go + aggregator interface, buffering, and compact rollup encoding.
- commit 2: instrument span enrichment and add span tag mappings so aggregator can join traces <-> log anchors.
- commit 3: add alert-entropy-governor implementation and runtime config (k8s ConfigMap + feature flag).
- commit 4: dashboards/observability-harvest.json: new Grafana panels for harvest rollups, entropic-alerts gauge, and suppression heatmap.
- commit 5: ops/runbooks/harvest-runbook.md and deploy/k8s/observability-collector.yaml.
- commit 6: unit and integration tests, CI infra changes for new service.

Files changed (representative):
- pkg/observability/harvest/aggregator.go (new): core aggregator, compaction windows, shard key logic
- pkg/observability/harvest/encoder.go (new): compact rollup encoding (jsonlines-friendly, gzipped blobs for long-retention)
- pkg/observability/harvest/collector_service.go (new): k8s entrypoint + graceful shutdown hooks
- observability/config/defaults.yaml: new sampling and suppression defaults
- dashboards/observability-harvest.json: Grafana dashboard and panel definitions
- ops/runbooks/harvest-runbook.md: incident playbook and troubleshooting steps
- deploy/k8s/observability-collector.yaml: deployment + RBAC
- pkg/alerting/entropy_governor.go (new): governor logic and debug endpoints
- tests/unit/aggregator_test.go, tests/unit/entropy_governor_test.go
- sdk/python/redwood/telemetry.py (minor): helper to emit harvest markers and sampling hints

Behavioral notes and compatibility:
- Default behavior is off for tenants without the new config flag. Enabling it for a tenant routes sampled fragments into the aggregator which writes rollups to the existing metrics index (metric names with prefix obs.harvest.*).
- The aggregator emits compact rollups at 1m and 5m windows; the 1m rollups are optional (configurable) and used by fast dashboards; 5m is the canonical retention.
- The entropy governor attaches a suppression score to alerts produced by existing alerting rules; rules can opt-in via annotations, and the governor will lower the alerting weight for cohorts with entropy > threshold. This is a smoothing/attenuation strategy, not a hard mute.

Review conversation (highlights, chronological):
- Sofia Alvarez (reviewer): "Nice isolation between collector and encoder. A couple of thoughts on backpressure — what happens if aggregator can't write to metrics index?"
- Jordan Meyer (author): "Added a bounded retry queue + circuit-breaker state. If write pressure persists we emit an observability.alert_event (low priority) and fall back to rolling local disk (configurable path)."
- Priya Nair (reviewer): "The entropy threshold tuning looks plausible, but we need a short RFC on how we compute entropy (per-token vs per-invocation). Also please ensure we don't shift false positives away from customer-facing SLOs."
- Jordan Meyer: "Added doc section in the design doc and unit tests that assert per-invocation entropy is computed over token-latency distributions; added a regression test simulating false-positive attacks and verified no SLO drift in replaybench."
- Ethan Li (reviewer): "Can we add an e2e that exercises suppression on the replaybench with a synthetic noisy cohort?"
- Jordan Meyer: "Added replaybench scenario 'harvest-noisy-cohort' and e2e pipeline job. CI included it as an opt-in slow test."
- Reviewer approval: Sofia (approved), Priya (approved after small doc updates), Ethan (approved).

CI notes:
- Initial run: build passed, unit tests passed, integration flakes: tests/e2e/replaybench/harvest_noisy_cohort timed out on first try.
- Rerun: flaky timing fixed by bumping timeouts in test harness; final CI status: pass.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (canary): deploy aggregator to observability namespace with flag disabled globally; enable for internal tenants only (2 days).
- Stage 2 (pilot): enable for 10 beta customers, monitor suppression effect and false-negative rate against annotated incidents (1 week).
- Stage 3 (gradual): roll out to 50% of tenants with progressive autoscale and alerting calibration.
- Rollback: toggle feature flag off; aggregator drains and flushes pending rollups.

Observability and monitoring:
- New metrics: obs.harvest.rollup.size, obs.harvest.rollup.latency_p50/p95, obs.harvest.write.errors, obs.entropy.suppression_score
- New spans: harvest.collector.receive -> harvest.aggregator.compress -> harvest.encoder.write (all instrumented with trace IDs for correlation)
- Logging: structured log field harvest_id and cohort_id added to sampled logs; debug endpoint /debug/harvest/state exposes in-memory queue lengths.

Runbook highlights (ops/runbooks/harvest-runbook.md):
- Symptoms: sudden increase in obs.harvest.write.errors or suppression_score spike
- Quick fix: toggle feature flag, restart aggregator pods in order
- RCA pointers: check disk pressure, metrics index write latency, and replaybench scenario results

Backwards compatibility:
- No breaking API changes. Metric names are new but the aggregator writes into existing metric store. The governor is additive and disabled unless explicitly enabled.

Security and privacy:
- Aggregator only consumes already-sampled fragments (no new PII surface created). Rollup encoding strips free-form text unless the tenant opts into enhanced retention (logged in config).

Testing:
- Added unit tests for entropy computation, compaction invariants, and governor attenuation math.
- Added replaybench e2e that simulates noisy cohorts at different shapes and verifies alert delta reduction without SLO drift.

Release notes: See release_notes field.

Misc:
- Added a small CLI tool (pkg/observability/harvest/ctl) to inspect and drain local queue for debugging (admin-only).
- Performance: Aggregator optimized for lock-free ring buffers and uses sharded workers; local bench shows ~5k fragments/sec per pod at 50th percentile CPU on c5-standard-4 equivalent.

Merge: Squash-merged into main on 2025-11-18 by Sofia Alvarez.
Added an invocation harvest aggregator service that compacts sampled invocation fragments into token-level rollups, enriched spans and structured logs; introduced an alert-entropy governor to reduce noisy alerting — configurable, off by default for older tenants.
payload.title: Introduce invocation-harvest aggregator + alert-entropy governor for noisy-signal suppression

payload.body:
Motivation: Tenant workloads show recurring micro-patterns that are not well captured by the existing static batch templates. This PR adds a batch-pattern compiler that consumes recent request traces and emits compact, tenant-scoped batching templates plus a paired compact quantization profile telemetry pipeline so the Optimize layer can recommend lower-cost model variants without losing quality. Scope: 1) batch-pattern compiler service (server component and CLI to compile patterns from trace snapshots); 2) compact quant telemetry exporter that aggregates per-pattern token distributions and per-model quantization sensitivity metrics; 3) lightweight simulation harness used by CI to validate unit economics vs baseline; 4) minimal Console integration: a read-only API endpoint surfaces the top-3 generated patterns for a tenant. Implementation notes: the compiler is conservative by default (max batch-size delta +/− 20%) and emits safe fallbacks. The telemetry export uses a compact protobuf envelope and ships via the existing telemetry pipeline with optional batching disabled for immediate visibility. Rollout plan: staged deploy to canary tenant group -> 48h metrics observe window -> ramp to 20% -> full. Includes feature flag redwood.features.batch_pattern_compiler and a tenant opt-in tag. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (ENG-4572) - [x] Compiler server + CLI - [x] Telemetry exporter + aggregator - [x] CI harness and smoke bench - [x] Console API + minimal UI stub - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs: runbook and operator notes What this PR is not: it does not change default batching in production (only suggests defaults via Optimize), it does not auto-apply quant profiles without a manual review. Backwards compatibility: existing batch templates remain untouched; compiler outputs are stored under tenant preference namespace v2. Related work: ENG-4572 (design), ENG-5031 (Optimize integration), SUP-1209 (customer request), RFC-2025 (telemetry envelope). Risks & mitigations: risk of overaggressive batching -> mitigated by conservative deltas and canary. Risk of telemetry volume -> mitigated by compact envelope, sampling, and off-peak upload window. QA notes: simulation harness compares cost-per-100k-tokens and p95 latency against mainline presets and fails CI if cost drops >30% with latency increase >15%. Merge: squash. Release notes included below.
Diego Morales: Can we guarantee the compiler will not increase median latency for small payloads? Suggest a regression test in sim harness.
Alyssa Chen: Added a latency regression check to CI harness; compiler has a small-sample guard that forces fallback to tenant preset for payloads < 64 tokens.
Priya Singh: Telemetry envelope looks good but we need retention spec; please add TTL and sampling notes to runbook.
Alyssa Chen: Added TTL=30d by default and sampling config. Updated docs/oncall/batch-pattern-runbook.md.
Evan Brooks: Code looks good, minor nit on variable naming in compact_aggregator_service.go (renamed in follow-up commit). Approved.
Final approval after CI was green and bench smoke passed. Diego and Priya signed off after latency & TTL mitigations were added. Plan: canary deploy 2026-03-02, observe 48h, ramp per runbook.
Introduce batch-pattern compiler: generates tenant-specific batching templates and compact quant telemetry to enable Optimize to recommend cost-saving model/quant profiles. Rollout is gated behind a feature flag and tenant opt-in. No automatic changes to production batching; operators can review recommended patterns in the Console. Includes CI simulation harness to prevent regressions.
Feature flag: redwood.features.batch_pattern_compiler. Tenant opt-in via tag 'batch-pattern-v2'. Canary cluster and helm values updated in charts/helm/redwood-values-cost-telemetry.yml. Monitor p95 latency, token cost, and telemetry ingress volume. If regressions detected, flip feature-flag-off and rollback helm release.

payload.body:
Introduce CredentialMode enum across Python/TS/Go SDKs, add a peekable streaming iterator to improve ergonomic consumption of chunked responses, harmonize retry/backoff presets, and bump SDK package versions to align with the new session APIs.
Context: Multiple SDK consumers requested clearer credential behaviors and a simpler streaming consumer pattern. This PR introduces a small, explicit CredentialMode enum (AUTO|PINNED|DELEGATED) across the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs, harmonizes default retry/backoff presets to match runtime SLOs, and adds a peekable stream iterator abstraction to make chunk-aware consumers easier to write. Motivation: reduce accidental double-refreshes, improve cross-lang parity for session lifecycle, and reduce user code complexity when implementing lookahead on streaming responses. Summary of changes: - Add CredentialMode contract and adapter in core session layer (sdks/*/session) - Implement CredentialMode-aware credential provider fallback chain with telemetry hooks - Add PeekableStreamIterator (py: IterablePeek, ts: PeekableAsyncIterator, go: PeekableChan) with small memory bounds and deterministic close semantics - Align retry presets and expose an ergonomic RetryProfile builder for advanced use - Add compatibility shim for Node backpressure (ts) preventing unbounded in-memory buffering - Update docs and migration notes and bump package versions (py 2.8.0, ts 1.16.0, go v0.10.0) Checklist: [x] unit tests for credential modes and adapter chains [x] integration tests for stream iterator under chunked responses [x] e2e smoke on hosted API against a Canary model [x] docs: cross-sdk migration guide and examples [x] changelog entries Impact: API surface additions are additive (new enum, new iterator helper). There is a recommended migration for advanced users who previously relied on implicit token refresh side-effects. See release notes for steps.
High-level: 1) If you previously relied on implicit refresh side-effects, set CredentialMode=PINNED to preserve behavior or migrate to AUTO with tests. 2) Replace legacy StreamHelper.peek hacks with PeekableStreamIterator for lookahead. 3) Update retry presets only if you used custom backoff - new defaults are safer for low-latency workloads.
Unit tests added for edge cases: stale token during long-lived stream, peek after close, concurrent peek+next races. Local fuzzing run (1000 randomized message boundaries) showed stable memory under the configured peek window. Manual verification: python example consumer using IterablePeek consumes first N tokens without needing to buffer the rest; TS sample shows backpressure preserved when piping to a writable stream. Go integration ran on a small Dedicated cluster and showed no deadlocks after the token fetch mutex fix.
Priya: Can we avoid shipping both Peekable and the older StreamHelper to prevent confusion? Author: Kept StreamHelper for backwards compatibility but marked deprecated and added a migration note. Liam: The CredentialMode.Auto fallback still triggered two refreshes in a race when the session lease expired; added a token fetch mutex in Go and a guarded promise in TS to serialize refresh. Diego: Request to expose telemetry tag for credential_mode in metrics; added tag and unit tests. Priya: CI flake on the typescript backpressure test; root cause was the Node stream draining order — added a small delay to the test and hardened the shim. Approvals: Priya approved after fixes, Liam approved after addressing double-refresh races, Diego approved with telemetry change.

payload.body:
Summary: This PR introduces a compact adapter layer across the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs that standardizes session telemetry envelopes, simplifies the streaming handoff surface, and provides a compatibility bridge so existing consumers can opt into the new ergonomics incrementally. Motivation: Multiple internal integrations observed inconsistent session envelope shapes, duplicated telemetry keys, and slightly different retry defaults between SDKs leading to confusion for platform teams and noisy alerting. This was called out in ENG-2143 and tracked as part of cross-SDK parity work in ENG-2199. Goals: (1) standardize the session telemetry payload and sampling keys across SDKs; (2) provide a minimal adapter that consumers can layer over existing session code to get the new semantics with zero downtime; (3) align retry default presets for streaming and token refresh so cross-language clients have comparable behavior; (4) bump SDK minor versions that contain the ergonomic API surface. Changes: - Core: new compact adapter module implemented in each SDK repo (redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-typescript, redwood-sdk-go) and exported from the polyglot 'redwood' root package so examples can import a single compatibility shims path. - Telemetry: unified envelope format: {"session_id","span_id","sampling_rate","client_version","env_tags"} and a lightweight sampler hook. Existing telemetry keys are preserved as aliases for backwards compatibility. - Streaming ergonomics: introduced 'CompactSession.handle' API that wraps existing pullstream/pushstream handles and provides a small set of methods (start, pause, drain, handoff) with clearer lifecycle semantics. - Retry presets: converged streaming retry presets to 'aggressive' (low-latency, limited retries), 'balanced' (default), and 'durable' (longer tail, idempotent workloads). SDKs ship default 'balanced' to avoid changing runtime behavior for most users. - Version bumps: python -> 2.6.0, typescript -> 1.9.0, go -> 1.5.1. - Tests: added cross-sdk unit tests for envelope normalization and an interop smoke test that runs in CI job 'sdk-interop'. Commits: - 7b1c3d1: add compact adapter interface and shared docs - 2aa9d4f: implement telemetry envelope normalization + sampler - e3f8b2a: converge streaming retry presets and add presets test - 5c9f6a4: add TS/Go adapter implementations and examples - a9d2f11: interop smoke test CI job + fixture changes - d1c7b52: docs and examples for migration guide Files changed (high level): - python: redwood_sdk/compact_adapter.py, tests/test_compact_adapter.py, setup.cfg - typescript: packages/sdk/src/compactAdapter.ts, packages/sdk/test/compactAdapter.spec.ts, package.json - go: sdk/compact_adapter.go, sdk/compact_adapter_test.go, go.mod - root redwood: docs/sdk/compact-adapter.md, examples/compact-adapter/* - ci: .github/workflows/sdk-interop.yml Testing & CI: First CI run: lint failures in python (docstring/typing) and a flaky TS unit test. Action: fixed typings and tightened test timing assertions in 2aa9d4f. Reran CI: all checks passed including 'sdk-interop' smoke test on linux-1 and linux-2 runners. Performance: microbenchmarks against the prior streaming surface show median latency unchanged and p50 token processing within 3%; memory overhead from the adapter is negligible for typical session sizes. Review thread (selected): - Samir Gupta (review): "Good shape overall. Please justify the chosen defaults for the retry presets in the PR body and add a short note on why 'balanced' is default." - Lena Park (author): "Added presets rationale to the PR description and unit tests that assert behavior. Balanced chosen to prioritize low-risk migration: ~3 retries with jitter for transient errors, preserves prior median latency in our benchmarks." - Priya Nair (review): "Please add a short migration snippet in docs showing how to opt-in with existing code (hand-off example). Also, add a telemetry alias map so that legacy dashboards can continue to work." - Lena Park: "Added examples/docs and telemetry alias map. Updated release notes accordingly." - Ethan Cole (approve): "Approvals from me after CI green and docs added. Small nit left about one TS naming choice; not blocking." Merge details: - Merge method: squash and merge - Merged by: Priya Nair - Merge commit message: "unify(session+telemetry): compact adapter bridge + sdk bumps" Post-merge actions and TODOs: - Backported minimal compatibility shims to the 2.5.x python branch for a critical partner (follow-up PR tracked in Linear ENG-2261). - Monitor telemetry for increased span_count/alerts for first 48 hours (feature flagging gated rollout). - Follow-up: add migration helper that converts historical telemetry in the ingestion pipeline (ENG-2230). Why this is unique from prior parity work: previous PRs focused on individual SDK surface parity (handshake and backoff semantics). This change is a small-footprint adapter + telemetry unification that lets teams adopt new ergonomics piecemeal without large refactors. It also surfaces an explicit compatibility story (alias map + migration docs) to reduce operational flash.
Adds a compact cross-sdk adapter to standardize session telemetry envelopes and reduces SDK surface for streaming handoff; bumps Python/TS/Go SDK versions to align UX. Backwards-compatible; opt-in via feature flag.
Opt-in via REDWOOD_SDK_COMPACT_ADAPTER=true
Interop smoke test added to CI
Minor version bumps across SDKs
payload.title: Unify session telemetry and introduce compact SDK adapter bridge

payload.body:
Context: As part of the model metadata schema v1 rollout + automated changelog generator effort, we need a consistent reviewer workflow for customer-visible release notes. Today reviewers can merge metadata changes without seeing what will actually be published (Console/docs), and we’ve had at least one incident where internal-only notes briefly leaked due to missing checks.

This PR adds a required CI check that (1) computes a model metadata diff for PRs that touch model metadata/schema/template inputs, (2) generates a release note preview (public + internal) using the same templating/category mapping used by the changelog generator, (3) uploads the preview as a GitHub Actions artifact, and (4) fails the build when required fields or redaction rules are violated.

What this does:
- New workflow: "Release note preview (model metadata)" runs on pull_request for changes matching:
  - model-registry/**/models/**/metadata*.json
  - model-registry/**/schemas/model-metadata-schema-v1.json
  - tooling/changelog/** (category mapping/templates)
- Generates two artifacts:
  - release-notes-preview.public.md (what customers will see)
  - release-notes-preview.internal.md (includes internal-only context + audit hints)
  - plus machine-readable JSON counterparts for downstream tools
- Adds validation gates:
  - Required public fields (for any version promotion / compatibility-affecting change): public.summary, public.category, public.severity
  - Redaction enforcement: public output must not contain internal-only fields (e.g., internal.rolloutReason, internal.incidentLinks, internal.evalRunIds)
  - "Breaking" classification guard: if compatibility constraints change (tokenizer/runtime requirements, API compat flags), category must be breaking and must include rollback guidance link
- Posts a GitHub Actions step summary containing:
  - A concise "Release notes preview" section
  - The list of model IDs/versions impacted
  - A reminder that only the artifact is authoritative (step summary is truncated for long notes)

Non-goals:
- This does not implement customer notifications/webhooks.
- This does not rewrite or backfill historical release notes.

Operational notes:
- The check is intended to be required for repos participating in metadata v1 (starting with redwood + redwood-model-registry). Connor will add it to branch protection after this merges.
- Failures are designed to be actionable: the validator prints the exact field path(s) missing / disallowed and links to the internal style guide.

Related:
- pr-18421 (schema v1 + fixtures)
- pr-18441 (changelog generator templates + filtering)
- pr-18435 (event emission for metadata changes)
- ENG-9825 (public vs internal redaction rules)

Test plan:
- Updated fixtures to include a known-good public note and an intentionally invalid note, validated in CI.
- Verified artifact upload and summary rendering on a fork run.
- Manually verified that internal-only fields are stripped in public preview output even when present in metadata.

Rollout:
- Land workflow behind a repo-level toggle (env var REQUIRE_METADATA_RELEASE_NOTE_PREVIEW=true). Defaults to false for now; Release Eng will turn it on per-repo as migrations complete.
Connor O'Brien (Release Eng): This is the gating we need. Two asks: (1) make the artifact name stable so branch protection docs can reference it, and (2) add a link to the style guide in the failure output.
Sahana Iyer (author): Done. Artifact names are now constant (release-notes-preview.*) and validator prints the style guide URL + the relevant section anchor based on the error code.
Marcus Lin (Security): Please ensure we are not printing internal fields into GitHub step summary (visible to anyone with repo read). The artifact is fine, but summary should only include public preview by default.
Sahana Iyer (author): Updated: step summary only includes public preview (first ~80 lines) + counts. Internal preview is artifact-only and requires downloading.
Michael Nguyen (Control Plane): Can we detect promotions vs metadata-only edits? We only want to require public.summary/category/severity on promotions and compat-affecting changes.
Sahana Iyer (author): Added a heuristic: required fields enforced when (a) version promoted flag present in diff, or (b) compat/requirements fields changed (tokenizer/runtime/min_rim_version/quant profile). Otherwise it generates preview but does not hard-fail missing summary.
Jada Williams (Console/Tooling): Please ensure category mapping matches the generator in pr-18441; we got drift once before.
Sahana Iyer (author): Preview generator imports the same category mapping module used by changelog generator (tooling/changelog/category_map). Added a unit test to prevent divergence.
Connor O'Brien: LGTM once you flip the default toggle to false (so we can roll out incrementally).
Sahana Iyer (author): Toggle defaulted to false; workflow exits early with a notice if not enabled.
Internal: Adds required CI check to generate customer-visible release note previews from model metadata diffs and fail PRs on missing required fields or redaction violations.
payload.title: Add CI check: release note preview artifact on model metadata diff

payload.body:
Motivation: We see recurring low-signal cost regressions tied to prompt-shape shifts (different prompt lengths / role-token mixes). Existing token-level cost metrics show totals but do not surface subtle distributional drift across segments of the prompt. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) a telemetry-gradient metric that tracks per-invocation changes in token-cost density across prompt segments (head/mid/tail) so we can detect gradual drift; 2) a 'cost shingle inspector' abstraction that slices invocations into fixed-size token shingles, computes lightweight histograms, and emits compact sketches for downstream aggregation and dashboarding.

Goals: - Detect prompt-shape drift earlier without full trace sampling. - Provide actionable panels in the Console to show which prompt segments and model stages (embedding/encode/generate) are driving cost changes. - Add tuned alerts for gradual drift (low-amplitude, long-window) and a higher-sensitivity alert for sudden spike in tail-cost.

Summary of changes: - telemetry/gradient: new metric generator in the observability pipeline. Computes per-invocation gradients between head/mid/tail cost densities and emits incrementally aggregated counters and sketches. - telemetry/shingle: shingle extractor that emits token-shingle sketches (count-min + percentile sketch) keyed by route + prompt-shape-bucket. Light-weight, safe for high QPS. - console/dashboards: new "Prompt Shape Drift" dashboard with:  * Shingle heatmap (fractional cost per shingle)  * Gradient trend lines (head vs tail)  * Attribution panels (by model stage and kernel) - alerts/rotation: new alert rules and suppression windows to avoid noisy alerts for stable seasonal prompts. - tests: unit tests for shingle extractor, integration test harness (synthetic replay) to validate drift detection and alert thresholds.

Backwards compatibility: instrumentation tags are additive; feature can be controlled by runtime flag telemetry.shingle.enabled=false for on-prem.

Rollout plan: - Stage 1: feature flag off in prod; enable for canary tenants (5%) with verbose sampling. - Stage 2: increase to 25% and enable dashboard ingestion. - Stage 3: global rollout with tuned alerting and canary auto-disable if cost overhead exceeds 1.5%.

Related: ENG-3412 (prompt-shape drift pilot), SUP-789 (customer incident that motivated tail cost alerts).
Evan: Can we bound the extra cardinality introduced by shingle keys? Priya: Shingle key is route + prompt_shape_bucket (3-5 buckets) + stage; we also apply reservoir sampling at 1% by default for high QPS tenants. Maria: Alert thresholds look aggressive for multi-tenant bursts. Suggest adding a rolling baseline with seasonal smoothing. Priya: Added seasonal baseline and a low-sensitivity 'warm' alert group; kept the 'spike' alert high-sensitivity. Samir: Nit: move constants to config and document default cost oversight. Priya: Addressed, moved to helm values and documented. Post-merge: Observability SRE to watch canary and adjust suppression windows on first week.
Added prompt-shape drift detection: telemetry-gradient metric and cost shingle inspector. New Console dashboard ‘Prompt Shape Drift’ and tuned alert rules. Feature gated; default sampling is conservative. Useful for teams tracking token-cost regressions tied to prompt changes.
payload.title: Introduce telemetry-gradient and cost shingle inspector for prompt-shape drift detection

payload.body:
Motivation: We see recurring long-tail latency spikes where downstream token generation spends extra time in prefetch/KV-prefill and late-arriving cache hydrations. Existing token-level metrics attribute cost but do not separate time spent in prefetch vs token emission, which makes root-cause for tail latency noisy and increases paging for on-call.

What this PR does: Adds a lightweight, sampled prefetch tracing layer + a token-delta-latency metric and Grafana heatmap to visualize per-token delta (time between token request and token emission) broken down by prefetch/hydration phases. The tracing hooks are sampled (configurable) and add low-cardinality tags; metric rollups are aggregated server-side and exposed in existing metric export pipelines. Also introduces alert tuning based on the 95/99 delta-latency rollups to reduce noisy incidents.

Changes included (high level): commits listed below; key files changed listed under changed_files. Implementation choices: sampling is controlled by feature-flag and rate-limited per-tenant to avoid PII/high-cardinality. We hash the prefetch-key to a 16-bit bucket to provide distribution visibility without raw keys. Heatmap panels are prepared as a JSON dashboard that can be imported into Grafana.

Backward compatibility and rollout: Feature gated behind runtime flag (runtime.prefetch_tracing.enabled) and a per-tenant rate cap. Default: off for all tenants; rollout plan: internal dogfood -> beta tenants -> global. No breaking API changes.

Testing and validation: unit tests for collector and hash-bucketing added; an integration test simulates KV late-arrival and asserts delta attribution and metrics emitted. Load-tested in perf lab at 2x baseline QPS with sampling enabled to verify <1% CPU overhead in the runtime trace path.

Follow-ups (future work): integrate heatmap with token-cost attribution view, add span-level correlation to user-facing request IDs for easier drill-down, and add a compact aggregation for long-term retention.

Checklist:
- [x] Add sampled tracing hooks and span enrichment
- [x] Emit token-delta-latency metric and rollup labels
- [x] Add Grafana heatmap and dashboard JSON
- [x] Documentation page and rollout notes
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Feature-flag and tenant rate limiting
Samir Patel (2026-02-16): This is great direction. Concern: are we introducing a new high-cardinality tag (prefetch_key)? Please confirm hashing and cardinality limits.
Author reply (Anika): We hash to a 16-bit bucket and rate-limit per-tenant. The raw key is never exported. Added tests to assert bucket distribution.
Marta Ruiz (2026-02-18): Can we expose the sampling rate metric so we can reason about observability coverage? Also add a Grafana panel for sampling rate.
Author reply (Anika): Added runtime.prefetch_tracing.sample_rate metric and included a small panel in the dashboard JSON (commit f9c3b22).
Ethan Cole (2026-02-20): Tests look good, but please add an integration test that simulates late KV hydration causing >50ms token delta.
Author reply (Anika): Added integration test that asserts metric rollup and trace presence (test/integration/prefetch_tracing_test.go). CI initially failed on lint; fixed import ordering and updated docs formatting.
Adds sampled prefetch tracing and token-delta-latency heatmap for better attribution of long-tail latency; feature-gated and rollout controlled; includes alert smoothing to reduce noisy delta-latency incidents.
payload.title: Introduce sampled prefetch tracing and delta-token-latency heatmap

Adds a runway reservation controller that allocates short-lived runway credits per tenant to smooth sudden spikes and a lightweight fallback path to best-effort pools when runway is exhausted. Includes new telemetry (runway_seconds, runway_depletion_rate) and config knobs for operators.
Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally experience short, high-frequency spike patterns that trigger emergency scaling and cross-tenant interference. Existing burst tokens are effective for single-shot bursts but do not account for recurring micro-spikes which cause oscillation. This PR introduces a lightweight ‘runway’ concept: a small, time-buffered reservation allocated per tenant that can be consumed continuously for short windows, enabling the autoscaler to absorb micro-bursts without immediate scale actions or draining warm pools.

Design summary: 1) RunwayReservationController: reconciles per-tenant runway balance (seconds * vCPU-equivalent) and top-ups based on observed admission rate and historical depletion. 2) Runway-aware admission path: admission checks consult runway balance first, decrementing in a streaming-safe manner; requests exceeding runway fall back to configured best-effort lanes instead of immediately failing or triggering scale-ups. 3) Depletion hedging: if runway depletion rate exceeds a configured threshold, the autoscaler receives a 'runway_pressure' signal which adjusts fast-path headroom and temporarily biases prewarming policies. 4) Telemetry and diagnostics: new metrics runway_seconds, runway_depletion_rate, runway_topup_events and runway_fallback_count; traces include runway decisions for sampled requests. 5) Operator controls: cluster-level defaults and per-tenant overrides; a conservative rollout plan with gated sampling and percent-of-tenants opt-in.

What changed (high level): - runtime/admission/runway_controller.go: reconciliation loop and in-memory ledger with epoched top-ups - runtime/admission/runway_store.go: durable checkpointing to etcd with backoff and compacting - runtime/admission/handler.go: admission path integration and fallback routing - autoscaler/signals/runway_pressure.go: emits signals consumed by scale decider - observability/metrics/runway.prom: metric definitions + dashboard snippets - docs/ops/runway.md: operator guide and rollout checklist - internal/tests/runway: unit + integration harness simulating spike patterns + load-tests updated to validate stability

Testing and CI: unit tests added for controller reconciliation and store failure modes; integration test simulates a tenant with micro-spike pattern and verifies reduced emergency scale events. CI initially showed a flaky integration test (integration/runway/reconcile_test) related to timing windows; fixed by switching to deterministic fake clock and adding tighter backoff expectations. All CI checks green at merge time.

Performance: internal mixed-workload benchmark (100 tenants, 30% bursty) shows ~12% improvement in p95 request latency tail and a ~35% reduction in emergency scale operations over the previous burst-token-only strategy. Memory and CPU overhead is small (controller steady-state ~60MB, negligible per-admission cost due to compact ledger).

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy controller disabled by default in staging; 2) Enable for 5% of tenants with conservative runway (3s equivalent) and monitor runway_depletion_rate + fallback_count for 72h; 3) Gradually increase to 25% and tune top-up heuristics; 4) Default-on for Dedicated clusters after 4-week observation and operator sign-off.

Migration and safety: runway store uses versioned keys; safe default when store is unavailable is 'no runway' which preserves pre-existing behavior (requests go to existing burst handling). There is an opt-out label per-tenant for immediate rollback.

Notes: this is an operationally-sensitive change — operations should watch the new metrics and the autoscaler fast-path behavior during rollout. See docs/ops/runway.md for full checklist.
Arjun Patel: Please add a clear invariant for runway bookkeeping on controller restarts — what guarantees do we provide for double-decrement?
Lila Chen: Added an epoched checkpoint and idempotency token to runway_store; controller reconciler uses idempotent top-up ops to avoid double-decrement on restarts (see runway_store.go lines ~120-210).
Sofia Martinez: Can we expose an emergency-disable flag to opt tenants out in case fallback causes regressions?
Lila Chen: Added tenant label opt-out and a cluster-level emergency_disable flag. Documented in ops/runway.md under 'Rollout and rollback'.
Ben Wallace: observed a race in the admission path when runways were exhausted and fallback routing tried to hit a cold best-effort pool; we should add a 50ms hedging window before fallback to prefer brief KV cache hits.
Lila Chen: Implemented a hedging window with a simple cooldown counter; tests added to cover the hedged path.
payload.title: introduce-runway-reservation-controller-and-fallback-burst-paths

Problem: our demo tenant Console views (usage, latency percentiles, error analysis, cost breakdown) frequently show empty/flat graphs right before a live demo, and the distributions look obviously “fake” when we do a quick manual warm-up. This PR introduces a synthetic traffic generator that continuously produces realistic, policy-driven demo traffic and emits the same telemetry path as real inference (usage + latency + error + trace hooks) so dashboards stay populated and believable. What’s included: (1) a k8s CronJob + ad-hoc runner that hits the demo org’s routes via the public gateway (not direct ingestion) to exercise auth, rate limits, routing, and fallbacks; (2) preset configs (steady, executive-10min, spike, rollout-canary) to cover common demo narratives; (3) a small library for sampling realistic request shapes (prompt length distribution, streaming vs non-streaming mix, tool-calling frequency, structured output schema usage) and injecting controlled error rates (timeouts, 429s, tool validation failures) without overwhelming the tenant; (4) guardrails to ensure this can ONLY target the demo org/project allowlist and cannot run against prod/customer orgs. Motivation: make the demo tenant resilient to “dashboard emptiness” and give SEs a one-command way to warm up the tenant prior to a call, while also generating data that makes cost/latency tradeoffs and reliability/fallback flows visible in the Console. Rollout plan: merge behind DEMO_SYNTH_TRAFFIC_ENABLED, enable in demo env only, then let SRE tune the default schedule/caps after a week of observation.
Traffic is generated via the same public gateway path used by the demo app (so we get auth, quotas, routing, retries, and streaming behavior); requests are labeled with `x-redwood-traffic-source: demo_synth` and scenario tags (scenario=steady|spike|rollout_canary, feature=streaming|tool_calling|structured_output, region=us-east|eu-west). Presets control: QPS target + jitter, streaming ratio, model mix weights, token length distributions, tool-call rate, structured output schema selection, and “controlled failure” knobs. Guardrails: hard allowlist on org_id + project_id, environment check (must be DEMO env), and a max spend cap per hour (tokens + embeddings units) with immediate stop on breach. The CronJob uses a dedicated service account with egress restricted to the gateway; it does not have permissions to call internal admin endpoints.
Unit: distribution sampling (p50/p95 bounds), config parsing, allowlist enforcement; Integration (staging): `rw demo traffic run --preset executive-10min --dry-run=false` against staging demo org, verified dashboards populate within ~2–4 minutes; Load sanity: steady preset capped to avoid triggering 429s (unless explicitly enabled via spike preset).
Logan Wright: Can we confirm these events follow the same aggregation windows as real traffic? If we’re tagging them, we should make sure dashboards default include them (or at least demo views do).
Mei Lin (author): Yep—these are real gateway requests, so telemetry is emitted through the normal pipeline. I added `source=demo_synth` as a tag, but dashboards are not filtering it out. We can add a future improvement to let Console toggle “exclude synthetic”.
Chloe Martin: Please avoid creating new “special” ingestion paths. Looks like this is using gateway, which is good. One concern: structured-output scenario should not depend on any flaky schema validation service; can we keep it self-contained?
Mei Lin (author): Agreed. Structured output uses inline JSON schema and validates locally in the runner (and still sends the schema in the request). No external dependency besides the inference route.
Allison Grant: For the spike preset, can we ensure it doesn’t page us by default? We should route alerts for demo env separately, but until that’s fully in place I’d prefer spike preset disabled unless explicitly run.
Mei Lin (author): Updated presets: CronJob only runs steady; spike preset is manual-only via CLI and has an explicit `--i-understand-this-may-trigger-alerts` confirmation gate.
Sean Gallagher: Add a hard cap to prevent runaway spend if someone bumps QPS. Also, if gateway returns 401/403 (key rotated), runner should fail fast and surface a crisp error message.
Mei Lin (author): Added `max_tokens_per_hour` + `max_requests_per_run` caps and fail-fast on auth errors with a remediation message pointing to the key rotation runbook. Also added a health summary at end of run.
Markus Klein: This is exactly what the SE team needs. Please include a quick-start snippet for ‘dashboards empty’ so we can paste into Slack during a panic.
Mei Lin (author): Added `docs/internal/demo/demo-dashboards-warmup.md` with a 30-second copy/paste section and expected time-to-first-graph.
Merged via squash into main; follow-up task: tune CronJob schedule and caps after observing a week of demo usage (ENG-4879 alerts will land separately).
Internal-only: Demo environment now has a synthetic traffic generator (CronJob + CLI) to keep Console dashboards populated with realistic distributions; supports presets for steady traffic and common demo narratives.
payload.title: Seed synthetic traffic generator for demo dashboards (job + presets)

Motivation: customers operating in regulated jurisdictions require stronger evidence about access decisions and KMS usage, plus automated detection of unusual privilege changes. This PR adds three coordinated pieces: 1) an RBAC Anomaly Detector that samples policy decisions and surfaces statistical deviations (new service + control plane telemetry), 2) a KMS Usage Ledger that records per-tenant, per-key KMS call metadata for non-repudiable audit and residency verification, and 3) a Jurisdictional Pin Gate that enforces region-pin policies at the KMS allocation layer and emits canonical audit events for downstream compliance pipelines. The goals are: reduce investigation time for policy breaches, provide provable KMS usage trails for compliance audits, and enforce region pin constraints at the decision point to avoid accidental cross-region key use. Changes in this PR touch: policy evaluation path, audit forwarder, KMS allocation middleware, migrations for the ledger schema, the console telemetry surface, and operator-facing rollout flags. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-9485) - [x] Unit + integration tests for policy sampler - [x] Ledger write path is idempotent and signed - [x] Backwards-compatible migration and feature flag - [x] Console telemetry panels added - [x] e2e scenario for region-pin enforcement (simulated cross-region request) Backwards compatibility: the anomaly detector is opt-in and behind "rbac_anomaly_enabled" feature flag. KMS ledger writes are opt-in per-tenant until a migration window closes. Rollout plan: gradual enablement by tenant cohort, tie ledger writes to audit retention throttles, monitor error rates and key write latency. See commits for incremental scope and the review thread for design clarifications.
Liam Nguyen (2025-02-13): Nice direction. Two asks: (1) how do we bound false positives for the anomaly detector so SRE doesn't get paged? (2) ledger writes need to be resilient to transient DB errors. Can you add backoff and non-blocking fallback?
Aisha Patel (2025-02-13): Replied: added exponential backoff + circuit breaker for ledger writes, detector uses an adjustable baseline window and an anomaly-confidence threshold; default is conservative (only P>0.999 alerts). Added config to route low-confidence alerts to a noiseless 'review' stream instead of pages.
Sofia Alvarez (2025-02-14): We need a clear privacy/legal review for storing KMS call metadata. Please ensure tenant opt-in and a data-retention TTL per-tenant. Also: mandate KMS key-id hashing before storing any identifier in non-secure stores.
Aisha Patel (2025-02-15): Replied: implemented per-tenant opt-in flag, retention TTL, and HMAC-prefix hashing of key IDs before writing to ledger. Sensitive raw IDs are only stored in the sealed PostgreSQL column encrypted with CMK; non-sensitive indexes use hashed prefixes.
Marcus Reed (2025-02-16): Test comment: e2e simulated tenant with region pin should reject cross-region KMS allocation and emit a signed audit event; test flaked once in CI (timing).
Aisha Patel (2025-02-16): Flakiness debug: extended the test timeout and added an eventual consistency assertion for the fanout queue. Reran locally and CI.
Liam Nguyen (2025-02-18): Approve after nit fixes.
Sofia Alvarez (2025-02-19): Approve. Note: legal signoff attached to the Linear ticket SEC-223.
Added opt-in RBAC anomaly detection service, per-tenant KMS usage ledger for verifiable audit trails, and a jurisdictional pin gate preventing KMS allocations across pinned regions. Feature is behind flags; see docs/compliance/kms_ledger_guide.md for tenant opt-in, retention controls, and migration steps.
payload.title: Introduce RBAC anomaly detector, KMS usage ledger, and jurisdictional pin gate

Context and motivation: We've received recurring feedback that SDK consumers want an explicit, ergonomic concept for short-lived auth leases, and a small set of named retry profiles that can be wire-mapped across Python/TS/Go to avoid subtle divergence. This PR introduces a lightweight 'lease' lifecycle API (acquire/renew/release/annotate) and a compact mapping of retry 'flavors' (optimistic, balanced, aggressive) that the SDKs expose in parity. It also clarifies pullstream semantics: deprecates the older opaque resume-token surface in favor of a checkpoint cursor and documents recommended migration paths.

What this changes (high level):
- Adds a Lease abstraction to SDK core (py/ts/go) + low-overhead heartbeat shim for long-running streams.
- Introduces named retry flavors and a small declarative adapter so platform defaults can be propagated across languages.
- Pullstream: replace ResumeToken v1 surface with CheckpointCursor v2; provide compat shim that translates legacy tokens at runtime to minimize breakage.
- Adds cross-sdk integration tests that exercise lease renewals during streaming disconnects.
- Minor telemetry/metrics labels to differentiate lease renewals vs token refreshes for cost/ops visibility.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked, [x] unit tests added, [x] cross-sdk integration tests, [x] update changelogs/versions, [x] migration notes for users.

Design doc: https://linear.redwoodhq.com/ENG-2145
Migration notes: docs/sdk/migration/lease-and-checkpoint.md
Diego Rivera: This design looks sensible; can we make the Lease.renew() non-blocking by default? Some consumers run renewals on a background timer and expect a soft failure path.
Asha: Good catch — changed renew() to accept {blocking?: boolean} and added a lightweight callback hook for errors.
Lena Hoffmann: Strong +1 on named retry flavors but request: ensure the mapping to underlying backoff multipliers is documented and not changed silently.
Asha: Added explicit constants doc block and an integration test that asserts the mapping is stable.
Marcus Lee: There's a race in the Go shim when legacy ResumeToken joins a stream mid-lease. Requesting an explicit test and a short delay backoff.
Asha: Added test 'TestCompatResumeDuringLease' and a 150ms jittered backoff in the shim to avoid thundering renewals.
Add non-blocking renew API and ensure all SDKs expose an ergonomic default
Document retry flavor mappings and add integration asserts
Add compatibility test for resume-token -> checkpoint conversion under lease churn
Addressed non-blocking renew: updated SDK signatures in py/ts/go and kept blocking semantics available via option
Added docs/runtime assertions for retry flavor mapping and a changelog note
Added compat integration test that reproduces previous flake seen in incident SUP-4021
- Introduce Lease API (acquire/renew/release/annotate) across Python/TypeScript/Go.
- Add named retry flavors (optimistic, balanced, aggressive) and documented mappings.
- Pullstream: CheckpointCursor v2 introduced; compat shim provided for ResumeToken v1.
- Cross-SDK integration tests for lease renewals and resume compatibility.
- SDK version bumps: python 0.22.0, typescript 1.12.0, go v0.9.1.
This PR intentionally provides a compat shim for ResumeToken v1 to avoid an immediate breaking migration. We plan to mark ResumeToken v1 deprecated in the next minor release and remove the shim in one major cycle. Ops: added telemetry labels lease.renew and lease.acquire to help SREs tune defaults.
payload.title: Introduce first-class lease auth profiles, named retry flavors, and pullstream clarifications across SDKs

Context: Production incidents in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 showed fast cross-region evictions during short egress saturation bursts. The SLO enforcer responded by aggressively evicting tenants, which amplified load and extended recovery windows. This PR introduces the 'pacing sentinel' — a small runtime controller that makes eviction decisions with an additional telemetry-anchored soft eviction fence and a sticky probe mechanism to avoid cascade eviction during transient egress spikes. Motivation: reduce tenant churn during short-lived regional surges while preserving SLO enforcement guarantees. Key behaviors: 1) Telemetry anchoring: the sentinel consumes recent egress and latency quantiles and computes a confidence-weighted egress pressure score. 2) Soft eviction fence: when egress pressure is near threshold, instead of immediate eviction, the sentinel applies a soft fence that reduces new admission tokens for lower-priority tenants (pacing tokens) and delays hard eviction by a short, bounded window. 3) Sticky probe: once a tenant is soft-fenced, a periodic sticky probe (single-request probe) checks if the tenant can be restored without causing oscillation; probes are rate-limited and randomized to avoid synchronized restarts. 4) Gradual restore: when pressure subsides, tokens are restored incrementally with a warmup period to avoid immediate re-surge. Files touched: runtime eviction state machine (pacing_sentinel.go), telemetry anchor (egress_anchor.go), SLO enforcer integration (enforcer.go), helm toggle and values, tests, docs, and console UI for observability. Checklist: - [x] Design doc: docs/architecture/pacing-sentinel.md - [x] Unit tests: tests/slo/pacing_sentinel_test.go (coverage for fence decisions, probe timing, restore path) - [x] Integration tests: local canary run in us-west-2 simulating egress spikes - [x] Console metrics/alerts wired: web/console/alerts/pacing-sentinel-ui.tsx - [x] Helm flag: deploy/helm/values-eviction.yaml (feature gated) - [x] Backwards compatible: integrates with existing enforcer without schema changes. Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind helm feature flag off by default. 2) Enable in us-west-2 for 10% of traffic (canary) for 24h while monitoring these metrics: egress_pressure_score (p50/p95), eviction_rate_by_tenant, soft_fence_rate, restore_success_ratio. 3) If canary is stable (<5% change in end-to-end tail latency and eviction_rate decreases), expand to region. 4) Global rollout only after two full days of regional stability. Observability and alerts: added pacing_sentinel.fence_applied, pacing_sentinel.probe_failures, pacing_sentinel.restore_rate. Alert thresholds included in docs. CI: initial CI run failed on lint/format; fixed in final commit d4f7a90. Final CI: all unit tests pass and integration harness completes in simulated canary mode. Review summary: Jin Park: requested clearer bounds on probe frequency and token decay; added deterministic rate limiter and updated tests. Noah Patel: asked for telemetry smoothing window to avoid reacting to single outlier spike; implemented EWMA smoothing with configurable alpha. Sandra Li: requested canary rollout recipe and runbook addition; added runbook steps and rollback procedure to docs/architecture/pacing-sentinel.md. Merge notes: Squash merge to preserve a single logical change. Backout plan: helm toggle off; sentinel is stateless and leaves existing eviction logic untouched when feature flag is off. Risks and mitigations: Risk of increased tail latency if probes cause sudden burst — mitigated by randomized probe jitter and strict probe rate limits. Risk of under-eviction leaving system overloaded — we keep hard-ejection fallback after soft-fence window expiry and also expose emergency override via SRE console. Release notes: "Introduce pacing sentinel: a telemetry-driven soft eviction fence and sticky probe to reduce cascade evictions during short regional egress surges. Can be enabled via helm feature flag. Adds new metrics and alerts for monitoring." Merge method: squash and merge.
Jin Park: Please clarify probe frequency and add bounds so probes don't overload a recovering node. — Marisol: added deterministic token bucket limiter for probes and unit tests for bounds.
Noah Patel: Suggest smoothing telemetry to avoid reacting to a single large outlier. — Marisol: implemented EWMA smoothing on egress pressure with configurable alpha and updated docs.
Sandra Li: Add canary rollout and runbook steps for SRE. — Marisol: included step-by-step canary recipe and rollback instructions in docs/architecture/pacing-sentinel.md.
Introduce pacing sentinel: a telemetry-driven soft eviction fence and sticky probe to reduce cascade evictions during short regional egress surges. Can be enabled via helm feature flag. Adds new metrics and alerts for monitoring.
payload.title: Pacing sentinel and soft eviction fence for regional surges
