Context and motivation: In several recent incidents we observed rapid flip-flopping of regional circuits during noisy partial outages. That behavior amplified client retries and triggered downstream capacity cascades. This PR introduces an ephemeral circuit limiter that enforces a short-lived, tenant-aware deny window with a paced reopen strategy to smooth recovery and avoid mass reopen storms. The aim is graceful degradation: let high-priority SLO-bearing tenants continue where possible, slow-roll reopen lower-priority tenants, and surface telemetry to trace circuit lifecycle decisions.

What this changes (single-line continuous body including checklist, testing, and rollout): Implement ephemeral CircuitLimiter that tracks per-tenant deny-windows (TTL), a pacing controller that schedules staggered reopen tokens based on tenant weight and recent success rate, an opt-in config flag in cluster config (runtime.ephemeral_circuit.enabled), and metrics/traces for circuit decisions. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-3421) and reviewed, [x] unit tests for limiter and pacing policy, [x] integration test for multi-tenant reopen pacing, [x] added telemetry (circuit_events, pacing_backoff_ms, tenant_priority) to console dashboards, [x] feature flag + gradual rollout strategy. Testing: unit tests + small cluster integration run on perf-canary; e2e flaky test (region-sim) was rerun twice before green; CI shows all checks passing on final run. Rollout plan: enable feature flag in prod for 10% of traffic per region for 24h, monitor circuit_events and p50/p99 latency; expand to 50% then 100% if no regressions.

Commit summary (high-level): - add CircuitLimiter core with TTL and tenant-weighted token bucket reopen scheduler - integrate limiter into regional failover path and load-shed decisioning - add config flag and admin endpoints to query/clear ephemeral windows - expose telemetry and add Grafana/Console panels - tests + docs + rollout scripts

Changed areas (high level): src/serving/circuit/ephemeral_limiter.rs, src/serving/circuit/mod.rs, src/serving/failover/regional_coordinator.rs, src/serving/pacing/pacing_scheduler.rs, config/cluster/runtime.yaml, observability/metrics/circuit_events.yaml, console/dashboards/ephemeral_circuit.json, tests/integration/ephemeral_reopen.rs, docs/operational/ephemeral-circuit.md. Small code snippets: limiter enforces deny window and returns ReopenSchedule { delay_ms, token_id } rather than immediate reopen; pacing scheduler computes next token time as base_backoff * (1 + jitter * tenant_priority_weight).

Review conversation (summary): Marcus Lee: "Looks good overall — could we avoid holding the global lock while computing next token? Might block failover hot path." Author (Anika): "Good catch — moved computation to lock-free path and added benchmark micro-tests." Ewa Nowak: "How does this interact with existing SLO enforcer? If the enforcer reduces tenant throughput will pacing delay make it worse?" Author: "Pacing is tenant-aware and consults SLO priority; high-SLO tenants get minimal or zero pacing. Also added integration test to assert that high-priority tenants are not delayed under normal success rates." Diego Ramos: "Suggest adding an admin API to clear ephemeral windows for individual tenant during incident." Author: "Added /admin/circuits/clear?tenant_id= and tests; documented in ops runbook." Approvals: Marcus Lee approved after lock fix; Ewa approved after SLO integration test; Diego approved after admin API.

CI summary: CI pipeline (build -> unit -> integration -> e2e) initially failed on e2e region-sim due to timing flakiness; updated test to use simulated clock and retried; final run green. Checks: build (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-tests (pass), e2e (pass on rerun), lint (pass), benchmarks (baseline stable).

Merge and post-merge actions: Squash-merged to main after approvals. Post-merge: feature flag gated; ops runbook updated (docs/operational/ephemeral-circuit.md) with rollout steps and monitoring thresholds. Created console alerts: "EphemeralCircuit: mass-reopen-rate > 5/min" and "EphemeralCircuit: pacing_backoff_ms_p99 > 10s".

Why this is different from previous approaches: Instead of a sticky long-lived circuit or a purely exponential backoff we use short ephemeral windows plus a paced token-based reopen flow that reduces synchronized reopen storms without permanently reducing capacity. The design prioritizes tenant SLOs and observability so SRE and product teams can make data-driven rollout decisions.
Marcus Lee: Looks good overall — could we avoid holding the global lock while computing next token? Might block failover hot path.
Anika Shah: Good catch — moved computation to lock-free path and added benchmark micro-tests.
Ewa Nowak: How does this interact with existing SLO enforcer? If the enforcer reduces tenant throughput will pacing delay make it worse?
Anika Shah: Pacing is tenant-aware and consults SLO priority; high-SLO tenants get minimal or zero pacing. Added integration test to assert high-priority tenants are not delayed.
Diego Ramos: Suggest adding an admin API to clear ephemeral windows for individual tenant during incident.
Anika Shah: Added /admin/circuits/clear?tenant_id= and tests; documented in ops runbook.
Introduce ephemeral circuit limiter with tenant-aware paced reopen to reduce synchronized reopen storms. Feature gated behind runtime.ephemeral_circuit.enabled. Rollout controlled; see docs/operational/ephemeral-circuit.md for thresholds and runbook.
Start with 10% traffic per region, watch EphemeralCircuit: mass-reopen-rate and pacing_backoff_ms_p99. Use admin clear endpoint to force immediate reopen for a tenant during incident. To disable, flip runtime.ephemeral_circuit.enabled=false and clear existing windows.
Integration tests use simulated clock to avoid timing flakiness. Manual canary verification: inject controlled failures in perf-canary and assert staggered reopen across tenants. Verify admin clear works and metrics reflect cleared windows.
payload.title: Introduce ephemeral circuit limiter with paced reopen for regional soft-failover

payload.body:
Motivation: long-lived KV cache entries and block fragmentation were causing elevated tail latency and increased GPU memory pressure under mixed-sequence workloads. This PR introduces a 'soft pin' block allocation strategy and stronger reuse heuristics for the paged KV block manager to reduce allocation churn and eviction storms. Summary of changes: 1) New soft-pin concept for blocks: blocks can be marked soft-pinned when referenced by in-flight decode contexts; they are excluded from immediate eviction but eligible for reuse by same-owner contexts to avoid duplication. 2) Segregated free lists per size class with compact LRU buckets to improve reuse locality. 3) Eviction ranking that factors in last-access timestamp, owner affinity, and live-kv-count to avoid evicting hot multi-token KV pages. 4) GC/compaction path to coalesce small free fragments when fragmentation exceeds threshold. 5) Runtime knobs: kv.soft_pin_v2 (bool), kv.free_list_threshold (int), kv.compact_fraction (float). Design notes: the soft-pin is a lightweight per-block ref-bit plus ownership tag; ownership is used only as a hint for reuse and does not bypass safety checks. Reuse is conservative: blocks reclaimed for reuse must not have active external pointers. Benchmarks: local microbench (mixed chat + completion load, seq distribution 8-1024) shows 10-14% reduction in p99 token-latency and ~12% throughput improvement on T4-equivalent nodes; memory overhead reduced ~6% due to less duplicated KV pages. Rollout plan: feature gated, canary on 5% of hosted traffic, ramp to 50% after 48h if perf signals stable. Backout: revert kv.soft_pin_v2 or set kv.free_list_threshold high. Related work: follow-ups planned to integrate with continuous batching's slot-aware scheduling to further co-locate reuses. Linear tickets: ENG-2143, ENG-2178. Risks: potential subtle race during concurrent eviction and decoder handoff; mitigated with additional CAS checks and stress tests. Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] perf benchmarks, [x] canary script, [x] doc update.
Ravi Gupta: Can you explain why we prefer soft-pin over exclusive pin? I'm worried about stalling eviction under bursty load.
Ava Martinez: Soft-pin is intentionally low-friction; it prevents immediate eviction only for active handoffs and still allows reuse for same-owner contexts. We observed exclusive pins increased memory pressure because pages couldn't be reused quickly.
Marta Lopez: Nit: add a test for concurrent reuse where two decoders race to acquire the same reclaimed block.
Ava Martinez: Added block_allocator_unit.cc to cover that exact race and added CAS checks in reclaim path.
Kenji Sato: lgtm for allocator design; please add a metric for 'soft_pin_reuse_hits' to track benefit post-rollout.
Ava Martinez: Added metric kv.soft_pin_reuse_hits and a perf dashboard row in docs/architecture/kv_cache_design.md.
Improved paged KV block manager with 'soft-pin' allocation, better reuse heuristics, and compaction to reduce fragmentation; expected p99 token latency improvements and reduced memory duplication. Feature gated behind kv.soft_pin_v2.
Canary config provided in scripts/perf/canary_kv_softpin.yaml. Watch metrics: kv.evictions, kv.soft_pin_reuse_hits, kv.compaction_runs, gpu_memory_peak, request_p99_token_latency. Backout: disable kv.soft_pin_v2 and reroute canary traffic.
Local perf: 12% throughput increase under mixed-seq load; p95 improved ~6%, p99 improved 10-14% in T4-like environment. Canary early signal: 8% p99 improvement on 5% traffic after 24h with no increase in evictions.
feature: paged-kv: soft-pin allocator and reuse heuristics (kv.soft_pin_v2) — reduces fragmentation and tail latency.
payload.title: paged-kv: implement soft-pin block allocator and reuse heuristics to reduce fragmentation

payload.body:
Customers observed intermittent microburst patterns that repeatedly pushed Dedicated tenants past short-term P95 latency SLAs despite healthy long-window utilization. This PR introduces a reservoired burst-accountant and a configurable steady-window SLO profile to explicitly decouple short burst allowances from steady throughput guarantees.

What this changes: added a credit reservoir model (per-tenant, per-fleet) that accrues credit when observed usage is below a configurable steady-window baseline, and draws down when short-term bursts exceed nominal throughput. Credits are persisted in the reservation ledger with TTL and soft-eviction semantics. A new steady-window SLO profile (window length, baseline qps, burn-rate caps, recovery rate) can be attached to tenant reservations and accepted by the autoscaler and admission controller. The admission controller now consults the accountant to allow transient overcommit within the credit budget, and emits telemetry so ops can see effective burst headroom and expected exhaustion times.

Why: previous autoscaling heuristics conflated short-term spike handling with long-window capacity planning, leading to noisy scale-ups and SLA flapping. The reservoir model reduces unnecessary scale churn, improves tail latency consistency, and provides an audit trail for transient overages.

Compatibility and opt-in: new behavior is gated behind the feature flag "reservoired_burst_accountant" and is enabled by default for Dedicated fleets started after the release date. Existing fleets will remain on traditional burst heuristics unless opt-in is performed via the Console or API. Backward-compatible admission paths exist: if the accountant data is unavailable, the system falls back to current conservative limits.

Testing and validation: unit tests for ledger persistence, integration tests simulating realistic burst profiles, and a small-scale canary (10 fleets) run in perf-lab. Load tests show P95 latency improvements of 12-18% on bursty workloads and reduced autoscale events by ~28%.

Rollback plan: revert feature flag (ops) to disable accountant and fall back to baseline burst limits. Post-merge tasks: telemetry dashboard, Console opt-in UI, and a follow-up PR to add a per-tenant dry-run mode that reports but does not enforce credit draws.

- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Canary run in perf-lab
- [x] Console flag + API toggle (backend scaffolding included)
- [x] Documentation skeleton for operator-facing runbook

Related: Linear ENG-1829, ENG-1892 (observability follow-up).
Diego Alvarez (review): Could you clarify the semantics when ledger persistence lags? The fallback path looks conservative but we should document the failure modes.
Maya Chen (author): If ledger reads fail we fall back to the existing burst caps; added comment and an integration test that simulates DB latency. See commit d4cbb21.
Priya Raman (review): Telemetry looks good, but can we add a derived metric for credit burn rate per-minute? Ops wants to alert on sustained >80% burn for 5m.
Maya Chen: Added expected_exhaustion_seconds and a burn-rate gauge; will follow up with alerting rules in the observability PR (ENG-1892).
Tomoko Saito (approval): Verified canary results and unit tests locally; LGTM after minor doc wording nit fixed.
Tomoko Saito (merge): Approved and merged via squash.

Motivation: Production teams want a single, explainable signal that summarizes invocation health (latency, cost, cache-warmth, model-fallbacks) and a short-term forecast of token burn to reduce noisy alerts during predictable bursts. This PR introduces a lightweight per-invocation 'inference_health_score' (0-100) plus a token-cost forecast panel that surfaces 1h/6h/24h EWMA forecasts and a confidence band.

What this changes (high level):
- Instrumentation: runtime emits 'inference_health_score', and additional tags: token_cohort, kernel_slot, hw_tier, prefix_warmth. Implemented in serving/telemetry/health_scorer.rs and runtime/tracing/span_enricher.cpp.
- Aggregation/worker: observability/pipelines/forecast_worker.go computes per-tenant EWMA forecasts for token-cost (tokens/sec and token-cost/sec) and writes forecast series to the metrics cache. Forecasts use an EWMA with adaptive alpha (short/long windows) and a confidence band from recent variance.
- Dashboard: grafana/dashboards/inference_health_and_forecast.json adds: health-summary heatmap, forecast sparkline (1h/6h/24h), cohorted bar (by token_cohort), and a causal-log-mosaic link column that deep-links into the trace inspector.
- Alerts: alerting/rules/forecast_slo_rules.yaml includes a forecast-aware alert rule that defers paging if projected 1h burn is within hysteresis threshold; it still fires if the health_score drops below 30 or if a critical fallback rate is observed.

Design notes:
- health_score composition: 40% latency SLO distance, 25% token-cost z-score, 20% prefix_warmth (higher is better), 10% kernel_queue_penalty, 5% recent-model-fallback-rate. The metric is normalized to 0-100 with guarded NaN handling. The algorithm is intentionally transparent (implemented as a deterministic rule in health_scorer.rs) to make RCA easier.
- Forecasting: we opted for EWMA-based forecasting to keep compute cheap in the ingest tier. The worker maintains short (1h), medium (6h), and long (24h) windows and exposes a 'forecast_confidence' derived from window variance.
- Alert tuning: new rule adds a 'forecast_quiet_window' if the projected burn explains the deviation; an 'explainability' label is attached listing the dominant contributor (e.g., "arrival_profile", "kv_cache_cold").

Backward compatibility & opt-out: default is enabled. For Dedicated/Private customers we provide an opt-out via config: observability.features.health_scorer=false. Metric names are stable and documented in docs/observability/metric_catalog.md.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests: health_scorer unit tests cover composition edge cases, NaN handling, and bucket assignment (tests/health_scorer_test.rs).
- Integration: forecast_worker was run in a staging replay (replaybench) for a 72h synthetic workload; dashboard panels validated against the replay and matched expected forecasts within 3% on average.
- Load: worker CPU and memorystore usage measured on staging 2x baseline with no observable impact on ingest pipeline; added a 50ms budget cap per-window evaluation to avoid tail amplification.

Files changed (high level):
- serving/telemetry/health_scorer.rs (+1 file, +210 + / -12) - new scoring logic and unit tests.
- observability/pipelines/forecast_worker.go (+1 file, +120 / -0) - forecast aggregation worker.
- grafana/dashboards/inference_health_and_forecast.json (+1 file, +45 / -1) - dashboard panels and links.
- alerting/rules/forecast_slo_rules.yaml (+1 file, +18 / -0) - alert rule with forecast deferral.
- docs/observability/metric_catalog.md (+1 file, +9 / -0) - documentation for new metrics.
- runtime/tracing/span_enricher.cpp (+1 file, +10 / -50) - minor span tag plumbing.
- ci/observability-tests.yml (+1 file, +0 / -26) - new CI job wiring for dashboard smoke tests.

PromQL examples used in panels (copied here for reviewer convenience):
- health score (per-tenant 90th): quantile_over_time(0.9, inference_health_score{tenant="$tenant"}[1m])
- token burn forecast sparkline: forecast_token_cost{tenant="$tenant", window="1h"}
- cohort breakdown: sum by(token_cohort) (rate(tokens_total[5m]))

Commits (summary):
- Add health scorer implementation and unit tests
- Add forecast worker and integration harness
- Add Grafana panels and alert rules
- Docs: metric catalog and rollout notes
- Fix linting and CI flakiness after initial run

Review conversation (abbreviated, inline):
- Ethan Morales (review): "Algorithm looks reasonable but please split the 40% latency bucket into two (initialization vs running) so we can debug cold-start vs in-flight latency impact."
- Maya Chen (author): "Done — split latency components in health_scorer and added test cases for cold-start contribution."
- Priya Singh (review): "Can we ensure forecasts can't be gamed by synthetic high-variance workloads? Add an upper cap to confidence band and a minimum-window sample requirement."
- Maya Chen: "Added min_samples=20 and capped confidence at 5x rolling stddev; added integration test in replaybench."
- Luca Bianchi (approve): "Nice visualization. One nit: include token_cohort in deep-link to trace inspector so downstream can filter."
- Maya Chen: "Added cohort param to deep-link and updated dashboard JSON."

CI summary: initial run (linux-unit-tests) failed lint (tools/clang-format) — fixed formatting in span_enricher.cpp and health_scorer.rs; re-ran end-to-end observability smoke which passed. New CI job ci/observability-dashboard-smoke was added and passed on staging GRP.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy forecast_worker to staging (done 2026-02-12) and run 72h replaybench.
2) Enable health_scorer (default on) in canary (5% tenant cohort) for 24h; monitor error budgets and dashboard.
3) Gradually ramp to 100% over 72h if no regressions.
4) For Dedicated/Private customers target release notes and an opt-out path.

Rollback: toggle observability.features.health_scorer=false in control-plane or roll worker to previous image. Metrics are additive; disabling removes scoring but does not affect raw latency or token metrics.

Notes for SRE/oncall: the alert rule includes an explanation label and a 'forecast_suppressed' counter; add to runbook: if many suppressed alerts coincide with a high forecast_confidence, treat as expected burst unless health_score < 30.

Thanks to the telemetry and frontend teams for pairing on the dashboard layout and to runtime for quick span-tag plumbing.

Adds a per-invocation inference health score metric and a Grafana forecast panel for token-cost prediction. New alert tuning uses forecasted burn to reduce alert churn. Backwards-compatible instrumentation; opt-out via feature flag.
Ethan Morales: Split latency into cold-start vs runtime — addressed in fd3a1b and tests added.
Priya Singh: Add min_samples and cap confidence band — implemented, replaybench tests included.
Luca Bianchi: Deep-link should include token_cohort — added in dashboard JSON.
QA (automated): observability-dashboard-smoke passed on staging after fix.

Motivation: Reduce sensitive-audit volume while preserving forensic fidelity and ensuring per-call KMS provenance for operator-scoped actions. This PR implements a differential audit-sampling layer (route + risk aware) integrated with an end-to-end KMS call-path reconciler to ensure any sampled event carries provable KMS metadata that can be traced back to the operator credential used. Changes include a sampling policy engine, hooks in the RBACv2 enforcer to emit sampling signals, and a background reconciler that annotates audit events with KMS proofs and retries failed attestations. Checklist: - [x] Sampling engine core + config (feature flagged) - [x] RBAC enforcer hooks for per-request risk tagging - [x] KMS call-path reconcilier with exponential backoff and backfill - [x] Integration tests for sampled vs full-audit behavior - [x] Docs + migration notes - [x] Performance microbenchmarks to validate <3% p50 overhead Related tickets/links: Linear ENG-4820, SEC-900; design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4820/differential-audit-sampling-design; compliance note (internal): https://redwood.internal/docs/compliance/kms-provenance. Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag rbacv2.diff_audit_sampling; default off for enterprise accounts. When enabled, low-risk routes use probabilistic sampling, high-risk routes (policy change, KMS key ops, operator escalation) are always retained. The reconciler runs asynchronously and attaches kms_proof:{provider,region,key_id,nonce,signature} when available. If reconciliation fails after configured retries the audit event is marked audit_status:reconciler_failed and forwarded to a high-priority fanout for compliance reviewers. Backwards compatibility: existing audit consumers see an added metadata block but retain old fields. Migration note: operators that rely on 100% audit capture must set force_full_audit:true per-route in console before enabling this flag.

Lukas: Overall nice work; please add a short doc section explaining the probabilistic seeding so SRE can reason about retention guarantees.
Priya: Added detailed seeding section to docs/compliance/differential_audit.md and included probabilistic bounds; PTAL.
Diego: We need explicit metrics for reconciler failures exposed to the console; please add a counter and prometheus scrape label by region.
Priya: Exposed reconciler.failure_count and reconciler.attempt_latency; added region label and instrumented reconciler.go. Diego approved the change.
Maya: Integration tests look good but flakey locally — I requested the harness seed to be deterministic for CI.

Security review (automated): no cryptographic misuse detected but recommend rotating the temporary nonce format; addressed in c2d9f44 commit.
Integration: deterministic replay harness with seeded RNG (CI-only seed). Added unit tests for sampler policy evaluation (edge cases: 0% and 100% routes). Manual: ran replay with 10M events on perf-lab to validate overhead and reconciler throughput. Observed reconciler steady-state of ~1200 events/s on a 4-vCPU worker with median attach latency 85ms.
Risk: medium. This changes audit volume semantics and adds async reconciliation which temporarily leaves some events without KMS proofs until reconciliation completes. Mitigations: feature flag, console override to force full-audit, reconciler retry/backoff, high-priority fanout for failed reconciliations and alerting. Security: signed KMS proof attached; crypto-review completed.
- Introduces differential audit sampling (feature-flagged) to reduce audit storage cost while preserving forensic coverage for high-risk routes. - Adds KMS call-path reconciler to attach provenance proofs to sampled audit events. - New runtime flags + per-route force_full_audit override. - Metrics: reconciler.failure_count, reconciler.attach_latency, sampler.evaluation_time.

Motivation: This PR adds the 'Econ Orchard' suite — a compact, production-safe set of tools that generate conservative default batching/caching presets, a lightweight micro-sampler for workload-shaped telemetry, and a small quantization profile curator to recommend safe quant variants per SKU. The goal is to accelerate onboarding for customers who want unit-economics-aware defaults without running large-scale profiling jobs.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Implements a mini-sampler agent (orchard-sampler) that runs lightweight request sampling in the runtime path to collect sequence-length distributions, prefix reuse ratios, and short-term tail latency histograms; introduces a Quant Curator service that maps observed telemetry to a small set of tested quantization presets with a safety score; adds an econ-defaults generator that synthesizes tiered batch/cache/quant defaults per deployment SKU (burst, steady, latency-sensitive) and exposes them via the CLI and the Console defaults API; includes a new 'unit-econ quick-checker' CLI command that simulates expected cost/latency delta for candidate presets against recorded traces.

Files and surface changes: - runtime/orchard/mini_sampler.py: sampling agent with extremely small overhead path and failsafe circuit. - runtime/orchard/kv_prefetch_policy.py: new conservative prefetch policy for small caches. - optimizer/quant_curator/*.py: mapping and scoring logic for quant presets. - cli/econ_tool.py: `redwood econ quick-check` and `redwood econ apply-defaults` commands. - docs/quickstarts/econ-orchard.md: one-page guide and safety guidance. - tests/unit/test_mini_sampler.py, tests/integration/test_econ_cli.sh: end-to-end smoke tests.

Operational safeguards: sampling runs at 0.5% by default (configurable), includes an opt-out header for privacy-sensitive customers, and uses moving-window aggregation with caps to avoid memory blowups. The Quant Curator only recommends profiles that were previously exercised on a compatible architecture; every recommendation carries a 'safety_score' and default action is conservative (prefer higher precision when score < 0.9).

Compatibility and rollout: Feature-flagged behind runtime.feature.econ_orchard; we add a canary rollout sequence in the deployment manifest. Defaults generated by this tool do not auto-roll out — they are surfaced in Console and can be applied manually or via the CLI.

Testing and benchmarks: Adds microbenchmarks for sampler overhead (observed ~0.12% median CPU uplift at 0.5% sampling rate), integration test that runs quick-check simulations against a recorded trace and verifies unit-econ delta within expected bands, and end-to-end CI coverage for CLI flows.

Notes and follow-ups: - Follow-up ticket ENG-3301 will add the automatic suggestion card to the Console. - We intentionally keep the quant-curator rule set small (4 presets) to limit complexity and allow easier A/B testing.

Aiden Park: Can we quantify sampler overhead across a corpus of 10 customers? Suggest adding a histogram in the test artifacts.
Sofia Nguyen: Added a microbenchmark and uploaded histogram artifacts in CI; sampler median CPU uplift ~0.12% at 0.5% sampling, 95th ~0.4% (see CI artifact link).
Priya Raman: The safety threshold of 0.9 seems arbitrary. How was that chosen? Can we document the failure modes?
Sofia Nguyen: Threshold chosen after offline replay testing across 6 model/seq combos. Added explanation in docs and a ticket (ENG-3302) to make it tunable per-customer with a controlled experiment pipeline.
Marco Diaz: Small nit — prefer `econ quick-check` to return non-zero exit code on simulated SLA breach so CI can catch it.
Sofia Nguyen: Changed CLI to return code 2 on SLA breach and updated tests accordingly.
Priya Raman: Approving once the CLI help text includes the opt-out header example and the docs call out privacy considerations.
Priya Raman: Approved.
Add Econ Orchard: lightweight sampling, conservative quant profile curator, and tiered default presets (CLI and Console). Opt-in feature-flagged; safe defaults, low-overhead telemetry, and unit-econ quick-checker for previewing cost/latency tradeoffs.
Canary manifest added under deployment/manifests. Enable feature runtime.feature.econ_orchard in canary cluster first. Sampling defaults are 0.5% and can be lowered to 0 for sensitive environments.

payload.body:
Motivation: Customers repeatedly ask for safe, repeatable ways to adopt cost-reduction defaults (batching, prefix caching) and curated quantization profiles while preserving serving SLOs. This PR introduces a human-readable runbook + an 'auto-apply' curation flow for tenant defaults that is conservative by default and observable via telemetry. The runbook ties together: 1) declarative preset profiles (batch/cache/quant) for common workload archetypes; 2) a dry-run simulator that evaluates unit-economics and SLO risk; 3) an opt-in auto-apply path that materializes safe changes as tenant overrides; 4) telemetry hooks and audit records for traceability.
Design summary:
- Presets: new YAML schema under services/econ-runbook/presets/ describing batch_shape, cache_policy, target_quant_profile, acceptable_latency_delta_pct, and rollout_guard. Presets map to tags (e.g., "interactive-small", "batching-high-thr").
- Dry-run simulator: leverages existing workload traces to simulate token-cost, GPU utilization, and 95/99 latency shifts; generates an econ delta report with suggested confidence bands.
- Auto-apply: an operator-approved flow. A runbook action produces a proposed tenant override set stored in the config service; the operator may 'apply' which triggers a canary rollout (5% traffic) followed by a 1h observation window. Automatic rollback if latency/SLO breach or error rate spike > 2x baseline.
- Telemetry: new metrics and spans (econ.runbook.proposal.*, econ.runbook.apply.*, econ.runbook.simulation.summary) with links to correlated traces and the tenant audit log entry.
- Quant profiles: introduce a curated whitelist of quant strategies (q8_qat, q4_vnni-lite, q6_mixed) tied to model families and validated by the simulator. For model families not whitelisted, the runbook recommends fallback-safe profiles.
- Safety: rollout_guard enforces 'no more than X% unit cost reduction per 24h' and refuses aggressive quant profiles for low-latency SLO tenants.
Implementation notes:
- Added a small service (services/econ-runbook) that owns presets, simulation, and runbook state machine.
- Integrations: runtime change applier (runtime/config-applier) which applies overrides to serving runtime; simulator reuses workload-synth from perf-canary.
- UI: console/ops shows proposals and simulation artifacts (CSV and charts).
Checklist:
- [x] Preset schema and example presets
- [x] Simulator implementation and unit tests
- [x] Auto-apply workflow with canary + rollback hooks
- [x] Telemetry and audit log entries
- [x] API surface: POST /runbook/propose, POST /runbook/apply, GET /runbook/simulate
- [x] Docs: runbook README and console help
- [x] Dry-run-only flag for customers to preview without applying
- [x] End-to-end smoke test in CI
Caveats and tradeoffs:
- The simulator is trace-driven; corner cases with extreme tail distributions require conservative rollout_guard thresholds.
- Auto-apply is intentionally gated behind an operator approval in the first rollout; we can relax to fully automated in a later follow-up when we have more historical validation.
Related work and links: Linear ENG-4219 (preset catalog); ENG-4301 (simulator improvements); perf-canary reuse: services/perf-canary/workload-synth; console ticket: DES-88.
Migration: existing tenant defaults are left untouched; proposals create tenant override entries in config service so rollback restores prior state.
Rollout: merged to main, enabled behind feature flag runbook.auto_apply_v1 for a small set of early customers.
Liam O'Neill: Overall this looks strong. Two asks: add a synthetic scenario for high tail-latency and tighten the default rollout_guard for interactive tenants.
Author (Maya Patel): Added high-tail scenario and reduced default acceptable_latency_delta_pct from 10 -> 5 for interactive presets. See commit 11a2f4b.
Diego Alvarez: Please add unit tests that assert auto-rollback triggers when the simulated 99p crosses the SLO threshold.
Author (Maya Patel): Added test_simulation.py::test_auto_rollback_condition that covers the case. Marked as flaky on Windows in CI matrix.
Priya Raman: Telemetry looks good. For audit logs, ensure tenant_id is obfuscated in downstream logs for PII safety.
Introduce an operator-facing econ runbook to propose conservative batching, cache, and quant presets with a simulator-driven dry-run and opt-in canary auto-apply. Feature gated and available to pilot customers. Includes telemetry and audit logs.

payload.body:
Background: Regional incidents and maintenance windows frequently force temporary redistribution of SLO responsibility across regions. Existing failover semantics are abrupt: either route fully to a fallback region or trigger a global throttle, which causes avoidable churn and user-visible latency spikes. This PR implements a SLO Lease Rebalancer that permits soft, capacity-aware handoffs: regions can donate or acquire SLO leases over a bounded window, with attenuated traffic shifts, circuit-aware backoff, and an emergency reclaim path for correctness. Design highlights: 1) Lease model: each region holds leases for tenant partitions with a lease_window_ms TTL and an associated capacity_score updated from per-route throughput and node health. 2) Rebalancer algorithm: periodic scoring pass computes donors and receivers and proposes chunked lease transfers sized by capacity_delta and handoff_threshold_pct. Transfers are staged over windows with exponential backoff on transient failures. 3) Soft resume: receivers apply an attenuated activation that gradually increases weight (0 -> target) so downstream caches and KV warmup reduce cold-start SLO violations. 4) Circuit interplay: when a receiving region has active circuits tripped for a tenant, the transfer is paused and marked for retry; donors maintain temporary sticky leases until a safe handoff can complete. 5) Observability: new lease_migration_success/failure, lease_transfer_duration_ms, and region_capacity_score metrics plus handoff traces. 6) Safety: emergency_force_reclaim shortcut (operator-triggered) for edge cases and a conservatively defaulted handoff_threshold_pct=0.25 to avoid aggressive churn. Changes made: - runtime/lease_manager.go: core rebalancer, scoring, transfer orchestration, retry/backoff. - runtime/lease_manager_test.go: unit tests covering scoring, chunking, backoff semantics. - routing/handshake.go: handshake extension for staged weight updates and compatibility checks. - observability/metrics/lease_metrics.prom: metric definitions and dashboard hints. - docs/operational/lease-rebalancer.md: runbook, default knobs, and troubleshooting. - deploy/k8s/upgrade-hooks.yaml: prestop hook to drain leases on node removal. - cli/ctl-handoff.sh: convenience operator script to trigger handoffs or force-reclaim. - ops/runbooks/slo-hand-offs.md: incident runbook additions. - examples/handshake-sim.json: simulation scenarios used in testing. Testing and validation: comprehensive unit coverage added; integration test in perf-canary simulated a cross-region outage and validated a staged handoff with 0.12% SLO breach delta (within target). Chaos testing included region-level partitioning and node terminations; rebalancer paused transfers and resumed once capacity stabilized. Performance: small CPU overhead (~3% p99 increase during active rebalances) observed in canary, within SLA. Rollout plan: canary at 5% traffic in us-west-2 for 2h, monitor lease_migration_success, slo_violation_rate, region_capacity_score and downstream error/latency. If stable, ramp to 25% for 4h then global. Auto rollback on >0.5% sustained increase in SLO breaches for 15m or >2s median token latency regression. Backwards compatibility: no changes to public APIs; all behavior behind runtime feature-flag runtime.slo_lease_rebalancer.enabled=false by default for safe staged rollout. Operator knobs: lease_window_ms (default 900000), handoff_threshold_pct (default 0.25), max_chunk_size (default 100 partitions), emergency_force_reclaim (manual). Migration and upgrade notes: ensure dedicated nodes have upgrade-hooks applied to allow graceful lease drain; upgrade order should follow cross-region canary then control plane. Known limitations and mitigations: in extreme multi-region partition churn the rebalancer defers transfers to avoid oscillation; we log deferred_transfer_* metrics to aid future tuning. Documentation added and internal runbooks updated. Checklist: [x] Implementation and tests, [x] Integration/perf canary, [x] Observability and runbooks, [x] Operator scripts, [x] Reviewed and approved. This description consolidates rationale, design, testing, and rollout guidance for operators and reviewers.
Introduce SLO Lease Rebalancer: enables controlled handoff of SLO responsibility between regions with time-boxed soft resume and capacity-aware lease migration. Config knobs: lease_window_ms, handoff_threshold_pct, emergency_force_reclaim. No user-facing API changes.
Ethan Patel: Can you explain how this avoids oscillation when two regions try to rebalance simultaneously? Reply: The scoring pass is leader-elected per-tenant-partition and uses monotonic timestamps plus a proposed-token based compare to avoid split decisions; we also add a jittered backoff on retries.
Riley Gonzales: Request: add metric for deferred_transfer_count and a debug flag to force single-step transfers. Reply: Added deferred_transfer_count and ctl-handoff now supports --force-single-step for operator testing.
Samira Noor: Question about SLA impact on hot path: why not warm cache before weight increase? Reply: soft resume increments weight in 10% steps with 30s spacing by default; this was tuned in canary to balance warmup vs failover speed.
Ethan Patel: Approve after addressing lint and adding runbook section on emergency_force_reclaim. Reply: Lint fixed and runbook extended.
Riley Gonzales: Approved on green CI.
Unit tests exercise scoring and backoff; integration tests simulate cross-region outage; perf-canary measured p50/p95/p99 token latency and CPU; chaos engineering (region partition) validated pause/resume semantics. Synthetic traffic sim harness included in examples/handshake-sim.json.
Canary 5% traffic in us-west-2 for 2 hours, monitor lease_migration_success and slo_violation_rate; if stable ramp to 25% for 4 hours then global. Auto rollback on >0.5% sustained SLO breach increase for 15m.
Feature-flag flip to disable runtime.slo_lease_rebalancer.enabled=false instantly disables rebalancer; operator script ctl-handoff.sh --reclaim can force donor sticky leases back. In case of systemic regressions, revert the commit on main and trigger emergency reclaim per runbook.
payload.title: SLO Lease Rebalancer for Soft Regional Handoffs

payload.body:
Context: Our KV cache has increasing fragmentation and frequent small spill writes under mixed workloads (short chat traces + occasional long contexts). Motivation: reduce tail latency and spill I/O amplification by keeping hot keys co-located in contiguous page 'silos' and by making the evictor prefer locality-preserving demotions. This PR implements a page siloing allocator, a locality-preserving eviction policy, and a spill attenuation controller that defers and coalesces spill writes when under transient pressure. Changes are gated behind a runtime flag (kv.page_siloing_enabled) and incremental by default. Design summary: 1) Page siloing allocator groups allocations into silos by tenant and affinity score computed from recent access fingerprinting. Silos aim to keep related KV entries on contiguous page ranges to reduce fragmentation and sequentialize spill write patterns. 2) Locality-preserving evictor selects victims not only by recency/heat but also by silo contiguity score so evictions prefer reclaiming whole subranges that yield contiguous free segments. This substantially reduces micro-fragmentation. 3) Spill attenuation controller monitors spill sink bandwidth and in-flight spill latency; when spikes occur it switches from immediate per-page spill to deferred coalesced-write mode (batching multiple evicted pages into a single larger write, limited by a configurable max_coalesce_bytes). 4) Integration with scheduler: the evictor now exposes a hint to the continuous-batching scheduler so that inflight generation batches avoid pinning tokens to pages that are being reclaimed, reducing KV lookup latency spikes during concurrent eviction. 5) Telemetry and evaluation: new metrics (kv.silo_fill_ratio, kv.eviction_contiguity, kv.spill_coalesce_ratio) and an end-to-end perf test harness that simulates mixed short+long context traffic. Implementation notes: - New package/runtime files: kv/silo_allocator.{cc,hh}, kv/evictor_locality.cc, kv/spill_attenuator.cc, scheduler/evictor_hints.go - Conservative default config: silo max size = 8MB, coalesce window = 50ms, max_coalesce_bytes = 2MB - Backwards compatible: no public API changes, feature off by default. Migration path: customers can enable per-tenant via console or feature flags; rollout plan includes dark launches and Canary pool in Dedicated. Test plan: unit tests for silo placement, fuzz tests for contiguity heuristics, integration perf job in perf-canary (redwood/perf-canary) comparing tail latency and WAN spill traffic. CI: initial CI run failed on an intermittent scheduler race in continuous batching; fixed by adding a small handshake between evictor and scheduler (evictor_hints now uses a version token to ensure stale hints are ignored). Outcomes: synthetic perf runs show 18-28% reduction in spill IOPS for mixed workloads and 6-12% tail latency improvement (95th/99th) in our canary environment. Risk/Tradeoffs: - Coalescing spikes into larger writes increases latency of reclaim path under sustained pressure; attenuation controller uses conservative defaults to avoid unbounded backlog. - Siloing increases internal fragmentation risk for extremely small tenant workloads; mitigated by letting small tenants share silos until threshold. Related: follows patterns from ENG-2143 and borrows parts of earlier spill-backpressure work (SUP-4021).
Introduces page siloing and a locality-preserving evictor to reduce fragmentation and spill I/O; adds adaptive spill attenuation knobs and telemetry; no API changes.

Priya Natarajan: Silo metadata is ~128 bytes per active silo; silos are sized to amortize metadata. Hot path uses a lock-free fastpath (see silo_allocator.h comment) and falling back to a per-thread slab under contention.

Owen Park: CI reported a flake in continuous-batcher when evictor hints were delayed. Did you add ordering guarantees?

Motivation: We have three divergent retry/reauth implementations across TypeScript, Python and Go that produce subtle UX differences (backoff defaults, token refresh hooks, streaming reconnect semantics). This PR introduces a compact, language-agnostic connector interface and lightweight compatibility shims so each SDK can adopt the same surface with minimal breaking changes. The goal is to: 1) reduce maintenance cost by consolidating core retry logic, 2) improve streaming reconnect ergonomics (resume/cursor semantics), and 3) make cross-SDK behavior predictable for users migrating between languages.

Summary of changes (single-pass string): Added a compact connector spec and reference implementation in internal sdks/connector; plumbed connector adapters for TypeScript (sdks/typescript/src/retry/compactConnector.ts), Python (sdks/python/redwood/retry/connector.py) and Go (sdks/go/retry/connector.go). Introduced compatibility shims so older init patterns continue to work (examples and changelogs updated). Normalized backoff defaults to exponential with jitter and capped max_delay=60s. Streaming: added a small resume token handshake and a typed cursor wrapper in each SDK so streamed generators/iterables expose consistent .resume() semantics. CI/workflow: expanded sdk-matrix to run cross-lang streaming integration tests and bumped matrix to include go1.21, node20, python3.12.

Migration notes: Existing code using previous retry factories will continue to work via shims but will log a deprecation warning for one release cycle. To opt in to the new connector explicitly: pass { connector: compactConnector() } (TS/Go/Python examples in docs). If you rely on custom token rotation hooks, the connector supports a single async refreshToken() callback; adapters translate older refresh hooks automatically.

Testing: Added unit tests for new connector in each SDK, integration tests for streaming resume across language pairings, and CI job that runs a three-way compatibility matrix (TS <-> Python <-> Go) for the most common streaming handshake scenarios. Local perf: compact connector reduced median token generation CPU time by ~7% in our micro-benchmarks (see bench notes).

Rollback: Reverting the feature branch restores previous behavior because shims were applied; however a revert should be coordinated with SDK consumers if they already adopted the named connector import.

Related: ENG-2041 (cross-sdk retry consolidation), ENG-2090 (streaming ergonomics).
Riley Chen (review): We should make the backoff window configurable per-instance; hardcoding a cap can bite us for low-latency use-cases.
Asha Kapoor (author): Agreed; added optional maxDelay param and default to 60s. Documented in migration notes.
Matt Bell (review): TypeScript examples rely on older .stream() iterator shape; ensure adapter preserves .resume() and iterator close behavior.
Asha Kapoor (author): Adapter wraps legacy iterator and exposes .resume() delegation. Added integration tests that verify both shapes.
Sonia Patel (review): CI failure on first run showed flakiness in Go streaming test (race on token cache). Can you add a lightweight mutex around cache access?
Asha Kapoor (author): Added sync.Mutex to connector.go token cache, re-ran CI — passed on subsequent run.

Motivation: SDKs historically contained duplicated retry/backoff and stream ergonomics code that diverged subtly between Python/TypeScript/Go. That made cross-SDK behavior inconsistent (different default jitter, different max_retry windows) and increased maintenance burden. This PR extracts a transport-agnostic RetryProfile and introduces a tiny, consistent set of lightweight stream helpers for each SDK so app code can be ported with fewer surface changes.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduce a core RetryProfile concept and backoff parameter mapping used by all SDKs (max_attempts, initial_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms, jitter_mode, hedged_retries).
- Replace ad-hoc retry logic in each SDK with small adapters that map RetryProfile -> transport specific retry strategies.
- Add ergonomic streaming helpers: Python async generator wrapper (stream.iter_lines_safe), TS async iterable shim (stream.consumeSafe), Go StreamHandle interface + convenience ReadPump.
- Add cross-SDK unit/compat tests that assert parity on default retry timeline for common scenarios (auth 401 then refresh, transient 429, slow downstream).
- Documentation: migration guide and explicit examples for moving from the legacy per-SDK backoff flags to the unified RetryProfile.
- Version bumps: python sdk -> 0.12.0, typescript sdk -> 1.27.0, go sdk -> 1.8.0.

Why transport-agnostic RetryProfile: Teams run heterogeneous stacks (frontend TS, backend Python, microservice in Go). Previously, moving a workload between services required tuning three different knobs. The RetryProfile is a single well-documented primitive that can be serialized as JSON, stored in config, and applied consistently across languages.

Migration notes:
- If you set per-SDK backoff env flags (RETRY_INITIAL_MS, RETRY_MAX_MS, RETRY_ATTEMPTS), they will continue to be read but are deprecated — migrate to a RetryProfile config shipped to your service.
- Streaming helper names changed: start_stream -> open_stream is preserved at the transport level but helper names for safe iteration are new (see examples in docs/sdk/migration/retry-profile.md).

Scope and risk: The change is primarily additive (new adapters + helpers) but rewires retry decision points in each SDK. We validated with end-to-end test harness and Canary run against staging traffic for 48h.

Release notes (summary): Unify retry/backoff semantics across SDKs, add safe streaming helpers, improve cross-language portability, bump SDK versions.
Ethan Kim: Please add a short benchmark showing latency/regression of the new adapter vs old logic for a 1-5 token fast-path. The overhead must be negligible.
Sofia Martinez: Added microbenchmarks under redwood-sdk-python/tests/bench_retry_adapter.py and included results in the PR description. Overhead <1.2% for our sample workload.
Priya Rao: In TS helper, can we expose an optional onBackpressure callback so clients can surface metrics?
Sofia Martinez: Added optional callback parameter (onBackpressure) with test; wired it to the consumeSafe shim as a noop by default.
Luca Bianchi: Go adapter looks good. One nit: prefer context-aware Close for StreamHandle to make cancellation explicit.
Sofia Martinez: Updated interface to CloseWithContext(ctx) and kept Close() for compatibility. Added deprecation comment for Close().
Add unified RetryProfile across SDKs; introduce safe streaming helpers (iter_lines_safe / consumeSafe / StreamHandle ReadPump); bump SDK versions: python 0.12.0, typescript 1.27.0, go 1.8.0; migration guide added.

Summary: Adds a non-destructive backward-compatibility layer that maps legacy v1 'tool envelopes' and mixed-mode streaming events into the current structured tool-calling shape. This is a runtime-level, opt-out behavior controlled by a lightweight request header (X-RW-Compat: legacy=1) and a server-side fallback profile. Motivation: We continue to see client integrations that emit the older tool/function envelope format and interleave streaming 'event' fragments that do not align with the v2 structured tool-call and streaming framing. These cause either broken tool invocation or stream mangling for customers who cannot upgrade immediately. This PR provides a safety net so clients can continue to operate while we deprecate v1 on a scheduled timeline.

What this change does (single-line sections concatenated into this description): - Adds a LegacyEnvelopeMapper in the API gateway that coalesces fragmented streaming events into a canonical tool-call request object when the compat header is present. - Introduces X-RW-Compat header handling and a short-lived server-side flag for rollout (defaults disabled). - Adds unit and integration tests that simulate partial streaming frames, nested tool payloads, and mixed text-with-tool streams. - Exposes a per-tenant opt-in via Console feature flag and adds telemetry to track how often mappings are used and whether coercion dropped any fields. - Adds a best-effort deterministic fallback for ambiguous payloads: the mapper will prefer tool metadata in this order: explicit tool_name > envelope.tool > legacy_inferred_name.

Implementation notes and constraints: - The fallback is intentionally conservative: fields are not removed; ambiguous sub-fields are placed under a legacy_metadata map on the coerced payload so v2 handlers can log and surface them without losing data. - Mapper runs early in the request handling pipeline to preserve KV cache keys and batching behavior. - This PR does not change the public schema contract unless the compat header is supplied.

Tests and CI: - Commits include a new suite that replays recorded incident streams (replay fixtures) where older clients sent 3-part event envelopes; these fixtures were captured from a postmortem trace and scrubbed. - CI matrix covers gateway unit tests, end-to-end gateway->runtime smoke, and SDK regression checks. - Initial CI run failed on a flaky streaming test; flake fixed with a deterministic buffering tweak.

Commits (high-level): - feat(gateway): add legacy envelope mapper and header parsing - test(gateway): add replay fixtures and streaming integration tests - feat(console): tenant opt-in flag and telemetry hooks - fix(tests): deterministic buffer improvement to stabilize CI - docs: add compatibility guide and scheduled deprecation note

Files changed (high level): - gateway/compat/LegacyEnvelopeMapper.go (core mapping logic and heuristics) - gateway/handlers/stream_decoder.go (stream coalescing, small buffering change) - runtime/handler/tool_invoker.go (adds legacy_metadata passthrough) - console/flags/compat_flags.go (tenant opt-in surface) - telemetry/mappers/compat_telemetry.go (usage counters and histograms) - test/fixtures/legacy_stream_replays/ (three JSONL fixtures) - docs/compatibility/legacy-to-structured.md (how to opt in/opt out and examples)

Review conversation highlights (excerpted and paraphrased into a single string): - Oliver Park: "Nice conservative approach. Question: what happens to token-level billing attribution when we coalesce fragments?" Author reply: "We preserve token counts and annotate the coerced payload; billing code reads token totals from the annotated envelope unchanged." - Sana Iqbal: "Ensure mapper is O(1) memory for tiny fragments; we don't want it to buffer entire large streams." Author reply: "Mapper bounds to max 8KB aggregation window, then emits partial-coercion with legacy_metadata and a telemetry counter for truncated envelopes." - Diego Morales requested an additional integration test for tool-call failure paths; author added it in second commit. CI status and reruns: - First pipeline: failed (1 flaky streaming test) - Second pipeline: pass after deterministic buffer fix - All required checks (unit, integration, lint, go vet) passed before merge

Release notes / migration guidance (user-facing blurb): "Introduced a temporary compatibility mode for legacy tool envelopes. Customers still on older SDKs may opt into X-RW-Compat: legacy=1 to keep behavior stable during migration. This is planned for deprecation; watch Console announcements for timelines." Rollout and telemetry plan: - Feature flag gated per-tenant; rollout started on beta tenants 2025-02-18. - Telemetry collects mapping.count, mapping.truncated_count, mapping.ambiguous_count; SRE will monitor for error increase and latencies. - Plan to enable campus-wide read-only audit logs for 30 days before turning on auto-coercion by default.

Related work and follow-ups: - Follow-up task ENG-3381: adapt SDKs to emit the new structured tool payloads (Python and TS patches). - Deprecation RFC will be published and linked in Console and docs; schedule will be at least 90 days after default-on. Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2025-02-20 after approvals from Oliver Park and Sana Iqbal. No breaking changes introduced.
Temporary compat header X-RW-Compat: legacy=1 enables soft-mapping of legacy tool envelopes and fragmented streaming events into current structured tool-call requests. Opt-in via Console flag; telemetry added. Planned deprecation with 90+ day notice.

Summary: Introduces the 'Cohort Traceback Fanout Conductor' (CTFC), a rollout controller that prioritizes session-coherent cohorts for canary/A-B promotions, supports interruptible rollbacks mid-fanout, and exposes an explainable rollback oracle that surfaces the minimal contributing signals when a promote fails.

Motivation: Recent incidents showed large blast radii when promotions ignored session affinity and when rollbacks were binary and opaque. CTFC reduces user-visible regressions by ensuring fans are constrained to cohort boundaries, enabling on-the-fly interruption, and providing triageable telemetry to SREs and PMs.

Changes:
- New controller binary: controllers/ctfc with core reconcile loop, progress checkpointing, and interrupt logic.
- Exhaustive telemetry: telemetry/ctfc_metrics.go + new events for "fanout_step", "rollback_interrupt", and "counterfactual_smoke".
- Explainable rollback oracle: a modular evaluator that runs a compact counterfactual smoke replay on recent samples and returns ranked signal contributions.
- Safety budget integration: honor existing rollout budget tokens and expose a credit refund when early-interrupts avoid downstream degradation.
- Dry-run mode: a CLI flag and API path that runs validation without committing traffic.
- Tests: e2e smoke harness that replays recorded traffic and unit tests for oracle scorer.

Review thread (abridged):

- Omar Ruiz: "Telemetry looks good; can you emit an event for 'fanout_resume' as well? It's helpful when resuming after interruption."

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the public API additive and optional; default rollout controllers remain unchanged unless organizations opt into CTFC via rollout policy. The explainable oracle is designed for triage not for automated overrides; the team can later expose a trust score if product requires it. Related: Linear ENG-4821, SUP-3101 (customer-reported session-affinity regression), design notes at /design/ctfc.md
Add a Cohort Traceback Fanout Conductor that enables session-coherent A/B promotions, interruptible rollbacks, and a lightweight explainable rollback oracle. Includes new telemetry hooks and a dry-run smoke-replay mode for pre-promote validation.

Motivation: transient daypart and seasonal patterns were generating noisy token-cost alerts and paging on short-lived shifts. This PR implements a lightweight 'Temporal Tilt Detector' that combines a daypart-aware baseline (hour-of-day/week-of-day bucketing), an EWMA trend baseline, and a seasonal-trend decomposition stage to produce a bounded tilt_score per route/tenant. The tilt_score is emitted as a low-cardinality metric and as a span tag to enable correlated traces for root-cause. Changes include: (1) new telemetry exporter fields (tilt_score, daypart, rolling_baseline) and bounded aggregation keys; (2) trace enrichment for tilt tagging; (3) a Grafana dashboard "Daypart Tilt & Cost Smoothing" with panels for tilt, smoothed token-cost, raw vs baseline, per-tenant drift heatmap and suggested mitigation actions; (4) updated alert rules that use dampening (15m suppression window for small tilts) and hysteresis to avoid flapping; (5) incident-bot integration to defer low-severity pages automatically when tilt is transient and non-regressive; (6) unit + integration tests and a micro-benchmark to validate detector latency on median payloads. Design notes: to control cardinality we bucket daypart into 6 coarse zones and restrict tilt emission to aggregation keys {route, model_family, tenant_tier} by default with an opt-in fine-grained label. We include a sampling guard for high-cardinality tenants and aggregate sketches for rollups. See docs link: RFC https://linear.app/redwood/ENG-1987 for algorithm rationale. Checklist: [x] implement detector algorithm prototype; [x] exporter + trace tag; [x] Grafana dashboard; [x] alert rule changes; [x] tests and bench; [x] docs and quickstart example.
Ethan Liu: Overall great direction. Concern: tilt_score might create high-cardinality if we emit with fine-grained labels. Can we ensure default emission is aggregated?
Priya Natarajan: Alert dampening makes sense. Please add a runbook stanza that lists manual override steps and how to revert the suppression window quickly in case of regression.
Liam O'Connor: Performance: detector runs in the ingest hot path. Bench shows 1.6ms median, but I'm seeing P95 at 12ms in initial runs. Need to validate under burst (10k rps).
SRE Team (comment): Prometheus scrape and storage impact needs estimates. Provide expected cardinality delta and retention guidance.
Maya Patel: Addressed cardinality by defaulting daypart -> 6 coarse bins and emitting tilt only for aggregation keys {route, model_family, tenant_tier}. Added opt-in label 'tilt_detail=true' for customers who want per-call tilt. Sampling guard added for >1k unique tenants per minute.
Maya Patel: Added runbook section in docs with explicit steps to toggle alert dampening and suggested rollback play. Saved a sample Linear task for runbook follow-ups ENG-1999.
Maya Patel: Investigated perf: optimized hot-path by moving seasonal smoothing to async micro-batch when latency budget tight. Re-ran bench: median 0.9ms, P95 3.8ms under 10k rps synthetic load (see bench_results.md).
Maya Patel: Included a small cardinality impact table and retention recommendations in the RFC. Prometheus storage impact estimated <3% for default config; opt-in detailed mode increases cardinality and should be monitored.
Add Temporal Tilt Detector: emits tilt_score and daypart labels for coarse drift detection; new Grafana dashboard 'Daypart Tilt & Cost Smoothing'; updated tilt_deviation alert with dampening and incident-bot defer integration. Default config is low-cardinality and non-breaking.

Motivation: many customers hit higher-than-expected unit costs because sensible batching, cache, and quantization defaults are either too aggressive for small tail workloads or too conservative for high-throughput tenants. This PR introduces a compact defaults matrix generator plus a fallback planner that simplifies autopilot behavior for Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments and gives ops explicit, auditable rules for graceful degradation. Key changes: 1) defaults matrix builder that consumes workload sketches (p95 latency, seq length distribution, qps buckets) and emits a small set of presets (batch_size, prefill_budget, kv_cache_ttl, quant_profile) tuned by cost-latency tradeoffs; 2) fallback planner that maps SLOs and capacity tiers to ordered fallback strategies (scale, model-variant, quant-fallback, regional-failover) and exposes a deterministic evaluation function for rollouts; 3) telemetry and unit-econ calibration hooks (metrics + synthetic-sample harness) so we can measure expected unit cost delta before enabling a profile; 4) CLI and Console surface to preview and apply suggested defaults; 5) docs and canary rollout plan. Checklist: implements unit tests and integration smoke tests; adds example workload sketches; includes rollout playbook and rollback steps; updates docs. Rollout plan: staged canary on 10% of new Hosted signups -> 25% -> 100% across regions with observability gating on unit_econ_regression and latency_violation alerts. Related work: ENG-4321 (cost defaults), ENG-4390 (fallback routing policies), SUP-1209 (customer support case patterns). Notable limitations: profiler relies on representative replay traces; aggressive quant profiles are gated by quality regression monitors. Requested reviewers: runtime and SRE for safety; CLI/docs for UX. Links: Linear ENG-4321 (internal), Support ticket SUP-1209 (internal).
Evan Summers (2025-11-07): Can you add an explicit safety budget for prefill that caps memory usage per-GPU? Otherwise high prefill on bursty tenants may OOM. Response: added prefill_budget cap and unit test in commit 7.
Priya Nandakumar (2025-11-09): The planner looks good but we need an opt-out for Dedicated customers with strict isolation. Response: added a policy flag and Console toggle; documented in docs file.
Jorge Alvarez (2025-11-11): CI flaked on the telemetry integration — looks like a timing dependency. Response: added retry/backoff in test harness and moved to deterministic mock clock.

Context: As the repo has grown, presubmit hooks have accumulated ad-hoc ordering and duplicated setup costs across multiple language runners. This caused noisy flakiness in CI, slow feedback for small changes, and sprawl in scripts maintained across teams. Motivation: unify presubmit sequencing, surface CI-level telemetry (duration, cache hit/miss, matrix cardinality), and provide early guidance for dependency hygiene so engineers remove unnecessary devDependencies during PRs. Summary of changes: 1) Add a small Go-based presubmit-orchestrator (ci/orchestrator/) that defines ordered hook groups (setup, lint, unit, integration-smoke). It exposes a declarative manifest (ci/presubmit.yaml) that can be updated per-repo or per-path glob. 2) Introduce ci/telemetry-exporter: a lightweight helper that emits metrics (presubmit.duration_ms, cache.hit, test.flaky_count) to our internal telemetry endpoint and as a debug artifact in artifacts/ci-telemetry.json. 3) Dependency-hint linter (tools/dep-hint) that statically analyzes package manifests (package.json, go.mod, pyproject.toml) and heuristically flags devdeps that are not referenced by tooling paths in the patch. 4) Split lint runners into language-aware shards (ts-lint, go-lint, py-lint) and wire adaptive caching so only affected shards run by default. 5) Add a staged release hook that enforces a lightweight smoke test (release/smoke.sh) before promoting artifacts to the release pipeline. Migration steps: - No required action for developers. The orchestrator autodetects existing hook files and migrates them into the new manifest where safe; teams will get a migration PR in their subpackages if the heuristics are uncertain. - To opt out of telemetry, set ci/telemetry.yaml.disable: true in repo root. - Dep-hint linter can be disabled per-path with .dep-hint-ignore. Testing & validation: - Local unit tests for orchestrator and dep-hint included (ci/test/orchestrator_test.go, tools/dep-hint/tests/). - Ran presubmit smoke across core packages (redwood/, redwood-sdk-python/, redwood-helm-charts/) with representative patches. - Nightly run enabled for 48 hours in the feature branch to capture telemetry before merge. Rollout & safety: - Feature gated under repo-level flag ci.presubmit.orchestrator.enabled; turned on for main by this PR after a 7-day telemetry observation window. - Fallback: if orchestrator fails, the old scripts are executed (compat shim at ci/compat/). - Performance: median presubmit wall time reduced ~18% in observed workloads; cold-cache improvements from targeted shard execution reduced setup time by ~25%. CI details & history: - Initial run (workflow: presubmit/main) failed due to a flaky test in integrations/smoke (flake count: 1). Reproduced locally, added a small timeout backstop and retriggered. - Second run succeeded; telemetry exporter produced artifacts/ci-telemetry.json with aggregated bucketed latencies. - Lint stage produced actionable hints for ~27 open PRs across org (most common: unused jest-devtools and stale ts-node entries in package.json). Security considerations: - Telemetry exporter only sends aggregated numeric metrics and anonymized job tags; no source code or secrets. It is behind an allowlist and uses existing CI tokens with restricted scope. - Dep-hint linter is read-only and runs in CI; it does not modify manifests automatically. Implementation notes: - The orchestrator is intentionally small (~900LOC Go) to keep startup deterministic. It uses a manifest-driven model to allow future per-team tweaks without code changes. - Adaptive shard selection uses path globs and a cached mapping at .ci/cache/shard-map.json which is updated by a periodic job. - Added documentation in docs/dev/ci-presubmit.md and a migration guide docs/dev/dep-hint.md. Related: ENG-4287 (presubmit orchestration), ENG-4290 (ci telemetry), SUP-214 incident notes on flaky presubmits.
Introduces a presubmit orchestrator to centralize hook sequencing, adds a lightweight ci-telemetry exporter for pipeline metrics, and a dependency-hint linter that surfaces unnecessary devdeps. Improves presubmit latency and reduces noise in lint/test pipelines. No runtime API changes.
Liam O'Connor: Nice consolidation. Can we make the telemetry exporter opt-in at org-level? I don't want teams sending extra metrics by default.
Priya Nair: Agree. Added an explicit disable flag and documented the opt-out in docs/dev/ci-presubmit.md.
Maya Singh: dep-hint produced a bunch of false positives for packages that are only referenced by script paths. Can we refine heuristics?
Priya Nair: Refined heuristics to look for common script paths and added a per-path ignore file (.dep-hint-ignore); added tests to cover the cases you saw.
Ethan Park: The presubmit manifest looks good; please ensure the fallback path is resilient in case of panics.
Priya Nair: Orchestrator now runs hooks under a supervisor that falls back to ci/compat when a panic occurs; added integration test to validate.

Motivation: Large fleets see varying request shapes; a single batching policy + flat quant profile leaves money on the table. This PR introduces 'SlateLine' batch lanes and a hierarchical quant allocator that together provide per-tenant/per-workload batch shaping and a priority-ranked quant fallback tree to reduce unit cost while respecting SLOs. Design summary: SlateLine divides the serving runtime batcher into lightweight lanes (fast-latency lane, balanced lane, throughput lane) with a tiny per-lane selector that uses recent shape histograms and token budget hints to pick the lane for each request. The hierarchical quant allocator maps model variants into a tree of quantization profiles: top nodes are high-fidelity (FP16/quant8-mixed) and leaves are aggressive int4/int2 variants. At runtime the allocator prefers higher-fidelity nodes but can step down along the tree when budget or capacity policies trigger. Key behaviors implemented: 1) lane selector service integrated into serving runtime (stable, lock-free sampling path), 2) lane-specific batching windows and kv-cache sharing limits, 3) quant allocator with soft budget quotas and graceful degradation path, 4) telemetry hooks for unit-econ attribution (tokens, lane, quant-level), 5) rollout flags and tenant override controls. Migration and safety: rollout gated by feature flag "slateline_enabled" per-cluster; default off. A conservative rollout profile named "slateline-conservative" is included which only enables lanes and allocator simulation (no quant fallbacks) to collect metrics for 24-72h. A second progressive profile enables live allocator step-downs with strict latency SLO enforcement and automatic revert if error or p95 latency regressions exceed thresholds. Testing: unit tests for allocator tree traversal, integration tests that run synthetic workloads exercising the three lanes, e2e perf test harness added to perf-canary to simulate tenant traffic and assert p50/p95 tail behavior and cost delta. CI: flaky integration test fixed by a deterministic seeding of the request sampler. Observability: new metrics: redwood.slateline.lane_chosen, redwood.slateline.quant_level, redwood.slateline.alloc_decisions, and taggable labels for unit_econ (tenant_id, route). Documentation: console docs and API playground snippets added under redwood-docs to explain flags and tenant override API. Live fallback thresholds are configurable via the console and via the cluster config file under runtime/batcher/slateline.yaml. Rollout plan: 1) enable simulation in canary region for 48h, 2) conservative flag in 2 small tenants for 72h, 3) progressive enable on low-risk tenants for 1 week, 4) full enable with automatic revert. Impact: internal perf-canary runs show roughly 7-12% token-cost reduction on mixed workloads with <2% p95 latency delta using conservative policies; aggressive policy hits 18-25% savings at cost of slightly higher p50/95 in synthetic throughput bursts. Related work: complements recent tenant-prefill and quant-profile recommendations; differs by pushing decision logic into the runtime and providing lane-aware batching rather than global batch windows. Motivation: Our presubmit lanes have accumulated long-running lint shards and a growing transitive dependency surface that slows feedback and increases CI cost. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) a lightweight Go-based dependency pruner (dep-pruner) run as a pre-merge check that detects and optionally removes unused devdeps/transitive entries from package manifests and (2) a stage-aware lint orchestrator action that re-groups lint shards into fast/medium/slow lanes with an adaptive fastpath for small PRs. Goals: reduce presubmit latency, shrink devdep churn, and provide a safe rollout path for lint reshuffling.
Summary of changes: - tooling: add tools/dep-pruner (Go) with CLI and a minimal heuristics engine (import scan + package-lock cross-check) and CI adapter to auto-suggest PR comments with diffs - actions: add .github/actions/lint-orchestrator (TypeScript) that inspects changed files and classifies lint shards; it can short-circuit slow shards for touch-limited changes - workflows: update .github/workflows/presubmit.yaml to add a new presubmit job "dep-pruner-check" and to wire the lint orchestrator into the lint matrix - docs: docs/contrib/ci-practices.md with developer guidance and rollback steps - helper: scripts/ci/prune-report.sh to surface pruning impact in CI artifacts
Checklist: - [x] dep-pruner CLI implemented with unit tests - [x] lint-orchestrator action implemented and unit-tested - [x] integration tests in CI to validate action gating - [x] rollout plan defined and smoke-tested in canary repos - [x] docs and troubleshooting added
How dep-pruner works (high level): - static import scan across changed packages + cross-validate against package-lock/npm-shrinkwrap - heuristics to avoid pruning packages that appear only in native build steps or dynamic requires - output: a suggested patch (npm ci edit/patch) and a compact report with removed/transitive candidates
Safety and rollout: - initial run mode is detection-only (false-positive rate < 2% in our samples) - auto-fix mode gated behind a Linear approval and only enabled for canary orgs - lint orchestrator respects explicit overrides via .ci/lint-config.yaml - we add a short cooldown (48h) window before auto-fix is allowed to merge
Metrics & results from canary run: - median presubmit time (fast-path) reduced from 4m20s to 2m55s (~32% improvement) - overall presubmit compute (GH runner minutes) down ~18% across canary repos - dep-pruner flagged ~412 devdeps as safe-to-prune across 6 repos (manual triage reduced to 28 auto-fix patches)
Testing: - unit tests cover parsing heuristics and false-positive detection - e2e runs on canary repos with diffed files to ensure lint shards are routed correctly - CI smoke: presubmit.yaml now includes a temporary job to run the pruner in simulation mode on all incoming PRs for 72 hours before enabling baseline gating
Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main in detection-only mode 2) Enable lint orchestrator fastpath for org:canary after 48h 3) Run dep-pruner auto-fix on canary during low-traffic window and ensure rollbacks are available 4) Gradual expansion to 25% of repos, then 100% Related: ENG-2314 (ci presubmit speedups), ENG-2350 (dep hygiene initiative). Notes: this PR touches CI logic and developer workflows; please read docs/contrib/ci-practices.md before approving. If you see a false-positive pruning suggestion, comment with the package path and tag @infra-team.
Jonah Reed: Nice work — can we add a fast-fallback to revert an auto-applied prune if downstream integration fails?
Maya Patel: Jonah — yes, added a revert hook in scripts/ci/prune-report.sh and documented rollback steps.
Aisha Nguyen: The orchestrator is promising; please ensure license scanning still runs in slow lane.
Maya Patel: Aisha — license-scan preserved; added explicit step in presubmit.yaml so it always runs for changed packages.
Introduce detection-first dependency pruner and a stage-aware lint orchestrator to speed up presubmit feedback loops and reduce dev dependency churn. Disabled auto-fix by default; enable via Linear approvals.
Focus review on pruning heuristics in tools/dep-pruner/pruner_test.go and the lint classification thresholds in .github/actions/lint-orchestrator/src/index.ts. Pay particular attention to false-positive avoidance and license-scan preservation.
