Motivation: token-level and per-invocation metrics currently provide high-cardinality point traces that make it hard to understand session-level latency behavior (bursty tails, intra-session skew) without expensive trace rehydration. This PR adds compact, session-windowed latency sketches and a small invocation replaybench to synthesize representative token sequences for validation and alert tuning.

Goal: give SREs and platform engineers a low-cost, queryable summary of per-session latency distributions and a reproducible synthetic generator to exercise hot paths for alert calibration and dashboarding. This supports automated alert dampening and more robust long-tail detection without blowing up storage or cardinality.

What's included (summary):
- New runtime sketch collector: compact reservoir-backed, time-windowed latency sketches keyed by (tenant, route, session_id window). Sketches are optimized for low-allocation hot paths and expose percentiles + tail-mass estimates.
- Replaybench CLI + Python harness: generates synthetic invocations (token timing, token sizes, kv-cache states) from historical traces or randomized shingled bootstraps to validate SLOs and CI jobs.
- Minor server-side ingestion path: lightweight proto for session-sketch telemetry and conversion to rollups stored in the metrics pipeline.
- Grafana dashboard and alert rule examples: session-latency-overview dashboard with cohorting controls and a new alert template that uses session sketch tails for alerting instead of raw p95/p99 spikes.
- Tests: unit tests for sketch ingestion + deterministic replaybench integration tests.
- Docs: observability guide for using sketches + replaybench and recommended alert thresholds.

Checklist:
- [x] API for runtime to emit sketches with minimal allocations
- [x] Backfill connector: best-effort adapter to convert 24h of sampled traces into sketches (used for initial seeding)
- [x] Replaybench integration in CI (sanity only)
- [x] Dashboards + alert rule RFC example
- [x] Performance microbench: <5% added p50 CPU on the metrics emitter in high-throughput path

Implementation notes:
- The sketch uses a bounded reservoir with exponential decay for recency weighting and a separate compact q-digest to summarize tail mass. This lets us cheaply answer p50/p90/p95/p99 and estimate the % of tokens above a configurable latency bucket.
- Session windows are configurable: default 60s tumbling windows, configurable per-route. We attach a small 16-byte session window ID hash to metrics to keep cardinality modest.
- The replaybench emits sequences with token inter-arrival times and token lengths; the harness can replay against both the runtime (via a local loopback) and the sampling ingest path to validate histogram/sketch consistency.

Commits (high level):
- feat(telemetry): add session_sketch runtime collector and proto definitions
- feat(replaybench): initial replaybench CLI + python harness
- perf(telemetry): optimize sketch allocation hot path, add pooling and pre-sized buckets
- infra(metrics): add conversion adapter for historical trace -> sketch backfill tool
- docs(observability): session-latency guide + dashboard JSON
- test: deterministic replaybench integration test + unit tests for q-digest impl

Files changed (high level):
- src/telemetry/sketches/session_sketch.go
- proto/telemetry/session_sketch.proto
- tools/replaybench/README.md
- tools/replaybench/harness.py
- dashboards/session_latency_replay.json
- metrics/backfill/trace_to_sketch.go
- tests/telemetry/test_session_sketch.go
- tests/replaybench/test_replaybench.py
- docs/observability/session-latency.md

Review conversation (abridged):
- Ava Patel: "Nice direction — can we bound worst-case cardinality? The 16-byte hash is fine but let's add explicit eviction policies per-tenant."
  - Priya: "Added eviction policy (LRU with max windows per tenant) and a config knob; updated docs with knobs and recommended limits."
- Diego Morales: "Sketch design looks good; can we get an integration microbenchmark against high-throughput emitter?"
  - Priya: "Included microbench results under perf/benchmarks/session_sketch.md and reduced allocations by pooling; added automated perf run to CI (sanity only)."
- Sofia Chen: "Alerting change is significant; ops will need guidance on threshold calibration to avoid alert storms."
  - Priya: "Included replaybench presets that map historical cohort percentiles to suggested thresholds and a small RFC section in docs."

CI and checks:
- unit tests: pass
- integration (sanity): pass (deterministic replay run against snapshot)
- staticcheck/lint: pass after fixups
- perf microbench: pass (regression <5% CPU p50 on emitter)

Release notes:
- Introduced session-windowed latency sketches and a replaybench for synthesizing invocations. Adds a new dashboard and recommended alert rule templates. This feature is opt-in via telemetry.config.session_sketch.enabled. Backfill adapter provided for one-time seeding of historical traces.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- Sketch emission is opt-in; existing raw token traces remain unaffected. Backfill converter can be used to populate sketches for historical windows if customers choose to enable.

Security considerations:
- Session ID is hashed with a tenant-specific salt before being emitted to avoid raw identifier leakage. Salt management is documented and uses existing key rotation practices.

Merge details:
- merge_method: squash
- merged_at: "2026-02-25"

Ava Patel: Can we bound worst-case cardinality? Added LRU eviction and config knobs.
Diego Morales: Please add perf microbench. Added under perf/benchmarks and CI sanity check.
Sofia Chen: Ops will need guidance on thresholds. Added replaybench presets and RFC in docs.
Session-windowed latency sketches (opt-in) and replaybench for synthetic invocation testing. Includes dashboard and alert templates. Backfill adapter provided for historical seeding.

Motivation: Recent production incidents and an increase in OpenAI-compat traffic exposed two recurring problems: 1) inconsistent chunk/fragment semantics between proxies caused fncall handshakes to drop or duplicate events under backpressure, and 2) route-level capacity spikes allowed oversized payloads to consume downstream buffer budgets and cause transient OOMs on proxy workers. This PR standardizes an explicit stream-fragment protocol header, tightens routing precedence for capacity-limited routes, and adds soft/hard payload guards per route. Summary of changes: standardized X-Redwood-Stream-Proto header to declare chunking mode and fragment sequence markers; streaming proxy now manages an explicit buffer manager with adjustable window_ms and per-connection fragment budget; routing rules updated so capacity-guarded routes (annotated in config) are routed to isolated worker pools to prevent headroom contention; payload validation early-rejects requests above route soft limit and returns structured JSON error with OpenAI-compat error fields when appropriate; fncall/toolcall handshake now tolerates reordered fragments by buffering until end-sequence marker or per-fragment timeout; compatibility mode for the OpenAI adapter preserves prior behavior when header is absent but emits a deprecation warning header to clients; default config changes: route_payload_soft_limit_bytes=256000, route_payload_hard_limit_bytes=1048576, stream_window_ms=60. Impact and rollout plan: default rollout is canary to 5% of traffic for 48 hours with metrics on proxy buffer utilization, stream-reassembly latency, fncall error rate, and route rejection rate; a follow-up will expose these controls in the Console. Backwards-compat notes: we maintain backward behavior if X-Redwood-Stream-Proto is not present; however the hard-limit enforcement is applied regardless to protect workers. See linked Linear items for QA and rollout tasks.
Luca: Can you share numbers for buffer memory savings and reassembly latency? Also request automated test coverage for reordered fragments.
Priya: Added microbenchmarks in CI and a unit test suite for reordered fragments; buffer pressure dropped ~38% in our synthetic replay and median reassembly latency is 12ms (was 23ms). Tests are in ci/tests/stream_reassembly_test.go (included).
Marta: We should be careful about silent rejections in the OpenAI adapter; prefer an explicit structured error indicating route quota vs global limit. Requested change to include error type 'route_capacity' in response body.
Priya: Updated error mapping to include 'route_capacity' and added a small e2e test asserting the OpenAI-compat error shape. Also added Console-facing telemetry tags for rejection_reason=route_capacity.
Ethan: LGTM modulo one nit on logging verbosity from BufferManager at DEBUG only. Please reduce info logs and keep metrics.
Priya: Reduced log level for routine fragment bookkeeping to DEBUG and left warnings for window exhaustion. Pushed change.
Luca: Approved after numbers and tests; Marta approved after error mapping; Ethan approved on logging change.
Rollout: Canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 96 hours with monitoring checks
Follow-ups: Console controls for per-route stream_window_ms and soft/hard limits (ENG-5654)
Safety: hard-limit enforced immediately in canary to prevent worker OOMs; ops runbook updated
Introduce stream-fragment protocol header (X-Redwood-Stream-Proto), per-route payload soft/hard limits, and an isolated capacity-guarding routing path to prevent proxy buffer contention. Backwards compatible if header is absent; hard limits protect proxy workers.

Adds per-tenant privacy profiles (opt-in), KMS wrap helper for deterministic pseudonymization, a dry-run RBACv1->v2 shim, operator docs, and tests. Backwards compatible; feature gated behind `privacy_profiles` flag.
Summary: Add a tenant-level 'privacy profile' feature that lets customers opt tenants into a constrained audit footprint. This PR implements: 1) a small, opt-in transport shim that applies deterministic pseudonymization to configured audit fields before logs leave the control plane, using envelope KMS wrapping for provenance; 2) a KMS wrap helper to derive per-tenant wrapping keys (no new persistent keys — uses existing CMKs with derived encryption context); 3) an RBAC migration shim that allows operators to run RBACv1->v2 evaluation in dry-run mode and produce a compatibility report; and 4) operator docs, e2e tests, and CI checks.
Motivation: customers in regulated industries requested a way to limit personally identifiable fields in audit streams while preserving provable integrity and KMS-backed provenance for forensics. Previous approaches either stripped too much context (lossy redaction) or required full service-side key management. This approach balances audit usefulness and privacy by pseudonymizing identifiable fields deterministically and signing the wrapped envelope with existing CMKs so auditors can prove authenticity without revealing raw values.
Compatibility and safety: feature is opt-in per tenant via tenant config; no default behavior change. The RBAC migration shim runs in passive mode unless explicitly enabled and emits decision diffs only to the operator audit bucket.
Checklist:
- [x] Design doc: ENG-4211 (linked)
- [x] KMS wrap helper implementation
- [x] Audit pseudonymizer middleware
- [x] RBACv2 compatibility shim + reporter
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] End-to-end test against redwood-private-installer local cluster
- [x] Operator docs and runbook
- [x] Feature flag gating
Implementation notes:
- Added audit/pseudonymizer middleware which takes a tenant privacy profile (list of paths to pseudonymize) and replaces values with HMAC-based pseudonyms. The HMAC key is derived via KMS GenerateDataKey with a tenant-specific encryption context; the raw HMAC key is never persisted.
- Implemented kms/wrap helper that performs a single AES-GCM envelope wrap where the wrapping key material is derived from an AWS/Cloud KMS CMK and the tenant id+profile tag as the encryption context. The resulting envelope contains a provenance header with CMK ARN and encryption context fingerprint.
- RBAC shim: new rbac/migration/dryrun service that, given a tenant and a set of requests, evaluates against RBACv1 and RBACv2 paths and emits a compact diff. Reports are JSON-lines stored to the operator-only S3 bucket by default.
- Telemetry: added metric privacy.profile.applied{tenant} and privacy.profile.pseudonymize_latency_seconds.
- Security: HMAC derivation uses KDF with KMS-provided key material and HKDF-SHA256, nonce per pseudonymization call, and the pseudonym is base64url of first 16 bytes; raw values removed from the emitted audit line.
- Rollout plan: feature flag privacy_profiles toggles middleware; start with canary tenants, roll to 10% via console, then full rollout.
- Mitigations: we keep a reversible provenance envelope (wrapped key + CMK reference) for forensic reconstruction in emergencies but require an elevated operator workflow with approvals and audit gating (SUP-3248).
Commits:
- 1f4c2b3 Add tenant privacy profile schema and config plumbing
- 8b9d0a2 Implement audit/pseudonymizer middleware and unit tests
- c3a7f02 Add kms/wrap helper + envelope provenance headers
- bc4e91d Add rbac migration dry-run service and reporter
- 2d0a11e End-to-end test harness and local cluster job
- a8c7b59 Add operator docs and runbook for privacy profiles
- fa9013b Fix: ensure pseudonymization is idempotent across restarts (store salt derivation metadata in envelope)
- e2b4d66 CI: add integration job and flake handling on test harness
High level files changed (representative):
- api/tenants/privacy_profiles.go
- services/audit/pseudonymizer/middleware.go
- services/kms/wrap_helper.go
- services/rbac/migration/dryrun.go
- tools/e2e-tests/privacy-profile-e2e.yaml
- docs/ops/privacy-profiles.md
- docs/ops/privacy-playbook.md
- scripts/ci/integration-privacy-profile.sh
- tests/unit/pseudonymizer_test.go
- tests/integration/privacy_profile_flow_test.go
- tools/e2e-tests/privacy-profile-e2e.yaml
Testing notes:
- Initial CI run hit a flake in the e2e harness (timeout waiting for local cluster), test fixed in fa9013b with retry/backoff logic.
- Added an integration matrix covering AWS and GCP KMS providers in CI to validate encryption-context usage.
- Manual runs against a demo tenant confirmed pseudonymization is deterministic and provable using the envelope provenance.
Review conversation (selected):
- Marcus Holt (reviewer): "This is an important feature for compliance customers. Two concerns: 1) risk of exposing KMS ARNs in audit output; 2) potential performance impact on high-throughput tenants. Can we avoid leaking full ARNs and measure latency?"
- Asha (author): "We include a CMK fingerprint (sha256 truncated) rather than full ARN by default. I added metric privacy.profile.pseudonymize_latency_seconds and a note in the runbook about TTFB. Also added an optional config to redact CMK identifiers in operator-view reports."
- Tessa Nguyen (reviewer): "Please ensure the migration shim cannot be toggled by tenant-level admins; only operator roles should run it."
- Asha: "Agree — restricted via operator-only RBAC role; enforced in rbac/migration service and tested in unit tests."
- Ravi Kapoor (reviewer): "The reversible envelope for emergency reconstruction is sensitive — require two-operator approval and time-limited access."
- Asha: "Added a runbook section requiring two operator approvals and a signed ticket (SUP-3248). Envelope unwrapping writes to an operator-only audit channel and is logged with the approval reference."
Follow-ups and fixes:
- fa9013b: add retry/backoff to e2e harness (addressed flake).
- e2b4d66: tighten logging to avoid recording raw fields on errors (security review request).
CI and checks summary:
- unit tests: pass
- integration (local): pass after rerun
- lint: pass
- static-analysis (gosec/dep): pass with a single LOW finding (documented)
- e2e-privacy-profile job: pass on second run
Merge: squashed and merged via "Squash and merge" on 2026-03-06.
Post-merge tasks:
- [x] Publish operator docs to internal KB
- [x] Add privacy_profiles flag to console feature flags list
- [x] Schedule canary rollout for 2026-03-10
- [x] Add follow-up ticket to re-evaluate CMK fingerprinting strategy (ENG-4280)
Known limitations and notes:
- Pseudonymization reduces but does not guarantee irreversibility if attacker gains CMK access; rely on CMK protections and operator approval gating.
- Migration shim focuses on decision parity; complex policy constructs may need manual review.
- Performance overhead: measured median pseudonymize latency 4.8ms on a canary tenant; batching will be considered in a follow-up if customers require sub-ms SLOs.
Contributing docs and operator runbook included in docs/ops. If there's concern about the provable envelope, please reach out to the security group (SEC-88) for threat modeling.

Marcus Holt: Please add e2e coverage for GCP KMS as well as AWS.

Motivation: our presubmit and lint/test pipelines have accrued a lot of language-specific runners and duplicated setup steps. This PR extracts a small, language-agnostic CI adapter layer (Go) and a lightweight dependency-visibility gateway that centralizes dev-dependency detection, stale-lock telemetry, and a permissive gate for fastpath merges. Goals: reduce presubmit startup time, provide clearer visibility for dep churn, and make staged release hooks less noisy.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds cmd/ci-adapter: a compact Go binary that normalizes workspace bootstrap across languages, caches toolchain leases, and exposes a small HTTP health/sanity endpoint used by GitHub Actions.
- Introduces tooling/dep-visibility: a minimal service (local-only in CI) that computes a dependency surface summary, flags transitive devdeps, and emits a compact dependency fingerprint to a cache key used by staged CI lanes.
- Replaces language-specific presubmit shell fragments in the main workflows with calls to the ci-adapter; reduces duplicated logic in .github/workflows/presubmit-*.yml.
- Adds a presubmit-fastpath label and automation rule: small changes (docs/infra) can skip heavy integration shards when dep-visibility and unit/linters pass.
- Cleans up legacy Makefile targets used only by CI and moves canonical behavior into the adapter.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation of ci-adapter and dep-visibility modules
- [x] Replace presubmit workflow fragments and update action inputs
- [x] Add telemetry counters (dep-change-rate, presubmit-latency) to internal CI metrics bridge
- [x] Add docs/ci/README.md describing the adapter and fastpath rules
- [x] Add migration note in docs and small rollout plan

Why this is safe: the adapter is opt-in behind workflow updates; the presubmit workflows are staged behind a rollout flag for the first week. Dep-visibility only influences fastpath gating and does not block default presubmit lanes. Release automation is unchanged in this PR (no artifact signing changes).

Rollout plan: merge to main -> opt-in on small team repos -> enable for core services after 1 week of telemetry. We will monitor presubmit-latency and false skips; rollback by re-enabling legacy fragments if needed.

Related: Linear ENG-4821 (presubmit feedback), ENG-4956 (dep surface telemetry).
Aaron Kim: Suggest keeping a short compatibility shim for repos that still invoke make ci locally. Maya: added Makefile targets that forward to the adapter and included migration note.
Lucia Gomez: Can dep-visibility run in parallel with unit tests to avoid adding latency? Maya: yes — the adapter kicks off dep-visibility asynchronously and only waits for its fingerprint when evaluating fastpath rules.
Ravi Shah: Add a feature-flag env var to gate the fastpath behavior during rollout. Maya: added CI_FASTPATH_ENABLED and defaulted to false in workflows; documented rollout steps.
Addressed reviewer feedback: compatibility shim, async dep-visibility, rollout flag added; all reviewers approved
Ran presubmit simulations locally and on ephemeral runners. Observed median presubmit bootstrap time drop from ~14s to ~7s for node/python shards. Telemetry hooks exercised in staging for 48h before merge.

Motivation: We continue to see noisy circuit flips in islanded regions during transient backend blips which cause rapid reopen/close churn and SLO spikes for tail latency. This churn also propagates to downstream routing decisions and makes capacity autoscalers overreact. This PR introduces an ephemeral health gate that groups circuits into lightweight cohorts and applies a short consensus quiet-window before allowing reopen transitions. The feature is guarded behind a runtime flag (default: off) and is intended for staged rollouts to Dedicated/Private deployments.

What this changes: 1) cohort builder: lightweight hashing that groups circuits by region+model+capacity-class so that short-lived flaps are evaluated at cohort level instead of per-circuit. 2) consensus quiet-window: when a circuit transitions to open, reopening requires a quorum of cohort members to report healthy for a configurable quiet_window_ms to avoid single-node noisy reopen. 3) soft-lease on circuits: reopened circuits obtain a soft-lease which decays if the cohort health remains marginal — this prevents immediate re-eviction storm. 4) autosolve flow: a periodic reconciler reevaluates cohort health and will progressively restore circuits in small batches if conditions are met. 5) metrics + debugging: new metrics (cohort_health_score, cohort_quiet_window_hits, cohort_reopen_batches) and a console dashboard JSON to visualize cohort state and recent quiet-window events. 6) hotfix: fixes a race in circuit snapshot restore where metrics timestamps could be nil causing occasional panics during node restart.

Rollout plan: gated behind feature flag redwood.experimental.ephemeral_health_gate; staged canary in eu-west-1 on Dedicated for 48h, promote to remaining Dedicated clusters if cohort_health_score stays > 0.95 and no SLO regressions observed. If increased reopen churn is detected, the reconciler supports auto-rollback.

Compatibility and config: default behavior does not alter existing circuit semantics unless the flag is enabled. Config knobs added to runtime/config: cohort_size_hint, quiet_window_ms, reopen_quorum_pct, soft_lease_ms, and batch_restore_size.

Testing: added unit tests for consensus math and cohort builder, integration test simulating transient flaps and verifying cohort-level damping, and a canary script used during manual rollout.

Related: addresses recurring incidents documented in SUP-321 and complements ENG-1543 (staged fallback orchestrator).
Anjali Kapoor requested changes: please add detailed unit tests for quorum edge-cases and document behavior when cohort size is 1 (we should fall back to legacy semantics).

Motivation: CI costs and queue times have grown with the test matrix and the monorepo size. This PR introduces three coordinated changes to reduce CI runtime and cache pressure: (1) test-slicing: split integration/unit suites into deterministic shards by changed modules, (2) sparse-checkout in CI runners to limit workspace files downloaded for each job, and (3) dep-minimizer: a lightweight analysis tool that prunes unrelated dependency versions from the effective dependency set used for install caches.

Summary of changes: Added a test-slicing executor (tools/test-slicer) with heuristics for affected-package detection and deterministic shard assignment. Updated .github/workflows/ci.yml to run lightweight changed-file detection as a short-circuit step and only spin up full runners when needed. Integrated sparse-checkout logic into the checkout step to reduce workspace size for long tests. Added infra/dep-minimizer which analyzes lockfiles and module imports to produce a reduced lock overlay used only for CI, keeping production lockfiles untouched.

Why this is safe: All changes are opt-in and guarded by repository config flags (ci.test_slicing.enabled, ci.sparse_checkout.enabled, ci.dep_minimizer.enabled). The dep-minimizer outputs a diagnostics report and cannot be enabled unless a repo admin flips the flag. Test-slicing preserves global test order determinism by seeding shard assignment with repository-wide salt and PR number.

Testing and CI: Local unit tests for the test-slicer and dep-minimizer are included. The workflow contains a smoke job that runs a full-suite against a preserved baseline when the config is changed. In this PR the smoke job was run twice against main and head to validate parity. CI run summary appears in checks_summary.

Compatibility notes: No library API changes. Developers will notice faster pre-merge feedback and smaller checkout times in CI. Teams that rely on full workspace integration tests should opt into slicing gradually; docs/ci/onboarding.md includes migration steps and troubleshooting.

Checklist: - [x] Adds test-slicing implementation and unit tests - [x] Adds dep-minimizer implementation and unit tests - [x] Adds sparse-checkout integration into CI - [x] Feature flags and safe defaults - [x] Migration docs and rollout plan in docs/ci/onboarding.md

Rollout plan: 1) Merge opt-in feature flags and tools; 2) Enable per-team via repo config for low-risk services; 3) Monitor per-route latency and CI cache hit-rate for 2 weeks; 4) Gradually enable wider.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on correctness of affected-file detection and shard determinism (see tools/test-slicer/README.md). dep-minimizer intentionally avoids rewriting production lockfiles; verify the overlay generation and diagnostics in infra/dep-minimizer/README.md.
Evan Park (2026-02-13): Left a few nit comments on documentation and a question about shard seeding collision with external merges — can we base the salt on repo UUID instead of human-readable name?
Maya Thompson (2026-02-13): Reply: switched to repo UUID-based salt in next commit (8a1f3d2), added a short note in README explaining determinism guarantees.
Rita Alvarez (2026-02-15): Concern: dep-minimizer might miss dynamically imported modules in backend services. Suggest running fallback full-install when dynamic imports are detected.
Maya Thompson (2026-02-15): Reply: added heuristics to detect common dynamic import patterns and a conservative fallback that forces full install for affected packages (d4b7c9a).
Samir Patel (2026-02-16): Approved after verifying unit tests and running the smoke job locally. Left a comment to monitor cache hit-rate dashboards after rollout.

Context: Prefill-decode handoff continues to be a major driver of tail latency for long-context workloads. We observed oscillating KV cache prefetch patterns and redundant prefill work across microbatches which inflate kernel contention and increase cost. This change introduces an "epochal prefill consolidator" that groups closely-timed prefill work into short-lived epochs and a complementary "entropy-aware decode scheduler" that biases decode kernel placement to minimize KV cache thrashing.

Motivation: Existing speculative prefill flows operate per-request or per-microbatch and can cause duplicate KV priming when many requests share prefixes or similar attention windows. By introducing epoch-level aggregation we reduce duplicate kernel work, enable per-epoch KV prewarming (single warmup per working set), and give the scheduler better signals to reduce cross-epoch eviction.

Design summary: 1) Epochal prefill consolidator: a lightweight coordinator that opens a short time window (configurable, default 6ms) and merges prefill intents into a single consolidated prefill op when affinities (model version, seq length, prefix hash) match. Consolidator emits a single prefill token map and an epoch id that callers use to associate decode requests. 2) Entropy-aware decode scheduler: a scoring function that uses per-epoch entropy (diversity of prefix hashes, KV hit-rate estimate, and kernel queue depth) to bias decode kernels to nodes with warmer KV caches and lower eviction risk. 3) Per-epoch KV prewarming: when consolidation produces a prefill, a single accelerated KV warm path is invoked that registers the epoch id to the KV cache to prevent soft-evictions for the epoch lifetime. 4) Backwards-compatibility: all new components are opt-in behind runtime flags and fall back to existing per-microbatch prefill if disabled.

What changed (high level): - New epochal consolidator module and API surface (src/runtime/prefill/epochal_consolidator.*) - Entropy-based scheduler hooks and scoring (src/runtime/scheduler/entropy_scheduler.*) - Per-epoch KV prewarmer with lifecycle management (src/runtime/kv/kv_prewarmer.*) - Metrics and tracing additions for epoch boundaries and consolidation rate (docs/observability/prefill-metrics.md; src/runtime/README-prefill.md) - Integration tests and microbench harness (tests/integration/prefill_epochal_test.py; examples/perf/epochal-bench.yaml)

Checklist: - [x] Consolidator implementation - [x] Scheduler integration - [x] KV prewarming lifecycle - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Observability (histograms for epoch size, consolidation ratio, epoch lifetime) - [x] Canary rollout plan documented

Testing: Unit tests for consolidator logic and scheduler scoring added. Integration test simulates 1000 concurrent short-prefill requests with synthetic prefix collisions. Benchmarks run on perf lab GPUs show consistent p99 tail reduction and cost-per-token improvements.

Rollout: Feature flag off by default. Gradual canary (1%, 10%, 50%, 100%) across hosting and dedicated clusters with extra tracing enabled during canary. If KV eviction warning rate rises by >5% during canary, auto-rollback is triggered.
Rafiq: Nice approach — consolidating prefill windows should cut duplicated kernel work. Two asks: add guardrails for memory blowups when an epoch accumulates too many intents, and ensure the prewarm pin uses soft pins so the cache can still evict under pressure.
Maya: Added epoch size cap (configurable, default 128 intents) and changed prewarm to soft-pin semantics. Also added metrics to track soft-pin evictions.
Ellen: Scheduler scoring looks good but the entropy formula needs calibration. Can we add an experiment flag to toggle entropyWeight and collect per-epoch hit/miss stats?
Maya: Added runtime flag --prefill-entropy-weight and instrumented per-epoch hit/miss counters. Updated tests to validate scoring range.
Diego: Integration test failure on initial run — saw intermittent flakiness in perf harness. Root cause: race in epoch close path.
Maya: Fixed by making epoch close atomic and added a small jitter to close window to avoid thundering herd. Re-ran and green.
Introduce epochal prefill consolidation and entropy-aware decode scheduling. Opt-in feature (runtime flag). Expected improvements: fewer duplicate prefill kernels, reduced KV thrashing, improved tail latency and lower cost per token. Rollout gated and observable.
Feature flag default off. Canary to 1% of traffic for 24h with elevated tracing -> 10% for 48h -> 50% for 72h -> 100%. Metric gates: p99 tail, KV eviction rate, consolidation ratio. Automatic rollback if KV eviction rate increases >5% or p99 regresses >10%.
This PR focuses on runtime-level consolidation and scheduler hints; it does not change model kernels themselves. Follow-ups planned: GPU-side kernel hinting for better co-location and adding per-epoch persisted statistics for long-running Dedicated clusters.
payload.title: epochal-prefill-consolidator-and-entropy-aware-decode-scheduler

payload.body:
Context and motivation: onboarding and fast feedback for local CI iterations has regressed as our CI matrix grew. This PR introduces a lightweight local dev runner (tools/fastdev) and a minimal toolchain stub (dev/Toolchain.toml) plus a small workflow that developers can run locally or in ephemeral self-hosted runners to get the same sanity checks as CI without the full matrix. This is an opt-in developer convenience feature that reduces time-to-first-green and iteration time on lint/test changes. Summary of changes: - add tools/fastdev/runner.go: small Go binary that runs a subset of checks in-process with conservative timeouts and filesystem caching - add tools/fastdev/README.md: usage, examples, and how to wire into VS Code tasks - add dev/Toolchain.toml: lightweight list of pinned tool versions for local dev (go, node, python, prettier, husky minimal config) - add .github/workflows/dev-local.yaml: workflow targeted at self-hosted/dev-runner label and usable as reference for local runs - add .pre-commit-config.yaml entries and Makefile target fastdev - add scripts/ci/sanity-check.sh to share common checks between CI and fastdev Why not full devcontainer? Full devcontainers are heavier and we want a quick path for contributors who already have the environment. The Toolchain.toml is intentionally minimal and human-editable; it is not authoritative for production. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-4172) [x] unit tests for runner logic [x] small e2e smoke used locally by author [x] docs and README for opt-in usage Implementation notes: the runner currently shells out to the language toolchain where appropriate but uses a caching layer (tools/fastdev/.cache) to avoid repeated installs during rapid iterations. It ships a dry-run mode and a --ci-compat flag which performs the same commands as the CI sanity lane (lint, go vet, pytest -k sanity). Small illustrative snippet of the workflow (from .github/workflows/dev-local.yaml):
name: Dev local referenced
on: [workflow_dispatch]
jobs:
  fastdev:
    runs-on: self-hosted
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: ./tools/fastdev/runner --ci-compat

Changes are conservative: no production CI lane behaviors removed; existing CI still the source of truth. Rollout plan: merge to main and advertise opt-in in the contributor guide; monitor adoption and iterate. Performance expectations: local fastdev runs should be ~30-60s for small changes on modern dev machines, substantially faster than full CI matrix. Risks and mitigations: - risk: divergence between fastdev and CI -> mitigation: include --ci-compat mode that runs identical commands, and we add a CI check that runs the fastdev dry-run in a nightly job to detect drift. - risk: contributors rely on the stub as authoritative -> mitigation: call out in README that Toolchain.toml is a local convenience. Related PRs & notes: this PR intentionally avoids changing release automation and focuses on developer feedback loops; follow-ups will propose integrating a thin prebuild cache and a remote runner for fast-path checks.
Marco Ruiz (2026-02-16): Nice small surface area. Please add an explicit smoke e2e test that exercises --ci-compat mode against a small repo subset so we can run it in nightly drift detection.
Lina Chen (2026-02-16): Added a minimal smoke script and referenced it in the README. It runs pytest -k sanity and go vet in a tiny project fixture. See commit c4f2e11.
Priya Nair (2026-02-17): Can we ensure the tool doesn't hide flaky tests? Suggest adding a --no-cache flag to force fresh installs and a clear message when cache is used.
Lina Chen (2026-02-17): Added --no-cache and improved log lines when cache hits/misses occur in commit b5f6a2e.
Ethan Park (2026-02-18): Suggested pinning the go version in Toolchain.toml to avoid surprising local failures; also asked to avoid modifying production CI in this PR.
Lina Chen (2026-02-18): Pinned go and node entries in Toolchain.toml and verified that CI remains unchanged. Responded that release automation changes will be a separate follow-up.
Marco Ruiz (2026-02-19): Approving after small nits addressed. Marked approval in github UI.
Priya Nair (2026-02-19): Approved. Left a note to follow up on telemetry for opt-in usage.

Motivation: Production workloads exhibit mixed sequence length distributions and intermittent sparsity from rotary/rope quantization artifacts. Existing Flash-style kernels are high-throughput for dense attention but underutilize opportunities where token locality and structured sparsity exist. This PR introduces 'signal-attn', a hybrid kernel that combines a fast-path Flash-like matmul for dense regions and a lightweight sparse-merge engine for rotary-sparsity lanes. The kernel integrates with the serving runtime scheduler using a signal-driven prefetch heuristic for the KV cache and a continuous-batching hint that reduces tail latency without sacrificing throughput.

Summary: Implement a new attention kernel and scheduler hooks that: 1) Detect per-batch rotary-sparsity patterns (simple entropy+mask heuristics) and route attention work to either dense or hybrid execution path. 2) Fuse rotary/rope application into the QKV projection pipeline to avoid an extra transpose+allocate in the hot path. 3) Add KV prefetch scheduler hints that prioritize hot shards and stagger prefetch to avoid PCIe contention under bursty arrival patterns. 4) Expose a runtime config flag to tune the hybrid threshold and continuous-batcher latency budget.

Benchmarks: Microbenchmarks run on p4d-like instance (A100 style) with representative models: - 7B dense: 15% throughput increase, 12% median latency reduction, 9% p99 reduction. - 13B mixed-length: 22% throughput increase, 17% median latency reduction, 18% p99 reduction. - 70B semi-sparse eval (synth rope sparsity): 25% throughput uplift on best-effort routing, 23% p99 reduction after warm-up. End-to-end synthetic RLHF workload saw a 14% token-cost reduction due to fewer recomputations and better batching. Full benchmark logs attached in artifacts.

Commits: single continuous-string summary of commits in this PR: "commit 1: core: add signal-attn kernel and hybrid exec path; commit 2: runtime: KV prefetch scheduler hints, continuous-batcher integration; commit 3: bindings: python and ts exposed config, tests and docs; commit 4: perf: microbench harness and regression tests; commit 5: fix: lint and CI fixes after review"

Changed files (high-level): "src/serve/attn/signal_attn_kernel.cpp", "include/serve/attn/signal_attn.h", "src/serve/attn/rotary_fuse.cpp", "src/serve/kernel_router.cpp", "src/serve/kv/prefetch_scheduler.cpp", "python/redwood/serve/attn.py", "ts/sdk/attnConfig.ts", "benchmarks/perf/signal_attn_harness.py", "tests/attn/test_signal_routing.cc", "docs/operational/attn_hybrid.md". Small API additions: config flag --attn.hybrid_threshold, --attn.kv_prefetch_window_ms.

Compatibility and safety: The hybrid path is opt-in by default and gated behind runtime config and per-model capability checks. Numeric stability tests (fp16/fp32) were added; all existing attention unit tests remain unchanged and pass. The kernel falls back to the dense Flash-compatible path if the mask/entropy heuristic is inconclusive or if quantized kernels are required.

Review notes: This PR intentionally keeps the rotor/rope fusion local to the attention hot path to avoid changing serialized model weights or checkpoints; only runtime transient transforms are applied. The rotary fuse uses aliasing-friendly in-place transforms to minimize extra allocations. The KV prefetcher introduces conservative heuristics first, with a progressive rollout via the continuous-batcher budget parameter to reduce the risk of PCIe saturation.

Operational impact: Rolling this out on Dedicated pools is recommended behind a canary policy (5% traffic) due to the scheduler prefetch behavior. Observability: added counters and histograms: attn.signal_route_{dense,hybrid}, attn.kv_prefetch_{issued,skipped}, attn.hybrid_fallback_reasons. These are surfaced in the console dashboards and can be used to tune hybrid_threshold and prefetch window.

Notes on tests: Added unit tests for routing heuristics and rotary fusion correctness, integration tests for continuous batching semantics, and perf harness scripts used for the measurements above.
Introduce a hybrid attention kernel (signal-attn) that fuses rotary sparsity paths and improves KV prefetch heuristics; ~12-18% end-to-end p99 latency reduction and 15-25% throughput uplift on common LLMs when using continuous batching.
Add signal-attn hybrid kernel; integrate with runtime router and KV prefetch scheduler; expose config flags and sdk bindings; add perf harness and tests; follow-up lint fixes.
Sofia: 'Please add more deterministic benchmarks and include cold-start numbers; also confirm behavior with multi-GPU KV sharding.' Author reply: 'Added cold-start traces to artifacts and a multi-GPU section in perf logs; router preserves shard affinity so prefetch is local-first.' Evan: 'Can we keep rotary fuse as a separate compile unit to ease bisects?' Author: 'Kept API boundary clear and added a BUILD flag so it can be toggled during bisect runs.' Maya: 'Lint/formatting failed on first CI run; please rebase and run codegen.' Author: 'Fixed formatting and regenerated codegen in second commit.' Approvals: approved by Sofia and Evan after fixes, Maya gave thumbs-up on tests.
CI run history: initial CI (linux-clang, lint) failed on formatting -> fixed. Second CI run passed unit tests and integration tests. Performance job (nightly) flagged a 2% regression on one microbenchmark that was traced to a suboptimal store ordering; patch applied and nightlies green. Final CI: all checks passed.
Merged via squash-merge into main on 2026-03-05. Merge commit includes summarized perf notes and rollout instructions. Canary rollout policy documented in docs/operational/attn_hybrid.md.
Detailed benchmark artifacts attached: artifacts/signal_attn/bench-20260301.tar.gz. Representative results: 7B dense (throughput +15%), 13B mixed (+22%), 70B semi-sparse (+25%). See bench harness for test harness parameters.
Canary 5% on Dedicated pools for 48 hours, monitor attn.signal_route_hybrid, attn.kv_prefetch_issued, and GPU PCIe stall metrics. If attn.hybrid_fallback_reasons > 5% revert hybrid_threshold down or disable feature flag.
This PR aims to be conservative and opt-in; follow-up work will add adaptive hybrid_threshold tuning and more aggressive prefetch heuristics for enterprise customers.
See description list; key modifications are in src/serve/attn/*, src/serve/kv/prefetch_scheduler.cpp, and bench/tests/docs additions.
CI artifacts: ci.redwood.io/79801/artifacts; bench artifacts: artifacts/signal_attn/bench-20260301.tar.gz

Title: econ-sandbox: introduce autotune sandbox CLI for batch/cache/quant defaults.
Summary: Adds a developer-facing CLI and small platform hooks to run a fast, local 'econ sandbox' that simulates tenant request shapes against candidate batching, cache warmup, and quantization profiles and outputs recommended defaults and unit-econ estimates.
Motivation: Teams repeatedly run ad-hoc scripts to tune batching, cache prefill, and quantization for new tenants. This PR formalizes a lightweight sandbox that codifies the heuristics we use in production autotuners so engineers can iterate faster and generate reproducible suggestions tailored to tenant traffic patterns. The tool is intended to accelerate onboarding of Dedicated/Private customers and reduce manual tuning work that currently costs engineering time and leads to suboptimal unit economics.
What this changes: 1) New CLI command: redwood econ sandbox run --profile=<yaml> --dry-run|--apply which loads a small YAML workload signature and candidate profile list, runs a fast probabilistic simulation and returns ranked recommendations with estimated token-cost and p95 latency impact. 2) New config schema: /configs/econ/sandbox-profiles/*.yaml (three sample profiles added: conservative, balanced, aggressive). 3) Telemetry additions: econ.sandbox.recommendation_score, econ.sandbox.simulated_p50_ms, econ.sandbox.simulated_p95_ms, econ.sandbox.estimated_cost_tokens. 4) Safety gate: recommendations flagged with a latency-risk tag if simulated p95 exceeds the target SLO; these recommendations are excluded from --apply unless --force is passed. 5) Small API surface: a sandbox runner library under pkg/econ/sandbox that can be reused by the existing autotuner and by integration tests. 6) E2E smoke test and a new unit-econ regression test in ci/econ that validates scoring stability over a canonical trace.
Implementation notes: The simulator is intentionally approximate: it uses an event-driven, light-weight replay that models batching dynamics, KV-cache hit rates (with configurable prefix skew), and quantization model latency profiles (sampled from per-device latency histograms). It supports 'dry-run' mode that emits a JSON recommendation bundle and a human-readable summary. The CLI also supports --compare <baseline-id> to diff the proposed defaults against an existing tenant profile.
Commits (summary): initial scaffold and CLI wiring; sandbox runner core simulation and workload YAML parser; three sample profiles and docs; telemetry probes and metric docs; e2e smoke test and CI job; address review fixes and test flakiness; polish and squash for merge.
Files touched (high-level): pkg/econ/sandbox/{runner.go,simulator.go,profile.go} (new); cmd/redwood/econ_sandbox.go (new CLI wiring); configs/econ/sandbox-profiles/{conservative.yaml,balanced.yaml,aggressive.yaml} (new sample profiles); internal/telemetry/metrics.go (added metrics and docs string constants); ci/econ/smoke_test.sh (new); docs/ops/econ-sandbox.md (new). Diffs are intentionally focused on orchestration/config and the sandbox library; no runtime kernel changes included.
Testing and CI: Added a small e2e smoke test that runs the CLI in dry-run against a canned trace; unit tests for scoring and p95 estimation; CI job added to the econ test matrix with a 10m timeout. The CI run for this PR initially failed due to a flaky telemetry mock; a follow-up commit stabilizes the mock and CI greened. The final CI status is pass across linux/amd64 unit and e2e matrices.
Review thread (high level): - Liam Chen (reviewer): "Nice. Please add more explicit p95 budget examples and make it obvious when a recommendation trades cost for latency." Author reply: "Added latency-risk tagging and explicit example in the docs; updated CLI help to show cost/latency tradeoff table." - Diego Rivera: "Can the sampler handle multi-tenant bursty shapes? Also please ensure telemetry cardinality is bounded." Author reply: "Sampler supports configurable burst distributions; limited metric labels to profile_id and tenant_class to avoid cardinality explosion. Added note in metrics docs." - Marta Gomez: "Unit tests look good but one e2e flaked on GH runner - saw occasional timeouts" Author reply: "Added retry and smaller trace for CI e2e; left the larger trace for local runs only." - Security (inline): "Tool runs only on authorized operator CLI; ensure apply path requires RBAC check." Author reply: "CLI apply path checks operator role via existing auth hook; added unit test asserting unauthorized apply is rejected."
Requested changes prior to approval: include latency-risk safety gate, bound telemetry labels, stabilize e2e smoke test, and add example tenant profile. All requested items were addressed in follow-ups.
Post-review approvals: Liam Chen approved after docs added; Diego approved after sampler changes; Marta approved after e2e stabilization.
Merge: Squash merge to main.
Migration/Operational notes: - New metrics emitted by the sandbox are low-frequency and behind a feature flag econ.sandbox.enabled which defaults to off in production config. - Sample profiles are shipped with clear disclaimers; operators should run the sandbox and validate before applying to production tenants. - Docs added at docs/ops/econ-sandbox.md with example workflows and recommended guardrails.
Backwards compatibility: None of the changes alter runtime serving behavior unless an operator explicitly uses the CLI to apply recommendations. The package API is additive.
Rollout plan: Feature flagged in config; enable for internal SRE and solutions teams first; collect telemetry and iterate on scoring.
Release notes: Adds econ sandbox CLI for local autotune simulation with sample profiles and safety gates; suitable for engineering and solutions workflows.
Known limitations and follow-ups: - Current simulator does not model multi-device cross-shard sharding penalties precisely; follow-up ticket ENG-4999 to extend the simulator with shard-aware latency profiles. - Recommend a follow-up to add a 'batch-size ladder' visualizer (ENG-5002) and an autotuner connector that pipes sandbox recommendations into the existing autotune pipeline (ENG-5003).
Add new econ-sandbox CLI to simulate tenant workloads and propose batching/caching/quant defaults; includes e2e smoke, safety gates for latency SLOs, and documentation; non-breaking

Motivation: Recent support tickets (SUP-903) and internal postmortem identified two recurring pain points: (1) RBACv2 rollouts often over-provisioned operator bindings leading to unexpected KMS calls crossing geo boundaries; (2) audit logs and KMS access records were not reconciled, making longitudinal investigations slow. This PR ships a three-part solution: a policy synthesizer that emits minimal effective RBAC patches, a KMS usage reviewer that tags KMS calls with derived decision traces and residency flags, and an audit-reconciliation job that cross-checks authz decisions, KMS events, and immutable audit envelopes to flag inconsistencies.

Design summary: - policy/synthesizer: a deterministic pass that consumes role-presets + service-claim annotations and outputs minimal allow-lists (keeps deny semantics untouched). It is implemented as an idempotent compiler stage used by the policy orchestrator during canaries. - kms/reviewer: sidecar-style aggregator (service behind /internal/kms-review) that enriches KMS telemetry with policy-decision-ids, tenant-residency, and operator-scope to enable quota/residency checks. - audit/reconciler: periodic job (configurable cadence) which performs joins across authz_decisions, kms_access_log, and audit_envelopes to produce a per-tenant discrepancy report written to compliance.reconciliations. The job includes a lightweight dedupe and fingerprint algorithm to avoid noisy alerts.

Implementation notes/changes: - new package: internal/policy/synthesizer (Go) with unit tests and fakes for operator presets. - new service: services/kms-reviewer (small Go HTTP service + Prometheus metrics), deployed as a singleton per-region. - migration: add reconciliations table (+ schema v43) to postgres; migration includes backfill script limited to 30 days. - observability: new metrics policy_synth_runs_total, kms_reviewer_calls, reconciler_discrepancies_by_type; tags include tenant_id and region. - ops: added a cron manifest at deploy/cron/reconciler.yaml and a Helm values section to opt-in for high-compliance tenants.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for synthesizer compiler logic
- [x] Integration tests for kms-reviewer enrichment route
- [x] Migration and backfill tested on staging
- [x] Metrics and logs instrumented
- [x] Documentation: docs/rbac/policy-synthesizer.md and docs/ops/reconciler-runbook.md
- [x] Security scan (snyk/gosec) passed after fixing two low-severity findings

Commits (high level): - 1) add synthesizer core + tests - 2) implement kms reviewer service and client shim - 3) add reconciler job + migration - 4) add Helm charts + deploy manifests - 5) docs and runbook - 6) fixes from reviewers (metrics labels, retry tuning)

Changed areas (high level): - internal/policy/synthesizer/* - services/kms-reviewer/{cmd,handlers,metrics} - jobs/reconciler/* - cmd/infra/migrations/043_add_reconciliations.sql - deploy/helm/redwood/templates/cron-reconciler.yaml - docs/rbac/policy-synthesizer.md - docs/ops/reconciler-runbook.md

Review conversation (summary): - Ethan Chu: "Can we avoid an N^2 policy expansion in the synthesizer?" Reply: added a constraint-sweep that limits expansion to cross-service grants only; added tests and a benchmark fixture. - Marta Kaczmarek: "Metrics need tenant and region labels for SLO slicing." Reply: added tenant_id and region labels, instrumented with cardinality guard and sample rate. - Samir Patel: "Make migration backward-compatible for mixed-version clusters." Reply: reconciler backfill is guarded by a feature flag and uses a read-path fallback when reconciliations table is not present.

CI summary: - unit: pass - integration: pass (flaky test fixed in commit 5) - lint: pass - e2e: pass on staging deployment - security-scan: initial fail (gosec findings) -> patched -> pass. Full pipeline passed on rerun.

Operational notes: - Default deployment is opt-in for enterprise tenants via Helm values `reconciler.enabled`. - KMS reviewer runs as a regional singleton to keep cross-tenant telemetry coalesced. - To troubleshoot mismatches, use the new /internal/debug/reconciler endpoint (RBAC-protected) which returns sample joined artifacts for a reconciliation ID.

Merge outcome: Squashed and merged to main. Post-merge: run migration v43 during next maintenance window; operators on Dedicated/Private should coordinate with infra for opt-in. Release note included. If any tenant relies on implicit operator bindings, they should schedule a canary with policy.synth.enabled=false to avoid immediate rollbacks.
Added RBACv2 policy synthesizer (auto-minimization), KMS usage reviewer service, and periodic audit reconciliation job. No API changes to public endpoints. Ops: add new cronjob and a small DB migration.
This PR was intentionally split into small commits to make the security review easier; product/ops are informed. No public SDK changes.

Motivation: Recent incident (SUP-3021) showed tenancy-level P95 excursions in single regions causing noisy cross-region failovers. This hotfix introduces a lightweight latency-budget enforcer that applies probabilistic, low-impact shedding when a tenant's short-window budget is exceeded, and a regional tilt detector that attenuates admission from a tilted region while preserving global fairness. Goals: 1) Reduce noisy cross-region re-routing during short surges, 2) Keep impact per-tenant minimal (soft drop vs hard eviction), 3) Provide observability hooks for incident triage. Changes included: - introduce serve/shedder/latency_budget.go: sliding-window budget calculator (50ms buckets, configurable window), probabilistic soft-shedding with exponential cooldown per-tenant - introduce serve/router/tilt_detector.go: region-level tilt detector using asymmetric ingress delta and heat score, exposes tear-down signal to router - add console/telemetry/tilt_metric_exporter.go: new metrics: redwood.region.tilt_score, redwood.shed.rate_by_tenant, redwood.shed.recovery_cooldown - k8s config tweak deploy/k8s/redwood-config.yaml: runtime feature flag runtime.flags.latency_soft_shed (default=true) and tilt_sensitivity (0..1) - tests/tests/tilt_simulation_test.go: deterministic simulation harness and unit tests to validate scoring/backoff - docs/docs/ops/tilt-mitigation.md: operator runbook and suggested runbooks for threshold tuning Checklist: - [x] implement algorithm and unit tests - [x] add telemetry and dashboards (minimal) - [x] add runtime flag and config override - [x] integration test simulation - [x] manual canary in staging / smoke ok Commits (high level): - 1a2b3c4 add latency budget enforcer and tests - 2b3c4d5 add regional tilt detector and router integration - 3c4d5e6 export tilt metrics and add flags - 4d5e6f7 fix cooldown off-by-one and add more unit coverage Review summary: Initial design reviewed by Luca and Priya; Luca asked for stronger metrics around false-positive shedding and a runtime override; Priya flagged potential interaction with existing KV-preserve logic. Changes made: added shed.reason tag, exposed runtime.flags.latency_soft_shed, adjusted backoff to avoid immediate reopen oscillation (cooldown doubled). Review conversation (abridged): - Luca Romano (2026-02-19): "Good direction. Please add shed.reason tag and a counter for false positives so SRE can tune sensitivity." - Maya Patel (2026-02-19): "Added shed.reason tag and a rejected_count metric; also added an operator flag to force-disable soft-shed for emergency rollback." - Priya Singh (2026-02-20): "Check interaction with kv-preserve path: we must avoid shedding requests that carry recoverable KV state." - Maya Patel (2026-02-20): "Added explicit bypass for KV-preserve marker headers; added unit tests covering that path." - Alex Kim (2026-02-21): "Integration test failed on first run (e2e timeout). Reran and passed; left one flaky test marked with @flake label." CI and validation: - First pipeline: unit & integration passed, e2e timed out (one test). - Reran e2e after increasing test timeout and isolating flake; final CI green. Merge decision: After two approvals (Luca, Priya) and green CI, PR was squashed and merged. Post-merge actions: - Stage rollout: feature enabled by default in staging and canary, runtime flag off for top-tier customers for 48h to observe. - Telemetry: added Grafana panel redwood.region.tilt_score and alert redwood.tilt.high (threshold tuned conservatively). Observed behavior in canary: slight reduction in cross-region failovers and tenant-level P95 drop ~12% on simulated tilt workload. Operator notes: - If false positives observed, set runtime.flags.latency_soft_shed=false for the affected namespace and open ENG-4991. - Tilt sensitivity is conservative by default; for aggressive mitigation increase tilt_sensitivity to 0.6 but test in canary first.
Hotfix: add latency-budget enforcer (probabilistic soft-shedding) and regional tilt detector to reduce cross-zone impact during asymmetric spikes. Adds telemetry for tilt incidents and a runtime flag to tune soft-shed aggressiveness.

Motivation: SDKs had subtle divergences in telemetry keys and streaming reconnect behaviour that make cross-language observability and incident triage harder. In particular: (1) telemetry field names and types were inconsistent across Python/TypeScript/Go, (2) streaming clients in TS/Go could drop/lose a cursor when a reconnect happened during a partial frame, and (3) retry defaults were aggressive for short-lived network blips and caused short-lived request storms. This PR synchronizes a compact telemetry schema, preserves stream cursor state across reconnects, and relaxes retry presets to 'soft' profiles across all three SDKs.

Design summary:
- Introduce a canonical telemetry envelope (telemetry.v=1 -> telemetry.schema=redwood_sdk_v1) and add typed fields: request_id, sdk.name, sdk.version, route.hash, client.sequence_hint. Old keys are mapped in a one-time shim for backwards compatibility.
- Streaming: add a small resume protocol that atomically persists the last completed frame id and pending buffer during reconnect; implement idempotent resume handshake in TS and Go streaming clients, and ensure Python client exposes the same resume token.
- Retries: change default retry/secondary backoff parameters to be less aggressive (lower attempt multiplier, wider jitter window, short circuit on HTTP 429->respect Retry-After).

Implementation notes:
- Python: sdks/python/redwood/telemetry.py added telemetry envelope; streaming client updated to expose resume_token; bumped python SDK to 0.12.5.
- TypeScript: packages/sdk-stream/src/resume.ts implements client-side cursor preservation; telemetry mapper added; bumped ts SDK to 1.27.1.
- Go: sdk-go/telemetry/map.go and stream/resume.go add mapping and resume support; adjusted retry.Backoff presets; bumped go SDK to v1.8.1.

Commits (high-level):
- refactor(telemetry): canonical telemetry envelope and compat shim
- feat(stream): resume-token persistence and atomic handshake (ts/go/py)
- fix(retry): soften default backoff and add Retry-After handling
- test: cross-language integration tests for resume and telemetry propagation
- docs: API surface update and migration notes

Tests & CI: unit test additions for all three SDKs, an integration matrix job that exercises reconnect/resume with a mocked server, and telemetry contract tests. The CI run initially had a flaky e2e for TS streams (timeout on first run) which was re-run; all checks passed on the second run.

Files changed (high level):
- sdks/python/redwood/telemetry.py
- sdks/python/redwood/streaming/client.py
- packages/sdk-stream/src/resume.ts
- packages/sdk-stream/src/telemetry-mapper.ts
- sdk-go/telemetry/map.go
- sdk-go/stream/resume.go
- sdk-go/retry/backoff.go
- docs/sdks/migration/telemetry.md
- tests/integration/stream-resume-matrix.yaml

Migration & compatibility: The telemetry shim maps legacy keys (trace_id -> telemetry.request_id, SDK -> sdk.name) for one release cycle; no customer-facing breaking changes expected. Streaming resume uses a resume_token that is sent by the client on reconnect; servers that don't understand it fall back to full restart, so behavior is graceful.

Release plan: squash-merge to main, then publish patch releases for py/ts/go SDKs. Bump notes: py 0.12.4 -> 0.12.5, ts 1.27.0 -> 1.27.1, go v1.8.0 -> v1.8.1

Review summary & discussion:
- Marco: "Telemetry mapping looks sane; can we add a metric for number of resume attempts?" Author: "Added sdk.resume.attempts counter in telemetry patch; included unit tests."
- Sophie: "TS resume handshake needs a deterministic timeout for partial frame reassembly." Author: "Added a 250ms default reassembly window with override in client options."
- Diego (security): "Confirm resume token doesn't leak sensitive prompt text." Author: "Resume token contains only sequence ids and short checksums; no payload is stored or transmitted."

CI notes:
- unit-tests (py): pass
- unit-tests (ts): pass
- unit-tests (go): pass
- integration/stream-resume-matrix: initial fail (ts timeout) -> rerun -> pass
- lint: pass

Merge: merged with squash via GitHub UI; commit message prefixed with "sdk: sync telemetry & resume across sdks". Post-merge: published SDK patch releases and updated SDK compatibility table in docs.

Observability: added a dashboard query snippet to Console docs (docs/sdks/migration/telemetry.md) showing join keys to use when correlating cross-lang traces.

Follow-ups (tracked in ENG-2021):
- monitor resume success rate and surface alert if resume attempts exceed 2% of stream sessions.
- consider server-side resume token acknowledgement to reduce fallback restarts.

Overall impact: improved cross-language parity for telemetry and streaming ergonomics; fewer noisy retries during transient network issues; better observability for triage.
Backwards-compatible telemetry schema alignment for SDKs; streaming cursor preservation on reconnect; softer retry defaults to reduce downstream rate spikes. Patch-level SDK bumps (py/ts/go).

payload.body:
Context: we observed higher tail latency and sporadic OOMs when serving mixed workloads containing Mistral, Qwen and Llama family models. Root causes were: (1) suboptimal kernel selection for fused rotary/attention on Mistral and some Llama variants, (2) misaligned group-quantization (GQA) code paths that spilled to host under certain MQA layouts, and (3) a KV-cache pointer/stride bug in Qwen cache layout that created fragmentation under continuous batching. This PR introduces a model-family aware kernel picker (heuristics based on model_family, hidden_size, seq_dist) that prefers fused-rotary + threaded attention kernels for Mistral/Llama; adds quantization-aware attention execution paths to handle GQA/MQA edge cases (avoids fp16->host spills by switching to a compact packed layout when group sizes mismatch); fixes Qwen KV-cache stride/pointer arithmetic and compacts cache layout to reduce working set; and adjusts continuous-batcher thresholds and micro-batch sizing per-model to prevent cross-model OOMs. Also includes unit/integration tests, perf microbench harness updates, and a staged rollout plan (canary -> 30% -> global). Motivation and impact: these are production-facing fixes that improve latency and stability without requiring model rewrites. Backwards-compatible toggles are exposed as runtime knobs (kernel_picker.mode, quant.tune_mode, kvcache.compact_layout) that default to safe behavior. Rollout notes: start with canary in us-west-2 for 48 hours, monitor token-level latency and OOM counts, then 30% for 72 hours before global.
Diego Martinez: Can you add stable perf numbers with a replayed mixed workload? The initial numbers look promising but we need determinism.
Ava Chen: Added deterministic workload harness and results in perf_benchmarks, also wired CI perf check to run with fixed seeds.
Priya Kapoor: The quant fallback looks safe but please call out any additional mem overhead. Also prefer a feature flag for 30-day grace.
Ava Chen: quant.tune_mode default uses compact-packed only when group sizes misalign; documented expected ~0.6-1.4% peak memory overhead in worst-case and added a runtime flag quant.tune_mode=off for emergency rollback.
Ethan Li: Verified that fused_rotary path is a pure opt for Mistral-7B and doesn't regress Llama-7B; approved after smoke tests on dedicated pools.
Improved model-family kernel selection for Mistral/Llama, fixed Qwen KV-cache stride fragmentation, and added GQA/MQA-safe quantization fallback. Result: lower p50/p95 latency and fewer OOMs under mixed workloads. Exposed runtime knobs for gradual rollout and rollback.
Repro: mixed-workload harness (Mistral-7B, Llama-13B, Qwen-14B) ran for 100k requests with deterministic seeds. Added CI perf job that runs 3x stable-seed trials. Canary in us-west-2 for 48h with observed telemetry; then 30% for 72h. No regressions in unit/integration suites.
Mistral-7B small-chat workload: p50 token latency -11%, p95 -22%, throughput +18% (adaptive batching)
Llama-13B mixed prompt workload: p50 token latency -8%, p95 -19%, throughput +12%
Qwen-14B long-context streaming: p50 token latency -10% after KV-cache compaction, memory working set reduced ~14%
Small model fleet (7B family) aggregate mixed load: average tokens/sec +20% and OOMs reduced from 6->0 in stress runs

Context and motivation: We observed intermittent client-side crashes and invalid JSON errors when streaming long chat responses through the OpenAI-compat SSE adapter. Root cause: a mix of small TCP packet boundaries, server-side aggressive chunking, and occasional delimiter bytes embedded in model token escapes resulted in mid-JSON fragments being emitted without clear boundaries. Prior fixes focused on delimiting heuristics but still allowed tight races where a fragment split removed the terminal '}' or a tool-call sentinel.

This PR implements a two-part strategy: (1) a quarantining window for suspect fragments so the parser doesn't emit partial JSON to higher layers until it has greater confidence; (2) a delimiter-healing state machine that uses lightweight delimiter fingerprints, sequence-checkpoint hints, and backoff/hedging to reconstruct or request missing spans where possible. Together these reduce spurious parse errors, avoid delivering truncated structured outputs to callers, and maintain OpenAI-compat behavior for function/tool calling.

What changed (high level):
- Introduced pkg/sse/healer.go: quarantine buffer, delimiter fingerprinting, and a non-blocking repair loop that attempts local reassembly before escalating to a retry/hedge policy.
- Parser changes in pkg/sse/parser.go: tag suspicious chunks with a quarantine flag, defer JSON emission until healer signals a boundary-safe span. Added hooks for seq checkpoints emitted by the runtime.
- Compatibility adapter update in api/openai/compat/streaming_adapter.go: preserve original event ordering and ensure function-call sentinel handoff is only exposed after heal/commit.
- New unit and fuzz tests in pkg/sse/healer_test.go covering: escaped delimiter collisions, UTF-8 split across frames, and synthetic out-of-order fragment arrivals.
- Added an e2e scenario harness tests/e2e/sse_partial_json.yaml to reproduce previous customer-visible failure.
- Documentation: docs/streaming-framing.md expands the guidance on quarantine behavior and rollout knobs.

Implementation notes and heuristics:
- Quarantine window is size-bounded (config default 4KB, configurable per-route) and time-bounded (default 500ms). Suspicious fragments are identified by checksum mismatch of delimiter fingerprint and by trailing-token heuristics (incomplete UTF-8, unbalanced braces, dangling tool-call sentinel).
- Delimiter fingerprint: a tiny canonicalization of trailing bytes and escape context to detect fragmented delimiters without maintaining full tokenization state. This allows cheap detection and grouping of fragments that likely belong to the same logical JSON span.
- Healing flow: local coalescing -> fingerprint match -> emit; if local coalescing fails within the window we fall back to issuing a hedged request for the missing tail from the model-serving layer (configurable; default off in hosted to avoid duplicate billing).
- Backpressure: create a soft-fence that slows downstream delivery if quarantine occupancy grows; integrates with scheduler to prioritize completing suspect spans.

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests added for all heuristics and edge cases. Fuzz harness included to stress UTF-8 splits and delimiter collisions.
- E2E harness reproduces the customer failure vector and shows the new parser reduces invalid-JSON delivery rate from 0.9% to <0.01% under synthetic congestion.
- CI: lint + unit + e2e (the e2e job is gated behind an opt-in label in CI to keep default runs fast).

Rollout and compatibility:
- Feature gated behind experimental flag 'sse_quarantine_healer' controlled at route-level in the config. Default: off for non-Redwood dedicated/private until a quiet period of 72 hours in canary.
- No breaking API changes. The adapter preserves OpenAI stream semantics but delays commit of structured outputs until the fragment is healed; client-visible behavior only differs by fewer parse errors and a bounded (~500ms) potential additional delay when quarantine heuristics trigger.

Checklist:
- [x] Parser q/o quarantine flag
- [x] Healer state machine + unit tests
- [x] Integration tests for function-call sentinel ordering
- [x] Fuzz tests for UTF-8 and delimiter collisions
- [x] Docs update and rollout notes
- [x] CI green (with opt-in e2e)

Notes and follow-ups:
- Instrumentation: added metrics sse.quarantine.size, sse.heal.attempts, sse.heal.success_rate for the console. Follow-up: add trace tags to token-level traces for postmortems (ENG-4527).
- Consider exposing a per-tenant hedging opt-in for Dedicated customers; this is tracked as ENG-4579.

Related work: references prior SSE fixes but takes a different approach by quarantining ambiguous fragments instead of immediate delimiter-normalization. This is complementary to the checksum/seq approaches in earlier PRs and reduces noisy false-positives in structured output parsing.
Priya: 'Can you clarify the hedging cost implications for hosted customers? We should default hedging off for hosted and document tradeoffs.'
Ava: 'Hedging is off by default for hosted; added comment and config doc. See docs section and linked linear.'
Diego: 'Healer looks good; two nits on test naming and make the fingerprint function cheaper.'
Ava: 'Addressed Diego's nits; simplified fingerprint and added benchmark to show <2% CPU impact under heavy stream load.'
Ethan: 'Approved after confirming no regression in function-call order with adapter change.'
Merge: squash by maintainer after CI passed.
- Reduce partial-JSON parse errors by quarantining suspect SSE fragments and employing a lightweight delimiter-healing state machine.
- New route-level feature flag: sse_quarantine_healer (default: off).
- Metrics: sse.quarantine.size, sse.heal.attempts, sse.heal.success_rate.
bugfix(streaming): quarantine ambiguous SSE fragments and heal delimiter-boundary races to avoid partial-JSON delivery

Motivation: Our presubmit hooks and release preflight are implemented as a mix of bash entrypoints and GitHub Actions composites. This has led to several flakes (subshell quoting, inconsistent PATHs), poor testability, and slow iteration for repo-standard tooling. This PR decomposes core CI hooks into small, versioned Go-based actions (ci-toolchain-bootstrap, ci-lint-adapter, ci-release-smoke) and updates repository license headers to a standard SPDX header for legal compliance.

What changed (high level):
- Introduced a lightweight Go-based action runner under infra/ci/plugins/ that replaces the long-running bash entrypoints. These are intentionally single-responsibility CLIs that read JSON config from stdin for easier testing.
- Bootstrapping: moved toolchain bootstrap logic into ci-toolchain-bootstrap (pins go/node/python versions and provides a hermetic toolcache path). This reduces matrix size by detecting host capabilities at runtime and avoiding unnecessary matrix axes.
- Lint/test adapters: added ci-lint-adapter which normalizes linter invocation across repos and acts as a compatibility shim for legacy configs. This allowed us to simplify the workflow files to a single lint job with sharding hints.
- Release smoke: added ci-release-smoke, a small action used by the release workflow to run a minimal end-to-end smoke test (deploy to staging, run sanity prompts, validate response shape) before signing artifacts.
- License headers: standardized SPDX license headers across changed files and added a simple license-check step to the precommit flow.
- CI changes: updated .github/workflows/ci.yml to use the new actions, trimmed the test matrix by consolidating platform axes, and introduced a fastpath presubmit lane for changes limited to docs and examples.

Why Go actions: Go binaries are hermetic across runners, compile to a single artifact, and are easier to unit test compared to shell scripts. They also avoid frequent quoting and environment issues we saw in bash-based hooks.

Checklist:
- [x] Add Go action sources + build scripts
- [x] Update workflow YAML to use new actions
- [x] Add license header updates and license-check job
- [x] Run full CI and fix resulting lint/test regressions
- [x] Smoke-tested release workflow in staging

Testing notes / validation steps:
1) Local: make -C infra/ci/plugins/ build && ./bin/ci-toolchain-bootstrap --dry-run
2) CI: confirm GitHub Actions 'ci/build' and 'ci/lint' pass (they now exercise the Go binaries via action wrapper)
3) Release smoke: tested on staging tag v2026.02.28-smoke and validated failure/fallback behavior

Related work: ENG-4821 (ci-era modernization), ENG-4999 (release reliability). Also follows-up on past bash-to-go experiments in infra/ci (see PRs: refactor/ci-go-experiment).

Motivation: several operational incidents exposed long-lived delegation grants and unverifiable audit links when operators replayed requests across regions. This change introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) an RBACv2 policy TTL enforcement layer that rejects or soft-expunges stale delegation bindings; 2) an audit-link HMAC signing scheme so downstream consumers can validate event continuity without exposing key material; and 3) a KMS region-affinity validator that checks KMS wrap/unwrap requests against the tenant's declared region pins and fails fast when mismatches are detected. The work here is intentionally conservative: enforcement is gated behind a feature flag and we ship a migration helper to identify bindings that would be impacted. Checklist: - [x] implement policy TTL validator with unit tests - [x] wire TTL checks into policy evaluation path (non-blocking mode behind flag) - [x] implement audit-link signing middleware and verification util - [x] implement KMS region-affinity validator and attach to crypto-proxy - [x] add migration script to identify stale bindings and generate a remediation plan - [x] add e2e tests exercising an operator delegation lifecycle across regions - [x] update docs and runbook snippets - [x] telemetry: policy_denied_ttl, auditlink_verify_ok, kms_affinity_mismatch KB/Linear references: ENG-4891 (policy TTL enforcement), SEC-102 (audit-link design), SRE-317 (kms affinity checks). Rollout plan: 1) deploy to staging with feature flags OFF. 2) run migration scanner (tools/bin/scan-stale-bindings) against a snapshot and produce remediation CSV. 3) enable TTL soft-deny mode (record metrics and allow override via operator flag) for two weeks. 4) enable hard deny for tenant groups with low risk. 5) enable HMAC signing and rotate audit verification keys via the key-manager endpoint. 6) enable KMS affinity validator in read-only mode (log+metric only) for 1 week then hard-fail. Backwards compatibility: audit-link signing uses an optional header (X-Audit-Link-Signature). Legacy consumers ignoring the header will continue to receive events. The RBACv2 evaluation path accepts both TTL-marked bindings and legacy bindings; the migration script annotates bindings that require attention. Security considerations: the HMAC secret is stored in KMS-scoped secrets; verification keys are published to the internal key-discovery service with ACLs. The KMS validator only checks location tags and does not change crypto operations. Migration tool: tools/migration/identify_stale_rbac_bindings.py ships in this PR and produces CSV (tenant_id, binding_id, expiry, last_seen, recommended_action). Testing: unit tests for validator logic (policy, auditlink, kms) included; e2e uses a local crypto-proxy test harness and a vm-simulated multi-region runner. Follow-ups: tie TTL metrics to Optimize so customers get suggestions for binding pruning; add a remediation UI in Console; and add an operator CLI to bulk-revoke stale bindings.

Amina Patel: added per-tenant feature flag and updated migration tool to emit tenant-safe list in commit a9e3b21.

Monitor metrics policy_denied_ttl and kms_affinity_mismatch during rollout.

Motivation: Customers frequently accept our defaults but still overprovision or underutilize cache/batch settings. This PR introduces the 'Cost Gardener' and a Default Curator that cultivates tenant-specific starter profiles for batching, KV-prefill, and quantization bands. The goal is to reduce first-touch unit cost while keeping latency SLO regressions <= 5% and providing a safe hedge policy for fallbacks.

What this PR does (high level): 1) Adds gardener service (redwood/econ/gardener) that synthesizes per-tenant default bundles from historical sampling and lightweight local-sim-mode. 2) Default Curator CLI (redwood/cli/cost-garden) that can produce: seed-batch-presets, cache-prefix-presets, and rounded quantization bands with safety thresholds. 3) Implements a small policy engine for automated rollback/hedge (tenant-level policy: prefer latency-safety over token-cost when delta > threshold). 4) Telemetry hooks and new metrics: cost_gardener.score, gardener.seed_count, gardener.rollback_trigger. 5) Docs and a guided quickstart: ops can run the curator in dry-run to preview expected unit-econ impact.

Checklist: - [x] Core algorithm + API - [x] CLI and dry-run mode - [x] Telemetry + dashboards (basic) - [x] Unit tests and integration smoke - [x] Docs and examples

Why different: instead of one-size defaults this system emits conservative per-tenant 'seed profiles' based on a compact fingerprint and growth heuristics (garden bed model). The approach prioritizes explainability (why a seed was chosen) and a safety-first rollback policy.

Backward compatibility: defaults are additive; existing default config remains unless an operator applies a curated seed. The gardener only annotates profiles and never forces live rollout without opt-in or configured automatic rollout window.
Evan Li: Nice isolations; can you decouple the local-sim-mode so it can be swapped with a remote simulator later?
