Context: During the hot-route capacity protection rollout we introduced new overload event metrics (shed/admission_control) that were intended to be low-cardinality (route_group, tier, region, reason). In the last merge window we accidentally started emitting per-request / per-tenant labels on the overload event counters due to a tag plumbing change in the gateway -> telemetry bridge. This caused a rapid increase in series count in Prometheus and intermittent ingestion backpressure, and it also made the SRE dashboards noisy/slow to load. What changed: (1) Add a strict label allowlist for overload event metrics in the telemetry emitter and drop/ignore all non-allowed labels (e.g., tenant_id, request_id, trace_id, api_key_id, user_agent, model_revision). (2) Split the old overloaded "overload_event" into two metrics: redwood_overload_shed_total and redwood_overload_admission_denied_total with a stable label set {route_group, tier, region, reason}. (3) Add a lightweight counter redwood_overload_labels_dropped_total{metric_name,label_key} to make future regressions visible without paging the fleet. (4) Update dashboard queries to use the new metrics and remove the accidental group-by on tenant_id. Notes: This is intentionally conservative and enforces invariants close to the emitter to avoid future regressions from upstream tag propagation. This does not change overload behavior itself; only metric emission. Validation: Verified in staging by replaying overload simulation traffic and confirming series count stays flat; production canary (us-east) shows series count returning to baseline within ~30 minutes after rollout. Checklist: [x] Unit tests for allowlist behavior + label drop accounting [x] Update dashboards/recording rules in monorepo bundle [x] Backwards-compat shim: keep the old metric name as an alias for 7 days (deprecated) to avoid alert breakage during rollout [x] Added runbook note: "If series count spikes, check labels_dropped_total". Rollout plan: Merge + deploy with standard gateway release train; no flag required. Monitoring: prometheus_remote_write_queue, series_count by job=telemetry, and the hot-route protection dashboards (ENG-4926).
Logan Wright (review): Can we guarantee we never re-introduce tenant_id via shared context tags? The code path currently merges request-scoped tags by default in a couple places.
Nadia Rahman (author): Yep — this change applies the allowlist at the last possible step (right before emit). Even if upstream merges request context tags, they’ll be dropped for these metric names. Added a unit test that simulates request tags containing tenant_id/request_id/trace_id to ensure they never make it through.
Allison Grant (review): Please keep naming consistent with the metrics standard doc: *_total suffix and reason label values should be stable enums. Also avoid label_key cardinality explosion in labels_dropped_total.
Nadia Rahman (author): Updated metric names to *_total and normalized reason values to the existing enum set (quota, overload, capacity, circuit_open, unknown). For labels_dropped_total, label_key is limited to a small allowlist of known-problem keys (tenant_id, request_id, trace_id, api_key_id, user_agent, model_revision) to keep it bounded.
Rafael Mendes (review): For SRE: will this break existing alerts today? We had a paging storm risk if panels fail to load during an event.
Nadia Rahman (author): Added a 7-day alias gauge/counter mapping (old name emits the same value with the same stable labels) and updated dashboards/recording rules in this PR. Alerts should continue to work immediately, but they’ll use the new rules once deployed.
Caleb Johnson (review): Any evidence this fixes remote_write lag? Also, can we add a note to the runbook on how to confirm cardinality is back to baseline?
Nadia Rahman (author): Added staging evidence to the PR description and included a runbook snippet pointing to series_count{job="api-gateway"} and top label keys via promtool/cardinality panel; also added labels_dropped_total to the dashboard so on-call can confirm the guardrail is working.

Motivation: Multi-tool call ergonomics have been a recurring source of edge cases in production: duplicated side-effects when retries occur, inconsistent result injection order when tools run in parallel, and poor streaming behavior for OpenAI-compatible clients when tool outputs are interleaved. This PR implements a small surface and runtime contract to make parallel tool execution idempotent-safe and to provide deterministic result coalescing while preserving streaming semantics for OpenAI-compat streaming endpoints.

What this changes (single-string summary): Adds a lightweight 'fanout coalescer' in the call_executor to collect tool outputs, canonicalize ordering, and attach deterministic metadata (call-id, attempt-id) so retries are recognized and dropped when duplicate. Introduces an idempotency key into the tool invocation layer; retries with same key now produce deduplicated results at the injector. Adjusts streaming adapter in the OpenAI compatibility layer so that streaming events for tool outputs are emitted as a consistent, monotonic sequence and include a new 'tool_chunk' envelope for downstream SDKs to reassemble. Updates SDK TypeScript helper to surface tool attempt metadata to application code and adds end-to-end integration tests.

Design notes: The coalescer maintains per-request transient state in memory (bounded map keyed by tool-call-id) and attaches an ordinal slot for each tool invocation based on the logical call graph generated during planning. When a tool returns, its output is buffered briefly (100ms by default) to allow aligned arrival of parallel calls; this avoids janky interleaving in the streaming API while keeping latency impact small for common workloads. The idempotency key is generated by the platform caller (or can be provided by the SDK) and is propagated through the public API headers. On receiving a retry, the coalescer checks (tool-call-id, idempotency-key, attempt-id) triple to determine uniqueness.

OpenAI-compat streaming adjustments: Previously, tool outputs interleaved raw tokens into the top-level event stream which caused downstream reassembly problems for clients expecting coherent 'tool' blocks. This patch adds a lightweight 'tool_chunk' event envelope: {"type":"tool_chunk","tool_id":"...","offset":123,"attempt_id":"...","data":"..."} so SDKs can accumulate chunks and publish a single 'tool_result' once coalesced. The server still emits partial results as streaming chunks but tags them explicitly to avoid confusion with assistant tokens. The compatibility adapter also upgrades connection-level metadata so that older SDKs still receive assistant tokens unchanged if they do not understand the 'tool_chunk' envelope (backwards compatible).

Developer ergonomics and API surface: - New header: X-Redwood-Tool-Idempotency: <opaque-key> (optional). If omitted, the platform synthesizes one per request. - Tool call metadata available in streaming events and final result: attempt_id, idempotency_key, call_index. - Behavior guarantees: a single final tool_result will be injected per (tool-call-id, idempotency_key) pair, even with multiple attempts.

Testing and validation: Added integration tests that simulate parallel tool fanout with intentional delays and generated retries. Tests cover: deterministic ordering, deduplication on retries, streaming chunk reassembly, and fallback to legacy stream behavior for old clients. Load microbenchmarks show median end-to-end add-on latency of +8ms for typical 2-tool fanout and worst-case +43ms for bursty 8-tool scenarios (configurable buffer window reduced for latency-sensitive tenants).

Migration: No breaking changes. SDKs updated but older SDKs continue to work: they will receive chunked tool outputs as additional assistant tokens (compat path). We recommend SDK upgrades to take advantage of attempt metadata for safer side-effect handling.

Operational concerns: The coalescer uses an in-memory bounded cache with TTL; in Dedicated/Private deployments this stays node-local. For strict cross-node idempotency (rare), we added a toggle to persist minimal idempotency markers to the global metadata store (disabled by default). Metrics: new counters for tool_coalesce_count, tool_dedupe_count, tool_stream_chunk_bytes; new alert when tool_dedupe_rate > 5% over 5m.

Notes on rollout: Canary disabled by default in hosted; canary rollout plan added to Redwood Console: 10% traffic for 48h then 50% for 24h, monitor dedupe_count and latency.

Files changed and rationale (high level): server/tooling/call_executor.py - coalescer + idempotency checks; server/openai/compat/streaming_adapter.py - tool_chunk envelope and compatibility logic; sdk/ts/src/tooling.ts - helpers to reassemble tool chunks and expose attempt metadata; docs/api/tooling.md - updated API docs and header notes; tests/integration/test_tool_retries.py - new end-to-end scenarios; tests/unit/test_coalescer.py - unit coverage.

See commits for incremental steps and review comments below.
Aisha Patel (reviewer): Overall 👍. Two requests: make the coalescer buffer timeout config per-tenant and add a metric for coalescer-buffer-waits. Also please document the compatibility fallback clearly in docs.
Lena Thompson (author): Thanks — added per-tenant config with a sane default (100ms) and exposed tool_coalescer_buffer_waits metric. Updated docs to call out the fallback behavior and the header semantics.
Miguel Rivera (reviewer): Can you clarify behavior when a tool returns partial streaming then fails and is retried? Is the partial stream replayed or suppressed?
Lena Thompson (author): Partial streams are buffered and emitted as 'tool_chunk' pieces; on fail+retry we drop chunks from previous attempts that share the same (call-id, idempotency_key, attempt_id) triple. We retained a short tombstone window (500ms) to avoid race replays. Added unit test to cover this scenario.
Samir Gupta (reviewer): Unit tests look good. CI integration flaky: test_integration::test_tool_retries sometimes times out on macos-latest; re-run passed. Please monitor flaky test and file follow-up (ENG-4388).
Lena Thompson (author): Filed ENG-4388 for flaky CI, added increased timeout as a mitigation in this PR until the CI root cause is addressed.
Aisha Patel (approval): Approved after addressing metrics and docs.
Miguel Rivera (approval): Approved.
Samir Gupta (approval): Approved.
User-visible: deterministic tool result ordering for parallel tool calls; idempotent retries prevent duplicate side-effects when SDK supplies X-Redwood-Tool-Idempotency; streaming now emits explicit 'tool_chunk' events for easier reassembly. Operators: new metrics (tool_coalesce_count, tool_dedupe_count, tool_stream_chunk_bytes) and config for per-tenant coalescer buffer window.
payload.title: Tool fanout result coalescer + idempotent retry semantics, OpenAI-compat streaming adjustments

Summary: This PR implements an adaptive 'shadow fusion' controller that continuously evaluates shadow traffic fidelity and can promote traffic slices to a staged canary when a multi-metric confidence threshold is met. It ships a 'rollback mitigator' subsystem that generates and validates dry-run rollback plans (snapshots + quick-rewind playbook) to reduce mean time to recover when regressions are detected. Motivation: Customers running shadow validations before canary promotion wanted fewer manual gating steps and faster recovery options. This change reduces manual toil, shortens promotion windows, and makes rollbacks reproducible and auditable.

What changed (high level):
- New controller: controller/promotion/shadow_fusion_controller.go — fusion logic evaluates grouped shadow traces, computes a fused fidelity score across latency/cls/semantic drift metrics, and coordinates staged promotions.
- Rollback mitigator: server/rollback/mitigator.go + docs/runbooks/rollback-mitigator.md — builds dry-run rollback plans, snapshots model pins, and verifies replays in a sandboxed dry-run.
- Telemetry federation: telemetry/federation_collector.go — aggregates short-lived session histograms from shadow lanes to compute cohort-level fidelity without sampling bias.
- Small API: api/rollouts/v1/promote.proto + api/rollouts/handlers.go — expose a PromotePreview endpoint that returns a promotion score and a precomputed rollback plan id.
- E2E tests: tests/e2e/shadow_fusion.spec.ts + tests/unit/mitigator_test.go — cover fusion scoring, smoke promotion, and rollback dry-runs.

Design notes and safety gates:
- Fusion scoring is ensemble-based: a weighted median of normalized metrics (p95 latency delta, token-level perplexity proxy, semantic embedding cosine drift, error-rate uplift). We enforce a quorum (>=3 of 4 metric bands must be within configured thresholds) to avoid single-metric flapping.
- Promotion is staged: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50%. Each stage requires the fusion score to remain above the acceptance threshold for a stability window (configurable; default 10 minutes).
- Rollback mitigator creates an immutable rollback plan (snapshot of model version, routing table, KV-cache checkpoint) and runs a dry-run replay in a sandbox. The mitigator scores the rollback plan for safety and time-to-recover and attaches cost/time estimates to the PromotePreview response.

Example usage (PromotePreview):
- Client: POST /v1/rollouts/preview with target model and cohort selector
- Response: {"fusion_score": 0.92, "quorum": true, "rollback_plan_id": "rb-20260218-89af", "estimated_recovery_minutes": 3}

Small code snippet (fusion heuristic):
- normalized := map[string]float64{"latency": norm(p95Delta), "perplexity": norm(ppDelta), "embed": norm(1-cosineDrift), "errors": norm(errorUplift)}
- scores := values(normalized)
- fusionScore := median(scores) * quorumFactor(scores, thresholds)

Testing and CI: All unit tests and e2e runs pass in the CI job. Added targeted flake-resistant tests that exercise time windows using the testclock in controller/testutil. CI job summary: build: pass, unit: pass, integration: pass, e2e: pass.

Rollout plan and observability:
- Default rollout policy uses the new fusion controller. Operators can opt out by setting annotation rollout.strategy=legacy.
- Console: new per-rollout panel (Console -> Rollouts) shows fusion score, contributing metrics, rollback plan id, and sandbox replay outcome.
- Alerts: two rule templates added: rollout-fusion-drop and rollback-mitigator-failure.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- No breaking API changes; new PromotePreview endpoint is additive.
- Existing rollouts remain on the stable promotion controller until annotated.

Risk and mitigation:
- Risk: improper weighting could bias promotions. Mitigation: default weights conservative, staged increases small, and PromotePreview surfaces the plan for manual review.
- Risk: rollback dry-run could be slow for very large models. Mitigation: mitigator supports fast-path lightweight snapshots and prioritizes KV/cache-less reverts when full snapshot is costly.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation of fusion controller and rollback mitigator
- [x] Unit tests for fusion heuristics and mitigator planner
- [x] E2E shadow->canary smoke tests
- [x] Console panel + runbook entry
- [x] Linear tasks updated (ENG-2345, ENG-9876)

Commits summary: see commit list.

Related work: builds on prior shadow-promote efforts but differs by producing an explicit, runnable rollback plan and scoring promotions with a fused, quorum-driven metric. Links: Linear/ENG-2345, Runbook link: docs/runbooks/rollback-mitigator.md

Notes for reviewers: focus on the fusion thresholds (controller/promotion/shadow_fusion_controller.go) and mitigator sandbox isolation (server/rollback/mitigator.go). The mitigator intentionally keeps the dry-run environment resource-limited to avoid noisy neighbour effects.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after CI green and approvals.

Introduces an adaptive shadow->canary promotion flow with an automated rollback mitigator. Adds telemetry federation for fidelity scoring and a dry-run rollback planner for faster, safer reverts.
Raj Patel (reviewer): Could the quorum requirement be relaxed for low-traffic cohorts? Concerned about overfitting to noisy embedding signals.
Maya Chen (author): We added a per-cohort override — low-traffic cohorts use a longer stability window and a lower quorum threshold; documented in the controller config. Also added a unit test for the longer window behavior.
Elena Gomez (reviewer): The mitigator's sandbox needs a hard CPU/memory cap to avoid interfering with production. Where is that enforced?
Maya Chen (author): Sandbox limiter is enforced in server/rollback/sandbox_manager.go (new file) — it's configured via rollout.sandbox.* flags. I included the default caps in docs/runbooks/rollback-mitigator.md.
Ibrahim Noor (approver): Verified e2e smoke locally with the staging cluster; fusion scores behave as expected. Approving.
payload.title: Adaptive shadow fusion with staged canary promotion and rollback mitigator

Motivation: production workloads show intermittent token-level tail spikes when many concurrent prefill requests attempt to hot-prime the KV cache at the same time. Spiky KV priming increases decode jitter and occasionally pushes requests over latency SLOs. Goal: reduce prefill burst jitter without increasing mean latency or adding heavy serialization.

What this PR does (single-string summary): introduce a staggered per-microbatch KV warmup offset, add a lightweight decode-handshake (2-token soft barrier) that enables safe interleaving of prefill and decode stages, and extend the scheduler with a small credit-based backpressure knob that prefers staggered prefill windows for latency-sensitive routes.

Design notes and rationale: the approach intentionally avoids strict serialization between prefill and decode; instead we: 1) compute a deterministic offset for each microbatch using request hash + configurable stride to scatter KV priming across a small time window (default 6-12ms) so that multiple prefill-heavy arrivals aren’t synchronized; 2) add a non-blocking handshake where the prefill stage returns an early 'ready-for-decode' token after priming critical prefixes (first 2 tokens), allowing the decode stage to start generating while the KV warmup continues in the background for long contexts; 3) expose a scheduler hint (prefill_stagger_ratio) and a credit token mechanism per route so critical low-p99 routes get preferentially staggered windows and credits avoid accidental reentrancy bursts.

Implementation highlights: changes touch the serving scheduler, runtime prefill pipeline, kernel priming logic, and observability hooks. Key new modules: scheduler/prefill_staggerer (algorithm + config), runtime/kv_warmup/offset_priming (deterministic offset generator + randomized jitter fallback), runtime/decode/handshake (soft barrier and token exchange), and metrics/runtime_prefill_jitter and metrics/scheduler_prefill_stagger_ratio.

Compatibility and safety: default behavior is conservative (staggering disabled for routes with very short sequence lengths). All knobs are runtime-configurable via the existing route config proto; safe defaults chosen after internal perf runs. Added unit and integration tests cover deterministic offset behavior and handshake timeout/fast-paths.

Benchmark summary: microbenchmarks on p4d (internal harness) show 8-18% reduction in 99th token latency for mixed prefill+decode workloads at 75% load with no regression in median latency or throughput. KV priming CPU overhead is +1.9% on average due to offset accounting; scheduler overhead is negligible (microsecond-scale).

Operational notes: added two new metrics and one debug flag (enable_prefill_staggering) available via runtime flags. Recommended rollout: enable staging with enable_prefill_staggering=false for canary, then flip on for specific low-p99 routes and monitor metrics/runtime_prefill_jitter and per-route cost.

Related: this complements earlier work on kv-prefetch strategies and prefill windowing; see ENG-3149 for rollout plan and ENG-3161 for dashboarding.

Checklist:
- [x] scheduler and runtime changes implemented
- [x] unit tests for offset generator and handshake timeout
- [x] integration tests for mixed prefill/decode flows
- [x] basic perf runs attached to PR
- [x] runtime flag and route config knobs

Diego Martinez: Can we get a quantified regression budget for median latency? Also please add an opt-out path for the tiny routes we discussed.
Lena Zhou (author): Added median latency check to the CI perf job and route-level opt-out via route_config.proto default false for sequences < 64 tokens.
Ayesha Kapoor: The deterministic offset seems fine but we saw a corner case with identical request hashes from replayed traffic. Can we add fallback randomized jitter?
Lena Zhou (author): Implemented jitter fallback (bounded < 2ms) when offset collisions are detected in a short window; added unit test to simulate collisions.
Samir Patel: Please surface the new metrics in the console dashboards before merge so SRE can monitor. Also confirm there is no unsafe blocking in hot paths.
Lena Zhou (author): Metrics are wired and dashboard PR queued (ENG-3161). Handshake is non-blocking on fast path; added microbench that asserts no syscall in critical loop.
Initial staggered offset generator and unit tests
Add decode handshake path and non-blocking token exchange
Scheduler: credit token implementation and route hint plumbing
Metrics: runtime_prefill_jitter + scheduler_prefill_stagger_ratio
Integration tests and perf harness bindings
Docs: add runtime flags and rollout notes
Introduce staggered KV warmup and a lightweight decode handshake to reduce prefill burst jitter; exposes runtime flags and metrics. Recommended staged rollout for latency-sensitive routes.

Motivation: We frequently see noisy, one-off token-cost/latency incidents that are hard to reproduce and tune alerts for. Ops needs a compact, privacy-safe snapshot that can be replayed (in a sandboxed path) to validate alert thresholds, fallback policies, and model routing behavior. This PR implements a reproducible invocation fingerprint (the 'Deja-Vu Index') and an Alert Replay Gateway to drive deterministic replays of sampled invocations through the serving stack.

What this PR adds (high level):
- a Deja-Vu Index generator that computes a stable fingerprint for an invocation using prompt-shape hash, token-phase histogram, model variant, KV-cache hit profile, and lightweight kernel-queue signature; designed to be stable across minimal tokenization/whitespace differences
- a compact Invocation Snapshot format (sanitized, pseudonymous) that stores the Deja-Vu ID, truncated prompts, token shape metrics, KV cache markers, and a replay hint bundle
- an Alert Replay Gateway service (internal only) that can accept a snapshot and execute a deterministic replay path through a dedicated canary runtime with replay-only tracing hooks
- three Grafana dashboards: DejaVu Explorer, Alert Replay Runs, and Replayed SLO Deltas
- metric and span tags: invocation.deja_vu_id, alert_replay.run_id, replay.trace_phase
- a sampled-log compactor that keeps a delimited, privacy-safe excerpt for each snapshot for human triage
- migration that registers the new metric names and adds a lightweight retention TTL for snapshots.

Why it's safe: Snapshots are sanitized: full user PII is redacted, embeddings are not stored, and prompt payloads are truncated and hashed. The replay path is constrained to dedicated canaries and does not feed outputs back into production logs or billing pipelines. Access to replay snapshots gated by RBAC and audit-logged.

Checklist:
- [x] Deja-Vu Index algorithm and unit tests
- [x] Snapshot format + encoder/decoder
- [x] Replay gateway prototype + integration tests (uses canary runtime)
- [x] Dashboards and example alert-run (example run attached)
- [x] CI: unit/integration/e2e (replay e2e runs in sandbox)
- [x] Docs: docs/observability/deja-vu-replay.md
- [x] Migration: metrics registration and retention TTL

Notes & follow-ups:
- Performance: index computation adds ~120us median overhead per invocation in the fast path; we sample 0.5% by default. We can move to async sidecar if overhead becomes problematic.
- This PR intentionally avoids storing full prompt text; product requested hashed + truncated payloads to allow meaningful triage without exposing PII.
- Next steps: add a replay-run A/B harness to automatically attempt replays for high-confidence SLO regressions and surface suggested alert threshold edits.
Jonas Patel: Nice approach. Two asks: (1) can we add a deterministic seed in the index so replays are bit-identical where possible? (2) please confirm storage TTL and deletion path for snapshots so compliance can sign off.
Maya Chen: Reply to Jonas - added deterministic seed (falls back to zero if unavailable) and added migration + admin API to purge snapshots older than TTL. Updated docs with retention and RBAC notes.
Evelyn Ruiz: Integration tests look good. Found one flaky test on macOS CI (test_replay_gateway::test_replay_path) — looks like a timing assert. Suggest switching to event-driven sync in test harness.
Maya Chen: Fixed test to wait on replay-run-complete event instead of a fixed sleep. Re-ran CI; e2e passed.
Marco Alvarez: Approving from SRE after verifying canary isolation and no billing side-effects. Small nit: add a metrics tag for 'replay.sandbox' true/false.
payload.title: Introduce invocation deja-vu index and alert replay gateway

Motivation: During the 2026-02-22 regional surge incident we observed cascading retry amplification and persistent p99 SLO breaches in the eu-west cluster. Existing circuit breakers reacted too late and per-node shedders were oscillating, causing tenant starvation and repeated requeues. This PR introduces an anticipatory, quota-aware load trimming policy that forecasts short-term queue pressure and issues soft drops for low-priority requests before queues saturate. It also adds a lightweight gossip protocol between edge proxies to share short-term queue forecasts so neighboring nodes avoid synchronized shedding spikes.

Design summary: single continuous change set implementing a new policy object (AnticipatoryLoadTrimmer) in the runtime proxy. Key characteristics: forecast window = 500-1500ms, priority-weighted trimming using tenant SLA weight, hysteresis to prevent flip-flops, and cross-proxy smoothing via a small gossip payload (3 keys: queue_estimate, last_updated, node_weight). The algorithm prefers local in-memory KV cache hits and only trims requests whose configured importance <= LOW. On loss of gossip messages the policy falls back to the existing local token-bucket shedder and sticky-circuit behavior.

Feature gating and rollout: behind feature-flag runtime.enable_anticipatory_trimmer (default false). Small canary enabled for region eu-west-1 and for Dedicated customers only. Added remote-config flag to allow per-tenant opt-out. The rollout plan: experimental in perf-canary -> 24h smoke -> broad canary -> full enable if SLO delta < 0.5%.

Implementation details: - New class: proxy/shedder/anticipatory_trimmer.go - Gossip component: proxy/gossip/queue_forecast.go (UDP-based, bounded small payload, integrated into existing heartbeat loop) - Config: added to runtime/config.yaml and runtime/feature_flags.go - Metrics: anticipatory_trim{result=(dropped|soft_pass|bypassed)}, queue_forecast_estimate_ms, gossip_messages_received_total - Tests: unit tests for forecast window and hysteresis, integration test in perf-canary harness that replays production traces with injected surge.

Performance and safety: Load tests against perf-canary traces show p99 tail latency reduced by ~18% under surge scenarios vs baseline; global request drop rate increased by 0.9% skewed to LOW-priority requests only. No measurable change to average token cost. The gossip payload adds ~120B per heartbeat per proxy (negligible). Hysteresis and backoff timers avoid re-open storms.

Files changed (high level): - proxy/shedder/anticipatory_trimmer.go (new) - proxy/gossip/queue_forecast.go (new) - runtime/config.yaml (tweak) - runtime/feature_flags.go (tweak) - tests/interval_surge_simulation_test.go (new) - perf-canary/job-configs/anticipatory-trimmer.json (new) - docs/operations/anticipatory-trimmer.md (new)

Commits: ["a1b3c4c add anticipatory trimmer skeleton and interfaces", "b2d4f8e implement gossip forecast sharing + unit tests", "c3e7a1f hotpatch: tune hysteresis/backoff timers and update docs"]

Review conversation: Reviewer Hannah Lee: "Nice approach, reduces coupling to the global SLO enforcer. Please add an e2e that verifies no tenant gets starved when gossip is partitioned." Author reply (Priya): "Added perf-canary trace that simulates partial partition in tests/interval_surge_simulation_test.go and verified per-tenant fairness metrics remain within bounds. See second commit." Reviewer Diego Morales: "One concern: UDP gossip may be dropped in noisy networks. Can we detect persistent misses and fall back faster?" Author: "Yes — added detection logic: if gossip_messages_received < 3 over 10s we halve the forecast window and rely on local token-bucket for trimming. Documented fallback in operations doc." Reviewer Samir Kothari: "CI flaked on integration test initially (timeout). Reran and passed. Approving now."

CI: Initial CI run failed on a flaky integration test (timing) - workaround: increased test timeout and added deterministic clock in tests. Reran CI: all checks passed. Jobs: go-build (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-perf (pass), lint (pass), docs-check (pass).

Rollout notes and mitigation: - Feature flag controls canary scope; recommend 6h small canary with close monitoring of anticipatory_trim.dropped.by_priority and p99 latency. - If observed unfairness: set runtime.enable_anticipatory_trimmer=false and reboot proxies in canary set. - On partial-deploy issues the sticky-circuit (existing) provides a safe fallback path.

Related: Linear ENG-2039 (investigation), ENG-2042 (implementation); SUP-4182 recorded customer-facing impact.

This PR is a hotpatch introduced to reduce incident blast radius during short surges and to stabilize SLOs while longer-term capacity and routing adjustments are coordinated.
Hannah Lee: please add e2e for gossip partitioning; otherwise looks good.
Priya Nambiar: added partitioned perf-canary test and tuned hysteresis timers (second commit).
Diego Morales: +1 after fallback-on-gossip-miss added.
Samir Kothari: CI flake fixed, approving.
Release lead (Marta Ivanov): merging as squash hotpatch per incident playbook.
Hotpatch: add anticipatory load trimming with cross-proxy gossip to reduce cascading retries and stabilize SLOs during short regional surges.
payload.title: Anticipatory load trimmer with gossip-based regional backpressure (hotpatch)

Summary: Implements the new Console page for Redwood Optimize → Optimization suggestions (beta). This is the list + details experience for batching/caching suggestions only. The UI is gated behind a feature flag (optimize_suggestions_beta) and a read permission (optimize:suggestions:read). The page presents estimated savings ($/day + %) and estimated latency deltas (p50/p95), plus a Low/Medium/High risk badge with explanatory copy. Includes list/table layout with filtering/sorting, pagination, a details drawer with assumptions + guardrails, and complete empty/error states. Context: This is the frontend half of the beta Suggestions experience described in PM-842 / ENG-19358. API contract work landed separately (see pr-21934). Risk badge component is shared and comes from pr-21983. Telemetry events are intentionally limited here to basic page-view instrumentation; full funnel events are tracked in pr-22011. Feature gating: (1) Feature flag: optimize_suggestions_beta (org-scoped, remote-config driven). (2) Permission: optimize:suggestions:read (RBAC; UI hides nav + blocks route when missing). When the feature flag is off: the navigation entry is hidden and direct-route access redirects to /optimize (with a toast). When permission is missing: render AccessDenied with a link to internal docs for requesting access (kept behind isInternal guard in prod builds). UX overview: Entry point is Optimize → Suggestions. Default view is a table grouped by Route + Model (not hard-grouped, but those are primary columns). Columns: Suggestion (type: batching/caching), Estimated savings (primary metric, sortable), Risk (badge + tooltip), Confidence (chip), Updated (stale indicator + timestamp). Filters: Model, Route, Region, Suggestion type (Batching / Caching), Risk (Low/Med/High), and a toggle to show dismissed (beta-only; hidden unless ?debugSuggestions=1). Sorting: savings desc (default), savings asc, risk, updated_at. Pagination: server-driven cursor pagination; table supports page size 25/50 (default 25). Details drawer: Clicking a row opens a right-side drawer with: (a) What we recommend (human-readable title), (b) Why we recommend this (top signals, e.g., concurrency, cache hit rate, sequence length distribution), (c) Estimated impact (savings + latency delta with confidence band), (d) Risk & guardrails (explain that risk is performance/reliability risk; not security risk), (e) How to enable (deep links to batching/caching config pages + docs). Drawer also surfaces suggestion_id and stale_as_of timestamp for support/debug. Empty + error states: Added 4 distinct empty states per design spec: No suggestions yet (but telemetry present) → show onboarding text + links; Insufficient telemetry → show requirements (min window + signals) and link to telemetry setup; Feature not enabled → show request access CTA (beta); API error → show retry and status text, plus a small disclosure for request id. Also added skeleton loading for initial fetch and drawer fetch. Implementation details: New route: /optimize/suggestions (lazy-loaded bundle). Data layer: console-web uses the typed REST client; added OptimizeSuggestionsClient with getSuggestions({ filters, sort, cursor, limit }). Normalizes response into table rows; uses suggestion_id as the stable key. State management: useUrlState hook for filters/sort/pagination so the view is shareable and persists across reloads; drawer open state uses suggestion_id in querystring (?sid=...). Accessibility: Table supports keyboard row focus + Enter to open drawer; drawer traps focus; risk badge tooltips are keyboard accessible. Verified color contrast in dark mode for risk badges (relies on shared component from pr-21983). Minimal illustrative snippet (not a full diff): Added route registration: routes.ts: registerRoute({ path: '/optimize/suggestions', featureFlag: 'optimize_suggestions_beta', permission: 'optimize:suggestions:read', component: lazy(() => import('./pages/OptimizeSuggestions')) }); Added URL state for filters: const { state, setState } = useUrlState(schema, { sort: 'savings_desc', limit: 25 }); Testing: Unit tests for filter serialization + URL state roundtrip (8 cases) and for rendering each empty state given mocked API responses. Added mocked API fixtures for: insufficient_telemetry, no_suggestions, permission_denied, stale_suggestions. Basic Playwright smoke (existing suite) updated to ensure the route doesn’t register when flag is off (guards nav item). Manual QA steps (recommended): 1) With flag OFF: confirm nav item hidden; direct hit /optimize/suggestions redirects. 2) With flag ON + no permission: AccessDenied renders; no API call. 3) With flag ON + permission: table loads; filters update URL; pagination works. 4) Open drawer: verify deep links, stale timestamp, tooltip copy. 5) Simulate API 500: error state shows retry and request id. Screenshots: Attached in PR: (a) Default list view with filters, (b) Details drawer with assumptions + guardrails section, (c) Insufficient telemetry empty state, (d) Access denied state. Notes / follow-ups: - This PR intentionally does not emit expand/dismiss/apply funnel events; see pr-22011 / ENG-19402. - Copy for risk tooltips is pulled from shared strings; final review on wording tracked in DES-640. - Dismiss action is not implemented in beta UI (non-goal); a debug-only toggle exists for internal testing of dismissed rows but is not visible to customers. - Need to verify RBAC permission name matches backend enforcement once pr-22026 lands in prod (currently behind the same beta flag). Release/rollout: Safe to merge behind flag. Default flag state remains OFF in all envs except staging. Beta enablement via internal runbook (how-to-enable-suggestions-beta-feature-flag). Review notes: Dylan requested we avoid fetching suggestions when AccessDenied is known; addressed by moving permission check earlier in route guard. Tessa requested clearer distinction that “risk” is performance/reliability, not security; updated tooltip + drawer header accordingly. Chloe requested we handle cursor pagination consistently when filters change; fixed by resetting cursor on filter/sort changes. CI: web-console lint/test, typecheck, and Playwright smoke passed. One initial flake in Playwright (timing on drawer animation) was fixed by waiting on drawer heading instead of CSS transition end. Merge: Squash merged to main.
Console: Added Optimization suggestions (beta) page (feature-flagged) with savings/latency estimates, risk badges, filters/sorting, and a details drawer for batching/caching recommendations.

payload.body:
Motivation: customers integrating structured output (json-schema) want early, actionable feedback when schema mismatches occur in streaming responses but do not want hard failures by default. This PR implements a lightweight "lazy schema probe" that runs a shallow validation on the first N tokens or first structural boundary, emits explainable hint events into the stream and logs, and only triggers a rollback+hard-failure path if the probe detects irrecoverable mismatches and service config requires strict enforcement. Changes: 1) runtime/pkg/schema_probe: new probe implementation that does minimal token/shape checks and returns a list of human-friendly hints (e.g., 'missing field "user_id"', 'expected array but got string at path /items') instead of raw validator dumps; 2) streaming runtime: attach probe to stream start and create check-pointing token (rollback_token) that allows rewinding to pre-probe state if a subsequent hard validation fails; 3) API: response_format negotiation now accepts 'json_schema:soft' and 'json_schema:strict' and emits hint events via the existing stream event channel so OpenAI-compatible clients get hints as structured events; 4) openai adapter: map legacy function_call and toolcall parse errors into schema-hint events when possible to improve backwards compatibility; 5) telemetry: new metrics probe_latency_ms, schema_hint_count, schema_failure_clarity (labels: missing_field,type_mismatch,coercion_needed) and tagging for probe sensitivity setting; 6) SDK updates (python): convenience helper to surface hint events and recommended prompt edits; 7) Docs and tests. Compatibility and safety: default behavior for hosted API is conservative: lazy probe is behind the feature flag redwood.feature.lazy_schema_probe and default off for older tenants; 'json_schema' without explicit modifier keeps existing behavior. Rollout plan: feature flag gated rollout to first 5% of traffic, perf monitor for probe_latency and request p50/p95; if 3 consecutive regressions in latency or error-rate occur, auto-disable for that tenant. Testing: unit tests cover probe heuristics for common schema shapes, integration tests simulate partial streams and ensure rollback token rewinds and produces consistent final payloads, fuzz tests for malformed model outputs included. Observability: console dashboard (telemetry/schema-probe) added to show hint distributions and top failing paths. Implementation notes: probe is intentionally approximate (heuristic-first) to avoid CPU blowup; it runs with a short soft timeout and uses cached compiled schema footprints to speed up repeated validations. Migration notes: customers who need strict enforcement should explicitly request 'json_schema:strict' or enable the Strict Schema Runtime policy. Related: builds on work in ENG-1121 (stream checkpoints) and complements the schema clarity metrics introduced in ENG-1203. Checklist: - [x] Implement probe + rollback token - [x] OpenAI adapter mapping - [x] SDK helper and docs - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Telemetry registration - [x] Feature flag and rollout config
Adds shallow preflight schema probe with explainable hints, rollback token for stream repair on hard failures, OpenAI adapter mappings for schema-related function_call errors, telemetry and SDK helpers, plus tests and docs.
Added a lightweight lazy schema probe that emits explainable hints without aborting streams; introduced a soft_strict mode for warnings-only schema enforcement; implemented stream rollback token and resume behavior for hard failures; extended OpenAI-compat layer to surface schema hints for function_call errors; telemetry to surface probe latency and failure clarity metrics.
Diego Morales: How much CPU/latency does the probe add in p95 workloads? We should gate this aggressively and ensure cached compiled schema footprints are used.
Ava Chen: Diego, probe is bounded by a 30ms soft timeout by default and uses a per-tenant LRU cache for compiled schema snippets. See telemetry/probe_latency metrics added in this PR.
Priya Kapoor: Suggest clearer metric names and additional tag for 'probe_sensitivity' so we can correlate failures to sensitivity levels.
Ava Chen: Updated metric names to include probe_sensitivity label and added dashboard tile; also added tests for sensitivity=high/low paths.
Ethan Zhang: Edge case: if probe emits hints and the model self-corrects mid-stream, we must not surface a downstream hard failure or duplicate hints. Also ensure rollback token plays well with KV cache eviction.
Ava Chen: Added integration test 'test_probe_self_corrects' and fixed checkpoint_manager to mark token idempotent for resume in presence of KV cache eviction.

payload.body:
Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and reactive spill storms continue to surface at tail latency under mixed batch/streaming workloads. Small-object churn (tens to low hundreds of bytes) creates many tiny free fragments that the allocator cannot efficiently reuse, causing spill bursts and I/O pressure. This PR introduces an 'adaptive reservoir' layer and a shear-driven compaction pass plus a prioritized spill-tier policy to smooth memory reclamation and reduce tail latency.
a1f4c2b: reservoir: add adaptive reservoir metadata and life-window tracking
d4e9f7a: compaction: implement shear-driven compaction pass and async workqueue
b7c8d33: spill: add prioritized spill tiers and backpressure hooks to scheduler
e2b4a11: tests: unit + integration tests for reservoir heuristics and spill orchestration
f34d9c5: docs: add design note + rollout instructions
pkg/kv/allocator/reservoir.go (new) — core reservoir structure, lifecycle heuristics and statistics hooks
pkg/kv/allocator/shear_compactor.go — incremental compaction algorithm; lock-free compaction seeds and worker coordination
pkg/kv/evictor/spill_tiers.go — prioritized spill tiers, spill scoring, integration with tenant quotas
pkg/kv/scheduler/orchestrator.go — eviction orchestration API and scheduler backpressure signals
cmd/bench/kv_simulator/main.go — new bench harness for mixed batch/streaming churn workloads
internal/docs/kv-reservoir.md — design note and rollout guidance
pkg/kv/allocator/reservoir_test.go — unit tests covering fragmentation thresholds
pkg/kv/integration/reservoir_e2e_test.go — e2e test exercising spill tiering under load
Elena García (reviewer): Can you clarify how the reservoir interacts with existing slab reservations? Is this orthogonal to the slab allocator or does it replace any path?
Author (Rajiv): The reservoir is an overlay that sits above slabs: it tracks small-fragment pools and leases reclaim windows to the compactor. It does not change the slab layout; it simply surfaces candidate segments for coalescing without blocking fast-path allocations.
Marcus Lee (reviewer): The compaction worker looks potentially heavy for multi-tenant hosts — what are the CPU and lock guarantees?
Author: Compaction is sheared into many tiny CPU-friendly tasks limited by a per-host token bucket and tenant fairness slots. There are explicit CPU caps and a low-priority scheduling class so it won't compete with inference kernels. Added metrics for compaction CPU and throttled_count.
Priya Kapoor (reviewer): I saw a flaky unit failing in CI once; can you add a retry or stabilize the timing in that test?
Author: Replaced time.Sleep-based assertion with explicit event notification; triggered a CI re-run and the suite passed.
Local cluster run (8x A100 simulated) using kv_simulator with mixed 70/30 streaming/batched requests: 95th tail token latency reduced by 18% compared to baseline; median latency unchanged; spill frequency (spike events >3x baseline) reduced from 7/day to 1/day in a 24h simulation. Memory utilization smoothed: peak memory variance decreased 27%.
Start on dedicated staging fleet with reservoir.enabled=false, enable in canary mode for 2% traffic for 48h, monitor compaction_cpu, spill_count, tail_latency. If metrics stable, ramp to 25% over 24h then to 100% after 72h. Fail-open: compaction can be disabled dynamically and spill_tiers fall back to prior LRU policy.
Add adaptive reservoir overlay to reduce small-fragment churn and smooth memory usage.
Introduce shear-driven incremental compactor to coalesce fragments with bounded CPU budget.
Add prioritized spill tiers to reduce I/O spike frequency and improve tail latency under mixed workloads.
Runtime knobs: reservoir.enabled (bool), reservoir.compaction_cpu_limit (percent), spill.tier_weights (map).
This PR focuses on stabilization and observability. Follow-ups planned: 1) integrate kernel prefetch hints into compactor to reduce page faults during coalescing, 2) extend reservoir heuristics to tenant-specific coldspot detection, 3) add amber alerting for compaction throttling.
payload.title: Adaptive KV reservoir: shear-driven compaction and prioritized spill tiers

payload.body:
Summary:
Introduce an 'Adaptive Degraded Mode Operator' (ADMO) that centralizes runtime decisions for graceful degradation during high-pressure events, plus a lightweight 'Priority Triage Probe' that classifies burst traffic patterns and applies fast-path admission controls. This addresses recurring incidents where noisy telemetry + regional spikes caused wholesale circuit flips and unnecessary regional failovers. The change is scoped to runtime admission, telemetry sanitization, and operator-facing rollout hooks.

Motivation & Context:
- Several incidents over the last quarter (see ENG-4421) showed cascading circuit resets during short, tenant-localized bursts.
- Current heuristics conflate metric noise with genuine SLO pressure; regional failovers sometimes trigger before KV-preserve drains complete, losing hot cache and amplifying latency.
- We need a compact, explainable decision layer that: (1) deduplicates noisy telemetry, (2) fast-classifies traffic type (burst vs sustained, high-cost vs low-cost), and (3) applies a prioritized admission policy that preserves latency SLOs where possible while shedding non-essential load.

What this PR does (single-line checklist):
- Adds ADMO: a runtime operator that consumes existing health/telemetry streams and produces ranked actions (trim, soft-deny, defer, escalate).
- Adds Priority Triage Probe: an inline probe (O(100us) path) that tags inflight requests by cost profile and source cohort for fast admission rules.
- Introduces a Telemetry Sanitizer filter to smooth out high-frequency spikes from noisy clients.
- Adds a safe fallback: if ADMO becomes unreachable, the system reverts to the current static shedder config.
- Exposes operator-facing flags in ops/recipes for staggered rollout and automatic canary unfreeze.

Implementation notes / commits summary:
- commit 1: runtime/operator: new admode package + decision engine (rule interpreter + simple exp backoff scheduler).
- commit 2: serving/probe: priority triage probe integrated into request admission path; small inline fast-path hooks.
- commit 3: telemetry/filter: sanitization pipeline with configurable windowing and percentile-trimming.
- commit 4: ops/recipes: deployment manifests and rollout script to enable ADMO behind a feature flag with a staggered 10% -> 50% -> 100% rollout.
- commit 5: tests: unit tests for rule interpreter, integration test that validates fallback behaviour, and a load test script to simulate tenant-localized bursts.

Files changed (high level):
- src/serving/admission/admode.go (+admode_test.go) -- core operator and decision loop.
- src/serving/admission/probe.go (+probe_test.go) -- Priority Triage Probe, small deterministic classifier.
- pkg/telemetry/sanitizer.go -- smoothing filter and config validation.
- ops/recipes/admode-rollout.yaml -- k8s job + canary traffic split.
- infra/monitoring/dashboards/admode-overview.json -- new dashboard panels for operator decisions and triage distribution.
- tests/load/burst-simulator.go -- deterministic burst patterns used for integration.
- docs/observability/admode.md -- operator playbook and debugging steps.
- ci/flakeguard.yaml -- add test flake guard for burst-simulator to reduce CI noise.

Behavioral guarantees and safety: (important)
- No breaking changes to API surface. ADMO runs behind a feature flag by default (off).
- When enabled, ADMO makes only non-destructive decisions (soft-deny / priority tag). The system will never evict tenant state; full evictions remain operator-controlled.
- If ADMO fails health checks, an automatic reversion to the static shedder occurs within 10s.

Review notes and decisions:
- Performance: The probe path is <150ns additional median overhead in microbenchmarks; see tests/load results included. We intentionally keep the probe classifier deterministic and tiny to avoid GC pressure.
- Explainability: ADMO decision logs include a decision-context payload (cohort, recent-latency-p95, kv-pressure-ratio) to help on-call triage.
- Telemetry: The sanitizer defaults are conservative (window=30s, trim=95th->80th mapping) but can be tuned via config.

Review conversation (excerpted, chronological):
- Evan Zhao (reviewer): "Looks good overall; need stronger invariants around 'admode unreachable' fallback to avoid split-brain where half the cluster thinks ADMO is on and half off."
- Author (Maya): "Added a liveness fence and a quorum check in admode.go; ADMO toggles only after a 3/5 coordinator quorum window. See admode.go:Start() changes."
- Evan: "Please include a small integration test showing fallback behavior and a CI job to exercise it."
- Author: "Added tests/load/burst-fallback_test.go and wired it into ci/flakeguard. Reran CI."
- Priya Menon (reviewer): "Telemetry sanitization looks reasonable, but we should surface the sanitizer's applied-trim metric to dashboards."
- Author: "Added applied_trim gauge and dashboard panel in infra/monitoring/dashboards/admode-overview.json."
- Liam O'Connor (approver): "Approving after seeing canary rollout recipe and the integration tests pass."

CI and validation history: 
- Initial CI run (unit + lint): failed on go vet in admode.go (unsafe nil-check). Fixed in commit 2.
- Second CI run (unit + integration): flake in burst-simulator; added flakeguard and made test deterministic.
- Final CI run: all checks passed (unit, integration, e2e-canary on staging).

Manual testing and incident rehearsal: 
- Ran staged canary (10% of traffic) for 24 hours against staging cluster while generating tenant-localized bursts. Observed: ADMO applied priority trims to identified low-cost cohorts, preserved latency for VIP tenants, and avoided circuit flips during 3 simulated overloads. KV-preserve drains completed in >95% of evict-invocations vs 70% baseline.

Rollout and rollback plan: 
- Enable behind feature flag: admode.enabled=false by default.
- Rollout path: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 days with automated metric checks: regional-p95, canary-error-rate, kv-drain-success-rate.
- Automatic pause: if canary error-rate increases > 0.5% absolute or kv-drain-success-rate drops below 85%, the rollout pauses and a rollback job runs to disable ADMO.

Release notes (for changelog):
- "Add experimental Adaptive Degraded Mode Operator for SLO-aware admission control and a Priority Triage Probe to classify burst traffic. Improves regional stability during tenant-localized spikes; opt-in behind a feature flag. Includes observability and rollout recipes."

Follow-ups (not included in this PR):
- Policy DSL for ADMO rules (ENG-4502).
- SDK hooks so customers can surface priority tags to downstream telemetry.

Merge details:
- Merge method: squash and merge.
- Commit message condensed to: "admission: adaptive degraded-mode operator + priority triage probe; telemetry sanitizer; ops rollout"

Contact / On-call:
- Primary owner: Maya Patel (runtime team).
- Slack channel: #runtime-admode.

Notes for on-call: when investigating ADMO-induced soft-deny events, start with the admode-overview dashboard and confirm quorum-health. If quorum-health is stale, the system will revert to static shedder; escalate to runtime if reversion does not happen within 20s.

End of PR description.
payload.title: Introduce adaptive degraded-mode operator and priority traffic triage probe

payload.body:
Motivation: our GitHub Actions setup had grown organic cruft: duplicated workflow YAML, inconsistent caching, and ad-hoc release steps across repos. This PR consolidates reusable workflows, standardizes caches and test matrix behavior, and enables deterministic release automation using release-please. The change set is focused on developer-experience and repo hygiene (no product logic changes).

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds .github/workflows/reusable-ci.yml and reusable-lint.yml to centralize build/test/lint behavior.
- Replaces three repo-specific workflows (ci-python.yml, ci-node.yml, ci-go.yml) with small entrypoint workflows that invoke the reusable workflows.
- Introduces a common action cache policy (key includes os, runner, node-version/python-version, and lockfile hash) to reduce cold-cache flakiness.
- Adds a test sharding strategy using matrix.include shards for the python test suite and parallelization hints for pytest-xdist when applicable.
- Migrates dependency automation from dependabot to a unified renovate configuration with onboarding for major monorepo rules (lockfile maintenance, group upgrades for devDeps).
- Bumps key CI dev deps: actions/checkout@v4, actions/cache@v4, pnpm/setup-pnpm@v2, actions/setup-node@v4 and setup-python@v4.
- Adds a release-please config and a GitHub workflow (release-please.yml) to create draft releases and CHANGELOG entries using conventional commits. This will replace manual release steps and the previous ad-hoc scripts in scripts/release/*.
- Removes legacy shell-based lint/test wrappers in scripts/ci/ in favor of reusable composite actions under .github/actions/ci-helpers/.
- Small refactors to tests to make them hermetic: pinning ephemeral network calls in two integration tests and reducing reliance on system time via freezegun in python tests.

Checklist (manual steps validated):
- [x] Cross-repo reusable workflow shape validated locally with act and against a staging branch in a sandbox repo.
- [x] Cache keys stress-tested (cold/warm) across linux/macos runners.
- [x] release-please created draft release during a dry-run using --dry-run.
- [x] Dependabot->Renovate migration: tested PR creation on a small sample group repository.
- [x] Flaky tests observed in previous builds were stabilized (see review comments).

How to review: the core is the reusable workflows and the release config; I recommend reviewing the YAML files first (.github/workflows and .github/actions), then the scripts/ci removal. Test-specific changes are intentionally small and annotated inline.

Rollout plan: merge to main will flip on the reusable workflows by renaming the old workflows to .disabled (kept for a week for quick rollback). After two successful main runs we will delete the .disabled files and mark this PR as fully applied. Release automation will be enabled in day-1 but set to create draft releases only (no auto-publish) until we validate changelog generation for 2 release cycles.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: subtle differences in runner env captured by old per-repo workflows. Mitigation: included explicit runner labels and expanded matrix combinations in reusable workflow; staged dry runs were executed.
- Risk: renovate onboarding churn. Mitigation: initial schedule is weekly and grouping policy limits PR noise for devDeps.

Related work items: ENG-4021, ENG-4278, OPS-189.

Notes: this PR intentionally keeps functional changes out of scope; any follow-up feature changes should be in separate PRs.
Ravi: please add a short note on the cache key format so we can debug future cache misses (addressed)
Ellen: can we keep a fallback to the old release script for one release cycle? (we keep it disabled for now, added docs)
Mateo: nginx integration tests are flaky on macOS runners — added a pinned fixture and re-ran matrix (green)
CI bot: nightly lint step failed on first run due to older node version, fixed by bumping setup-node in reusable workflow
Consolidated CI workflows; added deterministic release automation (release-please); bumped CI action versions and migrated dependency automation to renovate. No product changes. Follow-up: delete .disabled legacy workflows after 1 week of successful runs.

payload.body:
Motivation: We observed two classes of intermittent regressions in CUDA graph capture/replay on production traffic: (1) replays running with kernels chosen for a different shape/sequence regime after autoscaling or dynamic batching, and (2) cold KV cache misses during replay warmup that cause latency spikes and token-accounting regressions. This PR introduces a deterministic replay coordinator plus an explicit probing warmup phase that runs short, bounded probe traces to classify the current execution regime and prepopulate KV cache before allowing full golden-path replay. The design goals were: deterministic behavior across restarts, minimal added tail latency for the probe, and safe rollback to the legacy fallback behavior when probes detect incompatibility.

Summary of changes (single-string): Added a ReplayCoordinator component that sequences: (a) probe generation and execution on a pinned worker, (b) deterministic kernel mapping selection recorded with a small capture manifest, and (c) KV-cache prepopulation hooks that run side-effect-less prefix traces. Introduced a lightweight probe-trace generator that synthesizes 3 short traces representative of common sequence length distributions derived from recent request histograms. New metrics and tracing: replay_probe.duration_ms, replay_probe.outcome, replay_coordinator.state, cudagraph.capture_manifest (hash), and kvcache.prefill_hits. Added end-to-end integration tests that run a deterministic simulated traffic harness to validate replay idempotency and fallback paths. Added a regression test that replays a captured session across an artificial kernel mapping change to ensure the coordinator triggers an immediate safe-fallback.

Commits summary: ["feat(replay): add ReplayCoordinator and probe runner (M. Chen)", "perf(cudagraph): record deterministic kernel mapping manifest and checksum (A. Patel)", "tests(replay): add simulated traffic harness and regression tests (N. Rivera)", "fix(replay): tighten probe timeout & fallback race fix (M. Chen)"]

Files changed (high level): ["runtime/replay/coordinator.cpp", "runtime/replay/probe_runner.cpp", "runtime/replay/capture_manifest.h", "runtime/kv_cache/prefill.cc", "runtime/scheduler/pinned_worker.cc", "tests/integration/replay_probe_harness.cc", "docs/observability/replay_metrics.md", "ci/test_data/replay_samples/*"]

Detailed notes on implementation: The ReplayCoordinator lives inside the serving runtime's replay path and participates only when cudagraphs are enabled for a model. On incoming warmup requests the coordinator first checks for a recent capture_manifest match: if present and checksum matches, we skip probing. Otherwise coordinator schedules up to three probe traces onto a pinned worker (fixed GPU stream) using a short, deterministic schedule (no wall-clock jitter). Probe traces are small prefix inputs that exercise the model's typical branching (long/short token counts) while avoiding external side effects (no writeback to stateful stores). The probe runner records kernel mapping fingerprints: kernel ids + launch config serialized into the capture_manifest. If all probes succeed within configured tight timeouts and kernel fingerprints match expectations, the coordinator invokes the cudagraph capture flow and pre-populates the KV cache by replaying the same probes into the cache warmup path. If a probe fails or mapping mismatch is observed, the coordinator marks the session as INCOMPATIBLE and routes live traffic to fallback path (legacy per-token execution) and emits replay_probe.outcome=failed. To minimize risk, we bound probe work to a single GPU worker and limit retries per minute by default.

Observability and CI: New metrics implemented with tagging by model_id and region. Added a dashboard tile showing probe success rate and average prefill_hits. Unit + integration CI initially flagged a flaky test "ReplayProbeHarness.TimeoutRace" on the first run; I tightened the probe timeout, added an epoch-based probe seed (to remove timer-jitter dependence) and the CI suite passed on re-run. The full CI matrix on main (linux-gcc-14, cuda-13.3) passed; smoke tests on a pinned small GPU in CI were used to avoid noise from shared GPU pools.

Backward-compat & safety: feature gated behind runtime flag "cudagraph_replay_probe" (disabled by default for <=stable-2025.08 customers). All probe activity is non-destructive; KV prefill uses separate, ephemeral keys that are promoted only after successful probe validation. The coordinator emits an event for any fallback decision to help SRE surface regressions quickly.

Release notes: "Added an opt-in deterministic replay coordinator and probing warmup to improve cudagraph capture stability and reduce KV-cache cold-start regressions. Disabled by default; opt-in via runtime flag."

Why this is different from prior work: Prior PRs focused on heuristic warmup thresholds and relaxed shape guards. This change introduces a short, deterministic probing phase and an explicit manifest of kernel mappings to make replay decisions reproducible across restarts and after autoscaling. The manifest plus probe sequence reduces silent regressions where a replay would succeed in capture but fail at replay time due to unexpected kernel scheduling decisions.
Arjun: The manifest serialization looks good; one question: how do we prevent the manifest from staling after a kernel update? Consider adding a versioned field in serialization.
Maya: Added versioned manifest header and checksum. If checksum mismatch is detected we explicitly fall back. See capture_manifest.h (version field added).
Noelle: Found a race where probe completion could race with worker reclamation in high churn load; suggested stronger ownership token.
Maya: Applied ownership token and pinned_worker now refuses to evict in-flight probes (see pinned_worker.cc). Added a unit test for eviction-safety.
Diego: CI showed a flaky TimeoutRace; narrowed probe timeout and switched to epoch-based probe seeding to remove nondeterminism from system timers.
Approved-by: Diego Morales
payload.title: introduce probing replay coordinator and deterministic warmup phase for CUDA graph replays

payload.body:
Motivation: Investigations into SLO regressions often require high-fidelity traces and short-lived metric retention for a small set of problematic routes, which is expensive at full cardinality. This PR introduces a lightweight "pulse sampler" that can be toggled per-route (or globally) to temporarily increase telemetry fidelity for affected invocations, plus an adaptive retention controller that shortens raw-timeseries TTLs for metrics that are only needed during incident windows.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a pulse-sampler component in the serving runtime to attach a small high-priority trace + detailed token-phase metrics for sampled invocations. Pulse samples are limited by a budget and decay automatically.
- Implements an adaptive-metric-retention controller that: 1) marks metric families as "investigation" when a pulse sample occurs, 2) sets a short high-resolution retention policy (e.g., 7d@1s) for those families, and 3) automatically rolls them back after an inactivity window.
- Exposes an operator API and console flag (SLO investigator mode) to trigger manual pulses and view currently elevated retention families.
- Adds a compact dashboard (slo-investigator.json) that surfaces pulse frequency, retained metric sets, and estimated storage delta.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- The sampler captures only a constrained subset of data (callsite, token-phase timings, small KV cache deltas, top-3 logits for degen debugging) to bound per-invocation cost. It does not send full logs or request/response bodies.
- The retention controller operates at metric-family granularity to avoid explosion of retention rules per tag. We intentionally bias towards low-cardinality families (route, model, deployment).
- Budgeting: pulse budget is configurable per-tenant and enforced by a token-bucket in the control-plane; pulses beyond budget are logged and dropped.

Migration and rollout:
- Default behavior is gated behind feature flag observability.pulse_sampler=false. The console UI and API can enable investigator mode per-tenant.

payload.body:
Context: Certain open models (notably newer Qwen variants and some Llama forks) expose heterogeneous head layouts and intermittent head-wise padding which causes our existing prefetch+kernel selection logic to trigger suboptimal kernels, increased KV fragmentation, and occasional micro-stalls under continuous batching. Motivation: Reduce tail latency and token cost for mixed GQA/MQA traffic while preserving deterministic correctness. Summary: This change implements a hybrid prefetch holdback policy and a model-aware kernel-splitting pass that splits attention kernels into head-homogeneous subops at dispatch time when a heterogeneity signature is detected. The prefetch holdback introduces a small delay window to allow incoming batch items to better align head-dim distributions, avoiding premature KV prefetch that forces bloated KV slabs. Kernel-splitting ensures that when fragmentation is unavoidable we dispatch narrow, head-consistent kernels to preserve throughput without wasting compute on padded lanes. Design highlights: 1) New heterogeneity detector that samples the model metadata and early token traces (cheap checks only) to classify runs as homogeneous/heterogeneous. 2) Prefetch holdback: configurable window (default 2ms) that temporarily defers prefetch for head-misaligned batches; the window decays for low-latency SLO tenants. 3) Kernel-splitting pass: at plan generation we may emit 1..N sub-kernels, each tagged with head-mask metadata for the runtime scheduler to place on appropriate GPU lanes. 4) KV windowed-thresholds: tighten eviction and compaction thresholds for slabs affected by heterogeneous access patterns to reduce fragmentation over long-lived chat sessions. Backwards compatibility: All changes are guarded by runtime feature flags and default to conservative behavior for dedicated/private customers unless enabled. Tests & validation: - Unit tests for heterogeneity detector and splitting logic. - Integration tests with continuous batching harness covering MQA and GQA synthetic traces. - End-to-end perf runs against qwen-1.2 and llama-3-13b variants. Results are summarized below. Commits: initial prototype; detector refinements; kernel pass and scheduler hooks; perf tuning and config flags; tests and docs. Files touched include runtime scheduler, kernel planner, kv slab manager, baking harness and a short config schema addition. CI: full unit/integration/perf pipeline passed. Merge: squash and merge to main after two approvals. Motivation links: ENG-1938 notes on MQA tail-latency incidents; ENG-2045 prototype spike in bench lab.
Introduce a hybrid prefetch holdback and model-aware kernel splitting to reduce KV fragmentation and tail latency for heterogeneous-head models (Qwen/Llama). No user-facing API changes. Performance improvement for MQA/GQA workloads; rollout via runtime config flag.
Diego Martinez (review): This is a dense change — can you clarify the invariant guarantees of the split kernels vs original fused kernel?
Author (Priya Nair): The split kernels are semantically identical to the fused path; we only partition heads that are homogenous in dim and mask. I added comments and an assert in planner to ensure equivalence with a reference slow path in debug builds.
Sofia Chen (review): I saw a small perf regression on small-batch, low-latency tenants when the holdback was enabled. Can we gate by tenant SLO?
Author (Priya Nair): Yes, holdback is tenant-configurable and defaults to off for latency-sensitive tiers. Added a config override and unit test to validate gating.
Liam O'Connor (approve): Verified perf numbers and test coverage. Approving for merge.
CI Bot: All checks passed. (unit=✅, integration=✅, perf=✅)
Release Manager: Merged via squash on 2026-01-27 after approvals.

payload.body:
## Summary
Adds a small set of standardized scheduler saturation metrics to the Redwood metrics pipeline so we can reliably diagnose (and alert on) scheduler contention vs. downstream GPU/runtime issues. This is intended to support Incident Bot v2 context cards and reduce “is it capacity vs config vs deploy?” time in the first 5 minutes.

## Motivation
During recent Sev1/Sep2 incidents we had GPU utilization and request error rates, but not enough visibility into the scheduler layer itself. In particular:
- We couldn’t distinguish GPU saturation from scheduler queueing (high queue depth / high queue wait) when batching settings changed.
- We lacked a consistent backpressure indicator when admission control kicked in.
- Existing per-component gauges were inconsistent across hosted and dedicated pools and weren’t being exported with stable label sets.

## What’s in this PR
### New metrics (exported)
All metrics are emitted from the scheduler and exported via the existing OTel -> metrics pipeline.
- `redwood.scheduler.queue.depth` (gauge): current queue depth at scheduler admission.
- `redwood.scheduler.queue.wait_ms` (histogram): time spent waiting in scheduler queue prior to admission.
- `redwood.scheduler.backpressure.active` (gauge, 0/1): whether backpressure is currently asserted for a pool.
- `redwood.scheduler.backpressure.drop_total` (counter): requests dropped/failed fast due to backpressure.
- `redwood.scheduler.admission.reject_total` (counter): admission control rejects (e.g., pool overloaded / max inflight).
- `redwood.scheduler.inflight` (gauge): currently admitted inflight requests tracked by scheduler.
- `redwood.scheduler.admission.limit` (gauge): configured inflight limit (exported for context; useful when config changes).

### Labels / cardinality guardrails
To keep series count bounded and bot queries cheap:
- Allowed labels: `region`, `pool`, `service`, `route`, `deployment_mode` (hosted|dedicated|private)
- Explicitly NOT labeled by tenant/customer/model_version/request_id.
- `route` is normalized (existing route-normalizer) and capped (unknown -> `other`).

### Pipeline changes
- Extends `metrics/registry/scheduler_metrics.ts` and wiring in scheduler runtime.
- Adds `metrics/allowlist.yaml` entries for the above names.
- Adds exporter mapping for histogram buckets and renames to match existing naming conventions.

### Tests
- Unit tests for metric emission paths (queue depth gauge and admission reject counters).
- Golden snapshot test for allowlist + exporter mapping.
- Integration test verifies metrics appear in the local metrics sink with expected label set (region/pool/service only).

## Rollout / risk
- Metrics are additive.
- Backpressure gauges/counters are behind an internal runtime flag `scheduler.metrics.backpressure_export` default ON in staging, ON in prod after 24h.
- Histogram volume: `queue.wait_ms` is sampled at 1.0% by default; can be increased temporarily for incident analysis.

## Follow-ups (not included)
- Add/update dashboards and alert thresholds in observability-pack (separate PR).
- Wire these signals into Incident Bot v2 saturation card (ENG-5423 follow-up tasks in incident-bot repo).

## Validation
- Staging: verified new series present for `us-east-1` hosted pool; queue wait histogram populated under synthetic load.
- Prod canary: verified no increase in metrics pipeline ingestion errors; series count increase within budget (+~1.8k time series across all regions/pools).

Refs: ENG-5423, incident-bot diagnostics initiative; aligns with ongoing saturation signal standardization work.
Logan Wright (review): Can we confirm we are not emitting tenant_id anywhere on these? Also concerned about `route` label explosion if it includes full paths.

Nadia Rahman (author): Confirmed: scheduler emission points only pass region/pool/service/route/deployment_mode. No tenant context available in scheduler layer. For `route`, this uses the same normalizer as gateway metrics (template routes), plus a cap so anything unmapped goes to `other`. Added an integration test asserting label keys.

Allison Grant (review): Naming: we’ve been using dot-separated names in OTel, but dashboards/alerts often use Prom-style. Are we consistent with the rest of the pipeline?

Nadia Rahman: Yep—OTel names are dot-separated (`redwood.scheduler.queue.depth`) and exporter mapping keeps existing conventions. The dashboard PR will reference the exported names via the standard macro.

Aisha Bello (review): Histogram sampling at 1% is good, but incident-bot may want p95 queue wait. With sampling, do we lose utility?

Nadia Rahman: For bot context we plan to use gauge/counter signals for “is it queueing/backpressure?” and link to dashboards for deeper percentiles. We can temporarily bump sampling via runtime flag if needed. Added note in PR + flag description.

Ravi Menon (review): Admission limit gauge—where does it come from? Config propagation can be partial during incidents; please ensure it’s pulled from the scheduler’s active config, not control-plane desired state.

Nadia Rahman: Good call. Updated to export the scheduler’s effective runtime config (post-merge + defaults). Added a comment and a test to ensure we’re reading from `SchedulerConfig::effective()`.

Jacob Stein (review): Please add a short section in the metric docs about interpretation: queue depth high + gpu util low means scheduler contention vs GPU saturation.

Nadia Rahman: Added inline docstrings and a brief blurb in `scheduler_metrics.ts` for interpretation; runbook/docs update will be in follow-up (ENG-5431).

Final: reviewers approved after label normalization + effective config export changes.
payload.title: Add scheduler saturation metrics (queue depth, backpressure, admission control) to metrics pipeline

Context: SRE and product teams have asked for finer-grained timing breakdowns that surface where latency accumulates inside an invocation (request parsing, routing, model execution phases, post-processing, and streaming handoff). Existing per-request spans are coarse and confound root-cause during incidents. This PR adds: 1) a phased latency schema emitted by the runtime that splits an invocation into deterministic phases and per-phase micro-latencies; 2) an adaptive log-slicer that samples log payloads tied to high-phase-latency cohorts to keep cardinality bounded; 3) dashboard panels and an alert calibration helper that uses phase-level percentiles to mute noisy alerts and surface phase regressions; 4) a small SDK change to tag traces with phase fingerprints for downstream joins. Implementation notes: phased schema uses a compact enum for phases (parse, route, kv-warm, model-exec, stream, finalize) and attaches per-phase duration_ms and token_count where applicable; the log-slicer keeps a reservoir per-tenant-phase-cohort and uses a decay window to favor recent regressions; dashboard includes a Sankey-ish phase-flow panel, phase heatmap, and per-phase p50/p95/p99 histograms. Migration: old spans are still emitted; phased spans are additive and backward-compatible. Checklist: add phased schema and emission in runtime; add ingestion mapping and new telemetry tags; implement reservoir slicer and expose sampling metrics; add dashboard JSON and template variables; add unit tests and e2e integration test against a synthetic workload. Rollout plan: staged feature flag, enable for 10% of traffic in prod, monitor sampling overhead and cardinality, expand to 50% then 100% if metrics look good. Impact: expected increase in telemetry cardinality (controlled by slicer) and modest CPU overhead at max qps; no customer-visible API changes. Related: ENG-4821 tracks alert tuning follow-ups, SUP-987 recorded the customer incident that motivated this work.
