Motivation: Recent incidents showed noisy long-tail log retention and spiky cost alerts that produced pager fatigue. This PR implements two complementary subsystems to reduce noise while preserving fidelity for root-cause: 1) epochal log tiling: a retention/compaction scheme that buckets invocation logs into time-anchored 'epochs' and keeps variable-fidelity tiles (high-fidelity for recent epochs, compacted digests for older epochs). 2) cost-gradient alert smoother: an adaptive alert thresholding algorithm that considers the short-term gradient of per-tenant token cost to suppress transient spikes and surface persistent regressions.

What this PR changes (summary): - New epochal tiler microservice (observability/log-tiler) with configurable epoch length and tile retention policy. - Retention controller that coordinates between object store (S3/GCS) and hot cache to keep recent tiles at full resolution. - Token-correlated lightweight phase metrics (metrics/token_phase_sampler) to enable low-cardinality attribution of where cost changes originate (prompt/response/kv-cache). - Cost-gradient alerting library (alerts/cost_gradient) with hysteresis and adaptive dampening; integrates into existing SLO pipeline. - New Grafana dashboard panels and an operator guide (docs/observability/epochal-tiling.md). - Unit and integration tests + upgrade notes.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2418/epochal-log-tiling-and-cost-gradient-smoother - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration test in CI (observability smoke) - [x] Docs/ops runbook added - [x] Backwards-compatible: retention defaults preserve current retention windows unless operator flips the feature flag

Compatibility and rollout plan: This is feature-gated behind the runtime flag observability.epochal_tiling. Default is off in hosted. For Dedicated/Private customers runbook describes a staged rollout: enable on a small of tenants (10%) for two weeks, validate artifacts and SLOs, then scale. Cost-gradient smoother is opt-in per-tenant and exposes tuning knobs (window_length, slope_threshold, damping_factor).

Related work: ENG-2389 (prefetch sampler), PR #126712 (contextual log anchors) inspired decisions on digest formats. SUP-1221 documented a high-severity incident where noisy alerts obscured cost regressions.

Notes: The description intentionally avoids exposing internal S3 key formats; see docs/observability/epochal-tiling.md for operator-facing details.
Adds epochal log tiling and an adaptive cost-gradient smoother, plus dashboards and docs. Implements operator-safe defaults and feature flags to allow staged rollout. Introduces a low-cardinality token phase sampler to help pinpoint whether cost slope changes stem from prompt length, generation length, or KV cache misses.
Ethan Park: Can we make the default epoch length conservative (30m) in hosted to avoid retention blowups? Also requested that tiler metrics expose per-epoch bytes written so we can monitor the compaction ratio.
Maya Chen: Responded - set hosted default to 30m and added tile_bytes_written metric (+dashboard sparkline).
Rita Gomez: Requested unit tests around edge-case where epoch boundary moves during long-running invocation; suggested adding a deterministic boundary cut test.
Maya Chen: Added deterministic boundary unit test and an e2e integration test that replays long prompts across epoch boundaries.
Liam O'Neill: Approved after CI green and docs updated — noted one minor style nit in smoother.py (renamed variable to damping_factor).
Introduce epochal log tiling (configurable, feature-gated) to reduce long-term log storage costs while preserving high-fidelity recent logs. Add cost-gradient alert smoothing to reduce alert noise for transient token-cost spikes. New dashboard panels and operator runbook included.
Dedicated/Private: ensure object-store lifecycle policies are compatible; migrations are non-destructive by default. Hosted: rollout handled by platform ops. See docs/observability/epochal-tiling.md for tenant-level knobs.
Feature flags allow immediate disable of epochal tiling and smoother. If unexpected retention regressions occur, operators should flip observability.epochal_tiling=false and run backfill/rehydrate job as described in docs/observability/epochal-tiling.md.
Focus reviews on: 1) retention controller failure modes (controller.go), 2) smoother tuning defaults and unit tests (alerts/cost_gradient/smoother.py), 3) dashboard queries for tile_bytes_written and compact_ratio. Perf impact on hot path is minimal; token_phase_sampler is sampled at 0.1% by default.
payload.title: Introduce epochal log tiling and cost-gradient alert smoother

payload.body:
Motivation: We need a deterministic, auditable record of rollout decisions (promote, hold, rollback) that can be replayed and simulated to answer operator questions and automate rollback suggestions. This PR introduces a lightweight decision ledger and an advisory layer that synthesizes telemetry, cost signals, and counterfactual replay to provide safe canary/A-B/shadow promos. Design summary: 1) decision_ledger service stores immutable decision events (reason, inputs, heuristics, confidence) and exposes a read/write API for the rollout controller; 2) rollout_advisor component ingests live telemetry streams plus recent ledger entries and computes an action recommendation (promote/retain/backout/partial-backout) with an explainability payload; 3) shadow_seeder implements a cost-aware reservoir sampler that seeds shadow traffic across slices based on unit-cost budgets and quality risk; 4) a counterfactual replayer re-executes a bounded sample of requests against candidate model revisions using stored KV prefixes and deterministic RNG to estimate delta metrics; 5) safety gates include sample-size thresholds, latency/cost SLO thresholds, and a multi-metric risk score that weights user-impacting regressions higher than cost regressions. Implementation notes: The decision ledger is implemented as an append-only protobuf log with local write buffering and durable flush to the existing rollout-snapstore. The advisor exposes a gRPC endpoint used by the rollout controller; recommendations are annotated with evidence keys that map to ledger entries and telemetry traces for audit. The shadow seeder introduces a small policy DSL (JSON) to express cost caps per cohort and decay windows. The counterfactual replayer runs off a dedicated worker pool and emits a synthesized delta metric event that the advisor consumes. Testing: Added unit tests for ledger ordering and idempotency, property tests for the reservoir sampler, an e2e flow test that runs a simulated canary (10k synthetic requests) and validates advisor decisions under injected latency regressions, and a small chaos test that verifies safe backout when the ledger becomes temporarily unreachable. CI story: initial CI run failed integration tests due to a race in the snapshot flush path under high concurrency (flaky: tests/rollout/test_snapshot_race.py). The fix introduces a per-snapshot write lock and reduces flush window drift; all tests and linters pass after the fix. Backwards compatibility and rollout: default behavior is no-op unless the operator enables the decision-ledger flag. Rolling rollout of this PR will be gated with a feature flag at the controller level and an admin UI toggle in the Console. Security and privacy: ledger entries can be redacted by policy; no raw user inputs are written. Observability: added new metrics rollout_decisions_total, rollout_advisor_latency_seconds_bucket, counterfactual_delta_histogram, and a debug trace tag advisor.evidence_id that links to trace and ledger event. Docs: updated docs/rollouts/decision-ledger.md and added a short runbook in docs/rollouts/runbooks/rollback-advisor.md. Related work: builds on past canary frameworks (see ENG-1022) and complements the automated rollback advisor in SUP-9123. Migration notes: existing rollout snapshots remain compatible; a migration script (tools/ledger/migrate_snapshots.py) converts legacy snapshot metadata to ledger pointers. Why this is different: rather than only reacting to threshold breaches, the advisor reasons over a small universe of counterfactual outcomes and cost constraints and then records each decision for later forensic replay. This enables reproducible incident analysis and cautious automation.
Ava Chen: Nice isolation of ledger I/O, please add a short note about retention policy and compaction on the proto file so operators aren't surprised.
Lina Morales: Added compaction/retention section to decision_ledger.proto and docs; ledger uses configurable retention window and compact-to-references beyond 90d.
Marcus López: The advisor risk weights look reasonable but we should expose them as a tunable policy; can we default to conservative values?
Lina Morales: Exposed risk weights in advisor config with conservative defaults (safety bias = 1.5, cost_bias = 0.5).
Priya Patel: The e2e seemed slow in CI; can we make synthetic traffic deterministic so reproducing fails is easier?
Lina Morales: Made the synthetic request generator deterministic via seed and reduced sample size for CI; full-scale sim runs in nightly tests.
Ava Chen: Approving after the snapshot lock fix and docs updates.
Marcus López: Minor nit in seeder policy parsing fixed in last commit.
CI Bot: Integration tests failed on first run (snapshot race). Rerun requested and passed.
Added decision ledger and rollout advisor: opt-in feature flag, cost-aware shadow seeding, counterfactual replayer, new telemetry metrics, and runbook. Operators should review retention default and advisor config before enabling in production.

payload.body:
Context: Customers and auditors have requested a clearer separation between operator-level key usage and service-account-bound KMS activity, plus consistent, region-aware audit retention enforcement. This PR delivers two coordinated changes: (1) an operator KMS isolation gate that prevents operator-scoped credentials from being used against customer-scoped KMS key identifiers unless a safe-bridge template is configured; (2) a new lightweight Audit Adjudicator service that deduplicates KMS-related audit events, annotates them with tenant residency claims, and enforces TTL-based retention policies per tenant/region.

What changed (high level):
- Runtime: add operator_kms_isolation middleware to the vault/kms client chain. The middleware rejects requests where the auth principal is an operator-managed service and the target key belongs to a tenant-scoped namespace, unless a tenant-operator binding is present in the operator_allowlist.
- Control plane: introduce operator_kms_bindings CRD (private deployments) and a new admin CLI (redwoodctl kms bind) to author bindings. For hosted instances this is implemented as an admin API with RBAC guards.
- Audit pipeline: new adjudicator service (go) that subscribes to audit forwarder events, performs signature-level dedupe, enriches events with residency assertions (region pin / tenant claims), and writes canonical events to the audit store with a retention TTL field. The adjudicator exposes a readonly metrics endpoint and a small control API for graceful replays.
- Tests: unit + integration tests for the middleware, end-to-end smoke for adjudicator + forwarder, and a workload test validating that operator-scoped tokens are rejected for tenant keys.

Motivation: Prior incidents showed operators inadvertently using elevated operator credentials to access tenant CMKs in edge cases during maintenance windows. Separating operator usage and providing explicit bindings reduces blast radius. The adjudicator reduces audit noise and ensures tenant-region retention policies are applied consistently across heterogeneous audit forwarders.

Backwards compatibility and migration: On merge we add a migration job that scans operator key metadata and attempts to synthesize bindings for safe existing usages. Customers with custom KMS integrations are flagged and required to run redwoodctl kms bind or approve suggested bindings via the console. Documentation and migration playbook included.

Commits:
- initial: add operator_kms_isolation middleware and unit tests
- add: operator_kms_bindings CRD + redwoodctl cli commands
- add: audit adjudicator service, dedupe algorithm and retention enforcement
- tests: integration tests and e2e smoke
- docs: migration guide and admin API docs

Changed files (high level):
- go/services/kms/middleware/operator_isolation.go
- go/services/kms/middleware/operator_isolation_test.go
- go/ops/crds/operator_kms_bindings.yaml
- tool/redwoodctl/cmd/kms_bind.go
- services/audit/adjudicator/main.go
- services/audit/adjudicator/dedupe.go
- services/audit/adjudicator/retention_policy.go
- services/audit/adjudicator/integration_test.go
- infra/helm/charts/adjudicator/Chart.yaml
- infra/helm/charts/adjudicator/values.yaml
- docs/ops/kms_operator_bindings.md
- docs/migrations/2026-02-kms-binding-playbook.md
- examples/kms-binding/sample-binding.yaml
- terraform/modules/audit-forwarder/main.tf
- ci/pipeline/adjudicator.yml
- pkg/metrics/metrics_registry.go

Notes on implementation details (continuous string): The operator_isolation middleware checks the auth principal type from the request context (operator_service | service_account | tenant_token). For operator_service types we resolve the target key's namespace by calling KeyMetadataService (cached) and validate a binding lookup against the operator_kms_binding index. Bindings support glob patterns for keys and optional temporal windows for maintenance. Failure modes return a well-documented 403 with an error code (KMS_OP_ISOLATION_VIOLATION) so callers can programmatically detect attempted breaches. The adjudicator dedupe algorithm uses a triple-key (event_signature, key_id, minute_bucket) and keeps an in-memory LRU with a configurable maximum TTL to avoid reemitting duplicate events within the bucket. Events are enriched by calling the residency-assertor (local cache + verifier) and attaching region_pin and tenant_claim fields. The adjudicator writes canonical events to the audit store via the existing audit-writer interface and sets retention metadata using retention_policy.go rules which map tenant_region -> TTL.

Review summary and rationale for merge: Security and SRE reviewers validated threat model and failure behavior. Performance impact measured: operator_isolation middleware adds ~0.4ms median overhead to KMS calls in local bench; adjudicator runs as a sidecar/standalone service with <10% CPU at 50k events/minute in our load tests. Migration tooling minimized risk for hosted customers (auto-suggest bindings). Given low runtime cost and high security benefit the change was approved for merge.
Ethan Zhao: Can we guarantee that the binding lookup won't become a hotspot? Priya: We added an in-memory index with async invalidation and fall back to a cached KeyMetadataService; perf tests show <1% latency outliers.
Sofia Martinez: Need to ensure hosted customers get meaningful upgrade notices. Priya: Added migration job and console flags to preview suggested bindings; docs updated with playbook.
Liam O'Connor: How do we handle multi-provider KMS keys that don't return metadata? Priya: We added a fallback mode that requires an explicit binding for keys without metadata; the migration job flags such keys for manual approval.
Security review (Anna Kim): threat model looks good, but require observability on rejects -> added metrics (reject_count by reason) and a SLI dashboard.
SRE comment (Marco Santos): Helm chart values require a resource hint; added cpu/memory defaults and HPA stanza.
Author response: addressed comments, added more tests, and updated helm/values with resource defaults.
Final: Reviewed-by: Ethan Zhao; Approved-by: Sofia Martinez.
CI pipeline: lint -> go unit -> integration -> helm lint -> container scan. Initial run: one flaky integration test in adjudicator (replay timing) failed; re-run fixed it. All checks passing on final run. Container scan: no critical findings; two low-risk linter comments fixed.
Add operator-scoped KMS isolation enforcement and deploy an audit-adjudicator service that deduplicates and enforces tenant-region audit TTLs. No user-facing API changes. Admin config required for private deployments.
Introduces explicit deny posture by default: operator requests to tenant-scoped keys are denied unless a binding exists. Audit Adjudicator ensures consistent retention tagging; retention enforcement is pluggable per deployment. Admin approval required for auto-synthesized bindings in hosted mode.
deployed adjudicator to staging via canary, ran migration job in staging and produced binding suggestions for ~23 keys. Runbook created and added to docs. Ops scheduled a phased rollout in private clusters over two weeks.
payload.title: introduce-operator-service-kms-isolation-and-audit-adjudicator

Context: As part of Hosted canary rollouts GA work, we need a data-plane primitive that can split traffic on a Hosted route between a baseline target and a canary target by percentage, with deterministic cohort assignment (sticky per caller) and region-aware enforcement. This PR adds a new routing primitive `canary_split` to the Smart Routing evaluation + enforcement path. The primitive is intentionally minimal: it takes two compatible upstream targets (baseline + canary), a canary weight (0-100), and a deterministic cohort key, then selects the target for a request. This will be wired into the Rollout Orchestrator/control plane in follow-ups. What’s included: (1) New route config primitive `canary_split` with validation (weights must sum to 100, baseline/canary targets must be same modality and compatible model family; canary weight can be 0-100; guardrails around missing/invalid fields). (2) Deterministic cohorting: compute `cohort_bucket` = xxhash64(<cohort_key> + <route_id> + <rollout_id?>) mod 100; bucket < canary_weight => canary else baseline. If rollout_id is omitted we still include a stable config hash so cohorting does not flip on unrelated route config changes. (3) Cohort key derivation: prefer `x-redwood-cohort-key` header (set by gateway / console preview tools); fallback to API key id; final fallback to stable client IP hash when key id is unavailable (internal-only paths). We explicitly do NOT use request body content. (4) Region-aware behavior: the split is evaluated locally in each region using the same deterministic algorithm to preserve the global percentage distribution while avoiding cross-region coordination; we include region in logs but not in the hash input to avoid region-driven cohort flipping for clients that fail over. (5) Retries/streaming handling: we ensure the chosen target is pinned for the lifetime of a request (including internal retries) by storing `selected_target` in request context; for streaming requests we do not re-evaluate mid-stream. (6) Observability hooks: adds structured routing logs fields (`route_id`, `primitive=canary_split`, `cohort=baseline|canary`, `cohort_bucket`, `canary_weight`, `target_id`) and emits a low-cardinality counter `routing.canary_split.selected` with `cohort` and `region` tags only. Metric tagging with `rollout_id` is intentionally excluded here to avoid cardinality; it will be added at the gateway/telemetry layer where we can control aggregation (tracked in ENG-9152). (7) Safety: if validation fails or canary target is unhealthy/unavailable at evaluation time, we fall back to baseline and emit `routing.canary_split.fallback_to_baseline` with a reason code. Notes / decisions: - The deterministic hash input includes route_id to avoid cross-route correlation (same cohort key should not always land in canary across all routes). - We intentionally do not include region in the hash to preserve stickiness when a client fails over between regions. - This primitive does not implement auto-stop/rollback; it only selects a target. Control plane/orchestrator will adjust `canary_weight` and state transitions. Test plan: - Unit tests for validation + cohorting distribution (bucket boundaries, 0/100%, stable behavior). - Integration tests in `smart-routing-sim` to confirm selection is pinned across retries and streaming. - Manual in staging: configure a test Hosted route with 10% canary split; send requests with fixed `x-redwood-cohort-key` and observe consistent cohort selection + logs. Rollout plan: - This ships behind `routing.enable_canary_split_primitive` flag (default off). - Console/orchestrator will not emit this primitive until backend support is enabled tenant-by-tenant. Follow-ups: - Wire `rollout_id` + cohort tags end-to-end at gateway/telemetry (ENG-9152). - Console preview + validation endpoint to render the split plan (part of orchestrator/console backend PR). - Guardrail policy enforcement (max step, soak) is out of scope here (policy engine).
Mina Haddad: Please confirm whether including region in the hash input would cause cohort flips on failover. I think we should not include it.
Ravi Menon (author): Agree. I removed region from the hash input and added an explicit comment + test case for failover stickiness.
Emily Zhao: How do we ensure retries don’t bounce between baseline/canary if the gateway replays the request?
Ravi Menon (author): We pin `selected_target` in request context after first evaluation and reuse it for internal retries; added an integration test covering 2 retries with forced upstream 502.
Zachary Hill: Validation: do we need to enforce baseline/canary compatibility (same modality / model family)? Otherwise we may route chat -> embeddings accidentally.
Ravi Menon (author): Added a compatibility check in validator: both targets must have matching `target_type` and `interface` fields; rejects mismatches with a clear error.
Allison Grant: Metric cardinality: please avoid tagging with route_id/rollout_id for now; we can add cohort selection counts but keep tags bounded.
Ravi Menon (author): Done. Metrics use only `cohort` and `region`. Route/target info is in structured logs.
Ethan Park: Can we make the hash input stable across unrelated config changes? If config hash changes often, cohort assignments will churn.
Ravi Menon (author): Updated: we use route_id + (explicit rollout_id if present else `split_config_stability_key`). The stability key is derived from baseline/canary target ids + weights only.
Mina Haddad: Looks good. Please add a flag gate and default off.
Ravi Menon (author): Added `routing.enable_canary_split_primitive` with default false and documented expected enablement flow.
Mina Haddad: Approved.
Emily Zhao: Approved after retry pinning test landed.
Allison Grant: Approved.
Internal: Adds `canary_split` routing primitive for Hosted routes (behind feature flag). Enables deterministic baseline/canary traffic splitting in the data plane; control plane/orchestrator wiring in follow-ups.
payload.title: Smart Routing: add Hosted route canary split primitive (deterministic cohorting + region-aware enforcement)

Context and motivation: Production inference workload analysis for several enterprise tenants showed high variance in small interactive requests (median tokens < 32) that repeatedly blocked larger batch lanes and inflated per-token cost. This PR introduces a 'folding prefill conductor' that groups and shapes low-latency requests into compact micro-batches when safe, and a complementary 'quant stowage' feature that packs lightweight model subgraphs into targeted quant profiles to reduce memory pressure and improve throughput. Goals: 1) reduce unit-econ for small-chat workloads without degrading tail-latency SLOs; 2) provide deterministic simulation tooling so operators can validate before enabling tenant-wide; 3) surface observability hooks and rollout guardrails.

Summary of changes: single-line overview of the main commits and surface files changed. - Runtime: introduce prefill folding scheduler (go/runtime/prefill/folder.go), shaping policy (go/runtime/prefill/shape_policy.go), and scheduler tests. - Quant: add quant stowage registry and packer (py/quant/stowage.py), stowage heuristics and unit tests. - CLI/sim: add prefill-sim CLI that runs workload traces against folding and quant stowage logic (tools/prefill_sim/README.md, tools/prefill_sim/sim.py). - Console: dashboard tiles (console/dashboards/prefill-folding.json) and runtime metric labels. - Docs: RFC and quickstart (docs/rfc/prefill-folding-quant-stowage.md, docs/ops/enable-prefill.md).

Design notes and tradeoffs: Folding is conservative by default: we only fold requests with identical route/model/type and when predicted aggregate latency remains within the tenant SLO + buffer. The folding scheduler uses a configurable wait window (default 6ms) and an adaptive shape cap so we don't accidentally create overly long sequences. Quant stowage maps lightweight ops (prefix-only attention, short sequence MLP paths) into narrower quant profiles (4/8-bit mixed paths) using a runtime tag so we can safely fallback to full-precision for unfamiliar model variants. Both features are opt-in per-tenant and gated behind rollout flags.

Checklist (author): - [x] Implementation and unit tests for folding scheduler - [x] Quant stowage registry and heuristics - [x] Prefill sim CLI and sample traces - [x] Console tiles + docs - [x] Telemetry and metrics (fold_attempts, fold_successes, stowage_hits, stowage_fallbacks)

Release notes: Introduces an opt-in prefill folding conductor to improve micro-batch economics for small requests and a quant stowage facility to pack low-cost execution paths into compact quant profiles. Disabled by default; operators must enable per-tenant via Console or API. See docs/ops/enable-prefill.md for rollout steps and simulated dry-run guidance.
Miguel Rios: Please add a short benchmark (p95 latency) comparing folded vs unfurled requests under 500 rps synthetic chat load. Also confirm memory overhead of tracker objects.
Asha Patel: Added prefilling microbenchmark script and updated metrics. Results included in docs/rfc/prefill-folding-quant-stowage.md (p95 improved by ~12% on sample trace). Tracker peak memory under 1.8MB per tenant for 1k concurrent folds.
Liang Chen: The adaptive shape cap is clever but could cause oscillation when traffic suddenly spikes. Can we add a conservative hysteresis and a fast-path abort if latency crosses tenant SLO?
Asha Patel: Implemented hysteresis and fast-path abort. See go/runtime/prefill/shape_policy.go + new unit test that simulates a sudden spike.
Feature gated and disabled by default. Recommended rollout: 1) Dry-run simulation (tools/prefill_sim) with tenant traces; 2) Enable opt-in for a small cohort (5% tenants) with telemetry checks for fold_success_rate and p99 latency; 3) Ramp to 25% then 100% if signals stable. Automated rollback if p99 latency increases > 3% or fold_fallback_rate > 5%.
1) Build runtime and start local dev cluster: make dev-up; 2) Run sample traces: python3 tools/prefill_sim/sim.py --trace tools/prefill_sim/sample_traces/tenant_chat_small.json --mode dryrun; 3) Enable flag for tenant: curl -X POST $CONSOLE/api/tenant/123/flags -d '{"prefill_folding":true}' ; 4) Monitor metrics: fold_attempts, fold_successes, stowage_hits. See docs/ops/enable-prefill.md for full checklist.
Based on internal sim with three sample tenants, expected unit-cost reduction of 8-16% for small-chat workloads with negligible p99 regressions when follow rollout. Quant stowage reduces memory footprint on GPU worker by ~6-9% in tests.
This PR intentionally keeps folding conservative — it's meant as a low-risk first step so operators can experiment with tenant-level economics without large surface changes. Follow-up work: automated tenant scoring for suggested enabling and a dashboard card that shows estimated cost-savings per tenant.
Add opt-in prefill folding and quant stowage to reduce unit cost for small requests; disabled by default.
payload.title: Folding Prefill Conductor and Quant Stowage: shape-aware prefill + quant packing

payload.body:
Motivation: debugging regional failovers and SLO-driven load-shedding has repeatedly required correlating traces with ad-hoc logs and customer tickets. Engineers lack a consistent, queryable record of why a request was routed, shed, or tripped by a circuit. This PR introduces a transparent decision-logging pipeline that emits structured per-request decision traces (sampled) from the failover router and circuit-enforcer so operators can audit and replay routing decisions. Changes include: 1) a lightweight decision logger that records the decision path (policy match, SLO bucket, circuit state, fallback chosen, region/zone metrics snapshot) as a structured JSON event; 2) integration hooks in the regional failover router, SLO enforcer, and circuit-breaker module; 3) a sampled export path to the observability pipeline (default sampling 1%, 100% when a region is in degraded mode) with opt-in 100% tracing via feature flag for incidents; 4) redaction rules to strip PII and prompt content; 5) a small hotfix to avoid a duplicated load-shed event when KV-drain and preemption race; 6) unit + integration tests and a canary rollout plan. Performance: micro-benchmarks show ~0.4% p50 and ~0.6% p99 overhead at baseline canary traffic when sampling at 1%; under 100% tracing overhead is higher but permitted under incident feature flag. Deployment plan: staged canary -> 25% -> 100% for all regions; feature-flag kill-switched to rollback quickly. Migration note: a shim is included to backfill decision traces for the last 72h from existing router logs (best-effort) during rollout.

Adds opt-in per-tenant segregated warm pools for Dedicated and a surge circuit-breaker to prevent noisy-neighbor blast radius; new telemetry metrics and feature flag behind 'segregated_warm_pools_v1'.
Motivation: Customers running Dedicated have reported SLA regressions when a single tenant's warm-pool thrash causes sustained headroom depletion across a shared warm pool. This PR introduces two related controls: (1) a segregated warm-pool controller that can allocate warmlets in tenant-scoped pools to limit noisy-neighbor effects, and (2) a surge circuit-breaker that detects rapid utilization spikes across a pool and temporarily gates new reservation commits to protect overall throughput guarantees.

Design summary: segregated warm-pools are configured via the existing FleetConfig API with an optional 'segregation_policy' (none|per-tenant|per-namespace). The controller keeps warm-pool bookkeeping and exposes a small allocator API: AllocateWarmlet(tenant_id, preferred_pool) which prefers tenant pools and falls back to shared pools if disabled. The surge circuit-breaker monitors per-pool short-window utilization (1m/5m) and an estimator for headroom volatility. On breaker trip, the controller emits SurgeBreakerTripped{pool, reason} and enforces a reject-or-defer policy configurable per-fleet. The circuit uses an exponentially decaying trip score to avoid flip-flopping.

Telemetry & observability: new metrics exported via /metrics and console dashboards: redwood_warm_pool_usage_by_pool, redwood_warm_pool_alloc_failures_total, redwood_surgebreaker_state{pool}, redwood_surgebreaker_trips_total, redwood_surgebreaker_backoff_seconds. Added tracing spans for AllocateWarmlet and BreakerEvaluate to make correlation with request traces easier.

Compatibility & rollout: feature gated under 'segregated_warm_pools_v1' feature flag. Default behavior unchanged. Backward-compatible config additions allow tenants to opt into segregation. Documented default thresholds and suggested tuning for small/medium/large fleets in the console docs.

Commits (high-level): 1) 8a3f2b4 - introduce segregated warm-pool controller skeleton + API surface. 2) 2b7d9c1 - wire warm-pool allocator into dedicated reconciler, add unit tests and mocks. 3) d4c11e0 - add surge circuit-breaker logic, telemetry, e2e test harness and docs.

Files/areas changed (high-level): controllers/warmpool_controller.go, controllers/allocator.go, autoscaler/surge_breaker.go, telemetry/metrics_registry.go, console/docs/dedicated-warmpools.md, api/v1/fleet_config.proto, pkg/featureflags/flags.go, internal/tests/e2e/dedicated_surge_test.go, several unit tests and mocks. No schema-breaking RPCs; proto additions are additive.

Testing: unit tests added for allocation fallback logic and breaker hysteresis (coverage + branch checks). Integration e2e harness simulates noisy-tenant load to assert that segregated pools prevent cross-tenant headroom collapse and that the breaker prevents sustained SLA breaches under pathological bursts. CI run initially failed lint due to a formatting regression (fixed in second commit). One intermittent e2e flake in warmlet lifecycle observed in CI; added retry and bolstered assertions to stabilize. All checks green on final run.

Review conversation (summary): - Luca Romano: asked for clearer failure modes when tenant pool is exhausted; requested explicit metrics for allocation rejections. Response: added redwood_warm_pool_alloc_failures_total and a graceful fallback to shared pool when allowed; noted in docs. - Priya Shah: requested tests around breaker decay parameters and an API knob to toggle reject vs defer semantics. Response: added parameter 'surge_policy' to FleetConfig and two additional unit tests to cover both paths. - Diego Morales: requested performance microbenchmark and memory allocation audit for controller caches. Response: added microbench harness results to PR and reduced controller cache retention to avoid long-lived allocations. After addressing comments, reviewers approved.

CI summary: Lint: initially fail (fmt) -> fixed. Unit tests: pass. Integration: pass (one rerun due to flake). Benchmarks: included as artifacts. Coverage: unchanged within tolerance.

Backwards compatibility & migration plan: default off; opt-in migration recommended for fleets with per-tenant SLA issues. If a customer enables per-tenant segregation, warmlets already allocated in a shared pool are gradually drained and re-backed into segregated pools during maintenance windows to avoid instant capacity churn.

Release notes / rollout: ship behind feature flag; enable canary in dedicated-staging, monitor new metrics (surgebreaker_trips_total, warm_pool_alloc_failures). If breaker trips more than 1% of windows for a tenant, recommend tuning thresholds or increasing reserved warmlets for that tenant.

Merge outcome: squashed and merged to main on 2025-11-13 after approvals.

Follow-ups (next PRs planned): - autoscaler suggestion engine: recommend per-tenant reserve sizing based on historical warmlet churn (ENG-2229). - UI controls in Console to visualize segregated pool allocations and to manually trigger backfills.

Context: We need a unified coordinator that can manage small-to-large rollouts (canary, A/B, shadow) while enabling a deterministic, replayable rollback when a safety gate trips. Motivation: Existing controllers handle traffic split and canary phases but lack a deterministic priming step for cohorts and a compact, replayable rollback ledger. This PR introduces the Traffic Lifecycle Coordinator (TLC): a lightweight state machine that manages eligibility priming, shadow priming, phased promote, telemetry gated holds, and a replayable rollback record for bisect/diagnostics. Changeset summary: - Add TLC service (go) with state transitions: PRIMING -> SHADOW -> CANARY -> GRADUAL -> PROMOTED -> ROLLBACK_REPLAY - Implement eligibility priming: cohorts are pre-registered and warmed in shadow mode with controlled sampling to surface integration regressions before traffic is split - Add a compact rollback ledger: snapshots (metadata-only) of routing and cohort assignments are persisted to etcd and an append-only ledger for deterministic replay during rollback or bisect - Telemetry gating: integration with metrics pipeline to evaluate SLOs (p95 latency, 5xx rate, quality regression delta) and hold or trigger rollback when thresholds cross - Replay harness: debug endpoints to simulate replay of a snapshot in dry-run mode against recorded trace samples - Safety gates: sample-weighted statistical checks, time-windowed holds, minimum-sample thresholds, manual-latch override - Operational APIs: rollforward, hold, abort, snapshot, replay-dryrun, audit-export - Migration: automated conversion for existing rollout objects to TLC schema; backward compatible for simple split-based rollouts Backwards compatibility: TLC can be opted-in per namespace. Existing split/canary resources are untouched unless migrated. Checklist: - [x] Service + controller logic implemented - [x] Unit tests for state machine transitions - [x] Integration tests for priming -> canary -> promote -> rollback path - [x] Telemetry gate simulated in CI smoke tests - [x] Migration tool + docs - [x] E2E smoke on staging with shadow priming A/B scenario Performance considerations: priming step uses sampled shadow traffic with throttled concurrency to avoid resource spikes. Ledger entries are compact (<= 2KB per snapshot) and TTL-ed after 30 days by default. Rollback replay reuses existing offline replay infra to minimize new resource requirements. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: mis-priming leads to false positives. Mitigation: default conservative priming sample (0.5% traffic), and manual override. - Risk: telemetry noise causes unnecessary rollback. Mitigation: dual-window gating and minimum sample counts, and a soft-hold mode that requires either two metric windows or manual confirmation. Notes: Linear tickets referenced above capture the product requirements (ENG-1282 describes priming UX; ENG-1305 captures replay ledger format). This description consolidates the scope and operational playbook for reviewers.
Arjun: Nice design. A few questions: how do we protect against ledger growth in a tenant with continuous small rollbacks?
Maya: Ledger entries are metadata-only and TTL-ed; we've added a compaction job to aggregate old snapshots weekly (see ledger.go).
Liam: The replay dry-run looks useful; can it be used to drive automated bisection?
Maya: Not in this PR — replay exposes hooks and instrumentation. I added a follow-up Linear task to plumb automated bisection (ENG-1350).
Sofia: CI didn't exercise the telemetry dual-window gating; can we add a deterministic unit test?
Maya: Added tlc_gates_integration_test.go to simulate sliding windows. That test is part of this PR and passing in CI.

Maya: Addressed both in follow-up commits; added comments and a unit test for migration rollback semantics.
Liam: Approved
Sofia: Approved
Introduce Traffic Lifecycle Coordinator (TLC): manages eligibility priming, shadow priming, phased canaries, telemetry gating, and introduces a compact, replayable rollback ledger. Opt-in via tlc CRD. Includes migration tool to convert split-based rollouts.

Context and motivation: recent incidents showed rapid region-wide evacuations triggered by transient KV pressure and probe flapping. This caused churn and prolonged degraded SLOs for multi-tenant customers. This PR implements a lightweight Standby Evacuation Holdoff Coordinator that: 1) aggregates probe signals and KV pressure heuristics; 2) defers irrevocable tenant evacuation for a configurable holdoff window when probes are noisy; 3) surfaces a rejoin-safe signal to the regional failover conductor. Goals: reduce oscillatory evacuations, avoid unnecessary tenant migration, and provide observability for holdoff decisions.

What changed (high level): commits summarize the implementation and tests. Key behavior: - New coordinator service that listens to region health probes and KV pressure events, produces a per-tenant holdoff decision (HOLD/ALLOW) with TTL semantics. - Synthetic probe integration: injected, short-lived synthetic probes that validate stable latencies before ALLOW. - Backoff policy: exponential holdoff with jitter for repeated flaps. - Telemetry: holdoff_decisions counter, holdoff_duration histogram, probe_consistency gauge, and debug traces when a decision blocks evacuation. - Compatibility: coordinator provides non-blocking advisory API; existing evacuation conductor will consult advisory and escalate only after advisory ALLOW or holdoff expiry.

Design notes: the advisor is purposely advisory so we can fast-rollback. The holdoff window defaults to 8s and is configurable per tenant cohort. Synthetic probes run at most twice during holdoff to prevent probe amplification. We avoid extending global SLO timers; escalation to mandatory evacuation occurs after 3x holdoff windows or when KV saturation exceeds a hard threshold.

Files changed (high level): src/services/evac/holdoff_coordinator.go - core coordinator and TTL store; src/services/evac/probe_integration.go - synthetic probe runner and reconciler; src/runtime/slo/enforcer.rs - small adapter that calls advisory API; pkg/telemetry/metrics.yaml - definitions for new metrics; tests/integration/evac_holdoff_integration_test.py - deterministic integration tests and a new flaky-probe scenario; docs/runbooks/evacuation.md - updated runbook and rollback steps; scripts/deploy/helm/values-evac.yaml - config knobs and defaults.

Commits: ["implement holdoff coordinator and TTL store", "add synthetic probe runner and reconcile loop", "adapter in slo enforcer to consult advisory API", "integration tests for probe flapping scenarios", "docs and telemetry definitions"].

Tests and CI: unit tests and lints passed on first run. Integration suite initially failed two flaky tests related to timing assumptions; fixed by using a deterministic clock interface in the tests and re-ran CI. E2E smoke ran in staging and validated that evacuation is skipped under transient probe failures and that eventual evacuations still proceed under sustained KV pressure. CI summary: build: pass; unit-tests: pass; integration-tests: pass; e2e-staging: pass.

Review conversation (high level): - Asha: "Can we make the per-tenant default holdoff configurable via operator UI and expose a metric for active holdoffs?" Answered: added values-evac.yaml knob and holdoff_decisions metric. - Liam: "Concerned about probe amplification — what's the upper bound on synthetic probes during large-scale incidents?" Reply: synthetic probes capped at 2 attempts per tenant per holdoff; implemented a global probe-rate limiter. - Noah: "Telemetry looks good, but add a trace for decisions that block evacuation for >30s" Actioned: added debug trace event. - Asha: approved after metrics addition; Liam approved after probe-rate limiter added.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan: coordinator exposes an advisory HTTP/gRPC endpoint; rollout is phased: feature-flagged off by default, enable for internal canary tenants first, then 10% region traffic, then global. Telemetry and a dashboard will be used to monitor: holdoff_rate, average holdoff duration, subsequent evacuation rate, and SLO windows. Rollback: disable feature flag and the advisory returns ALLOW immediately.

Observability & SLOs to watch: - holdoff_decisions{result=HOLD} - probe_consistency - downstream_evacuation_count (should drop for noisy incidents) - request_latency_p50/p95 (no regressions) - tenant_rebalance_ops (should not spike unexpectedly)

Security and safety: advisory API is authenticated and rate-limited; synthetic probes run with a limited call-path and are traceable in audit logs. No tenant data is persisted by probes.

Related work: references ENG-2873 for incident postmortem and SRE-618 for telemetry dashboard request.

Merge outcome: merged via squash; changelog entry added to release notes.

Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] docs updated, [x] telemetry added, [x] feature-flagged rollout config included.

Why this is different: instead of immediate eviction we now have a short, observable, configurable holdoff that uses synthetic validation to avoid noisy evacuations and reduce cross-region churn.
Introduces a standby evacuation hold-off coordinator to reduce noisy regional failovers; adds synthetic probe integration and new telemetry to detect safe rejoin windows.

payload.body:
Context & motivation: High P99 decode tail latency on mixed workloads comes from long-running decodes blocking short, latency-sensitive requests when CPU/GPU kernels are monopolized by large batches. Existing continuous-batching + prefill strategies reduce throughput cost but struggle when a small high-priority request arrives mid-prefill window. This PR introduces a deadline-aware scheduler that enables lightweight decode preemption combined with proactive KV cache warmup (priming) and a micro-slice packing layer that coalesces tiny decode slices to retain throughput.

Design summary: We add three cooperating components: (1) deadline_scheduler - assigns soft deadlines to incoming requests and can preempt pending decode slices when a higher-deadline candidate arrives; (2) micro_slice_packer - splits large decode work into micro-slices (configurable slice size) and packs small latency-sensitive slices opportunistically to avoid throughput loss; (3) kvcache warmup_manager - issues async KV priming requests for expected future continuations for requests that are likely to be preempted or for high-hit-rate prefixes. The scheduler uses a simple EDF-inspired heuristic with a preemption budget per worker to avoid thrashing. The warmup manager is conservative by default (configurable aggressiveness) and integrates with existing KV eviction/soft-evict signals.

Implementation notes: The scheduler lives in src/runtime/scheduler/deadline_scheduler.rs and exposes hooks into dispatcher (preemptible_dispatch.rs). Preemption is cooperative: decode kernels must check a preemption token at kernel slice boundaries; we use a fast atomic flag and a small handshake to migrate half-completed KV cache slots. Micro-slice packing is implemented as an intermediate layer before kernel submission; the code ensures token cache coherency by carrying a short-lived KV priming context with each packed slice. All new components are behind runtime feature flags (runtime.features.decode_preemption, runtime.features.kv_warmup) and can be toggled per model or route in configs/profiles/deadline_defaults.yaml.

Benchmarks & results: CI microbenchmarks and a patched perf lab run show: median latency change: -3% (unchanged for bulk workloads), p95: -12% for mixed traffic (10% small latency-sensitive requests), p99: -28% on a 80/20 small/large mix using slice_size=64 tokens and preemption_budget=3. Throughput drop observed in heavy bulk-only synthetic runs is <2% when micro-slice packing is enabled. KV warmup reduced cold-KV miss rate for preempted continuations from 42% to 9% in our instrumented traces.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests cover scheduler invariants, preemption handshake correctness, and KV warmup backoff. Integration tests exercise multi-request interleaving and ensure no state leakage between slices. Benchmarks/bench_decode_preemption.py reproduces perf numbers. Rollout strategy: enable feature flag in staging for 2 weeks with conservative defaults (slice_size=64, preemption_budget=1, kv_warmup=low); ramp to canary (5%) then to 50% with observability dashboards (decode latency heatmaps, kvcache hit/miss per route) added in this PR.

Risks and mitigations: Primary risk is preemption-induced cache churn hurting throughput. Mitigations: preemption budget, conservative default warmup policy, and automatic rollback if aggregate throughput drops by >5% in a rolling window. Another risk is kernel compatibility: we added a lightweight kernel callback to check preemption token — legacy kernels fall back to non-preemptible path.

Related: Linear ENG-4321 (deadline scheduling proto), ENG-4389 (KV warmup design). Sup ticket SUP-7823 reported customer incidents where short requests suffered huge tail latency.

Checklist: [x] design doc updated (docs/architecture/decode-preemption.md) [x] unit/integration tests [x] perf benchmarks added [x] feature flags + config profile [x] rollout/monitoring notes

Ethan Caldwell (reviewer) on 2024-10-03: Great direction. Can you explain why we chose cooperative preemption vs immediate kernel termination? Concerned about GPU kernel teardown overhead.
Maya Singh (author) on 2024-10-03: Answered: cooperative avoids heavy teardown; we split kernels into micro-slices and check a preempt flag at slice boundaries. Empirical overhead of a slice boundary check is <0.2% (measured).
Luca Moretti (reviewer) on 2024-10-04: Suggestion: add a safeguard that disables preemption on low-util hosts to avoid unnecessary packing overhead. Also request metrics for preemption counts per worker.
Maya Singh (author) on 2024-10-05: Implemented an API to read host utilization and added preemption gating; added metrics decode.preemptions.total and decode.preemptions.per_worker. Updated tests to cover gating behavior.
Zoe Chen (reviewer) on 2024-10-06: Please make warmup aggressiveness configurable per-model and ensure it respects privacy flags for private deployments.
Maya Singh (author) on 2024-10-07: Done - config supports per-model overrides and warmup is disabled automatically for models/routes marked privacy.sensitive. Added docs note.
Ethan Caldwell (reviewer) on 2024-10-09: CI flake on bench job; re-ran and green. Approving pending changelog entry.
Maya Singh (author) on 2024-10-10: Added changelog entry and a short migration note in docs. Marking ready to merge.
Introduce deadline-aware decode preemption and KV warmup scheduler. Improves P99 decode latency on mixed workloads by allowing short high-priority requests to preempt long-running decodes while maintaining throughput via micro-slice packing. Feature gated behind runtime.features.decode_preemption and runtime.features.kv_warmup.

Context and motivation: Customers running Private deployments and Dedicated clusters asked for stronger guarantees that operator/service credentials cannot be used to route KMS calls outside an operator's allowed geozone. This PR implements a lightweight constraint layer in the operator credential allocator and an audit fence that records (and can backfill) region assertions on requests so compliance teams can prove residency behavior.

What this PR changes: single commit series implementing three coordinated pieces: (1) operator KMS credential constraints: enforces a set of allowed KMS regions on operator-issued short-lived creds, applies at allocation time and at token refresh; (2) audit fence middleware: a pluggable server-side middleware that stamps all incoming requests with a canonical region_claim, signs a short proof token and emits enriched audit events; (3) audit backfill CLI: a best-effort tool that scans historical audit records and attaches computed region_assertions for events where KMS routing decisions can be deterministically inferred.

Checklist: - [x] Credential allocator changes + unit tests - [x] Audit fence middleware + integration tests - [x] Backfill CLI + dry-run mode - [x] Documentation (security/region-pin.md) - [x] Chart values and installer flag for private deployments - [x] E2E residency test in CI (staged)

High-level commits: commit 1: implement operator region constraint model and config + unit tests commit 2: wire constraints into operator credential allocator commit 3: add audit fence middleware, sign/verify helpers, and telemetry hooks commit 4: add backfill CLI with dry-run and sample output commit 5: docs, helm values, and e2e test scaffolding

Files changed (high level): - pkg/rbac/compiler.go (new constraint checks and policy mapping) - internal/kms/allocator.go (enforce allowed_regions at allocation/refresh) - pkg/audit/fence.go (new middleware that attaches region_assertion and signs proof) - cmd/tools/audit-backfill/main.go (CLI for backfilling legacy events) - e2e/residency/region-backfill.test.go (integration test using local audit sink) - docs/security/region-pin.md (operator guide and migration notes) - charts/private/values.yaml (new flags to enable enforcement in installer)

Testing and CI: Unit test coverage added for allocator and fence logic. E2E test runs in the CI staging matrix and initially failed due to a race in the fake-audit-sink wiring (flaky test). I fixed the sink by using a transient buffer with deterministic ordering and re-ran CI — all checks passed on the final run. CI summary: linux-unit (pass), go-integration (pass), helm-lint (pass), e2e-residency-staged (pass), security-scan (pass).

Rollout plan: The feature is default-disabled for hosted Redwood API. For Dedicated and Private, the installer exposes a new flag --enforce-operator-kms-regions (disabled by default). We plan a shadow rollout: enable audit-fence in accept mode for 2 weeks to gather metrics, then flip enforcement in a minor release after customer opt-in. Backfill CLI will be provided as a tool customers can run once to attach assertions into their local archival audit store.

Backward compatibility and risks: The constraint layer is additive and only applies to operator-issued creds. Service accounts with existing long-lived keys are not modified; we added a migration checklist in docs. Risk: misconfigured allowed_regions could break operator workflows; we added a safety throttle and an emergency bypass knob documented in the installer notes.

Security review notes: Priya performed an initial threat model review: confirmed signing keys are KMS-wrapped and not persisted in plaintext, audit fence proof tokens use short TTLs (default 1 minute), and backfill CLI performs no writes unless --apply is specified.

Migration notes for compliance teams: docs/security/region-pin.md explains how to enable audit-only mode, run backfill in dry-run to review changes, and execute apply mode once validated. Also includes recommended query snippets for our audit-log-exporter to produce residency reports.

Why this is different from previous residency/KMS work: Prior PRs focused on routing and policy enforcement at runtime. This change introduces an operator-scoped credential constraint and an explicit audit-proof primitive that makes region assertions first-class in the audit trail and provides tooling to reconcile older records. That combination makes regulatory attestations (e.g., 'data processed in EU only') provable from audit histories rather than inferred from routing logs.

Diego Alvarez: Please add a defensive unit test for the allocator when allowed_regions is empty — we should default to no-enforce rather than panic.
Sana Kapoor: Added test and updated allocator to treat empty list as 'no constraints' (see commit a4e6b9d).
Priya Nair: How are proof signing keys rotated? Need to mention KMS rotation policy and key access logs in the docs.
Sana Kapoor: Documented key rotation and added KMS key ACL recommendation; proof tokens are short-lived and signed using a key that must be KMS-wrapped (docs updated).
Owen Lin: Backfill CLI looks good but could be slow for very large archives. Add batching and a dry-run summary of write counts.
Sana Kapoor: Added batching and summary output; default dry-run prints top-5 inferred regions per day.

payload.body:
Motivation: large shadow traffic bursts (spikes from canary seeding and replayed consumer traffic) can transiently blow through cost budgets or push latency p95s above SLOs even when user-facing traffic remains stable. Existing shadow lanes are either fully on or off and rely on global throttles; that makes short-lived surges noisy and causes blunt rollback decisions.

What this PR does (single-string description): Implements a lightweight 'shadow surge governor' that dynamically gates shadow traffic per-model and per-cohort using a combined cost and latency signal. The controller exposes two levers: (1) a soft throttle that reduces shadow fraction with a decay curve when cost burn exceeds a configured budget, and (2) an urgency gate that pauses shadow forwarding when latency SLOs (p95/p99) breach configured thresholds. The controller integrates with the rollout planner to surface a 'surge advisory' so canary and A/B orchestrators can preemptively throttle new promos rather than triggering full rollback.

Key features: 1) Per-model budget windows (sliding 1h/6h/24h) for cost and request-count; 2) latency-conditioned pause (configurable percentile and margin); 3) session-coherent decays so a user's in-flight shadow session is not dropped mid-request; 4) simulated dry-run mode that runs the throttle policy on mirrored traffic and emits an estimated cost/latency delta to the rollout planner; 5) a lightweight replay verifier that runs sampled shadow requests through a canary variant in a sandbox to detect regressions before a throttle decision triggers rollback; 6) telemetry hooks for Console: predicted burn, throttle factor, and advisory signals.

Compatibility and scope: Works across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Uses existing shadow mirror pipeline and rollout APIs; adds a small runtime sidecar to handle session coherence for Private installs where kernel-level network mirroring is not available. No model format changes.

Testing and rollout plan: Unit tests for policy math; e2e with the canary orchestrator in benchmark-lab using synthetic surge traces; phased rollout behind a feature flag with a 0%->10%->50% canary of internal traffic. Monitoring dashboards and alerting thresholds added to the Console playbook.

Why it's different from previous work: Prior PRs implemented static shadow quotas or global throttles. This PR ties throttle decisions to both cost budgets and latency SLOs and surfaces advisory signals directly to rollout orchestrators so the system can perform gentle throttles instead of blunt rollbacks. It also prioritizes session coherence and includes a sampled replay verifier to avoid false positives from noisy upstream infra.
Evan Chen (2026-02-11): Can we ensure the throttle math is stable with heavy downsampling? In particular I'm worried about oscillation when p95 temporarily recovers. Requested change: add hysteresis window to the urgency gate.
Author (Priya) (2026-02-12): Added a 15s hysteresis by default and made it configurable per-deployment. See policy/decay_policy.go changeset. Also added tests that simulate oscillatory latency patterns.
Marta Ruiz (2026-02-13): The replay verifier looks good, but for Private installs the sidecar will add CPU. Please add a knob to always sample on a separate, low-priority queue. Requested change: document resource expectations and provide config defaults.
Author (Priya) (2026-02-14): Documented sidecar resource profile and added 'replay.priority' to the private installer defaults. Verified bench-lab e2e with reduced CPU allocation; added note in console playbook for capacity planning.
Liam O'Connor (2026-02-15): CI flap: tests/e2e/shadow_governor_test.go failed intermittently on the first run (race on simulated clock). Re-run CI after test fix. Approved once green.
CI Bot (2026-02-16): Initial pipeline: fail (e2e flaky). Re-run triggered. Second pipeline: pass. Required approvers: 2 of 3 -> Evan and Marta approved (2026-02-17).
Introduces shadow surge governor: dynamic, cost- and latency-conditioned throttles for shadow traffic; dry-run advisory mode for rollout planners; replay verifier for sampled checks. Default off behind feature-flag.

Impact: improves stability of staged rollouts by preventing transient shadow spikes from causing unnecessary rollbacks. Admins should review Console playbooks for new metrics and adjust cost budgets as needed.

payload.body:
Context: Customers require a single control-plane primitive to run multi-arm A/B tests and staged feature rollouts while guaranteeing either instantaneous or safe rollback semantics. Existing controllers occasionally left the system in an inconsistent state when a control-plane failure occurred mid-rollout (traffic split applied but assignment metadata missing), or when deterministic canaries needed to be committed atomically across the routing plane and feature flags.

What this PR does: Implements a Staged A/B Orchestrator that supports: 1) atomic commit semantics for model swaps and traffic assignments (two-phase commit with short-lived leases); 2) schedule-aware windows and blackout periods to prevent rollouts during known maintenance windows; 3) preflight validators and lightweight shadow replays as fallback hooks; 4) a rollback oracle that performs targeted snapshot replays against a representative cohort and votes on a rollback if SLOs regress beyond configured thresholds; 5) an audit-friendly journaling layer to replay and reconcile partially-applied rollouts.

Design highlights: The orchestrator separates plan and apply phases. A plan describes cohorts, routing weights, validation probes, and a commit deadline. Apply uses a lease-based coordinator that first attempts a control-plane prepare step (allocating ephemeral assignment keys), then issues phased routing changes to edge proxies with a fast path for single-step atomic swaps (when config allows). If any validator fails, the apply either triggers a rollback hook or pauses and marks the plan as quarantined for manual inspection.

Safety gates and metrics: Validators include latency delta, error-rate delta, schema-conformance for structured outputs, token-level perplexity regressions (for generated text), and a sampling-based equality test between primary/shadow outputs for deterministic models. The rollback oracle aggregates weighted signals and includes hysteresis to avoid flapping. All actions are emitted to tracing and an audit journal for later replay.

Why unique: Unlike prior rollout controllers, this implementation focuses on atomic semantics across the control and data planes rather than optimistic, eventually-consistent handoffs. It also integrates lightweight shadow replay and a configurable rollback oracle as first-class primitives.

Testing and rollout: Unit and integration tests added for the prepare/apply/commit phases, and an end-to-end chaos test that kills the coordinator mid-apply to validate the reconciliation/journal path. Feature rollout plan will be gated behind a feature flag and enabled for internal tenants first, then open to customers after a one-week canary.

Notes: This PR touches control-plane reconciliation, routing proxies, and the telemetry schema. Backwards compatibility kept by exposing the new API under /v2/rollouts and keeping v1 behavior intact.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked in Linear ENG-3872; [x] unit tests; [x] integration tests; [x] chaos tests; [x] docs stub in repo; [x] telemetry and alerts updated.

Related: builds on previous work in ENG-3410 (cohort rollouts) and PM-114 (experiment lifecycle).
Miguel Santos (reviewer): Nice end-to-end testing. Two requests: 1) can we reduce the default commit lease TTL to 12s? 2) add a unit test covering validator timeouts.
Aisha Khatri (author): Reduced commit lease TTL to 12s and added validator timeout test in validators/tests/test_timeouts.py. Updated doc to explain tradeoffs.
Priya Raman (reviewer): The perplexity probe looks good but we should not use absolute token-level thresholds across models. Suggest model-scoped baselining and a per-model historical z-score threshold.
Aisha Khatri (author): Switched to z-score based thresholds stored in model profiles; added implementation and tests. Also added a note in docs about baselining data retention.
Jonah Lee (reviewer): Can we ensure that partial apply leaves a deterministic journal entry so reconciliation is idempotent? Also flagged a minor race in the lease renewal path.
Aisha Khatri (author): Journal entries are now strictly append-only with explicit prepare/commit markers; fixed race in lease renewal by serializing renewals on the lease object. Added comment and test.
Introduces v2 rollout API with atomic commit semantics, schedule-aware A/B scheduling, preflight validators, shadow replay fallback, and a rollback oracle. Feature gated; no user-facing breaking changes. See docs/rollouts/v2.md for usage.
Monitor rollout.events.* metrics and set alert for 'rollback_oracle.votes' > 5 within 10m. Keep the feature flag off for critical customers until internal canary completes.
payload.title: Staged A/B Orchestrator with Atomic Commit and Fallback Hooks

payload.body:
Problem: During pilot with predictive inputs enabled (see SUP-28479 + incident follow-ups), we observed replica count oscillation caused by noisy/stale forecast deltas and small target changes around the steady-state. This manifested as jittery queue depth and p95 latency spikes, even when we stayed within min/max bounds (PR #48218). This PR adds three guardrails to the Dedicated autoscaler decision loop: (1) per-direction cooldowns to prevent back-to-back flips (scale-up immediately followed by scale-down), (2) dampening / smoothing of predictive desired replicas using an EWMA + a limited lookback window, and (3) minimum step sizing + hysteresis around the current capacity so we don’t chase 1-replica fluctuations. These changes apply only when predictive mode is active OR when the autoscaler classifies the input signal as noisy (high variance in desired over a short window). Reactive saturation/queue depth overrides remain authoritative, and all results are still clamped to customer bounds. Summary of behavior: - Compute raw_desired from reactive + predictive arbitration (existing logic). - Clamp to bounds => bounded_desired_raw. - Apply dampening to bounded_desired_raw to produce dampened_desired (EWMA with alpha=0.35 by default; configurable per deployment in the policy, defaulted off unless predictive enabled). - Apply hysteresis: require |dampened_desired - current| >= min_step_replicas OR min_percent_change before taking action. - Apply per-direction cooldowns: if last_scale_event was < cooldown_{up,down}, hold desired at current (unless reactive override requires immediate scale-up for safety; scale-up bypasses cooldown when queue_depth/latency breach thresholds). - Emit structured reason codes + metrics for each hold/action for auditability and debugging. Defaults were chosen to preserve existing behavior for deployments without predictive enabled (no cooldown/dampening applied) and to make predictive mode safer out of the box. Related: - PR #48227 (predictive provider + fallback) - PR #48218 (hard min/max enforcement) - PR #48241 (desired vs bounded metrics) - Hotfix PR #48321 (prevent scale-to-zero when predictor returns null) Testing: - Unit tests for cooldown boundary conditions and hysteresis thresholds - Property-style tests with randomized desired sequences to ensure no oscillation under small noise - Simulation replay updates (lightweight) to validate reduced event rate without increased underprovisioning under standard ramp traces
Vanessa Ortiz (review): Cooldown semantics look good, but I’m worried about blocking legitimate scale-down after an emergency scale-up. Can we make scale-up bypass cooldown when reactive override fires, but keep scale-down cooled? Also please confirm we still always respect min/max. Keiko Yamamoto (author): Updated. Scale-up cooldown is bypassed when reactive_override=true (queue depth / saturation breach), but scale-down still obeys cooldown_down unless bounded_desired == min and reactive is green. Bounds clamp happens before dampening and again after rounding. Added tests for clamp order and a docstring. Jordan Lee (review): Where does alpha live? If this becomes a policy field, we need to ensure validation ranges and sane defaults. Also, avoid per-request state; this should be per-deployment keyed with TTL. Keiko Yamamoto: Alpha is a constant default (0.35) with optional override read from policy cache (0.05..0.9). State is per deployment_id in the autoscaler process with eviction after 2h of inactivity; no request path impact. Added guardrails when predictor staleness > 15m => disable dampening and fall back to reactive-only desired (existing fallback). Rafael Mendes (review): Please add explicit metrics for “hold due to cooldown” vs “hold due to hysteresis” so on-call can reason about why it’s not scaling. Also ensure we don’t hide an unmet-min condition behind cooldown. Keiko Yamamoto: Added metrics: dedicated_autoscaler_hold_total{reason=...}, dedicated_autoscaler_cooldown_active{direction=...}, and dedicated_autoscaler_dampening_delta. Unmet-min bypasses all holds (we keep requesting min) and we emit hold_reason=none with state=degraded elsewhere. Samantha Roy (review): Any risk this increases time-to-react during ramps? We should verify with the replay runner. Keiko Yamamoto: Ran replay on ramp_with_spikes fixture: scale event count -41%, p95 queue depth +2.3% at peak but stayed below alert threshold; time-to-recover unchanged. Notes added to README. CI: Initial run failed on gofmt in stabilizer.go; fixed in follow-up commit. Final checks green (unit/integration/sim). Approvals: Vanessa ✅, Rafael ✅, Jordan ✅. Merged via squash.
Dedicated autoscaler: added cooldowns, dampening, and minimum-step sizing to reduce oscillation when predictive scaling inputs are noisy; includes new hold-reason metrics for observability. No behavior change unless predictive mode is enabled (or policy explicitly opts into stabilization).
payload.title: Dedicated autoscaler: add cooldown + dampening + min-step guardrails to reduce oscillation (predictive mode)

payload.body:
Summary: Add a telemetry-guarded restart orchestration and a soft circuit dampener to reduce cascade failures during region/restart operations. Motivation: During the Feb 10 incident we observed coordinator-driven rolling restarts triggering collateral SLO violations in adjacent regions when restart timing overlapped with transient KV pressure and increased tail latency. This change prevents restarts from progressing for a region while its SLO trend is degrading and reduces circuit flipping noise by adding a soft dampener that increases reopen cooldown when restarts are in-flight.

What I changed (single-line sections for CI parsing):
- runtime/shedder/guard.go: new SLOTrendGuard that consumes slo_trend_score and decides restart_holdoff_seconds.
- controlplane/prober/restart_coordinator.go: restart sequencing extended to consult SLOTrendGuard and to annotate restart tickets with telemetry snapshot.
- circuit/dampener.go: implement soft dampener that adds exponential reopen debounce when restart context is present.
- telemetry/metrics_registry.go: add slo_trend_score and restart_holdoff_seconds metrics, and small tagging for restart_context.
- observability/alerts.yaml: add alert rule to surface prolonged holdoffs and sidecar KV pressure correlation.
- docs/ops/restart-playbook.md: describe new restart gating, metrics to watch, and manual override steps.
- test/guard_test.go + test/dampener_integration_test.go: unit + integration tests covering gating and cooldown behavior.

Commits (high-level):
- a1b2c3: initial implementation of SLOTrendGuard and config knobs.
- b2c3d4: integrate guard into RestartCoordinator; add telemetry snapshotting.
- c3d4e5: add soft dampener; tune reopen cooldown parameters.
- d4e5f6: add metrics + alerts and update docs.
- e5f6g7: fix flaky test and update mocks for prober (CI failure rerun).

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/shedder/guard.go (+210/-12)
- controlplane/prober/restart_coordinator.go (+120/-30)
- circuit/dampener.go (+95/-10)
- telemetry/metrics_registry.go (+45/-4)
- observability/alerts.yaml (+22/-0)
- docs/ops/restart-playbook.md (+180/-0)
- test/guard_test.go (+40/-0)
- test/dampener_integration_test.go (+70/-0)
- config/defaults.yaml (+30/-131)

Small snippet (for reviewers):
- runtime/shedder/guard.go: decision loop (illustrative):
  func (g *SLOTrendGuard) ShouldHoldoff(region string) bool {
      score := g.telemetry.CurrentSLOTrend(region) // score in [-1.0, +1.0] where negative is degrading
      if score < g.config.HoldoffThreshold {
          g.log.Infof("Holdoff: region=%s score=%0.2f holdoff=%ds", region, score, g.config.BaseHoldoffSeconds)
          return true
      }
      return false
  }

Testing and CI: Initial CI run reported a flaky integration test in prober mocks (test/dampener_integration_test.go) caused by timing assumptions. I updated the test to use a deterministic simulated clock and increased a debounce margin; CI was re-run and passed. Checks: unit (pass), integration (pass after rerun), lint (pass), e2e (smoke) (pass). Final CI status: pass.

Review convo (highlights captured as single string):
- Marcus Delgado: "Can we avoid adding a new metric name per region when high cardinality customers are enabled? Consider using tags and sampling."
  - Priya Rao (author): "Agree. metrics_registry now reuses existing region tag and uses gauge sampling; updated tests to assert tag presence rather than new metric series per tenant."
- Ethan Park: "This looks good but please ensure the restart_holdoff_seconds is exposed as a debug-only gauge for some customers until we validate in staging."
  - Priya Rao: "Added defaults.yaml flag restart_holdoff_exposure=staging_only and gate for Private/Dedicated config. Docs updated."
- Lina Soto: "Circuit dampener parameters look conservative; can we add a feature flag for rapid rollback if we see negative impact?"
  - Priya Rao: "Added feature flag circuit.soft_dampener.enabled (default true) and backout instructions in docs/ops/restart-playbook.md."

Rollout plan / mitigation:
- Step 1: Merge to main and deploy to staging with restart_holdoff_exposure=staging_only for 48h.
- Step 2: Observe slo_trend_score correlation with in-flight restarts; verify no increase in 99th P90 failures and KV pressure.
- Step 3: Flip exposure for a small subset of Dedicated customers via config and monitor.
- Backout: disable circuit.soft_dampener.enabled and set restart_holdoff_exposure=off, then restart coordinator service if necessary.

Related work / context: Linked to ENG-4321 (restart orchestration stabilizer) and SUP-1274 which reported collateral SLO degradations during a coordinated rolling restart. This PR is intentionally conservative — all gating is opt-in via config flags and metrics exposure is default-staged to avoid surprise telemetry costs.

Why this is different from previous PRs: many prior fixes focused on shedding or eviction logic; this change focuses on preventing operator-triggered or automation-triggered restarts from amplifying transient infra signals by coordinating with SLO trends and by dampening circuit reopen behavior only while a restart is ongoing.

Manual verification steps:
- In staging: trigger a simulated restart in region "eu-west-1" with slo_trend_score artificially dropped to -0.6; confirm RestartCoordinator defers restart and emits restart_holdoff_seconds metric and log line.
- Verify dampener prevents rapid circuit reopen by toggling a short failure window and checking that reopen backoff increases (exponential) while restart_context tag present.

Notes: teammates oncall were notified for post-merge monitoring window (24h). This PR was merged via squash after approvals from all reviewers and successful CI re-run.
- Introduces telemetry-guarded restart window to avoid cascade restarts across regions.
- Adds a soft circuit dampener (region-level) that prevents rapid open/close flips during rolling restarts.
- Exposes new metrics (slo_trend_score, restart_holdoff_seconds) for SLO-driven restart orchestration.
- Backwards compatible: defaults are conservative and toggled by config flags for Dedicated/Private customers.
