payload.body:
Adds an explainability shim for RBAC v2 decisioning and a hardened audit forwarder that attaches KMS call-proof bundles to outbound audit records. Feature gated and off by default in private deployments; opt-in via feature flag.
Context: Customers and auditors have asked for both (1) better machine-readable explainability for RBACv2 decisions (so operators can understand why a request was allowed/denied without deep diving logs) and (2) stronger binding between KMS usage and audit events for non-repudiation.

This PR implements two coordinated features: an RBACv2 Explainability Layer (explain middleware + compact decision blobs) and a KMS Call-Proof Audit Forwarder (bundles signed call-proofs with audit events when available).

Design summary:
- RBACv2 Explainability Layer: When enabled, the auth middleware emits a compact decision blob for each evaluated request. The blob contains the matched policy rule ids, relevant attribute values (redacted by policy), decision timestamps, and a deterministic decision fingerprint. Blobs are persisted to the audit pipeline and indexed for short-term retrieval (retention controlled by config). Explanations are intentionally terse and signed by the authorization service to prevent tampering.
- KMS Call-Proof Audit Forwarder: For KMS operations routed through the in-house KMS proxy, the proxy now returns a call-proof envelope (signature over request metadata + region claim). The audit forwarder attaches the envelope to the audit event payload and emits a single canonical record to the compliance ingest (and to a separate secure archive bucket if enabled). Forwarding is best-effort and resilient: when call-proofs are unavailable we still emit the audit with a "call-proof-missing" tag to avoid blind spots.

Migration & compatibility: Feature is disabled by default in hosted; enabled in opt-in private installs via config flag (rbac.explainability.enabled, audit.kms_forward.enabled). Existing audit schemas are preserved; new fields are opt-in and live under audit.extras.rbac_explain and audit.extras.kms_proof. No breaking API changes.

Implementation notes:
- New packages: pkg/rbac/explain, pkg/audit/forwarder/kms_proof
- Authorization service signs decision blobs with service key (rotated via existing KMS tooling)
- Forwarder deduplicates call-proofs by request fingerprint to avoid duplicate attachments during retries
- Added a short-lived explainability cache (LRU) to avoid re-evaluating heavy policy trees on retried requests

Tests & CI: Unit tests added for decision blob construction, redaction rules, and call-proof verification. Integration test harness includes an end-to-end flow: request -> auth -> explain blob -> audit forwarder -> mock KMS proxy. CI history: first run failed fmt/lint in pkg/rbac/explain (missing gofmt and docstring), then fixed in subsequent commits.

Security & privacy considerations:
- Explanations redact attributes marked sensitive by data-classifier; developers must add attributes to allowlist when absolutely necessary.
- Call-proofs contain minimal metadata and never include plaintext customer data; proof payloads are signed and stored in the secure archive with access controls.
- Operators can opt-out of storing full call-proof envelopes by setting audit.kms_forward.archive=false.

Rollout plan:
1) Canary behind feature flag for internal accounts (48h)
2) Gradual opt-in for selected enterprise tenants (via console toggle)
3) Wider opt-in and documentation release.

Observability: Added per-route metrics: rbac.explain_emitted, rbac.explain_cache_hit, audit.kms_proof_attached, audit.kms_proof_missing.

Docs & runtime config: Updated docs/ops/security/rbac_explainability.md and docs/ops/security/kms_audit_forwarder.md.

Linear & Jira: ENG-4213 tracks the feature work; SUP-342 captures support runbooks.

Risks & mitigations:
- Performance: explainability adds ~1.5ms median to auth path in microbenchmarks; mitigated by LRU cache and sampling config.
- Storage: decision blobs increase audit volume; mitigated via configurable retention and sampling (rbac.explain_retention, rbac.explain_sample_rate).

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration tests
- [x] Docs
- [x] Config flags
- [x] Security review by SRE
- [x] Manual canary verification

Maya Chen: Answered — redaction allowlist is a configmap for private installs and a console-only toggle for hosted; added docs section and an audit event when attributes are allowlisted.
Sandeep Rao: The call-proof envelope format needs a version field for future migration and tool compatibility — please add.
Maya Chen: Added version field (v1) and included schema in docs; updated tests to assert presence of version.

Maya Chen: Implemented a 200ms batching window and de-dup logic in archive_writer; added metric audit.kms_proof_batch_dropped.

Motivation: Reduce unit inference cost for variable workloads by introducing a tenant-aware hybrid quantization schedule and a sliding 'cost window' that couples prefill/caching defaults to short-term demand signals. This PR implements the autosuggest and enforcement pieces so tenants get safe, reversible quant and cache defaults without manual tuning.

Summary of changes: adds a hybrid quant scheduler that can apply mixed int8/int4 profiles per-tenant during low-cost windows; introduces a cost_window manager that computes short-term demand percentile (p50/p95) and proposes cache TTL and batching presets; exposes a CLI dry-run (--preview) and an API endpoint for previewing suggested defaults; integrates rollout gating via feature-flag + canary tenants; adds end-to-end smoke tests and telemetry for unit-econ impact.

Design notes: the hybrid quant scheduler maintains a compatibility matrix for model variants and uses a safety score (based on eval regression thresholds) before recommending a more aggressive quant step. The cost_window manager aggregates 1m windowed metrics (qps, avg latency, tokens/sec) and estimates marginal cost delta if the tenant moves to suggested presets. Recommendations include: batch_shape, cache_prefill_ttl, quant_profile, fallback_profile, and staging_window_seconds. All recommendations are returned as a single suggested_profile blob for simplicity.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag feature.hybrid_quant_windowing=false by default. 2) Enable for internal canary tenants (tenant ids listed in REDWOOD_CANARIES) for 48h. 3) Run econ-sim dry-run (CLI) against canary traffic to validate <=2% quality regression and >=6% cost reduction target. 4) Gradually enable with 10/30/100% tenant cohorts and automated rollback if quality/regression alerts fire.

Safety and fallback: fallback_profile keeps original model variant and cache TTL; scheduler supports immediate rollback and rolling reconfiguration without losing KV cache state. A hard SLI guard is enforced during staged rollout: if p99 latency increases by >10% or quality delta exceeds 2% BLEU/ROUGE-equivalent metric for tenant evalset, the system auto-reverts recommendations for that tenant and notifies SRE and the author.

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the compatibility matrix loader (hybrid_quant/compat.go) and the new telemetry tags (telemetry/labels.go) used to correlate "suggested_profile" with unit_econ traces. The CLI (tools/econ-sim) supports --preview and --apply flags; --apply is gated.

Backwards compatibility: config defaults remain unchanged unless the feature flag is enabled per-tenant. Admins can opt-out at tenant level.

Related work: builds on previous prefill/autotune pieces (ENG-3987) and the prefilling telemetry refactor in ENG-4609.

Testing: added unit tests for scheduler heuristics, integration tests for the preview API, and a small-scale canary simulation in tools/econ-sim/sim_test.go.

Release notes: new opt-in feature for tenant-aware hybrid quantization and automated cost-window presets. Admins can preview suggestions before applying.

Miguel Torres: Please ensure scheduler respects tenant pinned model_version; i saw a path where model_variant could be updated without honoring pin.
Anya Patel: Good catch — added tenant pin check in compat.go and added unit test to cover pinned variants.
Rae Chen: CI flake on sim_test.go; random seed leads to nondeterministic assert. Can we fix for deterministic?
Anya Patel: Replaced randomized sampling with a fixed seed for tests and added comment explaining reasoning.
Omar Farouk: Add a telemetry tag to correlate suggested_profile id with rollout trace for easier debugging.
Anya Patel: Added telemetry tag suggested_profile_id and included it in canary traces.

Motivation: Several incidents in Q4 revealed gaps when operator-scoped JWTs were accepted without a short-lived proof of locality. This PR introduces a lightweight operator-claim-witness service that records ephemeral operator claims, attaches a KMS-backed escrow proof, and returns a geo-seal assertion used by the RBAC v2 decision path and audit pipeline. Goals: (1) provide cryptographic, per-request operator provenance that can be verified by downstream services; (2) enforce region pinning for operator actions where tenant or service policies demand locality; (3) integrate with existing audit forwarder so proofs are attached to audit events for non-repudiation.

Summary of changes: added a new internal service (operator-witness) with a slim HTTP/gRPC API for SubmitClaim and VerifyClaim, wired KMS envelope wrapping for escrowed claim blobs, added a geo-seal module that signs an assertion including zone-id and kms-key-tag, augmented the RBAC v2 admission path to consult the witness verifier when a tenant policy requires geo-sealed operator proofs, and extended the audit-forwarder to index claim references and include proof metadata. This is implemented behind a runtime feature flag (operator_claim_witness.enabled) and a staged rollout plan is included.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc: ENG-8591 attached - [x] Unit tests for witness store and verifier - [x] Integration tests exercising RBAC decision when geo-seal required - [x] KMS key policy templates for escrow keys - [x] Helm chart values and installer notes for Private deployments - [x] Migration plan (stepwise rollout, opt-in tenants) - [x] Security review and threat model completed by SEC-117

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy witness service to canary region (staged as feature flag off by default). 2) Enable verification-only mode: services accept proofs if presented but do not require them. 3) Once telemetry shows correct acceptance rates, flip tenant policies to require geo-sealed proofs for selected self-hosted tenants. 4) If verification errors exceed threshold, automatic fallback to native RBAC decision is applied and an alert fires.

Testing: unit tests (pkg/witness/*) and integration harness (tests/integration/witness_flow) added. Manual test steps and LocalStack-compatible KMS shim included for developer QA. Full e2e tested in perf-canary for latency impact (adds ~6ms median to authenticated operator path when using local KMS cache).
Diego Morales: Overall design looks solid. Two asks: make the RPC idempotent for retries and ensure verifier handles clock skew gracefully.
Ava Park: Addressed both. Added idempotency token to SubmitClaim and a 2-minute tower for skew tolerance in verifier (configurable).
Priya Shah: Please add explicit attestations in the audit event schema so downstream SIEMs can map proofs to operator sessions.
Ava Park: Added proof_reference and proof_kms_key fields to the audit event envelope and updated forwarder indexer. Added schema migration note in docs.
Ethan Liu: CI showed intermittent flake in tests/integration/witness_flow due to LocalStack KMS throttling. Can we add a retry in the test harness?
Ava Park: Added exponential backoff in harness and a flag to use cached test keys to avoid throttling in CI. Reran CI and green.

payload.body: Motivation: Add fine-grained per-invocation energy attribution and lightweight trace anchors so oncall and SRE can correlate inference latency/cost regressions with measured GPU/host energy variation across Dedicated clusters. This change introduces energy-metering annotations derived from node-level power samples, ties meters to invocation traces via a stable anchor ID, and surfaces the data in a new dashboard and a low-noise alert for energy drift. Summary of changes: 1) runtime/telemetry: new invocation_energy meter computed as sum(joules) across scheduled device intervals; exported as metric redwood.invocation.energy_joules with labels {model, model_version, tenant, gpu_type, hw_split, invocation_phase}. 2) tracing: inject trace anchor (trace_anchor_id) into span metadata and attach a short energy sample digest (min/median/max joules over invocation) as span attributes for quick triage. 3) observability: Grafana dashboard 'Inference Energy Explorer' with per-model sparklines, percentile cohorting, and an energy drift panel that shows model-level energy per-token over time. 4) alerts: new alert rule energy-drift-high which triggers when median energy per-token increases by >25% over baseline for 10m and is evidence-backed by >500 invocations in the window. 5) sampling and costs: energy attributes are stamped only for sampled traces by default (1%) to limit cardinality; a per-tenant opt-in flag enables 100% sampling for Dedicated customers. 6) tests & docs: unit tests for energy aggregation, e2e replaybench with synthetic power traces, and developer docs describing how anchors map to traces and billing reports. Checklist: - [x] Telemetry metric schema defined and registered - [x] Runtime aggregation implemented with microbenchmarks - [x] Tracing attribute injection and anchor propagation - [x] Grafana panels and dashboard JSON added - [x] Alert rule and playbook drafted - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Dev docs and migration notes Non-goals: This PR does not change billing pipelines or cost accounting; energy_joules is advisory for now and will be used as an ops signal only. Commits summary: - Add energy sampler and aggregator to runtime (5 commits) - Trace anchor propagation and span attribute encoder (3 commits) - Add Grafana dashboard JSON + panels (2 commits) - Alert rule + Prometheus query + runbook (1 commit) - Tests and docs (2 commits) Files changed (high-level): - runtime/telemetry/energy_sampler.go - runtime/telemetry/energy_schema.yaml - runtime/trace/anchor_propagator.go - runtime/trace/span_encoder.go - observability/grafana/dashboards/inference_energy_explorer.json - observability/alerts/energy_drift.rule.yaml - observability/playbooks/energy_drift.md - tests/replaybench/energy_replay_test.go - docs/observability/energy_telemetry.md - sdk/ts/examples/energy-anchor-usage.ts - plumbing/metrics/registry.go - deployment/helm/values-observability.yaml - ci/test-e2e-energy.yml - scripts/clients/energy-sim.py Review conversation summary: - Ethan Morales (reviewer): "Can we avoid adding high-cardinality labels on the core metric? model_version and tenant are okay but please don't include full prompt hashes." Author reply (Priya): "Agreed. Metric schema keeps cardinality minimal; prompt hashes were dropped. Added model_stage and hw_split flags only for Dedicated telemetry and behind a config toggle." - Lina Zhang (reviewer): "Alert looks noisy for small tenants. Can we require minimum sample count?" Author reply: "Yes, alert now includes a sample count clause (>500 invocations) and is suppressed below that threshold. Added per-tenant auto-quiet window for low-traffic tenants." - David Perez (approver): "Looks good, small nits in dashboard layout. Approving after nits fixed." - Post-review followup: adjusted panel time ranges, tightened PromQL aggregation windows, and added unit tests for sample-weighting. CI checks: - golangci-lint: pass - unit-tests: pass - integration-e2e-energy: pass (replaybench) - dashboard-lint: pass - helm-lint: pass Observability and operations notes: - Sampling defaults to 1% global to limit ingestion cost; Dedicated tenants can enable 100% sampling via Observability flags in the Console. - trace_anchor_id is a stable 64-bit hex token derived from invocation id and node hash; it is not PII. - The dashboard includes a 'Top contributors' panel that correlates high energy with model stage (embed/decoder), sequence length, and kernel occupancy. - Playbook: when energy-drift-high fires the runbook instructs on checking trace anchors, fetching the short energy digest from the span (via traces UI), and correlating with GPU kernel queueing and host throttling metrics. Migration notes: - Consumers of telemetry should watch for redwood.invocation.energy_joules label schema pinned in runtime/telemetry/energy_schema.yaml. - No downstream billing changes; a follow-up will propose a normalized energy_rate token cost if product approves. Rollout plan: - Canary on staging and 2 Dedicated clusters for two weeks. - Flip sampling toggle for 2 pilot tenants, monitor ingestion and alert noise. - If stable, enable global 1% for Hosted and add docs for Dedicated opt-in. Release notes: "Introduce per-invocation energy telemetry and trace anchoring to aid ops triage for inference regressions. Adds new dashboard and an energy drift alert; sampling defaults to 1%."

payload.body:
Background: We continue to see production traces where streaming responses (SSE) emit JSON fragments split mid-structure and interleaved by heartbeats or auxiliary events. This leads to two classes of customer-visible failures: 1) partial JSON objects being forwarded to SDKs which then throw parse errors / discard tokens; 2) event delimiters ("\n\n"/event markers) being duplicated or stuck to the next payload and breaking client reassembly heuristics. Motivation: Previous PRs addressed chunk coalescing and delimiter ordering but did not prevent a pathological case where a delimiter byte sequence becomes 'sticky' to the following event after a retry/backpressure window, or where sequence holes allow reordering when small windows are replayed. This PR proposes a defensive sanitizer at the SSE boundary plus a lightweight reassembly index to guarantee idempotent reconstruction of JSON frames and preserve function/tool-call sentinels.

What this change does (single-string summary): Adds an SSE boundary sanitizer that normalizes trailing delimiters, a sequence-hole detector that rejects out-of-order apply windows and requests replay, a small reassembly index for ongoing streams to ensure JSON object boundaries are not emitted until complete, and targeted SDK compatibility tweaks to avoid raising parse errors for temporarily incomplete structured outputs.

Implementation highlights: - sse/parser.go: introduce boundarySanitizer that trims repeating delimiters, collapses \r/\n variants, and tags frames with a local assembly id. - sse/stream_manager.go: add per-stream reassemblyIndex and hole detection (lastSeenSeq) which triggers a gated replay path when seq mismatch detected. Replay path is conservative: re-request missing chunks from the producer, reapply cached partials. - sdk/python/openai_compat/streaming.py: tolerate "incomplete-json" interim tokens by buffering until the server emits an assembly-commit marker; previously the SDK raised JSONDecodeError. - tests/sse_fuzz_test.go + tests/integration/sse_replay_test.py: new deterministic fuzz harness and an integration test that simulates delimiters split at UTF-8 boundaries, heartbeat interleaves, and backpressure-triggered replays. - docs/sse-framing.md: new doc describing the sanitizer heuristics and runtime knobs (sanitizer.threshold, replay.window, assembly.commit-timeout).

Why this approach: Conservative server-side enforcement avoids pushing parsing complexity into every SDK and reduces noisy client errors. The reassembly index is intentionally small (per-stream, bounded by 32 partial frames) to keep memory overhead minimal. The sanitizer heuristics are tunable and guided by production traces included in the linked Linear items.

Compatibility notes: - Minted a short-lived assembly marker (\u0002ASSEMBLY_COMMIT\u0002) in the SSE stream that SDKs will ignore as a control sentinel but use to flush buffered frames. This marker is additive and does not alter existing valid streams. - Backwards-compatible: servers will not drop or mutate user payload bytes; we only reorder/emulate replays when we detect missing sequence windows.
1) introduce sse boundary sanitizer, reassembly index and tests (A. Park)
2) add SDK buffering for assembly commit sentinel and update docs (A. Park)
3) fix race in stream_manager reapply path and add extra logging (A. Park)
4) adjust flakey test timeouts and CI config (Tom Becker)
Marco Singh: Please explain the memory bounds on reassemblyIndex and why 32 was chosen.
Aisha Park: 32 was chosen after analyzing window lengths from production traces; it covers >99.7% of partial sequences without noticeable memory pressure. Tunable (sanitizer.max_partial_frames) if we observe changed distributions.
Elena Ruiz: The assembly-commit sentinel is additive, but can we avoid using a non-printable char? Risk of toolchains stripping control chars.
Aisha Park: We considered printable markers but that risks colliding with user payloads; using a wrapped control sentinel makes accidental collisions extremely unlikely. SDKs ignore unknown control sentinels except the exact assembly marker.
Tom Becker: CI caught a race on reapply that we observed locally too. Can you add a retry backoff metric?
Aisha Park: Added stream.replay.retry_count and replay.backoff_ms as counters/gauge in the last commit.
Marco Singh (approval): Looks good with the sanitized heuristics and tests. Approving pending minor docs tweak.
Elena Ruiz (approval): Approved after we moved the sentinel constant to a central compat package.
Fixes for SSE streaming that prevent partial JSON emissions and duplicated/sticky delimiters. Adds a server-side sanitizer and conservative replay mechanism to ensure structured outputs and function-call sentinels are emitted only when complete. Includes SDK buffering changes for OpenAI-compat streaming. Backwards compatible; enables runtime knobs for tuning.

payload.body:
Motivation: tool/function-calling workloads increasingly accept file/attachment payloads from third-party clients. We observed two classes of failures in production: (1) malformed/fragmented multipart streams that cause the streaming parser to drop the connection or OOM when client resumes with overlapping offsets; (2) clients that upload compressed archives (zip/tar/gzip) containing large uncompressed payloads which bypass per-file byte limits because limits were applied to compressed size only. This PR introduces a conservative, backwards-compatible set of guardrails to make the OpenAI-compatibility layer and streaming ingestion more robust.

Summary of changes (high level):
- Add streaming reassembly layer that normalizes chunk sequence and rejects overlapping/duplicated ranges with clear structured errors (422/409 mapping) instead of panics. The layer supports resumable uploads by validating a server-side digest and an expected "resume_at" offset in the protocol.
- Implement content-type sniffing using a lightweight signature check (magic bytes) for commonly abused archive formats (zip, tar, gzip, 7z) and image/video containers. We now compute both compressed_size and an estimated_uncompressed_size using heuristics when streaming (for gz/tar) and enforce per-tool uncompressed byte budgets.
- Introduce per-tool policy configuration: max_files_per_call, max_compressed_bytes_per_file, max_uncompressed_bytes_per_file, max_total_uncompressed_bytes. Policies default to permissive but are tunable via the compat layer config and Dedicated/Private runtime flags.
- Add a controlled server-side archive inspection path: small archives are inspected inline; larger archives are offloaded to a temporary local streaming scanner which checks for nested archives, large uncompressed members, and forbidden filetypes. Offload path uses a bounded temp-store and is subject to eviction/backpressure to protect the runtime.
- Improve OpenAI-compat error semantics: return structured error blobs for attachment validation failures with machine-readable reason codes (attachment_too_large, nested_archive, invalid_mime, stream_overlap) and suggested client actions. Map these to compat HTTP codes (413, 415, 422, 409) so existing OpenAI clients get expected behavior.
- Add integration tests that exercise resumable uploads, compressed->uncompressed size estimation, nested archive detection, and error mappings. Tests include a simulated flaky client that intentionally resends overlapping ranges to ensure we fail fast.
- Docs: add a new guide in redwood-docs describing the attachment lifecycle, recommended client upload patterns (use the new resumable headers), and sample error handling for SDKs.

Compatibility notes: the guardrails are additive. Existing clients that do not stream large archives will not observe changes. The resumable header is optional; when absent, we fall back to existing behavior with stricter streaming sanity checks. We intentionally avoid a breaking-change rollout: feature gated behind a runtime flag that is enabled for API-internal dogfooding then gradually flipped for customers.

Testing and CI: unit tests added for the reassembler and sniffers; integration tests added to the e2e suite. One flaky test (integration/archive-offload) failed on first CI run due to a timing race around temp-store eviction; we added a deterministic lease in the test and re-ran. Final CI status: all checks passed.

Operational playbook: when an attachment_too_large or nested_archive error is seen, the recommended steps are: (1) ask client to follow resumable upload flows (SDKs have helpers), (2) if customer needs to send large compressed archives, increase per-tool budgets and enable offload scanner for that org, (3) for suspicious nested archives escalate to security for static scanning.

Files changed summary (high level): streaming reassembly and sniffing in redwood/runtime/streaming; compatibility layer changes in redwood/compat/openai/attachments; per-tool policy config in redwood/api/config; offload scanner and temp-store in redwood/runtime/offload; docs under redwood-docs/guides/attachments.md; tests under integration-tests/attachments.

This PR touches runtime code paths so reviewers: please pay attention to memory accounting in the scanner and the choice of heuristics for uncompressed size estimation.

Related: Linear ENG-3421 (attachment resiliency), ENG-3498 (compat layer error mappings).
Diego Alvarez: Left a couple of comments around edge cases in reassembler.handleResume — what happens when client sends a zero-length chunk with resume_at equal to current offset? Please add a defensive check.
Maya Chen: Added check and unit test to assert zero-length chunks are rejected with 400 + reason=invalid_chunk. Also tightened logging to include upload_id for easier tracing.
Samir Patel: Offload scanner looks good, but please ensure we don't create unbounded goroutines per upload. Suggest using a worker limiter and add a metric for active scanners.
Maya Chen: Added worker limiter and active_scanners gauge; updated tests to assert limiter behaviour.
Rina Kapoor: Approving after changes. Verified error payloads and docs.
Add streaming reassembly and attachment inspection to improve robustness for tool attachments; introduces per-tool attachment budgets and structured error responses for invalid uploads. Backwards-compatible and feature-gated.
payload.title: streaming archive reassembly and content-type sniffing guardrails for tool attachments

payload.body:
Context and motivation: We observed a class of incidents where simultaneous small spikes across two regions caused oscillations in regional failover decisions, leading to cascading circuit flips and transient SLO breaches for 95th+ latency. Existing backoff and tenant-priority heuristics mitigated some cases but did not prevent quick cross-region thrash when health signals were noisy. This PR introduces a coordinated lightweight mitigation we call 'surge sneeze' — a short-lived, conservative admission and sync fallback designed to stop cascading state churn and allow KV caches + warmups to converge.
- services/scheduler: new surge sneeze state machine with thresholds based on rolling 1m/5m tail latency, error rate deltas, and in-flight queue growth. The machine emits 'sneeze_start', 'sneeze_extend', 'sneeze_end' events and sets a short candidate lock to avoid repeated re-entrance.
- controlplane coordinator: when a sneeze is active in a region, we preferrably route best-effort traffic to neighboring regions that are healthy; we also expose a regional sync fallback that temporarily reverts to a conservative KV-preservation policy (avoid aggressive evictions).
- api-gateway: adds a transient admission multiplier (0.6 by default) exposed via config to reduce acceptance during sneeze windows for non-critical routes.
- kv-cache: preserve sticky keys during sneeze to speed warmup after region flapping.
- telemetry: new events and tags (sneeze.reason, sneeze.duration_ms, sneeze.initiator) and a Prometheus gauge for active sneezes.
- tests: e2e reproducer that injects small latency spikes in two regions and asserts no more than one global failover within the sneeze window, and that 95th latency recovers within expected bounds.
- docs: operational runbook + dashboard for tracking sneezes and manual rollout guidance.
Revert is safe: feature gated behind runtime flag 'enable_surge_sneeze' defaulting to false for nightlies and enabled in prod after canary. Rollback steps: 1) set enable_surge_sneeze=false in controlplane configmap and reload; 2) scale restart coordinator pod if necessary; 3) monitor sneeze_active Prometheus gauge to ensure value returns to 0. Configmap rollback takes effect within 30s to 2m depending on config reload cadence. No DB migrations involved.
- Unit tests for state transitions and guardrails.
- Integration test with simulated cross-region spike (flaky initially; increased timeouts and added deterministic clock in test harness).
- Canary rollout: enabled for 5% of traffic for first 24 hours, increment to 25% if no regressions, then 100%.
- Telemetry assertions added to alerting to detect unintended long sneeze windows (> 2 minutes) and high rejection rates (> 5% of baseline).
New telemetry: sneeze_active_gauge, sneeze_events counter; dashboard with timeline and per-region breakdown. Alerts: SNOOZE-01 (sneeze_stuck) fires if sneeze_active_gauge > 1 for 10 minutes; SNOOZE-02 (sneeze_rejection_spike) fires if admission rejections attributable to sneeze exceed 5% sustained over 5m. Runbook added in docs/operational/surge_sneeze.md.
Benchmarks (staging controlled test): under dual-region 30% request spike over 60s, baseline caused two regional failovers and a 40% increase in 95th latency; with surge sneeze enabled, we saw 1 failover-less oscillation and 12% lower 95th on average. CPU overhead negligible (tiny state machine + counters); memory impact: KV-preservation increases transient memory retention for sticky keys (~1-3% per region in worst-case).
- Default runtime flag: enable_surge_sneeze=false (nightly), enabled in prod after canary.
- Config knobs exposed: sneeze_min_error_delta, sneeze_min_cohort_size, sneeze_admission_multiplier, sneeze_max_duration_ms.
- Suggested defaults: 3%, 1000, 0.6, 120000.
- Escalation: if SNOOZE-01, set enable_surge_sneeze=false and investigate region health signals; see runbook for deeper steps.
- Arjun: 'Can we ensure the sneeze can't be triggered by routine autoscaling transient? Suggest adding a minimum delta threshold on 5m error rate change.'
- Maya: 'Added a minimum delta filter (3% error-rate delta) and a cohort size check so tiny tenants don't trigger global sneeze. See commit 3a7b2f.'
- Lena: 'Telemetry looks good; please add correlation id on sneeze events for trace linking.'
- Maya: 'Added correlation id and unit test; pushed.'
- Tom: 'Integration test flaky on CI (timing). Suggest deterministic clock; also please document config knobs and safe defaults.'
- Maya: 'Reworked test harness to use deterministic clock and reduced flakiness; updated docs with default values and canary plan.'
- Arjun: 'Approved after verifying metrics and simulated load locally.'
- Lena: 'Approved.'
- Tom: 'Approved once CI green.'
CI initially failed a single e2e due to timing; test harness updated to use deterministic clock and the e2e passed on retry. Lint and unit tests green. Load test job (staging-load-2) ran and reported median 95th-latency improvement of ~12% during controlled spike when sneeze was allowed to run vs baseline emergency failover. All checks green at merge time.
Adds a coordinated surge mitigation mechanism ("surge sneeze") that triggers lightweight regional sync fallback and transient admission throttles to stabilize tail latency under multi-region traffic spikes. No customer-visible API changes.
This PR implements a conservative, observable mitigation for cross-region spike-induced oscillations. The 'surge sneeze' reduces admission briefly while preserving KV cache, avoiding repeated failovers and smoothing SLO impact. Feature gated, well-tested, and merged with telemetry and runbook in place.
payload.title: introduce-surge-sneeze-and-regional-sync-fallback

payload.body:
Context and motivation: Mixed-length traffic in customer workloads causes large padding inefficiencies when using fixed bucketing or single-window continuous batching. Prior PRs implemented static bucketing and slot-duration batching, but we still see suboptimal kernel utilization when short and long sequences interleave. This PR introduces a variable-window cohort packing heuristic that forms transient cohorts using a small lookahead window and a seqlen-aware cost model. Motivation: reduce padding tokens across the common long-tail of sequence lengths, improve kernel alignment (so kernels process similarly shaped tensors), and maintain SLOs for p50/p95/p99 latency.

Design summary: Implemented a cohort_packer that buffers incoming requests for a variable delta (configurable: default 8ms max lookahead) and groups them into cohorts by a lightweight seqlen cost heuristic. The heuristic computes an expected padding cost and a kernel-alignment benefit score; cohorts are closed when marginal cost of adding a request exceeds a threshold or when the lookahead timer fires. A smoothing factor prevents starving long requests: if a request exceeds a seqlen threshold it gets a higher urgency weight, which reduces its maximum wait time. The packer integrates with the existing continuous batcher by emitting micro-batches aligned to kernel-friendly shapes.

Runtime and kernel changes: Added kernel selection hints from cohort metadata so the kernel_selector can prefer fused kernels (e.g., grouped attention fast path) when cohort variance is low. Added a small KV cache warm-start hint that tags cohorts containing continuation requests; runtime can prefetch KV segments for those cohorts to avoid cold-cache spikes. The scheduler slot_prioritizer receives cohort urgency scores to decide slot assignment order to avoid head-of-line blocking.

Files and high-level diffs: Summaries of the nine modified files: cohort_packer.cpp/.h (new core heuristic, config parsing, tests hooks), slot_prioritizer.cpp (uses cohort urgency to prioritize), kernel_selector.cpp (adds hint processing and a small selection rule), kv_warm_hint.cpp (attach warm-start metadata to cohorts), microbench harness and example runner, rollout config, and a short doc explaining the runtime flag. No public API changes.

Commits (high-level):
- feat(cohort): initial variable-window cohort packer implementation and tests
- perf(batcher): integrate cohort packer with continuous batcher and add kernel hints
- feat(kv): kv warm-start hint plumbing and unit tests
- perf(scheduler): integrate cohort urgency into slot prioritizer
- test(bench): microbench for mixed seqlen workload and CI benchmark job
- docs: rollout guide and tuning notes

Performance experiments: Benchmarked on p4d-like cluster using mixed synthetic workload (short=8–16 tokens, medium=64–128, long=512–1024) and a production-sampled trace. Results on our perf cluster: median padding tokens per batch reduced by ~22% on synthetic mix and ~18% on production trace; token cost reduced 8–12% depending on model; overall throughput increased 6–9% for mixed workloads. P99 latency improved up to 15% in congestion scenarios due to urgency weighting and reduced head-of-line blocking. KV-warm hints reduced KV miss spikes for continuation-heavy cohorts by ~30%.

Testing and CI: Added unit tests for the cohort closure logic, fuzz tests for edge windows, and an end-to-end microbenchmark that runs in CI (marked flaky on first run and rerun automatically). CI initially reported a flaky benchmark timeout; retriggering the job passed and the PR shows final CI status as pass.

Rollout plan: Feature gated by runtime flag `enable_variable_cohorting` and rollout config in configs/rollouts. Canary rollout to 5% of serving nodes for three days, then 25% if error and latency budgets hold, then 100%. Observability: added cohort-level metrics (cohort_size, avg_padding, avg_wait_ms, kv_warm_hits) and tracing tags for cohort_id to help perf debugging.

Review notes and discussion (summary):
- Reviewer Miguel: requested clarification on starvation bounds and suggested explicit max-wait enforcement for long sequences; addressed by urgency weight and added tests.
- Reviewer Priya: asked for more telemetry; added cohort-level metrics and a small dashboard query in docs.
- Reviewer Liam: requested kernel selection API to remain advisory (non-blocking); adjusted kernel_selector to treat cohort hints as soft preferences.
- Post-approval: small follow-up perf tweak to default lookahead from 12ms to 8ms after canary showed slight latency bump on very bursty workloads.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc inline (docs/running/variable_cohorting.md)
- [x] Unit tests and microbench
- [x] CI green (after rerun)
- [x] Rollout config and metrics
- [x] No public API breaking changes

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main on 2026-02-25 after approvals.

Notes for follow-ups: Evaluate interplay with existing seqlen bucketing when both are enabled (there is a small compatibility note in docs), and consider exposing an adaptive lookahead controller in a later PR that tunes the window based on observed arrival variance.
Introduce a variable-time-window cohort packing heuristic that groups incoming requests into short-lived cohorts based on observed sequence-length distribution and a small lookahead buffer; reduces padding and improves kernel alignment for mixed-length workloads. Backwards-compatible toggle via runtime flag and rollout config.
payload.title: variable-window cohort packer: lookahead cohorting for seqlen-aware continuous batching

payload.body:
Motivation: Tenants frequently override batching/caching defaults and shipping quantization profiles is brittle. This PR introduces 'cost-handyman' — a small orchestration binary and library that assembles tenant-facing defaults (batch shapes, cache window, prefill thresholds) and exports deterministic, versioned quantization profile bundles (JSON + proto) for downstream runtime and Dedicated/Private installers.

Summary: Adds an assembler service that: 1) merges global defaults, tenant overrides and workload-sampled signals into a canonical defaults manifest; 2) serializes quant profiles and a light checksum for safe rollouts; 3) emits telemetry hooks so Optimize/Console can surface suggested deltas; 4) provides a CLI dry-run and a declarative import endpoint for admin workflows.

What's included (high-level): assembled defaults algorithm with conservative fallthroughs, quant profile serializer (v1 JSON + protobuf schema), CLI (dry-run, push, rollback), SDK helpers for Python/Go to consume assembled manifests, unit economics validator that flags >10% unit-cost regressions vs baseline.

Migration notes: Runtime will continue to accept legacy presets but will prefer a manifest annotated with manifest_version:1 produced by cost-handyman. During rollout we will enable the manifest consumer behind 'cost_defaults_v2' feature flag. There is a small data-migration job that converts existing tenant overrides to the new manifest shape (included as a one-shot script).

Checklist:
- [x] Core assembler library + tests
- [x] Quant serializer + proto + roundtrip tests
- [x] CLI: dry-run/push/rollback
- [x] Python SDK helpers and docs snippet
- [x] Telemetry hooks + sample dashboard queries
- [x] E2E smoke in staging

CI notes: Integration tests initially failed on the quant roundtrip due to proto mismatch; fixed by tightening the proto schema and bumping the compatibility tests. All CI checks passing on merge.

Risks: Low. Default merge behavior is conservative: the assembler never reduces tenant cache or batch windows by more than a configured percentage without explicit approval. The unit-econ validator blocks automatic pushes that would increase unit cost by >10%.
Luca: Can the assembler preserve tenant overrides that are explicitly pinned? (answered: yes, pinned fields are preserved by merge priority and tested)
Mei: Unit-econ validator blocks push in some noisy workloads; suggest a dry-run-only default for first 48h (author: added a flag and updated workflow to dry-run by default for new tenants)
Omar: Telemetry looks sparse for sampling - can we emit delta histograms? (author: added delta histograms and example dashboard queries)
Mei: Please add a smoke e2e that verifies runtime accepts manifest_version:1 (author: added test and CI target)
Luca: Small nit on CLI help text (author: addressed)
Codeowner bot: package ownership OK for pkg/assembler (approved)
- Introduce cost-handyman: assembler service that composes batching/caching defaults
- Add deterministic quant profile serializer (JSON + protobuf) for safe rollouts
- CLI for dry-run/push/rollback and Python SDK helpers
- Unit-econ validator to guard against >10% unit-cost regressions
- Telemetry hooks and sample dashboard queries for Optimize/Console
Enable feature flag 'cost_defaults_v2' in staging first. Run scripts/migrate-overrides-to-manifest.py with --dry-run and review diffs. Observe telemetry delta histograms for first 72 hours. Ops rollback: use CLI rollback command which is idempotent.

Background: We continue to converge Redwood's chat API with the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions surface so customers can switch between backends with fewer surprises. This PR focuses on two pain points seen in recent toggles: 1) noisy/underdocumented parameter edge cases (stop arrays, role aliases, temperature/top_p interactions) that produced surprising token-level divergence, and 2) intermittent stream reassembly failures when tool/function calls are emitted alongside logprob fragments. Goals: canonicalize and slim the param mapping to a minimal, well-documented set that preserves intent; make stream framing robust to interleaved function-call envelopes and partial logprob deltas; and preserve tool metadata so that downstream toolchains (router/arbiter) can rely on stable fields. Changes: - Param slimification: introduce a canonicalizer that maps OpenAI-style params to Redwood runtime flags. Resolves ambiguities around stop arrays vs stop regex lists, merges role aliases (assistant/system/user) and rejects deprecated param combinations (e.g., presence_penalty + penalize_role simultaneously) with clear warnings. - Stop/logprob handling: normalize stop priority by length then explicit weighting; ensure logprob fragments emitted as part of framed JSON envelopes are re-anchored to the token index from the canonicalized request. We also add a fallback heuristic to emit a full token logprob snapshot when deltas are discontinuous. - Stream resiliency: make the framers idempotent for repeated fragments and add a lightweight heartbeat sentinel to prevent stalled consumer reads (configurable per-route). Partial frames that include fn_call/tool metadata are now buffered and merged deterministically. - Tool/function routing metadata: tool calls coming from model responses now include a stable routing key derived from tool_id + semantic_hash so platform routing can shard deterministically. The OpenAI-compat wrapper attaches this metadata in the outbound framed JSON without changing user-visible tool payloads. - Tests & docs: new integration tests that simulate interleaved toolcalls + logprob chunks, and docs example for the /v1/chat.completions compatibility matrix. Checklist: - [x] Add canonicalizer code and unit tests - [x] Stabilize stream framer and add heartbeat sentinel - [x] Preserve and attach routing metadata for tool calls - [x] Integration tests for interleaved fragments - [x] Update compat docs and changelog Rollout plan: merged to main behind a feature flag (compat.chatv1_stream_v2). We will enable route-by-route, monitor token-level regressions via Redwood Optimize evals, and roll forward full default only after 2 days of stable metrics on canary routes. Backcompat: default behavior unchanged until feature flag flip; warnings are emitted to logs for deprecated param combos. CI: initial run failed due to flaky integ test (stream reassembly) — fixed by adding a 10ms jitter coalescer on the test harness and re-ran. CI now green. Why this matters: customers switching between Redwood hosted models and OpenAI-compatible endpoints reported subtle differences in stop-handling and occasional truncated tool JSON blobs during streaming. This PR reduces those divergences and makes the stream protocol more fault-tolerant without exposing new surface area.
Ariella Chen: Please add a unit test for stop priority when overlapping stop sequences are present.
Evan Morales: Added test case stop_priority_overlap in stop_normalizer_test.go — PTAL.
Marcus Beaumont: Framer change looks good but add a comment documenting idempotency guarantees and the sentinel format.
Evan Morales: Comment added in framer.go; expanded docstring and included sequence diagrams in docs/compat-matrix.md.
Priya Kothari: Can we make the routing_key derivation stable across restarts? Concern about non-determinism for shard placement.
Evan Morales: routing_key uses tool_id + stable semantic_hash (sha256 truncated) and a version byte; documented in tool_routing.go and added a deterministic-seed test.
Marcus Beaumont: CI flaky integration fixed by harness jitter — approve once CI passes.
Improve OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parameter mapping and streaming stability: canonicalize select params, better stop/logprob handling across framed streams, tool routing metadata preserved. No public API breaking changes.
payload.title: chat.v1 param slimification + stream resiliency and tool-routing for OpenAI /v1 parity

payload.body:
Summary: Adds an operator-scoped KMS audit signer service and an RBACv2 policy mapper to ensure audit envelopes are signed with tenant-aware KMS leases while translating legacy operator roles into RBACv2 constraints. Motivation: We need stronger non-repudiation for audit events emitted by control-plane operators that act across tenant boundaries. Current audit logs can be indistinguishable when operators perform cross-tenant maintenance — this PR attaches KMS-backed origin proofs and maps operator identities to RBACv2 temporal/amphibious constraints to limit blast radius. Design: 1) kms-audit-signer: a lightweight service that requests ephemeral, operator-scoped KMS leases, signs an audit envelope (protobuf) with the lease-derived key handle, and attaches a signed provenance header (X-Redwood-Audit-Signature, X-Redwood-Audit-KMS-Ref). The signer validates that the operator principal is allowed to request the lease via a policy evaluator before signing. 2) rbacv2-policy-mapper: translation shim that reads existing operator roles and emits RBACv2 assertions (timebound, region-anchored, tenant-scoped) used by the policy enforcer. The mapper supports a simulation mode that logs proposed assertions for 7 days before enforcement. 3) Compatibility: signer falls back to current unsigned envelope when running in legacy mode controlled by feature-flag "operator_kms_audit_signing". Migration: Run mapper in simulation mode for 7 days, monitor policy_simulator metrics and audit_signed:percentage; then flip to enforce per-operator cohorts. Checklist: - [x] Implement KMS lease request flow and short-lived key handles - [x] Audit envelope signing and verification logic - [x] Policy evaluator integration for lease grants - [x] RBACv2 mapper with simulation mode and logging - [x] Unit + integration tests for signer and mapper - [x] End-to-end test against private-installer local cluster - [x] Feature-flag gating and canary rollout plan Testing: Unit tests added for lease lifecycle and envelope verification. Integration tests exercise signer against a fake-kms implementation and validate provenance header format. A small end-to-end smoke test was run in the staging dedicated cluster using 3 operator avatars. CI: One flaky test (pkg/serving/scheduler_test) failed on first run due to timing; rerun succeeded. Rollout plan: 1) Enable feature-flag in staging with mapper in simulation mode. 2) Canary: enable signer and enforce mode for 5% of operator traffic (dedicated canary cluster) and validate signed audit acceptance and policy gate metrics for 48 hours. 3) Ramp to 50% then 100% in 3-day windows. 4) Post-deployment: monitor audit-signature-verification-failures < 0.01% and policy-deny spikes. Security notes: - Lease TTL defaults to 10 minutes and is enforced by the KMS gateway. - Signed audit envelopes include a canonicalized provenance block; verification requires access to KMS public handles and the audit public key registry. - RBAC mapper emits explicit deny rules for cross-region/system-operator actions by default. Observability: New metrics: audit_sign_requests_total, audit_sign_success_total, audit_sign_failure_total, rbac_mapper_suggested_assertions_total, rbac_mapper_enforced_assertions_total. Logs include structured fields: operator_id, tenant_id (if applicable), region_hint, kms_ref, signature_id. Backward compatibility: When feature-flag disabled, behavior is unchanged. Context: During internal beta for Optimize quality gates, we hit a rare deadlock when a gate run is canceled while the eval-harness callback is concurrently finalizing results. This surfaced as gate runs stuck in RUNNING forever (no terminal state), blocking apply/rollout, and caused a near-miss where a canary pipeline sat waiting until manual intervention. Root cause is a lock ordering inversion between (a) GateRun state transitions in Optimize (DB row lock + in-memory mutex keyed by gate_run_id) and (b) cancelation handler that attempted to revoke the eval job and update state while holding the per-run mutex, while the callback path held the DB transaction and attempted to acquire the same mutex to emit completion events. Fix: remove the cross-path mutex dependency by (1) making cancelation idempotent and purely DB-driven, using a single conditional UPDATE that only transitions RUNNING->CANCEL_REQUESTED, (2) moving external side effects (eval-harness revoke + audit event emission) out of the DB transaction, and (3) ensuring the callback finalization path uses compare-and-set semantics and respects CANCEL_REQUESTED by transitioning to CANCELED (with artifacts preserved) instead of writing PASSED/FAILED. Also adds a deterministic regression test that simulates callback + cancel racing under a controllable scheduler and asserts we always reach a terminal state within a bounded time. Post-incident notes: This was first observed in eu-west during GPU scarcity where retries stretched gate duration, increasing the probability of cancel/finish overlap; see incident thread #incidents 1764369002 and support ticket SUP-18487 for timeline. This PR is a hotfix targeted for beta stability and does not change gate policy/threshold behavior.
Behavioral changes: (1) Cancel requests are now represented as a durable intermediate state CANCEL_REQUESTED rather than an in-process flag; (2) The only paths allowed to write terminal states are the callback finalizer and the cancelation reconciler, both using conditional updates on expected prior state; (3) If eval-harness returns success/failure after a cancel request, we record the metrics/artifacts but the gate_run state becomes CANCELED (reason=canceled_by_user or canceled_by_system) to avoid unblocking apply based on results the user intended to cancel. Safety: This maintains defense-in-depth at the apply boundary (apply still requires PASSED or explicit override), while ensuring cancelation cannot wedge the system. Observability: Added a counter for gate_run_cancel_finalize_race_total with tags {resolved_state, path} and a histogram for cancel_reconcile_latency_ms; both are low-cardinality and intended for beta-only dashboards (will keep if useful).
Olivia Grant: The fix makes sense. One question: in the callback finalizer, you’re conditionally updating RUNNING->PASSED/FAILED, but now also checking CANCEL_REQUESTED. Can we end up in CANCEL_REQUESTED forever if revoke fails? Please confirm reconciler covers that case.
Jordan Lee (author): Yep. The reconciler runs on a short interval and moves CANCEL_REQUESTED->CANCELED regardless of revoke outcome (revoke is best-effort). We persist revoke_error in metadata and emit an audit event so oncall can see it, but we never block the terminal transition on external revoke.
Sean Gallagher: Please add a bounded-time assertion in the regression test (no infinite waits) and ensure the test fails deterministically if the scheduler doesn’t progress. We’ve had flakes from concurrency tests.
Jordan Lee (author): Done. Test now uses DeterministicScheduler with an explicit step budget; if terminal state isn’t reached within 200 steps, it fails with a dump of executed tasks and last observed state.
Michael Nguyen: DB-side: The conditional UPDATE introduces a new state value. Did you update the enum / check constraint migration and backfill for existing rows? Also ensure read paths don’t choke on unknown state.
Jordan Lee (author): Added migration to extend the gate_run_state enum with CANCEL_REQUESTED and CANCELED (CANCELED existed logically but wasn’t in the DB enum everywhere). Read paths already treat unknown as RUNNING; updated to treat CANCEL_REQUESTED as running-ish but non-applyable. Also added a small backfill to normalize legacy 'CANCELLED' typo to 'CANCELED'.
Sahana Iyer: CI concern: any changes to the callback signature / retry behavior? I want to ensure eval-harness doesn’t need a coordinated deploy.
Jordan Lee (author): No contract changes. We only changed how we handle callback ordering on our side. Callback payload unchanged. This is safe to roll independently.
Olivia Grant: Approving. Please link the incident note in the PR description so folks can find context later.
Jordan Lee (author): Linked to #incidents thread id in description and added a short internal note under services/optimize/docs/quality_gates_cancelation.md.
Internal beta hotfix: Fixes rare deadlock where canceling a running quality gate could leave it stuck in RUNNING. Gate runs now reliably transition to a terminal state (CANCELED) even when cancel and completion race. Adds regression test to prevent reintroduction.
payload.title: Fix deadlock in quality gate run cancelation + add regression test

Context: As part of Dedicated throughput guarantees, we need first-class SLO alerting that is (a) burn-rate based (fast/slow), (b) scoped per Dedicated deployment, and (c) correctly routed to oncall + CS escalation paths. This PR adds burn-rate alert rules for the Dedicated Throughput Floor SLO and wires them into our paging policies. It also adds the runbook links and dashboard deep-links to make the alerts actionable. Scope: - New Prometheus rules for Dedicated throughput SLO burn-rate (page + ticket) - Tier-aware routing labels (Standard/Plus/Premium) to support different urgency/paging - Alertmanager routes + PagerDuty service mapping (SRE oncall; non-page tickets to #customer-success triage) - Annotations: customer/deployment identifiers, region, model, and links to the Dedicated Throughput dashboard panels - Guardrails: suppress alerts when deployment is in provisioning/warmup window or explicitly marked 'customer_throttled' by admission-control telemetry Notes: The burn-rate computations follow the SLO Toolkit conventions (fast: 2h window, slow: 24h window) but are implemented using Redwood’s in-repo rule templates to avoid an additional dependency at runtime. Related: ENG-19244 (metric emission), ENG-19257 (tier-aware admission control).
Rafael Mendes (review): Can you confirm these are burn-rate alerts (multi-window, multi-burn) and not just thresholding on tokens/sec? We should avoid paging on transient dips if error budget isn’t burning.

Aisha Bello (author): Yep. The rule fires on burn rate of the SLO ratio (good/total over windows). Fast path is 2h window, slow path is 24h; page requires both fast+slow burn to reduce noise. The underlying SLI is still tokens/sec floor vs observed, but we alert on the error-budget burn.

Sean Gallagher (review): Please link the canonical SLO name/id in the annotations so SLO reporting can join on it. Also, can we add explicit exclusions for (1) provisioning/warm pool period and (2) customer-side throttling / 429s?

Aisha Bello (author): Added `slo_id: dedicated.throughput_floor` annotation + updated the suppressor to ignore the first 20m after `deployment_ready=true`. For customer throttling, I added a suppression predicate when `dedicated_admission_denied_total{reason="customer_quota"}` dominates and `request_rate` is below committed (i.e., they aren’t sending).

Allison Grant (review): Routing: for now, please keep all pages going to SRE PD. If we want tier-specific paging later, encode tier as a label but don’t create multiple PD services until we see volume.

Aisha Bello (author): Ack. I kept a single PD service (`pd-sre-primary`) and added `tier` label purely for context + future routing. Ticket route goes to Slack triage channel + creates Opsgenie ticket via webhook.

Sergio Costa (review): Dashboard deep-link should land on the per-deployment panel with deployment_id pre-filtered. Also: use the public dashboard slug (not the internal jsonnet path).

Aisha Bello (author): Updated annotations to use `https://console.redwoodinference.com/ops/dedicated/throughput?deployment_id={{ $labels.deployment_id }}` which resolves to the correct panel view.

Rafael Mendes (follow-up): Can you add rule unit tests with a synthetic time series showing a sustained burn vs a transient dip?

Aisha Bello (author): Added promtool-style tests in `tests/alerts/test_dedicated_throughput_rules.py` for (1) sustained under-floor => page, (2) short dip => no page, (3) warmup window => suppressed.

Sean Gallagher (approval): Looks good. One nit: set `severity=page` only for the multiwindow condition; keep the single-window signal as `severity=ticket` to avoid paging on partial data.

Aisha Bello (author): Done (split into `DedicatedThroughputSLOBurnRateHigh` (page) and `DedicatedThroughputSLOBurnRateElevated` (ticket)).

Rafael Mendes (approval): Approved.

Allison Grant (approval): Approved once lint passes.

Motivation: tail latency for interactive requests can spike when prefill and decode stages contend on kernel/kv bandwidth and when large prefills cause decode starvation. This PR introduces a hybrid warmup slice orchestrator that staggers small "warmup" slices to softly prime the KV cache and a decode-slip mitigator that enforces a lightweight pacing budget for decode-stage kernels. The two components are designed to operate together to preserve continuous-batching efficiency while reducing tail spikes and offering operators actionable knobs (warmup budget, slice width, kernel pacing target).

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a WarmupSliceOrchestrator that creates short, high-priority prefetch slices for long prefill requests; these slices prime the KV cache for frequently hit keys without performing full decode work. Warmup slices are cancellable and have configurable budget per-request.
- Introduces a DecodeSlipMitigator that monitors per-GPU decode token throughput and inserts micro-yields (kernel pacing) when decode latency growth exceeds a windowed threshold. This prevents runaway decode kernels from starving pending prefill kernels.
- Exposes two runtime-config flags and one tenant-level tuning param: warmup_budget_tokens, warmup_slice_max_len, decode_pacing_target_ms. Values are surfaced in the runtime config and Redwood Console tuning UI (follow-up UI PR planned).
- Adds continuous-batching hooks so warmup slices are batched with prefill kernels when compatible; when not compatible the orchestrator uses a fast-path small-batch dispatch.
- Conservative defaults: warmup_budget_tokens=64, warmup_slice_max_len=16, decode_pacing_target_ms=4. These provided significant improvement in the internal perf benchmarks for mixed interactive workloads.

Benchmarks & results (internal perf harness, steady-state 24h runs):
- 95th percentile tail latency for interactive mix (median sequence length 64, 20% long prefill requests) reduced by ~32%.
- Median per-token CPU/GPU scheduling jitter reduced ~18% across the candidate cluster.
- End-to-end throughput maintained within 3% of baseline for 95th-percentile throughput configs (small loss due to micro-pacing but improved SLA stability).

Testing & incremental rollout plan:
- Unit tests for orchestrator scheduling logic and DecodeSlipMitigator heuristics.
- Integration perf test with the benchmark-lab harness (added bench script).
- Stage rollout: canary -> regional staging -> full main rollout. Operator flag gates included to disable warmup slices or disable pacing independently.

Related: ENG-3627 (smoother prefill-decode handoff), ENG-3690 (kv warmup strategy). This PR intentionally keeps the policy surface small; later PRs will add console defaults and more adaptive heuristics (entropy-aware warmup).

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for new modules
- [x] Perf harness integration and benchmark result artifact
- [x] Feature-flaggable configuration
- [x] Docs (ops tuning guide) added to docs/ops/prefill-tuning.md

Merge notes: squash merge. See merge commit for aggregated changes and perf artifact link.
Ethan Park: Can you clarify how warmup slices are batched with prefill kernels? It looks like we might double-dispatch for small prefill+warmup cases.
Maya Chen: Warmup slices use a batching affinity token; when prefill kernels have matching affinity they get coalesced. If affinity mismatches, we use a fast-path micro-batch dispatch to avoid double-dispatch overhead.
Liam O'Connor: Mitigator heuristics look reasonable but we should avoid global timers per-GPU for scale. Suggest using the existing sched window sampler—see inline comment.
Maya Chen: Switched to scheduler window sampler for GPU-level throughput stats (addressed in commit 4). Removed per-GPU timer, replaced with sampler callback.
Sofia Alvarez: CI flaky with perf benchmark on first run, re-ran tests and verified stable results. Approving pending small doc tweak.
Maya Chen: Fixed doc wording and added console example. Thanks!

Operators can tune warmup_budget_tokens and decode_pacing_target_ms in runtime_flags; disable warmup via runtime_flags.warmup.enabled=false for safe rollback. Observe metrics kv.warmup_hits and kernel.decode_pacing_events to validate behavior.

Motivation: Customers using structured output and function/tool calling request more robust, composable constraint support beyond the current monolithic implementation. Existing constrained-decoding broke streaming stability in several cases (constraints spanning token boundaries, long-regex patterns, and ambiguous CFG rules). This PR introduces a pluggable constrained-sampling backend interface and two reference implementations (CFG and regex) plus a tokenizer-safety layer to prevent constraint logic from being invalidated by tokenizer splits. Summary of changes: adds a ConstrainedBackend interface, implements GrammarBackend (nearley-inspired runtime) and RegexBackend (incremental DFA checks), introduces TokenizerSafety middleware to normalize constraints vs tokenizer tokenization, updates the OpenAI-compat layer to surface constraint errors early, and adds end-to-end streaming tests and benchmarks. Compatibility notes: Default behavior preserves existing runtime semantics when no constraints are supplied; operators can opt into the new backends via config. Streaming notes: validators now run incrementally on partial tokens and on new decoder tokens; when a backend signals impossible constraints we gracefully emit a structured error and fallback to the configured policy (fallback_model or unconstrained decode). Security and perf: RegexBackend compiles patterns to bounded DFAs and enforces a max-state budget to avoid exponential blowups; GrammarBackend compiles to a guarded form with a static limit on lookahead. Tests: unit + integration + new e2e tests for streaming + tokenizer edge cases. Linear tickets: ENG-1248 (pluggable constrained backends), ENG-1302 (tokenizer-safety for constraint validation).

Motivation and summary: We observed rare streaming stalls and malformed structured outputs when constrained decoding (hybrid CFG + regex) encountered decoder-side backpressure during high-concurrency workloads. Root causes: (1) priority arbitration between regex and CFG backends allowed mid-token rewrites to be applied after partial token flushes to the stream, (2) tokenizer escape sequences split across subtoken boundaries were not reconciled when constraints requested insertions or rewrites, and (3) the streaming path did not have a consistent stall/resume protocol with the decoding kernel, which led to partial outputs being emitted and then corrected out-of-band. This PR introduces a coordinated backpressure protocol between the decoder and streamer, a constraint-priority arbitration shim that guarantees atomic application of rewrites at subtoken boundaries, and a tokenizer escape reconciliation pass that normalizes escapes before constraint matching. Design highlights: - Add DecoderStreamBackpressureManager to signal stall/resume and to hold partially emitted subtokens until constraints are applied. - Implement PriorityArbiter to deterministically merge CFG and regex backends using a ranked policy that avoids last-moment substitutions during emission. - Introduce TokenEscapeReconciler that coalesces escape sequences across subtokens into canonical forms for constraint checking. - Expose new decoder flags: enable_backpressure_coordinator (opt-in), constraint_priority_policy (ranked|last-wins|cfg-first), preescape_normalization (true|false). Testing and rollout: unit tests for tokenization edgecases, E2E tests with streaming clients and synthetic backpressure injected, and perf regression tests to ensure <2% p95 latency impact. Rollout plan: feature flags default to off; staged enablement for canary clusters, then 20% traffic, monitored via new metrics introduced below. Related artifacts and links: linear tasks ENG-3210 (regression triage), ENG-3284 (priority arbiter), SUP-4412 (customer report #1143). Checklist: - [x] Add unit tests for TokenEscapeReconciler - [x] Add integration tests for streaming under backpressure - [x] CI green on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 - [x] Docs entry in API compat notes for opt-in flags - [x] Rollout playbook entry for staged enablement Backwards compatibility: No changes to existing public API; behavior is opt-in. Edge cases considered: multi-byte unicode escapes, mixed UTF-8+BPE tokenizer hybrids, function-call delimiters crossing subtoken boundaries. See files_changed for implementation locations and small illustrative snippets.
Improve stability of streaming constrained decoding under backpressure.
Better reconciliation of tokenizer escape sequences across regex/CFG constraint boundaries.
No API surface changes; opt-in via decoder config flags.

Priya Nair: I'm worried about p95 regressions; show me perf numbers. Author: Added benchmark results to the PR and gated on flag; observed 0.9% p95 token latency increase in worst-case synthetic load.
Miguel Santos: Add more tests for mixed BPE/byte-tokenizers. Author: Added additional tokenization fixtures and a failing-to-passing test case to the suite.
QA (Luca Moretti): Found a race in stream resume path under slow clients; fixed in 3c7b9a8 commit.

Motivation: Multiple SDKs exposed slightly different streaming / iterator ergonomics and had several modal token refresh behaviors that caused blocking stalls during long-lived streams. This PR unifies the consumer-facing async iterator surface across Python/TypeScript/Go, introduces a nonblocking reauth shim that refreshes tokens opportunistically in the background and falls back to a short-lived reauth handshake only when necessary, tightens default retry/backoff settings for streaming reconnects, and applies minor semver bumps across SDKs.

The goals are: 1) avoid user-visible stalls during token rotation on long streams; 2) provide consistent iterator behavior and simpler migration; 3) ship small compatibility-safe version bumps.

Changes:
- Add background token refresher (nonblocking) to each SDK client; exposes a configuration hook (token_refresh_window_ms) and a guard that prevents concurrent blocking reauths.
- Rework async iterator/shim in Python to return an AsyncGenerator that implements a .cancel() handle and consistent error translation.
- Align the TypeScript AsyncIterable protocol to yield TypedEvent objects (same shape as Python and Go) and improve stream backpressure by batching small frames.
- Fix a go-stream sink leak that kept goroutines alive when the consumer dropped the iterator; add a pooled context cancel pattern.
- Normalize default retry/backoff to an exponential cap with jitter and shorter initial retry for 401->reauth flows.
- Bump versions: python -> 2.8.0, typescript -> 1.9.0, go -> 0.12.1.

Migration notes:
- Most users will not need to change call sites. If you relied on the old streaming error types, switch to the TypedEvent union; a compatibility shim is provided for one release.
- If you implemented custom token rotation by intercepting low-level sockets, opt into token_refresh_window_ms or disable background refresh.

- [x] Add unit + integration tests for long-lived streams and auth rotation

payload.body:
Motivation: Under certain mixed workloads we observed tail-latency spikes and increased fragmentation when the paged KV cache accumulated low-utilization slabs that were never reclaimed aggressively. This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: 1) a hinted KV block cycler that incrementally promotes eviction on blocks tagged by runtime heuristics, and 2) a lazy slab sanitizer that performs low-cost in-place compaction and inconsistency checks during quiet CPU cycles. The combination reduces fragmentation and amortizes reclamation work without harming p99 latency.

Design & assumptions: The cycler receives lightweight hints from the scheduler and serving runtime (miss counters, inter-request gaps, and occupancy heat markers). Hinted blocks are placed on a prioritized circular queue (cycler ring) where aging promotes eviction eligibility, but they are not forcibly unpinned; instead the allocator will prefer these blocks for reuse when creating new allocations. The lazy slab sanitizer watches for under-utilized slabs (below a configurable occupancy threshold) and performs gentle compaction steps: moving live entries to neighboring blocks where possible, repairing small allocation metadata inconsistencies, and emitting metrics if repairs exceed a tolerance. Sanitizer work is strictly throttled by a CPU budget token so it only runs in less busy windows.

What changed (summary): Implemented cycler ring data structure, hook points in the scheduling pipeline to emit hints, allocator preference logic to consume hinted blocks first, and a background lazy_slab_sanitizer worker with adaptive backoff. Added unit tests for cycler behavior, integration tests simulating mixed read/write workloads, and a small e2e perf harness used in the canary cluster. Updated docs for tuning knobs (cycler.window_ms, sanitizer.occupancy_threshold, sanitizer.cpu_budget_ms).

Commits: 
- 3f8b2a1: introduce cycler ring and basic enqueue/dequeue semantics
- 8d9c4f0: wire scheduler hint emission and lightweight telemetry aggregation
- b27f1de: allocator: prefer hinted blocks and add allocation scoreboard
- a4c91e3: lazy_slab_sanitizer worker and compaction primitives
- d1e4ab9: tests + perf harness + docs

Files touched (high-level): 
- runtime/kv/cycler.cc (new) 
- runtime/kv/cycler.h (new) 
- runtime/kv/allocator.cc (modified): consume hinted blocks path, allocation scoreboard
- runtime/kv/sanitizer.cc (new) 
- runtime/scheduler/hints.cc (modified): emit hints based on request patterns
- tests/kv/cycler_test.cc (new)
- tests/kv/sanitizer_integration_test.py (new)
- docs/ops/kv_tuning.md (modified)

Review conversation (high level): 
- Diego Alvarez: "Overall looks good; two main asks: add a safety metric for sanitizer-induced copying and make sure cycler hints cannot starve optimistic reuse paths."
- Maya Chen (author): "Added sanitizer.copy_bytes metric and a sanitizer.max_copy_bytes_per_window config; cycler now sets a soft TTL per-entry to avoid indefinite deprioritization of blocks."
- Priya Nair: "Can you add a deterministic unit test for the ring wrap case and a CI job exercising sanitizer under high concurrency?"
- Maya Chen: "Added cycler_test for wrap and a lightweight high-concurrency integration test; heavy stress runs tracked in attached perf harness (not in CI)."
- Evan Brooks: "Minor: please document knobs in docs/ops/kv_tuning.md and include suggested defaults for Dedicated and Hosted tiers."
- Maya Chen: "Docs updated; defaults: cycler.window_ms=5000, sanitizer.occupancy_threshold=0.22, sanitizer.cpu_budget_ms=10 per core."

CI & checks: 
- unit (linux) — pass
- integration (small) — pass
- lint — pass
- perf-canary — initial run flagged a small regression on a synthetic write-heavy workload (p50 unchanged, p99 up ~5%); reran with sanitizer off-by-default in canary and adjusted sanitizer backoff heuristics; final canary run passed.

Benchmarks: 
- Mixed read/write synthetic (50/50 at 8k qps): net reduction in allocator fragmentation metric by ~38%, average memory overhead down ~12MB per node, and CPU cost of sanitizer approx 3% of spare cycles in steady state. Observed 7-12% reduction in allocation latencies in high-churn scenarios.

Migration & ops notes: 
- The sanitizer is off by default in hosted for the first rollout. Operators can enable via runtime flag sanitizer.enabled=true. The cycler is safe to enable by default because it only changes preference heuristics and does not force evictions. Tuning guidance in docs/ops/kv_tuning.md.

Release notes: 
- Introduces hinted KV block cycler to reduce fragmentation under mixed workloads.
- Adds lazy slab sanitizer that performs safe low-cost in-place compaction.
- New tuning knobs: cycler.window_ms, sanitizer.occupancy_threshold, sanitizer.cpu_budget_ms.

Risks & mitigation: 
- Risk: sanitizer could increase p99 if aggressive; mitigation: default off in hosted canary, strict CPU budget and backoff, explicit safety metrics to auto-disable if regressions detected.
- Risk: incorrect hinting could delay reuse of useful blocks; mitigation: soft TTL on hints and fallback to normal allocation after TTL.

Merge outcome: Approved by reviewers after two rounds of changes. All CI checks green on final run. Squash-merged into main by Diego Alvarez on 2026-02-24.

Diego Alvarez: Overall looks good; two main asks: add a safety metric for sanitizer-induced copying and make sure cycler hints cannot starve optimistic reuse paths.
Maya Chen: Added sanitizer.copy_bytes metric and sanitizer.max_copy_bytes_per_window; cycler sets a soft TTL per-entry.
Priya Nair: Can you add a deterministic unit test for the ring wrap case and a CI job exercising sanitizer under high concurrency?
Maya Chen: Added cycler_test for wrap and a lightweight high-concurrency integration test; heavy stress runs in perf harness.
Evan Brooks: Minor: please document knobs and include suggested defaults for Dedicated and Hosted tiers.
Maya Chen: Docs updated; defaults included.
Diego Alvarez: LGTM after tests and docs. Approving.
Priya Nair: Approve.
Evan Brooks: Approve.
Adds hinted KV block cycler to prioritize reuse of low-utilization blocks and a lazy slab sanitizer for safe in-place compaction. Default sanitizer disabled for hosted canary; operators can tune via new knobs.
Sanitizer off by default in hosted rollout. Enable via sanitizer.enabled=true. Recommended defaults: cycler.window_ms=5000; sanitizer.occupancy_threshold=0.22; sanitizer.cpu_budget_ms=10 per core. Monitor sanitizer.copy_bytes and allocator.fragmentation metrics.
Mixed 50/50 workload: ~38% fragmentation reduction, ~12MB/node memory reduction, sanitizer CPU ~3% of spare cycles, 7-12% lower allocation latency in high-churn scenarios.
