payload.body:
Context: During perf characterization + Hosted canary for runtime 1.21, we saw a p99 regression on long-context workloads (>=16k prompt tokens) on L40S and some A100 pools when kernel auto-selection v2 classified certain requests into the “mid” prefill bucket and chose FA3 prefill variants that are great for short/mid contexts but showed allocator/workspace churn at long context (and worse tail when batch composition is mixed). This PR tightens the v2 rules to prevent mis-selection in the long-context regime while keeping determinism guarantees and preserving the gains on short/mid prompts. Changes: (1) Adjust prefill-length bucket boundaries and add a small hysteresis band to reduce flip-flopping around thresholds when scheduler-provided distribution hints are noisy. (2) Add an explicit long-context guard: for ctx >= LONG_CTX_TOKENS (default 12288), prefer the “lc_prefill” kernels when available, otherwise fall back to the known-stable v1-equivalent prefill path. (3) Add SKU-aware exception for L40S where the problematic kernel variant was disproportionately impacting tail; we now require a stricter threshold before selecting it and we prefer the stable alternative when decode_len is small (prefill-dominant requests). (4) Add unit tests covering boundary conditions + replay determinism around bucket edges, including cases with mixed scheduler hints. Bench results: See attached before/after plots from perf suite run 2026-02-14 and canary replay slice. Summary on L40S (long-context summarization profile, 16k/256): p95 1.38s -> 1.11s (-19.6%), p99 2.74s -> 1.63s (-40.5%). On A100 (same profile): p95 1.02s -> 0.98s (-3.9%), p99 1.88s -> 1.61s (-14.4%). No correctness diffs observed (golden outputs match within expected nondeterminism bounds; selection remains deterministic for fixed inputs). Notes: This is intended as a targeted rule tweak; no changes to telemetry schema. Rollout: safe to land in release/1.21 behind existing gates; recommended to promote to Hosted canary first, then Dedicated pools after 24h with the rollout dashboard guardrails. Artifacts/plots: Before/after plot bundle: gs://redwood-perf-artifacts/kernel-select-v2/28522-longctx-prefill-thresholds/plots/index.html ; Comparison table: gs://redwood-perf-artifacts/kernel-select-v2/28522-longctx-prefill-thresholds/summary.csv . Checklist: [x] Adds/updates unit tests for bucket boundaries and long-context guard [x] Verifies selector determinism tests still pass [x] Runs perf suite subset (Llama/Mistral long-context + mixed) on A100 + L40S [x] Confirms no telemetry cardinality changes [x] Updates release/1.21 notes comment (see thread) to mention long-context fix (internal) [x] Linked SUP-31842 for traceability
Hiro Tanaka (review): The guard looks right, but I’m worried about thrash around the boundary when scheduler hints are “mostly long” but a single request is 8–10k. Can we ensure we don’t oscillate between kernels within the same warm pool? Also please justify the 12288 default. Yuki Sato (author): Added hysteresis band using a two-threshold approach when distribution_hint is present (enter long_ctx at 12k, exit at 10k) to reduce oscillation. Default 12288 matches the prefill workspace knee we saw in perf plots across L40S and A100; linked plot bundle in description. Lena Fischer (review): For mixed workloads, can you include decode_len in the guard? Some of the worst spikes were prefill-dominant. Yuki Sato: Updated rule ordering so the long_ctx guard checks (ctx_tokens >= 12288 && decode_tokens <= 512) before the generic bucket-based choice, which matches the spike signature. Omar El-Sayed (review): Please confirm we’re not changing telemetry cardinality; last week’s incident thread was noisy. Also add a log-only counter for how often this guard triggers so we can validate during rollout. Yuki Sato: No schema changes. Added a single aggregated counter kernel_select_v2.long_ctx_guard_triggered (no extra tags beyond existing model_family/gpu_sku/region sampling policy). Marcus Reed (review): Bench numbers look good, but I’d like to see at least one run on Qwen long-context profile as well. Yuki Sato: Added Qwen2.5-14B long-context run results to the same artifact bundle; deltas are neutral-to-positive (p99 -9% on L40S). Allison Grant (review): Can we add a short note to release/1.21 internal notes so oncall knows this is the fix for SUP-31842? Yuki Sato: Added a brief entry under “Kernel selection v2” in the internal known-issues/release notes file. Approvals: Hiro (approved), Lena (approved), Omar (approved), Marcus (approved).
Internal: Kernel auto-selection v2 adjusts long-context prefill thresholds/guard to prevent tail-latency spikes on long-context, prefill-dominant workloads (notably L40S). No user-facing config changes; controlled via existing feature gate.

Introduces a wave-based swap conductor that performs phased traffic handoffs with an embedded circuit-breaker heuristic and automatic rollback triggers. Improves safety of multi-wave canaries and reduces blast radius for model swaps.
Context: Large model swaps have been brittle for stateful session workloads and high-concurrency routes. Existing cohort canaries either move too fast or require manual gating. This PR implements a wave-phased swap conductor that coordinates a sequence of controlled swap waves, observes safety signals, and engages a circuit-breaker that halts progress and executes automated rollback heuristics when prespecified thresholds are breached. Design: The conductor maintains a lightweight state machine (WAVE_IDLE -> WAVE_IN_PROGRESS -> WAVE_VALIDATION -> WAVE_COMMIT) and a sliding safety window that evaluates multiple signals (P50/P95 latency, error-rate, token-quality regression via eval hook, and request-drop). A circuit-breaker with exponential backoff pauses wave advancement and can fast-fail to rollback if sustained violations are observed. Rollback heuristics prefer incremental reversion to the last known-good variant and record a rollback-journal for postmortem playback. Implementation summary: 1) controller/service: new services/rollout/wave_conductor.py implementing the state machine, validation adapters, and circuit-breaker. 2) runtime integration: non-blocking swap path in serving runtime to allow partial route attachment during wave windows. 3) observability: new rollout trace spans, per-wave metrics, and a canary-dashboard view. 4) console: operator UI to visualize wave progression and manually apply or abort waves. 5) CRD updates and helm charts for the new rollout strategy. Testing and validation: unit tests for state transitions, integration canary simulation harness added under tests/integration/test_wave_phasing.py, and performance smoke tests to verify no regression in steady-state latency. CI: integration-canary job runs wave simulations using historical traffic traces. Rollout plan: staged rollout to Dedicated clusters (5% of clusters first) with feature flag rollout.wave_conductor enabled. Early-warning Linear task ENG-4127 tracks production telemetry for 72 hours; auto-disable path present if any cluster shows repeated circuit-breaker activation. Related: builds on work in ENG-3981 (traffic-mirroring abstractions) and complements the recent rollback-journal PR. Checklist: [x] controller + state machine implemented [x] runtime swap hooks added [x] observability and tracing added [x] integration tests and simulation harness [x] docs and operator runbook written. Follow-ups: add continuous eval integration to compare semantic drift for embedding-based rerankers (ENG-4199).
Liam Chen: Can the circuit-breaker thresholds be overridden per-customer? Response: Added per-tenant override and cluster-defaults, documented in CRD.
Sofia Martinez: Suggest adding a sanity check to prevent overlapping waves on a single route. Response: Added mutual exclusion at route-level and a unit test.
Ethan Brooks: Concern about stateful session loss during partial swaps. Response: runtime non-blocking attach path preserves active KV cache; added a migration hook to flush sessions to new variant in opt-in mode.
Sofia Martinez: Please add runbook steps for manual rollback and postmortem extraction. Response: Runbook included under docs/operator/runbooks/wave-phased-swap.md.
Liam Chen: CI flaky on integration-canary when trace collector is slow. Response: added retry and increased timeouts; job retried and passed.
Merged after two approvals. Squash-merged. Post-merge: rollout-sim validation job executed on staging and passed. Feature flag gate enabled for 5% Dedicated rollout.
Operator runbook published, telemetry dashboards added. ENG on-call to monitor ENG-4127 for 72 hours. Follow-up tasks created for continuous eval integration and extended rollback analytics.
Circuit-breaker is conservative by default with cluster-scoped defaults. Per-tenant overrides require admin RBAC. Automatic rollback preserves rollback-journal for replay and forensics. Stateful migration is opt-in to reduce risk.
Add: wave-phased swap conductor (opt-in) with circuit-breaker and automated rollback heuristics. Improves safety for multi-wave canaries and reduces risk during large model swaps.

Motivation: On a number of multi-tenant incidents we observed alert storms triggered by tenant-level token bursts causing noisy paging and masked root causes. This PR introduces two complementary features: 1) Burnview Inspector: a focused observability surface that shows per-tenant token burn over time with breakdown by model variant, stage (prompt vs completion), and hardware tier; and 2) Tenant Alert Throttle: a runtime/alerting shim that rate-limits noisy per-tenant alerts and escalates persistent issues to cross-tenant channels. The PR also adds a lightweight synthetic probe harness that can inject representative invocation traces and cost spikes to validate alert curves and TTLs. High-level changes: added a Burnview API endpoint (observability service) that aggregates prefix/KV cache hit-adjusted token accounting and exposes Prometheus-compatible metrics (redwood_burnview_tenant_tokens_total, redwood_burnview_tenant_tokens_by_stage, redwood_burnview_probe_success), updated tracing spans to add burn.view.{tenant,stage} attributes and a new span kind burn.probe for synthetic probes, introduced a tenant_alert_throttle component in the alerting gateway with per-tenant sliding-window counters and an exponential backoff escalation policy, and added a Grafana dashboard (dashboards/burnview-inspector.json) and alerting rule templates (alerts/burnview-throttle.rules.yaml). Testing: unit tests for aggregation and throttle logic, integration test that replays synthetic probe traces into the observability pipeline, and manual visual QA of the Burnview dashboard. Rollout plan: feature gated by runtime flag observability.burnview.enabled and alert throttle default disabled for 48 hours in canary; monitor burnview_probe_success and alert_rate_reduction metrics before enabling globally. Linear/JIRA: ENG-1912 implements the throttle algorithm; PM-88 tracks dashboard UX. Notes and caveats: the aggregation endpoint currently samples large tenants to preserve query latency; sampling knobs are exposed in config and will be tuned during canary. This change does not alter billing records; token accounting here is for observability only.
Add Burnview Inspector dashboard for token burn analysis and a tenant-scoped alert throttle to reduce noisy alert storms; includes minor Prometheus metric additions and a synthetic probe harness for alert calibration.

Motivation: customers with mixed steady and spiky workloads want more granular committed capacity without committing to full GPU units. This PR introduces a Commitment Fractionalizer that lets Dedicated commitments be expressed in fractional units (e.g., 0.25 of a slot) and a Supply Hysteresis Allocator that smooths cross-zone rebalances to avoid cascading preemptions. This change is gated behind a rollout flag (dedicated.fractional-commitments) and designed to be conservative by default.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a fractionalized commitment model on the reservation ledger and allocator: commitments are stored as fixed-point milli-slots to preserve determinism; admission, headroom and burst accounting are adapted to factor fractional reservations; 2) Implements a supply hysteresis layer in the inter-zone allocator that requires a delta threshold and a minimum stable window before moving fractional supply between zones; 3) Enhances telemetry: new metrics tenant_fractional_committed_{milli_slots}, tenant_effective_utilization_mavg_1m/5m/15m, and supply_age_seconds to reason about aged warm capacity; 4) Introduces a fairness tweak where fractional commitments are rounded only at execution time to nearest device slice to avoid starving tiny tenants; 5) Adds migration tool to convert existing integer commitments to milli-slot representation with a rollback path.

Compatibility and safety: - The fractional model is backwards compatible; integer commitments continue to be honored. - Rollout is opt-in per-cluster via feature flag. - Autoscaler and accounting paths include conservative checks: any bucketed admission that would reduce previously observed headroom below safety thresholds is disallowed. - Extensive unit tests and an integration job simulate mixed workloads (steady batch + microbursts) to verify no SLO regressions.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc (Linear ENG-4492) linked - [x] Unit & integration tests added - [x] Telemetry dashboards updated (grafana/dashboard id: cft-commit-fractionalizer) - [x] Feature flag gating - [x] Migration + rollback tooling - [x] Perf benchmarks (50k requests/min mixed load)

Related work: builds on prior autoscaler headroom work (ENG-4111) and the supply decay sampler (PR pr-41237). See perf notes in commits.

How to test locally: 1) enable feature flag dedicated.fractional-commitments=true in dev cluster; 2) run ./devctl alloc simulate --tenants 60 --fractional=true; 3) observe tenant_effective_utilization_* metrics and supply_age_seconds; 4) run migration tool: ./tools/migrate-commitments --dry-run.

Rollout plan: 1) Canary on staging with 10% traffic ~48h; 2) Monitor 95th/99th latency, token cost per-tenant and eviction counts; 3) Gradual 10% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks only when eviction delta < 3% vs baseline.

Risks and mitigation: - Fractional rounding could cause micro-preemptions: mitigated by executing rounding at allocation time and by supply hysteresis window. - Accounting drift: added conversion & verification job. - Performance cost: fixed-point math is optimized and covered by benchmarks; no meaningful CPU-added overhead observed in 95th percentile under load test.
Diego Morales: Please confirm rounding semantics when multiple fractional commitments exceed a single device slice — should we maintain FIFO or proportional assignment?
Maya Patel (author): We chose proportional assignment with deterministic tie-break by tenant id; added comment in fractional_admission.go and tests for saturation scenarios.
Renee Chen: CI failed initially on integration due to time-sensitive flakiness in the stable-window test. Could you add a backoff?
Maya Patel (author): Added exponential backoff and extended the stable-window to 5s in the test; CI re-run passed.
Arjun Singh: Suggest exposing supply_age_seconds with histogram buckets to help detect both very young and very stale supply — done.
SRE: Can we add an alert for supply_age_seconds > 600s in staging? Work item created SUP-9821.
Release Manager: Ensure migration tool logs are retained for 30 days; added retention flag and docs note.
payload.title: Commitment Fractionalizer and Supply Hysteresis: fractional reservations + cross-zone supply allocator

Title: Introduce fast-presubmit lane, dep-throttle orchestrator, and lint-adapter

Summary: This PR adds a low-latency presubmit lane designed to give developers fast feedback for small, focused changes while offloading heavyweight checks to staged lanes. It also introduces a lightweight 'dep-throttle' orchestrator that gates automated dependency rollouts to avoid mass churn during peak CI usage, and a lint-adapter shim that lets us run a slim quick-lint for premerge and a full-lint in the nightly pipeline. The goals are faster inner-loop developer feedback, fewer CI collisions during dependency upgrades, and clearer separation between quick checks and full verification runs.

Motivation and context: Over the last quarter we observed increased median feedback time for small PRs due to a growing integration test matrix and aggressive automatic dependency rollouts. ENG-1287 captured the developer frustration with slow presubmit feedback. ENG-1303 proposed isolating dependency upgrade traffic and staged lint execution so that small edits (docs, comments, small refactors) get sub-5m feedback. This work implements the orchestration and the GitHub Actions lane changes to realize that.

What changed (high-level):
- Add `.github/workflows/presubmit-fastpath.yml` — a slim presubmit action that runs: staged-quick-lint, unit tests (fast shards), small integration smoke (file-change aware), and a lightweight cache warm.
- Add `tools/dep-throttle/` — small Go service and a cli used by the dependency automation pipeline to detect ongoing rollout windows and delay non-urgent upgrades.
- Add `scripts/lint-adapter.ts` — Node shim that maps existing eslint/rulesets into fast/run-on-delta mode and reports in the same annotation format as full-lint.
- Update `internal/ci/runner.go` to introduce 'lane' concept (fast, full, nightly) and expose lane hints to the executor.
- Docs: `docs/presubmit.md` describing the lanes and contributor guidance.
- Tests: Add `tests/ci/presubmit_fastpath_test.go` and integration smoke harness additions to cover the new lane behavior.

Commits (summary):
- 8a2c9f2  Add presubmit-fastpath workflow and quick-lint runner hooks.
- b4f1d17  Implement dep-throttle service and CLI gate.
- c1e3a88  Add lint-adapter shim and integrate with annotations.
- d9f7b21  Expose lane hints in internal/ci runner and add unit tests.
- f7a2b05  Docs and contributor guidance; add e2e smoke to nightly pipeline.

Files changed (high-level):
- .github/workflows/presubmit-fastpath.yml
- tools/dep-throttle/main.go, tools/dep-throttle/README.md, tools/dep-throttle/config.yaml.example
- scripts/lint-adapter.ts
- internal/ci/runner.go, internal/ci/runner_test.go
- docs/presubmit.md
- tests/ci/presubmit_fastpath_test.go, tests/ci/smoke/fastpath_sample.yaml

Key implementation notes:
- presubmit-fastpath uses path-aware triggers: only runs on PRs where changed files match a predefined fast-path globs file (docs/, examples/, small package changes). Changes to core service code continue to trigger full lanes.
- dep-throttle exposes a simple HTTP API for the dependency-automation bot to query current window state; it implements a token-bucket style limiter so multiple concurrent upgrades are serialized and retried with backoff. The default config keeps throttle off-peak and moderately aggressive during business hours.
- lint-adapter performs delta-based linting: it runs eslint only on changed files and returns annotations in the same format as full-lint so the Console and PR show consistent feedback. It intentionally avoids expensive autofix passes in the quick lane.

Review flow and decisions:
- Request: Please review the runner API additions and the dep-throttle semantics (Ruben Park).
- Main debate: whether to centralize presubmit triggers in a single repository-level glob file vs. per-repo YAML. We elected for a single source-of-truth under `docs/presubmit.md` with a nightly job that validates the globs.
- Security: dep-throttle is read-only by default and requires the automation bot token for write operations; Aisha audited the service and recommended a short-lived token pattern to limit blast radius.

Review conversation (excerpt):
- Ruben Park (reviewer): "Runner changes look ok, but can we avoid adding a new long-lived goroutine per PR? Concerned about memory under high parallelism."
- Marina Lopez (author): "Good catch — updated runner.go to use a pooled worker per executor rather than per PR; tests updated (runner_test.go) to simulate 200 concurrent jobs."
- Aisha Patel (reviewer): "dep-throttle config is reasonable; please add an opt-out label for repo owners who want immediate rollouts."
- Marina Lopez: "Added `dep-upgrade/skip-throttle` label support and documented behavior in README for dep-throttle."
- Liam Chen (reviewer): "lint-adapter annotations look fine; add a smoke harness so we can validate the annotation format in the Console parser."
- Marina Lopez: "Added tests/ci/smoke/fastpath_sample.yaml and console-parser wrapper in scripts/ to validate annotation format."

CI:
- Initial run: unit (pass, 8m), fast-integration (fail, flake in smoke harness), lint (pass quick-lint), build (pass), e2e (skipped for fastpath).
- Fix: Addressed race in smoke harness (test flakiness) and re-ran CI. Final: all checks pass.

Merging and rollout:
- Merge method: squash and merge.
- Merged on 2026-03-04 by Marina Lopez after reviewers approved and CI passed.
- Post-merge: presubmit-fastpath workflow was enabled in a staged rollout — initially opt-in for active contributors via a repo label; after monitoring 48 hours with no regressions we flipped default to on for non-core directories.

Operational notes and follow-ups:
- Follow-up ticket (ENG-1340): add telemetry to dep-throttle to capture delay/queue metrics and expose them in Console.
- Follow-up ticket (ENG-1341): add an admin UI for temporary throttle overrides behind SSO+audit logging.
- Follow-up ticket (ENG-1342): migrate monolith lint rules to staged rule-sets so the quick-lint remains stable at scale.

Why this is different from prior PRs: Instead of only trimming matrices or changing cache keys, this PR introduces an orchestrator artifact (dep-throttle) plus a runtime lane concept and a lint translation shim. The intent is to operationalize CI load management and give predictable developer feedback without sacrificing full verification for risky changes.

Notes for release and cross-team communication:
- Notify developer experience channel on Slack about the new fast lane and the label opt-in flow.
- Post guide in the contributor docs and update the onboarding checklist so new contributors understand why their PR may only run the fast lane.
- Dependency automation team to update their bot to check dep-throttle before opening batch upgrades.

Contact: Marina Lopez (author) for follow-up and troubleshooting.
- Add a fast-presubmit GitHub Actions lane for low-latency feedback on small diffs.
- Deploy `dep-throttle` service to limit external dependency upgrade churn during high-traffic windows.
- Introduce `lint-adapter` to translate repo lint rules into a faster, staged runner so linting can be split between quick and full checks.
payload.title: Introduce fast-presubmit lane, dep-throttle orchestrator, and lint-adapter

Motivation: A recent incident (SUP-2021) revealed that a misbehaving model-sidecar could amplify KV pressure and trigger region-level fallbacks. Existing circuit and load-shedding logic is conservative but reacts too late when a single noisy sidecar starts leaking latency/egress. This PR adds a lightweight transparent-sidecar graceful-ejector plus an SLO-keeper that preserves a soft-path budget to avoid aggressive region failover.

What this changes: 1) runtime: sidecar_health_detector module that observes per-sidecar ingress latency, outstanding-kv, and egress-saturation and marks a sidecar as candidate-for-eject when thresholds cross short windows; 2) graceful-ejector: a staged sequence that (a) drains new requests for the candidate sidecar, (b) migrates cached KV prefixes to peer nodes where applicable, (c) marks the sidecar as sidecar:ejected in the registry with an expiration and backoff; 3) SLO-keeper: a per-tenant soft-path budget that reserves a small portion of regional capacity for low-latency degraded responses rather than full failover; 4) telemetry: new metrics (sidecar_eject_attempts_total, sidecar_eject_success_total, slo_keeper_budget_used, slo_keeper_recoveries) and a small dashboard; 5) small fixes to fallback handshake so warm fallback respects in-flight KV leases.

Design notes: The ejector is conservative by default (v1 thresholds tuned to reduce false positives). The ejector is transparent: it does not change the client-facing routing decision set, only reduces load on the offending sidecar and signals the control plane. Ejection is timeboxed with exponential backoff and is reversible. The SLO-keeper implements a soft budget that decreases eviction aggressiveness instead of triggering immediate circuit-open.

Checklist: - [x] unit tests for sidecar_health_detector and ejector state machine - [x] integration test that simulates noisy sidecar and verifies traffic re-route and KV-preservation - [x] load test (bench) showing <2% extra token cost during ejection scenarios - [x] telemetry panels and alert (non-firing by default) - [x] docs: short note in runtime/CHANGELOG and SRE runbook update

Testing and rollout: CI: full unit + integration passed (See CI summary). Staged rollout: feature flag redwood.enable_graceful_ejector default=false; staged enable in canary region (us-west-2 canary pool) for 24 hours then wide. Monitoring: dashboards for sidecar_eject_* and slo_keeper_* added; initial alert threshold set high to collect signals. Rollback: flip feature flag to false; ejector reverses within two minutes for active ejections; emergency circuit: manual reclamation endpoint added to control-plane api to force-restore any ejected sidecar.

Risk and mitigation: False positives ejecting healthy sidecars is the main risk. Mitigations: conservative thresholds, multi-signature detection (latency + kv_pressure + egress), short ejection windows and exponential backoff, canary rollout. We also added an audit log entry for every ejection for post-incident analysis.

Related: SUP-2021 incident timeline, ENG-1983 proposal doc (linked in Linear).
Maya Gupta: Can we make the default thresholds stricter? I saw 30s window in tests — suggest 60s to avoid noisy signals.
Riley Santos (author): Good point, tightened to 60s and added multi-signal gating (latency+kv+egress). Updated tests to cover the new window.
Oliver Park: Integrations look good. One nit: move metrics names to metrics_registry constant file so other teams can subscribe without schema drift.
Riley Santos: Done — metrics were centralized in telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml.
Samira Khan: Approving on SRE side pending canary monitoring. Please ensure alert thresholds are high during canary.
Maya Gupta: Verified canary for 24 hours in us-west-2; ejector triggered twice for a legitimate noisy sidecar and auto-healed. Approving merge.
Hotfix: Add transparent sidecar ejector to remove misbehaving sidecars without full-region failover; SLO-keeper introduces a soft-path budget to prevent aggressive circuit tripping; telemetry: new ejection and soft-path metrics and dashboards.
payload.title: Introduce transparent sidecar graceful-ejector and SLO-keeper for soft-path preservation

Context and motivation: Customer-facing incidents in January showed a lot of noisy SLO alerts driven by long-tail invocation variance and extremely high cardinality of metric labels (prompt_id, model_revision, region). This PR introduces two cooperating features: 1) invocation summaries: a compact per-invocation rollup that attaches a small set of canonical attributes (invocation fingerprint, cohort, token_count_bucket, model_variant) and consolidated phase timing; 2) batch-metric-optimizer: an offline/nearline pipeline that collapses high-cardinality metrics into cohort-backed aggregates and automatically suggests alert quieting knobs.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a small runtime hook that emits InvocationSummaries to the observability pipeline (compact protobuf-like json, max 1kB). Summaries capture phase-level timings, token counts, cache hit flags, and a generated invocation_cohort tag.
- Introduces a batch-metric-optimizer service (k8s deployment) that consumes recent InvocationSummaries and produces: cohort aggregation rules, per-alert quieting suggestions, and a reconciled metrics export that replaces combinatorial labels with cohort keys.
- Adds Grafana dashboard panels and an alert playbook that uses cohort-weighted thresholds and a quiet-window derived from median tail latency per-cohort.
- Provides a compatibility shim so customers that rely on per-token labels see no functional regression; the optimizer exports both raw and cohorted views until customers opt-in.

Checklist (tested):
- [x] Unit tests for summary serialization and validator
- [x] Integration test that verifies cohort assignment and aggregator correctness (small sample)
- [x] End-to-end smoke: summaries -> optimizer -> metrics export -> dashboard renders
- [x] Load test: emitter rate at 5000 invocations/s with <3% extra CPU on the metrics forwarder
- [x] Security review: PRD for minimal PII (no prompt content emitted)

Commits summary: This branch was developed across multiple commits (see commits field). Major logical commits include: "invocation summaries: serializer + emitter", "batch optimizer: aggregator core and rule exporter", "dashboard: cohort panels + runbook links", "compat shim and opt-in toggle", "tests and load profile adjustments".

Files changed (high level): see files_changed list for exact paths. Notable additions: src/observability/invocation_summary_emitter.py, services/batch_metric_optimizer/main.py, dashboards/cohort_rollup_panels.json, docs/observability/invocation-rollups.md, tests/test_invocation_summary.py.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Aaron Liu (reviewer): "Can we guarantee the cohort assignment won't drift during a rollout? If cohorts change semantics we will mute important signals."
  - Author reply: "We implemented stable cohort hashing based on (model_family, sequence_length_bin, cache_miss_flag) and included a cohort-translation table for rollbacks. Added test to assert stable mapping across restarts."
- Marisol Vega: "The optimizer could accidentally remove labels that customers need for billing. Please ensure the export keeps raw metrics behind a feature flag."
  - Author reply: "Agreed. The optimizer writes cohorted metrics to a separate metric namespace (redwood.cohorted.*) and does not overwrite redwood.raw.* until the customer toggles opt-in. Added docs and a console toggle."
- Tom Bennett: "Dashboard looks useful but we should add a synthetic SLO replay to validate suggested quiet windows."
  - Author reply: "Included a small synthetic replay harness under services/batch_metric_optimizer/replay that replays sampled InvocationSummaries and scores quiet-window proposals. Added to CI smoke step."

CI and rollout notes:
- CI: unit and integration tests passed in the last run (flaky network test retried once). Build artifacts pushed to our internal registry.

Motivation: We observed recurring microburst-induced tail spikes when the continuous batcher handled many small, bursty requests that briefly overran slot reservations. This caused KV-cache pin contention and repeated kernel warmups leading to high p99. This PR introduces a microburst dampener plus an adaptive warmup path that uses lightweight kernel hinting and proactive KV partial prefetch to smooth transient load without raising steady-state latency or cost. Design: 1) Microburst dampener queue: lightweight in-memory leaky bucket placed ahead of the continuous-batcher admission path. It absorbs sub-second bursts by smoothing admission rates per-shard and per-priority-class while preserving headroom for latency-critical requests. 2) Adaptive warmup with kernel hinting: the runtime emits a small, cheap kernel-hint request when it detects repeated short sequence workloads; the planner uses these hints to select a slightly warmer kernel path (e.g. fused attention variant) for the next N requests for that model-shard, reducing full warmup cycles. 3) KV partial prefetch scoring: a fast heuristic predicts likely KV keys for upcoming prefixes and issues low-priority prefetches that are cancelable on eviction to avoid long-term memory pressure. 4) Fairness shepherding: per-priority token buckets with decay windows to avoid starvation of low-priority streams under repeated dampening. 5) Timeouts and guardrails: configurable soft timeouts for the dampener to ensure requests are not delayed beyond SLA; automated fallback to direct admission for SLA breaches. Implementation notes: changes are isolated under runtime/continuous_batched and runtime/kernel_hints; scheduler added MicroburstDampener and WarmupHintManager; KV prefetch is an opt-in flag behind rollout config. Testing: unit tests for dampener invariants, integration harness runs comparing p50/p95/p99 against main baseline with synthetic burst traces, and a long-run soak with multi-tenant traces. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked - [x] unit tests - [x] integration traces - [x] internal perf run - [x] config flag and rollout plan - [x] docs note in operations guide Rollout: feature gate default off; staged rollout to non-production clusters, metric monitoring for p99 latency, KV evictions, GPU utilization, and kernel warmup count. Expected outcome: 5-12% reduction in p99 for bursty microburst workloads, negligible impact on average latency and <2% increase in tokens cost in worst case. Risks: mis-tuned prefetch can increase memory churn; warmup hints could make wrong kernel selection for rare workloads. Mitigations: conservative defaults, telemetry, and quick rollback via feature flag.
Ethan Park: High level LGTM but let's ensure we have a fallback to bypass the dampener for SLA-exempt routes.
Marisol Ortega: Added bypass and explicit route tag checks in queue_admitter. Also added test for SLA bypass.
Priya Menon: Can the warmup hint frequency be rate-limited? Concerned about kernel thrash.
Marisol Ortega: WarmupHintManager now enforces per-shard cooldown (default 30s) and a global budget; documented defaults in experimental_flags.yaml.
Liam O'Connor: Integration run shows a small increase in KV eviction in one trace, can we make prefetch cancelation more aggressive?
Marisol Ortega: Prefetch cancelation now cancels any outstanding low-pri prefetches when memory pressure > 70% in the shard; re-ran perf suite, see CI.
Introduces an opt-in microburst dampener and adaptive kernel warmup hints to reduce p99 latency on bursty, small-sequence workloads. Feature is gated behind runtime.experimental.microburst_dampener and disabled by default.
Default off. To enable in a staging cluster: set runtime.experimental.microburst_dampener=true and runtime.experimental.prefetch_scorer=true in the cluster config. Monitor metrics: continuous_batched.p99_ms, kernel.warmup_count, kv.prefetch_hits, kv.evictions. If kv.evictions spike, disable prefetch or lower prefetch_budget_pct.
A targeted runtime change that smooths short bursts and reduces p99 by combining a leaky-bucket style queue dampener with conservative kernel warmup hints and cancelable KV prefetching; rolled out behind a feature flag with safety guards and observability.

### Context
During game day and recent regional brownouts, the fastest safe mitigation is to shift Hosted API traffic between regions without waiting for Terraform applies. We currently do this via manual console operations, which is error-prone.

### What this PR does
- Introduces `trafficctl`, an audited CLI wrapper around our GSLB provider API
- Adds commands to:
  - read current targets + weights
  - set weights for api.redwoodinference.com
  - set record TTL (temporary)
- Enforces RBAC via the `infra-traffic-admin` role
- Writes an audit log event for every invocation (who, what record, old/new weights)

### Usage
```
trafficctl gslb get --record api.redwoodinference.com
trafficctl dns set-ttl --record api.redwoodinference.com --ttl 60
trafficctl gslb set-weights --record api.redwoodinference.com --weights us-east-1-gw=0,us-west-2-gw=100
trafficctl dns set-ttl --record api.redwoodinference.com --ttl 300
```

### Rollback
- Disable the `trafficctl` GitHub Actions release workflow and revert to manual console operations
- No data-plane changes are required to roll back this PR

- `pkg/gslb/*`
- `pkg/auditlog/*`

Context: we see large volume of noisy SLO alerts that are driven by short-lived micro-spikes in token-phase latencies and tail-cost jitter. Existing alert heuristics operate on coarse per-route percentiles which amplifies noise from low-volume shapes. This PR introduces two orthogonal improvements: (1) Sliced Metric Exposures: a new lightweight metric surface that emits per-route + prompt-shape slices (prompt length bucket, early/late-phase token ratio) for key token-level signals (token_latency_ms, token_cpu_ns, token_cost_microunits) with compact labels to keep cardinality bounded; and (2) Stepped Alert Decimation: an alerting preprocessor that reduces noisy flapping by applying a time-stepped decimation algorithm (shape-aware smoothing + spectral spike suppression) before evaluation by the SLO engine.

Design summary: Sliced exposures are implemented as a thin aggregation layer in observability/metrics that subscribes to the token telemetry stream and emits rollup counters/histograms at three slice dimensions (route, prompt_shape_bin, token_phase). We chose coarse bins to preserve signal while keeping series < 6x existing cardinality. The latency echo matrix dashboard visualizes these slices as a heatmap: x-axis is token phase (init/mid/finish), y-axis is prompt-shape bin, each cell shows median/95/99 latency plus a small sparklines for recent burstiness. The alert decimator lives as an independent pre-eval stage (alerts/step_decimator.py) and exports debug metrics so we can observe how many candidate alerts are decimated vs passed.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged (ff:obs.sliced_exposures) and gated behind a per-tenant sampling opt-in for first 2 weeks. Step 1: enable sliced exposures for internal tenants and run dashboard in read-only mode to validate cardinality and performance. Step 2: enable alert-decimator in passive mode (only record decisions, do not suppress) and run for 72h. Step 3: switch to active decimation for low-volume shapes (<= 10 rps) and monitor alert volume. Step 4: broad enable with gradual increase in shape volume threshold if metrics stable.

Testing and validation: unit tests for decimator logic and e2e integration in tests/alert_decimator_test.go. Load bench for metric emitter to ensure <3% CPU overhead on a busy worker (bench results included in the commit message). Dashboard JSON has been validated with scripts/ci/validate-dashboards.sh. Observability cost impact estimate: ~0.8% ingestion increase for routed tenants, we measured ~2.3% additional disk usage on synthetic replay for internal tenant due to hist granularity; this is acceptable within Dedicated capacity budgets.

Motivation & trade-offs: We intentionally keep slice cardinality coarse to avoid high cardinality explosion. This is not a replacement for per-invocation traces; it is a complementary rollup that lets oncall and the SLO system reason at shape granularity. The decimator uses conservative thresholds by default and is tunable via config in helm/values-observability.yaml.

Related: ENG-2048 (alert noise reduction epic), ENG-2101 (latency dashboarding refactor).See docs/runs/metric-exposure-design.md for detailed diagram and rationale.

Merge notes: squash-merged after gating changes and final CI green. Backfill plan: no data backfill required, metrics start emitting on flag enable.
Evan Kline: Nice approach; can you justify the chosen prompt_shape buckets? Concerned about underfitting rare shapes.
Maya Chen: We iterated on buckets with a replay dataset; attached quantiles in the design doc. We prefer fewer bins to keep cardinality predictable. I added a config map to tune bins per-tenant if needed.
Priya Nair: Request changes: expose a debug gauge for decimation decisions per-route and add a fallback to disable active decimation if suppressions exceed 5% of alerts in a rolling 1h window.
Maya Chen: Added decimator.debug_decisions_total and the safety-window check; updated tests to cover the 5% path.
Luca Bianchi: Verified dashboard visuals and alert suppression metrics in staging. Approved pending CI fixes (flake in validate-dashboards).

Motivation: customers have asked for stronger guarantees that tenant-scoped service accounts can only request KMS operations for keys provisioned in their pinned region, and that every KMS call is traceable back to an immutable audit envelope. This PR adds a lightweight coherence middleware (coherence-mw) in the API gateway and a small runtime enforcement shim to bind tenant claims -> KMS key hints -> audit envelope IDs.

What this does (high-level): coherence-mw normalizes incoming identity claims (service_account + tenant_id + region_hint), validates tenant KMS entitlement via the policy engine (uses existing tenant_policy cache), injects a canonical kms_key_hint header when appropriate, and emits an audit_envelope_id that the downstream KMS proxy and audit pipeline use to correlate logs. The runtime shim enforces region pin for KMS token allocation (early reject if mismatch), and RBAC v2 mappings are extended to include service-account-scoped roles for tenant-bounded operations.

Design notes: the middleware intentionally avoids key material management; it only attaches a signed hint (key ARN hint signed with service gateway key) plus a residency assertion token from the policy engine. The audit_envelope_id is generated deterministically from tenant_id + request_nonce + epoch and signed to prevent tampering; the audit pipeline already accepts this envelope format after a small parser upgrade (included). The RBAC mapper changes add a new principal type "tenant_service_account" and a deterministic role expansion rule that prefers tenant-scoped roles over org-wide fallbacks.

Compatibility and rollout: feature guarded behind a runtime flag (feature.tenant_kms_coherence). Default behavior unchanged. We plan a staged rollout: enable in staging, monitor audit-correlations/latency for 48 hours, then enable canary in us-west-2. The PR includes a migration note for operators to seed tenant_policy cache with residency-assertions when enabling.

Testing and validation: unit tests for middleware, policy cache mocks, integration test that exercises a full request path (gateway -> runtime shim -> kms-proxy -> audit-collector). Added an end-to-end test that asserts the audit_envelope_id is present and the kms_key_hint matches the tenant_policy mapping.

Checklist: [x] Add middleware and shim [x] Extend RBAC v2 mapper [x] Add audit envelope parser [x] Add tests and CI jobs [x] Add release notes entry [x] Add Linear links and rollout plan

Related: builds on ENG-10234 (tenant policy cache improvements) and SEC-2045 (KMS entitlement evaluation).

Implementation details: the description below lists commits and high-level file changes. See changed_files for file-level pointers and review_comments for conversation context.

Aisha Ramos: Added mapper fallback test and a comment referencing the canonical resolution order.
Jon Park: CI flake on integration test (timeout). Suggest increasing the e2e timeouts and making the KMS proxy mock deterministic.
Aisha Ramos: Increased timeout and made the mock deterministic; re-ran CI.
Operator-facing: Add tenant KMS coherence middleware behind feature flag. Requires seeding tenant policy cache with residency assertions before enabling in production. Adds deterministic audit_envelope_id to correlate KMS calls with audit logs. No customer-facing API changes.

Motivation: Long-tail token-cost and token-latency regressions generate noisy alerts and high investigation overhead. We need a low-cost, on-demand mechanism to capture high-fidelity token-level traces for the tail of invocations and a hysteresis policy layer for cost-regression alerts to avoid flapping during transient spikes.

What this PR does: Adds an on-demand tail sampler (sampling triggered by alerts, manual query, or synthetic probe) that captures compact token snapshots + invocation metadata; introduces an alert hysteresis adapter that requires sustained deviation before promotion to high-severity; ships a new Grafana dashboard with tail-sampled invocation panels and a compact cost-regression timeline; and exposes a small sampling API for troubleshooting teams.

Scope checklist:
- [x] Implement on-demand tail sampler service and API endpoint (telemetry/service/tail_sampler.py)
- [x] Add compact token snapshot proto and storage adapter (telemetry/models/token_snapshot.proto, telemetry/storage/snapshot_store.go)
- [x] Integrate sampler with alerting to allow automatic capture on low-severity token-cost alerts
- [x] Implement cost-regression hysteresis policy in alerting backend (alerts/hysteresis_adapter.py)
- [x] Add Grafana dashboard JSON and a README for interpreting tail samples (dashboards/tail-sampler.json, dashboards/README_tail_sampler.md)
- [x] Add unit and integration tests for sampler and hysteresis logic (telemetry/tests/*)
- [x] Add lightweight sampling quota checks and tenant-scoped limits to prevent runaway storage

Notes and constraints: Tail samples are compact by design (only first/last n tokens, token-cost deltas, top-5 KV misses). Samples are tenant-scoped and retention defaults to 7 days. The sampling API is authenticated and rate-limited. This PR intentionally keeps payload sizes small to make on-demand sampling feasible for high-traffic tenants.

Related items: ENG-5473 has the original design doc; SUP-2217 is a customer incident that motivated the hysteresis behavior.

High-level commit summary: see commits field for per-commit blurbs.

Behavioral expectations after merge:
- New low-severity token-cost alerts will, by default, elicit an on-demand tail sample (configurable per alert rule).
- Alert severity escalation to P1 requires hysteresis window of sustained deviation (configurable via alert policy).
- Observability teams can request immediate samples via console or API for active investigations.
Priya Nair: Nice approach to make samples compact. Two asks: (1) can we include a tenant privacy review note? (2) ensure the snapshot proto explicitly marks PII fields for redaction.
Avery Chen (author): Added README section about PII handling and redaction markers in token_snapshot.proto; added a privacy checklist to the runbook.
Lucas Romero: Hysteresis adapter looks good but please add a backfill guard — don't suppress alerts for already open incidents. Also add telemetry for hysteresis decisions.
Avery Chen: Added hysteresis decision metric (alerts.hysteresis_decision{action=promote|hold}) and a guard that ignores currently acknowledged incidents when computing sustained deviation.
Emilia Park: Request to add a dashboard panel that correlates sampling frequency with storage consumption so ops can tune tenant defaults.
Avery Chen: Added panel and a lightweight alert on sampling.storage_utilization > 75% for tenant-scoped buckets.

Motivation: We continue to see transient spikes in reauth calls and duplicated token refresh logic across SDKs, which increases tail latency for streaming workloads and complicates operator mental models. This PR introduces a cross-SDK 'session lease' shim: a short-lived leased token that the SDK refreshes proactively on a coordinated cadence, together with a small state machine that exposes lease health to the streaming layer. The goal is to reduce auth thrash, align retry/backoff semantics across languages, and provide ergonomic stream handles for application authors.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Adds SessionLeaseManager to Python, a Lease-aware Transport and StreamHandle to TypeScript, and a lease-enabled connection pool in Go. Harmonizes retry windows and backoff formulas for auth failures vs transient network errors. Adds ergonomic stream APIs: Python async iterator variant that yields typed frames, TypeScript streamHandle with close() and attemptResume(), and Go StreamSink with CancelableContext and LeaseInspection hooks. Also bumps SDK package versions and updates changelogs.

Design notes and constraints: Leases are short-lived (default 60s) and renewed proactively at 70% of lifetime. Renewals are serialized per process-connection (to avoid stampeding) and use randomized jitter. The shim is backward-compatible: if server does not advertise lease headers, the SDK falls back to existing token rotation behavior. No server contract change is required for forward compatibility, but servers can optionally send X-Session-Lease TTL headers to tune client behavior. We added telemetry hooks (lease.acquire/renew/fail) consumed by the console for debugging.

Commits (high-level):
- d4f1a2b: introduce SessionLeaseManager interface and local tests (python)
- e6b3c9f: add lease-aware transport adapter and stream handle to ts-sdk
- a7c21d4: integrate lease manager with go-transport and clientpool
- c8f9b11: harmonize retry/backoff constants and unit tests across SDKs
- b5a2f77: ergonomics: python aiter_stream_frames, ts streamHandle.close, go StreamSink.Cancel
- f2d0a3e: bump versions, changelogs, and release notes

- after: export class StreamHandle { async close(graceful: boolean = true): Promise<void> { /* honor lease-aware drain */ } async attemptResume(): Promise<boolean> { /* try resume using cached cursor */ } }

Motivation: Improve safety and confidence when promoting models from shadow (rehearsal) to canary by anchoring promotion decisions to per-cohort fidelity checks and a lightweight consensus checkpoint. This PR implements a rehearsal-to-canary promotion flow that runs synthetic smoke tests and telemetry validation against user cohorts, preserves session affinity during promotes, and exposes new observability/alerting for rehearsal fidelity regressions. Summary of changes: - New rehearsal controller that orchestrates phased shadow runs with per-cohort evaluation windows and a consensus checkpoint algorithm that requires agreement across latency, correctness, and top-k freshness metrics before promotion. - Affinity-preserving handoff: session-token mapping persisted during promote to avoid user-visible session drift. - Synthetic rehearsal harness: replayable, budgeted synthetic traffic generator that exercises edge cases and records fidelity snapshots. - Rollback oracle: automatic fast-fail rollback trigger that can take immediate traffic revert and record forensic snapshot for postmortem. - Ops and runbooks: a runbook for on-call to interpret rehearsal diagnostics and a console dashboard for cohort fidelity heatmaps. Implementation notes: The promenade algorithm uses a sliding-window aggregator with per-cohort thresholds derived from baseline historical percentiles. To avoid noisy single-metric flips, the consensus requires two out of three metric gates plus a monotonicity check on recent samples. Default config is conservative; teams can opt into more aggressive thresholds via rollout policy. Backwards compatibility: rollout schemas are extended with a new optional "rehearsal_policy" block. Default behavior when omitted is unchanged (canary flows remain as before). See release notes for migration guidance. Checklist: - [x] Runtime controller and scheduler hooks - [x] Affinity manager integration - [x] Synthetic harness and e2e tests - [x] Console dashboard and alerting - [x] Runbook and operator playbook - [x] Performance microbenchmarks - [x] Migration guide and schema migration path Known limitations: - The initial version requires a short warmup window (30s) and relies on stable cohort sampling; very low-traffic cohorts may need custom thresholds. - Rehearsal replay currently supports HTTP/text workloads; streaming audio/video not in scope for v1. Rollout plan: Feature gated behind "rehearsal_promote" feature flag. Start with internal beta on staging, then opt-in customers, then broad GA after 2 weeks of telemetry stability.
Key files changed (high-level):
- src/rollout/rehearsal_controller.go: new controller implementing phased shadow runs and consensus checkpointing
- pkg/serving/affinity/affinity_manager.go: persist/restore session-token mapping during promotes
- ops/sim/rehearsal_harness.py: synthetic traffic generator and replay CLI
- test/e2e/rehearsal_promote_test.go: end-to-end smoke and regression tests
- console/dashboards/rehearsal_fidelity.jsonnet: cohort heatmap and gating dashboard
- docs/runbooks/rehearsal_playbook.md: operator runbook and diagnostics guide
- infra/telemetry/alerts/rehearsal_fidelity_rules.yaml: new alerts and thresholds
- api/schemas/rollout_schema_v2.json: optional rehearsal_policy block
Plus small updates across CI configs and mocks for deterministic tests.

Anika: Added additional unit tests and clarified tie-breaker semantics in comments.
Ethan: Noted a potential race on session mapping writes during rapid rollback; please ensure idempotency.
Anika: Fixed by making mapping writes conditional and idempotent; added a mutex in affinity_manager.
Sasha: E2E flakes seen on first CI run; suspected time-dependent assertions in harness. Suggest polling/timeout improvements.

Motivation: Dedicated fleets still see short-lived microbursts that are expensive to satisfy with hard reservation policies. This PR introduces a lightweight WarmPool Oracle and a soft-capacity hedging adapter that allow fleets to accept limited temporary overcommit while preserving throughput guarantees. The goal is to reduce cold-start allocations and avoid aggressive scale-ups for short spikes, and to expose defensible telemetry so SRE and customers can tune hedging windows.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a WarmPool Oracle service that maintains a compact probabilistic model of warmlet readiness per pool (warm_index, recent-prewarm-rate, drain-backoff). 2) Introduces a SoftCapacityHedge admission adapter in the fleet allocator that can issue provisional credits (soft_burst) with configurable TTL and prioritized fallback routing when hedges are exhausted. 3) Implements throughput-fallback contracts: when a soft hedge cannot be honored, requests are rerouted to a lower-cost compatible model variant or throttled according to priority bands with deterministic backoff. 4) Emits new telemetry and SLIs- a per-pool warm_index gauge and a per-tenant hedged_admissions counter plus percentile-backed latency impact histograms. 5) Adds an opt-in feature flag (enable_warmpool_oracle) and rollout plan (canary on us-west-2 followed by gradual region expansion).

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in PR (ENG-2145 design) - [x] Unit tests for oracle state transitions - [x] Integration tests for hedge expiry and fallback routing - [x] E2E load test with synthetic microburst traces - [x] Docs update (console UI & config reference)

Backwards compatibility and safety: All new behavior is behind the feature flag; soft hedges are bounded by a configurable safety cap (soft_hedge_cap_per_pool) to avoid systemic overcommit. Fallback routing uses the existing model-variant affinity rules so we do not introduce new model incompatibilities.

Rollout notes: Start with canary enabled for dedicated pools in us-west-2 at 10% of traffic for one week. Monitor redwood_throughput_guarantee_violations_total and warmpool_oracle_warm_index percentiles; abort if guarantees spike > 0.5% over baseline.

Related: ENG-2145, ENG-2190, SUP-1122.
Maya Chen: Nice design. A few questions: how do you ensure the oracle model cannot be gamed by noisy tenants? Suggest adding an upper bound on soft_hedge credits per tenant.
Author (Ishaan): Added soft_hedge_cap_per_tenant and documented in config. Oracle uses exponentially damped counters to avoid short-term amplification.
Diego Rivera: Please add a unit test for oracle state 'stale->refill' transition under concurrent updates.
Author: Added TestOracleRefillConcurrent in warmpool_test.go and a race-check CI job for the integration stage.
Priya Nambiar: Telemetry names look good. Can we tag hedges with pool_id and particle (prewarm) bucket for easier dashboards?
Author: Telemetry now includes pool_id and bucket label; dashboards updated in console commit.

Motivation: Several customers in regulated jurisdictions requested stronger enforcement that KMS keys used for encryption are resident in the tenant-declared region and that noisy audit streams do not overwhelm the central audit pipeline. This PR introduces two coordinated middleware components: (1) an operator-scoped KMS residency lock that enforces per-operator KMS region affinity and rejects (or transparently routes) requests that would use a cross-region CMK unless explicit consent is present; (2) an audit-throttle middleware that deduplicates high-volume audit events and applies configurable rate limits and burst controls to audit-forwarding so the audit ingestion system remains available under noisy tenants.

Summary of changes: added new middleware in the KMS and audit stacks, updated RBAC v2 policy checks to include a temporal operator claim used during short-lived cross-region escalation, added a small migration to backfill residency tags for recent audit entries, and a feature-flagged canary rollout with observability and rollback hooks. This is primarily server-side code with a small config/ops surface in deploy/feature-flags and docs for enterprise customers.

Design notes: - KMS residency lock operates at the operator service boundary: it inspects the request's operator identity (claim) and tenant residency metadata. If the key candidate is outside the tenant region, middleware will consult the ConsentStore; absent consent, the request is rejected with a 403 and a structured audit event that includes the reason. - Audit-throttle is placed before the audit-forwarder. It implements keyed sampling + token-bucket per-tenant controls, and a dedupe window for identical audit payloads. Dedup and throttle rules are configurable per-tenant via the console and default to conservative limits. - RBAC change: introduce a short-lived claim type "operator:region-escalation" for automated canaries and on-call operator flows; checks are additive and behind a feature flag. We explicitly avoid widening existing permissions by requiring the claim and audit evidence.

Checklist: - [x] Middleware implementation and unit tests - [x] Integration tests (KMS residency rejection + consent flow) - [x] Migration script to backfill "residency_region" audit tags - [x] Feature flag + console documentation - [x] Metrics and dashboards (latency, throttle_rejected, dedupe_rate) - [x] Canaries and rollout plan in deploy/feature-flags.yaml

Commits: - feat(kms): operator-scoped residency lock middleware
- feat(audit): audit-throttle middleware with dedupe window
- perf(middleware): batch consent cache lookups and add circuit-breaker
- test: integration tests for residency and audit throttle flows
- ops: add feature flag and rollout config, migration backfill script

High level files changed: ["service/kms/middleware_residency.go", "service/audit/middleware_throttle.go", "pkg/rbac/v2/claims.go", "tools/migrations/backfill_residency_tags.sql", "deploy/feature-flags.yaml", "docs/enterprise/kms-residency.md", "tests/integration/test_kms_residency.py", "tests/integration/test_audit_throttle.py", "service/audit/audit_forwarder.go", "pkg/consent/consentstore.go", "pkg/metrics/metrics_definitions.yaml", "Makefile"]

Review conversation (high level): - Alex: requested clearer metric names and suggested moving dedupe default from 60s -> 30s to reduce perceived duplication during spikes. Implementation updated and metric names prefixed with "residency_" and "audit_throttle_". - Priya: asked for explicit consent-store TTL and circuit-breaker instrumentation. Added tests for consent cache eviction and a Prometheus gauge for circuit-breaker state. - Rory: asked for a migration rollback plan; added documentation and an idempotent SQL script that can be re-run safely. Minor lint fixes and added a unit test to cover a previously flaky path.

CI summary: Initial CI run failed on a flaky integration test (tests/integration/test_audit_throttle.py::test_dedupe_window) in the concurrency harness. Reran CI with the stabilized harness and tests passed. Full checks: unit, integration (canaries), linters, schema checks. All gates green on rerun.

Operational notes: Rollout is gated behind feature flag "redwood.kms_residency_lock". Canary at 10% for 48h measuring reject_rate, latency_p95, audit_throttle_rejects. If reject_rate > 0.5% for non-test tenants or latency_p95 increases > 20% we will rollback. Migration backfill is safe to run offline and is idempotent; ops runbook included in docs/enterprise/kms-residency.md.

Related work: ENG-7432 (residency policy audit), SEC-211 (enterprise KMS compliance checklist). This complements previous residency-oriented changes but differs by focusing on operator-scoped enforcement plus audit ingestion protection.

Priya Singh: add consent cache TTL tests and circuit-breaker metric
Rory Blake: include migration rollback steps and idempotency notes

payload.body:
Context: As part of SIEM-ready audit export beta (ENG-5127), downstream delivery is at-least-once and we need stable dedup keys plus a consistent category taxonomy for filtering + mapping into Splunk/Datadog. This PR updates core audit event emission to include: (1) `event_id` (stable unique id per event) (2) `schema_version: 2` and canonical `category` / `subcategory` / `action` fields (3) a compatibility mapping layer so existing producers that still emit legacy `event_type`/`operation` continue to work while we progressively migrate call sites.

Summary of changes: Add `event_id` generated at emission time using UUIDv7 (time-ordered, collision-safe) and plumbed through the AuditEvent struct. Introduce an enum-backed category taxonomy with a small canonical set and a `category_version` constant to make future taxonomy evolution explicit. Add a `legacy_event_type` field (optional) and a mapping table from legacy strings to v2 taxonomy, used for any call site still emitting legacy types. Update JSON serialization + redaction hooks so `event_id` is always present and never redacted, while category fields are required and validated. Add golden fixtures + unit tests to lock schema output. No changes to retention/storage semantics in this PR.

Taxonomy (v2, initial): categories = {authn, authz, workspace, api_key, model, deployment, billing, data_access, security, system}. `subcategory` is optional but recommended for high-volume categories (e.g., `api_key.rotation`, `authz.role`, `deployment.route`). `action` remains a verb phrase in present tense (create/update/delete/rotate/enable/disable/login/logout/impersonate/etc) and is required.

Compatibility: Existing events that provide `event_type` will have `legacy_event_type` set, and the mapping table populates `category/subcategory/action`. If mapping is missing, we default to `category=system`, `subcategory=audit.unknown_legacy_type`, `action=emit` and include a structured warning log (rate-limited) so we can clean up unmapped call sites before GA.

Follow-ups: (a) migrate remaining emitters to pass v2 taxonomy explicitly, removing reliance on legacy mapping (b) update docs + examples in security/compliance Confluence (c) exporter service uses `event_id` for idempotency keys (separate PR).

Testing: unit tests for UUIDv7 generation + monotonicity (best-effort), mapping table tests (known legacy types), JSON golden files for representative events, and a redaction regression test to ensure `event_id/category/action` survive redaction.

Rollout: behind `AUDIT_SCHEMA_V2_ENABLED` (default ON in dev/staging, OFF in prod until exporter beta gate is ready). When flag is OFF, we still emit legacy fields only and omit v2 additions.

Risk: Low-medium. Primary risk is unexpected unmapped legacy event types causing `system/audit.unknown_legacy_type` categorization; mitigated via logs + metrics + follow-up cleanup.
Kevin Osei (review): Can you clarify the id generation strategy and whether downstream should treat `event_id` as globally unique across tenants? Also please confirm we are not putting any extra PII in the new fields.

Marcus Lin (author): Using UUIDv7 generated at emission time; uniqueness is global (across all tenants) and safe to treat as a dedup key. No PII added: event_id is random/time-ordered, category/subcategory/action are controlled vocab/verbs only. No IP/user agent changes in this PR.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): +1 on adding the v2 fields, but I’d like validation behavior spelled out. What happens if an emitter passes an invalid category? Also, please ensure RBAC-sensitive events don’t end up in a generic bucket without visibility.

Marcus Lin (author): Added validation: invalid category/subcategory/action causes emission to fail closed in dev/staging (throws) and fail open in prod (drops v2 fields, emits legacy + increments `audit_schema_v2_validation_failed_total`). For generic bucket: when legacy mapping missing we emit `system/audit.unknown_legacy_type` AND a metric + warning log so we can track it.

Ethan Park (review): Flag default worries me. We need predictable behavior for exporter (it will assume event_id exists). Suggest: v2 flag ON everywhere but keep legacy fields for now; or make exporter gate separate.

Marcus Lin (author): Adjusted per your suggestion: `event_id` is always emitted when v2 flag is ON; prod default remains OFF until exporter readiness, but we’ll enable both together via the tenant allowlist flag. Added a TODO in ENG-5127 checklist and updated the flag description to reflect coupling.

Logan Wright (review): Please add a metric for unknown legacy mapping and include the legacy value as a *low-cardinality* label (or not at all). We don’t want cardinality explosions.

Marcus Lin (author): Added `audit_unknown_legacy_type_total` with labels `{service, env}` only. The legacy string is logged (rate-limited) but not a metric label.

Benji Okafor (review): Golden fixture tests look good. One nit: `subcategory` format should be consistent (dot-separated). Some fixtures use underscore.

Marcus Lin (author): Fixed fixtures + added a test enforcing `^[a-z0-9]+(\.[a-z0-9]+)*$` for subcategory when present.

Approvals: Kevin Osei (approved), Kaitlyn Nguyen (approved), Ethan Park (approved), Logan Wright (approved).

Merge: Squashed and merged after CI green.
Audit logs (schema v2, gated): add `event_id` and canonical category taxonomy to support SIEM export filtering + downstream deduplication.

Context: Our full presubmit lanes are costly and provide slow feedback for small, targeted changes. This PR introduces a lightweight 'mini-fastlane' presubmit lane that runs a compact set of checks selected by a change-sensitive heuristics scorer, and a new dependency-metrics-adapter service that exports simple dependency health signals to our telemetry pipeline. Motivation: speed up developer feedback for small edits, reduce CI cost, and provide early visibility into dependency rot/vuln hotspots across affected packages. What this PR does: 1) mini-fastlane presubmit runner: - New GH Actions workflow .github/workflows/mini-fastlane.yml that runs fast checks for PRs with low impact diff by using a change classifier (rust/python/ts path heuristics + diff size thresholds). - Implements file-pattern scoring so affected-language specific linters (eslint, go vet, pyflakes) and a small test subset run instead of full matrix. - Adds a presubmit opt-out annotation (ci:full) for cases that still need full validation. 2) dependency-metrics-adapter: - A small Go binary (cmd/dep-metrics-adapter) that parses lockfiles (package-lock.json, go.sum, poetry.lock) and computes simple signals: lockfile_age_days, transitive_depth_estimate, unresolved_version_count, and a computed staleness_score. - Exposes /metrics (Prometheus) and periodic export to our telemetry pipeline (http POST to telemetry ingestion). - Lightweight policy: warns on staleness_score >= 0.7 for packages touched by the PR. 3) Refactor: - Extracts the language routing logic from the monolithic presubmit runner into a plugin interface (pkg/presubmit/plugin) so future lanes can be composed with the mini-fastlane logic. - Moves several bash init scripts to small Go CLIs to reduce flakiness in runners. Rollout plan: - Step 1 (canary): Enable mini-fastlane for label-friendly repos and 30% of PRs in redwood/* for 48 hours behind a feature flag. - Step 2: Observe CI cost delta and time-to-green; if <10% regression in test coverage signal, expand to 75% for 7 days. - Step 3: Default to opt-in across repo groups; allow toggling via repo settings and annotation. Operator notes: - mini-fastlane will skip heavyweight integration tests by default; these remain gated under the full presubmit. - To force full validation add the PR body line: ci:full. Testing performed: - Local integration with dockerized runners and a simulated 50k-line repo to validate classification heuristics. - E2E smoke on redwood/examples with 60 sample PRs; median feedback reduced from 12m -> 3.8m for mini-fastlane eligible PRs. - Unit tests for dep-metrics-adapter included; mocked telemetry ingestion used in CI. Security & privacy: - dep-metrics-adapter uses only repo-local lockfiles and does not send source diffs outside telemetry; telemetry payloads are aggregated counts and package names only. Checklist: - [x] add GH workflow and documentation (docs/ci/mini-fastlane.md) - [x] implement presubmit plugin interface - [x] add dep-metrics-adapter and Prometheus metrics - [x] add integration + unit tests - [x] add rollout feature flag in infra/flags.md Backlinks: Linear ENG-2781 (mini-fastlane), ENG-2782 (dep-metrics telemetry). Commands to exercise locally: - make dev-presubmit-run TARGET=mini - ./bin/dep-metrics-adapter --scan . --dry-run Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the whitelist of checks conservative (lint + fast unit tests + typecheck) to avoid false negatives. Future work: integrate vulnerability scanner scores and surface suggested bump PRs, add language-specific learned classifiers for file importance.
1) Add mini-fastlane workflow and presubmit plugin interface (Aisha Patel)
2) Implement change classifier and language routers (Aisha Patel)
3) Add dep-metrics-adapter service and Prometheus exporter (Aisha Patel)
4) Migrate init scripts from bash to Go helpers (Aisha Patel)
5) Tests + docs + feature flag wiring (Aisha Patel)
Riley Chen: Nice approach — can we ensure the classifier thresholds are configurable via org flags? (request change)
Aisha Patel: Agree, thresholds are feature-flagged in infra/flags.md; added a section in docs to tune them.
Markus Lim: dep-metrics-adapter looks useful but we should avoid sending full package trees to telemetry — confirm payload shape.
Aisha Patel: telemetry payloads are limited to [{package, staleness_score}] and counts; clarified in code and docs.
Priya Singh: Suggest adding an opt-out label for infra teams so they can opt to always run full CI for sensitive repos.
Aisha Patel: added repo-level opt-out and annotation rules in infra/flags.md
Introduce mini-fastlane presubmit for faster feedback on small diffs; add dependency-metrics-adapter to export simple dep-health signals to telemetry; refactor presubmit runner into plugin interface for composability.

Motivation: Operators need a compact, actionable surface that ties invocation-level telemetry (cost, latency, kernel occupancy) to hardware split and tenant cohorts so oncall can prioritize fixes without digging through long traces. This PR introduces the "signal orchestra" feature: a set of quantized cost bands, a cohort heatmap visualization, and an alert prioritizer that weights alerts by observed cost/latency impact.

Summary of changes: Adds a new dashboard (Observability -> Signal Orchestra) with a Sankey-style cost-lifecycle visualization, a cohorted heatmap keyed by prompt-shape/tenant/model, and trending quantized cost bands that map token-level cost buckets to backend resource splits (kernel/GPU/mem). Introduces a service-side decomposer that emits three new metrics (cost_band, cohort_id, hw_split) and enriches existing spans with cost_bucket tags. Provides an alert prioritizer that post-processes firing alerts and reorders alerts in the UI/Slack pager based on a weighted score (cost*latency*affected_tps). Includes a rollout plan with feature flagging, telemetry-driven canary thresholds, and an A/B comparison against current alert order.

Design notes: The cost quantization uses logarithmic bucketing with 7 bands to ensure stable cardinality while preserving tail resolution. Cohorts are derived from a lightweight fingerprint of the prompt shape + model family to avoid PII. hw_split tags indicate whether the token cost was dominated by kernel time, memory bandwidth, or host CPU. The alert prioritizer computes a normalized score per alert window and supports an override map for enterprise tenants. Implementation focuses on efficient tag emission (no additional RPCs during hot paths) by piggybacking on existing span finalizers.

Testing & performance: Unit tests for decomposer logic and deterministic cohort hashing included. Integration tests validate tag emission for sync/streaming responses and exercise dashboard queries against a synthetic replaybench. Perf microbench on dev cluster: end-to-end tail latency for streaming responses increased by ~0.6ms P50 (within SLO), token-cost metric emission adds <0.3% CPU at 95th percentile. Observed a 9% reduction in mean time-to-action in a simulated alert exercise when using prioritized alerts.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy decomposer behind feature flag to 10% of requests and validate metrics ingestion. 2) Enable dashboard in read-only mode for internal tenants and collect feedback. 3) Flip prioritizer for internal oncall only (Slack/Console) for 2 weeks; monitor missed-severity regressions. 4) Full rollout after 4 successful Canary windows. Backout toggles exist for decomposer and prioritizer.

Checklist: - [x] Decomposer service + metrics emission - [x] Dashboard panels and saved queries - [x] Alert prioritizer service + config - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Runbook and rollback steps in runbooks/observability/signal-orchestra.md - [x] Linear tasks linked

Related: ENG-2042 (observability: cohort-based prioritization), ENG-2099 (alert fatigue: prioritizer prototype).
Avery Chen: Nice work. Two requests: 1) can cohort fingerprint be made stable across restarts? 2) add a small opt-out for tenants with strict telemetry policies.
Priya Kapoor: Reply: cohort fingerprint uses a deterministic hash seeded with a topology-stable constant; added TENANT_TELEMETRY_OPT_OUT in defaults.yaml and documented in runbook.
Diego Martinez: Please add a short-circuit if hw_split is unknown to avoid creating high-cardinality tags.
Priya Kapoor: Added a fallback 'unknown' band and tightened the tag cardinality by enforcing the 7-band cap. Updated tests to assert cardinality bounds.
Leah O'Neill: UI nit: add a time-range pill to the cohort heatmap to make comparisons easier.
Priya Kapoor: Added a range selector to dashboard and a permalink example in docs.

Introduce a lightweight token stream fidelity metric plus a pragmatic alert age-decay suppression policy to reduce noisy fidelity alerts on transient downstream churn. This PR adds a Prometheus metric token_stream_fidelity{route,model,cohort} (histogram + gauge summary), enriches trace spans with fidelity_score and fidelity_reason tags for easier correlation, and ships a Grafana dashboard that correlates fidelity dips with per-token cost slope. The change is aimed at improving SRE's ability to quickly triage long-tail quality regressions while avoiding alert fatigue from short-lived backend variance. Changes include a sampling-based log enrichment path for fidelity dips, an alert rule that employs an exponential age-decay to reduce repeated firing for the same degradation window, and unit + e2e tests to validate metric shapes. Motivation: recent incidents highlighted noisy fidelity alerts during upstream model restarts; instead of raising thresholds globally, an age-decay suppression retains sensitivity to sustained regressions while muting flapping. Related Linear: ENG-1842.
