Context: During a 2026-02-09 incident we observed aggressive cross-region failover decisions caused by transient KV-cache pressure and short-lived CPU spikes. Immediate failover was triggering cascading load to secondary regions and exacerbating latency SLO violations. This PR introduces two coordinated mitigations: 1) a deferred failover window (soft holdoff) that delays irreversible cross-region failover decisions for a small, configurable window to let transient errors recover; and 2) a per-tenant rate warmup queue that staggers new traffic ramps after failover or node additions to avoid cold-ramp bursts. Motivation: Reduce noisy failovers and downstream amplification that caused higher 99p latency and tenant evictions, without removing the ability to failover for genuine sustained outages.

What this changes: - Introduces failover_controller.deferredWindowMs and a state machine transition path that moves a region into a "pending-failover" state before executing a hard failover. If health metrics (latency, error-rate, KV cache pressure) recover within the window, the controller cancels the failover and records the recovery reason. - Adds a tenant-level QueueWarmup with token-bucket backed gradual admission; new tenant/route traffic is admitted at a configured ramp-rate for the first N seconds after a topology change. - Adds telemetry: failover.window_started, failover.window_cancelled, warmup.admitted_tokens, warmup-throttled-tenants. These feed the existing Grafana dashboards and alerting rules are adjusted to avoid noisy alerts during the window. - Tight coupling between the two features: when a pending-failover is active, warmup ramp-ups for tenants routed to the impacted region are applied more conservatively to avoid overloading fallback regions.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for state transitions and queue warmup behavior (failover_controller_test.go, queue_manager_test.go). - Integration tests simulating transient KV pressure with deterministic clock advance to verify window cancellation and metrics emission. - Load test in benchmark-lab mimicking a cold failover: results show 30% reduction in spike QPS to fallback region and 22% improvement in 99p latency during the recovery window. - Local fault injection runbook and chaos experiment notes included.

Rollout plan: - Canary on dedicated us-west-2 region (10% of cross-region traffic) for 48 hours, with tight SLO watch and auto-rollback if 99p latency increases >5% vs baseline. - After canary, staged rollout across regions with slow warmup ramps and ops watch. - Ops playbook updated with steps to override the deferred window (immediate failover) in case of sustained outage.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation code and tests
- [x] Telemetry and alert tuning
- [x] Benchmark results attached
- [x] Verified canary plan
- [x] Docs PR (link in comments)

Related: Linear ENG-3892 (incident follow-up), ENG-3918 (failover hardening). Jira SUP-2147 contains the customer escalation that motivated a fast patch.
Marco Li: Left a few suggestions around naming and ensuring the pending-failover state is observable. Can we add a metric with the pending reason?
Aisha Malik: Added pending_reason label to failover.window_started and emit pending_reason on cancellation. Updated tests to assert label presence.
Priya Desai: Can we make the default window conservative (250ms) and expose via feature-flag? Concerned about long windows increasing user-facing error tolerance.
Aisha Malik: Default set to 250ms, feature-flag controlled per-region. Ops can bump via config for region-specific tuning.

payload.body:
Motivation: teams repeatedly tune batching, cache allocation and quantization per workload to hit unit-econ targets. Manual tuning is slow and error-prone. This PR introduces Cost Watchtower: an automated controller + CLI that continuously observes tenant unit economics (cost/token, p95 latency, reuse ratio) and applies conservative adjustments to batching, cache slice allocation and quantization aggressiveness using a new "reservoir cache profile" format and a safety-curve translator.

What this changes: introduces a new process (cmd/cost-watchtower) that can run as a standalone control-plane sidecar or as a cluster service behind the Redwood Console. The controller collects summarized per-tenant signals (telemetry ingestion via internal/telemetry), scores economics against per-tenant goals, and proposes or applies changes through the existing runtime policy API. Changes are always gated by safety curves and tenant-level cooldowns to avoid oscillations.

Key concepts: reservoir cache profiles: small JSON/YAML descriptors that describe how a tenant's KV/prefix cache should be partitioned and how much spare capacity to reserve for bursts. safety curve: maps observed latency/cost deltas to allowed quantization steps and batching targets (e.g., conservative -> -2 quant steps; permissive -> -4). cost smoothing: an exponential moving average window (configurable) that prevents reacting to single spike events.

Operational model: Cost Watchtower supports three modes: dry-run (no mutations, only suggested ops), manual-approve (creates an admin review task in Linear + annotated diff), and auto-apply (applies changes with canary routing to a configurable tenant percentage and automatic rollback on SLA breaches).

Backward compatibility: profiles are additive and opt-in; existing tenant configs are not modified by default. Controller will only act on tenants that have opted into the automated tier or when a tenant-specific override is present.

Testing and rollout: included integration e2e harness (tests/integration) that runs the controller against the cost-simulator workloads. We validated on a small staging fleet with three tenants for two weeks; no regressions in p99 latency and median cost dropped ~12% for the sampled workloads.

Docs & runbook: docs/ops/cost-watchtower.md contains configuration reference, troubleshooting, and rollback steps. Helm chart added under deploy/helm/cost-watchtower with sane defaults and a toggle to enable dry-run by default.

Checklist: - [x] Controller loop and policy engine implemented - [x] Reservoir profile schema and generator - [x] CLI for dry-run and apply - [x] Helm chart and default values - [x] Integration tests and simulator scenarios - [x] Docs and runbook

Priya Nair (reviewer): Concern about telemetry cardinality — are we aggregating per-tenant at the right resolution to avoid high ingestion cost?
Olivia Park (author): The controller consumes aggregated rollups produced by existing sampling aggregator (internal/telemetry/metrics_costs.go) at 1m granularity. We added a config knob to lower to 5m for high-cardinality tenants. Added notes to runbook.

payload.body:
Context: We observed recurring tail-latency spikes on token generation workloads driven by sporadic cold misses in the paged KV cache. Existing pinning strategies (full-span sticky pins) reduce miss rate but increase memory pressure and harm throughput under mixed workloads. This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: 1) a lightweight, trainable hotset predictor that drives proactive asynchronous prefetching for likely-needed KV pages, and 2) a sparse-pin coordinator that pins only a sampled subset of page spans based on access probability and epoch stability heuristics. Together these reduce cold-miss latency while keeping resident working set size bounded. Goals: reduce 95/99th token latency for long-chat workloads, keep average token throughput stable under bursty traffic, and avoid regressing memory utilization for multi-tenant Dedicated pools. What changed (high level): - new hotset predictor module (serving/cache/hotset_predictor.{rs,py}): uses an exponential-weighted frequency sketch + tiny exponentially decaying LSTM-lite model (feature-engineered) for per-model hotness score; cold start tuned to avoid aggressive prefetch. - async prefetcher (serving/cache/async_prefetch.{rs}): issues low-priority non-blocking prefetch requests to the block manager; integrates with scheduler to respect latency SLOs and capacity quotas. - sparse-pin coordinator (serving/cache/sparse_pin_coordinator.{rs}): replaces sticky span pins with epoched sparse pins; pins are probabilistic and promoted when repeated hits occur within an epoch. - scheduler hints and kernel integration (serving/runtime/scheduler_hints.{rs}, runtime/kernels/kv_hinting.h): prefetch/pin hints are exposed to the runtime kernel selection layer to prefer lower-latency execution paths for predicted-hot requests. - metrics, tracing, unit and microbench tests (observability/metrics_hotset.md, tests/kv_prefetch_tests/*, bench/continuous_batching_prefetch_bench). Performance summary (benchmarks run on Dedicated dev cluster with A100s): - 95th token latency improved by 18% on long-chat trace (1000-3000 tokens) with mixed concurrency (20-60 clients). - 99th token latency improved by 24% on same trace. - End-to-end tokens/sec unchanged (within +/- 4%) for steady-state high-throughput runs; under bursty tail scenarios throughput improved by up to 10% due to fewer blocking cache fills. - Resident memory usage grew by ~3.2% on average for workloads with high locality; for low-locality workloads sparse-pin coordinator reduced peak resident set by ~6% vs previous sticky pins. Safety and operational controls: - prefetch throttles are on a per-customer quota and global circuit-breaker. - feature is behind a runtime flag (redwood.runtime.features.prefetch_predictor) and rollout controlled via console. - onboarded canary tests in perf-canary repo to exercise bursts and low-locality mixes. Rollout plan: - Step 1: internal canary (10% of Hosted traffic) with aggressive logging for two weeks. - Step 2: Dedicated pools opt-in via console; default off for existing Dedicated customers. - Step 3: gradual ramp to 50% if metrics stable. Motivation and trade-offs: The predictor purposely favors conservative precision to avoid wasteful prefetch; we found that false positive prefetches are cheaper than synchronous blocking misses but only up to a point, hence the sparse-pin approach which narrows what gets pinned. This design reduces tail-latency but requires careful quota management and visibility to customers. Related work: builds on previous allocator improvements (see ENG-4321-style block coalescing), but intentionally orthogonal to the block-pool compaction changes in PRs that focused on defragmentation. See linked Linear tasks for tuning experiments.
Jonah Li: Please add a safety cutoff so prefetch can't exceed X% of bandwidth during cold starts. - Addressed in async_prefetch throttle and added tests.
María Ortega: The LSTM-lite model looks promising but we should add a non-ML fallback that uses simple EWMA counts in case customers disable models. - Added hotset_predictor.py fallback and a runtime toggle.
Evan Chen: Can you quantify memory accounting per tenant when pinned spans are promoted? Edge cases for multi-tenant we should document. - Added per-tenant accounting and docs section; included a canary to validate isolation.
Performance CI: initial run flagged flaky bench; reran with -j1 and confirmed improvements are stable.

Motivation: Some upstream open checkpoint variants and third-party model binaries sometimes omit token-level logprobs or produce incomplete logprob payloads when streaming tool/function outputs. Client integrations (and the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compat layer) expect consistent presence or a clearly defined fallback behavior; otherwise SDKs and streaming consumers must special-case many rare models. Separately, fragmented tool outputs (tool responses emitted in multiple partial stream frames) caused out-of-order 'end-of-tool' markers in a small number of production traces, leading to truncated tool results for function-calling flows.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a configurable logprobs_fallback_policy to the OpenAI compatibility adapter that supports three strategies: "prefer_model" (use model-provided logprobs if present), "synthesize" (estimate per-token logprobs using a light-weight softmax approximation over top-k logits when the model omits them), and "omit" (leave logprobs absent and mark the message metadata). Default remains "prefer_model" to preserve historical surface. 2) Implements a stream-boundary-synchronizer in the runtime streaming coordinator that buffers and sequences tool/function fragments until a definite terminal token or explicit tool_complete sentinel is observed, then emits deterministic framed events to the client. The synchronizer also exposes heuristics for max-fragment-linger and early-flush to avoid unbounded buffering. 3) Normalizes stop param variants from OpenAI-form inputs (string | array | null) into a canonical array at the compatibility layer and ensures stop tokens are honored consistently across synthesized logprob paths. 4) Adds a diagnostic flag `x-rw-debug-stream-fragments` to trace fragment reassembly for egress logs without leaking PII.

Compatibility notes: This change keeps the external /v1/chat.completions surface unchanged; new behavior is controlled by an adapter-level config flag and a small optional parameter (`logprobs_fallback_policy`) in the wire for advanced customers. Synthesis uses only top-k logits (k configurable, default 16) and is disabled for models that do not expose logits at all.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests cover param coercion permutations, synthesized logprob consistency checks, and stream fragment ordering. Integration tests run a small simulated runner that emits fragmented tool payloads. Feature gated behind a runtime flag and released with a canary rollout to 5% of hosted traffic before full rollout.

Related work: ENG-1934 (stream fragment coordinator), ENG-2110 (openai compat param normalization), SUP-5271 (support ticket reproducing missing logprobs).
Jordan Malik (2026-02-13): Do we have guardrails for synth policy skewing token probabilities in downstream safety evals? If synthesized logprobs differ materially it could affect reranking/filters.
Ava Chen (2026-02-13): Reply: synthesis is explicitly excluded from training or safety signals by default. We add a metadata flag `logprobs_source` set to 'synthesized' when fallback is used. We also added a test assert that KL divergence vs model-provided probs (when available) is within a conservative threshold for the sampled top-k set.
Leah Kim (2026-02-15): Nit: add a unit test for the null stop param case coming from older clients. Also the TS SDK normalization should keep order for arrays — currently it coerces to Set semantics in one place.
Ava Chen (2026-02-16): Reply: fixed the TS coercion to preserve ordering and added null-case unit tests. Updated files_changed to include the test.
Mateo Alvarez (2026-02-17): Approve with comment: the early-flush heuristic threshold default (100ms) might be aggressive for high-latency backends; consider exposing as tunable per-destination.
Ava Chen (2026-02-18): Follow-up: made early-flush configurable via runtime routing metadata and documented the knob in observability docs.
Added configurable logprobs_fallback_policy to the OpenAI v1 compat adapter (prefer_model | synthesize | omit). Introduced stream-boundary-synchronizer to deterministically reassemble fragmented tool/function outputs; default behavior preserves backwards compatibility and is behind a runtime canary flag. SDKs updated to expose the new optional parameter.
Enable feature flag `compat.logprob_fallback_canary` to start 5% rollout. Monitor metric rw.stream.fragments.reassembled.count and rw.compat.logprobs.fallback.count. If synthesized fallback exceeds 0.5% of traffic in a customer environment unexpectedly, contact infra@redwood for rollback guidance.

Motivation: We observed tail regressions and elevated spill rates under mixed-length streaming workloads where hot small-context requests repeatedly displaced long-lived KV pages. This PR introduces the "pagedrag orchestrator" (a lightweight scheduler that prevents hot small-key churn from dragging cold large pages into spill paths) and the "fragmentation healer" (adaptive compaction windows that heal micro-fragmentation without full stop-the-world compaction). Design summary: 1) PageHeatScore - a combined metric of recency, write density and sequence-length bias which feeds both eviction and compaction decisions. 2) Locality buckets - pages are tracked by tenant-locality and sequence-length histograms so eviction favors low-locality/low-value pages. 3) Soft-quarantine lanes - recently-evicted small pages enter a probation lane for a bounded window to avoid repeated promote/evict cycles. 4) Pagedrag orchestrator - a scheduler hook that defers heavy compaction or spill-triggering actions during continuous-batching bursts, instead staging pages into a low-priority background queue with backoff. 5) Fragmentation healer - incremental in-place compaction that targets high-fragmentation segments using tenant-aware lease windows to avoid IO spikes. Backwards compatibility and rollout: default flags disabled, auto-enable for Dedicated clusters after canary. No changes to external APIs. Benchmarks & results: synthetic mixed streaming benchmark (50% small chat tokens, 50% long-context embeddings) shows 28% reduction in KV background CPU, 12% lower p95 token latency on small requests (due to fewer KV misses), and 45% fewer full-disk spill cycles in our canary cluster over 48h. Implementation notes: core logic in src/runtime/kv_cache/pagedrag_orchestrator.rs, fragmentation heuristics in src/runtime/kv_cache/fragmentation_healer.rs, scheduler hooks in src/runtime/scheduler/priority_hints.rs, new unit & simulation tests under tests/kv_simulator/, and docs/perf/kv_pagedrag.md documenting knobs and rollout recipe. Rollout plan: canary to 3% host pool, observe spill/sla for 72h, then 25% with guardrails, automatic rollback if spill rate increases >10% or p99 latency regresses.

Lena Park (author): Added state machine comments and extra unit test covering lane transitions.
Priya Raman: Could we add a microbenchmark for compaction cost so we can tune window sizes automatically?
Lena Park: Added a simple cost-estimator and an experimental autotune flag (disabled by default) documented in kv_pagedrag.md.
Marco Giuliani: CI flake on test_probation_lane — looks like a timeout on CI runner. Requesting increase in simulated timeouts.
Lena Park: Increased test timeouts and mocked the monotonic clock for determinism; CI green now.
Initial CI showed a transient integration timeout on test_probation_lane; fixed timeouts and deterministic clock mocks. Final CI run: all checks passed (unit, integration, flake8/rustfmt, cross-platform simulation).
Introduces pagedrag orchestrator and fragmentation healer for KV cache: reduces thrash and spill cycles in mixed streaming workloads. Disabled by default; enable via kv_pagedrag flags for Dedicated clusters. See docs/perf/kv_pagedrag.md for tuning and rollout guidance.
Canary observed expected improvements. Ops playbook added to docs for emergency rollback (flip kv_pagedrag.enabled=false) and for toggling probation window sizes.

Motivation: transient spikes and noisy tenants were causing sudden SLO violations when our admission controller applied a binary denylist during overload windows. Binary denylists were too blunt: low-volume noisy tenants would be fully blocked while higher-impact noisy tenants kept consuming capacity, producing uneven service degradation and noisy SLO signals. This PR introduces an SLO Sentinel subsystem that implements a graded denylist (per-tenant penalty scores with configurable enforcement tiers) and a complementary backfill recovery mechanism to ensure capacity reclaimed by eviction is used to reduce overall SLO drift rather than causing sharp latency drops elsewhere.

What this change does (summary):
- Introduces graded denylist logic in the admission controller: tenants are assigned a penalty score computed from recent error/latency SLO signals and request surge profile. Enforcement is tiered: soft-warn, rate-cap, partial-deny (probabilistic drop), and hard-deny.
- Adds a backfill recovery agent in the scheduler that tracks reclaimed capacity from denied requests, and backfills queued requests from low-penalty tenants before escalating to hard-deny for others. Backfill is throttled to respect node-level latency budgets.
- Metric and tracing additions for observability: new counters and histograms (redwood.slo.sentinel.penalty_score, redwood.slo.sentinel.enforcement_level_total, redwood.slo.sentinel.backfill_success_total, redwood.slo.sentinel.backfill_latency_ms) and a SLO tag (slo_loss_reason) on request spans to surface denylist-driven degradation.
- Control-plane config: introduces a SLO Sentinel policy CRD (for Private deployments) and new config flags in the hosted control plane for tuning tier thresholds and backfill aggressiveness.
- Safety and rollout: default policy starts in soft-warn mode (no drops) for 72 hours, then automatically enables rate-cap in permissive mode; can be toggled per-customer.
- Tests: unit tests for penalty score computation, integration test (simulated multi-tenant overload) verifying graceful degradation, and e2e smoke for backfill under partial-deny.

Files and areas changed (high level):
- runtime/admission/sentinel.go (new): graded denylist core and enforcement API;
- runtime/admission/policies.go (update): hooks to read penalty and enforce tiers;
- scheduler/backfill_agent.go (new): capacity bookkeeping and backfill algorithms;
- controlplane/policies/sentinel_policy.yaml (new): CRD and default policy;
- telemetry/metrics_registry.go (update): register new metrics and sampling logic;
- docs/observability/slo-sentinel.md (new): runbook and metric meanings;
- tests/unit/sentinel_test.go (new), tests/integration/sentinel_overload_sim.go (new), tests/e2e/backfill_smoke.yaml (new).

Commits (summary):
- feat(admission): add graded penalty computation and tiered enforcement (Maya Chen)
- feat(scheduler): implement backfill recovery agent and throttle policy (Maya Chen)
- chore(controlplane): add sentinel policy CRD and default permissive policy (Maya Chen)
- feat(telemetry): register sentinel metrics and annotate spans with slo_loss_reason (Maya Chen)
- test: add unit/integration/e2e tests for sentinel and backfill (Maya Chen)
- fix(lint): address golangci lint errors found by CI (Maya Chen)
- docs: add SLO Sentinel observability and tuning guide (Maya Chen)

Review conversation (high level):
- Arjun requested reducing global lock contention in penalty computation and suggested switching to atomic windows rather than a single mutex around the tenant record.
- Author reply: replaced global lock with tenant-local sharded counters and used atomics for hot-path score updates; updated tests for concurrency.
- Lena flagged metric cardinality risk for per-tenant histograms; requested aggregation knobs.
- Author reply: removed per-tenant histograms from the hot path and added aggregated percentiles plus an opt-in per-tenant debug histogram behind config.
- Samir asked for a safety rollback switch and a staged rollout plan for hosted customers.
- Author reply: added a feature-flag gate and a 72-hour soft-warn default policy plus an emergency disable endpoint for operators.
- CI initially: lint failed (golangci had a nil-check warning) and one flaky integration test failed on first run. After fixes: CI passed all checks.

Why this is safe to merge:
- Backfill logic only activates once the enforcement tier is at or above rate-cap unless explicitly enabled in config; default behavior is soft-warn (no request drops).
- New metrics and runbook included so SREs can monitor impact in the first 72 hours.
- Includes unit/integ/e2e tests and a rollback feature flag.

Migration and operational notes:
- Private customers can install the new CRD via controlplane upgrade; sample sentinel_policy.yaml provided.
- SDKs unaffected; API surface unchanged.
- Observability: dashboards in the Console will be extended in a follow-up PR to plot penalty distribution and backfill effectiveness.

Follow-ups (planned):
- Console dashboarding and alert thresholds for sentinel metrics (ENG-4902).
- Adaptive penalty tuning using model-based anomaly scores (research spike ENG-4977).
- Per-tenant debug view and timeline in Console for customers on Dedicated plans.

Related work: references many prior soft-shed and graceful-fallback efforts (ENG-27109, ENG-314271, SUP-3912), but this PR focuses on per-tenant graded enforcement and actively using reclaimed capacity for backfill instead of leaving it idle.

Merge outcome: squash and merge after approvals; post-merge deploy gated by feature flag rollout and a 72-hour soft-warn observation window.
Arjun: Locking in penalty computation needs reducing; can we shard tenant state and use atomics?
Maya: replaced mutex with tenant-local shards and atomics; added concurrency unit tests.
Lena: per-tenant histograms will explode cardinality; add aggregation and opt-in per-tenant histograms behind config.
Maya: removed hot-path per-tenant histograms; added aggregated percentiles and config opt-in.
Samir: add an emergency disable and staged rollout plan for hosted; include documentation for SREs.
Maya: added feature-flag gate, emergency disable endpoint, and runbook in docs.
CI: initial run failed lint; fix applied and CI passed on rerun.
Arjun: approved after lock changes; Lena: approved after metric aggregation; Samir: approved after rollout plan.

Context and goal: presubmit job start-up time and noisy short-lived runners have been a major source of feedback delay and flakiness for teams. This PR reduces cold-start latency for the majority of PRs by consolidating presubmit runner pools, standardizing a slim preflight image, and introducing a merge-prober (Release Peacekeeper) that gates merges briefly to catch transient CI flakiness and release automation race conditions. Summary of changes: 1) Add a lightweight presubmit bootstrap image (ci/images/presubmit-slim.Dockerfile) optimized for common language toolchains and with layered caching for pip/go/npm installs; 2) Rework .github/workflows/presubmit.yml to introduce fast/slow lanes and to run a trimmed lint/smoke set in the fast lane; 3) Consolidate presubmit worker pool definitions to ci/runner/pools.yaml and add pool affinity rules to reduce runner churn; 4) Add a merge-prober service (ci/tools/merge_prober/) that watches merge events and re-triggers a short sanity check across a matrix before the final merge commit; 5) Pin several GitHub Action SHAs and bump action-tooling in .github/actions/ to reduce unexpected upgrades; 6) Refresh lockfiles (package-lock.json, go.sum) and update small transitive deps flagged by dep-audit. Why this is safe: the slim presubmit image runs only a curated set of checks by default; full integration tests remain on the slow lane. The merge-prober intentionally runs a short set of smoke checks and will not block manual merges with an override label if an urgent hotfix is required. Related: ENG-9876 (presubmit perf), ENG-1023 (release hardening), SUP-412 (customer incident that motivated faster feedback). Checklist: - [x] CI green on fast/slow lanes - [x] pool size validated in staging - [x] no regressions in lint output - [x] docs updated (docs/dev/ci-presubmit.md) - [x] rollback plan documented (ci/rollback/README.md). Commits: see commits array below. Files changed (high level): see files_changed array below. Review conversation (short): reviewers asked for clearer signal boundaries between fast and slow lanes and for an opt-out for large repos; implemented by adding explicit path filters and a repository-level opt-out label. Priya requested that the merge-prober retry logic back off exponentially; updated accordingly. Liam validated the pinned action SHAs and ran a canary across 10 repos. CI results: initial lint flake due to a transitive eslint rule, fixed by a lockfile refresh; subsequent CI pass on main matrix. Merge notes: merged by squash after two approvals and a final canary run across staging. Post-merge actions: monitor presubmit latency metric (ci.presubmit.startup_ms) for 72 hours, watch requeue rate and merge-prober false-positive rate, and follow up with a staged rollout of pool consolidation if any service team reports regression.
Reduce presubmit cold-start latency; Merge-prober prevents transient green merges; Consolidated presubmit pools reduce flakiness; Updated several GitHub Actions to pinned SHAs; Small dependency bumps and lockfile refresh.

Ava Martinez: Added repo-level opt-out label and path-filter rules; merged exponential backoff into retry loop

Motivation: Customers repeatedly ask for safe, opinionated defaults for batching, caching and quantization tailored to common workload archetypes. Ad-hoc defaults have drifted across components; operators end up copying heuristics into tenant configs. This PR introduces a small, auditable DSL ("recipes") and an accompanying CLI linter 'costchef' to generate, validate, and suggest tenant-level prefill/batching/caching/quant defaults.

What this PR does: - Adds a recipes schema and canonical set of three starter recipes (conversational-light, high-throughput-short, embedding-batch). Recipes encode: preferred batch shapes, kv-cache windowing, warmup prefills, quantization profile hints (int8/int4-fallbacks), and safe rollback thresholds. - Implements a lightweight server-side resolver that maps tenant workload tags to a chosen recipe and emits enforcement suggestions through the routing layer (no automatic enforcement in this PR). - Adds costchef CLI: validate <recipe>, diff <tenant-config> <recipe>, suggest <tenant-id> --dry-run. The CLI also runs an econ-linter that flags recipe constructs likely to increase unit-cost without latency benefit (e.g. large batch windows for sub-20 token median). - Adds unit tests, integration tests for the resolver, and a docs page with examples and migration notes.

Design notes and safety: Recipes are intentionally conservative: every hint has an associated fallback and a stability score. The resolver uses a deterministic scoring function (tenant usage histogram vs recipe signature) so suggestions are reproducible. This PR takes the conservative path: suggestions are emitted as config proposals and telemetry only; applying them requires an operator action (future PRs will add canary rollouts).

Checklist: - [x] schema, starter recipes, and recipe loader - [x] resolver & mapping logic - [x] costchef CLI + lint rules - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs page and example cURLs - [x] changelog entry + release notes

Related: ENG-4231 (prefill defaults project), SUP-1298 (tenant asking for automated suggestions). For usage examples see docs/prefill-recipes.md and the CLI help.

Notes for reviewers: the key behavioral change is the resolver suggestion stream; the serving runtime is not altered in this PR. I focused on test coverage for the default heuristics; please pay attention to the econ-linter thresholds (src/cli/costchef/lint_rules.py) and the mapping function in optimizer/recipe_resolver.py.

Operational impact: ships as a non-breaking addition. No database migrations. The resolver reads recipes from the same config bucket used for tenant defaults. Backwards-compatible: if no recipe matches, behavior is unchanged.
Daniel Morales (2025-08-11): Nice direction — two asks: 1) can we add a simple perf-smoke that measures median p95 token latency for the three starter recipes on a small model so we can ensure no regression? 2) Move the econ thresholds into a single config file so SRE can tune them without code changes.

Adds a clearer, backwards-compatible retry and idempotency contract for the OpenAI compatibility layer and API gateway. This PR introduces an opaque backoff token header (X-Redwood-Backoff-Token) and normalizes Retry-After parsing to accept three canonical formats: numeric seconds, HTTP-date string, and a new 't=<unix_ts>' timestamp form in order to reduce ambiguity across clients and proxies. Also formalizes a structured error envelope field 'retry_hint' and 'backoff_token' in JSON error bodies returned by the compatibility shim and the runtime. Motivation: customers hit intermittent 429s and ambiguous retry semantics when proxying through older HTTP clients and when streaming function/tool calls; different SDKs parsed Retry-After inconsistently which caused retries to happen too early or not at all. This PR implements parsing/serialization in the API gateway, maps legacy Retry-After values to the canonical envelope in the OpenAI adapter, and surfaces an opaque backoff token that encodes server-side backoff state for more precise backoff duration estimation across retries and across routed fallbacks. The change includes: compatibility layer mapping rules, SDK-compat tests, updated end-to-end test scenarios for multiplexed streams, a migration/compatibility guide in docs, and a short deprecation timeline for legacy Retry-After-only reliance. Rollout plan: feature-flagged for two weeks, telemetry monitoring enabled for backoff-token usage, staged SDK updates recommended but server will continue to accept older Retry-After formats for 90 days. See release notes for client migration guidance.

Summary: Adds a 'privilege-cage' enforcement layer to RBAC v2 which can enforce short-term throttles on high-privilege operator roles, route KMS calls through a consumption sandbox adapter for accounting and safe-failover, and enrich audit events with consumption buckets and dry-run indicators. Motivation: incidents over the last quarter showed operators and automation agents consuming disproportionate KMS quotas during emergency flows, increasing latency and SLO risk. This PR gives platform teams a way to cap and observe operator-level KMS consumption, run dry-runs, and progressively enforce via feature flag.

Design highlights: privilege_cage middleware (services/authz) inspects RBAC v2 decision, looks up temporal throttles from policy cache, and either allows, rate-limits, or short-circuits requests. KMS sandbox adapter (infra/kms) is an in-process proxy that annotates requests with a sandbox-id, enforces per-operator consumption budgets, and can route to a safe-fallback KMS provider on budget exhaustion. Audit fanout sanitizer records pre/post consumption estimates, bucket labels, and whether the request was enforcement or dry-run. All persisted as structured audit fields for downstream compliance pipelines.

Rollout plan: gated behind 'privilege_caging' feature flag. Step 1: enable read-only dry-run globally to populate telemetry (two weeks). Step 2: soft-enforce for a small subset of tenants (canary) and monitor alarms. Step 3: full enforcement for operator roles after OK from compliance and SRE.

- [x] Middleware implementation and unit tests
- [x] KMS sandbox adapter and integration tests with mock KMS
- [x] Audit enrichment and retention config updates
- [x] Feature flag + config schema migration

Testing: added end-to-end integration harness exercising per-operator budget exhaustion, fallback routing, and audit emission. Load tests simulating operator spikes were run in benchmark-lab with observed KMS consumption isolation and <3% end-to-end latency impact under typical traffic.

Backward compatibility and migration: policy cache schema extended with optional TemporalThrottle metadata. If absent, legacy behavior is unchanged. KMS sandbox adapter exposes a pass-through mode when the 'sandbox_mode' config is off.

Security considerations: sandbox adapter signs sandboxed requests with a short-lived operator-bound token; audit records include only pseudo-identifiers when configured for residency/anonymization. See docs/security/privilege-caging.md for details.

Motivation: CI runtime and flakiness have been increasing with a wide lint/test matrix and global monolithic entrypoints. This PR extracts lint adapters into a small registry, introduces atomic build hooks to make release steps idempotent, and wires a dependency-provenance helper to support staged dependency upgrades. Approach: 1) Add tools/lint/plugins/registry.py and a minimal plugin API so language-specific linters load only for changed packages. 2) Introduce tools/build/profiles.yaml with 'fast-dev' and 'full-ci' profiles; CI workflows now select profile by changed path heuristics. 3) Replace heavy one-shot release script with .github/workflows/release-staging.yml that runs atomic hooks (preflight, package-stage, tag-and-bump) and records provenance. 4) Add scripts/dep_provenance.py to emit a small JSON manifest used by the release automation and dependency updater. 5) Update Makefile and dev container to expose the lightweight runner. Impact: expected median CI duration reduced for PRs touching single-language packages; lower noise from irrelevant linters; safer, restartable release flow with provenance artifacts for audits. Migration: ops: run tools/lint/plugins/register_local.py once in CI runner image migration window; repo: no manual changes required but maintainers can opt into per-package plugin configs under .lintrc. Rollback: remove registry flag and restore previous workflows if needed; all changes are guarded behind conditional selectors and tested in staging. Testing: unit tests for registry adapter loading and atomic hook idempotency added; integration smoke job 'release-staging/smoke' introduced that runs on a synthetic package. CI: initial run had one flaky smoke failure (reproducible locally) fixed by introducing a 250ms backoff in the hook runner; subsequent full CI passed. See commit list and CI checks below.
Adds a lint plugin registry (language-aware adapters loaded on-demand), introduces an atomic build hook mechanism for staged release automation, and adds lightweight 'fast-dev' and 'full-ci' build profiles. Reduces CI matrix and prepares metadata for safer dependency rollouts.

Implements retention/TTL enforcement for the audit logs storage layer and wires it into the control-plane retention policy evaluator. This is a core dependency for the “Retention controls + compliance reporting pack” project (ENG-18434). Summary: (1) Adds a background purge job for audit logs using the purge job framework (PR #28489). (2) Evaluates effective retention policy per tenant + region + data class (audit_logs) via the control plane evaluator (ADR-017 / PR #28427). (3) Enforces safe defaults and guardrails: minimum TTL by tier, optional legal hold override (no deletes while hold is active), and deletion safety limits to avoid DB pressure. (4) Adds verification metrics for TTL lag + deletion counts + failures with labels constrained to avoid cardinality blowups. (5) Adds integration tests covering policy changes, cache invalidation, and idempotent purge runs.

Implementation details (high level):
- New scheduled job: AuditLogTtlPurgeJob (runs per shard, per tenant batch). Pulls candidates by created_at < now - ttl, deletes in bounded batches, and emits metrics.
- Retention resolution: uses RetentionPolicyEvaluator.getEffectivePolicy(tenant_id, region, data_class='audit_logs') and caches results for 60s; invalidated on policy change events.
- Legal hold: if hold is active for tenant (or incident hold is set), purge job skips and emits audit_logs_ttl_hold_skipped_total.
- Safety: deletion batch size defaults to 5k rows, hard cap 50k rows per run per shard; job yields between batches.

DB notes:
- Adds/validates supporting index on (tenant_id, created_at) for audit_logs table to keep deletes bounded.

Illustrative snippet:
- cutoff = now() - effective_ttl; delete where tenant_id = ? AND created_at < cutoff LIMIT batch_size;

Testing:
- Unit tests for policy evaluation wiring + hold semantics.
- Integration tests (dockerized PG) validating purge idempotency + policy cache invalidation.

Rollout:
- Feature-flagged by store: audit_logs_ttl_enforcement_enabled (default off).
- Staged enablement plan in ENG-18434: internal -> design partners -> GA.

Follow-ups (not in this PR):
- Dashboard + alerts wiring (ENG-18452; metrics are emitted here but dashboards ship separately).
- Exporter packaging attachment of retention config (audit-log-exporter PR #627).

Risk/mitigation:
- Risk: large backlogs causing DB pressure. Mitigation: hard caps per run + per-tenant batching + visibility via ttl_lag_seconds and backlog gauge.
Marcus Lin (review): Can we confirm the purge job will not delete audit events required for security incident response when customers set extremely low TTLs? Also, what’s the behavior under legal hold?
Kevin Osei (author): Guardrails are enforced in the evaluator (min TTL by tier). Additionally, if legal hold is active we skip deletion entirely (and emit a metric). For incident response, min TTL for Hosted/Dedicated is 30d; Private can go lower only when customer-managed and explicitly configured.
Sean Gallagher (review): Please add a hard cap per run to prevent DB pressure and add a backoff/yield between delete batches. Also request metrics need to be low-cardinality.
Kevin Osei (author): Added cap 50k rows/run/shard, default batch 5k, with yield between batches. Metrics labels are limited to {store, region, result} and tenant_id is NOT included.
Jordan Lee (review): Cache invalidation: how do we ensure policy changes take effect quickly? 60s seems okay but we need explicit invalidation on change history updates.
Kevin Osei (author): Hooked invalidation to retention policy change events (control plane). Added integration test that updates policy and asserts cutoff changes without waiting for TTL expiry of cache.
Logan Wright (review): Nice. One nit: the ttl_lag_seconds calculation should be based on oldest-undeleted record vs cutoff; otherwise we’ll miss backlogs when job is capped.
Kevin Osei (author): Updated lag metric to compute (now - ttl) - min(created_at among remaining eligible candidates), with guard when none exist. Added a test for capped run scenario.
Priya Natarajan (review): Ship it once the migration guard is safe in multi-tenant partitions. Also please link SUP-3917 since it’s related to missing event types — not caused by TTL but the same customer will ask.
Kevin Osei (author): Added migration check to no-op if index already exists (for partial deployments) and linked SUP-3917 in the PR metadata/notes. TTL enforcement is behind a feature flag, default off.
CI bot: integration tests failed (timeout) on first run.
Kevin Osei (author): Re-ran; looks like a flaky runner issue. Added a small sleep jitter in the test harness around job scheduling to reduce contention.
Marcus Lin (approval): Approved. Please ensure the runbook mentions hold semantics and who can enable the flag.
Sean Gallagher (approval): Approved after caps + metric constraints.
Jordan Lee (approval): Approved.
Logan Wright (approval): Approved.
Audit logs retention enforcement can now be enabled (feature-flagged) using the retention policy evaluator; includes purge job, hold semantics, and verification metrics.

Summary: Add a focused credential memoization layer across SDKs and introduce a lightweight stream adapter that reduces allocation churn, improves backpressure signaling, and harmonizes retry hints between Python/TypeScript/Go. Motivation: We saw recurring hot-path overhead from credential lookups and excessive per-chunk allocations in high-throughput streaming customers (internal canary). This PR reduces token-path auth calls, provides a small in-memory memo for short-lived credentials, and replaces a heavyweight stream wrapper with a zero-copy-friendly adapter that surfaces retry/backoff hints to the transport layer.

Changes included (high level):
- New cross-language credential memoization module (ttl-based, fast-path lookup, opt-out). Implemented in core client layer and exposed as an optional config in each SDK.
- Lightweight StreamAdapter: a smaller internal abstraction that exposes explicit pause/resume hooks, consumer-visible ProgressHints, and a typed transient error wrapper used by retry policies.
- AdaptiveRetryAdapter: glues transport errors and ProgressHints into adaptive backoff selection (latency-aware).
- Minor ergonomic surface changes: clearer async generator docstrings/examples, a dedicated 'close_gracefully' helper, and improved type comments for TS/Go.
- Tests and benchmarks: unit tests for TTL memo, integration tests for streaming resume, and a micro-benchmark showing ~22% reduction in per-request auth latency and ~15% lower allocations in stream-heavy scenarios.

Commits (summary):
- 9c2b1d3: Introduce cred memo interface + Python/TS/Go implementations and feature flags.
- 4f7e2a9: Replace StreamWrapper with StreamAdapter; wire ProgressHints into transport layer.
- a7d9c3b: Add AdaptiveRetryAdapter and update retry presets to consult ProgressHints.
- b1f0e5a: Docs examples, migration notes, and changelog entries; add unit + integration tests.

Files/areas touched (illustrative):
- sdk/core/auth/memo.go (Go) - TTL memo + lru-lite
- sdk/py/redwood/auth/memo.py - TTL memo + opt-out config
- sdk/ts/src/auth/credMemo.ts - lightweight memo implementation
- sdk/*/stream/adapter.* - new adapter implementations for each SDK
- sdk/*/retry/adaptive_adapter.* - adapter glue for retry selection
- docs/sdk/auth.md - new section describing memo tradeoffs and toggles
- examples/streaming/stream_retry_hints - updated example that uses close_gracefully and ProgressHints

Compatibility / migration notes:
- Default behavior remains unchanged for existing customers; memoization is enabled by default but limited to a conservative TTL (30s) and a small entry cap to avoid long-lived caching of rotated credentials. Ops teams can opt-out via client config or environment toggle.
- StreamAdapter is an internal refactor that preserves public async/iterator ergonomics; consumers using private internal wrapper types must update (rare). We added a compatibility shim for one release cycle.

Benchmarks & testing:
- Micro-bench harness under benchmark-lab shows median auth lookup reduced by 22% under our canary workload (many short-lived stream requests).
- Streaming allocation profiler demonstrates ~15% reduction in allocations per chunk with the new adapter in the Node runtime.
- CI ran full unit test matrix across py/ts/go, integration streaming tests in CI sandbox, and performance smoke tests in perf-canary. All checks passed on final run.

Review conversation (high level extract):
- Omar Li: "Nice, this addresses a clear hotspot we measured. Two asks: ensure TTL is configurable and add opt-out; and include a brief note for infra about potential KMS traffic changes."
- Nadia Park (author): "TTL is configurable via client opts (doc added). KMS traffic should be unchanged since we only short-circuit local credential lookups; added note to ops as requested."
- Priya Shah: "Can the ProgressHints be extended later to include percent-complete? I want to avoid API churn."
- Nadia Park: "We intentionally kept ProgressHints minimal (bytes/chunks/last-event) to avoid surface area growth; percent-complete can be added but will be additive-only and annotated in the doc. Added a unit test to ensure extension won't break adapters."
- Ethan Moore: "Small nit: rename close() -> close_gracefully() to signal flush semantics."
- Nadia Park: "Renamed and updated examples."

CI history: initial run flagged a flaky TS test (stream-chunk-order) — root cause: nondeterministic setImmediate ordering in our test harness. Fix committed in a7d9c3b and rerun. Final CI summary: all checks green (unit, lint, integration, perf-smoke).

Why this approach: The memoization solves frequent short-lived auth lookups (hosted auth rotations and delegated tokens) without introducing long-term caching risks. The StreamAdapter reduces allocation churn and gives the runtime explicit hints to make smarter retry/backoff choices under partial-progress conditions (e.g., intermittent network stalls). Keeping the change opt-out and conservative by default preserves safety for enterprise customers with strict key rotation rules.

Risk assessment: Low-medium. Main risk is mis-caching long-lived credentials; mitigations: small default TTL, explicit opt-out, and telemetry to surface unusual hit rates. We added a guardrail that emits a metric when an entry exceeds 5x the configured TTL.

Merge: Squash-merged to main on 2025-11-07 after approvals from Omar Li and Priya Shah.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-4521: Add telemetry dashboards for memo hit/miss and oversized entries (next sprint).
- ENG-4598: Backfill minimal examples and bump SDK minor versions (py: 2.14.0 -> 2.15.0, ts: 1.28.0 -> 1.29.0, go: v1.8.0 -> v1.9.0).

Notes for release: include short doc blurb in the SDK changelogs and a compatibility note in the Private installer upgrade guide.
Improved cross-SDK credential memoization and a slimmer streaming adapter - non-breaking. Suggest SDK version minor bumps for Go/Python/TS to pick up ergonomics and perf fixes.

Context: Production chat and short-sequence workloads show high per-token overhead from attention kernel dispatch and excessive KV cache churn when multiple low-latency requests are interleaved. This PR introduces a new rotary-aware attention kernel that performs asynchronous prefetching of Q/K/V tiles and a hybrid-striping scheduler that balances warp-level striping with bank-coalesced micro-tiles. In addition, an adaptive KV cache gating mechanism is added to reduce memory thrash for streaming workloads.

What this PR does (high level): - Adds a new CUDA kernel (async_prefetch_attn) that prefetches rotated KV prefixes asynchronously while computing QK product, avoiding a strict blocking fetch for common rotary/rope layouts. The kernel is rotary-aware (computes sin/cos transforms fused into the prefetch path). - Implements a hybrid-striping scheduler that chooses between warp-striping and micro-tile striping based on sequence length distribution and batch shape heuristics. This reduces bank conflicts on medium-short sequences (<=512) while preserving throughput on long sequences. - Adds adaptive KV cache gating: a runtime policy that decides when to materialize KV entries for in-flight contexts vs. reference-prefetch-only paths to reduce memory pressure on multi-session streaming. - Introduces scheduler hooks and config knobs (hybrid_striping_mode, async_prefetch_enable, kv_cache_gating_threshold) exposed through the runtime config API and Redwood Console. - Adds microbenchmarks, unit and integration tests, and documentation for the new kernel and knobs.

Motivation: Teams running interactive assistants and streaming pipelines saw tail-latency amplification when many short requests shared GPU pools. The combination of prefetch stalls and KV cache churn was the primary contributor. This change targets those hotspots with an optimized kernel and a smarter scheduling policy.

Compatibility and rollout: The kernel is guarded behind a runtime feature flag (async_prefetch_enable=false by default for private installs). For hosted/dedicated we enabled it in canary pools with automatic fallback to the existing flashbridge kernel when the new kernel fails or when CUDA capability/driver versions are unsupported. The PR also includes runtime detection for CUDA >= 11.8 and a safe fallback path.

Benchmarks: See performance_summary field for a short summary. Full benchmark scripts are in tests/bench.

Notes: The description contains implementation rationale and a short checklist. See release_notes for user-visible items.
Microbenchmarks (A100, fp16 accumulation enabled, continuous batching on): median latency down 10-18% for sequences <=64, p95 down 8-12%; end-to-end throughput +12-16% for 4-8 concurrent streams. For long sequences (>1024) no measurable degradation; hybrid-striping defaults to long-path. KV gating reduced working set memory by ~22% on chat-heavy traces, lowering OOM and eviction rates in canary runs.
Add rotary-aware async-prefetch attention kernel (opt-in initially)
Introduce hybrid-striping scheduler with runtime knob hybrid_striping_mode
Adaptive KV cache gating to reduce memory churn on streaming workloads
Expose feature flags: async_prefetch_enable, kv_cache_gating_threshold; default off for private installs
Diego Ruiz: Overall nice work, the microbench harness is convincing. Requested: please add an assertion for CUDA compute capability at kernel launch to avoid miscompiles on older drivers.
Author (Ava): Added capability guard and unit test in tests/unit/test_kernel_capability.py, pushed in commit 4/6.
Priya Nambiar: Can we avoid materializing sin/cos tables per-thread? Suggest sharing per-block precomputed tables for common rotary dims; this will reduce register pressure.
Author (Ava): Implemented block-shared sin/cos cache with fallback to per-thread compute for rare dims; updated microbench to measure register usage impact.
Ethan Zhao: Approve after CI green. Noted a small formatting nit in hybrid_striping config docs; resolved.
Release lead (comment): Please ensure canary rollout is coordinated with SRE; added post-merge job to kick off canary validation.
SRE (comment): Canary on dedicated pools shows no OOMs after 48h; metrics look good.
QA (comment): Regression test failed on a precision edge-case (fp16 accumulation disabled). The PR includes a fallback that disables async-prefetch for that config; added test citing the behavior.

Motivation: During a recent regional degradation window we observed rapid eviction/reinstate cycles for noisy tenants which amplified tail latency and caused cross-region failovers. This PR introduces a transient-hedge allocation and a per-tenant eviction lockout to prevent immediate re-eviction (thrash). It also adds a small orchestrator that coordinates short-lived hedges across regional controllers and a fastpath lockout in the circuit-breaker to reduce flip-flapping for sub-minute SLO violations.

Summary of changes: 1) transient hedge allocator: small, ephemeral capacity pool that can be spun up for a tenant for a configurable TTL (default 2 minutes) to absorb short spikes without triggering full eviction workflows; 2) eviction lockout: when a tenant is evicted, mark a lockout window (configurable, default 90s) preventing automatic re-eviction or immediate re-provisioning churn; 3) orchestrator: lightweight controller that ensures hedges are evenly spread across available nodes/regions and enforces a max-concurrent-hedges setting per-region to avoid cascading resource pressure; 4) circuit fastpath lockout: CB will now enter a short lockout after reopen if reopen occurred within a configured hysteresis window to reduce repeated open/reopen cycles; 5) telemetry + alerts: new metrics (tenant_hedge_allocations, tenant_eviction_lockouts, hedge_conflicts) and dashboards; 6) tests and docs: unit/integration tests for allocator and lockout logic plus runbook entry for on-call.

Why this is safe as a hotfix: changes are additive and guarded by feature flags. Default behavior preserves existing eviction semantics until flags are enabled per-cluster. Hedged capacity is bounded by conservative defaults and can be disabled from the Console.

Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-7894) - [x] feature-flagged implementation - [x] unit tests for allocator and lockout - [x] integration test exercising cross-region orchestrator decision - [x] dashboard panels added - [x] smoke-tested on staging cluster - [x] canary rollout plan attached

Related artifacts: linear ENG-7894 (transient hedges), ENG-7930 (eviction stabilization). Runbook: docs/runbooks/eviction-stabilization.md (new section).

Aisha: Lockout state is persisted to the lease KV with compacted TTL semantics; added test for simulated leader migration.

Motivation: Small-scale canaries (mini canaries) are widely used across services to validate model swaps without the overhead of a full canary lane. Current controllers either treat mini canaries like full canaries (high cost) or rely on coarse shadow mirroring (no fast rollback signal). This PR introduces a 'brokered' mini-canary mode that mediates canary traffic through a lightweight broker, applies adaptive shadow throttling based on signal noise and capacity, and supports heartbeat-resume to safely continue paused promotions.

What this PR does: Adds a CanaryBroker runtime component, a small in-cluster control loop that maintains leases for mini canaries, tracks heartbeat pings from canary workers, and coordinates incremental traffic handoffs. Shadow traffic is routed through the broker and throttled by an adaptive policy (decays throttle when variance is high). Heartbeat-resume allows paused canaries to resume after operator-acknowledged quiesce windows; automatic resume only occurs when telemetry gates are green for 5 consecutive minutes. Includes a safety playbook that triggers auto-revert if error-rate or latency regressions cross configured thresholds for the canary window.

Design notes: - Broker leases are ephemeral and scoped to cluster/namespace; no cross-tenant state. - Adaptive throttling uses an exponential moving variance estimator over 60s windows; throttles shadow traffic to maintain stable sampling budgets. - Heartbeat is a 1s ping from canary worker; missing 3 consecutive heartbeats will pause the canary and drain canary fraction gradually. - Telemetry gates are evaluated using existing SLO metrics (p95 latency, error_rate, and a custom quality metric) with configurable tolerances.

Commits summary: - c1a2f3d: controller: add CanaryBroker skeleton and lease controller - b2d4e6f: routing: brokered route plumbing + shadow throttle hook - d3e5f7a: telemetry: gate evaluator + unit tests - a4b6c8e: cli: rollout CLI flags for brokered mode - e5f7g9h: docs: canary playbook and examples

Files changed (high-level): - controller/pkg/broker/*: new broker loop and lease manager - routing/handlers.go: brokered route integration and throttle hook - telemetry/gates.go: gate evaluator + mocks - helm/charts/redwood/templates/rollout-crd.yaml: new config fields - docs/runbooks/mini-brokered-canary.md: operator playbook - tests/*: end-to-end for mini canary lifecycle

Review conversation (high level): - Daniel Park (reviewer): "This looks solid; my main concern is lease churn under heavy churn. Can we backoff renewals?" - Author reply: "Added jittered exponential backoff for renewals; added unit test for backoff behavior." - Amina Lopez: "Suggest making the default throttle conservative (10%) until teams opt-in." - Author reply: "Default set to 5% and documented. Added feature flag canary.brokered.defaultThrottle." - Marco Stein: "Telemetry gating logic needs an audit trail for post-mortem." - Author reply: "Added trace events and audit log entries for gate evaluations; they appear in console under rollout-traces.

CI summary: - unit-tests: pass - integration-e2e (k8s:1.27): pass (flaky test retried once) - lint: pass - benchmark-smoke: pass - canary-simulation: pass

Validation: End-to-end smoke run against staging cluster demonstrated a mini canary promoting 2% -> 10% -> 30% with shadow at 50% throttled down to 10% dynamically; heartbeat pause/resume exercised by killing canary worker and restoring it; auto-revert triggered correctly when injected latency jump exceeded threshold.

Backward compatibility and rollout: Backwards compatible; brokered mode is opt-in via YAML flag canary.brokered.enabled=false by default. No changes to existing rollout CRDs unless flag enabled. Release notes in CHANGELOG.

Merge: squash-and-merge performed after CI green and 2 approvals. Merged by Priya Nandakumar on 2026-02-02.

Introduces a mini-brokered canary controller that enables low-latency canary routes with adaptive shadow throttling; adds heartbeat resume to automatically recover paused canaries. Backwards compatible. Config flags under 'canary.brokered' in rollout CRD.

Adds a scenario-driven cost tuning CLI and non-breaking defaults for quant profiles; no migration required.
Motivation: teams frequently ask for a guided way to translate high-level cost objectives (budget per 1M tokens, latency SLOs, and quality thresholds) into safe batching, cache and quantization defaults. This PR introduces a small opinionated toolchain (CLI + server-side recommendations) called the Budgetary Scenario Catalyst that produces tenant-scoped suggestion bundles and human-readable guidance.

Scope: - Add a CLI subcommand 'redwood cost-catalyst generate' that accepts simple scenario inputs (budget, percentile latency, loss tolerance) and emits a candidate defaults bundle. - Implement an internal ranking function that trades off unit-economics (tokens/$), tail latency estimates, and a conservative quality penalty derived from prior evals. - Provide a set of vetted non-breaking quantization guidance profiles (qp-conservative, qp-balanced) and batch/cache safe defaults that can be surfaced in Console and used by Dedicated/Private agents. - Wire minimal telemetry events to track adoption and simulation outcomes.

What changed (high level): - CLI: pkg/cli/cost_catalyst.go, cmd/redwood/cost_catalyst/*. - Core: inference/econ/catalyst/recommender.go (ranking and safety filters). - Defaults: config/quant_profiles/*.yaml (two new profiles) and defaults/batching_safe_defaults.yaml. - Docs: docs/ops/cost-catalyst.md with usage examples and decision guidance. - Tests: integration tests that run a lightweight cost-sim over representative trace samples.

Checklist: [x] design doc referenced (Linear ENG-3421) [x] unit tests for ranking function [x] integration smoke test with simulated traces [x] docs + CLI help [x] telemetry events gated behind feature flag

Testing and rollout: Local smoke runs included in CI use a synthetic trace (tests/fixtures/trace-small.json) and assert that the suggested bundle does not reduce estimated quality below the supplied tolerance. We will roll out behind a feature flag for hosted first, enable read-only suggestions in Console, and only recommend auto-apply for Dedicated customers after a 2-week pilot. The suggestions are non-destructive by default and marked as 'proposed' in the UI.

Backward compatibility and safety: The quant profiles are additive and will not be automatically applied. The recommender uses conservative clamping rules: it will only suggest changes to batch/caching/quant that are compatible with the pinned model family and the customer's latency SLO. There are explicit opt-outs for tenants that disable automated recommendations.

Related work: draws from earlier econ heuristics (ENG-1810) and the tenant warmstart proposals; integrates with Console telemetry (PM-907).
Luca Ramirez: high-level looks good; please add a short benchmark of ranking runtime on a 100k-sample trace.
Author (Asha Menon): added a micro-benchmark in the integration test harness and documented expected runtime in docs.
Priya Shah: ensure telemetry doesn't leak tenant-sensitive identifiers; move _sim_result event to safe schema.
Author (Asha Menon): telemetry updated to use hashed tenant id and feature-flag gate, test added.
Tomoko Ito: minor nit on CLI UX; prefer --quality-tolerance as float between 0 and 1. Patch applied.
Luca Ramirez: approved after checks passed. Priya Shah: approved. Tomoko Ito: approved.
This is intentionally conservative tooling: the primary value is surfacing plausible defaults and reducing manual tuning. Product will run a short pilot with three mid-market tenants before enabling any auto-apply behavior.

payload.body:
## Summary
This PR adds first-class overload protection rules to the policy engine, introduces strict schema validation (server-side) with safe defaults, and includes a one-time migration for existing tenant configs to the new `overload_policies` stanza.

## Motivation
As part of Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding (ENG-4821), the gateway and router need a single source of truth for tenant/tier/model-level overload behavior (admission caps, shed behavior, Retry-After hints, and optional degradation flags). We also need to prevent unsafe or foot-gun configurations (e.g., disabling shedding globally or setting unlimited concurrency for self-serve tiers) while still allowing per-tenant overrides for enterprise.

## What’s included
- New rule types under `overload_policies.v1`:
  - `admission_control`: token bucket + concurrency caps (per route/model selector)
  - `load_shedding`: shed response configuration (status mapping, Retry-After bounds, error code override policy)
  - `degradation_flags`: allow/deny list for feature reduction under duress (e.g., enforce `max_tokens` cap, streaming concurrency limit)
  - `breaker_thresholds`: threshold hooks (e.g., queue depth, scheduler backlog) as named signal references (actual signal evaluation stays in gateway/runtime; policy engine owns config)
- Schema validation + guardrails:
  - Enforce upper bounds for concurrency/max_tokens by tier (self-serve defaults are stricter)
  - Require explicit allowlist for any degradation mode (default deny)
  - Disallow selectors that would match “all tenants” unless caller is privileged (protects tenant isolation)
  - Validate Retry-After range (min/max) and forbid missing retry guidance when `shed_behavior=retryable`
  - Validate model selectors resolve to known catalog IDs (or `*` only where allowed)
- Safe default policies:
  - Introduce tier defaults (`self_serve`, `hosted_enterprise`, `dedicated_hosted`) applied when tenant config omits `overload_policies`
  - Defaults are intentionally conservative and can be overridden per tenant via existing config override flow
- Migration:
  - Adds a migration that backfills `overload_policies.v1` into existing tenant config documents with the tier defaults
  - Includes a “dry-run” validator mode used during migration to log-but-not-block when legacy fields are present; after migration, validation is strict for new writes
- Tests:
  - Golden tests for schema validation error messages
  - Migration unit tests (idempotency, rollback behavior)
  - RBAC tests for privileged “global selector” usage

## Rollout / operational notes
- Feature is behind `policy_engine.overload_policies_v1_enabled` (default ON in staging, OFF in prod until gateway wiring lands).
- Migration runs in read-repair mode during the first config fetch/write cycle; no mass rewrite job.
- Added metrics:
  - `policy_engine.validation_errors_total{domain="overload"}`
  - `policy_engine.migration_applied_total{name="overload_policies_v1"}`

## Follow-ups
- Gateway middleware will start consuming these rules for admission control (ENG-4823).
- Smart routing will consume fallback config (separate PR; this PR only establishes policy scaffolding).

## Screenshots / examples
Example tenant override (abridged):
- Self-serve: `concurrency_cap=12`, `retry_after_seconds=[1,8]`, `degradation_flags=[]`
- Hosted enterprise: `concurrency_cap=80`, `retry_after_seconds=[1,3]`, `degradation_flags=["cap_max_tokens","limit_stream_concurrency"]`

## Checklist
- [x] Backwards compatible (new fields additive)
- [x] Validation messages are actionable (include JSON pointer + tier)
- [x] Migration is idempotent + safe on partial failures
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Docs comments included for config authors
Jordan Lee (review): The overall direction looks good. Two asks: (1) can we make validation errors include the tier name and the selector that matched? (2) please add an explicit guardrail against `retry_after_seconds` being omitted for retryable shed behavior — we saw this create client retry storms in staging.
Benji Okafor (author): Added tier + selector context to all ValidationError instances, and made Retry-After mandatory when `shed_behavior=retryable`. Also added golden coverage for both cases.
Ethan Park (review): Concern: tier defaults are currently applied on read even when tenant doc has legacy admission fields. That could result in confusing behavior if gateway starts reading both. Can we ensure legacy fields are ignored once overload_policies exists and we emit a deprecation warning?
Benji Okafor (author): Updated config resolution order: overload_policies.v1 wins; legacy admission fields are ignored when v1 present. Added `policy_engine.legacy_overload_fields_seen_total` metric + a warning log with tenant_id for cleanup tracking.
Rafael Mendes (review): From SRE side: please cap the maximum concurrency for self-serve. I’m fine with a high number, but it cannot be unbounded. Also want a metric for validation failures split by write path vs read-repair.
Benji Okafor (author): Added hard cap for self-serve concurrency (max 64) and a separate label `path={"write","read_repair"}` on `validation_errors_total`.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): RBAC: the “global selector” restriction needs to be enforced server-side even for internal callers unless they have the privileged role. Please add a test that a normal service token can’t write a selector that matches all tenants.
Benji Okafor (author): Done. Added `selector_privileges` check to the write path and a unit test covering service-token behavior.
Christine Wong (review): Looks good. Minor: can we rename `breaker_thresholds.signal_ref` to `signal_name` so it matches runtime naming conventions? The rest of the system uses `*_signal_name`.
Benji Okafor (author): Renamed to `signal_name` and added a migration shim so existing staged configs don’t break.
Jordan Lee (review): Approved.
Rafael Mendes (review): Approved after latest changes.
Ethan Park (review): Approved.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): Approved.
Christine Wong (review): Approved.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: On several recent incident postmortems we observed that operator credential revocations and cross-region audit merges were slow to converge: revoked operator tokens remained valid at edge proxies for several minutes and audit entries arriving out-of-order made forensic timelines difficult to trust. This PR implements three coordinated pieces to mitigate these risks: 1) an operator revocation webhook that immediately invalidates operator-issued tokens and notifies edge caches; 2) a KMS attestation handshake to require provable key provenance for operator-scoped CMK operations; 3) an audit timeline reconciler that ingests per-region audit event streams and produces a canonical, deduplicated ordered timeline for post-incident analysis and compliance audits.

Implementation summary:
- Operator revocation webhook: new HTTP endpoint (/internal/v1/operator-revoke) implemented in src/auth/operator_webhook.go. When a revocation event is recorded (SQL migration adds operator_revocations table), the webhook writes a revocation tombstone and publishes an event to the internal pubsub used by edge proxies. Edge caches subscribe to the existing token-introspect topic and apply tombstones immediately. Revocation semantics are idempotent and implement an after-image to avoid race windows during near-simultaneous issuance and revocation.
- KMS attestation handshake: pkg/kms/attestor/attestor.go implements an attestation verifier that accepts signed key-provenance envelopes from supported KMS providers (AWS/GCP/Azure). The attestor validates envelope signatures, checks the CMK region/alias against tenant residency claims, and annotates the authorization decision with a signed attestation token included in the downstream audit entry. This prevents silent CMK proxying across pinned regions.
- Audit timeline reconciler: tools/audit/reconciler/main.go implements a lightweight reconciler service that consumes Kafka topics produced by the audit-forwarder from each region. It uses sequence anchors and a hybrid logical clock to reorder events, dedupe retries using idempotency keys, and emits canonical timeline shards to the compliance ingest. The reconciler also produces reconciliation markers (watermarks) that are ingested by the Console to show timeline completeness.

Rollout and compatibility:
- Database migration migrations/20240514_add_operator_revocation_table.sql adds operator_revocations and a small index; migration is zero-downtime (backfill handled by a small job).
- Feature flag config/rollout/operator-revocation-ff.yaml gates publishing of pubsub tombstones; default rollout: shadow -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%. Edge proxies will ignore tombstones until they receive a compatible client update; rollout plan coordinates SDK bump.
- KMS attestation is additive: if the attestation envelope is missing, existing behavior is preserved until the enforcement guard (config) is enabled.

Tests and validation:
- Integration/e2e test tests/integration/operator_revocation_e2e.test covers issuance -> immediate revocation -> edge cache expiry across simulated regions.
- Unit tests for attestor include mocked signed envelopes for AWS/GCP.
- Audit reconciler has an integration test that replays out-of-order streams and asserts canonical ordering and dedupe.

Observability and SLOs:
- New metrics in observability/metrics/operator_revocation.promql: revocation_queue_latency_ms, attestation_verification_latency_ms, reconciler_reorder_lag_ms.
- Added tracing spans and tags for attestation.provider and reconciler.watermark to aid debugging.

Security and compliance notes:
- Attestation tokens stored in audit payloads are base64-signed proofs; no plaintext key material is logged.
- The reconcilers strip sensitive data per existing audit-scrub rules.
- This PR addressed Linear items ENG-5584 and SEC-219 for time-to-revoke and audit-timeline-trust.

Commits (high level):
- 1d9b2f5: add operator revocation webhook handler and basic pubsub publish
- afc4e10: add DB migration for revocations and backfill helper
- b2c7d44: implement KMS attestor and test fixtures for AWS/GCP envelopes
- 8f0e7a2: add audit reconciler service skeleton and integration tests
- c4a123b: observability metrics and rollout config
- 7b9f0d1: docs and e2e tests

Feedback and review conversation:
- Daniel Park (review): "Overall looks good; two production concerns: (A) revocation pubsub storm detection — we need a circuit breaker so a compromised CI key can't flood edge caches; (B) schema migration: please add an index and a short-lived TTL cleanup job."
- Author reply (Aisha): "Added a token-flood circuit-breaker on the publisher (max 500 revokes/min globally, with exponential backoff). Migration now creates an index on (operator_id, revoked_at) and we added a one-off cleanup job (backfill script included)."
- Sven Ortega (review): "Need to measure reconciler memory usage and worst-case reorder window; we shouldn't buffer more than X MB per shard."
- Author reply: "Reconciler now exposes reconciler.buffer_bytes gauge and enforces a soft cap; on overflow it emits a reconciliation_failure metric and spills older events to an archived bucket for offline forensics."
- Maya Lin (approve): "Tests and docs look solid. Please add a short blurb to the on-call runbook about reconciling missing audit shards."

CI summary: initial run: unit tests passed, integration suite failed on flaky network test; reran integration suite and passed. E2E run passed in canary. Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main on 2024-05-20 by Daniel Park after approvals from Maya Lin and Sven Ortega.

Post-merge actions:
- Coordinate SDK bump (edge proxy client) to respect revocation tombstones (scheduled with SDK team; tracking ENG-5612).
- Start 5% shadow rollout and monitor revocation_queue_latency_ms and reconciler_reorder_lag_ms for 48h.
- Compliance: added entry for audit timeline reconciler to internal compliance tracker (SEC-219).

Notes for auditors: reconciler emits watermarks per region so auditors can reason about gaps; attestation tokens are available in the audit archive but redacted for PII. 
Adds operator revocation webhook and KMS attestation verification; introduces audit timeline reconciler service to dedupe and reorder cross-region audit events. Backwards-compatible, canary rollout behind feature flag.
