Motivation: Introduce a light-weight 'custodian' sentinel that validates operator-scoped claims and enforces region consent before KMS routing. Customers with strict residency requirements sometimes observe requests routed to a fallback provider during capacity pressure; this PR adds a consent gate and a throttled assertion path so operator sessions cannot inadvertently override tenant residency constraints.

Summary of changes: adds a new custodian service (pkg/custodian) that acts as a pre-authorizer for operator-scoped requests; extends rbacv2 decision pipeline with a sentinel hook; augments audit middleware to attach a custody-hash header for post-hoc verification; introduces a region-consent proxy component that annotates KMS routing decisions when tenant consent is present; adds unit, integration, and e2e tests for operator/assertion flows.

Checklist:
- [x] implement custodian sentinel and integrated tests
- [x] extend policy-compiler hooks for operator-scope assertions
- [x] add audit header (X-Redwood-Custody-Hash) and docs
- [x] implement region-consent proxy and KMS affinity tagging
- [x] add feature flag for gradual rollout (feature.custodian.enabled)
- [x] add SLO-preserving throttling when consent validation falls back to async verification

Commits summary: commit 1/6: scaffold custodian service and basic decision interface; commit 2/6: wire sentinel into rbacv2 pipeline and add unit tests; commit 3/6: add audit header producer + signing helper; commit 4/6: implement region-consent proxy and KMS-tag mapping; commit 5/6: add integrational tests (mock KMS, mock policy compiler); commit 6/6: feature flag, config, docs and migrate CI matrix.

Changed areas (high level): pkg/custodian/ (new) - custody decision and claim normalizer; services/rbac/decision_pipeline.go - sentinel hook integration; services/audit/middleware.go - header emission and signer invocation; services/kms/proxy.go - annotate routing decisions with consent tags; integrations/installer/vars.yaml - enablement flag and defaults; docs/security/operator-claims.md - rationale and operational guidance; tests/e2e/operator-consent.test.js - scenario coverage; charts/redwood-helm/templates/custodian-deployment.yaml - k8s manifest and resource requests.

Testing and CI: initial CI run showed a flaky e2e related to the mock KMS race; added deterministic hook and retried. Final CI: build: pass, unit: pass, integration: pass, e2e: pass, lint: pass. Cargo-culted some mocks from pkg/testutil to avoid cross-test interference.

Review conversation (high level):
- Daniel Park: "Can the sentinel be bypassed by elevated operator tokens? Need an explicit denylist if a token has 'operator:override' claim."
  - Author: "Design intentionally treats operator:override as a high-risk claim and requires an explicit enterprise allowlist; added config.operatorOverride.allowlist and unit tests to assert deny by default."
- Sofia Martinez: "Audit header contains base64 signature, but we should avoid leaking raw tenant IDs to downstream telemetry."
  - Author: "Switch to custody-hash (HMAC over request-id + tenant-id) and documented verification steps; telemetry receives only the hash and a minimal audit envelope."
- Jun Li: "What is the performance impact?"
  - Author: "Benchmarks in benchmark-lab showed ~0.6ms median added latency for hot paths when feature flag enabled and async verification turned on; included a throttling policy to eliminate load amplification."
- Reviewer QA thread: "Please add a smoke test that simulates fallback KMS provider and validates consent gate blocks override flows."
  - Author: "Added tests/e2e/operator-consent.test.js scenario 'fallback-no-override' to cover this."
Daniel Park: Please ensure operator-override is opt-in via enterprise allowlist; default must deny. Added config.operatorOverride.allowlist and tests.
Sofia Martinez: Do not include raw tenant IDs in audit headers. Switched to custody-hash and documented verification.
Jun Li: Add benchmarks for the hot-path performance. Attached benchmark-lab results and included throttling policy.
QA: added smoke e2e for fallback/provider override. Verified on staging; no regression observed.
Add custodian sentinel to enforce operator-scope claims and region consent; introduces X-Redwood-Custody-Hash audit header; feature-flagged behind feature.custodian.enabled (default off); recommended upgrade notes included in docs/security/operator-claims.md

payload.body: Context: High tail latency for small, KV-heavy requests in continuous batching clusters under sustained load. Motivation: Prior admission controls were aggressive and caused live requests to starve when KV pins and kernel warmup skewed the batch composition. This PR introduces a 'gentle prefetch shepherd'—a windowed admission adapter that gives transient, decaying prefetch credits to flows that would otherwise starve, while preserving global fairness and latency SLOs. Summary of changes: 1) new windowed admission adapter (pkg/batcher/windowed_adapter.go) that allocates a small, time-bounded prefetch budget to low-progress flows; the budget decays exponentially and is charged against a soft-reservation counter to prevent abuse. 2) prefetch_shepherd scheduler component (pkg/scheduler/prefetch_shepherd.go) that tracks per-flow progress, KV-pin state, recent kernel misses, and signals the adapter when to issue credits. 3) kernel affinity hints (runtime/kernel_affinity.go) so dispatcher prefers quantized/fast kernels for shepherded slots to minimize additional warmup cost. 4) KV gentle-evict hook (pkg/kv/pin_manager.go) which tolerates short-lived pins from shepherded slots and schedules cooperative evictions rather than hard drops. 5) tests and microbench harness additions (tests/integration/prefetch_shepherd_test.go, benchmarks/prefetch_shepherd_microbench.json). Design notes: The adapter keeps a sliding window per-cohort instead of strict per-request leases; this reduces jitter and makes admission decisions smoother under bursts. Credits are small (configurable default 2 tokens) and decay with an exponential half-life to avoid long-term priority inversion. The prefetch shepherd observes kernel-warmup events and will not issue credits that would force the dispatcher to run a cold heavy kernel if a warm fast kernel is available for alternatives. Safety and fairness: We added global credit caps, cohort-weight-aware decay, and a backoff on repeated credits to avoid gaming. The admission path includes instrumentation to report credit issuance, decay events, and credit exhaustion to the Console so operators can tune policy. Benchmarks: Microbench runs show median token latency unchanged, 95th reduced by ~8-12% on KV-heavy small-request workloads, and P99 down ~6% under sustained 90% load with mixed kernel types. CPU/GPU overhead measured at infra-level is <1.5% in steady state. Backwards compatibility: configuration defaults disable shepherding for Dedicated private installs until customer opt-in; the feature is off by default for older clusters. Review notes: Addressed concerns about priority inversion by adding cohort-weight-aware decay and global caps; added an E2E test that simulates long-lived KV-pin churn. Checklist: - [x] Design doc referenced (Linear ENG-4882) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Benchmarks recorded - [x] Feature gated and rollout plan documented in docs/operational/continuous-batcher-tuning.md Commits summary: a1b2c3d: introduce soft-prefetch-credit type and basic bookkeeping; b2c3d4e: implement windowed admission adapter with decay passthrough; c3d4e5f: kernel affinity hints for dispatcher to prefer quantized kernels; d4e5f6a: KV pin gentle-evict hook and backoff integration; e5f6a7b: add unit + integration tests and microbench harness. Files changed at a glance: windowed_adapter.go (core logic + config knobs), prefetch_shepherd.go (cohort tracking + heuristic signals), kernel_affinity.go (dispatcher hints), pin_manager.go (gentle eviction), integration test harness, docs and benchmark artifacts. Review conversation snapshot: Aaron Patel: "Initial read looks solid; main worry is credit leakage in pathological churn. Can you add an explicit drain path at flow termination?" Maya Chen: "Added drain in d4e5f6a; adapter closes outstanding credits on flow end and reports metrics." Sofia Martinez: "Please ensure we expose a per-tenant cap; ops will want to throttle on multi-tenant hosts." Maya Chen: "Added per-tenant cap and config, default conservative; docs updated." Eliot James: "Benchmarks look promising; please run perf canary on staging with mixed kernel pool." Maya Chen: "Canary run scheduled and green; CI/bench reports attached." CI: unit tests passed, integration tests passed on staging, perf microbench passed; two flaky lint warnings fixed in follow-up commit. Merge: squashed and merged into main after reviewer approvals. Operational notes for SRE: Watch for rapid credit churn metric (batcher.prefetch.credit_churn) and credit_exhaustion alarms; default alert thresholds provided in docs. Rollout plan: feature flagged, enable in canary cluster for 48h, monitor P95/P99 and credit churn, then ramp 10/30/100%. Why this is different: instead of preemptive hard reservations or aggressive deadline relaxations, this approach uses a small bounded, decaying credit mechanism tied to kernel warmup and KV state to mitigate transient starvation without distorting long-term fairness.
payload.title: Gentle prefetch shepherd: windowed admission adapter for starvation prevention

Context and motivation:
We continue to see noisy presubmit runs caused by transitive dependency updates and an increasingly monolithic presubmit graph. This PR introduces a lightweight, pluggable presubmit router and a dependency allowlist harness so teams can opt-in to narrower presubmit footprints and allow CI to skip expensive lint/test shards for allowed changes. The long-term goal is to decouple presubmit routing logic from monorepo-specific assumptions and make it easier to onboard targeted fast-feedback lanes.

What this PR does (summary):
- Introduces a presubmit router abstraction (infra/presubmit/router.go) that dispatches changes to configured lanes based on file globs, manifest hints, and dependency signals.
- Adds a dependency allowlist harness (pkg/ci/allowlist.go) that marks dependency-only changes as low-cost; teams can opt these into a slim presubmit path.
- Replaces the single presubmit workflow with a small composition layer in .github/workflows/presubmit.yml that wires the router to existing jobs.
- Adds small helper scripts and a lightweight base image for slim presubmit runs (ci/docker/presubmit-slim.Dockerfile, scripts/ci-slim-run.sh).
- Documentation and onboarding notes (docs/ci/presubmit-routes.md) and test coverage for the router logic (infra/presubmit/router_test.go).

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- The router is deliberately small: it evaluates a set of ordered rules and emits a route token. Complex route computation is deferred to future indexed heuristics to keep the initial roll-out safe and auditable.
- The allowlist harness uses package- and manifest-level heuristics (lockfile diff + manifest path mapping) to reduce false-positives. It is opt-in and can be disabled per-team via a config flag.
- We keep the full presubmit path intact and use the router only to select a smaller initial lane. Full tests run on merge to prevent regressions.

Checklist (what I tested locally / CI):
- Unit tests: router + allowlist (infra/presubmit/*_test.go)
- Integration smoke: presubmit workflow runs against a synthetic change set to validate routing decisions
- Verified fallback: when route resolution fails, we default to the existing monolithic presubmit to maintain safety
- Ran a canary rollout in the `contrib/ci-canary` team with the allowlist enabled for dependency bumps (observed ~48% reduction in average presubmit runtime for dependabot PRs)

Commits summary:
- 1f2a8c4: introduce presubmit router interface and rule evaluation engine
- 3b7d45a: implement file-glob + manifest rule sources and canonicalize input diff
- c9e012b: dependency allowlist implementation + allowlist config struct
- 6a4d2f0: presubmit workflow composition and slim runner image
- 5e9b3fa: docs, tests, and small infra fixes

Changed areas (high level):
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yml: compose router + existing jobs (small, explicit mapping)
- infra/presubmit/router.go, infra/presubmit/router_test.go: router implementation and tests
- pkg/ci/allowlist.go, pkg/ci/allowlist_test.go: allowlist harness and heuristics
- ci/docker/presubmit-slim.Dockerfile, scripts/ci-slim-run.sh: slim runner and invocation helper
- docs/ci/presubmit-routes.md: onboarding and operator notes

Review conversation (highlights):
- Ethan Park (review): "Nice split — main question is safety. Can we make the allowlist conservative by default and require an explicit flag per team? Also suggest adding a debug header to the presubmit job showing which route was chosen."
- Maya (author): "Agreed. The allowlist is off by default; added `--allowlist-enabled` flag to team configs and a PRESUBMIT_ROUTE env var emitted by the router (see workflow)."
- Neha Singh (review): "Router looks good, but add more unit tests around lockfile diffs for yarn/pip/poetry cases."
- Maya: "Added additional lockfile diff fixture tests and a small note in docs describing heuristics and how to opt out."
- Liam O'Connor (approval): "Approach LGTM. Keep an eye on flaky route detection in the first week and we should surface route telemetry in the console."

CI status and reruns:
- Initial CI run: failed (flake in integration smoke due to ephemeral runner timeout)
- Re-run: pass across all checks (unit, integration-smoke, lint)
- CI notes: added a short timeout backoff to the presubmit smoke job to reduce noise (see commit 5e9b3fa)

Rollout and monitoring:
- Canary rollout completed for `contrib/ci-canary` and `infra-team` with allowlist opt-in; we observed a median presubmit runtime reduction of ~42-50% for dependence-only bumps in those teams.
- Added a route telemetry counter (instrumentation) that will be exposed in a follow-up PR to avoid inflating this change.

Merge notes:
- Squash-merged to main after approvals and green CI. No migration required; behavior is opt-in and non-breaking. Teams can opt into router/allowlist via a repo-level config in `.presubmit-config.yaml` (sample in docs).

Follow-ups planned:
- Expose presubmit routing telemetry in Redwood Console for team-level adoption metrics (ENG-2301).
- Add an indexed rule backend for higher-accuracy route decisions and per-PR fast-path scoring (deferred to ENG-2359).

If you want to test locally:
- See docs/ci/presubmit-routes.md for a short recipe. Use `scripts/ci-slim-run.sh` to emulate a slim presubmit and `make presubmit-smoke` for the full canary workflow.

Contact:
- Author: Maya Hernandez (@mhernandez) — happy to walk through the router and assist with on-boarding teams.
Adds a pluggable presubmit routing layer and an opt-in dependency allowlist to reduce presubmit churn and speed feedback. No behavioural changes to existing presubmit policies unless explicitly enabled.

payload.body:
Motivation: We need first-class signals to (a) protect non-burst tenants via fast detection of neighbor impact precursors and (b) make burst behavior explainable/supportable (clear denial reasons, pool saturation, and telemetry health). This PR adds a minimal, low-cardinality Prometheus metric set for burst pools and admission decisions, wired into the burst admission controller + routing call site, with guardrails to avoid tenant-level cardinality.

What’s included: (1) Pool-level saturation and supply signals: redwood_burst_pool_capacity_gpus{region,hw_class,pool} (gauge) and redwood_burst_pool_inuse_gpus{region,hw_class,pool} (gauge) and derived redwood_burst_pool_saturation_ratio{region,hw_class,pool} (gauge). (2) Admission decision counters: redwood_burst_admission_requests_total{region,hw_class,pool,decision} (counter) and redwood_burst_admission_denials_total{region,hw_class,pool,reason} (counter). (3) Queue/backpressure: redwood_burst_admission_queue_depth{region,hw_class,pool} (gauge) and redwood_burst_admission_queue_wait_seconds_bucket{region,hw_class,pool} (histogram). (4) Telemetry health/lag: redwood_burst_telemetry_lag_seconds{region,hw_class,source} (gauge) and redwood_burst_telemetry_last_update_timestamp_seconds{region,hw_class,source} (gauge). (5) Routing integration: propagate decision + denial reason into gateway stats without adding tenant_id labels; we only emit route_class and customer_tier where present (bounded sets).

Cardinality policy: This PR explicitly does NOT label metrics by tenant_id, org_id, request_id, model, or endpoint path. Allowed labels are region, hw_class, pool, decision, reason, source, plus customer_tier (gold/silver/standard) and route_class (chat/embeddings/rerank) where bounded. A lint test is included to block accidental high-cardinality label additions.

Notes on semantics: decision is one of {baseline,burst_admitted,burst_denied,fail_open,fail_closed}. Denial reason aligns with pr-23795 enums: {pool_saturated,tenant_cap_reached,fleet_safety_cap,cooldown_active,telemetry_stale,priority_budget_exhausted,internal_error}. telemetry_stale is emitted when telemetry_lag_seconds exceeds the configured freshness window at evaluation time.

Rollout/usage: Dashboards/alerts are handled in observability-pack (separate PR). For now, this PR provides the signals needed for: (a) SRE alerting on sustained saturation + rising denials, (b) gating rules to disable burst when telemetry is stale, and (c) support debug workflows (denial reason breakdowns).
Allison Grant: Metric set looks right and label bounds are good. Can we ensure we never attach model_name or route path here? Those will explode cardinality in practice.
Logan Wright (author): Yep—added pkg/metrics/label_policy.go allowlist + a unit test that fails if any burst metrics register labels outside the bounded set. Also kept route_class instead of raw path, and no model labels.
Sean Gallagher: For SRE paging we’ll want a clean separation between "denied due to guardrail" and "denied due to internal error". Can you make sure internal_error is its own reason and emitted on evaluator exceptions?
Logan Wright (author): Added reason=internal_error for exception paths and decision=fail_closed where applicable. We still count the request in requests_total with decision=fail_closed; denials_total increments with reason=internal_error.
Peter Holtz: Queue wait histogram buckets: can we align with our standard latency buckets? Also, please confirm queue depth is per-pool (not per-tenant queue).
Logan Wright (author): Updated buckets to match pkg/metrics/latency_buckets.go (5ms..30s) and confirmed queue depth is a single per-pool gauge. No per-tenant queues are exported.
Keiko Yamamoto: telemetry_lag_seconds source label—what are the values? Please keep it bounded. Also, do we have a freshness window constant to compare against in dashboards?
Logan Wright (author): source is one of {fleet_telemetry,pool_allocator}. Both bounded. Freshness window is already in config (burst.telemetry.max_staleness_seconds); dashboards can overlay that value. This PR just exposes lag + last_update.
Allison Grant: Approved. Please make sure metric HELP strings include units (seconds/gpus).
Logan Wright (author): Done—HELP strings updated in metrics registry + helptext.yaml.
Sean Gallagher: Approved (SRE). This unblocks ENG-4833 dashboard work.
Added Prometheus metrics for burst pool saturation, admission requests/denials (with reason codes), queue depth/wait time, and telemetry lag to support dashboards, alerting, and rollout gating.
payload.title: Add Prometheus metrics for burst saturation, denials, queue depth, and telemetry lag

Motivation: In heavy KV-heavy workloads we observed long-tail queuing where a small fraction of requests aged in the continuous batcher and hit slow kernel paths or stale KV state, leading to starvation and tail latency spikes. This PR introduces a Queued Timebound Recovery (QTR) sentinel inside the continuous batcher that tracks per-request queue age, emits an aging score, applies soft-timeout escalation, and triggers preemptive KV warmup and proactive kernel selection to recover slow-path requests before they become irrecoverable. Design summary: QTR attaches a compact timestamp/age token to queued entries; an aging detector computes a cohort score over sliding windows and exposes a per-batcher "hunger" signal. If a request crosses a soft threshold it is marked for recovery: the scheduler opportunistically moves it into a recovery lane that prefers warm KV-aware kernels and smaller micro-batches, signals the KV prefetcher to hydrate likely keys, and applies jittered soft-timeouts to avoid synchronized evictions. If recovery fails and the hard threshold is hit, the request is routed to a fast-fallback kernel or an alternate model variant depending on policy. Implementation highlights: - New qtr/age_token type and compact in-queue metadata for O(1) checks. - Cohort aging histogram implemented as a lockless ring buffer to avoid contention in hot fast-paths. - Recovery lane scheduling that cooperates with existing slot-reservation logic and respects fairness quotas. - Integration points with KV prefetch component: best-effort prefetch requests emitted with backpressure and rate-limiting. - Kernel selection hint API: when a request is flagged for recovery we prefer single-stream optimized kernels and lower-latency quantized paths where accuracy impact is acceptable. - Config flags and runtime knobs: qtr.enabled, qtr.soft_ms, qtr.hard_ms, qtr.prefetch_budget, qtr.jitter_pct. Rollout plan: feature is behind qtr.enabled flag defaulting to off for canary hosts. We ran an internal canary across 10 p50-sized serving nodes and then a broader opt-in across dedicated pools before enabling for all hosts. Benchmarks: in a synthetic KV-heavy chat workload with sustained 200% arrival spikes, 99.9th latency improved from 2.4s to 1.1s and the number of requests hitting the fallback kernel dropped 78%. Tests: unit tests for ring-buffer aging and token propagation, integration test for recovery path with a mocked KV layer, e2e stress test with arrival spikes. Safety: recovery paths are best-effort and non-blocking; prefetching is rate-limited; we instrument metrics and added alerts for qtr.prefetch_exhausted and qtr.recovery_rate. This PR includes docs for the flags, a console observability panel for qtr metrics, and a migration note. See commits and changed files for details.
Adds Queued Timebound Recovery (QTR) sentinel to continuous batcher to detect long-queued requests, trigger KV warmup, and gracefully route near-timeout requests to fast kernel paths; enabled behind runtime flag and safe rollout by default; improves tail latency and prevents request starvation.
Diego Marquez: Nice approach and addresses the root cause we saw in the May incident. A couple of questions: how do we ensure prefetch doesn't overwhelm KV store at scale?
Asha Patel: Prefetching is budgeted per-batcher; qtr.prefetch_budget enforces backpressure and we added a global token-bucket in the KV prefetcher that shares quotas across batchers to avoid spikes.
Linus Chen: Can the cohort histogram become noisy with many small batches? Consider exponential decay rather than fixed window to make it more stable.
Asha Patel: We evaluated both fixed sliding window and exponential decay; for fast-path stability ring-buffer window provided tighter control with lower GC. Added a metric to expose window variance; we can flip to decay if noisy in production.
Morgan Blake: Tests look good. Please add a smoke test in the canary pipeline that asserts qtr metrics appear and prefetch budget is respected.
Asha Patel: Added canary smoke test in infra/ci/batcher_integration.yml that validates qtr.enabled hosts emit qtr.recovery_rate > 0 and qtr.prefetch_exhausted == 0 for 60s spike run.
Diego Marquez: Approve after small nit fixes in comments.
Linus Chen: Approved.
payload.title: Queued Timebound Recovery: sentinel to recover long-queued requests and prevent KV-starvation in continuous batcher

Context and motivation:
We recently had a post-incident review (SUP-721) where operator-initiated KMS calls and scripted operator tools made it difficult to quickly distinguish authorized agent activity from anomalous operator behavior. This PR adds two complementary controls: 1) an operator behavior whitelist that constrains the kinds of operator-initiated request contexts allowed to perform certain KMS operations, and 2) a KMS transparency log stream that records operator-originated KMS interactions to a write-once, append-only store for forensic and compliance queries. The goal is to make operator actions auditable and to provide an emergency revocation path when operator tooling misbehaves.

Summary of changes (high level commits):
- commit 1: introduce operator-behavior-whitelist service and config schema (security/whitelist service, unit tests)
- commit 2: instrument KMS proxied calls to emit transparency-log events and add a minimal WAL-backed append-only sink (audit/transparency)
- commit 3: add RBAC v2 policy checks to operator token path to consult whitelist and attach enforcement decisions to audit payloads
- commit 4: telemetry and dashboards: new metrics (operator_whitelist_denied_total, transparency_log_ingest_latency) and Grafana dashboard JSON scaffold
- commit 5: docs and migration notes (console and operator-runbook)

Files changed (high-level overview):
- security/operator_whitelist.go (core enforcement + matcher)
- api/rbac/v2/policy_engine.go (hook to consult whitelist during operator-scoped checks)
- kms/proxy/handler.go (emit transparency log events on proxied calls)
- audit/transparency/wal_store.go (lightweight write-once append-only store with checksum)
- docs/runbooks/operator-audit.md (runbook for responding to whitelist denials and transparency entries)
- telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml (new metrics)
- grafana/dashboards/operator-audit.json (dashboard scaffold)
- tests/integration/operator_whitelist_integration_test.go (integration test harness)

Key behavioral notes and compatibility:
- Default behavior: whitelist is empty by default (deny-by-exception for the most sensitive KMS operations). Existing operator tokens will continue to work for non-KMS paths.
- Enforcement is opt-in per deployment via operator_whitelist.enabled in config; in Hosted we plan a staged rollout under feature flag.
- Transparency log does not change KMS response paths; it is asynchronous by design to avoid adding latency to customer requests. A best-effort sync path is provided for forced flushing during incident investigations.

Security design summary:
- Whitelist entries are small assertions: service identity, allowed operation set (Encrypt/Decrypt/Wrap/Unwrap), optional source IP / region predicate, temporal window. The matcher uses RBAC v2 attribute filters for evaluation so policies can be expressed in the same policy language engineers already use.
- When a whitelist denial occurs, the system emits a high-fidelity audit event that contains the operator token id, matched policy id (if any), request context (redacted CI/secret fields), and KMS key fingerprint. Denials increment a counter routed to the security incident queue.
- Transparency log entries are SHA-256 hashed and store a minimal canonicalized envelope: (timestamp, operator-token-hash, operation, key-fingerprint, region, enforcement-result). The WAL writes the canonical envelope and then the checksum; the entry is immutably stored and available via an internal query API for compliance tooling.

Tests and CI:
- Unit tests cover matcher edge cases, policy translation, and WAL corruption detection.
- Integration tests spin up a test KMS proxy and assert transparency events are emitted and the append-only store remains consistent after simulated restarts.
- CI initially failed on linters (gofmt) and a flaky integration that depended on ordering; I fixed formatting and hardened the integration test by adding a deterministic wait-for-commit pattern. Final CI run: all checks green.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Diego Morales (reviewer): "Can we avoid linking operator token ids in cleartext to transparency logs? Need to ensure we can't re-identify users in compliance workflows."
- Aisha (author): "We store operator-token-hash (salted with a rotating server secret) and expose only the hash in the log. The reverse mapping is possible only with platform secrets in a PRC-only workflow. Added notes in docs and code comments."
- Priya Natarajan: "Consider adding a bounded retention enforcement and a retention-override workflow for legal requests."
- Aisha: "Added retention config (audit.transparency.retention_days) and a service-account guarded override API documented in the runbook."
- Liam Chen: "Dashboard looks good; we should add an alert when denied_count spikes > 10/min across all regions."
- Aisha: "Added operator_whitelist_spike alert in grafana/dashboards and wired it to the security pager."

Operational runbook summary (also included in docs/runbooks/operator-audit.md):
- How to query transparency logs for a given time window and operator-token-hash.
- Steps to rotate the server salt used for hashing operator tokens (two-phase: add new salt, start emitting, then sunset old salt after two weeks).
- Emergency revocation: deny-by-operator-policy toggle and a KMS call blackhole for a given key fingerprint for isolation.

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Deploy combined service in staging with whitelist disabled; collect transparency events for baseline.
2) Enable whitelist in enforcement mode for a small set of non-critical operator operations (opt-in list) and observe false positive rates for 72h.
3) Expand policy to critical KMS ops if <2% false positives and provide support contacts in runbook.

Backward compatibility and data residency implications:
- No customer-visible API change. Transparency logs are stored in the same region as the operator proxy to respect region pinning and data residency controls. For Private deployments, the WAL store writes to local persistent storage; Hosted uses region-bound append stores.

Follow-ups and TODOs (tracked as ENG-1387):
- UI: add transparency log explorer in Console (limited to SOC and Compliance roles).
- Policy generator: helper to translate a list of operator-runbook rules into RBAC v2 entries.
- Long-term: consider storing signed transparency checkpoints to an external attestation service.

Merge outcome:
- Approved by reviewers Diego Morales and Priya Natarajan after two rounds of changes. Squash-merged into main on 2026-02-18, release-note entry added to the changelog.

If interested in a quick demo for SOC, I can run the staging flow and show the transparency log query API and the new dashboard.
Introduce operator behavior whitelist, KMS transparency log stream for operator-originated KMS calls, and audit metadata enrichment. Backwards compatible; no customer API changes.
payload.title: Add operator behavior whitelist and KMS transparency log for operator-initiated requests

Motivation: We frequently see long-running release hooks and monolithic lint pipelines delaying merges and producing noisy failures downstream. This PR introduces a lightweight, stage-aware release sandbox for preflight verification and replaces the top-heavy monolithic lint workflow with a compact lint router that dispatches targeted lint shards based on changed paths. Goals: 1) shorten presubmit feedback for most PRs, 2) isolate release-side effects in a sandboxed step that can run asynchronously, 3) reduce CI cost by avoiding unnecessary full-lint runs, and 4) make rollout reversible with feature flags. What this changes: - New scripts/release/sandbox-invoke.sh: a minimal, hermetic sandbox runner that reproduces release hooks (changelog validation, artifact dry-run, signature check) in ~90s on CI images. - CI: ci/workflows/release-sandbox.yml added as a staged post-merge gated job that can be toggled via repo settings. - Lint: ci/workflows/lint-router.yml replaces the previous lint.yml. The router inspects the git diff and maps files to lint shards (js/ts, python, go, infra). For small diffs the router runs a single shard and reports results quickly. - Tooling: scripts/ci/path-mapper.py implements the diff->shard mapping and includes heuristics to prefer fast linters for docs/markdown. - Rollout: feature flag infra/ci:enable_sandbox set to false by default; ops can flip per-branch. Checklist: - [x] Add sandbox job + script - [x] Implement lint router and path mapper - [x] Add unit tests for path-mapper - [x] Update README/CONTRIBUTING with new CI guidance - [x] Canary rollout to non-critical repos (done) - [x] End-to-end smoke: create+merge test PR in staging (passed) Testing summary: unit tests for path-mapper (100% branch coverage on mapping heuristics), local end-to-end against a small sample repo, canary runs across three internal repos for 48h with 0 regressions in lint detection. CI behaviour: initial runs will still run the monolithic lint in a fallback lane for PRs that modify >200 files; that fallback will be removed after two weeks of monitoring. Migration notes: maintainers should consult CONTRIBUTING.md updates which describe how to opt-in/out, and how to add file patterns to the router mapping. Related: ENG-2847 (CI cost targets), ENG-2910 (release automation hygiene).
Diego Ramos: Nice approach. Please ensure path-mapper handles nested monorepos; add tests for mono/ packages.
Morgan Li (author): Added tests for nested monorepos and updated path-mapper heuristics to prefer package.json discovery over top-level globs.
Ava Patel: Can we reduce sandbox runtime further by parallelizing signature checks? If so, please file a follow-up.
Morgan Li (author): Filed follow-up ENG-2989 for parallel signature check improvement; kept sandbox serial for determinism during rollout.
Samir Noor: CI job matrix looks good. One nit: move the feature-flag file to infrastructure/flags to follow convention.
Morgan Li (author): Moved flag file and added backwards-compatible lookup; updated docs.
Introduce a staged release sandbox and compact lint router to improve presubmit feedback times and reduce CI cost. Default behavior unchanged until feature flag enabled. See CONTRIBUTING.md for opt-in instructions.
Feature flag infra/ci:enable_sandbox=false by default. To enable: update infrastructure/flags/ci_flags.yaml on main and flip flag, monitor sandbox job duration and prometheus metric ci_sandbox_duration_seconds. Fallback behavior removed after two-week observation window if no regressions observed.
payload.title: Introduce staged release sandbox and compact lint router

Motivation: rapid incident response for suspected key compromise requires an operator-level ability to temporarily freeze tenant KMS usage without deleting keys or changing customer config. Existing region-pin and KMS-scoping controls handle placement and residency, but there's no safe operational 'fuse' that gates signing/encrypt operations while preserving forensic audit trails. This PR adds a low-risk revocation-fuse primitive and an auditor-facing replay-safeguard for immutable audit segments.

Summary of changes: single continuous description string with checklist and high level details.
- Add KMS revocation-fuse service (revocation-controller) that flips a tenant-scoped fuse flag. When fused, KMS calls return a controlled error code (KMS_TEMPORARY_FUSED) and are routed to an enforceable fallback path in the serving runtime. The fuse is time-bound and requires an operator-signed token to clear.
- Extend audit pipeline with sealed segments: when a fuse event occurs the pipeline generates an immutable sealed-audit segment containing request/response digests and operator metadata; sealed segments can be replayed by investigators using time-limited replay-tokens that are emitted by the audit service.
- RBAC v2 additions: introduce a new scoped role operator.kms.fuse with minimum privileges and a policy template for emergency-fuse workflows. Update role mappings and policy simulator tests.
- Residency/region interaction: ensure fuse operations are honored regardless of region pin; add cross-region signal to replicate fuse state to active failover replicas within the residency bounds.
- Observability: add metrics (kms_fuse_events_total, kms_fuse_active_count), tracing tags (fuse.operator_id, fuse.reason) and dashboard tile.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc: linear ENG-9482 attached in PR description (internal link).
- [x] Unit + integration tests for controller and runtime fallback.
- [x] End-to-end test verifying sealed-audit segment immutability and replay-token scoping.
- [x] Minimal docs for operators and runbook: runbooks/operators/kms-fuse.md added.
- [x] Security review: SEC-1120 signed off (see reviewer thread).

Commits (high-level):
- feat(kms): add revocation-controller and API endpoints (fuse, unfuse, status)
- feat(audit): sealed-audit segment generator + replay-token endpoint
- perf(runtime): fast-path for KMS_TEMPORARY_FUSED and graceful fallback to cached-wrapped-key path
- chore(rbac): role template and simulator test cases
- docs: operator runbook and console tile instructions

Files changed (high level):
- services/kms/revocation_controller.go (new) -- core fuse state machine + API
- services/kms/handlers.go (mod) -- integration hooks and error codes KMS_TEMPORARY_FUSED
- runtime/kms_adapter.go (mod) -- fast-path handling and fallback strategy code comment added
- audit/sealed_segmenter.py (new) -- creates sealed segments with digest+operator metadata and stores to sealed-audit S3 namespace
- audit/replay_service.go (new) -- mint replay-tokens scoped by investigator id and time window
- rbac/templates/operator_kms_fuse.yaml (new) -- role template for operator.kms.fuse
- docs/runbooks/operators/kms-fuse.md (new) -- operational steps and post-mortem checklist

Small illustrative snippet (runtime fast-path): ``if err == KMS_TEMPORARY_FUSED { return ErrFuseActive } // caller triggers fallback`` (kept intentionally concise).

Review conversation (condensed into chronological thread):
- Linda Park (review): "Nice minimal surface. Please ensure the replay-token audience is one-time and can't be used to extract raw key material."
- Aisha Kumar (author): "Replay tokens are scoped to sealed-audit object IDs, include nonce+expiry and require investigator cert via mTLS. Added tests in audit/replay_service_test.go to prove token revocation on expiry."
- Marco Ruiz (review): "What happens if the operator mistakenly unfuses? Can we add an undo audit event and an automatic cooldown?"
- Aisha Kumar: "Added cooldown config (default 1h) and an explicit operator.reason field that is required for unfuse; we log undo events to sealed segments too."
- Sasha Ivanov (security): "Simulate cross-region replication -- ensure fusion state doesn't break residency guarantees."
- Aisha Kumar: "Added cross-region signal logic with residency guard; fuse replication is only broadcast to replicas within the tenant's residency zone (see revocation_controller.go)."
- CI: initial lint failed on audit naming; fixed. Integration pipeline passed; security scan flagged a missing KMS permission in a test role which was corrected. Final CI status: pass.

Operational notes and runbook summary:
- Fuse semantics: time-bound (configurable), operator-initiated, tenant-scoped. Intended for suspected compromise / emergency halts. Not for routine deployments.
- Audit guarantees: sealed segments are append-only, content-addressed (sha256), and stored under sealed-audit/<tenant>/<segment-id>. Replay tokens allow read-only access to a single segment for a limited window and are issued by the audit service after operator request with justification.
- RBAC: operator.kms.fuse is intentionally narrow; plan to gate in RBAC policy bundle for SOC2 environments.

Release notes: "Add emergency KMS revocation-fuse primitive and sealed-audit replay safeguard. Operators can temporarily freeze tenant KMS usage while preserving immutable audit artifacts for investigation. Includes RBAC templates and runbook."

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after approvals from Linda Park and Sasha Ivanov.

Follow-ups (post-merge):
- ENG-9610: add UI controls to Redwood Console for safe-fuse initiation and justification capture.
- SEC-1203: threat-model audit of replay-token lifecycle and HSM usage for sealed segment signing.

Contact: author Aisha Kumar (aisha.k@redwood.ai) for questions and rollout coordination.
payload.title: Introduce KMS revocation-fuse and audit-replay safeguard

Problem: presubmit lint jobs are expensive and noisy; transient dependency spikes increase CI latency. This PR introduces a lightweight, long-lived lint runtime pool (shared JVM/Node environments) plus a scheduled dependency grooming task to keep devdeps compact. Goals: reduce presubmit latency variance, cut install IO, and make small dependency churn visible for engineering teams.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a new presubmit runner material: .github/workflows/presubmit-lightweight.yml that routes lint-only PRs into the lightweight pool.
- Implements a lint pool coordinator: ci/lint/pool_coordinator.go (small state machine, in-memory leases with optional Redis backing).
- Replaces heavy per-job toolchain bootstrap for JS/TS linters with a cached shared environment (ci/images/presubmit-lint.tar).
- Adds tools/dep-groom.sh, a scheduled task (GH Action scheduled workflow) that runs `npm audit --json`-style checks, reports candidate devdep removals in an issue, and pins transient transitive dependencies when safe.
- Adds metrics and tracing hooks: observability/lint_pool.md and light opentelemetry spans in the coordinator.

Why now: recent infra telemetry showed a 30% tail latency increase in presubmit stage during peak weekdays (Q1), driven by fluctuating package install times and cold runner boot. The lightweight pool removes repeated full bootstrap costs and surfaces dependency churn for owners to handle proactively.

Backward compatibility and rollout: default main presubmit lane unchanged. New lightweight lane is opt-in by adding label `ci:light-lint` (and later we will add detection for lint-only changes). The dep-groom workflow runs weekly and creates issues rather than auto-mutating lockfiles for safety.

Checklist:
- [x] Add lightweight GH workflow and pool coordinator implementation
- [x] Add small shim script to create/restore cached toolchain images
- [x] Add scheduled dep-groom workflow and reporting stub
- [x] Add observability docs and dashboard stubs
- [x] Unit tests for coordinator lease behavior
- [x] Integration smoke run using CI preview environment

Commits summary: 
- 7 commits: initial coordinator prototype; workflow and image shim; dep-groom script + report template; unit tests; docs and dashboard; CI fixes; squash and tidy.

High-level files changed (examples): 
- .github/workflows/presubmit-lightweight.yml
- .github/workflows/dep-groom-schedule.yml
- ci/lint/pool_coordinator.go
- ci/images/Makefile (add presubmit-lint image target)
- ci/scripts/cache_toolchain.sh
- tools/dep-groom.sh
- observability/lint_pool.md
- tests/ci/lint_pool_test.go

CI notes: initial run failed on flaky image extraction (fixed in commit 4). Unit tests pass locally and in CI after the fix. Nightly smoke run against the preview cluster validated end-to-end path (job leased, runner executed, artifacts uploaded).

Rollout plan (post-merge): enable lightweight lane for the infra and docs teams for 1 week, measure presubmit median and p95 latency, then expand opt-in labels to auto-detect lint-only PRs. Dep-groom will be observed for 4 cycles before any automation for lockfile edits is considered.

Related Linear tickets: ENG-4021 (presubmit latency investigation), ENG-4090 (dep grooming spec). Related past work: some ideas derived from presubmit-minifier RFC and prior presubmit-prober experiments.

Notes for reviewers: focus review on coordinator lease edge-cases, security around cached images (we do not elevate privileges), and the dep-groom report format (it intentionally avoids automated changes).
Ava Chen: Overall looks good. Two concerns: lease stealing needs a small backoff to avoid tight loops; also please add a comment about why Redis is optional.
Laila Kapoor: Reply: added jitter on lease renewal and documented Redis optionality in code and observability/lint_pool.md
Diego Morales: Suggestion: make presubmit-lightweight workflow opt-in via label (good to avoid accidental routing). Implemented.
Priya Nair: Security note: cached images must be rebuilt on base image CVE updates. Added remediation note in observability doc.
Introduce opt-in lightweight presubmit lint lane (label: ci:light-lint) that uses a shared cached toolchain to reduce presubmit latency; add a weekly dependency grooming reporter that surfaces devdep churn for owners. No automatic lockfile edits.

payload.body:
Context: SIEM-ready audit export is entering limited beta and needs safe rollout controls at the tenant boundary. This PR adds (1) a hard kill switch, (2) a tenant allowlist gate, and (3) internal admin tooling to manage the allowlist without code deploys. The goal is to ensure we can enable a small cohort (hosted + dedicated) while maintaining strict tenant isolation and giving SRE a fast rollback lever during incidents.

What this changes: Adds feature flags under the `audit_export` namespace: `audit_export.enabled` (global kill switch, default=false) and `audit_export.beta_tenant_allowlist` (explicit allowlist of tenant IDs, default=empty). Both must evaluate true for a tenant to access audit export configuration APIs and for the exporter control-plane sync to serve configs for that tenant. Gating points: (a) Control plane: export config CRUD endpoints and status endpoints return `404` when the tenant is not enabled (to avoid feature discovery and reduce support confusion). (b) Exporter config feed: non-allowed tenants are filtered server-side to ensure exporter never receives configs for disabled tenants. (c) Console: UI endpoints use the same gating and show a generic "not available" empty state when gated.

Admin tooling: Adds an internal-only admin endpoint + CLI wrapper for manipulating the allowlist (add/remove/list) behind `internal:feature_flags:write` and `rbac:tenant_admin` checks. All allowlist mutations emit an audit event (`audit_export.rollout_allowlist.updated`) that includes actor, tenant_id, and diff (added/removed tenant ids) with PII-safe redaction rules.

Safety/operability: Adds a single kill switch that immediately blocks new config writes and stops serving configs to the exporter on next poll. Includes a small runbook snippet in the internal docs page referenced by SRE: expected propagation time (<60s), how to confirm gate status, and how to safely re-enable (stage: enable kill switch -> add tenant(s) -> verify exporter lag/health -> notify PM).

Testing: Unit tests for flag evaluation + authorization; integration tests for the control-plane endpoints returning 404 when gated; smoke test for exporter config feed filtering; and a minimal CLI e2e in CI (mock control plane).

Rollout plan: Land behind default-off flags. For beta accounts, we will enable `audit_export.enabled=true` and add tenant ids to allowlist via admin tooling. This PR does not change any defaults for existing tenants.

Notes / non-goals: This does not add Private/on-prem controls beyond flag plumbing; Private support remains out of scope for beta. No changes to delivery semantics (at-least-once) in exporter; this is strictly rollout gating.

Screenshots: N/A (backend + internal tooling only).

payload.body:
Context & motivation: production workloads show frequent short-lived bursts (chat multiplexer fan-out, streaming completions) that create temporary KV cache pressure. Under those patterns the paged block allocator can stall on synchronous evictions and cold reads, producing p99 latency spikes. This PR implements a proactive reclaim + prefetch path in the block allocator and ties it into the request scheduler so hot-path requests can pre-warm adjacent blocks instead of blocking on synchronous allocations.

What this PR does (high level): single continuous description of changes: added a background reclaim worker that tracks a lightweight hotset, heuristically reclaims low-utility blocks during idle CPU cycles, and issues async prefetches when a request accesses a prefix that suggests near-future access (sequence-aware prefetch). The allocator exposes two knobs: reclaim_budget and prefetch_threshold. We wire allocator events into the continuous batching scheduler so that batches containing "fast-path" tokens can trigger immediate prefetch of the next chunks, reducing synchronous page faults. The design favors bounded background work and cooperative prefetch to avoid increased GPU stalls.

Key design points: 1) Epoch-based reuse counters: reduce contention by only promoting reuse candidates at epoch boundaries (cheap atomic counters). 2) Hotset detector: probabilistic LRU sketch that feeds reclaim priorities; tiny memory overhead. 3) Async prefetch: non-blocking I/O to warm KV pages on host or NVMe before kernel hot path needs them. 4) Scheduler integration: a request tag "fast-path-prefetch" is added by the runtime when continuous batching predicts short next-token windows. 5) Safety: reclaim never frees blocks in use (pin-bit + epoch); prefetch is best-effort and fails silently.

Performance summary (canary & lab): microbench with synthetic bursty fanout (100ms bursts, 10x QPS): p99 latency reduced from ~210ms to ~120ms on our standard benchmark rig; median unchanged. End-to-end RL workload (multiplexed chat) showed 38% fewer synchronous allocation stalls and 7% lower token CPU cost due to fewer kernel re-compiles from miss patterns. Canary across 10 customers for a week: no regressions, average request error rate unchanged.

Backward compatibility & rollout: opt-in feature flag allocator.mode=proactive; default off for release build. Gradual rollout plan included in the PR: feature gated, mobile canary, then platform-wide release. No external API changes.

Test plan: unit tests for reclaim worker, hotset sketch, and epoch reuse; integration test that simulates prefetch race and ensures no double-free; end-to-end perf test added to perf-canary suite. CI includes deterministic allocator fuzz harness.

Files changed (high level): implemented new allocator core (runtime/kv/block_allocator/proactive_allocator.{cc,h}), hotset sketch (runtime/kv/hotset_sketch.h), scheduler hooks (runtime/scheduler/prefetch_integration.cc), config bindings and docs (docs/allocator.md), tests (tests/kv/proactive_reclaim_test.cc, tests/kv/prefetch_integration_test.cc), and updates to perf-canary configs.

Short code/config snippet (illustrative): allocator:
  mode: proactive
  reclaim_budget: 32  # max blocks reclaimed per idle epoch
  prefetch_threshold: 0.25  # fraction of hotset hit probability that triggers prefetch

Edge cases and mitigations: 1) noisy tenants: sketch adapts decay rate per tenant; heavy noisy traffic yields lower prefetch aggressiveness. 2) NVMe-backed stores: prefetch has backpressure and is capped by prefetch_budget to avoid I/O queuing. 3) Memory storms: background reclaim is throttled when memory pressure crosses a configured watermark.

Commit summary (see commits/ below): initial implementation + unit tests; hotset sketch; scheduler hook; add config bindings; integration tests; perf tweaks and CI fixes; docs and release notes.

Review & approvals: reviewers requested clarifications on reuse semantics (answered: epoch decouples pin lifetime from immediate reuse) and on what happens during host OOM (answered: reclaim will be opportunistic but never evict pinned blocks). Performance owner asked for microbench plots; attached results. After two rounds of feedback and a small refactor to reduce allocator lock contention, reviewers approved.

Merge: squashed and merged to main after CI passed.

Why this is different from previous allocator work: previous PRs focused on compacting or reusing freed blocks in-place and softpin heuristics. This change is behaviorally different: it proactively reclaims during idle windows and prefetches predicted pages, which reduces synchronous blocking on first access and complements reuse/pin improvements.

Monitoring & rollout notes: added allocator.reclaim.rate and allocator.prefetch.hits metrics and dashboard tile. Alert: reclaim_rate_drop -> investigation. Canary showed stable reclaim_rate ~20-30 blocks/s on typical medium workloads.

Follow-ups: 1) experimental cross-tenant prefetch global budget, 2) GPU-side prefetch hints to the kernel for faster device-side warming, 3) quantized prefetch prioritization for embd-heavy workloads.
Introduce a proactive block allocator with background reclaim and prefetch heuristics for the paged KV cache. Improves p99 tail latency under bursty workloads; opt-in via config. No API changes.
Liam Chen: please clarify when epoch counter increments and how it avoids ABA; author: epoch increments on allocation boundary not per access, avoids ABA by combining pin-bit check.
Priya Nair: what happens on NVMe slowdowns? author: prefetch_budget caps and prefetch backpressure prevents I/O queue saturation.
Diego Alvarez: lock contention observed in microbench; author: refactor applied to move hotset updates off hot path and use per-shard atomics; re-run benchmarks and attached results.
CI bot: allocator fuzz harness flaky twice; author: added deterministic seed and fixed race in test harness; CI passed after fix.

Context: We see a class of hard-to-debug latency/cost regressions where short prefixes or cold KV cache invocations (e.g. chat threads resumed after long idle periods) cause disproportionate per-token cost and increase GPU batch-drop incidents. Root cause analysis showed that some invocations with near-zero KV hits still get co-batched with warmed calls and amplify backpressure or OOM scenarios. Goal: provide low-noise signals to (1) quantify per-invocation 'warmth' so teams can correlate latency/cost to cache warming, and (2) attribute batch drops to the invocation(s) most likely responsible so SREs and runtime engineers can triage scheduling/kernel hotspots. This PR introduces a token-warmth-meter and batch-drop attribution pipeline.
Adds a runtime 'token_warmth' metric and batch-drop attribution counters; new dashboard panels and an alert to surface cold-prefix driven cost/latency regressions.
feat(telemetry): add token_warmth gauge and histogram (runtime/metrics)
perf(runtime): compute warm_score from kv_hit_rate and prefix_len in serving path
feat(obs): dashboard + panel for token-warmth distribution by model/tenant
fix(tests): make warmth meter deterministic for unit tests
chore(docs): telemetry guide for interpreting token_warmth and batch-drop metrics
runtime/serving/kv_cache.go - compute kv_hit_rate per invocation and expose to metrics
runtime/serving/warmth_meter.go - new component to derive warm_score and labels
telemetry/metrics_registry.go - register token_warmth gauge and warm_score histogram
observability/dashboards/token-warmth-panel.json - new Grafana panels and notes
alerts/batch-drop-attribution.yaml - alert rule + runbook for batch-drop spikes
sdk/python/examples/telemetry_warmth_example.py - example for capturing warm_score client-side
docs/telemetry/warmth.md - explanation, interpretation, and suggested remediation steps
Ava Chen: Nice signal — can you clarify the warm_score formula? The PR text mentions kv_hit_rate and prefix_len but doesn't show the exact mapping.
Author (Marisol): Warm_score = 0.6 * kv_hit_rate + 0.3 * min(1, prefix_len/32) + 0.1 * recent_invocation_rate_normalized. I added inline comments and a short doc section explaining the weights and rationale.
Devon Ross: Concern: adding histogram cardinality by tenant+model may increase storage. Can we coarse-bin tenant to tier (free/prod/enterprise) instead?
Author: Switched tenant label to tenant_tier in metrics registry to limit cardinality; retained model and route labels.
Priya Natarajan: Tests flaked on CI (telemetry deterministic test). Please add a deterministic seed for mock clock.
Author: Added deterministic clock seed and fixed a race in the test harness. CI green on rerun.
CI run 1: unit tests failed (telemetry deterministic test) - flaky due to clock non-determinism
CI run 2: unit + integration + lint passed after fixing test harness and reducing metric label cardinality
E2E perf bench: token-warmth emissions add ~0.2% p99 latency overhead in serving hot path (measured)
New dashboard: Observability > Token Warmth - shows warm_score distribution by model/tenant_tier and rolling cost-per-token by warm_score bucket
New alert: BatchDropSpike -> fires when sum(batch_drop_count) / sum(invocations) > 0.01 for 5m AND median(token_warmth) < 0.35 for same window. Runbook links to interpret batch attribution panel.
Guidance: If alert correlates to low warm_score, recommend prefix-warmup caching, request coalescing backoff, or conservative scheduling for cold invocations.
Metrics: token_warmth gauge per-invocation, token_warmth_bucket histogram (0.0-1.0 in 10 buckets), batch_drop_reason label on batch_drop_count
Storage: tenant label reduced to tenant_tier to limit cardinality; additional metric volume estimated at ~0.8% of current telemetry traffic
Runtime: warm_score calculation is a few arithmetic ops; measured overhead ~0.2% p99 latency on hot paths
Rollout: feature-flagged behind telemetry.optimizer=true for 2 weeks then enabled account-wide
Unit: warm_score edge cases, deterministic clock; added mocks for kv cache hit scenarios
Integration: end-to-end invocation with synthetic cold/warm sequences and batch-drop injection
Perf: microbench harness showing <1% throughput regression; end-to-end bench showed 0.2% p99 latency overhead
No sensitive data emitted. token_warmth is numeric and coarse labels only include tenant_tier, model, route. Confirmed with Security - no PII risk.
Metrics endpoint rate-limited; no change to auth model.
Squashed and merged after reviewers approved. Adjusted metric cardinality per review and fixed a test race. Dashboard and runbook files included in the merge commit.
Monitor token_warmth histogram in staging for 48h to detect unexpected cardinality or cost impact
Enable alert in staging, then promote to prod after 48h if no false positives
Schedule a short cross-team sync (obs + runtime) to review early signals and proposed throttling knobs

Adds a rehearsal lane controller with reservoir-based shadowing and an automatic revert path when telemetry gates fail. No user-facing API changes. Backwards compatible with existing rollout policies.
Motivation: we want a lightweight, low-risk way to rehearse model promotions using live traffic without impacting production SLOs. Existing shadow lanes either capture 100% of a chosen slice or mirror at fixed fractions; they lack a flow-control mechanism that prevents rehearsal storms and they require manual rollback procedures. This PR introduces a 'traffic reservoir' concept for rehearsal lanes: a bounded token pool that gates how many concurrent rehearse requests are admitted during a time window, plus an autorevert controller that automatically rewinds the rehearsal if safety gates are tripped.

Design summary: implement a RehearsalScheduler and ReservoirManager integrated into the rollout orchestrator. Key ideas: 1) Reservoir sizing heuristic derived from historical concurrency and SLO headroom; 2) Time-windowed token buckets per cohort to limit rehearse admission spikes; 3) Snapshot-based rehearsal mode that can playback a small sample deterministically for offline replay; 4) Telemetry tags (rehearsal_id, reservoir_token_id, cohort_tag) injected to tracing/metrics for direct attribution; 5) Autorevert runs a safe rewind (session-affinity-aware) and records a revert snapshot for postmortem.

What changed (high level): added services/orchestrator/rehearsal_scheduler.go, services/orchestrator/reservoir_manager.go, ops/playbooks/rehearsal-runbook.md, tests/integration/rehearsal_end_to_end_test.go, docs/rollouts/rehearsal-lanes.md and small hooks in services/orchestrator/traffic_router.go and telemetry/tags.go. The scheduler exposes a short-lived REST control endpoint for ops to query reservoir state.

Testing: unit tests for reservoir token lifecycle, integration test that runs a synthetic traffic burst and asserts no production latency regression, smoke runbook included for oncall. Telemetry includes a new gauge rehearsal.reservoir.available and histogram rehearsal.latency.replay.

Rollout plan: land behind feature flag rollout.rehearsal_v2; enable in staging for 48h with canary cohorts (1% of traffic, deterministic cohort id). After a clean staging run, enable in prod with gradual cohort increase 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 24h windows. Autorevert is enabled by default for rehearsals in prod.

Rollback and safety: autorevert is automatic when either (a) rehearsal error rate delta > 2x baseline AND > 0.5pp absolute, or (b) p99 latency regression exceeds 25% vs baseline for two consecutive windows. Revert is executed as a transactional swap with session affinity preservation where possible; if affinity cannot be preserved, revert will trigger a short-lived shadow replay of affected sessions to ensure correctness before commit.

Related: builds on ENG-2049 (cohort tagging infra) and ENG-2098 (telemetry gating primitives). See SUP-4821 for an incident that motivated automatic revert tooling.

Checklist: [x] unit tests added [x] integration smoke [x] docs updated [x] runbook + playbook [x] alert rules for rehearsal.* metrics [x] feature flagged

Notes: this change is focused on rehearsal lanes (non-user-facing) and should not alter production routing unless the feature flag is turned on. The reservoir heuristic can be tuned remotely via ops API for emergency throttling.
Aisha Gupta: Can you clarify the reservoir sizing default? We should avoid a conservative default that blocks all rehearsals in smaller tenants.
Author: Default uses a 95th percentile concurrent baseline from 7d and adds a 10% headroom; ops can override via control endpoint. Updated comment in reservoir_manager.go.
Marco Chen: Race condition looked plausible in transactional revert path; please add a test that covers concurrent revert+promote.
Author: Added fix and unit test 'revert_race_test' and included a short-circuit to serialize revert/promote actions per cohort. See tests/unit folder.
Leah Ortega: Why are rehearsal tags at DEBUG level only? We need them at INFO for short-term debugging during rollout.
Author: Switched to INFO for first 24h post-enable and added sampling for long-term retention. See telemetry/tags.go.
Aisha Gupta: Approving — LGTM after CI green and runbook added.
Marco Chen: Verified integration test locally, CI flake unrelated. Approved.
CI Bot: All required checks passed. Ready to merge.

Summary: Implement hedged autoscaler and burst fractionation to improve service continuity and smoother shared burst behavior for Dedicated fleets. Motivation: previously, large tenant microbursts could either exhaust warm pools or force heavy on-demand provisioning spikes. This PR adds a soft-headroom hedging strategy plus a deterministic fractionation algorithm to split burst budgets into smaller microcredits so that warm pools and queueing interact more predictably. The implementation is opt-in via fleet configuration flags (hedge_mode, burst_fractionation_factor) and defaults to off for safety during rollout.

Detailed changes: 1) Autoscaler: new hedged_autoscaler.go implements a soft-headroom model that maintains an anticipatory reserve (fraction of committed capacity plus ephemeral buffer) per-availability-zone. The controller monitors recent allocate/release latencies and computes a hedge score; when hedge_score > threshold the allocator keeps additional warmlets instead of decommitting immediately. New configuration options: hedge_mode=(off|passive|aggressive), hedge_target_percent, hedge_decay_seconds. 2) Burst fractionation: burst_fractionator.go provides deterministic tokenization of tenant burst budgets into microcredits (default size = 5% of tenant burst, configurable via burst_fractionation_factor). Microcredits are accounted separately in the burst ledger and have TTL/aging to avoid long-term accumulation. 3) Metrics & telemetry: add throughput_headroom_p50/p90, burst_fraction_in_flight, microcredit_reuse_rate, credit_age_seconds histograms. These metrics feed the Console dashboard and autoscaler decision logs. 4) Fairness & safety: an updated reservation allocator enforces per-tenant minimum guarantees when fractionation is enabled; a soft-fallback path routes excess microcredits to a spill queue serviced by on-demand pool to avoid hard rejections. 5) Backwards compatibility and migration: feature gate checks added around allocation path; existing reservation files and metrics remain unchanged unless feature enabled. 6) Tests & CI: unit tests for fractionation edge cases, integration test that simulates overlapping bursts across two tenants, and a lightweight e2e canary in perf-canary that ran in the CI job.

Why unique / important: This approach reduces large allocation churn and smooths out headroom consumption spikes by allowing the system to service bursts as a sequence of smaller credits while still preserving tenant guarantees. It also provides richer telemetry to make autoscaler tuning observable.

Risk & rollout plan: default is feature-gated off. Rollout steps: 1) Merge behind feature flag; 2) Enable passive hedge_mode in a single dedicated fleet used for internal load tests; 3) Monitor new telemetry for 48h (throughput_headroom_p90, microcredit_reuse_rate, and credit_age_seconds) and evaluate cost/latency; 4) enable burst_fractionation_factor gradually via canary; 5) optionally move to aggressive mode after 2 weeks of stable metrics. Backout: disable feature flags and drain warmlets; hedged autoscaler intentionally keeps conservative defaults to avoid regressions.

Observability & ops notes: Added traces around allocate/deallocate with a new trace tag "hedge_score" and an allocation_reason enum (scheduled|hedge_hold|microcredit). Console dashboard panels suggested in the PR description (linked in this PR) include per-tenant microcredit usage heatmap and AZ headroom trend.

Configuration examples: fleet.yaml snippet: hedge_mode: passive hedge_target_percent: "8" hedge_decay_seconds: "600" burst_fractionation_factor: "0.05"

Related work: touches autoscaler core (pkg/autoscaler), allocator (pkg/allocator), ledger (pkg/burstledger), and telemetry plumbing (pkg/observability). See Linear ENG-3221 and ENG-3309 for product/engineering requirements.

Files changed (high level): pkg/autoscaler/hedged_autoscaler.go pkg/allocator/burst_fractionator.go pkg/burstledger/ledger_accounting.go pkg/observability/metrics_registry.go config/fleet_defaults.go test/integration/burst_fractionation_test.go test/unit/hedge_score_test.go examples/fleet-hedge.yaml docs/operator/hedge-autoscaler.md CI: added perf-canary job linking to the new test harness.

Commits summary: - initial hedged autoscaler scaffolding and interfaces - fractionation token model and ledger integration - conservative allocation fallback and fairness checks - telemetry hooks, metrics registry entries and Console dashboard suggestions - unit and integration tests + CI job - docs and configuration examples

Merge notes: squashed to a single commit; post-merge follow-ups include a telemetry naming normalization pass and a small refactor of warmlet lifecycle to expose reuse metrics.
Adds an opt-in hedged autoscaler mode and a burst fractionation mechanism for Dedicated fleets. Introduces new telemetry metrics for headroom/credit utilization and a set of knobs to tune burst microcredits. No user-facing API breaking changes.
Aisha: please add a safety net to avoid double-counting microcredits when migrations occur; noted and added (ledger idempotency). Marco: can we bound memory usage for microcredit queue? response: added ttl-based compaction and a fixed memory cap per-tenant. Liang: request clearer metric names and unit tests for credit aging; addressed and expanded tests. Approvals: Aisha approved after idempotency test, Marco approved after memory cap added, Liang approved after metric name change. One CI flaky e2e retried and passed.

Adds a mediating layer to SLO enforcement that coordinates per-region tenant slowdowns and a soft-quarantine circuit braid to reduce oscillation during failovers; includes telemetry and a targeted hotfix for region failover TTL regression.
Summary: Implements a lightweight 'SLO mediator' service that sits between the global enforcer and regional routers to coordinate soft-quarantine windows and tenant circuit braided state, preventing rapid reopen flaps during region failover. Motivation: recent incidents showed oscillation when multiple regions reopened simultaneously causing overload and cascade evictions. The mediator introduces short-lived, coordinated windows and a quorum-driven reopen handshake to smooth transitions without hard tenant eviction. Changes: 1) pkg/slo/mediator.go: new mediator implementation with stateful leases, quorum reopen handshake, and exponential reopen backoff per-tenant; 2) pkg/slo/enforcer.go: hooks to consult mediator before applying emergency eviction and a fast-path when mediator unavailable; 3) runtime/router/region_failover.go: integrate mediator calls into regional failover flow and drift-tolerant TTL handling; 4) charts/slo-mediator/: Helm chart + canary config; 5) telemetry/metrics.yaml: added slo_mediator.* counters and histograms and circuit_braid.state gauge; 6) test/fixtures/slo_mediator/: deterministic unit tests and a small harness that simulates cross-region reopen storms; 7) cmd/installer/templates/manifest.yaml: optional mediator sidecar flag for Private installs. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear ENG-1482 - [x] Unit tests (pkg/slo/*) - [x] Integration smoke harness (simulated cross-region) - [x] Canary Helm chart with probe thresholds - [x] Telemetry and dashboard notes for oncall Runbook notes: When enabling mediator, start in read-only mode (consult-only) for 24h canary, then flip to active for tenants flagged by the rollout list. The mediator exposes debug endpoints to snapshot quorum state and active soft-quarantine windows. Notable fixes: During integration we found a TTL regression in region_failover.go where a reopened region could carry stale lease durations; this PR includes a hotfix that normalizes TTLs against mediator-provided epoch time to eliminate drift. Commits summary: - Add mediator core and tests (Anjali Rao) - Hook mediator into enforcer and router (Anjali Rao) - Helm/chart + installer template (Sofia Alvarez) - Telemetry + dashboards (Kai Nakamura) - Fix TTL drift bug discovered in integration (Anjali Rao) Files changed (high-level): pkg/slo/mediator.go, pkg/slo/mediator_test.go, pkg/slo/enforcer.go, runtime/router/region_failover.go, charts/slo-mediator/values.yaml, telemetry/metrics.yaml, cmd/installer/templates/manifest.yaml Review conversation: Miles Chen: "High level LGTM, please add more assert coverage around quorum failure modes and a comment on the expected lease jitter." Author (Anjali): "Added tests for quorum miss and a code comment describing jitter math; included a small doc note in the chart README." Sofia Alvarez: "Can we gate the mediator rollout by tenant label to keep blast radius small?" Author: "Yes — added a feature flag and per-tenant opt-in list in the Helm chart and installer template." Kai Nakamura: "Telemetry looks good; please ensure the histograms use the standard buckets. Also request a short-run load test on perf-canary." Author: "Adjusted histogram buckets to match platform convention and ran a 30m perf-canary against canary config; results attached in the CI run." Approvals & gating: Miles approved after tests green; Sofia approved after gating flag added. CI summary: linux/build: pass; unit-tests: pass (98% on slo package); integration/smoke: failed initially due to TTL race, fix pushed and rerun: pass; lint: pass; perf-canary: ran 30m canary — stable under 20% extra latency on failover path; e2e: skipped for canary (manual e2e planned during staged rollout). Rollout plan: 1) Deploy mediator in consult-only mode to staging; 2) Canary in us-west-2 for tenants flagged in rollout list (24h); 3) Flip to active for rollout cohort; 4) Expand regionally with 6h observation windows and automated rollback on SLO regressions. Post-merge actions: create dashboards in Grafana team-space (ticket created ENG-1490), update runbook with mediator debug steps, and schedule a 2-hour post-deploy watch. Merge: squashed and merged to main after approvals. Impact: reduces reopen oscillation and emergency eviction churn during multi-region failovers; expected to lower eviction rate by ~35% in simulated reopen storms. Hotfix note: TTL normalization also prevents a class of cross-region lease drift that could have caused persistent false-positive circuit closures. CI artifacts and canary logs are attached to the PR in GitHub.
payload.title: Coordinated soft-quarantine: regional SLO mediator and tenant circuit braid

Background: complex edge and Dedicated customers require deterministic model swap semantics across heterogeneous edge nodes and mid‑deployment failover windows. This PR introduces the 'EdgeLayer Orbit' — a declarative rollout primitive that binds staged traffic slices to deterministic snapshot escrows and an automated rollback escrow reclaim protocol. Motivation: existing canary/AB flows handle traffic fractioning but lack an atomic escrow for KV cache and session affinity state; on partial failures customers saw inconsistent session continuity and difficult manual rollbacks. Proposal summary: 1) a CRD-style declarative config (edge_orbit.yaml) that describes staged bindings (fractions, cohorts, continuity hints), 2) an escrow manager that snapshots lightweight session/KV metadata to short‑lived object blobs with integrity hashes, 3) a decision graph executor that drives staged traffic transitions with safety gates and automatic rollback if escrow restore checks fail. Key behaviors: - atomic escrow checkpoint before each stage cutover - validate-then-commit: new model is exercised by mirrored traffic to canary cohort while escrow proof-of-restore runs in parallel - rollback escrow reclaim: if any stage reports divergence on fidelity metrics or restoration checksum, the executor triggers escrow restore and session rehydration path with telemetry markers - graceful drain with session affinity preservation across multi-region edges

What this PR changes (high level): - runtime/orbit: new EdgeOrbit controller (+ unit/integration tests) - runtime/escrow: escrow manager module with S3-compatible persistence and TTL policies - serving/proxy: staged-binding feature flags and lightweight session snapshot hooks - telemetry: new rollup metrics (orbit.stage_{start,commit,abort}, escrow.restore_latency_ms) and tracing spans for escrow operations - docs: rollout playbook and operator runbook in docs/rollouts/edge-orbit.md

Checklist: - [x] Design doc attached (ENG-2345) - [x] Unit tests for controller and escrow validation - [x] Integration smoke harness against localminikube and s3mock - [x] Telemetry dashboards draft - [x] Backwards-compatible: config defaults to disabled

Testing and rollout plan: staged by feature flag: start with internal Dedicated customers in us-west only; enable mirrored shadow traffic and quiet-canary for 48h, then enable staged commit with 5% cohort, watch orbit.stage_commit_success_rate and escrow.restore_latency_ms for 72h, then ramp. Emergency escape: operator can force 'orbit.abort' to immediate escrow restore (playbook linked). Related: follows patterns from ENG-2761 and borrows session snapshot format from SUP-8891. Rollbacks will emit rollback.reason tags for downstream billing and SRE postmortem aggregation.

Author (Aisha) (2025-08-15): 'Agree, escrow payloads explicitly redact user-identifying fields; added pseudonymization utility and unit tests.'
Priya S. Iyer (2025-08-16): 'What happens if object storage experiences eventual consistency delays? Could the restore checksum be stale?'

Eleni Kouris (2025-08-18): 'Telemetry looks good, add an alert for prolonged escrow restore latency >120s.'
