Motivation: our monolithic lint runner has grown heavy (multi-language toolchain installs, slow cold starts) and is the largest contributor to presubmit setup time. This PR splits lint into language-aware runners and introduces an incremental toolchain verifier to dramatically reduce setup cost while preserving hermeticity and reproducibility. Goals: 1) Reduce presubmit walltime for common small changes by avoiding full toolchain installs; 2) Make CI more debuggable by isolating language-specific failures; 3) Keep a safe fallback to the legacy monolithic runner during rollout. What I changed (summary): - Introduced four lightweight lint runners: lint-python, lint-typescript, lint-go, lint-rust. Each runner uses a trimmed container image with only the language runtime, package manager, and cached toolchain artifacts. - Added ci/toolchain-manifests/* per-language manifests (pinned installers + checksums) and a new step: incremental-toolchain-verifier that verifies a workspace against the manifest and only fetches missing pieces. - Reworked .github/workflows/presubmit.yml to fan out lint jobs based on changed paths (path filters) and added a small orchestrator step to fall back to legacy-lint when multiple languages change in the same PR. - Added a local dev shim (scripts/ci/dev-lint-emulate.sh) so engineers can run the same verifier locally and reproduce CI behavior. - Improved caching: toolchain layer cache-key is now deterministic based on manifest hash + distro snapshot. Rollout plan: staged rollout by repo tag group; enable language-aware runs for high-volume repos first, enable fallback-window metric for 72 hours, then flip monolith off. Observability: new presubmit metrics (presubmit.setup_time_ms, presubmit.cache_hit_ratio) and alerts for >30% fallback rate. Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains unchanged until repo opt-in; the orchestrator emits a deprecation-warning event post-rollout to help teams migrate. Checklist: - [x] implement language-specific runner images - [x] add toolchain manifests and verifier - [x] update presubmit workflow with fan-out and fallback - [x] add local dev shim and docs - [x] metrics + alerts - [x] smoke rollout in infra/* repositories How this reduces cost/time: measured on the infra repo sample, median presubmit setup drops from ~95s to ~28s for small Python/Ts changes (cache hit path). For cross-language large changes the legacy fallback path keeps correctness. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: manifest drift causing unexpected CI failures. Mitigation: verifier fails clearly and suggests the exact manifest delta; automatic bot PRs to update manifests when onboarding new tool versions (future work). - Risk: flakier path detection. Mitigation: early rollout with high-verbosity logging and a quick revert plan. Related: ENG-2123 tracks the orchestrator feature; SUP-4521 is a customer incident that motivated faster presubmit feedback.
Ethan Cole: Nice separation. Two asks: 1) can we keep a single cache key helper rather than duplicated logic across runners? 2) add a short-circuit if manifest hash matches workspace hash to reduce verifier overhead.
Priya Desai: Addressed — introduced ci/cache/key-helper.sh and added an early-exit in verifier when hashes match (second commit).
Marco Alvarez: Please add a note about how this affects release branches (we must not change presubmit on release/*). Added a guard to the workflow to ignore release branches.
Lina Zhou: Approve after CI passes and a short live rollout in infra/* (I ran a smoke test on infra/observability and results look good).
Introduce language-specific lint runners and an incremental toolchain verifier to reduce presubmit setup time and improve debuggability. Opt-in rollout, no immediate breaking changes. See docs/ci/language-runners.md for migration steps.

Motivation: Our presubmit CI has accumulated several small composite actions and bash scripts for preflight checks (dependency scanning, lint gating, and path-aware test slicing). These scripts are a frequent source of flakes and OS-level differences. This PR consolidates thin workflow plugins into a single lightweight Go-based runner, introduces an explicit dependency-visibility manifest to track declared vs. referenced packages across packages in the monorepo, and adds a preflight job that fails fast when untracked transitive deps are introduced.

Scope of changes: Consolidate the plugin surface (composite actions + bash -> single binary), add tools/dep-visibility (manifest + scanner), tighten CI action pinning for critical steps, and replace the presubmit shell integration with a stable Go CLI used by workflows. This reduces flakiness and speeds up Docker/container-based runner cold starts.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces tools/dep-visibility: manifest schema (tools/dep-visibility/manifest.yaml) and a scanner (tools/dep-visibility/scan.go compiled into dep-visibility-check).
- Replaces scripts/presubmit-checks.sh with small Go runner tools/ci/plugin-runner/main.go that load a plugin manifest and run checks in parallel with bounded concurrency.
- Updates .github/workflows/ci.yml to call the Go runner for preflight, and adds a new preflight lane invoked by pull_request to run fast dependency-visibility checks and path-aware test selection.
- Pins a short list of third-party actions in ci/actions/pinned-action-versions.yml and updates workflow references accordingly to improve hermeticity.
- Adds docs/ci/dependency-visibility.md and README.ci.md describing the manifest format and maintenance process.

Checklist:
- [x] Add dep-visibility manifest and scanner (ENG-2029)
- [x] Migrate presubmit shell logic to Go runner (ENG-2030)
- [x] Pin critical GH Actions used in presubmit lane
- [x] Add CI docs and local run instructions
- [x] Performance verification: preflight cold start latency reduced ~30% in sample runs

Why Go: the presubmit scripts previously depended on bash + multiple utilities (jq, awscli, docker) and behaved differently on macOS vs Linux runners. A small Go binary gives reproducible behavior, easy cross-compilation, and a single dependency surface recorded in go.mod. The binary is intentionally minimal and owned by infra.

Rollback plan: revert the workflow change, restore scripts/presubmit-checks.sh, and re-pin action versions. The Go runner is backwards-compatible with current workflow inputs; we can flip back in under 10 minutes if a regression is observed.

Notes for maintainers: update tools/dep-visibility/manifest.yaml when adding new top-level packages or introducing new language ecosystems. The scanner emits a SARIF-like artifact to aid triage and can be run locally with `make check-dep-visibility`.

Related: ENG-2029 (dep visibility), ENG-2030 (ci plugin consolidation), SUP-7123 (support ticket triggered by flaking presubmit).

payload.body:
Summary: This PR introduces the Commitment Thaw Controller and a companion Grace Period Allocator to reduce unnecessary permanent revocations of committed capacity during brief, transient overcommit spikes. Motivation: customers on Dedicated often see allocation churn when short-lived surges cause the autoscaler to decommit reservation commitments aggressively. Permanently revoking commitments for a tenant when the pressure is transient causes increased tail latency and unnecessary warm-up cost when the tenant soon needs capacity again. The goal here is to give recently-decommitted commitments a short, configurable thaw window during which they may be re-bound without counting as a new cold allocation.

What changed (high level):
- New controller: redwood/pkg/autoscaler/thaw_controller.go — reconciles decommitted reservations, tracks 'thaw tokens' per-tenant, and exposes an API to attempt 'thaw binds' that prefer recently-held reservations for a short grace period.
- Allocation layer: redwood/internal/allocator/grace_allocator.go — decorator over existing allocator that observes thaw tokens and prefers soft reclaims when within the grace window.
- API surface: reservation.proto updated with two optional fields: thaw_token and thaw_expires_at (RFC3339 string). Reservation manager persists thaw metadata to existing reservation store (no schema migration required — stored as reservation metadata map).
- Telemetry: new metrics and events added (reservation_thaw_attempts_total, reservation_thaw_success_total, reservation_thaw_failure_reason_count, reservation_grace_active_gauge). Added traces for thaw attempts (tagged by tenant_id, cause).
- Config flags: console and dedicated config: dedicated.autoscaler.commitment_thaw_window (default 30s), dedicated.autoscaler.max_thaw_reclaims_per_minute.
- Tests: unit tests for controller backoff logic, allocator integration tests, and small e2e in perf-canary verifying behavior under a synthetic 90s spike.
- Docs: Redwood Console docs page (docs/observability/commitment-thaw.md) describing metrics and recommended knobs.

Commits (summary):
- 4 commits: initial controller scaffolding; allocator wiring and proto updates; telemetry and tests; fixes for race in reservation store integration.

Files touched (representative):
- redwood/pkg/autoscaler/thaw_controller.go (+220 additions)
- redwood/internal/allocator/grace_allocator.go (+160)
- proto/reservation.proto (+12)
- internal/storage/reservation_store.go (+36) — small metadata persistence changes
- observability/metrics/registry.go (+18)
- tests/autoscaler/thaw_controller_test.go (+120)
- perf-canary/scenarios/thaw_reclaim_smoke.yaml (+18)
- docs/observability/commitment-thaw.md (+28)
- go.mod / go.sum updated for prometheus client patch

Behavioral notes and design decisions:
- The thaw window is intentionally short (default 30s) and configurable. We ship conservative defaults to avoid gaming where tenants hold thaw tokens indefinitely.
- Thaw tokens are per-tenant, time-limited, and rate-limited (configurable). Reclaims using a thaw token do not count as 'cold allocations' for warmup heuristics.
- We implemented a soft-preference in the allocator: when both a thawable reservation and fresh capacity are available, allocator chooses the thawable reservation until its quota is exhausted or the thaw window expires.
- No schema migration: thaw metadata is stored in the reservation metadata map so older controllers ignore the keys safely.

CI and tests:
- Initial CI run failed (race detected in reservation_store test) — root cause was a map write without lock in the fake store. Fixed by adding proper locking in the test helper and adjusting the controller backoff to avoid tight busy loops.
- Unit coverage added for controller state transitions and allocator preference logic. e2e smoke verifies that a paused tenant regains equivalent capacity without triggering a new reservation allocation metric.
- CI summary: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration: pass (perf-canary smoke), lint: pass, e2e: pass.

Review thread (high level):
- Aisha Patel: Asked for clarity on race conditions between allocator preference and eviction. Requested explicit unit test where thaw token expires mid-reclaim. Also asked to expose metric for thaw token churn. Comment: "Add a test where thaw_expires_at is reached during an allocation — we should ensure we don't double-count quota."
- Author (Evelyn): Added thaw expiry test, exposed reservation_thaw_failure_reason_count and documented failure reasons. Updated PR with additional test and minor allocator simplification to check token expiry atomically.
- Marco Reyes: Suggested making the default window shorter (20s) for now; we kept 30s after discussion because some customers exhibited <10s bursts; added a console toggle to override per-deployment.
- Jonas Müller: Noted potential telemetry cardinality and requested tenant_id be a label only on traces and not on Prometheus metrics; changed metrics to use tenant UUID hashed label for low-cardinality and added trace/span attributes with full tenant id.
- Final approvals from Aisha and Marco after small test additions and doc updates.

Backward compatibility and safety:
- The controller is guarded behind a feature flag in dedicated config (enabled by default for this release); the allocator decorator is opt-in via config so we can rollback quickly.
- Metrics added are additive and use low-cardinality labels by default.

Risk and mitigations:
- Risk: Thaw tokens could be abused to hog freed capacity. Mitigation: rate limits and max_thaw_reclaims_per_minute enforced; tokens expire quickly; allocator prefers thawed reservations but still honors tenant-level throttles and SLA-based admission checks.
- Risk: Increased allocator complexity introduces subtle fairness regressions. Mitigation: added unit/regression tests and a perf-canary scenario to validate fairness under mixed workload.

Merging:
- Squashed and merged to main on 2024-11-13 after CI green and two approvals. Merge method: squash. Merge commit: c4b9f3e2a8d6c1b4f9e2d7a6b3c1f0e5d6a7b8c9.

How to validate in staging:
1) Enable dedicated.autoscaler.commitment_thaw_window on staging and set small limits for max_thaw_reclaims_per_minute.
2) Run perf-canary scenario perf-canary/scenarios/thaw_reclaim_smoke.yaml; observe metrics: reservation_thaw_attempts_total increments on spikes and reservation_thaw_success_total matches expected rebinds.
3) Check that warmup metrics do not increment for thaw-based reclaims (ensures we didn't create cold allocations).

Related work:
- ENG-3412 (feature request for transient reclaim behavior)
- ENG-3499 (telemetry for reservation lifecycle)
- SUP-1873 (customer report that motivated conservative rollout)

Notes for follow-ups:
- Consider exposing tenant-scoped UI in Console to observe active thaw tokens and recent thaw history.
- Explore automatic tuning of thaw window per-tenant based on observed spike duration.

Checklist:
- [x] Controller implementation
- [x] Allocator decorator wiring
- [x] Telemetry + registry
- [x] Unit tests + integration test
- [x] Docs
- [x] Perf-canary scenario

If reviewers want, I can split telemetry, API, and controller pieces into smaller PRs to simplify backporting to older stable branches.

Introduce a Commitment Thaw Controller that allows recently-decommitted tenant reservations to temporarily re-claim capacity during short overcommit spikes. Adds telemetry and a configurable grace window.

Context and motivation: Our presubmit latency has regressed ~25% in the last quarter due to monolithic lint/test runners and a growing dev-dependency surface. This causes larger PRs to wait longer and increases CI cost for iterative work. This PR splits the presubmit lint runner into delta-aware fast shards and a smaller full shard for less frequent runs, and introduces a 'dep-minimizer' utility that prunes unused devdeps from language package manifests during CI to reduce install time and cold-cache overhead.

Goals: 1) Cut median presubmit feedback time for small changes by ~40%. 2) Reduce average CI setup time by trimming devdeps in the hot path. 3) Keep default developer experience unchanged for local workflows (no forced removal of declared deps).

What changed (high level):
- Introduce .github/workflows/presubmit-split.yml: declares two lanes: lint-delta (fast, path-aware) and lint-full (conservative, nightly and explicit run).
- Add infra/lint/divider: a small Go binary that maps changed files to lint shards (JS/TS, Go, infra, docs) and emits a compressed shard key used by the workflow matrix.
- Add tools/dep-minimizer: a Python script run in CI that analyzes package.json/go.mod + the changed file list and removes devdeps not touched by the change for the duration of the job (reinstated after CI finishes). This is opt-in per-repo via .depmin-config.toml.
- Update .github/README-presubmit.md with new troubleshooting and opt-in flags.
- Small edits to package.json and go.mod in packages/* to add dep metadata that dep-minimizer uses (devMeta.ignore and devMeta-scopes).

Commits (summary):
- 9b1f5a2: add presubmit-split workflow and initial lint-delta job
- d7c3f9e: introduce lint divider binary + tests
- f32a1bd: add dep-minimizer tool + CI integration
- 5e2c4f0: wire up opt-in config and documentation
- a1b9d44: instrumentation and metrics for presubmit-run-duration

Files changed (representative list):
- .github/workflows/presubmit-split.yml
- infra/lint/divider/main.go (new)
- infra/lint/divider/README.md (new)
- tools/dep-minimizer/minimizer.py (new)
- .depmin-config.toml (new, opt-in)
- .github/README-presubmit.md (updated)
- packages/sdk-js/package.json (devMeta added)
- packages/serving/go.mod (devMeta comments)
- scripts/ci-bootstrap.sh (small hook to run minimizer)
- ci/metrics/presubmit_latency_dashboard.json (minor update)

Design notes and trade-offs: The divider uses a conservative mapping to avoid false-negatives: some file paths map to multiple shards (e.g., changes touching infra scripts and JS code). That means occasionally we run more shards than strictly necessary, but the delta lane dramatically reduces worst-case latency for small author-only changes. The dep-minimizer runs inside the ephemeral CI workspace and only mutates the transient environment; it never commits changes to manifests. We intentionally did not change local dev workflows or yarn/npm lockfile generation.

Testing and validation: Unit tests added for divider mapping (infra/lint/divider/*_test.go) and end-to-end smoke on a synthetic repo in tools/dep-minimizer/testdata. Staging presubmit was exercised on the redwood monorepo for a week via a canary tag; median presubmit latency dropped 36% for PRs touching a single package. We measured CI bootstrap time reduction of ~18% on average for jobs that used minimizer.

CI: Initial run failed due to a flaky network fetch in tools/dep-minimizer integration test; reran the failing job and all checks passed. CI summary: lint-delta smoke (pass), lint-full (skipped for this branch except on nightly), unit tests (pass), go vet/staticcheck (pass), e2e-minimizer (pass after rerun).

Review conversation (highlights):
- Samir Gupta (2026-02-16): "Nice separation — can we ensure the divider respects repo-level overrides?"
  - Maya: "Added .depmin-config.toml and divider now consults .lint-shard-override if present; updated README with examples."
- Lina Chen (2026-02-17): "Dep-minimizer looks useful but I'm wary about edgecases with postinstall scripts. Please add a safety mode that skips minimization when postinstall is defined."
  - Maya: "Added skip for package.json with postinstall and an opt-in flag to force-run (intended for infra repos). Tests updated."
- Tomás Rivera (2026-02-19): "Can we emit telemetry so SRE can alert if minimizer changes CI success rates?"
  - Maya: "Added presubmit_metric.presubmit_minimizer_skipped/ran and posted dashboard update; SRE tagged in the PR."
- Samir (2026-02-20): "Approve after small nits on README."

Follow-ups captured as Linear tasks: ENG-4521 (tune divider mappings per-team), ENG-4680 (expand minimizer heuristics to Python/Poetry), SUP-2045 (support request: opt-out guidance for internal integrations).

Security and compliance: The minimizer runs only in CI ephemeral runners with no persisted secrets. It does not contact external servers except for standard package registries during install. We added a CI hook to abort minimizer if GITHUB_WORKFLOW is not present to avoid accidental local runs.

Rollout and operational notes: Feature is behind a repo-level opt-in flag .depmin-config.toml — initial rollout applied to packages/* and mainstream infra repos. The presubmit-split workflow runs lint-delta by default on PR open/update; lint-full is scheduled nightly and can be triggered manually. Metrics are wired to the presubmit latency dashboard; set an alert if median delta lane latency goes above 60s.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged on 2026-02-22 after approvals and green CI. Changelog entry prepared.

If anything regresses: revert is trivial (single squash commit) or disable minimizer by removing the config file.

Notes: This PR focuses on CI/infra ergonomics and does not change runtime code paths. It should unlock ~faster feedback loops for engineers and measurable CI cost improvements.

Adds a traffic-conditioned throughput confidence fence for canaries; introduces hysteresis-driven rollback budget and dashboarding for throughput SLOs.
Context and motivation: We observed false-positive throughput regressions during short-lived traffic bursts and cross-tenant traffic spikes when running canaries. This PR introduces a traffic-conditional throughput confidence fence: a statistical estimator that normalizes throughput delta signals by recent traffic modality and owns a hysteresis rollback budget so transient spikes do not immediately trigger rollbacks. The feature is intended to reduce noisy canary failures while keeping the fail-fast property for sustained regressions. Implementation summary: 1) Introduced a lightweight traffic-modality classifier that tags windows as steady, bursty, or ramping based on rate derivatives and per-cohort heatmaps. 2) Added a Bayesian throughput delta estimator that conditions on modality and produces a calibrated confidence interval for observed throughput change. 3) Implemented a hysteresis-backed rollback budget: the fence exposes a budget that decays with confirmed regressions and replenishes slowly; rollbacks only occur when inferred regression exceeds confidence threshold and budget allows. 4) Integrated guard into canary orchestrator: policy knobs (sensitivity, lookback, budget-rate) are plumbed through canary config; automatic fallback to conservative rules for low-traffic tenants. 5) Telemetry and dashboarding: new metrics (throughput_delta_ci_lower, throughput_confidence, modality_tag, rollback_budget) + console panels and alert rules. Tests and verification: unit tests for estimator math, deterministic simulation harness that replays historical traffic traces (production and synthetic) to validate false-positive reduction, and an end-to-end integration run in perf-canary staging. Backwards compatibility: feature is opt-in at the canary policy level; default remains previous detector. Rollout plan: feature flagged; staged rollout to internal tenants for 2 weeks, then opt-in for 25% of external canaries before full opt-in. Related items: ENG-1967 (reduce noisy canary rollbacks), ENG-2011 (hysteresis policy design).
Arjun Kapoor: Could the modality classifier be driven from existing rate metrics instead of adding a new collector? Concern about additional cardinality.
Author (Maya Chen): We reuse existing rate streams where possible; added a thin collector only for per-cohort derivatives to avoid increasing global metric cardinality. Updated docs to explain storage impact.
Sophie Alvarez: The hysteresis budget parameters look sensitive; can we expose safe defaults and a debug endpoint to inspect budget state?
Author (Maya Chen): Added a read-only /canary/debug/budget endpoint and set conservative defaults (replenish=0.05/min, drain_threshold=0.95) in config. Included guidance in rollout notes.
Liam O'Neill: Integration test flaked once on CI due to timing; recommend switching the sim to deterministic time base.
Author (Maya Chen): Switched the sim harness to a mocked clock and re-recorded the golden traces; CI stabilized.
Sophie Alvarez: Approve after docs and metrics schema clarified.
payload.title: traffic-conditional throughput confidence fence and hysteresis rollback policy

payload.body:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally face bursty traffic that transiently exceeds committed capacity and existing burst credit pools. We need a cluster-level slack allocator that dynamically carves short-lived slack budgets from underutilized pools and a gating mechanism at the ingress to avoid amplification storms when reclaimed capacity is delayed. This PR implements a Cluster Slack Allocator (CSA) and a Burst Throttle Gate (BTG) to improve throughput guarantees and reduce end-to-end latency tail during multi-tenant bursts.

Summary of changes: - New runtime controller (cluster/slack_allocator.go) implementing CSA with time-weighted slack accounting and per-pool fairness heuristics. - Ingress gate component (gateway/burst_throttle_gate.go) that consults CSA via a lightweight API to accept/reject burst requests and emit backpressure signals compatible with the existing gateway circuit. - Telemetry: introduce slack_utilization and burst_gate_decisions metrics with percentile sampling and per-pool tagging (telemetry/metrics.go). - Autoscaler integration: the allocator exports short-lived allocation hints to the fleet autoscaler, enabling opportunistic warm-pool adjustments without violating reservation contracts. - Tests: unit tests for allocator invariants, integration test that replays synthetic burst traces to validate fairness and latency impact. - Docs: configuration docs and tuning guide (docs/dedicated/cluster-slack.md).

Checklist: - [x] Design doc link: internal/ENG-6421 (architecture and tradeoffs) - [x] Unit tests added for allocator invariants - [x] Integration harness replayed against perf-lab traces - [x] Backwards-compatible config defaults - [x] Canary plan included in release notes

Commits (high level): 1) initial prototype of CSA and gate (wip, refactor) 2) add metrics and telemetry labels 3) autoscaler hint integration and config knobs 4) add unit + integration tests 5) fix edge case for eviction while reallocating slack 6) performance tweaks (lock-free path for common case) 7) docs and release notes 8) address reviewers comments and CI fixes

Files changed (high level): - cluster/slack_allocator.go - gateway/burst_throttle_gate.go - autoscaler/hints.go - telemetry/metrics.go - docs/dedicated/cluster-slack.md - tests/allocator_invariants_test.go - tests/integration_burst_replay_test.go - internal/config/defaults.yaml - internal/config/schema_v2.go - build/ci/flake-retry.sh - go.mod - go.sum

Behavioral notes (what this does at runtime): - CSA periodically samples per-pool utilization and computes a short-duration slack budget (usually 30-120s) using an exponential decay window. - Slack budgets are fractionally loaned to requesting pools with proportional fairness and a configurable max-burst-per-pool cap. - The BTG intercepts incoming requests tagged as bursty; it queries CSA for available budget and returns either PASS, DELAY (short throttle token issued), or REJECT. DELAY responses carry a short TTL token that the gateway can queue with a bounded wait to smooth spikes. - When CSA reclaims slack (e.g., utilization rises), it emits a voluntary revoke signal; the BTG converts revoke events into early DELAY/REJECT decisions and logs diagnostic traces for tracing. - The autoscaler receives hints (not hard commits) to opportunistically warm GPUs; hints are advisory and respect reservation accounting by default.

Performance and safety: - Added fast-path in allocator that avoids locks for common accept flow; benchmarks show ~1.8x throughput for gate decision path compared to previous best-effort admission. - Fail-open semantics: if CSA becomes unavailable, BTG falls back to conservative static burst caps to preserve safety. - All config knobs default to conservative values to avoid changing behavior for existing fleets unless explicitly enabled.

Review discussion (condensed): Reviewer: Jun Park: "Allocator looks solid; concerns around race between reclaim and autoscaler hints—can we add a linearizable handoff?" Author: "Added a short-lived lease token and extended tests to simulate concurrent reclaim; lease avoids double-counting and is documented in config." Reviewer: Marcus Li: "Metrics look useful but could be high-cardinality. Limit per-pool labels to pool-id truncated to 8 chars." Author: "Truncated tags and added a sampled dimension for high-cardinality pools; updated telemetry/metrics.go." Reviewer: Olivia Chen: "We need a canary plan. Add incremental rollout steps and a rollback knob." Author: "Canary plan added to docs and release_notes field; added runtime flag 'csa.enable' for swift rollback."

CI summary: - Initial CI run failed (race detected in allocator unit tests under -race); I fixed the race by switching a condition to atomic and re-ran. - Integration perf job showed small memory spike which was mitigated by a pool object reuse change. - Final CI: all checks pass (unit, integration, lint, gosec).

Testing / validation: - Unit tests cover allocator invariants (no double-allocation, fairness under contention). - Integration replay runs on perf-lab dataset: 1M requests replayed across 120s bursts, showing 23% fewer 95th percentile latency spikes and 12% improved throughput under the same reserved capacity vs baseline. - Canary rollout plan: 5% of traffic in canary pool -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with metric thresholds and automatic rollback on tail-latency regressions.

Related work: Compared to reservoir-based designs, CSA focuses on short-duration slack loans with stronger fairness and ingress-level gating to avoid queue amplification. It complements existing warm-pool and credit-based systems rather than replacing them.

Release notes: - feature: cluster slack allocator and burst throttle gate to improve burst handling and reduce latency tail on dedicated fleets. - telemetry: new metrics slack_utilization and burst_gate_decisions. - config: csa.max_burst_per_pool, csa.window_seconds, csa.enable (default false).

Merge outcome: squash-and-merge after approvals. Changelog entry created and included in release candidate for dedicated platform v1.9.

Operational runbook (summary): - If observed "csa-unavailable" events, set csa.enable=false and watch gateway throttle rate; follow rollback instructions in docs/dedicated/cluster-slack.md. - To tune: adjust csa.window_seconds (shorter = more nimble, longer = more stable) and csa.max_burst_per_pool (cap per-tenant).

Introduce cluster slack allocator (CSA) and a gateway burst throttle gate (BTG). Improves burst handling for dedicated fleets, adds telemetry metrics slack_utilization and burst_gate_decisions. Defaults disabled; enable via csa.enable=true and tune window_seconds and max_burst_per_pool.
payload.title: introduce-cluster-slack-allocator-and-burst-throttle-gate

Context: Customers operating under strict regulatory regimes asked for two improvements after a recent post-mortem: (1) automated, opinionated guidance for oncall and SRE when KMS-related failures or residency warnings appear; (2) reduce missed audit signals during transient KMS failures while limiting storage costs. This PR delivers an operational 'policy compliance playbook' plus two runtime components: a KMS circuit-breaker and a differential audit sampler. Motivation: reduce incident toil and audit gaps while preserving data residency guarantees and minimizing spike in audit storage. Implementation summary: - Playbook: docs/compliance/playbooks/kms-residency-playbook.md with runbooks, escalation matrix, and example Linear templates for Paging and Postmortem. The playbook is vendor-agnostic and includes step-by-step commands for Dedicated and Private installs. - KMS circuit-breaker: runtime/kms/circuit_breaker.go adds a health-score based breaker that consumes KMS latency/error metrics and enforces per-tenant affinity windows. When the score crosses thresholds, requests are routed to configured fallback providers or to an offline-mode that returns explicit 5xx with an audit tag indicating redaction-required. Circuit-breaker supports operator-configured cooldown and jitter and exposes metrics: redwood_kms_breaker_state, redwood_kms_failover_rate, redwood_kms_last_signalled. - Differential audit sampler: observability/audit/sampler.go implements policy-based sampling where tenants marked as high-risk (by policy) get 100% audit capture during anomaly windows; low-risk tenants are sampled at a lower baseline. The sampler supports retrospective backfill: when an event is redacted due to KMS failure, a lightweight proof entry is retained and a backfill job (tools/audit/backfill_runner.py) attempts to reconcile once KMS returns. - RBACv2 policy templates: config/rbacv2/templates/compliance_templates.rego contains OPA snippets for enforcement points used by the sampler and breaker (e.g., allow_kms_failover_for_operator). - Tests and infra: Added unit tests for the breaker logic, integration test that simulates KMS latency spikes with a fake provider in perf-canary harness, and terraform changes to expose new alerts and SLOs in observability-pack. Checklist: - [x] Playbook drafted and reviewed by Security and SRE - [x] Breaker implemented with unit tests - [x] Sampler implemented and wired into audit pipeline - [x] Integration perf-canary scenario created - [x] Docs added and referenced in console runbook - [x] Linear tasks and alerts created (ENG-2145) Commits (top-level summaries): ["playbook: add initial kms residency and compliance playbook","runtime(kms): implement circuit-breaker with health scoring","observability: add metrics and dashboards for kms breaker","audit: implement differential sampler and backfill proof entries","rbacv2: add OPA templates for failover and sampler decisions","tests: add unit + perf-canary integration tests","infra: expose breaker alerts and create PagerDuty escalation policy","docs: link playbook from onboarding guide"] Changed files (high-level): ["docs/compliance/playbooks/kms-residency-playbook.md","runtime/kms/circuit_breaker.go","runtime/kms/circuit_breaker_test.go","observability/metrics/dashboards/kms-breaker.json","observability/audit/sampler.go","tools/audit/backfill_runner.py","config/rbacv2/templates/compliance_templates.rego","perf-canary/scenarios/kms-failure-spike.yaml","terraform/observability/alerts/kms_breaker.tf","console/runbooks/kms-failover.md"] Review conversation (high-level entries): ["Ibrahim Khan: Can the breaker be tenant-scoped so a noisy tenant doesn't impact others? Response: yes, breaker uses per-tenant windows and a global fallback flag; implementation note added.","Sofie Alvarez: Please ensure the backfill proof entries are safe to store without leaking PII — suggested a redact-only hash form. Response: sampler retains only a CRC+timestamp+policy-id; code updated to avoid message bodies in proofs.","Rachel O'Neill: Add an integration test that simulates provider rotation during an ongoing flow. Response: Added perf-canary scenario and CI run step.","Security review (J. Patel): Approve after small rego policy change to deny automatic failover for tenants with strict data-residency attribute. Response: Updated compliance_templates.rego to include residency-allowlist check.","SRE review: Request to expose breaker state on the /healthz endpoint for easier runbook checks. Response: Exported breaker state and added a cached health endpoint with 1s TTL."] CI summary: "All CI checks passed on merge: unit tests (go, python) passed, linter fixed, perf-canary integration scenario ran in the CI cluster and flagged minor timing flakiness that was addressed by adding retry backoff. E2E job completed against an internal staging env with a fake KMS provider. No policy violations found by the rbac linter." Risk and mitigation: "Risk: Improper failover could violate residency constraints. Mitigation: RBACv2/OPA denylist prevents failover for tenants with residency constraints; PR contains an emergency kill-switch boolean operator flag and automated audits that alert on any route-to-fallback events. Risk: audit storage blowup. Mitigation: differential sampling caps baseline sampling for low-risk tenants and only escalates during anomaly windows; backfill proof entries are compact and do not contain full payloads." Deployment plan: "Staged rollout: enable breaker in shadow mode for 72h (metrics only), then enable per-tenant targeted rollouts behind a feature flag environment variable, then global opt-in after 2 week observation. Playbook linked for oncall. Merge method: squash and merge. Merged by: Sohail Mehta on 2026-02-03." Additional notes: "This PR intentionally keeps the playbook vendor neutral and includes explicit command snippets for both Dedicated and Private installer workflows. Follow-on work: metrics-driven auto-tuning of breaker thresholds (ENG-2201).

Motivation: aggressive quant/batch defaults can produce cost wins but sometimes cause regressions for tail-latency or prompt-sensitive workloads. This PR introduces a conservative "shelving" concept (shelf profiles) plus warmstart/warmup templates and a minimal unit-economics metric export so ops can safely adopt cost presets with observability. Summary of changes: 1) new shelf profile schema (conservative, balanced, aggressive) with explicit gating flags to opt-in to quantization/compact kernels; 2) warmstart templates that run a short sequence of safe-prefill steps when a model shard is cold, reducing cold-start token overhead and smoothing SLO regressions; 3) unit-econ export under /metrics/econ with per-route per-model cost breakdown (tokens, GPU-time-ms, cache-hit-rate); 4) CLI: rw-econ apply-shelf and rw-econ simulate to preview econ impact; 5) docs and migration guide. Checklist: - [x] Add shelf schema and runtime enforcement - [x] Implement warmstart templates and scheduler hook - [x] Expose unit-econ metrics and Prometheus labels - [x] Provide CLI simulation and YAML examples - [x] Add docs + upgrade notes - [x] E2E smoke tests in canary cluster Release impact: non-breaking default; conservative profile is the default to avoid regression risk. Ops can opt into balanced/aggressive profiles per-route or per-tenant. Related: ENG-7843 for shelf design, ENG-8019 for unit-econ metric format. Testing: local unit tests (econ package), e2e smoke run on canary, synthetic load profiles showing 8-12% token cost reduction on balanced and 18-24% on aggressive for batch-friendly workloads while conservative preserves baseline latency. Rollout plan: merge to main, enable conservative shelf by default in Hosted canary for 72h, collect econ metrics, then ramp clients and expose profile chooser in Console. Risks and mitigations: aggressive profile can degrade tail-latency on small prompts; mitigated by conservative default, automatic fallback when cache-hit-rate < 0.3, and rollback via per-route policy. Follow-ups: telemetry to detect if warmstart runs are failing; automated Linear tasks to track customer opt-ins.
Marcus Li: Looks good overall, but please add a short-circuit to the warmstart path when KV cache warming is disabled by tenant policy.
Author response (Elena): Added short-circuit in shelf_validator.go and unit tests to cover the disabled-cache case.
Priya Raman: CI flaked on the canary e2e run — please split the long-running canary into a separate e2e job or mark as flaky for main CI.
Author response (Elena): Split canary job into e2e_canary in our GitHub Actions matrix and marked it optional; main CI now runs fast smoke. See .github/workflows/e2e.yml change.
Dmitri Volkov: Suggest adding a Prometheus label econ_profile to make dashboarding easier.
Author response (Elena): Added econ_profile and route_id labels to exporter and dashboard example in docs.
Add conservative shelf profiles and warmstart templates; introduce unit-econ metrics at /metrics/econ; new rw-econ CLI to simulate and apply shelf profiles. Conservative profile is the default to avoid latency regressions.

Context: we see production flaps where clients concurrently reconnect en masse (region failovers, mobile flurries) causing thundering reconnect bursts that manifest as transient toolcall duplication, frequent session eviction, and tail latency spikes. Motivation: reduce client reconnection storms, avoid accidental duplicate tool invocations when clients reconnect and retry, and allow short client-side pauses (mobile backgrounding) without immediate session eviction. This PR introduces three coordinated mechanisms: 1) reconnect splay: the server returns a randomized reconnect-backoff-splay window in the reconnect-accept payload and the client SDK is instructed to apply jitter prior to reconnect attempts; server-side admission respects splay windows to evenly smooth reconnect bursts across backends; 2) per-session idle-extension: sessions now carry an idle-extension token with a default grace window (configurable per-customer) that can be dynamically extended by authenticated heartbeats from the client or SDK during short backgrounding; server TTL eviction checks consider the extension token so short pauses do not force replays; 3) speculative toolcall guard: when a reconnecting client indicates it is resuming an in-flight streaming session, the server marks recent toolcall intents as speculative and routes tool calls through an idempotency fence which requires a client-sent resume-proof to commit a speculative toolcall. Without a proof the speculative call is rolled back or retried safely. Implementation summary: - Protocol: updated resume handshake includes splay_window_ms and optional resume_proof header; client SDKs get backward-compatible behavior (old clients default to 0ms splay and no resume_proof, speculative guard is conservative). - Server: admission controller implements splay smoothing across replicas, session store tracks idle_extension_until and speculative_toolcall table with commit/abort state and short retention. - Tooling: new tracing spans and metrics (stream.reconnect.splay.ms, stream.session.idle_extension.count, stream.toolcall.speculative.*) and dashboards updated. - Backwards compatibility: safe defaults ensure no regression for older clients. - Testing: end-to-end system tests simulate mass reconnects, unit tests for idempotency fence, fuzz tests for resume_proof mismatches. Rollout plan: staged feature-flagged rollout to 10% customers for 48h with observability alerts on increased speculative-toolcall abort rates, then 50% for 72h before global enable. Linear tasks referenced in linked_linear. This PR also includes VS code SDK hints and notes for SDK teams to update resume behavior.
Liam O'Connor: Please clarify how splay interacts with client-side exponential backoff; suggestion to cap server-specified splay to 5s to avoid long user-visible delays.
Maya Patel: Added splay cap configuration and updated docs to recommend SDK backoff integration; servers still honor client-configured max when present.
Priya Rao: Concern about speculative toolcall retention size under heavy reconnects; request for GC window and metrics to monitor abort ratios.
Maya Patel: Added retention GC and metrics (stream.toolcall.speculative.retention_ms) and throttle path for speculative table growth; updated tests.
Diego Martinez: Verified OpenAI-compat resume header semantics; asked for compatibility note in the SDK changelog.
Maya Patel: Added changelog entry and compatibility test; CI green locally.
- Add server-issued reconnect splay window to smooth client reconnect storms.- Add per-session idle-extension token to avoid eviction during short client backgrounding.- Add speculative toolcall guard with resume-proof-based commit to avoid duplicate tool invocations on reconnect.- Metrics and dashboards for reconnect splay and speculative toolcall flows.
Simulated a 10k-client reconnect spike with/without splay: with splay, peak admission rate reduced 78% and speculative-toolcall aborts dropped 92%. Fuzzed resume_proof mismatch cases to ensure no accidental toolcall commit. Performed load test with passive heartbeat extensions to validate GC behavior.
payload.title: Reconnect splay, per-session idle-extension, and speculative toolcall guard for streaming

Motivation: Customers operating across multiple jurisdictions occasionally surface ambiguous region claims from upstream services (missing/contradictory region headers or stale residency assertions). These cases increase compliance risk and complicate KMS routing and audit retention. This PR introduces a lightweight control plane component (Residency Quarantine Gatekeeper) plus RBACv2 delegation telemetry hooks that together: 1) automatically quarantine requests with conflicting or absent residency assertions, 2) emit high-fidelity delegation telemetry to help SRE/security triage suspicious operator flows, and 3) annotate KMS proxy calls with immutable locality context to improve auditability without changing key material.

Summary of changes: Adds gatekeeper and feature-flagged rollout path, RBACv2 instrumentation (delegation telemetry), and audit-sampling profiles that increase retention for quarantined flows. Also includes a small operator-honeypot detector used only for telemetry and alerting (no automated revocations). All behavior is behind the new feature flag security.residency_quarantine.

Design notes: The gatekeeper runs as a policy middleware in the API ingress path. It evaluates (in order) explicit region claims, tenant pinned-region metadata, and operator-delegation traces. If evaluation yields ambiguity or contradictions, the gatekeeper either: (a) mark request as QUARANTINED and forward to normal processing while tagging audit metadata and increasing sample rate, or (b) short-circuit and return 409 with an explanatory header when the tenant policy requires strict enforcement. The KMS proxy accepts an additional signed-locality header (populated by gatekeeper) for richer provenance but does not change key selection logic. Delegation telemetry emits a compact tuple (operator_id, delegate_chain_hash, policy_path, decision_timestamp) to the secured telemetry stream for SRE review.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests for gatekeeper policy evaluation
- [x] End-to-end tests for quarantine + audit sampling bump
- [x] Load test of added middleware at p99 path
- [x] Security review and threat model notes attached
- [x] Feature flag gating + rollout playbook included

Commits (high-level):
- add: pkg/gatekeeper/residency_quarantine.go (core policy evaluation + feature flag checks)
- add: services/kms/locality_proxy.go (signed-locality header handling + passthrough)
- feat: pkg/rbacv2/delegation_telemetry.go (emit delegation tuples to telemetry pipeline)
- perf: audit/sampler.go (add dynamic sampling rules for quarantined flows)
- docs: docs/compliance/residency_quarantine.md (runbook + rollout steps)
- test: e2e/quarantine_flow_test.go and unit tests + fixtures

Files changed (illustrative):
- pkg/gatekeeper/residency_quarantine.go
- services/kms/locality_proxy.go
- pkg/rbacv2/delegation_telemetry.go
- pkg/audit/sampler.go
- docs/compliance/residency_quarantine.md
- deploy/helm/templates/quarantine-rbac.yaml
- e2e/quarantine_flow_test.go

Small snippet (policy evaluation logic, illustrative):
if regionHeader == "" && tenantPinned == "" {
  // Ambiguous — mark for quarantine and increase audit sample
  ctx.Metadata.Put("residency.status", "QUARANTINED")
  audit.SampleRate.Bump(ctx.RequestID, 100)
}

Rollout plan: feature flag default=off. Staged rollout to: dev -> staging (10%) -> prod (shadow mode) -> prod (enforce 1%) -> prod (enforce broader) per playbook in docs/compliance/residency_quarantine.md. If any false positive spike in errors >3% QoS, rollback to shadow mode and revert sampling change only.

Testing: Added unit tests covering 8 evaluation permutations, e2e tests simulating tenant pinned-region mismatch, and a small load harness that validated additional middleware adds <0.8ms median and <2% p99 tail at 500 RPS.

Security and compliance considerations: The gatekeeper adds no new key material and does not persist sensitive payloads. Delegation telemetry is PII-minimized (operator_id is hashed at source, full operator lookup only available to authorized analysts). KMS locality header is signed with service signing keys and validated by the proxy; signature proof is included in audit logs. Threat model reviewed by security (SEC-710) and notes attached in Linear.

Backwards compatibility: No customer-visible API changes except optional 409 responses for tenants that opt into strict quarantine in their policy. All other behavior is additive and behind a flag.

Related work: Complements ENG-2145 (operator delegation audit) and SUP-4321 (support ticket: ambiguous region claims causing KMS misrouting).

Merge: squash and merge.

Anya Chen: Please add a unit test that covers operator-honeypot detection edge case where delegate_chain is empty (done in latest commit).
Liam O'Connor: Can we ensure the signed-locality header is validated against the service signing key and reject if signature timestamp older than 5m? Addressed and added validation; updated tests.
Sofia Ramos: Confirm audit retention bump is configurable per-tenant — replied: retention is per-tenant via policy and defaults to 30d/90d for quarantined flows (added documentation).
Security: threat model reviewed and approved (SEC-710).
Add Residency Quarantine Gatekeeper (feature-flagged), RBACv2 delegation telemetry, KMS locality header proxy, and increased audit sampling for quarantined flows. Rollout via staged feature flag. No breaking changes by default.
Playbook and rollback steps in docs/compliance/residency_quarantine.md. Default behavior is off; safe shadow mode recommended for 48h in production before any enforcement. Monitor metrics: quarantine.rate, quarantine.fp_rate, delegation.telemetry.event_rate, kms.proxy.signature_rejects.

Context and motivation: Production teams have observed long-tail token-path instability where a small fraction of requests deviate mid-invocation (e.g., branch into a different decoding path or trigger a late fallback) causing disproportionate cost and latency outliers. Existing token-cost and latency breakdowns capture endpoints but do not attribute path continuity or the exact point of divergence. This PR introduces a continuity metric (per-invocation and per-token) and a late-bound log-fork visualizer that makes path divergence explicit in traces and dashboards.

What this changes (high level): Implements continuity score computation in telemetry, annotates trace spans with "fork-edge" tags, surfaces a continuity visualizer dashboard that highlights where invocations diverge, and adds a tuned alert rule for "continuity degradation" that suppresses noise for low-volume tenants. Also includes a small SDK surface to expose continuity scores for downstream features (e.g., cohorting, sampling).

Checklist: - [x] Collector and reader implementation (collector.py / reader.go) - [x] Trace annotation and span-edge tagging (log_forker.go) - [x] Continuity visualizer dashboard (dashboards/continuity-visualizer.json) - [x] Alert rule with tenant-volume gating (alerts/continuity-degradation-rule.yml) - [x] Unit tests and replay example (tests/..., examples/...) - [x] Docs and rollout playbook (docs/observability/continuity.md)

Commits summary: 5 commits — prototype, scoring, trace wiring, dashboard + alerts, tests/docs. Key implementation notes: - Continuity score is computed as the normalized "path stability" over a sliding 5-minute window; score components are phase-switch penalty, token-drop penalty, and KV-cache miss multiplier. - To avoid hot-path overhead we added a small LRU for span-edge indices and a feature flag to enable full-edge sampling only for canary tenants. - The log-fork visualizer is implemented as a companion panel to the invocation timeline allowing interactive expansion of forked edges.

Files touched (high level): telemetry/collector + reader (collection, scoring), platform/tracing (span annotation), dashboards (visualizer), alerts (SLO + suppression rule), SDK (continuity API helper), docs/tests/examples.

Review and iteration: Reviewers requested cache to avoid extra lookups (addressed via LRU in reader.go), tooltip and docs for the visualizer (added explanatory panel and docs), and alert damping for low-volume tenants (added tenant-volume gating and changed default threshold to conservative value). CI: initial run had one flaky telemetry test; flake retried automatically per ci/flake_retries.yml and subsequent run passed.

Testing and rollout plan: - Unit tests and synthetic replay (examples/observability/continuity-replay.yaml) included; replay validated continuity score behavior across controlled forks. - Feature flag gated rollout: start with internal canary tenants (10% traffic) for 48 hours, then expand to 50% while monitoring continuity SLO and alert hits. - After 2 weeks of stable signal, enable full-sampling for tiered customers.

Impact and rationale: Provides a missing attribution axis for long-tail cost/latency — rather than just blaming model latency, teams can see when and where invocations fork and quantify the per-token continuity penalty. This enables targeted mitigations (prompt shape changes, caching prefetch) and reduces alert fatigue by correlating divergence to per-invocation causes.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main (merge commit a1b2c3d4). Post-merge actions: monitor continuity SLO dashboards (dashboards/continuity-visualizer) and report early regressions to ENG-2145.
Diego Alvarez: Nice approach — can we avoid an extra lookup in high QPS paths? Suggest caching span-edge indices for 30s.
Priya Nair (author): Added an LRU cache layer in reader.go and a feature flag to roll out. See reader.go#LRU_CACHE commit.
Marina Kovalev: Dashboard is helpful, but the log-fork visualizer needs a tooltip explaining continuity score components.
Priya Nair: Added explanatory panel and short doc in docs/observability/continuity.md per Marina's suggestion.
Samir Patel: Alert threshold looks aggressive in staging; can we add a 5x quiet window for low-volume tenants?
Priya Nair: Added a tenant-volume condition to the alert rule and moved the default to a conservative threshold; will monitor for two weeks.
CI: unit tests flaky (telemetry) on first run — retried and passed on second run; recorded in CI logs.
payload.title: Introduce continuity metrics and late-bound log-fork visualizer for token-path decomposition

Motivation: customers building deterministic, schema-driven pipelines reported incompatibilities when using the new Responses v2 variants through our OpenAI-compat adapter: structured_output schemas were being flattened in the proxy, and tool/function call handshakes sometimes lost the deterministic seed and metadata headers during streaming reassembly. This PR ensures structured_output schemas are preserved end-to-end and introduces an explicit tool-handshake binding so tool calls keep deterministic flags and metadata passthrough throughout streaming. Summary of changes and checklist: - Add schema-preserve pass in the OpenAI adapter to map Responses.v2 structured_output -> internal structured token framing without losing field-level annotations. - Implement an idempotent tool-handshake binding between the adapter and runtime so tool/function calls are associated with the same request seed and metadata across retries and reconnects. - Improve streaming frame reassembly to tolerate partial toolcall frames and avoid dropping trailing annotations (fixes regression where last frame lost rng/determinism hints). - Add deterministic-seed propagation in transport headers and ensure the seed is embedded in the framing for replay and offline eval. - Add e2e smoke tests and integration fixtures for tool-binding across reconnects, and a deterministic-seed test harness for CI. - Update Python SDK client behavior to forward structured_output schema and deterministic options when using the OpenAI compat layer. - Documentation: compatibility notes and migration steps (docs/compat/responses-v2.md). Checklist: [x] unit tests updated [x] integration tests added [x] e2e smoke runs green [x] changelog entry [x] rollout plan included Rollout plan: staged rollout behind a feature flag (resp_v2_schema_preserve). Start with internal canary, then gated beta for customers with explicit toggles, fallback to strict-openai-compat if issues observed. Backwards compatibility: adapter defaults are no-op until the feature flag is set. This change preserves OpenAI-contracted behavior unless the customer opts-in to the new schema-preserve mode. Breaking change: none expected; feature gate ensures safe rollout. CI: small flakiness observed in e2e tool-binding test on first run; re-ran with increased timeouts and it stabilized. See CI summary below. Detailed commit summary, files changed and review notes are included as separate fields in this PR JSON for traceability.
Initial review by Priya: requested a clear invariant test for seed propagation across reconnects; flagged potential perf impact in adapter pass. Author response: added targeted unit test and micro-bench for the adapter pass; optimized annotation map to be allocation-light. Liam requested doc examples showing SDK call patterns to opt into the feature flag; added examples to docs/compat/responses-v2.md. Diego found a race in the handshake path under high concurrency; fixed by moving handshake state into the runtime-side request context and added a concurrency test. After fixes, reviewers approved. Approvals: Priya (approved), Liam (approved), Diego (approved).
Unit tests: adapter mapping (+), framer (+), handshake idempotency (+). Integration: tool-binding reconnect scenarios (stable after timeout increase). E2E: deterministic-seed smoke tests run in CI canary with feature flag on; first run flaky, second run passed. Load tests: micro-bench shows <3% overhead when schema_preserve pass is enabled for typical short-chat workloads.
For customers using OpenAI-compat and Responses v2: - To opt-in, set 'resp_v2_schema_preserve=true' at the route config or runtime feature flags. - SDKs (Python) will forward structured_output and deterministic options automatically when feature is enabled. - If your tooling depends on legacy flattened fields, do not enable until you confirm downstream consumers accept the structured format. - For tool integrations, ensure your tool handshake satisfies the new idempotency semantics (stateless resume supported).
Feature flag will be initially enabled only for internal canary cluster and a small beta cohort. Monitor telemetry: schema-preserve failure rate, handshake retry counts, stream-reassembly error rate. If regressions observed, flip feature flag to disable and roll back the compat pass. Update SDKs with explicit opt-in examples in next patch release.
Preserve structured_output schemas through the OpenAI-compat adapter and introduce an idempotent tool-handshake binding that keeps deterministic seeds and metadata intact during streaming and reconnects. Rollout behind feature flag 'resp_v2_schema_preserve'.
This PR intentionally keeps the adapter change behind a feature flag to reduce blast radius. The design preserves compatibility with existing OpenAI-contracted flows unless explicitly enabled.

Motivation: We currently only expose coarse KV cache metrics (hit/miss) which makes it hard to diagnose sustained evictions and cache thrash that drive token tail latency and increased per-token cost. This PR introduces a compact set of time-series and dashboard panels that show KV cache occupancy trends, eviction/insert rates, per-tenant occupancy ratio, and a cross-correlation panel between occupancy spikes and token-latency tails.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds runtime metrics emitted by the serving runtime: kv_cache_total_slots, kv_cache_occupied_slots, kv_cache_evictions, kv_cache_inserts, kv_cache_partitioned_occupancy{tenant,shard}. Metrics are exposed with labels to support rollups without increasing cardinality.
- Introduces a lightweight occupancy estimator in the runtime that updates at low frequency (default 10s) to avoid polling overhead. Estimator is opt-in behind a feature flag and off by default for private installs.
- Adds a new observability dashboard (dashboards/kv_occupancy_trends.json) with occupancy sparkline, eviction heatmap, tenant-occupancy percentiles, and a correlation scatter between occupancy and 95p token latency.
- Implements alert tuning: new SLO-friendly alert rule observability/alerts/kv_occupancy_slo.yaml fires only when sustained occupancy > 85% for 5m and eviction rate > 0.5/sec averaged across 1m. Alerts include suggested remediation links and on-call runbook reference.
- Adds context-aware log redaction: a small logging filter (observability/logging/context_redactor.py) that redact PII from prompt/context but preserves a compact token fingerprint and sampling context necessary for post-mortem (sample id, token-cost-bucket, shard). Redaction preserves observability while addressing privacy compliance.
- Adds docs and runbook notes for ops and privacy teams (docs/observability/kv-occupancy.md).

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- To avoid high cardinality we aggregate occupancy per partition/shard and expose percentiles rather than per-invocation labels. The occupancy estimator updates infrequently to minimize CPU overhead on hot paths.
- Context-aware redaction keeps a deterministic token fingerprint (sha256 truncated) plus a sampling_id so that developers can join traces without seeing raw prompt text. The default is conservative (redact-on) for hosted; private installs can enable or disable via feature flag.
- The alert thresholds were calibrated from historical traces (see ENG-4021) and include a rate condition (evictions/sec) to reduce noisy alerts from short bursts.

How to enable / rollout:
- Feature flag: obs.kv_occupancy.enabled = false (default). Ops can flip to true in staging and run the dashboard.
- The occupancy estimator has config knobs: poll_interval_seconds (default 10), min_sample_traffic (default 100 invocations/min).
- Context redaction is behind obs.redaction.mode with values [off, conservative, permissive]. Hosted default = conservative.

Security & privacy review: SEC-118 reviewed the redactor logic and recommended deterministic fingerprinting + single-hop salt per-tenant. We added an integration test that verifies redacted logs contain no raw prompt substrings for a set of training PII patterns.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for estimator logic and redactor (telemetry/unit/*).
- Integration run against synthetic workload (bench/perf/kv-occupancy-replay) with comparison dashboards in the PR.
- Load impact measured: ~0.6% CPU on a 16-vCPU serving node when enabled at 10s poll interval.

Rollout plan: stage -> canary (10% of traffic) -> all. Alerts initially set to P0-monitor only (no paging) for 48h, then escalated if stable.

Links: Linear ENG-4021, SEC-118, runbook reference: runbooks/kv-cache-thrash.md

Checklist: - [x] Metrics implemented and registered - [x] Dashboard panels added - [x] Alerts tuned with hysteresis - [x] Privacy review and tests - [x] Docs updated
Jonas Lee: Nice instrumentation. Can we ensure the occupancy metric scales for multi-tenant aggregation? Suggest exposing a per-partition_percentile label instead of per-tenant when traffic is small.
Aisha Verma: Good point — switched to partition-level percentiles and added tenant_ratio metric. Updated docs to show aggregation examples.
Marta Ruiz: Security review: confirm that redaction removes known PII and that fingerprints are irreversible. Also request an integration test demonstrating redacted output for sample inputs.
Aisha Verma: SEC-118 provided review and we added deterministic truncation + tenant salt. Integration test added at telemetry/unit/test_redactor.py. Details in PR comment.
Samir Patel: Performance concern: what is the CPU impact at 5s poll interval? We should default to 10s. Also add guard so estimator skips when traffic < min_sample_traffic.
Aisha Verma: Added config guards and adjusted default poll_interval_seconds to 10s. Bench results added to PR description.
CI bot: lint failed on context_redactor.py (line length). Author fixed and pushed. Rerun CI: all checks passed.
Marta Ruiz: Approval: looks good from security side.
Jonas Lee: Approved after minor doc tweaks.
Samir Patel: Approved (perf).

Context and motivation: Our presubmit and lint pipelines have accumulated ad-hoc bootstrapping steps which slow down fast feedback and make small dependency churns noisy in CI telemetry. This PR introduces a lightweight CI sequencer component that consolidates lightweight preflight steps into a deterministically-ordered, cache-friendly execution path and a dependency-signal cleaner that suppresses spurious dep-change alerts (e.g., lockfile timestamp churn, auto-formatter tool bumps) while preserving signals for real upgrades.

What this PR does (single-line summary): Adds ci/sequencer.py (small orchestrator), refactors existing ci/bootstrap.* into ordered stages, and introduces tools/dep_signal_cleaner.py plus small lint/test wiring.

Design notes: The sequencer is intentionally minimal: it does not replace heavy presubmit orchestration, only the light-weight fastpath for quick feedback. It runs three stages: env-prepare (cache warm), quick-lint (fast linters + formatting check), and smoke (unit tests subset). Each stage reports structured exit codes for downstream telemetry. The dependency-signal cleaner is a post-commit hook run in CI that normalizes dependency metadata and emits a delta-summary; when the delta matches configured heuristics (timestamp-only or checksum-stable), it suppresses noisy alerts.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add sequencer implementation and minimal integration tests
- [x] Wire sequencer into lightweight CI lane (GH Actions composite)
- [x] Add dep-signal cleaner and heuristic rules
- [x] Update team CI docs with usage and opt-outs
- [x] Run small-scale dogfood on infra/canary and iterate

Commits (high-level): 
- 7e1a9b: initial sequencer skeleton and runner shim
- 4a2f3c: integrate sequencer into .github/workflows/fastpath.yml as a composite action call
- a9d44e: add dep_signal_cleaner utility and heuristics ruleset
- c12f80: add unit tests and small fixture lockfiles for cleaner testing
- d88b21: docs and examples, update team playbook

Changed files (high-level, illustrative): 
- ci/sequencer.py (new) - core orchestrator for fastpath lanes
- ci/steps/prepare_env.sh (moved/trimmed) - smaller, cache-friendly variant
- ci/steps/quick_lint.sh (new wrapper) - fast linters only
- tools/dep_signal_cleaner.py (new) - normalizes lockfile metadata and emits summary
- .github/workflows/fastpath.yml (updated) - invokes sequencer as composite action for fast feedback
- docs/ci/fastpath.md (updated) - usage and opt-out guidance
- tests/ci/test_sequencer.py (new) - unit tests for sequencing logic
- tests/tools/test_dep_cleaner.py (new) - fixture-driven tests for cleaner heuristics
- package.json / go.mod (small devdeps bumps) - pin a stable composite action helper

Review conversation (high-level snippets): 
- Ethan Morales (reviewer): "Overall looks clean. Two asks: make the sequencer idempotent across retries and add a short-circuit when cache hits make stages unnecessary."
- Nina (author): "Addressed: added retry-idempotency token and cache-hit short-circuit. See sequencer.py lines 78-108."
- Sofia Ivanov: "Dep cleaner heuristics look reasonable but add an allowlist for known formatter bumps (we see these every few weeks). Also please add a note on opt-out for repos that vendor lockfiles."
- Nina: "Added allowlist config and opt-out flag; documented in docs/ci/fastpath.md."
- Liam Chen: "CI job matrix logs look fine. One minor nit: prefer exit code 2 for suppressed-noise vs exit code 0 for success."
- Nina: "Switched suppressed-noise to exit code 2 and updated telemetry mapping."

CI summary during review: 
- Actions: fastpath.yml (composite call) -> lint (fast), unit-smoke, dep-cleaner-check
- Initial run: lint passed, unit-smoke flaky (1 failure) -> fixed by adding a small test fixture; rerun passed
- Integration run on infra/canary: green, overall run time for fastpath reduced from ~95s to ~75s on average (measured over 50 runs).

Risk and mitigations: 
- Risk: Dep-signal suppression could hide real upgrades. Mitigation: default heuristics are conservative and we added an allowlist/denylist and a telemetry mismatch alert if the cleaner suppresses >5% of dep deltas in a day. Additionally, the opt-out flag is available per-repo.
- Risk: Sequencer composite introduces new failure modes in GH Actions. Mitigation: keep legacy fastpath as fallback; sequencer-run is gated behind a feature flag (repo-level) for the first week and can be toggled via org config.

Performance and telemetry: 
- Measured ~20% median reduction in fastpath end-to-end time on small change PRs where full integration tests were previously run unnecessarily.
- Telemetry hooks added to emit stage durations and suppression counts to the CI metrics pipeline (metric names: ci.sequencer.stage.duration, ci.dep_cleaner.suppressed_count).

Merge notes: 
- PR was squashed on merge. Final merge commit includes cleaned changelog and docs update. All reviewers approved. CI green on final run.

Follow-ups (short list): 
- ENG-10214: Add a small dashboard to visualize suppression trends per repo (tracked in linked_linear).
- ENG-9213: Explore moving heavier presubmit orchestration into a staged worker model if sequencer proves effective.

If you want to reproduce locally: see docs/ci/fastpath.md for running sequencer against local changes; tools/dep_signal_cleaner.py has a --dry-run mode that emits the delta without suppressing alerts.

Introduces a small CI sequencer that orders lightweight preflight steps deterministically and a dependency-signal cleaner that reduces noise from transient dep updates. No customer-facing changes. Improves CI feedback time for small PRs by ~20%.

Context: We have recurring incidents where short-lived multi-tenant microbursts cause transient latency spikes and unfair capacity drain. Previous fixes tightened global headroom but hurt utilization. This PR implements a two-part approach: 1) BurstTemperer, a decision layer that tempers burst grants based on observed burst distribution (p95/p99) and current cluster slack, and 2) Obligation Awarder, a lightweight tenant accounting service that records 'earned' reservation credits and applies a decaying obligation balance used by the Temperer to favor tenants that honored previous reservations. Goals: (a) limit dangerous instantaneous spike grants without rigid hard quotas, (b) reward tenants that consume responsibly over time, (c) provide telemetry to iterate policies. Design summary: - BurstTemperer sits between the admission/gateway and the lease allocator. It computes a soft grant = min(request, policy_headroom * adapt_factor), where adapt_factor is derived from recent burstiness and tenant obligation score. - Obligation Awarder increments a tenant's obligation credit when they return unused reservation capacity or maintain steady utilization; credits decay with half-life configured per org. Credits lower the penalty applied by BurstTemperer. - Both components expose metrics: temperer.grant_ratio, temperer.rejections, obligation.balance, obligation.decay_rate, plus per-tenant histograms. - Fallback: If the allocator rejects due to real capacity constraints, the system falls back to existing soft-failure path (queue or fallback model). Why different from existing 'reservation' work: instead of reallocating cold reservations or changing commit windows, this focuses on tempering transient grants and adding a long-lived accounting signal to guide future decisions. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-1432) - [x] Implementation of BurstTemperer logic + unit tests - [x] Obligation Awarder service + storage migration (lightweight kv) - [x] Telemetry dashboards + Grafana panels stub - [x] Integration tests with autoscaler sim harness - [x] Backward compatible config defaults and feature flagging Rollout plan: gated feature flag per cluster and tenant; start with canary in staging, then 10% clusters, then broad rollout after 2 weeks monitoring. Monitoring: new alerts on temperer.rejections > 0.5% and obligation.balance skew > 10x between top/bottom deciles. Limitations: initial heuristics tuned for our common web-chat workloads; heavy bursty batch workloads may need alternate profiles.
Introduces a new BurstTemperer autoscaler component that soft-limits short-term surge allocation and a tenant Obligation Awarder that tracks earned credits and decays them over time. Improves tail-latency stability under multi-tenant bursty workloads and exposes new telemetry for per-tenant obligation accounting.
Marcus Li: The adapt_factor calculation is clever, but we should guard against noise when tenant request rates are low — add a min-sample threshold to avoid overfitting.
Sofia Park: Added min-sample (configurable) and unit tests covering low-sample case (temperer_test.go:+8).
Priya Raman: Storage migration looks fine but make sure backfill script is limited by cluster id to avoid throttling metadata DB.
Sofia Park: Backfill now paginates and supports dry-run; script updated.
Diego Alvarez: Integration run showed a small increase in 99th latency for long-running heavy tenants — I suspect the decay half-life is too aggressive for those orgs.
Sofia Park: Tuned default half-life from 6h -> 24h and added per-org override; reran sim (results attached in CI).
Marcus Li: Please add an e2e smoke in canary to confirm no regressed admissions under steady load before enabling broadly.
Sofia Park: Added canary smoke job and added alert thresholds in docs.
Merged via squash on 2026-03-01 by Marcus Li. Merge commit includes: final tweak to half-life defaults, added canary smoke job, and updated rollout notes.
Feature gated; to enable: flip featureflag.autoscaler.burst_temperer=true and ensure obligations DB migration applied. Recommended rollout: staging -> 3 canary clusters for 48h -> 25% traffic -> 100% after no significant spikes. Watch metrics: temperer.grant_ratio, temperer.rejections, obligation.balance.dist. If rejections > 1% for >1h, rollout rollback recommended.
Monitor dashboards for 72h across canary clusters
Schedule Config/Release to increase tenant override flags if necessary
Plan outreach to top 10 tenants with high obligation skew
Follow-up PR: add tenant-config profiles (ENG-1448)
