Context
This PR adds multi-region availability metrics and SLO-friendly aggregations needed for the Regional Failover Automation Upgrade (ENG-2411) and Multi-region Availability SLO 2026 workstream.

Problem
We currently have good per-region availability/error metrics, but we lack:
- A canonical definition of “multi-region availability” for services behind smart routing (Hosted API + Dedicated)
- Low-cardinality, burn-rate friendly time series suitable for SLO evaluation and alerting
- Consistent dimensions to explain *why* multi-region availability was lost (routing policy, reachability, capacity gating, control plane)

What’s in this PR
- New emitted counters/histograms in the routing/gateway path to capture multi-region outcomes:
  - routed request outcome (served locally vs served via failover vs dropped/overload)
  - effective region (where the request was ultimately served)
  - requested region (original target)
- New recording rules producing SLO inputs at fixed label sets:
  - `redwood:multiregion:requests_total` (by product, tier, route_class)
  - `redwood:multiregion:errors_total` (5xx + selected gateway/timeout categories)
  - `redwood:multiregion:availability_ratio` (precomputed ratio for dashboards; SLOs should use numerator/denominator recording rules)
- Guardrails to keep label cardinality bounded:
  - route is grouped into `route_class` (chat|embeddings|rerank|other) rather than raw path
  - tenant_id is not included; we rely on tier + product (hosted|dedicated)
  - model is intentionally excluded from SLO series; model-level views remain available in separate non-SLO dashboards
- Inline guidance (comments) adjacent to the rules for dashboard authors:
  - which rules are safe for alerting
  - expected query windows for 1h/6h burn-rate alerts
  - common pitfalls (mixing effective vs requested region)

Not in this PR
- Burn-rate alert rules (landed separately in PR-19818)
- Dedicated drain progress metrics (separate PR)
- Any changes to failover decisioning logic (policy engine/controller PRs)

How to validate
- Deployed to staging: `staging-us-east` and `staging-eu-west`.
- Confirm recording rules evaluate cleanly (no "many-to-many" joins; no missing series) and remain low-cardinality.
- Smoke queries included below.

Smoke queries
- Multi-region denominator:
  sum(rate(redwood:multiregion:requests_total[5m])) by (product,tier,route_class)
- Multi-region numerator:
  sum(rate(redwood:multiregion:requests_total[5m])) by (product,tier,route_class)
  - sum(rate(redwood:multiregion:errors_total[5m])) by (product,tier,route_class)
- Breakdown served via failover:
  sum(rate(redwood_multiregion_routing_outcome_total{outcome="served_failover"}[5m])) by (product,tier,route_class,from_region,to_region)

Rollout plan
- Stage 1: ship metrics emission behind `obs.multiregion_slo_metrics_enabled` (default off)
- Stage 2: enable in staging + internal canary tenants
- Stage 3: enable in production for Hosted (tier=free + tier=pro), then Dedicated

Risk notes
- Primary risk is metric cardinality growth; this PR includes explicit aggregation + label restrictions and a small unit test to prevent adding disallowed labels to SLO series.
- Secondary risk is semantic mismatch with SLO definition; reviewers from SRE/SLO dashboards signed off on the numerator/denominator choices.

Checklist
- [x] Metrics emitted and documented
- [x] Recording rules added with stable label sets
- [x] Added unit test to prevent accidental high-cardinality labels in SLO series
- [x] Staging validation
- [x] Linked to ENG-2418

Refs
- ENG-2418 Add failover metrics and SLO burn alerts
- Regional Failover Automation Upgrade (ENG-2411)
- ADR-042 Failover trigger signal hierarchy (related; not required for this PR)
- Adds standardized multi-region availability metrics for Hosted API and Dedicated routing outcomes
- Adds recording rules to produce low-cardinality SLO inputs (burn-rate friendly)
- Documents recommended dashboard panels + query patterns in code comments
Aisha Bello requested a clearer separation between SLO inputs (low-cardinality, stable) and exploratory breakdowns; author updated naming to use `redwood:multiregion:*` for recording rules and left the detailed breakdown on raw emitted metrics only. Sergio Costa flagged that `requested_region` vs `effective_region` was easy to misuse in dashboards; author added an explicit comment block with examples and renamed one label from `region` -> `effective_region` for clarity. Miles Thornton asked how overload/drop is treated; author clarified in description and code comments that overload responses count against availability for the multi-region SLO (consistent with customer impact), and included a breakdown metric to distinguish 5xx vs overload/timeouts. Ravi Menon noted a potential cardinality spike from `from_region,to_region` combinations; author limited those labels to the raw outcome counter and kept the SLO recording rules aggregated by product/tier/route_class only. Final approvals after staging validation screenshots were posted in the PR thread.
payload.title: Add multi-region availability metrics + SLO-friendly aggregations

payload.body:
Context and motivation:
We see two recurring pain points in production: (1) long-context generation workloads suffer from high memory pressure and degraded throughput due to monolithic KV cache handling, and (2) mixed small/large request workloads cause suboptimal batching decisions that harm latency-sensitive routes. This PR introduces a combined runtime change targeted at those two areas: a fused, chunked attention kernel ("weave-attn") that processes attention in contiguous chunks to improve memory locality and vectorization, plus a windowed KV caching layer that shards and trims KV state by logical token windows, and a continuous-batcher micro-scheduler that keeps the GPU feeding while preserving latency SLOs for small requests.

Design summary (high level):
- Fused chunked-attention kernel (runtime/attention/weave_kernel.*): implements a tiled attention path that accepts a per-request chunking strategy. For short sequences the kernel uses an in-register fastpath; for long sequences it streams chunks with overlap to maintain rotary/rope alignment. The kernel is written in CUDA with a CPU fallback and a compact C++ dispatch shim.
- Windowed KV cache (runtime/kv/windowed_cache.*): KV state is partitioned into fixed-size windows (configurable per-model). When sequence windows age out, the cache drops the oldest window instead of evicting by token-trace alone, which reduces cache churn for streaming decodes. The cache exposes a backward-compatible interface so existing scheduler logic can opt into windowed mode per-model.
- Continuous-batcher micro-scheduler (runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.*): a lightweight scheduler that keeps warm batches on a small timer and opportunistically merges tolerant small requests while respecting per-route latency budgets. Integrates with existing autoscaling/batching knobs and supports per-tenant configuration.

Commits (summary):
1) feat(attn): implement weave-attn fused chunked kernel (add CUDA + unit tests)
2) feat(kv): windowed KV cache implementation + integration tests
3) feat(scheduler): continuous-batcher scheduler + metrics/tracing hooks
4) perf: integration benchmark harness and batch shape simulator (bench/perf/weave_attn_bench.py)
5) docs: operator and rollout guide, API compatibility notes
6) test: add regression tests for rotary alignment across chunk boundaries

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/attention/weave_kernel.cu, weave_kernel.h, weave_dispatch.cpp
- runtime/kv/windowed_cache.h, windowed_cache.cpp, windowed_cache_test.cc
- runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.cpp, continuous_batcher.h, continuous_batcher_test.cc
- bench/perf/weave_attn_bench.py
- docs/operators/weave-attn-rollout.md
- sdk/python/redwood/rollouts.py (opt-in flag)
- tests/regressions/rotary_chunk_alignment.py
- ci/workflows/gpu-smoke.yml (added new perf job)

Benchmarks (representative, measured on p4d):
- Long-context throughput (32k tokens, batch=1): weave-attn end-to-end TP increases 1.8x versus baseline tiled kernel; GPU memory peak reduced ~15%.
- Mixed small/large request steady-state: continuous-batcher improves small-request P99 by 18% at 95th percentile load while maintaining >90% of baseline throughput for long requests.
- Prefix-heavy streaming workloads: windowed KV cache reduces KV write amplification and lowers token cost by ~12% on average for our synthetic newsroom workload.
Notes: absolute numbers vary by model and sequence distribution; included bench harness for reproducibility.

Compatibility and rollout:
- The new kernel and cache are behind feature flags. Models can opt-in via model config: pipelineOptions.kernel = "weave" and kv.cache_mode = "windowed". The SDK exposes an opt-in helper to mark routes for continuous-batcher.
- Backward compatible: default behavior remains unchanged until rollout is enabled. We provide a compatibility shim that translates existing KV pointers to the windowed layout for mixed nodes during rollout.

Testing and CI:
- Added unit and integration tests that validate rotary/rope index continuity across chunk boundaries and cross-node migration for cached windows.
- CI matrix includes gpu-smoke (new), cpu-unit, integration, and flake8/lint. First CI run hit a nondeterministic race in the batcher timer (GPU smoke failed intermittently); fixed by introducing a scoped wakeup token and retry logic. Final CI status: pass across matrix.

Review thread (highlights):
- Miguel: "Nice work on the chunked kernel — can you explain how we preserve rotary index offsets when we stream overlapping chunks?"
- Author (Ava): "We implemented an index remap layer inside weave_dispatch.cpp that carries per-request base offsets and applies an incremental offset when emitting kv slices; tests included to validate wrap-around cases."
- Priya: "Concern: continuous-batcher may increase tail latency for very low-concurrency tenants. Can we add a tenant-level opt-out?"
- Author: "Added per-tenant gating and a rate-based quick-path that bypasses batching for latency-critical tenants; added docs and tests."
- Daniel: "Please add a rollout plan and kill-switch for autoscaling regression. Also request to surface metrics for window eviction rate."
- Author: "Added rollout doc with kill-switch and added window_evictions/sec and evicted_window_age histograms to the metrics surface."
- Approval: Miguel and Priya approved after fixes; Daniel did final approval with minor nits addressed.

CI details and troubleshooting:
- Initial lint failure due to formatting in weave_dispatch.cpp (fixed).
- Intermittent GPU smoke failure due to batcher timer race; repro in bench harness, fix landed in commit 3.
- Final CI: all checks green (unit/integration/gpu-smoke/perf bench runs).

Merge and release notes:
- Merge method: squash and merge to main. Merge commit: 0f3b7c9 (squash)
- Merged by: Miguel Torres on 2026-03-09
- Release note (operators): Opt-in kernel 'weave' and 'windowed' KV cache. Expect throughput gains for long-context workloads and lower memory usage; monitor window_evictions and batcher_queue_latency.

Follow-ups and TODOs:
- Investigate a hybrid eviction policy that is size-aware inside windows (ENG-9124).
- Add adaptive window sizing based on request distribution (ENG-9150).
- Port a subset of microbenchmarks to the on-prem installer to validate behavior in Private deployments.

Author's testing checklist (from PR body):
- [x] Unit tests for kernel numeric equivalence on fp16/fp32 paths
- [x] Integration tests for chunk boundaries and rotary alignment
- [x] Benchmarks added and reproducible locally
- [x] Metrics and dashboards updated
- [x] Rollout doc and kill-switch implemented

Summary: This PR is a performance-oriented change set that combines kernel-level improvements with cache and scheduler enhancements to address real production pain points. It is feature-flagged, tested, and merged with a controlled rollout plan.

Introduces a new fused chunked-attention kernel (weave-attn) with windowed KV caching and a continuous-batcher micro-scheduler. Improves throughput for long-context workloads and reduces P99 latency for small requests; includes opt-in rollout and compatibility shim for pinned models.
payload.title: weave-attn: chunked fused-attention kernel + windowed KV caching + continuous-batcher

payload.body:
Motivation: Long-tail latency and cost spikes often correlate with specific invocation phases and prompt shapes which are under-sampled by uniform trace capture. This PR implements a lightweight contextual span weighting algorithm to bias sampling toward spans with high phase-contribution and a coordinating token-cost conductor service that ties sampler budgets, token-cost estimates, and alert thresholds into a single runtime control plane. The result is higher-fidelity telemetry for the parts of the invocation lifecycle that drive cost and latency without increasing overall sampling volume. Design and changes: 1) span_weighting module implements a per-invocation phase scorer that consumes phased timing buckets and prompt-shape hashes to produce a dynamic weight for each span. 2) token_cost_conductor service exposes a gRPC control endpoint and REST read-only surface to allocate per-route sampling budgets, reconcile token-cost estimates with billing data, and emit sampling directives to downstream collectors. 3) telemetry samplers (prefetch and fallback samplers) were updated to honor span weights and conductor directives. 4) dashboards: new "Conductor Cost Rhythm" and "Phase Heatmap Detail" panels added to the observability space with linked drilldowns. 5) alerts: added adaptive alerting rule that scales alert thresholds by conductor-provided cost multipliers to reduce alert noise during known high-cost prompts. 6) docs and runbook: new runbook section describes how to tune conductor budgets, interpret phase-weighted traces, and rollback. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag observability.phase_weighting and conductor.enabled. Default rollout: internal canary in us-west for 48 hours, followed by staged rollout to all regions over one week. Observability validation: unit tests for span weighting and conductor reconciliation, integration test that simulates prompt-shape distribution and validates sampler directives, and a synthetic replay that shows 38% more high-impact spans sampled at equal budget. Backwards compatibility: collectors ignore conductor directives if the conductor is unreachable; sampling falls back to local defaults. Related work and tracking: links to linear tasks ENG-4217 and OBS-88 for tuning and alert adjustments.
Adds phase-aware span weighting, a token-cost conductor service, new dashboard panels, and an observability runbook entry.
payload.title: Introduce contextual span weighting and token-cost conductor for observability

Motivation: our presubmit runs have grown noisy and slow; many PRs re-run large test suites even when changes only affect docs or a single package. This PR introduces an adaptive presubmit scheduler that selects a minimal test profile based on changed paths and historical test runtime signals, plus a dependency-surface shrinker that prunes development-only transitive deps from the frontend build graph to reduce install times. The change set touches GH workflows, a small custom action (presubmit-scheduler), a lightweight Go service used in CI to compute test selection, helper scripts for path classification, and a handful of lockfile updates. Key goals: 1) reduce median presubmit wall-clock time, 2) avoid unnecessary e2e / heavy integration runs for doc/infra-only PRs, 3) shrink CI install latency by trimming developer-only transitive deps detected in our monorepo. Motivation: We need finer-grained control for canary releases that respects temporal user segments (timezone/active-window), session affinity, and short-lived metric shocks. Current staged canaries at Redwood focus on percentage-based splits and cohort anchors; customers asked for time-windowed phasing (e.g., release to early-morning users first) and a conservative rollback fence for rapid metric regressions during local peak windows. This PR introduces a Temporal Segmented Canary Controller (TSCC) with heuristic rollback scoring and session-affinity reconciliation.

What this PR does: Adds a controller that can schedule canary percentage ramps bound to temporal segment definitions (time-of-day, local timezone, business hours), maintain session-affine buckets to avoid mid-session model swaps, and run an automated rollback heuristic that combines rate-of-change of key SLOs, cohort drift scores, and cross-segment divergence. The rollback heuristic uses a decaying severity score so transient blips are deprioritized while sustained degradations trigger an automated rollback.

Key behaviors: 1) Temporal fencing: define segments by cron-like windows and user timezone mapping so traffic can be phased across local-active windows. 2) Segment-aware shadowing: sample-preserving shadow runs that maintain the same user-session routing to avoid introduction bias when promoting. 3) Session-affinity reconciliation: a small sticky-lease to avoid replacing a model mid-session (configurable TTL). 4) Rollback heuristic: weighted aggregation of latency P95 delta, error-rate delta, quality-regression signal (from eval hooks), and session-conflict rate. 5) Visibility: emits per-segment metrics, a confidence score time-series, and a suggested action label for the Console rollout timeline.

Compatibility: Backwards compatible with existing rollout CRD. New optional fields are added to the rollout spec (temporalSegments, sessionAffinityTTL, rollbackWeights, confidenceDecaySeconds). If omitted, controller defaults to legacy percentage ramps.

Testing and validation: Unit tests cover scheduler edge windows (DST boundaries), session-affinity transitions, and heuristic math. Integration test harness runs simulated traffic across 6 timezones and validates that rollouts respect windows and that automated rollback triggers only on sustained metric regressions. End-to-end smoke includes Canaries + Shadow promotion flow against the mock serving runtime.

Release plan: Merge to main behind feature flag rollout.temporal_canaries. Rollout on infra staging for 2 weeks then enable for early access customers. Observability dashboard panel and alert rules are included to monitor per-segment confidence and session-conflict counters.

- [x] Design doc: ENG-2145 linked
- [x] Unit + integration tests

- [x] Feature flag gating

Notes: This is targeted at customers running production canaries where traffic locality and business-hour exposures matter (e.g., financial trading hours, regionally-peaked consumer services). The rollback heuristic parameters will be tuned in staging before general availability.

payload.body:
Context & motivation:
We observed intermittent throughput regressions during canary rollouts where traffic shape shifts (short bursts from mobile clients) amplified tail latency and confounded our baseline detectors. Current canary signal fusion treats slices independently and produces noisy attributions, resulting in unnecessary rollbacks or over-conservative throttles.

This PR introduces a causal attribution layer for the perf-canary pipeline and pairs it with an adaptive throttle fence that enforces traffic-aware soft throttles during uncertain attributions. The goal is to reduce false-positive rollbacks while maintaining SLO protection for high-risk cohorts.

What this changes (high-level):
- New component: causal_attributor service that uses lightweight counterfactual shadowing + propensity scoring to estimate whether observed degradation is attributable to the candidate model or to traffic covariates.
- Adaptive throttle fence: a pluggable rollout guard that applies transient, cohort-weighted throttles when attribution confidence is low and risk to SLOs is high. Throttles decay automatically once attribution confidence improves.
- Probe prioritizer: schedules synthetic probes into under-represented cohorts to improve attribution confidence faster.
- Metric augmentation: adds per-cohort traffic features (median payload size, client-type, concurrency bucket) to the canary feature set used by detectors.
- Telemetry & runbooks: new dashboards, traces and an on-call guide for interpreting attribution scores and throttle events.

Why this is different:
Instead of only thresholding metric deltas, the attributor estimates a counterfactual by shadowing a small fraction of production traffic (shadow traffic is forked and routed to the candidate model without impacting the real response path) and measuring divergence conditioned on covariates. The system then uses inverse-propensity weighting to reduce confounding from traffic shifts. The throttle fence is conservative: it starts as a soft traffic cap (reduce candidate share for specific cohorts) and falls back to full rollback only if the attribution and direct perf signals both indicate regression.

Checklist (PR owner):
- [x] Implement causal_attributor core algorithm and service scaffold
- [x] Integrate throttle fence into rollout controller with config knobs
- [x] Add probe prioritizer and probe scheduling hooks
- [x] Add schema changes for cohort-level features and migration script
- [x] Unit tests for attributor, throttle decay, and probe prioritizer
- [x] Integration tests with canary e2e harness (local emulation)
- [x] Dashboard and alert updates + runbook draft
- [x] Load-tested candidate path with synthetic spike scenarios

Commits (summary):
- 6a3b2f1: initial causal attributor implementation + unit tests
- e4d9b77: expose attributor as internal gRPC service and auth layer
- b7f6c04: add cohort feature extractor and DB migration v20260210
- c9a1d2e: throttle fence implementation and controller integration
- 73f4a90: probe prioritizer + scheduler hooks into canary prober
- 2d5e8c3: dashboards/alerts/runbook updates
- 9b1f0ab: integration tests and CI flake fixes

Changed files (high-level):
- canary/attributor/causal_attributor.py  (core algorithm, ~420 lines)
- canary/attributor/protobufs/attributor.proto  (gRPC API)
- canary/controller/throttle_fence.go  (controller integration)
- canary/prober/prioritizer.py  (probe prioritizer)
- canary/schema/cohort_features.sql  (migration)
- canary/tests/test_attributor.py
- infra/helm/canary-values.yaml  (config knobs for fence)
- dashboards/canary-attribution.json  (grafana)
- docs/runbooks/canary-attribution.md
- telemetry/metrics_definitions.yaml  (new per-cohort labels)
- canary/e2e/test_synthetic_spike.yaml

Small illustrative snippet (core heuristic used):
"""python
# inverse-propensity weighted divergence estimator (simplified)
weight = 1.0 / max(propensity(candidate), 1e-6)
divergence = weight * kl_divergence(prod_distribution, candidate_distribution)
confidence = 1.0 - sigmoid( a * divergence + b * covariate_variance )
# low confidence -> trigger soft throttle for affected cohorts
"""

Testing & CI notes:
- Local integration harness used to replay production slices and synthetic spikes; added new e2e scenario that reproduces a mobile-burst tail event.
- CI initially failed on a flaky probe scheduler test (test_probe_backoff) — root cause: race in the test harness; fixed by adding deterministic clock injection.
- All unit and integration checks now pass in CI.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag default=off; enable for internal canaries only (team: perf-canary)
2) Stage to 5% of rollouts for 48h with verbose debugging enabled
3) Close-loop: if throttle fence events >3 in 24h for same cohort, auto-disable and page oncall for investigation
4) After stability window (2 weeks) progressively increase to 25% then global enable for non-critical releases

Runbook excerpt (how to interpret events):
- Attribution score near 0.8+ AND throughput delta > 5% -> likely candidate regression; consider rollback if SLOs at risk.
- Attribution low (<0.4) and covariate variance high -> suspect traffic shift; throttle fence will reduce candidate share for high-variance cohorts while probes collect more signal.
- Throttle fence log example: "fence: cohort=mobile-102, action=soft-cap, new_share=0.12, decay=15m, reason=low-confidence-high-variance"

Related work & references:
- ENG-3421: background on cohort-based detectors
- ENG-3499: earlier experiment with shadowing for rerankers

Notes for reviewers:
- The attributor includes approximations (IPW and lightweight shadowing) to keep CPU/GPU overhead low; we intentionally avoided heavy causal inference libraries to minimize ops burden.
- Config knobs are intentionally conservative; we expect tuning after a canary window.
- Security: shadowing forks only headers+payload to candidate and respects PII redaction pipeline; included a KMS-backed toggle for further access control.

Merge outcome:
- Approved by reviewers Maya Chen and Diego Alvarez after two rounds of feedback.
- Requested change: make throttle decay configurable per-cohort (addressed in commit 9b1f0ab).
- CI green on final build; merged via squash to main on 2026-02-18.

Release notes:
- New canary capability: causal attribution + adaptive throttle fence for cohort-aware rollouts. Reduces false-positive rollbacks during traffic shifts and adds safer soft throttling behavior.

Motivation: We observed rare but repeatable user incidents where streaming responses terminated with partial JSON payloads or interleaved fncall tokens when the transport split occurred inside multi-byte UTF-8 sequences or when heartbeats and event payloads were coalesced. This caused downstream OpenAI-compat clients to error on parse or lose function call ordering. Summary: Introduce a conservative byte-stitcher that coalesces adjacent SSE chunks across transport boundaries, an escape-coalescer to avoid splitting JSON escape sequences, and an explicit ordinal watermark for function-call events so the tool/function-caller reconciler can re-order or re-emit lost events deterministically. The change is limited to the OpenAI-compat SSE emitter and the streaming parser path; it does not alter non-streaming API behavior.Design highlights: 1) SSE byte-stitcher: buffer up to 256 bytes across chunk boundaries when a chunk ends with an incomplete UTF-8 codepoint or an open JSON token (open quote, backslash, or unclosed brace). Stitcher emits a tight checksum (8-bit XOR) in a non-protocol header for local reassembly checks during dechunking. 2) Escape coalescer: detect trailing backslashes and ensure escape sequences (e.g., \uXXXX) are not split across writes. 3) Fncall ordinals: attach a monotonic ordinal to fncall sentinel events (X-Redwood-Fn-Ordinal header emitted inline as event detail) and a small resume-ack handshake that allows clients to request retransmit of ordinal ranges on reconnect. 4) Heartbeat slab adjuster: reduce heartbeat-induced coalescing by introducing a 10ms jitter in heartbeat emission when higher-priority fncall events are pacing through the emitter to avoid interleaving.5) Safety and performance tradeoffs: Default behavior is opt-in via server flag --sse-stitcher=enabled for rollout. Stitcher only engages for chunk sizes < 4KB and when a heuristic detects likely split. The checksum and ordinal metadata are intentionally tiny to limit overhead.Testing: Unit tests added for UTF-8 split cases, escaped unicode sequences, and fncall ordinal monotonicity. Integration tests simulated TCP-level fragmentation and reassembly using a faker transport; we replayed production captures that previously triggered the bug. Load test: end-to-end latency impact measured under production-like batching; median token latency increased ~0.3ms and P99 remained within SLOs. Rollout and migration: feature gate enabled in staged Canary for 48 hours in us-west-2, then expanded to 20% of traffic, monitored via new metric sse.stitcher.rescue_count and fncall.ordinal-mismatch. Backout plan: gate off and fall back to previous emitter; reconnect resumes without user-visible data loss (clients will see a small chance of duplicated fncall which is guarded by idempotency in the function-caller reconciler).

payload.body:
Motivation: Continuous batchers have a soft window where short-lived (latency-sensitive) requests can be coalesced into larger batches to improve GPU utilization. However, we observed KV-pin storms and cold-KV miss sequences that either cause starvation for long-tail requests or create oscillations in batch sizes. This PR introduces an adaptive, slice-based idle coalescer that dynamically adjusts wait-slices per-queue using lightweight telemetry and a probabilistic backoff to avoid synchronized wavefronts.

Summary of changes: Implements an idle-coalescer module in the batcher scheduler that: 1) splits the existing linger window into N adaptive slices; 2) tracks per-model and per-tenant recent KV-hit ratios and uses a sliding EWMA to bias early-slice admission for KV-hot traffic; 3) applies a small randomized jitter to slice deadlines to break synchronization; 4) exposes two new knobs -- "slice_target_ms" and "slice_decay_factor" -- for ops tuning; 5) adds a probe path that allows a tiny number of requests to bypass coalescing when starvation is detected; 6) surfaces metrics and traces (batch_coalesce.slices, kv_hint_evictions, starvation_probes) for SLO reconciliation. Additionally adds a minor kernel-dispatch alignment hint that groups prefetch-friendly dispatches to reduce KV cache thrash on the hot path.

Why this is different: Instead of one global linger window we use fine-grained slices with explicit fairness quotas per scheduling class. This reduces head-of-line blocking caused by large requests while retaining coalescing benefits for high-throughput models. The probabilistic probe prevents silent starvation without a heavyweight preemption mechanism.

Testing & results: Microbenchmarks (local perf lab) and a 2-hour canary on staging with mixed traffic (chatty short requests + long-context reranks) show: - 18% reduction in p99 latency for short requests under 60% load; - 12% throughput improvement for medium-length generations at 90% GPU occupancy; - kv-hit stabilization (variance reduction) on models with high KV churn. Load tests and canary logs attached in the commits.

Rollout plan: Feature-flag guarded (batcher.enable_adaptive_slices=false by default). Gradual rollout: enable for one tenant group, monitor metrics for 24h, then expand. Ops knobs documented in the console and in the scheduler tuning guide.

Checklist: - [x] design doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4821/adaptive-slice-coalescer-design - [x] unit tests added - [x] integration test in perf-lab harness - [x] telemetry and dashboards wired - [x] feature-flag gating
Diego Alvarez: Design looks solid overall; please justify the choice of EWMA window size in the comment and add a short note on worst-case added latency.
Maya Chen: Responded: increased EWMA alpha from 0.2 to 0.35 after running sensitivity tests. Added comment in code explaining rationale and worst-case bound (~slice_target_ms extra).
Rina Patel: Can we ensure the probe path cannot amplify load during a KV storm? Recommend an absolute cap per-queue.
Maya Chen: Added a per-queue probe cap (configurable ops knob) and unit tests asserting cap enforcement.
Tomás O'Neill: CI flakes on perf-lab harness when kernel hint is enabled; please add a guard to skip the hint on older CUDA drivers.
Maya Chen: Added driver detection and a safe fallback path. Re-ran canary; no regressions observed.

Motivation: recent incidents showed oscillation during geo failovers where the regional fallback policy would rapidly flip routes and trigger downstream cache churn, increasing 95th latency and exhausting error budgets. This PR introduces a stabilizer that: 1) converts the fallback decision into slot-scored windows so that a region must hold a score threshold for a minimum hysteresis window before traffic is moved, and 2) couples the decision to a telemetry-weighted SLO smoother that discounts transient spikes and only triggers emergency fallback when sustained error-budget drain is observed. This is a small hotfix aimed at reducing failover flapping while preserving fast failover in true outage cases. Changes: - Add slot-based hysteresis scoring and cooldown for regional fallback decisions. - Introduce session-aware eviction: requests in a session keep KV-cache affinity unless an aggressive outage threshold is crossed. - Telemetry-weighted SLO smoother: blend of recent error-rate and longer-window error-budget consumption to avoid reacting to noise. - Expose two new runtime knobs: fallback.hysteresis_window_ms and fallback.slot_threshold and a debug metric fallback.stabilizer_score. - Hotfix fallback: when stabilizer detects persistent high error-budget drain for >2 minutes, it lowers slot threshold and triggers an emergency fallback path (configurable). Rollout plan: staged canary 5% EU -> 25% EU -> 10% NA -> global after 24h monitoring. Rollback: immediate rollback if canary sees >1.5x baseline 95th latency or any SLO regressions in alerting groups. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for scorer logic - [x] Integration tests for canary policy - [x] Perf bench with synthetic failover - [x] Dashboard panels for fallback.stabilizer_score and hysteresis windows - [x] Linear/SUP links in PR body Related: ENG-4219 for long-term routing rewrite; SUP-8843 incident that triggered this hotfix. Notes: This is intentionally conservative: default hysteresis_window_ms is 1500ms and slot_threshold 3 (three consistent slots within window). Emergency fallback path is more permissive but gated by sustained telemetry. See release notes for behavior and knobs.
Diego Alvarez (requested_changes): The hysteresis window is fine but we should verify the memory growth on long-running SlotScorer instances; can you add an eviction of old region entries after 20 minutes of inactivity?
Asha Menon (reply): Added a weak-expiration for region entries and unit tests cover the expiry path (see commit d4e5f6a).
Priya Kothari (comment): Can we expose an opt-in feature flag for enterprise customers to tune slot_threshold without config rollouts?
Asha Menon (reply): Added runtime flag support via config/defaults and a console toggle placeholder in docs/runbooks for on-call to toggle during incidents.
Liam O'Neill (approval): Verified canary runs in staging for eu-west-1 and us-east-1. Observed 73% reduction in fallback-flap events during synthetic outage; approved for merge.
CI Runner (note): One integration flake initially (test_canary_fallback_flow) - re-ran CI and it passed.
Hotfix: stabilize regional fallback decisions to prevent routing oscillation under partial outages. Adds slot-based hysteresis, session-aware eviction to preserve KV affinity, and a telemetry-weighted SLO smoother. Defaults are conservative and tunable via runtime flags.

This PR introduces a compact RAG micro-orchestrator called 'Step Inspector' — a local-first playground and authoring kit aimed at making multi-tool RAG workflows easier to debug and iterate. Motivation: teams repeatedly tell us that diagnosing where a multi-step agent goes off-track (tool contract mismatch, embedding drift, prompt variant regressions) is time-consuming. The Step Inspector bundles: a) a minimal browser dev UI that renders the step graph, per-step prompt/response, and KV cache snapshots; b) a headless playback runner for deterministic CI smoke tests; c) a lightweight local proxy that can stub tool backends and record wire traces; d) TypeScript and Python adapter examples that show typed tool contracts and structured output checks; e) docs site walkthroughs and a short tutorial notebook. The focus is on authoring, deterministic replay, and low-friction debugging for engineers authoring tool-calling RAG flows. Motivation: Several enterprise customers requested a single control that enforces jurisdictional routing for sensitive workloads (data residency + KMS locality) while ensuring every KMS interaction emits a verifiable audit envelope. This PR implements the Regulatory Zone Enforcer (RZE) and an in-path KMS Audit Gateway that signs and stamps KMS requests with tenant zone assertions.

Summary of changes: Implement policy layer that evaluates tenant jurisdiction profiles and denies or redirects requests that violate region pins. Add KMS Audit Gateway service that performs pre-flight KMS scope checks, attaches signed audit headers (x-rw-kms-audit) and emits immutable audit records to the audit ingestion pipeline. Integrate RZE checks into the API gateway request flow and the private installer for on-prem topology.

Design notes: The RZE is a lightweight policy decision point that consults tenant profile metadata (tenant_zone, allowed_zones, residency_enforced) cached with TTL. Decisions are deterministic and include a short decision fingerprint to avoid replay ambiguity. The KMS Audit Gateway wraps all outbound CMK operations with a signed envelope (proof = HMAC-SHA256 over {tenant_id, request_id, region, timestamp, decision_fingerprint}) and forwards the envelope to the audit stream. The gateway supports fail-open behavior controlled by org-level policy for legacy customers and an opt-in failover that routes to a cross-region fallback CMK when allowed by contract.

Checklist: - [x] Policy evaluator and cache implementation - [x] KMS Audit Gateway service with signing + envelope schema - [x] API gateway integration and middleware hook - [x] Private installer hooks + migration script for existing on-prem configs - [x] Unit and integration tests for policy decisions and envelope validation - [x] E2E test in perf-canary with synthetic tenant profiles - [x] Documentation for compliance and operator runbook

Commits: ["e1f3b9d: rze: add policy evaluator and TTL cache", "a4c2d01: kms-audit-gateway: initial service and envelope signer", "5b6f7aa: api-gateway: insert rze middleware for pre-route checks", "c9d2e5f: installer: add rze role and installer flag", "d3f4b22: tests: policy evaluator unit tests + integration harness", "f8a0b11: docs: compliance guide and operator runbook" ]

Files changed (high-level): ["services/policy-enforcer/rze_evaluator.go", "services/policy-enforcer/cache.go", "services/policy-enforcer/README.md", "services/kms-audit-gateway/main.go", "services/kms-audit-gateway/envelope.go", "services/kms-audit-gateway/handler_test.go", "api-gateway/middleware/regulatory_zone.go", "installer/manifest/rze-roles.yaml", "pkg/audit/ingest_client.go", "pkg/audit/envelope_schema.md", "docs/compliance/regulatory-zone-enforcer.md", "infra/helm/kms-audit-gateway/values.yaml"]

Small snippet (policy decision sketch): "if tenant.residency_enforced && !tenant.allowed_zones.contains(request.region) { decision = DENY; reason = "region-pin-violation" } else { decision = ALLOW }". Envelope sketch: "{ "tenant_id":..., "req_id":..., "region":..., "ts":..., "fingerprint":..., "signature":... }"

Testing & CI: CI matrix runs unit tests, integration containerized tests for the kms-audit-gateway (with local fake-KMS), and a linting pass. One transient test failure seen in initial run (integration timeout on fake-KMS); rerun passed. Load test profile against perf-canary validated the RPS target with <1% added p50 latency for the gateway in canary configuration.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy kms-audit-gateway behind feature-flag in canary region. 2) Enable RZE middleware for internal test tenants. 3) Gradual ramp to customers with residency contracts; for others leave fail-open route. 4) Enable Strict mode (deny on violation) after 2 weeks of telemetry. Operator notes and migration script included in installer patch for private installs.

Backward compatibility: Default behavior is no-op unless tenant profile signals residency_enforced or operator flips strict_mode. Gateway can be configured to only attach audit envelopes and not enforce routing.

Security review: Key signing uses rotated HMAC keys stored in our CMK-backed secrets store. We added strict TTL and nonce checks to envelopes to mitigate replay. Roadmap: next step is to add automated policy lint rules in the RBAC compiler to detect conflicting residency claims across tenant profiles.

Related work: ENG-3205 (jurisdictional routing), ENG-3212 (audit stream hardening), SUP-1884 (customer support case for region pin breach).

Notes for reviewers: Look at envelope.go and regulatory_zone.go for the core logic. The installer manifest includes a migration helper that safely annotates existing tenant profiles with default allowed_zones; please validate the migration in your dev clusters before merge. If we can get two approvals we can squash-merge and begin the canary rollout.
Add Regulatory Zone Enforcer and KMS Audit Gateway. This enables per-tenant jurisdictional enforcement, region pinning checks at the ingress, and a signed audit envelope for all KMS operations. No customer-visible API changes; rollout via canary and feature flags.
Eliot Summers (2026-02-11): Looks good overall; can you call out TTL reasoning and expected cache miss amplification?
Priya Nambiar (2026-02-11): TTL defaults to 60s with jitter; added bench numbers in policy-enforcer/README.md
Jingwei Zhou (2026-02-12): Please add validation for tenant.allowed_zones format and add unit tests for malformed profiles
Priya Nambiar (2026-02-12): Added validation and tests in d3f4b22
Marta Kline (2026-02-13): Security nit: move HMAC key rotation to keymanager interface and add integration test to prove rotation works
Priya Nambiar (2026-02-14): Addressed: introduced keymanager shim and rotation test; updated docs
Eliot Summers (2026-02-14): Verified canary metrics; approved
Jingwei Zhou (2026-02-14): Approved after test fixes

payload.body:
Motivation:
Service teams continue to ask for safer, lower-latency canary and A/B experiments that can retroactively revert decisions when slow signals emerge. Existing staged canary controllers rely on forward-only gating; they lack a consistent way to 1) fan out short-lived probe traffic across heterogenous model variants, 2) record time-indexed probe outcomes for retroactive policy evaluation, and 3) trigger deterministic replay rollbacks when post-commit regressions are detected.

This PR introduces the Probe-driven Fanout Controller (PFC) and a lightweight Retroactive Rollback Ledger (RRL). The PFC coordinates probe traffic (synthetic and sampled real requests) across model variants (canary, baseline, shadow lanes) with configurable probe patterns (burst, periodic, stratified). The RRL records probe events and metric snapshots so automated rollback policies can evaluate historical windows and perform deterministic replay-based rollbacks.

Summary of changes (single-string description kept continuous):
- New controller: serving/orchestrator/pfc/controller.go + pfc/scheduler.go + pfc/config.go implement probe scheduling, cohort allocation, and safepoints for fanout phases.
- Retroactive ledger: serving/orchestrator/ledger/ledger.go + ledger/store_sql.go + ledger/compact.go implement an append-only time-indexed ledger with compaction helpers and replay hooks.
- Policy adapters: serving/orchestrator/policies/retro_policy.go adds evaluation hooks for thresholded retroactive rollbacks and windowed scoring.
- Console integration: console/rollouts/ProbeRolloutCard.tsx + console/rollouts/api.ts add UI to visualize probe timelines and a manual rollback/replay action.
- E2E and integration tests: infra/tests/integration/test_probe_fanout.py + infra/tests/e2e/replay_rollback_smoke.py exercise scheduling, ledger replay, and rollback fidelity.
- Docs: docs/rollouts/probe_fanout.md and docs/rollouts/retro_rollback_playbook.md describe configuration and runbook.
- Small API change: new optional field rollout.probePattern on the Rollout CRD (backwards compatible default behavior) and a RolloutStatus.probeTimeline for UI.

Why this is safe: the controller operates under existing rollout admission and only allocates probe fractions (defaults to 0.5% of traffic) unless explicitly configured. Ledger writes are append-only and sharded by rollout ID; compaction runs asynchronously. All changes are feature-flagged under rollout.feature.probe_fanout.

Checklist:
- [x] Controller scheduling and fanout logic implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Ledger append/replay semantics covered by integration tests
- [x] Policy adapter with safe defaults (auto-abort on >20% metric regression in probe window)
- [x] Console UI to surface probe timeline and manual replay/rollback
- [x] Feature flag gated and documented
- [x] Performance sanity: probe scheduler adds <1% CPU to control-plane under 5k active rollouts

Compatibility and migration notes:
- Rollouts without rollout.probePattern continue to behave as before (no probe fanout).
- Rollouts opting into probe_fanout will have small ledger writes; operators should enable compaction cron in Dedicated/Private installer to bound storage.
- The RolloutStatus.probeTimeline is additive and read-only for clients.

Testing notes and CI history (summary):
- Unit: all new unit tests pass (coverage +2.1%).
- Integration: initial run failed on flaky test infra (infra/tests/integration/test_probe_fanout.py) due to timing assumptions; fixed by adding deterministic clock injection.
- E2E: replay_rollback_smoke validated rollback fidelity on a synthetic latency regression scenario.
- Load: controller performance bench shows median scheduling latency 14ms under 2k active probes.

Commits:
- "pfc: initial probe-driven scheduler and config (Maya Chen)"
- "ledger: append-only ledger and basic SQL store (Maya Chen)"
- "policies: retro_policy evaluation + tests (Maya Chen)"
- "console: probe rollout card + timeline visualization (Ivy Tran)"
- "tests: integration/e2e for replay rollback scenarios (QA/infra)"

Files changed (high level):
- serving/orchestrator/pfc/controller.go
- serving/orchestrator/pfc/scheduler.go
- serving/orchestrator/pfc/config.go
- serving/orchestrator/ledger/ledger.go
- serving/orchestrator/ledger/store_sql.go
- serving/orchestrator/ledger/compact.go
- serving/orchestrator/policies/retro_policy.go
- console/rollouts/ProbeRolloutCard.tsx
- console/rollouts/api.ts
- infra/tests/integration/test_probe_fanout.py
- infra/tests/e2e/replay_rollback_smoke.py
- docs/rollouts/probe_fanout.md
- docs/rollouts/retro_rollback_playbook.md

Operational runbook snippet (embedded):
- If a retroactive rollback triggers unexpectedly, the controller sets rollout.status.phase=HOLD and emits rollout.events with a rollback_ticket ID. Use console -> Rollouts -> "View probe timeline" to inspect probe windows; replay can be started from the UI which performs deterministic replay against a frozen input snapshot.

Usage example (Rollout CR snippet):
rollout:
  id: recommend-v2
  model: redwood/gpt-medium:2026-02-01
  probePattern: "stratified(period=5m,fraction=0.005,burst=50)"
  policies:
    - type: RetroactiveThreshold
      window: 30m
      metric: p95_latency_ms
      threshold: 1.20

Notes on follow-ups: ledger retention policy management and cross-region ledger replication are out of scope for this PR (tracked in ENG-2499).
Diego Morales (2026-02-19): Overall looks solid. A few nits on scheduler backoff and a suggestion to move metric window computation into a shared util. Please address.
Maya Chen (2026-02-20): Thanks Diego — moved the window math into metrics/window.go and added unit tests for boundary cases.
Sofia Patel (2026-02-21): Policy adapter should short-circuit when probe data is incomplete to avoid noisy rollbacks. Can we add a minimum sample check?
Maya Chen (2026-02-22): Added minSamples param (defaults to 50) and updated docs + UI to surface sample counts.
Liam O'Connor (2026-02-23): Integration test flake fixed. Approving pending green CI.
CI Bot (2026-02-24): Integration tests initially failed (timing). Reran with deterministic clock; all checks green.
Sofia Patel (2026-02-25): Approved and verified UI screenshots in staging.
Release Manager (2026-02-26): Merged via squash. Changelog updated.
Adds a probe-driven fanout rollout controller that enables retroactive rollback triggers and replayable rollback ledger; backward compatible with existing rollout policies.

payload.body:
Motivation: Continuous batching has reduced unit cost but occasional tail spikes and starvation of small, latency-sensitive requests persist under mixed workloads. This PR introduces a timed fair slot reshaper that dynamically reshapes admission windows to preserve fairness while maintaining high aggregation efficiency.

Summary of changes: Adds a timed-slot reshaper that sits between the admission queue and the batch coalescer. The reshaper keeps soft time windows per logical lane and tracks recent slot consumption to bias upcoming time slices toward starved lanes. It introduces a starvation sentinel that will preempt a small portion of a batch when a lane's historical wait exceeds a threshold, and a short randomized soft-timeout jitter to avoid synchronization under bursty arrivals. The reshaper emits metrics that let the console detect if the reshaper is actively rebalancing slots (reshaper.active_pct) and lane-level wait quantiles. Additionally, the reshaper exposes a lightweight hint interface for the KV cache layer so prefetch hints can be applied when a request is admitted but delayed to the next slot — this reduces cold-kv misses for starved lanes. The feature is designed to be opt-in via runtime config flags and to fall back to existing behaviour when disabled.

Design notes: - Timed-slot windows are sized relative to target latency SLOs and request size histograms. Small/interactive lanes get smaller windows with higher reshaping priority. - Starvation sentinel counts per-lane wait time and uses an exponential backoff to avoid oscillation. - Prefetch hinting: when a request is deferred to the next slot, we call KV prefetch_hint(keyset) asynchronously; prefetch path is lockfree and best-effort. - Kernel hint handshake: reshaper emits an inline hint that the kernel selection layer can use to favor lower-latency kernels for lanes marked interactive (heuristic only).

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in PR: ENG-3421 design notes included in description - [x] Unit tests for reshaper logic and starvation sentinel - [x] Microbench perf harness (mixed small+large reqs) - [x] Integration test with kv cache hint path - [x] Metrics, logs, and docs - [x] Rollout plan with feature flag and staged percentage - [x] Non-blocking rollback via feature flag

Testing & results: Microbench (locally) with 10k qps mixed workload (80% small interactive, 20% large generation) shows 95th latency of small requests reduced from ~220ms to ~140ms and 99th reduced from ~560ms to ~310ms. Throughput drop under full aggregation was <2% when feature enabled. CI perf job initially flagged a small regression in a large-model continuous batcher integration test; that was due to an overly-aggressive default window cap — adjusted defaults and re-ran CI.

Rollout: Default state is disabled. Deploy stage: (1) Enable on low-traffic cluster with reshaper metrics monitored; (2) Ramp to 10% routes; (3) Ramp to 50%; (4) Global on. Backout via feature flag toggles immediately reverts to previous behaviour.

Risks and mitigations: - Overly aggressive reshaping can reduce batch efficiencies: mitigated by conservative default caps and runtime tuning via console. - KV prefetch hints could increase transient memory usage: prefetch is best-effort and bounded per-lane. - Kernel hint is advisory only and will not change kernel selection unless explicit opt-in is set in model config.

Notes: This is intentionally conservative change surface: core admission path is unchanged when disabled, and all new bookkeeping is kept lockfree where feasible. Full design doc and tuning guidance included in docs/ops/reshaper.md.
Liu Chen: The starvation sentinel is promising. Can we add a safety cap to ensure we don't preempt more than 12.5% of batch tokens?
Miguel Santos: Added cap and unit test; default is 8% with runtime override. See slot_reshaper.rs:line ~214 test_preempt_cap.
Asha Iyer: Please add console graphs for lane wait quantiles and active_pct; operators will want to see reshaping events as a heatmap.
Miguel Santos: Added metrics and example dashboard JSON in docs; pinged infra to add alert for reshaper.active_pct > 60% for 5m.
Noah Patel: Integration perf test flaked once — CI failure was because the default window cap was too low; adjustable configs look good now.
Liu Chen: Approving pending CI green and a smoke run on staging.
CI: Re-run perf job on staging cluster; results match local numbers; approving to merge.
payload.title: timed-fair-slot-reshaper: reduce tail latency and starvation in continuous batcher

payload.body:
Context and motivation: We observed repeated slowpath thrashing in small regional spikes where tenants would rapidly oscillate between normal admission and slowpath fallback. That behavior caused elevated p99 tail latencies and KV cache churn during short-lived node slowdowns. This PR adds a telemetry-backed, ephemeral weighted-penalty cooldown that gates slowpath fallthroughs for tenants and routes, smoothing oscillations without permanently favoring any tenant. Intended as a focused hotfix for release/v1.42 to mitigate production noise and buy time for a longer-term scheduling improvement.

What this changes (single-line summary): Introduce PenaltyManager with per-tenant weighted penalty decay, wire telemetry signals into the admission controller, add a short soft-deny window (configurable) with exponential cooldown, and ship dashboards and integration tests. Also include conservative defaults and a fast opt-out toggle for customers using Dedicated/Private.

Key design notes: - Penalty units are charged when a request falls back to slowpath due to resource pressure or explicit circuit decisions. The unit is weighted by request cost (token estimate + KV impact). - PenaltyManager exposes a remaining_penalty float [0..1] per tenant/route. Admission controller multiplies slowpath acceptance probability by (1 - remaining_penalty) during the soft-deny window. - Decay uses an exponential backoff: penalty_t = penalty_0 * exp(-t / tau), with tau configurable per deployment tier. - Telemetry thresholds derive from the serving runtime's slowpath_error_rate and kv_drain_ratio metrics over a short sliding window (30s). We purposely avoid coupling to long-lived aggregates to keep reactions local and fast.

Commits (summary): - 8c9d2ab: introduce penalty manager core + in-memory store + unit tests - 1f4b7e0: admission controller integration and soft-deny evaluation - e22f4b3: telemetry hooks + mappings and sampled tags for tenant/route - 4a7b2c1: add integration test reproducer and CI job - 9a1c6f0: docs and operational runbook + dashboard YAML - bf3e4d2: compatibility note for private installer and opt-out flag

Files changed (high level): - pkg/serving/slowpath controlador.go: admission path updated to consult PenaltyManager and apply probabilistic soft-deny. Small, contained change with clear feature flag. - pkg/serving/penalty/penalty_manager.go: new package implementing charges, decay, and a small LRU to bound memory. - pkg/telemetry/metrics/telemetry_mappings.go: map existing slowpath and kv metrics to the penalty trigger. - internal/sre/telemetry_dashboards.yaml: new SLO-focused dashboard panels (penalty heatmap, per-tenant decay curves). - integration-tests/slowpath_repro: new repro and deterministic test using stubbed metrics. - docs/operational/soft-deny-windows.md: runbook + troubleshooting.

Backward/forward compatibility: The feature is behind a runtime feature flag enabled on release/v1.42 for the rollout cohort. The opt-out flag lives in config/deploy and is documented for Private/Dedicated customers. Telemetry mappings are additive and rely on existing metric names; where name drift exists the patch includes a compatibility shim (deploy/patches/telemetry-migration-compat.md).

Testing and CI: Added unit tests for PenaltyManager decay math and admission gating (pkg/serving/penalty/*). Integration repro runs in CI with a new deterministic slowpath test that stubs the telemetry feed to emulate 30s spikes. CI initially failed on a flaky timing assumption in tests; fixed by switching to virtualized clock in the integration harness. Final CI status: all checks passed (lint, unit, integration, e2e smoke).

Performance and resource considerations: The LRU size is conservative (default 10k tenants) with an upper bound guard; memory usage for the penalty store is negligible relative to the runtime (~2MB at default). The admission check is a single in-process lookup + float math; microbenchmarks showed <1% added CPU on the critical path at 1000rps.

Rollback plan: Feature flag gating allows safe rollback by disabling the soft-deny window. If a rollback is required post-deploy we will revert the feature flag and optionally flush penalty state; a brief out-of-band job can clear the LRU if needed.

Review conversation (highlights): - Aisha: "Can we avoid tenant starvation when penalty accumulates across multiple short spikes?" Reply (author): "We cap accumulated penalty per epoch and add a decay floor — the decay tau is shorter for transient tiers; added test coverage to assert no permanent starvation." - Claire: "Telemetry mapping needs a compatibility note for older private installs." Reply: "Added telemetry-migration-compat.md and a config toggle; private installer will include the shim in the next non-critical release." - Tom: "Integration repro timed out on CI initially." Reply: "Fixed by switching to a virtual clock and reducing wall-clock waits — see commit 4a7b2c1." Approvals: Aisha, Claire approved after small nits were addressed. Tom gave final +1.

Operational notes and dashboards: New panels added to SRE dashboards showing per-tenant penalty heatmap, global slowpath trigger rate, KV drain ratio, and effective acceptance probability. Pager trigger adjusted: we avoid new alerts for penalty charge events; instead we alert on sustained (>3m) global slowpath rate increase.

Why this is different from previous approaches: Instead of hard circuit flips or coarse global throttles, this PR implements a short-lived, telemetry-anchored smoothing mechanism that probabilistically gates slowpath acceptance. It reduces oscillation without imposing long-term restrictions and is lightweight to roll back.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to release/v1.42 on 2026-02-18 after CI green and approvals. Backported notes: included a minimal backport to 1.41 branch as a separate patch for a customer experiencing repeated p99 spikes; that backport is tracked in ENG-4730.

Follow-ups: - ENG-4799: evaluate adding cross-node penalty replication for very large tenant footprints (design doc stubbed). - ENG-4801: consider adding a small multiclass penalty weight based on model and route cost. - Cleanup: remove telemetry compatibility shim after 3 releases.

Checklist (author): - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration repro - [x] Docs and runbook - [x] Dashboard panels - [x] Feature-flagged and opt-out toggle - [x] SRE runbook entries

If anything goes wrong during rollout contact oncall SRE and the author (Diego Morales).
Hotfix: Add telemetry-driven soft-deny cooldown to reduce slowpath thrashing during regional slowdowns; include new metrics and dashboard; update docs and tests.

payload.body:
Motivation: production rollouts increasingly require fine-grained, low-cost sampling across cohorts to detect regressions without high traffic overhead. This change introduces a Sparse-fuse scheduler that interleaves micro-sampled traffic (sparse fuse lanes) with standard canary/A-B lanes and a Delta Quarantine subsystem that quarantines cohorts when statistically significant deltas are detected across a configured metric set. Summary: implement a scheduler that maintains per-cohort micro-sampling tokens, a quarantine controller that triggers automated isolated rehearse-replay probes, and CI/console hooks to visualize sparse lanes and quarantine decisions. This PR contains: 1) new scheduler engine (server/rollout/scheduler.go) implementing fused scheduling and tokenized micro-sampling, 2) delta detector and quarantine lifecycle manager (server/rollout/quarantine.go) with configurable thresholds and backoff, 3) integration test harness for replayed micro-samples (tests/integration/sparse_fuse_rehearsal.test), 4) Console UI additions to show sparse lanes and quarantine state (console/ui/rollouts/controls.tsx, console/ui/rollouts/quarantine_view.tsx), 5) telemetry and metrics for sparse sampling rate, quarantine triggers and replay success (telemetry/metrics/rollout_metrics.prom), 6) helm values and operator tweaks to enable feature gates (operator/helm/values.yaml). Backwards compatibility: default behavior is inert unless feature gate rollout.sparseFuse=true; existing rollout specs remain valid. Rollout plan: staged rollout to internal clusters with 0.1% sparse fuse enabled for two days, then raise to 1% with quarantine enabled. Safety: quarantine isolates traffic and automatically replays sampled requests to a shadow instance for validation before rollback; any quarantine with repeated failures escalates to on-call via PagerDuty integration already wired into the quarantine manager. Testing: unit tests for scheduling logic, deterministic simulation harness for delta detection, and an end-to-end integration test included. Related work:ENG-8247 implements the sampling API used here; ENG-8301 tracks quarantine playbook automation. Checklist: [x] design doc reviewed [x] unit tests added [x] integration test added [x] doc stub added [x] console changes verified locally. Notes: tuned default thresholds conservatively to avoid false positives; telemetry export includes delta magnitude and sample counts for offline analysis.
Adds fused micro-sampling scheduler to enable low-cost per-cohort sampling
Implements automated quarantine lifecycle and replay-based validation
Console and telemetry additions for operator visibility
Feature gated and opt-in via helm / operator flags
Introduces the Sparse-fuse Rollout Scheduler and Delta Quarantine controller behind a feature gate (rollout.sparseFuse). Enables low-overhead micro-sampling, automated quarantine and replay, console visibility, and telemetry. Disabled by default.
Enable rollout.sparseFuse feature gate in operator/helm/values.yaml to turn on the feature
Start with sparseSampling.rate=0.001 for initial traffic and monitor rollout_sparse_sample_count and quarantine_trigger_count metrics
Quarantine records auto-archive after 30d by default; configurable via operator values
Arjun Patel: Overall looks solid. Two requests: tighten the unit test coverage around token underflow and add a simulation for long-tail latency sensitivity.
Maya Chen: Added additional unit tests and the long-tail latency sim. Adjusted token refill semantics to avoid early starvation under bursty traffic.
Lena Ortiz: Quarantine state machine is clearer now. One nit: add a short TTL to archived quarantine records to avoid DB churn.
Maya Chen: Added TTL and retention config with sane defaults in operator/helm/values.yaml.
Tomás Ríos: Verified telemetry exports and dashboard panels in staging. Approving pending green CI.
CI Bot: Integration pipeline passed on rerun (tests/integration/sparse_fuse_rehearsal.test).
payload.title: Sparse-fuse Rollout Scheduler with Delta Quarantine and Micro-sampling Rehearsal

payload.body:
Motivation: Customers using the OpenAI-compatible Responses endpoints reported two classes of issues in high-concurrency streaming scenarios: (1) reassembled chunks occasionally produce malformed JSON for structured outputs when fragments arrive out of order, and (2) tool/function-call handshakes (tool metadata + trigger signals) are sometimes lost when intermediary proxies rewrite streaming frames. This PR introduces a lightweight 'stream sanitizer' in the OpenAI-bridge layer and a small protocol handshake for tool/function calls to ensure deterministic seed passthrough and opaque metadata forwarding across the bridge.

What this does (single-line summary): adds stable chunk framing/sequence validation, emits tool-handshake events to guarantee toolcall integrity, and forwards client-supplied seed/determinism and arbitrary metadata through the bridge without mutation.

Key changes (design notes): - Stream sanitizer: attaches sequence ids and checksums to streaming frame envelopes within the bridge. Frames that fail validation trigger a deterministic re-request path (soft-retry) or out-of-order buffering with a bounded window (configurable via runtime flag STREAM_SANITIZER_WINDOW_MS). This reduces JSON reassembly errors for structured outputs. - Toolcall handshake: introduces a brief "tool-ready" / "tool-accept" event pair in the streaming protocol used only between bridge and runtime; this is backward-compatible because clients that do not implement the new events will still receive final toolcall events (handshake is honored internally). - Seed & determinism passthrough: any incoming seed/rng_hint fields from OpenAI-style requests are preserved in the request context and propagated to the runtime and any downstream model variants. We add an explicit metadata header (X-Redwood-Rng-Hint) in the bridge-to-runtime path. - Metadata passthrough: arbitrary top-level request metadata is now passed through the bridge unchanged (we treat it as opaque key:value pairs and log a sanitized subset for observability). - Structured output preservation: the sanitizer treats codeblock/JSON tokens specially (preserve token boundaries when possible) and validates JSON well-formedness at reassembly time; if reassembly fails we emit a stable error object that clients can detect and optionally request a fallback sync response.

Compatibility & rollout: - Feature guarded behind a runtime config flag (enabled-by-default in staging, opt-in on older Dedicated stacks). - Backward compatibility: bridge will not drop frames for older clients; it falls back to streaming passthrough if the client signals legacy compatibility header (X-Redwood-Legacy-Resp). - Migration: docs/compatibility/resp-streaming-migration.md added to the docs site; SDKs updated to expose the new seed passthrough header in Python/TS.

Testing & validation: - Unit tests for envelope framing and checksum validation (bridge tests). - Integration tests: end-to-end toolcall flows including a mock external tool and JSON-structured outputs. - Load/perf: perf-canary run included; sanitizer added ~1.8% p99 latency in worst-case synthetic fragmentation but eliminated ~95% of JSON reassembly failures. - Canary plan: staged rollout: canary -> region -> global over 72h with automated rollback on error-rate threshold (see rollout section in description).

Checklist: - [x] Add stream sanitizer implementation and tests - [x] Implement tool-handshake events and adapters - [x] Propagate rng/seed hints through bridge -> runtime - [x] Add docs and migration guide - [x] Update Python/TS SDK headers to expose passthrough hint - [x] Canary and perf runs completed

Merge notes: squash merge to preserve a single logical change. See release notes at the bottom for customer-facing summary.
Samuel Irving: Can you clarify how the bounded buffer window prevents head-of-line blocking under very high fragmentation? If the window is too large we risk memory blowup.
Author (Anya Patel): Buffer window is strictly bounded and measured in ms; we also limit per-client buffer size. Added config STREAM_SANITIZER_MAX_FRAMES to avoid OOM; added tests in stream_sanitizer_test.go to simulate pathological fragmentation.
Renee Cho: LGTMed overall. Please add a small migration note for Dedicated customers so they can opt-out during upgrade.
Author (Anya Patel): Added docs/compatibility/resp-streaming-migration.md and a short section in release_notes. Also wired in config toggle for Dedicated upgrades.

Context: Console needs a single, tenancy-safe API to render SIEM Audit Export health (lag, last success, last error) for the beta cohort. Exporter already emits metrics and maintains checkpoints, but Console cannot safely query Prometheus and we don’t want to expose exporter internals directly. This PR adds a control-plane endpoint that returns a per-tenant summary derived from exporter status + persisted checkpoints, with short TTL caching to protect the exporter/control plane from noisy UI refreshes. What’s in this PR: (1) New endpoint: GET /v1/audit-exports/status (feature-flagged; requires audit_exports.status:read) that returns: overall enabled/paused state, export_lag_seconds, last_success_at, last_attempt_at, last_error (normalized code + safe message), and per-destination health (adapter type + last_success/last_error). (2) Tenancy + RBAC checks: scope is derived from the caller’s workspace/tenant in auth context; optional workspace_id param is validated to belong to the tenant; rejects cross-tenant reads even for org admins; permission gate matches the new RBAC bundle work (view status but not secrets). (3) Caching: in-process cache keyed by (tenant_id, workspace_id) with TTL=15s and jitter; cache entries are invalidated on export config updates (create/update/delete/rotate) via existing config change event bus hook; adds a circuit-breaker style fallback that returns cached (stale=true) for up to 2 minutes if exporter status fetch is timing out (to keep Console responsive during downstream incidents). (4) Status aggregation logic: control plane queries exporter “/internal/status” endpoint via service auth (mTLS) and merges with checkpoint rows in control plane DB (audit_export_checkpoints) to compute lag (now - last_checkpoint_event_ts) and to avoid reporting lag=0 when exporter is down but checkpoints are old. (5) Safe error normalization: adapter error strings are mapped to a small enum set (AUTH_FAILED, DEST_RATE_LIMITED, DEST_UNREACHABLE, DEST_FORBIDDEN, CONFIG_INVALID, INTERNAL) and messages are truncated/redacted to avoid leaking tokens/URLs; destination hostnames are omitted for Splunk/Datadog adapters and only S3 bucket ARN prefix is shown. (6) Tests + docs: unit tests for tenancy/RBAC, lag computation, stale-cache fallback, and redaction; added OpenAPI schema + example response; added Console integration notes in /docs/internal/console/audit-export-status.md. API response example (shape only): {"workspace_id":"ws_...","enabled":true,"paused":false,"export_lag_seconds":42,"last_success_at":"2025-04-15T21:03:11Z","last_attempt_at":"2025-04-15T21:03:41Z","last_error":{"code":"DEST_RATE_LIMITED","message":"downstream throttling (429)"},"destinations":[{"id":"dest_...","type":"splunk_hec","health":"degraded","last_success_at":"...","last_error":{"code":"DEST_RATE_LIMITED","message":"..."}}],"stale":false}. Rollout / gating: endpoint is behind feature flag audit_export.status_endpoint (tenant allowlist continues to be managed by the existing beta allowlist). Console will use this endpoint only when audit_export.beta_enabled is true, otherwise the UI remains hidden. Observability: added metrics redwood_control_plane_audit_export_status_cache_hits_total, ..._misses_total, ..._fetch_latency_ms, ..._stale_served_total; added structured logs with request_id, tenant_id, workspace_id (hashed), and result (ok/stale/error). Notes for SRE: exporter status fetch has a 750ms timeout with 2 retries (full jitter backoff) and will not page on failure by itself; paging continues to be based on exporter lag SLO, not UI status. Security considerations: no secrets are returned; error normalization redacts known token patterns and strips querystrings from URLs; tenancy guardrails prevent enumerating destination IDs across workspaces. Follow-ups (not in this PR): (a) Console: wire status endpoint into the settings page (DES-311/ENG-5177), (b) Status history: store time series for “last 24h failures” (out of beta scope), (c) Private deployments: status fetch mechanism differs (no direct exporter endpoint) and will be handled in ENG-5202. Screenshots: N/A (API-only).
Chloe Martin (Console backend) - 2025-04-11: Can we guarantee this endpoint is cheap enough for the UI polling cadence? Console currently refreshes settings pages ~every 10s when open. Also, can you include a boolean that makes it easy to show 'data may be stale' without parsing timestamps?
Benji Okafor - 2025-04-11: Added in-process cache TTL=15s (with jitter) keyed per tenant/workspace, plus stale=true flag when we serve cached due to exporter timeouts. Also added cache invalidation on config update events so UI reflects changes quickly even with TTL.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (Auth/RBAC) - 2025-04-12: Please ensure org-level admins can’t use workspace_id to enumerate other workspaces under a tenant unless they have the correct scope. Also want confirmation that we’re not leaking hostnames or tokens in error messages.
Benji Okafor - 2025-04-12: Updated guard to require either (a) caller is scoped to the workspace, or (b) caller has workspace:read on that workspace via RBAC membership; otherwise 404. Added strict redaction/normalization: removes URLs/querystrings, truncates messages, and masks token-like substrings; also removed Splunk/Datadog hostnames from response fields.
Logan Wright (Telemetry) - 2025-04-13: Metric names look good; please cap label cardinality. Avoid raw workspace_id in labels. Also can we add a metric for 'stale served' to track exporter timeouts impacting UI?
Benji Okafor - 2025-04-13: Done. Metrics do not include workspace_id; only 'result' label (ok/stale/error) and adapter_type. Added redwood_control_plane_audit_export_status_stale_served_total and fetch latency histogram.
Rafael Mendes (SRE) - 2025-04-15: Timeout/retry settings: make sure we don’t amplify exporter issues with retries across many tenants. Also: if exporter is down, do we return 5xx and spam Console?
Benji Okafor - 2025-04-15: Set exporter call timeout to 750ms with 2 retries but capped by overall 2s budget and cache-first behavior; in failure path we serve stale cached response (stale=true) for up to 2 minutes if available; otherwise return 503 with a safe error. This should reduce UI-induced load during incidents.
