Adds a small orchestration service and CLI to synthesize tenant-level cost posture defaults and a minibatch inspector that samples live traffic to validate batch/cache/quant profiles against unit-econ targets. Motivation: customers repeatedly hit suboptimal defaults for low-volume tenants and edge workloads; we need a lightweight automation loop that recommends safe defaults and validates them against production signals before wide rollout. This change introduces: 1) cost-posture-orch service (golang) that compiles tenant signals into prioritized profile suggestions; 2) minibatch-inspector (python) that pulls sampled traces and computes per-tenant unit-econ deltas for candidate batch/cache/quant presets; 3) a small decision model and rules engine (~30 rules) used to flag unsafe recommendations; 4) CLI 'rwcpo' to run dry-runs and export suggested presets as YAML; 5) telemetry hooks and dashboards for the unit-econ probe. Includes migration path and safety: suggestions are only written to a staging namespace by default; rollout requires a separate apply step or an automated canary via the console. Testing: unit tests for rules and decision graph, integration tests against a local runtime shim, and an e2e smoke harness used in CI. Rollout: staged canary (10 tenants) for 48 hours, monitor unit-econ delta < 5% and tail latency within SLOs. Checklist: ensure infra team creates secrets for sampling, update ops runbooks, inform SRE on dashboards. Related: ENG-4821 tracks improvement to tenant defaults; SUP-1347 is a customer incident that motivated the work.
Riley Chen: Suggest decoupling the scoring from concrete hardware assumptions; favor normalized cost units. Can you add a normalization layer?
Asha Patel: Reply: added cost-normalizer in commit b3d9c7a; updated tests to cover AMX and non-AMX instances.
Marcus Li: Perf note: the inspector's sampling loop could spike worker threads under very high tenant cardinality. Recommend a bounded worker pool or backpressure.
Asha Patel: Reply: implemented worker pool and adaptive backoff in c7d12f4; added integration test to validate max concurrency.
Priya Nair: Security: ensure sampled traces redact PII and secrets. Please confirm sanitizer behavior.
Asha Patel: Reply: minibatch-inspector now runs the redaction sanitizer and emits only aggregated metrics by default; see tools/minibatch-inspector/samplers/README for config.
Marcus Li: Approve after minor nits fixed.
Riley Chen: Approved.
Adds 'cost-posture-orch' service and 'minibatch-inspector' tool; introduces tenant suggestion YAML export and unit-econ telemetry for staged rollouts; no user-facing API changes
payload.title: Introduce cost posture orchestrator and minibatch inspector

Summary: Adds the initial Console metering sanity dashboard (v1) plus backend endpoints to power tiles and drilldowns. This is intended for Finance/RevOps + Telemetry/SRE use during the 2026Q1 metering hardening push. Motivation: We currently rely on ad-hoc SQL + screenshots to validate that usage events reconcile to the billing ledger and to spot data-quality regressions (late-arriving events, missing dimensions, duplicate/idempotency failures). This PR makes the checks visible, reviewable, and consistent across teams, and lays the groundwork for alert links/runbooks (ENG-4421 / pr-27574). Scope (v1): (1) Backend: /console/api/metering-sanity/* endpoints that query the reconciled aggregation tables and return time-series + top-K breakdowns; (2) UI: dashboard page with key tiles and a filter bar (env, time range, account, model, region, meter_type); (3) Drilldowns: click-through to a breakdown table with sample event IDs and links into existing log search (restricted). Included checks/tiles: Freshness: max(event_ingested_at) lag vs now, per pipeline stage (usage_events, usage_rollups, billing_ledger_export). Drift: % difference between usage_rollups and billing_ledger_export (billed_tokens, requests, embeddings_units) with thresholds and a 7d sparkline. Duplicates/idempotency: duplicate_event_rate (by event_id + dedupe_key), and “late_duplicate_rate” (dupes arriving > 6h after first seen). Null / missing dimensions: null_rate for account_id, model_id, region, meter_version, cache_hit fields. Outliers: p99 tokens/request and extreme spend spikes (top accounts) to help catch obvious blowups. Guardrails & access: This is Console-internal and requires billing-data entitlement. The endpoints are gated behind RBAC permission console.billing.read and are audit logged (route + filter set). No customer-facing changes in this PR. Data sources: Reads from snowflake shared views (billing_recon.usage_rollups_hourly_v1, billing_recon.ledger_rollups_hourly_v1) produced by the reconciliation export pipeline. The queries are constrained by time range and capped breakdown sizes. Performance: All endpoints are aggregated; drilldowns fetch at most 200 rows and require account filter to prevent broad scans. Notes: Thresholds displayed are initial defaults; tuning will happen with ENG-SRE as we get real-world usage/noise. Code overview (high level): Backend: console-server/src/routes/metering_sanity.ts (new), console-server/src/services/metering_sanity/*.ts (new), console-server/src/auth/permissions.ts (adds console.billing.read), console-server/src/audit/audit_log.ts (logs new routes). Frontend: console-web/src/pages/metering/SanityDashboard.tsx (new), console-web/src/components/metering/SanityTiles.tsx (new), console-web/src/components/metering/BreakdownTable.tsx (new), console-web/src/hooks/useMeteringSanity.ts (new). Schema: uses existing rollup columns; no schema migrations in this PR. Illustrative response payload (trimmed): GET /console/api/metering-sanity/drift?start=...&end=... {"series":[{"ts":"2026-02-20T14:00:00Z","usage_billed_tokens": 1234567,"ledger_billed_tokens": 1239988,"drift_pct": -0.44}],"top_dimensions":[{"dimension":"region","key":"us-east-1","drift_pct":-0.12}]} (actual response is typed and includes units + confidence flags). Rollout: Hidden behind feature flag console_metering_sanity_v1. Enabled for: Finance (billing) group, RevOps, Telemetry/SRE on-call, and Product Ops. Follow-ups: (1) Wire alert annotations + runbook links (pr-27574), (2) Add dedicated GPU-seconds view (pending pr-27492/ENG-4426), (3) Add incident timeline markers from status page/incident tool, (4) Add “shadow billing compare” toggle when available (pr-27518). Testing: Unit tests for query builders + RBAC; UI tests for tile rendering and drilldown navigation; manual verification against known discrepancy samples from Feb audit (restricted).
Mei Lin (review): Love that this is finally in Console. Two concerns: (1) Drift math should be explicit about denominator (ledger vs usage), and (2) the drilldown endpoint can be called without account_id which could cause a large scan. Can we require at least one of account_id or model_id? Aisha Bello (author): Good catch. Updated drift series to include drift_denominator=ledger and changed label copy to “(usage - ledger) / ledger”. For drilldown, I added server-side validation: require account_id OR (model_id AND region) and cap time range to 72h if account_id missing. Also added a warning banner in UI when using non-account drilldown. Caleb Johnson (review): Query patterns look ok, but Snowflake warehouse usage can spike if someone sets 30d range with breakdown=account. Please add hard limits to topK and ensure we use the hourly rollup tables only. Aisha Bello (author): Added hard caps: max_range_days=14 for any request; max_topk=50; breakdown=account requires account filter (so top accounts tile uses precomputed “top_spend_accounts_hourly” view). Confirmed all endpoints only touch billing_recon.* hourly rollups. Logan Wright (review): RBAC looks right, but audit log should include whether the request included account_id (sensitive) and time range. Also we should log the feature flag state so we can prove who had access when. Aisha Bello (author): Updated audit log payload to include time_range_hours, has_account_filter=true/false, and feature_flag=console_metering_sanity_v1. Nadia Rahman (review): UI copy: please avoid “double billed” language; call it “duplicate usage events” and note that ledger is the billing source of truth. Also in drift tile, add a tooltip that known late-arriving events can temporarily create negative drift. Aisha Bello (author): Updated copy per spec language. Added tooltip and an “incomplete window” badge when end_ts is within ingestion_lag_slo. Ethan Park (review): Looks good. One more request: move permission name from console.billing.read to console.metering_sanity.read so it’s scoped. Aisha Bello (author): I’d prefer to keep it under billing since data is still billing-grade and we’re sharing the same entitlement group. Compromise: added new permission console.metering_sanity.read but it aliases the billing group for now; we can split later. Ethan Park (review): Works for me. Approved. Approvals: Mei Lin (approved), Caleb Johnson (approved), Logan Wright (approved), Nadia Rahman (approved), Ethan Park (approved).
Internal-only Console dashboard for metering sanity checks (freshness, drift vs ledger, duplicates, null dimensions) with drilldowns by account/model/region and incident annotations.
payload.title: Console: Metering sanity dashboard v1 (API + UI + drilldowns)

TL;DR: Reduce presubmit feedback time by moving long-running integration tests into a quarantined 'longtest' lane (scheduled + optional on-demand) and add a lightweight 'toolchain-shadow' loader that pre-warms minimal toolchains for fastlint/fastunit runs. This PR splits the heavy integration test surface from the primary presubmit lanes, introduces a quarantine lane with clear opt-in and opt-out paths, and adds a small toolchain preloader to reduce cold-start latency for lint/test runners. Motivation: our median PR CI time is dominated by a small set of longtests that run on a minority of changes; they add noise and slow down iteration for common changes. The quarantine lane keeps those tests running continuously (nightly and on-demand) and surfaces failures as blocking via a policy instead of always gating merges. The toolchain-shadow loader addresses long setup time that inflates all presubmit jobs (node/rust/python virtualenvs). Summary of changes: 1) workflows/ci/presubmit.yml: introduce new job matrix that excludes longtest tags by default; add new logical lane longtest-quarantine that runs nightly and via workflow_dispatch with concurrency control; updated job annotations for faster cache warm. 2) .ci/toolchain-shadow/: add a small Go-based preloader (shadow-loader) that creates minimal cached toolchain artifacts (node_modules skeletons, rust sysroot partial cache, pip wheel index snapshot) and uploads them to the runner cache service; includes a README and unit tests. 3) scripts/ci/mark_longtests.py: small utility to label tests for quarantine based on file paths and patterns. 4) Makefile targets: ci-shadow-prep, ci-longtest-run. 5) docs/ci/README.md: added operational runbook for quarantined lane, SLAs, and troubleshooting. Design notes: - Quarantine lane semantics: tests marked with [longtest] or matching patterns in mark_longtests are excluded from the fast presubmit lane. Quarantine runs nightly at 02:00 UTC and on-demand via the new workflow_dispatch endpoint. Failed quarantine runs are reported to a dedicated channel and create an alert in Ops if a regression trend is detected. - Opt-in gating: teams can opt to re-run longtests on-demand in the PR (button to trigger) for fast validation; gating rules allow a team-level override for critical branches. - Toolchain-shadow loader: written in Go for a small, hermetic binary that runs in the CI environment with a tiny memory footprint; it prefetches packages, lays out a minimal module graph, and populates remote runner cache with a labeled snapshot. The loader is intentionally conservative — it only prefetches the artifacts proven to reduce setup time for 95% of jobs. Migration plan: 1) Roll out in canary: enable for a subset of repos (sdk-python, redwood-examples) for one week. 2) Observe cache hit rate, presubmit median latency, and quarantine failure volume. 3) Expand to core repo if signals are positive. Backout plan: rollback is removing exclusion rule from presubmit.yml and disabling the longtest-quarantine workflow; shadow snapshots are TTLed and can be disabled from runner cache service. Risk assessment: - Flaky longtests could increase noise in the quarantine lane but won't immediately block merges. We added a regression detector to elevate recurring failures. - Mis-tagging tests could cause regressions; mark_longtests.py includes a dry-run mode and we will run it across the repo in a follow-up PR that documents the suggested tags. Release notes: "Introduce quarantined longtest lane and toolchain-shadow preloader to speed up presubmit feedback; admins can opt into early rollout." Checklist: - [x] Add quarantine workflow and matrix exclusion - [x] Add toolchain-shadow loader + unit tests - [x] Add make targets and scripts - [x] Add docs and runbook - [x] Run canary in sdk-python and redwood-examples - [x] Post rollout notes to #ci-status Commits (high level): - init: add toolchain-shadow loader skeleton and go.mod - ci: add presubmit exclusion and longtest-quarantine workflow - infra: add mark_longtests utility and wiring - docs: ci runbook for quarantine lane - tests: unit tests for shadow loader and mark_longtests - chore: Makefile targets for ci-shadow-prep and ci-longtest-run CI summary: Initial run had a single flaky integration test failure in the quarantine lane (flaky-db-restore). Re-ran the quarantine job after quarantine infra patch; overall presubmit lanes now consistently finish ~34% faster in canary repos. Full CI matrix: - build (linux/amd64) — pass - unit tests — pass - lint — pass - integration-longtests (quarantine) — pass after re-run - smoke-nightly — pass - deploy-sim — pass Changed files (high level list): - .github/workflows/presubmit.yml - .github/workflows/longtest-quarantine.yml - .ci/toolchain-shadow/loader/main.go - .ci/toolchain-shadow/README.md - scripts/ci/mark_longtests.py - Makefile (added ci-shadow-prep, ci-longtest-run) - docs/ci/README.md - tools/cache/runner-cache-config.yaml (small TTL changes) - tests/shadow_loader_test.go - tests/mark_longtests_test.py - .ci/ci-config.yaml - README.md Impact metrics observed in canary (sdk-python, redwood-examples): - median presubmit time: 18m -> 12m (34% reduction) - median setup time (toolchain): 5m -> 2m (60% reduction) - nightly longtest failure rate: 0.9% -> 1.2% (expected slight bump during quarantine seeding) Review thread highlights: - Mateo Ruiz: "Looks good overall. Please add telemetry for shadow snapshot hit/miss and a small CLI switch to force a dry-run mode." (author) Aisha: "Added telemetry hooks and --dry-run flag in loader; updated README with instrumentation notes." - Priya Singh: "Can we ensure opt-out for repos with sensitive data or custom bootstraps? Also suggest adding a label for quarantined test runs." Aisha: "Added repo opt-out support via .ci/ci-config.yaml and quarantine-run label. Ran opt-out on redwood-private-installer in canary." - Liam O'Connor: "Please include a short migration script to tag current longtests so the initial rollout is predictable." Aisha: "Included mark_longtests.py and a one-off run in CI for initial tagging; will follow up with an audit PR to list tags." Merge details: merged by Mateo Ruiz on 2026-02-24 using squash merge. Follow-ups: - ENG-7842: audit longtest tag coverage across monorepo - ENG-7901: add quarantine regression detector enhancement to notify on trending failures - small perf ticket: evaluate shadow loader TTL policy for runner cache

Summary: Adds a tenant-aware 'blueprint' generator that emits recommended batching, cache, and quantization defaults per tenant profile. Includes a compact set of quantization presets (q4_0/q4_1-like variants tuned for throughput on V100/A100/Inferentia), a CLI preview command (rwctl econ preview) for estimating unit economics, and telemetry hooks so Optimize and Console can show projected cost/latency tradeoffs. Motivation: Many customers want safe, opinionated defaults that reduce inference cost without manual tuning. Existing autotuners were global; this change lets us target tenant workload shape and SLOs while retaining runtime safety fallbacks. Design/what changed: - pkg/econ/blueprint.go: core blueprint generator and policy combinator (tenant SLOs, request size distribution, preferred latency-cost tradeoff). - pkg/econ/profiles/compact/ : three compact quant profiles (conservative, balanced, aggressive) expressed in YAML, with metadata for runtime compatibility. - runtime/compat/fallbacks.go: deterministic compatibility checker and automatic fallback to higher-precision profile when kernel support is missing. - cmd/rwctl/econ_preview.go: CLI to load a tenant sample, apply a blueprint, and output estimated unit-econ table (tokens/second, p99 latency, cost-per-1M tokens). - observability/telemetry/blueprint_events.go: events for blueprint proposals, applied profiles, and regression signals. - docs/operational/econ-blueprints.md: operational runbook and examples for Dedicated/Private customers. - tests/*: unit and integration tests that validate blueprint generation across synthetic tenant profiles, and e2e smoke that exercises rwctl preview. Commits: - 9 commits (feature scaffolding, profile YAMLs, runtime fallback integration, CLI and tests, docs). High-level commit summary: 1) scaffold econ blueprint package; 2) add compact quant profiles and metadata; 3) implement runtime compatibility/fallback logic; 4) implement rwctl preview with sample loaders; 5) telemetry + metrics + docs; 6) add unit and integration tests; 7) fix test flakiness and add mock kernel table; 8) address reviewer feedback on race conditions; 9) final cleanup and squash. Files changed (high level): - pkg/econ/blueprint.go - pkg/econ/profiles/compact/balanced.yaml - pkg/econ/profiles/compact/conservative.yaml - pkg/econ/profiles/compact/aggressive.yaml - runtime/compat/fallbacks.go - cmd/rwctl/econ_preview.go - observability/telemetry/blueprint_events.go - docs/operational/econ-blueprints.md - tests/econ/blueprint_test.go - tests/e2e/rwctl_preview_integration_test.go - internal/telemetry/mappers.go - examples/tenant_samples/* Review conversation: - Ethan Park (reviewer): "Nice shape overall. A couple of requests: 1) make the runtime fallback deterministic for concurrent lookups, 2) add a short-circuit when tenant has explicit quant ban, and 3) add a basic perf microbenchmark to track p99 impact." - Author (Sofia): "Thanks Ethan — addressed determinism by introducing a per-model compatibilityCache and added a tenant-level explicit_quant_ban flag. Added a microbenchmark harness under tests/bench/ and wired CI to run a minimal iteration." - Maya Singh (reviewer): "We need clearer UX for rwctl preview output; add a CSV output and reduce noise for default output." - Author: "Added --format csv and compact table mode. Included an example in docs and updated integration test to assert CSV columns." - Jonas Becker (reviewer): "Telemetry events look good; ensure we don't log tenant PII. Also please add a schema version to profiles so future rollouts are safe." - Author: "Stripped PII from events and incremented profile metadata with schema_version: 'v1'." - Diffs after review: race fix in runtime/compat/fallbacks.go, added explicit_quant_ban checks in blueprint generator, CSV output flag for CLI, microbench harness, and docs update. CI: - build: passed - unit tests: passed (pkg/econ unit suite) - integration tests: passed (rwctl preview integration against mock runtime) - lint: passed (go vet/gofmt/golint) - bench-smoke: passed (quick run) Merge: Squash and merge on 2026-03-01 by Maya Singh. Post-merge actions: - Scheduled a small Canary rollout to Dedicated region us-west-2 for two tenants with low-risk traffic; monitoring configured in Console dashboard sample. - Added a telemetry alert that fires if projected cost savings exceed 35% but measured p99 degrades >10%. Backwards compatibility & safety: - No breaking API changes to public inference endpoints. The blueprint generator produces suggestions only; operators must opt-in to apply. - Runtime fallback ensures that if a compact quant profile cannot be serviced on chosen hardware, we fall back to a safe higher-precision profile at runtime. Tests & verification: - Unit coverage added for blueprint combinator logic, fallback determinism, and explicit_quant_ban path. - Integration tests cover rwctl preview end-to-end and CSV export. - Bench harness provides data for future perf regressions and is wired to CI as a minimal smoke run. Operational notes: - Docs + runbook include step-by-step for enabling tenant auto-apply, previewing changes with rwctl, and rolling out via Canary. - Recommend enabling blueprint telemetry in staging for at least one week before enabling auto-apply for a tenant. Known limitations & follow-ups: - Compact quant profiles are tuned for a subset of hardware; additional tuning needed for upcoming H100 kernels (ENG-12902). - We purposely left online autotune disabled; the generator outputs blueprints and an optional manual apply to reduce risk. - Follow-up PR planned to add a UI flow in Console to preview/approve blueprints per tenant (ENG-13044). Overall impact: This PR reduces the friction of adopting cost-savvy defaults by providing tenant-aware recommendations, safe fallbacks, and a lightweight preview experience for operators.
- Add tenant-aware cost blueprint generator (safe defaults for batching/caching)
- Add compact quantization profile library with runtime fallbacks
- New rwctl econ preview command to simulate unit-econ impact per tenant
- Observability integration: blueprint telemetry and regression hooks

Summary: This PR adds the first cut of retention policy management to the control plane: CRUD endpoints, request/response types, validation rules, and audit log events for all policy mutations. This unblocks wiring retention enforcement in downstream stores and enables the compliance reporting pack to export tenant retention configuration.

Context: As part of the Retention controls + compliance reporting pack project (ENG-18420 / PM-842), we need a durable, auditable policy object that can be referenced by logging/telemetry subsystems. Policy evaluation and caching will be layered in a follow-up PR (see pr-28427) but the API surface and auditability need to land first so dependent teams can integrate.

What’s included: (1) RetentionPolicy model + persistence in control-plane DB (tenant-scoped, immutable id, mutable spec). (2) REST endpoints: POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention-policies, GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention-policies/{policy_id}, PATCH /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention-policies/{policy_id}, DELETE /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention-policies/{policy_id}, GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention-policies (with basic filtering/pagination). (3) Validation: name length/charset, description length, per-data-class TTL bounds (coarse bounds for v1; detailed tier-aware bounds and disabled-logging interactions will be tightened in pr-28455 + schema doc update), consistency checks (e.g., legal_hold cannot be set via this API), and rejection of unknown data classes. (4) Audit trail: emits audit events for create/update/delete with actor, tenant, policy_id, diff summary, and request correlation id; ensures PATCH includes an explicit field mask so the audit diff is stable. (5) RBAC: endpoints require SECURITY_ADMIN or PLATFORM_ADMIN for tenant; read/list also permitted for AUDITOR role (tenant-scoped) to support evidence workflows.

Not included / follow-ups: (a) Policy evaluation and precedence rules (pr-28427). (b) Attaching policies to tenant logging config and migration/back-compat (pr-28455). (c) Console UI surfaces (DES-912). (d) Export endpoint and change history (pr-28526).

API shape notes: Spec is modeled as a map keyed by data_class (request_logs, audit_logs, traces, metrics, artifacts) with {ttl_days, purge_mode}. For now purge_mode is accepted but only 'hard_delete' is supported; values are validated and stored so we don’t break clients as we add modes. PATCH supports partial updates for name/description/spec; updates are last-write-wins but include an optimistic concurrency token (etag) returned on GET; clients may send If-Match to avoid overwrites.

Security/Compliance: All mutation endpoints log an audit event; we intentionally do not allow setting legal hold via this API (hold is a separate workflow with approvals). Payloads are validated to avoid accidentally allowing unbounded retention; server enforces max TTL bounds even if client is compromised.

Testing: Added unit tests for request validation, RBAC gates, etag behavior, and audit event emission. Added integration-ish tests using the in-memory DB harness for CRUD lifecycle and pagination. Manually tested using curl against dev control plane (notes in commit message).

Rollout: Safe to merge behind feature flag retention_policy_service.enabled (default off in production). The API routes are registered only when flag is on; migrations are included but do not affect existing tables. We will enable flag in staging once pr-28427 is merged so evaluators can start consuming these objects.

Screenshots/Docs: None (API-only). Docs update tracked in ENG-18460.

Open questions: (1) Tier-aware TTL min/max bounds: in this PR we use conservative global bounds; Product/Security to confirm exact defaults per Hosted/Dedicated/Private in the schema doc. (2) Data class naming: we aligned on audit_logs vs request_logs based on Security thread; confirm final canonical list before public docs.
Ethan Park: Can we avoid allowing ttl_days=0? We should treat that as invalid rather than “disabled retention”. Author (Benji): Agreed. Updated validation to require ttl_days >= 1 and added explicit 'logging disabled' handling as a separate concern for tenant logging config (follow-up in pr-28455). Added tests.

Marcus Lin: Audit events need to include request_id/correlation_id; also please ensure we don’t accidentally log full policy spec in the event payload (could contain future fields). Author: Added correlation_id, and changed the audit payload to include a redacted summary + stable diff (field mask + old/new ttl_days only). Spec is stored in DB; audit log now contains metadata and a minimal diff.

Jordan Lee: PATCH should require a field mask or we’ll get ambiguous diffs and accidental overwrites. Author: Implemented field_mask on PATCH, required unless If-Match is provided with full replacement semantics. Updated controller and tests.

Chloe Martin: For the Console, list endpoint needs pagination with stable ordering. Right now it sorts by created_at desc; can we order by (created_at, id) for determinism? Author: Updated list query ordering and pagination cursor to include both fields.

CI note: First run failed lint due to unused enum in retention_policy_validation.ts; removed and reran.

Approvals: Ethan Park approved after changes. Marcus Lin approved after audit payload tweaks. Jordan Lee approved after field mask changes. Chloe Martin approved after pagination fix.

Merge: Squash merged to main.
Internal: introduces tenant-scoped retention policy CRUD APIs (create/read/update/delete/list) with server-side validation and audit trail entries; no customer-facing UI changes in this PR.

Motivation: We continue to see tail latency and memory pressure in high-concurrency KV workloads due to small-object fragmentation and episodic spill bursts when many small entries are freed/rewritten. This PR implements two complementary runtime changes: 1) a lightweight background microcompaction that opportunistically coalesces adjacent small free slots into larger free ranges, reducing fragmentation and improving allocator fit behavior; 2) a stepped evictor/pager that applies graduated spillback pressure instead of an immediate all-or-nothing spill when the spill queue grows. Both changes are intended to reduce the frequency and magnitude of on-disk spillover events while keeping P99 latency stable.

Summary of changes (single-line list): - new runtime module src/runtime/kv/microcompact.rs implementing a compact-on-threshold micropass - refactor of evictor into src/runtime/kv/evictor.rs with SteppedEvictor strategy and spill throttling knobs - allocator heuristics: tune slab bin coalescing and introduce per-tenant retention windows - new metrics and telemetry hooks to measure compaction runs, reclaimed_bytes, spill_throttle_events - integration tests and microbench harness: tests/kv/fragmentation_sim.py, bench/kv/microcompact_bench.rs - docs: docs/kv/pager-tuning.md with recommended settings and notes on tradeoffs

Checklist: - [x] Benchmark microbench and internal perf harness (bench results in PR comment) - [x] Unit & integration tests added - [x] Telemetry (metrics + tracing) added - [x] Docs for ops: pager-tuning.md - [x] Reviewed and approved by SRE and runtime leads

Commits (high level): ["a1b2c3d - implement microcompact pass and unit tests","b2c3d4e - implement stepped evictor with throttle state machine","c3d4e5f - expose metrics and tracing spans for compaction","d4e5f6a - perf tune thresholds and add linear ticket references","e5f6a7b - docs: pager tuning and rollout notes"]

Changed areas (high level, small snippets included where helpful): [
  "src/runtime/kv/microcompact.rs - new: lightweight compaction pass that iterates free runs and performs coalesce_if_adjacent(). Snippet: 'if run.length <= micro_threshold { try_coalesce(run) }'",
  "src/runtime/kv/evictor.rs - refactor and new SteppedEvictor state machine (idle -> warn -> throttle -> spill). Snippet: 'match state { State::Warn => increase_backpressure(), State::Throttle => schedule_spill_rate(limit) }'",
  "src/runtime/kv/allocator.rs - adjust slab bin sizing and per-tenant retention windows to avoid hot churn on small objects",
  "bench/kv/microcompact_bench.rs - synthetic workload with 70% small-object churn to validate P99 impact",
  "tests/kv/fragmentation_sim.py - fuzz harness for allocation/free patterns, asserts on reclaimed bytes and spill counts",
  "docs/kv/pager-tuning.md - ops guidance and recommended defaults for steady vs bursty workloads"
]

Design notes and rationale: The microcompactor is intentionally conservative: it runs on a dedicated low-priority executor and limits compaction work by reclaimed-bytes-per-second so it does not interfere with latency-sensitive token generation. The stepped evictor introduces an intermediate 'throttle' level where we slow down incoming allocation admission and rate-limit background spill threads rather than immediately launching large spill jobs. This reduces IO bursts and results in smaller, more frequent spill batches which our benchmarks indicate yields lower tail latency and better average throughput for mixed-size requests.

Benchmarks (summary): Using bench harness with 200 concurrent connections and a 70% small-write churn workload, we observed: - 18% reduction in mean mem-usage under steady load - 34% reduction in spill bytes during short bursts (2-10s) - 12% improvement in P99 latency for KV-heavy paths (end-to-end generation unaffected) Full bench log attached in comment 'bench-log-88766.txt'.

Review conversation (high level): - Jonah Li (reviewer): "Can the microcompaction lead to pathological CPU usage under sustained free churn?" - Aisha (author): "We cap compactor work to 50MB/s by default and it yields negligible CPU in our perf runs; added metric runtime.kv.microcompact.cpu_ms to monitor." - Priya Suresh: "Need clear ops knobs per cluster (steady vs bursty); recommend adding a chart and default override per-pool." - Aisha: "Added docs/kv/pager-tuning.md with per-pool recommendations and a Grafana dashboard template." - Marco D'Angelo: "Please sanity-check cross-tenant fairness when retention windows are enabled." - Aisha: "Retention windows are tenant-scoped and opt-in; added tests to ensure tenant A's compaction does not bump tenant B's eviction priority."

CI notes: One flaky test (kv::integration::evictor_race) failed on first run due to a test harness timing assumption; test was made resilient and CI re-ran. Final CI status: all checks passed; new metrics compilation warnings fixed.

Rollout and ops: This change is behind two feature flags: runtime.kv.microcompact.enabled (default: on) and runtime.kv.evictor.stepped_enabled (default: on for dedicated and private; off for hosted until staged rollout). Ops should watch metrics: runtime.kv.reclaimed_bytes, runtime.kv.spill_throttle_events, runtime.kv.spill_bytes, and runtime.kv.microcompact.cpu_ms. Docs include recommended defaults and a migration path for clusters with very large slab sizes.

Merge: Squash-merged to main. Migration notes included in docs/kv/pager-tuning.md.
Jonah Li: Can the microcompaction lead to pathological CPU usage under sustained free churn?
Aisha Moreno: We cap compactor work to 50MB/s by default and it yields negligible CPU in our perf runs; added metric runtime.kv.microcompact.cpu_ms to monitor.
Priya Suresh: Need clear ops knobs per cluster (steady vs bursty); recommend adding a chart and default override per-pool.
Aisha Moreno: Added docs/kv/pager-tuning.md with per-pool recommendations and a Grafana dashboard template.
Marco D'Angelo: Please sanity-check cross-tenant fairness when retention windows are enabled.
Aisha Moreno: Retention windows are tenant-scoped and opt-in; added tests to ensure tenant A's compaction does not bump tenant B's eviction priority.
CI: kv::integration::evictor_race failed initially; updated test harness timing and re-ran CI.
Reduced KV fragmentation and spill bursts by adding microcompaction and an adaptive stepped evictor. Improved P99 under high small-object churn. Ops: see docs/kv/pager-tuning.md for rollout and tuning knobs.
Feature flags: runtime.kv.microcompact.enabled and runtime.kv.evictor.stepped_enabled
Watch metrics: runtime.kv.reclaimed_bytes, runtime.kv.spill_throttle_events, runtime.kv.spill_bytes, runtime.kv.microcompact.cpu_ms
Recommended defaults included in docs/kv/pager-tuning.md; staged rollout for hosted clusters

Adds a declarative AB graph runner and automatic rollback annotation tooling. Backwards compatible with existing promote/canary manifests. New runbook and e2e tests included.
Motivation: enable teams to express A/B experiments as declarative acyclic graphs with explicit transition edges and automated rollback annotations that generate runbook snippets and telemetry links. This PR implements a graph-driven runner that evaluates edges against policy gates (SLOs, cost targets, smoke results) and emits annotated rollback triggers which can be consumed by the operator UI and the abort/autoremediation subsystem. Key goals: reduce imperative rollout scripts, make rollback provenance searchable, and provide autodoc snippets for SRE/playbook. What changed: 1) orchestrator/graph_runner: core evaluator and scheduler for AB graph edges; supports parallel and sequential branches, deterministic cutover semantics, and soft-holdpoints; 2) orchestrator/rollback_annotations: converts policy evaluation results into structured rollback annotations and runbook fragments; 3) manifests: AB graph v1 schema and examples for sessionless and sticky traffic; 4) console: small status UI components to render graph progress and rollback rationale; 5) tests: integration and fuzz tests for edge evaluation and rollback generation; 6) docs: runbook and developer guide with examples and Linear links. Compatibility: existing promote and canary controllers are unchanged; the graph runner is opt-in via an annotation in rollout manifests. Testing: unit coverage added for edge scoring and annotation generation; integration test simulates a failing metric triggering annotated rollback and ensures the merge path and telemetry link are present in generated runbook. Migration notes: no automatic migration required; manifest examples included. Checklist: [x] unit tests [x] integration smoke [x] docs updated [x] runbook snippets generated [x] rollout examples. Rollout plan: merged to main behind feature flag; gradual rollout to staging clusters for two weeks then enable by default for customers opting into A/B graphs. Risks and mitigations: risk of noisy rollbacks when metric thresholds are tight — mitigated by a conservative default threshold, smoothing window, and a dry-run mode that emits but does not act on rollback annotations. Feedback requested on the runbook wording and schema naming.
Elliot Park: 'Can you explain how we guarantee deterministic cutover when edges complete concurrently?' Author: 'We serialize final commit decisions using a quorum step in graph_runner.go; added comment and unit test to validate deterministic winner.' Samir Gupta: 'Need clearer visibility of cost impact per-edge.' Author: 'Added per-edge cost estimate in annotations and console tooltip; see commits b4e5f6a and e1f2a3b.' Lena Ortiz: 'Docs look good but add a short troubleshooting section for false positives.' Author: 'Added troubleshooting subsection and example dry-run command.'
Feature is gated by featureflag 'ab_graph_runner' default disabled. To enable for a cluster: set featureflags.ab_graph_runner=true and apply ab_graph_v1 manifest. Runbook snippets available at /docs/runbooks/ab_graph_rollout.md. Telemetry links include trace id placeholder and can be forwarded to oncall. Monitor rollout.progress and rollout.rollback_triggered metrics.

Motivation: Canary detectors frequently flag regressions during short-lived traffic spikes or scheduled traffic bursts (batch jobs, cron traffic). This PR adds a synthetic burst injection harness to exercise the canary evaluator under controlled short-duration bursts and pairs it with a stability-credit guard that grants temporary credit during verified transient episodes to avoid false-positive rollbacks. Implementation: 1) perf-canary/burst_injector.py implements a configurable synthetic traffic injector (steady, ramp, and burst profiles) that can be scheduled as a canary probe; 2) perf-canary/credit_guard.py implements a windowed stability-credit algorithm: credits accumulate under stable baseline and are consumed when detected metric deltas exceed thresholds; credits allow limited burst tolerance before triggering a rollback; credits decay and are observable via metrics; 3) adds CI integration to run a short burst-injection scenario in the perf pipeline and a set of unit+integration tests; 4) observability: new dashboards and traces for burst events and credit accounting. Backwards compatibility: the stability-credit guard is off by default and gated behind a feature flag (perf.canary.credit_guard.enabled). Testing: unit tests for credit arithmetic, integration tests that simulate transient CPU/latency spikes with synthetic bursts, and canary job e2e run in staging that demonstrates reduced false positives under scheduled burst load. Checklist: - [x] Implement burst injector and profiles; - [x] Implement stability-credit algorithm and API hooks; - [x] Add feature flag and config knobs; - [x] Add unit and integration tests; - [x] Add dashboards and tracing spans; - [x] Update docs and examples; - [x] Run staging canary e2e and collect telemetry. Impact: reduces noisy rollbacks from scheduled or environmental bursts while preserving sensitivity to sustained regressions. Related work: ENG-4123 (canary false-positive reduction), ENG-4210 (burst-probing harness), SUP-9981 (customer incident where cron spikes triggered canary rollback).
Mateo Ruiz: The credit decay constants look reasonable but can we expose an autoscale factor derived from baseline RPS distribution? Also add a short explanation in the doc for how credits interplay with prefix/KV cache effects.
Author (Asha Menon): Added autoscale factor config and updated docs to explain KV cache caveats. Kept default conservative to avoid masking real regressions.
Ling Zhao: Tests look good; please add a small performance microbenchmark to ensure injector overhead is negligible under high RPS.
Author (Asha Menon): Added microbenchmark that runs injector with no-op backend; overhead <1% p50 and <3% p99 on staging GPU nodes. Results attached to CI artifacts.
Priya Satish: Approve after addressing comments; please ensure feature flag rollout docs are included for Dedicated customers.
Author (Asha Menon): Added rollout notes for Dedicated and Private deployments and included migration steps for enabling the guard behind the feature flag.

Motivation: Some enterprise customers require a formal, auditable pathway to declassify tenant data residency after explicit legal consent or a compliance exception. Today our platform supports region pinning and KMS-scoped envelopes, but there is no standard mechanism to (a) accept operator-triggered declassification consent, (b) bind that consent to a short TTL-limited RBAC grant, and (c) synthesize audit records that prove the consent-to-declassification decision chain. This PR implements a lightweight 'consent pulse' handshake with the KMS allocator, a TTL-bound RBAC declassification role, and an audit-synthesis shim that consolidates multi-hop audit events into a single verifiable envelope. Summary of changes: 1) New RBAC rule type (declassification:ttl) + policy compiler support to emit timebound grants for declassification calls; 2) KMS allocator changes to accept consent-pulse tokens and annotate created wrapping keys with consent metadata (region_from, region_to, legal_basis_id); 3) API and operator endpoint for initiating a declassification flow that returns a consent-pulse token after multi-party approvals; 4) Audit synthesis shim that listens to audit events from operator-service, kms-allocator, and routing-proxy and emits a canonical signed envelope (sha256) that can be used in compliance reports; 5) Migration: configuration flag residency.declassification.enabled (off by default) and a rollout plan with staged enablement and a canary on 10% of operator flows. Backwards compatibility: unchanged unless the feature flag is enabled. Rollback: feature-flag toggle + queue drain; hotfix path documented. See release notes at the end of this PR for customer-facing behavior.

Priya Natarajan (author): Agreed, default TTL is 1 hour; changed templates to enforce max 6h. See internal/rbac/templates/declassification.tpl.
Marina Kovalenko: Audit envelopes need a stable signing key and rotation policy; where do we store the signer's key and how do we attest it?
Priya Natarajan: Added envelope_signer backed by the KMS allocator with a dedicated signer key (rotated quarterly) and a 'signer_proof' field included in the envelope. Documented rotation in docs/runbooks/declassification.md.
Diego Ruiz: Integration test flaked on CI (timing). Can we add deterministic clocks/stubs?
Priya Natarajan: Added deterministic clock to tests and parameterized backoff; reran CI and integration pipeline passed.
Marina Kovalenko: Request small change to audit envelope format to include linear ticket id (SEC-118) as provenance.
Priya Natarajan: Included linked_ticket in envelope metadata and updated console UI to surface it.
- Add opt-in tenant declassification feature: operator-initiated region declassification with consent pulse and KMS annotations.
- New RBAC declassification role type (timebound).
- Audit synthesis: single signed envelope representing multi-service consent chain.
- Feature disabled by default; enable with residency.declassification.enabled=true and follow runbook.
Rollout: enable flag in staging first, monitor audit-envelope error rate and KMS allocator latency. Canary at 10% of operator flows for 72 hours. If audit-synthesis error rate > 0.1% or KMS latency > 95th p90 baseline + 150ms, roll back by toggling residency.declassification.enabled=false and drain pending consent queues. Forensic: audit envelope contains signer_proof, linked_ticket, region_from, region_to, legal_basis_id and timestamp. Preserve envelopes in append-only audit store for 365 days.
None for customers that do not opt in. When enabled, operator flows that request declassification will create transient keys and emit audit envelopes. Tenants requiring strict residency will need to review declassification runbook; declassification operation requires multi-party approval and is gated by policies.

Adds a non-blocking 'lint-shadow' CI lane to evaluate proposed lint rule changes and a lightweight dependency-alert gateway that surfaces new vulnerability notices to #deps-alerts and creates Linear cards.
Motivation: New lint rules and dependency alerts keep breaking PRs or creating noise because they are introduced with no opt-in runway. This PR adds two pieces: (1) a lint-shadow CI lane that runs the full lint suite but does not block merges and reports rule violations to a dashboard + PR comment; (2) a dependency-alert gateway that accepts Snyk/OSSF notifications and posts summarized notices to #deps-alerts and creates Linear cards for triage. This allows teams to validate stricter lint policies in a shadowed environment before flipping them on, and to centralize dep alerts for faster response.

What changed (high level):
- New CI workflow .github/workflows/lint-shadow.yml: schedules on PRs and nightly, uploads lint output artifact, posts summary comment. Runs same lint matrix as main lint but uses "shadow" reporter and exit code 0.
- Centralized lint rules in infra/lint/config.yaml and a small runtime that can enable/disable rules per-team (infra/lint/manager.py). Existing repo rules were migrated from scattered package.json/.eslintrc files.
- Dependency alert gateway service under infra/dep-alert/gateway.py: small Flask lambda-compatible endpoint that consumes webhook payloads, filters noise, posts to Slack via tools/slack/post_message.py and creates Linear cards using tools/linear/create_card.sh.
- Tests: added unit tests for rule parsing and gateway filter logic under infra/tests.
- Docs: docs/ci/lint-shadow.md and docs/ops/dep-alerts.md with rollout plan and how to opt-in teams.

Testing and rollout:
- Ran lint-shadow on a selection of active repos for one week; collected violations against a curated rule subset (see docs).
- Gateway was dry-run for 48h with real Snyk feed; false-positive rate measured ~7%.
- Rollout plan: enable lint-shadow by default; after 2 weeks, convert highest-confidence rules to 'blocking' behind a Linear-threaded rollout. Gateway will be enabled in production after another 1-week dry run.

Checklist:
- [x] Add non-blocking lint-shadow workflow
- [x] Centralize lint configs and add manager
- [x] Implement dep-alert gateway with Slack/Linear integrations (dry-run first)
- [x] Add docs and rollout notes
- [x] Unit tests for parsing and filtering

Notes on scope and rationale: The shadow lane is intentionally noisy initially but non-intrusive. Teams can opt to subscribe to reduced noise categories. The gateway keeps the source of truth for alerts out of email, centralizing triage in Linear.

Elliot Zhang: Please gate the Slack notifications behind a dry-run flag so we don't flood channels.
Nina Patel: Gate added in gateway.py and workflow secrets; dry-run default true for initial rollout.
Samir Gupta: Can we reduce the lint-shadow matrix to only changed packages to cut CI cost?
Nina Patel: Good point — lint-shadow uses a file-changed detector (infra/lint/changed_packages.py) and falls back to full matrix on schedule.
Laura Kim: Suggest adding a short-lived toggle so product teams can opt-out for 72h while migrating.
Nina Patel: Added 'team-exempt' label handling and documented opt-out flow.
Elliot Zhang: Verified unit tests and smoke-run on staging; approving.
Samir Gupta: Approved (looks good, re-run CI once more to clear intermittent flake).
When enabling gateway in production, provision a webhook secret and set DEP_ALERT_DRY_RUN=false in secrets. Monitor #deps-alerts and Linear queue for incoming cards; rate-limit to 5 cards/minute to avoid burst storms.
Risk: noise from lint-shadow may create alert fatigue. Mitigation: non-blocking by default, team opt-out label, rule-level confidence tags, and a dashboard to surface only top-priority violations. Risk: gateway could create many Linear cards. Mitigation: initial dry-run + deduplication logic and rate-limiting implemented.

payload.body:
Motivation: Dedicated pools occasionally experience short-duration spikes where preemptive node eviction causes oscillation and SLA violations. This PR introduces a deferred-eviction safety buffer paired with a predictive cohort-scaling signal to reduce churn while keeping throughput guarantees intact.

Summary: Implement a cohort-based credit window that defers non-critical evictions for a short, bounded interval when a tenant's ephemeral burst is detected. Meanwhile, a lightweight predictive estimator (cohort scaler) monitors cohort-level short-term rate-of-arrival and triggers proactive cohort scale-up when sustained utilization is likely. The design prioritizes predictability: eviction deferral is bounded, credits decay deterministically, and we prefer scaling over eviction when cost/latency budget allows.

Key behaviors: 1) Each tenant in a dedicated fleet is assigned a cohort_id (cohort grouping is configurable by tenant tag). 2) When eviction pressure would normally remove warmlets, the eviction controller consults the cohort credit store; if credits exist, eviction is deferred and credits are consumed. 3) Credits are minted when burst mitigation budget is available, and decayed on a fixed half-life to avoid long-term accumulation. 4) A predictive cohort scaler uses short-window exponential smoothing over request arrival to decide on a proactive scale-up; it emits a scale recommendation instead of forcing immediate provisioning, enabling controlled rollouts by the autoscaler.

Files: See changed files for implementation + tests + docs. The RFC contains configuration knobs and migration guidance.

Backward compatibility / migration: Defaults preserve current behavior (credits disabled). Operators can enable cohort grouping and configure default credit windows in the dedicated helm chart. No data migration required; the cohort credit store is schemaless and backed by existing etcd-backed controller state.

Testing: Unit tests for allocator logic and credit decay, integration test that simulates ephemeral spike and verifies reduced eviction churn, e2e smoke verifying no regression to throughput SLO under normal load. CI initially failed one flaky test related to timing; fixed by replacing wall-clock sleeps with injected clock in tests.

Rollout plan: 1) Feature gated off by default. 2) Enable in canary pools for 48h with detailed metrics. 3) If no regressions, enable for non-critical tenants, then expand cohort coverage. 4) Monitor new metrics and runbook (added) for when deferred-evictions exceed threshold.

Related: ENG-2105 (work item), SUP-4221 (customer request for reduced churn during bursts).
Arjun Patel (review): Overall looks good, but we need to be careful about metric cardinality for cohort_id. If cohorts are per-tenant we could explode Prometheus series. Consider sampling or hashing and provide high-cardinality knobs.
Maya Thompson (author): Agreed. Updated eviction_metrics.go to emit cohort histogram buckets and a sampled tag (cohort_bucket) instead of raw tenant id. Added docs on recommended cardinality sizing and a flag to cap cohorts emitted to metrics.
Lin Zhao (review): The predictive scaler could introduce false positives during noise. Did you validate the smoothing window choices?
Maya Thompson (author): Added unit tests over multiple arrival scenarios and included a canary config in values.yaml that uses conservative thresholds. We also expose smoothing alpha as an operator-configurable knob.
Samir Kapoor (approval): Verified e2e smoke on canary pool; observed ~62% fewer eviction events during ephemeral spikes in test runs. Approving pending CI green.
CI (system): One flaky test timed out (cohort_allocator_test.go:TestCreditDecay) on first run. Replaced time.Sleep with injected clock and re-ran CI - all checks passed.
Merge coach (bot): Squash-merge approved; please ensure release notes entry is present.
Introduce deferred-eviction safety buffer and predictive cohort scaling: feature gated for Dedicated. Reduces eviction-induced churn during ephemeral bursts and adds new observability for cohort-level utilization. See docs/rfc for configuration and rollout steps.
payload.title: deferred-eviction-safety-buffer-and-predictive-cohort-scaling

payload.body:
Motivation: Production incidents during multi-tenant microbursts highlighted cases where GPU slot counts alone produced misleading free-capacity signals when network bandwidth or PCIe saturation constrained tail latency. This PR introduces a lightweight capacity proctor that normalizes available headroom by an observed bandwidth factor and a complementary differential burst tuner that enforces proportional burst admission across tenants based on recent delta-utilization. Design summary: 1) capacity_proctor: observes per-pool token spend, per-node network transmit/receive bytes, and an exponential moving estimate of IO pressure to compute an effective capacity multiplier (0.0-1.0) applied to reservations/burst budgets. 2) diff_burst_tuner: maintains a short-window delta-utilization ledger per-tenant, penalizes repeated burst wins with a decay multiplier, and seeds proportional burst allowances from the normalized capacity. 3) Safety: hard caps remain on absolute concurrent slots and a passive fallback route to the existing soft-reservation bank if network-normalized capacity drops below 20%. 4) Config: new autoscaler flags: --proctor-window-ms, --io-pressure-alpha, --delta-decay, --min-normalized-cap, and a per-tenant annotation allow-burst-weight to tweak proportional share. 5) Telemetry: exported metrics for proctor_normalized_capacity, tenant_delta_util_90, burst_win_penalty, and decision_trace_id for sampled decisions. Migration notes: deployable as a non-breaking feature behind the runtime flag autoscaler.enable_bandwidth_proctor=false by default; can be enabled cluster-by-cluster. Test plan: unit tests for proctor math and ledger decay, integration e2e that simulates node-level IO saturation and verifies throttling, canary rollout to one dedicated pool. Checklist: [x] RFC 2026 written and linked [x] unit tests added [x] e2e fixture and simulator added [x] metrics and dashboards sketched [x] docs/RFC updated [x] feature flagged and defaults off Related work: builds on prior work for soft-reservation bank and warm-pool smoothing, references ENG-4219 and RFC 2021. Impact: reduces tail latency regressions attributable to IO-bound nodes during tenant microbursts and provides a knob for operators to constrain burst admission when non-GPU resources are the limiting factor.
Leah Chen: Nice separation of concerns. Can you clarify how the proctor interacts with multi-pool routing? I want to ensure we don't double-count capacity when requests can failover to another pool.
Ava Park (author): Good point. The proctor is per-pool and we attach a decision_trace_id to requests that get rerouted; the router will re-evaluate normalized_capacity on the target pool and use the trace to attribute the original admission decision. Added a note in docs/observability/bandwidth_proctor_dashboard.md.
Miguel Soto: The decay multiplier looks aggressive in the unit tests; what's the rationale? Could we expose a safer default?
Ava Park (author): Adjusted default delta-decay from 0.75 to 0.9 and added a unit test for pathological repeated wins. Kept config tunable for ops to reduce conservatism.
Rahul Iyer: CI flaky on integration (timing). Please add a retry/backoff in the e2e fixture to reduce flakiness.
Ava Park (author): e2e fixture now includes a deterministic backoff loop and a marker file to assert saturation onset; re-ran integration and CI stabilized.
Leah Chen: Approved after responses and test stabilization.
SRE: Noted that dashboards should include per-node IO percentile. Added request to ops runbook to surface node IO alerts before autoscaler kicks in.
- Adds bandwidth-normalized capacity proctor to reduce tail latency when IO/PCIe/network is the bottleneck. - Introduces differential burst tuner for proportional burst admission and decay penalties. - Metrics: proctor_normalized_capacity, tenant_delta_util_90, burst_win_penalty. - Feature flag autoscaler.enable_bandwidth_proctor=false by default.
Reviewers requested clarifications on multi-pool routing, decay defaults, and e2e flakiness. Author updated defaults, improved tests and observability, and added documentation. Approval obtained from Leah Chen and SRE acked the runbook item.
Feature gated rollout recommended: enable in canary pool, monitor proctor_normalized_capacity and tenant_delta_util_90 for 48 hours before cluster-wide enable.
payload.title: Bandwidth-normalized capacity proctor and differential burst tuner

Motivation: customers running multi-tool conversations saw non-deterministic toolcall ordering after client disconnect + rapid reconnects which caused out-of-order side effects in third-party systems. This PR introduces server-side ordering guarantees for tool/function calls across reconnect/resume boundaries plus a client disconnect splay (randomized small backoff applied server-side to accept/reconcile reconnects) to avoid thundering reconnections. Design: 1) Sequence numbers: each stream session assigns a monotonic sequence number to each emitted event that can invoke a tool. Sequence numbers are signed by the server lease and attached to events sent to the client. 2) Reconciliation window: on reconnect the client can provide latest-acked-seq; server replays pending events in-order and drops duplicates. 3) Idempotency + ordered-apply: tool call invocations include an ordered_id composed of session_id:seq so downstream adapters (and the OpenAI compat shim) can apply tools in sequence. 4) Disconnect splay: when many clients disconnect during scale events we introduce a small randomized acceptance delay (0-300ms configurable) before reattaching the session lease to avoid simultaneous inflight reconnections overwhelming the tool adapters. 5) Config and compatibility: the OpenAI compatibility layer now accepts and emits ordered_toolcalls metadata on streaming endpoints and falls back to previous behavior when the flag is off. 6) Safety: added checks so that a resumed stream with an older lease is rejected; client must re-negotiate if server lease id mismatches. Rollout plan: feature gated behind streaming.reconnect.ordered_toolcalls, enabled for canary customers for 48 hours, metric-driven rollouts tied to toolcall error-rate and tail-latency. Tests: unit tests for seq assignment and validation, integration tests simulating N concurrent reconnects with artificial clock skew, e2e tests validating toolcall ordering against a mock adapter. Docs: docs/streaming/reconnect.md updated with semantics and migration steps. Implementation notes: implementation touches the session manager, ack manager, and OpenAI adapter layers to wire ordered ids into structured output. Commits are small and focused to ease bisecting. Backwards compatibility: when the client does not provide ordered metadata we maintain existing behavior; SDKs are updated to opt into the new behavior. Observability: added metrics streaming.reconnect.splay_applied and streaming.reconcile.ordered_replays to monitor adoption. 
Adds ordered reconciliation for tool/function calls during stream reconnects and introduces a randomized disconnect splay to reduce reconnect storms. OpenAI compatibility layer now preserves toolcall ordering and surfaces deterministic idempotency tokens. Behavior is opt-in via streaming.reconnect.ordered_toolcalls config; rollout staged behind a feature flag.
Ethan Cole: Nice focused change. Can we ensure the sequence number fits in 64 bits across long-lived sessions? Also request an extra unit test for seq wrap-around detection.
Maya Patel (author): Seq is u64 currently; added a test for wrap-around detection and defensive error path that forces session renewal when seq would overflow.
Ravi Singh: The disconnect splay param seems low for high fan-out events. Suggest making the upper bound configurable per deployment and exposing metric when splay is applied.
Maya Patel (author): Made upper bound configurable via streaming.reconnect.splay_max_ms and added streaming.reconnect.splay_applied metric and dashboards in observability pack.
Priya Nair: Integration test flaked in the first run due to timing; can we add a deterministic clock or retries to stabilize? Also ensure SDK changes have clear migration notes.
Maya Patel (author): Switched integration harness to use fake clock for deterministic behavior and added migration note in docs/streaming/reconnect.md. Marking as ready-for-merge after CI green.
Merged via squash on 2026-02-24 by Maya Patel after approvals from reviewers. Feature gated; no immediate global rollout. Canary enabled for 3% of streaming traffic and monitored for 48 hours.
Behavior is opt-in via streaming.reconnect.ordered_toolcalls; default remains backwards compatible.
SDKs: python/ts updated to include helpers for reconstructing ordered toolcall ids; patch released in minor versions.
Observability: new metrics added; dashboards updated in observability-pack repo.
Operational: when enabling globally, consider raising tool-adapter concurrency limits for first 24 hours to absorb ordered replays.

Motivation: we observed a class of customer-visible failures where SSE fragments that contained the tail of a JSON object (e.g. end of a tool call payload) were dropped or emitted out-of-order under transient backpressure, producing partial JSON at the client and broken OpenAI-compatible toolcall handoffs. This PR introduces two complementary guards: (1) a fragment hedging timer that holds small tail fragments for a configurable window and attempts reassembly before emitting; (2) a lightweight toolcall leasing mechanism that quarantines toolcall sentinel events until their JSON spans are validated or a safety timeout elapses. Goals: reduce partial-JSON starvation, preserve event ordering for function/tool calls, avoid increasing steady-state latency for healthy streams. Implementation notes: - New hedging buffer lives at the streamer output layer; it tracks fragment anchors and a short timer (default 30ms) to allow late-arriving bytes to be coalesced. Hedging is adaptive: it uses recent reorder/latency metrics to shrink/expand the window. - Toolcall lease inserts a synthetic lease token for any tool/function sentinel (OPENAI "tool_call" style) and defers downstream handoff until either the hedger confirms the JSON span or lease timeout (default 120ms) fires. - Introduces an SSE anchor header (X-SSE-Anchor) that marks the logical span id for debugging and metrics; it is optional and not sent to external clients unless debug mode is enabled. - Backpressure behavior: when internal queueing indicates saturation, the hedger will prioritize anchor-complete fragments and emit partials with explicit "incomplete":true flag in a compatibility envelope to preserve downstream parsers. Rollback plan: feature gated via streamer feature flag (sse_frag_hedge_v2); can be disabled remotely. Test plan: unit tests for hedger state machine, deterministic reorder/integration tests with synthetic delayed segments, end-to-end with openai-compat layer using function call emulation, and perf benchmarks to confirm <5% P95 latency regression under normal load. Documentation: added notes and config knobs in docs/notes/streaming-frag-hedge.md. This description is a single continuous string (sections separated by hyphens).
Diego Alvarez: Nice approach. Two high-level asks: (1) can we make the default hedging window configurable per-tenant? (2) need a fail-safe that avoids head-of-line blocking if many anchors are incomplete.
Maya Chen: Answered — made window per-tenant via StreamerConfig and introduced an eviction policy that escalates oldest anchors with an 'incomplete' compatibility envelope to avoid HOL blocking.
Priya Kapoor: Please add explicit metrics for hedger_emits/{coalesced,forced_partial,timeout} and toolcall_lease/{granted,expired}. We should also expose a debug sampling mode.
Maya Chen: Added metrics and an optional debug sampling flag documented in the config. Also added X-SSE-Anchor header (disabled by default).
Liam O'Connor: Integration tests look good. One nit: increase lease timeout to 120ms to accommodate high-latency inter-region spikes (suggested by earlier incident logs).
Maya Chen: Increased default lease timeout and added adaptive backoff when consecutive expirations are observed.
- Introduce SSE fragment hedger to reduce partial JSON emission under transient reordering/backpressure.
- Add toolcall lease mechanism to preserve function/tool call ordering and avoid broken handoffs.
- New optional debug header X-SSE-Anchor and metrics for hedger/toolcall leasing.
- Feature gated; rollout controlled via streamer flags.
payload.title: sse-frag-hedge-and-toolcall-lease-to-prevent-partial-json-starvation

payload.body:
Context: We continue to see intermittent CI noise and long presubmit queues caused by dependency-related flakiness and heavy longtest lanes. This PR introduces a lightweight presubmit handoff routing layer that forwards high-noise PRs to a quarantined 'ghostbuster' lane and a companion dep-ghostbuster tool that heuristically detects rarely-touched transitive dependencies likely to cause nondeterministic failures. Goals: 1) reduce wasted presubmit cycles by routing flaky PRs away from the fast feedback lanes, 2) provide automated hints and safe-removal candidates for transitive deps, 3) integrate with release automation so quarantined PRs still progress under a measured window. Summary of changes: - Add presubmit handshake router in .github/workflows/presubmit-routing.yml. The router tags PRs with a noise score based on recent flaky-test history and upstream dependency churn. - Add tools/dep-ghostbuster: a lightweight scanner (Go) that computes file-usage heuristics and runtime footprint for transitive deps and emits candidate removals as a single-line JSON record for automation. - Add ci/handshake: a small serviceless script (scripts/ci-handoff.sh) that applies labels, posts annotated comments with remediation steps, and re-runs a narrow smoke lane. - Update ci-utils and presubmit runners to accept a conditional HOOK_HANDOFF=true flag to opt-in routing behavior per-repo. - Small release automation hook changes in .github/workflows/release-smoke.yml to allow ghostbuster-suppressed merges under a 24h quiesce window. - Docs: docs/ci/presubmit-handoff.md and docs/ci/dep-ghostbuster.md with operator runbook and Linear links. Rollout plan: staged opt-in across teams. Start with redwood/runtime and redwood/sdk-* for two weeks, monitor presubmit queue length and false-positive quarantines, then widen. Backout: feature flag on router and CI flag; revert easy through git revert or disabling workflow. See Linked LINEAR items and metrics in the PR body. Checklist: - [x] implement routing workflow and router logic - [x] implement dep-ghostbuster scanner and CLI - [x] integrate basic annotations and comments - [x] docs and operator runbook - [x] add smoke-run gating for release automation - [x] unit tests for the scanner and router heuristics - [x] flaky-test telemetry hooks added - [x] rollout and monitoring dashboard annotated Related: ENG-1298 (presubmit reliability), INF-211 (release smoke adjustments) Observability: emits presubmit.noise_score histogram, dep_ghostbuster.candidate_count gauge, and presubmit.handoff.events counter. This description is a single-line continuous string and includes context, motivation, changeset summary, rollout, and checklist.
Jordan Lee: Nice approach, caught one question on the noise score window — can we make it configurable per-team?
Marta González: Good call, added HOOK_HANDOFF_WINDOW env and default 3d; updated docs to describe overrides per-repo.
Anika Patel: dep-ghostbuster looks useful but worried about false-positive removals; can we surface a 'usage snapshot' in the PR comment?
Marta González: Added a usage snapshot to the annotation output and a link to the interactive candidate page; scanner will not auto-remove without manual approval.
Simon Barrett: CI footprint change looks safe but please run canary on redwood/runtime first; approve after canary passes.
CI Bot: canary-run completed on redwood/runtime (2026-02-18) — all smoke checks passed.
Anika Patel: Approved with one non-blocking nits on doc phrasing.
Jordan Lee: Approved — squash merge when green.
Introduce presubmit handoff router that quarantines high-noise PRs and add dep-ghostbuster scanner to identify rarely-used transitive dependencies; opt-in rollout and operator runbook included.

payload.body:
This PR refactors SDK streaming ergonomics by splitting authentication lifecycle hooks from streaming primitives, renaming iterable types for clearer ergonomics, and standardizing retry schema names across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Motivation: teams reported confusion when auth warmup and token rotation logic lived on stream objects (caused surprising reauths during short-lived streams) and inconsistent names across SDKs made cross-team migrations error-prone. Changes include: 1) Introduce AuthProvider and AuthWarmup hooks (optional) that are registered on the client factory so streaming objects no longer mutate credential state. 2) Rename public pull/async iterable types: Python async_iter -> StreamReader, TS PullStream -> StreamReader, Go PullIterator -> StreamReaderIterator for clearer intent and parity. 3) Split retry configuration into retry_presets (user-facing friendly presets) and retry_profiles (runtime-configured profiles) and wire them into the SDK config vignette. 4) Minor runtime opt: reduce token handshake frequency for rapid reconnects by caching last-successful-sig per-session. 5) Bump SDK versions: py->3.2.0, ts->2.7.0, go->v1.6.4. Migration notes included in release_notes. See linked Linear tickets for benchmarks and adoption plan. Checklist: - [x] Implement AuthProvider + warmup hook - [x] Rename iterable types and update all internal references - [x] Migrate retry names and docs - [x] Add compatibility shims for one release cycle - [x] Run integration test matrix (py/ts/go) - [x] Update changelogs and examples
SDKs: Introduce AuthProvider and AuthWarmup hooks; rename stream iterables to StreamReader variants for clearer cross-language parity; separate retry_presets (user-facing) from retry_profiles (runtime); compatibility aliases provided for one release; SDK versions bumped: Python 3.2.0, TypeScript 2.7.0, Go v1.6.4. See docs/sdk-migration/retry-profiles.md and examples/getting-started/streaming-migration.md for migration steps.
Ava Patel: Nice separation surface, but can we preserve the old names for one release? request: add compatibility shims and deprecation warnings — requested changes
Priya Nair: Added compatibility shims (StreamReader alias types) and deprecation warnings in CHANGELOGs — reply
Jonah Li: Found a subtle race during token warmup in the TS client on reconnect; suggested ensuring warmup runs under client-level lock — requested changes
Priya Nair: Moved warmup to client factory lock and added unit test to validate no concurrent warmups — reply
Marisol Gomez: Please add a short perf note on handshake caching; verify it does not mask auth failures — comment
Priya Nair: Added perf microbench results to docs and retained fallback path for failed cache verification — reply
Marisol Gomez: Approving after the added tests and docs — approved

Adds a residency assertion proxy to centralize per-request jurisdiction checks and a RBAC policy attenuator that enforces temporal limits and operator-scope filters. No user-facing API changes.
Background: Customers in regulated jurisdictions were asking for stronger per-request residency proofing and a simpler way to express short-lived operator delegations. This PR introduces a lightweight residency-assertion-proxy service and an RBAC policy attenuator that can be composed into the request path to enforce timebound and locality-scoped grants. Motivation: consolidate residency checks in a single place, improve audit signals with residency provenance, and reduce policy complexity for cross-region operator flows. Changes are designed to be opt-in via config flags and default to non-blocking with telemetry-only mode.
services/residency-proxy/main.go: new HTTP proxy that validates per-request residency token and attaches residency.proof header
internal/rbac/attenuator.go: new policy attenuator applying max-duration and geo-allowlist filters
pkg/audit/enricher.go: attach signed residency provenance to audit events
pkg/kms/provenance.go: propagate kms-region hint and verify wrapped-key origin
integration/tests/residency_proxy_test.go: integration scenarios for cross-region failover
docs/security/residency-proxy.md: design and config options
charts/redwood/templates/residency-proxy.yaml: helm chart with feature flag
ci/flake-fix: small lint cleanup and timeout bumps

payload.body:
Context: we observe tail-latency and cost variance when the prefill (token priming) stage either over-primes (wasting KV cache fills) or under-primes (starving decode kernels). This PR introduces a lightweight prewarm orchestration layer and a decode-side concurrency adapter to reduce oscillation between prefill and decode stages while improving KV cache coherence. Motivation: reduce p95/p99 token latency and smooth GPU kernel scheduling by aligning prefill chunk size and pacing with observed decode consumption and KV hit efficiency. This is complementary to existing speculative and chunked prefill work but approaches the problem from an orchestration + feedback perspective rather than low-level kernel fusion. What changed: - PrewarmChunkOrchestrator (services/serving/scheduler/prewarm_orchestrator.py): groups incoming prefill requests into adaptive-sized chunks based on a sliding window of recent KV hit-rate, sequence length distribution, and decode concurrency hints. Uses a configurable hysteresis to avoid rapid chunk-size oscillation. - DecodingConcurrencyAdapter (services/serving/scheduler/decoding_concurrency_adapter.py): decode stage publishes a small set of runtime indicators (active_decode_slots, avg_decode_runtime_ms, preferred_prefill_batch) which the orchestrator consumes to modulate prewarm pacing. - KV cache integration (runtime/kv_cache/*): new metrics exported (kv_prefill_hits, kv_prefill_evictions, kv_prefill_latency) and a minor eviction-policy tweak to prefer retaining keys for actively decoding shards. - Metrics & observability: added dashboard hooks and tracing annotations for prewarm lifecycle, chunk boundary events, and decode backpressure signals. - Tests & benchmarks: unit tests for orchestrator and adapter, benchmark harness config and comparison run showing 7-12% improvement on p95 for interactive chat traces at medium concurrency, and 4-6% token cost reduction due to higher KV reuse. - Docs & examples: ops doc describing tuning knobs and an example script demonstrating prewarm enrollment. Checklist: - [x] Implement orchestrator and adapter - [x] Unit tests for orchestrator and adapter - [x] KV metrics and small eviction tweak - [x] Benchmark config and run - [x] Docs and examples - [x] CI green (flaky test addressed) Backwards compatibility and rollout: default behavior is opt-in via a feature flag (SERVING_PREWARM_V2). On by default for dedicated clusters in canary for 2 weeks before global rollout. No changes to public API surface. Related: follows up on ENG-6123 study into prefill inefficiencies and is intentionally orthogonal to kernel-fusion efforts (see ENG-7901). Performance notes: aggregated benchmark (benchmarks/prefill_vs_decode/2026-02-25-prewarm-bench.yaml) indicates consistent p95 reductions on small/medium sequence mixes when KV hit-rate is above 18%. Edge cases: when KV hit-rate is very low the orchestrator reduces chunking aggressiveness and falls back to single-request prefill to avoid wasted work. Implementation detail summary: the orchestrator uses a token-bucket-esque pacing loop and groups requests up to a configurable max_chunk_tokens. The adapter subscribes on the internal event bus; to keep the critical path small the adapter only sends +- integer suggestions (increase/decrease) rather than full histograms. See docs/ops/prewarm_and_decode.md for tuning guidance.
Luca Romano: Nice separation of concerns. Two asks: (1) can we add a small end-to-end integration test that simulates a decode slowdown to validate the backpressure loop? (2) the hysteresis constants look aggressive; please parameterize them and add defaults tuned to 95th percentile workloads.
Asha Patel: Added a synthetic e2e test (runtime/tests/test_prewarm_orchestrator.py) that simulates decode slot starvation and asserts orchestrator backs off within 200ms. Hysteresis constants are now configuration fields with conservative defaults; documented in docs/ops/prewarm_and_decode.md.
Priya Menon: I saw a local failure on test_kv_eviction_policy showing timing sensitivity. Can you stabilize that test?
Asha Patel: Fixed by switching that test to use deterministic clock advance and increased the eviction grace window in policy.py; added a comment explaining the time-coupling. Re-ran CI.
Samir Gulati: Metrics look good. One nit: the dashboard panels should expose kv_prefill_hits as a rate not a counter. I left a small suggestion in the dashboard yaml. Approving after CI is green.
Priya Menon: Approve (looks reasonable; bench shows clear improvement).
