Motivation: Long-tail latency and token-cost spikes frequently correlate with transient kernel queue saturation on Dedicated clusters and with pathological prompt shapes. This PR introduces a low-cardinality invocation signature (X-Invocation-Sig) and a first-pass dashboard that correlates kernel queue metrics with token-level latency and cost to speed RCA and automated alert tuning.

What I changed (high level):
- Add X-Invocation-Sig header generation upstream in our gateway: stable hash of (tenant_id, route, first-128-bytes-of-prompt, model_family) with a configurable salt and TTL to keep cardinality low. This header is propagated to internal request context and tracing.
- Trace enrichment: include invocation_sig as a tag/span attribute in all inference-related spans and in tenant billing traces so cost rollups can be grouped by signature.
- Metrics + exporter changes: emit kernel_queue_depth_p99_per_signature (sampled; reservoir per-signature) and token_latency_variance_per_signature as low-cardinality rollups. Added safe cardinality gating to avoid explosion (per-tenant cap + sampling).
- Dashboard: new Grafana panel group under Observability -> Inference -> Signatures that shows: kernel queue depth time series, token-latency variance sparkline, and a scatter panel overlaying token-cost (y) vs queue-depth (x) with opacity by invocation count. Also includes a small table of top-10 signatures by cost delta.
- Alerts: a new alert recipe (informational by default) that ties moderate queue-depth increases to disproportionate token cost growth for a signature over a 15m window; rule includes auto-mute if signature has <100 invocations in the window.
- Tests & e2e: unit tests for header generation and salt rotation; integration test that simulates queue saturation and asserts the signature propagates onto traces and the exporter produces one rollup metric per signature.

Why this is different from existing token-cost rollups: instead of full-token lineage or per-request high-cardinality traces, this approach intentionally creates a low-cardinality invocation fingerprint for operational grouping. It trades some exactness for signposting consistent operational patterns (prompt shards, misrouted batches, model-family hotspots) while protecting metrics storage and query performance.

Implementation notes:
- Header is generated in api/gateway (http middleware) and attached to the request context. Implementation lives in pkg/api/signature. Salt is read from config KMS-backed secret and rotated with a TTL config.
- Trace enrichment uses a small shim in the tracing library to attach invocation_sig to all subsequent spans (configurable to opt-out for Private installs).
- Metrics rollups are emitted from the serving runtime collector with a short-lived in-memory reservoir per-signature; periodically aggregated by telemetry-ingester into compact rollups in the timeseries DB.
- Dashboard JSON and panels are added under observability/dashboards/invocation-signatures.json and a migration script registers the board on deploy.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add gateway header generation and tests
- [x] Propagate signature through context + traces
- [x] Emit guarded low-cardinality metrics
- [x] Add Grafana dashboard + migration script
- [x] Add alert recipe with auto-mute gating
- [x] Manual QA on staging cluster using replaybench

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy header generation and trace enrichment to staging (opt-in via env var).
2) Enable metric rollups in telemetry-ingester in a low-rate sampling mode.
3) Deploy dashboard and preview to SRE + DX.
4) Gradually increase sampling rates for tenants with high invocation volume.

Security & privacy: The signature intentionally truncates the prompt payload to 128 bytes and is salted to avoid reconstructing user data. Private installers can disable header propagation via a single runtime flag.

Operational notes: A per-tenant cardinality cap is enforced; if exceeded the exporter emits a metric export_suppressed_by_signature_cardinality with a tag for tenant. The alert is muted automatically while suppression is active.

Testing instructions:
- Unit: run make test-packages pkg/api/signature pkg/tracing.
- Integration: run ./tools/replaybench --profile kqueue-spike --enable-signature and verify the grafana board shows the signature in the top-10 table.
- Manual: trigger a small canary on Dedicated and watch the new alert channel (observability-sig) for noisy signatures.

Related items: ENG-9420 (dashboard for kernel queue correlation), ENG-9483 (low-cardinality grouping exploration). Linked support ticket SUP-4319 reported a tenant with repeated cost spikes that motivated the pilot.

Adds a low-cardinality invocation signature header propagated to traces and a new dashboard correlating kernel queue depth, per-token latency variance, and token-cost hotspots. No API surface breaking changes.
Marco Liu: Nice focused approach. A couple questions: 1) can we make the truncation length configurable per-tenant? 2) confirm that private installer will default to disabled. (requested changes)
Eleni Park: Answered - truncation is configurable but default is 128; Private installer will default to disabled and docstring updated in config. Pushed a commit to make that explicit.
Samira Patel: Please add a short note in the observability runbook about when to increase sampling rates and when to increase the per-tenant cap. (approved after patch)
Jordan Reyes: Lint caught a small formatting issue in signature_test.go; fixed in the latest amend. (approved)
payload.title: Introduce invocation-signature header and kernel-queue <> token-cost correlation dashboard

Problem: Our presubmit lanes are heavy and frequently run a large surface of lint/test jobs even for trivial doc or single-file typos. Separately, dependency churn has been causing transient CI failures and noisy alerts. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) a lightweight presubmit 'sieve' that quickly classifies changes into light/medium/heavy lanes so small changes get fast feedback, and (2) a dependency-entropy sweeper tool that scans PRs for noisy transitive dep changes and suggests minimal lockfile edits.

What this PR does (summary): compresses fast-feedback checks into a new fastpath workflow; adds a small Go-based dep-sweeper binary invoked as an optional presubmit step; wires a conditional lint-router that dispatches to the appropriate job profile; updates docs and CI templates; provides a migration guide for teams that want to opt into strict dep-sweeper gating.

Why now: reducing developer wait time by 40-60% on trivial PRs was flagged as a top pain point (ENG-2120). Simultaneously, spike analysis showed ~12% of flaky CI failures originate from lockfile churn across package managers. The sweeper helps reduce noise and surfaces minimal actionable changes.

Checklist:
- [x] Add presubmit-sieve workflow and fastpath job definitions
- [x] Implement dep-sweeper (Go) and integrate in CI as opt-in check
- [x] Add documentation and migration notes (docs/ci/presubmit.md)
- [x] Add unit tests for dep-sweeper and integration smoke test for conditional routing
- [x] Run dogfood on two internal repos for one week

Migration notes: The new sieve is opt-in by default for all repos; repo owners can flip the presubmit profile via .github/presubmit-profile.yaml. The dep-sweeper emits a JSON summary but does not block merges until enabled by repository policy. To enable strict gating, add label ci/strict-deps to your repo config.

Rollback plan: Remove workflow or set sieve to 'always-heavy' in repo config. Dep-sweeper is non-blocking until enabled, so rollback is low risk.
Evan Miller (reviewer): Can we keep the fastpath job resource footprint intentionally tiny? Suggest limiting matrix/containers to 1 to avoid scheduling delay.
Priya Kapoor (author): Good call — reduced fastpath to a single lightweight container and added a comment in presubmit-sieve.yaml explaining the rationale.
Sofia Ramirez (reviewer): The dep-sweeper output looks useful, but can we avoid JSON noise in logs? Consider writing summary to artifacts instead of stdout.
Priya Kapoor (author): Updated sweeper to write condensed summary to /tmp/dep-sweeper-summary.json and uploaded as a CI artifact; kept full verbose dump behind --debug flag.
Liam Chen (reviewer): Please add a short integration smoke test that exercises a benign lockfile change to ensure the sweeper doesn't crash on unexpected formats.
Priya Kapoor (author): Added tests/integration/presubmit-sieve/smoke.sh and CI step that runs it on a small fixture.
payload.title: Introduce lightweight presubmit sieve and dependency-entropy sweeper

payload.body:
This PR introduces a first-class dry-run mode for the regional failover controller. In dry-run, the controller evaluates current region signals and routing policy state, computes the recommended policy flips (failover / partial shift / no-op), and emits a structured audit event describing the decision and evidence signals, but it does not execute any routing changes or drain actions. Motivation: we need a safe way to validate trigger hierarchy + policy evaluation end-to-end (including dashboards/alerts and incident-bot hooks) before enabling automation in production. This is a prerequisite for the Q1 2026 controlled failover game day and for gradually rolling out automation behind feature flags. Scope: controller behavior + config + audit event emission + metrics. Out of scope: the actual execution path (policy flips), approval hooks, and rollback semantics (tracked separately). Design notes: (1) Dry-run is controlled via config flag failover_controller.mode = "dry_run" (default remains "disabled" in prod, "enabled" only via explicit Helm values). (2) The recommender uses the deterministic signal evaluation API from policy engine (see PR #19812) and the region health aggregator client (see PR #19810) when present; missing signals are treated as "unknown" and surfaced in the output for operator visibility (no implicit failover on unknown in dry-run). (3) Recommendations are returned via an internal endpoint and also logged periodically (rate limited) with a stable decision hash to support correlation and avoid log spam. (4) Audit events are written to the existing audit sink with event_type=failover.recommendation so downstream tooling can render and annotate dashboards without requiring that a real failover occurred. Acceptance criteria for ENG-2415: - Operators can enable dry-run in staging and see computed recommended actions with evidence. - No routing policy writes occur in dry-run (asserted via unit tests + integration test with a fake policy store). - An audit event is emitted for every recommendation cycle and includes region, route scope, recommended action, trigger(s), and decision hash. - Metrics reflect recommendation cycles and "would have flipped" counts to help tune thresholds without customer impact. Testing: added unit tests for mode gating and write suppression; added an integration test running the controller against a fake signal stream and verifying audit emission; ran staging deploy with dry-run enabled for /v1/chat routes only and confirmed no config writes. Rollout: land behind flag; staging config pack will enable dry-run by default; production remains disabled until go/no-go.
Miles Thornton (review): The recommender/executor split looks good. Can we guarantee no writes at all in dry-run, including incidental "touch" calls to the policy store? Also please include the specific trigger evidence we used (reachability / 5xx burn / latency burn / capacity) in the event payload so game day observers can debug why the recommendation happened. Benji Okafor (author): Added a strict interface for PolicyStore where write methods are not even constructed in dry-run (dependency injection picks NoopExecutor + ReadOnlyPolicyStore). Added unit test that fails if any write method is invoked. Also expanded evidence to include signal snapshot with "unknown" markers. Ravi Menon (review): For the decision hash, ensure stable ordering of evidence keys; otherwise we will churn hashes and spam audit. Also rate limit audit emission; we only need it on decision change or every N minutes. Benji Okafor (author): Implemented deterministic canonical JSON serialization for decision hash input and added an emission policy: emit on decision change, plus a heartbeat every 10 minutes. Allison Grant (review): Metrics labels: please avoid route_id/cardinality explosions. Use coarse dimensions (tier, region, action, trigger_primary). Benji Okafor (author): Switched to bounded labels and added a comment on cardinality constraints. Ethan Park (review): Internal endpoint should be auth-protected; ensure it’s only reachable from the ops network / service-to-service auth. Benji Okafor (author): Hooked into existing internal auth middleware and restricted to "ops" service identity. Final: Miles approved after verifying the write-suppression test and the audit payload fields.
Internal-only: adds failover controller dry-run mode to compute and report recommended regional failover actions without executing routing changes; includes audit events and low-cardinality metrics to support controlled failover validation.
payload.title: Failover controller: add dry-run mode (recommendations + audit events, no execution)

Motivation: Our lint/test config is scattered across multiple workflows and repo roots which causes inconsistent linting results and hard-to-debug failures. At the same time dependency upgrade PRs generated by the bot are noisy and often require human triage for innocuous version bumps. This PR does two related things in one deployable change: 1) create a single source-of-truth lint manifest (ci/lint/manifest.yaml) and rewire all GH Actions + internal CI runners to reference it; 2) add a small dependency-approval GitHub App shim (scripts/ci/dep-approver) that auto-labels and fast-tracks low-risk dependency bumps while queueing complex upgrades behind a manual review gate. Summary of work: - Consolidate ESLint, Prettier, and TypeScript lint entrypoints into a single manifest that defines per-package overrides, allowed rule exceptions, and path-based exemptions. - Replace duplicate workflow-level rule lists with a manifest reader action (ci/actions/read-lint-manifest). - Collapse three lint workflows into one staged-lint.yml with explicit fast-path lanes for docs/examples and a full-lint lane for core packages. - Implement dep-approver shim that evaluates depdiffs using lightweight heuristics (semver range, presence in protected-files list, changes in transitive deps) and applies labels: dep/auto, dep/manual, dep/risky. - Add a new merge gate step in staged-lint.yml that fails fast for lint regressions and posts inline annotations to the PR via the GH Checks API. Rollout plan: - Deploy manifest and action in feature branch (this PR). - Run staged-lint.yml in parallel on a small subset of active repos for 48h using a flag controlled in repo settings. - Inspect metrics (lint pass-rate, queue-times) and dep-approver labels for 7 days. - Flip default behavior for all repos and remove deprecated workflows. Checklist: - [x] Consolidate lint rules and publish manifest - [x] Implement read-lint-manifest action - [x] Replace existing lint workflows with staged-lint.yml - [x] Add dep-approver shim and unit tests - [x] Update README and CONTRIBUTING docs with new lint rules and how dep-approver labels map to automation - [x] Run canary on three active repos for 48h - [x] Add alerting for lint pipeline regressions (console/alerting/lintrunner) Related: ENG-9142 (lint consistency), ENG-9201 (reduce dep noise), SUP-3345 (customer incident referencing broken lint gating). Notes: The dep-approver deliberately errs conservative: any dep touching server/runtime/infra files is labeled dep/manual. The heuristics are intentionally simple to make future audit easier.
Priya Shah: Please add unit tests around the manifest parser for path-based overrides.
Ethan Park: Added tests in scripts/ci/fixtures and updated heuristics.test.ts (see commit 71d0c6e).
Diego Martinez: The fast-path condition looks risky for mono-repo changes touching docs and packages. Can we gate by a repo-level flag first?
Ethan Park: We implemented the gate flag and the staged-lint workflow reads repository.settings.ci_fastpath (defaults to false) — docs updated.
Lena Karp: CI run failed initially due to an action permissions issue when posting annotations. Re-ran with GH_TOKEN scope fix.
Priya Shah: Approving with one nit: make the dep-approver logs more verbose when labeling dep/risky for triage.
Ethan Park: Added structured log lines and a follow-up ticket ENG-9358 to extend the runtime knowledge graph.
Checks: unit-tests (pass), integration-smoke (pass), staged-lint (pass after 1 rerun), e2e-nightly (skipped for this PR), dependency-scan (pass). One transient failure in staged-lint due to action permissions; rerun succeeded.
Consolidated lint configuration into a single manifest and replaced multiple lint workflows with a staged pipeline. Added a dependency-approval shim that auto-labels low-risk upgrades and reduces noisy manual triage. No functional changes to runtime. Rollout controlled by repo-level flag.
- Remove deprecated workflows in a follow-up cleanup PR
- Monitor metrics: lint pass-rate, PR queue time, dep-approver label distribution for 2 weeks
- Create ENG-9358 to expand dep heuristics and integrate with model-registry for runtime-sensitive dependencies
If the staged-lint job starts to fail for many PRs, flip repo.settings.ci_fastpath=false and open an incident runbook; alerting is configured at console/alerting/lintrunner/alert-rule.yaml. The dep-approver can be disabled by revoking its app installation or setting scripts/ci/dep-approver/config.enabled=false in repo settings.

Motivation: recent regional latency spikes caused aggressive circuit opens and tenant evictions that degraded customer experience. Existing load-shedding reacted to healthy-appearing signals too coarsely and lacked a localized slowpath that can softly trim admission without full eviction. This PR introduces an 'admission tamer' layer coupled with a lightweight 'graceful escort' to manage inflight requests for tenants during transient overloads. The design preserves SLOs by trading reduced concurrency for better p99 latency stability and avoids hard tenant quarantines where possible. Key features: 1) Localized soft-shedding policy that applies per-tenant per-zone admission limits derived from short-window latency histograms; 2) Circuit hint propagation so downstream routers can prefer compatible slowpath variants instead of hard-failing; 3) Graceful escort: an admission queue with time-bounded draining and hedged short-circuit fallback to prevent head-of-line stalls; 4) Telemetry hooks for tracing admission decisions and a new metric (admission_tamer_trim_rate) to drive rollouts; 5) Opt-in runtime flag to enable staged rollout by region. This PR includes unit/integration tests, a small load test harness, and updated docs for the operator flags. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (https://linear.app/ENG/4182/admission-tamer-localized-soft-shedding) - [x] Implementation of runtime admission tamer - [x] Circuit hint propagation and header mapping - [x] Telemetry + dashboards (skeleton) - [x] Tests (unit + integration) - [x] Feature flag + rollout notes Impact: should reduce p99 latency spikes from tenant-driven surges and reduce hard-evictions observed during previous incidents. Rollout plan: enable in a canary region for 48h with observability thresholds before global rollout.
Lena Ortiz (2026-02-11): Please add a short-lived control to disable escort queueing per region for quick rollback. Also call out expected metric cardinality in the docs.
Maya Thompson (2026-02-11): Added region-scoped feature flag and clarified metric cardinality in docs. See config/defaults.yaml and docs/operators/admission_tamer.md
Carlos Nguyen (2026-02-13): Minor nit on time constants: 50ms probe window looks tight in heavy-e2e; suggest 100ms initial window and decaying backoff. Also add unit test for probe expiry edge case.
Maya Thompson (2026-02-13): Increased initial probe window to 100ms, implemented exponential decay and added unit test test_probe_window_expiry. Updated commit d4e6ab3.
Priya Menon (2026-02-15): Telemetry looks good; please ensure admission decisions are logged at debug level only to avoid log noise at high QPS. Approved pending CI.
CI Bot (2026-02-16): Integration test test_graceful_escort.py failed on first run (flaky timeout). Rerun succeeded.
Adds a localized admission tamer and graceful escort for soft-shedding to improve p99 latency stability under tenant spikes. Provides opt-in region rollout, new telemetry (admission_tamer_trim_rate), and header-based circuit hints for safer downstream fallbacks. No breaking changes. Operators: see docs/operators/admission_tamer.md for flags and rollout guidance.
This change was driven by incident 2026-01-27 where region us-east-1 experienced a tenant surge that cascaded through kv warmups. The admission tamer is conservative by default and disabled in global config until canary completes. Ops can instantly disable via feature flag and the gateway will stop propagating circuit-hints if disabled.

Motivation: multiple SDKs implemented ad-hoc credential refresh + stream adapters which caused subtle parity bugs and developer confusion. This PR introduces a lightweight Credential Orchestra (a single coordination surface and policy registry) and ergonomic stream adapters for TypeScript async generators, Python async iterators, and Go channel-based consumers. It also publishes coordinated SDK version bumps and small docs/samples. Summary of changes: 1) credential/orchestra: new orchestrator that exposes a pluggable policy interface (rotate/prefetch/fallback) and telemetry hooks to emit credential events for tracing and audit. 2) sdk-ts: add async-generator->pullstream adapter, new retry presets that bind to credential profile, bump ts-sdk to v1.6.3. 3) sdk-py: introduce typed async iterator wrappers that surface credential hints + backoff presets, bump py-sdk to v0.9.7. 4) sdk-go: add channel-friendly stream adapter with context-aware cancel and a compact credential adapter, bump go-sdk to v1.5.2. 5) tests and e2e: cross-sdk integration tests that validate failover, token rotation during long-lived streams, and telemetry emissions. 6) docs: new design doc and migration notes. Backwards compatibility: default policies preserve existing behavior; users can opt in to the new orchestrator by providing a policy registry when constructing the client. Checklist: - [x] Design doc attached and discussed in ENG-1182 - [x] Unit tests for each SDK adapter - [x] Crosslang e2e validating rotation under load - [x] Telemetry and debug logs verified - [x] Release notes drafted Testing notes: ran full CI, flake on integration test "stream-token-rotation" was investigated and mitigated by increasing retry windows; reran the e2e twice. Rollout plan: squash-merge to main, coordinate SDK package publishes in next release train. Migration notes: examples provided for migrating custom token providers to the new policy interface. Links: Linear ENG-1182 design thread; minimal user-facing examples moved to docs/sdk-migration/credential-orchestra.md
Miguel Ortega: Nice consolidation. Two asks: (1) can we reduce surface area of the public policy interface (it looks like we expose too many internal methods); (2) add a small perf benchmark that measures overhead of orchestration under 1000TPS. Asha: responded that public interface trimmed and added a microbenchmark under integration/benchmarks/cred-orch-bench.ts.
Rina Sato: Telemetry looks good but the event names collide with existing auth.events namespace. Please rename to auth.orch.*. Asha: renamed events and updated docs and tests accordingly.
Evan Cole: Go adapter uses a buffered channel of size 4 by default which caused backlog in one test. Suggest making buffer configurable via client opts. Asha: made buffer size configurable and defaulted to 1 for low-latency consumers.

Motivation: During a recent regional failover we observed abrupt traffic cutovers causing cold KV/cache churn and immediate SLO pressure on the hot region; this led to cascading circuit flips and tenant-visible errors. This change introduces an "attenuated warmup" path for regional fallthrough: when a region is marked as failing/evacuating, the router can opt-in to a gradual handoff that ramps token budgets, warms prefix/KV caches opportunistically, and applies an SLO guard window to avoid immediate full-throughput reroutes. Summary of changes: 1) routing/controller: add WarmupState machine with three phases (sample, ramp, normal) and per-region warmup timers; 2) slo-enforcer: plumb warmup coefficients into budget calculation so SLO-based throttles are relaxed according to ramp schedule but still bounded by tenant SLA; 3) cache-warming: introduce non-blocking async prefetch hooks on routed fallthrough requests to populate KV and prefix caches without stalling the request path; 4) telemetry: new metrics (region_warmup_phase, warmup_allowed_tokens, warmup_cache_prefetch_rate) and detailed auditing for decisions; 5) ops: config knobs and rollout flags (warmup.enabled, warmup.default_window_ms, warmup.initial_fraction) with sensible defaults. Implementation notes: The warmup approach is intentionally conservative: initial_fraction defaults to 0.05 (5% of steady-state token allowance) for the first window_ms (default 15s), then exponentiates towards 1.0 over the configured window with jitter to avoid herd effects. Token allowances are applied at the router token-bucket layer and are additive with existing tenant quotas; this avoids bypassing tenant limits. Cache prefetches are rate-limited and use a bounded worker pool to protect hotspots. The change also adds an operator-visible endpoint to kick a region into warmup manually for postmortem-driven recovery. Backwards compatibility: All warmup behavior is feature-flagged off by default for non-enterprise clusters and scoped to release channels. The router falls back to existing immediate-failover path if warmup is disabled or if the receiving region reports insufficient capacity. Testing and validation: - Unit tests for WarmupState transitions and token math. - Integration tests simulating region drain with synthetic traffic, asserting no spike in 95/99 latency and no increase in error-rate above configured thresholds. - Perf bench (perf-canary) simulating 50k qps burst with warmup enabled showed 0.6x drop in cold-start errors vs immediate failover and a 12% transient increase in median latency during ramp windows (acceptable per SRE policy). - Canary rollout plan described in Ops notes below. Related work: Linear ENG-19345 (regional-fallthrough-warmup) and ENG-19702 (slo-enforcer-budgets). Also references incident notes INC-2026-02-11 where abrupt failover caused regression. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration canaries green - [x] Telemetry metrics added and dashboards drafted - [x] Ops runbook and rollback included - [x] Feature-flag and defaults set to safe values Rollout plan: 1) Enable warmup in preprod and staged perf-canary at 10% of traffic for 24h. 2) Monitor new metrics and 95/99 latency, token drop rate, and cache-prefetch success. 3) Gradually increase traffic to 100% in target region across 48h if no regressions. 4) If SLO regressions occur, operator can toggle warmup.enabled off or reduce warmup.initial_fraction. Rollback: immediate toggle of warmup.enabled to false reverts behavior; warmup state is ephemeral and does not change persisted tenant quotas. Observability: dashboards added in observability-pack with alerts on warmup_failed_prefetch_rate > 1% and region_warmup_phase stuck > 120s. Security and safety: no new privileged data paths added; prefetches respect tenant data access controls and are performed with the same request-scoped principals. Review thread and conversation summary: - Ethan Kline: asked for stronger guardrails around tenant opt-outs; we added tenant opt-out via attribute warmup.allow_opt_out=false and documented in README. - Maya Ruiz: requested a stricter upper-bound on aggregate warmup tokens to avoid overall capacity blowouts; we added a per-region aggregate cap and unit tests. - Samir Ghosh: flagged potential double-counting with existing autoscaler signals; added a regression in autoscaler integration test and a short-circuit that prefers autoscaler capacity hints. Merge notes: CI passed after two reruns of flaky e2e; perf-canary results attached. Merged using squash-and-merge. Reasons this PR is different: rather than an immediate circuit/fallback flip, this introduces a controlled ramp with cache-warm strategies and SLO-aware token math to reduce cascading failures during regional handoffs.

Motivation: We’ve had multiple reports (staging + early beta) of Console results appearing stale and/or routing decisions not reflecting recent experiment config edits. Today we can infer this indirectly from logs and a few cache hit-rate metrics, but we don’t have a first-class signal for “how far behind is the data plane from the control plane” and “are we serving configs older than our intended staleness bound”. This PR introduces a small set of canonical propagation-lag and staleness metrics for route experiments, emitted from the router/policy-evaluator, and wires them into the standard OTel metrics pipeline so they can be used for dashboards + alerting. What’s included: (1) New metrics emitted on config fetch/apply path: redwood.experiments.config_propagation_lag_seconds (histogram), redwood.experiments.config_version_age_seconds (histogram), redwood.experiments.config_stale_reads_total (counter), redwood.experiments.config_last_good_version_timestamp_seconds (gauge), redwood.experiments.config_apply_errors_total (counter). (2) Metric semantics: propagation_lag = now() - config.published_at (as stamped by control plane) at the moment we apply a config snapshot; version_age = now() - config.version_created_at (helps detect long-lived “stuck” versions even if republished); stale_read is incremented when version_age exceeds the router’s configured max_staleness_seconds OR when we fall back to last-known-good due to fetch failure. (3) Dimensions are intentionally limited to avoid cardinality blowups: {region, environment, route_id_normalized} only. We do NOT tag by experiment_id/variant_id. (4) Dashboard exposure: metrics are exported via existing otel-metrics pipeline under the experiments namespace; Grafana dashboards/alerts are tracked in observability-pack (separate PR), but this PR includes the naming + units that those dashboards assume. (5) Draft alert thresholds (not enabled here, for SRE review): Warning if p95(config_propagation_lag_seconds) > 60s for 10m in any region; Critical if p95 > 300s for 5m OR stale_reads_total rate > 1% of config_reads for 10m. These thresholds are intended to align with the control-plane propagation SLO work-in-progress and to be tuned post-beta. Testing: unit tests for lag computation (published_at missing, clock skew guard), integration test that simulates config update and validates histogram observation, and a benchmark check to ensure no significant overhead in the hot path. Notes: This PR is additive and safe to roll out behind existing experiment feature flags; metrics emission occurs regardless of whether a request is assigned to a variant (it’s tied to config apply, not request processing). Related: Slack thread 1736039442-route-experiments-config-propagation-lag, ENG-9023 caching/propagation controls, and SUP-24910 (Console results not updating).
Allison Grant: Can we confirm units and bucket boundaries for the histograms? We’ve had issues where defaults made p95 meaningless. Also please document the exact dimension set; dashboards will assume it.
Logan Wright (author): Good call. Added explicit view config for config_propagation_lag_seconds and config_version_age_seconds (buckets: 1s, 5s, 10s, 30s, 60s, 120s, 300s, 600s). Also updated internal docs with dimensions and an explicit “no experiment_id/variant_id tagging” note.
Sean Gallagher: Two concerns: (1) how do we handle control-plane clock skew vs data-plane? (2) we need a metric for ‘last known good’ usage because that’s operationally distinct from being merely behind.
Logan Wright (author): Added a clamp to 0 when now < published_at (treat as 0 lag and emit config_apply_errors_total with reason=clock_skew_suspected). Also added config_stale_reads_total with reason=last_known_good_fallback and a gauge for last_good_version_timestamp_seconds so we can see when we’re pinned to a snapshot.
Jordan Lee: route_id_normalized dimension: are we using the same normalization as attribution (template path) or raw route key? Raw paths will be a cardinality bomb.
Logan Wright (author): Using normalized route ID from the routing policy layer (template-style ID). Added a small comment + test that ensures we never attach raw path.
Rafael Mendes: Draft thresholds look aggressive for beta. Can we separate ‘propagation lag’ from ‘aggregation lag’ so on-call isn’t chasing the wrong thing?
Logan Wright (author): Agreed; this PR is only data-plane config propagation. Updated docs to call out non-goals (analytics rollups). The alert threshold text is now labeled “draft” and includes guidance to correlate with aggregation job delay metrics before declaring Console stale results as propagation-related.
Allison Grant: Please add to the metrics allowlist and confirm we won’t exceed our standard tag policy.
Logan Wright (author): Added to allowlist_experiments.yaml and kept tags at {region, environment, route_id_normalized}.
Sean Gallagher: Approving with note that enabling alerts should be a separate PR after SLO doc lands.
Rafael Mendes: Approved; please link runbook once created (ENG-9033).

Adds a prefill scoring compiler to generate tenant-aware defaults and attaches per-request quantization tags to telemetry for downstream unit-econ analysis.
Summary: Introduce a prefill scoring compiler that converts workload signals into deterministic default prefill/batching/caching suggestions and emits quantization-tagged telemetry so downstream econ tooling can correlate unit economics with quant profiles. Motivation: Default heuristics are currently noisy across tenants; operations teams request a deterministic, auditable way to derive defaults from sampled traffic, and Research needs request-level quant tagging so regression/delta analysis can surface when quant profiles impact quality-cost tradeoffs. This change bundles three cross-cutting pieces into a single, test-covered PR.

What changed (high level):
- pkg/econ/scorer: new deterministic prefill Scorer with compiled rule pipeline (score, effect estimate, confidence).
- pkg/econ/compiler: compiler that compiles tenant-level workload histograms into static default sets (batch size, cache window, quant profile).
- telemetry/annotator: attaches quant_profile and prefill_score attributes to request telemetry events and spans.
- cmd/prefill-sim: lightweight simulator to validate compiled defaults against sampled traces (used by integration tests).
- docs/operations/prefill-compiler.md: usage and migration notes for Platform/SEs.
- tests/*: unit and integration tests, plus a small e2e using a synthetic tenant trace.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked (ENG-1823)
- [x] Unit tests for scorer and compiler
- [x] Integration tests for telemetry annotations and simulator
- [x] Backwards-compatible telemetry schema (adds optional fields)
- [x] Ops doc for usage and rollback instructions

Commits (summary):
- 1a2b3c4: add scorer prototype and interfaces
- 2b3c4d5: implement compiler optimization pass and rule folding
- 3c4d5e6: telemetry annotator and proto update (telemetry optional fields)
- 4d5e6f7: simulator CLI and e2e test harness
- 5e6f7g8: test hardening, lint fixes, and docs

Files changed (illustrative):
- pkg/econ/scorer/scorer.go (+512/-21)
- pkg/econ/compiler/compiler.go (+392/-98)
- telemetry/annotator/annotator.go (+128/-6)
- cmd/prefill-sim/main.go (+78/-0)
- docs/operations/prefill-compiler.md (+11/-0)
- tests/integration/prefill_compiler_test.go (+166/-307)

Design notes and compatibility:
- The compiler emits an immutable Defaults object per tenant version; Defaults are intended to be suggested values surfaced to the Console and optionally auto-applied by the policy engine. Defaults carry a confidence score and an opaque compiler-version tag so rollbacks and audits can be performed.
- Telemetry adds two optional string fields: telemetry.prefill_score and telemetry.quant_profile_tag. Both are optional to avoid breaking existing consumers; annotator only populates them when the request traverses a node with the annotator middleware (hosted and Dedicated paths).
- Quant tags are stable strings derived from the quant profile name + short hash to allow cheap grouping in analytics pipelines.

Review conversation (summary):
- Asha Patel: "Overall looks good but we should avoid unbounded growth of compiler rules in memory; can we bound compiled rule size and surface a warning?"
- Lina Zhou: "Added a soft cap (maxCompiledRules) and an eviction metric; compiler emits a telemetry.warning when cap is hit. See commit 2b3c4d5."
- Miguel Santos: "Suggest adding a circuit-breaker so if the simulator indicates >5% regression when applying defaults we don't auto-apply."
- Lina Zhou: "Added simulator threshold check and platform flag to opt-in auto-apply. Documented in docs/operations/prefill-compiler.md."
- Ethan Park: "CI shows a flaky test in TestSimulatorLatency under heavy docker load; re-run on CI and consider test stabilization."
- Lina Zhou: "Stabilized by lowering thread reliance and adding a deterministic RNG seed. Re-ran CI; passes now (one rerun)."

CI details:
- Build: passed
- Unit tests: passed
- Integration tests: passed after one rerun (TestSimulatorLatency flaky under heavy host load)
- Lint: passed with gofumpt fixes included

Why this is different from previous prefills:
- Deterministic compiler (not heuristic service) — compiled defaults are stable artifacts that can be versioned and audited.
- Per-request quant tagging — previously quant profiles were only visible at deployment time; now telemetry can tie per-request outcomes to the quant profile used, enabling precise unit-econ regressions and cohorting.
- Lightweight simulator included to validate defaults before any auto-apply action.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy annotator to hosted inference edge (reads optional fields, safe to deploy).
2) Run compiler in dry-run mode for 48h and surface suggested defaults to Console (no auto-apply).
3) Run simulation reports for top 10 tenants and review with SRE/solutions.
4) Flip platform flag to opt-in auto-apply for non-critical tenants behind canary.

Post-merge actions (tracked in ENG-2110):
- Add Console UI for reviewing compiled Defaults (follow-up PR).
- Add an alert for compiler eviction warnings.
- Expand simulator dataset to include production traces (coord with Data team).

Merge: Squash-merged by Asha Patel on 2026-02-19.

If rollback is required:
- Defaults are only suggestions until auto-apply flag is set; disabling the flag prevents further auto-applies. Any applied defaults can be reverted using the Defaults history endpoint (documented).

Motivation: Release orchestration logic and ad-hoc scripts in the repo have diverged over time. This makes multi-stage releases fragile (rollout smoke, artifact signing, and cutover steps are distributed across shell scripts and Circle config). Additionally, recurring dependency churn obscures which packages are most likely to cause presubmit flakiness. This PR introduces a small, deterministic release-phase orchestrator plus a lightweight dependency heatmap generator so teams can see dep-change impact across services.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a release-phase orchestrator binary (go) that defines named phases (prepare, build, smoke, promote, sign, notify) and a YAML phase manifest. The orchestrator runs existing CI tasks in a stable order and provides idempotent hooks for pre/post steps. 2) Replaces several ad-hoc bash release scripts with thin shims that call the orchestrator. 3) Adds an opt-in step in CI to emit a dependency-change fingerprint and contribute to a repo-level heatmap index (compact NDJSON lines). The heatmap output is viewable locally with a small Python viewer script added to tools/dep_heatmap.py. 4) Introduces a minimal migration document and a canary release profile that gates the new orchestrator behind a feature flag in the Circle workflow. 5) Adds unit tests and an integration smoke harness that runs the new phases against the staging release pipeline.

Rollout plan:
- Merge to main behind feature flag and enable canary profile for infra-team.
- Monitor canary for 48 hours, verify release timing and artifact signatures.
- Flip feature flag for more teams and retire legacy script variants after two successful production runs.

Backwards compatibility: The orchestrator defaults to running legacy targets and shells out to pre-existing tooling when a phase has no new handler. No hard-breaking changes to release semantics.

Risks and mitigations:
- Misordered steps could delay releases: added unit tests and a staging harness to validate manifests.
- Heatmap data growth: stored as compact NDJSON with rotation and TTL policies (see tools/heatmap/README).
- Missing env for signing: orchestrator validates secrets up front.

Checklist:
- [x] Orchestrator binary and manifest schema implemented
- [x] Shims for existing scripts added
- [x] CI opt-in step implemented and tested in staging
- [x] Heatmap generator + viewer added
- [x] Unit and integration tests added
- [x] Migration doc + runbook added

Notes: The orchestrator intentionally keeps the phase language minimal to prevent coupling with other infra projects; we plan to iterate on phase hooks if adoption shows friction. Related: ENG-4021 (release reliability initiative), SUP-1182 (support incident that prompted audit). Links: internal runbook https://linear.app/company/ENG-4021 and runbook notes in docs/release/orchestrator.md. Commands to exercise locally: ./bin/release-orch --manifest=examples/demo-manifest.yaml --dry-run and python tools/dep_heatmap.py view data/heatmap.ndjson. This description is intentionally consolidated into a single field per repo PR format guidelines.

Team consensus: move forward with orchestrator behind feature flag, gather canary metrics for 48 hours, expand rollout if stable. Reviewers requested and confirmed exit-code preservation, missing-secrets fail-fast behavior, and a rotation/TTL policy for heatmap artifacts.

Motivation: customers and internal compliance teams requested clearer per-tenant KMS billing signals and cryptographically verifiable residency evidence for data residency audits. This PR implements two cooperating pieces: (1) a KMS usage ratecard emitted by the control plane that tags tokenized usage with KMS key identifiers, key-scopes, and billing tiers; (2) a residency evidence collector that accumulates signed residency assertions per request and writes a compact, append-only proof bundle to the audit store. Scope: server-side control plane (api gateway and audit service), small runtime shim to attach KMS-metadata to request envelopes, and an optional background processor that bundles and signs residency evidence for long-term retention. Backwards compatibility: ratecard fields are additive and gated behind feature flag beta.kms.ratecard; the residency collector is opt-in per-tenant via tenant config allow_residency_proofs=true. Design highlights: - KMS ratecard: emits structured labels (kms_key_id, cmk_scope, provider, billing_tier) in the existing usage event schema to avoid schema proliferation. A new mapping layer converts key metadata (from the KMS catalog) into ratecard tiers using a compact rule table. - Residency evidence collector: request-level residency assertions (region_pin, node_zone, key_origin) are bundled with a short canonicalized context and signed by the audit service's attestation key. Bundles are produced in small epochs (5m) and uploaded to the audit store as gzipped ndjson. - Security controls: residency bundles are encrypted-at-rest using the platform CMK and include a Merkle root to enable spot-check proofs without revealing contents. RBAC: introduced two new fine-grained roles: audit.residency.viewer and billing.kms.rate_reader. These map to RBAC v2 attribute rules so operators can grant cross-account read access for audits without granting write or key unwrap rights. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout in three stages (canary tenants -> beta customers -> all tenants). Beta tenants will get a telemetry dashboard showing KMS usage attribution to validate ratecard mapping. Tests: unit tests for mapping rules and serialization, integration test that verifies signed bundles validate with the attestation public key, end-to-end test that ensures events with kms metadata flow into billing pipelines. Monitoring and alerts: new dashboard panels for ratecard mismatches and residency bundle upload failures, alert on >1% bundle-signing failures in 1h. Operational notes: - Storage retention default 365 days for proof bundles (configurable per-tenant) - Collector runs with a soft quota; exceeding quota results in sampling with downstream notice - Signing keys are rotated using existing CMK rotation job; old bundles retain verification material. Documentation: added docs pages for the ratecard schema and for how to request residency evidence for audits. Implementation details and migration steps are included below.
Marco Silva: Please ensure the ratecard mapping table is deterministic across control-plane replicas; I suggest adding a lockless versioned map and unit tests.
Aisha Patel: Addressed by making the mapper read-only after load and adding a version header to events; added unit tests in mapping_test.go.
Renee Cho: Who can read residency bundles? We need strict RBAC and an audit trail for access.
Aisha Patel: Added audit.residency.viewer role, documented the access patterns, and enforced server-side check before decryption.
Liam O'Connor: CI failed on lint in epoch_producer.go earlier. Please run gofmt and re-run the pipeline.
Aisha Patel: Fixed formatting and adjusted the goroutine shutdown sequence; CI passed on rerun.

Introduced residency evidence collector producing signed proof bundles for audits (opt-in per-tenant).
New RBAC roles: audit.residency.viewer, billing.kms.rate_reader.
Telemetry dashboards and alerts for ratecard mismatches and bundle-signing failures.

Motivation: Many tenants run with generic batching/cache/quant defaults that either miss cost savings or breach latency SLOs depending on workload shape. This PR adds a lightweight "cost telemetry profile" pipeline that synthesizes per-tenant (and per-model) batch/cache/quant recommendations from observed token-length distributions, cold-start rates, and KV-cache hit patterns. The goal is automated, safe defaults that reduce unit cost while preserving latency SLOs and providing conservative fallbacks.
This change introduces: 1) a telemetry-driven profile generator (ct-profilegen) that consumes sampling metrics and emits a ranked set of candidate profiles (batch size, batch timeout, kv_cache_ttl, quant_profile_id) with confidence scores; 2) a small runtime hook in the batch orchestrator to accept a profile priority list and apply the highest-confidence compatible profile at request routing time; 3) a compact on-disk catalog format (pkg/telemetry/cost_profiles.yaml) and migration/backfill tooling to propose profiles for existing tenants; 4) Console integration: a profile suggestions card (Console) with Explain mode showing expected cost delta and latency impact; 5) safety controls: feature-flagged rollout, canary assignment by tenant cohort, and automatic rollback if 95th-pct latency regresses beyond configured budget. Backfill is opt-in: ct-profilegen backfill --tenant <id> returns a dry run. Benchmarks: end-to-end simulation on sampled traffic shows 8-14% token-unit cost reduction for medium-tail workloads and no measurable p95 latency regression under our test harness. The PR includes unit tests for the scoring heuristics, e2e backfill dry-run tests, and a small perf harness used for the numbers above.
Diego Mendez: Can we make the scoring function more explainable? Request adding a breakdown of component contributions (batching vs kv vs quant).
Author (Aisha): Added a scoring breakdown in the CLI --explain output and a unit test for the breakdown algorithm (commit 7890ab).
Claire Zhou: Please validate that quant_profile selection never picks unsupported quant formats for a given GPU family; also add a fallback path.
Author (Aisha): Added compatibility check and fallback to 'float32' safe profile; added compatibility matrix in cost_profiles.yaml.
Oliver Park: CI flakes on the perf harness occasionally; make the harness tolerate small variance or run as tolerable-smoke.
Author (Aisha): Perf harness now runs under a stable-seed mode in CI and has a 2% tolerance threshold; CI green on rerun.
- Add telemetry-driven cost profile generator (ct-profilegen) to propose batching/cache/quant defaults per tenant.
- Console: profile suggestion card with explain mode and estimated cost/latency delta.
- Runtime: orchestrator respects profile priority lists and falls back to safe defaults.
- Migration: opt-in backfill CLI and catalog format.
- Safety: feature flag, canary rollout, and automatic rollback on latency regressions.
Run: cli/ct-profilegen --sample-source=metrics-db --dry-run --tenant=<id> to get suggested profiles
Deploy feature-flagged orchestrator and assign a small tenant cohort for canary
Validate Console shows expected delta in the Suggestion card and clicking Explain shows scoring breakdown
Run tests: make test-unit && make test-e2e(cost-profile-backfill)
The cost_profiles.yaml includes compatibility matrix entries. If you observe unexpected latency spikes after applying a profile, use the 'profile revert' endpoint or disable the feature flag. Backfill uses historical sampling and will not autopromote profiles without manual approval unless the tenant is part of the auto-apply cohort defined in charts/values-ctprofiles.yaml.
unit_cost_delta_pct: -8 to -14 for medium-tail workloads; p95_latency_delta_ms: ~0 (safety budget 5%); kv_cache_hit_increase_pct: 2-6

Motivation: Cross-language inconsistency in stream backpressure hints and retry presets was causing client confusion and subtle production regressions when teams migrated code between Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. This PR introduces a compact, explicit surface for 'stream-advice' (an optional per-request metadata envelope), a small RetryProfileCompiler that emits canonical presets (fast, balanced, conservative), and ergonomic helpers across the three SDKs so callers get the same defaults and names regardless of language. Main goals: 1) Parity of defaults and environment variable names, 2) Small ergonomic helpers to set common retry/backoff shapes, 3) Maintainable codegen-friendly templates so future SDKs can pick up presets automatically. What changed (high level):
- Introduced a lightweight 'stream-advice' header that transports backpressure hints and a client-visible 'preferred-batch-ms' integer. The wire representation is opaque JSON under X-Stream-Advice but SDKs expose typed helpers. Example (Python usage): client.stream(messages, stream_advice=StreamAdvice(preferred_batch_ms=10, urgency="balanced"))
- Added RetryProfileCompiler: takes a small declarative profile (max_attempts, initial_backoff_ms, backoff_multiplier, jitter) and compiles to SDK-specific retry configs. Compiler lives in /internal/retry/presets and emits JSON templates checked into each SDK package for codegen.
- Converged env vars and flags: REDWOOD_SDK_RETRY_PRESET (values: fast|balanced|conservative), REDWOOD_STREAM_HINTS_DISABLED for compatibility.
- SDK surface changes: * Python: new module redwood.retry.presets and StreamAdvice dataclass, high-level helper client.with_retry_preset("balanced") returns wrapped client. * TypeScript: exported RetryPresets and streamAdvice() factory in @redwood/sdk (ts) with typed interfaces and improved JSDoc. * Go: added retry/presets package and StreamAdvice struct, plus functional options on client.New to pick presets.
- Auth interaction: preserved existing token rotation behavior; RetryProfileCompiler emits header-safe recommendations only. No auth protocol changes.
- Tests: added cross-sdk smoke harness (scripts/ci/smoke_cross_sdk.sh) that runs a small end-to-end scenario against local dev runtime with streaming toggled. Also added unit tests for compiler and per-SDK adapters.
Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear (ENG-1138) - [x] Added unit tests for compiler and adapters - [x] Added cross-sdk smoke CI job (gated) - [x] Backwards compatibility flag (REDWOOD_STREAM_HINTS_DISABLED) - [x] Release notes drafted Why this approach: By keeping the runtime semantics optional and encapsulated behind a small header + typed helpers we avoid making breaking wire changes while getting strong ergonomics and parity for developers migrating across SDKs. Rollout plan: Feature gated off by default in hosted canary, opt-in in dedicated/private during initial rollout. Monitoring: Added telemetry events when a non-default preset is used (sdk.preset.{name} with anonymized counts).
Ravi Patel: Can we avoid adding another env var surface? Suggest reusing REDWOOD_SDK_RETRY_PRESET and adding a value 'none' instead of REDWOOD_STREAM_HINTS_DISABLED.
Maya Chen (author): Good call. Updated to reuse REDWOOD_SDK_RETRY_PRESET and accept 'none' as disabled in the SDK adapters; preserved explicit REDWOOD_STREAM_HINTS_DISABLED only for legacy toggles in runtime (kept for canary compatibility).
Owen Kim: Tests look good, but the TS JSDoc needs an example showing how streamAdvice interacts with streaming backpressure in the browser. Also request: add an integration test where preferred_batch_ms is respected by the local runtime mock.
Maya Chen: Added browser-focused example to README and expanded smoke script to assert preferred_batch_ms in the runtime mock. PTAL.
Sofia Martínez: Approve after CI green. Observability hooks look fine; please ensure telemetry counts are low-cardinality.
Liam O'Connor: Minor nit: go client option API should return an error only if invalid preset name; otherwise default. Fixed in follow-up commit.
User-facing: Introduces optional stream-advice header and cross-sdk Retry Presets (fast|balanced|conservative). SDKs provide ergonomic helpers: Python: StreamAdvice dataclass + client.with_retry_preset; TypeScript: streamAdvice() factory and RetryPresets export; Go: presets package + client option. Backwards compatible by default; set REDWOOD_SDK_RETRY_PRESET=none to disable. Internal: adds RetryProfileCompiler and cross-sdk smoke job.
Run scripts/ci/smoke_cross_sdk.sh against a local dev runtime (see docs/sdk/streaming-advice.md). Unit tests in each SDK package were added; run pytest -q in redwood-sdk-python and npm test in redwood-sdk-typescript and go test ./... in redwood-sdk-go.

Motivation: Our lint and formatting jobs have drifted into multiple ad-hoc entrypoints (JS, Python, docs), causing duplicated setup and flakey caches. This PR centralizes the lint entrypoint, standardizes environment setup across runners, and adds a lightweight dep-staleness CI check to proactively surface out-of-sync lockfiles and requirement pin drift.

What this PR does (summary):
- Introduces .github/workflows/lint-orchestrator.yml: a single workflow that dispatches language-specific jobs (node, python, md) with consistent bootstrap steps and cache keys.
- Adds tools/ci/lint-entrypoint.sh: unified bash entrypoint used by all lint jobs; loads environment variables, prepares venv/node_modules, and invokes the language-specific linters.
- Adds scripts/check-dep-staleness.py: a small, fast script that verifies lockfiles (yarn.lock, poetry.lock, requirements.txt) are in sync with manifests; exits non-zero when drift is detected and prints actionable remediation commands.
- Bumps dev deps: eslint@8.55.0, prettier@2.9.0 (minor bumps kept intentionally minimal), poetry-core pinned to 1.6.x in CI to avoid transient resolver differences.
- Removes duplicate CI steps from legacy workflows and replaces them with references to the new orchestrator via workflow_call.
- Update README/CONTRIBUTING with quick instructions for running the unified lint locally and resolving lockfile drift.

Checklist: 
- [x] Centralize lint orchestration and remove duplicated setup steps
- [x] Add dep-staleness CI job with clear error output
- [x] Keep dev dependency bumps conservative and opt-in for runtime dependencies
- [x] Add docs for contributors and CI troubleshooting

Why this approach: consolidating the entrypoint reduces maintenance burden and standardizes cache key logic which was a major source of flakiness. The dep-staleness check is intentionally lightweight (no full dependency resolution) and acts as an early-warning to avoid post-merge grind where lockfiles are out of sync across language stacks. Linear: ENG-4981 tracked the lint flakiness; ENG-5013 requested lockfile checks for cross-team stability.

Notes for reviewers: The shell entrypoint contains guardrails for CI (fast-fail on missing interpreters, clear hints for fix commands). The python script is pure stdlib except for typing and runs on GitHub's Ubuntu images. If you want a separate action later we can extract the script into a composite action, but keeping it in-repo keeps iteration fast.

Release impact: None on runtime code. This is CI/tooling only.

Related: references to prior CI cleanups (see ENG-3720 and pr-71220) for historical context.
Reviewer Asha: requested clearer error output and an example in CONTRIBUTING.
Author: implemented expanded error messages and added an example failure output.
Reviewer Carlos: asked to avoid pulling in new third-party GH actions; author replaced the external composite with a workflow_call.
Reviewer Maya: requested a smoke test for the staleness checker; added a small unit smoke and CI run to exercise the path.
All reviewers approved after the follow-ups.

2) add dep-staleness checker and unit smoke (Jordan Kim)
3) replace legacy lint jobs to call orchestrator (Jordan Kim)
4) update CONTRIBUTING and add local run docs (Jordan Kim)

Motivation: we see recurring noisy alerts driven by high-cardinality token-level signals and duplicate symptom alerts at both the invocation and per-token levels. This PR adds a compact per-token phase aggregator ("token-stepper") plus an alert deconfliction layer that correlates per-token anomalies with invocation-level health to reduce duplicate noisy alerts and improve SRE signal-to-noise. Design summary: token-stepper collects phase durations for each token (parse/encode/kv-lookup/generation/postprocess) but emits a laddered histogram with 8 fixed buckets per phase to keep cardinality bounded; each metric includes a three-bit sampler tag so we can reconstruct representative traces for tail cases without full trace capture; the alert deconflict engine receives candidate alerts from token and invocation pipelines, computes a lightweight correlation score (time overlap, tenant, route, and prompt-shape hash) and suppresses or groups noisy duplicates according to configurable thresholds and backoff windows. Implementation highlights: new collector: observability/metrics/token_stepper_collector.go implements collection + bucketing + sampler tag; tracing bridge: observability/tracing/stepper-trace-bridge.go maps sampler tags to trace sampling decisions; alerting engine: pkg/alerting/alert_deconflict.py implements correlation algorithm and backoff policy and exposes a metrics endpoint for deconflict decisions; dashboard: observability/dashboards/token-stepper-overview.json (Grafana) for laddered latency stacks, deconflict rate and suppression breakdown; docs and runbook: docs/runbooks/token-stepper.md documents rollout steps, expected metric shapes and how to debug suppressed alerts. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind token_stepper_v1; staged rollout to 10% of traffic for 48h (observability tests + manual SRE review), then 50% for 24h, then global; backward-compatible: if feature flag disabled, collectors emit no new metrics; metric name namespace is opt-in. Migration notes: new metrics use a short 3-character suffix to avoid collision with existing metric families and require a lightweight TSDB schema bump to add laddered histograms; there is a one-time migration job described in the runbook. Testing: unit tests for bucketing and deconflict logic added (tests/unit/test_stepper_bucket.py, tests/unit/test_deconflict.py); integration tests simulate tail sampling and verify trace backfills (tests/integration/test_token_stepper.py). Performance: collector optimized to perform per-token accounting inline with amortized allocations; benchmark in perf/bench_token_stepper.md shows <1% p99 latency impact at 90% traffic sampling. Safety: added rate limits to deconflict decisions to avoid thundering herd suppression; added a fallback path to always surface invocation-level alerts for critical error classes. Why different from previous work: focuses on bounded-cardinality per-token shapes plus a heuristic deconflict engine to reduce alert duplication rather than more expensive span-join strategies. Links: Linear ENG-4215 covers design; SUP-3321 is the support ticket describing noisy alerts observed in production. Checklist: [x] tests added [x] docs/runbook added [x] dashboard added [x] feature-flag gated [x] perf bench completed; See changed_files for exact diffs and runbook for operational guidance.
Ravi Kapoor: Can we guarantee the metric cardinality bound across diverse prompt shapes?; Asha Patel: We limit per-route and per-phase labels and use 8 fixed buckets + a 3-bit sampler tag. We canonicalize prompt-shape via a stable shingled hash to avoid explosion.; Marta Svensson: Alert deconflict looks promising but please add a conservative default so we don't drop critical alerts; Asha Patel: added backoff windows and a whitelist of critical error classes; updated runbook to surface suppressed alerts and how to opt-out per-tenant.; Liam O'Connor: unit tests look good; could you add a small benchmark to demonstrate overhead?; Asha Patel: added perf/bench_token_stepper.md and included microbenchmarks showing <1% p99 impact at configured sampling rates.; Marta Svensson: approved; Ravi Kapoor: approved after small naming nit; Maintainer (merge): squash-merged after green CI and manual SRE signoff.
Adds a bounded-cardinality per-token phase metric (token-stepper) and an alert deconfliction engine to reduce duplicate invocation/token alerts. Feature-flagged rollout. Improves SRE signal-to-noise and adds a Grafana overview and runbook.
Feature flag token_stepper_v1 must be toggled per-cluster; run the provided TSDB migration job before enabling on >50% traffic; follow docs/runbooks/token-stepper.md for rollback; monitor metric token.stepper.deconflict.suppressed_rate and token.stepper.ladder.* buckets during rollout.
Enable feature flag on staging, run tests/integration/test_token_stepper.py, drive synthetic tail traces using perf/bench_token_stepper.md harness, verify deconflict metrics drop duplicate alert rate by >30% in dashboard, ensure critical invocation alerts still surface.
payload.title: introduce-token-stepper-metrics-and-alert-deconflict

Motivation and summary:
This PR brings parity improvements for the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions surface focused on: (1) demultiplexing 'stop' signals that mix arrays and token-level heuristics, (2) providing a deterministic fallback path when streaming encounters tool/function-call boundaries, and (3) normalizing logprob/role metadata in structured responses so downstream SDKs receive stable envelopes. The goal is to reduce customer migration friction for chat parity while improving streaming stability for tool-calling workloads.

What changed (high level):
- Added a StopDemux module that canonicalizes stop inputs (string | array | regex-like tokens) into a unified internal predicate used by the streaming agent.
- Implemented StreamFallbackCoordinator: when the streaming pipeline detects an impending tool/function call boundary or partial JSON emission, it flushes a deterministic final chunk and seamlessly switches to a framed non-stream mode for the remainder of the response, avoiding truncated tools and malformed structured output.
- Normalizer for logprobs and role annotations that converts token-level logprob arrays into a concise envelope if the client requested logprobs=true. This preserves compatibility with OpenAI clients expecting token/prob pairs while keeping streaming deltas small.
- Tests and integration harness updates to exercise mixed stop forms and tool-calls under high-concurrency, including a synthetic replay of a customer prompt that surfaced earlier truncation issues.

Commits (summary):
- 1a2b3c4: add stop demux and unit tests
- 2b3c4d5: implement stream fallback coordinator and integration tests
- 3c4d5e6: normalize logprob envelope and role metadata serializer
- 4d5e6f7: update chatv1 adapter to use new canonical stop predicate
- 5e6f7g8: add e2e harness scenarios and CI flaky test fixes

Files touched (illustrative):
- runtime/streaming/stop_demux.go (new) - core canonicalizer for stop inputs
- runtime/streaming/fallback_coordinator.go (new) - arbitration logic for streaming->framed fallback
- runtime/structured/role_logprob_normalizer.go (modified) - output envelope changes
- api/adapters/openai_chat_adapter.go (modified) - wire new components into /v1/chat handler
- tests/e2e/fixtures/stop_variants.json (new) - replay corpus

Small snippet (stop demux public API):
- CanonicalizeStop(input interface()) -> StopPredicate
- StopPredicate.Match(token string) bool

Review convo highlights:
- Marco Silva (reviewer): "Great separation between the demux and the streaming coordinator. Two asks: add property-based tests for exotic stop inputs and make the fallback window tunable via config with a reasonable default."
- Author (Priya): "Added quickcheck-style property tests that fuzz arrays/strings/null; added FallbackWindowMs config with default 50ms and documented in runtime/README.md."
- Ana López (reviewer): "Concern about metric cardinality when creating distinct fallback causes per request — recommend coalescing reasons."
- Author reply: "Coalesced fallback reasons into 'tool_boundary', 'malformed_json', 'timeout' enums; added a single tag on the request trace."
- Devon Carter (approver): "Verified e2e scenario. CI green locally and on GHA; approved for cherry-pick to release/* if we want the backport."

CI and QA notes:
- GitHub Actions: unit (pass), integration (pass), e2e (pass), lint (pass). One flaky test (stream/heartbeat_test) was stabilized by increasing the emulated scheduler quantum in the harness.
- Performance: microbench shows <3% median latency increase for non-streaming requests; streaming tool-call flows see a 10-15% decrease in truncation-related retries.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- API contract unchanged: incoming /v1/chat parameters continue to accept 'stop' as string or list. Internally we canonicalize — no client change required.
- For clients that parse token-level logprob arrays, the envelope is preserved when logprobs=true; the normalizer emits a compact token/prob list and a 'logprob_format' header set to 'compact-v1' so SDKs can detect the shape.

Merge details:
- Merge method: squash and merge
- Merged by: Ana López
- Changelog: added to v0.42.0 changelog under 'OpenAI compatibility' as 'robust stop handling and streaming fallback for tool-calls'

Follow-ups and TODOs:
- ENG-2459: Add telemetry to measure how often fallbacks occur by customer (privacy-safe sampling).
- ENG-2460: Expose a user-facing parameter to prefer framed-mode for responses that will include heavy JSON/tool payloads.
- Cleanup: remove a couple of internal debug flags after one-week canary across dedicated clusters.

Notes for on-call / SRE:
- If customers report double outputs or partial tool-call duplications, check the 'stream_fallback_reason' tag in traces and correlate with FallbackWindowMs setting.
- Rollout plan: gradual canary to 10% of hosted traffic for 48h, then 50% for 24h, full rollout. This PR was deployed to canary and monitored for 72h with no regressions.
Normalization of /v1/chat stop signals and stream fallback to stable framing for tool-calls; no API surface break.
added to v0.42.0 changelog under 'OpenAI compatibility' as 'robust stop handling and streaming fallback for tool-calls'

Context: Customer onboarding requests for region-restricted service principals and recent audit incidents revealed gaps in how principal attributes were propagated to downstream KMS routing and audit signing. This PR introduces a location-aware service-principal assertion model and increases entropy in audit signing to make header-level deduplication more robust while preserving existing RBAC v2 evaluation paths. Motivation: 1) Ensure RBAC decisions can be made using the originating service principal's declared location and its verified KMS affinity. 2) Prevent collision and replay in signed audit envelopes across tenants and regions by adding a low-cost entropy field into the audit signature payload. 3) Make KMS envelope routing tolerant of missing explicit region claims by falling back to an asserted principal location with configurable trust policies. Changes in this PR: - Add a new attribute 'principal.location' to service principal attestation and map it into RBAC v2 attribute sets. - Implement a location assertion verifier that consults configured identity providers and tenant allowlists; verifier emits a 'location_strength' metric. - Update KMS routing policy to check for explicit request-level kms.region, then principal.location, then tenant.fallthrough_region in that order. - Introduce AuditEntropySigner: adds a nonce and timestamp into audit signature preimage, signed with existing envelope keys. Nonce is deterministic-per-request-path+timestamp to keep envelope size small. - Add unit and integration tests covering attribute propagation, routing fallback, and audit envelope uniqueness. - Documentation: new security guide for operators on configuring principal trust levels and KMS routing precedence. Migration and rollout notes: The feature is behind an opt-in feature flag (feature.location_principals). Default behavior is unchanged. Rollout plan: enable in canary region for 48 hours, monitor location_strength and audit_signature_collision metrics, then progressive rollout. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed by Security and Platform - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Metrics and dashboards updated - [x] Docs added - [x] Feature gated behind flag

High level implications: - No immediate breaking changes; policies that rely on principal claims will be able to opt into using principal.location selectors. - Enables more precise KMS region pinning for service principals when request-level region is absent. - Improves audit envelope resistance to accidental collisions in high-throughput tenants.
Liam O'Connor: Why is the nonce deterministic? We discussed non-deterministic nonces for stronger replay resistance. Response: deterministicNonce combines request path + truncated timestamp to keep envelope size small while still avoiding same-path collisions; we also increment timestamp granularity. Added tests demonstrating reduced collision windows.
Priya Desai: Need clearer operator guidance when identity provider cannot assert location. Response: added section in docs with examples and feature flag to fallback to tenant-level region or fail-open/fail-closed options.
Evelyn Soto: CI failure on TestKMSRoute_when_no_region; fix by handling nil tenant.fallthrough_region. Response: added guard and new unit test.
Added support for asserted service principal locations used by RBAC v2 and KMS routing. Introduced AuditEntropySigner to reduce audit envelope collisions. Feature is opt-in via 'feature.location_principals'. Operators should read the new security guide for configuration and migration steps.
1) To enable: set feature.location_principals=true in operator config and restart authz service. 2) If identity provider cannot assert location, configure fallback: tenant.fallthrough_region or allow fail-open to use request region. 3) Monitor telemetry/secure-principal-location.json dashboard and watch 'audit_signature_collision' metric during rollout.
Unit tests cover attribute mapping, verifier edge cases, and audit signer nonces. Integration tests deployed to canary region simulating mixed identity providers. Observed zero collisions in 72h synthetic traffic test at 10k req/s for canary tenant.
payload.title: introduce-location-aware-service-principal-assertions-and-audit-entropy
