Context: As part of the Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping rollout, we need baseline reporting for the last ~90 days (and optionally 2 quarters) so we can validate category distribution and SLA compliance by type/owner. Not all historical incidents have incident_type set in incident-bot (or the value is missing due to older bot versions / INT-772). This PR adds an offline backfill job that infers incident_type/subtype from existing logs/annotations (incident-bot events, alert payloads, and a small set of high-signal routing/serving markers) and writes the result into the analytics store used by incident dashboards. This is explicitly not used for live incident routing or gating; it is for historical reporting only.

What this does: (1) Adds a backfill pipeline stage `incident_taxonomy_backfill` that consumes incident timeline events and related alert/log records over a configurable time window. (2) Implements an inference function that maps symptoms/signals to v1 taxonomy categories (e.g., 5xx overload, latency regression, streaming disconnects, routing fallback misbehavior, capacity/fleet shortage, control plane outage, auth/RBAC failure, telemetry blind spot, private connectivity/config). (3) Emits `incident_type`, `incident_subtype`, `inference_source`, and `confidence` to the `analytics.incidents_enriched` table and keeps the original human-entered fields intact (we never overwrite). (4) Adds a CLI entrypoint for one-off runs and a scheduled job definition for the standard “last 90 days” backfill.

Accuracy + caveats (important): This is best-effort classification with known limitations. It is intentionally conservative: when multiple types match or the evidence is weak, it emits incident_type=unknown and a low confidence score. We also preserve contributing signals for audit/debug in logs, but we do not store raw log lines in the analytics output. The mapping is based on an allowlist of v1 types/subtypes to avoid label/cardinality explosion. This should be good enough for aggregate reporting (top categories, trend lines), but not for per-incident root cause analysis.

Signals used (high level): incident-bot fields/tags where present; alert payload fields (service/route, http status family, SLO burn labels); routing fallback_reason enums (from pr-28437) where available; a small set of runtime symptoms (OOM/kv-cache thrash/scheduler stall markers) when they appear as structured log annotations; and control plane error codes for config write failures. The inference prioritizes explicit incident-bot taxonomy when present, then structured alert payload taxonomy when present, then falls back to heuristics.

Testing/validation: Added unit tests for the inference rules and golden fixtures for a few representative incident timelines. Added a dry-run mode that reports distribution by inferred type and % unknown so we can iterate without writing. Ran on staging for 14 days of data: ~71% inferred with >=0.7 confidence, ~19% unknown, ~10% low-confidence inferred (mostly multi-cause capacity+routing incidents). We expect unknown to drop as more historical incidents have explicit taxonomy set via the bot.

Follow-ups: (a) Tune heuristics for multi-cause incidents (primary vs contributing) after taxonomy workshop feedback; (b) add a small manual review UI/workflow to correct a subset of low-confidence inferences; (c) document the intended use (aggregate only) in the dashboards spec and ops guide.

Privacy/security: The enriched table contains only incident identifiers, timestamps, taxonomy fields, and a small set of non-PII structured attributes (service, region, tier). No customer prompts/responses, request bodies, or IP addresses are persisted by this job.
Allison Grant (Observability): Please confirm we’re not introducing any new high-cardinality labels or writing raw log lines into analytics. Also, can we ensure the output values are strictly the taxonomy allowlist (unknown included)? Mei Lin (author): Confirmed. Output is constrained to `incident_taxonomy_allowlist.py`; unknown is the only fallback. We do not persist raw log lines; the job only reads structured fields and writes taxonomy + a small set of attributes (service, region, tier). Added an explicit schema validation test to fail if an out-of-allowlist value is produced.

Aisha Bello (SLO/SLA dashboards): How will we avoid confusing inferred values with human-entered values in dashboards? We need to be able to filter/compare. Mei Lin: Added `inference_source` (human|alert_payload|heuristic|unknown) and `confidence` to the output. The dashboard query can default to human when present; otherwise use inferred. I also added a note in docs/ops/incident-taxonomy/backfill-job.md.

Rafael Mendes (SRE): Multi-cause incidents: if the timeline has both fleet capacity alerts and routing fallback_reason spikes, which wins? Mei Lin: Current priority is (1) human-set taxonomy (if present), (2) control-plane outage/auth failures (more specific), (3) capacity/fleet shortage when we see sustained saturation/provisioning lag without healthy fallback, (4) routing fallback misbehavior when fallback_reason indicates policy/health misrouting and 5xx increases are tied to routing changes. When both match strongly, we emit unknown + low confidence rather than guessing. I added tests for the “capacity then routing” fixture.

Ethan Park (Control plane): Any coupling to control plane internals that could break? Mei Lin: Only uses stable error codes and structured incident annotations already emitted; if absent, the rule doesn’t trigger. No direct reads from control plane DB.

Sergio Costa: Minor: Can we add a dry-run summary output (counts by type + % unknown) to make iterations faster? Mei Lin: Added `--dry-run` and `--print-summary` to CLI; wired into job logs in staging.
Internal: Added an offline backfill job to infer incident taxonomy for historical incidents to support reliability reporting. Does not affect live incident routing or customer-facing behavior.
payload.title: Backfill incident_type/subtype from logs pipeline for historical reporting

payload.body:
Adds the Console backend endpoint used by the new “Rollback” button for Optimization Config versions. This PR focuses on server-side confirmation/guardrails so the Console UI can remain thin and we avoid dangerous client-only checks.

Key behavior
- New endpoint: POST /internal/console/optimization-config/rollbacks
  - Triggers a rollback for a given scope (tenant + model + region) to a target config_version_id.
  - Returns a rollback_operation_id and the initial operation state.
- Confirmation model
  - Requires a confirmation payload computed server-side and echoed back by the client (type-to-confirm UX can be driven from this).
  - The server recomputes the confirmation on request and rejects if it doesn’t match (prevents stale modal confirmations).
- Guardrails (server-enforced)
  - Blast-radius summary + limits: rejects requests that exceed allowed scope cardinality for Console-triggered rollback (e.g., wildcard tenant + wildcard model).
  - Cooldown: prevents repeated rollback thrash for the same scope within a configurable window (default 15m) unless caller has override permission.
  - Safety checks: disallow rollback while an apply operation is actively progressing for the same scope (must pause/cancel first).
  - Version checks: cannot rollback to a version that is not in the “promoted/known-good” state unless override is present.
  - Idempotency: supports optional Idempotency-Key header to avoid duplicate rollback operations on retries.
- RBAC / audit
  - Enforces permission optimization_config.rollback at the endpoint.
  - Emits audit events: optimization_config.rollback_requested and optimization_config.rollback_rejected with standardized fields (request_id, actor, scope, from_version, to_version, reason, confirmation_hash).

API details
- Request fields (high level)
  - scope: tenant_id, model_id, region (no wildcards from Console path)
  - target_version_id
  - reason (required; displayed in history/audit)
  - confirmation: { summary_hash, typed_phrase } (typed_phrase is validated against the server-provided phrase)
- Response fields (high level)
  - rollback_operation_id
  - state: queued|running|completed|failed
  - active_version_before
  - target_version
  - effective_cooldown_until (when applicable)

Implementation notes
- Confirmation computation lives in ConsoleRollbackConfirmationService and includes: scope display name(s), current active version, target version, and a deterministic hash of {scope, from, to, cooldown_bucket}.
- Cooldown is stored in control plane as a scope-keyed record with TTL; implemented with a compare-and-set to avoid race conditions under concurrent requests.
- Conflict detection uses the existing rollout/apply operation table: if there is a non-terminal apply operation for the same scope, rollback is rejected with HTTP 409 and a machine-readable error code APPLY_IN_PROGRESS.
- Keeps the endpoint under /internal/console/* for now; public rollback API remains in the control plane service surface (tracked separately) and will call into the same underlying RollbackOrchestrator.

Testing
- Unit tests cover confirmation mismatch, blast-radius rejection, cooldown enforcement, and idempotency.
- Integration tests cover 409 on apply-in-progress and a happy-path rollback request emitting audit events.

Rollout
- Endpoint is feature-flagged (console_optimization_rollback_enabled) and returns 404 when disabled to avoid exposing partial functionality.

Follow-ups
- Hook up Console UI to show effective_cooldown_until and suggested next action (“wait” vs “request override”).
- Add support for Dedicated “shard” scopes once shard-based rollouts land (ENG-4824).

Refs
- Linear: ENG-4828, ENG-4825
- Related audit taxonomy work: ENG-4826
- Addresses internal on-call confusion from INT-3390 by making permission errors explicit and returning required_permission in the error payload.
console-backend: add rollback controller + request/response DTOs
guardrails: implement blast radius checks + scope validators
cooldown: add scope-keyed rollback cooldown store with CAS
security: enforce optimization_config.rollback + structured audit events
tests: add unit + integration coverage for conflicts/idempotency
Chloe Martin (review): Can we avoid trusting any client-provided blast radius fields? I only want the server to compute what’s being rolled back and what phrase is required.
Hannah Rivera (author): Yep — updated so the client sends only scope + target_version_id + reason. Server recomputes summary + typed phrase requirement and validates a summary_hash derived from server computation. Client cannot widen scope without failing validation.
Jada Williams (review): For the confirmation hash, include something that changes if cooldown changes; otherwise a user could keep an old modal open and confirm later unexpectedly.
Hannah Rivera (author): Added cooldown_bucket (floor(now/5m)) to the confirmation hash input. Also the endpoint recomputes the confirmation on every request; stale confirmations get CONFIRMATION_STALE.
Sean Gallagher (review): Cooldown default 15m seems ok, but we need a way for on-call to override during a Sev. Please ensure the error includes the remaining cooldown and a clear next step.
Hannah Rivera (author): Implemented override via permission optimization_config.rollback.override. Rejection now returns cooldown_until and required_permission in the payload. Console can surface the remaining time and an escalation path.
Marcus Lin (security review): Audit events need to include request_id and actor type (human vs service) for SIEM correlation. Also avoid logging the typed phrase verbatim.
Hannah Rivera (author): Added request_id propagation + actor_type. Typed phrase is not logged; we log only confirmation_hash and whether typed_phrase_valid=true/false.
Chloe Martin (review): One more thing — reject rollback if an apply is running for the same scope. We don’t want mixed states.
Hannah Rivera (author): Added conflict check against non-terminal apply operations; returns 409 APPLY_IN_PROGRESS with the active_operation_id for linking to the rollout page.
Jada Williams (approval): LGTM. The server-side recompute + hash validation should prevent stale confirms and client spoofing.
Sean Gallagher (approval): Looks good for beta. Please make sure the dashboard annotations pick up rollback_operation_id (handled in other PR).
Marcus Lin (approval): Approved contingent on not logging typed_phrase and having required_permission in authz failures — both addressed.
Console backend now supports triggering Optimization Config rollbacks with server-side blast-radius confirmation and cooldown guardrails (feature-flagged).
payload.title: Console: add rollback trigger endpoint with server-side confirmation checks

payload.body:
Context: Customers reported rare production hangs when streaming long responses with function calls and structured JSON boundaries via the OpenAI-compat endpoint. Symptoms included stalled client streams when upstream frames were coalesced across network segments, duplicated trailing delimiters on reconnect, and occasional corrupt partial-JSON emitted to downstream consumers. Repro: long chat with streaming function_call followed by large JSON output and intermittent packet drops; reproduce with tests/sse/test_fragment_replay.py and a patched netem dropping 1/1000 packets. Root cause: two interacting issues: (1) the handshake/ack window between API gateway and runtime allowed non-atomic flushes where a delimiter byte could be emitted without its subsequent JSON tail when the downstream backpressure closed mid-chunk; (2) replay logic was non-idempotent for partially-applied fragments, causing duplicated delimiters and out-of-order function-call sentinel emission on reconnect. Changes: 1) Introduce an atomic chunk handshake: a 1-byte preamble (0x7E) announces an incoming logical frame and the runtime now buffers until frame-complete or explicit EOT; handshake moves boundary decisions to sender to prevent orphaned delimiter emission. 2) Add idempotent replay tokens at the fragment granularity: every fragment now carries a stable fragment-id and sequence checksum so replays can be deduped safely. 3) Tighten delimiter handling: normalize custom delimiter to 

 and ensure trimming only at frame assembly stage to avoid UTF-8 split issues. 4) Prevent function_call split: implement a sentinel reassembler that guarantees function_call start/end tokens are not split across coalesced network reads. 5) Backpressure windows: gate flushes on ACK from the gateway and introduce a soft timeout fallback to avoid head-of-line blocking under partial failure. 6) Add extensive unit + integration tests and a synthetic long-stream scenario in tests/bench/stream_replay_bench.py. Rollout: feature-flagged behind runtime.feature.sse_atomic_handshake; staged Canary rollout to Dedicated clusters for 72h, then broad rollout. Backout: flip feature flag; revert is a single commit removal. Risk/compatibility: no API-level breaking changes; new preamble is internal within runtime transport and only enabled via feature flag; release_notes included below. Testing: added ~60 unit tests, 5 integration tests, and a regression harness that reproduces previous failures. See commits for details and ci checks below.
Fixes a rare stream hang and duplicate delimiter emission for long streamed responses. Introduces an opt-in atomic SSE handshake and idempotent fragment replay to improve streaming stability during network jitter. Flagged rollout; no breaking API changes.
Evan: Can you explain why we chose 0x7E as the preamble byte? Is there a chance of collision with user content?
Priya: 0x7E was chosen for low collision probability and because it's filtered at framing layer; not exposed to user payloads. Added comment in framing.go.
Lena: The ACK gating looks race-prone under network partitions; add a soft timeout to avoid total stalls.
Priya: Added soft timeout default 250ms and made it configurable via runtime.config.sse_ack_timeout_ms.
Samir: Need perf numbers: how much latency does buffering add at 95th percentile?
Priya: Benchmarks added; 95p latency increases by ~6ms for long streams, overall token throughput unchanged. See ci artifact benchmarks.
payload.title: Atomicize SSE chunk handshake and idempotent replay to fix backpressure edgecases

payload.body:
Motivation: We need a more robust way to attribute per-invocation cost and latency to high-level causes for SLO triage without exploding cardinality in metrics or tracing. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) an Invocation Affine Cost Mapper (IACM) that maps token/phase-level cost and latency into compact, continuous attribution buckets using an affine transform + learned offset per-model-stage; and 2) a Log Cohorter that groups invocation logs into small cohorts based on lightweight fingerprints (prompt-shape, route, kv-cache-hit pattern) so debugging traces/alerts can surface representative log excerpts rather than noisy full streams.

Summary of changes (single-line format for docs consumption): Adds IACM service, cohorter worker, dashboard panels, alert calibration helper, and e2e test harness for cohort sampling.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc: Linear ENG-17429 (link included in ticket)
- [x] Unit tests for mapper and cohorter
- [x] Integration test: synthetic invocation replay through telemetry pipeline
- [x] Dashboard and runbook snippets
- [x] Backwards-compatible (adds new metrics/labels only)

What IACM does: The mapper ingests per-token phase metrics (kernel-latency, queued-time, decoding-time, kv-cache-status, gpu-queue-depth) and applies a cheap 2-param affine transform per-phase to produce a continuous cost attribution score in [0,1]. Scores are emitted as a new series invocation.affine_cost_score with low-cardinality labels (model_family, route_group, phase). This compresses signal for downstream rollups and enables percentile attribution without adding token-level high-cardinality labels.

What Log Cohorter does: A background worker consumes sampled logs and generates cohort ids using a small fingerprint (hashed prompt-shape, top-2 token-types, kv-hit-runlength). Cohort ids are attached to traces (span tag cohort_id) and to compact log excerpts stored in the telemetry-compact-bucket for quick slices. The cohorter supports deterministic sampling seed for reproducible debugging and an API that returns the top N representative logs per cohort.

Dashboard and alerts: Adds a new dashboard 'Invocation Affinity Matrix' with panels:
- Affine cost score distribution by route_group and phase (ECDF + heatmap)
- Cohort prevalence sparkline and representative log excerpts panel
- Alert calibration helper that suggests adjusted SLO thresholds based on cohort-weighted percentiles (linked to Linear ENG-17454).

Compat and rollout: Feature-flagged via feature.observability.iacm and feature.observability.cohorter. Default is off for existing tenants; flag rollout plan in runbook. New metric names prefixed with invocation.affine_* and telemetry.cohort_* to avoid collisions.

Risks and mitigations:

Related work: This complements the existing token-cost-attribution and span-synthesis efforts but targets compact continuous attribution and representative log sampling rather than per-token histograms (see ENG-17201 and ENG-17110 for prior attempts).

Thanks - folded routes into route_group in mapper config (see config.yaml).
Added backoff and increased test timeout; added comment on determinism for sampling seed.
Renamed metric as requested and updated dashboard panel queries.
CI: lint ✅, unit tests ✅, integration replay ✅ (after rerun). Performance bench: no regression on p50/p90; p99 reduced by ~1.8% on our synthetic mix.

Motivation: Cold-start prefill and aggressive batching can save tokens but occasionally regresses latency or tail SLOs for bursty tenants. This change introduces an on-demand economic telemetry gate that uses recent unit-econ signals (cost-per-inference, cache-hit-rate, tail-latency anomaly score) to decide whether to allow prefill/batching optimizations for a tenant in the next 60s window. The gate is conservative by default and only flips to permissive when telemetry crosses heuristics derived from historical tenant profiles.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Adds a telemetry-driven gating layer between the request router and the prefill/batcher pipeline, implements a lightweight running-window unit-econ scorer, extends the runtime config model with tenant_econ_policy and fallback_quant_profile, adds a dry-run CLI mode to simulate gate decisions, and wires metrics and logs to the Console dashboards.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-1442), [x] unit tests for scorer, [x] integration test exercising gate decision against synthetic bursts, [x] dashboards updated, [x] backward-compatible config defaults, [x] documentation snippet in runtime/README.

Design notes and links: The gate uses three signals: normalized_cost_delta (tokens/cost drift vs baseline), cache_hit_rate_ewma (50s window), and tail_latency_z (90th-99th zscore). We compute a weighted score and compare to tenant thresholds that are auto-derived (see design doc). If the gate denies prefill, the router falls back to a minimally-batched fast-path and an optional lower-quant profile (fallback_quant_profile) that prioritizes latency. Implementation choices emphasize safety: thresholds require 2 consecutive positive windows to enable aggressive prefill, and an emergency override exists for operator lock-in. See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1442/telemetry-gating-for-cold-batches and runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/cost-gate-runbook.

Commit summary: - introduce econ/gate package with scorer and policy types - runtime: add tenant config and gating hook into request router - batcher: expose prefill_enable_hint and fast-path execution - cli: add gate-simulate dry-run with sample traces - console: add minimal metrics (tenant_gate_decision, econ_score_components) - tests: unit and integration harness updates

Files changed (high level): - runtime/router/gate.go: new gate integration and feature flag checks - econ/scorer/scorer.go: running-window scorer and tests - batcher/prefill_hint.go: hint plumbing to respect gate decision - config/tenant_policy.yaml: new defaults and example tenant override - cli/gate_simulate.go: dry-run mode to replay traces and print decisions - console/metrics/telemetry_defs.yaml: metric definitions + panel links - tests/integration/gate_integration_test.go: synthetic burst scenarios

Behavior and safety: The default tenant_econ_policy is conservative: gate is opt-in per-tenant, and global default is disabled for free-tier tenants. The change introduces no forced quant changes; fallback_quant_profile is an explicit tenant config that admins can set. The gate is feature-flagged (runtime.feature_flags.enable_econ_gate) and initially off for all clusters.

Observability: New metrics: tenant_econ_score_total (gauge), tenant_gate_decision{tenant,decision}, tenant_cache_hit_rate_ewma, tenant_cost_delta_norm. Logs include structured events when a gate flips state and when fallback quant is applied. Dashboards and alert rules added under Console > Prefill Safety > Econ Gates.

Testing notes: Local unit tests exercise scorer weight combinations and edge windows. Integration harness replays recorded traces and asserts that tail latency degradation does not increase >1% when gate denies prefill. Load tests on benchmark-lab show median latency improvement for permissive tenants ~6% and unit-cost reduction ~8% for batched flows.

How to review: Focus areas are scorer correctness, router integration race conditions, and telemetry cardinality for metrics. Suggested reviewers: runtime for router changes, infra for metrics cardinality, and who owns batcher behavior.

Related work: ties to ENG-1463 (batch-safety-playbook) and earlier work on tenant-warming (pr-457321). This implementation intentionally separates econ gating from the autoscaler and from quota enforcement to avoid permission coupling.

Merge strategy: squash and merge after approvals and green CI.

Maya Chen (2026-02-20): @carlos good catch — updated gate.go to use request.Context metadata pool and added microbench under runtime/benchmarks/gate_bench_test.go
Priya Iyer (2026-02-21): The scorer weights look hand-tuned. Can we expose a tenant-level override and make the default profile conservative? Also request clearer comments on how zscore is computed for tail_latency_z.
Maya Chen (2026-02-22): Exposed tenant override in config schema and added explanatory comments and unit test for zscore computation. Kept default conservative as requested.
Ethan Walsh (2026-02-23): Integration tests flaky once (timeout). CI rerun resolved it. Approving after green CI.

Adds RBACv2 attribute-level denylist support, a consent-mapper for multi-KMS routing, and a sampled audit fanout path. No public API surface changes. Admins can opt-in via feature flag.
Motivation: Customers asked for a simple, policy-driven way to block known-sensitive attributes from being used in operator- or tenant-scoped RBAC decisions, and for clearer proof of KMS consent when routing encryption requests across providers. This change introduces three cooperating pieces: 1) an attribute-level denylist in the RBACv2 policy evaluator (configurable per-namespace or global), 2) a KMS consent mapper that binds service/operator claims to an explicit consent token and preferred KMS region/provider, and 3) an audit fanout pipeline that can sample, redact, and forward audit events to multiple sinks (internal ledger + compliance S3 + SIEM) with deduplication. Design summary: - Attribute denylist: a lightweight predicate that runs during policy normalization and rejects or tags attributes that match denylist patterns. The denylist supports exact values, prefix/suffix, and regex with explicit allow-overrides. - KMS consent mapper: small middleware in the crypto allocator. If a request has an operator/service claim that maps to a consent profile, we attach a signed consent-reference header and prefer the listed KMS providers in order. Consent lookup is cached with TTL=5m and has an opt-out fallback to default KMS. - Audit fanout: new audit adapter that accepts canonical audit envelopes, applies provenance stamping, optional PII redaction rules tied to the denylist, and forwards to multiple configured sinks with sampling rules per-sink. Deduplication uses a short-lived HMAC-based fingerprint. Backwards compatibility: feature gated under admin flag "rbacv2-attr-denylist" and runtime flag "audit-fanout-v1". No changes to public REST API. Linear/Jira refs: ENG-9311 (policy), SEC-140 (kms-consent), COMPL-22 (audit). Checklist: - [x] Policy format addition and parser tests - [x] Middleware integration tests - [x] End-to-end KMS consent flow test with mock providers - [x] Audit fanout unit tests + integration with sample SIEM sink - [x] Documentation added to security playbook - [x] Feature flags wired and documented Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to staging with flags off and run policy/consent smoke tests. 2) Enable denylist in shadow mode (tagging only) for 48h to collect metrics. 3) Enable enforcement for a small set of tenants (canary). 4) Gradually expand and enable audit-fanout in passive mode, then active forwarding. Monitoring: Added metrics rbac.attr_denylist.matches, kms.consent.miss/hit, audit.fanout.forwarded_by_sink, audit.fanout.fingerprints_deduped. Impact/risk: Low-medium. Denylist misconfiguration could block legitimate actions — mitigated by allow-overrides and shadow mode. KMS consent mapping errors fall back to default KMS. CI: all unit/integration tests pass in this branch. Notes: This PR intentionally keeps policy syntax conservative; a follow-up will add a small UI for denylist management in the Console.
3 commits:
- Add attribute denylist data model, parser, and unit tests
- Implement KMS consent mapper middleware and caching layer
- Add audit fanout adapter, sampling and dedupe logic; update config docs

Asha Menon (2025-09-13): Precedence: explicit per-tenant allow wins. Added tests in commit 2. See denylist_test.go line 48.

Asha Menon (2025-09-14): Added metric and exposed ttl via config with sensible default in commit 3.
Priya Kapoor (2025-09-15): Audit fanout dedupe approach is sensible; confirm HMAC key rotation plan and retention on S3 sink (compliance asked for 7 years).
Asha Menon (2025-09-15): We'll wire rotation through key-manager and document retention policy in docs; compliance acknowledged in COMPL-22.

Marco Silva (2025-09-17): Approved.
Priya Kapoor (2025-09-17): Approved with documentation note added.

Motivation: Operator sessions that traverse proxy layers were losing origin context which caused KMS region decisions to pick incorrect key scopes and produced duplicate audit noise during retries. This led to two operational pain points: 1) keys being allocated in a different region than the claimed tenant residency, and 2) audit pipelines being flooded by near-duplicate events from session replays.

This PR implements three coordinated components to address the problem while preserving backward compatibility and enabling a staged rollout: 1) RBAC Origin Rewriter: a middleware that normalizes operator session identity by injecting an immutable origin annotation (origin=<region|edge-id>) derived from a verified forwarding header and operator attestation. This makes RBAC decisions region-aware without requiring callers to change their principals. 2) KMS Region Token Bridge: a short-lived signed token issued by the control-plane that binds a request to a KMS region claim; the serving runtime accepts the token and enforces CMK selection by token region affinity. Tokens are TTL-bound and auditable. 3) Audit Rate-Fence: event fingerprinting + leaky-bucket rate-fence placed at the audit-forwarder to coalesce repeated session-replay events into a single representative record with an aggregated count and delta metrics.

What changed (high level): added middleware and runtime handlers, proto for region-token, an audit coalescer service, docs and migration guide, integration tests and e2e canary job. Backwards compatibility: older clients without tokens continue to work; RBAC Origin Rewriter falls back to existing principal path when no verified origin header exists.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4921) - [x] Unit tests for origin rewriter and token bridge - [x] Integration tests for cross-region key selection - [x] Audit forwarder coalescing validation - [x] Helm flag to opt-in rollout - [x] Staged canary deployment run on staging cluster

Rollout plan: stage=off by default; enable via helm flag in a single region, monitor KMS selection and audit ingestion metrics, expand to regions with canary percentage, then enable cluster-wide. If KMS token mismatch occurs runtime falls back to model-variant with no secret use and emits a high-severity audit alert (safe-fail behavior).

Notes on security: tokens are HMAC-signed with rotating signing keys managed by the control plane KMS; token parsing is constant-time to avoid timing leaks. Audit coalescer preserves original raw events in a short-term hotstore (72h) for forensic replay.

Related work: ENG-4921 design, PRs TBD that wire operator attestation into edge proxies.

Marisol Vega (author): Added explicit deterministic ordering and unit test that asserts attestation wins over forwarded header.
Hannah Kim (reviewer): KMS token parsing should validate the token clock skew; add metrics for skew rejections.
Marisol Vega (author): Added skew-metric and a config knob for allowed clock skew; documented in region-token-bridge.md.
Luca Rossi (reviewer): Audit coalescer compresses too aggressively by default; can we surface a per-tenant sampling override?
Marisol Vega (author): Added tenant sampling override via helm values and a runtime per-tenant header that the coalescer honors (disabled by default).

Motivation: Production incidents showed a single tenant spike can cascade through regional nodes and force SLO-driven evictions that impact other tenants. Existing circuit breakers operate at node/region level and are too coarse. This PR implements a tenant-level, lease-based soft-quarantine and a probabilistic admission gate to contain noisy tenants while preserving cluster-wide SLOs. Design summary: 1) Probabilistic admission gate: computes a moving percentile estimator (configurable window) of recent per-tenant latency and uses a probability function to early-reject or defer low-priority requests when a tenant exceeds configured thresholds. This reduces peak load without immediate hard-eviction. 2) Soft-quarantine orchestration: a short-duration lease (default 30s with exponential backoff) marks a tenant as degraded; new requests are routed to a lightpath (lower-cost model / reduced decoding length) and given lower concurrency. The lease is leadership-managed so multiple routers enforce a consistent view. 3) KV cache drain smoothing: when a tenant enters quarantine, its KV entries are drained on a staggered schedule to avoid simultaneous cache purges that would spike downstream access patterns. 4) Safe rollout and flags: all behavior behind a feature flag toggled per-region and per-tenant; canary in us-west-2. 5) Observability & tracing: new metrics (tenant_quarantine_state, tenant_admission_reject_rate, kv_drain_progress) plus trace tags for quarantine decisions. Implementation notes: admission hook inserted in routing layer, policy stored in tenant catalog, lease allocator added to control-plane service (leadership-guarded), and admission probability calibrated using recent percentiles and a configurable aggressiveness parameter. Tests & checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in description - [x] Unit tests for admission probability, edge cases - [x] Integration tests for lease lifecycle and leadership failover - [x] E2E chaos test exercising node eviction while quarantines active - [x] Observability: dashboards and alerts added - [x] Feature flag gating for canary rollout - [x] Ops runbook and roll-back instructions. Rollout plan: enable in staging, canary in us-west-2 at 5% tenant traffic (72h observation), expand to additional regions in controlled steps, automatic rollback if 95th token latency increases by >1% or error-rate delta exceeds configured threshold. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is no-op unless feature flag enabled; no schema changes to persisted models. See commits and files changed for concrete diffs.
Anya Koval (reviewer): Please add a safety cap to the admission probability to avoid rejecting >50% of requests for high-priority tenants.
Author (Priya Rao): Added a priority-exempt threshold and maximum reject cap (see tenant_admission.rs).
Diego Martinez (reviewer): Lease coordination looks racy when leader flips during issuance. Can we persist a pending-lease marker to avoid double-quarantine?
Author (Priya Rao): Reworked allocator to write a short-lived pending marker to raft-backed store; added integration test for leader failover.
Ethan Zhao (reviewer): Add more granular metrics for monitoring KV drain contention — required for SRE dashboard.
Author (Priya Rao): Added kv_drain_progress and kv_drain_batch_size metrics and updated dashboards; responded with screenshots in the doc.
Unit tests cover admission probability edge cases and priority exemptions. Integration tests simulate leader failover while leases are active. E2E chaos test evicted a node while quarantines were active to validate that degraded traffic remains isolated and cluster SLOs stay within tolerance. Load testing with synthetic tenants showed a 3-7x reduction in cross-tenant noisy neighbor incidents on spike scenarios.
1) Feature flag in staging; 2) Canary: us-west-2 at 5% tenant traffic for 72h; monitor tenant_admission_reject_rate, 95th token latency, error rate; 3) Gradual expansion to us-east-1 and eu-west-1 with 50% steps over 24h windows; 4) Full enable across regions if no regressions; Automated rollback triggers: +1% 95th token latency or >0.5% absolute error-rate increase versus baseline.
Adds tenant-level probabilistic admission gate and soft-quarantine orchestration to reduce cross-tenant cascade during regional spikes; safe feature-flagged rollout.

Summary: Backport and hotpatch that implements a geo-aware slowpath fallback attenuation plus a probabilistic shedding layer for slow or degraded regions. This change avoids hard circuit-breaker trips for transient token or KV-cache pressure by applying a decaying slowpath multiplier and a controlled probabilistic shed that preserves a minimal control-plane and probe traffic. Motivation: We observed several incidents in the last month where overloaded regions abruptly opened global circuit-breakers, causing large-scale failovers and degraded tail latency across customer deployments. This PR implements a conservative, release-safe fallback: instead of tripping circuits, traffic to a degraded region is attenuated to a slowpath rate and a small fraction of requests are shed probabilistically based on SLO credit debt and recent probe success rates. Design/Implementation notes: - Geo-aware policy: decisions use per-region SLO debt windows (60s rolling) and probe health metrics; policy is intentionally conservative when downstream KV-cache misses are high. - Slowpath attenuation: introduces a multiplier (0.1–0.5 configurable) applied to routing tokens for affected regions; multiplier decays back to 1.0 over a soft-backoff window (configurable, default 10 minutes) if proxies report improving probe success. - Probabilistic shedding: uses a stochastic drop governed by (SLO_debt / SLO_budget) with an upper cap (default 0.25) and a lower floor (default 0.01) to guarantee some baseline traffic for health checks and maintain warm caches. - Probe prioritization: separate, high-weight probe tokens still flow to preserve health signals; they are excluded from shedding and count towards healing windows. - KV-cache protection: when cache miss rate > threshold, shed favors non-cacheable API patterns first (e.g., long-stream/payload-heavy routes). - Backport constraints: no surface API changes; all knobs are flags and environment-controlled, added feature-flag gate for release rollout. - Telemetry: new metrics (geo_slowpath_active, geo_shed_rate, geo_slo_debt, geo_probe_success) and logs added to the observability pipeline. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-5724) - [x] Unit tests for policy calculations - [x] Integration test: simulated multi-region pressure - [x] Metrics emitted and dashboard updated - [x] Feature gated and default-off for customer-configs - [x] Backported to release/v1.18 (hotpatch) Commits (high level): - feat(geo-fallback): add region SLO debt window & probe inputs - feat(attenuator): slowpath multiplier implementation and decay scheduler - feat(shedding): probabilistic shedding controller (configurable cap/floor) - test: add unit tests and integration harness scenarios - ci: add canary checks for metric emission Changed areas (summary): - services/routing/geo_policy.go (+312/-44): new decision graph and decay scheduler. - services/routing/attenuator.go (+178/-12): multiplier application and config plumbing. - services/routing/shedding_controller.go (+254/-36): shedding algorithm and metrics. - internal/observability/metrics_definitions.go (+34/-0): new metric names and tags. - tests/integration/geo_fallback_scenarios_test.go (+98/-12): synthetic pressure tests and assertions. - docs/ops/geo_fallback.md (+56/-2): operator-facing toggles and escalation playbook. Small illustrative snippet (attenuator decision): func decideMultiplier(regionState) { if regionState.sloDebt < config.lowThreshold { return 1.0 } return max(config.minMultiplier, 1.0 - decayFactor*regionState.sloDebt) } Review thread (selected messages, condensed): - Miguel Santos (reviewer) 2026-02-21: "Nice approach — prefer attenuation to hard fail; main ask is to make the decay window explicit in config and ensure unit tests cover boundary conditions. Also flag the behavior when multiple regions degrade simultaneously." - Lena Park (author) 2026-02-21: "Added decay window config and expanded unit tests to cover simultaneous-region scenarios. See second commit that adds integration harness changes." - Asha Kapoor (reviewer) 2026-02-22: "Observability looks good; please ensure new metrics are tagged with region and route for downstream dashboards. Also double-check that probe tokens are never counted towards normal SLO debt computation." - Lena Park 2026-02-22: "Fixed metric tags and adjusted SLO accounting so probe-only tokens are excluded (added comment and unit test)." - Jonah Reed (reviewer, SRE) 2026-02-23: "Requested a temporary kill-switch env var (RELEASE_HOTPATCH_GEO_SLOWPATH=off) for emergency rollback. Also asked for a canary rollout to 2 internal regions first." - Lena Park 2026-02-23: "Added kill-switch and canary rollout plan to docs. Canary tests passed in staging." CI and checks: - pipeline/unit-tests: initially failed (one flaky timing-based test), rerun and passed - pipeline/integration: passed on canary scenario - lint: pass - e2e/canary: pass (internal regions a, b) - infra/helm: no changes required Merge notes: - This was merged to release/v1.18 using squash merge after approvals from Miguel, Asha, and Jonah. - Merge method: squash-and-merge - Rationale for backport: urgent reliability improvements observed in production incidents; approach is backward-compatible and feature-gated. Operational guidance (for on-call and operators): - Default flags are OFF; enable via: RELEASE_GEO_SLOWPATH=true RELEASE_SLOWPATH_MIN_MULTIPLIER=0.1 RELEASE_SLOWPATH_MAX_SHED=0.25 - Start with a canary rollout to two lower-traffic regions and monitor geo_slo_debt and geo_shed_rate dashboards. - If unexpected global performance regressions are observed, use RELEASE_HOTPATCH_GEO_SLOWPATH=off to instantly revert behavior and open requests back to normal routing. Related work: ENG-5724 (design), ENG-5788 (incident retrospective), follow-up planned: add adaptive per-route multipliers and ML-driven shed probability tuning.
Backported geo-aware slowpath attenuation and probabilistic request shedding to release/v1.18 to reduce cross-region blast radius during transient token-spike incidents. Improves SLO stability without hard-circuit trips.

Motivation: Our lint and test presubmit paths have accumulated bespoke scripts and many repo-level exceptions. This PR replaces legacy Gruntfile-based bootstrapping and the ad-hoc lint-runner with a compact, language-aware 'lint orchestrator' and a dependency-sync 'stamp' that records the source-of-truth lockfile snapshot used for a given presubmit run. Goals: 1) reduce presubmit startup time by consolidating initialization and parallelizing linter setup; 2) provide a lightweight dependency stamp that ties CI results to a deterministic lockfile snapshot to help triage flakes caused by transitive dep churn; 3) make lint config per-language pluggable and easier to opt teams into; 4) keep rollout safe (feature-flagged, gradual). Changes in this PR: - Add a new orchestrator binary (scripts/ci/lint_orchestrator.go) that enumerates changed files, dispatches language-specific linters, and creates a short-lived execution plan with concurrency limits tuned for ephemeral runners. - Introduce dep sync stamp (tools/dep_sync/stamp.json.template + scripts/ci/emit_dep_stamp.sh) which writes a small fingerprint (lockfile hash, package-manager, timestamp, runner-id) into build metadata. - Replace legacy grunt bootstrap in package.json -> scripts->ci:lint with a shim that invokes the orchestrator. - Split the monolithic lint job into three staged steps in .github/workflows/presubmit-lint.yml: prepare-orchestrator, run-orchestrator, collect-results; the new flow emits structured annotations to GitHub checks and uploads a small per-run artifact with the dep stamp. - Add light backward compatibility: if orchestrator not available, runner falls back to previous node-based lint entrypoint for two-week grace window. - Update docs: docs/ci/lint-orchestrator.md describes opt-in, environment variables, and telemetry. - Add unit and integration tests for orchestrator dispatch logic (test/lint_orchestrator_test.go) and small e2e smoke job in tools/ci-smoke/ that runs orchestrator against a synthetic workspace. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed in ENG-2871. - [x] Unit tests added. - [x] Integration smoke added and green locally. - [x] Feature gated via CI env var LINT_ORCH_ENABLED. - [x] Rollout plan added to PR body. Rollout plan: enable LINT_ORCH_ENABLED=false by default; flip to true for team/rust and team/js canaries for one week; monitor flaky lint failures and dep-stamp mismatches via an introduced metric (ci.dep_stamp.mismatch). If any regressions are observed, flip feature off and revert via a small hotfix. Related: ENG-2899 coordinates the dep-stamp ingestion into internal flakiness dashboard. Security notes: orchestrator does not change credential handling; dep stamp contains no secrets, only lockfile hash and meta fields. Testing and validation performed: CI smoke on ephemeral runner (simulated slow network) showed 22% median presubmit latency decrease on JS-heavy changes and 11% on mixed-language changes. The stamp was used to correlate one flaky eslint plugin upgrade to a transient registry mirror issue during the canary. See commits for iteration history. CI: initial run failed due to path assumptions on Windows runners (fixed in commit 3), final pipeline green. Merge notes: squash-merged to main after approvals and CI green.
1) scaffold: add lint_orchestrator.go with dispatcher interface and concurrency config
2) feat: emit dep stamp from orchestrator and add stamp template
3) fix(ci): handle windows path join and use consistent tmpdir across OS
4) ci(workflows): split presubmit-lint job into prepare/run/collect stages
5) docs: add docs/ci/lint-orchestrator.md and rollout plan
6) test: add unit tests for matching changed-file->linter rules
7) chore: shim package.json ci:lint -> calls orchestrator if enabled
8) ci: add smoke e2e runner and update workflow artifact uploads
Daniel Koh (reviewer): Nice consolidation. Two nits: (1) can you expose concurrency via env var with sane max to allow teams to opt-down? (2) please add comments on error cases where we continue vs fail the job.
Priya Nair (author): Responded: both addressed — added LINT_ORCH_MAX_CONCURRENCY default=6 and added detailed error handling docstrings; updated unit tests to cover non-fatal linter crash.
Marisol Vega (reviewer): Approved after second pass. Left note about telemetry labels to help filter canaries from production runs.
Ethan Moran (reviewer): Asked for a short compatibility window and a one-line revert playbook in the PR body.

Introduce a language-aware lint orchestrator and a dep-sync 'stamp' for deterministic CI provenance. Reduces presubmit latency, adds dependency fingerprinting to help triage flakiness. Backwards compatible via two-week shim. No user-facing API changes.

Motivation: some tenants require cryptographic proof that operator-held keys used for KMS wrapping are pinned to a jurisdiction and that operator key custody adheres to policy; this PR adds an RBACv2-aware middleware that validates operator key custody assertions against KMS attestors and enriches audit logs with residency proof metadata. Changes: 1) new middleware pkg/security/key_custody/attestor.go that validates a signed custody receipt produced by the KMS attestor service and rejects requests when custody proof does not match the tenant residency policy; 2) RBAC v2 policy extension to allow per-operator custody exemptions and timebound delegation profiles (src/rbac/v2/policy_types.go, src/rbac/v2/engine.go); 3) audit enrichment: add audit header x-residency-proof and audit fields for custody_proof_id and kms_provider in audit-writer (internal/audit/writer.go); 4) KMS integration shim that supports verifying attestation tokens from AWS KMS and a reference HSM attestor (pkg/kms/attestor_aws.go, pkg/kms/attestor_hsm.go); 5) helm chart toggle and feature flag (deploy/helm/values.yaml and charts/feature-gates.yaml) for controlled rollout; 6) e2e tests and unit tests (tests/e2e/kms_custody_test.go, tests/unit/key_custody_test.go); 7) docs and compliance playbook updates (docs/compliance/operator-key-custody.md). The description below details reviewer feedback, test matrix and rollout plan. Testing: unit tests cover 92% of attestor logic; e2e covers AWS KMS flows in staging with a mock HSM; CI includes new contract-test against the attestor API. Backwards compatibility: when the feature flag is off, behavior is unchanged and custody headers are ignored. Rollout strategy: feature-flagged canary 5% global -> 25% -> 100% with telemetry gating. Related: ENG-1983 tracks the policy schema change and SEC-44 is the compliance request from a customer. NOTE: the description is a single continuous string to satisfy PR export format.
Aisha Khan: Can the attestor verifier accept both compact JWS and detached signatures? If not, add a compatibility shim for legacy KMS token shapes.
Connor Li: Right now the verifier accepts compact JWS and base64detached signatures; added a small compatibility layer to attestor_aws.go with a toggle guarded by the feature flag.
Miles Ortega: Audit retention teams need an immutable custody_proof_id persisted; don't rely on request headers alone. Persist to audit index and include a replay detection TTL.
Connor Li: Persisting custody_proof_id to the audit index is implemented; added replay-detection via a short-lived cache and outlined the TTL in docs (default 48h).
Priya Raman: RBAC change looks fine, but we should ensure the policy linter flags when timebound delegations are missing expiry. Add a linter rule.
Connor Li: Added linter rule src/rbac/v2/linter/timebound_checks.go and tests to ensure delegation entries include expiry. CI updated accordingly.
Security Bot (automated): gosec flagged potential weak crypto usage in attestor_hsm.go line 72; please explain reasoning or remediate.
Connor Li: The flagged code uses SHA256 over the attestation envelope per upstream HSM spec; added explicit comments and a test vector validating the envelope shape; also replaced deprecated helper in favor of crypto/hmac with constant time compare.
QA: e2e failures observed intermittently in CI on mock HSM cert rotation; added exponential backoff and retries for cert discovery in tests.
Connor Li: Increased stability of e2e tests and added retry with backoff; re-ran CI and green.
Squashed feature and test commits; performed canary rollout gated by feature flag; monitored telemetry for increased 5xx on attestation failure path (none observed). Post-merge tasks: notify compliance, add example to deploy/README; schedule a short incident runbook drill for operator custody failures.

payload.body:
Motivation: We see recurring small-cost regressions where prompt/response shape drift (token count + role distribution) causes sudden changes in token-level latency and cost profiles. Existing telemetry shows per-route aggregates but does not surface prompt-shape distribution shifts or prioritize logs by information content. This PR adds two complementary pieces: 1) a prompt-shape bucketing + drift dashboard (Prompt Shape Drift and Prompt Entropy Explorer) so SREs and ML engineers can see shape cohorts over time, and 2) an entropy-weighted log sampler that biases sampled logs towards high-information invocations to reduce noise and improve alert triage.

What was changed (summary):
- New bucketing logic that computes a compact 'prompt shape key' (role histogram + token-length quantile) at ingest time and emits a shape_id tag on invocation spans.
- A drift detection job that runs daily and annotates shape cohorts with KL divergence vs baseline, exposed as metrics and dashboard annotations.
- Entropy-weighted sampler that assigns a lightweight entropy score (sampled token ngram surprise + role diversity) and uses a tunable reservoir sampler to increase sampling probability for high-entropy invocations.
- Dashboard panels: Prompt Shape Drift (trend + heatmap), Prompt Entropy Explorer (sparkline + sampled log links), Cohort Alert table with auto-suggested hysteresis.
- Docs and runbook describing how to interpret drift signals and how to tune sampler thresholds.

Design notes:
- The shape key is intentionally compact (16-bit hash) to avoid cardinality explosion; cohort rollups are stored in a daily aggregated counter and backed by a downsampled histogram for long-tail shapes.
- Entropy calculation uses a single-pass prefix model and only considers first 64 tokens to keep CPU cost bounded. The sampler is gated behind a feature flag and configured per-tenant with a 1% default bump for high-entropy traffic.
- To avoid alert noise from expected model updates, the drift job supports a 'release-ignore' window; releases tagged in our Linear workflow will automatically suppress drift alerts for the first 24 hours.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for shape-key generation and entropy scorer (observability/tests/*).
- E2E test that injects synthetic prompt shapes and validates that the drift metric moves and that the sampler selects high-entropy traces in the reservoir.
- Load test: ran a 30m canary on staging with 10k rps and observed <3% CPU overhead on telemetry workers with default sampling window.

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag default off. Stage rollout: internal telemetry team -> beta tenants -> all tenants over 2 weeks.
- Dashboard panels added to the 'Invocation Insights' org dashboard; access controlled by dashboard role.

Related work: builds on ENG-742 (invocation fingerprinting) and supplements ENG-8421 (cohorting telemetry).

Checklist:
- [x] Shape key library implemented and unit tested
- [x] Drift job and metrics exporter
- [x] Entropy-weighted sampler with feature flag and per-tenant config
- [x] Dashboard JSON + panel templates
- [x] Documentation and runbook
- [x] Load + e2e validation

Runbook excerpt (short):
- If drift spikes for a given shape cohort, check recent model rollouts or prompt template changes; use the Prompt Entropy Explorer to link sampled logs. If high-entropy invocations coincide with increased cost, consider adding explicit prompt prefix caching rules for that cohort.
Maya Chen: Nice approach. Please add telemetry on sampler select vs baseline select rate so we can measure sampling bias. Also, how does this interact with per-tenant RBAC?
Sofia Ramirez: Added metrics observability.sampler.selected_count and observability.sampler.baseline_count; sampler honors tenant sampling overrides and follows existing RBAC rules for log access (only stores links to logs, logs are gated).
Liam O'Connor: Concerned about cardinality. How do we avoid shape_id explosion for templated prompts with small changes?
Sofia Ramirez: We quantize token-length into coarse buckets and hash role histograms; added a TTL and aggressive downsampling for shapes with <0.01% daily frequency. Updated code to cap observed shape growth and emit a cardinality metric.
Priya Nair: Unit tests look good. Please ensure the feature flag default is off and add a safety kill switch for the drift alerting job.
Sofia Ramirez: Feature flag default is off; added emergency.disable_prompt_shape_drift boolean and a manual mute endpoint.

Problem: Recent compliance reviews highlighted a gap in our supply-chain integrity story: operators and installer tooling could not cryptographically assert that deployable artifacts (helm charts, installer bundles) were provisioned with a customer-scoped KMS key provenance. This limits our ability to produce non-repudiable audit records for Private installations and on-prem flows.

Goals: 1) Add an attestor service that validates a signed provenance blob against configured KMS providers and emits a tamper-evidence header used by RBACv2 decisioning. 2) Integrate a lightweight RBAC hook (tamper-guard) that rejects operator-scoped role grants when provenance checks fail. 3) Provide an operator-facing runbook and CI guards to validate the attestation flow.

What this PR does: Adds a new internal attestor component (pkg/attestor) which consumes artifact metadata, verifies KMS-wrapped signatures across our supported KMS adapters (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault), and returns a signed assertion with a canonicalized audit fingerprint. Introduces an RBAC enforcement hook (pkg/rbac/tamperguard.go) that consults the attestor via gRPC and attaches a tamper-evidence claim into the authorization pipeline. Installer/helm changes wire the attestor sidecar into Private and Dedicated installers with a default disabled flag. Includes e2e CI job and a new compliance runbook that documents expected signals in the audit logs.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4121) - [x] Unit tests for attestor parsing and KMS adapters - [x] Integration test for attestation + RBAC decision loop - [x] Compliance runbook drafted - [x] Backwards-compatible by default (attestor disabled in hosted API)

Compatibility notes: The tamper-guard is opt-in per-namespace via a new policy flag (rbac.enable_tamper_guard). When disabled, behavior is unchanged. When enabled, operator role grants that lack a valid provenance assertion will receive a scoped denial. Rollout plan: Canary on staging, enable for Private installer images in a gated rollout, then flip default for new installs after 4 weeks of telemetry.

References: Linear ENG-4121, Security ticket SEC-98, SUP-1234 for support escalation.
payload.title: Introduce supply-chain KMS attestor and RBAC tamper-guarding hook

Motivation: We observed two incidents where a burst of shadow traffic (from a large A/B experiment) caused backend saturation on Dedicated pools because shadowing was naively mirroring production QPS. This PR implements a Shadow Surge Moderator: a policy-driven admission controller that throttles, staggers, or aborts shadow requests when capacity or latency pressure is detected, while recording explainable audit artifacts for post-mortem and automated rollback decisions.

What this PR does (high level): 1) Adds a shadow admission controller component to the routing plane that applies per-cohort policies (fraction, max-concurrency, staging-window). 2) Implements staggered abort: when a cohort exceeds tolerance, we transition shadow traffic through a staged backoff (reduce fraction -> stagger -> abort) rather than an immediate kill, to avoid noisy replays. 3) Captures an audit-replay bundle for any staging/abort event (request sample, model variant metadata, KV cache snapshot pointer, short perf profile) so downstream tools (rollback advisor, incident playbooks) have explainable context. 4) Integrates the moderator with the rollout controller so shadow-induced pressure can feed automated remediation recommendations (canary throttle, pause promote, or automated revert). 5) Exposes metrics and traces and adds a lightweight UI slice in the Console under the rollout diagnostics tab.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/ENG-2472/shadow-surge-moderator-design - [x] Unit tests for admission logic and policy parsing - [x] Integration tests with staged abort behavior and replay bundle generation - [x] Added metrics (shadow.throttled.count, shadow.abort.reason, shadow.replay.generated) - [x] Console UI slice (read-only) + docs page detailing playbook examples - [x] Backward-compatible; toggled behind feature flag 'shadow_moderator_v1'

Related work: This complements the cohort-aware shadow drain flow (see pr-883567) but focuses on preventing backend saturation by controlling the shadow emitter rather than relying solely on downstream drains. It also feeds our rollback advisor (ENG-1994) with richer context for automated recommendations.

Commits summary: - feat(moderator): core admission controller and policy types - feat(router): integrate moderator into shadow routing path - feat(collector): replay bundle writer and minimal serializer - perf: non-blocking sampling for replay bundles - ui: console diagnostics slice and read-only timeline - test: unit + integration harness for staged abort scenarios - docs: playbook and operator guide

Changed areas (high level file list): - src/orchestrator/shadow/moderator.go - src/orchestrator/shadow/policy.go - src/orchestrator/shadow/replay_bundle/writer.go - src/router/handler_shadow.go (hook in for admission) - dashboard/console-rollouts/src/components/ShadowDiagnostics.tsx - helm/redwood/templates/feature-flags.yaml - docs/rollouts/shadow-moderator.md

Testing notes: Local integration harness simulates three cohorts with synthetic latency spikes. CI run initially failed on a flaky timing test (integration/staged_abort_test) caused by a rare timer race; added deterministic clock injection and re-ran. Production dogfood in the canary cluster showed the moderator reduced shadow-induced backend CPU by ~42% under a burst while still preserving 95% of shadow samples for replay.

Operational notes and safeguards: The moderator is disabled by default. When enabled it respects per-team quotas and a global safety budget. Staggered abort is conservative by default: fraction drops in 3 steps (0.5 -> 0.25 -> 0) spaced by a configurable staging window. Replay bundles are written to an append-only bucket with size limits and TTL; bundles are indexed and checksumed for reproducible replay.

How rollback advisor uses bundles: When the moderator escalates to abort, it emits an event with the bundle pointer. The rollback advisor evaluates the bundle (perf regressions, error patterns) and can return a suggested action (pause promote, scale up Dedicated, or revert model). Those suggestions are surfaced in the rollout UI with reasoning derived from bundle analysis (latency spike at Xms for model vY with KV hit rate Z).

Backwards compatibility and migration: Policy defaults preserve previous behavior (unthrottled shadow) unless feature flag and policies are explicitly set. Helm chart includes a feature-flag toggle.

Release notes (short): Add Shadow Surge Moderator to control shadow traffic bursts, provide staged abort behavior, generate explainable replay bundles for automated rollback recommendations, and surface diagnostics in Console.

Merge: squash and merge after approval and a successful canary in the staging cluster.
Maya Chen: Can we make the staging window configurable per-cohort? Some teams run very short-lived experiments and the default 30s window might be too long.
Author (Ethan Park): Yes — added per-cohort staging_window_ms policy and described behavior in the docs. Default remains conservative at 30s but teams can set 5-10s for short experiments.
Diego Ramos: Replay bundles look large in the integration trace; can we cap with sampling and still keep deterministic seeds for reproducibility?
Author (Ethan Park): Implemented deterministic sampling with a 128-bit seed derived from cohort + rollout id. Added size cap and a 'full_replay' opt-in flag for enterprise audits.
Liam O'Connor: The console slice needs RBAC guard — only rollout owners and SRE should see bundle pointers. Also add a quick action to request an immediate snapshot.
Author (Ethan Park): Added RBAC check and a 'request snapshot' button that triggers an on-demand bundle generation (rate-limited).
Maya Chen: CI flake fixed — added deterministic clock in the integration harness. Approving after green CI.
Diego Ramos: Approving. Verified staging canary numbers and metrics.

Summary: Adds a lightweight session-lease enforcement layer to the RBAC v2 decision path and a KMS usage quarantine policy that temporarily isolates keys used by sessions whose residency or consent signals are ambiguous.

Motivation: We observed two classes of risky behavior in production: (1) long-lived delegated operator sessions that outlive intended short leases, widening blast radius when operator credentials are stolen; (2) intermittent KMS requests that lacked clear residency or consent metadata and therefore could be routed to the wrong region. This PR implements a policy gate that enforces session TTLs at the policy-evaluator level and tags KMS requests for quarantine until residency/consent is confirmed.

Design:
- Session lease enforcer: a middleware in the RBAC v2 evaluator that checks 'session_lease_expires_at' on operator claims and rejects or flags requests where the lease has expired. Supports a transparent renewal hint flow for SDKs to surface a 412-ish signal to callers.
- KMS quarantine: KMS client interceptor that writes an audit-quarantine tag and routes the request to a holding queue for short-circuit validation (residency check, consent cache lookup). If validation completes within the configured grace window (default 5s) the request is forwarded; otherwise the request is rejected with a clear error and audit entry.
- Metrics and tracing: new counters and histograms (security.session_lease.rejects, security.kms.quarantine.duration_ms) plus trace annotations to link the original request to quarantine evaluation.
- Config: per-tenant defaults with operator override guardrails; global feature flag 'session_lease_enforcer_v1' for staged rollout.

Backwards compatibility: If the feature flag is off, behavior is identical to today.

Checklist:
- [x] RFC approved by security and product
- [x] Unit tests for lease expiry + renewal hint
- [x] Integration test for KMS quarantine happy path and timeout path
- [x] Console metric dashboards added
- [x] Docs: security-runbook snippet and SDK hint guide

Changes (high-level):

- kms/interceptor/quarantine.go (new): quarantine tagging and short-circuit logic
- kms/queue/inmemory_adapter.go (new): in-memory adapter used in tests and dev clusters
- sdk/common/hint-renewal.md (new): guidance for SDKs how to surface renewal hints
- observability/metrics_defs.yaml (modified): new metrics and dashboards
- api/errors.go (modified): new error codes KMS_QUARANTINED / SESSION_LEASE_EXPIRED

Tests & CI:
- Unit: added 24 unit tests covering TTL boundary conditions and renewal hint semantics
- Integration: mocked KMS + residency service to verify quarantine acceptance and timeout failure
- CI: build / unit / integration / lint passed on first run; flake rerun for integration was not required

Review thread (selected):
- Alex Kim (reviewer): "This is a solid approach. Two asks: (1) ensure the default grace window is conservative for high-latency regions, (2) add a short note on operational cost impact for the holding queue."
- Author (Priya): "Addressed both: grace window moved to 8s for global default, with tenant override. Added dashboard lines to show queue depth and per-tenant quarantine counts so cost can be tracked."
- Marta Lopez (security): "Please ensure audit records include original region claim and consent token fingerprint."
- Author: "Included region and consent_fingerprint in audit envelope; left consent token out of logs."
- Daniel Rivers (sre): "How will this interact with Dedicated clusters?"

- Approval: "LGTM" from Alex Kim on 2025-11-27; approved by Marta Lopez same day.

CI summary:

Rollout plan:

2) Canary on 10% of tenants with durable queue adapter and dashboards watched for 72h
3) Gradual ramp to 100% with tenant opt-out for initial 48h if compatibility issues detected

payload.body:
Context
We already mirror a sampled subset of non-streaming generation requests to one or more shadow targets. For streaming requests, we need deterministic, safe behavior that (a) does not impact the user-visible stream, (b) keeps compute/capture costs bounded, and (c) yields usable artifacts for async scoring.

This PR defines and implements the streaming shadowing semantics in the router. Key goals are: fail-open, bounded overhead, and predictable capture/cancellation.

What this PR does
- Adds streaming-aware mirroring behavior for shadow traffic.
- Introduces partial capture modes for shadow outputs (so we can score something even if we don’t wait for full completion).
- Defines termination semantics for shadow streams (timeouts, cancellation on client disconnect, and max-capture limits).
- Extends telemetry to record whether a shadow artifact is partial vs complete and why it terminated.

Behavior changes / semantics
1) Control stream is always authoritative
- We continue to stream the control response to the client exactly as before.
- The shadow request is dispatched asynchronously and never participates in the client backpressure path.

2) Shadow request dispatch for streaming
- For streaming control requests, we send the same normalized request payload to shadow targets.
- We request streaming from the shadow target (so we can stop early without waiting for full generation), but we buffer shadow chunks internally (never forwarded to client).

3) Partial capture modes (configurable)
New policy fields (plumbed from shadow policy → router config):
- shadow_stream_capture_mode: one of
  - "none" (don’t capture output; still emit request-level telemetry)
  - "first_n_tokens" (capture up to shadow_stream_max_tokens)
  - "first_t_seconds" (capture until shadow_stream_max_duration_ms)
  - "until_control_done" (capture until the control stream completes, then cancel shadow)
- shadow_stream_max_tokens (default: 256)
- shadow_stream_max_duration_ms (default: 1500)
- shadow_stream_max_bytes (default: 64KiB) cap across all buffered chunks

Notes:
- "until_control_done" is the default for internal dogfood because it tends to match user-perceived latency windows while bounding tail exposure. If the shadow is still running when control finishes, we cancel it.
- "first_n_tokens" is recommended for high-QPS routes where we mostly care about format adherence and early safety/refusal signals.

4) Termination semantics (always fail-open)
Shadow streams can be terminated for several reasons; we persist a termination_reason for downstream scoring/analytics:
- completed: shadow model ended normally
- cancel_control_done: control stream ended (until_control_done mode)
- cancel_client_disconnect: client disconnected early (we propagate cancellation to shadow to avoid wasted compute)
- timeout: exceeded shadow_stream_max_duration_ms
- max_tokens: exceeded shadow_stream_max_tokens
- max_bytes: exceeded shadow_stream_max_bytes
- circuit_open: router circuit breaker open for shadow path
- shadow_error: shadow target errored (recorded, but user path unaffected)

Implementation detail: cancellation uses the existing request context cancellation token; we ensure shadow cancellation does not cancel the control context.

5) Telemetry additions
- Emits shadow_streaming_summary event with:
  - is_streaming=true
  - capture_mode
  - captured_tokens (best-effort estimate)
  - captured_bytes
  - termination_reason
  - shadow_latency_ms (until termination)
- For partial captures, we still emit artifact references so eval workers can score what was captured (with "partial" flag).

Files / areas touched (high level)
- router/shadowing:
  - streaming mirror worker + buffered chunk accumulator
  - termination controller (time/tokens/bytes)
  - cancellation semantics + error handling
- config:
  - ShadowTrafficPolicy schema updated with streaming capture options
- telemetry:
  - adds termination_reason/capture_mode dimensions (cardinality-safe; fixed enum)
- tests:
  - unit tests for termination controller
  - integration tests covering: client disconnect, control completion cancellation, max-bytes, timeout

Illustrative snippet
- Termination reason propagation (simplified):
  - if bytes >= max_bytes => terminate("max_bytes")
  - else if tokens >= max_tokens => terminate("max_tokens")
  - else if now-start >= max_duration => terminate("timeout")
  - else if control_done && capture_mode==until_control_done => terminate("cancel_control_done")

Why these defaults
- 256 tokens / 1.5s / 64KiB keeps artifacts useful for v1 quality metrics (refusal/format/instruction-following proxy) while protecting costs.
- Cancellation on client disconnect is important for cost control for high-volume streaming customers.

Risk / rollout
- Feature gated behind shadow_traffic_streaming_enabled.
- If anything goes wrong, router treats shadow dispatch as best-effort and drops shadowing (records circuit_open / shadow_error) without affecting control.

Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Wire capture_mode defaults into Console creation UX (currently policy-only; Console shows whatever policy sets).
- Add scoring templates that explicitly understand partial artifacts (some rubrics should treat partial as "unknown" rather than negative).
- Extend per-chunk shadow telemetry (intentionally deferred due to cardinality/volume).

Testing
- Unit: router_shadow_stream_termination_controller_test
- Integration: shadow_streaming_cancel_on_control_done, shadow_streaming_cancel_on_client_disconnect, shadow_streaming_max_bytes
- Load test: ran local perf-canary scenario (streaming chat, 5% sampling) — no measurable change to control p99, shadow worker CPU +3–5% in the router process at 2k rps.

Links
- Linear: ENG-5414
- Related: ENG-5402 (base mirroring), ENG-5415 (backpressure/circuit breaker hardening)

Checklist
- [x] Fail-open behavior verified (shadow errors do not impact control)
- [x] Bounded capture (tokens/time/bytes)
- [x] Telemetry includes termination reason
- [x] Docs comments in policy schema

Ravi Menon (review): Can we clarify if we request streaming from the shadow target or do a non-streaming call and just cap max_tokens? If we do streaming, we must ensure no coupling to client backpressure.
Vikram Singh (author): We request streaming from the shadow target but consume it on a detached task with its own bounded buffer. Nothing is written to the client stream. Added a comment in mirror_streaming.rs and a test that simulates a slow client while shadow completes quickly.
Mina Haddad (review): Default capture mode — I’d prefer first_n_tokens rather than until_control_done for cost predictability. until_control_done can be long for long-running streams.
Vikram Singh (author): Agreed it’s workload-dependent. I left router-side defaults as until_control_done but capped by max_duration_ms (1.5s) and max_tokens (256). So worst-case is still bounded. Also added a note in schema docs: set first_n_tokens for very long streams.
Sean Gallagher (review): Cancellation semantics: do we cancel shadow on client disconnect? That’s important for cost, but ensure we don’t accidentally cancel the control context in shared code paths.
Vikram Singh (author): Yes. Shadow uses a child cancellation token. Client disconnect cancels shadow token; control token is unchanged. Added an integration test that disconnects at chunk 3 and asserts control path completes without errors while shadow terminates with cancel_client_disconnect.
Nadia Rahman (review): Telemetry dimensions look OK, but please keep termination_reason as a fixed enum and avoid recording raw error strings as labels.
Vikram Singh (author): Done. termination_reason is an enum; error strings go only into sampled debug logs and the structured event payload (not as metric labels).
Chloe Martin (review): For Console drilldowns we’ll want to show whether artifacts are partial. Is that recorded in the artifact metadata or only in the summary event?
Vikram Singh (author): Both. The artifact metadata now includes partial=true/false plus termination_reason; the summary event includes the same so aggregations can be computed without fetching artifacts.
payload.title: Shadow traffic: support mirroring for streaming requests (partial capture + termination semantics)

payload.body:
Motivation: tighten operator-scoped KMS usage assertions and improve audit non-repudiation for service-level region pinning. This PR introduces an operator-scope KMS claim enforcer that validates KMS key origin and tenant/service binding at request time, a lightweight non-repudiation audit proxy that signs audit envelopes with a platform key and cohorts sensitive audit entries to reduce PII blast radius, migration for service metadata to store kms_zone, and feature-flagged rollout to avoid immediate global impact. Changes include RBAC v2 policy hooks to surface operator-scoped decisions, updates to the decision cache to include KMS provenance assertions, and a new audit proxy that sits between the request pipeline and the audit sink to add signed envelopes and cohort headers. Commits: 1) add operator_kms_assertor core logic and interfaces; 2) wire RBAC v2 evaluator to pass KMS provenance into decision context; 3) add DB migration to persist kms_zone on service records; 4) implement non-repudiation audit proxy and envelope signer; 5) feature flag and rollout scripts; 6) integration tests for region pinning and KMS enforcement; 7) docs and runbook. Migration notes: run migrations/20241115_add_kms_zone.sql before enabling feature flag. Rollout plan: enable flag in staging, 5% canary in prod for 24h, monitor audit signing rates and RBAC decision failures, then ramp. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is allowlist fallback where missing kms_zone or legacy services fall through to existing KMS resolver until metadata is populated.
