Introduces an RBACv2 micro-compiler for constraint validation, runtime KMS consent orchestration middleware, and immutable audit stamps. Backwards-compatible rollout with staged feature flag. See docs/security/rbac-microcompiler.md for migration notes.
Motivation: We need a compact, verifiable runtime for RBACv2 constraints that can be compiled to a small evaluation graph and checked at high QPS without pulling the full policy graph into request-critical paths. This PR introduces a micro-compiler that emits a minimal decision DAG (JSON) for per-route checks, adds a KMS consent orchestrator middleware to validate KMS region pins and consent tokens before key operations, and attaches immutable audit stamps for non-repudiation.

What this changes: - rbac/microcompiler: new package that parses RBACv2 constraint templates and emits a minimal decision DAG used by the request-time guard. The compiler runs at policy-deploy time and outputs compact artifacts stored in policy-store. - api/middleware/kms_consent_orchestrator.go: middleware that enforces KMS region pinning and verifies consent receipts (signed by operator KMS). Includes fallback logic to consult the residency cache when consent is ambiguous. - audit/enricher/immutable_stamp.go: appends an immutable, canonical audit stamp (hash+sig) to every cross-region KMS usage event. - deployment: helm chart tweak to add an opt-in feature flag redwood.rbac.microcompiler.enabled=false by default and a policy-bucket lifecycle hook. - tests: unit and integration coverage for compiler, orchestrator, and audit stamps.

Compatibility and rollout: The micro-compiler is gated behind the feature flag and a staged rollout (canary -> 10% -> 100%) controlled by the existing rollout service. When disabled, the system continues to use the legacy PDP policy evaluator. The KMS consent orchestrator is opt-in per-namespace; existing tenants see no change until they opt in.

Testing done: - Unit tests for compiler parser, optimizer, and DAG emitter (rbac/microcompiler/*_test.go). - Integration test that deploys a sample policy artifact, exercises route-level checks under 1000 qps in perf-canary harness. - Fuzz test for malformed consent receipts. - CI: lint, go test (pkg), build images, helm lint.

Security review & compliance: We consulted with security and compliance on the audit stamp format; stamps include a deterministic canonicalization of the audit record and a signing envelope tied to the operator key. Migration doc includes suggested retention settings and an explainability endpoint for inspectors to map micro-compiled checks to source policy templates.

Checklist: - [x] micro-compiler: AST -> DAG emitter implemented - [x] KMS consent orchestration middleware implemented - [x] audit stamp appended and verified in ingestion path - [x] feature flags and helm values added - [x] tests and basic perf validation - [x] documentation: docs/security/rbac-microcompiler.md

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the emitted DAG format conservative (no recursion, bounded node types) to simplify on-host evaluation. Follow-ups: a) add a small policy-diff validator to detect semantic changes that require full redeploy, b) add a dashboard in Console to show which tenants have micro-compiled artifacts active.

Motivation: we continue to see intermittent latency spikes driven by cold kernel invocations and inefficient prefetch behavior for long prefixes. This PR introduces a set of observability artifacts to surface prefetch effectiveness (hit/miss/age distribution), a token-position cost/latency heatmap, and lightweight kernel-warmup traces so SRE and runtime teams can correlate cold starts with token-level cost.

What this PR adds (summary): 1) metric: runtime.prefetch.hit_ratio and runtime.prefetch.age_bucketed (tiled histogram) by model+pool, exposed via metrics pipeline; 2) metric: token.position.heatmap (downsampled 2D histogram keyed by model, route, and sequence-length-bin); 3) tracing: kernel.warmup.span with attributes (model, device_type, kernel_id, warmup_phase, kv_prefetched) and short-span sampling at 1% with deterministic reservoir for correlation; 4) dashboard: "Prefetch & Warmup" Grafana dashboard with three panels (prefetch hit-ratio over time, token-position heatmap, recent kernel-warmup traces linked to trace IDs); 5) alert: prefetch-miss-rate-high (SLO-aware reframe) that auto-suppresses during known release windows and triggers a debug runbook.

Implementation notes: - Metrics are emitted from runtime/prefetch_manager and aggregated in observability/metrics/exporter with a compact histogram encoding to keep cardinality low. - Token-position heatmap is calculated in the invocation summarizer: we sample the first 256 positions and bucket by quartiles of sequence length. The heatmap uses a tiled downsampled store so dashboards don't fetch raw high-cardinality series. - Kernel warmup spans are added to the kernel scheduler hot path; spans are created only when (a) a kernel requires binary reinitialization or (b) prefetch miss triggers a fallback path. Warmup spans are intentionally short and use a special trace tag to avoid inflating normal trace retention. - Dashboard JSON lives in observability/dashboards/prefetch-warmup.json and includes drilldowns to the trace explorer and cost explorer panels.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests: metrics encoders and histogram bucketers (runtime/prefetch_manager/*_test.go). - Integration: end-to-end run in the perf-lab using a synthetic workload that simulates long prefix usage (script: perf-lab/synthetic/prefetch-smoke.sh). - Observability QA: deployed dashboard to staging and verified correlations between forced kernel reloads and heatmap spikes. - Performance: microbench shows ~0.6% p99 latency delta at very high QPS when warmup spans are enabled; span sampling and downsampling mitigations keep steady-state overhead <0.2%.

Rollout plan: feature flagged behind observability.prefetch_warmup_metrics. Initial rollout to staging (complete), then canary to 5% of edge pools for 48 hours, then 25% for 24 hours, then global. Alert created in staging and set to notify the runtime-oncall channel in canary.

Docs and runbook: added runtime/docs/prefetch-metrics.md with metric definitions, alerting thresholds, and a short runbook for on-call. The runbook outlines steps to confirm whether a spike is caused by model variant changes, kernel kernel-cache eviction, or network-mounted model manifests.

Related work: complements ENG-2086 (kv-cache-profiler) and ENG-2310 (token-heatmap-exploration). Not a replacement for model cost attribution work but provides high-fidelity signals useful for root cause.

Notes: kept cardinality low by scoping metrics at model+pool and bucketing sequence lengths; token-position heatmap is intentionally approximate to avoid explosion of series.

Asha Patel: Yes — metrics are emitted with model and pool tags only; variant and tenant are not present. Added explicit tests to prove card remains bounded.

Asha Patel: Updated alert to be SLO-aware and added an auto-suppress rule during release windows in the alert yaml.

Motivation: We observed intermittent latency spikes originating from the prefetch path in the serving runtime. On investigation, spikes correlate to a small number of heavy shards where prefetch work queues pile up and cause backpressure across concurrent requests. Existing telemetry exposed only request-level prefetch timings; we lacked shard-level visibility and a reliable way to reproduce the long-tail behavior in CI. This PR adds shard-scoped prefetch metrics, a synthetic token-trace generator to reproduce prefetched-KV patterns, an observability dashboard to surface shard hotspots, and tuned alerts that reduce false positives from noisy tenants.

What this PR changes (summary):
- Instrumentation: add per-shard prefetch metrics (prefetch_latency_ms_histogram, prefetch_queue_depth_gauge, prefetched_tokens_count) with stable labels: tenant_id, route, model_name, shard_id, and prefetch_reason. Metrics are emitted from the prefetch worker and at request-join points to correlate request latency with outstanding prefetch work.
- Synthetic trace generator: introduce telemetry/traces/synthetic_generator.py, a small harness that emits OpenTelemetry spans representing token-level generation with configurable prefix lengths, KV prefetch delays, and per-token compute latencies. The generator can be run in CI/canary clusters to inject controlled workloads and validate sampling, aggregation, and alerting behavior.
- Dashboards: add a new prefetch-shard heatmap dashboard (observability/dashboards/prefetch-shard-heatmap.json). Panels include: shard p95/p99 latency heatmap, queue-depth time-series, request-to-prefetch waterfall, and a drilldown for top-N noisy shards by tenant.
- Alerts: introduce per-shard adaptive alerting rule (observability/alerts/prefetch-shard-alerts.yaml). Alerts use a two-stage detector: (1) p95/p99 surge detector with short window for immediate action, (2) per-shard noise suppression using decaying suppression windows to avoid chasing noisy tenants. Alerts surface shard_id and tenant_id for quick triage and include runbook links.
- Tests and examples: add unit tests for metrics emission and an example HCL job that runs the synthetic generator against a canary telemetry endpoint (examples/telemetry/prefetch-replay.hcl). Also add docs describing how to run the generator and interpret the dashboard (docs/observability/prefetch-tracing.md).

Why this implementation: Shard-level metrics let us isolate that a small subset of shards cause disproportionate delay. The synthetic generator provides deterministic replay for CI and debugging without requiring production traffic. The alert tuning reduces noisy alert fatigue while preserving signal for genuine regressions.

Compatibility and rollout plan:
- Metrics use new metric names with stable labels and are gated behind an opt-in runtime flag (ENABLE_PREFETCH_SHARD_METRICS) to allow gradual rollout.
- Synthetic trace generator is behind a telemetry feature flag and can be deployed only to canary clusters initially.
- Dashboard and alerts are added to the default observability repo but alerts are disabled by default; they are promoted to enabled during the canary monitoring phase after two days of stable signals.

Testing performed:
- Unit tests for metrics emission and label cardinality checks (serving/prefetch/prefetch_test.go).
- Integration run on staging canary: synthetic generator replayed 10k synthetic invocations over 6 hours to validate histogram buckets and alert thresholds.
- CI: lint, unit, and telemetry e2e run passed in canary environment.

Release notes: "Adds shard-level prefetch telemetry, a synthetic token trace generator for replaying prefetch-heavy workloads, a new dashboard to surface shard hotspots, and tuned per-shard alerts to reduce noisy paging."

Context: Production has seen short-lived traffic spikes that flip regional circuits and trigger repeated failovers within a 60s window. These micro-flaps undermine tail-latency SLOs and generate noisy incident churn. This PR implements two complementary mitigations: 1) a lightweight per-region "SLO reservoir" that absorbs transient token bursts by allowing a small, time-bounded credit pool per SLO class and tenant cohort; 2) a "circuit lull respite" policy that imposes an adaptive reopen delay and a soft drain phase before full circuit restoration to reduce flip-flop. Motivation: previous mitigations (hard throttle/circuit immediate reopen) either impact steady traffic or allow rapid re-open/close cycles. The reservoir smooths short token bursts without degrading long-tail throughput; the lull respite stabilizes circuit state transitions. Design summary: reservoir: configurable credits expressed in token-ms (tokens*ms) per region and SLO tier, refill with exponential backoff when saturated, borrowing allowed across tenant cohorts within a reserve budget, overflow triggers a predictive soft-shed (prefers non-blocking degrade paths). circuit lull respite: state machine extension with LULL state between CLOSED and OPEN; LULL enforces slower reopen ramp (soft-concurrency limits + KV-preserve hints), records a lull_score derived from recent circuit events and telemetry, and extends reopen windows when score is high. Interaction and invariants: 1) reservoir deficits surface to the SLO controller which will prefer reservoir-backed admission over full circuit trip; 2) when reservoir exhausted, the existing circuit trip path remains intact; 3) lull respite consults reservoir pressure before permitting a transition to CLOSED to avoid reintroducing load. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated, default off for all customers; staged canary to 5% of traffic in us-west-2 for 48h, then 25% and 100% after metric stability checks. Telemetry and alerts: new metrics added: slo_reservoir_available_tokens, slo_reservoir_refill_rate, circuit_lull_score, circuit_lull_state_transitions. Alerting: reservoir_high_spill (>5% tenants spill for >5m) and lull_reopen_oscillation (>3 reopen-close cycles per minute). Testing: unit tests for credit math, property tests for refill/borrow semantics, e2e with synthetic burst harness in perf-lab, chaos test to validate circuit lull behavior under repeated spike patterns. Compatibility: conservative defaults maintain existing behavior; operators can tune reservoir sizes and lull thresholds. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-8421) [x] unit tests added [x] load tests in perf-lab executed [x] telemetry dashboards sketched [x] feature flag gating in place [x] docs/ops playbook updated Impact and rationale: reduces incident noise and preserves tail SLOs by smoothing transient demand and preventing immediate reopen churn. Related: this complements transient-hedge and graceful-evac modules (see ENG-8477). TODO/Follow-ups: automatic tuning loop (future work), RBAC controls for per-tenant overrides, and a UI control in Console for reservoir sizing.
Aarav Singh: Nice approach. Please add guardrails to ensure a tiny reservoir can't be abused by high-concurrency bursty tenants.
Maya Chen: Added borrow cap and tenant-level max_credit in controller config; documented in ops playbook.
Priya Kapoor: Concern about metrics cardinality if we emit per-tenant tokens for every tenant. Can we aggregate?
Maya Chen: We only emit per-tenant spill events at 1m throttle and aggregate reservoir availability at region-tier level; added comment and ROI calc.
Liam O'Connor: Can we bump the default lull reopen ramp to be more conservative for Dedicated clusters?
Maya Chen: Exposed cluster_type override; default remains conservative for Dedicated in config
Introduces a configurable SLO reservoir to smooth transient token bursts and a circuit lull respite policy to reduce reopen flip-flop. Defaults are opt-in behind a feature flag and safe for conservative rollouts. Adds telemetry and dashboards for monitoring reservoir pressure and circuit lull state.
Operator action: enable feature flag for canary region and monitor slo_reservoir_available_tokens and circuit_lull_score. If spills observed, reduce reservoir size or enable soft-shed to avoid tenant impact.

Motivation: tail latency and occasional starvation remain a concern for long-lived continuous batching workloads that mix very small and very large KV-aware requests. Existing admission logic can leave low-priority small requests waiting behind large KV-heavy slots for extended periods, especially under transient load spikes and kernel-switch latencies. This PR introduces two coordinated mechanisms: 1) Soft slot compaction: a background compaction pass that opportunistically collapses underutilized slots to reduce fragmentation and improve batch packing without violating latency SLOs; 2) Reverse probe (starvation recovery probe): a low-overhead probe that periodically injects high-priority short-circuit admissions from the tail of the queue to validate progress and trigger rebalancing when starvation is detected. Design summary: soft slot compaction tracks slot utilization windows and merges adjacent underutilized soft slots when the expected merge latency benefit outweighs requeue cost; compaction runs with adaptive backoff tuned by observed kernel context-switch cost and current throughput. Reverse probe uses a lightweight preempt token that can be granted to small requests older than a configurable threshold; if a probe succeeds it increments a decay counter and relaxes admission gating for similar requests for a short epoch. Both features are KV-aware: compaction respects KV pin locality hints and avoids merging slots across incompatible KV caches; probes include a kernel hint so the runtime can choose a faster, lower-quantization kernel path when available. Implementation notes: scheduler.go implements soft slot compaction state machine and compaction heuristics; kv_cache.go exposes lease-safe merge primitives; selection.go includes a fast-path for probe-elected admissions and kernel_hint metadata; a new metrics set is added (batcher.compaction.* and batcher.probe.*) and knobs exposed via the dynamic config system. Testing and benchmarks: microbenchmarks with mixed 80/20 small/large request distributions show 95th tail latency improvement of 22-28% in steady-state and 30-45% improvement under spike scenarios with preserved median latencies. Throughput impact is +/- 2% depending on the workload; CPU overhead for compaction is measured at <0.6% on our benchmark fleet. Rollout plan: feature toggles default off in regions with strict latency SLOs; gradual rollout using canary groups and telemetry gating. Fallback: compaction and reverse probe are reversible via config, and compaction only performs non-destructive merges; if regressions are observed the rollout will be halted and automatic rollback triggered. Related work: builds on earlier admission and holdback experiments (see ENG-1122, ENG-1209), and complements prefix/KV caching improvements in ENG-1256. Documentation: RFC added under docs/rfc/soft_slot_compaction.md and runtime knobs documented in ops/console. Risks and mitigations: compaction could increase requeue churn if misconfigured; mitigated by conservative defaults, adaptive backoff, and safety guards that prevent compaction when kernel latencies exceed configured thresholds. The PR includes extensive unit and integration tests and a release note entry. 
Mateo Rivera: Overall this looks promising. Two high-level asks: (1) add a safety guard to disable compaction when kernel context-switch cost exceeds N ms, and (2) clarify the compaction backoff math in the RFC. Please address before approving.
Ava Chen: Added configurable safety_guard and added explicit formula/graph to RFC; expanded unit tests to include high kernel-latency path.
Priya Singh: Tests look good. I'd like to see an additional integration run with KV pin churn enabled; the current e2e looks synthetic. Can you run that and paste results?
Ava Chen: Ran pinned-kv churn scenario in integration cluster; attached perf numbers to CI artifact and noted results in PR description. No regressions observed in our run.
Liam O'Connor: Minor: rename metric batcher.compaction.attempts -> batcher.compaction.attempt_count for consistency. Also please add a short note in release notes about default-off rollout.
Ava Chen: Renamed metric and added release note entry. Thanks.
Soft slot compaction + reverse probe for continuous batcher to reduce 95th tail latency under mixed small/large workloads. Feature default-off; rollout by canary. Knobs: batcher.compaction.enabled, batcher.compaction.backoff_ms, batcher.probe.threshold_ms.

payload.body: Context: A recent incident showed rapid autoscaler oscillation combined with aggressive regional load-shedding can flip tenant circuits repeatedly for short surges, causing elevated tail latency and client-visible 5xx spikes. This PR introduces a short-lived autoscale circuit buffer and an ephemeral tenant throttle controller to smooth transient surges and prevent circuit thrashing. Motivation: reduce noisy reopen/close cycles for circuits, minimize KV drain races during fast failovers, and provide tighter telemetry for SLO enforcement windows. Summary of changes: 1) runtime/circuit/buffer: new in-memory short TTL buffer that holds recent circuit-state transitions and suppresses immediate reopen requests for a configurable damping window; 2) controlplane/throttle: ephemeral throttle controller that applies micro-throttles (soft rejects) for tenants that trigger >X circuit flips within Ys; throttles are non-persistent and decay exponentially; 3) autoscaler: small heuristic adjustment so the autoscaler consults buffer signals before aggressive scale-out decisions during high-frequency spikes; 4) kvsync: add KV-drain guard to avoid concurrent drain + reopen race that produced sticky circuit state in the incident; 5) telemetry: new metrics (circuit_buffer_suppressed, ephemeral_throttle_active, kv_guard_blocked_ops) and a dashboard tile; 6) tests: unit + integration tests for buffer hysteresis and throttle decay, and a small perf benchmark that runs 10k synthetic short spikes showing reduced reopen rate. Rollout plan: feature-gated behind runtime.feature_flags.experimental_circuit_buffer; enable in staging for 24h, then canary 5% traffic for 6h, then progressive ramp if no regressions. Monitoring / runbook: added runbook section with alert tuning (circuit_reopen_rate > 5/min for 5m) and recommended rollback steps. Backports: small patch backported to release-1.8 branch (see backport commit). Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-4821) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Perf benchmark - [x] Updated metrics and dashboard - [x] Runbook and rollout instructions Related: incident postmortem SUP-1192, previous PRs on circuit resilience. Risk: medium — touching circuit and autoscaler interactions; mitigations include flag gating, tight canary window, and conservative defaults.

payload.body:
Context: We observed a slow degradation pattern in regional SLOs where per-tenant resource commitments were leaking over time (tokens/second and KV cache pressure) even though instantaneous load and queueing looked healthy. This manifest was distinct from burst load failures: clients would slowly consume more shared resources and trigger eviction heuristics only after long-tail accumulation, causing noisy partial failures and cascading tenant evictions. Motivation: Improve early detection of SLO 'leaks' (gradual resource drift) and introduce a low-impact, reversible soft-suspend mode that gracefully reduces a tenant's share before hard eviction or regional failover. This is a hotpatch to prevent recurring multi-hour incidents while we implement longer-term scheduling ledger changes. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce "differential_slo_leak_detector" in control-plane that computes short-window vs long-window resource usage deltas per tenant and flags progressive drift when long-window >> short-window beyond tuned hysteresis. 2) Add "soft_suspend" orchestrator that applies staged shedding policies (metadata-only flags propagated to serving runtime) with three grades: advisory, throttled, and paused. These grades map to token rate caps, KV cache TTL reduction, and request admission reduction respectively. 3) Fix a bug in the previous suspend/unsuspend path where unsuspend attempts raced with regional rejoin flow, leaving tenants stuck in a suspended state. 4) Telemetry: new metrics slo_leak_score{tenant,region}, soft_suspend_state{0,1,2,3}, suspend_action_reason and audit logs for suspend/unsuspend operations. 5) Rollout: feature-flag gated, staged rollout by traffic weight, region, then full global enable. Checklist: - [x] Design doc + local simulation (ENG-5421) - [x] Unit tests for detector scoring - [x] Integration tests between control-plane and serving runtime (simulated tenants) - [x] Load test showing reduced eviction churn - [x] Monitoring dashboards and alert rules added How it works (short): The detector compares an exponential moving average (EMA) over 6h vs 5m windows to compute a leak score normalized by tenant baseline. When leak_score > threshold and sustained for N cycles, the orchestrator triggers advisory flag which causes runtime to begin conservative caching changes and lightweight rate caps. If the score grows, escalate to throttled then paused. All suspend actions include TTLs and automatic backoffs; manual overrides from Console/SRE are supported. Files and high-level diffs: (described below in files_changed) Migration notes: No DB schema changes. New feature flags: enable_diff_slo_leak_detector, enable_soft_suspend_grades. Monitoring/alerts: slo_leak_score high per-tenant -> PagerDuty SRE on first escalation; advisory stage pages only to on-call Slack channel. Rollback plan: Toggle feature flag off to stop orchestrator and automatically clear soft_suspend states after the TTLs expire. If stuck states observed, a one-off admin unsuspend API is included. Risks & mitigations: Risk of false positives for tenants with legitimate long-running workloads -> mitigated by conservative defaults, two-window confirmation, whitelist config. Runtime coordination bug mitigated in this patch by adding idempotent suspend/unsuspend tokens and a leader-lease around unsuspend flows. Related: ENG-5421 (design), ENG-5503 (follow-up ledger work), SUP-893 (customer incident), internal runbook updated.
Evan Miller: Can we avoid a full new metric per tenant explosion? Suggest histogram buckets and sampled tenants first. Also please annotate the metric with tenant_tier.
Priya Shah (author): Good catch — detector will initially sample at 5% and we emit slo_leak_score only for sampled tenants; histogram and tenant_tier label added in telemetry commit.
Jared Kim: Unsuspend race fix looks solid but add unit tests for leader-lease expiry edge case.
Priya Shah (author): Added leader-lease expiry tests; extended lease TTL in edge environments and documented behaviour in runbook.
Sofia Ramirez: UX looks good. Please ensure admin override records an audit entry. Approved after CI green.
CI: integration tests flaky on first run (timeout in slo_leak_simulation), rerun passed. Build: pass, Unit tests: pass, E2E: pass (with one flaky re-run)
Hotfix: Add differential SLO leak detection and a staged soft-suspend orchestrator to reduce eviction churn and enable graceful degradation for slow-resource-leak scenarios. Feature gated and staged rollout. Admin unsuspend API and runbook included.
Local sim reproduces leak pattern; staged canary at 2 regions for 24h with traffic shadowing showed 60% reduction in hard evictions and stable latency for non-affected tenants. Load tests ran at 10x baseline to verify idempotency and TTL expiry paths.
1) Promote feature flag to additional regions over 48h. 2) Monitor slo_leak_score and suspend_action_reason dashboards. 3) Follow-up ENG-5503 for long-term ledger-based quotas.

Summary
Adds control plane schema + persistence scaffolding for per-deployment autoscaling policy on Redwood Dedicated. This PR introduces customer-configurable min/max capacity bounds and a predictive autoscaling mode toggle at the schema layer only (no autoscaler behavior changes in this PR).

Motivation
Enterprise Dedicated customers are asking for explicit guardrails around scaling: (1) a hard ceiling to control spend, (2) a hard floor to preserve baseline throughput/SLOs, and (3) an opt-in predictive mode to reduce queue buildup during known ramps. We need these fields in the control plane first so Console/API work and autoscaler enforcement can follow behind feature flags.

What changed
- Introduced a new ScalingPolicyV1 object on Dedicated deployments:
  - min_replicas (optional)
  - max_replicas (optional)
  - scale_up_cooldown_seconds (optional)
  - scale_down_cooldown_seconds (optional)
  - predictive_mode (enum: OFF | ADVISORY | ACTIVE)
  - reactive_fallback (bool; default true when predictive_mode != OFF)
- Validation rules:
  - min_replicas >= 0
  - max_replicas >= 0
  - if both set: min_replicas <= max_replicas
  - cooldown seconds must be within [0, 3600] (0 means "no additional cooldown beyond platform defaults")
  - predictive_mode cannot be ACTIVE unless deployment is Dedicated (guard to prevent accidental use in Hosted)
- Defaulting/backward compatibility:
  - Fields are nullable and do not alter existing behavior unless autoscaler + API enablement is turned on (follow-up PRs).
  - If scaling_policy is absent, evaluation continues to use platform defaults.
- Migration scaffolding:
  - Adds the new column / JSON blob storage slot for scaling_policy on the dedicated_deployments row (implementation detail: JSONB payload with versioned schema).
  - Includes no-op backfill migration to initialize the field to NULL (explicitly not setting defaults to avoid unintended behavior changes).
- Telemetry hooks (schema-level only):
  - Adds structured validation error codes returned by the control plane so Console can render field-specific error states later.

Out of scope
- Autoscaler enforcement (clamping desired replicas to min/max) (tracked in ENG-22140)
- Predictive signal ingestion + forecast interface (tracked in ENG-22142)
- Console endpoints + RBAC wiring for update operations (tracked in ENG-22144 / PR-48252)

Testing
- Unit tests for schema validation and error mapping
- Migration tests: apply/rollback on a representative dedicated_deployments fixture

Rollout notes
- This PR is safe to land on its own: the fields are stored but unused until feature flags are enabled and autoscaler support is deployed.
- Follow-up PRs will add: policy evaluation service behavior, autoscaler clamp + metrics, and Console UI.

References
- Linear: ENG-22141, PM-1842
- ADR draft referenced in architecture thread: autoscaling bounds precedence + safety invariants (pending merge)

Checklist
- [x] Schema versioned and backwards compatible
- [x] Validation errors return stable, documented error codes
- [x] Migration is additive and safe to roll back
- [x] Tests cover edge cases (min > max, negative values, cooldown bounds)

Ethan Park (review): Please make predictive_mode an enum rather than a boolean. We’re likely to need an intermediate state for "advisory" / shadow eval.
Benji Okafor (author): Agreed. Updated to OFF | ADVISORY | ACTIVE. Validation now blocks ACTIVE outside Dedicated.
Jordan Lee (review): Validation should return stable error codes for Console; please avoid string matching on message bodies.
Benji Okafor (author): Added ScalingPolicyValidationErrorCode and mapped to API errors with field paths.
Michael Nguyen (review): Migration should be additive and avoid backfilling defaults; otherwise we risk changing behavior when autoscaler starts reading it.
Benji Okafor (author): Migration now adds JSONB column only; no backfill beyond NULL. Left a follow-up note for ENG-22153 to handle defaults under a flag.
Chloe Martin (review): Can we ensure cooldown bounds are not "magic"? Add constants and tests for min/max allowed values.
Benji Okafor (author): Added COOLDOWN_SECONDS_MIN/MAX constants and expanded test coverage.
Ethan Park (approval): Looks good. Please link the ADR once merged; otherwise fine to proceed.
Jordan Lee (approval): Approved after enum + error code changes.

Motivation:
The KV cache is showing increasing internal fragmentation for workloads with many variable-size keys and time-varying tenant footprints. Fragmentation increases spill frequency and surface tail latency during continuous batching. This PR introduces a low-impact background compaction \"page sculptor\" and an eviction-pruning heuristic to prefer packing and keep hot working sets contiguous, reducing spill pressure and improving p99 latency.

Design/Changes (high level):
- Background Page Sculptor: a cooperative background worker that compacts free holes inside a page by relocating live records into contiguous regions using an occupancy bitmap and in-place memmove helpers. The sculptor runs with a bounded CPU budget and is tenant-aware to avoid impacting busy tenants. It is non-blocking for foreground readers and writers: compaction uses versioned moves and a short CAS window to switch pointers.
- Fragmentation Score: each page now maintains a lightweight fragmentation score (0-100) derived from occupancy runs and average free-region size. The score is exposed to the eviction layer.
- Prune-evict heuristic: eviction now accounts for fragmentation score and expected relocation cost. Pages with high fragmentation are deprioritized for immediate eviction; instead, the sculptor is scheduled for those pages and eviction will target low-fragmentation pages first to reduce future churn.
- Soft spill annotations: when free memory pressure crosses a soft threshold, pages are annotated for preferred spill candidates and the allocator avoids allocating new variable-size entries into highly fragmented pages. This reduces immediate spill-over to disk by preferring cheaper relocation or eviction.
- Scheduler & Batcher integration: continuous-batching path now prefers slices that touch compacted/low-fragmentation pages first, improving cache locality for batched token generation and reducing KV miss latencies.

Benchmarks:
- Long-sequence conversational workload (mixed-size keys): 10-14% increased sustained throughput at p50 token throughput for a 2048-token distribution; p99 end-to-end latency reduced by 12-25% depending on tenant mix.
- Cold-start heavy churn test: 22% reduction in spill-to-disk operations and a 30% reduction in write amplification from spill cycles.
- CPU overhead: sculptor runs with a 3-6% CPU budget on production-like machines; net CPU spend was reclaimed via fewer expensive spill operations.

Testing and stability:
- Added unit tests for sculptor invariants and move/rollback behavior.
- Integration tests for eviction ordering and fragmentation score propagation.
- Perf harness runs on perf-lab with representative tenant mixes; a perf regression flagged during initial run was resolved by limiting sculptor concurrency and adding tenant throttling.

Rollout plan:
1) Canary on low-traffic capacity pools with sculptor disabled by default (feature flag).
2) Enable sculptor in read-heavy tenants and validate decreased spill rates for two weeks.
3) Gradual enablement on high-throughput pools with dynamic CPU budget tuning.
4) Monitor fragmentation, spill counts, p99 latency; automatic rollback if spill increases >10% vs baseline.

Notes & related work:
- Complements earlier allocator improvements (segmented slab work) by addressing intra-page free-space fragmentation rather than coarse-grained slab sizing.
- Related Linear: ENG-1298 (KV fragmentation monitoring), ENG-2114 (scheduler affinity hooks).

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc (docs/rfc/page-sculptor.md)
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Perf runs in perf-lab
- [x] Feature-flag gated and rollout plan

Miguel Torres: Overall this looks promising; two asks: add a safety timeout for in-place moves and justify the serialization window in the design doc.
Evelyn Park: Added timeout and expanded the doc with the CAS window justification + microbench numbers (see docs/rfc/page-sculptor.md).
Sophie Lin: Can sculptor cause tail latency spikes if scheduled on very busy tenants? Recommend tenant-throttling and budget caps.
Evelyn Park: Implemented tenant-aware budget and fallback to mark-for-evict when sculptor is starved; added tests to assert no tail regressions under load.
Daniel Park: perf numbers look good; confirm that metric exposure includes fragmentation histogram and sculptor CPU burn. Approved pending CI pass.
CI system: perf/regression check passed on re-run (no regressions >1% across tracked metrics).
Merge bot: Merged by squash into main (merge_method: squash).
Introduce Page Sculptor (background compaction) and fragmentation-aware eviction ordering; reduces spill events and improves p99 latency for variable-size KV workloads. Feature gated; enable via feature flag 'page_sculptor' and tune sculptor.cpu_budget.

Motivation: Close remaining gaps in /v1/chat.completions parity for parameter handling, role preservation, stop+logprob reconciliation, and structured tool responses while reducing streaming edge-case flakiness. This PR introduces a lightweight "param sanitizer" that accepts both legacy and canonical v1 forms, a deterministic role policy to avoid role aliasing regressions, and a compact synthesis layer for tool/function outputs that produces a consistent framed JSON payload usable by both streaming and non-streaming clients.

What changed (high-level):
- v1 param sanitizer: normalizes `messages`, `temperature`, `top_p`, `max_tokens` and maps deprecated aliases (e.g., `n_predict` -> `max_tokens`) while preserving unknown fields for forwards-compatibility. The sanitizer runs early in the request pipeline and emits stable attribute metadata used by downstream components.
- Role policy: enforces role canonicalization (user/assistant/system/tool) and attaches an explicit `role_source` header when an incoming message had an alias. This prevents attribute loss during partial stream rehydration and ensures consistent role ordering for logprob alignment.
- Stop/logprob reconciliation: when model-provided logprobs are missing for stop-delimited termination, the runtime performs a deterministic backfill pass that adjusts end-token attribution and attaches a `logprob_backfilled: true` flag to the response envelope.
- Tool/Function response synthesis: introduces a compact framed-json schema v2 for tool outputs that supports both immediate tool-call streaming and post-hoc synthesized tool payloads. Synthesis handles three modes: passthrough (original tool JSON), wrapped (adds metadata and stable id), and flattened (tool output merged into assistant message with provenance fields).
- Streaming stability fixes: small coalescer adjustments to avoid duplicated sentinel emissions during rapid tool-handshake sequences; heartbeat window widened by 30ms to reduce spurious disconnects observed in high-concurrency traces.
- Observability + docs: added per-request sanitizer metrics (redwood.sanitizer.normalized), a tracing span for `param_sanitizer`, and documentation updates in docs/openai-compat.md describing the v2 framed-json tool response format and migration notes.

Compatibility and rollout: The sanitizer is opt-in via a feature flag `enable_v1_param_shim` (default enabled for hosted API, configurable for Dedicated/Private). The role policy preserves original alias strings in `role_source` so customers can detect prior behavior. The framed-json v2 is backward-compatible with v1 framed consumers; runtime will emit v1-compatible envelope when `compat_mode=v1` is present in the request.

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests for sanitizer permutations (aliases, missing fields, extra unknown keys).
- Integration tests exercising streaming tool handshake + coalescer with synthetic high-concurrency load.
- Manual validation against OpenAI-v1 compatibility test vectors (included under tests/compat/fixtures) and a small runtime canary deployed to staging for 48 hours.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-8120: Add telemetry alert for excessive logprob_backfilled occurrences.
- ENG-8197: Extend framed-json v2 to carry structured evaluation hints (for Optimize).

Notes: The description above condenses a few design docs (links: Linear ENG-7892) and the implementation follows the runtime kernel selection guards so there is no measurable token-latency regression in internal benchmarks (0.5% p50 change).
Liam O'Connor: Please add a small backwards-compat test that asserts compat_mode=v1 still yields the original envelope shape.
Maya Patel (author): Added tests/compat/fixtures and unit asserting compat_mode behavior in integration harness.
Sofia Ramirez: Can you log an event when role_source is non-empty so we can measure alias prevalence?
Maya Patel: Added a counter metric (redwood.sanitizer.role_alias_seen) and a trace tag.
Ethan Park: The coalescer tweak looks good but we saw a single flaky CI run on streaming-integration. Recommend rerunning the job.
CI: initial run had one flaky streaming test; after fix and squash, CI passed.
Approvals: Liam O'Connor approved, Sofia Ramirez approved, Ethan Park approved.
v1 chat parity: normalized param handling, deterministic role alias preservation, logprob backfill for stop-terminal cases, and framed-json v2 for tool responses (backwards-compatible).

Context: We see recurrent small-fragment churn in tenant KV caches under mixed-generation workloads (short prompt inference + chat continuations). Frequent small-page evictions increase spill frequency and disk IO, which amplifies latency variance and costs. This PR implements a new eviction strategy (Granular Coalesce Evictor, GCE) combined with kernel-aware routing signals to reduce unnecessary spills and improve tail latency for production workloads.

What this PR does: Implements GCE that: (1) detects clusters of small adjacent fragments and coalesces them in-memory before choosing to spill; (2) uses a hybrid scoring function that weights fragmentation impact, tenant priority, and an estimated kernel recompile/execution cost to prefer evicting entries that are cheaper to rehydrate; (3) introduces a burst-aware coalescer that defers full compaction under sustained IO pressure. Integrates eviction signals with the kernel selector so routed requests prioritize model/kernel variants that minimize recompile overhead for likely-evicted keys.

Design notes: - Coalescing is opportunistic: we never block foreground allocations; coalesces run in background workers with adaptive throttling. - Scoring: score = w_frag*frag_score + w_tenant*priority + w_kernel*kernel_recompile_cost_estimate. Kernel cost heuristic is derived from recent kernel switch counters and sequence-length histograms. - Backpressure: the coalescer watches node-level IO/sustained-spill-rate and transitions from aggressive -> conservative -> disabled modes. - Safe-paths: in case coalescer fails or causes regressions, we fall back to previous LRU-evictor via config flag kv.evictor.mode = legacy.

Why kernel-aware routing: Small fragments often belong to short-seq workloads that map to lighter kernels; when eviction will likely occur we prefer to route new requests to kernels that avoid heavy recompile penalties. This coordination reduces overall CPU/GPU kernel churn and improves p95 for mixed workloads.

Testing and rollout: Unit and integration tests exercise scoring, fallback, and backpressure. Added bench harness in perf-canary with mixed chat + short-generation workload. Canary rollout configured: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 72h with automated regression gate (p95 latency and spill-rate).

Notes on runtime config knobs added: - kv.evictor.coalesce_window_ms (default 200) - kv.evictor.max_coalesce_size_bytes (default 256KB) - kv.evictor.kernel_weight (default 0.4) - kv.evictor.io_backpressure_threshold (MB/s)

Related: ENG-8421 (kv memory management), ENG-9153 (kernel selection improvements).
Marco Silva (2026-01-25): Great design. Two asks: (1) please add a unit-test that simulates sustained IO pressure and verifies coalescer transitions; (2) document the expected CPU overhead of coalescing under no-spill conditions.
Ava Chen (2026-01-26): Added integration_backpressure_test and instrumentation for CPU cost counters. Bench numbers included in PR description. Replied inline about adaptive duty-cycle to bound CPU impact.
Priya Kapoor (2026-01-28): Question on eviction scoring: how sensitive are weights? Suggest adding a diagnostic metric exposing chosen-weight contributions to make tuning easier.
Ava Chen (2026-01-29): Added kv_gce_metrics:score_components which breaks down the score into fragment/tenant/kernel components. Also added runtime knobs for each weight.
Liam O'Neill (2026-02-02): Verified perf canary results and asked to add rollback playbook steps in the RFC.
Ava Chen (2026-02-03): Expanded RFC with rollback procedure and added 'kv.evictor.mode=legacy' gate for immediate rollback. CI green and ready to merge.
Perf bench (mixed chat + short gen): - baseline (legacy evictor): p50=62ms p95=248ms spill_rate=0.48/spill-eviction-per-1k-ops fragmentation_score=0.71 - GCE + kernel-aware routing (this PR): p50=60ms p95=218ms (-12%), spill_rate=0.30 (-37%), fragmentation_score=0.55 (-22%). Token cost estimate: ~6% reduction due to fewer asynchronous spill penalties. Note: results averaged over 12h canary with 95% CI attached in perf artifacts.
- Introduces Granular Coalesce Evictor (GCE) to reduce small-fragment spills and improve tail latency.
- Adds kernel-aware eviction scoring to reduce kernel churn for likely-evicted entries.
- New runtime flags to tune coalescing behavior and IO backpressure.
- Backwards compatible; legacy evictor available via kv.evictor.mode=legacy.
1) Run unit tests (kv evictor suite). 2) Run integration_backpressure_test locally. 3) Deploy perf-canary mixed workload manifest to perf-canary cluster; monitor p95 latency and spill_rate. 4) Gradual rollout 5%->25%->100% with automated gates; rollback immediately to legacy via kv.evictor.mode if spill_rate increases or p95 regresses >10%.
Ops: watch metrics kv.gce.coalesce_ops_per_min, kv.gce.current_mode, kv.gce.spill_rate, kernel.selector.switches_per_min. If node-level IO > kv.evictor.io_backpressure_threshold for 5m, GCE will enter conservative mode; consider scaling capacity or disabling GCE if conservative mode persists >30m.
payload.title: kv: granular coalesce evictor and kernel-aware routing for spill reduction

payload.body:
Motivation: reduce per-token compute and memory pressure for mixed-length workloads by introducing a blockwise attention microkernel that applies rotary embeddings in-place and a coalesced KV slab layout to reduce eviction churn under continuous batching. This is targeted at production inference workloads where many short requests interleave with occasional long sequences, and where KV cache eviction/compaction hurts tail latency and throughput.

Design summary: single-string overview of the changes and rationale. The change introduces: 1) a blockwise attention microkernel (C++/CUDA) that operates on fixed tiles (configurable tile sizes per-device) and performs matmul, rotary application, and softmax reduction across tiles to improve register reuse and reduce intermediate memory traffic; 2) in-place rotary application baked into the microkernel so we avoid an extra QKV transform buffer and extra memcopies for rotary/rope, enabling a fused Q*K pass for short sequences; 3) a coalesced slab layout for KV cache where cache entries are allocated in device slabs grouped by model-shard and sequence-block to reduce fragmentation and avoid frequent small reallocations; 4) scheduler hints to prefer homogenous micro-batches (same tile shapes) and a lightweight placement heuristic that pins streams to slots with matching slab affinity; 5) an opt-in runtime flag redwood.runtime.attn.blockwise_enabled and a dynamic tunable redwood.runtime.attn.tile_size that defaults to 64 for A100/B100 families but is auto-tuned during warmup.

What changed (high level):
- Serving runtime: new kernel registration and selection path for blockwise_attn (kernel selector picks blockwise_attn when model architecture and sequence distribution fit heuristics).
- Kernels: new CUDA microkernel (src/serving/kernels/blockwise_attn.cu) and a small CPU fallback (src/serving/kernels/blockwise_attn_cpu.cc).
- KV cache: allocator and layout changes (src/serving/kv/coalesced_slab.h, .cc) plus eviction policy tweaks to prefer LRU within slab groups.
- Scheduler: runtime/router updates to emit tile-shaped batch groups (src/serving/scheduler/tile_grouping.{cc,h}) and added placement hints in request metadata.
- Config/flags: runtime config and console flags for tuning.

Benchmarks (perf-lab A100, end-to-end inference with standard chat workload and continuous-batching enabled):
- Seq=128, batch mix skewed to short: throughput +1.9x, median latency -22%, p95 latency -18%.
- Seq=512, mixed: throughput +1.4x, p95 -11%.
- Seq=4096 (long): p95 latency -12% due to reduced KV eviction stalls when long sequences interleave.
- Token/dollar improvement measured at 1.45x on our internal cost model for typical production mix.

Safety / compatibility: feature gated behind redwood.runtime.attn.blockwise_enabled=false by default for private/dedicated until validated per-customer. The API surface (generation/embeddings endpoints) is unchanged: kernel selection is internal. Backwards compatible with pinned model-versions and will not run when a model requires a kernel not supported by blockwise_attn (e.g., certain fused custom ops).

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for slab allocator and eviction (tests/kv/coalesced_slab_test.cc).
- Microbench harness added under perf/bench/blockwise_attn_bench.cc with autotest runs on perf-canary.
- Integration smoke tests in CI: python-sdk functional tests and a reduced perf-smoke were run; perf smoke was flaky once but the rerun passed.
- End-to-end perf runs recorded in perf-lab and uploaded as artifacts (perf-lab job IDs in comments).

Checklist: [x] Kernel correctness tests [x] Bench harness added [x] Perf regression guard rails [x] Feature flag + config [x] Documentation: docs/ops/blockwise_attn.md added (usage, tradeoffs, tuning guidance) [x] Rollout plan: staged canary -> dedicated pool opt-in -> wider default.

Changed files (high level): list of key files modified and purpose. Small illustrative snippets included only where helpful.

Related tickets and context: Linear: ENG-4892 (continuous-batching KV eviction reduction), ENG-5031 (kernel selector improvements). Also follows up on earlier work on fused rotary/flash integration but purposely uses a simpler, narrower microkernel to increase robustness and support a broader range of models.

Merge: squash-merged after perf lab artifacts matched expectations and two approvals.

Notes for reviewers: pay special attention to memory ordering in coalesced_slab and the fallback slow path correctness. Tuning knobs are intentionally conservative; we expect incremental future improvements (auto-tiling, int8 kernels).
Introduces a blockwise attention microkernel with in-place rotary application and a coalesced KV slab cache layout. Provides up to ~1.9x throughput improvement on short-sequence heavy mixes and lower tail latency for mixed workloads. Feature is behind a runtime flag and opt-in for Dedicated/Private until fully validated.
Elena Gomez: left a comment on coalesced_slab eviction edge-case; please add assertion and an extra regression test.
Asha Mehta: addressed by adding slab_stability_test.cc and adjusted eviction to prefer hot-slot preservation; updated benchmarks.
Marcus Nguyen: requested perf numbers with continuous-batching disabled; added results to perf artifact and confirmed small regression on pure-long workloads (tradeoff documented).
Priya Shah: approved after verifying CI perf-smoke rerun and kernel fallback path tests.
payload.title: Blockwise attention microkernel with in-place rotary + KV coalescing

Motivation: presubmit latency and flakiness have increased due to heavy I/O (container pulls, repeated dependency installs, large integration fixture downloads). This PR reduces presubmit I/O by introducing a fast-presubmit profile, a toolchain lease for ephemeral runner cache reuse, and dependency-visibility heuristics so that only modules touched by the change install their deps. In addition, a lightweight release-prober workflow is added to smoke-check release bundles before the formal release window. Goals: 1) speed up common presubmit feedback loops (lint/unit) to <= 2m for small changes; 2) shift expensive integration artifacts to nightly or staged lanes; 3) provide a low-cost pre-release smoke check to catch packaging/regression regressions before human release checks. Summary of approach and changes: - Add .github/actions/fast-presubmit.yml and adapt presubmit dispatcher to pick profiles by changed paths and commit message flags (CI_FAST=true). - Add a toolchain lease agent (scripts/toolchain_lease.go + ci/toolchain-lease-proxy) that acquires a short-lived lease for runner-local cache volumes so concurrent CI jobs reuse image layers and node_modules across short windows instead of re-pulling every job. - Introduce dependency-visibility logic in the presubmit orchestrator (ci/presubmit/dep_visibility.py) which computes minimal dep sets for changed packages and only installs those. - Slim CI base images (docker/ci/Dockerfile.slim) and add Makefile targets for layer-splitting to reduce download size. - Move heavy integration tests and large fixture downloads into nightly/integration lanes and add gating in presubmit to only run smoke variants. - Implement .github/workflows/release-prober.yml: on candidate tag, run a 3-step smoke flow (install, basic e2e (10m), package integrity) with clear failure reasons and artifacts. - Emit telemetry: presubmit.profile and toolchain.lease.hits to help tune thresholds. Checklist: - [x] fast-presubmit action and dispatcher wired into existing presubmit workflow - [x] toolchain lease prototype and integration tests - [x] dep-visibility heuristics with test coverage and fallbacks - [x] release-prober manifest and runbook - [x] docs updated (ci/README.md) - [x] Linear tickets linked: ENG-3142 and ENG-3210 Notable constraints/rollbacks: the dep-visibility has a conservative fallback (full-install) when file mappings are ambiguous to avoid flakiness. The toolchain lease includes rate limits to prevent noisy cache thrashing on peak CI usage. Related work: follows earlier presubmit decomposition efforts (see ENG-2101), and complements nightly canary work to keep integration coverage.
Amit Rao: This looks promising; can you add metrics for lease hit/miss and a circuit-breaker when lease acquisition fails?
Maya Chen (author): Added toolchain.lease.hits/misses and a 10s acquisition timeout with exponential backoff. See metrics emitter commit.
Sofia Martinez: Please make sure the release-prober artifacts are preserved for 7d and redact secrets from logs. Also request to add an env var to opt-out in air-gapped installs.
Maya Chen (author): release-prober keeps artifacts in actions/upload-artifact and honors REDWOOD_CI_REDACT; added opt-out via CI_RELEASE_PROBER=false.
Reviewers approved after adding telemetry and opt-outs; one requested tightening of lease timeout defaults which was applied. Decision: conservative default (no aggressive dep prunning) to avoid CAKE/race conditions; ops to monitor metrics and iterate.
Introduce fast-presubmit profile to reduce feedback latency; toolchain lease to reuse runner caches and reduce pull-heavy CI; dependency-visibility to avoid installing unrelated packages; lightweight release-prober to smoke-check release candidates. Ops: monitor presubmit.profile and toolchain.lease.hits metrics to evaluate impact.
payload.title: Reduce presubmit I/O and add lightweight release prober

Motivation: Our CI has grown noisy and slow because full lint/test suites run for every push, and dependency bumps sometimes slip through without the intended curation. This PR introduces two coordinated improvements: (1) a staged build-hook orchestrator that runs quick sanity and path-aware linters first, then expanded checks only for affected packages; and (2) a dependency sanitizer that performs deterministic validation of package.json / lockfile diffs and rejects unsafe upgrades unless they match entries in the dep-curation manifest.

What this changes (single flow):
- Add .github/workflows/staged-ci.yml: a unified staged CI workflow with small, fast early lanes (quick-sanity, changed-path linting) and gated lanes (package lint, unit tests, integration smoke). Each lane is annotated with human-readable stage names and stage_timeout.
- Add tools/commit-paths.ts: utility to compute the set of repo packages and ownership paths touched by the diff; used to limit lint/test scope.
- Add scripts/dep_sanitizer.py: checks package manifest diffs, verifies lockfile integrity, and enforces dep-curation rules (allowed ranges and pinned-safe-flags). Emits machine-readable JSON for the bot to consume.
- Add build/hooks/README.md and small entrypoints for local dev (scripts/run-staged-ci.sh).
- Small changes to .github/labels.yml and CI job templates to expose retry and debug toggles.

Why this is different from prior PRs: Instead of just pruning tests or trimming matrices, this implements commit-path awareness and a deterministic sanitizer that ties dependency upgrades to a curated manifest. It avoids global test-skipping heuristics and focuses on reproducible gating.

Checklist (author):
- [x] Implement tools and CI workflow
- [x] Add unit tests for commit-paths utility (path edge cases, monorepo packages)
- [x] Add sanitizer unit tests to simulate lockfile tampering and allowed vs disallowed upgrades
- [x] Run end-to-end against CI in feature branch

Commits (summary):
- chore(ci): add staged-ci workflow and stage labels
- feat(tooling): introduce commit-paths utility with tests
- feat(scripts): add dep_sanitizer and unit tests + fixtures
- docs: document staged build hooks and feature-flag toggles
- ci: expose retry-count and DEBUG_CI env for flaky tests

Changed files (high-level):
- .github/workflows/staged-ci.yml
- tools/commit-paths.ts
- scripts/dep_sanitizer.py
- build/hooks/README.md
- scripts/run-staged-ci.sh
- .github/ci-templates/job-templates.yml (tweaks)
Introduce staged prebuild pipeline and a dependency sanitizer that validates package manifest diffs and enforces curated upgrades. Backwards-compatible; toggled via repo feature flag.
Ben Cho: Can we add a retry wrapper around the integration smoke stage? We saw flakiness on linux-x86 jobs. Request: add RETRY_COUNT (default 2) and an opt-out DEBUG flag.
Asha Patel: Added RETRY_COUNT to job templates and a DEBUG_CI env toggle. Also added small perf backoff in scripts/run-staged-ci.sh (exponential backoff up to 3 retries).
Lina Gomez: Dep sanitizer looks good; one nit - please tighten error messages to include the offending package path and the offending lockfile entry. Also request adding a regression unit test for yarn -> npm lock conversions.
Asha Patel: Tightened messages and added regression fixture for lockfile conversion scenario.
Initial run: failed (lint error in sdk/js due to new stricter rule) -> author fixed and pushed. Second run: pass across all lanes (quick-sanity, path-lint, package-lint, unit, integration-smoke). Coverage unchanged. Lint warnings reduced by 12. Build artifacts: none (workflow-only change).
Merged via squash after 2 approvals and green CI. Merge method: squash and merge. Changelog: internal; feature gated behind REPO_FEATURE_STAGED_CI.
Local: run scripts/run-staged-ci.sh --local to emulate staged lanes
Unit tests: commit-paths spec covers nested packages and symlinked paths
Sanitizer tests: fixture suite simulates allowed and disallowed upgrades, lockfile tampering
Feature gated by REPO_FEATURE_STAGED_CI (default: off). We'll enable for a subset of CI runners (fastlane tag) for 48h, monitor failure rate in canary, then enable full-run. If dep_sanitizer rejects a PR, maintainers can re-run with bypass token after manual review.
This PR intentionally avoids changing default test coverage. It is an orchestration and enforcement layer. If we see false-positives from the sanitizer, expand the dep-curation manifest and open ENG-8702 to triage recurring false-positives.

Motivation: We have strong token-level cost and latency metrics, but long-tail bursts and allocation-driven skew remain hard to attribute. This PR introduces two complementary observability primitives: (1) latency spectra — a multi-scale decomposition that captures per-invocation latency energy across ordered pipeline phases (network, scheduling, kernel, kv-warmup, generation) and produces compact spectral sketches suitable for low-cardinality rollups; and (2) contextual cost calibrator — a runtime-side annotator that tags token cost with allocator and lane metadata (GPU slot, prefetch bucket, quantization profile) and emits calibrated cost slices for accurate per-tenant chargebacks and alerting.
Add latency spectra: a multi-scale spectral decomposition of invocation latency producing compact rollups for long-tail analysis.
Add contextual cost calibrator: runtime annotator that tags and calibrates per-token cost by allocator and quantization profile for accurate tenant accounting.
New dashboard panels and alert rules for spectra-based anomalies and allocator-aware cost spikes.
No breaking changes to public API; opt-in feature behind feature flag `observability.latency_spectra` for gradual rollout.
Feature-flagged rollout: enable for 5% of hostnames for 48h, validate cost drift against billing summary, enlarge to 25% then 100%. Backout: disable feature flag and rely on rollup de-dupe to reconcile partial samples.
Unit coverage added for spectra decomposition. Integration uses synthetic_spectra_runner to produce deterministic hotpath and coldpath invocations. Bench run included to ensure emitter <2% p95 latency overhead. Manual QA: validated dashboard queries and alerts in staging and replayed 24h of production traces to check join heuristics.
docs/observability/latency-spectra.md describes algorithm, rollup schema, and runbook. Added observability playbook steps for triaging allocator-correlated spikes and instructions to backfill calibrated slices for billing reconciliation.
New alerts tuned with hysteresis: spectra_anomaly will open when spectral energy in generation band increases >30% vs baseline for 10m and calibrated-cost-spike will trigger when allocator-tagged cost increases across >5% of tenants. If noisy, increase alert quiet window or disable fine-grained alloc labels via feature flag.
Ethan Cho (reviewer): Nice approach — can you clarify how spectra handles late-arriving spans from KV cache hydration? I worry about double-counting in rollups.
Priya Menon (author): Spectra contains a 'late_energy' bucket that is emitted only if the late span does not match an existing invocation_id within the sampling window. The rollup job applies a de-duplication join keyed by invocation fingerprint to avoid double-counts. Added notes to docs.
Marina Volkova (reviewer): The allocator labels look high-cardinality (gpu_slot + prefetch_bucket + qprofile). We should provide an aggregated view for SLO dashboards.
Priya Menon (author): Agreed — added a normalized label 'alloc_cluster' that buckets low-volume combinations into 'other' at emitter time and added a fallback sampling path that drops fine-grained alloc tags for low-tier customers. See runtime/annotators/cost_calibrator.go changes.
Samir Patel (reviewer): CI failed on flaky test test_spectra_emission; looks timing-sensitive. Please make integration test resilient.
Priya Menon (author): Reworked test to use deterministic synthetic runner with fixed timestamps and added lightweight retry; CI green locally and on rerun.

Motivation: Streaming endpoints and the OpenAI compatibility shim currently emit minimal telemetry which makes it hard to stitch tool/function-call execution, partial stream fragments, and final response metrics in a single trace. This PR adds hop-by-hop propagation of request metadata through stream fragments, attaches per-endpoint telemetry tags to emitted metrics, and ensures function/tool-call spans surface the original request id and route information. Design summary: 1) attach a compact request metadata header (X-RW-Req: req_id|route|stage) to streaming chunk handshake and to internal tool RPC calls, 2) enrich structured JSONL access logs with endpoint, model_variant, route_tag and request_latency_ms, 3) propagate trace-context (W3C traceparent) into internal tool runner and include span references in the stream fragment payload, 4) add a per-route metrics tag layer so metrics collection (latency/p50/p95, token_count) can be filtered by route and OpenAI-compat route alias. Backwards compatibility: header is optional; older clients continue to work. The OpenAI shim will synthesize the header when an incoming OpenAI-compatible request lacks one so downstream systems see consistent tags. Rollout plan: feature-flagged on a per-cluster basis behind ff.obs.stream-meta. Start with internal canary traffic for 48h, then enable for 25% production traffic for 72h, then full rollout. Migration notes: observability consumers should update parsers to read the new JSONL fields: route_tag, request_id, traceparent, tool_span_id. Implementation details: server/api/stream_handler.go: adds handshake negotiation to exchange X-RW-Req and populates stream fragment metadata. pkg/telemetry/headers.go: header encoder/decoder and validation. pkg/logging/jsonl_writer.go: new structured keys and rate-limited marshalling for high-frequency streaming events. agents/openai_shim/adapter.go: synthesize headers for legacy OpenAI-compatible requests and map openai.endpoint->route_tag. internal/toolrunner/client.go: propagate traceparent and attach parent_request_id to tool spans. Testing: unit tests for header encoding decode and property-based tests for corner-case separators. End-to-end e2e test exercises a multi-fragment streaming response that triggers a function call, asserts trace continuity and ensures final log emits request_latency_ms and tokens_emitted. Performance note: added micro-benchmark; minimal median latency impact (~0.3ms) and small memory for header allocations. Checklist: [x] header encoder/decoder implemented [x] stream handshake updated [x] toolrunner propagation added [x] jsonl fields added and backward safe [x] tests and e2e added [x] docs updated. Related: addresses ENG-1874 (trace fragmentation debugging) and ENG-1902 (openai shim telemetry gaps).
Marco: Overall looks good, one question on header size and separator collision—can you confirm the encoding handles edge chars?
Aisha: Yes, header uses base64 URL-safe encoding for any payload with predictable separator-free output. Added unit tests for separators.
Lena: Left comment to add a minor lint fix in jsonl_writer.go to reduce allocation; also suggested adding a metrics tag for model_variant.
Aisha: Addressed both comments; added model_variant to emitted tags and refactored marshalling to reduce alloc.
Olivia: Approved after CI green and a successful e2e run on staging.
Observability: streaming endpoints now emit request_id, route_tag, and traceparent in structured logs
OpenAI shim: synthesizes request metadata headers for backward compatibility
Metrics: per-endpoint tags available for latency and token metrics enabling route-level dashboards

payload.body:
Title: Usage Insights: reconciliation suite vs billing totals + CI drift gate

Summary
We’ve had a few early beta reports that “console totals don’t match invoice” (see SUP-24811) and a recurring internal concern that aggregation lag + rounding will cause subtle drift. This PR adds a reconciliation suite that compares Usage Insights rollups (route/model aggregates) against billing totals (metering hooks → invoice preview) within a defined tolerance, and wires it into CI + a nightly scheduled run with alert hooks.

Key goals
- Catch drift early (instrumentation regressions, bucketing/alias issues, timezone boundary mistakes, rounding deltas).
- Define and document a tolerance policy that is strict enough to catch real issues but robust to expected effects (late events, FX rounding, minimum billable units).
- Provide a runbook-friendly output: workspace/project, day/hour, route/model slices that contribute most to drift.

What’s included
1) Reconciliation job + report format
- New job: services/telemetry/reconciliation/usage_insights_vs_billing
- Compares totals for a given workspace_id + time range across:
  - usage_insights.route_model_agg (the dataset powering console breakdown tables)
  - billing.usage_totals (billing hook rollups used for invoice preview)
- Outputs both:
  - a single “gate” metric per workspace/time window (pass/fail)
  - a ranked list of top contributing slices (route/model/region/deployment_mode where present)

2) Tolerance policy (documented + implemented)
We gate on both absolute and relative drift, and we avoid evaluating windows likely to be incomplete.
- Windows evaluated:
  - Hourly buckets for last 24 hours (excluding most recent 2 hours)
  - Daily buckets for last 7 days (excluding current day)
- Late-event buffer:
  - Ignore the most recent 2 hours entirely to avoid normal ingestion lag.
  - For daily checks, only evaluate days older than 26 hours.
- Tolerance thresholds:
  - Absolute drift allowed: max($2.00, 2000 tokens worth of cost at the workspace’s effective blended rate) per evaluated window
  - Relative drift allowed: <= 0.50% per evaluated window
  - Gate fails if BOTH absolute and relative drift exceed thresholds (prevents false positives on small totals)
- Currency handling:
  - Compare in USD using billing’s canonical conversion for the period.
  - Usage insights cost uses the same price book snapshot key as billing (price_book_version) to avoid rate drift.
- Rounding:
  - Compare on unrounded micros (int64) where available; rounding only applied in the human report.

Tolerance helper (illustrative snippet):

function isDriftAcceptable({ expectedMicros, actualMicros }) {
  const driftMicros = Math.abs(actualMicros - expectedMicros);
  const rel = expectedMicros === 0 ? (actualMicros === 0 ? 0 : 1) : driftMicros / expectedMicros;
  const absOk = driftMicros <= ABS_TOLERANCE_MICROS;
  const relOk = rel <= 0.005;
  return absOk || relOk; // fail only if BOTH are violated
}

3) CI + scheduled runs
- Adds a Buildkite step (non-blocking in PRs, blocking in main nightly):
  - PR builds: runs reconciliation unit tests + one small integration fixture
  - Nightly: runs full reconciliation across allowlisted beta workspaces with paging
- New pipeline: .buildkite/pipelines/usage-insights-reconciliation.yml
- Artifacts:
  - Uploads a CSV and JSON summary for each run
  - Posts a summary comment to #eng-platform on failures with a link to artifacts

4) Alert hooks + runbook pointers
- On gate failure, the nightly job:
  - Emits metric: usage_insights.reconciliation.drift_exceeded{workspace_id, window_type}
  - Logs structured payload with top slices and suspected causes
  - Posts to Slack: #usage-insights-alerts
  - Creates a lightweight incident event (non-page) unless drift persists 2 consecutive runs, then page the on-call (aligns with SRE feedback from earlier threads)

5) Guardrails to avoid noisy failures
- Workspace allowlist for beta reconciliation (config in services/telemetry/reconciliation/config/beta_allowlist.yml)
- Suppression for known exceptions:
  - If billing is missing a price_book_version for the period (rare), mark “skipped” not “failed”
  - If insights freshness lag > threshold (uses existing freshness metadata), mark “skipped”

Why this approach
- We compare at the same conceptual level as customers: “what billing says you owe” vs “what console says you spent”.
- We still include drill-down slices to make debugging actionable (route/model/region).
- Late-event handling is explicit and conservative; we don’t want to treat expected lag as correctness drift.

Files / areas changed (high level)
- services/telemetry/reconciliation/usage_insights_vs_billing/*
- services/telemetry/reconciliation/lib/tolerance.ts
- services/telemetry/reconciliation/lib/report.ts
- services/telemetry/reconciliation/config/beta_allowlist.yml
- .buildkite/pipelines/usage-insights-reconciliation.yml
- docs/internal/runbooks/usage-insights-reconciliation.md
- libs/billing/pricebook/resolve_pricebook_version.ts (small helper to align snapshots)

Test plan
- Unit tests:
  - tolerance calculations (edge cases: 0 totals, tiny totals, large totals)
  - rounding behavior (micros vs displayed dollars)
  - skip logic (freshness lag, missing pricebook)
- Integration tests:
  - fixture dataset with:
    - retries + fallbacks
    - model alias → version bucketing
    - streaming endpoints
  - verifies:
    - aggregation totals match billing totals within tolerance
    - top-slices ranking is stable/deterministic
- Manual:
  - Ran job for HelioChat staging workspace on 2026-02-16 (7d window) and validated output against invoice preview totals.

Rollout notes
- Nightly reconciliation initially scoped to beta allowlist only.
- If the nightly job is noisy, we can widen the late-event buffer or adjust absolute tolerance; prefer changing absolute tolerance first.
- No change to customer-visible console behavior.

Links
- Linear: ENG-3817
- Related PRs: pr-23114 (aggregation job), pr-23135 (query API)
- Support: SUP-24811

Reviewer notes / questions to focus on
- Tolerance policy: are we comfortable gating on “abs OR rel” instead of “abs AND rel”? (current implementation is intentionally forgiving on small totals)
- Skip windows: is 2 hours sufficient buffer for late events in all regions?
- Alerting: does the ‘2 consecutive runs before paging’ rule match SRE expectations?

---

Conversation (abridged)

Allison Grant (Observability) — 2026-02-11
“Please make sure this does not page on first failure. Also can you include a metric with a ‘skipped_reason’ label so dashboards can separate drift vs ‘data not ready’?”

Cole Summers — 2026-02-11
“Good call. Updated: first failure posts to #usage-insights-alerts + emits metrics; paging only after 2 consecutive failures. Added skipped_reason label to reconciliation outcome metric.”

Nadia Rahman — 2026-02-12
“Double-check retry accounting: billing counts retried requests as billed tokens; insights should too. Your fixture needs at least one retry case where the first attempt generated some tokens.”

Cole Summers — 2026-02-12
“Added fixture scenario: partial generation then retry; billing expected includes both attempts. Reconciliation now compares on metering_event_id aggregation rather than request_id when available to avoid undercounting.”

Logan Wright — 2026-02-13
“Perf: the nightly query looks like it’ll scan too much if we do 7 days across many workspaces. Can we do workspace-by-workspace, partition prune by day, and cap to allowlist?”

Cole Summers — 2026-02-13
“Adjusted: strictly allowlist, query per workspace, partition filter on event_day; added a hard cap of 200 workspaces. Also added a note in the pipeline config to expand gradually.”

Kevin Osei (Security) — 2026-02-14
“Make sure report artifacts don’t include customer prompts/content. I see route/model; ok. But please avoid including raw request IDs if they can be correlated.”

Cole Summers — 2026-02-14
“Removed request_id from exported artifacts; only includes hashed route_key + model_key + bucket timestamps + cost/tokens metrics.”

Chloe Martin — 2026-02-15
“The tolerance uses a blended rate estimate for the token-based absolute threshold. Can we just use a flat USD micros threshold and keep it simple?”

Cole Summers — 2026-02-15
“Switched to flat $2 absolute threshold for now (micros), plus relative 0.5%. Kept the blended-rate note in comments as possible follow-up.”

Dylan Brooks — 2026-02-17
“Looks good. Please add a short section to the internal runbook: common causes (missing route tags, model alias bucketing, timezone boundaries) and first debug steps.”

Cole Summers — 2026-02-17
“Added runbook section + links to dashboards for freshness and metering ingestion.”

Approvals
- Allison Grant — Approved (2026-02-17)
- Nadia Rahman — Approved (2026-02-18)
- Logan Wright — Approved (2026-02-18)
- Kevin Osei — Approved (2026-02-18)

CI
- buildkite/redwood:unit-tests ✅
- buildkite/redwood:lint ✅
- buildkite/redwood:telemetry-integration-fixtures ✅
- buildkite/redwood:usage-insights-reconciliation-smoke ✅

Merge
- Merged via squash on 2026-02-18
- Squash commit: “Usage Insights reconciliation vs billing totals (ENG-3817)”
