Motivation: customers running long-lived Dedicated fleets observed intermittent SLA blips during correlated tenant surges where competing reservation reconciliations and backfills interleaved, causing transient queue amplification and unfair burst consumption. This PR introduces a sequential commitment allocator coupled with a throttle-frontier mechanism and a windowed backfill delegator to provide deterministic per-tenant sequencing, bounded inter-tenant preemption, and safer opportunistic backfill. Summary of changes: 1) allocation/sequencer: introduce a lightweight sequencer that assigns monotonic commitment tokens per tenant request batch to preserve FIFO across reservation reconciliation cycles; tokens are compact 64-bit ids and allow fast in-memory range checks. 2) throttle-frontier: a frontier tracker per pool that exposes an upper commit watermark and a soft throttle signal; when frontier pressure breaches a tunable threshold we apply graded token-holdbacks instead of blunt rejection to preserve throughput while protecting tight SLA tenants. 3) windowed backfill delegator: replaces the previous eager backfill with short time-windowed delegations that prefer local warm pools and decay based on recent eviction churn; this reduces noisy preemption across pools. 4) telemetry & reporting: new per-tenant sequence-lag histogram, frontier-pressure gauge, and backfill-delegation counters; TTLs and tags added for export to observability. 5) rollout: feature gated under runtime flag "sequential-commitments-v1" and default-disabled for Dedicated customers; rollout plan includes canary on 2 dev clusters then staged ramp. Checklist: [x] unit tests for sequencer and frontier logic [x] e2e replay test against synthetic surge traces [x] perf benchmark (steady-state) shows <3% median latency overhead, 15% reduction in tail SLA breaches during burst tests [x] telemetry wired to Console dashboards [x] regression windows and rollback plan documented Design notes: sequencer is intentionally single-writer per-pool to avoid cross-pool coordination; we rely on epoched persistence for graceful restarts. Throttle-frontier uses leaky-bucket style smoothing with two configurable thresholds (warning/critical) and exposes a fast path that avoids allocation stalls for tenants below their committed watermark. Backfill delegator maintains a per-tenant backfill score that decays exponentially and factors in eviction rate to avoid oscillation. Rollback plan: gate off feature flag and revert a single reconciler switch; state is ephemeral so rollback is low-risk. Testing: synthetic surge harness, integration with autoscaler suite, and a dedicated dedicated-fleet-canary in perf-lab. Related: references ENG-2147 for the original incident and ENG-2301 for backlog prioritization. This description intentionally condensed design rationale and the PR includes inline comments for more detail.
Ethan Cole: This overall direction looks solid. Two concerns: sequencer single-writer per-pool could be a hot-spot under extreme control-plane churn; can we prove there's no contention hotspot?
Marina Lopez: We added a sequencer sharding knob and a benchmark that shows <1% CPU increase in worst-case per-pool hot path. Added comment in sequencer.go explaining our single-writer choice and how shard count can be increased at runtime.
Priya Natarajan: Telemetry looks good; please ensure tags include tenant_id, pool_id and commit_epoch for indexing. Also suggest an alert when frontier_pressure>0.9 for 2m.
Marina Lopez: Added tags and an alert proposal in docs/operational/deploy-ramp.md. Adjusted metric cardinality by sampling low-cardinality tenants in high-volume pools.
Samir Patel: Windowed backfill seems safer but I'd like to see how it interacts with the autoscaler reclaim loop; could backfill starvation cause wasted GPU time?
Marina Lopez: The delegator now exposes a backfill-priority floor that autoscaler consults; default floor is 10% which we tuned in perf runs. Documented interaction and added unit test for prioritizer coupling.
Adds a sequential commitment sequencer, throttle-frontier to reduce inter-tenant interference during surges, and a windowed backfill delegator which reduces eviction churn across warm pools. Opt-in via feature flag. Improves burst fairness and reduces tail SLA breaches in surge tests.
Perf lab results: synthetic 10x surge trace reduced 99th percentile token latency by ~18% for reserved tenants while opportunistic backfill throughput retained ~92% of previous levels. Canary rollout completed on 2 clusters without incidents. Flag default remains off for GA.

payload.body:
Add SSE sequence gating and reassembly timeouts to reduce partial-JSON emission and mitigate delimiter storms. Improves stream ordering guarantees during bursty networks and late-fragment arrivals. Backwards-compatible; opt-in config for strict gating.
Context: We continue to see production cases where high-frequency delimiter emissions (heartbeats, toolcall sentinels) combined with late/fragmented network packets produce partial JSON objects downstream and interleaved event tokens. This change introduces a small sequence-gating layer (seq-gate) and an explicit reassembly timeout to 1) detect and hold candidate fragments until sequence continuity is established, 2) avoid emitting delimiter-only bursts as separate events, and 3) surface deterministic late-arrival recovery rules to the OpenAI compatibility bridge. Motivation: reduce partial-JSON artifacts and make function-calling/structured-output boundaries resilient to packet reordering and bursty clients. What I changed: implemented an in-memory seq-gate that tracks per-connection event sequence IDs (lightweight uint32 wrap-aware) and rejects/queues fragments that fall outside a small window; added a reassembly timeout (default 150ms, configurable per-route) that flushes best-effort reconstructed spans with annotated diagnostics if continuity cannot be established; added a 'delimiter-velocity' filter that suppresses consecutive sentinel-only emissions when they are within a short interval and likely to be coalesced by the client. Also: tightened the SSE framing parser to annotate partial-json spans with a recovery hint so downstream OpenAI-compat layer can decide to buffer vs. surface. Backwards compatibility: default gating is permissive (windowed) so existing clients see unchanged ordering; strict gating can be enabled via route config for customers who require atomic span guarantees. Testing: unit tests for wrapping sequence arithmetic, simulated out-of-order fragments, and delimiter storm scenarios; integration test harness with local tcp-proxy that reorders chunks and delays segments; fuzz tests added for the framing parser. Performance: microbenchmarks show ~1.8% p99 CPU increase for extremely high-throughput connections, but average latency SLOs are intact thanks to short window sizing and early fast-path for in-order fragments. CI: all tests passed; added new flaky timeout mitigation for the integration harness. Checklist: - [x] seq-gate implementation and docs - [x] reassembly timeout and config surface - [x] unit/integration/fuzz tests - [x] docs and compatibility notes - [x] manual canary on staging (ran 24h) Rollout plan: shipped behind feature flag and route-level opt-in; enabled for a subset of hostnames in staging, monitored structured-output error rates and SSE repair logs for 48h, then rolled to canary cluster. Observability: new metrics sse.seqgate.held_fragments, sse.seqgate.released_fragments, sse.reassembly.timeouts and a new log tag sse_recovery_hint for correlated trace searches. Related: references ENG-4812 (streaming stability epic) and SUP-9134 (customer incident showing delimiter bursts). Risks and mitigations: strict gating can delay emission for fragmented clients; mitigated by conservative defaults and the annotated diagnostic on flush so users can detect gating-related behavior. Migration notes: OpenAI-compat bridge picks up the recovery_hint field and will buffer if it sees 'hold-until-seq' (already implemented in this PR). See docs/compat/sse.md for config knobs. Commits: listed below. Merge: squash, CI green, merged to main after approvals.
Marco Ruiz: Can we make the reassembly timeout configurable via per-route rather than global? I worry about customers in high-latency regions. Response: yes, exposed as route-level config with a sane default; added route/route_config.go and docs to show override.
Samantha Liu: The seq id wrap logic should be well-tested for off-by-one when uint32 wraps. Request: add explicit wrap tests. Response: added fuzz + unit tests that exercise wrap-around and confirm ordering invariants.
Dmitri Orlov: Observability is great; please add a sampled trace tag when a fragment is held to aid postmortems. Response: added sse_recovery_hint trace tag and increased sampling for held_fragments to 1% by default.
Marco Ruiz (approval): Behaviour seen in staging looks solid. Approve for squash merge.

Summary: Introduces a lightweight request-side compatibility proxy (Schema Retention Proxy) and a Stream Sanitizer adapter to improve stability for legacy clients during schema rollouts. Motivated by recent regressions when clients and server disagree on the response envelope (structured output vs. raw text) and by intermittent streaming deserialization errors from older SDKs. This PR provides a conservative, opt-in path (X-Redwood-Schema-Beta header) to enable server-side coercion and sanitization while preserving default backward compatibility for clients that do not opt in.

What changed: 1) schema-retention-proxy: runtime middleware that records client-declared preferences (schema-version, prefer-structured) and attaches a compact capability token to requests hitting the model-serving layer. The token allows downstream components to apply targeted coercion rules instead of global rewrites. 2) stream-sanitizer: an interceptor for streaming responses that normalizes control frames (tool call markers, chunked JSON fragments) and emits consistent chunk boundaries for older clients. 3) response-coercer: a small, deterministic mapper that converts structured tool-call envelopes to legacy tool-call proto when the client indicates prefer=legacy via header or capability token. 4) tests and integration harness updates for OpenAI-compat layer to exercise mixed-version client/server scenarios.

Motivation and rationale: During staged schema rollouts we observed two primary failure modes: a) older SDKs choke on interleaved structured-JSON fragments in a stream and b) clients that assume legacy tool-call envelopes received unexpected fields leading to deserialization exceptions. Our strategy is to avoid hard breakages by keeping the default path untouched and offering an opt-in beta header that signals a client is prepared to receive coerced responses and streaming frames. The proxy also enables telemetry on negotiation failures to guide future migrations.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc: ENG-4192 linked - [x] Unit tests for proxy and coercer - [x] Integration tests: legacy SDK streaming test matrix - [x] E2E perf smoke to ensure <5% p95 latency regression - [x] Docs: Console and SDK notes (beta header usage) - [x] Add rollout plan and feature flag gating for 2-week canary

Commits (high-level): - a1b2c3: add schema-retention-proxy middleware and capability token format - b2c3d4: implement stream-sanitizer interceptor and chunk normalizer - c3d4e5: add response-coercer for tool-call envelopes with unit tests - d4e5f6: integration tests for mixed-version clients + harness updates - e5f6a7: docs and changelog entries; add feature flag and canary config

Files changed (high-level): - runtime/middleware/schema_retention_proxy.go: new middleware and token encoding - runtime/streaming/stream_sanitizer.go: interceptor that normalizes stream frames and drops invalid fragments for non-opt-in clients - runtime/response/coercer.go: deterministic map from v2 structured-tool to v1 legacy envelope - sdk/openai_compat/fixtures/: test clients and recorded streams for matrix - docs/platform/schema_rollout.md: beta header docs and migration guidance - tests/integration/legacy_stream_matrix.test: new integration scenarios - ci/rollout-config.yaml: canary policy for feature flag

Review conversation (excerpted): - Sofia Martinez (reviewer): "Thanks, overall this looks like a safe approach. Can we make the capability token size bounded to avoid header bloat for high-FPS clients?" - Author (Jinwoo): "Token is a 12-byte base64 blob; added a test to ensure header length <150 bytes for worst-case metadata." - Ravi Shah: "Stream sanitizer looks good, but we should avoid dropping frames silently; add a metric and a debug log line so SREs can triage." - Author: "Added sanitized_frame_drop_total histogram and debug logging behind debug flag." - Maya Thompson: "Docs callout: emphasize that beta header is required for coercion; otherwise behavior is unchanged. Also include suggested SDK upgrade notes." - Author: "Updated docs and changelog per suggestion."

CI: Initial run (linux-unit, integration, lint) showed a flaky integration failure around streaming timeouts (integration/legacy_stream_matrix.test). Root cause was an undersized context timeout in the harness for legacy clients; increased timeout and retried CI. Reran full pipeline: all checks passed (linux-unit: pass, integration: pass, lint: pass, e2e-smoke: pass).

Telemetry and rollout: Feature gated behind runtime feature flag runtime.enable_schema_coercion (disabled by default). Beta header X-Redwood-Schema-Beta: true opt-in required to enable coercion and the stream sanitizer's aggressive fixes. We will enable the feature flag for 2% of requests in staging for one week, then 10% in prod for a canary cohort before wider rollout. Telemetry added: negotiation_failure_count, sanitized_frame_drop_total, schema_coercion_applied_count.

Backward compatibility notes: Default behavior for clients that do not set X-Redwood-Schema-Beta is unchanged. The proxy only records metadata and will not modify responses unless the token indicates an opt-in or the feature flag is enabled for the specific request. This minimizes risk while allowing safe testing.

Release notes (user-facing): Adds an opt-in beta header (X-Redwood-Schema-Beta) to enable structured output negotiation and server-side stream sanitization for SDKs that opt into the new schema. No action required for most customers. SDK maintainers: see docs for migration/test suites.

Merge: After two approvals (Sofia Martinez, Ravi Shah) and a successful CI rerun, the branch was squashed and merged to main (squash merge). Merge commit: d3f7a1c9.

Follow-ups: - ENG-4192.1: add SDK helpers to emit capability tokens automatically - ENG-4192.2: observability dashboard tile for negotiation failures - PM-1299: schedule customer announcement if canary metrics remain stable
Adds a runtime proxy that retains request schema preferences, a beta header for schema negotiation, and a stream sanitizer to stabilize legacy client streams. Backwards-compatible by default; opt-in beta required for schema coercion.

Context
We’re standardizing audit logging coverage for sensitive actions across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Routing policy changes (incl. fallback rules) are security-relevant because they can alter what models serve which requests, potentially impacting data handling boundaries and reliability controls.

This PR instruments the policy engine to emit schema v1 audit events for routing policy CRUD + publish operations, with:
- A bounded diff generator (before/after) to support investigations
- Cardinality guards to prevent high-cardinality payloads from polluting downstream SIEMs
- Consistent actor/target semantics + correlation IDs per the v1 standard

What’s included
- Audit events emitted for:
  - Routing policy create/update/delete
  - Fallback configuration update (primary/fallback model sets, failure-mode rules)
  - Allow/deny list changes for model routing
  - Policy publish/activate (when a draft becomes effective)
- New event types (registered):
  - policy.routing.created
  - policy.routing.updated
  - policy.routing.deleted
  - policy.routing.published
  - policy.fallback.updated
- Diff summary generation:
  - Produces a stable, bounded summary string + structured keys for a small allow-list of fields
  - Drops/obfuscates unbounded data (e.g., free-form match expressions) and emits a reason tag (diff_truncated=true, truncated_fields=[...])
  - For lists (e.g., model allow-lists), emits added/removed counts and a capped sample (max 10) of normalized IDs
- Cardinality checks:
  - Enforces allow-listing for attribute keys on the audit event extension payload (policy.* namespace)
  - Normalizes/caps values: strings max 256 chars, lists max 50 entries, emits *_count fields for full sizes
  - Rejects emission only for the extension payload (event still emitted with minimal required fields) and logs an internal metric audit_extension_dropped_total{reason=...}
- Correlation + attribution:
  - request_id + trace_id propagated from gateway -> policy service
  - actor derived from auth context (user/service principal); supports impersonation context when present
  - source_ip captured when available (gateway forwarded header), otherwise omitted (not synthesized)

Files / components touched (high level)
- services/policy-engine
  - routing_policy_service.go: emit events on write paths
  - diff/routing_policy_diff.go: allow-listed diff generation + truncation
  - audit/policy_audit_emitter.go: helper to build v1 events + extension validation
- libs/audit
  - event_types_registry.ts: register new event types + required fields
  - cardinality/guards.ts: namespace allow-list + value caps
- tests
  - unit tests for diff (order-insensitive list behavior, truncation, cap enforcement)
  - integration test for routing policy update emitting policy.routing.updated with expected fields

Example emitted event (sanitized)
- event_type: policy.routing.updated
- action: update
- actor_type: user
- actor_id: usr_01HT…
- resource_type: routing_policy
- resource_id: rp_7f3a…
- scope: tenant
- schema_version: 1.0
- extension.policy.diff_summary: "fallback_mode: 'region' -> 'model_variant'; allow_list_models: +2/-1 (sample: [mdl_llama3_70b_q4, mdl_llama3_70b_fp16])"
- extension.policy.diff_truncated: false

Design notes / trade-offs
- We intentionally avoid embedding raw match expressions or full JSON policy documents in audit logs (PII risk + cardinality). Instead we emit:
  - A bounded diff summary
  - Counts + small samples of normalized IDs
  - A pointer to the policy_id/version to fetch the full policy from the control plane if the investigator has authorization
- Event delivery is best-effort for this service (aligned with ADR in progress), but we emit metrics on failures and do not block policy writes on audit sink issues.

Testing
- go test ./services/policy-engine/... (new diff + emitter unit tests)
- Integration: TestRoutingPolicyUpdateEmitsAuditEvent (uses audit test sink)
- Lint: event_type registry enforcement (fails build on unregistered types)

Rollout
- Behind feature flag: AUDIT_V1_POLICY_ENGINE_EVENTS (default on in staging, can be enabled per-environment)
- Observability: new metrics
  - audit_events_emitted_total{event_type=...}
  - audit_events_failed_total{reason=...}
  - audit_extension_dropped_total{reason=...}

Links
- Linear: ENG-4838 (policy engine audit events)
- Related: SUP-18477 (customer reports inconsistent fields in SIEM exports)

Review notes
- Please focus on: diff allow-list correctness, cardinality caps, and whether the event types/fields match the taxonomy we’re converging on.

---
Conversation / review timeline
2026-01-29 (Allison Grant): "Diff logic looks good, but please ensure truncation is explicit to the consumer. Also the sample list must be deterministic (sort) to avoid noisy SIEM diffs." 
2026-01-29 (Jordan Lee): "Ack. Added diff_truncated + truncated_fields and made model ID sampling sorted after normalization. Updated tests for determinism."

2026-01-30 (Ethan Park): "We should include policy_version in the event so investigators can correlate which revision was applied. Also: do we emit for publish vs update?" 
2026-01-30 (Jordan Lee): "Added resource_version (policy_version) and a separate policy.routing.published event emitted only on activate. Update continues to fire for draft edits." 

2026-02-01 (Marcus Lin): "Cardinality guard behavior: do not drop the entire event if extension fails validation; keep minimal event and record a metric. Also check source_ip handling (don’t trust arbitrary headers)." 
2026-02-01 (Jordan Lee): "Implemented ‘extension drop’ path: event always emitted with required fields; extension omitted on validation error; metric increments with reason. source_ip now only populated from gateway-provided verified context (not raw header) with fallback to empty." 

2026-02-03 (Logan Wright): "Can we add a small integration test assertion for correlation IDs? We’ve had gaps in request_id propagation." 
2026-02-03 (Jordan Lee): "Added assertion for request_id + trace_id in integration test when the test harness includes a trace context." 

CI
- Initial run failed (2026-02-02): lint rejected unregistered event type policy.fallback.updated (registry update was in separate commit) 
- Rerun after registry fix: all checks green

Final approvals
- Allison Grant: Approved (2026-02-04)
- Ethan Park: Approved (2026-02-04)
- Marcus Lin: Approved (2026-02-04)

Merge
Squash merged to main on 2026-02-04. Flag enabled in staging; production rollout tracked in ENG-4838 checklist.
Emits canonical audit events when routing policies and fallback configurations are created/updated/deleted. Events include a bounded diff summary and are validated against cardinality + redaction rules before emission.

payload.body:
This PR introduces a longitudinal capacity timeline subsystem and a deferred resequencing adapter to improve commitment application stability for Dedicated fleets. Motivation: we've observed oscillation when many overlapping reservations and decommits are applied in rapid succession, leading to ineffective warmups and spiky tail latency. The timeline records commitment events (reserve/adjust/release) with logical ordering and a windowed reconciliation pass that smooths immediate application, enabling the autoscaler to make informed steady-state decisions. The resequencing adapter defers application of high-frequency reservation deltas for tenants flagged as 'churn-prone' and replays them in an idempotent, coalesced form during quiet windows so we avoid repeated warm pool churn. Changes include a new timeline controller (redwood/fleet/timeline_controller.go) with unit + integration tests, a small DB migration to add capacity_timeline_events and a compacted_offset pointer, telemetry hooks that emit tenant_weekly_commitment_quantiles and timeline_replay_duration_ms, an autoscaler hook that consults the timeline's smoothed commitment rate before firing up additional capacity, and a CLI tool to inspect recent timeline windows (bin/rwctl timeline tail). The PR also adds a safety backstop that forces immediate application if replay is delayed beyond a configurable threshold to preserve correctness in corner cases. Implementation notes: event schema is intentionally compact and oriented to append-only semantics, replay is idempotent and safe under retries, the DB migration is backward compatible and guarded by a feature flag fleet.timeline_v1 which defaults to off for gradual rollout. Testing: included a deterministic simulation harness to reproduce the previously observed oscillation and a test scenario demonstrating >35% reduction in warm-pool churn under synthetic multi-tenant bursts. Deployment plan: feature gated rollout to 10% of Dedicated fleets in Canary followed by 100% after 48 hours of telemetry validation. See linked XS support ticket SUP-2109 for a customer incident that motivated this work.
Evan: This looks promising. Two questions: 1) how does replay interact with concurrent manual decommits? 2) can we bound DB growth?
Priya: Answered inline. Replay checks event idempotency tokens and honors manual decommit flags; compacted_offset truncation meets retention policy and we added a daily compaction job. Also added explicit tests for manual decommit race.
Marco: Please add an integration test that runs with the feature flag off to ensure no regressions for fleets that don't enable timeline.
Priya: Added tests and updated migration to be a no-op when the flag is off. CI now runs the matrix with feature flag on/off.
Hannah: Telemetry naming looks good, but add an alert suggestion in docs for timeline_replay_duration_ms exceeding threshold.
Priya: Added alert guidance and a Grafana panel snippet in docs/observability/timeline.md
payload.title: Longitudinal Capacity Timeline and Deferred Resequencing Adapter

payload.body:
Motivation: during a recent surge in ephemeral tenant load we observed premature eviction of connections and aggressive KV cache drops in the regional slowpath which caused cascading latency spikes and a larger-than-expected SLO breach. Root cause analysis showed short-lived heartbeat jitter + transient control-plane lag incorrectly flagged connections as idle. This PR introduces two cooperating mitigations behind a feature flag: (1) idle-heartbeat-stitcher: emits/forwards short synthetic heartbeat pings for connections that are edge-idle but have recent inflight KV usage; the stitcher is conservative (probabilistic sampling + exponential backoff) to avoid increasing overall load; (2) soft-evict protector: an eviction gating layer that applies a temporal occupancy window and telemetry-aware hysteresis to prevent mass-evictions when node-level KV pressure or probe latency briefly spikes. Changes: - serving/kv_cache.go: protects kv metadata with a small lock-free fastpath and exposes last-active timestamps used by the stitcher - scheduler/evictor.go: new SoftEvictProtector that defers evictions for a short grace window when metrics indicate transient pressure - controlplane/flags.go: feature flag + rollout gating + canary percentage - telemetry/metrics.go: new metrics (evict_protector_decisions, heartbeat_stitched_count, stitcher_sample_rate) and labels for region/cohort - tests/evictor_test.go + integration/evictor_integration_test.go: simulate jittered heartbeats and transient probe delays - charts/helm/redwood-evictor-values.yaml: defaults for feature flag and canary rollout Rolling plan: feature-flag off by default; enable for 1% of production in us-west-2 for a 30-minute canary with enhanced tracing. If canary looks stable, scale to 10% then 50% and full rollout. Observability: dashboards added to watch the new metrics and KV retention percentiles. Backout plan: feature-flag off; immediate eviction policy rollback script included. This description intentionally compresses design rationale and rollout steps into a single narrative for the PR body.
Marco Diaz: Can you explain why we chose probabilistic stitching vs always-forwarding a heartbeat? Concern: potential extra load on already constrained nodes.
Priya Kaur (author): We sample so only a tiny fraction (configurable default 0.5%) get synthetic heartbeats; we biased sampling toward flows that show KV touch in the last 5s to target only hot-but-idle connections. I added a note in the code and a metric stitcher_sample_rate so SRE can tune live.
Evelyn Chen: There's a subtle race where last-active may be updated concurrently while stitcher is reading; please ensure lock-free fastpath can't observe partial state.
Priya Kaur: Fixed: added an atomic load of lastActive and added a small critical section around the KV meta update in the latest commit g7b9d1f. Also added evictor unit test to reproduce the race and guard it.
Samir Patel: Integration test failed on first CI run — eviction deferred longer than expected in one scenario, causing memory pressure in a stress test. Can we bound total deferred items per node and add a circuit to force-evict if buffers grow too large?
Priya Kaur: Added bounded queue with hard cap and a fallback forced-evict when cap is exceeded; metrics will emit forced_evict_count. Re-ran integration locally before pushing fix.
Marco Diaz: Approve after the forced-evict cap and a clear rollout plan are included.
Evelyn Chen: LGTM — please coordinate with SRE for canary window and set up dashboard alerts for stitcher_sample_rate and forced_evict_count.
Merge note: Squash-merged by CI bot once all checks passed and approvals met.
Merged (squash) into main. Notes: feature is behind feature-flag 'idle_heartbeat_stitcher' and rollout gated at 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Canary observability playbook linked in the PR comments. Backout steps: disable feature flag or run scripts/rollback/evictor_reset.sh.
Hotfix: prevent mass premature evictions caused by heartbeat jitter and control-plane lag. Adds idle-heartbeat-stitcher (probabilistic synthetic heartbeats) and soft-evict protector (telemetry-aware eviction gating). Feature behind feature flag; default off. Observability metrics added: evict_protector_decisions, heartbeat_stitched_count, forced_evict_count.
During canary enablement watch: - stitcher_sample_rate (should match configured percentage) - evict_protector_decisions{region} - forced_evict_count (should be zero) - node_kv_retention_percentile p50/p90. If forced_evict_count > 0 or memory climbs > 5% above baseline, revert flag immediately.
payload.title: Introduce idle-heartbeat-stitcher and soft-evict protector (hotfix)

payload.body:
Motivation: After INC-2026-007 we observed cascading tenant failures when short-lived regional congestion caused long-lived circuit states and immediate full failovers. This PR implements a timed SLO-aware shedder that applies conservative token-level shedding for tenants approaching soft-SLO violation windows, and only triggers regional failover after a configurable cooldown and a transparent de-escalation period. The implementation also emits an immutable audit trail of circuit transitions so ops can reconstruct decisions after the fact.

What this PR changes (high level):
- New component: timed_shedder (pkg/serving/shedder) — evaluates tenant SLO error/latency windows and issues token-shed directives that the router applies as a per-tenant rate cap.
- Failover gating: a cooldown timer + quorum check prevents an immediate region-wide failover; only after the cooldown and persistent SLO breach we mark routes sticky-failover.
- Transparent de-escalation: when pressure subsides we decay shed allowances over a configurable window so callers see progressive capacity restoration rather than abrupt jumps.
- Audit logging: auditlog.go captures immutable JSON events for: shed_start, shed_update, failover_initiated, failover_aborted, deescalation_start, deescalation_complete. Events include tenant_id, reason, metrics_snapshot, and operator_request if present.
- Telemetry: new metrics for shed_rate, shed_duration, failover_cooldown_hits and per-tenant shed counters; integrated into metrics_registry.
- Tests: added e2e chaos yaml + deterministic integration test to validate cooldown gating and de-escalation semantics.

Backwards compatibility and rollout:
- Feature gated under runtime flag --enable-timed-shedder (defaults to false in private deploy values.yaml). Hosted will enable behind a canary rollout (10% traffic on dedicated pool first).
- No changes to public API. Router honors shed directives as a soft token cap so clients see throttling responses (503 with Retry-After) when their shed allowance is exhausted.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc referenced in Linear (ENG-4021)
- [x] Unit tests for shedder decision logic
- [x] Integration test for cooldown->failover path
- [x] Audit event schema validated and included in schema docs
- [x] Metrics registered and dashboards updated (console PR forthcoming)
- [x] Rollout plan in PR description

Commits (summary):
- 1a4c3b4: initial timed_shedder implementation, core decision loop, state machine
- 2b7d8ef: auditlog plumbing + JSON schema + append-only file sink for private installs
- 3f1e0aa: router hook to consume shed directives and expose per-request decisions in logs
- 4c8a9d2: metrics + registry integration, added dashboard IDs in comments
- 5d2b7f0: e2e chaos test + deterministic integration test harness updates
- 6e3f9c1: helm values default (feature disabled for private), docs and README

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/serving/shedder/timed_shedder.go: new state machine (cooldown, active_shed, decay) with unit-tested thresholds.
- pkg/serving/shedder/auditlog.go: immutable event emitter, serializer and sink interface (FileSink and kafkaSink implementations).
- internal/telemetry/metrics_registry.go: register new metrics + add explainers.
- cmd/console/handlers/shed_events.go: lightweight HTTP handler to fetch recent shed audit events for operator troubleshooting (RBAC-protected).
- infra/k8s/chaos-tests/timed-shedder.yaml: reproducible failure pattern used in tests.
- deploy/helm/values.yaml: new flag enableTimedShedder: false for private; hosted takes custom values to enable canary.
- tests/e2e/shedder_integration_test.go: deterministic scenarios that assert cooldown gating and de-escalation smoothing.

Review conversation (abridged, continuous):
Ethan Rivera (reviewer) 2026-02-20: "This looks promising — two asks: 1) add a short-circuit to prevent shedding below X tokens for admin/health checks, and 2) ensure audit event size is bounded; we can't have unbounded payloads on spikes."
Ananya (author) 2026-02-21: "Added short-circuit in router for health/admin paths (pkg/router/filters.go) — I kept it minimal and documented in README. Audit payloads now include a sampled metrics_snapshot with a configurable histogram bucket limit and a hard cap at 8KB; events exceeding cap are truncated with a truncated=true flag."
Priya Desai (reviewer) 2026-02-23: "Please confirm the cooldown defaults and guardrails. Also add a small e2e asserting de-escalation curve monotonicity."
Ananya 2026-02-24: "Cooldown default is 30s with exponential backoff up to 5 minutes; documented in README. Added monotonicity test in shedder_integration_test.go."
Luca Moretti (approver) 2026-02-28: "Verified in local chaos runs and flagged no regression against existing eviction logic. Approving for canary; recommend telemetry tag to indicate 'experimental' until we complete 1-week canary."

Operational runbook excerpt (included in PR):
- Enabling: flip enableTimedShedder in values.yaml and set canaryTrafficPercent. Monitor shed_rate and failover_cooldown_hits for the first 15 minutes.
- Abort: set enableTimedShedder=false and post an operator action with abort reason. Use console handler /api/operator/shed-events to retrieve last 1k audit events.
- Rollback: Helm rollback will disable feature; ensure Kafka sink is drained before rollback to avoid duplicate audit lines.

Merge outcome: squash-merged to main on 2026-03-02 by Ananya Kapoor. Merge commit: 7b9f4c3b3891da2f6d8f3a5c1a2d44fe2b8c3e93.

Notes and follow-ups:
- Console PR to add shed event dashboard (SRE-1304) will follow; kept dashboard instrumentation tags in metric comments.
- Consider adding tenant-level TTLs for audit events in high-volume tenants to avoid storage blowup (future work).
- Monitor for false-positive failovers during bursty embed workloads; we've added a sampling-based probe to the test harness to mimic that pattern.
Add a timed, SLO-aware token shedder that performs controlled regional failovers after a configurable cooldown; includes an audit log for circuit state transitions and new telemetry for per-tenant shed events. Backwards-compatible; defaults off for private installs.

payload.body:
Motivation: We need an automated way to detect and explain drift between declared RBAC v2 policy state (policy templates + per-tenant bindings) and observed access patterns in production audit logs, together with a lightweight KMS consumption profile so security teams can identify anomalous key usage or cross-region access. This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) rbac-drift-detector: a service that periodically compares the desired policy graph against observed allow/deny events and surfaces candidate drifts with an evidence score; 2) kms-consumption-explainer: a small analyzer that aggregates per-CMK usage (calls, envelopes, wrapped keys) and maps usage to tenant claims and region tags to detect cross-region calls and sudden consumption spikes; 3) audit-fingerprint-indexer: a compact indexer that computes stable fingerprints for audit entries (normalized caller, resource, action, region, timing) to make drift correlation and de-duplication efficient.

What changed (high level): added a new service under services/rbac-observability with CLI for one-off scans and a server mode for scheduled runs; new proto and index schemas in infra/audit-index; a migration that backfills a 7-day audit fingerprint shard for initial scoring; RBAC lint rules extended with a "shadow-observability" annotation to mark policies excluded from drift alarms during staged rollouts; integration tests to validate score heuristics and KMS explainers against synthetic workloads; docs and runbook entries for SOC/Platform teams describing investigation flow and mitigations.

Checklist / rollout plan: - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] runbook draft in docs/runbooks/rbac-drift.md - [x] feature flag gated under feature.observability.rbac_drift (default off) - [x] migration to create audit_fingerprint_shards table (backfill limited to 7 days) - [x] staged rollout to internal infra then canary tenants then wide release - [x] notify SOC and SRE channels and add alert templates for high-confidence drifts

Operational notes: The detector computes an evidence_score (0-100) using weighted signals: unexpected-allow-events, failed-authentication-probes, KMS-region-mismatch, rate-of-change in bindings. The KMS explainer outputs a short human-friendly justification per anomalous key event (example: "CMK arn:... used by service-account:svc-ingest in region eu-west-1, tenant claim shows region=us-east-1 => possible cross-region routing via proxy-operator"). The fingerprint indexer normalizes audit payloads (removes ephemeral request IDs, normalizes caller ids, canonicalizes resource ARNs) and stores a 64-bit fingerprint which is used to group events quickly in the web UI and in the alert payloads.

Migration and data retention: The migration creates a rolling 7-day backfill by default to limit storage and risk; teams can request longer retention via support. The migration is reversible (drops index shards) if rollback triggered. Backfill runs are rate-limited and instrumented to avoid load spikes on the audit store.

Security considerations: The new services run in a restricted operator role with read-only audit-store permissions and explicit deny for key-decrypt operations. We added an operator-bound KMS wrapper to ensure the analyzer never exports raw key material; only metadata (key id, region, usage counters) are stored. All artifacts are covered by existing audit pipelines and the new audit_fingerprint_shards table is encrypted-at-rest and access-controlled via RBAC v2 templates.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on scoring heuristics in detect/heuristics.go and the query plan in infra/audit-index/queries.go for potential performance bottlenecks across large tenants. The CLI provides --simulate to generate synthetic drift scenarios; use it with the canary dataset in infra/testdata/canary-audit.json.

Related: builds on discussions in ENG-6723 and complements earlier residency checks; will be used by SOC playbooks alongside the residency-enforcer gate. If approved, ops will flip feature.observability.rbac_drift on for internal tenants on 2026-03-01 and start canarying tenants with high churn.
Diego Alvarez: The evidence_score composition looks reasonable but I'm concerned about the CPU profile when scanning high-churn tenants. Suggest sampling by tenant and incremental anchors.
Asha Patel: Added a tenant_sampling window and incremental anchor logic in heuristics.go; tests updated to cover sample path.
Rina Sato: Please double-check the KMS explainer does not accidentally log key ARNs in plaintext in debug mode.
Asha Patel: Confirmed; explainer logs only key IDs and region; added unit test to assert no full ARNs are emitted.
Chris Morgan: Integration test failed on first run due to missing migration permissions in CI; bumped migration role in test harness and re-ran. CI green now. Approving for merge.
Add: RBAC drift detector service, KMS consumption explainer, and audit fingerprint indexer. Feature is feature-flag gated (feature.observability.rbac_drift) and rolled out to internal tenants for canarying. Security: operator role is read-only and migration is rate-limited.
payload.title: Introduce RBAC drift detector, KMS consumption explainer, and audit fingerprint indexer

payload.body:
Context and motivation: Dedicated fleets have increasingly divergent short-term throughput needs (steady commits vs transient spikes). Existing soft-burst banks and hard reservations interact in complex ways and can leave pledged capacity unused when tenants idle or shift traffic. This PR adds a small control-plane component (Throughput Pledge Coordinator) plus a complementary runtime admission helper (Ambulant Burst Throttler) to reclaim idle pledges and redistribute them as soft burst credits with safety guarantees.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces Throughput Pledge Coordinator: watches per-tenant committed throughput (pledges) and surface liveliness probes to detect stale or underutilized pledges. It exposes a read-only status API used by autoscaler and router.
- Adds Ambulant Burst Throttler: a lightweight admission controller that temporarily assigns reclaimed pledge as soft-burst tokens to neighboring pools according to safety windows and a configurable dampening factor. It implements conservative fairness heuristics to avoid starvation.
- Telemetry and reporting: new utilization reporter emits percentiles (P50/P90/P99) of pledge utilization, an "idle_pledge_seconds" counter, and a "pledge_reclaim_events" histogram. Reports integrate to Console per-route dashboards.
- Autoscaler integration: coordinator provides a "live_pledge_margin" signal to the dedicated autoscaler so scale decisions account for reclaimable headroom and avoid unnecessary scale-ups.
- Tests, docs, and rollout: e2e scenarios and an ops runbook for canarying.

Design notes and safety:
- Soft safety: reclaimed capacity is always issued as ephemeral soft-burst tokens with TTL; the underlying pledge is not revoked without a separate admin action. This keeps contractual guarantees intact while improving utilization.
- Liveliness probes: multiple heuristics (RPC ping, recent-sequence-window, kv-check) are fused to reduce false positives; probe backoff is configurable.
- Dampening and fairness: Ambulant Throttler uses a dampening coefficient (default 0.6) and per-tenant fairness windows (configurable) to avoid oscillation.

Benchmarks and results:
- Controlled cluster perf test (100 pools, mixed workload): reclaimed-then-burst path increased average utilization of committed GPUs by 9.4% and reduced median token-per-request cost by ~7.1% vs baseline.
- Tail latency: 95th percentile token generation latency impact across mixed workloads was +1.6ms (within SLO).
- Fairness: Jain's fairness index improved from 0.82 to 0.97 for short-lived burst consumers during a 10-minute spike.

Commits summary: see `commits` field for succinct messages.

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/fleet/pledge_coordinator.go: main coordinator logic, state caching, probe fusion.
- controller/autoscaler/pledge_margin_adapter.go: signal adapter for autoscaler.
- controller/admission/ambulant_throttler.go: runtime admission logic with token TTL and dampening.
- telemetry/utilization_reporter.go: percentile and histogram emitter + Console integration hooks.
- helm/redwood-dedicated/templates/pledge-coordinator.yaml: k8s manifests + RBAC.
- docs/ops/pledge-coordinator.md: runbook, canary steps, config knobs.
- tests/e2e/pledge-rebalance.test.ts: deterministic scenarios for pledge expiry and redistribution.

Review and iteration:
- Initial implementation (by author) pushed: added coordinator and basic throttler. CI failures on e2e (timing flakes) tracked.
- Reviewer Daniel asked for an explicit backoff for live probes and a safety flag to opt-out tenants. Author added probe backoff and `pledge.reclaimable=false` annotation support.
- Priya requested observable counters for "reclaimed_vs_returned" to detect misallocations; added histogram and alertable metric.
- Ethan suggested adding an autoscaler circuit-breaker if pledge signal oscillates; implemented hysteresis in pledge_margin_adapter and added unit tests.

CI history:
- Nightly integration flagged a flaky e2e on first run (timing). Increased time windows in tests and added retries.
- All CI (unit + integration + lint) passed on the final run.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature gate `PLEDGE_COORDINATOR=true` and canary config via helm (10% of fleet pools, read-only leader election).
2) Monitor `idle_pledge_seconds` and `pledge_reclaim_rate` in Console for 48 hours.
3) Gradual ramp to 50% if no regressions; enable autoscaler signal consumer after 72 hours.
4) Full enable and deprecate legacy reclaim cron after 2 weeks.

Operational notes:
- Admin can annotate tenant namespaces with `pledge.reclaimable=false` to opt out.
- Emergency rollback: set `PLEDGE_COORDINATOR=false` or scale down the coordinator Deployment.

Release notes: PLEDGE_COORDINATOR is an opt-in capability for Dedicated fleets to improve utilization by safely reclaiming idle committed throughput and redistributing it as ephemeral soft-burst credits. See docs/ops/pledge-coordinator.md for runbook.
Daniel Ortiz: request change - add exponential backoff to liveliness probes and a tenant opt-out annotation
Asha Mehta: addressed - added probe backoff and `pledge.reclaimable=false` annotation; updated tests
Priya Raman: request change - expose reclaimed_vs_returned counters for alerting
Asha Mehta: addressed - added histogram metric and alert recipe in docs
Ethan Clark: comment - autoscaler should ignore pledge noise; suggest hysteresis
Asha Mehta: implemented hysteresis in pledge_margin_adapter and added unit tests; added note to runbook
Priya Raman: approved after metrics and docs updated
Daniel Ortiz: approved after e2e timing fixes
Opt-in throughput pledge coordinator: reclaims idle committed throughput and exposes ephemeral soft-burst tokens. Includes new telemetry: idle_pledge_seconds, pledge_reclaim_events, reclaimed_vs_returned_histogram. Default behavior is safe (TTL tokens, tenant opt-out).

Context: customers with mixed bursty and steady workloads need better automated tuning of batching/caching defaults and quantization fallbacks without manual intervention. This PR introduces a feedback-driven autotune workflow that reads runtime econ signals (latency p95, token cost, cache hit ratio, failover count) and proposes adjusted tenant defaults; it also ships a lightweight reconciler that applies safe changes (non-breaking, rate-limited) to batch/cache/quant profiles. Summary of what changed: added econ-feedback service that consumes telemetry from Console/Runtime, a reconciliation controller in the admin plane, small runtime scoring hook to tag requests with candidate signals, and a CLI dry-run mode for operators to simulate applying profile deltas. Checklist: [x] backend service and API contract defined, [x] reconciler implemented with safety caps and cooldowns, [x] runtime scoring hook (non-blocking) added, [x] unit economics heuristics and gating rules included, [x] CLI dry-run and apply paths implemented, [x] e2e smoke test harness, [x] docs PR stub and changelog entry. Motivation: prior autotune attempts applied aggressive profile changes that sometimes regressed tail latency; this design favors conservative, telemetry-driven proposals with explicit operator or automated gating based on evaluation windows and synthetic checks. Risk and mitigations: potential for oscillation mitigated by exponential backoff and minimum-stability window; quantization rollouts are only applied to canary lanes first and will auto-revert if quality degradation is detected. How to validate: run `devctl econ simulate --tenant <id> --window 1h --dry-run` to preview suggestions; see Console -> Tenant Defaults for suggested diffs. Deployment notes: feature flagged behind `econ_autotune_v1`; reconciler disabled by default for on-prem installs. Related: builds on earlier telemetry/metrics work (ENG-3981) and ties into incident playbook SUP-1081 for rollback.

Adds a telemetry-driven autotune workflow that generates conservative suggestions for batching, caching, and quantization defaults. Includes a safe reconciler, CLI dry-run, and canary-first rollout mechanics. Feature-flagged. Admin docs included.

Motivation: we observe recurring short-lived oscillations in Dedicated fleet scaling where bursts followed by rapid drains produce noisy utilization signals. Existing percentile-based samplers underweight cumulative idle capacity and therefore trigger unnecessary scale-ups that later compete with corrections, increasing churn and tail latency. This PR adds a lightweight probing/telemetry component that measures cumulative available capacity across configurable windows and an anticipatory smoothing layer in the autoscaler that uses that signal to dampen reactive scale-ups.
This PR implements two coordinated features as a single user-facing capability (feature-flag gated): 1) cumulative-utilization-prober: a periodic probe that aggregates per-pool occupancy and idle-slot duration into a single timeseries (redwood.fleet.cum_idle_seconds and redwood.fleet.cum_utilization_ratio) reported at 10s and 2m rollups; it also computes an outlier-resistant decay-adjusted headroom estimate (redwood.fleet.decayed_headroom_est) for downstream decisioning. 2) anticipatory-scale-smoother: an autoscaler stage that ingests decayed_headroom_est and applies a predictive damping coefficient to scale decisions — effectively increasing the confidence threshold for scale-up actions when cumulative headroom suggests transient drain. The smoother operates as a multiplicative governor applied after the baseline scale decision and before any commitment/reservation steps. Rationale: the cumulative probe captures multi-second/multi-minute persistence of excess capacity which percentile samplers may miss, and the smoother prevents rapid oscillation between scaling states while preserving the ability to satisfy sustained demand.
- [x] Add cumulative probe logic and efficient aggregator
- [x] Expose metrics to Prometheus and internal telemetry bus
- [x] Implement decay algorithm and headroom estimator
- [x] Add anticipatory smoother hook in autoscaler pipeline
- [x] Unit tests for probe aggregator, decay math, and smoothing gating
- [x] Integration test with local sim harness and warm-pool emulation
- [x] Add control-plane feature flag and operator docs
- [x] Dashboard and alert runbook entries
3 commits: (1) cumulative-prober: core aggregator and metric plumbing; (2) anticipatory-smoother: autoscaler governor and configuration; (3) tests/docs: unit/integration tests, dashboard templates, and rollout notes.

Unit coverage: +18%. Integration tests simulate burst->drain patterns with and without smoother; result: 32% reduction in churned scale events in sim and 8-12% reduction in 95th token latency in controlled perf lab runs.
Feature is behind 'anticipatory_smoother' flag. Default off for 2 weeks in prod. Canary rollout plan: enable on 5% of Dedicated pools in us-west1 for 48h, monitor redwood.fleet.cum_utilization_ratio and tail L95 latency, then expand to 25% then 100% if stable. If cumulative_headroom drops unexpectedly or tail latency regresses >5% relative, rollback by toggling the flag. Operator docs updated with flag and tuning knobs: probe_window_seconds, decay_half_life_seconds, damping_min, damping_max.
Added dashboard 'Fleet Cumulative Headroom' and two alerts: 1) Alert if decayed_headroom_est < -0.1 for 5m across >10% of pools (possible sustained underprovisioning), 2) Alert if smoothing_coefficient frequently toggles above 0.95 causing suppressed scale-ups. Both alerts include runbook steps to flip feature flag and inspect sim logs.

No breaking API changes; autoscaler config adds optional fields with sane defaults. Backwards compatible with existing reservation and burst token systems. Smoother only modifies the in-memory decision pipeline and is reversible via the feature flag.
Added a telemetry-driven autoscaler smoother to reduce oscillatory scale events by considering cumulative idle capacity across short and medium windows; feature is opt-in behind a feature flag and will be canaried.

Motivation: Bring Redwood's /v1/chat.completions adapter closer to OpenAI parity while improving real-world stability for streaming and function/tool calling. This PR consolidates several interrelated fixes: 1) resilient parameter coercion and normalization for v1 inputs (temperature, top_p, stop as mixed types, role aliases), 2) move per-token logprob payloads into a stable envelope to avoid interleaving with delta tokens, 3) add an explicit functioncall handshake frame and deterministic tool-call framing for mixed streaming and non-streaming flows, 4) implement stream jitter mitigation and backpressure heuristics to reduce visible client-side reflow and duplicate partial tokens. Summary of changes: input layer: added a coercion/validation pass that accepts numeric strings for temperature/top_p, truncates extreme values to safe ranges, accepts stop as string or array or array-of-mixed, and emits canonical stop arrays; role normalization: map common role aliases and enforce precedence rules (system > user > assistant) to avoid prompt inversion bugs; streaming: introduce HEARTBEAT frames and a pacing layer that enforces a token inter-arrival smoothing algorithm (configurable via environment flag REDWOOD_STREAM_PACE_MS) and a high-water/low-water backpressure window to avoid buffering storms on slow clients; logprobs: decouple logprob data into a sibling envelope field "logprob_delta" that is only emitted when present to avoid JSON parse ambiguity in streaming clients; functioncall/tooling: introduce a 2-step handshake (FUNCTIONCALL_OFFER -> FUNCTIONCALL_ACK) when the adapter intends to forward tool calls to a downstream tool runner; tool outputs are wrapped in assistant.tools array with explicit metadata (tool_name, status, raw_output) so client SDKs can reliably detect structured tool results; compatibility: add heuristics for common OpenAI v1 mis-use (e.g., stop: null, temperature: "0.0") and emit deprecation warnings in the response metadata instead of hard errors where safe. Testing & stability: added deterministic unit tests for role/stop normalization, integration tests that exercise streamed functioncall sequences with intermittent connection loss, and a stress test for the pacing/backpressure logic. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag (compat_v1_relaxed_coercion=true) with a canary on 10% of hosted traffic for 48h, full rollout contingent on no regressions in CANARY_STREAM_LATENCY and no increase in token duplication errors. Checklist: - [x] implement param coercion and role normalization - [x] implement logprob envelope and streaming-safe framing - [x] add functioncall handshake and tool output envelope - [x] add pacing/backpressure module and feature flag - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] update adapter docs and changelog - [x] run canary and monitor metrics Backwards compatibility notes: default behavior preserves existing semantics unless the compat flag is enabled. Some edge-case clients relying on interleaved logprob deltas will need to opt-in to parsing the new envelope. Monitoring & observability: emit new metrics: stream.pacing.delays, stream.backpressure.trips, adapter.v1.coercion_warnings, functioncall.handshakes.total, functioncall.handshakes.failed. Security: no changes to auth surface. Performance: pacing slightly increases median tail by configurable ms but reduces duplication and re-transmit work overall. See release notes below for suggested migration steps.
Compatibility: Add optional relaxed v1 coercion to accept common OpenAI parameter shapes and role aliases. Streaming: introduce heartbeat frames and pacing/backpressure to mitigate jitter and duplicate tokens. Function calling: new 2-step handshake and explicit tool output envelope for deterministic downstream execution. Note: clients relying on interleaved logprob deltas must update to parse the new logprob envelope when the compat flag is enabled.
Ethan Zhao: Left a note about making the pacing window size configurable per-route; let's avoid global defaults for large tenants.
Maya Patel: Can we ensure the functioncall handshake tolerates idempotent replays? Add a request-id for dedupe.
Sofia Ruiz: Integration tests flaked on CI initially due to timer sensitivity; reworked tests to use fake clock. Approving after that change.

Background: Production customers observe short burst windows (10s-2m) that cause transient SLO violations and noisy paging. Motivation: reduce alert churn by surfacing predicted burst windows on dashboards and tagging incidents with a burst severity score so runbooks can use tuned mitigations. This PR implements a windowed burst SLO forecaster (sliding-window short- and medium-horizon predictors), a per-tenant burst severity metric, dashboard annotations for predicted windows, and an incident annotator that attaches burst context to PagerDuty/Slack alerts. The design is lightweight: forecasts are computed from rolling token-rate and latency histograms, score is normalized per-tenant using recent baseline percentiles, and predictions are emitted as sampled events to the tracing pipeline for enrichment. Changes include: 1) runtime: new metrics emission path for burst_score and burst_prediction events; 2) observability: Grafana panels and annotation overlay for predicted window ranges; 3) alerting: a library to attach burst context to outgoing incident webhooks; 4) ops: a Playbook document and a toggle (feature flag) to opt-out per-tenant. Rollout plan: feature-flagged on staging for 48h, canary to 5% tenants for 72h, full rollout after quality gates. Testing: unit tests for forecasting logic, integration test that injects synthetic bursts and verifies annotated events in traces, lightweight load runbook verifying no additional tail latency. See commit list and changed files for details.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: This PR implements a new attention microkernel ('ortho-fuse') that orthogonally fuses QK computation with rotary index transforms and introduces a small prefetch coordinator inside the serving scheduler to warm the KV cache and steer continuous batching. Motivation: long sequence workloads (4k-16k) were suffering from KV warmup stalls and Q-K/rotary roundtrip overheads that prevented the existing Flash variants from fully leveraging kernel-level data locality. The ortho-fuse design packs rotary index remapping into the same GPU tile as QK matmul when sequence windows permit, enabling a single pass over activation buffers and fewer global memory reads.

What changed (high-level): 1) New CUDA microkernel 'ortho_fuse_kernel.cu' with fused QK + rotary remap + softmax-shared workspace path. 2) Kernel registry and heuristic selector to choose ortho-fuse for window-aligned requests; falls back to flash/standard kernels for misaligned widths. 3) Prefetch coordinator in serving scheduler that pre-warms KV caches for active sessions and implements a lightweight KV 'peek' to populate hot lanes before model execution. 4) KV cache manager additions to support epoch-based warming and safe concurrent evictions with minimal locking. 5) Continuous batching adjustments: soft-enqueue policy tweak to avoid head-of-line blocking when prefetch is in-flight. 6) Tests, docs, and benchmarks.

Commits (summary): - Add ortho-fuse kernel implementation and unit integration (commit: 'kernel: add ortho-fuse fused qk+rotary path') - Add heuristic selector for ortho-fuse based on seq_len/window alignment ('runtime: ortho-fuse selector') - Scheduler: prefetch coordinator and KV peek API ('serving: introduce prefetch coordinator & kv peek') - KV: epoch warming and concurrent eviction fixes ('kv: safe warming and eviction') - Continuous batching tweaks and tests ('scheduler: soft-enqueue tweak to reduce HL blocking') - Benchmarks and perf doc ('bench: ortho-fuse perf notebook', 'docs: ortho-fuse performance notes')

Files changed (representative): runtimes/cuda/ortho_fuse_kernel.cu, runtimes/cuda/ortho_fuse_kernel.cuh, runtimes/cuda/kernel_registry.py, serving/scheduler/prefetch_coordinator.py, serving/kv/cache_manager.py, serving/kv/kv_peek.h, serving/scheduler/continuous_batcher.py, benchmarks/attn/ortho_fuse_bench.ipynb, tests/attn/test_ortho_fuse.py, docs/perf/ortho-fuse.md, tools/perf/compare_runs.sh, ci/perf-run.yaml, examples/ortho-fuse/README.md, CHANGELOG.md

Benchmarks: Microbenchmarks on p4d.24xlarge with fp16 models: - 8k seq, batch 1: throughput +18% tokens/sec, p50 latency -12% - 4k seq, batch 2: throughput +22%, p50 latency -14% - 16k seq streaming (sliding windows): throughput +25% with ortho-fuse windowing vs baseline flash-attn+separate-rotary. Memory: small increase (~4%) in peak scratch due to fused workspace allocation but net token-cost reduction. Real workload A (multi-turn retrieval): end-to-end latency 10% lower and 17% cost-per-token improvement by reducing KV re-reads.

Compatibility and fallback: The runtime selects ortho-fuse only when window alignment and headroom checks pass. Otherwise we fall back to the existing Flash kernels. We also expose a config flag 'enable_ortho_fuse' under runtime.experimental to allow staged rollouts. No changes to public API surface.

Testing and CI: Unit tests added for correctness vs baseline softmax outputs and rotary-aligned indices. Integration tests validate KV peek semantics under concurrent warmup/eviction. CI status: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, lint: pass, perf-run: initially flaky (missing perf artifact on first run) -> rerun and pass. Perf regression gateway shows improvements; no regressions.

Discussion and review notes: - Anil Kapoor: requested tighter bounds on numeric deviation vs baseline; asked to include differential test across sequence lengths. Response: added randomized numeric-diff test with tolerance 1e-3 and summary table in tests/attn/test_ortho_fuse.py. - Sofia Martinez: asked to ensure prefetch respects tenant isolation and does not leak KV slices. Response: prefetch coordinator uses session-scoped peeks and never exposes raw KV contents, and we added an audit log event for prefetch triggers. - Ethan Cole: suggested making the selector more conservative for small batches; implemented heuristic to require min_batch_tokens >= 512 before enabling ortho-fuse. - Performance engineering (review thread): suggested reducing shared workspace allocation; we added an allocation pool per-stream and reclaimed between calls.

Known limitations: - Ortho-fuse benefits are most pronounced when sequence windows align to kernel tile widths; pathological misaligned patterns will fall back to baseline and see no change. - Small-batch workloads under 512 tokens may see neutral or marginally worse latency due to additional prefetch coordination overhead if misapplied; selector prevents this.

Rollout plan: merged to main behind runtime.experimental flag. Post-merge: staged canary rollout to Dedicated clusters, monitor p50/p95 and KV miss rates. Ramp to hosted API only after 2 weeks of canary telemetry and no perf regressions.

Merge details: PR merged by Marina Alvarez on 2026-03-05 via squash. Linear: ENG-1489 closed. Release notes: add ortho-fuse kernel to perf improvements list.

If follow-ups are needed: - Fine-tune selector thresholds per-model family (TODO: ENG-1591) - Investigate lowering scratch allocation further for memory-constrained GPUs (follow-up perf PR).
Adds 'ortho-fuse' fused attention kernel optimized for windowed rotary indexing and a prefetch coordinator that warms KV cache and improves continuous batching. Expect ~15-25% throughput improvements on long-sequence workloads and reduced P50 latency. No public API changes.

Background: Investigations into high-cost invocations frequently require operators to stitch together multiple spans that contribute to token billing. This PR introduces deterministic "cost_phase" span tags written at token emission boundaries and a configurable priority-reranker in the ingestion path so high-impact spans are surfaced in compact traces and dashboards. What: 1) Runtime emits telemetry.cost_phase = prebill|billable|postbill for kernel, batching, kv, io spans when a token emission boundary or billing checkpoint occurs. 2) A priority-reranker computes a lightweight cost impact score (tokens_emitted * token_weight + kernel_ms * kernel_weight + kv_miss * kv_weight + wait_ms * wait_weight) and reorders the compact trace digest and the UI summary. 3) New observability assets: Cost Phasing overview dashboard (heatmap: prebill -> billable delta, per-route slope panel) and an alert rule "Per-route billable-slope" that uses the slope of billable tokens with a configurable window and backoff to reduce alert churn. Engineering notes: implementation in src/serving/telemetry/cost_phasing.go and telemetry/ingest/priority_ranker.go; feature gated by TELEMETRY_PRIORITY_RERANK (off by default). Tests include unit coverage for tag emission and score calc, an integration replaybench validating top-3 span recall in compact traces, and a canary against beta tenants. Rollout: gated default-off; staged to internal, then opt-in beta tenants; documented migration behavior (missing tags fall back to default ordering). Related work: ENG-2833 PM-1101; incident SUP-4502 raised need for better span surfacing.
Emily Zhang: Can we keep the number of tagged spans bounded to avoid explosion for high-fanout traces? (author reply: runtime now only tags spans that either cross a token emission or have tokens_emitted>0; micro-spans under threshold are ignored)
Rajiv Menon: Please add a runtime config to tune score weights per-tenant. (author reply: added per-tenant score_override via telemetry config; default weights documented)
Luis Ortega: The alert cooldown needs to honor existing oncall dedupe windows. (author reply: alert rule includes configurable cooldown and ties into existing dedupe policy; test added to replaybench)
Added: cost_phase span tags (prebill, billable, postbill) and a priority-reranker to surface cost-impact spans; Dashboard: Cost Phasing overview with heatmap and per-route slope; Alert: Per-route billable-slope with configurable window and cooldown. Opt-in via TELEMETRY_PRIORITY_RERANK feature flag.

payload.body:
Motivation: We currently see alert churn for bursty invocation patterns where many similar invocations repeatedly trigger the same SLO alerts within a short window. Root cause analysis shows many such alerts are transient and dominated by the same invocation fingerprints (hot prompts). This PR implements two complementary pieces: 1) a lightweight per-invocation ticker that emits stage-aligned heartbeat metrics so we can understand phase durations without full trace hydration, and 2) an alert decay controller that dampens alert signal for repeated fingerprints over a configurable decay window.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces a new metric set: redwood.invocation.ticker.duration_ms (histogram), redwood.invocation.ticker.stage (gauge labels: start/kernels/kv/cache/emit), redwood.invocation.ticker.status (counter: started/completed/failed).
- Adds redwood.alert.decay_score (gauge) and redwood.alert.decay_events_total which power the decay controller logic.
- Implements a pluggable AlertDecayController that subscribes to fingerprint counts from the agg layer and applies a decay multiplier to alert weights exposed to the alerting pipeline. The controller runs per-tenant and honors TTL and minimum floor thresholds.
- Adds a lightweight in-process ticker generator in the serving runtime. The generator emits minimal payloads (stage, elapsed_ms, invocation_fingerprint) to the metrics relay; it is turned off by default and can be enabled per-tenant via runtime config.
- Adds an observability dashboard (Invocation Ticker Stream & Alert Decay) with a live stream panel, fingerprint heatmap, and decay effectiveness view.
- Adds unit and integration tests for decay scoring and the ticker's stage transitions.

Why this approach:
- Full trace enrichment is expensive; a ticker gives a low-cardinality, cheap signal aligned to stages (prefix warmup, kernel queue, generation, post-processing) that is actionable for SRE and product.
- Decaying alert weight instead of hard-suppressing alerts preserves fidelity (we still record incidents) but lowers alert noise so oncall can focus on novel or persistent regressions.

Implementation notes: (single continuous description) The AlertDecayController maintains an LRU-backed fingerprint ledger with time-decayed scores. When an alert candidate arrives it is annotated with a decay_multiplier in [0.1,1.0] based on recent fingerprint activity; the alert router multiplies signal weight by this multiplier and only escalates if weighted score passes thresholds. Decay parameters are configurable via the existing observability configstore and default to a 10-minute half-life with a minimum floor of 0.25. The ticker is implemented as a non-blocking ring buffer inside the request worker; emission is batched to the metrics relay via the telemetry client. To limit cardinality we only publish the 64-bit fingerprint hash (not raw prompt) and expose a tenant-level sample rate.

Checklist:
- [x] Metric names and docs added (telemetry/metrics.md)
- [x] Runtime opt-in flag and tenant config
- [x] Alert router integration and decay multiplier plumbing
- [x] Dashboard JSON and runbook snippets
- [x] Unit tests for decay math and ticker state machine
- [x] Integration test that verifies reduced alert fires under simulated burst

Testing performed:
- Local unit tests: tick-state transitions and decay math (100% coverage for new modules)
- Integration: stressbench harness that simulates 10k invocations/min with 30% fingerprint reuse; alert fires dropped by ~78% while detection latency for persisted regressions remained < 2% worse.
- E2E in staging: enabled ticker for a single tenant for 48h; verified telemetry pipeline ingestion throughput increased by <2% and no regression in token-latency SLOs.

Operational concerns & fallbacks:
- The ticker is disabled by default in production; enablement is per-tenant. If telemetry relay backpressure occurs the emission is automatically sampled down and metric emissions are dropped with a counter.
- The decay controller logs a provenance event for any alert it attenuates so runbooks can identify suppressed incidents.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge and deploy server-side with ticker disabled. 2) Enable ticker+decay for internal QA tenants and run 48-hour validation (observability/qa). 3) Gradual ramp to high-traffic tenants with monitoring on redwood.alert.decay_effectiveness and redwood.alert.suppressed_total.

Docs & runbook: Added runbook section that explains when to tune half-life and floor, and how to disable decay per-alert.
Added invocation-ticker metrics, an alert decay controller to reduce alert noise for rapidly recurring invocation fingerprints, and a new dashboard panel for live ticker streams. No user-facing API changes.
--- a/observability/alert/router.go
+++ b/observability/alert/router.go
@@ -42,6 +42,14 @@ func RouteAlert(ctx context.Context, a Alert) error {
-   weight := a.Severity
+   // apply decay multiplier from controller
+   multiplier := decayController.GetMultiplier(ctx, a.InvocationFingerprint)
+   weight := float64(a.Severity) * multiplier
+   // record provenance
+   if multiplier < 1.0 {
+       provenanceLogger.Info(ctx, "alert attenuated", "fingerprint", a.InvocationFingerprint, "multiplier", multiplier)
+   }

    if weight < alertingThreshold {
        return nil
    }
Aisha: Could we make the decay controller realtime-configurable?
Maya: Yes — wired into configstore, can toggle per-tenant.
Jonas: Concerned about cardinality; can we avoid shipping raw fingerprint?
Maya: We only emit 64-bit hash; added sampling config to limit relay pressure.
Liam: Add provenance event for attenuated alerts so PagerDuty playbooks can find suppressed incidents.
Maya: Done — added provenanceLogger and runbook entry.

payload.body:
Motivation: noisy alert fatigue from long-running conversational sessions and duplicated context logs has obscured real regressions. This PR introduces two coordinated features: a lightweight Invocation Context Harmonizer that consolidates related traces/metrics into a single canonical invocation record, and an Alert Suppressor (noise-gate) that reduces alert churn by suppressing low-confidence SLO breaches that are attributable to expected context-reassembly behavior.

What this changes (high level):
- Harmonizer: canonicalizes invocation identifiers when requests are part of the same user session (heuristics: session cookie, model version, and contiguous timestamp bounds). It stitches partial KV-cache-prefetch traces and merges duplicate span edges so dashboards show a single invocation timeline instead of fragmented microtraces.
- Suppressor: adds an alert-preprocess step that tags potential context-reassembly incidents and applies an adaptive suppression window. Suppressed alerts are still recorded for offline analysis and surfaced in a new "suppressed_alerts" dashboard panel.

Implementation notes:
- New components live in telemetry/service: ContextHarmonizer (go) and AlertGate (go). A small shim in the tracing collector (collector/harmonizer_shim.go) enriches spans with harmonizer_id.
- Harmonizer emits two new metrics: telemetry.harmonizer.stitch_count and telemetry.harmonizer.stitch_latency_ms. Both exported with per-tenant labels and invocation_cohort.
- AlertGate implements a tunable policy table (yaml) stored in config/observability/alert_gate.yaml with defaults that favor short suppression windows for paid tiers.
- Backwards compatible: if the collector shim is disabled, the Harmonizer becomes a no-op and all existing metrics/traces flow unchanged.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests for shim and harmonizer heuristics
- [x] End-to-end replay with synthetic sessions (replaybench)
- [x] Integration in console: new suppressed_alerts panel + harmonizer sparkline
- [x] Feature flag gated (operator flag: enable_context_harmonizer)

Commits summary: 
- "add ContextHarmonizer core + unit tests"
- "tracing shim: enrich spans with harmonizer_id"
- "implement AlertGate with default policy and integration tests"
- "console: add suppressed_alerts panel and harmonizer sparkline"
- "docs: observability/guide update and runbook notes"

Files changed (high level):
- telemetry/service/context_harmonizer.go
- telemetry/service/alert_gate.go
- collector/harmonizer_shim.go
