payload.body:
Motivation: Heterogeneous sequence-length workloads create a tail-latency / padding tradeoff. Existing bucketing reduces padding but can increase scheduling overhead and miss kernel-fitting opportunities for hardware-aligned tile sizes. This PR introduces two complementary runtime heuristics: a latency-prioritized padding slicer and a KV-prefetch cohorter. Goals: reduce p99 generation latency for mixed-length traffic, lower average padding tokens (unit cost), and improve kernel utilization for common GPU tile sizes without changing public APIs.

Summary of changes: the padding slicer dynamically partitions incoming requests into cohorts using a stride-aware alignment strategy. Requests are mapped into alignment buckets based on sequence-length modulus against kernel-friendly stride sizes (configurable per-device). For cohorts where padding overhead dominates latency (many short sequences batched with a few long ones), the slicer opportunistically slices long sequences into aligned sub-requests for scheduling purposes only; semantics are preserved because slicing is local to the batch composition stage and recomposition happens before token emission. The KV-prefetch cohorter detects likely shared-prefix patterns (common in few-shot or template-driven workloads) and issues a low-cost asynchronous prefill of KV cache for cohorts to avoid repeated expensive prefill during the critical tail window. The runtime selects kernels per-cohort using a lightweight cost model that considers sequence-length distribution, expected padding, and kernel tile fit.

Benchmarks: microbenchmarks on an A100 cluster with mixed workloads (10k samples: 70% short <64, 20% mid 64-512, 10% long >512) show: median token latency ~3% improvement, p95 ~9% improvement, p99 ~15% improvement, and end-to-end padding token reduction ~10% in aggregate when feature flag enabled. Perf harness and scripts included for reproducibility (benchmarks/ci).

Compatibility and safety: feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.padding_slicer.enabled and runtime.kv_prefetch.enabled. Default off for Dedicated customers until validated in canary. Slicing is disabled for requests that declare stateful generation semantics (chat streams with user-turn continuity) — we detect via request metadata. KV-prefetch respects KMS/HSM isolation (no secrets exfiltration) and uses existing cache TTL controls.

Testing and validation: added unit tests for alignment logic and TTL semantics, integration tests that exercise continuous batcher end-to-end, and a perf harness. Canary run executed in internal cluster; telemetry dashboards added (docs/ops/patch_notes) with new metrics: padding_savings_rate, kv_prefill_hits, cohort_miss_ratio.

Migration & operator notes: operators can tune stride sizes per-device and set maximum per-request slice count (default 3) to bound recomposition work. See docs/ops/patch_notes/latency_padding_slicer.md for runbook. No API surface changes.

Risk and rollback: initial canary flagged an off-by-one alignment that could increase padding for a narrow range of lengths (fixed in a follow-up commit). We added a kill-switch in the console to disable the feature per-cluster.

Related work: ENG-8912 (padding cost modeling), ENG-9034 (KV cache improvements).

Detailed patches: listed below in files_changed. This description contains the rationale, implementation summary, tests, and rollout guidance.

Add latency-prioritized padding slicer and KV-prefetch cohorter with runtime flags, benchmarks, tests and docs. Improves tail latency and reduces padding waste for mixed-length workloads.
Introduce latency-prioritized padding slicer and KV-prefetch cohorter to reduce p99 tail latency and padding waste for heterogeneous sequence-length workloads. Feature behind runtime flag. No API changes.
Maya Chen: Can you quantify extra CPU overhead from slicing/recomposition? Author: measured <3% CPU increase on batcher process in our canary and added a knob to bound slice attempts.
Diego Alvarez: Ensure semantics-safe—how do we handle stateful chat? Author: slicing is skipped when request metadata indicates stateful generation; added test coverage.
Priya Patel: Please add perf reproducibility steps and compare to existing bucketer. Author: added benchmarks and comparison script; included results in PR description and docs.
Maya Chen (follow-up): Found off-by-one with stride 64 on inputs of length 128-191. Author: fixed alignment math and added regression tests (commit m3n4o5).
payload.title: Latency-prioritized padding slicer with KV-prefetch cohorter

payload.body:
Context: production workloads have exhibited sustained tail-latency amplification and higher than expected memory fragmentation in tenant KV caches when sequence length distributions vary dramatically between tenants. This PR introduces a two-part runtime change: (1) a lightweight region-hinting allocator that biases placement to minimize cross-region fragmentation and create eviction-friendly hot islands; (2) a stochastic region-prioritized evictor combined with a burst spill scheduler that coordinates async spillouts to external tiering when memory pressure spikes.

Motivation: previous evictors treated pages uniformly which worsened fragmentation for mixed-tenancy traffic. During bursty workloads the existing spill path serialized many pages and caused head-of-line stalls. The new approach reduces fragmentation score by consolidating same-lifecycle pages and schedules spill I/O in bounded bursts to avoid saturating PCIe/remote storage and blocking the fast path.

Design summary: region-hinting allocator adds a compact metadata hint on allocation (4 bytes) indicating "lifecycle class" and tenant affinity. Allocator attempts same-region placement using a fast path that prefers recently free buckets. The stochastic evictor periodically samples resident segments and scores them using a combination of residency age, fragmentation density, and hint-match score; eviction candidates are selected with weighted sampling to retain high hint-coherence. The burst spill scheduler introduces backpressure windows and token-bucket limits for async spill jobs; it groups pages by destination shard and issues coalesced write batches to reduce per-request latency.

Key behavior changes: - Reduced cross-tenant interleaving of hot/cold pages. - Evictions favor segments that free contiguous ranges to reduce fragmentation. - Spillouts are rate-limited during sustained pressure, preventing I/O from affecting generating latency. - Fallthrough behavior: when spill queue is saturated, the evictor will favor compress-on-evict (local quantized serialization) before remote spill.

Checklist: - [x] unit tests for allocator alignment and hint propagation - [x] integration test for eviction scoring under mixed workload - [x] stress benchmark showing fragmentation metric improvement - [x] CI build + linters - [x] docs: operator tuning guide

Rollout/Compatibility: feature gate KV_REGION_HINTS (off by default). Default config keeps previous eviction strategy unless enabled. Docs include recommended tuning knobs for burst_spill_tokens (default 16), spill_group_size (default 32 pages), and sampling_rate (default 0.02).

Impact: bench runs (see bench/kv/fragmentation_test.py) show a 28-44% reduction in fragmentation score on mixed short/long sequence replay and 12% lower 99p tail latency in synthetic tenant-switch workloads. Expected small uptick in memory metadata (~0.3% per-cache) due to hint bytes.

Notes: this is intended to be an iterative improvement; follow-ups will add adaptive learning of lifecycle classes from telemetry and an optional defragmenter pass during low-load windows.
Arjun Patel: Can you explain why we prefer stochastic sampling vs deterministic LRU scanning? Deterministic scans helped explainability for SRE. 
Leah Moroz: Stochastic sampling keeps CPU overhead bounded (we limit to sampling_rate * resident_pages) and empirically provides similar candidate quality. We also emit per-eviction rationale metrics for post-hoc analysis to satisfy SRE needs.
Sofia Nguyen: I see possible race on allocator free-list during concurrent compaction - please add a guard or annotate. 
Leah Moroz: Added a compare-and-swap guarded fast-path and a fallback locked path; included microbench numbers (allocator fast-path hit rate ~92% under load).
Marcus Li: CI had a transient failure on macOS builder for the bench harness. Re-run? 
CI bot: Re-run succeeded (all checks green).
Arjun Patel: Approve after docs update and a short operator guide for burst_spill_tokens. 
Sofia Nguyen: Approved. 
Merge Bot: Merged by squash on main (commit e8b4a5c).
Introduce experimental KV_REGION_HINTS allocator and stochastic evictor + burst spill scheduler. Reduces fragmentation and 99p tail in mixed-tenancy workloads. Feature is gated (off by default); operator tuning documented in docs/kv-ops.md.
payload.title: KV region-hinted allocator + stochastic evictor with burst spill scheduler

payload.body:
Context: During Dedicated autoscaling bounds + predictive mode pilot, on-call and CS have needed a fast way to answer: (1) what is the *effective* scaling policy for a deployment (after defaults + feature flags), (2) what has the autoscaler been deciding recently (requested desired vs bounded desired + reason), and (3) are we frequently hitting min/max bounds. This PR adds an internal-only admin CLI command to dump that info without spelunking multiple dashboards/log streams.

What’s in this PR: - New `rw-admin` subcommand: `rw-admin scaling policy debug` - Outputs:   - Effective scaling policy (raw config + evaluated defaults + feature-flag overrides)   - Last N scaling decisions (timestamp, requested_desired, bounded_desired, clamp_reason, signals summary)   - Bound-hit history summary (last 1h/6h/24h counters + max-bound saturation ratio) - Supports `--format=table|json` (json is intended for copy/paste into incident docs / support tickets) - Supports `--deployment-id` (required) and optional `--region` (defaults to deployment’s primary region) - Supports `--since` (e.g. `2h`, `24h`) and `--limit` for decisions - Adds guardrails: admin-only auth token required; redacts customer name by default; no prompt contents or request IDs printed.

Implementation notes: - CLI is Go (cobra) under `cmd/rw-admin` (internal toolchain already used by SRE). - Uses capacity-policy-service internal endpoints added in prior work:   - `GET /internal/v1/deployments/{deployment_id}/scaling/effective-policy`   - `GET /internal/v1/deployments/{deployment_id}/scaling/decisions?limit=...` - Bound-hit history is fetched via metrics-proxy (Prometheus query) to avoid direct access to Prometheus from laptops. The query uses low-cardinality labels (deployment_id, region) consistent with observability standards.

Example output (table):

$ rw-admin scaling policy debug --deployment-id dep_7f3a2 --since 6h
Effective policy:
  enabled: true
  min_replicas: 6
  max_replicas: 24
  cooldown_up: 60s
  cooldown_down: 180s
  predictive_mode: enabled (fallback=reactive)
  clamp: hard (min/max enforced)

Recent decisions (last 10):
  2025-08-13T00:41:12Z requested=18 bounded=18 reason=none signals=qdepth_high
  2025-08-13T00:39:12Z requested=26 bounded=24 reason=max_bound signals=predicted_ramp
  2025-08-13T00:37:12Z requested=26 bounded=24 reason=max_bound signals=predicted_ramp

Bounds summary (since 6h):
  max_bound_hit_count: 42
  min_bound_hit_count: 0
  max_bound_saturation_ratio: 0.18

Example output (json):

$ rw-admin scaling policy debug --deployment-id dep_7f3a2 --since 24h --format json | jq
{
  "deployment_id": "dep_7f3a2",
  "region": "us-east-1",
  "effective_policy": { ... },
  "recent_decisions": [ ... ],
  "bound_hit_summary": { ... }
}

Testing: - Unit tests for command parsing and response rendering - Golden tests for `--format=table` output stability - Smoke test for metrics-proxy query construction (no live Prometheus dependency)

Rollout/usage: - Internal-only binary; no customer-facing surface - Intended for SRE + Dedicated on-call + CS escalations (pairs with runbook section “Confirm effective policy + bound hits”).

Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Add `rw-admin scaling policy validate` to preflight proposed min/max bounds against current fleet availability by region (tracked separately).
Ethan Park (review): Can we confirm these endpoints are strictly internal and require admin auth? Also please ensure the CLI doesn’t print customer names by default (compliance). Jordan Lee (author): Yep — using the same admin token flow as other rw-admin commands; added `redactCustomerName()` with an explicit `--include-customer` flag (off by default).

Vanessa Ortiz (review): For “recent decisions”, can you include both requested_desired and bounded_desired plus the clamp reason. That’s the most useful part when diagnosing max bound saturation vs predictor overshoot. Jordan Lee: Added `requested_desired`, `bounded_desired`, and `clamp_reason` columns plus a compact signals string.

Allison Grant (review): Prometheus query should not use customer_id label (cardinality). Please query by deployment_id + region only. Jordan Lee: Updated metrics-proxy queries to use deployment_id + region; removed optional customer label entirely.

Rafael Mendes (review): Please add a short note to the Dedicated on-call docs with a copy/paste command; also make sure error messages are actionable when the metrics-proxy is unreachable. Jordan Lee: Added docs snippet in `docs/internal/oncall/rw-admin.md` and improved errors to suggest `--format json` and to check VPN/SSO.

Felix Schneider (review): JSON output should be stable (field names) since we paste into incident timelines. Also prefer RFC3339 timestamps. Jordan Lee: All timestamps are RFC3339 and JSON fields are fixed; added a small golden test for json keys order stability (via canonical encoder).

Outcome: Approved by all reviewers; merged squash.
Internal tooling only: new `rw-admin scaling policy debug` command to dump effective scaling policy, recent autoscaler decisions, and bound-hit history for a Dedicated deployment.
payload.title: Add internal admin CLI for scaling policy debug (effective policy + decisions + bound-hit history)

Motivation: Teams need a low-friction way to understand the near-term cost impact of prefill/warmup strategies and to generate conservative batching/quant suggestions before applying changes to production. This PR introduces a lightweight CLI (rwi prefill-inspect) plus a telemetry adapter that converts sampled prefill traces into tenant-level 'horizon' cost projections and candidate default profiles.

What this does: - Adds a CLI that can run against stored telemetry or live sampling (+ dry-run) to compute: 1) projected token cost across a configurable horizon window (days), 2) recommended micro-batch shapes and cache retention defaults, 3) conservative quantization candidates with estimated quality impact bounds. - Produces an exportable JSON report and a compact human-readable summary. - Introduces a telemetry adapter to normalize sampled prefill traces into the inspector's canonical format (tenant, route, sample_distribution, kv_hit_rate, seq_len_histogram). - Includes 'safe-mode' that enforces guardrails (max-q-drop, latency-slo-preserve) and a preview flag --apply-suggestions=false for manual adoption.

Checklist: - [x] CLI binary and help docs - [x] Telemetry adapter + mapping tests - [x] Unit tests for cost projection math - [x] Integration test against synthetic workload - [x] Docs page and quickstart example - [x] CI linting and build

Commits (high level): - a1b3f87: initial CLI skeleton, arg parsing and subcommand plumbing - 3c9d2e4: implement horizon projection (tokenize, unit-econ model, decay window) - 7f2a11b: telemetry adapter and mapping layer for sampled prefill traces - 5e4b99c: safe-mode guardrails and quant suggestion heuristics - b8d0f22: docs, examples, and tests - 9f7c55d: fixes from review (privacy opt-out for telemetry sampling)

Files touched (high level): - cmd/rwi-prefill-inspect/main.go (new CLI entrypoint) - internal/prefill/inspector.go (projection engine) - internal/prefill/quant_suggester.go (conservative quant heuristics) - pkg/telemetry/adapter.go (sample -> canonical format) - docs/cli/prefill-inspector.md - deployment/telemetry/otel-mapping.yaml - tests/integration/prefill_inspector_test.go - Makefile, CI pipeline hook to run integration test in sandbox

Review thread summary: - Marcus: "Nice compact design. Please add explicit unit tests around the decay math edge cases (zero-prefill, spike bursts). Also add a flag to cap assumed token price for simulations (some tenants use custom pricing)." -> implemented in 3c9d2e4 and tests added in b8d0f22.

- Lena: "Telemetry mapping looks good; two privacy asks: (1) make the adapter default to aggregated histograms not raw prompts; (2) add an opt-out env var for private installs." -> Added aggregation and PRIVACY_OPT_OUT env handling in 9f7c55d. Lena approved after CI passed.

- Tomás: "Behavioral concern: quant suggestions should never be suggested for routes with latency SLO violations. Add a sentinel to skip those routes." -> Added safe-mode check and explicit skip with logging in 5e4b99c. Tomás provided an approval after integration test updated.

CI and QA: - First CI run failed lint (gofmt) and one flaky integration test (timing). Author fixed formatting and stabilized integration test by replacing wall-clock sleeps with controlled fake clock. Re-ran CI; all checks passed (unit, lint, integration sandbox). CI status summarized in the checks section below.

Checks summary: - golangci-lint: pass - unit-tests: pass - integration-sandbox: pass (rerun after flake) - docs-checker: pass - smoke: pass

Operational notes and rollout: - The CLI is shipped as an opt-in dev tool. For Hosted customers we plan a small internal runbook that recommends "run inspector with --horizon-days=7 --sample-rate=0.05 --apply-suggestions=false" before applying any defaults. - For Dedicated/Private installs the telemetry adapter is disabled by default; enable via deployment flag and set PRIVACY_OPT_OUT to true to avoid sending histograms to Redwood telemetry. - Suggestions are conservative: quantization recommendations are always accompanied by an estimated quality impact band and an automatic fallback to the previous model variant.

Backward compatibility and safety: - No API surface changes. No breaking changes. - The CLI reads telemetry snapshots only and does not mutate serving configs unless invoked explicitly with --apply-suggestions. - All suggestions require a confirmation file when used in automated pipelines.

Follow-ups: - Add a web UI tab in Console to visualize inspector reports (ENG-2190). - Hook inspector suggestions to the defaults-as-code workflow (later PR). - Expand quant suggestion heuristics with a small eval pipeline to estimate quality delta in a lightweight manner.

Merge: squash merged by Lena Ortiz on 2025-04-02 after approvals from Marcus Chen and Tomás Rivera.

Notes for reviewers digging into code: - Start at internal/prefill/inspector.go to see the projection pipeline: sample normalization -> unit econ estimator -> horizon decay -> recommendation generator. - Quant suggestion uses a conservative LUT based on model family and current token-sequence statistics; see internal/prefill/quant_suggester.go. - Telemetry adapter contains mapping logic and aggregation heuristics; mapping config is in deployment/telemetry/otel-mapping.yaml.

If you want to run locally: go build ./cmd/rwi-prefill-inspect && ./rwi-prefill-inspect --tenant tenant_123 --horizon-days 14 --sample-rate 0.02 --dry-run --output report.json

End of PR description.
Adds a new CLI tool (rwi prefill-inspect) that computes tenant-level prefill horizon cost projections, suggests safe batching and quantization profiles, and ships a telemetry adapter for unit-econ snapshots. Backwards-compatible; disabled by default in private installs.
payload.title: introduce-prefill-horizon-cost-inspector-cli-and-telemetry-adapter

payload.body:
Add chain-aware span grouping for streamed responses and a lightweight stream-cost adapter to approximate per-token cost on partial/chunked responses. Improves trace readability and enables token-cost breakdowns for long streaming sessions.
Motivation: Streaming responses and multi-turn chains produce lots of small spans and partial tokens, which makes trace graphs noisy and costs hard to attribute. Customers running chat-heavy workloads asked for clearer trace grouping and approximate per-token costing for streamed chunks so ops can debug and attribute spend without having to rehydrate full sessions. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) a chain-aware span grouper in the tracing pipeline that coalesces consecutive spans belonging to the same logical chain/session into a single rollup span with aggregated metrics and deterministic keys; and 2) a Stream Cost Adapter that consumes chunked/partial token events and emits ephemeral cost-attribution metrics with conservative heuristics (prefix-fractioning + model-profile weights) so dashboards can show near-real-time token-costs for streaming responses. Checklist: - [x] Implement span grouper and config flags - [x] Add stream-cost adapter with pluggable model weight table - [x] Expose metrics: stream_tokens_total, stream_token_cost_estimate, chain_span_length, chain_span_error_rate - [x] Wire OTEL span attributes for chain_id, chain_role, chunk_index - [x] Add unit and integration tests for grouping heuristics - [x] Console dashboard: chain stream-cost view + example alert rules - [x] Backfill migration script: noop safe default - [x] Docs: observability streaming guide Summary of changes: Commits: - a9f3b9c: initial implementation of chain-aware span grouper (core logic + unit tests) - b4d1e2f: add stream cost adapter, model weight table, and conservative heuristics - c2d4a88: metrics export hooks and Prometheus labels for chain_id/model - d9f7b1a: add console dashboard JSON and alert example - e1b7f04: tests and CI fixes + docs updates Files changed (high level): - tracing/span_grouper.py: core grouping algorithm and deterministic key derivation - tracing/tests/test_span_grouper.py: unit tests that exercise boundary conditions - observability/stream_cost_adapter.py: adapter that converts partial chunk events into token-cost estimates - metrics/exporters/prometheus_chain_exporter.py: export hooks with chain labels - console/dashboards/chain_stream_cost.json: dashboard definition + example widgets - docs/observability/streaming-traces.md: how it works, tuning knobs, and migration notes - infra/ci/test_observability.sh: new test harness for integration run - examples/streaming/README.md: quickstart and expected traces Review/Conversation: - Diego Alvarez (reviewer): "Nice approach. Two requests: (1) make the group key stable across retries so we can join traces in storage, (2) add a note about accuracy bounds for the stream cost heuristic." - Author (Maya): "Added deterministic nonce derivation so group keys are stable when upstream request_id is present; otherwise we derive from session fingerprint. Also added a short accuracy section to docs listing our conservative +/-10–25% bound depending on model/quantization." - Priya Nandakumar (reviewer): "CI caught a flaky integration test on bursty streams — tracing pipeline was dropping some chunks under high concurrency." - Author (Maya): "Fixed: increased internal buffer window and added backpressure metrics. Re-ran integration; green locally." - Samir Patel (final approver): "Approach looks sound; leaving a couple of nit comments on logging verbosity." CI Summary: - unit tests: pass - lint: pass - integration (observability suite): initial run failed (trace_buffer_overflow flaky) -> buffer window increased and test retried -> pass - e2e smoke: pass Note on accuracy and safety: The Stream Cost Adapter is intentionally conservative: it attributes fractional token counts for partial chunks and multiplies by model-weight factors from the model profile table. We label these metrics with attribute cost_estimate=approximate and provide a confidence tag (high/medium/low) so alerting can ignore low-confidence metrics. Default behavior is opt-in via observability.enable_stream_cost_adapter=false to avoid surprising billing spikes for customers who rely on exact billing. Configuration and tuning: - observability.span_grouper.enabled (bool, default true) - observability.span_grouper.max_merge_window_ms (int, default 300) - observability.stream_cost_adapter.enabled (bool, default false) - observability.stream_cost_adapter.model_weight_table (config map) - observability.stream_cost_adapter.confidence_threshold (float, default 0.6) Backwards compatibility and migration: - Grouping is additive at the tracing ingest layer; original fine-grained spans are still stored for 7 days controlled by observability.span_grouper.keep_fine_spans_days (default 7) so users can revert. - Stream cost adapter metrics are namespaced with stream_ prefix and do not feed billing pipelines unless an explicit opt-in flag is set. Rollout plan: - Canary on a small subset of hosted region (10% of streaming traffic) for 48 hours - Monitor chain_span_length, stream_token_cost_estimate, trace_error_rate - If no regressions (latency or spike in metric cardinality) after 48h, increase to 50% and run full canary window - GA after two successful canaries and customer docs updated Observability dashboards and alerts added: - New dashboard: "Chain Stream Cost (Canary)" with per-model cost estimates and chain latency histograms - New alert: "StreamCost: high-unattributed-variance" (fires when estimate variance > 40% for 10m) - New alert: "TraceGrouping: buffer-saturation" (fires on buffer occupancy > 85%) Known limitations and follow-ups: - Edge cases where upstream partial retransmits can double-count chunks; follow-up ticket ENG-3310 to add idempotency tags - Model-profile table is conservative and needs periodic calibration; follow-up ENG-3312 to add automated calibration job - Large cardinality risk: chain_id labels increase high-cardinality metrics; we implemented a capped cardinality rollup and will monitor; follow-up ENG-3313 to add reservoir sampling for low-traffic chains Merge: Squash-merged to main after reviewers approved and CI green. Notes: small telemetry spike observed during canary but within expectations. Docs, tests and dashboard JSONs included so console team can iterate.

Motivation: Our presubmit lanes have accumulated bespoke lint/test configuration fragments across services and SDKs (node/python/go). This PR consolidates those into a small set of extensible 'checker-profiles' that encode sets of linters, shims and environment knobs, and additionally introduces an automated deprecation mapper that surfaces and labels transitive dependencies flagged for deprecation during CI. Finally, the presubmit runner now supports a devcontainer-aware quickpath so contributors on devcontainers get a fast local-equivalent feedback lane.

What this changes (single-string summary): Consolidate per-repo lint/test configs into profiles; add a binary 'deprecation-mapper' that parses lockfiles and advisory feeds to emit a deprecation score per dependency; wire deprecation metadata into PR annotations and the presubmit dashboard; introduce a devcontainer-aware presubmit lane that uses lightweight warmed caches and skips heavy integration shards when run locally; refactor existing composite actions to be profile-driven; add telemetry hooks (counter gauges) to measure presubmit latency and dep-staleness over time.

Checklist: - [x] Define stable checker-profile schema and backward-compatible shim layer - [x] Implement auto-deprecation-mapper and adapters for yarn/pnpm/pip/poetry - [x] Integrate mapper output into PR annotations and console UI - [x] Add devcontainer quickpath and cache-warm hook - [x] Update CI templates to accept profile param and enable opt-in quickpath - [x] Add unit + integration tests for new actions - [x] Run staging CI across representative monorepo subsets

Commits (high-level): - initial: introduce checker-profile schema, docs and sample profiles - action: refactor composite actions to accept profile input and env overrides - tool: add cmd/deprecation-mapper with parsing and advisory adapters - infra: devcontainer quickpath runner + cache-warm script - tests: add unit tests for mapper and e2e smoke for profile routing - docs: presubmit migration guide and migration script

Files changed (high level): - .github/actions/checker-profiles/* (new) - .github/workflows/presubmit.yml (updated to route by profile) - tools/deprecation-mapper/* (new CLI + adapters) - infra/devcontainer/quickpath-runner.sh (new) - docs/ci/checker-profiles.md (new migration guide) - sdk/python/.lint.yml, sdk/ts/.lint.yml, services/*/.presubmit (removed duplicates) - tests/ci/e2e/presubmit-profiles (new smoke harness)

Impact and risk: The change reduces duplication and should lower CI latency for local runs. Risk areas: the mapper may initially surface many deprecation warnings (noise) and some services rely on bespoke linter flags removed by the profiles. To mitigate we ship a compatibility shim and an opt-in flag to keep legacy behavior until teams migrate.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main with feature flag off for global presubmit. 2) Enable profile-driven presubmit for a small set of repos (sdk/python, redwood-docs) and collect telemetry for two weeks. 3) Gradually flip on default profile on a per-team basis, using the compatibility shim where needed. 4) After 4 weeks of telemetry with low noise, enable PR annotations for deprecation warnings by default.

Release notes: Consolidates per-repo lint/test config into shared 'checker-profiles', introduces an automated dependency deprecation mapper with PR annotations, and adds a devcontainer-aware quickpath to speed contributor feedback. Teams should read docs/ci/checker-profiles.md for migration steps.

Problem: each SDK implemented auth refresh, streaming iterators and telemetry tagging slightly differently which caused subtle disconnects in token handoff and inconsistent backoff behavior. This PR centralizes an "auth-proxy" shim pattern, introduces a small stream-iterator adapter for ergonomic async/iter consumers, and coordinates minor version bumps across Python/TS/Go SDK packages.

What this PR delivers (summary): single-line auth proxy (opt-in) for managed token wrapping, unified retry/backoff hints surfaced to application layer, a StreamIteratorAdapter that exposes a consistent async pull API across SDKs, lightweight telemetry tag propagation for session/stream spans, and package.json/go.mod/pyproject.toml updates for v1.11.x bumps.

Why now: customer incidents highlighted a race during token rotation under sustained streaming load; SDK teams agreed on a minimal stable surface that avoids breaking consumers while improving parity.

Compatibility and migration: auth-proxy is opt-in. Existing users are unaffected until they switch to the new constructor arg (credential_proxy=True / CredentialProxy()). StreamIteratorAdapter is additive; older iterator APIs remain. Releases include short migration notes for each SDK in their changelogs.

Checklist:

Motivation: During a recent regional instability incident we observed aggressive immediate load-shedding decisions that amplified transient probe failures and caused a cascade of tenant degradations. Root cause analysis showed the control-path probe we used for SLO enforcement was tied to the same request path and therefore observed correlated failures during short KV-drain windows and API spikes. This PR introduces an out-of-band (OOB) healthwatch probe and a short-lived deferred-shed state machine to prevent premature circuit flips. In concrete terms this change: 1) Adds an independent healthwatch goroutine that performs lightweight control-plane probes (small RPCs to local runtime control endpoints) and publishes a high-resolution OOB health metric. 2) Implements a deferred_shed decision layer that requires sustained OOB unhealthy state for a configurable window (default 30s) before promoting an aggressive shed action. 3) Exposes a runtime feature flag (deferred_shed_enabled) and a rate-limited manual override in the console for emergency ops. 4) Adds observability: new metrics (oob_probe_latency_ms, oob_unhealthy_seconds, deferred_shed_decision) and structured logs for handoff events. 5) Includes a small hotfix to revert a prior micro-optimization in the circuit evaluator that caused immediate reopen attempts during KV-cache drains. Rollout plan: default feature-flag is enabled in canary region us-west-2 for 2 hours with synthetic traffic (health-check + tenant traffic mix); if metrics show no regressions we will roll forward to us-east-1 and EU regions. Rollback: toggle deferred_shed_enabled=false or revert the feature flag; the revert commit is isolated and small. Tests: unit tests for state transitions, integration test that simulates KV drain + probe failures, and an end-to-end smoke that validates latency SLOs under synthetic spikes. This PR is focused on stability and is intentionally conservative in changes to the runtime hot path. Related: ENG-3241, links to incident notes and the postmortem. See commits and changed files for details.
Introduces an out-of-band health probe and a deferred shedding window to reduce premature load-shedding during transient control-plane instability. Backwards-compatible via feature flag. Hotfix reverts an immediate-reopen optimization that caused reopen-on-drain behavior.

Motivation: Tenant workloads show multi-modal request patterns where a single global prefill/batching policy either overspends or underperforms for different cohorts. This PR implements a hierarchical prefill autoscaler that composes tenant-level and global-level hints to produce safer defaults, plus a telemetry bridge that captures quantization-era metrics (post-quant latency/error deltas) so the optimizer can recommend conservative quant tiers.

What this PR does: Adds a new batch hierarchy controller in the serving runtime which: (1) evaluates tenant prefill profiles, recent cold-start rates, and latency SLO violations; (2) computes an autoscale suggestion that can be applied as a non-disruptive default or promoted to tenant overrides; (3) attaches conservative quantization recommendations to suggestions based on observed latency/error deltas captured by the telemetry bridge.

Key characteristics:
- Tenant-first but fallback-friendly: tenant hints are preferred; when missing we synthesize a safe global default.
- Conservative quant tiers: telemetry bridge measures inferred token-level latency and token-loss proxies after quant changes and uses a small exponential backoff to avoid flapping.
- Dry-run and safety: introduced a rwctl prefill-sim dry-run that shows expected unit-econ impact and SLO risk score before applying policies.
- Minimal runtime overhead: hierarchy eval runs on the batch controller worker thread with a 1s cadence and uses cached stats to avoid hot paths.

Files touched (high level): runtime/batcher/hierarchy_controller.go, runtime/batcher/hierarchy_policy_test.go, telemetry/quant_bridge/collector.go, telemetry/quant_bridge/proto/quant_telemetry.proto, cmd/rwctl/prefill_sim.go, examples/prefill-samples/tenant_profiles.yaml, docs/cost-automation/hierarchical-prefill.md, CHANGELOG.md.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for hierarchy scoring and quant-safety logic (coverage + edge cases for empty tenant history); integration test that runs a tiny local workload and asserts decision output and no regression in tail latency; manual smoke runs on staging with two tenants to validate dry-run numbers against simulated billing. CI: all checks passed (go test, linter, telemetry proto compile).

Rollout plan: merged behind a feature flag (feature.prefill_hierarchy) with default off for existing tenants. Stage rollout: enable in staging -> opt-in beta tenants -> gradual global rollout with metric gates (increase in 95th latency or token loss > 0.5% triggers automatic rollback).

Related: ENG-4872 (prefill autoscale design), ENG-5900 (quant telemetry schema), small follow-up planned to surface suggested defaults in the Console (separate PR).
Maya Li: Nicely scoped. Two asks before approving: (1) add a short circuit if tenant history is < 30 requests to avoid noisy decisions; (2) ensure the telemetry proto versioning has migration notes. Can you address?
Sofia Nguyen (author): Added the short-circuit and a unit test for low-history tenants, proto now includes a version enum and migration notes in docs. PTAL.
Daniel Park: One nit on variable naming in hierarchy scoring, otherwise lgtm. Also can we add a quick perf benchmark for the 1s cadence?
Sofia Nguyen (author): Renamed variables and added a micro-benchmark in runtime/batcher/bench_hierarchy_test.go showing ~120ns per evaluation on avg. CI green.

Sofia Nguyen (author): Noted in rollout plan and will follow up with the Console PR to surface the gate to SREs.
Add hierarchical tenant-aware prefill autoscaler and quantization telemetry bridge; introduce rwctl prefill-sim dry-run to estimate unit-econ impact. Feature gated behind feature.prefill_hierarchy. See docs/cost-automation/hierarchical-prefill.md for usage.

Replaced ad-hoc shell/curl build entrypoints with a small Go-based build runner for hermetic local dev and CI; removed unused dev dependencies and trimmed Docker build layers. No user-facing API changes.
Context: over the last year the repo accumulated multiple ad-hoc shell entrypoints (scripts/bootstrap.sh, ci/run-steps.sh, docker/entrypoint.sh) used by local dev, CI, and release automation. These scripts are hard to cache, fragile across platforms, and make the CI matrix rely on varying shell behavior. This PR standardizes build entrypoints on a tiny Go runner binary (cmd/buildrunner) that: 1) exposes a typed CLI for common steps (install-deps, build, test, package), 2) performs deterministic dependency pruning (devonly removal) for Docker/CI artifacts, and 3) emits structured logs and exit codes the CI can consume. Motivation: improve hermeticity, speed up CI by enabling consistent layer caching, and reduce surface area of devDependencies across SDKs. Changes are split into several logical commits and include CI workflow updates and documentation in dev/README.

Checklist: - [x] Introduce cmd/buildrunner Go binary with subcommands for install/build/test/package - [x] Replace shell entrypoints referenced by ci/workflows/* and Dockerfiles - [x] Add dep-prune step (node/yarn and python venv) used before packaging images - [x] Remove unused dev dependencies from package.json and pyproject.toml where safe - [x] Update CI workflows to call buildrunner and consume structured logs - [x] Add smoke CI job (ci/smoke-fast.yml) that exercises new runner - [x] Add docs/dev-build.md with migration guidance - [ ] Monitor CI for 48h post-merge (follow-up ticket ENG-2030)

Context notes: Linear ENG-2027 tracks the build runner work; SUP-773 was a customer support ticket where inconsistent build artifacts caused bad images in a Dedicated install. This PR is intentionally conservative with pruning rules (only removes devDependencies that are not referenced in runtime bundles per static analysis). For Python packages we pin wheel build path and remove test-only extras before packaging.

2) ci: replace shell entrypoints in ci/workflows with buildrunner invocations; add smoke-fast.yml

This PR adds a declarative onboarding path for cost-optimization defaults (batching/caching presets), a quantization safelist mechanism, and a small CLI to preview tenant unit economics before applying templates. Motivation: customers frequently ask for safe, predictable defaults that can be applied as a single operation during onboarding or for tenant migrations; operators also need a safe way to limit quant profiles to vetted options.

Key components:
- configs/default_onramp_templates.yaml: declarative templates grouping batching shape, cache TTL/policy, and quantization profile references. Templates are idempotent and reference the existing policy DSL.
- pkg/econ/templates.go and pkg/econ/loader.go: loader/validator that expands templates into RuntimeConfig objects and runs lightweight safety checks (latency budget, reserved batch size bounds).
- cmd/costctl: new CLI subcommand 'costctl onramp apply|preview|dryrun' that shows unit-econ impact estimates and writes audit-able changes.
- scripts/quant_safelist_generator.py: tool for maintainers to produce the quant safelist from offline benchmark CSVs; integrates with model-registry metadata.
- migration/migrate_onramp.go: one-off migration that applies a recommended template to tenants marked by Linear ENG-2841.
- docs/costs/onramp.md: operator guide and rollback instructions.

Checklist:
- [x] Add onramp templates and loader
- [x] Implement quant safelist enforcement in runtime config validation
- [x] Build costctl preview and dry-run
- [x] Add unit and e2e tests
- [x] Add docs and changelog entry

Safety model: templates are guarded by a conservative validator with three gates (syntactic, unit-econ threshold, and runtime-safety). Quant safelist enforces that only profiles present in /configs/quant_safelist.csv can be referenced by templates; referencing an unknown profile fails validation. The safelist is intended as a mechanism for staged rollouts and compliance with tenant policies.

Impact: Enables one-click application of a small set of curated defaults during onboarding and reduces manual tuning. The preview CLI provides estimated monthly token cost deltas and expected median latency changes so SREs can make informed decisions.

Related: ENG-2841 (onramp automation), ENG-2967 (quant governance), SUP-9021 (support ticket that motivated default presets).
Ethan Park: Left a few nits in templates.go around error wrapping; also question the default cache TTL of 5m for async workloads — can we make that tenant-configurable?
Priya Nambiar: Reply: made TTL tenant-overridable and added a unit test. Kept conservative default of 5m per ENG-2841 guidance.
Nora Wallace: Approve with comments: quant_safelist_generator.py looks fine but add README for maintainers. Also request that CLI output include a JSON machine-readable flag.
Priya Nambiar: Reply: added --json flag to costctl preview and a short maintainer README under scripts/
Diego Alvarez: Requested runtime-safety threshold be tightened; saw a flake in e2e tests on the 99th percentile latencies. Priya adjusted validator and re-ran CI.
- New: declarative cost-onramp templates for batching/caching/quant presets
- New: quant safelist enforcement to limit quant profiles to vetted options
- New: costctl preview/dryrun to estimate tenant unit economics before applying templates
- Docs: operator guide for onramp and rollback
This change was tested against the synthetic-workload lab (benchmark-lab) and a small internal tenant pilot. The quant safelist is seeded from historical benchmark runs; subsequent updates to the safelist will require an attendant compatibility note in the changelog.
payload.title: Introduce universal cost-onramp templates and quant safelist adapter

Context: We've seen a class of integration bugs from customers using OpenAI /v1/chat.completions shape — stop can be string or array, role aliases (assistant/system/user) are passed in different keys, and streaming logprobs previously emitted inline are causing JSON-framing ambiguity for framed streaming consumers. Motivation: provide a single-server-side normalization layer so downstream runtime and the OpenAI compatibility layer can expect a canonical parameter set (stop: array<string>, roles: canonical enum, logprobs: moved to `logprob_envelope`) and reduce client-side fragmentation. This PR implements a chatv1 'parameter sanitizer' middleware plus an opt-in streaming format migration for logprobs. What this changes: 1) Stop normalization: accepts string | array | null and canonicalizes to array of strings (empty => null). Preserves original stop intent via telemetry. 2) Role handoff mapping: accepts role aliases (e.g. "assistant", "bot", "system_prompt") and coalesces into canonical role values; adds a lightweight role-mapping table that is extensible. 3) Logprob envelope: streaming now emits a separate envelope event for token logprobs ("logprob_envelope") rather than inline delta tokens to prevent token/frame ambiguity for consumers that parse framed JSON. 4) Tool/function calling stability: small change to how function call boundaries are emitted in streams so the sanitizer can attach role-handoff annotations to the final toolcall chunk. 5) Backwards compatibility: old clients continue to receive legacy inline logprobs when the client sets header X-Redwood-Compat: legacy-logprob; otherwise new envelope is used. 6) Tests & docs: adds unit and integration tests covering common malformed inputs plus a migration guide in docs/chat/openai-compat.md. Checklist: - [x] Parameter sanitizer middleware implementation - [x] Streaming logprob envelope schema & encoder/decoder - [x] Backcompat header switch and tests - [x] Role alias mapping table with tests - [x] Integration tests against streaming consumer harness - [x] Docs and release note draft - [x] Perf bench run (latency regression <2% for 1-token responses) Related work: ENG-2145 (chat parity roadmap); SUP-834 (customer incident where stop string broke streaming parser). Commits summary: - feat(sanitizer): new chatv1 parameter sanitizer middleware + unit tests - feat(stream): implement logprob_envelope framing in stream encoder - feat(api): role alias mapping table and config - fix(stream): ensure function-call boundary annotated with role-handoff metadata - docs: add migration guide and examples - test(ci): add integration test to stream harness Known limitations: - The role alias table is intentionally conservative; we will expand mappings based on customer telemetry. - Very old client SDKs that hard-parse inline logprob deltas must opt into legacy mode via header. Migration notes: see docs/chat/openai-compat.md for examples and recommended server-side flagging. Merge: squash-merged to main after approvals and CI green.

Motivation: Teams were seeing alert storms from noisy long-tail tenant requests and false positives in per-route SLOs when a small subset of tenants generated sporadic token-heavy requests. This PR introduces a per-tenant SLO decomposition pipeline and an evidence-backed auto-suppression layer that dampens noisy alerts without hiding true regressions. Goals: 1) attribute latency and token-cost SLO violations to individual tenants and top contributing routes; 2) compute a sample-weighted anomaly score per tenant to distinguish systematic regressions from statistical noise; 3) provide a configurable auto-snooze/damping mechanism and an operator-facing SLO Lens dashboard to inspect suppression rationale. Changes included: - Telemetry pipeline: new per-tenant attribution keys (tenant_id, model_variant, route_signature) applied in the rollup job to produce tenant-level SLI rollups at 1m and 1h granularities. - Anomaly scorer: introduces a reservoir-weighted z-score computed from recent percentile deltas (p50/p95/p99) and token-cost deltas; scores are stored in the metrics-store as tenant_anomaly_score. - Auto-suppress policy: a stateful controller evaluates anomaly scores against configurable thresholds and historical persistence to either (a) auto-snooze alerts (with reason metadata) for short-lived spikes, or (b) apply a damping factor to alert firing probability when the signal is noisy but persistent. - SLO Lens dashboard: a compact UI panel (Console) that shows the decomposition waterfall, contributing routes, recent sample traces, and the suppression rationale with links to example traces. - Alert generator suggestion: when suppression is enabled, the system surfaces recommended dedup window and threshold bands per route/tenant to minimize pager noise. Implementation notes: - Rollup job: extended rollup-worker to emit tenant rollups and anomaly_score metrics; added a lightweight sketch-based reservoir to preserve rare-high-latency samples without exploding cardinality. - Controller: new controller service (slo-suppressor) runs as a low-throughput singleton per region and writes suppression decisions to the alerting-config store for evaluation by the alert router. - Backwards compat: existing per-route SLOs are untouched if tenant attribution is not present; suppression defaults to disabled. - Config: feature flag slo_decomp_autosuppress (off by default), per-tenant thresholds live in feature flags and can be adjusted via the Console. Testing and validation: - Unit tests for rollup and anomaly scorer (coverage added). - Integration test that simulates a tenant burst pattern and verifies suppression vs real regression behavior. - Load test: measured negligible overhead for rollup-worker (~1.6% CPU at 99th percentile on a stressed cluster). - Canary rollout plan: staged enabling on non-prod clusters, then opt-in beta customers, then gradual ramp with automatic revert if suppression masks >3 consecutive true regressions per week. Related work: references ENG-4829 for initial request, SUP-1937 for customer incident that motivated suppression heuristics, and dashboard design doc linked in Linear-ENG-4902. Risks and mitigations: suppression could hide real incidents if thresholds misconfigured — mitigated by conservative defaults, explicit evidence metadata (sample traces and contributing routes), and automatic rollback if we detect correlated increases in true-positive regression confirmations from alerts. Migration: no DB schema changes; metrics store adds new time-series keys (tenant_anomaly_score, tenant_sli_*). Rollout notes: feature flagged; requires console backend update and a single slo-suppressor replica per region. Checklist: - [x] Rollup emission and metric storage - [x] Anomaly scorer + unit tests - [x] Controller + integration tests - [x] Dashboard panel and links to traces - [x] Documentation (runbook + admin guide) - [x] Canary plan and automation
Ethan Cole: Can the scorer be gamed by clients that shard requests across tenants? Suggest adding a cross-tenant correlation check.
Priya Menon: Replyed: added a cross-tenant spike detector that increases sensitivity if correlated anomalies appear across a configurable fraction of tenants.
Maya Chen: Please add telemetry to surface when suppression suppressed an alert that later proved to be a true regression.
Priya Menon: Added a suppressed_alert_checkpoint metric and test that simulates late-truth confirmation.
Ibrahim Khalid: Approve after nit on naming and one additional integration test for failure mode detection.
Priya Menon: Addressed nits and added the test; pushing final commit.
Introduce per-tenant SLO decomposition rollups and tenant_anomaly_score metric
Add evidence-backed auto-suppression for alert noise with conservative defaults
Add SLO Lens dashboard panel showing contributing routes, sample traces, and suppression rationale
Feature flagged; disabled by default. Admin runbook included.
Enable slo_decomp_autosuppress flag to start collecting tenant rollups (no suppression until controller enabled).
Start with sensitivity: low and monitor suppressed_alert_checkpoint metric for false-suppression signals.
If suppression hides regressions, set controller mode to audit-only to collect evidence without muting alerts.

Introduces credential phasing to reduce stream reconnect churn; new compact retry profiles and minor ergonomic stream API surface changes across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Backwards compatible; minor SDK version bumps (py 1.13.0 -> 1.14.0, ts 2.9.1 -> 2.10.0, go v0.9.7 -> v0.10.0).
Summary: This PR implements an "auth phasing" pattern and a slimmed stream ergonomics surface across the three SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go). The goal is to reduce 'stream fidget'—reconnects and token races observed when credentials rotate out-of-band—and to offer a consistent, lightweight API for long-lived pull/push streams that is parity-friendly across languages. Motivation: Multiple production customers reported intermittent reconnect noise during credential rotation windows and inconsistent stream ergonomics across SDKs. Root-cause analysis (ENG-2150) showed a pattern: SDKs attempted immediate token swap mid-chunk which caused in-flight iterator cancellations and duplicate reconnections. This surfaced as increased p99 latencies and amplified token refresh storms under load. What this PR does: 1) Introduces a credential phasing mechanism (phase window + soft-swap): SDKs now enter a configurable 'grace phase' before switching to a newly fetched token. During grace, outgoing calls accept existing token while background refresh obtains primary replacement; only once phase completes do in-flight streams observe the new token. 2) Adds compact retry profiles: small, medium, and conservative presets tuned for streaming workloads, preserving latency SLOs while increasing robustness. 3) Stream surface polish: introduces a lightweight StreamHandle abstraction (py: StreamHandle, ts: StreamHandle, go: StreamHandle) that exposes pause(), resume(), and a small set of deterministic state transitions to avoid caller-level race conditions. 4) Cross-language parity shim: common spec document and test harness updated to define precise semantics for credential handoff and stream pause/resume semantics; SDK implementations adapted to match spec. 5) Version bumps in each SDK and updated changelogs/examples. High-level commits: - feat: credential phasing core logic and phasing config (py/ts/go) - feat: compact retry presets + telemetry hooks - feat: StreamHandle API and implementation for each SDK - test: cross-sdk contract tests for phasing and stream transitions - docs: spec and examples + migration notes - ci: matrix updates to run cross-sdk contract tests on PRs Review/revisions: Initial review requested by Diego Morales on 2026-01-20. Key comments: - Diego: "Please clarify how phasing interacts with cached KV entries for the runtime; ensure we don't leak stale auth into cache keys." Response: Implemented an explicit cache key invalidation hook in the py/ts/go runtime adapters; added unit tests. - Aisha: "TS surface looks ok but ergonomic names clash with existing helpers (pause vs suspend)." Response: Chose pause()/resume() to stay language-agnostic; added aliases to maintain backwards compat for TS helper suspend() -> pause(). - Ethan: "Can we avoid an additional API dependency in Go?" Response: Kept StreamHandle zero-dep by embedding into existing connection struct; added doc explaining no new external deps. CI and stability: Cross-sdk contract tests were added to the Github Actions matrix. The first CI run showed flaky test in TypeScript contract harness; fixed by adding deterministic seed and a 50ms jitter to token-refresh mock. Final CI status: all checks passed including unit, linters, cross-sdk-contract, and integration smoke tests. Files changed (selected highlights): - python/redwood_sdk/stream/stream_handle.py (new): implements StreamHandle and phasing state machine - python/redwood_sdk/auth/phasing.py (modified): core phasing logic and configs - python/tests/test_phasing_contract.py (new): contract tests for phasing - typescript/src/stream/stream_handle.ts (new): TS implementation + adapters - typescript/src/auth/phasing.ts (modified) - typescript/test/contract/phasing.spec.ts (new) - go/sdk/stream/stream_handle.go (new) - go/sdk/auth/phasing.go (modified) - docs/sdk-auth-phasing-spec.md (new): cross-language spec and examples - examples/streaming/credential-phasing-demo (updated) Migration notes for integrators: - Default behavior is off (phasing.enabled=false). Enable selectively in environments where token rotation storms observed. - Suggested presets: compact (low-latency), medium (balanced), conservative (max-robustness) mapped to retry/timeouts for streams. - Minor API aliasing added for TS to preserve existing helpers; Python/Go changes are additive. Performance/telemetry: Added telemetry hooks to surface "phasing events" and "stream state transitions". Benchmarks in the PR show a 2-7% reduction in observed p99 reconnect rate under a simulated rotation storm while maintaining median latency within 1% of baseline. Security/compatibility: No secrets stored differently; phasing only coordinates when token is swapped not how it's fetched. QA notes: Added stress tests that simulate overlapping rotations and high-concurrency stream churn. All stress tests are checked into python/tests/stress_phasing.py and equivalent harnesses in TS/Go. Rollout plan: - Canary the Python SDK in internal dogfood services for 2 weeks with logging level set to debug for phasing events. - After stable behavior, flip on TS and Go canaries. - Recommend opt-in for public customers initially, then consider enabling by default if no regressions. Related tickets and PRs: ENG-2150 (investigate stream reconnect storms), ENG-2187 (cross-sdk parity test harness). Merge outcome: squash-merged into main on 2026-01-28 after approvals from all reviewers. Notes: kept change surface intentionally small in the public API; most of the work is internal phasing orchestration and improved tests/examples.

Summary: This PR introduces the Cost Model API v1 internal endpoints to support Console cost breakdown views and Optimize what-if projections, with consistent auth/tenancy enforcement and strict request bounding to avoid cardinality and latency blowups. Endpoints added (internal): 1) POST /internal/cost-model/v1/estimate: returns a per-request cost estimate (total + major components) for a single request context (model/runtime/deployment inputs + token counts + cache/batch/quant profile). Intended for hot-path per-request queries (Console drill-down, debugging). 2) POST /internal/cost-model/v1/breakdown: returns an aggregated bounded breakdown over a query window (e.g., per model, per route, per deployment mode) using pre-aggregated telemetry inputs. Designed for dashboards; supports pagination and server-side caps. 3) POST /internal/cost-model/v1/what-if: returns projections for config changes (batching/caching/quantization) given a workload summary. Includes an explicit confidence field and guardrails (range validation + scenario caps) to prevent expensive computations and misuse. Auth/tenancy: Enforces service-to-service auth via the internal gateway auth middleware; requires caller identity and verifies allowed service principals (Console, Optimize, and internal batch jobs). Adds required tenant scoping: org_id is mandatory; project_id optional depending on query type; all downstream telemetry/model-catalog reads are filtered by tenant scope. Adds auditing fields to logs (org_id, project_id, caller_service, schema_version) with PII-safe policies. Versioning/compatibility: v1 endpoints accept an explicit schema_version in the request (defaulting to latest supported v1.x). Response includes schema_version and server_build for debugging. Unknown fields are ignored (forward-compatible) but unknown schema_version returns 400 INVALID_SCHEMA_VERSION with a supported_versions list in the message. Request bounds (perf + safety): estimate: max_input_tokens/max_output_tokens enforced (defaults: 128k input, 16k output); rejects negative/overflow; validates model_id + quant_profile_id exist in model catalog. breakdown: limits time window (max 31d), limits group_by keys (max 3), caps number of buckets returned (max 500), requires pagination token when truncated. what-if: caps scenarios (max 10), caps number of dimensions changed per scenario (max 3), validates allowed ranges for cache_hit_rate_delta, batch_size_target, and quant_profile_id. Also adds a server-side timeout budget with early exit returning partial results where applicable (explicit partial=true). Observability: Adds structured metrics and traces: cost_model_api_requests_total by endpoint + status, cost_model_api_latency_ms p50/p95, cost_model_api_bounds_rejections_total with reason, and cost_model_api_schema_version_distribution. Adds a trace span per endpoint with tags for org_id_hash (stable hash), caller_service, and schema_version. Error model: Standardizes error responses via Redwood API error envelope (code, message, request_id). Adds explicit codes: UNAUTHENTICATED, PERMISSION_DENIED, INVALID_ARGUMENT, INVALID_SCHEMA_VERSION, BOUNDS_EXCEEDED, UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE (telemetry/model-catalog), and TIMEOUT. Note: this PR intentionally does not change billing hooks or Console/Optimize usage; those are follow-ups. Related: schema types were introduced in pr-28451; policy guardrails are further tuned in pr-28495; Console adoption tracked in ENG-4825 and Optimize adoption tracked in ENG-4826. Testing: Adds unit tests for request validation and tenancy filtering; contract tests for error codes; and a small integration test that runs the handlers against a stubbed telemetry store + model catalog. Includes golden response snapshots for the three endpoints. Rollout: Endpoints are behind the internal gateway route allowlist. No external exposure. Safe to deploy; no existing endpoints modified. Known limitations / follow-ups: - what-if currently models cache changes as a direct hit-rate delta; warm-rate modeling is deferred (see ENG-4824 comments). - breakdown endpoint uses pre-aggregated telemetry; per-request joins are intentionally not supported in v1 to keep performance bounded. - need to align with drift monitoring job once scheduled pipeline lands (ENG-4827).
Internal-only: Introduces Cost Model API v1 endpoints for estimate/breakdown/what-if with tenancy enforcement, bounded requests, and standard error codes. Console/Optimize adoption remains behind feature flags in follow-up PRs.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (security): Tenancy scoping looks good, but we should require org_id for all endpoints, including breakdown where project_id is optional. Also please add caller_service to audit logs. Ethan Park (author): Updated validation to require org_id across the board and added caller_service from auth context to structured logs + traces. Added tests for missing org_id returning INVALID_ARGUMENT.
Logan Wright (telemetry): For breakdown, please ensure group_by values are a fixed allowlist; we cannot accept arbitrary tag keys or we’ll blow up cardinality. Ethan Park (author): Added allowlist for group_by (model_id, route, deployment_mode, region, quant_profile_id) and hard cap of 3 keys. Added BOUNDS_EXCEEDED on violations and metrics for rejection reasons.
Chloe Martin (Console): On hot paths, Console needs predictable response sizes; can we guarantee max buckets and include a next_page_token when truncated? Ethan Park (author): Implemented bucket cap 500 with deterministic sorting, added next_page_token + truncated flag, and documented pagination contract in internal docs.
Rafael Mendes (SRE): Please add explicit timeout handling and surface when results are partial. Also would like a metric for bounds rejections and upstream failures. Ethan Park (author): Added server timeout budget per endpoint, partial=true where applicable (what-if); exported cost_model_api_bounds_rejections_total and cost_model_api_upstream_failures_total.
Benji Okafor (platform): Endpoint names OK. One nit: error code INVALID_SCHEMA_VERSION should list supported versions in message. Ethan Park (author): Done. Error message now includes supported_versions=["cost-model/v1.0","cost-model/v1.1"].

Motivation: high-volume streaming endpoints were producing large volumes of traces and occasional silent stream truncations when proxies or clients dropped frames. This PR adds three coordinated pieces: 1) per-endpoint sampling config (server-side) so high-throughput routes can be sampled at configurable rates; 2) an opt-in stream checksum header (X-RW-Stream-Checksum) added by the OpenAI compatibility adapter to enable end-to-end payload integrity checks across proxies and the client-side SDK; and 3) a lightweight function-call span shim that ties tool/function executions (including external tool invocations) to the parent request span while recording function latency, exit code/exception, and output size. The OpenAI adapter enrichment is backward-compatible: it only sets additional response headers and emits structured telemetry events; it does not alter user-visible response bodies. This change also introduces a small server-side cache of last-checksum-per-connection to detect repeated retransmits and improve logging signal. The description below lists what changed and why. Changes are split across runtime (sampling engine), api gateway (header plumbing), openai-compat adapter (shim), and tests.
runtime: add per-endpoint sampling config and sampling decision cache
gateway: propagate X-RW-Stream-Checksum on streamed responses
openai-compat: attach function-call span shim and emit structured function_call telemetry
tests: add unit + integration tests for sampling and checksum mismatch handling
Raj Patel: Please make sampling rate configurable via the console/route config; hardcoding in yaml is not sufficient for customers.
Sofia Nguyen: The checksum header name looks good; we should ensure SDKs expose an opt-in client verification path so users can verify end-to-end integrity.
Marco Alvarez: Can we avoid allocating on every streamed fragment? Suggest reusing a buffer in gateway/streaming_handler.go.
Author (Elena): Addressed Marco's buffer reuse comment, added a shared buffer pool; moved sampling to an atomic decision cache to avoid per-request map lookups.
Raj: Left a minor nit on log message verbosity; otherwise LGTM after docs update.
Sofia: Approved after confirming SDK follow-up ticket.
Added per-endpoint telemetry sampling and an opt-in stream checksum header (X-RW-Stream-Checksum). Function-call executions are now correlated to parent request spans and emit structured telemetry (latency, size, success). These features are opt-in via route config and the OpenAI compatibility adapter; see docs/observability/streaming.md for rollout and SDK follow-up notes.

Motivation: SDK teams drifted on token refresh behavior and streaming consumer ergonomics. This PR introduces a compact CredMediator that standardizes refresh/failed-token semantics across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs and a SlimIterable v1 spec that defines a minimal pull-style streaming surface (next, ack, pause, resume, heartbeat). Core work lives in the redwood repo to run coordinated interop tests. Context and motivation:
We observed spikes in presubmit queue latency caused by expensive agent bootstrap and toolchain installation on ephemeral runners. This patch makes two complementary changes: (1) introduce a short-lived 'toolchain lease' that lets CI runners reuse prepared toolchains for a configurable window, and (2) shrink and optimize the CI agent bootstrap so cold-start overhead is minimized. Together these changes target ENG-3184 and ENG-3220 and are intended to reduce presubmit wall-clock time without changing test coverage.

What this PR does (high-level):
- CI agent: factor out heavy startup phases (image verification, full manifest expansion) into a fastpath that runs concurrently with a lightweight health probe. The agent now favors a cached toolchain when a valid lease exists.
- Toolchain lease: add a lease allocator service and local lease file (.ci/toolchain-lease.json) so subsequent jobs on the same runner can reuse validated toolchains for a TTL (configurable; default 15m).
- Presubmit routing: introduce a small fastpath in .github/workflows/presubmit.yml that directs low-risk changes (docs, examples, ci-config only) to a slim job that skips heavy integration shards.
- Observability: add metrics for lease hits/misses and agent bootstrap time, exported to Prometheus and surfaced in Console.

Commits (summary):
- Add minimal toolchain lease allocator and lease file handling (lease.go + allocator tests)
- Refactor agent bootstrap to use lease and add fastpath probe (agent.go + bootstrap tests)
- Update presubmit workflow to include fastpath routing and lightweight job profile (presubmit.yml)
- Small docker image tweaks: compress toolchain layers and remove unused buildtools (ci/Dockerfile)
- Telemetry and metrics: expose ci_toolchain_lease_hits and agent_bootstrap_seconds counters
- Tests and docs: unit tests for lease expiry and short integration smoke for presubmit fastpath; docs/ci/toolchain-lease.md

Files/areas changed (high level):
- scripts/ci/agent.go (refactor bootstrap path, add lease lookup)
- scripts/ci/lease.go (new: allocator and local lease file handling)
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yml (fastpath job + tagging rules)
- ci/Dockerfile (shrink image, remove python wheels we no longer use)
- build/toolchains/manifest.json (lease TTL default added)
- docs/ci/toolchain-lease.md (design + operational runbook)
- monitoring/prometheus/ci.rules (new metrics)
- test/ci/lease_test.go (unit coverage)
- test/ci/presubmit_smoke.sh (integration shim)

Testing and CI:
- CI run summary: unit -> pass, integration-smoke -> pass (one flaky matrix shard retried once), lint -> pass. The full presubmit matrix was exercised in the staging lane; we measured median bootstrap reduction ~28% on our staging runners.
- Performance numbers (staging): median agent bootstrap from 65s -> 47s; toolchain install frequency down 45% on consecutive jobs within TTL window.

Review conversation highlights:
- Diego: "Can we make TTL configurable per-queue? For long-running release lanes we'd want a shorter TTL to avoid stale toolchain drift."
- Author (Aisha): "Yes — manifest.json includes default TTL; I've added queue-level override support and documented it in docs/ci/toolchain-lease.md. We can add policy to L4 if we see drift."
- Lin: "Agent logs on lease miss look noisy; can we reduce INFO level noise and surface distinct lease miss metric?"
- Author: "Addressed — reduced log level to DEBUG for expected misses and added ci_toolchain_lease_misses counter. Also added a short backoff before re-install to avoid thundering-herd on lease expiry."
- Priya: "Pipeline safety: what happens if lease file becomes corrupted on disk?"
- Author: "Agent will treat corrupted lease as miss and recover; added defensive parsing and a documented cleanup script. Also added unit test covering corrupted lease file."

Edge cases and known limitations:
- This change improves hot-runner cases; ephemeral single-job runners (e.g., cloud-hosted ephemeral VMs that don't share filesystem) get limited benefit. We added a feature flag to gate lease allocator per-runner pool.
- Toolchain drift: leases are short by default and require owner to bump manifest when toolchain changes. Ops runbook includes steps to revoke leases cluster-wide if needed.

Rollout plan and safety:
- Feature gated behind ci.featureFlags.toolchainLease (default on for internal staging pools, off for external ephemeral pools).
- Gradual rollout: start internal staging -> dev runners -> all presubmit lanes over 72 hours while monitoring lease_hit_ratio and agent_bootstrap_seconds.
- Fallback: if regressions observed, feature flag can be toggled off and a small re-image of runners will clear stale toolchains.

Related work and links:
- Linear: ENG-3184 (toolchain leasing experiment), ENG-3220 (presubmit latency reduction)
- Design doc: docs/ci/toolchain-lease.md
- Small follow-ups expected: add per-repo leases, and consider shared network-attached cache for fully ephemeral pools.

Merge outcome:
- All reviewers approved; CI green; merged via squash on 2026-02-22. Post-merge: deployment of allocator to staging on 2026-02-23, monitored for 48 hours with no regressions.

Checklist (from PR template):
- [x] Tests added/updated
- [x] Docs updated (runbook + design)
- [x] Feature flagged for gradual rollout
- [x] Metrics added

If you're reviewing this after merge and want to poke at the runtime telemetry, the new metrics prefix is ci_toolchain_lease_* and agent_bootstrap_seconds is histo-bucketed for SLO tracking. For operational questions see docs/ci/toolchain-lease.md or ping @aisha on Linear ENG-3184.
Reduced presubmit latency by ~30% via lighter CI agent bootstrap and toolchain leasing. Added capability to hold short-lived toolchain leases to avoid repeated full bootstraps; routing rules for low-risk PRs introduced. No user-facing API changes.
Staging rollout monitored; no incidents. Follow-ups: per-repo lease, network cache exploration.
Adds small lease service (~600 LOC), minor Docker image shrink (~40MB), and CI workflow changes to accelerate presubmit feedback loops.

Add Unit Price Curator service and autoscale-aware micro-batcher. Provides tenant-level per-token price signals, autoscale batch size recommendations, and safe quantization profile fallbacks.
Summary: Introduce a lightweight service (unit-price-curator) that computes tenant-specific per-token pricing signals and exposes an API used by the autoscale micro-batcher to pick safe batch sizes and quantization presets. Motivation: customers running multi-tenant workloads need predictable unit economics; current autoscalers choose conservative batch sizes or require manual tuning. This PR wires an automated signal path: sample token distributions -> compute effective unit price and variance -> produce recommended batch shape + quant profile and a confidence score. Checklist: - [x] service skeleton + API (gRPC/HTTP) - [x] sampling worker and aggregation pipeline - [x] autoscale micro-batcher integration and decision hook - [x] safe quantization fallback matrix and rollback policy - [x] unit tests for sampling and decision logic - [x] end-to-end smoke test in perf-lab - [x] docs and runbook with operational heuristics Design notes: - Unit Price Curator (UPC) consumes recent token-level telemetry (prefix lengths, model SKU, quant tier) and tenant config. It computes a running weighted median cost-per-1000-tokens and a volatility estimate (sigma). The output is a small JSON recommendation: {batch_shape_hint, target_quant_tier, confidence, reason_tags}. - Autoscale micro-batcher now queries UPC during warm-start and on scaling events. If confidence is high, batcher applies recommended batch_shape within configured latency SLO bounds; if confidence is low, it triggers a conservative fallback and schedules a sampled dry-run. - Quantization: recommendations are conservative by default (e.g., int8 for tested models) and annotated with rollback policy (if output quality regression > threshold, revert). Implementation highlights: - new microservice under services/unit_price_curator with gRPC + HTTP translation layer - lightweight aggregator in telemetry/consumers that keeps a 60m sliding window per tenant - batcher hook in serving/runtime/batcher to request recommendations (async cache for 10s) - a new config flag: autoscale.enable_upc (false by default) Tests: added unit tests for curator math (edge cases for tiny tenants), integration test for batcher reaction to recommendation spikes, perf-lab run that validated no latency regressions for 99th p50-90. Operation: docs/runbooks/unit-price-curator.md contains troubleshooting steps, cardinal alerts (e.g., high volatility, repeated rollbacks), and recommended Linear tickets to open when observed behavior persists. Security: service uses mTLS internally and checks tenant scoping before returning recommendations. Backward compatibility: if UPC is unavailable, batcher falls back to existing heuristics. Migration: feature gated behind autoscale.enable_upc and rollout plan in the runbook. Risks & mitigations: - Risk: noisy telemetry could suggest aggressive quant tiers -> mitigation: a trust-layer that requires min_samples and volatility checks before promoting quant changes. - Risk: increased control plane latency -> mitigation: async cache and 50ms internal timeout. Related: ENG-1382 (tenant pricing signals), PM-402 (autoscale UX improvements).

Context: As we scale multi-stage rollouts (shadow -> canary -> promote) we observed rare but user-visible regressions caused by payload-sensitive model behavior and partial session handoffs. This PR implements a 'Lane Attestor' that augments our rollout pipeline with: 1) real-time attestation signals (smoke test pass, schema conformance, hallucination proxy score) used as gates; 2) sanitized shadowing for A/B analysis to avoid leaking broken inputs to downstream services; 3) resume-safe rollback anchors that preserve session affinity and allow immediate traffic rewinds without dropping in-flight sessions. What changed (high level): - New attestor core and policy engine (serving/orchestrator/attestor) that evaluates per-cohort signals and emits gate decisions. - Shadow proxy: sanitizes and tags shadow payloads, forwards them to variant replicas and to the replay buffer. - Rollback anchors: checkpointed session leases and lightweight snapshotting so a rollback can rehydrate session state and resume with the previous model variant. - Operator surface: Helm values, console flags, and a runbook for manual intervention. - Tests: unit, integration, and an e2e canary-sim harness. Rollout plan: staged rollout through Dedicated -> Hosted: 0.1 -> 0.25 -> 0.5 -> 1.0 with 30-minute holdpoints. Automatic rollback triggers: (a) latency P95 increase > 35% for 10 minutes; (b) hallucination-proxy rate > 3% absolute increase vs baseline for 10 minutes; (c) HTTP error rate > 0.5% absolute increase for 5 minutes.
