Motivation: Several customers surfaced intermittent failures when calling tool/function envelopes while we rolled out schema v3. We want a runtime-side, opt-in probe that detects client schema capability at request time, collects telemetry for gradual rollout, and applies a safe shim to preserve streaming and structured output guarantees. This PR adds a lightweight schema probe middleware to the proxy that inspects a single probe token at the start of the request when the client sets X-Redwood-Schema: v3-beta. The middleware implements: 1) a non-blocking probe step that attempts a minimal handshake compatible with v3 tool envelopes; 2) a fast-path toggle so probe cost is removed after capability confirmation for that session ID; 3) a deterministic fallback to v2 envelope semantics on explicit failure or timeout to preserve availability. The approach intentionally keeps changes on the runtime/proxy surface so most models and serving runtime paths remain untouched. Implementation details: Added runtime proxy middleware and header parsing in pkg/openai/compat to surface client-declared capability. Probe uses a single-token interaction and a 150ms timeout by default; failures are logged and increment a new metric openai_compat.schema_probe.failures. We added a short-lived session cache keyed by client-request-id to avoid repeated probes for the same client in quick succession. Telemetry and rollout plan: Emitted metrics include openai_compat.schema_probe.attempts, .successes, .failures, and .slow_path_count. We also emit labelled metrics by org_id and header value to measure adoption. Rollout: feature is gated behind a runtime flag and requires clients to opt in with X-Redwood-Schema: v3-beta to participate. Initial rollout will enable the probe for 5% of eligible traffic (canary) and then scale in 10% increments once failure rate <0.5%. Compatibility guarantees: If probe fails or times out, request is automatically coerced to v2-compatible envelope semantics with preserved streaming; structured output coercion is applied only when safe. Tests and docs: End-to-end tests simulating mixed v2/v3 clients added; a new doc page describes the opt-in header, telemetry, and migration guidance. Security and privacy: probes do not send customer payloads to external services and telemetry is aggregated. Checklist: - [x] add probe middleware and header parsing - [x] metrics and telemetry tagging - [x] unit and e2e tests - [x] docs and migration guidance - [x] runtime toggle and canary config - [x] update changelog and console release notes

Priya: Added header parsing unit tests and included a small fuzz harness to catch malformed values. See commit feat(compat): parse X-Redwood-Schema header and expose capability checks.
Anya: Can we ensure the probe cache respects multi-tenant isolation? I don't want a session id collision to leak capability state across orgs.
Priya: Cache is keyed by org_id + client-request-id now. Updated session_cache.go and added tests to assert isolation.

Added an opt-in runtime schema probe for clients declaring X-Redwood-Schema: v3-beta. The probe enables safe v3 rollouts by detecting client capability and applying a runtime shim/fallback to v2 semantics when necessary. Metrics and canary rollout config included. No breaking changes; opt-in only.
To enable the feature for a canary, set runtime flag enable_schema_probe=true and canary_pct=5 in deploy/flags/runtime_flags.go or via runtime config service. Adds a residency-aware RBAC adapter that propagates sensitivity labels, prioritizes RBAC rules by geozone and sensitivity, introduces a chained KMS fallback for region pinning, and reduces audit noise with a compressed audit funnel. Backwards compatible; rollout via canary.
Context: Several enterprise customers require stronger guarantees when requests cross geozones: enforce RBAC decisions based on declared sensitivity labels, ensure KMS usage honors region pinning with a tolerant fallback path, and avoid overwhelming audit pipelines with noisy telemetry. Motivation: Close gaps found during a recent compliance review (SUP-1820) where operator-scoped requests were permitted despite mismatched residency claims and audit traffic caused high ingestion costs. What this PR changes: 1) residency-adapter: a new sensitivity-aware RBAC adapter that enriches incoming operator/service claims with a derived sensitivity label and uses a decision-priority matrix to evaluate RBAC v2 rules. 2) kms/fallback: a chained KMS selector that attempts region-local CMK, then geo-fallback CMK in same legal zone, then a tenant-consent-proxy path; all attempts are recorded in an encrypted audit envelope. 3) audit/compression: lightweight compression and deduplication for repetitive low-entropy audit events, plus a sampling profile per sensitivity tier. 4) decision cache TTL heuristics: TTLs are now informed by sensitivity tier and recent policy changes to reduce cache poisoning risk. Design notes: The adapter is OPA-compatible and exposes a single decision endpoint used by the existing authz flow; policy ordering is explicit and documented in docs/security/residency-rbac.md; KMS selection is pluggable for private deployments. Testing and observability: unit tests, integration harness against a local kms-mock, and a canary that emits metrics to the console dashboard. Rollout plan: Canary 5% traffic on Dedicated for 48 hours with alerting thresholds on decision latency, KMS fallback rate, and audit ingest size; if stable, 25% for 72 hours then full rollout. Rollback steps: feature flag off and clear decision cache; kms calls fall back to previous selector. Security review: threat model completed, no new plaintext secrets, audit envelopes encrypted under tenant CMK where possible. Follow-ups: integrate with Optimize to recommend sensitivity-tagging on prompts and add a UI toggle in Console for residency strictness. See linked Linear ENG-6234 and ENG-6291 for eval prompt sets and migration steps.

Priya Sharma: Added a TTL table in docs/security/residency-rbac.md and linked the heuristics to ENG-6291.

Priya Sharma: Added encrypted audit envelope writing that includes attempted key IDs and a signed witness token; implementation in internal/audit/compression.go and chained_selector.go.
Ben Thornton: Integration tests are flaky in CI (kms-mock timeout). Please increase mock timeouts and add retry with jitter.
Priya Sharma: Increased timeouts and added exponential backoff in tests; re-ran CI.

Motivation: CI feedback cycles are noisy and slow when running full integration matrices for every dependency automation PR. Motivation: We observed subtle inconsistencies in credential selection and retry behavior across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs when the platform returns mixed TTLs and transient auth failures under load. These divergences led to duplicated token exchanges and increased tail latency for streaming consumers. This PR introduces a lightweight, cross-language design called "credential consensus" plus a streaming retry orchestration pattern named "stream-sentinel" to align behavior across SDKs, reduce redundant reauths, and provide deterministic backoff/abort semantics for long-lived streams.

What this PR does in one paragraph: Adds a consensus window and voting heuristic to credential selection so concurrent consumers converge on a single reauth path, implements a stream-sentinel that centralizes heartbeat/failover logic for streaming handles, harmonizes retry preset profiles across SDKs (fast-retry for short-lived unary calls, sentinel-backed adaptive backoff for streams), and bumps SDK package versions to capture the new API and bugfixes (python 0.12.0, typescript 1.8.0, go 1.5.2).

Design notes and rationale: Credential consensus: each SDK exposes a short-lived in-memory lease cache with a consensus epoch id. When a renewal is required, the first process to propose a renewal writes a proposal token to the local lease store; others observe the proposal and attach to the resulting token rather than racing. This reduces N-way token swap storms seen in high-concurrency serverless deployments. Stream-sentinel: streaming clients obtain a lightweight sentinel handle that owns heartbeat scheduling and initiates sentinel-heard fallback (switch to fallback credential or model variant) on sustained failures. The sentinel encapsulates abort hooks, recommended backoff profiles, and a visibility layer for observability.

Compatibility and ergonomics: The APIs are additive. Existing constructors gain an optional "credConsensusConfig" (defaults to off for historical parity but enabled in our SDK bundles for Redwood-hosted usage). Stream-sentinel is opt-in via "streamOptions.sentinel: true" for minor releases; the default in this PR for pre-bundled SDKs is enabled to reduce incidents in production. Migration notes are included below.

Testing and QA: Unit tests added for all three SDKs (consensus election, proposal expiry, sentinel failover paths). Integration tests run against a local dev harness that simulates mixed-ttl auth responses and concurrent stream attach/detach. Benchmark run: 2x reduction in auth-exchange rate under 200 concurrent clients in our perf-canary lab; 20% median tail improvement for long-lived streams under error injection. E2E staged rollout: feature-flagged on staging for 48 hours, then progressive rollout to 10%/50%/100% groups controlled by console toggle.

Rollout plan and observability: Feature gated via env var REDWOOD_SDK_CRED_CONSENSUS and REDWOOD_SDK_STREAM_SENTINEL. Console dashboard includes new metrics: sdk.cred.consensus.proposals, sdk.cred.consensus.attach_rate, sdk.stream.sentinel.fallbacks and sdk.stream.sentinel.heartbeat_misses. Alerts: increased sentinel fallback rate >1% triggers P1 channel.

Developer notes: - Python: introduces redwood.session.consensus module and SessionClient.consensus_config. - TypeScript: new CredConsensus class in @redwood/sdk-core and optional stream.sentinel flag on StreamHandle options. - Go: cred/consensus package and StreamSentinel struct with attach semantics. All three SDKs export a small diagnostics hook for troubleshooting (max 8KB JSON).

Upgrade guidance: Non-breaking by default. For teams that already implemented custom token rotation, set REDWOOD_SDK_CRED_CONSENSUS=off and keep existing behavior while validating sentinel in a subset of clients. See UPGRADING.md entries added to each SDK package for code samples.

Security review: This PR went through security review (Mei Chen) to ensure no credential material is persisted to disk and all leases are ephemeral and truncated to KMS-backed keys where present.

Related work: builds on ENG-3421 (reduce auth storms) and ENG-3490 (streaming resilience).
Rafael Ortega (reviewer): The consensus proposal TTL needs to be conservative to avoid single-proposer lockouts in noisy environments. Can we make it adaptive based on svc latency?
Priya K. Menon (author): Agreed. Implemented adaptive TTL that increases with observed auth latency; default remains 250ms but grows up to 2s under heavy auth latency (see consensus.py lines 78-104).
Mei Chen (security): Verified no secrets persisted. Please add a short fuzz test for proposal injection vectors.
Priya K. Menon (author): Added fuzz test in tests/integration/consensus_harness.py and documented attack surface in SECURITY_NOTES.md.
Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Nice. Two nits: (1) rename StreamSentinel.Attempt -> StartAttempt for clarity, (2) add an example to UPGRADING.md showing a streaming handler using sentinel.fallback().
Priya K. Menon (author): Addressed both nits; renamed and added example code snippets in UPGRADING.md for each SDK.
Merged via squash merge by Mei Chen on 2026-03-01. Changelog: 'sdk: cross-sdk credential consensus + stream-sentinel retry profiles; bump versions py 0.12.0 / ts 1.8.0 / go 1.5.2'.
Added cross-language credential consensus to reduce concurrent token exchanges; introduced StreamSentinel to improve streaming resilience and unify retry behavior across SDKs. SDK version bumps: python 0.12.0, typescript 1.8.0, go 1.5.2. Feature gated with environment flags; consult UPGRADING.md for migration steps.
Unit tests (py/ts/go) covering consensus election, TTL adaptation, sentinel failover paths added. Integration harness exercised mixed-ttl auth responses and 200 concurrent stream clients. Perf canary results attached. All CI green after one lint fix iteration.
Coordinate staged rollout with Console team to enable REDWOOD_SDK_CRED_CONSENSUS toggle. Ops should monitor sdk.cred.consensus.proposals and sdk.stream.sentinel.fallbacks during rollout. Inform SRE on first 10% step.

Motivation: production workloads show sustained 10-40% overhead from transient per-request scratch allocations and high fragmentation of GPU workspace under continuous batching. This PR introduces a slab-aware ring allocator that reuses per-GPU workspace across closely-packed requests and a lightweight async eviction heuristic for the KV cache to reduce peak working set. The goal is to lower peak GPU memory and workspace fragmentation without changing public APIs. Design: 1) Ring allocator (runtime/memory): maintain per-device ring of slab segments sized to power-of-two buckets; allocations try to reuse a hot slab if timestamp delta < reuse_window_ms. 2) Slab-awareness for kernels: kernel selection and workspace queries now accept a slab_hint to request contiguous segments and avoid splitting activation scratch. 3) Async KV eviction: background worker performs mild eviction of cold KV entries when projected peak > threshold, with safety margin to avoid cold-start latency spikes. 4) Scheduler integration: continuous batching scheduler pins small batches to existing ring slots to avoid repeated alloc/free for short-lived requests. 5) Telemetry: added fragmentation, slab_reuse_rate, async_evict_count metrics and a per-route workspace histogram. Checklist: - [x] implement ring allocator core - [x] integrate slab_hint into kernel workspace API - [x] add async KV eviction worker with backoff - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] perf microbenchmarks showing memory improvement - [x] rollout plan with feature flag and telemetry guardrails Testing: unit tests for allocator edge cases, e2e perf runs on 8k/4k token streams show peak workspace reduction of ~28% (8k seq) and ~18% (4k seq) across our standard Llama-family models, continuous batching throughput unchanged, median p95 latency within 3% of baseline. Observability: new metrics wired into console dashboards and a short-lived feature flag (mem_allocator_v2) used during canary. Rollout: canary on 10% of requests for 48h, then auto-promote after telemetry check. Risks & mitigations: risk of increased cold KV misses from over-eager eviction; mitigated by conservative thresholds and gradual backoff. Risk of kernel incompatibility with non-contiguous segments; mitigated by slab_hint fallbacks and kernel-level compaction path. Related: ENG-4219, ENG-4301. No public API changes, no customer-visible config changes except opt-in feature flag. See release_notes for details.
Jared Kim (2024-11-08): Nice direction. Two concerns: how do we bound worst-case fragmentation when many large requests arrive? Please add a compaction or fallback to arena allocation.
Maya Patel (2024-11-08): Reply: added a kernel-level compaction path and a fallback to the legacy arena when contiguous allocation fails (see ring_allocator.rs lines ~220-270). Compaction is rare in our perf runs.
Lina Gomez (2024-11-10): Can we make the async eviction thresholds per-tenant? Large enterprise customers may have different working set characteristics.
Maya Patel (2024-11-10): Reply: added a tenant-aware multiplier and a feature flag to enable per-tenant tuning; default remains global conservative thresholds.
Ankit Rao (2024-11-11): Approving after minor nits addressed in tests and added more telemetry for slab_reuse_rate.
CI (2024-11-11): Flaky test test_memory_fragmentation intermittent failure on first run; rerun passed.
Release Engineer (2024-11-12): Verified feature flag gating and rollout plan; ok to squash-merge.
Reduced peak per-request GPU workspace by ~28% on 8k-seq workloads and ~18% on 4k-seq. Introduces slab-aware ring allocator, slab_hint kernel integration, and an async KV cache eviction heuristic. Adds telemetry: slab_reuse_rate, workspace_histogram, async_evict_count. Rollout is behind mem_allocator_v2 feature flag. No public API changes.

Motivation: Our tri-SDK ergonomics diverged again after incremental fixes to async streaming and auth rotation. This PR standardizes the call surface for generation/chat/stream APIs across Python, TypeScript, and Go, centralizes retry/backoff presets (optimistic, conservative, throughput-aware), and applies a set of parity fixes discovered during cross-SDK smoke tests. Summary of changes is below.

What changed (high level):
- Introduce a compact retry Preset registry (Presets: optimistic, balanced, conservative) implemented in each SDK with matching semantics and telemetry hooks.
- Harmonize streaming call signatures: stream responses now expose the same iterator/async iterator names, error shapes, and heartbeat/close semantics across languages. Python: AsyncGenerator compatible with 'aiter_tokens()' helper; TS: AsyncIterable with 'streamTokens()' helper; Go: channel-based StreamToken iterator with Close() symmetry.
- Centralize auth handshake behavior: SDKs will attempt soft-refresh once per request on token expiry error, using the same retry predicate and backoff window.
- Small ergonomics: unify parameter names (timeout -> deadline_ms internally; retry -> retry_preset), flatten nested options for common use cases, and provide explicit migration notes.
- Tests and examples: added crosslang smoke harness and three sample notebooks/apps demonstrating parity.

Why this is different: instead of only copying shapes, this refactor extracts the retry policy definitions into a language-agnostic spec in the repo (docs/sdk/retry-presets.md) and implements concise SDK adapters that match the spec so behavior is reproducible across environments and easier to maintain.

Checklist: 
- [x] Spec doc for retry presets and stream semantics (docs/sdk/retry-presets.md)
- [x] Python implementation and minor API shim for backwards compatibility (packages/python/redwood_sdk/*)
- [x] TypeScript implementation and deprecation warnings (packages/typescript/redwood-sdk/*)
- [x] Go implementation with examples (packages/go/redwood-sdk/*)
- [x] Crosslang smoke tests and CI matrix entry
- [x] Changelogs and migration notes

Commits summary: see commits field below for compact list.

Changed areas (high level):
- packages/python/redwood_sdk/core/retry.py (new Preset registry and telemetry hooks)
- packages/python/redwood_sdk/streaming/async_stream.py (stream adapter and iterator helpers)
- packages/typescript/redwood-sdk/src/retry/presets.ts (matching presets and typed docstrings)
- packages/typescript/redwood-sdk/src/stream/streamAdapter.ts (async iterable helpers)
- packages/go/redwood-sdk/internal/retry/presets.go (preset registry and tests)
- packages/go/redwood-sdk/stream/stream.go (StreamToken iterator and Close semantics)
- docs/sdk/retry-presets.md (spec + examples)
- examples/tri-sdk-stream-mirror/* (three example apps)
- tests/integration/sdk-parity/* (smoke harness)

Notes on compatibility: For most users the surface should be compatible; we preserved older helpers but added clear deprecation warnings in TS (console) and Python (warnings.warn). Go retains current constructor signatures but introduces an options flattening helper NewClientWithDefaults(opts) that is recommended. Migration notes are in packages/*/CHANGELOG.md.

Risk assessment and mitigations:
- Risk: subtle difference in error shapes from streaming layer. Mitigation: added a mapping layer per SDK that normalizes errors (see packages/*/stream/error_map.go|py|ts).
- Risk: flaky crosslang CI. Mitigation: smoke tests run in a separate matrix and have retry on infra flakiness; temporary allowlist for known ephemeral failures.

Manual testing performed: tri-sdk parity run against local staging model, smoke stream tests with long-lived connections (30m), token-expiry simulation and soft-refresh checks, and example apps executed end-to-end.

References: Linear ENG-1042, ENG-1108; incident notes SUP-3482 (auth rotation flakiness).
Polish SDK call signatures across Python/TS/Go, add stable backoff presets and parity fixes; bump SDK minor versions (py 1.8.0, ts 2.3.1, go 1.5.0). No public API breaking changes expected for typical usage; migration notes included in changelogs.

Adds presubmit CI spend quotas, a lightweight dependency categorizer used by dep-bot to prioritize updates, and a rollout plan for canary and org-wide enablement. No user-facing API changes.
Motivation: Presubmit CI spend has been growing steadily as more teams enable full integration suites on every PR. This PR introduces two coordinated features: (1) a configurable presubmit cost quota system that estimates the expected CI spend per PR and enforces a soft quota to reduce wastey runs, and (2) a dependency categorizer service that tags third-party dependencies as stable, frequent, or volatile to inform dep-bot behavior and presubmit test selection. Changes are aimed at reducing CI cost (SLO: 20% reduction in unnecessary longtest runs) while keeping fast feedback for developers.
Design summary:
- Presubmit cost quota: a lightweight estimator (runner-second + cache-miss heuristic) attached to the presubmit planner. We compute an "estimated_ci_units" per PR at intake and surface it in the GitHub checks summary. Repos can specify per-team default quotas in .ci/config.yaml and override per-branch. If a PR exceeds the quota, the presubmit runner demotes long, non-blocking tests to a deferred lane and annotates the PR with quota details and a link to request a one-time quota bump.
- Dependency categorizer: a small service and build-time classifier that samples manifest changes (package.json / go.mod / pyproject.toml) across the monorepo and historical update frequency + CVE signals to assign categories: stable (rare updates, low churn), frequent (regular updates, active maintainers), volatile (rapid releases or high-security churn). Dep-bot uses the category to schedule automatic patch updates for stable deps, prioritized review for volatile, and aggregated rollups for frequent.
Implementation highlights:
- New presubmit estimator module (golang) integrated into the presubmit orchestrator and the GitHub composite action.
- .ci/config.yaml schema extended with 'presubmit_quota_units' and 'quota_behavior' (soft_warn, demote_longtests, block). Default: soft_warn.
- Dependency categorizer service (python) with a lightweight SQLite cache for signals (we avoided heavy infra to simplify rollout).
- Dep-bot adaptation: changes to the dependency update scheduling module so it reads categorizer labels and uses an updated backoff strategy.
- UI: GitHub check summary and a small presubmit-cost badge in the PR header.
Testing & rollout:
- Unit tests for estimator and categorizer added; integration tests run in the harness.
- Canary rollout to the "perf-canary" org for 48 hours: we ran ~250 PRs, observed a 24% reduction in longtest executions for PRs flagged over quota.
- Gradual enablement via feature flag: default off for teams; enable by setting .ci/config.yaml.
- Rollback path: feature flag off and revert presubmit planner config; quick patch to remove estimator if issues observed.
CI and checks:
- All CI checks passed in the canary runs (lint, unit, presubmit-sim, smoke-run).
- We added a short CI job "ci/quota-smoke" that validates estimator outputs for changed paths on PRs.
Migration notes:
- Teams with bespoke presubmit wiring will need to add the estimator shim (two-line change).
- Dep-bot config has a new optional field 'categorizer_policy' for teams that want to opt out.
Related work: ENG-1543 (presubmit-costs initiative), PM-987 (dep-bot prioritization).
Commands to exercise locally:
- make presubmit-estimate PATH=path/to/changed/files
- python tools/dep_categorizer/run.py --sample 100
Operational runbook (short):
- If estimator spikes unexpectedly, set override in .ci/config.yaml to avoid demotion, investigate via /ops/ci-quota-traces.
- Categorizer health: ensure sqlite cache not corrupted; small repair tool included.
Why this is different: prior PRs focused on CI job sharding, caching, and presubmit fastpaths. This PR ties explicit cost estimation to gating decisions and pairs it with dependency signals to make automated updates less noisy.
Marco: Please add unit tests for the cache expiry behavior in the categorizer (resolved: added tests and refactored cache TTL).
Evelyn: Can we surface the estimated_ci_units as a numeric metric for SLO dashboards? (resolved: exposed metric via prom gateway, added note in docs).
Darius: Request to make quota_behavior configurable per-branch; addressed by adding branch override in config and test coverage.
payload.title: Introduce presubmit cost quotas and dependency categorizer

payload.body:
Motivation: We observe recurring throughput regressions on MQA workloads for Llama-family models when sequence-length variance and multi-query attention interact with our default kernel selection. Two measurable pain points: (1) frequent small KV cache misses when token generations cross stripe boundaries, and (2) suboptimal kernel tiling choices for planar weight layouts that some Qwen/Mistral/Llama variants expose. This PR adds a lightweight stripe-prefetch scheduler and a planar-kernel routing heuristic that picks kernels based on observed layout and upcoming stripe patterns.

Summary of changes (single-line list): stripe-prefetch scheduler, planar kernel router, small scheduler API additions, new microbench harness for stripe workloads, unit+integration tests, documentation for tuning knobs.

What the patch does (detailed): The stripe-prefetch scheduler tracks the active KV stripe window for each session and enqueues prefetches for the next N stripes when continuous-batching is used and the workload matches MQA characteristics (multi-head quantized attention with per-head stride > 1). Prefetching is conservative: it is only issued when the current latency SLO isn't filling and when memory pressure estimator indicates a <15% overhead risk. The planar-kernel router adds a lightweight feature extractor that scores candidate kernels using (1) the weight memory layout (planar vs packed), (2) sequence length percentile, and (3) runtime tile fit (L2/L3 footprints). The router falls back to existing kernel routing for unknown/rare layouts.

APIs and config: two new config flags under runtime.tuning: runtime.tuning.stripe_prefetch.enabled (default true), runtime.tuning.stripe_prefetch.max_prefetch_stripes (default 2), runtime.tuning.planar_router.enabled (default true), and runtime.tuning.planar_router.score_threshold (default 0.12). These defaults were chosen after microbench tuning across common GPU families.

Benchmarks: Microbench harness (bench/stripe_mqa_harness) runs a 4k-16k token mix with 8-shot prompt patterns. On A100-40GB we measured: throughput +19% (p50 for batching throughput) for MQA-Llama-70B-quant profile, +12% for MQA-Mistral-7B in mixed-length traces. Median latency change at p50 was +1.8ms (within SLO) and p99 shifted by +6ms in worst cases when prefetching hit memory pressure; the policy prevented >10% p99 regressions in tuned settings. More details in commits.

Compatibility: Non-breaking by default. Flags can be switched off. Prefetch is session-scoped so cold-start behavior unchanged. We added a fallback to current kernel chooser if the new heuristics produce a score below threshold.

Testing: Unit tests for scheduler logic and router scoring (tests/runtime/test_stripe_prefetch.py, tests/runtime/test_planar_router.py), integration tests that run end-to-end generated traffic in the bench container (CI job bench/stripe-mqa), and a stress run that validated memory pressure gating.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc & perf plan discussed in ENG-4321
- [x] Microbench results checked in bench/outputs
- [x] Unit & integration tests added
- [x] Runtime flags exposed and documented
- [x] Backwards-compatible defaults

Related: PRs that touched kernel routing previously (see refs in commits). Linked support ticket SUP-1182 where a customer reported repeated stalls on Llama-MQA workloads.

Notes for reviewers: focus on (a) correctness of memory-pressure gating, (b) potential contention with existing batching path, (c) kernel routing thresholds. Perf graphs and raw numbers are in bench/outputs/38421/*.
- Add stripe-prefetch scheduler to reduce KV cache thrash for MQA workloads.
- Introduce planar-kernel router heuristics for memory-layout-aware kernel selection.
- Improved continuous batching behavior when token-length variance is high for Llama family models.
Ravi Kumar: can you justify the default max_prefetch_stripes=2? We saw marginal gains beyond 2 but risk higher memory use.
S. Ortiz: We ran grid search across 0-4 stripes; 2 gives best median throughput with acceptable memory on A100/RTX6000. I added bench/outputs/38421/prefetch_grid.csv to show this.

Elena Park: The router scoring is neat but I'm worried about cost of scoring per-request. Can we cache scores per model-version?
S. Ortiz: yes — we add a per-model-version score cache with LRU expiry (30 minutes) in commit 5 which addresses this.

Jonas Meyer: I hit a race on high concurrency where prefetch queue could be double-enqueued; fixed in last commit.

R. Kumar: Approved after the race fix and addition of the LRU score cache.
Elena Park: Approved.

Monitoring: Added perf alert rule 'mqa.stripe_prefetch_mem_pressure' (alerts when prefetch gated >30% of sessions and p99 latency increased >10%). We'll monitor for 2 weeks.
Rollback: flip runtime.tuning.stripe_prefetch.enabled=false if any widespread issues.
Owners: @samantha, @ravi_kumar
payload.title: stripe prefetch + planar kernel router: MQA/Llama throughput optimizations

Context and motivation: multiple internal and customer tickets called out repeated auth initialization and duplicated credential-warming code across examples and SDKs. This PR introduces a lightweight, opt-in 'credential bootloader' used by SDK entry points and examples to: 1) perform ambient credential priming (KMS/KV cache warmup) before first request, 2) optionally pre-open streaming channels with a shallow noop handshake to reduce first-stream latency, and 3) provide a small, well-documented helper API to wire credential refresh hooks into existing retry/backoff profiles. The change targets parity and ergonomics across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs while keeping public APIs stable (no breaking change).

What this PR does (summary):
- Add SDK-level helper: Bootloader.start(credentials, options) with per-language ergonomic wrappers (Python context-manager, TS async init, Go Bootloader.StartWithContext).
- Add generator/adapter utilities: TS provide createGeneratorStream(adapter) that returns an async generator compatible with existing docs; Py provides generator_adapter to convert streaming responses into async generators with built-in reauth hooks; Go adds StreamOperator helper to simplify io.ReadCloser-like stream consumption.
- Wire bootloader into example quickstarts and test harness to demonstrate reduced first-request latency.
- Add new integration tests that exercise warmup paths and stream resume under token rotation.
- Docs: update quickstarts and SDK migration notes; add a short recipe on when to opt into bootloader vs. lazy auth.

Checklist (checked): [x] design doc linked (ENG-9082), [x] unit + integration tests added, [x] example quickstarts updated, [x] API stability review completed, [x] release notes drafted.

Commits (high level):
- 7c9a2b0: initial bootloader scaffolding and crosslang spec (design comments inline)
- 8f1d3e4: python bootloader context manager + generator_adapter implementation + tests
- b1a7c8d: typescript createGeneratorStream adapter + examples + TS types
- d3e5f11: go compact session factory and StreamOperator helper + e2e test harness changes
- e9d2f44: docs and quickstart updates; release notes
- f0a4b55: fix flaky test by adding jitter to warmup backoff; CI retry fixes

Changed areas/files (illustrative, not exhaustive):
- sdk/python/redwood/bootloader.py (new)
- sdk/python/redwood/streaming/generator_adapter.py (new)
- sdk/typescript/src/bootloader.ts (new)
- sdk/typescript/src/streaming/generator_adapter.ts (new)
- sdk/go/bootloader/bootloader.go (new)
- sdk/go/stream/stream_operator.go (new)
- examples/quickstarts/auth_warmup/* (updated)
- docs/sdk/bootloader.md (new)
- tests/integration/test_stream_warmup.py (new)

Small snippet (Python context-manager wrapper):
"""with Bootloader.start(credentials, warmup=True) as bl:
    client = Client.from_bootloader(bl)
    async for chunk in client.stream(...):
        handle(chunk)
"""

Review conversation (summary, chronological, inline comments preserved in description):
- Jason Nguyen (reviewer): "High level — I like the bootloader idea. Two asks: 1) ensure all warmup behaviour is opt-in and clearly default-off, 2) please ensure the TS adapter preserves backpressure semantics."
- Elena (author): "Agree, defaults are opt-in. Updated TS adapter to return an async generator that awaits downstream pulls to preserve backpressure; added tests that assert we don't prefetch more than N frames."
- Priya Patel (reviewer): "In Python, the contextmanager API looks good but curious about interaction with existing credential hooks — does Bootloader register to the central credential registry?"
- Elena: "Yes — Bootloader accepts a CredentialProvider instance. By default it will use the SDK global provider, but callers can pass an explicit provider. I expanded the docs to clarify recommended usage for services with rotated tokens."
- Liam O'Connor (reviewer): "Go API is idiomatic but change to StartWithContext(ctx, opts) would make cancellations clearer."
- Elena: "Done — renamed helper and added tests for cancellation halfway through warmup."
- Michael Tan (approver): "Tests and docs look good. Approving if CI passes and flaky test is addressed."

CI and test notes: initial CI run failed a flaky e2e when running warmup concurrently on CI runners (test_stream_warmup.py::test_concurrent_warmup) — failure reproduced locally with race in the test harness. Fixed by adding jitter and consolidating the shared temporary directory setup. Final CI run: all checks green (unit, lint, typecheck, e2e warmup). CI summary: unit tests: pass, integration: pass, linters: pass, typechecks (TS/Py): pass.

Backward compatibility and ergonomics: Public client surfaces are unchanged; Bootloader is opt-in and documented as an advanced performance tool for high-latency environments or low-latency streaming start. The generator/stream adapters are additive helpers that simplify typical patterns in examples; we updated the quickstarts to prefer the adapter-based pattern for readability.

Alternative approaches considered: 1) fully automatic warmup on SDK import (rejected because it is surprising and heavy for serverless cold starts), 2) expose low-level warmup primitives only (rejected because it repeated boilerplate in each language). Bootloader is a compromise: small, explicit, and easily mocked in tests.

Post-merge actions and follow-ups:
- Coordinate with SDK maintainers to cherry-pick ergonomic wrappers into backport branches (ENG-9120).
- Monitor first-request latency on canary customers that opt in during the next two release cycles; add metric for 'bootstrap_latency_ms' in Redwood Console (follow-up PR).
- Draft a short blog post / migration note for customers with streaming-heavy workloads.

Merge outcome: Squash-merge to main. Changelog entry added under SDKs for v2.2.0.

If you want to validate locally: run tests in SDK directories (python -m pytest sdk/python tests/integration --filter warmup) and (cd sdk/typescript && yarn test -i) and (cd sdk/go && go test ./... -run Warmup).
Introduce a cross-SDK 'credential bootloader' to reduce auth boilerplate; add ergonomic generator/async-iterator adapters for TS/Py and a compact session factory for Go; bump SDK example versions to v2.2.0; no breaking API changes to public client surfaces.
Author ran a small local benchmark showing median first-stream latency reduced by ~18% when using bootloader in a 12 concurrent client profile. Benchmarks are small-scale and included in the PR as artifacts.
payload.title: Streamlined credential bootloader and generator adapter: reduce SDK auth boilerplate + ergonomic stream factories (v2.2.0)

Summary: This PR adds a binding inheritance guard to RBACv2, introduces a lightweight KMS provenance header (X-KMS-Origin-Chain) surfaced through the gateway, and a small audit consolidator used by the audit-forwarder to deduplicate events coming from chained proxies. Motivation: We observed two related classes of compliance gaps in multi-zone customers: (1) operator/service bindings that unintentionally inherited privileges when tenant objects were copied across geozone boundaries and (2) duplicated/misaligned audit entries from edge proxies that obscured key provenance. The changes here are intended to close those gaps with minimal disruption and a staged rollout. What changed (high level): - rbac/policy-compiler: add BindingInheritanceGuard module. The guard enforces that operator/service role bindings cannot be transitively inherited across geozone boundaries unless an explicit 'inherit: true' attribute exists on the target namespace and the tenancy claim includes an allowlist. - gateway/proxy: attach X-KMS-Origin-Chain header (comma-separated list of key-region:provider entries) to internal KMS calls and to outgoing audit envelopes when present. The header is signed by the gateway's operator key when crossing zone boundaries. - audit/forwarder: introduce AuditConsolidator which deduplicates events using (trace_id, request_id, key_provenance_hash) and tags consolidated events with provenance-summary for downstream retention/policy. - admission controller: validate new binding attributes on create/update and reject suspicious cross-zone binds in enforced mode. - policy migration: tooling to scan and annotate namespaces with 'inherit' flags and produce a remediation report. - tests: unit and integration tests for guard, header propagation tests under fault injection, and end-to-end audit consolidation test harness. Rollout plan: 1) Shadow mode (default): BindingInheritanceGuard runs in 'observe' mode, emitting structured telemetry to SLO/alerts and adding findings to the policy-migration report. 2) Canary enforcement: enable enforcement in a small set of non-production tenants for 72h. 3) Gradual opt-in: expose a tenant opt-in flag and run a migration job to annotate safe namespaces. 4) Full enforcement: after 4 weeks of canaries and zero high-severity findings, flip default to 'reject' for newly created cross-zone binding attempts. Backwards compatibility: X-KMS-Origin-Chain is optional. Old gateways without the header continue to operate; the consolidator treats missing provenance as 'unknown' and only applies dedupe heuristics with reduced confidence. Security review notes: The header is canonicalized and signed to avoid tampering; gateway signs using operator's zone key. Audit envelopes containing provenance are stored with a provenance hash to simplify forensic queries. Related work: references ENG-2247 (rbac policy hygiene) and ENG-4902 (kms provenance telemetry). See also SUP-78 (support ticket documenting customer incident). Migration steps included in the PR ensure we do not inadvertently block legitimate operator workflows. The description below includes the checklist and a short runbook for rollback. Checklist: - [x] Policy compiler change unit tests - [x] Gateway header propagation integration tests - [x] Audit consolidate integration tests - [x] Admission controller rejection tests - [x] Migration scanning tool and dry-run report - [x] Documentation updates (RBACv2 policy guide + operational runbook) Runbook (quick): - To disable enforcement quickly set ENV RBAC_BINDING_GUARD_MODE=observe on policy-compiler service and feature flag redwood.rbac.binding_guard=false in config-service. - To remove header propagation set GATEWAY_DISABLE_KMS_PROVENANCE=true and restart canaries. - To revert audit consolidation, flip AUDIT_CONSOLIDATOR_ENABLED=false and reprocess queued envelopes.
Introduce a guard to prevent cross-geozone inheritance of operator bindings, add X-KMS-Origin-Chain for provenance verification, and consolidate audit events to remove duplication across proxies. Backwards-compatible rollout with shadowing and gradual enforcement.
Diego Alvarez: Can you clarify the canonicalization algorithm for X-KMS-Origin-Chain? I want to ensure signing is deterministic across gateways.
Author (Maya Chen): We canonicalize entries as region:provider:keyid sorted lexicographically, then join by comma. The signature is over the canonical string plus request_id. Added comments and unit tests (see gateway/kms/provenance_test.go).
Priya Natarajan: Admissions rejection path looks strict — do we have an escape hatch for operator teams during migration?
Author (Maya Chen): Yes. The admission controller respects RBAC_BINDING_GUARD_MODE env which defaults to observe. We've added a tenant opt-in flag and a CLI remediation tool to annotate namespaces; noted in the docs.
Samir Patel: Audit consolidator dedupe key uses a combined hash; we should include a TTL window in the consolidator to avoid long-term collisions.
Maya Chen: Added TTL window 10m in consolidator and made it configurable via AUDIT_CONSOLIDATOR_TTL. Updated tests to cover timing edge cases.
Diego Alvarez: Approved after provenance canonicalization and signature tests were added.
Priya Natarajan: Approved with comment to monitor canary metrics for 72h.
Samir Patel: Left a minor comments fix which was addressed (naming and log level).
payload.title: Add binding inheritance guard and geo-key provenance header

Context: Dedicated customers observed P95 latency spikes during short high-frequency bursts that consumed warm-pool headroom and caused aggressive preemption of committed capacity; this PR introduces a Capacity Leasebook and a Throttle Harmonizer to smooth those microbursts and preserve long-running throughput guarantees. Motivation: decouple short-lived burst reservations from sustained commitments so that priority tenants see consistent throughput while still allowing opportunistic short bursts. High-level changes: new leasebook controller that issues timeboxed 'leases' for burst capacity; soft-lease arbitration algorithm (probabilistic decay + runway smoothing) to avoid synchronized drain; harmonizer in scheduler that computes gentle per-tenant throttles when short-lease utilization exceeds configured runway thresholds; telemetry for per-lease lifespan histograms, preemption counts, effective throughput by commit window, and headroom pressure signals. Rollout plan: feature-flagged (config.redwood.enableLeasebook=false by default), opt-in migration tool for existing reservations, canary on 10% of Dedicated clusters, full rollout after 2 weeks if no regressions. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (internal) and linear tickets referenced; - [x] unit tests for lease allocator and harmonizer; - [x] deterministic integration test for preemption/backoff scenarios; - [x] load tests showing P50/P95 SLO improvement for committed tenants; - [x] console metrics and dashboards updated; - [ ] staged rollout recipe applied to production fleets. Commits summary: 1) Add leasebook controller, CRD, and api types (6 files) 2) Implement soft-lease allocator and decay policy with tunables (3 files) 3) Integrate harmonizer with scheduler decision path + tests (4 files) 4) Add telemetry hooks, dashboards, and migration script (3 files) 5) Docs, changelog, and rollout notes (2 files). Changed areas (high level): pkg/controller/leasebook/*, pkg/scheduler/harmonizer.go, pkg/scheduler/decision.go (throttle hooks), pkg/telemetry/lease_metrics.go, deploy/helm/values.dedicated.yaml (feature flag), tools/migrate-reservations.sh, docs/dedicated/leasebook.md. Test plan and CI: initial CI run flagged a flaky util test (util/alloc_test) at first; reran unit and integration suites; all checks green on second run; e2e burst load validated on a 4-node Dedicated canary (results attached in PR CI artifacts). Review conversation summary: "Rohit Singh: please bound per-lease memory to avoid unbounded metadata growth;" -> "Author: added a bounded ring for short-lived leases and unit test exercising high churn;" "Lena Ortiz: add tenant and reservation tags to metrics for easier pivoting in console;" -> "Author: added tenant_id and reservation_type labels and updated dashboards;" "Ben Carter: can you provide a canary rollout recipe and rollback plan?" -> "Author: included canary recipe and automatic-disable hook, plus migration script that is idempotent;" Approvals: Rohit and Lena approved after requested changes implemented; Ben approved after canary notes. CI status: pass (lint/unit/integration/e2e). Merge: squash-and-merge by Maya Chen after approvals and green CI; merge commit: abcdef1. Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the default flag off to avoid surprise behavior for existing Dedicated customers; telemetry keys are versioned so downstream alerts won't break on rollout.
Rohit Singh: please bound per-lease memory to avoid unbounded metadata (resolved in allocator.go with bounded ring)
Lena Ortiz: prefer tenant_id and reservation_type tags on metrics for easy console pivot (added to lease_metrics)
Ben Carter: include canary rollout recipe and an automatic-disabling safegate (added tools/migrate-reservations.sh and deploy notes)
CI Bot: initial util/alloc_test failed (flaky) - rerun triggered and passed
Introduce Capacity Leasebook and Throttle Harmonizer: opt-in feature to stabilize Dedicated throughput under microbursts. Adds new CRD and scheduler harmonizer, configurable decay and runway parameters, and telemetry for lease lifecycles and preemption. Default off; requires staged rollout.

Motivation: We've seen frequent operator confusion during RBACv2 rollouts where small policy edits have unexpected residency or KMS consent implications. This PR delivers three developer/operator-facing tools to reduce rollout risk: 1) an RBACv2 diff tool (CLI + optional HTTP service) that highlights semantic changes (role inheritance, constraint changes, region/zone pins) instead of raw YAML diffs; 2) an offline KMS consent simulator that performs a dry-run of policy evaluations against a configurable set of tenant/residency scenarios and emits consent decisions and suggested fallbacks; 3) an audit sanity checker that scans request/ingest traces to detect missing audit headers, non-deterministic audit ordering, and probable replay windows. Summary of changes: - tools/rbac-diff: CLI and lightweight server with a policy-normalizer and semantic comparison engine. Produces structured reports with severity and suggested remediation steps. - tools/kms-consent-sim: Python-based simulator for local dev and CI that can replay historical requests against new policy sets to surface consent failures. - pkg/audit: added sanity_check.go with heuristics for missing immutable headers, duplicate sequence IDs, and anomalous timestamp skews; added lightweight auto-mitigation advisory generator. - pkg/policy/linter: RBACv2-specific lints for region pinning, tenant-scoped KMS usage, and operator-scoped role templates. - docs/security: onboarding guide for using the diff tool and simulator during canary rollouts and post-incident triage. Testing and rollout: unit + integration tests included; demo Canary run executed in staging against a production-like policy bundle; CI initially reported flaky integration tests (flaky DB transaction timing) which were fixed by adding a deterministic policy seed and a retry wrapper. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-3421) [x] unit tests added [x] integration tests added [x] security review requested (SEC-1187) [x] docs updated [x] staged canary performed in staging and observed no regressions Related work: this PR complements the policy-simulator work (ENG-2980) and the residency telemetry plumbing (ENG-3199). Migration notes: operators should run the RBAC diff against each release candidate and optionally run the KMS consent simulator against a sample of tenant policies prior to canary. The audit sanity checker is safe to enable in passive mode initially; it only emits advisories and does not block traffic. Linear/Jira: ENG-3421, SEC-1187, SUP-4129. Merge: squash merge after final approvals.
Add RBACv2 policy diffing utility (CLI + service), an offline KMS consent simulator for dry-running residency and consent checks, and an audit sanity checker that flags missing immutable headers and replay anomalies.
Ethan Kim: Nice work. Can the diff tool detect transitive deny rules? Please add a unit to cover that edge case.
Priya Narayanan: Added a transitive-deny detector and test (see commit c3d4f0a). The detector flags suspected indirect denies and includes a trace sample.
Liu Zhang: Integration test was failing in CI due to non-deterministic policy ordering. Recommend normalizing policy list before diffing.
Priya Narayanan: Normalization added in normalize.go; integration CI rerun is green.
Marisol Ortega: Security review: simulator looks fine but ensure simulated decisions never get logged with tenant PII. Confirmed simulator strips tenant identifiers by default.
Marisol Ortega: Approve after PII guard verified.

Background and motivation: we continue to see production cases where SSE fragments carrying partial JSON payloads interleave with heartbeat or tooling events and the existing delimiter heuristics misattribute trailing bytes, causing downstream JSON parse errors or function-call boundary loss. This PR introduces a stream synchronizer that (1) assigns per-connection event watermarks to detect sequence discontinuities, (2) realigns split delimiter-like byte sequences using a small rolling buffer, and (3) introduces an optional boundary-escape token to guarantee delimiter disambiguation for edge-case payloads. The change is conservative and feature-flagged so we can toggle behavior during rollout.

What this PR does: - New package: services/api/streaming/synchronizer.go implements a lightweight state machine for per-connection reassembly using watermarks and a rolling tail buffer. - SSE adapter updates: adapters/openai/sse_adapter.go uses the synchronizer to reframe incoming fragments before the JSON reassembler runs; this decouples framing concerns from JSON parsing. - SDK adjustments: sdk/ts/streaming-client.ts adapts the client-side stream parser to be tolerant of the escape token and to emit a new metadata field (event_index) used by observability. - Tests: services/api/streaming/synchronizer_test.go adds targeted unit tests for out-of-order fragments, partial-delimiter scenarios, and stress path for high-frequency heartbeat interleaving. - Docs: docs/compat/streaming-boundary.md documents the escape token format, the feature-flag, and rollout guidance for customers migrating from older streaming behavior. - Changelog entry and small CI script additions for a fuzz harness used in nightly e2e runs.

Compatibility and rollout: - Default behavior is backward compatible: the synchronizer is enabled under feature flag rts.stream_synchronizer=true. When disabled, the system behaves exactly as before. - The escape token is optional; existing clients do not need to emit it. When used, it removes ambiguity for binary or text payloads that include delimiter-like sequences. - Observability: new metrics (stream.sync.realigns, stream.sync.replay_needed, stream.sync.watermark_gaps) and a new event_index property are emitted for debugging.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests cover 98% of the synchronizer logic paths. - Integration tests run the adapter + runtime on a mini-cluster with a fuzz harness that replays truncated/merged fragments; CI showed an initial non-deterministic failure in e2e which was fixed by tightening the flush window. - Performance impact is negligible: the synchronizer keeps per-connection memory bounded (rolling buffer < 512 bytes) and adds a small CPU cost only during misaligned fragment events.

Checklist: - [x] Implement synchronizer and adapter integration - [x] Add unit and integration tests - [x] Add docs and changelog - [x] Feature-flag gating - [x] Observability hooks - [x] E2E fuzz harness and CI green

Related: ENG-4021 (stream stability epic), ENG-4072 (openai-compat adapter improvements). Links: internal runbook: https://linear.internal/ENG-4021, design doc: https://docs.internal/streaming-sync-design (internal).
Ravi Mehta: please add a comment on memory bounds for long-lived connections.
Author (Elena Park): added a bounded rolling buffer with a hard cap of 512 bytes and a circuit that triggers a replay if accumulated fragments exceed 4KB without a delimiter (tunable via config).
Sofia Alvarez: can we avoid changing the public SDK contract? The added event_index could break some downstream consumers.
Author: event_index is emitted as optional metadata; existing payloads remain unchanged. Updated SDK docs to emphasize optionality.
Jordan Liu: observed one e2e failure where heartbeat burst caused a false-positive replay.
Author: tightened the flush window and added a debounce so short bursts don't force replay. Added new unit test to assert stability under heartbeat bursts.
Ravi Mehta: CI looks good; approve after addressing minor linter note.
Sofia Alvarez: approving.
Merge: squash and merge after approvals.

This PR adds the read-only API surface for Optimization Config versioning: list versions (with filters + pagination), fetch version details, and retrieve diffs between versions. These endpoints are required for the Console history/timeline and the upcoming safe-apply workflow, and they are also used by internal automation (release tooling / incident response) to quickly answer “what config is active for tenant/model/region?” and “what changed between v12 and v13?”. Scope: hosted + dedicated control-plane APIs (private installer/helm wiring will land separately). Non-goals: create/apply/promote/rollback are not included here; this PR is strictly read-only + diff retrieval and enforces RBAC. API additions: (1) Public (customer/admin) endpoints under /v1/optimize/configs: GET /v1/optimize/configs/{config_id}/versions?scope=...&limit=...&cursor=... returns immutable version metadata sorted by created_at desc; GET /v1/optimize/configs/{config_id}/versions/{version_id} returns the full version record including validated schema, semantic warnings (if any), and resolved scope; GET /v1/optimize/configs/{config_id}/versions/diff?from={version_id}&to={version_id} returns a structured diff with “risky fields” annotations for Console highlighting. (2) Internal endpoints under /internal/optimize/configs for ops tooling include an additional query param include_deleted=true and return internal-only fields (storage IDs, writer actor IDs) gated by internal auth. Behavior notes: - Pagination uses an opaque cursor (base64-encoded keyset token). - The list endpoint supports filters: tenant_id, model_id, region, status (draft/validated/active/rolled_back), and time range (created_after/before). - Diff endpoint uses the same canonicalization logic as the validator to avoid noisy diffs (e.g., defaulted fields). - RBAC: requires optimize.config_versions.read for list/get/diff. Internal endpoints require redwood.internal plus optimize.config_versions.read. - Audit: this PR does NOT emit audit events (read-only), but it does attach request_id and actor to structured logs for traceability. Example (public) list response (abridged): {"items":[{"version_id":"ocv_01J...","created_at":"2025-12-01T19:22:11Z","created_by":"user_...","status":"validated","scope":{"tenant_id":"t_123","model_id":"m_llama3_70b","region":"us-east"},"summary":{"batching":{"max_batch_tokens":8192},"cache":{"prefix_cache":true},"quantization":{"profile":"q8_2025_11_30"}}}],"next_cursor":"eyJrZXkiOiJvY3ZfMDFKLi4uIn0="}. Console requirements covered: stable ordering, ability to fetch full config payload for a version, and a deterministic diff output for the diff view. Tests included: handler unit tests (authz + filtering + pagination), API contract tests (OpenAPI snapshot), and diff canonicalization tests. Follow-ups: create/apply endpoints (ENG-4824/4825) will reuse the same response types and pagination helpers; we should consider adding ETag support once Console caching is wired.
Ethan Park: Can we confirm the version_id is globally unique and not scoped to config_id? We need stable identifiers for rollback references later. Also please ensure the list ordering is strictly keyset-based to avoid duplicate/missing items under concurrent writes.
Benji Okafor (author): Yes — version_id is the primary key (ocv_*) and globally unique. I updated pagination to use (created_at, version_id) keyset and the cursor is an opaque encoded tuple. Added tests for concurrent insert between pages.
Jordan Lee: RBAC looks mostly right, but the internal endpoints are returning created_by_actor_id even when the caller is a customer with internal flag off. Please double-check that internal-only fields are guarded server-side, not just hidden in OpenAPI.
Benji Okafor (author): Good catch. I split the serializers: PublicVersionDTO vs InternalVersionDTO and the internal route uses a separate mapper behind authorizeInternal(). Added regression tests to assert actor_id is never present in v1 responses.
Chloe Martin: For Console, we need a single endpoint to fetch diff + both summaries so we can render the header without additional round trips. Can the diff response include from_version and to_version metadata (created_at, created_by, status, scope)?
Benji Okafor (author): Added from/to metadata blocks to diff response (same fields as list items). This keeps the diff endpoint self-contained. Updated OpenAPI examples accordingly.
Felix Schneider: Diff output is a little noisy when a field is omitted vs explicitly set to default. Can we canonicalize defaults before diffing so the UI doesn't highlight non-changes?
Benji Okafor (author): Implemented canonicalization using the schema defaulting logic (same as validation path) before diff. Added tests for omitted->default equivalence.
Marcus Lin: Please ensure request logging does not include the full config payload (may include customer-specific routing hints later). Also confirm error messages don’t leak internal IDs.
Benji Okafor (author): Logging now includes version_id/config_id and scope only; payload is redacted. Error messages return ocv_* and config_id only, not numeric DB IDs. Added a negative test for 404/403 body.
Ethan Park: Looks good after the cursor change + serializer split. Approved.
Chloe Martin: Approved — meets Console requirements. Thank you for adding metadata to diff response.
Marcus Lin: Approved with note: revisit ETag/caching once Console wires this to reduce control-plane read load.

Context: As part of the provision-to-ready automation sprint we need to enable the new orchestration + validation flow gradually (starting with us-east / A100 / Dedicated) and retain a fast rollback path if failure rates spike. This PR introduces a control-plane feature flag that gates whether the staged provisioning flow is enabled for a given node based on (region, pool type), with a global kill switch that forces legacy provisioning behavior. Summary of changes: (1) Adds a ProvisioningRolloutPolicy evaluator in the control plane that decides between LegacyProvisioning and StagedProvisioning for each node join event. The evaluator checks a global kill switch first, then a scoped allowlist keyed by region and pool_type (dedicated/shared), and finally defaults to legacy. (2) Adds admin-only APIs to update rollout policy (set allowlist entries, toggle kill switch) and read-only endpoints for internal tooling to query the current effective policy and last-updated metadata. (3) Emits audit logs + structured events when rollout policy changes (who/when/what), and includes the policy decision (legacy vs staged) as a tag in readiness transition events (without including per-node identifiers). (4) Adds docs for operators: how to enable staged provisioning by region, how to disable via kill switch, and how to verify via metrics and readiness service state. Behavior details: Global kill switch (provisioning.rollout.kill_switch=true) forces legacy provisioning for all regions/pools and suppresses any allowlist entries. Scoped rollout allowlist supports exact matches on region and pool_type; pool_type is taken from fleet metadata (dedicated/shared) and validated at the boundary. If metadata is missing/invalid we default to legacy and emit a warning event (no hard failure). Rollout changes take effect immediately for new nodes entering Allocated->Provisioning; we do not attempt to migrate nodes already in Validating mid-flight. Tests included: unit tests for policy precedence and default behavior; API authz tests (admin vs read-only); integration-style test that simulates a node join and asserts the provisioner selection. Rollout plan: Land behind the default-off policy. Infra will enable allowlist for us-east + dedicated only during the staged rollout window (ENG-4829) with SRE on-call coverage. Kill switch can be toggled by on-call with the existing break-glass admin role. Links: ADR-017 readiness state machine (policy decision is recorded as part of the provisioning step metadata), ENG-4822 control-plane state machine implementation, SUP-28411 customer report motivating faster rollback mechanisms.
Ethan Park: Can we make sure the kill switch is evaluated before any allowlist lookup? I want to be confident that flipping one flag is enough during an incident.
Jordan Lee (author): Yep — policy evaluation order is now: kill_switch -> allowlist match -> default legacy. Added a unit test that asserts allowlist entries are ignored when kill_switch=true.
Rafael Mendes: Please confirm we are not tagging per-node IDs in metrics/events. We just got bitten by high-cardinality tags last quarter.
Jordan Lee (author): Confirmed. The readiness/provisioning decision is included as a low-cardinality enum (legacy|staged) plus region + pool_type. No node_id tags; audit event includes actor + policy key only.
Vanessa Ortiz: How do we treat missing pool_type? Some older pools don’t have the tag in fleet metadata yet.
Jordan Lee (author): Missing/unknown pool_type falls back to legacy with a warning event (rate-limited). We can tighten this once Terraform tags are fully rolled out.
Connor O'Brien: Docs look good. Can you add one explicit 'rollback' section with the exact command and expected verification steps?
Jordan Lee (author): Added a rollback section to docs/internal/fleet/provision-to-ready/rollout-flags.md including rolloutctl examples and which dashboard panels to check.
Keiko Yamamoto: Minor naming nit: please align pool_type values with what autoscaling uses (dedicated/shared).
Jordan Lee (author): Updated constants and API validation to use dedicated/shared, added backwards-compatible parsing for 'on_demand' in case we see it from older tags.

Summary: Introduce a lightweight presubmit orchestration layer that assigns weighted lanes to PRs based on a small impact heuristic (file globs, language touchpoints, and directory ownership). The goal is faster feedback for routine docs/config/small SDK changes while retaining full test coverage for high-impact code paths. Additionally, replace bloated test images with slimline per-language toolchain profiles and a two-stage cache priming so most presubmit jobs skip heavy package installs.

Motivation: CI spend and latency have been steadily growing; many PRs touch only README or docs and still wait for full toolchain installs. This causes long feedback loops and discourages small iterative changes. We need a low-risk way to: 1) reduce average presubmit time/cost, 2) prioritize critical lanes for high-confidence verification, and 3) keep the system transparent and auditable for SRE/SEC. ENG-2345 tracks the cost objectives; ENG-2399 tracks the slim image rollout.

What changed (high level): - Introduced presubmit-weighted router (ci/presubmit/router.ts) that computes a lane weight {fast, standard, full} from heuristics: changed file globs, manifest diffs, and owner hints. - Added declarative lane definitions (ci/presubmit/lanes.yaml) with thresholds for required checks and time budgets. - Implemented toolchain profiles (ci/toolchains/README.md + profiles/*) that describe minimal package sets for fast lanes and fuller sets for standard/full lanes. - Introduced image layering and two-stage cache priming in Dockerfiles to allow skip-install quickstart for fast lanes. - Added a lightweight telemetry ping for presubmit decisions (metrics only; no PII) and an audit log to trace why a PR ran a particular lane. - CI changes: GitHub Actions composable workflows updated to use conditional job paths and a new presubmit dispatcher step.

Commits (summary): - feat(presubmit): add presubmit router and lane heuristics (A. Raman) - feat(ci): lanes.yaml and dispatcher workflow (A. Raman) - chore(toolchain): introduce slimline python/node/rust profiles + base images (J. Kim) - ci: add cache-priming step and telemetry shim (M. Ortega) - fix(ci): permissions for audit-sink and secrets in dispatcher (P. Shah)

Files touched (representative): - ci/presubmit/router.ts - ci/presubmit/lanes.yaml - .github/workflows/presubmit-dispatch.yml - ci/toolchains/profiles/python-slim.Dockerfile - ci/toolchains/profiles/node-slim.Dockerfile - ci/toolchains/cache-priming.sh - tooling/presubmit-audit/README.md

Testing and CI: - Local unit tests for router heuristics with mocked file lists. - Integration harness (ci/integration/presubmit-sim) to simulate PR diffs and validate mapping counts. - GitHub Actions matrix validated across linux/ubuntu-22/macOS (reused existing runners). - Initial rollout gated behind a feature flag in presubmit router to allow canary on small number of repos. - CI status: first run failed due to runner permissions on the audit sink; fixed in follow-up commit and then all checks passed; final CI status: pass.

Rollout plan and migration notes: - Default behavior preserved: if dispatch feature flag is off, existing presubmit flow unchanged. - Gradual canary: enable feature flag for 10% of repos (internal config) for 48 hours, validate false positives and missed coverage. - Telemetry and audit logs will be reviewed daily for the first week; an automatic rollback policy is in place if flakiness > 5% in critical lanes. - No repo changes required; teams can opt-out per-repo via ci/presubmit/lanes.yaml override.

Review conversation (condensed): - Miguel O: "Router looks reasonable; can you add a short circuit for monorepo-wide breakages so we don't under-test large changes?" — Aisha: "Added threshold on number of touched files to force full lane (see lanes.yaml threshold_count)." - Priya S: "Audit logs need stricter access; remove secrets from telemetry payloads." — Aisha: "Telemetry is metrics-only; audit sink ACL tightened in fix commit." - Liam O'C: "Please add a changelog entry and a brief explainer doc for platform teams." — Aisha: "Added tooling/presubmit-audit/README.md and release notes." - QA: "Observed flaky node-slim image layer on ubuntu runner" — J. Kim: "Pinned node-builder base and added retry logic to cache-priming step." Approvals: Miguel, Priya, Liam approved after fixes.

CI checks summary: - unit-tests (linux): pass - integration-sim (matrix): pass - lint (typescript/python): pass - image-build (node/python): pass after retry - release/signing-checks: pass

Security & compliance: - No secrets transmitted by router; audit sink access restricted to infra SRE role. - Toolchain profiles documented and reviewed by security to ensure no unexpected network egress in fast lanes.

Why this is different from previous PRs: Rather than monolithic CI refactor or simply trimming deps, this PR introduces an orchestration layer that can assign presubmit intensity based on an explainable heuristic and per-repo policies. It pairs policy with concrete engineering work (slim images + cache priming) to realize latency/cost wins without sacrificing safety.

Metrics observed in canary (internal): - Median presubmit time reduced 42% for fast lane PRs. - Average CI CPU-minutes reduced 31% across canary repos. - No regressions in flakiness for full lanes during 48-hour canary.

Follow-ups (tracked in Linear): - ENG-2401: add waterfall visualizer in Console to show lane assignment per PR. - ENG-2412: expose per-team override UI in Console. - ENG-2420: expand heuristics to use owner labels and historical flaky-test signals.

Merge: squash+merge on 2026-02-23 after all approvals and CI green.

Checklist: [x] Tests added/updated [x] Docs updated (tooling/presubmit-audit/README.md) [x] Linear tickets linked [x] Security reviewed [x] Rollout plan included

If anything unexpected shows up in post-merge CI telemetry, revert is prepared (branch: rollback/presubmit-weighted-298765).

Motivation: large multi-stage inference pipelines (fast path fallback to slower models, prefix replays, and multi-tenant routing) make per-token cost attribution opaque and introduce observability backpressure when telemetry fanout is naive. This PR introduces two coordinated subsystems: 1) Signal Railway: a lightweight router that normalizes, deduplicates and routes observability artifacts (metrics, traces, logs, billing events) to downstream consumers with backpressure and bounded buffering; 2) Cost Deblur: a post-processing reattribution step that reconciles overlapping token emissions across fallback/replica invocations and attributes cost to the originating invocation via provenance anchors. Scope: implements runtime adapter for emitting canonical railway envelopes, a small in-memory fanout queue with per-tenant QoS, the Cost Deblur service that consumes compact envelopes and emits corrected billing events, a new Signal Railway dashboard, and alert tuning to reduce billing-noise churn. Checklist: [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-4218) [x] End-to-end integration test [x] Performance microbench for fanout latency [x] Dashboard and runbook updates [x] Add feature flag (obs.signal_railway.enabled) Changeset summary: commits: - Add canonical railway envelope schema and runtime shim - Implement railway fanout worker with per-tenant QoS and bounded buffers - Add deblur service with provenance anchor matching and probabilistic eviction - Expose telemetry metrics: railway.queue_depth, railway.dispatch_latency_ms, deblur.rewrites, deblur.unmatched_events - Add Signal Railway Grafana dashboard and Alert: Billing deblur mismatch rate (>0.5% sustained) - Tests: unit tests for anchor matching, integration test with synthetic replaybench - Feature flag gate and rollout plan Affected files (high-level): observability/railway/envelope.go, observability/railway/worker.go, observability/deblur/service.go, telemetry/metrics/registry.go, dashboards/signal-railway.json, docs/observability/railway.md, tests/telemetry/test_deblur.py, ci/replaybench/README.md, ci/workflows/replaybench.yml.
instead of only adding extra telemetry points we introduce a first-class fanout router to protect collectors from load spikes and a corrective pipeline to reconcile billing artifacts — both aimed squarely at production stability during model fallback scenarios.
- Marco Delgado (reviewer): "Nice separation. Two asks: make buffer size configurable per-tenant and add a circuit-breaker metric so SRE can silence noisy tenants."
- Priya: "Added per-tenant config and exposed railway.circuit_breaker_trips; updated tests; see commit 0003b6."
- Sophie Lin (reviewer): "Deblur algorithm looks good; can we add a flag to disable heuristics and force strict provenance matching for compliance customers?"

payload.body:
Motivation: current batching heuristics group by coarse sequence-length buckets which reduces padding for common workloads but struggles when model-kernel performance varies across length ranges and quantization profiles. This PR introduces a weighted bucketing strategy plus a kernel-fit scheduler that jointly optimizes padding cost and kernel throughput fit, and integrates an async flush policy that reduces tail-latency for sparse long-sequence traffic.

Design summary: the change has three primary pieces: 1) Weighted Sequence-Length Buckets: instead of fixed-width buckets we compute a dynamic bucket boundary set per model based on recent sequence-length distribution and a padding-cost function. Buckets are scored by expected bytes-of-padding * weight(seqlen) where weight accounts for kernel throughput and quantization penalty. 2) Kernel-Fit Scheduler: a lightweight scoring function picks which bucket to flush based on combined score = latency_penalty * alpha + (padding_cost) * beta + kernel_fit_bonus. Kernel_fit_bonus prefers dispatching batches to kernels measured to have better throughput at that sequence-length range (collected from runtime telemetry). 3) Async flush + KV-cache warmup hints: for buckets with heterogeneous seqlen we perform bounded async flushes when estimated wait time exceeds a threshold; concurrently we issue KV-cache warmup probes for the dominant sequence prefix in the bucket so that subsequent decoding steps avoid cold-KV penalties.

Implementation notes: changes live in runtime/batcher/ and runtime/scheduler/ with a small config surface exposed via model-profiles. The scoring and bucket recomputation run in a sampling background task (low CPU). We store per-model bucket metadata in the runtime metadata store; schema is backward compatible. New knobs added: model.profile.bucket_target_cost, scheduler.alpha, scheduler.beta, scheduler.kernel_fit_threshold, bucket.async_flush_ms.

Behavioral checklist (also in PR description):
- [x] Generate bucket boundaries from empirical seqlen histogram (sliding window 30m)
- [x] Compute per-bucket expected padding cost using token-cost and latency SLO weight
- [x] Integrate kernel-fit bonus using runtime kernel benchmarks
- [x] Add async flush path with bounded concurrency to avoid queue amplification
- [x] Emit metrics: redwood.batcher.bucket_size, redwood.batcher.padding_bytes_est, redwood.scheduler.kernel_fit_score
- [x] Add unit tests for bucket reclustering and scheduler scoring
- [x] Add e2e perf test and compare against current production bucketing

Testing & results: microbenchmarks were run on a dedicated perf-cluster (p4d-like) with synthetic traffic mimicking a 70/25/5 short/medium/long split. Baselines: main (fixed-width buckets) and previous histogram-bucketed approach. Results: overall token-cost reduced 11.7% (95% CI ±1.2%), mean latency improved 6.4%, p95 latency improved 9.8% under steady load. For mixed-quantization setups (int8/4bit combos) padding-driven kernel mismatch p95 dropped by 14%. KV-cache hit rate for decoding prefix warmups rose by 3.2 percentage points for long-tail workloads.

Compatibility and rollout: feature gated by model.profile.bucketing=v2. Default remains legacy bucketer until rollout. We added a canary rollout config that enables the scheduler for 5% of traffic per model. No protocol changes to API. Backwards compatible model profile parsing.

Files changed (high-level): runtime/batcher/bucketer.py (new), runtime/batcher/bucketer_test.py (new), runtime/scheduler/kernel_fit.py (new), runtime/scheduler/async_flush.py (mod), runtime/telemetry/bucket_metrics.go (mod), infra/perf/harness/bucket_perf.py (new), configs/model_profiles/schema_v2.yaml (mod), docs/observability/buckets.md (new).

Commits summary:
- feat(batcher): initial weighted-seqlen-bucketer with histogram reclustering
- feat(scheduler): kernel-fit scoring and dispatch API
- perf(test): add e2e perf harness and comparison script
- fix(async): bound concurrent async flushes to prevent amplification
- docs: observability and rollout notes for bucket v2

Review conversation highlights:
- Ethan Moore (review): "Nice design; two asks: (1) ensure bucket recompute cost is bounded under high traffic and (2) add a regression threshold in e2e so we don't rollout if p95 increases."
- Author reply: "Added sliding-window sampling and bounded recompute; added regression gate to perf harness (see infra/perf/harness/bucket_perf.py)."
- Priya Nair (review): "Kernel-fit bonus makes sense but we should avoid overfitting to noisy kernel microbenchmarks."
- Author reply: "Kernel-fit uses exponentially-weighted moving average with minimum sample counts; fallback to neutral bonus if noisy."
- Liam Chen (approval): "Approach is pragmatic and observability is solid. Approve once CI passes and we have canary config."

CI: unit, integration, lint, and perf smoke runs passed. One flaky test (telemetry export) was retried and passed.

Release notes: "Introduce weighted sequence-length bucketing and a kernel-fit scheduler that reduces padding and improves kernel utilization for mixed-length workloads. Feature is behind model profile flag."
Ethan Moore: Nice design; two asks: (1) ensure bucket recompute cost is bounded under high traffic and (2) add a regression threshold in e2e so we don't rollout if p95 increases.
Sofia Patel: Added sliding-window sampling and bounded recompute; added regression gate to perf harness.
Priya Nair: Kernel-fit bonus makes sense but avoid overfitting to noisy kernel microbenchmarks.
Sofia Patel: Kernel-fit uses EWMA and requires minimum sample counts; falls back to neutral bonus if noisy.
Liam Chen: Approve once CI passes and we have canary config.
