payload.body:
Motivation: Users asked for a low-friction way to iterate on token-level cost/latency signals and validate alerting changes without flooding production dashboards. This PR introduces a developer-facing "Observability Playground" (opt-in) plus a data export called the Token Slice Exporter (v0.1) that emits compact, folded token-level slices for downstream dashboards and interactive analysis. Main changes: 1) Token Slice Exporter: a service that subscribes to sampled invocation spans, extracts per-stage timing (frontend, routing, kernel-queue, kernel-exec, kv-cache, postprocess), token counts, estimated per-stage energy proxy, and a compact prompt-shape fingerprint. To control cardinality we introduce "folded slices" which hash prompt-shape + stage sequence and emit counts/quantiles instead of raw high-cardinality labels. Export format is a simple NDJSON line per slice (schema v0.1) and a rolling aggregation path (v0.1-rollup) that supports windowed counters. 2) Observability Playground UI: a small React app available under /observability/playground (internal auth only) that lets engineers query token slices, pivot by prompt shape fingerprint, build ad-hoc cohorts, and export CSV for evaluation. 3) Dashboards: new Grafana panels added under Observability > Playground: Token Slice Explorer, Queue-Lag Cohorts, Energy Sparkline, and Folded-Slice Heatmap. 4) Alert tuning: SLO alert rule adjustments to de-weight transient burst events identified by the folded-slice fingerprint; added an alert damping adapter that suppresses duplicate alerts for the same folded-slice for a sliding 10-minute window. 5) Config & ops: feature flag telemetry.playground.enabled (default: false), documentation page with runbook and data retention notes, and e2e replay test that verifies exporter stability with synthetic real-world traces. Checklist: - [x] Implement exporter service + ingestion pipeline - [x] Add folded-slice hashing & rollup logic - [x] Add React Playground UI + internal route and auth gating - [x] Grafana dashboard panels and JSON models - [x] Unit + integration tests + e2e replay harness - [x] Docs + runbook updates - [x] Performance bench (small-scale) Summary of commits: - Add token-slice exporter, schema v0.1 and rollup worker - Instrument span hydrator to emit slice candidates - Folded-slice hashing implementation with coarse quantiles - Playground UI: query layer, results table, CSV export - Grafana: panels and dashboard JSONs - Alerting: add damping adapter and SLO rule tweaks - Tests: unit, integration, end-to-end replay - Docs: observability/playground.md and runbook Note on performance: Exporter runs as a separate opt-in service and consumes only sampled traces (default 0.5% sampling). Benchmarks run in this branch showed ~5% CPU overhead on a sample ingest node at 0.5% sampling and 2.3% memory overhead for the rollup worker under steady-state. We intentionally kept raw labels folded to avoid high-cardinality index growth. Changed areas (high-level): - telemetry/exporter/token_slice_exporter.py - telemetry/rollup/folded_slice_worker.py - runtime/span_hydrator/emit_slice_candidates.go - observability/ui/playground/* (React app) - docs/observability/playground.md - infra/grafana/dashboards/playground_token_slices.json - alerts/slo/token-slice-damping-rules.yaml - tests/e2e/replay/token_slice_replay_test.go - scripts/bench/token_slice_bench.sh Review notes & conversation: Reviewer (Ethan Brooks): "Nice shape — main concern is cardinality growth if teams enable this widely. Can we make folding stricter by default and add a sampling knob per-tenant?" Author (Maya Chen): "Agree — implemented tenant-level sampling in config and added an aggressive default fold (prompt-shape + stage seq -> sha1 -> 16-bit) with a feature flag to relax for experiments. See telemetry/rollup/folded_slice_worker.py for the parameterized window." Reviewer (Priya Rao): "Alert damping adapter looks promising but I'd like an integration test showing alerts suppressed for repeated folded-slice bursts." Author: "Added tests/e2e/replay/token_slice_replay_test.go which replays synthetic bursts and asserts damping behavior; locally CI showed suppression as expected." Motivation: production operators need a way to attribute tail latency and token-cost spikes back to the originating callsite (the application call path) rather than only per-route rollups. This PR instruments callpath-level metrics and introduces a deferred log enrichment worker that hydrates logs once trace context and invocation identifiers converge.

What this PR does: implements a lightweight callpath identifier (callpath_id) propagated end-to-end, emits callpath-scoped histograms and token-cost counters, adds an OTEL-compatible trace propagator for cross-queue handoffs, and ships a background enrichment worker that attaches trace and token attribution fields to earlier-logged events once the invocation completes. Also adds a small Grafana dashboard and a runbook note for tuning alert noise.

Design notes: callpath_id is derived deterministically from a hashed stack of callsite metadata the SDK emits (service, module, method, user_route_hint). We intentionally keep it opaque and stable across minor code moves. Metrics use a new prefix telemetry.callpath.{latency_ms,p50,p95,p99,token_cost_tokens} with labels {model,region,callpath_id,customer_tier}. The deferred enrichment worker subscribes to the invocation-complete queue; it looks up traces from the trace index and patches the original log event with token_cost and trace_id fields via an append-only enrichment store to avoid rewriting historical logs.

Rollout plan: feature gated via env var TELEMETRY_CALLPATH_ENABLED (off by default). Initial rollout to canary tenants (10 small tenants) for two weeks. If no significant increase in metrics cardinality and CI runs for enrichment show <1s median hydration, flip the flag for all hosted read-only telemetry. Private/Dedicated customers need to opt-in since the enrichment worker requires access to the trace index and S3-compatible staging.

Monitoring and alerting changes: adds a per-callpath cardinality guard metric (telemetry.callpath.cardinality_warning) and an alert that auto-suppresses on short-lived callpaths. Updates the token-cost SLO dashboard to include a callpath breakdown panel and a top-10 callpath spike breaker.

Testing: unit tests for the callpath hashing and propagation (Python and Go layers), integration test that simulates cross-queue propagation and verifies enrichment writes, and an end-to-end smoke bench that compares pre/post token_cost distributions.

Related: ENG-1987 (callpath attribution), ENG-2044 (deferred enrichment design), references to prior work on token-cost rollups (see PRs: pr-218334, pr-271456).

Checklist: [x] unit tests added, [x] integration test, [x] dashboard JSON checked in, [x] docs: observability/callpath-metrics.md, [x] feature-flag added, [x] runbook snippet in docs/runbooks/callpath_enrichment.md

Notes: kept the enrichment worker intentionally single-writer per-invocation to prevent double-enrichment races; this is captured in the worker implementation comments. Expect moderate telemetry index query load during initial rollout — infra capacity has been scoped in ENG-2090.

Summary: This PR implements a residency-aware enforcement path that ties service identity, declared residency, and permitted KMS backends into a single enforcement gate at ingress. Motivation: customers in regulated regions require proof that encryption operations and key usage are bound to allowed geographic providers and that access is auditable. The change set introduces: 1) a residency-proof middleware that validates a signed residency assertion attached to requests and annotates the authz context with residency claims; 2) a RBACv2 binding generator that compiles operator-provided residency policies into per-service allowed-KMS lists; 3) a KMS-origin-assertion header verifier and selector to ensure outgoing key operations use an approved provider; 4) an audit gate which stamps residency verification and KMS origin into the immutable audit envelope and rejects requests lacking required proofs when policy mandates; 5) migration helpers and a simulator to preview policy effects before enforcement. Checklist: [x] Add residency middleware and unit tests; [x] Add RBACv2 binding compiler and integration tests; [x] Add KMS selector and provider unit tests; [x] Add audit envelope augmentation and end-to-end tests; [x] Add docs and upgrade notes; [ ] Feature flag rollout gating in infra (follow-up infra task). Rollout plan: land behind feature flag redwood.residency_enforcer=false by default; run policy-sim in canary; enable enforcement for audited organizations only initially. Important implementation notes: residency assertions are JWT-like signed blobs generated by regional attestors (or customer-provided attestations). The middleware verifies signatures using configured attestor keys, canonicalizes the residency claim, and stores canonical residency tags on the request context used by RBACv2 decisions. The RBACv2 compiler accepts residency policies in YAML (examples/docs updated) and emits a compact allowlist keyed by service account and route. The KMS selector consults the allowlist and attempts to route requests to the highest-priority compatible provider; when none are available and policy requires residency, the request is rejected with 403 and an audit entry. The audit gate now writes an immutable residency.kms provenance field into the sealed audit envelope so downstream compliance tooling can consume it. Migration and safety: added a policy-simulator mode that runs decisions non-blocking and logs samples for 7 days; operators can use the simulator to refine policies before flipping enforcement. Related work items: ENG-21234 (policy compiler), ENG-21240 (audit envelope extension), SUP-4421 (customer support case for EU key pinning).
Add a residency-proof enforcement middleware, RBACv2 binding generator for service-account->KMS mapping, and an audit gating step which rejects requests missing verified KMS-origin claims. Backwards-compatible by default; rollout gated behind feature flag redwood.residency_enforcer.

Motivation: Dedicated fleets see frequent brief utilization drops (seconds->minutes) that trigger decommits and warmup thrash for certain tenants. This PR introduces a lightweight 'decommitment retainer' that holds recently-freed slots in a soft-retained state for a configurable short window (default 120s). If a tenant or pool re-requests capacity within the window, the retainer allows immediate reuse instead of a full reprovision. To observe the feature impact and simplify autoscaler tuning, this change also adds a utilization-delta reporter that emits per-pool and per-tenant utilization deltas across multiple windows (10s, 60s, 300s).

What this PR changes (high level):
- Implement core retainer: retention lifecycle, reclaim policy, and metrics (retained_slots_total, retained_slots_hit_count, retained_slot_age_seconds_histogram).
- Autoscaler integration: optional tightening/relaxing hooks where the autoscaler consults retained_capacity() to avoid aggressive decommits during transient dips.
- Utilization-delta reporter: sidecar component in fleet-controller that computes delta-series and exports prometheus-friendly counters and an aggregated HDR sketch for latency-targeted analysis.
- Console additions: two new tiles under Dedicated Fleet -> Utilization: "Retention hit rate" and "Utilization deltas (10s/60s/5m)" (feature-flag gated).
- Config: cluster-level feature flag dedicated.decommit_retention.enabled and per-pool retention_window_seconds; safe defaults keep feature off in production until rollout.

Implementation notes:
- Retainer is implemented as a small in-memory, eviction-aware structure persisted to the cluster state directory to survive controller restarts for short windows. It does not alter lease semantics; it only short-circuits the cold-provision path when reclaiming. The component exposes a clear metrics surface to evaluate value before making it the default behaviour.
- Utilization-delta reporter computes deltas using sliding windows and samples at controller tick; it keeps a rolling reservoir to bound memory usage and emits both raw counters and HDR sketches for percentiles.
- We intentionally avoided changing warm-pool reconciliation logic; retainer acts as a fast-path read for request admission. If warm-pools are enabled, they continue to operate and retainer is complementary.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag (off by default).
2) Canary enable in a single test cluster for 24 hours with debug metrics retention; review retained_slots_hit_count and warmup latency.
3) Gradual enable for 5% of Dedicated tenants using the feature gating service; monitor autoscaler oscillation and tenant SLOs.
4) If stable after 72 hours of production telemetry, increase to 100% and promote Console tiles to general availability.

Testing performed:
- Unit tests for retention lifecycle, eviction, and reclaim decisioning.
- Integration test simulating transient surge/decommit scenarios showing ~35-50% reduction in reprovision events for the test workload.
- Load test on perf-canary cluster with 10k small requests to ensure memory/CPU overhead of reporter is <2%.
- E2E smoke in staging with Console tiles validated.

Known limitations and future work:
- Currently retention is per-slot; future work will add affinity-aware retention (maintain slot locality for tenant affinity).
- Persistent backing is intentionally lightweight; long restarts beyond retention_window_seconds will naturally evict entries.
- Reporter currently uses a single sampling frequency; we may expose dynamic sampling for high-cardinality tenants.
Adds a short-window decommit retention mechanism for Dedicated fleets to reduce churn during transient drops, plus a new utilization-delta reporter metric stream and Console dashboard tiles. Default off; opt-in via feature flag. No API contract changes.

Context: Support/CS needs a safe way to mark checklist steps complete/reset during onboarding troubleshooting (e.g., customer rotated keys, telemetry backfill lag, or a step was missed due to earlier event-ordering issues). This PR adds admin-only override endpoints to the checklist progress service, plus audit logging and minimal UI plumbing for internal tools (Console will consume in a follow-up PR).

What’s included: (1) Admin override API endpoints to mark a checklist step COMPLETE/NOT_STARTED (or clear an override) for a tenant, with optional annotation text and an internal reason code; (2) Strict authorization (RBAC) so only Support/CS roles can call the endpoints, scoped to internal operators; (3) Immutable audit log entries capturing actor, tenant, step, previous state, new state, reason, and timestamp; (4) Telemetry events for override actions (PII-free) so we can monitor frequency and identify systemic onboarding issues; (5) Guardrails: overrides are additive on top of event-derived state and never delete raw events; step state transitions remain monotonic unless an override explicitly resets.

Why: Dogfood surfaced that a small number of tenants get “stuck” when event emission is delayed or the customer changes org structure. Support currently uses ad-hoc SQL/scripts to unblock customers; this creates risk and lacks auditability. We want an approved, logged, least-privilege path.

API summary: POST /internal/admin/onboarding/checklist/tenants/{tenant_id}/steps/{step_id}:override with body {"action": "MARK_COMPLETE"|"RESET"|"CLEAR_OVERRIDE", "reason_code": "AUTH_ROTATION"|"TELEMETRY_DELAY"|"CUSTOMER_CONFIRMED"|"OTHER", "note": "freeform"}. GET /internal/admin/onboarding/checklist/tenants/{tenant_id}/audit returns latest override actions (paginated).

Permissions: New RBAC permission "support:checklist_override" (role-bound to Support + CS internal roles). Requests require an operator identity (no API keys) and are denied for customer principals.

Audit retention: Audit records follow existing admin-action retention (18 months) and are excluded from customer-accessible logs. Notes are limited to 500 chars and should not contain customer secrets/PII.

Testing: Unit tests for authorization, idempotency, and audit writes; integration tests for typical override flows; added data-contract test to ensure override telemetry payload stays within cardinality constraints.

Follow-ups: (a) Console UI admin drawer + Support macro deep links (tracked in ENG-5852 subtask); (b) Add a “reason required” enforcement in UI for RESET actions; (c) Consider restricting RESET to a smaller set of steps if we see misuse.

Motivation: We observed repeated reopen oscillations for small regional clusters after capacity events which caused cascade retries and SLO noise. This PR introduces a lightweight holdoff mediator that enforces an adaptive reopen backoff with region-aware rollback logic and per-tenant smoothing to reduce noisy priority flips.

Summary of changes: implement an in-node holdoff mediator that tracks a compact epoch + EWMA of recent reopen requests, apply tenant-priority smoothing to avoid aggressive preemption on short spikes, add region-aware rollback heuristics that prevent double-fallbacks across zones, and surface operational telemetry and runbook guidance. Also includes a targeted hotfix for a double-charge edge-case in the rollback path that could increment tenant penalty counters twice under race conditions.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4721) - [x] Unit tests for holdoff mediator and EWMA smoothing - [x] Integration test for restart persistence and region rollback scenario - [x] Telemetry dashboards and alerts added - [x] Runbook update and rollout notes

Why this is different: existing SLO enforcement components focused on eviction and coarse tenant throttles; this change sits between admission and eviction and prevents feedback loops by mediating reopen attempts and smoothing priority deltas so downstream evictions are less likely to oscillate.

Implementation notes: the mediator keeps a minimal persisted state (epoch id, ewma_alpha, last_reopen_ts) in node-local metadata so restarts don't immediately re-open circuits. The EWMA smoothing uses a configurable alpha per-tenant with a safe default (0.2). Region-aware rollback inspects the last-failover vector to avoid reissuing rollback when the same tenant has already been rolled back in another zone; this prevents duplicate penalty accounting. We exposed three new counters and two gauges (holdoff_mediator_active, tenant_fairness_ewma_gap, mediator_reopen_attempts).

Testing: unit tests cover state transitions, alpha boundary conditions, and persistence; integration test simulates a transient capacity event across two zones and verifies mediator prevents reopen cascade and that metrics reflect stabilized state. CI initially failed in integration due to a timing window; probe window and jitter were adjusted and CI passed on the follow-up run.

Rollout: staged rollout recommended — enable mediator on a small canary region for 48h, monitor holdoff_mediator_active and tenant_fairness_ewma_gap, then progressively enable by region. If unexpected impact is observed, flip feature flag mediator.enabled=false; as a fallback the system reverts to previous admission behavior.

Ops notes: The runbook (docs/ops/holdoff-runbook.md) documents expected metric ranges and remediation steps. This PR also includes a short hotfix to region_failover.go to avoid double-charge under a racing rollback path.

Related: ENG-4721 (design), ENG-4850 (postmortem follow-up), incident INT-2121 referenced for context.
Introduce holdoff mediator core loop and tests
Implement EWMA-based tenant priority smoothing and metric hooks
Region-aware rollback decision and fix double-charge bug
Docs: add operational note and runbook section
Tests: add integration scenario for reopen oscillation

Rolling upgrade recommended: stagger by zone; monitor metric 'holdoff_mediator_active' and 'tenant_fairness_ewma_gap'; fallback: set mediator.enabled=false via config map.

Motivation: Our presubmit and release flows have accumulated ad-hoc toolchain manifests per repo and a heavy unified lint runner that adds latency to iteration. This PR introduces a small, opt-in 'toolchain-autopilot' daemon for CI that selects and materializes minimal toolchain manifests at presubmit time, a compact 'presubmit-lite' runner for quick feedback on common changes, and a dep-reshuffle helper to move rarely-used transitive deps into an opt-in dev-only bundle. Goals: reduce CI wall time for common PRs, shrink presubmit resource usage, and make repository toolchain upgrades safer and incremental. Design notes: - toolchain-autopilot uses .redwood/ci.toml in a repo to locate language profiles (python/node/go) and desired tool versions; when missing it falls back to a repo-heuristic. - presubmit-lite is a lightweight workflow that runs on path-sensitive triggers and executes a constrained subset of linters and fast unit tests; fuller suites are still run on the main CI lanes and nightly smoke. - dep-reshuffle is a scripted suggestion engine (scripts/dep-reshuffle.py) that proposes moving dev-only transitive deps to dev bundles and produces a patch to package manifests; the team still reviews before applying. Rollout plan: opt-in flag in repo config for initial 30% of repos, monitor presubmit latency and merge rate for 2 weeks, expand if stable. Checklists: - [x] Implement autopilot materializer and unit tests - [x] Add presubmit-lite workflows (GitHub Actions) - [x] Add dep-reshuffle script and local CLI - [x] Add telemetry for presubmit duration and toolchain cache hit-rate - [x] Add documentation in docs/ci/toolchain-autopilot.md - [ ] Monitor and iterate (post-merge) Change summary: - ci/toolchain/autopilot.go: new materializer service with cache and fallback heuristics - .github/workflows/presubmit-lite.yml: new fast-path workflow that runs on path filters - scripts/dep-reshuffle.py: analyzer and patch generator for package manifests - docs/ci/toolchain-autopilot.md: explainer and opt-in instructions - internal/telemetry/presubmit_metrics.go: new metrics for presubmit latency and cache hit-rate - ci/actions/toolchain-bootstrap/: small sharable actions to prepare micro-images - build/Makefile: expose a new 'ci-autopilot-test' target Tests and CI: unit tests added for autopilot heuristics, presubmit-lite includes smoke steps in Actions; end-to-end integration was validated on a canary repo (redwood-examples/ci-canary). Backwards compatibility: no repo is migrated automatically; the default behavior remains the existing toolchain until .redwood/ci.toml opt-in is present. Migration doc links included. Why this is different from previous CI refactors: rather than a monolithic rewire of all presubmit jobs, this PR provides an opt-in, minimal surface for teams to get quick wins and observable outcomes.

Eleanor Park: Added fallback unit test (autopilot_test.go) and documented the heuristic behavior in the doc. The fallback is also covered in the canary run.

Motivation: Dedicated fleets experience short, high-amplitude microbursts that cause repeated oscillation in autoscaler decisions and noisy utilization metrics. This PR introduces a burst mesh consolidator component and a deviation ledger to reduce sensitivity to ephemeral spikes while preserving throughput guarantees for latency-critical tenants. Summary of changes: 1) Add a burst mesh consolidator that aggregates per-tenant transient demand signals across pool boundaries and emits smoothed surge tokens to the autoscaler; 2) Introduce a deviation ledger that tracks signed deviations between observed utilization and committed throughput at multiple percentiles, enabling proportional soft-reservations and controlled preemption windows; 3) Add a stability window heuristic and probabilistic dampening so small bursts are consolidated into warmlet reservations rather than triggering full provision ramps; 4) Wire consolidated signals into the existing provisioner/vacuum path with a compatibility shim to fall back to legacy behavior when feature flag is off; 5) Instrument telemetry and dashboards with new HDR sketches and delta counters for auditability and SLO reconstructions. Checklist: - [x] Design doc: docs/design/burst_mesh_consolidator.md - [x] Unit tests for consolidator and deviation ledger - [x] E2E burst simulation job - [x] Dashboard and alert updates - [x] Feature-flagged rollout. Rollout plan: start gated rollout to internal Dedicated fleets with feature flag off by default, enable in Canary pool for 48h, evaluate SLO regressions and util stability, then widen to 20% then full. Backout strategy: immediate feature flag flip and reconcile reservations via ledger reversal if anomalous provisioning is detected. Context and related work: builds on prior warm-pool and headroom work (ENG-2148, ENG-2710) and addresses issues surfaced during incident RED-2025. This PR focuses on the control-plane signal handling and lateral aggregation, not on kernel-level serving changes, keeping serving runtime untouched. Why different: instead of hard quota bumping, the consolidator creates transient soft-reservations and issues conserved surge tokens; the deviation ledger provides a compact, auditable trail of what was reserved, granted, and reclaimed, enabling later chargeback and post-mortem reconstruction.

Nikhil Rao (reply): Added a stability window and probabilistic dampening to the mesh so that correlated microbursts only cause warmlet reservations until sustained demand persists. See mesh_consolidator.go:stabilityWindow()
Marta Kovacs: The deviation ledger persistence format needs a migration note for clusters that upgrade mid-surge. Please ensure ledger ticks are idempotent across restarts.
Nikhil Rao (reply): Ledger write is idempotent by design and includes a monotonic tick. Added migration tests and notes in docs/design. Also added reconciliation method ledger.Reconcile() to handle partial writes.
Ethan Li: CI flaked on e2e burst sim in one run, can you add retry and a shorter fixture to speed up runs?
Nikhil Rao (reply): Added backoff/retry and shortened default sim to 5m for CI. Full 30m sim runs as nightly job.
Introduce burst mesh consolidator and deviation ledger. Improves autoscaler stability during microbursts by consolidating transient demand into warmlet reservations and providing an auditable deviation trail. Feature-flagged rollout. No breaking changes to serving runtime.

Motivation: Customers running inference across unstable networks (mobile/edge) see bursty p95/p99 spikes that cause suboptimal retry decisions (either aggressive retries causing overload or conservative backoffs hurting latency). This PR introduces a latency-aware retry profile that adapts backoff floors using short-term p95 latency windows and exposes a small StreamOperator shim to normalize streaming cancelation / graceful-drain semantics across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Summary of changes: 1) Add network-aware retry profiles (LatencyAwarePolicy) and a lightweight metrics window used by the retry controller. 2) Introduce StreamOperator: a minimal cross-language adapter that provides Pause/Resume/Abort semantics and a consistent onClose reason propagation so SDKs behave identically when servers send partial error frames or mid-stream reauth redirects. 3) Ergonomic wrappers: Python convenience helpers (backoff presets + decorator), TS fluent builder for retry policies, and Go factory method for embedding LatencyAwarePolicy into existing client constructors. 4) Parity fixes: ensure session headers (x-rw-session, x-rw-lease) and retry metadata are forwarded on reconnect paths; align TypeScript streaming event envelope with Python/Go. 5) Docs, end-to-end integration tests, and microbenchmarks added. Compatibility notes: - Non-breaking by default: existing retry behaviors remain the same unless a LatencyAwarePolicy is explicitly enabled. - SDK version bumps: python -> 1.14.0, typescript -> 1.27.0, go -> 1.8.2. - No protocol changes to the server; shim operates client-side. Testing & validation: - Unit tests for policy decision logic and StreamOperator state machine included. - Integration tests simulate packet loss, reauth frames, and slow tails. - Benchmarks show median cost per token unchanged, p95 latency reduced 6-11% under simulated 10-20% packet loss. Rollout plan: - Canary enablement in Redwood Dedicated cluster with runtime flag for 2 weeks. - Gradual opt-in for Hosted API customers via SDK flag. - Telemetry: added retry_policy.name, retry.window_ms, stream.operator.events to debug traces. Checklist: - [x] Implementation in py/ts/go SDKs - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Docs + examples - [x] Benchmarks and CI green - [x] SDK version bumps and changelogs

payload.body:
Motivation:
As part of improving OpenAI function/tool calling compatibility we encountered two recurring issues in customer integrations: 1) ambiguity about which service produced a given streaming fragment when responses included interleaved assistant messages and tool invocation frames, and 2) loss of schema mapping metadata when the compatibility layer translated between native Redwood tool signatures and OpenAI-style function schemas.

Summary of changes:
- Add an optional Tool-Binding hint header (X-Redwood-Tool-Binding) emitted by the compatibility adapter when mapping a bound Redwood tool to an OpenAI function schema. This header carries a compact binding id and version (e.g. tb:search.v2) to be threaded through streaming fragments for attribution and debugging.
- Extend streaming envelope fragments with an attribution field in the framed protocol (compat-only): a lightweight "source" token ("assistant", "tool:<binding>", "system") added as a top-level framing tag so fragments can be disambiguated by downstream consumers without changing payload bodies.
- Preserve schema provenance: when the adapter synthesizes an OpenAI function schema from an annotated Redwood tool definition, we now inject a provenance comment block into the schema description (machine-parseable key/value pairs) so roundtrip tooling can rehydrate original binding metadata.
- Update the OpenAI-compat adapter to prefer explicit binding ids for tool_choice resolution. When multiple tools match, the adapter uses binding hints + deterministic score tiebreak instead of random selection.
- Add end-to-end tests that assert streaming fragment ordering, attribution tags, and schema provenance extraction; add a new conformance test that replays a recorded multi-tool dialog and verifies identical events after round-trip through the adapter.

Design notes and rationale:
We intentionally kept changes compatibility-friendly: all runtime changes are behind the compatibility adapter flag (openai_compat: { tool_binding_hints: true }) and default to off for existing customers. The attribution tag is a framing-level hint (not injected into user-visible assistant content) so downstream clients that depend on exact assistant text are unaffected. The tool-binding header is optional and can be omitted in environments where headers are stripped (e.g., some proxies). The provenance comment in the function schema uses a compact JSON snippet embedded in the description field to survive systems that only persist the function schema text.

Rollout and migration:
- Feature gate: openai_compat.tool_binding_hints (off by default).
- Canary plan: enabled for two internal customers and redwood-qa for one week, monitor deltas in streaming fragment counts and compatibility tests.
- Fallback: if downstream consumers observe malformed fragments we will revert the adapter toggle and publish a hotfix to remove the framing tag.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests for the binding id generator and schema provenance serializer.
- Integration tests that run the adapter in both streaming and non-streaming modes and assert no text delta in assistant outputs.
- New e2e conformance replay test recorded as fixtures in tests/fixtures/openai-binding-replay.json.
- CI: build -> unit -> integration -> e2e conformance. All checks green on merge.

Security and privacy:
The binding id is non-sensitive and deterministic; it encodes repo-local tool name and semantic version only. We explicitly do not leak backend credentials or internal routing topology. The provenance block is limited in length and sanitized to remove developer comments.

Related work and alternatives considered:
- Embedding binding ids inline into assistant messages was rejected because it modifies user-visible content.
- Serializing provenance to a separate event stream was considered but increases operational complexity for clients that only subscribe to the primary message stream.

Notes for SDK authors and integrators:
- SDK updates for Python/TS include helpers to read fragment attribution and re-associate tool frames; documented in docs/openai-compat/tool-bindings.md.
- The adapters expose a compatibility-only header mapping table so customers can map existing function names to canonical binding ids.

Action items post-merge:
- Publish release note summarizing opt-in nature and how to enable the gate for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Add a sample in redwood-examples demonstrating multi-tool streaming playback and attribution UI.

Marco: small nit on header name, prefer X-RW-Tool-Binding for consistency. Priya: switched to X-RW-Tool-Binding in adapter and doc.
Lina: can you add a test where headers are stripped by an upstream proxy? Priya: added integration test simulating header strip and adapter fallback.
Oskar: LGTM after minor serialization comment. Approved.
QA: observed one flaky e2e run related to ordering in a highly parallel canary; added a retry + stricter ordering assertion.
Opt-in: openai_compat.tool_binding_hints. Adds optional tool-binding header and streaming fragment attribution to improve tool/function calling debuggability and deterministic choice resolution. No breaking changes; off by default.

payload.body:
This PR adds a lightweight prefill orchestrator that synthesizes tenant signals (recent latency, token distribution, burstiness) to produce safe defaults for batching, cache TTLs, and quantization cohort recommendations. It also introduces a warmup prober that runs mirrored, low-impact sampling against a safe sandbox to warm KV caches and validate candidate batch shapes without affecting production capacity. The third major piece is a quant cohortizer which assigns tenants to one of several quant cohorts (fp16, int8, q4, q4_0) using a conservative gating policy and staged rollout plan with automatic rollback hooks. Motivation: many tenants run with conservative defaults and manual tuning is costly; automating safe initial defaults reduces tail latency/cost for most customers while preserving manual overrides and safe fallbacks. This change is intentionally conservative: everything is disabled by default and requires the `prefill.experimental=true` flag or a tenant opt-in. Key features: CLI dry-run mode (`rwd prefill plan --dry-run`) that simulates assignment and outputs unit-econ delta, a traffic-sandbox mode that mirrors 0.1% of traffic for validation, per-tenant rollback hooks, telemetry for cohort delta (latency/cost/accuracy heuristics), unit tests and integration smoke harness. Deployment notes: enable feature flags in helm (values.prefill.experimental) to opt-in; run the included dry-run against representative traffic before enabling. Checklist: 1) implement orchestrator core and cohortizer policy, 2) add warmup prober with safe mirroring, 3) CLI dry-run and plan exporter, 4) telemetry metrics and dashboards, 5) integration tests and canary rollout plan. Related: ENG-4312 (prefill policy spec), ENG-5421 (warmup sampling pilot).
Adds a heuristic prefill orchestrator and non-disruptive warmup prober plus a tenant quantization cohortizer. Backwards compatible; feature gated behind `prefill.experimental` and `quant.cohorts` toggles. Includes CLI dry-run and telemetry.
Liam O'Connor: This is promising. Concern: how do we ensure mirrored traffic can't exhaust experimental capacity? Suggest hard cap and backpressure path.
Ava Martinez: Added a global mirror cap and per-tenant throttles in mirror.go; default mirror rate 0.1% and a tunable max-requests-sampled flag. Updated docs with cap behaviour.
Priya Desai: Need stronger safety gating around quant cohort assignment — prefer a staged rollout with cohort A/B and immediate kickback to fp16 on error spikes.
Ava Martinez: Implemented staged rollout state machine and immediate fallback to fp16 if latency or error rate exceeds thresholds (configurable). Added unit tests for rollback path.
Jorge Alvarez: Can we calculate unit-econ delta in the dry-run output? That will help product and SRE make decisions.
Ava Martinez: Dry-run now outputs estimated token-cost delta and expected latency impact per tenant, plus a CSV for offline analysis.
Liam O'Connor: CI failed once due to flaky integration test; re-run looked good. Approving pending small nits in docs.
Priya Desai: Approved — nice safety-first approach.

payload.body:
Motivation: Reduce per-token cost by combining a lightweight prefill-sampler (shape-aware cold prefetch) with a staged quantization sentinel that safely expands aggressive quant profiles only where unit economics and quality tolerances are met. This PR implements an autotune path that: 1) observes real request length/shape distributions via a streaming sampler, 2) computes candidate batch/cache/quant presets for 'cold' and 'steady' windows, 3) deploys candidates to a shadow canary, and 4) promotes profiles when end-to-end unit-econ and quality signals pass thresholds.

This change spans runtime, planner, and ops tooling: runtime gets a non-blocking prefill-sampler that records sequence shape histograms and pre-warms KV caches for long-tail prefixes; the planner receives a new PrefillSamplerProfile and shape-aware batch templates; the quant service introduces the QuantSentinel which runs compact A/B tests with low-latency trials and enforces rollback on quality regressions. The CLI (rwd-econ) and console pages surface suggested profiles and a single-click promote/rollback flow.

Checklist:
- [x] implement prefill sampler and histogram collector
- [x] add planner heuristics for shape-aware batching templates
- [x] implement QuantSentinel with canary, shadow and rollback hooks
- [x] CLI + Console integration for profile suggestions and promotions
- [x] unit + integration tests for safety guards
- [x] perf benchmarks and smoke tests against common workloads

Impact summary: In internal synthetic workloads and three customer traces (chat, summarization, retrieval-augmented QA) default automated runs show 8–18% token cost reduction with median latency impact <5ms and observed quality delta within configured thresholds (ROUGE/acceptance tests). The autotune flow is conservative by default (dry-run for first 48h), and operators can opt into faster promotion windows.

Related: Linked Linear items and notes in the ticket; follows design from ENG-4183 and is complementary to existing econ-prescriptor logic. This is intended as an iterative step toward making default batching/quant presets a dynamic, workload-driven property rather than a static config file.
Ethan Park (reviewer): The sentinel rollback path looks good but ensure that the rollback decision uses a rolling window rather than a single failing trial. Also add an explainable metric in logs for why a profile failed.
Maya Chen (author): Added rolling-window evaluation (configurable via quant.sentinel.window) and a human-readable failure_reason field in the audit log. See commit e4f8a92.
Sofia Martinez (reviewer): Planner change looks fine; one nit about the batch template naming (use 'shape-<bucket>' to make dashboards readable). Consider a toggle to disable prefill warmup for memory-constrained hosts.
Maya Chen (author): Updated naming convention and added an opt-out flag prefill.disable_on_low_memory. See commit b77d3a8.
Noah Patel (approver): Verified perf numbers on canary cluster and reviewed safety tests. Approving with the expectation that we monitor cost regressions in the first week after rollout.
SRE Bot: Observability checks passed, canary metrics within thresholds for first 24h.
QA: Integration tests flaked once in CI on macOS runner, reran and passed.
Add a prefill-sampler and QuantSentinel to enable workload-driven batching and quantization presets. Ships conservative autotune flow with dry-run by default. Expect 8-18% cost reductions on targeted workloads; operators can promote/rollback via console or rwd-econ CLI.
Default deployment leaves autotune in dry-run for 48h. To enable automatic promotions set quant.sentinel.auto_promote=true in the econ config and ensure audit retention for 7 days. Monitor econ.unit_cost and quality.acceptance_rate dashboards after enabling.
Low-medium: changes are gated behind the sentinel and default to dry-run. Fallbacks are implemented for canary failures and cold prefill is opt-out. Quant aggressiveness is limited by safety thresholds and rollback hooks.
Unit tests cover sampler, planner heuristics, and sentinel controller. Integration test runs simulate trace replays for chat, summarization, and RAG. Perf smoke tests run across p3 and a100-backed clusters to validate latency regressions (<5ms median) and verify throughput stability.
Rollout plan: 1) deploy runtime and planner changes to staging; 2) enable prefill sampler (dry-run) on canary fleet; 3) start QuantSentinel in shadow mode and observe candidate trials for 48h; 4) review suggested profiles in console and promote manually or flip auto_promote; 5) monitor dashboards and metrics for 72h before broad rollout.

payload.body:
Motivation: Recent incidents and internal perf runs showed oscillatory autoscaling behavior in Dedicated fleets when handling erratic request bursts. Binary scaling decisions coupled with short-timescale utilization signals caused throughput overshoot followed by sharp scale-downs, which produced transient latency spikes for tail-sensitive workloads. This PR introduces a "thermostat"-style autoscaler that smooths control actions across multiple timescales, preserves a small configurable headroom for microbursts, and provides explicit hedging credits to avoid oscillation-induced SLA violations.

Summary of changes: added a new autoscaler controller (fleet/thermostat_autoscaler) that computes a smoothed target capacity using an ensemble of windows (short/medium/long) and a conservative bias term, integrates with the reservation ledger to honor committed capacity, exposes a microburst-credit bank for ephemeral surges, and emits a compact telemetry surface to power alerting and chargeback. The controller is pluggable as a replacement autoscaler for Dedicated pools and defaults to a conservative mode behind a feature flag.

Key behaviors: 1) Multi-window smoothing: combine recent short-window Utilization, median medium-window, and 95th percentile long-window signals to derive a blended utilization estimate. 2) Thermostat bias: a tunable proportional bias (thermostat_delta) nudges target capacity up when long-window trends rise and down very slowly on declines to avoid rapid churn. 3) Microburst hedging: maintain a small warmlet of ephemeral capacity funded by a microburst_credit token bank; tokens replenish gradually and can be borrowed with safety backoff. 4) Safety fences: never scale below reservation commitments, clamp scale-down rates with a ramp-limit, and add a transient cooldown for pools that recently accepted hedged tokens. 5) Observability: emit util_blend, bias_contrib, hedged_tokens_used, cooldown_state, and decision_reason tags for every decision; add dashboards and an alert rule template. 6) Rollout plan: feature-flagged on Dedicated, gradual canary across low-traffic pools then wider rollout with automatic rollback on increased tail latencies.

Commits (high-level): - feat(autoscaler): initial thermostat_autoscaler controller and state machine - perf(telemetry): summary metrics and hdr sketch integration - api: microburst_credit ledger API and gRPC surface - safety: reservation and ramp-limit enforcement hooks - tests: unit + deterministic simulation harness for stochastic bursts - ci: perf benchmark job + flaky test fixes - docs: ops runbook and tuning guide

Files changed (high-level): - internal/fleet/autoscaler/thermostat_autoscaler.go - internal/fleet/autoscaler/smoothing_windows.go - internal/fleet/autoscaler/hedge_bank.go - internal/fleet/autoscaler/simulation/harness_test.go - internal/fleet/api/credits.proto - internal/fleet/controllers/scale_reconciler.go (integration points) - pkg/telemetry/metrics_registry.go - docs/ops/thermostat-autoscaler.md - test/integration/dedicated_autoscale_sim.py - .github/workflows/perf-bench.yml

Example config snippet: feature_gate: thermostatic_autoscaler: enabled; thermostat_delta: 0.12; short_window: 30s; medium_window: 5m; long_window: 30m; microburst_credit_capacity: 4pools; ramp_down_pct_per_min: 5%

Testing and validation: included a deterministic simulation harness with synthetic Poisson and heavy-tailed burst generators used to validate stability across 1k simulation runs and measure transient latency exposures. Added integration test that replays a 6-hour production traffic trace (sanitized) against a local Dedicated pool to ensure no regression in steady-state throughput. Perf benchmarks were added to CI (perf-bench job) to ensure controller decision latency stays <50ms at 5000 pools.

Review convo (summary): - Diego Ramos: "Can we prove that thermostat_delta won't systematically overshoot commitments?" Answer: used long-window percentile with conservative bias and clamp against reservation ledger; added unit test for a simulated uphill trend and refactored to add a 'bias_decay' param. - Morgan Lee: requested stronger invariants on token accounting to avoid double-spend during reconciles; fixed by moving credit transfer into single transactional reconciliation step and added idempotency keys. - Kai Nguyen: flagged potential e2e flakiness due to perf-bench variability; added HDR-sketch bucketing and deterministic seeding. - Security review (Priya Shah): minimal exposure (ledger API authenticated) but requested audit log entries for token borrow/repay flows; added audit events. Two rounds of small follow-ups and then approvals from Diego and Morgan.

CI summary: initial test run (2026-02-16) showed failing integration tests due to a race in the hedging bank; fixed in commit 3 and re-ran. Final CI status: unit tests (pass), integration (pass), perf-bench (pass), lint (pass). Overall ci_status: pass.

Backward compatibility and safety: controller is feature-flagged and off by default. It respects reservation commitments and default ramp limits are conservative. No breaking changes to public APIs; credits.proto adds a backward compatible optional service.

Release notes: "Introduce Thermostat Autoscaler for Dedicated fleets: smoother autoscaling with microburst hedging, improved observability, and ops tuning guide. Feature-gated; opt-in rollout."

Follow-ups: - ENG-3124: auto-tune bias_decay using historical traces (tracked) - ENG-3187: add scheduler integration for locality-aware hedging - ENG-3301: expose per-tenant hedged-token billing metrics

payload.body:
Motivation: our presubmit lanes are noisy and heavy for small changes. This PR introduces a lightweight presubmit shim that fast-paths CI for change-aware patches and an "atomic dep pruner" that trims the lockfile surface for small code edits. The goal is faster feedback (median presubmit wall time from ~13m to ~3m for typical docs/infra tweaks), fewer false CI reruns, and safer dependency churn by making lockfile updates explicit and incremental.

What this PR delivers: 
- ci/presubmit/shim: a tiny Go-based binary (90kb) that inspects the git diff and consults path-based rules to decide a minimal job set (lint-only, unit-only, or full). The shim is intended as an opt-in fastpath for changes below a configurable size threshold.
- toolchain/microimage: a minimal container image (micro-toolchain:ci-compact) with only the linters and test harness required for fast lanes. This reduces container startup and image pull time on ephemeral runners.
- scripts/dep-pruner: an "atomic dep pruner" that computes the minimal set of packages touched by a change, runs a lockfile dry-run, and emits a compact patch to the lockfile rather than a full replace. When the change touches only docs or examples, the pruner can opt to skip the lockfile touch entirely.
- ci/orchestrator: small changes to our presubmit orchestration to accept the shim's job list and to gate expanded pipelines behind an explicit consent step (comment / label) for larger changes.

Design notes: 
- Safety first: the shim never skips coverage or security scans for code that touches core runtime packages. Path rules are conservative and live in repo-owned YAML so they can be iterated without code changes.
- Incremental dep updates: the pruner produces a separate commit (automatically attached to the PR) with a deterministic header and a one-line changelog so reviewers can easily approve or reject lockfile deltas.
- Opt-in rollout: feature flag + bot comment flow; default remains full presubmit for critical directories (runtime/, serving/).

Checklist:
- [x] shim binary and tests (unit + integration against sample diffs)
- [x] microimage Dockerfile + smallsize verification on our runner fleet
- [x] dep-pruner proof-of-concept and lockfile patch generator
- [x] presubmit orchestrator wiring and feature-flag gating
- [x] docs: CONTRIBUTING.md section + internal runbook for troubleshooting fastpath cases

Testing performed:
- Benchmarked 120 small PRs (docs/examples) on ephemeral runners: median presubmit reduced from 13m to 3m; 82% of those PRs completed without touching full integration lanes.
- Verified lockfile patches for 18 representative dep changes (node/python) and ensured deterministic diffs across two CI runs.
- Runbook smoke tests: bot-driven opt-in, rollback, and forced-full-run flows validated.

Rollout plan:
1) Enable as opt-in for engineers via label / comment.
2) After one week of opt-in (monitoring acceptance/error rates), enable for docs/* and examples/* paths by default.
3) Gradually expand to other low-risk directories.

Risks & mitigations:
- Over-eager skipping: path rules are conservative; we also added a per-PR safety check that automatically escalates to full presubmit if changed file list contains runtime/ or infra/ paths.
- Lockfile divergence: pruner produces small, reviewable commits and a deterministic stamp; regressions will be caught by a lightweight lockfile-verify job that runs in the expanded lane.

Related: ENG-1223 (presubmit velocity), ENG-9801 (dep hygiene), SUP-431 (customer incident that motivated faster rollback).

Notes for reviewers: focus reviews on path-rule correctness and the safety gating (orchestrator changes). I recommend running the integration harness with a few real PR diffs listed in the runbook.

Summary of changes and why: This reduces CI noise, accelerates small edits, and introduces an audited path for lockfile changes so reviewers aren't surprised by large transitive updates. The approach favors small, deterministic changes over large lockfile churns, improving throughput for the engineering org.
init: add presubmit shim binary and tests
ci: introduce micro-toolchain Dockerfile and CI image manifest
feat(dep-pruner): add lockfile patch generator and path-analysis module
ci: wire shim into presubmit orchestrator and add feature flag
docs: presubmit fastpath runbook and CONTRIBUTING update
chore: small refactors to runner caching and job metadata plumbing
Jordan Lee: Nice work — can we make the path-rule YAML opt-in per-team? I don't want infra rules accidentally overridden.
Ava Martinez: yes — added namespace support and validation tests; updated README to show team scoping
Priya Natarajan: observed flaky failure on ephemeral runner when microimage pulled; suggested adding retry and smaller layers
Ava Martinez: reduced layers and added retry logic to runner init; re-ran microimage verification
Samir Patel: approved after smoke run; requested a follow-up to add telemetry for skipped-presubmit counts
Jordan Lee: approval pending green metrics dashboard; verified 120-PR benchmark numbers
Introduce opt-in lightweight presubmit shim that significantly reduces feedback time for small edits; add atomic dep pruner to create minimal lockfile patches and a compact ci micro-image to speed runner startup. Feature gated and rolled out gradually.
Add telemetry for skipped-presubmit rates, add an automatic revert if skipped-presubmit leads to missed regressions, and iterate on path-rule coverage for more directories.

Context: Private deployments have diverse networking and secret storage topologies (node-local agents, projected KMS tokens, and external secret managers). We need a Helm-values-first approach to let operators select credential providers for init hooks and to schedule tenant init jobs with per-tenant rate, jitter and network-affinity profiles. This PR introduces a tenant-aware init scheduler and pluggable 'hook credential providers' for the Private Helm chart so operators can configure credential fetch semantics without patching templates. Motivation: reduce manual templating and ad-hoc post-install scripting during on-prem installs, and make upgrade/rollback safer by fencing init jobs on network prerequisites. What this PR does (summary): - Adds charts/private/values.schema.json additions describing new top-level keys: initScheduler, hookCredentialSources and networkPrereqs - Introduces templates: charts/private/templates/init-scheduler.yaml (CronJob-backed scheduler with per-tenant concurrency annotations), charts/private/templates/hook-credential-agent.yaml (sidecar/DaemonSet variant controlled by values), and charts/private/templates/_credential-helpers.tpl (sprig helpers and functions for provider selection) - Adds installer code: installer/hooks/credential_provider.go (small agent wrapper used for testing and local installers) - Adds e2e coverage: tests/e2e/private-init-network.test.ts and a fixture values file examples/values-private-credential-providers.yaml - Populates docs/values-hook-credential.md with recommended provider configurations (node-agent, projected-kms, external-vault) and migration instructions Migration path and operator notes: - New values are additive. Default behavior is unchanged: init jobs will continue to mount in-cluster secrets when hookCredentialSources is not set. - To opt into network-backed credentials, set hookCredentialSources.type to one of [node-agent, projected-kms, external-vault] and follow the docs for RBAC/volumeMount requirements. - For upgrades, a new values block initScheduler.fenceOnNetwork=true will gate init waves until a reachability probe succeeds (default off to avoid surprising long upgrades). Checklist: - [x] values.schema.json additions - [x] templates and helper functions - [x] minimal agent shim for installer tests - [x] unit tests for helper template functions - [x] e2e test covering network fence and credential retrieval - [x] docs and migration notes Commits: - chore(init-scheduler): scaffold tenant schedule template and CRD-like values - feat(credential-provider): add credential agent shim and helper template functions - test(e2e): add private init network e2e test and values fixture - docs: add values-hook-credential.md and migration guide - fix(helm): correct ownerReference handling and volume mount ordering Notes about implementation details: - The template helper _credential_provider takes the hookCredentialSources map and renders the appropriate volumes/volumeMounts for node-agent (hostPath + tolerations), projected-kms (projected service account token + projected config) and external-vault (CSI driver secret provider) - The init-scheduler is implemented as a namespaced CronJob that spawns tenant-specific Jobs with concurrencyPolicy set from values. We include annotations to allow Dedicated controllers to honor tenant throughput quotas. - The fence probe performs an HTTP/TCP check (configurable) against a values-defined endpoint and will pause rollout of subsequent tenant waves until check succeeds or timeout expires (values.initScheduler.fenceTimeout). CI: - unit (go/tests): pass - lint (helm/chart-lint): pass - e2e/private (k8s): initially flaky due to CI networking; second run passed. See ci/logs/1288883-e2e-run-2 for details Review summary and related Linear items: - Linked Linear: ENG-5219, ENG-6102 - Related support ticket SUP-8842 (customer requested node-attached hook secrets) Why this is different from previous hook work: previous PRs focused on sequencing and backoff semantics; this PR focuses on making credential sourcing pluggable and adding a network-aware fence for multi-tenant init waves. Backwards compatibility: no breaking changes by default; operators must opt into new providers.
- Added tenant-aware init scheduler with optional network fencing.
- Introduced hookCredentialSources to allow node-agent, projected-kms, or external-vault providers.
- New helper templates for credential wiring and migration guidance in docs/values-hook-credential.md.
Diego Alvarez (2025-11-13): Can we add a quick option to disable fence timeouts per-tenant? Some customers will prefer best-effort upgrades.
Maya Chen (2025-11-13): Added initScheduler.perTenantFenceTimeout with a sensible default and documented behavior.
Ravi Patel (2025-11-15): The helper template looks complex — please add unit tests for the sprig functions and an example values file for each provider.
Maya Chen (2025-11-16): Added unit tests for template helpers and three example value files under examples/; CI e2e initially failed due to flaky CI host networking, re-run passed.
Elena Morris (2025-11-18): Approved after verifying docs and e2e logs. Leaving a suggestion to monitor token refresh behavior for projected-kms in follow-up.

payload.body:
Motivation: We observed rapid cross-zone failovers during multi-zone pressure events that caused cascading cold-starts and SLO violations for high-priority tenants. This PR implements a zonal fallback condenser that reduces the frequency and breadth of cross-zone failovers by batching zone-level fallback decisions and applying a staggered drain to minimize simultaneous capacity movement. It also introduces an SLO-lease throttler which enforces short-duration request admission caps tied to per-tenant SLO credit windows (linked to ENG-12988 and SRE-402).

Summary of changes: 1) Fallback condenser: a coordinator that aggregates zone health signals and defers non-critical fallbacks for a small, randomized window to allow transient oscillations to stabilize. 2) Staggered drain: when an instance is marked for eviction, churn is reduced by phased connection draining with jittered offsets per shard. 3) SLO-lease throttler: a lightweight token bucket keyed by tenant SLO slices; integrates with existing prioritizer so critical routes are preserved. 4) Observability: added new metrics (zonal_fallback_decisions, zonal_drain_phases, slo_lease_rejections) and tracing spans for decision flow. 5) Safety: conservative default config and a runtime flag to opt-in per-deployment.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked in PR: Linear ENG-12988 overview
- [x] Unit tests for condenser state machine and lease accounting
- [x] Integration tests exercising staggered drain under simulated multi-zone load
- [x] End-to-end performance run verifying no statistically significant increase in median latency for mainline requests
- [x] Telemetry dashboards and alerts defined

Implementation notes: The condenser lives in serving/controlplane/fallback and exposes a small API consumed by the scheduler. Decision commits are timestamped and deduplicated for a 30s window to avoid flip-flops. The staggered drain uses per-shard seed derived from instance id to compute phase offsets; offsets are bounded (default 2–8s) to prevent long drains. SLO-lease throttler attaches to admission middleware and consults a compact in-memory lease table; leases decay linearly and can be bumped by emergency overrides from ops.

Testing and validation: Local unit/integration tests included under serving/controlplane/fallback/tests and admission/tests. Simulation harness (benchmark-lab/failover-sim) was used to replay a 2-hour production incident trace with condenser on/off toggles; condenser reduced multi-zone failover frequency by ~62% and decreased the number of concurrent cold-starts by 48% in the replay. Canary rollout was executed on a single staging zone for 24h before broad rollout.

Rollout plan: Feature gated via runtime flag fallback.condenser.enabled=false by default. 1) Canary on staging for 24h. 2) Canary to 10% of production traffic for 6h with close monitoring of slo.requests_p50/p95 and zonal_fallback_decisions. 3) Gradual increase to 50% then full rollout if metrics stable. 4) If any of slo.requests_p95 or error.rate increase by >10% relative to baseline, auto-rollback trigger will disable the feature.

Motivation: Our presubmit hygiene has drifted — stale lint configs, legacy release hooks, and duplicated cache warm logic add cognitive load and increase CI flakiness. This PR introduces a small, opt-in presubmit-groomer and a lightweight release-orchestrator to centralize release gate logic, reduce duplicate shell hooks, and provide a dry-run path for release validation. Summary of changes: bundled a new .github workflow (presubmit-groomer.yml) that runs nightly in dry-run mode and optionally mutates presubmit configs after a two-day observation window; added a release-orchestrator workflow that performs a staged dry-run (lint -> fast unit smoke -> lightweight artifact verification) before allowing tag creation; introduced scripts/ci/cache-prober.sh to exercise common caches and surface cold-cache penalties without blocking fast-feedback lanes; refactored tools/lint-adapter to accept stage-aware inputs so we only install heavy linters for final-stage checks; added infra/ci/runner-adapter.ts which provides a thin abstraction for runner capabilities and prevents double-triggering by release hooks; updated charts/release-hooks/values.yaml to route legacy hook consumers to the orchestrator. Testing: unit tests for runner-adapter and lint-adapter, e2e smoke for release-orch that simulates a dry-run release (CI job replays found in commits), and a staged rollout where presubmit-groomer starts in dry-run then moves to commit mode after 48h monitoring. Rollout plan: 1) merge to main behind a feature flag, 2) enable presubmit-groomer in dry-run for 48h and collect diffs, 3) flip to commit mode for low-risk repos only, 4) enable release-orchestrator in dry-run on a canary repo for one week, 5) expand if stable. Backout and recovery: groomer provides an allowlist and an explicit revert path (groomerctl snapshot + git revert); orchestrator provides an emergency bypass label and a one-click release via the Console for verified emergencies. CI and performance: added cache-prober with non-blocking timeout and exponential backoff to avoid lengthening fastpath CI; initial canary showed median presubmit runtime unchanged and a ~12% reduction in cold-cache retry rate for presubmit jobs. Security and permissions: release-orchestrator uses token-scoped credentials and requires a release:execute grant; presubmit-groomer only mutates .github configs from a service account with write-scoped perms. Related work: ENG-987 (presubmit hygiene initiative) and ENG-1024 (release automation groundwork). Follow-ups: bind presubmit-groomer to the dep-curation bot to auto-suggest package.json pruning, add RBAC audit events for configuration mutations, and add telemetry for how many groomer-suggested changes are accepted. Notes on review: addressed Arman's flake suggestion by adding retries + soft-timeouts; documented recovery steps at docs/ci/presubmit-groomer.md. Merge: squash-merged to main after final signoffs. This change targets infra and CI; no runtime production code paths were altered.
Introduce presubmit grooming job (dry-run then opt-in mutation), add a lightweight release orchestrator for pre-tag validations, add cache-prober for non-blocking cache warm checks, refactor lint adapter to stage-aware flow. Backwards compatible; feature gated and rolled out canary-first.

Summary: Implement a cohort-fenced model swap flow that provides session-consistent handover, automated rollback-replay for failing cohorts, and enhanced telemetry for per-cohort diagnostics. This PR introduces a new lifecycle controller component (cohort-fence controller), small runtime hooks to enforce session affinity during swaps, and a replay pipeline that captures request traces and payloads for repro.

Motivation and context: Customers running staged rollouts (canary, shadow, A/B) need deterministic semantics when a cohort is promoted or rolled back. Previously, partial traffic swaps could split sessions mid-flight (user experiences multiple model versions within a session) making debugging and quality validation difficult. In a recent incident (SUP-5123) we observed hard-to-reproduce regressions because rollback lacked deterministic replay for affected cohorts. This work implements three capabilities: (1) cohort fencing to guarantee session-consistent swapping, (2) an automated rollback-replay that replays captured cohort traffic against a candidate model snapshot, and (3) per-cohort telemetry (latency, token-cost, quality delta) surfaced to Console and to tracing backends.

Design highlights: - Cohort fence: a lightweight lease attached to routing metadata. When a cohort swap is initiated, the controller sets a fence lease and the router will maintain session affinity for the duration of the lease (configurable TTL). The fence improves safety for small, stateful cohorts and prevents split-session exposure during drain.
- Rollback-replay pipeline: on detection of safety gate violations (latency or quality thresholds), the controller marks cohort traffic for capture (sampling by cohort). Captured traces are stored in an encrypted replay bucket with metadata linking to the model build hash. A replay worker can then re-run requests against the previous model binary to reproduce the regression and produce a diff report.
- Telemetry: added cohort-level metrics (cohort.latency.p50/p95, cohort.token_cost.avg, cohort.quality.delta) and tracing spans that propagate model version and cohort_id. Console dashboards and SLO rules can now reference cohort.* metrics.

Checklist: - [x] Cohort fence controller implementation and unit tests - [x] Router affinity hooks and TTL enforcement - [x] Rollback capture and replay worker + e2e test harness - [x] Telemetry metrics + traces + Console dashboard wiring - [x] Migration docs and configuration defaults - [x] Performance benchmarks and microbench for router path

Files touched (high level): - services/rollout/controller/cohort_fence_controller.go (new) - services/router/affinity/lease_manager.go (changes) - services/capture/worker/ (new capture pipeline) - tools/replay/cli.py (new) - observability/metrics/cohort_metrics.yaml (new) - console/dashboards/cohort_rollouts.json (new) - tests/integration/cohort_swap_replay.test (new) - docs/rollouts/cohort-fence.md (new)

Small illustrative snippet (router lease check):

if fenceLease != nil && time.Now().Before(fenceLease.ExpiresAt) {
    // Preserve session affinity to original model until lease expiration
    chosenModel = fenceLease.ModelHash
} else {
    chosenModel = chooseByTrafficSplit(req)
}

Backward compatibility and migration notes: - Default TTL for cohort fence is conservative (30s) to avoid long-lived session pins; customers can tune via rollout policy. - Rollout objects that opt-in to capture must explicitly set capture: true; no existing rollouts are changed by default. - Replay artifacts are encrypted and retained per org retention policy (default 7 days).

Performance: Microbench results included in PR show router path overhead ~0.9% p50 and p95 increase under 99th percentile traffic profiles. Capturing path adds measurable I/O but is gated by sampling and cohort opt-in. Bench outputs attached to the PR artifacts.

How to test locally: - Start local rollout controller: make run-controller - Apply sample rollout with cohort fence enabled: kubectl apply -f examples/cohort_swap.yaml - Trigger a swap and observe cohort.* metrics in prometheus-local and trace spans in Jaeger-local. - Run replay CLI against captured bucket: tools/replay/cli.py replay --cohort-id <id> --model-hash <hash>

Migration docs: docs/rollouts/cohort-fence.md contains configuration knobs, examples for A/B and canary flows, and operator playbook for handling captured artifacts and replay analysis.

- Adds rollback-replay pipeline to reproduce failing cohorts;
- Improvements to rollout telemetry and tracing for faster incident triage.

Motivation: Our monolithic CI workflows have grown brittle and slow; long lint/test pipelines and duplicated scripts across repos increase maintenance overhead and merge friction. This PR introduces a lightweight orchestrator shim that standardizes stage-aware routing (fastpath/check/slow) and consolidates common bootstraps while performing repo-tooling hygiene and dependency pruning. Summary of changes: 1) New ci/orchestrator/handler.go + shim scripts that provide a small declarative stage map and load balancing between fastpath and full integration lanes. 2) Replace legacy bash lint bootstraps with a typed Node.js runner (ci/lint-runner) that supports staged sharding and caching. 3) Add a release preflight job (ci/preflight-check) which validates toolchain versions, signed changelog presence, and pinlist drift to prevent silent dependency breaks. 4) Remove unused devDependencies in package.json across repo roots and add a devdep-audit script to CI. 5) Consolidate action inputs and standardize cache keys to reduce flakiness and improve cross-repo reuse. Test plan and verification: - Local unit + integration runs for the orchestrator (go test, node unit tests). - CI smoke lane exercises fastpath and full-lane fallbacks. - Ran dep-audit against current repo state and fixed three transient transitive deps. - Manual release dry-run using the new preflight check. Why this approach: The orchestrator is intentionally lightweight (under 200 LOC for the core decision layer) and designed to be opt-in per repo via a small ci/config.yaml. It reduces duplication while preserving per-repo exceptions. Rollout plan: 1) Apply to redwood monorepo as opt-in on a few high-velocity packages (sdk-python, redwood, redwood-devtools). 2) Monitor presubmit latency and failure rate for two weeks. 3) Flip to default once metrics show >20% reduction in median presubmit latency and <3% regression in flaky test rate. Backwards compatibility: Existing workflows are preserved and the shim falls back to legacy behavior when ci/config.yaml is absent. Linked work: ENG-4821 (orchestrator core), ENG-4823 (presubmit sharding), related to prior dep hygiene efforts. Context and motivation: customer telemetry and recent prefilling/quant autosuggest work showed recurring incidents where tenant-level cost constraints and aggressive quantization profiles resulted in customer-visible quality regressions or unexpected bill spikes. We need a lightweight, auditable, and testable way to declare cost-safeguard policies that translate directly into runtime checks and CI-time linting. This PR introduces a small domain-specific language (Policy DSL) for cost safeguards, a runtime runner that enforces soft/ hard limits at the routing and serving layers, and a CI linter (unit-econ-lint) that validates tenant policy bundles before merge.

What this PR delivers: (1) redwood/costpolicy: a compact Policy DSL (YAML-first, JSON-compatible) and compiler that emits guard rules for the router and the serving runtime; (2) redwood/costpolicy/runner: evaluation library used by the gateway and by Dedicated control plane to block or attenuate requests that would violate tenant policies; (3) CLI: redwood policy apply/dry-run/compile for operators and SEs to validate changes; (4) unit-econ-lint: a CI plugin that validates policy semantics, checks for unreachable rules, and simulates sample workloads to spot risky quantization + batch combos; (5) integration shim in router to perform O(1) policy checks per request and a fallback path that will switch to conservative quant/profiles when a soft threshold is hit.

Design highlights: the DSL centers on three primitives: thresholds (absolute and relative cost/unit), signals (latency, token-rate, quality-regress indicators), and actions (attenuate-batch-size, prefer-legacy-model, refuse-model, downgrade-quant-profile). Policies are scoped at organization, tenant, and route levels. The compiler produces a compact decision graph that the runner evaluates with minimal allocations. The decision graph supports short-circuiting, stochastic rate-limiting, and graceful fallbacks (e.g. prefer-legacy-model + cached-response on overload).

Migration & rollout plan: default_policy.yaml is introduced as an admin-managed tenant fallback. No tenant changes by default. We roll the runner behind a feature flag, first in staging (2 days soak with traffic mirroring), then Canary in us-west with 5% traffic, then progressive ramp on Dedicated tenants who opt-in. The CLI supports dry-run modes for admins to preview simulated unit economics changes.

Testing and benchmarks: added unit tests (compiler semantics, edge-case precedence), integration tests (router + runner end-to-end), and a microbenchmark showing ~0.9us median overhead per request for the O(1) check in the router when the decision graph is cached. Load test scenarios included a stress profile where aggressive quant + large batch would previously exceed predicted unit cost; the runner prevented a spike by switching to conservative quant profile automatically.

Checklist:
- [x] DSL spec and examples (docs included)
- [x] Compiler and decision-graph output format stable
- [x] Runtime runner integrated with router and dedicated control plane
- [x] CLI commands with dry-run and compile subcommands
- [x] unit-econ-lint CI check added to policy directories
- [x] Migration guide and rollout playbook included
- [x] Performance microbench and integration load test results attached

Related work and references: builds on prior prefilling and quant profile work (see ENG-2154, pr-34177, pr-524681) but focuses on operational guardrails rather than autosuggest. Also complements cost-snapshotter telemetry changes in pr-104202.

Release notes: operational feature - add Policy DSL and runtime policy runner; admins can define tenant cost-safeguards (default off). Backwards-compatible by default but recommended for high-spend tenants.

High-level commits summary: 1) add DSL spec + examples; 2) implement compiler and serializer; 3) implement runner and router hook; 4) add CLI and dry-run; 5) unit-econ-lint CI integration; 6) docs + migration guide + tests.

Files of interest changed: see files_changed list below.

How to exercise locally: see docs/costpolicy/README.md - compile sample policy and run redwood policy dry-run --sample-traffic=small; to simulate failover use policy action refuse-model/downgrade-quant-profile.

Security considerations: policies are validated server-side and only admin-scoped policies can perform hard refusals. The runner enforces policy decisions within the serving process; no new network paths introduced. Audit logs added for every policy-triggered action for compliance and postmortem.

Rollout notes for SRE and Support: we added a feature flag redwood.policy_runner.enabled and a per-tenant opt-in toggle. SRE playbook included in docs/playbooks/policy-runner-incident-playbook.md.

Migration note for SDKs: no immediate SDK changes; we will expose a policy validation endpoint in the API in a follow-up small PR.

Maya Chen — Responding: added deterministic precedence rules and an example in spec.md; compiler emits a version field in the graph for compatibility and we validate on load.
