Context: Customers frequently see unit-cost regressions when cold-starts and early-batch shapes are not tuned to tenant traffic. Existing autotuners focus on steady-state batching and quantization; early warmup (seed) behavior is under-optimized and requires manual profiles. Motivation: provide an automated, conservative warmup profile generator plus a safe quantization recommender that ties recommendations to workload signatures and unit-econ estimates. This PR introduces two cooperating pieces: (1) Budgetcraft seed-warmup trainer: a workload-driven component that ingests recent trace samples and produces tenant-scoped warmup presets (initial batch sizes, initial cache prefix heuristics, and staged batch ramps). (2) Quantization Sherpa: a service that runs lightweight evaluation of quant candidates against representative prompt sets and returns a ranked set of quant profiles annotated with expected unit-cost delta and an estimated quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE/similarity proxies + config-specific thresholds). Design summary: - Budgetcraft operates as an offline trainer (cron + on-demand) that consumes sample windows emitted by the workload-sampler component. It scores candidate warmup ramps using a cost-weighted utility function that emphasizes early latency SLOs and conservative cost improvements. Output is a namespaced preset (tenant: preset-id) stored in the defaults registry and surfaced through the Optimize API. - Quantization Sherpa is a separate binary/service with a small sandbox harness. It runs quant trials using cached model shards and feeds eval metrics into a simple calibration model that maps quality deltas to user-facing risk levels (low/medium/high). Sherpa never auto-applies anything; it returns recommendations and a deterministic fallback policy for runtime use. Key changes: - runtime/prefill/seed_trainer.py: new trainer, sampling adapters, scoring function, and presets export. - optimize/quant_sherpa/service.go: new Go service that runs quant trials and exposes a recommendation API. - console/docs/cost-automation.md: new documentation page with guidance and example presets. - api/optimize/v1/types.proto: small additions for preset metadata and risk-level annotations. - charts/helm/templates/budgetcraft.yaml: helm template to deploy the trainer and sherpa in Private/Dedicated clusters. - tests/integration/prefill_trainer_integration_test.py: integration tests validating sample ingestion and preset creation. - ci/workflows/prefill-trainer-ci.yml: new CI workflow that runs unit/integration and e2e smoke tests in parallel. Migration/compatibility: - Defaults registry format extended with optional fields (warmup_ramp/v1). Clients that read presets will ignore unknown keys. - Sherpa recommendations include a stable recommendation-id and do not change runtime routing unless an explicit rollout action is taken. Rollout plan: 1) Internal dogfood: enable Budgetcraft for a small set of internal tenants (low traffic) for 2 weeks. 2) Monitor unit-econ drift, early latency SLOs, and quality regression alerts via Redwood Console dashboards (new panels added). 3) If green, expose recommendations to customers in Optimize Console (opt-in) and allow one-click apply for tenant admins. Tests: - Unit tests for scoring function and config serialization. - Integration tests that replay sampled traces and assert preset creation. - End-to-end smoke test: deploy trainer + sherpa in a test namespace and run a small trial against a canned workload. Security & privacy: Trainer operates on anonymized traces (hashed tenant ids and prompt fingerprints). Sherpa runs only on model variants available in the cluster and does not upload prompts externally. Open items / follow-ups: - Hook recommendations into the rollout CLI (follow-up PR that implements guarded apply with canary). - Add more robust quality metrics (human eval integration) for certain tenant classes. - Consider an online lightweight trainer for very high-throughput tenants. Related tickets: ENG-2187 (seed warmup initiative), ENG-2210 (quant recommendation telemetry).

Evelyn Park (author): Addressed — added bootstrap tests and switched to streaming JSONL ingestion to reduce peak memory. PTAL.
Asha Mehta: Need clearer telemetry around 'quality delta' — can Sherpa emit per-trial histograms we can hook into alerts?
Evelyn Park (author): Added trial-level histograms and an aggregate risk summary metric (optimize.quant_sherpa.trial_quality_hist).
Diego Fernandez: CI flake on integration e2e (env race) — re-ran workflow, green now. Approving.
Marcus Liu: Approved after minor nits (variable naming) — squashed commits and merged.
Introduce Budgetcraft seed-warmup trainer (automated warmup presets) and Quantization Sherpa (safe quant recommendations). Adds new Optimize API fields and Helm chart for deployment. Backwards-compatible defaults registry extension. Opt-in for customers via Optimize Console.

Context: Customers frequently ask for prescriptive starting points that balance latency, throughput, and unit cost for new workloads. Our existing recommendations are dispersed across docs, examples, and internal heuristics, which makes onboarding and repeatability hard. This PR introduces an automated Cost Playbook Generator: a small rule-driven engine that synthesizes tiling (batching + prefill) presets and quantization profile suggestions from a workload fingerprint. The output is a human-readable playbook (YAML) and a machine-usable preset that can be consumed by the autoscaler and the optimizer CLI.

What this change does: 1) new package pkg/econ/playbook_generator.go implementing a rule engine that maps workload signals (avg seq len, percentile tail latency, tokens/sec, qps distribution) to a prioritized set of presets; 2) tiling presets declared under cmd/tiling/presets.yaml capturing target batch shapes, max-latency budgets, prefilling thresholds and fallback strategies; 3) quantization profile recommendations in pkg/quant/profiles/defaults.json with compatibility hints for fp16/int8/4bit candidates; 4) a small simulator harness internal/sim that validates presets against synthetic traces and produces estimated unit cost deltas used by the generator; 5) CLI helper scripts (scripts/ci/generate_playbooks.sh) and Python SDK bindings (sdk/python/redwood/econ/playbook.py) to export and apply playbooks; 6) documentation (docs/econ-playbooks.md and website/docs/automation/cost-playbooks.md) and an end-to-end test (tests/e2e/econ_playbook_e2e.go).

Design notes: The playbook is intentionally conservative by default: each suggested preset includes a safety band (latency buffer and a fallback quant profile) to avoid regressions. The rule engine is extensible: new rules are added to pkg/econ/rules.go (single-file today) and unit-tested. The decision path is recorded in the generated YAML under metadata.decision_path to help SRE and customers understand the rationale. We also added telemetry hooks (tools/telemetry/econ-metrics.yaml) to measure playbook adoption and delta to unit cost over the first 48 hours after rollout.

Asha (author): "Added mapping field in decision_path and included Linear IDs for the initial ruleset (ENG-2109, ENG-2112)." Sofia Nguyen: "Simulator looks good — can we make synthetic traces configurable by seed so teams can reproduce results?" Asha: "Added seed parameter and deterministic mode in internal/sim, documented in the README." Diego Marquez: "One nit: prefer smaller default batch cap for G5x nodes to avoid GPU OOM with long prefixes." Asha: "Lowered G5x default cap to 128 and added explicit guardrails in presets.yaml."

CI and stability: The PR exercise runs unit tests, linters, and a lightweight e2e on staging. One intermittent flake in the simulator test was debugged and fixed (race on pseudo-random generator). All CI jobs reported green on the final run.

Why this is different: Instead of a single tune-for-cost heuristic, this work produces explainable, versioned playbooks that can be iterated and rolled out safely (canary via rollout policy). It bridges docs, autoscaler configs, and optimizer suggestions into a single artifact that teams can review and apply.

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: a too-aggressive quant suggestion might cause quality regression. Mitigation: every quant recommendation includes a fallback and we added an eval hook so teams can gate rollouts on minimum quality thresholds. - Risk: incorrect presets for niche workloads. Mitigation: playbooks are advisory and require opt-in; the generator includes a confidence score and a "manual review recommended" flag for low-confidence suggestions.

Next steps: - Expose a REST endpoint in the Console to preview playbooks (follow-up PR) - Add a policy compiler that translates playbooks into autoscaler + optimizer rules - Expand the ruleset with tenant-specific historical footprints

Related: ENG-2109 (playbook generator), ENG-2112 (tiling presets canonicalization), internal note: /docs/internal/econ-playbooks-notes.md

Merge outcome: Merged via squash after approvals by Liam, Sofia and Diego.
Introduce a Cost Playbook Generator that synthesizes tiling and quantization presets from workload fingerprints. Includes conservative defaults, simulator-backed scoring, SDK bindings, and docs. Playbooks are advisory and include fallbacks to prevent regressions.
This PR is intentionally conservative; follow-up work will add Console preview and per-tenant historical weighting for stronger suggestions. Telemetry will be monitored for 30 days post-rollout to validate unit-econ impact.

payload.body:
Context: customers reported unstable streams when a model emitted a tool/function call followed by immediate token streaming resume from a fallback model or when stop arrays and role aliases were present. This PR implements a more robust tool-handshake and stream-resume protocol that preserves OpenAI /v1/chat.completions semantics while enabling our internal optimizations.

What this changes: a) Introduces a handshake envelope for function/tool call boundaries so the stream can be cleanly suspended and resumed across model variants or retries; b) Adds a lightweight coordinator that computes weighted-stop heuristics and falls back to logprob-based termination when a stop sequence is partially emitted at stream boundaries; c) Normalizes role aliases (system/user/assistant) earlier in the pipeline to avoid duplicate role tokens in the prefill and while reconstructing deltas; d) Adds a compatibility gate (request header: X-OpenAI-Compat-V1) so customers can opt into v1-like behavior without changing their existing routing rules; e) Adds integration tests that simulate mid-stream fncall handoffs and partial stop sequences.

Implementation notes: the handshake is implemented as a framed JSON control message inserted between data CHUNKs. The coordinator maintains a small in-memory state machine per request (suspended, awaiting_ack, resumed) scoped to the connection ID. When a resume is requested and the target model cannot guarantee identical tokenization, we emit an idempotent resume envelope that instructs the client to rehydrate the last N tokens (configurable via compat param) or accept a logprob-fallback close. The weighted-stop heuristic computes candidate stop points across role boundaries and backfills stop-sentinels when the stream resumes to preserve deterministic termination behavior.

Backward compatibility: default behavior is unchanged. The new code path is behind the X-OpenAI-Compat-V1 header and a server-side feature flag. Migration plan includes a staged rollout, canary on 5% of production traffic, and a rollback knob.

Checklist:
- [x] Handshake envelope format and parsing implemented
- [x] Coordinator state machine with timeout and ack handling
- [x] Weighted-stop heuristic + logprob fallback path
- [x] Role alias normalization pass added to prefill
- [x] Integration + unit tests covering resume, partial stop, and fncall handoff
- [x] Documentation updated (compat guide + header semantics)

Related: Linear ENG-1984 tracks stream stability work. See SUP-8421 for customer incident that motivated this.

Summary of commits: single logical change implemented across runtime, api compatibility shim, and tests. Commits are squashed on merge.
Improves /v1/chat.completions OpenAI compatibility: streaming resume after function/tool calls, better handling for stop arrays and weighted stop heuristics, safer logprob fallback when tokens are omitted. No customer-facing API change required; opt-in behind a compat flag for now.
Main discussion centered on resume safety across tokenizer boundaries and how to surface the compat gate to customers.
Decided to keep default behavior unchanged and require explicit X-OpenAI-Compat-V1 header to opt in.
Follow-ups: add per-route perf telemetry (ENG-2003) and a backfill job to annotate historical logs with handshake events.
Jonah Kim: Left a couple of nit comments around timeouts and a question on whether the resume 'rehydrate N tokens' is safe across quantized kernels.
Aisha Verma (author): Answered - rehydrate N tokens is conservative (default 8) and is configurable per-route; added a test for cross-quantized-handoffs.
Lina Chen: Asked to add more logging fields (handoff_id, orig_model, target_model) to make postmortems easier. Requested a follow-up for perf impact analysis.
Mateo Ruiz: Approved after tests stabilized and CI flaked once but passed on rerun.
CI Bot: Integration tests passed (5/5), lint checks passed, flake detected in streaming integration on first run, reran and green.

payload.body:
Motivation: tighten operator privileges and improve region-aware audit provenance for operator-initiated actions. Production incidents in Q4 highlighted cases where long-lived operator credentials and ambiguous audit anchors complicated investigations across geo-replicated tenants. This PR introduces three coordinated changes: 1) scoped operator credentials with explicit region and action constraints (operator-credential-scopes), 2) per-region audit anchors that bind operator actions to a canonical region assertion and KMS provenance header, and 3) optional RBAC v2 temporal constraints (timebound grants) that allow operators to request short-lived elevation with automatic expiry.

Summary of changes (single-line checklist): 
- Add operator credential scope data model and validation in account-service and operator-service.
- KMS integration: add signed region-anchor header and minor helper in kms-client to produce per-request provenance stamps.
- Audit service: add anchor stitching that attaches region-anchor and operator-credential-hash to every operator audit event.
- Policy engine: extend RBAC v2 policy schema with a "time_window" field and evaluation path for timebound grants.
- CLI/agent: add operator token request flow and a new --region flag to the operator login flow; include client-side TTL enforcement.
- Tests: unit and integration tests for validation paths, plus e2e test that simulates cross-region operator action and verifies anchor.

Design notes: 
- Operator credential scopes are intentionally narrow: a scope contains {actor_id, allowed_actions[], allowed_resources[], region_affinity, max_ttl_seconds}. Operator tokens (JWT) issued by operator-service are signed and include a credential-hash claim to simplify server-side revocation checks.
- Per-region audit anchors are small signed envelopes produced by KMS with the claim {region, anchor_id, issued_at, kms_sig}. The audit service verifies the envelope signature and stores the anchor_id with the audit event. This enables downstream compliance pipelines to filter/aggregate by asserted region without relying on mutable request headers.
- RBAC v2 temporal constraints are additive and backward-compatible: existing policies without time_window behave as before. Policies that include time_window require the request context to have a matching timestamp within the window; the policy evaluator caches the parsed time_window for performance.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan: 
- Feature-flag controlled rollout (ff.operator_scopes + ff.region_audit_anchor + ff.rbac_timebound). Flags default to off in staging clusters.
- Phase 1: enable operator token issuance flow and KMS anchor stamping for a subset of operator roles (canary).
- Phase 2: enable audit stitching + collector indexing change (no enforcement).
- Phase 3: enable timebound RBAC evaluation for select teams and observe effects in policy-sim dashboards.

Testing and validation: 
- Unit tests added for operator-service validation, kms-client anchor creation, and rbac policy parser.
- Integration tests: operator-service -> api-gateway -> audit-service path using test KMS key.
- e2e scenario: create tenant T1 in us-west, operator request scoped token with region_affinity=us-west, perform action, verify audit anchor stored and KMS signature validated.

Security review: implemented HSM-backed signing via existing KMS client. Token rotation and revocation paths are supported through credential-hash and revocation-list lookups in account-service. No plaintext secrets added to codebase; environment flags used to select KMS key ARN.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: mis-specified region_affinity may bottleneck cross-region operator workflows. Mitigation: allow region_affinity to be a list and implement fallback policy (operator-service issues short-lived cross-region allowances after additional approvals).
- Risk: additional latency for audit anchor verification. Mitigation: verification is async for ingestion path and syntactic checks performed in the hot path; heavy crypto is offloaded to a bounded worker pool.

Related Linear items: ENG-3124, ENG-3378.

Notes for reviewers: focus on operator-service token issuance and policy evaluator changes. There is a small API bump for operator-token request payload; I included a compatibility shim in api-gateway to accept legacy requests and map fields.

Merge outcome: squash and merge after all checks pass.
Diego Alvarez: Please ensure the operator token rotation path is resilient to partial revocation propagation. Suggest adding a reconciliation job.
Maya Patel: Added revocation reconciliation as a background job in account-service (see c8d0910). Also added credential-hash to tokens to simplify lookup.
Priya Singh: lgtm overall. Two nits: clarify TTL units in CLI help and move expensive crypto off hot path.
Maya Patel: addressed both nits; updated CLI help and offloaded signature verification to worker pool in audit-service.
Liam O'Connor: Approved — verified e2e in staging; latency overhead < 4ms p50 on request path.
payload.title: Scoped operator credentials, per-region audit anchors, and RBAC v2 temporal constraints

payload.body:
Motivation: Customers requested stronger guarantees that KMS operations and audit headers are only allowed when tenant attributes (region, residency_class, and consent flags) align with key provenance. This PR implements an attribute-bound RBAC v2 guard and a lightweight KMS provenance mediator that validates KMS selection and injects immutable audit claims.

What this PR does (single-string summary):
- Introduces an attribute-fencing policy layer for RBAC v2 that evaluates explicit tenant attributes in the request context (tenant.region, tenant.residency_class, tenant.opt_in_kms_consent). Policies are declarative YAML under rbac_v2/policies/attribute_fence/*.yaml.
- Adds kms/provenance-mediator service: verifies candidate KMS provider locations against tenant attributes and signs a short-lived provenance token that downstream services must present to perform key operations.
- Adds an enforcement shim in the API gateway that rejects key-use when provenance token and tenant attributes mismatch, and emits sealed audit headers.
- Adds migration script to convert a subset of legacy role bindings to attribute-aware templates.

Design highlights and examples:
- Policy example (rbac_v2/policies/attribute_fence/tenant_region.yaml):
  condition: "request.attributes.tenant.region == resource.kms_region && request.attributes.tenant.opt_in_kms_consent == true"
- Provenance mediator: signs provenance token with service KMS and attaches header "X-KMS-Provenance" and an immutable audit tag "x-rrw-audit-tenant". Downstream services validate token expiry and the included kms_region claim.
- Fallback behavior: if tenant.opt_in_kms_consent is false, requests to region-mismatched KMS will be rejected with 403 and a clear error code (ERR_KMS_PROVENANCE_MISMATCH).

Checklist:
- [x] Spec and design doc (Linear: ENG-4217) attached
- [x] Unit tests for attribute evaluator and policy loader
- [x] Integration test that exercises mediator + gateway enforcement (flaky in CI, rerun passed)
- [x] Migration tool with dry-run mode
- [x] Docs: security/rbac/attribute-fence.md and operator notes in private-installer/README.md

Testing & rollout plan:
- Canary rollout using feature flag: rbac.attribute_fence.enabled per region. Start with US-East non-production, validate audit spikes and latency under load.
- Monitor metrics: kms.provenance.validation.latency, rbac.attribute_evaluator.failures, audit.forwarder.drop_rate. Default alert thresholds added to observability-pack dashboards.
- Rollback: disable feature flag, gateway rejects are replaced by permissive allow if in audit-only mode.

Backward compatibility and security impact:
- Backwards compatible by default (attribute_fence disabled). When enabled for a tenant, any mismatch causes explicit denial — this is a functional change for those tenants who opt in. Security posture improved by preventing accidental cross-region KMS use.

Migration notes:
- Migration script (tools/migrations/convert-bindings-attribute-aware.py) lists candidate bindings and can run in dry-run to produce a Linear ticket for manual approval.

References: ENG-4217, ENG-4389, SUP-1223.

Diego Marquez (review): The attribute checker looks good; please add a unit test for null tenant.region and ensure the policy loader rejects policies without explicit 'condition' field.
Author (Leah Park): Added null handling tests and a validation pass for missing condition. See commit 3rd. Also added a short note in docs that missing attributes produce explicit denies when enforcement is enabled.
Sofia Chen (review): Concern about latency — mediator adds an extra roundtrip. Can we cache provenance tokens per request window?
Author (Leah Park): Implemented a short-lived token cache (60s) keyed by (tenant_id, kms_region). Added metrics kms.provenance.cache.hit/miss and baseline numbers to observability dashboard. See commit 'perf: cache provenance tokens'.
Omar Hassan (security review): Approve after you sign the mediator image and add a small e2e asserting that the gateway rejects mismatched region with correct audit header.
Author (Leah Park): Added image signature verification step in the CI stage and the e2e. CI flake occurred on integration test; reran and it passed.
Adds opt-in attribute-bound RBAC policies and a KMS provenance mediator that prevents cross-region key use when tenant attributes do not match. Introduces audit headers for non-repudiation and a migration tool to convert role bindings to attribute-aware templates. Disabled by default; enable via feature flag per-tenant.
payload.title: Attribute-bound RBAC v2 and KMS provenance mediator with tenant consent orchestrator

payload.body:
Title: Introduce compact bootstrap images and atomic dependency reconciler to speed presubmit feedback

Description: This PR reduces presubmit latency and flakiness by introducing two coordinated changes: (1) compact bootstrap images + a minimal local runner shim that cuts toolchain and network setup time for fast-presubmit lanes, and (2) an atomic dependency reconciler that can apply consistent lockfile updates across workspace modules and generate a small, auditable reconciliation plan. The changes are intentionally conservative and gated behind a new fast-presubmit lane so we can measure impact before widening.

Motivation and context: Our presubmit feedback median has increased due to expanding toolchains and noisy devcontainer bootstraps. Teams frequently open dependency PRs that drift the lockfiles for different workspace modules; that leads to duplicate CI work and merge conflicts. This work combines an engineering effort to reduce CI setup time (compact bootstrap images + minimal-runner) with an infra tool (dep-reconciler) to make dependency updates atomic and reproducible. Related: ENG-3241 (presubmit fast-lane), SUP-1123 (support ticket for lockfile drift).

What this PR changes (high-level):
- Add ci/images/compact-bootstrap.Dockerfile: a trimmed build image that contains only the runtimes and tools required for lint/typed-check quickpaths.
- Add ci/workflows/presubmit-fast.yml: a new GitHub Actions workflow for fast-presubmit lanes that uses the compact image and a minimal-runner script. This workflow runs lint, typecheck, and unit smoke tests.
- Add scripts/bootstrap-minimal.sh: shell shim to bootstrap the repo in < 20s by reusing cached toolchain layers and skipping heavy steps (no full install, no generated-bindings).
- Add tools/dep-reconciler/: small Go CLI that inspects go.mod/package.json/yarn.lock variants across modules, computes a reconciled lockfile set, and emits a single patch (with provenance) that can be applied or opened as a PR. Includes a --dry-run and --apply mode and an opt-in Linear integration.
- Update ci/helpers/cache-primer.sh to be cache-aware for the compact image and to warm workspace metadata used by the minimal runner.
- Tests and CI: unit tests for dep-reconciler, smoke tests for minimal bootstrap, integration job that validates reconciler output on a sample workspace.

Commits (summary):
- 37f3a2b: introduce compact-bootstrap image and minimal-runner shim
- 4a9e71c: add fast-presubmit workflow and cache primer updates
- 9b0c2f1: add dep-reconciler CLI, unit tests, and sample reconciliation plan

Files changed (high-level):
- ci/images/compact-bootstrap.Dockerfile
- ci/workflows/presubmit-fast.yml
- scripts/bootstrap-minimal.sh
- tools/dep-reconciler/main.go
- tools/dep-reconciler/plan_test.go
- ci/helpers/cache-primer.sh (updated)
- docs/ci/fast-presubmit.md (new)
- .github/labels/ci-annotations.md (updated)

Testing performed:
- Local: built compact image, executed bootstrap-minimal.sh on mac/linux, measured cold vs warmed startup times (cold: ~120s -> warmed: ~18s for lint path).
- Unit: dep-reconciler tests cover semver merge behavior and detection of conflicting manifests.
- CI: new presubmit-fast lane included in this PR; initial runs had one flaky external network job which was retried and passed. Full matrix kept on the standard presubmit workflows to preserve coverage.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Ethan Kim (reviewer): "Nice reduction in setup time numbers. Concern: compact image might diverge from full build images and mask issues. Can we add an optional 'integration smoke' step that runs full-build in weekly scheduled job?"
- Maya (author): "Agree — added docs/ci/fast-presubmit.md to call out scope and added a weekly ci/workflows/presubmit-fast-integration.yml as a follow-up task (ENG-3287) to run full-builds on a sample subset. Kept the fast lane explicitly limited to lint/typecheck/unit-smoke for now."

- Sofia Morales: "dep-reconciler looks promising. Please add clear auditing info to the plan output (timestamp, git sha, module sources). Also ensure reconcile changes are not auto-applied without a PR in the default mode."
- Maya: "Plan output includes provenance fields and default behavior is --dry-run. --apply requires explicit flag and a service token; documented in docs/ci/dep-reconciler.md."

- Ravi Desai: "We should ensure that cache-primer changes are safe for existing runners and do not evict shared caches. Also add a small metric to track fast-presubmit success rate."
- Maya: "Adjusted cache-primer to scope cache keys to 'compact:' prefix. Added a basic CloudMetrics counter 'ci.fast_presubmit.success' increment on workflow completion; metric emitted via existing CI telemetry hook."

Author followups and fixes: 
- Reworked minimal runner to explicitly fail fast if missing critical tools rather than silently continuing.
- Reduced docker layer size by splitting the compact image into two stages and removing optional debugging packages.
- Added a small integration test that runs the reconciler against a synthetic multi-module workspace to verify patch semantics.

CI summary:
- Run 1: presubmit-fast initially failed due to external network flakiness in sample e2e fetch — retried run passed.
- Lint/test suites: pass on fast lane; full presubmit matrix unchanged and passed on this branch.
- Security scan: compact image scanned with Trivy; flagged no high-severity issues. Dep-reconciler dependencies are pinned and included in go.sum.

Rollout plan: 
- Enable fast-presubmit for core repos only for two weeks behind a feature flag. Collect telemetry (median presubmit start time, success rate, cache hit rate).
- Run ENG-3287 scheduled weekly integration job that executes full builds on a small sample to catch regressions.
- After two weeks and positive metrics, extend to more teams and add an automated bot that opens reconciler PRs on --apply requests.

Backward compatibility and risk: 
- No runtime or API compatibility changes. All changes are CI infra and tooling. The compact image intentionally omits heavy build-time artifacts so there is a risk of masking build-specific regressions; mitigations described above (weekly integration, preserved full presubmit). Dep-reconciler will not auto-apply changes unless explicitly requested.

Notes for maintainers: 
- The dep-reconciler code includes a small embedded example under tools/dep-reconciler/testdata/ that maintainers can run with 'go test ./... -run TestPlan'.
- The compact bootstrap Dockerfile includes a VERSION label; bump when base toolchain changes.

Merge outcome: Squash merged into main. Attribution: Maya Patel (author). Merge commit created and small follow-up cleanup PR opened to rename a script var (pr-197622).

If you'd like a follow-up: I can split the dep-reconciler into its own repo and add a GitHub App to open reconciliation PRs automatically (future work)."
Introduces fast presubmit lint path and compact bootstrap images to reduce CI setup time; adds an atomic dependency reconciler to harmonize lockfiles across repo modules. No user-facing API changes.

payload.body:
Context: During a cross-region capacity surge incident on 2024-12-28 we observed rapid circuit flips and noisy tenant reopen events causing cascading evictions and increased tail latency for best-effort workloads. This PR implements a 'surge moderation bridge' that sits between the SLO enforcer and the regional circuit manager and introduces an async circuit-state rewind path to prevent immediate reopen attempts after a soft-eviction window.

Motivation: reduce oscillation in circuit state and give regional autoscaler time to react without hard-evicting tenants, improving end-user latency and reducing overall token spend during incidents.

Summary of changes and checklist:
- Add a new coordination component: surge-moderation-bridge service with lightweight RPC between slo-enforcer and circuit-manager.
- Implement async circuit-state rewind: persist a minimal circuit snapshot to local DB and schedule a background reconcile that will attempt reopen only after a decayed, heuristically-computed cooldown.
- Introduce tenant tethering: a soft-quarantine token that de-prioritizes requests but allows progressive probe traffic for warmup.
- Expose new metrics: surge_bridge.active_windows, circuit_rewind.attempts, tenant_tether.count, tenant_probe.success_ratio.
- Integrate with regional autoscaler signals: added hooks to prefer gradual capacity increases instead of immediate full reopen.
- Tests: unit tests for cooldown heuristics, e2e test via perf-canary scenario, and documented runbook steps.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked in Linear (ENG-5243) [x] unit tests added and passing locally [x] perf canary validated with synthetic spike [x] telemetry dashboards updated [x] rollout steps recorded in runbook [x] security review of RPC (mTLS) completed

Commits (high-level):
- 9c2b1a3 add surge-moderation-bridge initial scaffold and RPC contract
- 2d5f4e7 implement async circuit-state snapshot and rewind worker
- a1e4b8d add tenant tether token and probe middleware
- c3b0d55 hook autoscaler signals into reopen decision flow
- f8e7a11 add metrics, dashboards, and unit tests

Changed areas (high-level):
- services/surge-moderation-bridge/*: new service with RPC handlers
- pkg/slo/enforcer/bridge.go: new coordination logic and feature flag gating
- pkg/circuit/rewind_worker.go: async reconcile and cooldown heuristics
- infra/helm/surge-bridge.yaml: deployment and HPA config
- docs/runbooks/surge-moderation.md: runbook and rollback steps
- telemetry/dashboards/surge_bridge.json: dashboard panels
- tests/perf/canary/surge_probe.yml: canary scenario

Review conversation summary (selected):
- Diego Martell (reviewer): "Can the cooldown heuristic be made tunable per-tenant class? Concerned about high-priority tenants being starved."
- Author (Aisha): "Yes — added tenant_tether.priority_factor and a per-tenant override via configmap. Defaults preserve current behavior for high-tier customers."
- Sophie Nguyen: "We should ensure the rewind worker is idempotent if it crashes mid-snapshot."
- Author: "Rewind worker uses a compare-and-swap on snapshot_version and writes to durable local DB; added integration test to validate crash-restart behavior."
- Ravi Chandran: "CI failed on lint first run; please fix import ordering and small interface nit."
- Author: "Fixed lint issues and added pre-commit hook to catch ordering."

CI summary:
- CI pipeline run 2025-01-21 08:22Z: build (pass), unit tests (pass), lint (initial fail -> fixed, pass), integration (pass), e2e perf canary (pass in staging).
- Flaky test: tests/perf/canary/surge_probe.yml had intermittent timing; added increased timeout and retry in canary harness.

Rollout plan and canary:
- Feature gated behind feature flag: surge_moderation_bridge.enabled=false by default.
- Step 1 (canary): enable for 1% of traffic in us-west-2 for 2 hours; monitor surge_bridge.active_windows and tenant_probe.success_ratio.
- Step 2: expand to 10% for 6 hours if metrics stable.
- Step 3: full rollout across regions with staged ramp if no regressions.

Runbook highlights (from docs/runbooks/surge-moderation.md):
- Abort criteria: sustained increase in 95p latency > 15% or tenant_probe.success_ratio < 0.9 for more than 10 minutes.
- Immediate rollback: flip feature flag to false and trigger circuit-manager forced-stable state.
- Emergency mitigation: if oscillation persists, toggle slo-enforcer to emergency-mode which will prefer immediate hard reopens (last-resort).

Observability and metrics:
- New Prometheus metrics added and Grafana panels created.
- Added tracing spans around bridge RPC and rewind attempts.
- Logs include structured event "surge_bridge.window_opened" and "circuit_rewind.attempt_scheduled".

Security/ops considerations:
- RPCs are mTLS-authenticated and audited; documented in infra/README.
- Surge bridge runs in its own K8s namespace and uses RBAC minimal privileges.

Post-merge actions and follow-ups:
- ENG-5389: tune cooldown parameters per workload class based on 2-week canary data.
- ENG-5410: A/B compare cost delta with/without tenant tethering.
- Add a dashboard alert for frequent rewind attempts (>5 per 5m) to detect oscillation.

Merge outcome:
- Merged via squash on 2025-01-22 by Aisha Patel after approvals from all reviewers.

Why this is different from previous approaches: Instead of hard immediate reopen or aggressive eviction, the bridge coordinates a staged, telemetry-backed decision and uses an async rewind to avoid noisy reopen cycles — focusing on smoothing transitions and giving autoscaling time to provision capacity.

Notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: all behavior is behind a feature flag and default parameters are set to be close to current production heuristics. The intent is to reduce incident blast radius while preserving the ability to rapidly recover once capacity has stabilized.
Backfills a new surge moderation bridge that coordinates soft tenant evictions during cross-region surge and adds an async circuit-state rewind to avoid noisy rapid reopen cycles.
payload.title: Surge moderation bridge and async-circuit rewind

payload.body:
Context: runtime-1.22 introduces tiered batching defaults (fast/standard/cost-efficient). For the staged rollout (internal canary → hosted subset → dedicated opt-in → broader default), we need a single automated “expand rollout” step that refuses to proceed unless the safety signals are green.

This PR adds rollout automation hooks used by release tooling (release-bot + Console rollout workflow) and implements a set of safeguard checks:
- Perf gates: verifies perf-canary tier SLO gates are green for the target model family/hardware class/region set (fast p99 + standard p95) for the current release build.
- SLO / error-budget gates: checks fast-tier p99 burn-rate and request error-rate over a configurable window and blocks expansion on sustained burn.
- Dashboard sanity: ensures required tiered batching panels exist + are populated (latency histograms, queue depth, batch size distribution) for the target rollout scope.
- Kill-switch readiness: validates the rollout config includes a kill switch target and that the current config is retrievable (guards against “can’t roll back” class failures).
- Guardrail enforcement: blocks expansion when overload mode is engaged above threshold (load shedding activated or queue depth above cap for >N minutes).

Design notes:
- This is intentionally conservative: checks fail-closed for “unknown” unless explicitly configured as warn-only (used for early internal canaries).
- All checks emit structured reason codes and a short human summary used by release-bot comments + Console UI.
- All queries are scoped with cardinality controls (tier/model/region) to avoid reintroducing the tier-label blowup issues.

Operational flow:
- Release tooling calls: POST /internal/rollouts/{rollout_id}/expand with {from_stage, to_stage}.
- The runtime control-plane runs checks, returns either APPROVE or BLOCK with reason codes, and writes an audit event.
- If BLOCK, expansion stops; operator can either remediate or override with an explicit “break-glass” flag (RBAC-gated; logged).

Follow-ups (not in this PR):
- Add a “dry run” expansion view in Console (DES-771) showing which checks would block for the next stage.
- Add dedicated-specific checks for tenant override precedence drift (ENG-18430).

Rollout / risk:
- Feature-flagged behind rollout_safeguards_enabled (default ON for tiered batching rollouts, OFF for older rollouts until we backfill dashboards).
- Timeouts + fallback behavior designed to avoid wedging release tooling: each check has an upper bound and returns BLOCK on timeout (operators can override if needed).

Testing:
- Unit tests for each check type + reason code mapping.
- Integration test with fake metrics provider to cover windows, missing dashboards, and “stale data” blocking.
- Verified against staging with a synthetic rollout in us-east-1 and eu-west-1.

Refs:
- Perf canary gating PR: github/perf-canary#489
- Tiered dashboards PR: github/observability-pack#933
Rafael Mendes (SRE): “Fail-closed on timeout makes sense, but I’m worried about false blocks when the metrics backend is degraded. Do we have an operator-visible reason code vs a generic ‘unknown’?”
Benji Okafor (author): Added explicit reason codes per check (e.g., PERF_CANARY_TIMEOUT, METRICS_BACKEND_TIMEOUT, DASHBOARD_STALE_DATA) and included a link to the relevant dashboard/query in the summary.

Sean Gallagher (SRE): “Please gate on burn-rate (multi-window) rather than raw p99 spikes. We should avoid blocking on a single short-lived hiccup.”
Benji Okafor: Updated SLO gate to use 5m/30m windows with sustained-threshold logic (configurable). Added tests for transient spikes.

Allison Grant (Obs): “Dashboard ‘exists’ isn’t enough; we need to know it’s populated and not stale. Also please ensure we don’t query high-cardinality tags.”
Benji Okafor: Implemented data freshness check (must have samples within last 3 minutes) and hard-coded allowed label set (tier, model_family, region, hw_class). Added a guard that rejects queries containing request_id/route_id.

Marissa Cole (PM Rollouts): “Break-glass override needs to be explicit + audited. Can we also make warn-only configurable per stage?”

Connor O'Brien (Release Eng): “Release-bot needs a stable, machine-readable output. Please don’t rely on human text parsing.”

payload.body:
Context and motivation: In recent incidents we observed inconsistent SLO accounting across regions during transient network partitions which caused simultaneous soft-evictions and unnecessary tenant throttles. This sequence led to request storms and a prolonged recovery window. This PR introduces two cooperating pieces: (1) an SLO Synchronizer that converges tenant SLO state across active regions with a conservative merge strategy; and (2) a Regional Lease Guardian that prevents concurrent hard eviction/lease actions when regions rejoin. Both pieces are designed to be low-risk and behind a feature flag (runtime.feature.slo_synchronizer).

Goals: reduce duplicate eviction actions during regional rejoins; ensure KV cache preservation during quick failover/rejoin cycles; provide richer telemetry and tracing to debug divergence windows.

What this change does (high-level):
- Adds a periodic SLO state syncer that exchanges compact diffs (tenant id, observed SLO credit, last-update-ts, epoch) between region control planes. The syncer uses a CRDT-inspired last-writer-with-epoch-and-penalty strategy to avoid oscillation.
- Introduces regional lease acquisition with short TTLs (default 8s) and a guardian that ensures only one region is permitted to perform critical eviction/lease-reconcile operations for a tenant cohort at a time.
- Adds conservative backoff when a guardian detects flapping leases: escalate to soft-fallback mode rather than hard-evict which prevents cascade failures.
- Adds a hotfix to the KV cache rebound path: previous rapid failovers could drop in-flight KV snapshots; we now checkpoint last-known KV generation and replay shallow deltas on rejoin.
- Instruments key metrics and traces: slo_sync.delta_bytes, slo_sync.conflict_resolutions, lease_guard.leases_acquired, lease_guard.flaps, kv_replay.replayed_keys. Also wires up a debug view in Console for canary customers.

Design notes and safety:
- Feature-flagged and gated by runtime.feature.slo_synchronizer; default off in production until staged canary.
- Sync payloads are size-limited and sampled for high-volume tenants to bound control-plane bandwidth.
- Lease Guardian intentionally does not change client-facing routing; it only gates internal eviction/lease decisions to avoid split-brain.
- The merge rule: prefer highest epoch, then most recent last-update-ts; on ties apply tenant-weighted penalty to prefer higher-importance tenants staying warm.

Checklist:
- [x] Core syncer implementation and leader-lease guard
- [x] KV cache hotfix and replay path for shallow deltas
- [x] Metrics, tracing spans, and Console debug UI hook
- [x] Unit tests for merge rule and lease flapping
- [x] Integration test simulating partition/rejoin with synthetic tenants
- [x] Documented rollout plan in ENG-4021

Commits (summary):
- 9c1d4b3 Add slo synchronizer control loop, compact payload proto and reconciliation logic
- 3b2f7a1 Introduce regional lease guardian and TTL heuristics
- a3e88f0 KV cache checkpoint + replay hotfix for rapid failover
- b7e2d11 Wire telemetry and Console debug hook; add feature flag gating
- f2c4c6d Tests: deterministic partition/rejoin integration test and unit cases

Changed files (high-level):
- src/controlplane/slo/synchronizer.go (new) - core periodic sync and merge logic
- src/controlplane/lease/guardian.go (new) - lease acquisition and guardian loop
- src/runtime/kv/replay.go (modified) - checkpoint + replay logic and tests
- src/telemetry/metrics_registry.go (modified) - new metric registrations
- console/src/debug/slo-sync-view.tsx (new) - lightweight debug surface
- tests/integration/slo_partition_rejoin_test.go (new) - integration test harness
- docs/operations/slo_synchronizer_rollout.md (new) - rollout instructions and rollback plan

Review conversation (condensed):
- Ethan: "This looks good overall. Concerned about lease TTL being too aggressive for high-latency regions. Can we make TTL adaptive based on median RTT in telemetry?" 
- Samira (author): "Good catch — implemented adaptive TTL in guardian.go. Default stays 8s but increases by 2x when median RTT > 250ms. Added unit tests (see f2c4c6d)."
- Priya: "KV replay logic is promising but let's assert we don't accidentally reintroduce stale tokens into cache leading to model corruption." 
- Samira: "Added generation checks and shallow-delta size limit; replay rejects deltas older than the checkpoint generation. See src/runtime/kv/replay.go lines ~120-165."
- Lars: "Agree with telemetry additions. Can we add a sampling tag for tenant cohort to the slo_sync traces?" 
- Samira: "Added tenant_cohort tag and sampling knob; will toggle in canary to keep traces manageable."
- Priya (approval): "Approved after addressing replay gen checks and TTL adaptivity."
- Ethan (approval): "Approved; minor nits in comments fixed in subsequent squash commit."

CI summary:
- build: pass
- unit tests: pass (coverage for new modules at 82%)
- integration (partition_rejoin): pass in CI env with 3-region simulation
- lint: pass
- canary-deploy pipeline: green for staging

Merge outcome: merged via squash-merge by Samira Kline on 2026-02-22. Post-merge tasks: enable runtime.feature.slo_synchronizer in a single canary region for 24h, monitor slo_sync.* and lease_guard.* metrics and the Console debug view. If conflict_resolutions spikes > 5% or lease_guard.flaps > 0.2% escalate to ENG-4120.

Telemetry and observability notes: added dashboards under "SLO / Sync" with prebuilt alerts for sustained delta sizes and lease flapping. Also added a regression eval in the telemetry pipeline to ensure the KV replay doesn’t increase per-token latency by >1.5ms on median.

Rollout plan (short):
1) Enable flag in staging and run partition_rejoin test schedule for 24h
2) Canary enable in region-us-west-2 for a small tenant cohort (+ debug tracing)
3) Expand canary to two more regions after 24h if metrics stable
4) Full enable across regions with 48h watch and rollback path documented in docs/operations/slo_synchronizer_rollout.md

Related items: ENG-4021 (design + rollout), ENG-4120 (incident runbook), SUP-8876 (customer-reported double-evict case).
Adds a cross-region SLO synchronizer and a regional lease guardian to reduce split-brain during failovers; hotfix preserves KV cache during rapid region transitions. Backwards-compatible. Flagged behind runtime.feature.slo_synchronizer for staged rollout.

payload.body:
## Context
Incident Bot v2 and Console deep links need to fetch saturation + SLO-adjacent signals safely on behalf of responders without accidentally widening scope across tenants, exploding cardinality, or issuing expensive queries during an incident.

Today we have a handful of ad-hoc metric query helpers spread across console-backend and diag tooling. They differ in defaults (time windows, step, label filters) and do not consistently enforce tenant isolation.

This PR introduces a small set of primitives in `telemetry-query-service` that:
- require an explicit tenant context (or explicit opt-out for global-only metrics)
- bound query cost (time range caps, max series, max datapoints)
- allowlist which metrics/label keys can be queried from diagnostics tooling
- return structured errors suitable for bot cards ("degraded mode": show cached context + links)

## What changed (high level)
1) **TenantContext + Scoping**
- New `TenantContext` type (`tenant_id`, `deployment_mode`, `region`, `requester_principal`, `purpose`) used by all query entrypoints.
- Default enforcement: queries must include a tenant constraint unless the metric is marked `GlobalOnly` in the allowlist.

2) **Allowlisted metrics + label constraints**
- Added `MetricQueryAllowlist` with:
  - allowed metric names (e.g., `gpu.utilization`, `scheduler.queue_depth`, `kv_cache.pressure_pct`, `http.5xx_rate`)
  - allowed label keys per metric (e.g., `region`, `pool`, `model`, `route`, `tenant_id`)
  - disallowed label filters for diagnostics (prevents arbitrary regex / high-card filters)
- Console deep-link generator and incident-bot callers will only be able to query metrics present in the allowlist.

3) **Query guardrails (cost + cardinality)**
- Hard caps:
  - max lookback: 2h (configurable per purpose: `DIAGNOSTICS` vs `CONSOLE_UI`)
  - max step resolution floor: 10s
  - max series: 200 (per query)
  - max datapoints: 20k (per query)
- Soft budgets:
  - per-tenant QPS limits (token bucket keyed by `tenant_id + purpose`)
  - request coalescing key (`metric + tenant_id + time_range + filters`) to reduce burst duplication

4) **Structured errors + degraded-mode hints**
- New error type `MetricQueryError` with `code` (`FORBIDDEN_SCOPE`, `ALLOWLIST_DENY`, `BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`, `UPSTREAM_RATE_LIMIT`, `INVALID_FILTER`, `TOO_MANY_SERIES`), `safe_message`, and `retry_after_ms`.
- Callers can render safe user-facing messages and decide between retry, fallback links, or cached context.

5) **Tests + docs**
- Unit tests for:
  - tenant constraint enforcement
  - allowlist behavior
  - series/datapoint caps
  - budget enforcement
- Added developer docs for adding a new metric to the allowlist (including cardinality review checklist).

## Why this approach
- Keeps the enforcement close to the data access layer (telemetry-query-service), not duplicated per caller.
- Explicit tenant scoping aligns with least-privilege requirements for incident tooling and upcoming audit events (handled in PR-29133).
- Allows Console deep links to be generated consistently with the same constraints used by incident diagnostics.

## Follow-ups
- Wire these primitives into incident-bot query aggregator (tracked in ENG-5427).
- Add audit events for privileged query calls (PR-29133).
- Expand allowlist with SLO burn-rate helper metrics after alert tuning lands.

## Validation
- Local: `bazel test //telemetry-query-service/...`
- Staging: ran synthetic diag queries for 10 tenants across 3 regions; validated caps + error messages.
- Load: replayed incident-bot burst pattern from INT-3341; coalescing reduced upstream calls ~62%.

## Rollout
- Default enabled for diagnostics callers.
- Console deep link path is feature-flagged (`console.metricQueries.v2`) and will be enabled after 48h in staging.

Risk: Moderate. This touches a shared query path. Guardrails are intentionally strict; expect some initial allowlist-deny errors until callers are updated (degraded mode should handle this).
Logan Wright (Telemetry): Can we avoid allowing arbitrary regex label filters? We had a cardinality incident last quarter. Also please confirm time range caps are enforced server-side (not just client defaults).
Caleb Johnson (author): Yep — server-side validation rejects regex filters entirely for diagnostics purpose (only exact-match allowed on allowlisted label keys). Time range caps are enforced in `guards.ts` before hitting the upstream query backend.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (Authz): Tenant scope enforcement looks good, but I want the API to require either (a) tenant_id or (b) an explicit `global_ok=true` with GlobalOnly metric. Otherwise callers will forget to set tenant_id and silently query global scope.
Caleb Johnson (author): Updated query route: missing tenant_id now fails with `FORBIDDEN_SCOPE` unless metric is `GlobalOnly` and caller passes `scope=global`. Added tests for both cases.
Jacob Stein (Diagnostics): For incident-bot cards, we need a stable error surface so we can render degraded-mode text consistently. Can we add `retry_after_ms` when budgets trip?
Caleb Johnson (author): Added `retry_after_ms` to `MetricQueryError` for budget + upstream 429 cases; default 30s for local budgets, passes through upstream if provided.
Chloe Martin (Console): Deep-link generator currently uses a 6h window for some dashboards. With 2h caps, links will still work but queries won’t. Can we expose caps to link builder so Console uses the same window?
Caleb Johnson (author): Added `getMaxLookback(purpose)` exported helper and updated Console deep links to default to 2h unless the destination is a dashboard link (dashboards can show longer windows without using this query API).
Nadia Rahman (Pipelines): Please ensure we’re not requiring `tenant_id` label on metrics that don’t have it yet (some GPU pool metrics are per-pool/region only).
Caleb Johnson (author): Allowlist supports `tenant_scoped=false` for region/pool metrics; in those cases we still require TenantContext but enforce scoping via `pool` + `region` constraints (and disallow querying across all pools). Documented in allowlist guide.
Logan Wright: LGTM after last push. Thanks for the guardrails and structured errors.
Kaitlyn Nguyen: Approved. Please make sure callers use service identity scopes; audit events coming next PR.
Jacob Stein: Approved — error surface works for bot degraded-mode cards.
Chloe Martin: Approved — Console links updated.
payload.title: Add tenant-aware metric query primitives for diagnostics + Console deep links

Motivation: Provide a composable, testable 'Cost Playbook' construct that bundles batching defaults, cache/prefill policies, and quantization profile recommendations into tenant-scoped artifacts that can be dry-run against workload traces and rolled out with safety gates. This PR implements the playbook assembler service, a CLI to generate/dry-run playbooks, a small policy language for combining batch/cache/quant hints, telemetry hooks for unit-econ evaluation, and migration logic to convert existing tenant defaults into playbook form. Key goals: reduce manual config drift, make autosuggest rules reproducible, and enable canary rollouts that automatically revert on quality or latency regressions. Highlights: implemented playbook assembler (internal API + controller), added costctl playbook subcommands (generate/dryrun/validate/apply), introduced a compact playbook JSON schema and a playbook catalog under tenant defaults, wiring to the prefiller and batcher to accept playbook hints (batch window, max_microbatch_size, prefill_budget_pct), integrated quant profile suggestions with safety thresholds (quality_delta_allowed=0.02), telemetry events (playbook.evaluation.start/finish, playbook.rollback.trigger), and end-to-end CI checks including dry-run simulation against 3 representative traces. Testing & rollout: unit tests for assembler, integration tests running dry-run traces in CI; local e2e playbook apply validated against a synthetic tenant in prefiller sandbox; staged rollout plan: alpha tenants -> canary pool (5 tenants) with latency SLO watch -> ramp to all tenants over 48h. Backwards compatibility: existing tenant defaults are migrated automatically to a single implicit playbook; users can opt out by setting tenant.playbook_mode=legacy. Migration includes a safe snapshot export and a rollback path. Security & privacy: no change to PII handling; playbook artifacts stored encrypted at rest. See docs update for cost playbooks and CLI usage. Checklist: [x] implement assembler core; [x] add playbook catalog UI endpoints; [x] add costctl subcommands; [x] add telemetry hooks; [x] add integration tests; [x] add migration tool; [x] docs and changelog updated. Related: references ENG-4021 (economy playbooks design), ENG-4109 (prefill policy consolidation).
Arjun Patel: Overall this looks good but we need a hard SLO hook in the controller to avoid cascading regresses; can you add a configured latency threshold and immediate rollback?
Lina Ortega: Added playbook.rollback.trigger telemetry and a controller-level threshold (config.playbook.latency_slo_pct=1.2) with immediate rollback action. Updated tests to cover rollback flow.
Marta Nowak: Suggest tightening default quality_delta_allowed to 0.015 for chat workloads; also add a note in docs about non-deterministic quant effects.
Lina Ortega: Reduced default to 0.015 for chat workload class and documented stochastic quant impacts. Left an escape hatch per-tenant.
Ethan Rios: CI flaky on dryrun against trace_latin intermittently; can we assert deterministic seeds in simulator?
Lina Ortega: Fixed simulator seed in tests and added a rerun step in CI config for flaky simulation jobs.
Added 'Cost Playbooks' framework: playbook assembler service, tenant playbook catalog, costctl playbook commands, safe migration path from tenant defaults, telemetry for evaluation and rollback, and guidance for canary rollouts and latency/quality safety gates. This enables automated, reproducible batch/cache/quant recommendations and dry-run simulations before applying changes to production tenants.

Motivation: Customers running long-lived streamed calls and tool/function invocations were losing correlation between the API request and downstream tool executions (adapters, subprocesses, external tool runners). This made debugging timeouts and tool errors difficult and reduced the value of per-endpoint metrics.

What this PR does (summary):
- Propagates a stable request_id + trace span id into any tool/function execution context (env vars + process args for tool-runner, and headers for remote tool adapters).
- Ensures every streaming fragment emitted from the API surface includes request_id and route labels so JSONL access logs can be correlated to traces and metrics.
- Adds per-route label enrichment to JSONL access logs and to Prometheus metrics produced by the API gateway, enabling route/model/route_version dimension tagging for latency and error metrics.
- Adds OpenAI-compat shim mappings so x-request-id / traceparent are honored and translated into internal request_id when present.

Key changes:
- runtime/toolrunner/exec.go: thread request_id + trace_span into child process env and command args; added short-lived span handoff logic.
- proxy/streaming/fragment_writer.go: include request_id and route.labels in each fragment envelope; backwards-compatible flag keeps legacy small fragments for older clients.
- observability/jsonl_writer.go: include route.labels map flattened to jsonl fields route_name, model, route_version; safe-serialize for non-string labels.
- metrics/route_labels.go: new helper to translate route config into prometheus label set; applied to endpoint_latency and endpoint_errors counters.
- adapters/openai_shim.ts: read x-request-id / traceparent and map to internal request_id header; update tests.
- test/e2e/tool_correlation_test.go: end-to-end test that fires a streaming request, executes a tool, and asserts logs/metrics contain same request_id.

Testing & CI:
- Unit tests added for toolrunner env injection and JSONL label formatting.
- Integration e2e test validates correlation across the gateway -> tool runner -> jsonl pipeline.
- First CI run failed on lint (ts-lint rule for header ordering); fixed in second commit and reran CI which passed.

Compatibility and rollout:
- Backwards compatible: if clients already send x-request-id or traceparent, we use those; otherwise a new internal request_id is generated. An opt-out feature flag (OBS_LEGACY_FRAGMENT) preserves prior fragment payloads for older clients.
- Rollout plan: feature gated under runtime flag. Gradually enable for 10% of traffic for 48h, validate metrics and increased observability dashboards, then ramp to 100%.
- Rollback: disable flag and redeploy gateway config to stop injecting request ids into fragments; no DB or persistent storage changes.

Notes for operators:
- New Prometheus labels for endpoint metrics will increase cardinality (route_name, model, route_version). We recommend updating scrape/recording rules to aggregate by route_name only where necessary.

Related:
- Linear ENG-9183 (streaming observability improvements)
- Support ticket SUP-4421 (customer debugging for tool hangs)

Checklist:
- [x] Propagate request_id into tool runs
- [x] Add request_id to every stream fragment
- [x] Add per-route JSONL fields and metrics labels
- [x] Add unit and e2e tests
- [x] Update OpenAI-compat shim header handling


Asha Patel: Please add a short unit test that verifies the toolrunner preserves request_id when spawning detached processes.
Riley Chen: Added unit + e2e test; also included an env-only mode for exec where we don't change args to preserve binary compatibility.
Diego Morales: Can we ensure this won't blow up prometheus with cardinality? Add docs/ops notes and recommend recording rules.
Riley Chen: Added docs/observability/route-labels.md and a small helper to limit labels used in high-cardinality metrics.
Samira Khatri: LGTM after CI green and a small nit on JSON escaping in jsonl_writer.go
Samira Khatri: Approved
Added request_id propagation into tool executions, per-fragment request_id tagging for streaming, and per-route JSONL/metering labels. Operators should review prometheus label usage before enabling at scale.
Run e2e/tool_correlation_test.go and validate that the generated jsonl access log line contains the same request_id observed in the tool runner stdout file. Validate Prometheus metrics include route_name label after enabling flag.

Introduce per-hop KMS proof tokens for safe cross-region rewraps and an ephemeral operator lease mechanism. Backwards compatible; opt-in via runtime flag. Improves auditability for rewrapped keys and reduces blast radius for operator actions.
Motivation: Customers in regulated regions require both strong audit proofs for any cross-region key rewrap and a minimized operator attack surface. This PR introduces a per-hop KMS proof token that accompanies a rewrap request when we proxy or re-encrypt data between regions, plus an ephemeral operator lease (RBAC v2 token) that gates operator-initiated rewraps and administrative KMS operations. The implementation includes a small policy evaluator, a runtime flag to enable hop-proofing, an automated consent-check that ties tenant residency assertions to rewraps, and an admin CLI to mint/inspect ephemeral leases.

What this changes: - Add new service middleware (kms/hop_proof_middleware) that emits a signed proof blob for each cross-region rewrap. The blob contains a canonicalized rewrap request fingerprint, timestamp, origin-region, target-region, and a nonce; it is signed with the platform KMS key and also recorded as a structured audit event. - Introduce ephemeral operator lease service (rbac/ephemeral_lease) which issues short-lived RBAC tokens scoped to specific actions (e.g., kms:Rewrap, kms:Grant). Leases are auditable and require an approval flag or a two-step consent when tenant residency is asserted. - Wire audit/logging to include proof_id and lease_id in existing request/span tags; added a deterministic audit watermark for rewrap sequences to detect dropped or replayed rewraps. - Add unit + integration tests, an end-to-end scenario in perf-canary that simulates cross-region rewrap traffic under dedicated capacity, and a migration that adds the new audit.table columns (proof_id, lease_id, rewrap_sequence_hash). - New CLI commands: redwood kms inspect-proof <proof_id>, redwood lease issue --actor <svc> --actions "kms:Rewrap" --ttl 5m --reason "incident remediation".

Compatibility & rollout: The feature is behind a runtime toggle (KMS_HOP_PROOF=off by default). Existing tenants see no change until enabled per-tenant or at the cluster level. Ephemeral leases require RBAC v2 policies to be present; a small helper migrator maps legacy operator roles to lease-capable templates. The rollout plan in the PR description describes a gradual enablement starting with internal-only canary, then selected enterprise tenants, followed by full opt-in.

Testing performed: - Unit tests for middleware, proof canonicalization, and lease issuance/validation. - Integration tests between runtime, kms-proxy, and audit writer. - End-to-end run in perf-canary with synthetic rewraps to validate sequence watermarking and audit queries. - Manual verification of CLI commands and a quick smoke test that shows proof blobs are recorded and can be inspected. CI initially failed on a flaky audit integration test (audit_writer_test::SequencerRace) — I added a retry and a stronger mutex in the migration; CI passed on second run.

Rollbacks and safety: The toggle ensures we can disable proof emission without schema rollback. Migration adds nullable columns and a backfill job guarded by a feature flag. Ephemeral lease issuance is separate from existing API tokens and cannot be used unless RBAC v2 policies allow it. If issues are seen, ops can set KMS_HOP_PROOF=off, revoke leases via redwood lease revoke --id, and run a short backfill-without-proof job.

Changelog (high level): - New middleware: kms/hop_proof_middleware.go - RBAC subsystem: rbac/ephemeral_lease.go + lease store - Audit: audit/writer add proof_id, lease_id, rewrap_sequence_hash fields and indexes - CLI: tools/redwood_kms.go + tools/redwood_lease.go - Tests: unit and integration suites + perf-canary scenario - Migration: db/migrations/20260210_add_rewrap_proof_columns.sql

See also: Linear ENG-2408 for product acceptance criteria and SEC-919 for the threat model and design review notes.
Markus Chen: Can we compress the proof blob schema to avoid blowup in the audit table? Audit storage is a concern for large-scale rewrap traffic.
Sana Iqbal: We include only a 32-byte fingerprint + 2 region tags + nonce (64 bytes total). The full details are stored in object storage keyed by proof_id and only the hash is persisted in the audit row. Added note in audit/writer.go and a storage TTL of 90 days.
Ravi Patel: Need a clear signal that operator leases are scoped to a single action and cannot be reused for unrelated actions. Also add a CI test for reuse attempts.
Sana Iqbal: Added reuse rejection test (ephemeral_lease_test::RejectsActionReuse) and an assertion in the lease validator.
Lena Ortiz: Please update runbooks/incident-handling.md to include steps to revoke leases and to interpret proof sequence mismatches.
Sana Iqbal: Runbook updated in a follow-up commit; linked in the migration notes.
payload.title: add per-hop kms proofing and ephemeral operator lease for cross-region rewraps

## Summary
This PR enforces a readiness gate in the control plane so newly provisioned GPU nodes cannot be added to serving pools (Dedicated or shared) until they have passed provision-to-ready validations and are in `Ready` state. This closes a gap we saw during early rollout where nodes could join the pool after kubelet join but before validations (GPU health / driver parity / NCCL smoke / perf canary) completed, causing avoidable brownouts and noisy remediation.

The gate is feature-flagged and supports a rollback toggle. It also includes safety checks to avoid deadlocking pool scale-ups if readiness signals are missing/late.

## Motivation / Context
- During the staged rollout we observed instances where the autoscaler/pool controller saw a node as schedulable and added it to a serving pool while it was still in `Validating`, leading to:
  - GPU driver drift errors surfacing as runtime failures
  - NCCL fabric issues showing up as elevated latency / timeouts
  - Increased quarantine after traffic had already been routed
- We already have canonical readiness states defined in ADR-017 and exposed by Fleet Readiness Service; this PR makes the pool membership controller respect that state.

## Behavior change
- Prior behavior: pool membership controller would accept nodes if they were:
  - registered in cluster AND
  - labeled as a GPU worker AND
  - passed basic kubelet/node conditions (Ready/Schedulable)
- New behavior (when flag enabled): to be eligible for pool membership, node must additionally have `fleet_readiness_state == Ready`.
  - Nodes in `Allocated/Provisioning/Validating` are blocked from joining.
  - Nodes in `Quarantined` are explicitly denied (and if already present, they are removed/drained depending on pool policy).

## Feature flag / rollback
- New flag: `fleet.readiness_gate.enabled` (default: OFF)
  - Scopes: region + pool type (Dedicated/shared) via existing rollout config
  - Kill switch behavior: when disabled, reverts to previous eligibility logic immediately (no schema rollback required)
- New config: `fleet.readiness_gate.fail_open` (default: true for staged rollout)
  - If Fleet Readiness Service is unavailable or returns an "unknown" response, controller will allow membership but emits a high-severity metric + structured log event.
  - Rationale: avoid deadlocking capacity bring-up during transient readiness-service incidents; we can flip to fail-closed after confidence increases.

## Safety checks / edge cases
- Race protection: readiness transitions are polled with monotonic event timestamps; we only treat `Ready` as authoritative if it is newer than the current membership reconciliation start.
- Stuck validating: nodes blocked >N minutes emit `pool_membership_blocked_total{reason="validating_timeout"}` and include readiness failure reason pointer when available.
- Manual override: on-call can set an allowlist annotation `fleet.redwood.dev/skip-readiness-gate=true` on a node for emergency capacity recovery (audited + metric). This is intentionally noisy and not intended for routine use.

## Observability
- Metrics:
  - `pool_membership_gate_checks_total{result, reason, pool_type, region}`
  - `pool_membership_blocked_total{reason, pool_type, region}`
  - `pool_membership_gate_readiness_lookup_latency_ms{pool_type, region}`
  - `pool_membership_gate_fail_open_total{pool_type, region}`
- Logs:
  - `fleet_pool_membership_gate` structured event with node_id (redacted to hash), pool_id, readiness_state, readiness_artifact_ref

## Testing
- Unit tests for eligibility logic (Ready vs Validating vs Quarantined)
- Integration-style tests using fake readiness service:
  - fail-open path
  - unknown node path
  - override annotation path
- Manual verification in staging:
  - scaled a Dedicated A100 pool from 0->5; nodes held out until validations passed; membership added within ~30s after Ready.

## Rollout plan (follow-up)
- Enable flag in us-east A100 Dedicated only (ENG-4829 checklist) with fail-open=true
- Monitor:
  - time-to-ready P95 and blocked counts
  - any increase in pool scale-up time
- If stable for 48h, flip fail-open=false and expand scope

## Links
- Linear: ENG-4822, ENG-4825, ENG-4829
- Support context: SUP-28433 (nodes stuck in validating; previously could still get traffic)
- Related PRs: pr-18421 (readiness states/API), pr-18429 (validation artifacts), pr-18452 (quarantine on repeat failures)

---
Checklist
- [x] Feature flag with safe default
- [x] Metrics + logs
- [x] Tests
- [x] Docs note in code comments for on-call override + auditing

Ethan Park: The fail-open default makes sense for rollout, but we should ensure we page loudly if we’re failing open for >5m. Can you add a counter + alert hook? Also confirm we don’t tag metrics with node_id.
Jordan Lee (author): Added `pool_membership_gate_fail_open_total{pool_type,region}` and removed node_id from all tags (log retains a hash only). Alert wiring will be in observability-pack PR; added TODO with owner (Aisha) + linked ENG-4827.
Vanessa Ortiz: For stuck nodes, can we expose the readiness failure reason pointer so fleet can triage quickly? Even if we can’t show full logs, an artifact ref helps.
Jordan Lee (author): Included `readiness_artifact_ref` in the log event when present, and we emit `reason="validating_timeout"` with a short string `failure_code` (low-cardinality) from readiness service.
Sean Gallagher: Concern about deadlock: if readiness service is degraded and we flip fail-closed too early, pools may not scale during incidents. Can we make the fail-open/closed policy per region so SRE can keep one region permissive temporarily?
Jordan Lee (author): Yes — `fleet.readiness_gate.fail_open` is now rollout-scoped by region via existing config. Also added an explicit runbook note in code comments for toggling during incidents.
Benji Okafor: Minor: readiness timestamp comparison looks off-by-one. If Ready event arrives exactly at reconciliation start, should we accept it? I think yes.
Jordan Lee (author): Good catch. Updated comparison to accept `>=` and added a test case for boundary condition.
Aisha Bello: Metrics look good. Please ensure `pool_id` isn’t a label (cardinality). Use pool_type + region only.
Jordan Lee (author): Removed `pool_id` from metric tags; kept it only in structured logs (with sampling).
Ethan Park: Approved after last push. Please coordinate enabling flag with release train checklist.
Vanessa Ortiz: Approved.

Context: Production rollout of a new decoder scheduling strategy (short-prefix KV-reshuffle) caused sporadic P95 latency regressions in long-lived sessions during an internal canary. Previous rollout controllers focused on traffic weight and cohort percentages but did not enforce session affinity or provide a sliding-latency gate per cohort.

Motivation: Provide a rollout primitive that can perform a gradual model swap targeted at user cohorts while preserving session affinity and enforcing latency SLO safeguards that can pause or partially roll back the swap automatically if latency degrades beyond configured thresholds. This PR implements a controller and API surface for 'CohortGradualSwap' with the following goals: 1) preserve session affinity for stateful users during swaps so in-flight conversations are not disrupted; 2) allow percentage-based cohort targeting (by user-id hash / cookie) with deterministic assignment; 3) enforce adaptive latency gates per cohort (short-term P95 and longer-term moving-average) and pause/roll back automatically when breached; 4) provide observability hooks and a simulator to validate policy behavior offline.

Design summary:
- New CRD: CohortGradualSwap (fields: cohort_selector, target_model, step_percentages, min_step_duration, latency_gates, session_affinity_ttl, fallback_policy).
- Controller: incremental reconciliation loop that applies swaps by annotating routes and updating ServeGraph with traffic weights. The controller retains session-affinity mappings in a small, sharded in-memory store and persists checkpoints to etcd every step to survive leader churn.
- Latency gates: two-layer gating: P95 window (1m granularity) and an exponential moving average (EMA) over 10m for softer stability. Gate evaluation uses existing metrics stream (prometheus exporter) and can be configured with slack multipliers.
- Automatic rollback: when a gate is breached for a cohort for >2 consecutive evaluation windows, the controller performs a targeted rollback of the cohort to the last known-good model and emits an event.
- Simulator: a new simulator binary (tools/rollout-sim) accepts workload traces and gate configs to run simulated rollouts and outputs expected traffic weights, rollback triggers, and estimated user impact.

Migration and backward compatibility: CohortGradualSwap is opt-in. Existing rollout controllers are unchanged. The controller supports a 'compat' mode to translate simple percentage-only swaps into the new CRD for teams that want to adopt incrementally.

Testing:
- Unit tests cover controller reconcilers, affinity mapping logic, and gate evaluation (pkg/rollout/*_test.go).
- Integration tests exercise the end-to-end swap with a mocked metrics sink and a fake ServeGraph (e2e/rollout_latency_test.go).
- Simulator tests include recorded traces from internal production sampling.

Observability and dashboards:
- Added per-cohort dashboards: per-cohort P50/P95, rollback events, session-affinity hit rate, and step progression.
- Tracing: added tags to swap-related spans for easier correlation.

Rollout plan and safety:
- Feature behind feature-flag (rollout.cohort_swap_v1).
- Start with internal canary (10% of users, labeled 'internal').
- Promote to staged cohorts (10 -> 30 -> 60 -> 100) with min_step_duration default 30m.
- The controller will not advance a step unless all gates are green for the cohort for the min_step_duration.
- Emergency kill switch: admin API to abort/pause all CohortGradualSwap controllers.

Related work: ENG-1423 (latency gating), ENG-1487 (session-affinity preservation).

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: affinity store growth with many ephemeral users. Mitigation: TTL-based eviction, bloom-filter precheck, and sharded backing to avoid hot keys.
- Risk: noisy metrics causing spurious rollbacks. Mitigation: dual-gate strategy (fast P95 + EMA) and require consecutive windows before rollback.
Ana Sato: Can we avoid persisting full affinity maps to etcd at every step? Suggest checkpointing only diffs.\nLena Park: Implemented diff checkpointing and shard-level compaction in affinity_store.go (see commit b2c3d4e).
Marcus Lee: Need clearer guarantees about exactly-once rollback actions during leader failover.\nLena Park: Added leader-observed generation token and idempotent rollback markers; documented behavior in design doc.
Priya Nambiar: Simulator looks great; can it model tail correlations between latency and payload size?\nLena Park: Simulator accepts custom trace hooks; added payload-size correlation model and sample traces used in tests.
