Rishi Malhotra (review): Please call out that invoice credits/refunds will not reconcile within the same day and can drift MTD, otherwise FP&A will get paged. Also: can we pin rate card version per window so we can re-run historical reconciliation even after rate card updates?
Mei Lin (author): Updated report header and README with a prominent limitation section (credits/refunds, timing). Added `rate_card_version` column and the job now requires a pinned version for the window; if not provided, it uses the version active at window end and marks `RATE_CARD_UNPINNED` as a warning (Finance asked for hard pinning for exec numbers).
Laura Bennett (review): Inclusion/exclusion looks correct. One request: make sure "billing totals" excludes taxes and one-time fees by default; we only want usage-based inference revenue/cost comparables here. Also please add a CSV export format that matches the KPI pack ingestion expectations (columns + naming).
Mei Lin (author): Default classifier now excludes TAX/FEES/ONE_TIME and anything tagged "manual_adjustment". Added `--format kpi-pack-csv` option that outputs the exact column set Rishi sent (day, window_tz, billed_usd, attributed_usd, delta_usd, delta_pct, reason_code, notes).
Chloe Martin (review): From Console side this will eventually power a "Reconciliation" tab. Can we keep the schema stable and avoid customer_id exposure? Also, please ensure the view is performant (no full scan for MTD queries).
Mei Lin (author): Schema uses only tier/region/model_family and does not include customer identifiers. For perf, the daily view is partitioned by day and materialized; monthly view aggregates from daily partitions. Added query plan notes in the doc.
Caleb Johnson (review): Reason-code prioritization: if billing lag AND metering incomplete, which one wins? For oncall triage we should surface metering first (we control it) but keep both in the notes field.

Motivation: certain model variants (mixed-head MQA/GQA and models with intra-head sparsity patterns) do not map well to our default kernel dispatch and KV retention policies. This leads to suboptimal kernel paths and premature KV eviction under bursty, low-latency workloads. Summary: implement a sparsity-probing kernel selector and a rolling KV-window eviction strategy that adapts retention to observed attention-density patterns per-request and per-model. The new selector probes a small representative head-slice at runtime to pick a kernel variant (dense / sparse-optimized / hybrid) and caches the choice keyed by model+seq_profile. The rolling KV-window keeps a sliding retention budget (ms-based) instead of a fixed token count, allowing high-density bursts to preserve KV while low-density requests compact more aggressively. Key changes: - runtime/kernel_selector.rs: new KernelProbe + selection cache - runtime/kv_window.rs: rolling window state machine, eviction policy, and metrics - runtime/scheduler_continuous_batching.rs: small smoothing update to avoid microburst thrashing - perf tests and regression benchmarks added under tests/perf - docs/perf/kernel-selection.md: rationale and tuning knobs - examples/bench-configs/microbatch.toml: sample params Safety & rollout: feature gated behind env var REDWOOD_RUNTIME_SPARSE_PROBE and disabled by default for Dedicated/Private until opt-in. Gradual rollout: enable in perf canary -> 10% region -> full. Local snippet (runtime kernel probe): "let probe = SampleHeads::new(4); let variant = probe.select(&attn_stats); cache.insert(model_id, variant);" Benchmarks (internal): - Llama-2-13B (MQA) @ 1024 seq: P95 latency down 9%, throughput +12% under mixed short/long workload - Mistral-7B (GQA) @ 512 seq: throughput +14% in continuous-batching mode - Qwen-7B variants: tail latency improved 6% and tokens saved ~3% by avoiding unnecessary kernel fallbacks Known limitations: kernel probe adds ~0.5ms overhead on first-seen model+profile but is amortized across sessions. The rolling window currently uses wall-clock ms which may skew under host clock drift; we instrumented for this and plan to switch to monotonic time in follow-up. Related work: ENG-1984 (kernel dispatch refactor), ENG-2003 (kv retention study). Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for eviction invariants - [x] Perf harness added - [x] Docs and knobs - [x] Canary rollout plan
Marco Silva: Please add determinism tests for eviction order when two sessions have identical scores. Also can you include a metric that counts probe failures? (requested changes)
Lydia Chen: Added determinism unit tests and a probe_failures counter exposed via runtime.metrics.probe_failures; addressed in commit 5.
Arjun Rao: Can we disable the probe by default in Dedicated until private rollout is validated? Also request a small doc blurb describing tuning knobs. (requested changes)
Lydia Chen: Feature gated via REDWOOD_RUNTIME_SPARSE_PROBE and documented tuning knobs in docs/perf/kernel-selection.md.
Nina Patel: Verified perf numbers in canary; looks safe to roll to 10% (approved)
Ethan Brooks: Squash-merge pending CI perf re-run (approval)
Initial prototype: sparse head probe and rolling window state machine
Add selection cache and TTLs; unit tests for cache expiry
Integrate with continuous batching scheduler and add smoothing
Perf harness and benchmarks; update docs
Address review: add monotonic-time TODO, tighten eviction invariants
Fix CI perf flakiness and update changelog

Context
We’ve had a few near-misses and one confirmed incident where the internal reset tooling was invoked from the wrong shell context / with stale env vars, resulting in a reset call being constructed against a non-demo org. Additionally, during live demos and dry runs we’ve seen multiple reset requests fired in quick succession (double-clicks, retries, Slack copy/paste), spiking control-plane load and leading to 429s in adjacent workflows.

This PR adds two things:
1) Safety rails to make it effectively impossible to reset a non-demo tenant.
2) Rate limits + idempotency semantics around reset actions to prevent repeated resets in a short window.

What changed (high-level)
- Added a server-side “demo tenant guard” check that must pass for any reset operation (CLI + API).
- Introduced a dedicated permission for reset execution (separate from general admin) and ensured it’s audited.
- Added a reset action rate limiter (token bucket) keyed by org_id + actor_id.
- Added request idempotency (Idempotency-Key header) for reset endpoints.
- Hardened the CLI with explicit confirmations and “environment fingerprint” verification.
- Updated the demo healthcheck report to surface rate limit state + last reset metadata.

Safety rails (server-side)
- New org attribute `org.flags.demo_tenant=true` must be present AND org slug must match `demo-*`.
  - Rationale: slug check catches accidental flag propagation; flag check avoids slug collisions.
- Reset endpoint now rejects any org not meeting the guard with HTTP 403 and an error code `DEMO_RESET_GUARD_FAILED`.
- Added allowlist support for emergency cases (single org_id list in config) but default is empty and requires on-call override.

Safety rails (CLI)
- `rw demo reset` now requires:
  - `--org` OR `--project` but resolves to org_id deterministically and prints it.
  - an interactive confirmation containing the org slug (e.g., type: `reset demo-acme-sbx`), unless `--non-interactive` is set.
  - when `--non-interactive` is set, requires `--confirm-org-slug=<slug>` (prevents CI jobs from blasting the wrong tenant).
- CLI now prints an “environment fingerprint” (control plane URL + account + org_id) before it sends the request.

Rate limiting + idempotency
- Reset endpoint now enforces:
  - 1 reset / 5 minutes / org_id
  - burst of 2 within 30 seconds / actor_id (to allow “oops, rerun” but avoid spam)
- 429 responses include `Retry-After` and a clear message tailored for SEs.
- Added `Idempotency-Key` support so retries from the CLI don’t create multiple resets.

Auditability / permissions
- New permission `demo.reset.execute` required for API calls.
- All reset attempts (pass/fail) write to audit log with:
  - actor_id, org_id, org_slug, reason (if provided), guard decision, rate limit decision, idempotency key

Changed areas/files
- control plane:
  - api/reset_controller.ts (guard + rate limit + idempotency)
  - services/demo_reset_guard.ts (org eligibility logic)
  - services/rate_limit.ts (reset limiter wiring)
  - auth/permissions.ts (new permission)
  - audit/audit_events.ts (new event type: DEMO_RESET_ATTEMPT)
- cli:
  - cli/commands/demo/reset.ts (confirmation + fingerprint)
  - cli/http/idempotency.ts (header helper)
- docs/runbooks:
  - docs/internal/demo/reset.md (updated flags + error handling)

Testing
- Unit tests:
  - demo reset guard: flagged vs unflagged orgs; slug mismatch; allowlist path
  - rate limiter: org-based window; actor burst
  - idempotency: same key returns same reset action id
- Integration tests:
  - e2e reset happy path on demo org
  - reset rejected on non-demo org
  - consecutive resets produce 429 with Retry-After
- Manual:
  - Verified CLI interactive flow + non-interactive flags in a staging sandbox

Rollout
- This is gated behind `features.demo_reset_safety_rails` (default ON in demo env; OFF elsewhere until next week).
- Once we confirm no regressions in demo tenant operations, we can enable globally for all environments.

Follow-ups
- ENG-4879: route rate limit metrics to demo alerting dashboards
- ENG-4894: align parallel demo namespaces with per-project reset semantics (today rate limit is per-org)

Notes
- This does not change customer-facing APIs. Reset endpoints are internal-only and require privileged auth.
- Error messaging is intentionally SE-friendly (actionable + suggests healthcheck / Retry-After).
Ethan Park (requested changes): The server-side guard needs to be authoritative; CLI checks are good but can’t be the only line of defense. Also please ensure the permission is separate from org admin and the audit event logs failures too.

Devon Price (author): Agreed. Pushed a commit that makes the guard mandatory in the API handler and adds `demo.reset.execute` permission + audit logging for both allowed and rejected attempts.

Sean Gallagher (requested changes): Rate limit windows look reasonable, but make sure 429 includes Retry-After and that the healthcheck surfaces “last reset” so SEs can self-diagnose. Also confirm we don’t accidentally rate limit healthcheck.

Devon Price (author): Added Retry-After header + human-readable message and updated demo healthcheck output to include last reset timestamp/action id + current limiter state. Healthcheck path is unaffected.

Allison Grant (comment): Please export metrics for guard rejects and rate limit hits; can be follow-up but at least add TODO + event tags.

Devon Price (author): Added tags to the audit event and a TODO referencing ENG-4879 for dashboarding/alerts.

Markus Klein (approval): CLI UX looks good for SE workflow. Confirmed the non-interactive flags will work in our runbook automation.

Ethan Park (approval): Looks solid. Thanks for adding the allowlist override with empty default + config-only.

Sean Gallagher (approval): Approved; aligns with demo incident learnings from SUP-4127.

Motivation: reduce tail latency and per-token GPU cost for mixed short/long chat workloads by introducing a new attention kernel (Chorus) that combines a banded tiled attention path with an in-GPU opcache for hot KV slices, and a lane-reservation scheduler to improve continuous batching locality. This PR implements the Chorus kernel, a lightweight opcache layer for KV hot slices (opcache), and an adaptive lane-reservation scheduler that maintains low SLO violations under bursty traffic. The changeset includes CUDA kernel code, scheduler integration, e2e perf harness updates, and unit/integration tests. Checklist: - [x] Implement Chorus attention kernel with fused rotary/op fusion path - [x] Add opcache for KV hot-slices with fallback to main KV store - [x] Integrate lane-reservation scheduler with continuous batcher - [x] Add synthetic and replay perf tests and baseline comparisons - [x] Add runtime flags and telemetry (metrics/traces) - [x] Add docs snippet for operator flags and rollout plan High-level approach: Chorus kernel implements a narrow-band tiled attention path for sequence windows up to 2048 tokens with a fused rotary multiplication and qkv-permute fusion to reduce memory traffic. The kernel supports an opcache region stored in GPU memory (configurable size) for recently-accessed KV slices; cache lookup is O(1) with an LRU-ish eviction tuned for prefix reuse patterns seen in chat workloads. Scheduler changes allow lane reservations: requests are mapped to ephemeral lanes keyed by model+session so that KV-cache hits are preserved across contiguous requests; the lane-reservation logic holds a lane for short periods (configurable 10-200ms) before releasing it, allowing continuous batching to coalesce while preserving latency SLOs. Rollout plan: staged canary on dedicated pool -> 10% hosted -> 50% hosted -> full by config. Observability: added metrics redwood.attn.chorus.opcache.hit_ratio, redwood.attn.chorus.evictions, redwood.scheduler.lane_reservations.active, per-route tail latency percentiles. Backwards compatibility: kernel registers as an alternate implementation selected by runtime policy. If opcache is disabled or memory constraints hit, runtime falls back to the existing flashbridge-attn path. Performance summary (internal perf harness, T4-like instance): - 95th latency improved by 18-28% for mixed short/long chat trace - per-token GPU cycles decreased by ~12% on average for warm sessions - throughput for long-context batch steady-state up by ~6% Commits: - Implement chorus kernel initial prototype and microbench harness - Add opcache allocator and eviction policy - Integrate lane reservation into continuous batcher and routing - Perf harness updates and new replay traces - Tests and docs, flag gating, unit tests - Fix CI failures (memory fence ordering, thread-safety) Merge notes: this was rolled as a squash merge after CI perf checks and a small canary run. 
Ethan Li: Overall looks promising. We need a microbenchmark showing worst-case eviction overhead — please add a synthetic KV-skew microbenchmark and include numbers.
Maya Patel (author): Added opcache_kv_skew.yaml and results; worst-case eviction overhead kept <4% of token time on our T4-like profile.
Samira Khan: Please gate opcache behind a runtime flag and make sure telemetry records when fallback occurs. Also add a perf CI check that runs the replay trace.
Maya Patel (author): Flag added (runtime.enable_chorus_opcache). Perf CI script added as ci/perf-checks/chorus_bench.sh and hooked into the perf stage. Telemetry metrics emitted on fallback paths.
Jonah Rivera: Thread-safety looks good but add a comment explaining the memory fence ordering for free path, I almost missed it during review.
Maya Patel (author): Comment added and reordered fence to be explicit, re-run CI.
CI system: initial perf-check failed (opcache_free race) -> fix applied -> perf-check passed
build: pass
unit-tests: pass
integration-tests: pass
perf-check: pass (chorus_mixed_chat: 95p latency -20% vs baseline, opcache hit_ratio 0.74)
lint: pass
security-scan: pass
Canary run on dedicated-nd8 pool for 24h: no increase in error-rate, 95p latency decreased 19% on routed sessions that used lane reservations
Observed opcache memory pressure on a small fraction (<0.5%) of nodes on first canary due to default opcache size; reduced default and added telemetry to detect saturation
Introduce Chorus attention kernel: a banded tiled attention implementation with fused rotary and an in-GPU opcache for hot KV slices. Adds lane-reservation scheduling to improve continuous batching locality. Performance: improved 95p latency for mixed chat workloads and reduced per-token GPU cycles for warm sessions. Rollout behind runtime flags. No breaking changes.

Motivation: We see recurring noisy alerts from high-traffic tenant routes where short-lived token-latency spikes cause broad SLO churn. This PR introduces a lightweight golden-route degradation detector that treats a small set of customer-designated "golden" routes as canaries for systemic degradation and couples that signal to an alert-fingerprint index used to suppress or reclassify noisy alerts.

What this PR does: implements an in-memory sliding histogram + exponential dampener for per-token latency/cost traces on golden routes; a compact alert fingerprint index (time-windowed, LRU-backed) that maps correlated metric+trace signatures to fingerprint IDs; a routing policy that tags alerts from dependent routes with the golden-route fingerprint when correlation exceeds threshold; dashboard and alerts updates to visualize correlation scores and fingerprint prevalence.

Design notes: the detector runs as a sidecar plugin in the observability pipeline (small CPU footprint, bounded memory). We intentionally avoid heavy join queries at ingest; fingerprint correlations are calculated via hash-augmented reservoir samples and a lightweight cosine similarity on binned latency/cost vectors. The fingerprint index is exported for downstream incident tooling and linked to existing trace IDs for deep-dive.

Testing and rollout strategy: feature guarded behind "observability.golden_route_detector" feature flag. Step rollout: 1) enable in staging and run synthetic canary traffic for 48h; 2) enable read-only in prod for telemetry collection; 3) enable alert annotation + auto-suppress on a 10% tenant sample; 4) expand as confidence grows.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of detector and fingerprint index
- [x] Unit tests for histogram/reservoir logic and correlation heuristics
- [x] Integration test for alert annotation path
- [x] Dashboard panels and example alerts
- [x] Feature flag gating and rollout plan
- [x] Release notes

Commits summary (high level): see commits section.

Changed areas (high level): core observability pipeline (detector), alert router, dashboards, a couple of SDK instrumentation helpers and tests.

Why this is safe: default mode is observation-only and memory bounded; correlation thresholds are conservative (0.8) and configurable. The change reduces alert noise by reclassifying alerts that match golden-route degradation fingerprints; it does not mute alerts without a matching fingerprint.

Related: linear ENG-6722 and ENG-6777, support ticket SUP-2123 for noisy tenant alerts.

Ethan Zhao: This looks solid overall. A couple questions: how do we avoid false correlation for multi-tenant bursts? Can we add a tenant isolation check to the correlation scorer?
Maya Patel: Added tenant-weight normalization and an isolation threshold (0.25) to the scorer in commit f3c2aa1. See tests/test_golden_route_detector.py for coverage. Commented the algorithm for later tuning.
Lina Gomez: Can we surface the fingerprint ID in the alert UI and link to recent traces? That will help oncall triage.
Maya Patel: Added UI annotation in console/components/alert-details.tsx and an API endpoint to fetch recent trace snippets for a fingerprint. Kept the trace fetch capped to 5 entries to avoid heavy queries.
Arjun Menon: CI flake on windows linting; restarted pipeline. Approving once CI is green.
CI: All checks passed after re-run.
Adds a golden-route degradation detector and compact alert-fingerprint index. The feature is opt-in behind a feature flag and reduces noisy alerts by annotating and reclassifying alerts that correlate with golden-route degradations.
payload.title: Introduce golden-route degradation detector and alert-fingerprint index

payload.body:
## Context
We need a repeatable way to evaluate autoscaling policy changes (min/max bounds enforcement + predictive signals) against historical Dedicated traces before piloting/GA.

This PR adds an offline simulation/replay harness that:
- Replays historical demand + fleet telemetry traces on a fixed timestep
- Runs the autoscaler decision loop (reactive-only, predictive-biased, bounded variants)
- Produces summary stats and a machine-readable report for comparisons/regressions

This is meant to support ENG-22147 ("load test and simulation replay for predictive mode") and unblock faster iteration on the predictive mode work (see PRs #48218, #48227).

## What’s included
- `rw-autoscaler-sim` CLI (internal) with `replay` subcommand
- Trace reader for JSONL "timeseries" traces (from fleet telemetry export) + basic validators
- Policy adapters:
  - `reactive_v1` (queue depth + saturation driven)
  - `predictive_v1` (uses forecast samples when present; falls back to reactive)
  - `bounded_v1` (clamps desired to [min,max] and tracks bound-hit time)
- Summary stats + report output:
  - time_to_recover_s (after ramp/spike)
  - p95_queue_depth / p95_queue_wait_ms (if available in trace)
  - bound_hit_rate_max / bound_hit_rate_min
  - scale_events_up / scale_events_down
  - replica_minutes (proxy for cost)
  - prediction_error_mae (when forecast data exists)
- Minimal plotting helper (CSV output + example gnuplot command in docs) — no heavy deps

## Usage
Example:
`./bin/rw-autoscaler-sim replay \
  --trace ./data/traces/hexagon-us-east-1-2025-06-10.jsonl \
  --policy reactive_v1 \
  --policy bounded_v1:min=6,max=24 \
  --policy predictive_v1:forecast=./data/forecasts/hexagon-forecast.csv \
  --step-ms 5000 \
  --out ./out/hexagon-2025-06-10.report.json`

Outputs:
- Human summary to stdout
- JSON report file containing per-policy stats + a compact timeline of desired/bounded decisions

## Trace format (v0)
JSONL rows keyed by timestamp:
- `ts_ms` (required)
- `observed_rps` (required)
- `queue_depth` (optional)
- `replicas_actual` (required)
- `gpu_utilization` (optional)
- `p95_latency_ms` (optional)

Forecast (optional CSV): `ts_ms, predicted_rps`.

## Why this approach
- Deterministic runs (seeded) so we can use it as a regression gate later
- Offline/airgapped friendly (no calls to control plane / fleet APIs)
- Lets us test edge cases: stale/missing forecasts, rapid ramp, periodic spikes, and bound saturation

## Safety / data handling
- Tool expects already-sanitized traces (no request content). Docs call out this requirement.
- Added a validator that fails if unknown fields look like payload content (e.g., `prompt`, `messages`).

## Docs
- `docs/infra/autoscaler/sim-replay.md` describes trace generation, running locally, and interpreting metrics.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Wire into perf-canary scenarios (tracked in ENG-22147)
- Add a small suite of "golden" traces in CI (needs storage/size decisions)
- Add additional metrics for min-bound unmet due to region shortage (see ENG-22151)

## Checklist
- [x] Deterministic output (stable ordering, seeded RNG)
- [x] Unit tests for trace parsing + clamping invariants
- [x] Basic docs
- [x] CI green

Related:
- Linear: ENG-22147, PM-1842
- PRs: #48218 (bounds enforcement), #48227 (forecast provider interface)
Vanessa Ortiz: Can we make sure this uses the same clamp semantics as the production autoscaler loop (incl. cooldown/step sizing)?
Jamal Pierce: Yep — bounded_v1 calls the shared clamp helper from pkg/autoscaler/policy. Cooldown/step sizing isn’t modeled yet; added a TODO in docs + follow-up note in ENG-22147.
Keiko Yamamoto: The report JSON looks useful. Request: include both requested_desired and bounded_desired per step so we can audit why the clamp was hit.
Jamal Pierce: Added `timeline.desired_requested` and `timeline.desired_bounded` arrays (downsampled by default, configurable with --timeline-sample-every).
Sana Farid: For prediction_error_mae, please clarify whether it’s MAE on RPS or replicas. Also add staleness handling so we don’t accidentally compare against shifted timestamps.
Jamal Pierce: Updated metric definition (MAE on predicted_rps vs observed_rps) and added `--forecast-max-staleness-ms` defaulting to 10m; stale forecast rows are ignored and counted in `forecast_stale_steps`.
Rafael Mendes: CI failure on integration_smoke: is this new binary included in the release image? I’d rather keep it internal only.

Background and motivation: production traces show persistent tail padding inefficiency when a small number of very short requests interleave with a long-running cohort, which inflates per-token cost and increases kernel launch overhead on multi-tenant queues. This PR introduces the 'sliding-cutoff length-fusion batcher', a hybrid heuristic that combines a dynamically-updated length cutoff with a greedy fusion pass to coalesce close-length requests into a fusion slot. Goals: reduce padding overhead for mixed-length workloads, preserve latency SLOs for short requests, and keep admission logic cheap for the hot path. Key ideas: 1) Maintain a lightweight moving-statistics window per-slot that estimates 90th/median seqlen distribution; 2) Compute a sliding cutoff T such that requests with length <= T are eligible to be fused into short slots while longer requests are routed to long slots; 3) Greedy fusion: within a short-slot, allow limited fusion of one long request if combined padding cost is below a configurable threshold; 4) Integrate with KV-cache prefill: when a fusion includes a long request, prefetch its KV slices ahead-of-time to avoid stall when fused into an ongoing short slot. Implementation summary: - runtime/batching/sliding_cutoff.py: new coordinator implementing per-slot moving windows (exponential EWMA) and sliding cutoff computation; admission APIs for is_eligible(request, slot) and try_fuse(request, slot). - runtime/batching/fusion_policy.py: fusion cost model and configurable thresholds, unit-tested. - runtime/serve/slot_coordinator.py: hook points where the batch scheduler consults the sliding-cutoff coordinator before enqueuing/fusing. - runtime/kv/prefetcher.py: small opt-in prefetch path to pre-populate KV-cache for fused long requests; guarded behind a feature flag. - tests/runtime/batching/test_sliding_cutoff.py and integration tests under tests/integration/batching/cover_mixed_lengths.py. Performance impact: on our internal mixed-workload harness (50% short < 32 tokens, 30% mid 32-256, 20% long > 1024) we observed a 12-18% reduction in average pad-tokens-per-request and a 6-10% improvement in avg tokens/sec normalized for identical GPU allocation. Tail latency p95 for short requests improved by ~8-12ms in heavy load scenarios due to avoidance of long-slot head-of-line blocking. Backwards compatibility and rollout: the feature is behind a runtime flag 'enable_sliding_cutoff_fusion' and defaulted-off for dedicated customers until 2 weeks of canary telemetry. The config surface includes: sliding_window_alpha, cutoff_percentile (default 90), fusion_cost_threshold, kv_prefetch_enabled (default false), and max_fusion_long_rate (safeguard against too many long fusions). Checklist: - [x] design doc (Linear ENG-2394) and microbenchmarks - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] feature-flag gating and telemetry hooks - [x] docs: short note in Batching Guide - [x] observability: added metrics for cutoff T per-slot and fusion decisions - [x] rollout plan attached to ENG-2411 Changeset summary: see commits list below. Related work: differs from bucketing/quantile approaches by keeping per-slot learned thresholds and allowing opportunistic fusion (rather than rigid buckets). This keeps scheduling cheap and adapts quickly to workload shifts. Caveats: in synthetic pathological patterns (bursty long-only tail) aggressive fusion can increase KV pressure; we protect against that via kv_prefetch_enabled=false default and by sampling-based backpressure metrics.
Miguel Santos: Nice approach, Aisha. Two questions: 1) how expensive is the per-slot EWMA in high-slot-count setups? 2) can you show a microbenchmark that isolates kernel launch overhead improvements?
Aisha Patel: EWMA is constant per slot (2 flops per update) and we keep the update in the scheduler hot-path with an inlined fast-path; added a microbenchmark commit that measures kernel-launch rate and pad-token stats. See commit b2c9e51.
Jingwei Zhao: Looks good overall. Please add a safety cap so that cutoff never goes below min_eligible_token (to avoid starving mids). Also request: emit a gauge metric for sampled fusion cost so we can tune the threshold without re-deploying.
Aisha Patel: Added min_eligible_token (config) and a fusion_cost_sample metric in c3d0a8f. Also added a test which verifies cutoff clamp behavior.
Oliver Grant: Approving after a couple nits in doc wording and renaming 'kv_prefetch_enabled' to be explicit in console UI. Please squash and rebase on latest main.
Aisha Patel: Addressed doc wording and updated flag name to 'enable_kv_prefetch_for_fusion' and rebased. Squash ready.
All checks passed: unit tests (runtime/batching) 24s, integration (cover_mixed_lengths) 2m12s, linting (python/ruff) 8s, typechecks 10s. One flake in earlier run was retried and cleared.
Merged by squash on 2024-11-12 by Miguel Santos. Merge method: squash. Merge commit message: "sliding-cutoff fusion batcher: adaptive cutoff + greedy fusion to reduce padding and kernel overhead (ENG-2394)"
Introduce sliding-cutoff fusion batcher (opt-in) to reduce padding overhead for mixed-length workloads. Default disabled; see Batching Guide for config and rollout notes.
Gated behind runtime flag 'enable_sliding_cutoff_fusion' and 'enable_kv_prefetch_for_fusion'. Recommended canary: enable on 2 dedicated slots for 48h and watch metrics: batching.cutoff_value, batching.fusion_attempts, kv.prefetch_hits, scheduler.pad_tokens_per_request. Rollback: flip feature flags off.

Motivation: Customers frequently ask for a way to codify budget/latency tradeoffs as shareable templates and to prevent overly aggressive quantization during automated rollouts. This PR introduces 'affordance-tiler', a small declarative templates-as-code subsystem plus a CLI previewer and a conservative quantization 'fence' that blocks quant profiles which historically increased perplexity by >X% in our evals.

What this PR does (single-line description followed by details):
- Adds a templates module that compiles tenant budget/latency constraints into batch/cache/quant suggestion bundles (JSON templates that can be applied via rwctl or the infra API).
- Provides rwctl affordance-tiler preview and dry-run commands so SRE/SEs can inspect expected unit-econ delta before applying.
- Introduces a quant_fence that hooks into the autosuggest pipeline: quant profiles flagged by the fence are listed as "blocked" and require manual approval. The fence is conservative by default and driven by threshold JSON shipped with the telemetry templates.
- Ships telemetry templates (telemetry/templates/budgeted_batch.json) that add unit-econ counters and delta histograms used by the Optimize team.
- Includes docs and examples for onboarding and a short e2e integration test for the CLI.

Why unique: Instead of pushing a single default, the affordance-tiler encourages templated tradeoffs (e.g., "latency-tier: moderate + budget: low") and provides a human-in-the-loop safety net for quantization that reduced past regressions. This is intended to be used together with the existing econ-suggester but as an opt-in policy layer for tenants.

Checklist:
- [x] Templates compiler + representation (pkg/econ/templates)
- [x] rwctl subcommand and dry-run preview (cmd/rwctl/affordance_tiler.go)
- [x] Quant fence implementation and config loader (pkg/econ/quant_fence.go)
- [x] Telemetry templates and example dashboards (telemetry/templates/budgeted_batch.json, docs/telemetry.md)
- [x] Integration test for preview and template apply (tests/integration/tiler_cli_test.go)
- [x] Docs and quickstart (docs/affordance-tiler.md)

Diff summary (high-level, not a full patch):
- New: pkg/econ/templates/tiler.go - template compiler and serializer (core logic + unit tests).
- New: pkg/econ/quant_fence.go - fence logic, threshold loader and API surface used by suggester.
- New: cmd/rwctl/affordance_tiler.go - CLI commands: preview, dry-run, apply (apply is gated behind an experiment flag).
- New: telemetry/templates/budgeted_batch.json - telemetry schema for unit-econ counters and delta histograms.
- New: docs/affordance-tiler.md - onboarding guide and examples.
- New: tests/integration/tiler_cli_test.go - integration test that runs preview and validates expected JSON output.

Commits (summary):
- feat(tiler): initial compiler and template model
- feat(cli): add rwctl affordance-tiler preview/dry-run commands
- feat(quant): quant_fence implementation and config loader
- docs: onboarding guide and telemetry examples
- tests: add integration test for CLI preview

Testing and CI notes:
- First CI run failed on unit test related to a flakey histogram helper (pkg/telemetry/hist_test.go). I fixed the helper and force-pushed.
- Second CI run passed all checks (build, unit, integration, lint). The PR was approved by Jonah and Priya after one round of feedback on error messages and logging verbosity.

Rollout plan:

- Run canary with 2 pilot tenants (internal staging tenants) and collect econ deltas for 48h.
- If deltas are within expected bounds and no regressions in NLU eval sets, flip feature flag and enable opt-in defaults in Console.

Backwards compatibility and safety:
- All changes are behind opt-in paths: templates are not applied automatically. The quant_fence returns metadata but does not mutate existing profiles.
- Telemetry schemas are additive.

Links: Linear: ENG-3123, PM brief: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3123/affordance-tiler, internal runbook: /docs/runbooks/affordance-tiler-canary.md

Maya Chen: Addressed. Added deterministic JSON marshal in tiler.go and appended a note about tail latency caveats in docs. PTAL.

Motivation: Customers with mixed steady and bursty workloads were hitting hard reservation limits and observed large tail-latency spikes when burst traffic attempted to consume headroom. This PR adds a rate-capacity orchestrator that treats tenant reservations as a budgeted rate window, synthesizes a progressive backoff when budget is exhausted, and provides a soft fallback routing policy to route acceptable burst traffic to fallback capacity (spot/overflow pools or lower-cost model variants) before rejecting requests.

What this implements: 1) a new controller (controllers/rate_orchestrator.go) that computes per-tenant rate budgets derived from negotiated reservations, recent utilization percentiles, and configured warmup windows; 2) a soft-fallback policy (pkg/orchestrator/fallback.go) with pluggable strategies: route-to-spot, degrade-model-quality, or enqueue-to-warm-pool; 3) a lightweight utilization sampler (pkg/telemetry/util_sampler.go) that emits p50/p75/p95/p99 utilization sketches every 10s and a compact percentile snapshot for billing and fairness; 4) config knobs exposed in Dedicated helm values and the private installer (values.dedicated.rateOrchestrator.*) for tuning horizons and grace windows; 5) an e2e test harness that simulates burst patterns and verifies SLA preservation across headroom loss and fallback.

Backward compatibility: The orchestrator is feature-flagged (feature.rateCapacityOrchestrator=false by default) and does not change existing admission paths unless enabled per-fleet. The soft fallback is additive and defaults to route-to-spot when available.

Testing checklist: - Unit tests for budget calculator, backoff policy, and fallback selector (new test files under pkg/orchestrator) - Integration test that runs against local-fleet simulator to validate fallback routing during headroom exhaustion - Load test scenario that verifies p99 latency does not regress by more than 10% under representative burst mix - Manual validation steps included in docs/dedicated/autoscale.md

Rollout plan: 1) behind feature flag in canary fleet for 48h, 2) enable soft-fallback to spot pools by default in canary, 3) monitor utilization sampler metrics and per-tenant rejection rates, 4) gradual rollout to remaining fleets in 2-week increments with automatic rollback if p99 latency increases >15% or rejection rates spike >3x.

Operational notes: The utilization sampler introduces a new metric series redwood.orch.util_pct_samples{tenant, pool} and a compact sketch export redwood.orch.util_sketch. Telemetry retention defaults to 7 days for these series. There is a new alert rule (alerts/dedicated/rate-orch-high-rejection.yaml) that fires if tenant rejection_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m after rollout.

Related work: builds on top of the warm-pool work (PR 81502) and the recent soft-reservation gateway changes; it also integrates with billing delta probes being shipped in ENG-9783.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the fallback decision deterministic (no randomized sampling) so we can reason about fairness during early experiments. Future iterations will add weighted probabilistic routing if we observe pathological queueing patterns.
Anjali Rao: Can we make the fallback selection pluggable via feature-flag so ops can prefer degrade-model over route-to-spot in regulated fleets? -- Reply: Yes, added a runtime-config toggle and documented ops behavior.
Markus Chen: Budget calc looks good; add comments explaining why we use EWMA with 30s half-life for short bursts. -- Reply: Added inline doc and a unit test that shows sensitivity to half-life.
Priya Natarajan: Telemetry cardinality concerns for samples per-tenant. How expensive is sketch export at 1s resolution? -- Reply: We keep sampling at 10s by default and export compact quantiles once per 10s; added config to reduce frequency and sampled tenanted export to the canary only.
Ops (Diego Alvarez): Make sure alert thresholds are conservative during rollout; reduced default alert floor to 0.5% rejection rate.
Introduce a rate-capacity orchestrator and soft fallback routing for burst traffic. Feature-flagged and off by default. Adds per-tenant utilization sampling metrics, fallback strategies, and helm/operator knobs for tuning. Backward-compatible rollout. See docs/dedicated/autoscale.md for details.
If enabling in a private fleet, set feature.rateCapacityOrchestrator=true and pick fallback.strategy in the helm values. Watch redwood.orch.util_pct_samples and alerts/dedicated/rate-orch-high-rejection.yaml. If using route-to-spot fallback, ensure spot pool capacity is declared in fleet config.

Motivation: tracing and metric volume from large token-producing workloads has grown nonlinearly; existing static sampling wastes signal and increases cost. This PR implements an adaptive sampling mechanism that reduces telemetry volume while preserving high-fidelity traces for tokens and phases that matter (e.g., model warmup, re-ranking, long-tail token spikes). It also attaches a lightweight token-phase annotation to spans so downstream rollups and dashboards can attribute latency/cost to logical phases.

Summary of changes: added an adaptive sampler service bound into the telemetry pipeline; exposed per-route token-phase sampling policies; emitted a compact token_phase tag on spans; introduced token-phase histogram rollup and an Observability Dashboard panel for phase-aligned latency/cost heatmaps; added an alert tuning helper that uses phase-aware baselines to reduce false positives.

Key design points: the sampler uses a two-stage decision: (1) fast local heuristic based on recent token rate and phase label density, (2) low-frequency Bayesian recalibration that ensures rare phases receive minimum coverage. Sampling is cost-weighted: high-cost invocations get higher sample probability. The phase tag is intentionally compact (enum string) and stored as "phase" in span tags so existing trace indexing works.

Compatibility: new feature is gated behind a runtime flag (telemetry.adaptive_sampler.enabled) and a per-tenant policy in the console. When disabled the pipeline preserves current, stable sampling. Backwards compatibility retained for older spans without phase tags.

Results from internal canary (2-week run across staging cluster): end-to-end trace volume dropped ~36% overall, token-attributed trace volume dropped ~42% for high-throughput routes, and error/latency alert noise reduced by ~18% (measured as reduced alert count on pilot tenants). CPU overhead for the sampler is <2% p95 for the telemetry node; memory delta negligible.

Testing and rollout: unit tests added for sampler heuristics and phase propagation; e2e replay bench validates sample rates versus expected distributions; dashboard panels exercised in a manual QA run. Rollout plan: enable flag in staging for 48h, then progressive canary across 5%/25%/100% tenants with monitoring checks (trace volume, SLOs, alert counts).

Related: complements ENG-8471 (phase tagging standardization) and SUP-1103 (customer request to reduce billing trace noise).
Omar Haddad: Please add a short note on how this affects billing traces for customers on Dedicated - we need to ensure billing accuracy.
Nina Rodriguez: Reply: sampler does not alter token cost computation, only which spans are retained; added explicit note in docs and console UI clarifying billing separation.
Lena Kim: Request changes: tighten unit tests around the low-frequency Bayesian recalibration edge case where phase cardinality is high.
Nina Rodriguez: Addressed - added deterministic seeding and an additional integration test (sampler_test.go::TestRecalibrationEdge) and fixed off-by-one in windowing.
Marcus Bell: Approved after CI green and a successful staging canary run (observed expected reduction in alert noise).
Introduces an opt-in adaptive telemetry sampler and token-phase span annotations. Reduces trace volume for high-throughput routes and provides phase-aware dashboards and alert tuning. Disabled by default; enable via telemetry.adaptive_sampler.enabled.

Motivation: customers and internal controls have asked for a mechanism to block specific KMS key identifiers (denylist) at the service boundary while ensuring audit logs remain consistent for residency policy enforcement. This PR introduces a service-level KMS denylist (operator-provided) that short-circuits key usage and records a deterministic audit 'fence' event when requests are refused due to residency/KMS policy conflicts.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds a KMS denylist lookup and enforcement hook in the KMS allocator middleware. Operator-provided denylist entries are loaded from the residency manifest and cached with TTL and proof-of-origin metadata.
- When a denylist hit occurs, the request is rejected with 403 + structured error code (residency.kms_denylist) and an immutable audit fence event is emitted with fields: request_id, tenant_id, claimed_region, denied_key_id, policy_version, decision_time. The fence event is formatted for downstream audit collectors and is tagged to prevent accidental redaction.
- Introduces an audit-consistency middleware that correlates KMS decisions with residency manifests to detect drift between deployed denylist entries and the operator manifest (background reconciliation job + one-off check endpoint).
- Adds small operator UI telemetry hooks and a README describing how to update the residency manifest, contract tests for fence event shape, and a migration job for older audit consumers.

Why this is safe:
- Denylist enforcement is opt-in per-cluster via operator config; default behavior is unchanged.
- We use a fast in-memory cache with signed manifest checks to avoid per-request crypto; background reconciler validates signatures periodically.
- All audit fence events are written to the existing immutable audit pipeline; no new storage paths are introduced.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests for KMS allocator denylist path and fence event construction.
- Integration tests that exercise reject+audit behavior in the staging audit pipeline.
- Canary rollout: bind denylist enforcement to flag operator.kms_enforce_denylist with percentage-based rollout.
- Post-rollout checklist includes monitoring for an increase in residency.kms_denylist metrics and reconciliation alerts.

Related work: Linear ENG-4301 (residency policy hardening), ENG-4479 (audit pipeline schema v2), and doc ticket DOC-189 (operator habits).

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed by security and compliance
- [x] Unit/integration tests added
- [x] Backwards-compatible audit format with migration notes
- [x] Canaries and feature flag support

Notes for reviewers: look closely at KMS allocator change for contention and the audit fence schema; there is a small risk of double-emitting events if the allocator retry path is exercised — I added an idempotency token derived from request_id + decision_time to dedupe in the audit sink.
Marco Li: Please check allocator hot path; are we doing a synchronous manifest verification on cold-start? That will spike latency.
Sofia Nguyen: Good point — manifest verification is async on startup; allocator consults cache only and triggers background verify. Updated both code paths and tests to cover that (see commit d4e5f6a).
Priya Patel: Audit fence schema looks fine but we need to ensure it is consistent with ENG-4479 schema v2. Can you add a compatibility shim?
Sofia Nguyen: Added a migration shim in fence_writer.go and documented the mapping in docs. Integration tests assert both formats.
James O'Connor: Approve after unit tests finish — particularly want assertions around idempotency tokens to avoid duplicate audit rows.
CI: unit tests failed on first run due to flaky reconciliation test; reworked test timing and re-run passed.
Introduces operator-managed KMS denylist enforcement and emits deterministic 'residency.kms_denylist' audit fence events on denied requests. Backwards-compatible audit migration shim included. Feature is off by default and gated by operator.kms_enforce_denylist.

Context: We need stronger guarantees that audit payloads emitted from downstream services are both integrity-signed and encrypted with tenant-aware keys, and that operator-scoped elevated actions are timeboxed via short-lived leases that are provable and revocable. This PR adds two coordinated features: 1) an audit envelope encryption policy that wraps audit events in an authenticated, tenant-bound envelope encrypted with a CMK-resident key (KMS-integrated); 2) an operator lease guard: a temporal RBAC layer where elevated operator tokens are issued with KMS-signed lease proofs and validated by the gate before performing sensitive actions.

What changed (high level): - audit/encryption: add envelope_writer and envelope_reader that construct AES-GCM envelopes with a per-tenant KMS-wrapped data key, plus a provenance header (kms_key_id, nonce, region_tag). Envelopes are versioned (v1). - auth/rbac: introduce lease_manager and lease_prover. Leases are requested via operator service, signed by a KMS asymmetric key (lease signing key) and carry expiry + operation-scopes. Gate middleware verifies signature and expiry and increments audit counters for issuance/validation. - migration: audit-forwarder updated to support transparent rewrap for legacy plaintext events during a staged rollout. A migration job (scripts/migrate-audit-to-envelopes) re-encrypts historical events into envelopes for customers that opt into full encryption. - helm/ops: add feature flags (audit.encryption.enabled, operator.leases.enabled) and a runtime toggle for staged rollout. - docs: new security runbook and operator lease docs (docs/security/operator-leases.md) and migration guide.

Why: This design gives: (a) tenant-scoped confidentiality for audit bodies while preserving deterministic indexing for metadata; (b) non-repudiable operator lease proofs allowing short-lived elevated actions to be revoked or audited; (c) clear migration path with opt-in rewrap to avoid customer-impact during rollout.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for envelope_reader/writer and lease signature validation - [x] Integration tests exercising KMS-wrapped data key generation (using KMS emulator in CI) - [x] Migration script + dry-run mode - [x] Helm values and runtime feature gate - [x] Docs and runbook - [x] Security review (SEC-129)

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to canary region with audit.encryption.enabled=false and operator.leases.enabled=false. 2) Enable audit.encryption in passive mode (writer emits envelopes, forwarder still accepts plaintext during transition). 3) Run migration dry-run and sample rewrap for selected tenants. 4) Flip opt-in tenants to envelope-only and enable operator.leases for SRE/SE teams. 5) Gradually expand. Rollback flips feature flags and runs rewrap-reverse tool if needed.

Testing: CI covers unit/integration with local KMS emulator. Manual smoke on staging included: issuance of lease -> signed token verification -> run privileged endpoint -> audit entry present and readable only via envelope_reader with tenant CMK.

Related: ENG-8421 (RBAC leasing), SEC-129 (audit encryption threat model), SUP-4421 (customer reported audit exposition).
Marcus Li: Left a few comments on key rotation semantics and cache expiry for wrapped DEKs. Also: please ensure envelope versioning is forward-compatible.
Aisha Khan: Addressed in a1f3d9c and b4e2f77 — added explicit rotation tests and a migration toggle. Reply: the cache TTL for wrapped DEKs is now a helm value (audit.encryption.dek_cache_ttl).
Sofia Patel: Can we add a monitoring metric for 'lease_validation_failures' and an alert for sudden rises?
Aisha Khan: Added metric lease_validation_failures and alert rule in deploy/helm/templates/alerts.yaml in follow-up commit f2aa4b0.
Diego Fernandez: Security scan flagged insufficient entropy in the emulator-only keygen helper — tests updated to use crypto/rand.
Add tenant-bound audit envelope encryption (opt-in) and temporal operator leases (RBAC) using KMS-signed proofs. Feature gated via helm values: audit.encryption.enabled and operator.leases.enabled. Migration tooling provided to rewrap historical audit events.
Operators must provision a lease-signing KMS key (asymmetric) and set KMS role bindings. Default helm values leave features disabled. Migration script supports dry-run. See docs/security/audit-encryption-migration.md for step-by-step commands.
Threat model appendix added to SEC-129; attacker incentives considered for replay, rewrap, and key compromise. Added mitigations: envelope versioning, short DEK cache TTLs, KMS key rotation guidance.

Motivation: Our lint/test feedback loop has grown slow and coupled to monolithic workflows. This PR splits the lint pipeline into modular executors (fast vs. full), introduces a fast 'dry-run' release prober that validates release artifacts without publishing, and standardizes the Go-based CI entrypoint used by multiple repos. The goals are: 1) speed up PR feedback for common edits, 2) make full lint/test runs deterministic and cacheable, 3) provide a preflight 'release dry-run' check that catches packaging/manifest/semantic-version regressions before any publish step.

What changed (high level): - Introduced ci/actions/lint-orchestrator.yml which dispatches to two lanes: fast-lint and full-lint. Fast-lint performs staged checks (tsc, gofmt, basic go vet) and runs only on changed packages. Full-lint runs full unit/integration suites and end-to-end static analyzers. - Added packages/ci/exec-runner: small Go binary used as a hermetic CI entrypoint to standardize environment setup, caching hints, and exit codes across runners. Replaces ad-hoc shell logic in several workflows. - Added tools/release/prober/dryrun.go (+ README) implementing a repository-aware dry-run that: validates release manifest, computes artifact hashes, simulates publishing to internal staging storage without side-effects, and reports a machine-readable report (json) to the CI log. - Updated scripts/ci/run_lint.sh -> now a thin wrapper that calls the Go exec-runner. Kept the shell wrapper to preserve dev local-run ergonomics. - Added lightweight caching strategy and path-aware warmup for node_modules and Go modcache in workflows. - Small housekeeping: pinned a handful of GH Action versions, bumped setup-go to 1.22 action to reduce flakiness.

Testing and rollout: - Iterative verification performed on staging by landing a draft in the redwood-internal:staging branch. - CI flakiness observed on first run (integration shard) due to an environment variable mismatch; fixed in commit 4 by adding explicit BUILD_ENV in orchestrator. - All tests green on final run and reviewers approved.

Checklist: - [x] Fast-lint lane implemented and tested locally - [x] Full-lint lane implemented and smoke tested on staging - [x] Dry-run prober covers manifests and artifact hashing - [x] Exec-runner binary cross-built for linux/amd64 - [x] Workflows updated and pinned action versions - [x] Documentation: tools/release/prober/README.md and ci/README.md updated

Rollout plan: Gradually enable fast-lint on low-traffic repos first (redwood-examples, redwood-sdk-typescript) then flip on core redwood once we observe stable cache hit rates. Dry-run prober will be wired into the release pipeline as a gated required check for release branches.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the old shell wrappers to avoid breaking local dev flows; long-term we plan to deprecate them with an opt-in migration guide in ENG-1180.

Add packages/ci/exec-runner Go binary and tests
Implement tools/release/prober dry-run logic and report schema
Wire exec-runner into existing lint scripts and update docs

payload.body:
Motivation: We observed intermittent tenant SLO regressions during throttle-policy churn and brief regional capacity spikes. Two common pain points: 1) tenant throttles are applied asynchronously (policy API -> control-plane cache -> runtime) which leads to short windows where priority queues become unbalanced; 2) client retry storms amplify short throttles and cause knock-on latency spikes. This PR introduces a three-part mitigation: a background soft-throttle reconciler, a fast-retry escape backoff path, and a degraded-standby routing policy for exhausted-tenant cases. Summary of changes: - runtime/throttle: add soft_throttle_reconciler component (periodic reconcile, transient-window smoothing, per-tenant hysteresis) so policy changes converge gently instead of flipping queues instantly - gateway/retry: implement fast-retry-escape (short, jittered client-facing backoff + local token dampener to prevent retries from re-entering the same hot path) - router: degraded-standby route selection that prefers lower-cost model-variants when tenant budget is exhausted but region health is OK - observability: new metrics (soft_throttle_reconciliations_total, fast_retry_escapes, standby_route_falls) and tracing spans for reconcile runs - config/feature-flag: runtime toggle (soft_throttle_reconciler.enabled) and staged rollout parameters - tests: integration test suite (soft_throttle_integration_test) plus unit coverage for reconciler and backoff logic Rollout plan: feature disabled by default. Canary enable in 3 internal namespaces for 48h, verify throttle smoothing metrics and absence of retry amplification, then gradual enable across regions. If SLO regressions appear, toggle off and the reconciler will stop accepting new smoothing windows within 10s. Backwards compatibility: reconciler reads existing policy payloads; no schema changes to API. Related work: ENG-8421 (throttle observability), ENG-8443 (retry-safety), SUP-4467 (customer ticket reporting repeated transient 503s).
Arjun Rao: Please add a small note about the reconciler run frequency and CPU budget; reconcile every 2s looks safe but we should gate by cpu_percent. Author (Maya): switched to adaptive interval (2s->10s) based on region load and added config soft_throttle_reconciler.cpu_budget_pct. Lina Morales: minor nits in metrics naming -- prefer _total suffix on reconciliation counter. Author: renamed metrics and updated dashboards. Jasper Wu: ran canary tests, saw one flaky test related to a time window; asked for test stabilization. Author: replaced real-time waits with virtual clock in test harness; CI passed. Approval: Arjun approved after CPU gating; Lina approved after metrics rename. Merge: squash-merged after green CI and canary verification.
Adds a soft-throttle reconciler to smooth tenant throttle policy changes, a fast-retry escape path to reduce retry amplification, and a degraded-standby routing mode. Feature is behind a flag and rolled out canary-first. No API breaking changes.
payload.title: soft-throttle: reconcile tenant throttles, fast-retry escape, and degraded-standby routing

payload.body:
Context and motivation: A recent incident (SUP-817) showed repeated cross-zone failovers causing mass KV cache invalidation, which amplified token latency and triggered SLO regressions for a small set of high-throughput tenants. The root cause was an aggressive circuit reopen path combined with global KV flush semantics during transparent fallback. This patch provides a fast hotfix with three coordinated pieces: 1) a 'KV sticky fallback' mode that preserves per-request KV/ prefix caches for short windowed failovers (configurable TTL), 2) a SLO Degradation Inspector service that computes lightweight per-tenant SLO drift and gates circuit state transitions, and 3) a conservative reopen backoff tweak for the regional circuit breaker to avoid oscillation.

Change summary (single-string):
- Introduced kv/sticky_fallback.go: implements a short-lived sticky reservation of KV prefixes when a request is redirected to a fallback model variant or region; ensures most recent KV entries are shadow-copied to the fallback path for the rescue window. Config options: sticky_window_ms, max_shadow_bytes_per_tenant.
- Added inspector/slo_degradation_inspector.go: background probe that samples per-route latency and error percentiles (p50/p95/err-rate) and exposes a DegradationScore used by the circuit manager to delay reopen when score > threshold.
- Modified circuit/region_breaker.go: integrate DegradationScore check into reopen path and apply exponential reopen backoff with jitter.
- Telemetry: added metrics slo_degradation.score, kv_sticky.shadow_hits, kv_sticky.shadow_misses, kv_sticky.shadow_bytes; added events for "sticky_assigned" and "sticky_released".
- Tests: unit + integration harness updates for sticky fallback scenarios and inspector thresholds; added a load test script used in the incident runbook.

Commits (high-level):
- commit 5e2a9f7: initial kv sticky fallback implementation and config
- commit 7b1c4d2: add slo degradation inspector and protobuf API
- commit 9f3d0a1: wire inspector into region breaker reopen path
- commit a7b6f3c: telemetry + dashboards + test harness updates
- commit f1c9e2b: backport hotfix to release/2026-02 for urgent rollout (cherry-pick)

Files changed (high-level snippets included):
- kv/sticky_fallback.go (new) -- core logic
  "// assign a short-lived sticky token to preserve prefix cache across failover\nfunc AssignSticky(ctx context.Context, tenant string, prefixes []string) (string, error) { ... }"
- inspector/slo_degradation_inspector.go (new) -- sampling probe
  "// DegradationScore in [0,100] computed from p95 latency delta and error-rate change\nfunc ScoreForTenant(tid string) int { ... }"
- circuit/region_breaker.go (modified) -- reopen gating
  "if score := inspector.ScoreForTenant(tid); score > cfg.InspectorDelayThreshold { backoff = backoff * 2 }")
- telemetry/metrics_registry.go (modified) -- new metrics registered
- cmd/loadtest/sticky_failure_scenario.sh (new) -- harness used by SRE during incident
- docs/operational/kv-sticky-fallback.md (new) -- quick runbook and config knobs
- tests/kv_sticky_test.go (new) -- unit tests

Design notes and constraints: sticky_fallback is intentionally conservative: shadow copies are bounded per-tenant, stored in memory on the node handling the fallback, and expire after sticky_window_ms. The design avoids persistent cross-node replication to prevent cascading capacity pressure. The Degradation Inspector samples lightweight histograms (not full traces) to keep CPU cost low and only affects circuit reopen decisions (it is read-only; failures default to permissive behavior after a safe timeout).

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for sticky assignment and release
- [x] Integration test exercising redirect + shadow-hit path
- [x] Load test scenario reproducing observed SLO drift (was run against staging cluster)
- [x] Telemetry dashboards added and annotated in PR
- [x] Backport cherry-pick to release branch for immediate staging rollout

Review conversation (selected threads, single-string):
- Maya Patel (reviewer): "Nice focused hotfix. Two asks: (1) please add a circuit manager metric for how often the DegradationInspector blocks reopen so we can confirm effectiveness; (2) ensure shadow copy size is configurable per-tenant (some tenants have large KV footprints)."
- Arjun (author): "Added metric slo_degradation.block_count and tenant-scoped max_shadow_bytes with default 4MB. Updated tests to validate tenant override."
- Elena Ruiz (reviewer): "Can we add a safety-to-fallback mode: if inspector service becomes unavailable, we should default to a short safe delay rather than immediate reopen. Otherwise risk noisy reopen when inspector is down."
- Arjun (author): "Implemented inspector health-check and default-delay of 2000ms when inspector is unavailable. Documented in runbook."
- Tom Becker (reviewer): "LGTM after nits. Would like an independent canary rollout to 10% of traffic in staging before prod." 
- Arjun (author): "Canary rollout planned; added rollout config and a staging canary job in CI."

CI summary: initial pipeline (unit + linters) passed; integration step failed on first run due to test harness timing (flaky loadtest). Fixed test timing and re-ran; full pipeline passed. e2e-staging run completed with canary routing to 10% for 2 hours and showed 61% reduction in failover-induced p95 delta for the affected tenant in staging.

Observability and post-merge runbook: docs/operational/kv-sticky-fallback.md includes commands to inspect sticky assignments, release them, and force a graceful release for a tenant. Dashboard names: "SLO Inspector - Degradation Score", "KV Sticky - Shadow Hit Rate". Suggested post-merge monitoring window: 48 hours with alerting on slo_degradation.score > 50 or kv_sticky.shadow_bytes > 80% configured budget.

Rollout and rollback plan: squash-merged to main and cherry-picked into release/2026-02 with a small canary (10%) for 2 hours then gradual ramp. Rollback is a single revert of the squash commit (documented) or temporary setting sticky_window_ms=0 to disable sticky mode quickly.

Merge outcome: merged into main via squash on 2026-02-17 after approvals from all reviewers.

Hotfix: improve cross-zone failover to preserve per-request KV cache when routing falls back; add SLO Degradation Inspector to prevent premature circuit reopen and surface tenant-level SLO drift by route.
This PR is targeted at runtime reliability; considered low-risk but urgent. The change is intentionally narrow and guarded by inspector metrics and a small default sticky window.

Introduces mini-bulkhead canary lanes with entropy-driven throttling and instant snapshot rewind support; backwards-compatible rollout API extensions; improved safety for high-churn A/B experiments.
Context: Large canaries introducing capacity spikes and correlated failures during multi-arm experiments motivated a small-surface change to the rollout controller. This PR implements a 'mini-bulkhead' primitive (tiny, isolated serving lanes) and an entropy-driven throttle algorithm that staggers fraction increases across cohorts to avoid synchronized traffic jumps. It also wires in a snapshot-based fast-rewind path: small, frequent snapshots of route state enable near-instant rollback using a rollback credit system that limits noisy fast retries. Motivation: make A/B and multi-canary promotions safer and cheaper for workloads that are sensitive to blast radius. Changes: controller/core: new MiniBulkheadManager, entropy_throttle sampler, rewind_credit ledger; api: rollout manifest v2 additions (miniBulkheads:[], entropySeed, rewindCreditPolicy); scheduler: fraction-step jitterer using per-cohort entropy seeds; snapshotter: lightweight, append-only snapshot journal with TTL and compaction; metrics: new rollout_traffic_jitter_seconds, rewind_credit_usage_total, mini_bulkhead_active_gpus; tests: end-to-end harness simulating 10k request-per-second traffic with synthetic drift; docs: design doc and quickstart; examples: AB YAML for staged micro lanes. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-1429) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added and flakiness investigated - [x] Docs and example updated - [x] Backwards compatibility smoke tested Rollout contract notes: default behavior is unchanged unless rollout manifest includes miniBulkheads; entropySeed is optional and falls back to controller-generated seed for deterministic but varied fractioning per rollout. Operational notes: rewind credits are consumed on each fast-rewind and replenished by time-based credit accrual; cluster admin can set global caps via operator config. Related: this helps mitigate incidents like SUP-5132 by reducing correlated promotion failures.
Unit coverage added for entropy_throttle and rewind ledger. Integration harness simulates drift scenarios and repeated promotions (10k RPS synthetic). Observed median promotion time increase of ~40ms due to snapshot bookkeeping; tradeoff accepted for safety. No regressions on existing rollout flows observed in smoke tests.
Miguel Soto: I like the isolation approach. Please add a brief note in the operator config explaining how rewind credits are topped up and what happens at zero-credit - operators need a predictable default.
Ava Patel: Added operator config defaults and doc blurb in operator/config/defaults.yaml and docs/rollouts/mini-bulkhead.md explaining credit accrual and admin caps.
Priya Ramesh: Integration tests are flaky on first run; I see a race between snapshot compaction and rewind. Can you add a retry/guard in the replay tool and a unit test for concurrent compaction?
Ava Patel: Added guard to snapshot_replay_tool.py and an additional unit test test_snapshot_compaction_race. Also reran the integration job locally to validate stability.
Liam Chen: Small nit: telemetry metric names should follow our snake_case convention exactly (rollout_traffic_jitter_seconds is fine) — please add help strings to the prom file.
Ava Patel: Added help strings and short descriptions in rollout_metrics.prom. Thanks!
Priya Ramesh: Approving pending green CI and one more integration run to be safe.
Miguel Soto: Approving after successful rerun. Recommend squash merge to keep history tidy.
Merged after two approvals and green CI. Squash merged on main. Release notes drafted and docs landed. Cluster operators will be notified of the new operator config flag for rewind credit caps.

payload.body:
Context and motivation:
This change introduces an entropy-driven prioritizer for trace sampling to bias collection toward invocations with high output entropy (a proxy for higher information content and failure likelihood). The goal is to improve signal-to-noise in long-tail SLO investigations without increasing overall ingestion costs. In parallel, we add a Prefetch Warmup Metering dashboard that helps SREs and runtime engineers understand effectiveness of prefetch/warmup heuristics and their impact on token-level cost and tail latency. Finally, we tune token-decay alert thresholds to reduce false positives caused by short-lived traffic spikes.

What this PR does (single continuous description):
- Adds an entropy sampler (observability/tracing/entropy_sampler.go) that computes per-invocation entropy from token logits or token probability distributions, normalizes the score per model family, and produces a priority weight used by the adaptive trace sampling queue. Implementation uses a rolling median absolute deviation (MAD) per model family to keep normalization robust to outliers.
- Introduces invocation_context_ratio (server/invocation_metrics.go) — a compact metric that captures the fraction of prefetched tokens versus total invocation tokens; emitted at the end of invocation. This helps correlate prefetch effectiveness with downstream tail latency and cost.
- Provides a Prefetch Warmup Metering dashboard (dashboards/prefetch-warmup-dashboard.json) with panels for invocation_context_ratio distribution, warmup success rate (measured by early token cache hits), prefetch-induced latency delta, and correlated entropy percentiles.
- Tunes token-decay SLO alert rules (alerts/token-decay-slo.yml): increases aggregation window for low-traffic tenants, adds a 3-minute quiet window to suppress transients from deployment bursts, and lowers alert sensitivity for invocations under a token threshold.
- Adds docs explaining entropy sampling design and migration notes (docs/observability/entropy-sampling.md).
- Updates CI to validate telemetry schema and dashboard JSON against the new metric name.

Checklist (what I did):
- [x] Implementation of entropy prioritizer and runtime hook
- [x] Unit tests for sampler normalization and edge cases
- [x] Emission of invocation_context_ratio and dashboard wiring
- [x] Alert tuning and runbook suggestions
- [x] Documentation and migration notes
- [x] CI updates and green pipeline

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests included (tests/telemetry/entropy_sampler_test.go) cover normalization across synthetic logits and minimum invocation lengths.
- Local e2e against small dev cluster: verified that high-entropy invocations are sampled more often (sample rate for top 5% entropy increased from 1.2x to ~6x under adaptive budget) and overall trace ingestion stayed within configured budget.
- Dashboard panels validated with synthetic metrics exported from a replay harness; sample screenshots attached in the internal Linear ticket.

Rollout plan and risk mitigation:
- Feature is behind a feature flag (telemetry.entropy_prioritizer.enabled) defaulting to off for existing tenants. We will enable for internal tenancy first, then a small canary, and finally global rollout.
- Metrics migration: invocation_context_ratio replaces the older invocation_prefetch_ratio metric; dashboards include a compatibility layer and a migration note.
- Alert tuning will be enabled as a separate flag; rollout includes a 24-hour shadow period before firing page rules to avoid on-call churn.

Operational notes and runbook updates:
- Added a short runbook section in docs/observability/entropy-sampling.md describing how to interpret entropy percentiles and how to temporarily disable prioritizer for a tenant if it causes unexpected sampling concentration.
- Prefetch Warmup dashboard includes export links to CSV for quick offline analysis.

CI summary:
- ci/telemetry-checks.yml updated to assert presence and schema of invocation_context_ratio and entropy sample tag.
- Full telemetry test suite (unit + small e2e replay) passed on linux/amd and linux/arm after reruns.

Review conversation (high level):
- Addressed reviewer questions about normalization and metric naming.
- Resolved CI flakes by widening test timeouts in the replay harness.

Merge outcome:
- Merged to main with squash on 2026-03-04 after approvals and green CI.

Follow-ups (post-merge):
- ENG-2118: schedule a week-long canary and capture pre/post token-cost and tail-latency deltas for the canary tenants.
- Instrument telemetry to emit sampler budget utilization metric (future PR).
- Add an alert that monitors sampler concentration imbalance (to detect if a small subset of calls consumes disproportionate sampling budget).

Ellen Park: Can you clarify how the entropy score is normalized across model families? Suggest adding a short paragraph in docs and a unit test covering a small Llama/Transformer parity case.
Maya Chen (author): Added normalization note and small parity test (entropy_sampler_test.go). The sampler uses median absolute deviation per model family to normalize; flagged in docs.
Samir Gupta: Looks good overall. Two nit picks: rename invocation_ratio -> invocation_context_ratio for clarity, and please add a short migration note in telemetry docs for dashboards relying on old metric name.
Maya Chen: Renamed metric and updated dashboard references. Added migration note under docs/observability/entropy-sampling.md.
Diego Morales: CI flake on linux/arm was unrelated (timeout). Re-ran tests and they passed. Approving once CI is green.
Ellen Park: Approved after docs update; good to merge with squash.

Motivation: multiple SDKs exposed subtly different credential shapes and streaming helpers which caused confusion in downstream platform code and in customer integrations. This PR introduces a small, explicit CredentialContract surface and three concrete, idiomatic streaming examples (Python async iterator, TypeScript async generator, Go channel-based iterator). The goal is ergonomics parity across SDKs while keeping the runtime backoff behavior unchanged. Changes include: extraction of a CredentialContract interface, adapter shims for legacy credential providers, a cross-sdk parity test harness, updated docs with copy-paste ready examples, and coordinated SDK version bumps. Checklist: - [x] Define CredentialContract and document expected behaviors (sync/async, heartbeats) - [x] Implement adapters in py/ts/go to present a consistent API - [x] Add unit + integration parity tests that exercise token refresh, reauth race, and abort semantics - [x] Update examples in docs site and README snippets - [x] Bump SDK minors to 1.21.0 (py/ts/go) - [x] Run CI and address lint/test failures Notes & links: design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/notes/ENG-1248/credential-contract-and-stream-examples; staging integration run: pipeline/infra-e2e/245. Backwards compatibility: legacy credential providers are supported via small adapter shims included in this change. No breaking changes expected for consumers that use official SDKs as shipped, but custom credential implementations that relied on an internal shape may need a one-line adapter. Test plan: cross-sdk parity harness (tests/parity/) runs the same scripted scenarios against each SDK in a containerized environment; added scenarios for rapid token expiry and network interruptions. Deployment: merged to main; no rollout gating required for hosted API surface changes, this affects SDK consumers only.
Liam Chen: Nice separation. Can we make the py contract accept both sync and async token providers without forcing the adapter to be async? Small nit: rename get_token -> fetch_token to communicate possible IO.
Author (Anika Rao): Good point; kept fetch_token as the canonical name and added a thin sync-to-async helper in python adapter to keep ergonomics for simple providers.
Sofia Martinez: Tests look solid. Please add an assertion that aborted streams release credential leases in the parity harness.
Author: Added lease release checks and updated parity harness to assert no stale leases after abort scenarios.
Ethan Patel: CI flake on macos-latest due to a timing-sensitive TLS test — added a small jitter and retry in the test harness to stabilize.
Author: Re-ran CI after jitter fix; all checks passed.
refactor(auth): extract CredentialContract interface and add docs
feat(py): credential adapter + async iterator streaming example
feat(ts): credential adapter + async generator example
feat(go): credential adapter + channel iterator example
test(parity): add cross-sdk parity harness and scenarios for token churn
docs: add copy-paste examples and migration note
chore: bump py/ts/go SDK versions to 1.21.0
SDKs: Introduce CredentialContract interface and concrete streaming examples for Python, TypeScript, and Go. Small adapter shims added for backward compatibility. Parity tests included. SDK versions bumped to 1.21.0. No user-facing breaking changes expected for standard SDK consumers.
