Motivation: After several rollout incidents where a small, high-variance cohort triggered repeated rollbacks and operator churn, we need a primitive that isolates new cohorts and provides deterministic fast-rewind. This PR implements an 'Orbital Cohort Throttle' that places newly promoted cohorts into an orbit with constrained throughput using a time-windowed leaky-bucket per-cohort, and a first-class Rollback Slate artifact that snapshots routing + model-version state so operators can instant-rewind to a known-good slate. It also introduces a Shadow Fidelity Sampler that adapts how much shadow traffic is fully executed versus trimmed based on resource pressure and signal fidelity, preserving telemetry without overloading serving. Changes: controller: new OrbitalThrottleController implementing orbit windows, per-cohort leaky-bucket, slot assignment and metrics; rollback: RollbackSlate struct, manifest_hash tagging, S3 prefix uploader and TTL enforcement; sampler: ShadowFidelitySampler with dynamic policy that can toggle full-path execution, KV-cache warmups, and trace tagging; API: rollout schema additions orbit_window_ms, throttle_qps, rollback_slate_ttl_s; Console: rollout detail shows active slate, rewind action button (ACL-gated); observability: metrics and dashboards for orbit slots, rollback queues and sampler rates; docs & runbook: operational playbook covering when to trigger rewind and abort decision tree. Backwards compatibility: all rollout config fields are optional and default to legacy behavior; RollbackSlate storage reuses existing snapshot S3 bucket under a new prefix. Testing: unit tests for controller logic and slate TTL eviction, deterministic integration replay testing for cohort injection and rewind idempotency, microbenchmarks show <3% p99 overhead for ShadowFidelitySampler. Deployment plan: alpha on internal dev/staging canaries, opt-in API flag for customers, default-off on public clusters. Linked tickets: ENG-1729, ENG-1850, SUP-342. Checklist: design doc linked, unit tests, integration replay, perf benchmark, Console UI, observability hooks, docs and runbook added.

Motivation: Production RBAC v2 policies are increasingly dynamic (timebound grants, operator leases, cross-region operator exceptions). We need an orchestrator that can express temporal RBAC boundaries, translate policy decisions into KMS-scoped evidence, and emit compact, signed audit envelopes that can be consumed by downstream retention/compliance tooling. This PR introduces a new higher-level 'policy-orchestrator' service and several runtime integrations: 1) Temporal RBAC interpreter (supports TTL-based grants and revocation windows), 2) KMS evidence hasher (computes a deterministic hash of claim bundles and attaches KMS-wrapped attestations so audit stores can verify provenance without storing raw tokens), 3) Audit bridge sharding (splits signed audit envelopes by residency/geo policy and emits metadata for retention pipelines), and 4) Dry-run and canary rollouts for existing RBACv2 policies.

What changed (high-level): Added a new service package redwood/services/policy_orchestrator with a lightweight engine that compiles OPA-like templates into decision graphs; added an adapter layer (redwood/internal/kms_evidence) that produces HMAC-like deterministic evidence and integrates with CMK wrapping; added an audit bridge (redwood/observability/audit_bridge) that emits sharded, signed envelopes to audit-writer with residency tags. Also added CLI flags and Console toggles for canary/dry-run modes and a new policy schema v0.3.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc (Linear ENG-2281) reviewed
- [x] Unit tests for temporal matcher and decision cache
- [x] Integration tests exercising KMS wrapping (mocks) and audit bridge sampling
- [x] Console feature flags and telemetry
- [x] Backwards-compatible policy translation for existing RBACv2 rules (v0.2 -> v0.3)
- [x] Manual canary run in staging (region=eu-west-1)

Commits summary: 3 commits; commit titles included in the merge: 1) initial policy-orchestrator scaffold and schema v0.3 (adds core interpreter, API surface); 2) kms_evidence adapter with deterministic hashing and CMK wrap integration + unit tests; 3) audit_bridge, console flags, and migration helper for v0.2->v0.3 plus integration test harness.

Files touched (representative): redwood/services/policy_orchestrator/engine.go, redwood/services/policy_orchestrator/schema_v0_3.yaml, redwood/internal/kms_evidence/hasher.go, redwood/internal/kms_evidence/wrapper.go, redwood/observability/audit_bridge/bridge.go, redwood/console/flags/policy_canary.go, redwood/cli/policy_migrate.go, go.mod, Makefile (test targets), tests/integration/policy_orchestrator_test.go, ci/policy-orch-workflow.yaml, docs/policy-orchestrator.md.

Testing notes: CI workflow (ci/policy-orch-workflow.yaml) runs unit, lint, and integration tests. Integration tests use a KMS mock that simulates CMK wrap/unwrappings and asserts the envelope contains a valid KMS-wrapped nonce. One flaky test (TestAuditBridgeShardSampling) failed intermittently on the first run due to race in the sampling timer; addressed by adding a jitter buffer and a deterministic seeding step in the test harness. All CI checks passing now.

Backward compatibility and migration: The PR includes a migration helper redwood/cli/policy_migrate.go that translates existing v0.2 policy files to v0.3 by injecting temporal defaults (e.g., ttl: infinite -> ttl: 0) and preserving operator assertions. Migration runs in dry-run by default and emits a summary of transformed rules. We do not change persisted policy storage layout; the orchestrator accepts both v0.2 and v0.3 at runtime with a warning in the logs for v0.2 inputs.

Operational considerations: Canary rollout steps are documented in docs/policy-orchestrator.md. Because KMS wrapping introduces synchronous latency ( ~6-12ms per decision in our staging CMK mock), the orchestrator falls back to unsigned evidence in best-effort mode if KMS is unavailable and annotates the decision with a 'kms_provenance: fallback' tag. This behavior is gated behind 'require_kms_proof' tenant-level setting for regulated customers.

Security review summary: SEC-381 requested an additional integrity check for audit envelopes which we implemented by adding certificate pinning for the audit-writer endpoint and a HMAC of the envelope signed by a short-lived operator key (rotated by the orchestrator). Privacy team reviewed residency sharding logic to ensure no payloads cross geozone boundaries when tenant flags enforce residency.
Luis Ortega: Please add an admit hook that rejects policies with ttl > 30d unless flagged — otherwise operators can accidentally create long-lived grants.
Maya Chen (author): Added an admit hook in engine.go and unit tests to enforce TTL limits per tenant; left a tenant override flag 'allow_long_ttl' behind a security review gate.
Priya Natarajan: Can we make the KMS evidence payload deterministic across equivalent claim orders? Tests flaked in staging.
Maya Chen: The hasher now canonicalizes claim lists (sorted by key) before hashing — updated hasher.go and added tests to demonstrate determinism.
Ivan Petrov: Audit bridge sampling introduces a small window where events could be routed inconsistently across replicas. Add an ordering pin.
Maya Chen: Added monotonic sequence numbers per tenant in the envelope header and adjusted shard keying to include that sequence prefix (preserves ordering semantics).
Introduces Policy Orchestrator (v0.3 policy schema), temporal RBAC support, KMS evidence hashing and audit bridge sharding. Dry-run and canary modes included. Backwards compatible with v0.2 policies via migration helper. See docs/policy-orchestrator.md for rollout steps.
Canary rollout recommended per docs: enable for a single region and tenant cohort, monitor 'policy_orchestrator.decision_latency' and 'audit_bridge.envelope_failure_rate'. If KMS latency spikes, toggle 'require_kms_proof' to false for non-regulated tenants to avoid tail latency impact. Rollback is a config toggle; service restart not required.
Adds a new policy orchestrator to support temporal RBAC and KMS-backed evidence, plus an audit bridge that shards signed envelopes by residency. Includes migration tooling and canary rollout support. CI passed and PR merged via squash.

Motivation: Production rollouts increasingly require fine-grained checkpoints that pause promotion for human or automated validation while preserving deterministic replay and fast recovery. This PR introduces a Variant Orchestration Protocol (VOP) that adds adaptive holdpoints and an explainable rewind mechanism to the rollout runtime.

Summary: Implement VOP primitives, extend the rollout CRD with holdpoints/rewind_policy/priority_succession, add a snapshot-backed rewind store, and wire telemetry anchors into the decision loop.

Key goals: 1) allow staged canaries to pause automatically when a metric drift is detected, 2) enable deterministic rewind-to-checkpoint with an explainability trace for why a rewind was triggered, 3) support priority succession for traffic-lease handoff so higher-priority cohorts can reclaim traffic without full rollback.

Design highlights:
- Holdpoints: declarative objects attached to a rollout that define gating conditions (metric anchors, manual gates, smoke tests) and an adaptive timeout that grows/shrinks based on historical approval latency.
- Rewind store: lightweight snapshot format capturing request routing state, active KV cache pointers, and a compact trace of decisions (anchors evaluated and signal deltas). Snapshots are retained for the rewind window and garbage-collected by TTL.
- Explainable rewind: when the controller triggers a rewind, it emits an audit trace that links the snapshot id, the anchor conditions that failed, and a minimal repro traffic sample. The trace is surfaced in the Console with a summarized reason and a link to the snapshot replay job.
- Priority succession: when multiple cohorts request the same capacity, the scheduler honors an ordered succession list; if a higher-priority cohort needs traffic, lower-priority cohorts are gracefully drained to an earlier holdpoint instead of being fully rolled back.

Backwards compatibility: rollout CRD retains previous fields; new fields are optional. Existing rollout controllers will ignore VOP fields if not present.

Migration: a small adapter converts legacy pause/resume annotations into a single holdpoint when upgrading clusters.

Tests and validation:
- Unit tests for holdpoint evaluation logic (anchors + adaptive timeout heuristics)
- Integration tests: cluster-level canary that simulates p99 latency spike and verifies automatic holdpoint insertion + rewind emission
- E2E against canary harness: replay snapshot and validate decision trace reproduction
- Load test: ensure snapshot write/read does not add >2% latency to decision loop

Observability: new metrics (vop_holdpoint_evaluations_total, vop_rewinds_total, vop_snapshot_write_latency_seconds) and logs with structured fields for snapshot_id/anchor_set.

Console changes: Rollout timeline gains checkboxes for holdpoints, a snapshot viewer with a replay button, and an explainable-rewind card.

Rollout plan:
- Rollout to staging feature-flagged for beta tenants
- Monitor vop_rewinds_total and snapshot GC metrics for 2 weeks
- Gradual enable across Dedicated tenants with opt-in in Console

Checklist: [x] CRD schema bump (v1.8 -> v1.9) [x] Controller implementation [x] Snapshot store (S3/GCS) adapter with local fs fallback [x] Console UI hooks [x] Unit + integration + e2e tests [x] Docs and developer guide included

Reviewer Mateo: 'Implementation looks solid but we should limit snapshot retention defaults to 48h and make them editable per-tenant.' Author (Ava): 'Agreed, default set to 48h; added config via infra/helm values and Console override.' Reviewer Priya: 'Need clearer SLIs for rewind frequency; can we emit a tag with candidate model id?' Author: 'Added model_id tag to snapshot writes and vop_rewinds_total label.' Reviewer Luca: 'Prefer non-blocking snapshot writes for high-QPS controllers — verify backpressure.' Author: 'Switched to buffered async writer with bounded queue and backpressure metrics; added tests.' Final: all reviewers approved after two follow-up commits.
Initial CI run reported a flaky e2e (replay_snapshot_test) timeout; rerun of that job passed. Unit and integration suites passed on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 runners. Lint and typecheck green. Performance job showed +1.6% median decision-loop latency on staging; within target <=2%.
Add Variant Orchestration Protocol (VOP): adaptive holdpoints, explainable rewind snapshots, and priority succession for cohort traffic. Opt-in via feature flag; CRD v1.9 required for new fields. Backwards compatible when not enabled.

payload.body:
Context: We’ve seen invoice disputes and internal drift checks flag double-counted billed_tokens when the server performs a retry/fallback during streaming responses (e.g., upstream timeout mid-stream, router switches to a compatible model/region, or control plane triggers a hedged request). The customer sees one response stream, but we were emitting usage events for both the initial attempt and the retried attempt, and the ledger aggregation was summing both. This PR fixes the retry/fallback accounting path for streaming so that billed token meters reflect the final successful attempt only.

Root cause: In streaming mode, we incrementally populated a per-attempt UsageAccumulator and emitted a usage_event on stream termination for each attempt (including attempts that were superseded). When a retry/fallback occurred after partial chunks, the original attempt emitted a terminal usage_event with partial token counts; the retried attempt emitted its own terminal usage_event; downstream billing ledger summed both because both had unique event_ids and the aggregator did not have a stable “superseded by” key.

Fix (high level): (1) Introduce a stable request-scoped usage_dedupe_key derived from (account_id, api_key_id, idempotency_key||request_id, billing_period_day, meter_version). (2) Emit attempt-scoped usage events with attempt_seq and a new terminal_reason enum. (3) Update ledger aggregation to bill only the max attempt_seq per usage_dedupe_key where terminal_reason == SUCCESS, and to ignore attempts where terminal_reason in {SUPERSEDED, RETRY_ABORTED}. (4) For the streaming handler, ensure we mark the prior attempt as SUPERSEDED before starting the retry path, and we do not emit a SUCCESS terminal event for any attempt that did not complete.

Details:
- New fields on usage events:
  - usage_dedupe_key: stable across retries/fallbacks for the logical request
  - attempt_seq: monotonic int starting at 0
  - terminal_reason: SUCCESS | ERROR | SUPERSEDED | RETRY_ABORTED | CLIENT_DISCONNECT
  - superseded_by_attempt_seq: populated on SUPERSEDED events
- Streaming retry semantics: When router triggers retry/fallback after partial streaming, we immediately close the old accumulator with terminal_reason=SUPERSEDED (not SUCCESS) and start a new accumulator for attempt_seq+1. Only the attempt that reaches stream completion and returns a final usage summary is eligible for billing.
- Metrics/observability: Added counters for retry_double_count_prevented_total and usage_events_superseded_total, plus a gauge for per-route superseded rate to help tune alerting. Added structured log fields for usage_dedupe_key and attempt_seq in the streaming gateway.

Tests:
- Unit tests in metering: simulate (a) stream completes without retry; (b) retry after N chunks; (c) fallback to different model mid-stream; (d) client disconnect then server retry does not run; verify billed tokens count equals final successful attempt only and that superseded attempts are excluded.
- Integration test: added a harness that forces an upstream timeout on first attempt and verifies the exported usage API returns a single billed record for the request (with billed_tokens matching the final attempt).
- Regression: added a fixture for OpenAI-compatible streaming endpoint where retries previously double-counted due to different request_id normalization.

Rollout notes:
- This change is behind feature flag billing.metering_stream_retry_dedupe_v1 (default off). Plan: enable in staging for 48h, then canary 5% of hosted traffic (US-East + two high-volume accounts), then ramp to 50% and 100% if drift checks remain within thresholds.
- Shadow-billing: for the canary phase, ledger will compute both old and new billable usage in parallel (annotated in the recon export) to quantify deltas; Finance/RevRec sign-off required before 100% rollout.
- Backfill: no backfill in this PR. If shadow-billing indicates material historical impact, we’ll follow the RevRec playbook for corrective credits rather than retroactive invoice edits.

Customer impact: Fixes an overbilling bug in specific streaming retry/fallback scenarios (primarily server-side retries). In most cases, customers should see billed token counts decrease slightly for affected days; usage API exports will show clearer attempt attribution fields once the related API surface PR lands.

Checklist:
- [x] Added unit coverage for streaming retry + fallback paths
- [x] Added integration coverage for forced retry in staging
- [x] Added metrics + logs for superseded attempts
- [x] Rollout plan documented + flag added
- [x] Linked to support escalation SUP-28463 and Linear ENG-4430

Notes for reviewers: Please focus on (a) dedupe key stability across OpenAI-compatible endpoints, (b) ensuring we never bill SUPERSEDED attempts, and (c) any edge cases where SUCCESS could be emitted after partial stream termination.
Logan Wright (review): The dedupe_key derivation uses request_id for non-idempotent requests — do we normalize OpenAI-compat request IDs the same way as native endpoints? Author (Cole): Good catch. I added normalization to strip the gateway-generated suffix and included a regression test for /v1/chat/completions streaming. Nadia Rahman (review): Can we guarantee terminal_reason cannot be SUCCESS for the superseded attempt if the client disconnects? Also please document semantics of CLIENT_DISCONNECT vs SUPERSEDED. Author: Updated the state machine so SUCCESS is only emitted from the finalization path that sees a completed stream; client disconnect now emits CLIENT_DISCONNECT and short-circuits retries. Added inline docs and tests. Aisha Bello (review): Please add a metric we can alert on for high superseded rates per route/model; also add log fields so SRE can join events. Author: Added usage_events_superseded_total with route+model labels (bounded), and structured log fields usage_dedupe_key/attempt_seq. Connor O'Brien (review): Rollout plan needs an explicit canary and revert procedure. Author: Expanded rollout section with percentages, regions, and revert steps (flag off, keep shadow-billing for 24h). Monica Patel (review): Ensure SDK retries using idempotency_key don’t change dedupe semantics. Author: Dedupe prefers idempotency_key when present; added a test that simulates client retry with same idempotency key and confirms single billable attempt. Final: Approved after changes; merged squash.
Fixes a bug where streaming retries/fallbacks could double-count billed tokens by ensuring only the final successful attempt is billable; adds retry attempt attribution fields and regression coverage; rolled out behind feature flag billing.metering_stream_retry_dedupe_v1 with shadow-billing support.

payload.body:
Summary: Adds a new "fragmentation index" metric and associated labels to the invocation telemetry pipeline, plus a Grafana cost-cohort grid and alert rule to surface sparse/high-cost invocation cohorts. Motivation: customers and SREs have been seeing a small number of invocations that account for disproportionate per-token cost due to model switching, repeated short-lived KV cache misses, and micro-batching fragmentation. Existing token-level cost traces show the symptom but not the cohort structure; this PR makes the cause visible and actionable.

What this changes (single continuous description):
- Telemetry: introduce invocation.fragmentation.index (float, 0..1) that summarizes the ratio of unique model-step fragments to effective tokens served. Higher values indicate higher fragmentation (more context switches/short bursts). Also instrument invocation.fragmentation.reason label with values: "microbatch", "model-switch", "kv-miss", "prefetch-miss", "other".
- Aggregation: add a cost_cohort_id label derived from (tenant_id, route, model_variant, prompt_shape_bucket) to group invocations by stable cost characteristics. This enables cohort-level rollups without high cardinality explosion.
- Pipeline: update the telemetry pipeline transform (telemetry/ingest/transformations/fragmentation.py) to compute the index from spans + token counts and emit compact rollups for 1m and 1h windows.
- Dashboard: new Grafana dashboard panel (dashboards/observability/cost_cohort_grid.json) that draws a 2D heat-grid: x-axis fragmentation-index buckets, y-axis median per-token cost; color = invocation volume. Rows can be filtered by model and route.
- Alerts: add alert rule (monitoring/alerts/cost_cohort_sparse_highcost.yaml) that triggers when a cohort with fragmentation-index > 0.6 has median per-token cost > 3x baseline and 95th-percentile latency > 2000ms for 5m. Alert includes a runbook link and an automated sampler job to capture a synthetic replay.

Summary: Adds a compact presubmit prober workflow plus a lightweight dependency-curation action that labels low-risk dependency bumps for the fastpath CI lane. Motivation: full CI runs are expensive and slow feedback on busy weekdays increases engineering cycle time. The presubmit prober provides a <30s healthcheck early in the pipeline; the dep-curator reduces noise by auto-classifying routine dependency bumps and allowing them to take a trimmed CI path. This PR implements the mechanism and the operational controls (opt-in label, denylist, and safety gate). --- Changes and intent: 1) .github/workflows/presubmit-prober.yml - new workflow that runs on PRs and executes a minimal matrix of fast health checks (lint-lite, small unit smoke, config-validator). It runs within seconds by using cached tool images and a dedicated fast runner. 2) .github/actions/dep-curator/action.yml - repository action that inspects dependency-related PRs (renovate/depbot) and applies the "ci/fastpath-eligible" label when bump passes heuristics (patch/minor semver, no native code/binary deps, test-only transitive changes). 3) scripts/prober/health_check.py - prober script that exercises crucial startup paths: model routing schema validation, minimal API contract smoke against mocked runtime, and config validator. 4) ci/fastpath-evaluator.py - small evaluator used by the curator to double-check changed files & run quick offline heuristics. 5) docs/ci/fastpath.md - operational guide describing how to opt-in/out, denylist edits, and how to troubleshoot prober failures. 6) .github/workflows/integration.yml - small refactor to add a gate that skips heavy integration shards when "ci/fastpath-eligible" label is present. --- Commits: - c1a2f6d: add presubmit prober workflow and prober script - e3b9a12: add dependency curator action and evaluator - f5d8b44: docs and CI gate wiring; comments and tests for edge cases --- Files changed (high level): - .github/workflows/presubmit-prober.yml (new) - .github/actions/dep-curator/action.yml (new) - scripts/prober/health_check.py (new, +120 lines) - ci/fastpath-evaluator.py (new, +80 lines) - docs/ci/fastpath.md (new) - .github/workflows/integration.yml (modified, ~30-line tweak) - .github/labels/ci.yml (updated denylist) --- Test matrix and CI: First run showed a lint error in health_check.py (flake8 E302) which was fixed in c1a2f6d::fix-lint. Unit smoke tests and a fast integration shard were added to the prober matrix. Final CI status: all checks passed (lint, unit-fast, prober-smoke, e2e-lite). The heavy integration shards are gated and did not run for the dep-curator candidate PRs once the fastpath label was applied. --- Review thread (high level): - Arjun Patel (review): "Nice idea. Please add metrics for prober false positives/negatives and a TTL for fastpath labels so we don't accidentally allow stale labels." - Maya Chen (author): "Added metrics.emit('ci.prober.result', ...) in c1a2f6d and added 7-day TTL enforcement in ci/fastpath-evaluator.py; updated docs." - Elena Alvarez (review): "Safety concern: what about deps that touch native bindings? Please add a denylist and explicit override for that class." - Maya Chen: "Added denylist and explicit override requiring manual review for files matching /native/ or glibc-binding patterns; documented it in docs/ci/fastpath.md." - Samir Gupta (approval): "Verified local runs of prober and curator; okay to squash-merge after fixing the small lint issues." --- Operational notes and rollout plan: - Feature flags: presubmit-prober is enabled by default for all PRs but the curator only labels PRs originating from renovate/depbot or with a title matching dependency bump heuristics. - Opt-out: maintainers can set label ci/fastpath-exempt to force full CI. - Monitoring: added CI metrics (ci.prober.latency, ci.prober.pass_rate, ci.fastpath.label_count) to the console dashboard; alert if prober pass_rate drops below 98% for a 1-hour window. - Safety: the curator rejects any PR touching files in the denylist (infra/native-build, third_party/binaries) and will not label those PRs. A manual review is required. - Rollout: rolled to canary org members for 24hrs, then rolled to all repos on the org-wide workflow runner. --- Rationale vs alternatives considered: - Could have used a heavier classifier or ML model for dep risk scoring; rejected due to operational complexity and inversion of the fast feedback loop. - Could have broadened the prober to run a subset of integration tests, but that increased runtime; we prioritized sub-30s execution. --- Merge and post-merge work: - Merge method: squash and merge. - Post-merge: monitoring dashboard tile added; follow-up tasks created ENG-2189 to expand denylist and ENG-2190 to add historical metrics backfill. --- Impact and risk assessment: - Expected: 25-40% reduction in full CI runs for dependency-only PRs, median PR feedback time down from ~12m to ~90s for fastpath-eligible cases. - Risk: misclassification of risky dependency bumps. Mitigation: conservative heuristics, denylist, TTL on labels, and dashboards/alerts. --- Manual steps performed during merge: - Verified canary runner logs, validated that curator did not label a known native-binding bump in canary. - Notified SRE and platform channels. --- Notes for maintainers: - To adjust sensitivity thresholds edit ci/fastpath-evaluator.py constant RISK_SCORE_CUTOFF. - If a repository prefers to disable the curator, remove the .github/actions/dep-curator binding in that repo's workflow. --- Related: ENG-2145 (fastpath design), ENG-2201 (CI cost reduction OKR), SUP-3421 (customer incident that motivated faster feedback). --- This PR is intentionally lightweight in code and conservative in policy; follow-ups will expand the heuristics and add an optional ML-based scorer behind a feature flag.
Adds a lightweight presubmit prober for fast sanity checks and a minimal dependency curator to mark low-risk bumps eligible for fastpath CI. No runtime API changes.

Motivation: teams running multi-variant A/B experiments and policy-driven canaries currently stitch together routing, rollouts, and replay logic across multiple controllers. This PR introduces 'Experiment Runway', a first-class orchestrator that sequences multi-variant experiments (A/B/n), supports weighted shadow traffic, session-affine variant routing, and a rehearsal-based rollback rehearsal step that validates rollback paths before exposing them to production traffic. Goals: (1) provide deterministic, auditable experiment lifecycles that reduce human error during variant swaps, (2) enable automatic rollback rehearsals to uncover failures in teardown/restore steps, (3) preserve session affinity for long-lived user sessions, preventing user experience drift when experiments change mid-session, and (4) surface clear telemetry and failure modes to Redwood Console. Summary of changes: Adds a new controller (experiment-runway) and a lightweight runtime adapter for multi-variant traffic shaping. Introduces a new Experiment CRD schema, per-variant safety gates (latency/error/regression thresholds), a rehearsal pipeline that runs teardown/rollback operations in a sandboxed shadow plane, and session-affinity cookies/token hashing integration. Includes e2e harness and smoke tests, console dashboard wiring, and Linear/Jira links to incident reproduction steps. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime.feature.experiment_runway. We will ship in two stages: Stage 1 enable only in staging for internal experiments and run canary on Redwood-owned traffic; Stage 2 enable by opt-in in Dedicated customers after release notes and migration guide. Backwards compatibility: existing canary and shadow controllers are untouched; Experiment Runway is opt-in and can co-exist. See release_notes for migration guidance. Related work: builds on ENG-1304 (cohort fencing) and reuses metric-gates from ENG-1248.
Jonah Kim: Nice direction. Two quick asks: (1) can you document the invariants the rehearsal runner promises? I worry about partial teardown leaving user sessions in a bad state, (2) please add a unit test for the hashing sticky cache eviction policy.
Maya Patel (author): Added an explicit invariants section in rehearsal_runner.go and added the sticky cache eviction unit test; see commits f2d88b2 and d44c1b0. The rehearsal runner will run teardown in a sandbox and only flip a 'rollback-ready' flag after snapshot verification succeeds to guard against partial-tear situations.
Priya Rao: The Experiment CRD validation looks good. Please ensure the UI does not expose weighted variants >100 without normalization. Also we need explicit metrics for rehearsal outcomes (success/failure/timeout).
Maya Patel: Normalization check added to CRD webhook and rehearsal metrics exported (observability/metrics added).
Evan Schultz: CI flaky on the e2e cluster repro — saw a timeout on roundtrip when the rehearsal sandboxpod scheduling was constrained. Could we add a scheduler priority class or a local fallback?
Maya Patel: Added scheduler priority class for rehearsal pods and a local fallback to run rehearsal as a lightweight in-proc replay when scheduling fails (see commit e12f7a6).
Introduce Experiment Runway (opt-in): orchestrator for multi-variant A/B tests with weighted shadowing, session-affine routing, and rehearsal-enabled rollback validation. Opt-in behind runtime.feature.experiment_runway. Migration guide in docs/migration/experiment-runway-migration.md.

Motivation: Dedicated fleets currently make autoscaling decisions based on instantaneous utilization and simple thresholds which are noisy during traffic spikes. We need a proactive path that (1) aggregates tenant-level committed capacity signals into a stable time-windowed view, and (2) uses a latency-targeted predictive autoscaler to warm capacity before p99 latency SLOs are breached. This PR introduces two related components: a Commitment Telemetry Aggregator and a Latency-Targeted Autoscaler. Design: - Commitment Telemetry Aggregator: collects per-tenant and per-pool committed capacity (reserved slots, reservation-window metadata, recent commit events) and computes rolling statistics: EWMA of committed tokens (configurable half-life), windowed percentile sketches (P50/P95) and a decayed headroom estimate. Outputs are exposed as metrics: redwood.commitment.window_ewma, redwood.commitment.p95, redwood.commitment.headroom_estimate and an on-disk snapshot for operator diagnostics. Aggregator is implemented as an in-process agent within the dedicated-controller with a lightweight persistence layer to avoid traffic loss during short controller restarts. - Latency-Targeted Autoscaler: consumes aggregated commitment telemetry + online latency curves (occupancy -> latency percentiles) to synthesize predictive scale decisions. The autoscaler runs a short-horizon Monte Carlo forecast (default 30s lookahead) using sampled arrival rates and the commitment window to produce a suggested delta of GPU slots. Key safety knobs: damping_factor (0..1) to avoid oscillation, proactive_warmup_budget capped per-tenant, and a cooldown window after every scale event. It prefers warm-pool borrow when available and falls back to ephemeral provisioning. Implementation notes and rollout plan: - New feature gate: PredictiveLatencyAutoscale (off by default). - Configurable defaults are added to helm values under dedicated.autoscaler.predictive.* - Canary rollout: 10% of pools by label (team=canary) for 48h, track p99 latency, scale churn, and cost delta. - Observability: dashboards added (observability/dashboards/commitment-oversight.json) and new traces for predictive decisions. - Backwards compatibility: aggregator exposes telemetry but leaves existing reactive autoscaler unchanged until gate enabled. Two concerns: 1) oscillation risk during correlated burst traffic, 2) accounting correctness when tenants have overlapping reservations.'", "Author (Maya): 'Added a damping_factor to the decision path and a 60s cooldown by default. For overlapping reservations we collapse by tenant id and compute committed tokens deduplicated by reservation hash; see commitment_aggregator.go line 148.'", "Priya: 'How do we ensure we don't starve the shared warm pool for small tenants?']", "Author: 'We introduced proactive_warmup_budget that is a per-tenant soft floor; the allocator pays from warm pool only if budget remains. Also added a fallback to ephemeral provisioning if warm pool < X percent'", "Liam: 'Please add a pressure test for long tail failure modes (controller flapping).', "Author: 'Added integration scenario with controller flapping and asserted no more than 1 scale-op per 2m in steady state. See integration/tests/e2e/predictive_scaling_scenarios.go'", "Diego (approved): 'Approach looks sound, leave in canary for 48h then promote if metrics stable.'", "SRE bot: 'CI flaky test recorded. Re-run requested.'", "CI (rerun): 'All checks passed after re-run.'"] CI checks and timeline: ["Initial CI (linux/unit): fail - TestPredictiveForecastRace (flake in stats aggregator)", "Triggered rerun after small locking fix in snapshots.go", "Rerun CI: pass", "Integration bench: pass (predictive_model_bench within cost budget)", "E2E (simulated): pass - no controller flapping detected under test harness"] Merge outcome: "merged via squash and merge. Rollout plan appended to docs and release notes. Canary label applied to 10% pools; operators notified in #dedicated-ops." Provides rolling commitment metrics and a predictive scaling path to keep p99 latency within configured targets. Disabled by default; see docs/ops/proactive-scaling.md for rollout guidance." Motivation: Our single global lint/test matrix is driving long presubmit feedback and noisy failures for unrelated teams. Several services still rely on legacy Makefile targets that bootstrap heavy toolchains in CI which inflates setup times and flakiness. This PR aims to: 1) decentralize lint configuration into explicit per-team profiles under .ci/lint-profiles.yaml so teams can opt-in to stricter or lenient rules without touching global CI; 2) add a lightweight compatibility shim that executes legacy Makefile test targets inside a hermetic container (tools/ci-runner/compat_shim) to avoid duplicating global bootstrap steps; 3) introduce a fastpath presubmit lane that only runs surface-level checks (format, basic typecheck, unit smoke) and pushes full lint/type/integration to a staged presubmit or nightly job; 4) bump a few dev dependencies (eslint -> 9.17.0, typescript -> 5.4.x) and add an automated lockfile-regeneration check on release branches to prevent drift. The description below summarizes the changes, rationale, and rollout plan.

Design details: The new .ci/lint-profiles.yaml maps repo paths (or teams) to a named profile. CI templates pick the profile based on changed files and set environment variables for the lint runner. Profiles are small YAML blobs (ruleset, allowed-errors, skip-patterns). The compatibility shim wraps make targets in a containerized environment and exposes a minimal contract (exit codes, artifact dir) so existing Makefiles require zero changes. The fastpath lane is opt-in per repo via the same profile file.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main with feature flagged fastpath=false cluster-wide. 2) Enable per-team profiles for a small set of repos (redwood-serving, redwood-sdk-python, redwood-docs) for two weeks. 3) Flip fastpath=true for low-risk repos, monitor premerge times and flaky counts via CI telemetry. 4) Gradually onboard teams and clean up obsolete Makefile bootstraps.

Risks & mitigations: eslint/TS bumps could surface new warnings. We included a codemod script (tools/ci-scripts/eslint-codemods/convert-opts.js) and a temporary suppressions whitelist per-profile. The shim increases hermeticity but adds an extra binary (docker-wrapper); we added health checks and retry logic.

Checklist: - [x] Add .ci/lint-profiles.yaml and loader in CI templates - [x] Implement compat shim (Go) and unit tests - [x] Fastpath lane template + telemetry hooks - [x] Devdep bump + codemod + lockfile check - [x] Docs in docs/ci/team-lint-profiles.md

Related: ENG-2145 (reduce CI presubmit time), ENG-2212 (legacy-service-onboarding), SUP-4321 (customer incident flagged flaky presubmit)
Lucas Chen: Can we avoid bumping ESLint and TS in the same PR? If codemods are non-trivial they might delay rollout.
Maya Patel: Agree, I split codemod run into opt-in step and included suppressions; the bump is required to use new rule sets in strict profiles. Happy to split if reviewers prefer.
Nora Alvarez: compat_shim looks good but please add timeout guards and a cleanup handler for ephemeral containers.
Maya Patel: Added timeout + cleanup in adapter.go and unit test.
Devon Brooks: Fastpath lane metrics look useful — can we add a histogram of presubmit latency buckets?
Maya Patel: Added telemetry hook to emit latency buckets; will wire dashboards in a follow-up.
Lucas Chen (approve): Approving with the caveat we'll monitor eslint rule churn closely and may cut a hotfix if regressions appear.
- Add per-team lint profiles (.ci/lint-profiles.yaml) allowing targeted rule sets and opt-in fastpath presubmit lanes. - Add a hermetic compat shim to run legacy Makefile targets in CI without global bootstrap. - Introduce presubmit fastpath lane to reduce noise and speed feedback. - Bump dev dependencies (eslint 9.x, typescript 5.4); include codemod and temporary suppressions. - Add lockfile-regeneration check for release branches.

Context and motivation: During recent incidents and customer reports, we observed inconsistent Retry-After semantics across the OpenAI-compat adapter and the direct Redwood API: some callers saw coarse second-level Retry-After headers while streamed tool callers received only opaque 429 bodies. This caused client-side backoff thrashing and made it hard to correlate idempotency collisions in telemetry. This PR standardizes the surface contract and adds observability to make post-incident analysis straightforward.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Standardizes Retry-After exposure, surfaces idempotency resolution state via headers, normalizes machine-readable error envelopes for 429/503 with a backoff_hint token, and emits new metrics for idempotency collisions and retry-window histograms. Also updates SDK shims and documentation to match the new contract.

Checklist: 
- [x] Define and implement X-Redwood-Retry-After header (RFC-3339 delta and millisecond token forms)
- [x] Add X-Redwood-Idempotency-Status header (values: accepted|replayed|collision|broken)
- [x] Extend 429/503 error_envelope to include backoff_hint and idempotency_state fields (machine-readable JSON)
- [x] Emit telemetry: idempotency_collision_count, idempotency_resolution_latency_ms histogram, retry_window_seconds histogram
- [x] Update OpenAI-compat shim to forward new headers for compatibility mode
- [x] Update Python and TypeScript SDK helpers with higher-level retry/backoff wrappers that read the new headers
- [x] Add integration tests covering streaming tool replays and idempotency collision attribution
- [x] Update docs for API surface and migration notes

Commits (high level):
- f8c11d3  Implement X-Redwood-Retry-After header format and parsing in gateway
- a4b9e20  Normalize error_envelope for 429/503 and add backoff_hint tokens
- 3d2f7b1  Add idempotency session manager metrics and collision handling hooks
- b7f2aa8  SDK: python/ts helpers to respect server backoff_hint and idempotency status
- 5c4e9f0  Tests + docs: integration test and docs page for migration and examples

Files changed (high level):
- services/gateway/src/handlers/retry_policy.rs: adds parsing logic for both numeric Retry-After and opaque backoff tokens and chooses which to emit based on client capability header. Small code snippet added to pick RFC delta or server-token form.
- services/streaming/src/idempotency/session_manager.rs: record resolution outcomes and expose state transitions (accepted -> replayed -> collision). Adds a lightweight in-memory histogram for resolution latencies.
- services/streaming/src/protocol/error_envelope.rs: change error envelope shape to { code, message, backoff_hint?, idempotency_state? } and add helpers for Marshaler/Unmarshaler.
- console/docs/api/retry_and_idempotency.md: new doc covering header semantics, SDK migration snippets, and example client behavior for streams and function calls.
- sdk updates: helpers in Python and TS that read X-Redwood-Retry-After and X-Redwood-Idempotency-Status, and expose a RetryPolicy object for callers to integrate with their event loops.

Review conversation summary: 
- Priya Kapoor: "Thanks — the telemetry additions look good. Two requests: make the backoff_hint token expire (we do) and ensure the SDK helpers provide a non-blocking async sleep path for streaming clients."
- Author (Ethan): "Added TTL to backoff tokens and switched the Python helper to an asyncio-friendly sleep that drains without blocking the event loop. See commit b7f2aa8."
- Liam Chen: "Please confirm we won't break existing clients that only parse numeric Retry-After. Suggest emitting both X-Redwood-Retry-After (RFC delta in seconds) and X-Redwood-Retry-Token when available."
- Author: "Gateway now emits both when the backoff_hint is present: RFC delta for basic clients and Retry-Token for advanced clients; documentation updated with examples."
- Sofia Martinez (approval): "Test coverage is solid and docs are clear. Approving after minor nits fixed in code comments."

CI and rollout notes: 
- CI: full test matrix passed (unit, integration, lint). E2E flaky in first run due to timing assumptions; fixed by making test tolerances explicit.
- Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag 'feature.api.backoff_v2' and will be enabled by gradual canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) to observe idempotency_collision_count before wide release.

Compatibility and migration: 
- Backward compatible: existing clients that read numeric Retry-After will continue to get a numeric delta when a server-side estimate is available. For stream/tool callers, clients that understand Retry-Token will be able to correlate server-side idempotency sessions and avoid duplicate tool execution.
- Telemetry: New Prometheus metrics added; Grafana dashboard provisioning file included so SRE can watch idempotency collisions and retry-window percentiles during canary.

Why this is different from prior work: previous PRs adjusted Retry-After formats or stream framing, but did not pair the header-level contract with explicit idempotency-state telemetry or emit a machine-readable backoff token that can be used by streaming clients to deterministically defer replays. This PR ties the contract to observability so we can quantify improvements in client behavior post-release.

Follow-ups: 
- Export backoff_hint correlation id to traces for end-to-end debugging (ENG-4910).
- Consider adding a server-side advisory for recommended jitter windows based on load profiles (ENG-4932).

Merge: Squash merge after approvals and CI green.

Testing notes: Integration test spins up a small streaming harness that simulates duplicate tool invocations and asserts that idempotency_state transitions to 'replayed' for the second attempt, and that idempotency_collision_count increments exactly once when true conflicts occur.

Contact: For migration questions, ping @ethan.brooks or open ENG-4872 in Linear.
Clarify and standardize Retry-After semantics and idempotency telemetry. Introduces X-Redwood-Retry-After and X-Redwood-Idempotency-Status headers, normalizes 429/503 error envelope to include machine-readable backoff_hint and idempotency_state, and exposes new Prometheus meters for idempotency collisions and retry-window distribution.

Adds a new attestation-anchor based RBAC v2 rejector and a lightweight KMS residency verifier used by policy decision flow and audit pipelines. Motivation: customers with strict data residency requirements reported edge cases where operator tokens or downstream KMS calls carried ambiguous region claims and audits could not reliably correlate key usage to tenant residency. This PR implements 1) attestation-anchor: an optional decision gate that verifies a signed attestation blob from upstream operator-token issuers and rejects requests when attestation does not match the tenant's pinned residency profile, 2) kms-residency-verifier: a synchronous verifier that checks KMS key metadata and remote-region provenance headers before allowing encryption/decryption calls, 3) audit-consistency-probe: a low-overhead verifier that writes a signed audit proof event when KMS residency differs from the request's claimed region to help downstream forensics, 4) config/rollout flags and feature gates for staged canary enabling and backwards-compatible fallback to previous behavior. Included migration steps, a Linear task list, and a short CLI tool to regressively validate tenant residency mappings. This is implemented behind an opt-in feature gate 'attestation_anchor_v1' and a service config flag 'kms_residency_enforce' that can be toggled per environment. Backwards compatibility: when both flags are false the runtime path is unchanged. Testing and verification: unit tests for attestation parsing and policy rule matching, integration tests with a fake KMS metadata service, e2e smoke tests that assert audit proof emission, and load-tested guarded path to ensure <5% median p50 latency regression under synthetic workloads. Rollout plan: enable in internal infra, dark-launch to 5% traffic, then 25% across regions with cross-checking turned on, then full enable after two days of stable telemetry. Related work: references ENG-4928 for long-term RBAC stability, SUP-1123 for customer support ticket, and SEC-317 design doc. Documentation: includes a new doc on operator attestation format and admin guide for tuning residency heuristics.
Priya Menon: Can we make the attestation signature verification pluggable so enterprise teams can bring their own verifier?
Luis Ortega: The residency verifier hits KMS metadata in the hot path; we should ensure it does not stall downstream RPCs. Can we cache negative results with TTL?
Daniel Kim: Minor nit: prefer explicit error enums for audit probe failures so SLO diagnostics can group them, not string matches.
Aisha Reddy: Approve pending a migration note explaining the operator token backwards compatibility and an admin flag to disable audit proof emission for PII-sensitive tenants.
Hannah Park: Pluggable verifier added via an interface and default implementation kept in this PR; docs updated with extension points.
Hannah Park: Added an in-memory negative cache with a 2m TTL and metrics for miss/evict counts. Also added a fallback fast-path that skips verifier when 'kms_residency_enforce' is false.
Hannah Park: Replaced string error paths with typed error codes and added mapping to telemetry fields.
Hannah Park: Added migration note and admin flag 'audit_proof_emit' to disable proof emission for selected tenants; updated policy and docs.
Introduce optional attestation-anchor RBAC gate and KMS residency verifier to strengthen tenant data residency enforcement. Feature is behind feature flags and disabled by default. Admins can enable audit proof emission to improve residency forensics.
When enabling in production turn on 'attestation_anchor_v1' in feature flags and incrementally enable 'kms_residency_enforce' via canary config. Monitor metric authz.attestation.reject_rate and audit.proof.emitted_count. If latency regressions exceed 10% consider increasing negative cache TTL or disabling enforcement temporarily.
Unit tests cover attestation parsing and verifier mocks. Integration test suite simulates KMS metadata responses and validates audit proof events. Load tests on perf canary show median p50 4% regression on canary machines with 500 concurrent requests, within target.

payload.body:
Motivation: The paged KV blockpool in hot workloads showed increasing fragmentation over long uptimes, causing uneven allocation latency and occasional batching stalls when contiguous runs were required for large KV pages. This PR adds a low-risk background coalescer/compactor that merges adjacent free pageframes asynchronously and introduces an explicit eviction-signalling path so the scheduler can preemptively prepare replacement pages before a high-latency allocation path is taken.

What this change does (high-level): Adds a pageframe coalescer thread that: 1) scans the free list priority buckets at low frequency, 2) attempts lock-free coalescing of adjacent free blocks, 3) posts compaction intents that are executed opportunistically by existing reclamation workers. Adds an eviction_signal API from the allocator to the scheduler which: 1) emits lightweight hints when a contiguous allocation cannot be satisfied quickly, 2) lets the scheduler trigger prefetch/reservation windows and adjust batching windows to avoid head-of-line stalls. Integrates coalescer with continuous batching heuristics so batching durations are shortened when eviction signals indicate imminent fragmentation pressure.

Implementation notes: - New modules: allocator/coalescer.{h,cc}, allocator/eviction_signal.{h,cc} - Modified allocator-free-list to expose physical adjacency checks and to return soft-reservation tokens for in-progress compactions instead of stealing blocks. - Reclamation workers accept compaction intents and will perform O(1)-amortized merges using a bitmap-assisted scan to avoid full list traversal. - Scheduler hooks: scheduler/placement.cpp checks eviction_signal before expanding batch windows; if signalled, it proactively reserves a small pool of pageframes and triggers prefetch. - Added metrics: allocator.coalescer.scans, allocator.coalescer.coalesce_success, allocator.eviction_signal.count, scheduler.prefetch_triggers. - Config knobs: coalescer.scan_interval_ms (default 5000), coalescer.cpu_budget_ms_per_scan (default 2), eviction_signal.prefetch_reserve (default 8 pages).

Benchmarks and effects: Microbench (mix of small random gets + occasional 8-page writes, 90/10 read/write): - Steady-state p50 token generation latency: -7% on average when fragmentation > 45% compared to baseline. - p95 improved by 12% during long-run tests where fragmentation would otherwise grow. - Memory fragmentation (measured as non-contiguous free runs fraction) reduced from ~48% to ~18% after a 6-hour mixed workload run. - End-to-end continuous-batching throughput increased ~4% on median and tail improved due to fewer batch stalls. System-level CPU overhead for coalescer measured at ~0.6% of a single core under default settings.

Compatibility and rollout: Backwards compatible with existing allocator snapshots. The coalescer is disabled by default for Dedicated customers with strict determinism requirements; can be flagged on via runtime config. Default for hosted runs is enabled. We ship metrics so SRE can observe coalescer activity before toggling for large fleets. No on-disk format changes.

Testing: - Unit tests for adjacency detection and compaction intents. - Integration tests: long-run fragmentation regression harness added (tests/allocator/frag_regress_test.cc) which runs a 200k-op workload and asserts fragmentation < 25%. - E2E CI job added to the perf-canary suite verifying p95 under the mixed workload. - Manual soak on staging for 72h with continuous traffic; observed stable memory usage and improved latency tails.

Risk and mitigations: Potential for extra contention if coalescer is misconfigured. Mitigations: very small default CPU budget, bitmap-assisted O(1) scans, soft-reservation tokens to avoid block stealing during compaction. Feature is toggleable via runtime flag and can be rolled back server-side without data migration.

Migration notes for operators: - To opt-in, set allocator.coalescer.enabled=true in runtime config or via Console toggle. - To monitor impact: watch the new metrics allocator.coalescer.coalesce_success (should trend positive) and allocator.eviction_signal.count (should be low during steady state). - If p95 worsens after enabling, lower coalescer.cpu_budget_ms_per_scan or increase scan_interval_ms.

Related work: This addresses recurring production incidents where long lived fragmentation interacts badly with bursty large writes (see ENG-3245). Complements earlier softpin and reservation changes (previous PRs) by giving an async path to reduce fragmentation rather than only reactive pinning.

Notes on design alternatives considered: - Aggressive in-line compaction at allocation-time rejected due to latency impact. - Fully lockless global compaction was overly complex; hybrid opportunistic compaction using reclamation workers provides good tradeoff between complexity and effectiveness.

Summary: Low-risk background coalescer + eviction signalling reduces fragmentation and tail latency with tiny CPU cost and an opt-in switch for environments that need deterministic behaviour.
Introduce a background pageframe coalescer and eviction signal path that reduces fragmentation and improves steady-state latency under mixed workloads. No API changes.
Diego Ramos: Great idea, Aisha. A few nitpicks around the bitmap scan - prefer clear comments about concurrency model and ABA assumptions.
Aisha Patel: Addressed in allocator/free_list.cc and added comments to coalescer about epoch guarantees. PTAL.
Mei Lin: Can we add a stress test that toggles the coalescer on/off during a run? Observed a small spike in one of the staging runs.
Aisha Patel: Added toggling stress test in frag_regress_test and pushed perf tweak to lower default cpu_budget_ms_per_scan. Staging soak re-run looks stable.
Connor O'Neill: Approving pending a tiny doc clarification on operator flags.

Motivation:
Streaming constrained decoding (CFG / regex backends) has repeatedly hit edge-cases when token boundaries split grammar tokens or regex groups across byte/utf boundaries. These issues manifested as: truncated JSON outputs during streaming, invalid function-calling payloads when tool arguments contained emoji or non-BMP characters, and mismatches between the OpenAI-compat layer's incremental transcript and the runtime's internal tokenization state.

This PR implements a tokenizer-aware regex/grammar constrained-decoding backend that: 1) tracks token boundary alignment between the tokenizer and the constrained automaton, 2) defers constraint acceptance until a full tokenizer-aligned unit is available (so streaming partial tokens don't prematurely satisfy regex groups), and 3) exposes a deterministic fallback policy for cases where a constraint would otherwise block progress (configurable to emit escape tokens, apply best-effort repair, or route to a fallback model variant).

What changed (high level):
- Add TokenBoundaryAdapter: a small shim that normalizes tokenizer tokenization events (including multi-codepoint grapheme clusters, surrogate pairs, and byte-encoded tokens) into canonical "token spans" used by constrained backends.
- Regex backend update: convert the streaming regex matcher to operate on token-span sequences rather than raw bytes/characters. This prevents false-positive group matches when a regex group crosses a tokenizer split.
- CFG backend adjustment: similar token-aligned acceptance checks added to avoid accepting a parse on partial token streams.
- OpenAI-compat streaming bridge: ensure delta messages emitted to clients reflect token-aligned content and include explicit "partial_token" flags when the client wants the in-flight bytes (opt-in). By default we keep the previous behavior but correct ordering so that client-visible incremental JSON tokens are valid JSON fragments.
- Function-calling fixes: ensure tool arguments reconstructed from streaming fragments preserve high-level token boundaries. Add tests covering emoji and non-Latin scripts in tool args.
- New tests: unit + fuzz harness for token boundary + regex interactions, integration test for streaming OpenAI-compat outputs, and canary tests that run a constrained-decoder workload against the internal perf canary cluster.
- Docs: document new config knobs (constraint_fallback: [escape|repair|fallback_model], streaming_partial_tokens: [true|false]) and guidance on selecting policies for low-latency vs correctness tradeoffs.

Checklist:
- [x] TokenBoundaryAdapter implementation and unit tests
- [x] Regex backend streaming migration and tests
- [x] CFG acceptance update and tests
- [x] OpenAI-compat bridge ordering fix and streaming flag
- [x] Integration tests + canary bench run
- [x] Docs + changelog entry

Commits summary:
- 7e3c1d7 add TokenBoundaryAdapter, unit tests for surrogate/emoji cases
- b2a9f4e migrate regex backend to token-span matcher and add fuzz harness
- c14d99a fix openai-compat streaming ordering + add partial_token opt-in flag
- d0a2f5b function-calling: preserve token grouping for tool args and add integration test
- e55b73c docs: config knobs and migration notes

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/decoders/token_boundary_adapter.rs
- runtime/decoders/regex_token_matcher.rs
- runtime/decoders/cfg_acceptor.rs

- new: matcher.feed_token_spans(&[TokenSpan]) -> regex compiled against token-levelized string with join markers.

Review conversation (abridged chronological):

Fixes several streaming correctness bugs where tokenization boundaries (emoji, multi-codepoint glyphs, and non-ASCII scripts) could cause malformed JSON or incorrect function-calling payloads during streaming. Adds a configurable fallback policy for stalled constraints and an opt-in partial_token streaming flag. Backward compatible by default; see docs for migration steps."

Motivation:
We see long presubmit setup times (cold docker pulls, large toolchains) and occasional flakiness from installing large dev dependencies on CI. This PR introduces two complementary changes: (1) a set of thin presubmit images focused only on runtime/test deps to reduce container size and pull time; (2) a dep-curation adapter that integrates with our presubmit prober to report and optionally quarantine high-risk transitive dev-deps.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds devtools/presubmit-images/ with two Dockerfiles (node-thin, python-thin) and a small make target to build and push ephemeral tags for CI.
- Reworks .github/workflows/presubmit.yml to add a thin-image fastpath lane that runs faster smoke tests for small changes. Full matrix runs fall back to the previous image.
- Adds ci/toolchain/presubmit_adapter.go: an opt-in adapter that queries a curated dev-dep allowlist and annotates presubmit runs with a risk score.
- Adds scripts/presubmit/cache-warm.sh to prefetch common layers & warm runner caches for nightly builds.
- Updates docs/dev/presubmit.md with the new workflow and guidance for maintainers.

Design notes:
- Thin images only contain runtime libs and the minimal test harness; heavy build steps (e.g. full webpack, wheel building) still run in the standard image. This reduces pull time for fast feedback while preserving correctness for full CI runs.
- The dep-curation adapter is intentionally read-only by default. When the presubmit prober flags a high-risk transitive dep, it adds an annotation and opens a Linear task suggesting quarantine. Quarantine policy is opt-in and gated behind the "dep-curation" label.

Checklist:
- [x] Build thin images locally and verify size reduction (~65% smaller node image in our tests)
- [x] Smoke presubmit runs on branch using thin-image lane (green)
- [x] Full matrix runs on standard image (green)
- [x] Integration test: adapter annotates runs when encountering an allowlist miss (verified in SUP-4122 repro)
- [x] Docs updated and maintainers notified via #dev-infra

Testing and rollout plan:
- Initial rollout enables thin-image fastpath for PRs that change <= 10 files and are not in build-critical paths. We monitor flakiness/false-negatives via presubmit metrics (latency, failure rate) and will toggle coverage thresholds if we detect regressions.
- Dep-curation adapter will be deployed in monitoring mode for 2 weeks: it will only annotate. After stabilization we will enable automated quarantine for packages with repeated incidents.

Notes on compatibility & migration:
- No changes to public APIs. This is an infra-level optimization. Individual repos can opt-out by adding a PRESUBMIT_NO_THIN_IMAGE file at the repo root (documented in presubmit.md).

Related work: ENG-1829 (ci fast feedback), ENG-1893 (dep hygiene), SUP-4122 (support incident that exposed flaky dev deps).
Marcos Li: Can we add a small compatibility test that runs the thin image against a couple of sample repos? Concern: false negatives when build step omitted.
Asha Patel: Good point — added a lightweight compatibility test to the presubmit fastpath that runs yarn build/pytest in a minimized form; if it fails we fall back to the full image (see commit g6a7c88).
Priya Nair: The dep-curation adapter is neat; please ensure annotations include a reproducible fingerprint (package + version + transitive path). Also add opt-out flag for mono-repos with heavy internal tooling.
Asha Patel: Added fingerprinting and PRESUBMIT_NO_THIN_IMAGE opt-out. Doc updated.

Motivation and summary: Long-sequence streaming workloads still suffer from tail-latency spikes due to rotary/rope rematerialization and KV cache misses during continuous batching. This PR introduces two complementary runtime features: (1) an "anchored-rope prefetcher" that anchors rotary/rope offsets to streaming lanes and proactively warms per-lane KV segments, and (2) an "attention-bridge" microkernel path with a hotpath scheduler that routes short-latency streaming requests to a fused rotary+qkv transform with minimal memory movement. Together these reduce p50/p95/p99 latency and increase steady-state throughput for mixed streaming and batched workloads.

What changed (high level):
- runtime/attention/attn_bridge.cu: new attention-bridge microkernel that applies fused rotary transforms on pinned buffers and calls the existing flash-backed matmul path. The bridge minimizes device->device memcpy and reorders transforms to enable earlier KV population.
- runtime/kv/anchored_prefetcher.cpp / .h: implementation of anchored-lane prefetcher, lane bookkeeping, and adaptive reservoir eviction. Prefetcher exposes lane affinity hints to the scheduler.
- runtime/scheduler/hotpath_scheduler.cpp: continuous batching scheduler extension that creates "hotpath lanes" for low-latency streams and uses lane-aware batching windows. Includes admission control and graceful fallback to default batcher.
- runtime/config/feature_flags.yaml: flags to toggle anchored prefetcher and bridge kernel independently for dogfooding.
- python/tests/test_anchor_rope.py: unit/integration tests covering lane affinity, KV warming, and fallback.
- perf/benchmarks/anchored_rope_trace.json: synthetic trace used for perf numbers and CI benchmark.
- docs/perf/anchored-rope-prefetch.md: design rationale and guidance for tuning lane counts and eviction thresholds.

Checklist:
- [x] design doc reviewed (ENG-2145)
- [x] microbench (unit GPU kernels) and end-to-end perf harness runs
- [x] backward-compatibility fallbacks implemented and tested
- [x] feature flags and docs added
- [x] safety: kernel asserts and bounds checks included

Commits (summary):
- 7f3b2d1 Add attention-bridge microkernel and basic API
- 4c0d8aa Implement anchored prefetcher + lane bookkeeping
- a9d5e22 Integrate hotpath scheduler with continuous-batcher and lane hints
- 2b18f4f Add tests and docs; feature flags and perf trace

Files touched (high level diffs / snippets):
- runtime/attention/attn_bridge.cu (new) -- key snippet: "// apply fused rotary in-place on pinned lane buffer; call flash_mm for qk/kv"
- runtime/kv/anchored_prefetcher.cpp (new) -- key snippet: "void Prefetcher::warm_lane(int lane_id, SequenceKey k) { // async prefetch KV into lane pool }"
- runtime/scheduler/hotpath_scheduler.cpp (mod) -- key snippet: "if (lane_affinity.requested()) route_to_hotpath(); else default_batch();"

Performance results (summary):
- Workloads: Llama-style 32k-token synthetic traces and 1:many real streaming traces from internal RL agent traces (anonymized).
- Median latency (seq=1024): -12% vs baseline (continuous-batcher + existing kernels)
- Throughput improvement (mixed streaming + batch): +20% steady-state tokens/sec under typical load
- p99 tail latency (seq=4096, streaming prioritization): -30% (most visible in mixed low-qps streaming lanes)
- Cost estimate: ~15% lower per-token GPU compute due to improved KV reuse and reduced redundant rotary ops

Compatibility and safety:
- Feature flags allow gradual rollout per-customer and per-cluster.
- If the bridge kernel or prefetcher detect unrecognized model layouts (legacy QKV packing), they fall back to existing kernels.
- We added unit tests that assert numeric closeness (relative error thresholds) between bridge path and baseline flash path for representative layers.

Review conversation (high-level):
- Miguel Torres (reviewer): "Nice design; main concern is memory amplification from per-lane KV reservoirs under many concurrent streams. Can we cap resident lane pages and add backpressure?"
- Author (Asha): "Added reservoir cap with LRU-proportional eviction and admission control in hotpath scheduler. See anchored_prefetcher.cpp:EvictIfOverBudget(). Also added metric kv.lane_resident_pages to monitor."
- Liam Chen (reviewer): "Bench results look promising. Please add an end-to-end CI run against the collector traces and confirm no regression on small-batch throughput."
- Author: "Triggered an extended perf job: perf-ci/anchored-rope on 2026-02-25; results attached to the CI. Small-batch microbench unchanged or slightly improved due to earlier rotary fusion."
- Sarah Nguyen (approver): "Code looks clean; I approve once the perf CI is green and we add the doc section on tuning lane count."

CI / checks:

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flags (this PR).
2) Canary on Dedicated clusters with small lane_count (2) and reservoir_budget=16GB for a week. Monitor metrics: kv.lane_hit_rate, kv.lane_resident_pages, scheduler.hotpath_miss_rate, inference.p99
3) Gradually increase lane_count for streaming-heavy customers and tune eviction thresholds using the provided scripts in docs/perf.

Known limitations and follow-ups:
- Current bridge kernel assumes rotary is applied per-head in a single contiguous buffer; follow-up will add non-contiguous head layout support (ENG-2201).
- Prefetcher warms at lane granularity; future work: sub-lane warm granularity for very large models to reduce resident memory footprint.

Notes for on-call / SRE: If rollout causes increased OOMs, disable "anchored_prefetcher" flag and set scheduler.hotpath_enabled=false. Metrics exposed: kv.lane_resident_pages, kv.lane_evictions, scheduler.hotpath_routes, attn.bridge_fallbacks.
Miguel Torres: Nice design; main concern is memory amplification from per-lane KV reservoirs under many concurrent streams.
Asha Patel: Added reservoir cap and LRU-proportional eviction; metric kv.lane_resident_pages added.
Liam Chen: Please add end-to-end CI run against collector traces and confirm no regression on small-batch throughput.
Asha Patel: Triggered perf-ci/anchored-rope on 2026-02-25; initial failure due to eviction bug, fixed and reran -> pass.
Sarah Nguyen: Approve once perf CI green and docs updated with tuning guidance.

payload.body:
Motivation: Customers using the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer reported subtle regressions when combining stop arrays with streaming and tool/function calls. Specifically: (1) no way to express relative stop importance (we had only boolean stops), (2) toolcall argument/role metadata lost when intermediary framing happened, and (3) streaming consumers observed non-deterministic logprob attachments when fragments were reassembled. This PR implements a minimal, backward-compatible extension to address these gaps. Design summary: - stop_weighting param: allow an optional numeric weight per stop token or sequence. The field is an array matching stops semantics: when provided, runtime uses weighted-stop arbitration instead of first-match-only. Defaults to uniform weights to preserve existing behavior. - toolcall-preserve: ensure the tool/function call envelope preserves role and argument metadata across stream fragmenting/reassembly. This required threading a small immutable metadata header through the stream coordinator and adding a stable boundary marker so tools can resume. - framed-logprob-envelope: coined a compact logprob envelope that is emitted only when the streaming frame is closed (or when a heartbeat indicates finality). Logprobs are now deterministic by construction (we serialize sorted token indices and a base64 payload) which eliminates assembly race conditions. Implementation highlights: - API adapter: v1 compatibility adapter now accepts stop_weighting (v1 -> internal mapping stop_weights[]) and normalizes numeric strings to floats. Old clients that send only stop are unaffected. - Serving runtime: added weighted-stop comparator that can be pluggable in the step loop; microbenchmarked to <2% p99 delta at typical batch sizes. - Stream coordinator: added a lightweight frame header (0xFA marker + 3-byte version) and a finalization heartbeat for long-running streams. - Toolcall handoff: preserved tool role/args in the tool-metadata header and added a reconcile step in the response-synthesizer so downstream SDKs receive the original call payload. - Tests: unit tests for the comparator, integration tests covering streaming frames with simulated packet reordering, and an end-to-end suite verifying v1 clients with/without stop_weighting. Commits: - a1b2c3d: adapter: accept stop_weighting (parse and normalize) - e4f5g6h: runtime: weighted-stop comparator and tests - i7j8k9l: streaming: frame header and heartbeat, stable logprob envelope - m0n1o2p: tooling: preserve toolcall metadata through frames - q3r4s5t: tests: add integration flakiness harness and docs Changes (high level, not exhaustive): - src/compat/v1/adapter.go: add parsing/validation for stop_weighting; map into internal StopPolicy - runtime/stop_policy.go: new weighted comparator implementation - runtime/stop_policy_test.go: unit coverage with many edge cases - services/stream/coordinator.go: attach frame header, heartbeat, and finalization path - services/stream/logprob_envelope.go: compose deterministic logprob blob, base64 serialize - services/tool/handshake.go: persist toolcall role/arg metadata and reconcile on reassembly - docs/openapi/v1_chat.yaml: document stop_weighting field and compatibility notes Small illustrative snippet (compat adapter normalization): "if len(req.StopWeighting) > 0 { for i, w := range req.StopWeighting { req.StopWeights[i] = parseFloat(w) } }" Review conversation (excerpt): - Marta Li (reviewer): "Please validate that empty/partial weight arrays fall back to uniform behavior and add a test for mismatched lengths vs stops." - Aisha Kumar (author): "Added validation to adapter.go to reject mismatched lengths with a clear 400 and unit tests covering mismatches; fallback semantics now documented." - Jared Simms: "Can we avoid copying the full tool payload in the hot path? Concern about extra allocations." - Aisha Kumar: "We store a small immutable reference header (<=256 bytes) on the coordinator hot path and only materialize the full payload when a tool handshake is invoked; benchmark attached." - Omid Rezai: "CI failed once on streaming_reassembly_test previously; make sure the flakiness harness is deterministic." - Aisha Kumar: "Fixed a race in test harness by seeding the reorder RNG and added an assertion to ensure consistent ordering when replayed." CI and validation: - Initial CI run: lint passed, unit tests passed, streaming_integration flaky (1/3 failures) due to test harness race. - After fix: all checks green. Motivation:
This PR introduces a lightweight enforcement layer (CommitWindowConstrain) for per-tenant commit windows and a GranularBurstReclaimer that reclaims unused burst credits more smoothly. The goal is to improve throughput guarantees for Dedicated tenants during sustained load while avoiding hard throttles that cause cascaded latency spikes.

What it changes (high level):
- New controller commit_window_controller: monitors tenant commit windows, underlying pool headroom, and soft-limits per-tenant based on recent usage profiles.
- GranularBurstReclaimer: returns unused burst credits back to the shared reservoir on a smoothed schedule (exponential decay + jitter) instead of instant forfeiture.
- New telemetry exports: 99/95/50 utilization percentiles for tenant pools, per-tenant headroom gauge, and a "reclaim_ramp" histogram to help correlate reclaim behavior with latency.
- Configuration surface: a new dedicated section in values.yaml and a runtime config map with knobs: commit_window_ms, reclaim_half_life_s, min_burst_floor, tenant_penalty_backoff.
- Tests and benchmarks: unit tests for controller logic, integration scenario using the perf-canary harness to validate throughput under synthetic long-tail sequences.

Why different from previous autoscalers:
Existing autoscalers optimize fleet size and coarse burst allocation. This work focuses on contract enforcement at the request admission level: rather than immediately blocking tenants that exceed burst expectations, the controller nudges soft-limits and reclaims credits gradually so downstream services see bounded, smooth degradations. It is intended to complement (not replace) existing reservation and warm-pool logic.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of controller + reclaimer
- [x] Unit tests for core decision functions
- [x] Telemetry integration and dashboards (draft)
- [x] Perf scenario validated end-to-end
- [x] Docs: runbook describing knobs and troubleshooting

Related: ENG-2345 (throughput-contracts iteration), ENG-2890 (observability for reclamation).

Backwards compatibility and rollout:
Behavior is gated behind a dedicated feature flag (commit_window_enforce=false by default). Chart / values.yaml ship with conservative defaults (commit_window_ms=2000, reclaim_half_life_s=120). We plan a canary rollout to two pools for 48h with close telemetry watch before enabling by default.

Notes for reviewers:
- The key heuristic lives in commit_window_controller.go (decision function is documented in comments). We opted for a conservative soft-penalty approach: reduce tenant burst cap by proportional delta and schedule reclaim; after repeated violations tenant_penalty_backoff grows.
- Reclaimer uses a token-based accounting system; the implementation includes a small deterministic jitter to avoid synchronized spikes across tenants.
- The telemetry names are intentionally explicit (tenant_headroom_gauge, tenant_util_p95, reclaim_ramp_ms_hist) — reviewer feedback on naming is welcome.

Small code excerpt (decision logic) for context:
```
// if tenant usage over window exceeds commit_window, compute soft reduce
if observed > config.commit_window_limit {
  penalty := min(max_penalty, (observed-config.commit_window_limit)/observed)
  new_cap := current_cap * (1 - penalty)
  scheduleReclaim(tenant, reclaim_half_life)
}
```
Ethan Morales (2025-02-18): Nice direction. Can you justify the default reclaim_half_life_s=120? Feels long for some interactive workloads.

Priya Khatri (2025-02-18): The 120s default is conservative to avoid oscillation in production; we validated 30s/60s/120s in the canary and saw 30s caused sharp reclaim pulses under bursty traffic. We can expose an aggressive preset in values.yaml for low-latency tenants.

Lena Fischer (2025-02-19): Unit tests look good. Please add an assertion that tenant_penalty_backoff caps at the configured bound (to prevent runaway).

Priya Khatri (2025-02-19): Added cap and test; pushed a small follow-up commit.

Samir Patel (2025-02-19): Telemetry naming: tenant_util_p95 duplicates an existing metric name in a different package. Suggest prefixing with "dedicated_" to avoid scrape collisions.

Priya Khatri (2025-02-19): Renamed metrics to dedicated_tenant_util_p95, dedicated_tenant_headroom_gauge, and reclaim_ramp_ms_hist -> dedicated_reclaim_ramp_ms_hist. Updated dashboards reference.

Ethan Morales (2025-02-20): Integration runs looked stable for the canary pools. Approving pending squash and changelog entry.

- Add commit-window enforcement controller (feature-flagged); provides soft, proportional tenant cap reductions to protect throughput contracts.
- Add GranularBurstReclaimer to return unused burst credits on a smoothed schedule.
- Export dedicated_* tenant utilization and headroom metrics for improved observability.
- Default gated behind feature flag; canary rollout recommended before enabling cluster-wide.
Enable feature flag commit_window_enforce in chart to turn on controller; monitor dedicated_tenant_util_p95 and dedicated_reclaim_ramp_ms_hist. Recommended canary: 2 pools for 48h. If unstable, lower reclaim_half_life_s or increase min_burst_floor.
