Context and motivation: This PR implements three coordinated controls to harden cross-tenant operator access, ensure KMS request metadata is not leaked to logs, and produce a signed residency assertion attached to audit events. Motivation came from an internal review (SEC-88) and a support escalation (SUP-3214) where operator-assisted recoveries could surface sensitive KMS origin headers and ambiguous residency markers in logs. Goals: 1) prevent operator console / support tooling from seeing raw tenant KMS tokens or service account tokens (operator snooping guard), 2) sanitize all KMS authorization material before passing to audit pipelines (KMS token scrubber), 3) emit a concise, signed residency assertion that can be attached to audit events and used by downstream policy evaluators (residency signer).

Summary of changes: - Introduces operator-snooping-guard HTTP middleware that enforces RBAC-v2 decisions for operator-scoped requests, blocking or masking fields if the operator principal lacks explicit read scope for tenant-sensitive headers. The middleware consults the policy cache and falls back to a synchronous policy fetch only on cache miss. - KMS token scrubber: central filter in the audit-proxy which replaces Authorization and X-KMS-Origin headers with stable redacted placeholders and emits a scrubbed_sample to the audit payload. Scrubbing is pluggable by provider (aws/gcp/azure) and configurable per-tenant residency policy. - Residency signer: small service that signs a canonical JSON assertion containing region_pin, kms_provider, and token_scope_hash using a cluster-local signing key (KMS-backed). The signed assertion is attached to the audit envelope as residency_assertion and stored in the audit stream for downstream verification. - Adds unit and integration tests for middleware, scrubber, and signer; adds end-to-end test that exercises operator console flow, ensuring scrubbed headers are not present in operator-accessible logs. - Feature flag gate: security.operator_snoop_guard (disabled in prod by default until rollout plan completes).

Checklist (from author): - [x] Design doc: linked in PR description (Linear ENG-5421) - [x] Unit tests for scrubber and signer - [x] Integration test for operator console flow - [x] Load-test smoke to confirm latency overhead < 2ms p50 - [x] Feature flag added and documented - [x] Documentation: added runtime-config entry and rollout notes

Commits (high-level): - Maya Chen: add operator snooping guard middleware and tests - Maya Chen: implement kms token scrubber and provider adapters - Maya Chen: residency signer + signing key bootstrap integration tests - Diego Alvarez: fix policy cache race found during review - Aisha Patel: update telemetry and tracing spans

Files changed (high-level): - services/gateway/middleware/operator_snoop_guard.go (new) - services/audit/proxy/scrubber.go (new) - services/audit/signer/residency_signer.go (new) - internal/policy/cache.go (touched) - config/feature_flags.yaml (touched) - test/e2e/operator_snoop_flow_test.go (new) - docs/security/operator_snoop_guard.md (new) - deployments/helm/values-security.yaml (touched) - scripts/bootstrap_signing_key.sh (new) - ci/pipeline/security_checks.yml (touched) - observability/metrics/README.md (touched)

Review thread (condensed): - Diego Alvarez (reviewer): "Overall direction looks good. Two asks: make the scrubber deterministic for reproducible audit deltas and please add a knob to retain redacted originals for delayed forensic retrieval behind a strict access guard." Maya: "Added deterministic hashing for scrub placeholders and a 'forensics_retention' config that writes encrypted originals to a restricted S3 bucket (access audited). See scrubber provider adapters." Diego: Approved after follow-up commit. - Aisha Patel (reviewer): "Concerned about policy cache staleness causing false denies for live operator workflows." Maya: "Cache TTL default is 30s; added forced synchronous fallback path and metrics for cache_misses and fallback_latency. Also added a migration note in docs." Aisha: "LGTM after tests." - Connor McBride (approver): "Please ensure the signing key bootstrap script is idempotent for private deployments." Maya: "Script updated to be idempotent and to log safe warnings on first-run. Added verification test." Connor: Approved.

CI matrix and outcomes: - unit-tests: pass - integration-tests (audit): pass - load-smoke: pass (p50 overhead < 1.5ms, p99 < 6ms) - lint: pass - security-scan (dependency-check): pass after bumping a transitive parquetlib dep that caused a warning - e2e: flaky at first due to race; fixed by increasing test harness wait for policy propagation; final run: pass

Rollout and operational notes: - Feature is behind security.operator_snoop_guard flag. We plan a staged rollout: enable on internal-only tenant pool for 72h -> enable on low-traffic dev customers -> enable for all non-enterprise tenants -> enterprise tenants by opt-in. - Telemetry: metrics added: security.snoop_guard.cache_miss_total, security.scrubber.redacted_total{provider,tenant}, security.residency.sign_requests_total, security.residency.verify_failures_total. Alerts proposed in console runbook. - Forensics path: when forensics_retention is enabled, scrubber stores encrypted originals to a tenant-specific S3 prefix with strict bucket policies and an operator access workflow that requires a second approver. - Backwards compatibility: no changes to public API surfaces; audit envelope extended with residency_assertion which downstream consumers should ignore if unknown.

Security considerations: - The signing key is provisioned via KMS and never exported. We added a CI gating check that ensures signing key references are not present in PR diffs. - The scrubber uses a deterministic HMAC with tenant-scoped master key to prevent correlation cross-tenant while keeping placeholders reproducible for dedupe. - RBAC: operator-snooping-guard enforces RBAC-v2 attribute checks; we added a policy simulator to test common operator flows and a small migration guide for teams that rely on operator-level visibility.

Merge outcome: Merged via squash on 2024-12-03 after approvals from Diego, Aisha, and Connor. Release note entry added to CHANGELOG under Unreleased -> Security.

Context: Dedicated fleets suffer occasional coordinated warmup costs when multiple tenants ramp simultaneously; autoscalers overprovision to avoid SLA blips. Motivation: reduce cost and transient latency by predicting short-term usable capacity and adjusting the warm-pool sparsity without weakening burst guarantees. What this PR does: 1) Adds a fleet-level capacity fingerprinter that ingests recent allocation events, per-pool occupancy histograms, and node provisioning latency to produce a lightweight short-horizon capacity fingerprint used by the autoscaler and admission controller. 2) Implements a sparse warm-pool adjuster that intentionally leaves a subset of warm slots in a probabilistic 'sparse' state and opportunistically pre-warms them when the fingerprint indicates pending demand. 3) Exposes telemetry and an opt-in tuning API for Dedicated customers to control warm-pool density and aggressiveness. Design notes: fingerprint is an exponential moving sketch (capacity/occupancy histograms with decay) stored per-fleet with configurable horizon (default 2m). The adjuster uses a conservative pre-warm policy to preserve the existing burst SLAs; when the fingerprint predicts >50% sustained headroom drawdown in the horizon, the adjuster transitions sparse slots to warm sequentially, bounded by a warm-rate cap. Safety: admitted capacity guarantees are unchanged; a short-lived burst fallback path was added to admission to use reserved cold slots (no impact to correctness). Rollout: feature gated for Dedicated clusters behind --enable-fleet-fingerprint and Opt-in flag in tenant config. Monitoring: new metrics (fleet.fingerprint.horizon_seconds, warmpool.sparse_fraction, warmpool.prewarm_rate, fingerprint.predicted_headroom_pct) and dashboards included. Testing: unit tests for sketch decay and adjuster logic; cluster integration tests with synthetic coordinated-ramp scenarios; canary rollout on two Dedicated pools for 48h. Impact: expected 6-12% reduction in warmup GPU-hours for typical multi-tenant patterns and 10-25% fewer transient latency SLO breaches during coordinated ramps. Related: builds on prior telemetry work (ENG-7123) and complements the warm-pool prewarm feature (ENG-7940).
Introduces a lightweight fleet-level capacity fingerprint for short-term headroom prediction and a sparse warm-pool adjuster to reduce warmup costs while maintaining burst guarantees. Backwards compatible; no customer config required but opt-in tuning flags available for Dedicated customers.
Owen Patel (reviewer): Can you explain why we chose an EM sketch vs full HDR histograms? Concerned about memory use for large fleets.
Author (Maya): EM sketch gives bounded memory and makes decay semantics explicit for short horizons. HDR would give more precision but is heavier; we profiled both and EM was ~6x lighter with comparable short-horizon accuracy in our traces.
Rita Gomez (reviewer): Need stronger safety net around admission path; if the adjuster prewarms too aggressively we should not evict lower-priority tenants.
Author: Added a prewarm_rate cap and tenant-priority-aware ordering; adjuster will never prewarm beyond reserved slow-path capacity. Added unit tests and a canary plan to monitor eviction-like events.
Noah Kaplan (reviewer): CI flaked once on integration test due to timing; please make the test less time-sensitive or add tolerances.
Author: Made test less timing-sensitive and replaced fixed sleeps with event-driven waits. Reran CI and green.
5 commits: initial fingerprint data model and API; sketch decay and ingestion worker; sparse warm-pool controller and admission hook; telemetry, dashboards and unit tests; canary rollout docs and feature gate wiring.
Merged via squash. Canary monitored for 48h with no regressions; rollout flag enabled on two Dedicated regions, follow-up tickets created for gradual global rollout if telemetry matches expectations. Post-merge: created ENG-8410 for rollout automation and ENG-8411 for tenant-facing tuning docs.

payload.body:
Motivation: We need stronger guarantees that operator/tenant bindings are timeboxed, that operator keys presented to the control plane are proven (KMS POP), and that audit exports do not leak residency-sensitive attributes during the GDPR pilot. This PR introduces three cooperating pieces: 1) a temporal-binding-validator middleware that enforces max-duration and step-down rules for RBAC v2 bindings; 2) KMS-backed proof-of-possession (POP) verification for operator credentials used during delegation flows; 3) an audit-scrubber pipeline that redacts or pseudonymizes residency-related attributes from exported audit rows when the tenant is in pilot mode. Design summary: - Temporal validator: implemented as an admission-style check in the policy-enforcer service. Validates binding metadata: start_ts, expiry_ts, delegation_chain_length, and enforces a configurable per-operator max_ttl. Short-lived bindings can be auto-extended only with a separate approval flow. The validator is feature-flagged (feature.temporal_binding_validator) and defaults to off. - KMS POP verifier: adds a KMS client shim that requests a signed nonce challenge and verifies signatures against tenant CMKs / operator-wrapped keys; supports primary providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and a mock provider for testing. Verification occurs during operator credential registration and when creating operator-scoped temporary bindings. - Audit scrubber: a streaming processor that subscribes to the audit-forwarder topic and applies residency filters for pilot tenants. Redaction rules are pluggable via config/residency_rules.yaml and support pseudonymization (HMAC with tenant salt) or full redaction. The scrubber emits both scrubbed events (for external exports) and retains full events in encrypted internal stores for compliance with retention contracts. Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flags (temporal_binding_validator, kms_pop_verifier, audit_scrubber_pilot). 2) Enable KMS POP in staging for a small set of operator accounts and run POP-only mode (failures logged but not blocking). 3) Enable temporal validator in constrained mode (warnings + non-blocking). 4) Enable scrubber for pilot tenants only. 5) After two weeks of telemetry and a manual compliance review, flip to blocking mode and expand to additional tenants. Backwards compatibility: All behavior is opt-in. Existing bindings and operator flows remain unchanged unless feature flags are toggled. Migration: migration script added to policydb/migrations/20260214_temporal_binding.sql to add max_ttl and issued_at columns and backfill from existing metadata where present. Security considerations: - POP requires KMS IAM roles; the shim includes retry/backoff and safe-fail behavior to avoid large production outages if KMS is throttled. - Scrubber keeps an audit provenance tag (sha256) for each scrubbed row so legal/compliance can rehydrate under strict process. - Unit and integration tests included for edge cases: missing expiry, long delegation chains, KMS transient failure, scrubber rule mismatch. Testing: - New unit tests: 62 files covering validator logic, KMS shim, scrub rules. - Integration test harness: deploys local mock-kms and runs end-to-end binding issuance and audit export flow. - Load test: temporal validator added to perf-canary with lightweight rule set; observed median +1ms added to policy-check path under 1000 RPS. Checklist: - [x] Design doc: docs/security/temporal-binding-validator.md - [x] Migration script added - [x] Feature flags created and documented - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Observability: metrics (validator.rejects, pop.verifications, scrubber.redactions) and traces added - [x] Security review queue: SEC-71 referenced Known limitations: - POP currently supports only RSA/ECDSA keys via KMS sign; hardware-enclave keys (HSM attestation) are TODO. - Scrubber pseudonymization relies on tenant salt; key rotation semantics added to docs but not automated in this PR. Notes: This PR purposefully keeps the scrubber and POP verifications non-blocking initially to gather telemetry and avoid unexpected production failures.
Anika Shah: Please add a unit test for the case where expiry_ts is missing and delegation_chain_length > 3. We should reject such bindings in strict mode.
Marcus Delgado: Added missing test and updated validator to log an explicit audit tag when issuing non-blocking warnings.
Priya Nair: KMS shim looks good. Can you add metrics for provider latency (pop.aws.latency_ms) and a circuit-breaker metric?
Marcus Delgado: Added latency histogram and simple circuit-breaker counters. Also added comments about safe-fail semantics in README.
Ethan Cole: Minor: run gofmt/clang-format on provider adapters. Also please include a short runbook for how to escalate KMS POP failures to oncall.
Marcus Delgado: Formatting applied, and runbook stub added at docs/runbooks/kms-pop-failure.md

payload.body:
Motivation: production workloads exhibit heavy variance in sequence length. Existing bucketing strategies are static and either overpad (wasteful cost) or force small batches (poor throughput). We need a lightweight scheduler that trades slightly higher scheduling complexity for measurable per-token efficiency and improved KV cache hit rates.

Design summary: add a Weighted Greedy Cohorter (WGC) scheduler in the runtime batch composer that: 1) scores ready requests by a two-part heuristic: (a) pad-cost reduction potential (estimated tokens saved if grouped with candidate cohort) and (b) kernel-fit alignment score (how well the candidate group matches an efficient kernel tile/shape for the target accelerator). 2) chooses cohorts greedily within a short time window (configurable micro-batching delay) to keep latency SLOs. 3) applies an opportunistic KV-prefetch policy: when a cohort is formed and its leader request has an existing KV cache miss probability above a threshold, the scheduler issues a lightweight prefill job to warm shards (best-effort, limited concurrency) before dispatch to the GPU.

Key changes (high level):
- runtime/scheduler/wgc_cohorter.{cc,h}: new scheduler implementation, configurable parameters (window_ms, weight_pad, weight_kernel, kv_prefetch_limit).
- runtime/batch_composer.cc: integration hooks, cohort scoring pipeline, metrics emission.
- runtime/kv_cache/prefill_worker.cc: small worker that performs async prefetches to shard cache with backpressure and rate limiting.
- runtime/kernel_selector.cc: add kernel-fit scoring hints to allow scheduler to prefer cohorts that map to high-throughput kernel variants.
- tests/unit/wgc_cohorter_test.cc: new unit tests for scoring and window behaviors.
- perf/canaries/wgc_endtoend_bench.py: microbenchmark harness to reproduce improvements.

Commits summary: 7 commits
- init: add WGC scheduler and config scaffolding
- scoring: implement pad-cost + kernel-fit scoring
- kv-prefetch: add prefill worker and integration
- metrics: add per-cohort pad_savings, kernel_hint, kv_prefill_attempts counters
- tests: unit coverage + mocked KV backend tests
- perf: add bench harness + scripts
- docs: api/config docs + migration notes

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/scheduler/wgc_cohorter.cc/h (new)
- runtime/batch_composer.cc/h (small changes)
- runtime/kv_cache/prefill_worker.cc (new)
- runtime/kernel_selector.cc (add hooks)
- proto/runtime_config.proto (add wgc params)
- tests/* (new tests)

Benchmarks (ci/perf runs):
- Microbench on p4d.24xlarge (mixed seqlen profile derived from production telemetry):
  - baseline (dynamic-bucket-heuristic v1): 100% token/s baseline
  - WGC + kv-prefetch: +13.4% token/s median, 11.2% token/s 95th
  - End-to-end cost model (tokens-per-second normalized): ~6.8% reduction in $/token due to less padding and higher kernel utilization
  - Tail latency (99th): improved by ~7% under high QPS thanks to KV warmups reducing backend waits

CI: all unit tests and integration tests pass. Perf canary job showed improvements; we included a short-running canary in CI that validated basic end-to-end flow. One flaky test (kv_cache/restart_test) was marked flaky and quarantined.

Review conversation (high level):
- Asha: "Nice pragmatic approach — can we make the KV-prefetch opt-in per-customer?" -> Added config flag and per-tenant override; documented defaults.
- Connor: "Concerned about scheduling cost at high QPS" -> Added an early-exit fast path for cohorts where window_ms==0 and implemented O(1) approximate scoring for common case; added benchmark proving <1% CPU overhead on control plane.
- Marta: "Please add more observability around failed prefetches and backpressure" -> Emitted new metrics and traces; added retry/backoff policy.
- Author response: implemented changes, addressed comments, ran additional perf runs.

Backward compatibility & rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime config (wgc.enabled=false by default). Rollout plan: staged rollout to Dedicated clusters, run perf canaries with production traffic profiles, enable per-customer opt-in via Console, monitor pad_savings and kv_prefill_attempts. Fall back to existing dynamic-bucket strategy if large cohort error rates observed.

Follow-ups (explicitly noted in PR):
- ENG-3201: autop-tune weight_pad/weight_kernel using historical traces (future work).
- ENG-3202: integrate with the Optimize suggestion engine to propose WGC params for customers.

Why this is different from previous bucketing work: WGC is not a static bucketing scheme — it is a short-window greedy compositor that scores live requests for both padding minimization and kernel efficiency while adding a modest opportunistic KV warmup path. Prior PRs focused on static histogram bucketing or pure seqlen clustering; WGC targets the intersection: quick on-line decision making that is kernel-aware and KV-aware, designed for continuous batching scenarios where micro-latency headroom can be used for better packing.

Merge outcome: merged to main via squash on 2025-11-15 after CI green and perf canary verification. Migration docs and feature flagging included.
Introduces a weighted greedy cohorting scheduler that reduces padding and opportunistically prefetches KV cache to improve steady-state throughput and tail latency for variable-length workloads.
opt-in by default
flag: runtime.wgc.enabled
perf: +13% token/s median on mixed seqlen profile
payload.title: Weighted greedy cohorter + KV-prefetch: scheduler heuristic to reduce pad waste and warm KV cache

Motivation: production workloads report oscillating batch sizes and noisy quantization rollouts across heterogeneous fleets. This PR introduces a runtime-side 'Econ Orchestrator Governor' that applies hysteresis and safe rollforward semantics to batching and compact/quantization profile changes to reduce unit-cost churn while preserving latency SLOs.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Adds a governor process that: (a) observes recent per-route latency/cost statistics, (b) computes stable batching targets using hysteresis windows to avoid flip-flops, (c) stages compact/quant profile rollforwards with canary windows and metric guards, and (d) exposes opt-in defaults for workspace-level econ profiles.

Key changes: 
- runtime/orchestrator: new governor implementation (governor.py) with hysteresis and stable-state detection; eventing hooks for policy engine.
- configs/econ_profiles/compact_defaults.yaml: curated conservative compact/quant profile defaults tuned for balanced latency/cost for small/med/large models.
- rollout logic: safe rollforward path that performs metric-based canaries (latency/accuracy/99p token-time) and automatic rollback on regressions.
- migration: workspace migration that annotates existing profiles with an opt-in 'governor:enabled' flag; default remains off for Dedicated customers unless explicitly enabled.
- console: UI panels to visualize governor decisions and canary progress (docs only; UI surfaces behind feature flag).
- tests: unit + integration tests that simulate oscillating load and quant rollforward scenarios.

Checklist:
- [x] Core governor implementation and unit tests
- [x] Canary and rollback plumbing with metric thresholds
- [x] Conservative default profiles for compact quantization
- [x] Integration tests covering hysteresis behavior
- [x] Documentation and RFC (docs/rfcs/econ-governor.md)
- [x] Backwards-compatible migration path

Risks and mitigations: the governor influences runtime decisions; it is gated by workspace opt-in and feature flagging. Rollforward always starts with a small canary fraction and metric guards to auto-rollback on P95/P99 or accuracy regressions. We also added observable traces and alerts for unexpected oscillations.

Related work: builds on ENG-7721 (batching heuristics) and ENG-8245 (quant profile metadata). Linear tickets: ENG-8742 (governor design), ENG-8899 (experimentation harness). Jira SUP-1187 captures customer request for safer quant rollouts.
Trevor: Left a few nit comments around threshold tuning and a question about the default canary fraction; suggested 1-2% to start. Aisha: Approved after seeing deterministic integration tests and added observability hooks. Jordan: Asked for an explicit guard on token-accuracy regressions; author added accuracy gating and extended integration coverage. CI initially failed on flaky timing of canary test; increased determinism by mocking monotonic clock and reran. Final CI green.

Author replies: responded to Trevor's threshold comments with rationale and added comments in code; implemented Jordan's accuracy guard (metrics/accuracy_check.py) and added a short note in the RFC.

Conversation snippet (single string): "Trevor Nguyen: Can we reduce default canary fraction to 1%? Some customers are latency-sensitive.
Lina Becker: Agree, lowered canary to 1% and added config override per-workspace.
Aisha Patel: Integration tests look stable, approving.
Jordan Kim: Add accuracy rollback gate.
Lina Becker: Implemented and added tests. CI initially failed, rerun passed.",
Initial pipeline failed on tests/integration/test_governor_hysteresis.py (timing-based flake). Deterministic test fix committed and CI rerun passed. Final CI: all checks passing (unit, integration, lint, e2e-mocks).
Added Econ Orchestrator Governor to provide stable batching targets and safe compact/quant profile rollforwards. Opt-in by workspace; conservative defaults provided. See RFC docs/rfcs/econ-governor.md for configuration guide and migration steps.
Feature gated. To enable for a workspace: set workspace.config.gov_enabled=true and pick a compact profile in configs/econ_profiles/compact_defaults.yaml. Watch gov.decision_rate and gov.rollback_alert metrics. Canary defaults to 1% traffic and will auto-rollback on P99 or accuracy regressions.
Run unit tests: pytest tests/unit/test_governor_state_machine.py. Integration: pytest tests/integration/test_governor_hysteresis.py --runslow. To simulate rollforward: use scripts/simulate_rollforward.py --profile small-conservative --traffic-pattern burst --observe-metrics.
payload.title: Introduce econ-orchestrator governor and safe compact profile rollforward

payload.body:
Context: Customers expect Redwood's /v1/chat compatibility layer to behave like OpenAI's chat completions for a wide range of legacy callers. We observed two classes of subtle but production-impacting differences: (1) callers passing loosely-typed params (e.g. "max_tokens" as string or stop as single string vs array) which produced surprising errors or different internal routing; (2) streaming edge cases where a sentinel (final fragment) and the last delta caused duplicated partial tokens or an out-of-order logprob envelope. This PR introduces a small compatibility shim that coercively normalizes incoming v1 chat params, clarifies/standardizes stop-array semantics, and strengthens the stream sentinel reconciliation handshake so that the final token is emitted exactly once and structured envelopes are preserved.

What this changes (summary): 1) Param coercion layer under server/proxy/openai_compat/param_coercer.py that safely coerces strings to numbers, coerces single stop string -> [string], and normalizes role aliases (assistant/system/user -> expected tokens). Coercion only runs on v1/chat entrypoints and is opt-out via a config flag. 2) Deterministic stop handling: stop arrays are canonicalized (de-duplicated, ordered by earliest-match precedence) and a clear tie-breaker is applied for overlapping stop sequences. This addresses customer reports where stop arrays produced non-deterministic truncation. 3) Stream sentinel reconciliation: added a lightweight handshake between the stream coordinator and the fragment assembler that tags sentinel fragments and defers final flush until the handshake confirms no trailing delta will arrive. The result eliminates a class of duplicate-character artifacts and prevents mis-merged logprob envelopes when function/tool-call fragments cross chunk boundaries.

Why this approach: Full strict validation broke many existing users that relied on forgiving behavior. A coercion shim provides a smoother migration path and reduces customer friction while keeping runtime invariant checks. The stream reconciliation is intentionally conservative (small delay window + deterministic ordering) to preserve latency SLOs while fixing correctness.

Checklist: - [x] Param coercion implementation + unit tests - [x] Stop-array canonicalization + unit tests - [x] Stream sentinel reconciliation + integration test (simulated chunk races) - [x] End-to-end QA against openai-compat test vectors - [x] Feature flag added and documented - [x] Back-compat smoke tests against production traffic sample

Testing notes: Added ~30 unit tests and 3 integration scenarios that replay previously failing traces (included as fixtures in tests/fixtures/stream-replay). Verified redis-backed KV-cache behaviour unchanged. Load-tested the stream coordinator under small variance and measured median latency increase of <0.5ms (within noise) with the reconciliation active.

Related: ENG-3412 (param stability), SUP-712 (customer incident #1223), ENG-3499 (streaming flake investigations).

Merge: squash and merge after CI green and one approval.
Normalize v1/chat param types (coercion for legacy callers); make stop-array handling deterministic and documented; improve stream sentinel reconciliation to avoid duplicate tokens at fragment boundaries.
Replay of production failing trace #1223 demonstrates stop array overlap previously truncating on the wrong boundary; after this change the output matches OpenAI v1 reference vectors. No user-visible change unless caller relied on previous nondeterminism. The coercion flag is off by default and will be enabled for the next minor release after staged rollout.
payload.title: v1/chat: param coercion, deterministic stop semantics, and stream sentinel reconciliation

Motivation: reduce token-level latency variance and CPU overhead for steady-state inference by leveraging CUDA graph capture/replay while avoiding correctness/perf regressions observed on variable-shape workloads. This PR adds an opt-in CUDAGraphRunner with replay support, conservative shape-guarding heuristics, targeted warmup sequences, and runtime feature flags to enable gradual rollout.

Summary of changes: consolidated the graph capture/replay plumbing into serving/runtime/cuda_graph_runner.{cc,h}, added shape guard metadata tracking to serving/runtime/request_shaper.{cc,h}, modified scheduler to insert warmup requests for newly-captured graphs (serving/scheduler/warmup_manager.{cc,h}), and extended KV cache interaction to mark graphs as non-capturable when cache aliasing is detected (serving/kv/cache_guard.{cc,h}). Added feature flag infra (platform/flags/feature_flags.cc) and a detailed e2e perf test harness (tests/perf/cudagraph_replay_endtoend_test.py).

Behavior and heuristics: capture only when the observed batch size, sequence length distribution and KV cache state are stable for N consecutive requests (configurable via feature flag). Shape guards are implemented as lightweight checks emitted alongside a captured graph; when a guard fails the runner falls back to the interpreter path and triggers a background recapture attempt with updated shape profile. Warmup mitigation: newly-captured graphs are first executed with a configurable warmup token sequence that exercises KV-cache hot paths to avoid first-predictable-token latency spikes.

Regression handling: upstream experiments found a ~4-8% end-to-end regression on workloads with frequent micro-batching and aggressive KV eviction. To address that, this PR introduces a conservative default policy (capture_threshold=20 stable requests) and a telemetry-driven automatic backoff. The PR also includes a diagnostic flag to forcibly disable capture for specific model tags.

Testing and benchmarks: included unit tests for guard logic and integration tests that validate correctness against the interpreter on randomized shapes. Perf numbers (internal): on long-lived chat traffic (median seq_len 512, stable batches=64) we see 12-18% lower p50 token latency and 28% lower p99 compared to interpreter path; on highly variable synthetic workloads the conservative defaults avoid regressions. See tests/perf/README.md for how to reproduce locally.

Rollout plan: feature gated (platform flag "cuda_graph_replay"), staged Canary rollout in Dedicated, telemetry collection for graph hit-rate, p50/p95/p99 deltas, and KV-guard trips. Default remains disabled for Hosted until 95% of canaries report neutral-or-positive latency deltas.

Notes: this PR intentionally keeps kernel selection unchanged; subsequent PR will add graph-aware kernel tuning. Backwards compatibility: no public API changes.

Related Linear: ENG-8123, ENG-8279.
Priya Singh (2026-02-19): Please add a short note in docs that capture is unsafe when KV aliasing is detected — otherwise approve after tests.
Ava Martinez (2026-02-19): Added serving/kv/cache_guard and docs/observability/cudagraph_metrics.md to explain KV guard metrics.
Ethan Zhao (2026-02-22): Observed two CI flakes in integration due to environment GPU reset timing. Recommend adding a small retry in tests and a backoff in capture attempt loop.
Ava Martinez (2026-02-23): Added retry/backoff in cuda_graph_runner and increased test tolerance; pushed follow-up commit.
Marta Lopez (2026-02-25): Did an informal perf run on Dedicated canary — p99 improved but we hit a 6% regression in a workload with frequent 1-token prefixes. Suggest shape-guard threshold tuning and default conservative values.
Ava Martinez (2026-02-26): Lowered default capture aggressiveness and exposed knobs via feature flags; added telemetry to auto-backoff when regressions detected.
Ethan Zhao (2026-03-01): Code LGTM, left a few nits; CI green on rerun. Approving to merge.
Priya Singh (2026-03-02): Approved and verified docs/observability updates.
Added opt-in CUDA graph capture/replay for serving runtime with shape guards and warmup mitigation. Feature is behind the 'cuda_graph_replay' flag and is disabled by default. Admins may tune capture thresholds and KV guard behavior via feature flags. Monitor cudagraph.hit_rate and cudagraph.guard_fail_count metrics during rollout.
payload.title: Enable CUDA Graph capture/replay with adaptive shape guards and warmup mitigation

Context and motivation: The paged KV cache has been a source of tail-latency spikes under mixed-read/write workloads. We observed eviction storms when hot ranges were repeatedly sampled by the global reclamation pass. This PR implements a striped reclamation allocator plus a prefetch-hysteresis heuristic and an async eviction slowpath to reduce stall amplification and improve locality.

What this changes (high level): Adds a striped reclaimer that divides the blockpool into lightweight stripes to spread concurrent reclamation work, implements an access-frequency-prefetch hint that primes adjacent pages on miss-heavy hot prefixes, and introduces a hysteresis threshold to avoid repeatedly prefeteching/evicting the same spans. Also moves expensive writeback scheduling off the fast path by introducing an asynchronous eviction queue processed by background workers; integrates with the scheduler to avoid eviction tasks blocking request threads.

Why this approach: Stripes reduce contention on a single global free-list and keep reclamation work proportional to active hot ranges. Prefetch hysteresis reduces oscillation between evicting and restoring the same pages when workloads oscillate at short timescales. The async eviction path prevents single-request latency from paying for I/O bound writebacks.

Compatibility and risk: No on-disk format changes. All behaviors are guarded behind a feature flag (env REDWOOD_KV_STRIPED_RECLAIM=1) and default to the existing allocator. We exercised both feature-flagged and default flows in CI and local perf runs.

Detailed changes (summary of commits): commit 1: bootstrap striped allocator scaffolding, add stripe metadata to block arena; commit 2: reclaimer algorithm and stripe-based free-list operations; commit 3: prefetch hinting and hysteresis policy driven by recent access counters; commit 4: async eviction queue + background worker integration with scheduler; commit 5: telemetry, unit tests, microbench harness and docs; commit 6: fix race in free-list handoff discovered during review.

Files touched (high level): pkg/kv/block_arena.go, pkg/kv/striped_reclaimer.go, pkg/kv/prefetch_hysteresis.go, pkg/serve/scheduler.go, pkg/kv/eviction_queue.go, pkg/metrics/kv_metrics.go, internal/bench/kv_hotspot_bench.go, docs/kv/allocator.md

Small illustrative snippet (striped free-list rotation):
- On allocation: map key hash -> stripe id -> try-local-free-list; fallback to global steal if empty.
- On reclaim: reclaimer picks stripes in round-robin and enqueues victims into async eviction queue instead of synchronous writeback.

Benchmarks and outcomes: Microbenchmark (kv_hotspot_bench) results on c5-like instance with 4 client threads: baseline median p99 latency: 720ms, after change p99 latency: 520ms (~28% reduction). Throughput under heavy mixed workload improved ~12% due to reduced stall time and localized reuse. Memory overhead: small stripe metadata (~0.7% of blockpool).

Tests: unit tests for allocator invariants, stress tests for concurrency and race detection, updated microbench harness. CI runs included a perf-job target that compares p95/p99 against baseline. One flaky test (pkg/kv TestEvictionOrdering) failed initially due to timing assumptions; it was made robust and re-run.

Review conversation (high level):
- Diego Ramos: "Nice isolation of allocation fast-path; a couple of comments around the locking order in striped_reclaimer.go — can we instead use tryLock + backoff to avoid priority inversion?"
- Maya Patel (author): "Addressed — I switched the stripe handoff to an optimistic try lock and fall back to a short backoff + yield. Updated comments and added benchmark showing no regression."
- Elaine Chung: "Prefetch hysteresis looks promising; request: make hysteresis threshold configurable via runtime knob and expose a metric for hysteresis-triggered-prefetches."
- Maya Patel: "Added REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH_HYSTERESIS_MS env var and exported metric kv_prefetch_hysteresis_count. Also documented behavior in docs/kv/allocator.md."
- Samir Khatri: "Can we ensure the async eviction queue honors tenant priority?"
- Maya Patel: "Queue now reads a priority token from the request context; default behavior preserved for existing requests. Added unit tests for priority honoring."

CI summary and merge readiness: All required checks passed after fixes: unit, integration, lint, cross-compile. Perf job indicates consistent improvement and no regression on stable workloads. Security scan clean.

Merge outcome: Squash merge into main after approvals from Diego and Elaine. Changelog entry added to docs/releases/2025-11-21.md. Feature toggles documented for staged rollout.

Follow-ups and TODOs:
- ENG-1301: evaluate stripe count auto-tuning based on active concurrency (linked linear).
- ENG-1357: extend telemetry to expose eviction latency breakdown per-stripe.

Notes for operators: Feature disabled by default. To safely roll out enable feature behind canary routing and monitor kv_prefetch_hysteresis_count and kv_eviction_async_queue_len. Watch for sustained increase in background writeback IOPS which could indicate too-aggressive eviction.

Reduced tail latency for KV-heavy workloads by up to 28% in microbenchmarks; introduces a new striped reclamation allocator and async eviction/fallback path. No API or storage layout changes.
payload.title: Striped reclamation allocator with prefetch hysteresis and async eviction path

Motivation: We saw two incidents where KMS selection mismatches caused requests to be routed to non-preferred regions, and audit logs exposed full service-principal identifiers in downstream systems. This PR adds three coordinated changes: 1) a lightweight KMS Introspector to fetch and cache key metadata (region, provider, tags) for decisioning; 2) Residency Soft-Guard, a policy shim that enforces residency decisions but allows configured soft fallbacks with enriched audit annotations; 3) Audit Obfuscator, an opt-in audit layer that pseudonymizes operator/service principal IDs using a per-tenant salt stored in the secrets store.

Summary of changes (single continuous narrative): The Introspector exposes an internal read-only API (kms_introspector.v1) used by the runtime routing layer and by the policy-enforcer to determine key residency claims without performing decrypt/encrypt operations. Residency Soft-Guard plugs into the RBAC v2 policy evaluation pipeline: when a request would violate a strict residency rule, Soft-Guard will consult fallback profiles (configured per-tenant) and, if a compatible fallback exists, allow the request with an audit annotation explaining the substitution. If no fallback exists and the tenant is in strict mode, the request is rejected. Audit Obfuscator runs as a final step before log export: it replaces full subject identifiers with salted pseudonyms and emits a keyed mapping to the internal audit vault accessible only to security ops. The mapping is HMAC-SHA256(salt, subject) with tenant salt rotation support.

Checklist:
- [x] KMS Introspector service and cache
- [x] Residency Soft-Guard policy shim and config schema
- [x] Audit Obfuscator with per-tenant salt rotation
- [x] Integration tests for policy decision paths
- [x] End-to-end canary in staging with simulated cross-region keys
- [x] Documentation and config examples for operators

Commits (high-level):
- "add kms introspector service and caching layer"
- "introduce residency soft-guard shim into rbac v2 pipeline"
- "implement audit obfuscator and mapping vault client"
- "add feature flags and operator config for fallback profiles"
- "integration tests and docs"

Changed areas (high level):
- services/kms_introspector/* — new read-only service plus cache adapter
- runtime/policy/enforcer/softguard.go — policy shim logic and config parsing
- runtime/audit/obfuscator.go — obfuscation pipeline and vault client
- api/internal/registry.proto — added kms_introspector.v1 RPC
- docs/compliance/residency_softguard.md — operator guide
- helm/values.yaml — flags to enable/disable features per-environment
- tests/integration/residency_softguard_test.go — simulated scenarios

Small illustrative snippet (policy decision annotation):
- "audit_annotation: 'residency_fallback=eu-west-1 -> eu-central-1;fallback_profile=geo-compatible;reason=operator-override-allowed'"

Review conversation (condensed as single stream):
- Marco Li (reviewer): "Nice separation of concerns. Two asks: (1) can we make cache TTL tenant-configurable? (2) please add a stronger guard when the mapping vault fails — we must avoid leaking unmapped IDs into exported logs."
- Aisha Patel (author): "Updated cache to be tenant-configurable and plumbed a fail-closed behavior for the mapping vault. Implementation note: when vault is unavailable and tenant is strict, we reject export; when soft mode, we emit 'subject=unmapped-placeholder' plus alert to ops."
- Grace Nguyen: "Integration tests look good. One nit: add a small comment documenting the HMAC key rotation procedure." 
- Daniel Kim: "Approved after minor nits resolved. Verified CI rerun passes."
Adds a KMS metadata introspector service, a residency soft-guard policy shim that can fallback to compatible key pools when strict residency enforcement is not configured, and an audit obfuscator that pseudonymizes operator/service principal identities while preserving traceability for security analysts.
Feature flags: helm.values.features.kmsIntrospector (bool), features.residencySoftGuard.mode (strict|soft). Default: disabled in stable; enabled in canary. Operators must provision per-tenant salt in secrets/vault/tenant-salts/<tenant-id>. Rolling rotation requires replay window setting to avoid mapping mismatches.
Stage: deploy with helm values enabling kmsIntrospector and residencySoftGuard.mode=soft. Run tests/integration/residency_softguard_test.go against mocked KMS endpoints. Validate audit exporter emits pseudonyms and that mapping vault entries are created. For strict tenants, assert requests are rejected when no compatible key found.
Introspector relies on KMS metadata tags; legacy keys without region tags will be treated as 'unknown' and require operator remediation. Audit mapping vault is an internal scoped secret — if that service is unavailable, exports behave as configured per-tenant (fail-closed for strict, placeholder for soft).
Planned follow-ups: (1) UI in Console to visualize fallback decisions and mapping lookup traces (ENG-2380); (2) add automated migration tool to backfill missing key-region tags (SEC-130); (3) evaluate adding cryptographic blinding to pseudonyms to support cross-tenant correlation under consented forensics flow.
Marco Li: request tenant-configurable cache TTL and fail-closed mapping vault
Aisha Patel: implemented changes and added tests
Grace Nguyen: small comment re: HMAC rotation added
Daniel Kim: approved
payload.title: Introduce KMS Introspector, Residency Soft-Guard, and Audit Obfuscator

Context: Customers with strict data residency requirements have asked for a lightweight, gateway-level enforcement that propagates a tenant's declared data-zone claim through the call chain, attaches a verifiable KMS-origin proof to encrypt/decrypt calls, and records compacted, integrity-checked audit metadata. This PR implements a middleware chain that (1) validates incoming data-zone claims in service tokens, (2) injects a signed KMS-origin header for downstream services, and (3) emits a compact audit envelope optimized for high-throughput paths. Motivation: existing enforcement lived deep in the policy enforcer and was costly to evaluate per-request; it also duplicated audit payloads and made post-facto verification expensive. Design summary: - DataZoneClaimPropagator: reads tenant-level claim from request context (Authorization JWT or tenant metadata header) and canonicalizes it to a single header X-Redwood-DataZone. If a request is missing an explicit claim, the propagator applies the customer's pinned-region default from tenant metadata; if no default exists the request is marked with X-Redwood-DataZone=unknown and flagged to the audit pipeline. - KMSProofMiddleware: for requests that require KMS-bound operations, the middleware attaches X-Redwood-KMS-Proof which is a compact signature (ed25519) over request id + data-zone + timestamp. The service uses a short-lived signing key derived from the operator's KMS identity; the middleware delegates to the existing kms-client interface for key lookup and signing. - AuditCompactEnvelope: replaces the verbose audit JSON for high-throughput endpoints with a CBOR-encoded envelope that contains a stable fingerprint, sequence id, and a digest of the full JSON audit payload stored asynchronously in the audit store. This drastically reduces per-request logging bandwidth while preserving verifiability and replay protection. Backwards compatibility: the middleware adds both the new compact envelope header (X-Redwood-Audit-Env) and preserves the existing full-audit outbound call in the background for 30 days behind a feature flag (audit.compact_rollout). Rollout plan: stage rollouts by route (default: text-gen heavy paths first) with a canary at 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Include a kill-switch at service config (feature flag + operator override) to revert to previous auditing behavior immediately. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for propagator normalization and fallback rules - [x] Integration tests that exercise KMS proof creation and verification (local kms mock) - [x] Audit compact envelope roundtrip tests (encode/decode and digest verification) - [x] Load test to validate added middleware latency < 1.5ms p50 on our benchmark-lab profile - [x] Security review with cryptography team completed - [x] Linear -> SUP ticket linking for support ops docs Changeset summary: - server/middleware/data_zone_propagator.go: new middleware, 150 LOC - server/middleware/kms_proof.go: new middleware that calls kms-client.SignCompact - audit/compact/envelope.go: encoder/decoder + digest helpers - cmd/rollouts/feature_flags.yaml: introduces audit.compact_rollout flag and canary config - docs/security/data-zone-claims.md: added operational documentation - test/integration/kms_proof_test.go and audit_compact_test.go - minor updates to existing policy-enforcer to read X-Redwood-DataZone when evaluating geofence rules Tests and CI: CI initially failed due to a flaky kms-client mock timeout in integration (CI run #342); fixed by increasing mock timeout and adding retry in test harness; subsequent CI run passed. Observability: added metrics: middleware.data_zone.propagated_total, middleware.kms_proof.signed_total, audit.compact.bytes_saved_estimate; added tracing spans for the propagator and kms proof sign step. Security considerations: - Signing keys are ephemeral and must be rotated by KMS; code ensures keys are not materialized in process except as ephemeral in-memory signatures. - Fallback 'unknown' data-zone is treated as highest-sensitivity by policy-enforcer to avoid accidental residency violations. - Audit compact envelope uses SHA-256 digest; the full audit payload is stored into the existing encrypted audit store, and the digest is included in the envelope to allow later retrieval and verification. Deployment notes: - Requires a coordinated rollout with edge gateways so X-Redwood-DataZone is honored across service boundaries. - Ops must enable kms signing key injection in the KMS policy for services; added a playbook steps in docs/security for tenant ops. - Feature flag default is off and will be enabled per-customer after acceptance testing. Related work: ties into ENG-2029 (RBACv2 policy reads of propagated claims) and SUP-4321 (customer support runbook for pinned-region misreports).
Ibrahim Noor (2026-02-27): Please ensure the KMS proof header cannot be replayed. Can we include a monotonic sequence id from the request router?
Maya Chen (reply 2026-02-27): We include request id+timestamp and the signing key is short-lived; added a sequence id field to the envelope per request-router contract in commit c3378a5.
Priya Sethi (2026-02-28): The propagator fallback to tenant default is fine, but add a test for when tenant metadata is malformed. Also please document operator steps for key provisioning.
Maya Chen (reply 2026-02-28): Added malformed metadata test and extended docs with key provisioning steps.
Liam O'Connor (2026-03-01): CI flaky test observed earlier; thanks for the timeout fix. One concern: audit.compact_rollout default off for all services? Suggest default off for other regions until we validate storage dedupe behavior.
Maya Chen (reply 2026-03-01): Agreed — kept default off and added per-region gating in feature_flags.yaml; will coordinate with infra for canary in us-west-2 first.
Introduces DataZone claim propagation middleware, compact KMS-origin proofs for downstream verification, and an audit compact envelope to reduce logging bandwidth on high-throughput paths.
Rollback: feature flag audit.compact_rollout=false or disable at service config to restore previous auditing behavior.
payload.title: add-data-zone-claim-propagator-and-kms-proof-middleware

Summary: Introduces a short-lived regional 'cooldown' (aka snooze) window that suppresses aggressive eviction/rejoin cycles and pairs it with a circuit safety net that temporarily widens SLO thresholds for tenants during transit spikes. This change is intended to reduce cascade failures and oscillation when regions experience short-lived load/saturation bursts.

Motivation: We've observed repeated thrashing where the eviction/failover logic and circuit reopen logic tugged systems back and forth during transient spikes (see SUP-4821). Two correlated problems: (1) rapid tenant evictions followed by immediate re-joins causing KV-coherence churn and elevation of backend latency, (2) circuit state flips that force broad fallback and subsequent noisy restores.

Design:
- Regional cooldown (snooze): when a region hits an SLO breach threshold, instead of immediately starting aggressive per-tenant evictions and rollbacks, we enter a short cooldown window (config default: 45s) where we prefer soft-rate-limiting, localized prefetch throttling, and conservative eviction scoring.
- Circuit safety net: when circuits would normally open for a tenant because of increasing error/latency rates, a transient safety net increases the circuit open threshold and attaches an exponential backoff before hard-open. The safety net is bounded (max 2x threshold, max 90s) and only applies when regional cooldown is active.
- Telemetry/decisions: we emit a new metric region_cooldown_active{region,reason} and per-tenant cooldown_score to help debugging. A debug endpoint in the control plane exposes active cooldown windows for troubleshooting.
- Rollout: gated behind feature flag runtime.alpha.regional_cooldown. Off by default for Dedicated accounts; enabled on host infra for gradual canary.

Checklist:
- [x] Core algorithm implementation (eviction scorer + safety net)
- [x] Unit tests for cooldown transition states
- [x] Integration test simulating short-lived spike and verifying reduced eviction/rejoin cycles
- [x] Telemetry and dashboards (initial grafana panels)
- [x] Runtime flag and ops docs
- [x] Backstop: automatic disable if region metric stream is stale

Commits summary: - c1f6b9f: implement cooldown state machine and compositor - d4a2e11: integrate safety net into circuit policy - a89d77e: add metrics and control-plane debug endpoint - 9b4c002: tests + docs + runtime flag wiring

Files changed (high level): - pkg/runtime/cooldown/state_machine.go (new) - pkg/runtime/circuit/safety_net.go (new) - pkg/eviction/scorer.go (patched: adjust scoring when cooldown active) - controlplane/handlers/debug_cooldown.go (new endpoint) - tests/integration/cooldown_integration_test.go (new) - docs/ops/regional_cooldown.md (ops runbook) - dashboards/cooldown_overview.json (grafana) Note: changes are purposely small in each file; internal logic is conservative and additive.

Testing and CI: - Local unit test coverage added for state transitions and scoring. - Integration test runs in harness simulate a 60s spike and asserts: fewer than 2 evictions per tenant during spike vs 5 in baseline; KV rejoin latency reduced by 30%. - CI: all checks passed after one flakey test re-run (flaky: end-to-end load harness warmup). ci_status: pass

Review conversation (high level): - Carlos Mendez (reviewer): "Great approach. Can we ensure the cooldown window is observable per-tenant and does not hide persistent failures?" - Author (Priya): "Yes — cooldown_score is emitted per-tenant and we have a secondary detector that escalates if the score stays high for 3 windows." - Evelyn Tran (reviewer): "Concern about bounded safety net increasing operator confusion. Add clear ops docs and a kill-switch." - Author: "Added docs + runtime flag and a control-plane kill-switch endpoint; included in release notes." - Daniel Kim: "Do we need a migration path for Dedicated clusters?" - Author: "Flag disabled by default for Dedicated; ops can enable per-cluster. We'll coordinate with infra rotation." Approvals: - Carlos Mendez approved on 2026-02-23 - Evelyn Tran approved on 2026-02-24

Merge: - Merge method: squash - Merge note: "merged with squash; timed canary to follow for 48h" - Post-merge actions: ops playbook created and channel #infra-cooldown created.

Backwards compatibility and safety: - Default OFF for Dedicated deployments. - Feature flag ensures instant roll-back without binary redeploy. - Additional guard: if control-plane telemetry becomes stale we auto-disable.snooze to avoid masking outages.

Why this is different from previous approaches: Earlier PRs attempted to tune eviction aggressiveness or tweak circuit reboot timers independently which reduced symptoms but not root cause. This PR introduces an explicit temporal decoupling (snooze) combined with a bounded safety net so decisions have short-term tolerance without permanently widening safety margins.

Notes for on-call: - If you see region_cooldown_active continuously fired for >10 minutes, run the disable endpoint and follow runbook in docs/ops/regional_cooldown.md. - For Dedicated customers, check dedicated-config for runtime.alpha.regional_cooldown flag.
Adds a regional cooldown snooze window and soft circuit safety net to reduce oscillation during short-lived SLO spikes. No config changes required by default; ops can tune via runtime flags.
payload.title: Introduce regional cooldown (snooze) and circuit safety net for transient SLO spikes

payload.body:
Motivation: provide a safer pattern for short-lived elevated operator grants by introducing temporally-bound RBAC v2 grants that are cryptographically attested and paired with an audit blinding shim. This addresses live-operator attack windows, noisy audit channels for sensitive escalation events, and the need for KMS-backed proof of intent for compliance reviews. Summary of changes: 1) RBAC runtime: add temporalGrant API and evaluator that supports start/expiry, one-time-use tokens, and constraint expressions (namespace, service, action). Grants are persisted to the policy store with an HMAC and a KMS-wrapped signature for non-repudiation. 2) Attestation flow: operator requests a grant via existing operator API; a new attestation service performs policy checks, issues a short-lived attestation token signed with KMS CMK, and stores a compact proof in the attest-store. 3) Audit blinding shim: conditional blinding layer on the audit pipeline that replaces sensitive fields with reversible tokens and writes a blinded copy to the public audit stream; a separate sealed-audit vault holds the reversible mapping encrypted with the customer's CMK. 4) Compliance hooks: add an admin-only replay endpoint that rehydrates blinded audits after authorization and verifies attestation signatures before returning plaintext. 5) Migration and compatibility: new temporal grants are optional behind the feature flag security.temporal_attested_rbac. Old static grants continue to work; the evaluator performs precedence checks so temporal grants can be scoped more narrowly. Checklist: - [x] design doc (Linear ENG-4521) linked - [x] unit tests for evaluator and attestation signer - [x] e2e flow test for operator request -> attestation -> audited event - [x] KMS integration tests with test CMK - [x] basic load test to validate attestation service under 500 rps - [x] docs and console UI hint copy Draft rollout plan: enable feature flag off by default; deploy attestation service and evaluator in canary mode to a subset of control-plane nodes; on success, enable for orgs in pilot; after 2 weeks, global rollout. Security review: design reviewed by SecEng (SEC-213) and approved with minor hardening suggestions applied. Migration notes: no automated changes to existing RBAC policies; admins can opt-in by creating temporal grants via console or API. Observability: new metrics rbac.temporal_grants.requested, rbac.temporal_grants.issued, attest.sign_failures, audit.blindings.emitted added to control-plane telemetry; new audit tag "attestation_id" is included in blinded and sealed records. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: misuse of blinding could hide malicious activity. Mitigation: sealed-audit vault access requires CMK unwrap and admin rehydration flow with multi-party approval (two approvers). - Risk: KMS latency impacts attestation path. Mitigation: local caching of attestation proofs with short TTL and fallback signed HMAC when KMS unavailable (telemetry flagged). Rollback: remove feature flag and expire issued temporal grants; attestation tokens remain verifiable but enforcement disabled. Full description and design are in Linear ENG-4521 and design doc attached to the PR.
Evan Brooks: Overall this looks solid; please add a fast-path for KMS-unavailable mode and measure effect on median latencies.
Maya Chen: Added local proof cache with 1m TTL and documented the failure mode; results from load test included in CI artifacts.
Sanjay Rao: Audit blinding is powerful but dangerous — we need a strict RBAC check around rehydration endpoint and HSM audit of access. Please add guardrails.
Maya Chen: Rehydration endpoint now requires two admin approvals and logs a non-blindable event to the sealed-vault access log; added e2e asserting approval flow.
Priya Nair: Integration tests show intermittent flakiness with test CMK in the CI matrix; suggest an integration-only retry wrapper.
Maya Chen: Added retry wrapper with jitter to integration KMS calls and a test-only deterministic stub in CI to stabilize builds.
Introduces opt-in temporal RBAC grants with cryptographic attestation and a reversible audit blinding shim. Admins can use temporal grants for short-lived operator elevation; blinded audit streams protect sensitive fields while sealed audit vaults retain rehydration capability under strict approval. Feature gated behind security.temporal_attested_rbac.

payload.body:
Context: We observed recurring multi-tenant incidents where the KV cache produced high spill IO bursts caused by fragmentation hotspots and synchronized eviction windows. Existing heuristics performed global eviction and coarse-grained compaction which either caused noisy neighbor spill or left cold fragments that never reclaimed. This PR implements a region-aware compaction scheduler plus a spill rationer that smooths asynchronous spill IO and prioritizes tenant-local compaction to reduce cross-tenant interference.

What changed (high level):
- Add region-aware compactor (kv/compactor/region_compactor.{cc,h}) that tracks fragmentation score per region and schedules local compaction jobs during low-util windows.
- Introduce spill rationer (kv/spill/rationer.{cc,h}) to cap instantaneous spill throughput and convert excess spill into delayed background migration when safe.
- Scheduler hooks to prefer in-place defragmentation for regions with high reuse probability; fall back to spill when memory pressure is sustained.
- New config knobs: regional_compaction.enabled, regional_compaction.min_fragment_score, spill_rationer.max_burst_tokens, spill_rationer.delay_backoff_ms.
- Tests and benchmarks: unit tests for fragmentation scoring, e2e perf benchmark harness for synthetic tenant churn, and integration test that validates bounded spill throughput under bursty load.

Design notes / algorithm summary:
- Fragmentation score: a lightweight estimator (region_hotness * free_fragment_ratio * age_weight) computed incrementally during eviction scans to avoid global passes. Regions with score > min_fragment_score are enqueued for compaction.
- Compaction policy: compaction is time-sliced using a metronome to avoid long blocking work. Each slice attempts local object relocation within the region and marks relocated ranges as warm to enable immediate reuse. Compaction retries are backoff-limited per-tenant to avoid starvation.
- Spill rationer: rather than immediate unbounded spill writes when eviction pressure spikes, we quantify a per-region spill budget. If budget is exhausted, candidates are queued and converted to lower-priority background migration tasks or reclaimed with a higher eviction penalty, depending on tenant priority. Burst smoothing uses a token-bucket fed by steady-state IO capacity.

Kernel & scheduling integration:
- Introduced a non-blocking async IO path for spill writes that batches small spill candidates into contiguous write vectors to improve kernel I/O efficiency. This reduced syscall overhead and allowed the rationer to make finer-grained decisions.
- Scheduler now exposes a compaction token pool shared across workers; tokens are consumed by compaction slices and replenished on a fixed cadence to guarantee fairness across tenants and shards.

Benchmarks (cluster-scale synthetic):
- Workload: 20 tenants, 50% working set overlap, randomized churn with periodic allocation spikes.
- Baseline: main branch (no regional compaction / unbounded spill).
- Result: median cross-tenant spill IO decreased by 34%, overall spill write bandwidth down 38% during spikes, p95 request latency under memory pressure improved from 420ms -> 310ms, and average background compaction CPU overhead increased by ~6% (acceptable tradeoff).

Testing & CI:
- Unit tests added for fragmentation scoring and rationer token accounting.
- Integration tests run in perf-lab with isolated SSD-backed nodes; tests assert bounded spill bandwidth and no regressions on cold-start memory use.
- CI note: initial run had a flaky integration test (kv_compaction_integration) failing due to timing assumptions; test updated to use condition-based waits and reran. Final CI: all checks green.

Migration / rollout plan:
- Feature gated off by default: regional_compaction.enabled = false. Turn-on plan: staged rollout to Dedicated clusters first, enabling min_fragment_score conservatively (0.6) and monitoring spill metrics.
- Backwards compatibility: config defaults ensure no impact for clusters not enabling the feature. Spill rationer defaults to permissive (max_burst_tokens = large) to avoid accidental throttling.

Commits (summary):
- 1) kv: add region compactor core and interface (initial scaffolding)
- 2) kv: implement fragmentation score and enqueueing
- 3) kv/spill: add rationer token-bucket and async batching path
- 4) runtime: integrate compaction token pool into scheduler
- 5) tests: unit + integration + perf harness updates
- 6) docs: configuration and rollout notes in ops docs

Files changed (high level):
- kv/compactor/region_compactor.cc (new)
- kv/compactor/region_compactor.h (new)
- kv/spill/rationer.cc (new)
- kv/spill/rationer.h (new)
- runtime/scheduler/compaction_tokens.cc/h (modified)
- tests/kv/fragmentation_score_test.cc (new)
- tests/integration/kv_compaction_integration.cc (modified)
- perf/bench/kv_spill_rationer_bench.py (new)
- docs/ops/kv_compaction.md (new)

Review conversation (condensed):
- Jared Liu: "Nice direction — fragmentation scoring looks lightweight. Can we make the age_weight adaptive based on allocation rate?"
  - Author: "Agreed; added a follow-up TODO to expose age_weight as a dynamic parameter and instrument it in perf runs. Kept default static for this PR to limit scope."
- Priya Menon: "Compaction slices look good, but worried about long-tail CPU when many regions are queued."
  - Author: "Scheduler token pool enforces a hard cap and we added telemetry counters to surface queued region backlog; added a guard to convert oldest queued compaction to a low-priority background migration if backlog > 1000."
- Carlos Alvarez: "Async spill batching kernel changes could interact with OS-level writeback; did you validate on linux with both ext4 and xfs?"
  - Author: "Yes — perf-lab runs included ext4 and xfs profiles; added an opt-in knob to disable write-vector coalescing if a particular filesystem shows regressions."
- Jared Liu: "Please add an upgrade note for dedicated clusters and mention default off flag."
  - Author: "Added ops doc and release notes."

CI details: initial run: unit and lint passed; integration failed once due to timing; rerun caused green. Key checks: build (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration (pass after fix), lint (pass), perf-suite (pass in nightly).

Merge: Squash and merge on 2025-09-18 by Priya Menon after approvals from Jared and Carlos.

Follow-ups / TODOs:
- EXP-1: make age_weight adaptive (instrumentation + controller)
- EXP-2: expose per-tenant compaction budgets and RBAC controls for enterprise customers
- EXP-3: run additional perf on larger clusters (100+ tenants) and add automatic heuristics to tune min_fragment_score

Notes for on-call: enable regional_compaction.enabled=false in hotfix builds; to rollback if production regressions occur, remove feature flag or set spill_rationer.max_burst_tokens to a high value.

Related issues: ENG-3421 (multi-tenant spill incidents), SUP-501 (customer reported spikes).
Improves KV cache fragmentation recovery and reduces cross-tenant spill IO by ~30-40% under bursty workloads. Adds regional compaction scheduler and spill rationer config knobs.

payload.body:
Motivation: We observed recurring SLO spikes during rapid regional failovers triggered by transient egress congestion. Root cause analysis showed two contributing factors: (1) the admission controller aggressively replays queued requests during short reconnect windows, and (2) the circuit flip logic reopens too quickly when KV pressure is still settling, causing rapid oscillation and downstream queuing. This PR implements a conservative admission policy ('soft-admit/leanback') and a new stall-mitigation bridge we call 'silk-bridge' to reduce cross-region surge while preserving graceful degradation.

What this PR changes (summary): (a) soft-admit admission controller: instead of immediately draining queued requests after a region rejoin, we apply a configurable linear ramp with jitter to the admitted rate for the first N seconds, driven by observed KV sync progress and per-node token pressure metrics; (b) stall-timer for circuits: introduce a cooldown timer that prevents immediate circuit reopen for a minimum window unless explicit healthy probes pass; (c) silk-bridge fallback: when a region signals persistent KV lag, requests are rerouted to a warm standby region with 'KV-hint' metadata that preserves eventual KV continuity without aggressive replays (best-effort hinting, not a hard migration); (d) telemetry and alerts: new metrics (admission.ramp_pct, silk_bridge.routed, stall_timer.cooldown_seconds) and a lightweight SLO guard that suppresses automated rollouts if 5xx rates increase >2x during the ramp.

Why this is a hotfix: the fix is conservative, low-risk, and addresses an on-call incident (SUP-1984) where customers experienced intermittent latency spikes and retries during a brief multi-zone egress issue. The changes avoid bulk draining and limit cross-region burst amplification.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged by default (feature.silk_bridge.enabled=false). Rollout steps: enable in canary on dedicated-01 for 30m -> monitor admission.ramp_pct and p50/p95 latency for 10m -> enable in regional staging for 1hr with increased telemetry retention -> global enable with slow ramp (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%). If 5xxs or token cost regresses beyond thresholds abort and revert via the flag.

Testing: unit tests for admission ramp and stall timer added; integration harness includes a synthetic egress congestion scenario that validates silk-bridge routing and KV-hint tagging; added a canary test that runs a failover sequence in the perf-lab.

Operational notes: On severe KV lag silk-bridge opts for routing at reduced concurrency (configurable default = 0.25 of normal concurrency) and attaches a header x-silk-bridge:1 to routed requests for downstream observability. There is also an emergency toggle to force immediate drain behavior (feature.admission.immediate_drain=true) for legacy behavior in debugging.

Documentation: Added a short section to the runbooks (internal link: Linear ENG-4217) describing expected telemetry signals and rollback triggers.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration scenario for egress congestion
- [x] Telemetry hooks and alerts
- [x] Feature flag gating
- [x] On-call runbook update

Related: SUP-1984 (support case), ENG-4217 (Linear), and follow-up RFC planned for a more general admission controller rewrite.
Diego Ramos: Nice conservative approach. Two questions: how do we guarantee no request reordering once silk-bridge is used? (author reply below)
Maya Reynolds: Reply: silk-bridge attaches KV-hint metadata; the downstream router treats hints as best-effort and does not surface reordering guarantees. We explicitly document that silk-bridge is a soft fallback and app-level idempotency is still recommended.
Priya Khanna: Please add an explicit test for the cooldown timer preventing reopen during partial KV sync (left a TODO).
Maya Reynolds: Added test in integration-tests and a unit test for stall_timer; expanded comments to describe probe gating.
Liam O'Connor: CI flaked on python lint in first run; reran and green. Approving after green runs.
Diego Ramos: Approved with comments (minor naming nit in controller.go).
Hotfix: conservative admission ramp + stall cooldown timer + silk-bridge soft fallback to reduce SLO spikes during regional failovers. Feature-flagged; off by default.
If you see silk_bridge.routed > 0 and p95 latency regressing: flip feature.silk_bridge.enabled=false and watch admission.ramp_pct go to 0. If circuits are sticky after a failover, check stall_timer.cooldown_seconds and health probe success rate. SUP-1984 runbook updated in runbooks/pg-recovery.md.

Summary: Fix oscillatory reopen behavior after emergency load-shedding and add a guarded, telemetry-driven reopen gate with a transient-mute recovery window. Motivation: During the incident on 2025-10-29 we observed tenants repeatedly flip between shed and active states when the quick-reopen path allowed immediate rejoin; that caused downstream KV pressure spikes and increased tail latency. This patch introduces a controlled reopen gate that enforces a graded thaw interval and a rate-limited reopen token. The gate is governed by two signals: (1) local reopen_quiet_count (per-node counter of successful quiet windows) and (2) cluster-level reopen_budget sampled from recent SLO headroom metrics. Changes: - Implement ReopenGate in serving/runtime: enforces minimum quiet interval, exponential backoff on repeated failures, and a token bucket for reopen attempts. - Add TransientMuteRecovery in router/fallback: tenants moved to transient-mute state are permitted staged reinstate with diminishing concurrency until stability. - Telemetry: new metrics reopen_attempts_allowed, reopen_backoff_state, transient_mute_count and reopen_budget_percent; dashboard panels added. - Tests: unit + integration tests to reproduce fast-flip scenario and assert monotonic backoff. - Ops: rollout is a canary on 2 nodes per region with feature flag reopen_gate.v1; fallback to legacy immediate-reopen on config toggle. Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to canary cluster and monitor reopen_attempts_allowed and transient_mute_count for 48h. 2) If false positives / increased long-tail latency, revert via feature toggle. 3) Gradual ramp to 50% of nodes, then full rollout. Backwards compatibility: config defaults to enabled=false; enable only for SRE supervised rollouts. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration test reproduces flip - [x] Telemetry emitted to metrics backend - [x] Ops runbook updated (ops/reopen-gate-runbook.md) Related: ENG-1198 (post-incident), SRE-451 (runbook).
Marco Ruiz (2025-11-07): Nice narrow hotfix. Two asks: (a) add a metric that counts failed reopen attempts per tenant to help SRE triage; (b) consider a short jitter on the backoff to avoid thundering reopens.
Priya Desai (2025-11-07): Added reopen_failed_attempts metric and jittered backoff implementation (configurable). PTAL.
Elena Park (2025-11-08): Tests look good. One nit: the default enable flag should be false in helm values (I verified it's false). Approved after CI passes.
Samir Khan (2025-11-08): Verified integration reproduction; +1 for merge. Recommend squash merge to keep history clean.
Hotfix: Prevent rapid reopen/evict oscillation by gating tenant reinstates after emergency shedding. Adds guarded reopen gate with telemetry and ops runbook.
Integration harness includes synthetic spike generator that alternates aggressive shedding; verify reopen_attempts_allowed stays below configured token allowance and transient_mute_count stabilizes within 2x baseline.
Flip helm flag reopen_gate.enabled=false and deploy; if issues persist, revert chart to previous release-tag and notify SRE via #incidents.
Dashboard panels: reopen_budget_percent, reopen_backoff_state, reopen_failed_attempts. Alert if reopen_failed_attempts > 100/min for 5m or reopen_budget_percent drops below 10% for >10m. Runbook at ops/reopen-gate-runbook.md.
Low when disabled. When enabled, expect reduced immediate rejoin throughput for tenants recently evicted; overall goal is to lower KV pressure and tail latency at cost of delayed reinstates.
