payload.body:
Context: We continue to see incidents where sudden tenant spikes exhaust warm pools and cause cascading latency SLO violations across dedicated pools. Existing reactive autoscalers and soft-reservation hedges are effective but respond after degradation has already begun. This PR implements a proactive SLA floor controller that maintains a short-term throughput floor for tenants approaching their SLO budget and a cross-pool spillover throttle that enforces graded backpressure when a tenant would otherwise cause systemic headroom collapse. Motivation: reduce tail latency incidents and improve availability by combining predictive signals with conservative reserved bandwidth. Design summary: 1) SLA Floor Controller: monitors per-tenant short-window utilization (1s/10s/1m histograms) and predictive classifier output; when a tenant is predicted to spike beyond its active headroom, the controller pins a transient throughput floor (tokenized micro-reservations) to a pool or warmlet set for the duration of the spike window. Floors are sized based on recent percentile throughput and an operator-configurable safety multiplier. 2) Predictive Workload Classifier: lightweight online model (feature set: req/sec trend, kv-cache hit ratio, mean token length, recent p50/p95 latency deltas) that emits a 30s spike-likelihood score. The classifier runs in the serving control plane and is intentionally conservative to avoid false positives. 3) Cross-Pool Spillover Throttle: when a tenant's projected demand would exceed remaining headroom across all pools, the throttle introduces a graded backpressure token that reduces enqueue priority or routes additional requests to an overflow path (degraded model variant or lower-cost pool) based on tenant tier. 4) Telemetry and Auditing: new utilization exporter exposes winsorized percentile metrics (p50/p90/p95/p99) over multiple windows (10s/1m/5m) and an event trail for reactive investigations. Implementation notes: - Controller implemented in orchestration/autoscaler/sla_floor_controller.go with unit tests and integration harness - Classifier implemented as a pluggable function in autoscaler/predictive/online_classifier.go; default is rule-based logistic estimator, with a simple feature normalizer. - Throttle implemented in routing/spillover_throttle.go with backward-compatible policy interface; existing routing fallbacks remain intact. - Telemetry exporter added under observability/exporters/tenant_util_percentiles.go; adds a new metrics namespace redwood.dedicated.utilization.percentiles. Checklist: - [x] Spec doc in Linear: ENG-4821 - [x] Unit tests for controller and throttle - [x] Integration tests in perf-canary with synthetic spike scenarios - [x] Backwards compatibility preserved (default feature flag off) - [x] Docs update draft in redwood-docs (link below) Testing and results: - Ran perf canary with three synthetic tenants (steady, bursty, noizy) across two pools. Compared baseline (no proactive floor) vs this branch. Observed 72% reduction in p99 latency spikes for non-noisy tenants during noisy tenant bursts, and 18% lower warm-pool churn. CPU overhead of classifier + controller ~2.3% at 10k rps. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout by customer cohort; enable in internal staging for 48h, gradual ramp to 10% of dedicated customers, then 50% over 72h, monitor p99 latency and warm-pool replenishment. Ops knobs: sla_floor.watermark (percentile basis), sla_floor.safety_multiplier, spillover.throttle_granularity, predictive.classifier_threshold. Backwards compatibility: all routing fallbacks and autoscaler behaviors preserved unless the feature flag is enabled. Security and cost: no new secrets. Slight additional control-plane CPU cost; no notable GPU or per-request cost. Documentation: draft changes in sources/github/redwood-docs/docs/dedicated/sla-floor.md and runbook in ops/playbooks/sla-floor-runbook.md Related: ENG-4890 (investigate headroom collapse), SUP-1287 (customer incident postmortem).
Introduce proactive SLA floor controller to guarantee per-tenant throughput floors and a cross-pool spillover throttle that prevents noisy tenants from causing headroom collapse. Adds predictive workload classifier and new utilization exporter with percentile windows.
Rohan Patel: Nice approach — can you clarify how we size floors when tenant history is sparse?
Maya Chen (author): We use a damped estimator that falls back to cluster median and a conservative multiplier; doc updated with formula and tests to cover sparse-history path.
Grace Lee: The classifier looks good but we should avoid DDoS amplification. Add a hard cap on pin duration and token count.
Maya Chen (author): Added hard caps (config: sla_floor.max_duration, sla_floor.max_tokens) and unit tests covering caps.
Omar Ruiz: Telemetry naming collides slightly with existing percentiles. Please use winsorized/prefix and add migration notes.
Maya Chen (author): Renamed metric namespace to redwood.dedicated.utilization.percentiles and added migration note in observability/UPGRADING.md.
Grace Lee: Integration numbers look promising. Approving pending CI green.
CI bot: All checks passed on rerun. Approving and ready to merge.
Repo maintainer (Julian Park): Squash-merged after resolving minor docs nits.

payload.body: Motivation: reduce long-tail memory fragmentation and noisy-evictions in the KV cache under mixed-size keys/values workloads while avoiding large synchronous spill events. This PR implements a compact buddy-style slab allocator tuned for KV cache objects, an eviction-probing layer that prioritizes low-cost candidate eviction candidates by occupancy and live-score, and a spillback attenuation controller to soften tenant-induced burst spillovers. Key goals: reduce fragmentation, lower p99 eviction latency, and reduce peak disk spill events during traffic spikes. What changed: 1) allocator: introduce src/kv/buddy_allocator.rs implementing a lock-sharded buddy allocator over existing slab segments with coalescing and split hints driven by live occupancy histograms; 2) fragile-score: add a per-page fragmentation scoring heuristic and per-tenant decay window to bias reclaim toward high-frag pages; 3) eviction-probe: new evictor stage that probes short-lived candidate objects using a lightweight LRU-probe path before taking heavy-weight writeback/spill actions; 4) spillback-attenuator: rate-limiter that applies adaptive backpressure to tenants that trigger repeated spill rounds within a short window; 5) observability: new metrics (kv.buddy.alloc_latency_ms, kv.frag_score, kv.evict_probe_hit_ratio, kv.spillback_rate_limiter_actions) and dashboard updates; 6) tests and benchmarks: unit tests for allocator invariants, integration test for spillback attenuation under synthetic churn, and a microbench harness that reproduces production-like size distributions. Performance summary: in CI microbench and internal canary runs we see median allocation latency stable (~20us), 99th allocation latency reduced by ~2.1x vs previous slab strategy for mixed-size workloads, p99 eviction latency improved by ~1.8x, and peak disk spill events dropped by ~35% on a tenant-heavy replay. Risk and rollout: new components are guarded by runtime feature flags (BUDDY_ALLOCATOR, EVICT_PROBE, SPILLBACK_ATTEN). Default remains legacy allocator for safety. Rollout plan: enable for 10% traffic in canary ring, collect frag_score and probe metrics for two weeks, increase to 50% and 100% if no regressions. Backwards compatibility: no wire/API changes. Feature flags can be toggled per-tenant. Related: follows up on ENG-1209 and complements the async spillover controller work. Checklists: - [x] allocator implementation and unit tests - [x] eviction-probe implementation and integration test - [x] spillback attenuation controller and integration test - [x] metrics and dashboards - [x] benchmark harness - [x] doc: design writeup and rollout notes Links: design doc: docs/design/buddy_allocator_design.md. Commits summary: - Implement buddy allocator core and sharded freelist + tests (commit: maya/buddy/core) - Add fragmentation scorer and occupancy histogram integration (commit: maya/buddy/frag-score) - Introduce eviction-probing stage and integrate with existing evictor pipeline (commit: maya/evict/probe) - Add spillback-attenuator, feature flags, metrics and dashboards (commit: maya/spill/attenuator) - Fix race in freelist reclaim and CI test flakiness (commit: maya/buddy/fix-reclaim) Changed files (high level): ["src/kv/buddy_allocator.rs","src/kv/evictor.rs","src/kv/frag_score.rs","src/kv/spillback_attenuator.rs","src/kv/mod.rs","docs/design/buddy_allocator_design.md","docs/runbooks/spillback_debug.md","tests/kv/allocator_unit_tests.rs","tests/kv/evict_probe_integration.rs","bench/microbench/alloc_bench.rs","dashboard/kv_buddy_overview.json","pkg/feature_flags/flags.yaml","Cargo.toml"]. Review conversation: - Arjun Patel (reviewer): "Can you explain how we avoid increased lock contention under high concurrency? The sharded buckets help but I'm worried about corner cases with split/coalesce under contention." - Maya (author): "We use 64 lock shards by default and try-lock in the fast path; split/coalesce use an epoch-based defer queue to avoid holding global locks. I added a microbench that simulates 10k concurrent alloc/free and the allocation latency remained bounded. See bench/microbench/alloc_bench.rs results attached in the PR CI artifacts." - Liam O'Connor (reviewer): "Please add a stress test that injects pathological sequences to ensure we don't regress memory accounting for tenants." - Maya (author): "Added tests/kv/allocator_unit_tests.rs with randomized sequence harness and accounting assertions; also added extra asserts behind a nightly-only cfg to avoid perf impact in release runs." - Sofia Alvarez (approver): "Verified canary telemetry for frag_score and evict_probe_hit_ratio in staging; approves for gradual rollout. Left a minor nit on log wording." CI summary and iteration: - Initial CI run: failed unit test due to race in freelist reclaim; author pushed fix in commit maya/buddy/fix-reclaim - Second CI run: all checks passed (unit tests, integration tests, lint, cargo fmt, bench smoke) - Canary run: enabled BUDDY_ALLOCATOR for 10% of traffic in canary cluster; telemetry collected for two weeks with expected improvements; one tenant hit repeated spillback events, attenuator reduced spill rate successfully and an ops runbook was added. Merge: squash-and-merge. Merge commit message: "Introduce buddy allocator, eviction-probe, spillback attenuation; add metrics and rollout plan (ENG-1209)" Release notes: ["Introduce experimental buddy-style allocator for KV cache to reduce fragmentation and p99 allocation latency.","Add eviction-probing to prioritize low-cost evictions and reduce heavy-weight spill events.","Add spillback attenuation to smooth tenant-induced spillovers; guarded by runtime feature flags.","Metrics: kv.buddy.alloc_latency_ms, kv.frag_score, kv.evict_probe_hit_ratio, kv.spillback_rate_limiter_actions."] Additional notes: - Feature flags are toggled via pkg/feature_flags/flags.yaml and documented in docs/runbooks/spillback_debug.md. - The design doc contains detailed failure modes and migration steps. - Observability owners: @sre-team to monitor kv.frag_score and kv.spillback_rate_limiter_actions for first 30 days post-rollout.
payload.title: Introduce buddy-cache allocator with eviction-probing and spillback attenuation

payload.body:
Summary: This hotfix introduces a staged egress-trim safety-net and a 'degrade-safe-state' transition path for regions experiencing outgoing egress saturation. Motivation: during a recent regional egress saturation incident, abrupt circuit opens and aggressive tenant eviction caused downstream cache thrash and customer-visible 5xxs. The goal here is to provide a controlled, observable step-down that (1) trims outbound egress bandwidth gradually for lower-priority routes, (2) transitions affected nodes into a degrade-safe-state with constrained ingress admission and widened timeouts, and (3) avoid hard circuit flips by adding a short probation window and metric-anchored rollback. This PR is intentionally conservative: it implements a safety-net with conservative defaults and feature gates so we can enable/disable without full rollout.

Design & changes: - egress_trim controller (src/runtime/egress_controller.rs): new staged policy that accepts a priority-weighted trim plan and applies token-bucket caps to outbound egress per-route and per-tenant. It uses the existing scheduler hooks to avoid interfering with serving fast-path. - slo_manager (src/controlplane/slo_manager.go): adds SLO-derived triggers to recommend staged trims and to enter degrade-safe-state. SLO thresholds are evaluated on a 30s rolling window and include latency and error-rate margins. - degrade-safe-state (pkg/serving/degrade_safe.go): implements a lightweight state machine for nodes to reduce admission rates, increase internal request timeouts, and enable KV-preserve fastpath. State is reversible on stable telemetry. - telemetry and tracing (observability/egress_trim_dashboards.yaml + proto changes): added new metrics: egress_trim_applied, degrade_safe_entry, degrade_safe_exit, staged_trim_progress. Also added a structured trace annotation for decisions. - tests: unit tests for staged trim scheduling and an integration harness (tests/integration/egress_trim_simulator) that simulates regional egress saturation and validates no more than 2x customer-visible error amplification compared to baseline.

Rollout plan: feature gate off by default. Canary flow: enable in single non-critical region for 1% traffic, observe metrics 6h, increase to 10% then 50% as telemetry looks stable. Motivation: Production canaries today fail hard when a transient infra or metric anomaly triggers an automatic rollback. For stateful model swaps (session-affine routing, KV cache warmup) that leads to repeated costly warmups and poor user experience. This PR implements a resumable, checkpointed canary primitive that: (1) snapshots canary state (traffic assignment, KV cache warmups, small replay buffer) at stable points, (2) assigns time-bound traffic leases to cohorts so traffic ownership can be recovered or extended, and (3) evaluates canaries relative to metric anchors (baseline reference metrics) instead of absolute thresholds. Together these reduce unnecessary rollbacks and allow safe rewind/retry without full cold restarts.

What this PR delivers: single coherent implementation across the rollout controller and serving runtime that includes: - Checkpoint creation and storage hooks (controller side) for canary stages, with retention policy and compact delta format. - Traffic lease mechanism: tokenized lease metadata attached to cohort routes; leases are renew/evict aware and surface in the console. - Metric anchors: declarative baseline anchors you can pin per rollout (latency P95, error rate baseline, quality eval score). Anchors are used by the safety gates and reported in rollout traces. - Resume/rewind operator: when a canary fails transiently, operators can resume from a checkpoint and reassign traffic via lease transfer instead of full swap. - API + CLI additions: rollout.resume, rollout.checkpoint-list, rollout.pin-anchor. - Migration path: older rollout specs are backward compatible; new fields are optional.

Design notes (short): - Checkpoints are lightweight tar+manifest stored in internal objectstore (S3/GCS) with TTL. - Lease tokens encode cohort id, expiry, and a monotonically increasing epoch used by serving plane to avoid split-brain. - Anchors are stored as name->metric mapping; evaluation uses relative-delta scoring and a configurable conservatism factor. - Safety: resume paths require an explicit operator action (no automatic resume) unless CanaryPolicy.allow_auto_resume is set. Resume includes an idempotent verification step: recheck anchored metrics against a short shadow window before opening live traffic.

Backward compatibility and rollout rule changes: - Existing rollout specs remain valid. - New fields: .spec.checkpoints.enabled (bool), .spec.traffic.lease_ttl (duration), .spec.anchors[]. These default to safe values (checkpoints: false, lease_ttl: 0 meaning no lease, anchors: empty). - Default controller behavior unchanged until a rollout opts in.

Testing and evaluation: - Unit tests for checkpoint manifest serialization, lease token verification, anchor scoring (added ~45 new tests). - E2E canary smoke harness extended to simulated transient infra failures to validate resume reduces full cold restarts. - Local perf tests show checkpoint creation cost ~120ms for a typical model bundle snapshot, and resume path reduces warm-start latency by ~2.3x on average in our lab workloads.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc (linked in PR) and linear tickets referenced - [x] Controller implementation and unit tests - [x] Serving runtime hook to honor lease epochs - [x] Console UI hooks (staged; feature flag gated) - [x] CLI commands for ops - [x] Migration notes and docs update - [x] Observability: rollout traces, checkpoint metrics, lease renew/expire events

Commits (high-level): - feat(controller): checkpoint manager and TTL retention - feat(serve): honor traffic lease epochs and expose lease debug endpoint - feat(ui): checkpoint/lease controls behind feature flag - feat(cli): rollout.resume and rollout.checkpoint-list - fix(tests): stabilize anchor scoring unit tests - docs: rollout spec examples and migration guide

Files changed (high-level): ["controller/pkg/checkpoint/manager.go", "controller/api/v1/rollout_types.go", "serve/lease/handler.go", "serve/lease/protocol.md", "cli/rollout_resume.go", "ui/src/components/CheckpointPanel.tsx", "docs/rollouts/checkpointing.md", "tests/e2e/canary_resume_test.go", "observability/rollout_metrics.prom", "Makefile", "go.mod", "package.json" ]

Serving plane verifies epoch monotonicity and rejects lower-epoch reassignment. I added a note in serve/lease/protocol.md and an extra unit test simulating leader change." - Lina Chen (2026-01-20): "Suggest we expose checkpoint size and creation latency to the console; ops will need that when planning resume windows." - Author (2026-01-21): "Added checkpoint.size_bytes and checkpoint.create_ms metrics and wired to rollout traces." - Jordan Reyes (2026-01-24): "One CI flake on canary_resume_test.go due to a timing assumption; recommend increasing timeout with a comment." - Author (2026-01-25): "Fixed timing and annotated test to avoid future flakes. Reran CI."

payload.body:
Context: We frequently tune batching, cache and quantization defaults to reduce per-token costs, but changes that improve unit economics can sometimes surface subtle quality regressions or unexpected latency spikes for small tenant segments. This PR introduces an end-to-end operational playbook plus a lightweight CLI evaluator (costctl) to safely propose cost optimizations and perform staged, observable rollouts with automatic rollback triggers.

What this PR adds (high level):
- costctl evaluate --dry-run: simulates the application of a set of candidate changes (batch size, cache TTLs, quant profiles) against historical traces and returns estimated unit-econ deltas and risk signals (quality-regression score, tail-latency delta, token-saved estimate). The evaluator runs a fast deterministic simulation using the existing replay harness (sampling-based) and a new lightweight scoring function that flags risky changes.
- Playbook primitives: a JSON/YAML playbook format (playbooks/cost-fallback-v1.yaml) that encodes staged rollout steps: shadow-canary -> 5% canary -> 25% ramp -> full rollout, with configurable rollback signals and observed-metrics thresholds.
- Canary shadowing mode in serving runtime: a non-intrusive shadow path that computes responses from the candidate model/config but does not affect caller latency; it reports divergence traces and a compact regression fingerprint to telemetry for post-hoc analysis.
- Auto-rollback engine: a controller that monitors chosen SLOs (quality regressions, p99 latency, error-rate) and automatically reverts an in-flight rollout if thresholds are crossed. The engine supports automatic mitigation options: throttle back to previous batch/cache settings, revert quant profile, or pause rollout.
- Observability surface: dashboards and telemetry tags to show simulated vs observed unit-econ, divergence counts, regression fingerprints, and rollout state transitions. Also emits compact audit events for compliance.

Why this is different: previous PRs focused on generating recommended defaults. This work is operational: it safely closes the loop—simulate, stage, observe, and rollback—so teams can evaluate and apply cost improvements with bounded risk. The emphasis is on predictable, automated rollback behavior and an auditable evaluation path.

Implementation notes:
- costctl was added as a small Go binary (cmd/costctl) that orchestrates trace replay (using replay/sampler) and hits the new evaluator service (pkg/evaluator). The binary supports --dry-run and --apply (apply currently requires feature flag and elevated RBAC).
- The evaluator uses a deterministic sampling policy and a new scoring heuristic (pkg/evaluator/score.go) that combines: estimated token-savings, model-response divergence fingerprint (hash of structured fields), and synthetic latency delta computed from per-token kernel predictions. The heuristic weights are tunable via feature flags.
- The runtime changes include a shadowing hook (runtime/shadow.go) and a lightweight divergence recorder (telemetry/divergence_v1.proto) that attaches fingerprints without recording full responses.
- Playbook definitions live under playbooks/ and are validated during CI.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for evaluator scoring (pkg/evaluator/score_test.go) and playbook validation.
- Integration tests: simulator integration test that runs costctl evaluate --dry-run on archived traces (ci/traces/sample-2026-01.json.gz) and asserts estimates are consistent within a tolerance.
- Staging rollout: deployed to staging cluster for 48h with synthetic traffic; we ran three simulated canary rollouts and verified auto-rollback triggers on an injected regression (added in integration test harness).

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flag gated in main.
2) Enable costctl evaluate --dry-run for platform/infra users.
3) After 2 weeks of observational use and no false positives, enable apply for limited SRE users.
4) Gradual enable for product teams; monitor metrics and cadence.

Risks and mitigations:
- False negatives: simulator might miss rare divergence patterns. Mitigation: conservative defaults for rollout thresholds; require at least one human review for high-risk changes.
- Telemetry volume: divergence fingerprints are compact (single 64-bit hash + counters) and emitted at low sampling rate by default.
- Security: apply path requires RBAC and audit logging.

Files changed summary: modified runtime to add shadow hooks; added costctl; playbooks and tests; dashboards and migration for telemetry fields.

Related work: ENG-2001 (cost-sandboxing), ENG-2042 (batching defaults CI harness).

Notes for reviewers: please pay attention to the divergence fingerprint format and the default thresholds in playbooks/cost-fallback-v1.yaml. I intentionally chose conservative defaults to reduce blast radius for initial deployment.
Lena Ortiz: Nice end-to-end. Two nits: 1) Can we make the fingerprint algorithm explicit (xxhash64?) and 2) add a config toggle for sampling rate in telemetry?
Author (Marco): Reply: switched to xxhash64 and exposed sampling_rate flag in telemetry config. Updated tests accordingly.
Hiro Tanaka: The auto-rollback thresholds seem aggressive for p99 on multi-tenant noisy services. Suggest bumping the p99 delta threshold and require two consecutive evaluation windows before rollback.
Author (Marco): Agree, implemented hysteresis (two windows) and bumped defaults. Added an env var to tune behavior per-cluster.
Priya Desai: Integration tests are solid. One request: document RBAC for apply path in README.costctl.md.
Author (Marco): Added RBAC section to README.costctl.md and auth/rbac_rules.yml.
Introduces costctl dry-run evaluator, staged rollout playbook primitives and an auto-rollback controller to safely apply batching/cache/quant changes. Feature gated and initially conservative; see docs/operational/cost_playbook.md for usage.

payload.body:
Motivation: We observed several incidents where tenant KMS-related requests bypassed intended residency and tagging constraints because of malformed or missing KMS metadata. Additionally, audit streams contained duplicated events (retries and multi-hops) which inflate storage and complicate forensic queries. This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) a gateway middleware that validates KMS usage tags (origin, provider, region, tenant_id) against the canonical kms_schema and rejects requests that fail validation, 2) an audit deduplication service that computes a stable hash for incoming audit envelopes, persists an index with short TTL to collapse duplicates and emit a single canonical event for downstream consumers, and 3) an RBAC "rate-bound" shim that limits high-privilege cross-region role assignments per operator to mitigate blast radius for cross-zone operations.

Design summary: The kms_tag_validator runs early in the gateway request pipeline. It parses the KMS metadata header (x-kms-meta) and validates it against internal policy rules defined in internal/policies/kms_schema.proto. Rules include required keys, allowed region sets per tenant, and provider whitelists. Validation failures return 4xx with structured error payloads pointing to remediation links.

The audit dedupe service is a small idempotency layer in front of our audit buffer. For each incoming envelope, we compute dedupe_hash := SHA256(sorted_headers || payload_digest || kms_proof). The hash is written into a dedupe index table with insertion_ts and ttl (default 2 hours). If a duplicate is detected, the service increments a duplicate counter and drops subsequent writes to the long-term store; a canonical entry is bubbled to downstream subscriptions. The dedupe index is sharded by tenant to avoid cross-tenant collisions.

The RBAC rate-bound shim extends the RBAC v2 evaluator. It adds a configurable per-principal windowed allowance for sensitive operations (e.g., role-grant across regions, kms-provider-switch). The default policy is conservative: max 3 cross-region grants per operator per 24h. The window and thresholds are tenant-configurable via the existing policy manager.

Compatibility & rollout: All changes are behind the feature flag security.kms_tag_validation and a traffic-splitting flag for audit.dedupe. Default flags are OFF. We will enable in the following sequence: 1) enable validator in attr-check mode (log-only) for 48h -> 2) enable hard-reject for a small canary org list -> 3) expand to 20% of traffic -> 4) full enable for hosted tier. RBAC rate-bound is on-by-default for internal operators and rolled out to customers by policy push.

Testing and CI: Added unit tests, integration tests, and an e2e that simulates retried audit envelopes and malformed kms headers. CI initially failed due to a flaky test (tests/e2e/kms-tag-validation.test.js) where the test harness timed out on the first run; we increased the harness timeout and re-ran pipelines. Final CI: all checks passed (lint, unit, integration, e2e, security-scan). See ci/pipelines/security.yml for the security gating steps.

Security review notes: The validator rejects malformed kms metadata which prevents downstream KMS allocators from making unsafe assumptions. We ensured the validator does not leak any secret material in error messages. Audit dedupe keeps only hash and minimal index info in the dedupe table; raw audit payloads continue to be stored (when canonical) and are accessible under existing retention policies. We added an optional KMS-origin proof field that can be used to correlate wrapped-key IDs without revealing plaintext key material.

Migration: Database migration scripts to add dedupe_index table are included as services/audit/dedupe/dedupe_index_schema.sql and are compatible with online deploys. Terraform updates provide IAM bindings needed for the dedupe worker under deploy/helm/values-security.yaml and terraform/modules/kms/main.tf.

Review conversation (abridged):
- Jordan Kim (reviewer): "Can we guarantee that the dedupe hash won't collide across tenants? Sharding helps but callout the salt decision."
  - Author (Anika): "We explicitly prefix the hash with tenant_id and include shard id; added comment and unit test to assert isolation. See commit 'fix: include tenant prefix in dedupe hash'"
- Marcus Feldman: "The RBAC rate-bound default seems strict for some large platform teams. Can we make it configurable per-Tenant (tenant policy override)?"
  - Author: "Yes — policy manager override added; updated docs and feature flag description. We ship with a conservative default and document how to opt-up via policy push."
- Priya Nair: "Please ensure errors from the gateway validator include remediation links and do not contain KMS ARNs or secrets."
  - Author: "Removed ARN echoing and added remediation links to error schema. Added an integration test to assert no ARN present in error messages."
- Marcus: "Approve after minor docs nit"
- Jordan: "Approve"

Merge and post-merge: After approvals we squashed and merged. Post-merge tasks: monitor metrics 'security.kms_validator.reject_rate' and 'audit.dedupe.duplicate_rate' for the first 72h. An automatic rollback playbook is included in scripts/rollout/kms-tag-gate-rollout.sh.

Related: ENG-7823 (policy schema), SEC-412 (audit hardening), OPS-119 (rollout automation).

Context and motivation: We need a lightweight runtime-side rules engine to apply tenant cost policies (budget caps, preferred quant tiers, cache retention hints) close to the routing layer. Existing heuristics are scattered across scheduler/optimizer and CLI tooling, making rollout and observability slow. This PR introduces 'cost-fabricator', a small deterministic rules engine plus a 'quant-telemetry-adapter' that surfaces quantization efficacy signals (token-savings vs. quality delta) into the rules evaluation path so routing and fallback decisions can be made with direct telemetry.

What this PR does (high level): - New cost-fabricator service module (runtime/rules): evaluation DAG, templated policy language, safe-evaluation sandbox. - Quant telemetry adapter (telemetry/quant_adapter): aggregates per-model quant metrics (accuracy delta, token savings, failed-degradation-rate) and exposes a compact score. - Router integration: routing/policy layer can now call cost-fabricator.evaluate(tenant_id, workload_signature) synchronously (<=2ms p50) to get action suggestions: prefer_batch_profile, cache_ttl_hint, quant_tier_hint, fallback_model_set. - Defaults: introduces conservative tenant defaults and a tenant-overrides table stored in config store. - Tests: unit + integration harness that runs synthetic tenant policies against the routing simulator.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-2031) - [x] Rules engine core + evaluator - [x] Quant telemetry adapter + ingestion path - [x] Router integration + small synchronous API - [x] Unit tests and integration tests in sim harness - [x] Telemetry metrics and dashboard panels (ops) - [x] Backwards compatible defaults and migration notes

Commits (summary): - c1: initial rules-engine scaffolding and evaluation DSL - c2: add policy templates and tenant override plumbing - c3: quant telemetry adapter and ingestion consumer - c4: router integration and synchronous evaluation API - c5: tests + sim harness updates - c6: metrics, dashboards, and docs updates

Files changed (high-level): - runtime/rules/engine.py (new) - runtime/rules/dsl.md (new) - runtime/rules/tenants.py (new) - telemetry/quant_adapter/consumer.py (new) - telemetry/quant_adapter/score.py (new) - router/policy_integration.py (modified) - config/tenant_defaults.yaml (modified) - sim/smoke/policy_sim.py (modified) - tests/unit/test_rules_engine.py (new) - tests/integration/test_router_evaluate.py (new) - docs/ops/cost_fabricator.md (new) - dashboards/cost_fabricator.jsonnet (new) - infra/helm/values-cost-fabricator.yaml (new) - ci/pipeline/cost-fabricator-tests.yml (new)

Patch highlights and rationale: - Evaluation DSL: intentionally small (only logical operators, numeric threshold, and simple time-window aggregation) to keep evaluation deterministic and auditable. We avoid Turing-complete constructs to make rollout safe. - Quant score: a single float in [-1,1] where negative indicates quality regressions outweigh savings; positive favors more aggressive quant tiers. The score logic is pluggable for future ML-derived heuristics. - Synchronous API: kept sub-2ms by caching compiled policies and pre-warming tenant overrides in memory; we added metrics to monitor tail latency.

Review conversation (abridged, chronological): - Diego Alvarez (2026-02-17): "Nice direction. Can you add e2e test for a tenant with a tight budget that forces fallback to smaller batch sizes? Also please call out expected memory impact of keeping compiled policies in-process." - Priya Malhotra (2026-02-18): "Added sim test and documented memory footprint (~1.2MB per tenant policy compiled). Will add monitoring alert to catch growth." - Marta Nguyen (2026-02-20): "Lgtm but unit tests flaked in CI on windows runner, looks like path normalization in the sim harness. Please make path handling OS-agnostic." - Priya Malhotra (2026-02-21): "Fixed path normalization and re-ran tests. Added a small fixture to simulate Windows-style paths." - Liam O'Connor (2026-02-24): "A few nit: rename 'prefer_batch_profile' -> 'batch_profile_hint' for clarity; also add an integration test where quant adapter reports a transient spike in degradation and ensure router respects fallback policy." - Priya Malhotra (2026-02-25): "Renamed field and added integration test. Also implemented exponential backoff in fallback decisions to avoid oscillation." - CI run (2026-02-26): first run failed (flake in tests/integration/test_router_evaluate.py due to timing). Re-ran; second run passed (2026-02-27).

CI summary: - Unit tests: pass - Integration tests: pass (after fix) - Lint: pass - Typecheck: pass - Benchmark: small regressions noted in canary runs (p99 latency +0.6ms) — accepted after perf review because decision path remains within SLO and optimizations scheduled (ENG-2109).

Performance and safety considerations: - We added a new low-timeout synchronous path; measured medians are ~0.9ms, p95 under 2.5ms. We introduced a configurable circuit-breaker: if cost-fabricator latency exceeds 10ms or error rate >1%, router falls back to safe default policy. - Default conservative rules ensure no tenant suddenly opts into aggressive quant without explicit override and telemetry-confirmation. - We limit the size of compiled policies and enforce a max-clauses guard to prevent runaway policies.

Deployment plan: - stage: deploy to staging small cluster with feature flag 'cost_fabricator:v1' enabled for 5 canary tenants - monitor metrics/dashboards for latency and unit economics delta - after 48h and manual sign-off, enable for more tenants with progressive ramp - add rollout notes to release docs

Post-merge follow-ups (tracked in ENG-2109): - Add a feedback loop to promote quant tiers automatically after N successful requests - Explore ML-based scoring for quant_adapter (keeps pluggable) - Tighten bench perf: inline simple policies and reduce p99 by ~0.4ms

Notes for reviewers: The rules DSL intentionally keeps expressivity low for auditability. The quant adapter aggregates model-reported metrics and is deliberately conservative when producing positive scores. If we want to expand rules, we should add authorizations and review gates.

Context: Customers running private deployments have asked for a lightweight operator-level guard that prevents accidental cross-region KMS usage for operator-initiated actions (deploys, migrations, emergency keys) while improving audit granularity for residency-sensitive requests. This PR implements an operator geo-safeguard: a decision-time KMS binding gate that enforces operator locality constraints and an audit fanout path that stamps and forwards residency evidence to the audit pipeline.

Goals: 1) Reject operator-scoped KMS operations that violate configured geo-policies; 2) Emit compact residency evidence and immutable audit headers for downstream compliance systems; 3) Provide an opt-in shadow mode and safe rollout path for Dedicated/Private installs.

Summary of changes (single-line checklist): - [x] Add operator KMS binding evaluation middleware; - [x] Emit residency_evidence header and signed audit envelope for operator events; - [x] Shadow-rollout flag and CLI toggle; - [x] Unit + integration tests for decision paths; - [x] Docs updates (runbook + config examples); - [x] Telemetry (decision counters, rejection metrics).

Why this is different: Existing residency enforcement lives at request-level in the ingress. Operator actions are often initiated from the control-plane and use separate credentials; they historically bypass certain residency checks. This PR closes that gap by introducing a compact evaluation layer inside the operator service and re-using the policy decision engine (RBACv2 adapter) with operator-scoped constraints. It also fans out a signed audit envelope to the audit collector so compliance consumers can reconcile operator actions with tenant residency claims.

Rolling plan: feature flag "operator_geo_safeguard" defaults to shadow mode. After 2 weeks of shadow metrics and no false positives in staging, flip to enforce in Dedicated/private customer channels.
Diego Marquez (2026-01-12): Can we clarify how operator credentials are distinguished from user requests in the policy adapter? I see a tenancy claim is used but we should ensure there is no Privilege Escalation path.
Asha Rao (2026-01-13): The signed envelope payload is large — did we consider compressing the evidence or sending a reference blob? Could be important for high-throughput operator events.
Evan Chen (2026-01-14): Integration tests are great. I hit a flaky test on the CI run related to timing of the fanout retries — marking as a required followup to stabilize.
Security SME (2026-01-15): Suggest adding an MTLs guard when contacting external KMS providers in Private installs. Also ensure HSM/KMS provenance is included in the envelope.
Compliance (2026-01-16): Requesting example policy configs for EU vs non-EU tenants in the docs before enabling enforce mode for customers.
Maya Patel (2026-01-12): Diego — thanks, added explicit operator_claim handling and a negative test asserting no user-scope escalation. policy_adapter.go now rejects any request without operator_service:true in the caller_claims.
Maya Patel (2026-01-13): Asha — we added envelope compression (gzip) for high-rate paths and switched fanout to reference-mode for >8kb payloads; details in fanout_transport.go and docs.
Maya Patel (2026-01-14): Evan — increased retry backoff and added jitter to integration harness; CI flaky test re-ran and passed on second attempt. Marked stabilization ticket ENG-4890.
Maya Patel (2026-01-15): Security SME — added optional mTLS enforcement config and included kms_provenance in the signed envelope. See infra/config/operator_geo_safeguard.yaml.
Maya Patel (2026-01-16): Compliance — added two example policy snippets in docs/config-examples/geo-safeguard.yml for EU and non-EU tenants; also included suggested rollout notes.
Operator geo-safeguard: Adds an opt-in operator-level KMS binding gate that enforces geo residency for operator-initiated actions and emits signed residency evidence to the audit pipeline. Feature flag 'operator_geo_safeguard' defaults to shadow mode; see runbook for rollout steps.

Context: Dedicated customers are requesting explicit contractual guardrails on autoscaling to (a) cap spend and (b) ensure a baseline. This PR implements hard min/max enforcement inside the dedicated autoscaler control loop. The key behavior change is that the autoscaler always clamps computed desired replicas to customer-configured bounds (when enabled), and emits metrics/log fields that make the clamp visible (requested_desired vs bounded_desired + reason). This is intended to be deterministic and auditable, and to be safe under conflicting reactive/predictive inputs (prediction work is in a separate PR).

What changed: 1) Clamp desired replicas in the core reconcile loop: desired_raw = max(recommendations) (reactive signals), then desired_bounded = clamp(desired_raw, min_replicas, max_replicas). If bounds are not configured (or feature flag is off), behavior is unchanged. 2) Emit bound-hit metrics: - dedicated.autoscaler.desired_replicas (gauge, value=desired_raw) - dedicated.autoscaler.bounded_desired_replicas (gauge, value=desired_bounded) - dedicated.autoscaler.bound_hit_total (counter, labels: bound=min|max, reason=safety|customer_bound, deployment_id, region) - dedicated.autoscaler.bound_saturation (gauge 0/1 when desired_raw > max or desired_raw < min) Also includes structured log fields: scaling_policy_version, desired_raw, desired_bounded, clamp_reason. 3) Add unit + integration tests for edge cases: min > max validation is handled upstream, but autoscaler treats it as invalid and falls back to previous effective policy; max=0 is rejected; clamp behavior for desired_raw below min and above max; cooldown interactions (ensure clamp doesn’t bypass scale-down cooldown); missing policy (nil) is no-op.

Rollout notes: Bound enforcement is gated by account/deployment feature flag (DedicatedAutoscalingBounds). Metrics are emitted regardless of clamp activation, but with clamp_reason=disabled when the feature is off to simplify dashboard wiring.

Risk: The main risk is confusing operators/customers when the platform “wants” to scale but is capped by max. Metrics added here should make this visible and alertable (follow-up alert rules in observability-pack).

Testing: - Unit tests: autoscaler clamp logic, bound-hit counter increments, deterministic reason strings - Integration tests: simulated queue-depth spike, verify desired_raw vs desired_bounded and that fleet provisioning requests never exceed max - Load sim (local): replay of a ramp trace to ensure no oscillation introduced by clamping

Follow-ups: - Predictive signal integration + staleness fallback (ENG-22142) - Console UI surfaces bound-hit state + audit trail (ENG-22144/ENG-22146) - Alerts for max-bound saturation + queue buildup (ENG-22145)

Screenshots: N/A (backend only)

Release note: Internal only; customer-facing docs land with Console/API changes.
Vanessa Ortiz: Can we ensure this is a hard invariant even if future predictive code proposes something outside bounds? Please add a comment at the clamp site that bounds must be applied last, after arbitration.

Keiko Yamamoto: Added a comment + refactored to make clamp the final step before issuing provisioning requests (decision.go).

Jordan Lee: Two concerns: (1) reason strings should be stable (auditability) and (2) avoid high-cardinality metrics. deployment_id label on counters is probably too hot.

Keiko Yamamoto: (1) Introduced ClampReason enum with fixed values: min_bound, max_bound, disabled, invalid_policy. (2) For bound_hit_total, keeping deployment_id but behind an allowlist gate (only when dedicated.autoscaler.metrics.high_cardinality=true). Default is off; we still log deployment_id in structured logs. Added note to docs/internal/metrics.

Allison Grant: Naming: prefer dedicated.autoscaler.bound_hit_total with labels bound=min|max and clamp_reason=<enum>. Also please add a gauge that can be used in dashboards without counters (e.g., bound_saturation 0/1).

Keiko Yamamoto: Updated per suggestion; added bound_saturation gauge and ensured gauges are emitted every reconcile tick.

Miles Thornton: What happens if policy is temporarily unavailable from control plane? I want no behavior changes and no accidental scale-to-zero.

Keiko Yamamoto: If policy fetch fails or returns nil, we skip clamp and proceed with existing behavior; also added an integration test to assert we never request <1 replicas when deployment is active and min is unset.

Vanessa Ortiz: LGTM once you add a test for desired_raw below min under scale-down cooldown (should still respect cooldown, but bounded result should not violate min).

Keiko Yamamoto: Added test: when cooldown blocks scale-down, desired_bounded remains at current replicas but never below min.

Approvals: Vanessa Ortiz approved; Jordan Lee approved; Allison Grant approved; Miles Thornton approved.
Dedicated autoscaler now supports hard min/max replica bounds (feature-flagged).
Emits desired_raw vs desired_bounded metrics and bound-hit counters for observability.
payload.title: Dedicated autoscaler: hard-enforce min/max bounds + emit bound-hit metrics

payload.body:
Summary: This PR adds a first-class control-plane config surface for defining which models the perf-canary should exercise, scoped by region + capacity tier, with strict validation and audit logging. This unblocks phase-1 rollout in us-east with a small model set and gives SRE/runtime a safe way to expand coverage without code changes. Motivation: We need a single source of truth for the canary target list that (a) is auditable, (b) prevents accidental wide fanout (capacity burn / metric cardinality), and (c) allows staged rollout per region and tier. Previously, target lists were hardcoded in service config and required redeploys; that’s too risky for fast tuning. Design overview: Introduces a new config kind PerfCanaryTargets stored in the control-plane config service. Adds an admin write API (RBAC-gated) for setting/updating targets and a read API scoped to the perf-canary service account. The config is keyed by (region, tier) and contains a small list of model refs (canonical model_id + optional pinned model_version), plus optional per-target overrides (enabled flag, qps_budget, max_concurrency). All writes emit an audit event containing actor, request_id, before/after hashes, and a compact diff summary. Validation / guardrails: Validation happens on write in control plane. Rules: (1) tier must be one of: hosted-shared | dedicated | private; (2) region must be a known runtime region from the region registry; (3) max 10 targets per (region,tier); (4) qps_budget must be <= 0.2 QPS per target by default unless an explicit override is provided and the requestor has the perf_canary.admin_override capability; (5) each model_id must resolve via model-registry to a canonical model slug and is normalized to the canonical id; (6) if model_version is provided, it must exist and be runnable in that region (model-registry capability check); (7) duplicate model_id+version pairs are rejected; (8) config payload size is capped and validated to avoid accidental huge lists. Audit logging: All create/update/delete operations produce an AuditEvent {event_type=PERF_CANARY_TARGETS_CONFIG_CHANGED} and include: actor_user/actor_service, request_id, region, tier, old_config_hash, new_config_hash, change_summary, and a list of model ids affected (capped to 25; remainder summarized). Audit events go to the existing audit-log sink and are also emitted in structured logs for quick grep during incidents. Auth/RBAC: New permissions: perf_canary.targets.read (granted to perf-canary SA) and perf_canary.targets.write (granted to Runtime + SRE admin groups). The read endpoint is intentionally narrow (read-only, no list-all across regions unless caller has admin). API shape (internal): GET /internal/control-plane/v1/perf-canary/targets?region=us-east&tier=hosted-shared returns the resolved config (canonical ids) plus an etag. PUT /internal/control-plane/v1/perf-canary/targets?region=...&tier=... sets full config (replace semantics). Response includes validation warnings (non-fatal) and etag. Example payload (illustrative): {"targets": [{"model_id": "llama-3.1-8b-instruct", "model_version": "2026-01-10", "enabled": true, "qps_budget": 0.05}, {"model_id": "qwen2.5-7b-instruct", "enabled": true}], "defaults": {"max_concurrency": 2}}. Notes: The perf-canary service will consume this via its existing control-plane client (separate PR in perf-canary repo wires the new endpoint). This PR focuses only on control-plane surface area, validation, and auditability. Rollout plan: Feature-flagged behind control_plane.perf_canary_targets_config (default off). Once merged, we’ll enable in staging, seed us-east/hosted-shared with 2 targets, and verify canary reads + audit trails. Follow-ups: (1) add UI in Console for editing targets (tracked separately); (2) add optional per-SKU allowlists as we expand beyond phase-1; (3) add explicit “high-risk model” tagging once the model registry exposes it.
Logan Wright (review): Can we avoid exposing model_version as free-form? Worried about pinning leading to stale baselines / unexpected drift. Also, please confirm we’re not adding new high-cardinality labels anywhere in control plane logs. Connor O'Brien (author): Agreed on the risk; model_version is optional and validation checks it’s runnable in-region. The canary defaults to unpinned (latest stable) unless explicitly set. No new metrics labels in this PR; audit logs include model ids in a capped list and otherwise a count summary. Nadia Rahman (review): For the read endpoint: can we include an etag so the canary can cache + avoid hot-polling? Connor O'Brien: Yep—added etag derived from config hash. Response includes etag and server sets Cache-Control: private,max-age=30 for read calls. Allison Grant (review): Audit event needs request_id and actor fields standardized. Please use the shared AuditContext helper so incident-bot / SRE tooling can correlate changes. Connor O'Brien: Updated to use AuditContext; request_id is pulled from gateway middleware and actor is resolved from auth context (user vs service). Noah Patel (review): Validation max 10 targets per (region,tier) seems fine, but we should cap concurrency defaults too; otherwise someone could set qps_budget low but crank concurrency high and still add overhead. Connor O'Brien: Added defaults.max_concurrency validation (<= 4) and per-target override cap (<= 8) gated behind perf_canary.admin_override. Quentin Harris (review): Model id normalization should use canonical model registry id, not the display slug. Also ensure we’re checking capability by region/tier (some models not enabled in Dedicated). Connor O'Brien: Fixed—now we store canonical model_id from registry and validate region+tier availability via registry capability endpoint. CI: First run failed due to a missing generated swagger artifact; reran after adding generation step to presubmit, now green. Approvals: Noah Patel approved; Logan Wright approved; Nadia Rahman approved; Allison Grant approved with nit addressed. Merged via squash on 2026-01-22.
payload.title: Control plane: config surface for perf-canary target models (by region/tier) + validation + audit logging

payload.body:
Context: We observed intermittent SLA slips during slow scale-down windows where tenants experienced transient throughput drops shortly after nodes were removed. Root-cause analysis showed two contributing factors: (1) the autoscaler was evicting warm state too aggressively for pools with high short-term burst variance, and (2) there was no compact representation of the recent per-tenant throughput envelope available to routing and the admission controller.

What this PR does: Adds a throughput-envelope guard that maintains a compact, decaying quantile snapshot per-tenant (and per-pool) to inform decommit decisions and admission-fallback policies. It also introduces a tenant-utilization-exporter CLI and HTTP endpoint that emits aligned, timestamped utilization timelines (sequential snapshots) for downstream analysis and on-call debugging. The two features together improve safety of scale-downs and make post-incident analysis faster.

Design highlights: - Throughput envelope: a memory-efficient bounded sketch (HDR-like) per tenant that records token/sec percentiles over multiple windows (1m, 5m, 30m) with exponential decay. The envelope exposes: p50/p90/p99, burst index (p99/p50), and a stability score (variance-normalized). - Decommit guard: autoscaler consults the envelope before removing slots from a pool; if a tenant's envelope shows a high burst index or recent p99 spikes, the policy requires an elevated safety margin (elasticity_safety_margin) for that tenant's allocations. - Admission fallback: router uses the envelope to decide whether to route to a full-capacity variant or a cheaper quantized model when the observed workload risk is low. - Tenant util exporter: a unified mechanism to stream snapshots and to export historical timeline fragments in ndjson for forensic tooling and evicition-policy tuning. Includes a small CLI (redwood-util-export) to query S3/DB backfills and produce compact timelines.

Backward compatibility: Default behavior is no-op for clusters that do not enable the guard via config flag (autoscaler.enable_throughput_envelope_guard=false). The exporter is opt-in (telemetry.exporter.enabled=false by default). No schema changes to existing autoscaler DB tables; envelope stores are appended as a new minor table with a TTL.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for sketch correctness and decay behavior (edge cases around sparsity). - Integration tests with the autoscaler simulator added: simulated burst injection tests where previous policy produced >4x post-scale SLA slips; new policy brings median post-scale latency fold change down to 1.1x in simulations. - End-to-end dogfooding on a small dedicated fleet: 72h soak with synthetic burst patterns and tenant mix; no SLA regressions observed and reduced emergency rollbacks.

Rollout plan: 1) Feature gated behind flags and 24h metric retention toggle. 2) Canary rollout to staging fleets, monitor p99 latency and burst_drop_rate for 48h. 3) Gradual ramp to 20% production pool capacity, with automatic rollback if post-scale p99 increases >8%. 4) Full deployment to dedicated fleets after 7-day bake and SRE sign-off.

Migration notes: The envelope table is populated lazily; historical data is not backfilled. The exporter can be used to reconstruct utilization timelines for important tenants by replaying recent request logs if needed.

Related: ENG-2147 (autoscaler safety margins), ENG-2210 (telemetry export requirements).

Files changed: See files_changed. Commits: see commits. Review convo and CI details below.
Ethan Ross: The envelope_store memory accounting looks OK but can you add a circuit-breaker to avoid OOM if tenants spike to millions? Also add a prometheus gauge for envelope_count.
Maya Patel: Added allocator-based accounting and a hard cap with evict-oldest policy. Exporter now exposes envelope_count gauge (telemetry/envelope_count) and the CLI emits a size estimate for a requested window.
Priya Khanna: Autoscaler integration looks solid. Please add an explicit unit test for the safety margin math when stability_score is NaN (very sparse tenants).
Maya Patel: Added stability_score NaN guard; defaults to conservative margin when insufficient data.
Luca Moretti: Minor nit: add a short example in docs showing CLI usage to pull the last 12h timeline for a tenant. Also please ensure the rollout checklist includes an emergency rollback metric threshold.
Maya Patel: Docs updated with CLI example and explicit rollback thresholds.
payload.title: Introduce throughput-envelope guard and tenant utilization exporter
