Motivation: Continuous batching in high-concurrency tails occasionally starved small, latency-sensitive requests when large KV-heavy streams dominated the batch window. This PR introduces an adaptive holdback window plus a lightweight backpressure-hull admission policy to reduce starvation while preserving batch efficiency. Design summary: 1) adaptive_holdback: maintain a sliding holdback budget per worker based on observed per-client tail latency and recent admit/drop ratios; the budget reduces the effective batch window for new requests from noisy/kv-heavy flows so short requests can be admitted sooner; 2) backpressure_hull: a compact admission classifier that computes a 3-point hull (latency, kv_weight, size) to fast-reject requests that likely cause prolonged KV pinning and instead route them to a slightly slower lane (same model variant) that has prewarmed KV caches; 3) timeout_annealing: when a queue detects starvation for > SLO fraction, it anneals the per-slot timeout down for a bounded epoch to flush short requests; 4) kernel-hint passthrough: add a small runtime hint to kernel_selector to prefer the low-latency kernel path for requests admitted via the accelerated lane. The combined effect reduces p99 for short-requests by ~20% in local perf runs without materially increasing overall cost. The description below includes the checklist and testing notes. Checklist: - [x] API: add holdback config to ContinuousBatcher::Config - [x] Scheduler: implement adaptive_holdback and backpressure_hull admission paths - [x] Runtime: expose kernel_hint flag to kernel selector - [x] KV: add lightweight prewarm-lane tagging in cache manager - [x] Metrics: add holdback_budget, hull_rejects, anneal_epochs - [x] Tests: unit tests for admission, integration perf harness run - [x] Docs: short notes in docs/scheduling.md Rollout: feature-flagged (runtime flag continuous_adaptive_holdback) default off, enabled for Canary in DC-us-west-2. Migration notes: config defaults are conservative; operators can tune holdback.min_budget and anneal.window to trade throughput vs latency. See linked Linear tasks for tuning plans.
Ethan Park: Please add a metric for per-client holdback variance so we can detect noisy tenants (requested in review).
Maya Patel: Added holdback_variance metric and dashboard link; also included conservative defaults in config.
Lina Gomez: Unit test flakes on Windows build, looks like a timing assumption in holdback_test. Consider using the test harness clock.
Maya Patel: Switched tests to TestClock and added a retry guard; reran CI.
Omar Haddad: Approve after adding integration perf numbers and confirming no regression on steady-state throughput.
Maya Patel: Uploaded perf CSVs to the Linear ticket and squashed commits per request.
Perf summary: local canary (1000 qps mixed workload) showed p50 for short-requests unchanged, p95 reduced by ~8%, p99 reduced by ~20%. Throughput regression <1%. Follow-ups: add fine-grained per-tenant knobs and autoscaling policies (ENG-2140).
Introduce adaptive holdback window and backpressure hull admission to reduce starvation of short requests in continuous batching. Feature-flagged under continuous_adaptive_holdback. Includes metrics: holdback_budget, hull_rejects, anneal_epochs, holdback_variance.
payload.title: adaptive holdback + backpressure hull: reduce starvation in continuous-batcher

payload.body:
Summary: Adds a lightweight query regulator for the observability ingestion/query path and a trace backpressure agent that annotates invocations with upstream throttling signals. Motivation: During high-traffic incidents our observability ingestion cluster and query API can become saturated, leading to delayed dashboards, missed SLO alerts, and cascading retries that exacerbate load. This PR implements a defensive layer that (1) throttles/queues expensive queries leaving the observability API, (2) surfaces a backpressure signal in traces and metrics so downstream services can react, and (3) provides dashboards and tuned alerts to operate the system without over-alerting. Design/Changes: 1) pkg/observability/regulator.go implements an in-process regulator that exposes token-bucket and lease-style backpressure for outgoing query work. It can be configured by route, cost-estimate, and tenant priority. 2) telemetry/trace_agent/backpressure_injector.go adds a small span annotation (obsv.backpressure.reason, obsv.backpressure.latency_ms) and attaches an opaque backpressure_id to enable downstream correlate-and-suppress flows. 3) Added two new metrics: observability.query_backpressure.active (gauge) and invocation.token_lag_ms (histogram) which captures the extra latency introduced by query deferment for billing/alerting. 4) dashboards/observability/query-regulator-dashboard.json: Grafana panels for active backpressure, queue depth, token_lag percentiles and per-tenant ingress vs. served ratio. 5) alerting/rules/query-regulator-alerts.yaml: tuned alerts that alert on sustained queueing for 5m+ with progressive severity; we also include an automated quiet-window for scheduled heavy replays. 6) docs/observability/query-regulator.md: operational runbook and rollback instructions. 7) e2e tests: test/integration/query_regulator_integration_test.go (local regulator+mocked backend) and test/unit/backpressure_injector_test.go. Backwards compatibility: The trace annotation uses optional attributes and fields are added in a backward-compatible way. Configuration defaults keep the regulator disabled in small deployments; alpha runtime flag obs.query_regulator.enabled=false. Performance: Microbenchmarks included in test/bench/regulator_bench.go show median overhead <0.6ms for the fast-path when regulator is not applying backpressure; when active we avoid backend CPU amplification by dropping or queuing low-priority client queries. Rollout plan: 1) Canary enable in staging for internal tenants (2 days), 2) Enable for 10% of hosted traffic with conservative limits (48h), 3) Increase to 50% with adjusted thresholds (72h), 4) Global rollout if signal stable. Monitoring and SLOs: New dashboards and a dedicated SLO (obs.query_served_rate) added to track any impact to user-visible query completeness. CI/Tests: Unit tests + integration suite added. There was a flaky test on first CI run (TestRegulatorLeaseEdge) which was addressed and re-run; final CI green. Security: No new inbound surface area; regulator runs in-process and uses existing auth scopes. Files changed (high level): pkg/observability/regulator.go, pkg/observability/regulator_test.go, telemetry/trace_agent/backpressure_injector.go, telemetry/trace_agent/backpressure_injector_test.go, dashboards/observability/query-regulator-dashboard.json, alerting/rules/query-regulator-alerts.yaml, docs/observability/query-regulator.md, test/integration/query_regulator_integration_test.go, test/bench/regulator_bench.go, internal/config/flags.go, internal/config/defaults.yaml, scripts/loadtests/query_regulator_load.py, Makefile updates (test target). Risks and mitigations: Risk: improper tuning could mute legitimate SLO regressions. Mitigation: conservative defaults, staged rollout, added SLO that tracks query_served_rate and an active alert that routes to oncall only at severity P2 after 20m sustained. Risk: high-cardinality tenants generating many small queries. Mitigation: per-tenant budgeting and an opt-out blacklist for VIP tenants. Related work: ENG-2109 introduces tenant-aware budgeting; ENG-2180 tracks token-lag instrumentation. Release notes: "Observability: Add query regulator and trace backpressure agent to reduce overload during ingestion/query spikes. Includes dashboards and tuned alerts. Disabled by default." Merge notes: Squash-merged to main; see merge commit 2f9b6c3.
Ava Chen: This looks well scoped. A couple of nit comments: 1) regulator.go currently holds the mutex in the hot path for rate checks — can we try an atomic fast-path? 2) please add a short note in the dashboard JSON explaining the percentile windows used.
Jordan Park (author): Ack, switched to an atomic fast-path for the common case and added the dashboard note. See commit 3. Also updated tests to cover race conditions.
Miguel Santos: The per-tenant budgeting config needs a non-zero global cap to avoid OOM in internal stress tests. Can we default to conservative values in defaults.yaml?
Jordan Park (author): Done — defaults lowered and documented in docs/observability/query-regulator.md. Added an internal flag to opt-out VIP tenants.
Priya Nair: Alert tuning looks sensible. Please ensure runbook includes a quick rollback procedure in case of false positives.
Jordan Park (author): Added rollback steps and an automated route to mute alerts via the alerting/rules file and the console UI section in the runbook.
CI system: test/TestRegulatorLeaseEdge failed on first run (race in test harness) — re-run after author fix.
CI system: All checks passed on re-run.
Initial implementation of in-process query regulator (pkg/observability/regulator.go)
Add trace backpressure injector and tests (telemetry/trace_agent)
Dashboard and alerting rule for regulator metrics
Add integration test and bench; update defaults and runbook
payload.title: Introduce observability query regulator and trace backpressure agent

payload.body:
Context: We observed a recurring class of production incidents where a small fraction of invocations exhibit multi-segment token lag (latency concentrated in the middle segments of generation rather than coldstart or finalization). These long-tail segments cause cost spikes and noisy alerts because existing SLOs and alert rules attribute cost/latency to whole-invocation percentiles.

Goal: Provide finer-grained observability and alert control by: 1) emitting segmented token-lag histograms (pre-token, prefix, mid-segment, tail) and per-segment cost counters, 2) adding a fastpath detection flag to traces so low-cost single-chunk invocations can be squelched from noise-sensitive alerts, and 3) creating dashboard panels and an alert-squelch policy for noisy mid-segment blips.

What this PR includes: checklist - [x] runtime metric hooks for segment buckets and per-segment cost meters, [x] tracer enrichment with "fastpath" boolean and segment offsets, [x] aggregation rollup job for segmented histograms (hourly rollups + 7d downsample), [x] new Grafana dashboard panels (Segmented token-lag heatmap, fastpath ratio timeseries, per-tenant segment cost share), [x] alert rule change: add squelch rule to mute SLO-noise for invocations marked fastpath and for tenants with >95% fastpath within last 5m, [x] unit + integration tests, [x] short operational playbook fragment.

Backward compatibility and safety: Metrics use new stable names with tag-based versioning (telemetry.v=2). Tracing enrichment is additive and guarded behind a feature flag (obs.segmented_token_lag_enabled) rolled out by default for internal staging and opt-in for private deployments. Alert squelch is declarative and non-blocking; we keep original alerts and add an aggregated suppression layer that is reversible.

Notes/links: internal runbook reference: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2190/segment-lag-investigation; benchmark notes live in repo subdir observability/testdata/segment-bench.

Impact: initial rollout shows a ~28% reduction in alert noise on the nightly canary tenant and isolates the long-tail cost to a small tenant cohort for further tuning.

Testing: Local unit tests for histogram bucketing, end-to-end integration against the observability staging cluster with synthetic traces (script included). CI verifies telemetry schema and linting.

Requested merge strategy: squash and merge to keep metric commit tidy.
Rohan Iyer: Nice approach to bucket by segment offsets — two comments: can we make the mid-segment bucket boundary configurable and add a short note on how it maps to common generation lengths?
Maya Chen: Good point, added config via obs.segmented_bucket_boundaries and documented typical mappings in sdk/telemetry/schema_v2.md.
Lena Kovalenko: The fastpath flag looks fine but we should be careful about privacy for private deployments. Can we gate tracer enrichment behind KMS-enabled telemetry?
Maya Chen: Tracing enrichment is gated by the feature flag and we added an extra check so private installs with telemetry.upload=false will not emit fastpath. Added tests to confirm.
Diego Martinez: CI failure on lint in first run — minor formatting. Verified in second CI run after fix. Approved pending squash.
Rohan Iyer: Approved. Also pinged infra to watch rollup job memory usage during the first week.
Maya Chen: Addressed infra note, reduced in-memory aggregation window; added a 5% memory cap and metrics to alert if exceeded.
Introduce segmented token-lag telemetry and fastpath alert squelch. Adds new Grafana panels and a non-destructive alert suppression rule to reduce noise from short, single-chunk invocations. Backward-compatible metric names (telemetry.v=2).
1) If mid-segment cost spikes increase warnings: check segmented_token_lag_histogram and segment-rollup-mem-usage; 2) To disable fastpath squelch for a tenant: set tenant.alert_squelch.fastpath=false in monitoring config; 3) Rollback: revert feature flag obs.segmented_token_lag_enabled or disable rollup job via orchestration UI.
payload.title: Segmented token-lag profiles and fastpath alert squelch

payload.body:
Context: Each SDK implemented session and streaming primitives slightly differently over time (handoff, heartbeat, reauth). That drift made it hard to reason about cross-language behavior and complicated runtime code paths. This PR introduces a small core 'SessionFacade' abstraction in the redwood runtime and exposes lightweight, idiomatic adapters for Python, TypeScript, and Go that align on single-source semantics (lease-based session, deterministic retry windows, explicit lifecycle signals).

What changed (high level): - runtime: add SessionFacade interface + minimal lifecycle hooks (CreateLease, ExtendLease, Release, HeartbeatHint) and tests for deterministic retry windows. - python SDK: new redwood.session_facade.SessionFacade and an AsyncIterator wrapper (session_facade.AsyncStream) that emits typed chunks and surface ergonomic helpers (aiter_lines, aiter_json). - typescript SDK: export sessionFacade() factory; AsyncIterable wrapper emits chunk objects and exposes backpressureHint() to assist consumers. - go SDK: channel-based SessionAdapter and a StreamController that sends typed events to the consumer goroutine; simplified reconnect/retry API. - compatibility: implement per-SDK shims named LegacySessionCompat that map existing calls to the facade for a gradual migration. - docs/examples: migration guide snippets for each language and a codemod for the Python helper rename.

Motivation: unify behavior across languages so integrations that depend on token refresh, stream resume, and retry policy observe the same semantics without duplicating large swathes of logic in each SDK. This also simplifies the runtime surface area for session affinity and leased credentials.

Migration notes: - Current callers continue to work (LegacySessionCompat). - We recommend moving to the idiomatic adapters: Python: use 'async for chunk in session.async_iter()' TypeScript: 'for await (const chunk of session.asyncIterable())' Go: 'for ev := range session.Events() { ... }' - Small breaking edge-case: users relying on internal order of some low-level event enums should consult the migration guide; most apps unaffected.

Testing & CI: Added cross-language integration tests exercising token rotation, heartbeat, and session handoff under load. CI matrix includes Py 3.10/3.11, Node 18/20, Go 1.20/1.21. All checks green.

Rollout: staged rollout across hosted and dedicated infra with feature-flagged runtime behavior. SDK releases are coordinated; we published prerelease candidates internally and cut stable releases after this merge.
Adds a SessionFacade in the core runtime and language-specific adapters to provide idiomatic streaming/session APIs for Python (async iterator), TypeScript (AsyncIterable with backpressure hints) and Go (channel-based stream). SDKs bumped: python 2.3.0, typescript 1.11.0, go v1.5.4. Backwards-compatible shims provided for current callers; recommend migration for ergonomic improvements and clearer retry lifecycles.
Ava Patel: Can we avoid exposing heartbeat internals in the public TS surface? Suggest exposing only a hint rather than raw timestamps.
Author (Priya): Switched TS surface to backpressureHint() and added a comment explaining runtime-only timestamps remain private.
Marco Ruiz: Please add a unit test that simulates token refresh failure during handoff and validate fallback path.
Author (Priya): Added test in sdk/python/tests and expanded the Go integration to cover the token-refresh-failure fallback. CI updated.
Elena Chen: Rename CreateLease -> AcquireLease for clarity; small naming nit across all adapters.
Author (Priya): Renamed methods and updated migration docs. Left LegacySessionCompat alias for backwards compatibility.
Hotfix follow-up planned: reduce Python generator memory spike under extreme parallel streams (tracking ENG-1487)
SDK owners: coordinate minor release notes; callouts added to console deprecation page for legacy shim in 3 months
payload.title: Introduce SessionFacade and idiomatic SDK adapters (Python/TS/Go)

payload.body:
Context: production workloads show increasing KV cache fragmentation on long-lived hosts which leads to elevated memory churn, larger tail latencies when compact operations run, and suboptimal cross-tenant fairness under pressure. This PR introduces a two-part approach: (1) a Fragment‑Fuse Migrator that incrementally coalesces small free regions into compact segments without global stop-the-world compaction, and (2) a Liveness-Budget tenant throttling policy that enforces soft residency budgets per tenant and coordinates low-impact migrations during slack windows.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a new migrator component (kv/migrator) that performs locality-preserving fragment fusion: it identifies adjacent free+live fragment pairs and migrates live objects into target slots using low-priority IO/KV pathways to produce larger contiguous free segments. The migrator is incremental and bounded by time/scratch memory allowances.
- Introduces a tenant liveness budget manager that tracks per-tenant active-residency and issues throttles when a tenant's budget is exceeded. Throttling reduces admission to aggressive KV pinning and signals the migrator to prioritize that tenant's scattered regions.
- Extends the eviction priority scoreboard to incorporate fragmentation score and recent‑migrate credits so eviction decisions favor tenants whose fragmentation is high but whose liveness budget is within limits.
- Adds lightweight kernel mmap hinting for migrated regions (madvise(MADV_DONTNEED)/MADV_WILLNEED toggles) to reduce page-cache churn on hosts with mixed workloads. This only applies when migrator runs with 'low_io' gating.
- Safety and rollout: feature-gated behind runtime flag kv.fragment_fuse.enabled (default off); config knobs for migrator footprint, per-tenant budget, and scheduling windows. Gradual rollout via canary with metrics exposed.

Implementation notes:
- Migrator is implemented as a pluggable background worker under kv/runtime. It uses the existing allocator introspection APIs to read fragment maps and the KV relocation helpers to move entries while preserving CAS semantics for active requests. Key design points: bounded walker, backpressure via backlog counters, and coalescing heuristics that avoid moving recently-touched items (LRU-proximity cutoff).
- Liveness budgeting hooks are added at the admission path and the cache enforcement path; budgets are computed using an exponential moving average of residency over 5m windows and a tenant's committed capacity. Throttles emit structured events and metric tags to aid debugging.
- Eviction scoreboard changes are additive: a fragmentation_penalty term is added (configurable weight) and a recently_migrated credit subtracts penalty for tenants recently optimized.
- Kernel hinting is optional and gated per-machine profile; it's implemented as a small abstraction: mmap_hint(region, hint_type). For portability the code falls back to no-op on platforms without MADV_* support.

Benchmarks & results (internal canary):
- Synthetic fragmentation workload (mixed-size allocations, 24h run): median host RSS reduction 9.6%, 95th percentile latency improvement for KV eviction path 18%, and compaction IO reduced by 42% measured over 6h windows.
- Multi-tenant fairness test (5 tenants, one noisy neighbor): tail P99 increase reduced from +37% to +9% for non-noisy tenants after enabling liveness-budget throttling.
- CPU overhead: migrator at production defaults consumes <1.2% host CPU during steady state (measured on c5.4xlarge equivalent).

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for migrator heuristics, migration correctness, and budget math.
- Integration tests simulating admission throttles and eviction-score interactions in the eval harness (added test_kv_migrator_integration.py).
- Stress tests run in perf-canary infra for 72h with mixed alloc sizes.

Rollout plan:
1) Behind feature flag OFF in main; run internal canaries with flag ON on dedicated canary fleet.
2) Collect fragmentation_score, migration_rate, eviction_retries, and tenant_throttle events for 48h.
3) If metrics stable, enable for 10% production hosts and monitor.
4) Gradual ramp to 100% with config tuning and runbook updates.

Notes & caveats:
- This PR does not change on-disk layout or wire protocol. No migration required for persisted indices.
- Potential risk: aggressive migration can increase short-term IO; mitigated by conservative defaults and low_io gating.

Related: ENG-4829 (fragmentation reduction epic), SUP-1142 (customer incident analysis), previous work on arena compaction (see PRs in repo for background).
--- a/kv/migrator/migrator.rs
+++ b/kv/migrator/migrator.rs
@@ -10,6 +10,22 @@
+// bounded walker loop: checks time budget and scratch reservations
+while budget.not_exhausted() {
+  let pair = fragment_map.next_candidate()?;
+  if should_skip(&pair) { continue; }
+  relocate_live_objects(&pair.src, &pair.dst, MigrationPriority::Low).await?;
+}

--- a/kv/evictor/scoreboard.rs
+++ b/kv/evictor/scoreboard.rs
@@ -45,6 +45,10 @@
-let base_score = compute_lru_score(entry);
+let base_score = compute_lru_score(entry);
+let frag_pen = fragmentation_score(tenant) * config.frag_weight;
+let migrate_credit = tenant_metrics.recently_migrated_credit;
+let final = base_score + frag_pen - migrate_credit;

--- a/kv/liveness/budget_manager.rs
+++ b/kv/liveness/budget_manager.rs
@@ -1,3 +1,18 @@
+pub fn should_throttle(tenant_id: TenantId) -> bool {
+  let budget = budgets.get(tenant_id);
+  let residency = residency_ema(tenant_id);
+  residency > budget.committed * budget.alpha_threshold
+}

Diego Fernandez: Nice incremental design. Please ensure migrator respects KV transactional boundaries — I left a TODO on migrator.rs about double-checking CAS semantics.
Aisha Malik (author): Responded — migrator uses the same relocation helpers as the eviction path and preserves CAS via relocate_with_cas; added unit tests to cover races.
Maya Chen: Can we add a metric for 'migration_impact' (mv_bytes / mv_time) so SRE can tune defaults?
Aisha Malik (author): Added migration_impact and a per-host migration_rate cap; also exposed the config knob in docs/operational/kv-fragment-fuse.md.
Liam O'Connor: What about coordination with other background cleaners (compactor)? We should avoid running them simultaneously.
Aisha Malik (author): Migrator registers a coord token with the background scheduler; migration windows are aligned with compactor cooldowns — clarified in comments and tests.
Introduces a non-disruptive KV fragment coalescer (migrator) and per-tenant liveness budgeting to reduce fragmentation and improve tenant fairness. Feature is disabled by default and controllable via runtime flags.
Runtime flags: kv.fragment_fuse.enabled (bool), kv.fragment_fuse.migrator_budget_ms, kv.fragment_fuse.per_tenant_budget_pct. Monitor metrics: fragmentation_score, migration_rate, eviction_retries, tenant_throttle_events. Default config is conservative; start with canary.
payload.title: kv: fragment-fuse migrator and liveness-budget tenant throttling

This PR adds a new component, the Shadow Batch Allocator (SBA), and an associated CLI prober to automatically infer tenant-appropriate batching, prefill/cache defaults, and quantization suggestions via non-disruptive shadow experiments. Motivation: teams repeatedly tune batching/prefill/quant settings per tenant to meet unit-econ targets; this manual work is error-prone and slow. SBA runs shadowed dry-runs of candidate batch shapes and quant profiles in the background, measures tail P99 latency, throughput, and model-quality proxies (logprobs/response-length heuristics), and scores trade-offs against a configurable cost model. The initial implementation focuses on tenant-scoped defaults, not on live request mutation, so it is safe for rollout and can be enabled per-tenant as an opt-in flag. Key behaviors: 1) A lightweight probe client (rw-econ probe) captures anonymized request signatures and schedules them into shadow batching runs; 2) The allocator evaluates multiple batch-shape candidates (micro, mini, pooled) and quant profiles (FP16, int8-quantized candidates) with fixed-duration trials; 3) Results are synthesized into a ranked set of recommended defaults for batching_size, prefill_kv_cache, and quant_profile with expected unit-cost delta and estimated P95/P99 impact; 4) Recommendations are exported to the Console as a suggested tenant defaults bundle and to the CLI as a dry-run JSON that operators can review before applying. Implementation notes: SBA is implemented mostly in the runtime scheduler (scheduler/shadow_allocator.go) and an opt-in controller (controller/econ_probe_controller.go). A new small telemetry bridge (telemetry/econ-shadow-metrics) emits a compact set of metrics and a summary artifact stored in the existing tenant-metadata store for review and rollouts. The PR includes unit and integration tests, a dry-run simulation harness, and an example tenant defaults bundle. Scope exclusions: does NOT auto-apply recommendations; does not modify live routing or rollback rules; does not perform model fine-tuning. Security and privacy: payloads used for shadow runs are tokenized and schema-hashed; only duration, token counts, and response-length heuristics are retained for the summary artifact. Related work: follows on ENG-2745 (batching telemetry) and ENG-3012 (quantization suggestion UI).
Priya Patel: Can we clarify the safety boundaries? Make sure the prober can't leak user content to logs. (resolved)
Avery Chen: Payloads are tokenized and we only persist schema-hashed signatures; added a privacy section in docs and unit tests for redaction (see telemetry/econ-shadow-metrics).
Marco Ruiz: The cost model looks optimistic for int8 candidates on T4 classes; please add explicit calibration samples from 2 dev tenants. (addressed)
Avery Chen: Added calibration dataset and a regression test to ensure int8 estimates are within 12% of observed costs on CI-simulated runs.
Leah Thompson: We should gate the allocator behind a feature flag and tenant opt-in. Also add a rate limiter so probes can't overload schedulers. (addressed)
Avery Chen: Feature flag added (feature.econ.shadow_allocator) and probe-client rate limiter introduced with default conservative limits; documented in ops guide.
Add Shadow Batch Allocator and rw-econ probe: non-disruptive tenant-specific recommendations for batching, prefill, and quantization. Opt-in and behind feature flag. See docs/ops/shadow-batcher.md for rollout guidance.
This PR intentionally produces recommendation artifacts only; follow-up PR will add an operator workflow to apply bundles and a gradual rollout automation. Observatory dashboards added to Console but default retention is short; customers with longer retention must enable the telemetry add-on.

Context: Optimize recommendations (batching/caching/quantization profile changes) need to be gated by evals before they can be applied to production traffic. We’ve seen a few near-miss cases where an optimization proposal was syntactically valid but semantically unsafe (e.g., quant profile incompatible with model family + GPU SKU, or caching knobs that violate runtime invariants). This PR introduces a typed, versioned config-diff schema plus static validation and explicit rejection reasons so we can fail fast before spending GPU cycles running evals and before changes reach rollout controller. What’s in this PR: (1) ConfigDiff v1 schema: Adds a versioned diff payload used across Optimize -> eval-harness trigger -> audit log. We represent diffs as an explicit list of operations rather than "free-form JSON patches" to keep validation predictable and to make audit trails readable. The v1 payload is stable and backward-compatible within v1. (2) Static validation rules: Adds a server-side validator for config diffs that runs before eval execution. Validation covers syntax (required fields, enum validity), bounds/ranges, and cross-field constraints (e.g., batching policy constraints vs streaming mode, kv-cache constraints vs context window, quant profile constraints vs model family + runtime backend). (3) Rejection reason codes: Standardizes error codes returned to Optimize/Console so UI can display actionable failure reasons and link to docs/runbooks. These reason codes are also emitted to audit logs (without leaking customer prompt content). (4) Test coverage + fixtures: Unit tests for parsing/validation, plus golden fixtures for common diffs and expected failure modes. Schema overview (high level): - diff_version: "v1" - scope: route_id / model_id / deployment_tier (hosted|dedicated) - ops: list of typed operations (BatchingPolicyOp, KvCacheOp, QuantProfileOp) - baseline_ref: optional reference to baseline config id (required for certain change types; validated) Example (illustrative): {"diff_version":"v1","scope":{"route_id":"rt_8n3..."},"ops":[{"type":"BATCHING_POLICY","max_batch_tokens":8192,"max_wait_ms":8},{"type":"KV_CACHE","prefix_cache_enabled":true,"max_prefix_cache_entries":2000}],"reason":"optimize_recommendation","proposed_by":"optimize"} Validation rules (selected): - Common: reject unknown diff_version; require non-empty ops; enforce max ops count (currently 10) to keep reviews/audits readable. - BatchingPolicyOp: validate max_wait_ms within [0,50]; max_batch_tokens within per-model bounds; disallow max_wait_ms > 0 when route has "strict_latency" policy (pulled from route policy snapshot). - KvCacheOp: disallow enabling prefix cache if runtime backend does not support it for the route’s model family; enforce max_prefix_cache_entries <= 5000; if prefix_cache_enabled=false then max_prefix_cache_entries must be unset. - QuantProfileOp: require baseline_ref; validate profile exists; validate compatibility against (model_family, gpu_sku, backend) matrix; disallow switching to any profile marked "experimental" unless route gating policy allows it (flag + tier check). - Cross-op: reject diffs that modify both kv-cache and quant profile in the same diff for MVP (forces separate gate runs to simplify attribution); reject conflicting ops (multiple ops of same type). Rejection reasons (returned as code + short message): - INVALID_SCHEMA: missing/invalid fields, unknown op type, invalid enums. - UNSUPPORTED_CHANGE_TYPE: op type not allowed under current rollout (feature-flagged). - OUT_OF_RANGE: numeric bounds violated. - INCOMPATIBLE_WITH_RUNTIME: known incompatibility with backend/model/gpu. - UNSAFE_COMBINATION: cross-op conflict or forbidden combination. - BASELINE_REQUIRED: missing baseline_ref for ops that require it. - POLICY_VIOLATION: route/tier policy disallows this change (e.g., experimental quant). Integration notes: - Optimize service should call validateConfigDiffV1(diff, routePolicySnapshot) before triggering eval-harness (ENG-3922). - The validator returns a normalized diff (e.g., defaulted fields removed, canonical ordering of ops) to improve caching and audit diffs. - Console API will display error codes as-is; copy improvements are tracked separately. Backward-compat: This is a breaking change for internal callers that were sending untyped "config_patch" blobs to the Optimize service. We keep a temporary compatibility shim behind OPTIMIZE_ACCEPT_LEGACY_PATCH until 2026-02-01 (default off in prod; on in staging for migration). Testing: - Added unit tests for all op types + cross-op constraints. - Added property-ish fuzz tests for numeric bounds and unknown fields to ensure we don’t accept surprising payloads. - Updated existing Optimize recommendation tests to emit ConfigDiff v1 fixtures. Rollout plan: Merge behind feature flag OPTIMIZE_CONFIG_DIFF_V1_VALIDATE (enabled in staging by default; prod enablement will be paired with the eval-harness trigger PR rollout). Follow-ups: - Wire validator errors to audit log events (ENG-3927). - Consider allowing multi-op diffs after we have better attribution in gate artifacts. - Add a small docs page for reason codes and remediation suggestions (tracked in docs PR).
Noah Patel (review): Can we make the quant compatibility failure explicit vs bundling under INCOMPATIBLE_WITH_RUNTIME? We’ll want to distinguish "profile doesn’t exist" vs "exists but incompatible" for triage.
Benji Okafor (author): Good call. Split into QUANT_PROFILE_NOT_FOUND and QUANT_PROFILE_INCOMPATIBLE, both still map to a user-friendly message in Console. Updated validator + tests.
Olivia Grant (review): For eval-harness, we need normalized diffs to be stable across retries. Do we guarantee op ordering and omission of defaults?
Benji Okafor (author): Yes. Validator returns normalized payload: ops sorted by type, unset fields stripped, and defaults not serialized. Added a test that ensures stable JSON stringify across runs.
Jordan Lee (review): Policy snapshot usage looks fine, but ensure we don’t accidentally fetch live policy during validation (must be the same snapshot used for gate run).
Benji Okafor (author): Updated route handlers to pass the snapshot object explicitly; removed fallback to policy store. Added an assertion + logs when snapshot missing.
Michael Nguyen (review): Please include rejection code in structured logs and include diff hash (not full payload) for audit privacy.
Benji Okafor (author): Added diff_hash (sha256 of normalized diff) + rejection_code in logs. Payload only logged in debug mode in staging.
Noah Patel (approval): Approved after rejection code split + added invariant tests.
Olivia Grant (approval): Approved; normalization guarantee unblocks eval-harness contract work.
Jordan Lee (approval): Approved.
Michael Nguyen (approval): Approved.
payload.title: Add config diff schema + static validation rules for Optimize quality gates

payload.body:
Context: Following a regional incident (INT-8721) we observed oscillating circuit states when downstream capacity dropped and then recovered rapidly; this caused repeated degrade->reopen cycles and user-visible latency spikes. This PR implements a metric-anchored fallback smoother and a probationary regional warmup token mechanism to reduce circuit flip churn and provide graceful rejoin behavior. Changes include: 1) A new smoothing layer in the SLO enforcer that anchors fallback decisions to an aggregate latency percentile window (p95 over a 2m rolling window) rather than instantaneous error counts; 2) A probationary warmup token bucket for a region that has recently reopened (configurable tokens grant limited throughput so capacity can be validated without triggering global fallbacks); 3) Persistent circuit state audit log entries to avoid lost transitions during leader failovers; 4) Observability additions (metrics and traces) to measure 'probation_token_usage', 'smoother_decision_index', and 'regional_warmup_success_rate'; 5) Backwards-compatible defaults so existing deployments see no behavior change unless the hotfix flag is enabled. Motivation: reduce noisy reopen cycles, improve SLO stability during transient capacity restores, and give operators a safe window to validate capacity before exposing full traffic. Related work: ENG-4921 (post-incident stabilization), ENG-5120 (regional probations design doc), incident INT-8721 notes. Rollout plan: feature-flagged on main; deploy to canary regions for 24h with telemetry thresholds; if stable, flip for production; fallback path retains previous circuit behavior. Hotfix urgency: high — this has already been applied to one affected customer in a fastpatch, but we want mainline code and tests. Non-breaking change: defaults disabled for existing clusters except where hotfix flag true.
Liam O'Connor: Nice approach; can you add a tolerance parameter to avoid permanent soft locks when p95 is noisy? Requesting an extra unit test that exercises jittered p95.
Evelyn Park: Added 'smoother_tolerance_ms' param and unit test 'TestSmootherStabilityUnderNoise' in latest commit; ensured default is conservative.
Priya Nair: Observability looks good but please add an alerting rule suggestion for high probation token drain (we should detect if a region exhausts tokens repeatedly).
Evelyn Park: Added Alert/Playbook section in docs/runbooks/regional-warmup.md and a sample Prometheus rule 'SLOFallbackHighTokenDrain' (non-firing by default).
Dmitri Volkov: Concern about audit persistence race during leader failover; suggest explicit leader epoch write and test simulating failover.
Evelyn Park: Implemented epoch-stamped writes and added 'TestCircuitPersistenceDuringLeaderHandoff' to integration tests; I validated locally with a simulated leader flip.
Hotfix: Reduce circuit reopen churn and provide safe regional rejoin window. Key points: metric-anchored smoothing for fallback decisions; probationary warmup tokens for reopened regions; persistent circuit transition audit logs; new telemetry metrics and recommended alert 'SLOFallbackHighTokenDrain'. Default-off; enable via 'regional_warmup.hotfix' feature flag if you observed noisy reopen cycles.

Context: As part of the cross-language SDK parity initiative (ENG-5126 / ENG-5130), SDKs need a stable way to classify errors as retryable vs terminal without relying on brittle string matching or status code heuristics alone. We currently have a mix of legacy `code` strings (inconsistent casing/names across services), missing codes in a few gateway paths, and doc drift. This PR introduces a single, documented `error_code` enum intended for SDK consumption and cleans up gateway mappings so the field is present consistently across JSON errors (including OpenAI-compat routes via the shared formatter).

What this PR does: (1) Defines a canonical `error_code` enum in the gateway error schema and updates the error formatter to always emit `error_code`, `message`, `type`, `request_id`, `status_code`, and `retryable`. (2) Adds mapping logic from downstream service error payloads and legacy fields into the canonical enum (with conservative fallback to `UNKNOWN`). (3) Aligns 429/503/504 behaviors with the retry standard: 429 includes `Retry-After` (handled separately in PR-28411) and now uses `RATE_LIMITED`; 503/504 map to `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`/`GATEWAY_TIMEOUT` with `retryable=true`. (4) Documents the enum and retry semantics in the API docs (internal spec + developer-facing references used by SDK teams).

Non-goals: This does not change rate limiting policy, billing behavior, model semantics, or introduce new auth mechanisms. We also intentionally do not promise a 1:1 mapping between HTTP status and retryability; SDKs should prefer the `retryable` boolean + `error_code` for user messaging and analytics.

Error fields (shape): `{"error": {"type": "api_error", "error_code": "RATE_LIMITED", "message": "...", "status_code": 429, "request_id": "req_...", "retryable": true, "details": {...}}}`. Notes: `details` remains service-specific and is not part of the stability contract.

Enum values added/standardized (initial set): RATE_LIMITED, SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, GATEWAY_TIMEOUT, REQUEST_TIMEOUT, INTERNAL, BAD_REQUEST, UNAUTHORIZED, FORBIDDEN, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY, CONTEXT_LENGTH_EXCEEDED, MODEL_NOT_FOUND, MODEL_UNAVAILABLE, QUOTA_EXCEEDED, INVALID_API_KEY, INVALID_BEARER_TOKEN, POLICY_VIOLATION, STREAMING_DISCONNECTED, UNKNOWN.

Retry semantics: (a) `retryable=true` for RATE_LIMITED, SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, GATEWAY_TIMEOUT, REQUEST_TIMEOUT, INTERNAL (only when originating from gateway/infra), and STREAMING_DISCONNECTED when the gateway detects an upstream disconnect pre-first-token; (b) `retryable=false` for auth errors, validation errors, policy violations, and quota exceeded. (c) SDKs should still implement idempotency-safe retry guidance for streaming; the error code exists primarily for classification + user messaging.

Docs: Added/updated an "Error codes" section with a compatibility note: new field `error_code` is the stable contract; legacy `code` remains for now but is deprecated in docs. Included examples for JSON errors and OpenAI-compat error format.

Testing: Unit tests cover mapping table + formatter output; integration-style tests cover (1) 429 with Retry-After header still present, (2) downstream error passthrough/mapping, and (3) OpenAI-compat route formatting. Also validated that `request_id` is populated (ties into PR-28426 for broader request_id propagation).

Rollout: Safe to ship behind existing gateway deployment. No client break expected; SDKs can begin consuming `error_code` immediately, and we can later deprecate legacy `code` when all SDKs are updated.

Related: PR-28411 (Retry-After on 429), PR-28426 (request_id propagation), redwood-openai-compat PR-433 (align compat layer error shapes).

Checklist: [x] Updated docs/spec references used by SDK teams [x] Added tests for mapping + formatting [x] Security reviewed for no sensitive data added to error payloads [x] Coordinated with SDK parity owners (Ibrahim) for enum names/fields.
Allison Grant (SRE): Can we guarantee `retryable` is present for *all* gateway errors? We’ve seen some fall-through errors emit only `message` and status. Also please confirm `INTERNAL` won’t cause SDKs to retry on app-level 500s that are actually deterministic. Ethan Park (author): Updated formatter to always emit the full shape; added a final catch-all that maps unknown throwables to `UNKNOWN` with `retryable=false` unless status in {502,503,504}. For `INTERNAL`, we only mark retryable when the gateway is the origin or the upstream error is explicitly tagged as transient; added tests covering deterministic 500 from downstream maps to `INTERNAL` but `retryable=false` unless tagged.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (Auth): Please keep auth errors very explicit. I’d prefer separate codes for invalid API key vs invalid bearer token, and ensure we’re not echoing any credential fragments in messages. Ethan: Split INVALID_API_KEY vs INVALID_BEARER_TOKEN; messages are generic and we redact any header-derived values. Added a regression test to ensure formatter never includes Authorization header value.

Marcus Lin (Security): Deprecation note is fine, but don’t remove legacy `code` yet; some customers parse it. Also confirm `details` doesn’t include internal stack traces. Ethan: Kept legacy `code` untouched, docs mark it deprecated but still present. Updated mapping to strip stack traces from downstream errors (only pass whitelisted fields); added a test to assert `details.stack` is not emitted.

Ibrahim Khan (SDK parity TL): Naming: can we use `RATE_LIMITED` instead of `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` to avoid ambiguity with 429 vs quota exceeded? Also please include `request_id` for OpenAI-compat errors so SDK conformance tests can assert it. Ethan: Agree; standardized to RATE_LIMITED; QUOTA_EXCEEDED is separate. OpenAI-compat adapter now forwards request_id. Added tests.

Sean Gallagher (SRE leadership): Looks good. Please add a short section in docs about not retrying streaming unless idempotency is handled. Ethan: Added note in retries doc linking to SDK guidance.

Approvals: Allison Grant approved (2026-02-17). Marcus Lin approved (2026-02-17). Ibrahim Khan approved (2026-02-18).
API errors now include a stable `error_code` enum and `retryable` boolean for consistent SDK classification; docs added for codes and retry guidance; no user-visible behavior change beyond clearer/consistent error fields.
payload.title: gateway/errors: standardize error_code enum + docs for SDK retry classification

payload.body:
Motivation: Several teams reported friction when rolling credential changes and SDK upgrades in mixed-language environments. This PR introduces a small, focused compatibility layer plus ergonomics improvements to reduce migration effort and stabilize streaming surface parity across Python/TS/Go.

Summary of changes (single-pass):
- Add credential aliasing registry: a runtime shim that maps logical credential names (eg 'service-batch-writer') to concrete providers. This lets customers rotate or shadow credentials without code changes in callers across SDKs.
- Introduce a compact stream facade (pull-generator friendly) that standardizes resume tokens, heartbeat hints, and idempotent checkpointing. Surface is intentionally minimal: open(), nextChunk(), resume(token).
- Harmonize retry presets: add two named profiles ("latency-sensitive" and "throughput-optimal") and wire them into SDK defaults. Each preset is documented with concrete backoff/jitter parameters used by the service-side router.
- Bump SDK versions to align: py 1.12.0, ts 1.28.0, go 1.5.3 and update changelogs and compatibility matrix.
- Add migration guide and cross-SDK examples demonstrating alias registry usage and stream resume semantics.

Why this shape: The aliasing approach avoids embedding credential URLs/keys in multiple layers and enables canary/blue-green credential swaps. The compact stream facade gives apps a predictable, language-agnostic resume model (important for mobile, serverless and long-running consumers).

Compatibility notes and migration steps:
1) Install SDK bumps (links in docs) – default behavior is backward-compatible; alias registry is opt-in via a single small config block.
2) If you relied on SDK-specific stream resume tokens previously, switch to the new compact facade by calling .resume(token) — the facade accepts old tokens and translates where possible, but opaque tokens from proprietary shims may require a short migration step (outlined in migration guide).
3) Retry preset names are additive; existing custom retry configurations are unaffected.

Testing done:
- Unit tests added across py/ts/go for alias lookup, token translation and retry profile selection.
- Integration test harness validated stream resume across a simulated router with deliberate token expiry and credential rotation.
- End-to-end perf check: latency-sensitive retry preset reduced P99 latency by ~8% on short requests in our benchmark lab when compared to the previous default for small-message workloads.

Checklist:
- [x] credential alias registry implementation (py/ts/go)
- [x] compact stream facade implementation and docs
- [x] retry preset definitions and SDK wiring
- [x] migration guide and examples
- [x] unit/integration tests and CI green
- [x] changelogs and version bumps

Related: ENG-1842 (credential lifecycle), ENG-1978 (stream resume parity), SUP-9021 (customer support case that motivated aliasing).
Arjun Patel (2025-11-09): Can you clarify the guarantees for token translation when the upstream router drops metadata? Also request adding an explicit test where token translation fails and we provide a helpful error.
Leah: Added translation-failure test and a more descriptive error message; included failure case in docs.
Maya Chen (2025-11-14): The TS facade API looks ergonomically better but we lost a minor type-safety hint on the resume token shape. Suggest we expose a ResumeToken type alias in the public index.
Leah: Added ResumeToken export and updated examples. CI caught a missing export which is fixed in commit 'feat(ts): export ResumeToken'.
Sophie Alvarez (2026-01-21): Concern about alias registry defaulting to environment variable lookup causing surprising behavior in serverless. Recommend explicit opt-in via SDK config.
Leah: Changed default to opt-out (registry disabled unless configured). Updated migration guide to highlight this change.
Arjun Patel (2026-02-12): Last pass — re-run CI and minor nits in docs. Approve after CI green.
Maya Chen (2026-02-13): Approve.
Sophie Alvarez (2026-02-13): Approve.
CI (2026-02-13): initial run failed (flake in tests/integration/stream_resume_rotation_test.ts). Flake fixed by adding deterministic seed in test harness. Final CI (2026-02-14): all checks passed.
Added credential alias registry (opt-in), compact stream facade (resume tokens + heartbeat hints), and two named retry presets (latency-sensitive, throughput-optimal). SDKs bumped: py 1.12.0, ts 1.28.0, go 1.5.3. See docs/migration/credential-aliasing.md for migration steps.
Backport candidate for maintenance branches: include alias registry plumbing and retry presets only; defer stream facade backports due to contract changes. When backporting ensure changelog entries and test harness seeds are included.

Summary: Introduces a lightweight credential circuit scheduler and a simple, language-agnostic StreamFactory to unify idiomatic stream construction across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Motivation: Teams repeatedly build small adapters to coordinate credential fallback, heartbeat/ttl alignment, and stream lifecycle hooks. This PR centralizes a small runtime-side scheduler plus SDK-side ergonomic factories so apps get safe defaults without per-language boilerplate. What changed (high level): 1) Core design: credential circuit scheduler that drives reauth backoff windows, cooldowns, and a minimal circuit breaker to avoid thundering reauth storms. The scheduler emits signals (ready, cooldown, eject) consumed by language SDK adapters. 2) SDK ergonomics: StreamFactory added to each SDK to create cancelable, checkpointable streams with consistent hooks (on_start, on_chunk, on_end, on_error) and optional credential binding. 3) Retry profiles: new "latency-aware" and "conservative-auth" presets wired into SDKs; documentation and examples added. 4) Telemetry: lightweight event tags for credential lifecycle events (credential.prefetch, credential.eject, stream.resume) for better sampling in Console. 5) Version bumps: python 1.4.2, typescript 2.8.0, go 1.5.0. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-2642) - [x] Unit tests for scheduler logic - [x] Cross-SDK integration examples - [x] Telemetry tags added - [x] Version bumps and changelogs Updates: Addressed reviewer feedback on cooldown defaults (reduced from 45s to 20s), added defensive nil checks in Go adapter, and constrained the StreamFactory API to a single minimal surface for GA. Backwards compatibility: New default behavior is opt-in via factory.NewStream with backwards-compatible helpers for legacy constructors. Migration notes included in release notes.
Priya: Please justify the cooldown default; recommend 30s not 45s. Jonas: Why not expose an advanced API for custom backoff? Suggest keeping minimal surface and allow opt-in. Marceline: Go adapter panics on nil callback during drain, please add defensive checks. Author reply: Reduced cooldown to 20s after perf experimentation; advanced API left behind feature flag for now; added nil checks to Go adapter and added unit test to cover drain edge cases. CI history: Initial CI run failed on a flaky test in typescript stream factory (race on mock timer), reran individual pipeline after adding test stabilization, all checks green. Merge notes: Squash merge after final approval from Priya and Jonas. Merge method: squash
- Introduce credential circuit scheduler to reduce reauth storms and improve retry behavior. - Add StreamFactory to Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs: consistent cancelable/checkpointable stream primitives. - New retry presets: latency-aware, conservative-auth. - Telemetry: credential lifecycle event tags for Console observability. - SDK version bumps: python 1.4.2, typescript 2.8.0, go 1.5.0

payload.body:
Motivation: In high-concurrency serving workloads the prefill->decode pipeline can collapse under transient bursts: aggressive prefill bursts saturate KV cache bandwidth and GPU kernel queues while slow decodes backpressure request handling, resulting in token stalls and increased p99 latency. Existing chunking/speculative prefill work reduces some of this but doesn't uniformly apply backpressure or coalesce KV reads when many small prefill windows target overlapping keys.

What this PR does: Implements a lightweight synchronizer that enforces adaptive backpressure between prefill and decode stages, plus a micro-chunking prefill formatter and a KV shadow coalescer. Key behaviors: (1) dynamic token-budget backpressure: the prefill stage is throttled based on the decode-stage headroom metric (decode inflight tokens + kernel queue depth) instead of a static window; (2) micro-chunking: prefill requests split into small, aligned micro-chunks (typical 8-32 token units) that allow earlier KV priming for long sequences while keeping kernel launch sizes efficient; (3) KV shadow coalescer: in-memory transient index that detects overlapping KV reads from concurrent micro-chunks and merges them into a single backend fetch if within a configurable timebound (default 6ms); (4) graceful degrade to speculative-prefill: when coalescing is not effective or KV backend is slow, the synchronizer reduces prefill aggressiveness and instructs the scheduler to fall back to decode-first for low-latency requests.

Implementation notes: single-threaded hot-path changes are minimal. New components: runtime/pipeline/backpressure_synchronizer.{cpp,h} (core logic, metrics), runtime/pipeline/microchunk_formatter.cc (split/merge heuristics), kv/shadow_coalescer.cc (in-memory coalescer w/ eviction TTL), scheduler/handoff_manager.rs (exposes headroom metric to sync). Integration points: the prefill worker obtains a BackpressureTokenLease before issuing micro-chunks; the decode worker publishes headroom updates periodically (every 1ms) and on kernel completion. Metrics added: prefill.backpressure_throttled_ratio, kv.shadow_coalesce_rate, prefill.microchunk_size_hist, pipeline.headroom_ns.

Compatibility and safety: feature is behind runtime flag --prefill-backpressure-enabled (disabled by default in release branches). Default micro-chunk sizes and coalesce window are conservatively tuned to avoid regression on current benchmarks. There is a fast-path that bypasses coalescer for prefill requests with explicit KV pinning.

Testing and perf: unit tests and integration harness added in tests/pipeline/*; end-to-end perf harness updated to exercise bursty arrival patterns and long-sequence scenarios. Local cluster runs show median token latency unchanged, p95 reduced by ~7%, p99 reduced by ~18% on mixed burst workloads, and KV backend request count reduced 12% due to shadow coalescing.

Commits (summary):
- Add backpressure synchronizer core and header, basic metrics and tests
- Implement micro-chunk prefill formatter + API for chunk leases
- KV shadow coalescer with TTL + merge logic and unit tests
- Wire scheduler headroom publishing and update prefill worker handoff
- Add runtime flag, config knobs and docs for tuning
- Fix flaky timing in coalescer tests; update perf harness scenarios

Files changed (high-level):
- runtime/pipeline/backpressure_synchronizer.cpp (.h) — core algorithm and leases
- runtime/pipeline/microchunk_formatter.cc — chunking heuristics
- kv/shadow_coalescer.cc — in-memory coalescer + eviction
- scheduler/handoff_manager.rs — headroom export stub + tests
- runtime/metrics/registry.cc — new metrics registration
- tests/pipeline/prefill_backpressure_test.cc — integration tests
- perf/harness/bursty_arrival_scenario.yaml — new harness scenario
- docs/runtime/prefill_backpressure.md — operator tuning guide

Review thread (selected):
- Alex Gomez (review): "Overall approach looks promising. A few nitpicks: can we avoid global timer wakes for headroom updates? Also please double-check the lease revocation path for prefill micro-chunks — I saw a possible race when decode worker dies mid-lease."
- Samira (author): "Addressed: switched to event-driven publish from decode completion + keep an opt-in 1ms periodic tick for coarse metrics. Added explicit revoke sequence in synchronizer and added a test that simulates decode worker crash."
- Priya Shah (review): "KV coalescer complexity looks reasonable, but the eviction TTL will be critical. Suggest exposing a percentile-based adaptive TTL later. Approving after one more safety test."
- Samira: "Added adaptive eviction test that simulates skewed key reuse; left adaptive TTL as follow-up (ENG-2011)."
- Marek Novak (review): "Bench numbers look good. Two comments on instrumentation labels (use existing metric names) and a small memory accounting bug in coalescer — please patch."
- Samira: "Fixed metric naming to match registry conventions; added unit test for coalescer memory accounting. Ran CI again."
- Linus Berg (final): "Approach and tests LGTM. Approving to merge."

CI checks: build (pass), unit-tests (pass after rerun; initial run had one flaky timing test fail), lint (pass), perf-smoke (pass), e2e (pass). Rerun history: unit-tests failed once (tests/pipeline/timing_test flaky); fixed test by relaxing timing bound and adding mocked clock in coalescer tests.

Merge: squash and merge on main. Merge commit: 8c7a3f9d5b4e2a1f3d9c1e0b4a7f2a01c3d4e5f6

Release notes: "Introduce opt-in prefill/decode backpressure synchronizer with micro-chunking and KV shadow coalescing. Reduces p99 latency and KV backend load on bursty workloads. Disabled by default; operators should enable and tune via --prefill-backpressure-enabled and microchunk/coalesce knobs. See docs/runtime/prefill_backpressure.md for tuning guidance."
Alex Gomez: Overall approach looks promising. Can we avoid global timer wakes for headroom updates? Potential race on lease revocation.
Samira Patel: Switched to event-driven publish and added explicit revoke path + crash test.
Priya Shah: Suggest exposing adaptive TTL in future. Conditional approve after safety test.
Samira Patel: Added adaptive eviction test; left follow-up ENG-2011.
Marek Novak: Minor instrumentation and memory accounting fixes requested.
Samira Patel: Fixed metric names and memory test, re-ran CI.
Linus Berg: LGTM, approving.
Introduce opt-in prefill/decode backpressure synchronizer with micro-chunking and KV shadow coalescing. Disabled by default. Tune using --prefill-backpressure-enabled, microchunk.size and kv.coalesce_window_ms. See docs/runtime/prefill_backpressure.md for details.

payload.body:
Motivation: SDKs had small but persistent differences in how credential leases, heartbeats, and resume semantics were expressed. These differences caused incidental reauth calls under load and subtle resume failures when clients transitioned between network conditions. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) an auth-lifecycle-mapper that normalizes lease/ttl semantics and provides a compact policy abstraction across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs, and (2) a compact stream facade that exposes lightweight flow-control hints, checkpointed resume tokens, and a smaller ergonomic surface for pull/push streaming usage.

What changed (high level):
- New core: auth-lifecycle-mapper (lib/core/auth_mapper.*) - single policy entrypoint that maps token metadata (issued_at, expires_in, lease_window) into standardized prefetch/refresh decisions and a human-readable policy id. SDK language bindings (py/ts/go) receive the same policy decisions via a tiny protocol shim, reducing language-specific heuristics.
- Compact stream facade: new lightweight facade across SDKs (sdk/python/redwood/stream_facade.py, sdk/typescript/src/stream/facade.ts, sdk/go/stream/facade.go). It: emits flow hints (suggested_batch_ms, soft_deadline_ms), supports checkpointed resume tokens with opaque cursors, and provides a single Read/Write/Checkpoint API set that maps to each SDK's async model.
- Telemetry: added auth.lifecyle.{prefetch,refresh,fail} events and stream.facade.{checkpoint,flow_hint} metrics with consistent tag shapes across languages to aid cross-platform tracing.
- Ergonomics: renamed a few surface methods for symmetry (Python: StreamClient.resume -> StreamClient.checkpoint_resume; TypeScript: stream.resume -> stream.restoreCheckpoint; Go: StreamClient.ResumeCheckpoint). Backwards-compatible shims are provided with deprecation warnings.
- Tests & docs: end-to-end interop tests added to perf-canary harness and new README examples for migration.

Why this is different: instead of each SDK implementing ad-hoc lease/refresh heuristics we centralize decision logic into the auth-lifecycle-mapper which returns compact actions (noop/prefetch/refresh/evict) plus timing hints. This reduces redundant refresh calls and ensures identical behavior in multi-language clients. The compact facade intentionally avoids exposing heavy transport internals while giving enough control for production apps to implement checkpointed resumption and flow-control tuning.

Migration notes: the old resume APIs continue to work but will log a single deprecation warning for one release. Recommended migration steps are included below in the README changes. For teams using custom credential providers, implement the small shim api (get_token_metadata(token) -> {issued_at, expires_in}) to participate in mapped policies.

Testing & rollout: all unit tests run under CI; cross-SDK interop e2e added to perf-canary. Deployment is gradual: feature gated behind a runtime flag in Dedicated so we can A/B traffic for 48h before enabling by default.

Checklist:
- [x] Add auth mapper core and language shims
- [x] Implement compact stream facade in py/ts/go
- [x] Add telemetry and update schema registry
- [x] Add unit + interop e2e tests
- [x] Add migration docs and release notes

Files of particular interest: see files_changed for specific changesets. If you want a short demo of the new facade in Python, see examples/stream_facade_quickstart.py in this PR.
Miguel Torres (reviewer): Left a few questions around the prefetch jitter algorithm — suggested using a 10-20% backoff for bursty connections. Asha: addressed and added unit tests that simulate jitter (see test_auth_mapper.py).
Sofie Lange (reviewer): Flagged that TS public method rename needs explicit note in CHANGELOG. Asha: added changelog entry and a small codemod script for monorepo customers.
Diego Ramos (approver): Verified interop e2e locally and approved. Small comment to add a timeout guard on the Go resume path; addressed in b1c0d44.
Added auth-lifecycle-mapper (normalizes token lease and prefetch logic across SDKs); introduced compact stream facade with checkpointed resume tokens and flow-control hints; minor API renames with backward-compatible shims; updated telemetry tags for auth/stream events. See docs/sdk-migration for migration steps.
payload.title: Introduce auth-lifecycle-mapper and compact stream facade (py/ts/go)

Motivation: Customers running Dedicated fleets in multiple regions observed unfair burst admission across regions when a single global warm pool is exhausted. This causes noisy neighbors in one region to starve another region that is underutilized. We introduce a locality-aware grace-budget throttler that assigns a small ephemeral 'grace budget' per (region, tenant, priority) tuple that allows short microbursts without consuming long-lived commitments. The budget decays over a sliding window and is replenished based on recent sustained throughput and capacity signals. Design: - Per-region ephemeral budget allocation seeded from a configurable fraction of reserved capacity; budgets are orthogonal to tenant reservations. - Budget decay uses exponential decay with configurable half-life to avoid budget hoarding. - Admission checks consult locality budget first, then fall back to existing reservation/fallback paths. - Fastpath preemption: when global contention is high, low-priority budgets are shrunk proactively using a tunable aggression parameter. - Observability: new metrics expose budget size, consumption rate, decay rate, and locale hit/miss ratios. - Safety: budgets cannot increase a tenant's effective commit above a per-tenant ceiling; audit logs recorded for ad-hoc budget grants. Implementation: - New package pkg/throttler/grace_budget.go implements budget lifecycle and decay (test coverage > 90%). - autoscaler/controller.go integrates budget-aware admission in TryAcquireCapacity. - ops config supports per-region policy overrides (configs/ops/region-policies.yaml). - e2e scenario tests under test/e2e/region_grace_budget_test.go simulate cross-region microbursts and validate fairness SLAs. Rollout plan: 1) Deploy behind a feature flag default-disabled in canary region us-west-2. 2) Gather metrics (grace_budget/consumed, grace_budget/hits, grace_budget/decay) for 48h. 3) Gradually enable for additional regions and monitor SLOs. 4) If regressions observed, auto-disable and fall back to previous admission path. Checklist: - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Observability + dashboards - [x] Documentation - [x] Feature flag gate - [x] Release notes entry
Evan Martinez (reviewer): Can we quantify the default budget fraction? Also prefer using a decay constant rather than 'half-life' to align with existing metrics. -> Author: Set default to 2% of reserved capacity and added decay_constant field with migration note.
Lina Gomez (reviewer): Add a safety gate to prevent interplay with global warm pool prewarming. -> Author: Added per-region interaction tests and an explicit check preventing budget if warm pool has available warmlets.
Tomislav Novak (approver): Looks safe and well-tested. Added small nits re: logging levels; approved after changes.
Introduced a locality-aware ephemeral grace budget for Dedicated fleets to reduce cross-region starvation during short microbursts. Deployable behind feature flag. Observability metrics added under grace_budget/*.
payload.title: Introduce locality-aware grace-budget throttler for Dedicated fleet

Adds a documented KMS rotation playbook for operators and a lightweight RBAC provenance ledger to record policy mutations for audit; no behavioral change to runtime authorization by default (opt-in).
Motivation: This PR codifies two complementary compliance primitives requested in ENG-2244 and SEC-312: 1) an operator playbook and a small control-plane workflow to rotate customer-facing KMS keys (CMKs) without losing audit traceability; and 2) a compact RBAC provenance ledger that records policy diffs and the operator identity that applied them. Goals: make rotations auditable and reversible while minimizing blast radius and operational friction. Summary of changes: docs/playbooks/kms-rotation.md contains a step-by-step playbook with prechecks, staged rotation, rollback criteria, and CLI snippets for operators; control-plane/kms/rotation-controller.go implements an idempotent coordinator that sequences key rollover, writes replay-safe audit annotations, and temporarily aliases keys to avoid token churn; control-plane/rbac/provenance/ledger.go implements an append-only ledger format using gzipped JSON entries with SHA256 checksums and signatures; migrations/20251112_add_rbac_ledger_table.sql adds a small relational index for quick lookups; infra/helm/templates/rotation-job.yaml provides scheduled rotation and verification job templates; tests/integration/rotation_rbac_endtoend.test exercises rollover while requests are in-flight; sdk/python/examples/rotate_kms_key.py shows a sample tenant script; observability adds metrics kms_rotation_start, kms_rotation_success, kms_rotation_failure and an audit annotation audit.kms_rotation_note. Commit summary: Maya K: introduce kms rotation playbook and controller scaffolding; Maya K: implement provenance ledger encoding and table migration; Maya K: add helm job and CI integration tests; Fix: handle alias propagation race with KV cache warmers; Docs: polish playbook and add runbook checklist. Review conversation excerpt: Evan Brooks: Nice separation of concerns; a few comments on failure modes for alias propagation. Please add an idempotency test for the controller. Maya Kapoor: Added idempotency test and expanded alias propagation handling; see followup commit — thanks. Sana Iqbal: We need a clear CI gating step to ensure rotation metrics are emitted to the compliance pipeline before marking rotation complete. Can we add a verification job? Maya Kapoor: Added infra/helm verification job and CI integration test that validates metrics emission to the audit sink. Diego Marquez: Question about ledger size growth — are we capping retention? Also want to ensure ledger entries are signed. Maya Kapoor: Ledger entries are gzipped JSON with SHA256 checksums and signed by the control-plane signing key; retention policy is tenant-configurable (default 7y). Added schema to docs. Sana Iqbal: Approved after test and verification job updates. Evan Brooks: Approved. Merge-bot: PR squash-merged. CI history: initial CI run failed due to lint error in rotation-controller.go import ordering; subsequent run fixed and all checks green. Risk and rollout notes: Low-risk additive change. The provenance ledger is opt-in via a feature flag; the rotation controller is gated behind helm values rotation.enabled and supports rotation.dry_run for safe validation. Default behavior unchanged. Operational considerations: the playbook includes pre/post audit assertions, a checklist for legal/compliance, and an incident-playbook snippet for accidental key exposure. Ledger storage: entries stored both as HMAC-signed blobs in object storage and indexed metadata in the relational table; ledger blobs are immutable and include linked Linear ticket ID when present. Testing notes: unit tests for ledger encoding and signature verification added; an integration test simulates key rollover during in-flight requests and asserts no auth failures and correct ledger creation. Docs and runbook: docs/playbooks/kms-rotation.md describes operator steps, required permissions, rollback criteria, and sample artifact attachments for compliance review; rbac provenance spec documents delta format, checksum/signature scheme, and the reconciliation CLI control-plane/rbac/provenance/reconcile. Post-merge actions: enable feature in staging for two weeks and run a sample tenant rotation; security to review signing key handling and consider rotating the control-plane signing key; docs team to link playbook from compliance portal. Related Linear/Jira: ENG-2244, SEC-312. Merge: squash-merged into main on 2025-11-20.
payload.title: Declare KMS rotation playbook and RBAC provenance ledger

Motivation: In production canary rollouts we observed intermittent customer session disruption when a small percentage of traffic (hot canaries) experienced rapid capacity pressure or degraded resource signals. Existing rollback gates detected regressions but could still cause abrupt user-facing session resets because instances were evicted immediately. This PR implements a graceful eviction and automated rollback protocol that prioritizes session continuity while still enabling fast mitigation of bad model variants.

What this PR changes (high level): implements a session-aware drain path in the serving runtime, adds an eviction window and token-count based drain threshold, introduces a canary health probe that feeds the rollout controller, and extends the controller with a multi-metric rollback policy (latency P95, error-rate, cost-per-token anomaly). The protocol performs snapshot captures for replay on rollback and records per-session affinity so in-flight sessions can complete or be redirected to a fallback variant.

Key behaviors: 1) Opt-in by rollout annotation: rollouts that set rollout.k8s.redwood.io/hot-canary-eviction: "true" enable the protocol. 2) Graceful drain: instances marked for eviction enter a drain window (configurable, default 30s) and will only evict when remaining active token count < drain_threshold (default 1024 tokens) or time window expires. 3) Session-aware routing: session-affined requests are preferentially routed to the same model variant for the duration of the session; when eviction must proceed, the runtime attempts handoff to a compatible variant rather than immediate termination. 4) Multi-signal rollback: controller evaluates rolling window metrics and can trigger automatic rollback if configured gates breach for X consecutive windows. 5) Snapshot + replay: on automatic rollback, the controller archives a compact snapshot of recent requests for postmortem replay in the eval harness.

Implementation notes: runtime: added eviction hook in router and KV cache draining logic (runtime/eviction.go, runtime/session_affinity.go). controller: extended rollout API and controller state machine (controller/rollout/eviction_policy.go), added health probe aggregator (controller/telemetry/aggregate_probe.go). CLI/annotations: rollout annotations and defaults in docs and schema (api/v1/rollout_types.go). Observability: new metrics exported (rollout_eviction_start, rollout_eviction_complete, drain_token_count, canary_snapshot_size) plus tracing spans. Tests: unit tests for drain math and session routing, integration e2e harness that simulates hot traffic patterns and validates no session resets during graceful drains, chaos test target that simulates node OOM during canary.

Backward compatibility and opt-in: the feature is disabled by default and opt-in via rollout annotation. Existing rollouts are unaffected. The controller exposes feature flags for gradual enablement in Dedicated and Private deployments.

Commit summary: see commits below for incremental changes. CI: initial CI run had a flaky e2e (timing) which was addressed by making the drain window deterministic in the test; final CI run passed.

Related work and tickets: ENG-4821 (flow-level eviction model), ENG-4890 (rollback multi-signal gates), SUP-1002 (customer incident that motivated emergency patch).

Checklist: [x] design doc review completed, [x] unit tests added, [x] e2e harness updated, [x] metrics/tracing wired, [x] docs/annotation examples added, [x] canary in staging observed for 48h, [x] release notes drafted.

Merge notes: squash-merged after approvals; migration is configuration-only. Rollout to production will start behind a feature flag and with a 72-hour monitoring window.
Adds a session-aware eviction and automated rollback protocol for high-pressure (hot) canaries. Backwards-compatible opt-in rollout policy annotation; observability and test harness updates included.
Marco Chen (review): Can you clarify how session affinity affects cache reuse? The runtime change looks good but we need to avoid catastrophic cache fragmentation.
Aisha Patel (reply): The session affinity token is shallow and not used as a cache key by default. We added a fast-path that maps sessions to the same KV namespace to preserve cache locality; see runtime/session_affinity.go comments and unit tests.
Lena Müller (request changes): Increase observability on token-count decay calculation. I want a metric that samples pre/post drain token distribution.
Aisha Patel (reply): Added rollout_eviction_token_distribution histogram and a short note in docs with example Grafana panels.
Rajesh Iyer (approval): Verified e2e in staging; good safety checks and graceful behavior. Approving.
CI (automated): e2e/hot_canary_simulation_test.go failed on first run due to timing flake; rerun passed. All checks green.
payload.title: Graceful eviction and rollback protocol for hot canaries with session-aware drain

Motivation: Our presubmit lint and release smoke path are currently brittle when repos emit large numbers of minor infra changes. This PR adds a lightweight lint admission proxy that canonicalizes and throttles incoming lint jobs, plus a small 'release metrics bridge' to expose release window and rollout signals in our Prometheus stack. Goals: reduce presubmit noise, control lint executor saturation, and provide observability hooks for release automation.

What changed (high level): - ci/lint/proxy: small Go service that implements admission rules (whitelisting, compacting multi-file changes into single lint tasks where possible), a bounded in-memory queue with backpressure, and hooks to annotate job provenance. - ci/release/metrics: bridge that consumes release annotations (git tags + release annotation service) and emits release_window and rollout_phase metrics. - GitHub Actions: added a lint-admission step that POSTs a compacted job to the proxy before running heavy lint shards. - Helm + docs: values and runbook for deploying the proxy in Dedicated and Private.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for admission rules and compacting heuristics - [x] Integration smoke on staging runner - [x] Prometheus scrape config + dashboard tile - [x] Docs and runbook for rollback/feature flagging - [x] Linear tasks linked: ENG-2211, ENG-2219

Testing & rollout: Deployed to staging via helm chart (ci-lint-proxy.staging). Observed 60% reduction in concurrent lint jobs when cascading push hooks executed. Metrics validated against synthetic release annotations. Rollout plan: feature-flag the GitHub action to call proxy for 10% of PRs for 48h; increase to 50% if no regressions.

Backward compatibility & safety: The admission proxy is opt-in via the new action step; we can quickly disable calls in the workflow if we detect regressions. The metrics bridge is read-only and only emits aggregated signals; no writes to release control plane.
Marcus Lee: Overall good structure. Two requests: tighten the admission rule for generated-code changes and add a short-circuit for fast-path small edits.
Lena Ortiz (author): Added generated-code filter and fast-path based on file delta count (see commit 4d5e6f). Also added unit tests that exercise the fast-path.
Priya Nair: Can you add a small integration test that validates behaviour when the queue is saturated? Also please include a note about expected latency added by the admission call in the README.
Lena Ortiz (author): Added integration-saturation test using local runner and documented expected <150ms admission latency in proxy README.
Ethan Cole: LGTMs once CI stabilizes; flagged an intermittent flake in the integration smoke that I re-ran.
Marcus Lee: Approved — observed reduced presubmit churn on staging and metrics look good.
Adds a lint admission proxy that throttles and compacts presubmit lint jobs to reduce executor saturation. Adds a release metrics bridge to surface release-window and rollout_phase metrics. Opt-in via new GitHub Action step; rollout behind feature flag.
If presubmit latency spikes or lint executor falls behind after rollout, disable the admission step in .github/workflows/lint-admission.yml and revert helm chart chart values (ci.lintProxy.enabled=false). The proxy exposes /healthz and Prometheus metrics under /metrics for troubleshooting.
payload.title: Introduce lint admission proxy and release metrics bridge
