Summary: This PR adds Console backend endpoints needed for the Dedicated staged rollouts UI: (1) a stage timeline feed (including current stage, history, and state machine fields), (2) gate evidence retrieval for the currently-evaluated stage (and optionally for prior stages), and (3) action availability for promote/abort/hold based on rollout state, gate status, and caller RBAC. Motivation: Console UI currently relies on stitching together control plane plan data + telemetry + policy engine decisions, which is brittle and inconsistent across regions. The goal here is to provide a stable Console contract that matches the rollout state machine semantics and produces deterministic, auditable output with explicit “why” fields. Scope: DedicatedPoolRolloutPlan-backed rollouts only (reserved pools). No general experiment platform behavior. The endpoints are read-heavy and designed to be safe under telemetry lag; missing data is represented explicitly so the UI can render “unknown/stale” states and guide operators. Key points: 1) New endpoints (admin + customer console) - GET /console/v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollouts/{rollout_id}/timeline: returns ordered stage timeline entries plus rollout summary (state, active_stage, requested_stage, hold_reason if any). - GET /console/v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollouts/{rollout_id}/gates/evidence?stage_id=...: returns gate-by-gate evidence, including query window, observed values, thresholds, pass/fail/unknown, and reason strings (e.g., “insufficient samples”, “telemetry stale”, “policy engine evaluation error”). - GET /console/v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollouts/{rollout_id}/actions: returns available actions + required permissions + blocking reasons (e.g., “rollout is aborted”, “gate evaluation pending”, “hold requires dedicated_rollouts:write”). Note: action execution endpoints (promote/abort/hold) are handled by the control plane service (PRs 28458/28592); this PR is strictly Console backend read layer + policy. 2) Data sources and determinism - Timeline: sourced from control plane rollout plan state machine fields + audit events stream (for “who promoted/aborted/held and why”). - Gate evidence: sourced from policy-engine evaluation output (preferred) with a fallback to the telemetry query runner for debug-only fields; output explicitly indicates data_source=policy_engine|telemetry_fallback and includes staleness markers. 3) RBAC and customer visibility - Customer admins can view timeline and gate evidence for their own pools; action availability only indicates what they can do (no leaking of admin-only overrides). - Hold is exposed to internal operators by default; customer hold visibility is read-only (they can see “held” and the customer-safe reason, but cannot set/clear hold unless allowlisted via feature flag and role). 4) Observability + audit friendliness - Responses include request_id, evaluated_at, evaluation_window, and stable “reason codes” intended for audit logs and support triage (e.g., GATE_MISSING_DATA, GATE_STALE_DATA, GATE_THRESHOLD_BREACH, ROLLOUT_STATE_BLOCK). - Adds structured logging on endpoint handlers with pool_id, rollout_id, actor_type (customer|operator), and elapsed_ms. 5) Feature flagging - Endpoints are guarded by dedicated_staged_rollouts_console_read for customer traffic and dedicated_staged_rollouts_admin_read for internal tooling. Default off. API examples (trimmed): Timeline response sketch: {"rollout_id":"rpl_...","pool_id":"dp_...","state":"RUNNING","active_stage_id":"stage_10","stages":[{"stage_id":"stage_01","target":"1%","status":"COMPLETED","promoted_at":"2025-02-27T18:10:12Z","promoted_by":"user:ethan.park"},{"stage_id":"stage_10","target":"10%","status":"ACTIVE","started_at":"2025-02-27T18:26:44Z"}],"events":[{"type":"PROMOTE","stage_id":"stage_10","at":"2025-02-27T18:26:44Z","actor":"user:ethan.park","reason":"canary looked good"}]} Gate evidence response sketch: {"stage_id":"stage_10","evaluated_at":"2025-02-27T18:31:00Z","window":"5m","gates":[{"gate":"p95_latency_ms","observed":182,"threshold":220,"status":"PASS"},{"gate":"error_rate","observed":0.006,"threshold":0.01,"status":"PASS"},{"gate":"gpu_oom_rate","observed":null,"threshold":0.001,"status":"UNKNOWN","reason":"telemetry stale: last_sample_age=9m"}]} Action availability response sketch: {"actions":[{"action":"PROMOTE","available":false,"blocked_by":["GATE_UNKNOWN"],"required_permissions":["dedicated_rollouts:write"]},{"action":"ABORT","available":true,"required_permissions":["dedicated_rollouts:write"]},{"action":"HOLD","available":true,"required_permissions":["dedicated_rollouts:admin_write"],"customer_visible":true}]} Testing: - Unit tests for timeline assembly (audit + plan state ordering), gate evidence formatting (unknown/stale/insufficient samples), and RBAC filtering. - Integration tests using the staged rollouts simulator fixture (mock policy engine responses + delayed telemetry). - Added contract tests for the Console UI schema expectations (stage statuses, reason codes). Rollout plan: merge behind feature flags; dogfood via admin console first. Follow-ups: - The UI evidence panel bug in SUP-28605 was caused by telemetry tag mismatch; this PR makes missing evidence explicit and surfaces “tag mismatch suspected” hints when policy engine returns UNKNOWN but telemetry fallback sees samples without stage_id labels. - Force-promote and admin override semantics are in PR-28592; this PR already reserves reason code slots for OVERRIDE_* but does not expose the action. Risk: Moderate (Console contract changes). Mitigation: Feature flagged, additive endpoints, no changes to existing console endpoints; careful cardinality controls in logs and no raw query strings returned to customers.
Jordan Lee: Can we avoid calling telemetry directly from Console backend? We want policy engine to be the single source of truth for gate evaluation.
Chloe Martin (author): Agreed. Updated so telemetry is only used as an internal-only fallback for debugging and is never the default. The response includes data_source and we redact raw query strings for customer callers.
Allison Grant: Please ensure we do not explode cardinality in logs/metrics. Stage IDs can be high-cardinality in some customer plans.
Chloe Martin (author): Addressed: endpoint metrics are tagged only by route + actor_type. Structured logs include rollout_id/pool_id but those are sampled at 5% and excluded from metrics labels.
Kaitlyn Nguyen: RBAC: customer admins should not see operator-only hold reasons, and action availability must not leak the existence of admin overrides.
Chloe Martin (author): Implemented customer_safe_reason vs internal_reason. Also action availability is filtered to caller permissions; customers see HOLD state but not admin_write requirement details.
Logan Wright: For UNKNOWN gates due to staleness, can we include last_sample_age and a consistent reason code? Helps oncall triage.
Chloe Martin (author): Added last_sample_age_seconds and reason_code=GATE_STALE_DATA. UI can render guidance (“telemetry delayed”).
Jada Williams: Timeline ordering: promotions should be derived from audit events, not inferred from stage timestamps, otherwise retries can reorder in edge cases.
Chloe Martin (author): Updated assembler: audit events are the primary ordering; timestamps used only for display when event missing. Added a regression test for duplicate promote events with idempotency retries.
Jordan Lee: Approval after the fallback behavior change and redaction.
Allison Grant: Approved.
Kaitlyn Nguyen: Approved with note to re-review customer-visible hold semantics in PR-28592.
Logan Wright: Approved.

Motivation: Fleet reservations can oscillate under bursty tenant workloads and discrete reservation semantics. This creates transient SLA miss windows despite ample capacity. The goal of this PR is to introduce a smoothing layer for throughput contracts and a fallback adapter for reservations so that canaries and rollouts experience minimal churn while preserving throughput guarantees.

Summary of changes:
1) Add a reservoir-weighted smoothing algorithm for per-tenant throughput contracts (pkg/dedicated/contract/smoother.go). The smoother computes an exponential moving reservation target using request-rate and slot-utilization signals with separate short/long windows to capture bursts without overreacting to transient spikes.
2) Introduce reservation_fallback_adapter (pkg/dedicated/reservation/fallback_adapter.go) which mediates between desired reservation and actual slot allocation. When the adapter detects allocation lag or shortfall it applies a graceful fallback policy rather than immediately revoking or force-expanding reservations.
3) Autoscaler integration: new smoothing_policy implementation in the autoscaler decider replaces abrupt commit changes with delta-limited adjustments.
4) Telemetry: new metrics emitted (redwood.dedicated.contract.smoothed_target, redwood.dedicated.contract.raw_signal, redwood.dedicated.reservation.fallback_events) and per-tenant percentiles for smoothed utilization.
5) Operator tooling: ctl migrate_reservations can backfill smoothing state from recent utilization history; a safe, idempotent migration is provided.
6) Tests and perf: added unit tests and a dedicated e2e prow job that runs a 10-minute bursty workload to validate stability and headroom preservation.

Design notes and rationale:
- Smoothing uses dual-window aggregation (short=18s, long=180s by default) and a reservoir weight to bias towards long-term commitments when available. The dual-window avoids chasing short transients but still responds within bounded latency for sustained changes.
- The fallback adapter exposes three modes: NO_FALLBACK (legacy), SOFT_FALLBACK (preferred default), and AGGRESSIVE (for constrained clusters). SOFT_FALLBACK will throttle new allocations by a small margin, shift queued requests into warm-pool, and increment a fallback counter to show up in dashboards.
- This approach separates the responsibility of contract computation from allocator enforcement so downstream allocators can implement conservative allocation strategies without changing contract semantics.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind config flag dedicated.contracts.smoothing.enabled=false by default.
- Nightly canary on a single dedicated pool for 48h with telemetry baseline comparison.
- If telemetry shows below-1% increase in 99th percentile latency and no >5% delta in throughput for the canary tenants, progressively enable for 30% of dedicated pools, then 100% in 24h.

Migration:
- ctl migrate_reservations --smoothing-backfill reads 12h of utilization and seeds smoother reservoir; safe to run concurrently.

Metrics and observability:
- Added Grafana dashboard snapshot at observability/dashboards/dedicated_utilization.json.
- Emit structured fallback events to tracing to correlate with tenant latency regressions.

Testing and CI:
- Added unit tests covering corner cases for very sparse tenants and high-churn tenants.
- Added a perf script scripts/perf/bench_throughput_smoother.sh that reproduces an oscillating reservation pattern; results show 18-34% reduction in reservation churn under synthetic workloads.
- CI: new prow job deploy/prow/jobs/dedicated-e2e.yaml that runs the e2e smoke + perf harness; first run had a flaky assertion and was fixed by increasing test harness warmup.

Review conversation summary: "Anil Kapoor: Please clarify how the fallback adapter interacts with the warm-pool. Response: The adapter attempts to shift soft-fallback demand into the warm-pool by signaling warm-pool pre-warm hooks; if warm-pool capacity insufficient we emit a fallback_event and apply request-level throttling. Anil: Add a telemetry gauge for fallback_event.rate. Addressed in commit 4. Sofia Martinez: Add integration test that simulates allocation lag and verify no double-counting of reservation. Response: Added dedicated e2e job and a unit test simulating allocator latency in smoothing_policy_test.go. Sofia: Concerned about operator migration safety. Response: ctl migrate_reservations is idempotent and has dry-run flag; included docs/runbooks/reservation-fallback.md with instructions. Eliot Zhang: Tests look good; can we add a short note on how this impacts percent-of-capacity billing? Response: This PR does not change billing semantics; smoothing only influences allocation timing. Eliot approved and requested a perf run; perf showed expected improvement." 

Approvals and outcome:
- After two rounds of review and a successful e2e run the PR was squash-merged into main on 2026-01-21.

Impact and follow-ups:
- Ops: Recommend enabling smoothing in a limited set of nondestructive pools and monitor redwood.dedicated.reservation.fallback_events and 99th percentile latency.
- Follow-up work: add a cluster-level adaptive reservoir tuner (ENG-2101) and a Prometheus alert for sustained fallback_event rate.

Related work: ENG-1973 implemented a KV-cache aware occupancy sampler that provided the initial utilization signal used by the smoother.

Links: runbook: docs/runbooks/reservation-fallback.md, migration CLI: cmd/ctl/migrate_reservations, perf script: scripts/perf/bench_throughput_smoother.sh.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc and rationale included
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] e2e perf job added
- [x] Metrics and dashboard added
- [x] Migration tool implemented
Introduce smoothed throughput contract semantics and a reservation fallback adapter to reduce oscillation in dedicated fleet reservations. Adds new telemetry and a safe rollout plan; no user-facing API changes aside from an opt-in config flag.
This PR intentionally keeps the smoothing policy opt-in to limit blast radius. Config defaults are conservative; operators should follow the rollout plan in the runbook.
payload.title: Smoothed throughput contracts and reservation fallback adapter

payload.body:
Context: We’ve had a handful of scheduler regressions that only show up under “release branch” constraints (less churn, different knobs, tighter change control) but still need fast signal for backpressure + overload behavior. This PR adds a focused regression test suite for the runtime scheduler that is intended to run as a gating job on release/* and runtime-*-lts branches.

What’s in this PR: 1) New scheduler regression harness that runs deterministically in CI (time is simulated; no wall-clock sleeps) and asserts on queueing, fairness, and load-shedding outcomes; 2) Three core scenarios encoded as tests: (a) Mixed prompt lengths: interleave short (<=256) and long (>=4k) prefill requests and assert no starvation, bounded tail latency in simulated ticks, and correct per-tenant fairness; (b) Backpressure: saturate the prefill stage and assert correct propagation (429/overloaded errors) rather than unbounded queue growth; (c) Overload + recovery: induce overload, verify shed policy triggers at the right thresholds, then recover and verify steady-state returns without “sticky” throttling.

Why now: This is a prerequisite for Runtime LTS. Backports to release branches are higher risk in scheduling, and we need a fast, stable signal that catches the common failure modes without requiring full perf-canary runs.

Design notes: - The harness uses the existing SchedulerSim hooks and adds a thin adapter so we can feed a deterministic arrival trace and capture per-step metrics (queue depth, admitted reqs, rejected reqs, per-tenant service share). - Assertions are on invariants and relative bounds (e.g., starvation window in ticks) rather than absolute latencies. - Tests are tagged @release-branch and run in a dedicated CI job for release/* and runtime-*-lts branches; they also run on main as non-required to keep drift low.

CI / gating: - Adds a GitHub Actions workflow job `scheduler-regression-smoke` that is required on release/* and runtime-*-lts. - Runtime main: runs but is allowed-to-fail for now (we can flip once we’ve burned in for a couple weeks).

Follow-ups: - Add a “burst + jitter” arrival trace variant once we have the LTS perf gate thresholds finalized (separate PR). - Consider adding a minimal GPU-path integration test once runner capacity stabilizes (not part of this PR).

Testing: `bazel test //runtime/scheduler/tests:release_branch_regressions` and CI job `scheduler-regression-smoke`.

Risk: Low to medium. Touches test harness + CI only; no production scheduler behavior changes.

Refs: ENG-4831, Runtime LTS release branch gating work (ENG-4824).
Sofia Ivanova (review): The mixed-length test is exactly the failure mode we saw last quarter. Request: please avoid hard-coding queue depth numbers; can you assert on monotonic bounds / invariants instead? Also add a note on what “starvation window” means in simulated ticks.
Leila Farouk (author): Updated assertions to rely on invariants (no tenant goes >N ticks without admission while backlog exists) and changed queue depth checks to “does not exceed max_queue * 1.05” with explicit rationale. Added docstring explaining starvation window and how ticks map to scheduler loop iterations.
Connor O'Brien (review): For LTS gating, we need the workflow to run on runtime-*-lts and release/* branches. Can we also ensure it doesn’t require secrets so it can run in fork PRs? And can you make the job name stable for branch protection rules?
Leila Farouk (author): Workflow now uses only read-only permissions and no secrets. Job name set to `scheduler-regression-smoke` (stable). Triggers updated to include `release/**` and `runtime-*-lts` branch patterns. Added a short note in docs/ci/release-branch-gates.md.
Sahana Iyer (review): Bazel cache is missing; job time is ~18 min on cold runners. Can we add remote cache config (read-only) and mark the artifacts to upload the trace summary when it fails?
Leila Farouk (author): Added read-only remote cache (same config we use for other unit suites). On failure, the job uploads `scheduler_trace_summary.json` plus the per-test metrics dump for triage. Runtime stays under 7 minutes on warm cache in my reruns.
Marcus Reed (review): Please add a short section describing how these tests differ from perf-canary and why they won’t catch throughput regressions. I want to avoid over-selling this as a perf gate.
Leila Farouk (author): Added “Scope and limitations” to runtime/scheduler/tests/README.md: these assert correctness invariants under load patterns; perf-canary remains the throughput/latency regression gate. Also added a follow-up TODO for a minimal integration test once runner capacity is available.
Sofia Ivanova (final): Approved. Good balance of deterministic simulation and real scheduler invariants.
Connor O'Brien (final): Approved for release gating. Please coordinate with me when we flip it to required on main after burn-in.
payload.title: Add scheduler regression test suite for release branches (mixed lengths, backpressure, overload)

payload.body:
Motivation: customers in regulated environments require tamper-evident audit trails and strict enforcement of customer-managed key (CMK) locality. This PR introduces immutable audit signatures for every request that touches customer data and an enforcement layer that prevents use of CMKs outside of a tenant's allowed regions, with a configurable fallback to service-managed keys and a clear auditable decision path.

Summary of changes: adds a signing middleware that records an X-Redwood-Audit-Signature header (ECDSA over canonicalized audit metadata) stored alongside existing structured audit events; augments KMS policy evaluation to check key.region against tenant.allowed_regions and reject or downgrade to service-managed encryption based on tenant policy; wires attribute-driven RBAC v2 assertions so policy rules can reference kms_origin and audit_signature_verified.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-7890/cmk-region-lockdown-and-immutable-audit-signatures
- [x] Schema migration for audit_index.audit_signature (append-only)
- [x] Middleware + signer implementation (service key rotation compatible)
- [x] KMS policy evaluator changes and guardrails
- [x] RBAC v2 attribute mapping and tests
- [x] E2E regression tests and CI coverage
- [x] Ops rollout plan with feature-flagged canary across 5% of tenants

Risks and mitigations: signing increases latency on the critical path by ~0.4ms (benchmarked); signing is skipped for internal system-only calls via a new internal_identity flag. The KMS enforcement will block cross-region CMK use; default tenant policy is permissive with a warning mode to avoid unexpected failures. We added a migration that populates allowed_regions for legacy tenants using org metadata and a notification flow. For customers that rely on cross-region CMKs, operators can opt into a 'legacy-cross-region' shim that logs and downgrades instead of rejecting.

Rollout plan: feature flag rollouts: (1) audit signature middleware enabled for internal-only traffic (2) enable signing for canary tenants (5%) (3) enable enforcement in warning mode for 5% (4) enforcement on by default after 2 weeks and customer opt-in review.

Notes on compliance: signatures are persisted in audit_index and are immutable (append-only) and backed by retention/lock policies we coordinate with legal. This satisfies requirements for non-repudiation in our SOC2/RIMS controls when combined with key attestation.

Migration & operational playbook (short): new env vars: AUDIT_SIGNING_KEY_ROTATION_PERIOD, AUDIT_SIGNATURE_HEADER_NAME (defaults to X-Redwood-Audit-Signature), KMS_REGION_ENFORCE_MODE (disabled|warn|block). Ops runbook included in docs/ops/cmk-region-lockdown.md.

I intentionally kept the change modular: signing is an independent layer so other downstream consumers can opt in to verify signatures for high-sensitivity workflows.
Marcus Chen: Security review - can we include a proof of possession check for signing keys? Suggest adding a periodic key-attestation job.
Author(Aisha Patel): Added key-attestation job and unit tests in signer_attest_test.go; attestation runs daily and emits attest.audit_key_version metric.
Lena Rodriguez: SRE - this adds a small latency; put a histogram metric and ensure fallback on signer outage.
Author: Added audit.signer.latency histogram and circuit-breaker that switches to async-signing with eventual consistency when signer health < 0.8.
Omar Farouk: Compliance - need clear exportable evidence for audits. How do we surface signatures?
Author: Added api to fetch audit signature chain for a request id (internal-only), and docs for auditors describing verification steps.
Security bot (automated): Static analysis flagged potential time-of-check/time-of-use on allowed_regions lookup; added mutex and cache invalidation in kms/evaluator.go.
Author: Addressed - added cache TTL and lock around read-modify operations.
QA: Flaky test e2e/security/cmk_region_enforce.test.ts failed on first CI run due to race in test harness; fixed by adding deterministic test fixtures. CI re-run green.
Added immutable audit signatures (X-Redwood-Audit-Signature) and tenant CMK region enforcement. New feature flags: AUDIT_SIGNATURE_ENABLED, KMS_REGION_ENFORCE_MODE. Ops: review docs/ops/cmk-region-lockdown.md before enabling enforcement in block mode.
Unit tests for signer, kms evaluator, rbac mapping. Integration suite plus canary E2E validated: signer latency +0.4ms p50, no regression in throughput for standard workloads. Added smoke test to nightly regression suite.
If tenants see blocked encryption calls after enabling enforcement, check tenant.allowed_regions and server logs for kms_evaluator.decision. Support can toggle KMS_REGION_ENFORCE_MODE to warn to restore functionality while investigating.
Stronger non-repudiation guarantees; enforcement may break customers using cross-region CMKs — default mode is warn to surface issues before blocking. Signing keys are rotated and attested; private keys never leave HSM-backed KMS in production.
payload.title: Immutable audit signatures and CMK regional lockdown with RBAC v2 assertion

Motivation: We see recurring gaps between sampled traces and the low-level kernel warmup events that cause early bursts of GPU occupancy and token-cost variance for short inputs. This PR introduces two complementary observability features: 1) a lightweight Telemetry Stitcher that correlates sampled spans with sparse kernel warmup traces and async prefetch events; and 2) Kernel Warmup Profiling meters that surface warmup duration, first-token-latency delta, and warmup-trigger fingerprints per model variant.

What this PR does: Adds a Telemetry Stitcher service in the runtime that attaches compact context hashes to spans when available, performs best-effort enrichment of existing sampled traces with kernel-warmup fingerprints, and emits a compact warmup profile metric family (labels: model, quantization, seq_len_bucket, warmup_type). Also introduces Grafana dashboards (compact warmup heatmap + per-route first-token-delta panel), a new Prometheus exporter endpoint for warmup metrics, and a small SDK helper in the tracing instrumentation to propagate the stitcher context key.

Design notes: The stitcher is intentionally opportunistic and non-blocking; it writes a 128-bit base64 fingerprint to span attributes when it can reconcile kernel warmup events with invocation metadata. To avoid cardinality explosion we: (a) downsample fingerprint labels via an LRU-capped hashing window, (b) expose only three seq_len_buckets for metric rollups, and (c) rely on controlled sampling policies for high-cardinality routes. Warmup profiling uses reservoir sampling with a capped cardinality tag-set and emits aggregated histograms to minimize ingestion costs.

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.telemetry.stitcher (default off for Hosted for 2 weeks). We will enable in Dedicated non-critical cluster for 48 hours, validate dashboards and stepwise increase sampling. Manual kill switch in console and an autosuppress flow if metric cardinality exceeds thresholds.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for the stitcher context propagation added in redwood/serving/runtime/tracing/test_stitcher.py. E2E replay bench included that replays synthetic kernels to validate warmup-to-span correlations. Added integration test that asserts warmup metrics presence in the exporter after 100 synthetic short-invocation runs. Load test at scale was run on staging (summary in CI checks).

Migration notes: No data migrations. New metrics will appear with the warmup_ prefix and will be opt-in. SDK change is backward compatible; spans without the stitcher context are unaffected.

Related work: complements ENG-1482 (adaptive batching warmup mitigation) and ENG-1499 (token-cost attribution). Incident SUP-3421 prompted the initial investigation (root cause: fast short requests triggering kernel JIT warmup bursts).

Risks: Potential metric cardinality growth (mitigations above) and slight additional CPU usage in the runtime (<1% median p99 on staging observed).

Action items post-merge: Enable runtime flag for one Dedicated non-prod pool, validate dashboards for 72 hours, and file follow-ups for long-term agreggation (ENG-1527).
Samir Patel: Good direction. Two main asks: (1) can we avoid adding the stitcher header to every sampled span by default? (2) please add a fallback path when exporter is rate-limited.
Lena Wu: Addressed by adding a runtime flag and conditional propagation; added exporter backpressure logic with an async queue and drop-counter (see warmup_exporter.py).
Diego Martinez: Tests look solid; can you add a dashboard link in the PR description and a small note about expected cardinality?
Lena Wu: Dashboard files added and cardinality guidance included in docs/observability/warmup-profiling.md
Asha Kapoor: Approving pending CI green — watch for Prometheus scrape stability on staging after rollout.
Added Telemetry Stitcher and Kernel Warmup Profiling. New metrics: warmup_duration_seconds, warmup_first_token_delta_ms, warmup_trigger_fingerprint (compact). Grafana: Warmup heatmap and First-token delta panels. Feature is gated behind runtime.telemetry.stitcher flag. See docs/observability/warmup-profiling.md for rollout/mitigation steps.
Monitor warmup_* metric cardinality and the warmup_exporter.drop_count metric. If cardinality approaches threshold, set runtime.telemetry.stitcher=false for the pool and open ENG-1527 to centralize aggregation.
payload.title: introduce-telemetry-stitcher-and-kernel-warmup-profiling

Motivation: several inconsistencies remain across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs for session lifecycle and retry hint propagation. This has caused subtle resumption bugs during streaming reconnects (notably when a delegated credential path is used) and made it hard for platform teams to reason about retry budgets. This PR introduces an opaque SessionProxy contract (language bindings for Py/TS/Go) plus a small 'retry-spotlight' compiler that turns high-level retry policy hints into per-transport directives. The goal is ergonomics (minimize handshake surface for app devs), parity (same observable behaviour across SDKs), and opt-in stability (no automatic behavioural changes unless caller upgrades).

What I changed (summary):
- Add SessionProxy interface + minimal shim implementations in: sdk-python, sdk-typescript, sdk-go. The proxy centralizes heartbeat/refresh and exposes a single AcquireSession() call that returns an opaque handle.
- Implement retry-spotlight compiler in the TypeScript toolkit and wire a tiny portable JSON output that other SDKs can consume during bootstrap. Compiler maps our retry-dsl (temporal hints, jitter, failover precedence) into transport directives (max-retries, hedging-window-ms, circuit-salvage).
- Python/Go: add lightweight runtime to read the compiler output and apply per-request headers/metadata (no lock-step dependency on TS runtime).
- Tests: unit and integration tests for each SDK demonstrating resume semantics under credential swap and simulated network partial failures.
- Docs: add cross-sdk examples and a migration note in SDK upgrade guide.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked and reviewed (Linear ENG-2149)
- [x] Unit tests for Py/TS/Go
- [x] Integration test using local canary harness (perf-canary repo)
- [x] Add release notes entry
- [x] No breaking changes to public surface without explicit opt-in flags

Related: this ties to earlier work on credential fallback and session-lease (ENG-1991) and the stream-resume investigation from the incident on 2025-11-03.

Notes on compatibility: the SessionProxy is additive and the default SDK factories still return the legacy session behaviour unless callers request the proxy via new factory flag. The retry-spotlight compiler is an opt-in build-time toolchain addition; SDKs that don't consume the JSON output retain current retry behaviour.

If you want to prototype quickly: run packages/sdk-typescript/bin/retry-spotlight --input examples/retry-dsl.yaml --out dist/retry-spotlight.json then set REDWOOD_SESSION_PROXY=1 in the SDK factory environment to consume the spec.
Connor Blake: Overall looks good. Two asks: (1) can the TS compiler emit a minor version field in the JSON so Go/Py can validate compatibility at runtime? (2) tests: add a flakey-network job that toggles token-replacement mid-stream to validate hedging behaviour.
Priya Nair (author): Added a 'spec_version' field to the JSON and implemented a runtime validation check in Go/Python. Added the flakey-network integration test under sdk-typescript/test/integration and wired it into the canary matrix.
Sofia Martinez: Please document the performance implications of reading the compiler JSON on cold start. Suggest lazy-load behind a fast-path check to avoid adding latency to short-lived processes.
Priya Nair (author): Implemented lazy loader with a guarded fast-path (environment variable & factory flag). Updated docs with microbenchmarks (cold start + cached path).
Ethan Liu: nit: rename AcquireSession -> AcquireOpaqueSession to make intent explicit. Also, ensure Acquire returns a context manager / Closeable pattern in Go and Python to avoid leaks.
Priya Nair (author): Renamed to AcquireOpaqueSession and added Close() / __enter__ / __exit__ support. Updated tests accordingly.
payload.title: Introduce opaque session proxy and retry-spotlight compiler across SDKs

payload.body:
Motivation: several SDKs implemented lightweight token warmup / refresh in inconsistent ways (heartbeat vs periodic prefetch vs on-demand). That divergence caused production surprises when switching runtimes and resulted in duplicated logic in the platform tests. This PR standardizes a small, low-level "credential heartbeat" primitive across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs and consolidates the async streaming consumer surface so cross-lang examples and docs match.

Summary of changes (single-line description of each logical chunk):
- Add CredentialHeartbeat primitive to each SDK: a tiny, battery-friendly keepalive that emits prefetch hints and exposes an optical TTL that integrators can query. The heartbeat intentionally does not perform token exchange — it calls the configured credential provider's prewarm hook.
- Unify streaming surface: normalize the async consumer contract (pull-style iterator + typed event envelope) and add lightweight StreamBuilder helpers for ergonomic composition. The surface keeps existing helpers but adds shims so old code continues to work with deprecation warnings.
- Add cross-SDK tests and examples demonstrating prewarm flow + graceful stream restart.
- Fix a flaky Go unit test by pinning a third-party timer mock and adding deterministic jitter in the heartbeat tests.

Why this approach: keep the primitive minimal (no hidden auth behavior), provide an explicit opt-in prewarm hook, and standardize the observable stream contract so docs, examples, and internal harnesses can rely on the same semantics across languages.

Migration notes:
- Existing apps using ad-hoc prefetch should only need to switch to the new prewarm hook name (see examples) or keep current behavior via compatibility shim. Deprecation warnings will surface for one release cycle.
- Stream consumer changes are additive: the StreamBuilder is optional. If you used earlier async helpers, they remain available but will log a migration hint.

Examples (illustrative):
Python:
from redwood_sdk import Client, CredentialHeartbeat
client = Client()
hb = CredentialHeartbeat(client.cred_provider, interval_seconds=45)
hb.start()  # non-blocking prewarm hint

TypeScript:
import { RedwoodClient, CredentialHeartbeat, StreamBuilder } from '@redwood/sdk'
const client = new RedwoodClient()
const hb = new CredentialHeartbeat(client.credentials, { intervalSeconds: 45 })
hb.start()
const stream = new StreamBuilder(client).withModel('gpt-mini').build()
for await (const event of stream) { /* typed envelope */ }

Go (snippet):
hb := sdk.NewCredentialHeartbeat(cli.CredProvider(), sdk.HeartbeatOpts{Interval: 45 * time.Second})
go hb.Start(ctx)
stream := sdk.NewStreamBuilder(cli).Model("gpt-mini").Build()

Summary: This PR introduces the control-plane schema for ShadowTrafficPolicy and wiring needed to store/validate it in route/rollout configs. This is the first building block for shadow traffic (mirroring sampled requests to one or more shadow targets) and is intentionally scoped to schema/validation + migration scaffolding only (no data-plane mirroring, no telemetry). Motivation: We need a stable, versioned policy object that can be attached to routes and rollout variants, validated at write time, and safely no-oped until the data plane and telemetry paths are enabled. This keeps the upcoming work (ENG-5402/5403/5404) unblocked while making sure we don’t paint ourselves into a corner on defaults, RBAC, and security-sensitive fields. What’s included: (1) New schema objects: ShadowTrafficPolicy v1 and ShadowTargetRef. (2) Validation: sampling is bounded; max shadow targets enforced; timeouts bounded; mutually exclusive fields validated; required metadata controls validated. (3) Migration scaffolding: adds optional shadow_traffic_policy field to RoutePolicy and RolloutVariantPolicy (behind a feature flag gate) and includes a config migration stub to allow future move/rename without breaking existing configs. (4) Example configs and golden tests for JSON serialization. Non-goals: data plane mirroring behavior (ENG-5402), deterministic fingerprinting/bucketing (ENG-5403), telemetry schema + ingestion (ENG-5404), and retention/redaction implementation (ENG-5411). Design notes / defaults: Default is disabled unless explicitly enabled; fail_open defaults true (shadow path must never impact user response); sampling_mode is “deterministic” but bucketing implementation is not in this PR; shadow request headers default to allowlist-only and we explicitly disallow copying Authorization/Cookie by default; shadow targets are references (model_id / deployment_id / routing_policy_id) to avoid embedding large objects and to keep cardinality sane. Key fields (v1): enabled (bool), sampling_rate (0.0–1.0), sampling_mode (deterministic|bernoulli), max_shadow_targets (enforced globally), shadow_targets[] (target_ref + weight + per-target timeout_ms), request_copy (allowlist headers + metadata keys), fail_open (bool), shadow_deadline_ms (overall), tags (limited set; validated against allowlisted keys), created_by/updated_by (populated by control-plane). Tests: adds schema validation unit tests (happy path + boundary/invalid cases), JSON round-trip tests, and a migration test that ensures older configs without shadow_traffic_policy still parse with identical semantics. Rollout plan: This lands gated; no runtime behavior change until the routing layer consumes the policy (ENG-5402). After merge, we’ll start dogfooding in internal tenants with feature flag enabled in the control plane only.
Ethan Park: Can we make sure defaults are safe and do not accidentally enable shadowing when configs are partially specified? Specifically: if enabled is omitted, do we treat it as false? Also, please clamp/validate sampling_rate and enforce max targets at validation time, not in the consumer. Benji Okafor (author): Yup—enabled defaults false. Added explicit validation requiring enabled=true to allow any shadow_targets, otherwise we reject configs that try to specify targets while disabled (prevents accidental partial enable). sampling_rate is validated [0,1]. max_shadow_targets enforced at write time. Jordan Lee: Request copy semantics: we should not allow arbitrary header copy at first; please implement an allowlist and add validation to block known sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie, X-Api-Key). Also, tags need a bounded set so we don’t blow up cardinality downstream. Benji Okafor: Implemented header allowlist + explicit denylist for sensitive headers; validation errors include which header violated policy. Tags validated against allowlisted keys and max length; also limit to 10 tags. Paula Mendes: For Rollouts integration, do we attach this to the RoutePolicy or per-variant? We’ll need per-variant for comparing candidate variants vs control. Benji Okafor: Added optional shadow_traffic_policy field to both RoutePolicy (base) and RolloutVariantPolicy (override). RoutePolicy is the baseline; variant policy can override (e.g., add a new shadow target). Consumers can resolve effective policy via existing merge semantics. Marcus Lin: Please add audit fields placeholders (created_by, updated_by) but do not accept them from user configs; server should set. Also confirm that we’re not persisting raw prompts here. Benji Okafor: Added created_by/updated_by as server-populated fields (ignored on input); confirmed policy schema contains only routing/config knobs—no payload. Marcus Lin: LGTM once the input-ignore behavior is covered by a test. Benji Okafor: Added test for server-side fields not being accepted on input + updated docs comment. Ethan Park: One more: set fail_open default true and ensure we have an upper bound on shadow_deadline_ms (to avoid accidental huge timeouts). Benji Okafor: Done—fail_open default true; shadow_deadline_ms must be <= 2000ms and per-target timeout_ms <= 1500ms, both configurable later but bounded for beta safety. Ethan Park: Approved. Jordan Lee: Approved. Marcus Lin: Approved.
control-plane/schema: add ShadowTrafficPolicy v1 + ShadowTargetRef types
control-plane/validation: enforce sampling/timeout/target-count bounds
control-plane/config: attach optional shadow_traffic_policy to route + rollout variant policies (flag-gated)
control-plane/migrations: add v1 migration scaffolding + golden tests
docs(internal): add example configs + field-level comments
Adds control-plane schema and validation for ShadowTrafficPolicy (disabled by default) to support upcoming shadow-traffic quality evals; includes migration scaffolding for attaching shadow policies to routes/rollouts.

Motivation: Our presubmit pipeline has accrued multiple orthogonal hooks (lint, license, format, typed-interfaces) that run redundantly and slow down fast-feedback for small changes. This PR introduces a lightweight 'staged hook coordinator' that groups premerge checks into ordered stages (fastpath, safety, full) and a typed lint adapter so TS/Go/py linters expose a common interface for selective execution. Goals: 1) cut median presubmit latency for small change sets by ~40%; 2) make it trivial to opt a repo into staged lanes; 3) centralize hook configuration for easier audit and rollbacks.

What I changed (high level): Added a small Go-based coordinator (tools/presubmit/coordinator) that reads a manifest (.github/presubmit-manifest.yaml) and orchestrates staged runs against path-aware diffs. Reworked existing lint entrypoints into a typed adapter interface (tools/presubmit/adapters/typed_lint_adapter.go) so linters can be targeted to specific stages. Introduced a small Node shim (scripts/ci/stage-dispatch.ts) used by older workflows that cannot run the Go binary directly. Updated GitHub workflow templates to use the staged lanes with a fastpath that only runs quick checks (format, unit smoke, license) and schedules the longer lanes (safety/full) to run in parallel if needed.

Why this approach: A coordinator provides an explicit, auditable sequencing model for presubmit checks without forcing a monolithic rewrite of existing linters. Choosing Go for the coordinator keeps the binary small, statically linked, and easy to run in CI containers (also fits our existing preference for go-based CI helpers). The typed adapter pattern reduces ad-hoc flag parsing across many lint scripts and clarifies which linters support path filtering.

Rollback plan: The manifest is additive and defaults to conservative behavior that mirrors current presubmit. If the coordinator causes regressions we can revert the workflow templates to call the old script entrypoints. The coordinator exposes a --dry-run and --bypass flags to allow opt-out for any job until follow-ups land.

Testing: Local unit tests for manifest parsing and adapter contract added (tools/presubmit/coordinator/*_test.go). Integration smoke runs were executed on a fork with representative repo slices (redwood/core, redwood/console). Observed median presubmit time drop from 82s to 48s for small churn PRs in the test cohort. CI run history: first CI run failed on a flaky third-party linter invocation; fixed by pinning the linter runner and retrying. Final run passing. See CI summary below.

Checklist:
- [x] Coordinator binary and manifest schema
- [x] Typed lint adapter and two adapter implementations (eslint, go vet wrapper)
- [x] Workflow templates updated (.github/workflows/presubmit-staged.yaml)
- [x] Node shim for legacy runners
- [x] Tests and smoke integration
- [x] Docs: docs/dev/presubmit-staged.md

For reviewers: Focus on manifest semantics, adapter interface surface (Adapter.Run(paths []string) -> result), and the workflow changes in .github/workflows. I called out a few lines in changed_files where behavior decisions live (timeout defaults, concurrency). If we agree on semantics I will follow up with a small RFC to standardize stage names and SLAs.
Ava Chen: Nice separation of concerns. Two asks: 1) can the manifest support an allowlist for repos that must always run full-stage? 2) add a short note on how this interacts with required branch protection checks?
Author (Marisol Vega): Added support for repo-level overrides in manifest schema (see manifest.go). Branch protection note added to docs and workflow uses 'required' label to gate the PR merge. 
Diego Morales: The adapter interface looks good; suggest adding a context timeout to Adapter.Run to avoid jobs hanging under load.
Author (Marisol Vega): Added context timeout and a default of 5m for individual adapter runs; documented the variable as PRESUBMIT_ADAPTER_TIMEOUT.
Priya Kapoor: Observability request: can coordinator emit a small timing metric per stage so we can instrument slack alerts on slow presubmit?
Author (Marisol Vega): Coordinator now emits a simple prometheus textfile metric when PRESUBMIT_METRICS_DIR is set; will follow up with a small dashboard change in a separate PR.
CI bot: First run failed: eslint adapter used remote rule set (network). Workaround pinned to local snapshot and re-ran. Final CI: green.

Summary: Introduces three coordination pieces to tighten region-aware operator permissions and preserve auditable KMS usage while enabling downstream audit consumers. This PR adds: 1) an operator-scope sanitizer that enforces RBAC v2 operator allowlists and strips elevated attributes from operator-originated requests when not permitted; 2) a KMS Shield proxy that centralizes CMK selection and region pin checks with transparent retry/fallback semantics; and 3) an audit fanout dispatcher that duplicates audit events to residency-aware sinks (internal ledger + external compliance webhook) with ordering guarantees.

Motivation: Several customers requested stronger operator-scoping controls and clearer proof of KMS-residency decisions for compliance reviews (linked Linear ENG-8421). During an internal audit we found inconsistent operator headers and a handful of KMS calls missing a residency assertion. This makes post-hoc verification noisy and can require expensive manual triage. The goal is to make operator-origin assertions deterministic, ensure KMS usage is region-aware, and provide a durable, ordered audit stream for compliance consumers.

What changed: high-level code additions and config: - pkg/rbac/v2/sanitizer.go: operator-scope sanitizer logic and unit tests; enforceAllowlist(config) reads operator claims and strips disallowed attributes. - pkg/kms/proxy/shield.go: KMS Shield proxy with primary CMK selection, locale pin check, and safe fallback to customer-permitted multi-region CMKs. - internal/audit/fanout/dispatcher.go: fanout pipeline with in-order buffering and per-tenant routing. - cmd/installer/templates/kms-shield.yaml and deploy/helm/values-kms-shield.yaml: deployment defaults and feature toggle for Private installs. - docs/security/operator-scope-sanitizer.md: operator UX, migration notes, and troubleshooting tips. - tests/integration/test_kms_shield.sh: integration scenario that simulates cross-region operator and verifies audit payloads.

Compatibility & rollout: Feature gated behind config flags: rbac.operator_sanitizer.enabled and kms.shield.enabled. Default rollout is shadow mode (sanitizer logs but does not mutate) for two weeks in the canary cluster, followed by a staged enforcement rollout (tenant cohorts). KMS Shield is opt-in for Private installs via Helm value but enabled in Dedicated and Hosted clusters after signing a migration note.

Checklist: - [x] unit tests for sanitizer utilities - [x] integration test for KMS Shield happy path - [x] docs and migration guidance - [x] e2e audit verification against compliance webhook simulator - [x] security review completed

Risk & mitigation: The primary risk is unintended attribute stripping that could break operator workflows. Mitigations: shadow mode, detailed audit logs for every sanitized request, and an emergency rollback helm chart with immediate toggle of rbac.operator_sanitizer.enabled. Another risk is KMS latency introduced by the proxy; the proxy includes local caching of CMK metadata and async pre-warm of CMK handles.

Notes: This PR does not change customer-visible APIs, but it does influence how operator-originated service calls are authorized and how KMS usage is recorded for compliance. Migration steps are documented in docs/security/operator-scope-sanitizer.md and in the release notes section of this PR.
Marco Alvarez: Can we make the allowlist evaluation cache TTL configurable? also please add a short unit test for TTL expiry (addressed in commit d99a1ef).
Sasha Petrov: KMS Shield needs to propagate the residency assertion header for audits; ensure it is signed with the service key (implemented in b12d7f1).
Riley Chen: Concern about ordering guarantees for fanout under heavy load — request to add backpressure metrics and a shed policy. Added buffered queue metrics and shed policy hook in c4079b8.
Security Bot: static-scan found a potential path traversal in installer template; patched in d99a1ef (sanitized path variables).
Priya Kaur (author): Responded to comments, ran additional integration tests, and added docs for the TTL and rollback process.
Add operator-scope sanitizer (RBAC v2 allowlist enforcement), optional KMS Shield proxy with region pin checks, and an audit fanout dispatcher. Feature gated; default shadow mode rollout. See docs/security/operator-scope-sanitizer.md for migration steps and rollback procedures.

Motivation: Continuous batcher has edge cases where long-lived KV-pinned requests or heavy single-user tails can monopolize dispatch scheduling and cause starvation for short requests. Previous fixes (deadline windows, aging) reduced cases but we still see slippery fairness regressions under mixed workloads. This PR introduces a wait-score 'slab' bucketing approach plus an inexpensive redispatch slab to reduce tail-driven starvation while keeping scheduling overhead minimal.

What this PR changes (single-string description): - Add wait-score slab histogram: requests are scored by effective wait-time + penalty terms and placed into O(8) slabs instead of a full priority queue; slabs reduce contention and make redispatch cheaper. - Introduce a redispatch slab that holds recently-evicted or delayed requests and probabilistically re-injects them with jittered backoff to avoid synchronized storms. - Probabilistic starvation mitigation: a per-request decay token that increases chance of promotion for requests observed behind repeated dispatches; deterministic promotion path retained for strict deadlines. - KV pin detection hook: lightweight probe that marks requests touching long-term KV pins and biases them to the redispatch slab to avoid long-duration holds on hot lanes. - Timeout jitter window: jittered soft-timeouts to avoid thundering retransmit toward the scheduler at bucket boundaries. - Kernel hint plumbing: pipeline API accepts an optional hint (latency_sensitive|throughput_favored) used by the batcher to prefer compact batches with small latency-sensitive tokens; no model kernel changes here but this paves the way for per-batch kernel selection. - Observability: new metrics batcher.wait_score_slab_counts, scheduler.redispatch_injections, kv.pin_starvation_incidents and a dashboard template. - Config knobs: continuous.batch.wait_score_slab_count, continuous.batch.redispatch_fraction, continuous.batch.starvation_decay_ms, continuous.batch.timeout_jitter_ms. Defaults chosen conservatively to match current production tail numbers.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc referenced in Linear ENG-4512 - [x] Unit tests for slab placement and promotion - [x] Microbenchmarks for scheduling overhead - [x] E2E replay test showing improved 99th/99.9th percentiles on mixed workloads - [x] Observability dashboard PR (linked) - [x] Docs/CHANGELOG entry

Risk and rollout plan: Defaults are conservative (slab_count=8, redispatch_fraction=0.02). We will rollout as a progressive feature flag: 1) small internal canary (10% traffic), 2) cohort expand to 50% while watching scheduler.redispatch_injections and kv.pin_starvation_incidents, 3) full rollout if regressions are absent. Hot fallback: feature flag off reverts to previous queueing.

Notes: I intentionally avoided moving to a fully preemptive scheduler to keep the runtime lock-free paths and batching costs low. This change aims for <=1% CPU overhead at 8k qps while improving 99.9p by 15-35% in skewed KV workloads.
Jordan Kim: Curious about the synchronization cost of slab placement. Can we avoid atomics on the hot path?
Asha: We use per-worker slab lanes with eventual global merges; hot path does two relaxed atomics to increment slab counters. Microbenchmarks show ~0.25% overhead at 8k qps.
Riley Morgan: Please ensure the jitter distribution doesn't hide real SLO violations (i.e. don't push latency beyond client timeouts).
Asha: jitter window is soft and bounded by continuous.batch.timeout_jitter_ms (default 10ms), we added tests to prove no observable client timeout regressions in replay.
Samir Rao: Add an explicit e2e test for heavy KV-pin scenario to prevent regressions.
Asha: added tests/scheduler/test_redispatch_e2e.replay and a fixture in replay_tools.
CI bot: lint failed on first run (clang-format); author fixed style.
Riley Morgan: Approved after tests and small doc clarifications. Jordan: Approved with comment to watch redispatch_injections metric during rollout.

Microbenchmarks (internal replay harness): baseline vs this PR on mixed KV skew workload (100K requests, 10% heavy KV pins): - median latency: baseline 9.8ms -> PR 9.9ms (+1%) - 95p: baseline 17.3ms -> PR 15.1ms (-12.7%) - 99.9p: baseline 231ms -> PR 165ms (-28.6%) CPU overhead observed: +0.9% overall, scheduler CPU slice +3.4% but within headroom. End-to-end cost per token unchanged within noise. Observability replay shows drop in kv.pin_starvation_incidents by ~84%.
Unit tests added for slab placement and promotion. Integration replay verifies median/95/99.9p improvements. Canary rollout with telemetry checks, and a stress test (48h) on staging to ensure no memory growth from redispatch slab.
Flip feature flag continuous.batch.waitscore_enabled=false or revert the deployment. If redispatch_metric spike is observed, rollback immediately and investigate backpressure. Also provided a small k8s job script to toggle feature flags across clusters.
Introduce wait-score slab buckets and redispatch queue for continuous batcher; new tuning knobs for starvation mitigation; conservative defaults. Observability: new metrics and dashboards.
No API breaking changes. Added optional kernel hint field in batch metadata; server treats missing values as legacy behavior. Config defaults ensure parity with previous scheduling behavior unless feature flag enabled.
Added metrics: batcher.wait_score_slab_counts{slab=0..7}, scheduler.redispatch_injections, kv.pin_starvation_incidents, batcher.timeout_jitter_hist. Dashboard template at docs/observability/scheduler_waitscore_dash.yaml. Alerting recommendations: fire if redispatch_injections > 0.5% sustained or kv.pin_starvation_incidents > 10/min.
CHANGELOG updated with short note. Design notes in Linear ENG-4512 with diagrams. Added docs/observability and short README in src/serving/scheduler/README.md describing knobs and safe defaults.
Pipeline runs: linux-build (pass), unit-tests (pass after fix), integration-replay (pass), lint (fail -> fixed), e2e-replay (flaky -> deterministic after adding small sleep in fixture), perf-microbench (pass). One flaky test (test_replay_heavy_kv) caused rerun; root cause was test harness race and was fixed. Total CI time ~42m.
CI artifacts: scheduler_microbench_2026-02-18.html, e2e_replay_report_2026-02-19.json
Merged via squash-merge to main by Riley Morgan after approvals. Merge commit: feat(scheduler): wait-score slab + redispatch (squash). Post-merge actions: created rollout ticket ENG-4513-rollout and observability PR opened to add dashboard to tenant orgs.
5 commits: initial slab bucket implementation; redispatch slab + jitter; KV pin probe and heuristic; add metrics + dashboards; tests and docs. Commit messages: 
- feat(scheduler): add wait-score slab buckets and placement logic
- feat(scheduler): implement redispatch slab with jittered backoff
- perf(kv): add small KV-pin probe to bias long-lived requests
- test(observability): add metrics and dashboard template
- fix(ci): address lint and race in e2e replay test

All commits signed and unit-tested locally.

payload.body:
Motivation: Reduce blast radius for operator scope decisions and improve audit ingestion throughput for high-volume tenants. This PR decouples the in-memory operator-claim-cache into a small local read-optimized store plus an optional decentralized assertions layer, adds an ephemeral KMS "witness" flow for short-lived attestation tokens to reduce long-term key exposure, and implements an audit-compact pipeline that batches and cryptographically stamps compacted audit bundles before forwarding to upstream ingestion. The changes aim to improve compliance proofability while reducing KMS surface area and audit storage cost. What changed: 1) operator-claim-cache split: introduced local readonly cache with a pluggable backend adapter; added TTL-driven invalidation and a guarded refresh path to avoid thundering-herd effects; 2) kms-ephemeral-witness: new KMS orchestration component issues ephemeral attestation tokens scoped to a single request window and signs a compact claim digest; the runtime attaches the witness proof to audit bundles and to operator decision headers; 3) audit-compact pipeline: a new background service compacts per-tenant audit events into time-windowed bundles, computes a Merkle root, and signs the root with the ephemeral witness; bundles are forwarded with a minimal envelope and a compact provenance header; 4) telemetry and operator safety: added metrics for witness issuance latency, compacting throughput, cache miss hotpath counter, and new SLOs for audit-forward latency; 5) migration: graceful rollout with feature flag and canary route that falls back to full audit forwarding and long-lived KMS signing until attestation volume reaches threshold. Backwards compatibility: the attachment format is additive (new provenance header) and the full audit stream remains available for rollout; the KMS witness is optional per-tenant. Security considerations: ephemeral witness reduces lifetime of signing keys and limits key usage to a short window; the decentralized cache removes a single shared cache hotpath and reduces operator-scope blast radius. Testing: unit tests for adapter abstraction, integration tests for witness issuance against a dev KMS shim, load test scenario for compacting throughput. Rollout plan: staged canary by tenant-residency region, monitor witness error rate and audit-drop metrics before broad enablement. Related: ENG-1452, PM-322. Merge: squash and merge to main.
Jordan Lee (reviewer): How does the local cache handle clock skew across nodes? Concerned that TTL jitter could cause inconsistent denies during rollouts. Suggested adding a small leader-based refresh and documented fallback policy.
Maya Singh (author): Added leader refresh jitter and clarified fallback path in the description. The cache refresh uses a randomized backoff and a 'soft-stale' window so decisions continue to use slightly stale claims until refresh completes.
Priya Desai (security): Need explicit wording on KMS key usage limits and audit retention of ephemeral tokens. Asked to ensure ephemeral keys cannot be used for non-attestation operations.
Maya Singh (author): Confirmed the orchestrator requests KMS keys with constraints (purpose=attestation, ttl=5m, usage=sign-only) and we added enforcement in the KMS shim. Also added E2E test that rejects misuse attempts.
Alex Novak (ops): Observability looks good but the compacting service may delay forwarding under backpressure. Recommend a circuit-breaker and emergency-fallthrough to raw forwarding which we added in the latest push.
Raj Patel (approver): Verified integration tests in CI, load test results look fine for the canary size. Approving with one follow-up to add a migration playbook to runbook-owner. APPROVED

Context and motivation: We frequently run into cases where running a shadow validation pass (for quality and correctness) is not sufficient to immediately promote a model into canary traffic due to session affinity and lifecycle coupling (customers with stateful session stickiness or complex routing can't transition atomically). The Escort Orchestrator introduces a deferred-promote flow that decouples validation from promotion and provides a short-lived ‘escort’ lane that mirrors twin-shadow traffic while holding promotion in a quarantined lease until safety gates pass. This enables safer promotion for stateful and session-affine deployments without blocking other rollouts.

What this PR does (single-string body): Adds a new Escort Orchestrator controller that manages deferred promotions and twin-shadow validation, API and CLI surface for deferred promote, DB migration for escort run state, new telemetry for escort lifecycle, and e2e + load tests. Includes docs and an example manifest.

Key behavior and user-visible changes: - New Rollout API fields: escort { enabled: bool, hold_ttl_seconds: int, twin_shadow_ratio: float } and promote { deferred: bool } - CLI: rolloutctl promote --deferred applies a deferred promote which creates an escort run instead of an immediate canary swap - Escort run lifecycle: create -> mirror twin-shadow -> evaluate gates -> if gates pass within TTL then promote canary atomically; if gates fail or TTL expires, auto-revert and emit detailed telemetry - Safety gates evaluated: latency P95, error-rate delta, quality regression (scored via eval hook), and stability delta compared to baseline - Rollout state stored in new escort_runs table; runs are lease-backed and resumable after controller restarts

High-level implementation notes: - services/rollout/controller/escort_orchestrator.go: core state machine with optimistic lease updating and backoff for promote attempts - api/proto/v1/rollouts.proto: added EscortRun message and new flags; backwards-compatible changes with default values - migrations/20260213_add_escort_table.sql: escort_runs table and indexes to support efficient queries by rollout_id and created_at - pkg/safety/gates.go: extracted shared gate evaluation helpers and added twin-shadow comparator - internal/telemetry/metrics_rollouts.go: new metrics (escort_run_created, escort_run_promote_attempts, escort_run_reverts, escort_gate_violation_count) and labels for cohort and session_affinity_hint - pkg/kvcache/kv_cache_shard.go: minor change to shard indexing to avoid a race when promoting model versions during escort run rebinds - tests/e2e/escort_promote_smoke_test.go + scripts/load-tests: coverage for common error and success paths

Files changed summary (human): - Controller and state machine (majority of delta) - API proto and CLI plumbing - DB migration and model to persist escort run state - Observability (metrics, dashboard) - Examples, docs, e2e + load tests

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked and reviewed (ENG-4729) - [x] API proto backwards compatibility checked - [x] DB migration tested locally and idempotent - [x] Metrics and dashboard added - [x] e2e smoke + load tests included - [x] Docs and example manifest updated

Testing and CI: Initial CI run failed one flaky test (tests/e2e/replica_failover_test) due to unrelated test ordering; reran and all checks passed. Unit tests: 118 passed, 2 skipped. Integration: escort_promote_smoke_test (passing). Load test harness run locally against staging cluster at ~2k RPS to validate mirror load.

Review conversation (condensed): Oliver Chen (reviewer): "Very clear state machine. A few asks: 1) add a stricter TTL bound at controller side to avoid stuck runs, 2) surface gate failure reason in rollout API for operators." -- Author reply (Priya): "Added controller-side max_hold_window and included gate failure reasons in the run status (see escort_orchestrator.go and proto)." Marcus Feldman (reviewer): "Consider a limit on concurrent escort runs per cluster to avoid resource amplification." -- Author: "Added concurrent_run_limit to rollout config and enforced in controller startup path." Emily Zhang (approver): "LGTM after kv cache race fix" -- Author: "fixed in commit f6g7h8i and added unit test to reproduce previous race."

Operational considerations: - Default behavior is opt-in (escort.enabled = false) so existing rollouts unaffected - Added a cluster-wide config to cap concurrent escort runs (sane default 20) - Added dashboard with drilldowns for per-rollout runs and gate violation traces - Alerting: new alert rule for escort_run_revert_rate > 1% over 10m which surfaces regressions early

Backward compatibility and migration: API changes are additive. DB migration creates a new table and uses migration tooling; rollouts without escort fields will behave as before. Migration gate run was executed on staging; no data loss expected.

Merge outcome and post-merge actions: - PR merged by squash-and-merge. Merge commit: 9f8e7d6 - Post-merge: trigger migration job during next maintenance window (ops runbook updated). Ops checklist in docs/rollouts/escort-orchestrator.md includes rollback playbook if migration needs to be reverted.

Related work: linear ENG-4729 design thread; SUP-8842 incident follow-up where deferred promotion would have prevented a mid-promote outage.

Notes for followup PRs: - Add UI controls in Console for inspecting escort runs and manually overriding failed gates - Add a policy-driven auto-escalation that can escalate to human review instead of auto-revert - Tighten default gate thresholds after 2 weeks of telemetry

This description string intentionally includes full review thread, CI notes, and operational guidance in a single continuous blob to match PR page formatting.
Add Escort Orchestrator to enable deferred promotion from shadow to canary with twin-shadow validation; new rollout API flags; improved telemetry and safety gates.
Oliver Chen: request stricter controller TTL and gate reason visibility; Priya: added max_hold_window and gate reasons to status
Marcus Feldman: limit concurrent runs per cluster; Priya: added concurrent_run_limit and enforced at startup

Motivation: Constrained decoding using CFG/grammar backends repeatedly failed in streaming scenarios where tokenizers split grammar anchors across chunk boundaries. This surfaced as hard-to-debug 'no valid production' errors or truncated structured outputs for tool/function-calling flows. Existing fallback rules were either too aggressive (fall back to greedy sampling) or too permissive (allow invalid tokens).

What this PR does: Implements an anchored-grammar fallback strategy combined with a streaming fragment reassembler that: 1) detects when grammar anchors (literal tokens, opening braces, tool-call delimiters) are split across streaming chunk boundaries; 2) reassembles token fragments using the tokenizer's byte-level API and a small windowed buffer before invoking the CFG matcher; 3) if reconstruction fails within the buffer window, falls back to a deterministic regex-sampling backend that enforces anchor presence without permitting arbitrary tokens; 4) emits detailed telemetry and a new metric (constrained.fragment_reassembly.{attempts,succeeds,fails}) to tune buffer sizes.

Compatibility and opt-in: The feature is off by default for Dedicated/Private customers and enabled by default on hosted for 30% of traffic as a canary. Runtime is configurable via decoder.config: {"anchored_fragment_reassembly": {"enabled": true|false, "max_buffer_bytes": 48, "regex_fallback_threshold": 0.65}}. The decoder falls back to existing behavior when the tokenizer does not expose byte-level boundaries.

Implementation notes: - Added streaming buffer + fragment index in the runtime that ties to request IDs and cleans up on completion/timeouts. - Introduced an AnchorScanner that conservatively identifies anchor tokens in grammar ASTs and marks them as "fragile". - Reuse tokenizer's encode/offset map to attempt reassembly: we accept a maximum of 48 bytes of lookback; larger fragments trigger regex fallback to avoid unbounded memory. - Regex fallback implements a prioritized, deterministic sampler that only emits tokens that keep the anchor intact; it's deliberately narrower than full CFG to preserve semantics when reassembly fails. - Added conservative CPU path and a fast GPU-compatible path: GPU path avoids re-encoding where possible by consulting cached token edges.

Testing and CI: - Unit: new tests for splitter/reassembler, AnchorScanner edge cases, regex fallback determinism (added 23 unit tests). - Integration: end-to-end streaming test harness that simulates 1k fragmented streams across 12 grammars (passes). - Perf: microbenchmarks show a median inference overhead of +0.7% at max_buffer_bytes=48, 95th percentile +1.6% under high concurrency. - Canary: 30% hosted rollout with monitoring dashboards and auto-roll-back runbook.

Related: Addresses regressions surfaced by SUP-9987 and complements ENG-1283 (grammar robustness work). Does not replace larger constrained-solver redesign in ENG-1400.

Checklist: - [x] Implement AnchorScanner and reassembly buffer - [x] Add deterministic regex fallback sampler - [x] Add telemetry and dashboards - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Canary rollout config and docs snippets

Operational notes: - Consumers using custom grammars that embed binary blobs may see false positives; recommend setting max_buffer_bytes to 0 in those cases. - Metric alerts should be added for fragment_reassembly.fails > 0.5% over 1h during canary.

Rollout plan: Merge -> Canary 30% hosted (3 days) -> Evaluate metrics and error rates -> Ramp to 100% hosted -> Optionally enable default for Dedicated after feedback.

Contributors: Priya N. (author) + Diego A. (regex sampler), with reviews from Liam and Maya.
Add anchored-grammar fallback and streaming fragment reassembly to reduce constrained-decoding failures on token-boundary splits. Backwards compatible; opt-in via config. Improves stability for long-streaming schema/toolcall workloads.
Liam O'Connor: LGTM overall. A few nits on locking in stream_fragment_buffer (race on request cleanup). Please add a stress test that forces tokenizers with variable byte-length encodings.
Priya Natarajan: Addressed locking nit; added a stress test harness that runs mixed UTF-8/UTF-16 surrogate pairs and added a cleanup TTL of 5s. PTAL.
Maya Chen: Commented on regex fallback threshold semantics. Suggest making threshold 0.5 by default and moving the param into 'preserved_anchors' tuning group. Also requested a small doc blurb about Dedicated opt-in.
Priya Natarajan: Lowered default threshold to 0.5 and added Dedicated opt-in notes to docs. Responded to all comments.
Diego Alvarez: Approving after verifying deterministic outputs on sampled grammars and confirming metrics emitted as expected.

Summary: Introduce a reservoir-based preemption coordinator that tracks per-tenant preemption credits and applies a soft-backfill orchestrator to opportunistically fill freed capacity while preserving latency SLAs. Motivation: Dedicated clusters occasionally experience noisy preemption cycles that spike P99 latency for latency-sensitive tenants. Existing hard-preempt logic causes oscillations and unjustified eviction of warm slots. Design overview: 1) Preemption reservoir: each tenant is allocated a credit reservoir (configurable via FleetConfig). Credits are deducted when we preempt warm slots for higher-priority work; credits replenish at a slow, configurable rate so aggressive preemption is rate-limited. 2) Coordinator: central controller that enforces reservoir caps, simulates the cost of preemption (estimated latency/regression risk) and only issues preemption instructions when credit budget allows or when absolute safety thresholds are crossed. 3) Soft-backfill orchestrator: when capacity frees, this component posts best-effort backfill requests to lower-priority queues in a controlled, latency-aware fashion (throttled by windowed acceptance). Backfill uses predictive headroom signals to avoid thrashing warm caches. 4) Telemetry and accounting: new metrics (tenant_preempt_credit_available, preempt_attempts, preempt_success_rate, backfill_fill_pct, backfill_rejection_rate) and trace spans for preempt decision path. Rollout plan: gated behind feature flag fl_reservoir_preempt; staged rollout to 10% of Dedicated pools, monitor P50/P95/P99 and backfill success, expand to 100% over 7 days. Backout plan: disable flag -> coordinator stops issuing preemptions; drain outstanding backfill tickets. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-4721) - [x] Feature flag and config schema - [x] Coordinator core logic + unit tests - [x] Soft-backfill controller + e2e load harness - [x] Telemetry & dashboard (console change PR follows) - [x] RBAC checks for coordinator actions - [x] Integration tests in perf-canary - [x] Manual cluster soak for 48h Testing notes: unit tests cover credit accounting edgecases; integration tests run synthetic noise tenants against latency-sensitive tenants; perf-canary run showed 12% reduction in preemption frequency and 4ms P99 improvement for critical tenants under mixed workloads. Backwards compatibility: default reservoir sizes are zero for existing tenants (no behavior change) unless FleetConfig is updated. Security/ops: coordinator requires new permission preempt:write; installer will add RBAC rule when feature toggled. Migration: migration is a lightweight config bump and creation of a new telemetry namespace. Why this is different from previous autoscalers: rather than only relying on headroom signals we incorporate a bounded credit accounting layer to prevent runaway preemption and to make soft backfills behave predictably.
Ethan Li: Can we make the default reservoir size 0 to avoid accidental behavior changes? (author) Nadia: yes, default is 0 and docstring updated to make this explicit
Priya Desai: Please add a fallback path when credit store is unavailable so we don't block scaling decisions. Nadia: implemented a best-effort fallback that treats missing store as zero credits and emits a warning metric
Marco Silva: The replenishment rate seems aggressive in the proposal; can we parameterize per-tenant? Nadia: replenishment is per-tenant and uses min/max clamps; added unit tests for edgecases
Ops (comment): Ensure RBAC change is included in private-installer upgrade notes. Nadia: added k8s patch YAML and installer ticket in Linear ENG-4778
Introduce a reservoir-based preemption coordinator and soft-backfill orchestrator behind a feature flag. Enables bounded preemption behavior and controlled best-effort backfill to reduce P99 latency spikes caused by aggressive eviction. Telemetry and RBAC additions included.
1) Enable feature flag on a small dedicated pool. 2) Run e2e/perf/canary/reservoir_preempt_workload.yaml which launches mixed priority traffic. 3) Confirm preemption_attempts decrease and critical tenant P99 improves. 4) Verify backfill_rejection_rate stays below 5% in first 24h.
Feature flag fl_reservoir_preempt must be enabled per-cluster. Ensure role-preempt-patch.yaml is applied during installer upgrade. Watch metrics tenant_preempt_credit_available and backfill_fill_pct during rollout.
Console dashboard PR to visualize tenant preempt credit and backfill fill percentage (will be submitted after SDK + API surface stabilizes). Also consider a user-facing API for tenants to opt into a non-preemptible mode (future work).
