Introduces a deferred "limbo" lane for micro-cohorts; Electorate-driven quorum for promotion decisions; Rewind-credit accounting and replay hooks for safe rollback; Telemetry anchors for cross-metric consensus checks.
Motivation: Some production rollouts require holding tiny cohorts in a transient 'limbo' state until a multi-metric electorate (latency, error-rate, semantic-regression score) reaches a consensus. Existing canary and shadow primitives in redwood are expressive but assume immediate promote/rollback decisions; this PR adds a lightweight deferred lane that enables: 1) time-boxed observation windows, 2) electorate voting with configurable quorum and weightings, and 3) rewind-credit accounting so a cohort can be rewound (replayed) deterministically if a regression is later discovered. Design summary: - Controller: limbo-controller implements a simple state machine (PENDING -> OBSERVING -> QUORUM_EVALUATION -> PROMOTE/REWIND/RETAIN). - Electorate: pluggable voter adapters (telemetry, semantic-eval, infra-health) with per-voter thresholds and weights. - Rewind credits: when a cohort enters limbo, we snapshot request traces and assign replay credits proportional to cohort size and time-in-limbo; credits are consumed by a deterministic replay worker which attaches original request metadata for audit and bisect. - Safety: explicit holdpoints, max-limbo TTL, fast-path preempt for severe infra signals. - API: rollout manifest gains a `limbo` stanza (duration, electorate, quorum, replay_policy). - Observability: new dashboards and events (limbo-entered, voter-result, rewind-executed) and tracing hooks. Checklist and migration notes: - [x] Controller runtime wiring and leader-election safe-guard - [x] Manifest schema bump with backward-compatible parsing - [x] Telemetry voter using existing SLO service hooks - [x] Replay worker with deterministic ordering and idempotency markers - [x] End-to-end sim harness tests - [x] Docs and rollout playbook update Testing done: - Unit tests for state transitions and electorate math (coverage added). - Canary-sim: multiple simulated cohorts across skewed latency distributions; validated quorum decisions match offline evaluator. - End-to-end on staging: promoted to a 2% cohort in staging; manually triggered rewinds validated replay integrity. - Fuzz runs for voter timeouts and partial failures. Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind org flag off by default. - Gradual enable for a few internal customers, monitor limbo metrics for 48h, then wider enable. Metrics and rollback conditions: - Primary metrics used by electorate: p95 latency delta, errored requests ratio, semantic-regression (prompt-based eval) delta. - Quorum rules: default 66% weighted votes to promote; any single infra voter veto results in immediate rewind. - Rewind policy: automated rewind if semantic-regression > 2% or error ratio spikes > 0.5% within 30m post-promote. Compatibility: - Manifest parsing is tolerant: unknown `limbo` stanza ignored for older controllers. - Replay artifacts stored in existing audit-bucket with a new prefix; retention follows org policy. Related work and context: builds on ENG-2319 (cohort instrumentation) and ENG-2548 (semantic regression pipeline). This aims to close the gap between immediate rollouts and manual human-latched promotions by providing deterministic rewind paths and electorate-backed decisions.
Maya Rodriguez: Requesting clearer failure-mode behavior for partial voter timeouts — who decides when a timeout counts as abstain vs fail?
Avery Chen: Reply: added abstain policy with configurable timeout window and default 'abstain' semantics in electorate adapter; documented in manifest schema notes.
Samir Patel: Small nit — the replay prefix migration SQL should be idempotent, wrap in IF NOT EXISTS. Also can we gate archive retention via org policy?
Avery Chen: Fixed migration to use safe-create pattern and added config flag for retention TTL (default to org policy).
Lila Thompson: Approved after seeing deterministic ordering fix and added e2e test asserting idempotency markers.
CI Bot: e2e-rollout-sim failed on first run due to flaky sim timeout — re-run triggered by author.
Avery Chen: Re-ran e2e sim and addressed timeout by increasing harness backoff and adding better cancellation wiring.

Context: We’ve had multiple demo-impacting incidents where the Console looked empty or latency/errors spiked and the field only noticed mid-call (see SUP-4189 empty dashboards + SUP-4127 429 throttling). This PR adds demo-specific dashboards and alert routing so that demo regressions page the right audience (SEs/GT-Motion) without polluting production on-call. Scope: (1) create a small set of demo environment dashboards with “is the demo healthy right now?” signals, (2) add alert rules tuned for synthetic traffic and short-lived spikes, and (3) route notifications to a GTM-friendly Slack channel with clear runbook links and ownership. What’s included: Dashboard pack ("Demo Tenant – Overview" / "Demo Tenant – API Health" / "Demo Tenant – Console Ingestion") with defaults pinned to the demo org + seeded project tags; Widgets include request rate, p50/p95/p99 latency by route, 4xx/5xx breakdown, streaming disconnect rate, quota rejections (429) by key scope, fallback events by region/model-family, and dashboard freshness (last_ingested_at lag). Alerting: new alert group "demo-env" with rules: Demo API error rate (5xx > 1% for 5m, gated by rps>0.5), Demo 429 rate (429 > 0.5% for 5m, gated by rps>1), Streaming disconnect regression (disconnects > baseline+3σ for 10m), Console ingestion lag (lag > 6m for 10m), Synthetic traffic generator missing (no heartbeat event for 10m during business hours), and Demo route pinned model unavailable (pin resolution failures > 0 for 2m). Tuning notes: demo env is intentionally bursty (parallel demos + resets). Rules use: a) gating by RPS and business-hours schedule, b) separate severities (sev3 informational vs sev2 demo-blocking), and c) longer evaluation windows for ingestion lag to avoid false positives during reset. Summary: This PR implements three coordinated pieces to improve OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity and streaming stability: 1) a stream buffering layer that reduces partial-fragment dropouts and stabilizes function_call/tool-call handoffs under high concurrency, 2) a role normalizer that canonicalizes role aliases (assistant/ai/bot -> assistant; human/user/client -> user) and enforces role hygiene when migrating from legacy param shapes, and 3) a logprob_passthrough toggle that preserves token-level logprobs coming from model backends and surfaces them through the OpenAI-compatible envelope when enabled.

Motivation: Customers reported intermittent missing logprobs in streamed fragments and tool-call framing jitter when the KV cache prefetch overlapped with first-token emission. At the same time, a few customers rely on loose role naming ("bot", "human") which resulted in inconsistent behavior during assistant routing and stop token application.

Goals: - Eliminate stream fragment dropouts and reduce observed rebuffer events by >90% in canary workloads - Provide a safe, opt-in way to preserve provider-native logprob outputs for downstream evals - Make OpenAI role aliases transparent and backward compatible

Changes made (high level): - runtime/streaming/stream_buffer.rs: Introduces StreamBuffer with a windowed queue and backpressure-aware flush. Adds per-request prefetch fence for KV cache so first-token emission waits for a minimal prefetch if configured. - api/openai_adapter/v1_chat_adapter.py: Adds role normalizer function; maps legacy role names into canonical roles and emits warning telemetry when aliases are used. Adds new parameter mapping for 'logprob_passthrough' -> internal flag. - handlers/stream_coordinator.go: Integrates buffer handshake into function_call/tool-call path to ensure tool payloads are framed atomically with stream fragments. - tests/e2e/openai_streaming_stability_test.go: New end-to-end test that replays production fragment sequences with injected prefetch delays. - docs/openai_v1_migration.md: Documented role aliasing and the new logprob_passthrough flag, including examples and caveats.

Commits (summary): - Add StreamBuffer and KV prefetch fence (5 commits) - Wire OpenAI adapter to normalized roles and params (3 commits) - Stabilize tool-call framing and add end-to-end tests (2 commits) - Docs and release notes (1 commit)

Files changed (high level): - runtime/streaming/stream_buffer.rs - api/openai_adapter/v1_chat_adapter.py - handlers/stream_coordinator.go - models/role_normalizer.py - tests/e2e/openai_streaming_stability_test.go - docs/openai_v1_migration.md - several small refs and test fixtures

Review conversation (condensed): - Priya: "Can the prefetch fence be toggled per-deployment? We need to avoid global latency regressions." Author: "Yes, added a per-request hint and a global knob. Default is off for latency-sensitive customers; enabled for canaries and regressions." - Liam: "I saw a flake in CI for the tool-call framing test under race conditions." Author: "Fixed via a tighter handshake and added a deterministic scheduler in the test harness; re-ran CI." - Marisol: "Are we confident about telemetry volume from role alias warnings?" Author: "We consolidated alias warnings to sampled telemetry (1%) and emit a single aggregated counter per request batch to avoid noise."

CI summary: - unit (linux): pass - integration (k8s): pass - e2e canary replay: pass - lint/format: pass - security scan: pass

Performance and safety notes: - Canary on dedicated pool showed 0.8% median latency impact when KV prefetch is enabled, but 92% reduction in observed stream rebuffer events for the tested workloads. - Default behavior (no KV prefetch) preserves current latency profile; the prefetch fence is opt-in via API param or deployment config. - The role normalizer is backward-compatible and only rewrites role values before routing; the original role string is still available in metadata for auditing. - logprob_passthrough defaults to false; enabling it may increase payload sizes.

Migration notes: - Customers using non-standard role names do not need to change code; the adapter normalizes names automatically. We recommend explicitly using canonical roles going forward to avoid subtle stop-token mismatches in downstream tooling. - If you rely on per-token logprobs for evals, flip logprob_passthrough=true in your request to get provider-native logprobs; this flag is currently gated for enterprise plans and may require coordination.

Merge outcome: Squash and merge to main. Merged by Priya Kumar after all approvals and green CI. Backports: Cherrypick to release/2026-02 (patch) queued.

Tickets / follow-ups: - ENG-2203: Add metrics for "stream_buffer.backpressure_time" to Console dashboard - ENG-2204: Add configuration UI in Dedicated admin console for prefetch knob - ENG-2210: Run broader canary across multiple regions for edge cases
Add stream buffering resilience with KV prefetch, normalize OpenAI v1 chat role aliases, and introduce logprob_passthrough param for parity. No user-facing breaking changes.
Add stream buffering primitives; KV prefetch fence; role normalizer; logprob passthrough param; tool-call framing fixes; e2e tests and docs (total 11 commits).
Added deterministic scheduler for race reproduction; e2e replay test reproduces prior flaky trace and verifies no dropout under prefetch handshake; load tested at 200 RPS per worker for 30 minutes in canary pool.

## Context
Offline signed bundles (Redwood Private) now rely on a stable identifier to correlate: (1) the signed bundle manifest, (2) the installer’s verification/audit events, and (3) support tooling (support bundle + bundle inspection output). During pilot we had multiple “what exact build is this cluster running?” moments because the running control-plane version alone wasn’t enough to disambiguate rebuilds/RCs.

This PR introduces a single “build identifier” (`private_build_id`) and exposes it in two ways:
1) a small HTTP endpoint on the Private control-plane API that returns release metadata (intended for internal/support tooling, and for customer environments that allow local HTTP access), and
2) a build-time generated metadata file (`release-metadata.json`) included in Private build artifacts so offline tooling can read it without any network.

## What’s included
- New release metadata shape (v1):
  - `schema_version`: "v1"
  - `private_build_id`: stable identifier used in signed bundle manifest `bundle.build_id`
  - `git_sha`: commit SHA
  - `build_time_utc`: RFC3339 timestamp
  - `channel`: `stable|rc|nightly`
  - `bundle_version`: semantic bundle version (if set by pipeline)
- API endpoint:
  - `GET /api/private/release-metadata`
  - returns JSON with the above fields
  - explicit cache headers: `Cache-Control: no-store` (we’ve seen proxies cache “version endpoints” in customer networks)
- Build-time generation:
  - new build step writes `dist/private/release-metadata.json`
  - included in packaging output consumed by private bundle builder
- Wiring for audit/support:
  - adds `private_build_id` to the existing “system info” payload used by support bundle generation (so Support doesn’t need cluster access + git)

## Why both endpoint + file
- Air-gapped: support tooling may only have the bundle tarball, not a running cluster.
- Connected private/VPC: querying the cluster is simplest and avoids “what artifact was used to install?” confusion.

## Security / access considerations
- Endpoint is intended to be served only on the existing authenticated API surface. No anonymous endpoint is added.
- No customer secrets or environment configuration is returned.
- `private_build_id` is treated as non-sensitive but still useful for correlation; we avoid leaking internal build pipeline URLs.

## Implementation notes
- `private_build_id` is sourced from `REDWOOD_PRIVATE_BUILD_ID` when present (release pipeline), otherwise defaults to `<git_sha>-dev` for local builds.
- Canonical JSON generation for the file is stable across runs given the same env vars (keys ordered, UTF-8, LF), to avoid downstream signature instability when the file is included in the bundle.

## Tests
- Unit tests for env var parsing + defaulting behavior.
- Handler test for `GET /api/private/release-metadata` covering auth required + response shape.
- Golden-file test for generated `release-metadata.json` (schema v1).

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Teach `redwood-private-installer bundle inspect` to display `private_build_id` from bundle metadata if present (tracked in ENG-4826).
- Document the field in the signed manifest spec once the manifest schema PR lands.

## Checklist
- [x] No new anonymous endpoints
- [x] Stable schema versioning (`schema_version: v1`)
- [x] Added tests
- [x] Updated internal release packaging docs (comment in build script + README pointer)

Related: ENG-4822 (pipeline signing step), ENG-4826 (support tooling).
Connor O'Brien: Can we guarantee the JSON file output is deterministic? We can’t afford signature churn due to key ordering or whitespace.
Devon Price (author): Yep — file writer uses canonical encoder (sorted keys, no trailing spaces, LF) and the tests enforce it. `build_time_utc` is injected in tests; CI uses pipeline timestamp.
Jordan Lee: Please version the schema explicitly. We’ll want to evolve fields without breaking older installers/support tooling.
Devon Price (author): Added `schema_version: v1` and a small struct wrapper; endpoint + file both emit v1.
Ethan Park: Endpoint path naming — prefer keeping it under `/api/private/*` and require existing auth middleware.
Devon Price (author): Adjusted route to `GET /api/private/release-metadata` and confirmed it’s behind authn in the router.
Logan Wright: If this goes into support bundles, make sure it’s redaction-safe and doesn’t include hostname/cluster IDs.
Devon Price (author): Only build identifiers and git SHA; no environment identifiers included.

Summary: This PR introduces a lightweight 'autorun' set of RAG templates and a small local orchestration playground aimed at speeding developer onboarding and automated smoke-runs. The goal is to provide opinionated, tiny templates that wire together retrieval, a tool-calling agent, and telemetry probes so engineers can run a deterministic demo locally (devcontainer or node) and iterate on prompts, indexers, and tool stubs.

Motivation and context: We repeatedly see new users spending time wiring a minimal loop (index -> retrieval -> agent -> tool). Long-form quickstarts are great, but a small autorun scaffold reduces friction for running reproducible scenarios (useful for demos, evals, and CI smoke). This PR complements existing quickstarts by adding: 1) autorun TS templates for a single-step RAG session; 2) a tiny orchestrator to run sequences of tool-calls deterministically; 3) docsite guide and a short video link; 4) telemetry probe hooks for structured-output checks.

What I changed (high level commits):
- commit 1: feat: add autorun scaffold and example dataset (templates/autorun-ts, examples/demo-index.json)
- commit 2: feat: add lightweight orchestrator (packages/autorun-orch/index.ts) + README with run modes (local/devcontainer/ci)
- commit 3: docs: add docsite page and short runbook (docs/rag/autorun-playground.md)
- commit 4: test: add smoke CI job to exercise autorun (ci/autorun-smoke.yml)

Summary: This PR introduces the SessionCircuit adapter — a thin, cross-language surface that unifies credential windowing, retry presets, and a lightweight circuit-style session for streaming connectors. The goal is to: 1) provide a single mental model for credential refresh and short-lived leases across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs; 2) normalize retry profiles with clearer presets for interactive vs. batch streaming; 3) remove several SDK-specific shims so that session/stream ergonomics are consistent across languages; and 4) bump SDK package versions to reflect the compatibility contract.

Motivation and context: Over the past year we've accumulated multiple, slightly-different session/credential patterns across the three SDKs. That has led to mapping bugs in internal services (SUP-5312) and made polyglot clients harder to reason about. The SessionCircuit adapter provides a common behavioral contract: short-lived Lease tokens (TTL window), a circuit state (healthy/hesitant/tripped) to guide backoff decisions, and a minimal pull-stream facade for consumers. This is intentionally small: adapters are pluggable and backward-compatible; existing constructor helpers are deprecated with clear migration notes.

What changed (high-level):
- Core contract: added SessionCircuit interface (conceptual) implemented as SessionCircuitPy, SessionCircuitTS, SessionCircuitGo in the respective SDKs. These share the same lifecycle events: acquire/renew/release + onCircuitChange hooks.
- Auth + retries: standardized retry profiles (interactive, streaming, batch) and wired them into session lifecycle backoffs. Introduced a default hedged retry window for short-lived credentials to avoid thundering renewals.
- Streaming ergonomics: exposed a small PullStream facade (next, cancel, onClose) and an EventEmitter/async-iterator adapter for TS/Py to match pro-consumer patterns. Go exposes a Channel-iterator idiom.
- Parity fixes: aligned typed error enums (ErrAuthExpired / ErrSessionTripped) and common status codes across SDKs to make behavior deterministic for routing/fallback in the runtime.
- Deprecations: removed legacy session shims (SessionV1) and added Migration guide snippets in SDK docs.
- Version bumps: python 0.9.0 -> 0.9.1, typescript 1.7.0 -> 1.8.0, go v1.6.0 -> v1.7.0.

Commits (summary):
- 7c33a2f: introduce session-circuit core interfaces and tests (cross-lang spec).
- 9b2f0a1: python: SessionCircuit implementation + async iterator adapter + docs.
- 4d8b9ea: typescript: EventedStream + session lease manager + ergonomic factory.
- e52f74b: go: CircuitSessionFactory + channel iterator + typed errors.
- 0a1c4f7: common: retry preset registry, tests, CI matrix updates.
- 6f7de3b: docs: migration guide + examples + release notes.

Files changed (high level examples):
- sdk/python/redwood/session_circuit.py (new), sdk/python/streaming_async.py (adapter), sdk/python/tests/test_session_circuit.py
- sdk/typescript/src/session/circuit.ts (new), sdk/typescript/src/stream/pullstream.ts (adapter), sdk/typescript/tests/session.spec.ts
- sdk/go/session/circuit.go (new), sdk/go/stream/pulliter.go, sdk/go/errors/errs.go
- docs/sdk/migrations/session-circuit.md, docs/sdk/examples/session-circuit-quickstart.md
- ci/tooling/matrix.yml (add py/ts/go matrix for session tests)

Small illustrative snippet (python adapter usage):
from redwood import SessionCircuit
with SessionCircuit(cred_provider, retry_preset='interactive') as session:
    stream = session.open_pullstream(model='rwr/small')
    for chunk in stream:
        process(chunk)

Review notes and design decisions:
- Circuit states: healthy/hesitant/tripped — this model maps to runtime routing (fast path vs. conservative path). We debated explicit token prefetch vs. on-demand renew; settled on conservative prefetch with jitter to reduce correlated renewals.
- Backoff presets: interactive uses short jittered backoff (50-200ms), streaming uses a medium window with bounded retries, batch uses exponential floor/backoff. Presets are configurable by advanced users.
- Compatibility: the adapter implements a backwards-compatible facade: existing helper constructors still work but now log a one-line deprecation warning directing users to the new factory.

CI and testing: initial CI run failed on lint (import order) and a flaky go test that relied on time-based sleeps. I pushed two followups: fix import order and replace time.Sleep with a testable clock interface. CI rerun: all checks green (unit, integration, linters, contract-tests). Full CI summary: build (pass), unit tests (pass), integration session matrix (pass), linters (pass).

Review conversation (high level):
- Evan Park (reviewer): "Nice consolidation. Please tighten the doc examples to show migration path from SessionV1 and call out any behavioral differences for token refresh windows."
- Author (Priya): "Added migration guide and a small FAQ section. Clarified that the default window is slightly larger than the legacy V1 to reduce renew storms. Tests added to demonstrate backward-compatible behavior."
- Rosa Alvarez: "TS ergonomics look good but ensure the EventedStream doesn't leak listeners on cancel."
- Author: "Added unit tests to assert listener cleanup and a small lifecycle hook; also removed a lingering setTimeout in the adapter."
- Jonah Fischer: "Go iterator design is idiomatic but please ensure error types are annotated for easy mapping in the runtime router."
- Author: "Aligned error enums across SDKs and added mapping table in docs. Also added a couple of integration tests to exercise an end-to-end fallback scenario."

Approvals: Evan (approved), Rosa (approved after changes), Jonah (approved).

Release notes (short):
- Introduce SessionCircuit adapter: unified session/credential surface across SDKs. (non-breaking; migration guide provided)
- New retry presets: interactive/streaming/batch.
- Streaming ergonomic improvements: PullStream adapters and EventedStream for TS; async iterator parity in Py; channel iterators in Go.
- Version bumps: python -> 0.9.1, typescript -> 1.8.0, go -> v1.7.0.

Migration guidance (short):
- Most users can swap SessionV1(...) with SessionCircuit.factory(...) and opt-in to the retry_preset that matches prior behavior. See docs/sdk/migrations/session-circuit.md for examples.

Follow-ups and TODOs (tracked in ENG-1987):
- Add telemetry to measure renew jitter effectiveness in production (instrument events for renew attempts).
- Consider a global session pool for high-throughput multi-tenant hosts (design spike).
- Add more end-to-end scenario tests in perf-canary for long-running streams.

Merge outcome: after approvals and green CI the branch was squashed and merged into main on 2026-02-25. Tags and SDK package releases were staged by release tooling; package publishing jobs are scheduled to run as part of the next release window.

Notes: This PR purposefully keeps the public surface minimal and well-documented. If you want to prototype an aggressive prefetch or alternate circuit semantics, implement a custom SessionCircuitProvider and register it through the factory.

Motivation: Production workloads show oscillating token-cost vs latency tradeoffs across tenants. Existing static defaults either waste GPU time or trigger unacceptable latency tails for some customers. This PR adds two coordinated components: (1) a lightweight runtime controller called the 'cost thermostat' that adjusts batching aggressiveness and cache TTLs per-tenant based on observed unit-econ signals and SLO pressure, and (2) a 'quant steward' policy that safely recommends and phases in quantization profiles while enforcing output-quality guardrails.

Summary of changes: Adds runtime controller, new CLI and rwctl surface, telemetry hooks, unit-econ scoring, and a safety policy engine to prevent blind quant rollouts. The thermostat uses an exponential moving average of tokens-per-second, tail-p95 latency deltas, and per-tenant cost targets to nudge batch sizes and cache TTLs. The quant steward manages staged rollouts by creating short-lived candidate variants and capturing a lightweight prompt-regression score; it will pause/rollback if score drift exceeds configured thresholds.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-1847) and high-level diagrams in docs/cost-thermostat.md.
- [x] End-to-end unit tests for thermostat and steward behaviors.
- [x] Metrics (econ.unit_cost, thermostat.setpoint, steward.rollback_count) wired into observability.
- [x] rwctl command for dry-run simulation and apply.
- [x] Safety: default conservative thresholds and opt-in tenant flag.

Related: Builds on runtime batching hooks introduced earlier but intentionally avoids changing kernel selection. Implements conservative defaults and an opt-in experiment flag for customers. See Linear ENG-1847 and ENG-2053 for the decision rationale.

Commit summary: see commits field for granular entries.

Changed areas (high level): pkg/econ/thermostat.go - controller and policy; pkg/quant/steward.go - staged rollout logic and telemetry; cmd/rwctl/cost_thermostat.go - CLI dry-run/apply commands; docs/cost-thermostat.md - operator guide and recommended defaults; observability/metrics/econ_metrics.yaml - new metric definitions and dashboards; tests/econ/thermostat_test.go and tests/quant/steward_test.go - unit and integration smoke tests.

CI notes: Unit tests failed initially on steward edge-case (null prompt bin), fixed in commit 3. All checks green on final run: unit, integration (smoke), lint, and telemetry smoke.

Review & merge: Addressed reviewer feedback to add stronger guardrails, rollback telemetry, and a rwctl dry-run mode. Squash-merged into main on 2024-11-18.

Operational notes: The controller is disabled by default; enable per-tenant via tenant config or global feature flag rw.feature.cost_thermostat=true. Rollouts should start in simulate mode (rwctl cost-thermostat --simulate).

Priya Nair (2024-11-07): Question - how do we avoid oscillation when tenants have bursty traffic? Can thermostat add a cooldown or backoff?
Owen Brooks (2024-11-07): Reply - thermostat includes a configurable damping factor and exponential backoff (thermostat.cooldown_ms). Added tests demonstrating stability under synthetic burst patterns.
Lars Gunnarsson (2024-11-09): Request - quantify the rollback signal. Add a metric that captures 'steward.rollback_score' and emit the top-k prompts that triggered rollbacks for debugging.
Owen Brooks (2024-11-10): Done - steward now emits steward.rollback_score and a sampling of top rollback prompts to telemetry with PIIs stripped. Updated docs with instructions for using the prompt samples in evaluation harness.
Ethan Zhao (2024-11-12): Nit - CLI flags should be consistent with other rwctl subcommands (use dashed-names).
Owen Brooks (2024-11-12): Fixed - renamed flags to follow convention and added integration test for rwctl parsing.
Add cost thermostat controller to adapt batching and cache TTLs per-tenant; introduce quant steward for safe, staged quantization rollouts. Disabled by default; enable via feature flag or tenant opt-in. Includes new observability metrics and rwctl commands for simulation and apply.

Motivation: Our lint/test pipeline has grown multiple ad-hoc handlers for different languages and repositories. Adding new checks requires repo changes and CI config churn. Small change PRs still pay the full test/lint cost which increases build time and flakiness.

Summary: Adds a lightweight plugin system for the lint executor and a dynamic test catalog that maps changed paths to a curated set of checks. The plugin system lets teams register adapters (e.g., terraform, rustfmt, go vet, custom schema validators) without modifying the core runner. The dynamic catalog lives in a yaml manifest (test-catalog.yaml) and can be updated independently; CI computes which catalog entries apply to the PR and runs only the matching shards.

What changed (high level):
- New executor: internal/ci/lint/executor is now a plugin host which loads adapters from plugins/ (adapters are small node/ts or go shims).
- Dynamic catalog: ci/catalog/test-catalog.yaml introduced with rules (path globs, label hints, priority).
- CI pipeline: .github/workflows/ci-lint.yml updated to call the catalog resolver step and then spawn only required shards.
- Backwards compatibility shim: existing lint-wrapper scripts remain available for a transitional period; the plugin host can execute them via the provided shell adapter.
- Tooling: small CLI (bin/catalog-resolve) added to evaluate applicable catalog entries locally for debugging.
- Docs: docs/ci/plugin-runner.md and docs/ci/test-catalog.md with examples and migration guide.

Commits summary:
- a1b4c9d: scaffold plugin host and runtime API, basic lifecycle hooks (register, run, report).
- b2d33ea: add test-catalog schema and resolver CLI + unit tests.
- f7e9112: integrate catalog resolver into github action, update workflow to emit selected shards.
- 9c4b2fa: add node adapter shim for eslint/tslint + sample plugin.
- d4f011b: docs and migration guide, examples for OSS and internal teams.

Files changed (not exhaustive):
- internal/ci/lint/executor/host.go
- internal/ci/lint/adapter_interface.md
- plugins/node-eslint/adapter.ts
- ci/catalog/test-catalog.yaml
- .github/workflows/ci-lint.yml
- bin/catalog-resolve (executable)
- docs/ci/plugin-runner.md
- docs/ci/test-catalog.md

Testing & CI:
- Unit tests for the resolver and host (internal/ci/lint/*) added and passing.
- Integration smoke GitHub Action that runs the resolver on a synthetic changeset (added as a job in ci-lint.yml).
- Initial run flagged an environment-related flake in the adapter shim on Ubuntu-latest (node 18 vs node 20 mismatch). I updated the adapter to use nvm-run and pinned the action runner versions; rerun succeeded.

Review thread (high-level):
- Priya: Requested clearer upgrade path for internal teams that rely on custom scripts; I added the compatibility shim and documented the migration steps.
- Tom: Asked for telemetry points to measure adoption and skipped checks; added instrumentation hooks and a lightweight metric emission via the existing CI telemetry pipeline.
- Evan: Called out potential security implications of third-party plugins; we added a plugin vetting checklist to docs and limited host permissions (plugins run in a restricted sandboxed process).

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind the feature-flag CI_LINT_PLUGIN=on.
2) Enable for a single small repo (benchmark-lab) for 2 weeks and monitor shard selection coverage and CI time reduction.
3) Gradually onboard other repos and maintainers; plugin registry entries for internal adapters stored under plugins/ with PR review + vetting procedure.

Migration notes for consumers:
- To add a custom adapter, create a plugin under plugins/<name>/ with the adapter entrypoint and a short adapter.yaml describing inputs/outputs. See docs/ci/plugin-runner.md.
- Existing lint scripts will continue to run via the shell adapter; convert them incrementally to plugin adapters to get faster shard-level parallelism.

Operational considerations:
- Telemetry: counts of resolved catalog entries per PR, average CI time per shard, and skipped checks will be emitted (tagged by repo and catalog entry).
- Security: plugins are executed with limited environment variables and no network access by default; maintainers may request explicit allowances.
- Failure modes: if the resolver fails, the job falls back to the legacy full-lint job to ensure correctness (fail-open disabled).

Why this is different from previous work: Instead of hardcoding language handlers or expanding workflow permutations, this provides an extensible catalog and a lightweight plugin surface so teams can add checks without changing core CI logic. It targets the long tail of repo-specific linters and reduces unnecessary CI work for small changes.

Notes: The PR intentionally keeps the resolver implementation simple (no evaluation of complex expressions) to reduce surprises. Future work can add a remote catalog service and UI in the Console for global rules management.

If anything should be trimmed before rollout (e.g., remove sample node plugin), let me know and I can open a follow-up to strip samples post-adoption.
Introduces a plugin-based lint executor and a dynamic test catalog for path-aware test selection. Improves CI feedback speed for small changes and enables teams to add custom check adapters without repo changes.
Priya: request migration path -> added compatibility shim and docs; Tom: telemetry hooks added; Evan: security vetting checklist and sandboxing; Author: addressed comments, pushed follow-up commits, requested final approval.

Context: Promoting large sequence models in production can cause transient regression windows when KV caches, attention context, and model warmup are not aligned between shadow and canary lanes. This PR introduces an epochal shadow rehydration subsystem plus a transactional partial-swap controller that reduces blast radius for large model promotes by validating discrete epochs of shadow traffic with replayed state, and only performing cohort swaps when epoch-level invariants hold. Motivation: We need a low-risk path to promote heavyweight models (long context, large KV footprint, quantized variants) while preserving session affinity, deterministic failback, and quick automatic rollback when abundance of regressions are detected. High level changes: 1) new controller: rollout/controller/partial_swap_controller.go implements a 2-phase partial-swap protocol that can atomically move a subset of cohorts once an epoch passes validation gates; it includes commit/prepare semantics and a safety escrow to hold rollback metadata. 2) rehydration engine: rollout/controller/rehydration_engine.go that replays captured shadow traffic into an ephemeral rehydration environment to warm KV caches and validate token-level distributions before promotion. 3) recorder/reader: rollout/recording/* small helpers to chunk and index traffic epochs (epoch IDs are deterministic hashes of window start+policy). 4) simulation harness: rollout/sim/epochal_replayer_test.go that runs synthetic cohort traffic and verifies commit/abort flows under injected latency and partial failures. 5) metrics and alerts: observability/metrics/rollout_rehydrate.metrics registers epoch pass/fail counters, rehydrate latency histograms, and validation regression tags used by playbooks. 6) docs/runbooks/epochal-rehydrate.md runbook describing operator playbook, aborts, and postmortem steps. Checklist: - [x] Design doc attached in Linear (ENG-1229) - [x] Unit tests for controller happy path and rollback - [x] Integration harness for simulated replays (CI-only) - [x] Metrics and dashboards wired - [x] Runbook draft included - [x] Canary smoke on staging passed Summary of behavior: The controller divides shadow traffic into epochs (configurable window, default 5m). For each epoch we: 1) snapshot cohort assignments and record a replay bundle (requests + minimal metadata). 2) spin up an ephemeral rehydration session: warm the runtime with the replay bundle to populate KV caches and trigger kernel selections representative of real load. 3) run validation probes (latency percentiles, reply divergence ratio against golden baseline, and loss/score thresholds). 4) if epoch passes, mark epoch as validated and prepare commit for the cohorts included; once N consecutive epochs (configurable) pass, a transactional partial swap is executed which atomically flips the prepared cohorts to the promoted model while writing a rollback manifest. 5) on failure, cohorts remain on previous model and the system can automatically schedule dry-run rollback or escalate to operator. Safety and rollback: The prepare/commit phases create an escrowed snapshot object (small manifest) that includes input epoch digests, warmed KV checkpoints, and a deterministic revert path. A rollback executor can fast-replay the escrow snapshot to restore prior affinity semantics. Observability and SLOs: New tagging keys enable tracing per-epoch rehydration; dashboards show epoch-level pass rate, median rehydrate latency, and cohort-level divergence. We added alerts: epoch_pass_rate < 85% over 3 intervals triggers auto-quarantine and cancels pending commits. Tests and CI: There was a flaky test in attempt #1 (simulated network partition) which failed the integration job; I fixed a race in the rehydration engine (added a small mutex around ephemeral cache lifecycle) and re-ran CI. Final CI summary below. Migration and rollout plan: This change is behind a feature flag rollout.rollout.experimental.Operators will enable it for a single non-critical customer cohort for 24h, then widen coverage to 10% traffic after success, then 100% with a 2-epoch continuous pass requirement. Backwards compatibility: Existing rollout APIs unchanged; new optional fields added to rollout policies. No immediate breaking change to clients. Related work: builds on earlier shadow replays (ENG-1156) and the partial-snap swap RFC; ties into runtime warmup optimizations (ENG-1194).
Maya Chen: This looks promising — can you explain the decision to require N consecutive epochs? What if traffic is bursty and an intermittent spike causes false negatives?
Arjun Patel (author): Good question — default N=2; idea is to avoid single-epoch flakiness. We also expose epoch window size and require the operator to tune for bursty cohorts. Added a note in README about conservative defaults.
Eloise Kim: We should ensure the escrow manifests are small and don't leak PII. Are we stripping request bodies?
Arjun Patel (author): Escrow bundles contain digests and minimal metadata only (request lengths, hashed tokens). Bodies are not stored. Added unit tests to assert redaction. See rollout/recording/epoch_index.go for scrubber logic.
Rafael Sampaio: integration test failed under CI first run due to a race; the fix looks good. Please add a short comment where the mutex is used so future authors understand the lifecycle assumptions.
Arjun Patel (author): Added inline comments and an explanatory note in the rehydration_engine header.
Maya Chen: Approving once docs have a clear operator playbook and we have the alert thresholds wired.
Eloise Kim: Approving — tests and CI green.

Context and motivation: In recent incidents we observed rapid SLO re-evaluations at the regional level that produced near-simultaneous circuit openings and aggressive shedding. This PR adds a small, conservative runtime layer that smooths transient SLO gradients and a rate-cap smoothing middleware at the ingress path to reduce instantaneous pressure spikes. The design goal is to lower the probability of cascading circuit trips while preserving prompt reaction to sustained degradation.

What this changes (summary): 1) runtime/slo: introduced `GradientNormalizer` which computes a short-timescale moving-window gradient of SLO error and emits a normalized smoothing factor that downstream enforcers can consume; 2) gateway/rate_limit: added `smoothing_middleware` that converts hard instant rate-cap deltas into temporally-smoothed adjustments using the normalizer value; 3) controlplane: telemetry events for normalized SLO signals and an operator-configurable safe-rollout flag; 4) tests and docs: unit/integration tests and an operational playbook for tuning the smoothing window.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-6124) - [x] Unit and integration tests added - [x] Telemetry hooks instrumented - [x] Config flag and feature gate added for gradual rollout - [x] Canary plan documented in docs/operational/degradation_tuning.md

Testing notes: Initial CI surfaced a race in the normalizer when multiple region probes were run in quick succession; fixed by serializing the statistics collector with a lock and adding a deterministic test harness. Integration tests run across local multi-region simulator (5 regions) with both steady-state and spike workloads; results show 38% reduction in simultaneous circuit openings in the simulator with 4x synthetic spikes. Load tests validated no measurable tail latency regression under normal traffic; p95/p99 unchanged within noise.

Rollout plan: 1) Feature-flag off by default; release to canary (10% of capacity) for 48h. 2) Collect normalized_slo and circuit_open_rate metrics, evaluate for degradation or unexpected latencies. 3) Enable rate-cap smoothing at ingress for canary, then ramp to 50% for three days, monitor. 4) Full rollout if stable. Rollback is dropping the feature flag and restarting the middleware deployment; this PR includes a safe config map path for immediate disable.

Telemetry and alerting: New metric `slo.normalized_gradient` (double) and `slo.smoothing_factor` (0..1). Alert rule suggestions included in deploy/alerts/slo_smoothing_rules.yaml.

Risks and mitigations: Smoothing too aggressively could delay reaction to real outages. We kept the normalizer conservative (short window, tunable), and we added a hard override so sustained SLO breaches still trigger circuit logic after a configurable threshold.

Related: ENG-6124 (design), ENG-6140 (canary plan).
Adds a short-lived SLO-gradient normalizer and a rate-cap smoothing middleware to mitigate abrupt circuit trips across regions. Includes telemetry hooks and a safe rollout gate; reversible via config flag.
Diego Morales: Please justify the chosen smoothing window size; could we make it adaptive to traffic variance?
Aisha Patel: Answered - kept fixed short window by default for stability, added config knob and comment explaining adaptive mode is future work (ENG-6201).
Juniper Lee: Found a race during stress test where collector map was mutated without lock. Recommend serializing updates or using sharded locks.
Aisha Patel: Fixed in commit d4f6a2c; added simple mutex around stats collector and deterministic unit test to prevent regression.
Evelyn Chen: Can we ensure the smoothing middleware never increases rate caps above what the allocator intends (safety invariant)?
Aisha Patel: Confirmed middleware only scales downward smoothing factors; added explicit invariant check and a unit test asserting allocator cap is an upper bound.
Juniper Lee: Approving pending CI green
Diego Morales: Approved
Evelyn Chen: Approved - left a follow-up to consider adaptive windowing after rollout (ENG-6201).

payload.body:
Motivation: our current sampled-span coverage misses high-cost, mid-frequency invocation patterns that drive long-tail billing spikes. This PR introduces a lightweight weighted-span-sampler plus a token exposure map aggregator. The sampler biases sampling probability by a configurable weight computed from token-cost, latency anomaly score, and error-rate — allowing us to capture more signal from financially important invocations without increasing overall sampling volume. The token exposure map aggregates digest-level token and latency distributions per tenant/model/route/prompt-shape (shape = prefix length + top-k length bucket), producing a compact heatmap used by dashboards and alerting.

This is an end-to-end change: sampler in Python runtime path, aggregator in Go for the telemetry pipeline, dashboard JSON for quick visualization, and an alert rule set to reduce noisy alerts while surfacing real cost regressions. The description below is a single continuous string. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-4923) [x] unit tests added for sampler behavior [x] integration test against a small synthetic replay [x] dashboard and example queries [x] docs and runbook for SRE.

Key behaviors: the sampler exposes a 3-tier weight composition (token_cost_weight, latency_anomaly_weight, error_weight) and a global budget so expected sampled rate is stable across tenants. We use reservoir sampling with exponential decay windows to avoid bursty over-sampling. The aggregator produces weekly rollups and a near-real-time 1m index for the dashboard.

Backward compatibility & rollout: sampler is behind runtime flag sampling.experimental.weighted_span_sampler and defaults to off. Aggregator supports both new compressed ingestion and fallback to existing uncompressed schema; config toggles allow progressive enabling per telemetry cluster. Release plan in docs/token-exposure.md.

Related: SUP-1284 (customer reported unexplained token-cost drift), ENG-5021 (dashboard task), several observability infra tickets.
Owen Brooks (reviewer): The weighted formula looks reasonable, but we need clarity on how tenant-level budgets are enforced when multiple weight signals spike at once. Can we add a circuit that scales down weights deterministically?
Maya Patel (author reply): Added deterministic budget clamp and documented the scaling function in weighted_span_sampler.py. The unit tests include a stress scenario (see test_weighted_sampler.py::test_budget_clamp).
Sofia Martins (reviewer): The Go aggregator reads proto streams — can this cause a CPU hotspot if every aggregator tries to decode heavy payloads? Suggest adding a lightweight header-only index to short-circuit full decode for low-cardinality queries.
Maya Patel (author reply): Implemented header-only indexing for the common query path; full decode remains available. Added microbenchmarks and included results in the PR description.
Add weighted span sampler to prioritize cost/latency/error correlated traces; add token exposure map and dashboard to visualize per-tenant token and latency exposure. Rollout behind runtime flag; docs include runbook and upgrade guidance.
payload.title: Introduce weighted-span-sampler and token exposure map for per-tenant observability

payload.body:
Motivation: customers in regulated jurisdictions requested deterministic, auditable enforcement that a request originated from a tenant pinned to a jurisdictional policy (binary: allowed/denied), rather than relying on heuristic residency hints. This PR introduces a compact binary-claim model (tenant->geo bitmask) propagated through request headers, an ephemeral KMS binding step for short-lived keys used to sign audit envelopes, and typed audit headers so downstream consumers can reliably interpret provenance.

Summary of changes: added tenant geo-binary claim generation at auth issuance, claim validation middleware in the service gateway, a KMS ephemeral-binding controller that hands out time-limited DEK bindings scoped to tenant+region, and new audit header conventions (X-Redwood-Audit-Typed, X-Redwood-Geo-Claim). Also included is a conservative rollout plan (feature-flagged + canary routes) and an integration test harness that simulates cross-region operator calls.

Design notes: the geo-binary claim is intentionally compact: a 64-bit hex mask where each bit maps to a jurisdictional zone we enumerate in config. Consumers only need bit testing semantics ("allowed" if the tenant bit for the request's target zone is set). This reduces ambiguity compared to textual region pins and avoids per-request heavy lookups. The KMS binding flow issues an ephemeral binding object: {tenant_id, zone_mask, issued_at, expires_at, wrapped_key_reference}. The runtime presents the wrapped_key_reference to the KMS provider for unwrap using a tenant-scoped CMK; unwrapping requires operator-scoped RBAC checks.

Backward compatibility: when the feature flag is off, services behave exactly as before. When on, services that do not opt into the middleware will receive a soft-failure (audit header present with status=unbound) for 2 weeks; after that we enforce reject-on-mismatch for protected routes only. Add explicit compatibility unit tests for both paths.

Security review: the ephemeral binding lifetime defaults to 5 minutes and is configurable per-tenant. We added extra nonce entropy to the binding to mitigate replay. All unwrapped keys are zeroized on use. The middleware enforces RBACv2 policies for operator roles: only operators bound to the tenant and zone can request unwrapping. We ran threat-modeling with SEC and addressed privilege escalation vectors by requiring two-step operator attestations for cross-zone unwraps (commented in code).

Testing and CI: included new integration tests in integration/geo_binding_test.go that exercise the end-to-end path (claim issuance -> gateway validation -> ephemeral KMS unwrap -> audit envelope emission). CI shows an initial flaky test (auth-refresh timeout) which was fixed by increasing a test harness deadline; CI now passes all jobs.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged gate deploy to 10% of clusters, monitor audit-typed header rates, KV-cache hit/miss for ephemeral bindings, and KMS unwrap latencies. If unwrap error rate > 0.5% for 5m we auto-roll back to soft-fail mode.

Files/areas touched (high-level): pkg/auth/claims.go, pkg/gateway/middleware/geo_claims.go, pkg/kms/ephemeral_binding_controller.go, internal/audit/typed_headers.go, cmd/installer/feature_flags.yaml, integration/geo_binding_test.go, docs/security/geo-binary-claims.md, deployments/manifest-canary.yaml

Small illustrative snippet (middleware check):
```
// pseudo-code
if !featureFlagEnabled(ctx, "geo-binary-enforce") {
  // attach typed-audit header but do not reject
  attachHeader(res, "X-Redwood-Audit-Typed", "geo=soft-unchecked")
  return next(ctx, req)
}
if !tenantMask.test(zoneBit) {
  auditReject("geo-mismatch", req)
  return httpError(403, "tenant not allowed in target zone")
}
```

(request changes)", "Maya: Added docs mapping, and included a migration note with a script to convert textual region pins to mask bits. Reply: see docs/security/geo-binary-claims.md. (author reply)", "Greta: Security nit: ensure we have audit entries for unwrap failures with operator identity. Please add operator identity to the failing audit record. (request changes)", "Maya: Added operator identity to audit envelope and unit tests. (author reply)", "Samir: Approve after CI green. (approved)"]

Motivation: long-tail token latencies and micro-patterns inside model invocations are a leading signal for both perf regressions and cost drift, but the current token telemetry is either too heavy (full KV snapshot per invocation) or too coarse (endpoint-level aggregates). This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) an invocation spectral breakdown that classifies token emission latency into compact frequency bands (burst, steady, tail) and exposes a small set of numeric fingerprints per invocation; 2) a deferred KV hydrator that records lightweight cache-miss + hit markers inline and only hydrates full KV metadata asynchronously for sampled traces to keep telemetry CPU and network cost low. What this delivers: - Per-invocation spectral fingerprint: a 3-value vector (burst/steady/tail percentiles) plus a dominant-shape tag that lets dashboards cluster invocations with similar emission patterns. - Compact cost anchors: token-cost attribution tied to spectral bands so we can see whether tail tokens or early bursts drive cost. - Deferred KV hydrator: reduces per-request telemetry payload by ~4x in internal load tests while still allowing full context on sampled traces. Implementation notes: - New lightweight proto for spectral fingerprint attached to invocation spans (spectral.band_burst, spectral.band_steady, spectral.band_tail, spectral.shape_hint). - Telemetry path: runtime emits the fingerprint synchronously; hydrator enqueues KV fetch jobs to an internal async queue and updates trace logs when available. - Dashboard: new panels in Observability -> Invocations: spectral scatter, band heatmap, and cost-anchor stacked bars. - Alerts: new alertrule invocation-spectral-regression that watches dominant-shape drift and a low-noise alert for tail-percentile increase using an EWMA smoothing. Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind telemetry.feature.spectral and default-off for <beta> orgs. - Canary: enable for 5% of traffic for 48 hours, then 25% for 72 hours, then global. - Monitoring: dashboards include a canary health panel and hydrator queue lag. - Rollback: revert the feature flag; hydrator is async so turning off feature immediately stops extra queueing. Backwards compatibility: spectral footprint is additive to span tags and does not change existing trace shapes. Privacy: the hydrator avoids returning raw prompt content in async fetches and respects redaction policy. Checklist: - [x] Runtime: compute fingerprint and emit span tags - [x] Telemetry: add compact proto and ingestion path - [x] Deferred KV hydrator service with rate limit and backpressure - [x] Console: dashboard panels and example queries - [x] Alerts: new rules and test alerts - [x] Tests: unit tests for fingerprinting; integration test for hydrator queueing - [x] Docs: observability guide snippet and rollout steps Usage notes: sample query strings and example dashboard links are in the Files Changed section. Known limitations: very short invocations (<8 tokens) have noisy band composition and are excluded from banded metrics by the runtime. Future work: add model-architecture-aware band thresholds and automatically synthesize fingerprint baselines per-model.
Aisha Patel: Nice work overall — can you quantify expected telemetry bandwidth reduction in the PR description? The hydrator queue needs rate-limiting knobs (suggested: per-tenant QPS and global throttle).
Jorge Morales: Added numbers to the description (approx 4x payload reduction in internal load tests) and implemented per-tenant qps and a global token bucket in hydrator/service.go. PTAL.
Samir Desai: The EWMA smoothing window in alerts looks tight for high-variance tenants; suggest 15m by default and make it configurable per-tenant.
Jorge Morales: Switched alert default to 15m EWMA and added a tenant override via console. Also added test fixture for a high-variance synthetic tenant.
Elena Kovalenko: Small nit: spectral.proto should include a version field for future schema migration. Also please add a migration note in telemetry/ingest/README.md.
Jorge Morales: Added schema_version to spectral.proto and a short migration note. Thanks for catching that.
Add invocation spectral fingerprints and deferred KV hydrator to reduce telemetry overhead and provide banded token cost/latency breakdowns. New dashboard panels and an alert rule for spectral drift included. Feature gated; rollout controlled via telemetry.feature.spectral.

Adds a new rollout safety controller (Traffic Lantern) that enables fine-grained holdpoints, session-consistent shadow queues, and deterministic rewind-playback for safe cutovers. No API breaking changes; opt-in via rollout policy config.
Motivation: We need a compact, opt-in safety controller for model cutovers that operates at slice and session granularity. Traffic Lantern provides holdpoints, a lightweight session-consistent shadow queue for fidelity checks, and deterministic rewind-playback to reproduce and revert suspect slices.
Design summary: Traffic Lantern is implemented as a policy plugin to the rolls controller; it maintains an in-memory heatmap of slice acceptance rates, exposes a safety budget per rollout, and gates traffic by canonical holdpoints (pre-commit, smoke, canary, promote). The plugin integrates with the existing telemetry pipeline and emits metric anchors used by the rollout conductor.
Changes include: 1) controller/lantern: new policy implementation and config schema; 2) runtime/router: small adapter to tag session ids and mirror to shadow queue; 3) telemetry: new metric labels and a debug trace endpoint; 4) e2e and unit tests.
Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-2482) - [x] Policy schema added with default-safe values - [x] Backward compatible: Lantern is opt-in via rollout.policy.type - [x] Added e2e smoke that replays a failed canary and validates rewind-playback - [x] CI green (after a flaky test fix).
Testing & validation: Local fuzzed traffic tests, CI integration tests with synthetic heatmaps, and a staged demo in the perf-canary infra.
Rollout plan: feature flagged and staged to canaries for 48h, promote only if rollback-rate < 0.5% and latency P95 delta < 10ms for two consecutive windows.
Migration notes: Operators must add a \"lantern\" policy block to rollout specs; otherwise behavior unchanged.
Related work: builds on shadow-bridge plumbing in controller and reuses the session-lease code in redwood-router.
Security: no new network surfaces; shadow queue is internal-only and subject to existing RBAC.
TODOs: follow-up for UI visualization (Console ticket ENG-2499) and optional persisted heatmaps for long-running rollouts.
Julian Park: Nice compact design. Two asks: clarify memory bounds for the heatmap and add a short-circuit when safety budget is exhausted.
Author (Ava): Added memoryBound config and early-fail path in lantern.go; updated description and tests to cover exhaustion case.
Lina Zhang: Can we ensure mirrored shadow traffic respects sampling and does not double-count quota? Please add quota-aware enqueueing.
Author: Router adapter updated to respect sampling and a feature-flag gate; added unit tests for quota-aware enqueueing.
Rohan Gupta: e2e looks good; would like a clearer metric name for the rewind-playback event so SLO alerts can reference it.
Author: Renamed metric to rollout_rewind_playback_total and updated telemetry docs.
CI: initial run failed on flaky integ test (timeout). Subsequent run passed. Approval set by Julian and Lina.
Julian Park: Approve after fixes.
Lina Zhang: Approve.

Motivation: Customers with strict data residency and operator scopes require a single control plane to coordinate RBACv2 policy decisions, per-tenant CMK (customer-managed key) residency constraints, and high-fidelity audit trails. This PR implements an orchestration layer that evaluates RBACv2 policy templates, enforces CMK residency constraints via a residency broker, and improves audit reconciliation to detect mismatches between decision logs and key usage.

What changed: Added rbac-orchestrator service (lightweight controller) that composes policy templates, an in-memory decision cache with TTL and invalidation hooks, and a CMK residency broker that mediates KMS provider selection based on tenant residency claims. The audit pipeline was extended to include decision_id correlation, key_origin metadata, and an audit-reconciliation worker that runs nightly to surface anomalies. Configuration changes include new feature flags (rbacv2_orchestrator_enabled, residency_broker_mode) and safe defaults for on-prem/private installations.

Design notes: The orchestrator implements a deterministic evaluation order: service-level allowlist -> tenant-scoped overrides -> operator-timebound grants. CMK residency broker matches tenant claims against KMS provider capabilities and returns a signed residency_assertion header for downstream services. Audit reconciliation performs delta comparisons between decision logs (rbac decisions) and KMS key usage events; discrepancies create low-priority tickets and telemetry events.

Files changed summary (high level) and rationale: small, targeted changes in authz/, kms/, audit/ and infra/ to keep runtime impact low. No changes to the public API surface except opt-in config flags and additional audit metadata emitted.

Testing and rollout: feature-flag gated rollout with staged canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and a fallback to previous policy evaluator if the orchestrator signals an error. Backward compatibility: when disabled the system uses legacy policy evaluator.

Related work: ENG-3421 (policy templates), SEC-881 (audit hardening).
Diego Alvarez: Can the residency broker return a soft-fail mode when no matching CMK provider is available? Reply: Maya Chen: implemented a 'fallback_provider' config and documented behavior; broker will emit a telemetry event and fall back to region-agnostic managed key only when feature flag is off.
Priya Nair: Audit payload size grew—will this affect our ingestion pipeline? Reply: Maya Chen: added batching and a compressor step in audit/ingest and increased index throughput for the short window; load tests show <3% CPU increase on ingest nodes.
Samir Patel: Add a rate-limiter around the orchestrator evaluation to prevent cascading retries. Reply: Maya Chen: added token-bucket limiter, tests included.
Security review (Automated): verified that residency_assertion is signed with service key and validated at downstream call sites. Note: rotation guidance added to docs/security/rbacv2-orchestrator.md
Adds RBACv2 orchestration and a CMK residency broker to enforce tenant key-residency constraints; audit logs now include decision_id and key_origin for improved traceability. Feature gated behind 'rbacv2_orchestrator_enabled'.

Summary: Implements a lightweight "Surge Attenuation Gateway" that sits in the rollout control plane and mediates sudden traffic spikes during heterogenous staged promotions (canaries, A/B lanes, shadow funnels). Motivation: we've seen two incidents where an aggressive promotion + uneven cohort distribution caused transient overload on smaller model variants and downstream caches. This PR introduces a policy layer that enforces handshake pacing, per-cohort "grace tokens", and a short-term smoothing window so downstream allocators and model pools can stabilize before full cutover.

What it does (high level):
- Introduces a new controller component (RolloutGateway) that enforces surge budgets and handshake backoff.
- Adds per-cohort "grace tokens" allocated from a global surge budget; tokens are consumed when a cohort receives ramped traffic and replenished on cooldown.
- Adds deterministic session-affinity passthrough so sessions started during attenuation keep consistent routing until a safe commit.
- Integrates with the existing rollback-oracle: if telemetry gates trip during the smoothing window, the gateway triggers an autonomous quarantine and fast-rewind path.
- Exposes metrics and traces for surge_budget_used, cohort_backoff_seconds, handshake_failures, and attenuation_decisions to the console.
- Adds a small e2e smoke harness (simulator) that can replay synthetic bursts to validate smoothing and rollback behavior.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc and simulation results attached (Linear ENG-4123)
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] End-to-end smoke replay harness added
- [x] Backwards-compatible config (existing rollout specs ignored if gateway disabled)
- [x] Observability: dashboards, Grafana queries, and alert snippets included
- [x] Runbook notes for SRE and on-call (linked)

- feat(gateway): initial controller scaffold + policy engine (3 commits)
- feat(metrics): expose attenuation metrics and tracing spans

Files/areas changed (high level):

Testing performed: unit tests (100% for new package), integration tests against local docker-compose allocator, simulated burst e2e runs (100+ runs across different cohort size distributions). Observability validated by creating dashboard panels showing metric behavior during a synthetic surge: surge_budget_used tracks expected consumption; cohort_backoff_seconds increases for smaller cohorts.

Telemetry and alerting: added Grafana alert rule (alert: SurgeAttenuationHighUsage) that fires when surge_budget_used > 90% for 2m. Added an SLO guard that surface 'attenuation_quarantine' events to the rollout SLO channel.

Runbook (short): when attenuation quarantine occurs, SRE should: check the 'attenuation_decisions' trace, inspect cohort latency/rate changes, and if the rollback-oracle recommends auto-rewind, verify snapshot integrity and then execute the snapshot rewind playbook. The runbook contains manual override steps to bypass gateway for emergency cutovers.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Arjun Patel (reviewer): "Nice approach; can you clarify interaction with autoscaler? If gateway holds traffic, will autoscaler over-provision?"
  - Author reply (Maya): "Gateway exposes a short-lived 'attenuation window' header so autoscaler receives capped RPS signal; we also added an integration test to cover this. See tests/integration/rollout_gateway_test.go:TestAutoscalerSignal."
- Lena Rodriguez: "Please add a schematic showing token flow and replenishment policy in docs."
  - Author: "Added diagrams to docs/runbooks/attenuation_playbook.md and a small inline ASCII diagram in gateway.go header."
- Samir Kapoor: "Edge case: what if cohort affinity identifiers are ephemeral and can't be relied on? Might lead to session drift."
  - Author: "We fallback to token-bound sticky cookies for ephemeral cases and mark session as best-effort sticky; documented tradeoffs in README."

Requested changes and resolution:

- Add a feature flag to disable gateway globally: done (config flag rollout.gateway.enabled=false).

CI: All checks passed on final run: unit (pass), integration (pass), lint (pass), gosec (pass), proto-gen (pass). A flaky test in early runs was traced to simulated clock drift in test harness and was fixed by deterministic clocks in sim.

Performance impact: Microbenchmarking shows attenuation adds a median 0.6ms to control plane decision latency (acceptable for rollout windows). No changes to token path or inference path were added; this is strictly control-plane logic.

Telemetry examples (console queries):

- rollout.cohort_backoff_seconds{cohort_id="canary-42"}

Compatibility & migration notes: Existing rollout specs are untouched unless the operator enables the gateway. For Dedicated/private installs, the gateway can be configured as a sidecar or centralized controller; documentation added for both patterns.

Why this is different from previous mechanisms: instead of abrupt on/off treats, Surge Attenuation Gateway enforces a smoothing policy that considers global budget, cohort sizes, and downstream allocation signals, reducing noisy rollbacks and improving stability for heterogenous model fleets.

Merge notes: Squash-merged into main after approvals from Arjun, Lena, and Samir. Merged with CI green and post-merge smoke run completed on staging.

Follow-ups (planned):

This PR was driven by a pair of incidents in Dec-2025 where rapid promotions caused small variant thrash.
Authors: Maya Chen (lead), paired with Samir for policy tests.

Motivation: Interactive, low-token requests (chat-like workloads) suffer from per-request kernel startup and small-batch inefficiencies when prefill and decode stages are treated as rigidly separated phases. This PR implements a lightweight heuristic sampler that drives chunked prefill sizes and enables opportunistic decode-merge when the sampler predicts decode can overlap without harming KV cache locality. The change reduces mem churn from tiny kernel launches and improves p95/p99 latency under mixed workloads.

What this PR does (summary): 
- Add heuristic prefill sampler that observes request token-length distribution, recent KV hit rates, and inflight queue depth to pick a chunking strategy per-request.
- Introduce an opportunistic decode-merge path in the scheduler that merges adjacent short-decoding slices into a single kernel dispatch when safety heuristics pass (memory headroom, kv locality, and time budget).
- Handshake rate limiter: a microcontroller that prevents the prefill->decode handshake from overwhelming the decode worker pool; it enforces a token-based backoff when decode backlog is high.
- Expose kernel hint metadata so the scheduler can select a slightly different GEMM/kern path for merged-decode vs standalone-decode, improving throughput for fused slices.
- Small changes to KV cache priming: aggressive prefix warming for requests that the sampler marks as likely to decode soon (reduces cold-kv misses).
- Add perf harness and new benchmark scenario for interactive workloads (100ms/req target class).

Design notes: 
- Heuristic goals are conservative: we prefer slightly smaller merge decisions over aggressive fusion that could increase worst-case memory usage. The sampler is rules+lightweight EWMA; no ML model.
- Merge only occurs when (1) combined tokens < merge_token_budget, (2) current KV miss rate < kv_miss_threshold, and (3) memory headroom > safety_margin. All thresholds are tunable via runtime flags.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests for sampler decision logic and edge cases
- [x] Scheduler integration tests for merge/unmerge paths
- [x] Microbenchmarks comparing baseline vs new logic on 3 model sizes (small/medium/large)
- [x] Docs note for ops (flags and safe default values)
- [x] Feature gated behind runtime flag (runtime.opt.enable_heuristic_prefill)

Commits (high level):
- feat(prefill): add heuristic_sampler module and unit tests (author: Maya Patel)
- feat(scheduler): opportunistic decode merge path and handshake rate limiter
- perf(kernel): kernel hint metadata and small kernel selection path for fused decodes
- infra: add interactive workload perf scenario and CI benchmark job
- docs: newcomer notes and runtime flags documentation

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/prefill/heuristic_sampler.cc (new) and heuristic_sampler.h (new)
- runtime/scheduler/decode_merge_scheduler.cc (new) and decode_merge_scheduler.h (new)
- runtime/scheduler/handshake_rate_limiter.cc (new)
- runtime/kernel/hint_registry.cc (small additions)
- runtime/kv/cache_warmup.cc (tweak to accept sampler hints)
- tests/unit/test_heuristic_sampler.py
- tests/integration/test_decode_merge.py
- benchmarks/interactive_workload.yaml
- docs/notes/prefill-decode-heuristics.md

Performance summary (internal perf rig, synthetic mixed traffic):
- p50: ~unchanged (-0.5% on average)
- p95: -14% latency improvement for interactive class
- p99: -21% latency improvement for interactive class
- token throughput: +6% for small request mix (due to reduced kernels per request)
- memory: peak +3% in worst-case fused scenarios (within configured safety_margin)

Review conversation (high level):
- Liam: "Great approach. Two asks: add a failsafe to never merge if memory pressure > 70% and add a unit test that simulates KV churn."
- Maya: "Added memory headroom guard and two KV churn unit tests in commit 4c2a9f"
- Priya: "CI benchmark numbers look promising; please document the operational flags and safe defaults."
- Maya: "Docs added under docs/notes/prefill-decode-heuristics.md with recommended defaults for Dedicated and Hosted tiers."
- Ethan: "Nit: prefer 'merge_token_budget' be expressed in estimated activation bytes rather than tokens; consider follow-up."
- Maya: "Agree - opened ENG-1502 to iterate on activation-byte budgeting (out of scope for this PR)."
- Approvals: Liam (approved), Priya (approved), Ethan (approved after nit fixed)

CI history: 
- Initial CI: fail (lint) -> fixed whitespace and header includes in kernel_hint_registry patch -> rerun
- Benchmark CI: initially flaky on medium model test due to noisy machine; re-ran successfully
- Final CI: pass all (unit, integration, perf smoke)

Operational / rollout plan: 
- Feature off by default. To try in staging: set runtime.opt.enable_heuristic_prefill=true and keep runtime.opt.merge_token_budget conservative (default 64 tokens).
- Monitor: p99 latency, kv_miss_rate, decode_queue_depth, and peak memory. Alert if p99 increases >5% or memory grows >10% over baseline.
- Gradual ramp: start with 5% traffic, 25%, 50%, then 100% with health checks on each step.

Backward compatibility / risk: 
- No API surface changes. All runtime changes are behind a flag. Small increase in peak memory when fusion is chosen — controlled by safety_margin.

Notes for on-call:

Ethan: Consider switching to activation-bytes budgeting - tracked in ENG-1502

Context: During a recent tenant surge we observed premature circuit flips caused by uniform SLO windows and a spike in long-lived inflight connections that amplified KV cache pressure. This PR adds two coordinated mechanisms: (1) a SLO Grace Mapper that translates global SLI windows into per-tenant soft-grace allowances based on recent error/latency histograms and tenant weight, and (2) a Deferred Connection Clipper which caps new long-lived connection admits when KV memory pressure or slot exhaustion is detected, releasing a small, telemetry-anchored fast-eviction path for idle connections. Goals: reduce noisy circuit flips, avoid regional chain-retries, and give high-impact tenants bounded soft slack to absorb short surges without full fallback.

What I changed (high level):
- runtime/slo_grace_mapper.go: new component that computes per-tenant "grace_seconds" and a short-term SLO slack multiplier using a rolling SLI window and tenant-weight heuristic.
- controlplane/connection_clipper.go: deferred admission controller that clips admits for connections with large KV footprints; integrates with runtime health signals and exposes clip events to tracing.
- runtime/eviction_fastpath.go: small fast-evict hook that can remove idle connections with a conservative scoring function to free KV / slot resources.
- telemetry/metrics.yml and telemetry/alerts.yml: new metrics (redwood.slo_grace_seconds, redwood.conn_clip_events, redwood.fast_evict_rate) and an alert to detect miscalibration of grace mappings.
- config/feature_flags.yaml: feature flag and rollout ramps (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with per-cluster opt-out.
- tests/*: unit + deterministic integration tests for mapper heuristics and clipper state machine; added e2e scenario that simulates a KV-pressure surge and validates graceful degradation behavior.

Migration and rollout notes: feature-guarded behind feature/slo-grace and feature/conn-clipper flags. Default flags off for dedicated/private deployments; enabled in canary for 10% of hostnames for 24h, then 50% after telemetry sanity. No DB migrations. Backstop: if clipper misbehaves, flip feature flags to fully disable fast-evict and the mapper falls back to prior static windows.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for SLO mapper heuristics
- [x] Integration test simulating KV pressure
- [x] Metrics and dashboards added
- [x] Feature flags added for staged rollout
- [x] Docs: short runbook section added to ops guide
