payload.body:
Motivation: We see frequent transient regressions and overload events when shadow traffic is promoted too aggressively. This PR introduces a Shadow Quarantine Adapter that sits between the shadow bridge and promote controller and provides: 1) cohort-level quarantine when shadow error/quality thresholds are exceeded, 2) a cohort fuse primitive that prevents immediate promotion for cohorts that have recently been quarantined, and 3) surge-hedge logic to automatically throttle shadow injection when upstream serving capacity is under pressure. The goal is to reduce noisy rollouts and automatic promote-induced overloads while keeping promotion fast when signals are healthy.

What changed (high level):
- New adapter implementation (rollout/quarantine_adapter.go) that evaluates per-cohort metrics and emits quarantine actions to the rollout controller.
- Cohort fuse state machine (rollout/coseq_fuse.go) to track cooldown windows and allow probabilistic early-retry.
- Surge hedge integration (serving/surge_hedge.go) that consumes runtime capacity signals and scales back shadow fraction.
- Config schema updates (api/v1/rollout_schema.yaml) to expose quarantine thresholds, fuse durations and hedging policies.
- Observability: added metrics, tracing spans and a lightweight audit event for quarantines (observability/metrics_quarantine.md and metrics instrumentation in code).
- Tests: unit and integration tests that simulate cohort drift and surge scenarios (tests/quarantine/*).

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-2487)
- [x] Schema bump + migration-safe defaults
- [x] Unit tests for fuse transitions and quarantine decision logic
- [x] Integration test simulating promote with surge
- [x] Metrics and dashboards: added telemetry and Grafana panel templates
- [x] Feature-flag gated behind rollout.experimental.shadow_quarantine

Commits (summary):
- Add initial quarantine adapter and interfaces (priya/quarantine/initial)
- Implement cohort fuse state machine and unit tests (priya/quarantine/fuse)
- Wire surge hedge signals into shadow runtime throttler (priya/serving/surge)
- Schema and API updates + docs (priya/api/schema-docs)
- Address review feedback: race fixes and extra metrics (priya/review/fixes)

Files changed (representative):
- rollout/quarantine_adapter.go (+420/-78)
- rollout/coseq_fuse.go (+180/-0)
- serving/surge_hedge.go (+92/-16)
- api/v1/rollout_schema.yaml (+46/-2)
- observability/metrics_quarantine.md (+120/-0)
- tests/quarantine/adapter_test.go (+72/-4)
- tests/quarantine/integration_surge_test.go (+130/-30)
- examples/quickstart-shadow-quarantine.yaml (+12/-0)
- docs/rollouts/shadow_quarantine.md (+70/-0)

Testing & CI:
- CI run initially failed on a timing-sensitive unit test (fuse expiry test) in linux/amd64. The failure reproduced locally under heavy load; I fixed a race by switching the fuse timer to use a monotonic clock and added deterministic timers to the unit tests.
- After the fix CI passed on the second run. E2E integration in the perf-canary lab showed a ~3.8x reduction in transient promote-induced overloads in the simulated scenario (see benchmark comments).

Review notes / conversation (abridged):
- Liam O'Connor (reviewer): "Adapter looks solid; main concern is the fuse timer race and potential lock contention if many cohorts concurrently quarantine. Can we micro-benchmark the lock and consider lock-free CAS for the hot-path?"
- Priya (author): "Good catch — I replaced the heavy mutex with an atomic state and moved the cooldown bookkeeping to a low-frequency janitor goroutine. Added micro-benchmarks under tests/quarantine/bench_fuse.go; numbers attached in the PR comments."
- Marta Ruiz (reviewer): "We need clearer SLOs around hedging. If surge hedging is too aggressive we risk hiding regressions. Please add metric alerts for hedge-triggered promotions so SRE can triage."
- Priya: "Added hedging alert rules and a dashboard panel. Also added an opt-out for enterprise Dedicated customers via rollout config."
- Ethan Zhang (approver): "Approach looks safe; feature-flagged and well tested. Approving after minor nits fixed."

Risk assessment: Low-to-moderate. The quarantine adapter is opt-in and feature gated. The surge hedge reads existing runtime signals and only lowers shadow fraction; it does not alter traffic for primary production models. The main risk area was the fuse timer race (addressed) and metric cardinality; we intentionally coarsened the cohort histogram buckets to bound metric volume.

Backward compatibility: Configs that do not set the new fields use conservative defaults and the adapter remains disabled unless rollout.experimental.shadow_quarantine=true. There are no breaking API changes.

Operational playbook (short):
- Rollout: enable feature flag in canary region with shadow_fraction=0.05, monitor hedging metric and quarantine_audit events.
- If quarantine_audit spikes unusually: scale back shadow_fraction and investigate cohort-specific regressions. Use the provided replay tool to re-run captured traffic against candidate model.
- To rollback: toggle rollout.experimental.shadow_quarantine=false and the adapter drains state after the configured grace window (default 5m).

Merge: Squash-and-merge after approvals. Merged by Priya Kothari on 2026-02-18 (squash).

Related: builds on prior work in ENG-2130 (shadow bridge refactor) and is intended to be composable with the cohort-level promote policies introduced in ENG-1629.

Notes for follow-ups:
- Consider an adaptive fuse that shortens cooldown for cohorts with repeated safe promotions.
- Evaluate an ML-based hedging policy that predicts interference rather than relying solely on capacity signals.

Overall: This PR provides a practical, opt-in safety layer for shadow-to-canary promotions that reduces blast radius while preserving fast iterability for model rollouts.
Adds a shadow quarantine adapter to isolate failing shadow cohorts, introduces cohort fuse and surge hedging to protect serving runtime during promotion, includes new metrics and rollout hooks. Backwards compatible with existing rollout configs; opt-in via feature flag.
payload.title: Shadow Quarantine Adapter with Cohort Fuse and Surge Hedge

Motivation: persistent fragmentation and reactive full-spill behavior observed on multi-tenant workloads caused elevated P99 latency and repeated cold spills under transient load bursts. This PR introduces the 'Residency Governor'—a lightweight tenant-aware residency quota and healing controller that smooths demotion, schedules compact-on-read windows, and stages spillback to a deferred zero-copy spill pipeline to avoid synchronous eviction stalls. Changes include: a) quota-based per-tenant soft reservations with backpressure signals to the scheduler; b) probabilistic fragmentation scoring to trigger low-impact 'healing' compactions rather than full-page reclaims; c) compact-on-read heuristic that opportunistically compacts hot fragmented segments during KV reads to amortize work; d) graceful spill staging: small pages are batched into a spill queue and written asynchronously with backoff, reducing tail stalls; e) minor kernel-path annotations to favor eviction-friendly page shapes to reduce fragmentation over time. Checklist: - [x] design doc updated (docs/ops/kv-residency-governor.md); - [x] unit + integration tests added; - [x] benchmark harness: microbench and end-to-end spike tests; - [x] added feature flag for gradual rollout. Related: ENG-7192 design discussions and a postmortem reference at SUP-1114. This description summarizes the implementation, tests, and measured impact (see CI/perf).
Miguel Santos: Please add a short note about how the quota interacts with Dedicated burst capacity — can we avoid tenant starvation if Dedicated is low?
Ayesha Kapoor: Reply: quotas are soft by default, and will be bumped to a higher class when Dedicated burst is available; added a test that simulates Dedicated pressure (see integration test).
Erin Wallace: Request changes: make the compaction budget configurable via runtime flags to avoid perf regressions in small-instance deployments.
Ayesha Kapoor: Addressed: compaction budget is now tunable and defaults are conservative; added e2e spike tests to validate defaults.
Priya Natarajan: Observability ask: please emit fragmentation_score and staged_spill_queue_depth as tags for tenant routing. Ayesha: added metrics and console dashboard tile.
Introduce Residency Governor: tenant-aware soft reservations to reduce synchronous spills.
Enable compact-on-read to amortize compaction work and reduce long-tail evictions.
Staged asynchronous spill writer to lower eviction-induced latency spikes.
Metrics: fragmentation_score, staged_spill_queue_depth (available in Console)
Default behavior behind feature flag kv_residency_governor=false; gradual rollout planned across Dedicated clusters.
payload.title: kv residency governor and fragmentation healing paths

Motivation: Long-tail investigations showed that per-stage signal loss (drops between frontend, router, and serving stages) obscures token-level cost attribution and makes SLO blame messy. This PR introduces a light-weight cross-stage 'signal fabric' that tags and forwards minimal attribution tokens and introduces a proxy component that synthesizes a per-invocation token attribution trace. Goals: 1) make token-cost/latency attribution resilient to partial telemetry loss; 2) provide a compact join key for cross-stage tracing without increasing high-cardinality payloads; 3) enable a new dashboard for per-route token-attribution heatmaps and an alert that suppresses noise when attribution confidence is low. Design summary: - Signal fabric: small in-process publisher/subscriber with protobuf-encoded envelopes; each envelope carries a compact attribution header (trace_id, invocation_id, token_hashes[], stage_vector) and optional sampling hints. The fabric is pluggable: implemented in observability/collector as SignalFabric interface with in-memory and grpc-forwarder implementations. - Token attribution proxy: a lightweight aggregator (observability/attributor) that listens to fabric events and joins partial signals using a time-bucketed bloom join; it outputs a canonical attribution record per invocation. The join strategy favors recall for debugging (configurable to favor precision for billing pipelines). - Backward compatibility: components fall back to existing behavior if the fabric is disabled. The fabric attaches a small header to existing spans (no change to RPC payloads). Implementation notes: - New packages: observability/fabric (fabric API + inproc impl), observability/attributor (joiner + exporter), telemetry/protos/attribution.proto (message definitions) - Hooked fabric into route-router (router/ingest.go) and serving runtime pre-KV-flush path; the router publishes prefix-warmup and multi-stage scheduling hints while runtime publishes token-phase markers. - Efficiency: payloads are compact (<256B typical). Fabric uses scatter-gather with bounded queues and cooperative backpressure so critical fast-paths never block. - Configuration: default ON for dedicated/private deploys, OFF for hosted by default; rollout gated by feature flag redwood.observability.crossstage_fabric. Tests & CI: - Unit tests for bloom joiner, envelope roundtrip, and backpressure paths added. - Integration test harness in ci/observability-integration.yml spins up inproc fabric + attributor and validates end-to-end attribution for synthetic traces (coldstart, burst, partial-loss). - One flaky integration test (joiner/flaky-window) initially failed due to timer skew; fixed by tighter clock drift tolerance and re-run in CI. Files changed (high-level): observability/fabric/fabric.go, observability/fabric/inproc.go, observability/attributor/attributor.go, telemetry/protos/attribution.proto, dashboards/token-attribution-dashboard.json, docs/observability/signal-fabric.md, ci/observability-integration.yml Migration plan: - Canary rollout: enable flag for 5% of traffic in us-west-2, monitor attribution coverage and CPU on the attributor service. - Observability: new dashboards added (token attribution coverage, join latency, attribution confidence histogram) and an alert (ATB-01) that triggers if attribution coverage drops >10% or join-latency 95p > 2s. - Rollback: disable feature flag and drain attributor queues; the system will revert to per-stage raw spans. Security & privacy: we avoid storing token plaintexts — the fabric only exchanges token_hashes and size-limited context blobs. Operational notes: this introduces a new service job (attributor) that should be co-located in the observability tier; resource estimates: ~0.5 vCPU per 1000 rps of observed invocations, memory modest (128MB per shard) Remaining work (follow-ups): - Add an opt-in precision mode for billing pipelines that retains exact token indices (requires vault KMS review) - Dashboard drilldown widgets for invocation-level reconstructed traces - Add a Prometheus exporter for attributor internals Rollout/merge notes: landed after approvals and CI re-run. All changes behind feature flag to avoid customer impact.
1) init: add attribution proto and fabric interface
2) impl: inproc fabric + attributor joiner
3) integ: add integration harness and CI job
4) docs: signal fabric design doc and dashboard json
5) fix: adjust join window skew handling after flaky CI
Leo Ramirez: Could the bloom-joiner produce false positives that bias cost allocation? Please add a confidence score per record.
Aisha Patel (author): Added per-record attribution_confidence (0-100) exported to the dashboard; default joiner params tuned for low FP.
Daniel Kim: Small nit - inproc queues should expose a metrics tag for queue_depth by shard. Also, please mark the attributor pod as BestEffort in the chart?
Aisha Patel (author): Added queue_depth metric and updated helm chart suggestion (docs/observability/signal-fabric.md) with resource guidance; left scheduling as Burstable for now per perf team ask.
Soren Dahl: Integration test failed on first run (joiner window). After the skew fix I re-ran and tests passed. Please note in the changelog why the timer tolerance increased.
Initial CI run: unit tests passed; integration job failed (joiner window flake). Fixed clock tolerance and pushed commit 5; re-ran CI. Final CI: all checks passed. Observability e2e test runtime ~4m. Coverage: +3.2% on observability package.
Add cross-stage signal fabric and token attribution proxy: improves resilience for token-level cost and latency attribution across multi-stage request paths. Adds dashboards and an alert for attribution coverage. Default off for hosted; feature-flagged rollout for dedicated/private.
If ATB-01 fires (attribution coverage drop or join-latency spike), first check attributor pod logs for 'join-window-exceeded' errors, verify feature flag rollout percentage, and if needed disable redwood.observability.crossstage_fabric for the affected region to restore prior behavior.
payload.title: Introduce cross-stage signal fabric and token attribution proxy

Problem: the new cache telemetry (hit/miss counters, eviction events, wasted prefill) is intentionally emitted at request boundaries and (in a few places) per-cache-event to support attribution. Under some workloads (streaming chat retries, high QPS short prompts, and continuous batching), this can become a high-volume signal source. We need guardrails so we don’t introduce p95/p99 latency overhead in runtime or create a sudden telemetry cost spike in prod.

This PR adds two layers of protection:
1) Deterministic sampling for event-style cache signals (and optionally for a subset of histograms) with stable sampling keys so ratios remain interpretable at aggregation time.
2) A lightweight local rate limiter in the runtime emitter path that caps the maximum number of cache telemetry emissions per process per interval, with self-observability metrics for drops.

What’s included (high level):
- New config surface (runtime) for cache telemetry sampling + rate limits:
  - cache_telemetry.enabled (default: on in staging, off in prod until rollout gate)
  - cache_telemetry.event_sample_rate (default: 0.05 in staging)
  - cache_telemetry.histogram_sample_rate (default: 1.0; can be reduced if needed)
  - cache_telemetry.max_events_per_second (token bucket; default: 2,000/s)
  - cache_telemetry.burst (default: 5,000)
- Deterministic sampling based on a stable key derived from request_id + route_id + model_version_id. (No prompt content is used; privacy-safe.)
- Rate limiting is applied after sampling, so we keep behavior predictable and don’t overwhelm the emitter path on pathological spikes.
- Drop counters + reason tags so SRE can tell “real hit-rate change” vs “telemetry is being throttled”:
  - redwood.cache.telemetry.dropped_total{reason=rate_limited|disabled}
  - redwood.cache.telemetry.sampled_total{signal=pfx_event|kv_event|evict_event|wasted_prefill}
- Updates to docs/comments in the runtime telemetry module to clarify which signals are sampled and how to interpret them downstream (aggregation must scale by 1/sample_rate for sampled signals).

Non-goals:
- No changes to metric definitions / ADR semantics.
- No ingestion-side cardinality policy changes (handled separately).

Testing:
- Unit tests for deterministic sampling boundaries and token bucket behavior.
- Load test in perf-canary branch (manual run linked in comments) showed no measurable regression at 5% event sampling + 2k/s cap; without cap we saw occasional emitter contention in debug builds.

Rollout plan:
- Staging: enable cache_telemetry.enabled=true + 5% sampling by default.
- Canary: enable in 1% prod traffic with max_events_per_second=500 initially; ramp after 24h if no latency regression and dropped_total remains <1% of sampled_total.

Follow-ups:
- PR-18429 will wire these flags into our environment config defaults and make them operator-tunable via the control plane; this PR keeps the knobs local to the runtime config struct + CLI/env config parsing used in tests.

Risk notes:
- Sampling changes require careful interpretation in dashboards; this PR emits explicit sampled_total/dropped_total so we can sanity check the effective sampling rate and throttling behavior before we rely on the signals for recommendations.
Logan Wright (review): Can we ensure sampling is deterministic so dashboards don’t jitter day-to-day? Also please confirm no prompt content participates in the key.

Thomas Baird (author): Yes—sampling uses a stable 64-bit hash of (request_id, route_id, model_version_id). request_id is already a UUID generated at gateway and propagated; route/model ids are stable join keys. No prompt bytes or token content is included. I added a comment + unit test that sampling decisions are stable for a fixed key.

Nadia Rahman (review): We should emit explicit “dropped due to rate limit” counters, otherwise ingestion drops vs runtime throttling will be hard to diagnose. Also prefer reason enums that won’t churn.

Thomas Baird (author): Added redwood.cache.telemetry.dropped_total{reason=rate_limited|disabled} and kept the reason set intentionally small. Also added sampled_total by signal so we can compute the effective rate.

Omar El-Sayed (review): Why are we sampling histograms at all? Hit/miss counters are cheap but per-event emissions are the concern. I’d rather keep histograms unsampled unless we have evidence they’re hot.

Thomas Baird (author): Agree. Default histogram_sample_rate=1.0; only event-style signals are sampled by default. The knob exists as an escape hatch if we find a specific histogram is too expensive under extreme QPS.

Marcus Reed (perf review): Any evidence of overhead? Please include perf numbers or at least show we’re not adding locks on the hot path.

Thomas Baird (author): Limiter uses an atomic token bucket with a fast-path check; no mutex. I added unit tests and included results from a local perf run in tools/perf/notes/cache-telemetry-sampling.md. In release build, delta in p95 was within noise; the main win is preventing spikes under bursty cache-event emission.

Caleb Johnson (review): Rate limiter defaults: 2k/s seems high for prod; can we start lower for canary and ramp?

Thomas Baird (author): Yep—updated rollout notes: start canary at 500/s. Defaults in this PR are staging-oriented; prod defaults will be set in PR-18429 via environment config.

Final approvals:
- Logan Wright: Approved
- Nadia Rahman: Approved
- Omar El-Sayed: Approved
- Marcus Reed: Approved (perf note acknowledged)

Merge: Squash merged after CI green. Post-merge note: please coordinate with Allison/SRE before enabling in prod so dashboards include drop counters and we don’t misread throttled telemetry as a cache regression.
payload.title: Cache telemetry: add sampling controls + local rate limiting for high-volume events

Motivation: polish remaining edge-cases in our /v1/chat.completions compatibility shim so customers using OpenAI-style params see consistent behavior when using streaming, functions, and structured outputs. This PR focuses on three practical gaps discovered during a PLG customer migration: role aliasing when clients send nonstandard role labels, stop-array coalescing with mixed encodings (bytes vs strings), and a graceful logprob fallback when models do not provide exhaustive token logprobs during framed streaming.

What this change does: normalizes alias roles (system/meta -> system, usr/user -> user), coalesces stop sequences at both the adapter and runtime stream boundary to avoid double-truncation, and introduces a logprob-fallback path that synthesizes stable per-token probability hints (not full logprobs) when upstream models return partial data. Additionally this PR refines the function-call handshake in the stream envelope: we now emit a preflight "fncap" delta to indicate function schema acceptance before tool payloads arrive, and when a function is invoked we ensure the framed JSON body uses the same structured-shape negotiated by the v1 adapter.

Compatibility notes: preserves existing Redwood streaming framing for native clients; changes are gated behind the chatv1 compatibility flag and a runtime toggle so we can roll back quickly if there are regressions. Unit and integration tests added; a small e2e with the Python SDK demonstrates parity with OpenAI's behavior for the customers' test prompt set.

Checklist:
- [x] role alias normalization
- [x] stop array coalescing at adapter+runtime
- [x] logprob fallback path with safety heuristics
- [x] function-call preflight delta (fncap) + shaped payloads
- [x] integration tests + sample SDK snippet in docs
- [x] feature toggle and metric emitted (chatv1.compat.polish.enabled)

Related: ENG-3241 (param parity backlog), ENG-3309 (streaming flakiness triage).
Sasha Patel: Nice, role aliasing is straightforward. Can we add a small metric for how often 'usr' maps to 'user' for visibility?
Author (Avery): Added chatv1.compat.role_alias_count metric and doc note; also included a sample Grafana panel.
Juniper Lee: The fncap preflight looks good but please ensure it doesn't increase median latency for short responses. Suggest a microbenchmark.
Author (Avery): Added microbenchmark in stream/framing/bench_fncap_test.go; no measurable p50 increase in our local tests (<0.2ms).
Marcus Nguyen: Integration test flaked once in CI due to a timing window between adapter coalesce and runtime flush — suggested adding a small deterministic flush in test harness.
Author (Avery): Implemented deterministic flush in e2e harness and retried CI.
- ChatV1 compatibility: normalize role aliases and reduce client-side mismatch errors.
- Stream stability: coalesce stop arrays across adapter/runtime to prevent premature truncation.
- Function calling: introduce fncap preflight delta and enforce structured function payloads for v1 clients.
- Logprobs: synthetic fallback path to avoid noisier null/omitted logprobs during streaming.
(Flagged behind chatv1.compat.polish toggle; no user-visible breaking changes expected)
payload.title: chat-v1 compatibility polisher: function handoff & structured response parity

Motivation: Tenants with bursty traffic were seeing premature evictions during transient spikes because autoscaler cooldowns and eviction heuristics were uniform. This change introduces a per-tenant soft-eviction window that decays with observed burst tail latency and an adaptive throughput accountant that tracks committed vs observed throughput to make eviction decisions more tolerant of short surges. The PR contains: design and rationale, implementation, telemetry, and migration guidance. Key points: 1) soft-eviction-window: per-tenant parameter persisted in the reservation ledger with safe defaults and policy-driven overrides; windows are smoothed using an EWMA of recent burst durations. 2) throughput-accountant: a sliding-window counter that exposes committed_tokens, observed_tokens, burst_headroom and a degradation_score used by the admission controller. 3) eviction policy integration: admission controller consults throughput-accountant and soft-eviction-window before marking slots for preemption; we bias toward preemption of ephemeral warmlets when degradation_score is low. 4) Telemetry: added metrics tenant_soft_eviction_window_seconds, tenant_throughput_committed, tenant_throughput_observed, tenant_degradation_score, eviction_considered_count, eviction_preempted_count, and a per-tenant histogram for preemption_latency. 5) Controls: new API knobs on Dedicated config to override default window and accountant sensitivity, documented in console and terraform provider. 6) Backwards compatibility: new fields are optional; behavior defaults to current autoscaler. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked ENG-2043, - [x] Implementation with unit and integration tests, - [x] End-to-end canary on staging clusters, - [x] Telemetry dashboard template and alerts, - [x] Migration notes and rollback plan. Follow-ups: tune EWMA alpha across regions, expose a Lite-mode for low-cardinality tenants. See commits and changed files for specifics.
Arjun: Can you explain how the EWMA alpha was chosen and whether it should be tenant-configurable? Maya: Chose alpha=0.25 based on 48h sampling of staging traces; added Dedicated knob to override per-tenant; will expose in follow-up tuning RFC.
Rosa: The metric tenant_degradation_score seems correlated with CPU saturations in some clusters, should we normalize by node capacity? Maya: Good catch, added a normalization factor and a comment in accountant.go; left a TODO to surface node-level capacity in the console.
Liam: Integration tests flaked twice on arm64 CI due to timing assumptions in preemption latency test, please make clock deterministic. Maya: Switched to fake clock and added retries; CI now green.
QA: How do we rollback if customer sees increased latency after enabling? Maya: Rollback plan added to docs: flip knob in Dedicated config, reapply previous reservation snapshot; warmlet prewarming logic is safe to revert without eviction storm.
Added per-tenant soft eviction windows and an adaptive throughput accountant to make eviction decisions more tolerant of short bursts. New telemetry and config knobs for Dedicated deployments. No breaking changes.
payload.title: Per-tenant soft-eviction-windows and adaptive throughput accountant

Context
We’re standardizing cost computation primitives so Console + Optimize can consume the same numbers and semantics. To keep Cost Model output stable across runtime/telemetry changes and to prevent regressions (e.g., prefill/decode split, cache-hit attribution, overhead allocation rounding), we need deterministic, versioned golden fixtures and CI enforcement.

This PR adds:
- Golden fixture datasets (JSON) for Cost Model v1 inputs/expected outputs
- Deterministic unit + integration tests that replay fixtures through the library/service computation path
- A CI target that runs the golden suite and fails on drift outside defined tolerances

What’s included
1) Golden fixtures (v1)
- sources live in: cost-model/tests/golden/v1/
- fixtures cover:
  - hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment contexts
  - multiple hardware SKUs (A10/L4/H100 equivalents as represented in model catalog test data)
  - prefill/decode accounting with KV-cache hit/miss
  - batch efficiency variations (single request, small batch, near-capacity batch)
  - quantization profile deltas (baseline fp16, int8 profile id), including explicit “not supported” cases
  - overhead allocation policy buckets (request-attributable vs shared), with finance-aligned rounding rules

2) Deterministic behavior
- normalizes rounding and formatting to avoid flaky snapshot diffs:
  - all monetary values in outputs are asserted in microdollars (USD * 1e6) and rendered consistently
  - uses explicit decimal quantization for percentage fields exposed to Console breakdown tables
- fixes test-time nondeterminism from “current time” inputs by injecting a fixed clock
- pins the fixture runner ordering (stable sort by fixture id)

3) Test runner + CI integration
- new test entrypoint:
  - //cost-model/tests:golden_fixtures_test
- adds CI step (required) to the main pipeline:
  - “cost-model-golden-fixtures”
- adds a documented workflow for updating fixtures (requires two reviewers + explicit rationale in commit message)

Why now
- We’ve already seen drift/regression risk show up in customer-facing differences (SUP-31844, SUP-31877) and internal drift alerts. These tests provide a fast, deterministic guardrail while the telemetry contracts and runtime exports are still evolving.

Implementation notes
- Tolerances:
  - By default, assertions are exact on integer microdollars.
  - For a small subset of fields derived from sampling-based “what-if” projections (not part of this PR’s fixtures), the runner supports a per-field tolerance; for v1 fixtures in this PR, tolerance is set to 0.
- Fixture format:
  - Each fixture includes: schema_version, input, expected_output, and notes.
  - The runner validates schema_version negotiation to ensure we catch accidental breaking changes.

Test plan
- bazel test //cost-model/tests:golden_fixtures_test
- bazel test //cost-model/service/... (ensures service path uses same library computations)
- Verified deterministic output across:
  - local (macOS)
  - linux CI runner

Rollout / risk
- Low runtime risk (tests + fixtures only), but CI will now block merges when cost outputs change.
- Updating goldens requires sign-off from Platform (Ethan) + Telemetry (Nadia/Logan) or Finance (Laura/Rishi) depending on the field impacted.

Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Add “what-if” fixture coverage once ENG-4824 results format stabilizes (include confidence intervals + guardrails).
- Wire a small subset of these fixtures into drift monitoring backtests for early warning (ties into ENG-4827).

Related
- PR #28451 (schema package v1)
- PR #28457 (service endpoints)
- PR #28509 (runtime export for KV cache stats)
- PR #28490 (drift monitoring job)

Checklist
- [x] Fixtures are versioned and include notes + provenance
- [x] Tests deterministic (no wall clock; stable ordering; explicit rounding)
- [x] CI job added and marked required
- [x] Docs added for updating/regenerating fixtures
Nadia Rahman: Can we avoid floating-point comparisons entirely? Prefill/decode split has been flaky in other repos. If you can assert integer microdollars + integer token counts, we should do that.
Leila Farouk (author): Yep. Updated expected outputs to microdollars and moved token fields to integers everywhere. Also added a guard that fails the runner if it sees NaN/Inf in any computed field.
Thomas Baird: Please add explicit bounds checks in the runner so a malformed fixture can’t accidentally produce an unbounded breakdown (cardinality explosion). Even if it’s “just tests”, it’s a good practice and will mirror service constraints.
Leila Farouk (author): Added a per-fixture max breakdown rows assertion (defaults to 50) and a hard cap in the runner (200) to prevent accidental blowups.
Allison Grant: CI job naming is good, but make sure it’s marked required for main. Also, include a short doc for ‘how to update goldens’ with approval requirements to prevent silent drift.
Leila Farouk (author): Done. Added docs/internal/cost-model/testing/golden-fixtures.md + updated pipeline to required. Also added a check that the PR description includes 'golden update rationale' when any fixture changes.
Rafael Mendes: From SRE perspective, I’m happy with this. One nit: please ensure the fixture runner logs the first diff clearly so the failure is actionable (field path + expected + actual).
Leila Farouk (author): Implemented field-path diff output + prints fixture id + schema version at top of failure. Added an example to the doc.
Ethan Park: Looks good. Requested change: include a dedicated-capacity fixture that exercises the overhead policy buckets explicitly (request-attributable vs shared) with the rounding behavior Finance asked for.
Leila Farouk (author): Added fixture v1/dedicated_overhead_allocation_rounding.json and included explicit notes referencing the policy. Please re-review.
Ethan Park: Approved.
Nadia Rahman: Approved.
Internal: Cost Model now has golden fixture coverage + deterministic CI enforcement to prevent regressions in cost computations used by Console/Optimize.
payload.title: Add golden fixtures + deterministic tests for Cost Model computations (CI)

Context and motivation:
This PR adds two cross-sdk features that were requested by platform and integrator teams: 1) an adaptive delegated-auth mode (delegation to environment-specific token providers based on request hints) to reduce hot credential sprawl and simplify enterprise integrations, and 2) streaming checkpoint hooks that let consumers record stream progress (sequence/token offsets) so mission-critical consumers can resume gracefully without reprocessing large prefixes.

What changed (high level):
- New auth adapter: 'DelegatedAuthProvider' (python/ts/go) that accepts a chain of candidate token providers and a small selection policy (region, customer-tier, route metadata). The runtime will try the cheapest eligible provider first, falling back to higher-privilege providers when a request indicates an elevated SLO. This reduces token vending traffic and enables safer delegation for hosted/dedicated/private installs.
- Streaming progress API: consumers can now pass an optional 'checkpoint_hook' when opening a stream. Hooks are simple callables in each SDK that receive small progress markers (stream_id, offset, timestamp, optional metadata). Hooks are synchronous/async based on SDK idioms and intended to be lightweight (default noop).
- Unified retry profiles: hook points added so the SDK retry builder can nominate different retry profiles for delegated requests vs regular requests (lower retry floor for delegated providers that are expected to be ephemeral).
- Ergonomic surfaces: Python: contextmanager Stream.checkpointed(), TypeScript: startStreamingWithCheckpoint(opts), Go: StreamWithCheckpoint functional option. Each surface exposes the same minimal semantic: emit_checkpoint(marker) or await checkpoint acknowledgement from user hook.
- Tests and docs: added cross-lang examples and a new docs page (docs/sdk/checkpoints.md) describing recommended checkpoint semantics for idempotent vs at-most-once consumption patterns.
- Version bumps: python 0.11.0, typescript 1.27.0, go 1.8.0 (SDK minor/patch-lines adjusted accordingly).

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation in Python/TypeScript/Go
- [x] Unit tests for provider selection and checkpoint glue
- [x] Integration test: streaming resume scenario (flaky environment rerun)
- [x] Telemetry: added metrics for 'delegated_auth.provider.chosen' and 'stream.checkpoint.emitted'
- [x] Docs & changelogs updated

Related: Linear ENG-3001 (delegated auth), ENG-3002 (stream checkpoints), SUP-8123 (customer request to reduce token vending).

Notes and tradeoffs:
- DelegatedAuthProvider uses a conservative selection policy by default (prefer local short-lived tokens, then dedicated service tokens, then global long-lived tokens) to minimize blast radius. Customers can supply a custom selector.
- Checkpoint hooks are intentionally small; we avoided building a full checkpoint store to keep SDK surface minimal. Platform customers should use the hook to persist markers to a store that meets their durability SLOs.
- This PR does not change server-side routing or fallback policies; it only exposes client-side selection and telemetry. A follow-up will add server-side hints to improve provider scoring (ENG-3005).
feat(auth): add delegated auth provider chain and selection policy
feat(stream): add checkpoint hook interface across py/ts/go
chore(sdk): bump versions py->0.11.0 ts->1.27.0 go->1.8.0
test: add unit/integration tests for checkpoint resume and provider fallback
docs: add checkpoints.md and examples for idempotent consumers
perf: micro-optimizations to stream envelope path to minimize checkpoint overhead
Diego Alvarez: Can we make the default selection policy pluggable via environment variable? Suggest adding REDWOOD_AUTH_DELEGATION_POLICY. (addressed in commit 4)
Priya Nair: Telemetry naming looks good; rename 'stream.checkpoint.emitted' -> 'stream.checkpoint.created' to match existing metric conventions. (updated in telemetry-metrics.yaml)
Liam O'Connor: Tests look solid but integration stream resume was flaky on the first CI run; added deterministic smoke harness and reduced timing jitter. CI re-run passed.
Maya Chen (author): Responded to comments; added env var hook, docs note about durable persistence, and adjusted metric name. Ready for final review.
Diego Alvarez: Approved after small docs wording nitfixes.
Add delegated auth provider chain (pluggable selection policy) and lightweight streaming checkpoint hooks across SDKs. Introduces telemetry for chosen auth providers and emitted checkpoints. Minor SDK version bumps: python 0.11.0, typescript 1.27.0, go 1.8.0.

payload.body:
Background: customers running mixed canary + A/B experiments were seeing noisy autoscale events and prolonged partial promotions when a model variant caused transient resource pressure. This PR adds a coordinator that runs alongside the rollout runtime to: 1) orchestrate simultaneous shadow seeding for A/B arms so traffic can be safely validated off-path, 2) surface autoscale pressure signals to the rollout decision graph and trigger graceful failback windows, and 3) provide a deterministic, snapshot-backed revert that can be executed instantly if safety gates trip. Motivation: reduce time-to-rollout for multi-variant experiments while preventing cascade-induced promotions and providing reproducible rollback. Changes: - new service: rollout/hybrid_coordinator (golang) with a light state machine for shadow seeding and autoscale feedback. - API: A new RolloutPolicy extension (policy.type: hybrid-shadow-ab) and two new hooks: autoscale_metric and shadow_sample_rate. - Scheduler changes: minor patch to servegraph reconciler to add coordinator callbacks and to make promotes interruptible by external abort signals. - Telemetry: added coordinator.* metrics, trace spans for shadow seed lifecycle, and a diagnostic event for deterministic-reverts. Migration: existing RolloutPolicies are unchanged; the new policy is opt-in. Checklist: [x] unit tests for coordinator state transitions, [x] integration test with canary + A/B scenario in perf-lab, [x] API docs and schema additions, [x] observability dashboards updated, [x] smoke-run in staging. Notes: kept the runtime changes minimal; most logic is in the coordinator service to allow safe rollback without kernel-level changes. See linked Linear ENG-9876 for design doc and ENG-10234 for perf plan.
Introduces Hybrid Shadow-A/B Coordinator: enables coordinated shadow traffic seeding alongside A/B routing with autoscale-aware failback and a deterministic instant-revert path. Backwards compatible with existing rollout policies.
3 commits: 1) rollout: add hybrid coordinator service and tests (golang) 2) api: extend RolloutPolicy schema + docs 3) reconcile: scheduler callbacks + telemetry and staging smoke-run tweaks
Elliot Moreno: Left an initial pass; concerned about edge-case where autoscale signal oscillates. Can we debounce and expose a backoff TTL?
Priya Shah: Added a debounce window (configurable via policy.autoscale_debounce_ms) and unit tests to verify oscillation logic. See commit 2.
Cara Liu: Request to ensure the deterministic revert uses an immutable snapshot reference (not a sliding window). Also asked for an explicit audit event on revert.
Priya Shah: Rework: coordinator now creates a snapshot manifest at seed start and the revert action references that manifest. Audit event added to telemetry and policy history log. See commit 3.
Diego Alvarez: Verified perf-lab results; suggested reducing default shadow_sample_rate for small models to reduce KV pressure. Accepted and lowered default to 0.02 in the schema.
Elliot Moreno: Approving now that debounce and snapshot fixes are in. +1 from SRE for staging smoke-run results.
CI: integration suite passed (rollout unit/integration/telemetry). Final e2e flaked once, retriggered, passed.
payload.title: Hybrid Shadow-A/B Coordinator with Autoscale Failback and Deterministic Revert

payload.body:
Summary: This PR adds low-cardinality trace annotations for prefix cache + KV cache events so we can correlate cache behavior (hit/miss, miss reason, reuse depth) with request latency in traces without introducing high-cardinality metrics. Motivation: We have solid cache counters/histograms now, but during regressions it’s still hard to answer: “did p99 spike because cache misses increased, because misses are TTL/version related, or because we’re evicting under pressure?” Traces already include latency breakdowns; adding carefully-scoped span attributes/events lets oncall and runtime engineers connect the dots for individual slow requests and then pivot back to aggregate dashboards.

Design constraints / privacy & cardinality: - No prompt text and no prompt hashes. - No tenant_id/route_id/model_version in the trace annotations (those are already present in gateway/request context spans where allowed, and we don’t want to duplicate or widen propagation). - Only emit annotations when the span is recording (i.e., sampled), so we don’t add overhead to non-sampled requests. - All values are either booleans, enums, or pre-defined buckets.

What’s included: 1) Prefill span annotations: - Adds an event on the request span at end of prefill: event name: cache.prefill.summary - attributes: cache.prefix.hit (bool), cache.prefix.reused_tokens_bucket (enum), cache.prefix.reuse_ratio_bucket (enum), cache.kv.reused_blocks_bucket (enum), cache.kv.miss_reason (enum; only set when miss), cache.wasted_prefill_tokens_bucket (enum), cache.eviction_pressure (enum: none|low|high) 2) Decode span annotations: - Adds cache.decode.kv_cache status when decode starts (hit vs miss-driven recompute) to help explain decode tail latency when prefill was cheap but decode was expensive. 3) Trace safety guardrails: - All annotations are behind: runtime.cache_telemetry.trace_annotations_enabled (default: true in staging/canary, false in prod until rollout gate flips) - Emission checks span.is_recording() to avoid extra work when tracing is not sampled - Bucket mappings live in a single file (shared with metric bucket definitions where possible) to avoid drift.

Implementation notes: - We attach annotations to the existing request root span (redwood.request) and the prefill child span (redwood.prefill) when present. If spans are absent (tracing disabled), the instrumentation is a no-op. - Miss reason uses the same enum as the metrics work (capacity, ttl_expired, policy_disabled, hash_mismatch, version_mismatch, unknown). - “wasted prefill” in traces uses the same bucketization as the metric, computed from the prefill accounting that already exists; we do not introduce per-token logging.

Testing: - Unit tests validate bucket mapping boundaries and enum serialization. - Integration test extends the cache-metrics test harness to assert trace annotations appear for sampled spans (and not for non-sampled). - Manual: verified in staging with trace UI that cache.prefill.summary event shows up and can be filtered by miss_reason.

Perf/overhead: - Incremental overhead measured in perf-canary is within noise when tracing is disabled or not sampled; for sampled traces, additional allocations are bounded (string constants + small attribute set). - We intentionally avoid per-request dynamic strings; event names/keys are static constants.

Rollout plan: - Land behind flag (this PR). - Enable in staging immediately. - Enable in perf-canary + a small prod canary cell (Connor O’Brien to flip) after 24h stability. - If we see any trace volume or CPU regressions, roll back via config flag.

Screenshots/links: - Trace UI example (staging): internal link redwood-tracing://staging/trace/9b3d... (see comment). - Related: PR-18421/22/23/24 for cache metrics + wasted prefill; PR-18425 for sampling/rate limits.

Checklist: - [x] No high-cardinality labels/attributes added - [x] No prompt material logged - [x] Guarded by is_recording() - [x] Tests for bucketing + integration trace assertion - [x] Release note not required (flagged off by default in prod)

Review discussion highlights: Omar requested reusing the miss-reason enum from metrics to keep taxonomy stable and asked to ensure we don’t attach model_version in trace attrs; updated accordingly. Nadia asked for explicit bucket enums instead of raw token counts; updated to use *_bucket fields only. Allison requested a single “prefill summary” event rather than multiple events to reduce trace noise; consolidated events into one summary event and kept decode annotation minimal.

Outcome: Merged (squash) into main. Follow-up: once enabled in prod canary, SRE/Observability will add a saved trace query for cache.miss_reason=version_mismatch to accelerate triage (tracked in ENG-4824 notes).
Omar El-Sayed (review): Love the direction. Two asks: (1) reuse the existing MissReason enum (don’t re-declare strings), and (2) please confirm we’re not adding model_version/route_id as span attrs here. Those are already on the gateway span and we don’t want to widen propagation.
Samir Qureshi (author): Updated to import MissReason from cache metrics module and map to a stable string set. Also removed the earlier model_version attr; now only the cache-specific buckets/enums are attached. Added a comment explaining why.
Nadia Rahman (review): +1 on keeping this out of metrics. For traces, can we avoid raw token counts? Buckets only please; otherwise people will start filtering by exact values and we’ll get pseudo-cardinality in tracing storage.
Samir Qureshi (author): Done. Switched to reused_tokens_bucket / reuse_ratio_bucket / wasted_prefill_tokens_bucket. Raw counts remain local variables only.
Allison Grant (review): Request: please collapse multiple events into a single prefill summary event; otherwise traces get noisy and hard to scan during incident triage. Also ensure we only emit when span.is_recording().
Samir Qureshi (author): Consolidated into cache.prefill.summary with ~6 attrs and gated on is_recording(). Also moved all keys to static constants to avoid per-request allocations.
Noah Patel (review): One more: in batched prefill, are we attributing reuse to the correct request? The earlier hit-attribution bug made me nervous.
Samir Qureshi (author): Good call. This instrumentation reads the same per-request accounting used by the fixed metrics path (post PR-18433). Added an integration assertion that in a batched prefill scenario, the sampled request sees only its own summary event values.
Omar El-Sayed (approval): Looks good now. Thanks for consolidating events + bucketing. Approving.
payload.title: Add trace span annotations for cache events (prefix/KV) to correlate with latency

payload.body:
Motivation: we observed a pattern of transient reconnects and duplicated session warmups across SDKs in high-latency networks. Root cause analysis showed inconsistent default handshake timeouts and retry windows between Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs, plus divergent retry presets that led to different observable behaviors for the same customer workload. This PR aligns default handshake timing, exposes a compact retry profile set, and introduces lightweight typed shims to make the change low-friction for integrators.

What this PR does (summary): unify handshake timeout semantics (connect/handshake/heartbeat) across sdks, add "compact" retry presets optimized for low-latency server environments and high-latency client links, expose an opt-in environment variable and programmatic flag to opt out of the new defaults, add tests and docs, bump SDK package versions (py -> 0.14.2, ts -> 1.9.0, go -> 1.4.0).

Checklist:
- [x] Safety: preserve opt-out path (env var REDWOOD_SDK_LEGACY_HANDSHAKE=1)
- [x] Backwards compatibility: surface compatibility notes in changelogs
- [x] Tests: unit + e2e streaming replays added
- [x] Docs: SDK handshake doc and migration note added
- [x] Benchmarks: quick perf run to show no regression in median latency

Commits summary: squash of 7 commits (tweak timeouts, add retry presets, tests, docs):
- normalize: sdks/* handshake timeouts and comment rationale
- add: compact retry profiles and presets registry
- feat: SDK flags and env var for opt-out
- test: e2e streaming replay and flaky-case assertion
- docs: add handshake.md and migration guidance
- bump: package.json/pyproject/go.mod version pins
- ci: increase e2e timeout in flaky job to reduce spurious failures

Changed files (high level): sdks/python/session.py, sdks/python/handshake_policy.py, sdks/typescript/src/stream/handshake.ts, sdks/typescript/src/retries/presets.ts, sdks/go/connector/handshake.go, sdks/go/retry/presets.go, docs/sdk-handshake.md, tests/e2e/stream-resume.test.ts, tests/unit/retry_presets_test.py, changelogs/CHANGELOG-RELEASES.md, CI/workflows/e2e-streams.yml

CI / checks: initial runs showed a flaky e2e streaming failure on Linux AMD runner (timeout). I increased the test timeout and retriggered; full CI passed on rerun (build, unit, lint, e2e). Final ci_status: pass.

Reviews: iterative review cycle with perf and SDK leads. Key feedback addressed: clarify default values in docs, provide explicit opt-out, add a short compatibility note to changelogs, shrink default handshake window for hosted tier but leave dedicated/private unchanged unless customer opts in.

Merge: squash-and-merge. Release notes below.
- SDKs: unified handshake timeout defaults across Python/TypeScript/Go (opt-out available via REDWOOD_SDK_LEGACY_HANDSHAKE).
- SDKs: introduce `compact` retry preset optimized for lower-tail latency; exposed programmatic preset selection.
- Tests: added e2e streaming replay tests and unit coverage for retry presets.
- Docs: new docs/sdk-handshake.md with migration steps and compatibility notes.
- Versions: py 0.14.2, ts 1.9.0, go 1.4.0
Maya Chen: Please add explicit migration guidance for customers with custom network proxies. Resolving with docs/sdk-handshake.md added.
Carlos Rivera: The compact preset seems aggressive for some mobile networks — added opt-in and preserved legacy behavior behind env var.
Lena Hoffman: CI e2e flake observed; increased timeout and added an assertion to make the test deterministic. Verified on rerun.
payload.title: Polish SDK handshake timings and compact retry profiles across Python/TS/Go

payload.body:
Problem: Dedicated throughput SLO reporting was overcounting tokens for streaming requests. We were incrementing `deployment_tokens_generated_total` per-stream chunk (delta tokens) and then incrementing again on stream completion using the final `usage.completion_tokens` value. For non-streaming, the completion-path increment is correct; for streaming, it results in ~2x token totals (shape/model dependent) and skews derived tokens/sec in the SLO evaluator + dashboards.

Customer/ops impact: This primarily affects Dedicated throughput SLO compliance tracking (tokens/sec floor) and internal saturation indicators. It also contributed to customer confusion when comparing Console throughput graphs vs request-level `usage` totals (see SUP-18510). Billing exports are not impacted (billing uses metering events, not the SLO throughput counters).

Fix: Make streaming accounting single-source-of-truth by only emitting token increments from the streaming path, and skipping the completion-path increment when `streaming=true`. Additionally, guard against duplicate “final chunk” emission by tracking `last_emitted_completion_tokens` on the stream session and only emitting positive deltas.

What changed: - `api-gateway`: adjust token accounting so the completion handler does not increment throughput counters for streaming requests; the counter is incremented only via the stream chunk emitter. - `telemetry`: add explicit `streaming` + `accounting_source` labels to aid debugging (chunk vs completion). - tests: add unit tests for streaming lifecycle (N chunks + final usage) asserting exact token totals; add regression test covering the previously failing scenario where both chunk deltas and final usage were emitted.

Rollout notes: This changes the magnitude of streaming throughput counters immediately on deploy (expected ~-50% for affected traffic). SRE/Obs have been pinged to annotate the Dedicated throughput SLO dashboard and ignore pre/post comparisons for 24h.

Follow-ups (not in this PR): 1) Backfill/annotation for SLO reports that span the deploy window (SRE to decide). 2) Consider moving all throughput SLO computations to request-level usage events once metering latency is acceptable.

Validation: - Replayed a production trace set in staging (mixed streaming/non-streaming) and confirmed `deployment_tokens_generated_total` matches sum(usage.completion_tokens) within expected variance from retries/cancels. - Verified SLO evaluator output for a known Dedicated deployment no longer shows >2x spikes during high streaming traffic.
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Can you confirm this won’t undercount if the client disconnects before the final usage payload? Author: Yes—stream chunks already carry deltas. If the stream ends early, we count what was actually emitted; the completion-path increment was previously attempting to “catch up” but was double-counting when the final usage did arrive.
Allison Grant (Observability): Please add a label so we can distinguish stream chunk vs completion in case we have to debug again. Author: Added `accounting_source={chunk|completion}` and ensured completion source is only used for non-streaming.
Sergio Costa (Obs): Dashboard query expects `deployment_tokens_generated_total` without extra labels; will this break it? Author: Counter name unchanged; new labels are additive with stable defaults. Queries aggregating by deployment_id remain valid.
Owen Phillips (Support Eng): SUP-18510 mentions a mismatch between Console and customer-side totals; are we aligning with `usage.completion_tokens`? Author: Yes. For streaming, the sum of chunk deltas equals the final usage total (modulo cancels). We now avoid adding the final total on top.
payload.title: Fix throughput metric double-counting for streaming responses

payload.body:
Motivation: CI feedback latency and spurious presubmit failures have been increasing as the repo grows. Two compounding causes: (1) flaky external checks masking unhealthy runners, and (2) a large surface area of transitive devdeps where stale packages cause occasional lint/test regressions. This PR introduces a lightweight CI health prober alongside a sparse dependency curator and a dark-launchable presubmit path to reduce noise while enabling incremental rollout.

What this change does (summary):
- Adds a small prober service (.github/workflows/ci-health-prober.yml + tools/ci/prober) that periodically validates runner images, network egress to common package registries (npm/pypi/go proxy), and the workspace mount behavior that has been the root of several flakes. The prober exposes a simple JSON health endpoint consumed by the CI dispatcher to deprioritize flaky runners.
- Introduces a sparse-dep-curator CLI (tools/dep/curator.py) that computes a minimal devdep set based on changed packages and a light heuristic to prefer pinned semver ranges. The curator emits a delta manifest consumed by presubmit bootstrappers to avoid installing the entire monorepo devdep graph on short-lived CI lanes.
- Adds a dark-launchable presubmit shim (scripts/presubmit_darklaunch.py) which can be enabled per-team via repo config. When enabled in dark mode the shim runs the new fast-path (curator + small bootstrap) alongside the full presubmit and reports parity metrics without blocking merges. The idea is to gather confidence and telemetry before flipping the fast path for all repos.
- Small refactors to existing lint/test bootstrappers to accept a curated manifest and fall back to full install when the curator is unavailable.

Why this is safe: changes are opt-in by default (dark-launch off), prober runs only read-only checks and timeouts are controlled, and the curator never mutates lockfiles or registry state. Rollout plan is included in the checklist.

Testing performed:
- Local unit tests for curator heuristics (tools/dep/tests).
- Integration run in ephemeral staging CI pool for 48h comparing: full-presubmit vs curated-presubmit; parity rate for lint/pytest was 99.1% over 3200 PRs sampled in staging.
- Prober deployed to staging runners for 72h; dispatcher successfully suppressed two runners exhibiting stale network mounts.
- Manual QA: enabling dark-launch for one team for 72h; metrics collected via /internal/ci-health (see rollout notes).

Checklist (complete):
- [x] Add prober workflow and service code
- [x] Add sparse-dep-curator CLI + tests
- [x] Make presubmit bootstrappers accept curated manifest
- [x] Add dark-launch toggle in repo config and runtime flag
- [x] Add minimal observability (metrics + parity logging)
- [x] Documentation: docs/ci/health-probe.md and docs/ci/curator.md
- [x] Integration testing in staging pool

Rollout notes: start with dark-launch for one team (config: teams/infra/ci-config.yaml), run for 2 weeks, validate parity metrics and error budget. If parity > 99% and prober reduces runner flakiness, flip to default for short-lived lanes and keep full install for long tests for three more weeks before full migration.

Related work: ENG-6215 (ci health observability), ENG-6217 (dep surface reduction).

Notes for reviewers: the core logic for the curator is intentionally conservative — it prefers correctness and reproducibility over aggressive trimming (we only remove packages if they're unused by changed packages or devtools with explicit allowlist). The presubmit shim includes a telemetry flag to trace false positives (curator trimmed something that led to a real break).

Ethan Moore: Could we add a timeout guard around the network checks? Prober should never block runner lifecycle. -- Done in 18a3f9d; timeouts 10s.
Lina Kovács: Add a flag to force full install for flaky PRs while we evaluate parity. -- added --force-full in presubmit shim.
Omar Hassan: Curious if curator handles private internal packages behind our artifactory proxy. -- curator supports registry mapping via CURATOR_REGISTRY_MAP; default map added to team config.
CI run summary: initial pipeline failed on lint due to shellcheck in presubmit bootstrap; fixed in follow-up commit. Final run: all checks passed (unit, integration smoke, e2e staging).
Introduce CI health prober to detect flaky runners and a sparse dependency curator to speed up presubmit installs. Dark-launchable presubmit path added to gather parity before full rollout. Opt-in; no breaking changes.
- Turn on dark-launch for infra team (teams/infra/ci-config.yaml)
- Run parity rollover analysis after 2 weeks
- Add curator metrics to CI dashboard (observability team)

Prober runs use runner credentials to probe network only; add CURATOR_REGISTRY_MAP to enterprise installs that use private registries. See docs/ci/health-probe.md for incident runbook.
payload.title: Introduce CI health prober + sparse dependency curator; slim presubmit dark-launch

payload.body:
Motivation: Customers integrating OpenAI-style function/tool calling see intermittent failures and unexpected 'tool_choice' semantics when streaming fragments arrive out-of-order or partial. This PR introduces a canonical invocation envelope (the 'lattice') that sits inside the OpenAI compatibility layer and normalizes incoming tool/function messages into a compact, ordered, idempotent structure. The lattice addresses three customer pain points: 1) streaming fragment reassembly and fragmentation-related field duplication, 2) deterministic tool_choice tie-breaking when multiple candidates are emitted across fragments, and 3) a graceful fallback/backoff policy for tool invocations when downstream tool adapters are busy or transiently failing.

What this PR does (high level): implements a canonical envelope serializer/deserializer in the compat shim; adds a tool schema mapping layer that normalizes names/params across our internal tool registry and OpenAI schemas; introduces a choice arbitration component that accumulates candidate tool choices across fragments and resolves them with configurable tie-breakers (confidence, recency, explicit client preference) rather than first-seen wins; implements a short exponential backoff for automatic noop/fallback to non-tool output when adapters fail or become overloaded; and exposes telemetry for choice provenance and fallback triggers.

Design notes: the lattice is intentionally lightweight: it keeps per-invocation provenance tokens, fragment sequence indices, and a small canonical choice list (choice_id, source_fragment, score_normalized, mapped_schema_ref). Mapping is pluggable: we include a default mapper that handles common OpenAI -> Redwood name and parameter patterns (e.g., openai 'name' vs internal 'tool_id', primitive param coercions). The choice resolver allows ordered tie-breakers configured via API flags (default: score -> explicit preference -> recency).

Migration and compatibility: the compat shim will honour clients that send single-message invocations as before; the lattice only activates for streaming/fragmented payloads or when the incoming message contains more than one candidate. We add a runtime flag to opt-out in case a customer needs legacy behaviour for short windows.

Testing: included unit tests for mapping edge cases (null params, aliased keys), integration tests that simulate fragmented streams with out-of-order delivery, and a small load test for backoff behaviour to ensure we don't excessively fall back under transient adapter saturation. See tests/compat_invoke_lattice_test.py for scenarios. CI initially flagged a flaky integration test; I adjusted the test harness timing and re-ran.

Observability and metrics: new metrics (compat.choice_resolutions, compat.fallbacks, compat.fragment_coalesces) and structured traces that include the canonical choice list and the chosen resolution cause. These are available in the console under the OpenAI-compat dashboard.

Risk and rollout plan: opt-in flag for first 48 hours for a small set of customers, then default-on after telemetry shows stable resolution rates and no increase in error budgets. No breaking API changes expected; documented fallback semantics in the changelog.
Marcus Lee: Can you clarify how we handle conflicting parameter types across fragments? It looked like we coerce to the first-seen type — why not prefer numeric when ambiguity?
Priya Nair (reply): We coerce using a small heuristic (`number` > `string` > `object`) because numeric coercions are safer for downstream adapters; added tests to cover ambiguous cases and a config flag if customers prefer strict typing.
Jordan Kim: Integration test 03 was flaky on ci/integration_openai_compat. Is there a timing dependency?
Priya Nair (reply): Good catch — the test assumed synchronous adapter ack; updated harness to allow async ack and added a retry window; CI rerun passed.
Ava Martinez: We should expose the resolved choice provenance in traces to help customers debug. Can you add a stable key?
Priya Nair (reply): Added compat.choice_provenance tag to the trace payload and documented it in the dashboard notes.
OpenAI-compat: introduce canonical invoke lattice to stabilize fragmented tool/function streaming
Tool mapping: default OpenAI->internal name/param mappings; pluggable mappers for custom registries
Choice arbitration: deterministic tie-breakers and telemetry for provenance
Fallback policy: short exponential backoff with metrics to avoid noisy failures
payload.title: Function invoke lattice and graceful choice fallback

payload.body:
Context: As part of the auto-rollback on SLO breach work, we need canonical, dashboardable metrics for (a) SLO evaluation outcomes and (b) the controller’s resulting decision (pause/rollback/suppress/no-op). This PR implements the runtime/controller-side metrics only (no dashboards/alerts here) and bakes in label/cardinality constraints so we don’t accidentally ship a rollout_id label and melt Prometheus. Related: ENG-4837, PRs #28411 (evaluator hook), #28458 (monitor adapter), #28463 (debounce/min sample). What’s in this PR: 1) New metrics (names + types): - rollouts_slo_eval_total (counter): increments once per evaluation tick per scope, labeled with outcome + signal. - rollouts_slo_eval_duration_seconds (histogram): evaluator loop duration (end-to-end), labeled with outcome only. - rollouts_auto_action_total (counter): increments when we take (or suppress) an action, labeled with action + reason. - rollouts_monitor_state_total (counter): monitor fetch results (ok/stale/missing/error), labeled with provider + result. - rollouts_policy_applied_total (counter): increments when we apply/resolve a policy version for a rollout scope (useful to verify config propagation), labeled with policy_source + policy_version_hash. 2) Canonical label set (bounded) applied consistently across metrics: - service: rollout controller target service (e.g. "gateway", "embeddings") - route: normalized route name (bounded; uses route template, not full path) - model: model family (e.g. "llama-3.1") - model_version: pinned serving version (bounded per environment; validated by controller) - region: cloud region (bounded) - customer_tier: self_serve|dedicated|private - signal: latency_p95|latency_p99|error_rate|saturation (only on eval counters) - outcome: ok|breach_fast|breach_slow|insufficient_samples|monitor_stale|monitor_missing|monitor_error|suppressed_known_incident - action: none|pause|rollback|shift_to_baseline|suppressed (only on auto_action counter) - reason: fast_burn|slow_burn|stale_data|missing_monitor|min_samples|holdoff_active|manual_suppress|incident_override|policy_guardrail (only on auto_action counter) 3) Explicit cardinality guardrails: - DO NOT include rollout_id, org_id, project_id, or raw model_id in metric labels. This PR adds a small helper that rejects disallowed label keys at construction time (unit-tested). - rollouts_policy_applied_total uses policy_version_hash (8-char prefix of sha256) instead of full policy version string to avoid label explosions. - route label uses a precomputed route template from the router config (e.g. "/v1/chat/completions") rather than user-provided paths. 4) Examples + docs in-code for dashboards/queries: Added a doc block with PromQL snippets for the observability-pack PR to copy/paste: - Auto actions by service/region over 1h: sum by (service, region, action) (increase(rollouts_auto_action_total[1h])) - Missing/stale monitors rate: sum by (service, region, result) (increase(rollouts_monitor_state_total{result=~"missing|stale"}[15m])) - Breach outcomes by signal: sum by (signal, outcome) (increase(rollouts_slo_eval_total{outcome=~"breach_.*"}[30m])) - Evaluator overhead p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(rollouts_slo_eval_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))) Notes/behavioral details: - rollouts_slo_eval_total is emitted after the evaluator computes a terminal outcome for that tick (including staleness/missing/sample gating), so we can distinguish “no breach” from “no data”. - rollouts_auto_action_total increments only when the controller writes a decision (including suppressed decisions) to the audit stream; it should correlate 1:1 with audit events once #28435 is live. - We intentionally keep “reason” and “outcome” separate: outcome describes the SLO evaluation; reason describes why we took (or didn’t take) an action. Tests: - Unit tests for label allow/deny list, route normalization, policy hash shaping, and “no rollout_id in labels” regression. - Golden test verifying metric names/types and label sets. Rollout/compatibility: - No breaking change for existing metrics. - Metrics are behind the existing feature flag rollouts.slo_evaluator.enabled for now; when disabled, no new series should be emitted. - Follow-up: observability-pack PR will add dashboards + alert rules once naming is locked. Checklist: - [x] Metrics names reviewed against observability standards draft - [x] Cardinality review (no rollout_id/org_id) - [x] Added unit tests - [x] Verified metrics in staging via /metrics and local prom scrape
Allison Grant (review): Please confirm we are not introducing rollout_id or anything user-scoped as a label. Also, can we keep label keys aligned with the draft rollouts/SLO naming standard (service/route/model/model_version/region/tier)?
Caleb Johnson (author): Confirmed: no rollout_id/org_id/project_id labels; I added a denylist enforced in code + tests. Label keys match the standard: service, route (template), model, model_version, region, customer_tier. Signal/outcome/action/reason are bounded enums.
Aisha Bello (review): For dashboards, I’d like an easy way to see “monitor missing/stale” vs “insufficient samples” so oncall knows whether to blame telemetry vs real regression. Can outcome include those as terminal states?
Caleb Johnson (author): Yep — outcome includes monitor_missing, monitor_stale, monitor_error, insufficient_samples. Also added rollouts_monitor_state_total with provider+result so we can alert on missing/stale separately from eval outcomes.
Jada Williams (review): rollouts_policy_applied_total: do we really need policy_version as a label? That can blow up if customers roll policies often.
Caleb Johnson (author): Agree. I switched to policy_version_hash (8 chars) and kept policy_source. Also gated emission behind the same evaluator feature flag so we don’t emit for every rollout in prod until we’re ready.
Logan Wright (review): Histogram buckets: evaluator duration doesn’t need super fine granularity. Can we use the standard latency buckets from telemetry lib and keep outcome as the only label? We don’t want signal/action on histograms.

Context and motivation:
This PR introduces an 'accrual ledger' for Dedicated fleets: a lightweight per-tenant credit accounting system that lets tenants accumulate unused capacity as credits and spend them for controlled bursts later. Motivation came from multiple customers whose bursty workloads either starved other tenants or caused over-provisioning. Instead of hard reservation or coarse burst tokens, the accrual approach provides fine-grained economics-aware bursting with safety fences.

Design highlights:
- AccrualKeeper component (control-plane): keeps an EWMA-based balance per tenant and enforces a max-credit cap. Credits accrue when tenant utilization is below a configurable target window (default: 5m EWMA w/ 30th percentile headroom).
- Thresholded refill: when a tenant's credit drops below refill_threshold%, the system will gradually grant refill tokens from a dedicated warm pool subject to cluster headroom limits and fairness constraints.
- Spend policy: tenants consume credits at request admission time; consumption is proportional to requested concurrency and seqlen estimate (tokens). Excessive spend is rate-limited by a soft per-minute drain.
- Fairness & safety: cross-tenant fairness implemented via proportional-share weights and a short-term anti-saturation clamp to prevent single-tenant hogging during refill windows.
- Telemetry: new metrics (tenant_credit_balance, tenant_credit_accrual_rate, tenant_refill_granted, tenant_credit_spend) + paging-friendly alerts for declining cluster-wide accrual health.

Why different from prior work:
- Unlike burst token pools that assign a fixed token budget, accrual credits are a continuous accounting primitive tied to actual underutilization, making sustained burst patterns predictable and reducing wasted reserved capacity.
- Works with existing warm-pool and headroom controllers via a thin admission proxy; does not replace autoscaler decisions but provides a tenant-visible budget signal used for admission/fallback.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement control-plane AccrualKeeper and API surface (gRPC)
- [x] Integrate admission-side spend checks in dedicated admission-proxy
- [x] Metrics + opencensus wiring and Grafana dashboard stub
- [x] Unit + integration tests for accrual math and refill gating
- [x] Canary e2e against small dedicated pool in CI
- [x] Feature gate: enabled by default for dedicated clusters but controllable via cluster config

Operational knobs (config keys):
- accrual.window_ms (default 300000)
- accrual.max_credit_per_tenant (default 10000 units)
- accrual.refill_threshold_pct (default 25)
- accrual.refill_rate_limit_per_min (default 2000 units/min)
- accrual.weight_overrides (per-tenant map)

Compatibility and rollout plan:
- Backwards-compatible: if AccrualKeeper is disabled or not present, admission-proxy falls back to existing burst token logic.
- Rollout: feature-flagged. Start with canary on one Dedicated pool, monitor tenant_credit_balance and tenant_refill_granted.
- Rollback: clear the feature flag & drain in-progress refill grants; metrics and logs allow reconstruction of state for auditing.

Testing notes:
- Unit tests cover accrual math under synthetic workloads and ensure no negative balances; added 26 unit tests.
- Integration test adds a synthetic workload in perf-canary that toggles between 20% and 180% of baseline to verify accrual/refill behavior.
- Added property tests for monotonic accrual under constant underutilization and bounded drains under continuous high spend.

Open items and followups (post-merge):
- Analytics: map tenant credit usage to per-token cost for billing (ENG-3499).
- Autoscaler integration: allow autoscaler to read aggregated credits for smarter scaling (future PR).

References:
- ENG-3456: tenant burst fairness initiative
- internal doc: RFC - accrual-ledger (linked in Linear ticket)

Morgan Lee: 'Looks great overall. Two asks: (1) add a guard that prevents refill grants if cluster free headroom < X, and (2) unit test to cover time-skewed accrual (clock drift). Please add a note in the runbook about DB migration concurrency.'
Priya (author): 'Addressed: added cluster headroom check; unit test for time skew included; runbook updated to include migration guidance. PTAL.'
Sergio Kim: 'Please make the default refill_threshold_pct conservative (25% instead of 10%) and add a feature-flag to opt out tenants via annotation.'
Priya: 'Changed default to 25% and added tenant annotation opt-out; updated tests.'
Dana Park: 'Telemetry looks sparse for alerting — recommend adding tenant_credit_balance_drop_rate metric. Also please ensure metric tags include tenant_id, pool_id.'
Priya: 'Added metric and tags; updated onboarding dashboard. Ready for final.'
Approvals: Morgan Lee (approved), Sergio Kim (approved after change), Dana Park (approved)
