payload.body:
Motivation:
Many deployments at Redwood use staged canaries, A/B experiments, or shadow validation. We observed a recurring pattern where abrupt traffic increases during promote phases spike latencies or push dependent backends to transient errors, causing noisy rollouts and manual rollbacks. This PR introduces the Traffic Hydrator controller: a light orchestration layer that smooths traffic transitions, enforces SLO-aware gating, and wires automated rollback/playbook actions when gates breach.

What this PR does (single-summary):
- Adds a new controller (traffic-hydrator) that accepts rollout intents (canary/A-B/promote) and issues fine-grained traffic change plans (micro-steps) to the routing layer.
- Integrates SLO gates (latency P95, error-rate, backend saturation) with configurable windowing and confidence thresholds.
- Exposes per-rollout telemetry: planned vs actual traffic, gate signals, and anomaly reason codes.
- Implements an automated fallback playbook: when the SLO gate is violated repeatedly within a fast-fail horizon, the controller triggers a graceful rollback, shadow-quarantine, or scaled-back slow-path depending on policy.
- Backwards compatible: the controller is opt-in per-rollout via rollout.policy.hydrator.enabled (defaults to false). Existing rollouts behave unchanged until teams opt in.

Design notes and rationale:
- Micro-step approach: instead of a single large traffic delta, we apply small fractional increments with inter-step observation windows to surface regressions early without causing large SLO regressions.
- SLO-aware thresholds: thresholds can be absolute (e.g., p95 < 120ms) or relative to baseline (e.g., p95 <= 1.25x baseline), supporting both strict and adaptive policies.
- Failure-mode policy matrix: when a gate trips we consult rollout.policy.hydrator.fail_action which can be: pause-and-alert, rollback, shadow-quarantine (route affected cohorts to shadow), or slow-path (force quantized/low-cost variant).
- Observability: new metrics (hydrator.step_duration_seconds, hydrator.step_success_total, hydrator.gate_violations_total) and trace spans for step decisions. We added Dashboard templates for rollout observers.

Files changed (high level):
- controller/traffic_hydrator/*: core controller and reconciler loop.
- api/v1/rollout_policy.proto: new hydrator policy fields and enums.
- routing/runtime_adapter.go: new smooth-apply API surface to accept micro-step plans.
- telemetry/dashboards/rollout_hydrator.json: dashboard for SREs and release owners.
- docs/runbooks/hydrator-playbook.md: human-readable playbook for incidents and manual overrides.
- tests/integration/rollout_hydrator_e2e_test.go: integration scenarios (canary success, gate-failure -> rollback, shadow-quarantine).

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Ship controller disabled by default (feature flag).
2) Early adopter opt-in: add rollout.policy.hydrator.enabled = true to a small set of internal services.
3) Observe telemetry for 2 weeks, iterate on default step sizes and window lengths.
4) Gradually flip default to enabled for non-critical namespaces after proven stability.

Checklist:
- [x] Controller scaffolding and reconciler loop implemented.
- [x] API proto changes with migration notes and default values.
- [x] Routing adapter to accept micro-step plans and apply safe rollback hooks.
- [x] Observability (metrics + dashboard) added.
- [x] Integration tests for happy/failure paths.
- [x] Runbook and playbook documented.
- [x] Feature-flag gating implemented for safe initial rollout.

Testing notes:
- Integration tests mock backend saturation and synthetic latency bumps to validate gate behavior.
- Load lab runs with perf-canary show median overhead of the hydrator ~0.3% CPU and negligible added latency (controller runs asynchronously).
- Simulated A/B experiments show reduced incident rate during promotes when hydrator microsteps are used.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Overly conservative step sizes could prolong rollouts. Mitigation: we provide adaptive step heuristics and an opt-out per-rollout.
- Risk: Misconfigured SLO thresholds may cause spurious rollbacks. Mitigation: we support baseline-relative thresholds and recommend a short observation period before enabling auto-rollback.

Related tickets: ENG-3421 (hydrator prototype), ENG-3490 (rollout telemetry agreement), SUP-7812 (customer incident that motivated micro-step logic).
Aisha Patel: This looks good overall. Two asks: (1) add TL;DR on expected operator actions in the runbook, (2) can we expose the observation-window as a rollout-level override?
Author (Marina Lopez): Added operator TL;DR to the top of docs/runbooks/hydrator-playbook.md and made observation_window_ms configurable per-rollout with sane defaults.
Liam Chen: In reconciler.go there was a potential for double-apply when reconcile restarts quickly. Suggest using an in-flight guard keyed by rollout ID.
Author (Marina Lopez): Implemented in-flight guard and added unit tests for concurrent reconcile; clarified comments.
Sofia Martins: Metrics names look good. Add a histogram for step durations and label by rollout cohort to help debugging.
Author (Marina Lopez): Added hydrator_step_duration_seconds histogram and cohort label in metrics exporter.
Aisha Patel: Approving after small nits fixed (docs phrasing).
Liam Chen: Approved.
Introduces Traffic Hydrator: opt-in rollout controller to smooth traffic promotes, enforce SLO gates, and trigger automated rollback/playbook actions on gate failures. Feature is disabled by default; enable via rollout.policy.hydrator.enabled. Added metrics, dashboard, and operator runbook.
Feature gated. Coordinate canary with platform-team. Ensure observability dashboards are installed in staging before enabling in prod. We recommend enabling on low-traffic namespaces first.
1) Deploy controller helm chart to staging with feature flag off. 2) Install dashboards. 3) Opt-in 2 internal services for 1 week. 4) Collect telemetry and iterate.
Related to SUP-7812: customer reported repeated backend saturation during large traffic promotes; hydrator addresses this pattern by micro-stepping and SLO-aware fallbacks.

Motivation: multiple SDKs had slightly divergent credential caching semantics and retry defaults which caused flap in long-lived streaming clients and inconsistent behaviour across runtimes. This PR centralizes a lightweight on-disk/in-memory credential cache implementation, harmonizes retry profile names and default windows, and smooths streaming consumer ergonomics so application authors get consistent reconnect/backoff and easier-to-reason-about stream iterators across languages. Summary of changes: 1) new cred cache abstraction (CredCache) added to all SDKs with a tiny adapters layer so platform-specific stores (in-memory, file, credential helper) can be swapped; 2) single source-of-truth retry profiles (fast, balanced, conservative) with explicit token refresh windows and jitter rules; 3) streaming consumer helpers (StreamHandle in TS, StreamIterator in Python, StreamReader in Go) that expose a pause/resume/backpressure hint API instead of ad-hoc generators; 4) minor ergonomics: better typed error variants, clearer reconnect exceptions, and safer default timeouts for handshake; 5) docs and CHANGELOG updates and semver bumps for published packages. Compatibility notes: the public call signatures are preserved for standard non-streaming APIs; streaming consumers will need very small updates if they used internal iterator internals (we provide a short migration guide). Testing & CI: unit suites updated for each SDK, e2e session replay harness used to validate long-run stability (48h soak), and cross-language conformance tests exercised retry windows and restart behaviour. Deploy plan: staged release of SDK packages followed by a runtime compatibility gate; rollout pinned to 2 Canary customers for Dedicated before broad rollout. TL;DR: fewer token race cases, consistent retry behaviour, and smoother streaming ergonomics across Python/TS/Go SDKs.
Unified credential cache across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs; consolidated retry profile config and defaults; improved streaming consumer ergonomics and backpressure hints; minor SDK semver bumps (py 1.12.0, ts 2.8.0, go 0.9.4); no breaking API changes for typical call sites.
Elena Park: Please ensure the retry window values are documented and provide reasoning for the 75% refresh threshold instead of our previous 60% -- this is subtle and impacts token churn.
Author (Jordan Patel): Answered - moved threshold to 70% after tests showed lower refresh rate reduced hotspotting; added comment and docs section with benchmark data.
Marcus Li: Nit: TS StreamHandle pause() needs a JSDoc example showing recommended usage pattern to avoid lost events during reconnect.
Author: Added example and a small utility (drainWithBackpressure) exposed from the helper module.
Priya Nair: CI flake observed on go integration test when run under race detector; can we add a retry decorator to the sensitive test or fix underlying timing?
Author: Root cause was a tight loop in the test; relaxed timing and added a deterministic hook for CI race builds; reran, green.
All checks passed on final run: unit tests (python/ts/go) green, linters fixed, integration matrix green, e2e soak completed. Two earlier pipeline runs flagged a flaky TS stream test and a go race test; both addressed in follow-up commits and verified.
Ship SDKs in the following order: typescript@2.8.0, python@1.12.0, go@0.9.4. Recommend coordinating with runtime team to enable compatibility gate and run warmup traffic for 48h. Add migration link to release announcement.

payload.body:
Expose read-only burst endpoints for Console (usage series, effective limits, denial reason breakdown).
Adds RBAC scopes and internal-only routing for Console callers; no data plane behavior changes.
Summary: Console needs a reliable, supportable way to display (1) current/effective burst configuration (enabled, caps, cooldown), (2) customer-facing burst usage over time (GPU-seconds + request-level counters), and (3) denial breakdowns by standardized reason code (from pr-23795) with enough detail to debug without exposing sensitive fleet internals. This PR adds a small set of read-only Control Plane endpoints and backing query plumbing (metering + admission controller aggregates) to power the new Dedicated Burst pages in Console (DES-219 / ENG-4855).

Context / Motivation: During beta onboarding we’ve been hand-walking customers through Grafana + internal tools to answer basic questions like “how close are we to our burst cap?”, “why did we get a spike in denials?”, and “did we hit a cooldown or a fleet safety gate?”. Support also needs a consistent surface to reference in tickets (e.g. SUP-28503 / SUP-28411) without having to grant wide dashboard access. These endpoints are intentionally read-only and are scoped to a tenant + region/hardware class view that matches what we promise in the product.

What’s included (API): Adds GET endpoints under the internal Control Plane API (Console-facing) with stable response contracts and pagination/limits:
- GET /v1/console/tenants/{tenant_id}/burst/status?region=us-east&hardware_class=h100
  - Returns: burst_enabled (bool), priority_tier, effective_baseline_gpus, max_burst_gpus, max_burst_ratio, per_window_burst_gpu_seconds_cap, cooldown_seconds, current_cooldown_state, updated_at, updated_by (redacted actor), and a small set of computed fields (effective_max_throughput_hint, is_fleet_circuit_breaker_active).
- GET /v1/console/tenants/{tenant_id}/burst/usage?start=...&end=...&step=60s&region=...&hardware_class=...
  - Returns time series: burst_gpu_seconds, burst_requests_admitted, burst_requests_denied, burst_requests_queued (if enabled in config), plus an optional top-level summary (max/avg) for the window.
  - Enforces max range (7d) and min step (60s) to control cost/cardinality.
- GET /v1/console/tenants/{tenant_id}/burst/denials?start=...&end=...&region=...&hardware_class=...
  - Returns breakdown by denial_reason_code (e.g. CAP_REACHED, COOLDOWN_ACTIVE, POOL_SATURATED, FLEET_SAFETY_CAP, TELEMETRY_STALE, POLICY_DISABLED, RATE_LIMITED) and counts, plus an optional “most_recent_denial_at”.

Key implementation details:
- Data sources:
  - Usage series comes from the metering aggregation tables (same pipeline used for billing exports) but explicitly filtered to “burst portion” (above baseline allocation). This uses the idempotency fixes from pr-24108 to avoid double-counting retries.
  - Denial breakdown comes from admission controller decision logs aggregated into a small rollup table (1m buckets). We intentionally do not return raw decision logs to Console.
  - Effective limits are computed by composing tenant config (control plane tenant model), region/hardware rollout gates (feature flags), and global circuit breaker state (pr-23919).
- Caching:
  - Adds 30s server-side cache for status endpoint; usage/denials are uncached but benefit from rollups.
  - Adds ETag support on /status to reduce Console polling cost.
- Auth/RBAC:
  - New permissions: tenant.burst.read and tenant.burst.console_read.
  - Console service uses service-to-service auth with mTLS + JWT claims; endpoint enforces “Console caller only” gate and tenant scoping.
  - Response field updated_by is returned as one of: "customer", "redwood_admin", or "automation" (no raw email), matching Security guidance.
- Error handling contract:
  - 400 for invalid ranges/step; 404 for unknown tenant; 409 when bursting is not rolled out in region/hardware (Console can show “not available”); 503 when upstream rollup store is unavailable (Console should degrade gracefully).
  - Uses standardized error codes in body for Console to map to UX states; does not leak internal pool IDs.

Files/areas changed (high level):
- control-plane/api/console/burst_endpoints.go (new handlers)
- control-plane/service/burst_read_service.go (compose effective limits + query rollups)
- control-plane/auth/scopes.go (new scopes)
- metering/rollups/burst_usage_rollup.sql (new view + retention notes)
- admission-controller/rollups/denial_reason_rollup.sql (new rollup job)
- proto/controlplane/console_burst.proto (response contracts)
- docs/internal/console-burst-api.md (internal consumer doc + examples)

Example (curl): GET /v1/console/tenants/tnt_8f3.../burst/denials?start=2025-04-30T00:00:00Z&end=2025-04-30T06:00:00Z&region=us-east&hardware_class=h100 -> {"window":"2025-04-30T00:00:00Z/2025-04-30T06:00:00Z","denials":[{"reason_code":"CAP_REACHED","count":1842},{"reason_code":"COOLDOWN_ACTIVE","count":311},{"reason_code":"POOL_SATURATED","count":97}]}

Tests:
- Unit tests for range validation, RBAC enforcement, and effective limit composition.
- Integration tests with seeded rollup data (golden fixtures) verifying stable output ordering and reason code mapping.
- Added a small load test for /usage (step=60s, 7d max) to ensure query time stays < 500ms P95 on staging.

Operational notes:
- Retention for the rollup tables is 30 days (Console uses 24h/7d defaults). Long-term reporting remains via scheduled exports (pr-24091).
- Added dashboards for endpoint error rates and latency under the existing Console API folder; alerts are non-paging (warning) unless sustained 5xx > 2%.

Review/Discussion highlights:
- Dylan: requested ETag + cache on /status to avoid tight polling; added.
- Ethan: asked to ensure determinism between “effective limits” in status and enforcement; status now reads the same compiled policy bundle used by the admission controller (same revision hash returned in response).
- Allison: called out label cardinality risks for denials; we only aggregate by reason_code (bounded set) and do not expose per-route labels.
- Sean: asked for explicit behavior when rollout gate blocks region/hardware; added 409 BURST_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_REGION and documented Console fallback UX.

CI:
- build-and-unit-tests: pass
- lint (go + buf): pass
- db-migrations-check: pass
- integration-tests-control-plane: pass

Merge: Squash merged into main. Follow-ups: (1) Console wiring PR to switch from Grafana links to these endpoints (owned by Console team, tracked in ENG-4855), (2) add “denial sample traces” for internal-only support tooling (separate PR; keep Console surface aggregated).

payload.body:
Add per-request location assertion middleware for RBAC v2 and a KMS affinity tie-breaker; enrich audit logs with location proof headers; default behaviour preserves existing global fallback. No customer-facing API changes.
Context and motivation: customers with strict data-residency requirements want stronger per-request enforcement when requests arrive through multi-region frontends and operator/back-office tooling. Current RBAC v2 decisions are made from tenant config + service-level defaults; this PR introduces a lightweight, opt-in per-request location-assertor shim that canonically translates request attributes into a location claim used by RBAC evaluation and a KMS affinity tie-breaker so KMS allocations prefer region-bound keys when available.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds middleware (services/apigateway/middleware/location_assertor.go) that validates a request-scoped location proof header (X-Redwood-Location-Proof) or falls back to a cached tenant region. The middleware sets a normalized claim 'location:region:<zone>' that RBAC v2 can match against.
- Extends RBAC v2 matcher (policies/rbac/v2/matcher.go) to accept 'location' claims at decision time and to evaluate region-aware policies.
- Implements a KMS affinity tie-breaker (services/kms/allocator/affinity.go) so the allocator prefers CMKs bound to the asserted region; it preserves existing cross-region fallback behavior.
- Enriches audit payloads (pkg/audit/writer/enrich.go) with the asserted location and the evidence source (header | cached-tenant | operator-leased) to make retrospection deterministic. Audit header name: X-Redwood-Location-Proof-Source.
- Adds feature gate and config knobs: config/security.enableLocationAssertor, and kms.affinity.enabled with sensible defaults (off for legacy tenants).
- Tests: unit tests for matcher and allocator, integration test that exercises header-present and header-absent flows (tests/integration/location_assertor_test.go).

Commits included:
- 8f3d9a3 add location-assertor middleware and initial tests
- 2b7f4d1 hook RBAC v2 matcher to request claims and add policy tests
- c1e7a80 implement kms allocator affinity tie-breaker and integration test
- d5a9b21 audit enrichment and feature flags + docs

Files changed (high-level):
- services/apigateway/middleware/location_assertor.go (new)
- policies/rbac/v2/matcher.go (mod)
- services/kms/allocator/affinity.go (new)
- pkg/audit/writer/enrich.go (mod)
- infra/helm/values.yaml (mod) - new feature flag defaults
- docs/security/location-assertion.md (new)
- tests/integration/location_assertor_test.go (new)
- Makefile / CI job config (tweaks to run integration suite under -short toggle)

Small illustrative snippet (location header validation):
- validator: if header present -> verify signed proof TTL <= 5m -> set claim 'location:region:eu-west-1'

Compatibility and rollout plan:
- Feature is disabled by default for tenants with no residency constraints.
- For customers using region pinning, ops can enable the assertor via tenant-level flag; otherwise middleware only sets a cached-tenant region claim.
- KMS allocator affinity is a soft preference; when no region-bound CMK is available the allocator falls back to the existing global pool to avoid outages.

Review conversation highlights (condensed):
- Ethan Zhao: "Nice end-to-end. My concern is the synchronous call to the location proof verifier — that could add ~10-20ms per request under heavy load. Can we cache verification results keyed by proof id?"
  - Author (Maya): "Added an in-memory LRU cache with TTL and integrated it into the verifier; documented tunable TTL in helm values. See middleware cache layer and unit tests."
- Rashida Khan: "Need to be explicit in the docs about what constitutes 'proof' and how we fall back to tenant locality. Also request more audit fields (we added source but need evidence hash)."
  - Author: "Added evidenceHash to audit payload and expanded docs/security/location-assertion.md with threat model + examples."
- Oliver Martin: "Allocator changes look good but add a metric for 'kms_affinity_miss' so SRE can tune key placement."
  - Author: "Added kms.affinity.miss counter and a dashboard note in observability-pack."

CI and tests:
- Initial CI run: unit suite passed; one flaky integration test 'kvcache_integration_test' failed (unrelated).
- Reran CI after test isolation change; all checks passed. Final CI status: pass.

Security review:
- Security (SEC-221) reviewed threat model: accepted. We added signer rotation guidance for the proof verifier and limited proof TTL to minimize replay risk.

Operational considerations:
- Default telemetry added: rbac.location_assertions.total, rbac.location_assertions.from_header, kms.affinity.miss, cms.allocator.prefers_region.total.
- Documented recommended knobs for large fleets to disable per-request verification and instead rely on tenant caches.

Merge outcome: merged to main via squash on 2026-02-25 after approvals from Ethan and Rashida and green CI. Release notes prepared for the next patch release; no automatic breaking changes.

Notes for follow-ups:
- Add a migration guide for tenants that will flip the feature gate (include example helm overrides).
- Explore signed short-lived operator leases for edge cases where header proofs are not available.
- Consider a lightweight protobuf-based proof to reduce header size in streaming scenarios.

Design doc / further reading: docs/security/location-assertion.md (new) includes motivation, threat model, and sample RBAC v2 policy snippets for region-restricted service roles.

payload.body:
Context: Prefill and decode stages continue to be a major source of tail latency variance when workloads mix many short chat turns with occasional long generations. Existing prefilling approaches either block decode threads waiting for large contiguous prefill windows or aggressively prefetch and pollute KV cache for short requests. This PR implements an asynchronous 'prefill sampler' that chooses prefill granularity per request using a priority-window abstraction and introduces a token-horizon backpressure smoother to avoid bursty prefill spikes. Motivation: Reduce decode-head-of-line blocking, lower KV cache churn, and improve end-to-end tail latency without sacrificing overall throughput.Design summary: 1) Prefill sampler: a lightweight coordinator that receives request metadata (estimated output length, priority hint, client latency SLO) and emits prefill jobs split into small 'microsegments' (typical 8-64 token slices). The sampler maintains sliding priority windows per GPU worker to schedule microsegments with locality and age bias. 2) Priority windows: each worker exposes N concurrent windows that hold prefetch priority; the sampler places microsegments into windows using a score combining request priority and recency. Windows drive GPU kernel prefetch batches that prefer co-resident KV pages. 3) Token-horizon backpressure smoother: rather than immediately issuing all prefill microsegments for a single request, the sampler applies an exponential moving-average estimator of outstanding token horizon per worker and gates speculative microsegments to keep the worker's horizon within SLO-driven bounds. This reduces worst-case spikes where many large prefill jobs overwhelm the KV memory and scheduler. 4) KV warmup markers: microsegments carry a compact warmup hint that indicates which KV keys/blocks are likely to be accessed by upcoming decode; worker-side KV cache proactively pins hot blocks with a soft TTL tied to window priority. Implementation highlights: - New module src/runtime/scheduler/prefill_sampler.rs (Rust) implements the async sampler and priority-window allocator; designed to be low-allocation and lock-free where feasible. - Kernel changes in src/runtime/kernels/chunked_prefill.cu add support for microsegment-driven prefill batches and an optional 'cohort pin' flag that pins a small set of KV pages for the batch. - Worker-side admission logic in src/runtime/worker/kv_manager.rs tracks token-horizon metrics and exposes a simple API to the sampler for admission decisions. - New config knobs in runtime/config/prefill.toml: window_count, microsegment_size, horizon_alpha, speculative_fraction. Default values tuned conservatively. - Perf harness tests under tests/perf/prefill_sampler_mixed.yaml with synthetic and replay traces. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-4521) - [x] Unit tests for sampler allocator - [x] Integration tests with kv_manager pin/unpin - [x] Perf runs across p4d and a100 clusters - [x] Feature flag gating (runtime config) - [x] Observability: added metrics and tracing spans Backward compatibility and rollout: The sampler is feature-flagged and disabled by default. The rollout plan is staged: enable on canary hosts, monitor KV hit rate, token-horizon metric, and 99p latency for 24h, then expand. Risk and mitigation: - Risk: Overpinning KV pages could increase memory pressure. Mitigation: cohort pin limited to <1% of worker KV capacity and TTL-based unpinning. - Risk: Incorrect length estimates could cause suboptimal prefetch. Mitigation: sampler falls back to conservative microsegment sizes when estimates are missing. Observability additions: - Metrics: prefill_microsegments_emitted, window_fill_ratio, token_horizon_estimate, kv_cohort_pins, speculative_pruned_count. - Tracing spans: sampler.alloc, sampler.admit, sampler.emit_batch, kv_manager.pin. Perf summary (full results in perf/artifacts/934305): - Mixed synthetic trace (70% short <32 tokens, 30% long >512 tokens): 99p latency down 18% on p4d, throughput +6% at 95ms SLO. - Replay of customer trace A: 12% reduction in median latency, 22% reduction in 99p. - KV hit rate improved by +4.3 percentage points on mixed workload. Two asks: (1) please add a short comment about race conditions between window refill and worker shutdown; (2) can we expose horizon_alpha as a percentage-based knob in the config UI?" - Ava Chen: "Added comments and exported horizon_alpha as 0-100 in the config and translated to alpha internally. Added a test covering worker shutdown path." - Priya Nair: "Can you show a microbenchmark isolating KV cohort pin overhead? I want to see the worst-case memory churn." - Ava Chen: "Added microbench in tests/perf/kv_cohort_pin_bench.yaml and included numbers in the artifacts; pin overhead shows <2.8% memory churn in stress tests." - Luca Rossi: "Approve after CI green and runbook added." See docs/runbooks/prefill-sampler.md for troubleshooting tips and rollout checklist.

Motivation: customers expect /v1/chat.completions parity for structured output, sensible stop semantics, and graceful streaming when upstream models omit logprobs. This PR introduces a focused compatibility adaptor that sits in the chatv1 parameter layer and the streaming coordinator to: 1) coalesce role metadata into a stable structured-output envelope (preserve role aliases and attach source metadata) so downstream tooling and analytics can rely on deterministic keys; 2) implement a prioritized stop arbitration layer that accepts multiple stop sources (explicit `stop` param, system-enforced sentinels, and runtime heuristic sentinels) and emits a deterministic stop reason with configurable priority and soft/hard semantics; 3) add a streaming logprob fallback that synthesizes conservative token-probability estimates when the backend returns no logprobs (avoids breaking token-level scorers and rerankers in streaming mode); 4) wire a short-lived streaming handshake for function/toolcall events to avoid interleaving partial tool payloads across fragments; 5) include a compatibility shim for OpenAI-style role arrays (user/assistant/system) so legacy clients see exact shape while we keep internal canonical structure. What changed: chatv1 adaptor and param normalization that maps /v1 semantics to internal runtime flags, a stop-priority arbiter implemented in streaming/stream_coordinator, a small logprob estimator module with conservative heuristics and tests, update to function-call streaming framing to include handshake markers, and docs + examples showing expected framed JSON. Testing: unit tests cover the arbiter matrix and fallback modes, integration test simulates an upstream model that omits logprobs and verifies downstream scorers remain functional. Backwards/forwards compatibility: feature is guarded behind a flag `compat.v1_chat_output_adaptor` (default on for hosted) and the logprob fallback is configurable per-tenant. Migration notes: none required for stored prompts; consumers relying on raw token-level logprobs should enable the experimental flag and validate. See linked Linear items for rollout plan and canary criteria.
Luis Ortega: The arbiter matrix looks good but we need explicit coverage for overlapping stop tokens and streaming prefix truncation - please add a test for stop that crosses fragment boundary.
Maya Chen: Added cross-fragment stop test in integration suite and documented the expected behavior in the streaming doc. PTAL.
Zara Patel: Can we make the logprob fallback conservative by default? Concerned about downstream rerankers getting optimistic scores.
Maya Chen: Fallback returns -Inf probabilities as a sentinel for unknown when configured `mode=conservative`. Default heuristic returns a low-prob lookup (-12 to -6 logp) but migration flag can force conservative behavior.
Evan Kim: Lint failures on initial push (import order) — resolved in second commit.
Zara Patel: Approved pending small doc nit (remove duplicate example snippet).
payload.title: chat.v1 output adaptor: prioritized stop signals and streaming logprob fallback for OpenAI /v1 parity

Context: Hot-route capacity protection adds a policy evaluation hop on the request path (gateway/routing -> policy engine) that must remain low-overhead to avoid shifting tail latency. In canary load tests we were seeing policy eval add ~2.0–3.5ms p95 at peak QPS, largely due to repeated lookups (tenant/tier/route-group) and per-check datastore reads for quota + budget state. This PR reduces end-to-end policy eval time by introducing (1) a request-scope evaluation cache and (2) batch retrieval for the quota/budget state used to decide admission/priority.

What changed: - Add request-scope cache keyed by (tenant_id, route_group, priority_class, region) for derived policy artifacts: resolved route-group match, tier defaults, priority class mapping, and compiled rule set (post-validation) - Add batch read path to quota/budget state store: evaluator builds a set of required keys (route budget, per-tier budget, per-tenant quota windows) and fetches them in a single call rather than N sequential reads - Short-circuit evaluation for common allow paths (enterprise allowlisted traffic + no overload signal) to avoid constructing unused decision objects and reduce allocations - Add microbench + production-facing metrics: policy_eval_cache_hit, policy_eval_batch_fetch_ms, policy_eval_total_ms, policy_eval_store_calls (guardrails for regression) - Preserve determinism/auditability: decision log still includes resolved rule IDs + store read versions; cache only stores derived artifacts, not mutable state - Add safe fallback: if batch fetch fails or returns partial results, evaluator falls back to prior per-key reads and annotates decision metadata with "degraded_store_mode=true"

Performance results (local bench + canary): - Local microbench (go test -bench): eval p95 improved from 2.8ms -> 1.1ms at 1000 concurrent with synthetic ruleset; allocations/op reduced ~35% - us-east canary (routing -> policy): policy eval overhead improved ~1.9ms -> ~0.7ms p95 at peak; store calls per eval from ~6.2 -> ~1.4 average - No change in decision outcomes in replay tests (golden logs) and integration tests for tiered quota windows

Why this is safe: - Cache invalidation: request-scope only (lives for the evaluation span); no cross-request stale policy issues - Batch fetch is read-only aggregation; decision semantics unchanged (verified by replay tests) - The fallback path ensures we don’t fail-closed on store hiccups; we keep existing behavior and visibility

Rollout plan: - Ship behind feature flag policy.eval.batch_fetch (default OFF) - Enable in us-east canary allowlist first (paired with ENG-4928 rollout guardrails) - Monitor new metrics and alert on policy_eval_store_calls regression + policy_eval_total_ms p95

Related: - ENG-4923: priority class evaluation + deterministic decision logging - PR #27441: overload reason codes for 429 responses - PR #27427: routing admission control driven by capacity signals

Testing: - Unit tests for cache keys + rule compilation caching - Integration tests covering quota windows and overload/admission behavior unchanged - Added bench tests in policy/engine/evaluator_bench_test.go

Notes for reviewers: Most of the diff is evaluator refactor; please focus on correctness parity (decision equivalence tests) and the store batch API contract. Telemetry naming follows the overload metrics cardinality guidance (no per-tenant high-card tags).
Mina Haddad (review): Can you confirm the cache is strictly request-scope? I’m worried about stale rules if policy bundles update mid-rollout. Also, do we log whether a decision used cache?

Jordan Lee (author): Yep, cache lives inside EvalContext created per request in the policy service handler; it’s dropped after response. No cross-request memoization. Added decision metadata field eval_cache.hit=true/false (not included in customer-facing payload, only internal decision log) so we can debug performance and parity.

Vikram Singh (review): BatchGet returning partial results is tricky. In fallback mode, are we potentially double-reading and increasing store load under pressure?

Jordan Lee (author): We only fallback for missing keys; we don’t re-fetch keys that were returned. Also we annotate degraded_store_mode so we can quantify it. In normal operation it’s a single call. Under store flakiness this may increase reads but preserves correctness. If it becomes frequent we can choose fail-open for best-effort only, but I’d prefer visibility first.

Logan Wright (review): Metric names look fine but please avoid tagging route_group as raw string if it’s high-card. Can we cap it to protected route groups only or use an enum?

Jordan Lee (author): Good call. Updated to tag route_group_class = {protected|unprotected|unknown} and keep the raw route_group only in logs (not metrics). Also added a unit test asserting no tenant_id tag usage.

Cole Summers (review): For quotas: we should keep window alignment semantics identical. Does batch path reuse the same rounding logic?

Jordan Lee (author): It does; BatchGet keys are built by the same KeyForWindow() helper used by the old per-key reads. Added integration tests comparing decision output for a set of window boundaries.

Amara Diallo (review): Any impact on 429 reason codes? We’ve had customer confusion (SUP-18421).

Jordan Lee (author): No behavior change; reason code generation happens after policy decision. This PR should reduce the chance of policy timeouts causing ambiguous 5xx -> which was contributing to confusing client behavior.

CI note: Initial run failed due to flaky integration test (timeout) in routing/policyclient; re-run passed after increasing test server deadline by 2s.

Approvals: Mina (approved), Vikram (approved), Logan (approved w/ metrics change), Cole (approved).

Merged via squash after addressing metric cardinality feedback and adding degraded_store_mode annotation.
Internal: Reduced policy-engine evaluation overhead via request-scope caching and batch quota/budget reads (behind feature flag policy.eval.batch_fetch). Added metrics to monitor eval latency and store call rate.
payload.title: policy-engine: reduce policy eval latency with request-scope cache + batch lookups

payload.body:
Motivation: during a recent regional egress saturation incident we saw repeated circuit flips as failover and rejoin events raced with KV-drain and egress throttles. This PR introduces a lightweight "safety latch" that gates circuit transitions when cross-region egress or KV pressure is detected, plus a delayed circuit-unwind path that staggers reopen attempts to prevent global flapping. Scope: runtime changes to the circuit breaker state machine, a small orchestration hook to make rejoin attempts exponential with jitter, telemetry additions, unit/integration tests, docs and an ops playbook. Key behavioral changes: 1) Safety latch: when a region experiences sustained egress saturation (configurable threshold) we mark the region as "latched" and disable automatic immediate reopen for tenant circuits that were tripped due to remote egress failures. Latched state can be observed via telemetry and toggled by ops. 2) Delayed unwind: instead of immediate circuit re-open attempts after cooldown, reopens are windowed and backoff-ed per-tenant cohort; the earliest reopen path only allows a small percentage of requests (10%) for validation probes. 3) KV-drain coordination: we add a transient hold state during KV draining so in-flight requests do not trigger reopen noise. 4) Soft rollback: a runtime flag (safety_latch.enabled=false) allows rollback without restart. Commits: - add safety latch state machine and guards (runtime/circuit_breaker/latch.go) - make reopen scheduler pluggable and add delayed-unwind implementation (runtime/circuit_breaker/unwind_scheduler.go) - KV drain hold-state integration and tests (runtime/kv/kv_drain_hold.go, runtime/kv/kv_drain_hold_test.go) - telemetry: new metrics and labels (telemetry/metrics/safety_latch_metrics.yaml) - docs and ops runbook (docs/ops/safety-latch.md, ops/deploy/hotfix-rollback.md) Testing: unit tests for state transitions (100% coverage on new state machine), integration test simulating cross-region egress stress (integration_tests/slo_regression.yml). CI: initial run showed one flaky integration test (inflight preservation under extreme backpressure) which was addressed by increasing a test time window and re-recording golden traces; final CI passed. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag, start with Canary region in us-west-2 for 24h, monitor slo_regional_reopen_rate and slo_error_budget_burn metrics, then increment to 25% of regions before global. Ops/rollback: runtime flag for immediate disable, runbook added describing steps to un-latch a region and force reopen for urgent recovery. Related work: follows on ENG-4207 (regional failover jitter work) and complements ENG-4310 (kv-coordination fixes). Merge notes: squash-merged after approvals and green CI. This PR was driven as a precautionary hotfix to reduce incident recurrence and to provide better observability for coordination between egress, kv-drain, and circuit state transitions.
Aisha Kapoor: High-level LGTM. Please add an observability note about the new metric cardinality. Asked to ensure the telemetry labels are low-cardinality. (ACTION: addressed in telemetry commit).
Miguel Santos: Requested change: make the latch TTL configurable per-region and add unit tests for TTL expiry. Also asked for explicit gating so tenant-specific reopen percent can be changed at runtime. (ACTION: added region TTL config and test coverage in latch_test.go).
Riya Patel: Noted a potential race between kv-drain hold and scheduled reopen; suggested adding a small reconciliation loop that re-checks kv state before allowing probe requests. Evan replied that a lightweight reconciler was added to unwind_scheduler.go and included tests. Approved after CI green.
Introduce regional safety latch to prevent mass reopen flapping during egress/KV pressure, and delayed circuit-unwind to stagger reopen attempts. Configurable per-region TTL and runtime flag for rapid rollback. Improves SLO stability during failover events.
Risk: new state machine could delay legitimate reopen for some tenants and increase latency for recovery. Mitigations: feature-flagged rollout, canary in us-west-2, runtime toggle to disable latch, observability hooks (slo_reopen_rate, safety_latch_state, kv_drain_hold_count) and a runbook for forced unlatching.
payload.title: regional-safety-latch-and-delayed-circuit-unwind

Motivation: During a recent regional spike we observed cohorts with bursty traffic remaining in a degraded state for extended periods due to a conservative reopen algorithm and uniform penalty decay. This PR introduces a cohort-weighted shedding policy that: (1) computes tenant cohort weights from recent request distributions, (2) applies proportional shed probabilities rather than hard cuts, and (3) adds an ephemeral recovery unwind path that allows small successful probes to accelerate a cohort's penalty decay. The change is intentionally conservative by default (feature-flag gated) and aims to reduce both tail latency and prolonged tenant starvation during soft failures.

Implementation summary:
- New coordinator: services/serving/shedder/cohort_controller.go implements a sliding-window cohort weight estimator and exposes an API to query a cohort's effective shed probability.
- Shedder logic: services/serving/shedder/probabilistic_shedder.go applies weighted probabilistic drops and consults the ephemeral_recovery manager before applying long-term penalties.
- Recovery manager: services/serving/shedder/ephemeral_recovery.go keeps short-lived probe state and allows fast unwind on verified light traffic.
- Metrics & telemetry: ops/telemetry/metrics.yaml adds cohort_priority_ratio, cohort_probe_success_rate and shed_decision_reasons.
- Config and feature flag: deployments/helm/values.yaml adds featureFlags.cohortWeightedShedding and default thresholds.
- Tests: services/serving/shedder/cohort_controller_test.go and integration/region_failover_cohort_test.go cover expected behavior under synthetic bursts and recovery scenarios.

Rollout & safety: feature-flag disabled by default. If enabled, the default policy enforces a maximum shed of 50% per cohort; SLO enforcer still has final veto.

Hotfix rationale: a small production incident where a single tenant cohort remained in soft-quarantine for hours motivated a fast, backwards-compatible fix that reduces dwell time while preserving fairness.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration test (regional simulation)
- [x] Telemetry added
- [x] Feature flag guarded
- [x] Dev review and canary run notes included
Marco Liu: Can you clarify how cohort weights are computed across region boundaries? We should ensure a regional failover won't reset weights unexpectedly.
Priya Menon: We persist only short window aggregates per-region; during failover we either rehydrate from the target region's recent window or fall back to global uniform weights. Added comments and a small integration test to cover this (region_failover_cohort_test).
Aisha Patel: Please add an explicit cap on maximum shed probability at runtime to avoid a misconfigured input causing >100% drops.
Priya Menon: Added runtime cap and validation in helm values; added a unit test for validation.
Jamal Carter: Verified metrics look sane in canary run. Approving pending small doc tweak.
Priya Menon: Updated release notes and added a note on enabling the feature flag during canary procedures.
Reviewers requested regional boundary clarification and a runtime cap; both addressed. Canaries ran with no SLA regressions and metrics showed reduced cohort dwell. CI green; merged via squash. Ops to coordinate controlled enablement behind feature flag for next canary wave.
Enable featureFlags.cohortWeightedShedding=false in prod by default. For canary: toggle on in a single region for a limited tenant cohort set using helm override values. Monitor ops/telemetry#cohort_probe_success_rate and ops/telemetry#cohort_priority_ratio. Rollback: set feature flag to false and the system will resume legacy behavior immediately.
Hotfix: Introduce cohort-weighted probabilistic shedding with ephemeral recovery unwind. Feature-gated and off by default. Reduces long-lived cohort quarantine dwell and improves tail latency under bursty tenant traffic.
payload.title: Cohort-weighted surge shedder with ephemeral recovery unwind (hotfix)

Motivation: We continue to see integration friction in customer apps when upgrading SDKs due to subtle differences in streaming ergonomics (cancel/peek semantics), credential reauth races, and inconsistent retry profiles across languages. This PR introduces a lightweight coordination primitive (SessionEnvelope) and a set of ergonomic streaming adapters to bring TypeScript/Python/Go behavior into near-parity while keeping the APIs minimal for client code.

Summary of changes: Adds a SessionEnvelope abstraction (server-agnostic session metadata + lease hint + heartbeat helper), normalizes retry profiles to RetryProfile v2 (backoff windows, jitter presets, idempotency hints), and exposes a new ergonomic async iterator surface with cancelable iteration and peek/cork hints. The PR also adds a small token refresh hook interface to avoid token-swap races during stream reconnects and introduces telemetry hooks for session lifecycle events. Finally, coordinate-version bumps were applied: typescript SDK -> v1.7.0, python SDK -> v0.9.4, go SDK -> v1.5.3 (minor).

Compatibility and migration notes: Default behavior is fully backward-compatible: old consumers keep existing flows. To opt into the ergonomic iterator, import `createCancelableStreamIterator()` and pass an optional SessionEnvelope from the credential provider. The token refresh hook is optional and defaults to the current refresh flow. RetryProfile v2 is selectable via a short feature flag (recommended for Dedicated workloads). Full migration steps are documented in the SDK changelogs and examples folder.

Checklist:
- [x] SessionEnvelope core and server contract docs
- [x] TS SDK ergonomic async iterator implementation and tests
- [x] Python shim to mirror iterator semantics (compat tests)
- [x] Go iterator facade and typed errors parity adjustments
- [x] Normalized RetryProfile v2 implementation and unit tests
- [x] Token refresh hook and integration tests with token rotation simulator
- [x] Bumped package.json / pyproject / go mod with versions and CHANGELOG excerpts

Why this is in redwood repo: Coordination touches generator templates and shared protocol docs that live in this repo; the SDK repos are version bumps that are published after merge. This PR stages the shape and tests across all three languages so downstream SDK releases can be fast and consistent.
Initial reviewer comments requested clearer separation between SessionEnvelope (transport-agnostic) and existing session headers; asked to add explicit invariants for heartbeat interval and lease expiration. Author response: added protocol doc and unit tests asserting heartbeat invariants and boundary behavior. Carlos requested a typed error mapping for Go; author added redwood/errors package shim and updated Go tests. Lina asked to ensure the TS ergonomic iterator keeps the same memory profile under long-lived streams; added stress test with 10k short messages and recorded memory allocations. After addressing comments, reviewers approved and requested a small CI rerun for flaky token rotation tests.
Added SessionEnvelope (opt-in), ergonomic cancelable stream iterator across TS/Py/Go, normalized RetryProfile v2 (opt-in), token refresh hook abstraction, minor SDK version bumps (TS 1.7.0, Py 0.9.4, Go 1.5.3). No breaking changes by default; opt-in upgrades documented.
payload.title: introduce cross-sdk SessionEnvelope and ergonomic streaming adapters; normalize auth/retry profiles; bump SDK versions

payload.body:
Problem: Dedicated fleet clients can see hard failures when slot leases evict unexpectedly during transient cluster pressure (scale-down, preemption, or spot churn). These failures disproportionately impact low-latency SLAs because callers are routed to a slot that immediately becomes unavailable. Context: We've historically relied on short-lived leases + immediate eviction propagation; that model reduces tail capacity but doesn't hedge for short window churn. This PR introduces a two-part approach: 1) a Slot Lease Hedger that maintains a small local safety pool by renewing a fraction of expiring leases proactively and amortizing renew attempts across the cluster; 2) a Fallback Router that routes in-flight requests away from slots with elevated churn risk and ensures an in-request fallback path to a compatible warm slot (same model/quantization family). Goals: reduce hard-failure rate during transient churn by >60% while keeping reserved capacity waste under 3% of active pool. Changes in this PR: - runtime: slot lease hedger (pkg/fleet/lease/hedger.go) with jittered renew windows, exponential backoff, and per-tenant soft caps. - router: fallback route selection in internal/allocator/router.go that augments the routing score with a volatility penalty derived from lease-failure rates and recent heartbeats. - control plane: metrics and tracer hooks for hedger decisions (deploy/charts/dedicated/values.yaml and docs/operational/slot-lease-hedging.md). - e2e: deterministic failure simulator to reproduce preemption windows and verify fallback behavior (e2e/tests/slot_failover_test.go). - docs: operator guide, rollout checklist, and an opt-out runtime flag for tenants. Design notes: - Hedger selects up to N hedges per node where N = max(1, ceil(0.02 * node_slots)) but respects tenant soft caps. Hedging is cooperative: nodes advertise hedges to avoid duplicated renews. - Fallback routing uses a volatility score aggregated by the control plane with 1m and 5m windows; slots with volatility > threshold are penalized. - Fallback path prioritizes warm slots with recent KV cache affinity to reduce cold-token overhead. Tests and validation: - unit tests for hedger state machine and backoff logic. - integration tests for routing scoring with synthetic volatility signals. - e2e failure replay demonstrating a 68% reduction in hard-failures and 1.9% extra slot utilization in a 2000-slot cluster (results embedded below). Rollout plan: 1) feature gated off by default; enable as opt-in for a small set of Dedicated customers; 2) monitor metrics (hard_fail_rate, hedger_success, fallback_latency) for 72h; 3) progressively enable cluster-wide with a 1%-10%-50% ramping policy. Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] e2e failure-replay - [x] docs and operator runbook - [x] feature flag + telemetry - [x] post-merge canary rollout knobs
Mateo Ruiz: Please add a brief note explaining how hedger cooperation avoids thundering renews under clock skew. Also unit-test the advertise/claim path.
Priya Shah: Added an advertise/claim unit test and a comment in hedger.go explaining the cooperative arbitration; moved the advertise jitter to a config knob (see hedger.go lines ~120-160).
Oliver Grant: Router scoring looks good; two nits: (1) make volatility window configurable via helm; (2) cap the maximum volatility penalty to avoid starving low-throughput tenants.
Priya Shah: Addressed both nits: added values.yaml entries and a hard cap; updated docs with guidance on penalty tuning.
Sofia Park: Integration test flaked once on CI due to timing of synthetic preemption. Can we make the e2e harness resilient to 1s jitter?
Priya Shah: Increased harness timeouts and added deterministic seed control for preemption events; CI run post-fix passed.
Mateo Ruiz: Approving after observed metrics on internal canary show expected failure reduction (sampled dashboard attached).
Introduce Slot Lease Hedger and Fallback Router for Dedicated fleets. Reduces hard-failure rate during slot churn with minimal extra slot utilization. Configurable via helm: hedger.enabled, hedger.max_fraction, router.volatility_window_ms, router.volatility_penalty_cap. Opt-in controlled; recommended gradual rollout.
Canary run results (2000-slot cluster, 48h): baseline hard_fail_rate=0.0125 -> hedger+fallback=0.0039 (68% reduction). Average extra slot utilization=1.9% (within target <3%). Median fallback_latency=6ms, p99 fallback_latency=38ms. Observed hedger_success=98.6% and hedger_redundant_renewals=0.6% (advertise cooperation effective).
payload.title: slot-lease hedger and fallback router for Dedicated fleet

payload.body:
Context and motivation: We observed that the current bucketing/batching approaches still suffer from two practical inefficiencies in production: (1) tail sequences cause either excessive padding or underfilled kernels, and (2) first-token stalls due to KV cache misses when coalescing heterogeneous inflight requests. This PR implements a complementary heuristic — length-strata merging with adaptive windowing and a selective KV prefetch step — which aims to reduce pad overhead while improving kernel occupancy and reducing head-of-batch stalls.

Summary of changes (single continuous description): This PR adds a new scheduler pass 'LengthStrataMerger' that groups inflight requests into dynamic strata instead of static buckets. The pass computes stratified quantile boundaries from an exponential moving window of recent sequence length samples. Within each stratum we perform a greedy sliding-window merge guided by a kernel-fit scoring function that estimates effective occupancy for a target kernel (int8/float16). Before committing a merged batch, the runtime optionally issues a lightweight KV-prefetch proto that populates dispatcher-level KV entries for prefixes likely to be requested by merged candidates (configurable via kv_prefetch_limit). The merger also respects a pad_cap_percent to guarantee latency SLOs for latency-sensitive routes by limiting allowed padding relative to the median sequence length in a window.

Why this is different from existing bucketers: Instead of deterministic static buckets, the strata are adaptive (quantile-driven) and the sliding merge window scales with observed variance (window_scaling_alpha). Unlike pure pad-minimization that can starve small sequences, this approach balances pad reduction with kernel-fit and tail latency via explicit constraints and a kernel-fit penalty. We also couple KV prefetching for merged cohorts to eliminate the common first-token latency spike introduced when multiple requests hit cold KV pages simultaneously.

Key files changed (high level):
- runtime/scheduler/length_strata_merger.cc (new) — core logic for quantile estimation, sliding-merge, kernel-fit scoring.
- runtime/scheduler/length_strata_merger.h (new) — public interface and config struct.
- runtime/kv/cache_prefetcher.cc (mod) — lightweight prefetch API and metrics hooks.
- runtime/config/defaults.yaml (mod) — default knobs for length_strata_count, window_scaling_alpha, kv_prefetch_limit, pad_cap_percent.
- perf/perf-canary/bench_strata_merger.py (new) — microbench harness for synthetic seqlen distributions.
- tests/scheduler/test_length_strata_merger.py (new) — unit tests for scoring and merging invariants.
- docs/ops/strata_merge.md (new) — operator-facing explanation and config guidance.

Commits (high level):
- feat: add length strata estimator and merger pass (initial impl)
- feat: integrate kernel-fit scoring and pad_cap enforcement
- feat: add KV prefetch API and connect to merger
- test: unit tests and perf-canary harness
- docs: operational runbook and config examples
- ci: flake fixes and lint adjustments

Internal API notes and knobs:
- length_strata_count (int, default 8): number of quantile strata; lower counts reduce overhead on scheduling thread.
- window_scaling_alpha (float, default 0.5): controls how much the sliding merge window grows when seqlen variance is high.
- kv_prefetch_limit (int, default 16): max number of KV entries to prefetch for a merged cohort. Prefetch is no-op when KV cache hit rate is above configured threshold.
- pad_cap_percent (float, default 30.0): maximum allowed padding ratio relative to stratum median for latency-sensitive routes (overrides full pad minimization).

Benchmarks (perf-canary summary):
We executed perf-canary runs with three synthetic mixes: short-heavy (median 16, long tail 512), bimodal (16/256), and uniform (1..1024). Key observed improvements vs baseline (existing bucketer + greedy packer):
- pad token reduction: 35% (short-heavy), 28% (bimodal), 15% (uniform)
- throughput uplift (tokens/sec): +12% (short-heavy), +9% (bimodal), +4% (uniform)
- p95 latency: improved by 7–18ms depending on mix; first-token tail reduced by ~30% on workload mixes where KV cold misses were common.
Measurement caveats: absolute numbers depend on model, sequence length distribution, and instance type. Results were gathered on G4dn-like testbed and a subset of optimizations (kernel-fit weighting) is more impactful on int8 paths.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests added for quantile estimator, window scaling invariants, kernel-fit scoring and pad_cap enforcement.
- Integration test in perf-canary runs (bench_strata_merger.py) added and marked flakiness-tolerant.

Review conversation (highlights, chronological):

- Anya Petrov (approval): "Approach wise this looks safe and the metrics hooks let ops tune behavior. Approved."

Operational notes for rollout:
- Default config kept conservative; feature is disabled for routes flagged with 'strict_latency: true' unless route opts in.
- Gradual rollout strategy suggested: enable on low-traffic staging clusters, evaluate pad_token and p95 traces, then flip on for selected non-urgent public routes.
- Expose metrics: strata_count, avg_window_width, pad_ratio_by_route, kv_prefetch_hits, kv_prefetch_failures, kernel_fit_score_histogram.

Related work and upstream links:

- ENG-2101 (Linear): KV cache prefetch prototypes and telemetry.
- Related PRs: references to earlier packing/bucketing work were left in docs for context; this PR is intentionally incremental and interoperates with existing bucketers via runtime flags.

Merge strategy and outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals and CI green. Merged as a single-change commit to keep the runtime change atomic.

- Explore a learned kernel-fit model (small NN) instead of the heuristic scoring function used here.
- Add more perf-canary runs on low-memory/edge GPUs to tune default knobs.

If you want to validate locally: build runtime target //runtime:scheduler and run perf/perf-canary/bench_strata_merger.py with the included synthetic profiles. Configuration examples are in docs/ops/strata_merge.md.

End of PR description.
Introduces an adaptive length-strata merging heuristic that reduces padding overhead and improves kernel utilization. Adds KV prefetch windowing to reduce first-token stalls for merged cohorts. Config knobs: length_strata_count, window_scaling_alpha, kv_prefetch_limit, pad_cap_percent.

payload.body:
Motivation: tensor-parallel workloads with many short sequences and mixed batch sizes produce a high number of small NCCL collectives and fragmented KV cache allocations. This increases kernel launch overhead and reduces effective GPU bandwidth and KV cache locality under contention.

Summary: introduce a Delegated Collective Coordinator (DCC) plus a KV Slots Optimizer. The DCC defers small collective launches within a short policy window (default 1-3ms) and groups compatible launches so we execute fewer, larger NCCL operations. The KV Slots Optimizer packs small KV cache allocations into shared slabs and provides a lightweight slot reclamation heuristic that reduces fragmentation and allocation stalls. The change includes: new coordinator component (runtime/tp/collectives/coordinator.cpp/.h), a CUDA slab allocator for KV slots (runtime/kv/slot_slab.cu/.h), a runtime flag and policy knobs (config/runtime_flags.toml), observability (tracing + metrics for deferred_collectives and kv_slot_fragmentation), and tests/benchmarks.

Key ideas and design decisions: DCC runs as a per-process scheduler that inspects pending collective descriptors (shape, datatype, peer-mask). If multiple descriptors are compatible within the policy window and would target the same peer group, they are coalesced into a single NCCL launch with minimal reshaping. Compatibility rules are conservative (identical dtypes, contiguous tensors, same op type) to avoid correctness edge cases. We also added a fallback path that replays individual launches if the coalesced launch fails (NCCL errors or mismatched device topology).

KV Slots Optimizer uses a slab-based allocator for short-lived KV entries created by continuous batching. It maintains per-GPU slab pools and a best-fit small-slot index. A lazy compaction pass runs opportunistically when free space drops below 18%. The allocator was implemented to be lock-free within a stream where possible and falls back to spinlocks for cross-stream reclaim.

Performance: microbenchmarks on a 4x A100 p3dn cluster with a representative TP model and synthetic seqlen mix show: 
- aggregated token throughput +18% (steady-state) with 32-token workload, +26% with variable short sequences;
- 95th percentile latency tail reduced by ~12ms in mixed-batch tests;
- KV allocation stalls (measured as allocation latency > 0.5ms) reduced by 72%.
Real-world customer trace (anonymized) showed 14% lower per-token GPU utilization variance and fewer spike recoveries.

Safety and toggles: feature gated behind runtime flag (runtime.flags.enable_delegated_collectives = true) and a per-tenant policy. Default rollout: disabled on main; enabled in Dedicated canary clusters for 2 weeks before global rollout. We added an emergency kill switch and an automatic revert hook if error rate jumps > 2x.

Testing & validation: unit tests for slot allocator and coordinator matching rules, integration test that compares outputs vs legacy path (bitwise equality for deterministic layers, statistical check for nondeterministic ops), synthetic perf bench harness, and CI integration tests. Benchmarks are reproducible under benchmarks/tp/kv_slots_bench.md.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-1427) [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] perf bench results attached [x] metrics + tracing added [x] docs/rollout notes added

Migration notes: no user-visible API changes. Admins may see new runtime flags. Rollout should be gradual to catch topology-specific regressions (heterogeneous link rates).

Risks: coalescing adds complexity to scheduling; conservative compatibility checks chosen to avoid correctness issues. NCCL multi-op fusion depends on topology (NVLink vs PCIe) — DCC respects peer-group bandwidth hints.

Files of interest and short rationale: runtime/tp/collectives/coordinator.cpp - core DCC logic and coalescer; runtime/kv/slot_slab.cu - slab allocator for small KV entries (optimized CUDA kernels for memcpy/memset coalescing); runtime/scheduler/slot_allocator.rs - integration with continuous batching to reserve slots ahead of a batch; tests/tp/collective_integration_test.py - end-to-end validation; docs/perf/kv_slots.md - operational guidance and flags.

Next steps: canary rollout, telemetry monitoring, and follow-up improvements to allow multi-shape coalescing (future work ENG-1502).
Owen Reyes (request changes): Please surface the runtime flag via the console rollout UI config and add a safety timeout for deferred window (what if descriptors never align?).
Author (Priya): Added console config mapping and a max_deferral_ms parameter with a default of 3ms; if descriptors don't align we execute the oldest descriptor at max_deferral_ms.
Marta Ivanov (suggestion): The CUDA allocator path should avoid host synchronization in fast path. Also add a microbenchmark that measures slab compaction cost.
Author (Priya): Reworked allocator to use stream-ordered release and added a compact_cost microbench in benchmarks/tp/kv_slots_bench.md.
Jasper Liu (approval): Verified integration test outputs and perf runs on 4-GPU and 8-GPU CI bench node. Approving after CI green.
Introduce Delegated Collective Coordinator to coalesce small NCCL collectives and a KV Slots Optimizer to reduce KV allocation fragmentation. Improves throughput and latency for short-sequence tensor-parallel workloads. Feature is disabled by default and gated via runtime flag.
Enable runtime.flags.enable_delegated_collectives on canary clusters first. Monitor metrics: runtime.deferred_collectives.count, runtime.deferred_collectives.coalesce_rate, runtime.kv_slot_fragmentation, and per-tenant error_rate. Rollback if error_rate > 2x or coalesce_rate remains near 0 (indicates compatibility mis-match).

payload.body:
Context and motivation: Long prefills for high context windows cause decode stalls and KV cache churn under mixed workloads (short interactive vs long-batched). Existing chunked prefill heuristics are coarse-grained and do not adapt to instantaneous latency SLO pressure or KV priming state. This PR introduces an end-to-end latency-adaptive "mini-chunk" prefill flow that breaks large prefill windows into small opportunistic mini-chunks, coordinates speculative KV priming for upcoming decode slices, and gates decode start based on a latency-aware sampler.

Design summary: The feature has three cooperating components: 1) Mini-chunk scheduler: continuous batching layer that slices prefill work into small prioritized mini-chunks (default 8-32 tokens) and schedules them across GPU streams to improve overlap with decode. Chunk size is adaptive and computed from recent token-latency distribution and SLO headroom. 2) Decode gating / sampler: a lightweight feedback loop running in the request path that decides when to start decode based on current SLO headroom, active batch occupancy, and KV primer state; it can delay decode by one or two mini-chunks to allow KV primer or kernel warmup to finish when beneficial. 3) KV primer (speculative priming): a best-effort background task that prefetches KV entries for high-confidence next-token prefixes (using a short ngram predictor) and maintains a soft TTL per context to avoid premature evictions. The primer also exposes hints to the scheduler so mini-chunks that would populate hot KV entries are prioritized.

Why this is different from previous work: Prior PRs focused on larger chunking, prefill/decode handoffs and fixed-stage overlap windowing. This change targets the micro-scheduling level: mini-chunks trade a small increase in overhead for substantially better overlap between prefill and decode and reduce tail latency variance by avoiding large single-shot prefill spikes. The adaptive sizing lets workloads with bursty short requests benefit without regressing throughput on long batched sessions.

Implementation notes: Key changes across components: - src/runtime/prefill/mini_chunk_scheduler.cpp/h: new scheduler module, token-size estimator, and queueing primitives. - src/runtime/kv/kv_primer.*: speculative primer implementation and soft TTL management. - src/runtime/scheduler/latency_sampler.cpp: SLO-aware sampler that computes headroom and advises gating. - src/runtime/ops/prefill_dispatcher.cpp: integration hooks to split prefill requests into mini-chunks and attach primer hints. - python/eval/bench/mini_chunk_bench.py: microbench harness for p95/p99 token latency and KV hit-rate. - docs/ops/mini-chunk.md: operator guide and rollout steps.

Backwards compatibility and safety: All behavior is behind a runtime flag "enable_mini_chunk_prefill" (default off in this PR for controlled rollout). The primer is best-effort and non-blocking; failures are logged and do not change request correctness. We add metrics and a conservative automatic fallback to legacy prefill when certain counters exceed safety thresholds (e.g., primer_error_rate > 0.5% or kv_miss_rate rises > 3%).

Testing and results: Extensive benching on the perf-lab across 3 model families (Llama2-13B, Red-7B, small-embed toy model) and mixed traffic templates. Representative results (lab, p95 token latency, compared to baseline): - Llama2-13B mixed interactive: p95 reduced 8.3%, p99 reduced 4.7%, throughput neutral (+0.7%). - Red-7B high-batch long contexts: throughput improved 2.4% and p95 reduced 5.1% due to better stream overlap. - Small-embed stress test: kv_miss_rate down 1.9 percentage points and prefix_latency variance down 12%. Note: microbench is deterministic but production numbers will vary; rollout uses canary gates.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag. 2) Enable for internal perf canary pool (10% of traffic) for 48 hours, monitor metrics (token_latency_p95, kv_miss_rate, batch_size_histogram, primer_error_rate). 3) Gradual ramp to 50% over a week if metrics stable, else roll back. An automated rollback rule is included (p95 regression > 3% for 1 hour triggers rollback).

Open items / follow-ups: - Experiment with adaptive decay for primer TTL based on model and workload (ENG-9052). - Integrate prefix-aware kernel selection hints (follow-up PR). - Add JS/TS SDK toggle for customers to opt-in.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation and unit tests - [x] Microbench harness added - [x] Docs and rollout notes - [x] Safety gates and metrics - [x] Perf numbers collected and reviewed

Ethan Brooks (2025-03-13): Nice approach. Two asks: (1) please add a short explanation of why mini-chunk sizes default to 8-32 tokens in code comments, and (2) ensure the sampler does not spin-check busy loops; prefer event-based signals.
Priya Narayanan (2025-03-13): Addressed both. Added comments in mini_chunk_scheduler.h; sampler now subscribes to batch occupancy events instead of tight polling.
Sofia Martinez (2025-03-15): Can we get a safety net that disables primer if memory pressure spikes? Also saw one flaky test on CI, test_mini_chunk_scheduler::handles_concurrent_inserts; please investigate.
Priya Narayanan (2025-03-16): Added primer memory_pressure guard and adjusted unit test timing to remove nondeterminism. CI rerun passed.
Alex Chen (2025-03-17): Approving assuming canary monitors are ready. Suggestions: expose kv_primer.enabled as a runtime knob in ops docs for quick rollback.
Priya Narayanan (2025-03-17): Done—docs updated and ops toggle exposed. Ready to merge behind flag.
Introduce latency-adaptive mini-chunk prefill with speculative KV priming and decode gating. Opt-in via runtime flag 'enable_mini_chunk_prefill'. Improves p95 token latency on mixed workloads and reduces KV miss noise. See docs/ops/mini-chunk.md for rollout and monitoring guidance.

Context: We observed unit-econ regressions on spiky workloads where aggressive batching + static rate limits caused token-level cost overruns and cold-KV cache thrash. This PR introduces an adaptive token-rate limiter at the batch scheduler boundary paired with lightweight metering for token-prefill usage and a small quant-profile seeder that suggests tenant-scoped quantization presets based on early workload signals. Motivation: provide an automated safety net that keeps latency SLOs while reducing per-token cost for multi-tenant workloads and give operators a low-friction way to bootstrap quant profiles for new tenants. What changed: 1) runtime/batcher: add adaptive_token_rate_limiter which monitors per-second token consumption, outstanding KV cache hits, and recent decode latency to dynamically adjust allowed tokens-per-second for new micro-batches; 2) telemetry: emit token_meter.{tenant,route,model} counters and a prefill_efficiency gauge that feeds Optimize heuristics; 3) optimizer/quant: add quant_profile_seeder service that ingests short-lived telemetry windows and proposes quant presets (int8/int4/ffn-compression candidates) to the profile store; 4) policy: fallback rules so when latency or error signals spike the limiter aggressively reduces batch token budgets and favors lower-quantization safety tiers. Backwards compatibility: opt-in via feature flag "adaptive_batch_rate_v1" with default off for Dedicated/Private; telemetry schema additions are additive. Security/privacy: no model weights or request payloads are shipped; only aggregated token counts and micro-batch level latencies are emitted. Testing & validation: unit tests for limiter/hysteresis, integration test with local serving runtime that simulates spike traces, and an end-to-end smoke run against a staging tenant. Related Linear/Jira: ENG-4201 (adaptive limiter design), ENG-4202 (quant seeder prototype), SUP-1337 (incident that prompted throttle). Checklist: - [x] Design doc updated - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Docs/ops note added - [x] Feature flag gated - [x] Telemetry hooks added Migration notes: operators should enable the flag in staging for 24–72h to collect seeder suggestions before enabling in production. Rollout plan: canary 5 tenants -> 20% traffic -> 100% after 72h stable metrics.
3 commits: 1) add adaptive_token_rate_limiter with hysteresis and config knobs; 2) wire telemetry and feature-flag gating; 3) implement quant_profile_seeder and CLI export of suggested profiles
Diego: 'Limiter looks sensible but add a guard for KV evictions — we saw regressions in a previous patch.' Asha: 'Added eviction-aware backoff and unit test (limiter_test.go).' Lena: 'Telemetry protobuf needs a stable name; prefer token_metering.v1.' Asha: 'Renamed and kept backward additive changes.' Ravi: 'Please ensure seeder proposals are advisory only and not auto-applied.' Asha: 'Seeder defaults to 'suggest' mode; applied only via admin approval; added CLI to export suggestions for review.' CI: first run failed on flake in tests/integration/test_adaptive_rate_seeder.py (timeout); re-ran after increasing test timeout and replaced a deterministic sleep with a wait-for-condition; CI passed on second run. Approvals: Diego approved (2026-03-01), Lena approved with comment (2026-03-02), Ravi requested one minor change (made).
Introduce adaptive token-rate limiter to control batch token budgets under bursty traffic; add token-level metering telemetry and a quant profile seeder that proposes per-tenant quant presets. Feature gated behind 'adaptive_batch_rate_v1'.
Enable feature flag in staging for 24-72h. Watch prefill_efficiency and token_meter.{tenant} counters. Seeder suggestions are exported to /var/lib/redwood/quant_suggestions/<tenant>.json by default. If latency increases, disable the flag to revert to static batch budgets.
Local unit tests cover limiter hysteresis and eviction backoff. Integration simulated scenario with 3x traffic spike and validated limiter throttles new micro-batches within 120s. End-to-end smoke on staging tenant showed 12% reduction in per-token infra cost with stable p95 latency.
Telemetry fields are additive; downstream Optimize pipelines will consume token_metering.v1. Quant seeder outputs a ranked list of safe->aggressive presets. Be conservative when auto-applying presets; the PR keeps manual approval for now.
Low risk when gated. Expected positive cost delta for bursty workloads where prefill inefficiency was >20%. No breaking API changes. Operational overhead: small additional telemetry ingestion and a background seeder job that runs every 15 minutes.
