payload.body:
Runtime request logs and traces now include quant_profile_id and quant_profile_resolution (applied|fallback|disabled) to improve debuggability during route-level quantization rollouts.
Context: With route-level quantization profiles (ENG-5816) we need a deterministic, low-friction way to answer: (a) which profile was requested/resolved for a given request, and (b) whether the runtime actually applied it vs fell back to baseline. We already emit aggregate metrics (see pr-18463) but oncall/support and design partners are repeatedly asking for request-level attribution in logs/traces. This PR adds structured log fields and OpenTelemetry span attributes for quant_profile_id and resolution outcome across the request lifecycle. What’s included: 1) Structured request logs: add fields `quant_profile_id` (string) and `quant_profile_resolution` (enum: applied|fallback|disabled). For fallback paths we also emit `quant_profile_fallback_reason` (enum) to avoid forcing operators to infer from error text. 2) Tracing: set OTel attributes on the request root span (and propagate to child spans via context) `redwood.quant.profile_id` and `redwood.quant.resolution`. We intentionally do not add per-token or per-layer annotations. 3) Determinism: values are populated from the post-policy resolved profile ref that is already pinned in the request context; we do not re-query registry/policy during logging. 4) Performance/safety: annotations are added to the existing structured logger payload; no additional allocations on hot decode loop; profile_id is bounded (registry-signed IDs) and should not introduce unbounded cardinality beyond expected profile versions. Example: quant enabled + applied: {"request_id":"req_...","route":"chat-prod","model":"llama-3.1-70b","quant_profile_id":"qpl_llama-3.1-70b_int8_v3","quant_profile_resolution":"applied"}. Quant enabled but incompatible -> fallback: {"request_id":"req_...","quant_profile_id":"qpl_llama-3.1-70b_int8_v3","quant_profile_resolution":"fallback","quant_profile_fallback_reason":"incompatible_hardware"}. Quant feature off / no ref configured: {"request_id":"req_...","quant_profile_id":"","quant_profile_resolution":"disabled"}. Notes: This is intentionally scoped to annotation only (no new dashboards). Downstream dashboards/alerts will key off these fields via existing log-based metrics work in ENG-5817. Testing: unit tests for resolution mapping + OTel attribute propagation; integration test ensures log payload contains fields for applied/fallback/disabled without changing existing log schema for other requests.
Hiro Tanaka (review): Can we guarantee we annotate the span after resolution but before decode starts? Want to be sure child spans inherit attributes for kernel selection profiling.
Noah Patel (author): Yep—attributes are set on the request root span right after policy resolution and before engine dispatch. Child spans read from the request context. Added a regression test to assert attribute presence on decode span too.
Caleb Johnson (review): Please prefix the OTel attribute keys with a stable namespace (we’ve been using `redwood.*`). Also, avoid `profile_ref` terminology in logs—customers keep asking for `quant_profile_id` specifically.
Noah Patel (author): Updated keys to `redwood.quant.profile_id` + `redwood.quant.resolution` and standardized field name to `quant_profile_id` everywhere. Left internal `profile_ref` in code comments only.
Mina Haddad (review): For fallback, can we include a reason code? Otherwise it’s hard to distinguish incompatible hardware vs max context vs artifact fetch failure.
Noah Patel (author): Added `quant_profile_fallback_reason` with a small enum (incompatible_hardware, incompatible_model, max_context_exceeded, artifact_unavailable, kill_switch_enabled, unknown). The runtime already has these branches; this just surfaces the classification.
Connor O'Brien (review): Any concerns about cardinality in log-based metrics if profile_id is high-cardinality?
Noah Patel (author): Profile IDs are versioned but expected to be low (single digits per model family). We also emit resolution even when profile_id empty (disabled) so we can measure baseline share without grouping by ID.
Hiro Tanaka (approve): LGTM after the decode span assertion. Thanks for keeping this out of the hot loop.
Caleb Johnson (approve): Approved. Attribute naming and schema update look good.
Mina Haddad (approve): Approved. Reason codes will help a lot for routing triage.
payload.title: runtime: annotate logs/traces with quant_profile_id + resolution outcome

payload.body:
Motivation:
High-fragmentation scenarios in multi-tenant KV pools were triggering large, reactive spillovers and multi-page churn that elevated tail latency and cost. Existing eviction heuristics aggressively greedified hot tenants or compacted large ranges, which worked poorly when small, interleaved allocations prevented contiguous reclaim. This PR adds a page-fence evictor and tenant slack reservation mechanism to provide smoother reclaim behavior, pre-emptive micro-reclamation windows, and tighter integration with the continuous batching scheduler.

What this change does (summary):
- Adds a page-fence eviction algorithm that marks soft fences around hot ranges and prefers fenced-localized reclamation to reduce cross-range fragmentation.
- Introduces tenant-level slack reservations (configurable per-tenant) so tenants keep a small working-set buffer that avoids immediate spillover when transient bursts occur.
- Hooks the evictor into the continuous batching scheduler so reclamation work is batched with background kernel scheduling cycles to avoid latency spikes.
- Provides a gentle degradation mode: when global pressure is high, the evictor expands fence windows gradually and triggers cooperative eviction across tenants.
- Tests, benchmarks, and operational docs for on-call tuning.

Implementation notes (high level commits):
- commit 1: implement page_fence_evictor core loop, estimate fragmentation score per-page and fence creation heuristics.
- commit 2: tenant_slack reservation API and persistence; per-tenant token bucket-style slack ledger.
- commit 3: scheduler integration: continuous_batching: schedule_reclaim_hook and low-priority reclaim worker.
- commit 4: telemetry: metrics for fence_count, fence_hit_ratio, slack_consumption, and spillover_events.
- commit 5: unit/integration tests and a small e2e benchmark harness under test/kv_fence_bench.*

Files changed (high-level):
- kv/evictor/page_fence_evictor.rs - new algorithm and core logic (approx 480 lines).
- kv/allocator/tenant_slack.rs - reservation ledger and API hooks.
- runtime/scheduler/continuous_batching.rs - hook to schedule reclaim windows and backoff policy.
- tests/unit/test_page_fence.rs - unit tests for fence creation and scoring.
- tests/integration/kv_stress_slack.py - integration script to validate spillover behavior under mixed tenants.
- docs/operational/kv_tuning.md - guidance for tenant slack sizing and fence thresholds.
- observability/metrics/registry.yaml - added new metrics and alert knobs.

Behavioral details and knobs:
- page_fence_evictor computes a per-page fragmentation score using occupancy variance and neighbor-free-run-length. Fences are created when localized fragmentation exceeds the configured fence_threshold (default 0.65). Fences are soft: they bias reclaim decisions but do not hard-pin pages.
- tenant_slack is a small soft-reservation expressed in pages (default 4 pages) and can be configured per-tenant via ControlPlane configs. Slack is drawn down during bursts and replenishes at a small steady rate; if a tenant exhausts slack and global pressure is high, they become eligible for cooperative reclaim.
- Scheduler integration ensures reclamation work is grouped into the low-priority continuous batching pass. This prevents per-request latency interference by performing defrag/reclaim work in micro-batches between request batches.

Benchmarks and results (summary):
- micro-bench (10 tenants, 50% hot working set): tail P99 latency reduced by ~22% vs master under identical GC/evictor settings.
- spillover event frequency reduced by ~55% on synthetic fragmentation traces (small, interleaved allocations).
- small throughput regression (approx 0.8%) observed under extreme global pressure due to additional reclaim work; mitigated by tuning reclaim_backoff_ms and fence expansion rate. Detailed numbers in docs/operational/kv_tuning.md.

Testing done:
- Unit tests for fence scoring and slack ledger (coverage added).
- Integration stress test across 1000 simulated tenants and a replay of production hotspot traces (redwood/bench/replays/trace-2026-01-10).
- Canary rollout over dedicated cluster: watched memory metrics, fence_hit_ratio, and spillover_events for 48h. No customer-visible errors.

Migration/compatibility:
- No external API changes. Tenant slack defaults are benign; operators must opt-in via ControlPlane to increase/decrease slack.
- If older control planes do not supply tenant slack settings, the default runtime behavior remains compatible.

Operational guidance (short):
1) Start with default fence_threshold=0.65 and tenant_slack_pages=4.
2) For tenant bursts with frequent small allocations, increase slack to 8 pages and reduce fence_threshold to 0.55.
3) If reclaim work increases CPU at peak, increase reclaim_backoff_ms or throttle reclaim windows in the ControlPlane rollout.

Checklist (as used in review):
- [x] Code compiles and unit tests pass.
- [x] Integration stress tests run and baseline compared.
- [x] Telemetry added and dashboard + alerts updated.
- [x] Docs updated with tuning guidance.
- [x] Rollout plan and canary verification documented.

Review conversation (high level):
- Maya: "Great direction. Can we make fence_threshold per-tenant override?"
- Author (Noah): "Added per-tenant override option in tenant_slack.rs and ControlPlane schema; defaults preserved."
- Diego: "Concern: reclaim work might cause CPU spikes for small nodes. Can we bind reclaim to low CPU scheduling class?"
- Author: "Scheduler hook uses the continuous batching low-priority worker and respects cpulimit_throttle. See continuous_batching.rs lines ~220-280."
- Priya: "Add metrics for fence_hit_ratio and slack_eviction_count so SRE can alert."
- Author: "Added metrics and dashboards; alerts added to observability/metrics/registry.yaml."
- Maya: "LGTM after a small nit on doc clarity."
- Maya (approval): "Approved with docs nit addressed."

CI details:
- Initial CI run failed lint on kv/allocator/tenant_slack.rs (naming conventions). Fixed in commit 3.
- Unit and integration pipelines ran; a flaky test (kv_evictor::integration::spill_replay) was muted and tracked under ENG-5210; rerun passed.
- Final CI status: pass.

Merge outcome:
- Merge method: squash and merge.
- Merged on 2026-02-20 by release-bot after all approvals and CI green.

Notes / follow-ups:
- Follow-up task created (ENG-5267) to explore adaptive slack algorithms based on tenant SLOs.
- Monitor fence_hit_ratio and spillover_events in the next 2 weeks; SRE to adjust alerts if noise appears.

Contact: @noah (Noah Singh) for runtime/evictor questions.
Introduces a page-fence based evictor and tenant-level slack reservation to reduce high-fragmentation-induced spillovers. Improves steady-state tail latency by reducing reactive paging under bursty workloads. No API changes.
payload.title: page-fence evictor and tenant slack reservation to reduce fragmentation and spillover

payload.body:
Motivation: After several incident postmortems we observed that automatic rollouts often kept progressing past the earliest signals that correlated with recent incidents (high tail latency, error spikes tagged in our incident system). This PR adds a release throttle that integrates postmortem/incident signals into rollout controllers and an operator latch that lets on-call or release engineers hold/resume promotions without taking the full release offline.

Summary: Implements a Postmortem-Driven Release Throttle (PDRT) and Operator Latch. PDRT consumes a compact incident summary feed (severity, tags, implicated services, confidence) from the incident service (SUP pipeline). When a relevant incident is active or within a configured cooldown window, the throttle reduces commit velocity of canary/A-B/staged rollouts by applying a soft cap to promotion percentage and enforcing additional smoke validation checkpoints. The Operator Latch is an override mechanism visible in Console and CLI that allows authorized users to: (1) force-hold a rollout, (2) force-resume with audit comment, or (3) enable temporary fast-path for emergency fixes. Audit logs and KMS-backed signatures are recorded for all latch actions.

What changed (high-level):
- rollout/controller: add PDRT integration point, incident consumer, and throttle policy evaluation.
- orchestration/api: expose latch endpoint (POST /rollouts/:id/latch) with RBAC checks and audit recording.
- console/ui: add a compact latch control and incident context summary on rollout details page.
- telemetry: new rollout_throttle.{applied,reason} metrics and histograms for throttle_fraction.
- rollout-playbooks: default canary manifest updated to include incident_cooldown and soft_throttle settings.

Design notes:
- The incident consumer is intentionally compact and defensive: it only considers incidents with scope:inference, tags intersecting ["latency", "timeout", "model-serving"], and severity >= P2. Default cooldown is 2h after incident resolution.
- Throttle is a soft policy: it scales down target traffic fraction according to severity-weighted budget. Example: severity P1 -> cap 10% per 15m increment, P2 -> cap 30%, P3 -> no cap.
- Operator latch is independent of PDRT. Users with release:manage or sre:respond roles can act. All actions record an audit entry and create a telemetry event for retrospective analysis.

Rollout behavior examples: (embedded in the controller logic)
1) Canary started at 1%. Simultaneous P1 incident detected that matches model-serving tags -> throttle applies cap to 10% and pauses auto-escalation beyond that until additional smoke checks pass or incident cooldown ends.
2) A/B experiment: throttle will rebalance incremental allocations to new variant conservatively while preserving minimum retention for control.
3) Shadow seeding unaffected but sampling rate is reduced if incident indicates saturation on GPU nodes.

Security & compliance: Latch endpoints require RBAC and audit trails. Audit entries are forwarded to the existing audit-log-exporter pipeline. We added KMS signature stamps for manual overrides to prove operator intent for postmortem timelines.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests: controller policy evaluation, incident filter heuristics, latch RBAC.
- Integration tests: simulated incident feed via test harness that asserts throttle_fraction metrics, rollback triggers, and latch audit entries.
- E2E: staged canary in perf-canary cluster with synthetic incident generator used to validate soft-throttle behavior and safe resume paths.
- Load test: ensure telemetry tag cardinality remains bounded when many incidents correlate.

Commits: ["feat(controller): add postmortem throttle policy and evaluation", "feat(api): latch endpoints + RBAC enforcement", "ui: add latch button and incident context panel", "chore(tests): add integration tests for incident feed", "docs: rollout playbook and operator guide"]
Add postmortem-driven release throttle and an operator latch to allow manual intervention during automated rollouts. Enables tighter incident-to-rollout feedback and safe overrides for urgent responses.

Priya Kapoor: can we make the cooldown window configurable per-namespace? (answered: yes, namespace override added)
Marco Ruiz: request to add acceptance test for RBAC negative case (added)
Anika Shah: responded with rationale for soft vs hard throttle and linked simulation graphs: https://internal.redwood/graphs/pdrt-sim-2026-02
merged by squash on 2026-02-18 (merge commit: feat: add pdrt and latch; reviewers: Liam Chen, Priya Kapoor). Post-merge actions: feature flag rollout enabled at 0% for internal org, scheduled incremental enable to 10% after 48h of stable telemetry.
Behind feature flag release.postmortem_throttle; rollout plan: internal 0% -> 10% after 48h -> 50% after 7d with SRE sign-off. Operator guide and playbook added under docs/operator/release-latch.md.
Initial rollout to 0% observed expected telemetry events. Integration test harness recorded throttle_fraction histogram buckets consistent with simulated severity weights. No regressions in canary pipeline. One minor UI accessibility note fixed in follow-up PR.
Add postmortem-driven soft throttle and operator latch for controlled rollouts. Improves safety of automated promotions during incident windows.

Context: Dedicated burst capacity needs guardrails that are (a) configurable, (b) deterministic, and (c) explainable. Admission Controller and Routing both consume the policy engine for decisions, so we need first-class rule support rather than ad-hoc config parsing.

This PR adds a BurstGuardrailsV1 rule set to the policy engine bundle to express:
- per-tenant max_burst_ratio (e.g., 1.5x baseline)
- per-tenant burst cooldown window (min seconds between allowed burst intervals)
- per-region/hardware global fleet safety caps (absolute + percentage) and an optional emergency disable bit

The goal is to make guardrails expressible entirely via policy bundle config (with defaults), while keeping evaluation deterministic under telemetry lag. This PR DOES NOT change admission behavior by itself; it extends the policy engine schema + evaluation result so downstream services (admission controller, router) can rely on a stable contract.

Key decisions/semantics:
- Determinism: evaluation is a pure function of (request context, tenant config, policy bundle, fleet snapshot metadata). This PR defines which fleet fields are allowed inputs and forces explicit snapshot_ts propagation.
- Cooldown is evaluated using a monotonic server time provided in the context (now_ms) plus a stable last_burst_admitted_ms in the tenant runtime state passed to the policy engine. No lookups inside the policy engine.
- Max burst ratio is expressed against tenant reserved_baseline_gpus (or reserved_capacity_units); if missing, policy returns a validation error and defaults to deny-burst (fail closed).
- Global caps can be expressed per (region, hardware_class) with an override wildcard ("*") entry.

Implementation overview:
- Adds new policy schema types in policy/guardrails/burst_guardrails_v1.{go,proto}
- Adds bundle validation with clear error messages (surfaced to control plane on publish)
- Adds evaluation output: burst_guardrails_decision { allowed_max_burst_units, cooldown_remaining_ms, global_cap_remaining_units, deny_reason_code }
- Adds unit tests + golden tests for common configurations and edge cases
- Adds minimal docs/comments in policy bundle examples

Testing:
- Unit tests for parsing/validation
- Golden tests for evaluation determinism
- Fuzz test for schema decode + unknown fields handling

Follow-ups:
- Admission controller will consume burst_guardrails_decision (ENG-4810) and wire last_burst_admitted_ms + fleet snapshot inputs
- Routing will consume deny reason + recommended backoff when denied (ENG-4812)

Refs:
- ENG-4821 Guardrails: cooldown + fairness enforcement
- ENG-4902 Fleet safety cap and global circuit breaker

Risk: low-to-medium. Changes are gated to the new rule name (BurstGuardrailsV1). Existing bundles are unaffected unless they opt in.

Release note: none (internal contract change; feature still behind flags).
Ethan Park (review): Can we make sure cooldown uses the same notion of time as admission controller? We’ve been burned by mixed wall/mono time in past rate limiters.

Jordan Lee (author): Yep — I changed context to require now_ms (provided by caller) and disallowed any internal time.Now() usage in the guardrails evaluator. Added a test that fails if evaluator touches system time (via a fake clock that panics).

Keiko Yamamoto (review): For global caps, can we support a wildcard default per region? Some regions will not have per-HW overrides at launch.

Jordan Lee (author): Added resolution order: exact (region, hw) -> (region, "*") -> ("*", "*"). Validation enforces at least a ("*", "*") entry if rule is enabled so we don’t end up with implicit infinity.

Sean Gallagher (review): Please ensure fail-closed behavior is explicit for missing baseline fields. I’d rather deny burst than guess.

Jordan Lee (author): Agreed. Validation error on publish, and evaluation returns deny_reason_code=POLICY_INVALID_CONFIG if baseline missing. Downstream can surface this as "misconfigured" rather than "capacity".

Mina Haddad (review): Router needs deterministic deny codes for retries/backoff. Are we locking down reason codes here?

Jordan Lee (author): Added enum-like string constants in policy/guardrails/deny_reason_codes.go and tests. Codes included: COOLDOWN_ACTIVE, TENANT_CAP_REACHED, GLOBAL_CAP_REACHED, FLEET_SAFETY_DISABLED, POLICY_INVALID_CONFIG.

Benji Okafor (review): Can we keep the policy output small? We don’t want to explode label cardinality if people start emitting these fields as metrics.

Jordan Lee (author): Output is intentionally compact (ints + a single deny code). Also added guidance in docs to avoid emitting raw tenant ids with deny codes.

Ethan Park (approval): Looks good. Please add one more golden case for the wildcard cap resolution and I’m good.

Jordan Lee (author): Added golden test `wildcard_resolution_region_default`.

Keiko Yamamoto (approval): Approved.

Sean Gallagher (approval): Approved; thanks for the explicit fail-closed behavior.
payload.title: Extend policy engine with burst guardrail rules (max ratio, cooldown, global fleet caps)

Context: production traces showed intermittent tail-latency spikes when serving mixed quantized variants (INT8 baseline with FP8 fallbacks) under continuous-batching. Root cause: imbalance between scheduling lanes where early-arriving requests warmed KV cache and later lanes incurred repeated dequant/scale passes, amplifying GEMM latency and creating hot tails. Motivation: restore predictable latency SLOs without disabling quantized fastpaths or adding global serialization.

What this PR does: implements a dynamic per-lane throttler and a KV shared-window propagation mechanism plus small kernel-level fuses to eliminate an extra dequant pass in the common path. Key components: (1) scheduler: per-lane token budget and adaptive slack calculation (lane throttler) that temporarily delays tokens from the fastest lanes to improve alignment and KV locality; (2) KV cache: windowed propagation so that a warmed prefix from one lane is opportunistically exposed to nearby lanes within a small time/sequence window, reducing redundant cache loads; (3) kernels: new hybrid-quant microkernel that fuses smoothquant scale application into the GEMM prolog for INT8->FP32 accum paths, avoiding a separate dequant broadcast; (4) continuous batching: request metadata includes lane affinity hinting so the runtime groups requests likely to share KV prefixes.

Design notes and trade-offs: the lane throttler is adaptive and conservative by default: it targets 95th percentile tail improvements with a small throughput impact (<1–3%) in microbenchmarks. The KV window uses a compact bloom-like prefix hint to avoid copying large prefixes — conservative conservative memory overhead and remains optional via runtime flag. Kernel fusion prioritizes correctness; we added code paths for FP32 accumulation to avoid precision regressions on edge models.

Compatibility and toggles: all features are behind config flags and a runtime feature gate (env REDWOOD_FEATURE_LANE_THROTTLER / REDWOOD_FEATURE_KV_WINDOW). Fallback to previous behavior on any assertion or if perf regressions exceed thresholds. No surface API changes.

Testing and validation: unit tests for scheduler heuristics, KV window correctness tests, and kernel unit smoke tests were added. End-to-end microbenchmarks measured on c6g-gpu-class clusters show 18–34% reduction in p99 latency for mixed INT8/FP8 chat workloads (p50 unchanged). Additional stress tests run for 48h to verify stability.

Checklist: [x] scheduler + throttler implementation; [x] KV shared-window; [x] fused kernel path and safety fallbacks; [x] unit and integration tests; [x] perf benchmarks and reporting; [x] docs note.

Related: ENG-4129 (lane-scheduling), ENG-4190 (quant-kernel optimizations).
Maya Chen: Can you add a microbenchmark that isolates the kernel fused path vs the legacy path? The numbers in the description are promising but we need reproducible harness results.
Ibrahim Noor: Added benchmarks under benchmarks/perf and updated the PR summary with p99 numbers and methodology.
Diego Alvarez: The KV window bloom adds memory — please quantify worst-case overhead and show an opt-out path.
Ibrahim Noor: Documented worst-case RAM usage (bounded to ~8KB per worker) and added feature flag with graceful opt-out.
Priya Patel: Small nit: please add a logging metric when throttler kicks in so we can tune thresholds in staging.
Ibrahim Noor: Added metric runtime.scheduler.lane_throttler.evictions; added tests to verify metric emitted.
payload.title: Dynamic per-lane INT8/FP8 throttler and KV window propagation to reduce tail latency

Motivation: Progressive model promotes (canaries/A-B/slice-based promos) occasionally expose a mixed-state where some user cohorts see new model variants while others remain on the old model. This can surface cross-slice regressions and complicate rollback. This PR introduces a "slice-lock" concept: a short-lived per-slice lease that pins a slice's requests to a single model variant during promote/handshake, enabling deterministic drain, replay, and a safe resume path on rollback.

Summary of changes: implemented a slice-lock controller in the rollout subsystem, wire up promote and rollback paths to acquire/release locks, added handshake lease renewal (to avoid premature eviction for long-running sessions), added telemetry reconciliation window logic to delay final commit until slice-level metrics are within tolerance, and introduced operator-visible metrics and CLI commands for inspection and manual resume. Also includes integration tests, docs, and CLI helpers.

Design notes: the slice-lock is lease-based (default 30s). During a promote, the controller will: 1) create a promote token and attempt to acquire locks for N target slices based on policy; 2) pin incoming requests for locked slices to the candidate variant while the slice is draining from the old variant; 3) collect slice-level telemetry (latency, error-rate, qa checks) for a configurable reconciliation window (default 3 minutes); 4) if metrics pass, commit the promote and release locks; 5) on metric regressions or operator abort, perform a rollback: the controller triggers a resume that re-acquires locks to steer the slice back to the previous variant while preserving session stickiness.

Safety features: handshake-lease renewal to prevent race during long requests; stale-slice-eviction policy with exponential backoff; quorum-confirmation threshold (percent of slice coverage required before commit) to avoid tiny-sample commits; auto-fallback to global routing when locks cannot be acquired after a timeout.

Backward compatibility: controllers default to disabled for existing rollouts. New rollout policy schema has optional "slice_lock" stanza; older rollout specs continue to work unchanged.

Configuration (new fields): slice_lock.enabled (bool), slice_lock.lease_seconds (int), slice_lock.reconcile_window_seconds (int), slice_lock.quorum_percent (int), slice_lock.eviction_backoff_ms (int).

Testing: unit tests for lock state machine, integration test suite that simulates multi-slice traffic and injected regressions, e2e canary test that runs a staged promote with a deliberate rollback. Notable: integration tests were flaky on first run due to timing assumptions; added wait-for-handshake and explicit clock advances in harness to stabilize.

Rollout plan: feature gated via a cluster config flag. We'll ship docs and a sample rollout manifest in the next minor. Gradual rollout to production tenant groups: start with internal/dev clusters for two weeks, then opt-in beta for projects with slice-based experiments, then broad enable. The rollout controller includes telemetry gates that automatically abort commit if delta thresholds exceed configured SLOs.

Related: builds on prior work for session-affine canaries (ENG-2156) and cohort handoff (ENG-7412). Linear tasks above track followups for UI surface and additional observability.

Checklist: [x] controller implementation; [x] unit tests; [x] integration tests; [x] docs (docs/rollouts/slice-locks.md); [x] CLI inspect/promote helpers; [x] metrics and alerts; [x] changelog entry.
Samir Patel: Can you clarify how the lease renewal works for long-running streaming requests? (comment)
Maya Chen: Reply: handshake.renew() is invoked by the serving runtime on each keepalive token; added a test case for streaming with an explicit renewal path. (resolved)
Lina Alvarez: Suggestion: add an operator-visible metric for 'slices_in_pending_promote' and make the reconcile window configurable via runtime config (comment)
Maya Chen: Added metrics and config binding; updated docs with recommended defaults. (addressed)
Thomas Nguyen: Are there any cache-warmup implications when a slice snaps to the new model? Could this cause a false-positive regression? (comment)
Maya Chen: We introduced a 'warmup grace'—the reconcile window delays final commit until after warmup period; documented best-practices for heavy KV cache models. (addressed)
Lina Alvarez: Approved and ran a staged integration job on staging cluster (approval)
Introduce optional 'slice_lock' rollout policy to allow lease-based per-slice promotes with auto-resume rollbacks. Provides deterministic drain and safer progressive promotes for session-affine traffic. Config flags: slice_lock.enabled, lease_seconds, reconcile_window_seconds, quorum_percent. Backward compatible: disabled by default.
Enable feature-gate 'slice_lock' in cluster config to test. Start with lease_seconds=30 and reconcile_window_seconds=180. Watch new metrics: rollouts.slice_lock.acquired, rollouts.slice_lock.evicted, rollouts.slice_lock.reconcile_failures. Recommended alert: reconcile_failures > 5% over 5m for manual inspection.
payload.title: Granular slice-locks for progressive model promotes with auto-resume rollbacks

Motivation: Improve automated reaction to subtle throughput/latency regressions observed by canaries by introducing a runbook-driven responder and an adaptive quarantine window. This PR implements a lightweight responder that maps detected signals to pre-authorized actions (traffic quiesce, isolate model variant, scale-up, notify on-call) and an adaptive quarantine policy that tunes isolation duration based on signal stability and historical recovery likelihood. Why now: several incidents (see ENG-2418) showed oscillation between short-lived mitigations and reintroducing bad variants; this change reduces churn and gives operators a deterministic, reversible path. High level changes: 1) canary/responder: new module that evaluates severity and consults a runbook table to decide actions 2) quarantine: adaptive timer using exponential-backoff with exponential-decay memory of prior recoveries 3) telemetry: adds correlation-matrix snapshots and action tags for postmortem analysis 4) integrations: ties responder into existing canary pipeline and PagerDuty/Slack playbooks. Checklist: - [x] design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2345/runbook-guided-canary-responder - [x] unit tests for responder decision tree - [x] e2e smoke canary in perf-canary harness - [x] observability dashboards updated - [x] on-call runbook snippets added - [x] staged rollout config (canary only) Security/ops notes: actions initiated by responder are limited to pre-authorized playbook steps; no automatic model deletion. Follow-on: add ML-driven action scoring (separate PR).
3 commits: (1) add responder framework and runbook mapping; (2) implement adaptive quarantine timer and persistence; (3) instrumentation, tests, and docs updates.
Evan: 'Can we ensure the responder only performs actions flagged as safe for automated execution?' Priya: 'Yes — the runbook table distinguishes AUTO vs MANUAL actions; only AUTO entries are executed by default. I added extra audit logs.' Marisol: 'How do we avoid cascading quarantines across regions?' Priya: 'Responder tags actions with scope; quarantine is per-traffic-partition and we added a circuit-breaker threshold so the responder pauses automation if >3 partitions quarantine within 5m.' Jian: 'CI flake in test_quarantine on first run.' Priya: 'Fixed race in the timer by adding deterministic clock in tests and re-run CI.' Approvals: Evan approved after addressing AUTO flagging; Marisol approved after adding partition-scoped tags. Jian gave final approval after CI pass.
Initial CI: lint failed (unused import) -> fixed. Unit tests: failing (race) -> fixed by deterministic clock. Integration smoke: passing (perf canary echoed expected quarantine). Final CI: all checks passed (unit, integration, lint, security-scan).
Merged by Priya via squash-merge on 2026-01-20. Commit message consolidated includes responder framework, adaptive quarantine, telemetry, and docs. Post-merge: feature gated behind canary feature flag; rolled out to 10% of canaries then 100% after 48h monitoring window.
Added automated runbook-driven canary responder and adaptive quarantine policy. Defaults are conservative; automation only runs for actions marked AUTO in runbook_table. Improves stability by reducing reintroduction churn and providing clearer audit trails for mitigation actions.

Motivation: presubmit latency and noisy lint runs were slowing local dev and CI; current monolithic lint pipeline runs many rules for small changes and rebuilds whole config on workspace splits. This PR breaks the lint configuration into a lightweight workspace-aware adapter and an opt-in fastpath lane for churn-heavy directories. Goals: 1) reduce presubmit latency for busy workspaces (sdk, examples) 2) keep full lint coverage gated on staged lanes 3) enable incremental lint caching and simpler rule scoping. What I changed: introduced a new `lint-adapter` manifest that composes per-workspace config, added `fastpath` labels and routing in presubmit-orchestrator, moved shared eslint/ruff config into `ci/lint/shared/` and added a small shim that loads only relevant plugins based on changed files, added a small Go helper to compute workspace scopes in CI, and bumped a handful of lint-related devdeps (eslint -> 8.48.0, ruff -> 0.12.0). Rollout plan: deploy adapter to presubmit staging, enable fastpath for `redwood-sdk-python` and `redwood-examples` for 48h, monitor presubmit latency and lint failure rate, then flip for other repos. Rollback: revert head branch or disable fastpath label mapping in presubmit orchestrator. Performance: on a synthetic workload of 150 small PRs the average presubmit lint runtime dropped from 2m14s to 32s on the fastpath lane (60% less overall CI time observed across sample). Testing: unit tests for adapter loader, integration smoke for presubmit routing, e2e on a snapshot of sdk and examples. Notes: kept full lint runner unchanged; this is an additive refactor with opt-in fastpath; consumers needing stricter rules will continue to go through the full lane. Related: ENG-1742 (presubmit latency), ENG-1815 (lint infra hygiene).
Miguel Soto (requested changes): Please add a short grace period metric to avoid flapping when files move between workspaces. Concerned about false negatives from partial plugin loads.
Aisha Rahman (author reply): Added a 30s debounce in presubmit-orchestrator and added an explicit opt-out annotation for repos that want full-lint always. See ci/presubmit/orchestrator/main.go diff.
Lena Fischer (approved): Verified presubmit staging runs and observed stable fallbacks. Small request: include a note in the release docs about how to opt into fastpath.
Tom Wu (comment): Can we add a lint-cache TTL override as a follow-up? Not blocking.
Add workspace-aware lint adapter and opt-in fastpath presubmit lanes to reduce presubmit latency for large repos. Includes devdep bumps for eslint and ruff and a new workspace scope helper. Fastpath is opt-in and can be rolled back by disabling label mapping in the presubmit orchestrator.

Motivation: During multi-region surges we've observed cascading circuit flips and noisy tenant retries that cause oscillation and disproportionate impact to small tenants. This PR implements a probabilistic hedged-fallback strategy combined with a lightweight tenant-weight reservation token to reduce cascade risk and enable a gentle, soft-reopen path for circuits. Summary: 1) Hedged-fallback policy: when a request times out or latency SLO is at risk, we trigger probabilistic hedged calls to alternate compatible regions/models with configurable p(success) weights. Hedging probability is driven by tenant SLO weight and recent error trends. 2) Tenant-weight reservation: a per-tenant soft reservation token budget that guarantees low-rate access to stable slowpaths (regional standbys) during surges so small/high-value tenants are not fully starved. 3) Soft-reopen policy: circuits reopen with phased probe traffic and exponential jittered backoff to avoid synchronized reopen storms; reopen attempts are rate-limited and tracked in persistent circuit state so restarts survive process restarts. 4) Telemetry and observability: added metrics for hedged call ratio, reservation consumption, reopen attempts, and circuit-probe success rates; new tracing spans for hedged decision path. 5) Config and rollout: runtime flags in charts/values.yaml with safe defaults (off by default); feature gate hedged_fallback.v1; canary rollout script included. Design notes and trade-offs: - Hedging is probabilistic rather than deterministic to bound additional cost while still reducing tail latency and improving availability for prioritized tenants. - Reservation tokens are soft quotas (borrow/repay model) to avoid hard isolation; token refill is configurable by tenant tier. - Persisting circuit reopen state increases complexity but significantly reduces repeated reopen oscillations observed in incident INC-2025. Checklist: - [x] Core hedging runtime and decision logic implemented - [x] Reservation manager and lease/borrow APIs - [x] Circuit persistence and soft-reopen backoff - [x] Unit tests for decision boundaries - [x] Integration/E2E test simulating regional degradation - [x] Metrics and tracing instrumentation - [x] Canary rollout script - [x] Runbook entry added Tests and validation: unit tests cover hedging probability schedules and reservation accounting; e2e sim injects latency/failures into primary region and asserts stable failover without tenant starvation. Load tests on bench-lab show p50/p95 improvements for 99th-percentile tenants with <5% additional token cost for hedged requests. Rollout plan: merge to main, enable feature gate in canary region via charts/values.yaml, monitor hedged_ratio and reservation_consumption; if anomaly, flip feature off and rollback via canary script. Backwards compatibility: no breaking API changes; all defaults keep behavior unchanged. Related: Linear ENG-2034 (hedged failover initiative), ENG-2101 (tenant fairness work).
Diego Alvarez (2026-01-13): Can we bound the maximum extra cost from hedged calls per tenant? Please add a protective throttle at the tenant level.
Maya Chen (2026-01-13): Added reservation soft-quota with borrow/repay semantics and a tenant-level cap. See reservation_manager.go for policy knobs.
Priya Nair (2026-01-14): Circuit persistence is good; add a recovery test for process restart during a soft-reopen window.
Maya Chen (2026-01-15): Added e2e that simulates process restart and validated no reopen storms; also added metrics to alert if reopen attempts spike.
Elliot Park (2026-01-16): Minor race found in refill path, pushed a fix in cc55a66. Recommend squash-and-merge after CI green.
CI Bot (2026-01-17): Integration flake due to bench-lab network; reran and all checks passed.
Introduces an opt-in probabilistic hedged-fallback mechanism and a soft tenant-weight reservation to improve availability during regional degradation; adds persistent soft-reopen policy to reduce circuit reopen storms. Feature is behind a feature flag and off by default.
payload.title: Probabilistic hedged-fallback with tenant-weight reservation and soft-reopen policy

- Demo tenant keys are now created with scoped permissions by default (project + route + operation). - Added rotation helper to generate/roll keys and verify audit-log entries. - Added audit log coverage for key create/rotate/revoke events (including actor + reason).
Context: SEs and AEs have been sharing a single broadly-permissioned demo API key for convenience. This has caused a few recurring problems: (1) unclear blast radius when a key leaks in a screen share/recording, (2) brittle access when RBAC mappings change (INT-993), (3) hard-to-debug 429s / quota overrides (SUP-4127) because traffic sources are indistinguishable, and (4) audit log gaps for key lifecycle events. This PR tightens demo-tenant API key scopes to least privilege, adds rotation helpers for the demo reset flow, and ensures we emit consistent audit-log events for key create/rotate/revoke. Summary of changes (single-tenant + parallel demos friendly): 1) New scoped key model for demo workflows: - Introduce explicit permission bundles for demo use cases: `demo.chat.invoke`, `demo.embeddings.invoke`, `demo.routes.read`, `demo.console.read`, `demo.eval.run` (internal), `demo.traffic.seed` (job-only). - Scope keys by (org_id, project_id) and optionally (route_id); default is project scope + specific route allowlist for the standard demo routes. - Disallow admin/control-plane mutations from demo keys by default (no model pin edits, no org role changes, no billing settings). - Add optional `--ttl` for short-lived keys (defaults to 24h for SE-run keys, 2h for externally shared “live demo” keys). 2) Rotation + safe sharing helpers: - Add `rw demo keys create` and `rw demo keys rotate` helpers used by the reset runbook. - Rotation is implemented as: create new key -> update demo app secret refs -> revoke old key (with a 10 minute overlap option). - Adds a `rw demo keys verify-audit` command that checks for expected audit log events over the last N minutes and prints pass/fail with reasons. - Adds guardrails to prevent generating demo keys outside the demo org (requires `DEMO_ORG_ID` match and `--i-know-what-im-doing` escape hatch for on-call). 3) Audit logging: - Emit audit events for `api_key.created`, `api_key.rotated`, `api_key.revoked` with consistent fields: actor_id, actor_type (user/service), org_id, project_id, key_id (opaque), scope_summary, ttl_seconds, reason, ip/user_agent (when applicable). - Ensure rotations emit both `created` (new key) and `revoked` (old key) with `rotation_id` correlation for easier demo incident review. - Add a small backfill shim in the audit pipeline for demo keys created via legacy endpoints (so we don’t regress reporting during rollout). 4) Migration/compatibility: - Existing demo keys continue to work but are marked as `legacy_unscoped=true` and will be refused by `rw demo reset` after 2025-12-15 (soft enforcement: warning now, hard error later). - The demo app (redwood-examples) is unchanged in this PR; it only relies on the hosted inference endpoints. However, the default demo-tenant bootstrap now provisions route-specific keys so the app doesn’t require broad project permissions. Why this approach: - We need demo keys to be shareable (screen share) but low-risk. Route allowlists plus short TTL makes accidental exposure less consequential. - Separating “seed traffic” permissions keeps the synthetic traffic generator from inheriting unnecessary inference permissions. - Audit log correlation makes it easy to answer security-review questions live (“show me key creation, who did it, and when”). Testing: - Unit tests for scope evaluation (project + route allowlist + operation) and TTL enforcement. - Integration test: create scoped key -> call chat completion on allowed route -> expect 200; call embeddings on disallowed route -> expect 403 with `scope_denied`. - Integration test: rotate key -> old key revoked -> verify audit events exist with same rotation_id. - Manual: Markus ran through the SE demo runbook on staging demo tenant; verified the console read-only key can view dashboards but cannot edit routes/models. Rollout plan: - Merge behind feature flag `demo_scoped_keys_default=true` for demo org only. - Enable in demo prod tenant after PR-28531 healthcheck rollout so SEs have a single pass/fail signal. - Communicate to GTM: new default keys are time-bound; reset tooling will automatically refresh them. Security considerations: - No customer data impacted (demo-only). - Avoid logging raw API key material anywhere (only key_id and scope summary). - Audit event payload intentionally excludes key prefixes. Follow-ups: - Add UI affordance in Console to show “scope summary” for a key (read-only) for SE demos (tracked in ENG-4855 subtask). - Update internal demo docs/runbook with the new commands (Elliot to pick up once merged).
Naomi Feldman (Security): Can we confirm we never include the key prefix in audit logs? I’ve seen teams accidentally log first 6 chars for “debugging.”
Ethan Park (Author): Confirmed. Events include only key_id (UUID) + scope_summary. I added a test asserting we don’t serialize `api_key` fields into the audit payload, and I removed one debug log in the legacy endpoint that printed `token_hint`.
Marcus Lin (Security Eng): TTL defaults—24h for SE keys feels long for something that gets screenshared. Could we make “live demo” keys default to 2h and require an explicit flag for longer TTL?
Ethan Park (Author): Done. `rw demo keys create` defaults to 2h unless `--purpose se-run` is specified (24h). The reset command uses `--purpose se-run` so internal dry-runs don’t constantly rotate mid-demo. Added messaging in CLI output: “do not paste into chat / slides; use vault link.”
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Please ensure rotation is non-disruptive. Overlap window + rollback path?
Ethan Park (Author): Rotation helper supports `--overlap=10m` (default). It writes the new key first, validates healthcheck call, then revokes the old key. If validation fails, it leaves the old key active and prints a clear rollback message. I also wired `verify-audit` to fail soft (warning) so we don’t block demos if the audit pipeline is delayed.
Chloe Martin (Console): For `demo.console.read`, are we sure it doesn’t grant access to billing tabs / org settings? We’ve had accidental exposure during exec demos.
Ethan Park (Author): It’s scoped to Console resources under Project only (dashboards, traces, rollouts view) and explicitly denies org/billing endpoints. I added a regression test for `GET /org/settings` returning 403 when using a console-read key.
Markus Klein (Demo owner): Ran through the reset flow. Much better. One request: CLI output should print “where to paste” (env var name) and redact the token in logs by default.
Ethan Park (Author): Updated CLI: prints token once to stdout with a “copy now” banner; subsequent logs only reference key_id. Also added `--json` mode for automation that returns the token in a single line (no extra logging).
Naomi Feldman (Security): Approving contingent on a follow-up to document least-privilege rationale for sales enablement so SEs can answer ‘why do you need this permission?’ quickly.
Ethan Park (Author): Agree. I added a short section to tools/rw-cli/README.md and linked ENG-4855 for the full enablement doc update.

Context & motivation: customers running shadow traffic into new model variants frequently see noisy short-lived regressions that are hard to correlate with session state (sticky sessions, multi-request flows). This PR implements a session-coordinated promotion path: when a model variant shows stable behavior on shadowed sessions for a configurable observation window, we automatically promote a controlled subset of those same sessions into a canary lane rather than random users. The goal is to reduce promotion flakiness, increase signal fidelity for multi-request flows, and provide deterministic rollback hooks when regressions emerge.

Design summary: 1) Session fingerprint capture: the shadow bridge records a compact session fingerprint (hash of session-id, user-metadata-sanitized, request-seed) in the shadow telemetry blob; fingerprints are stored in the short-lived promotion cache (TTL configurable, default 10m). 2) Promotion eligibility: a variant becomes eligible for session-promotion after meeting coverage and success thresholds on shadowed sessions (configurable metrics: per-session success rate, median latency, absence of catastrophic errors). 3) Controlled promotion: eligible session fingerprints are used to seed canary routing so those same sessions are routed to the candidate variant (seeded canary allocation) keeping session affinity intact across multi-request flows. 4) Safety gates & rollback: we wire automatic rollback triggers (latency delta > 30% p50, error rate spike > 1.5x baseline, regression on key quality evals). When a trigger fires we immediately 1) pause new promotions, 2) drain candidate variant from promoted sessions, 3) escalate via the embedded rollback playbook (automated notifications, runbooks with one-click revert in Console). 5) Observability: new telemetry tags (session_promoted=true/false, promotion_reason, promotion_window_id) and per-session traces for promoted flows.

Configuration: new API in rollout policy: "promotion_mode: session_promote", keys: observation_window, session_ttl, min_session_coverage, success_thresholds, rollback_triggers, promotion_rate.

Migration and compatibility: default behavior is off. Operators can opt-in at rollout creation; we also include a CLI migration helper to convert existing canary definitions to session-promote-enabled templates.

Testing & safety: unit tests for controller logic, integration tests simulating multi-request flows, and a canary-sim harness that runs 10k synthetic sessions with injected latency/error faults to validate rollback conditions. We added a small staged e2e run on perf-canary lab.

Implementation notes: primary implementation lives in serving/orchestrator/promotion_controller.go and serving/bridge/shadow_bridge.go; a light-weight cache backed by redis (configurable to in-memory for dev) stores session fingerprints; telemetry is emitted via observability/telemetry_v2.

Backwards compatible: other rollout modes unchanged. Related: builds on ENG-7812 (shadow telemetry pipeline) and ENG-7824 (canary routing seeds).

Motivation story: this surfaced during a customer incident where a model change was promoted globally after shadow metrics looked stable, but multi-request checkout flows failed only for sessions that had been shadowed; session promotion reduces that risk by promoting the same sessions that were exercising the flow.

Rollout plan: 1) land as a feature-flag off, 2) enable in internal staging and run 72h synthetic session run, 3) enable for a small set of customers via Dedicated testing, 4) open opt-in in Console and document playbook.

Risks & mitigations: fingerprint collisions addressed with 128-bit HKDF-based fingerprints plus per-window salt; privacy: no PII is stored and we provide a built-in sanitizer for common identifiers; operational complexity: promotion cache TTL defaults conservative.

Ask from reviewers: please validate the rollback thresholds, the runbook phrasing, and the upgrade path for Private deployments.
Adds a session-aware promotion path from shadow to canary with automated rollback triggers and an operational playbook. No user-facing API changes.
5 commits: 1) add promotion controller and session fingerprinting, 2) integrate promotion cache with shadow bridge, 3) telemetry and trace tags for promoted sessions, 4) rollout policy schema + CLI migration helper, 5) tests and runbook docs. Each commit scoped and unit-tested.
Jordan Li: Left a few nits on the promotion cache size and TTL — suggest default TTL 10m rather than 5m. Ava: updated in commit 3 to 10m and added config knob.
Priya Desai: Can you enumerate the exact metrics and query expressions used for success_thresholds? Need them for alert alignment. Ava: added exact counters (request.success_count, request.latency_p50_ms) and example PromQL in docs; please re-review.
Ethan Brooks: Do we have a clear privacy review? Fingerprinting could be sensitive. Ava: yes — the sanitizer is pluggable and defaults to hashing only non-PII fields; also filed a privacy check ENG-7901 for an audit; included mention in docs.
Jordan Li: Approved after TTL and PromQL changes. Priya Desai: Approved with one follow-up to add a Console toggle in a subsequent PR. Ethan Brooks: Approved — left a suggestion to add telemetry cardinality caps (won't block).
After deploy: monitor promotion_rate, promoted_session_error_ratio, promoted_session_latency_delta. Default rollback thresholds are conservative; if you plan to enable at scale, prewarm the promotion cache or set session_ttl to match client session behavior.
payload.title: Session-coordinated shadow promotion with rollback playbook

Context: Several customers and internal e2e tests surfaced subtle races between token refresh timing and long-lived streaming consumers (pull/push streams). This PR harmonizes the ergonomic surface for a token lease / keepalive abstraction and updates the pullstream async-iterator shape consistently across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Motivation: reduce surprising reconnects, simplify application-level token lifecycle, and make cross-language examples portable. Changes: 1) Introduce a minimal TokenLease interface with keepalive() and expire_at() helpers and a light-weight TokenProxy shim for older credential providers. 2) Add a PullStreamAdapter/AsyncPullIterator facade in each SDK that exposes a consistent next_chunk()/close() pattern and emits explicit "lease_refreshed" events for observability. 3) Centralize retry/backoff integration so stream consumer retries defer to configured retry profiles (short-circuit for idempotent snapshots). 4) Slight API surface bumps (minor semver) and packaging/version updates: python->1.14.0, typescript->1.9.2, go->v0.8.5. Compatibility: a backwards-compatible TokenProxy shim is provided so existing credential providers continue to work; docs and migration notes included. Checklist: - [x] design doc and cross-SDK API sketches (linked in PR) - [x] Python implementation and unit/integration tests - [x] TypeScript implementation and browser/node tests - [x] Go implementation and concurrent stream smoke tests - [x] end-to-end test against hosted staging with long-lived stream scenarios - [x] docs + changelogs updated - [x] version bumps and CI green Related: ENG-4021 (stream-resilience), ENG-3908 (cred-session-leases).
Polish: unify token-lease keepalive and pullstream async iterator surface across SDKs; bump Python/TS/Go SDK packages. Backwards-compatible shim included for older consumers.
Aisha: Can we avoid a second goroutine in Go by using a context-aware ticker? The current implementation spawns a refresher goroutine per stream which might be heavy under extreme fanout. -- Riley: I've changed the goroutine to use a shared lease manager for sessions with >1 active streams; see packages/sdk-go/stream/lease_manager.go (added) in the follow-up commit.
Miguel: In TS, how does next_chunk() differ from the existing iterator.next() semantics? Will it break for existing for-await-of usage? -- Riley: next_chunk() preserves async iterator semantics; a for-await-of wrapper is provided. Migration section in docs shows both patterns.
Lena: race on close() observed in go unit test when token expires during send; request that we add an explicit close handshake. -- Riley: Added an edge-case test and a close handshake (pullstream_adapter.go) that drains the send path before canceling the lease refresher.
Aisha: please add a telemetry dimension for 'lease_refresh_outcome' (success/failure/latency bucket). -- Riley: telemetry metric added to python/ts/go adapters and wired to console tracing; see observability note in docs.
payload.title: session-meld: keepalive token-lease and pullstream interface harmonization across Python/TS/Go

Context: Customers asked for better explainability when operator or service actions trigger cross-region KMS usage and complex RBACv2 decisions. This PR implements a decision-telemetry pipeline that attaches policy decision fingerprints, attribute vectors, and KMS call metadata to audit events so downstream compliance tooling can correlate 'why' with 'how' a key was used. Motivation: reduce time-to-root-cause for residency/audit questions, allow post-hoc policy analytics, and provide non-invasive correlation for KMS usage without leaking sensitive plaintext. Scope: 1) policy-decision-telemetry service (new internal component) that subscribes to PD-DECIDE events and emits canonicalized telemetry blobs; 2) KMS-usage-correlator that enriches audit events with kms_call_id, key_region_hint, wrap_mode, and decision_fingerprint; 3) retention-classifier rules to mark high-sensitivity audit envelopes for longer retention; 4) SDK changes to forward decision-context headers. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (ENG-1298) reviewed and linked - [x] Unit tests for the correlator and serializer - [x] Integration test in staging with mock KMS - [x] Minimal schema migration for audit index - [x] Backward-compatible header handling in public API Commits: "Initial decision-telemetry scaffold"; "Add correlator: attach kms_call metadata to audit payload"; "Retention-classifier and configurable thresholds"; "Tests and schema migration"; "Docs: console telemetry toggle and explainer" Changed areas (high-level): - internal/telemetry/decision_service.go: new subscription and serializer - internal/audit/correlator.go: enrichAuditEventWithKMS(...) implementation (adds kms_call_id and decision_fingerprint) - api/headers.go: expose X-Decision-Fingerprint and X-KMS-Call-ID passing - migrations/20260220_audit_schema.sql: add telemetry fields to audit_index - docs/telemetry.md: new user-facing explanation and console toggle - tests/mocks/mock_kms_server.go: integration harness snippet - sdk/python/redwood/audit_forwarder.py: opt-in header forwarding Example snippet added (illustrative only): enrichAuditEventWithKMS(ae, meta) -> ae.audit_metadata["decision_fp"] = meta.fp Review conversation: Miguel Rivera: "Can the correlator add a short HMAC of the decision_fingerprint to avoid accidental leakage?" Author (Sasha): "Added hmac_claim in the second commit; keyed by telemetry service secret and only stored in telemetry blobs not plain audit message." Anita Singh: "We need to ensure this doesn't increase median ingest latency above 4ms." Author: "Benchmarks in CI show 0.5-1.2ms p50 and a 2.9ms 99th at staging traffic with batching enabled." Ethan Cho: "Approve after small naming nits and a migration rollback test." Author: "Addressed naming and added migration rollback step to migration script." CI summary: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration-tests (staging harness): pass, lint: pass. Performance: microbench shows correlator adds ~1.1ms p50 and 2.5ms p99 when running with default batching; can be toggled by per-tenant flag. Security review notes: secrets for HMAC are stored in vault and rotated automatically; correlator only stores KMS metadata pointers (no ciphertext). Compliance notes: The retention-classifier supports per-tenant overrides and region-pin awareness to comply with data residency policies. Rollout plan: 1) Canary enable telemetry for internal tenants in staging for 72h. 2) Enable for a small set of opt-in customers (sales/SE coordinated) with monitoring dashboards. 3) Gradual tenant rollout with rollback toggle exposed in Console. Migration strategy: non-blocking schema migration that populates new telemetry fields only for events after the migration timestamp; rollback implemented by dropping new columns and a small audit of synthetic telemetry events. Backwards compatibility: if the SDK does not send X-Decision-Fingerprint header the system treats decision context as unknown and still records KMS metadata. Edge cases: for customers using external KMS proxies we attach only stable call identifiers to prevent region leaks. Follow-ups: - ENG-1345: add a privacy-preserving aggregation layer for telemetry - ENG-1402: surface RBAC explanation links in Console audit viewer Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2026-02-24 after green CI and approvals from Anita Singh and Miguel Rivera. 
Adds RBACv2 decision telemetry pipeline and a correlator that ties KMS envelope/wrap calls to policy decisions. Exposes opt-in per-tenant telemetry for compliance audits and introduces a light-weight retention classifier for sensitive audit events.
payload.title: Introduce RBACv2 decision telemetry and KMS usage correlator

Motivation: In production we observed intermittent client-visible 429/RateLimit errors during streaming sessions where backpressure and cross-region retries led to duplicated retry timers and ambiguous Retry-After semantics. Additionally, idempotency resolution in the OpenAI compatibility shim treated X-Redwood-Idempotency keys as purely local and could re-run tool calls across fallback routes, causing duplicate external side-effects. This PR unifies three related concerns into a single, minimal-surface change: (1) normalize rate-limit/time-window headers from upstreams and expose a single canonical Retry-After value to the OpenAI shim, (2) add a bounded retry-window policy for streaming connections to avoid overlapping timers, and (3) tighten idempotency resolution to include route-fingerprint and last-success timestamp to prevent cross-route replays.

Summary of changes: single continuous commit series implementing normalization and safety checks, tests, and docs. Key points: consolidate RateLimit-* and Retry-After header parsing into a shared parser; expose a best-effort canonical_retry_after_ms in the OpenAI compatibility response pipeline; enforce a streaming_retry_window_ms config (default 2000ms) that deduplicates concurrent retry attempts per-client/request hash; store idempotency records with route_fingerprint and last_success_ts and refuse replays across non-matching route_fingerprint.

Checklist:
- [x] unit tests for header parsing and window dedupe
- [x] integration test: streaming session restart does not cause duplicate tool calls
- [x] e2e regression test against openai-compat shim
- [x] docs: compatibility notes and migration guidance

Commits (high level):
- normalize: shared header parser for Retry-After and RateLimit windows (parser/rate_headers.go, parser/rate_headers_test.go)
- streaming: add streaming_retry_window to runtime config and dedupe logic (runtime/stream_manager.go)
- idempotency: augment idempotency store entries with route_fingerprint & last_success_ts and enforcement (services/idempotency_store.go)
- openai-shim: surface canonical_retry_after_ms in /v1/responses header mapping and error body (adapters/openai_compat/response_mapper.go)
- tests/docs: add unit/integration tests and note in docs/compatibility/openai-rate-limits.md

Files changed (high level):
- parser/rate_headers.go (new)
- parser/rate_headers_test.go (new)
- runtime/stream_manager.go (modified)
- services/idempotency_store.go (modified)
- adapters/openai_compat/response_mapper.go (modified)
- adapters/openai_compat/streaming_adapter_test.go (new)
- docs/compatibility/openai-rate-limits.md (modified)
- config/defaults.yaml (modified)

Small illustrative snippet (response_mapper.go):
- old: "retry_after = ctx.headers.get('Retry-After') || 0"
- new: "retry_after = parser.ParseCanonicalRetryAfter(ctx.headers) // returns ms or 0 if unknown"

Testing and validation:
- added unit tests covering RFC-compliant "Retry-After" (delta-seconds, HTTP-date), nonstandard RateLimit-Window headers (RateLimit-Window, X-RateLimit-Window), and corrupt values (fallback to best-effort estimate).
- streaming integration test simulates transient region failover + backpressure to ensure only a single retry timer per request hash fires within streaming_retry_window_ms.
- idempotency tests ensure requests with same idempotency key but different route_fingerprint are not replayed; same key+fingerprint within last_success_ts returns 409/Conflict per OpenAI semantics.

Operational notes / rollout:
- defaults.yaml introduces streaming_retry_window_ms: 2000 and idempotency_grace_window_ms: 300000 (5min) which is conservative; operators can tune via config.
- backward-compatible: if upstream does not send RateLimit-* headers we fall back to Retry-After or to a safe circuit-breaker.
- telemetry: new metrics: openai_compat.canonical_retry_after_ms.histogram, stream.retry_dedup.count, idempotency.replay_block.count

Migration: existing idempotency store entries are compatible; the store will lazily backfill route_fingerprint for new entries only. No forced DB migration performed in this PR to keep upgrade simple.

Related: SUP-912 (customer reported duplicate tool runs), ENG-3019 (streaming resiliency epic).
Ethan Zhao: Overall this sharpens several previously ambiguous behaviors. Please add a short comment explaining why we chose 2s default for streaming_retry_window_ms and include a metric for dedupe ops.
Maya Patel (author): Added comment and new metric stream.retry_dedup.count in latest push. Also added a test that asserts only one retry timer fires in 2s window.
Leah Kim: We should be careful about clock skew when checking last_success_ts across regions. Can we use monotonic sequence numbers or include server_id in idempotency record?
Maya Patel: Good point — opted for last_success_ts + server_id fingerprint to allow cross-region rejections but still avoid identical-but-shifted clocks causing acceptance. Documented in idempotency_store.go header.
Carlos Mendoza: CI failure on golangci-lint in services/idempotency_store.go (unused import). Fixed in 3rd commit. Approving pending green CI.
Ethan Zhao: Approved. Verified integration test against chaos simulation in perf-canary lab.
Stabilize OpenAI compatibility: canonical Retry-After parsing, streaming retry deduplication, and stricter idempotency resolution to prevent duplicate external tool calls. Defaults are conservative and tunable via config.
If customers report 429s during streaming after this change, verify their upstreams' RateLimit-* headers and recommend adjusting streaming_retry_window_ms or idempotency_grace_window_ms. Use new metrics (openai_compat.canonical_retry_after_ms, stream.retry_dedup.count, idempotency.replay_block.count) for triage.

Context and motivation: Customers reported subtle mismatches between SDKs when recovering long-lived streaming sessions after auth refreshes and when applying retry windows. That caused duplicated reconnect logic in application code and intermittent token-exchange races during prefilling/heartbeat flows. This PR implements a lightweight cross-SDK credential conduit and a small set of ergonomic pullstream helpers to make authentication transitions (rotate, prefetch, drain) observable and consistent between Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Summary of work: - Introduced a credential_conduit / CredentialConduit abstraction (language idiomatic wrappers) that centralizes token lookup, priming, and optional lease semantics. - Added PauseablePullstream / PauseableAsyncIterator / PullStream.Pause helpers so consumers can checkpoint/prime/cooldown without ad-hoc buffering. - Standardized retry profile defaults used by streaming reconnects (latency-aware backoff with small hedging window). - Harmonized telemetry labels emitted from auth/stream transitions so backend traces can aggregate cross-language. - Minor public surface tweaks for ergonomics: clearer javadocs/docstrings on session pinning, added transient_error sentinel for typed errors. - Version bumps: python-sdk -> 1.12.0, typescript-sdk -> 2.7.0, go-sdk -> 1.9.0. Compatibility notes: This change is additive. Existing auth flows continue to work. Consumers who used internal/undocumented token hooks should migrate to the conduit API for improved correctness; migration notes included in CHANGELOGs. Test plan and verification: Unit tests added for credential conduit priming and pause/resume semantics in all three SDKs. Integration tests exercised streaming reconnects against the local mock server with token rotation scenarios. We also ran a limited canary of the TS SDK in staging (5% traffic) for 48 hours and observed zero increase in reconnects; latency tail improved slightly for long-duration sessions. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-9123) - [x] unit tests for py/ts/go - [x] integration tests with mock server - [x] docs/CHANGELOG updates - [x] release notes drafted - [x] package publish scripts validated Rollout: Merged to main. SDK packages will be published as part of the coordinated release job: py v1.12.0, ts v2.7.0, go v1.9.0. Followups: - expose an opt-in telemetry flag to increase conduit diagnostics (ENG-9270) - document patterns for graceful session handoff in Redwood Console examples.

Motivation: production rollouts we see frequently fail when session-affine traffic and short-lived transactions are promoted without an ordered handoff. This PR implements a transactional promotion choreography that guarantees session-consistent promotions by combining a short-term session drain window with a traffic adhesion policy. The intent is to make model promotions atomic from the caller's perspective while enabling safe, observable, and reversible phased rollouts. Design summary: 1) Promotion transaction: a three-phase protocol (prepare -> reconcile -> commit) that records cohort state and ensures either full promotion for in-flight sessions or safe fallback. 2) Session adhesion: an adhesion policy pins existing sessions to the origin model for the duration of the drain window; new sessions can be routed to target cohort according to the normal sampling policy. 3) Drain policy: a configurable soft- and hard-drain timer plus an escape hatch that rebinds sessions to origin during failures. 4) Telemetry and safety gates: built-in SLO/metric gates (latency, error-rate, token-variance) and automatic rollback triggers. Backwards compatibility: the protocol is opt-in per rollout and defaults to legacy behavior for existing rollout specs. Migration: small schema bump to rollout CRD with optional fields (promotion_mode, adhesion_window_seconds, transactional_id). Tests: unit tests for protocol state machine, simulated multi-cohort e2e test that exercises session handoff, and load test scripts that verify no request duplication under session-affine traffic. Checklist: - [x] Implement state machine and storage hooks - [x] Add session-adhesion router integration - [x] Add telemetry and gates wiring - [x] Add e2e simulations and unit tests - [x] Add runbook and console UI for configuring adhesion/drain - [x] Perf smoke to validate latency impact - [x] Docs and changelog Notes: This description includes the core design and operational assumptions. For a short playbook see docs/runbooks/promotion_choreography.md. Linked issues: ENG-2031, ENG-2119. CI is green after flake rerun. Merge strategy: squash-merge with commit message summarizing the choreography and runbook.
Liam Ortiz: Overall design looks solid. Please add an explicit invariant test that proves no session sees mixed-model responses during the prepare->commit window.
Maya Chen: Added an invariant-based unit that locks session routing during the prepare phase; see e2e test for deterministic handoff.
Priya Menon: Concern about latency impact when adhesion_window_seconds > 30s. Suggest telemetry sampling at the edge to avoid extra RPCs.
Maya Chen: Added a sampling optimization to avoid pinging the promotion coordinator for cold requests; documented the trade-off in the runbook.
Omar Khalid: Approve after minor comments on CRD docs formatting and console accessibility labels.
Maya Chen: Fixed CRD formatting and added aria-labels on the adhesion slider component.
Introduce transactional promotion choreography (opt-in) with session-adhesion and drain policies. Provides safer model promotions for session-affine workloads; includes telemetry gates and automatic rollback triggers. See docs/runbooks/promotion_choreography.md for operational guidance.
When enabling transactional promotion: 1) start with adhesion_window_seconds=10, monitor latency and request error-rate gates for 30 minutes; 2) if gate breaches, abort prepare and fall back to origin; 3) use the console to trigger manual commit once smoke passes; 4) to rollback, issue abort transaction which rebinds sessions and drains new traffic back to origin. Emergency escape hatch: set adhesion_window_seconds=0 to immediately stop binding new sessions.
If you see session-mismatch alerts, run /bin/promo-checker --transaction=<id> to inspect cohort state and use 'promo abort' to revert. Telemetry tags: rollout.transactional=true. Contact @maya for escalation.
payload.title: Transactional promotion choreography with session adhesion and drain policy

payload.body:
Context: We saw a pattern of short-duration tenant bursts that caused clustered SLO violations because cold KV state and cold model caches delayed first responses and triggered downstream circuit breakers. Previous mitigations (longer prewarm windows and coarse throttles) either increased cost or introduced higher latency during steady state.

This PR introduces an 'Ephemeral Admission Gate' and a complementary 'Hedged Warmup' manager. The admission gate is a lightweight per-tenant connection/admission controller that applies a short, sliding priority window: new connections for low-priority tenants are admitted at a reduced rate while higher-priority tenants (or requests with active grace credits) can bypass. The Hedged Warmup manager creates a short-lived, speculative warmup path: when the gate delays a request, we kick off a low-cost hedged warmup that attempts to prime KV and token caches in parallel; if priming completes within the admission window, the request proceeds with warmed state. If priming fails or times out, the request falls back to a fast-degraded reply path (bounded short responses / partial content) rather than blocking and risking downstream cascades.

Goals: reduce spike-driven SLO violations, avoid long tail cold-start latency, keep incremental cost small during spikes, and provide operational knobs for tenants/regions.

What changed (single-string body): Implemented ephemeral admission gate (controlplane/admission/gate.go) with per-tenant sliding windows and crediting. Added HedgedWarmupManager (runtime/scheduler/warmup_manager.go) which schedules micro-warmups and coordinates with KV priming shim (runtime/kv/priming_shim.go). Exposed metrics for admission rates, warmup success latency histogram, and fallback-rate. Updated k8s manifest to deploy the admission controller as a sidecar optional for Dedicated and Private. Added integration smoke test to simulate burst patterns and verify SLOs under load (tests/integration/admission_smoke_test.py). Added metrics definitions and dashboards pointers in telemetry/metrics_definitions.yaml.

Checklist (what I validated): - Unit tests for admission gate logic (edge windows, credit decay) - Integration test that replays burst traces and asserts 99th p95 SLO improvement - Load lab run (synthetic tenant bursts) with telemetry snapshots attached - Lint, build, and e2e smoke passed in CI - Configuration defaults chosen to be conservative for existing deployments (feature gated off in release by default)

Operational details: - Default behavior: gate is feature-flagged off. When enabled, default sliding window = 3s, priority bucket sizes = [high, medium, low], initial grace credits = 10 per tenant/hour. - Hedged warmup TTLs: 150ms attempt window, KV priming uses lightweight HEAD request to internal cache service. - Fast-fallback behavior: when warmup fails, return a bounded partial reply with header 'X-Redwood-Degraded: true' and telemetry tag. Context: Auto-rollback on SLO breach needs the rollout controller to fetch burn-rate status for the exact rollout scope (route/model_version/region/customer_tier) and make decisions with guardrails (sample size + staleness handling). This PR adds a monitor adapter in `redwood` that queries the internal slo-toolkit and normalizes results for the rollout controller.

What’s in this PR:
- New `SloMonitorAdapter` interface + `SloToolkitAdapter` implementation.
- Fetches burn-rate status for latency (p95/p99) and error-rate SLOs, returning both fast/slow windows (e.g., 5m/30m) and per-window sample sizes.
- Staleness detection:
  - Treats a monitor result as STALE when `now - data_timestamp > staleness_threshold` (default 2m; configurable).
  - Treats missing timestamps or NaN burn-rate as UNKNOWN (distinct from OK/BREACH).
- Resilience:
  - Timeouts + bounded retries when calling slo-toolkit.
  - Small in-process cache (TTL 10s) keyed by (scope + slo_type + objective) to avoid hammering slo-toolkit during rollouts.
  - Explicit UNAVAILABLE state when toolkit is down; includes error string for auditability.
- Adds adapter-level metrics (low-cardinality) for call volume/errors/staleness/latency.
- Tests: unit tests for staleness + parsing + caching behavior; integration test with a fake slo-toolkit server.

Notes / follow-ups:
- The rollout controller will still apply its own minimum-sample gating + debounce (ENG-4861 / PR-28463). This adapter returns sample sizes and timestamps so the controller can decide fail-open vs fail-closed per policy.
- slo-toolkit endpoint used here expects rollout-scoped labels; the corresponding toolkit work is in slo-toolkit PR-221.

Screenshots: N/A (backend-only).

Risk: Moderate. Adapter is behind `rollouts.slo_adapter.enabled` and is not invoked unless the rollout policy enables SLO-based actions.

Rollout plan:
- Merge behind flag.
- Enable in staging for internal canary route `chat/completions` (internal tenant only).
- Observe adapter error rate + staleness metrics for 48h before expanding.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration test with fake toolkit
- [x] Metrics added (cardinality reviewed)
- [x] Flag default OFF
- [x] Docs/commented example response payload
TypeScript (normalized response):

export type SloEvalState = 'OK' | 'BREACH' | 'UNKNOWN' | 'STALE' | 'UNAVAILABLE';

export interface WindowBurnRate {
  window: '5m' | '30m';
  burnRate?: number; // undefined when UNKNOWN/UNAVAILABLE
  sampleSize?: number; // requests in window (or undefined when unknown)
}

export interface SloMonitorSnapshot {
  scopeKey: string; // stable hashed key (no high-cardinality raw labels)
  sloType: 'latency_p95' | 'latency_p99' | 'error_rate';
  objective: string; // e.g. "p95<=1200ms" or "error_rate<=0.5%"
  state: SloEvalState;
  fast: WindowBurnRate;
  slow: WindowBurnRate;
  dataTimestamp?: string; // RFC3339 from provider
  fetchedAt: string; // RFC3339 now
  provider: 'slo-toolkit';
  providerMonitorId?: string;
  error?: string;
}
