Problem: production customers running mixed workloads were seeing unpredictable token-unit economics because prefill choices (when to prefill KV/cache and how much) were independent of tenant budget profiles and quantization compatibility heuristics. This PR introduces a budget-aware orchestration layer that ties prefill aggressiveness to tenant budget tiers and a lightweight quantization hint adapter that signals conservative/experimental quant profiles to serving nodes.

What this changes: 1) new orchestration service component (prefill/orchestrator) that consumes tenant budget metadata and runtime latency SLOs and produces prefill decisions (none/minimal/aggressive) as a short-lived decision token; 2) quantization hint adapter that annotates requests with a per-tenant model-compat hint (e.g., q4_0_safe, q4_1_gain) so runtime can choose an appropriate kernel path and fall back automatically; 3) telemetry hooks (metrics and events) covering decisions, estimator confidence, budget consumption, and fallback counts; 4) an operator-configurable policy file and a canary rollout that targets 5% then 25% then 100% of tenants; 5) unit + integration tests and a synthetic workload harness used in CI.

Motivation: automating sensible defaults for prefill and quantization reduces manual tuning, protects tenants on tight budgets from aggressive prefill/cost regressions, and enables the runtime to pick quant paths with graceful degradation. This complements the existing econ prescriptor work by providing a runtime-facing decision token that is cheap to evaluate and transparent in telemetry.

Design notes: - Decisions are intentionally stateless and short-lived; they can be recomputed from tenant metadata and recent SLO telemetry. - The quant hint adapter does not change model artifact files or perform quantization in-line; it only annotates requests so the serving runtime can select prebuilt variants. - Safety gate: when the runtime detects >5% mismatch error rate for a quant hint, it will automatically downgrade to the safe profile for that tenant for 1 hour and emit an alert.

Testing and rollout: - Unit tests for policy parsing, decision logic, and hint format. - Integration test harness simulating mixed chat/embedding load with synthetic sequences to validate budget churn and fallback behavior. - Canary rollout script and config added to tooling so SRE can advance percentage in a controlled rollout.

Backward compatibility and migration: - No customer-facing API changes. - New small DB table (prefill_profiles) added via migration script; existing tenants get a default conservative profile. Migration script is included and idempotent.

Commits summary: - "init: budget-aware prefill orchestrator skeleton" - "impl: decision token format and policy parser" - "feat: quantization hint adapter and request annotation" - "telemetry: add metrics for decision count, fallback count, budget spend" - "tests: add unit & integration harness" - "docs: operator playbook and rollout guidance" - "ci: add synthetic workload job and canary gating"

Changed files (high level): server/prefill/orchestrator.go, server/prefill/decision_token.proto, server/quant/hint_adapter.py, api/tenant_profiles/migrations/20241112_add_prefill_profiles.sql, telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml, tooling/canary/rollout_playbook.md, tests/prefill/integration/harness.go, docs/operators/prefill-and-quant-playbook.md, examples/tenant_profiles/sample_policy.yaml, ci/workflows/prefill-canary.yml, scripts/migrate_prefill_profiles.sh, webapp/admin/prefill_overview.ui.tsx

Notes for reviewers: - Focus review on the policy parser (edge cases where overlapping rules apply) and on the quant hint wireformat compatibility with existing runtime headers. - Pay special attention to the migration script for idempotency on retry.

References: Linear ENG-2561, design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2561/budget-aware-prefill, and internal RFC (rfc/prefill-budget-2024-10.md).
Adds a tenant-budget-aware prefill orchestrator with a quantization hint adapter; includes new telemetry and a canary rollout. No API breaking changes; safe fallback to existing profiles enabled.

Motivation: High variance bursts in prefill traffic cause transient KV cache thrashing and CPU/GPU scheduling jitter that degrades P95 latency for small-chunk decodes. This change introduces a two-part runtime optimization: 1) light-weight KV-prefetch hints emitted during prefill to warm hot key ranges for imminent decode windows; 2) a burst-smoothing scheduler that converts high-frequency small prefill arrivals into controlled micro-batches for the decode stage while preserving low tail latency. Design summary: implement a KV-prefetch interface (runtime->kvcache) that accepts token-range hints and priority, add a non-blocking prefetch worker pool, and introduce a burst-smoother policy in the prefill->decode handoff that applies adaptive holding intervals and latency budget accounting to decide when to forward a micro-batch. The scheduler uses a short token-budget lookahead (by default 16 tokens) to avoid splitting decode work across fragile inter-kernel boundaries. Backpressure: when kvcache memory pressure is detected we gracefully reduce prefetch aggressiveness and fall back to standard handoff. Compatibility: this is opt-in via config flags (runtime.prefetch.enabled, runtime.burst_smoother.enabled) and defaults to off for Dedicated customers until fully validated. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked: https://linear.app/redwood/brief/ENG-2145-prefetch-burst-smoothing - [x] Unit tests for scheduler decision logic - [x] Integration test with kvcache warm/cold scenarios - [x] Perf harness runs for p50/p95 token throughput - [x] Feature gated and rollout flags for canary. Observed impact (internal perf lab): end-to-end P95 reduction of 18-24% on chat-heavy traces with many short completions, 6% median improvement, and a 12% drop in KV cache miss rate for targeted keys. No measurable regression on long-sequence throughput. Migration notes: operators can toggle runtime.prefetch.enabled=true to test; defaults off in existing clusters. Related work: builds on prior chunked-prefill and stage overlap efforts but focuses on proactive kvcache warming and burst control rather than larger chunk boundaries.

Ava Chen: Added runtime.metrics.prefetch_entries gauge; measured <2 MiB/s sustained for our benchmark trace when enabled. See tests/prefetch_tests.py for validation.
Priya Rao: Scheduler looks good; we should ensure the default lookahead (16 tokens) is configurable per-model. Also add a unit test for when kvcache signals pressure.
Ava Chen: Made lookahead configurable via runtime.scheduler.lookahead_tokens and added kvcache-pressure test. Performance regressions minimal on long seqs.
Eliot Summers: Approved pending a small doc tweak to rollout notes.
Eliot Summers: Docs updated; approving.
CI Bot: All checks passed (unit, integration, lint).
Added opt-in prefetch and burst-smoothing handoff to reduce tail latency for short-chat workloads. Defaults off; enabled via runtime.prefetch.enabled=true. Improves P95 latency and reduces KV cache miss rate in targeted workloads.

Motivation: Customers in multiple jurisdictions require consistent enforcement of KMS key usage policies and predictable audit retention windows tied to region pinning. This PR introduces two coordinated components: (1) a KMS Usage Policy Harmonizer that normalizes and evaluates operator/service-level KMS usage against jurisdictional allowlists and fallback rules, and (2) an Audit Epochizer that embeds an immutable retention-epoch annotation into audit events so downstream retention processors can make deterministic retention and export decisions. The goal is to reduce policy drift between RBAC v2 decisions and KMS routing, surface mismatches as explicit telemetry, and provide a safe migration path for existing region-pin config. Impact/Risks: low-risk rollout while gated; possible latency increase on first request per-operator due to cache fill (mitigated by warmup job). See linked Linear tickets for rollout checklist.

Motivation: Teams repeatedly ask for smaller cognitive-surface SDKs that still offer production-quality connection pooling, resilient retries, and minimal per-language boilerplate. This PR introduces a Compact Connection Orchestrator (CCO) and an Adaptive Retry Builder (ARB) surfaced as light ergonomic shims in the Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. The goal is to provide a single, documented pattern for: (1) shared connection pooling across streaming and unary flows, (2) adaptive per-request retry policies that can be tuned per-model/route, and (3) a lazy auth adapter that prefetches credentials just-in-time to reduce cold-start auth latency while avoiding credential overfetch in high-concurrency apps.

What changed:
- Core: new compact/conn/orchestrator module that centralizes socket/http2/ws pool management and exposes a minimal lifecycle API: start(), borrow(), return(), drain(). Pools are short-lived by default but can be pinned by higher-level SDKs for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Retry: adaptive/retry/builder implements sample-windowed backoff adjustments. ARB monitors transient error rates and average token latency to automatically scale between three preset profiles (fast, balanced, conservative). Developers can still provide static RetryPolicy objects.
- Auth: auth/lazy_adapter defers credential fetch until the first borrow() for a connection and attaches a lightweight lease that heartbeat-refreshes only when streaming or long-lived connections are observed.
- Streaming ergonomic facades: the SDK stream client now exposes a Pause/Resume hook and a heartbeat callback for reconnect hints; streaming consumers can opt into bufferless line-mode or chunked-accumulate mode.
- Cross-language: small per-language shims implemented for ergonomics and naming conventions; no API breaking changes to existing top-level client constructors. Each SDK bumped: Python -> 1.12.0, TypeScript -> 2.5.0, Go -> 1.4.3.

Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves previous semantics: existing clients that do not opt into the orchestrator continue using the prior per-request connection behavior. To opt in, set client.opts.connectionOrchestrator = {enabled: true, pinPool: false} or call RedwoodConnection.orchestrate() when bootstrapping.

Performance and telemetry: added telemetry hooks for pool utilization, borrow latency, retry-profile-switch events, and auth-lease heartbeats. These are emitted to existing SDK telemetry endpoints and surfaced in Console under the new "SDK connection" dashboard.

Testing and CI: unit tests cover pool lifecycle, borrow/return racing, adaptive window transitions, and lazy auth expiry. Integration tests validate streaming resume semantics with simulated auth rotation and HA proxy failover.

Migration: documented migration guide with step-by-step opt-in examples and a short checklist for Dedicated/Private customers (KMS/HSM considerations).

Rollout: feature flags enabled on staging for 48h smoke; rolled to main and tagged for GA.

Context and motivation: We observed repeated burst-induced SLA pressure for medium-sized tenants in Dedicated pools where short spikes consumed available headroom and caused tail latency regressions. Existing autoscaler signals (95th util + simple buffer) react too slowly to sub-minute surges and do not account for variance observed in tenant request traces. This PR introduces two cooperating pieces: a lightweight Reservation Advisor that synthesizes a utilization-anchored reservation recommendation, and a Surge Signature Prober that produces high-frequency ‘surge fingerprints’ to let the advisor reason about short-tail burst risk.

Summary of changes: 1) controller/autoscaler: add ReservoirReservationAdvisor (configurable windowing + confidence bands) and an admission curve that blends steady-state reservation with short-lived surge buffers; 2) telemetry/exporter: add surge_signature histogram and a new nightly-sample exporter to surface per-tenant burst skew; 3) runtime/router: small admission hook to allow short soft-burst grants when advisor certifies low collision risk; 4) tests/docs: unit + integration tests for statistical sampling and a how-to in docs/dedicated/reservations.md.

Why this is different: Unlike our previous headroom heuristics, the advisor models both central tendency and burst skew using a reservoir sampler + exponential decay to weigh recent high-frequency signals. The Surge Signature Prober classifies patterns (spike, ramp, plateaus) and reports a compact signature that is cheap to compute (<200us per sample) and stable across languages. This enables faster preemptive soft grants and reduces reactive overprovisioning.

- [x] Implement Surge Signature Prober and telemetry hooks

Motivation: We've seen a recurring class of regressions where short-lived allocation spikes cause the autoscaler to oscillate or prematurely drain dedicated pools, which negatively affects throughput guarantees for tenants. This PR introduces the "stability conservator" autoscaler module and a companion throughput covenant reporter to (1) anchor scaling decisions on a conservative headroom estimate derived from historical occupancy windows, (2) surface signed throughput covenants per-tenant for downstream routing/fallback, and (3) provide high-fidelity utilization decomposition telemetry for postmortem and SLO reporting.

Design highlights: The autoscaler computes a "conservator headroom" using a decayed histogram over the last N minutes of occupancy, combined with an outlier-trimmed peak sketch. Decisions apply a two-stage gating: a quick soft-scale for transient mismatches and a guarded hard-scale requiring confirmation windows. The throughput covenant reporter emits per-tenant percentiles (P50/P95/P99) of served RPS and token throughput mapped to reservation tiers; these are written to telemetry and annotated on the tenant object for routing to prefer lower-latency model variants if guarantees are at risk.

What changed (summary): Added new controller pkg/autoscaler/conservator.go and associated unit tests; introduced telemetry/throughput_covenant.go to compute and emit covenant documents; instrumented pool allocator to read conservator advised headroom; small helm chart changes to expose new flags charts/dedicated/values.yaml; docs/designs/stability-conservator.md detailing the algorithm and rollout notes; e2e/nightly tests exercising burst scenarios and synthetic regressions.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-1987) - [x] Unit tests for headroom estimator and gating - [x] Integration tests for allocator fallback behavior - [x] Telemetry backed by histogram + hdr sketch - [x] Canary rollout plan included in docs - [x] Feature flags guarded: autoscaler.enabled, conservator.mode, covenant.reporting=true

Rollout plan: Deploy conservator in passive mode for 48h to stream suggested headroom without influencing scaler; enable active mode in a single pool (canary) for 24h; if SLO regressions observed, rollback via feature flag. The covenant reporter is enabled in read-only reporting initially to allow SRE to tune routing tolerances.

Related: Linear ENG-1987 (design), ENG-2033 (telemetry dashboard), Incident INT-342 (regression that motivated this change).

Motivation: Customers consistently ask for safe, tenant-specific defaults for batching, cache prefill, and quantization that balance latency SLOs and unit cost. Manual profiling is slow and error-prone. This PR introduces a lightweight automated bench/telemetry pipeline (cost-bench) that runs microbenchmarks against representative request samples and uses observed token-latency/cost curves plus live telemetry to recommend conservative defaults and quantization presets for tenants and models.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a CLI command (cmd/costbench) that runs deterministic microbenchmarks against a selected model variant and tenant config, emitting a compact report and a candidate "defaults.json" for that tenant.
- Implements an on-device scoring function in internal/econ/benchscore.go that converts observed per-token latency + memory footprint into a unit-econ score and risk band (safe / experimental / avoid).
- Adds telemetry exporter hooks (telemetry/exporters/costbench) to upload sanitized microbenchmark summaries into the existing econ telemetry stream for later aggregation. Export includes model id, sequence profile, batch size tried, quant profile, p50/p95 per-token latency, and score. No customer PII is included.
- Adds an advisor service (internal/econ/advisor.go) that consumes bench results + historical telemetry to pick a recommended batch size, cache presize (kv-prefetch), and quant preset (int8 / fp16 / q4_* profiles) with a confidence score and suggested rollout plan.
- Adds integration tests and a smoke test harness to perf-canary that validates recommendations don't regress p95 beyond tenant-configured SLOs.
- Adds docs: docs/cost-bench.md with usage examples and a section on safeguards and how to interpret the produced defaults.json.

Design notes:
- The bench runner is conservative by default: it starts at the tenant's current baseline and only proposes smaller batch sizes or more aggressive quant when unit-econ improves with <5% p95 latency increase (configurable).
- Recommendations are accompanied by a rollout recipe: canary percent, safety timeout, and an automatic rollback trigger if live p95 increases >2x from bench prediction.
- Benchmarks are sampled from tenant traffic or synthetic traces; the CLI supports a --synthetic flag for reproducible experiments.

Introduces a non-disruptive tenant soft-quarantine (TTL-based) to dampen request surges, reduces cascading circuit flips, and provides a safe rollout path with metric-backed rollback.
Motivation: During sustained cross-tenant spikes we observed oscillating circuit states and noisy neighbor slowdowns even after capacity throttles engaged. This PR adds a lightweight, time-to-live (TTL) based 'soft quarantine' layer in the routing stack that temporarily attenuates low-priority tenant traffic without an immediate hard eviction. Goals: 1) reduce circuit thrash by avoiding immediate hard cutovers, 2) allow short-lived surge noise to decay rather than escalate to regional failovers, 3) preserve high-priority SLA traffic while making degradation observable and reversible.

What this change does: 
- Introduces a SoftQuarantineManager that tracks per-tenant quarantine epochs with a configurable TTL and decay window.
- Adds a fallthrough router path (attenuated path) that scales request throttling progressively based on tenant priority weight and observed SLO breach score.
- Implements a sticky-circuit hint: when a tenant is moved into soft quarantine, subsequent requests carry a hint so downstream nodes can prefer cached results and avoid repeated cold starts that worsen latency.
- Adds metrics and tracing: quarantine.entered, quarantine.exited, quarantine.ttl_remaining, quarantine_request_ratio, circuit_hint_hit. These are surfaced in Console and used by autoscaling policies.
- Fastpatch behavior for hotfix rollout: feature toggled behind runtime flag 'soft_quarantine.enabled' and 'soft_quarantine.ttl_seconds' with defaults conservative (30s TTL, 3x decay ramp).

Compatibility and safety: The soft quarantine is additive and layered before hard evictions and tenant-throttler gates. It will never drop requests outright; instead it applies progressive token-based acceptance and lower-cost execution paths. It is designed to be disabled at runtime with zero restarts.

Checklist (all items in this single paragraph to keep description contiguous): - [x] design doc referenced (Linear ENG-9821) - [x] unit tests for QuarantineManager TTL logic - [x] integration test for fallthrough router behavior under synthetic surge - [x] telemetry hooks added and dashboards updated - [x] feature flag and safe rollback plan - [x] staged rollout to Dedicated then Hosted regions

Testing and benchmarks: Synthetic replay of a known noisy-tenant incident (SUP-4112) shows 42% reduction in circuit flips over a 10-minute window and 18% improvement in p95 tail for prioritized tenants. Cost impact negligible: slightly higher per-request CPU on attenuated path but fewer expensive failovers overall.

Rollout plan: 1) Canary in one dedicated pool (low-traffic) for 24h with soft_quarantine.enabled=true and TTL=30s. 2) Stage to two regions with TTL ramp to 60s over 48h. 3) Global enable with default TTL 30s and monitoring alarms on quarantine_request_ratio > 0.25 and circuit_flip_rate > baseline + 10%.

Rollback: Toggle soft_quarantine.enabled=false or set TTL=0. Both are instantaneous and will be used automatically if alarm thresholds trigger.

Related work: This complements existing SLO enforcer changes from ENG-9873 and reduces coupling between the throttler and hard eviction code paths.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on QuarantineManager concurrency (lock-free tombstone expiry), the router admission policy heuristics, and the impact on token accounting. Metric names are intentionally short to avoid cardinality blowups.

Ethan Liu (reviewer): Can you clarify how TTL expiry interacts with the local cache pruning? I worry about stale tombstones causing prolonged attenuation.
Author (Asha): The manager emits tombstone events to the local cache agent; expiry triggers a tombstone_remove event which allows immediate cache refresh. I've added a unit test to validate tombstone_remove != tombstone_gc to avoid cache stalls.
María Gomez (reviewer): Prefer configurable backoff multiplier per tenant class rather than hardcoded 3x. Also please ensure metric dimensions do not include tenant ID (use priority class only).
Author (Asha): Switched to backoff multiplier surface in runtime flags and removed tenant_id dimension from telemetry. Updated tests and docs.
Owen Patel (reviewer): Observability looks good. Suggest adding alert for quarantine_request_ratio sustained over 200% of baseline for 5m.
Author (Asha): Added alarm to Console dashboard and included thresholds in the rollout section.

Motivation: Progressive promotes (canary -> gradual promote -> full) need a middle 'probationary' phase where traffic is steered to the candidate but held to cohorts and observed under stricter telemetry gates. Existing staged-promote controllers either move too fast or rely on static windows; customers request an observation-conditioned probation with a scheduled rollback planner (ENG-3456).

This PR implements a Probationary Promote Orchestrator that: (1) creates a transient probation lane after initial canary where cohorts are admitted incrementally, (2) attaches fine-grained observation gates (latency, error-rate, semantic-regression signal) with configurable thresholds and sample budgets, (3) supports per-cohort probation timeouts and grace tokens, (4) computes a rollback schedule dynamically based on historical noise and SLO budget, and (5) integrates with the Console rollout UI and existing rollout policies.

Checklist:
- [x] Design + spec linked (Linear ENG-3456)
- [x] Runtime admission controller + probation state machine implemented
- [x] Telemetry gating hooks + metric aggregators added
- [x] Rollback scheduler and playbook generator implemented
- [x] Unit + integration tests covering edge cases and failover
- [x] Documentation snippets for Console and CLI

Technical notes: The orchestrator introduces a small state-machine (Pending -> Probation -> Observed -> Promote/Abort) and a probation allocator that uses cohort opacity (fraction of users for sampling) and grace tokens to tolerate transient blips. Observation gates evaluate a prioritized rule-set: latency p99 delta, request error rate, model-quality regression score (from the eval pipeline). Each gate is evaluated over rolling windows; thresholds are configurable per-policy. The rollback scheduler uses a probabilistic backoff if telemetry is noisy: a candidate rollback time is proposed, then refined as more observations arrive; operators can opt into an automated rollback or prefer an alert-only mode.

Compatibility: The change is opt-in via rollout policy YAML (probation: enabled: true). Existing promotes without probation continue to function unchanged. No API contract changes for inference clients.

Commits summary: squash of feature branch into main. Key commits: probationary state machine, telemetry gate adapters, rollback scheduler, Console wiring, test harness updates.

Files changed (high-level):
- controller/probation_orchestrator.go: core state machine and admission logic
- controller/rollback_scheduler.go: policy-driven scheduler and playbook generator
- telemetry/gates/adapter.go: adapters for latency/error/model-quality signals
- console/src/rollouts/probation-ux.tsx: small Console UI to toggle probation and show cohort status
- e2e/tests/probation_flow.test.ts: end-to-end smoke tests
- docs/rollouts/probation.md: user-facing docs and config examples

Testing: CI runs the unit suite and e2e smoke with a mocked telemetry stream. Stress tests simulate noisy telemetry and confirm rollback schedule stability. On initial run the lint/build/test pipeline passed; a flakiness fix was added to the e2e harness (replayed events window increased).

Related: ENG-8890 tracks further work to add causality checks from the evaluation harness. This PR focuses on operational safety and the scheduling model.

Introduces a probationary promote orchestrator that enables observation-conditioned staging windows, per-cohort probation periods, and a configurable rollback scheduler. Backwards-compatible with existing rollout contracts; opt-in via policy config.
Diego Ramos: Nice design. Two comments: (1) can we make the default probation window small so self-serve users don't get slowed, and (2) please add observability tags to identify probation cohort traces.
Asha Menon: Thanks Diego — default probation window set to 5m for self-serve tier; added "probation.cohort" tag to tracing (see telemetry/gates/adapter.go).
Evan Chen: I worried about false positives from p99 spikes. Recommend adding a noise-aware comparator (rolling median + MAD). Can we gate that behind policy?
Asha Menon: Added noise-aware comparator and toggle in policy schema; default off. See commit 3c4d5e6. Also added unit tests for comparator edge cases.
Priya Kapoor: Approving pending minor nit on docs wording (clarify rollback vs abort semantics).
Asha Menon: Docs updated per Priya's suggestion; re-requested a docs review and then merged after CI green.

payload.body:
Motivation: We frequently see noisy correlated signals where a downstream alert creates a cascade of symptom alerts and noisy paging. This PR introduces a lightweight metric dependency graph and an alert orchestrator that uses that graph to: 1) compute transitive impact scores for alerts, 2) suppress or de-duplicate follow-on alerts for 60s by default, and 3) publish derived metrics (root-cause-likelihood, alert-impact-score) for dashboards and SLO decomposition. Design summary: - graph_builder: constructs a directed weighted graph from time-series cross-correlation and historical co-incident alert windows. We persist the graph as a compact adjacency list and per-edge confidence scores. - orchestrator: a service that subscribes to alert events and consults the graph to decide suppression, priority escalation, and annotated alert payloads. - derived metrics: we emit root_cause_prob and impact_score per-alert as time series with tags (route, model, tenant). - dashboard: new "Metric Dependency Explorer" dashboard that visualizes the graph, highlights high-impact nodes, and provides a ranked list of candidate root causes for a selected incident. - token-level tie-in: when an alert is related to inference performance we annotate impact_score with token_cost_delta and tail_latency_fraction to assist SREs in triage. Rollout plan: - deploy graph_builder and orchestrator to staging behind feature flag (obs.dep_graph=true). - collect 72h of graph telemetry, validate edges against known incidents. - enable passive mode (annotate-only) for 24h in prod, then enable suppression for a small subset of tenants. - full rollout after two production incidents validated and no regressions in alerting noise. Migration notes: - existing alert pipelines are unchanged when feature flag is off. - a small database migration adds dep_graph_v1 table; migration script included and is backwards compatible. Checklists: - [x] Graph construction pipeline implemented and unit tested. - [x] Orchestrator service with circuit breaker and rate limit implemented. - [x] Dashboard panels and quickstart doc added. - [x] Integration tests in qa/staging for end-to-end alert flow. - [x] Runbook draft linked. Testing: - unit tests cover graph heuristics and suppression logic. - synthetic incident generator used to validate no increased false negatives on a sample of historical incidents. - load test: orchestrator sustained 10k alerts/min with 12ms median decision latency in staging. Risks & mitigations: - risk: incorrect graph edges could suppress a true root alert. mitigation: default to annotate-only mode for new edges below confidence threshold 0.6; suppression requires confidence >= 0.85. - risk: increased cardinality on derived metrics. mitigation: we bucket tenant tags for derived metrics and sample low-volume tenants. Notes for reviewers: focus on graph weighting heuristics (graph_builder/weights.py) and suppression safety checks (orchestrator/safety.go). Link to runbook: https://linear.app/redwood/obs/dep-graph-runbook. Related: ENG-1429 (alert noise reduction), ENG-1484 (token-cost triage integration).
Luca Martinez: Can you explain how the graph handles transient correlations (e.g. release day spikes)? Suggest adding time-decay to edge weights.
Priya Natarajan (author): Added exponential time-decay factor and a configurable decay window (defaults to 7d) in weights.py per your suggestion.
Sara Cho: Suppression safety looks good but please add metrics to track suppressed_alerts_count and recovery_false_negatives. Also add a flagged_rollback tag when suppression is reversed.
Priya Natarajan (author): Added suppressed_alerts_count and recovery_false_negative gauges. Orchestrator sets flagged_rollback tag when a suppression is undone. Tests updated.
Ethan Blake: The dashboard is helpful; can we add a CSV export for selected subgraphs? Could be handy for oncall handover.
Priya Natarajan (author): Added export endpoint to dashboard JSON (link to export job) and small UI note in metric-dependency.md.
Luca Martinez: CI flaked on e2e once; re-ran and green. Approving pending a small nit in docs formatting.
Sara Cho: Approving — verified no noisy regressions on staging after 48h annotate-only run.

payload.body:
Motivation: Our monolithic CI stage graph has become increasingly hard to reason about and expensive to maintain. Small changes to the orchestration code were triggering widespread presubmit churn and made it difficult to apply targeted presubmit behavior (e.g. fastpath lint-only lanes, staged release smoke). This PR refactors the CI execution graph into a set of declarative stage manifests and implements a dependency gating layer that blocks merges when a curated set of transitive dependencies are flagged as unsafe. The intent is to make CI change-aware, reduce presubmit surface, and give the dep-safety team a simple manifest-driven way to apply quarantines without code changes. Summary of work: 1) introduce a manifest schema (ci/manifests/*.yaml) that declaratively defines stages, resource profiles, shard selectors and fallbacks; 2) runtime: replace the inlined stage-graph builder with a small interpreter that composes manifests into the execution plan; 3) dep-gating: add a dependency-gate step to presubmit that consults dep-snapshot and the Dep Quarantine list, failing fast for affected PRs; 4) migrate existing lint/test/release pipelines to manifests and add lightweight compatibility layer for older pipeline annotations; 5) improve observability: add per-stage telemetry and a small CLI tool (scripts/ci/manifest-inspect) to preview the plan locally. Impact: reduced presubmit average wall-clock time for small repo-only changes by ~22% in our experiments (see CI run history), and a clear operational path to quarantine transitive deps without runtime rollouts. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout across three phases: opt-in manifest mode on canary runners, mirror mode (manifests + legacy graph), and finally deprecate the legacy builder. Checklist: - [x] manifest schema RFC and schema tests - [x] interpreter implementation with unit tests - [x] presubmit dep-gate integrated and tested against mirror snapshot - [x] migration scripts for top-20 pipelines - [x] small e2e smoke on canary runners - [x] docs: ci/manifests/README.md and devdocs/ci-declarative.md - [x] added telemetry and local preview tool Notes: This description is intentionally a single contiguous string; additional context is present in commits and review thread below.
Priya Shah: Nice clean split — the manifest schema is compact. Two asks: add a doc section about how to write selectors for monorepo subtrees, and add an integration test that exercises legacy compatibility.
Diego Martinez (author): Added devdocs/ci-declarative.md with selector examples and included the compatibility integration test in tests/ci/manifest_integration_test.go.
Liam O'Connor: The dep-gate looks correct but we need a rate-limited cache on lookups to avoid hammering the dep snapshot service on large presubmit batches.
Diego Martinez (author): Implemented a small in-memory TTL cache in presubmit/hooks/dep_gate.py and measured cache hit rates (~85%) during smoke runs.
Maya Chen: Add a rollback plan for the manifest interpreter; how do we ensure a quick revert path if manifests misbehave?
Diego Martinez (author): Added a feature flag and a compatibility shim (ci/legacy_builder_compat.go). Rollback steps documented in devdocs/ci-declarative.md.
Liam O'Connor (LGTM): Approving once the dep-cache TTL is documented and the rate metrics are surfaced to the CI dashboard.
Priya Shah (approved): Verified migration script output for top-20 pipelines; looks good.
- Introduce declarative CI manifests (ci/manifests) to define stages, shards and fallbacks.
- Add manifest interpreter and local preview tool (scripts/ci/manifest-inspect).
- Add presubmit dependency-gate that prevents merges when transitive quarantined deps are present.
- Migration scripts for the top-20 pipelines; staged rollout behind a feature flag.
Canary deployment rolled out to 3 runners on 2025-11-17. Observed ~22% presubmit wall-clock improvement for small edits. Dep-team can now quarantine transitive deps via configs/dep-quarantine-list.json without runtime releases. Metrics and rate-limits added to avoid snapshot service overload.

Context and motivation:
This PR implements a conservative telemetry gating mechanism for autoscale-driven cost workflows plus a managed lifecycle for quantization profiles. Our goal is to reduce noisy/expensive attempts to run full tenant cost simulations when upstream telemetry shows negligible unit-econ improvements and to provide a safe path for quant profile promotion/retirement across Dedicated and Private deployments. The work responds to ENG-4217 (reduce wasted autoscale sim runs) and ENG-4299 (make quant profile lifecycle explicit).

What changed (single continuous description):
- Telemetry gate: new lightweight filter that examines the recent unit-econ stream (token-level latency, per-token cost, cache hit ratios) and decides whether a full simulation run should be scheduled. Gate lives under services/econ/telemetry_gate.go and exposes a minimal API used by autoscale_controller. Gate decision respects a new config key telemetry.gating.enabled (default true) and a tenant override. Gate uses heuristics + a short simulated micro-eval to estimate probable ROI before scheduling heavy work.
- Quant profile lifecycle: add profile states (candidate, promoted, deprecated) and a background reconciler that safely rolls forward promotions only after passing stability checks. Implementation in models/quant/profile_store.go plus a DB migration to add state columns (migrations/20260301_quant_profile_migration.sql).
- CLI and ops: new CLI command rw cost-sim run --dry-run and rw cost-sim promote-profile to experiment with gating behavior without committing changes. Docs added at docs/ops/cost-telemetry-gating.md.
- Observability and safety: telemetry schema extended (internal/metrics/telemetry_schema.yaml) and new histograms + slog lines to trace gate decisions. Gate emits reasons for skip vs schedule to make postmortems easier.
- Tests: unit tests for gating heuristics and profile lifecycle (tests/econ/telemetry_gate_test.go, tests/quant/profile_lifecycle_test.go) and an integration smoke test for the CLI.

Files changed summary:
- services/econ/autoscale_controller.go: wire in gating decisions before enqueuing large simulations; add safe fallback path when gate fails-open in test mode. (~+120/-14)
- services/econ/telemetry_gate.go: new file; implements policy engine and micro-prober. (~+260)
- models/quant/profile_store.go: add lifecycle state and promotion/rollback helpers. (~+140/-6)
- migrations/20260301_quant_profile_migration.sql: migration to add profile_state, promoted_at, retired_at. (~+34)
- tools/cli/cost_sim.go: new CLI surface for ops and SRE. (~+90)
- docs/ops/cost-telemetry-gating.md: operational runbook and troubleshooting. (~+40)
- tests/*: added test files and fixtures. (~+48/-108)

Review conversation summary (high level, single string):
- Miguel: requested a clearer separation between tenant-level overrides and global gating flags; asked for audit events when a profile is auto-promoted.
- Author (Aisha): implemented tenant override precedence and added an audit event emission in profile_store.go; pushed a small follow-up commit and noted migration considerations for private installs.
- Tess: asked for a unit-econ simulation stub to avoid flaky integrations; author added a local deterministic micro-prober used by gating heuristics to reduce CI variability.
- Connor: called out logging volume risk for high-throughput tenants; author added rate-limiting on gate rationale events and documented expected logs in docs.
- Approvals: Miguel and Tess approved after follow-ups; Connor approved pending a small lint cleanup that was addressed.

CI and stability notes:
- Initial CI run failed on one flaky test (tests/econ/telemetry_gate_test.go) due to timing assumptions; replaced timing with deterministic probes and re-ran. Final CI status: pass across unit+smoke suites. Performance hammer tests (perf-canary) were run as a follow-up job in staging and showed a median reduction of 18% in scheduled full-sim jobs for tenants with low-change windows.

Migration and rollout plan:
- DB migration is backward-compatible: profile_state defaults to 'candidate' and the reconciler only touches profiles that have explicit candidate markers. Ops: run migration during maintenance window; feature gate can be toggled with telemetry.gating.enabled=false while backfilling.
- Safe rollout: default-on for new tenants, opt-in for existing via tenant flag. We will enable for 10% of tenants via release toggles for two weeks and monitor the gate_decision.{skipped,schedule} metrics and profile_promotion.{attempt,succeed,rollback}.

Why this is different from earlier cost/autotune PRs:
- Rather than changing batching/quant heuristics directly, this PR introduces a lightweight pre-filter that prevents expensive downstream work unless telemetry indicates potential unit-econ improvement. It complements, not replaces, the autotuners and batchers. The quant profile lifecycle element clarifies promotion/retirement semantics so that ops can reason about automated promotions initiated from autotuners.

Testing performed:
- Unit tests for heuristics and profile transitions (deterministic micro-prober).
- CLI smoke tests in CI and a staging run against a 50-tenant synthetic workload.
- Perf canary job to validate that gate reduces unnecessary simulation load.

Follow-ups / TODOs captured in ENG-4217:
- Add a simulation-cost estimator to the gate to quantify expected token-cost savings per run.
- Expose per-tenant gate tuning via Console (UX/Frontend work).

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main on 2026-03-02 after approvals and CI green. Migration SQL included in the merge commit.

Notes for on-call and SRE:
- If unexpected profile promotions occur, toggle telemetry.gating.enabled=false and run rw cost-sim promote-profile --dry-run to inspect candidates. Gate rationale metrics: telemetry_gate.rationale (labels: tenant, reason).

This description and checklist are intentionally compact to keep the PR focused; full operational guidance is in docs/ops/cost-telemetry-gating.md.
Adds telemetry gating for autoscale-driven cost simulations and a lifecycle for quantization profiles. Backwards-compatible storage migration included.

payload.body:
Motivation: our continuous perf canaries occasionally trigger false-positive regressions during traffic spikes or when cohorts have high variance, which results in unnecessary rollbacks and alert noise. This change implements a traffic-adaptive probe sparsifier that dynamically reduces probe density when steady-state traffic and SLO headroom indicate low risk, and a fallback lattice that steps probe density back up deterministically when signals show degradation. Goals: lower probe-induced noise and cost, improve signal-to-noise ratio of canary evaluations, and provide deterministic fallback behavior so that regressions are still detected quickly. What changed: 1) core algorithm: a rolling-variance estimator + headroom calculator drives a sparsifier that throttles probe samples per tenant per-window; 2) fallback lattice: three discrete escalation tiers (sparse, normal, dense) with hysteresis and decay timers to avoid oscillation; 3) routing integration: probes can be shadowed to a replay queue for enrichment when an escalation is triggered; 4) rollout guard hooks: added thresholds (p50/p95/p99, error-rate delta, and throughput delta) with configurable time windows and confidence requirements; 5) ops: dashboards, runbook, and alert tuning; 6) tests: unit, deterministic sim harness, and integration runs in the perf-canary lab. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind ff/perf/sparsifier, staged rollout to 5% of tenants for 24h with synthetic probe burst tests, then 25% for 48h, then 100% if no regressions. Automated guard: if p95 latency increases > 20% with >95% confidence, or error-rate increases > 0.5pp and sustained for 3 windows, the rollout lattice forces immediate density increase and triggers an automatic rollback policy depending on severity. Backwards compatibility: algorithm runs as an opt-in config per canary and does not change historical metrics. Related work: follows ENG-3281 proposal for probe-cost-reduction and ENG-3302 for rollback lattice design. Checklist: - [x] design docs and linear tickets linked - [x] unit tests added - [x] simulation scenarios with synthetic traffic - [x] integration runs in perf-canary lab - [x] dashboards and runbook updated - [x] staged rollout plan and automated guard configured More context and the runbook: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3281/perf-probe-sparsifier-runbook
Adds an adaptive probe sparsifier to reduce noisy probe traffic and a fallback lattice that progressively increases probe density when instability is detected. Includes rollout guard integration, dashboards, runbook updates, and automated rollback triggers.
Adds adaptive probe sparsification and a deterministic fallback lattice to reduce false-positive perf canary alerts and probe cost, with staged rollout and automated rollback guards integrated into existing canary controller.
Ethan Zhao: Nice approach. Can you clarify the decay timer math under heavy oscillation? Suggest adding a max-escalation-rate limiter to avoid thundering probe increases.
Sofia Martinez: Added a limiter and annotated the decay math with examples; included tests that simulate oscillation and verify hysteresis behavior.
Priya Nair: Please ensure the per-tenant default config cannot be lowered below our minimum detection density for critical customers. Also check cost accounting for added shadowing.
Sofia Martinez: Default floor set to 10 probes/min for critical tenants; shadowing is conditional and billed to feature-cost center; added dashboard cost projection.
Luca Romano: Integration run failed once due to a flaky test json roundtrip, re-ran CI and it passed. Approving after fix.
Priya Nair: Approved pending addendum to the runbook with triage steps for late-array anomalies.
SRE oncall (automated comment): Observability alerts created: PERF-SPARSER-01 (sustained p95 increase), PERF-SPARSER-02 (hysteresis-fail)

payload.body:
Context and motivation: During recent regional overload incidents we observed noisy long-running low-priority requests occupying ephemeral slots and preventing short-lived high-priority traffic from meeting SLOs. This PR introduces an ephemeral lease revocation mechanism plus a priority preemption policy that reclaims ephemeral capacity with a soft handoff (preempt-with-grace) to preserve SLOs while minimizing client errors. Motivation is to reduce tail latency and error rate for priority traffic during capacity pressure without hard-evicting user KV caches or dropping active model state.

What this PR does (single-line sections but continuous): Implements a lease manager (ephemeral_lease_manager) that issues timeboxed leases for ephemeral allocations; adds a lease revocation RPC to allow schedulers to request a graceful drain; introduces a preemption policy that ranks requests by priority and age and uses a configurable "preempt window" (default 200ms) to ask lower-priority leases to yield; integrates the protocol into region_coordinator so reclaim decisions can be region-aware and avoid cross-region instability; exposes metrics and traces for lease acquire/revoke and preemption decisions; provides a small docs how-to and an optional canary manifest for rollout.

Checklist and rollout plan: - [x] Unit tests for lease manager state transitions - [x] Integration tests for revoke handshake and graceful drain - [x] E2E canary job (regression and SLO smoke tests) - [x] Metrics and dashboards updated - [x] Feature gate config.ephemeral.preempt_enabled=false by default; canary enables true - Rollout: enable in single region as canary for 48 hours, monitor ephemeral_lease_revoke_rate, p95 latency for high-priority traffic, and error_rate; if regression, flip gate off and rollback.

Commits (high-level summary): commit 1 - add lease proto and manager skeleton; commit 2 - implement revoke handshake and graceful stop path; commit 3 - introduce priority preemption algorithm + tests; commit 4 - integrate with region_coordinator and expose metrics; commit 5 - docs, canary manifest, CI pipeline updates; commit 6 - follow-up test fixes and flake fixes.

Files changed (high level): - allocator/ephemeral_lease_manager.go: main state machine and lease book - scheduler/preemption_policy.go: algorithm implementing age/priority ranking and preempt window - runtime/lease_protocol.proto: revoke Acquire/LeaseExpired messages - region_coordinator.go: decision logic to prefer local soft-preempt over remote failover - metrics/ephemeral_leases.prom: new counters/gauges for observability - docs and tests: canary + integration.

Design notes and rationale: We intentionally chose a soft-revoke flow instead of immediate eviction to reduce broken in-flight KV/state for long-running streams. The preemption decision uses a score = priority_weight * priority + age_weight * (1 / age_ms) to avoid starvation and to prefer reclaiming recently-started low-priority allocations. A configurable grace window allows providers/SDKs to finish small critical sections; if the client does not yield within the grace window the runtime falls back to a hard revoke which preserves capacity but is counted as a user-facing failure and emitted to metrics.

Observability and alerts: New metrics: ephemeral_lease_acquire_total, ephemeral_lease_revoke_requested_total, ephemeral_lease_revoke_succeeded_total, ephemeral_preempt_hard_failures_total. New tracing span: lease.revocation.{request,ack}. Added dashboard rows keyed by region and priority-class. Alert: if ephemeral_preempt_hard_failures_total > 5/min during canary, autoswitch gate to false and page SRE.

Testing notes: Integration tests simulate mixed priority traffic and assert that high-priority token p95 reduces by >= 15% under controlled reclaim scenarios. E2E canary (regression job) runs in dev region with feature gate and validates no more than 1% increase in 99th error rate for low-priority workloads.

Review conversation (high-level): Miguel Torres: "Can we avoid revoking leases for streams that report active tool-use?" Response (Aisha): "Added an exemption hook: lease manager now checks a stream_activity marker (best-effort) before hard-revoke; documented behavior in examples." Samir Patel: "Preemption score formula seems sensitive to weight tuning; can we add per-tenant overrides?" Response (Aisha): "Added config.allow_tenant_weights with safe defaults; kept global defaults for canary." Ruth Kim: "CI flake on revoke path (race) — failing test observed." Response (Aisha): "Addressed race by adding a small jitter in the revoke ack path and a targeted unit test; reran CI." CI: initial pipeline failed lint in telemetry parser; fixed Python lint and re-ran — all checks passed.

Backward compatibility and safety: The feature is behind config.ephemeral.preempt_enabled=false; default runtime behavior unchanged. Lease proto adds a new optional field 'grace_ms' and will be ignored by older nodes; region_coordinator will fallback to non-preempt behavior when communicating with older control-plane peers. No breaking API changes.

Canary results summary (post-merge): In the dev canary region after 48h with the gate enabled for a narrow cohort, high-priority p95 latency improved by 18% during injected overload windows. Hard revoke failures remained under 0.3% of revokes due to the grace window. No cross-region failovers observed. We consider this ready for controlled roll out to two additional regions.

Merge outcome: squash-merged into main on 2026-02-20 after approvals from Miguel and Ruth. Follow-ups: ENG-9127 on per-tenant weighting dashboard; operational runbook note added to SRE handbook.
Adds ephemeral lease revocation and priority-based preemption to reclaim transient capacity under overload; opt-in via config.ephemeral.preempt_enabled; improved observability (ephemeral_lease_acquire/revoke metrics) and a safety window to avoid user-visible request failures.

Summary: Introduce a lightweight 'econ-bootstrapper' service that auto-generates tenant-specific batching/cache defaults and an optional compact sample pruner used to seed quantization/compact profiles. Motivation: onboarding new tenants often produces cold unit-econ and cache profiles; manual tuning is slow and conservative leading to higher costs. This change automates a safe warmstart that provides conservative batch and cache defaults plus a compact sample selection strategy for early quantization profile suggestions. Design: 1) econ-bootstrapper service runs as a short-lived job after tenant creation or when requested via admin API. 2) It ingests a small anonymized sample of traffic (configurable sampling rate), computes per-tenant sequence length distribution, warm cache prefix candidates, and candidate micro-batch size that respects latency SLOs. 3) The compact sample pruner selects representative traces under size and privacy constraints using a distance heuristic (L2 on token-length histograms and metadata bucketing) and outputs a 1-10KB summary used by the quantizer/optimizer. 4) Results are written to the tenant defaults store and emitted as a suggested profile in the Console UI; changes are opt-in and gated by safety checks. Rollout and safety: default generated profiles are conservative by design with guardrails: a) batch sizes are clamped to preserve 99th percentile latency targets, b) quantization profile suggestions are flagged as "suggested" and not auto-applied, c) bootstrap runs are rate-limited and sampled to avoid platform-wide burst. Implementation highlights: - New service package under internal/econ/bootstrapper with a small state machine, sampling adapters, and a compact pruner module. - Tenant defaults model extended (tenant_defaults.v2) with source=autogen, confidence, and sample_signature fields. - Admin API endpoint POST /admin/tenants/:id/bootstrap that triggers a run and returns a candidate profile preview. - Console additions: new "Suggested Defaults" card with a one-click apply + dry-run option. Testing and telemetry: added unit tests for sample pruner heuristics, integration tests for tenant_defaults migration, and a lightweight end-to-end perf check that runs in CI with mocked samples to validate latency clamps. Telemetry emitted: bootstrap.run.{start,success,failed}, bootstrap.profile_confidence, bootstrap.applied_by. Migration notes: tenant_defaults.v1 is read-first; v2 is written only when autogen runs or when applying a suggested profile. Rollback plan: autogen writes are non-destructive and can be rolled back by clearing source=autogen entries. Docs: console and API docs updated, plus a short runbook in docs/operators/bootstrapping.md. Related work: overlaps with ENG-1842 (tenant warmstart RFC) and ENG-2017 (quant profile suggestion API). Checklist: [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] console card [x] e2e perf smoke [x] docs [x] Linear link included.

Context: We currently rely on per-request RBAC checks and a general audit pipeline, but operator access patterns across regions lack deterministic evidence for residency decisions and post-hoc compliance reviews. This PR introduces two coordinated features: 1) an operator-proof catalog (OPC) — a compact registry of signed operator access assertions and their provenance that surfaces during policy evaluation; and 2) a KMS locality enforcer — a middleware that validates KMS key locality against tenant residency claims and annotates audit envelopes when a locality mismatch is resolved.

Motivation: Several recent compliance reviews and audits revealed gaps where operator actions could be executed via stale operator credentials or cross-region operator sessions without a canonical claim in the audit trace. The OPC provides an immutable, signed assertion referenced by RBAC v2 decisions. The KMS locality enforcer prevents keys from being used in unintended regions and records the enforcement rationale in a tamper-evident audit envelope.

High-level design: OPC is a small service (service/opc) that stores signed operator assertions: operator id, role template, scoping (geozone), issuance time, and optional approval tokens. Assertions are minted by the operator-approval flow and are signed with a platform signing key; the policy engine fetches a short-lived proof when evaluating decisions. The KMS locality enforcer plugs into the kms client path (pkg/kms/guard) and cross-checks the key location against the tenant's pinned-region header and the OPC scoping claim. When an enforcement decision is made, the enforcer appends a compact proof entry to the audit envelope (audit/enrichers/locality.json) including a hash pointer to the OPC assertion and the KMS metadata.

Behavioral guarantees: - RBAC v2 decisions that depend on operator-scoped assertions are denied if no OPC proof is presented unless the request comes from an explicit operator-exempt route (documented). - KMS locality checks produce deterministic deny/allow decisions; allow decisions record a proof, denies produce a sanitized audit record and an operator-level alert.

Migration and rollout plan: - Feature-flagged behind ff.opc and ff.kms_locality. - Phase 1 (canary): enable in staging and 5% of traffic for dedicated accounts for 2 weeks; collect metrics (latency, deny-rate, proof-miss-rate). - Phase 2 (shadow): run checks in shadow mode for all regions to build profiler data and operator assertion coverage. - Phase 3: opt-in enforcement for enterprise tenants, followed by global enforcement after policy signoff.

Testing and verification: Added unit tests for the signature verifier, integration tests that simulate cross-region operator sessions, and an e2e compliance test that asserts that the audit envelope contains the locality proof when a KMS call is allowed. Load tests show a median 0.4ms added latency on the KMS call path under normal conditions.

Related work: builds on ENG-1188 (rbacv2 policy templates) and complements the new audit-envelope-v3 (PR #564738). Linear references: ENG-2029 (OPC design), SEC-87 (KMS locality requirements).

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked and reviewed by security
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] Feature flags in place
- [x] Migration/runbook drafted under docs/compliance/opc-migration.md
- [x] Observability: metrics and tracing spans added

Impact and risk: The change touches authz and KMS hot paths; risk is mitigated by flags, canary rollout, and a fast rollback path (feature flag kill-switch). No breaking changes to public APIs.

Release notes: Introduces operator-proof catalog (OPC) and optional KMS locality enforcement to improve residency proofing and audit fidelity. Enterprise customers can opt-in before global enforcement.

Implementation notes (concise): - service/opc: store + sign assertions using platform key (pkg/crypto/sign). Assertions are compact (protocol buf artifact) with an indexed hash. - pkg/policy/opa_adapter: fetch OPC proof in EvaluateRequest; cache proof for 30s to avoid extra roundtrips. - pkg/kms/guard: validate key region against tenant header and OPC scoping claim; annotate audit envelope via audit/enrichers/locality.go. - cli/rbacctl: new subcommand rbacctl proof inspect <assertion-hash> to fetch human-readable assertion for ops.

Security considerations: All OPC assertions are signed and stored encrypted at rest. The OPC service requires an additional operator-approval scope; assertions are TTL-bound and revocable. Audit envelopes include only compact proof references (hashes + reason) to avoid exponentiating sensitive payloads.

Documentation: docs/compliance/opc-overview.md and docs/platform/kms-locality-runbook.md added; rbacctl docs updated.

Ben Whitaker: 'Design looks strong; want to understand cache staleness risk for OPC proofs when operator assertions are revoked.'
Aisha Kapoor: 'We implemented TTL + revocation marker: policy engine consults revocation index when a proof is older than 30s; added tests to cover revocation path.'
Marta Li: 'Please ensure the audit envelope does not leak key material or operator tokens.'
Aisha Kapoor: 'Audit entries only contain proof hash, KMS region, and enforcement rationale; added explicit assertion to the docs and an automated linter that fails if PII-like fields are present in the enricher output.'
Omar Hernandez: 'Can we add a non-disruptive mode where we record deny reasons but allow the call for 48 hours?'
Aisha Kapoor: 'Added shadow mode (ff.kms_locality=shadow) per request; comments updated with rollout steps.'
Approvals: Ben Whitaker approved after two iterations; Marta Li approved. Omar requested one small doc change which was addressed.

Motivation: During last week's regional degradation incident we observed rapid circuit flips when a cascading egress pressure spike hit a subset of nodes. The result was oscillating failovers and noisy telemetry spikes that caused several short-lived SLO breaches. This PR introduces a small runtime shim ("softdown-translator") that translates aggressive circuit state transitions into timeboxed, telemetry-anchored softdown windows and tethers SLO relaxation to a bounded budget.

What I changed (high-level):
- New softdown translator component in the routing stack that receives raw circuit events and emits 'softdown' directives. Softdown directives temporarily reduce SLA expectations for a tenant/cohort but do not immediately trigger cross-region failover.
- SLO tethering: a budgeted counter per-tenant/cohort that caps cumulative softdown time over sliding windows (configurable default 10m/1h). This prevents unlimited silent degradation from eating into customer SLOs.
- Telemetry anchoring: each softdown is stamped with the triggering metrics snapshot (latency p50/p95, token queue depth, kv-cache pressure) so downstream observers and the console can correlate degradations with root signals.
- Backstop hotfix: an emergency unwind path that forces immediate circuit reset if softdown windows exceed a safety threshold (to avoid stuck softdown states after controller crashes).

Design notes:
- The translator is conservative: it aggregates identical circuit-flip events from the same region for 250ms before emitting a softdown. This coalescing reduces noise from connection churn.
- Softdown directives carry a reason code (eg: "egress_surge", "kv_pressure", "probe_timeouts") used by the console and rollback policies.
- SLO tethering budget operates on two axes: per-tenant and per-region. Per-tenant budgets prevent noisy tenants from hogging softdown credits; per-region budgets prevent a single region from silently defaulting to a degraded state across customers.
- Configs are feature-flagged and default to disabled for Dedicated/private installs; the hosted control plane enables a conservative default.

Checklist:
- [x] Add translator module and unit tests
- [x] Wire translator into routing pipeline with minimal critical-path overhead
- [x] Add budget store and Redis-backed persistence with TTL
- [x] Emit telemetry fields for Console and SLO engine
- [x] Add emergency unwind path and e2e smoke test
- [x] Docs stub for config knobs and rollout notes

Commits summary:

- feat(slo): add tethering budget store and APIs
- fix(hotfix): emergency unwind on stuck softdown state
- perf(routing): 250ms coalesce window + micro-optimizations
- docs: softdown + tethering operational guide (stub)

Files changed (high level):

- runtime/routing/translator_test.go (unit tests)
- runtime/slo/tether_store.go (budget persistence + TTL)

- console/telemetry/softdown_events.proto (telemetry schema)
- scripts/e2e/softdown_smoke.sh (smoke test harness)
- docs/operations/softdown-tethering.md (operational notes)

Small snippet (translator coalescing logic):
"if recentSameEvent && now - lastEmit < 250ms { mergeCount++ ; return } emitSoftdown(now, reason)"

Testing and CI:

- Integration smoke test runs in CI that simulates an egress spike and asserts that the translator emits a single softdown directive and tether budget decrements.
- Lint and go vet passed. A flakey e2e test flaked once on CI; re-run succeeded.

Review conversation summary:

- Author (Aisha): "Addressed: added config flag softdown.coalesce_ms and tether budget floor in tether_store.go. Added histogram with tag:region. See commit feat: expose coalesce and metrics."
- Priya Sharma: "Can hosting enable this by default? We need a migration plan for existing SLO reports so we don't create noise in dashboards."
- Author: "Plan added to docs/operations: we enable in 'gradual' mode where softdown directives are emitted but do not affect customer-visible SLOs for the first 72 hours; after telemetry review we flip the operational flag. Included Linear ENG-4392 for rollout."
- Ethan Liu (approval): "Code looks good; tests are reasonable. Minor nit about error message wording in tether_api.go."

Motivation: customers operating across multiple jurisdictions send heterogeneous region claims and rely on tenant-level KMS consent. This PR implements a rules based claim normalizer plus a consent multiplexer that chooses an authorized KMS provider per effective tenant region, addressing mismatches between operator assertions and downstream key policies while producing richer audit metadata. What changed: 1) services/claim-normalizer service that canonicalizes incoming location claims, supports fuzzy mapping tables and tenant overrides, and emits canonical_region into request context. 2) pkg/kms/consent_mux that evaluates tenant consent profiles, KMS provider allowlists, and per-request residency constraints to select a provider or return a deterministic denial. 3) Integration with policy compiler so RBACv2 decision engine receives normalized claims for accurate policy evaluation and logging. 4) Audit enrichment middleware that stamps canonical_region, kms_provider_hint, and consent_verification into sealed-audit headers. 5) Backfill script and a canary rollout plan behind feature flag rbac.jurisdictional_normalizer. Rollout and safety: feature is gated under opt-in flag, default behavior preserves prior claim passthrough. Canary strategy described in the PR checklist below. Testing: unit tests for normalization rules and mux decision matrix, integration tests exercising policy compiler + KMS selection against mocked provider endpoints, and end-to-end smoke in staging. Backwards compatibility: no public API surface change; operator-managed mappings are additive. Operational notes: added alerts for decision latency and consent cache miss rate, metric labels for canonical_region. References: ENG-3321 for rule set design and SEC-89 for threat model. Summary: This PR adds a small, opinionated 'onramp' for tenant cost-optimization: a CLI-driven starter profile generator plus a lightweight quant-snapshot exporter service. Motivation: many customers ask for safe, quick wins to reduce per-token cost without manual tuning. This delivers curated batching, cache and quantization starter profiles that are conservative by default and a deterministic snapshot export to enable safe quant rollouts. Add a slew-rate-aware throttler into the canary evaluation pipeline to prevent noisy transient traffic spikes from triggering aggressive rollout changes. Motivation: we observed several incidents where sudden upstream traffic bursts caused the canary evaluator to overreact, rapidly shifting traffic weights and creating oscillations that hurt tail latency and customer experience. This PR implements a compact time-derivative metric (request_rate_slew) and a configurable smoothing/throttling policy that gates traffic weight updates when the instantaneous slew exceeds a safety threshold. The implementation is conservative by default, exposes runtime knobs (window_ms, slew_threshold, max_step_pct, cooldown_ms) and integrates with existing rollout guards so that canaries only change weight if both quality metrics and slew constraints are satisfied. Included are unit tests, a synthetic e2e job that reproduces the original oscillation, dashboard panels, and alerts for sustained-high-slew conditions. Also added docs outlining recommended thresholds for common traffic shapes and an opt-out flag for legacy canary behaviors.
Ravi Patel requested changes: please tighten the unit test around the edge case where slew decays right at the cooldown boundary and add a comment explaining why we choose exponential smoothing instead of simple moving average.
Ava Martinez replied: added additional test and inline comment, left the smoother parameterized so teams can choose SMA vs EMA via config.
Sofia Li approved: verified behavior on staging canary cluster, observed elimination of oscillation in synthetic burst test.
Jonah Becker approved with comment: consider exposing a per-namespace opt-out in a follow-up to reduce blast radius for legacy services.
Added slew-rate-aware canary throttler to reduce noisy traffic-driven rollout oscillations; config knobs available under charts/canary/values.yaml; dashboards and alerts added for request_rate_slew.

Motivation: customers with reserved/dedicated capacity asked for precise throughput guarantees tied to commitments and a way to reclaim unused reserved capacity when commitments expire. This PR introduces a commit-anchored throughput contract model and an expiry ledger that tracks per-tenant commitments, their effective windows, and decay/transfer rules. Design: 1) commit_ledger component: records commitments as immutable anchors with start/expiry timestamps and nominal throughput qps values; 2) soft-expiry policy: on expiry a commit enters a decay window instead of immediate revocation so running workloads get graceful degradation; 3) reservation harmonizer: background controller that reconciles current capacity against active anchors and soft-expired entries, producing reallocation suggestions; 4) autoscaler hook: the scale decider reads the ledger to satisfy guaranteed throughput first, then opportunistic capacity; 5) telemetry exporter: new metrics exposed (commit_effective_qps, commit_decay_fraction, ledger_reclaimed_qps) and a per-tenant utilization report that correlates committed vs consumed throughput using HDR histograms. Backwards compatibility: ledger is additive and default policies preserve current autoscaler behavior unless teams opt into commit enforcement via a per-tenant flag. Rollout plan: gated feature flag, staged rollout to internal dedicated clusters, 2-week canary, then opt-in for customers, finally default-enforcement after telemetry validation. Testing: unit tests for ledger reconciliation, integration test that simulates commit expiry, load tests to validate autoscaler interaction under saturation. Security and observability: audit events for create/extend/expire are emitted; metrics are labeled with tenant_id and commit_id; RBAC checks added to commit API. This description contains links and references inlined: Linear ENG-3182 covers API surface; ENG-4221 covers telemetry format. Checklist: [x] spec doc updated [x] ledger storage migration safe [x] autoscaler integration tests [x] telemetry dashboard prototype [x] docs and console UI follow-up PR

Priya Menon: Added autoscaler unit and an integration harness that pins opportunistic capacity to zero; new test 'TestScaleRespectsCommitGuarantee' added. Instrumentation metrics 'autoscaler_decision_override' included.

Motivation: We observed that direct shadow-to-canary promotions cause stepwise metric volatility for sparse cohorts and stateful sessions. Small cohorts spike evaluation noise and trigger noisy rollbacks. This PR implements an opt-in 'Incremental Shadow Promote' strategy that incrementally converts shadowed traffic into promoted traffic by stochastic cohort smoothing and a credit-based rollforward/rollback policy. Design summary: 1) Cohort Smoothing: a lightweight sampler produces smoothed promotion increments per cohort using a configurable smoothing factor and jitter distribution to avoid synchronized bursts. 2) Promotion Credits: each cohort accrues 'promotion credits' from successful smoke checks (latency, error-rate, output-quality evals). Credits are consumed to increase promoted percentage; negative deltas trigger staged refunds and holdpoints. 3) Session Affinity Preservation: promotion decisions respect session affinity keys if provided; we ensure sticky sessions are not split mid-request by tagging candidate sessions and draining on safe commit. 4) Metric Alignment Gate: a multi-metric aggregator computes an aligned score across latency P95, error-rate, and eval-quality delta; the aligned score is compared to per-cohort dynamic thresholds before any credit spend. 5) Replay-safe Rollback: when a rollback is triggered, the controller attempts a partial rewind using shadow capture snapshots and a limited replay to surface representative failures for debugging; this is gated by a replay budget. Implementation notes: - New controller: service/rollout/incremental_promote_controller.go implements the reconciliation loop, credit accounting, and cohort state machine. - Sampling lib: internal/rollout/sampler.go contains the stochastic smoothing sampler with deterministic seeding for test determinism. - Metric adapter: observability/adapter/promote_metrics.go adds the aligned score computation and exposes debug traces for the console. - Session draining helpers: infra/session/drain.go with small helpers used by the controller to mark and drain affected sessions. - Config: api/rollout/v1alpha2/policy.proto extended with PromoteStrategy enum and strategy params (smoothing_factor, replay_budget, credit_window). Tests and validation: - Unit tests for sampler and credit accounting in service/rollout/*_test.go. - Integration smoke tests in examples/rollout/smoke that run a 3-cohort scenario with synthetic metrics. - e2e test harness addition: perf-canary/test/incremental_promote_e2e.yaml covering a simulated rollback and replay. Backwards compatibility and opt-in: The new PromoteStrategy is behind a feature flag and defaults to the existing promote behavior. No customer-facing API changes unless customers opt into the new strategy. Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag. 2) Deploy controller to staging and run e2e harness; opt-in a synthetic customer via console. 3) Run 2 week A/B experiment comparing 'IncrementalShadowPromote' to the baseline. 4) If results are stable, enable as GA with telemetry dashboard and rollout recipe. Operational considerations: - Telemetry: added per-cohort credit burn rate and replay budget metrics. - Alerts: new alert 'promote-credit-depletion' to avoid stalled promotions. - Cost: replay budget is intentionally tiny for GA to limit cost, adjustable per-customer. Related work: Builds on the shadow-capture and cohort-anchoring projects (see ENG-1198 and ENG-1740). This PR is intentionally focused on the controller and safety gates; it does not change kernel-level serving runtime or KV cache logic. Security and compliance: replay snapshots are sanitized and honor PII redaction hooks before any storage. Code review highlights: - Deterministic tester seed ensures reproducible test failures. - Credit ledger persisted as annotations on the rollout resource to survive controller restarts. - Metrics are tagged with cohort_id and promote_strategy for downstream dashboards. Known limitations: - Very large numbers of tiny cohorts may increase controller memory; we cap cohort caching and evict based on LRU with a configurable retention window. - Current replay uses a sampled subset of requests; it is not a full fidelity replay system. 
Adds an opt-in 'incremental shadow promote' controller that gradually promotes shadow traffic to live with cohort smoothing and rollback credit accounting. Backwards compatible. Toggle via rollout.v1alpha2.policy.promoteStrategy=IncrementalShadowPromote.
Luca Martinez: Nice approach. Question: how sensitive is aligned score to highly skewed latency distributions? Could we add a robust mean or trimmed mean?
Priya: Good point. I added a trimmed-mean option and made it configurable (smoothing config). Default remains median-based to be robust to tail noise.
Anika Chen: Need to ensure credit ledger writes are idempotent in case of controller flapping.
Priya: Ledger writes are implemented as compare-and-swap on rollout annotations; added tests to simulate controller restart races.
Samir Patel: Add an opt-out for replay snapshots for customers in high compliance orgs.
Priya: Added a config flag 'replay_snapshot_allowed' and circuit-breaker check before any snapshot is taken.
