Motivation: We observed a class of failures in long-running streaming responses where partial JSON objects emitted as SSE 'delta' fragments could be delivered out-of-order or combined with delimiter anomalies after network retries or proxy replays. This manifested as broken tool/function-call payloads, intermittent JSON parse errors in downstream OpenAI-compat clients, and rare duplicate function-sentinel emissions under high-concurrency bursts. The goal of this PR is to make SSE delta emission atomic with explicit boundary guards so clients can deterministically reassemble structured outputs and tool call payloads even under retries or fragment reordering.

Summary of changes: implemented an atomic delta buffer on the SSE emitter that guarantees each logical token/event batch is emitted as an indivisible unit (either fully emitted or retried in full), introduced locked boundary markers around JSON object starts/ends to avoid partial-object exposures, added a lightweight per-event seqid + checksum header to assist client-side resynchronization, hardened the parser reassembly path to prefer checksum-confirmed joins, and added a suite of deterministic integration tests and CI gating.

What this fixes: prevents partial-JSON leak where a truncated object was emitted without its closing brace; eliminates cases where function-call sentinels (e.g., "__CALL_START" / "__CALL_END") could be split across SSE chunks causing the OpenAI-compat layer to misinterpret tool call boundaries; reduces duplicate-sentinel emission by ensuring retries replay whole delta units rather than individual token fragments.

Behavioral notes and compatibility: the emitter adds an additional SSE metadata header (X-Redwood-Seqid and X-Redwood-Checksum) to each delta event. Clients that do not inspect these headers will continue to work unchanged because the payload format is unchanged; clients that adopt the headers can detect out-of-order or partially-applied windows and request deterministic resync. The change preserves existing API contracts and is opt-in from a client-resync perspective, so this is non-breaking.

Testing and validation: added new unit tests for the parser reassembler (tests/sse/test_delimiter_race.py), end-to-end integration tests that fuzz split points across UTF-8 boundaries and function-call sentinels (tests/sse/test_token_ordering_integration.py), and deterministic fixtures under src/runtime/testing/fixtures/sse_partial_json.json. CI pipeline was extended with a gated job (infra/ci/sse_pipeline.yml) that runs the integration suite under multiple network fragmentation patterns. Post-merge load test (internal): 48-hour run simulated 12k concurrent streams with median latency unchanged and visible reduction in parse-error rate from 0.37% to 0.01% on the sampled workload.

Docs and observability: added docs/compat/sse-guidelines.md describing the seqid/checksum model and best practices for client resync. Emitted per-event metrics (pkg/observability/sse_metrics.ts) for delta-retries and checksum-mismatch events to help operators identify degraded client reassembly behavior.

Checklist: - [x] design and API review with API and runtime teams - [x] unit + integration tests added - [x] CI gating for sse integration suite - [x] docs updated - [x] observability hooks added - [x] rolled out to canary region and monitored

Rollout plan: merged to main -> staged canary in eu-west-1 and us-west-2 for 48 hours -> monitor checksum-mismatch and delta-retry metrics -> graduate to global. Controlled fallback: runtime exposes a config flag runtime.sse.atomic_delta=false for emergency rollback.

Related work: references ENG-3912 (flaky function-call parsing incident) and SUP-2213 customer report about partial JSON in streamed tool output. See also prior SSE work (various PRs) for framing history.

Notes on code areas: src/openai_compat/sse/parser.rs: added resync path that uses seqid/checksum, tolerant whitespace handling, and stricter sentinel anchoring. src/runtime/streaming/sse_emitter.cpp: atomic buffer implementation, per-event header encoding, and retry semantics. src/api/handlers/streaming_handler.go: small handler updates to propagate emitter headers through proxy layers. tests/*: deterministic integrations and fuzz harness.

Potential follow-ups: - upstream client library helpers to consume seqid/checksum and offer automatic resync - expand checksums to cover KV cache prefix fragments for cached responses - further reduce allocations in emitter buffer for extreme-scale workloads

This PR was intentionally kept focused on correctness and observability; subsequent PRs will drive micro-optimizations to reduce peak memory from the new buffer under extreme burst patterns.
Marcus O'Neill (reviewer): Overall approach looks solid. A couple of questions: can we avoid adding headers for internal proxies that might strip non-standard headers? Also, how does this interact with streaming over HTTP/2 multiplexed connections?
Ava Chen (author): Good point on proxies — the headers are emitted as SSE comment-prefixed meta fields (":seqid: <id>" / ":checksum: <hex>") so they survive intermediaries that do not strip comment lines; added a note in docs about proxies. Regarding HTTP/2: implementation is transport-agnostic; emitter guarantees delta units and header comments are part of the SSE event payload, so HTTP/2 fragmentation only affects chunking but not logical delta atomicity.
Priya Kapoor (reviewer): Tests look comprehensive. Can we add a small unit test that simulates a proxy that reorders two entire delta events to show resync via seqid?
Ava Chen (author): Added tests/sse/test_token_ordering_integration.py with a targeted reordering case and assertion on checksum-mismatch metric emission.
Diego Rivera (approver): Verified canary metrics and load run. Approving — please squash commits and merge when CI passes.
CI (system): All checks passed on rerun (unit, integration, lint). sse pipeline completed in 18m.

Context: We’ve had recurring customer confusion/disputes where billed token attribution diverges between OpenAI-compatible chat/tooling flows vs. non-tooling flows, and we’ve also seen internal drift after small parser changes. This PR adds a focused unit test suite that locks down token metering behavior for (a) tool/function calling and (b) structured output (JSON mode / schema-guided output) so we can safely evolve request parsing + model adapters without accidentally changing billed_tokens attribution. Scope: tests only (no meter logic changes). What’s covered: (1) ChatCompletions tool_calls: assistant emits tool_calls with function name + arguments; verify prompt_tokens vs completion_tokens counts align with our meter spec and stay stable across adapters. (2) Tool role messages: tool result messages included back into the context; verify they are counted as prompt tokens on the next model call, not completion, and that tool “name” fields are handled consistently. (3) Parallel tool calls: multiple tool_calls in a single assistant turn; verify deterministic serialization and that we don’t double-count the tool call wrapper fields. (4) Structured output: response_format=json_schema and json_object modes; verify that schema scaffolding tokens are treated consistently and the emitted JSON is counted only in completion. (5) Regression fixtures for known bug: previously we counted the function.arguments string twice when adapters re-materialized tool messages; the tests would have caught this. Notes: These tests intentionally assert on billed_tokens (not raw tokens) and include a small helper that runs the same cases through the OpenAI-compat layer and native Redwood route to ensure alignment. Related: SUP-28451 (invoice tokens do not match usage export) and ongoing metering hardening work in ENG-4410 / PM-1842. Follow-up: streaming partial-chunk tests live in ENG-4410/ENG-4410 follow-on; this PR keeps unit tests deterministic and fast (<2s).
Nadia Rahman (review): The direction is right. Two nits: (1) Please assert on billed_tokens breakdown (prompt/completion) rather than only total, and (2) ensure the parity harness pins the same model tokenizer config so we don’t get false positives when model defaults shift.
Leila Farouk (author): Updated assertions to check prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, and billed_tokens_total. Also wired the harness to explicitly pass tokenizer_profile='rw-tokenizer-v4' to both paths (native + openai-compat).
Cole Summers (review): Can we add a regression for the double-materialization scenario we saw in SUP-28451? Specifically: adapter builds tool message then downstream re-serializes tool_calls again. That’s where we doubled function.arguments in February.
Leila Farouk (author): Added fixture tool_calls/double_materialization_case.json and a test that simulates the adapter path by passing both tool_calls and an equivalent tool role message; verifies we only count the arguments once. Linked the test comment to SUP-28451 for future archaeology.
Allison Grant (review): Please avoid hardcoding exact token counts for every fixture unless needed; it tends to be brittle across tokenizer profile changes. Prefer invariants where possible (e.g., tool result must be prompt tokens; JSON output must be completion tokens). Where you do pin counts, add a short note explaining why it must remain stable (billing semantics).
Leila Farouk (author): Agreed. Converted most tests to invariants and kept exact token snapshots only for two billing-critical fixtures (simple_tool_call + json_schema_user_profile). Added comments + README section explaining what’s pinned vs invariant and why.
Monica Patel (review): Looks good. Small suggestion: include a case where function.name is non-ASCII / contains hyphens to match what SDKs allow, and make sure serialization doesn’t normalize it unexpectedly.
Leila Farouk (author): Added function name 'search-v2_β' fixture and verified we preserve it in serialization and token attribution. Tests pass.
Nadia Rahman (approval): Approved. Thanks for keeping these fast/deterministic and for asserting on billed_tokens specifically.
Cole Summers (approval): Approved. This should reduce churn in Finance recon whenever we touch request parsing.
Internal: Added unit test coverage to prevent regressions in billed token attribution for tool/function calling and structured output flows (OpenAI-compat + native parity).

Motivation: our presubmit lanes are large and noisy for small changes, CI feedback is slow for developer iteration, and transitive dependency churn continues to cause flakey premerge failures. This PR introduces a lightweight presubmit router that routes edits through a fast-path lint runner for path-local changes, instrumentation hooks to surface lint/runtime telemetry, and a dependency-rotation adapter that automates a conservative rotation of devdeps on a scheduled cadence. Summary of changes and checklist: - introduce scripts/ci/presubmit-router.ts to detect change surface and pick fast lanes for lint/quick-tests - add .github/workflows/presubmit-fastpath.yml that runs an opt-in fast lint path for small PRs - add telemetry hooks (telemetry/lint-hooks.ts) that emit per-lint-run duration, cache-hit, and rule-count tags to our internal metrics sink - wire lightweight runner into existing presubmit dispatcher with safe fallbacks to the full presubmit pipeline - implement tools/dep-rotation/adapter that can generate candidate bump PRs for developer review and emit a compatibility report - update developer-contrib.md with new presubmit guidelines and examples - small packaging updates (package.json scripts, Makefile targets) - add a smoke harness for release pipelines to validate the presubmit router under a production-like event (tools/release-smoke/) Checklist: [x] Unit tests for presubmit-router logic [x] E2E smoke runner added and exercised locally [x] Telemetry schema reviewed with data-platform (ENG-2203) [x] Docs updated in contributor guidelines [x] Gradual rollout plan added in PR notes Testing notes: local unit tests, a small matrix of Node/Go test runners and an isolated CI run were executed. The integration job failed once on an unrelated docker image pull flake and was re-run; final CI green. Rollout plan: enable presubmit-fastpath as opt-in via repo label and progressively enable for low-risk repos. Fallback: presubmit-router falls back to main presubmit pipeline when any heuristics are ambiguous or when telemetry indicates a sustained error rate. Why distinct from previous work: previous PRs optimized CI caching and shard split; this focuses on routing logic, observability for lint fastpaths, and an automated yet conservative dependency rotation mechanism to reduce manual churn.
Owen Patel: Nice separation — can we guard the fastpath to only run for < 10-file diffs initially? Added a suggestion to the router heuristics.
Maya Chen (author): Good call — added a max-files threshold default to 8 and a repo opt-in label; preserved fallback behavior when threshold exceeded.
Ravi Singh: Telemetry looks useful; please add a metric for cache-hit-rate and ensure the emitted tags are stable (avoid high cardinality).
Maya Chen (author): Added cache_hit boolean and lint_rule_count integer tag; removed file-level tags to limit cardinality.
Elena Morales: dep-rotation PR generator is neat but make sure the adapter labels generated PRs with 'dep-rotation' and includes a human-readable compatibility summary. Also requested an explicit opt-out via .dep-rotate-ignore.
Maya Chen (author): Implemented label + compat-report and added .dep-rotate-ignore parsing.
Deployment/rollout: presubmit-fastpath is feature-flagged; operations will observe new telemetry (metric names: ci.presubmit.lint.duration, ci.presubmit.lint.cache_hit, ci.presubmit.lint.rule_count). The dep-rotation adapter is scheduled in staging for a two-week experiment; generated PRs are labelled and require human approval. Backout: remove the opt-in label to disable fastpath immediately. Monitoring: alerts added for >5% error rate or increased presubmit failure rate after rollout.
During CI run on 2026-02-20 an unrelated docker hub rate-limit caused a transient failure in the e2e-matrix job; we retried and added a retry wrapper around docker pulls in runner-wrapper.sh to reduce flakes.
Add lightweight presubmit routing to speed feedback; introduce telemetry hooks for lint fastpath; integrate a dependency rotation adapter to reduce monorepo churn.

Motivation: We observed subtle per-head scale drift when fusing dequant+attention kernels for mixed INT8/FP8 inference on long-context workloads. The drift reduces softmax stability and causes quality jitter at tail tokens, forcing either conservative dequant choices or pay-for-precision fallbacks. This PR introduces two coordinated changes: 1) an attenuated-scale drift correction pass in the quant fusion pipeline that applies a calibrated per-head attenuation and lightweight renormalization to preserve numeric stability when fusing dequant + attn; and 2) a KV-prefetch adapter that warms KV cache for fused fast-path microkernels to avoid cold-start p99 spikes during continuous batching and interactive patterns. Design: - attenuated_scale_pass: a compiler/pipeline pass that inserts a small per-head multiplicative correction (scale attenuation + bias adjust) when the fusion identifies asymmetric per-head ranges. The pass emits metadata so that runtime microkernels can choose a fast-path that avoids a full recompute of scales. The correction is designed to be idempotent and toggled via model config or per-route rollout flags. - requant microkernel (kernels/requant_vperm.S): adds a vectorized requantization path optimized for AVX-512/ARM SVE that uses lane-aligned vperm and fused mad instructions to reduce scalar renormalize ops. The kernel returns a compact scale tag consumed by the runtime. - kv_prefetch_adapter (scheduler/kv_prefetch_adapter.cc): a scheduler hook that observes continuous batch characteristics (steady-state token rate, active prefixes) and proactively issues lightweight KV fetches for expected upcoming prefixes using the model's prefix-hash hints. It is conservative (deadline-aware) and disabled for GPU memory-constrained pools. - runtime integration: runtime/quant/attenuated_scale_pass.cpp wires pass metadata through the model descriptor and runtime/runtime_kv_bridge picks fast-path kernels when metadata present. Rollout plan: 1) opt-in per-model by default off 2) staged canary on dedicated clusters 3) gradual rollout to hosted after 2 weeks of canary metrics Observed results (internal bench): - Llama-13B INT8-smoothed baseline vs this PR: p99 latency down ~18% on interactive traces, median latency up to 10% improved for short sequences, overall throughput +27% at 95th percentile load. - Token-level quality regression: negligible on our eval prompt set (<0.2% BLEU-like drift), with occasional alignment differences on adversarial prompts (added to eval set). Tests and QA: - unit tests for attenuated_scale_pass and microkernel correctness included. - end-to-end integration test simulates continuous batching + KV warmup. - bench/bench_quant_prefetch.py reproduces p99 improvements in CI perf job (internal). Checklist: - [x] Implementation of attenuated-scale pass and microkernel - [x] Scheduler KV-prefetch adapter - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Benchmarks and perf dashboards updated - [x] Docs note added (docs/notes/quant-prefetch.md) Security/compatibility notes: - No change to model weights. - New runtime metadata is backward compatible; fallback to existing dequant path if microkernel not available. - Feature guarded behind rollout flag. Related work: ENG-1289 (quant stability), ENG-1310 (kv cache p99), SUP-4421 (customer-reported cold-start p99 incident).
1) init: add attenuated_scale_pass pipeline and tests (Maya Chen)
2) kernel: add requant_vperm microkernel and arch tests (Oliver Park)
3) scheduler: kv_prefetch_adapter and config knobs (Samir Patel)
4) runtime: wire metadata and fast-path selection (Maya Chen)
5) docs: quant-prefetch notes and bench harness (Galina Petrova)
Oliver Park: Noted a potential misalignment on ARM SVE for odd lane counts; requested an AVX/SVE cross-arch smoke test.
Maya Chen: Added cross-arch smoke test and guarded the SVE path behind lane check; added comments.
Samir Patel: Asked for clearer rollout metrics and a kill-switch.
Maya Chen: Added metrics dashboard links in the PR body and an emergency config flag 'quant_drift.disable' in runtime config.
Galina Petrova: Reviewed docs and asked to include a short troubleshooting guide for customers seeing quality drift; author added docs/notes/quant-prefetch.md.
Oliver Park: Approves after small nit on comment formatting.
Samir Patel: Approves with perf numbers validated on dedicated canary cluster.
Add attenuated-scale drift-correction pass for quant fusion and KV-prefetch adapter to reduce cold-start p99; opt-in via model config. See docs/notes/quant-prefetch.md for rollout and troubleshooting.
Enable 'quant_drift.disable' in runtime config to revert to previous dequant path. Can be toggled per-deployment. Watch metrics: quant/attn/p99_latency and kv/prefetch/hit_rate.

Context: Production customers report noisy long-tail attribution for token-level cost and latency, especially when prompts cross KV-cache boundaries and when short auxiliary tokens dominate cost noise.
Motivation: provide a compact, indexable signal that (1) ties latency/cost to token affinity groups (e.g., system prompts, user prefix, user continuation, tool calls) and (2) produces a lightweight per-request signature that can be stored in traces and aggregated efficiently for dashboards and alerts.
This PR introduces two pieces: token-affinity meters (runtime instrumentation that tags token spans with an affinity label and local cost weight) and compact cost signatures (a fixed-size, base64-encoded summary included as a trace/log annotation).
Summary of changes:
- runtime: observability/metrics/token_affinity_meter.go: new meter to classify tokens into affinity buckets and emit per-span counters and reservoir samples.
- collector: observability/collector/compact_cost_signature.go: implements incremental signature builder (sketch + small histogram) and base64 encoder used in traces/logs.
- console: console/dashboards/token_affinity_dashboard.json: new dashboard with per-affinity P50/P95/P99 latency and cost share, plus a compact signature explorer.
- tracing: tracing/span_enrichers/affinity_enricher.go: attaches compact signature and affinity tags to sampling spans.
- alerts: observability/alerts/affinity_slo_rules.yaml: tuned alert thresholds to suppress high-cardinality noise via signature-based aggregation and reservoir sampling.
- docs: docs/observability/token-affinity.md: motivation, interpretation, and query examples.
- tests: tests/integration/test_token_affinity.py and tests/e2e/affinity_smoke.sh.
Checklist:
- [x] implementation and unit tests
- [x] integration tests (local)
- [x] perf microbench (see performance notes)
- [x] docs and dashboard JSON
- [x] feature-flag gated rollout plan
Rollout plan: gated behind feature flag REDWOOD_OBS_TOKEN_AFFINITY (default off). Staged rollout: enable in staging -> 10% of canary -> 50% -> 100% after 72h. Backout: disable flag and clear local reservoirs; signature format has version header for safe backcompat.
Testing & validation:
- unit tests for meter classification and signature encoding.
- integration test replays sample prompts (see tests/integration) and validates signature invariants (idempotence given identical tokenization and affinity rules).
- canary perf microbench: median CPU overhead ~0.6% at P99 request rate; memory delta ~3% per serving worker; p50 latency increase <1ms.
Observability consequences: compact signatures are small (32–48 bytes) and added to span tags and logs; ingestion cost increase estimated ~0.5% for traces. The collector compacts signatures again at ingestion to remove duplicates.
How to use (examples):
- Console: open "Token Affinity" dashboard and use the signature explorer to search recent 24h sessions by signature.
- Traces: filter by span.tag[affinity.signature]=="<base64>" to find sessions that share cost profile.
Related: ENG-4921 (long-tail attribution), ENG-4988 (kv-cache cross-boundary noise).
Links: internal doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4921; dashboard sample: console/dashboards/token_affinity_dashboard.json
Notes: this PR intentionally keeps affinity buckets coarse (system|prefix|continuation|tool|output) to limit cardinality. Future work: automatic bucket calibration, probabilistic prefix grouping, and integrating signature-based deduping into billing pipelines.
Ethan Park: Can we keep the affinity buckets configurable per-tenant? A: yes, buckets defined in config with sane defaults; note in docs.
Clara Mendez: Unit test coverage looks good; please add a spec for signature versioning. Aisha: added signature v1 header and tests in b78c9e1.
Jun-Woo Lee: Concerned about cardinality if we allow user-defined buckets. Request to add reservoir sampling to the meter. Aisha: implemented reservoir sampler and added integration test; see commit f2c1c8b.
payload.title: Introduce token-affinity meters and compact cost signatures for long-tail observability

Adds a stability layer to Dedicated autoscaler: adaptive warmup for warm pools, scale-down grace window, soft-throttle fallback to preserve throughput SLAs, and sampled per-tenant utilization telemetry. Config knobs are behind feature flag `stability_layer_v1`.
Motivation: we observed repeated throughput regressions during scale-down and cold-start cycles on Dedicated clusters when tenants with bursty patterns decommit suddenly. This PR introduces a 'stability layer' between the autoscaler and the provisioner that reduces oscillation and preserves throughput SLAs during capacity transitions. Key ideas: 1) adaptive warmup: when new cards are provisioned into a warm pool we incrementally ramp concurrency targets over a tunable warmup period derived from observed tail-latency and model sequence-length distribution; 2) decommit grace window: avoid hard deallocations within a tenant-specific hysteresis window computed from recent utilization decay rates; 3) soft-throttle fallback: on sudden capacity contraction we prefer temporary token-level concurrency throttles (per-tenant) and micro-shed before evictions to avoid large latency spikes; 4) sampled telemetry: lightweight reservoir sampling of per-tenant utilization sketches to feed the autoscaler and downstream billing/alerting without full-card telemetry costs. Implementation: adds a new autoscaler/stability package (stability_layer.go) that wraps existing decision logic, a warmup controller (pkg/provision/warmup.go) to drive progressive concurrency targets, changes to the provisioner API to accept soft-throttle hints, and new metrics and traces (stability_* metrics and warmup events). All behavior is gated behind the feature flag `stability_layer_v1` with a rollout plan described below. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-2389) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] perf bench and canary runs - [x] metrics + alerts - [x] docs for operator knobs - [x] feature-flagged rollout
Local perf lab: reduced 95th token latency spikes during scale-down by ~38% and end-to-end tail P95 for multi-tenant bench by 22%. Cost delta on steady-state traffic: +0.7% for warm pool retention at default settings; prevented two incidents in internal canary (estimated avoidance of ~1800 failed requests).
1) Enable `stability_layer_v1` in staging for 24h on a single fleet; 2) run synthetic burst generator for 48h and monitor stability.* metrics + p95 token latency; 3) Canary enable on 5% of Dedicated fleets with linked alerting (autoscaler-sla-deviation); 4) Gradually increase to 30% over 72h if no regressions; 5) Full rollout to Dedicated after 7d and retrospective tuning; rollback: toggle feature flag off and scale warm pools down via reclamation job.
Unit coverage: autoscaler/stability 87% branch coverage; integration: warmup path + soft-throttle adapter simulated across scaled-up clusters; e2e: canary harness verifies no >2x SLA breaches during forced decommit events. CI: all checks passed including lint, go-test, integration-suite, and canary-smoke.
Operators will get extra metrics and a new helm value group under `stabilityLayer.*`. Default values keep behavior off. Expected operator actions: tune warmup_target_fraction for high-burst tenants and set max_warm_age to control memory footprint.
This PR is intentionally conservative: core autoscaler heuristics are unchanged unless the feature flag is enabled. The stability layer exposes a small set of knobs designed for operators: max_warm_age, warmup_target_fraction, decommit_hysteresis_base, soft_throttle_floor. Immutable model-serving contracts were preserved; provisioner changes are additive and backward-compatible.
Diego: Can you clarify how the decommit grace window is calculated? Maya: The window is computed from an exponential smoother of per-tenant utilization slope; we default to max(30s, 3x smoothed decay half-life) and it is configurable. Lina: Is soft-throttle observable to users? Maya: Yes, we emit stability.soft_throttle.active and per-tenant throttled_tokens_count; operator docs added. Owen: Concern about billing/chargebacks—will sampled telemetry be sufficient? Maya: We deliberately keep full billing telemetry unchanged; sampled sketches are for autoscaler heuristics and can be turned off. Diego: Please add a safety limit to avoid indefinite warm pools. Maya: Added a configurable max_warm_age and an automated reclamation path in warmup.go. Lina: Tests look good, but add a canary rollout plan. Maya: Added rollout_plan in PR which includes staged canary and automated rollback on alert triggers. Owen: Approving after CI green.
ENG-2420 follow-up will add automatic knob tuning using a small MLE to set warmup length per-model family and add finer-grained per-card eviction scoring.

payload.body:
Summary: Introduces a multi-tier emergency credit bank and a sustained-minimum-throughput enforcer that together protect committed tenant throughput during multi-pool contention. Adds a lightweight KV-warmth correlator that ties KV-cache hit ratio and warm-pool occupancy to proactive warmlet pre-baking signals. This PR is gated behind the new 'tiered_credit' feature flag and the autoscaler 'min_throughput_enforcer' config.

Motivation and context: We continue to see incidents where short, high-amplitude bursts cause warm-pool churn and evictions that temporarily violate per-tenant throughput SLAs. Existing burst tokens are effective for transient events but do not cover scenarios where pool-level headroom is exhausted and warm-pool replenishment lags due to cold KV caches. This change implements a safety-first flow:
1) Tiered emergency credit: soft -> reserve -> emergency credits that are consumed in order. Emergency credits are a small, decaying buffer reserved for SLA preservation and are paid back on stable utilization periods.
2) Sustained-minimum-throughput enforcer: when a tenant has a defined committed throughput (reservation), the enforcer monitors short-window utilization and proactively reduces non-committed concurrency or routes best-effort requests to lower-cost model variants to preserve the committed floor.
3) KV-warmth correlator: lightweight telemetry aggregation that computes per-pool correlation between KV-cache hit ratio and warmlet warmup success. These correlations are used to adjust warm-pool pre-bake thresholds and prioritize tenants whose request prefixes show high cache sensitivity.

What changed (high level):
- Autoscaler: added TieredCreditBank (soft/reserve/emergency) and reconciler to decouple credit lifecycle from warm-pool allocator.
- Enforcer: new SustainedMinThroughputEnforcer module with admission filters and a pluggable fallback strategy interface (route to quantized model / queue / 429).
- Telemetry: KVWarmthCorrelator job, new telemetry fields (kv_cache_hit_ratio, warmlet_prebake_success_rate, emergency_credit_consumed) and a combined 'elasticity_safety_score' metric emitted for SLO dashboards.
- Tests/bench: unit tests, integration test harness simulating multi-tenant bursts across two pools, and a small perf benchmark measuring p50/p95 under synthetic cold-cache bursts.
- Config/API: new runtime config knobs under dedicated.autoscaler and dedicated.enforcer; admin console controls for tuning emergency credit budgets and canary toggles.

Commits (summary):
- feat(autoscaler): add TieredCreditBank and reconciliation loop
- feat(enforcer): introduce SustainedMinThroughputEnforcer and fallback strategy interface
- feat(telemetry): KVWarmthCorrelator and new telemetry exports
- test(integration): burst-sim harness + synthetic KV miss patterns
- docs: admin guide for configuring the enforcer and credit tiers
- chore: feature-flag gating + migration job for existing token pools

Changed areas / illustrative files:
- services/autoscaler/credit_bank.go
- services/autoscaler/credit_reconciler.go
- services/autoscaler/enforcer/min_throughput_enforcer.go
- services/telemetry/kv_warmth_correlator.go
- operators/helm/dedicated/values.yaml (new knobs)
- integrations/tests/burst_sim/README.md
- integrations/tests/burst_sim/run_bench.sh
- docs/dedicated/emergency-credit.md

Benchmarks & telemetry (before -> after, canary run across 10 medium tenants):
- p50 tail during sustained 120s burst: 28ms -> 26ms (7% improvement)
- p95 tail during same burst: 520ms -> 498ms (4% improvement)
- Incidence of cross-pool eviction leading to SLA drop (measured events per 100 bursts): 12 -> 3 (75% reduction in observed SLA violations in our synthetic harness)
- Emergency credit consumption rate (per-pool): median 0 -> small consumption during peak; credits decay to zero over 15m once headroom restored

Safety, rollout & migration:
- Feature-flagged as 'tiered_credit' + 'min_throughput_enforcer'. Default off for all customers.
- Canary rollout: 5% tenants (internal fleet) for 48h, then 20% for a week, then 100% if metrics stable.
- Backwards compatibility: defaults are conservative (small emergency bucket, enforcer uses queue/429 policy unless tenant opt-in for model fallback). Migration job converts existing burst-token pools to TieredCreditBank with equivalent soft/reserve sizes.
- Observability: new Grafana dashboards and an alert 'Dedicated: EmergencyCreditDepletion' when emergency credits remain >0 for >10m.

Risk and mitigations:
- Risk: overly aggressive enforcer could throttle legitimate traffic. Mitigation: canary gating, per-tenant dry-run mode, and explicit opt-in for model-variant fallback.
- Risk: incorrect correlation heuristics could bias warm-prebake. Mitigation: thresholds are learned with a 24h conservative smoothing window and require delta > 8% before changing pre-bake decisions.

Related work & tickets: Linear ENG-3421 (autoscaler roadmap), ENG-3520 (dedicated SLO incident follow-ups), SUP-789 (customer-reported sustained throughput drops). Also ties to warm-pool prioritizer RFC (internal).

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration harness updated
- [x] Benchmarks included
- [x] Docs updated
- [x] Feature flags added

Notes for reviewers: Focus review on the credit accounting math (credit_bank.go) and the admission path in min_throughput_enforcer.go. The correlator is intentionally low-frequency (30s bucket) to keep overhead minimal. For the fallback strategy, there is a simple default implementation; product has requested a follow-up to plumb tenant-level opt-in for fallback to quantized models.
Ethan Cole: Nice direction. Can you add a unit test covering credit decay edge cases?
Maya Singh: Added credit decay tests and a small table-driven test for multi-tier consumption (see credit_bank_test.go).
Lena García: We need clearer docs on knob ranges for operators. Can you add example values to helm values.yaml?
Maya Singh: Added examples and comments in operators/helm/dedicated/values.yaml. Kept defaults conservative.
Arjun Rao: CI flake in integration smoke test — reran and it passed. Approving pending one minor nits fix.
Maya Singh: Addressed nits (naming/variable comments). Ready to merge.

payload.body:
Motivation: Console, Optimize, telemetry attribution, and billing hooks currently compute “cost” with subtly different definitions (prefill vs decode splits, cache hit accounting, batching efficiency, overhead allocation). This PR introduces a single versioned schema package for Cost Model v1 so downstream callers and producers can converge on the same canonical inputs/outputs, with docs and conformance/serialization tests.

Scope (v1):
- Add a new versioned schema package: //packages/cost-model/schema/v1
- Define canonical request-level inputs (what we can know at request time) vs observed inputs (what runtime/telemetry provides post-hoc) and the canonical cost outputs used by Console/Optimize/finance.
- Provide stable field semantics and naming (aligned with cost breakdown taxonomy work), including “unknown/unavailable” handling.
- Add JSON serialization + round-trip tests and golden fixtures to prevent accidental wire-format drift.

Non-goals:
- Not implementing the Cost Model API service in this PR (handled in ENG-4821/PR-28457).
- Not replacing billing/RevRec; this package defines primitives that billing hooks can consume.

Versioning policy:
- v1 is additive-only for minor releases; any rename/removal requires new major schema version.
- Consumers must ignore unknown fields; producers must not change semantics of existing fields.
- Fields are tagged with stability notes and explicit unit/precision expectations.

Notes for reviewers:
- The schema is designed to support both synchronous request-path estimation and async aggregation. Some fields are marked “required for estimate” vs “required for reconciliation” (telemetry-backed).
- All currency is expressed in USD micros to avoid float ambiguity.
- Token counts are expressed as integers and split by stage (prefill/decode) with optional cached-token attribution.

Follow-ups:
- Wire runtime-exported KV cache metrics into ObservedInputs (ENG-4828).
- Ensure model catalog exposes stable quantization profile identifiers referenced by this schema (ENG-4829).

Docs:
- Schema docs live alongside types and are intended to be source-of-truth for Console/Optimize field semantics until Confluence pages are finalized.

Risk:
- Low runtime risk (types-only). Main risk is accidental churn; mitigated via golden serialization tests and CI checks.
Key schema concepts added in v1: (1) CostModelVersion: explicit version string required on all payloads. (2) DeploymentContext: hosted/dedicated/private + region + hardware_sku + capacity_tier. (3) ModelContext: model_id + model_version + quantization_profile_id + tokenizer_id. (4) RequestUsage: prompt_tokens/complete_tokens with required stage split (prefill_tokens, decode_tokens) and optional cached_token attribution. (5) RuntimeEfficiency: batch_size_effective, queue_time_ms, kv_cache_hit_rate (optional in v1; required once runtime instrumentation lands). (6) CostBreakdown: request_attributable vs overhead_allocated, each split by compute/memory/egress/other; overhead explicitly marked as policy-driven and time-windowed. (7) Confidence: optional confidence interval for estimate-only outputs to support Optimize “what-if” flows; defaults to unknown for observed/reconciled outputs.

The package intentionally avoids embedding product-specific concepts (Console chart buckets, Optimize recommendation IDs). Consumers should map from product concepts into these canonical fields.
Logan Wright: Can we clarify which fields are telemetry-backed vs caller-provided? Right now it reads like everything is required. Also, please call out the expected source of truth for token counts (metering vs runtime).
Ethan Park: Updated docs to tag each field with Source: caller | runtime | metering | finance-policy. Token counts: metering is canonical for billing/reporting; runtime is used for stage split when available (and must reconcile to metering totals within tolerance).
Chloe Martin: Console needs a stable, bounded breakdown for UI tables. Can we guarantee the set of breakdown keys is finite? Also would prefer enum values to match Console naming (prefill/decode).
Ethan Park: Added explicit enum for stages (PREFILL/DECODE) and constrained breakdown categories to a fixed taxonomy. Also documented that per-request breakdown returns a bounded list (no arbitrary tag explosion) and that any additional segmentation happens via aggregation endpoints in the service layer.
Aditya Rao: For Optimize, we need to represent uncertainty for what-if estimates, but it can’t leak into “observed” cost. Can we keep confidence fields optional and clearly scoped?
Ethan Park: Done. Confidence is only valid when output.kind == ESTIMATE (not OBSERVED/RECONCILED). Added validation enforcing that.
Allison Grant: Please align errors/validation wording with internal API standards. Also add a note about ignoring unknown fields for forward compatibility.
Ethan Park: Added compatibility notes and validation guidance; also included a short section in schema/README about forward/backward compatibility expectations.
Sofia Ivanova: batch_size_effective needs a definition (mean over decode? per scheduling window?). Otherwise runtime can’t implement consistently.
Ethan Park: Added precise definition: effective_batch_size is the average concurrent sequences during decode, weighted by decode tokens, over the request lifetime. Also added a placeholder for a future field to capture scheduling window granularity (v2 candidate).
Nadia Rahman: One nit: currency micros should be int64, not number in TS to avoid precision issues. Also ensure JSON uses string encoding if needed.
Ethan Park: In TS we represent micros as string to avoid precision loss; docs updated and golden fixtures now encode micros as strings. Validation enforces digits-only strings.
Elliot Price: Docs are good but please add one end-to-end example payload for Console and one for Optimize so teams don’t guess.
Ethan Park: Added two examples under src/examples with commentary and referenced them from README.
Final review: All requested changes addressed. Approved.
Internal-only: Introduces versioned Cost Model schema package v1 for use by Cost Model API service, Console cost breakdown, Optimize ROI modeling, telemetry attribution, and billing hooks. No customer-facing changes in this PR.
Consumers should import from packages/cost-model/schema/v1 and include cost_model_version on all payloads. Do not import from the unversioned packages/cost-model/schema root except for shared tooling. Unknown fields must be ignored to allow forward-compat evolution. Currency micros are strings in JSON; do not parse into JS number.

payload.body:
Motivation: We saw a recurring pattern where partial-region capacity pressure caused abrupt circuit flips and large simultaneous failovers that violated customer latency SLOs. Existing load-shedding is binary per-node and the circuit reset probe is too aggressive, causing oscillation during transient overloads. This hotpatch introduces a "drip-throttle" controller that gracefully sheds traffic in small increments per-region with weighted circuit states to prioritize traffic according to region health and customer tiers.

Design summary: 1) RegionalDripController (traffic-router): periodically computes a small shed fraction for each region based on recent 95th/99th latency and error rate windows; 2) WeightedCircuitState: circuits are no longer binary open/closed—each circuit has a weight (0..1) and a probabilistic probe path that incrementally increases allowed traffic if probes pass; 3) Sticky cooldown and decay: weight increases/decreases use asymmetric time constants to avoid oscillation; 4) Telemetry: new metrics and tags (drip_fraction, circuit_weight, probe_rate, region_priority) and tracing annotations for decision points; 5) Config: degradation policy schema extended with per-region priority and default weights for dedicated vs hosted customers.

What changed (high level files): services/traffic-router/controller/drip_throttle.go - new controller and core algorithm; services/traffic-router/circuit/weighted_state.go - state machine and probe logic; config/schemas/degradation.yaml - new fields for per-region priority and defaults; telemetry/metrics.yaml - new metric definitions and dashboards; tests/e2e/drip_throttle_sim.go - simulation harness used for canary validation; docs/ops/degradation-runbook.md - updated runbook and rollback steps; services/traffic-router/handler/routing_middleware.go - hook to consult controller decision.

Checklist (what I did): [x] unit tests for controller logic and state machine [x] simulation harness with synthetic spike patterns [x] added metrics and dashboards for canary observation [x] instrumentation to tag traces with decisions [x] rollout plan and rollback steps in runbook [x] coordinated canary in us-west-2 for 2 hours then gradual rollout across other regions

Testing and results: Local unit tests and the e2e simulation show substantially lower tail latency and fewer full-circuit flips in scenarios with partial-region CPU pressure. Sim results: under a 30% sustained traffic spike to a subset of hosts, full-circuit count fell by ~78% compared to baseline and 99p latency improved by ~18%. The CI initially failed due to a race in probe cleanup; fixed in commit d2b8f7a and re-run.

Review conversation (abridged): - Maya Patel (review): "Can we avoid adding another periodic goroutine per region? That was causing flakiness in previous controllers." -- Noah: "Implemented a single reconciler tick with per-region state update to avoid goroutine explosion; added a stress test to ensure no drift." - Liam O'Connor (review): "Metrics look good; add an event when circuit_weight crosses 0.8/0.2 boundaries to aid alerting." -- Noah: "Added 'circuit_weight_transition' event and dashboard annotation in telemetry config." - Sofia Ivanov (review): "The default probe cadence seems high for low-tier customers." -- Noah: "Introduced tiered defaults and made them configurable; low-tier defaults have lower probe_rate and longer cooldowns."

CI summary: - Unit tests: initially failed (race in probe cleanup), fixed in second commit and passed. - Linters: minor formatting warnings fixed in commits. - Integration e2e (staging): passed in canary region with synthetic load.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main as hotpatch (squash) 2) Deploy to canary region (us-west-2) behind traffic ramp for 2h while monitoring metrics and SLOs 3) If stable, rollout to mid-tier regions over 24h with automated health checks and auto-rollback on >1% SLO breach 4) Full global rollout after 48h of stable metrics

Rollback: The runbook includes immediate configuration toggle to disable drip controller (degradation.policy.enabled=false) and an automated reversion to prior defaults. Documented manual steps for emergency rollback if needed.

Merge outcome: Approved by Maya Patel and Liam O'Connor after fixes; merged via squash. Post-merge actions: created alert to watch 'drip_fraction' > 0.25 sustained for >15m and a dashboard tile for circuit_weight transitions.

Notes: This PR is intentionally conservative in the control loop to avoid overreaction. Future follow-ups: - take probe success rate into account to accelerate recovery for high-confidence probes - integrate with Dedicated capacity signals to remove shed fraction for reserved nodes - add per-customer override API for escalation during incidents

Hotpatch: introduce regional drip-throttle controller with weighted circuit-state probing and revised defaults to reduce SLO spikes during partial-region overloads. Rollout: canary -> gradual global.
Canary run completed 2026-02-20 us-west-2. No customer-facing incidents tied to this deploy. Observability tags added to support faster triage.
payload.title: Regional drip-throttle with weighted circuit states (hotpatch)

payload.body:
Motivation: customers with mixed-region deployments required deterministic KMS routing while preserving auditable, append-only commitments for cross-region fallback. This PR introduces a lightweight per-tenant residency assertor, an operator-configurable KMS operator allowlist, and an "audit commitment gateway" that signs short commitment records for any request that is routed off-region or to a fallback key.

What it does: Adds a residency assertor that derives a tenant region preference from (in order) tenant metadata, residency claim headers, and recent routing history (sticky hints). When explicit tenancy region is missing, the assertor emits a deterministic candidate list rather than a single decision to enable safe canary rollouts. KMS selection now consults an allowlist and a staged preference table; if the chosen KMS is outside the tenant's pinned region, the request is annotated and forwarded through the audit commitment gateway, which atomically records a signed commitment (SHA256 -> operator KMS sign) and returns a short commitment id that is stored in the request audit trail.

Rollout plan: feature is gated behind feature flag "residency_assertor_v1" with three rollout modes: disabled, observe-only (assertions emitted to audit but not enforced), and enforce. We will start in observe-only across a small percentage of traffic, then flip to enforce for specific enterprise tenants. Backwards compatible: if not enabled, runtime behavior is unchanged.

Configuration: new Helm values documented under deploy/helm/redwood-private/values-residency.yaml. Operators can configure: operator_kms_allowlist (ARNs), fallback_policy (prefer-nearest|prefer-cost|consent-first), commit_signer_key (service principal), and audit_holdback_window_seconds (short buffer window used by commitment gateway for transient redaction requests).

Security and compliance notes: commitments are signed by a dedicated signing key stored in the operator KMS; commitments include a compact mutation-proof vector (timestamp + request-hash + origin-region) to support later non-repudiable verification. Audit-forwarder retains commitment IDs and can fetch the signed commitment for external compliance queries. Access to the commitment verification endpoint is RBAC-protected via a new v2 policy template.

Testing and validation: added unit tests for deterministic candidate ordering, a simulation harness to exercise cross-region fallback under random failure, and an integration test that verifies the signed commitment roundtrip against the operator KMS emulator. Performance overhead measured at ~0.6ms median added latency in observe-only mode, 1.8ms in enforce mode for off-region fallbacks.

Migration / Operational guidance: operators should seed operator_kms_allowlist before enabling enforce mode; enable observe-only for 72 hours and review audit commitments using the console (Audit -> Commitments view). We include a small migration script to backfill missing residency hints from a 30-day routing history.

Related: Linked Linear ENG-4123 (residency policy), PM-982 (enterprise residency product work). Addresses support ticket SUP-2345 about inconsistent KMS selection for EU-regulated tenants.
Arjun: Requested a clearer failure mode when the commit signer is unavailable; asked to add metrics for commit gateway failures.
Author(Maya): Added an exponential backoff and a new metric audit.commitments.failures, documented behavior in the helm values.
Lucia: Asked for RBAC policy language to limit access to the verification endpoint to tenant-auditors only; requested unit test for policy generation.
Author: Added commitment_verifier_policy.yaml and unit tests.
Samir: Performed load testing and asked to gate the signing call with a sampled sampling rate for high-traffic tenants; author added a sampling config with conservative defaults.
Final: All reviewers approved, security review signed off pending key-rotation guidance added to docs.
- Introduce Residency Assertor for deterministic tenant-region recommendations.
- Add Audit Commitment Gateway for signed, non-repudiable records when requests are routed off-region.
- New operator KMS allowlist and selection policy.
- Helm values for residency and migration backfill script.

Operators: enable via feature flag residency_assertor_v1 and follow the observe-only rollout documented in docs/security/kms-residency.md.

payload.body:
Hotfix: add soft pause window and connection hedging to mitigate mass reconnect storms after regional failovers. Improves stability and reduces downstream KV pressure; no API changes.
Context: During the 2026-02-03 regional incident we observed amplified reconnect churn when standby regions were promoted and clients re-established connections in tight bursts. That churn caused spiky KV cache pressure and transient SLO violations. This PR introduces a server-side soft-pause window and a preemptive connection-hedge to smooth reconnection patterns, tie reconnection admission to SLO pressure signals, and preserve sticky KV leases during graceful failover. Design: 1) soft_pause_window: a tunable short-duration window (default 3s) applied to nodes that are rejoining after failover; new connections are staggered using jittered backoff buckets to avoid synchronized storms. 2) connection_hedge_agent: the agent monitors SLO proxies (latency quantiles, token pressure, kv_write_latency) and reduces concurrent reconnection admission when metrics indicate stressed state; this is implemented as a leaky-bucket admission with a short warmup ramp. 3) sticky_lease_escape: an escape hatch that delays lease revocations by a configurable grace if the remote region reports “failover_in_progress”, helping KV-preserve important prefixes. 4) telemetry and tracing: new metrics (soft_pause_applied_total, reconnect_admit_rate, kv_lease_delayed_total) and a span annotation added to reconnect traces so we can correlate reconnection decisions with downstream KV latency spikes. 5) config and rollout: feature gated under redwood.features.soft_pause (off by default for Dedicated/Private) and a transient rollout schedule: enable in canary for 10% of regional failovers for 24h, then 50%, then full. Motivation: smoothing reconnects reduces tail latency and prevents cascade failures in backend caches without requiring client changes. Backwards-compatibility: no API changes; behavior only differs when redwood.features.soft_pause is enabled. Hotfix rationale: the change is small, localized, and addresses a severe recurrence vector that caused customer-visible SLO regressions. Testing: unit tests for admission/leaky-bucket logic, an integration scenario in the canary harness that simulates mass reconnects, and load tests demonstrating 3x reduction in reconnect storm peak. Rollout notes: monitor soft_pause_applied_total and reconnect_admit_rate and kv write latency (p99). If reconnect_admit_rate drops too low for sustained periods, the agent will auto-relax after a configurable cooldown. Related: ENG-4829 documents incident postmortem and SRE-231 is the follow-up for automating safe rollouts.
Marco Chen (reviewer): Can we make the default window conservative (2-3s) and ensure per-tenant overrides? Reply: Agreed; default is 3s and we added per-tenant override via config. Updated code accordingly.
Priya Desai (reviewer): How does this interact with current KV lease expiration? Could we cause sticky leases to remain too long? Reply: We added sticky_lease_escape that only delays lease revocation when the remote node reports failover_in_progress and only up to a bounded 30s; also added metric kv_lease_delayed_total and alerting guidance.
Lucas Emery (reviewer): CI flaky test observed earlier when simulating reconnections under TLS; did you validate certificate handshake path? Reply: Fixed test harness to reuse certs and added an explicit TLS warmup path in the integration test. CI passes now.
QA (automation): Found a throttling regression on micro VMs at high concurrency in the first iteration; author: reduced token bucket granularity and added warmup ramp; new benchmarks show no regression.
SRE (post-review): Request to limit the initial canary to regions with low customer criticality; author: added canary region selector in deploy patch and rollout plan in docs.
All CI checks passed after two iterations. Unit suite: pass. Integration reconnect harness: pass. Load benchmarks: pass (see artifacts). Lint: pass. Flaky test discovered and fixed in PR iteration 2.
When enabling in production, set redwood.features.soft_pause=false initially. Enable in a single low-traffic region for 1 hour, watch soft_pause_applied_total and reconnect_admit_rate. If kv write latency p99 improves and reconnect_admit_rate does not drop below expected thresholds, expand canary. Emergency rollback: set redwood.features.soft_pause=false and trigger rolling restart of serving pods to clear any in-flight bucketing state.
Create a dashboard tile for reconnect_admit_rate and kv_lease_delayed_total
Add alerts: reconnect_admit_rate < baseline for >10m, kv_lease_delayed_total spike > threshold
Schedule follow-up to add client-visible backoff hints in SDKs (tracking ENG-4902)
payload.title: Introduce soft-pause-window and connection-hedge to prevent mass-reconnect storms

payload.body:
Motivation: During a recent soft-surge incident we observed noisy-tenants causing large transient backpressure that led to cascading latency increases across regional pools. This PR introduces a lightweight tenant-level "ballast" (localized quarantine) plus a priority shepherd that gently redirects best-effort traffic into a slowpath pool instead of applying blunt, global SLO relaxations. Goals: 1) contain noisy tenants quickly with minimal collateral impact; 2) preserve strict SLOs for high-priority tenants; 3) enable safe, observable rollouts via a small config surface and feature flag.

What this changes (single-line checklist and summary): - Adds tenant ballast controller that marks tenant sessions as quarantined when local latency and token backlog exceed adaptive thresholds. - Introduces priority shepherd that classifies requests into strict/standard/slowpath and routes them to pre-provisioned fast and slow execution lanes. - Soft-quarantine eviction policy that de-escalates based on moving-window health metrics (no hard tenant disable). - Metrics/tags and new tracing span for tenant-quarantine lifecycles, including reasons and duration. - Admin endpoints to list active quarantines and to manually lift quarantines for debugging.

Implementation notes: The controller runs inside the routing plane (router/service) and subscribes to per-spot latency histograms and in-flight token counters. Thresholds are computed per-tenant using an EWMA of 1m/5m windows with a safety multipler derived from tenant SLA tier. When a tenant crosses the soft-surge boundary, we mark their sessions with quarantine=true and route new requests into the slowpath pool. Existing in-flight requests are allowed to complete to avoid amplification. Quarantine entries are time-boxed and decay through a penalty-decay factor; repeated violations increase decay length (exponential backoff) but never exceed configured hard limit.

Risk and mitigation: The slowpath uses cheaper quantized model variants to reduce cost. To avoid quality regressions we enforce a per-tenant "canary token budget" — a small fraction of requests may still be served via the fast lane for continuous quality checks. The feature is gated behind a runtime flag and rollout is gradual (10% of tenants first, then ramp). Ops runbook added describing emergency rollback (gate=false) and manual quarantine lifting.

Checklist (completed): - [x] Controller logic and adaptive thresholding implemented - [x] Router routing table changes + slowpath pool wiring - [x] Metric and tracing instrumentation - [x] Unit + integration tests for routing decisions - [x] End-to-end staging canary run

Checklist (follow-ups after merge): - [ ] Add dashboard panels for quarantine churn per-region - [ ] Add automated alert for quarantine storm (more than N active quarantines in window) - [ ] Progressive rollout to Dedicated pools (next sprint)

Commits summary: - feat(quarantine): initial ballast controller and config schema - feat(router): attach priority shepherd and slowpath routing - perf: tighten slowpath model selection and batching defaults - test: integration tests for quarantine lifecycle - docs: runbook and config docs

Changed areas (high level): - router/service/router_quarantine.go - controller/tenant_ballast.go - services/slowpath_pool_manager.go - metrics/observability_quarantine.md - tests/integration/quarantine_lifecycle_test.go - ops/runbooks/quarantine-runbook.md - proto/routing.proto (small additions)

CI and validation: All unit and integration suites passed in CI; load tests run in the benchmark-lab staging cluster showed a 62% reduction in cross-tenant latency amplification during injected noisy-tenant scenarios. No regressions in existing latency SLOs for strict-tier tenants.

Merge notes: Squash-merged after address of reviewer comments; feature left behind runtime flag feature.quarantine.tenant_ballast=false by default for safe rollout.
Diego Alvarez: Nice approach. Please add a unit test for the EWMA threshold computation (edge cases: zero requests and burst reset).
Asha Menon (author): Added tests and adjusted the EWMA reset to use a min-weight floor. PTAL.
Kai Thompson: Can we expose a debug-only endpoint to list current quarantines with reasons? Ops will need it for incident triage.
Asha Menon: Added ops endpoint at /internal/quarantines and limited it to admin tokens. Documented in runbook.
Priya Nair: Approve after CI passes. Minor nit on naming in routing.proto.
Asha Menon: Addressed proto naming nit and rebased on latest main.
Introduces tenant-level soft quarantine and priority routing to limit cross-tenant amplification during soft surges. Administrators can monitor and lift quarantines via an ops endpoint. Rollout is behind a runtime flag. Recommended: enable in staging and monitor quarantine churn dashboards before enabling on production.
If quarantine storms are observed (many tenants quarantined quickly), set feature.quarantine.tenant_ballast=false to disable and investigate with /internal/quarantines output. Use runbook to lift stuck quarantines.
payload.title: Localized quarantine + priority shepherd for soft-surge events (tenant-level ballast)

payload.body:
Motivation: Long-tail noisy invocations and cross-tenant log flood make signal extraction for SLOs and cost attribution brittle. This change introduces two complementary observability primitives: 1) Invocation Fusion Metrics: runtime-side micro-aggregation that emits a compact per-invocation fingerprint and phased token emission histograms to attribute latency/cost across model stages without sampling every token. 2) Labeled-Log Tracer: a log enrichment path that attaches stable invocation labels (fingerprint, callsite-hash, model-variant-shadow id) to sampled log lines and spans to enable deterministic joins in dashboards. Goals: reduce cardinality explosion in dashboards, make alerting resilient to noisy tenants, and provide a low-cost way to reconstruct token-level latency/cost slices for investigation. What changed: - Serving runtime: add an optional InvocationFusion aggregator that computes a 128-bit fingerprint, per-phase token counts, and micro-latency sketches emitted as prometheus histograms and compact OTLP spans. The aggregator runs inline with request lifecycle but is gated by a config flag and budgeted CPU. - Tracing/logging: new labeled-log-tracer component that enriches existing span/log exporters with the fusion metadata and a tenant-stable short-id to allow cross-system joins. Added sampling filter to prioritize high-cost or anomalous invocations. - Telemetry pipeline: metrics mapping that turns fusion sketches into percentile rollups and a new downstream job that reconstructs token-latency deciles for dashboards without ingesting raw token traces. - Dashboards and alerts: a new dashboard (Invocation Fusion Explorer) with panels for per-phase token histograms, fusion fingerprint heatmap, tenant-noise quotient, and a cost-attribution panel. Alert dampening: introduce adaptive alert suppression rules that lower sensitivity for tenants with transient high-entropy fingerprints and escalate when consistent cost regressions are observed. - Tests and docs: unit and integration tests for the fusion aggregator, e2e smoke in the telemetry test harness, user-facing docs in observability guides, and a migration note for console users. Rollout plan: 1) Feature gated off by default; enable for internal staging traffic for 2 weeks. 2) Enable in canary for infra and platform tenants with metrics-only mode (no log enrichment) to evaluate overhead. 3) Gradually enable labeled-log-tracer for tenants that opt-in. Related work: builds on ENG-2098 (invocation summarizers) and SRE-121 alerting revamp. Notable constraints: we limit CPU budget per worker (default 0.5% of core) and cap emitted histogram cardinality to avoid increasing cardinality on prometheus. Observability cost: small increase in span metadata size but large downstream savings because token traces are sampled far less frequently. TODO/checklist: - [x] runtime aggregator implementation - [x] tracer enrichment and exporter adapters - [x] mapping job to flatten sketches into dashboards - [x] dashboard panels and runbooks - [x] unit/integration/e2e tests - [x] migration docs and opt-in controls
Aisha Raman: Can we quantify CPU and latency tail impact for p99 under 1000rps during the canary? Diego Marquez: Added a microbench in tests/integration and a benchmark summary in the PR description; expected p99 +0.8ms on our c5g-like instances with default budget. Jonas Pritchard: Need to make sure prometheus cardinality is bounded if many tenants opt in; consider a hashed short-id bucketization. Diego Marquez: Implemented tenant-stable short-id with 256 buckets and added a config knob to limit histogram labels. Jonas Pritchard: Also add a circuit-breaker to disable fusion if CPU budget exceeded. Diego Marquez: Added circuit-breaker and simulated overload tests. Marta Li: Minor nits on telemetry mapping job logging; please add more metrics around failed sketch decodes. Diego Marquez: Added failure counters and retries. Marta Li: Approving after changes. CI: initial telemetry integration job failed on sketch flattener (parsing edge case), reran after fix and all checks passed. Merge: squash and merge after approvals, perform a staggered canary rollout following playbook.
New: Invocation Fusion Metrics (compact per-invocation fingerprints and per-phase token histograms) and Labeled-Log Tracer for deterministic join keys in dashboards. Note: Feature is gated and opt-in; follow rollout runbook. Impact: small runtime CPU budget; reduces downstream trace ingestion needs and improves alert precision.
This PR intentionally keeps fusion sketches compact and introduces config flags for tenants to opt-in to labeled logs. Operators should monitor fusion_cpu_overruns and sketch_decode_failures when enabling for new tenants.
payload.title: Add invocation fusion metrics and labeled-log tracer with adaptive alert dampening

payload.body:
Context: Dedicated Burst capacity is rolling out behind guardrails and we need deterministic gating + a fast rollback path that does not depend on code deploys. This PR introduces feature flags and a global kill switch for burst admission, plus safe defaults for all existing/new tenants. Summary of changes: (1) Feature flags: adds a policy-evaluated boolean `burst_enabled` gate that must be true before routing/gateway can request burst capacity, and a separate `burst_admission_enabled` gate on the admission controller side (defense-in-depth). (2) Emergency kill switch: adds `burst_global_kill_switch` which, when flipped, forces all burst admission decisions to DENY with a consistent denial reason code and a short TTL cache to avoid thundering herds during an incident. (3) Region/hardware allowlist: adds a rollout allowlist (`burst_allowed_regions`, `burst_allowed_hw_classes`) to constrain burst to specific fleet pools while we ramp capacity. (4) Safe defaults: for all tenants (including new tenants) burst is disabled unless explicitly enabled via tenant config; for new regions/hw the default is deny until added to allowlist. (5) Observability hooks: emits a metric + structured log for kill-switch denies and includes a flag snapshot in admission decision traces (redacted). Behavior/semantics: a request is eligible for burst only if (a) tenant has burst enabled in tenant config AND (b) region/hw is allowlisted AND (c) global kill switch is off AND (d) admission controller feature flag is enabled. If any gate fails, we return an immediate deny (no queuing) with reason codes: `BURST_DISABLED_TENANT`, `BURST_DISABLED_REGION`, `BURST_DISABLED_HW_CLASS`, or `BURST_DISABLED_GLOBAL`. Notes: reason codes align with pr-23795 so Support/CS can explain denials; kill switch deny is intentionally fast and does not consult telemetry/fairness to keep incident behavior predictable. Testing: unit tests for policy evaluation + precedence, integration tests for routing path honoring deny reasons, and a manual runbook step validated in staging (flip kill switch and verify denial propagation within <60s). Rollout plan: ship behind internal-only flag, enable in staging, then dogfood `us-east/H100` allowlist before beta tenants. Follow-ups: (a) wire kill switch flips into oncall tooling + incident templates, (b) add alert annotations linking to runbook, (c) docs for customers on expected 429/retry behavior when burst is denied.
Jordan Lee: Can we confirm precedence? I want global kill switch to override everything, regardless of tenant config. Also please ensure determinism under telemetry lag (no telemetry reads when kill switch is on).
Benji Okafor (author): Yep — kill switch short-circuits before telemetry/fairness. Added tests for precedence order and ensured the handler returns before fetching telemetry snapshots.
Sean Gallagher: From an oncall standpoint, need a single switch we can flip during an incident and a metric that clearly indicates kill switch is active + the volume of denied burst attempts.
Benji Okafor (author): Added `burst_kill_switch_active{region,hw}` gauge and `burst_denied_total{reason}` counter. Also added structured log field `gating_reason` so incident searches are easy.
Mina Haddad: Routing needs to treat BURST_DISABLED_* as a hard deny and avoid retry loops. Do we have guidance on TTL/backoff so clients don’t hammer admission?
Benji Okafor (author): Routing path now treats these as terminal denials (no internal retry). The deny response includes a `retry_after_ms` hint (set to 1000ms on kill switch denies, 0 otherwise).
Keiko Yamamoto: Default allowlist should be empty for new regions/hw until Fleet provisions a pool. Please don’t accidentally enable burst on new SKUs via shared defaults.
Benji Okafor (author): Confirmed defaults: empty allowlist; deny by default. Added a comment + a regression test in defaults.yaml.
Ethan Park: Please add validation that tenant-level burst enablement cannot be set if global allowlist does not include the tenant’s region/hw (we can warn but should not hard fail).
Benji Okafor (author): Implemented a non-blocking validation warning (audit log + console warning) but allows config to be set ahead of capacity provisioning.
Dedicated: Burst capacity can now be gated per-tenant and per-region/hardware via feature flags.
SRE: Added a global burst kill switch for fast rollback and safer incident response.
Observability: New metrics/log fields to distinguish burst denies due to gating vs capacity/fairness.
payload.title: Add feature flags + emergency kill switch for Dedicated Burst capacity

Context: SDK users repeatedly requested parity between Python/TS/Go for auth handshakes and a simpler async-iterator surface for streaming. This PR extracts the transport-specific bits out of the middleware and exposes a small, well-tested adapter surface that SDKs can implement per-platform. Motivation: reduce duplicated logic across SDKs, make reauth behavior testable in isolation, and provide a minimal async generator 'sugar' that covers 90% of streaming use-cases with clear backpressure semantics. Summary of changes: extract AuthAdapter interface (transport-agnostic); introduce ReauthPolicy decorators that are composition-friendly; implement thin adapters for HTTP (TS), aiohttp/requests bridge (Py), and net/http (Go); add a MinimalGenerator facade in each SDK that wraps streaming responses into an ergonomic async generator/async iterable; unbundle the default retry decorator from the transport so users can opt-in or provide custom retry policies. Migration: default behavior remains unchanged for existing consumers; library authors who relied on internal middleware should switch to the adapter API (migration guide at docs/migration/auth-middleware.md). Checklist: - [x] Extracted interface and moved shared logic into sdk-common package; - [x] Implemented per-SDK adapters (py/ts/go) with parity tests; - [x] Added migration doc and examples; - [x] End-to-end smoke tests on CI and internal staging. Performance/regressions: end-to-end latency for small streaming sessions improved by ~6% on average due to reduced overhead in Python and TS paths; Go unchanged. Security: no change to auth token handling; adapters still call the same token provider hooks. Backwards compatibility: default exports and high-level client surface are preserved; advanced users can opt into adapter wiring. Commits summary and rationale provided below.
Adds transport-agnostic auth adapters and lightweight async generator facades for Python/TypeScript/Go; includes migration guide and default retry decorator unbundling; no breaking API surface changes for typical customers.
Ethan Cole: Can we keep the old middleware exported under a deprecated name for one release? (asked 2025-11-05)
Priya Nair: Yes — added deprecated shim in sdk/python/redwood/auth/compat.py and documented removal plan in the migration guide (reply 2025-11-06)
Marta Ruiz: The retry decorator unbundling is nice; can we add a short example showing how to attach a token-rotation-aware retry policy? (asked 2025-11-07)
Priya Nair: Added sample in docs and a unit test that simulates token expiry + background refresh (reply 2025-11-08)
Liam Zhao: Minor nit: TS generator's close handling should forward underlying socket close errors — added a suggestion (asked 2025-11-08)
Priya Nair: Addressed in a follow-up commit that tightens resource cleanup and adds a test (reply 2025-11-09)
Follow-up tasks: 1) track removal of deprecated shims in one minor release; 2) land performance micro-optimizations for the TS path (see TODO in minimalGenerator.ts); 3) coordinate a docs announcement and changelog entry. See linked Linear tasks for rollout plan.
Python adapter usage: client = Redwood(auth_adapter=MyAdapter()); async for chunk in client.stream(...): handle(chunk) -- TypeScript: const gen = minimalGenerator(client.stream()); for await (const c of gen) { /* ... */ } -- Go: gen := stream.NewGenerator(resp.Body); for gen.Next() { process(gen.Value()) }
payload.title: Refactor auth middleware into transport-agnostic adapters and sugar iterables
