Motivation: CI runtime and noise from multiple lint runners has increased feedback time. We want a single orchestrated action that runs language-specific linters in a predictable order, supports incremental linting based on changed files, and exposes a local fastpath. Additionally, large test suites are expensive; this PR adds an incremental test selector which picks affected tests using git diff + a small test-ownership map to run a smaller subset on pull requests (with a full test gate on release branches).

What this PR does:
- Adds .github/actions/lint-orchestrator: a composite action that sequences ruff/flake8 (Python), eslint/tsc (TypeScript), golangci-lint (Go), and pre-commit hooks. The action supports an INPUT_CHANGED_ONLY flag to limit linters to modified files.
- Introduces tools/test-selector/select-tests.py: a lightweight selector that maps changed files to test suites (pytest, jest, go test). It uses simple YAML ownership rules and falls back to full-test when uncertain.
- Updates CI workflows to use lint-orchestrator and a new staged test lane (fastpath for incremental tests, full for release).
- Pins linter versions and bump automation: golangci-lint -> v1.59.0, ruff -> 0.20.0, eslint -> 8.44.0; adds a compatibility shim in .github/actions/lint-orchestrator to surface version mismatches.
- Adds README-ci.md documenting local fastpath and how to run the selector locally.

Checklist:
- [x] Design: ENG-2412 
- [x] Implement composite action and selector
- [x] Update CI workflows and add staged lanes
- [x] Docs for local developer flow
- [x] Manual verification on a small set of PRs

Testing & verification summary:
- Ran lint-orchestrator in sandbox -> initially failed due to ruff minor API change; pinned ruff to 0.20.0 and re-ran.
- Fastpath CI lane ran on this PR: test selector chose 12 of ~3500 tests (~0.3%); all passed.
- Full test lane (release-main) remains unchanged and gated.

Backward compatibility & rollout:
- Default behavior of workflows is unchanged (full lint + full tests) unless repo-level flag fastpath-enabled=true is set for the branch or PR. We staged rollout by enabling fastpath for contributor teams and monitoring flaky rate for 48h.

Follow-ups planned:
- Expand ownership map across more packages (ENG-2468).
- Add telemetry to measure selector precision/recall and CI time savings.

Changed files (high level):

- .github/actions/lint-orchestrator/entrypoint.sh

Notes on design choices:
- Composite action: chosen over separate workflows so we can gate and centralize linting policies and report aggregated status. This also simplifies local invocation (act or local runner).
- Selector: intentionally conservative. If selector is unsure, it signals full-test to avoid regressions. Ownership map editable by teams; we included a small default mapping for core packages.

Security considerations:
- Linter pins avoid surprise behavior from upstream. Composite action validates versions and fails fast if runner images are out-of-date.

Rollout record:

- 2026-02-18: observed 42% median CI time reduction for fastpath runs, 0.3% increase in flaky detection (investigating)

Context: Some production rollouts require a human review gate when model changes touch high-risk paths (financial scoring, content filtering, PII transforms). Automated canaries and metric gates are necessary but not always sufficient when subtle distributional or failure-mode regressions appear. This PR implements a human-latchable canary flow that captures a replayable, compact snapshot of the traffic slice used for the canary, surfaces an inspection UI in the Console, and provides explicit accept/reject actions that can be recorded as part of the rollout decision. Motivation: give on-call/product owners a reproducible artifact (traffic snapshot + metadata + lightweight deterministic replay) so they can inspect model outputs offline, reproduce failure cases locally, and make a defensible, auditable manual decision without rolling back or keeping traffic frozen indefinitely. Goals: 1) Record a deterministic, privacy-aware snapshot of the canary traffic window (inputs, non-sensitive metadata, model response hashes, provenance) 2) Provide a fast UI for sampling and triage with redaction rules applied 3) Allow an operator to latch the canary into pause state and either approve (promote) or reject (auto-rollback) with a recorded rationale 4) Make snapshots small and signed so they can be archived and replayed locally with the same runtime pipeline and model variant 5) Integrate with existing rollout policies so the human latch is optional and composable with automated gates

What changed (high level): added a LatchController to the orchestrator runtime that can transition a canary to a PAUSED state and trigger a snapshot capture; implemented a replay_store component that packs sampled requests into a compact gzip+jsonl archive with signed manifest and anonymization hooks; extended the Console with a CanaryInspectPanel that lists samples, shows response diffs and allows downloading the replay package; added an API surface (openapi/rollouts.yaml) for latch actions and snapshot retrieval; updated CI pipeline to run the new integration test; added a runbook documenting when and how to use the human latch; small Terraform + Helm changes to surface the config toggle and RBAC for operators. The snapshot format is intentionally minimal: input tokens (truncated), deterministic response hash, request metadata (route, model_id, timestamp), and optional attached logs. Sensitive attributes are redacted by default via the anonymizer pipeline and the redaction rules are configurable per-customer.

Checklist:
- [x] LatchController implementation with state transitions and audit events
- [x] Snapshot packing + signing in replay_store
- [x] Console UI for triage + download
- [x] API contract and OpenAPI update
- [x] Integration tests covering pause, snapshot, replay download
- [x] Runbook and helm/terraform config
- [x] E2E CI job updated to include canary human-latch flow

High-level changed areas (files): services/orchestrator/src/canary (controller + replay store), console components for inspection, docs/runbooks, helm/values and RBAC, CI pipeline.

Testing and CI: local unit tests added for LatchController transitions and replay packing; added an integration test that spins up a lightweight orchestrator + dummy model to exercise capture and replay download (ci/pipeline was updated to run this in the canary stage). CI initially failed on lint (missing docstring in replay_store) and a flaky test; both were fixed in follow-ups. The overall pipeline now passes (see ci/pipeline/canary_pipeline.yml) and the PR shows green checks for build/test/lint/security-scan.

Backward compatibility and migration: The latch feature is gated behind a config flag (latch.enabled=false by default). Existing rollouts are unaffected unless operators opt-in. The snapshot schema is versioned (v1) and we included a lightweight backward-compatibility shim in replay_store to ignore unknown fields during replay. No DB migrations required; replay_store uses object storage buckets (S3-compatible) and stores manifests in a separate prefix.

Security and privacy: The anonymizer runs before snapshot packing and redacts fields matching configured patterns (PII, auth headers). Snapshot manifests are signed with the cluster key to prevent tampering. Access to snapshot download is RBAC-protected in Console and enforced at the API layer. We added a security-scan CI check to ensure no raw PII is persisted by default.

Operational notes: default behavior is to auto-archive snapshots for 7 days; retention can be configured per-tenant. Snapshots are intentionally limited to 5000 records and 5MB compressed to avoid storage blowup. The runbook documents emergency bypass procedures and how to run the local replay harness (scripts/replay/pack_snapshot.py + small container image used by SRE).

Open questions and future work: - Add per-metric sampling policies (sample biased by error class) - Integrate snapshot diffs into the Optimize pipeline for automated regression clustering - Add server-side replay runner to reproduce heavy tails in production without local env setup

Merge notes: squash-merged after approvals; migration not required; feature gated by config; rollout to production disabled by default. See release_notes below for operator-facing summary.
Connor Lee (reviewer): Nice work — can we make the default sample size smaller? Production S3 costs are a concern.
Asha Patel (author): I reduced default snapshot size to 5k/5MB and added retention config; updated docs/runbooks with cost guidance.
Mateo Alvarez (reviewer): Security review: confirm PII patterns and signing key rotation procedure.
Asha Patel: Added security-scan and docs for key rotation; replay manifests are signed and rotation is documented in docs/runbooks.
Priya Narang (reviewer): Integration test flaked in first CI run — looks like a timing issue with the latch TTL.
Asha Patel: Fixed sleep timing in test and added a deterministic clock in test harness; re-ran CI and all checks green.
Connor Lee: Approved-by-review — LGTM once CI green.
Operator-facing: Add 'human latch' canary option — captures a replayable, redacted snapshot of canary traffic for offline inspection. Feature is disabled by default and requires enabling 'latch.enabled' and appropriate RBAC. Snapshots are signed and stored in object storage with a default 7-day retention. See docs/runbooks/canary-human-inspection.md for usage and runbook steps.
If a human-latched canary fails or audit shows suspicious snapshot contents, revoke snapshot access key and follow runbook steps to rotate signing key. For emergency rollbacks, the latch UI has 'reject and rollback' which triggers the standard rollback path. Contact SRE on-call if snapshot download fails with 403.

payload.body:
Context: We see repeated short-lived canary flaps across heterogeneous traffic slices where small sample-size noise causes traffic fraction to oscillate and triggers false-positive rollbacks. This PR introduces an 'introspective canary stabilizer' that maintains statistical power while damping sample-weight oscillations and automatically widening smoke-test windows when variance is high. Motivation: reduce operational churn, avoid unnecessary rollbacks, and keep canaries meaningful for low-volume slices.

What this PR does (high level): Implements a sample-weight stabilizer component in the rollout controller that: 1) maintains a sliding reservoir of recent successful and failed sample outcomes per slice, 2) estimates effective sample variance and computes a damping factor for traffic weight updates, 3) applies an adaptive smoke threshold that increases tolerance under high variance and decays back as confidence accumulates, and 4) exposes metrics and debug traces for postmortem. Also adds a deterministic simulation harness used in unit and integration tests to validate behavior under bursty and adversarial noise patterns.

Implementation notes: New stabilizer service lives under src/rollout/stabilizer.go and is platform-agnostic (pure Go). It integrates into the existing promote/adjust pipeline via a Stabilizer interface with a single Evaluate(ctx, sliceState) -> StabilizedAdvice call. The advice carries a suggested weight delta and a confidence score (internal float) used by the controller. For testing and observability we added telemetry metrics (telemetry/metrics/canary_stability.prom), structured traces (tracing/tag=canary.stabilizer), and a small docs runbook describing expected behaviors and recovery steps (docs/runbooks/canary-stabilizer.md).

Testing and validation: Unit tests for edge cases (zero samples, perfect consistency, adversarial flips) are in pkg/rollout/stabilizer_test.go. We added simulated e2e scenarios in integration-tests/canary_e2e.yaml that previously caused flaps; the new stabilizer reduces reverts by ~72% in our synthetic replay harness. CI initially flagged an intermittent e2e smoke test; the test was flaky due to timing in the harness and was stabilized with a deterministic clock in the simulator.

Backward compatibility and rollout: The stabilizer is feature-flagged (rollout.introspective_stabilizer), default-off for Dedicated/Private until we finish a short canary in prod. Flag can be toggled per-tenant via rollout config. No API changes to external client-facing surfaces.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked (Linear: ENG-7892)
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration simulation added
- [x] Telemetry & tracing hooks
- [x] Runbook and release notes

Related: ENG-7892, ENG-8010; support ticket SUP-1345 noted repeated flaps in two customer clusters.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the Stabilizer.Evaluate contract and the damping constant defaults in stabilizer/config.go. The simulation harness is intentionally simplified — it's deterministic by design for reproducible CI runs.
Sana Patel: High level LGTM. Please call out in the runbook the expected magnitude of weight dampening for 95% CI so on-call engineers know when to intervene.
Author (Aisha): Added a small note in docs/runbooks/canary-stabilizer.md and left an example table of dampening values for 90/95/99% confidence windows.
Liam O'Connor: Concern: the sliding reservoir could grow memory-wise if a tenant has very many slices. Can we add an explicit cap and eviction strategy?
Author (Aisha): Added reservoir cap logic (configurable per-tenant) and eviction policy (LRU by timestamp). See src/rollout/config.go change and added unit tests to verify cap enforcement.
Miguel Torres: Telemetry names look fine. Suggest a counter for 'stabilizer_deferred_updates' when the advice is suppressed by confidence gating.
Author (Aisha): Added metric stabilizer_deferred_updates and a dashboard stub in telemetry/metrics/canary_stability.prom
- Add introspective canary stabilizer that reduces noise-driven rollbacks and smooths traffic adjustments
- New deterministic simulation harness for validating canary stability under noisy conditions
- Telemetry to track weight drift, deferred updates, and stabilizer confidence
- Feature-flag rollout (rollout.introspective_stabilizer) - default off for Dedicated/Private

payload.body:
Motivation: Staged rollouts for Dedicated pools need stage-scoped signals (latency/error/saturation/OOM) so the policy engine can evaluate gates deterministically and the Console can show evidence per stage. Today most metrics/traces are only tagged with pool_id/model/version/region, which makes it hard to attribute regressions to the canary partition vs baseline. This PR adds stage identifiers to a small set of request-scoped metrics and spans, with explicit cardinality controls (allowlist + value constraints) to avoid a repeat of high-cardinality label explosions. Summary of changes: (1) Introduce `rollout_stage_id` + `rollout_stage_idx` tags in the request context (propagated from router -> dataplane -> metrics/tracing). (2) Emit stage tags on key SLO/gate metrics only (request duration buckets, request error counters, 429/drop counters, queue depth, OOM counters), leaving the rest unchanged. (3) Add an allowlist-based label filter in the telemetry emitter with hard caps on value length and a denylist for free-form fields. (4) Add sampling + aggregation guardrails for span tags (only tag root request span + a single child span; do not tag per-token spans). (5) Feature flag `dedicated_rollout_stage_telemetry_tags` to allow safe enablement per environment/account. Notes on cardinality: `rollout_stage_id` is a short stable identifier (<= 16 chars, base32) and `rollout_stage_idx` is an int string (0..N). We explicitly do NOT include stage name, plan name, or arbitrary customer metadata. For multi-region pools, region remains a separate tag; stage_id is shared across regions for the same promotion step. Rollout stage tags are optional; when absent we emit no tag and do not substitute "unknown" to avoid creating a new high-cardinality value. Rollout/gates behavior: This PR does not change gate evaluation logic; it only emits the signals needed by ENG-5941/ENG-5941 follow-ups and the dashboards in observability-pack. Testing: unit tests for label allowlist/filtering, integration test that stage context from routing attaches to metrics, and a soak test config that validates the top-N time series count does not change materially when the flag is off. Rollout plan: land behind flag; enable in staging for 48h; then enable for beta Dedicated accounts only. If we see increased series churn, we can disable the flag with no config migration.
Allison Grant (comment): Please confirm we are not tagging per-token metrics/spans with stage_id; that would blow up our series count and trace payload size. Also, please document the label allowlist policy (what gets tagged and why). Caleb Johnson (reply): Confirmed: only request-level SLO metrics + root request span are tagged; per-token metrics remain unchanged and per-token spans do not get the stage attributes. Added explicit tests and a note in docs/observability/metrics-labeling-policy.md. Logan Wright (comment): The label filter needs to be centralized; right now we have a filter in metrics emitter but not in tracing. We should enforce the same constraints (max length, allowed keys) across both so future tags can't sneak in. Caleb Johnson (reply): Agreed; added `label_policy.go` and reused in tracing span tag helper. Both metrics and tracing now share allowlist/denylist and the value length cap. Sergio Costa (comment): For dashboards, can we also emit stage_idx? It's useful for ordered stage panels even when stage_id is opaque. Caleb Johnson (reply): Added `rollout_stage_idx` tag (stringified int) alongside stage_id; still optional. Mina Haddad (comment): Header propagation from router to dataplane: please ensure this cannot be spoofed by end users hitting the pool endpoint directly. Also should be stripped on external ingress. Caleb Johnson (reply): Updated middleware to only accept stage headers from internal trusted hops (mTLS service identity + internal network). External ingress strips `x-redwood-rollout-*` headers. Jordan Lee (comment): When stage metadata is missing, we should fail closed or mark it unknown? From a policy perspective, missing data handling matters. Caleb Johnson (reply): This PR intentionally emits nothing when absent; policy engine will handle missing stage tags (likely treat as insufficient evidence). Adding "unknown" would create a new time series and make dashboards noisier; aligned with SRE guidance in thread 1738976011. Requested changes: (1) add feature flag and default OFF in prod; (2) ensure stage_id length cap; (3) add series-budget CI check. Addressed in follow-up commits. Approvals: Logan Wright ✅; Allison Grant ✅; Sergio Costa ✅; Mina Haddad ✅; Jordan Lee ✅.
Internal-only: Adds optional `rollout_stage_id` / `rollout_stage_idx` tags to a limited set of request metrics and tracing spans to support Dedicated staged rollout gate attribution. Guarded by `dedicated_rollout_stage_telemetry_tags` feature flag; includes label allowlist and anti-cardinality protections.

payload.body:
Motivation: We see recurring micro-regressions where tenant-level unit economics drift upward after model/quant/profile changes; operators currently detect these manually via ad-hoc dashboards. This PR introduces an automated 'Cost Drift Investigator' that (1) runs shadow evaluations of candidate quant/profile changes per tenant, (2) synthesizes unit-econ deltas with confidence bands, and (3) enforces safe rollback policies when drift exceeds thresholds. We also introduce a gradual quantization strategy ("zipper quantizer") that steps precision down in controlled phases with live telemetry gating.

What this PR does (summary): 
- Tenant shadowing: pipeline to run candidate quant/profile variants in parallel (no user-visible outputs) and compute per-tenant cost-per-1000-tokens, latency p50/p95, and quality delta (based on existing eval harness signals). Shadow runs are stored as lightweight traces and sampled to control egress cost.
- Drift detection engine: rolling-window statistical detector that flags regressions based on configurable budget and quality tolerances. The detector emits alerts and an evidence bundle used for automated rollbacks.
- Automatic rollback policies: policy DSL to specify when to automatically revert to the last known-good profile. Policies support soft-rollbacks (route 10% of traffic back), canary rollbacks, and immediate full rollback. Rollback actions are idempotent and logged with audit events.
- Zipper quantizer: new quantizer mode that applies quantization in N progressive steps (e.g., 16->8->6->4 bits) and only proceeds to the next step when shadow telemetry stays within bounds for a stabilization window. This reduces large one-shot regressions and makes rollbacks cheap.
- CLI and Console hooks: add tenant-level controls to Redwood Console (read-only telemetry rows during shadowing and a rollback button), and new CLI flags for dry-run and force-apply.
- Telemetry and observability: unit-econ metrics, regression-confidence histograms, and a new prefixed namespace redwood.cost_drift.*. Dashboards and alert rules added under telemetry/playbooks.
- Tests and simulation: includes an offline simulator that replays historical traffic to estimate false-positive risk and a set of unit/integration tests.

Files changed (high level): 
- runtime/drift/investigator.py (core drift detector + policy enforcement)
- runtime/quant/zipper_quant.py (zipper quantizer implementation)
- runtime/shadow/runner.go (lightweight shadow routing and sampling)
- console/src/components/tenantShadow.tsx (Console UI rows and rollback button)
- cli/redwoodctl/cost_drift.go (dry-run/force flags)
- docs/ops/cost-drift.md (operator guide and policy examples)
- telemetry/dashboards/cost-drift-overview.json (dashboard panels)

Migration notes and backwards compatibility: shadowing is opt-in per-tenant by default; existing deployments are unaffected unless operators opt-in. The zipper quantizer is a new mode and does not replace existing quant workflows. Rollbacks are backward-compatible: if rollback engine cannot find prior profile it falls back to strongest safety profile and logs the decision.

Checklist (author): 
- [x] Core detector and policy engine implemented
- [x] Zipper quantizer with step gating
- [x] Console and CLI controls wired
- [x] Telemetry names and dashboards added
- [x] Unit + integration tests

Motivation: Long-tail latency/cost spikes are often correlated with subtle per-token phase variability (e.g., unexpected KV-cache churn, backend contention, or prompt-shape anomalies). Existing metrics capture aggregated per-invocation costs but lack a compact, explainable signature that surfaces phase-level entropy and a lightweight visual hint in the Console. This PR introduces an entropy-weighted token-phase signature metric, a compact sparkline attachment for invocation traces in the Console, and a synthetic replay harness to validate detection sensitivity across realistic prompt shapes. The description below is a single continuous string with context, implementation notes, and rollout plan. Implementation summary: 1) telemetry/metrics: add token_phase_entropy meter that computes per-invocation token-phase distributions (encode: prefix/kvcache/model-encoder/decoder phases) and emits a small fingerprint (64-bit base64) plus a float entropy score. 2) tracing: enrich sampled spans with token_phase_signature and sparkline url meta; signatures are deterministic hashes of the per-phase token counts so they can be correlated across tenants. 3) console: new sparkline "Phase Entropy" attachment on invocation detail panels (click-to-expand) with hover tooltips showing per-phase counts and delta to baseline. 4) dashboards: dashboard JSON with cohorting by signature cluster and a low-cardinality legend for fast triage. 5) alerts: provide an adaptive alert recipe that combines base token-cost SLO with a delta-over-baseline entropy bucketing to reduce false positives from benign bursts. 6) tests: unit tests for entropy calculation, integration replay bench (synthetic spikes), and an e2e Console render test. Rollout and safety: default telemetry emission is opt-in per-tenant via a feature flag (observability.token_phase_entropy = off). For hosted tenants we roll out for internal beta for 2 weeks, then staged gradual opt-in to customers with heavy debug billing permissions. Privacy: signatures are non-reversible hashes; no raw token text is emitted. Backwards compatibility: metrics use new metric names but do not change existing panels. Docs: internal runbook + playbook for oncall to interpret signatures. Plan to monitor cardinality for 30 days and add reservoir-based sampling if necessary. Links: Linear ENG-9203 (design), ENG-9378 (dashboard design), SUP-4421 (customer support case that motivated anomaly false positives).
+ func ComputeTokenPhaseEntropy(phases []int) float64 { /* discrete entropy over phase counts, smoothed */ }
+ {\n  "panel": "phase-entropy-sparkline",\n  "width": 6\n}\n
+ span.SetTag("token_phase_signature", signature) // deterministic 64-bit base64
Marcus Lee: Please add a short comment describing why the entropy smoothing constant is 0.5 (helps noisy short invocations).
Priya Kaur: Added comment and updated unit test to exercise edge-case of single-phase invocations.
Aisha Patel: Concern about cardinality — can we cap signature variants with a reservoir sampler?
Priya Kaur: Added feature-flag and noted reservoir sampler as follow-up if we exceed cardinality thresholds during beta. Also added a telemetry counter for unique-signatures-per-hour.
Diego Ramos: LGTm after small nits; requested one more perf microbench for ComputeTokenPhaseEntropy on hot paths.
Priya Kaur: Added microbench, numbers inline in commit message; no measurable allocation spike.
Squash merged by Aisha Patel after approvals and CI green. Changelog entry added to internal CHANGELOG.md. Feature gated by observability.token_phase_entropy flag; default off for external tenants.
Adds an entropy-weighted token-phase signature metric and a Console sparkline attachment for invocation detail pages. Includes a synthetic replay harness and an adaptive alert recipe to reduce false positives. Feature is feature-flagged and off by default for external tenants.
Unit tests for entropy and signature determinism; synthetic replay generates three waveform types (steady, burst, skew) and validates detection; e2e Console render test ensures sparkline layout; manual canary on internal tenants for 2 weeks before customer opt-in.
If an entropy alert fires, check invocation detail sparkline and signature cluster. Use synthetic replay to reproduce spike shape. Toggle observability.token_phase_entropy off for tenant if false positives persist.
ENG-9481: reservoir sampler for signature cardinality if >10k/hour
ENG-9510: expose signature cohorts in per-tenant timeline API
DOC-303: public docs and migration notes for observability token metrics

Motivation: Our CI runners spend a disproportionate amount of wall time downloading and installing language toolchains and devdeps for jobs that don't need them (docs-only, markdown linting, tiny choirs). This PR reduces cumulative install I/O, lowers average runner time by ~18% on the fast lanes, and introduces a 'quiet merge window' for low-priority post-merge tasks so we don't trigger heavy downstream work during peak traffic.

What changed (high-level):
- Introduce toolchain-lite job profiles and a new 'toolchain-stub' make target that skips heavy downloads for presubmit (fastpath) lanes.
- Shift large artifact fetches (container images, GPU toolchains) to a deferred post-merge optional job that runs on a different queue (post-merge/low-prio).
- Add path-aware fastpath: doc-only and non-code changes now run slimlint + spellcheck only; JS/Python install steps are gated behind changed files detection.
- Centralize and cache pip/npm/apt layers in the CI image and fall back to local network cache when present. Added an opt-in CI_CACHE_AFFINITY env flag for teams that want stronger cache locality.
- Quiet merge window: a configurable 15-minute window after a merge where non-blocking, heavy post-merge tasks are deferred to reduce contention for infra and to reduce surprise flakiness during high-traffic merges.

Commit summary: squash of 7 commits (dev -> CI hygiene):
- detect: add changed-files fastpath and toolchain-stub target
- ci: move heavy downloads to post-merge/low-prio queue
- build: cache pip wheel layer and npm node_modules tarball in runner image
- docs: add contributor notes for fastpath labels and quiet merge window policy
- infra: add CI_CACHE_AFFINITY flag and remote-cache fallback
- tests: add unit tests for changed-files detector and mock cache behaviors
- chore: update CI images & pin small set of apt deps for reproducibility

Files / areas touched (high-level):
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yml (introduce fastpath lanes, toolchain-stub conditionals)
- .github/workflows/post-merge.yml (add low-priority queue and deferred jobs)
- ci/toolchain/Makefile (toolchain-stub, toolchain-full targets)
- infra/runner-images/Dockerfile (cache layers for pip, npm, apt)
- scripts/changed_files_detector.py (new, lightweight changed-file classifier)
- docs/ci.md (policy for quiet merge window and label usage)
- tests/ci/test_changed_detector.py (unit tests)

Small illustrative snippet (presubmit.yml conditional):

jobs:
  presubmit-fastpath:
    if: contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'fastpath') || steps.changed_files.outputs.code == 'false'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: make toolchain-stub
      - run: make lint-slim

Design notes and tradeoffs: We intentionally keep the default behavior conservative: full toolchain installs still run on main integration lanes. Fastpath lanes are opt-in via label or automatic path classification; teams can opt out. The quiet merge window is a pragmatic step to reduce noise — it does not block any post-merge diagnostic, it merely reschedules heavy telemetry and slow analytics to a low-priority queue so merges remain fast and predictable.

Risk and mitigation: Introducing changed-files logic can cause false-negatives if detection misses a code change (rare). Mitigations: added unit tests, staged rollout behind the 'fastpath' label, and manual override via GITHUB_ACTIONS_FORCE_FULL_TOOLCHAIN env. Post-merge deferred jobs are run on a separate fleet with lower concurrency to avoid resource contention.

Migration and rollout plan: Start with a 10% rollout for active repos (toggle via org-level feature flag), monitor presubmit latency and rerun rate for 72 hours. If stable, expand to 100% and add a dashboard card for "CI install time" and "post-merge queue depth".

Related: ENG-2149 (CI cost reduction spike), ENG-2170 (runner cache prototype).
Liam O'Connor: Nice approach. Can we add a safety toggle so a repo owner can force full installs if the detector misclassifies?
Priya Nair (author): Added GITHUB_ACTIONS_FORCE_FULL_TOOLCHAIN env override and documented it in docs/ci.md
Sara Patel: Please add telemetry for "presubmit_install_time" and a short-term alert if it spikes after rollout
Priya Nair: Added a placeholder metric and a follow-up Linear (ENG-2184) to flesh out alerts
Ming Zhao: Dockerfile changes look good. Prefer pinning apt packages to reduce cache invalidation risk — done.
detect: add changed-files fastpath and toolchain-stub target
ci: defer heavy downloads to post-merge low-prio queue
build: bake pip/npm cache layers into runner image
docs: document quiet merge window and fastpath usage
infra: add CI_CACHE_AFFINITY and remote fallback
tests: add changed-files detector unit tests
chore: pin apt deps for image reproducibility
Improved CI performance: introduced fastpath presubmit lanes and toolchain-stub to reduce install I/O; added a configurable quiet merge window to defer non-essential post-merge tasks. Metric: ~18% faster presubmit on fast lanes (early rollout).
ENG-2184: add alerts and dashboards for presubmit_install_time
Rollout: enable org flag for 10% -> 100% after monitoring
Docs: update CONTRIBUTING.md with fastpath label guidance

Context: We need deterministic, tenant-aware defaults for prefill/batching/quantization that can be safely rolled out and audited. This PR introduces a small rule-engine that codifies tenant budget and latency SLOs into prefill decisions, and a quant-fingerprint registry that maps model+workload signatures to vetted quantization profiles. Motivation: reduce trial-and-error tuning, lower unit-econ variance across tenants, and provide a fast rollback path when quant changes regress quality. What this PR does: 1) Adds pkg/prefill/ruleengine which evaluates tenant profiles, historical prefill hit rates, and budget tiers to emit prefill templates; 2) Adds pkg/prefill/quant_fingerprint: a registry keyed by model hash, signature shape (seq_len, kv_cache_ratio), and workload skew that selects a safe quant profile; 3) Introduces rwctl prefill export/import commands (cmd/rwctl/prefill_export.go) to produce tenant-default YAMLs and to simulate dry-run recommendations; 4) Adds telemetry counters/gauges for prefill.hit_rate, prefill.unit_econ, quant.apply_failures and histograms for prefill.latency.p50/p95/p99; 5) Adds an administrative migration that seeds tenant defaults from historical sampling and marks fingerprints as "provisional" until verified by canary; 6) Implements a safe fallback path: when a fingerprint is unknown or unverified, the runtime falls back to the conservative quant profile for that model (configurable). Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-3204) - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] rwctl CLI UX validated locally - [x] Telemetry and alerts wired to staging Grafana dashboard - [x] Migration path implemented with dry-run only mode by default - [x] Runbook and rollback steps documented (docs/ops/prefill-rule-engine.md). Commits: Initial scaffolding and interfaces; rule engine core evaluation; quant fingerprint store and lookup with signer; rwctl CLI export/import; telemetry metrics and prometheus exporter; unit/integration tests; docs and runbook. High-level changed files: pkg/prefill/engine.go; pkg/prefill/rules.go; pkg/prefill/quant_fingerprint.go; cmd/rwctl/prefill_export.go; configs/tenant_defaults/seeded_presets.yaml; telemetry/prefill_metrics.prom; docs/ops/prefill-rule-engine.md; tests/prefill/engine_test.go; tests/integration/prefill_canary_test.go. Testing notes: Local unit tests and CI unit suite passed. Integration tests initially hit a flaky timing assertion in prefilling which was fixed by introducing a small backoff in the prefetch scheduler; integration re-run succeeded. E2E and canary runs executed against the staging cluster with a 0.5% tenant sample and showed no regression in p99; prefill hit rate improved for synthetic workloads. Migration and rollout plan: start with tenants flagged as "candidate" in the seeded_presets file, enable dry-run export to surface suggestions, then enable canary apply at 5% of traffic, monitor prefill.unit_econ and quality signals, promote to 25% and then 100% if stable. Observability and alerts: added rules in prometheus/alerts (prefill_unit_econ_drop, quant_apply_failure_rate) and a dashboard in staging Grafana. Security and data handling: fingerprints are computed from model metadata and anonymized workload signatures; no user PII stored. Backwards compatibility: existing tenant configs remain authoritative; this system only suggests defaults and requires explicit apply via rwctl or tenant-admin APIs when not in automatic mode. Limitations and follow-ups: automatic rollback is conservative and will be improved with a rollback window tied to quality evals; we will add a CLI diff/preview for quant profile changes. Related work: complements prefilling heuristics in pkg/prefill/shapers and the tenant warmstart work in ENG-2980. Merge notes: squash-merged after final green CI and approvals.
Adds a tenant-prefill rule engine and a quantization fingerprint registry. New CLI to export tenant defaults. Telemetry for prefill unit economics and safe fallback to conservative quant profiles. Backwards-compatible; automatic migration for tenant presets. Recommended rollouts: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with monitoring of prefill hit rate and p99 latency.
Owen Li (2026-02-11): Please verify metrics cardinality; prefill.hit_rate tags look like they could explode when we include model+tenant; suggest model-level and tenant-cohort tagging only.
Leah Park (2026-02-11): Good catch — reduced metric cardinality to model_family + tenant_cohort and added explicit cardinality limits in metrics.go.
Priya Nair (2026-02-13): Perf question: rule engine evaluator uses a read lock; under high concurrency we might serialize evaluation. Can we switch to lock-free copy-on-write for presets?
Leah Park (2026-02-13): Switched to a copy-on-write presets store and added benchmarks. See pkg/prefill/benchmarks_test.go commit.
Carlos Méndez (2026-02-15): Integration tests observed a flaky timing assert; please ensure prefetch scheduler uses jitter/backoff.
Leah Park (2026-02-15): Pushed fix with small jitter and backoff; re-ran integration suite — all green.
Priya Nair (2026-02-17): Approving pending minor doc nit. Left comment on the migration script about idempotency.
Leah Park (2026-02-17): Addressed idempotency and added a dry-run flag to migration script.
Owen Li (2026-02-18): LGTM. Telemetry reviewed and dashboard links provided.
Priya Nair (2026-02-18): Approved and performed squash-merge.

Summary: This PR adds audit logging for (1) scaling policy configuration changes (min/max/cooldowns/predictive toggles) and (2) autoscaler scaling decisions (requested desired vs bounded desired, reasons, signal inputs). Events are emitted from control plane services and the dedicated autoscaler loop, normalized into a common event shape, and shipped through the existing audit log pipeline for enterprise retention/export.

Why: Dedicated enterprise customers (and internal compliance reviews) need deterministic, reviewable history of who changed bounds and why capacity changed. For the autoscaling bounds + predictive mode rollout we also need post-incident forensics: the ability to answer “what did the autoscaler want”, “what did bounds clamp”, and “which signal(s) caused it”.

Scope:
- New audit event types:
  - dedicated.scaling_policy.updated
  - dedicated.scaling_policy.validation_failed
  - dedicated.autoscaler.decision
  - dedicated.autoscaler.decision_suppressed (cooldown / anti-oscillation)
  - dedicated.autoscaler.min_unmet (capacity shortage / provisioning failure)
- New shared schema + helper encoder to enforce determinism and PII constraints.
- Integration with audit-log pipeline (Kafka topic + sink) and SIEM export tagging.
- Unit tests + one integration test with a fake audit sink.

Event shape (high-level):
- All events include: event_id, event_type, occurred_at, actor_type, actor_id, request_id (if available), customer_id, deployment_id, region.
- Policy update events include: previous_policy_hash, new_policy_hash, changed_fields, validation_warnings.
- Autoscaler decision events include: requested_desired_replicas, bounded_desired_replicas, current_replicas, min_replicas, max_replicas, cooldown_active, reasons (enum list), signal_snapshot (bounded cardinality), prediction (optional; includes staleness + confidence).

Notes on safety and cardinality:
- No raw prompt/traffic payloads are logged.
- signal_snapshot uses a fixed set of numeric fields and avoids label fanout (no per-model/per-route labels here; those remain in metrics).
- actor_id is derived from auth principal; for system actions we emit actor_type=system and actor_id=dedicated-autoscaler.

Rollout:
- Emission is behind a feature flag: dedicated_audit_scaling_events.
- Default OFF for all accounts.
- We will enable first in us-east-1 canary Dedicated fleet after SRE review.

Follow-ups (not in this PR):
- Console UI surfacing audit history (DES-981/ENG-22144 dependent).
- Retention policy overrides per enterprise contract (Security/Compliance workstream).

Testing:
- Unit: schema encoding, redaction, stable hashing, changed_fields computation, and “decision” reason selection.
- Integration: autoscaler -> audit sink happy path; validation_failed emission path.

Risk:
- Increased audit event volume during oscillation scenarios; mitigated via suppression events + rate limiting (decision_suppressed emitted at most once per cooldown interval per deployment).

Screens/Examples:
- Example dedicated.autoscaler.decision JSON (redacted) included in docs comment in code.

Release note: Internal only (feature flagged).
Jordan Lee (review): Can we guarantee determinism in changed_fields ordering? Otherwise diffs become noisy in compliance exports. Also please ensure policy hashes are stable across JSON key order.
Felix Schneider (author): Good catch. Updated encoder to sort keys + emit changed_fields in canonical order (field name asc). Added unit test to lock behavior.
Benji Okafor (review): RBAC/actor attribution: updateScalingPolicy uses service-to-service auth for some console flows. We still want the end-user principal in actor_id when proxied. Do we have that in headers?
Felix Schneider (author): Yes, console gateway forwards x-rw-actor-*; I added extraction with fallback to service principal. Added a structured warning when actor is missing.
Miles Thornton (review): Volume: autoscaler loop runs frequently. Are we going to emit an event every tick even when bounded_desired == current and no action? That’ll be a ton of noise.
Felix Schneider (author): Decision emission is now only on “state transition” (scale up/down intent) OR when bounds clamp (requested != bounded) OR when cooldown suppresses an action. Added decision_suppressed to explain why we didn’t act.
Marcus Lin (security review): Make sure signal_snapshot cannot include customer-provided labels; also confirm no IPs/user emails leak via actor_id. Please document the data contract in the internal doc.
Felix Schneider (author): actor_id is internal principal id only; no emails. signal_snapshot is fixed numeric fields only. Added doc and a redaction test to prevent free-form fields.
Kevin Osei (review): For SIEM export we need a consistent field for retention tier. Please tag these events as 'enterprise_audit=true' but keep emission feature-flagged.
Felix Schneider (author): Added enterprise_audit=true attribute in the audit metadata for all event types introduced here (constant).
Jordan Lee (approval): Approved after last push. Thanks for tightening determinism and volume controls.
Miles Thornton (approval): Approved. Please coordinate flag enablement with SRE runbook before canary.

## Summary
Adds a summarized readiness endpoint intended for internal ops tooling (Console table views + drill-down): counts by readiness state and top failure reasons per filter scope. This is specifically to avoid the UI doing N+1 calls across nodes and to keep metric tag cardinality under control.

New endpoint (internal only): `GET /internal/fleet/readiness/summary`.

## Motivation / context
The staged rollout surfaced a bunch of operator workflows that currently require:
- querying per-node readiness state across pools
- separately querying validation artifacts to understand top failures
- manually deduping noisy failure messages

DES-301 is building the internal console view for readiness state + failure reasons. This endpoint provides:
- fast aggregate counts (Allocated / Provisioning / Validating / Ready / Quarantined)
- a "top failures" list with normalized codes + counts
- optional filtering by `region`, `pool_id`, `gpu_type`, `image_channel`, and time window

## API
### Request
`GET /internal/fleet/readiness/summary?region=us-east-1&pool_id=dedicated-8d4f&gpu_type=A100&image_channel=candidate&since=24h&top_failures=10`

### Response (shape)
- `as_of`: server timestamp for the snapshot
- `scope`: echo of applied filters
- `counts_by_state`: map of readiness state -> count
- `top_failures`: list of { code, step, count, example_node_id (optional), last_seen_at }

Note: `example_node_id` is omitted by default to avoid encouraging UI patterns that pivot back into per-node queries. It can be enabled behind an internal feature flag for debugging.

## Implementation details
- Aggregation is performed server-side in the readiness service using a single query (group by state) + a second query for top failures (group by normalized failure code + validation step).
- Failure normalization: we group using `failure_code` emitted by the validation agent / orchestrator where present; otherwise we fall back to a coarse mapping from common substrings (Xid, NCCL timeout, kubelet join) to reduce noise. Raw messages remain available in node-level artifact views.
- Performance:
  - Adds an index to speed up `WHERE updated_at > :since AND region = :region AND pool_id = :pool_id`.
  - Adds a small in-process cache (30s) keyed by (filters + since + top_failures). Console refreshes every ~15–30s; this prevents thundering herds during incidents.
- Authz:
  - Endpoint is under `/internal/*` and requires the `fleet-readiness-ui` service principal OR an operator session with `fleet.readiness:read`.
  - All requests are audit-logged with `actor`, `scope`, and `since`.

## Changed areas
- `control-plane/fleet_readiness/api/internal_routes.go`
- `control-plane/fleet_readiness/handlers/readiness_summary_handler.go` (new)
- `control-plane/fleet_readiness/store/readiness_summary_queries.sql` (new)
- `control-plane/fleet_readiness/store/indexes.sql` (adds composite index)
- `control-plane/authz/policies/fleet_readiness.rego`
- `control-plane/telemetry/metrics/fleet_readiness.go` (request duration + error counter)
- `control-plane/openapi/internal.yaml` (documents internal endpoint)

## Testing
- Unit tests for query filters and grouping behavior (including failure normalization fallbacks).
- Integration test against sqlite-backed store for:
  - correct counts by state
  - `top_failures` ordering + limits
  - authz enforcement
- Manual: hit endpoint in staging with seeded readiness data from the us-east A100 rollout.

## Screens / output
Example response (redacted): shows counts by state and top failures for `us-east-1` dedicated pool, last 24h.

## Rollout / risks
- Internal-only endpoint; no customer-facing surface area.
- Query + cache designed to be safe during incidents (bounded results, `top_failures` capped at 50, default 10).
- If this causes DB pressure, we can turn off caching and force the UI back to state-only counts (feature flag: `fleet_readiness_summary_enabled`).

## Review notes / follow-ups
- Follow-up: once DES-301 lands, we should confirm the UI does not request `example_node_id` except in a drill-down flow.
- Follow-up: replace substring-based failure normalization with explicit codes for remaining validators (tracked in ENG-4830).

---

### Commit summary
1) Add internal readiness summary handler + OpenAPI docs
2) Add store queries and composite index for recent updates
3) Add authz policy + audit logging
4) Add telemetry (request duration, 4xx/5xx counters) + tests

### CI
✅ build (bazel)
✅ unit tests
✅ integration tests
✅ lint/go vet

---

## Review conversation (highlights)
**Jordan Lee**: Can we guarantee result size bounds? Also please ensure we don’t expose per-node identifiers by default (cardinality + security). **Benji Okafor**: Added `top_failures` cap at 50 and removed `example_node_id` from default response; gated behind `fleet_readiness_summary_include_example_node` flag.

**Allison Grant**: Please add request-level metrics but do not tag by pool_id (cardinality). **Benji Okafor**: Added `fleet_readiness_summary_request_duration_ms` and `fleet_readiness_summary_errors_total` tagged only by `region` and `status_class`.

**Ethan Park**: Authz: prefer operator permission `fleet.readiness:read` + service principal allowlist; also add audit event for the scope. **Benji Okafor**: Updated rego policy, added audit log entry `FLEET_READINESS_SUMMARY_VIEWED` with applied filters.

**Miles Thornton**: For `since`, can we avoid arbitrary durations that lead to slow queries? **Benji Okafor**: Enforced `since` max of 7d and default 24h; returns 400 for larger windows.

Approved-by: Jordan Lee, Ethan Park. Merged via squash.
Internal-only: adds a readiness summary endpoint used by ops console to display counts by readiness state and top validation failures.

payload.body:
## Summary
This PR implements deterministic evaluation semantics for failover trigger signals in the policy engine and introduces a versioned config schema to express signal priority, corroboration requirements, and anti-flap dampening inputs. The goal is to eliminate ambiguous/unstable decisions under noisy signals (false positives) and to make controller recommendations reproducible across replicas and over time.

This is a core building block for the Regional Failover Automation Upgrade (Reliability Program). It aligns with ADR-042 (failover trigger signal hierarchy) and is intended to be consumed by the failover controller (dry-run + execution) and by routing decisioning for Hosted API + Dedicated.

## Motivation / problem
Today the policy engine effectively evaluates “best effort” based on whichever signal arrives first and the order of predicates in config. Under partial outages, slight differences in signal availability (or timestamp skew) can lead to:
- non-deterministic policy flip recommendations across replicas
- oscillation between regions when signals conflict
- hard-to-audit decisions (no consistent ‘why’ path)
- inability to safely validate dry-run recommendations against a recorded signal snapshot

## What changed
### 1) Deterministic evaluation pipeline
- Added `SignalHierarchyEvaluator` which produces a stable decision outcome for a given set of signals + config.
- Evaluation is explicitly ordered by configured priority (highest authority first), with deterministic tie-breaking.
- The evaluator produces a structured `DecisionTrace` capturing which signals were considered, which were missing/stale, and which rule fired.

Determinism rules:
- Signals are normalized and sorted by `(priority_rank, signal_type, region, source)`.
- Only signals within freshness windows participate (defaults, override per signal type).
- If a high-authority signal is present and crosses threshold, lower-priority signals cannot override it; they can only corroborate or contribute to confidence.

### 2) Config schema update (versioned)
Introduced `signal_hierarchy` config stanza with `version: v2` behind a feature gate; the legacy interpretation remains default.

New schema concepts:
- `priority_order`: an explicit ordered list of signal classes (e.g. `reachability`, `http_5xx_burn`, `tail_latency_burn`, `capacity_exhaustion`).
- `corroboration`: optional rules requiring a second signal to confirm before declaring a region impaired, except for “authoritative” signals.
- `freshness`: per-signal TTLs and maximum allowed staleness.
- `hold_down_inputs`: evaluator emits the recommended hold-down metadata (it does not enforce timers itself; enforcement stays with the controller/guardrails layer).

Default v2 order (per ADR-042): reachability > 5xx burn > tail latency burn > capacity exhaustion.

### 3) Policy predicate API changes
- Added `evaluate_with_trace()` for consumers that need audit/UX (controller dry-run, incident-bot summaries).
- Kept `evaluate()` intact, implemented as a thin wrapper that discards trace.

### 4) Unit tests + fixtures
- Added golden tests for deterministic traces given identical recorded signal snapshots.
- Added edge case tests:
  - missing signal streams (should not crash; should degrade to “insufficient evidence”)
  - stale reachability vs fresh burn-rate (ensure stale signal cannot block)
  - conflicting signals across regions (stable winner selection)
  - corroboration requirement satisfied/unsatisfied
  - tie-breaking stability across map iteration order

## Files / areas touched (high level)
- `controlplane/policy-engine/`
  - `signal_hierarchy_evaluator.{go,ts}` (new)
  - `policy_eval.{go,ts}` (wires in evaluator)
  - `decision_trace.proto` + generated types
- `config/schema/`
  - `routing_policy.schema.json` (adds `signal_hierarchy` v2)
  - `routing_policy.examples.yaml` (new examples)
- `controlplane/policy-engine/testdata/`
  - recorded signal snapshots (JSON)
  - golden traces

## Backwards compatibility / rollout
- Default behavior is unchanged unless `signal_hierarchy.version: v2` is set for a route/tier.
- The evaluator emits trace fields that are safe for internal logs (no customer payloads).
- This PR does not change controller behavior directly; it only provides deterministic evaluation + schema.

Recommended rollout plan (tracked in ENG-2412):
1) Enable v2 in staging for a limited set of routes and compare decisions vs legacy mode (diff tool in follow-up).
2) Turn on dry-run in prod for a limited tenant allowlist; emit audit events only.
3) Once confirmed, allow v2 default for multi-region routes.

## Testing
- Unit tests: added/updated across evaluator + schema validation.
- Config validation tests: ensure legacy configs continue to parse, and invalid v2 configs fail with clear errors.
- CI: `policy-engine-unit`, `schema-validate`, `lint`, `integration-smoke` all green.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Add a CLI command in the failover controller tool to pretty-print `DecisionTrace` (see ENG-2415).
- Add dashboard annotations derived from `DecisionTrace.reason` enums (observability pack PR).
- Add simulation endpoint to replay recorded signals and verify determinism end-to-end (tracked separately).

## Links
- Linear: ENG-2412
- ADR-042: Failover trigger signal hierarchy (authoritative priority + corroboration)
- Related: PR #19810 (Region health aggregator service)

---

## Review conversation highlights (abridged)
Miles Thornton: The priority rules look right, but we need to be explicit that reachability is authoritative only when freshness is valid. Otherwise it can freeze failover if the probe pipeline is down.
Jordan Lee: Agreed. Updated evaluator to treat stale/missing as “unknown” and added tests for stale reachability not blocking burn-rate.

Ravi Menon: Tie-breaking across regions should be stable and documented. Also please ensure we don’t accidentally rely on map iteration order.
Jordan Lee: Added deterministic sort key (priority_rank, signal_type, region, source) and a regression test that randomizes insertion order.

Benji Okafor: Can we keep legacy mode default and gate v2 per route? Also want a field in trace that indicates config version used.
Jordan Lee: Yes; v2 is opt-in and trace includes `config_version` + `policy_revision`.

Allison Grant: Please keep trace labels bounded; we’ll likely export a subset to metrics later.
Jordan Lee: Trace stores structured enums and bounded string fields (region, signal class). No raw error messages or free-form reasons.

Mina Haddad: Schema change needs examples in repo; on-call will copy/paste these.
Jordan Lee: Added `routing_policy.examples.yaml` including minimal v2 migration example.

Approvals: Miles Thornton, Ravi Menon, Benji Okafor, Allison Grant.

## Merge
- Squash merged to `main` on 2026-01-10.
- Squash commit message: "policy-engine: deterministic signal hierarchy evaluation (v2 schema)"
Adds deterministic evaluation of failover trigger signals in the routing policy engine. Introduces a versioned config schema for signal hierarchy and corroboration rules. No behavior change unless `signal_hierarchy.v2` is enabled.

Motivation: SDKs across Python/TypeScript/Go have diverged slightly in retry semantics and streaming ergonomics which complicates downstream client code and our recommended defaults for production workloads. This PR introduces a small, explicit DSL for retry profiles that encodes jitter/clock-drift-aware backoff windows and a compact compatibility layer for streaming primitives so polyglot clients observe the same resume/close behavior and fewer surprising timeouts. Scope: 1) Add jitter-aware retry profile DSL (name/value mapping, preset loader, and deterministic unit tests). 2) Implement a lightweight stream compatibility adapter in each SDK that normalizes: close order, cancellation propagation, and final chunk detection. 3) Coordinate minor version bumps and lockfile updates: py-sdk->2.3.0, ts-sdk->1.9.0, go-sdk->1.4.1. 4) Backwards-compatible migration helpers and changelog entries. Key changes: - retry: new RetryProfile type with parameters: base_delay_ms, max_delay_ms, jitter_strategy (full|decorrelated|none), max_attempts, retryable_codes. We expose a preset loader that loads recommended profiles from the redwood server or falls back to baked-in presets. - jitter: introduce auth-refresh jitter window (50-500ms) to avoid synchronized token refresh storms during high concurrency. - streaming: CompactStreamCompatAdapter available in all SDKs; introduces a 2-step close handshake (client-close -> graceful drain -> final-ack) and idempotent resume token semantics to prevent duplicated chunks on resume. - ergonomics: small API polishing: Python async iterator gains .close_now() helper; TS exposes withAbortSignal() view; Go adds Context-aware Reader wrapper. Testing: unit tests added for deterministic backoff, simulated concurrent token refresh to assert bounded burst, cross-language integration harness exercised via the existing interop test suite (all green on CI). Migration notes: existing Retry constructors remain supported; to opt into jitter-aware behavior callers must use RetryProfile.load("recommended") or pass jitter_strategy in the constructor. Release impact: non-breaking for typical users; opt-in benefits lower retry storm risk and more predictable streaming resumes. Rollout: rolled to staged canary customers and feature-flagged in hosted for two weeks before global enablement. References: Linear ENG-2103 (retry convergence), SUP-6543 (support case showing duplicated stream chunks).
Maya Chen: Nice concise DSL. Two asks: 1) add an example showing how a user overrides the preset in the hosted fallback case, 2) can we make jitter window defaults configurable via env var for Dedicated?
Sanjay Patel (author): Added a short example to examples/ and added a DEDICATED_JITTER_MS env hook that the preset loader will read. Updated tests to include env var path.
Elena Rodriguez: Integration harness passes but I observed a flaky TS test on CI intermittently failing around abort-signal timing. Please add an explicit 20ms slack in the harness.
Sanjay Patel (author): Added 20ms slack and a deterministic fake clock in the TS harness. Re-ran CI.
Jonah Lee: API ergonomics look good. One nit: consider naming .close_now() -> .abort_immediate() to make semantics explicit. Not blocking.
Sanjay Patel (author): Kept .close_now() for now to keep parity with other helpers; added docstring clarifying immediate abort semantics and a link to a future API rename RFC.
Maya Chen: Approved after changes.
Elena Rodriguez: Approved.
Jonah Lee: Approved.
Merged via squash with message: 'Introduce jitter-aware retry DSL + compact stream compat adapters; bump SDK versions' by Maya Chen. Included coordinated SDK version bumps and updated changelogs. Changelog entries for each SDK were added. No rollback required during canary. Merged to main and tagged for release pipeline.
SDKs: Add jitter-aware RetryProfile presets to reduce token-refresh storms and a compact stream compatibility adapter that normalizes resume/cancel semantics across Python/TS/Go. Minor version bumps: python 2.3.0, typescript 1.9.0, go 1.4.1. Migration: opt-in via RetryProfile.load("recommended") or pass jitter_strategy; streaming resumes improved without code changes but enable feature flag to roll out gradually.

Motivation: We observed two related failure modes during the outage window on 2026-02-08: abrupt full-tenant admission drops when an overloaded regional slowpath flipped circuits, and a correlated KV-cache pressure that caused long tail latency during rapid tenant replays. This PR introduces a coordinated, telemetry-driven 'staggered admission' failsafe plus a transparent regional-bridge that keeps traffic flowing via a lightweight forwarding path while preserving KV-coherency and SLO accounting.

Summary of changes: 1) admission_controller: implement a two-stage admit ramp (soft-reject -> graded-queue -> normal) with epoched tokens per tenant; 2) bridge_manager: new transparent bridge mode that can forward select routes to a warm standby region while preserving KV drain ordering; 3) telemetry: add bridging and admit-stage metrics + redo existing SLO counters so the SLO enforcer charges tenants correctly during staged admission; 4) hotfix utilities: kv-drain helper script and a short rollout playbook.

Why this is different: Unlike previous blunt load-shed patches, the staggered admit preserves request shaping — short requests and health-checks still pass in early stages while heavy batched jobs are deferred. The transparent bridge keeps clients online by routing to compatible model variants in a standby region without requiring DNS flips or long failover windows. Both are designed to be reversible with a single controller flag.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc updated (docs/ops/regional-bridge.md) - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Telemetry added and validated in staging - [x] Rollout plan written and exercised in canary - [x] Post-merge incident playbook attached

Testing and validation: Unit tests cover admit token lifecycles and queue transitions. Integration E2E simulates elevated latency in region A and asserts the bridge activates, KV-drain script preserves write-order, and SLO billing tags are applied (SLO tag emitted: admission_stage=soft). Staging rollout executed against two tenants with synthetic spike on 2026-02-11. Observed 3-5% higher latency for degraded requests but 99.9% successful responses vs previous 15% error rate.

Rollout strategy: 1) feature flag off in main; 2) enable central controller in staging for 24h with canary tenants; 3) enable bridge passive mode (no traffic forwarding) and assert metrics; 4) flip to active for 1% traffic with slow ramp; 5) monitor SLO / KV pressure dashboards for 1h buckets; 6) incremental increase to 25% then full. Backout is a single flag revert and a forced kv-drain abort if bridge misbehaves.

Backward compatibility: New admit stages are additive; default behaviour unchanged. Bridge only forwards routes if a model compatibility predicate is satisfied. No client-visible API changes.

Related work: complements ENG-4401 (proactive-slowpath-prefetch) and SRE-119 (regional failover runbook).

Notes for on-call: run scripts/hotfix/kv-drain.sh in the target region before promoting heavy traffic; telemetry metric names: redwood.admit.stage, redwood.bridge.forward_count, redwood.kvdrain.lag_ms.

Merging notes: squash-merged with a short commit message, rollouts coordinated with SRE team and Solutions Engineering.
Diego Alvarez: Nice approach. Can we guarantee write-order preservation when the bridge forwards to a standby in a different region? Suggest making kv-drain idempotent and instrumenting per-tenant lag.
Maya Chen: Answered — kv-drain uses per-tenant monotonically increasing drain tokens; the bridge manager attaches the same token before forwarding. Added per-tenant lag metric. See commit d3a0f41.
Priya Kapoor: CI flakes in integration on first run (timeout on E2E). Please add a retry and shorten default simulated timeout so the test is stable in CI.
Maya Chen: Added deterministic retry backoff and shortened simulated network latency in tests. Re-ran CI; integration now stable.
Noah Patel: Approving pending one telemetry naming nit — prefer redwood.bridge.forward_count to be a histogram for burst analysis.
Maya Chen: Switched metric to histogram in bridging_metrics.yaml and updated dashboards.
payload.title: Add staggered admission failsafe and transparent regional bridge

payload.body:
Motivation:
Clusters with aggressive warm-pool prewarming were repeatedly overshooting provisioned capacity for bursty tenants. The existing warm-pool controller allowed rapid growth whenever recent tail spikes were observed, which produced oscillation when spikes were short-lived or noisy (observed during cross-tenant promotional traffic). This PR introduces two complementary components: (1) a bounded warmth regulator that enforces growth cadence and headroom constraints on warm pools, and (2) a utilization-echo reporter that produces lightweight per-pool and per-tenant utilization sketches for more robust admission decisions and offline analysis.

What this change does (high level):
- BoundedWarmthRegulator: A controller that constrains warm-pool ramp-up by applying a per-pool cadence (min-warm-growth-interval) and a proportional cap relative to pool target size and current spare headroom. Growth is throttled when historical spike persistence is low; the regulator also exposes backoff signals to the autoscaler to avoid double-scaling.
- DelegatedEphemeralCredit: A small borrowing API allowing tenants to consume ephemeral credits from a warm pool for short bursts without immediately expanding fleet capacity. Credits decay automatically and are reconciled to prevent long-term drift.
- UtilizationEchoReporter: Periodically samples per-tenant and per-pool active concurrency and token throughput and emits HDR sketches + lightweight percentile samplings (p50/p90/p99) to Prometheus and a compact daily rollup to S3 for long-term analysis. The reporter intentionally samples at variable rates to bound instrumentation overhead.
- Feature flags: gated behind runtime flags (feature.warmth_regulator=true by default on canary) and a tenant opt-out list for customers with custom SLAs.
- Safety and rollback: regulator defaults are conservative; we added automatic fail-open behavior if the regulator detects sustained under-utilization.

Why this is different from previous approaches:
- Moves away from purely reactive prewarming driven by short-window maxima; instead combines persistence-aware cadence with proportional caps to avoid knee-jerk provisioning.
- Delegated credits let us satisfy short spikes cheaply without altering long-term commitment curves.
- UtilizationEchoReporter supplies richer, denoised signals (HDR sketches) that downstream controllers and offline tools can consume to adjust smoothing parameters.

Commits (summary):
- Add BoundedWarmthRegulator controller and unit tests
- Implement DelegatedEphemeralCredit lifecycle and reconciliation
- Add UtilizationEchoReporter, Prometheus metrics, and S3 daily rollup serializer
- Wire feature flags and tenant opt-out configuration
- Update autoscaler to consume regulator backoff signals
- Add e2e tests exercising short spikes and credit consumption

Files changed (high level):
- services/autoscaler/controllers/warmth_regulator.go
- services/autoscaler/controllers/warmth_regulator_test.go
- services/autoscaler/credit/delegated_credit.go
- services/autoscaler/credit/reconcile_test.go
- telemetry/reporters/utilization_echo.go
- telemetry/prometheus/metrics.yaml (adds new metric families)
- infra/feature_flags/defaults.yaml
- docs/ops/warmth-regulator.md
- e2e/tests/warmth_regulator_spike.sh

Testing:
- Unit tests added for regulator cadence logic, credit lifecycle, and reporter sampling (coverage ~86% for modified packages).
- Local e2e script simulates 1,000 tenants with randomized spike durations; tested across 3 warm-pool size profiles.
- Canary rollout on staging cluster ran for 48h with regulated on 20% of pools; CI ran full integration and linting. Initial CI run had a flaky metrics exporter test which was stabilized by retry logic.

Observability and metrics exposed:
- warm_pool_regulator.growth_decisions{pool=\"p1\",decision=\"throttle|allow|failopen\"} counter
- warm_pool_regulator.backoff_seconds gauge (seconds regulator advises autoscaler to wait)
- delegated_credit.consumed_total{tenant=\"t123\"} counter
- delegated_credit.active_credits gauge
- utilization_echo.hdr_sketch{pool=\"p1\",tenant=\"t123\"} (base64-encoded compact sketch in logs for offline aggregator)
- utilization_echo.sampled_percentiles{quantile=\"0.5|0.9|0.99\"} gauge
Notes: HDR sketches are emitted to the long-term S3 rollup only; Prometheus receives sampled percentiles to keep cardinality low.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind flags.
2) Enable on internal staging pools for 48h, observe warm_pool_regulator.growth_decisions and delegated_credit.consumed_total.
3) Enable on 10% of production pools for 24h with automated rollback if pooled headroom drops below safety threshold for 10m.
4) Gradually increase to 50% and then full rollout.

Backward compatibility / migration notes:
- Existing autoscaler behaviour unchanged unless feature flag enabled.
- DelegatedEphemeralCredit persists short-lived entries to existing credit ledger (compatible schema migration with add-only columns).

Related work:
- Refs: ENG-4123 (warm-pool stabilization spike), ENG-4199 (credit accounting improvements), and SUP-8842 (support ticket describing repeated overprovisioning during marketing promos).

Questions for reviewers / open items:
- Are HDR sketch emission intervals acceptable given S3 cost constraints? We set daily rollups by default and allow per-organization overrides.
- DelegatedEphemeralCredit uses a conservative decay constant; ops may want a knob exposed in Console.

Merge outcome:
- Squash-merged after minor test flake fix and two approvals. Canary signals confirmed a 27% reduction in sustained warmset growth and a 9% improvement in average hourly utilization for canaried pools.

Introduce a bounded warm-pool regulator to stabilize warm-set growth and a utilization-echo reporter that emits tenant- and pool-level utilization sketches and sampled percentiles. Improves scale stability and reduces sustained overprovisioning for spiky tenants.
Diego Martinez: Left a couple of nits in warmth_regulator.go; please add a comment explaining the choice of 30s sampling window. Also request a small defensive check if pool.TargetSize==0.
Ava Chen: Addressed nits, added comment and defensive guard. Updated unit test to include zero-target pool case.
Sofia Patel: Can we limit HDR sketch cardinality? Suggest emitting per-pool only and skipping tenants below 0.1% traffic — otherwise Prometheus will explode.
Ava Chen: Reporter now skips micro-tenants (configurable threshold) and only exposes percentiles to Prometheus; sketches go to S3 as rollups.
Ethan Brooks: Approve after CI fixes. Verified canary metrics and rollback triggers. Would like an ops runbook entry for emergency disable.
Ava Chen: Added docs/ops/warmth-regulator.md with rollback steps and feature flag overrides.

Problem: Under heavy concurrent streaming load the SSE reassembly window could be prematurely backpressured at the wrong byte offset, which in practice produced truncated UTF-8 runes, mis-ordered tool/function-call sentinels, and unrecoverable partial JSON payloads in the OpenAI-compat layer. This manifested as two visible classes of errors: 1) cheap client connections that were hit by backpressure would see mid-codepoint truncation and a "malformed UTF-8" parse path; 2) multi-segment events with function_call markers could have event boundaries shifted across the backpressure cut, producing interleaved tokens and duplicated sentinel sequences. Motivation: stabilize streaming output for customers using structured responses and function/tool calling (especially in platforms bridging OpenAI-compatible clients). Goal: ensure backpressure aligns to fragment/event boundaries when possible, transparently rescue incomplete UTF-8 runes and partial JSON fragments, and preserve strict ordering for function-call sentinels so downstream parsers never receive duplicated or reordered function tokens. Summary of changes: - Introduced a boundary-aware backpressure window in the sse/streamer layer that prefers draining up to the next event terminator (

 or data: ) when under pressure, falling back after a short timeout. - Added a UTF-8 rune reassembly helper: keep up to 4 trailing bytes in the fragment buffer and attempt a low-cost validation/rescue pass before emitting; if rescue fails, emit an explicit resync marker ("event: __resync__

") so clients can fast-fail or retry. - Implemented a function-call sentinel latch in the openai_compat module: an emitted function_call start token is never split across a forced backpressure cut; if the event is large, we escalate to an internal short-lived buffer and schedule a high-priority flush. - Added sequence-anchor metadata to SSE spans so the stream-stitcher can enforce relative ordering for concurrent shards and avoid duplicate sentinel replays during reassembly. - Extended the sse parser tests with fuzzed partial-byte splits and integrated a deterministic replay harness used in the failing incident noted in SUP-1287. Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag `sse_boundary_backpressure=true` and default-on for Hosted API; dedicated customers can toggle via runtime config. The change is backwards-compatible at the protocol level: when the feature is off, behavior is unchanged. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for boundary alignment and rune rescue - [x] integration test with function_call sentinel stress - [x] CI flake triage and rerun pass - [x] added logging gated behind debug flag for post-deploy diagnostics - [x] Linear tickets linked for followups Impact and risk: The change touches the hot path in the serving runtime and was optimized to add a bounded memory window and a short timeout to avoid long-held buffers. We observed <0.7% p50 latency regression in the worst-case synthetic throughput test but eliminated a ~3% error tail caused by malformed frames. Follow-ups: - ENG-4302: add opt-out telemetry for customers that need raw byte-level stream semantics - ENG-4339: consider a client hint header to prefer strict emit vs boundary-rescue

Diego Ramos: Can we make the rescue heuristic opt-in via a runtime flag? I want Dedicated customers to be able to opt-out. — ACK, made it a flag and default-on for Hosted.
Lina Chen: The UTF-8 rescue could mask real data corruption. Please add a resync marker so clients can detect when we did best-effort repair. — Added explicit event: __resync__ marker when rescue fails.
Marcus O'Neill: Stress test results look good but observe the p50 regression. Do we have telemetry to measure customer impact? — Added sse_boundary_rescues_total and a toggleable debug log; will follow up with ENG-4302 for telemetry opt-outs.
Anika Patel (author): addressed comments, pushed new commit; re-ran flaky CI and fixed a race in the test harness that caused intermittent failures.
