payload.body:
Fix: Prevent double-throttling during regional failover by coordinating tenant throttle windows across regions and making circuit resets idempotent. Includes tests and dashboards to monitor per-tenant throttle rate.
Context and motivation:
We observed multiple incidents where tenants experienced compounded throttling during cross-region failovers. The root cause was twofold: (1) the failover handoff path could temporarily apply a local tenant throttle in the target region while the source region still held a soft throttle; (2) circuit resets triggered by failover performed a non-idempotent KV eviction which could cause a tenant to be over-evicted and re-enter throttling sooner than intended.

This PR introduces a time-windowed tenant throttler that coordinates a short-lived leader token for per-tenant throttles across regions (windowed consensus) and a safe, idempotent reset token for KV/circuit resets. The goal is to make graceful degradation deterministic during failover windows and avoid double-application of throttles.

Design summary (high level):
- Add a lightweight reset_coordinator service that piggybacks on the existing region heartbeat stream; it issues a transient UTC-window token (window_id + expiry) for tenant throttles and resets.
- Throttler now accepts a window_token; when a region receives a handoff it consults local coordinator state to decide whether it should apply a new throttle or inherit an existing window token. Tokens are designed to be short-lived (default 6s) to limit cross-region staleness but long enough to cover KV handoff latency spikes.
- Circuit reset path changed to emit a reset_token (idempotent UUID tied to window_token). Applying a reset with the same reset_token is a no-op to prevent double-eviction.
- Fallback: if coordinator is unreachable, throttler falls back to deterministic tie-breaker (region-id hash) plus extended backoff to avoid immediate double-throttle while still allowing traffic.

What changed (summary of patches):
- src/serving/throttler.go: implement window-token acceptance, new decision path for applyThrottle().
- src/serving/consensus/reset_coordinator.go: new coordinator component (keeps in-memory window state, exposes minimal API).
- internal/kv/reset_idempotency.go: idempotent reset helper, persistent short-lived marker in local metadata store.
Lena Morris (2026-02-26): Requested changes - please make window duration configurable and add a defend-against-time-drift test for coordinator. Also include a short note in the RFC about token expiry semantics.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-27): Addressed - added config flag 'tenant_throttle.window_seconds' with default 6s and added TestCoordinatorClockDrift in handler_test.go. Updated RFC. PTAL.
Diego Alvarez (2026-03-01): Comment - we should avoid doing a network call on the hot path. Confirmed coordinator lookup is in-memory with eventual async refresh; added a note and microbenchmark. Approved after that clarification.
Sophie Chen (2026-03-03): Approved - tests look comprehensive. Suggest watching tenant-throttle rate per-region for a deployment window.
payload.title: windowed-tenant-priority-throttler-with-consensus-reset-hotpatch

payload.body:
Motivation: Some tenants observed large cost spikes from naive prefill decisions during bursty traffic. This PR introduces a prefetch policer that applies conservative token-prefill allowances per-tenant and a quant-fallback conductor that orchestrates safe transitions to lower-precision model variants when capacity or unit economics dictate. The goal is predictable unit economics while preserving latency SLOs where possible.

What this PR does (high level): 1) prefetch policer: a light-weight admission controller that consumes tenant budget profiles and recent warm-start telemetry to allow/deny or rate-limit prefill requests; supports soft/hard quotas and graceful degrade policies. 2) quant-fallback conductor: runtime coordinator that executes a 3-step safe transition (probe -> audition -> promote) to quantized model variants; performs output-sanity checks and automatic rollback when eval metrics degrade. 3) CLI: cost-manifest validator and dry-run simulator for tenant teams to preview how policies would apply to historical traces. 4) unit-econ smoke harness: small integration test that runs sampled traces in CI to detect large per-token cost regressions when policies are active.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in issue ENG-3912 - [x] Implementation of policer and conductor services - [x] Runtime hooks for model routing and cache-key tagging - [x] End-to-end tests for safe rollback behavior - [x] CLI docs and examples - [x] Telemetry: new metrics and traces instrumented

Commits summary: - Add prefetch policer service, admission API and in-memory policy store - Introduce quant-fallback conductor and state machine for safe transitions - Add policy CLI: validate / dry-run / export - Telemetry: prefill.allow/deny counters, quant.fallback.attempt/success/fail metrics - Tests: e2e smoke harness and unit tests for policy edge cases - Docs: CLI usage and operational runbook

Files changed (high level): - services/prefill/policer.go (new) - services/conductor/quant_fallback.go (new) - cli/cost-manifest/validate.go (new) - telemetry/metrics_registry.go (minor additions) - serving/router.go (hook points for policer/conductor) - integration/tests/prefill_smoke_test.go (new) - docs/ops/prefetch-policer.md (new)

CI and validation: CI run showed one flaky test initially (integration/prefill_smoke_test) due to nondeterministic synthetic traces; fixed by seeding generator and adding a retry on transient network binds. Full pipeline now passes (unit, integration, lint). Performance bench: small overhead (p50 +2ms) on cold starts when policer evaluates; typical steady-state shows no measurable latency regression thanks to async evaluation and cached policy decisions.

Review conversation snapshot: Marco Rivera: "Nice separation between admission control and fallback orchestration; can you add a circuit-breaker metric for the conductor to detect thrash?" Aisha Patel (author): "Added quant.fallback.circuit_open_count and test coverage; added note to runbook for knob overrides." Lina Zhang: "Concern: how does this interact with tenant Dedicated pools?" Aisha: "Policer consults tenant capacity hints; for Dedicated SKUs we default to permissive mode and only apply soft-prefetch caps unless explicitly configured." Tomás Ortega: "CLI is useful — add an example mapping a trace to policy output." Aisha: "Added three example traces and an explanatory section in docs. "

Operational notes and runbook highlights: - Default policy is permissive for enterprise Dedicated customers; strict for self-serve tenants with >10% warmup cost variance. - Safe-mode: when conductor sees >2 consecutive quant audition failures it opens circuit for 30 minutes and annotates traces. - Telemetry to watch: prefill.deny_rate, quant.fallback.success_rate, quant.fallback.rollback_rate, unit_econ.delta_cost_pct. - Suggested alert: quant.fallback.rollback_rate > 5% over 15m triggers on-call.

Merge details: squashed merge. Post-merge: deployed to staging with feature flag prefetch_policer.enabled=false by default; slowly enabled for two pilot tenants during the rollout window. No incident during rollout; pilot tenants reported 8-12% reduction in prefill-related token spend for bursty traces.

Follow-ups: - ENG-4110: policy-as-code export/import across tenants (separate PR) - Add long-term storage for policy decisions for offline auditing - Add adaptive thresholds based on observed unit econ deltas (research spike planned)
Adds a tenant-facing prefetch policer and runtime conductor that coordinates quantized fallbacks; includes CLI tooling to validate cost-manifests and a small unit-econ smoke harness.
Marco Rivera: please add a circuit-breaker metric for conductor; consider backoff for repeated auditions.
Lina Zhang: verify interactions with Dedicated capacity and document defaults.
Tomás Ortega: include CLI examples mapping traces to policy decisions.

payload.body:
Problem: Customers with mixed latency/cost SLOs often leave batching/caching/quantization defaults untouched. That produces suboptimal unit economics for tail workloads and bursty patterns. Motivation: introduce a lightweight routing and suggestion layer (Cost Scribe) that records per-route micro-econ signal, uses a latency-aware quantization suggester to create conservative quant profiles, and surfaces safe defaults in the Console so product engineers can opt-in without manual experimentation. This PR wires three pieces: 1) A routing heuristic that tags requests with a cost_economy score (serving/router/cost_scribe_router.go). Motivation: cold-start and microburst costs remain a top contributor to token-unit spend for low-traffic tenants. This PR adds a warmup heuristic rewriter that ingests historical prefill/kv-cache hit traces and compiles tenant-specific warmstart presets (compact prefill plans + safe decay schedules). The objective is to reduce unnecessary prefill tokens while maintaining latency SLOs.

What this PR does (summary):
- New analysis pass (services/prefill/warmup_rewriter.py) that turns time-series warm traces into compact warmstart profiles: sequences of prefetch shapes + TTLs.
- Tenant profile serializer in Go (services/prefill/profiles/tenant_profile_serializer.go) to persist presets to the config store with versioning and signatures.
- Prefill heatmap collector (telemetry/prefill_heatmap_collector.sql) to backfill required aggregated metrics for the rewriter.
- Console UI toggle + preview (console/ui/prefill-settings.tsx) so SRE/product can preview warm presets per tenant before rollout.
- Integration test harness and unit tests (tests/prefill/test_warmup_rewriter.py) plus a small CLI inspector (pkg/cli/prefill_inspector/main.go) for on-demand previews.
- Helm values and docs: charts/redwood-prefill/values.yaml and docs/ops/warmup-presets.md

Design notes: the rewriter uses a conservative compression heuristic: find repeated prefix patterns in observed prefill traces, collapse contiguous prefill events into a single compact plan with estimated TTLs and a confidence score. When confidence < threshold (configurable via console), the runtime will use the legacy conservative warmup behavior. This keeps the change non-breaking and safe for early rollouts.

Small illustrative snippet from warmup_rewriter.py: 
"""
# simplified: collapse contiguous prefill events into a compact step
def collapse(events):
    steps = []
    cur = []
    for e in events:
        if cur and e.start - cur[-1].end < GAP_THRESHOLD:
            cur.append(e)
        else:
            if cur:
                steps.append(compress(cur))
            cur = [e]
    if cur:
        steps.append(compress(cur))
    return steps
"""

Motivation: Recent incident analysis (SUP-3345) showed that sudden client-side retries can flood a single region's serving queue and exhaust capacity, causing cascading fallbacks and degraded p99 latency. This PR implements a graded priority decayer plus TTL-backed backoff that reduces the steady-state pressure from retry storms while preserving tail latency for high-priority requests.

What this change does: - Adds a GradedPrioritizer component that assigns a priority score to incoming requests based on route, token-tier, and recent success history. Priority decays over time using an exponential TTL decay window (configurable). - Implements a per-region token-bucket throttle that takes the graded priority into account; low-priority requests are admitted only if tokens are available or if they pass a fast-path for critical routes. - Adds a short-lived TTL backoff entry for detected retry loops: if a request is retried more than N times within M seconds, subsequent attempts get applied backoff weight for T seconds. - Wire up canary rollout policy (10% of traffic in region during first 1h, bump to 50% after checks) and automatic rollback on p95/p99 regressions. - Observability: metrics (region.prioritizer.admit_rate, region.prioritizer.drop_rate, region.prioritizer.ttl_entries, region.prioritizer.avg_priority), tracing tags, and two Grafana panels for quick health checks. - Tests: unit tests for the prioritizer and integration test that simulates retry storms with synthetic load.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-4821) - [x] Unit tests for prioritizer and TTL decay - [x] Integration test validating canary behaviour - [x] Metrics and dashboards added - [x] Canary rollout config + automatic rollback threshold - [x] Docs: brief runbook update in reliability/README.md

High-level commits: - introduce graded prioritizer core loop and config - add per-region token-bucket throttle and admit/drop logic - TTL backoff store with expiry and metrics - integrate prioritizer into request router path - add tests and observability wiring - canary rollout manifests and config

Files touched (high level): pkg/serving/prioritizer.go, pkg/serving/prioritizer_test.go, pkg/serving/region_throttle.go, pkg/serving/ttl_backoff_store.go, internal/observability/metrics_register.go, deployments/canary/prioritizer-canary.yaml, docs/reliability/README.md, pkg/router/middleware.go, e2e/tests/retry_storm_sim.go

Why unique: This approach focuses on decaying priority over time (instead of immediate blackholing) and couples that decay with TTL backoff to reduce repeated pressure from retry loops while keeping high-priority traffic unaffected. The per-region token-bucket respects existing SLO allocations and integrates with our existing smart-routing fallbacks.

Rollout plan: - Merge to main behind feature flag prioritizer.enabled=false - Deploy canary manifest to one replica in us-west-2 with prioritizer.enabled=true at 10% traffic - Monitor metrics for 60 minutes; if region.prioritizer.drop_rate > 5% or p99 latency regresses by >10%, auto-rollback. - Gradually ramp to 50% and then 100% across regions after manual review.

Related: ENG-4987 (observability requirements), SUP-3345 (incident that motivated fix).
Priya Malhotra: Nice clean design. Two asks: 1) make the default decay window conservative (30s) to avoid starving downstream caches; 2) add a unit test for the decay boundary condition.
Ethan Park: Addressed both points in the second commit. Default decay moved to 30s and added decay boundary test (prioritizer_test.go::TestDecayBoundary).
Sofia Turner: I ran the canary locally with the synthetic storm; admit_rate looks good but observed a small memory bump in ttl_backoff_store under heavy churn. Please defend memory usage or add a cap.
Ethan Park: Added a max-entries config and eviction LRU for ttl_backoff_store; measured mem usage in integration CI. Details in comments of ttl_backoff_store.go.
Carlos Rivera: Approving pending e2e stability run and final CI green. Consider adding a short blurb in the runbook for SRE response during early rollout.
Ethan Park: Added runbook blurb and bumped canary monitoring thresholds. CI green on final run.
Introduces a graded request prioritizer with TTL-based backoff for regional request queues. Improves resilience against sudden regional traffic spikes by decaying priority over time and applying per-region token-bucket throttles. Includes observability and a canary rollout plan.

Context: Our monolithic presubmit lint runner has become a bottleneck for rapid iteration — changes to TypeScript projects block unrelated Go/Scala/Docs changes and large dependency churn PRs cause repeated flakiness. This PR decouples language/runtime lint execution into lightweight runtime-specific runners, introduces a small dependency-curator helper that annotates dependency update PRs with a stability score, and adds a presubmit prioritizer to fast-path hotpath checks for low-latency feedback. Motivation: reduce presubmit turnaround for high-velocity teams, improve signal-to-noise for dep-updates, and make staged rollouts of lint rule upgrades safer.

Changes (high level): - Split the single .github/presubmit job into per-runtime lint runners (node-lint, go-lint, python-lint, docs-lint) with a shared minimal launcher. - Add tools/dep-curator: a small Go binary that computes a heuristic stability score for a dependency (based on release cadence, semver, vulnerability tags from DB) and writes status/context to dependency PRs. - Add scripts/presubmit-prioritizer.py: inspects changed files in a PR and triggers only the subset of runtimes that touch the changed paths; optionally triggers a full lint when a config/infra file changes. - Introduce a lightweight presubmit cache key based on changed directories to fast-skip irrelevant runners. - Update docs and contributor guide with migration notes and rollback plan. Checklist: [x] Design doc linked (ENG-1892) [x] Unit tests for prioritizer script [x] Integration smoke on ephemeral runners [x] Canary rollout to a 10% subset of active repos using repo flag [x] CI green on second run Known tradeoffs/risks: - Slightly more YAML in workflows; mitigated with templateization. - Dep-curator uses a best-effort heuristic and should not be relied on as a blocker; it only annotates and suggests labels. Migration steps: - Roll out workflow changes in canary mode for 2 days. - Observe presubmit latency and queue depth (console dashboards updated). - If regressions, revert to previous workflow via rollback branch hook. Rollout & follow-ups: - Add a nightly job that recalculates dep-curator scores for open dependency PRs. - Add opt-in strict gating for specific teams where dep stability matters more. Why this is different from similar past PRs: instead of trimming CI matrix or batching tests, this PR focuses on separation of runtime execution and active prioritization per-PR to reduce end-to-end feedback latency while providing structured metadata (stability score) for dependency automation.
Marco Chen (reviewer): Can we keep the monolith as a fallback path? If a templated job fails, we should still be able to run the old combined job. Author: added canary flag and a fallback job that can be enabled via repo settings.
Lena Ortega (reviewer): dep-curator sounds useful, but please ensure it never blocks merges. Suggestion: annotate only and add an opt-in action to auto-merge when score>0.8. Author: implemented annotation-only behavior and added an opt-in label automation in contrib/.
Priya Nair (approver): Verified that the prioritizer reduces Node-only presubmit runs on a sample of 150 PRs; latency improved by ~40%. Approving pending minor nit on caching script (fixed).
CI automation: lint and test passed after second attempt; first run hit flaky network test, rerun cleared it.
- Decouple presubmit lint into runtime-specific jobs to reduce feedback latency. - Add tools/dep-curator to annotate dependency PRs with a stability score (non-blocking). - Introduce presubmit prioritizer to only run relevant runtimes per-PR. Impact: faster presubmit for most PRs; no breaking changes to developer workflow.

payload.body:
Motivation: reduce tail latency and improve sustained throughput for medium-length sequences (32-512 tokens) while retaining stable KV cache behavior under continuous batching. Existing prefetched-KV code warms individual KV slots aggressively which causes redundant device memory traffic for mixed sequence workloads and increases p95 latency when many concurrent streams start/stop. Additionally, the rotary/rope offset handling in our fused-attention path added per-token remap overhead that scales poorly for interleaved micro-batches.

What this PR does: introduces a hybrid prefetch coalescer and a rotary offset simplifier in the redwood attention runtime. The coalescer groups prefetched KV ranges across inflight requests and issues fewer contiguous device IOs; it is continuous-batch-aware (maintains coalescing window boundaries across batch flushes). The rotary offset simplifier replaces the per-token modular arithmetic with a compact offset remap table for commonly used sequence deltas and falls back to the old path only for rare long-offset cases. Together these reduce memory bandwidth, reduce kernel launch overhead, and produce a cleaner fast-path for fused-attention kernels.

Design notes: - Prefetch coalescer: maintain a small (configurable) coalescing buffer per execution stream that accumulates KV page ranges for up to N in-flight requests or M tokens before emitting a merged prefetch. The algorithm is heuristic-driven: prefer contiguous ranges, merge adjacent ranges if gap <= threshold (default 64 bytes), and respect max prefetch size to avoid evict thrash. The coalescer exposes metrics (coalesced_prefetch_count, merged_bytes, wasted_prefetch_bytes) for telemetry.
- Rotary offset simplifier: build a remap table keyed by (rotary_base_mod, requested_offset) with an LRU-style warm path. For offsets seen in the last L requests, remap is O(1) and avoids integer division/mod; for misses we compute remap and insert into the table. Table size defaults to 2048 entries per device-context and is shardable across worker threads.
- KV slot compaction: small change to the lazy-KV eviction policy to favor contiguous freed ranges to increase mergeability.
- Fallbacks: behavior remains identical to previous release (bit-for-bit on outputs) except for perf-internal ordering differences; correctness tests validate outputs identical to previous kernels for the fast-path.

Files changed (high level): runtime/attn/prefetch_coalescer.cc/h, runtime/attn/rotary_remap_table.cc/h, runtime/attn/hybrid_attn_dispatcher.cc, runtime/attn/tests/prefetch_coalescer_test.cc, kernels/fused_attn_launch.cu (fast-path hooks), infra/metrics/registry.yaml (new metrics), docs/perf/rotary-prefetch.md, bench/compare/pipelines/seq_bench.toml and a small update to CI to run the new microbench harness.

Benchmarks: microbench on A100-80GB and T4 (single-GPU), mixed workload (uniform mix of seq lengths 32/64/128/256), continuous-batch mode enabled. Numbers below are median of 5 runs.
- A100 (32 batch, concurrency 16): throughput +18% tokens/s, p50 latency -10%, p95 latency -9%.
- A100 (dynamic batching, concurrency 64): throughput +22% tokens/s, p95 latency -11%.
- T4 (small memory): throughput +11% tokens/s, p95 latency -7%, observed 12% reduction in DRAM bandwidth for KV loads.
Memory: average extra remap table memory ~12KB per stream; coalescer buffer ~64KB worst-case.

Testing: unit tests for remap table and coalescer (deterministic seeding), integration tests that compare outputs against baseline fused-attention for 200 random seeds, and end-to-end bench harness that validates stability under 10k synthetic requests. CI updated to include perf-run stage for PRs labeled with perf.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.attn.hybrid_prefetch.enabled=false by default on main; enable in canary fleets for 48h under controlled traffic. Metrics and alerting dashboards created: pref_coalesce_ratio, remap_hit_rate, avg_prefetch_bytes. If remap_hit_rate < 60% or pref_coalesce_ratio < 1.1 we automatically flip flag off for that fleet.

Related: ENG-1724 defines the continuous-batching use-cases and microbench harness, ENG-1740 requested bandwidth savings for Dedicated customers.

Notes on correctness: end-to-end model output unit tests are bit-identical for all tested model families (OPT, Llama-variants) for sequences < 1024 tokens; long sequence QA tests run with fallback path exercised.

Development checklist: - [x] Implementation - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Microbench harness - [x] Docs - [x] Perf dash + alerts - [x] Feature flag gate

Merge outcome: merged to main via squash.

Evan Cho: Can you explain the eviction policy change risk for Dedicated customers?
Anika: The change biases eviction toward contiguous free regions; it does not force different end-to-end eviction schedules, only the tie-breaker. We added unit tests and a canary with KV integrity checks.
Diego Alvarez: Microbench numbers look promising. Did you test with long-running steady-state traffic?
Anika: yes — 72h stability run on canary (internal) showed no regressions and stable remap hit-rate ~92%.
Priya Reddy: Falling back on misses is a potential perf cliff. How often do misses occur?
Anika: Misses are <8% in our mixed workloads; we also log misses as a trace event for offline analysis.
Evan Cho: approve after small doc wording fix.
Anika: fixed the docs and updated the metric names per feedback.
A100: +18-22% tokens/s for mixed seq; p95 -9 to -11%. T4: +11% tokens/s; p95 -7%. DRAM bandwidth for KV loads reduced up to 12% in representative traces. Remap hit rate median 92% under production-like mixes.
Introduce hybrid prefetch coalescer and rotary offset remap table to improve attention throughput and tail latency. Feature behind runtime flag; opt-in via canary. Metrics added: pref_coalesce_ratio, remap_hit_rate.
This PR focuses on runtime perf and is safe for fast rollout. Observability hooks added to detect regressions early. If issues occur, flip runtime.attn.hybrid_prefetch.enabled to false for the affected fleet.

Motivation: During a regional traffic surge we observed a compounding failure mode where long-lived streaming/gRPC connections were occasionally left in an indeterminate state (backend shard restart + half-closed client streams). Orphaned streams kept KV caches pinned and worker slots occupied; at the same time the hedged-retry path was triggering retries with insufficient jitter which multiplied load and pushed regional p99 latency above the SLO. This PR introduces a conservative connection reaper plus hedged-retry backoff tuning to prevent recreation storms and free stuck resources quickly.

What this change does: 1) Adds a connection reaper that detects streams with depleted heartbeats or no progress for a configurable TTL and gracefully drains them (emit a Disconnect event, release KV cache handles, increment reaper metrics). 2) Adds an exponential-jitter cap to hedged-retries and a sliding window rate-limit that prevents more than N hedged attempts per tenant per-second. 3) Introduces a safety gate: if reaper-triggered disconnects exceed a threshold we ramp hedged-retry suppression to avoid correlated fallback storms. 4) Adds telemetry (reaper.count, reaper.duration_ms, hedged_retry.suppressed_count, hedged_retry.jitter_ms_hist) and dashboards/alerts for SLO impact.

Rollback and safety: feature is behind runtime flags and defaults to conservative settings. Reaper TTL is 30s in the default hotpatch profile, hedged retry jitter floor of 50ms and cap 500ms. We also added a canary rollout plan to 10% of region instances, with auto-rollback when p99 increases or reaper disconnects spike >0.5% of requests in a 10m window.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc (link: Linear ENG-9786) - [x] Unit tests for reaper detection and release semantics - [x] Integration test that simulates backend shard restart + client half-close - [x] Telemetry + dashboards - [x] Canary rollout config and rollback thresholds - [x] Post-merge incident note template prepared

Testing notes: Local sim harness exercised 10k concurrent streams, induced backend restarts; reaper reclaimed stuck streams within expected TTL and hedged retry suppression prevented retry amplification. CI required a second integration run to stabilize flakiness in the streaming test harness (see CI comments).

Why this is different from previous changes: Prior PRs focused on tenant-level soft-quarantine and load-shedding; this PR targets the lower-level resource leak that can exacerbate those mechanisms. Fixing the leak reduces pressure on eviction and SLO throttlers and prevents cascading failover.

Related: Linear ENG-9786, SRE-1023, incident INT-549.

payload.body:
Context: We observe multi-tenant fleets holding reservations longer than needed because the autoscaler lacks a stable per-tenant elasticity signal. This manifests as wasted reserved capacity during transient low-traffic windows and imprecise decay decisions, which in turn increases unit costs and causes headroom to be misallocated. Motivation: Provide a low-cost, low-impact probe that produces a reproducible per-tenant utilization fingerprint and an aggregated reservation-decay estimate consumers (autoscaler, capacity advisor) can use. Goals: 1) Generate tenant elasticity signatures (time-series features + quantiles) without adding latency to inference paths. 2) Export a small set of decay metrics (instantaneous decay-rate estimate, confidence-weighted half-life, and synthetic warmup penalty) to the telemetry pipeline. 3) Allow autoscaler policies to consume these signals to make smoother decommit/decay decisions and perform conservative fast-path decommits when confidence is high. Design summary: - prober agent runs as a sidecar-like binary (non-blocking) that samples reservation utilization via internal lease and slot APIs. Sampling is rate-limited and windowed to avoid spikes. - elasticity signature: vector of features capturing short/medium/long window utilizations (1m/5m/30m), burstiness index, service-time-weighted occupancy, and observed refractory periods. - decay model: lightweight online exponential-decay estimator with Bayesian confidence scoring that produces a recommended decay half-life per tenant. - exporter: maps model outputs to telemetry metrics (redwood.dedicated.decay_half_life_seconds, redwood.dedicated.decay_confidence, redwood.dedicated.util_fingerprint_hash). Metrics are tagged with tenant_id, pool, and model_family. - Autoscaler integration: new optional input feature (decay_half_life_seconds + confidence) used by the DecommitPolicy to bias decommit aggressiveness; default behavior is a conservative smoothing factor to avoid oscillation. Implementation notes: - code lives under pkg/autoscaler/prober and pkg/autoscaler/decay; a small CLI in cmd/fleet-prober for on-demand probing; Helm values added to enable/disable per-pool. - sampling only reads lease state and local counters; no extra RPCs to inference runtime except optional KV-cache sampling when enabled (disabled by default). - defensive practices: fail-open exporter, rate-limits, feature flag gated via helm values (enableElasticityProber=false by default). Testing and results: - unit tests for estimator math and feature extraction. - integration e2e that runs synthetic tenant traces (stable, bursty, seasonal) against a local autoscaler harness. - performance benchmarks: prober CPU < 0.5 vCPU per node at 1k tenants, memory < 50 MB. - pilot on a small Dedicated fleet reduced reserved-but-idle capacity by ~9.6% (median) and lowered 95th percentile unnecessary warm slot time by 12%. Checklist: - [x] Feature implementation - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Helm toggle and documentation - [x] Observability (metrics + local debug logs) - [x] Rollout plan included Migration/rollout: Opt-in rollout via Helm: set enableElasticityProber=true for a pool. Start with read-only exporter to telemetry (no autoscaler consumption). After 2 weeks of telemetry validation, enable autoscaler consumption via config: autoscaler.decay.inputSource=prober. Rollback is a single Helm toggle. Related: ENG-1623 (autoscaler decay policy refactor), ENG-1702 (telemetry tagging standard). Risks and mitigations: - Risk: noisy signals cause premature decommits. Mitigation: confidence-weighted smoothing and conservative defaults; autoscaler will require confidence>0.7 to take aggressive actions. - Risk: prober overhead under very large tenant counts. Mitigation: adaptive sampling throttle and global pool-level cap. - Risk: tagging cardinality growth in metrics backend. Mitigation: fingerprint hashed to reduce cardinality; only a small set of exported metrics per tenant. Documentation: Added docs/ops/reservation-decay.md with signal semantics, rollout playbook, and runbook steps. Link to runbook included in the PR description. 
Adds a non-invasive probing agent that computes per-tenant elasticity signatures and an exporter that synthesizes reservation-decay metrics used by the Dedicated autoscaler. No customer-facing API changes. Opt-in via helm values. Improves reserved utilization and reduces unnecessary capacity holds.
Ravi Patel: Can you add a short note explaining how the confidence score is computed? The current comment is a bit high-level.
Author (Maya): Expanded estimator comments and added a helper docstring with the math and pseudocode.
Elena Garcia: Suggest lowering the default prober sampling rate for pools with >10k tenants; otherwise we'll overload node CPU.
Author (Maya): Added adaptive throttle that halves sampling rate above tenant thresholds and added a unit test for throttle behavior.
Thomas Nguyen: Integration test flaked once due to timeouts on CI; please confirm stable timeouts or retry logic.
Author (Maya): Increased e2e timeouts and added a deterministic seed for synthetic trace replay; reran CI.
Ravi Patel: Approve after small telemetry naming nit (use decay_half_life_seconds instead of half_life_secs).
Author (Maya): Renamed metric and updated docs and dashboards accordingly.

Motivation: clients have been handling rate limits and transient errors inconsistently across the OpenAI-compat endpoints (chat/completions/streaming) and tool/function-call routes. Two practical problems we observed: (1) backend 429/503 responses returned ambiguous Retry-After or custom header shapes that SDKs interpreted differently, causing hot loops or wasted retries; (2) streaming frames had informal transient error markers that made deterministic restart/dedup of tool calls difficult for server-side and edge SDKs. This PR introduces a minimal, backwards-compatible error envelope and a small set of well-documented headers to provide deterministic backoff guidance and explicit idempotency semantics for tool/function invocations. Summary of changes: - new response header X-Redwood-Backoff-Hint with comma-separated hint tokens (e.g. "backoff=exponential,initial=200,cap=20000") - X-Redwood-Retry-After-Ms: canonical millisecond retry hint for clients that prefer a single numeric value - unified JSON error envelope field retry_hint_ms and backoff_strategy in the error body for both unary and streaming terminal error events - clarified Idempotency-Key handling for tool/function calls: server-side dedupe scope is "tool-execution:<model>:<tool-name>", TTL 7 days, and duplicate requests return 409 with original result location when available - streaming protocol: introduce stream_resume_id for resumable client reconnects and frame-level "terminal_error" frame with structured envelope for deterministic replays - documented migration notes and SDK helpers for Python/TS to decode headers or fallback to Retry-After semantics Compatibility goals: - preserve existing 429/503 HTTP codes and OpenAI-style error objects where present; the new fields are additive and optional - SDKs should prefer X-Redwood-Retry-After-Ms when present; fall back to Retry-After (seconds) header otherwise - no behavior change for customers who do not opt-in to Idempotency-Key headers; default semantics remain at-most-once for non-tool endpoints Checklist: - [x] Add header parsing and response generation in openai-compat shims - [x] Emit stream_resume_id on session start for streaming endpoints - [x] Implement server-side dedupe lookup for Idempotency-Key on tool calls - [x] Add docs and SDK helpers (python + typescript) - [x] Add unit tests for header parsing, envelope shape, and streaming terminal frames - [x] Run integration test matrix against dedicated + hosted CI Notes/links: Related Linear: ENG-2413. See docs at /docs/openai-compat/backoff.md. This description includes the representative header shapes and sample error envelope below. Example error envelope (HTTP 429 response body): {"error": {"type": "rate_limit", "message": "rate limit exceeded", "retry_hint_ms": 1200, "backoff_strategy": "exponential", "metadata": {"quota_group": "user"}}} Example headers: X-Redwood-Backoff-Hint: backoff=exponential,initial=200,cap=20000 X-Redwood-Retry-After-Ms: 1200 Migration notes (short): - Clients should read X-Redwood-Retry-After-Ms if present; else parse Retry-After seconds; else use the backoff hint as heuristics - SDKs will ship helpers: redwood.api.backoff.from_response() (py) and decodeBackoff(response) (ts) - Idempotency-Key: we recommend generating v4 UUIDs; server will return 409+Location if duplicate. This PR is intentionally additive; follow-up work will propagate these headers into Dedicated telemetry and create an opt-in rollout flag for strict dedupe enforcement.
Arjun: Requested we namespace headers to X-Redwood- to avoid surprising proxies; asked for explicit numeric ms header to avoid fractional seconds parsing. Maya: Updated headers to X-Redwood-Retry-After-Ms and added a strict parse path; left Retry-After fallback. Sasha: Asked for deterministic behavior when Idempotency-Key store is unavailable (network partition). Maya: Added fallback semantics: when dedupe store is unavailable and request is marked idempotent, server returns 202 Accepted with 'result_pending' and Location; added docs entry. Lauren: Requested explicit test for client reconnect resume and duplicate tool-call race; tests added. Conversation included small follow-ups and a final approval after CI turned green.
Additive: servers emit X-Redwood-Retry-After-Ms and X-Redwood-Backoff-Hint to provide deterministic client backoff guidance; Idempotency-Key semantics for tool calls clarified (dedupe scope, TTL=7d), streaming endpoints now support resumable sessions via stream_resume_id and explicit terminal_error frames.

## Context

payload.body:
Summary: Introduces a platform-level kill-switch to disable Quantization Profile application globally, regardless of per-route settings. This is intended for emergency response (quality regression, incompatibility bug, or unexpected runtime instability) and is designed to be deterministic, auditable, and fast to propagate.

Context/Motivation: Route-level enablement is the default control for v1, but we need a single knob for SRE/oncall to quickly halt profile application without editing individual route configs. This PR adds a config flag that is evaluated in the control-plane resolution path and propagated through routing to the runtime. When the kill-switch is active, the resolved quantization outcome is forced to baseline and we record a consistent reason code.

Design goals: (1) Default behavior unchanged when kill-switch is off. (2) Deterministic: the same request under the same config yields the same resolution outcome. (3) Safe: if the kill-switch config cannot be fetched, we fail closed to baseline (i.e., do not apply profiles). (4) Observable: metrics and logs clearly indicate kill-switch state and impact. (5) Auditable: config changes are recorded and visible to SRE/security.

Implementation details: Adds a new dynamic config key `quantization_profiles.global_enabled` (default: true). In policy evaluation, we resolve route quant settings as usual, then apply the global gate as the last step: if `global_enabled == false`, the quantization outcome is set to `disabled` with reason `killswitch_active` and the `quant_profile_id` is cleared. Routing propagates the resolved outcome to the runtime via the existing request metadata. Runtime enforces the gate as a backstop (defense in depth) in case of stale routing caches: if it sees `killswitch_active`, it bypasses profile artifact loading and uses baseline kernels/precision.

Observability: Adds `quant_profile_resolution_total{outcome=applied|fallback|disabled, reason=...}` and `quant_profile_killswitch_active` gauge at router and runtime. Adds a structured log annotation `quant_profile_resolution_reason` and ensures traces include the kill-switch decision.

Docs/Runbook: Adds an internal note under the quant profile rollback runbook describing when to use the kill-switch vs route-level disable, and the expected metric signatures during recovery.

Test plan: Unit tests for config parsing/defaulting, policy resolution behavior, and runtime enforcement. Integration test covers: route configured with profile -> apply when enabled -> forced baseline when kill-switch active -> returns to apply when re-enabled. Includes a regression test ensuring kill-switch does not mutate persisted route config.

Rollout plan: Ship behind existing quant profile feature gates. Enable the config key in staging first, then prod with default true. SRE can toggle via the standard dynamic config path; propagation target is <60s. Follow-up: wire into SRE runbook automation and dashboards (ENG-5817).

Checklist: - [x] Default behavior unchanged - [x] Deterministic resolution and reason codes - [x] Metrics/trace annotations - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Runbook update - [x] Security review for who can toggle dynamic config
Ethan Park (review): Can we confirm the order of operations? I want the kill-switch to override route-level enablement after compatibility checks so we still surface compatibility warnings when kill-switch is off, but never apply when on.
Benji Okafor (author): Yep — compatibility checks run first; we apply the global gate last. When kill-switch is on we set outcome=disabled reason=killswitch_active regardless of compatibility. When off, compatibility behaves unchanged.
Noah Patel (review): Runtime backstop is good. Please ensure we don’t even attempt to fetch profile artifacts when kill-switch is active (avoids thundering herd during incident).
Benji Okafor (author): Done in commit "runtime: defense-in-depth gate". Loader returns early before registry fetch; also added a metric to confirm early-return rate.
Marcus Lin (review): Who can toggle this config? We should reference the existing RBAC for dynamic config changes and ensure audit trail is preserved.
Benji Okafor (author): Toggling uses the standard dynamic config admin path with existing RBAC; audit event emitted by config service. I added a short note in the runbook with the audit event name and where to find it.
Connor O'Brien (review): Add explicit guidance: use kill-switch only for emergency; prefer route-level disable for targeted rollback. Also add a quick verification step (expected metrics trend).
Benji Okafor (author): Updated runbook section with decision criteria + verification steps (enabled_routes drops to ~0; fallback rate to baseline goes to 0; error rate should normalize).
Priya Natarajan (review): Looks good. One request: ensure fail-closed behavior on config fetch errors is documented. I’m +1 after that.
Benji Okafor (author): Documented in body + inline comment near config fetch. Also added unit test: missing config => treat as disabled (baseline).
Mina Haddad (review): Approved after last push. The reason code naming is consistent with other policy outcomes.
Noah Patel (review): Approved.

Motivation: We need a low-latency way to validate new model variants with live traffic while minimizing cost and reducing noisy metric drift from session churn. This change implements a session-aware batched shadow promoter that: (1) batches shadow traffic at a configurable session granularity to reduce per-request overhead, (2) computes delta safety checks against a pinned baseline using a lightweight metrics comparator during the shadow rehearse window, and (3) emits a snapshot that can be replayed to perform deterministic rollback playback if the delta gate trips.

Scope of changes: added a planner and runtime promoter for batched shadow routing, a delta comparator that supports configurable metric windows and thresholds, a snapshotting API for cohort state capture, tests (unit, integration, e2e smoke), and dashboard/update to the Rollouts console. No public API surface changes to the Redwood API, rollout behavior is behind a feature flag (rollout.batch_shadow_v2).

Checklist:
- [x] Runtime promoter implementation (service/rollout/promoter.go)
- [x] Delta safety comparator with histogram and rate-aware modes (service/rollout/delta_checker.go)
- [x] Snapshot and replay helpers (service/rollout/snapshot.go)
- [x] E2E smoke and integration tests (tests/e2e/shadow_promote.test.ts)
- [x] Observability wiring (console/dashboards/rollouts.jsonnet)
- [x] Docs and runbook update (docs/runbooks/batched_shadow_promote.md)

How it works (summary):
1) During a staged promote, the promoter mirrors a configurable fraction of traffic into a batched shadow queue keyed by session id. Sessions are batched for X ms or until N messages to amortize KV cache and runtime overhead.
2) The delta comparator samples metrics (latency p50/p95, token efficiency, error rate, and a lightweight embedding drift score) over aligned windows and computes a signed delta compared to baseline. If any metric exceeds configured thresholds or the composite risk score is above threshold, the promoter marks the rehearsal as failed.
3) On failure we persist a compact snapshot (cohort ids, sampling seeds, the last KV offsets) that operators can use to replay traffic deterministically against the new variant to reproduce the regression locally or in a test cluster.

Backward compatibility and rollout: all behavior is guarded by rollout.batch_shadow_v2. Existing staged/promote and shadow paths are unchanged. This feature can be toggled per-organization.

Performance: batching reduces shadow request overhead by ~2.6x in internal perf runs for session-heavy workloads (see benchmark-lab notes). The delta comparator is intentionally lightweight to avoid skewing latency SLOs.

Risks and mitigations: initial CI run surfaced a flake in the snapshot garbage collector; added deterministic GC windows and extra unit coverage. Also added a conservative default threshold and a cooling period to avoid transient rollbacks from short spikes.

Next steps: extend comparator to support scalar-weighted composite scoring and hook the promoter into autosurge controls for dedicated clusters.

Marco Alvarez (2026-01-22): Overall looks good. Please add a unit test asserting that session batching respects per-session ordering when batch flushes overlap; hygiene: a couple of small lints in promoter.go.
Priya Singh (2026-01-23): Addressed Marco comments: added ordered-session unit test, refactored the flush path to remove a race, fixed lints.
Lena Park (2026-01-25): Can you clarify how snapshot size scales with large cohorts? Also request to add an integration test for snapshot replay correctness with a token-level KV cache warmup.
Priya Singh (2026-01-26): Added compacted snapshot serializer and a new integration test that replays a 10k-sample cohort in CI; snapshot size measured ~45KB compressed in our benchmark lab (attached in CI artifacts).
Samuel Green (2026-01-28): Nice end-to-end coverage. One nit: delta thresholds should be surfaced in the rollout UI as editable knobs. Filing follow-up ENG-1985 to track console work.
Lena Park (2026-02-01): Approve after small doc clarification.
(Approvals: Lena Park, Marco Alvarez, Samuel Green)

Motivation: In long-lived SSE connections we continue to see glitches where a delimiter ("

") or event boundary can be interpreted inconsistently across proxies and our client reassembly, producing partial JSON objects or ordering anomalies when packetization aligns with UTF-8 multi-byte boundaries. This PR reworks how we mark and reassemble fragments to make consumer-side reassembly deterministic even when fragments arrive out of logical order or are split on codepoint boundaries.

What this changes: adds a compact per-fragment monotonic timestamp + seq-offset header emitted by the server runtime, applies a normalization pass that collapses ambiguous delimiter runs into a canonical marker before parsing, and hardens the stream parser to accept and reorder within a short, bounded window using timestamps rather than relying solely on arrival ordering. Also instruments a new set of observability metrics for fragment reorder, delimiter-normalization rate, and reassembly retries.

Checklist:
- [x] Reassembly algorithm with timestamp window and idempotent normalization implemented in runtime stream layer
- [x] Backwards-compatible framing header (optional; parser tolerates both old and new framing)
- [x] Unit tests covering UTF-8 split boundaries and proxy-induced chunk reordering
- [x] Integration test against nginx proxy emulation and node/ts client harness
- [x] Added metrics and dashboards for fragment reordering and normalization events
- [x] Release note entry prepared

Rollout plan: feature gated by runtime flag (sse.fragment_ts=on). Default enabled in canary and dedicated, monitor metrics for 72h, then flip global flag. If regressions observed, runtime will fall back to legacy framing for affected connections and emit a debug trace to support.

Backward compatibility: The framing header is optional and ignored by older clients. Normalization step is idempotent and only affects internal stream boundary resolution; it does not mutate payload content outside of delimiting sequences.

Related work: Builds on ENG-1209 (previous delimiter fixes) but differs by moving to timestamp/small-offset ordering rather than larger sequence windows. Linked Linear items: ENG-1347, ENG-1372. Support ticket SUP-8821 repro included in tests.

Stabilize SSE stream reassembly by introducing per-fragment monotonic timestamps and deterministic delimiter normalization. Addresses rare partial-JSON emission and out-of-order event delivery under heavy backpressure. No public API changes.
Connor Lee: Nice approach. Two questions: (1) how does this behave with replayed fragments from proxies that buffer and retransmit? (2) Do we need an escape if payload legitimately contains the delimiter sequence?
Asha Patel: For (1) we use a short monotonic window (300ms by default) and also detect replays by identical fragment payload+seq checksum; replayed fragments outside the window are treated as duplicates and dropped. For (2) delimiter normalization only runs on the stream framing layer before payload parsing and respects explicit "data:" event prefixes; we added tests for payloads with embedded delimiter-like sequences.
Maya Singh: Can you add a telemetry tag to connect fragment reorders back to connection id and upstream proxy?
Asha Patel: Added r.conn_id tag to fragment_reorder metric and a debug trace emitted when reorder_count > 3 in a minute.

payload.body:
Context
We need a safe way to roll RBAC v2 into production without breaking existing customers/internal workflows. This PR introduces feature flags and a dual-read evaluation mode where we evaluate both RBAC v1 and RBAC v2 for the same request, continue enforcing v1 (source of truth) during the migration phase, and emit metrics/logs on discrepancies.

What this PR does
- Adds a small set of rollout flags (per-environment) and a consistent config API usable by gateway + control plane:
  - rbac_v2.enabled: enables v2 evaluation codepaths (no enforcement by itself)
  - rbac_v2.dual_read: evaluate v1 + v2 and compare results; enforcement remains v1
  - rbac_v2.enforce: enforce v2 result (guarded; not intended to be turned on broadly yet)
  - rbac_v2.fail_open_on_error (default true in dual-read): if v2 evaluator errors/timeouts, do not block request; record error metrics
  - rbac_v2.sample_rate (default 1.0 in non-prod, 0.1 in prod): controls dual-read comparison sampling to bound overhead
- Adds comparison + observability:
  - Metric: authz.dual_read.total{service,route,action,scope_kind}
  - Metric: authz.dual_read.mismatch{service,route,reason} where reason ∈ {v2_denied_v1_allowed, v2_allowed_v1_denied}
  - Metric: authz.v2.evaluator_error{service,error_kind}
  - Structured log event (debug-level): authz_dual_read_comparison with request_id, subject_type, action, scope, v1_decision, v2_decision, denial_code (when available)
- Adds a common "decision wrapper" type in the authz library to preserve denial metadata without changing existing caller logic.
- Implements dual-read hooks at both enforcement layers:
  - API Gateway middleware: runs v1 check; optionally runs v2 evaluation in parallel and records mismatch; never blocks on v2 in dual-read mode.
  - Control Plane service interceptor: same behavior; ensures internal service-to-service calls also report comparisons.
- Adds dashboards + runbook pointers (internal links) to ensure the rollout is observable.

Design notes
- Determinism: comparisons are computed from the same normalized input (subject, action, scope) that the caller uses for enforcement. This PR adds a small normalizer to avoid "false mismatches" due to scope serialization differences.
- Performance: v2 evaluation is run concurrently with the v1 check when dual-read is enabled, and is sampled in production by default. We also cap time spent on v2 evaluation (timeout = 30ms at gateway, 50ms in control plane) to avoid tail latency regressions.
- Safety: any v2 evaluator error in dual-read mode is treated as "comparison skipped" (fail-open) and emitted as a metric; no customer-facing behavior change.
- Enforce flag is wired but guarded: rbac_v2.enforce requires rbac_v2.enabled and will refuse to start if enabled without an allowlist in prod (prevent accidental global enablement).

Changed areas (high level)
- services/api-gateway
  - Adds rbac_v2 flag plumbing
  - Adds dual-read evaluation in authz middleware (v1 enforced)
  - Adds metrics + structured logging
- services/control-plane
  - Adds server interceptor support for dual-read
  - Adds normalizer for scope and action strings
- libs/authz
  - Adds FeatureFlagProvider interface + default implementation
  - Adds DualReadComparator and Decision types
  - Adds Prometheus metric definitions
- ops/observability
  - Adds Grafana dashboard JSON and alert draft (mismatch spike / v2 error spike)

Testing
- Unit tests for feature flag parsing + precedence
- Unit tests for dual-read mismatch accounting and error handling
- Integration-ish test in gateway package to assert:
  - v1 decision is enforced
  - v2 evaluator errors do not change response
  - mismatch metric increments correctly

Rollout plan (follow-up)
1) Enable rbac_v2.enabled in staging and internal dev
2) Enable rbac_v2.dual_read at 100% sampling in staging
3) Enable dual-read at 10% sampling in prod (hosted) with dashboards
4) After permission inventory + policy bundle stability, start allowlisted enforcement trials with rbac_v2.enforce (separate change control)

Open questions
- Whether to expose mismatch details in a debug header for internal admins only (not included here; see discussion below)

Links
- Linear: ENG-18388
- Related PRs: gateway deny-by-default middleware (pr-28159), policy evaluator client w caching (pr-28203)

Checklist
- [x] No behavior change when flags are off
- [x] Dual-read mode is fail-open on v2 errors/timeouts
- [x] Metrics emitted for total, mismatches, evaluator errors
- [x] Sampling supported to bound overhead
- [x] Added tests + updated internal dashboard assets
- [x] Added release guardrails to prevent accidental global enforce in prod
Jordan Lee (review): Can we guarantee the v2 call never affects latency on the critical path? Even in parallel, awaiting it would. Please confirm we don't await v2 completion before responding in gateway dual-read.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Good call — gateway now fires v2 evaluation on a detached task with a per-request context that only writes metrics/logs; response path only awaits v1. Added a test asserting response is returned even if v2 blocks until timeout.
Amara Diallo (review): The mismatch metric labels include action and route. Action cardinality is bounded, but route can be high. Can we switch to a route template instead of raw path?
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Updated to use the gateway's route name (OpenAPI operationId) instead of raw path, and added a guard to default to "unknown" if not present.
Marcus Lin (review): In prod dual-read, please make sure fail_open_on_error defaults true and sample_rate defaults low. Also, can we add a hard safety check so enforce can't be enabled globally without an allowlist?
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Done. Defaults: prod sample_rate=0.1, fail_open_on_error=true. Added startup guard: rbac_v2.enforce requires allowlist env var RBAC_V2_ENFORCE_ALLOWLIST set, otherwise service refuses to start in prod.
Benji Okafor (review): The scope normalizer changes might affect v1 behavior if reused. Ensure it's only used for v2 comparison input.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Scoped to v2 comparator only; v1 callers are unchanged. Added unit test that v1 input serialization remains identical.
Connor O'Brien (review): Please add a short section to the rollout runbook about what to do if mismatch rate spikes (rollback steps and which flags to flip).
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Added "mismatch spike" playbook to docs/internal/runbooks/rbac_v2_rollout.md including immediate disable steps (rbac_v2.dual_read -> off) and triage checklist (top mismatched actions/routes).
Jordan Lee (review): Approving after the route cardinality fix + detached v2 eval changes. Nice.
Amara Diallo (review): Approved.
Marcus Lin (review): Approved with the enforce guardrail. Thanks.
payload.title: RBAC v2: add feature flags + dual-read evaluation (v1 enforced) for staged rollout

payload.body:
Motivation: Production workloads showed recurring tail-latency and KV eviction storms when serving mixed-model traffic (Llama/Mistral/Qwen) with heterogeneous token lengths and mixed GQA/MQA layouts. This PR introduces a set of coordinated runtime changes: 1) Token-aligned kernel dispatcher that groups requests by token-shift boundaries to avoid partial-head misalignment and reduce kernel polymorphism penalties. 2) KV resiliency layer that adds a soft-snapshot and watermark-driven eviction path so transient memory pressure no longer triggers full cache churn across slabs. 3) Continuous-batch fusion (lane-aware fusion) that coalesces many small requests into fused microbatches while keeping per-request latency SLOs via prioritized draining and lane affinity. 4) Per-model microkernel hints for known quirks (LLama head packing, Mistral attention stride, Qwen block-size alignment) so the scheduler can pick optimized kernel paths without expensive runtime probes. Implementation summary: token-aligned-dispatch introduces a light-weight fingerprint for the first 8 tokens and a shift-canonicalization step before kernel selection; the dispatcher prefers already-warmed kernel variants for identical shift classes. The KV resiliency component adds epoched snapshotting, an eviction watermark that triggers background compaction, and a degraded-read fallback that serves KV-miss slices from prefix-cache while compaction finishes. Continuous-batch fusion implements a lane allocator with soft-timers and a priority queue that favors latency-sensitive routes; fusion is abortable on headroom pressure. Performance: microbench on Llama-13B (open-proxy trace) showed 14% median latency improvement and 22% 95th-percentile reduction; combined workloads with MQA/GQA saw up to 1.35x throughput on saturated GPU pools with nearly identical quality. Safety and compatibility: changes are opt-in via runtime flags at deploy time and default to disabled for private deployments; added a compatibility matrix to models/quirks mapping. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for dispatcher and KV snapshotting - [x] Perf harness for fusion scenarios - [x] Back-compat layer for existing KVCaches - [x] Documentation in runtime/ops and models/quirks - [x] Manual canary rollout and observability dashboards Updated Linear tasks ENG-5124 and ENG-5179 with rollout notes and post-canary metrics.
Jonah Kim: Nice direction. Two asks: (1) can we make the token fingerprint length configurable via a flag? (2) please add a short doc about how per-model hints are validated during model onboarding.

Motivation: recent cross-region probe flaps caused noisy tenant-level throttle flips during short-lived control-plane hiccups (see SUP-9876). This PR implements an adaptive tenant throttle reconciler that smooths probe inputs, enforces SLO-aligned hysteresis, and provides a conditional lease fallback path to a standby serving tier when a tenant's primary region is unstable. The goals are: reduce rapid tenant preemptions, maintain latency SLO for high-tier customers, and provide a fast, auditable recovery path for transient control-plane probe failures.

What this changes (high level): adds a new reconciler service (reconciler/tenant_reconciler) that subscribes to health probes and tenant metrics, computes a stable lease state with exponential smoothing + min-stable-window, and issues conditional leases to the runtime scheduler. When a tenant's primary lease is revoked due to sustained instability the reconciler will offer a conditional fallback lease to a standby region/model variant instead of immediate eviction. The runtime scheduler receives a lease API (runtime/lease_manager.go) to accept/reject conditional leases and exposes a decision reason for observability.

Key behavior and knobs: single config flag enable_tenant_reconciler (default: false); smoothing_alpha (0.2); min_stable_window_ms (15000); fallback_grace_ms (120000); fallback_policy: [prefer-local-standby, degrade-quantize]. Reconciler emits metrics: reconciler.lease_decisions, reconciler.signal_smoothed, reconciler.fallback_offers.

Files changed include a small API surface on the scheduler and about six new modules for reconciler logic and tests. No model serving semantics were changed. Backwards compatibility: reconciler is gated by a feature flag and defaults to off. Rollout plan: feature-flag canary in eu-west-1 at 5% traffic for 24h, then 25%, then full rollout. Rollback: flip enable_tenant_reconciler=false and revoke conditional leases via admin endpoint.

Testing: unit tests for smoothing logic, integration test harness that simulates probe jitter and asserts stable decisions, and a small load canary run (k8s canary job) validated against latency SLOs. CI: lint, unit, integration (mock), end-to-end canary job.

Related: ENG-2345, ENG-2419, SUP-9876. Linear links and monitoring runbooks updated in internal doc ID: linear/ENG-2345.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc (linked in PR)
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Canary plan and rollback steps
- [x] Observability metrics and dashboards wired

Why this is different from previous approaches: instead of immediate tenant eviction this adds a temporal reconciliation step that prefers conditional fallback offers and gives the system time to absorb short probe regressions without noisy tenant churn. This reduces churn-induced latency spikes and decreases the number of urgent incident pages for probe flaps.
Lena Park (reviewer): Can we add a metric for 'fallback_offer_accept_rate' so we can see how often standby accepts are used? Also please document the expected cost delta for fallbacks.
Dmitri Volkov (author): Added metric reconciler.fallback_accept_rate and included cost note in runbook (docs/runbooks/tenant-reconciler.md).
Sameer Kapoor (reviewer): The min_stable_window of 15s seems conservative for small tenants; suggest making it configurable per-tenant tier. Consider adding tier_multiplier in config.
Dmitri Volkov (author): Exposed tier_multiplier in config and updated tests to cover high/low multiplier scenarios.
Marta Ruiz (approver): Verified canary telemetry (eu-west-1, 5%) for 24h. No increase in P95 latencies for gold tenants. Approving.
Introduce tenant-level reconciler to smooth probe signals and provide conditional fallback leases to standby regions. Feature gated; enabled via feature flag and rolled out by canary. Improves stability during short-lived control-plane probe flaps; reduces noisy tenant evictions.
Start canary in eu-west-1 at 5% traffic for 24h, monitor reconciler.lease_decisions and runtime.latency_p95 by tenant tier. Increase to 25% then full after 72h of stable telemetry. Rollback by disabling enable_tenant_reconciler flag and invoking admin revoke endpoint.

payload.body: Motivation: Customers and SDKs expect OpenAI-compat semantics for rate limits, Retry-After handling, and idempotency keys, but our adapter had subtle mismatches for streaming and tool/function-calling workflows which caused inconsistent retry behavior and duplicate tool invocations. This PR standardizes: 1) rate limit error mapping and payloads to match OpenAI conventions, including 'retry_after_seconds' and a consistent top-level 'type' of 'rate_limit' in the error object; 2) Retry-After header parsing that accepts both seconds and HTTP-date formats and surfaces a normalized numeric retry_after_seconds in both headers and JSON body; 3) idempotency semantics for streaming and function/tool-calling endpoints: the server will record idempotency keys for in-flight and completed invocations, return 409 + structured error when a duplicate non-idempotent request is detected, and permit safe reconnect/resume semantics for streaming where possible; 4) explicit guidance in the OpenAI adapter for SDKs on safe retry/backoff strategies and when to re-use idempotency keys for partial/complete responses. Changes include behavior and schema compatibility shims in the OpenAI adapter, runtime changes to the streaming multiplexer to persist partial KV checkpoints keyed by idempotency, API tests and e2e scenarios that emulate flaky upstream connections, and updated docs/examples. Checklist: - [x] Implement Retry-After parsing and normalized error payloads - [x] Persist idempotency state for streaming/tool calls (in memory for test + DurableStore for prod) - [x] Add unit + integration tests covering duplicate key paths and HTTP-date Retry-After - [x] Update OpenAI adapter docs and SDK notes - [x] Run full e2e and perf smoke tests Summary of impact: Backwards compatible for well-behaved clients. Clients relying on malformed Retry-After or on ambiguous duplicate behavior will now see deterministic errors and a numeric retry_after_seconds field to consume. Internal runtime changes add a small durable write per idempotent invocation; measured cost is minor vs value of avoiding duplicate tool side-effects.
payload.title: Clarify rate semantics, Retry-After handling, and idempotency for streaming/tool-calls in OpenAI adapter

Motivation:
High-volume incidents over the past quarter showed recurring 'spiral' behavior where retries + slowpath replays amplify tail latency and trigger regional failovers. This PR introduces a small runtime component (traffic spiral arrestor) that detects escalating retry/queue loops and applies a calibrated dampening token bucket per-route+region.

What this change does (single-string sectioned description):
- Adds a lightweight SpiralArrestor in the serving runtime that tracks request velocity, retry amplification, and slowpath replay counts. When a spiral signature is detected it throttles new requests for the affected route with a soft token-bucket backoff rather than hard-cut circuit breakers, reducing cascading evictions.
- Introduces a SoftSLOAdapter: a controller that maintains a transient SLO warming budget for routes recently impacted by degradation. The adapter adjusts per-route penalty decay and temporarily relaxes strict failover triggers to allow graceful recovery windows.
- Improves region replication for circuit state by adding a compact, eventually-consistent gossip of spiral markers so nearby regions avoid simultaneous hard failovers.
- Includes a targeted hotfix to fix a race where slowpath replay could reinitialize an in-memory KV cache shard leading to a brief correctness glitch under high concurrency.

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/serving/spiral_arrestor.go (new)
- runtime/slo/soft_adapter.go (new)
- runtime/slo/policy_test.go (tests)
- config/policies/spiral_policy.yaml (defaults)
- infra/deploy/rolling_canary.yaml (canary rollout tweak)
- docs/operational/spiral-arrestor.md (operator doc)

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for SpiralArrestor heuristics and token-bucket behavior
- [x] Integration test verifies warmup budget prevents noisy neighbor eviction in CI scenario
- [x] Canary deployment config and gradual rollout plan included
- [x] Operator docs added and alert rules suggested

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy to staging with canary flags enabled for 24h (observability dashboards in the PR)
2) Enable for 5% production traffic, monitor spiral markers and SLO burn rate for 4h
3) Gradually scale to 30% then full rollout if no regressions

Related Linear items and context: ENG-8792 (investigation), ENG-9024 (hotfix for KV replay race).

Notes: This PR intentionally avoids changing core circuit-breaker thresholds; the SoftSLOAdapter lives orthogonally to existing breakers and only exercises soft throttles and penalty decay. The goal is to limit blast radius of retry spirals while maintaining predictable SLO economics.
Diego Alvarez: Nice approach — can you add a jitter factor to token bucket refill to avoid alignment across regions?
Ava Thompson (author): Added 25-50ms randomized refill jitter and documented the rationale in spiral_arrestor.go comments.
Priya Nair: Tests look good. Request: add an end-to-end scenario where a synthetic retry storm triggers the arrestor and verify no regional double-failover occurs.
Ava Thompson: Added integration test in runtime/slo/policy_test.go that simulates retry amplification and asserts only soft throttles are applied; included CI pipeline job to run it.
Maya Chen: Minor nit — consider extracting magic constants into config/policies/spiral_policy.yaml so operators can tune without a rebuild.
Ava Thompson: Moved thresholds into spiral_policy.yaml and wired them into default config loading; operator docs updated.
Add traffic spiral arrestor to mitigate retry-amplification spirals and reduce cascading regional failovers.
Introduce Soft SLO Adapter to provide transient warming budgets and penalty decay for faster, smoother recoveries.
Hotfix: resolve KV cache reinitialization race during slowpath replay under extreme concurrency.
Operators: new policy file config/policies/spiral_policy.yaml and docs/operational/spiral-arrestor.md

Motivation: We see tail latency variance on long-context workloads and suboptimal throughput when small requests mix with long-running KV-heavy traces. This PR introduces a new hybrid attention microkernel ("flashmix") that blends a narrow-window FlashAttention path with a fused rotary precompute stage and a rotary-offset-aware tiling layout. It also wires a scheduler hint and continuous-batcher integration so the runtime dynamically switches tile sizes and KV pinning policies based on observed sequence-length distribution and prefix-hotness. The goals are (1) reduce p95 autoregressive latency for mixed workloads, (2) increase steady-state throughput for long-context reranking/LLM chains, and (3) provide a safe runtime fallback for hardware that cannot run the fused path. Summary of changes: added CUDA microkernel and CPU fallback (src/serving/kernel/flashmix_kernel.cu + .cc), rotary precompute fusion layer that materializes offset anchors to minimize per-step work (src/serving/kernel/rotary_fuse.h), a tiling-aware scheduler that exposes per-request hints and auto-selects tile dimensions (src/serving/scheduler/tiling_scheduler.cpp), KV cache pinning + eviction weight updates (src/serving/cache/kv_pinning.cpp), continuous-batcher adjustments to prefer pooling when many short requests dominate (src/serving/batching/continuous_batcher.cpp), unit and perf tests (tests/attn_flashmix_perf.py, tests/kv_pinning_unit.py), docs and rollout ops (docs/perf/flashmix.md, deploy/rollout/flashmix_flags.md). Backwards compatibility: the feature is behind a runtime flag (--enable-flashmix) and a model capability table entry; when disabled the runtime uses existing FlashAttention or fallback kernels. Rollout plan: Feature flag gated, staged rollout to 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated perf checks and automatic rollback on >5% quality or >10% latency regression. See ENG-2142 for evaluation prompts and perf harness configs.
- Add new 'flashmix' attention microkernel that fuses small-window FlashAttention with rotary precompute and tiling; disabled by default behind --enable-flashmix flag.
- Tiling scheduler with request-hint API to pick adaptive tile sizes at runtime.
- KV cache pinning policy to keep frequently-accessed prefixes resident and reduce eviction churn.
- Continuous-batcher tuning to prefer pooling for imbalance workloads.
- Performance improvements: p95 latency reductions for mixed short/long workloads and throughput uplift on long-context workloads.
p50 latency (32-token requests mixed with 4096-token traces): baseline 18ms -> flashmix 14.6ms (≈19% improvement)
p95 latency (same workload): baseline 92ms -> flashmix 68ms (≈26% improvement)
throughput (long-context continuous generator, batch=1 steady-state): baseline 520 tokens/s -> flashmix 640 tokens/s (≈23% uplift)
token-cost delta (est): -7% due to fewer KV fetches and improved batching packing
fallback path (no fusion hardware): p95 within 5% of baseline; safety fallbacks engaged automatically
Daniel Kim: Nice direction — can you add safe fallbacks for pre-amp hardware? Also add a unit test for rotary-anchor boundary conditions.
Elena Park: Added CPU fallback and expanded boundary unit tests; pushed follow-up commit e3f5a7b.
Priya Nair: Scheduler API looks good; prefer smaller default tile sizes for <128 sequence length. Please document the tradeoffs.
Elena Park: Updated docs/perf/flashmix.md with tile sizing guidance and added telemetry to capture tile selection distributions.
Marco Alvarez: Observed a flaky perf-reg test on our CI runner (gpuxl-5). Reran perf job with larger sample size; numbers stable now. Approving.
CI Bot: perf-regression check rerun passed (baseline vs flashmix)

2) Deploy to staging with 10% traffic and monitor tile-selection metric: runtime.scheduler.tile_selection_distribution
3) Validate model outputs for a representative prompt set (ENG-2142) to ensure no quality regressions
4) If metrics OK, increase rollout to 50% and then 100% with checks after each step
If rollout triggers >10% latency regressions, flip --enable-flashmix=false via the feature flag and the autoscaler will rollback canary; KV pinning changes are additive but may increase memory footprint — watch replica memory and OOM signals.

Motivation: reduce per-token latency for short-to-mid sequences and improve throughput for bursty, heterogeneous workloads by reducing memory traffic and improving kernel L2 reuse. This PR introduces a 'cyclic lane-stride' attention microkernel that fuses rotary/rope shift operations into the qk/v compute path and adds a small on-chip loopback prefetcher to warm the KV cache lanes during continuous batching.

Summary of changes: fused rotary-shift pass merged into the QK kernel to avoid standalone rotary transposes; introduced lane-stride tiling to improve SIMD coalescing on Ampere/Blackwell-class GPUs; added a lightweight loopback prefetcher that issues speculative KV loads for the next contiguous lane during continuous batching; extended the KV cache API with an "anticipated_lanes" hint used by the runtime scheduler for warmup; scheduler updates to support cyclic assignment of requests to lanes to minimize lane-switch penalties; microbench harness + unit tests and perf regression guardrails.

Checklist:
- [x] Microkernel implementation (CUDA + device intrinsics)
- [x] Runtime scheduler changes + continuous-batcher integration
- [x] KV cache extension and e2e tests
- [x] Benchmark harness and telemetry for new metrics
- [x] Documentation snippets in kernel/README and runtime/CHANGELOG

Benchmarks (internal harness, p99 reported as median across 5 runs):
- End-to-end latency (single-request, seq_len=128, batch=1): down 14% p99 compared to baseline attn-v2
- Throughput (mixed-length continuous batching, 256-token epoch): +18% tokens/sec
- GPU memory bandwidth observed: -9% host<->device transfers for typical chat workloads

Compatibility and fallbacks: When "anticipated_lanes" hint is not provided, runtime falls back to conservative lane allocation (no prefetch). On devices that do not support the lane-stride intrinsics we fall back to the previous QK kernel path (code is guarded with capability checks). The KV cache ownership model is unchanged; the hint is advisory only.

Related work: complements ENG-1831 (continuous batching improvements) and ENG-1824 (kv-warmup policies). This PR does not change model semantics.

Notes for reviewers: the CUDA microkernel is in kernel/cyclic_lane_qk.cu and contains device-level intrinsics; please pay attention to correctness under edge cases (odd-head counts, seq<tile). The scheduler changes are localized to runtime/scheduler/cyclic_allocator.{py,rs}.

Ethan: Can we get numbers on how often the prefetcher mis-speculates? Author: On our harness the mis-spec rate is ~3.2% for heavily shuffled streams; overall cost of mis-spec is bounded and still nets a throughput win. Lena: Need capability guard for older drivers — added runtime capability check and unit test. Marcus: Please add a regression alert on the new telemetry metrics — added alert rule and dashboard tile. Approver (Marcus): Looks good on my side, leaving an approval.

CI: linux-build (pass), cuda-tests (pass), py-lint (pass), perf-smoke (pass). Reran cuda-tests after small fix for odd-head indexing.
Introduced cyclic lane-stride attention microkernel that fuses rotary/rope ops and adds loopback prefetch for KV warmup. Improves latency for short sequences and increases throughput for continuous batching workloads. Backwards compatible: advisory KV hint only.
