Adds operator session audit proxy and server-side attribution of KMS calls; no public API changes.
Summary: Introduce a lightweight operator-session-aware audit proxy and a KMS usage attributor that binds KMS requests to operator session assertions and RBAC v2 decisions. Motivation: customers and SRE teams requested stronger non-repudiable attribution for operator-driven KMS operations and clearer audit trails for cross-tenant/operator activity (see SEC-210). This PR provides a server-side shim that enriches audit records with operator_session_id, resolved RBAC decision trace, and a KMS call nonce that links the crypto operation to the audit record.

What changed (high-level):
- services/auditproxy: new service that accepts internal operator session-forwarded requests, validates operator JWTs, fetches RBAC v2 decisions via the policy-evaluator, attaches decision-trace metadata, and forwards requests to the KMS facade with an attributor nonce.
- pkg/kms/attributor.go: new package that generates deterministic per-request attribution tokens (HMACed nonce with key rotation support) and exposes Verify/Annotate helpers for downstream services.
- rbac/v2/policies/operator_bindings.yaml: RBAC v2 policy templates to ensure operators cannot escalate cross-region KMS usage; adds policy conditions for operator_session_id presence and region pin.
- api/docs/audit-proxy.md: operational runbook, rollout steps, config knobs (audit retention, signing key rotation, rate limits).
- tests/integration/auditproxy_e2e_test.go: end-to-end tests that simulate operator sessions and assert attribution propagation into audit logs and KMS call metadata.
- infra/helm/audit-proxy-values.yaml: optional helm chart values for Dedicated/Private deployments (feature gated by platform flag).

Commit summary:
- a1b2c3d Add initial auditproxy skeleton, JWT validation and proxying
- b2c3d4e Implement KMS attributor and deterministic nonce format
- c3d4e5f Wire RBAC v2 policy checks into proxy; add policy templates
- d4e5f6a Add e2e tests and fixture operator session tokens
- e5f6a7b Docs and helm values

Files changed (high-level): services/auditproxy/*, pkg/kms/attributor.go, rbac/v2/policies/operator_bindings.yaml, tests/integration/auditproxy_e2e_test.go, api/docs/audit-proxy.md, infra/helm/audit-proxy-values.yaml

Behavioral notes and invariants:
- The audit proxy does not change public REST surface for customers; it is an internal server-to-server shim used by operator tooling and RBAC enforcement. Deployments can opt-in by enabling the feature-flag `operator_session_audit_proxy`.
- KMS nonces are HMACed with a platform signing key and carry a bounded timestamp window (default 30s) to reduce replay risk. The attributor exposes verification endpoints for offline auditors.
- RBAC v2 policies introduced require operator_session_id to be present for any operator-scoped KMS role grants. Missing session IDs cause a deny decision and are logged for SRE investigation.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Marcus Liu (reviewer): "Nice isolation of attributor logic. Two asks: (1) show how keys rotate without breaking verification of recent nonces, (2) prefer context.Context threading rather than global logger in pkg/kms/attributor.go." — Addressed in commit d4e5f6a (added key-rotation grace window and context propagation).
- Diego Ramirez: "We should ensure the audit proxy masks tenant PII before forwarding; add a sanitizer step." — Implemented in b2c3d4e (sanitizer middleware) and added tests that assert PII redaction.
- Claire Morgan: "Operationally, we need metrics for attributed KMS calls per-operator and per-tenant; add Prometheus counters and dashboards." — Added counters in e5f6a7b and a Grafana template in api/docs.
- CIbot: flagged a flaky test on first run (tests/integration/auditproxy_e2e_test.go) — rerun passed. A slow e2e was quarantined and marked with [slow].

CI summary:
- unit (go test ./...): pass
- lint (golangci-lint): pass
- integration (sanity subset): pass
- e2e (slow): flaked once, rerun passed
- security-scan (deps): pass

Backwards compatibility and migration:
- No breaking public API changes. Existing operator tooling must set operator_session_id header when calling internal KMS endpoints to get attributed audit entries; fallback behavior logs an audit warning and denies RBAC policies created by this PR.
- Migration plan: staged rollout across regions: enable in Canary -> Dedicated staging -> global. Helm chart exposes `operatorSession.audit.enabled` and `kmsAttributor.rotationWindow`.

Rollout and monitoring
- Initial rollout gated behind feature flag and a 96-hour canary window. We will monitor:
  - audit.attributed_kms_calls_total by region/operator
  - audit.missing_session_id_denies_total
  - auditproxy.request_latency_ms P95
  - integration test healthcheck signals

Motivation: We observed recurring tenant-level memory amplification and transient OOMs during mixed workloads (small chat requests + occasional long generation). Root causes were fragmented KV slabs and uncoordinated spill decisions that created cascading I/O pressure. This PR introduces a tenant-aware memory coordinator that schedules a windowed compaction pass and a rate-limited spill regulator to reduce fragmentation, smooth spill throughput, and improve tail latency. Design summary: 1) Windowed compactor: background compaction runs in configurable time windows per-tenant to coalesce fragmented segments without impacting short-lived latency SLOs. Compaction work is budgeted in CPU + device-time and yields are inserted to keep p99 latency stable. 2) Spill regulator: spill decisions are rate-limited and smoothed by a token-bucket style regulator per-device and per-tenant. Regulator exposes backpressure signals to the scheduler so batching and placement can prefer warm KV regions. 3) Tenant memory coordinator: centralizes fragmentation metrics and admission signals so we avoid simultaneous heavy compaction + spilling across tenants on the same GPU. 4) Evictor changes: eviction ranking now includes fragmentation risk score and recent compaction history to avoid repeatedly evicting the same hot prefixes. Implementation notes: - New modules: src/kv/compactor.rs, src/kv/spill_regulator.rs, src/kv/memory_coordinator.rs. - Metrics: kv.fragmentation_pct, kv.compactor.window_secs, kv.spill.regulator_fill, kv.spill.backpressure_events (per-tenant labels). - Config knobs: compaction_window_seconds (default 30s), compaction_cpu_budget_ms (default 25ms/interval), spill_regulator_rate_tokens (default 4/s), aggressiveness per-tenant. - Feature flag: kv.windowed_compactor (off by default for older deploys). Observability/telemetry: dashboards added in docs/ops/kv_compaction.md and console runbooks included for when kv.spill.backpressure_events > 50/min. Performance summary (canary): - Median token latency unchanged. - p95 generation latency reduced by ~6-9% under mixed workloads. - Memory churn (allocation hotpath) down ~18% in canary tenants. - In cluster soak we saw 62% fewer transient tenant OOMs during bursty load compared to baseline. Rollout plan: 1) Deploy as feature-flagged to canary nodes (10% traffic) for 48h. 2) Monitor kv.spill.backpressure_events and p95 serve latency; regress if p95 increases by >3x or spill regulator fill > 90% for >5m. 3) Gradual ramp to 100% over 7 days if stable. Backwards compatibility: default knobs safe; compactor disabled unless feature flag explicitly enabled. TODO/checklist: - [x] Add unit tests for compaction scheduling and spill regulator token logic - [x] Add integration test to validate coordinator prevents simultaneous compactions on same GPU - [x] Add metrics and docs - [x] Perform perf bench harness runs - [x] Feature-flag gated rollout - [x] Added migration notes for config defaults

Asha Mehta (author): Added cap and explicit yield points; clarified in the compactor code comments and tests.
Marta Alvarez: How does the spill regulator react to transient I/O spikes? Will it delay required spill and cause memory pressure?
Asha Mehta (author): Regulator is conservative: on sustained I/O spikes it will raise a backpressure signal to the scheduler and accelerate eviction ranking for low-value prefixes. Added integration test to simulate I/O spike.
Ravi Singh: Please ensure tenant labels are included on new metrics and the console dashboards show top-10 tenants by fragmentation.

Can reduce p95 under mixed workloads and significantly lower transient tenant OOM rate when enabled.

Motivation: multiple teams reported subtle inconsistencies between SDKs around token refresh semantics and streaming cancellation ergonomics which make cross-language client behavior fragile under transient auth failures and client-side aborts. This PR introduces a lightweight SessionMiddleware abstraction and a StreamCancelToken shim implemented in Python, TypeScript, and Go to unify retry/backoff behavior, document lifetime of long-lived streams, and provide a single hook for token rotation and diagnostics. Changes include a consolidated RetryPolicy config (retry.window -> retry.window_ms and a deprecation shim), SessionMiddleware that centralizes credential refresh + per-session metadata (client_id, region, last_healthy_at), an opt-in StreamCancelToken that allows application-level cancellation of active streaming iterators without tearing down underlying network connections, and cross-sdk test harnesses that verify parity for 1) auth-refresh-before-request, 2) in-flight stream reauth (graceful reconnect), and 3) abort-without-leak semantics. This is a cross-repo SDK change touching SDK clients in redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-typescript, and redwood-sdk-go; it also adds a small server-side compatibility shim in the redwood monorepo to emit structured stream preamble events used by the cancel token. Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserved; migration path documented; small config rename documented with deprecation logs for one release. Linear tickets: ENG-4219 and ENG-4235. See commits_summary and changed_files for details.
Cross-SDK: add SessionMiddleware (centralized credential refresh), StreamCancelToken (graceful client cancel), unify RetryPolicy config keys. No breaking runtime changes; config rename deprecated for one release. Bumped SDK versions: python 0.28.0, typescript 1.14.0, go v0.10.0.
5 commits: initial middleware interfaces and types, python implementation and unit tests, typescript implementation and documentation, go implementation and integration tests, server-side stream preamble feature flag and compatibility tests.
Evan Park: Can the SessionMiddleware be composed so existing users can opt-in without API churn? Author: yes, middleware is opt-in and we added a helper factory in each SDK to wrap the existing Client with minimal code change.
Diego Ruiz: The rename retry.window -> retry.window_ms will surprise some infra configs; we should emit a clear deprecation warning and a mapping layer. Author: added a compatibility shim that accepts both keys and logs a WARN once per process.
Priya Nair: Tests flaked in the GH matrix on go streaming cancellation. Author: added deterministic timeouts and a backoff stub to the go harness; reran CI and all jobs are green.
QA (manual): Verified canary on staging with a low-traffic Dedicated pool, confirmed no leaked goroutines or hung sockets after repeated cancels.
unit: python pytest suite covers credential rotation and cancel token semantics
integration: cross-language streaming interop matrix in GH Actions (py/ts/go)
canary: staged Dedicated pool run for 48 hours to validate connection reuse and cancel frequency
Migration notes: 1) default behavior unchanged; to opt into SessionMiddleware call Client.with_session_middleware(SessionConfig(...)) or set SDK_SESSION_MIDDLEWARE=enabled. 2) rename retry.window -> retry.window_ms supported for one release; update config files to the _ms variant to avoid deprecation warnings. 3) StreamCancelToken is opt-in; see examples/streaming for usage patterns and cleanup recommendations.

Motivation: Presubmit/lint startup latency has been a recurring source of slow feedback (ENG-4876). On average, developer CI workflows saw 25-60s extra boot time on cold runners due to devdep installs, heavy node/npm setups, and monorepo-wide tool initializers. This PR introduces two complementary changes: (1) a lightweight 'dep-stitcher' utility that builds a minimal compatibility map for dev dependencies and (2) a refactor of the lint presubmit entrypoint to an incremental loader + selective devdep fetch.

What changed (high level):
- dep-stitcher: a tiny Go-based tool under tools/dep-stitcher/ that collects package metadata from package.json/Pipfile/pyproject for workspace packages and emits a compact stitch.json that maps top-level devdeps -> pinned shims. The stitch file is created in CI prewarm and used to avoid expensive install work for many repos.
- presubmit bootstrap refactor: replaced monolithic scripts/presubmit/bootstrap.sh with scripts/presubmit/boot-incremental.{sh,py} that: (a) consult stitch.json, (b) prime only the subset of devdeps required for changed paths, (c) reuse the shared presubmit base image with layered caching.
- CI template updates: added a new presubmit step ci/presubmit-primer that runs 'dep-stitcher --scan' on the changed subgraph and caches stitch.json keyed by repo+stitch-hash. The presubmit job now has an early exit path when nothing relevant changed.
- Tooling: introduced a small cache warm helper and documentation: docs/ci/presubmit-boot.md.

Why this approach: The goal is pragmatic: reduce no-op work and accelerate feedback. dep-stitcher is intentionally conservative (no automatic upgrades) and outputs a deterministic map so cache keys remain stable. The incremental loader keeps behavior transparent for teams while reducing unnecessary installs.

Checklist:
- [x] Design and lightweight spec (ENG-4876)
- [x] dep-stitcher implementation + unit tests
- [x] Presubmit refactor + integration smoke test against redwood-examples/
- [x] CI template and cache priming
- [x] Docs and README for teams to opt-in

Commits (summary): 1) add dep-stitcher initial implementation and unit tests; 2) refactor presubmit bootstrap to use incremental loader; 3) add CI primer job and cache keys; 4) docs and small e2e smoke test; 5) fix flake in boot-incremental script after reviewer feedback.

Files changed (high level):
- tools/dep-stitcher/main.go (new)
- scripts/presubmit/boot-incremental.sh (rewrote entrypoint)
- ci/presubmit-template.yaml (add presubmit-primer step)
- docs/ci/presubmit-boot.md (new)
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yml (wire in new template)
- tests/ci/smoke/presubmit-boot.test (new smoke test)
- scripts/presubmit/compat-mapping.json (stitch example)

Review thread (high-level extract):
- Diego Ramos (review): "Nice reduction in surface area. Can we ensure stitch.json generation is hermetic on CI images? I hit a flake where local node resolution picked a higher semver patch and cache keys diverged."
- Author (Asha): "Added a step to normalize package metadata by reading exact lockfiles when present and emitting a canonical sorted map — addressed in commit 3. Also added a unit test to guard against non-determinism."
- Priya Kapoor (review): "Presubmit early-exit looks good. Two asks: (1) add an opt-out for repos that intentionally want full installs, (2) make the cache key include the presubmit template version so rollbacks are safe."
- Author: "Opt-out added via .presubmit-config.yml allow_full_install: true. Cache key updated to include presubmit-tool-version. See last two commits."
- Jordan Li (approval): "Local smoke ran, behavior matches expectations, landing unless additional concerns."

CI summary and checks: ci/presubmit (lint + unit tests) — pass (after one rerun). ci/e2e-smoke — pass. actions/cache priming — hit original mismatch on first run due to non-deterministic lock reading, fixed and rerun. Lint: minor shellcheck warnings fixed in follow-up commit. Overall status: green.

Risk and rollout: The changes are opt-in initially — teams add a small pointer to cache in their CI or allow the presubmit template to run for them. No automatic changes to production-serving code. The dep-stitcher runs only in CI prewarm and outputs artifacts stored in workspace caches; it never mutates repo lockfiles.

How to validate post-merge: Run the new presubmit template against a few representative repos (redwood-examples, redwood-sdk-typescript) using --dry-run and compare cold-run vs warmed-run timings. Early tests showed ~35-50% presubmit boot time reductions on node-heavy targets.

Related: ENG-4876 (presubmit latency), ENG-4920 (devdep hygiene).
- Reduce presubmit lint warm-up time by ~40% across common developer profiles.
- Add a small 'dep-stitcher' binary that coalesces devdeps into a compact compatibility map used by the incremental loader.
- Prefer lightweight presubmit base image and opt-in lazy devdep fetch for low-risk repos.
init: add dep-stitcher tool and basic unit tests
refactor: replace bootstrap.sh with boot-incremental loader
ci: add presubmit-primer job and cache key scheme
docs: presubmit boot guide and caveats
fix: normalize lockfile parsing to prevent cache divergence
Diego Ramos: Can we ensure stitch.json generation is hermetic on CI images? I hit a flake where local node resolution picked a higher semver patch and cache keys diverged.
Asha Menon: Added normalization to prefer lockfiles and emit canonical sorted maps. Unit test added to detect non-determinism.
Priya Kapoor: Please add an opt-out for repos that intentionally want full installs, and include the presubmit template version in the cache key.
Asha Menon: Opt-out added via .presubmit-config.yml allow_full_install: true. Cache key updated to include presubmit-tool-version.
Jordan Li: Local smoke looked good. Approving to merge once CI is green.

Summary: During regional impairment/failover and capacity exhaustion, we currently manifest overload primarily as timeouts or inconsistent 5xx responses depending on which layer trips first (gateway timeout vs upstream rejection vs routing redirect). This tends to cause aggressive client retries and amplifies thundering herd at the worst time. This PR standardizes overload responses across the gateway so clients receive explicit backoff guidance via Retry-After, and we preserve consistent error shapes for observability and support.

Motivation / incident context: In staging rehearsals and the Q1 controlled failover prep work, we saw short spikes of 5xx and tail latency coincident with routing policy flips. A large portion was attributed to clients retrying quickly after gateway timeouts (no Retry-After) and some SDKs treating 503 differently from 429. We want deterministic, documented behavior to support graceful degradation instead of cascading overload.

What’s included: (1) Standard overload response helper (shared for all endpoints) that emits a consistent JSON error payload and sets Retry-After (seconds) for overload conditions; (2) Status code mapping: 429 for "shed / backpressure" (capacity pressure, retryable) and 503 for "temporarily unavailable" (hard-unavailable or upstream unavailable, retryable) with Retry-After; (3) Wiring into circuit breaker + upstream timeout paths so we return an explicit overload response before the request hits the global timeout when the retry budget is exhausted or the region is in a degraded state; (4) Streaming behavior: if we detect overload before first byte, return the standard overload response with Retry-After; if overload occurs after headers are sent, we send a structured terminal event (best-effort) and close, and the docs clarify client reconnect guidance; (5) Metrics: overload_response_total labeled by route + reason (bounded set), and retry_after_seconds histogram to support tuning.

Error payload (example): {"error": {"type": "overloaded", "message": "Service is temporarily overloaded. Please retry.", "retryable": true, "reason": "capacity_shed"}} plus header Retry-After: <seconds>. Note: this is intentionally aligned across chat/completions/embeddings/rerank so SDKs can implement one retry policy.

Retry-After computation: We derive Retry-After from the circuit breaker/open state + queue depth + retry budget state. Default is 2s with jitter (0–250ms). When in sustained shed mode, we increase up to 10s (capped) to dampen retry storms. We keep it conservative to avoid pushing clients into very long waits unless the system is clearly unhealthy.

Compatibility: This is not a breaking change in the sense of schema removal, but clients that were keying off specific 5xx codes may see more 429s during overload. Both are retryable. We document the guidance and ensure the error payload retains existing fields where present. For enterprise customers requesting auditability, this change improves the determinism of the user-visible symptom and makes it easier to correlate with failover events.

Testing: Added integration tests for each route ensuring: (a) overload path returns 429/503 as expected; (b) Retry-After exists and is within expected bounds; (c) error payload is consistent; (d) no accidental caching of overload responses; (e) streaming overload pre-first-byte returns a standard JSON response. Manual test notes included for staging with induced queue pressure.

Rollout plan: Guarded behind feature flag gateway.overload_retry_after_v1. Enabled in staging by default. In production, we will enable for a small percentage of Hosted traffic first (by tenant tier / allowlist) and watch: overload_response_total, overall 5xx rate, client retry amplification (request rate after overload), and p95/p99 latency. On-call runbook note: during regional failover tests, seeing 429/503 with Retry-After is expected and preferable to timeouts.

Follow-ups: This does not change SDK retry behavior directly (handled in SDK repos), but it unblocks predictable client backoff and better behavior during failovers. Also pairs well with ENG-2419 timeout/retry budget tuning and the streaming reconnect work.

Checklist: - [x] Added metrics (bounded labels) and updated cardinality review notes - [x] Updated docs for error semantics + client guidance - [x] Integration tests added for headers + payload - [x] Feature-flagged + default off in prod - [x] Alert annotations will be added in a separate PR when the controller emits failover events consistently

Notes for reviewers: Please pay special attention to (a) status code mapping choices (429 vs 503) and whether we should collapse to one; (b) streaming behavior after headers are sent; (c) label cardinality safety in overload_response_total.

---

CI: Buildkite (monorepo) ✅ build / unit ✅ lint ✅ integration ✅ gateway-e2e. One initial failure due to a flaky streaming integration test (timing); rerun passed after adding deterministic clock injection in the test harness.

Review conversation (highlights): Miles Thornton: "Can we ensure Retry-After is always present for the overload paths? Clients will do the wrong thing if it’s omitted." Author (Peter): "Yep, enforced in overload helper; added an assertion test for all overload responses." Mina Haddad: "Status code mapping: I like 429 for shed, but we should confirm we’re not violating any existing contract." Peter: "Agreed; updated docs and added release note. Also preserved existing error.type=overloaded." Ravi Menon: "Please ensure the reason labels are bounded; we can’t afford unbounded reason strings." Peter: "Changed reason to enum (capacity_shed | upstream_unavailable | retry_budget_exhausted | regional_degraded)." Allison Grant: "Add histogram for retry-after to help tune; also need a panel for overload vs timeout." Peter: "Added retry_after_seconds histogram; dashboard update will land in observability-pack." Tomáš Novák: "Runbook should mention that timeouts dropping while 429/503 rises is expected during a controlled failover." Peter: "Added note to docs/operator guide; runbook refresh tracked under ENG-2423."

Merge: Squash merged to main after approvals. Feature flag remains off in production by default; staged enablement planned during next game day rehearsal window.
payload.title: Standardize overload responses + Retry-After to improve client backoff during regional events

Context: For the public benchmark report launch, the marketing site needs a reliable way to fetch versioned benchmark artifacts (JSON) without exposing raw object store paths or internal run identifiers. This PR adds an internal service endpoint that returns the latest (or pinned) benchmark dataset for the web experience and enforces allowlisted auth. Summary of changes: (1) Add `GET /internal/benchmarks/results` endpoint in `benchmark-results-service` that serves a precomputed JSON bundle (schema-versioned) from object storage via a cache layer. (2) Add service-to-service authentication: requests must include `X-Redwood-Internal-Token` (rotating secret) OR `Authorization: Bearer <svc_jwt>` depending on caller environment; the marketing web backend will use svc_jwt in prod, token in dev/staging. (3) Add caching and conditional requests: Redis cache with 5m TTL + ETag support; if the upstream artifact version matches, return 304. (4) Add redaction guardrails: response is validated against the public schema and stripped of internal fields (runner hostnames, internal fleet IDs, raw trace IDs). (5) Add observability: latency, cache hit rate, bytes served, 4xx/5xx by reason, and structured logs with request_id. Why now: The docs PRs for the interactive benchmark page need a stable ingestion path (and we want to avoid the marketing site directly reading from storage). Security notes: endpoint is not exposed publicly; it is behind internal ingress + allowlisted caller identity. Additionally, response payload is constrained to the public schema and has a hard size limit to prevent accidental leak of raw logs. Testing: unit tests for auth modes, ETag handling, cache behavior, and schema validation; integration test in CI that loads a fixture artifact and asserts redaction. Rollout: ship behind feature flag `benchmarks_results_api_enabled` default OFF; enable in staging once docs site is ready; production enable coordinated with PMM + SRE. Follow-ups: Add rate limiting at ingress (tracked in ENG-18610) and ensure artifact publisher writes `latest.json` + `manifest.json` in the expected location (ENG-18477).
Felix Schneider (review): Can we support a pinned version param for the web UI so we can roll forward/back without redeploying? Also please confirm we’re not making the marketing site hit this on every page load (cache headers matter here). Logan Wright (author): Added `?version=` optional query. If omitted, uses `latest`. For caching, endpoint returns `Cache-Control: private, max-age=60` and ETag; the web backend will cache in-process and respect 304. Mei Lin (review): Please ensure the payload doesn’t include per-run records; web only needs the aggregated table + metadata. Also add a hard size limit so we don’t accidentally ship raw logs. Logan: Updated bundling contract to only accept `public_bundle` schema; size limit set to 5MB (configurable) and returns 413 if exceeded; added a test using a synthetic oversized payload. Naomi Feldman (security review): Two asks: (1) don’t accept static internal tokens in prod, (2) log reason codes without leaking auth headers. Logan: Implemented env gate: `X-Redwood-Internal-Token` accepted only in dev/staging; prod requires svc_jwt validated against issuer/audience. Logs now include `auth_mode` + `auth_failure_reason` but never include header values. Sean Gallagher (SRE review): Cache stampede risk if Redis is cold and launch traffic spikes. Please add singleflight / in-flight request coalescing per version key, and export cache hit ratio. Logan: Added in-process singleflight keyed by version; added metrics `benchmarks_results_cache_hit_total` and `benchmarks_results_origin_fetch_total`. Henry Cho (product): Make sure the docs reflect what’s internal vs public and that we include disclaimers for consumers of the dataset. Logan: Added internal doc page with clear language: internal endpoint, not for customer use; points to the public methodology + artifact export pipeline. Final approvals: Felix ✅, Mei ✅, Naomi ✅, Sean ✅, Henry ✅.
Internal-only: adds benchmark results endpoint for marketing site ingestion with auth + caching. No customer-facing API changes.
Enable flag in staging after ENG-18477 publishes first signed-off `public_bundle_v1.json` artifact; coordinate production enablement with SRE on-call during launch week.

This PR introduces the Quality Gate Run state machine and persistence layer in the Optimize service. Optimize recommendations (batching/caching/quantization profile changes) will be required to attach a gate run before they can be applied to production, but this PR only implements the core data model + transition logic + initial API endpoints (wiring to eval-harness and Console happens in follow-ups). The state machine is intentionally strict and idempotent to support retries, partial failures, and eventual coupling to rollout promotion. Includes DB migrations, internal admin endpoints, and notes for backfilling existing recommendations with `gate_required=false` until policy enforcement lands.
New endpoints (behind `optimize_quality_gates_enabled`): POST /internal/optimize/v1/quality-gates/runs (create a gate run for a config-diff + baseline ref; returns gate_run_id + initial state=PENDING), GET /internal/optimize/v1/quality-gates/runs/{gate_run_id} (read model + latest state + timestamps), GET /internal/optimize/v1/quality-gates/runs?recommendation_id=... (list runs for a recommendation). State transition endpoints are intentionally NOT exposed yet; transitions happen via internal workers (future: eval-harness callbacks) using the repository methods with optimistic concurrency.
Adds `quality_gate_runs` (one row per run) and `quality_gate_run_events` (append-only event log). `quality_gate_runs` fields include: gate_run_id (uuid), recommendation_id, config_diff_hash, baseline_ref, tier (SMOKE|FULL), state, state_reason_code, created_by, created_at, started_at, completed_at, expires_at (for overrides), last_heartbeat_at, attempt_count. `quality_gate_run_events` records every transition with actor_type (system|user), actor_id, from_state, to_state, reason_code, message, created_at. Event log is designed to be audit-friendly and to support future Console views.
States: PENDING -> RUNNING -> PASSED | FAILED. Terminal/exception states: CANCELED (from PENDING/RUNNING), OVERRIDDEN (from FAILED only, time-bound via expires_at). Allowed transitions are validated centrally in GateRunStateMachine with reason codes required for FAILED/OVERRIDDEN/CANCELED. Idempotency: repeated transitions to the current state are treated as no-ops if reason_code/message match, otherwise rejected with 409 to prevent silent overwrites.
Migration applies two new tables. No backfill required. Existing recommendations continue to work because enforcement is not enabled in this PR; the Optimize apply path will consult policy in a later PR and treat missing gate runs as allowed only when `gate_required=false` for the route/tier. Rollback: safe to roll back application code after migration; tables will remain unused. Local dev: run `pnpm db:migrate` (or `make optimize-migrate`) and ensure `OPTIMIZE_QUALITY_GATES_ENABLED=true` to hit the new endpoints.
Includes a lightweight reaper job that marks RUNNING gate runs as FAILED with reason_code=RUN_TIMEOUT if `last_heartbeat_at` is stale for > 45m (configurable). This prevents stuck runs from blocking later policy enforcement. Emits counters for transitions and a gauge for in-flight RUNNING runs (names to be finalized in ENG-3926).
Jordan Lee: Can we guarantee we never end up with two concurrent RUNNING runs for the same recommendation/config diff? Michael Nguyen: Added a unique constraint on (recommendation_id, config_diff_hash, tier) for non-terminal states and create endpoint now returns existing gate_run_id when the same idempotency key is reused. Benji Okafor: Please document the reason codes and enforce them at the boundary. Michael Nguyen: Added enum + validator; failing transitions must provide one of: QUALITY_REGRESSION, EVAL_ERROR, INFRA_TIMEOUT, RUN_TIMEOUT, USER_CANCELED, OVERRIDE_APPROVED. Chloe Martin: The GET endpoint should include latest event metadata for UI summaries later. Michael Nguyen: Added `latest_event_at` and `state_reason_code`/`state_message` on the run record so consumers don’t need to join events for the common case. Sean Gallagher: 45m seems high for timeouts; we’ll need separate thresholds for smoke vs full gates. Michael Nguyen: Tier-specific timeout added (SMOKE 15m, FULL 45m) behind config; default values can be tuned without redeploy. Paula Mendes: Make sure OVERRIDDEN is time-bound; do not allow “forever overrides”. Michael Nguyen: OVERRIDDEN requires expires_at (max 7 days) and actor_type=user; system cannot override. Paula Mendes: Approver auth? Michael Nguyen: This PR only adds the data model; the override endpoint is not implemented here. OVERRIDDEN can only be set through repository in internal admin tooling for now, protected by existing admin RBAC. Follow-up PR will introduce a proper approval flow + audit events.
Merged via squash into main by Jordan Lee. Post-merge note: coordinate with Olivia Grant on eval-harness callback shape before adding transition endpoints; avoid coupling state transitions to HTTP callbacks without idempotency keys.
Wire Optimize -> eval-harness trigger and callback handling (ENG-3922 / PR-19523)
Add config diff schema + static validation before gate creation (ENG-3930 / PR-19511)
Enforce apply blocking when gate fails (PR-19531)
Add override flow + expiration + audit events (PR-19537)
Add metrics/alerts/dashboards (ENG-3926 / PR-19593, PR-883)

Context: Shadow Traffic generates additional artifacts (request/response pairs + scoring payload references). We need strict data minimization by default and deterministic redaction so we can store enough to compute quality deltas while meeting Dedicated/Private constraints. This PR implements (1) retention defaults by deployment mode, (2) a redaction/transform pipeline for shadow artifacts, and (3) configuration toggles + audit-friendly metadata to support regulated customers. Summary of changes: - Adds `shadow_artifact_retention` config with safe defaults (Hosted: 24h; Dedicated: 7d; Private: 0h unless explicitly configured) and per-tenant overrides with validation. - Introduces `ShadowArtifactRedactor` (server-side) that transforms prompts/inputs and outputs before persistence: structured allowlist, truncation, hashing of identifiers, and regex-based PII scrubbing. - Adds storage layout for artifacts with TTL enforcement (DB TTL where supported + object-store lifecycle rules) and a periodic GC job for backends without native TTL. - Adds knobs for Dedicated/Private: `retention_hours`, `store_raw_prompts` (default false), `store_raw_responses` (default false), `redaction_profile` (standard|strict), and `export_audit_metadata` for SIEM export. - Updates ingestion to persist only redacted payloads; raw payloads never leave the request handler boundary (fail-closed for raw capture, fail-open for shadowing overall). - Adds metrics + logs for redaction effectiveness and retention GC: `shadow.redaction.actions_total`, `shadow.redaction.bytes_dropped`, `shadow.retention.gc.deleted_total`, and `shadow.retention.gc.lag_seconds`. - Docs in code comments reference Confluence: Security & Compliance > Shadow traffic data retention and redaction (v1). Behavior details: - Redaction is applied prior to enqueueing scoring payload references; scoring workers fetch only redacted text blobs. - Prompt redaction uses a best-effort regex pass (email/phone/SSN-like patterns) plus an allowlist for structured inputs (`messages[].role`, `messages[].content`); everything else is dropped unless explicitly allowed. - Content truncation defaults: prompts 8KB, responses 16KB (post-redaction), configurable only for Dedicated/Private with max caps enforced. - Stable hashing uses HMAC-SHA256 with a per-tenant key (KMS-managed) for `user_id`, `session_id`, and request fingerprints so customers can correlate within their tenant without exposing raw values. - Retention is enforced on both the artifact table and associated blob objects; deletion is idempotent and safe to re-run. Risk/mitigations: - Cardinality: we do not emit raw identifiers in metrics; only redaction action counts and coarse-grained profiles. - Performance: redaction runs in the async persistence path; synchronous request path only copies required fields into an internal buffer and immediately drops raw references after redaction. - Private deployments: when object-store lifecycle rules are unavailable, the GC job is mandatory and will run as part of the telemetry stack; documented in release notes for Private packaging. Testing: - Unit tests for allowlist behavior, regex scrubber, truncation, and hashing determinism. - Integration test that verifies raw prompts are not persisted when `store_raw_prompts=false`. - Migration test for existing shadow artifact rows (backfill redaction on read is NOT supported; this PR gates storage behind the feature flag so we don’t create mixed-mode tables). Rollout: gated behind `shadow_artifacts_persist_redacted_v1` (default off). Dedicated/Private can override via control plane config. Follow-ups: - Implement customer-configurable field-level allowlists for JSON tool inputs (deferred; requires product + security review). - Add UI surfacing of retention profile in Console (tracked in ENG-5408).
Marcus Lin (Security) [review]: Can we confirm raw prompts never get written to disk when `store_raw_prompts=false`? Also please document the regex patterns used and the known limitations (false positives/negatives) so we don’t oversell this as "PII safe". Kevin Osei (author): Confirmed: raw prompts are only held in-memory in the handler scope; we construct a redacted payload and only that crosses into the persistence layer. Added an integration test (`noRawPromptPersistence.test.ts`) that asserts the DB row + blob contain only redacted content and the raw buffer is dropped. I also added a comment block in `ShadowArtifactRedactor.ts` describing the regex set + limitations. Naomi Feldman (Compliance) [review]: Private default retention should be 0 unless explicitly set. Dedicated default 7d is fine but ensure max cap exists to prevent "accidental 90d" configs without approval. Kevin: Updated defaults: Private=0h (disabled). Added validation caps: Hosted max 72h; Dedicated/Private max 30d unless `compliance_override=true` (control plane-only, not exposed in Console). Logan Wright (Telemetry) [review]: Please ensure no high-cardinality tags are emitted. The metric names look fine; can we remove `tenant_id` from the structured log? Kevin: Removed `tenant_id` from info logs; kept it only in restricted audit logs (RBAC-protected) and as a hashed `tenant_key` for correlation. Nadia Rahman (Pipelines) [review]: GC job: what happens if it falls behind? We need a metric and an alert hook. Kevin: Added `shadow.retention.gc.lag_seconds` and `shadow.retention.gc.last_success_timestamp`. SRE can alert on lag > 6h for Dedicated and > 24h for Private. Sean Gallagher (SRE) [review]: Fail-open requirement: ensure redaction failure does not impact user response; but we should fail-closed for artifact persistence (don’t persist raw). Kevin: Implemented: if redaction throws, we drop the artifact and increment `shadow.redaction.failures_total`. Shadow routing remains unaffected. Benji Okafor (Control plane) [review]: Please align naming with other policy objects (`*_hours`, `*_enabled`). Kevin: Renamed fields to `retention_hours` and `persist_artifacts_enabled`; added migration alias handling for the earlier draft fields. Approvals: Marcus Lin approved after changes. Naomi Feldman approved. Logan/Nadia approved. Sean approved with note to wire alert rules in follow-up (ENG-5409). Merged after CI green.
Shadow traffic artifacts are now stored redacted by default with strict retention defaults (Hosted 24h; Dedicated 7d; Private disabled unless configured). Dedicated/Private deployments can configure retention and redaction profiles via control plane values. Adds GC job for environments without native TTL and new metrics to monitor retention enforcement and redaction behavior.
payload.title: Shadow traffic: retention defaults + prompt/response redaction pipeline

Motivation: SDK users keep needing to wire custom retry logic and independent backpressure controls for long-running streams across Python, TypeScript, and Go. This causes duplication, inconsistent observability, and subtle mismatches in retry semantics between sync/pull-stream and push/stream transports. This PR introduces a small, explicit retry DSL and backpressure-aware stream helper utilities that are implemented in the three official SDKs and surfaced via a coordinated API contract.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a lightweight RetryProfile DSL (max_retries, jittered_backoff_ms, retry_on_codes, idempotency_hint) and a canonical JSON schema used for cross-language exchange.
- Introduces BackpressureAwareIterator (Python), PullStreamThrottle (TS), and StreamLeaseGuard (Go) to provide a consistent ergonomic surface for consumers that need pause/resume semantics and cooperation with SDK-level batching.
- Normalizes auth retry hooks so token refreshes (short-lived session tokens) can be nested inside the retry loop without creating duplicate in-flight requests.
- Bumps package versions: python 0.38.0, typescript 2.1.0, go 1.5.0 and publishes migration notes.
- Adds e2e smoke test that runs a simulated bursty load against the local dev server and validates per-token latency budget and total token cost delta.

Checklist:
- [x] API design review (design doc attached)
- [x] Cross-language unit tests
- [x] Integration smoke test against dev runtime
- [x] Docs snippet and migration notes in CHANGELOGs
- [x] Telemetry hooks for retry/backoff events

Testing notes: The initial TS integration run revealed a race when the stream consumer called .cancel() concurrently with a retry; addressed in a follow-up commit that adds a cancel-safe fence in the TS iterator and adds a deterministic unit test. Python and Go had small behavioral diffs around token refresh timing; added explicit token-handshake points to the DSL so implementations can opt into optimistic vs conservative refresh semantics.

Motivation: CI latency and flakiness on presubmit lanes is a recurring drag on engineer feedback loops. This PR introduces a lazy test initializer that defers expensive per-test setup until the runtime actually requires it, combined with a dependency-declutter pipeline that prunes rarely used devdeps at build time. Goals: (1) reduce average presubmit walltime by ~20-30% for the Python and TypeScript stacks, (2) reduce toolchain install noise and transient version conflicts, (3) surface an automated dep-prune report for maintainers. Changes are implemented so they are opt-in via a lightweight flag in .github/workflows/presubmit.yml and default enabled for fastpath lanes. Checklist: - [x] Implement lazy initializer shim for pytest/xdist and Jest worker boot - [x] Add dependency declutter script and CI step that produces an actionable report - [x] Add integration tests for initializer behavior and a smoke job for the declutter pipeline - [x] Update docs and console runbook links - [x] Gradual rollout via feature flag in CI; tested on staging. Related: Linear ENG-1289 (CI fastpath improvements), ENG-1342 (dep hygiene backlog). See presubmit metrics snapshot: https://internal.redwood/ci/metrics/ENG-1289. This description is continuous: the PR also contains a small operator to fallback to the previous eager initializer if a runtime probe detects regressions, and a no-op path for repos that rely on non-standard test entrypoints.

Motivation: We observed a multi-region incident where aggressive rejoin behavior and aggressive failback caused repeated oscillations of traffic between regions. This triggered SLO thrashing and higher tail latency for customers routed through small-capacity regions. This hotfix introduces two coordinated mechanisms: an adaptive capacity harmonizer (server-side quota reservoir + per-region rejoin damping) and a sticky fallback inspector (diagnostics + short-term sticky fallback policy) to prevent rapid oscillation during regional recovery windows. Summary of changes: implement quota reservoir to reserve a tiny emergency budget when a region reports healthy but not yet warmed KV caches; add rejoin damping (cooldown fence + exponential rejoin backoff) to the node lifecycle; expose fallback-inspector endpoint for on-call debugging and live decisions; wire new metrics (fallback.harmonizer.*, fallback.inspector.*) and add tracing spans for decision points; add unit/integration tests, a small docs incident writeup, and a canary rollout config. This PR is a targeted hotfix intended to stabilize regional failover behavior while we work on a longer-term scheduler rewrite. The change is runtime-only and non-breaking for customer APIs. See linked Linear ticket ENG-4218 for design notes and postmortem rationale.
Ethan Park: The harmonizer algorithm looks good overall. Nit: rename 'reservoirSlack' to 'reservoirBuffer' to match other code. Can you add a short comment documenting the math for reservoir decay?
Priya Nair: Thanks Ethan, updated variable name and added inline math comment. Also added a short unit test that asserts the decay curve (fallback_hysteresis_test.go).
Marisol Vega: Question: how do we ensure we don't permanently starve small customers in a region with frequent brief outages? Please add a per-customer minimum allocation and a test that covers churn scenarios.
Priya Nair: Added per-customer floor of 1 token and a churn simulation integration test. Documented trade-offs in the incident doc.
Jonah Klein: Approving. Observability is in place and the inspector endpoint returns a compact JSON with reservoir state and recent rejoin timestamps. Recommend squash-merge and immediate canary to the 'staging-eu' pool.
CI Bot: Lint failed on first run: harmonizer.go: exported method needs docstring.
Priya Nair: Fixed linter issues and pushed. Rerunning CI.
Hotfix: Stabilize regional failover by adding an adaptive capacity harmonizer (reservoir) and rejoin damping; add a fallback-inspector admin endpoint for diagnostics. Reduces failover oscillation and tail latency during region recoveries. No customer API changes.
Monitor metrics: fallback.harmonizer.reservoir_utilization, fallback.harmonizer.rejoin_attempts, fallback.inspector.latency
Run postmortem checks at +24h and +72h; if reservoir_utilization > 80% for >1h, escalate to SRE and revert to emergency thresholds

Context: LTS customers (Dedicated/Private) have been clear that they want predictable latency and stable scheduling behavior across patches. The experimental batching heuristic we enabled on main in late 1.18 ("adaptive length bucket + opportunistic merge") does improve aggregate throughput on a subset of workloads, but it also increases run-to-run variance and can amplify p95 tail latency under bursty mixed-length traffic. For LTS we want fewer moving parts and more deterministic behavior by default.

What this does: On runtime-1.18-lts, default the experimental heuristic OFF and guard it behind an explicit opt-in flag. This keeps the codepath available for debugging/controlled experiments without making it part of the supported LTS default behavior.

Changes:
- LTS defaults: `scheduler.batching.experimental_heuristic = false`.
- Added explicit opt-in via config/env: `RW_RUNTIME_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BATCHING_HEURISTIC=1` (docs included). Note: on non-LTS branches the existing default remains unchanged.
- Added targeted scheduler regression test covering mixed prompt lengths + burst arrivals to ensure the stable path remains stable.
- Added a release-note blurb for LTS patch notes generator (throughput tradeoff + guidance).

Perf impact (perf-canary summary attached in CI):
- Mixed-length chat (bursty): p95 improved ~3-8% and variance reduced (fewer oscillations across runs).
- Long-form generation (steady load): throughput decreased ~2-6% depending on model/GPU (expected).
- No change in correctness outputs; only scheduling/batching decisions.

Why not remove entirely? Keeping it behind a flag helps if a customer explicitly wants it and accepts the tradeoffs, and it allows us to reproduce issues from main when triaging backports.

Rollout/ops: This is intended for the first LTS patch line. Support/CS should treat the opt-in as "best-effort / not recommended" unless Release Eng + SRE sign off for a given account.

Refs: ENG-4821 (Runtime LTS initiative), ENG-4831 (scheduler smoke tests).
Connor O'Brien: Can you confirm this only changes defaults on runtime-1.18-lts and doesn't accidentally affect main via shared config defaults?
Sofia Ivanova: Yep. The default flip is scoped to the LTS defaults table; mainline defaults remain unchanged. I added a unit test to assert the LTS default is false and main default is untouched.
Marcus Reed: Perf numbers look reasonable. Can we make sure the perf-canary summary artifact is linked in the PR description so release managers can find it later?
Sofia Ivanova: Done. Added link in CI section and included a short summary in the description (p95 variance reduction + throughput delta).
Allison Grant: For ops, I want a clear statement that enabling the heuristic is not a supported LTS default. Add one sentence to docs + note that Support should escalate before recommending.
Sofia Ivanova: Added guidance to docs/runtime/lts/known-behavior.md and included an ops note in the PR description.
Mateo Alvarez: Ship it for LTS. The opt-in flag name is a mouthful but explicit is good; approve after the docs change.
Samir Qureshi: One nit: make the env var parsing reject non-0/1 values (fail closed) so customers don't accidentally enable. Otherwise looks good.
Sofia Ivanova: Updated env parsing to accept only 0/1/true/false and default to disabled on invalid values (with a warning log).
Connor O'Brien: Approved. Please add a one-liner to the LTS release notes hints so it gets surfaced under Performance/Behavior changes.
Sofia Ivanova: Added to tools/release-notes/lts_hints.yaml under Performance -> Batching/Scheduling.
LTS: Experimental batching heuristic is now disabled by default on runtime-1.18-lts to reduce tail latency variance under bursty mixed-length traffic.
LTS: Customers may explicitly opt in via `RW_RUNTIME_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BATCHING_HEURISTIC=1`, but this may increase p95 variance and is not recommended without Redwood guidance.
Performance: Expect a small throughput decrease (observed ~2-6%) on steady long-form generation workloads when left disabled (default).

payload.body:
Context and motivation: We observed a class of customer bugs where OpenAI-compatible tool calls produced multiple candidate tool invocations or partially overlapping schema outputs in streaming scenarios (e.g., assistant suggests both 'create_ticket' and 'open_case' with overlapping fields). Existing heuristics (first-wins / highest-confidence) are brittle when tools have similar signatures or when streaming fragments arrive out-of-order. This PR implements a lightweight consensus resolver and an affordance mapping layer that: 1) aggregates partial and final tool outputs during a request, 2) scores candidates by schema affinity, declared affordances, and runtime provenance, and 3) emits a single canonical invoke envelope to downstream backends while preserving a decision provenance header for audit and debugging.

Summary of changes: Implemented consensus resolver in the OpenAI compatibility adapter, added affordance mapping proto/schema and config, extended streaming framer to tag tool fragments with sequence provenance, added unit/integration tests and a small docs page. Key goals: minimize latency impact for the common single-tool case, improve determinism for ambiguous tool outputs, and provide observability into the resolver decisions.

Commits (high-level): - Add consensus resolver component and public API + tests - Introduce affordance map proto and loader with migration guide - Extend streaming framer to include fragment provenance tags and repair logic - Emit telemetry (resolver.reason, resolver.score_vector, resolver.input_digest) - Add config flag and console toggle for rollout - Fix flakiness in integration test by adding deterministic seeds and timeouts

Files touched (high-level): - src/openai_compat/resolver.py: new consensus resolver, core scoring heuristics, tie-break rules - src/openai_compat/affordance.proto: new affordance schema, enums and mapping fields - runtime/streaming/framer.go: attach fragment_provenance headers and coalescing helpers - api/handlers/tool_invoke_handler.go: adapt to accept canonical envelopes + provenance header - docs/openai-compat/toolcall-consensus.md: design rationale and rollout instructions - tests/openai_compat/test_consensus.py: unit & integration coverage - telemetry/metrics.yaml: new metrics and labels (resolver_reason, resolver_winner, resolver_confidence) - examples/quickstarts/consensus-config.yaml: sample opt-in config

Design notes (condensed): - Scoring: we compute an affinity score combining schema overlap (tokenized field names & types), declared affordance weights (configured per-tool; default neutral), and runtime signals (model confidence, fragment completeness). Scores normalized to [0,1]. - Tie-breaking: prefer tools with explicit affordance dominance, then higher schema specificity (more required fields matched), then lower inferred risk (user-specified risk tags on affordance map). - Streaming safety: fragments carry a provenance vector {seq_id, is_final, partial_digest}. The framer coalesces fragments by seq_id. If two distinct tool bodies are both final, resolver attempts a lightweight merge by field union when schemas are compatible; otherwise it applies tie-break rules and emits the losing candidate as a telemetry artifact (not invoked). - Backwards compatibility: if consensusResolver=false or affordance map missing, behavior falls back to previous first-wins semantics. - Observability: each decision emits a resolver_provenance header with a compact JSON blob (string-encoded) and metrics are tracked for alerting on increased ambiguity rates.

Testing and CI: - Local unit tests added for scoring edge cases, schema affinity fuzz tests, and streaming fragment reordering. - Integration tests simulate two competing tools with overlapping outputs and assert canonical envelope invariants and telemetry emission. - CI initially failed on lint (line length and typo in proto comments); fixed and re-ran. Final CI: all checks passed, integration run (flaky tests) passed on second attempt.

Review conversation (highlights): - Diego Morales (reviewer): "Strong improvement for ambiguity cases. Two asks: (1) can we avoid copying full payloads into telemetry? keep digests. (2) add a small benchmark for common single-tool path to validate latency impact." Author response: implemented digest-only telemetry, added microbenchmark harness under perf/consensus and included results in the docs (latency ~+0.4ms p50). - Riley Patel: "Edge-case: merging fields when types differ (string vs object) — prefer conservative behavior and emit conflict reason." Author: adjusted merge to bail to tie-break and added a conflict_reason label. - Samir Gupta: requested clearer rollout plan and console toggle. Author: added config flag redwood.openai.consensusResolver and a console feature flag with canary to 10% by default.

Manual QA and rollout plan: - Feature gated behind config + console toggle. - Start with 10% canary in hosted, monitor metrics resolver_ambiguity_rate and resolver_invocation_failures for 48h. - If stable, increment to 50% and monitor SLOs for latency and error rates. - For Dedicated/Private customers, opt-in via config; documented migration steps in docs/openai-compat/toolcall-consensus.md.

Notes on future work: - Add a lightweight ML model to improve schema affinity for polysemantic tools (tracking as ENG-7740). - Expose per-customer affordance overrides via Console UI. - Consider a re-run/hedge strategy where losing candidate is invoked in background if confidence difference < threshold (opt-in).

Merge: squash and merge. Changelog entry included. Rollout toggle enabled off by default.

Related: SUP-4412 incident inspired tie-break completions; referenced earlier PRs for streaming framer improvements in runtime.

Contact: ava.chen@redwood.ai for follow-ups and rollout questions.
Adds a consensus-based resolver for OpenAI-style tool calls that canonicalizes multi-tool results, introduces an affordance map for deterministic tie-breaking, and emits decision provenance telemetry. Backwards compatible; opt-in via redwood.config.openai.consensusResolver=true.

Motivation: we continue to see tail-latency regressions driven by KV cache fragmentation and sudden spillback storms when compaction and eviction happen concurrently with large continuous batching workloads. This PR introduces the 'slate compactor'—a lightweight in-memory reassembly pass that coalesces fragmented slab ranges into contiguous 'slates' prior to eviction—and a complementary spillback backpressure mitigator that smooths eviction-induced I/O bursts. Summary of work: added a slate compactor component in the KV residency controller that opportunistically merges small adjacent fragments into larger eviction candidates, introduced a preemptive reclaimer policy that marks low-utility slates for background rewrite, and implemented a spillback shaper that rate-limits and staggers on-disk spill operations based on current scheduler load and batching latency SLO signals. Design notes: the slate compactor is designed to be incremental and lock-friendly; it walks per-shard free lists and builds coalescing windows up to a configurable slate size. It emits rewrite intents rather than performing synchronous copies; the rewriter runs as a background task with tenant-aware rate limits. The spillback mitigator hooks into the runtime scheduler to measure active batch queue depth and KV delta write throughput and applies an exponential dampener to spill concurrency when the batch latency percentile exceeds configured SLOs. The implementation keeps the default behavior unchanged for small deployments but enables compaction aggressiveness for Dedicated/Private tiers via runtime flags. Backwards compatibility: metadata format is unchanged and the slate compactor writes a short-lived 'slate manifest' in the cache metadata that is ignored by older nodes (safely forward-compatible). Testing: unit tests cover compaction window selection heuristics, rewrite intent lifecycle, and stall scenarios; integration tests simulate high-continuous-batch workloads with synthetic KV footprints to validate tail-latency improvements and reduced spike IO. Observability: new metrics (kv.slate.coalesced_bytes, kv.slate.rewrite_intents, kv.spillback.throttle_factor) and trace spans (kv.compactor.window, kv.rewriter.job) were added; a dashboard patch is included to expose spike correlation between batch latency and spill events. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag 'kv.slate_compactor.enabled' and 'kv.spillback_mitigator.mode' (off/gradual/aggressive). Suggested canary sequence: 2 hosts -> 10 hosts -> full fleet with monitoring of p99 latency, spill IO throughput, and disk queue length. Risk & mitigation: the main risk is increased background IO from rewrites; mitigations include tenant-aware pacing, a conservative default, and an emergency disable flag. Related: ENG-4981 (fragmentation investigation), SUP-1892 (customer incident involving spill storms), ENG-5023 (scheduler-batching SLO hooks).
Add slate compactor to reduce fragmentation, background rewriter for safe in-place coalescing, and spillback shaper to smooth eviction IO during heavy continuous batching. Metrics, traces, tests, and rollout flags included.
Improves KV cache memory efficiency and reduces spillback-induced latency spikes. Feature is off by default; enable via kv.slate_compactor.enabled. See docs/runbooks/kv-slate-compactor.md for rollout steps.
Marco Ruiz: please add a conservative default slate size and document recommended values for Dedicated vs Hosted.
Author (Priya): added runtime flag kv.slate_compactor.max_slate_bytes with comments and tuned defaults (16KB hosted / 256KB dedicated).
Aisha Patel: can the rewrite worker be preempted when latency SLOs spike? We need an emergency backoff.
Author (Priya): rewrite worker now subscribes to scheduler SLO channel and backs off to zero concurrency when p99>target for two consecutive windows.
Connor Li: integration test is solid but add an assertion on kv.slate.coalesced_bytes monotonicity after compaction run.
Author (Priya): added monotonicity check and fixed an edge-case where tiny fragments were double-counted during window merge.
QA (Liam Chen): ran canary on dedicated cluster with tenant mix; p99 reduced by ~18% under the synthetic continuous batch job and spill IO sparked by evictions dropped 63%.
Decision: Approved-by: Marco Ruiz, Aisha Patel. Merging via squash after green CI.

Motivation: Dedicated capacity customers observed sporadic fragmentation of reservation windows that caused short-lived throughput cliffs during tenant bursts. This PR introduces a Reservation Contiguity Controller (RCC) that consolidates adjacent reservation segments at allocation time and an HDR-sketch based Utilization Reporter to provide robust, memory-efficient percentile signals for autoscaler decisions.

What this changes: RCC enforces a best-effort contiguity policy when creating or extending reservations so that tenant burst tokens are less likely to span many small, discontinuous slots. The contiguity heuristic prefers minimizing boundary churn while respecting placement constraints and soft-commitment SLAs. The HDR-sketch reporter replaces the previous fixed-bucket sampler for per-tenant utilization percentiles (P50/P90/P99) and feeds a new utilization-summary protobuf to the autoscaler.

Compatibility and safety: All changes are opt-in behind the feature flag dedicated.rcc_enabled and telemetry.hdr_enabled. Default rollout is off for existing Dedicated clusters; the controller is safe to run in a dry-run mode (dedicated.rcc_dry_run=true) where it only emits metrics and reconciliation logs. The reporter emits both the new sketch payload and the legacy bucketed metrics to avoid alerting gaps during rollout.

Key design notes: - Contiguity is soft: RCC will not preempt higher-priority reservations to coalesce windows. It attempts best-effort compaction within the same allocation cycle. - HDR sketch chosen due to bounded memory footprint and mergeability across pools; percentiles computed server-side for autoscaler logic. - Autoscaler integration: the autoscaler now consumes sketch-aggregated percentile signals and a new continuity_score field to weigh recent fragmentation in scale decisions.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for controller reconciliation, compaction heuristics, and conflict resolution. Integration tests mock multi-tenant allocation churn showing a 37% reduction in short-lived boundary violations in the synthetic harness. E2E job added to the dedicated-lab CI that runs against a small dedicated cluster image and validates no SLA regressions under bursty load.

Rollout plan: 1) Enable telemetry.hdr_enabled in telemetry-only clusters and validate percentile stability for 48h. 2) Enable dedicated.rcc_dry_run across canary fleet and monitor continuity_score and allocation churn metrics for 72h. 3) Flip dedicated.rcc_enabled in 10% of fleets, watch tail latency and SLA events, then scale to full roll.

Checklist: - [x] RFC and Linear attached (ENG-1129) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Canary e2e job - [x] Backwards-compatible telemetry fallback - [x] Docs: operational runbook added to internal wiki (link: https://linear.app/internal/rcc-runbook)

Related: touches allocation/allocator/core, autoscaler/decision, telemetry/collector and the dedicated console's reservation view. Linear/PM tickets: PM-401 describes the customer SLA acceptance criteria.

Notes: This PR intentionally leaves the strict defragmentation phase out of scope (future work) and focuses on preventing fragmentation at allocation time and improving percentile signal fidelity for the autoscaler.
Evan: Can contiguity cause suboptimal packing under heavy fragmentation?
Maya: Controller is best-effort and will not preempt existing higher-priority allocations; added unit tests to prove safe fallbacks.
Sara: Sketch memory usage concerns for large pools?
Maya: HDR sketch uses bounded 16KB per-tenant (configurable); included memory-impact smoke tests and a prometheus gauge for total-sketch-bytes.
Carlos: Autoscaler needs a smoothing window on continuity_score to avoid flip-flops.
Maya: Added 5-minute exponential smoothing in autoscaler consumer and documented rationale.
Approvals: Evan approved (LGTM), Sara approved after sketch memory clarifications, Carlos approved pending smoothing verification which passed in canary runs.
Add Reservation Contiguity Controller to reduce reservation fragmentation and an HDR-sketch based utilization reporter to improve percentile signals for autoscaling. Feature gated and rolled out via canary. Impact: expected smoother tenant burst behavior and improved autoscaler stability.

Motivation: We observed a persistent tail in streaming first-byte latency caused by frequent kernel preemption for very small microbatches and sporadic KV-cache misses that trigger synchronous warms. This PR introduces two complementary runtime techniques: 1) a predictive token-spill buffer that accepts very small emissions and defers kernel handoff until a short prediction window elapses (reduces preemption churn), and 2) a cooperative kernel-handoff mechanism that groups compatible streams into a short-lived cooperative run on the GPU to amortize kernel launch and context-switch cost. The result is lower p95/p99 TTFB across mixed short/long requests without increasing p50.

What changed (high level): added a predictive spill buffer and eviction heuristic, a cooperative handoff scheduler that matches by model variant and seqlen-range, speculative KV-cache rewarm hooks for in-flight spills, and a new live canary test and metrics to validate behavioral regressions. The description below contains a brief walk-through of the commits, changed areas, testing, and review notes. All narrative is continuous in this field.
- 0001Introduce predictive spill buffer and basic eviction policy
- 0002Implement cooperative kernel handoff coordinator and APIs
- 0003Add speculative KV rewarm hooks tied to spilled streams
- 0004Telemetry: metrics + tags for spill path and handoff latency
- 0005Integration tests and a small streaming canary; docs and examples
- 0006Fix race in handoff state machine after reviewer feedback
- 0007Tighten early-commit threshold and add feature flag (off by default)

Claire Huang: Added a CAS-based guard in 0006, and added unit test coverage to exercise the transition.

Claire Huang: Added a guardrail: feature flag to enable handoff only for models with average response > 32 tokens and an opt-in annotation per route; default remains off for small-chat routes.
Rina Okafor: CI failed on the initial integration run (streaming_canary) due to flaky timing in the simulated KV warm; suggest a small backoff loop.
Claire Huang: Added a micro backoff and deterministic timing in canary harness; reran CI and green.
Ethan Cole: Approve after tests green and metrics look sane on canary.
Samir Patel: Small nit on metric names, but OK to merge once metrics doc updated.
Claire Huang: Addressed metric name nits and updated docs.
Merge-bot: Squash merged as commit 7a3d9c (squash).
Initial CI: failure on streaming_canary (timing-race) -> fixed by adding deterministic backoff and re-run. Full integration and unit test matrix passed. Binary smoke tests (linux-x86, cuda12) passed.
Unit tests added for handoff state transitions and spill eviction; end-to-end streaming canary simulating mixed short/long workload. Canary results: p50 unchanged, p95 improved by ~18%, p99 improved by ~22% on a mixed 70/30 short/long traffic mix. Added microbench script for developers to reproduce: ci/integration/streaming_latency_check.sh
Feature gated behind runtime flag 'predictive_spill_enabled' (default off). Route-level opt-in annotation 'streaming.handoff=enabled' introduced. No API breaking changes to public SDKs.
New metrics: runtime.spill.count, runtime.spill.evictions, runtime.handoff.coop_latency_ms, runtime.handoff.batch_size, runtime.kv.rewarm.attempts. Docs updated at docs/observability/metrics_spill_handoff.md with guidance for alert thresholds.
Feature is behind a cluster-level flag; recommend canary rollout to 5% of traffic in a non-critical region and monitor runtime.handoff.coop_latency_ms and runtime.spill.evictions for 48h before enabling globally. For Dedicated customers, coordinate with SRE for node-level kernel affinity settings.

Context: Dedicated capacity is often fragmented by many small reservations and short-lived allocations. This fragmentation reduces effective utilization and drives unnecessary autoscaler churn. Previous approaches (aggressive backfilling and larger warm pools) either increased cost or exposed tenants to noisy neighbors.

This PR implements two coordinated pieces: 1) a rate-limited 'reservation stitcher' that periodically merges adjacent, compatible reservations into larger contiguous reservation blocks to reduce fragmentation, and 2) a new tenancy allocator named 'FairBank' that uses weighted proportional allocation with soft budget banking to preserve per-tenant throughput guarantees while improving global packing efficiency.

Key design points: the stitcher only operates on reservations that are compatible by model family, region, and isolation constraints; it applies a token-bucket rate limiter to stitch operations to avoid allocation storms during recovery windows; every stitch is recorded as an atomic plan so it can be safely rolled back on failure. FairBank maintains per-tenant debt/balance counters and enforces a soft spend floor so high-usage tenants cannot immediately consume freshly stitched capacity; the allocator includes a configurable rebalancing window and cooldown to prevent oscillation.

Telemetry and knobs: added metrics stitcher_ops_total, stitch_reverts_total, stitched_capacity_ratio, fairbank_balance_gauge, and fairness_index_p99. Config flags: feature.gate.reservation_stitcher (opt-in), stitcher.rate_limit_qps, fairbank.rebalance_window_seconds, allocator.cooldown_seconds. Default gates off for release to enable staged rollouts.

Testing & results: unit tests for stitch plan generation and rollback; race tests for concurrent stitch attempts; integration-scale job that simulates 150 tenants with realistic reservation churn. Results on benchmark lab: 6-12% utilization gain on mixed workloads, tail latency unchanged within 1-2% for tenant-controlled SLOs.

Migration & rollout: ship behind gate; start with stitcher.rate_limit_qps=0 (disabled), enable in canary region with conservative qps, monitor stitched_capacity_ratio and stitch_reverts_total. If reverts spike, reduce qps or disable. Fallback path: allocator can run in legacy compatibility mode by setting fairbank.mode=legacy.

Why this is different: rather than aggressive prewarming or larger warm pools, stitching reclaims fragmented capacity in-situ with minimal cross-tenant disturbance, and FairBank provides a budget-aware allocation scheme that prevents short-term allocation storms from consuming newly stitched resources.

Related: ENG-1429 (fragmentation investigation), PM-387 (cost-efficiency objective), SUP-721 (customer report about cold starts during commit storms).
Introduces a rate-limited reservation stitcher and a new FairBank tenancy allocator to improve dedicated-fleet utilization without compromising per-tenant throughput guarantees. Feature is behind a gate and can be rolled back. Improves average GPU utilization on synthetic traces by ~6-12% and reduces fragmentation-related cold starts.
Ethan Park: This looks promising. Two concerns: (1) concurrent stitch operations on overlapping reservation ranges could race; can you guarantee idempotency? (2) how do we ensure stitch rollback doesn't violate SLOs?
Maya Lopez: For (1) stitch plans acquire a lightweight reservation lock (sharded by node-range) and are implemented as compare-and-swap on plan version; redundant attempts are no-ops. For (2) we record pre-stitch capacity fingerprints and do a quick sanity check post-commit; if we detect SLO deviation we immediately revert and emit stitch_reverts_total for alerting.
Liang Zhou: Please add an explicit metric for stitch_lock_conflicts and name the fairness metric fairness_index_p99 to match existing dashboard conventions.
Maya Lopez: Added stitch_lock_conflicts and renamed the metric to fairness_index_p99 in latest commit.
Sofia Martinez: Ran the integration harness on benchmark-lab. Util gain is visible and tail latency unchanged in the canary trace. Approving pending small nits on docs.
Ethan Park: Left a small comment about backoff strategy; once that's addressed and CI is green I'm happy to squash-merge.
payload.title: Rate-limited reservation stitcher and FairBank tenancy allocator
