Context and motivation: We frequently see tenants that could benefit from a coordinated set of defaults across batching, cache warmup, and quantization profiles. Individually tuning each knob is error-prone and expensive; operators often pick conservative defaults to avoid regressions which increases unit cost. This PR introduces the Cost-Fusion Agent: a lightweight service that aggregates short-term workload signals and historical unit-econ estimates to propose tenant-specific defaults and an accompanying Quant Annealer that tests gentle quant steps in a safety-first way. The goal is to push reasonable cost wins with minimal manual intervention while preserving quality and latency SLOs.

What this change does (high level): Adds a new service (cost-fusion-agent) and an optional background job (quant-annealer) that work together to generate and validate default configurations per tenant. The agent observes request size distribution, tail latency, hot KV cache hit rates, and historical model accuracy deltas (from eval sets) to synthesize a recommended triplet: batch_size_default, cache_warmup_policy, quant_profile_candidate. The annealer materializes short, controlled validation runs against a shadow queue of traffic or replay samples and records unit-econ delta and quality checks. If the candidate passes safety gates, the recommendation is written into the tenant defaults store as a suggested profile, and surfaced in Console and CLI as a non-destructive suggestion.

Backward compatibility and opt-in: All behavior is behind the feature-flag COST_FUSION_AGENT enabled per-tenant. Defaults remain unchanged for tenants who do not opt-in. For Private deployments we add an env toggle (ENABLE_QUANT_ANNEALER=false) to avoid running anneals in air-gapped installations. No runtime interface changes to external APIs.

Design notes and safety: The annealer uses conservative quant steps (e.g., float32->int8 via calibrated PTQ path with KV-cache compatibility checks) and never auto-promotes a profile without explicit approval or a positive safe-window (observed for N consecutive anneals and unit-econ improvement above threshold). Quality gates include prompt-set BLEU/ROUGE or internal similarity scores, latency and p99 tail overhead, and a rollback timer. The agent exposes a dry-run mode in the Console for operators to preview expected cost delta.

Migration and deployment plan: 1) Deploy cost-fusion-agent as a new deployment in the host cluster (small resource footprint); 2) Enable feature-flag for internal dogfood tenants; 3) Run annealer in dry-run mode for two weeks and review suggestions dashboard; 4) Gradually roll to more tenants with manual approvals. For Dedicated customers we will enable the agent as an opt-in addon in the console.

Testing and observability: Added metrics: fusion.agent.suggestions.count, fusion.agent.approved.count, annealer.run.duration_ms, annealer.quality.failures, annealer.unit_econ.delta. New Console panels: tenant-suggested-profiles and quant-anneal-history. E2E tests include simulated tenant traces with controlled latencies and a replay harness that checks the annealer's quality gates. CI: matrix runs across small/medium/large sample sizes.

Files changed (summary):
- services/cost-fusion-agent/{main.go,agent.go,simulator.go,proto/api.proto}  -- new service and core logic
- services/quant-annealer/{annealer.go,runner.go,profiles.go} -- annealing/validation logic and safe-fallbacks
- pkg/tenants/defaults_store.go -- add write/read API for suggested profiles with metadata and audit fields
- console/components/tenant-suggestions.tsx -- UI for previewing suggested defaults
- test/replay/fixtures/{small,medium}/ -- new fixtures for annealer e2e
- ci/workflows/annealer-matrix.yml -- adds an annealer job matrix for CI
- docs/ops/cost-fusion-agent.md -- operational runbook and toggles

Small illustrative snippet (agent rule matcher):
- services/cost-fusion-agent/agent.go +37 @@
   func scoreSample(s Sample) float64 {
     // estimate token-weighted cost impact and quality delta
     costDelta := estimateCostDelta(s)
     qualityRisk := estimateQualityRisk(s)
     return costDelta / (1.0 + qualityRisk)
   }

Review conversation (selected):
- Mai Tran (reviewer): "Nice end-to-end, biggest question is annealer safety. Please ensure the annealer cannot ship promoted profiles without a manual approval toggle for tenants with >500k monthly tokens."
- Author (Aisha): "Added manual-approval toggle per tenant (defaults_store supports approval flags). For tenants >500k tokens the annealer will only propose suggestions to Console, not auto-apply. Documented in ops runbook."
- Lucas Rivera (reviewer): "Two nits: 1) move the feature flag to runtime flags package, 2) add a short-circuit to skip annealer when replay sample quality is stale."
- Author: "Addressed both in latest commit; moved flag and added freshness check with TTL on replay samples (configurable)."
- Jonah Brooks (reviewer): "CI flaked once on quantized runner on aarch tests, looks resolved after the runner isolation fix."
- Jonah Brooks (approval): "LGTM after CI green and docs added."

CI summary: Initial CI run failed on one aarch quant integration (flake). Reran matrix with isolated runner image; all checks passed. New workflow annealer-matrix runs: linux/amd64, linux/aarch64, small/medium/large fixtures. Unit, integration and e2e smoke tests passed.

Merge outcome: Squash merged into main. Post-merge actions: created console ticket to add a Dashboard card (PM-198) and ops pager recipe for annealer failures. Added a follow-up ticket to extend tenant sampling heuristics (ENG-7301).

Notes and rationale: We purposely keep the initial annealer conservative and visible in Console to build operator trust. The fusion approach reduces repeated manual tuning and captures cross-lever interactions (e.g., a larger batch size may increase cache contention; the agent accounts for that). This PR is intentionally large but modular: agent and annealer live in separate services, defaults_store change is minimal, and UI surfaces are lightweight.

If you'd like to run this locally: see docs/ops/cost-fusion-agent.md for quickstart (docker-compose override that boots agent + annealer local harness).

Adds a Cost-Fusion Agent service that synthesizes tenant workload signals to auto-propose batching, cache-warmup and quantization defaults; includes a small annealer process to refine quant profiles with safety fallbacks. No breaking changes to public API.
payload.title: Introduce cost-fusion agent and quant annealer for tenant-specific defaults

Motivation: Our monorepo accumulates outdated dependency ranges that increase CI flakiness and slow down lint/test feedback. This PR implements a lightweight dependency-staleness sentinel (a small service + CI gate) to mark crates/npm packages that haven’t been updated for >9 months and surfaces a compact remediation plan. It also refactors lint/test CI into staged shards (fast-feedback lanes + extended lanes) so quick edits get sub-60s feedback while full checks run in parallel without blocking merges.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds tools/dep-sentinel/ (Go) and a small GitHub Action that runs weekly to produce a compact report and a dependency-provenance.json used by CI.
- Introduces a new CI lane (staged-lint) that shards linters by path heuristics and runs a fast subset (typechecks + critical ESLint rules + go vet) on PR hotpaths.
- Adds a pre-merge dependency gate that fails PRs when the sentinel flags a direct dependency with a critical security patch available or if a package is >18 months stale and used by a server path. The gate is configurable via .github/dep-gate-config.yaml.
- Moves heavy lint/format passes to nightly and to the extended CI lane to reduce pre-merge latency.
- Adds lightweight dashboards and telemetry hooks for dependency churn (console alerts/metrics).

Checklist: 
- [x] Implement dep-sentinel service and CI action
- [x] Integrate sentinel output into staged CI lane
- [x] Add path-aware lint sharding logic and tests
- [x] Add docs/ci/dep-sentinel.md and update CONTRIBUTING.md with quickfix steps
- [x] Run migration on main to backfill dependency-provenance.json

Backwards compatibility and safety: The dependency gate is opt-in per repo via .github/dep-gate-config.yaml. Default behavior is advisory (warn-only) for the first two weeks after rollout; this PR toggles warn->fail after a staged rollout and a cross-team sync. All changes are behind feature flags and infra configs so we can quickly revert to advisory mode.

Why this is different from previous dependence/CI work: Rather than a broad, heavyweight dependency prune, this approach gives observable, actionable signals (staleness + vuln presence + owner suggestion) and pairs those signals with a CI flow that reduces developer pain (fast lint on hotpath, full checks async). The dep-sentinel is intentionally small (single binary + periodic job) to minimize ongoing maintenance.
Diego Alvarez: Nice small sentinel—can we keep the weekly job output under 64KB? If the report grows too big it breaks action artifacts. Please add trimming logic.
Asha Menon: Good catch — added a truncate+summary routine and pagination for full reports in tools/dep-sentinel/main.go (commit a1f4e2c).
Mira Patel: The pre-merge gate looked scary at first; can we default to warn for the first rollout? Add an override flag for emergency opt-out.
Asha Menon: Configured default to advisory mode and added .github/dep-gate-config.yaml -> fail_after_days to allow staged enforcement.
Samir Gupta: CI runtime improved locally. Two nits: (1) add unit tests for sharder heuristics edge cases, (2) document how to opt-out for infra-only repos.
Asha Menon: Added tests/test-sharder-heuristics.py and docs/ci/dep-sentinel.md with opt-out instruction.
--- a/.github/workflows/staged-lint.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/staged-lint.yml
@@ -1,4 +1,12 @@
 name: Staged Lint
+on: [pull_request]
+jobs:
+  fast-feedback:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - name: Run fast lints
+        run: scripts/ci/fastpath-dispatch.sh --fast
Adds a weekly dependency-staleness sentinel, a configurable pre-merge dependency gate, and staged lint sharding to speed up PR feedback. Default gate behavior is advisory for staged rollout. See docs/ci/dep-sentinel.md for operational details.
Rollout plan: week 0 (warn-only), week 2 (fail for server-touching deps older than 18 months), monitor dep_sentinel.stale_count and dep_gate.reject_rate dashboards. To revert to advisory quickly toggle .github/dep-gate-config.yaml -> mode: advisory and re-deploy the action.
Backfilled dependency-provenance.json on main and triggered a one-time run of dep-sentinel weekly job. Opened follow-up tasks: ENG-4201 (auto-PRs for critical deps), ENG-4202 (nightly full-lint to S3 archival).

payload.body:
Summary: This PR tunes the cost-efficient SLO tier to prefer larger, more GPU-efficient batches (especially on decode-heavy traffic), while adding guardrails that prevent unbounded queue growth during bursts. Motivation: Early perf runs for the tiered defaults showed meaningful $/1K token improvements from more aggressive batching, but the naive configuration can create queue blowups under sudden concurrency spikes (tail latency + timeouts + cascading retries). For the cost-efficient tier we explicitly accept higher latency, but we still need bounded behavior and predictable degradation (backpressure/load shedding) so that bursty customers don’t take the whole cluster into a retry storm. Changes: (1) More aggressive batching targets for cost-efficient tier: increase target_batch_tokens for decode, allow larger max_batch_tokens for compatible model families, bias scheduler toward forming fuller decode batches when queue is healthy. (2) Burst guardrails: add queue depth / queued tokens hard caps for the cost-efficient tier; when exceeded, we escalate through overload modes (clamp batch growth -> tighten max_wait_ms -> admission control) rather than continuing to accumulate queued work. (3) Backpressure behavior: introduce a cost-efficient-only "soft reject" path that returns 429 with Retry-After when the queue caps are exceeded, instead of accepting requests that are likely to timeout. (4) Stability knobs: add a per-tier "burst_window_ms" accounting mechanism so short spikes don’t immediately trip hard load shedding; instead we allow a small debt window before escalating. (5) Metrics: add counters/gauges to observe queue caps and overload escalations (tier labeled, with cardinality-safe tags). Non-goals: this PR does not add profile selection reason codes (tracked in ENG-18426 / PR-28473), and it does not change fast-tier tail protection (ENG-18424 / PR-28458). Default values (cost-efficient only, subject to further tuning in benchmark-lab): - max_batch_tokens: 8192 -> 16384 (model-family dependent; guarded by existing model metadata for max supported batch tokens) - target_decode_batch_tokens: 4096 -> 8192 - max_wait_ms: 8ms (unchanged) but dynamically clamped to 4ms in overload mode 1 - queue_max_queued_tokens: new, default 2 * max_batch_tokens - queue_max_queued_requests: new, default 512 (primarily for tiny prompts) - burst_window_ms: new, default 250ms Bench results (local A100 + H100 sanity + mixed workload replay; see linked perf artifacts): - Throughput: +12–18% tokens/sec vs previous cost-efficient candidate profile on decode-heavy mixes - Median latency: +3–7% (expected trade-off) - Tail behavior under burst: p99 stabilized vs prior candidate (previously saw multi-second tail due to queue growth; now bounded with 429s under sustained overload) Testing: - Added unit tests for overload state machine transitions and queue cap enforcement. - Added integration test that simulates burst concurrency ramp and asserts queue caps prevent unbounded queue growth. - Ran perf suite scenario "mixed_workload_cost_efficient" with 3 seeds; results attached in CI artifacts. Rollout: guarded behind existing tiered defaults feature flag; no behavior change unless cost-efficient tier is enabled. Notes for SRE: cost-efficient tier will surface 429s earlier under sustained overload rather than timing out; this is intentional and aligns with predictable degradation guidance in the rollout playbook. Follow-ups: - PR-28492 will further constrain metric cardinality for tier labels once the final taxonomy is locked. - Consider raising queue_max_queued_requests for embedding-like workloads once we have separate tier profiles per route type (not in scope).
Sofia Ivanova (review): The direction looks right, but I’m worried about queue_max_queued_tokens being expressed as 2x max_batch_tokens globally. For small models we’ll hit the cap too early and shed load more aggressively than necessary. Can we make the cap proportional to in-flight decode concurrency instead? Marcus Reed (author): Good call. I added burst_window_ms and made the cap scale with "effective_decode_parallelism" (defaults to scheduler’s current estimate, bounded). I kept the 2x as a fallback if the estimate is unavailable. Added tests for both code paths. Omar El-Sayed (review): The clamp from 8ms -> 4ms in overload mode 1 makes sense. Please confirm we don’t starve long-prefill requests when cost-efficient is mixed with other tiers on the same worker. Marcus Reed (author): Confirmed: the clamp is tier-scoped and only affects queues tagged cost-efficient. The global anti-starvation logic remains unchanged. I also added a regression test with mixed short/long prefill showing forward progress for long requests. Sean Gallagher (review): From an SRE perspective, returning 429 is preferable to timeouts, but we need metric signals to page/triage (cap hits rate, overload mode duration). Are these exported and tagged safely? Marcus Reed (author): Added scheduler_queue_cap_hits_total, scheduler_overload_mode (gauge), and scheduler_overload_transitions_total. Tags: tier + region; model is not included to avoid cardinality blowups. Allison Grant (review): Please ensure the metric names match the taxonomy draft and that tier labeling is consistent with the other PRs. Also, can we add a log line on first transition into overload mode? Marcus Reed (author): Updated names to match the draft taxonomy. Added rate-limited structured log on first transition per worker per minute (includes tier, overload_mode, queue_depth, queued_tokens). Lena Fischer (review): Can we keep the default values conservative until benchmark-lab runs land? I’d prefer max_batch_tokens 16384 only where we have validated kernels and memory headroom. Marcus Reed (author): Agreed. I gated 16384 behind model metadata (max_batch_tokens_supported) and defaulted to 8192 for unknown families; updated config comments and added a validation check in schema loading. Sofia Ivanova (final): LGTM after the scaling change + tests. Sean Gallagher (final): Approved; please link this in the rollout checklist so oncall knows to expect earlier 429s for cost-efficient. Marcus Reed (author): Done (added note in internal overload_modes doc; rollout checklist link will be updated in the Drive doc separately).
Runtime: cost-efficient batching tier is more throughput-oriented (larger target batches) with new safeguards under burst/overload (bounded queue growth, backpressure escalation, and automatic batch-size clamp).
payload.title: Cost-efficient tier: aggressive batching + burst guardrails to prevent queue blowups

Motivation: customers require stronger guarantees that service endpoints and operator actions cannot be used to cross regional boundaries for regulated tenants. This PR adds three coordinated pieces: (1) a region-locked service alias layer that lets operators declare service aliases bound to a specific residency zone and rejects cross-zone resolution at the gateway; (2) an RBACv2 policy adapter and migration shim to convert legacy role bindings to attribute-driven, region-aware constraints; (3) a KMS provenance tracer that records per-request KMS key metadata, signs audit payloads with a provenance envelope, and exposes a compact proof for compliance ingestion. The change is designed to be opt-in initially via a FeatureFlagRegionLocking gate and rolled out to Dedicated and Private deployments first. Checklist: - Feature flag gated in config and console UI toggles added; - Migration tool (cli/rbacv2-migrate) with dry-run and apply modes; - E2E tests for cross-region request rejection and audit proof shape; - Backward compatibility: legacy bindings are still honored until admin-run migration completes; - Rollback plan: disable feature flag and revert adapter deployment; - Monitoring: added metrics rbac.adapter.migrations, kms.provenance.failures, gateway.regionlock.rejections. Migration notes: run `./bin/rbac-migrate --linear ENG-9821 --dry-run` to preview policy transformations; when ready, run with --apply, then enable feature flag for tenants incrementally. Audit path: the provenance tracer attaches signed metadata (kms_key_id, kms_provider_region, envelope_sig) to audit entries and writes a compact index entry to /audit/proofs for downstream retention pipelines. Compatibility: the tracer supports existing CMKs and AWS/GCP provider plugins; new providers can implement the ProvenanceDriver interface. Security review summary: threat modelling concluded that signed provenance reduces ambiguity in audit stores by preventing KMS-origin spoofing; however, care taken to limit sensitive payloads in traces. Document links: RFC attached in PR; migration playbook added to docs/security/region-locked-services.md. Merge: squashed and merged after approvals and green CI.
Carlos Ruiz: Request changes - the adapter currently rewrites bindings without preserving annotation metadata; please keep original mapping as a comment blob to assist audits.
Maya Chen: Reply - added preserved_annotation field in adapter output and tests to assert it is included in migrate --apply output.
Anika Patel: Nit - extract the signature envelope construction into a helper so driver code remains thin. Also add one extra unit test for malformed key metadata.
Maya Chen: Reply - factored envelope helper and added negative test for missing kms_provider_region; CI covers this now.
Ethan Li: Approve - validated canary run in staging with migration dry-run; metrics look good and rejection path logs include helpful context.
Merged via squash on 2026-01-18 after approvals from Anika Patel and Ethan Li. Post-merge jobs executed: canary migration dry-run and provenance indexer smoke job. No merge conflicts.
Adds region-locked service aliases to enforce residency at gateway level; introduces RBACv2 migration adapter with dry-run/apply CLI; introduces KMS provenance tracer that signs audit proofs for downstream compliance ingestion. Feature is behind a feature flag and off by default. Admins should run rbac-migrate in dry-run before enabling.
payload.title: Introduce region-locked service aliases, RBACv2 adapter, and KMS provenance tracer

payload.body:
Motivation: We see recurring false-positive token-cost alerts when high short-lived bursts (e.g., chatbots hitting a prompt loop or synthetic traffic) spike per-tenant token consumption for a few seconds. Existing rules fire aggressively and shift on-call attention away from real regressions. This PR adds a lightweight 'Token Cost Hedger' service that detects burst patterns, annotates traces, and provides a graded alerting adapter that reduces noise while preserving SLO sensitivity. Changes in this PR: 1) telemetry/hedger: new hedger service that ingests summarized per-invocation token counts and maintains a short epoch-based baseline per-tenant+model. Detects burst anomalies using an exponentially-weighted moving baseline and a burst-window score; exposes hedger decisions via traces and metrics. 2) tracing: add token_hedger.evaluate span and hedger decision tags to invocation traces so downstream tools can join hedger annotations to existing spans. 3) alerts: adaptive alert policy token_cost_burst.yaml that uses hedger.score and quiet-window gating before escalating alerts. 4) dashboard: observability/dashboards/token-hedger.json with a per-tenant sparkline, burst-score heatmap, waterfall token-cost decomposition (kernel queue, generation, streaming). 5) docs: docs/observability/hedger.md describing configuration knobs (window size, sensitivity, fallback suggestions). 6) tests: hedger unit tests and a small integration harness that replays synthetic bursts. Rollout plan: deploy hedger as opt-in behind feature flag (.observability.hedger.enabled = true) for 7 days on a shadowing mode (emit metrics/trace tags but do not influence alert routing), then enable gating for canary tenants (5%) before turning on platform-wide. Backout plan: feature flag off; alerts fall back to previous rule. Design notes: hedger keeps only ephemeral per-tenant state (TTL 10m) and applies reservoir sampling for high-cardinality tenants to keep cardinality bounded. Hedger exposes three primary metrics: hedger.epoch_baseline_tokens, hedger.burst_score, hedger.noise_suppressed_alerts. Privacy/security: hedger operates on aggregated counts and tenant IDs; no request payloads stored. See linked linear tasks for evaluation and SLO calibration. CI status: initial lint failure due to docs formatting; fixed in a follow-up commit. All tests green on final run. Merge outcome: squash-merged to main.
Introduce a burst-aware token-cost hedger service plus a contextual per-tenant dashboard and an adaptive alert policy. Hedger reduces noisy alerts during short token surges and provides suggested fallback actions (model fallback, quota bump, quiet window). Includes sampling and cardinality controls to limit telemetry cost.
Start in shadow mode for 7 days, enable gating for 5% canary tenants, then ramp to 100% over 48h. Monitor hedger.noise_suppressed_alerts and hedger.burst_score distributions; rollback if suppressed_alerts for high-severity SLO violations > 1% for two consecutive 10m windows.
Low operational risk; hedger only annotates traces and emits metrics in shadow mode. When gating is enabled it will suppress noisy alerts but keeps a fallback path to notify on sustained regressions. Telemetry cost increase is bounded by reservoir sampling and 10m TTL. Expected benefit: reduce pager churn from short-lived bursts and improve signal-to-noise for oncall.
Miguel Ortega: This is promising—can you quantify the expected reduction in alert noise? Also worried about unbounded cardinality if we tag traces per-tenant. Could we add reservoir sampling?
Aisha Raman (author): Added reservoir sampling and a per-tenant cardinality cap; updated docs to call out TTL and sampling behavior. I ran a 48h synthetic replay and saw ~72% reduction in short-lived alert churn on noisy tenants (measured in dev replay).
Priya Shah: Please add a small experiment to ensure SLO detection power isn't reduced for multi-minute regressions. Also request an e2e-observability job covering hedger gating logic.
Aisha Raman: Added e2e-observability tests that simulate sustained regressions vs spikes; hedger only suppresses when burst_score > threshold and duration < burst_window. Added metric hedger.noise_suppressed_alerts for monitoring. Tests added and CI updated.
Ethan Liu: Approve after addressing cardinality and adding the runbook section for incident response. Left one minor nit about naming hedger.metric -> hedger.epoch_baseline_tokens.
Priya Shah: Approved; e2e run passed on canary tenants.
payload.title: add-burst-aware-token-cost-hedger-and-contextual-alert-policy

payload.body:
Motivation: Customers with strict SLAs (latency and cost envelopes) need a proactive, low-cost way to detect drifting signal that will impact promised SLOs before pager noise spikes. This PR introduces a lightweight observability scan that anchors metric baselines to declared SLA windows and surfaces a contextual alert matrix that recommends remediation owners and severity. What changed at a glance: 1) a periodic 'SLA scan' job that computes per-route SLA deltas for latency, tail-latency, and token-cost drift (bucketed by prompt shape), 2) an alert matrix UI component (Dashboard: 'SLA Anchors') which shows prioritized cells with suggested owners and an auto-suppression TTL heuristic, 3) query and metric pipeline optimizations to run the scan cheaply across tenants (incremental rollups + single-pass aggregation), 4) a small set of instrumentation additions to token-phase timing spans so the scan can attribute per-token cost shifts to model/kernel phases, 5) a safety fallback policy that automatically lowers alert noise by auto-squelching alerts with <10 invocations in the detection window. Implementation notes: - SLA scan: implemented as a scheduled worker in observability/scan that reads per-route SLA definitions from the config service and computes three delta metrics: sla_latency_delta, sla_cost_delta, sla_tail_delta. Deltas are computed with exponential windowing so short spikes don't dominate. - Aggregation: added a new incremental rollup path in metrics/rollup that emits compact summaries keyed by (tenant, route, prompt_shape_bucket, model_variant). We reuse the existing reservoir histograms to approximate tails. - Token-phase timing: lightweight span tags added in runtime/trace_instrumentation to record phase durations (encode: token_gen_phase_ms, kv_cache_phase_ms, kernel_exec_phase_ms). Tags are categorical and low-cardinality. - UI: Dashboard tile 'SLA Anchors' added under observability/dashboards with matrix cells that link to per-route timeline, suggested owner, and a quick-run synthetic probe button. - Alerting: A new alert type sla-anchor-critical with tuned thresholds and a noise gate middleware that auto-suppresses churning cells. Backwards compatibility: Configs default to disabled for tenants without explicit SLA entries. Rollout plan: feature flag rollout over 2 weeks: 1) internal telemetry-only (week 1) 2) opt-in for customers via console (week 2) 3) default-on for tenants with SLAs (week 3, contingent on telemetry sanity). Checklist: - [x] Worker implementation and unit tests - [x] Rollup path and performance tests - [x] Low-cardinality span tags added and validated - [x] Dashboard and linking - [x] Alert policy and noise gate - [x] Documentation (console help + runbook) Testing and performance: Benchmarked the scan (10k routes across synthetic tenants) and confirmed the incremental rollups add ~0.8% CPU and <1% additional ingestion bytes by leveraging histogram compression. Synthetic probe generator was used to validate owner suggestions by correlating recent deploy tags and kernel-version changes. Rollback plan: Feature flag to turn off scan + a TTL to delete generated synthetic alerts. Related: ENG-3420 (SLA alert rationalization), ENG-3499 (token-phase minimal spans), SUP-7812 (customer reported early-warning requirement).
Diego Morales: Can you confirm retention implications for the new rollups? If we keep 30d rollups for all tenants this could grow; suggest tenant scoping.
Author (Aisha): We scoped rollups to tenants with SLA entries only and emit a compact 1KB summary per route per epoch; added note in deploy/feature_flags to ensure default-off for non-SLA tenants.
Priya Patel: The auto-suppression TTL seems aggressive for low-volume routes; suggest increase from 10m to 30m and add a decay-based re-alert window.
Author (Aisha): Agreed; bumped TTL to 30m and added exponential backoff for re-alerts in alerts/policies/sla_anchor_policy.yaml.
Liam O'Connor: Unit tests look good. One nit: prefer reservoir seed determinism in test_sla_scan to avoid flaky tails.
Add SLA-anchored observability scan and SLA Anchors dashboard: provides early detection of latency and cost drift tied to SLAs, plus an alert matrix with owner suggestions and noise gating. Disabled by default for tenants without SLA entries.
If alerts begin firing en masse after rollout, flip feature flag sla_anchor_flag to off and run the synthetic_probe/generator local run to reconcile which routes caused highest variance. The scan writes compact rollups to metrics.rollup.sla_* metrics; monitor cardinality if retention policies are changed.
payload.title: SLA-anchored observability scan and contextual alert matrix

payload.body:
Context: Recent incident (SUP-7890) exposed a pathological interaction between regional KV-drain timing and our egress throttles that caused aggressive connection reopens during transient egress pressure, amplifying downstream latency spikes. This PR introduces a graded egress dampener to smooth egress capacity reductions and a proactive rejoin guard to reduce stormy connection re-establishes. Summary of changes: 1) egress/dampener: new graded dampener module that applies a token-bucket backed smoothing window on egress reductions, with decaying step sizes per-tenant so sudden egress caps are ramped over a configurable window (default 30s). 2) recon/probe: proactive rejoin guard that tracks last-closed-epoch per connection and enforces a jittered exponential backoff with a lightweight health probe before allowing full-weighted rejoin; ties into existing lease metadata (prevents churning when upstream regional probes are noisy). 3) telemetry: added telemetry hooks and SLI emitters (egress_dampener_effect, rejoin_backoff_count, rejoin_probe_latency_p50/p95) and an SLO inspection alert rule that surfaces rapid tenant rejoin churn. 4) safety: feature-gated behind runtime flag runtime.features.graded_egress_dampener; default enabled only in regions with high egress variance. Motivation: Smooth, predictable degradation preserves SLOs for high-value tenants by avoiding oscillatory reopen-and-evict cycles that lead to KV mis-synchronization and cascading failovers. Checklist: - [x] design doc reviewed (ENG-4215) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] local chaos testing with synthetic egress spike harness - [x] telemetry & dashboards updated - [x] canary rollout plan attached Testing performed: unit tests for dampener thresholds and backoff logic; integration runs in perf-lab with staged egress caps verifying 70-90% reduction in rejoin churn; end-to-end smoke in canary region us-west2 for 6 hours with no regression in latency P95 and controlled increases in tail when egress intentionally reduced Rollout plan: 1) Deploy feature-gate off to main rollout across regions 2) Enable in canary region (us-west2) for 24h, monitor egress_dampener_effect and rejoin_backoff_count 3) Gradually enable in other regions with 10% traffic ramp every 2h 4) After 72h stable, flip default to enabled for all regions Rollback plan: flip runtime.features.graded_egress_dampener=false which immediately disables dampener and restores previous egress behavior; rejoin guards have a fast-fail safety mode when disabled Observability notes: - New dashboard: Reliability / Egress Dampener (panels for effect size, per-tenant smoothing, probe success) - Added SLO alert rule: SLO-REJOIN-CHURN (fires on >5% tenants with >3 rejoins/min sustained for 10m) Security & compliance: no changes to data plane or persisted PII. KMS/HSM not touched. Related: references SUP-7890, ENG-4215 and includes follow-up work item to tune tenant decay constants (ENG-4301).
Aisha Karim (2026-02-21): Asked for clarification on tenant decay defaults and whether multi-tenant pods would unfairly bias smoothing; responded with concrete fairness bounds and adjusted algorithm to apply per-tenant tokens — resolved.
Jonah Lee (2026-02-21): Requested additional CI integration coverage for simulated KV-drift during a slow egress ramp; added integration scenario and test — addressed.
Priya Nair (2026-02-22): Approved after verifying telemetry emits and dashboard panels. Left a note to follow up on alert thresholds in staging.

payload.body:
Motivation: Long-lived canaries add operational cost and delay rollback decisiveness. This PR introduces a lightweight 'ghost' canary primitive — an ephemeral, instrumented traffic slice that can pop in (shadow-mode) and pop out rapidly with deterministic rewind semantics. The goal is faster detection with minimal warm-up cost and automatic refunding of a 'rewind credit' budget when a ghost canary is torn down to accelerate failover and preserve SLAs.

What this PR does (high level): Adds a ghost_canary orchestrator component, a rewind-credit allocator, and integration hooks so the routing plane can promote a ghost from shadow to micro-canary with a single transactional cutover. Ghosts are intentionally short-lived (default TTL 5m) and are constrained by a per-namespace rewind credit pool. If the ghost signals a regression, routing will immediately trigger a rewind using the pre-allocated credits to roll back traffic and fast-track a larger failover.

Design notes: 1) Ghost lifecycle: create -> observe in shadow -> optionally promote -> short TTL -> auto-expire. 2) Rewind-credit: accounts tracked per-customer (namespace) and per-release; credits are consumed on promote and refunded on automatic or manual rollback depending on policy. 3) Consistency: state changes are recorded in the rollout ledger (idempotent operations) and we use the existing snapshot store for model version checkpoints so rewinds are deterministic. 4) Safety: multiple independent gating metrics (latency P99, error spikes, model drift score) are evaluated by the safety-checker before promoting. Non-deterministic regressions trigger immediate rollback without consuming additional credits.

Checklist: - [x] Core orchestrator implementation (ghost_canary.go) - [x] Rewind-credit allocator and accounting (credits.go) - [x] API for ephemeral canary config (schema + validation) - [x] Routing integration + transactional promote endpoint - [x] Integration tests simulating fast failover - [x] Docs + runbook for on-call

Testing done: unit tests for allocation logic, integration tests covering promote and rewind flows, end-to-end smoke that creates a ghost, promotes it, simulates a regression, and asserts that refunding semantics are correct. Load tests show ghost creation adds <2% overhead to routing path.

Migration notes: Adds a new optional rollout config field 'ghost_ttl' defaulting to 300s. Existing rollouts opt-in via the new field; no automatic behavior change for current canaries.

Related: ENG-1287 (fast rollback primitives), ENG-1299 (cohort budgeting).

Merge strategy: squash and merge after approval and successful CI.

Operational playbook (short): 1) When experimenting, create ghost with small cohort (0.5-1%) and set ghost_ttl to 2-10m. 2) Watch the ghost dashboard; if safety gates fail, system consumes rewind credit and rolls back automatically. 3) If ghost is healthy, can be promoted to micro-canary which consumes remaining credits for a transactional cutover.
Ethan Zhou: This is an interesting primitive. Concern: what prevents noisy signatures causing repeated promote/rewind churn?
Maya Patel (author): We added an exponential backoff for promotions and a per-namespace cooldown window tied to the credit allocator. Churn beyond the cooldown requires manual override.
Priya Malik: Can we ensure refunds are audited and appear in billing traces? Ops needs visibility into credit refunds for finance reconciliation.
Maya Patel: Credits are emitted as ledger events (credits.refund) and the billing pipeline is subscribed to these events; added unit tests to validate emission.
Luis Fernandez: Tests look good but add a deterministic replay test to prove rewinds restore exact model snapshot state.
Maya Patel: Added snapshot restore assertions to test_ghost_canary.py — now restores and validates tokenization checksum after rewind.
Introduces ephemeral 'ghost' canary primitive and rewind-credit accounting to enable fast failovers with deterministic rewinds. Ghosts are opt-in via 'ghost_ttl' and have minimal runtime overhead. See docs/rollouts/ghost-canaries.md for usage and on-call runbook.
payload.title: Ephemeral ghost canaries and rewind-crediting for fast failovers

payload.body:
Motivation: Fragmentation and synchronous spill to disk were a recurring cause of p99 tail spikes under mixed workloads. Evicting and immediately writing many small fragments forces page splits and stalls kernels that expect contiguous runs. This PR introduces a new small subsystem, the 'Cache Librarian', and a soft-demote probe flow that reduces eviction churn and coordinates preemptive spill orchestration with the scheduler. High-level changes: 1) Soft-demote probe: instead of immediately evicting suspect entries we mark them as 'soft-demoted' which lowers their admission score and makes them first-class candidates for background coalescing or preemptive spill. Soft-demoted pages remain readable but are excluded from continuous batching hot-paths for a configurable probe window (default 30s). 2) Cooperative preemptive spill orchestrator: long-running spill work is offloaded asynchronously using a non-blocking IO path (io_uring-style) with a bounded concurrency token pool so that spill writes do not interfere with low-latency token allocation for generation requests. 3) Fragmentation-aware scoring: eviction score now combines recency, a fragmentation penalty (favoring contiguous spans), tenant weight, and a kernel-contiguity bias that prefers victims which can be coalesced without page splits. 4) Background librarian compaction: when the node is underutilized the librarian opportunistically consolidates adjacent soft-demoted ranges into larger contiguous runs to reduce future spill overhead. 5) Scheduling hooks: the runtime scheduler uses librarian hints to avoid scheduling large compaction jobs during latency-critical windows and prefers idle windows and low token-rate shards. Implementation notes: The change is primarily in core/kv/cache_librarian.{cc,h}, runtime/scheduler/eviction_policy.h, and the spill manager runtime/io_offload.cc. Care was taken to minimize lock contention by using per-shard probe queues and atomic soft-demote bitflags. Rollout plan: unit tests -> perf lab -> canary 10% (5 hours) -> 50% (24h) -> full rollout. Monitoring: new metrics soft_demote_count, soft_demote_duration_seconds (histogram), librarian_coalesce_bytes, spill_token_queue_length. Performance: microbenchmarks on perf-lab show a 7% median and 12% p99 reduction in small-reads tail latency on mixed workloads (write-heavy background with hot reads). Memory fragmentation (measured as contiguous_free_run_median) improved ~2x in steady state, and average disk write amplification from spill fell by 18%. Backwards compatibility and safety: soft-demote is a no-op toggle (off by default), and all spill orchestration has a strict fallback to the existing synchronous spill path if io offload fails. Testing: added 22 unit tests and 6 integration tests (kv_librarian_integration). Changed files: small, focused diffs; no change to public APIs. Checklist: [x] design doc linked internally (ENG-2113) [x] unit tests added [x] perf benchmarks added and recorded [x] canary plan documented [x] metrics + dashboards prepared [x] feature-flag guarded (on via runtime flag)
Rina Sato: Please add a histogram for soft_demote duration so we can detect long-lived demotes that may starve tenants.
Aisha Patel: Added soft_demote_duration_seconds histogram and a dashboard panel. See commit d4e5f6a.
Liam O'Connor: Can we guarantee that async spill fallback won't increase tail on failure? Need clear fallback and observed behavior in perf tests.
Aisha Patel: The offload path is wrapped with a bounded retry and immediate fallback to the synchronous path on repeated failures. I added an integration test that simulates io failure and asserts latency remains bounded.
Marcus Nguyen: Minor: prefer smaller default probe window (30s is fine but make it runtime-configurable). Also please document behavior under high churn.
Aisha Patel: Probe window is exposed as a runtime flag and documented in docs/architecture/kv-librarian.md. Added note on behavior under churn and recommended defaults.
Introduces Cache Librarian with a soft-demote probe and preemptive spill orchestration to reduce eviction churn and improve tail latency. Feature is behind a runtime flag and rolled out via canary. Metrics: soft_demote_count, soft_demote_duration_seconds, librarian_coalesce_bytes, spill_token_queue_length. Advisories: monitor soft_demote_duration_seconds and spill_token_queue_length during early rollout.
payload.title: KV: Cache Librarian - soft-demote probe and preemptive spill orchestration

payload.body:
Context: tail-latency spikes in mixed short/long workloads trace back to prefill bursts that saturate kernel queues and then stall decode steps while KV cache warming proceeds. This PR introduces a lightweight "wavefront" prefetch coordination layer and a decode handshake synchronizer so that prefill kernels emit formal readiness signals before occupying decode resources. Goals: reduce tail latency under continuous-batching workloads, avoid long-lived decode kernel starvation, and maintain KV-cache warmup effectiveness.

Design summary: single-threaded coordination object per GPU pool (PrefetchWavefrontCoordinator) that tracks prefill window boundaries and grants time-sliced decode permits. Prefill operations run as usual but enqueue a compact readiness token instead of immediately grabbing decode semaphore; the Synchronizer batches tokens into decode grant frames to enable controlled overlap across prefills. The handshake is non-blocking for short-prefill flows (small contexts) and backpressures large batched prefill work by deferring decode grants. The coordinator is kernel-agnostic and uses existing kernel launch metadata (sequence length distribution and quantized-window hints) to prioritize grant order.

Key changes (high level): added a coordinator abstraction in runtime/scheduler, wire up a CUDA-side signal channel for kernel-to-runtime readiness (low-overhead flag + epoch id), integrate synchronizer into continuous-batching path, and new metrics/tracing points to expose wavefront latency and grant skew. Also added a micro-benchmark to reproduce mixed short/long workload tails.

Behavioral notes: this intentionally reduces instantaneous decode concurrency during heavy prefill spikes but shifts load to staged decode windows to keep average throughput stable while reducing 99.9p latency. KV cache warmup remains effective because prefetch tokens still carry KV warming hints; the coordinator only controls decode start, not KV population.

Testing and validation: unit tests for coordinator state machine and handshake edge cases, e2e bench under lab harness (mixed 8-token and 2048-token requests) showing 22% reduction in 99.9p tail latency and no regression in median throughput. CI: initial lint/build failed due to header ordering; fixed in second commit.

Migration and rollout: feature gated under runtime flag runtime.experimental.wavefront_prefetch (off by default). Suggested canary rollout to Dedicated customers with synthetic traces before broadly enabling on hosted.

Related: ENG-8421 tracks instrumentation additions; ENG-8489 is the incident ticket prompting this work.
Arjun Patel: high-level looks good, but can you explain how this interacts with existing KV soft-evict heuristics? Need to ensure we don't create a steady-state oscillation.
Maya Chen: reply - coordinator only gates decode start; we keep existing soft-evict timers and add a grace window so the eviction heuristics see continuous warming signals. Added tests to validate no oscillation under synthetic traces.
Lena Ortiz: requested change - move metric tag from 'pool' to 'gpu_pool' to align with dashboards
Maya Chen: addressed - updated metrics and dashboards references in commit f7e2b11
Tomás Rivera: approval - saw perf runs and unit tests; please add a short note to the runbook describing the toggle and how to interpret grant skew metrics before rollout.
payload.title: Prefetch wavefront and decode handshake synchronizer

payload.body:
Motivation: kernel auto-selection v2 performs well when the request regime is stable (e.g., mostly short prompts or mostly long-context), but we saw tail-latency spikes and kernel thrash on mixed workloads where the instantaneous request length differs from the steady-state mix for a route/pool. The scheduler already maintains rolling aggregates for seq-length regimes for batching decisions; this PR threads a quantized, low-cardinality "seq distribution hint" from the scheduler into the selector so the selector can make a more stable choice for the *current pool/route mix* rather than overfitting to single-request length.

What changed: 1) Add a lightweight WorkloadSeqHint struct to the scheduler execution context, derived from the scheduler’s existing rolling window stats (prefill tokens, decode tokens, and long-context rate). 2) Quantize/clip the hint into stable buckets (to preserve determinism within a given hint input and avoid metric cardinality blowups). 3) Pass the hint through the runtime request context to the kernel selector interface. 4) Update selector scoring/rules to optionally consult the hint (behind the existing kernel selection v2 feature gate + new sub-flag `selector.use_seq_distribution_hint`). 5) Emit the hint buckets in selection telemetry/debug dumps so perf triage can reproduce decisions.

Hint details: - `prefill_bucket`: {S, M, L, XL} based on p90 prefill tokens in the rolling window (default window 60s, min samples 200). - `decode_bucket`: {S, M, L} based on p90 expected decode tokens. - `long_context_rate_bucket`: {LOW, MED, HIGH} based on fraction of requests with prefill > long_context_threshold. - `mixedness_bucket`: {LOW, HIGH} computed from entropy across seq buckets. The selector only uses the hint when `hint_freshness_sec <= 90` and `min_samples` satisfied; otherwise it falls back to per-request signals only.

Safety/determinism: The selector remains deterministic given identical inputs (model tags, gpu sku, seq bucket, and hint buckets). We intentionally quantize hints to keep decisions stable and replayable. The hint is included in selection trace dumps and structured telemetry, and can be disabled per env/region/model via config. No change when kernel selection v2 is disabled.

Perf expectations: For mixed workloads, we expect fewer oscillations between prefill-optimized vs decode-optimized kernels and improved p99 stability (especially on long-context-heavy routes with intermittent short requests). Micro-overhead is negligible (scheduler already computes aggregates; we only bucketize and copy a small struct).

Testing: Added unit tests for bucketing, freshness gating, and selector behavior with/without hints. Added a scheduler integration test that simulates a mixed regime and asserts stable kernel choice across a sequence of requests. CI includes a small synthetic benchmark that validates no regression in selector eval time.

Rollout: Behind feature gate; default OFF for all envs. Intended to be enabled in Hosted canary first for a small allowlist once dashboards confirm selection distribution stability.

Refs: kernel selection v2 epic ENG-4821; prior seq bucketing work in PR #28439; telemetry work in PR #28466.
Yuki Sato (review): Interface change looks fine, but please confirm we’re not increasing selector key cardinality in caches/metrics. Also: should hint be part of the selection cache key or only used during scoring?
Sofia Ivanova (author): Good call. Hint is NOT included in the persistent compilation cache key. It only affects selector decision among already-available candidates. For telemetry, we only emit bucket enums (no raw token counts). I also added an explicit comment in selector_v2.cc and a unit test asserting we never add raw counts to labels.
Noah Patel (review): Concern about determinism guarantees: if the hint changes over time, the same request could select a different kernel depending on recent traffic. That’s acceptable for “policy” behavior but we must ensure replayability and clear guardrails. Can you add (1) explicit freshness gating and (2) make sure the hint is dumped in the selection trace so incident triage can reproduce?
Sofia Ivanova (author): Agreed. Added `hint_freshness_sec <= 90` gating and `min_samples` gating. Also updated the selection dump (`--dump_kernel_selection`) to include the 4 hint buckets + freshness so oncall can replay with `--force_seq_hint_buckets=...` (flag added in follow-up commit).
Lena Fischer (review): Bucket thresholds: XL prefill starts at 8192 tokens in this PR; our long-context regressions were already starting around 6k on some models. Can we align with the long-context threshold used elsewhere and ensure it’s configurable?
Sofia Ivanova (author): Updated thresholds: L=4096–8191, XL>=8192 remains, but `long_context_threshold` is now read from existing runtime config (defaults to 6144). long_context_rate_bucket uses that threshold. Added docs + a test for config override.
Omar El-Sayed (review): Telemetry: please verify we don’t blow up event size. Also, avoid adding the hint as a string field; keep it numeric enums. Any additional sampling?
Sofia Ivanova (author): Kept it as fixed enums in the proto (4 fields, each uint32 enum). No extra sampling; payload increase is ~8 bytes. Added a note in the PR description and in telemetry emitter code about cardinality and size.
Marcus Reed (review): The mixed-workload integration test is good but currently uses a 10s rolling window; prod is 60s. Can we match prod to avoid overfitting test behavior?
Sofia Ivanova (author): Updated test window to 60s and adjusted synthetic traffic generator to hit `min_samples` quickly (by simulating timestamps). Now it matches prod defaults while staying fast (<300ms).
Buildkite (bot): perf-smoke-selector-overhead failed: flaky timing threshold exceeded by 3.2%.
Sofia Ivanova (author): Reran; passes. I also relaxed the threshold to 10% with a median-of-5 measurement to reduce flake while still catching real regressions.
Noah Patel (review): Approved with the added gating + dump fields. Please ensure default remains OFF.
Yuki Sato (review): Approved. Thanks for keeping hints bucketed and low-cardinality.
payload.title: Scheduler: pass seq-length distribution hints into kernel selector (mixed workload stability)

payload.body:
Motivation: Several customers and the compliance team requested clearer controls on cryptographic operations (KMS calls) per tenant to cap noisy tenants and provide predictable billing. We also need a safe way to delegate short-lived RBAC v2 privileges to service identities used by 3rd party integrators, and to reduce high-cardinality audit log volume for high-throughput tenants while retaining attestation guarantees.

This PR implements three coordinated features: tenant-scoped key-usage quotas (soft throttles + hard caps), RBAC v2 delegation tokens (auditable, short TTL, scope-limited), and an adaptive audit-sampling pipeline (policy-driven sampling with deterministic attestation tags so sampled events can still be reconstituted for compliance).

What changed (high level):
- pkg/kms/quota: quota engine, tenant counters, integration points with the KMS proxy to enforce soft/hard limits and emit quota metrics. Quotas are configurable per-tenant via the console or infra config; overrides for dedicated/private customers are supported.
- services/rbac/delegation: new delegation token issuer, API surface for requesting delegated scopes, token revocation hooks, and integration with the policy evaluator. Delegation tokens are signed, include a tenant and scope claim, and are enforced by cluster gateways.
- observability/audit-sampler: adaptive sampling controller that runs alongside the audit forwarder. Policies can express deterministic sampling keys (e.g., request_id mod N) and preserve attestation headers so sampled traces are linkable to unsampled aggregates. Includes retention/rehydration markers for on-demand full replays.
- console: admin UI additions to configure tenant KMS quotas and delegation token lifetime.
- tests: unit + e2e tests covering quota enforcement under bursty load, delegation token authorization matrices, and sampling correctness with deterministic keys.

Design notes: quotas use a leaky-bucket approximation with configurable burst allowance and a hard enforcement path that returns a 429-like KMS policy error (mapped to our API error model). Delegation tokens are implemented as signed JWT-like envelopes with a signed key id and revocation list; we introduced a small CRDT-backed revocation cache replicated to gateways for low-latency checks. Audit sampling is pluggable and deterministic: the same request will always be sampled the same way given the policy, which keeps compliance proofs reproducible.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind a console flag + feature toggle. Initial rollout will be opt-in for a set of pilot tenants. We will enable metrics and set alerts on quota rejects, delegation token failures, and audit-sampler coverage drift.

Risk and mitigations:
- False positives on hard quotas: we added a 24-hour grace window and telemetry to quickly revert to soft-only behavior.
- Delegation token leakage: tokens are short-lived (default 5m) and scope-restricted. Revocation path added.
- Sampling losing required evidence: deterministic sampling keys + rehydration markers ensure we can reconstruct sampled events for an incident.

Related work: references SUP-9443 (support ticket), ENG-1218 (quota engine backlog), ENG-1229 (delegation token spec).

Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests in perf harness, [x] docs in security/README updated, [x] console feature toggles, [x] release notes

Omar Patel: Please add a safety toggle so we can flip quotas to soft-only quickly during rollout — addressed in engine.go by a feature gate (LEAH)
Sofia Kuznetsova: Need stronger unit tests around revocation cache cold-start — added a cache-warmup e2e and a retry path (LEAH)
Marcus Lee: CI flake on linux-amd64 integration; root cause was a time-dependent test, fixed by using a clock stub
Infra (automated): load-test job showed quota enforcement holds at 50k ops/s in perf lab, spikes degrade gracefully
Add tenant-scoped KMS usage quotas (soft/hard), RBAC v2 delegation tokens for service integration, and an adaptive deterministic audit-sampling pipeline. Feature is behind admin feature flag; pilot rollout recommended.
payload.title: Introduce tenant key-usage quotas, RBAC v2 delegation tokens, and adaptive audit-sampling

payload.body:
Background: customers observed rare but recurring corrupt JSON payloads when SSE stream fragments split inside complex nested JSON (tool calls / structured output). This manifested as mid-JSON truncation and downstream consumer errors (most commonly with OpenAI-compatible SDKs). Motivation: improve resilience of the stream adapter without changing wire protocol or breaking existing clients. This PR introduces two complementary changes: 1) an SSE chunk acknowledger (lightweight per-connection monotonic ack window) that lets the server detect and heal missing or reordered chunk deliveries during transient backpressure and reconnection; 2) a mid-JSON detection probe that heuristically detects likely-incomplete JSON spans inside SSE chunk boundaries and triggers safe flush/repair semantics for the OpenAI compatibility layer. Key points: - Non-breaking: no client-visible protocol changes. Chunk acknowledger attaches a small opt-in header on server->adapter control frames; adapters that don't understand the header ignore it. - Safety-first: the mid-JSON probe is conservative: it only triggers repair when braces/quotes/commas indicate a high-certainty mid-object cut and when the last N bytes fall on a non-UTF8 boundary or an unbalanced JSON token. - Toolcall ordering: added explicit handoff ordering enforcement between the stream parser and function-call bridge to avoid toolcall interleaving when a mid-JSON resync occurs. Implementation summary: - streaming/sse/acknowledger.go: new component that tracks send sequence and a sliding ack window. Implemented lock-free fast-path and a bounded slow-path to avoid head-of-line blocking. - streaming/sse/parser.rs: extended parser state machine with a MidJsonProbe state; probe scans for unbalanced braces, unterminated strings, and common toolcall sentinel patterns. - openai_compat/stream_adapter.py: integrates the acknowledger control frames and adds a repair handler that emits a safe checkpoint token and attempts to replay small last-N buffers before failing the connection. - streaming/tests/test_mid_json_probe.py and streaming/tests/test_toolcall_ordering.py: broad unit + property tests that exercise corner cases (nested arrays, escaped quotes, multi-byte UTF-8 split across chunks). - docs/compat/streaming.md: documented the heuristics, opt-in header name, and rollout notes for customers running private deployments. Test & validation: - Unit tests: added 28 tests; all pass locally. - Integration: e2e streaming test harness validated recovery across simulated packet drops and reconnections (50k simulated streams). - Load: microbenchmarks show <2% median tail latency impact under typical payload distributions; worst-case repair path triggers extra round-trips as expected. Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind runtime flag 'sse_midjson_probe' default=true for hosted; for private deployments flag off by default and added runtime knob in the console. - Canary on dedicated pools for 72 hours, monitor JSON error rate / fncall ordering regressions, then wide rollout. Backout: runtime flag and adapter simply disabled if a regression appears. Related: addresses customer reports summarized in SUP-504 and ties to ENG-2241 (streaming stability epic).
Leah Kim (reviewer) - Please add a short rationale in the docs explaining why the probe is conservative and how it avoids false positives. Also add a note to the upgrade doc for private installs.
Aisha Patel (author) - Added docs/compat/streaming.md section 'Conservative probe heuristics' and upgrade note. PTAL.
Diego Morales (reviewer) - The ack window looks good; can you explain the choice of window size and how it behaves under long-lived idle connections? Concern: memory growth.
Aisha Patel (author) - Ack window uses a bounded ring buffer (default 256 entries) and expires entries after 5 minutes of inactivity. Added comments and a microbenchmark in streaming/benchmarks/README.md.
Ethan Zhao (reviewer) - Tests are comprehensive but we still need a deterministic reproduction of the toolcall-ordering bug. Can you add a regression test that simulates mid-JSON cut during a function call that contains JSON in the args?
Aisha Patel (author) - Added streaming/tests/test_toolcall_ordering.py which includes a deterministic replay harness that produced the original failure; test now passes.
Leah Kim (reviewer) - CI flaky on integration initially but green after rerun. LGTM after fixes and test additions.
Leah Kim (maintainer) - Squash-merged by Leah Kim on 2026-02-18. Release note: streaming: introduce SSE chunk acknowledger and mid-JSON probe to reduce partial JSON errors in streamed OpenAI-compatible responses.
Introduce a conservative mid-JSON detection probe and an SSE chunk acknowledger to reduce occurrences of partial JSON and out-of-order toolcall emissions in streaming responses. No protocol breaking changes. Feature is runtime-gated and can be toggled per deployment.
Enable 'sse_midjson_probe' on a small canary pool first. Watch metrics: streaming.json_parse_errors, streaming.toolcall_order_mismatches, streaming.repair_invocations. If repair_invocations spike unexpectedly, toggle off and collect logs (streaming/repair/*.log) for root cause analysis.
Risk: conservative heuristics may under-capture some mid-JSON cases; mitigation: probe is opt-out for private customers and can be tuned. Risk: increased tail latency on repair path; mitigation: repair is limited to small replay window and work is instrumented with detailed metrics.
payload.title: Introduce SSE chunk acknowledger and mid-JSON detection probe to improve streaming stability

payload.body:
Motivation: Customers and internal compliance teams asked for a lightweight way to (1) attach an executable runbook identifier to anomalous audit entries, (2) help security engineers author RBAC v2 policies with suggestions and examples, and (3) route KMS requests to an escrow provider when geographic residency constraints prevent the primary KMS from being used. This change bundles three coordinated pieces: runbook hooks, RBAC hinting, and a KMS escrow router.

Design summary: - Runbook hooks: a new internal/compliance/runbook_hooks.go subsystem that consumes decision traces from the policy engine and appends a structured runbook_id and playbook metadata to audit envelopes when configured. Hooks are pluggable and emit a compact JSON blob to the audit pipeline so downstream incident systems can open the correct runbook automatically.
- RBAC v2 policy hinting: a small suggestion engine (internal/rbac/hint_generator.go) that scans policy attempts and provides template suggestions surfaced in the Console (console/frontend/src/rbac/PolicyHintPanel.tsx). Hints are generated server-side and cached TTL=5m; the Console shows contextual examples and one-click apply to a draft policy.
- KMS escrow router: pkg/kms/escrow_router.go implements a routing policy that selects an escrow KMS endpoint when residency or CMK location constraints are detected. The router performs a fast residency-check lookup (with a 100ms cache) and emits an audit tag kms.escrow_used=true when escrowing occurs. The router is pluggable and guarded by feature flag `feature.kms.escrow_routing`.

Configuration & rollout: - Both runbook hooks and KMS escrow routing are behind feature flags: feature.compliance.runbook_hooks and feature.kms.escrow_routing. By default flags are disabled for all tenants; platform operators can enable per-tenant via the Console and Helm values (deploy/helm/values-compliance.yaml). RBAC hinting is enabled in beta for internal orgs only.
- Migration plan: No schema migration required. Audit envelopes get a new optional field `runbook_id` and `runbook_meta` when the hook is enabled; consumers ignoring unknown fields will be unaffected. The KMS router adds an audit tag but does not change encryption contexts.

Backwards compatibility and safety: - All additions are additive to audit envelopes. - KMS escrow routing uses a safe-fallback: if the escrow endpoint is unreachable, the router falls back to the primary KMS and emits a warning metric and audit entry. Operators can enable strict-escrow mode to enforce hard-fail behavior (not default).

Summary: Adds an OPA-backed in-process RBAC decision cache to reduce repeated policy evaluation latency, a KMS geo-fallback proxy to gracefully route key operations to a secondary provider when region pinned providers are unavailable, and an audit-stitcher service that coalesces audit fragments from edge proxies into canonical, signed records. Motivation: We saw customer reports of elevated p99 auth latency and occasional KMS outages causing failed operator flows (Linear ENG-9142). This change reduces policy eval overhead, improves KMS resilience for region-pinned tenants, and makes audit trails more robust for downstream compliance pipelines. Design notes: 1) RBAC cache: an LRU with TTL keyed by (service, resource, action, flattened-claims-hash). Policy decisions are still authoritative from OPA but cache hits short-circuit RPCs; TTL is configurable per-tenant and honors explicit policy TTLs from the policy metadata. 2) KMS geo-fallback proxy: a sidecar/edge proxy that prefers tenant-bound KMS providers but can failover to a configured fallback provider (with explicit tenant consent flag). Failover is rate-limited and recorded in audit events. 3) Audit stitcher: receives audit fragments (signed) from regional proxies, deduplicates, orders by event-time, signs a canonical envelope, and forwards to the audit-ingest pipeline with provenance headers. Compatibility/rollout: defaults are conservative — cache is disabled for tenants with 'policy-cache: disabled' claim and KMS fallback is opt-in via tenant flag. We will roll out in stages: alpha (internal), beta (select tenants), global. Checklist: - [x] RFC and design reviewed by SEC and SRE - [x] OPA integration tests added - [x] KMS fallback simulation harness - [x] End-to-end audit stitcher verification with sample tenants - [x] Added feature flags and per-tenant toggles - [x] Updated docs (console + API) Testing: unit tests for cache correctness and eviction, integration tests against a mocked OPA and dual-KMS setup, chaos test that simulates regional KMS outage and verifies fallback telemetry. Observability: new metrics rbac.cache.hits, rbac.cache.misses, kms.fallback.count, audit.stitcher.latency. Security considerations: fallback only invoked if tenant config allows; all fallback KMS operations are tagged and require justification in the audit envelope. Data residency: audit-stitcher marks provenance and keeps 'origin-region' tag; fallback KMS operations include an explicit residency-consent header so downstream detection can enforce export rules. Migration/rollback plan: feature flags allow immediate disable; cache can be flushed cluster-wide and OPA traffic will revert to baseline. Notes on performance: synthetic load tests show ~12% reduction in policy-decision p99 and 18% reduction in mean end-to-end auth latency for CPU-bound operator flows; cache adds ~3% CPU overhead to the operator-auth service under steady state. Follow-ups: - a follow-up PR will add a policy TTL reconciliation job to surface stale policy TTLs - console UI will surface per-tenant cache metrics - extend audit-stitcher to attach KMS usage proofs for high-sensitivity tenants
Evan Liu: Can we document how cache invalidation behaves when policies change? Also request adding a metric for cache.evictions.
Priya Rao: Reply: added policy TTL and a policy-watch invalidation hook; metric rbac.cache.evictions included in metrics_defs.go.
Grace Kim: Security question: ensure KMS fallback cannot be used to exfiltrate region-locked keys. Please add tenant-level consent enforcement and audit justification.
Priya Rao: Reply: fallback requires tenant consent flag; we also add residency-consent header in the audit envelope and log an explicit justification entry. Added unit tests for enforcement.
Omar Alvarez: Perf: what is the CPU/latency trade-off? Can we limit cache size per-tenant?
Priya Rao: Reply: added per-tenant max_entries config and conservative defaults; included benchmark results in the PR description.
Grace Kim: Approve after tests and doc updates.
payload.title: Implement OPA-backed RBAC cache, KMS geo-fallback proxy and audit stitcher

Adds a HaltPointController that coordinates AB experiments with shadow-drain safety gates and automatic rollback triggers. Backwards-compatible; requires CRD install and a short console feature flag rollout.
Summary: Introduces a HaltPointController that provides explicit halt points in staged rollouts (canaries, A/B lanes, and shadow captures). The controller coordinates traffic draining for shadow lanes and enforces safety gates before promoting variants. Motivation: Several incidents (see SUP-4421) showed that implicit shadow drains combined with delayed telemetry can cause stale sessions and spurious successes—this PR implements explicit checkpoints and an automated rollback advisor to reduce blast radius and make promotes deterministic.

What this PR does: - CRD: haltpoint.redwood.ai/v1 (HaltPoint) to declare checkpoints, metrics anchors, and drain windows. - Controller: src/controller/haltpoint_controller.go implements reconcile loop, cohort-aware session fencing, and a traffic-drain state machine (Active -> Draining -> Quarantine -> Promoted/Aborted). - Traffic integration: pkg/rollout/traffic_splitter.go extended with a DrainHint protocol used by the routing layer to steer shadow and canary traffic during halt windows. - Safety gates: configurable SLO gates (latency percentile, error-rate, and quality regression) and a TTL-based quarantine where traffic is forced back to stable if metrics stop reporting. - Rollback advisor: a heuristic engine that scores signal divergence and recommends an automatic abort when score exceeds threshold; outputs annotated events to audit log for human review. - Tests: integrated canary simulation harness (tests/integration/haltpoint_sim_test.go) plus unit coverage for session fencing and drain transitions. - Console: adds a HaltPoint panel to the Rollouts UI (console/ui/rollouts/haltpoint-panel.tsx) that exposes live state, metric anchors, and a one-click abort/pause action.

Backwards compatibility & rollout plan: The controller is fully additive. To enable, operators must apply the CRD and a short feature-flag flip in Console (controlled rollout across accounts). We plan a staged rollout: internal canaries -> a small set of customer accounts -> global. Follow-up (small) PR will add RBAC scopes to Dedicated manifests.

Checklist: - [x] CRD schema and validation - [x] Controller reconcile and unit tests - [x] Integration simulation harness - [x] Console UI panel + telemetry endpoints - [x] Documentation: docs/operations/haltpoint-playbook.md - [x] Runbook and playbook linked to SU P-4421

Operational notes: The HaltPoint CRD allows short-circuiting promotes in case of missing telemetry (safety TTL). DrainHint is intentionally lightweight (header + routing annotation) so it can be applied to both hosted and private deployments. The Rollback Advisor emits a detailed event (reason, metrics snapshot, score) to make automated aborts auditable.

Example HaltPoint YAML (CRD usage): `apiVersion: haltpoint.redwood.ai/v1
kind: HaltPoint
metadata:
  name: canary-halt-2026-02
spec:
  targetVariant: v2
  cohortSelector: "region=eu,plan=premium"
  gates:
    latencyP95Ms: 220
    errorRatePct: 0.5
  drainWindowSeconds: 30
  quarantineTTLSeconds: 60
  rollbackScoreThreshold: 0.75`

Why this is different from other rollout controllers: HaltPoint makes the checkpoint first-class: it couples an explicit drain lifecycle with session-fencing semantics and a TTL for missing telemetry rather than silently proceeding. This reduces time-to-detect regressions for low-traffic cohorts and makes automated aborts explainable in audit logs.

Open follow-ups: - RBAC for Dedicated (small manifest change) - Add metric decay model to reduce sensitivity on sparse cohorts - UX: compact timeline widget for multi-haltpoint rollouts

Liam O'Connor (2026-02-14): Please expand on how the quota/quarantine TTL interacts with missing telemetry. Is there a default decay model?
Maya Chen (2026-02-14): Good question — we added a quarantineTTLSeconds field and the controller treats missing metrics as decayed after TTL; follow-up will add a decay curve. Documented in playbook.
Priya Nair (2026-02-17): Race looks possible during rapid promote->abort flips; can you add a linearizable locking step?
Maya Chen (2026-02-18): Added a lightweight session fence (compare-and-tag) in h8e0b11 and added a unit test that reproduces the window.
Diego Alvarez (2026-02-20): Integration sim flaked on CI with timing; tuned timeouts and added deterministic seed for sim. CI re-run passed.
Liam O'Connor (2026-02-23): Approved — leaving a note to product to review the console wording for the abort CTA.
Priya Nair (2026-02-24): LGTM. Comment: suggest follow-up to add RBAC to Dedicated manifests (don't block).

payload.body:
Motivation: We observed intermittent OOM and large memory spikes on hosts running heavy chat workloads with long contexts. Root cause was aggressive synchronous eviction + arena fragmentation when large KV entries were repeatedly allocated/evicted in short windows. This PR introduces two complementary mitigations: 1) eviction throttling to limit concurrent synchronous evictions that can block inference threads and cause head-of-line blocking, and 2) background heap defragmentation (arena compaction) that reclaims free fragments without affecting hot-path token decode.

Design summary: Eviction throttling: add a token-aware throttler that enforces a per-GPU soft-concurrency limit for synchronous evictions. When the soft limit is reached, eviction requests are enqueued and served by a small eviction worker pool. We expose a soft_limit and burst_limit and a configurable policy (priority=age/size). Eviction work is measured in bytes evicted, not number of entries, to better reflect memory cost.

Background defragmentation: introduce defrag_worker that runs asynchronously and performs per-arena compaction during low-util windows. It coalesces small free blocks into larger contiguous free spans so future large KV items don't trigger spill/pager allocations. Compaction is incremental with tunable batch_size and a max_io_budget to avoid interfering with streaming.

Scheduler integration: scheduler now signals backpressure when async eviction queue length exceeds a threshold; this causes temporary throttling of batch sizes for new requests to avoid creating more eviction pressure. Continuous batching path was adjusted to prefer prefetched KV entries and to avoid inflating batch size when eviction backlog exists.

Implementation details: key changes in runtime/kv_cache: - allocator.rs: introduced EvictThrottler with metrics and tunables; made free/alloc paths non-blocking where possible. - eviction.rs: eviction now returns an EvictionHandle that may be executed synchronously or queued. - defrag_worker.rs: incremental compactor that walks arenas using conservative heuristics to avoid touching hot KV entries. - scheduler/slot_allocator.rs: added hook to query eviction queue length and apply temporary batch size backoff. - telemetry: new metrics kv.eviction.queue_length, kv.defrag.cycles, kv.eviction.throttled_count.

Testing and validation: unit tests cover correctness of eviction bookkeeping and handle lifecycle. Integration tests (tests/kv_cache/eviction_harness.py) reproduce fragmentation pattern from ENG-4312 and assert memory usage stabilizes under load. Perf lab runs (perf/bench_eviction.py) show reduction in 99.9th percentile memory spike and a small (1-3ms) tail latency improvement on p3-like nodes due to reduced head-of-line blocking.

Rollback plan: all new features are behind runtime.flags.kv_eviction_throttle && runtime.flags.kv_defrag_enabled. Rolling back is a config flip; merge will leave flags default-on for main but ops can disable via runtime config.

Notes: this PR intentionally avoids introducing on-disk paging by default; spill-to-disk remains opt-in for private deployments and gated behind runtime.flags.kv_spill_to_disk.

Reduced KV cache OOM spikes by adding eviction throttling and background defragmentation. Default behavior is non-breaking; tunables exposed under runtime.config.kv_cache.*.
Ethan Browne (2026-02-15): Can you clarify the decision to measure eviction budget in bytes vs entries? Concerned about pathological cases where many small entries overwhelm queue. Response: We measure bytes to reflect real memory cost; added per-entry cost cap and a per-item weight so pathological many-small-entries are gated.
Lia Chen (2026-02-16): Defrag touching arenas worries me for latency sensitive tails. Did you add heuristics to avoid hot entries? Response: Yes — defrag skips arenas with recent access hotness above threshold and uses max_io_budget per cycle. We also added an opt-out flag for single-tenant machines.
Samir Gupta (2026-02-17): Integration tests flaky on aarch64 CI run. Request: add a short jitter to eviction worker to avoid contention. Response: Added randomized backoff and increased test timeouts. Re-ran CI.
Ethan Browne (2026-02-18): LGTM after tests pass. Approved.
Lab perf: baseline spike scenario (long chat workloads) showed peak RSS spikes of ~9.6GB -> after patch steady peaks ~7.2GB (25% reduction). 99th token latency reduced 1.8ms on average; 99.9th latency reduced 4.6ms. Eviction-related IO/CPU overhead below 2% in steady-state. Memory fragmentation measured at arena-level reduced from estimated 18% lost bytes to ~5% on synthetic churn workload.
payload.title: kv: eviction throttling and heap defragmentation to stabilize KV cache memory pressure
