Context: Customers observed malformed JSON in streaming OpenAI-compatible endpoints when server-side heartbeats interleaved with data frames and when UTF-8 escape sequences were split across chunk boundaries. This caused partial-object emissions, duplicate delimiters, and out-of-order function-call sentinels under load. This PR introduces a resilient reassembly state machine, a heartbeat coalescer that marks and defers delimiter emission while preserving token order, and an escape-boundary normalizer that rewrites split UTF-8/JSON escapes before attempting JSON incremental parse. Work done: - Implement sse/reassembly.go: compact state machine with seq-window, acked-offsets, and a soft-resume path for truncated frames. - Add heartbeat_coalescer in runtime/streaming: buffers interleaved "ping" events and merges adjacent delimiter tokens into a single canonical delimiter upon flush. - Introduce escape_normalizer in compat/openai_stream.go: maintains a two-byte lookbehind to fix split "\u" and multibyte UTF-8 escapes at chunk edges. - Tests: new unit and integration coverage under tests/sse_reassembly_test.go and tests/stream_chaos_integration.yaml (simulated TCP stalls, heartbeat bursts, partial writes). - Docs: note in docs/streaming.md about reassembly guarantees and developer-visible delimiters. Checklist: - [x] Core reassembly state machine implemented - [x] Heartbeat coalescing and canonical delimiter rewriting - [x] Escape normalization with minimal copying - [x] Regression tests for partial JSON, duplicate delimiters, function-call sentinel ordering - [x] E2E chaos test reproducing customer symptom - [x] Benchmarked impact: ~+2% CPU at peak under synthetic load. Commits summary: 5 commits (split tasks): 1) reassembly model + tests, 2) heartbeat coalescer, 3) escape normalizer + compat hooks, 4) integration tests and benchmarks, 5) docs and changelog. Files changed (high-level): - sse/reassembly.go: new - runtime/streaming/heartbeat_coalescer.go: new - compat/openai_stream.go: changes to streaming handler and resync points - tests/sse_reassembly_test.go: new - tests/stream_chaos_integration.yaml: new - docs/streaming.md: updated - pkg/tracing/stream_span.go: minor instrumentation - Makefile/CICD: add chaos job The fix is intentionally conservative: when the reassembly state detects an irrecoverable mid-object loss we emit an explicit <REPAIR> marker event (consumers can interpret this) and request client-level retry semantics; we avoid silent object truncation. Review timeline: - Initial draft posted 2026-02-14 - First pass review requested changes around lock contention and memory copies (LM); author reduced allocations by using a ring buffer. - Second pass asked for clearer sentinel ordering guarantees; added unit test for function-call sentinel ordering under interleaved heartbeats (ZM). - CI initially failed lint on import ordering; fixed. CI: 12 checks (unit, integration, lint, go vet, typescript build), final status: all passing. Merge: Squash-merged on 2026-02-28 after approvals and green CI. Notes for consumers: This patch tightens stream semantics: - Delimiters are now canonical on emission; mid-stream duplicate delimiters will be squashed. - Small chance of +2% CPU under pathological heartbeat rates; recommend enabling coalescer only for endpoints with heartbeat use via config flag streaming.heartbeat_coalesce=true. Backcompat: non-breaking for protocol consumers; but consumers relying on duplicate delimiter semantics should be updated. Related: ENG-4218 (customer incident), ENG-4301 (runtime reassembly agenda).
Liam Patel: Please ensure the lock in reassembly.go doesn't add contention under high parallelism; can we use CAS? (request changes)
Maya Chen: Reworked to use lock-free ring for the hot path; added benchmarks showing negligible contention.
Zoe Martínez: Add explicit test for function-call sentinel ordering when heartbeat arrives between tokens. (approved after test added)
Aaron Goldberg: CI flake on integration: reran infra job and it passed; looks good to me.
Fix streaming JSON truncation and delimiter duplication: resilient SSE reassembly, heartbeat coalescing, and escape normalization. Improves OpenAI-compatible streaming stability under interleaved heartbeats; enable via streaming.heartbeat_coalesce=true if desired.
payload.title: Stabilize SSE: recover interleaved heartbeats, prevent duplicate delimiters, and normalize escaped JSON boundaries

Problem: presubmit lanes frequently exceed acceptable feedback windows (lint steps commonly > 90s on large changes) and dependency churn results in stacked noisy PRs. Goal: reduce presubmit tail latency without sacrificing coverage and introduce a low-risk automated dev-dep rotator to keep devDependencies from stalling. This PR implements a constraint-aware lint scheduler (lint-slo-enforcer) that assigns lint tasks into SLO buckets and dynamically parallelizes heavy linters while honoring runner budgets, plus a minimal dep-rotator tool that creates batched PRs updating devDeps on a weekly cadence. Key changes: 1) new scheduler: internal/ci/lint_scheduler.go + entrypoint ci/scripts/lint-slo-runner.sh that reads presubmit annotations (presubmit-weight:S, M, L) and routes files to tuned containers; 2) split lint workflow: .github/workflows/lint-slo.yml—introduces short/medium/long lanes with fastfast failover and incremental cache priming; 3) dep-rotator: tools/dep-rotator/* (Go binary) that samples package.json/yarn.lock, proposes minimal updates, runs tests in ephemeral job, and opens a curated PR with changelog; 4) lightweight toolchain refactor: ci/toolchain/bootstrap.go to make presubmit images smaller and cacheable; 5) release automation tweak: release/actions/prepare_release.sh fixes a path regression observed in recent release runs. Migration plan: feature branch staged to canary org, enabled for 25% of repos via org-level flag for 48 hours, then ramp to 100% if canary metrics meet SLOs. Rollout checklist: - [x] Unit tests for scheduler logic - [x] Integration smoke runner for dep-rotator - [x] Canary traffic gating implemented - [x] Doc updates in docs/ci/presubmit.md - [x] Linear tickets linked (ENG-2319, ENG-2401) Backwards compatibility: default presubmit behavior unchanged when presubmit-weight absent; dep-rotator only opens PRs to the dev branch with opt-out label. Observability: added metrics lint_scheduler.bucket_latency, lint_scheduler.queue_depth and dep_rotator.prs_opened. Example usage: ci/scripts/lint-slo-runner.sh --files changed_files.txt --slo M. Motivation: reduces developer wait time and triage load from dependency noise while keeping updates safe and reviewable.
Reviewer Marcus: 'Can we quantify expected median improvement and add a flag to disable dynamic parallelization for low-tier repos?' Author (Avery): 'Added metrics and a feature flag (ci.flags.lint_dynamic_parallellism) in config; default is on for canary only.' Reviewer Sofia: 'Dep-rotator should not open large PRs that break bisectability.' Author: 'Dep-rotator now batches up to 5 devDeps per PR and runs integration smoke; added opt-out label ci/no-rotator.' Jordan: 'Please add an entry to the incident runbook if the release script change regresses.' Author: 'Added docs/ci/release-runbook.md and test entry to release pipeline.' Approvals: Marcus approved, Sofia requested one minor test change which was addressed and re-approved, Jordan approved. Final: 3 approvals.
Add constraint-aware lint scheduler to presubmit pipelines to reduce tail latency; introduce a low-risk dev-dependency rotator that opens curated PRs weekly; smaller toolchain images for faster presubmit startup; release automation path fix. No runtime breaking changes. Monitoring: lint_scheduler.* metrics added.

Motivation: We have recurring postmortems where partial streaming failures or dropped tool executions were difficult to correlate to the originating HTTP request because trace context or any stable correlation id was not consistently carried onto the tool/function execution path or into per-route metrics. This PR introduces a small, backwards-compatible observability surface that makes end-to-end correlation and per-route attribution easier while keeping the OpenAI-compat API unchanged. Summary of changes: 1) Add a short-lived correlation header X-RW-Corr-ID for every incoming API request. The value is generated once at the HTTP ingress and propagated on internal RPCs and to any tool/function invocations. 2) Ensure W3C traceparent (and optional baggage) is forwarded into function-tool workers where available; when tracing headers are absent we fall back to X-RW-Corr-ID so logs and metrics still join correctly. 3) Tag runtime metrics and JSONL access logs with route_name and model_variant labels (route-level keys) emitted as route.{route_name} and variant.{model_variant} tags to make per-endpoint SLO dashboards work without additional sampling. 4) Harden the streaming handshake: add an idempotent handshake ack path so retries during partial disconnects don't produce duplicate function calls; this is gated behind a feature flag and defaults on. 5) Add end-to-end tests that simulate network/backpressure interruptions and assert correlation id preservation and single tool execution. Checklist: - [x] Generate X-RW-Corr-ID at ingress - [x] Propagate traceparent/baggage when present - [x] Propagate correlation header to tool/function runner invocation layer - [x] Emit route_name and model_variant tags in runtime metrics pipeline - [x] Update JSONL access log format to include corr_id and route tags - [x] Add unit and e2e tests for streaming reconnect and tool-call dedupe - [x] Docs: add observability note to api/observability.md Rollout plan: feature is hidden behind the flag runtime.observability.corr_headers.enabled=true by default in staging. We will enable in 2 phases: enable for internal staging tenants for 48 hours and validate dashboards and error budgets, then enable globally. If we see duplicated tool executions beyond a safe threshold we will flip the handshake ack to off and revert with a toggle (no code rollout required). Backwards compatibility: Public OpenAI-compat API surface unchanged. The new X-RW-Corr-ID is internal-only and does not affect clients unless they observe additional headers in responses (we do not return the header to public responses). Testing notes: added e2e harness tests under telemetry/integration that spin up a mock tool-runner and assert a single execution and preserved corr_id across reconnections. Logs: sample JSONL change: {"timestamp":"...","req_id":"abc","corr_id":"rwd-xyz","route":"chat.completions","model":"gpt-4o-mini","status":"stream-closed"}. Monitoring: dashboards updated to include corr_id cardinality histograms and new per-route latency percentiles. Related: ENG-4821 (streaming resilience), ENG-4990 (tool-call observability).
Propagate a lightweight correlation header to downstream tool/function executions and attach per-route tags to runtime metrics and JSONL access logs. Improves debugability for streaming and tool-invocation failures without changing public API contracts.
Ethan Morales (request changes): The handshake ack looks reasonable but we need stronger invariants around idempotency at the tool-runner boundary. Can you add an explicit dedupe token persisted for the short TTL? Author reply: Added dedupe token store in runner/context.go and unit tests that assert single execution under concurrent reconnects.
Sofia Chen (approved): Verified metrics emission locally; the per-route tag cardinality looks safe for our current routes. Please ensure we don't accidentally tag high-cardinality input fields. Author reply: Confirmed we only tag route_name and model_variant, not user-provided identifiers.
Marco Ruiz (comment): CI flaked once on streaming_integration, reran and passed. Author reply: Added a small backoff to the integration harness to reduce race flakiness.
Squash merged into main by Sofia Chen on 2026-02-10. Merge commit message: "Add correlation header propagation, route tags, and stream handshake dedupe". Rollout started behind feature flag; monitoring alert added to SRE playbook for increased duplicate-exec rate.
Enable behind runtime.observability.corr_headers.enabled=true. No public API changes. Operators should watch duplicated tool_execution_count and corr_id cardinality for anomalies.
payload.title: Resilient stream propagation: inject correlation headers and per-route metadata for function/tool calls

payload.body:
Context: Dedicated fleets need predictable throughput guarantees while allowing short, network-safe bursts for traffic spikes. Current warm-pool semantics are binary (reserved vs ephemeral) and cause either wasted capacity or sudden noisy neighbor effects during bursts. This PR introduces a 'warmup credit exchange' broker and a 'burst cooldown controller' to permit controlled, graceful borrowing of reserved warm slots with automatic reconciliation and telemetry for debugging.

What this change does: Implements a broker that can (a) atomically transfer ephemeral warm credits from a tenant's reserved pool to its burstable allowance, (b) track and ledger transfers with idempotency keys so transfers can be reconciled after partial failures, and (c) support a lease-based model where credits time out if not observed in the runtime within a configurable lease window. Adds a cooldown controller that decays a tenant's burst budget on a configurable window and applies a soft-shed threshold when the tenant's negative balance exceeds a safety margin.

Motivation and tradeoffs: The exchange model favors availability and bounded latency for short spikes at the cost of small temporary overcommit; the cooldown controller prevents oscillation and long-term SLA erosion. We chose lease-based credits (instead of permanent re-reservation) so normal reserved capacity accounting is preserved and failures (eg. node crashes) can be reconciled quickly without manual intervention.

Checklist:
- [x] Broker and controller implementation with unit tests
- [x] E2E test harness for warmup flows simulating prewarm, burst, node eviction
- [x] Telemetry hooks (p50/p95 headroom gauges, credit-transfer counters, failed-reconcile alerts)
- [x] Runbook + operational notes in docs/runbooks/dedicated/warmup_and_burst.md
- [x] Backwards-compatible config (default behavior unchanged unless enabled)

Operational knobs added: warmup_credit_lease_seconds (default 60), burst_cooldown_decay_seconds (default 30, configurable), safety_negative_balance_ratio (default 0.3), enable_credit_exchange (off by default).

Testing notes: e2e harness runs simulated spike workloads and eviction events; CI initially flagged a flaky e2e test (race on credit reconciliation). I added an explicit reconciliation backoff and a deterministic clock in tests; CI green after re-run. Load test against a 200-node dedicated cluster shows 9-13% reduction in p99 token latency during spikes and <2% increase in steady-state reserved utilization for tenants that borrowed credits.

Rollout plan: feature gated via config and cluster-scoped FeatureFlag; opt-in rollout to a subset of dedicated fleets for two weeks, monitor p95/p99 latency and credit_reconcile_failure_count, then widen. Runbook contains rollback steps to revoke warmup leases and disable credit exchange globally.
Priya: Can you clarify the invariants for credit transfer during partial failures?
Noah: Added a section in credit_broker.go comments and a unit test simulating kubelet eviction; the broker rolls back uncommitted transfers and marks ephemeral credits as reclaimable.
Miguel (request changes): The telemetry window uses a 30s decay; please make it configurable and add a lower-bound to avoid oscillation.
Noah: Made decay configurable with a default of 30s and added p50/p95 headroom gauges. Resolved.
Evan (approved): Verified locally with the scale test harness; observed 12% lower tail latency during burst cooling. Approving.
Priya (approved): Reviewed reconciliation logic and runbook; minor nits addressed and approved.
- Introduces the "warmup credit exchange" broker to allow tenants to borrow reserved warm slots for short bursts with automatic reconciliation. - Adds a burst cooldown controller that gradually cools a tenant's burst allowance to avoid oscillation and reactive overprovisioning. - Exposes per-tenant headroom metrics (p50/p95/allocated) and credit flow telemetry for SLO debugging.

Context: We need a deterministic rehearsal path that can run production cohort snapshots against candidate model versions and produce a compact, auditable differential consistency report to drive automated rollback decisions. This PR implements 'Chronos Rehearsal', a coordinated snapshot-replay runner plus a differential consistency check engine.
Goals: 1) enable safe dry-run of model promotes using production traffic snapshots, 2) surface token-level and outcome-level divergences (KL, token-error rate, response-structure drift), 3) produce a single pass/fail signal that can be used by rollout orchestration to auto-backout or escalate to human review.
What changed (summary):
- runtime/rehearsal/runner: new Chronos runner that accepts cohort snapshot manifests, replays requests with preserved timing semantics, and collects deterministic inputs/outputs including KV cache warmup traces
- runtime/rehearsal/diff: differential engine that computes multi-dimensional metrics (KL over token logits, normalized BLEU-like string divergence for short generations, latency distribution shift, structured-output schema mismatches) and combines them into an explainable score
- api/console: new "Rehearsal Runs" page in Console with run timeline, top-k divergence traces, and per-cohort artifact downloads
- api: POST /v1/rehearsals start endpoint + GET status/GET artifacts endpoints
- orchestration: rollout adapter that triggers a Chronos rehearsal as a pre-promote gate; exposes an auto-rollback predicate when weighted-diff-score > threshold or when divergence persists on core metrics
- telemetry: new metrics and histograms: rehearsal.run.duration, rehearsal.diff.score, rehearsal.kv.warmups, rehearsal.token_divergence.p95
- infra: small job spec templates for Dedicated and Private that mount snapshot artifacts and run the runner with safe resource caps
- tests: deterministic integration test harness that replays a fixed 1k-record snapshot and asserts stable diff scores across runs
Why this is safe: rehearsal runs are read-only and run in sandboxed worker pools, snapshots are immutable and sanitized by the snapshot pipeline. The default rollout integration runs Chronos on a small seed cohort (1% traffic equivalent) and requires human opt-in to expand beyond 10% traffic until the score history is clean for 72h.
Rollback logic: the adapter supports three outcomes: pass -> continue, warn -> pause and human review, fail -> immediate reversal of promote and create an incident. The fail predicate is configurable; default uses weighted thresholds: token_divergence.p95 > 0.12 OR KL_avg > 0.25 OR schema_mismatch_rate > 0.02.
Developer checklist:
- [x] unit tests for diff functions
- [x] integration test for runner with small snapshot
- [x] Console UI wired to artifacts
- [x] rollout adapter integration tests
- [x] docs drafted (docs/rehearsal.md)
- [x] e2e smoke on staging CI
Notes about implementation details: Chronos preserves original inter-request spacing up to a configurable scale factor so timing-sensitive models are exercised; KV warming is replayed for session-scoped cohorts to approximate realistic cache states; the diff engine supports pluggable comparators for structured outputs (JSON-LD path checks) and a small scripted verifier for privacy-safe token redaction.
Backwards compatibility and migration: existing rollout policies without a rehearsal step continue to work. The rollout adapter is opt-in via policy field "pre_promote_rehearsal: chronos". For Dedicated/Private customers, the job spec includes a hint to use a local snapshot mount.
Operational considerations: rehearsal artifacts are stored for 30 days by default and can be configured per-org. Rehearsal runs are meterable (tokens+compute) and bill to the customer's reserved pool in Dedicated.
Security: snapshot ingestion pipeline applies PII removal and redaction; worker pools run under a restricted service account.
Related work items: ENG-6789 (rehearsal infra), ENG-6790 (diff comparators), SUP-1023 (customer request to gate promotions).
Rollout plan: feature flagged on main; enable in staging for 2 weeks, run smoke rehearsals on top 5 models, collect baseline diffs, then gradually enable orchestration adapter in production for internal orgs only.
Merge method: squash-merge.
Migration steps for platform operators: run `rehearsalctl migrate-v1` to create default job specs, update rollout policies to reference pre_promote_rehearsal where desired.
"Commit summary" and small snippet: added runner entrypoint and diff lambda; sample adapter config: "pre_promote_rehearsal: { type: 'chronos', seed_fraction: 0.01, auto_rollback: true }".
Ana Morales: Nice isolation model, but can we avoid replaying KV entries that include PII? Please add a toggle to disable KV warmups per org.
Priya Natarajan: Good catch — added sanitization step and org-level kv_warmup_allowed flag; updated docs to call this out.
Kenji Sato: The weighted-diff composite score needs a bit more explanation; request a short section in docs showing how weights map to failure modes.
Priya Natarajan: Added 'diff weight tuning' section in docs/rehearsal.md and added a small example JSON showing thresholds.
Initial CI run failed on flaky integration test; rerun passed after fixture stabilization. All unit tests and linters pass. E2E smoke in staging passed on macrotask instance. Security scan flagged no high-severity issues.
Adds Chronos Rehearsal: a snapshot-driven rehearsal runner and differential consistency checks that can be used as a pre-promote gate. Opt-in rollout adapter and Console UI included. Default safe thresholds and storage policies applied. See docs/rehearsal.md for configuration and operational guidance.
This PR intentionally keeps the rehearsal runner behind a feature flag and opt-in rollout policies to minimize blast radius. We will monitor rehearsal.run.duration and rehearsal.diff.score for the first week after rollout.

Motivation: Presubmit latency and brittle longtests are a recurring drag on developer velocity. The current presubmit harness was a mix of Makefile hooks, repo-specific scripts, and an opinionated husky/git-hooks layer that makes incremental changes and parallelization difficult. This PR replaces the hard-wired presubmit entrypoints with a small pluggable presubmit-prober service, migrates the Python test runner to pytest-xdist for deterministic parallel runs, and introduces a lightweight dep-compatibility checker that runs as a separate CI job to highlight risky upgrades before they hit main.

What changed (high level): - New ci/presubmit-prober: a Go-based binary + action that enumerates configured presubmit plugins per repo, runs them in a sandboxed, timeout-aware fashion, and reports structured results to GitHub checks. - Reworked python test matrix to use pytest + pytest-xdist (2 workers default on CI, configurable) and unified conftest helpers so tests are stable under parallelization. - Bumped pytest from 6.2.x to 7.3.x; upgraded pytest-asyncio and testfixtures to compatible versions. - Updated node test dependencies (jest 28.x -> 29.x, added jest-worker config) and migrated a small number of fragile tests to use jest.runInBand where they rely on process-global state. - Added ci/tools/dep-compat-checker (node script) that runs npm/yarn resolution against a set of representative lockfiles and reports semver-incompatible transitive updates. - Replaced legacy pre-commit hooks in .husky with a thin gateway to the presubmit-prober to keep dev experience minimal.

Checklist: [x] Add pluggable prober and GH Action wrapper [x] Migrate pytest invocation and add xdist config [x] Bump python/node test deps and update snapshots [x] Add dep-compat-checker job and docs [x] Smoke-run on redwood monorepo, and run nightly with sample repos

Testing and CI: - Initial CI run failed on an intermittent longtest (test/integration/runner/test_kv_cache.py) due to a shared temporary directory; fixed by isolating tmpdir usage and adding a conftest fixture. - After fixes, full presubmit pipeline passed on a re-run. - Added a short smoke job (ci/presubmit-prober/smoke.yml) that executes the prober against a trimmed sample of checks to detect bootstrap regressions quickly.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind a short quiesce window (done). 2) Enable the presubmit-prober action on redwood and redwood-examples with a 48h monitoring window. 3) If telemetry remains stable and flakiness decreases, deprecate legacy Makefile presubmit targets in a follow-up PR that removes the old scripts.

Risk and mitigation: - Risk: pytest-xdist can surface race conditions — mitigation: added a new test-parallelization checklist and isolated several tests that relied on process-global state; also provided opt-out via pytest.ini markers for tests that must run serialized. - Risk: dependency bumps could hide incompatible behavior — mitigation: dep-compat-checker will raise warnings on the PR and the team will triage. - Risk: developer local workflow changes — mitigation: .husky now forwards to the same prober (local lightweight shim) so local experience is preserved.

Related work: ENG-1212 (presubmit rework RFC), ENG-1350 (test-parallelization initiative), SUP-4523 (customer incident that exposed flaky longtests).
Introduce pluggable presubmit prober, migrate Python test runner to pytest-xdist for parallel presubmit runs; bump pytest/node test deps and add a dep-compatibility checker that gates risky upgrades. Improves presubmit latency and provides clearer dep upgrade telemetry.
Maya Li: Can we avoid pinning jest to a hard patch version? Pining causes noise on future upgrades. Suggest range ^29.5.0 unless we depend on a specific bugfix.
Priya Kaur (author): Good point — switched package.json to ^29.5.0 and added dep-compat-checker to warn on transitive changes. Left a follow-up TODO to relax if semver proves stable.
Diego Alvarez: The prober binary is Go; can we cross-compile in CI images to avoid build mismatch? Also request an integration test for the GH Action wrapper.
Priya Kaur (author): Added a small cross-build step in the presubmit-prober action and a smoke integration workflow that runs the action against a trimmed set of plugins (see ci/workflows/presubmit-prober.yml).
Omar Hassan: I saw first CI run fail due to a flaky longtest — thanks for the fix. Please add a short note in the runbook describing how to triage xdist failures (stdout interleaving).
Priya Kaur (author): Added a triage section in docs/ci/presubmit-runbook.md and included an example of collecting per-worker logs.

Internal only: adds canonical customer_tier dimension to metering/warehouse views for the Unit Economics dashboard; includes one-time backfill job + guardrails for edge cases (resellers, pilots/credits, dedicated/private routing).
Context: Unit Economics dashboard needs a finance-aligned, stable `customer_tier` dimension to support drilldowns and reconciliation. Today tier is implicitly inferred ad-hoc in queries (billing plan here, dedicated tags there), which creates mismatches and makes backfills painful.

This PR introduces a canonical derivation path for `customer_tier` and a safe backfill tool to populate the dimension for historical metering events used by the aggregation job.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a canonical `customer_tier` derivation function used in the metering/analytics ingestion path. Output values are a controlled enum: `self_serve | dedicated | private | enterprise | unknown`. 2) Establishes the source-of-truth precedence order (documented in code + comments) so we get deterministic outcomes across services: (a) Explicit contract metadata (enterprise/private flags) from Billing/Contracts snapshot (daily) (b) Dedicated/private routing signals from gateway/runtime (request metadata) (c) Billing plan / account type for self-serve (d) Fallback to `unknown` with a counter + sampling log.

Edge cases handled: - Resellers / channel: map to `enterprise` when `contract.channel_partner_id` is present and account is marked `invoice_billing=true`; otherwise `unknown` until Contracts snapshot has the mapping (we emit a warning metric so we can track this). - Pilots/POCs/credits: if `billing.plan=free_credits` but `contract.enterprise=true`, tier is `enterprise` (finance wants tier to reflect GTM motion/infra shape, not temporary credits). - Dedicated but billed under enterprise master agreement: dedicated routing wins (`dedicated`), since cost attribution differs (reserved pools) even if contract is enterprise. - Private deployments with shared control plane: tier is `private` if `routing.deployment_mode=private` OR `contract.private=true`; avoids mislabeling private traffic as enterprise hosted.

Backfill tooling: - Adds `tools/unit_econ/backfill_customer_tier` which replays metering rows for a time window, joins on the Contracts snapshot effective at event_time (with a 24h grace window), and writes the derived tier into the `metering_events_v2.customer_tier` column (or the sidecar dimension table when column is absent; see migration notes below). - The job is idempotent and chunked by hour partitions. It supports `--dry-run`, `--limit-hours`, and `--throttle-ms` to avoid overloading the warehouse. - Includes verification queries printed at the end (coverage %, unknown %, tier distribution deltas) for oncall/finance signoff.

Schema/migrations: - Adds `customer_tier` to the normalized dimension set in metering v2 (nullable during rollout). - Adds a compact mapping table `dim_customer_tier_source` for debugging (why a row got a tier) without exploding cardinality; values are `contract | routing | billing | fallback`.

Rollout plan: - Step 1 (this PR): derive tier on write + backfill tool behind feature flag `unit_econ_customer_tier_derivation`. - Step 2: run backfill for 2025-01-01..present during off-peak; monitor warehouse load + unknown rate. - Step 3: turn on the aggregation job to require non-null tier (with `unknown` allowed), and update dashboard queries.

Notes for reviewers: Finance cares most about deterministic mapping + reconciliation stability. SRE cares about backfill safety and not breaking ingestion when upstream contract snapshot lags. Please focus review on precedence rules and failure modes.

Screens/validation: - Staging: ran backfill for a 6-hour window; unknown rate 0.7% (expected, mostly reseller accounts missing contract linkage). - Verified dedicated traffic is correctly labeled via gateway `dedicated_pool_id` for internal dogfood accounts.

Follow-ups: - Add reseller contract linkage to Contracts snapshot (separate work item). - Once stable, remove legacy query-side tier inference in `warehouse/views/unit_econ_*`.
Logan Wright (review): Precedence order looks right, but I’m worried about contract snapshot lag causing tier flips hour-to-hour. Can we make the join time-bounded and sticky for 24h? Also add a metric for snapshot age.
Cole Summers (author): Good call. Updated join logic to use the most recent snapshot <= event_time + 24h grace and emit `contracts_snapshot_age_hours` gauge + `tier_source=fallback` counter when we miss. Added to README verification output as well.
Rishi Malhotra (review): For pilots/credits: please confirm that finance definition wants enterprise even if they’re on free credits. Also, can we ensure resellers don’t show up as self_serve ever?
Cole Summers (author): Confirmed with Laura/Rishi in the methodology thread: tier should reflect contract motion/infra allocation, not temporary credits. Updated rule + added explicit guard: if `invoice_billing` or `channel_partner_id` then never map to self_serve; it’s enterprise or unknown. Added tests.
Nadia Rahman (review): The dimension cardinality guardrails look fine, but we should avoid writing arbitrary strings into tier_source. Can we hard-enum it and validate on ingest?
Cole Summers (author): Done. tier_source is now a small enum with validation at ingest, and unknown values get dropped + counted under `unit_econ_dim_validation_failed_total{dim=tier_source}`.
Sean Gallagher (review): Backfill tool needs to be warehouse-safe. Please add a default throttle and a warning when targeting >72 hours, plus document the recommended maintenance window.
Cole Summers (author): Added default `--throttle-ms=150` and a hard prompt unless `--yes-really` is passed for >72 hours. README updated with maintenance window guidance and query to monitor warehouse queue depth.
Mei Lin (review): Migration does in-place updates on partitions; please ensure it’s partition-pruned and won’t full-scan. Also consider writing to a sidecar table for older partitions.
Cole Summers (author): Adjusted SQL to update by `(day, hour)` partition keys only, and for older partitions we write to `metering_event_dims_overrides` sidecar keyed by event_id. Aggregation view updated to coalesce override -> column -> derived-at-query-time (temporary).
Logan Wright (review): Approved once we add one more golden test for dedicated under enterprise master agreement.
Cole Summers (author): Added `test_dedicated_wins_over_enterprise_contract()` + fixture. Thanks.
Logan Wright: Approved.
Nadia Rahman: Approved.
Rishi Malhotra: Approved (finance review).
Sean Gallagher: Approved (SRE).
After merge: run backfill in staging first, then prod during off-peak; notify #eng-sre and #finance when unknown rate stabilizes <1% for 24h. Feature flag remains off by default until Finance signoff on reconciliation view.

Motivation: Streaming structured outputs and tool/function-calls can diverge when constraint backends (CFG grammar, regex, probabilistic samplers) disagree about partial-token state and escape sequences. This causes inconsistent framing for downstream tool callers and the OpenAI-compat layer, leading to truncated JSON or misrouted function calls. Goal: introduce a compact rule serializer and a probabilistic constraint bridge that aligns CFG/regex decisions with the tokenizer-aware streaming frontier, and add a small compat shim for OpenAI-style partial-token framing. Key changes: 1) Rule serializer: a compact, canonical on-wire format for grammar/regex constraints so the decoder and the streaming proxy can exchange constraint state efficiently; used for canary rollouts and replayability. 2) Probabilistic bridge: on token-edge ambiguity (subtoken splits, escaped delimiters) we compute a lightweight posterior over constraint accept/reject and use a deterministic tie-break policy to avoid flip-flopping mid-stream. This reduces streaming retractions for structured outputs. 3) Escape-sequence coordinator: normalizes model-provided escape sequences (backslashes, quotes, unicode escapes) into a canonical tokenized representation before constraint evaluation to avoid double-decoding. 4) OpenAI-compat shim: adds a tolerant framing mode that buffers the minimal number of bytes required to disambiguate toolcall boundaries while preserving early partial 'delta' streaming for latency-sensitive clients. 5) Tests & rollout: extensive unit tests for tokenizer-edgecases, newly added golden recordings for streaming canary, and a staged rollout plan with feature-flagged runtime toggles. Implementation notes: - The serializer is implemented as rule_serializer.{rs,py} (Rust core + Python bridge) and stores rule fingerprints and serialized predicate trees. - The probabilistic bridge lives in decoder/constraint_bridge.go and exposes a small API used by the streaming proxy. - The OpenAI compat shim is in openai_compat/stream_shim.ts and toggled via REDWOOD_OPENAI_COMPAT_STREAMING env. - Conservative performance opt: only compute the posterior when the tokenizer indicates a grapheme-split or when a rule fingerprint mismatch is detected. Compatibility and migration: - Backward compatible: old runtimes ignore unknown serializer versions and fall back to current CFG/regex backends. - Canary plan: enable serializer+bridge for 5% of production traffic, measure stream retraction rate and functioncall misfires for 72h, then 25% then full rollout. Testing: unit tests added for 42 tokenizer edgecases, integration tests with the example toolcall harness, and three new end-to-end recordings against the OpenAI-compat shim. Observability: new metrics: constraint.bridge.posterior_compute_count, streaming.retraction_rate, compat.shim.buffer_bytes_histogram. Migration checklist: - [x] Add serializer version header and compatibility guard - [x] Add posterior compute budget to runtime config - [x] Add feature flag + rollout plan - [x] Add golden streaming recordings - [x] Add e2e toolcall test harness run in CI Notes and follow-ups: we will follow up with a separate PR to expose the rule fingerprint format in the model catalog and add SDK helpers for users to pin serializer versions. Related: ENG-3421, ENG-3499, SUP-2101. Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3421/constraint-serializer-design (internal), test recordings stored in /bench/streaming/gold/serializer-bridge.
Aisha Kapoor: Nice approach. Two concerns: 1) computing a posterior per ambiguous token could be expensive under high throughput. Suggest adding a budget or sampling mechanism. 2) Need an explicit plan for serializer version skew during rolling restarts.
Morgan Lee: Addressed both. Added posterior_compute_budget config and fast-exit when tokenizer indicates non-ambiguous grapheme. Serializer carries a version header and runtimes ignore unknown versions to remain compatible.
Diego Martinez: Please add more unit tests around escaped unicode sequences (e.g. \u2028) and verify the shim doesn't change byte-level streaming for clients that rely on single-byte framing.
Morgan Lee: Added 12 unicode-specific edgecases and end-to-end recordings showing identical byte stream when shim operates in 'tolerant=false' mode. See tests in runtime/serializer and e2e recordings.
Yvonne Chen: CI flaked once in canary job, reran and passed. Approving for merge after small doc polish.
Morgan Lee: Polished docs and added clarifying note about SDK helpers planned for follow-up PR.
Release manager (informal): Please note release_notes mention when rolling out; this touches streaming and may require comms to integrators.
Introduce rule serializer and probabilistic constraint bridge to reduce streaming retractions and toolcall misfires; add OpenAI-compat streaming shim; feature-flagged rollout and new observability metrics.

Motivation: Recent incident (SUP-4421) showed the control plane's abrupt circuit opens caused aggressive KV cache invalidation and a sharp regen spike when regions recovered. Operators need a low-risk operator action to stop accepting new work for a tenant/region while preserving runtime state and enabling a gradual handoff. This PR implements two cooperating features: (1) temporal SLO snapshots: periodic, atomic snapshots of per-tenant SLO state and connection leases that can be used to restore a consistent soft-state after a transient failure, and (2) a soft kill-switch at the routing layer: an operator-facing API/CLI to probabilistically reject new requests for a target scope (tenant/region) with configurable pacing and holdoff semantics so in-flight requests and KV caches are preserved. What this changes: atomic snapshotting of SLO and lease tables into the control plane's ephemeral store; a restore path used by the regional reconciler to fast-reinstate leases without forcing cache flush; routing-level soft-kill with token-bucket based pacing and a TTLed holdoff window that is recorded in the snapshot; new rwctl commands to trigger soft-kill/restore; metrics and tracing hooks for snapshot durations, reject-rate, and restored-lease counts. Implementation notes: snapshots are lightweight (only pointers and compacted SLO deltas) to avoid I/O pressure; we added a two-phase restore (metadata rebind then lease re-announce) to prevent races with the KV cache drainer. The soft kill is implemented as a middleware in the routing stack that consults an in-memory holdoff policy with a probabilistic rejection decision and a warmup cooldown schedule. Operator actions are persisted to the snapshot store so manual soft-kills survive control plane failover. Testing: unit tests for snapshot encoder/decoder, integration test that simulates control plane failover and verifies no mass KV flush, e2e runway (lightweight) that exercises rwctl soft-kill + restore path. Load tests on perf-lab show <2% additional p99 request latency under steady-state. Migration and rollout: feature-flag guarded (enable: controlplane.temporal_slo_snapshot = true). Default off in main; rollout plan is: internal canary -> staged rollout -> org-wide opt-in. Docs and rwctl help updated in this PR. Checklist: [x] Feature flag guarded [x] Unit + integration tests [x] rwctl subcommand and docs [x] Telemetry (metrics + traces) [x] Load validation in perf-lab Related: ENG-1249 (slo drift at failover), ENG-1302 (kv regen storms), SUP-4421 (incident)
Arjun Patel: Nice design. Two concerns: race between restore and KV drainer - can you add a guard that delays drainer until metadata rebind completes?
Maya Thompson: Added two-phase restore (metadata rebind -> lease re-announce). See commit a9c3f11. Also added an explicit 'drainer_holdoff' signal in the snapshot store so drainer checks it before flushing.
Leah Kim: Please add Prometheus labels to the reject-rate metric to distinguish tenant vs region and include the feature-flag name in logs for easier triage.
Maya Thompson: Added labels and feature-flag log prefix in 8d2e6b0. Also updated docs to mention metric cardinality tradeoffs.
Diego Rivera: CI showed a flaky test on Mac builders; looks like a timing assumption in snapshot_restore_test.go. Can you make it deterministic?
Maya Thompson: Converted the test to use a deterministic fake clock and bumped the test timeouts. Fix in c4b7ffa.

Motivation: Live SSE streams sometimes emitted delimiter tokens that split structured JSON spans and reordered tool/function call sentinel boundaries under high-concurrency prefix-merge scenarios. This resulted in partial JSON objects reaching clients and occasional toolcall ordinal inversion when late-arriving fragments were applied. This PR introduces two coordinated mitigations: 1) a Span Resolver that tracks logical JSON/structured-output spans across chunk boundaries and emits explicit endcap markers to guarantee atomic span delivery, and 2) a per-stream Semaphore Flush that enforces an ordered drain/flush point before switching handoff to function/tool callers. Summary of changes: add sse/span_resolver module with deterministic span ID assignment and reassembly checkpoints; implement endcap markers ("__span_end:<id>__") emitted only when a span is fully reassembled; introduce semaphore-based flush/handshake in sse/stream_coordinator to serialize toolcall handoffs and prevent ordinal inversion; add a lookahead delimiter probe to avoid splitting UTF-8 multibyte sequences across chunk boundaries; add backwards-compatible compatibility layer that strips internal endcap markers when running in openai-compat mode; tests: comprehensive unit/integration set covering fragmented JSON reassembly, racey toolcall handoff, and roundtrip compatibility with older clients. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag sse.span_resolver.enabled (default off). Canary deploy to edge region us-west-2 for 48 hours with traffic shaping; flip global runtime flag after canary metrics show <1% elevated latency and 0 regression in structured-output acceptance tests. Backwards compatibility: openai-compat mode removes internal endcap markers so clients that expect vanilla SSE semantics see original stream. Related work: builds on ENG-12011 (previous checkpointing experiment) and implements learnings from incident SUP-4821. Notes on cost and perf: semaphore flush introduces a small serialization point when a toolcall is actively being handed off; we added batching windows to amortize overhead and measured median token latency increase of ~2.3ms in stress tests but eliminated 100% of observed partial-JSON incidents. CI and testing: added deterministic fragment-replay harness and fuzzing job for SSE chunk permutations. Documentation: runtime flag, migration notes, and compatibility guidance added to docs/sse_streaming.md.
Diego Ramos: Generally LGTM but please add a comment documenting the invariants for span IDs and GC behavior.
Asha Menon: Added detailed doc comments in span_resolver.rs and a small GC test that exercises long-running spans.
Katherine Liu: Found a race when multiple toolcalls were queued for the same connection; suggested an explicit queue drain before handshake. Implemented queue drain and added test.
Mason Patel: CI flagged a flake in the fragment replay harness; narrowed down to nondeterministic timer in test harness and replaced with fake-time. Rerun CI.
Diego Ramos: Approving after fixes and CI green.
Fixes an issue where SSE streaming could emit partial/unterminated JSON objects and reorder tool/function call boundaries under high-concurrency fragmentation. Adds a span resolver and handshake semantics to ensure atomic structured-output spans and deterministic toolcall ordering. Backwards-compatible in openai-compat mode.
New deterministic fragment replay harness included. Run 'cargo test --manifest-path runtime/Cargo.toml --features=sse' plus the fragment_replay_test locally. Fuzzer: ci/fuzzers/sse_fuzzer.yml. Canary plan described in description.
Added metrics: sse.span_reassembled_count, sse.endcap_emitted_count, sse.semaphore_flush_wait_ms (p99). Dashboard tile added to Runtime > SSE Streams.

payload.body:
Context and motivation:
Long-tail invocations with many short-lived spans were causing high cardinality in our span-store and noisy per-token cost attributions. Teams running cost-sensitive workloads reported that existing sampled traces frequently missed small but expensive token hotspots (e.g. aggressive multi-tool reroutes), while dashboards were overloaded with near-duplicate short spans. This PR introduces a compact-span compactor, a token-bucket provenance index, and microtrace stitching to improve signal quality and reduce storage/ingest costs.

What this changes (high level):
- compact-span compactor: a lightweight component that deduplicates and coalesces sequences of short spans within an invocation into a compact microtrace representation. Compact microtraces retain timing buckets, aggregate token counts, and provenance markers but remove repeated low-entropy payloads.
- token-bucket provenance index: a per-invocation, per-segment index that attributes token cost to provenance labels (e.g. prompt-prefix, model-fallback, tool-call). Enables authoritative per-token cost rollups without needing full span payloads for every invocation.
- microtrace stitching: when a full sampled trace exists, compact microtraces are stitched into the trace summary UI so users can expand compressed segments on demand. This keeps storage low while preserving explorable context for root-cause.
- Dashboard: added "Token Provenance Lens" panels under Observability > Invocation Explorer and a compact microtrace timeline panel. Panels surface cost by provenance bucket and show compact vs full trace fidelity.

Context: weekend traffic spike exposed a pathological interaction between hard circuit resets and the SLO enforcer that led to prolonged regional evictions. This PR implements a 'surge absorber' soft-circuit and a fast-recovery path to reduce time-to-recovery while bounding quality impact. Motivation: avoid long outage windows caused by repeated hard-circuit trips and quota thrash during bursts; maintain availability for small/low-cost requests without sacrificing operator control. Implementation summary: introduce a per-route transient token-budget bucket and a soft-circuit state machine (open -> absorbing -> degraded -> recovering), integrate with the SLO enforcer to mark degraded responses and emit explicit degradation_reason tags, add a fast-recovery router that routes compact responses to a low-latency fast-model replica when allowed, add feature flag gating (runtime.surge_absorber.v1) and canary rollout controls, and update dashboards/runbook. Backwards compatibility and ops: feature is opt-in; default off for Dedicated and Private deploys. Operators can configure per-tenant thresholds and disable fast-recovery routing. Checklist: [x] unit tests for state transitions and budget accounting; [x] integration tests with SLO enforcer; [x] perf-canary in benchmark-lab; [x] dashboards and alerts updated; [x] runbook and rollback steps documented; [x] Linear ticket(s) referenced (ENG-1823). Rollout plan: staged canary in eu-west-1 then us-west-2; automated gates on error-rate, degraded_response_rate, and embedding/regression signals; automatic rollback if quality regress > 3% on canary. Metrics added: runtime.surge_absorber.state, runtime.surge_absorber.recovery_time_ms, runtime.surge_absorber.degraded_response_rate. Notes: this is a targeted reliability improvement (not a model change). See ENG-3890 for follow-up harmonization across other soft-circuit implementations.
Marco Jensen: Can we ensure the budget bucket is persisted across short process restarts? Response: we persist the bucket epoch to etcd; kept the retention tiny to avoid state bloat and added tests around restart semantics.
Priya Nair: Concern about double-counting tokens when fallback triggers; please add a guard. Response: added atomic accounting and a new unit test (surge_absorber_test.go::TestNoDoubleCount) and recorded the invariant in comments.
Ethan Cole: Please add observability to distinguish soft vs hard circuit evictions. Response: added runtime.surge_absorber.degraded_response_rate and emit evict_reason label (soft|hard) for existing eviction metrics.
Priya Nair (approval): Verified canary in eu-west-1 for 6h, metrics within thresholds. Approving to merge.
Unit: 12 new tests, 40 updated. Integration: SLO enforcer integration tests passing. Perf-canary: benchmark-lab 20-minute 2x-load run showed 41% fewer full-region evictions and 18% lower mean recovery time. Canary: staged 6-hour run in eu-west-1 with automated gates; no quality regressions observed above thresholds. CI: all checks green.
Adds a gated ‘surge absorber’ soft-circuit to reduce full-region evictions during spikes and a fast-recovery routing path for low-cost responses. Opt-in via runtime.surge_absorber.v1. Includes metrics, dashboards, and an updated runbook.
Hotfix intent: addresses a production incident 2026-01-17 where repeated hard-circuit resets caused cascading regional evictions. This change reduces blast radius and improves recovery time; follow-up work planned to generalize soft-circuit policy across other routing layers (ENG-3890).

Motivation: customers running at constrained budgets need a lightweight, tenant-scoped prefetch controller that trades small increases in cold-start latency for measurable cost reductions and stable tail latency. This change adds a pocket-prefetch regulator service that applies budget-aware prefilling decisions, a small CLI to generate tenant-level unit-economic reports and recommended quantization/batching presets, and new telemetry to measure prefill cost vs. latency trade-offs. Key goals: (1) provide a low-risk opt-in controller for Dedicated/Private deployments, (2) surface unit economics so SREs and platform engineers can reason about cost/latency trade-offs, (3) enable automated safe rollouts with a canary policy. What changed: a) new service module prefetch/regulator implementing a percentile-based budget allocator and a short-lived prefill queue; b) policy DSL extension to allow 'pocket' budget rules per-tenant (prefill_budget_pct and tail_latency_slo); c) CLI command redwood unit-econ generate --tenant <id> that collects recent telemetry and recommends quant/batch defaults; d) telemetry: prefill_cost_scorer, prefill_tail_latency_p95, prefill_hit_ratio; e) small changes to admission logic to allow soft-prefill paths that can be degraded to on-demand when budget is exceeded. Rollout plan: merge behind feature flag pocket_prefill.v1 defaulted off; enable for internal staging tenants and run 72h smoke; if p95 latency regressions < 5% and unit-cost improves >= 8% we will schedule a gradual tenant opt-in by capacity. Checklist: - [x] design doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/ENG-1219/pocket-prefetch-regulator-design - [x] unit tests for regulator allocator and CLI parsing - [x] integration smoke test for refill/degrade path - [x] observability dashboards updated - [x] feature flag gating implemented - [x] release notes entry drafted How to validate manually: 1) deploy with pocket_prefill.v1=true for a staging tenant; 2) run workload generator with mixed short/long sequences (templates in perf-lab/prefill-scripts); 3) run `redwood unit-econ generate --tenant staging-42 --output json` and inspect recommended batch/quant profiles; 4) compare /metrics for prefill_cost_scorer and prefill_tail_latency_p95. Backwards compatibility: all changes are feature-flag gated; default behavior unchanged. This is additive to the policy DSL and does not change runtime API shapes. Related work: touches prefill orchestration, telemetry composer, and the CLI surfaces used by platform engineers. Referenced Linear tasks and SUP ticket above.
Aisha Kapoor: Please add stronger bounds on the allocator to prevent noisy tenants from consuming >50% of budget. Also add a unit test for the overflow case.
Priya Desai: Addressed — added bounding factor and overflow test; pushed commit b4e2d11.
Dmitri Ivanov: Telemetry looks good; can we expose a short windowed moving-average alongside p95 so we can detect sudden regressions?
Priya Desai: Added prefill_tail_latency_5m_avg and updated dashboard; pushed c8812d4.
Marcos Ramirez: CLI output is handy; suggest adding --dry-run that prints expected cost delta without applying recommendations.
Priya Desai: Added --dry-run and safety checks; documented in README.md, commit d33f1ab.

This enables budget-aware prefill with safe degrade-to-on-demand behavior. No breaking changes.

Context and motivation: Customers operating across multiple cloud regions asked for a way to grant operators limited admin capabilities that are scoped both by service and by region, and for KMS usage to be auditable without expanding global key access. This PR introduces a conditional RBAC role model (RBAC v2 predicate-based roles) that can express 'service X in region Y' constraints, adds KMS routing assertions that follow requests through the stack, and a pluggable server-side audit redactor to strip sensitive fields from logs for regulated tenants.

What changed (summary):
- New predicate-based RBAC conditions and enforcement in the policy engine; policies can include attributes: region, service, task (read/write), and temporal windows.
- Middleware to derive and propagate a signed KMS-routing assertion header (x-rw-kms-assertion) populated from the request's tenancy + region preference.
- Audit redactor component that consults tenant compliance profile and redacts or hashes configured fields before persisting to the audit store. Redaction rules are configurable via the security-config map.
- Migration script and feature flag (security.conditional_rbac) to allow gradual rollout and rollback.
- Unit and integration tests plus a small performance sanity suite demonstrating <0.7ms median add-on latency for the new middleware when enabled.

Checklist: [x] policy model defined and documented; [x] enforcement integrated into request pipeline; [x] migration script added; [x] tests covering policy evaluation and KMS header correctness; [x] docs updated; [x] feature-flag gated rollout.

Commits (high level):
- feat(policy): introduce predicate AST and evaluator with region/service attributes
- feat(middleware): add kms routing assertion generator and verifier
- feat(audit): implement pluggable redactor with config-driven rules
- chore(migrations): add 202601_rbac_region_migration.sql and migration runner hook
- test: add security integration tests for cross-region role enforcement

Files changed (high level):
- src/auth/policy_engine.go  -- new predicate AST, evaluator, policy loader (key changes)
- src/middleware/kms_assertion_mw.go  -- generate/verify x-rw-kms-assertion, sign with service key
- src/audit/redactor.go  -- redact/hash PII depending on tenant profile
- scripts/migrations/202601_rbac_region_migration.sql  -- creates region attribute index and default policies
- config/security/security-config.yaml  -- new redaction rules and feature flag
- tests/security/test_rbac_region.yaml  -- end-to-end test scenarios
- docs/security/rbac-region-pin.md  -- design + operator guide for migration/rollback

Small illustrative snippet (policy syntax example):
policy allow-operator-region {
  subject: role:service-operator
  resource: service:storage-queue
  action: write
  condition: region == "eu-west-1" && hour >= 08 && hour <= 18
}

Review conversation (high level):
- Arjun: "Great model. Two requests: make the predicate evaluator iterative to avoid recursion on deeply nested policy trees, and add a benchmark for policy eval with 200 active rules."
- Maya: "Addressed by switching to a worklist algorithm and adding policy_bench_test.go; saw 15% improvement for the worst-case rule-set."
- Lena: "Please ensure redactor rules are explicit about reversible vs irreversible hashing; we must ensure audit replayability for security audits."
- Maya: "Added explicit rule types (redact/hash/mask) and documented constraints in security-config.yaml. Reversible hashes require extra key material and are disabled by default."
- Samir: "One nit: use the existing metrics tag 'operator_id' rather than 'op_id' to keep dashboards compatible."
- Maya: "Fixed and updated dashboards in docs."
- Arjun (approve): "LGTM after fixes - squash on merge."

CI and validation:
- CI run 1 (initial): lint passed, unit tests failed (flake in policy loader test) -> author reworked loader and added stabilizing test harness.
- CI run 2: all unit tests passed, integration suite passed in GHA fanned runners, security static analysis reported 1 minor issue (unused var) fixed.
- Performance: micro-bench for middleware shows ~0.5–0.7ms median extra cost when the feature flag is on; disabled by default so host impact is zero until rollout.

Migration and rollout notes:
- Migration script creates new policy attribute indexes and a small set of default service-scoped operator roles. The feature is gated behind security.conditional_rbac; we recommend enabling for a single region and observing metrics for 48h before full rollout.
- Rollback: disabling feature flag returns policy evaluation to prior behavior; migration script is reversible but requires manual cleanup when removing indexes.

Security considerations:
- KMS routing assertions are signed using the service signing key; verification is required in downstream services before any key use.
- Audit redactor cannot be used to hide system-level security events; the redactor runs only on tenant-level event payloads, and system events are preserved.

Merge outcome: Squash merged into main by Arjun Patel. No follow-up blockers noted.

Adds conditional RBAC roles scoped to service+region, propagates KMS routing assertions into request metadata, and implements server-side audit redaction rules. Includes migration script and feature flag rollout.

payload.body:
Motivation: We observed intermittent cudagraph warmup regressions when serving mixed-prefix workloads (wide variance in prefix lengths and KV cache tiling). Captures would occasionally pick kernels that later proved incompatible with longer/shorter prefix permutations causing immediate replay failures or a cascade of fallbacks that amplified latency spikes. This PR implements a defensive, adaptive approach to reduce warmup flaps while preserving the latency wins of cudagraphs.

What this PR does (single-pass overview):
- Adaptive replay-window contraction: the replay manager now tracks a time-weighted history of successful captures keyed by (model, device_arch, kv_tiling, prefix_bucket). When shape variance within a bucket exceeds a threshold we conservatively contract the replay window for that bucket (i.e., reduce the number of replayed iterations and increase probe frequency) to avoid committing to an unstable capture.
- Scheduler integrity guard: a lightweight verification layer in the scheduler verifies kernel / convolution selection stability before a captured graph is promoted to long-lived use. If the guard detects a mismatch during priming, we trigger a controlled backoff (temporary non-cudagraph path) and schedule a probing capture instead of immediate promotion.
- KV-cache tiling alignment: continuous-batching and KV cache placement can skew memory layouts causing kernel-compatibility differences at capture time. We introduce a tiler that aligns KV-cache layout heuristically at capture time and tags the capture with the tiling signature so replays are matched only when layout-compatible.
- Backoff & graceful fallback: instead of immediate wide rollback, the runtime now performs exponential backoff of replay promotion and falls back to the non-graph path for a fixed number of iterations to allow the workload to stabilize. The backoff is jittered to minimize synchronized retries across workers.
- Observability and instrumentation: new telemetry metrics (cudagraph.replay_backoff.count, cudagraph.replay_promotion_latency_ms, cudagraph.kv_tiling.mismatch_count) and logging traces for captures/promotions. Added debug-only histograms that helped diagnose the original regressions in perf lab runs.
- Feature gating and rollout: the entire new logic is gated behind the runtime feature-flag "replay_adaptive_guard_v2" and defaults to off for Dedicated customers. Admins can opt in per-deployment and per-model.

Design notes / rationale:
- We intentionally avoid altering kernel-selection heuristics; instead we add a safety layer that verifies kernel stability across short-term shape variance. Changing kernel heuristics directly proved brittle in previous experiments and caused regression blasts when run across heterogeneous GPUs.
- The replay-window contraction is tuned to prefer shorter, fast-probing windows on high-variance buckets (interactive workloads with many short prefixes) and wider windows for stable, long-sequence workloads. This keeps throughput benefits where safe and reduces warmup regressions where not.

Performance & validation (summary):
- Perf-lab synthetic mixed-prefix test (80% short prefixes <64 tokens, 20% long prefixes >512 tokens): warmup failure rate before fix: ~9.8% (cudagraph replays that fallback at least once per 1k captures); after fix: ~2.1% (78% reduction). Measured with 8xA100 pool.
- Tail latency (p95) on the synthetic trace improved by ~7% during steady-state due to more stable graph promotions; transient p99 spikes decreased by ~42% because fewer fallback cascades occurred.
- Microbenchmarks show a 1.5%-2.3% overhead for the integrity guard checks in priming path (amortized away for promoted graphs). We added configuration knobs to disable aggressive checks if ultra-low overhead path is required.

Commits (high-level):
- Add adaptive replay window state machine and persistence layer
- Introduce scheduler integrity guard & promotion policy
- Implement kv_cache tiler and tiling-signature matching
- Add telemetry metrics + dashboards and unit/integration tests
- Add feature flag and rollout script + docs

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/cuda/replay_manager.cpp
- runtime/cuda/replay_manager.h
- runtime/scheduler/integrity_guard.cpp
- runtime/scheduler/integrity_guard.h
- runtime/kv/kv_tiler.cpp
- runtime/kv/kv_tiler.h
- runtime/config/feature_flags.cpp
- telemetry/metrics/cudagraph_metrics.md
- tests/integration/cudagraph_replay_variance.test.cpp
- tests/unit/scheduler_guard_test.cpp
- docs/runtime/replay_adaptive_guard_v2.md

Review conversation (high level):
- Diego Morales (requested changes, 2025-08-24): "Please add a deterministic unit test that simulates two workers racing on promotion and verify the jitter/backoff avoids thundering-herd promotions. Also add a comment explaining why we don't bake tiling into kernel selection heuristics." 
  - Author reply (2025-08-25): "Added scheduler_guard_race_test in tests/unit and expanded comments in integrity_guard.h. Race test uses deterministic fake clock and verifies backoff windows across 3 workers." 
- Priya Nair (performance review, 2025-08-27): "Can you share the perf-lab config and raw histograms? Need to validate across 4xV100 and 8xA100 configs before approval." 
  - Author reply (2025-08-28): "Attached perf lab job ids and added dashboards link in the PR description. Verified histograms for both configs; summary included above." 
- Ethan Zhang (observability, 2025-08-29): "Add a tag to traces to correlate replay promotion attempts with kv_tiling signatures and include a severity for repeated mismatches so ops can alert." 
  - Author reply (2025-08-30): "Added cudagraph.kv_tiling.signature tag to traces and a severity label on mismatch metric. Updated dashboard panels and added alert runbook references in docs/runtime/replay_adaptive_guard_v2.md." 
- Final approval from Priya and Diego (2025-09-01) after small nits fixed.

CI notes:
- Initial CI run (2025-08-26) failed two flaky integration tests; rerun and fixed a timing dependency in tests/integration/cudagraph_replay_variance.test.cpp. Final CI status: pass.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main gated off by default.
2) Canary rollout to perf-canary cluster for 48 hours with 5% traffic. Monitor new metrics and p99 regressions.
3) Gradual increase to 25% then 100% for non-Dedicated customers. Dedicated customers are opt-in.
4) If mismatch_count or replay_backoff.count increases by >3x baseline, automatic rollback hook will disable the feature flag cluster-wide.

Testing & QA:
- Added deterministic unit tests covering promotion backoff, tiling signature matching, and scheduler guard race conditions.
- Integration tests in perf-lab ran synthetic mixed-prefix traces with multiple GPU configurations.
- Local stress harness validated jittered backoff reduces synchronized promotions across 16 worker processes.

Migration notes:
- No customer-facing API changes. Config default remains off. Admins who opted in previously will see new metrics and must ensure feature flag is set to true for both runtime and console rollout.

Follow-ups (future work):
- Investigate optional safe encoding of tiling signatures in model metadata so capture/replay matching can happen across model version pinning events.
- Explore light-weight kernel-selection feedback loop that uses promotion history to recommend per-model capture targets (separate PR).

Summary: This change reduces cudagraph warmup flaps for mixed-prefix workloads by combining an adaptive replay-window with a scheduler integrity guard and KV-cache tiling alignment. It is conservative by default, observable, and opt-in for Dedicated customers. Merged to main via squash on 2025-09-02.

Introduces adaptive replay-window contraction and a scheduler integrity guard to reduce cudagraph warmup flaps across variable-prefix workloads; adds KV-cache tiling alignment for stable kernel selection; safe rollout behind feature flag.

payload.body:
Motivation: improve structured-output UX and streaming stability for tool/function calling by introducing a lightweight contract handoff and fenced toolcall checkpoints. This change addresses two recurring issues from production traces: 1) downstream consumers saw partial JSON fragments in streaming mode without a clear recovery path; 2) function/tool calls could leak open tokens into user-visible streams when a model emitted a call mid-object.

What this PR does (summary): adds a "handoff marker" convention emitted by the runtime when a response_format contract (json_schema_v3) is in play; introduces fenced toolcall emission so function calls are produced as a discrete handoff event (separate frame in streaming mode) and are reconciled with the JSON contract; implements a soft strictness level ("warn") that returns structured validation warnings without hard failing streaming responses; maps validation failures to OpenAI-compat error codes and payload shape for downstream SDKs.

Key behaviors: - Handoff marker: when response_format is present the runtime emits a single short marker frame ("__contract_handoff__") to signal the start of contract-enforced emission and to prime downstream consumers for partial-object checkpoints. The marker is idempotent and only emitted once per request. - Toolcall fencing: tool/function calls are emitted in a fenced frame (type=toolcall) that is guaranteed to be a discrete event in the streaming protocol; when a toolcall occurs inside a JSON object the runtime will close the current partial object and resume after the toolcall to avoid malformed object fragments. - Soft strict mode: strict_mode has three allowed values (off|warn|strict). warn will deliver the full stream but append structured validation-warnings in metadata and emit a final validation-summary frame; strict will abort the response and return a mapped error. - OpenAI compatibility: validation failures and toolcall errors are translated to an OpenAI-compatible error object (type, code, message, details) so existing integrations can adopt without protocol changes.

Why this approach: pragmatic rollback-friendly changes that increase streaming stability for web clients and SDKs, while preserving backwards compatibility and giving customers an escape hatch (strict mode) for enforcement.

Checklist: - [x] Runtime: handoff marker + fenced toolcall frames - [x] API: accept strict_mode values in response_format config - [x] SDKs: mapping layer for OpenAI-compatible errors (Python + TS stubs) - [x] Tests: unit + integration + a small canary against staging streaming gateway - [x] Docs: console API notes and quick example

Related work: linear/ENG-1981, ENG-2010, earlier PRs touched streaming schema enforcement but either hard-failed too eagerly or fragmented toolcall frames. This PR aims to be the middle ground and unblock client integrations.
Asha Patel: Please add an opt-out safety check for legacy clients that can't handle the extra frames. -> Added response header X-Contract-Handoff: false for legacy fallbacks, and SDKs will negotiate the header at connect time.
Diego Ramirez: Does toolcall fencing impact latency for short responses? we should measure. -> Added microbenchmarks in streaming/benchmarks; median p50 delta < 2ms for 0-64 token responses.
Karen Liu: We need a clear error mapping table for OpenAI consumers. -> Added openai-compat/mapper.go and docs section with code table and examples.
Samir Banerjee: Tests flaked on CI initially due to ordering of frames. -> Fixed: deterministic frame ordering in stream_emitter and added a test asserting frame sequence.
Introduce contract handoff marker and fenced toolcall frames for improved streaming stability and structured-output validation. Adds response_format.strict_mode (off|warn|strict) with OpenAI-compatible error mapping. Backwards compatible by default (off).

payload.body:
Summary: Introduce a deterministic CMK selection algorithm (DKSP) and an Audit Token Bridge to provide verifiable, privacy-preserving proofs of key selection for region-pinned workloads. Motivation: customers operating under data residency constraints require deterministic, auditable routing of encryption operations to region-appropriate CMKs while minimizing disclosure of key identifiers to downstream services and logs. This PR implements a deterministic selection function based on tenant affinity, region policy and key-rotation epoch, an opaque audit-token envelope that proves which CMK was used without exposing raw key IDs, and RBAC v2 policy mappings that gate who can request or verify audit tokens. Design: (1) DKSP: a small deterministic hash that combines tenant_id, region_tag, and rotation_epoch and maps to a stable cmk-alias-anchor; fallback rules route to regional fallback pools if mapping is missing. (2) Audit Token Bridge: service-side component that mints a signed envelope (audit_token) containing a blinded reference to the CMK alias, a signed nonce, and a compliance assertion. The token is verifiable by compliance tooling using the platform's audit public key; verification returns only "alias-hash" and compliance attributes, not plaintext key ARN. (3) RBAC v2: new attribute-driven policies that add "kms:verify-audit-token" and "kms:mint-audit-token" permissions scoped to service principals and linear-linked tickets. (4) Private installer hooks: installer performs a preflight to verify local CMK alias registrations and deploys local verifier keys for air-gapped customers. Testing and rollout: unit + integration tests added; e2e ran across us-west-2, eu-central-1 and a simulated air-gapped environment. Rollout uses a staged feature flag gated by ENG-2146 and SEC-802; initial rollout to Dedicated customers with region-pin opt-in. Backout plan: feature flag toggle and a deterministic fallback to legacy round-robin CMK allocator. Security review notes: keys are never exported; audit tokens rotate with audit key TTL and are short-lived (5m by default). Compliance owners validated token schema and verifier workflow. Context and motivation: Customers running in regulated jurisdictions have asked for finer-grained node/operator controls when a request must be pinned to a geographic key location. This PR introduces 'regionmatic' KMS escrow (a short-lived, provenance-bearing crypto proxy) plus RBAC v2 mappings that enforce least-privilege for operator roles that can request key-wrapping or escrow operations. The goal is to provide: (1) deterministic region pin enforcement early in the routing stack, (2) an operator-limited crypto proxy that performs ephemeral key wrapping only when the requestors' RBAC attributes and audit flags permit it, and (3) canonical-region audit enrichment so downstream auditors can reconstruct residence decisions without leaking sensitive attributes.

What this change does (high level): Implements a small proxy service (kms-escrowd) and an admission/shim layer that validates a request's "region_claim" against customer-configured per-service region policies. Adds RBAC v2 policy templates and a policy compiler hook so operator roles get transient grants (time-limited) instead of broad privileges. Adds audit header canonicalization (X-Redwood-Region-Canonical) and an audit sanitizer that strips ephemeral claims when forwarding to third-party sinks. Adds tests and a canary rollout config to Dedicated and Private installers.

Problem: Dedicated fleets that span regions were occasionally double-allocating burst credits and emitting duplicate utilization spikes when tenant requests were shifted by global load-balancers. This led to transient SLA overshoots and noisy telemetry across regions. Motivation: provide a lightweight cross-region commit coordination mechanism and a fanout adapter for burst signals so autoscalers and ledgers see a single authoritative event stream per logical surge. What this PR does: (1) introduces a Commit Coordinator controller that reconciles 'provision intents' across regional controllers using a compact lease protocol (gossip + tombstones) and a per-tenant commit horizon to avoid racey double-commits; (2) adds a Granular Burst Signal Fanout layer that deduplicates and annotates burst events with origin region, sequence, and sanity TTL before writing to the utilization pipeline; (3) instruments new telemetry hooks and tracing spans to show cross-region reconciliation latency and de-duplication ratios; (4) adds an operator command (redwoodctl provision commit-status) to inspect commit horizon for a tenant and force-safe-rewind for legacy reservoirs. Design notes: the coordinator is intentionally conservative — it serializes commit windows at 1s granularity to preserve correctness while letting local pools maintain low-latency admits for steady state. The fanout performs idempotency checks using sequence+origin and guards the ledger using a short-lived consensus token (not full Raft). We favored an eventual-consistent reconciliation with fast local admits plus a graceful revoke path rather than strong synchronous global locks to avoid latency regressions. Migration/rollout: feature-gated via cluster config (ENABLE_INTERREGION_COMMIT_COORDINATOR). Default is off; rollout plan is: canary in single interregion tenant pool, observe dedup ratio and commit lag, then enable by regions. Backwards compatibility: coordinator tolerates older regional controllers — they will continue emitting events and coordinator will reconcile without requiring immediate upgrades. Testing: unit tests for dedupe logic, integration E2E across two-region kind clusters, load soak verifying no >2% additional latency in the steady path, synthetic chaos test that flips region leadership. Related: references ENG-1942 for rollout plan and SRE-23 for runbook updates. 
Marcus: Can we avoid another cross-region RPC in the hot path? Author: The hot path remains local admits; the coordinator runs async and reconciles within the commit horizon. Only the fast revoke path will incur an interregion call and that is gated. Diego: What about clock skew across regions affecting sequence TTL? Author: We use monotonic sequence per origin and include a TTL window of 5s with wall-clock tolerant checks; tests simulate 2s skew. Priya: Add a metric for 'dedupe_ratio' and an alert threshold. Author: Added metric and SLO proposal in SRE-23. Marcus: Please add stronger unit tests around tombstone expiry. Author: Added two unit tests and an integration chaos test. Diego: CI flaked on e2e; reran and passed. Final: Approved by Marcus and Diego after addressing tests. 
- New: Interregion Commit Coordinator to prevent burst double-allocation in multi-region fleets.
- New: Granular Burst Signal Fanout reduces duplicate telemetry across regions and exposes dedupe_ratio metric.
- Ops: redwoodctl provision commit-status command for inspecting commit horizons.
Rollout: feature-gated. See docs/runbooks/interregion-commit-coordinator.md for rollout steps and runbook.
