Motivation: presubmit runtimes have grown linearly with repo size and noisy dependency updates cause frequent churn and flakiness. This PR introduces a lightweight presubmit 'shepherd' that batches small changes into a single validation run, and a dependency quarantine mechanism that automatically isolates suspicious transitive updates for manual review. Summary: - Add a batched presubmit workflow (GH actions-based) that groups related commits in the same push into one validation run (saves CI tokens and reduces queue pressure). - Introduce tools/dep-quarantine to detect semver-skew and newly-introduced transitive dependencies, and mark them as quarantined in the presubmit context so tests run against a guarded environment. - Add a minimal Python-based presubmit shepherd service (scripts/presubmit_shepherd.py) that coordinates event aggregation for a short window (30s by default) and triggers a single CI job per batch. - Add documentation and runbook at docs/ci/presubmit-batching.md and docs/ci/dep-quarantine-runbook.md - Add a small set of unit and integration tests for the shepherd and quarantine detectors. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-4512) - [x] Tests added (unit + integration smoke) - [x] CI config updated - [x] Runbook and oncall playbook added - [x] Backwards compatible default behavior (batch window defaults to 0 in local dev) Why this matters: large teams were repeatedly spinning up duplicate CI runs for trivial commits which increased queue latency and CI cost. The quarantine ensures we don't silently accept risky transitive changes into release branches. Backwards compatibility & rollout: This is feature-flagged via a repo-level config (infra/ci/presubmit-config.yaml). New behaviour is off for the first 48 hours post-merge (automated toggle) to monitor telemetry. Related: ENG-4630 (dep curation initiative), SUP-2103 (customer-reported flaky presubmit). Migration notes: - Small ops change: add a webhook-secret entry to prod secrets store for the shepherd service. - Ops should monitor CI queue length and quarantine alerts for 72 hours after rollout. Rollout plan included in docs/ci/presubmit-batching.md.
Ola Henriksen: Nice direction — can you be explicit about how this interacts with branch-protection enforced status checks? We need to ensure quarantined PRs still block merges until manual review.
Maya Rivera: The presubmit shepherd marks quarantined PRs with a required status 'quarantine/manual-review' and we added steps in the GH workflow to fail that check. Branch protection mapping documented in docs/ci/dep-quarantine-runbook.md.
Priya Nair: The batched workflow looks good but CI cache keys might collide when multiple language stacks are involved. Suggest namespacing the cache by repo path + batch id.

Motivation: We saw a recurring production pattern where tenants that hit the system after a cold window (KV cache misses + cold model kernels) caused short-lived latency spikes and oscillatory shedding across ephemeral worker pools. Root cause analysis showed two compounding effects: (1) backpressure signals were emitted immediately and independently by each worker which amplified bursts into synchronized shedding, and (2) the retry/priority re-enqueue logic over-reacted to transient queue lag, immediately reintroducing load and causing near-immediate re-shed. This PR implements a runtime-level synchronizer and a light-weight cold-queue latency compensation to reduce oscillation and stabilize SLOs during cold/ephemeral traffic patterns. Summary of changes: - Add ephemeral backpressure synchronizer that aggregates per-worker pressure signals over a sliding window and emits a smoothed, weight-adjusted control signal to the tenant prioritizer. The synchronizer sits in the serving runtime and is opt-in per capacity pool. - Introduce cold-queue lag compensation that applies a transient holdoff and staggered requeue policy for requests that experience kernel cold starts or KV cache misses; reduces immediate re-enqueue flood on transient latency events. - Add a new runtime metric set (runtime.backpressure.sync.*) and two Grafana dashboard panels for visualizing synchronizer state, hysteresis, and compensator effectiveness. - Integrate an e2e stress test that reproduces the cold-start oscillation pattern (integration/tests/backpressure_e2e.yaml) and add unit tests for timing edge cases. - Document behavior and knobs in docs/observability/backpressure.md and add a short operations runbook for toggling the feature per-pool or rolling it back. Rollout plan: feature is behind a per-pool runtime flag defaulted to OFF. Rollout sequence: 1) Canary on a small set of non-critical pools with observability enabled; 2) Monitor SLOs and dashboard for 72 hours; 3) Gradual ramp to additional pools if stable. Rollback plan: flip per-pool flag to OFF and allow workers to drain (no code rollback required). Testing & validation: included unit and integration tests, local perf bench harness added to benchmark-lab with deterministic cold-start traces, and a staging soak run for 48 hours. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for synchronizer logic and timing - [x] Integration e2e reproducer + regression assertion - [x] Added metrics and dashboard panels - [x] Ops runbook and rollback procedure - [x] Security review (no surface changes) Known limitations & follow-ups: - The synchronizer currently uses an in-memory aggregation. We'll follow-up to add a bounded, replicated option for multi-node pools (ENG-7220). - Some microsecond-level latency introduced by the smoothing window; measured <1ms p50 in benchmarks but will be monitored. Impact and rationale: this change reduces shed/retry oscillation, lowers observed p95/p99 latency spikes during cold windows, and keeps tenant SLOs more predictable without impacting steady-state throughput. 
Aisha Kumar: Great isolation of signal aggregation — one question: can the smoothing window be tuned dynamically? Suggest a runtime knob and metric for window size.
Jordan Lee (author): Added a per-pool runtime knob (sync.window_ms) and exposed it as a metric. Updated docs to show recommended defaults for different pool sizes.
Tomás Álvarez: Integration test reproducer is helpful. I saw one flaky run due to clock skew in CI, recommended using a monotonic clock in the test harness.
Jordan Lee (author): Switched the test to the monotonic timer abstraction and re-ran CI — flakiness resolved.
Meera Shah: Ops runbook looks good; please add a dashboard alert for 'backpressure.sync.hysteresis_count' > 5 in 5m before full rollout.
Jordan Lee (author): Added the alert and an automated escalation note in the runbook.
payload.title: Ephemeral backpressure synchronizer and cold-queue latency compensation

payload.body:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets have experienced cascading reservation failures when a subset of nodes report transient allocation errors (OOM or driver hiccups). Those failures cause aggressive decommitment, which amplifies pressure and leads to mass throttling for tenants. This PR introduces a reservation failure isolation mechanism and a soft-quota fence to reduce blast radius and preserve throughput guarantees for unaffected tenants.

Summary of changes: implement a per-reservation finality window (short TTL) that treats transient allocation errors as isolated until a small failure budget is exhausted; introduce a soft-quota fence layer that saturates capacity reduction slowly using a circuit-state (open/half-open/closed) per-tenant quota; expose configuration flags and rollout gates; add telemetry and alerts that surface isolated vs systemic reservation failures.

Design notes: the finality window keeps a reservation in a "probation" state for the first N allocation failures (configurable, default N=3) before escalating to full decommit. During probation the autoscaler will: reduce newly-admitted concurrency by a configurable fraction (default 20%), avoid immediate slot reclamation from other tenants, and start a backoff timer per-reservation. The soft-quota fence is a lightweight token-exchange implemented in the reservation allocator: when overall pool utilization is high and a tenant's circuit is open, the allocator applies a staged floor reduction (soft fence) rather than an immediate hard revoke. The fence supports rate-limited bleed-down and a fast recovery path (half-open) for healthy traffic.

API & config: new flags in the dedicated config: --reservation-probation-count, --probation-concurrency-penalty, --soft-quota-fence-enabled, --fence-bleed-rate. A new status field was added to the tenant reservation protobuf: reservation_state={HEALTHY,PROBATION,QUARANTINED}. Backwards compatibility is preserved: if the new config is disabled, behavior defaults to current immediate-decommitment flow.

Telemetry & observability: added metrics: reservation_probation_enter_total, reservation_probation_exit_total, reservation_quarantine_total, soft_fence_bleed_bytes, tenant_fence_state_count{state}. Dashboards: a dedicated panel that separates isolated probation events from system-wide failures; alerts: >5% of reservations quarantined for >10m triggers P1.

Testing & rollout: unit tests for allocator state machine and quota fence transitions; integration tests that simulate transient allocation failures and assert throughput delta <5% for unaffected tenants; a canary rollout plan that enables probation only for 10% of pods, followed by 50% and global if no regression. The PR also includes a smoke test harness for failure-injection.

Deployment considerations: default configuration is conservative; operators can tune probation count and bleed rate for their fleet profile. The rollout plan recommends enabling telemetry first and verifying alert thresholds before widening the gate.

Related: references ENG-2426 for incident context and ENG-2489 for tenant SLA requirements.

Checklist:
- [x] design doc linked and reviewed
- [x] unit + integration tests added
- [x] telemetry and dashboards updated
- [x] canary rollout plan documented

Notes: this PR intentionally avoids changing long-term reservation accounting; it focuses on transient failure isolation and graceful degradation to keep the majority of tenants unaffected during short-lived node faults.
Evan Chu: Nice approach — can you clarify why we prefer a probation counter over exponential backoff?
Priya Shah: The probation counter keeps the failure handling bounded and makes it easier to reason about SLA windows. We add a backoff timer separately for admission; both are combined in the probation state.
Miguel Torres: Please add a metric for probation-age distribution so SREs can detect long-tail stuck reservations.
Priya Shah: Added reservation_probation_age_seconds histogram in the last commit.
Janelle Park: Integration tests look flakey on my run; I saw a timing race in the harness. Can we make the harness write deterministic logs?
Priya Shah: Fixed harness race by switching to mocked clock in integration tests; re-ran CI.
Miguel Torres: Approve after nit on config naming (probation -> probation_count) addressed.
Evan Chu: Approved. Recommend squash merge; leave detailed changelog entry in release notes.
Introduce reservation failure probation window and a soft-quota fence to reduce blast radius from transient allocation errors. Adds new config flags and telemetry. Default behavior is conservative; see docs for tuning guidance.
Enable telemetry panels and watch reservation_quarantine_total closely during canary. Start with --reservation-probation-count=3 and --fence-bleed-rate=0.05 per-minute. If tenant throughput degrades, reduce penalty or widen probation count.

Summary: Introduces a staggered toolchain initialization flow and a lightweight release prober to reduce noisy presubmit and release flakiness while improving developer feedback time. Motivation: CI latency and flakiness spike during full toolchain boot (terraform/pyenv/npm installs) on large changes. Teams reported long presubmit warmups and occasional release-blocking transient failures that are expensive to triage. This PR decomposes bootstrap into three phases (minimal, background, final) and adds a quiet release prober that runs a minimal set of deterministic sanity checks post-build. Key changes: 1) toolchain/bootstrap/phase-0.sh - minimal runtime needed for quick presubmit checks; 2) toolchain/bootstrap/phase-1-bg.sh - background fetch/restore of heavy devdeps with resilient retry/backoff; 3) toolchain/bootstrap/phase-2-final.sh - completes remaining optional setup and writes a lockstamp for reproducibility; 4) .github/workflows/presubmit.yml - split presubmit into fastpath (phase-0) and slowpath (phase-1 background scheduled) lanes; 5) tools/release/prober.py - quiet release prober that runs deterministic smoke tests and artifact checks and reports to CI telemetry without hard-blocking by default; 6) scripts/ci/warm-cache.sh - warmed caches for node/python layers; 7) tests/smoke/release_smoke.py - harness for prober. Commits summary: - c1a9fa2: introduce phase-0 bootstrap and fastpath presubmit lane; - 9b2d4e1: implement background phase-1 boot sequence and resume semantics; - e7f3b8c: add release prober, telemetry hooks, and non-blocking reporting; - 4a6d33a: docs and examples + adjust presubmit workflow conditions. Files changed (high level): toolchain/bootstrap/* (new scripts), .github/workflows/presubmit.yml (refactor), tools/release/prober.py (new), scripts/ci/warm-cache.sh (modest additions), tests/smoke/* (new), docs/dev/toolchain.md (clarify phases). Tests & CI: All presubmit checks passed after iterating on flaky network fetch logic. CI matrix: build: pass; lint: pass; unit-tests: pass; integration-smoke: pass; e2e-release-smoke: pass. Performance: Median presubmit cold-start reduced from ~240s to ~95s on sampled Linux runners; steady-state developer feedback improved in local trials. Rollout plan: staged opt-in across teams via repo-level boolean flag (ci.toolchain.staggered=true) then orgwide flip after 2 weeks of telemetry. The release prober is non-blocking by default; ops can set RELEASE_PROBER_ENFORCE=true in release workflows to escalate failures. Review conversation (high level): - Ava Martinez (reviewer): "Nice decomposition, can we make phase-1 background retries exponential and cap disk usage?" - Riley Chen (author): "Added exponential backoff with jitter and a disk footprint cap; background tasks will clean temp caches older than 7 days." - Jordan Patel (reviewer): "Please add a README for maintainers and make telemetry tag names consistent with ci.tooling.*" - Riley Chen (author): "Added docs/dev/toolchain.md and normalized telemetry keys to ci.tooling.toolchain.*" - Samir Gupta (reviewer): "Would like a toggle to opt-out specific repos during rollout." - Riley Chen: "Added ci.toolchain.staggered=false opt-out and an org-level opt-in recommendation in the PR description." Requested changes: enforce more aggressive timeout for phase-0 fetches (addressed), robust handling of intermittent network 429s (addressed by retry + exponential backoff), and clearer log lines for prober failures (addressed). Approvals: Ava Martinez approved, Jordan Patel approved after changes, Samir Gupta approved with minor comments. Merge notes: Squash-merged to main after last CI run succeeded. Post-merge actions: 1) monitor ci.telemetry.tooling.presubmit_latency for spike regressions; 2) run org-level opt-in on a canary team for one week; 3) schedule a follow-up PR to add a quiet-mode dashboard and automated throttle heuristics if background boot persists. Related: ENG-4527 (reduce presubmit TTR), ENG-4590 (quiet rollout validation). Impact: reduces developer iteration cost and isolates heavy devdeps from fast presubmit lanes while providing safer, low-noise release verification. Rollback plan: flip ci.toolchain.staggered=false and revert presubmit workflow change if unexpected regressions occur.
Introduce tiered toolchain bootstrap to reduce presubmit latency and add a non-blocking 'quiet' release prober that validates artifacts and flags regressions without blocking rollouts unless configured to escalate.

Motivation: During a recent multi-region incident we observed oscillatory regional failovers and repeated tenant quarantines caused by aggressive immediate SLO enforcements when transient latency spikes or KV pressure briefly crossed thresholds. This PR introduces two complementary runtime controls: a windowed SLO dampener (temporal smoothing of violation signals) and an evacuation sentinel (graceful, rate-limited node/tenant evacuation coordinator) to reduce flip-flopping and noisy circuit state changes.

What this changes (summary):
- Add a windowed SLO dampener that computes an exponentially-weighted moving percentile of latency/error signals per-tenant and per-region and requires sustained breach over a configurable window before triggering enforcement actions.
- Implement an evacuation sentinel that converts immediate hard-evacuate actions into a staged, tokenized evacuation process with a rate limiter and sticky-lease reconciliation to preserve KV locality where possible.
- Introduce a probation window for recently-evacuated tenants: short-lived soft-deprioritization to avoid immediate re-evacuation during recovery spikes.
- Instrumentation: new metrics (slo_dampener.windowed_p95, evacuation_sentinel.tokens_in_use, tenant_probation.state) and tracing spans to make decision boundaries auditable.
- Backwards-compatible config flags () and rollout knob via runtime-config to allow turning on dampener/evac-sentinel per-region.

Commits (high level):
- 1f8c2b2: core: add slo_dampener module with EWMA percentile state machine
- 2a9d5e1: controlplane: expose dampener config and rollout API to runtime-config service
- 4c3e7f9: runtime: evacuation_sentinel coordinator + tokenized evacuation protocol
- 7b1a9f0: kv: sticky-lease reconciliation and pause-on-preserve mode
- 9d0b4c4: telemetry: add metrics and tracing; dashboarding updates; alerts tuned
- b5f6a2d: tests: unit + integration harness for windowed breach scenarios and evacuation pacing

Files touched (high level):
- runtime/slo/dampener.rs (new)
- runtime/evac/sentinel.rs (new)
- controlplane/runtime_config/api.go (expose flags)
- kv/sticky_lease_manager.go (integration hooks)
- telemetry/metrics_registry.yml (metrics added)
- integration-tests/evacuation_playbooks/ (new scenarios)

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for dampener state transitions (stable) and sentinel token accounting (edge cases).
- Integration canary in us-west-2 for low-traffic tenants for 72hrs verifying: reduced double-evacuations, stable KV hit-rate during recovery, and no SLO regression for top 99% of tenants.
- Load tests with synthetic latency spikes show >60% reduction in region flip-flop events in the simulated environment.

Operational notes / rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind runtime-config flag: rollout to 10% of regional traffic for 48h, then 50%, then global after metrics verified.
- New dashboards created under "SLO Dampener / Evac Sentinel" with target thresholds to watch: dampener_suppressed_triggers, evacuation_token_throttle_rate, tenant_probation_count.
- Rollback: flip runtime-config to off; sentinel will drain tokens and finish in-flight reconciliations within a bounded interval (configurable), no hard state lost.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration scenarios
- [x] Telemetry wired
- [x] Docs: runtime-config flags and operator guide
- [x] Security review: no new privileged surfaces

Related: ENG-1892 (reduce regional failover oscillation), ENG-2045 (tenant-quarantine noise reduction).
Diego: Requested clearer invariants for when dampener marks a sustained breach — clarified threshold as configurable EWMA window and added unit tests.
Priya: Asked for eviction rate safety caps; added tokenized limiter and a hard ceiling tied to region capacity.
Noah: Ran integration canary and reported a KV-preserve regression in one corner case; fixed sticky-lease race by adding a short jitter and idempotency token.
Author replies: addressed all comments; re-ran canary and posted results in the PR thread.
Introduce a windowed SLO dampener to prevent reactive oscillations and an evacuation sentinel that stages node/tenant evacuations to avoid noisy failovers. Feature is rollout-gated and can be disabled via runtime-config.
Monitor new slo_dampener.* and evacuation_sentinel.* metrics for 72h; promote to additional regions if no regressions. Run a retrospective after full rollout to verify reduction in double-evacuations.
If an unexpected tenant SLA regression is observed, disable the dampener flag to fall back to immediate SLO enforcement. If evacuation tokens saturate unexpectedly, scale sentinel token bucket and investigate rapid node churn.

Motivation: SDK consumers reported inconsistent stream lifecycle hooks (onOpen/onChunk/onClose) and reauth behavior across Python/TS/Go. This caused subtle bugs when applications relied on deterministic reconnect semantics and led to duplicate reauth attempts under load. This PR unifies the consumer surface and reduces auth jitter by moving to a rotating short-lived token window with centralized jitter logic.

What I changed (single PR touching all three SDKs):
- Introduced StreamHookAdapter (Python: StreamHookAdapter, TS: StreamHookAdapter, Go: streamhook.Adapter) that normalizes onOpen/onData/onEnd/onError semantics and provides an optional rewindable Cursor helper.
- Added typed Cursor/Iterator helpers to expose a consistent, lazy iterator API for streaming consumers.

Motivation: multiple SDK customers reported cognitive overhead when handling credential rotation + streaming retries. This PR introduces a small, backward-compatible "session pivot" concept that centralizes credential lookup and exposes a single lightweight adapter surface for streaming consumers. Goal is to reduce cross-SDK mental friction, harmonize retry presets for transient auth errors, and tighten PullStream ergonomics so cross-language examples are closer to parity.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces a SessionPivot facade in the core SDK bindings that normalizes credential lookup and lease refresh semantics.
- Adds language-specific adapters: a thin Python 'SessionProxy', a TypeScript 'sessionPivot' helper, and a Go 'sessionadapter' with identical public intent.
- Reworks PullStream API ergonomics: smaller iterator primitive, clearer cancelation points, and an explicit resume() primitive for resumable consumers.
- Harmonizes retry preset names (auth_transient -> auth_recoverable) and attaches them to session refresh hooks so streaming consumers get coherent automatic reauth.
- Adds migration notes and compatibility adapters so consumers can opt-in incrementally.

Why this is safe: all adapters are additive and the original Polling/Token interfaces remain available. The new helpers are designed for opt-in migration (no forced break). A compatibility shim translates old retry config to the new preset names at runtime for existing clients.

Checklist: 
- [x] SessionPivot facade implemented in core SDK glue.
- [x] Python adapter + unit tests.
- [x] TypeScript helper + integration tests.
- [x] Go adapter + small e2e harness.
- [x] Docs / migration guide updated.
- [x] Version bumps: python -> 1.8.0, typescript -> 2.3.1, go -> 1.5.2.

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the retry semantics in "session_pivot/README.md" and the types in the TS helper (I preserved structural typing so it should be non-invasive). The Go adapter intentionally avoids reflection for simpler onboarding.

Release notes: Add new SessionPivot helpers for easier credential rotation handling across SDKs; minor ergonomics improvements to PullStream API; non-breaking migration shims.

Related: ENG-1459 (streaming auth ergonomic issues), ENG-1503 (retry preset consolidation).
Ethan Cole: Overall this looks good. Two requests: (1) add a short test that simulates a token expiry mid-stream and verifies resume() recovers without duplicating events, (2) call out the performance cost of an extra hop in the Python SessionProxy in the README.

Context: Customers operating across multiple jurisdictions need a robust, auditable mechanism to enforce data-residency and KMS usage constraints without scattering logic across services. This PR introduces a Residency Policy Orchestrator (RPO) service and a lightweight KMS Consent Fanout to centralize policy evaluation, evidence collection, and audit enrichment in the request path. Motivation: reduce duplication of residency logic, provide a single point for canarying stricter region-pin policies, and attach KMS consent proofs to audit events for downstream compliance tooling. Changes include: 1) New service: rpo/ - a small Go service that evaluates RBACv2-style residency policies, resolves tenant claims, and returns structured decisions plus proof metadata. 2) KMS consent fanout: a non-blocking fanout that records KMS provider selection and consent provenance to the audit enrichment pipeline. 3) Policy format: introduces a compact JSON policy spec (schemas/policy_v1.json) that supports per-tenant overrides, operator-scoped exceptions, and temporal bindings. 4) Middleware hooks: lightweight HTTP/GRPC middleware added to serving-runtime and api-gateway to call RPO and attach decision headers (X-RPO-Decision, X-KMS-Proof). 5) Observability: dashboards and new metrics (rpo.evaluations, rpo.cache_hits, kms.consent_fanout.latency) plus tracing integration. 6) Tests and migration: unit tests for policy evaluation, integration test that exercises the fanout with a mocked KMS consent provider, and a staged rollout plan (feature flag) to migrate traffic gradually. Rollout plan: - Feature flag controlled in config; default off for main traffic. - Canary rollout to 5% of traffic for a single region (us-west-2) for one week, with automated rollback on error-rate or decision-delta alerts. - After canary, enable in all regions and flip audit enrichment fully on. Backward compatibility: when the RPO is unavailable or feature flag off, middleware short-circuits to existing legacy residency checks. Security considerations: RPO signs decision blobs using the service key and includes non-replayable nonce/timestamps to be validated by audit pipeline. KMS fanout only records consent metadata (no secret material). Testing: - Local unit + CI (policy fuzz tests) - Integration harness with a fake KMS provider and audit queue - Load test shim shows <2ms added p95 on decision path at 1000 rps (when RPO cached). Related: ENG-987 (policy designer), SEC-204 (audit enrichment), SUP-442 (customer support ticket requesting per-tenant residency exceptions). Documentation: updated design doc (docs/residency-orchestrator.md) and API notes for middleware.
Liam Chen: Please ensure service key rotation is documented and the RPO validates notarized timestamps to avoid replay attacks.
Sofia Nguyen: Added a section to docs/residency-orchestrator.md about key rotation and nonce handling; RPO now includes timestamp+nonce in signed decision blob.
Priya Rao: I'm concerned about fanout backpressure when audit queue is down. Can we make the fanout best-effort and surface a metric?
Sofia Nguyen: Fanout is implemented as non-blocking; writes to audit queue are retried with bounded buffer and we emit kms.consent_fanout.dropped when buffer overflows. Documented behavior in middleware comments.
Marco Alvarez: Tests look good but add a regression test for legacy short-circuit when RPO times out.
Sofia Nguyen: Added integration test rpo_kms_integration_test.go which verifies timeout short-circuit and legacy path behavior.
Adds a residency policy orchestrator microservice and KMS consent fanout; enables staged rollout of region-pin enforcement and audit enrichment. Backwards compatible default policies retained.

Motivation: Intermittent production incidents showed that when clients send rapid small SSE chunks from heterogeneous networks we sometimes emit adjacent delimiter tokens that collide with partial JSON fragments, causing consumer libraries to mistake boundary-free fragments for complete JSON units. This resulted in malformed structured output, duplicated function/tool-call sentinels, and occasional token-order inversion when fragments were reordered by the proxy. This PR introduces a deterministic token-wrap reconciliation layer and a lightweight delimiter disambiguator to avoid mid-JSON collision while preserving low-latency streaming. Changes include: 1) a sequenced anchor inserted at chunk boundaries (non-user-visible, opt-in via runtime flag) to allow reassembly without altering event semantics, 2) a delimiter disambiguator that rewrites ambiguous trailing delimiter runs into an internal guarded form (transparent to OpenAI-compat consumers), 3) preservation ordering policy that tags function-call sentinel candidates with sequence stamps so interleaved fragments reserialize in canonical order, 4) additional unit and fuzz tests exercising reordered and split-UTF8 scenarios, and 5) a small runtime flag and migration note for Dedicated clusters to opt-in before rollout. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-1458) [x] unit tests added [x] integration test harness with proxy reorder simulation [x] benchmark smoke to verify <1ms median added latency under typical loads [x] compatibility shim preserves existing OpenAI-compat tokens. Impact/risk: low surface-area change to stream emitter; could affect custom proxy middleware that depends on exact byte-level framing. Rollout: staged feature-flagged rollout with Canary and Dedicated opt-in, automatic fallback to old path on runtime errors. Related: ENG-1458, PRs: #361112 (stream-test-harness), #364001 (sse-proxy-sim).
Reviewer Mateo: Found a race in the sequence-stamp propagation when a fragment is dropped by the proxy; suggested tagging with per-request monotonic counter instead of timestamp; Author Ava: switched to per-request monotonic stamp and added test simulating dropped fragments. Reviewer Priya: asked about Dedicated upgrade implications and KMS key handling for private clusters; Author: documented opt-in flag and fallback behavior, added migration note. Reviewer Samir: requested a small benchmark measurement for median p99 latency; Author: added bench-smoke job and confirmed <1ms median delta; approved after minor cleanup. CI initially failed on lint; fixed and reran; final CI green.
Fixes cases where SSE chunk boundary collisions could produce malformed partial JSON or duplicate function-call sentinels by introducing token-wrap reconciliation and delimiter disambiguation. Opt-in rollout for Dedicated clusters; no API changes for hosted customers.

Context and motivation:
This PR implements an SLO-focused admission smoothing layer (ephemeral throttle harmonizer) and a small but critical standby drain probe that prevents mass KV cache drains during regional failover. We shipped a small change to circuit reopen logic to stop rapid flip-flops observed under surge conditions (root cause seen in recent incident SUP-3321). Goal is: reduce tenant-level oscillation, protect downstream serving nodes from simultaneous heavy KV work, and provide richer telemetry so on-call can reason about reopen events.

What it changes (high level):
- runtime/admission/harmonizer.go: new SLO-aware harmonizer that aggregates short-term token usage and produces a smoothed per-tenant admission score. Uses exponential smoothing with configurable alpha and a soft cap window; integrates with existing admission API.
- runtime/drain/standby_probe.go: probe that runs during region-standby transitions; verifies KV cache health and delays non-critical drains until probe passes or soft timeout.
- runtime/circuit/reopen_guard.go: per-tenant cooldown (backoff multiplier + jitter) to avoid reopen flapping; records reopen_reason and reopen_attempts into telemetry.
- operator/helm/templates/configmap.yaml: new config knobs to tune harmonizer alpha, probe timeout, and reopen cooldown values.
- tools/eval/promptset_stability.yaml: test harness additions to simulate bursty tenant traffic and verify harmonizer behavior.
- docs/observability/reopen-telemetry.md: docs for the new telemetry fields and alert guidance.
- release/2026-02-hotfix/*: minimal backport for release branch with opt-in flags.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for harmonizer smoothing and timeout behavior.
- [x] Integration scenario in eval harness that reproduces incident-like oscillation and demonstrates improvement.
- [x] Added metrics/traces and dashboard snippets for reopen events.
- [x] Backported opt-in hotfix for release channel and documented escape hatch.
- [x] SRE review and oncall runbook entry drafted.

Commits (summary):
- c1a2b3f: initial harmonizer implementation and basic tests
- d4e5f6a: add standby drain probe and integrate with region state transitions
- f7a8b9c: reopen cooldown + telemetry fields; update dashboards
- a1b2c3d: helm chart knobs + backport to release branch
- b2c3d4e: test harness scenarios and flaky-test fixes

Files changed (high level list):
- runtime/admission/harmonizer.go (+270 lines)
- runtime/admission/harmonizer_test.go (+120 lines)
- runtime/drain/standby_probe.go (+98 lines)
- runtime/circuit/reopen_guard.go (+65 lines)
- operator/helm/templates/configmap.yaml (+12 lines)
- tools/eval/promptset_stability.yaml (+34 lines)
- docs/observability/reopen-telemetry.md (+210 lines)
- release/2026-02-hotfix/patch.yaml (+56 lines)

Review conversation (selected):
- Samir Patel (reviewer): "This addresses the production flip-flop we've seen. Two asks: 1) add a metric for harmonizer smoothing lag so SRE can detect stuck state, 2) ensure probe can't block critical KV drains during progressive rollout."
- Priya (author): "Added harmonizer.smoothing_lag_gauge and a probe fast-path for critical drains (configurable). Both changes are in the last commit a1b2c3d."
- Elena Kirov (reviewer): "Unit tests look good, but the integration harness needs an assertion on request latency tail to ensure we didn't regress P99. Can you add a regression assert?"
- Priya: "Added latency tail assertion in tools/eval/promptset_stability.yaml; CI shows this scenario improves P99. See b2c3d4e."
- Marcus Li (approver): "Read through the helm knobs. Good opt-in defaults. Approving for merge after CI passes. Consider follow-up to expose harmonizer knobs per-tenant via console (tracked ENG-4210)."

CI and rollout notes:
- CI summary: unit (pass), integration (initially failed due to test ordering), integration rerun (pass), lint (pass), e2e (skipped on hotfix backport). One flaky test (tools/eval/promptset_stability) retried once and green.
- Canary plan: staged rollout behind feature flag 'harmonizer.enabled' and 'standby_probe.enabled'. Canary on a small non-critical namespace for 24h, monitor harmonizer.smoothing_lag_gauge, reopened_circuit_count, kv_drain_duration, and request p99. If reopen rate increases unexpectedly, flip feature flag off — the harmonizer is designed as non-blocking and can be toggled without restarts.

Why this is safe as a hotfix:
- The change is opt-in by default (harmonizer.enabled=false in release hotfix), the reopen cooldown only adds a conservative backoff (no functional change unless enabled), and the standby probe defers only non-critical drains behind a soft timeout. The backported patch keeps defaults unchanged and exposes knobs so SRE can enable gradually.

Follow-ups / TODOs:
- ENG-4210: Console controls for per-tenant harmonizer tuning and telemetry dashboards.
- ENG-4232: Evaluate cost impact of harmonizer on batching effectiveness and provide guidance in Redwood Optimize.
- Small perf tuning on harmonizer loop to reduce goroutine wakeups; tracked in follow-up branch.

Merge outcome:
- Merge method: squash and merge.
- Merge commit summary: "squash: introduce ephemeral throttle harmonizer and standby drain probe; reopen cooldown; config knobs; tests; docs"
- Post-merge action: backport applied to release/2026-02-hotfix and flag defaults set to false. Oncall runbook updated under docs/ops/oncall/harmonizer.md.

- traces: span names 'harmonizer.evaluate' and 'standby_probe.run' with attributes tenant_id and region
- logs: reopen_reason logged with structured field reopen_reason and reopen_attempts

If there are any concerns about rollout risk or additional telemetry needs we should address them before enabling harmonizer in production namespaces. Overall, this PR is scoped to reduce oscillation during regional load perturbations and to prevent mass KV drains during failover windows while providing SRE with the signals needed to diagnose failures.
- Introduce 'ephemeral throttle harmonizer' to smooth tenant-level admission throttles across regions and reduce oscillation.
- Add 'standby drain probe' to avoid KV cache drain storms during regional failover.

payload.body:
Context: After merging the region normalization work, we noticed intermittent drops in hourly unit economics aggregates where a small (but non-trivial) slice of metering rows had region unset or had a value that didn’t map (e.g. legacy colo labels, nulls from older gateway paths, or "unknown" emitted during partial outages). The aggregation job used an INNER JOIN to the canonical region mapping table, which caused those rows to be dropped entirely. This under-counted output_tokens and made $/1M output tokens look artificially worse/better depending on which spend inputs were present for that hour.

What this PR does: Update the unit economics aggregation query and the region mapping helper to be null-safe and non-dropping: (1) switch the join to LEFT JOIN, (2) COALESCE to a canonical region value of "unknown" when mapping fails, and (3) emit an explicit counter for unmapped rows so we can alert on drift instead of silently losing data. Also adds a small regression test covering null + unmapped region values.

Why this is safe: The change only affects how we assign the region dimension for rows that previously disappeared; mapped rows are unchanged. Downstream views already treat region as a dimension with a bounded value set, and adding "unknown" is within our cardinality guardrails.

Test plan: Run unit tests for the query builder + add a warehouse integration test fixture that includes null and unmapped region inputs; validate that output_tokens totals match pre-join totals and that the "unknown" bucket contains the expected rows.

Rollout: Deploy with the next scheduled analytics job release; monitor (a) unit_econ.region_mapping.unmapped_rows, (b) hourly completeness checks, and (c) reconciliation deltas vs billing totals. If the unmapped counter spikes, we’ll investigate upstream emitters rather than letting the aggregator hide the issue.
Before:
  ...
  FROM metering_events e
  JOIN dim_region_map m
    ON e.raw_region = m.raw_region

After:
  ...
  FROM metering_events e
  LEFT JOIN dim_region_map m
    ON e.raw_region = m.raw_region
  -- Preserve rows even if mapping is missing; bucket them explicitly.
  SELECT COALESCE(m.canonical_region, 'unknown') AS region,
         ...
  
  -- Emit unmapped rows metric for visibility.
  unmapped = (m.canonical_region IS NULL)
  metrics.increment('unit_econ.region_mapping.unmapped_rows', 1, { raw_region: COALESCE(e.raw_region, 'null') })
Logan Wright (review): Good catch. Can you confirm this doesn’t change mapped rows and only affects the missing mapping cases? Also please add an explicit metric so we can alert when this starts happening.

Mei Lin (author): Confirmed. The SELECT now uses COALESCE(m.canonical_region, 'unknown') but for mapped rows m.canonical_region is unchanged. Added unit_econ.region_mapping.unmapped_rows counter with raw_region tag bounded to 'null' or the raw string (still low cardinality in practice, but let me know if we want to hash).

Caleb Johnson (review): +1 on surfacing visibility. We should avoid high-cardinality raw_region tags. Can we bucket raw_region into {null, empty, unknown, other}?

Mei Lin (author): Updated. Tag value is now one of ['null', 'empty', 'unknown', 'unmapped_other']. We still log the exact raw_region to structured logs for debugging, but not as a metric label.

Cole Summers (review): Does this impact reconciliation vs billing totals? We’ll see token totals increase for hours that previously dropped rows.

Mei Lin (author): Yes, it will increase output_tokens in those hours (more accurate). This should reduce reconciliation deltas. I added a note in the PR description + the runbook about the 'unknown' region bucket.

Sean Gallagher (review): Please ensure we don’t silently treat unknown as a real region in dashboards. Any UI impact?

Mei Lin (author): No UI changes here, but the dashboard already treats dimensions as enumerations. 'unknown' will show up in the breakdown tables; we can decide later if we want to hide it by default. For now, it’s better than dropping data.

Approvals: Logan Wright approved. Caleb Johnson approved after metric label change. Sean Gallagher approved.
Fixes undercounting in unit economics aggregates by retaining rows with null/unmapped region and bucketing them into region='unknown'. Adds an unmapped-row metric for alerting and a regression test.
payload.title: Bugfix: preserve rows when region mapping is null/unknown in unit economics aggregation

payload.body:
Motivation: Bring the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer closer to parity while improving streaming resilience for tool/function outputs and preserving per-token logprobs for stop demarcation. Several customers reported mismatches between framed JSON tool outputs and legacy clients that expect compact deltas; this PR introduces a backwards-compatible coalescing mode and a role-aliasing layer to reduce downstream mapping complexity.

What this PR does: Implements a three-part compatibility strategy: (1) stop coalescing modes (hard|soft|legacy) that determine how stop tokens are applied and how partial tokens are attributed to logprobs during streaming; (2) a role_aliases mapping in the v1 adapter so callers can provide aliases (e.g. assistant -> system-assistant) while the runtime maps them back to canonical roles for scoring and safety checks; (3) framed JSON chunk batching for tool/function outputs with optional compact-delta fallback for older clients. Also: adds thorough integration tests and updates the Python/TS SDK adapters.

Changes included (high level): - adapter: v1/chat_completions adapter param parsing and new "stop_coalesce_mode" flag - runtime: streaming coalescer that tracks token boundaries and retains token-level logprob attribution when stops are encountered mid-chunk - tool-output: framed JSON slice metadata (slice_id, seq, eof) and a compact_delta_fallback toggle - SDKs: Python and TypeScript wrappers expose new param mappings and provide automatic client-side fallback heuristics - docs: migration guide and examples for new flags and role_aliases mapping

Checklist: - [x] API adapter param mapping and validation - [x] Runtime coalescer + perf tests - [x] SDK bindings (python + ts) - [x] Integration tests for streaming + tool handoff - [x] Docs + migration guide - [x] Security review (audit of role alias resolution)

Commit summary: - add v1 stop_coalesce_mode parsing and validation - implement streaming coalescer with token-logprob tethering - add framed JSON slice envelope and compact-delta fallback - expose role_aliases mapping in v1 adapter and SDKs - add integration tests and test fixtures for fragmented tool outputs - docs: add openai compat migration / examples

Changed areas/files (representative): - src/api/v1/chat_completions_adapter.rs - runtime/streaming/coalescer.cpp - runtime/streaming/coalescer.h - sdk/python/redwood/openai_compat.py - sdk/typescript/src/openaiCompatAdapter.ts - docs/openai_compatibility/migration_chat_completions.md - tests/integration/test_chat_parity_stream.py - tests/fixtures/framed_tool_slices/*.json - .github/workflows/stream-integration.yml

Testing & QA: Ran unit tests and the integration stream harness locally and in CI. The integration/stream-harness showed a transient failure on the first run due to test timing; a rerun passed. Added a new e2e scenario that simulates a mid-chunk stop token and asserts that token-level logprobs are attributed to the prior token and that the framed JSON slices reconstruct correctly when reassembled. Performance impact: coalescer adds negligible CPU overhead in hot paths; added microbenchmarks to perf-canary.

Migration notes: - Default behavior remains legacy-compatible (stop_coalesce_mode=legacy). Administrators can enable soft or hard modes per-route to tighten stop enforcement or prefer minimal token chopping. - role_aliases is optional; when present the adapter will map incoming role names into canonical roles before applying safety checks. Motivation: Users across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs reported inconsistent streaming backpressure hints and divergent retry semantics that cause duplicate partial responses and suboptimal batching. This PR converges three concerns: 1) a unified, explicit backpressure/throttle hint model; 2) a small family of retry profiles with consistent semantics across SDKs; 3) an ergonomic fluent builder API for streaming options to make common patterns simple and reduce misuse. Scope: changes touch the three SDK packages, a small protocol header for optional hints, updated docs and end-to-end tests. Backwards compatibility: new headers and structured options are optional. When callers use the old ad-hoc flags the SDK translates them to the new model so there are no breaking runtime changes for existing customers. Design summary: - Introduce StreamingThrottleHint (Soft|Hard|Adaptive + numeric target tokens_per_sec) to express consumer preferences. - Introduce RetryProfile (fast-retry, conservative-windowed, idempotent-only) with well-defined backoff and idempotency rules. - Add FluentStreamingOptions builder in each SDK to compose throttle + retry + diagnostics (e.g., progress callbacks, chunk policy). - SDKs annotate outgoing requests with X-Stream-Hint and X-Stream-Retry-Profile when available (opaque, opt-in). Implementation notes: - Python: new streaming.builder.StreamingOptions class with chainable methods and a from_legacy_flags adapter. - TypeScript: StreamingOptionsBuilder exported from client/streaming and used by examples and docs. - Go: StreamingOptions struct + option funcs to follow idiomatic functional options pattern. - Small runtime change: server accepts the new optional headers; when present runtime will attempt to honor Soft hints and prefer batching heuristics for Adaptive. Migration notes: - Existing apps keep working. - Recommended migration: replace ad-hoc kwargs with StreamingOptions builder to get predictable batching and retries. - Release notes include code snippets showing before/after for each language. Tests: unit + integration harness added to verify: 1) throttle hint propagates through gateway and affects batching decisions in the perf canary; 2) retry profile semantics maintain idempotency during streaming aborts; 3) cross-language parity tests that exercise identical behavior across py/ts/go. Checklist: - [x] Spec and design doc linked in Linear ENG-1987 - [x] Implementations in py/ts/go - [x] Unit tests + integration tests - [x] Docs + snippets updated - [x] Version bumps for SDK releases - [x] CI green (flaky linter fix for TS was addressed) Migration snippet (Python) BEFORE: client.stream(prompt, max_tokens=256, retry=True, backoff=0.5) AFTER: opts = StreamingOptions().with_throttle_soft(tokens_per_sec=120).with_retry_profile('conservative-windowed') client.stream(prompt, max_tokens=256, options=opts)

Motivation: Our dependency-rotation process has relied on ad-hoc scripts and manual windows which causes noisy PRs and occasional infra churn during releases. This change introduces a lightweight scheduler + coordinator for rotating non-critical transitive deps, a pre-release smoke-check workflow that runs a small matrix of critical integration paths before tagging releases, and a small refactor that normalizes lint entrypoints across TS/Python/Go packages to reduce CI surface area.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds .github/actions/dep-rotation-scheduler.yml: a scheduled action that triggers a coordinator which selects eligible modules for rotation and opens atomic PRs with clear risk metadata. Rotations are rate limited and honor per-repo exclusion lists.
- Adds .github/workflows/release-smoke.yml: a lightweight workflow that runs on release candidates and validates 3 critical flows (API compile, hosted runtime smoke, basic e2e for console). It is intentionally small and fast (~6-8m).
- Introduces scripts/dep-rotate/scheduler.py: coordinator logic and dry-run mode used in PRs for visibility.
- Unifies lint entrypoints by moving from multiple bespoke scripts to tools/lint/entrypoint.ts and small wrappers in package.json; this removes duplicate environment bootstrapping across repos.
- Updates ci/README.md with operator guidance, rotation windows, and rollback steps.

Checklist:
- [x] Scheduler dry-run mode implemented and tested locally
- [x] Release smoke workflow validated in staging (reran once after transient timeout)
- [x] Lint entrypoint smoke-tested across python, ts, go packages
- [x] Added Linear tasks and documentation for SRE/operators

Risk & mitigation: Rotations could introduce dependency incompatibilities. The scheduler uses a staged rollout: always opens PRs as drafts and annotates risk (major bump vs patch), runs dependency-compatibility CI job before marking PR ready. Releases run the smoke-check before final tag. Operators can opt-out repos via .github/dep-rotation-ignore.yml.

Why not a monolithic bot: We intentionally split the scheduler (coordinator) from the PR runner so operators can inspect dry-run output and hand-off high risk rotations rather than having an automated merge. This keeps noise low while enabling automation for low-risk updates.

Motivation: On high-cardinality workloads we observed a lot of alert noise from short-lived token cost spikes and flapping alerts. Existing sampling and alerting thresholds amplify noise for low-volume tenants and obscure real regressions for mid-volume workloads. This PR implements a combined approach: per-SLO hysteresis windows to reduce sensitivity to transient bursts, and a quorum-based token sampler that ensures sampled traces reflect cohort-level behavior rather than single outliers. Goals: 1) reduce alert flapping for transient token bursts; 2) preserve signal for sustained regressions; 3) keep downstream storage and index costs bounded with adaptive sampling; 4) expose tuning knobs in Console and a migration plan for existing alerts. Design summary: - Hysteresis controller: each SLO route maintains a small state machine (stable->warming->violated->recovering) with configurable enter/exit windows expressed in seconds and minimum sustained token-rate percent. The controller uses exponentially-weighted windows to avoid hard re-eval cadence. - Quorum token sampler: instead of per-invocation independent sampling, the sampler groups recent invocations by route+tenant+prompt-shape window and applies a quorum rule (sample when >=N invocations in window OR when median token cost exceeds X percentile). Quorum threshold is adaptive based on tenant volume (low-volume tenants can use a lower quorum to retain signal). - Integration: the sampler tags traces with sampling_reason and quorum_id; the alert pipeline consumes those tags and performs quorum-aware aggregation for alert evaluation and incident grouping. - Backcompat: defaults preserve current sampling rates; behavior opt-in via a feature flag and cluster-wide rollout plan described in docs. Implementation highlights: - New package src/observability/sampling/quorum_sampler.rs implements the grouping index, quorum heuristics, and TTL eviction; heavy use of probabilistic reservoir sketches to keep memory bounded. - Alerts middleware telemetry/alerts/hysteresis.go adds SLO lifecycle state and emits state_transition spans to tracing. - Console doc docs/observability/token-sampling.md documents knobs and recommended defaults. - Helm chart value changes infra/helm/values.yaml add feature flag and tunables. - Tests: tests/sampling/integration_test.go covers behavior across volume tiers; loadbench results included below. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed with SREs and Console PM - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs updated - [x] Feature flag gating and rollout plan included - [x] Performance bench and memory check Results and rationale: - On a synthetic mixed workload (10k tenants, Pareto distribution), average alert count per hour dropped by 46% for routes with high short-lived bursts; true positive detection latency for sustained regressions remained within 5% of baseline. - Quorum sampler memory budget measured ~0.9MB per 10k active route-tenants (within our budgets); CPU overhead on sampling path measured +3.2% p90. - Uncovered and fixed an edge-case where very low-volume tenants would never sample; added adaptive floor to quorum threshold. Rollout plan: 1) Canary enable in staging for top-10 noisy routes; 2) 1% of production traffic with realtime dashboard; 3) 25% ramp after 48h, 100% after verification. Metrics to watch: alert-frequency, alert-flapping-rate, sampled-trace-rate, sampler-memory-usage, slo-state-transition-rate. Migration: existing alerts that use raw per-invocation counts should be migrated to quorum-aware aggregates; migration helper CLI in tools/obs-migrate included.

Maya Chen: Added adaptive floor and adjusted doc guidance; low-volume fallback now uses min_quorum=1 after 5m of inactivity.

Maya Chen: Added eviction chaos test in integration_test.go and annotated expected memory dispersion.

Introduce adaptive SLO hysteresis and quorum-based token sampling to reduce alert noise from transient token bursts. Feature gated; default behaviour unchanged. Includes Console docs and migration helper CLI.

Motivation: As we run more shadow traffic experiments at scale, individual cohorts that overlap (by user, session or feature flag) create noisy signals that delay safe promotions. This PR introduces 'shadow-tiling' — a deterministic tiling scheme that partitions shadow traffic into cohort-convergent slices and wires a rollback-oracle that recommends automated short-circuit rollbacks if multi-signal divergence is detected.

What this PR does: - Introduces a server-side deterministic tiling algorithm which maps incoming requests into shadow tiles based on a convergent hash (combining user_id, country, and experiment_salt). Tiles are stable under resharding and respect session affinity. - Adds a cohort convergence evaluation step to the rollout controller: each tile reports metric deltas (latency, error rate, quality regressions), and the controller aggregates with outlier-resistant statistics (median-of-means) per-cohort. - Implements a rollback-oracle that watches multi-metric divergence patterns and recommends / auto-applies short rollbacks when configured. The oracle uses a simple credit system so transient spikes don't cause oscillation. - Adds observability surfaces: per-tile metrics, convergence score, oracle decisions, and a replayable audit trail for post-mortem. - Exposes rollout.spec.shadowTiling.{enabled,shard_count,convergence_window,credit_budget,auto_rollback} in the API and documents defaults.

Checklist: - [x] Core tiling + mapping implemented in rollout controller and router layer - [x] Aggregation & median-of-means implementation with unit tests - [x] Rollback-oracle with config and safety credits - [x] Console dashboard panels and telemetry hooks - [x] Backwards-compatible API additions (feature-gated) - [x] End-to-end smoke test against the perf-canary harness

Compatibility notes: The changes are additive. Existing rollouts remain unchanged unless shadowTiling is enabled. We ship a default conservative budget for auto_rollback=false in order to let operators adopt slowly.

Related: ENG-3124 (cohort signalling improvements), ENG-4198 (rollback automation roadmap).

Aisha Rahman (2026-02-26): Added docs section and a new simulation test (tests/e2e/shadow_tiling_smoke_test.go) that replays bursts to validate the credit logic. See latest commit 1b9c3da.
Dana Ortiz (2026-03-01): Ran the perf-canary with 10k req/s mix. Router changes added ~0.6ms median p50 on shadow-enabled paths — acceptable but please ensure the console highlights when shadow-tiling is enabled to avoid operator surprises.

Context: CI feedback latency and noisy presubmit runs have been a recurring developer friction point. This PR introduces a lightweight presubmit prober that detects change scope and schedules a minimal set of lint/test shards in a stage-aware fashion, plus a small 'release adapter' shim to decouple release hooks from strong CI invariants. The goal is to reduce developer iteration time without sacrificing coverage.

What this PR does (high level): 
- Adds a presubmit prober service that inspects changed paths, runs a fast heuristic to pick required lint/test profiles, and emits a scoped job matrix.
- Splits lint into stage-aware profiles (quickstyle, type-only, full-lint) to enable fast fastpath feedback.
- Introduces a release adapter that runs final release-orchestration steps asynchronously and provides a stable API for release tooling so main CI is not blocked by transient release hooks.
- Provides docs, devcontainer scripts, and a small golang-based prober binary for hermetic local runs.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add presubmit prober service and CLI (ci/prober). 
- [x] Update .github workflows to use the prober output for presubmit matrices. 
- [x] Split lint profiles and add quickstyle runner. 
- [x] Add release adapter shim and backward-compatible env flags. 
- [x] Add observability: presubmit probe metrics and quickpath hit rate. 
- [x] Run dogfood on redwood/* and redwood-sdk-* repos for 48h.

Testing notes: 
- Dogfooded across core monorepo for two working days; observed median presubmit latency drop from 12m -> 5m for small changes. Quickpath (quickstyle only) hit rate ~42% on typical PRs. 
- CI runs: full integration and nightly smoke passed. A lint runner flake in early iterations was fixed by tightening the module cache initialization. 

Rollout plan: 
1. Merge to main behind feature flag PROBER_ENABLED=false. 
2. Enable for SDK repos (redwood-sdk-python/ts/go) for 72h and monitor quickpath metrics. 
3. Gradual opt-in across monorepo by team using per-repo config. 
4. Remove flag after 4 weeks of stable metrics.

Backward compatibility: release adapter uses environment opt-ins and keeps existing release hooks unmodified unless RELEASE_ADAPTER=enabled is set.

Motivation and tradeoffs: This PR trades a small amount of additional infra (prober binary + metrics) for large developer productivity gains. We preserve safety by keeping slow full runs as fallback and by retaining the previous full-matrix behavior behind a flag.

Related: ENG-1729 (presubmit speed initiative), ENG-2104 (release automation hygiene), SUP-981 (customer incident prompting quicker release decoupling).

Summary: Add compatibility shims and resilient reassembly logic for the OpenAI Responses v15 streaming shape. This PR improves tool/function-call handshake semantics, preserves determinism/seed hints across fragmented stream frames, and implements a fragmentation-resilient reassembly layer so that large structured outputs and tool call payloads are robustly reconstructed even under partial retransmits or chunk reordering. Motivation: customers running structured tool-calling workloads observed missing tool arguments or truncated JSON objects when gateway/network proxies produced out-of-order frames or when the streaming adapter split tokens mid-JSON attribute. v15 of the OpenAI Responses shape introduces a few new metadata flags (seed_hint, rng_hint, response_annotations) which we need to forward without mutation; it also allows tool-call frames to arrive interleaved with assistant delta frames. This work prevents silent data loss and preserves deterministic seeds passed from upstream.

What changed (high-level): - Introduced a StreamFrameSequence reassembler in the openai-adapter that tracks per-stream fragment ids and assembly windows; supports idempotent reassembly on duplicate fragments. - Added a toolcall handshake protocol: HEAD/ACK pair encoded as small control frames so receiver can atomically mark tool invocation boundaries before parsing. - Propagate seed_hint and rng_hint verbatim from incoming v15 frames to Redwood Responses internal envelope and to log traces. - Preserve annotations and metadata_passthrough map; added tests and logging around annotation collisions. - Added a compatibility shim for older downstream clients: if a downstream sends a legacy toolcall frame we synthesize v15-compatible control frames to avoid parsing errors. - Observability: new trace spans for reassembly time and a labeled metric for fragmented messages reassembled_count.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-5123) - [x] Unit tests for reassembler and handshake - [x] Integration test: chunk-reorder + duplicate-fragment scenarios - [x] E2E test against openai-bridge fixture v15 - [x] Backward-compatible: falls back to previous behavior when fragmentation not detected - [x] Release notes entry - [x] Ops rollout plan added

Commit summary: - a1b3c2e: add StreamFrameSequence reassembler + unit tests - d4f7b8a: implement toolcall HEAD/ACK control frames and parsing hooks - e9f0a12: pass-through seed_hint/rng_hint and wire annotations; update tracing - f2c3d45: integration tests for reordered/duplicated fragments - 9b1a7fd: docs and release-notes; minor lint fixes

Files changed (high-level): - openai-adapter/stream/reassembler.py (new) - openai-adapter/stream/handshake.py (new) - openai-adapter/handlers.py (modifications to parsing/dispatch) - responses-proxy/compat/shims_v15.py (compat shim for legacy toolcalls) - telemetry/tracing.py (new spans) - tests/integration/test_stream_fragmentation.py - docs/compat/openai_v15.md (compatibility notes)

Review conversation (highlights): - Diego Rivera (reviewer): "Nice isolation of reassembly logic. Two nits: rename get_window -> current_window; add an assertion on fragment sequence monotonicity." - Author (Aisha): "Renamed and added assertion; assertion guarded behind debug flag to avoid perf impact in prod." - Mei Chen (reviewer): "Concern: head/ack control frames increase control surface — how do we avoid DOS by sending many small HEAD frames?" - Author: "Handshake includes a per-connection rate limit; we treat excessive HEAD frames as malformed and metric it. Added tests.`" - Lucas Ortega (approver): "Integration tests caught an edge-case with duplicate fragments; LGTM after addressing the post-merge follow-up for improved metrics labels." - Ops (comment): "Needs a slow rollout — fragmentation edge cases correlate with older LB versions; will coordinate canary on Dedicated clusters."

CI / Checks: - unit-tests: pass - integration-tests: pass - lint: pass (one auto-fix) - benchmark-smoke: pass - security-scan: pass

Merge outcome: Squash merged to main (merge commit: squash/72645-openai-v15-toolcall-frag-resilience). Merged by Lucas Ortega on 2026-02-22.

Deployment & Rollout: - Canary rollout to 5% of Hosted region-us-east first, monitor reassembled_count and toolcall_error_rate. - If reassembled_count increases above baseline (expected during canary), validate that toolcall success rate increases and deterministic seeds are present in traces. - Ops will pause and rollback if toolcall_error_rate rises > 2x baseline for 10m.

Backward compatibility notes: - Default behavior unchanged for non-fragmented streams. - Legacy toolcall frames are auto-upgraded by the shim to avoid client changes. - The seed_hint and rng_hint are forwarded but not interpreted by Redwood runtime; they are available to eval/trace tooling.

Follow-ups (tracked as Linear): - ENG-5180: Add structured-output schema validator for reassembled payloads - ENG-5234: Expose reassembly diagnostics in Console per-route tab - ENG-5299: Hardening for very large multi-MB toolcall payloads (chunking policies)

Release notes: Adds v15 OpenAI Responses compatibility: robust streaming reassembly, improved tool/function-call handshake, and metadata passthrough for seed/rng hints. This reduces truncated toolcall payloads and preserves determinism annotations across the gateway.

Adds jurisdiction-aware routing for KMS requests, a consent coordinator service for cross-region key usage, RBAC v2 policy templates for region-scoped operator bindings, and audit header normalizers. Backwards-compatible; requires config toggles for rollout.
[Summary] Add a small orchestration layer (kms-consent-coordinator) and accompanying RBAC v2 policy templates to enforce per-tenant region pinning for KMS usage, plus an audit header clarity sanitizer to make residency decisions auditable and debuggable. | [Motivation] Customers running Private and Dedicated deployments require deterministic behavior when tenant traffic needs to be pinned to a geographic jurisdiction (data residency) while allowing safe fallbacks to alternate KMS providers when consent is present. Previously, routing logic and KMS consent checks were scattered across services and produced noisy audit entries; this PR centralizes consent negotiation, makes routing deterministic, and produces a compact, signed audit envelope. | [What changed] 1) services/kms-consent-coordinator/: new lightweight HTTP service that performs a deterministic consent handshake between operator claims, tenant residency profile, and available KMS providers. Exposes /v1/consent-check and /v1/tokenize endpoints. 2) pkg/authorizer/policy_templates/region_scoped_bindings.go: new RBAC v2 templates to create operator-scoped, region-bound role bindings with TTL and audit annotations. 3) audit/proxy/clarity_sanitizer.go: middleware that canonicalizes residency headers (X-Resident-Region, X-KMS-Origin) and emits an audit envelope field audit.residency_hint for downstream indexing. 4) tools/migrate_region_bindings.py: migration helper to translate legacy tenancy labels into new RBAC templates. 5) integration/region_routing_e2e.test: new e2e harness that simulates multi-KMS environments and asserts deterministic routing and audit envelope contents. 6) docs/ops/kms-region-consent.md: operational runbook and feature flags for staged rollout. | [Commits] - Add kms-consent-coordinator service and tests - Implement region-scoped RBAC templates and migration script - Add audit clarity sanitizer and telemetry - Wire-up integration tests and CI job - Fix linting and type issues reported by reviewers | [Files of interest] services/kms-consent-coordinator/server.go, services/kms-consent-coordinator/consent_handler.go, pkg/authorizer/policy_templates/region_scoped_bindings.go, audit/proxy/clarity_sanitizer.go, integration/region_routing_e2e.test, tools/migrate_region_bindings.py, docs/ops/kms-region-consent.md | [Testing] Unit tests for policy template generation and consent coordinator logic; integration test running against a two-KMS local harness (mock-AWS-KMS, mock-azure-kms). CI added a new matrix row (region-routing-e2e) which runs on a thin VM image; initial runs failed due to missing mock KMS certs, fixed by adding test fixtures. Performance: average consent-check latency is ~12ms under load in the e2e harness; the coordinator is async-friendly and supports piggybacking with existing tokenization flows. | [Security considerations] Consent coordinator signs consent decisions with a short-lived key and includes a stable nonce to prevent replay. RBAC templates include explicit audit annotations and deny-by-default semantics for operators outside tenant's geozone. KMS tokens are never stored by the coordinator; it only mediates proof-of-consent and issues ephemeral delegation handles. | [Compatibility and rollout] Feature gated under agent.config.region_pinning.enabled (default false). Migration script converts legacy labels to RBAC bindings; recommended staged rollout: enable audit_sanitizer in canary, run migrations as dry-run, enable coordinator in canary region, progressively flip flag. | [Review conversation highlights] - Luis Ortega: "Please add a unit test that verifies audit envelope contains 'residency_hint' for edge cases (tenant no-preference)." Adds a lightweight contextual entropy indexer and heuristic alert weighting for prefetch/pipeline paths. Improves observability of token-level prefetch effects and reduces noisy alerts for transient warmups.
Motivation: We see recurring noisy alerts and high-cardinality telemetry around prefetch and prefix-warmup activity that obscures real regressions. This PR introduces a compact "contextual entropy indexer" to fingerprint invocation prompt-contexts, attaches entropy deltas to token-phase spans, and layers a heuristic alert-weighting engine so alerts triggered by prefetch/warmup churn are de-emphasized. The change is explicitly scoped to observability: no runtime behavior changes beyond additional light instrumentation and a configurable sampling hook.

What changed (summary):
- Added an entropy indexing library (pkg/observability/entropy_index) that computes a compact 64-bit context sketch and streaming delta per invocation. The index is intentionally small to avoid metric cardinality explosion.
- Instrumented token-phase spans to emit entropy_delta and prefetch_hint tags when a request used the prefetch path. These are exposed as OTEL attributes and as metric labels for rollups.
- Introduced an alert heuristics layer (services/alerting/heuristics) that consumes token-phase histograms + entropy deltas and applies noise attenuation for alerts matching prefetch signatures. Heuristics are configurable via experiments/heuristics.yaml.
- Dashboard: added observability/dashboards/prefetch-entropy-panel.json — a focused dashboard showing "prefetch rate", "entropy-delta distribution per-route", "token-latency split by prefetch_hint", and a time-series of heuristics attenuations applied.
- Tests and sim harness: added prefetched-invocation synthetic traces to eval-harness/prefetch-sim to validate alert dampening under warmup bursts.

Why this is safe: The entropy index is deterministic and uses only hashed context summary (no PII). Instrumentation is additive and sampled by default (5% global, adjustable per-tenant). Heuristics only change alert scoring; they do not suppress telemetry or modify request routing.

Checklist: 
- [x] pkg/observability/entropy_index: go implementation + docs (see README in package)
- [x] Instrumentation added to runtime span emitter (runtime/telemetry/token_phase_emitter.go)
- [x] Alert heuristics engine and configuration (services/alerting/heuristics/*)
- [x] Prefetch dashboard JSON and dashboard setup script
- [x] Unit + integration tests for indexer and heuristics
- [x] Performance sanity run (prefetch-sim) and spike replay tested on staging

Testing results (high level):
- Synthetic warmup burst (1000 prefetched traces/min for 10 minutes) in prefetched-sim: baseline alerts reduced by 72% after heuristics compared to control, true-positive regression alerts preserved.
- End-to-end telemetry CPU impact: +0.6% median on telemetry-ingest workers at 5% sampling; estimated p50 overhead per-request for the indexer is ~120µs when enabled unsampled.

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/observability/entropy_index/index.go
- runtime/telemetry/token_phase_emitter.go (added attributes entropy_delta, prefetch_hint)
- services/alerting/heuristics/engine.go
- services/alerting/heuristics/config.go
- experiments/heuristics.yaml
- observability/dashboards/prefetch-entropy-panel.json
- eval-harness/prefetch-sim/*.py (synthetic trace generator)
- integration tests/instrumentation/prefetch_entropy_test.go

Commits: [
  "a1c8f9d  Add entropy indexer core and tests",
  "b3f2a41  Emit entropy_delta and prefetch_hint from token_phase_emitter",
  "d9b7c22  Add alerting heuristics engine and config loader",
  "e4a990a  Dashboard for prefetch entropy and heuristics metrics",
  "f5c3b11  Add prefetched-sim harness and integration tests",
  "a7f6d90  Polish docs, add deployment notes and experiments.yaml"
]
Ethan Cole: Can we make the default sampling for the indexer tenant-configurable? Suggest exposing via tenant config with a conservative default (5%).
Maya Singh (author): Good call — added tenant override and documented in experiments/heuristics.yaml.
Priya Nair: The alert heuristics look promising but can we add a fallback rule to escalate if entropy_delta correlates with error-rate instead of latency?
Maya Singh: Added correlation check to heuristics (engine.go) — heuristics now auto-escalate when error-rate > 0.5% over window.
Liam OConnor: Dashboard looks good; consider coloring changes for prefetch vs non-prefetch latency bands.
Maya Singh: Updated panel colors and added hover tooltip explaining prefetch_hint semantics.
Deployed to staging on 2026-02-23, promoted to prod 2026-02-25 after smoke tests. Ops playbook added at docs/observability/prefetch-entropy-playbook.md. To rollback, disable heuristics via experiments/heuristics.yaml flag or revert sampling to 0%.
1) Set experiments/heuristics.yaml heuristics.enabled: false and deploy config; 2) If immediate telemetry removal required, set telemetry.sampling.entropy_indexer: 0% in tenant config; 3) Revert commit feature/observability/contextual-entropy-indexer if needed.
Oncall should watch alert-weight-adjustments histogram (dash: prefetch-entropy-panel -> heuristics attenuation). If legitimate alerts are being suppressed, set heuristics.override=true for the affected route and escalate. The playbook includes a quick query to surface suppressed alerts for the last 15m.
Entropy indexer uses non-reversible hashing and stores only 64-bit sketches. No contextual content is logged or stored. Reviewed by Security (SUP-4421) and approved for deployment.
Prefetch warmup noise reduction: -72% noisy alerts in sim. Telemetry overhead: ~0.6% CPU at 5% sampling. Storage: marginal increase in metric cardinality due to entropy_label but mitigated via bucketing and reservoir sampling.
This PR aims to improve signal-to-noise in SLO alerting for common prefetch/warmup patterns without hiding real regressions. Config knobs exposed so we can iterate on attenuation heuristics per-customer.
