Motivation: our presubmit and lint surface has grown many small, slightly divergent composite actions and ad-hoc dependency rollup jobs. This PR introduces an "inline lint orb" (composite action pattern kept in-repo for now) and a small "dependency choreography" toolset that groups dependency updates into ecosystem-aware batches, plus a churn detector to reduce noisy dep churn PRs. Goals: 1) shrink presubmit job graph and reduce redundant installs, 2) create a single reusable lint adapter that supports language-specific shims, 3) reduce dependency churn and make rollups deterministic, 4) provide a light-weight cache priming step to improve presubmit latency.

What changed (high level):
- Added a composite-ish action under .github/actions/inline-lint-orb that centralizes linters (eslint, go vet, rustfmt) with a small shim to select language adapters at runtime. This replaces three separate lint composite actions used across presubmits.
- Introduced tools/dep_choreographer (Go) which inspects lockfiles across packages, groups updates by ecosystem (npm, pip, go) and emits a deterministic rollup manifest. The rollup manifest is used by a new workflow job to produce a single rollup PR instead of many per-package updates.
- Added tools/churn_detector (Python) that runs in CI to compute a churn score for dependency PRs (based on number of transitive updates + touch frequency). If churn > threshold the job annotates the PR and recommends a staged rollout instead of automated merge.
- Modified .github/workflows/presubmit.yml to use the inline lint orb and split the presubmit into three fast lanes: quick-lint (fast), unit-smoke (short unit tests), and full-presubmit (longer integration tests). A cache-warm step runs in parallel to reduce cold-install latency.
- Small release automation tweak: release/prepare step now skips dependency rollups from the choreographer unless the linear ticket is referenced (prevents accidental release noise).
- Docs: docs/ci/README.md documents the new presubmit lanes, lint orb usage, and choreographer config.

Description/details (continuous): The inline lint orb is a single entrypoint action that accepts a "languages" list and a "shim_version" variable. Internally it uses language-specific adapters stored in .github/actions/inline-lint-orb/adapters/ which are small shell wrappers that invoke the project's canonical linter commands. The presubmit uses a language detection heuristic to avoid running unnecessary linters on PRs that touch only unrelated subtrees. The dep_choreographer performs analysis across package lockfiles (package-lock.json, poetry.lock, go.sum) and emits a rollup manifest manifest/dep-rollup-<sha>.yaml which the workflow consumes to create a single rollup branch. The churn_detector computes churn = transient_update_count * log(age_in_days + 1) / touched_packages and annotates PRs with the score and recommended action. This is intentionally conservative—high churn does not block merges, it annotates and triggers the staged merge flow if auto-merge is enabled.

Testing & CI: Presubmit pipeline initially failed on flaky integration tests (known flake: tests/network/test_routing.py) which caused a rerun; after isolating the flake the presubmit succeeded. New unit tests added for churn_detector (tools/churn_detector/tests/test_score.py) and integration smoke for dep_choreographer (tools/dep_choreographer/integration/verify_rollup.sh). Local developer flow: developers can run ./tools/dep_choreographer/cli rollup --dry-run to preview rollup manifests. There is a small linting migration script that updates repo-level linters to the orb-compatible entrypoints.

Rollout plan: merge to main behind feature flag (CI uses env REDWOOD_CI_LINT_ORB=true), monitor presubmit latency and number of lint jobs via the Redwood Console dashboard for 72 hours. After stability window, flip feature flag and deprecate the legacy per-language composite actions.

Related: Linear ENG-2741 (converge presubmit adapters), ENG-2789 (dependency rollup strategy). See internal doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2741 and design doc: https://redwood-internal.company/docs/ci/choreographer-design (internal).
Jordan Blake: Can we avoid running eslint on Go-only PRs? The new language detection heuristic looks fine but add tests for the path filter.
Maya Lin (author): Added unit tests for the path filter and adjusted the heuristic to prefer explicit path globs when present.
Priya Menon: dep_choreographer looks promising. Two asks: (1) add a --limit flag for max packages per rollup, (2) make rollup manifest schema backward compatible.
Maya Lin (author): Added --limit and a simple schema version key to the manifest (v1).
Ethan Zhou: Churn detector needs a clear opt-out for bots creating large updates (we missed renovate's noise footprint).
Maya Lin (author): Added RENOVATE_BYPASS label support, detector ignores PRs with that label. Also added docs entry describing the staged rollout path.
Priya Menon: CI flake during initial run. Rerun after isolating tests, passes now. Approving pending green CI.
Jordan Blake: Approve. Nice cleanup — please add a short migration note for integrators.
First presubmit run had a failing integration test due to a known flake; rerun succeeded. New jobs added (churn_detector + dep_choreographer smoke) are light and run on ubuntu-latest with short timeouts to avoid blocking mainline. Cache warm step reduced cold install median by ~18% in internal canary.
Introduce an in-repo reusable lint adapter (inline-lint-orb) that consolidates language linters and shrinks presubmit graphs; add dep_choreographer to produce deterministic dependency rollups and churn_detector to annotate high-churn dependency PRs. No breaking changes to developer workflow; opt-in feature flag during rollout.
Local: ./tools/dep_choreographer/cli rollup --dry-run; run lint orb locally with act or GitHub Actions runner: act -P ubuntu-latest=nektos/act-environments-ubuntu:18.04 -j quick-lint. For churn detector unit tests: python -m pytest tools/churn_detector/tests.
1) Monitor presubmit job counts and latency in Redwood Console for 72h. 2) Flip REDWOOD_CI_LINT_ORB feature flag and deprecate old composite actions after 1 week. 3) Run choreographer weekly for first month and evaluate rollup size/accuracy.

Motivation: Long streaming responses and multi-model fallbacks produce disconnected traces and duplicated token cost attributions. This PR introduces a lightweight recursive trace-linking layer plus a compact, slabbed histogram format for per-invocation token-cost that is cheap to emit and easy to aggregate. Goals: 1) join partial/continued streaming traces into a single logical invocation for accurate latency/cost SLOs; 2) emit a low-cardinality, quantized token-cost histogram per invocation to surface tail cost patterns without exploding cardinality; 3) keep runtime overhead under 2% P50 and avoid added high-cardinality labels. Design: - Recursive trace-linking: each streaming chunk now references an ancestor invocation_id and a small link vector (up to 3 ancestor edges). The agent runtime synthesizes a single root span when the final chunk arrives or after a configurable timeout. Link vectors are encoded as short stable IDs to avoid tagging high-cardinality tenant/model names. - Compact slabbed histograms: per-invocation histogram represented as 8 fixed-cost slabs (0-8 tokens, 9-32, 33-128, 129-512, 513-2k, 2k-8k, 8k-32k, 32k+). Hist counts are emitted as an 8-byte base64 payload on a single metric line (metric: redwood.invocation.token_cost_hist) with labels {model_variant, route, tenant_tier}. This keeps metric series low-cardinality while enabling rollups and percentiles. - Backwards compat: Existing token-level metrics (redwood.invocation.token_cost as a gauge/counter) are still emitted for compatibility; ingestion pipelines will use the new histogram when available. - Rollout plan: feature-flag default off; enable for 10% traffic via routing policy then 100% after 2 weeks of monitoring. - Telemetry sanitization: stripped user-provided keys, no PII in link vectors. Implementation summary: runtime (go) changes to span manager, emission sink adapters, and agent protobuf for link vector; metrics ingestion service decoding + rollup job to materialize p50/p95/p99 from slabs. Testing: unit tests for encoder/decoder, e2e synthetic stream scenario, staging rollout with synthetic cost anomalies, load test to confirm <2% latency overhead. Links: Linear ENG-9421 for streaming traces, ENG-9750 for compact histograms. Checklist: - [x] design doc (doc/telemetry/recursive-linking.md) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] load test results attached - [x] telemetry deprecation plan for legacy counters - [x] privacy review completed
Miguel Torres: Can we guarantee the link vector doesn't reintroduce high cardinality for multi-tenant deployments? Response (Asha): link vector uses stable short ids and we limit depth to 3; added sanitizer that strips tenant-unique metadata. Jae Kim: Please add a metric for 'link_reassembly_failures' so we can alert on missing final chunk. Response (Asha): Added link_reassembly_failures counter and alert in the rollout stage. Renee Wu: ingestion job looks fine but we should document how to backfill histograms for historical dashboards. Response (Asha): Added rollup job that can replay recent 7 days; documented backfill steps in docs. Miguel Torres: +1 after small nits. Jae Kim: Approved. Renee Wu: Approved.
Added: recursive trace-linking for streaming chunks and a compact slabbed token-cost histogram metric (redwood.invocation.token_cost_hist) to improve accuracy of per-invocation cost and tail analysis. Rollout behind feature flag; initial enablement at 10% traffic.
payload.title: add recursive trace-linking and compact token-cost histograms for streaming responses

Motivation: Dedicated fleet customers were seeing periodic decommits during sustained high-throughput bursts which caused partial SLA regressions for a small subset of tenants. Root cause analysis showed the existing static headroom model didn’t adapt quickly enough to shifted tail behavior and a conservative decommit path occasionally over-reacted during correlated utilization spikes.

This PR introduces two coordinated components: (1) a differential headroom tuner that continuously estimates per-pool headroom requirements using short and long-window utilization deltas, and (2) a decommit safety probe that probabilistically exercises a soft-failover path before accelerating decommit decisions. The goal is to reduce spurious decommits while bounding long-term capacity drift.

Design summary: the headroom tuner computes a per-pool headroom multiplier from two signals: an exponential short-window delta (30s) and a median long-window delta (10m). Multipliers are clamped and smoothed with a configurable hysteresis window. The decommit safety probe emits lightweight probe reservations (0-cost token reservations) to validate whether reclaiming slots will cause SLA slippage; probe failures increase decommit hold timers. Both components expose telemetry and parametrization through the existing autoscaler config surface.

Changes included: - autoscaler: add diff_headroom_tuner module with test coverage; integrate into allocate/reserve path. - controller: add decommit_probe controller that coordinates soft probes and influences scale-down votes. - telemetry: emit headroom_multiplier, probe_success_rate, probe_latency, and probe_inflight_count for per-pool dashboards. - helm: add new config keys and defaults to values.dedicated.yaml. - docs: ops runbook describing knobs, safe rollout steps, and SLO impact analysis.

Backward compatibility: all new behaviors are opt-in via feature flag and default to conservative fallbacks identical to current behavior. No config schema breakage.

Testing & validation: unit tests for tuner math and probe orchestration included. Integration test harness simulates sustained 95th-percentile load patterns and shows a 42% drop in scale-down-induced SLO regressions in local perf runs. CI initially surfaced linting and a flake in the probe timing test which were fixed in subsequent commits.

Rollout plan: staged rollout to canary fleet (5% of Dedicated pools) for 48h with closewatch alarms on per-tenant tail-99 latency and decommit-rate. If metrics remain stable, expand to 25% then 100% over two weeks. Automated rollback if probe_success_rate < 90% or decommit_rate increases by >25% over baseline.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration scenario - [x] Telemetry dashboards updated - [x] Docs runbook - [x] Feature-flag gated - [x] Helm config defaults added

Related: ENG-3245 (scale-down regression triage), SUP-9842 (customer incident: regressed latency after decommit), ENG-4018 (telemetry standardization).
Julian Kwan: Please add a short note in the tuner code explaining the rationale for the 30s/10m windows and reference the perf numbers that informed those choices.
Maya Patel (author): Added comments and a link to the perf doc in the tuner module. Also added a small unit test that validates window edge cases.
Samir Desai: The probe path looks good but could cause bursty API traffic if probes are too frequent. Can we cap concurrent probes per pool and add exponential backoff?
Maya Patel (author): Implemented per-pool probe_inflight cap (default 3) and exponential backoff with jitter; added integration test to assert stable probe volume under churn.
Ava Thompson: CI reported a flake in probe timing on macOS runners; suggest tightening test timing tolerances or mocking clock.
Maya Patel (author): Replaced real-time sleeps with a fake clock in the test harness to eliminate nondeterminism.
Julian Kwan: Approving. Minor nits addressed. Recommend a small canary release and close monitoring as documented in the runbook.
Adds an opt-in differential headroom tuner and a decommit safety probe to reduce spurious scale-downs; exposes telemetry for tuning; Helm knobs added. Recommended canary rollout and monitoring guidance included in docs.

Context: Customers have intermittent tail-latency incidents attributed to unseen GPU-side queueing and scheduler backpressure. Existing telemetry exposed per-invocation latency and kernel timings but lacked per-device queue depth, kernel wait-time histograms, and an end-to-end trace showing where scheduler backpressure cascades into request stalls. Motivation: provide deterministic signals for (1) detecting kernel saturation before request SLOs are violated, (2) surface backpressure spans across scheduler -> runtime -> GPU driver boundary, and (3) reduce alert noise by tuning thresholds using real queue metrics. Changes in this PR: added a Prometheus collector for per-GPU queue depth and producer/consumer rates; emit OTLP spans at scheduler enqueue/dequeue points with a backpressure.reason tag; propagate a lightweight backpressure_trace_id through KV cache and runtime worker handoff; add kernel_wait_time histogram and per-queue tail-percentile gauges; new Grafana dashboard panels (device queue depth heatmap, enqueue/dequeue rate timeseries, kernel wait waterfall) and an alerting rule that triggers when device queue depth > 90% for 30s AND kernel_wait_p95 > 200ms. Rollout plan: feature gated via telemetry.enable_gpu_queue_metrics (default: false) and staged rollout to dedicated infra then hosted canaries for 48h. Observability: dashboards and alerts added; playbook drafted (link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2301) for runbook steps and mitigation (scale-up, redistribute shards, apply per-tenant throttles). Testing: unit tests for collectors and propagator, e2e integration against a synthetic kernel-saturation bench, manual verification on a dedicated pool. Backwards compatibility: propagation uses optional header and degrades to no-op for older runtimes. Risk: low-risk telemetry addition; a potential perf impact from extra metrics is mitigated by sampling and batching in the collector. See changed_files for code pointers and short snippets. Merge: squash-merged after two approvals and CI green.
Marcus Diaz: Can we avoid emitting per-invocation tags that increase cardinality? Suggest adding a sampled backpressure.reason and restricting gpu_id label cardinality.
Ava Chen: Addressed — added sampling and coalesced gpu_id into device_group label for the collector. Updated tests to assert label cardinality remains bounded.
Priya Iyer: Nit: prefer histogram buckets aligned with kernel latencies observed in perf lab (5ms, 10ms, 25ms, 50ms, 100ms, 250ms, 500ms). Also asked for a clear rollback flag.
Ava Chen: Updated histogram buckets and added telemetry.enable_gpu_queue_metrics=false default and telemetry.force_disable_gpu_traces for emergency rollback.
Liam O'Connor: Verified e2e bench reproduces queueing; approved after CI fixed intermittent flaky test (fixed by increasing test timeout).
Instrumented GPU scheduling queue metrics and backpressure traces: new Prometheus collectors, OTLP spans at enqueue/dequeue, Grafana panels for queue depth and kernel wait times, and an alert rule to detect kernel saturation. Feature is gated and disabled by default.
payload.title: Instrument GPU queueing and backpressure span propagation

Motivation: long-tail conversational traffic and multi-tenant variability mean the KV cache is frequently evicted from mini-batches even though reusing older KV fragments would save tokens and improve unit economics. Separately, tenant-facing quantization defaults are too coarse: some tenants can accept int8 for background low-SLO routes while others require fp16 for latency-sensitive chat. This PR adds two coordinated pieces: 1) a deferred-KV-eviction policy in the serving runtime that postpones eager KV eviction for low-probability prefix reuse and exposes eviction scoring for per-tenant policies; 2) a quant-tier-orchestrator service + CLI that evaluates unit-econ vs latency tradeoffs and dynamically routes tenants to quantization tiers (fp16, int8, int4-probative) with safety fallbacks. Changes include a lightweight controller that ingests tenant cost/latency targets and historical token shapes, an offline candidate generator to produce per-tenant compact quant profiles, runtime hooks to switch quant mode per-route, telemetry to record econ delta per rollout, and a CLI command (redwood econ profile apply --dry-run) for safe dry runs. Safety: automated rollback if P95 latency increases > 20ms or hallucination regressions detected via evaluation hooks; default fallthrough to fp16 for tenants without profiles. Backwards compatibility: config flags default to off to avoid surprise behavior; operator opt-in required for private/dedicated installs. Checklist: - [x] Implement deferred eviction scoring + runtime hook - [x] Add quant-tier-orchestrator service and API - [x] CLI and presets for tenant profiles - [x] Telemetry + eval hooks for rollback detection - [x] Unit + integration tests and canary rollout plan. Impact: expected unit-econ improvement ~6-15% across sampled tenants in our load test depending on prefix re-use. Related: ENG-1983 (tenant econ objectives), ENG-1991 (quant safety gates).
Ethan Cole: Nice separation between eviction scoring and enforcement. Suggest exposing a per-tenant decay factor so platform teams can be conservative on enterprise tenants.
Priya Natarajan: Added tenant decay factor, default 0.3 for enterprise in defaults.toml and config flag --deferred-kv-decay.
Maya Lopez: We should ensure switching quant tiers doesn't recompile kernels synchronously on hot paths. Can we pre-warm compiled paths?
Samir Gupta: Added pre-warm path for common model families and quant profiles; expanded test coverage to simulate kernel warmup latency (see integration test).
Maya Lopez: CI lint flagged unused import in orchestrator.go, fixed in next commit.
Infra CI Bot: Integration suite flaked once (telemetry ingest timeout), reran and passed.
Security Review (Samir Gupta): No new network endpoints other than internal orchestrator API; added ACL check and auth header validation.
Introduce deferred KV eviction and a quant-tier orchestrator that enables tenant-specific quantization profiles and safe rollouts. Operator opt-in behind flags; includes CLI for dry-run and rollback safety hooks. Expected unit-econ improvements for workloads with moderate prefix reuse.
payload.title: Introduce deferred-KV-eviction + quant-tier orchestrator and tenant econ profiles

Adds phase-aware invocation telemetry and alert attenuation. No user-facing breaking changes; new metrics and dashboards for SREs and platform owners.
Motivation: Long-tail alert noise and cost attribution errors are frequently caused by short-lived or transient invocations (e.g. interactive CLI calls, probe requests, and ephemeral batch jobs) that skew token-level latency/cost aggregates. This PR introduces a phase-aware "invocation lifespan" telemetry surface and an alert attenuation adapter that reduces false positives from transient invocations while preserving signal for sustained regressions.

What this PR does (single string description): Adds an invocation lifecycle enrichment that tags spans and metrics with invocation_phase values (init, warmup, steady, teardown), emits phase-durations and phase-token-cost metrics, provides a new dashboard with phase-aligned latency/cost breakdowns, implements a configurable alert attenuator that silences or downweights alerts dominated by short-lived invocations, and adds a small sampling policy so high-volume short invocations don't over-index metrics. Includes end-to-end tests and docs.

Checklist:
- [x] Instrumentation: span and metric enrichers for invocation_phase and phase_durations
- [x] Metrics: new metrics export (invocation.phase.duration_ms, invocation.phase.token_cost) with labels for model, route, tenant
- [x] Tracing: span attribute propagation and a lightweight phase marker in the root span
- [x] Dashboard: phase-aware latency/cost breakdown, short-invocation cohort filter, and long-tail alert explorer
- [x] Alerting: attenuation adapter that can be toggled per-tenant or per-route
- [x] Tests: integration test in observability harness; unit tests for attenuator logic
- [x] Docs: console docs and runbook for interpreting phase charts and tuning attenuation thresholds

Backward compatibility notes: All new metrics use new metric names and labels; existing dashboards remain unchanged. The attenuator defaults to disabled for all customers; enabling is a safe opt-in.

Data volume concerns: sampling defaults to 10% for invocations with lifetime < 250ms to bound cardinality; sampling rate is configurable per-tenant.

Operational notes: On merge we will roll the feature on to the staging observability cluster, validate dashboards with a 48h synthetic run, then enable the attenuator in canary mode for internal tenants only.

Context / Related work: This complements ENG-4520 (token phase attribution) and ENG-4721 (cohort-aware alerting). It is intended to reduce alert churn and improve per-token cost attribution for SLA dashboards.
Owen Kim: Please add a short note on cardinality controls and a fallback to avoid label explosion — requested adding the per-tenant sampling knob and a short-invocation aggregation path.
Marisa (author): Added per-tenant sampling and an aggregate fallback metric for short invocations; updated docs.
Priya Nair: CI failed initially on the integration timing test; after increasing the test timeout the suite passes. Recommend a short flakiness run in staging.
Alex Mendes: Approved with comment to follow up and expose attenuation metrics in the console (attenuated_alert_count, attenuation_ratio).
Merge action: Squash-merged after CI re-run and staging verification.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: Customers increasingly enable response_format/schema on streaming endpoints and then rely on concise error messages to debug integrations. We observed two recurring problems in production: (1) opaque schema validation errors that are hard to map back to a user prompt or tool invocation, and (2) validation failures that surface mid-stream with no way to continue or repair the in-progress stream. This PR introduces three coordinated improvements: a policy linter run at request-compile time, a structured human-readable error format with hint codes, and a stream resume token that allows the runtime to checkpoint validation state across partial payloads.

What this change does: (1) Schema policy lints: adds a new request validation pass that runs when response_format/schema is present. The linter enforces recommended policies (examples present for required top-level objects, disallowing additionalProperties by default unless explicitly allowed, bounding array lengths for large embeddings outputs, and requiring explicit enum lists where applicable). Lints emit warnings (non-blocking) by default and can be promoted to errors with the response_format.strict flag. (2) Human-readable validation errors: validation failures now return an error payload that includes: human_message (concise), hint_code (stable short token), location_path (JSON Pointer), and actionable_suggestion (one-line remediation). These are surfaced consistently across hosted and OpenAI-compat endpoints. (3) Stream resume tokens: when streaming structured output, the runtime emits lightweight resume tokens every time a schema checkpoint is validated. If a later chunk fails, the client (or a server-side repair flow) can provide the last-good token to resume validation without re-processing earlier tokens; this enables graceful repairs and deterministic tool-call fencing.

Compatibility and OpenAI-compat: we preserved the existing response_format and function_call semantics. The OpenAI adapter maps new error hint_codes to openai-compatible error messages, and the adapter will include an x-openai-error-hint header for downstream clients that expect OpenAI-style text. No breaking changes to request shapes when strict is not enabled.

Checklist: - [x] Add policy linter implementation (runtime/request/compiler) - [x] Add structured error schema and serialization layer - [x] Implement resume token generation and verification in streaming runtime - [x] OpenAI-compat adapter mappings and headers - [x] Unit and integration tests for linter + streaming checkpointing - [x] Docs updates (response_format.md and troubleshooting)

Testing and validation performed: - Unit tests (schema linter rules, hint code mapping, resume token deterministic encoding) - E2E smoke against openai-compat harness with simulated partial chunks and mid-stream recovery - Load-tested stream resume in perf-canary (no measurable latency regression at p95) - Manual validation with several customer prompt sets that previously tripped opaque errors

Limitations and follow-ups: - Linter rule set is conservative; we intend to iterate rules and expose a customer-visible policy bundle in a follow-up (ENG-4650). - Resume tokens are intentionally opaque HMACs; we may offer a debug-mode that expands them for internal debugging. - Edge-case: tools that receive partial tool-call bodies still must rely on the tool-call fencing behavior; this PR clarifies behavior but does not change the tool contract.

Notes on rollout: The feature is behind a runtime flag feature.enable_schema_lints and enabled for canary users by default. response_format.strict must be explicitly enabled by customers to convert lints to hard errors.

Arjun Rao (reviewer): Left a couple of nits on naming and asked for clarity on the linter promotion semantics. Requested unit tests for a failing strict case.
Maya Patel (author): Addressed naming nits in follow-up commit and extended tests to cover strict=true promotion. Clarified promotion behavior in the PR description.
Lina Gómez (reviewer): Requested that hint codes be stable and documented; asked to add a brief mapping table to docs. Also suggested a smaller resume token (reduce entropy) to cut header size; author explained token HMAC size tradeoff and kept it but added a future task to evaluate size.
Samir Desai (approver): Verified the OpenAI-compat mapping and perf numbers. Approved with one suggestion to log the linter warnings at debug level only for hosted-by-default mode.
payload.title: Introduce schema policy lints, human-readable validation errors, and stream resume tokens for structured output

Context: We need stronger, verifiable audit metadata for tenant-scoped operations and more usable RBACv2 explanations for auditors. This PR introduces an 'audit-prooflet' envelope (compressed, signed metadata blobs) that KMS can attest to and a new internal-only API /internal/rbac/explain that returns deterministic decision traces for RBACv2 policy decisions. Motivation: existing audit headers are verbose and often out-of-band; auditors requested compact cryptographic proof attachments that can be validated independently and the security team requested a machine-readable explainability endpoint to debug policy regressions in canary rollouts.

What this PR does (summary): 1) Adds audit-prooflet envelope format and signing flow (api/audit/prooflet.go, infra/kms/prooflet_signer.go). 2) Plumbs prooflet creation into request ingest: prooflets are created at the audit-ingress stage and stored as compressed blobs in the audit-indexer with a KMS signature reference. 3) Adds /internal/rbac/explain endpoint (api/rbac/explain_handler.go) which returns a sanitized, canonical decision trace and the prooflet reference for the decision. 4) Adds DB migration to add prooflet index column (migrations/20241118_add_prooflet_index.sql) and a background backfill job (jobs/prooflet_backfill.go). 5) Console telemetry: exposes a read-only prooflet verification status and latency histogram. 6) Tests: unit tests for signing/verifying, integration test against kms-fake that simulates failure cases, and a small e2e that verifies a labeled tenant can request explains.

Design notes: - Prooflets are intentionally small (max 8KB) and use zlib compression + JSON-LD footprint to make them verifiable and language-agnostic. - KMS signer returns an ephemeral signature that includes a key-hash and region tag; we store the signature metadata with the prooflet index rather than embedding large KMS artifacts in the main audit row. - RBAC explain output is intentionally sanitized (no raw secrets, no long-lived tokens) and includes policy fingerprint, matched rules, evaluated claim set and short path to allow auditors to reproduce decisions offline. - Migration strategy: create the column as NULLABLE and enable prooflet creation behind a feature flag audit.prooflet.enabled defaulting to false; run backfill with tenant opt-in.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag. 2) Deploy prooflet signer service in canary region and enable flag for internal tenants only. 3) Run backfill on a sample tenant cohort and verify prooflet integrity via a new admin tool proofletctl verify. 4) Gradually enable for all tenants over 4 weeks. 5) Add tenant-facing docs and sample verification script in redwood-examples.

Backward compatibility and safety: - If KMS signing fails we fall back to a plain audit header with a synthetic prooflet-ref stamped as "unsigned" and emit a telemetry metric audit.prooflet.sign_failure. - Prooflet size is enforced at creation time; oversized events are truncated with a deterministic hash to preserve reproducibility.

Testing and CI: - Initial linting failed due to fmt changes; fixed in second commit. - Added unit and integration tests (CI matrix includes kms-fake and sqlite job-runner).

Security review notes: - Priya and Lina performed threat modeling focusing on: replay attacks, signature spoofing, and key-residency leakage. Mitigations: include timestamp+nonce in envelope, rely on KMS key-hash and region tag, and no plaintext keys are persisted.

Open items: - We will iterate on the prooflet JSON-LD schema with Compliance (task ENG-4210). - Consider adding per-prooflet ACL if auditors request restricted access.

References: Linear ENG-4210 (prooflets design), internal RFC: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4210/prooflets-rfc, and compliance ticket SUP-987.

Checklist:
- [x] Prooflet format and signer implementation
- [x] Request plumbing and storage index
- [x] /internal/rbac/explain endpoint with sanitized output
- [x] DB migration and backfill job behind feature flag
- [x] Unit/integration/e2e tests
- [x] Console telemetry and docs stub

Jared Wu: high level looks good. Can we make sure the prooflet index is sharded so it won't cause a single hot row on high-throughput tenants?
Maya Chen (author): added sharding hint in prooflet_backfill.go and added a shard_key in migration comments; made prooflet_index sharded by tenant hash.
Lina Ortega: Threat model OK but we need explicit TTL for prooflets in the retention policy to avoid unbounded storage growth.
Maya Chen (author): added retention config audit.prooflet.retention_days with default 365 and telemetry to track storage usage.
Priya Nair (security): Please ensure signature verification rejects unexpected region tags (we should not accept prooflets signed for eu-west in us-east tenant contexts).
Maya Chen (author): verification enforces region affinity; added unit test verifying mismatch is rejected and metric emitted.
Carlos Mendes: CI failing on go vet for unused var in kms_fake; looks fixed in last commit. Approving pending small docs typo fix.
Docs owner (auto): docs/prooflets.md minor grammar nit; fixed by author.
Jared Wu: approving — small nit about log level adjusted, resolved.
payload.title: Add audit-prooflet envelope and RBACv2 explainability endpoint

payload.body:
Motivation: Our presubmit pipeline has become a major contributor to developer feedback latency. Large monolithic presubmit jobs (lint + unit + integration + e2e) amplify queue times and make dependency-refresh PRs (dependabot and internal) spike CI load, causing noisy failures and long iteration cycles. This PR introduces two complementary changes: (1) a partitioned presubmit runner that routes changes to lane-specific job sets (fast, standard, integration) to reduce median feedback time and deconflict heavy test jobs; and (2) a dependency-refresh orchestrator that schedules and staggers dependency bump PRs to avoid CI thundering herds and to allow rolling canary validation of larger upgrades.

Summary of changes (high level):
- Add a presubmit router action (actions/presubmit-router) that labels PRs with presubmit-lane based on file globs, change size, and modified services. The router is implemented as a small TypeScript GitHub Action and a config file at .github/presubmit-lanes.yaml.
- Split the monorepo GH workflow into three lanes: presubmit-fast.yml, presubmit-standard.yml, presubmit-integration.yml. Each workflow runs a subset of jobs and reuses composite actions to keep duplication low.
- Introduce a lightweight orchestrator service (tools/dep-refresh/orchestrator) that sequences dependency bump PRs. The orchestrator uses a lease mechanism (Redis) and posts status checks to coordinate canary runs and staged rollouts.
- Refactor existing lint/test scripts (scripts/ci/*) to accept lane hints and to produce lane-aware artifacts/annotations.
- Add new observability hooks: CI lane metrics (prometheus/meter tags) and a short-run smoke test that runs when dep-refresh orchestrator promotes a PR to canary.
- Tests and infra: unit tests for the router and orchestrator, integration test harness for lane routing logic, and updated action metadata.

Commits (summary):
- feat(presubmit): add presubmit router action and config
- ci(workflows): split presubmit into fast/standard/integration lanes
- feat(deps): add dep-refresh orchestrator service with lease logic
- refactor(ci): make scripts lane-aware, add lane annotations to test runners
- test(ci): add unit/integration tests for router and orchestrator
- docs: document presubmit lanes and rollout plan in docs/dev/presubmit.md

Changed files (representative):
- .github/actions/presubmit-router/action.yml
- .github/actions/presubmit-router/index.ts
- .github/presubmit-lanes.yaml
- .github/workflows/presubmit-fast.yml
- .github/workflows/presubmit-standard.yml
- .github/workflows/presubmit-integration.yml
- tools/dep-refresh/orchestrator/main.go
- scripts/ci/run-tests.sh (refactor to accept LANE env var)
- docs/dev/presubmit.md
- ci/metrics/presubmit_lanes.prom (meter tpl)

Testing and validation:
- Local unit test coverage added for router and orchestrator: 82%/78% respectively.
- Staging runs: executed against the staging org (redwood-staging) with a synthetic mix of 200 small PRs and 20 dependency PRs. Median presubmit latency improved from 9m45s to 2m30s for fast-lane PRs and from 18m to 7m for standard-lane PRs. Integration-lane queue depth reduced by ~60% under load.
- Dep-refresh orchestrator: successfully sequenced a batch of 12 dependency bumps; canary promotion prevented two regressions by isolating them to the canary cohort.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy router action and workflows to staging and enable presubmit-lane labeling behind feature flag (gh:presubmit-router=on).
2) Run canary on 10% of dev teams for 48h; monitor CI latencies, failure modes, and lane label accuracy.
3) Gradually enable for all, then enable dep-refresh orchestrator in a dry-run mode for 72h before authorizing automatic promotions.

Notes / alternatives considered:
- We evaluated single-workflow sharding via test slicing but found lane-level partitioning simpler to reason about and better aligned with developer expectations.
- We considered using GitHub queue API (if available), but opted for an independent router to keep control and observability.

Related: ENG-9876 (presubmit latency initiative), ENG-10021 (dep refresh safety improvements).

CI checks summary: unit-tests (pass), integration-smoke (pass), lint (pass), action-build (pass), staging-canary (pass).
Diego Alvarez: Left a few nits on the TS action (prefer async/await across the action boundary) — see inline comment on index.ts:42
Maya Chen: addressed the async/await nit; pushed a follow-up commit to normalize error handling
Priya Nair: Can we ensure the orchestrator lease fallback is resilient to transient Redis failures? Also requested a short-circuit for manual takeover in docs
Maya Chen: added exponential backoff + circuit breaker in orchestrator; documented manual takeover steps in docs/dev/presubmit.md
Ethan Brooks: Approved after verifying the staging canary metrics and seeing the median latency improvements in the perf run
CI Bot: All checks passed on rerun (action-build 1/1, unit-tests 1/1, integration-smoke 1/1)
Maintainer (A. Singh): Squash-merged after approvals and green CI; noted a follow-up task to tune lane heuristics (ENG-10100)
- Introduce presubmit lane partitioning (fast/standard/integration) to reduce developer feedback latency.
- Add presubmit-router GitHub Action and configuration file.
- Add dependency-refresh orchestrator to sequence and canary dependency bump PRs.
- Refactor CI scripts to be lane-aware and add lane metrics.
This PR intentionally keeps the router heuristics conservative for initial rollout (prefer explicit path globs and small-change thresholds). Follow-ups will iterate towards more aggressive auto-classification.
payload.title: Partition presubmit runner across lanes and add dependency-refresh orchestrator

payload.body:
Problem: Finance/RevRec needs a stable, auditable export table to reconcile billing ledger totals against usage events and customer usage exports. Today the process relies on ad-hoc queries across mutable upstream tables with inconsistent joins and unclear ownership, which increases close risk and slows dispute investigations.

What this PR does: Adds a first-class reconciliation export pipeline that materializes billing-ledger line items into a finance-owned Snowflake schema, with a documented schema contract and strict access gating. This export is designed for month-end close workflows and for automated drift checks (ledger vs usage events) without exposing sensitive per-request data.

Deliverables in this PR: (1) New export table: `FINANCE_RECON.BILLING_LEDGER_EXPORT_V1` (daily partitioned) containing invoice-period usage aggregates and the minimal dimensions required for reconciliation. (2) A scheduled job (hourly + end-of-day hardening run) that populates the export from the billing ledger source-of-truth while preserving an immutable snapshot per `billing_run_id`. (3) Schema documentation in-repo, including field definitions, nullability guarantees, and join keys to telemetry/usage events. (4) Access gating: write access limited to the metering pipeline service role; read access limited to `FINANCE_RECON_READER` (Finance/RevRec + explicitly approved RevOps users). (5) Guardrails: row-count and checksum assertions, and a canary query used by the metering sanity job to catch incomplete loads.

Schema highlights (v1): Primary grain is one row per (billing_run_id, account_id, usage_day, product, meter, model, region, price_plan_id). Core fields include `billed_tokens_prompt`, `billed_tokens_completion`, `billed_tokens_total`, `request_count_billed`, `embedding_units_billed`, `amount_usd`, `currency`, `invoice_id` (nullable until invoicing), `contract_id` (nullable), `dedupe_key_version`, `source_table_version`, `generated_at`, and `data_freshness_lag_seconds`. We deliberately exclude raw prompt text, user identifiers, and per-request IDs; where a join is needed for investigations, Finance can request temporary scoped access to the underlying ledger detail table via INT-932 workflow.

Operational notes: The export is append-only by `billing_run_id` (immutability), so backfills create a new billing run instead of mutating prior snapshots. The job supports a `--dry-run` mode that writes to `FINANCE_RECON._STAGING_BILLING_LEDGER_EXPORT_V1` for validation. Late-arriving ledger adjustments are captured via a new billing run and can be compared using `previous_billing_run_id`.

Access control: Adds a new Snowflake role `FINANCE_RECON_READER` and grants SELECT on the export table + schema usage. Grants are managed via `infra/snowflake/roles/finance_recon_reader.sql` and audited in the existing access-log sink. This aligns with the metering data retention/access policy and reduces the blast radius compared to granting direct access to ledger tables.

Testing: Includes dbt schema tests (not_null, accepted_values, unique key), unit tests for the transform mapping, and an end-to-end staging run validation query. CI runs the transform unit tests; dbt tests run in the data-ci environment.

Follow-ups (out of scope): Wire this export into the Console metering sanity dashboard drilldowns (ENG-4415) and use it as the canonical input for the month-end checklist automation. Also pending: add `cache_hit_billed_tokens` once PR-27485 lands and we confirm the finance reconciliation joins.

Risk: Low. Internal-only pipeline + gated table. No changes to metering logic or invoice generation in this PR.

Docs/links: Confluence reconciliation playbook will link to this schema doc after merge; owners are Finance (Emily Stone) + Eng Telemetry (Mei Lin).
Logan Wright: Can we guarantee immutability for month-end audits? I don’t want Finance querying a table that silently changes.

Mei Lin (author): Yes — the export is append-only keyed by billing_run_id. We never UPDATE prior runs; backfills create a new run with `previous_billing_run_id` pointing back. Added that explicitly to the doc + a unit test to fail if the job attempts to update existing billing_run_id.

Caleb Johnson: The job currently runs hourly. What’s the expected freshness SLA and what happens if it falls behind?

Mei Lin (author): Added `data_freshness_lag_seconds` and a simple canary query that computes lag from ledger ingestion watermark. This will be wired into the sanity job/alerts; for now it logs WARN > 2h. Aisha is adding alerting thresholds in the metering dashboard PR.

Emily Stone: Please confirm the export excludes any fields that could be considered customer content or personal data. Also need a clear list of who can access it.

Mei Lin (author): Confirmed: no prompt/response text, no end-user identifiers, no request_ids. Added a “Data classification” section to docs and updated grants to only FINANCE_RECON_READER. Access requests go through INT-932 and are audit-logged.

Aisha Bello: The assertions query should check both row counts and amount_usd checksum to catch partial loads.

Mei Lin (author): Done — added `sum(amount_usd)` vs ledger watermark window plus a per-day row-count floor. Both checks run in the staging validation and in CI (data-ci).

Logan Wright: Looks good. Please add a short section describing how to join to usage events for drift checks.

Mei Lin (author): Added join keys + example queries (by account/day/model/region) and caveats about meter_version changes.

Approvals: Logan Wright approved. Caleb Johnson approved. Emily Stone approved (Finance sign-off). Aisha Bello approved.
Internal-only: introduces `FINANCE_RECON.BILLING_LEDGER_EXPORT_V1` for RevRec reconciliation and drift monitoring; gated to FINANCE_RECON_READER role. No customer-facing changes.
payload.title: Add billing-ledger reconciliation export (Snowflake) + schema docs + access gating

payload.body:
Context and motivation: customer tenants with bursty short-lived traffic observed frequent cold-start spikes despite warm pools sized by static heuristics. Current warm pools are per-cluster and use LRU eviction which doesn't respect tenant burst budgets, causing unfairness and surprising latency spikes for tenants that recently paid for reserved capacity. This PR introduces a lease-backed warm pool allocator plus a utilization-proxy telemetry component to (1) reduce cold-start jitter by holding short-term leases for tenants who request burst capacity, (2) decouple warm-pool lifetime from raw LRU so tenant-level agreements and soft-return windows are respected, and (3) export a normalized utilization proxy across heterogeneous GPU types for better autoscaler decisions.
Implements lease-backed warm pool (controller + runtime hooks), soft-return window for leases, per-tenant burst-debt accounting, and a utilization-proxy exporter that normalizes GPU footprints and reports per-tenant warm efficiency metrics to the metrics pipeline.
New CRD-like in-memory Lease structure: contains tenant_id, lease_id, acquired_at, duration, soft_return_window, and debt_marker
Controller: reconciliation now assigns warmlet instances to tenants by creating a lease rather than marking an instance 'reserved' in the old LRU list
Runtime: added lease gRPC endpoints to acquire/release and a non-blocking 'renew' call that returns a probabilistic extension to cut frequency of churn
Autoscaler: utilization-proxy takes raw GPU metrics + model footprint and outputs a normalized 'proxy-units' metric used by headroom estimator
Eviction: eviction policy changed to respect soft-return windows and per-tenant minimum lease floor before reclaiming
Console: new UI table and per-tenant charts for warm-pool efficiency and 'burst debt' over time
Docs: operator tuning guide with recommended lease durations, soft-return windows, and impact on billing metrics
Unit tests for lease logic and eviction ordering; integration e2e that simulates 100 tenants with bursty traffic verifying P95 tail latency improves and cold-start events decrease; a smoke test for utilization-proxy exposing consistent values across two GPU families (A100 and H100 profiles). CI ran integration stage with a simulated cluster; one flaky e2e was rerun and passed.
In a staged perf run with 200 simulated tenants we saw cold-start tail latency (P99) drop by ~37% for microburst flows while warm-pool memory overhead increased by ~4% due to short leases. Autoscaler contamination reduced because utilization-proxy decouples raw GPU % from model-kernel footprint.
Default lease duration set to 90s with soft-return-window 30s. Operators can tune via Helm chart (charts/redwood/values.yaml). Lease decisions are idempotent and safe to roll back: controller will mark leases as expired and return warmlets to the common pool. Deprecated flags: warmpool-size-static is still supported but superseded when leaseback enabled.
Rajesh: Can you explain how leases interact with Dedicated reserved capacity? If a tenant holds a lease but has an active reserved pool, do we double-count their allocation?
Samantha: Good question. Leases are orthogonal — if a tenant has reserved capacity the lease will preferentially allocate from their reserved warmlets; the debt_marker records whether the warmlet was served from reserved vs shared. The utilization-proxy includes a 'source' dimension so downstream billing and autoscaler logic can subtract reserved footprint.
Linus: Eviction ordering needs stronger tests for rare race windows where renewals and eviction collide.
Samantha: Added two edge-case e2e tests (lease_renewal_race and eviction_during_renew) and fixed a race in lease_reconciler by making the compare-and-swap idempotent.
Mei: The normalized units algorithm is neat but we need a note about how we map quantized models (4-bit) vs fp16 — are we penalizing quantized models for lower raw GPU utilization?
Samantha: The normalizer uses a model-footprint heuristic combined with measured kernel throughput; quantized models typically show lower GPU occupancy but similar effective throughput — we run a per-model calibration sample during onboarding and store a footprint coefficient which the proxy uses. Added docs and a calibration job script.
Added lease-backed warm pool allocator to reduce cold-start jitter for bursty tenants; introduced utilization-proxy metric to normalize utilization across GPU families; operator tunables for lease duration and soft-return window. Backwards compatible; opt-in via Helm flag 'warmpool.leaseback.enabled'.
ENG-2410: evaluate long-term billing implications of short leases and add a usage-reporting export
ENG-2415: expose per-model calibration job in the model registry onboarding flow
ENG-2432: consider lease persistence across controller restarts for faster recovery (opt-in)
PM-412: document migration plan for customers currently using static warm-pool sizing
payload.title: Leaseback warm-pool and utilization-proxy: reduce cold-start jitter and unify utilization signals

payload.body:
Motivation: enable more autonomous, telemetry-driven promotions and rapid containment for cohorts during model rollouts. This PR introduces a Cohort Triage Orchestrator that classifies traffic cohorts into healthy/quarantine/monitor lanes, runs gated A/B evaluations (gated-eval) with checkpointed baselines, and supports autonomous rollforward when safety budgets are satisfied. Key user stories: 1) platform teams get low-touch canary promotion when cohort-level metrics meet objective windows; 2) problematic cohorts are automatically attenuated/shadowed rather than fully disabling traffic; 3) operators can define per-cohort policies and handshake windows via declarative config. What this changes: new controller (cohort_triage_controller) that consumes telemetry streams and rollout intents, a lightweight policy DSL for triage rules, integrations to the console for cohort dashboards, and end-to-end tests and benchmarks. Design notes: the controller keeps a moving safety budget per cohort, computes delta metrics against pinned baselines, and triggers autonomous rollforward only after ensemble checks (latency P95, error rate, semantic regression score) remain stable for an observation window. For borderline cases the controller will initiate a gated-eval: a short-lived A/B experiment with deterministic seeding, enriched sampling, and automatic snapshot checkpoints to allow deterministic rollback and repro playback. Safety features: attenuation rules to reduce shadow weight gradually, quarantined shadow lanes with compact KV cache isolation to avoid cross-cohort cache pollution, manual latches for human-in-the-loop intervention, and audit logging for every automatic action. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is opt-in via rollout policy annotations; existing rollouts are unaffected until a policy is attached. Related work: follows ENG-3245 and ties into the rollout telemetry work from ENG-3301. Checklist: - [x] Core controller implementation - [x] Policy schema and validation - [x] E2E integration tests - [x] Unit tests for safety heuristics - [x] Console dashboard and example policy - [x] Docs and release notes - [x] Benchmarks for decision latency Known limitations: initial semantic-regression scorer is heuristic-based and will be replaced in a follow-up with a model-driven scorer (ENG-3450). Follow-ups: fine-grained audit retention toggle, RBAC for autonomous actions, and a canary simulator for offline what-if analysis.
Diego Morales: We should ensure KV cache isolation when running quarantined shadows, otherwise noisy cohorts can degrade other tenants. Asha: Added compact KV cache per-quarantine lane and tests to validate isolation.
Helen Fischer: The gated-eval snapshot format needs to be stable across upgrades. Can we pin a schema version? Asha: Added snapshot schema v1 and backward compatibility hooks in snapshot manager.
Priya Nair: Can we make the autonomous rollforward opt-in per workspace? Asha: Defaulted the policy to disabled and added an override at workspace level in the policy schema.
Integration CI: flaky E2E on first run due to timing window. Re-ran and passed. Note: increased test window and added deterministic seeding in gated-eval tests.
Introduce Cohort Triage Orchestrator: opt-in cohort-level autonomous rollforward with gated A/B evals, quarantine shadow lanes, policy DSL, and console dashboard. Operators can opt into per-cohort automated promotions and attenuation policies. See docs/rollouts/cohort-triage.md for configuration and examples.
Performance: decision path latency median 12ms in our bench environment; worst-case when computing semantic delta for long observation windows is ~85ms. Safety: initial rollout tested on internal beta with two Canary runs and no regressions observed. Telemetry retention for triage windows set to 72 hours by default to bound memory.
payload.title: Cohort triage orchestrator with autonomous rollforward and gated-eval

payload.body:
Motivation: during recent regional surges we observed sharp SLO regressions caused by wholesale failovers and aggressive global load-shedding; this PR introduces two cooperating pieces: (1) a tenant-fallback-sampler which selects a bounded fraction of requests per tenant for controlled fallback to lower-cost/compatible model variants and (2) a traffic-shepherd controller that sequences regional handoffs, preserves KV prefix state during partial evacuations, and ramps traffic according to SLO telemetry. The sampler is probabilistic with configurable per-tenant caps and time-decay so we can gather quality telemetry and allow staged rollouts without impacting steady clients. The shepherd implements an epoch token that prevents rapid circuit flips and coordinates graceful KV draining and resumptions across zones. This PR also contains a small hotfix to the circuit state machine to fix a race that caused transient double-opened circuits. Scope: code in serving runtime (sampler + control loop), controlplane controller, observability hooks, config schema, unit + integration tests, and k8s manifests. Risk: medium — affects routing decisions and failover sequencing; guarded behind feature flags and opt-in config. Rollout plan: 1) merge to main behind feature flag, 2) canary to internal tenants in us-west for 48h, 3) monitor new SLO and quality dashboards, 4) gradual increase of sampling fraction and shepherd aggressiveness. Related: ENG-2281 (graceful failovers post-incident), ENG-2314 (telemetry capture for fallback quality).
Implements a bounded probabilistic tenant fallback sampler and a regional traffic shepherd controller, wires telemetry for fallback attempts and outcomes, adds feature-flagged k8s manifests, and includes a hotfix for a circuit-state race. Tests and runbook included.
Adds a probabilistic tenant fallback sampler and a traffic shepherd controller that coordinates graceful regional failovers and KV preservation. Includes telemetry events, dashboards, and a small hotfix for circuit-state flapping.
Unit tests for sampler edge cases, integration tests exercising shepherd sequencing under synthetic load, e2e scenario to validate KV preservation, microbenchmarks showing median routing decision latency increase +0.6ms under sampling enabled. CI ran full test matrix; integration tests retried once due to flakiness and passed on rerun.
Miguel Torres (2026-02-17): Great approach — can we add a guard so sampled fallback never routes to a model with different tokenization? Risk of client-facing corruption.
Evelyn Li (2026-02-18): The epoch token solves flapping but make sure controller persists last-seen epoch across restarts; otherwise we can re-open circuits prematurely.
Jordan Kim (2026-02-19): Integration test failed in first CI run with a race in shepherd start; please add deterministic startup ordering and a TTL to the epoch lock.
Miguel Torres (2026-02-22): Telemetry looks good, add a histogram for time-to-first-success after fallback so we can correlate quality regressions.
Evelyn Li (2026-02-24): Is the per-tenant cap enforced in the router policy or sampler? Make sure both enforcement and accounting are colocated to reduce drift under high concurrency.
Asha Patel (2026-02-18): Added tokenization compatibility check in router_policy.go and unit tests to assert model variant compatibility before fallback.
Asha Patel (2026-02-19): Persisted epoch in controller state store and added startup reconciliation logic to shepherd. Also added TTL to epoch lock to prevent deadlocks.
Asha Patel (2026-02-20): Fixed startup race by sequencing shepherd init after config load in the controller; updated e2e to assert stable startup ordering.
Asha Patel (2026-02-23): Added time-to-first-success histogram and a new dashboard tile. Enforced per-tenant cap inside sampler and added an optimistic local counter in router policy for rapid checks.
Asha Patel (2026-02-25): Ran additional bench runs; sampling adds ~0.6ms median latency to routing decision, 95th still within SLO for canary tenants.

payload.body:
Problem: Customers and internal compliance teams requested finer-grained control over how audit records are retained and routed depending on data residency/tenant constraints and transient operator scopes. Existing audit pipeline attached a single retention policy per-tenant which made temporary operator actions (eg emergency operator fixes) either over-retain or under-retain sensitive entries, and RBACv2 transient bindings were not annotated for audit delivery that respects retention labels.

Solution: This PR introduces a small pluggable middleware in the api-gateway/audit path that labels audit records with an explicit retention class (P0/P1/ephemeral) derived from combined inputs: tenant policy, request-scoped operator binding, and optional KMS affinity headers. In parallel this change adds a new RBACv2 transient-binding type that carries a short TTL and a retention_preference attribute. The middleware consults the rbac service for transient-binding metadata, merges it with tenant policy (tenant-level minimums are enforced), and emits an audit envelope with retention_label and delivery_hint metadata. The delivery pipeline can then route short-lived envelopes to the ephemeral-store and mark persistent ones for long-term retention.

This PR contains: 1) API changes to RBAC service to expose transient-binding metadata (read-only surface used by middleware), 2) gateway middleware that annotates audit envelopes, 3) audit-forwarder modifications to inspect retention_label and route to ephemeral vs durable stores, 4) a short e2e smoke test and unit tests for merge logic, 5) docs and release notes describing the new retention classes and operational knobs.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add retention_label plumbing in api-gateway middleware
- [x] Add transient-binding TTL and retention_preference field to RBACv2 schema (backwards compatible)
- [x] Ensure tenant-level minimum retention enforced (rejects shorter TTL than tenant min)
- [x] Audit-forwarder routing based on retention_label and delivery_hint
- [x] Unit tests and integration smoke test
- [x] Console docs draft and changelog entry

Backward compatibility: New RBAC transient-binding field is optional and defaults to null; any binding without retention_preference is treated as 'tenant-default'. Audit envelope schema adds optional retention_label/delivery_hint - older consumers ignore unknown fields. Rollout: feature gated behind flag feature.audit_retention and toggled off by default. We plan a staged rollout: gate flipped in staging for 48h, then Canary, then global.

Motivation and security considerations: the retention label is a conservative opt-in from transient operator bindings; tenant policy always wins when it requires longer retention to meet compliance. We explicitly disallow extension of retention by transient bindings (i.e., an operator cannot force longer retention than tenant min). We added integration tests exercising KMS affinity header usage to ensure audit routing metadata cannot be spoofed without proper authenticated KMS tokens.

Notes: This is primarily an infra and compliance surface change; no user-visible API surface changes except RBACv2 schema extension which is backward compatible. See release_notes for operator actions required when upgrading dedicated/private clusters (RBAC schema migration job included).
Evan Miller: Please add a unit test covering the tenant-minimum override when a transient binding requests shorter TTL — current tests only cover equal/longer cases.
Priya Desai: Added test 'TestMergeRespectsTenantMin' and updated rbacschema migration notes. Also added a guard to reject transient bindings that attempt to set ttl < tenantMin.
Sofia Martinez: The migration SQL could block in older clusters - suggest a non-blocking background migration and feature flag. Can we add a migration plan in deploy docs?
Priya Desai: Split migration into two steps and added 'scripts/migrations/2026-02-rbac-transient-bindings-async.sql' to perform schema changes first and backfill retention_preference in the background. Added deploy notes in docs/ops/audit_retention.md.
Liam O'Connor: CI flake on forwarder test - test uses a real postgres connection; please switch to test harness mock to avoid network dependency.
Priya Desai: Replaced postgres-backed test with in-memory forwarder harness; re-run CI.
Evan Miller: Approved after test fixes and docs updates.
SRE Bot: canary-checker passed for staging region us-west-2 after 24h.
Security Review: noted one low-risk issue about KMS affinity header validation - added stricter check to verify KMS token signature - addressed in gateway middleware.
Priya Desai: responded and added verification helper 'kms/verify_affinity_token.go'.
Unit tests added for merge logic and tenant minimum enforcement. Forwarder tests use in-memory harness to verify routing. A small e2e smoke test deploys gateway+forwarder to test namespace and verifies ephemeral vs durable buckets receive expected envelope counts. Canary run in us-west-2 for 48h showed 0 failures and expected retention label distribution. Manual security review verified KMS affinity token signature check.
Introduce audit retention labels and RBACv2 transient-binding TTL/retention_preference. Feature gated behind 'feature.audit_retention'. Operators must run the provided non-blocking migration if upgrading clusters older than 2026-02 and review console changes for transient binding creation. See docs/ops/audit_retention.md for migration steps and operational guidance.
When enabling feature.audit_retention: 1) Ensure background migration script '2026-02-rbac-transient-bindings-async.sql' is scheduled; 2) Confirm ephemeral store (S3 prefix or ephemeral DB) configured for locality-sensitive ephemeral audit; 3) Monitor 'audit.retention.label' metric and set alerts if >5% of operator actions are labeled 'ephemeral' unexpectedly.

Motivation: Long-running invocations and verbose token-level traces make triage costly for SREs. We need a compact, low-cardinality synopsis per invocation plus a lightweight RCA suggestion layer that correlates invocation fingerprints with SLO signal shifts. This PR implements a sampled Invocation Synopsis pipeline and an SLO Root-Cause Mapper to reduce time-to-blame and surface high-probability causes without exploding telemetry cardinality. Summary of changes: add a new invocation_summary v1 schema, a synthesizer that compacts the invocation shape (prompt length buckets, kv-cache-miss-flag, kernel-wait-buckets, observable tool-calls) into a short fingerprint, a priority sampler that emits summaries for a configurable fraction of invocations, dashboard panels for aggregated synopsis views and sample drilldowns, SLO-RCA alert rules that surface correlated signals (kernel contention, queueing percentiles, prefix-cache-hit-rate) and a rollout feature flag. Implementation notes: invocation_synthesizer runs in the telemetry producer to avoid extra RPC hops; we use a deterministic sharding hash to limit ephemeral label cardinality; the sampler is backpressure-aware so overhead at peak RPS stays bounded. Backwards compatibility: new metric name invocation_summary_total and associated labels are additive only; all existing spans and token metrics remain unchanged. Testing: added unit tests for synthesizer logic, integration tests for sampler ingestion, and end-to-end dashboard smoke tests in CI. Rollout plan: gate by feature-flag, enable low-rate sampling in staging for 48h, then increase sampling and enable SLO-RCA alerts behind a second flag for SRE verification. Checklist: 1) Telemetry schema added and proto-validated. 2) Sampler and synthesizer implemented and unit-tested. 3) Dashboard + alert rules added and smoke-tested. 4) Docs/Runbook updated. 5) Feature flags added for gradual rollout. Performance: initial benchmarks included in docs show <1% CPU overhead at 100k RPS and p99 added latency <1.5ms for the telemetry path when sampling at 1%. CI: first run failed lint in console TS; addressed in follow-up commit; full test-suite passed on second run (unit, integration, dashboard-smoke). Review: Diego raised cardinality concerns and requested TTL/capping which was implemented; Priya requested perf numbers which are now in docs; Ethan requested no change to SLO baselines and a gated rollout. Merge: after approvals, PR was squashed and merged into main on 2026-02-26. Impact and next steps: monitor invocation_summary_total and invocation_synopsis_error_rate for 2 weeks, collect sampling coverage metrics and adjust sampling policy; follow up with an augmentation that ties sampled synthetics to full-span replay when an SLA breach is detected. Related: linked Linear tasks ENG-4821 and ENG-4890 and support ticket SUP-1223.
Diego Marquez: Concern about cardinality introduced by invocation_summary labels; asked for explicit cardinality bounds and fallback path. Author response: added tokenized shape hashing and capped label cardinality with documented TTL for ephemeral keys.
Priya Nair: Asked for perf numbers for sampler overhead under 100k RPS. Author response: added benchmark numbers to docs (avg 0.8% CPU, <1.2ms p99 added latency with sampling enabled on a 16-vCPU instance).
Ethan Brooks: Requested that alerts not change existing SLO baselines; suggested feature-flag gating. Author response: implemented rollout flag and added migration notes for SRE runbook.
CI Bot: initial lint failure for TS formatting. Author: fixed formatting in second commit. Diego: approved pending one doc clarification. Priya: approved. Ethan: approved and merged.

This PR adds a set of internal rollout cohort dashboards (Grafana) and alert templates (Prometheus rule groups + notification routing defaults) to support Hosted canary rollouts. The intent is to standardize the signals SRE/Oncall and product teams watch during a rollout, reduce time-to-diagnosis when the canary regresses, and provide sensible defaults for the auto-stop/rollback thresholds work. The dashboards are built around the new rollout_id + cohort tags (baseline/canary) and include guardrails to avoid high-cardinality views by default.

What’s included: (1) Grafana dashboards: A “Hosted Rollout Overview” dashboard (per tenant + route) that shows rollout state context (rollout_id, step %, regions) and top-line SLO signals side-by-side for baseline vs canary: request rate, 5xx rate, timeout rate, cancellation rate (streaming), and p50/p95/p99 latency. A “Cohort Comparison Deep Dive” dashboard with latency heatmaps by model + region, tokens/sec (where present), and a panel to compare deltas (canary - baseline) with a configurable lookback. A “Rollout Debug” dashboard focused on data-plane symptoms: routing decisions, cohort assignment distribution, retry rates, and mismatch indicators. All dashboards default to route + region filters and require explicit rollout_id selection for per-rollout drilldown.

(2) Alert templates: Adds alert rule groups intended for oncall and as building blocks for the rollout orchestrator auto-stop logic: ElevatedCanary5xxRate, ElevatedCanaryTimeoutRate, CanaryP95LatencyRegression (relative to baseline), and CanaryErrorBudgetBurn (short window) with recommended thresholds and evaluation windows aligned to minimum soak time. Alerts are written to be cohort-aware and to suppress noise when traffic is < N req/min (to reduce false positives in early steps like 1% and 5%). We also add a companion alert “RolloutCohortMetricsMissing” to catch telemetry gaps (e.g., rollout_id tag not present or aggregation pipeline lagging).

(3) Docs/runbook pointers embedded in dashboards: Each dashboard has a “What to do next” text panel linking to the internal runbook for stuck/bad split and to the hosted rollouts SLO metrics guidance so that oncall has a single place to start.

Cardinality / performance notes: dashboards intentionally avoid top-K by rollout_id across all tenants. The only global view is a rollup by route + region with optional drilldown. Where queries require rollout_id, they are gated behind a variable and are scoped to a single tenant. There is also a new recording rule to pre-aggregate cohort rates by (tenant_id, route_id, region, cohort) to keep dashboard queries fast.

Testing: Verified in staging with a seeded canary rollout (10% step) and validated panels render under 5s. Confirmed alert rules load and evaluate without missing series. Also validated that early-stage traffic (< 30 rpm) does not trigger latency regression alerts.

Rollout plan: Land behind internal enablement only; dashboards are not customer-visible. SRE can import the dashboards via the existing grafana-sync job. Alert rules are deployed with the standard prometheus-rules bundle and are disabled by default in prod until beta tuning is complete.

Follow-ups (not in scope): (a) Add a UI link from Console rollout page to the internal Grafana dashboard for employees (requires auth boundary work). (b) Quality-metric panels once we have standardized quality signals. (c) Dedicated/Private dashboard variants once cohort tags are enabled there.

Refs: ENG-9152 (telemetry tags + aggregation), ENG-9158 (auto-stop/rollback), PM-1859 (GA checklist - monitoring + runbooks).
Sean Gallagher: Love the direction. Two asks: (1) ensure alerts don’t fire at 1% when traffic is tiny, and (2) add an explicit panel for cohort split distribution (expected vs observed) because we’ve already seen mismatch issues in beta.
Aisha Bello (author): Added a traffic floor (req/min) to all regression alerts and documented it in the alert README. Also added a “Cohort distribution” panel to the Debug dashboard using the routing decision counter and the cohort tag, scoped to route+region.
Thomas Baird: Query cost looks OK for single-tenant drilldown, but the overview dashboard still has a variable that defaults to ‘All tenants’ and could be expensive. Can we hard-disable ‘All’ for tenant_id and require explicit selection?
Aisha Bello (author): Good catch. Updated dashboard variables: tenant_id is required (no ‘All’), and rollout_id is hidden until tenant_id is selected. Also moved some rate calcs to recording rules to reduce panel query complexity.
Allison Grant: Can we tighten the latency regression definition? Relative deltas can be noisy if baseline is already degraded. Suggest adding an absolute guard (e.g., canary p95 > X ms) OR use baseline+delta. Also please add a note about streaming vs non-streaming routes since p95 for streaming time-to-first-token is different.
Aisha Bello (author): Implemented baseline+delta style: canary_p95 > baseline_p95 * (1 + pct) and canary_p95 > absolute_ms. Added separate panels for TTFT vs end-to-end latency when the metric exists, and noted streaming caveats in the dashboard info panel.
Logan Wright: Looks aligned with the tagging work. One concern: recording rule labels include rollout_id in one rule group—can we drop rollout_id from recording rules to avoid cardinality issues and keep per-rollout drilldown on raw series only?
Aisha Bello (author): Agreed. Removed rollout_id from all recording rules. Per-rollout drilldown panels now query raw series filtered by rollout_id (scoped to tenant+route+region). Recording rules only cover (tenant_id, route_id, region, cohort).
Felix Schneider: Minor: Can we rename ‘baseline’/‘canary’ legend labels to match Console wording (‘Control’/‘Canary’)? Also the dashboard description mentions ‘tokens/sec’ but we don’t have that everywhere.
Aisha Bello (author): Updated legend aliases to Control/Canary. Adjusted tokens/sec panels to be conditional with a ‘not available for this route/model’ text when series are missing.
Sean Gallagher: Final pass looks good. Approved once the prod default for alerts is disabled and there’s a clear enablement note.
Aisha Bello (author): Added ‘disabled by default’ in the rule manifest and a comment with the enablement steps + owner (SRE) for beta tuning.
Sean Gallagher: Approved.
Allison Grant: Approved.
Thomas Baird: Approved.
Internal only: adds standard Grafana dashboards and Prometheus alert templates for Hosted rollout cohort monitoring (baseline/control vs canary), including latency/error/timeout regressions with traffic floors and a metrics-missing alert to detect tagging/aggregation gaps.
