payload.body:
Summary: Fixes intermittent streaming corruption seen when SSE chunk boundaries split tool/function sentinel sequences and partial JSON payloads. This PR introduces a lightweight staggered checkpoint control event, a boundary-anchored emit heuristic for tool/function calls, and improved reassembly bookkeeping to guarantee ordered emit or safe resync. Motivation: In the field we observed rare but high-impact cases where a tool call sentinel ("tool_call_start" / "tool_call_end") would be split across network chunk boundaries and the downstream OpenAI-compat client would reconstruct a malformed partial JSON object or invoke tooling out of order. These failures mainly happened under head-of-line reordering during multi-tenant batching and when clients used aggressive chunk streaming. The goal is to stop premature emission of tool-boundary-anchored JSON fragments while keeping tail latency and streaming experience intact. Design: 1) Introduce a new SSE control event type: "checkpoint" with a lightweight seq_id and crc-like short checksum. The checkpoint is emitted at safe flush points (e.g., after a function-call sentinel completes, and periodically for long streams). 2) Staggered checkpointing: checkpoints are allowed to overlap in a staggered window so senders may emit a checkpoint for the earlier span before the later span finishes; receivers use seq_id to reorder or detect missing spans. 3) Emit heuristic for tool/function boundaries: the runtime defers emitting a closing tool sentinel until one of three conditions: a) matching checkpoint observed, b) KV-cache prefix confirms completeness for the span, or c) timeout (50ms default) expires. This avoids holding tokens for long but protects against split-sentinel corruption. 4) Reassembly bookkeeping: augment the stream ledger with minimal per-span metadata (seq_id, expected-boundary-hash, length-hint) so receivers can attempt in-order reassembly and safe resync on checksum mismatch. Implementation notes: - Added sse/checkpoint event encoder and parser with backward-compatibility: old clients ignore unknown event types. - Tight integration with the framing layer: checkpoints are emitted as distinct SSE events (event: checkpoint) with a compact payload. - Adjusted the stream flusher to prefer emitting hard checkpoints at tool-call boundaries and every ~512 tokens in long-lived streams. - Added a receiver-side resync routine: when a boundary checksum fails, the client tries windowed reassembly using adjacent chunks and waits up to 120ms before dropping to a resync marker event (rescue) to avoid silent truncation. Commits (high-level): - 3c1a8d9: add checkpoint event encoder/decoder and unit tests - 9b2f7a3: integrate staggered checkpoint emit points into flusher and toolcall sequence - a7f4d21: receiver ledger bookkeeping, resync heuristic, and integration tests - b8e5c2f: add e2e SSE stress test harness and flaky-case reproduction fixture - d4f6e11: docs and release notes, config knobs for checkpoint-timeout Changed files ( high level): - sse/encoder.go (new) - sse/parser.go (changed) - sse/checkpoint.proto (new small event schema) - runtime/flusher.go (changed) - runtime/toolflow.go (changed) - client/reassembly.go (new) - tests/sse_integration_test.go (new) - tests/fixtures/partial_tool_split.json (new) - docs/streaming-stability.md (changed) Tests and CI: - Unit tests: new coverage for checkpoint encode/decode, seq_id validation, and timeout paths. - Integration tests: added a deterministic split-case that previously reproduced the bug; initial run showed a flaky failure under network jitter simulation. - E2E stress tests: added harness that simulates multi-tenant batching with intermittent chunk reorder. - CI history: first run: unit pass, integration flaky failure (timing-based), lint pass. Re-ran integration with increased jitter seed; passed. Final CI: all checks passing. Review timeline and conversation (condensed): - Diego Ramirez (reviewer): "Nice approach; small concern about the default 50ms hold — could it increase tail latency for tiny requests?" - Author (Maya Chen): "Agreed. Tunable config added (stream.toolBoundaryHoldMs) and we set default to 50ms after internal perf sweep. Added benchmarks to docs to justify tradeoff." - Asha Patel: "Receiver resync seems complex; can we avoid adding too much state to clients?" - Maya Chen: "Receiver state is intentionally minimal: seq_id + 8-byte boundary-hash + length-hint. Fallback is identical to pre-PR behavior (rescue event) if we can't reconcile quickly. Also included a feature flag to gate behavior for canary rollout." - Liam O'Connor: "Integration test is great. Please add metric for resync events so we can monitor in prod." - Author: "Added metrics: sse.resync_attempts and sse.checkpoint_mismatch_rate. Also added a dashboard note in docs." Review actions and changes made: - Added configuration knobs for hold timeout and checkpoint cadence - Reduced memory footprint of ledger entries (compact encoding) - Added metrics and dashboard guidance - Clarified docs and added example for backwards compatibility with older clients Approvals: - Diego: approved after timeout knob change - Asha: approved after ledger size reduction - Liam: approved after metrics added Merge: Squash-and-merge on 2025-10-11. Post-merge actions: - Feature-flag rollout: enabled for 10% of production traffic for one week, monitor sse.checkpoint_mismatch_rate and sse.resync_attempts. - If mismatch rate spike > 0.1% roll back flag immediately. Observed results during canary: no regressions in tail-p99 latency, resync attempts rare (<0.02%). Notes to integration teams: - Clients who rely on the exact timing of partial frames should not assume immediate emission of tool_call_end; instead, respect checkpoint control events and rescue markers. - Server-to-client backward compatibility preserved: older clients will ignore checkpoint events and continue to receive raw chunks (but may be vulnerable to split-sentinel cases). - Recommend SDK update (client-side reassembly) shipped in redwood-sdk-typescript and redwood-sdk-python shortly to improve client robustness (follow-up PRs linked). Related/Follow-ups: - ENG-5832: SDK client reassembly helpers (follow-up) - ENG-5891: telemetry alerting for streaming mismatches Unique considerations and rationale: - We deliberately chose a short hold timeout (50ms default) because empirical testing showed most split-sentinel races resolved within a few tens of milliseconds; longer holds harm latency. - Staggered checkpoints avoid global pause points and keep streaming semantics intact for long-running responses. - Minimal receiver ledger keeps overhead low for edge clients and makes the change safe to roll out gradually. Triage notes: This PR addresses a cluster of customer-reported incidents (SUP-112) where downstream tool invocation order was observed to be incorrect for a small subset of streaming sessions. The fix reduces incidence dramatically in canary and is backward-compatible.
Fixes edge-case SSE reassembly where tool/function call sentinel events could be emitted before surrounding JSON frames were fully reassembled. Adds a staggered checkpoint control event to stabilize delimiting and reduces partial-JSON emission regressions. Backwards compatible with existing clients.

payload.body:
Motivation: We continue to see noisy alerts tied to tail invocation cost/latency signals where single noisy features (e.g. transient kernel queueing) dominate. Instead of ad-hoc suppression rules, this PR introduces a lightweight decision-tree scorer for invocation telemetry that assigns an explainable risk score and a deterministic decay policy. In addition, this PR adds a synthetic-alert replayer (replaybench) that can ingest sampled invocation logs and rerun alert scoring to validate tuning before rollouts.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Adds a new telemetry pipeline stage (invocation_decider) that computes invocation.decision_score and invocation.decision_reason_tags; surfaces aggregated decision histograms and cohort breakdowns to the telemetry store; ships a replaybench utility that can run historical invocation samples through the same decision logic to simulate alert churn and estimate false positive reduction; provides new Grafana dashboard panels and alert rule variants for staged rollout; adds e2e tests and unit tests, and extends CI to run the replaybench on a small synthetic dataset.

Files changed (high level): lists core scorer implementation (telemetry/decision_tree/scorer.py), replay harness (telemetry/replaybench/runner.py), sampler adapter (telemetry/adapters/sampled_ingest.py), schema migrations (telemetry/schemas/2025_11_invocation_decider.sql), dashboards (dashboards/decision-tree-invocations.json), alert rules (alerts/invocation-decision-rules.yaml), docs and runbook (docs/observability/decision-tree-runbook.md), and a small integration test (tests/integration/test_replaybench_end2end.py).

How it works: The decision-tree scorer is a shallow deterministic tree (trained offline and checked-in as a static rule set) that combines binned features: kernel_queue_ms, kv_cache_miss_ratio, prefix_length, model_variant, and cpu_percentile. The scorer produces a numeric score 0..100 and a compact set of reason tags (e.g. "queueing:high", "kv:missy"). The replaybench loads historical sampled invocations, computes scores and simulates alert triggers with current threshold configs, and reports per-cohort FP/TP estimates and expected alert volume delta.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for scorer logic and tag extraction. Integration test runs replaybench with a 20k-sample fixture (stored in test-fixtures/) and asserts alert volume reduction >= 10% without degrading recall for verified incident cases. CI change: a new workflow job (observability/replaybench) kicks off on PRs touching telemetry/ or alerts/ and runs a small synthetic dataset (fast) in CI.

Rollout plan: Canary rollout on staging telemetry ingest for 48h with decision_score exposed but not used for suppression; observability dashboard bookmarked for SRE. Next, staged alert rule variant (alpha -> beta -> global) toggled via feature flag on the console. Rollback mechanism: drop the decision flag or revert rule in the alerting engine.

Runbook and operational notes: New runbook at docs/observability/decision-tree-runbook.md documents how to interpret decision_reason_tags, query alert replays, and how to tune thresholds for specific tenants. The replaybench output includes per-tenant delta tables and recommended threshold adjustments.

Related: ENG-2382 (alert-noise-reduction), PM-4125 (observability UX for decision scores).
Priya Kapoor (request changes): Please confirm worst-case compute cost for the replaybench; CI shouldn't run full 20k fixture on every PR.
Ethan Brooks (author): Added a small fast fixture for CI (telemetry/replaybench/fixtures/ci_sample.ndjson) and gated the large replaybench behind a --full flag. Updated CI job to use the fast fixture.
Marcel Nguyen (comment): The decision_reason_tags look useful; can we add a short label set mapping in the runbook for SRE queries?
Ethan Brooks (author): Added mapping table in docs/observability/decision-tree-runbook.md with example queries and recommended tag filters.
Sofia Martinez (approve): Verified scoreboard on staging; observed 12% reduction in non-actionable alerts across sampled tenants.
Addressed CI cost concerns by introducing a small CI fixture and gating the large run; added runbook mapping for tags; reviewers approved after staging verification.
Add invocation decision-tree scorer and synthetic replaybench for validating alert tuning. Exposes invocation.decision_score and invocation.decision_reason_tags; includes dashboards and staged alert variants.
Run telemetry/schemas/2025_11_invocation_decider.sql against the telemetry store. Backfill is optional: run replaybench with --backfill to annotate historical invocations. Toggle decision scoring via feature flag in the console under Observability -> Feature Gates.
Unit tests cover scorer boundaries and tag extraction; integration test uses a 2k-sample CI fixture and a larger 20k fixture for local verification. Replaybench can be run locally: python -m telemetry.replaybench.runner --input test-fixtures/20k.ndjson --simulate-alerts --output replay-report.json
If alert volume drops unexpectedly for a tenant after rollout, query invocation.decision_score distribution and run replaybench for that tenant ID to compare triggers. Revert alert variant via console feature flag or edit alerts/invocation-decision-rules.yaml.

Motivation: Our monolithic presubmit pipelines have grown slow and brittle. Small iterative PRs (docs, small SDK fixes) incur the same full integration battery as large runtime changes which increases feedback time and developer context switching. This change introduces a presubmit router that categorizes PRs into fast, standard, and full lanes using a deterministic set of rules and a lightweight risk score computed from touched paths, labels, and historical flakiness.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a deterministic presubmit router service (ci/presubmit-router/) which evaluates PR metadata and outputs a lane decision. 2) Adds a minimal toolchain bundle image and accompanying scripts (scripts/toolchain-bundle/) to provide hermetic, fast warm images used by fastpath CI and local dev containers. 3) Reworks our .github workflow entrypoints to support conditional lane selection and staged job expansion. 4) Introduces a small shim library (packages/ci-utils) that other repos can call to mirror routing decisions locally (devcontainer and CI parity).

Design notes and tradeoffs: - Router criteria are intentionally conservative: fast lane excludes runtime, serving, infra, and docs that touch build tooling itself. The initial rule set is configurable via a simple YAML config checked into ci/presubmit-router/config.yaml. - The toolchain bundle is purposefully minimal (clang, go, node, python pinned versions) to avoid large image sizes; it reduces cold build variance and speeds up hotspot tests. - We deliberately avoid replacing the existing QA gates; this is a progressive optimization that only skips heavy jobs for low-risk PRs.

Checklist implemented: - [x] Presubmit router service implementation and unit tests. - [x] Workflow templates updated to call router and expand job matrix conditionally. - [x] Toolchain bundle image build scripts and README. - [x] Shim library with local router client and a thin CLI. - [x] Integration smoke: fastpath jobs exercised on a canary org. - [x] Docs: docs/ci/README.md describing rules and how to override.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind a feature flag defaulting to off. 2) Run canary on low-risk repos (docs, examples, sdk- typescript) for one week. 3) Collect fastpath hit/miss metrics and adjust rule set. 4) Gradually enable for more repos once flakiness < 1% and false-skip rate < 0.5%.

Backwards compatibility: Workflows maintain an opt-out label (ci/full) and an environment variable to force full runs. Existing presubmit behavior remains available.

Related: ENG-2992 for fastpath metrics collection and ENG-3010 for toolchain pinning policy. SUP-1128 tracked a support incident where a flaky test was exacerbated by cold toolchain images.

Testing summary: Unit tests cover router logic, e2e smoke in a sandbox org verified job expansion, toolchain bundle built and validated in both Linux and macOS runners. CI initially flagged a flaky lint job which was fixed by improving the linter wrapper to respect workspace node_modules in devcontainer images.

Summary: Introduces the Slot Duration Batcher, a new adaptive batching heuristic that packs requests into time-slots sized by predicted sequence-duration rather than fixed seqlen buckets. Motivation: observed pad-waste and frequent kernel-context switches when workloads contained wide variance in sequence lengths; existing bucketing reduces waste but causes kernel churn for marginal length differences and doesn't account for KV cache locality. Design/heuristic: 1) compute light-weight duration estimate for each request using prefix-length, model profile and estimated decode budget; 2) place incoming requests into active slots where the predicted extra padding cost is minimized, preferring slots with similar decode-duration to preserve kernel locality and KV cache reuse; 3) apply soft slot expiration (ms granularity) to avoid latency tail; 4) kernel-hinting: expose per-slot dominant sequence-length to the kernel selection layer so it can pick quantized kernels optimized for that effective seqlen. API/Config: opt-in runtime flag runtime.batch_strategy=slot_duration plus tunables: slot_max_wait_ms, slot_duration_quant, pad_waste_threshold. Implementation notes: added a lightweight slot manager in runtimes/batching with O(1) amortized insert/evict, a kernel-hint propagation path to the scheduler, and KV-cache affinity heuristics to prefer grouping requests that touch overlapping key-ranges. Benchmark summary: - Mixed chat workload (Pareto: 70% short <64, 30% long 256-1024): baseline dynamic bucketing: mean latency 83ms p50 45ms p95 220ms; slot-duration-batcher: mean latency 76ms p50 42ms p95 190ms (-9% mean, -14% p95) and token-cost reduced by ~11% due to pad reduction. - Large-batch throughput test on A100 80GB: sustained throughput improvement +6-9% for heterogeneous sequences. Safety: batch strategy is opt-in; fallbacks to existing bucket-based batcher if slot saturation occurs. Rollout plan: feature gated on dedicated and hosted; start with low-traffic rollout, monitor token-cost and latency SLOs. Commits: ["Add slot-duration-batcher core loop and tests","Expose kernel-hint path to scheduler and unit tests","KV-affinity heuristics and metrics","Config knobs and console visibility","Bench harness and perf numbers"] Changed files (high-level): ["runtimes/batching/slot_duration_batcher.py","runtimes/scheduler/kernel_hint_manager.cc","runtimes/kv/kv_affinity_tracker.cc","runtimes/batching/slot_metrics.prom","benchmarks/mixed_length/slot_bench_runner.py","docs/runtimes/slot_duration_batcher.md","console/frontend/src/routes/batch-optimizer.tsx","tests/batching/test_slot_packing.py"] Small illustrative snippet: "if slot.can_accept(req) and slot.pad_increase(req) < config.pad_waste_threshold: slot.add(req) else create_new_slot(req)" Testing: unit tests for slot packing heuristics, integration tests that compare token counts vs existing bucketer, e2e perf harness against current production traces. Metrics added: slot.pad_waste_bytes, slot.kernel_switch_count, slot.kv_affinity_hit. Observability: console exposes per-model slot histogram and per-route token-savings estimate. Review conversation (high-level): ["Omar Liu: Can you clarify worst-case queueing latency when slots wait for longer requests? Request adding tests that simulate pathological long tail.", "Diya Patel: Added soft-expiry and new integration test 'test_slot_tail_latency' that asserts 95th latency impact < +10ms for skewed workloads.", "Sofia Martinez: Kernel-hint path looks good, but please ensure we don't leak scheduler internals into public console telemetry.", "Diya Patel: kernel-hints are private runtime attributes; console shows aggregate histograms only. Adjusted console component to strip internal tags.", "Liam O'Connor: Approve after CI fixes for flakiness in test_slot_packing.py.", "Diya Patel: Fixed race by substituting deterministic clock in tests; re-ran CI."] CI history: initial run: unit fail (flaky timer) -> fix applied -> rerun -> all checks passed (unit, integration, lint, typecheck, bench smoke). Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2026-03-09 after approvals. Notes for maintainers: watch slot.kernel_switch_count for early signs of regressions; slot_duration_batcher can be toggled off without restart. Related work: prior PRs experimented with sequence bucketing and padding minimization; this approach targets operational stability and kernel locality together. Linear/Jira: ENG-4821 (slot batcher design), ENG-4890 (kernel hint plumbing), SUP-3302 (customer report on pad-waste), internal link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4821.
Introduces Slot Duration Batcher: an opt-in runtime batching strategy that groups in-flight requests into variable-duration slots to reduce padding waste and minimize kernel warp transitions. Enabled via runtime config; no API changes. Improves throughput for mixed-length workloads and reduces per-token cost in common web-chat workloads.

Adds a hierarchical token cost atlas for per-tenant/route/invocation attribution; new dashboards and an alert fallthrough policy to reduce noisy long-tail SLO pages. Feature gated; no behavior change until enabled.
Motivation: Long-tail token cost + latency noise makes SLO paging noisy for routes with highly variable prompt shapes. Existing token-level metrics are flat and expensive to query when you want to slice by route -> model-stage -> tenant. This PR introduces a compact, hierarchical token cost atlas to make per-segment attribution fast and shippable to dashboards/alerts.

Goals: 1) provide a compact index (atlas) that aggregates token cost/latency by hierarchical keys (tenant, route, model_stage, segment_shingle) while remaining query-friendly; 2) power a conservative alert fallthrough policy that escalates pages only when multiple hierarchy levels show correlated degradation; 3) minimize runtime overhead using sketch summaries and reservoir rollups; 4) expose a Console viewer and Grafana-ready panels for exploration.

What this change does: single continuous implementation across the telemetry pipeline: (a) a changed telemetry collector that emits atlas records (compact sketches + top-k signatures) to the metric store; (b) a lightweight span enricher that attaches atlas_signature and token.bucket_id to long-running spans; (c) an aggregation service that materializes daily/rolling atlas rollups; (d) dashboard JSON for the Console and Grafana panels: Token Cost Atlas, Atlas Explorer, and Route Correlator; (e) new alerting policy engine additions implementing the fallthrough logic (alert groups with progressive sensitivity and correlation windowing).

Backward compatibility & rollout: The feature is behind an observability feature flag (obs.hierarchical_token_atlas). When disabled nothing is emitted. New metric names are under the redwood.atlas.* namespace. Migration steps are in docs/observability/hierarchical-token-atlas.md. We coordinate retention changes with infra; default retention unchanged.

Performance & cost: Microbenchmarks show ~3-5% CPU on collector when atlas is enabled for high-traffic clusters; we use count-min sketches and a fixed-size reservoir to bound memory and cardinality. Integration tests include a synthetic replaybench (tests/atlas_integration_test.go) exercising worst-case cardinality.

Rollout plan: Feature-flag rollout to internal canary -> tenant opt-in in Console -> enable by default for Dedicated in 2 weeks if no regressions.

Risks & mitigations: Risk of label explosion mitigated by signature shingling and atlas bucketization; alert noise avoided using fallthrough groups and correlation windows.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the atlas writer and downstream query API separate so dashboards can be swapped to other stores later. More follow-ups planned: automated atlas compaction, per-tenant retention tuning, and a small SDK addition to pull atlas slices for offline evals.

Motivation: Long-lived streamed tool/function calls can fail transiently in places that make naive retries unsafe (partial frames, duplicated tool executions, or inconsistent state). We need a minimal, backward-compatible on-the-wire contract that lets clients express retry intent and lets servers reason about whether a retry is safe without requiring full request bodies to be replayed. This PR introduces two complementary primitives: (1) Retry-Token: an opaque, short-lived token clients attach to retry attempts to indicate a controlled replay window; (2) Idempotency-Session: a server-scoped session identifier used to sequence tool-call frames and ensure at-most-once semantics for side-effecting frames. The goal is pragmatic: improve robustness of streamed tool calls and streaming responses, while preserving OpenAI-compat adapter behavior when present.
Background: we observed two classes of production incidents: (1) clients retrying after a stream ECONNRESET leading to duplicate external tool execution; (2) partial frames being repeated causing downstream consumers to misinterpret state. Prior fixes relied on best-effort client behavior and documentation. This PR provides a portable primitive that explicit clients can opt-in to and servers can use to enforce safe replay windows. It also harmonizes the OpenAI-compat layer: we map Idempotency-Key for unary calls to Idempotency-Session when appropriate, but streaming paths prefer the new headers.
OpenAI-compat: unchanged semantics for simple (non-streaming) completions that already use Idempotency-Key. For streaming endpoints the shim will accept both the legacy OpenAI header and the new X-Redwood-* headers; when both are present X-Redwood-* takes precedence. SDKs: published a minor client release with helpers. Rolling deploy: server defaults ensure no immediate behavior change for callers that do not send headers.
Added unit tests for token validation and TTL eviction; end-to-end integration tests simulate: normal execution, reconnect-with-retry-token/resume, concurrent retry attempts, and failure modes (expired token, session mismatch). Test matrix run in CI included Linux amd64 and a lightweight macOS matrix for SDK tests. All tests green.
Evan Liu: overall this looks good. A couple of safety checks: ensure session leases are bounded and cannot be abused to hold memory indefinitely. Also add metrics for session expiration and forced eviction.
Author (Maya Patel): responded: added a lease TTL with 5 minute default and a hard eviction after 1 hour; implemented metrics 'stream.idempotency_session.active' and 'stream.idempotency_session.evicted'.
Carlos Gomez: noted a potential race where two concurrent retries with different Retry-Tokens could both succeed if the initial run is slow. Suggest atomically claiming a session sequence index before executing side effects.
Author: implemented sequence claim in session_manager.go and added integration tests that simulate concurrent retries; updated docs with sequencing guidance.
Priya Menon: approved after verifying tests and SDK header helpers. Left a small docs nit which was fixed.
CI: all checks passed (unit, integration, lint, go vet). Merge queued and completed via squash merge.
Adds Retry-Token header and Idempotency-Session behavior for streamed tool calls. Backwards compatible: servers accept requests without tokens and default to previous behavior; OpenAI-compat shim maps existing Idempotency-Key. Users should update SDKs to use the helper for retries to avoid duplicate side-effects. See docs/api/retry_and_idempotency.md for migration steps and examples.

Context and motivation: We continue to see production noise from repeated delimiter emission and mid-stream partial-JSON bursts under variable network conditions. This causes downstream OpenAI-compat layers and SDK consumers to reparse/repair fragments frequently, increasing CPU and spurious function-call ordering anomalies. The goal of this PR is to reduce churn at the protocol boundary by introducing a lightweight stream sync heuristic combined with a delimiter-damping window that suppresses noisy delimiter repetition while preserving strict event ordering and function/tool-call semantics.

What changed (high level): 1) delimiter_damping: a short-time-window dampener that collapses repeated stream terminators (",\n\n"/"\n") emitted in rapid succession into a stable single terminator plus a compact marker. This is intentionally conservative: we only collapse when sequence IDs and token cursors indicate no intervening payload could have been lost. 2) sync heuristic: compute a trailing-kv-length fingerprint and seq-ack delta over the last N fragments. When the heuristic detects stable ack progression, we allow coalescing and a small reordering tolerance for heartbeats. 3) function-call handoff: ensure that tool/function call sentinel ordering is maintained by adding a final flush-to-epoch barrier before emitting a functioncall sentinel; this prevents off-by-one cases where a delimiter coalescer delayed earlier bytes. 4) compatibility adapter: small changes to openai_compat stream adapter to accept the compact marker and resume reassembly without triggering a partial-JSON repair path.

Commits (summary):
- 1a3f2b5 introduce delimiter damping module and tests
- 2c7d9e4 add trailing-kv-length sync heuristic and integration with parser
- b4f88d1 adjust functioncall flush ordering and add epoch barrier
- d9e2ab0 update openai_compat adapter to recognize compact marker and resume
- 8c6f0e7 add benchmarks and regression tests for partial-JSON scenarios

Files touched (high level):
- server/streaming/parser.rs (new damping + heuristic hooks)
- server/streaming/heuristics/damping.rs (core algorithm and tests)
- server/streaming/heuristics/sync.rs (trailing-kv fingerprint logic)
- sdk/openai_compat/stream_adapter.py (compact marker handling)
- bench/streaming/partial_json_bench.py (bench harness and datasets)
- server/streaming/tests/test_partial_json_reassembly.rs (integration tests)
- docs/streaming/damping-notes.md (design rationale and configuration)

Testing and CI: Unit tests added for the damping module and sync heuristic. Integration tests replicate upstream partial-JSON scenarios recorded from PROD incident logs (SUP-883). Benchmarks show ~48% reduction in reparsing events on a simulated 100ms jitter path, and a 12% CPU reduction in the OpenAI-compat adapter under heavy burst traffic. The CI run initially failed one flake (async test timeout) on macOS runners; reran the job and green across all matrices._CI details: build ↦ pass, unit-tests ↦ pass, integration-tests ↦ pass, lint ↦ pass.

Review thread summary:
- Ethan: asked for proof that coalescing doesn't mask genuine loss — provided the sync fingerprint checks and updated comments. Requested that the damping window be configurable at runtime (added via parser config).
- Maya: requested a microbenchmark for functioncall ordering — added bench and synthetic test. Also asked for a clear fallback path if the compact marker is unrecognized by older clients (added a compatibility parity mode that emits both traditional delimiter + marker for one epoch).
- Lucas: questioned safety of collapsing newlines when UTF-8 sequences span fragments — added explicit UTF-8 boundary checks and tests for split-UTF8 sequences.
- Author replies: clarified heuristics, added comments, and tightened gating conditions. All reviewers approved after two iterations.

Notes on rollout and ops: default damping window set to 80ms and can be tuned via the stream_parser.damping.window_ms flag in the config. The rollout plan is canary to 5% for 24h with enhanced observability (emit "damping.event" metric and "sync.heuristic.score" histogram). If any increase in client-side repair rates is observed, we will revert via feature flag.

Release notes: Reduce partial-JSON reparsing and improve stability of SSE streaming by collapsing noisy delimiters and adding a stream-sync heuristic. Backwards compatible; safe default.

Related work: builds on prior stream-resync and fragment-checkpoint efforts (see ENG-2141 and PRs that introduced span checkpoints), but differs by focusing on short-term delimiter noise suppression and a lightweight trailing fingerprint instead of heavy checkpointing.

Ethan Zhang: please prove coalescing doesn't hide dropped payloads -> added trailing-kv fingerprint checks and config tunables.
Maya Singh: functioncall ordering microbenchmark? -> added bench + synthetic ordering test, added compatibility dual-emission mode.
Lucas Ortega: UTF-8 split safety? -> added explicit boundary checks and tests for split-UTF8 fragments.
Author (Priya Rao): addressed comments, clarified gating, added feature flag and metrics. Approvals after two iterations.

Rollout: staged canary at 5% for 24h with damping.event and sync.heuristic.score telemetry. Metrics to watch: client-repair-rate, stream-reassembly-latency, damping.suppression_count.

Motivation: provide a lightweight, engineering-facing analysis and suggester (CLI + runtime hints) that produces per-route batching and quantization tier recommendations using sampled traffic, token distributions, and a simple unit-econ model. This reduces manual tuning for common workloads and enables safe, observable defaults for inference cost controls.

What this PR introduces: single-string CLI 'redwood sculptor analyze' that ingests a small traffic sample or evaluation prompts, produces a ranked list of candidate batch sizes, a compact quant-tier map (A/B/C tiers), and an annotated risk score for each suggestion. Adds a runtime "mini-batcher" hint that prefers many small microbatches for latency-sensitive routes (configurable) and a safe fallback path to previous scheduler behavior. Includes config schema extensions for "quantTiers" and "miniBatchHint" with sensible defaults.

Checklist: - [x] CLI and analysis engine implementation - [x] Runtime scheduler hook and unit tests - [x] Integration tests against smoke model and small synthetic traffic - [x] Docs and quickstart example - [x] Telemetry events for suggested change adoption and regression guardrails - [x] Linting and CI fixed after initial run

Usage summary (single-line examples are included in docs): run 'redwood sculptor analyze --sample ./traffic.json --model gpt-small --route /generate' to get recommendations. Output includes estimated tokens/cost saved, suggested batch size, quant-tier mapping (tier_A,tier_B,tier_C), and a conservative accuracy delta estimate based on eval prompts if provided.

Safety and rollout: suggestions are advisory only; the runtime requires an explicit apply step (or a rollout via Console) to change serving config. The runtime scheduling accepts a boolean guard 'enforceMiniBatchForRoutes' and an on-degradation fallback to model-size-preserving variants (e.g., fallback to float16) for routes that see output-quality regressions.

Implementation notes: the econ model is intentionally simple (token-rate x latency SLO x per-GPU cost) so teams can reason about numbers and extend it. We added telemetry hooks to measure pre/post token cost and accuracy on provided eval prompts so that the Optimize team can later build RL-style policy tuning on top.

Backwards compatibility: schema additions are opt-in; defaults keep current behavior. No DB migrations required; workload profiles are optional local artifacts or stored as an appendix in existing profile store (new key 'sculptor-profiles' but not required at runtime).

Related: ENG-5781 (econ cli kickoff), ENG-5799 (mini-batcher scheduling spec), SUP-2147 (customer asked for safer quant recommendations).
Ibrahim Patel: Nice focused tool — helps bridge the gap between profiling and ops. A few asks: add a telemetry field for "suggestion_confidence", unit-tests for the scheduler when many small concurrent routes exist, and ensure the CLI returns non-zero exit codes on parse errors.
Maya Chen (author): Thanks — added suggestion_confidence to telemetry and a new scheduler test 'TestMiniBatcherHighConcurrency'. CLI now returns structured codes; updated tests.
Sofia Martinez: Please ensure the default quant-tier mapping is conservative (tier_A should not recommend int8 unless model flagged as 'quant-verified'). Also, docs should show the safe-fallback lifecycle.
Maya Chen: Adjusted default mapping: tier_A -> q4_0 by default; introduced 'quantVerified' boolean in suggestions. Docs updated with fallback flow.
Ethan Brooks: CI flagged a lint error in pkg/config/schema_v2.json; once fixed, approve. Also request a smoke e2e in perf-canary that runs the suggester on 10k synthetic requests.
Maya Chen: Fixed linting, added a lightweight canary job in ci/perf-scripts (kept it gated to nightly).
Ibrahim Patel: Approving — tested suggested batch sizes against synthetic traffic and saw 18-26% token cost reduction for tail-insensitive routes with no quality regression in our eval set. Recommend monitor alerts on adoption.
Introduce 'workload-sculptor' CLI to generate per-route batching and quantization suggestions; add 'mini-batcher' runtime hint to improve tail latency for latency-sensitive routes; safe defaults are applied only when explicitly accepted. See docs/econ/workload-sculptor.md for usage and migration guidance.
This is a non-breaking, opt-in feature. Recommend staging rollout: enable CLI and telemetry in staging, run nightly canary, then enable 'enforceMiniBatchForRoutes' flag via Remote Config for a small set of routes. No DB schema changes required.

Motivation: alert fatigue on token-level SLO anomalies and noisy long-tail alerts make incident triage slow. This PR implements a lightweight, entropy-based anomaly scoring pipeline and attaches compact token-lineage attributes to traces to make root-cause attribution faster and cheaper. The goal is to reduce false-positive rate for token-level anomaly alerts while preserving signal on true regressions and to enable cheap joins between traces and tokenized cost/latency telemetry.

What this change does: adds a server-side entropy scorer that consumes token stream histograms and sequence-level entropy deltas to produce a normalized anomaly_score metric; propagates a stable token_lineage_id (SHA256-based short id) through OTEL spans and logs; enriches span tags with token_lineage attributes (prefix_hash, seed_length, quant_profile) for low-cardinality joins; ships a new dashboard and alert updates; adds a migration path and feature flag for gradual rollout.

Design notes: entropy scorer runs in the telemetry ingestion pipeline with two modes: streaming (per-request fast approximation using incremental histogram sketch) and batch (windowed reservoir for more precise scoring). The scorer produces both a gauge (token_entropy) and an anomaly_score (0..1) plus categorical reasons (e.g. "kv_cache_miss_entropy", "prompt_shift_entropy") for downstream grouping. Token_lineage_id is intentionally short (base62 12 chars) to avoid high-cardinality explosion; full provenance is kept in a separate, TTL-limited blob store for deep investigations.

API and schema changes: added metrics: redwood.telemetry.token_entropy (gauge), redwood.telemetry.token_anomaly_score (gauge), redwood.telemetry.token_lineage_samples (counter). New span attributes: telemetry.token_lineage_id, telemetry.token_prefix_hash, telemetry.seed_length, telemetry.quant_profile. OTLP exporter and internal log enricher are updated to include these attributes when present.

Rollout plan: behind feature flag telemetry.entropy_anomaly.enabled (default: off). Step 1: enable streaming scoring for 10% of traffic and export metrics only (no alerts). Step 2: enable lineage propagation for 10% of traffic; validate cardinality and storage. Step 3: promote to 50% and update alert thresholds; Step 4: full rollout and deprecate previous heuristic alert. Rollback via flag toggle.

Observability artifacts: added Grafana dashboard snapshots and a lightweight Kibana view for token-lineage joins. Alerts: replaced the previous token-slo-long-tail alert with TOKEN_ANOMALY_SMALL (windowed, p95 scoring threshold) and TOKEN_ANOMALY_AGG (aggregated across prefix cohorts). Alert tuning guidance included in runbook.

Performance and cost: streaming scorer adds ~0.7% CPU for the telemetry ingestion fleet in our benchmark (1k rps synthetic token bursts). Storage impact controlled by base62 lineage id + TTLed blob store; expected cardinality growth measured and capped via sampling policy (token_lineage_sample_rate, default 0.02). Benchmarks show ~18% reduction in noisy alert volume on a Canary (50k requests/day) and 12% lower median time-to-root-cause in SRE tabletop simulation.

Security and privacy: no raw prompt contents are stored in lineage blobs. Prefix_hash is a salted HMAC of the first N tokens (configurable) and is non-reversible. This was reviewed by security (Maya).

Compatibility: no changes to public API surface for users of Redwood API. Internal SDKs are augmented to propagate telemetry.token_lineage_id when available; fallbacks are safe.

Testing: unit tests for scorer math and propagator included (telemetry_test.go); integration job added to CI that runs scorer on replayed traces (small synthetic corpus). Load test harness shows negligible tail latency impact on ingestion pipeline.

Docs & runbook: added docs/runbooks/entropy-anomaly-tuning.md and docs/telemetry/token-lineage.md describing interpretation, thresholds, and troubleshooting steps.

Migration steps for infra teams: update OTEL collectors to v0.35+ for attribute passthrough; enable feature flag in canary; monitor token_lineage cardinality dashboard.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation and unit tests - [x] Dashboard & alert updates - [x] Runbook and docs - [x] Security review - [x] Canary rollout plan

Why unique: unlike previous work which focused on cost-attribution rollups or token heatmaps, this PR targets anomaly reduction via an entropy-first signal and provides a low-cardinality lineage key to tie telemetry together for faster triage.
Leo Zhang: Can we quantify the expected cardinality growth with the default sampling? Please add a dashboard panel that shows unique token_lineage_id per hour.

Ava Martinez: Added panel to dashboard; included cardinality estimates in docs and added sampling config. Estimated unique IDs: ~30k/day for high-throughput tenants at 2% sampling.

Maya Patel: Security review done. Concerned about accidental prompt capture — ensure we never store raw token slices and add automated scrub tests.

Ava Martinez: Added scrub tests and confirmed HMAC prefix hashing.

Jonah Reed: CI flaked on integration test once, reran and passed. Also asked to add a fast-path that skips lineage propagation for sub-10-token system prompts.

Ava Martinez: Implemented skip for short prompts and added unit tests.

Approvals: Leo and Maya approved with comments addressed. Jonah gave final +1 after CI green.
Merged to main via squash merge on 2026-02-19 after CI green. Release note: Add entropy-based token anomaly scoring and token-lineage telemetry for improved triage and reduced alert noise. Feature behind telemetry.entropy_anomaly.enabled flag.
Add entropy-based anomaly scoring and token-lineage telemetry. Metrics: redwood.telemetry.token_entropy, redwood.telemetry.token_anomaly_score. New span attributes for lineage. Feature gated; see docs for rollout and tuning.
Enable behind flag; watch dashboards: Observability / Entropy Anomalies and Token Lineage Cardinality. Default sampling is conservative (2%). Follow runbook if token_lineage cardinality > expected thresholds.
Security reviewed (Maya Patel): no raw prompt storage, prefix hash uses HMAC with per-tenant salt, lineage blobs TTLed and access-controlled.
Implements an entropy-based anomaly scorer and token-lineage propagation to reduce noisy token-level alerts and speed up triage. Includes metrics, span attributes, dashboards, alerts, docs, and a controlled rollout behind a feature flag.

Context: This PR harmonizes credential adapter abstractions and introduces a small, typed shim layer for streaming consumers across the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Motivation: multiple downstream teams and platform demos relied on slightly different credential lifecycle hooks and stream iterator ergonomics; this leads to duplicated adapter code and subtle reauth/retry behavior mismatches. Work: - Introduce a lightweight CredentialAdapter contract and a minimal session-priming helper used by all three SDKs. The adapter surface is intentionally small: fetch(), refresh_hint(), and close() so it can work with KMS/HSM-backed stores as well as ephemeral token services. - Add typed StreamShim helpers (py: StreamIteratorShim, ts: streamShim, go: StreamCursorShim) that centralize resume semantics, graceful drain on cancel, and expose a small backoff-presets hint for SDK callers. - Add a RetryPreset enum and small compat shim that maps platform policies to SDK-friendly retry profiles. - Keep breaking changes to a minimum: the previous auth helpers are deprecated with warnings and adapter factories provided to bridge existing callsites. - Version bumps for SDK packages: python 1.13.0, typescript 2.6.0, go 1.5.0 to capture new helpers and typed exports. This single string contains the full description, checklist and testing notes. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4121) - [x] Cross-SDK API alignment meeting held 2026-01-30 - [x] Unit tests added for adapter edge-cases - [x] End-to-end sample updated (chat-demo/credential-adapter) - [x] Docs updated with migration notes - [x] Version bumps wired into packaging scripts Migration notes: existing clients using auth helpers should call bridge_factory() to avoid any immediate changes; see docs/sdk/migration/cred-adaptor.md. Monitoring: added telemetry hooks for adapter refresh latency and shim resume failures (instrumentation key: cred.adapter.latency).
Liam O'Connor: Nice consolidation — can we keep the public surface minimal? Suggest making refresh_hint optional on the interface to support legacy token stores.

payload.body:
## Summary
Adds a scheduled "meter sanity" job that aggregates key correctness/freshness signals for usage metering and emits alert hooks (Prometheus metrics + Alertmanager rules) with initial thresholds and per-env configuration.

This is the first step toward catching billing-impacting issues (late-arriving usage events, duplicates from retries/backfills, and drift between usage-event aggregates vs billing ledger) before Finance sees them at invoice preview.

## Motivation / context
We’ve had a few recent investigations where we only noticed metering anomalies after:
- customer disputes (invoice vs usage export)
- month-end close reconciliations
- experiment readouts looking "off" due to missing dimensions / duplicate events

This PR wires up automated daily checks and a small set of core KPIs so we can tune thresholds over time and start building an incident trail for "meter health".

Related:
- Linear: ENG-4421 (alert on drift vs billing ledger), PM-1842 (sanity-check KPIs), ENG-4415 (Console dashboard consuming the same aggregates)
- Support threads/tickets: SUP-28463 (double-charged retries), SUP-28451 (invoice vs usage export mismatch)

## What’s included
1) Scheduled job (k8s CronJob) that computes and stores daily aggregates
- Runs hourly for freshness checks + daily rollups at 02:30 UTC
- Writes results into `billing.meter_sanity_daily` (Snowflake) and also emits Prometheus gauges for near-real-time alerting
- Job is idempotent per (day, meter_version, env) and safe to re-run

2) Aggregation queries (initial set)
Per day, broken down by `account_id`, `product`, `meter`, `region`, `model`, `endpoint_family`:
- Freshness: max event lag (p95), % events arriving > 6h late
- Completeness: null-rate for required dimensions (region/model/account_id)
- Duplicates: duplicate usage_event_id rate; dedupe-key collision counts
- Drift: absolute and relative drift between usage-event aggregates vs billing ledger (tokens, requests, embeddings units)
- Outliers: z-score based spikes in per-account billed tokens vs trailing 7d baseline (guarded to reduce noise)

3) Alert hooks + configuration
- Adds Prometheus metrics namespace `meter_sanity_*`
- Adds Alertmanager rules (behind a feature flag by env):
  - `MeterSanityFreshnessSLOViolated` (page SRE + Telemetry)
  - `MeterSanityLedgerDriftHigh` (page Telemetry, notify Finance channel)
  - `MeterSanityDuplicateRateHigh` (ticket + Slack)
- Thresholds are configurable via `config/meter_sanity.yaml` and can be overridden per environment.

## Initial thresholds (subject to tuning)
These are intentionally conservative to avoid paging storms during rollout.
- Freshness: page if p95 event lag > 90 minutes for 2 consecutive runs
- Ledger drift: warn at >0.75% relative drift AND >$250 estimated impact (per account-day); page at >2.0% AND >$1,000 impact
- Duplicate rate: warn at >0.10% duplicate usage_event_id; page at >0.50%
- Missing dimensions: warn at >0.05% null region; page at >0.25% (per region/model breakdown)

Notes:
- The $$ impact estimate uses current pricebook table in Snowflake (approx; intended for prioritization, not accounting).
- Drift checks compare "eligible" rows only (same meter_version, excludes backfills tagged with `is_backfill=true` by default).

## Implementation details
- New service module: `billing/ops/meter_sanity_job`
- Query runner uses our existing Snowflake client with statement tagging (`app=meter-sanity-job`) for auditability.
- Stores both raw counts and normalized rates; emits metrics with labels capped to avoid cardinality blowups (account_id is hashed for Prometheus labels, full values only in Snowflake table).
- Adds a small library of query templates so ENG can extend without touching CronJob wiring.

## Files / areas changed (high level)
- `billing/ops/meter_sanity_job/*` (new)
- `billing/sql/meter_sanity/*.sql` (new)
- `deploy/k8s/cronjobs/meter-sanity.yaml` (new)
- `config/meter_sanity.yaml` (new)
- `observability/prometheus/meter_sanity.rules.yml` (new)
- `lib/snowflake/statement_tags.ts` (tagging)
- `docs/runbooks/meter_sanity.md` (initial runbook + triage steps)

## How to test
- Unit: `pnpm test billing/ops/meter_sanity_job`
- Local dry run against dev Snowflake: `./bin/meter-sanity --env=dev --day=2026-02-01 --dry-run`
- Staging:
  1. Deploy CronJob
  2. Verify `billing.meter_sanity_daily` populated for last 2 days
  3. Verify Prometheus targets scrape `meter_sanity_*`
  4. Temporarily set drift threshold to 0.0001 in staging to validate rule wiring (then revert)

## Rollout plan
- Merge behind `METER_SANITY_ALERTS_ENABLED=false` by default
- Enable in staging for 48h, tune thresholds
- Enable in prod with paging disabled for first week (notifications only)
- After 1 week, move drift/freshness to paging based on observed baseline

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Wire this dataset into Console dashboard tiles (ENG-4415)
- Add per-endpoint-family token counting invariants for OpenAI-compat endpoints
- Add explicit reconciliation hooks for month-end freeze window

---
## Review notes / discussion
**Logan Wright:** Please cap Prometheus label cardinality; do not put raw account_id in labels.
**Author:** Done. Account label is `account_hash` (sha256 truncated) for metrics; full `account_id` only in Snowflake table.

**Nadia Rahman:** Drift should be gated on comparable populations. Backfills and shadow billing comparisons can skew.
**Author:** Added `is_backfill` exclusion by default and a separate metric `meter_sanity_backfill_rows` so we can monitor when exclusions are hiding drift.

**Mei Lin:** Need a Finance-friendly view of the table + statement tags for audit.
**Author:** Added statement tags + documented the table schema in the runbook. Export permissions remain restricted.

**Aisha Bello:** Alert text should include pointers to queries/runbook and avoid paging on single-run spikes.
**Author:** Added 2-run confirmation on freshness/drift and included runbook + dashboard links in annotations.

## CI
- build: pass
- unit tests: pass
- lint: pass
- integration (staging dry-run): pass (reran after fixing missing env var in CronJob manifest)

## Release notes
Internal: Adds automated metering sanity checks (freshness, duplicates, drift) with initial alert hooks and configurable thresholds. No customer-facing changes.
payload.title: Add scheduled meter sanity check job + alert hooks (drift/dupes/freshness)

payload.body:
Background: We see frequent noisy SLO alerts driven by short-lived token-cost spikes from high-priority invocations (interactive debugging and REPL use). These spikes often cascade into alert churn because the alerting rules treat each invocation window equally and are sensitive to single high-cost tails. This PR introduces an invocation-priority-decayer metric and a derived token-cost-oracle aggregation to 1) downweight ephemeral priority bursts, 2) provide a deterministic per-invocation cost estimate for alerting, and 3) enable quieter SLO rules with reduced false positives.

What this PR does: adds server-side metric instrumentation, dashboard panels, alert rule adjustments, and sampling helpers: - invocation-priority-decayer: a per-invocation exponential decay counter capturing recent priority history (labels: tenant_id, route, priority_tier) - token-cost-oracle: a compact aggregate that fuses measured token-cost, KV-prefetch contribution, and decayed-priority to yield an adjusted cost estimate used in alerts - sampled-contextualizer: sampling hook that tags traces used by the oracle for easy backfill and debugging - dashboards: new dashboard JSON with oracle visualizations and a quiet-window simulator - alert rules: adjusted cost SLO rule that uses oracle_estimate and a 5m quiet-window fallback policy (auto-mute for single-interval spikes)

Checklist: - [x] Instrumentation added and unit-tested - [x] Dashboard JSON validated in staging - [x] Alert rule updated with canary release and documented - [x] Migration notes and runtime config knobs added - [x] Docs (observability/priority-decayer.md) and upgrade guidance included

Migration / runtime knobs: the decayer is controlled via feature flags (obs.priority_decayer.enabled) and decay_rate per-tenant. Default is opt-in in staging for 72 hours then ramp to all. Operators can tune quiet-window length and oracle weight.

Testing notes: initial integration run failed due to missing metric label on some legacy invocations; fixed by commit that adds safe-labeling fallback. Full e2e and canary checked on staging with synthetic high-priority traffic and saw a 62% reduction in alert firing for known noisy tenants with <1% impact on true positive alerts.

Motivation / rationale: rather than moving alert thresholds (which masks regressions), the oracle provides a mechanistic cost estimate that reflects expected steady-state cost while allowing the alerting system to remain responsive to real regressions. This reduces operational toil for SREs and gives product teams a clearer signal when model/unit changes actually affect serving economics.
Aaron Cho: Please add an integration test that simulates legacy invocations which lack 'priority_tier' and ensure the safe-labeling fallback is exercised.
Nina Patel: Added f0a1b22 with a unit and integration test that injects legacy headers; the metric now emits priority_tier=unknown for older clients.
Maya Stein: The metric cardinality looks OK in the small canary, but we should cap tenant-level decay_rate to avoid high-cardinality churn. Suggest adding a tenant-level max label bucketing in metricExporter( ).
Nina Patel: Added a guard in invocation_priority_decayer.go to bucket decay_rate into 'low|medium|high' labels before export. Also documented the cardinality implications in the migration notes.
Leo Anders: Approved after verifying dashboards and that CI greened on the rerun. Left a small nits comment about log message verbosity which Nina addressed in the last commit.
payload.title: Add invocation-priority-decayer metric and token-cost oracle for quieter SLOs

payload.body:
Motivation: Customers in regulated regions require per-tenant KMS usage constraints and auditable evidence that keys were selected only from an approved region whitelist. This PR introduces a compact KMS region whitelist enforcement piece and a residency assertion translator that synthesizes a tamper-evident audit header for downstream observers. High-level changes: 1) pkg/kms/whitelist: a KMSKeyWhitelist service that validates requested CMK locations against tenant-configured allowed regions; it exposes a pluggable verifier used by both hosted and private runtimes. 2) pkg/audit/residency_translator: middleware that consumes the request context and KMS decision and emits X-Redwood-Residency-Assertion header (base64 of signed assertion) and a hashed short form X-Redwood-Residency-Hash used for high-volume logs. 3) rbac/v2: an optional mapping rule that ties operator/service-account roles to allowed region sets; the mapper is behind a feature flag to preserve backward compatibility. 4) helm/private values: new toggles and defaults to turn on whitelist enforcement in Private installs and to configure signing key references (KMS or HSM). 5) integration tests and e2e test harness updates to assert header presence and to simulate multi-region key selection. Rollout plan: feature-gated by config.private.kms.regionWhitelist.enabled and config.runtime.residencyAssertion.enabled defaulting to false; staging rollout for 48 hours with audit-only mode (enforce=false but assert header emitted) before turning enforcement on. Security and compliance notes: assertion header contains tenant id, key id, chosen region, verifier fingerprint and timestamp; the header is HMAC-signed by the service signing key (configurable) to avoid leaking plaintext keys. Migration notes: when enforcement is enabled, requests attempting to use a KMS key outside tenant whitelist will be rejected with 403 KMS_REGION_NOT_ALLOWED and an audit entry. Backward compatibility: when gate disabled the runtime behaves as today. Testing: unit tests for whitelist logic (edge cases for wildcard region lists and operator overrides), integration tests for header round-trip and log ingestion; manual privacy review performed by SEC team. Checklist: [x] design doc in Linear ENG-1428 [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] security review approval SEC-33 [x] helm config docs updated. Related work: builds on earlier residency-audit work but takes a different approach by producing a signed assertion header for downstream immutable logging systems.
Aamir Patel: Please add a defensive fallback when the signing key is not available in the private installer; we shouldn't fail open. Marina: Added signing fallback to use local ephemeral HMAC when explicit signing key reference missing and documented risk.
Sofia Ruiz: Can we avoid leaking tenant region lists in logs? Suggest hashing the region list in the audit payload. Marina: We now only include chosen region plaintext and hashed bucket for allowed set; updated translator accordingly.
Gina Hollingsworth: Request more coverage for wildcard region entries and operator-override path. Marina: Added table-driven tests covering wildcard and explicit operator allowlist; also added a small e2e scenario demonstrating operator-override approval flow.
Compliance (SEC): Approved with one follow-up to rotate signing keys on a 90-day cadence; ops playbook entry added.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: We've observed recurrent rapid circuit flips and cross-region failovers during short inbound spikes that saturate KV pressure and trigger aggressive load-shedding. These events temporarily violate SLOs even when overall capacity would have handled most traffic if the load had been smoothed. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) an anticipatory health gate that evaluates short-term KV and queue pressure signals and holds admission for a short, configurable holdoff window; (2) a 'shear-throttle' — a graduated probabilistic rejecter that slices burst traffic by percentiles rather than binary circuit trips. Together these reduce oscillation, prevent cascading regional failovers, and keep the system in a stable degraded state while autoscaling and recovery occur.

What changed (summary):
- New admission controller module: agent/health_gate.{cpp,py} implementing a sliding-window forecast of KV pressure and request queuing; exposes decision diagnostics via /debug/health-gate.
- Shear-throttle implementation in serving/runtime/throttle.{rs,go}: supports tiered probability curves keyed by tenant priority and route.
- Telemetry: added metrics (health_gate_hold_time_seconds, shear_throttle_rejection_ratio, shear_throttle_decision_histogram) and tracing annotations when a request is held or probabilistically rejected.
- Config: config/operations/antici_health_gate.yaml with default thresholds and canary rollout flags.
- Tests: unit tests for decision logic and an integration test that replays a synthetic spike trace to assert fewer circuit state transitions.

Commits (high level):
- feat(health-gate): initial anticipatory gate and metric hooks (Maya P.)
- feat(throttle): shear-throttle probabilistic backoff and tenant weighting (Maya P.)
- test: deterministic spike replay integration and new CI job (Luca R.)
- perf: lightweight sampling hook to avoid hot-path allocations (Ethan G.)
- fix: adjust default thresholds after internal canary (Maya P.)

Files changed (high level):
- serving/runtime/throttle.rs (new), serving/runtime/throttle.go (adapter), agent/health_gate.cpp, agent/health_gate.py, config/operations/antici_health_gate.yaml, infra/ci/spike-replay-test.yaml, telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml, tests/integration/spike_replay_test.py, docs/ops/health-gate.md, CHANGELOG.md, pkg/telemetry/exporter.go

Design notes and rationale:
- Anticipatory gating uses a short-time autoregressive estimate of KV pressure and in-flight queue growth to predict when accepting a request would likely push a node over its soft pressure threshold within the next 200-800ms. Instead of immediate shedding, we gate for a small holdoff (configurable, default 250ms) and signal upstream clients with Retry-After and structured annotations so SDKs can apply jittered retries or fall back to a lower-cost model variant.
- Shear-throttle reduces binary failure semantics. For each admission decision we compute a rejection probability that grows smoothly with the short-term forecasted pressure and tenant weight. High-priority tenants receive a lower slope; low-priority tenants see a steeper curve. This preserves fairness and reduces total rejected requests compared to abrupt circuit trips.
- We intentionally keep the hot-path decision cheap: a small number of integer ops, a ring buffer read, and one exponent lookup for the sigmoid curve when enabled. There is an opt-out config for legacy critical paths.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests cover gate decision boundaries and throttle curve shapes.
- Integration spike_replay_test replays a recorded 30s burst (from last incident) and asserts: (a) 50% reduction in circuit flip count, (b) <5% additional tail latency regression on non-sheared requests, (c) correct telemetry tags set.
- CI initially failed due to a flaky time-based test (infra/ci/spike-replay-test.yaml); flake fixed by switching to deterministic clock in tests and bumping the replay tolerance. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, lint, integration, perf-smoke).

Review conversation (high level):
- Luca Romano: "Can we surface an opt-in canary per region and a fast kill switch? Also please add a per-tenant override for emergency customers."
  - Maya: "Added config flags and a kill-switch endpoint (POST /ops/health-gate/kill). Documented in docs/ops/health-gate.md. Per-tenant override implemented via tenant policy -> health_gate.enabled: false."
- Priya Desai: "Need clear SLO telemetry that ties rejections to tenant impact for billing/alerts."
  - Maya: "Added shear_throttle_rejection_ratio with tenant label and a dashboard link. Also added a Linear ticket to instrument alert thresholds."
- Ethan Green: "Concerned about allocations on hot path."
  - Maya/Ethan: "Added sampling hook and micro-optimizations in perf commit; measured 0.4% p50 CPU increase under synthetic load."
- Final: approvals from Luca, Priya; Ethan approved after perf numbers.

Rollout plan:
- Canary: enable in region us-west-2 with canary flags for 72h (config/operations/antici_health_gate.yaml has canary=true for that region). Monitor two dashboards (health-gate and shear-throttle).
- Gradual ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 7 days if no regressions. If rejection_ratio for high-priority tenants exceeds 0.5% or circuit flip rate increases, rollback immediately.

Monitoring and alerts added:
- health_gate_hold_time_seconds P95 alert (>500ms sustained)
- shear_throttle_rejection_ratio alert per-tenant (>2% sustained for 5m)
- circuit_flip_rate decrease expected; if flip rate increases by >20% alert SRE-runbook.

Rollback plan: kill-switch endpoint and config revert via infra/ci/rollout-revert job. Additionally a feature-flag gate per region to disable without full deploy.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- Default off for private deployments (config flag) to avoid unexpected behavior on older runtimes. Hosted default is ON with conservative thresholds after successful internal canary.

Security/Audit:
- Kill-switch endpoint requires ops role and is audited. Added audit log entries for per-tenant overrides.

Why this is different from previous approaches:
- Prior changes relied on reactive circuit breakers with hard thresholds. The anticipatory approach smooths transient spikes and prefers probabilistic degradation which empirically reduces SLO violations during recovery windows.

Follow-ups (post-merge):
- ENG-1896: tune curve parameters per-tenant cohort and instrument cost-savings per tenant.
- ENG-1902: SDK guidance for Retry-After handling and lower-cost fallback templates.

Merge notes: Squash-merged after approvals and CI green. Change was rolled out via canary to us-west-2 on 2026-02-18; full rollout completed 2026-02-20.

References: Linear ENG-1889, ENG-1896; SUP-412 incident replay. Docs: docs/ops/health-gate.md.
Adds an anticipatory health gating layer and a graduated shear-throttle to smooth regional surges and reduce circuit flip frequency; exposes new metrics and rollout knobs.
payload.title: Introduce anticipatory health gate and shear-throttle for regional ingress stability

payload.body:
Adds a new advisory layer that enforces contractual elasticity targets and a burst-safeguard path; enables opt-in telemetry for percentiles and burst reconciliations; no public API breaking changes.
Motivation: Customers on Dedicated want predictable throughput guarantees that map to contractual SLAs while preserving the ability to safely accept short microbursts. This PR introduces the Contractual Elasticity Advisor (CEA): a control-plane advisory that computes target scale actions based on per-tenant commitments, multi-window utilization signals, and an explicit burst-safeguard budget that can be consumed without violating long-term guarantees. Design summary: CEA runs as a periodic evaluator (default 30s) and emits recommended scale intents with a confidence score. The serving reconciler consumes intents and applies a two-stage policy: 1) fast-path transient scale for burst budgets (ephemeral, bounded by burst tokens and short TTL), 2) sustained provision driven by contractual targets and smoothed utilization estimates. To avoid oscillation, we introduce a capped ramp limiter and probabilistic hysteresis that factors recent rollouts and active fallbacks. Telemetry: new time-series metrics (cea.intent_confidence, cea.recommended_delta, cea.burst_budget_consumed, cea.windowed_util_p95) and an event stream for intent->action transitions. Rollout plan: feature gated (config flag: enable_cea) and staged rollout to 10% of Dedicated clusters for 72 hours, with automated rollback if p99 latency or error rate increases by >5% relative. Backfill behavior: when burst budget is exhausted, requests are routed to compatible fallback model variants (lower-cost quantized variants) according to the tenant's fallback policy. Safety: added guarded path that pauses any scale-down that would drop committed throughput below the contract margin. Related work: follows ideas in ENG-4021 (throughput guarantees) and reuses telemetry conventions from ENG-4176. Testing and validation: unit/integration tests added, added e2e canary to perf-canary harness. Migration: default off; telemetry namespaced under cea.*; runbook updated for SRE and customer success.
Ethan Cho: Overall this looks good. Question: how do we ensure the ephemeral burst allocations don't cause hot pod churn? Suggest adding a soft-min window before making another transient scale for the same tenant.
Priya Raman (author): Added probabilistic hysteresis and a two-minute soft-min per-tenant. See reconciler_integration.go:applyIntent for implementation.
Marina Vassilev: Can we expose an opt-out for customers that use third-party autoscaling? Also add a feature flag at cluster level.
Priya Raman (author): Added cluster-level feature flag enable_cea and tenant-level override; documented in docs/runbooks/cea-rollout.md.
Diego Alvarez: Telemetry looks solid; request adding a p99 of burst allocation latency to the dashboard.
Priya Raman (author): Added cea.burst_alloc_latency_p99 and updated dashboards/cea-summary.json.
Marina Vassilev: CI flake on integration test; reran and green.
Reviewer: approved (Ethan Cho), ready to merge after squash

payload.body:
Problem: When a route has both (a) a fallback policy (e.g., model fallback / region fallback) and (b) a route experiment (A/B variants), the router currently evaluates fallbacks first and only then attempts experiment selection. In practice that means experiments can be silently bypassed during mild capacity pressure or transient model health flips, and worse, attribution becomes misleading because traffic that should be split is instead routed via fallback and never hits the intended variant. This PR changes the routing order so experiment selection happens before fallback evaluation, while preserving safety behavior when experiment config is missing/invalid/unavailable. New order (high-level): 1) Resolve route + canonical route_id; 2) Evaluate eligibility + deterministic assignment for the experiment (if enabled and applicable) to pick a target variant; 3) Evaluate fallback policy for the selected variant target (model/region/tier) to ensure we still land on a healthy/available endpoint; 4) If fallback results in a different model/region than requested by variant, emit explicit metrics + debug fields so the results pipeline can reason about ‘variant overridden by fallback’. Safety/default behavior: If experiment evaluation fails closed (config fetch error, config not yet propagated, invalid variant configuration, missing stickiness key when required by policy), we fall back to the existing route default selection path and then evaluate fallback as before (i.e., no new failure mode for request routing). This is also gated behind the existing route-experiments feature flag in the router config so we can roll out gradually. Metrics added: router.route_experiments.pre_fallback_selected_total (count of requests where experiment assignment occurred prior to fallback), router.route_experiments.fallback_overrode_variant_total (count of requests where assignment happened but fallback changed the chosen target), router.route_experiments.assignment_error_total (assignment attempted but failed, labeled by error_type), and router.route_experiments.evaluator_latency_ms (timing for experiment evaluation). These metrics are emitted with low-cardinality tags (route_id, experiment_id, variant_id where present; region and model_id only on sampled spans per existing OTel conventions). Logging/attribution: The request context now retains both ‘assigned_variant’ and ‘final_routed_target’ so downstream telemetry can distinguish ‘variant traffic’ vs ‘variant selected but overridden’. This PR does not change the attribution schema itself (ADR-048); it ensures the router produces consistent assignment decisions earlier in the decision graph. Testing: Added unit tests covering precedence behavior and ensured existing fallback tests still pass. Added an integration test harness case that simulates a degraded primary model for one variant and validates that fallback occurs after assignment (and increments fallback_overrode_variant_total). Rollback plan: (1) flip router feature flag off to restore previous evaluation order without redeploy; (2) if needed, revert commit (safe: no persisted schema changes); (3) monitor SLO guardrails: error rate, p99 routing latency, and fallback_overrode_variant_total spike as a sign of misconfigured variants. Notes: This matches the decision captured in the routing/rollouts precedence discussion (apply experiment first, then allow fallback to preserve availability). This unblocks Console from showing meaningful ‘variant health’ even when fallbacks are active, because we can now measure how often a variant is being overridden rather than silently skipping the experiment.
Mina Haddad (review): Can we confirm the precedence with canary rollouts is unchanged? We need a single deterministic order when both are configured.
Elena Popov (author): Canary precedence stays the same; this PR only moves experiment evaluation earlier relative to fallback evaluation. Canary vs experiment precedence remains handled in route_decision_graph.ts (canary first, then experiment), and then fallback applies to whichever target was selected. I added an explicit test for canary+experiment+fallback ordering to make this less implicit.
Jordan Lee (review): Please ensure the bucketing inputs don’t change due to fallback (e.g., hashing model_id after fallback would break determinism). Assignment should be based only on stable request/route inputs.
Elena Popov (author): Agree. Assignment now happens before any target mutation, and the evaluator only uses {route_id, experiment_id, stickiness_key, salt}. No model_id/region inputs. Added a regression test that the hash inputs are identical regardless of fallback outcome.
Jada Williams (review): What happens if the experiment config fetch times out? We should not add tail latency to routing.
Elena Popov (author): Evaluator uses the cached config snapshot; if the snapshot is stale/unavailable we short-circuit to ‘no experiment applied’ in <1ms and increment assignment_error_total{error_type=cache_miss_or_stale}. No synchronous network call on request path.
Sean Gallagher (SRE review): Metrics cardinality risk: experiment_id + variant_id across all routes could blow up. Are we sampling any tags? Also add a metric for fallback override so we can alert if a variant is being completely masked.
Elena Popov (author): Tags follow the current experiment tagging guidance: route_id + experiment_id + variant_id only on metrics that are already per-experiment; model_id/region only on sampled spans. Added fallback_overrode_variant_total as requested; it’s low-cardinality and essential for dashboards/guardrails.
Rafael Mendes (review): Rollback plan looks good, but please add a note to the oncall doc about how to interpret ‘assigned_variant != final_target’. Support will ask.
Elena Popov (author): Added a short section to services/router/docs/oncall/route_experiments_precedence.md with examples and the metric mapping.
Mina Haddad (final): Approved. This aligns with the precedence decision and makes the routing behavior observable. Please coordinate with Logan/Caleb on dashboard wiring once merged.
Sean Gallagher (final): Approved with SRE sign-off given feature-flag gating + no new request-path dependencies.
Routing precedence updated for route-level experiments: experiment assignment now occurs before fallback policy evaluation, improving split integrity and observability when fallbacks are active.

payload.body:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally overshoot soft reservation budgets when an inbound surge is followed by a long tail of small requests. This PR introduces a lightweight reservation derater and a utilization-correlation service that together make small, bounded adjustments to per-tenant reservations based on short-term utilization fingerprints and cross-tenant correlation signals.

Goals (high level):
- Prevent sustained oversubscription following transient surges by applying gentle, time-decayed reservation derates.
- Improve observability by correlating fleet-level utilization spikes with reservation adjustments, enabling post-mortem attribution and tuning.
- Keep changes safe and conservative: derates are capped and annotated so any downstream admission control can opt-out.

What this PR contains (single-string summary):
