Introduce Multi-Horizon Queue Reshaper: dynamic deadline bands, per-tenant slot aging, and KV warmup smoothing to reduce starvation and tail latency for continuous batching workloads.
Motivation: Continuous batching previously used a single deadline window and a simple aging mechanism which led to starvation of small, latency-sensitive requests behind KV-heavy long-running batches in mixed workloads. This PR introduces the Multi-Horizon Queue Reshaper: a scheduler component that maintains multiple deadline bands (hot/warm/cold) and a lightweight reshaping step that shifts requests across bands based on observed waiting time, estimated token cost, and KV-pin pressure. The reshaper also drives a KV warmup smoother that pro-actively warms small-slot KV pins for cohorts likely to be served soon, reducing cold-KV latency spikes. Changes include: 1) new scheduler component scheduler/reshaper.go that implements multi-horizon bands and periodic reshaping pass; 2) per-tenant slot-aging state to avoid long-lived reservations starving high-priority short requests; 3) kv/kv_warmup_smoother.go which tracks recent KV access patterns and issues soft prefetch hints; 4) a new config surface to tune band windows and reshaping frequency; 5) added unit and integration tests plus e2e bench harness and docs. Commits: "initial reshaper skeleton and interfaces" introduces the reshaper plugin interface and metrics hooks; "implement banded deadline logic and slot-age bookkeeping" wires the reshaper into the continuous-batcher loop; "kv warmup smoother and integration tests" adds KV warmup heuristic and test coverage including synthetic mixed-workload scenarios. Testing/CI: unit tests and integration tests passed on the run after addressing a race in slot-age bookkeeping (race fixed in second commit). Perf: microbenchmarks on a 4-GPU staging cluster show 12-18% tail latency reduction (p99) for mixed KV-heavy + text-small workloads and up to 8% throughput improvement under 75th percentile latency SLOs. Rollout plan: feature gated behind a runtime flag default-disabled; gradual enable via canary on low-traffic tenants, then cohort expansion with rollout monitoring dashboards. Backwards compatibility: config defaults preserve prior behavior when disabled. Documentation: add docs/queue-reshaper.md with design and tuning guidance. Follow-ups: 1) add adaptive reshaping frequency derived from batch fullness signals (ENG-4879); 2) expose KV warmup metrics in console to correlate cold-KV incidents (ENG-4821).
Carlos Vega (review): Nice design; please add a short comment explaining why we pick three bands instead of a continuous score — we should also document the expected cost of the reshaping pass under heavy load.
Priya Menon (author): Added inline comments and a benchmark for reshaper CPU overhead in scheduler/reshaper_test.go, showed <1% CPU cost at 10k req/s in staging.
Marta Ivanova (review): Found a potential race on slot-age map when a slot is reclaimed and immediately reallocated — requested locking or swap semantics.
Priya Menon (author): Fixed by switching to a copy-on-write slot-age snapshot during reshaping; included test that previously flaked on race detector.
Darren Chu (review/approval): Verified perf numbers and integration tests locally; approved pending CI green.
CI System: Unit+Integration tests passed after rerun. E2E perf bench completed and attached in perf/benchmarks.
payload.title: multi-horizon-queue-reshaper: dynamic deadline bands and KV warmup smoothing

Motivation: a recent regional surge incident (INC-2026-03-01-01) exposed a window where partially-served long-running requests amplified tail latency and triggered cascading node-level evictions. This PR introduces a short-lived 'inflight-request quarantine' state for requests that are selected for graceful backpressure during regional SLO violations and adds targeted telemetry to make quarantine behavior observable.

What this PR does: 1) runtime: marks selected in-flight requests as quarantined, preventing partial KV-cache flushes and ensuring either graceful completion or deterministic early-reject; 2) scheduler: introduces a quarantine-aware backpressure token so the load-trimmer can exclude quarantined inflight ops from aggressive preemption; 3) gateway: adds a 409 early-reject path for requests exceeding quarantine TTL to avoid indefinite resource holds; 4) telemetry: emits three new metrics and two audit log events to help correlate quarantines with downstream evictions and tenant SLO impact.

Design decisions: quarantine TTL is conservative (default 2s) and configurable via runtime flags; quarantine is applied only when regional SLO controller sets the region into 'soft-throttle' to avoid impact during normal operation; quarantine state is ephemeral and not persisted across node restarts. This is intentionally lightweight to fix the immediate incident vector with minimal rollout risk.

Checklist: - [x] add runtime state and token plumbing - [x] add gateway early-reject path and explicit HTTP 409 mapping - [x] add metrics and audit events - [x] unit tests added - [x] integration test in canary harness - [x] performance regression <1% on p95 in synthetic load tests

Erik Thompson (review): gateway early-reject maps to 409; confirm clients treat 409 as retryable with backoff. Consider adding guidance to SDKs.
Maya Singh (author): added SDK guidance note to docs/operations/quarantine.md and marked early-reject as retryable with exponential backoff (recommended).
Samir Desai (approval): validated canary runs against a tenant-replay trace and saw quarantined_count correlate with reduced eviction churn. Approving.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: Dedicated fleets currently support per-tenant reservation credits and a burst token pool. In practice we've seen long-lived unused reservations and noisy signals that cause persistent warm pools and elevated cost. This PR introduces an intervalized reservation ledger: reservations are represented as deposits that decay/settle on finite intervals (configurable, default 1m).

Goals: reduce long-tail reserved capacity, make burst windows explicit for accounting, enable safe reclaim of stale credits, and expose interval-level utilization telemetry so autoscalers can reason about short-term vs sustained load.

Design summary: The ledger stores credits keyed by tenant+reservation-id with an interval epoch (iso8601 minute bucket). New reservation deposits are stamped to the current epoch. Consumption (allocation) subtracts from the active epoch first, then older epochs if allowed by policy. A background reconciler periodically (default every 30s) performs reclaiming: it marks epochs older than a configurable grace window as reclaimable and emits audit events. Reclaim is soft by default (marks credits as 'draining' and prevents new allocations from using them) and is switchable to hard reclaim (instant withdraw) for aggressive cost-saving.

API changes and config knobs:
- new config: fleet.reservations.interval_seconds (default 60)
- new config: fleet.reservations.grace_intervals (default 3)
- new config: fleet.reservations.soft_reclaim=true/false
- admin endpoint: POST /admin/ledger/force-reclaim?tenant={id}&epochs=2 (RBAC-protected)
- exported metrics: redwood_fleet_reservation_epoch_count{tenant,epoch_status}, redwood_fleet_reservation_reclaimed_total{tenant,method}

Implementation notes: core logic implemented in pkg/fleet/ledger.go and an IntervalizedAllocator wrapper in pkg/fleet/allocator/intervalized_allocator.go. The reconciler runs as a bounded goroutine with a name and backoff; ledger updates use a CAS loop on the reservations KV to ensure correctness under concurrent allocators. We added an in-memory mock to the existing lease simulator for unit/integration tests.

Safety and rollout: default behavior is backward compatible (interval_seconds set to 60, grace_intervals high enough that no immediate reclaim occurs). Feature gated behind feature flag "intervalized_reservations" configurable per-cluster. Rollout plan: ship as opt-in (console flag + operator config), collect telemetry for 2 weeks, then enable conservative reclaiming for low-risk tenants.

Migration: existing reservations are migrated to an initial epoch equal to the current server minute on first reconcile. No migration downtime expected.

Testing: added unit tests for ledger arithmetic, CAS correctness, and TTL/reclaim transitions. Integration test simulates burst traffic and asserts reclaimed credits are not used after drain. Performance microbench shows ~3% CPU overhead and sub-ms median allocation latency for common fast-paths.

Related: ENG-3421 (fleet reservation decay prototype), ENG-3498 (reclaim telemetry unwind).
Adds an intervalized reservation ledger that credits and reclaims tenant reservations on fixed windows to improve burst fairness and reduce long-lived overprovisioning. Exposes per-interval utilization metrics and soft reclaim policies.
Nina Patel (review): Can we guarantee atomicity when two allocators reduce the same epoch concurrently? The CAS loop looks okay but add a comment and a unit test for the race case.
Avery Chen (reply): Added a unit test that simulates concurrent allocators and documented the CAS loop in ledger.go (see commit d2c9e54).
Diego Morales (review): Telemetry cardinality looks high if we label by epoch timestamp per-tenant. Can we bucket epochs in retention or expose only current/older/total?
Avery Chen (reply): Changed metrics to expose epoch_status label (current/draining/reclaimed) and emit epoch identifiers only to the audit log. This keeps Prometheus cardinality bounded.
Harper Liu (review): What is the operator upgrade path? If an operator restarts mid-epoch will we duplicate reclamation?
Avery Chen (reply): Reconciler is idempotent; we mark reclaimed epochs via an idempotent state transition and use lease ownership to ensure only one reconciler per cluster runs reclaim. Added integration test to simulate restarts.
payload.title: Intervalized Reservation Ledger and Credit Reclaiming for Dedicated Fleet

payload.body:
Context and motivation:
We frequently see short, high-intensity spikes (burst windows) that are costly to service with long-lived reservations. Existing warm pools and soft-burst credits reduce cost but can be slow to react at the sub-minute granularity we need for certain tenant workloads (video-summarization, nightly batch-query fans). This PR introduces an "episodic lease" concept: lightweight, short-duration leases allocated from a small dedicated reservoir to service micro-bursts with an immediate fallback controller that routes to compatible model variants or lower-cost regions when leases are exhausted. Goals: reduce tail latency for bursts while keeping long-term reserved footprint small, and provide clear telemetry for burst economics and SLA adherence.

What this changes (high level):
- Episodic lease allocator: negotiates short leases (typically 10s-90s) per-tenant with configurable max concurrency and per-epoch caps; leases decrement real-time and are auto-reconciled when nodes are preempted.
- Immediate-fallback controller: when a request cannot acquire an episodic lease, it consults a prioritized fallback graph (local spare pool > secondary region > quantized model variant) and issues a routed request with transparent cost/latency annotations.
- Accounting & safety: soft-fallback budget windows, lease burn-rate smoothing, and a safety throttler that prevents a tenant from exhausting cluster-level episodic reservoir.
- Telemetry: lease_allocations_total, lease_consumption_seconds, fallback_activations_total{reason}, episodic_reservoir_utilization_percent, per-tenant-burst_headroom_gauge. Added tracing spans for lease negotiation and fallback decision path.
- Config: feature gated under dedicated.autoscaling.episodicLeases.enabled=false by default; tuning knobs for epoch_length, max_lease_duration, per_tenant_epoch_quota, reservoir_size_pct.

Design notes and rationale:
- Short leases let us treat burst servicing as a different resource-class than reserved capacity; that reduces steady-state reservation pressure while preserving micro-SLOs.
- Immediate fallback is optimistic: route before retrying to avoid queuing-induced latency spikes. We attach TTL/cost metadata so callers and observability can distinguish fallback hits.
- We intentionally keep the episodic reservoir small and conservative in default values to avoid surprising sustained cost increases.

Commits summary:
- Add episodic lease controller and persistence layer (4 commits)
- Add fallback router and policy evaluator (2 commits)
- Telemetry + tracing additions (1 commit)
- Configuration + helm values (1 commit)
- Integration tests and e2e fixture (2 commits)

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/autoscaler/*: allocator, store and reconciliation logic (~650 LOC)
- pkg/routing/*: fallback policy evaluator and routing glue (~180 LOC)
- pkg/telemetry/*: metrics and dashboards wiring (~40 LOC)
- integration-tests/*: deterministic burst replay and assertion harness (~220 LOC)
- docs/ops/episodic-leases.md: operator guidance and tuning playbook

Testing and CI:
- unit tests for allocator/store logic (go test coverage ~86% for new packages)
- integration test simulates 1000 tenant bursts across 3 nodes and validates reservoir invariants and fallback correctness
- load-run job recorded 95th/99th percentile tail reduction for burst requests in our perf lab: P95 latency - 28% vs baseline, P99 - 16%
- CI initially flagged a flake in an unrelated test; rerun pipeline completed green (full build + e2e smoke).

Observability and alerting changes:
- New dashboards: "Episodic Leases Overview" and "Lease Consumption by Tenant"
- Alerts: High Episodic Reservoir Utilization (>85% sustained 5m) and Increased Fallback Rate (>1% sustained 10m) with links to runbook.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-gated, off by default. Canary rollout to dedicated clusters: small -> medium -> fleet, starting with non-critical regions.
- Ops playbook added in docs/ops/episodic-leases.md; quick rollback toggles available via console and helm.

Backward compatibility and safety:
- No changes to existing reservation or warm-pool semantics unless feature enabled. Fallback paths preserve request semantics (cost/region/model variant annotated) and honor tenant-configured routing preferences.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Maya Singh: "Can we add a hard upper-bound on per-tenant epoch quotas to prevent noisy neighbors at cluster scale?"
  Evan Calder: "Added safety_clamp in lease_store and a default aggressiveness factor in config; also added unit tests demonstrating clamp behavior."
- Liam O'Connor: "Trace spans are great but can be high-cardinality. Can we toggle per-tenant tracing for leases?"
  Evan Calder: "Added a tracing sampling config and limited high-cardinality attributes on default path."
- Sofia Park: "Integration test looks solid; can we add a canary smoke that verifies fallback reasons are surfaced to billing?"
  Evan Calder: "Added a billing-annotation step and a short canary test that verifies fallback annotations are included in the cost blob."
- Approvals: Maya, Liam approved after changes; Sofia approved after canary test addition.

Follow-ups (planned separate PRs):
- Cross-cluster episodic lease peering for geo-local bursts (ENG-4878).
- Cost modeling tool to convert lease activations into expected monthly spend (ENG-4891).

Related work and references:
- See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4829/episodic-lease-controller-design
- Prior art: warm-pool warmlets, burst credits (see PRs pr-81502, pr-70333 for historical context).

Summary: This PR adds an opt-in episodic leasing layer and an immediate fallback controller to improve micro-burst tail latency while limiting long-term reserved capacity growth. It is gated, tested, and includes observability and operator guidance for safe rollouts.
Maya Singh: Can we add a hard upper-bound on per-tenant epoch quotas to prevent noisy neighbors at cluster scale?
Evan Calder: Added safety_clamp in lease_store and a default aggressiveness factor in config; added unit tests.
Liam O'Connor: Trace spans can be high-cardinality — can we toggle per-tenant tracing?
Evan Calder: Added tracing sampling and limited attributes.
Sofia Park: Please ensure fallback reasons surface to billing.
Evan Calder: Added billing-annotation and canary test.
CI: initial pipeline failed due to flake in pkg/observability; rerun succeeded.
Ops: recommend starting canary in non-production dedicated pool with reservoir_size_pct=5% and per_tenant_epoch_quota=3.
Introduces an episodic lease allocator to provide short-duration burst capacity with an immediate fallback path; adds metrics for lease consumption, fallback activations, and headroom accounting. Backward-compatible; opt-in behind config flag.
payload.title: Episodic lease orchestrator and immediate-fallback capacity controller

payload.body:
Motivation: our presubmit images and toolchain bootstrap time have trended upward as we accumulate optional build helpers and devdeps. This PR refactors the CI build orchestrator to produce a smaller default presubmit image, introduce a dependency fingerprint index for targeted dep-refresh, and add a safe dep-prune pass that can be toggled per-team. The changes aim to reduce CI startup latency, make premerge effects of dependency updates auditable, and lower presubmit I/O on heavily changed branches.

Summary of changes: 1) Introduce 'slim-presubmit' microimage variant that omits optional language SDKs and heavy native toolchains; the orchestrator now selects slim vs full images based on profile tags in the monorepo manifest. 2) Add artifact-dep fingerprinting: CI computes a compact fingerprint of the graph (hash of lockfile + toolchain manifest + changed globs) and writes entries to a small index used to gate dep-refresh. 3) Add an opt-in binary 'dep-pruner' step that runs a dry-run prune and uploads a changelog artifact; when enabled it will annotate PRs with suggested removals. 4) Normalize build DAG generation to reduce duplicate prep steps across language workspaces (reduces parallel container starts). 5) Update presubmit templates and README with how to opt in/out and how to read fingerprint index entries.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for fingerprint generation and index storage - [x] E2E smoke for presubmit selection in staging - [x] Add telemetry counters for presubmit image sizes and startup times - [x] Documentation and team opt-in guide - [x] Backwards-compatible default: teams not opting in see no change

Rollout & safety: the new orchestrator respects an opt-in label and a per-team CI profile. We rolled out to the infra and sdk teams for one week, observed ~28% reduction in average presubmit container start time and ~12% fewer packages mounted during preflight. If regressions appear the orchestrator provides a 2-minute fail-open path: set CI_PROFILE=full or add the label ci/force-full-image to a PR.

Notes on motivation vs alternatives: we considered a global forced dep-prune, but that is high risk for large monorepos. Fingerprinting gives a safe gate to only attempt pruning when the fingerprint changes in a way consistent with removal candidates.

Related: ENG-3842 (presubmit-costs), ENG-3910 (dep-curation).
Marco: Can we ensure the fingerprint format is stable across minor Python runtime bumps? Recommend including a format version header to future-proof.
Author (Ava): Added format version header 'v1' and included a migration test. See commit 'feat(ci): add fingerprint format v1 header'
Priya: The DAG dedupe logic looks good; observed 20% fewer container spin-ups in staging. Please add a note in docs about how to debug if a step is skipped incorrectly.
Author (Ava): Added debug flag '--ci-dag-debug' and expanded docs on debugging skipped steps.
Ethan: Integration tests flaked on the dep-pruner E2E in the first run (network timeout). Reran and passed; may need a retry wrapper for the HTTP upload.
Author (Ava): Added exponential backoff to artifact uploads and a retry for transient network errors.
Marco: Approving -- small nit to the Dockerfile caching comments, not blocker.
Priya: Approving after verifying metrics in staging.
Introduces a slim presubmit image profile to reduce CI startup time, adds dependency fingerprinting to safely gate dep-prune attempts, and introduces a reversible dep-pruner dry-run that annotates PRs with suggested removals. Backwards compatible unless teams opt in.

Motivation: Our presubmit lanes run expensive linters and full integration matrices even for trivial doc/README or single-package tweaks. This PR introduces 'slim' presubmit profiles that are diff-aware and run a minimal fast-path pipeline for small, low-risk changes. It also introduces a tiny 'release-safety-oracle' used by release automation to validate dependency provenance and enforce a configurable release window before promoting release candidates. Goals: reduce average presubmit latency for common edits, reduce CI cost, and add a safety gate for automated promotions.
Adds lightweight presubmit profiles to speed CI for small changes; introduces a small release-safety oracle that validates dependency provenance and release-window constraints before promotion; no public API changes.

Motivation: long-tail production incidents are often driven by subtle changes in per-token behavior over the life of an invocation (e.g. warmup spikes, backend stalls during midstream, or finalization overheads). Existing token aggregates (total tokens, avg latency) miss shape-level regressions. This PR adds a lightweight "token trajectory" metric that summarizes per-token latency/cost as a normalized time series per invocation and exposes cohort-level summaries for alerting and dashboards.

What this change does: 1) Collect per-token delta samples in the serving runtime and emit a compact trajectory sketch per invocation (quantiles of normalized token index vs latency/cost). 2) Introduce token_trajectory_score and token_trajectory_cohort labels to group invocations by shape (e.g. front-loaded, mid-spike, tail-heavy). 3) Add an alert weighing/composer service that re-calibrates SLO alert thresholds based on cohort volatility and traffic weight to reduce noisy long-tail alerts. 4) Provide a Grafana dashboard (trellis view) and a small set of evals to catch regressions in trajectory shape.

Design notes: collection uses reservoir sampling + compact histogram to cap memory and network overhead. Trajectory sketches are emitted as additional metric series (prometheus remote write friendly) and as optional trace annotations when the invocation crosses a latency or cost threshold. The alert composer subscribes to cohort drift signals and calculates a weighted threshold multiplier per route/tenant; thresholds are bounded to avoid masking true outages.

Checklist: 
- [x] Runtime sampling and sketch plumbing (telemetry/metrics/token_trajectory.go)
- [x] Cohort classifier and stable hashing (observability/cohort/classifier.go)
- [x] Alert weighing/composer and integration tests (alerts/composer.go)
- [x] Grafana panels and saved dashboard JSON (dashboards/token-trajectory.jsonnet)
- [x] Unit + integration tests 
- [x] Feature flag gated rollout (feature_flags.enable_token_trajectory)

Backward compatibility: trajectory emission is opt-in behind a feature flag and defaults to off for tenants with strict quota. No breaking API changes.

Performance: local microbenchmarks show ~0.3% median throughput regression at 99th percentile concurrent serving with the default reservoir size. Memory overhead is capped per-worker (configurable).

Related: complements ENG-8421 (cohort-aware alerting), follows up on previous token shape telemetry work but focuses on per-invocation shape and alert weighting rather than aggregate rollups.

Sofia: The alert composer looks promising but I'm worried about risk of muting real regressions for small tenants. Can we add a minimum sensitivity floor?
Elena: Composer now enforces a per-tenant floor based on historical outage rate (see composer.go lines ~220). I added a unit test for floor behavior.
Jian: Integration test flaked once on CI due to timing assumptions in the synthetic generator; suggest stabilization by waiting on a signal instead of fixed sleep.
Elena: Updated generator to use coordination channel; CI re-run succeeded.
QA: Verified dashboard panels render with synthetic data and cohort buckets behave as expected.
SRE: Please add an advisory to ops playbook describing the feature flag rollout and rollback steps.

Adds opt-in token trajectory telemetry and cohort-aware alert weighing. Feature is behind a flag. Recommended for teams investigating long-tail token regressions.

payload.body:
Problem: During the predictive autoscaling pilot we saw a few Dedicated deployments get into “config churn” where Console (and a couple of customer scripts) would rapidly flip scaling policy fields (min/max, predictive mode, cooldowns). This amplifies oscillation in the autoscaler loop and produces noisy audit trails. We also had at least one pilot support escalation where repeated updates were masking the root cause (forecast staleness + max-bound saturation). This PR adds server-side throttling for scaling policy updates and emits explicit warnings/audit events when updates are rejected or de-duped. Approach: (1) Introduce a per-deployment token bucket on the UpdateScalingPolicy API (Capacity Policy Service). Default: 5 updates / 10 minutes / deployment, burst=2. (2) Add a per-account “global” safety bucket (50 updates / 10 minutes) to protect control plane resources during bulk automation mistakes. (3) When throttled: return HTTP 429 with Retry-After, include a stable error code (CAPACITY_POLICY_UPDATE_RATE_LIMITED) and a human-friendly message for Console. (4) Emit audit events for both successful updates and rejected updates (capacity_policy.update_throttled), including actor, request_id, deployment_id, and limit window parameters. (5) Emit a structured log + counter metric for SRE visibility. (6) Provide a bypass for internal admin tooling only (RBAC: role=platform_admin) to unblock incident response, still audited. Notes/semantics: - Rate limiting is applied after auth/RBAC checks but before validation/mutation. - “No-op” updates (request body equals current effective policy after normalization) are accepted but do not consume a token; they still emit a debug log (not an audit event) to avoid audit spam. - Limits are enforced consistently across regions using Redis-backed buckets; if Redis is unavailable we fail open (allow update) but emit an error log + metric (policy_update_rate_limit_backend_error) so we can detect degraded protection. Rollout: Guarded behind feature flag dedicated_scaling_policy_update_throttling (default off). Pilot accounts can be enabled via existing per-account flag plumbing. Follow-up: Console UX will handle 429 by showing a non-blocking banner with retry guidance and linking to the autoscaler troubleshooting runbook.
Ethan Park (review): Can you confirm where in the request pipeline the limiter runs? We should not leak any signal before auth/RBAC. Also please document fail-open vs fail-closed behavior if Redis is down.
Benji Okafor (author): Limiter now runs after auth + RBAC (see scaling_policy.ts). Added a short comment + metric + log for Redis failures; we fail open to avoid blocking legitimate config changes during an incident.
Jordan Lee (review): Default values: 5/10m feels ok, but we should ensure we don’t consume tokens for no-op updates (Console tends to resubmit on save). Also are you normalizing fields before comparing? (e.g., cooldown seconds defaulting).
Benji Okafor (author): Good call. Added normalization before equality compare; no-op updates don’t consume tokens and return 200 with unchanged policy. Added tests for both cases.
Rafael Mendes (review): For SRE: please add a paging-safe metric name and include labels that won’t explode cardinality. We should avoid actor_id in metric labels. Also: do we have a way to bypass during incident response?
Benji Okafor (author): Metric is capacity_policy.update_rate_limited_total with labels {region, outcome, limiter_scope}. No actor labels. Added RBAC-gated bypass for platform_admin only; still audited.
Felix Schneider (review): Console needs stable error code + Retry-After. Please include request_id in response body so support can correlate easily.
Benji Okafor (author): Added CAPACITY_POLICY_UPDATE_RATE_LIMITED and Retry-After header. Response body now includes request_id (already generated by gateway) and limit window details.
Ethan Park (final): Looks good. Please add a short entry to internal runbook on interpreting 429s and where to see throttling metrics.
Benji Okafor (author): Added section under “Config churn / repeated updates” with metric name and audit event type. Thanks.
Ethan Park: Approved
Jordan Lee: Approved
Rafael Mendes: Approved
Enable dedicated_scaling_policy_update_throttling for pilot accounts only. Monitor: capacity_policy.update_rate_limited_total (outcome=throttled), audit event volume for capacity_policy.update_throttled, and Redis error metric policy_update_rate_limit_backend_error. If we see legitimate automation blocked, adjust defaults via config without redeploy.
Internal: Added server-side throttling on Dedicated scaling policy update endpoints to prevent rapid config churn; rejected updates return 429 w/ Retry-After and emit audit events for compliance/debugging.

Summary: Introduce an adaptive queue-fence with epoched hedging to reduce starvation and pathological queue growth under skewed continuous-batching workloads. Motivation: Long-tail latency for small, KV-heavy requests increases when continuous-batcher windows preferentially pack throughput-oriented inputs; persistent lockstep arrivals can starve lighter but latency-sensitive traffic and delay KV cache warmups. This change adds an epoched fence that periodically hedges admission for starved lanes and coordinates a low-cost probe admission that prioritizes KV-warmup affinity. Implementation: - Add runtime/batcher/epoched_fence.go: epoch manager, token accounting, and hedged admission path with jittered epochs. - Integrate epoch boundaries with scheduler heuristics (runtime/scheduler/epoched_admitter.go) so hedging can override soft reservations without violating global throughput targets. - KV warmup hints propagated from admission path to runtime/kv/cache_warmup.go so hedged requests can acquire KV pins and avoid repeated cold starts. - Add fine-grained config knobs: epoch_length_ms, hedge_fraction, probe_rate, and adaptive_decay that decays hedge intensity if throughput pressure is observed. - Include unit and integration tests (runtime/batcher/epoched_fence_test.go, integration/epoched_fence_e2e.yaml) and CI benches (benchmarks/ci/continuous_batching/epoched_fence.yaml). Backwards compatibility: All knobs default to 0 (no hedging) to preserve existing behavior; flags can be toggled per-pool. Benchmarks: Microbenchmarks on c6g.large-ish infra with representative mixes (60% large generation, 40% small KV-heavy requests) show: - 99th percentile latency for small KV requests reduced from 410ms to 120ms under steady load with no throughput regression. - Median latency unchanged (<5ms delta). - Overall tokens/s throughput within 1.8% of baseline. Observability: New metrics epoched_fence.hedge_attempts, epoched_fence.hedge_success, and epoched_fence.decay_events exposed to Redwood Console. Runtime traces include epoch_id and probe_id for easier correlation. CI: All unit tests and integration benches pass on CI (linux + mac + windows). Rationale: Rather than a strict per-queue quota or hard-preempt, an epoched hedge gives bounded, periodic relief to starved lanes and lets KV warmup be opportunistic without causing unbounded interference. This pattern is especially effective for mixed workloads with stable skew where starvation risks are persistent. Release notes: Improves tail latency for KV-heavy and low-token-count requests under mixed continuous-batching workloads; disabled by default; configurable per-pool. Related: builds on earlier admission heuristics from ENG-5312 and KV hints work in ENG-5370.
7a1d3f2: add epoched fence admission path and basic API
e3b4a9c: integrate epoch manager with scheduler and expose config knobs
c2f9d80: wire KV warmup hints through admission path
d4b2f55: add unit and integration tests for epoched fence
f9a8c11: add benchmarks and CI job for epoched fence scenarios
a1b7c99: fix race in probe counter and add stress test
Aamir Khan: Please ensure hedging cannot starve high-throughput lanes under bursty conditions; suggest adding an adaptive_decay that backs off when capacity pressure observed.
Marisol Vega (author): Added adaptive_decay and unit tests simulating bursty capacity; hedge intensity decays exponentially when queue occupancy exceeds threshold.
Sophie Laurent: Can we make epoch_length_ms configurable per-pool in addition to global? Some customers require different sensitivity profiles.
Marisol Vega: Exposed epoch_length_ms in pool config with safe defaults; updated docs and unit tests.
Diego Morales: Minor nits in naming and a potential race in probe counter under heavy concurrency.
Marisol Vega: Fixed race by moving probe counter updates under admission lock and added stress test that reproduced prior flakes.
Approvals from Aamir and Sophie after addressing adaptive decay and configurability. Diego gave final +1 after race fix.

Context: Our presubmit lane has grown monolithic: lint, test orchestration, and dependency hygiene are all handled by a single runner which results in slow startup, noisy caching, and frequent interruptions when we update tooling. This PR decomposes the presubmit orchestration into a small language-aware sidecar runner and introduces a scheduled rolling dependency bumper workflow to keep devdeps fresh without spamming PRs. Motivation: Reduce presubmit latency for fast feedback, isolate language tooling concerns, and automate safe minor dependency bumps so teams can focus on feature work. This also primes the repo for future lightweight local CI images.

What I changed (high level):
- Added .github/workflows/presubmit-sidecar.yml: new workflow that launches a persistent presubmit sidecar container for language-aware runners to connect to; optimizes warm caches and shares toolchain leases.
- Added tooling/presubmit/sidecar/README.md and sidecar runner service (Go): sidecar implements a tiny RPC for job registration, incremental test selection, and lint job routing by language.
- Split existing monolithic presubmit entrypoints into language plugins under tooling/presubmit/plugins/{go,js,py}. Each plugin is lightweight and focuses on the language-specific linter/test invocation.
- Introduced .github/workflows/dependency-bump-rolling.yml: weekly scheduled workflow that runs dependency intelligence, creates batched bump PRs scoped to teams, and tags owners for review.
- Added scripts/dep-bumper/main.py: the core bump logic with opt-in rules, safety checks, and changelog aggregation.
- Updated docs/ci/presubmit-migration.md with rollout/migration instructions and how to opt out teams during the ramp.
- Small lint/config changes: .golangci.yml tweaks and package.json devdep pruning.

Why this approach: The sidecar keeps heavyweight toolchain boot time amortized across multiple presubmit runs and avoids rebuilding caches for each ephemeral job. Language plugins allow teams to own and fast follow linter/test updates without touching the orchestration layer. The rolling dependency bumper reduces PR noise by batching minors and auto-annotating risk level. Compatibility: Sidecar exposes a minimal contract; legacy presubmit entrypoints are preserved for three weeks and flagged by a deprecation linter that emits a non-failing diagnostic.

Testing and CI:
- Local integration tests added for the sidecar RPC protocol (tooling/presubmit/sidecar/sidecar_test.go).
- Unit tests for the dep bumper with fixture lockfiles (scripts/dep-bumper/tests/*).
- CI pipeline: initial runs showed intermittent flakes on go-test; fixed by pinning the test cache path in runner. Full CI: lint / unit / integration / smoke passed on final run. See ci checks summary below.

Migration and rollout: 1) Merge this PR to main with feature gate disabled by default. 2) Enable sidecar on an opt-in message in team repos (via a small config file .presubmit.yaml). 3) After two weeks of observation we will flip default to on and deprecate legacy entrypoints in the linter. 4) Rolling dependency bumper starts in "dry-run" mode for one month before opening PRs.

Checklist:
- [x] Sidecar runner implemented and unit tested
- [x] Language plugins moved and smoke-tested
- [x] Dep bump script + scheduled workflow added
- [x] Docs and migration guide included
- [x] Backwards compatibility for three weeks
- [x] Reviewed and approved by infra and SRE

Notes and follow-ups:
- Follow-up ticket ENG-1420: add metrics for sidecar cache hit rate and presubmit latency per-language.
- Follow-up ticket ENG-1421: add circuit-breaker if sidecar becomes overloaded.
- This change touches the presubmit surface; expect a small increase in e2e dev infra usage during the ramp.
Evan Chu: Nice decomposition. Two asks: 1) can the sidecar accept immutable leases for cross-PR caches so we don't leak artifacts? 2) add a health endpoint for SLO alerting.
Author (Maya): answered — added lease scoping and a /health endpoint with simple prometheus metrics; clarified in README.
Lena Martinez: dep-bumper looks promising. Request: make batch size configurable per team and add a changelog snippet for reviewers.
Author (Maya): addressed — batch size is config-driven and bumper now aggregates changelog fragments into the PR body.
Tomás Rivera: small nit on plugin scripts — prefer bash strict mode and fewer subshells.
Author (Maya): updated entrypoint.sh for all three plugins with set -euo pipefail and comments.
SRE (automated comment): observed increased presubmit container count during integration tests; recommend rolling enablement.
Author (Maya): noted in migration guide and added default-off gating.
Merged to main via squash after approvals from infra and SRE. All CI checks green on final run. Migration gated by feature flag and documented.
- Introduce presubmit sidecar to reduce presubmit latency and centralize toolchain leases.
- Add language-specific presubmit plugins (Go/JS/Py).
- Add scheduled rolling dependency bumper (dry-run initially).
Keep legacy presubmit entrypoints available for at least three weeks. Monitor sidecar cache hit rate and test runner queue length (ENG-1420). If load spikes, flip the feature gate off and open follow-up to tune leases.

Adds graceful tenant hibernation for extreme oversubscription scenarios; introduces an egress taxonomy adjuster to preferentially reduce cross-region egress; introduces a slew-rate controller on the circuit fuse to prevent rapid flip-flopping; includes telemetry and migration script.
Context: During a recent regional surge incident we observed tenants with unexpected cross-region egress patterns causing egress-driven overload and rapid circuit flips during failovers. Small tenants throttled aggressively were still contributing to noisy KV evacuation and triggering stale circuit reopen attempts. This PR introduces a controlled 'tenant hibernation' mechanism coupled with an egress taxonomy adjuster and a circuit slew-rate controller to provide a graceful, observable way to remove noisy tenants from active serving while preserving SLOs for healthy tenants.

What I changed: 1) tenant hibernation controller: a short-lived lifecycle that marks tenants as HIBERNATED when their combined cost and egress weight exceeds the soft budget; hibernation preserves KV sticky entries and provides a timebound suspend window for the tenant's requests to drain; it is reversible and tier-aware. 2) egress taxonomy adjuster: classifies egress per-request into LOCAL, CROSS_REGION, and HIGH_BANDWIDTH buckets and adjusts admission/egress budget tokens to preferentially reduce CROSS_REGION egress before dropping LOCAL traffic. This helps keep regional capacity local during failovers. 3) circuit slew-rate controller: prevents the circuit fuse from toggling rapidly by enforcing a configurable min-open window and a programmable reopen-slew curve (linear backoff with jitter cap). 4) telemetry: new metrics and events (tenant_hibernate.enter, tenant_hibernate.exit, egress.adjustment, circuit.slew_applied) and dashboards added. 5) migration: a small config migration that populates default taxonomy weights and enables tenant hibernation opt-in for Dedicated customers.

Why this is different: Existing soft-degradation and eviction mechanisms target admission or priority queues. Tenant hibernation is an explicit tenant lifecycle state that preserves data locality and KV coherence while suspending acceptance of new requests; paired with egress classification it reduces cross-region thrash, and the slew controller addresses the oscillation vector we witnessed during the incident.

Tests and rollout: Unit tests for controller state transitions and egress classification added. Integration test harness simulates a regional egress storm and asserts that hibernated tenants do not cause KV re-evacs and that healthy tenants keep SLOs. Canary rollout: default off for hosted customers, opt-in for Dedicated; smoke canary in prod region us-east-1 with a 1% sample; automated rollback if 5xx rate increases by >0.5pp over baseline.

Related work: ENG-4982 tracks the wider egress taxonomy initiative; ENG-5021 is the incident follow-up with proposed controls. SUP-7214 is a support ticket for a customer impacted by egress-driven failover.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the controller state machine (controller/tenant_hibernate.go), the egress classifier rules (runtime/egress_taxonomy.go), and the circuit slew implementation (runtime/circuit_slew_controller.go). The migration script is under infra/migrations/2026-02-tenant-hibernate.sql and must be safe to run during rolling upgrades.

Diego Morales: Overall looks good. Two concerns: a) migration - can we make the SQL idempotent for older clusters? b) the default taxonomy weights look aggressive; suggest conservative defaults that we can ramp.
Maya Chen (reply): Migration is idempotent - we use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT and a safe backfill; updated default weights to be 20% cross_region reduction instead of 40%.
Asha Patel: I'm worried about hibernation for latency-sensitive tenants. Can we expose a per-tenant opt-out and surface an audit event when hibernation is applied?
Maya Chen (reply): Added tenant-level opt-out flag and audit events (tenant_hibernate.audit). Also documented operator guidance in docs/operational/tenant-hibernate.md.
Oliver Nguyen: Tests look thorough. One nit: the circuit slew jitter cap currently uses a deterministic seed in tests; switched to mocked jitter for stability.
Maya Chen (reply): Fixed tests to mock jitter and added an integration scenario for KV-drain race reproduction.
Canary enabled in us-east-1 at 2026-02-23 03:00 UTC for 1% sample - monitoring hooks on dashboards/tenant-hibernate.json
SRE: watch tenant_hibernate.enter/exit counts and circuit.slew_applied histogram for first 48h
Rollback: revert deploy/helm/values.yaml toggles and run infra/migrations/rollback-2026-02-tenant-hibernate.sql if migration needs to be undone

Motivation: The existing paged KV block manager performs well for uniform block sizes but shows tail latency variance and allocation churn for mixed-size workloads (short prompt-heavy vs. long-context streaming). This PR introduces a tiered reservoir allocator that separates small/medium/large block pools, a fastpath soft-pin mechanism for hot prefixes, and a heterogeneous reuse policy that prefers same-size reuse but can gracefully coalesce when fragmentation is high.

Design summary: A lightweight reservation layer classifies block requests into three tiers (4KB, 32KB, 256KB logical slots) with per-tier free rings and a reservoir of muted reservations that can be loaned across tiers under pressure. Soft-pin is implemented as a per-request hint that keeps recently-used slots on a fast reuse queue for N subsequent allocations; the queue is lockless for the common case and falls back to a per-shard slow path. The heterogenous reuse policy introduces an LRU-weighted scoring function that balances locality (reuse same-size blocks) and compaction pressure (allow coalescing of adjacent free slots into larger logical blocks). Kernel/hint guidance: allocator exposes optional CPU hints so the runtime can prefer GPU-friendly pin candidates during token-level KV cache warmups.

Testing and validation: Unit tests cover reservation handoff, soft-pin expiry, and coalescing invariants. Integration tests run against the runtime harness with continuous batching enabled; we added a soak test (10k mixed-size requests over 4 hours) and crash-injection to verify no deadlocks. Benchmarks were run on a c5n-like machine and a dedicated inference box with A100s to compare tail-latency, P50/P95, and allocation stalls.

Migration notes: New config flags added under runtime.blockpool.*. Defaults retain previous behavior (fallback reservoir disabled), rollout gated behind experiment flag `blockpool.tiered_reservoir=true` for first 10% of traffic. Admins can tune per-tenant tier thresholds and soft-pin window via Redwood Console.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked (ENG-4532)
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] Benchmarks + regression alerts
- [x] Config flags + rollout plan

Related: ENG-4532 (tiered-reservoir design), ENG-4680 (kv-cache warmup kernels), SUP-1204 (customer incident that motivated reuse), RFC-2025 (allocation hint API).
initial tiered-reservoir allocator implementation and API surface
add soft-pin fastpath: lockless hot-queue + fallback path
heterogeneous reuse: scoring-based coalescer and stress tests
expose kernel hints for runtime routing and warmups
integration tests and soak harness updates
addressed reviewer feedback and tightened invariants
docs: runtime config, rollout steps, console knobs
Asha Patel: Gate the rollout behind an experiment flag (done) and ensure default config preserves prior behavior (author: added experiments/flags.yaml and defaults).
Miguel Rivera: Concern about lockless queue ABA; ask for epoch stamps on entries (author: added 64-bit epoch tags and unit tests to prevent ABA).
Sofia Chen: Observe P95 improvement but saw small regression in long streaming requests at low QPS; suggestion to make cross-tier loans bounded per-shard (author: implemented per-shard loan caps and added regression test).
Ben Thompson: Requested clearer console knobs and a migration doc for Dedicated customers (author: added console/recipes/blockpool-rollout.md and docs/runtime/blockpool.md).
Author response: Addressed all requests, added more unit coverage for coalescer invariants, and re-ran benchmarks after fixes.
Introduce a tiered reservoir blockpool allocator with soft-pin fastpath and heterogeneous reuse policy. Improves tail latency and reduces allocation churn for mixed-size KV cache workloads; rollout is experiment-gated. Admin knobs available in Console.
P50: -4% (allocation stalls reduced), P95: -18% (tail latency improvement for mixed workloads), mean allocation latency: -22%, memory fragmentation ratio: -12% with default config. Soak test: no allocator-related crashes over 4 hours at 10k mixed requests.
No automatic data migration required. New flags: runtime.blockpool.tiered_reservoir (bool), runtime.blockpool.soft_pin_window_ms (int), runtime.blockpool.tier_thresholds (comma separated sizes). Default: tiered_reservoir=false to preserve current behavior. Enable behind canary before wider rollout.
If allocation stalls appear after rollout, disable experiment flag 'blockpool.tiered_reservoir' to revert to legacy allocator. Check metrics: blockpool.alloc_stalls, blockpool.cross_tier_loans, blockpool.softpin_evictions. If soft-pin queue shows high churn, reduce soft_pin_window_ms.
medium: introduces allocator path changes but gated behind experiment. Thorough tests and soak harness reduced risk. Monitor fragmentation and cross-tier loans metrics during rollout.

Context and motivation: Large tenants see wide variance in per-tenant unit economics driven by traffic shape, prompt lengths, and tail latency constraints. Our existing autotuners are powerful but heavy-weight and assume long-running background sampling. This PR introduces a light-weight 'tenant cost compactifier' that builds compact, deployable cost templates by sampling a short representative window and synthesizing conservative batch/cache/quant defaults. Paired with the 'quant-mentor' CLI, operators can simulate safe rollouts and get human-readable advice for quant profiles and batching shapes.

What this PR does (high level): 1) New compactifier service that ingests sampled request metadata and outputs a compact template (batch shapes, cache-presets, quant-tier recommendation, safety margins). 2) Quant Mentor CLI (bin/quant-mentor) with subcommands: profile, simulate, export. 'profile' generates a deterministic recommendation; 'simulate' runs a metric-level dry-run against historical traces; 'export' emits a profile artifact compatible with Dedicated/Private defaults. 3) Telemetry hooks to emit cost delta and latency delta estimates per-candidate profile. 4) End-to-end integration tests & unit coverage for heuristics.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-5124) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration smoke tests - [x] Telemetry events (cost_delta_estimate, latency_delta_estimate) - [x] Backward-compatible profile export format - [x] CLI help and man page

Commits summary: 1) Add compactifier core + heuristics (heuristics/compactifier.py + sampling connectors) 2) Add quant-mentor CLI and simulation runner (cli/quant_mentor.py) 3) Integrate telemetry and cost model adapter (telemetry/cost_adapter.go) 4) Tests and small refactors to the profile serializer (profiles/serialize.go) 5) Docs and examples (docs/compactifier.md, examples/quant-mentor-demo.json)

Changed areas (high-level): - server/compactifier/* (new) - cli/quant_mentor.py (new) - telemetry/cost_adapter.go (mod) - profiles/serialize.go (mod) - tests/compactifier_test.py, tests/quantmentor_integration.sh - docs/compactifier.md, examples/quant-mentor-demo.json

Review conversation: Maya: "Nice incremental design — two high-level concerns: how do we avoid overfitting to a short sample window, and do we provide safe defaults for latency-sensitive routes?"
Jordan (author): "Compactifier emits a confidence score and enforces a conservative safety margin on batch size if the confidence < 0.7. By default latency-sensitive routes (route metadata ms95 < 200) are assigned latency-first templates. Comments added linking to the confidence heuristics code paths (heuristics/compactifier.py:estimate_confidence)."
Leo: "CLI UX is good; suggestion to add a --shadow flag that can run the profile in shadow mode in Dedicated for one hour."
Jordan: "Added --shadow-duration and a telemetry opt-in; documented in docs/compactifier.md. Shadow runs are gated by a tenant opt-in flag to avoid surprises."
Priya: "Please include a short migration note for Dedicated operators so they can import exported profiles."
Jordan: "Added docs/compactifier.md section 'Importing to Dedicated' and an examples/import.sh script."

CI summary: Unit tests: pass; Integration: initial flaky e2e (timeout in warmup) -> reproduced locally -> increased warmup timeout in tests -> rerun -> pass; Lint: pass; Benchmarks: microbenchmark shows 6-12% per-token cost reduction on sampled tenant traces in the lab harness. Full CI run green.

Merge details: Approved by Maya and Leo after two rounds of review. Merged via squash on 2025-08-27. Post-merge: rollout plan executed to staging; one tenant group opt-ed into shadow run and observed expected cost delta within predicted band.

Backward compatibility and impact: export format is backwards compatible; profiles that don't specify quant_tier will be interpreted as 'preserve existing'; migration doc included. There are no API surface changes for hosted API. The feature primarily affects Dedicated and Private deploy workflows and the operator CLI.

Followups planned: - ENG-5402: auto-schedule periodic re-sampling for compactifier - ENG-5420: add ML-based confidence estimator to replace heuristic score - PM-318: surface compactifier suggestions in Console Defaults UI

Motivation: multiple customers and internal teams hit edge cases where a single static credential/provider was insufficient (short-lived tokens, external STS exchanges). This PR introduces a delegated credential chain abstraction plus optional pluggable reauth hooks so SDKs can proactively refresh tokens and fall back to a chain of providers. While adding the chain we also took the opportunity to improve streaming ergonomics by introducing thin async iterable wrappers (TypeScript/Go iterator facade, Python async generator shim) so users have a consistent ergonomic surface across languages.

Scope (single-string): - Add DelegatedCredentialChain (SDK core) with priority/fallback semantics and configuration via environment/constructor. - Add PluggableReauthHook interface (optional) that credential providers can implement to receive renew signals and to perform async exchange. - Implement shims in sdk/python, sdk/typescript, sdk/go to adopt the chain and call renew when token TTL <= threshold. - Introduce AsyncIterable/AsyncGenerator wrappers for streaming APIs that normalize chunk events across runtimes. - Bump package versions and update CHANGELOG entries. - Tests: unit + integration + basic e2e smoke on hosted test cluster.

Checklist: [x] Design doc linked in Linear (ENG-4321). [x] Implement core credential chain and hook interfaces. [x] SDK adaptors implemented for python/ts/go. [x] Add cross-language test harness for simulated short-lived tokens. [x] Update examples and quickstarts. [x] Release notes drafted.

Implementation notes: - Credential chain is configured with a list of providers. The first provider that returns a valid token is used; on failure we iterate providers. Providers can optionally implement renew(ctx) which the SDK will call proactively (TTL-driven) or reactively on 401. - Renew semantics are best-effort and asynchronous; errors bubble to the request path and will trigger fallback policies. - Async iterable wrappers unify error propagation, backpressure signals, and resume semantics; they intentionally keep a minimal surface (Symbol.asyncIterator / AsyncGenerator for TS/Python; channel-like iterator for Go). - To avoid duplication we factored shared logic into the redwood/sdk-core package and added thin language bindings.

Compatibility & migration: - Default behavior is backward compatible: existing providers and code continue to function. - If you want proactive refresh, implement the optional renew() method on your provider or wrap an STS exchange provider included in examples. - Streaming wrappers are additive; existing callback-based streaming APIs remain supported for a deprecation cycle.

Performance & reliability: - Added targeted microbenchmarks: proactive renew latency added ~0.3ms median per request for checked TTL paths (cold path only). Batching and cache hits are unaffected. - Integration tests included a failover scenario: primary provider returns 401 -> chain falls back to swap provider -> request retried once with new token.

Files changed snapshot (high level): Listed below with small illustrative snippets in repo.

Testing: - Unit: python pytest, ts jest, go test. - Integration: ran against staging router with short-lived tokens. - E2E: basic request+stream smoke.

Merge notes: CI initially flagged an integration test failure (ratelimit flake). Rerun of integrations passed. After approvals from Ravi and Lena and a final sign-off from Diego this was squash-merged to main on 2026-02-03.
Adds a delegated credential chain and pluggable reauthentication hooks across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs; introduces lightweight async iterable wrappers for streaming responses; bumps SDK versions: python v1.12.0, typescript v2.4.0, go v1.6.1. Migration note: credential provider interface gains an optional renew() hook — existing providers continue to work but implementing renew enables automatic proactive refresh.
Ravi Patel (request changes): Please add a unit test that exercises fallback between two providers when the primary returns a 401. Also clarify error propagation in delegated_chain doc block.
Maya Chen (author): Added fallback unit test and expanded doc block to describe error bubbling and retry semantics; pushed commit b9a0e3d.
Lena Hoffmann (comment): The TS async iterable should surface a cancel() signal for GRPC streams to avoid leaks in browser contexts. Can you add a small test?
Maya Chen (author): Added cancel() hook and test in async_iterable_shim.ts; implemented a no-op for runtimes that don't support explicit cancellation (polyfilled via AbortController).
Diego Alvarez (approval): Verified python + go adapters in local smoke. No blocking issues. Approving.
CI (note): integration tests failed on first run due to intermittent rate-limit in staging; tests re-run and passed.

Summary
Adds a lightweight GPU CI smoke test that exercises the FP8 + INT8 kernel paths and validates correctness against a baseline implementation on a small, representative shape set.

This is explicitly not a performance benchmark. It is meant to catch:
- obvious numerical blow-ups (NaNs/Infs)
- dispatch / shape-guard regressions (wrong kernel selected, missing fallback)
- alignment/stride edge cases (KV cache and packed layouts)
- GPU-arch-specific correctness differences (within configured tolerances)

Context
We are landing a bunch of FP8/INT8 kernel work during the benchmarking sprint (ENG-7421). We already have unit tests for some kernels, but they are not consistently run on real GPUs in presubmit.

This PR introduces a single, fast test that can be used as a correctness gate for quantized-kernel changes.

What’s in the smoke test
Target: //runtime/tests/quant:quant_kernel_smoke_test

The test runs a small matrix of cases (kept intentionally small for CI):
- Matmul (INT8 and FP8) cases that match common projection shapes:
  - (m,n,k) in {(16,4096,4096), (32,4096,8192), (16,8192,8192)}
  - alignment variants: k % 128 == 0 and a single “near-miss” alignment case that should force fallback
- Attention (FP8 path + baseline) cases:
  - head_dim = 128
  - num_heads in {32, 64}
  - prefill seq_len in {16, 128}
  - decode step with kv_len in {128, 512}
- Batch in {1, 4}

Checks performed per case:
- outputs are finite (no NaNs/Infs)
- max abs / relative error vs baseline within tolerance
- baseline uses deterministic settings where possible; we also seed inputs for reproducibility

Baseline + tolerances
Baseline is the existing (non-quantized) kernel path for the same op, executed in FP16. Tolerances are stored in runtime/tests/quant/quant_kernel_smoke_tolerances.h and are intentionally conservative for CI:
- FP8: slightly looser tolerance than INT8 (expected)
- INT8: tighter but still tolerant of minor implementation differences

CI integration
New job: gpu-quant-smoke
- Runner: self-hosted GPU CI pool (L4)
- Expected runtime: ~6–8 minutes wall clock
- Artifacts: test log + per-case summary (pass/fail, worst error)

Presubmit behavior:
- Default: opt-in for PRs (comment “/run gpu-quant-smoke” or label run-gpu-ci)
- Nightly: runs by default on main to ensure drift is caught even when presubmit is skipped

Rationale: We don’t want to force every PR to wait on GPU capacity, but we do want an easy, standard gate for kernel PRs and a nightly safety net.

How to run locally
1) Build container used by CI (see ci/scripts/run_gpu_quant_smoke.sh)
2) Run:
   ./ci/scripts/run_gpu_quant_smoke.sh \
     --test_filter='*QuantKernelSmoke*' \
     --cuda_visible_devices=0

Notes:
- The script pins the same deterministic flags as CI.
- If you’re on an H100/A100 and see different tolerances needed, please add a per-SKU override in quant_kernel_smoke_tolerances.h (don’t just globally loosen).

Review notes / discussion
- Grace requested we include at least one case that exercises the dispatch fallback (unsupported alignment). Added (m,n,k)=(16,4096,4096) with a deliberately misaligned stride variant.
- Rina asked about flakiness and non-deterministic reductions. We now force deterministic algorithm settings where supported and report the worst-case error (so we can see if noise is growing).
- Noah flagged that the INT8 path previously had a shape-guard bug in one branch; this test includes the shape that triggered it in the Slack thread and will fail if dispatch regresses.

CI results
- gpu-quant-smoke: PASS (L4)
- runtime-unit (cpu): PASS
- clang-tidy: PASS
- bazel test //runtime/...: PASS

Rollout / risk
No production impact. This is test + CI wiring only.

Follow-ups
- Add an H100/A100 weekly run (separate pipeline) to cover Hopper/Ampere-specific paths once capacity is allocated.
- Consider folding the quick quality sanity suite (eval-harness) into a separate non-blocking signal for model-default flips; this smoke test is strictly numerical correctness.

Related
- ENG-7422 Update benchmark harness for quantized kernels
- ENG-7424 INT8 matmul dispatch and shape guardrails
- PR-19841 INT8 matmul dispatch and guardrails
- PR-19827 FP8 attention integration behind flag

Context: Provision-to-ready automation needs actionable failure modes and durable artifacts (logs, summaries) per node before we can safely gate nodes from joining serving pools. Today the orchestrator/agent emits logs, but we lose structured per-step results once a node is recycled, and operators have to grep raw logs to understand why a node is stuck in Validating. This PR adds persistence for validation step results and a structured failure reason field to the Fleet Readiness service, with an API to fetch the latest results for a node and an API-friendly summary intended for internal tooling (ops console/runbooks). Scope: store step name, start/end timestamps, duration_ms, status, failure_reason_code/message, and an artifact pointer (URI + checksum) to bundled logs uploaded by the validation agent. Also adds minimal telemetry for write/read success and payload sizes (no per-node high-cardinality tags). Out of scope: changing the canonical readiness state machine (see ADR-017) or adding UI surfaces; those are in follow-on PRs. Rollout: gated behind a server-side config flag `readiness.persist_validation_results` default OFF; staged enablement planned with SRE after initial data quality checks. Security/PII: artifacts are pointers only; we do not store raw log bodies in Postgres, and artifact URIs are restricted to internal buckets and require service authz to read.
Data model: new table `validation_step_results` keyed by (node_id, attempt_id, step_name) with `status` enum (PASS|FAIL|SKIP|ERROR), `duration_ms` bigint, `started_at`/`finished_at` timestamptz, `failure_reason_code` (short, stable string), `failure_reason_message` (operator-facing, sanitized), `artifact_uri` (s3://... or gs://... depending on env), `artifact_checksum` (sha256), and `artifact_bytes` (int). We also add `last_failure_reason_code/message` and `last_failed_step` denormalized onto `nodes` for fast list queries (used by tooling) and to avoid joining large result sets in summary endpoints. Ingestion: validation agent/orchestrator emits `ValidationStepCompleted` events; the readiness service now upserts step result rows and updates the denormalized last_* fields if the step failed. API: `GET /internal/fleet/nodes/:nodeId/validations?attempt_id=...` returns ordered step results (most recent attempt by default) and includes the denormalized summary. Artifact pointers: the service stores a pointer only; the agent is responsible for uploading a gzipped bundle and providing uri+sha256. We intentionally do not store `artifact_uri` on PASS steps when no logs were uploaded (field nullable).
Unit: schema validation for enums + sanitizer on failure_reason_message. Integration: upsert idempotency (duplicate events), ordering by started_at, and authz coverage for internal read endpoints. Load check: local benchmark verifying ingestion path adds <3ms p95 per step event with Postgres on dev settings. Manual: replayed a real validation agent payload from staging (redacted) and confirmed artifacts show up via API and denormalized summary fields update correctly.
Ethan Park: Can we avoid storing arbitrary large messages in Postgres? I’m worried about someone dumping logs into failure_reason_message.
Benji Okafor (author): Agree. Added `sanitizeFailureMessage()` with max length 512 + newline stripping + common secret patterns redaction. Also clarified in docs that full details belong in artifact bundle.
Allison Grant: Please confirm metrics won’t include node_id/pool_id as tags. We already had a cardinality incident risk flagged for this sprint.
Benji Okafor (author): Confirmed. Metrics are only by step_name, status, and region. No node_id, no attempt_id. Added a lint check in telemetry helper to block forbidden tags.
Jordan Lee: Does denormalizing last_failed_step violate ADR-017 (authoritative signals)?
Benji Okafor (author): It’s derived from stored step results, not a separate source of truth. The canonical readiness state still comes from the state machine transitions; this is a query optimization for operator UX.
Aisha Bello: Can we add a histogram for artifact_bytes to catch accidental blowups?
Benji Okafor (author): Added `readiness.validation_artifact_bytes` histogram + alertable dashboard query in follow-up (kept this PR to metrics only; dashboards PR will consume it).
Miles Thornton: What’s the behavior when agent uploads artifact but checksum is missing?
Benji Okafor (author): We reject the artifact pointer (store nulls) and mark the step ERROR with reason code ARTIFACT_METADATA_INVALID. This keeps the node from being marked Ready and gives a clear remediation path.
Ethan Park: Looks good after sanitizer + upsert tests. Approved.
Allison Grant: Approved (thanks for the cardinality guardrail).
Aisha Bello: Approved.
Flag `readiness.persist_validation_results` remains OFF in prod. Plan: enable in us-east dedicated A100 only after 24h of staging verification; monitor `readiness.validation_results_write_errors` and artifact_bytes distribution; rollback by disabling flag (data will remain but ingestion stops).
Wire summary fields into internal ops console (DES-301)
Add retention policy for old attempt results (likely 14 days) + periodic cleanup job
Add endpoint to fetch artifact download pre-signed URLs (internal only) once authz story is finalized
Coordinate with validation agent to always upload artifacts on FAIL/ERROR steps

Motivation: We have drift between the Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs in two areas that frequently confuse integrators: credential composition/rotation APIs and stream primitive names. This PR introduces a small, explicit CredentialFactory abstraction across all three SDKs (py/ts/go) to centralize token provider wiring, make prefetch/refresh policies composable, and provide a single upgrade path for future delegated auth features. It also consolidates and renames stream primitive exports under a clearer namespace (PullStreamReader, PushStreamWriter -> PullReader, PushWriter) to improve discoverability and reduce API surface duplication across languages.

Summary of changes: 1) New cross-SDK concept: CredentialFactory. Each SDK exposes a factory constructor that accepts a canonical set of options (provider, prefetchWindowMs, jitterProfile, metricsScope). This is intentionally small to make migration easy. 2) TokenProvider interface clarified and documented; adapters provided for existing token shapes (static API key, rotating refresh-token, platform-delegated credentials). 3) Stream namespace reshuffle: flattened stream exports and added thin aliases for backwards compatibility for one release. 4) Retry preset mapping: the SDKs now share a canonical mapping from server-side retry-profile names to client presets; added adapter hooks to override profile->preset resolution. 5) Tests: added cross-language integration fixtures that exercise a credential rotation scenario with concurrent streams to validate no race during token swap. 6) Docs and examples updated for all three SDKs and we added a migration guide.

Compatibility and migration notes: - We retained old stream names as deprecated aliases that log a single deprecation warning on first import. The aliases will be removed in the next major version. - CredentialFactory is additive; existing TokenProvider implementations can be wrapped with factory.compose() helpers. Migration guide included in sdks/*/MIGRATION.md. - Minor surface change in config shape for session creation: sessionConfig.credential -> sessionConfig.credentialFactory (both accepted for now).

Testing and CI: - Unit tests added/updated in py/ts/go. - New integration matrix in CI exercises: (python client + redwood local runtime), (typescript client + hosted staging), (go client + local runtime). - Flaky integration test in TS (stream-reconnect/test) was quarantined and re-run; the final CI matrix is green.

Why this is incremental: The design intentionally provides thin, language-idiomatic facades while centralizing the mental model (factory + token provider). The goal is to reduce follow-up churn when we add delegated auth (edge proxies) or pre-warmed leases.

Related: ENG-4231 (credential strategy consolidation), ENG-4302 (stream naming ergonomics).
Kai Huang: Nice consolidation; please ensure the factory surface is intentionally minimal. Please add a unit test that exercises simultaneous token refresh from two streams in the Python SDK.
Ava Moreno (author): Added test python/tests/test_concurrent_refresh.py and documented the reasoning for single-refresh dedupe in the factory implementation.
Lina Patel: TS types look good; request small rename: PullStreamReader -> PullReader across public exports to match other language conventions. Also add an explicit example in the ts example folder.
Ava Moreno (author): Renamed the exported type in src/stream/index.ts and left a compatibility alias with a deprecation comment. Example added at examples/credential-factory/ts/README.md.
Marco Reyes: CI flaky job re-run looks stable. One comment: the go adapter uses a goroutine-per-subscriber refresh that may cause bursty refresh; can we add a jitter config?
Ava Moreno (author): Added jitterProfile option to the factory and documented default values; updated go factory implementation to use the jitter when scheduling refresh backoffs.
Add CredentialFactory across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs to standardize token provider wiring; consolidate stream primitive exports and provide backward-compatible aliases; add migration guide and cross-SDK integration tests.

Motivation: under mixed latency-throughput workloads the paged KV cache has seen repeated hotset churn where short-lived peaks evict blocks belonging to steady low-throughput streams. This PR introduces a page-aware age-bucket allocator plus a lightweight per-request sticky pin heuristic to reduce unnecessary reclaims and improve end-to-end tail latency and CPU utilization. Summary of changes: 1) age-bucket allocator: split free/pinned free lists into 4 age buckets based on last-access epoch to bias reuse toward recently used blocks and prefer eviction from oldest buckets; 2) per-stream sticky pinning: when a request stream accesses more than N sequential pages we mark a lightweight sticky pin token for that stream for M seconds so subsequent nearby allocations prefer previously-resident blocks and avoid KV fetch churn; 3) soft-reserve fastpath: introduce a per-worker fast reserve that can hand out small contiguous spans without global lock for latency-sensitive allocations; 4) eviction hinting API: add hint payloads to eviction scorer so callers (e.g., scheduler) can prioritize eviction when under transient load; 5) metrics and tracing: new histograms for "kv.alloc.latency_ms" and per-bucket occupancy gauges plus trace spans for sticky-pin lifecycle; 6) tests and benchmarks: microbench harness for mixed read/write streams and an end-to-end canary config used in perf-canary repo. Backwards compatibility: allocator keeps same public behaviour; sticky-pin tokens are internal and time-bounded. Checklist: [x] design doc linked [x] unit tests [x] bench scripts [x] e2e canary config [x] metrics added [x] rollout plan included. Rollout plan: staged canary -> 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback on sustained tail latency regressions. Related work: follows principles from ENG-4819 (KV cache reclaim refactor) and complements pr-129876 lazy-reservation work. No user-facing API changes.
Ethan Cho (2025-11-07): High-level this looks good; can you quantify expected memory overhead for the extra bucket lists?
Sofia Martinez (2025-11-07): The extra pointers are ~8 bytes per page; for a 128GB working set this is ~64MB and we include a feature flag to disable buckets if memory is constrained.
Priya Nair (2025-11-08): Request change: the sticky-pin lifetime needs a backoff when a stream becomes cold to avoid permanent reservations. Please add exponential decay.
Sofia Martinez (2025-11-08): Added exponential decay to token TTL and added test to validate token expiry under intermittent traffic.
Marco Liu (2025-11-09): CI flaky on allocator_tests.rs on macOS runner, appears due to timing in bench harness; suggested using a polling loop with deadline instead of fixed sleeps.
Sofia Martinez (2025-11-09): Updated tests to use deadline-based waits; re-ran CI.
Ethan Cho (2025-11-11): Approved and verified perf numbers in canary: 95th latency down ~18% and CPU sys% down ~7% for mixed workload W-2. Marking ready to merge.
Add a page-aware age-bucket allocator and per-stream sticky pinning to reduce KV cache churn and improve tail latency and CPU efficiency; metric and tracing additions included

Context: Three SDK teams have drifted on small-but-cumulative differences in auth windowing, retry presets, and streaming consumer ergonomics which cause intermittent resume failures and inconsistent telemetry. This PR harmonizes behavior across the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs: 1) introduces a shared retry-profile artifact (lightweight JSON schema) and per-transport tuning hooks, 2) aligns the streaming async iterator/pullstream surface so all SDKs expose a pause/resume-friendly API (named StreamHandle in TS/Go and StreamSession in Python) with consistent backpressure hints, and 3) bumps SDK package versions to signal the ergonomics changes and minor breaking renames. Changes are additive where possible; a migration note is included for clients using raw internal session objects. Motivation: reduce cross-language surprises for platform users integrating with multi-service deployments and enable unified telemetry and experimentation of retry profiles. Summary of changes: - add /sdk/common/retry_profiles/schema.json and a small generator that emits language-specific presets - Python: add redispatch layer for retry presets, expose StreamSession.pause() and .resume(), docstrings and typed stubs updated - TypeScript: introduce StreamHandle with pause()/resume()/signalBackpressure(), migrate existing generator adapter to use new retry hook - Go: add RetryProfileLoader and StreamHandle type; ensure zero-allocation resume path for KV-cache hot path - tests: cross-sdk golden fixtures for backpressure signaling, end-to-end flaky-auth simulation harness - docs: migration guide under sdk/*/MIGRATING.md and cross-sdk examples under examples/streaming/multi-lang.md Testing and CI: unit tests for each SDK, cross-language e2e that runs a simulated auth rotation and intermittent 503s, linting and typechecks for all three SDKs passed. Release: bump py to 1.11.0, ts to 2.6.0, go to v1.9.0. Backwards compatibility: most surface additions are non-breaking; renames are documented and shims provided for a single minor release. Rollout plan: staged canary for hosted customers and library deprecation notices sent to heavy users.
