Motivation: Alert noise from token-cost and latency spikiness is often driven by repeated, near-duplicate prompt shapes and small config differences (quantization, seq_len, model variant). On incidents we repeatedly see many invocations that differ only in a few context tokens or client-side flags—this makes grouping noisy and rules brittle. This change introduces a lightweight invocation context hasher (config + prompt shape fingerprint) to group similar invocations, surface drift signals for prompt/token-shape distribution, and wire those signals into the alerting pipeline for adaptive alert suppression and automated reclassification of noisy bursts.

What this PR does (high level): add a deterministic invocation context hasher that emits a 64-bit stable fingerprint attached to traces and metrics; record per-fingerprint rollup metrics (invocation_count, p50/p95 latency, token_cost_mean, kv_cache_hit_rate); introduce drift detectors that compare recent fingerprint distributions against a rolling baseline and emit an anomaly tag; add a dashboard and exploration panels for fingerprint cohorts; add an alert tuning adapter that can downweight or suppress alerts when a single fingerprint accounts for >80% of cost/latency in the window (configurable).

Key goals: reduce alert churn from repetitive prompts, provide engineers a stable grouping key for triage, surface prompt-shape and model-config drift early, and keep overhead minimal (sampling and compact hashes).

Implementation notes: the hasher is a compact, collision-aware mix of: model identifier (model_id + quantization profile), sequence-length histogram (binned), top-k prompt token shape signature (shingled FNV64 over the first/last N tokens), and a small invocation feature vector (user_flags, streaming_mode, tool_calls_present). The hasher lives in the telemetry pipeline (in server-side pre-processor) and is attached as invocation.fingerprint to OTLP spans and metrics. Rollups are implemented as a new aggregation path that keeps reservoir sketches keyed by fingerprint for a 1h/24h window. Drift detector uses a lightweight JS divergence approximation and emits fingerprint.drift_score > 0.0 as a boolean tag after thresholding.

Backwards compatibility & privacy: fingerprint is not reversible; prompt tokens are not stored or transmitted. The fingerprint is a 64-bit hex string and should be treated as an opaque grouping key. We document PII considerations in the privacy section of the runbook.

Checklist:
- [x] runtime: context hasher implementation (Rust) with feature flag
- [x] telemetry: OTLP span/metric enrichment and schema bump
- [x] aggregation: add fingerprint-keyed rollups and reservoir sketches
- [x] dashboard: new fingerprint cohort panel + drift timeline
- [x] alerts: adapter to suppress alarms for single-fingerprint storms
- [x] tests: unit, integration, and end-to-end replay tests
- [x] docs/runbook: triage guidance and privacy notes

How to validate locally: follow observability/README.md run-local pipeline, set FEATURE_CONTEXT_HASHER=1, run replaybench against samples/observability/large-burst-cases.json, then open the dashboard at http://localhost:9090/d/fingerprint-cohorts.

Related work: builds on ENG-1953 (invocation cohorting prototype) and complements the alert-hysteresis work (ENG-2314). Incident INT-707 motivated the >80% cohort suppression heuristic.

Risks and mitigations: risk — collisions cause distinct prompts to join the same cohort. Mitigation — we added a collision monitor that emits fingerprint_collision_count and a sampling debug span with unhashed short token prefixes for the small percentage of flagged samples (opt-in). Performance risk — extra aggregation; mitigation — we used compact 64-bit keys and reservoir sketches to keep memory bounded.

Release notes: Adds invocation.fingerprint for telemetry, a fingerprint cohort dashboard, and a configurable alert adapter to suppress single-fingerprint storm noise.
Sofia: Can we confirm the privacy doc covers the case where customers intentionally log tokens? Author reply: Added a note and opt-in flag in docs/runbook/alert-tuning-and-privacy.md.
Noah: Suggest adding a CanaryConfig to limit suppression to non-production tenants. Author reply: Added canary flag and tests in alerts/adapters/fingerprint_suppressor.go.
Jules: Minor nit on OCI naming and schema bump. Author reply: Fixed schema version and updated telemetry migration file.

Motivation: tenant workloads show variable cold-start costs and suboptimal quant profiles across regions. This PR adds a low-risk daemon+controller (Prefill Runner) plus an offline/online calibration service (Econ Calibrator) that uses recent telemetry to generate tenant-specific prefill heuristics and suggested quantization safety bands. The change aims to reduce per-token unit cost for long-tail tenants by improving prefill coverage and safely nudging quant profiles where eval metrics indicate negligible quality impact. High-level changes: 1) controller/operator that schedules per-tenant prefill jobs and exposes a small, authenticated API for trigger control; 2) new econ-calibrator service that ingests compact workload summaries and runs a small simulation to recommend prefill batch sizes and quant-safety thresholds; 3) a CLI tool for operators to preview recommended changes and run canary rollouts; 4) lightweight schema extension for tenant preference objects and a safe fallthrough policy; 5) metrics/tracing and a new smoke test harness. Rollout plan: canary 5 tenants in us-west for 48h, monitor unit_cost, p50/p95 latency, and quality regression flags; automatic rollback if quality regressions >0.5% or latency SLO breaches. Docs: added a short quickstart and a runbook entry. Links: Linear ENG-1289 and ENG-4310 referenced, internal design doc: /docs/design/prefill-runner-econ-calibrator. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for controller and simulator - [x] e2e smoke that runs a canary profile - [x] CLI dry-run mode - [x] docs and runbook - [x] security review scopes and KMS integration notes - [x] load test at 10% production traffic simulated. Notes: this is intentionally conservative on automatic promotion of quant changes (suggest-only primary flow), the operator must opt-in to apply quant recommendations.
Maya: Can the calibrator run in offline-only mode for customers who require no control-plane changes? Author: yes, calibrator supports offline suggestions only and CLI can generate a YAML suggestion for manual review. Diego: Are quant suggestion thresholds conservative by default? Author: Yes, default policy is suggest-only and the suggested quant delta is capped to 2 bits change and validated by the simulation harness. Jessica: Approve after minor nits on logging strings were fixed. CI flake required a re-run of e2e-smoke which passed.
Add Prefill Runner and Econ Calibrator: tenant-aware prefill scheduling and suggestion-based quant recommendations. Default is suggest-only; operators must opt-in to apply quant changes. Includes CLI for dry-run and canary rollout support.

Motivation: Users integrating structured outputs and function calls need clearer, deterministic guarantees when streaming and when tool calls are emitted. Currently we have ad-hoc schema checks at the end of a response which leads to silent failures or expensive re-rolls for streaming clients. This PR introduces an output policy layer that participates in the streaming path to validate increments against a declared JSON schema, plus a "function-call fence" that prevents malformed tool-call payloads from being emitted downstream. The change also updates the OpenAI-compat adapter mapping so clients get actionable, stable error codes and suggestions for recovery.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds an Output Policy component to the runtime which can be configured per-request via response_format.schema and response_format.mode. The policy runs lightweight streaming checkpoints (schema latching) and can either annotate, buffer-and-repair, or abort depending on mode.
- Implements a Function Call Fence in the tool-calling pipeline that validates the function payload shape against the declared function schema before any side-effecting emission. If the fence trips, the runtime returns a structured diagnostic and prevents the call from reaching executors.
- Exposes a compat layer in api/openai_adapter to translate policy failures into OpenAI-compatible error payloads (with new error_type codes: schema_violation, function_fence, stream_checkpoint_failed). These payloads include guidance (retry with mode=permissive, attach failing token range, etc.) to help SDKs implement automated recovery.
- Adds a feature flag (runtime.output_policy.enabled) and a request-level toggle (response_format.mode) with values: permissive | warn | enforce. Existing clients default to permissive to preserve behavior.

Design notes:
- Streaming checks are implemented as checkpoints at sentence/JSON-boundary heuristics to minimize per-token overhead; the policy uses the same compiled validator as the final validation step to avoid drift.
- Buffer-and-repair attempts a single repair pass using the existing coercion helpers; we avoid iterative retries in this PR to keep latency predictable.
- Function-call fence hooks into the tool-call serializer; validation happens before any K/V caching or dispatch to external executors. This prevents partial side effects if a payload later fails validation.

Files touched (high level): crates/runtime/src/output_policy.rs, crates/runtime/src/streaming/checkpoint.rs, api/openai_adapter/response_mapper.py, api/openai_adapter/errors.py, sdk/python/redwood/schema_client.py, docs/response_format.md, tests/integration/test_stream_policy.py, tests/unit/test_function_fence.rs, infra/feature_flags/flags.yaml, examples/structured-output/annotated-example.json

Checklist:
- [x] Runtime output policy implementation with unit tests
- [x] Function call fence and unit tests
- [x] OpenAI adapter error mappings + tests
- [x] End-to-end streaming integration test (CI flaky capture added)
- [x] Docs for response_format.mode and migration guidance

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests cover validator wiring and fence rejection cases.
- Integration test simulates a streaming response where the generated JSON fragment would break the target schema; observed behavior: with mode=warn we emit a warning event in the stream and continue; with mode=enforce the stream terminates with a structured error and a resume token for clients that want to retry with permissive mode.
- Function call fence tests simulate malformed function args; the call is blocked and an action-level diagnostic is returned.
- We ran the change against the main CI matrix; two unrelated flaky e2e tests were retriggered and both passed on rerun.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan:
- Default remains permissive to avoid breaking existing customers.
- Feature-flag rollout across dedicated clusters for 48h, followed by gradual rollout to hosted API.
- SDKs will add helpers to surface new error_type codes; PRs for python/ts sdks will follow in a separate change (linked in linear).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Decide whether buffer-and-repair should be multi-pass for certain schemas (performance trade-off).
- Consider exposing structured 'stream events' for warnings to the Console/Observability so customers can alert on schema warnings.

Related: ENG-1429 (streaming schema deliverable), SUP-4052 (customer reported misrouted function call in streaming), ENG-1581 (openai compat error taxonomy).
Introduces an output policy layer that enforces JSON schema contracts at streaming checkpoints and fences function/tool-call emissions; includes OpenAI adapter mappings for clearer error codes. Rolling update behind feature-flag with compatibility toggle.
Eve Nakamura: Nice separation of concerns. Two questions: 1) what's the expected CPU impact for high qps streaming endpoints? 2) do we need an opt-in header for Dedicated customers?
Aisha Patel: Answered: we measured ~2-3% additional CPU at 1k qps with sentence-boundary checkpoints; we will gate via runtime.output_policy.enabled and expose runtime flag for Dedicated clusters. Added perf measurements in a follow-up benchmark PR.
Diego Morales: Can we avoid duplicating validators? The change looks like it references the same compiled validator but make that explicit in the code comments. Also please add a test for large arrays where checkpoint heuristics might split mid-structure.
Aisha Patel: Added code comment and unit test for large-array checkpointing (tests/unit/test_checkpoint_large_array.rs).

Context: As part of the audit logging standardization work, we need automated verification that every “sensitive action” emits a canonical v1 audit event (and that the payload validates) across Hosted and Private. This PR adds end-to-end integration tests that execute representative sensitive actions and assert that: (1) an audit event is produced, (2) event_type matches the taxonomy registry, (3) required fields are present and schema_version is set, and (4) correlation fields (request_id/trace_id/admin_action_id) are populated and consistent. Motivation: We have active customer escalations where coverage is hard to prove quickly (SUP-18421, SUP-18477). These tests are intended to become part of our “100% coverage” gate and to provide fast signal on regressions when new admin flows are added.

What’s included: Test harness: A new audit-event test helper that polls the audit ingest test sink with bounded retry and supports filtering by (tenant_id, actor.user_id, admin_action_id) to avoid flakiness and high-cardinality queries. Hosted fixture: Runs against the standard integration environment (api-gateway + control-plane + console-backend) using a service account to perform admin operations. Private fixture: Runs against the “private-mode” docker-compose test stack (single-node control plane + local audit sink) to ensure parity on event emission and schema tagging. Assertions: JSON Schema validation for v1 (via the shared validator library introduced earlier) plus targeted assertions for actor/target semantics (actor_type, actor_id, actor_session_id, source_ip where available). Correlation: Ensures request_id and trace_id are present; when an action spans multiple internal calls, the tests assert all emitted events share the same admin_action_id.

Sensitive actions covered (initial set): RBAC: Create role, update role permissions, assign role to user, remove role assignment. API Keys: Create key, rotate key, revoke key (asserts key material is never present; only key_id + truncated display_name). Policy/Routing: Update routing policy (fallback config) and verify event includes a stable policy_id and a bounded diff_summary. Export Config: Update audit log export destination (tests only the control-plane config write path; UI validation is covered elsewhere).

Not included / follow-ups: We intentionally did not add “data residency/retention change” tests in this PR to keep runtime manageable; those will land with the residency event producers (ENG-4839) and will reuse this harness. We also do not enforce “exactly one event per action” because some actions legitimately emit multiple events (e.g., policy change + rollout application); instead we assert at least one matching primary event_type and that any additional events validate.

Implementation details: The tests use a new TestAuditSinkClient with exponential backoff (max 30s) and a deterministic query key built from admin_action_id. We tag each test action with an x-admin-action-id header generated once per test and propagated through the request context (requires prior propagation work from ENG-4830; this PR includes small glue in test clients only). Where source_ip is not reliably present in local/private runs, the test asserts that source_ip is either a valid IP string OR omitted, but it must never be a free-form value. The schema validator runs in “strict required fields + allow namespaced extensions” mode so teams can add x_redwood_* extensions without breaking tests.

Changed areas (high level): packages/audit/audit-schema-validator: add a test-friendly entrypoint for validating a decoded payload and returning a concise error list (no stack traces) packages/audit/audit-testkit: new helper for polling the sink and matching events by predicate services/control-plane/tests/audit_sensitive_actions_test.go: RBAC + API key lifecycle scenarios services/policy-engine/tests/audit_policy_change_test.go: routing policy update scenario services/audit-ingest/test-sink: adds support for querying by admin_action_id with TTL-limited in-memory index (test-only build tag) ci/integration: wires new suite into nightly + gated “security” job (gated on files under services/control-plane, services/policy-engine, packages/audit)

Sample assertion (illustrative): Expect event_type == "rbac.role.updated"; schema_version == "1.0"; event_id is non-empty; occurred_at is RFC3339; actor_type == "user" (or "service_account" in fixtures); actor_id matches requester; tenant_id matches; request_id/trace_id present; admin_action_id equals injected header; target_type == "rbac_role"; target_id equals created role id; diff_summary length < 1024 and contains only allowlisted keys; no secret-like fields appear (regex guard against token/key/pem/private_key).

CI: - unit: pass - lint: pass - integration-hosted (new suite): pass - integration-private (new suite): pass Note: integration-private initially failed due to the test sink index not being enabled under the correct build tag; fixed in commit 6/7.

Risk/rollback: Low risk. Changes are test-only except for the test-sink query index behind a test build tag. If we see flakes, we can temporarily move these tests to nightly-only by toggling the CI job condition, but the intent is to keep them gated for sensitive areas.

Docs/ops: Adds a short README to packages/audit/audit-testkit describing how to run locally and how to add new sensitive action cases. Follow-up: Logan is adding a coverage dashboard view that correlates expected event_types to observed events; these tests will be one of the inputs.

Checklist: [x] Tests cover both Hosted and Private fixtures [x] Validates payload against schema v1 [x] Asserts taxonomy-compliant event_type [x] Guards against secrets/PII leakage in payload [x] CI wired with stable runtime (< 9 minutes for new suite)

Refs: Linear ENG-4834. Related: PR-21984 (schema validator), PR-21991 (event registry), PR-22047 (correlation). Customer context: SUP-18421, SUP-18477.
Marcus Lin (review): Good coverage set. Two asks: (1) please make sure we don’t assert source_ip in private runs where it’s not stable, and (2) can we tighten the secret-leak regex to catch PEM blocks? Leila Farouk (author): Updated assertions to allow missing source_ip but reject non-IP formats; added PEM block detection and a denylist for common secret keys. Logan Wright (review): The polling window at 30s seems high—can we reduce to avoid masking latency regressions? Also make the query keyed off admin_action_id so the sink scan doesn’t explode. Leila Farouk: Polling uses exponential backoff with early exit; max remains 30s to accommodate cold starts in CI. Added admin_action_id index to the test sink (test-only) and reduced default poll to 15s with override for private. Ethan Park (review): For RBAC tests, please assert target_type/target_id semantics (role vs assignment) and ensure diff_summary is bounded. Leila Farouk: Added per-event assertions for target_type and bounded diff_summary (<1024 chars) + allowlisted keys only. Sahana Iyer (review): CI wiring looks good; please add a short README on how to add new cases and run locally. Leila Farouk: Added docs/internal/audit-logging/adding-sensitive-action-tests.md and a minimal README in audit-testkit. Sean Gallagher (review): Flake risk: avoid strict ordering assumptions and don’t require exactly one event. Leila Farouk: Tests now assert “at least one primary event_type” and validate all matched events; no ordering assumptions. Approvals: Marcus Lin approved. Logan Wright approved. Ethan Park approved. Sahana Iyer approved. Sean Gallagher approved.

payload.body:
Background and motivation:
Services using Dedicated fleets exhibit frequent autoscaler churning when tenant traffic arrives as short high-frequency microbursts. The existing single-signal headroom estimator (90th-percentile EWMA) under-reacts to transient demand and over-reacts when bursts happen repeatedly, producing oscillation. This PR implements two complementary mechanisms: 1) an ensemble headroom calibrator that combines multiple short- and medium-horizon predictors to produce a more stable headroom suggestion, and 2) a burst-quieting cooldown adapter that temporarily suppresses aggressive autoscaler decommits when microburst patterns are detected.

High-level summary of changes:
- runtime/autoscaler/ensemble_calibrator.go: New ensemble estimator that fuses EWMA, short AR(1) predictor, and a quantile sketch (P2 approximation) into a weighted headroom suggestion per-tenant. The weights adapt based on recent prediction error.
- runtime/autoscaler/cooldown_adapter.go: Burst quieting logic that creates a per-tenant quiet window after burst detection. During the window, scale-down decisions are delayed or softened (graceful decrease factor applied).
- runtime/telemetry/utilization_reporter.go: Added smoothed-percentile metrics (p50_smooth, p90_smooth, p99_smooth) and a burst_event counter/taggable by tenant and fleet. Telemetry uses the same batching path as existing metrics to avoid increased cardinality.
- config/defaults.yaml: New feature flags and tunables (ensemble.enabled, ensemble.weights, quieting.window_ms, quieting.threshold_tokens). Defaults are conservative (disabled by default) to allow staged rollout.
- test/autoscaler/ensemble_calibrator_test.go and test/e2e/burst_quieting_integration_test.go: Unit and integration tests covering estimator convergence and cooldown semantics under synthetic microburst traces.
- docs/observability/metrics.md: Documentation for new metrics and recommended dashboard panels.

Design notes and rationale:
- Why ensemble? No single estimator performed well across tenants with different burstiness profiles. The ensemble balances short-term sensitivity (AR(1)) and stability (EWMA + sketch quantiles). We adapt weights via a simple inverse-error scheme to avoid heavy meta-learning complexity.
- Why cooldown adapter? Autoscaler oscillation primarily occurred on scale-down paths when warm pool and decommit heuristics reacted to transient reductions. Quieting prevents premature contract of capacity that forces subsequent immediate scale-ups. The adapter is deliberately conservative: it only applies when burst detection confidence exceeds configured threshold and when warm pool utilization is below a safety cutoff.
- Telemetry trade-offs: To remain cost-conscious we reuse existing metric aggregation flows and avoid high-cardinality labels. Burst events are taggable by tenant id but emitted as sparse events (counter+last_seen timestamp) to support downstream anomaly detection without blowing ingestion costs.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag (ensemble.enabled=false).
2) Enable on a single non-critical dedicated fleet in canary mode with extra telemetry retention for two weeks.
3) If metrics show reduced scale churn and no SLO regressions, enable on 20% of fleets via targeting rules.
4) Full rollout to all dedicated fleets after 6 weeks of positive signals.
Feature flags allow immediate rollback.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests cover estimator behavior across controlled traces (steady, ramp, repeated microburst).
- E2E replayed traces show 35–60% reduction in scale-down+scale-up cycles for microbursty tenants in canary fleet.
- Performance: ensemble_calibrator introduces a small CPU cost (~0.7% median p50 on autoscaler process); benchmarks attached.

Commits (summary):
- a1f3d4e: initial implementation of ensemble calibrator and interfaces
- b2d4c5f: add burst detection and cooldown adapter, wiring into autoscaler flow
- c3e5f6a: telemetry metrics and docs + feature flag integration
- d4f6a7b: unit & e2e tests, benchmarking harness, CI adjustments

Files changed (high-level):
- runtime/autoscaler/ensemble_calibrator.go
- runtime/autoscaler/cooldown_adapter.go
- runtime/telemetry/utilization_reporter.go
- config/defaults.yaml
- test/autoscaler/ensemble_calibrator_test.go
- test/e2e/burst_quieting_integration_test.go
- docs/observability/metrics.md

Review conversation (highlights):
- Lukas Meyer (review): "Can we guard the ensemble path with a strict CPU/budget check? Autoscaler loop is latency sensitive and we should gate extra cycles. Also please add an experiment flag for weights so we can A/B tune without code changes."
- Priya (author): "Added a cheap fast-path: if the tenant request rate is below min_samples we skip the ensemble and fall back to EWMA. We also exposed ensemble.weights via config and Linear ENG-2104 is tracking the tuning experiment."
- Aisha Patel (review): "Telemetry names look good. Please ensure burst_event emission doesn't add high-cardinality labels. Also we should emit a 'quieting_applied' gauge so SRE can monitor suppressed decommits."
- Priya: "Burst events remain sparse and tenant tags are optional; added quieting_applied as a boolean gauge per-tenant (low-cardinality since only applied tenants will report)."
- Diego Ramirez (approval): "Test coverage is good. I ran the e2e with production-like traces; behavior is stable. Approving subject to small nit on doc wording."

CI and checks:
- go vet: pass
- unit tests: pass (coverage +1.8%% for autoscaler pkg)
- integration tests: pass (e2e harness reproduced microburst scenario)
- lint: pass after minor fixes

Merge outcome:
- Merged via squash-merge to main after approvals. Feature gated behind ensemble.enabled=false by default.

Follow-ups / operational notes:
- ENG-2049 will track the weight-tuning experiment and dashboards for quieting effectiveness.
- Create a Grafana panel (suggested in docs) that correlates burst_event count with scale cycles per tenant for post-rollout evaluation.
- Monitor CPU impact on autoscaler process for the first 2 weeks of canary.

If you want a quick demo: checkout the branch and run test/e2e/replay.sh with testdata/microburst-tenant.json to see the quieting behavior and generated telemetry.
Introduce ensemble-based headroom calibration and tenant-level burst quieting. Improves autoscaler stability under microbursty workloads and provides new smoothed utilization and burst-event telemetry. Safe rollout via feature flag and gradual canary on dedicated fleets.
Lukas Meyer: Can we guard the ensemble path with a strict CPU/budget check? Autoscaler loop is latency sensitive and we should gate extra cycles. Also please add an experiment flag for weights so we can A/B tune without code changes.
Priya Natarajan: Added a cheap fast-path: if the tenant request rate is below min_samples we skip the ensemble and fall back to EWMA. Exposed ensemble.weights via config (ENG-2104 tracks tuning).
Aisha Patel: Telemetry names look good. Please ensure burst_event emission doesn't add high-cardinality labels. Also add a 'quieting_applied' gauge so SRE can monitor suppressed decommits.
Priya Natarajan: Burst events are sparse and tenant tags are optional; added quieting_applied gauge per-tenant. Updated docs to recommend low-cardinality panels.
Diego Ramirez: Tested with production-like traces, behavior is stable. Approving after doc nit fix.

payload.body:
Introduces a decommit-gradient controller and a fair-headroom allocator to reduce waste during scale-downs while preserving tenant SLAs; telemetry emits leak-adjusted utilization percentiles for better autoscaler decisions.
Motivation and summary: This PR adds a decommit-gradient controller and a fair-headroom allocator aimed at smoothing Dedicated fleet scale-downs and reducing wasted reserved capacity. Current abrupt decommits caused short-term SLA blips for tenants with bursty traffic. The decommit-gradient gradually releases reservation capacity over a tunable window based on utilization deltas and tenant priority weights. The fair-headroom allocator rebalances remaining headroom proportional to tenant earned credits and recent SLO slippage.

Design highlights and behavioral guarantees: - Decommit gradient: when a fleet/zone is marked for capacity reduction, we calculate a decaying commit fraction over the configured window (default 10m). The controller issues soft-decommit events first (allowing tenants to voluntarily release warmlets) and only escalates to hard decommits if soft steps are not observed. This reduces mass preemption and preserves KV cache locality for recent active tenants. - Fair-headroom allocator: maintains per-tenant weights (configurable via the tenant manifest) and computes redistributed headroom using a proportional fairness objective. It protects minimum floor reservations and ensures that tenants with recent SLO regressions receive extra headroom within configured caps. - Telemetry: exports leak-adjusted utilization percentiles (p50/p90/p99 of effective utilization after factoring in soft-decommit leakage) and a "decommit-residual" gauge to help autoscaler tune hysteresis.

Config example (added to dedicated/autoscaler/configs):
- decommitGradient:
    enabled: true
    window_seconds: 600
    soft_step_percent: 20
    escalation_threshold_seconds: 180
- fairHeadroom:
    enabled: true
    min_floor_per_tenant: 0.05
    redistribution_cap_percent: 40
    sllo_slack_weight: 2.0

Commits (high-level): - f1a2c3d: add decommit-gradient controller scaffold + unit tests - b4e5f6a: implement soft/hard decommit state machine + integration stubs - c7d8e9f: add fair-headroom allocator implementation and unit tests - d0e1f2a: telemetry exporter for leak-adjusted percentiles + Prometheus metrics - e3f4g5h: config docs, sample tenant manifest, end-to-end e2e test harness updates

Files changed (high-level): - dedicated/autoscaler/controller/decommit_gradient.go (+214/-34) - dedicated/autoscaler/allocator/fair_headroom.go (+132/-8) - dedicated/autoscaler/config/defaults.yaml (+24/-0) - observability/metrics/decommit_telemetry.go (+26/-6) - e2e/tests/decommit_gradient_test.go (+88/-32) - docs/operators/decommit-gradient.md (+18/-4) - pkg/tenant/manifest_schema.go (+10/-5)

Small illustrative snippet (decommit policy state machine):
- soft -> observationPeriod -> escalate -> hard

Review conversation (condensed into a single continuous narrative): Diego Morales: "This looks promising for reducing 1-2 minute SLA blips during scale-downs. Can we guarantee we won't starve small tenants when redistribution happens?" Aisha Raman (author): "FairHeadroom enforces min_floor_per_tenant and a redistribution_cap_percent; we also include sllo_slack_weight to bias leftover headroom toward tenants with recent SLO slack. Added unit tests for corner cases." Claire Jensen: "Need CI signals for the new Prometheus metrics — add those to observability/metrics-ci job." Aisha Raman: "Added metrics to observability CI and a lightweight smoke test (e2e) to validate gauge emissions." Ravi Patel: "Please ensure the escalation_threshold_seconds is conservative; we saw tight thresholds cause churn in previous rollouts." Aisha Raman: "Default set to 180s; made it configurable and documented recommended tuning." Diego Morales: "Verified perf numbers locally; merge after CI passes."

CI summary: - linux/unit: pass - linux/integration (flaky): pass (rerun) - e2e/decommit-smoke: pass - lint: pass - observability/metrics-ci: pass

Benchmarks and measured impact (staging cluster tests): - baseline burst SLO violations during scale-down: 2.8% of requests in 10m window - with decommit-gradient + fair-headroom: 0.6% (-78% relative) - average reserved-waste (unused reserved capacity) during 30m busy->idle transition: baseline 17.2% -> after change 9.3% (-46% relative) - tail latency p99 during scale-down: baseline 210ms -> after change 190ms (+/- noise)

Rollout plan and safety: - Feature behind a gate (dedicated.autoscaler.decommitGradient.enabled=false by default in earlier releases). We enabled it in staging for 2 days with synthetic bursty tenant traffic and longer soak. - Canary rollout 10% of fleets for 24h with conservative window_seconds and soft_step_percent. - Monitoring runbook updated (docs/operators/decommit-gradient.md) with exact alerts: high decommit-residual, headroom-imbalance score, and increased eviction-rate.

Related work and references: ENG-2143 proposed per-tenant earned-credit accounting we reuse here; ENG-2199 introduced prefix KV cache affinity metrics that informed the decision to favor soft-decommits. This PR does not change billing behavior or tenant quotas.

Merge outcome: merged via squash with commit message: "Add decommit gradient controller and fair-headroom allocator; telemetry and docs."

payload.body:
This PR adds structured audit log events for route-level quantization profile changes. We currently persist route config changes and have an audit log primitive, but quantization profile settings were not emitted with enough structure to support compliance exports, internal forensics, and Console change history views. This change emits explicit events when (a) quantization is enabled/disabled at the route level and (b) quantization_profile_ref changes (including transitions to/from "default"). Events include actor identity, tenant + route identifiers, the resolved change type, and a normalized diff payload so downstream exporters/SIEM can index reliably.

Scope:
- Emit new audit event types for quant profile changes in the route config write path.
- Include actor (user/service), auth context, tenant_id, route_id, and change diff fields.
- Normalize diff schema to support both API and Console changes (same event contract).
- Add unit tests + golden fixtures for event payloads.
- Add minimal docs for event fields for the audit exporter pipeline.

Non-goals:
- No approval workflow/2-person review gating (tracked separately).
- No retroactive backfill of historical route config changes.
- No changes to policy evaluation or runtime behavior.

Event contract (v1):
- event_name: one of quant_profile.enabled, quant_profile.disabled, quant_profile.ref_changed
- actor_type: user|service
- actor_id: stable id from auth token
- actor_email: populated for user actors when available
- tenant_id, route_id, route_name
- request_id + trace_id (when available)
- diff: normalized string fields (see tests) with old/new values for quant_profile_ref and enabled boolean

Notes:
- We intentionally log the user-supplied profile ref (e.g., "qp:llama3-70b:int8:v3" or "default") rather than the fully resolved runtime selection, to avoid ambiguity and keep the audit record tied to configuration intent.
- PII: actor_email is already present in other audit events; we follow the same redaction controls and retention.

Related:
- INT-9170: ensure audit exporter includes quant_profile_id/ref and route identifiers.
- PR-18496: Console backend route settings endpoints.
- PR-18566: Console changelog view (consumes these events).
Chloe Martin (review): Can we guarantee we only emit one event per request? If a user flips enabled=false and also clears ref in the same PATCH, are we emitting multiple events?
Jada Williams (author): Currently yes: we emit (1) enabled/disabled when the enabled flag transitions and (2) ref_changed when the ref changes. That matches other audit areas (multiple events per request) and is easier to query. I added request_id/trace_id so the exporter can correlate events.
Ethan Park (review): Please ensure we never log the resolved profile (post-policy) here. Audit should reflect config intent. Also, include route_name to make SIEM queries readable.
Jada Williams (author): Ack. Updated emitter to log only the user-specified quantization_profile_ref. Added route_name as a top-level field with route_id/tenant_id.
Naomi Feldman (security review): Actor fields: actor_email is ok but we should keep it optional for service actors and ensure redaction rules remain consistent. Also confirm RBAC failures do not emit events.
Jada Williams (author): actor_email is only present for actor_type=user; service actors include actor_id + service_name. RBAC failures short-circuit before any emit call; added a test asserting no audit events on 403.
Kevin Osei (audit export review): INT-9170 asks for quant_profile_id. Are we using id or ref? Exporter allowlist needs stable fields with clear semantics.
Jada Williams (author): We don’t have a stable numeric id at the config layer; we store a ref string (includes version). I updated naming to quant_profile_ref consistently across the event payload and exporter allowlist. Added docs entry clarifying it’s the configured ref, not resolved selection.
Chloe Martin (review): Nit: diff payload should be consistent strings; avoid nested objects in the proto so exporters don’t have to special-case. Can we flatten diff.* keys?
Jada Williams (author): Done. diff is now a set of string fields: diff_field, diff_old, diff_new, plus diff_enabled_old/new for the toggle path. Updated golden fixtures.
No migration. Safe to deploy behind existing audit log pipeline. Verified in staging by toggling quantization on a test route and confirming three events: ref_changed, enabled, disabled (on revert). Exporter allowlist updated so fields appear in downstream exports.
Internal: Audit log now records route-level quantization profile enable/disable and profile ref changes with actor/route metadata for compliance exports and Console change history.

Motivation: Tenant workloads show multimodal sequence-length and arrival distributions; static batch/caching defaults lead to suboptimal unit economics. This PR introduces the Tranche Econ Tiler (TET) — a runtime component plus a small CLI to infer tenant-prefill "tranches" (batch shape + KV-cache allocation + quant tier) from historical traffic and cost signals, and emit safe defaults for the autoscaler and cost-suggester.

What this changes: Adds a new runtime component (tranche-tiler) that runs as part of the prefill pipeline. TET: (1) ingests sample windows, (2) computes candidate tranche templates using a tiling strategy that balances latency SLOs vs tokens/unit cost, (3) scores candidates with the unit-econ evaluator, and (4) exposes an HTTP endpoint and a CLI to export curated defaults as YAML presets. The CLI supports dry-run mode and a deterministic seed to reproduce tranche generation.

Key features: safe fallback to existing autopilot defaults; explicit quant-tier suggestions (fp16/int8/awq-based hints) tied to a conservative quality budget; cache-budget mapper to allocate KV cache capacity per tranche; lightweight telemetry counters (tranche.created, tranche.applied, tranche.fallback) and unit-econ drift metrics.

Why different from previous work: existing PRs tuned batch/caching heuristics at global or tenant-profile level. TET introduces hierarchical "tranches" so one tenant can have multiple coexisting templates (short-form, interactive; long-form, batch) and the runtime will route requests to the most cost-effective tranche without breaking existing SLO routing rules. It emphasizes reproducible presets-as-code that can be reviewed in Git.

Compatibility and safety: Generated presets are opt-in by default. When applied in Managed/Dedicated environments the runtime performs an A/B rollout (canary 5%, 25%, 100%) with automatic rollback triggers tied to latency or quality regressions. The PR wires into existing rollback hooks.

Testing and rollout plan: unit tests for tiler heuristics + end-to-end integration tests with prefiller harness included. CI runs a small synthetic traffic replay to validate no regressions at scale. We plan a staged rollout: internal dogfood -> beta customers on Dedicated -> default opt-in after 4 weeks of telemetry.

Notes: this PR contains a new small CLI binary (redwood-tiler) and a migration that adds a new config section to defaults/cost_profiles.yaml. Please focus reviews on runtime contention points and the safe-fallback orchestration logic.
feat(prefill): add tranche tiler runtime with basic tile-generation pipeline
feat(cli): add redwood-tiler CLI with export/dry-run/seed options
chore(config): add tranche templates schema and default examples
test(prefill): integration test for tiler with synthetic replay
perf(prefill): lightweight caching of sample windows to reduce memory surge
Ben Carter: overall design looks solid; please add a short doc blurb about memory accounting when multiple tranches are active (resolved in c3f5a1e)
Lina Zhou: suggest limiting quant suggestions to model families that have been experimentally validated (requested change: added whitelist in quant_suggester.go)
Ethan Brooks: CI failed flake on integration test first run; reran and green (see CI logs). Also requested a canary rollout test — added a small e2e that simulates 5/25/100 percent traffic split
Introduce Tranche Econ Tiler (TET) — runtime and CLI to generate tenant-prefill tranche presets. Adds conservative quant-tier hints, cache budget mapper, and rollout safety hooks. Opt-in by default. See docs/cli/redwood-tiler.md and examples/presets/tranche-presets.example.yaml for usage.

payload.body:
Context: We currently rely on simple token-rate ceilings and percentile-based utilization for tenant throttling and autoscaler decisions. This leads to two operational gaps: 1) sudden bursty tenants can repeatedly cause short-lived tail latencies and capacity churn, and 2) our utilization signals (avg/p90) do not capture temporal volatility which is useful for preemptive autoscaling. Motivation: Introduce a lightweight runtime 'rate envelope' controller that enforces soft per-tenant concurrency/throughput envelopes with graceful degradation and backoff, and add a 'utilization entropy' reporter that quantifies temporal variability in per-tenant utilization to inform the autoscaler and the operations dashboard. High level changes: - New runtime controller pkg/autoscaler/rate_envelope_controller.go that enforces tenant envelopes and exposes a ranked violation metric. Envelope semantics are soft: requests that would exceed the envelope are accepted where possible but marked for best-effort throttling and may be routed to a lower-cost variant when SLA tier allows. - Utilization entropy reporter at pkg/telemetry/util_entropy_reporter.go that computes a rolling entropy-like score over time-bucketed utilization histograms (per-tenant, per-pool) and emits metrics util.entropy{tenant, pool} and util.entropy_percentile. - Autoscaler integration: the dedicated autoscaler now ingests util.entropy and uses a hysteresis-weighted scaling factor to favour scale-up on high-entropy tenants. Implementation notes and knobs: - rate_envelope is configurable via tenant config: envelope.max_concurrency, envelope.max_tokens_per_sec, envelope.penalty_backoff_ms. Defaults mimic current soft-burst limits but add a decay window. - util_entropy uses 1m buckets by default, 12-bucket rolling window (12 minutes), config at telem.entropy.window_size and telem.entropy.buckets. - A new admin API endpoint /admin/tenants/{id}/envelope lets SRE inspect and override envelopes for an incident. Rollout plan: 1) Feature gated, default off for existing Dedicated customers. 2) Enable for a small pilot pool (canary) for 48h with increased telemetry retention. 3) Gradual ramp across remaining dedicated pools subject to per-pool validation. Tests and verification: - Unit tests for envelope admission, backoff penalty, and decay behavior. - Integration test that replays a bursty workload showing reduced tail latencies and fewer scale churn events. - Simulated autoscaler runs showing earlier scale-ups for high-entropy tenants and reduced oscillation. Backwards compatibility: Soft semantics preserve current behavior when feature disabled; metrics are additive. Related work: follows on ENG-4521 (tenant burst policy revamp) and ENG-4590 (autoscaler signal enrichment). See design doc: /docs/infra/rate-envelopes.md. Security: no new secrets; admin API requires existing admin RBAC.
Marina Chen: Nice model — can you explain why we chose entropy over variance? The design doc briefly mentions robustness to multi-modal patterns but I want a short justification in code comments.
Author (Nikhil Rao): Added inline comment in util_entropy_reporter.go explaining that entropy captures distribution shape and is less sensitive to single large outliers than variance; linked to a short note in the doc.
Luis Gomez: The admission path needs clearer telemetry for dropped vs penalized requests. Please emit envelope.admit{ok,penalized,dropped} counters and include the penalty reason label.
Author: Added counters and a small label set (reason: backpressure|variant-route|quota). Updated tests to assert counters.
Reza Haddad: Integration test shows a 12% reduction in tail latency for pilot. We should add a safety timeout to admin override to prevent accidental long-term overrides.
Author: Implemented admin override TTL with default 1h and updated API docs and console UI to show TTL.
Introduce: rate envelope controller (soft per-tenant concurrency/throughput envelopes), util.entropy telemetry (temporal variability score) and autoscaler integration that uses entropy to reduce oscillation; Admin: new /admin/tenants/{id}/envelope override with TTL. Notes: feature gated for Dedicated; opt-in pilot followed by gradual rollout.
Integration replay: p99 latency for pilot pool down 12% under same provision; autoscaler churn events reduced from 7->3 over 1h simulated window; CPU overhead ~0.6% in telemetry aggregator for 10k tenants.
When enabling on a pool: increase telemetry retention to 30m for entropy buckets during pilot, monitor metric util.entropy and envelope.admit_penalized. If penalized rates >5% sustained, inspect tenant workload and consider increasing envelope or routing policy.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: production inference workloads show wide variation in token density (short prompts with long completions vs long prompts with short completions). Existing seqlen bucketing reduces padding but fails to consider token-density skew inside a slot and how KV cache hits change effective cost per request. This PR introduces a token-density-aware orchestrator that (1) estimates per-request token-cost density at enqueue time, (2) consolidates "elastic slots" by greedily coalescing high-density with low-density requests to balance GPU occupancy, and (3) applies a small kernel-alignment hint when forming device batches so quantized kernels avoid pathological padding overhead. Goals: reduce padded tokens across the workload, lower p95 latency variance during mixed workloads, and keep throughput stable without SLO violations. Design summary: - Token density score: a heuristic combining prompt_len / (prompt_len + expected_completion_len) with model-specific kernel-cost coefficients learned from runtime telemetry. The score is computed on request arrival and stored as a short-lived annotation for batching decisions. - Elastic slot consolidation: rather than fixed seqlen buckets, we create slots with a target token-budget. New requests are placed into existing slots where adding them increases expected utilization but keeps padding cost under a threshold; otherwise we open a new slot. Slots have a soft timeout to avoid head-of-queue starvation. - KV-aware dispatch: requests tagged with high KV-hit probabilities are preferentially grouped to the same slot when kernel alignment hints indicate contiguous KV cache layout to reduce cache thrash. - Kernel alignment hints: small metadata (~1 byte) attached to slot composition to request specific CUDA kernel shapes or quantization-friendly paths. Implementation highlights: - runtime/batcher/elastic_slot_batcher.{cc,hh}: new orchestrator implementation with slot bookkeeping and token-density scoring. - runtime/scheduler/kv_aware_dispatcher.{cc,hh}: compact dispatcher that uses KV hit probability to bias slot assignment. - runtime/metrics: added token_density_histogram and slot_utilization_ratio metrics and dashboard panels. - config: new flags in rconfig: batch.slot_target_tokens, batch.max_slot_pad_ratio, batch.elastic_timeout_ms. - migration: existing seqlen bucketing remains available and is the default; the new orchestrator is behind rconfig flag batch.strategy=elastic_token_density for controlled rollout. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for token-density scoring and slot consolidation logic - [x] Integration test with synthetic mixed workload generator - [x] Canary run on perf-canary with 72h windows - [x] Dashboard panels and alerts for slot starvation & padding regression Compatibility & safety: default behavior unchanged (seqlen bucketer remains default). The orchestrator is opt-in via rconfig and feature flag; metrics gated for first-stage rollout. Benchmarks (perf-canary synthetic workload that mixes 20% long prompts/short completions, 80% short prompts/long completions): - end-to-end token cost reduction: 18% median vs default seqlen-bucketed batching - p95 latency: improved by 12% on average across runs - tail variance: 25% lower measured as sigma(p95) across machines Observability & CI: added deterministic unit tests; CI pipeline shows full runtime build + integration_e2e suite passing. The canary run revealed an early KV-cache hotpath contention which was fixed by changing map iteration order in kv_aware_dispatcher and re-running canary. Review conversation (high level): - Marco Ruiz: requested clearer invariants around slot timeout and starvation; asked for an automated test that simulates prolonged high-density bursts. - Author (Aisha): added integration test burst_simulator.py and tuned soft timeout from 80ms->120ms after discussion. - Leah Chen: asked for explicit fallback when kernel alignment hint is unsupported; author added fallback to default kernel path and test coverage. - Omar Siddiq: approved after confirming telemetry and dashboards show no regression on memory usage. CI summary: initial run had one flaky test (kv_cache_eviction_test) failing on macOS runners; flaky test was stabilized by reducing time sensitivity and rerun passed. Merge notes: squash-merged to main after canary gating completed and perf metrics validated. Files touched (high level): - runtime/batcher/elastic_slot_batcher.cc - runtime/batcher/elastic_slot_batcher.hh - runtime/scheduler/kv_aware_dispatcher.cc - runtime/scheduler/kv_aware_dispatcher.hh - runtime/metrics/token_density_metrics.cc - runtime/config/rconfig_defaults.yaml - tests/batcher/test_elastic_slots.py - tests/integration/burst_simulator.py - docs/rfcs/2026-02-token-density-batching.md - dashboards/perf/token_density_orchestrator.json - examples/quickstarts/elastic-token-density.yaml How to try locally: set rconfig.batch.strategy=elastic_token_density and rconfig.batch.slot_target_tokens=4096; run bazel test //tests/..., start local runtime with --enable-experimental-batcher. Release notes: Introduces opt-in token-density-aware batch orchestrator with elastic slot consolidation, KV-aware dispatch, and kernel-alignment hints. Expected benefits: lower padded tokens and improved p95 latency for mixed-density workloads; no change to default behavior. Related: ENG-17834 (design), ENG-17902 (telemetry integration), SUP-6342 (customer report motivating KV-aware grouping).
Marco Ruiz: Please clarify slot starvation invariants and add a high-density burst test. - Response: added burst_simulator and adjusted timeout to 120ms
Leah Chen: What is the fallback if kernel-alignment hint is unsupported? - Response: added fallback to default kernel path and test coverage
Omar Siddiq: Verified telemetry and memory usage; LGTM after CI fixes.

payload.body:
Reliability: burst capacity is now guarded by an automated SLO gate that reduces/halts burst allocations when non-burst tenants experience sustained tail-latency regression. Includes alert annotations and a rollback-safe feature flag.
Context: During burst beta we saw a small but meaningful class of incidents where a subset of non-burst tenants experienced elevated p95/p99 latency when a burst pool approached saturation (ref: SUP-28455 + internal beta notes). The existing global circuit breaker (pr-23919) protects the fleet when *burst pool* safety caps are exceeded, but it does not directly gate on the user-facing SLO impact we care about most: non-burst latency. This PR adds an SLO-based gate that automatically reduces or disables burst when neighbor (non-burst) latency regresses beyond configured thresholds for a sustained window. The gate is intentionally conservative and rollback-safe, with explicit hysteresis and auditability. Summary of changes: (1) Introduce BurstSloGate evaluator that consumes per-region/hardware SLO signals (non-burst p95/p99 latency + baseline) and emits a gating decision: ALLOW, REDUCE(max_burst_ratio=N), or DISABLE. (2) Wire gating decision into the burst admission controller so burst tokens/permits are capped or denied when gate is active; denial reasons are surfaced as `SLO_GATED` with details in debug endpoint. (3) Add configuration in policy engine for thresholds/windows/hysteresis (defaults are global; can be overridden by region/hardware allowlist for rollout). (4) Emit new metrics and annotate alerts so on-call can quickly see when/why the gate tripped and whether it is the dominant source of denials. Behavior (high level): - We compute `nonburst_tail_regression` as (current non-burst p95 latency / rolling baseline p95 latency) and similarly for p99. Baseline is a 30m EWMA excluding current 5m window to avoid self-inflation. - Gate enters REDUCE when regression exceeds threshold for `enter_window` (default 3m). In REDUCE we clamp effective `max_burst_ratio` (e.g., from 2.0 -> 1.2) and apply a minimum cooldown before reevaluating. - Gate enters DISABLE when regression exceeds a higher threshold OR when regression persists longer than `disable_after` (default 10m). DISABLE denies new burst permits immediately, but does not tear down existing in-flight requests. - Gate exits only after regression remains below `exit_threshold` for `exit_window` (default 10m) to avoid flapping. - Gate is scoped by region + hardware class (e.g., us-east/H100), and only enabled when `burst_slo_gate_enabled` flag is true and the region/hw is allowlisted. Non-goals: - This does not attempt to detect prompt-level or tenant-specific latency issues; it is a coarse safety mechanism. - This does not replace pool saturation circuit breaker; it complements it by keying off protected SLOs. Implementation notes: - SLO signal source: we reuse the existing latency histogram series aggregated by `tenant_class=dedicated_nonburst` (introduced in pr-23822 dashboards work) and compute regression in a lightweight evaluator in the admission controller process to avoid adding a new service dependency on the hot path. - Determinism: gating decision is computed on a fixed cadence (10s) and cached; admission requests within the cadence interval see the same gate decision. We also add smoothing + min-evaluation interval to reduce jitter under telemetry lag (aligns with hotfix approach in pr-23944). - Auditability: whenever the gate transitions state we emit an audit-style event to the internal event bus (not customer audit log) and add structured log fields (`gate_state`, `gate_reason`, `gate_metrics_snapshot`). - Observability: new Prometheus metrics include `burst_slo_gate_state{region,hardware}`, `burst_slo_gate_transitions_total{from,to,reason}`, and `burst_denials_total{reason="slo_gated"}`. Testing: - Unit tests for regression computation, hysteresis, and state transitions. - Integration test for admission controller: when gate=DISABLE, burst requests are denied with reason `SLO_GATED` and deterministic retry-after semantics are preserved. - Load test sanity: validated in staging with synthetic p95 inflation to ensure the gate trips and recovers without flapping. Rollout plan: - Behind feature flag + region/hardware allowlist (initially: us-east/H100 + eu-west/L40S staging only). - Once dashboards confirm sane behavior, we can enable for internal dogfood and then beta tenants. Operational notes: - On-call can manually override by disabling the flag or adjusting thresholds in config; both are logged and appear in debug output. - Alerts: add an alert when gate is DISABLE for >5m AND non-burst regression continues to worsen (indicates deeper issue than burst gating).
Sean Gallagher (review): Can we guarantee we’re not keying off a metric that includes bursting tenants? We need this to be strictly non-burst class, otherwise we can create a feedback loop. Also, what’s the expected time-to-mitigate once non-burst p95 regresses?
Peter Holtz (author): Good call. The series used is `tenant_class=dedicated_nonburst` only; I added a guard that fails closed (DISABLE) if that label is missing/empty. Time-to-mitigate is enter_window (3m) + cadence (<=10s). For severe regressions we jump straight to DISABLE on the higher threshold.
Keiko Yamamoto (review): Please add a minimum clamp (e.g. don’t reduce below 1.0 unless DISABLE) and ensure cooldown won’t starve recovery. Also would like to see the default thresholds called out clearly.
Peter Holtz (author): Added `min_reduced_burst_ratio=1.0` invariant. Cooldown is now `min(2m, exit_window/2)` and we continue sampling during cooldown (we just don’t flip-flop states). Defaults documented in code + internal doc.
Jordan Lee (review): Determinism under telemetry lag: the evaluator running in-process could see partial scrapes. What happens if we miss a point? I’d prefer explicit stale detection and a stable cached decision, not jittering every 10s.
Peter Holtz (author): Implemented stale detection: if samples are older than 60s, gate transitions to REDUCE (not DISABLE) with reason `telemetry_stale` and keeps last good baseline. Admission path reads a cached decision updated on a ticker; it won’t change mid-request. Added tests for stale handling.
Mina Haddad (review): Routing behavior when `SLO_GATED`: should we treat it like capacity_exceeded and apply the same fallback policy? Also ensure the denial reason is surfaced to the router for logging.
Peter Holtz (author): Yes—router already treats burst denials similarly; I updated the mapping so `SLO_GATED` is categorized as non-retryable burst admission denial with existing fallback behavior (stick to baseline dedicated capacity). Also added `gate_state` to the structured denial payload consumed by routing logs/debug.
Allison Grant (review): Metric label cardinality: don’t add tenant labels. Region/hardware is fine, but please don’t add model. Also add an alert annotation that links to the overload mitigation runbook section specific to this gate.
Peter Holtz (author): Confirmed: metrics are region+hardware only, no tenant/model labels. Added alert annotations and a short internal doc section; also linked the alert to the existing burst pool overload runbook with a new subsection for SLO gate.
Sean Gallagher (final): Looks good. Please ensure we have a manual kill switch documented and that the alert doesn’t page during planned load tests.
Peter Holtz (author): Kill switch is `burst_slo_gate_enabled=false` (feature flag) and `burst_slo_gate_allowlist=[]` to hard-disable. Alert is warning by default; paging only when DISABLE > 15m and non-burst regression persists. Updated alert routing notes.
Sean Gallagher (approval): Approved.
Keiko Yamamoto (approval): Approved.
Jordan Lee (approval): Approved.
payload.title: Add SLO gate to automatically reduce/disable burst when non-burst latency regresses

Motivation: Customers in regulated geographies requested stronger guarantees that residency decisions (which KMS provider/region is chosen for a tenant) are both auditable and stable across retries, and that RBAC v2 policy decisions are traceable for compliance reviews. This PR adds a tenant residency decision auditor that records immutable decision envelopes to the audit log and introduces a lightweight telemetry shield around RBAC v2 decision paths to prevent sensitive claim material from leaking into high-cardinality metrics.

What this change does (high level):
- Implements a Residency Decision Auditor service that emits signed, immutable audit envelopes for every residency decision taken by the policy router. Envelopes contain a hashed decision payload, resolution path, and signer metadata (no plaintext PII).
- Adds a telemetry shield middleware around rbac-v2 decision engine that scrubs or buckets high-cardinality tokens before emitting telemetry. Shield rules are configurable per-tenant using the existing policy config node.
- Wire-ups to the audit-forwarder: envelopes are enqueued to the existing audit sink and annotated with origin and policy-version tags to support downstream retention/archival rules.
- Integration tests and a small migration to add policy metadata to tenant profiles.

Design notes:
- Auditing: To keep audit logs small while retaining forensics value, the envelope stores a SHA256 of the decision payload and a compact decision trace (sequence of policy checks and short identifiers). The full decision payload can be retrieved via a signed retrieval API (authorization-guarded) for legal requests.
- Signing: Envelopes are signed using the service signing key (rotated by our key manager). Signatures are verified in CI smoke tests.
- Telemetry shield: Shielding rules support three actions: redact, bucket(<n>), and hash. Default for tenant-scoped identity claims is bucket(10) for high-cardinality and redact for long strings (length > 128).
- Backwards compatibility: The residency decision evaluator keeps the existing decision output shape unchanged; the auditor runs as a side-effect and is off by default behind a feature flag and an allowlist for early pilot tenants.

Testing and rollout:
- Unit tests for evaluator, signer, and shield logic.
- Integration test exercises audit-forwarder enqueue and signature verification (test/integration/residency_audit_e2e_test.go).
- Staged rollout plan: enable feature flag in non-prod for 48 hours, opt-in 3 internal tenants, then gradually enable for customers that signed the residency contract.
- Observability: Added dashboards for audit envelope rates, shield drop counts, and verification failures.

Security & privacy considerations:
- No plaintext customer secrets or full keys are written to audit logs. All sensitive fields are hashed or redacted.
- Retrieval API requires a legal/compliance token and an internal-only service role.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation code
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Docs for operators and runbook entries
- [x] Linear tickets linked
- [x] Feature-flag gating and pilot plan

References: Linear ENG-2143 (residency auditing), SUP-785 (customer support incident describing mismatch), design doc: docs/design/residency-audit.md

Asha Patel: Measured with synthetic worst-case trace; max envelope ~1.6KB. I added a safeguard to switch to 'hash-only' mode if length > 1.9KB.
Lin Zhao: Telemetry shield looks good, but add a unit test to cover bucket boundaries (bucket(10) vs bucket(100)).
Asha Patel: Added bucket boundary tests and clarified config doc. PTAL.
Connor Hayes: Signed-off on migration approach; ensure retrieval API logs are audited as well.
Connor Hayes: Approved
Miguel Torres: Approved after envelope size check and tests

Motivation: customer integrations and internal SDKs have hit intermittent failures and duplicated fragments when simultaneously supporting Redwood native streaming and the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility path. This PR introduces a coexistence layer to reliably translate and normalize parameters and streaming frames between both paths, a stream coalescer to reduce fragment duplication and reordering, and a configurable tool fallthrough policy so function/tool calls that cannot be routed to a registered tool surface predictable structured output instead of being dropped. Changes include protocol-level canonicalization for roles/stop/logprobs, a logprob reconciliation pass to fill missing probabilities when upstream models omit them, and a structured-json-envelope canonicalizer for downstream SDKs.
Adds a compatibility coexistence layer for /v1/chat.completions clients, improves streaming stability with a stream coalescer, and introduces a tool fallthrough policy to avoid silent tool-call drops. No breaking changes for existing Redwood API users; OpenAI-compat clients may observe more stable streaming and clearer function-call envelopes.

- [x] Implement stream coalescer and heartbeat suppressor to reduce spurious short fragments -- runtime/stream/coalescer.rs
- [x] Add tool fallthrough policy and default of 'structured-fallback' for v1 clients -- runtime/tooling/fallthrough.go

Motivation: Reservation fragmentation from many small tenant commitments results in underutilized GPU slots and higher unit costs for Dedicated. This PR introduces a compact reservation coalescer that opportunistically merges adjacent low-utilization reservations into compact buckets without violating per-tenant throughput guarantees and a jitter-tolerant burst controller that smooths microbursts to reduce transient allocation churn.

Summary of changes: Add a new controller (ReservationCoalescer) that periodically scans per-pool reservation timelines, identifies candidates for safe coalescing using a time-windowed overlap heuristic and a safety headroom check, and performs transactional merge operations with undoable checkpoints. Introduce BurstHedger which applies randomized holdback windows and proportional token dampening to spread microbursts slightly in time to avoid synchronized allocation spikes. Add telemetry (HDR sketches for occupancy_histogram, counters for coalesce_ops, hedger_backpressure_events, and per-tenant headroom_reserve_bytes). Add canary rollout config and an operator flag to enable conservative mode.

Checklist: - [x] reservation reconciliation loop and coalescer reconciler - [x] safe merge transaction with rollback path - [x] jitter-tolerant burst hedger implementation - [x] metrics and tracing spans - [x] unit tests for merge/rollback and hedger token logic - [x] e2e scenario and load runner job - [x] docs: ops runbook and configuration guide

Backward compatibility & safety: Coalescer is behind a feature flag and defaults to disabled for existing clusters. Merge transactions are guarded by a conservative safety check: min-utilization threshold, per-tenant throughput budget checks, and a 5-minute observation window before any irreversible changes in non-conservative mode. BurstHedger is opt-in per-pool and exposes tuning knobs for holdback_ms and randomized_jitter_pct.

Why different from prior autoscaler work: This PR focuses on reducing fragmentation at the reservation layer (not autoscaling thresholds) and on microburst smoothing at the request admission layer rather than large-scale rebalance — the net effect is fewer short-lived allocations and lower scheduler thrash under bursty multi-tenant patterns.

How to test: unit tests simulate race between create/delete and coalescer to assert no lost reservations; e2e uses a synthetic mix of 1000 small reservations across 50 pools with bursts to validate correctness and measure cost impact.

Maya Chen: This looks promising, the merge transaction shape is the key risk. Please add more comments on the undo path and an instrumentation span for the merge critical section.

Arjun Patel: Added explicit 'merge-undo' span and comments in the reconciler; clarified txn boundaries and persisted checkpoint structure in the runbook.

Lena Gomez: How does this interact with WarmPool prewarming and existing reservation drift reconciler? Could we end up double-moving the same reservation?

Arjun Patel: Coalescer annotates reservations with a coalesce_lock annotation to hand off ownership; reconciler checks warmpool controller's annotation presence and abstains when warmpool prewarm is active. Added integration test simulating warmpool/no-warmpool modes.

Carlos Ruiz: CI flake: TestReservationMergeRace failed on first run (race on reservation index map). After initial fixes the test still flaked under heavy concurrency; added a lock around index updates and re-ran CI which passed. Recommend a short post-merge soak for two clusters.

Maya Chen: Approve after CI green and a short soak plan in release notes.

Arjun Patel: Addressed comments and added soak plan in release_notes. CI rerun green.

Merge: squash-merge performed by release-bot.
Enableable feature: reservation coalescer and burst hedger. When enabled the platform may reduce total reserved GPU footprint by coalescing small low-util reservations; conservative defaults are safe. Operators must monitor reservation_coalescer.coalesce_ops and hedger_backpressure_events. Soak plan: enable in 5% of pools for 24h, then 25% for 48h, then full rollout.
Observed perf: synthetic load showed ~6.5% reduction in reserved GPU-hours at steady-state and a 7% decrease in scheduling churn. Median generation latency impact <2ms, p95 unchanged, p99 reduced by ~40ms in noisy microburst scenarios.
Unit tests added for merge semantics and rollback. E2E scenario simulates 1k small reservations across 50 pools with synthetic bursts; loadrunner script included under tests/e2e. Bench harness run on staging cluster 'dedicated-stg-3' for 6h. CI initially failed on TestReservationMergeRace due to race; fixed by serializing index updates. All CI checks passed on second run.
Staging run (dedicated-stg-3) with mixed-tenancy workload: reserved GPU-hours down 6.5% over 6h window, avg scheduler rebinds per-minute down 12%, tail scheduling latency (p99) decreased 40ms during burst windows. Cost projection: estimated 4.8% monthly infra cost saving for clusters with >=25% small reservations.
Operator knobs: --enable-reservation-coalescer, --coalesce-min-util=0.12, --coalesce-window=5m, per-pool hedger config under charts. Follow runbook in docs/ops/reservation-coalescer-runbook.md before enabling in production.

Motivation: tenants frequently land on conservative batching/caching defaults that underutilize available KV-cache or over-quantize models to save cost, producing avoidable latency or quality regressions. We need an automated, tenant-aware generator that combines short traffic fingerprints, unit-economics targets, and model compatibility to produce pragmatic defaults: batch shapes, prefill hints, cache TTLs, and a ranked set of quantization profiles.

What this PR does: introduces the Dynamic Econ Configurator service and a small CLI to dry-run tenant-level defaults. The configurator ingests a short traffic fingerprint (percentiles for request size, seq lengths, warm/cold start ratio), a tenant SLO/cost target, and model metadata, then emits a candidate defaults bundle and confidence score. It also wires in telemetry and a dry-run flow integrated into the onboarding pipeline.

High-level design: the service contains three components: (1) fingerprint collector (lightweight sampling hook in runtime/prefill) that produces anonymized histograms, (2) decision core that maps fingerprints to templates using a compact rule-set + simple regression to estimate per-token cost and tail latency, (3) profile composer that emits batching, cache, and quantization presets as a single bundle. The decision core prefers smallest-risk changes first (cache TTL and prefill thresholds) and only suggests quantization when unit-econ delta exceeds threshold and quality risk score is low.

Checklist (what I changed):
- [x] new service: services/econ-configurator with HTTP API and proto definitions
- [x] fingerprint collector hook in runtime/prefill (sampling + anonymization)
- [x] CLI: ./bin/econctl dry-run --tenant <id> --fingerprint <path>
- [x] telemetry: metrics for suggestions, confidence, and estimated unit-econ impact
- [x] unit and integration tests (decision core offline tests + end-to-end dry-run)
- [x] docs: docs/guide/econ-configurator.md with usage and safety notes

Backward compatibility & safety: output is opt-in; runtime treats emitted bundles as suggestions unless applied via the Console or the econctl apply command. All suggestions include a safe rollback plan and an automatic A/B canary policy when applied. No runtime behavior is changed by default.

How we tested: unit tests cover the rule-set edgecases; an end-to-end dry-run was executed on a synthetic tenant trace (see tests/fixtures/synthetic-tenant-1.json) and compared against baseline defaults. Perf-smoke runs showed median latency within 1% and cost estimate improvement ~14% in the synthetic run. Integration tests ran in CI and passed after one flake rerun.

Next steps: hook configurator into onboarding pipeline to suggest initial defaults and expose an opt-in batch for gradual rollout (ENG-3499). Longer-term: replace the regression estimator with a lightweight trained model once we have 10k tenant fingerprints.
Asha Patel: Can we ensure fingerprint sampling has bounded CPU and does not allocate per-request? Suggested using a sync.Pool and probabilistic counters. | Reply Maya: switched to reservoir sampling with sync.Pool in runtime/prefill; added microbench in tests.
Diego Martinez: Decision core looks good but we should surface estimated quality risk when suggesting quant profiles. | Reply Maya: added quality_risk field and a conservative quant threshold; updated docs and tests.
Samir Rao: Add an integration test that runs the dry-run end-to-end and asserts the bundle format. | Reply Maya: added tests/e2e/dryrun_test.go and included the synthetic fixture.
Asha Patel: please add a small note in the docs about tenant opt-in and rollback defaults. | Reply Maya: docs updated; added 'safe-rollback' section.
- New: Dynamic Econ Configurator service to generate tenant-level batching/caching/quantization suggestions (opt-in)
- New: econctl dry-run to preview suggested bundles
- Metrics: econ.suggestions.count, econ.suggestion.confidence, econ.estimated.unit_econ_delta
- Safety: suggestions are non-destructive by default and include rollback plans

Summary: This change introduces two coordinated runtime features targeted at Mistral MQA/GQA quirks: (1) a heterogeneous kernel fusion policy that lets the dispatcher choose fused kernels by head-group shape and stride characteristics, and (2) a shadow-KV prefetch manager that speculatively materializes small KV windows for likely-needed slabs on multi-query workloads. Motivation: Mistral MQA workloads show head-wise asymmetry and frequent small-span KV access patterns that lead to suboptimal kernel selection and repeated memory fetches. On certain sequence-length distributions we observed 10-20% higher p95 latency compared to fused-kernel paths used for dense heads. Design: Hetero fusion: a lightweight policy module analyzes runtime head stride and per-request shape metadata to select a fused-kernel variant or fall back to baseline kernels. Fusion decisions are cached per-model-version for the session and invalidated on rollout. Shadow-KV prefetch: the manager maintains a per-request shadow KV buffer (bounded, preallocated slab) that prefetches likely next-window keys based on last N-step head access history. Prefetch heuristics include head-affinity scoring, recent-token locality, and explicit model hints delivered via model metadata. Safety and fallback: both features have runtime config flags and a safe-mode that disables fusion/prefetch for models marked with known quirk tags. The dispatcher falls back to standard kernel paths if fusion fails or if contention rises. Observability: new metrics (fusion_path_hit, shadow_kv_prefetch_hits, prefetch_evictions, fusion_decisions_by_model) and traces for prefetch latency were added. Performance: microbenchmarks on our MQA synthetic harness show median p50 improvements of 8% and p95 gains up to 14% on Mistral 7B MQA with bursty short bursts (seq<=64). For mixed consumer workloads the continuous-batching throughput improved 7% and per-token CPU/GPU utilization smoothing reduced tail jitter. Cost impact: preliminary infra runs indicate a 6-10% effective token cost reduction for high-mqa traffic after feature rollouts. Testing: added unit tests for fusion policy decision logic and shadow-KV eviction semantics; added an end-to-end microbench that exercises continuous batching interaction. CI flakiness: one flaky test in scheduler was fixed by stricter order guarantees and a small sleep removed from the test harness. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime feature flag hetero_fusion_v1 and shadow_kv_prefetch_v1. Canary rollout plan: enable for 5% of traffic on dedicated pools first, monitor metrics for increased memory pressure, fusion_path_hit ratio, and end-to-end latency regressions. If regressions exceed thresholds (p95 latency +10% or memory pressure +15%) automatically disable. Related work: follows ENG-8342 (kernel dispatch refactor) and ENG-8397 (mqa evaluation harness).
