Motivation: we continue to see sporadic long-tail bursts where a small subset of invocations generate sudden token spikes that materially increase per-tenant unit cost and SLO burn. Existing static alert thresholds cause either noisy paging or missed incidents during workload drift. This PR introduces a lightweight token-burst fingerprint and an adaptive alert threshold pipeline that reduces false positives while still surfacing high-impact bursts. Changes: 1) token_burst_detector: new streaming detector that computes a compact fingerprint for bursty invocations using an epochal sliding histogram and decaying reservoir aggregation; the fingerprint is a short static key useful for grouping repeated burst patterns. 2) adaptive_thresholds: a controller that computes per-route and per-tenant z-score thresholds on rolling windows (configurable: 1h/6h/24h) and exposes candidate alert thresholds to the alerting service via a feature-flagged endpoint. 3) dashboards: new Grafana dashboard (Token Burst Explorer) with burst fingerprint heatmap, per-route epochal histograms, and an automated remediation suggestion panel. 4) alerts: a new alert rule bundle that can operate in 'suggest' or 'enforce' mode; initially rolled out in suggest mode to gather telemetry. 5) small SDK enrichment: attach burst_fingerprint to traces/logs as attribute "burst.fingerprint" and to metric labels for correlation. Backwards compatibility: detectors are opt-in per-tenant via the telemetry feature flag. Rollout plan: canary 5% of traffic in staging -> suggest-mode in prod for 24h -> adapt thresholds based on observed false positive reduction -> enforce mode for tenants that opt-in. Notes on cost and performance: detector runs as a sidecar on telemetry ingest nodes; it processes derived token counts and does not alter the serving runtime or KV cache hot path. Tests: unit tests for histogram synthesis and fingerprint collision properties; end-to-end smoke that validates dashboard panels; a perf microbenchmark validates <1% CPU overhead on typical ingest nodes. See commits and files changed for details.
Adds token-burst detection metric and dashboard; introduces adaptive alert thresholds for long-tail cost/latency surges. Backwards-compatible. Requires alert rule update in prod after rollout.
Unit tests cover histogram synthesis, collision rate for fingerprinting (<1/1e6 on synthetic workloads), and threshold controller convergence. Benchmarks show <1% CPU on telemetry ingest in a 10k req/s synthetic replay. Recommend staging canary for 48h before full rollout.
Feature flag: telemetry.token_burst.enabled (default: false). Alert rule supports 'mode: suggest|enforce'. When switching to enforce, update alert routing to include cost-on-call for first 7 days. Ops runbook path: ops/runbooks/observability.md#token-burst-fingerprint
1) Enable telemetry.token_burst.enabled=true for staging canary tenants. 2) Deploy alert bundle in suggest mode. 3) Monitor Token Burst Explorer dashboard for 24-48h. 4) Flip specific tenant alerts to enforce via ops runbook.

payload.body:
Summary: Implements the first pass of the Top cost drivers + What changed? backend for In-console usage insights. Adds heuristic scoring for common cost deltas (token out growth, cache hit-rate drop, retries/fallbacks, model mix shifts, longer contexts, streaming overhead) and returns explainability strings suitable for direct rendering in the Console. Includes a fixture-based test suite for delta scenarios and guardrails to avoid misleading output.

Context: This is the service-side component for ENG-3819 (Top cost drivers service) and unblocks the console cards/table work in the beta. We intentionally keep the output explainable and non-causal (“likely drivers”) and include confidence/coverage checks. Reconciliation vs billing totals is handled elsewhere (ENG-3817), but this change ensures we only explain changes when the underlying aggregated totals are within tolerance.

API shape (response excerpt): Adds `drivers[]` to the existing breakdown delta response used by the insights console. Each driver contains: `driver_code`, `title`, `summary`, `details`, `estimated_impact_usd`, `estimated_impact_pct`, `direction` (increase|decrease), and `confidence` (low|medium|high). Copy strings are generated server-side so that UX doesn’t have to re-implement heuristics-specific wording.

Heuristics implemented (v1): 1) TOKENS_OUT_DELTA: Detects week-over-week increase in output tokens as a primary spend driver; provides a context-length distribution note when p90 context increases in the same window. 2) CACHE_HIT_RATE_DROP: Attributes increased spend to lower cache effectiveness (prefix/KV cache miss). Includes the miss delta and a reminder that cache effectiveness is sensitive to prompt variation and routing changes. 3) RETRIES_INCREASE: Uses metering retry_count and request_count deltas to flag increased retries; suppresses if retry attribution coverage < 95% for the selected route/model. 4) FALLBACK_RATE_INCREASE: Flags increased fallback usage (e.g., model variant fallback due to capacity) and estimates impact by comparing effective blended unit price across the two windows. 5) MODEL_MIX_SHIFT: For a route rollup, highlights when traffic shifted toward higher unit-cost models (family/version bucketing aware). 6) STREAMING_OVERHEAD: When streaming is enabled and average chunk count per request increases, flags potential overhead (extra tokens and/or compute) with a caveat that it may be intentional for UX latency. 7) LATENCY_CORRELATED_SPEND: When p95 latency grows alongside spend for the same tokens, flags likely compute inefficiency (e.g., longer decode, lower batching) and points to Optimize levers; this is confidence=low unless the correlation exceeds the threshold and request volume is sufficient.

Guardrails / correctness constraints: - Only emit drivers when baseline volumes meet minimum thresholds (default: >= 500 requests OR >= $50 spend in the comparison window) to reduce noise. - Suppress drivers when attribution coverage is low for required fields (route_tag/model_bucket/cache fields). - Suppress driver ranking when reconciliation drift (aggregated totals vs billing hook totals) exceeds the configured tolerance for the workspace/time range; return a single driver: DATA_INCOMPLETE with a friendly message and action (“Try a shorter range” / “Data is still processing”). - All “impact” estimates are bounded to the observed total delta and we clamp negative impacts to 0 for increase-only drivers.

Explainability copy: Copy is centralized in `TopDriversCopy.ts` (server) with simple templating and localized number formatting. Titles are short and stable (used as keys for future i18n). The `details` field is written to be finance-friendly (explicitly states the metric deltas) and includes a non-causal disclaimer where appropriate.

Tests: Adds fixture-driven tests under `packages/usage-insights/top-drivers/__fixtures__/` representing common real-world deltas: - token_out_spike_simple.json - cache_hit_drop_with_stable_tokens_in.json - model_mix_shift_aliases.json (regression coverage for model alias bucketing) - retries_increase_partial_coverage.json (ensures suppression) - fallback_increase_blended_price.json - latency_correlation_low_confidence.json - data_incomplete_reconciliation_drift.json (matches SUP-24811 patterns) Each fixture includes input aggregates for window A/B and expected sorted drivers with impact/clamped values and exact copy strings (with stable formatting).

Implementation notes: - Driver computation is pure and deterministic; we pass in pre-aggregated metrics for a route/model (or route rollup) and a comparison spec. - Ranking is by estimated_impact_usd (primary) then confidence then code tie-breaker for stability. - Added a small `formatDelta()` helper to keep copy consistent across drivers.

Files / modules touched (high-level): - services/usage-insights/src/topDrivers/computeDrivers.ts - services/usage-insights/src/topDrivers/driverCodes.ts - services/usage-insights/src/topDrivers/copy/TopDriversCopy.ts - services/usage-insights/src/topDrivers/thresholds.ts - services/usage-insights/src/routes/v1/usageInsightsDeltas.ts (wire drivers into response) - services/usage-insights/test/topDrivers/*.test.ts - services/usage-insights/test/topDrivers/__fixtures__/*.json

Rollout: Feature-gated by `usage_insights_top_drivers` (server-side). Console will ignore the field if absent; safe to merge ahead of UI. This PR does not change storage/aggregation schema.

Follow-ups: - Tune thresholds with beta feedback (especially for low-volume workspaces). - Consider splitting streaming overhead into token vs request overhead once we have consistent chunk telemetry across regions. - Add docs links in `details` once the docs URL is finalized by DevEx.

Screenshots: N/A (backend only).

Changelog / release notes: Internal-only beta capability; no public changelog entry yet.
Logan Wright (review): The pure function approach is good. Two questions: (1) can we guarantee driver ordering stability when impacts are near-equal due to rounding? (2) can we avoid emitting MODEL_MIX_SHIFT for route+model views (it’s only meaningful for route rollups).

Nadia Rahman (author): (1) Added secondary sort keys (confidence then driver_code) and we rank on unrounded impact_usd internally. (2) Agreed; I gated MODEL_MIX_SHIFT to only run when the query scope is route_rollup.

Chloe Martin (review): Copy: the “cache miss” wording is a bit accusatory. Can we make it clearer that it may be expected if prompts vary? Also, we should include the cache hit-rate before/after in the details.

Nadia Rahman (author): Updated CACHE_HIT_RATE_DROP details to include “Hit rate: 62% → 41%” and added a note about prompt variability + routing changes. Also softened the title from “Cache misses increased” to “Cache hit rate dropped”.

Allison Grant (review): Please add a guardrail so we don’t report latency-correlated spend unless we have enough samples. Also, can you add metrics coverage checks for retries/fallbacks? We’ve seen partial coverage in streaming endpoints in one region.

Nadia Rahman (author): Added min sample size for LATENCY_CORRELATED_SPEND (default 1k requests) and coverage gating for retry_count/fallback_count presence. Added fixture `retries_increase_partial_coverage.json` to ensure suppression.

Markus Klein (review): From customer calls, people will ask “is this causal?”. Suggest including an explicit disclaimer in the driver details and a link to docs later.

Nadia Rahman (author): Added a standard disclaimer line for low/medium confidence drivers (“This is a correlation based on observed telemetry; validate in your app logs.”). I left a TODO hook for docs URLs to be injected when available.

Chloe Martin (review): One more thing: impacts should never exceed the observed total delta for the scope; otherwise it reads wrong.

Nadia Rahman (author): Implemented clamping so sum of driver impacts is bounded by total_delta_usd and individual impacts cannot exceed delta_usd.

Allison Grant (approval): Looks good with guardrails + fixtures.

Logan Wright (approval): Approved; thanks for adding deterministic ordering.

Merge: Squash merged by Nadia Rahman after green CI.

payload.body:
Motivation: Large multi-tenant deployments showed non-linear token cost increases when a small set of noisy tenants drove batching and cache pressure. This PR introduces a tenant-aware sample-rate limiter (a lightweight per-tenant leaky bucket + sampling controller) plus a complementary quant-basis optimizer that selects compact quant profiles based on observed sample distributions. Goals: reduce cross-tenant tail cost, limit expensive mini-bursts that break batching efficiency, and provide safe quantization defaults per-tenant without manual tuning.

What this changes (summary): Implements a tenant-weighted sampling controller that throttles sampling rate per tenant when their burstiness meaningfully reduces global batch fill probability. Adds a runtime hook to compute short-window sample statistics and feed a heuristic that picks a quantization "basis" (int8/ptq/awq-inspired profiles) tuned to the tenant's response-length distribution and generation temperature. Introduces a cost-simlation utility used by the console to surface estimated per-tenant unit economics for proposed profiles.

Design highlights: - Sampling controller lives in runtimes/scheduler and operates at request admission time; it emits metrics (tenant.sample_rate, tenant.throttle_events) and respects per-tenant SLA hints. - Quant-basis optimizer evaluates 3 lightweight profile candidates online using cached microbenchmarks and a conservative quality delta estimate; it never upgrades to a more aggressive profile without an offline eval approval. - Fallback safety: if latency or quality regressions are observed, the system reverts the tenant to the last safe profile and marks the candidate as disqualified for 24h.

Testing and rollout plan: unit + integration tests added; canary rollout to a small set of non-critical tenants for 72h with metric gates (99th p90 latency, token cost delta < 8%). Console exposes an opt-in suggestion card for tenant owners to accept or reject quant profile changes.

Rollback: switch off feature flag, drain scheduler caches, and revert tenant sample rates to per-tenant defaults.

Notes: This PR focuses on runtime heuristics and conservative defaults; a follow-up will add an A/B evaluation harness that ties application-level quality signals (from evals) into the quant acceptance decision.

payload.body:
Introduce telemetry-driven soft-eviction dampener and sticky-circuit repair to reduce circuit flapping during transient KV pressure events; no API changes.
Motivation: During a transient KV pressure incident in region-eu we observed rapid circuit opens/closes for a cohort of tenants leading to amplified failover churn and degraded tail latency for hosted customers. This PR introduces a telemetry-led 'circuit rescuer' that reduces oscillation by smoothing backpressure signals, applying a soft-eviction dampener, and performing a controlled sticky-circuit repair based on recent success windows.

Summary of changes: This is a small cross-cutting hotfix across runtime, control plane, and telemetry pipelines that implements four coordinated pieces: 1) Backpressure Signal Normalizer: applies a windowed median filter to upstream node health signals and removes short spikes from driving immediate circuit state transitions. 2) Soft-Eviction Dampener: when eviction pressure is detected, we transition tenants through a staged 'soft-evict' state (reduced priority, token-bucket throttle) instead of an immediate hard eviction; this reduces client-visible failures and gives KV pressure a chance to recover. 3) Sticky-Circuit Repair: a repair controller that will attempt a single guarded reconnect (hedged probe) after a small cooldown when metrics indicate recovered success probability; the controller records a sliding success score to avoid repeated flips. 4) Telemetry anchors and audits: emit circuit_rescue.* metrics and structured audit events so owners can see damping windows and automated repairs in the Console.

Implementation details: - runtime/connection_manager: add BackpressureNormalizer and SoftEviction state machine (soft_evict -> probation -> restored) with a small state-machine test harness. - controlplane/repair_controller: implement StickyRepair reconciler that uses recent_operation_success_rate and inflight_kv_latency_percentile as inputs. - telemetry/metrics: add circuit_rescue.events, circuit_rescue.success_score, backpressure.normalized and two dashboards (Console dashboard ids referenced below). - cfg: default tuning opts are conservative (soft window=10s median, probation=30s, single-repair-probe) and feature-flagged under feature.flags.circuit_rescue to allow incremental rollout.

Testing and validation: - unit tests for normalizer and state machine added. - integration harness run in perf-canary with KV pressure simulation for 2h; observed circuit flip rate reduced by ~78% and tail latency improvement of 12th-99th percentile. - telemetry dashboards were validated end-to-end and alert thresholds adjusted in SLO enforcer runbook.

Rollback and rollout plan: - feature-flagged by default off in main. On merge we will enable in canary region (us-west-2) at 1% traffic for 24h, monitor circuit_rescue.success_score and slo.tail_latency; if stable, incrementally roll to 25% then 100% over 48–72h. Rollback: flip feature flag off and drain in-flight repair attempts; no schema or API changes.

Checklist: - [x] Design reviewed (ENG-1623) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Canary integration - [x] Telemetry dashboards added - [x] Rollout plan documented

Related incidents/work items: SUP-421 (incident follow-up), ENG-1623 (design doc). Console dashboards: Console-DB:circuits/telemetry/CR-41, Console-DB:eviction/soft-evict-views.

Notes to reviewers: Focus on the state machine boundary between SoftEvict and probation; ensure the repair probe is strictly rate-limited to avoid thundering-herd reconnections. Also validate the metric label conventions to guarantee downstream aggregator compatibility.
Ethan Zhou (reviewer): Could the median window be too slow for very short spikes? Consider a smaller percentile option.
Maya Patel (author): Answered: We intentionally pick 10s for the median to avoid flip loops; added config knob backpressure.normalizer.window_ms and doc note explaining tradeoffs.
Priya Nair (reviewer): Please add a safety check to avoid issuing repair probes if inflight > X to prevent overload.
Maya Patel (author): Added inflight cap in RepairController and unit tests to assert probe-rate is bounded.
Luca Romano (approver): Verified dashboards and integration run. Approving for squash-and-merge.

payload.body:
Context and motivation:
We see recurring high cost and storage growth from high-fidelity logging during bursty or anomalous traffic. Existing sampling policies are static and do not reliably surface the small fraction of invocations that drive most token-level cost and tail latency. This PR adds a lightweight invocation-clock metric stream that breaks down per-invocation time into phases (enqueue, scheduling, KV lookup, kernel run, token_emit). Those phase timings are used by a new adaptive log-fidelity controller to raise fidelity for suspicious invocations (high kernel time, high token-cost, or unusual phase skew) and to reduce fidelity on stable, low-cost traffic, reducing overall log volume while improving signal-to-noise for incident investigations.

Summary of changes (single-line commits high-level):
- add services/invoke/clock_metrics.go: record phase timestamps, emit compact phase histogram and per-invocation cost tags
- add controllers/log_fidelity/controller.go: adaptive policy engine + tenant policy store + safety throttle
- add observability/dashboards/token_clock_cost_panel.json: dashboard panels for phase-level tail and cost attribution
- add observability/alerts/phase-slow-alerts.yaml: new alert rules (SLO-calibrated) for per-phase tail regressions
- add docs/observability/log-fidelity.md: operator guide and tuning knobs
- unit tests for controller policy logic and load tests for safety throttle
- small SDK change: redwood-sdk-python -> expose phase metadata in responses for opt-in debugging

Files changed (high level):
- services/invoke/clock_metrics.go (core instrumenting, ~250 LOC): emits compact proto with phase micros, token counts, model size & quant flags
- controllers/log_fidelity/controller.go (policy engine, ~420 LOC): supports rules: threshold, percentile-based triggers, running-window decay, cost-budget gating
- controllers/log_fidelity/policy_store.go: pluggable tenant policy store (in-memory + redis backend hooks)
- observability/dashboards/token_clock_cost_panel.json: new panels (phase waterfall, cost contribution table, phase skew heatmap)
- observability/alerts/phase-slow-alerts.yaml: alerts for 95/99 phase latency increases and for safety throttle activation
- docs/observability/log-fidelity.md: instructions, recommended policies, and rollback guidance
- sdk/python/redwood/response_meta.py: attach opt-in _phase_clock metadata to responses
- tests/controller_policy_test.go, tests/invoke_clock_integration_test.go: unit/e2e tests

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Clock encoding: we emit a compact int32 microsecond vector per-phase with a shared invocation id. This keeps payloads small and allows downstream rollups.
- Controller is conservative by default: default policy increases fidelity only after a 3-sample sustained signal or single high-cost invocation marked by kernel>500ms and cost>5 tokens-equivalent.
- Safety throttle: controller includes a global circuit-breaker: if log-ingest rate > 1.5x baseline for a tenant or total qps spike causes >20% CPU on the log pipeline, controller enters temporary backoff and switches to header-only sampling. This avoids cascading cost spikes.

Review conversation (high level, preserved chronology):
- Alex Nguyen (review): "Nice instrumentation. Two asks: 1) can we avoid adding a hot path allocation in services/invoke for the common fast-path? 2) policy_store needs a TTL eviction test."
- Maya (author): "Addressed: pool-allocated proto buffer and moved TTL eviction test into policy_store_test.go. PTAL."
- Priya Rao (review): "Controller logic looks solid. Suggest adding an explicit metric for 'fidelity_switch_count' so we can track controller churn."
- Maya: "Added fidelity_switch_count and documented expected bounds in docs. Also added an integration test to assert the throttle flips no more than once per 10s in the synthetic traffic scenario."
- Liam O'Connor (SRE): "Alert tuning: 95->99 thresholds look noisy in canary; reduced sensitivity and added a rolling baseline compare (last 30m vs prior 6h). Also requested a dashboard panel showing budget burn rate."
- Maya: "Adjusted alerts and added budget burn-rate panel. CI flake: tests/invoke_clock_integration_test.go failed intermittently due to timing in CI; added deterministic clock stub in tests to stabilize."
- Approvals: Alex, Priya, Liam approved after fixes.

CI and rollout details:
- CI: build, unit tests, integration tests (invocation simulation), linters. Initial CI run: one flaky integration failure; rerun green. Final CI status: pass.
- Canary rollout: controller rolled out to canary cluster for 48h with tenant opt-in flag enabled. Observed 34% reduction in high-fidelity log volume for non-anomalous tenants and zero safety-throttle incidents. Two tenants opted into higher fidelity and provided immediate SRE-relevant traces that tracked down an upstream kernel contention bug.

Operational runbook and rollback:
- docs/observability/log-fidelity.md contains runbook: how to disable controller (feature flag), how to adjust per-tenant policy, how to read fidelity_switch_count and throttle events.
- Rollback action: disable feature flag and flush in-memory policy cache; policy_store persisted configs are unaffected.

Why this is different from existing work:
- We instrument per-invocation phase timings (clock) rather than coarse per-stage histograms, enabling precise attribution of token cost to specific runtime phases and better targeting of log fidelity increases where they matter. The adaptive controller ties telemetry to operational cost, not just latency alone.

Testing and benchmarks:
- Unit coverage: controller policy branching ~85% coverage.
- Load bench: synthetic 10k rps mix, observed controller CPU overhead <2% on control plane and log-ingest reduction of 28-40% depending on policy aggressiveness.

Merge outcome:
- PR merged via squash on 2026-02-18 after approvals and green CI. A follow-up PR will add an RBAC entry for tenant policy editing UI in the console (tracked ENG-410).

Notes for follow-ups:
- Expose phase-level histograms to the metrics-aggregation tier for low-cost rollups (ENG-401).
- Investigate ML-based anomaly policy to replace heuristic thresholds (ENG-402).
Introduces invocation-phase timing metrics (enqueue/schedule/kv/kernel/emit), an adaptive log-fidelity controller that dynamically adjusts log sampling per-tenant based on cost and tail latency signals, new dashboard panels for token-clock cost attribution, and a safety throttle to prevent logging ingestion storms.

payload.body:
Context: We observed noisy long-tail alerting and poor signal in SLO investigations where traces lacked stable invocation context (caller annotations, client SDK version, and prompt-shape bucket). This PR introduces an invocation context enricher in the telemetry pipeline, a compact cost-drift dashboard panel for fast triage, and an alert decorrelator to reduce duplicate notifications from correlated token-cost spikes. The description below summarizes motivation, what changed, CI notes, and rollout plan. Motivation: SRE and platform engineers spend too long correlating traces with billing spikes; many incidents are repeated across downstream callers with identical upstream characteristics. The enricher creates a compact, stable context fingerprint (invocation_family) using hashed callsite, sdk metadata, model variant tag, and prompt-shape bucket. It is sampled and attached to spans and metrics as a low-cardinality tag to enable rollups without exploding cardinality. What changed: 1) pkg/observability/enricher/context_enricher.go: new pipeline stage that hydrates a sampled context bundle and attaches invocation_family, prompt_shape, sdk_version, and client_region on sampled spans and on a low-volume metrics stream. 2) internal/telemetry/transformers/token_cost_labeler.go: minor changes to include invocation_family for cost rollups and to emit compact cost drift markers. 3) dashboards/compact_cost_drift_panel.json: new Grafana panel that shows per-invocation_family cost drift sparkline and a compact histogram for last-24h to speed triage. 4) alerting/decorrelator/config.yaml: new adaptive decorrelator configs that group alerts by invocation_family and suppress duplicates when overlap > 80% and within 15 minutes. 5) webapp/src/components/CostDriftChart.tsx: UI for the sparkline and on-hover attribution. 6) tests/integration/test_context_enricher.py + unit tests. High-level commits: "init: add invocation context enricher and basic sampler"; "feat: emit invocation_family on metrics and spans"; "ui: add compact cost drift panel and hover attribution"; "feat: alerting: adaptive decorrelator config and implementation"; "test: add unit and integration tests"; "chore: CI fixes and lints". Files changed (high level): context enricher code, metric labeler changes, alert decorrelator config and small engine change, new dashboard JSON, small UI component, docs and tests. Review conversation summary: - Omar: "This looks good overall; can we keep invocation_family stable across minor SDK bumps?" Context: We observed several customer incidents where transient regional load spikes caused sticky circuit state and long-lived inflight queues for multi-tenant routes. Root cause: connection stalls + aggressive kv-drain heuristics interacting with tenant-weighted admission causing some tenants to remain dormant while others monopolized inflight reservation slots. Motivation: reduce blast radius of sticky circuits and provide a short-term prioritized reservation path for critical tenants to avoid prolonged hard quarantine during region instability. Goals: 1) Add an ephemeral 'circuit quarantine' state that temporarily isolates circuits flagged as high stall-risk and drains inflight safely; 2) Add a prioritized reservation bucket (time-limited) to allow small-quantity critical requests to bypass soft-quarantine and validate recovery; 3) Ensure telemetry and debug hooks for post-mortem (per-tenant circuit timeline + tokenized drain traces). Design summary: - Introduced a transient circuit state TRANSIENT_QUARANTINE with a short TTL (configurable, default 30s) that isolates the failing circuit from normal routing but continues to accept low-priority probes and health rechecks. - Implemented a prioritized_reservation slot allocator: shards maintain N prioritized slots per epoch (configurable by tenant tier). Requests tagged with priority:critical may acquire a reservation if available; reservations have a strict max tokens/call and are rate-limited to avoid starving background drains. - Modified admission controller to favor prioritized reservations over ordinary warmup paths while still observing global latency SLO budgets. - Added heuristics to avoid circuit stickiness: when a circuit transitions to TRANSIENT_QUARANTINE we set a soft-reopen backoff that grows exponentially per re-open attempt but imposes an upper bound to avoid permanent blackholing. - Telemetry: emit circuit_quarantine.{enter,exit,reopen_attempt} counters, per-tenant prioritized_reservation.granted/denied gauges, and structured traces that include kv-cache sizes and drain progress at transition boundaries. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged unless tenant is opted into prioritized reservations via account tier or config flag. Checklist: - [x] Spec and design doc in Linear (ENG-842) - [x] Unit tests for reservation allocator and TTL transitions - [x] Integration test: simulated regional stall scenario - [x] Telemetry included and wired to Console dashboards - [x] Feature flag gated rollout plan - [x] Docs update for SLO guidance (docs/observability/quarantine.md) Commits (summary): - Add TRANSIENT_QUARANTINE state machine and state transitions (Priya Shah) - Implement prioritized_reservation allocator with per-epoch accounting (Priya Shah) - Admission controller: prioritize reservations & enforce token caps (Ben Turner) - Telemetry: counters/gauges + trace annotations (Aisha Khan) - Tests: unit + integration + flake fixes (Miguel Ortega) Files changed (high-level): - runtime/circuit/state_machine.go (new states + transitions) - runtime/admission/prioritized_reservation.go (allocator) - runtime/admission/allocator_test.go (unit tests) - serving/probes/quarantine_probe.go (probe and health checks) - observability/metrics/registry.go (new metric defs) - console/dashboards/quarantine-overview.json (dashboard) - docs/observability/quarantine.md (documentation) - sdk/python/examples/prioritized_reservation_example.py (example usage) Testing & CI: - Local integration harness: simulated region egress stall, verified TRANSIENT_QUARANTINE TTL respected and prioritized reservations allowed 25 requests/min for smoke tenants. - Load test: 10k concurrent tenants, prioritized reservations did not increase 95th percentile latency by >1.2% for main region under test. - CI: unit and integration suites passed on first run; flakiness fix for allocator test added in second commit. Review conversation (high level): - Miguel: "Please add an additional guard to ensure reservation tokens can't be hoarded by a single connection; otherwise LGTM." - Priya: "Added per-connection cap (tokens_per_connection) and a unit test covering edge case." - Aisha: "Would like a clearer rollback path in rollout plan; add a safety kill-switch via feature-flag and an immediate metric alarm." - Priya: "Added feature-flag bypass and an alert rule tied to circuit_quarantine.enter spike rate; described in rollout section." - Ben: "Telemetry looks good; can we annotate traces with tenant tier?" - Priya: "Done, traces now include tenant_tier metadata." Approvals: - Aisha Khan: approved - Miguel Ortega: approved - Ben Turner: approved CI checks: - unit-tests: pass - integration-tests: pass - lint: pass - e2e: pass Rollout plan: - Stage 1 (canary): enable feature-flag in staging + 2 small production clusters with monitoring enabled (24h). - Stage 2 (tiered rollout): enable prioritized reservations for tier:critical customers only for 72h, monitor circuit_quarantine.enter rate and P95 latency. - Stage 3: toggle on for tier:standard with conservative slot counts and an automatic auto-off if circuit_quarantine.enter increases > 3x baseline within 1h. - Rollback: disable feature-flag (instant) and publish patch to revert state transitions if necessary. Post-merge tasks: - Add a Console runbook entry and a Linear follow-up for quota tuning (ENG-872). - Engage SRE on daily checks for first 72h. Related incidents / why-hotfix: SUP-1198 documented a production outage where several tenants experienced extended cold starts after a short regional egress throttling event. This change aims to reduce repeat incidents by avoiding sticky negative circuit state and giving critical tenants a fast-path to remain responsive. Merge: squashed and merged via merge commit (SHA: ab12cd34ef56). Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the prioritized reservation small and rate-limited to reduce potential SLO regressions; we will iterate on sizing after initial telemetry. Documentation and Console dashboard updated as part of the change.
Miguel Ortega: Please add a per-connection token cap to prevent hoarding - addressed in commit 3c4d5e6.
Aisha Khan: Add rollback/runbook details and an alert threshold tied to spike in circuit_quarantine.enter - addressed in docs and alert rules.
Ben Turner: Add tenant_tier metadata to traces for correlation - addressed in telemetry commit.
CI Bot: integration-tests flake on allocator_test, rerun passed after fix (commit 5e6f7g8).
Introduces transient circuit quarantine to reduce sticky circuit incidents and a prioritized reservation path for critical tenants. Feature is behind a flag and default limits are conservative. See docs/observability/quarantine.md for guidance.
Conservative rollout and telemetry-first approach. Follow-up task ENG-872 for tuning reservation sizes after initial telemetry.

Added aggregate per-session token rollups, a prompt-shape cohort heatmap dashboard, and updated alerts to use percentile-based tuning for token-cost excursions.
Motivation: Investigations of long-tail cost spikes showed that many high-cost invocations cluster by prompt shape and session lifetime. This PR introduces per-session token rollup aggregation, prompt-shape tagging on spans, and a Grafana cohort heatmap to make those clusters visible.

What this changes: Adds a session-aggregator that computes per-session token_count and token_cost_usd rollups at 1m and 5m windows; enriches OTEL spans with prompt_shape and token_cost_usd attributes; exposes new metrics (redwood.inference.session_token_rollup.count, redwood.inference.session_token_rollup.cost_usd, redwood.inference.prompt_shape.cardinality); introduces a cohorted heatmap panel and a summary widget for top prompt-shapes by cost. Replaces the previous static alert on average token cost with a percentile-based alert (P95 over rolling 30m 3-hour lookback) with dampening to reduce noisy flaps.

Checklist: [x] Instrument rollup producer and consumer [x] Add span enrichment in runtime path [x] Add Grafana dashboard JSON + panels [x] Add unit + small e2e telemetry smoke tests [x] Update docs and runbook entries [x] Add migration to backfill historic 7d aggregates (small job included)

Why this is safe: Aggregations are additive and non-destructive. Rollup emission runs as opt-in; default is off for new clusters until customers enable in console. Backfill job runs at low priority and has throttling. Alert thresholds are initially conservative and documented in runbook.

Related: ENG-4127 (observability backlog item), SUP-1283 (support case that triggered investigation).

Aisha Patel: Implemented hashed prompt_shape and added cardinality gauge + doc note about sampling; pushed commit 3.
Marisol Gutierrez: Can we make the backfill job throttleable via a helm value? Please add helm value and default to disabled in hosted clusters.

Operational runbook added at docs/observability/runbooks/session-rollup.md with guidance for enabling, threshold tuning, and how to troubleshoot high prompt_shape cardinality. Housekeeping: flagged deprecation of old token-cost-avg alert; it will be removed in 2 weeks after no active triggers.

payload.body:
## Context
We found a metering bug on the embeddings endpoint when customers send batched inputs (OpenAI-compatible `input: string[]` and Redwood `inputs: string[]`). The current meter path tokenizes only the first element in the batch and emits that as `input_tokens`, while the request handler still returns a single `usage` object. This causes under-counting for batched embedding calls and makes ledger vs usage-export reconciliation noisy.

This came up in the embeddings batch repro thread (eng-platform) and also overlaps with the broader meter hardening initiative (Finance/RevRec reconciliation + experiment integrity).

## What this PR changes
1) Correctness: for embeddings requests with multiple inputs, compute total input tokens as the sum of per-item token counts.
- If `input` is `string`: tokenize and count.
- If `input` is `string[]`: tokenize each string and sum.
- If `input` is `number[]` (token ids): count length.
- If `input` is `number[][]`: sum lengths.

2) Emit batch metadata in usage event
- Add `batch_size` (int) to `usage_event.dimensions`.
- Add `meter_version = embeddings_v2` so Finance can segment pre/post without relying on deploy timestamps.

3) Shadow billing compare plumbing
- When `METER_SHADOW_COMPARE=1` (staging + select prod canaries), emit both v1 and v2 computed fields into the shadow compare payload. No invoicing behavior changes in this PR; it only corrects the event values and makes the diff visible.

4) Tests
- Unit tests for metering logic over the four supported `input` shapes.
- Golden tests for mixed batches (empty string, whitespace-only, long strings truncated by request limits).
- OpenAI-compat request/response integration test verifying:
  - returned `usage.prompt_tokens` matches summed token counts
  - usage event `billed_input_tokens` matches returned usage
  - `batch_size` dimension is present

## Why this is safe
- The change is isolated to embeddings metering; no changes to model execution.
- Backwards compatible: usage event schema only adds optional dimensions; existing consumers ignore unknown keys.
- Shadow-compare mode enables Finance/Eng to validate deltas before any billing ledger changes.

## Example
Request:
- input[0] = "hello world"  (2 tokens)
- input[1] = "goodbye"      (1 token)

Before:
- usage_event.input_tokens = 2

After:
- usage_event.input_tokens = 3
- usage_event.dimensions.batch_size = 2
- usage_event.dimensions.meter_version = embeddings_v2

## Test plan
- `bazel test //services/usage_metering/...`
- `bazel test //services/openai_compat/...:embeddings_usage_test`
- Staging: run `scripts/replay_embeddings_batches.py` against `meter-shadow-compare` env and verify v1 vs v2 diff report.

## Follow-ups
- Finance: once shadow compare is clean for 7 days, we should flip invoicing to consume `meter_version=embeddings_v2` values for embeddings (separate change-control PR).
- Observability: add a panel for embeddings batch_size distribution and v1/v2 token deltas to the meter sanity dashboard.

References:
- Slack: 1770164099-embeddings-batch-metering-bug-repro
- PRs nearby: pr-27518 (shadow billing compare mode), pr-27510 (recon export)
- Project: Meter hardening + pricing experiment integrity (pre/post segmentation)
Nadia Rahman: Can you confirm we are summing tokens across the entire batch, not taking max? Also please add a meter_version dimension so Finance can segment without guessing deploy boundaries.
Cole Summers (author): Yep, now `total_input_tokens = sum(per_item_counts)` for all supported input types. Added `meter_version=embeddings_v2` to dimensions and included it in shadow compare payload.

Logan Wright: Any risk of double-tokenizing if the handler already tokenizes for truncation? We’ve been bitten by “count twice” paths.
Cole Summers (author): The handler doesn’t tokenize embeddings inputs today; it validates request size in bytes. Meter path tokenizes once, and for token-id inputs we just count lengths. Added a regression test that asserts a single tokenizer invocation per item.

Mei Lin: Please ensure the recon export won’t break (new dims). Also add a queryable `batch_size` field; useful for drift analysis.
Cole Summers (author): Schema remains key/value dims; export is tolerant. `batch_size` added as a top-level dimension so it’s available in Snowflake export and Grafana panels.

Emily Stone: For RevRec, we need to demonstrate no retroactive invoice changes. Can we keep this shadow-only for now?
Cole Summers (author): Confirmed: this PR only changes usage event values + shadow compare; billing ledger consumption remains unchanged. We’ll do a separate change-control PR once shadow diffs are reviewed and signed off.

Final: Nadia approved after requesting a small test addition for `number[][]` inputs; Logan approved after CI green; Mei approved with a note to add dashboard panel as follow-up.

Summary: This PR implements a "harmonizer" layer in the serving scheduler that time-slices GPU kernel execution between prefill and decode stages, introduces microburst quotas, and adds an opportunistic KV-cache reclaim path during decode idle windows. Motivation: In mixed workloads (large prefill bursts followed by many short decodes) we observed priority inversion and tail-latency spikes when prefill kernels monopolize compute for long slices. Existing chunked-prefill and speculative prefill approaches reduce some tail effects but either increase decode stall frequency or over-fragment work. Harmonizer goal: provide deterministic, low-latency decode windows while preserving aggregate throughput by slicing long prefill kernels into bounded time quanta and reclaiming KV-cache slots opportunistically during decode-dominated micro-windows. Key changes and rationale: 1) Kernel time-slicing: the scheduler now enforces a per-kernel timeslice (default 8ms, adaptive) for prefill kernels above a configured duration threshold. Long prefill work is split into logical continuations; the runtime kernel adapter exposes a continuation token so the GPU kernel can resume without extra host-side model reinitialization cost. This reduces blocking time for decode kernels and reduces tail latency. 2) Adaptive timeslice estimator: a lightweight moving-window estimator adjusts timeslice size based on recent decode tail P95/P99 and prefill throughput. The estimator biases toward smaller slices when decode tail is increasing and toward larger slices when decode latency is healthy. 3) Microburst quotas: decode requests are granted short-run quotas (number of tokens or microseconds) that guarantee a minimum execution window before prefill resumptions. This prevents tiny decodes from being starved. 4) Opportunistic KV reclaim: when the harmonizer detects decode idle intervals inside a timeslice boundary (e.g., waiting on network/IO), the runtime performs a soft-evict hint on cold KV entries and background-prefetch low-cost priming for imminent prefill continuations. This reduces cold-KV misses when prefill resumes. 5) Metrics & observability: new metrics harmonizer.timeslice_ms, harmonizer.prefill_splits, harmonizer.decode_quota_acquired, kvcache.soft_evictions, and harmonic.prefill_continuations were added. Tracing hooks mark harmonizer decisions so we can correlate decisions with latency outcomes. 6) API/Config: exposed config knobs in runtime config: harmonizer.enabled, harmonizer.base_timeslice_ms, harmonizer.max_splits, harmonizer.decode_quota_us. These are gated behind an opt-in feature flag for staged rollout. Performance summary (internal bench): - Mixed workload (50% large prefill 50% small decodes): p99 decode latency reduced by ~12% (from 310ms to 275ms), p95 by ~9%. - Aggregate token throughput for prefill-heavy runs decreased by ~3% worst-case; in practical settings we saw throughput flat or +2% due to reduced KV thrashing. - For steady-state decode-only workloads, no measurable regressions. Compatibility and risk: The continuation token requires small changes to the kernel entry path but keeps ABI stable; fallbacks in place for older kernels (no splitting). KV soft-evict is conservative and uses a background thread with rate limits to avoid noisy eviction. Testing and rollout: Unit and integration tests added for scheduler behavior and continuation correctness. Microbench harness extended to validate timeslice adaptation. Canary rollout plan: opt-in flag -> small fleet in europe region (low RPS) -> ramp to all hosted runs over 2 weeks while monitoring new metrics and regressions. Checklist: - [x] Scheduler time-slice implementation - [x] Kernel adapter continuation token - [x] Adaptive timeslice estimator - [x] Microburst decode quota enforcement - [x] Opportunistic KV reclaim path - [x] Metrics + tracing hooks - [x] Unit/integration tests - [x] Benchmarks and perf report - [x] Feature-flag gate and config knobs Commits: (summary) - a1bf3d4: harmonizer: core scheduler loop & timeslice enforcement - c2d9e01: kernel-adapter: continuation token & split/merge helpers - e4f7ab2: kvcache: soft-evict hint and background reclaim worker - 9b2c7d1: config: harmonizer feature flags and runtime knobs - 5d7a9ef: metrics + tracing for harmonizer decisions - 3f8bd44: tests: unit and microbench harness updates - 7ea5d2c: docs: runtime config reference and migration notes Files changed (high level): - runtime/scheduler/harmonizer.cpp (new) - runtime/scheduler/harmonizer.h (new) - runtime/kernel/adapter.cc (continuation token + resume interface) - runtime/kernel/kernel_entry.S (small glue changes for continuation fast-path) - runtime/kv/soft_reclaim.cc (new) - runtime/config/feature_flags.yaml (opt-in knobs) - runtime/metrics/harmonizer_metrics.cc - tests/harmonizer_scheduler_test.cc - benchmarks/microbench/harmonizer_mixed_workload.py - docs/runtime/harmonizer.md - docs/config/runtime_flags.md - scripts/canary_rollout.md Review summary and decisions: Reviewer Ethan Zhao: "High level: this direction looks promising. Two immediate concerns: (1) contiguity of KV eviction — we must not evict hot KV while prefill is mid-continuation; (2) timeslice tuning defaults may need to vary by GPU architecture." Author reply (Nina): "Both addressed: soft-evict respects 'do-not-evict' tags set at prefill slice boundaries and rate-limits are per-GPU; added arch-weighted default table (A100=8ms, H100=10ms, V100=6ms) and config override." Reviewer Priya Sinha: "We need signal / guardrail alerts for when harmonizer is throttling prefill heavily (throughput regression)." Author response: "Added metric harmonizer.prefill_throttle_ratio and alert playbook entries in scripts/canary_rollout.md." Reviewer Marco Valdez: "Edge case: extremely long single-token prefill ( > 300ms ) — splitting might add visible overhead due to repeated kernel launches." Author: "We added a threshold to only split kernels above 32ms and a fast-resume path that avoids host-side model re-setup; microbench shows overhead < 1% for this case." CI / checks: - unit-tests: pass - integration-tests: pass - lint: initial run flagged style in harmonizer.h -> fixed - benchmarks/regression: pass (bench harness comparisons attached) - canary-sanity: pending during initial PR, green pre-merge Performance artifacts: attached benchmark output (benchmarks/microbench/results/214450-mixed.json) and flamegraph samples (benchmarks/microbench/flamegraphs/214450-prefill-slice.svg) Merge: PR was squashed and merged by Priya Sinha after CI turned green and a 48-hour canary in eu-west. Merge method: squash. Post-merge actions: - release_notes: "Add harmonizer scheduler to reduce decode tail latency in mixed prefill/decode workloads; opt-in via harmonizer.enabled; see runtime/harmonizer.md for tuning." - Incremental rollout scheduled and post-release metric dashboards created (runtime/harmonizer-dashboard). Known limitations and follow-ups: - Follow-up ENG-7612 will add model-aware timeslice (longer slices for transformer configurations that pay high resume cost). - Experiment ENG-7688 will evaluate merging harmonizer with the speculative prefill controller for further gains. Overall notes: This PR trades bounded prefill kernel slices for improved tail decode latency and steadier decode QoS. Implementation favors conservative defaults and is gated by feature flag to allow observational rollout.
Ethan Zhao: High level: this direction looks promising. Two immediate concerns: (1) contiguity of KV eviction — we must not evict hot KV while prefill is mid-continuation; (2) timeslice tuning defaults may need to vary by GPU architecture.
Nina Park: Both addressed: soft-evict respects 'do-not-evict' tags set at prefill slice boundaries and rate-limits are per-GPU; added arch-weighted default table (A100=8ms, H100=10ms, V100=6ms) and config override.
Priya Sinha: We need signal / guardrail alerts for when harmonizer is throttling prefill heavily (throughput regression).
Nina Park: Added metric harmonizer.prefill_throttle_ratio and alert playbook entries in scripts/canary_rollout.md.
Marco Valdez: Edge case: extremely long single-token prefill ( > 300ms ) — splitting might add visible overhead due to repeated kernel launches.
Nina Park: Added threshold to only split kernels above 32ms and a fast-resume path that avoids host-side model re-setup; microbench shows overhead < 1% for this case.
CI Bot: lint: style issue in harmonizer.h (fixed in c2d9e01).
Bench Reviewer: Please add a comparison vs chunked-prefill baseline; initial bench attached shows harmonizer improves p99 decode vs chunked-prefill by ~6% for our mixed scenario.
Merged via squash by Priya Sinha after canary and CI green. Feature gated behind harmonizer.enabled; docs and playbook updated.
Add harmonizer scheduler to reduce decode tail latency in mixed prefill/decode workloads. Opt-in via runtime config harmonizer.enabled. Default timeslice tuned per GPU architecture. Follow-up work planned for model-aware timeslicing.

Summary: Adds a KMS constraint matrix that declaratively maps tenant attributes and service roles to allowed KMS providers and regions, plus an RBAC v2 condition evaluator that checks kms:allowed_regions during token/operation authorization and an audit-enforcement hook that attaches signed audit envelopes to KMS requests. Motivation: customers operating with data residency requirements need stronger enforcement at the inference platform level so KMS requests are restricted by tenant policy and auditable end-to-end. This PR provides enforcement points at policy evaluation, request routing, and auditing to prevent accidental cross-region key usage. Design: 1) constraint matrix YAML (docs/compliance/kms-region-matrix.md) representing providers, region sets, and tenant attribute predicates; 2) condition evaluator integrated into rbac/v2 to surface kms:allowed_regions as a first-class condition that short-circuits incompatible key usage; 3) request-level hook in pkg/kms/enforcer that validates target key location, records decision to the audit log and attaches a signed audit envelope containing decision metadata and policy fingerprint; 4) migration CLI (cmd/admin/kms-migrate.go) that annotates existing keys with derived region assertions and generates a one-time report for ops; 5) integration+e2e tests exercising edge cases (multi-provider fallback, tenant attribute migration, and failure modes). Backwards compatibility: new evaluator is additive and disabled for clusters without the constraint matrix; feature flag redwood.security.kms_region_matrix controls enforcement rollout. Implementation notes: uses existing KMS abstraction so provider-specific checks are plumbed through provider adapters; signature uses current audit signing key and rotates via KMS signing wrapper. Checklist: ensure policy authoring docs updated; run migration in staging; verify audit retention export; coordinate with SRE for rollout and alerting. Testing: unit tests for evaluator and hook, integration tests using sandbox KMS providers, e2e scenario with tenant migration. Risks and mitigations: false positives on legacy keys mitigated by migration tool and flag; performance impact limited by caching region assertions and validating on key resolution path only. Related: ENG-2189 for policy editor work and SEC-412 for compliance review.
Evan Carter: Can we make the migration idempotent? If the CLI is re-run we should not flip existing assertions. Author: Migration is idempotent, it only sets missing annotations and emits a report; updated CLI to no-op on existing tags.
Marta Liu: Audit envelope size could affect downstream KMS proxy buffers. Can we compress or use a fingerprint? Author: envelope contains minimal decision metadata and a policy fingerprint; added compression and unit test for envelope size.
Omar Hassan: Will this block cross-region failover in DR scenarios? We need a delegation escape hatch. Author: added operator-only bypass flag and an approval audit entry; escape hatch requires signed operator intent and is gated behind a feature flag.
Security review (Ana Ruiz): Ensure keys used for signing are restricted and rotated. Action: documented signing key lifecycle and added KMS signing wrapper integration tests.
QA (Ben): flake in e2e when sandbox provider returns 503; added retry with exponential backoff and improved test stability.
payload.title: Introduce KMS constraint matrix and audit-enforcement hook with RBAC v2 condition evaluator

Motivation: a number of tenants rely on implicit fallback to a cluster-default KMS which masks residency guarantees and creates audit gaps. This PR introduces a runtime residency-flagger plus static RBACv2 contract checks to: 1) disallow implicit tenant-level KMS when a tenant has residency constraints, 2) detect RBACv2 policies that reference region-ambiguous roles, and 3) surface audit entries that clearly tie KMS usage to tenant residency decisions. The change is implemented behind a feature flag 'residency-flagger.v1' so we can roll out progressively. The description below is a single contiguous string and includes checklist, design, testing and rollout notes. Checklist: - [x] residency-flagger runtime adapter (feature flag guarded) - [x] RBACv2 policy contract linter and CLI check - [x] audit envelope enhancement: KMS provenance field and residency_assertion tag - [x] migration script to rewrite tenants relying on implicit KMS to explicit per-tenant CMKs or mark as exempt - [x] automated unit and integration tests - [x] docs update for Operators Console and private installer Design summary: residency-flagger is a small middleware placed in the request authorization path that inspects tenant metadata, requested KMS provider, and a policy-derived residency profile. If the tenant has a region-bound residency profile and the request would use the cluster default KMS, the flagger rejects the request with a clear actionable error (HTTP 403 + structured reason). The RBACv2 contract linter parses policy manifests and flags ambiguous role bindings that omit the 'region' or 'residency' claim when used against KMS-protected routes. Audit changes: outgoing audit envelopes now include kms_provenance: {provider:..., key_id:..., tenant_explicit: true|false} and residency_assertion: {profile:..., verified_by:...} so downstream retention and legal workflows can prove locality decisions. Migration: a one-off migration CLI maps existing tenants with implicit KMS to explicit CMK choices; an 'exemptions' list is maintained in the tenancy service for historically permitted tenants and monitored for drift. Backwards compatibility & safety: default behavior is unchanged until the feature flag is turned on. The migration script emits a report and does not change live traffic. Testing: local unit tests for middleware, end-to-end tests in perf-canary env with synthetic tenants, and a canary rollout to 10% of production traffic. Rollout: enable feature flag in shadow mode first (log-only), then block mode for canary tenants, then full rollout. Related work: ENG-1824 (residency infra), SEC-77 (audit model update), OPS-401 (migration orchestration).
Adds runtime residency-flagger that enforces explicit tenant KMS selection; provides RBACv2 policy contract linter and a migration path for tenants using implicit KMS. No runtime downtime expected; rollout is gated behind feature flag.
Grace Li (reviewer): Overall design looks sound. Two asks: 1) make the rejection error include a remediation URL, 2) add metric 'residency_flagger.rejected_by_policy' with tenant and region tags.
Elena Sokolov (author): Addressed both points, added remediation_url in errors and increment metric. Updated tests to assert metric tags.

Motivation: We observed intermittent race conditions during release windows where a small burst of traffic combined with concurrent rollout jobs caused temporary 5xx spikes. This PR adds two orthogonal primitives: (1) a graceful release drain hook implemented as a lightweight controller that coordinates a short, deterministic connection quiesce window before changing routing rules; (2) a preflight verifier that runs a slim set of smoke checks (lint, schema validation, basic e2e smoke against a test model) as a gating step in the release pipeline. Goals: reduce transient errors at cutover, shorten investigation time by surfacing failing preflight checks, and keep developer feedback fast for day-to-day releases. Changes in this PR: - New release drain controller: cmd/release-drain (Go) with a simple leader election using existing raft lease; exposes an HTTP health endpoint and emits metrics to the console. The drain window is configurable per-release via release annotations. - Preflight verifier: ci/preflight/verifier (TypeScript) that executes a curated set of fast checks (lint subset, protobuf schema validation, lightweight model response smoke test). The verifier is invoked as an optional pre-merge job for non-critical changes and required for release/* branch merges. - CI pipeline updates: .github/workflows/release.yml updated to call the verifier and to POST drain requests to the coordinator during deployment orchestration. - Observability: added two new Prometheus metrics and a dashboard snapshot in observability/dashboards/release-drain.json. - Docs: docs/runbooks/release-drain.md with operational runbook and rollback guidance. Checklist: - [x] Implement release drain controller - [x] Add preflight verifier and integrate with workflows - [x] Add metrics + dashboard - [x] Update runbook and README - [x] Tests (unit + smoke) Backwards compatibility: The drain controller is opt-in via release annotations and defaults to disabled. Preflight verifier is enabled for release branches only; existing PRs to feature branches are unaffected unless contributors opt in. Rollout: merged to main behind feature flag and enabled for the next scheduled release window. Related: ENG-4982 (investigation into release flaps), ENG-5031 (preflight checklist for release automation).
Marcus Lee: Nice approach to leader election — can we tolerate the existing 5s raft lease for clusters with high churn? Suggest exposing lease TTL as a config map entry.
Priya Nair (author): Good point — added leaseTTL in config and defaulted to 15s. We fallback to 5s if not set. See internal/drain/lease.go.
Elena Rodriguez: Preflight verifier looks clean; can we split lint subset to run only changed-language linters to shorten runtime?
Priya Nair (author): Implemented change-aware linter selection: verifier probes changed files list from PR metadata when available, otherwise runs full subset. Keeps normal runs fast.
Samir Patel: Observability looks good — add an alert for drain-window > 2m to catch misconfigured releases.
Priya Nair (author): Added alert rule and dashboard note in docs/runbooks/release-drain.md.

payload.body: Context: As Dedicated customers require predictable throughput guarantees while avoiding excessive overprovisioning, we need a controller that issues soft throughput certificates per-tenant and uses a damped autoscaling loop to smooth provisioning during transient spikes. This PR introduces a Thresholded Throughput Certifier (TTC) and a Smoothing Autoscaler that consume utilization and token-bucket style signals to certify short-term throughput guarantees and drive scale decisions. Motivation: Prior reactive autoscalers caused sharp up/down churn and noisy billing for tenants with bursty but bounded traffic. TTC establishes an explicit, decaying 'certified throughput' envelope based on recent high-percentile delivery and a configurable safety margin. The Smoothing Autoscaler uses the envelope to prefer gradual upscales, limited fast ramps for confirmed certificate breaches, and conservative downscales with a deploy-time hysteresis. Summary of changes: 1) telemetry/throughput_certifier.go: new certifier that computes sliding-window p95/p99 throughput, applies configurable thresholds, issues TTL-bound certificates, and emits metrics: ttc_cert_issued, ttc_cert_expired, ttc_cert_utilization_ratio. 2) autoscaler/smoother_controller.go: new controller that ingests certificates, utilization histograms, and queue-length signals; implements damped rate-of-change limiting, emergency ramp path (for sustained 30s breaches), and soft-fallback to lower-cost model variants when cold-starts risk SLOs. 3) api/throughput_cert_crd.yaml: CRD schema for ThroughputCertificate objects (versioned v1alpha1). 4) docs/operations/throughput-certifier.md: operator playbook for tuning margin, TTL, and emergency ramps. 5) tests/smoother_unit_test.go and e2e/scale_scenarios.yaml: unit and end-to-end scenarios covering synthetic microbursts, steady increases, and noise robustness. 6) examples/private/tenant-cert-example.yaml: example tenant config showing certificate goals and conservative-downscale flags. Commits: "init: add throughput certifier prototype and CRD","autoscaler: integrate smoother controller and emergency ramp path","telemetry: wire metrics and unit tests","docs: add operator playbook and examples","tests: add e2e scenarios and CI gating" Files changed (high level): - pkg/autoscaler/smoother_controller.go: core logic (~420 LOC) with comments and exported tuning knobs - pkg/telemetry/throughput_certifier.go: calculation and metrics (~180 LOC) - api/throughput_cert_crd.yaml: CRD and validation schema - docs/operations/throughput-certifier.md: ops playbook and tuning guide - tests/smoother_unit_test.go: 9 unit tests - e2e/scale_scenarios.yaml: three workload profiles Highlights and rationale: - Certificate model: compute sliding-window 5m p95 and 1m p99 delivery rates, then apply a margin multiplier (default 0.85) and an exponential decay with configurable half-life to produce a TTL-bound certificate. Certificates are advisory but surfaced to autoscaler and Console. - Autoscaler behavior: default is conservative smoothing (max 10% scale-up per minute, max 5% scale-down per minute). If certificate breaches are sustained beyond emergencyWindow (30s by default), an emergency ramp can increase capacity up to a configured fastRampPct. - Cost controls: when emergency ramp triggers, system prefers cheaper model variants (quantized) for newly provisioned capacity; this is opt-in per-tenant. - Observability: added tracing spans for cert issuance and scale decisions; Console dashboard tiles baked into docs. Backwards compatibility: the CRD is opt-in; default behavior when TTC is not present remains unchanged. Tests: unit tests verify certificate math, TTL decay, and controller damping. E2E scenarios run against local canary cluster and assert bounded churn and sustained SLOs for synthetic tenants. Review summary and conversation: "Arjun Patel requested more fine-grained metrics and explicit labels on certificate objects for tenant-scoped aggregation; noted potential race between CRD reconciliation and autoscaler informer cache." "Author (Maya Chen) replied: added ttc_cert_tenant and ttc_request_scope labels, and increased informer resync in controller; added comment and test to demonstrate reconciliation order resilience." "Leila Gomez asked for hard limits to prevent runaway emergency ramps; author responded by adding a global emergencyBudget and test coverage for budget exhaustion behavior." "Tomás requested clearer operator guidance on margin selection; docs updated with sample SLI-to-margin mapping and a tuning checklist." CI and validation: initial CI run had a flaky e2e failure in scale_scenarios (test flaked under 1% variance); reran with e2e test stabilization patch and all checks passed. CI checks: unit tests (pass), linters (pass), build (pass), e2e (pass). Security review: quick pass for CRD validation schema and RBAC rules; no privileged access added. Merge notes: squashed and merged to main after approvals from Arjun and Leila. Merge method: squash. Merge commit: "squash! Thresholded throughput certifier and smoothing autoscaler (Maya Chen)" Rollout plan and ops notes: - Begin as opt-in per-tenant by applying ThroughputCertificate objects. - Monitor metrics: ttc_cert_issued, ttc_cert_utilization_ratio, autoscaler_smooth_scale_events. - Start with conservative margin (0.7-0.85) and longer TTL (default 10m) for first 2 weeks. - Track billing deltas and adjust emergencyBudget to cap rapid cost spikes. Release notes: "Introduce Thresholded Throughput Certifier (TTC) and Smoothing Autoscaler to provide advisory short-term throughput guarantees and reduce autoscaling churn. TTC is opt-in via CRD. Adds new metrics and operator guidance for tuning." Breaking change: false
payload.title: Thresholded throughput certifier and smoothing autoscaler

payload.body:
Context: Streaming endpoints intermittently show long tail latency when many small realtime requests interleave with longer context generations. Root causes observed in perf lab: (1) scheduler unfairness that allowed long-running token loops to hold kernels for multiple micro-batches, (2) KV cache misses at first map-access for recently hot prefixes, and (3) flush cadence that was optimized for throughput not tail latency. Goal: reduce p95/p99 token emission latency for single-token and low-length streams without regressing throughput for bulk workloads. Summary of changes: 1) Scheduler: added a lightweight per-worker priority bucket and a short-lived kernel pin (100-300ms) for streaming lanes so that in-progress streaming requests get priority on the active compute slice. This is implemented in scheduler/slice_scheduler.cpp with minimal state and a new metric scheduler_streaming_preemptions. 2) KV cache prefetch: introduced heuristic-based soft prefetch for likely next-key accesses for streaming requests. The runtime now probes kv_cache asynchronously on token generation hot-paths and fills a fastmap before the kernel executes (runtime/kv_prefetch.{hh,cc}). Prefetch is gated behind a runtime flag (--streaming-prefetch=on) and respects memory pressure. 3) Microbatch flush cadence: replaced fixed flush intervals with a latency-first adaptive flush policy that dynamically reduces flush windows to favor low token-latency under observed tail events. Implemented in batching/flush_policy.cpp; default remains throughput-friendly but will transiently reduce to 1-3ms for streaming-critical lanes. 4) Kernel selection hint: added a lightweight hint to the kernel selection path to favor lower-latency kernels for streaming lanes, skipping heavier fused kernels that increase single-token latency. This is a heuristic, not a hard override, so it does not change results, only kernel choice. 5) Observability: new metrics streaming_tail_latency_p95, streaming_kv_prefetch_hit, scheduler_streaming_preemptions and dashboard panels. Tests and validation: - Microbench harness: new microbench stories added to benchmark-lab that mimic interleaved streaming+batch workloads. - End-to-end smoke tests: streaming throughput and correctness retained; no API surface changes. - Perf results: p95 reduced by ~28% and p99 by ~19% across lab workloads with <2% throughput loss on bulk workloads. Implementation notes: commits break changes into focused logical units so reviewers can gate each piece. Prefetch path uses lock-free queues and backpressure tokens to avoid memory amplification. The kernel-hint path is an annotation only accepted by compatible kernels. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag; enabled by default on streaming-optimized clusters after a staged rollout with canary traffic. Related work: complements earlier backpressure improvements (see ENG-9120) and streaming flush cadence experiments (ENG-9402).
9 commits: 1) add scheduler streaming priority and preemption counters; 2) implement kv prefetch async path and unit tests; 3) adaptive flush policy with config knobs; 4) kernel hint plumbing and tests; 5) metrics and dashboards; 6) microbench stories; 7) integration test tweaks; 8) docs/console notes; 9) small fix to prefetch memory accounting.
Arielle Hu: Requested that prefetch be gated by an additional LRU threshold to avoid warming cold prefixes. Diego: Added LRU gating and updated tests to simulate memory pressure. Sven Petrov: Asked for more conservative default pin duration; reduced from 500ms to 100-300ms adaptive window. Maya Kapoor: Noted potential regression on multi-tenant Dedicated pools; added rollout gating and a cluster-level toggle. CI initially: pipeline failed on lint for missing header include in kv_prefetch.hh; fixed in commit 6 and retriggered. Performance CI: first perf nanobench run showed a small regression on a 4k-token bulk synthetic; we limited kernel hint to streaming lanes only and re-ran. Final CI: all checks passed including unit, integration, lint, and perf. Review outcome: approvers Arielle Hu and Sven Petrov approved after two iteration cycles; Maya approved conditionally and re-verified on canary. Merge details: merged via squash, merge_commit_sha: "a1f3b9c6e2d4f8b7"; merge method: "squash".
Reduced streaming token tail latency via scheduler priority, kv prefetch, and adaptive microbatch flush cadence. p95/p99 improvements for interleaved streaming workloads. Flag: --streaming-prefetch (default on for streaming clusters).

payload.body:
Context: As part of ENG-2027 we need a rollout primitive that lets product-facing model swaps run two lanes in parallel (a light canary lane + a low-latency shadow lane) while guaranteeing safe, fast rollback without overcommitting capacity. This PR implements a "dual-track handshake" primitive plus a novel "fallback crediting" ledger that: (1) reserves a configurable rollback budget at deploy time, (2) attaches credits to sessions so we can gracefully failover sessions back to the last-known-good variant, and (3) powers a safe, automated rollback playbook when telemetry gates trip.

Motivation: Existing promote/shadow mechanisms either hold too much traffic hostage or allow promotes that leave the system unable to revert quickly under load. The fallback-credit system ensures we never complete a cutover unless we have reserved the rollback capacity and a path to rehydrate session affinity for affected users. This is especially important for Dedicated and Private deployments where capacity is constrained.

Summary of changes (high level):
- runtime/orchestration/dual_track_handshake.go: New handshake coordinator implementing state machine for dual lanes, session pinning, credit reservation, and coordinated promote/revert.
- runtime/orchestration/fallback_credits.go: Fallback credit ledger (in-memory + optional persistent store hooks) and REST endpoints for credit ops.
- console/rollouts/handshake_playbook.md: Playbook for SREs and PS engineers describing how credits are consumed and how to interpret playbook signals.
- telemetry/metrics/handshake_metrics.yaml: New metric definitions and dashboards (reserved_credits, credits_consumed, session_rehydrate_success, lane_mismatch_rate).
- api/rollouts/v1/handlers.go: API surface additions for creating dual-track rollouts and querying credit state.
- docs/deployments/dual_track_handshake.md: User-facing docs and examples for canary/AB/shadow configurations using the new primitive.
- tests/rollouts/dual_track_handshake_test.go: Unit and integration tests covering state transitions, credit accounting, and playbook-triggered rollback.

Checklist: [x] Unit tests added and passing; [x] Integration smoke tests; [x] Documentation (console + user docs); [x] Playbook for on-call; [x] Telemetry dashboards and alerts; [x] Backwards-compatible API (existing promote endpoints still supported).

Commits (summary):
- 1a2b3c4: initial dual-track coordinator state machine and API wiring
- 2b3c4d5: credit ledger implementation + simple in-memory store and REST ops
- 3c4d5e6: session pinning and rehydrate path for rollback
- 4d5e6f7: dashboard metric instrumentation and alert rules
- 5e6f7g8: docs, playbook, and test coverage additions; lint fixes after CI run

Changed files (illustrative snippets):
- runtime/orchestration/dual_track_handshake.go (+420 -12): core state transitions (INIT -> HANDSHAKE -> MIRRORING -> PROMOTE -> COMMIT/REVERT). Key exported API: StartHandshake(ctx, spec) -> handshakeID.
- runtime/orchestration/fallback_credits.go (+230 -8): ReserveCredits(handshakeID, amount) and ConsumeCreditOnRevert(sessionID).
- api/rollouts/v1/handlers.go (+46 -6): POST /rollouts/dual_track -> validates credit policy and returns reserved budget.

Review conversation (high level, condensed into single string):
- Ethan Liu (review): "Nice separation of concerns. Two asks: (1) make credit ledger pluggable so Dedicated customers can persist to K/V store, (2) add a smoke test that simulates a sustained traffic spike during revert."
- Maya Patel (author): "Addressed both: ledger exposes a CredStore interface and we added an integration test that ramps traffic and verifies session rehydration under CPU pressure. See commits 3c4d5e6 and 5e6f7g8."
- Sofia Ramos (review): "Please add more telemetry around credit exhaustion reasons (insufficient_capacity vs policy_block). Also note we should avoid noisy alerting on ephemeral short reverts."
- Maya Patel: "Added credits_* tags and a bounded deduper on the alerting rule; updated playbook with guidance to silence short-duration reverts. See telemetry changes and playbook section."
- Jordan Kim: "CI failed lint on a goroutine leak in tests; good catch. After fix CI green."

CI summary: Initial run: fail (golangci-lint goroutine-check), rerun after fix: pass. Integration pipeline exercise: smoke tests + perf canary with small local cluster: pass. Telemetry dashboard snapshots attached in PR attachments.

Edge cases and known limitations:
- Fallback credit ledger currently relies on eventual persistence for long-lived rollouts; in this PR we wire a simple CredStore interface with an in-memory implementation. A follow-up will add a Dedicated-backed K/V adapter for HA (Linear ENG-2099).
- Session rehydration is best-effort for long-lived websockets; short-lived tokens may not rebind immediately — playbook documents mitigation steps.

Operational playbook (condensed):
1) Create dual-track rollout with reserve_credits=20% (default) via Console or API.
2) Monitor reserved_credits and credits_consumed; if consumed > 50% within first 5 minutes, hold promote and run smoke bisect.
3) If telemetry gates fail (latency SLO or error budget delta), trigger automatic Revert => credits are consumed to rehydrate sessions; if rehydrate_success < 90% within 60s, escalate to on-call and consider capacity-based backout.

Why this is different: instead of a passive shadow or an immediate swap, dual-track handshake treats promote as a two-party commit that requires a rollback budget to be reserved up-front and ties credit consumption to session-level handoff. This reduces the blast radius of failed promotes and gives SREs deterministic playbook actions.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main on 2026-02-21 after green CI and approvals from Ethan, Sofia, and Jordan. Backported doc changes to release/v1.8 branch in a follow-up PR.

Related work: See ENG-2027 design doc (link in Linear), follow-ups: ENG-2099 (persistent cred store), PM-189 (console UX for credit tuning).
Introduces a dual-track handshake rollout primitive with session-coherent canary and shadow lanes, plus a fallback crediting mechanism to reserve rollback capacity and prevent unsafe promotions. Includes observability, doc updates, and a rollout playbook.

Motivation: Different SDKs implemented ad-hoc credential prefetch and streaming guard code over time which made telemetry sparse and client ergonomics inconsistent. This PR introduces a small, explicit CredentialSnapshotter with observable lifecycle events and a declarative StreamGuard primitive that standardizes precondition checks, early cancellation hooks, and common retry/backoff presets across Python, TypeScript, and Go. The goal is improved operational visibility (why a request reauth'd / was prefetched) and a single ergonomic story for streaming consumers without changing runtime behavior for most callers. Changes are additive and guarded by opt-in configuration.
