Context: During the rollback gameday + a customer escalation (SUP-18503), we reproduced a race where an operator-triggered rollback could overlap with an in-flight apply stage. In certain interleavings, some workers would commit the new optimization config while others would revert to the previous version, leaving the fleet in a mixed state until the next periodic reconcile. This PR makes the runtime apply pipeline linearizable per (tenant, model, region) scope by introducing an apply-epoch token and CAS-style commit semantics at the worker checkpoint boundary.

What changes: (1) Control plane now includes a monotonic `apply_epoch` in the runtime apply intent payload; apply and rollback both bump epoch. (2) Workers persist the last committed (config_version, apply_epoch) and will only commit intents with epoch >= current; older intents are treated as no-ops and still ACKed for idempotent retries. (3) Apply pipeline checkpoint is updated so "download + validate" can run speculatively, but "commit" is gated on epoch comparison and a per-scope mutex to avoid mixed state inside a worker when concurrent reconciles fire. (4) Rollback now cancels any in-flight apply for the same scope by bumping epoch and emitting a `rollback_supersedes_apply` marker used by the rollout controller.

Why this fixes the bug: previously the pipeline compared only config_version and assumed apply/rollback were mutually exclusive at the orchestrator. Under retries, controller restarts, or delayed worker polls, a stale apply intent could arrive after rollback and overwrite the rollback state on a subset of workers. With epoch monotonicity + CAS commit, stale intents cannot regress the committed state.

Tests: adds deterministic concurrency tests that simulate (a) apply and rollback crossing in time with delayed worker polls, (b) controller retry storms, and (c) partial apply followed by rollback while some workers are mid-download. The new tests fail on main and pass with this patch.

Operational notes: This is a backwards-compatible change with a safe default epoch=0 for older orchestrator payloads. After rollout, we should see fewer "mixed_version" warnings in runtime logs. This is a hotfix candidate for the Limited GA safe-apply flag cohort.

Follow-ups: a separate PR will plumb epoch through Console rollouts UI and add a metric dimension on `optcfg_apply_epoch` for debugging (not required for correctness).
Omar El-Sayed (review): Can you clarify the commit boundary? If download happens speculatively, do we risk extra GPU memory churn when a stale intent is dropped at commit time?
Noah Patel (author): Yep. Download/parse can happen, but we don’t touch the live applier state until commit. For KV/cache-related toggles the commit path is the only one that triggers invalidation. Stale intent is dropped before invalidation, so churn is limited to a small CPU-side parse + any staged blob fetch. Added a note in `ConfigApplier::CommitIfNewerEpoch`.
Sofia Ivanova (review): The mutex is per-scope per-worker. Does it block batching scheduler updates too long under retry storms?
Noah Patel (author): Mutex is held only around the commit section (epoch check + swap + metric emit). Download/validate happens outside. Worst case we serialize commit bursts, but commit is <2ms in perf tests. Added a benchmark comment and a micro-timing metric `optcfg_commit_duration_ms`.
Sean Gallagher (review): Please add an explicit log + metric when we reject a stale intent so on-call can see this quickly during incidents.
Noah Patel (author): Added `optcfg_intent_rejected_total{reason="stale_epoch"}` and a single-line warn with scope + epoch pair. Also threaded the request_id when available.
Benji Okafor (review): Control plane serializer sets epoch=0 for older configs; any chance we accidentally treat new intents as stale if worker already has epoch>0 and controller restarts?
Noah Patel (author): Controller persists epoch in the rollout state; restart will reload and continue incrementing. If it can’t load, we fail closed (rollout pauses) rather than emitting epoch=0. Added a unit test for restart path in `rollout_controller.test.ts`.
Omar El-Sayed (review): One nit: ACK semantics on stale intent should be explicit in the RPC comment. Otherwise someone might “fix” it later.
Noah Patel (author): Done. Updated proto comment and added a short design note in the applier header.
Sean Gallagher (approve): LGTM. This aligns with gameday findings. Please coordinate backport if we’re cutting a runtime patch release for the cohort.
Sofia Ivanova (approve): Looks good. Thanks for keeping commit critical section small.
Omar El-Sayed (approve): Approved after changes. The regression tests are solid.

runtime/optcfg: CAS commit semantics + per-scope mutex during commit
rollout: treat rollback as epoch bump; mark superseded applies
tests: deterministic race regression harness for apply/rollback interleavings
docs: update internal comments + troubleshooting log messages

Motivation: Customers need safe, automated defaults for batching, cache warmup, and quant profiles that reflect real traffic patterns without risking regressions. This PR implements a supply-demand based cost scaler that synthesizes conservative presets from live or synthetic traffic, plus a "shadow-run" collector that can run alongside existing routes to gather signals for profile generation. The goal is to provide high-quality starter profiles for Redwood Optimize that reduce unit cost while preserving latency SLOs and sample quality.

What this change includes:
- New service: econ.scaler.Service - takes traffic histograms and capacity/latency targets and outputs candidate presets (batch_size, max_batch_latency_ms, kv_cache_ttl, quant_profile).
- Shadow-run collector: lightweight in-proc tracer that logs per-request latency/seq-length/kv-hit metrics when enabled for a route. Config is off by default and gated behind canary flags.
- Presets generator CLI: rwd-econ generate-presets --input ./shadow.json --output presets.yaml to create YAML presets that can be applied via Console or Dedicated configs.
- Simulation harness: a small Monte Carlo workload prober (economics/sim) used in tests to validate that suggested presets meet cost & latency constraints under synthetic scenarios.
- Metrics & dashboards: adds econ.* Prometheus metrics and a Grafana dashboard JSON to observability-pack.

Commits (high-level):
- feat(econ): add supply-demand scaler core algorithm (2 commits)
- feat(cli): presets generator and simple YAML serializer (1 commit)
- feat(shadow): add collector middleware and sampling knobs (3 commits)
- test(econ): add simulation harness and unit tests (2 commits)
- docs: usage guide + Console integration notes (1 commit)

Files/areas changed (high level):
- src/economics/scaler.go (new)
- cmd/rwd-econ/main.go (new)
- pkg/shadow/collector.go (new), pkg/shadow/middleware.go (updated)
- observability/dashboards/econ-presets.json (new)
- internal/sim/montecarlo_test.go (new)
- docs/optimizers/presets.md (new)
- Makefile + CI: added econ unit and integration job shims

Small illustrative snippet (presets YAML example):
  # presets.yaml (generated)
  route: /v1/generate
  preset_name: conservative-small
  batch_size: 8
  max_batch_latency_ms: 40
  kv_cache_ttl_ms: 30000

Testing and CI:

- CI matrix covers go1.20 and go1.22 builds. Final CI status: pass.

Review conversation (summary):
- Diego Martinez (review): "Nice isolation of the scaler logic. Two notes: 1) ensure metadata about canary sampling rate is surfaced in Console; 2) consider making the quant_profile suggestion conservative (prefer higher-precision by default)."
- Ava Chen (author): "Addressed both: added console flag docs and bumped default to q4_0_opt; added unit tests to assert no more than 5% quality drop in simulation for suggested profiles."
- Priya Srinivasan (review): "Can we add an opt-out annotation for Dedicated customers that don't want shadow telemetry?"

Safety and rollout plan:

- Presets are generated as suggestions only; application requires explicit apply via Console or CLI to change runtime settings.
- Added an "inspect-only" mode for the CLI to evaluate presets without writing to disk.

Backward compatibility: No runtime-breaking changes. All defaults remain unchanged until a preset is explicitly applied.

Performance notes: In internal load tests, presets generated by the scaler reduced per-token CPU time by ~12% on median workloads while keeping p99 latency within configured SLOs. Results vary by model and sequence-length distribution.

Related work: ENG-7123 (project to standardize unit-econ signals), ENG-7190 (presets UI flow).

Motivation: SDK consumers reported subtle mismatches in streaming ergonomics and retry semantics across Python, TypeScript and Go. This caused odd edge-case reauth and backoff behavior in long-lived streams. This PR introduces a lightweight typed-stream bridge contract and a compact retry profile bundle that each SDK can adopt to achieve parity without duplicating orchestration logic.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a typed-stream bridge specification in /specs/sdk/typed_stream_bridge.md and a compact JSON retry-profile catalog at /specs/sdk/compact_retry_profiles.json (consumers: py/ts/go SDKs).
- Implements bridge adapters in the runtime API surface (redwood/sdk-contracts) for aligning cursor semantics, heartbeat hints, and backpressure cues.
- Updates SDK-facing examples and test matrices for Python, TypeScript and Go to demonstrate behavior with the compact retry profiles (adaptive-window, conservative, optimistic).
- Harmonizes default retry/backoff parameters and exposes a compatibility flag for legacy behavior.
- Bumps SDK compatibility matrix entries in docs and emits changelog fragments for all three SDKs.

Why this approach: Centralizing a small typed contract and reusable compact profiles lets us iterate on backoff defaults and stream cursors without cross-repo churn. SDK teams can adopt the spec by importing the JSON/profile and wiring the bridge adapter; no protocol wire change required.

Compatibility and rollout: The default remains backward-compatible; adopters can opt-in to the new bridge via client config: {"stream_bridge": "v1-compact"}. A feature flag on the server side will gate the richer cursor metadata until clients opt in.

Testing: Added unit tests in redwood/sdk-contracts, integration tests that spin up the local stream harness and run through reauth scenarios, and cross-SDK smoke tests validating that TokenRefresh events and Pause/Resume semantics are consistent across languages.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the spec doc for contract clarity, the compact retry profile values (especially adaptive-window math), and the bridge adapter API shape which will be imported by SDKs.

Checklist: Added tests; updated docs; added changelog fragments; validated CI on Linux/macOS; coordinated with SDK owners for follow-up PRs that will adopt the spec.
Jonah Reyes: Can we tighten the adaptive-window growth factor? In heavy contention it looks like the optimistic profile can double too aggressively.
Marina: Adjusted from 2.0 -> 1.5 and added a unit test to simulate congestion; see commit 'tune-adaptive-window'
Priya Shah: The TS adapter shape returns a nullable cursor in a few paths which complicates downstream typing. Can we return an explicit union type instead?
Marina: Converted nullable returns to a discriminated union (type StreamCursor = {kind: 'ok', cursor: string} | {kind: 'pending', nextHintMs: number}). Updated examples and test assertions.
Luca Bianchi: Go code uses time.Sleep in test harness which inflates CI time. Any chance to replace with a virtual clock?
Marina: Replaced the slow sleeps with the harness' mock clock; CI run dropped ~90s in integration stage.

Context: customers building multi-tenant connectors asked for a minimal delegated-auth pattern plus more ergonomic streaming consumers across languages. This PR implements a lightweight delegated-auth proxy interface on the platform client, a language-agnostic retry shim with named presets, and small ergonomic stream "views" that make pull-streams cancelable, checkpointable, and typed. Work spanned runtime client, SDK bindings (Python/TS/Go), and integration tests. Summary of changes: 1) Add DelegatedAuthProxy interface and server-side adapter (token-lease, bind-to-origin) so connectors can request short-lived tokens without embedding full service credentials. 2) Introduce RetryProfile DSL (latency-first, cost-first, durable) and a shim layer used by all SDKs so consumers can select behavior without wiring backoff params. 3) Implement StreamView abstractions: Python AsyncPullView (async iterator with checkpoint/seek), TypeScript PullStreamView (AsyncIterable with .checkpoint()), and Go CancelableIterator (context-aware Next/Close). 4) Small API ergonomics: typed envelopes for chunk frames, clearer error classes (TransientRetryableError, PermanentError), and improved README snippets. 5) SDK version bumps: python->2.7.0, typescript->1.9.0, go->1.14.2. 6) Tests: unit tests per SDK, e2e smoke tests against a local delegated-auth emulator, CI matrix added for cross-language integration. Checklist: - [x] design doc (ENG-3429) - [x] prototype (local) - [x] SDK bindings for py/ts/go - [x] docs/examples update - [x] integration tests - [x] release notes entry Motivation: reduce secret surface area for third-party connectors, standardize retry semantics across polyglot clients, and make streaming consumption less error-prone. Rollout: behind opt-in flags for existing customers; default behavior preserves prior semantics. Backwards compatibility: existing SDK call signatures still work; new types are additive or gated behind feature flags. CI notes: initial run failed on go linter (unused var) and flake8 in python; fix commits added. Merge strategy: squash and merge to keep SDK bumps atomic.
Bump Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs; add delegated-auth proxy and token-lease mode; introduce consumer-friendly stream view abstractions and reusable retry presets; no breaking changes by default; opt-in flags for new ergonomics.
Alyssa Chen (reviewer): Can we make the default retry preset exactly preserve current backoff numbers so customers without opt-in see no behavioral change?
Samir Patel (author): Yes - RetryProfile default maps to the existing numeric backoff; added explicit test to guarantee parity.
Diego Ruiz (reviewer): The delegated auth API shape looks good but we should document threat model and recommended KMS rotations in docs/delegated-auth.md.
Samir Patel (author): Added a security section and clarified token lifetime recommendations.
Ivy Nguyen (reviewer): Go iterator Close semantics need to be deterministic on cancelled context; added a comment and a small refactor request.
Samir Patel (author): Addressed: CancelableIterator.Close now idempotently drains and cancels the internal context. CI green after lint fixes.
Marcus Li (approver): Approved and tested with local emulator; SDK bumps look safe.

payload.body:
Context: We have an ongoing metering hardening push and have confirmed duplicate usage events under a few conditions: (a) server-side fallback/retry paths where request logging is re-emitted, (b) partial pipeline failures where the producer retries publish, and (c) backfills that re-process request logs without stable idempotency keys. These duplicates can inflate billed_tokens / request counts and show up as drift vs billing ledger and customer usage exports (see SUP-28463 and recent Finance discrepancy sampling).

What this PR does: Introduces a v2 idempotency scheme for usage events with deterministic event_identity, ingestion-time de-dupe, and explicit backfill semantics. The goal is that a single customer request maps to a stable set of billable usage events even if the producer retries, the consumer replays, or we re-run backfills.

Key changes: 1) New event_identity_v2: We compute a deterministic SHA256 hash over stable dimensions: account_id, workspace_id, request_id, route_id, model_id, meter_kind, meter_version, usage_window_start_ms, usage_window_end_ms, and a stable attempt_ordinal. For streaming we include stream_id and chunk_ordinal ONLY for non-billable debug events; billable usage remains per-request aggregated to avoid chunk-level duplication. 2) Producer behavior: Producers now always emit request_id + attempt_ordinal. attempt_ordinal is incremented only for server-side retries/fallbacks that would otherwise create distinct billable work; client retries should reuse the same idempotency key and will be treated as the same request if request_id matches. 3) Consumer / storage: The usage-events writer now performs an idempotent upsert (MERGE) keyed on event_identity_v2 when writing to the canonical usage_events table. If an older event_identity_v1 exists for the same request_id + meter_kind + meter_version window, we keep it but mark it superseded_by_v2 to prevent double aggregation in downstream rollups. 4) Dedupe window + metrics: Added explicit counters and SLO signals: usage_events_dedupe_hit_total, usage_events_dedupe_miss_total, usage_events_conflict_total (same key, differing payload), and usage_events_late_arrival_seconds histogram. Conflicts page only when above threshold (initially warn-only) and are annotated in the meter sanity dashboard. 5) Backfill mode: Backfill jobs now set backfill_run_id and backfill_reason and MUST preserve attempt_ordinal. Backfills write with the same idempotency key, so re-running a backfill is a no-op unless the payload is materially different (in which case it is flagged as a conflict and excluded from billing until reviewed).

Why this is safe: This change is additive and does not change the meaning of billed tokens; it reduces duplicates. Downstream rollups are updated to prefer v2 identity when present, and we keep v1 fields for audit/debug. Shadow-billing compare will continue to compute old/new totals; the expected delta should be negative or ~0 (duplicates removed). Any positive delta is treated as a bug and should block rollout.

Test plan: - Unit: deterministic hashing stability, conflict detection, producer attempt_ordinal semantics. - Integration: replay the same request log N times and assert only 1 billable usage row; simulate consumer crash mid-batch and re-run; simulate backfill rerun; verify rollups unchanged except duplicate removal. - Perf-canary: existing streaming + retry scenarios should no longer show double-counting.

Rollout: Stage behind feature flag usage_events_idempotency_v2 for 48 hours in staging + 7 days in prod in shadow mode only (write v2 key + metrics; still aggregate on v1). Then flip aggregation preference to v2 for Hosted API meters; Dedicated/Private unaffected but will benefit if they share the same ingestion path.

Follow-ups: - Coordinate with PR-27518 (shadow billing compare mode) for alert annotations. - Update Finance recon queries to join on event_identity_v2. - Remove legacy v1 rollup path after 30 days of clean drift checks.
Logan Wright (review): Can you clarify the contract for attempt_ordinal? I want to be sure client retries don’t cause accidental dedupe when they actually represent a new request.
Cole Summers (author): Yep — attempt_ordinal is only for server-side retry/fallback inside the same gateway request_id. Client retries should generate a new request_id (SDK default) unless the client explicitly sets idempotency_key; in that case we treat it as the same billable request by design. Added comments + a unit test for this case.
Nadia Rahman (review): For streaming, please confirm we are not hashing chunk_ordinal into billable identity. Otherwise disconnect/reconnect will produce different identities and we’ll reintroduce drift.
Cole Summers (author): Confirmed. Billable identity is per-request aggregated; chunk-level events are debug-only and never enter billing rollups. Updated writer to enforce meter_kind != 'billable' for chunk_ordinal inclusion, and added a guardrail test.
Mei Lin (review): Finance recon currently joins on (request_id, ts_day, meter_kind). If we keep v1 rows, we need to prevent double aggregation. I see superseded_by_v2, but do we guarantee rollups exclude them everywhere?
Cole Summers (author): Good catch. I updated common_filters.sql used by all hosted rollups to exclude superseded_by_v2 = true. Also added a regression test that compares rollup totals for a replay dataset pre/post v2 write.
Aisha Bello (review): Conflict metric paging: please make sure we don’t page on low-volume staging oddities. Can we start warn-only and add to dashboard first?
Cole Summers (author): Done. Conflicts are warn-only and dashboarded; paging threshold set to 0.1% of events per 15m window and only in prod. Added runbook link to drilldown query.
Caleb Johnson (review): MERGE upserts in Snowflake can be expensive. Any perf impact on the writer? We need to keep within ingestion SLA.
Cole Summers (author): Measured on staging replay at 2x peak: writer CPU +6%, warehouse credits +3% due to MERGE. We batch MERGE by partition (hour, region) and only MERGE keys seen in the batch. Added metric usage_events_writer_merge_seconds and a guardrail alert at p95.
Logan Wright (final): Approved after the rollup filter fix + perf metric.
Nadia Rahman (final): Approved.
Mei Lin (final): Approved.
Aisha Bello (final): Approved.
Internal only: Usage event idempotency v2 reduces duplicate billable events from producer retries, consumer replays, and backfill reruns. Adds dedupe/conflict metrics and updates rollups to avoid double aggregation.
payload.title: Hardening usage event idempotency + dedupe keys (reduce duplicate billable events on retries/backfills)

Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally see short, high-frequency microbursts that evade reactive autoscalers because provisioning latency is nontrivial. This leads to transient SLA slippage and increased tail latency for affected tenants. This PR implements two coordinated features: (1) a proactive 'reserve hedge' that maintains a small, configurable pool of warm slots computed per-pool and weighted by recent burstiness, and (2) a Delta Utilization Auditor that computes smoothed per-tenant utilization deltas and exports them so policy and SRE can audit headroom decisions.

What this changes (high level):
- Autoscaler strategy: add proactive_reserve.go which computes a soft reserve target using a burst metric (burst_rate, burst_variance) and a decay-weighted EWMA on delta-utilization. The reserve is advisory and will only be used when the cluster has spare capacity or when policy permits burst borrowing.
- Safety net: introduce a decaying credit pool (reserve_credits) that can be consumed by tenant bursts; credits decay if unused to avoid long-term overcommit.
- Telemetry: add delta_auditor.go to collect per-tenant utilization deltas, EWMA windows, and reserve consumption events; export new Prometheus metrics (redwood_reserve_target, redwood_reserve_consumed, redwood_delta_util_ewma) and a lightweight per-tenant HDR sketch summary for offline analysis.
- Operator flags and config: helm values and operator config support for reserve_hedge.enabled, reserve_hedge.target_fraction, reserve_hedge.decay_seconds, and reserve_hedge.max_credits_per_tenant.
- Rollout and safety: feature gate reserve_hedge.mode with values [off, observer, active]; observer mode only emits metrics and no allocation changes. Canary rollout plan added to deployment docs.

Checklist: [x] design doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1123/proactive-reserve-hedge-design [x] unit tests for reserve math and decay behavior [x] integration test: simulated burst harness to validate no regressions in normal traffic [x] Prometheus metrics + dashboards stubbed [x] helm/operator config documented [x] canary rollout plan included in release notes

Commits summary (high level):
- feat(autoscaler): add proactive reserve strategy and decision API (proactive_reserve.go)
- feat(telemetry): delta auditor and exporter with HDR sketch support (delta_auditor.go)
- feat(prom): wire new metrics into Prometheus exporter (reserve_metrics.go)
- chore(config): add helm values and operator CRD fields (values.yaml, operator_crd.md)
- test: burst simulation harness + unit tests (autoscaler_test.go, delta_auditor_test.go)
- docs: rollout and configuration guide (docs/dedicated/reserve-hedge.md)

Files touched (high level):
- redwood/autoscaler/strategy/proactive_reserve.go
- redwood/autoscaler/controller.go (hook for advisory reserves)
- redwood/telemetry/aggregator/delta_auditor.go
- redwood/telemetry/exporters/prometheus/reserve_metrics.go
- charts/dedicated/values.yaml
- operator/config/crd/reserve_hedge.md
- test/harness/burst_simulator.go
- autoscaler/autoscaler_test.go
- docs/dedicated/reserve-hedge.md

CI: initial lint run flagged API docs mismatch and a formatting issue in delta_auditor.go; fixed in a follow-up commit. Unit tests for autoscaler math cover EWMA edge cases and decay semantics. Integration harness simulating 1000 tenants with synthetic microbursts showed reserve consumption reduces observed tail latency by ~18% in canary runs. All checks green after fixes (build, unit, integ, lint).

Review discussion (condensed):
- Daniel Cho: "Nice approach. Please make defaults conservative (small target_fraction) and ensure credits cannot be transferred cross-tenant."
- Author: "Defaults set to 0.03 target_fraction, max_credits_per_tenant default 5; explicit guard added to prevent cross-tenant borrowing."
- Priya Nair: "Add an observer mode to avoid allocation churn during rollout."
- Author: "Added reserve_hedge.mode with observer option; operator docs updated with canary rollout steps."
- Luca Romano: "Telemetry looks comprehensive; would like an HDR sketch for offline spike analysis."
- Author: "Added HDR sketch export and a Grafana stub in docs."
- Priya: "Please add a safety timeout for credits to avoid long-held capacity."
- Author: "Implemented credit decay (configurable decay_seconds) and unit tests cover decay curve."

Merge: Squash and merge performed by "release-manager" on 2026-02-02; merge commit: "squash! Proactive reserve hedge and delta utilization auditor". Post-merge: feature gate defaults to observer; active rollout scheduled after one week of observer telemetry review.

Daniel Cho: Defaults look conservative; ensure per-tenant caps and no cross-tenant transfer.
Ava Martinez: Added per-tenant max_credits and explicit guard in allocation path.
Priya Nair: Observer mode needed to avoid allocation churn during rollout.
Ava Martinez: Implemented reserve_hedge.mode and documented canary steps.
Luca Romano: Request HDR sketch for offline analysis.
Ava Martinez: Added HDR sketch export and Grafana stub in docs.
CI bot: lint failure on delta_auditor.go (formatting) - fixed in follow-up commit.
SRE automation: observed 18% tail latency improvement in canary after reserve consumption (observer mode simulated).
Introduce proactive reserve hedge: maintains a small warm pool to absorb short microbursts for Dedicated fleets (observer mode by default)
Add delta utilization auditor and new metrics for per-tenant burst analysis
Operator flags: reserve_hedge.enabled, reserve_hedge.mode, reserve_hedge.target_fraction, reserve_hedge.decay_seconds, reserve_hedge.max_credits_per_tenant
Canary rollout recommended: start in observer mode for 7 days, then enable active mode for low-risk pools

Motivation: enable a lightweight, reproducible mini-canary that uses a small synthetic traffic generator informed by orbit simulator traces to calibrate A/B and canary weight ramps without impacting production traffic. This change introduces: 1) a weighted synthetic-smoke generator that produces controllable request distributions (user-agent, payload size, session-stickiness) derived from sampled orbit traces; 2) a rendezvous runner that schedules mini-canaries in a sandboxed slice with automatic health probes and rollback triggers; 3) an autorepair handler that attempts graceful remediation (restart, warmup-snapshots, degrade-to-shadow) before triggering full rollback; 4) console controls and runbook docs for operators to start/stop and visualize synthetic smoke; 5) e2e fixtures and CI gating to reduce flaky failures. Security/privacy: synthetic traces are aggregated and anonymized; no customer PII is used. Rollout plan: gated rollout to staging for 48h, opt-in on Dedicated clusters, monitor canary_metrics and latency/accuracy deltas, then gradual rollout to production lanes. Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration e2e harness, [x] docs + runbook, [x] alerting hooks, [x] Linear links. Impact: reduces risk for model promotes by allowing pre-promote calibration and automated self-heal attempts, lowers manual triage for transient infra noise. Related: ENG-2314 for orbit sampling, PM-989 for canary UX improvements.
c0a8f9d: add orbit-based synthetic traffic generator and sampling adapters
7b3d2e1: introduce mini-canary rendezvous runner and sandbox slice abstractions
9a4f1c2: autorepair handler with restart/warmup snapshot logic and degrade-to-shadow path
d12b7e4: console UI components for synthetic-smoke controls and telemetry panels
f5c3b88: e2e fixtures and synthetic traffic profiles + helm values for opt-in
e5f6a3b: tests, docs, and runbook; CI adjustments to tolerate controlled flakiness
Liam Patel (2026-01-21): Nice approach. Two questions: how do you ensure synth traffic doesn't accidentally leak to prod edge? Please confirm sandboxing boundaries.
Aisha Kumar (2026-01-21): We run synthetic lanes on dedicated slice namespaces with network egress disabled by default and an admission webhook to prevent non-sandboxed scheduling. Added notes in docs/runbooks/mini-canary-operator.md.
Sofia Moreno (2026-01-22): Can we add a metric that measures representativeness of synthetic traffic vs sampled orbit traces? If not perfect, add a confidence score to telemetry.
Aisha Kumar (2026-01-22): Added canary_metrics.synth_representativeness gauge and a derived confidence score; updated observability dashboard config.
Devon Brooks (2026-01-23): CI flaked on e2e: test 'canary-flow-identity' failed once. Recommend retry logic and mark known-temporary in pipeline.
Aisha Kumar (2026-01-23): CI pipeline updated to rerun flaky e2e once automatically; also added stricter fixture teardown to reduce leftover state.
Introduces an opt-in mini-canary workflow driven by orbit-sampled synthetic traffic for pre-promote calibration and a best-effort autorepair flow that attempts warmup or degrade-to-shadow before full rollback. Operators: see docs/runbooks/mini-canary-operator.md for runbook and console controls.

payload.body: Summary: Adds a connection 'hold' state and deterministic resume negotiation to reduce spurious session aborts on transient client disconnects and to ensure ordered, idempotent tool/function calls after reconnect. Also introduces an explicit server-enforced soft-timeout for passive streams and an ACK gating mechanism so tool-calls are only committed once the client has acknowledged sufficient progress. Motivation: In production we've observed two classes of failures: 1) brief client network interruptions cause immediate session tombstoning causing loss of in-flight tool calls and confusing clients; 2) dual-path commit races where the server retries or replays tool/function calls after reconnect, causing duplicate side-effects for non-idempotent tools. This PR implements a protocol-level negotiator to keep sessions in a hold/quarantine state during short disconnects, a deterministic resume handshake to reconcile in-flight operations and KV cache offsets, and an ACK gating rule to defer tool-call finalization until the client confirms receipt of stable progress. Design: 1) New state machine: ACTIVE -> HOLD -> RESUME_NEGOTIATION -> ACTIVE or EVICT. HOLD is entered on TCP/websocket disconnect or prolonged socket stall; it prevents immediate tombstoning and continues short-lived resource reservation. 2) Resume negotiation: client re-connect includes a resume token + last-ack-offset; server reconciles inflight queue, deduplicates tool-calls using run-id + sequence, and returns an explicit commit plan. 3) Tool-call ACK gating: tool integrations now accept provisional execution IDs; final side-effect commit only proceeds after a client ACK or when a server soft-timeout elapses with conservative hedging. 4) Soft-timeout: default 45s soft hold timeout for passive streams; configurable per-customer tier and override via Dedicated/Private policies. 5) OpenAI compatibility layer: stream adapter updated to expose resume semantics via the same SSE/websocket boundaries while preserving existing top-level API surface. Backwards compatibility: existing clients that do not send resume tokens will see unchanged behavior (server falls back to previous eviction rules). New ACK gating is opt-in via a request-level header X-Redwood-ack-mode=provisional which defaults to off for older SDKs. Implementation notes: - runtime/streaming/negotiator.py: new state machine and reconciliation code. - api/openai_compat/stream_adapter.go: updated handshake and resume flow mapping to the OpenAI streaming model. - sdk/python/redwood/streaming.py and sdk/typescript/...: client helpers to emit resume tokens and manage provisional tool call lifecycle. - hooks added to observability to surface hold-duration histograms and resume outcome counts. Testing and validation: unit tests for state transitions and deduplication logic added (tests/unit/test_negotiator.py). Integration tests simulating flaky networks and duplicate tool-call scenarios (tests/integration/test_stream_resume.py). Load bench locally showed median additional CPU <2% for streams under normal traffic. Rollout plan: Feature gated under runtime flag stream_resume_negotiator_v1, will be enabled for internal E2E only, then staged to Canary customers (low-traffic tenants), after 2 weeks open for all Hosted, then included in Dedicated/Private release notes with config knobs. Observability: new metrics: stream.hold_duration_ms, stream.resume_outcome{success,merge,eject}, toolcall.commit_lag_ms, toolcall.duplicate_detected_count. Migration and operator actions: Dedicated/Private operators may override soft-timeout via deployment config; documented in docs/streaming/hold_resume.md. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] OpenAI adapter mappings validated - [x] Docs draft added - [x] Feature-gate present - [x] Canary run plan appended Commits: ["a1c3f2b: implement negotiator state machine and tests","b2d9c4e: add resume token serialization + client helpers","c3e8a7f: openai adapter handshake mapping and SSE glue","d4f1e3a: toolcall ack gating and provisional commit path","e57ab9c: metrics and docs for hold/resume"] Changed files (high level): ["runtime/streaming/negotiator.py","runtime/streaming/state_machine.proto","api/openai_compat/stream_adapter.go","sdk/python/redwood/streaming.py","sdk/typescript/src/streaming.ts","tests/unit/test_negotiator.py","tests/integration/test_stream_resume.py","console/observability/metrics.yaml","docs/streaming/hold_resume.md","deploy/feature_flags/stream_resume_negotiator_v1.yaml","integrations/tool-adapters/http_adapter.go","scripts/bench/run_stream_bench.py"] Review conversation: ["Evan Liu: Nice separation of concerns. Two asks: make the default soft-timeout configurable via env var for Hosted and add an additional metric for resume_conflict_count.","Maya Kapoor (author): Addressed; added STREAM_SOFT_TIMEOUT env var and metric resume_conflict_count. Also updated docs to highlight env var for Dedicated/private.","Sofia Martens: Please add an integration test covering a reconnect that causes partial toolcall visibility (client ACK arrives mid-tool-exec) so we exercise provisional->final commit shift.","Maya Kapoor: Added test_integration reconnect-driven-ack test and clarified the commit hedging logic; PTAL.","Diego Alvarez: Linter flagged a few shadowed variables; fixed. Approving after CI passes.","CI Bot: initial CI failed (flake in test_stream_resume.py on macos runner), retriggered and passing on rerun."] CI summary: ["build: pass","unit-tests: pass","integration-tests: pass (flaky rerun)","lint: pass","bench: report generated"] Release notes: ["Improves streaming reliability by introducing a hold/resume negotiation that prevents session tombstoning on transient disconnects.","Adds a provisional ACK-based gating mechanism to reduce duplicate side-effects from reconnect-induced retries.","Feature gated; configurable soft-timeout for Dedicated/Private."] Additional notes: This is intentionally conservative; no change is made to default behaviour for older clients. The feature gate can be disabled quickly if we see unexpected tail latencies. Contact ops on rollout: @oncall-streaming.

payload.body:
Motivation: Streaming structured output with function/tool-calling is brittle when tokens for bracket characters or regex anchors are split across streaming chunks. This causes downstream parsers (OpenAI-compat tool callers and schema validators) to mis-parse partial frames, resulting in spurious tool invocations or broken structured outputs.

Summary: Introduce a streaming schema enforcer shim that sits in the OpenAI-compat layer and does three things: 1) atomize and reassemble tokenizer edges that would split structural tokens (quotes, braces, function-call separators) across chunks; 2) wire a lightweight CFG-aware fast-fallback parser compiled for CPU when GPU kernel path can't satisfy complex regex/grammar constraints; 3) add explicit toolcall framing markers and heuristics so partially-emitted tool payloads don't trigger tool invocation until a syntactic commit point is reached.

Key changes (single-line checklist): [x] Enforcer shim added to integrations/openai/compat_layer.py and runtime/streaming_shim.rs; [x] Tokenizer splitter/atomizer added in runtime/tokenizer/splitter.cu + fallback C implementation; [x] CFG CPU fallback engine implemented in runtime/grammar/fallback_cpu.c (small footprint + permissive fallbacks); [x] Toolcall framing rules added and exposed via API flag `prefer_strict_toolcall_framing`; [x] Unit and e2e tests (including flaky-token-chunking matrix) added under tests/e2e/; [x] Docs updated with migration notes and opt-in flags.

Design notes: The shim intercepts streaming token batches before they are forwarded to the OpenAI-compat streaming interface. It examines the tokenizer tokenization boundaries and holds back emission of structural tokens when they are part of a longer multi-token delimiter (e.g., CRLF-anchored regexes, multi-byte quote characters). When the runtime cannot guarantee atomicity on the GPU path (e.g., due to current kernel fusion heuristics), the shim falls back to a compact CFG checker on CPU to validate that the partial output cannot form a valid constraint-satisfying completion. Toolcalls are only relayed to the tool-runner once the framing heuristic sees either the full function signature and a closing marker or a validated CFG parse. This reduces false positives during streaming and ensures behavior matches batch decode semantics.

Performance: Microbenchmarks show median end-to-end streaming latency increase of ~3ms on 2048-seq workloads when shim is enabled (GPU path), with a tail P99 increase of ~12ms in the worst-case when CFG fallback is used. Unit token throughput remains within 95% of baseline in typical workloads. See perf numbers in the PR body.

Testing: Added deterministic unit tests for tokenizer atomization, property tests for chunk boundary permutations, and e2e tests exercising toolcall sequences with artificially split tokens. CI includes a new flaky-token-chunking matrix job that runs smaller variants of the chunk-split permutations to catch regressions. Locally validated against existing OpenAI-compat integration tests.

Migration and rollout: Default for `prefer_strict_toolcall_framing` is OFF; to avoid changing existing customers' runtime semantics we ship this as opt-in. For Hosted we will enable the shim behind a feature flag and roll to canary tenants first. Dedicated and Private customers can opt into the flag in their config.

Risks: The primary risk is subtle differences in toolcall timing for apps that intentionally rely on partial toolcall streaming. To mitigate we keep the flag off by default and document behavior. CFG fallback correctness for complex grammars is intentionally permissive (we prefer false negatives over false positives) and is covered by unit tests.

Related: Linear: ENG-2109 (streaming stability), ENG-2140 (tokenizer atomizer). Support ticket SUP-914 captured an incident that inspired this work.

Notes for reviewers: Look at runtime/streaming_shim.rs for the emission state machine, runtime/tokenizer/splitter.cu and splitter_fallback.c for atomization logic, and integrations/openai/compat_layer.py for wiring into function/tool-call paths. The e2e tests are the best reproducible signal (tests/e2e/toolcall_streaming.test).
Ravi Patel (2025-11-05): Nice direction. Two comments: 1) We need numbers on P99 impact in high concurrency, 2) please add a test where the closing brace is split across two chunks. Can you add perf counters for shim hot-path?
Emilia Chen (2025-11-06): Added e2e test covering split closing brace case and added counters (shim_emit_count, shim_fallback_count, shim_hold_ms). Updated PR with perf microbench numbers.
Diego Morales (2025-11-07): Requested change: the CFG fallback currently treats some regex anchors as strict; prefer a permissive-mode toggle. Also flagged a memory allocation on hot-path in streaming_shim.rs.
Emilia Chen (2025-11-08): Implemented permissive-mode toggle and addressed allocation by reusing a small ring buffer. Updated tests to cover permissive and strict modes.
Ava Thompson (2025-11-10): CI showed a flaky matrix failure (intermittent ordering in e2e). Re-ordered assertions and added retry-with-backoff for timing-sensitive checks. Approving pending green CI.
Sophie Li (2025-11-11): Approved — verified docs and migration notes. No security concerns after review.
Adds an opt-in streaming schema enforcer that reduces false-positive tool invocations and improves structured-output stability across chunked token streams. Includes tokenizer atomizer/fallback and a permissive CFG CPU fallback. Opt-in via `prefer_strict_toolcall_framing`. Default OFF.
payload.title: Streaming schema enforcer + toolcall framing and tokenizer splitter for OpenAI compat

Context: During a recent regional spike (INC-8872) we observed a class of failures where overloaded nodes would prematurely drop connections while the control plane was still reconciling KV cache state. Symptoms included long tail latencies and an elevated rate of 'stalled-resume' errors when requests were re-admitted immediately after a circuit flip. Motivation: We need a low-risk, quick-to-rollout hotfix that reduces oscillation during regional pressure without changing tenant-facing admission semantics. This PR introduces two cooperating components: (1) grace-prober: a lightweight remote probe that exercises the fastpath on candidates before allowing full traffic rejoin; probes are inexpensive and additive to health probes, and (2) stall-resume-optimizer: a heuristic controller in the admission layer that enforces a short, tokenized resume-backoff for connections that previously saw KV drain or fastpath stalls. Design summary: - grace-prober runs as an in-process goroutine (non-blocking) that emits a single RPC to the local fastpath runtime; success is measured by a sub-5ms p90 response and a successful KV cache hit. Failure increments a regional 'probe-failure' metric and extends resume backoff. - stall-resume-optimizer maintains a small LRU of recently-evacuated connection IDs with a token bucket-like allowance per-tenant; when tokens are depleted, rejoin requests are delayed up to a configurable jitter window (default 250ms). - Both features are guarded behind runtime feature flags (runtime.enable_grace_prober, runtime.enable_stall_resume_opt) and a canary rollout is implemented via the node meta label (node.canary=true). Telemetry and alerting: - New metrics: runtime.grace_prober{result=success|failure}, runtime.stall_resume_delay_ms (histogram), runtime.stall_resume_token_usage. - Added a Grafana panel to the regional runtime dashboard and a low-severity alert that fires when probe-failure ratio > 5% for > 10m. Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to canary nodes in us-west-2 (node.meta.canary=true) for 4 hours, monitor probe success and p99 latency. 2) Gradual ramp to 25% nodes in the region over 2 hours if no regressions. 3) Global roll once telemetry is stable. Backout plan: disable runtime.enable_grace_prober and runtime.enable_stall_resume_opt via console flags, rollback node image if needed. Testing: - Unit tests for probe callback, token bookkeeping, and race conditions around LRU eviction. - Integration test that simulates KV drain and ensures the optimizer prevents immediate rejoin churn. - Load test in benchmark-lab that reproduces the INC-8872 pattern; we measured a 42% reduction in stall-resume error rate and a 18% drop in p99 tail under synthetic pressure. Checklist: - [x] Feature-flagged changes - [x] Basic unit + integration tests - [x] Perf/load test results attached - [x] Telemetry dashboards + alert added - [x] Canaries and rollout plan specified Changes: Small, focused runtime additions and admission controller wiring. See files_changed for specifics. Related: ENG-3921 (reduce rejoin oscillation), ENG-3898 (regional KV drain telemetry).
Andre Patel (2026-01-18): Left a few nits but overall LGTM. Can you add a note about worst-case memory growth of the LRU?
Maya Chen (2026-01-18): Reply: LRU is capped at 1024 entries per-node by default; added a comment and test to assert cap behavior.
Priya Raghavan (2026-01-19): Please confirm telemetry cardinality - don't create per-tenant high-card metrics. Suggest aggregate by tenant_cohort instead.
Maya Chen (2026-01-19): Reply: Changed metric labels to tenant_cohort and added aggregation in the dashboard; updated tests.
Sergei Ivanov (2026-01-19): Approve after CI passes. Noted the canary rollout timing in the PR description.
CI Bot (2026-01-19): All checks passed (unit, integration, lint). Load test run completed: infra/benchmark-lab confirmed improvements.
Hotfix: introduce a grace prober and stall-resume optimization to reduce oscillation during KV drain events. Default flags are off; enabled behind runtime flags and canary rollout. Reduces stall-resume error rate under pressure.
When enabling globally: monitor runtime.grace_prober{result=failure} and runtime.stall_resume_token_usage. If probe-failure >5% sustained, revert feature flag and investigate KV drift. Ensure canary nodes have node.meta.canary=true before enabling.

Motivation: Customers running multiple tenants on shared Dedicated/private deployments asked for finer-grained cost automation that respects tenant SLAs and billing profiles. Existing econ presets are tenant-agnostic and sometimes recommend aggressive quant profiles that violate latency SLOs for premium tenants. This PR introduces a tenant-aware Cost Curator service and "priority quant lanes" that let us apply conservative quantization and cache/batching defaults for high-tier tenants while still optimizing cheaper tiers automatically.

What this PR does (single-pass summary): Adds a transparent Cost Curator microservice that consumes workload signals (p99, token distribution, KV hit rate), tenant metadata (tier, SLA, billing class), and current model profiles to produce per-tenant runtime hints: batching targets, prefix cache TTLs, quantization preference order, and a fallback plan. Introduces priority quant lanes: ordered quant profile queues with explicit latency budgets so premium tenants never get quant variants that breach configured SLOs. Implements tenant override layer and rollout hooks in the routing plane.

Key features and approach: - New config schema (yaml/json) for tenant-cost-profiles with explicit fields: "max_latency_ms", "preferred_quant_order", "batch_size_target", "cache_ttl_ms", "cost_target_pct". Defaults are provided but tenants can pin or opt-out. - Cost Curator uses a lightweight policy engine (rule-based with pluggable scoring) and a confidence score to avoid oscillation. - Priority quant lanes are defined per model family; each lane lists quant variants from safest to most aggressive along with measured p95 delta. The router consults the lane and tenant budget before choosing a variant. - Safe fallback: if an aggressive quant increases errors or latency beyond thresholds, requests are automatically routed to a compatible safer variant and the Curator receives a telemetry event. - A/B rollout: new lanes are enabled via rollout_flag/tenant selectors, supported by Canary and Shadow evaluation modes.

Checklist: - [x] Add Cost Curator service and API (internal) - [x] Persist tenant profile schema and migration job - [x] Router changes to consult Curator and quant lanes - [x] Add telemetry hooks (latency/cost/quality) - [x] Unit tests + integration harness (simulated tenants) - [x] End-to-end perf benchmarks and safety regression tests - [x] Docs: console UI fields + CLI migration commands

Testing and results: Microbenchmarks on our staged cluster (a mix of A100 and L40) across three synthetic workloads (chat-short, instruction-long, embeddings-heavy) show median cost savings of 18% overall and 12% for premium-tier tenants (because of more conservative lanes). P99 latency observed: within target for premium tenants (+3ms median variance), and aggressive-tier tenants saw average latency reduction of 22% when allowed. Regression tests added to ensure no failure-case routes to an unsupported quant variant.

Migration and rollout: Added a one-shot migration that backfills tenant profiles from usage snapshots; default profiles are assigned when tenant metadata is absent. Rollout planned in stages: internal dogfooding -> opt-in customers -> auto-suggested profiles -> auto-apply after 4 weeks of stable telemetry.

Backward compatibility and safety: The Curator is opt-in by default and respects explicit tenant pins. Feature flags added so SRE can flip behavior per cluster. All recommendations are logged with a confidence score and reasoning for auditability.

Risk and mitigation: Risk: over-eager quant selection could impact quality. Mitigation: priority lanes + runtime guardrails + instant fallback routing + safety alerts.

Related: ENG-4921 (tenant-level econ), ENG-4975 (quant routing).
Diego Alvarez: Please add a short-circuit in the router to avoid extra RPCs when tenant has a pinned profile (resolved in commit d4e5f6a).
Priya Kapoor: Can we include a degradation test for embeddings where quantization often hurts quality? Added in tests/integration/tenant_e2e.rs (commit e5f6a7b).
Luca Romano: Suggest logging the chosen quant variant and the Curator confidence score on each route for telemetry; added and wired through telemetry events.proto.
Maya Chen (author): addressed comments and added rollout docs + feature flags. CI rerun green on 2026-02-16.

Motivation: On-call engineers and platform SREs need faster context when investigating token-cost and latency anomalies. Current traces and dashboards show metrics but don't surface playbook guidance or condensed invocation context. This PR introduces two complementary observability features: 1) lightweight invocation breadcrumbs (callstack anchors + token-cost hints) that travel with sampled traces and are surfaced in the Console and dashboard tooltips; 2) an internal 'telemetry-playground' dev launcher that lets engineers replay or craft synthetic invocations, annotate breadcrumbs, and validate alert tuning changes without affecting production metrics. Summary: - New 'breadcrumbs' header (x-rd-breadcrumbs) and ingestion path that stores compact anchors: route id, invocation fingerprint, top-3 hot kernels seen, token-cost-estimate, and optional runbook id hints. Breadcrumb items are intentionally small (<= 512 bytes) and are scrubbed for PII before indexing. - A runbook registry service mapping runbook ids to short descriptions and playbook links; Console surfaces suggestions when breadcrumbs match known patterns (e.g., kernel queueing + high token energy). - Telemetry-playground: a small local+dev-only UI and server that can replay sampled payloads, attach synthetic breadcrumbs, and run the alert evaluator against modified thresholds. - Dashboard updates: Grafana panels (observability/dashboards/token-cost) get a new compact sparkline with breadcrumb annotations and a runbook link action. - Alert tuning helper: CLI endpoint and Console flow that recommends band adjustments and quiet windows when a breadcrumb cluster spikes. Checklist: - [x] Breadcrumb header parsing and ingestion path - [x] Runbook registry + migration script (no DB downtime) - [x] Console: breadcrumb hover panel + runbook link - [x] Telemetry-playground package and quickstart - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Grafana JSON updates - [x] TLS and auth checks for playground dev server (disabled in prod) Safety/PII: breadcrumbs are scrubbed by the telemetry-scrubber with a new rule set; we do not persist user prompt text. The playground stores only synthetic or sampled, scrubbed payloads. Migration notes: the ingestion schema adds an optional breadcrumbs column to invocation_metadata; migration is additive and backwards compatible. Rollout plan: feature-flag controlled: breadcrumbs ingestion default off for existing customers; Console surfaces links only for internal tenants initially, then opt-in for customers. Impact: expected small storage increase for sampled traces (~0.8% daily ingest), but improved MTTR for SREs.
Diego Marquez: Please add an explicit schema version marker in the migration so old readers can skip unknown fields.
Ava Kline: Added migration comment and schema_version column in 20260218_add_breadcrumbs.sql, updated ingest code to check version.
Priya Shah: We need a stronger scrubber rule for quoted blobs in breadcrumbs; runbook ids are fine but sometimes user-provided metadata slips through.
Ava Kline: Tightened scrubber regex and added unit tests (tests/integration/test_breadcrumb_flow.py). Note: we still do not persist prompt text.
Ethan Wong: Console hover looks good; request to make runbook link open in a new tab and capture metric context.
Ava Kline: Updated Console hover to include route/model context and added telemetry metadata to the open link.
Priya Shah: Can playground be accidentally exposed? Ensure auth defaults to disabled in prod and require developer token.
Ava Kline: Playground server defaults to localhost-only and requires dev token; documented in playground/README.md.
Diego Marquez: Approve after minor nit about metric name token_cost.breadcrumbed -> token_cost.breadcrumb.
Ava Kline: Renamed metric and updated dashboards accordingly.
CI: initial integration timeout traced to test harness; increased wait+retries and reran CI.
Add small per-invocation breadcrumbs for faster SRE triage; runbook-linked suggestions in Console; telemetry-playground for safe alert tuning and replay. Feature is behind a feature flag and scrubbed for PII.
When enabling breadcrumbs ingestion for a tenant: 1) monitor telemetry.ingest.breadcrumbs.size and telemetry.scrubber.dropped_count for first 48 hours; 2) ensure runbook registry is seeded before enabling Console links; 3) playground should only be run in dev networks; if exposed, rotate dev tokens immediately.
Integration tests cover end-to-end ingestion -> scrub -> index -> Console hover rendering. Local playground quickstart: make dev token, run 'make playground-dev', use sample payloads in tests/fixtures to replay. Included synthetic replaybench to assert alert tuning behaviour.
Low-medium: additive schema change and new ingestion path. Main risks are PII leakage (mitigated by scrubber) and increased indexing volume (estimated <1% for sampled traces).

Context: We saw two transient zone outages in the last quarter where sudden traffic surges caused regional controllers to flip circuits too aggressively, resulting in a cascade of tenant evictions and noisy failovers. This PR introduces a lightweight "soft-fuse" layer that sits between regional health signals and the circuit breaker to provide a short, silent absorb window for spikes that match a transient signature. Motivation: Reduce noisy mass-evictions and prevent unnecessary global failover during short-lived pressure bursts. Goals: 1) absorb sub-second to multi-second surges without creating long-lived penalty states; 2) emit telemetry to distinguish soft-fuse events from hard circuit trips; 3) provide safe rollout with immediate rollback and canary settings. Design summary: - Soft-fuse controller: evaluates rate and latency jitter signatures for a specified region, and can transiently apply a soft-fuse state which throttles non-critical backends and increases internal admission thresholds without marking the region as unhealthy. - Decay model: soft-fuse has a configurable exponential decay and a max duty window to avoid masking sustained overloads. - Telemetry: new metrics soft_fuse_engaged{region,reason}, soft_fuse_duration_seconds and a histogram for pre/post latency to validate effect. - Policy hooks: soft-fuse integrates with existing SLO enforcer to adjust per-tenant weight only while active; on fuse expiration the policy reconciler runs a quick validation pass to avoid abrupt eviction waves. Rollout and operational plan: 1) feature flag gated off by default; 2) enable in canary region (us-west-2) for 48h with metric alarm for continued degradation; 3) if telemetry shows reduced eviction rate and no higher end-user latency percentile, expand to 50% regions; 4) provide immediate kill switch via Console and CLI. Backwards compatibility: No API changes. Controller lives behind runtime feature flag and is opt-in per-region via config. Tests and validation: - Unit tests for decay math and policy transitions added. - Integration harness simulates jittery traffic; included test scenarios for transient spike and sustained overload. - Load lab run on canary showed 27% fewer tenant evictions during 10x short bursts. Risks and mitigation: - Risk of masking sustained overload: mitigated by max duty cycle and a hard circuit that still trips if SLOs are violated for configured window. - Telemetry blind spots: added high-cardinality tags for region and tenant class, and a conservative default sampling for raw traces. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-2123) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Telemetry dashboards and alerts (ops/dashboard/soft-fuse) - [x] Feature flag gating and Console controls - [x] Rollout plan in release notes Release notes: "Add soft-fuse sanctuary: transient surge absorber that reduces noisy mass-evictions; opt-in per-region via runtime config. See ENG-2123 for details."
Ethan Cole: Overall this looks good. Two requests: 1) make the default duty window smaller (10s) and 2) add a guard in the reconcilers so we don't re-apply tenant weight changes if the tenant had been manually adjusted. The canary plan looks safe.
Priya Anand: RE Ethan: lowered default duty window to 8s (commit a1f3c8b) and added a reconcilers guard to skip manual overrides (commit c7e9f45).
Marta Ruiz: Can we ensure the metrics include an explicit tag for "candidate_reason" so SRE can filter by spike type? Also add a short circuit for controlplane signals that are older than 5s.
Priya Anand: Added candidate_reason tag and controlplane age guard. Updated telemetry docs in ops/soft-fuse-sanctuary.md.
Linus Park: Integration test flaked once on CI (timing). Please mark the harness test as stable and add a retry loop; also confirm CPU impact is <1% in controller in production runs.
Priya Anand: Added retry loop and micro-benchmark; controller CPU median is 0.4% in canary runs. Rerun CI.
Merged after two approvals (Ethan, Marta) and green CI. Squash merge used to keep history concise. Feature gated by runtime flag; ops instructed to enable only in us-west-2 initially.

SRE: monitor dashboards/ops/soft-fuse for 72h, paging threshold is 5% increase in p95 latency
Doc: add troubleshooting steps to docs/ops/soft-fuse-sanctuary.md

Context: We observe intermittent throughput regressions during canary cutovers where aggregate throughput declines for a subset of tenants even when median latency remains within SLOs. Existing canary detectors focus on latency percentiles and total error rates but miss short-lived throughput contractions that later amplify into capacity pressure. Goal: Add an allocator and rollout safeguard that detects negative throughput derivatives at cohort granularity, attributes them to candidate changes, and enforces a staged cutover with an automated rollback budget if pressure accumulates. Design summary: 1) Throughput stability allocator (runtime/scheduler): computes per-cohort throughput time series and a smoothed derivative (EWMA of first differences) to surface early negative momentum. 2) Cutover safeguard controller (console/canary): when staged traffic increases are scheduled, controller simulates expected throughput headroom using historical tail ratios and the allocator signal; it blocks cutover if predicted shortfall exceeds configured budget. 3) Adaptive rollback budget: a budget accrual system that allows limited transient regressions but triggers an automated soft rollback when cumulative shortfall exceeds threshold. 4) Instrumentation & dashboards: new SLI (throughput-derivative-negative-seconds), guard traces linked to rollout IDs, and a canary heatmap for early ops triage. Implementation notes: changes touch scheduler, canary controller, and the console visualization layer. The allocator is implemented as a thin C-extension-backed Python module to keep hot paths low-latency; the controller runs as part of the canary orchestration service with a lightweight simulation engine. Tests & validation: unit tests for derivative computation and budget accounting; integration tests using the perf-sim harness to replay historical traffic and inject synthetic regressions; blue-green smoke runs on staging with a mix of synthetic tenants. Feature gate & rollout: gated behind feature flag "throughput_stability_allocator"; initial rollout to internal canaries only, then opt-in for customer canaries. Rollout checklist included below. Backwards compatibility & safety: changes are additive, default budgets conservative (fail-open to manual review for extreme cases) and monitored by new alerts. Related work: extends ENG-2970 (canary orchestration refactor) and complements recent latency-focused detectors. See linked Linear ENG-3421 for evaluation plan. Deployment plan: merge to main -> enable flag in staging -> 1-week internal telemetry -> opt-in external canaries -> gradual increase. Impact: estimated to catch ~70% of early throughput contractions in our historical canary corpus in simulation, reducing restart/scale events by ~18% in the staging trace set. Checklist: - [x] design doc + simulation notes linked in Linear ENG-3421 - [x] unit/integration tests - [x] perf benchmarks for C-extension path - [x] console UI mockups reviewed - [x] Ops runbook updated - [x] feature flag + kill-switch implemented - [x] staging rollout and smoke runs completed
Ava Martinez: Can you clarify how cohorts are defined? Will small tenants generate noisy signals?
Samira Khan: Cohorts are traffic-shaped groups (tenant-size x workload-class). The allocator applies an adaptive smoothing window proportional to request volume to reduce noise for small tenants.
Jordan Li: Micro-benchmark results? The C-extension looks promising but we need numbers for 99th CPU on p4d.
Samira Khan: Added micro-benchmarks in the PR and moved the hot loop to the native path; 99th CPU reduced from 28ms to 6ms in our runner for 1k-sample aggregation.
Priya Nandakumar: What are the safe default budgets? We should avoid aggressive rollbacks during traffic spikes.
Samira Khan: Default budget is conservative: 3% cumulative shortfall per rollout session or 10s of sustained negative derivative at cohort-level, whichever hits first. Ops can tune per-organization.
Ava Martinez: Please add more observability around why a cutover was blocked (traces + simulated headroom).
Samira Khan: Added canary trace links and a short textual reason in UI (signal snapshot + budget delta).
Initial CI run: lint OK, unit tests failed (allocator edge cases) -> fix -> re-run -> integration perf-sim flaky on net20 -> re-run -> all checks passing on second rerun. Full test matrix: linux/py3.11 integration (pass), mac/lint (pass), perf microbench (pass)
Introduce throughput stability allocator and automated cutover safeguard: adds cohort-level throughput derivative detection, simulated cutover headroom checks, and an adaptive rollback budget to reduce rollout-induced capacity regressions. Feature-gated and disabled by default.
Feature flag: throughput_stability_allocator. If cutovers are blocked unexpectedly, use the kill-switch in infra/feature_flags.yaml to disable immediately. Runbook in docs/runbooks/throughput-cutover-guard.md describes manual override and post-rollback steps.
Perf-sim scenarios are in services/canary/tests/perf_sim/*.yaml. To reproduce: run perf-sim with historical_trace=2025-11-23 and inject negative throughput deltas at 5%-20% magnitude. Expected detection within 45s on medium cohorts.

payload.body:
Motivation:
We observe two correlated phenomena under multi-tenant mixed workloads: (1) high fragmentation inside the KV cache leading to lower effective residency and more frequent paging; (2) bursty spill/paging activity where multiple tenants or background workers simultaneously trigger large rewrites, creating I/O storms that spike tail latency. Existing heuristics (occupancy, LRU age) are insufficient to capture region-level fragmentation patterns or to coordinate background rewrite activity across tenants.

Summary of changes (single-string description):
- Introduce an entropy-aware region scorer (kv/region_entropy.rs, kv/allocator/entropy_score.cpp): computes a lightweight entropy metric for slab/region fragmentation based on occupancy histogram + scatter metric; used to prioritize rewrite candidates that yield the highest compaction benefit per byte rewritten.
- Add a soft-spill coordinator (kv/spill_coordinator.go, runtime/scheduler/spill_coordinator.cpp): a cross-tenant cooperative controller that sequences background rewrites and spillbacks using budget windows and global backpressure signals to avoid concurrent heavy I/O.
- Implement incremental page-sieve rewrites (kv/rewrite_engine.cc): opportunistic, low-priority rewrites that run in short time-slices and prefer high-entropy regions with warm hot-set affinity to reclaim contiguous pages without blocking foreground operations.
- Expose tuning knobs in the config plane and console (console/config_schema.yaml): entropy threshold, rewrite_window_ms, per-tenant soft_spill_budget, global_backoff_alpha.
- Add unit and e2e tests; add microbench harness measuring rewrite throughput and tail-latency under synthetic workloads.

Commits (high-level):
- commit 1: introduce RegionEntropy struct and histogram collector + unit tests (kv/region_entropy.rs).
- commit 2: incremental rewrite engine & low-priority scheduler integration (kv/rewrite_engine.cc, scheduler/*).
- commit 3: soft-spill coordinator with budget windows and global backpressure signal (kv/spill_coordinator.go, runtime/scheduler).
- commit 4: console knobs, docs, and tests; benchmark results.

Files/areas changed (high level):
- kv/region_entropy.rs (new), kv/rewrite_engine.cc (new), kv/spill_coordinator.go (new)
- runtime/scheduler/* (integration hooks), console/config_schema.yaml (tuning knobs)
- tests/kv/entropy_rewrite_test.go, perf/bench/rewrite_throughput.py

Design notes / rationale:
- Entropy metric: instead of complex compaction cost modeling, the entropy score approximates fragmentation by measuring occupancy variance across fine-grained buckets inside a region plus a scatter factor that penalizes small, widely distributed live objects. This gives a cheap, monotonic score that correlates with compaction benefit in our internal traces.
- Soft-spill coordination: background rewrites are low priority but still cause I/O. The coordinator imposes a global budget window (ms per second) and sequences rewrites across tenants; a simple exponential backoff (global_backoff_alpha) increases delay when I/O queues exceed thresholds. This avoids synchronized rewrite waves following a GC or failure recovery.
- Incremental rewrites: rewriter runs as micro-slices to respect latency SLOs. When it picks a region, it writes only the contiguous hot ranges that reduce page fragmentation most per byte written.

Benchmarks (summary):
- Setup: 8-GPU dedicated cluster, mixed tenant workload (30% writes, 70% reads), 100k keys per tenant, skewed Zipf(1.2).
- Baseline: previous heuristic (LRU + occupancy)
- Results: median p50 tail token latency unchanged (~12ms), p95 reduced from 45ms to 32ms, p99 reduced from 210ms to 150ms under sustained background rewriter load. Effective cache residency +8% on average (same memory) and background rewrite I/O bursts reduced by ~60% measured as peak MB/s. Rewrite throughput cost increased by ~12% CPU but stayed within budget due to micro-slicing.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests for entropy scoring and rewrite invariants added.
- Integration tests simulate tenant waves and verify coordinator prevents simultaneous large rewrites across tenants.
- Perf canary: feature gated by console flag; staged rollout to Dedicated clusters with per-tenant budget defaults conservative (soft_spill_budget=10ms/s).
- Migration: no on-disk format changes; runtime will fall back to legacy path if coordinator disabled.

Review thread (highlights):
- Diego Morales: "Nice metric — can you add a short doc snippet describing entropy correlation with compaction gain? Also please ensure the scorer is cheap on the hot path."
  - Author reply (Ava): "Added doc comment and a micro-benchmark; scorer uses 1 atomic per region and amortized histogram updates, see kv/region_entropy.rs. Benchmarks show <1% overhead on hot-path write tail in our microbench."
- Ethan Park: "Concern: global budget might starve low-priority but high-ROI rewrites during sustained heavy load. How do we prevent starvation?"
  - Author reply: "Coordinator uses a two-tier window: guaranteed_min_ms (per tenant) + shared_pool that is fairly allocated by ROI-weighted tokens. Added tests to ensure minimum progress for each tenant."
- Priya Nair: "CI flake was a transient file handle limit in perf harness; reran and passed."

CI details:
- Unit tests: pass
- Integration tests: pass
- Perf bench: flaky on first run (fd exhaustion), rerun passed
- Lint: pass

Migration / compatibility:
- No data format changes; feature is opt-in via console flag and config. For Private installs, default is off to allow controlled enablement by SRE.

Operational notes:
- Monitoring: added metrics kv.region_entropy.score_distribution, kv.softspill.coordinator.tokens_used, kv.rewriter.slice_duration_ms. Added alert when coordinator backoff > 5s for >3m.

Follow-ups (listed in PR body):
- ENG-9021: integrate entropy score into eviction policy for tenant-prioritized retention.
- ENG-9105: experiment with guided compaction that considers kernel-level page alignment for better OS-level collapse.

Merge outcome:
- Approved by reviewers after two rounds of feedback. CI green after rerun. Squash-merged into main on 2026-02-26.

Notes for on-call / SRE: if you observe elevated rewrite CPU or unexpected I/O, disable the coordinator via console toggle (soft_spill_enabled=false) and the system will revert to legacy per-node background rewrites.

Introduces an entropy-driven compaction heuristic and a cooperative soft-spill coordinator to smooth paging spikes and reduce fragmentation; improves p50/p95 latency under mixed workloads and reduces background I/O storms.
payload.title: KV: entropy-aware region rewrite and soft-spill coordinator to reduce fragmentation and page storms

payload.body:
Context: Over the last 3 weeks we've seen transient latency spikes in several regions during short-term autoscaler churn and model warmup windows. Those spikes caused the tenant SLO enforcer to escalate to circuit state and eviction before transient load and warmup completed, resulting in customer-visible errors and unnecessary failovers. This PR introduces two coordinated fixes: 1) a SLO Grace Period Manager that tracks short-lived SLO breaches with a decaying credit window and only surfaces enforcement actions after a configurable sustained breach threshold; 2) a lightweight Ephemeral Warmup soft-weight which temporarily raises the tolerance for newly scheduled or recently-warmed backends so they aren't penalized while their KV caches and JIT paths populate.

Summary of changes: Introduces new runtime component (grace_period_manager) implemented in runtime/slo/grace_period_manager.go with a small in-memory sliding-credit store per-tenant and per-region. Adds an API hook for the enforcer to query transient breach state before flipping circuits. Adds a warmup label to node metadata and a soft-weighting function in scheduler/weighting.go that decays over a warmup window (default 30s). Adds feature-flag gate (feature.slo_grace_period) and canary rollout config (deploy/overlays/us-west-2/canary.yaml). Instrumentation: new metrics redwood.slo.grace_window_credit{tenant,region}, redwood.slo.warmup_weight, and events for grace_period_expiry and grace_period_persisted. Rolling upgrade plan: canary in us-west-2 (10% of serving fleet), monitor error-rate and activation_rate metrics for 2h, then 50%/100% if safe. Backout: toggle feature.slo_grace_period=false will revert behavior immediately and flush in-memory credits on restart.

Why this approach: Previous fixes focused on aggressive eviction and conservative failover; they either tolerated bad latency for too long or acted too fast. Using a decaying credit window provides a low-cost, stateless-ish mechanism to distinguish short spikes from sustained regressions without requiring long-term historical storage. Ephemeral warmup weighting reduces false positives during normal autoscaler activity and model cold starves during scale-up.

Testing: unit tests for credit decay and xor-edge removal in runtime/slo/grace_period_manager_test.go; integration test in perf-canary harness that simulates bursty autoscaler events (tests/perf/autoscale_burst_slo_test.go). Local perf-lab run measured reduction of reactive-evictions by ~78% in synthetic warmup scenarios. CI showed one flaky e2e related to test harness timing; that test was stabilized and re-run. QA verification checklist included: canary traffic ramp, metric thresholds validated, do-not-evict tag respected.

Rollout and monitoring: Canary deploy via overlays with feature flag. Dashboard: dashboards/slo/grace-period-overview.json contains target panels. Alerts to watch: SLO.Enforcer.SustainedBreachRate > 0.5% for 10m (post-deploy), Serving.Evictions > baseline + 3 sigma. On anomalies, immediate rollback by disabling feature.slo_grace_period or scaling canary group to zero.

Related: ENG-3421 (primary work item), ENG-3499 (follow-up for persistent store option), SUP-7842 (customer incident).
Ethan Moore: Can we make the decay window configurable per-tenant? If so, add a connector to tenant config and default to global setting.
Aisha Patel: replied: added tenant override hook and ensured global default remains 30s. Documented behavior in runbook.
Sofia Chen: Concern about memory growth for large tenant cardinality — can we bound entries?
Aisha Patel: replied: implemented LRU cap with eviction and metrics; added unit tests to validate cap behavior.
