Summary: Adds an 'Econ Onramp' pathway to ship small-tenant friendly defaults for batching and prefix caching plus a lightweight, conservative quantization autoscaler ('lite-quant') with telemetry-driven rollouts and safety gates. Motivation: Many small customers and PoCs waste cost due to conservative global defaults or risky one-size-fits-all quantization suggestions. This patch provides a low-friction starter configuration that safely reduces per-token cost, gives clear opt-in via CLI/console, and exposes unit-econ telemetry so SRE/Product can monitor regressions. Scope: config presets, simple autoscaler service, CLI opt-in flag, server-side safety checks, telemetry and eval hooks, and docs/examples for onboarding. Not included: full tenant-customization UI and multi-tenant quota enforcement (follow-ups planned). Checklist: [x] presets for batch_size/cache_ttl/kv_prefill; [x] lite-quant autoscaler with snapshot-based conservatism; [x] canary rollout wiring and A/B assignment; [x] telemetry for unit-econ and quality regressions; [x] CLI flag and quickstart example; [x] docs and changelog entries. Risk notes: Lite-quant is conservative by design (no forced re-quantize on production without manual tenant opt-in), quality measurement hooks are required on tenant side for aggressive ramps. How it works (high-level): 1) Onramp presets: a small JSON config shipped under /configs/econ_onramp.json that suggests batch target ranges, cache TTL defaults, and a prefill strategy optimized for short-sequence OLTP workloads; 2) Lite-quant autoscaler: stateless controller that watches sampled inference traces and suggests a quant-tier for tenant traffic with a confidence score; suggestions are stored as draft profiles that require tenant CLI/console approval or an explicit opt-in flag for automatic application; 3) Safety: server-side validators simulate a short shadow-run with the suggested quant tier on a sampled subset and compare token-level perplexity proxy and smoke-test prompts before applying to production; fallback to higher-precision variant if any regression exceed thresholds; 4) Telemetry: new unit_econ metrics (cost_per_k_token, latency_p95_by_quant, quality_probe_failures) and alert thresholds. Merge outcome: squash-merged to main after two approvals and green CI; canary staged to 10% tenants for 48h before global opt-in promotion. Release notes: new 'Econ Onramp' starter profiles and `--econ-onramp` CLI flag; lite-quant autoscaler in beta behind a feature gate; telemetry metrics and alerting dashboards added. Follow-ups: UI to review suggested quant tiers, tenant-level tuning CLI, expand preset coverage for long-sequence workloads, automated rollback playbooks.
Marco Li: Left a few nits on naming and suggested making the safety thresholds configurable via per-tenant policy. Also asked for more explicit logs for shadow-run failures.
Author (Asha): Addressed naming nits and added policy plumbing; exposed SAFETY_QUANT_DELTA env var and added structured logs for shadow-run comparisons.
Sofia Nguyen: Approved after seeing added e2e smoke tests and dashboard wiring. Requested follow-up ticket to add UI review flow.
Daniel Park: Noted CI flake on one test run; re-ran and green. Suggested limiting default canary to 5% for specific regions; updated rollout config to support region-scoped canaries.
Introduces 'Econ Onramp' starter profiles (batching/cache defaults) and a conservative 'lite-quant' suggestion engine. Beta behind feature gate. New CLI flag --econ-onramp for tenant opt-in and telemetry metrics under unit_econ.*. Recommended for PoCs and small tenants to reduce per-token cost safely.
Squash-merged after 2 approvals; canary rollout scheduled via deployment pipeline. Feature gated under 'econ_onramp' flag; default CLI flag disabled for existing tenants.
Canary target default is 10% of eligible tenants for 48h; region-scoped canary supported via rollout config. If quality_probe_failures > 0.5% for 10m, autoscaler suggestions are paused and previous profiles restored. See observability/metrics/unit_econ.promql and telemetry runbook.
payload.title: Econ Onramp: starter batch/caching defaults and lite-quant autoscaler

Motivation: Following a recent outage reconstruction (SUP-4512) we observed an oscillation during regional rejoin where multiple nodes aggressively tried to reclaim tenant KV slots, triggering cascade redistributions and transient SLO violations. This PR introduces a short-term hotfix to: 1) introduce a gentle rejoin backoff window (per-tenant jittered delay + exponential cap) to avoid synchronized reclaims; 2) add a controlled load-trim path that softly sheds low-priority traffic during rejoin windows; and 3) emit new telemetry to make oscillation and rejoin latency visible in the Console. This change is intentionally conservative: defaults apply only during detected rejoin epochs and are disabled outside of a rejoin recovery window. Changes: - runtime/scheduler/rejoin_coordinator.go: add rejoin state machine with randomized tenant backoff and exponential cooldown logic; add tests for staggered rejoin timings. - runtime/load_trim/trimmer.go: implement priority-aware soft-trimmer that signals request proxies to shed non-critical classes via header flag and emits approximate token savings. - controlplane/telemetry/v2: add rejoin_epoch metric, tenant_rejoin_backoff_seconds histogram, and soft_trim_shed_count counter. - config/defaults.yaml: new toggle rejoin_relay.enabled (default true for this rollout window) and rejoin_relay.default_backoff_ms. - docs/ops/rejoin-playbook.md: updated playbook with diagnostic queries and rollback steps. Rollout plan: - Stage: feature gated behind rejoin_relay.enabled. - Canary: enable for 5% of tenants in us-west-2 for 2 hours, observe rejoin_epoch and token/shed metrics. - Ramp: 25% after 6 hours if no increase in 95th latency or error rate; full rollout after 24h stability. Backout: flip rejoin_relay.enabled=false; will disable new path immediately. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for coordinator state transitions - [x] e2e simulation harness run for tenant rejoin storm - [x] metrics wired to Console dashboards - [x] docs updated - [x] post-merge telemetry alert to watch for increased shed volume Monitoring and alerts: new SLO probe rule added to detect >3x baseline soft_trim_shed_count in 10m window; alert routed to SRE runbook. Notes: This is a hotfix to reduce immediate customer impact while we finalize a larger, model-aware eviction redesign. See ENG-9821 for the long-running redesign epic.
Liam Chen: Suggest capping the exponential backoff at 30s to avoid long tenant cold-starts; also add a histogram bucket for 10s-30s in tenant_rejoin_backoff_seconds.
Sofia Ramirez: Added cap to 30s and new histogram buckets in telemetry commit b3. Verified in e2e simulation.
Priya Kapoor: Code looks good. Please ensure load-trim header uses the established proxy contract (X-Redwood-Trim: soft|hard).
Sofia Ramirez: Updated trimmer to emit X-Redwood-Trim: soft and added proxy-side acceptance test.
Ethan Park: Ran canary in staging for 2h, rejoin_epoch spikes reduced and 95th latency unchanged. Approving for merge.

Motivation: Customers with varied tenant footprints asked for a guided way to pick cost/latency tradeoffs without running a full workload recorder or manual tuning. The Tenant Frugalizer Policy Wizard is an interactive backend + console flow that produces tenant-scoped defaults for batching, cache prefill, and quantization profiles based on a small synthetic probe and a set of policy goals (cost budget, p95 latency target, and quality guardrails). This PR adds the server-side orchestrator, a lightweight probe job, a policy DSL translator, and console wiring. Changes are intentionally conservative: the wizard emits recommended configs (not auto-applied) and includes a dry-run estimator to surface expected unit-econ impact. Highlights: - New service: econ-wizard-orchestrator: schedules short probe jobs, aggregates measured latency/throughput profiles, and runs a compact cost-simulator to generate ranked presets. - Probe job: a safe, bounded synthetic sampler that targets representative routes; supports warmstart and coldstart modes. - Policy DSL: simple YAML schema to express budget/latency/quality goals per-tenant and translate them into ranked candidate presets (batch_size, prefill_kv, quant_profile). - Console: new wizard UI entry and results page (draft) that shows top 3 presets and estimated cost delta and p95 impact. - Visibility: adds telemetry metrics (wizard.probe.duration, wizard.simulation.cost_delta_est, wizard.candidates.count) and trace hooks. Safety & opt-in: wizard recommendations are opt-in and accompanied by a dry-run estimator and a canary rollout guideline in the UI. The orchestration keeps probe jobs limited (< 60s per tenant by default), uses sampling rate caps, and never writes configs to tenant runtime unless explicitly confirmed. Checklist: - [x] backend orchestrator service + unit tests - [x] lightweight probe implementation + integration tests - [x] policy DSL and translator + validation - [x] dry-run cost estimator and basic simulator - [x] console wiring + initial UX copy - [x] observability metrics and traces - [x] docs draft for admin guide and safety practices Known limitations and follow-ups: - Probe currently picks up to 3 routes per tenant; future work will add weighted route selection and historical sampling. (Follow-up ENG-3250) - Simulator uses simplified CPU/GPU cost model for quick feedback; accuracy improvements tracked under ENG-3308. - UI is intentionally minimal; product will iterate on copy and rollout controls (PM-430). Backwards compatibility: no runtime defaults are changed. Wizard only stores suggestions as a tenant-scoped recommendations blob; existing serving logic remains unchanged. Migration: none required. Testing: ran end-to-end validation on staging with 12 tenants and synthetic workloads; smoke-tested canary application of a recommended preset to a non-critical tenant. CI: full unit/integration test run, lint, TypeScript compile, backend contract checks. Merge notes: squash-merged after 2 approvals. Related: references the prefab cost-sim harness in tools/econ-sim and the console UX framework change in redwood-console (see commits).
Aisha Kapoor: Left a few small nits on error handling and rate limiting; requested an explicit cap config. Miguel Santos: Asked for an additional metric to capture candidate confidence; author added wizard.candidate.confidence and updated simulator doc. Priya Nair: Approved after verifying that recommendations are opt-in and dry-run is visible in the UI. Author replies: addressed comments, added config keys for probe.timeout and probe.rate_limit, added candidate confidence metric, and extended simulator unit tests for edge cases. CI reran and passed.
Introduces the Tenant Frugalizer Policy Wizard: an opt-in guided flow to generate tenant-scoped batching, cache, and quantization recommendations based on a quick probe and cost estimator. Initial release is experimental and must be opt-in by admins.
Smoke: canary applied suggested preset to non-critical tenant; observed p95 impact within estimated bounds and cost delta within simulator error margin (~8%). No serving regressions observed in 1h stability window.
Default probe caps: probe.timeout=60s, probe.rate_limit=0.05 (5% of traffic) and probe.max_routes=3. Operators can adjust via admin config. Wizard writes recommendations to tenant.recommendations.v1 and only applies on explicit confirm. Consider tagging probe traces with tenant.id and wizard:true for easier filtering.

Context
We’ve accumulated a few FP8/INT8-related flags across the sprint (kernel integration, autoselect heuristics, and perf-canary gating). During the kickoff and variance triage we had repeated questions in Slack about:
- the canonical flag names (runtime vs runner vs perf-canary)
- which flags are safe to toggle in production vs benchmark-only
- how to stage enablement to avoid customer-impacting regressions

This PR updates internal runtime docs + flag comments so engineers and SREs can quickly find the correct knobs and the safe rollout procedure.

What’s in this PR
1) Canonical flag names + semantics (internal)
- Documented the runtime-level flags used for the FP8/INT8 sprint and clarified naming conventions.
- Added explicit “DO NOT USE in prod” notes for benchmark-only toggles.

Key flags (as documented)
- runtime.kernel_mode
  - Values: baseline | fp8 | int8 | auto
  - Notes: Prefer auto in prod; force fp8/int8 only for controlled canary/bench experiments.
- runtime.kernel_autoselect_profile
  - Values: default | fp8_int8_sprint_v1
  - Notes: fp8_int8_sprint_v1 is the new heuristics profile gated by perf canary.
- runtime.fp8.attention.enabled
  - Default: false (until canary sign-off)
  - Notes: Attention-only FP8; matmul may still be baseline/int8 depending on dispatch.
- runtime.int8.matmul.enabled
  - Default: false (until model-specific eligibility is proven)
  - Notes: Includes shape guardrails; falls back automatically when unsupported.
- runtime.quantized_kv_cache.enabled
  - Default: true
  - Notes: Alignment constraints called out; links to the relevant bugfix PR.

Perf-canary / rollout-related flags (control plane / rollout layer)
- canary.kernel_enablement.mode
  - Values: off | shadow | enabled
  - Notes: shadow compares metrics without serving customer traffic on the new path.
- canary.kernel_enablement.allowlist
  - Dimensions: model, region, sku
  - Notes: Prefer smallest viable cohort; expand by region after stability.

2) Safe rollout practices (linking to the runbook)
- Added a “Safe Rollout” section that points to the canonical Confluence runbook and summarizes the minimum steps:
  - enable behind a flag
  - start with shadow (if available) or a small cohort
  - monitor TTFT/TPOT/tokens-s, error rate, and GPU OOM/evictions
  - require an explicit rollback trigger and owner
  - expand cohort only after stable window

Confluence runbook reference
- Perf canary rollout for new kernels: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENGRUNTIME/Perf+Canary+Rollout+for+New+Kernels (source: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/perf-canary-rollout-for-new-kernels.json)

3) Docs discoverability
- Updated internal docs index to include “FP8/INT8 flags” so new oncall engineers can find it from the runtime docs landing page.
- Added cross-links to:
  - kernel autoselect heuristics PR
  - perf canary gating PR
  - benchmark methodology page (for interpreting wins/regressions)

Out of scope
- No functional runtime behavior changes.
- No changes to perf-canary threshold math; only documentation of which profiles/flags exist.

Testing
- Docs build/link-check
- Grep-based CI check that referenced flags exist in the codebase (added in this PR)

Rollout / Release notes
- Internal only. No customer-facing release notes.

Related
- ENG-7431 (release plan)
- ENG-7426 (perf canary thresholds)
- PRs: #19827 (FP8 attention integration), #19841 (INT8 matmul dispatch), #19863 (autoselect heuristics), #19896 (per model/region canary gating), #19871 (KV cache alignment edge case)

Claire Dubois: Can we be explicit about what 'auto' means (which layer decides) and how to interpret fallback? This was confusing in the kickoff thread.
Noah Patel (author): Good call — added a short paragraph under runtime.kernel_mode explaining that 'auto' delegates to runtime.kernel_autoselect_profile + dispatch guardrails, and that fallback is expected behavior (not an error) unless it violates the canary expectation.
Rafael Mendes: Please include the rollback triggers we’re using for the sprint (TTFT/TPOT deltas) and call out the owner-oncall expectation. SRE needs it in one place.
Noah Patel (author): Added a minimal 'Rollback triggers (default)' subsection with the metrics list + pointed to Confluence for exact thresholds since those are tuned per SKU/model. Also added 'must have a named owner' line.
Rina Kobayashi: Flag names look right but we should add 'benchmark-only' warnings for the runner env vars too; folks keep setting them in staging and then asking why numbers don’t match.
Noah Patel (author): Added a warning callout for BENCH_* env vars and clarified they belong to the benchmark harness/runner only (not runtime service config).
Connor O'Brien: Any concerns merging this during the RC window? Doesn’t touch runtime logic but it does touch docs CI.
Noah Patel (author): Docs CI change is additive; ran it in this PR and on latest main. Should be safe for RC.
Rina Kobayashi: Approved.
Rafael Mendes: Approved (thanks for adding rollback + owner notes).

Motivation: customers with strict data residency requirements asked for a deterministic, enforceable mechanism to pin an entire service's requests to a region+KMS shard so operator actions and data never cross jurisdictional boundaries. This PR implements a policy-level 'service region pin' that is enforced by RBAC v2 decision filters, coupled with a KMS shard affinity allocator and a compact audit sampling pipeline to keep evidence bandwidth reasonable while preserving compliance fidelity.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces a new RBAC v2 predicate (ServiceRegionPin) that is evaluated early in the policy pipeline and denies cross-region routing for services that opt-in to pinning. Policy lives under services/policy-engine/rbacv2 and is feature-flagged for staged rollout.
- Adds a KMS shard affinity allocator so KMS requests for pinned services are routed to the correct regional shard; allocator supports soft-fallback to a read-only audit-only shard if the primary is degraded.
- Implements an audit sampler with deterministic sampling by tenant cohort and variation for high-risk operations (admin/elevation events are always retained). Sampling reduces storage/ingest costs for long-running tenants while preserving required trails for audits.
- Adds migration tooling and a small migration SQL to backfill existing service metadata with region-pin annotations for services that already declared data residency in metadata.
- Exposes openapi changes and a new console hint for "Service > Deployment > Region Pin" so operators can opt-in during rollout.

Design notes:
- Policy order: ServiceRegionPin short-circuits routing decisions and is designed as a hard deny early in the evaluation chain. It emits a standardized denial reason code (RESIDENCY_PIN_VIOLATION) used by both API and observability hooks.
- KMS affinity: a lightweight shard key is derived from tenant id + service id + declared region. The allocator is conservative and will not perform cross-region promotions unless an explicit graceful-failover policy is set by Dedicated/Private customers.
- Audit sampling: deterministic hashing ensures reproducible sample windows for replay and evidence reconstruction. Admin paths, operator impersonation attempts, and KMS allocation failures are exempt from sampling.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flag behind flags.security.service_region_pin.
- Canary 1 (internal): enable for 3 internal services in staging for 48h, validate deny codes and KMS affinity logs.
- Canary 2 (beta customers): opt-in for 2 beta tenants on Dedicated, validate audit replays, and measure ingest reduction.
- Global: enable for all new services by default, existing services require explicit opt-in or migration.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for policy predicate evaluation, KMS allocator edge cases and hash determinism added.
- Integration test simulates cross-region request and expects RESIDENCY_PIN_VIOLATION. A flaky timing-based integration test was retried in CI and passed on the second run.
- Load bench validated allocator latency impact at 95th pct (sub-ms median change, 2–4ms tail in synthetic tests).

Operational/Docs:
- New operator playbook: docs/compliance/service-region-pin-playbook.md explains opt-in, audit expectations and incident runbook.
- Console hint and API docs updated so customers can see pin status and KMS shard association.

Checklist:
- [x] Design review with security and compliance (ENG-4821)
- [x] Testing (unit + integration)
- [x] Docs + console hint added
- [x] Migration script included
- [x] Feature flag gating and rollout plan included

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: accidental denial of traffic during rollout. Mitigation: feature flag + canary + explicit migration script.
- Risk: KMS outage causing pinned service failures. Mitigation: read-only audit-only shard fallback and operator-visible degraded state.

Related PRs / context: this complements recent RBAC v2 work and audit compaction efforts. See ENG-4821, SEC-170 for policy acceptance criteria.
Arjun Patel: Please document the exact guarantee of the allocator under failover—what happens on multi-region replica writes?
Maya Chen (author): Allocator will not rewrite primary region; we added explicit text in the playbook and a conservative fallback to read-only audit shard. See migration notes in the PR description.
Leah Gomez: Suggest making the denial code machine-parsable for alerting systems (e.g., use a fixed numeric code).
Maya Chen (author): Added RESIDENCY_PIN_VIOLATION as a stable string and numeric code 4501 in pkg/observability/events/denial_reasons.go. Unit tests added.
Thomas Rinehart: Integration test timing was flaky in CI; increase timeout and retry once. Also add explicit assertion that KMS shard id matches expected region in logs.
Maya Chen (author): Increased timeout and added deterministic log assertion. CI reran and passed.
Arjun Patel: Approving after validation in staging. Left a minor suggestion about telemetry labels which I recommend in a follow-up small PR.
Leah Gomez: Approved. Verified documentation and console hint UX with product.
Merge bot: All required checks passed. PR merged by squash.
- Added Service Region Pin RBAC v2 predicate to enforce service-level residency pinning.
- KMS shard affinity allocator ensures region-local KMS usage for pinned services.
- Deterministic audit sampler reduces ingest while preserving compliance evidence; admin/elevation events always retained.
- Migration script to backfill service metadata and console hint for opt-in.
Adds a compliance control to prevent cross-region routing for pinned services; KMS affinity reduces risk of key exposure across jurisdictions. No new secrets introduced. Review completed by security team (SEC-170).
1) Small telemetry follow-up to add 'region_pin=true' label to latency metrics (Arjun's suggestion). 2) Consider a lightweight operator CLI to bulk-opt services during migration for large orgs. 3) Evaluate long-term storage tiering for sampled audit events.

payload.body:
Context: We need safer, lower-latency detection and automated isolation when new model variants cause subtle regressions only visible if you consider traffic slices over time (e.g. time-of-day or chronological cohorts). Existing canary/quarantine mechanisms are good for static slices but do not express time-bound behavior or shadow-based gated isolation. This PR introduces a 'chronometric slice quarantine' primitive and a lightweight 'shadow-circuit' bridge for replaying a compact smoke of production traffic to validate hypotheses before widen/rollback.

What this PR does: implements a quarantine controller that treats slices as first-class, time-aware units. Key ideas: (1) chronometric policy windows: a slice can be quarantined for a sliding time horizon (N minutes/hours) and automatically released after telemetric criteria stabilize; (2) shadow-circuit: when suspicious signals are triggered we spin up an isolated shadow bridge that replays a selected smoke set (prefix sampling + session affordances) against the candidate model off the main path; (3) smoke replay harness: deterministic compact replay (configurable sample seeds) to reproduce errors and exercise KV-cache warm paths; (4) rollback advisor hooks: quarantine events feed the rollback advisor with provenance and small synthetic deltas to recommend immediate rollback or staged drain.

Why: improves detection and response for regressions which manifest as temporal bursts or session-coherent failures, reduces noisy full-cutrollbacks by enabling targeted quarantine and deterministic reproductions to aid SREs and on-call.

Design summary and components changed: single continuous description below. Controller and policy: rollout/controller/chronometric_quarantine.go — new controller implementing time-windowed slice locks and backoff semantics; quarantine policy objects allow window length, sample budget, and fuzz factors for early-release. Shadow bridge: integrations/shadow/circuit.go — lightweight bridge that captures a sampled prefix and forks it into a shadow lane with session stickiness and KV-warm replay. Smoke harness: telemetry/smoke/replay.go and tests under tests/integration/rollouts_smoke.yaml — deterministic replay with seed-based sampling and reproducible KV-cache priming. Rollback advisor integration: rollout/rollback_advisor.go — small adapter to transform quarantine evidence into priority suggestions. Runbook: docs/runbooks/rollouts.md updated with operational playbook and CLI commands.

Testing and verification: unit tests added for controller state transitions (stable -> quarantined -> released), e2e smoke replay test that runs shadow-circuit against a toy variant, integration manifest for canary scenarios, and a small load test verifying that shadow-circuit imposes <2% extra latency on the main path in sampled scenarios. CI: all checks green after two reruns of flaky integration tests.

Checklist: - [x] Controller implementation and unit tests - [x] Shadow bridge + replay harness - [x] Integration test manifest - [x] Runbook and CLI docs - [x] Telemetry dashboards (minimal metrics added) - [x] Rollback advisor hooks

Backward compatibility: quarantine policies are additive; existing rollout flows unchanged unless a policy is attached. No migration needed for existing customers.

How to exercise locally: make an env var ROLLUP_QUARANTINE=true and run ./devctl rollout simulate --manifest tests/integration/rollouts_smoke.yaml; to reproduce smoke replay use TELEMETRY_REPLAY_SEED=42 and inspect telemetry/trace/span ids for the shadow-circuit lane.

Notes: This PR contains behavior-sensitive surface area (quarantine auto-release). We intentionally default to conservative windows in the config and require explicit opt-in in release profiles for autoscale-heavy workloads.

Related work: complements ENG-2197 (session-anchored canaries) and ENG-2412 (shadow fidelity metrics); sup ticket SUP-4422 contains customer logs that motivated the design.
Diego Morales: Can you clarify why we need a separate shadow-circuit vs existing shadow lanes? The isolation and deterministic seeding is the main rationale — reduced blast radius for reproductions.
Ava Chen: Reply: shadow-circuit is intentionally narrow: it binds session prefixes and a compact KV priming step so replay is deterministic and safe to run repeatedly without affecting caches used by the live lanes.
Priya Suresh: Please add an opt-out flag for high-throughput customers; we risk added load if sampling not controlled.
Ava Chen: Added QUARANTINE_SAMPLE_CAP and conservative defaults; updated docs and integration manifest to make caps explicit.
Liam O'Neill: unit tests look good, integration was flaky but passed on rerun. Approving after CI stabilization.
Diego Morales: Approved and left minor nits on logging verbosity which are addressed in the last commit.
payload.title: Chronometric slice quarantine with shadow-circuit and smoke replay

Context: We observed two operational gaps during recent compliance reviews: 1) policy drift where temporary emergency RBAC allowances persisted beyond intended windows, causing noisy audits and manual cleanup; 2) lack of strong provenance metadata in audit records when KMS-wrapped operator credentials were used, which makes forensic reconstruction across multi-region KMS providers difficult. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (A) an authorization-policy safelist that lets platform teams declare short-lived, auditable allowlists for specific routes/operators with enforced TTLs and auto-expiry, and (B) a KMS provenance decorator that appends stable provenance metadata (provider, key-alias, wrapping-hash) to audit events and signs it with a dedicated service key so downstream compliance tooling can validate origin and detect cross-region wrapping mismatches.

Motivation: enable safe emergency allowances without long-term policy drift, and give compliance & SRE reliable cryptographic provenance in audit streams for incidents and periodic attestations.

Changes: - Introduced new RBACv2 safelist API surface (yaml policy snippets + runtime enforcement). Safelist entries are declared as: route, operator_set, valid_from, ttl_seconds, justification_id. - Runtime enforcer validates TTL on read; expired entries are rejected and logged as policy violations. - Admin console surface: basic UI form + staged rollout flag. This change is feature-flagged (feature.authz_safelist) and defaults to off. - KMS provenance decorator: middleware that reads KMS usage context when operator-scoped credentials (<operator-kms-token>) were used, constructs a compact provenance JSON, computes a provenance-hash, and attaches a signed envelope to the audit event (audit.provenance_envelope). The decorator supports a primary KMS and a fallback vault for HSM signing in air-gapped installs. - Added a small verification CLI (tools/kms-provenance-verify) used by compliance automation to validate envelope signatures and compare wrapping-hashes across audit windows. - Policy linter updates to warn when a safelist is created without justification_id or without explicit expiry. - Migration: This PR includes a one-time background job that scans existing temporary roles labeled "temp-emergency" and emits reconciliation suggestions as ticketed findings (Linear: ENG-4221).

Tests and validation: - Unit tests for safelist TTL, expiry handling, and linter warnings. - Integration test that simulates operator credential flow across two KMS providers and verifies the provenance envelope is present in the audit payload. - End-to-end smoke test that exercises console create/edit of safelist entry (flagged).

Rollout plan: - Stage 1 (week 0): Merge behind feature flag; run integration tests in canary. - Stage 2 (week 1): Enable feature.flag for internal platform-only orgs; run compliance validation (provenance verification) against historical audit samples. - Stage 3 (week 3): Controlled enablement for customers with dedicated capacity, opt-in.

Monitoring: new metrics added: authz.safelist.created, authz.safelist.expired, audit.provenance.envelope_count, audit.provenance.verify_failures.

Backout plan: disable feature.authz_safelist and rollback the middleware image; provenance decorator can be disabled by config.provenance.enabled=false.

payload.body:
Motivation: Services that proxy requests (edge -> ingest -> runtime) were losing tenant region assertions on the hop, causing KMS calls to use fallback providers in another geo and noisy escalations. Additionally, transient KMS error spikes caused hard failures instead of graceful degradation. Finally, RBAC v2 temporary elevation tokens issued by the operator queue had inconsistent TTL enforcement across services, increasing the window for accidental privilege retention.

This PR introduces three coordinated changes in the region-residency + crypto + auth surface: 1) a light-weight region-claim propagation cache (in the request context layer) that persists the residency/assertion header across internal retries and service handoffs; 2) a KMS soft-fallback path: on KMS provider timeout or 5xx, we attempt a controlled local-encrypt fallback using a short-lived per-node AES key from the node keystore and mark the audit entry with fallback_reason; 3) a TTL enforcer middleware for RBACv2 temporary-elevation tokens to ensure tokens are rejected if TTL drift is detected (clock skew protection and server-authoritative TTL check).

Design details: the region-claim cache is a request-scoped in-memory map keyed by tenant_id + hop_index and expires after 2 minutes by default. It is pluggable via the request-context interface so Dedicated/Private runtimes can replace with a distributed cache. KMS fallback is guarded: fallback only used when all configured providers return transient errors (timeouts, 502/503). The AES soft-encrypt key is sourced from the node keystore which itself is encrypted with the customer's CMK; we never upload plaintext keys. Audit pipeline now emits residency_cohort and fallback_reason fields for downstream analysis. RBAC TTL enforcer centralizes token TTL validation, rejects tokens with TTL > configured maximum or with drift > 30s, and logs token_origin and evaluated_at in audit.

Testing and rollout: unit tests for propagation cache, middleware, and KMS fallback harness added. Integration test harness simulates cross-region proxying and KMS timeout to assert fallback path and audit flags. Gradual rollout: feature flag region_claim_cache_v2 defaults off; KMS soft-fallback behind k_soft_fallback gate (start in staging, enable canary 5% on prod). RBAC TTL enforcer is on-by-default but has a safe-mode opt-out for older private deploys via operator-config.

Backward compatibility: headers are additive (X-Redwood-Residency, residency_cohort in audit). Fallback produces clear audit metadata so operators can detect and revert. Private installer notes included for operator-config knobs.

Related work: ENG-1942 (region assertion stability), ENG-1951 (kms error hardening), SUP-879 (customer-reported cross-region crypto errors).
Add: region-claim propagation cache for cross-service requests; Add: KMS soft-fallback path and local encrypted cache for transient failures; Add: TTL enforcement for RBAC v2 temporary elevation tokens; Improve: audit entries include residency-cohort field and failure-retry reasons.
Liam O'Connor: The RegionClaimCache looks fine but I'm concerned about memory growth on high fanout requests. Please add a max-entries guard and metrics for cache evictions.
Priya Shah: Added max_entries (default 10000) and eviction metrics (region_claim_cache.evictions) in the latest commit. Also documented the operator knob to reduce size for tiny nodes.
Marta Ruiz: KMS soft-fallback is clever but we need a clear operator-visible metric and an alert when fallback rate > 0.1% for 5m. Also add a test to ensure we never leak AES node keys in stack traces.
Priya Shah: Added fallback_rate metric and alert rule to the observability dashboard; added unit test to assert AES key zeroization on drop.
Squash-merged after approvals. Key changes: region claim cache (request-context), KMS client soft-fallback, central RBACv2 TTL enforcer, audit enrichment, operator config defaults and docs.

Context & motivation: We've seen recurring customer asks and internal playbook churn around tenant warmup, sensible batch/cache defaults, and consistent quantization profiles during rollouts. Ad-hoc scripts and manual onboarding have produced subtle unit-econ regressions (ENG-2145). This PR introduces a small, composable orchestrator (hyperseed) and a companion CLI (hyperseedctl) that: (1) seeds tenant-level default batch/cache parameters based on sample traffic shapes, (2) applies an immutable 'quant-anchor' profile to model deployment metadata to ensure predictable inference cost paths during canary rollouts, and (3) emits unit-econ telemetry events so downstream billing/forecasting can attribute warmup costs. High-level changes: - New service: src/orchestrator/hyperseed.go implements an idempotent seed flow with safe-readback and tenant-scoped locks. - CLI: cmd/hyperseedctl with 'plan/apply/dry-run' subcommands and JSON/YAML profile import. - Quant-anchor: controlled metadata blob attached to model manifests; runtime checks enforce fallback when an incompatible quant profile would be selected. - Defaults catalog: data/defaults/catalog.json (compact, balanced, latency-first presets) plus a small selector that maps traffic percentiles -> batch/cache suggestion. - Telemetry: emit econ.seed.* events and tag traces with tenant.seed.variant. - Safety & rollbacks: seed is opt-in; a 'revert' command and automatic rollback if the runtime surface error rate increases beyond threshold. What this is not: hyperseed is not an autoscaler replacement or a global policy engine — it's focused on seeding safe defaults and attaching quant-anchor metadata for predictable cost behavior. Implementation notes & design tradeoffs: - The orchestrator collects a short 5-minute sample of request size/seq distribution from the tenant's recent traces (or accepts a supplied sample file) and runs a lightweight heuristic to choose batch_size, prefill_window, kv_cache_retention. - Quant-anchor supports three tiers: preserved-fp16, safe-int8, compact-quant (post-training calibration suggested). Anchors are intentionally conservative to avoid quality regressions during canaries. - We added an opt-in 'economics' mode which annotates profiles with estimated tokens-per-dollar using last-7-day price curves; this is only advisory in the first rollout. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in ENG-2145 - [x] CLI with plan/apply/dry-run/revert - [x] Runtime guard to refuse incompatible quant anchors - [x] Telemetry + basic dashboards (prefill heatmap, econ.seed trends) - [x] Unit + integration tests for idempotency + rollback plan - [x] Load tests demonstrating <2% p99 latency regression on moderate traffic Summary of test results: - Unit tests: 98% coverage on new packages. - Integration: staged on dedicated dev cluster for 48h with a synthetic mixed-load profile; CPU/GPU utilization unchanged within noise, observed warmup token cost increase of ~6% on first 10 minutes but steady-state improvement of ~3% token cost per request for low-compute tenants. - Canary: 5 tenants ran hyperseed in canary mode for 72h; no quality regressions; two tenants with heavy long-context traffic were suggested 'balanced' instead of 'compact' by the selector. How to use: - Plan: hyperseedctl plan --tenant <id> --sample sample.json - Apply (dry-run): hyperseedctl apply --tenant <id> --profile compact-warmup --dry-run - Apply: hyperseedctl apply --tenant <id> --profile compact-warmup - Revert: hyperseedctl revert --tenant <id> --since 2026-02-20 Rollback plan: - If post-seed error-rate increases >1% absolute or p99 latency degrades >10% relative for 30m, the operator-run hook will auto-trigger a revert and flag the tenant for manual inspection. Observability: - econ.seed.* metrics, new dashboard panels under Console -> Prefill -> Hyperseed. - New tags: tenant.seed.variant, tenant.seed.profile, quant.anchor.id Related work & references: - ENG-2145 (seed defaults playbook), ENG-2190 (quant anchor RFC). - Smaller companion PRs will follow to add tenant onboarding templates to the quickstarts repo. Security & compliance: - No secrets added. CLI requires operator role; RBAC checks in orchestrator code. Performance considerations: - Orchestrator runs as a low-priority job in the control plane; sampling window is configurable. - We intentionally limit per-tenant parallelism to 2 concurrent seed runs to avoid thundering. Migration notes: - Existing tenants who want to opt-in can run hyperseedctl. Nothing changes by default. - Operators can run a tenant-batch to seed on a schedule for low-touch onboarding. Open questions & next steps: - Expand quant-anchor tiers after collecting more evals. - Consider a 'shadow-apply' mode that applies defaults in the control plane but doesn't modify the runtime until confirmed.
Maya Jensen: Nice approach. Two asks: (1) add explicit idempotency unit test for double-apply, (2) expand docs with examples for long-context tenants.
Leah Park: Added double-apply test and an examples section in docs/operations/hyperseed.md (see latest commit). For long contexts we added a selector override and documented heuristics.
Ravi Patel: Left a small nits in anchor.go re error wrapping; also suggested tightening the runtime fallback logging to avoid noise. Fixed in f4a7c8e.
Carlos Ruiz: Verified telemetry keys and added dashboard links; approved once CI is green.
Adds hyperseed orchestrator and hyperseedctl CLI to seed tenant defaults and attach conservative quant-anchor profiles. Opt-in; adds telemetry for unit-econ attribution and a small dashboard. No default behavior changes. CLI and control-plane safeguards included.

Summary: Adds Playwright E2E coverage for the Console “Optimization suggestions” beta page focusing on (1) RBAC denied flows, (2) empty/insufficient telemetry states, and (3) pagination + sorting correctness for the suggestions table. Motivation: We’ve had repeated regressions during beta iteration where the Suggestions page either silently rendered empty for users lacking optimize:suggestions:read or showed the wrong empty-state CTA when telemetry lagged. This PR converts the checklist in ENG-19501 into deterministic E2E tests that run in CI and exercise the real routing/table components rather than unit-testing the view model. What’s included: - RBAC denied: verifies that a user without optimize:suggestions:read sees the access denied panel, does not fire list fetch retries, and does not emit “impression” analytics events. Also verifies that a user with project access but missing optimize scope is denied (org membership alone is insufficient). - Feature flag gating: validates that when the Suggestions beta flag is off, the navigation entry does not appear and direct navigation shows the “not enabled” state (with link to internal setup doc in non-prod builds). - Empty states: (a) “insufficient telemetry” state when API returns empty with reason=INSUFFICIENT_TELEMETRY, confirms CTA deep-links to telemetry setup page; (b) “no opportunities” state when API returns empty with reason=NO_SUGGESTIONS and telemetry_present=true; (c) stale estimate banner rendering when response includes stale_as_of older than threshold. - Pagination/sorting: asserts that query params are forwarded correctly (page_size, cursor, sort_by, sort_dir) and that the table updates deterministically when changing sort from savings_$ to risk and back. Also verifies that stable suggestion IDs are used as row keys (no row duplication when paginating). Test approach: - Uses Playwright with seeded org/project fixtures and two test users: qa-suggestions-read and qa-no-suggestions-read. RBAC is configured via test-only authz bootstrap endpoint already used by other console E2Es. - Network layer: stubs /optimize/suggestions responses with recorded fixtures for each scenario; additionally asserts request payload/params to catch UI regressions around sorting/pagination. - Flake control: avoids arbitrary timeouts; waits on explicit “table loaded” data-testid markers and ensures all fetches are resolved before snapshotting key panels. - Analytics: intercepts /events ingestion endpoint and asserts event emission (or lack thereof) for impression/expand in the allowed vs denied cases. Out of scope: validating estimator math (covered by unit tests in pr-22044) and backend RBAC enforcement (covered by API tests in pr-22026). Screenshots: attached in PR artifacts (playwright-report) for denied/empty states. Risk: low; tests only. Backward compatibility: N/A. Notes for reviewers: please focus on determinism/flake risk and whether we’re asserting the right empty-state copy/CTAs per latest design.
Kaitlyn Nguyen: Can we ensure the denied flow doesn’t emit impressions? We’ve had audit concerns about recording UI events when access is denied. Leila Farouk: Yep — added an explicit assertion that /events has zero calls for the denied user and one call for the allowed user after page load. Felix Schneider: For empty states, can we assert the reason value rather than matching copy? Copy is still moving. Leila Farouk: I’m asserting the visible state header + CTA destination, and also that the API fixture includes reason=INSUFFICIENT_TELEMETRY vs NO_SUGGESTIONS. Happy to reduce copy matching; updated to target data-testid + link href rather than exact strings. Nora Ahmed: Sorting test looks brittle; it assumes the first row is always X. Better to verify the request params + that the column sort indicator changes. Leila Farouk: Good call — refactored to assert the outgoing sort_by/sort_dir params and the aria-sort attribute on the column header; removed dependence on row order except for ensuring no duplicate IDs across pages. Dylan Brooks: Any new data-testid hooks must be stable and not leak into public docs. Leila Farouk: Added only data-testid attributes under existing patterns; no user-facing changes. Approvals: Kaitlyn Nguyen approved after analytics assertion change. Nora Ahmed approved after sorting test refactor. Felix Schneider approved. Dylan Brooks approved.

payload.body:
Motivation: Production teams have asked for a single, compact signal that captures invocation-level resilience (successful flow through phases, retries, fallbacks) so SRE and product owners can spot gradual degradation that doesn't surface in percentiles alone. This PR adds an Invocation Resilience Index (IRI) that is computed from phase success flags, retry counts, and fallback activations and exports a decayed-smoothed scalar per invocation. The goal is to provide a low-cardinality, high-signal metric for dashboards and alerting, plus a companion contextual-log coupler that attaches a small, privacy-respecting log excerpt to sampled traces for faster RCA.

What this PR does (summary):
- Introduces the IRI computation in serving/telemetry: telemetry/iri_calculator.go (proto + implementation) and an exporter to metrics pipeline (IRI gauge + histogram for distribution).
- Adds a lightweight trace enrichment microservice (trace-coupler) that joins sampled spans with tenant-permitted log excerpts and injects a compact context blob into traces. The coupler uses existing KMS-tagged retention rules to strip sensitive fields.
- New Grafana dashboard: observability/dashboards/invocation_resilience_index.json (overview, per-route rollup, cohort heatmap).
- Alert tuning: adds an alert rule (slo/resilience_degradation.rule) that uses IRI rolling quantiles and a mute policy for low-volume routes. Includes playbook docs: docs/runbooks/resilience_index_playbook.md.
- Tests: unit tests for IRI weights, end-to-end smoke test that simulates retries/fallbacks and verifies a trace enrichment payload exists for sampled traces.

Checklist:
- [x] IRI proto, computation, and exporter implemented
- [x] Trace coupler implemented with privacy filters
- [x] Dashboard and panel descriptions added
- [x] Alert and playbook committed
- [x] Unit and integration tests included
- [x] Load test (synthetic runner) validating <1% p99 overhead under baseline traffic

High-level commits:
- "add iri proto and baseline computation" (telemetry/iri.proto, telemetry/iri_calculator.go)
- "export iri to metrics pipeline and add histograms" (exporters/metrics/iri_exporter.go)
- "trace coupler: service + privacy filters" (services/trace_coupler/*)
- "dashboard and alert rules" (observability/dashboards/invocation_resilience_index.json, slo/resilience_degradation.rule)
- "tests and synthetic runner harness" (test/e2e/iri_smoke_test.go, bench/synthetic_resilience_runner)
- "fix: synthetic runner shutdown race"

Files changed (high-level):
- telemetry/iri.proto
- telemetry/iri_calculator.go
- exporters/metrics/iri_exporter.go
- services/trace_coupler/main.go
- services/trace_coupler/filter_privacy.go
- observability/dashboards/invocation_resilience_index.json
- slo/resilience_degradation.rule
- docs/runbooks/resilience_index_playbook.md
- test/e2e/iri_smoke_test.go
- bench/synthetic_resilience_runner/README.md
- ci/pipelines/iri-integration.yml
- go.mod / go.sum updates

Notes on implementation details:
- IRI computation is intentionally simple and explainable: a base score from phase successes (input parsing, kv cache lookup, kernel dispatch, response stream) with additive penalties for retries and fallbacks and a multiplicative decay based on invocation age. Weighted config is exposed via telemetry/config and can be adjusted via feature flags.
- The trace coupler subscribes to our sampling bus; when a trace is selected it performs a fast join against a ring-buffered log cache and attaches at most 5 short log lines (sanitized) and a small metadata map (route, model, kernel tag). Coupler runs in the observability namespace and respects per-tenant retention policies (implemented as filter_privacy.go).
- Dashboard shows IRI distribution, delta from baseline, per-route cohort heatmap, and a small panel with coupler-sampled traces (link to trace viewer).

CI / test history: initial CI run reported a flaky e2e failure in iri_smoke_test (random timeout on synthetic runner). Investigated and found the synthetic runner had a race in its goroutine shutdown; fixed in commit "fix: synthetic runner shutdown race". Re-ran CI: all checks passed. Integration harness ran on an isolated cluster (ci/pipelines/iri-integration.yml) and validated end-to-end enrichment at low sample rates. Load bench showed ~0.6% p99 overhead on request path when coupler sampling enabled at 0.1%.

Review conversation (high level):
- Miguel Ortega (comment): "Can you call out how this interacts with existing span sampling? I want to make sure we don't double-sample or leak extra logs for high-volume tenants."
- Asha (reply): "Coupler respects the sampling bus; we do a fast tenant-eligibility check before joining logs. I added a note in filter_privacy.go and the playbook. Also, coupler uses a per-route rate limiter."
- Claire Huang (requested changes): "The dashboard needs clearer labels for the decay window and a toggle for cohort vs route aggregation. Please add panel descriptions and default thresholds in the JSON so PMs understand what's being shown."
- Asha (commit): "docs(dashboard): add panel descriptions + default thresholds" (observability/dashboards/invocation_resilience_index.json)
- Samir Gupta (approval): "Implementation looks good; tests cover weight tuning and the privacy filters suffice for now. Approving after CI green."

Approvals: Miguel Ortega approved (comment + suggestions addressed), Samir Gupta approved, Claire Huang approved after dashboard tweaks.

Merge: squashed and merged into main via squash merge (merge_method: squash). Merge commit message: "Introduce invocation resilience index and trace coupler — adds metric, dashboard, alert, and trace enrichment (A. Patel)"

Operational runbook & follow-ups:
- Runbook (docs/runbooks/resilience_index_playbook.md) includes mitigation steps: temporarily lowering weight of fallback penalty, disabling coupler sampling per-tenant, and an automated throttler runbook.
- Follow-ups filed: ENG-3120 (expose IRI per-model variant in dedicated), ENG-3180 (add ingestion-side aggregation to reduce metric cardinality for per-route histograms).

Risks and mitigations:
- Privacy: coupler strictly enforces retention rules and redaction before attaching logs. We added a short audit log when coupler attaches context to a trace.
- Cost: additional exporter and coupler add CPU; we measured and kept overhead under 1% for default sampling. We will enable gradual rollout by feature flag only for orgs with volume above threshold.

If you want to run locally: see bench/synthetic_resilience_runner/README.md for how to simulate a mix of successful, retry, and fallback invocations and validate the IRI metric series and trace enrichment payloads.
- Add Invocation Resilience Index metric and dashboard
- Ship a log/trace coupling service to attach contextual snippets to sampled traces
- New alerting recipe: resilience-degradation-critical with auto-mitigation playbook
Rolled out to canary tenant group (5% of traffic) for 48h with no alerts. Will monitor IRI drift and adjust thresholds next week.
If the IRI alert fires for a route, reduce fallback_penalty in telemetry/config or disable coupler sampling for that tenant, then assess trace-sampled payloads via the dashboard links.

payload.body:
Motivation: Prefill-heavy workloads still exhibit GPU stalls when large prefill windows block decode progress for shorter requests. Existing speculative approaches either overfetch KV state or serialize stages too conservatively, wasting throughput. This change introduces two coordinated mechanisms: (1) a microbatch interleaver scheduler that interleaves small prefill microbatches with decode work to reduce idle GPU time, and (2) a KV primer hint that conditionally prefetches KV entries only for sequences predicted to need them soon. The design balances latency and memory pressure and is configurable per-route.

What this PR does (single-line continuous description): Adds Scheduler::MicrobatchInterleaver, an interleaving policy that slices prefill windows into microbatches and opportunistically schedules decode kernels between slices; introduces kv_primer hint propagation from request admission through scheduling to the runtime kernel selector; implements a predictive prefetch heuristic (sequence-length + remaining budget) that gates KV priming; introduces guards to limit concurrent primer memory usage; updates runtime kernel selection to accept primer hints and avoid eager KV expansion for low-probability sequences.

Commits summary: [commit 1] introduce microbatch interleaver scheduler and unit tests; [commit 2] add kv_primer hint plumbing and API surface; [commit 3] predicitive prefetch heuristic and memory guard; [commit 4] runtime kernel changes to honor primer hints and avoid eager KV expansion; [commit 5] integration tests and perf canary config; [commit 6] address reviewer feedback and add stress test for memory regression.

Files/areas changed (high level): src/scheduler/microbatch_interleaver.cc/h, src/scheduler/policy_registry.cc, src/runtime/kernel_selector.cc, src/runtime/kv_primer.cc/h, src/serving/route_config.cc (new per-route config flags), integrations/perf/canaries/microbatch-interleaver.yaml, tests/scheduler/microbatch_interleaver_test.cc, tests/runtime/kv_primer_integration_test.cc. Small edits: docs/observability.md (added notes about new per-route metric microbatch.interleave.ratio) and examples/quickstarts/microbatch-config.yaml.

Backward compatibility and flags: Feature guarded behind runtime config microbatch_interleaver.enabled (default: false). KV primer is off by default and enabled via route-level config kv_primer.mode = "conditional". No changes to public API or client SDKs. Migration: operators can flip the flags and tune microbatch_interleaver.max_microbatch_tokens and kv_primer.memory_limit_mb.

Performance results: Internal perf canary on T4-like nodes with mixed workloads (60% short requests <= 32 tokens, 40% long prefill requests) showed: p50 generation latency -7%, p95 -12% on mixed traffic; effective throughput increased ~8% for the same GPU pool; small memory increase at peak when kv_primer enabled (+4% RSS) but within configured limits. Deterministic unit tests added and integration stress harness to detect KV memory regressions.

Testing: Unit tests for scheduler heuristics and priority inversion cases; integration tests simulating interleaved prefill/decode streams; added perf canary (microbatch-interleaver) which runs nightly and reports microbatch.interleave.ratio and kv_primer.hit_rate. CI: all checks green after rerun (one flaky test in mem-monitor was retried and passed).

Review conversation (selected entries): Reviewer Aisha: "Can we make the heuristic more conservative when route concurrency is high? I saw a spike in RSS on one run." Author: "Added kv_primer.memory_limit_mb and conservative scaling based on concurrency; tests included in last commit." Reviewer Marta: "Please add a fallback to disable interleaving for very large prefill batches to avoid excessive kernel churn." Author: "Added microbatch_interleaver.max_microbatch_slices and early-exit if slice_count > 16; documented in route_config." Reviewer Ravi: "Nit: rename primer -> kv_primer for clarity in logs." Author: "Renamed; updated metrics and docs." Reviewer Aisha (approve): "Looks good after memory guard and test additions." CI bot: "mem-monitor flaky; rerun job passed."

Known limitations and follow-ups: The sequence-length predictor is simple (based on prompt length + model-specific token ratio) — follow-up ENG-4689 will explore a learned predictor and cross-request batching hints. Also plan to add a telemetry-driven autoscaler that adjusts the microbatch slice size based on observed interleave ratio.

Security and telemetry: No new surface for customer data; kv_primer only touches model-internal KV entries and does not persist customer data. Added microbatch.interleave.ratio and kv_primer.hit_rate metrics to help ops tune configs.

Merge: Squash-merged into main after approvals and CI green. Merged-at: 2026-03-02.

Elliot: Added kv_primer.memory_limit_mb and conservative scaling based on concurrency; tests included.
Marta: Please add a fallback to disable interleaving for very large prefill batches to avoid excessive kernel churn.
Elliot: Added microbatch_interleaver.max_microbatch_slices and early-exit if slice_count > 16; documented in route_config.
Ravi: Nit: rename primer -> kv_primer for clarity in logs.
Elliot: Renamed; updated metrics and docs.
Aisha: Approve after memory guard and test additions.

payload.body:
Motivation: progressive rollouts frequently hit cross-slice state thrash and KV cache invalidation when small changes are routed broadly. This PR introduces traffic tiling with slice affinity and an autorestore reconciliation to contain regressions to narrowly scoped traffic tiles and automatically restore healthy routes when transient regressions resolve. Design summary: 1) Tiling engine that slices traffic by request fingerprint and route hints so user sessions are routed to a deterministic tile; 2) Slice affinity heuristics prefer colocated KV cache warm slices to reduce cold-start token overhead; 3) Autorestore controller that tracks slice health signals (latency p50/p95, error rate, inference SLO) and performs staged restores with cooldown windows and rate-limited step increases; 4) Safety gates integrated with existing rollout controller: metric gates, canary holdpoints, and manual abort signals. Implementation highlights: added a new tile reconciliation loop in services/rollout/controller/tiling_controller.go, a Python slicer library with unit tests at pkg/orchestrator/slicer.py and pkg/orchestrator/slicer_test.py, helm-configurable feature flag via charts/redwood/templates/tiling-configmap.yaml, and an e2e scenario in tests/integration/tiling_e2e.yaml that exercises partial-restore and abort scenarios. Testing and CI: unit tests added, integration e2e added; one flaky e2e test required a rerun during CI and was stabilized by adding a deterministic seed to the request generator. Migration and rollout notes: feature gated by traffic_tiling=false by default. To enable in Dedicated or Private, set tiling configmap and prewarm KV caches for low-latency slices. Rollout playbook appended to docs/rollouts/traffic-tiling-slice-affinity.md. Backwards compatibility: non-tiling routes fall through to existing routing. Related work: references ENG-7421 for slice affinity heuristics and ENG-7590 for autorestore reconciliation engine.
Marina Gomez: Nice approach Priya. Two quick asks please add a unit test that covers concurrent reconcile on the same slice and document the expected backoff behavior in the controller.
Priya Raman: Added concurrent reconcile unit in slicer_test and clarified backoff and jitter behavior in code comments and docs.
Liam O'Connor: Can we add an opt-in telemetry label for slices so customers can correlate cost and latency per tile? Also please confirm memory overhead per worker when tiling is enabled.
Priya Raman: Added telemetry label traffic.tile_id and added memory budget config in tiling-configmap. Measured peak per-worker additional RSS ~18MB in our perf lab with 32KB average payload.
Introduce traffic tiling with slice affinity and autorestore to improve progressive rollout safety. Feature is opt-in behind traffic_tiling flag. Includes docs and helm toggle. See ENG-7421 and ENG-7590 for follow-ups.
payload.title: Traffic tiling with slice affinity and autorestore for safe progressive rollouts

payload.body:
Context: under production traffic shapes with long-tailed KV access patterns we observed recurring starvation of low-volume cohorts inside the continuous batcher. Existing admission and slot reservation prevent overtakes but do not address cohorts that slowly accumulate 'stuck' requests because they never hit a favorable batch alignment. Motivation: reduce 99p and tail variance without raising median latency or increasing GPU memory churn. This PR implements a deferred cohort rebalancer that periodically reshuffles low-throughput cohorts into transient priority lanes and applies a capped fast-path kernel hint to shorten their service time, combined with conservative KV-cache pin damping to avoid thrashing.

What this change does (summary):
- Add redwood/pkg/scheduler/cohort_rebalancer.go: core algorithm that tracks cohort age, recent dispatch misses, and fairness score; triggers deferred reassignments when a cohort's starvation_score exceeds a threshold.
- Introduce a lightweight priority lane (continuous-batcher:lane_deferred) that accepts small micro-batches pulled from aged cohorts; these lanes use a short-ttl kernel hint that prefers single-token dispatch paths to lower per-request overhead.
- Modify redwood/pkg/kv/cache_pin.go to add exponential decay to pin weights for cohorts that are temporarily escalated to the deferred lane, preventing long-term cache eviction churn.
- Add instrumentation hooks and metrics: cohort_rebalance.count, cohort_rebalance.latency_gain, cohort_rebalance.pin_decay.events. These feed into existing per-route dashboards.
- Add integration test bench redwood/cmd/bench/continuous_batcher_deferred_test.go and an ops rollout doc docs/ops/cohort_rebalance_rollout.md.

Design notes:
- The rebalancer runs asynchronously and is conservative by default: initial thresholds are tuned to only trigger when a cohort has been delayed for >150ms beyond its expected dispatch window and has at least N=3 outstanding requests. This avoids moving transient spikes.
- To avoid prioritization inversion, a global budget caps concurrent deferred-lane capacity to 6% of GPU slots per worker; the scheduler will drain lanes before creating new deferred micro-batches.
- Kernel hinting is opt-in per model via model manifest; default off for safety. When enabled, hinting picks a lightweight kernel path (reduced kv prefetch, contiguous attention path) that reduces single-request overhead but may slightly lower throughput for very large batches.

Testing and benchmarking:
- Unit tests: 28 new unit tests covering starvation scoring, decay math, and lane lifecycle.
- Integration: rerunnable bench harness replicates production skew (90/10 hot/cold key split) across 4 replicates. Results: 99p latency reduced by 25-40% on KV-heavy scenarios; median latency change within +/-3%. CPU/GPU and KV cache eviction traces show reduced pin churn when decay is enabled.
- Canary rollout plan: staged rollout on Dedicated pools with feature flag redwood.scheduler.deferred_rebalancer, 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 72h with automated rollback if 99p latency regresses >10% or error rate increases by >0.5%. See docs/ops/cohort_rebalance_rollout.md.

Related: ENG-2468 (continuous batching SLA hardening), ENG-2471 (kv-cache pin stability).

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed by runtime team
- [x] Benchmarks attached and reproducible in bench harness
- [x] Unit and integration tests added
- [x] Rollout plan included

Notes: This is intentionally conservative; follow-up PR planned to add adaptive threshold tuning based on live latency signals and to expose knob controls in the Console for enterprise tenants.
Introduce a deferred cohort rebalancer to improve fairness and reduce request starvation in continuous batching. Microbenchmarks show 25-40% reduction in 99th percentile latency under heavy skewed KV-heavy workloads.
Liam Chen: Could you add a guard for models with extremely large attention memory so the kernel hint doesn't regress throughput? — Addressed: added model-manifest opt-in and a runtime size check.
Priya Nair: Need more visibility into cache pin decay parameters for SRE teams. — Addressed: exposed decay alpha and ttl via metric tags and docs/ops page.
Diego Alvarez: Is the 6% slot cap empirical? Would like a link to microbench results. — Reply: yes, included bench results in the PR; cap is conservative and will be adjustable via runtime flag.
payload.title: Deferred cohort rebalancer: reduce starvation in continuous-batching under skew

Context: As we move Dedicated burst capacity through beta → GA, CS and customers need a consistent, auditable report they can pull (or receive on a schedule) that answers: (1) how much burst they used, (2) when they hit peaks, and (3) why they were denied. This PR adds a small reporting pipeline in the control plane that generates per-tenant burst usage exports (CSV + JSON), stores them in our reporting bucket, and exposes them via an RBAC-protected API used by Console + internal CS tooling. The report is time-windowed (daily by default; weekly optional), includes region/hardware segmentation, and aggregates by denial reason code. Key outputs: burst GPU-seconds and tokens (from metering), peak burst ratio vs baseline (from tenant config + runtime usage), denial counts/rates by reason (e.g., FLEET_SAFETY_CAP, TENANT_BURST_CAP, COOLDOWN_ACTIVE, POOL_SATURATED, TELEMETRY_LAG_GUARD), and top peak windows (15m buckets). Scheduling: a new scheduled job runs at 00:20 UTC daily; backfill endpoint supports on-demand export for a given window (guarded). Storage: reports are written to s3://redwood-reporting-prod/burst-usage/v1/{tenant_id}/{yyyy}/{mm}/{dd}/... with server-side encryption and a 90-day retention lifecycle rule (configurable). Access: GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/reports/burst-usage?start=...&end=... returns metadata + a short-lived signed URL; Console shows "Download report" and internal CS tool can fetch via the same endpoint. Security/compliance: adds audit events for report generation and download, and ensures tenant_id scoping + support read-only role gating. Observability: emits report generation duration, failures, and export size metrics; adds a dashboard panel link in the runbook. Notes: This intentionally does not introduce email delivery in v1 (CS asked for it; we can add later once we align on templates + unsubscribe policy).
GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/reports/burst-usage (list report artifacts for a time window; returns signed download URLs)
POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/reports/burst-usage:export (on-demand export/backfill; support/admin only; rate-limited)
Job runs daily at 00:20 UTC; retries with exponential backoff; hard timeout 10m per tenant/window.
If metering aggregates are delayed > 30m, report is generated with partial_data=true and a warning in notes; next day's report will include fully reconciled numbers.
Signed URLs expire after 15 minutes; report listing endpoint returns only the metadata for authorized callers.

Context: teams saw subtle mismatch in behavior when a pipeline of token refresh, heartbeat, and stream resume interacted under high churn. Motivation: reduce auth noise, provide a single compact credential lifecycle primitive ("CredentialCompactor") that coalesces refresh calls, exposes a stable lease window, and surfaces a minimal ergonomic streaming facade that standardizes resume vs restart semantics across SDKs. What this PR does: 1) Introduces CredentialCompactor implementations in sdks/python, sdks/typescript, and sdks/go. The compactor centralizes TTL jitter, backoff damping, and a single-flight refresh that prevents refresh storms; it also exposes metrics hooks for telemetry. 2) Adds an ergonomic StreamFacade which unifies async generator/async iterator behavior (Python/TS) and the pull-based iterator for Go, with explicit resume tokens and idempotent retry semantics. 3) Harmonizes retry presets: we standardized the SDK retry weights and hedged/latency-aware defaults so cross-language behavior is consistent under the same linear test scenarios. 4) Adds 3 new end-to-end parity test suites (py/ts/go) that exercise credential handoff during stream preemption, token rotation under heavy churn, and resume semantics after transient network partitions. 5) Small doc updates and examples demonstrating migrating from per-call refreshers to the compactor primitive. Design notes: the compactor is not a session store; it is lightweight, in-process, and intentionally exposes a small surface: acquire_lease(), refresh_hint(), and close(). It uses a soft lease window (lease_expiry - jitter) and singleflight semantics to ensure no concurrent outbound refreshes for the same logical credential key. StreamFacade provides two high-level behaviors: resume_if_token_present (resumes with KV cursor) and restart_clean (explicit restart that drops cached prefixes). This PR keeps the legacy lower-level hooks for backwards compatibility but marks a small set of helpers as deprecated with migration notes. Tests & CI: unit tests added for all languages, cross-sdk conformance harness validates identical traces for three canonical scenarios, and the e2e matrix ran on GHA against a mocked control plane. CI summary: unit: pass; lint: pass (TS required minor typemap fix); typecheck: pass; integration: pass after one flaky test was retried and stabilized; e2e: pass. Migration plan: ship as minor releases for sdks (Python 1.13.0, TS 1.27.0, Go 1.8.0) and mark legacy helpers deprecated but not removed. Rollout: feature flagged on server side for a small percentage initially, with telemetry counters to detect increased refresh latency or unexpected rejection rates. Backward compatibility: compat shim keeps previous per-call refresh working; most customers can opt-in to compactor by replacing the token provider with the compactor wrapper. Security: compactor integrates with existing KMS/HSM token unwrap code paths; no new secrets are persisted. Implementation highlights: Python: sdks/python/redwood/auth/compactor.py (CredentialCompactor class), sdks/python/redwood/stream/facade.py (async generator wrapper), tests: tests/e2e/parity/test_compactor_parity.py. TypeScript: sdks/typescript/src/auth/compactor.ts (compactLease, singleFlightRefresher), sdks/typescript/src/stream/facade.ts (AsyncGeneratorFacade), tests: tests/integration/compactor-parity.spec.ts. Go: sdks/go/auth/compactor.go (Compactor), sdks/go/stream/facade.go (PullIterator facade), tests: internal/e2e/compactor_parity_test.go. Commits: see commits list below. Files changed: see changed_files list below. Review conversation summary: initial review flagged two things: (a) TS type export leakage where an internal symbol was accidentally exported; (b) potential deadlock in Go compactor when Close() races with an in-flight refresh. Both were addressed: TS fix narrowed exports and added an extra type alias for the public surface; Go fix added cancelation propagation and a small lock ordering rework. Final reviewers approved. Merge: squash and merge after green CI. Why this is different from previous auth/retry work: instead of only synchronizing retry presets or token handoff, this PR consolidates the lifecycle orchestration pattern (coalescing refresh) into an intentionally small primitive and pairs it with a standard stream consumer facade across languages, improving developer ergonomics and making parity tests less brittle. Known limitations: compactor is in-process and therefore does not handle multi-process credential caching (future follow-up will add a sidecar/shared cache pattern); resume behavior assumes models that support cursor resume semantics; some older examples using per-call refreshers might require small adapter code. Related: ENG-3421 (investigate refresh storms), ENG-3490 (parity test plan). Merge method: squash and merge. 
Adds a lightweight credential compactor and ergonomic streaming facade across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs; improves auth/retry parity and adds conformance tests. No public API breaking changes; minor version bumps planned for each SDK.
Liam Chen: Nice consolidation. Question: will compactor introduce any additional memory retention for long-lived processes? Please document expected memory footprint and lifecycle. (addressed)
Priya Kapoor: TS type leak - some internal types were exported from src/auth/index.ts. Please narrow exports. (addressed in d4e6f7a)
Diego Martinez: Go Close() potential deadlock when context cancels during in-flight refresh; add test to reproduce and fix. (added repro and fixed in e5f7a98)
Liam Chen: Suggest adding a telemetry tag for 'compactor.singleflight.misses' to quickly detect config regressions. (added)
payload.title: Multi-SDK credential compactor + ergonomic stream facade (py/ts/go) and parity test suite

Motivation: enterprise customers requested an explicit operator consent flow for delegated operator roles and stronger KMS provenance signals in audit logs to satisfy compliance reviews. This PR introduces an operator consent bridge (a lightweight policy and cache that records short-lived operator approvals tied to a tenant and operation signature) and a KMS audit funnel that tags forwarded audit events with provenance headers and a dedupe key to reduce downstream duplication. Key design points: consent entries are scoped to (tenant, operator, action, resource) with TTL and revocation hooks; consent checks are introduced as a middleware early in the request path to avoid expensive KMS calls when denied; KMS audit funnel accepts batched audit payloads, attaches kms_provenance and audit_dedupe_id, and forwards to audit-forwarder service with exponential backoff and idempotency. Backwards compatibility: defaults are disabled via feature flags enable_operator_consent=false and kms_audit_funnel_mode=passthrough. Migration: when enabled, an onboarding job seeds consent cache from operator-approvals table and a one-time audit backfill tags recent events. Checklist: [x] policy model and schema, [x] middleware and cache, [x] KMS header enrichment, [x] audit funnel with dedupe, [x] unit+integration tests, [x] e2e with audit-forwarder in staging, [x] docs + console toggle. Testing plan: unit tests for policy matching, load test for consent cache under 10k req/s, integration test verifying audit envelope includes kms_provenance header, manual compliance review with security team. Related: ENG-1422 and SEC-87 for design review.

Sofia Patel: Added a leaky-bucket based circuit breaker and instrumentation. See audit/kms_funnel.go lines where backoff is applied. Marked in tests.
Aisha Gomez: Policy model looks good but needs explicit deny precedence in the matcher; a later allow should not override an earlier deny for the same scope.
Sofia Patel: Adjusted matcher to short-circuit on deny and added unit tests that assert deny precedence.
Marcus Rivera: Approve after CI green. Minor nit: please add a log field for consent_cache_hit to the middleware tracing.
Sofia Patel: Added tracing tag consent_cache_hit=true/false and incremented a metric (consent.cache.hit/miss).
Aisha Gomez: Security review completed; ensure the KMS provenance header is signed and includes minimal PII.
Adds an operator consent bridge to allow short-lived delegated operator approvals and a KMS audit funnel that enriches forwarded audit records with kms_provenance and dedupe ids. Disabled by default behind feature flags. Config: enable_operator_consent, kms_audit_funnel_mode. See docs/security/operator-consent.md for enablement and migration steps.
Introduces additional audit metadata (kms_provenance, audit_dedupe_id) that improves non‑repudiation and reduces duplication. Consent cache stores TTL-limited operator approvals; data stored is tenant+operator+action+resource and is encrypted at rest. KMS headers are HMAC-signed with service KMS key to prevent tampering.
