Context: Kernel auto-selection v2 relies on stable, explainable feature signals. This PR adds a lightweight model-family classifier that produces a canonical `model_family` + `arch_tags` from the loaded model config/metadata and threads that signal into the selector rules. The classifier is designed to be deterministic, cheap (no weights inspection), and resilient to common finetune/variant naming patterns. Summary of changes: (1) Introduce `ModelFamily` enum (LLAMA, MISTRAL, QWEN2, GEMMA, UNKNOWN) and `ArchTags` (e.g., `rope`, `gqa`, `moe`, `sliding_window`, `long_context`) derived from config fields such as `model_type`, `architectures`, `rope_scaling`, `num_key_value_heads`, and attention impl hints. (2) Add normalization and variant handling: recognize common finetune prefixes/suffixes ("-instruct", "-chat", "-it", "-sft"), vendor forks ("vicuna", "openhermes", "nous", "dolphin"), and local registry names; prefer explicit config fields over string matching; fall back to UNKNOWN if signals disagree. (3) Route the feature into v2 candidate generation: selection rules now include per-family kernel preferences (e.g., LLAMA/GQA-friendly decode kernel, MISTRAL sliding-window prefill kernel) while maintaining existing v1 behavior when v2 is gated off. (4) Add unit tests and golden fixtures for representative configs and edge cases; tests assert determinism (same input config -> same family/tags) and ensure we do not misclassify long-context variants that require different prefill kernels. Notes: This PR intentionally avoids adding any learned/scoring logic; it only makes the family/tag signal available so the rule-based selector can remain explainable and debuggable. Follow-ups: ENG-4823 will consume GPU SKU + driver gates; ENG-4824 will add per-request telemetry fields including `model_family` and `arch_tags` with sampling controls.
Hiro Tanaka: Can we avoid name-based heuristics as much as possible? I’d like config-first classification, otherwise forks will be painful. Also please document precedence rules.
Yuki Sato (author): Yep—updated classifier to prefer `model_type` and `architectures` and only use name normalization when those are missing/empty. Added a short precedence section to the doc and a test for a forked "vicuna" name with llama config fields.
Noah Patel: Concern: misclassifying long-context llama variants could cause tail spikes once seq buckets are introduced. Can we add a tag that explicitly captures rope scaling / context length signals even if family is LLAMA?
Yuki Sato (author): Added `long_context` + `rope_scaling_present` tags derived from rope_scaling + max_position_embeddings delta. Selector rules in this PR don’t change behavior based on that yet, but the signal is now available for the long-context guardrails in ENG-4825/PR-28522.
Lena Fischer: Please include a fixture for sliding-window attention (Mistral style) and ensure we don’t accidentally tag it as generic rope long-context. That distinction matters for prefill kernels.
Yuki Sato (author): Added sliding-window fixture and explicit `sliding_window` tag; tests assert it remains set even if rope_scaling is present.
Marcus Reed: Any measurable overhead? This is on request path eventually (feature extraction).
Yuki Sato (author): Classifier runs at model load time and emits cached features; request path uses the cached `SelectorFeatures`. Added a micro-benchmark stub note; overhead is negligible in profiling (<0.01ms at load).

Yuki Sato (author): Added `conflicting_signals_falls_back_to_unknown` test; we still emit tags but set family=UNKNOWN and mark conflict for debug logging.
Noah Patel: Approved. Please ensure the selector remains deterministic and that logging is debug-only.
Yuki Sato (author): Done—no randomness, stable ordering, and logs are behind `RUNTIME_LOG_LEVEL=debug`.

Context and motivation: Customers using long-lived streaming sessions reported hard-to-diagnose hangs during transient infra disruptions and application shutdowns. This PR implements a non-blocking heartbeat protocol extension (HB-1), a cross-SDK session facade that exposes explicit graceful shutdown primitives, and ergonomic helpers per-language so consumers can signal cancel/close without leaking goroutines/async tasks. Summary of changes: adds HB-1 control frame and processing on the server; introduces SessionFacade abstraction in each SDK with Start/Heartbeat/Drain/Close (sync + async variants); adds client-side backpressure hints that let the runtime prioritize draining cached KV frames; exposes graceful shutdown integrations: Python contextmanager/asynccontext, TypeScript AbortSignal friendly close(), Go CloseNotifier and WaitForDrain; adds telemetry points (session.heartbeat.sent, session.drain.start, session.drain.complete, session.shutdown.error) and ties them into console dashboards. Testing and validation: new integration harness that simulates packet loss, delayed ACKs, and process SIGTERM; unit tests for state transitions; cross-sdk interoperability test matrix to verify HB-1 negotiation and fallback to baseline heartbeat behavior. Checklist: - [x] Design doc posted in Linear (ENG-8451); - [x] Wire protocol draft reviewed by infra and SRE; - [x] SDK implementations for Python/TS/Go added; - [x] Backwards compatibility: negotiate HB-1 and fall back when peer does not support it; - [x] Telemetry and dashboard tiles created. Rollout plan: feature gated behind the runtime flag "enable_session_facade"; default off in hosted for two weeks then opt-in canary; SDKs ship minor bumps informing users how to opt into explicit shutdown flows. Impact and risk: reduces leaking client tasks during shutdown and provides SRE better visibility into stuck streams; risk is low if gating and fallbacks are respected. Related: ENG-8622 (runtime drain path improvements), SUP-4221 (customer incident reproducer).

Background: Customers and SRE reported noisy audit streams and ambiguous KMS routing when operator-originated requests cross region boundaries. This PR introduces a small, focused gateway that validates per-tenant residency claims (KeyProof assertions), binds them to a short-lived KMS envelope, and surfaces compact audit events. Goals: 1) Enforce an explicit per-request KeyProof claim for operator-invoked KMS operations; 2) Reduce audit volume by emitting sampled, canonicalized audit records (audit sparsity controller); 3) Provide a rollout path with opt-in config flags and a dry-run mode for policy verification. Work included: - New service: claims-gateway (Go) that validates tenant claims, checks RBAC v2 decision via PDP, and annotates KMS requests with provenance headers. - Audit sparsity controller (agent) that deduplicates repeated operator events and emits sampled canonical audit envelopes. - RBAC policy templates (OPA) and a migration helper to translate existing operator bindings into claim-aware templates. - Integration hooks in kms-proxy to accept and verify KeyProof envelopes and to secret-wrap ephemeral per-request keys. - Console telemetry additions: new dashboard panels for claim failure rates, sparsity sampling ratios, and KMS sticky routing hits. Checklist: - [x] MVP claim validator implementation - [x] OPA policies and unit tests - [x] kms-proxy integration and e2e test harness - [x] Migration tool: rbacv2-claim-adapter (dry-run compatible) - [x] Docs: internal RFC + runbook link: internal/rfc/claims-gateway.md Deployment and rollout plan: 1) Deploy claims-gateway and sparsity controller in shadow mode (dry-run) for 2 weeks in staging and a subset of prod regions. 2) Enable enforcement for dedicated capacity customers only; allow tenant opt-out for first 30 days. 3) Monitor claim-failures, KMS fallback rate, and audit volume delta. 4) After stability window, widen enforcement and enable KMS envelope wrapping by default. Migration notes: - We provide rbacv2 translation helpers that add the new attribute claim: operator:origin=service and tenancy:residency=region-*. The helper emits an RFC-friendly preview. - No direct breaking changes to the public API; operator callers without claims will be routed to compatibility fallback during rollout. Security considerations: - KeyProof envelopes are signed by operator service-mTLS and verified against operator cert pins. - The gateway enforces TTL of 5 minutes for envelopes and rejects replays. - Audit sparsity intentionally reduces noise but preserves canonical hashes for forensic reconstruction. Testing: - Unit tests for OPA policy (>=85% coverage). - Integration tests that run kms-proxy and a fake KMS to assert envelope binding and failover. - Load tests to validate that gateway adds <2ms p99 latency to operator paths under 95th percentile traffic. Related work: Linear ENG-1429; RFC at internal/rfc/claims-gateway.md; runbook at internal/runbooks/claims-gateway.md

Motivation: production traffic contains wide sequence-length variance which forces large padding and suboptimal kernel selection; continuous-batching by arrival time amplifies wasted compute. This PR introduces a length-aware dynamic batching heuristic with four coordinated pieces: (1) lightweight seqlen bucketing using streaming percentile estimates to avoid global sorting, (2) per-bucket padding-minimization that enforces a configurable padding budget and postpones filling under low-latency pressure, (3) adaptive merge policy that allows merging small buckets when latency SLOs permit, and (4) kernel-selection hints and scheduling tie-ins so the runtime prefers long-seq kernels when a batch majority exceeds configured thresholds. The design also adds KV-cache awareness: requests with warm caches are preferentially co-batched to reduce KV miss churn. This change exposes a runtime config key batching.seq_len_bucket_policy with options (off, conservative, aggressive) and metrics batch.padding_overhead, batch.bucket_size_distribution, batch.bucket_merge_rate. Implementation notes: bucketing uses 8 approximate buckets by default, bucket boundaries are recomputed periodically using exponentially-weighted percentile accumulators to adapt to workload shifts; padding budget is expressed as max_fraction_of_padded_tokens and defaults to 0.2; merge policy respects request-level latency budget and a new scheduling token that represents expected kernel time. Benchmarks: mixed RLHF-style workload (seqlens: 16/128/512/2048) on p4d-type nodes shows +18% throughput and -12% P95 latency for long-tail requests; cost-per-token reduced ~7% after enabling conservative policy. Rollout: feature-flagged behind batching.seq_len_bucket_policy; default remains off for Dedicated early canaries. Backwards compatibility: users can disable via config; no API break. Checklist: [x] design doc linked, [x] implementation, [x] tests, [x] benchmarks, [x] docs and rollout plan. Related Linear items: ENG-2171, ENG-2210.
Marco Liu: Nice approach, main concern is bucket boundary churn causing jitter — can we add a stability window?
Asha Kapoor: Added EWMA percentile window and a min_stability_period config; included tests to ensure boundaries don't flip within 10s under steady distribution.
Dana Roberts: Kernel selection hinting looks good, but we should quantify kernel switch overhead — consider a threshold to avoid thrash.
Asha Kapoor: Added a kernel-switch hysteresis and instrumentation to measure switch rate; unit added to the scheduler metrics.
Priya Nambiar: KV-cache co-batching is promising; please ensure we don't violate privacy constraints by cross-customer co-batching. 
Asha Kapoor: KV-cache co-batching is scoped to tenant-id and respects isolation; added explicit checks and a dedicated unit test.
CI: flaky test test_batch_padding_budget failed on first run; rerun passed.
Adds length-aware batching heuristics (bucketing + padding minimization) to reduce compute waste for heterogeneous sequence-length workloads. Opt-in via batching.seq_len_bucket_policy. Improves throughput on mixed-length workloads; no API changes.
payload.title: Length-aware dynamic batching: bucketing & padding-minimization heuristics

Motivation: Engineers building long-lived streaming integrations across Python/TypeScript/Go repeatedly reimplement retry logic and ad-hoc backoff glue. That results in subtle behavioral drift between SDKs and brittle consumer ergonomics when streams need to be paused, reauthenticated, or resumed during transient failures. This PR introduces a small, explicit "retry template" surface plus a lightweight stream-consumer helper library (triad-stream-helpers) to provide consistent defaults and ergonomics across the three SDKs. Summary of changes: 1) Add retry template definitions (fast-fail, conservative, balanced) expressed as declarative profiles with windows, jitter, and idempotency hints. Templates are compiled down to SDK-specific policy objects at build-time for TypeScript and Go and at import-time for Python to keep runtime cost low. 2) Introduce stream consumer helpers: pauseable async iterator wrappers, token-rotation callbacks, and a resumeHints API that surfaces whether a resumed connection can safely reuse the previous KV-cache. 3) Small public API additions: RetryProfiles enum (Py/TS/Go), StreamHelpers.attachResumeHints(stream, opts), and a new RetryConfig.fromTemplate(name, overrides). 4) Cross-language tests and examples in examples/triad-retry/ demonstrating a canary reconnection flow and a long-lived chat consumer. 5) Version bumps: redwood-sdk-python -> 2.0.0-rc1, redwood-sdk-typescript -> 1.30.0, redwood-sdk-go -> v1.9.0. Compatibility & migration: This is intentionally additive; existing RetryConfig constructors remain supported. Consumers that opt into templates will get consistent defaults across SDKs. Important migration notes are included in the release_notes field below. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-1987) - [x] Cross-SDK API alignment session with SDK leads - [x] Unit + integration tests for reconnection scenarios - [x] Examples and README updates - [x] Telemetry counters for retry decisions included - [x] Docs site snippets staged. How to review: Focus on the template semantics (the JSON/YAML-like canonical template) and the cross-SDK mapping layer. For Python, inspect cost of import-time compilation; for TS/Go, focus on compile-time bundling and tree-shaking behaviour. Tests: Included unit tests for 12 reconnection permutations and an integration canary that ran on the internal perf-lab. CI notes: initial CI run showed a flaky TS e2e (timeout in node12 matrix) which was fixed by increasing the test harness timeout, rerun green. Runbook: If consumers see resumed streams misapply KV-cache, the StreamHelpers.attachResumeHints will log a diagnostic telemetry event under telemetry.retry.resume_hint_mismatch and fall back to a safe cold-start. Related: ENG-2034 work on credential windows and session-lease informs the token-rotation callback surface.
Daniel Kim: Nice work pinning the failure modes. Two asks: (1) can we expose a hook so infra can inject per-customer jitter multipliers for heavy-tenant accounts? (2) Please add a short benchmark for Python import-time cost in the PR CI so we have a baseline.
Asha Patel (author): Reply to Daniel: added 'jitter_multiplier' optional param on RetryConfig.fromTemplate and added a microbenchmark test under tests/benchmarks/import_cost_py.py. The benchmark is gated behind CI label 'bench' so it won't slow regular runs.
Marta Lopez: Please ensure the TS bundle stays tree-shakable; helpers should be split to a separate entrypoint. Also requested a comment on expected behavior when resumeHints indicates 'unsafe'.
Asha Patel: Split helpers into 'stream-helpers' package entrypoint and added inline comment + unit test for resumeHints==unsafe falling back to cold-start. Updated bundle size automation to detect regressions.

Motivation: tighten operator session surface and telemetry for KMS usage while making region/residency violations detectable and actionable. This PR implements three coordinated changes: 1) server-side enforcement that elevating operator actions (role grants, policy changes, operator impersonation) require an active MFA assertion on the operator session; 2) lightweight per-key KMS usage telemetry (aggregated counters + tenant affinity) and a Grafana dashboard so platform + security teams can audit KMS access patterns; 3) request-time validation of residency/region tags for KMS-bound operations to reject calls that would cross a tenant's region pin or configured residency constraints.

What changed (high level): added an MFA-check middleware and an operator-privilege gating hook; enriched audit events with mfa_result and location_assertion fields; plumbed per-key telemetry events into the telemetry pipeline with an efficient aggregator; added a residency-tag validator to the KMS request path and failing fast with clear audit reasons; simple Console UI link to the new "Policy explainer" and a one-click jump to KMS usage for that key.

Files of note and rationale (single-string summary): all code changes are backwards-compatible for normal user flows; operator-level APIs now return 403 when MFA is missing for elevated paths. We intentionally do not roll MFA into token issuance here to avoid large-scale invalidation - this is an enforcement shim on elevated endpoints only. Telemetry uses existing metrics ingestion with a small new label "kms_key_id" and uses cardinality limits per-tenant to avoid explosion. Residency validation consults the tenant metadata cache and rejects calls where the key/provider does not satisfy the tenant's residency policy.

Checklist:
- [x] MFA middleware and unit tests
- [x] Audit enrichment and integration tests
- [x] KMS telemetry producer + dashboard (grafana json)
- [x] Residency validator unit + integration tests
- [x] Console link and docs stub
- [x] Performance microbenchmarks (latency impact < 3ms p50 on KMS proxy path)

Testing & verification: added targeted unit tests (service/auth, service/audit, service/kms) and an end-to-end integration test that simulates operator session without MFA attempting an elevated change (assert 403 + audit event contains mfa_result: "missing"). Telemetry smoke tests validate per-key counters increment and are visible on the new Grafana panel. Load test on staging (10k TPS mixed workload) shows <2% CPU increase on KMS proxy fleet and <3ms median added latency.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind config.security.operator_mfa_enforce (default: off). We will enable in a staged rollout: tenant pilot -> orgs with strict compliance -> global. Telemetry and residency enforcement are safe to enable globally but we will watch dashboards for unexpected 403 spikes.

Operational notes & migration: no token format changes. Ops should watch the new dashboard and the audit stream (location_assertion, mfa_result). If a tenant sees unexpected rejections set config.security.operator_mfa_enforce=false while investigating.

Known limitations: policy explainer in Console links to effective-policy view but does not yet simulate cross-tenant delegations (follow-up ENG-5643). Telemetry currently exposes only counters and does not retain raw per-call samples (by design, to limit PII).

References: Linear ENG-5491, SEC-302 for threat model; internal runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/mfa-kms-residency (doc stub).
Luca Moretti (review): Please add a latency microbenchmark for the residency check path — what happens when tenant cache is cold?
Priya R. Sharma (author): Added a microbenchmark in service/kms/proxy/bench_test.go and clarified cache warmup behaviour; cold-cache adds ~1.8ms median (measured on staging) — included in PR notes.
Aisha Khan (review): Telemetry cardinality: ensure tenants cannot create high-cardinality keys and blow up metrics. Can we limit tags?
Priya R. Sharma (author): Telemetry aggregator enforces per-tenant cardinality cap (config.telemetry.kms_cardinality_limit) and we drop/aggregate labels beyond the cap. Added tests that assert cap behaviour.
Daniel Park (review): We need to ensure audit log schema bump is backward compatible for downstream consumers.
Priya R. Sharma (author): Audit schema change is additive; consumers can ignore new fields. Added docs and a compatibility note in service/audit/README.md.

Context: CI presubmit latency and flakiness have been steadily increasing due to many small toolchain image pulls and repeated CI restarts caused by transient dependency upgrade failures. This PR introduces two tied changes: 1) a lightweight 'toolchain fuse' artifact that consolidates frequently-used toolchain bits into a single small, cacheable bootstrap image; 2) a 'dependency rollback batcher' that groups transient lockfile/upgrade failures and offers an automated, reversible rollback batch for presubmit blockers. Motivation: reduce cold presubmit time, reduce infra load from many parallel image fetches, and make dependency rollback actionable and low-noise for maintainers. Implementation notes: - Toolchain fuse: build step that composes minimal runtime bits from existing toolchain microimages (node, go, python helpers) into a deterministic tarball + manifest. It is emitted as an artifact to the CI cache with a content-hash key per toolchain-profile. The presubmit runner will prefer the fused artifact when the profile hash matches, falling back to the legacy microimages. - Dep rollback batcher: a small serverless job that listens to CI failure events tagged with the new 'auto-rollback-candidate' annotation. It aggregates failures over a 10 minute window, groups by lockfile diff, and posts a proposed rollback commit (branch + PR template) to the repo. The proposed PR includes a dry-run of the affected presubmit matrix and an explicit revert test step. Safety: rollback PRs are draft by default and require a human approval step; the batcher supports dry-run-only mode and an allowlist for repositories. Rollout plan: feature gated by repo-level flag; start disabled org-wide, enable for redwood/benchmarks and redwood/examples for 2 weeks, then wider rollout after metrics review. Checklist: - [x] design doc and metrics (ENG-4921) - [x] toolchain fuse build and publish - [x] runner fallback and cache-key unit tests - [x] batcher event consumer + grouping tests - [x] e2e smoke in redwood-examples - [x] staged rollout plan committed - [x] documentation for repo owners and ops See also: design doc link: https://linear.app/eng/issue/ENG-4921/toolchain-fuse-and-rollback-batcher and internal playbook: docs/internal/rollback-batcher.md. This description summarizes commits and changed files below.
Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Nice approach — I like the content-hash key. Question: what's the expected cache-hit rate on first rollout?
Maya Chen (author): Early run on redwood-examples shows ~70% hit rate for stable profiles; benchmarks improved presubmit cold time by ~22% median.
Priya Desai (reviewer): Security review: did we consider SBOM for the fused artifact?
Maya Chen (author): Yes — fuse build emits SBOM.json alongside the artifact; infra validates SBOM on publish.
Ethan Brooks (reviewer): The batcher looks useful but could spam maintainers. Add a debouncing window and draft PRs by default.
Maya Chen (author): Implemented debouncing (10m) and draft-only mode; updated description and tests.
Add compact toolchain fuse to reduce presubmit cold-starts; introduce a safe, draft-first dependency rollback batcher to group transient upgrade failures and propose reversible rollbacks. Rollout gated and documented.
1) Monitor presubmit median cold-start latency + cache hit rate for 2 weeks (dashboard: infra/ci/toolchain-fuse). 2) Ops to enable allowlist entries as requested. 3) Follow-up: expand SBOM enforcement to CI publish path (ENG-5012).

Improves KV cache memory utilization under mixed hot/cold workloads by introducing a compact-on-write allocator and a temperature-aware pager; reduces long-tail eviction spikes and spill I/O for multi-tenant serving.
Motivation: Production workloads observed increased fragmentation and bursty spill events for tenants with highly skewed key temperature distributions. Existing slab allocator keeps allocations in place until eviction, which leads to unusable fragments for long-lived cold keys. The pager triggers coarse-grained spilling that causes I/O bursts and latency SLO violations.

This PR implements two coordinated subsystems: (1) a compact-on-write slab allocator that opportunistically compacts small fragmented regions when a write touches a page, reclaiming contiguous slots without global stop-the-world compaction; and (2) a temperature-aware pager that maintains a lightweight per-tenant temperature histogram and prioritizes spill/coalesce operations for cold clusters while deferring noisy hot clusters. The pager also supports selective recompression for very cold values before spilling to reduce bandwidth.

Key changes (single-line summary): compact-on-write allocator, temperature histogram + pager, selective recompression codec integration, new benchmarks and e2e regression tests, and updated observability for eviction/compaction events.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of compact-on-write allocator (kv/allocator/compact_on_write.*)
- [x] Temperature histogram + pager (runtime/pager/temperature_pager.*)
- [x] Selective recompression pipeline (storage/compress/selective_recompress.cc and codec bindings)
- [x] Unit tests for allocator invariants and pager heuristics
- [x] Microbenchmarks for mixed hot/cold workloads and long-lived cold keys
- [x] Dashboard panels for compaction rate, recompression saved bytes, and pager decisions
- [x] Documentation: design note + rollout guidance in docs/ops/cache-compaction.md

Commits (high-level):
- a1f6d3b Add compact-on-write allocator and basic unit tests
- 9c3d2f4 Integrate allocator into kv residency controller and eviction path
- 5b8e1a2 Implement temperature histogram and pager policy API
- 4e0b7d1 Add selective recompression codec hook and storage write-path changes
- d63f9a0 Add benchmarks: benchmark/kv_compact_on_write and benchmark/pager_temp_distribution
- 2a7b8c5 Add tracing metrics and console dashboards for compaction/pager

Files changed (high level):
- kv/allocator/compact_on_write.cc, kv/allocator/compact_on_write.h
- runtime/pager/temperature_pager.cc, runtime/pager/temperature_pager.h
- storage/compress/selective_recompress.cc, storage/compress/codec_registry.cc (codec integration)
- controller/residency_controller.cc (hook for compact-on-write)
- benchmark/kv_compact_on_write_test.cc, benchmark/pager_temperature_test.cc
- docs/ops/cache-compaction.md
- console/dashboards/compact_on_write.json

Small illustrative snippet (compact-on-write allocator):
"When handle_write(page, slot, size) -> if slot.is_fragmented() then coalesce adjacent free slots up to target_run_size and relocate live entries into run using transient buffer; update resident offsets atomically."

Behavioral notes and safety: Compaction is opportunistic and bounded by per-tenant CPU and GC budgets to avoid interfering with token-serving SLOs. The implementation acquires only page-local locks and uses per-page transient buffers to move entries; if budget is exhausted the operation aborts and falls back to existing eviction path. Selective recompression runs inline when network bandwidth > threshold is detected (configurable) and is disabled for encrypted entry payloads to avoid double-encryption issues.

Benchmarks and results: Microbenchmarks were executed on benchmark-lab nodes (A100-based). Representative results (median across 5 runs):
- Mixed workload (90% reads, 10% writes) with hot/cold skew 100:1: tail 99th percentile latency improved from 48ms -> 31ms and spill bytes reduced by 42%.
- Cold-heavy workload (many long-lived cold keys): peak spill I/O reduced by 60% and eviction churn reduced by 35%.
- Memory overhead: transient buffer and histogram add ~1.8% resident working set for our config (tunable per-tenant).

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag `kv_compact_on_write` and pager flag `temp_pager_v1`. Default off for Dedicated/Private during initial rollout. Gradual canary across tenants: 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback if eviction rate or SLO deviations exceed thresholds.

Related work and references: This builds on prior eviction and spill smoothing work (ENG-1621, PRs implementing soft-spill controllers) but diverges by performing localized compaction on write paths rather than large-scale offline compactors. The temperature histogram is inspired by multi-generational caching heuristics used in other systems but optimized for tenant isolation and low-overhead updates at serving scale.

Migration and compatibility notes: No on-disk format changes. Pager recompression writes are compatible with existing loader path; loader checks codec metadata and decompresses appropriately. If selective recompression is enabled, spilled files include a compact metadata header for codec versioning.

Open items and follow-ups:
- Add an LRU-aware variant of the pager that considers time since last write in addition to temperature buckets (ENG-2045).
- Evaluate hardware-accelerated compression paths (NVMe offload) for very large cold spills.
- Tune thresholds per-tenant automatically using Optimize recommendations.

Marcus Viera: Please add a safety net when transient buffer allocation fails; consider falling back to single-entry write path to avoid blocking writes.
Author (Priya): Added fallback path to write without compaction and instrumented a metric 'compact_on_write_fallback' to track occurrences.
Arianna Chen: Can you add a benchmark that simulates noisy neighbor churn? I want to see pager stability under tenant interference.
Author (Priya): Added pager_temperature_test that injects churn and measured stable spill reductions across churn scenarios.
Tobias Müller: The histogram update is currently hot on the write path; consider batching histogram deltas to reduce contention.
Author (Priya): Batching added with a per-page delta buffer and background flusher; microbenchmarks show 6% lower write CPU.
CI Bot: Unit tests passed (72/72), integration suite passed (12/12), lint shows two style nits fixed in follow-up commit.
Security Review (SRE): No new network attack surface observed; recompression skips for encrypted blobs noted and documented.
Enable feature flags kv_compact_on_write and temp_pager_v1 on canary ring; monitor metrics eviction_rate, spill_bytes, compact_ops, compact_on_write_fallback; rollback if eviction_rate increases >10% or 99p latency regresses >15%.

Motivation: Customers use response_format/schema to lock model outputs for downstream tool calls. We observed intermittent streaming truncation and partial object emission when a model and the server disagreed on schema handshake semantics. This PR introduces an 'output gatekeeper' middleware that validates schema conformance during streaming, provides deterministic tool-call fencing, and translates internal error taxonomy into OpenAI-compatible error shapes for the openai-compat adapter.

What this change does: Adds a streaming handshake step at request start that negotiates response_format (v1/v2) and a soft/strict mode. During token streaming the gatekeeper computes a lightweight incremental JSON state, emits checkpoint tokens, and rejects tokens that would irreparably violate the target schema. When violation occurs the gatekeeper can either: (a) fail-closed with a clear GATE-ERR code and resume token for client replay, or (b) fail-open (configuration: gatekeeper.fail_open=true) where the stream continues but a metadata failure event is emitted.

Compatibility: Default rollout is feature-flagged off. The openai adapter maps the following internal codes to OpenAI-style responses: GATE-ERR-SCHEMA => 400 with structured error.payload.schema_error, GATE-ERR-TOOLCALL-FENCE => 409 with tool_call_rejected. When response_format is omitted we preserve previous permissive behavior.

Implementation notes: - New core components: pkg/streaming/gatekeeper.go (handshake + incremental validator), pkg/streaming/checkpoint.go (resume token generation), enterprise/api/compat/openai_adapter.go (error mapping and header injection). - SDK surface: sdk/python/redwood/response_contract.py exposes ResponseContract.validate_stream and ResponseContract.resume_from_token. - Observability: console/telemetry/gatekeeper_metrics.go exposes gatekeeper.schema_violation_count, gatekeeper.resume_token_issued, gatekeeper.fail_open_count. - Config: charts/redwood/templates/gatekeeper-configmap.yaml and console/flags/feature_flags.go add a gatekeeper.enable and gatekeeper.fail_open flags.

Testing & CI: Added integration test tests/integration/test_schema_handshake.py that simulates pausing mid-object and verifies resume token correctness. Unit tests for incremental validation and resume behavior were added. Local stress runs indicate negligible latency overhead (~0.8ms median per-request) when gatekeeper is enabled. CI: all checks passed after a flaky streaming test was stabilized (re-run).

Rollout plan: - Stage 1 (internal canary): gatekeeper.enable = true, gatekeeper.fail_open = true for 10% traffic. - Stage 2: gatekeeper.fail_open = false for 25% traffic, capture telemetry for 7 days. - Stage 3: increase to 100% after monitoring verification.

Docs & examples: Updated docs/api/response_format.md with handshake semantics and examples for resume tokens. Added an example in redwood-quickstarts showing graceful tool-call fencing with strict mode.

Risks & mitigations: Strict fail-closed mode can surface new 400/409 errors for customers with loose models; mitigated by feature flags and a telemetry-backed opt-in. Resume tokens are short-lived (default 5 minutes) and cryptographically signed to avoid replay attacks.

Related: ENG-1247 (schema contract reliability), PM-893 (customer ask: stable tool calls), SUP-4321 (support ticket showing a broken toolcall during streaming).
Ravi Patel (reviewer): Can we avoid blocking the critical path for small responses? Suggest async telemetry flushes and a minimal fast-path.
Author (Maya): Added fast-path in gatekeeper.go: bypass incremental validation for single-token non-JSON responses; retained full check for JSON/object streams.
Elena García (reviewer): Resume tokens look good but need explicit TTL in docs and rotate key support.
Author (Maya): Documented resume token TTL and added key id header for rotation support in checkpoint.go.
Noah Brooks (reviewer): Approve after test stabilization. Noted a small race in shutdown path.
Author (Maya): Fixed shutdown race by draining the gatekeeper queue on shutdown and added a unit test.
payload.title: Introduce output gatekeeper for schema handshake and streaming stability in OpenAI compatibility layer

Summary: Adds a 'policy provenance bridge' that attaches immutable provenance claims to sensitive requests, dual-writes provenance metadata to KMS-backed envelopes and an append-only compliance ledger, and validates region-pin manifests during request admission. Motivation: Customers requested stronger non-repudiation guarantees for KMS usage and clearer enforcement of tenant region pins without brittle ad-hoc checks. This change ties RBAC v2 decision outputs to a provenance claim that is recorded in two independent backends to make post-hoc audit and compliance investigations more robust. Design: 1) provenance middleware (api/middleware/provenance.go) that gathers RBAC decision context, service identity, model id, route, and region pin and emits a canonical claim object; 2) kms-dualwrite daemon (cmd/provenance-daemon) which takes claims and performs an atomic-dual-write: a wrapped KMS envelope (customer CMK context) plus an append to the immutable ledger (ledger client with HMAC anchoring); 3) region-pin validator (api/middleware/region_pin.go) which consults a new region-pin manifest and rejects/rewrites requests failing residency constraints; 4) RBAC mapper extension (rbac/policy_mapper.go) that surfaces assertion hashes used in claims; 5) migration script (scripts/migrate-add-provenance.sh) to backfill policy fingerprints for active tenants. Commits: 4 commits, high-level: create provenance bridge and schema; implement kms-dualwrite and ledger client; add region-pin manifest validation and unit tests; add integration test harness and deployment manifests. Files changed (high level): pkg/provenance/bridge.go, cmd/provenance-daemon/main.go, api/middleware/provenance.go, api/middleware/region_pin.go, rbac/policy_mapper.go, scripts/migrate-add-provenance.sh, deploy/helm/provenance-daemon.yaml, internal/ledger/client.go, tests/integration/provenance_e2e_test.go, tests/unit/region_pin_test.go, docs/security/provenance.md, go.mod. Migration notes: run scripts/migrate-add-provenance.sh in staging to compute policy fingerprints and pre-seed the ledger for active tenants; daemon reads configuration from KMS and LEDGER URIs and requires a new service account with kms:Encrypt/kms:Sign and ledger:Append. Rollout plan: 1) feature flag off by default; 2) enable provenance middleware in Canary region for low-traffic tenants; 3) deploy provenance-daemon in dedicated namespace with scaled-to-zero safe probe; 4) enable region-pin validation in soft-fail mode (log only) for 48h, then hard-enforce. Testing: unit tests for policy_mapper and region_pin, synchronous integration tests that assert dual-write atomicity via ledger stub, e2e tests that exercise full flow with KMS dev envelope. Backwards compatibility: middleware is opt-in; requests without provenance continue to use legacy audit path. Security review: key usage and HSM access patterns documented in docs/security/provenance.md. Release notes: adds provenance bridge and optional KMS dual-write daemon for stronger audit trails and region-pin manifest enforcement. CI and rollout checklists included below.
Priya: This looks promising; can we ensure the dual-write has a clear retry policy? Aisha: Added exponential backoff with idempotency tokens and a dead-letter topic for manual reconciliation. Liam: Please add integration tests for partial failures where ledger append succeeds but KMS envelope fails; we should validate the compensating flow. Aisha: Added tests and a reconciliation command to the daemon. Marco: Region-pin manifest format looks good but we should enforce schema validation on ingest. Aisha: Added JSON schema validation and a manifest lint CI job. Priya: Approve after CI green. Liam: Approved and merged once migration script was validated in staging.
Adds an opt-in provenance bridge that attaches immutable claims to RBAC decisions, a provenance-daemon to dual-write KMS-wrapped envelopes and ledger entries, region-pin manifest validation middleware, migration helper script to backfill policy fingerprints, and docs with operational runbook. Feature gated behind 'provenance_bridge' feature flag. Requires new service account with KMS and ledger permissions.

Context and motivation: Customers operating in multi-region and regulated environments frequently require both a primary KMS provider (customer-managed CMK) and a provider fallback (Redwood-managed key or alternate cloud KMS) when region-scoped keys are unavail-able or during DR. At the same time, audit logs contain potentially sensitive identifiers that must be redacted before leaving region boundaries. This PR implements a combined approach: 1) a KMS provider selection and fallback layer that respects tenant KMS bindings, geofence constraints, and an allowlist/denylist for cross-region wrapping; 2) a streaming audit-redaction pipeline that enforces configurable field-level redaction rules and provenance markers before logs are forwarded to external collectors.
Summary of changes: - Add pkg/kms/provider_router.go: provider router with policy evaluation (tenant binding, region affinity, providers priority, and DR fallback rules). - Add pkg/kms/provider_store.go: lightweight provider metadata store with caching and TTLs. - Add pkg/audit/redactor.go and pkg/audit/pipeline.go: streaming redaction stages, rules engine, and provenance header enrichment. - Add internal/rbac/policy_generator.go: small utility to synthesize RBAC v2 role bindings for the new KMS proxy service roles and audit-forwarder roles. - Add deploy/helm/templates/kms-proxy.yaml and audit-forwarder config: helm hooks to install default policies and seeding jobs. - Add migrations/20260220_kms_binding_table.sql: table to persist tenant->provider bindings and residency hints. - Tests: integration test harness in test/integration/kms_provider_fallback_test.go and unit tests for redaction rules.
Commits (high-level): - 0f7c8d9: initial provider router and interface with unit tests - 1a2b3ef: redaction pipeline + provenance headers, test harness - 9c4d2ab: RBAC generator and helm templates - d22e5b7: migration SQL and deployment config - 7b0b6a1: fix flaky test (time-dependent TTL), CI flake mitigation
Changed areas (high level): - pkg/kms/* (provider routing, policy checks) - pkg/audit/* (redaction pipeline, rule definitions) - internal/rbac/* (policy generator) - deploy/helm/templates/* (k8s manifests and seed job) - migrations/* (DB schema) - test/integration/* (integration harness)
Review conversation (abridged in-line): - Ethan Park (reviewer): "Can the provider router produce deterministic results when multiple providers have equal priority? Suggest tie-breaker by provider id and to add metrics for fallback counts." - Maya Chen (author): "Added deterministic tie-breaker (provider id) and metric kms.provider_fallback_total. Also added unit test to assert deterministic selection." - Soraya Patel: "Audit redaction rules look good, but I'm concerned about performance for high-throughput tenants. Can we ensure the pipeline is non-blocking and gives backpressure signals to the serving runtime?" - Maya Chen: "Pipeline uses lock-free ring buffer and offloads heavy regex redactions to worker pool; we added e2e perf test with 10k rps and included backpressure metrics audit.pipeline_backpressure_seconds." - Luca Romano (security approver): "Please include a migration plan for tenants with existing provider bindings; confirm rollback semantics." - Maya Chen: "Included migration script and added a rollout playbook to the PR description; rollback will re-seed previous bindings and flip a feature flag to disable fallback selection."
CI details: - CI run #4521: lint ✅, unit tests ✅, integration (k8s) initially flaky (timeout on test harness) -> rerun -> passed ✅. - Coverage: global change +0.3%. - Security scanning: dependency-check flagged transient dev dependency; upgraded and re-scanned.
Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2026-02-27 by Soraya Patel. Merge method: squash and merge.
Post-merge actions performed: - Helm seed job run in staging to populate provider binding table with test tenants - Feature flag rollout started (kms.fallback.enabled) scoped to internal accounts - Metrics dashboard added: security.KMS Fallback Rate and audit.Pipeline Backpressure - Notified infra and SRE channels about the migration window
Rollout and migration notes (what ops must do): - Run migrations on dedicated DB cluster during scheduled maintenance window (script location: migrations/20260220_kms_binding_table.sql). - Seed tenant bindings for customers that have provided CMKs using the helm job (deploy/helm/templates/kms-seed-job.yaml). - Toggle feature flag kms.fallback.enabled to gradually enable fallback behavior; observe metric kms.provider_fallback_total and audit.pipeline_backpressure_seconds. - If rollback required: disable feature flag, run rollback seeding job (deploy/helm/templates/kms-rollback-seed.yaml), and ensure no new wrapped keys are created by fallback path.
Backwards compatibility / impact: - No changes to public API surface. - Internal service-to-service auth: new service roles created via RBAC generator; operators must run the seeding job to provision role bindings in clusters using RBAC v2. - Audit exporters: consumers will receive redacted logs with a provenance.header x-rw-audit-provenance containing provider id and redaction-version.
Testing instructions: - Unit tests: run go test ./pkg/kms - Integration: run make integration-kms with local kind cluster; use test/integration/README.md for harness config. - Manual verification steps are included in deploy/helm/README.md
Post-merge follow-ups (in Linear): - ENG-8472: monitor fallback rates and adjust policy thresholds - SEC-1905: verify audit redaction rules with compliance team - OPS-312: schedule DB migration window
Summary: This PR delivers a pragmatic multi-provider KMS selection and fallback implementation together with a streaming audit redaction pipeline and supporting RBAC generator and deployment artifacts. The work is production-ready, CI green, security-reviewed, and merged to main with a controlled rollout plan and metrics to observe behavior.
Adds multi-provider KMS binding with geofence fallback and safe-audit redaction pipeline; requires a short rollout with policy sync. No user-facing API changes.

Motivation: reduce attention kernel overhead and memory footprint for long-context workloads (>=512 tokens) by combining a multi-granular tiling strategy with a fused rotary/rope micro-op path and light-weight KV hotset hints. FlashMosaic is a new kernel variant that: 1) applies adaptive block tiling (mosaic tiles) to better utilize shared memory across variable head sizes, 2) fuses rotary/rope position transformations into the Q/K compute path to avoid an extra memory pass, and 3) exposes a small KV hotset hint to the scheduler to prefer resident KV shards for streaming/batched sequences. This PR implements the kernel, integrates it into the kernel selection layer, and adds microbenchmarks + tests.

What changed (summary): added a new CUDA kernel implementation (flashmosaic) with C++ wrappers and a CPU fallback; extended the kernel selector to emit a FlashMosaic path when heuristics match (seq_len >= 256, head_dim % 32 == 0, GPU L2 >= 6MB); introduced a fused rope/rotary micro-op that is applied in-register during Q/K compute to eliminate a separate transpose + mul pass; added a KV hotset hint API to runtime and a scheduler heuristic that pins frequently accessed KV shards to resident pools when memory pressure allows; added microbenchmarks (runtime/bench/bench_flashmosaic.py), unit tests, and documentation snippets in docs/perf/.

Checklist:
- [x] Kernel implementation (CUDA + wrappers)
- [x] Kernel selector / fallback logic
- [x] Unit tests for numerical parity vs existing flash variant
- [x] Microbenchmarks and CI performance gate
- [x] Documentation of heuristic knobs and runtime flags
- [x] Backwards-compatible CPU/GPU fallback

Performance highlights (internal bench):
- Up to +18% throughput at seq_len=1024, batch=8, model=7B on A100 GPUs (fp16)
- Median token latency decrease of ~9% for streaming small-batch workloads due to fused rotary path
- L2 load reduction measured in microbench: ~12% fewer global loads for fused rotary case
- KV hotset hint produced a 6-10% tail-latency improvement for bursty interactive workloads in our canary runs

Compatibility and safety: the kernel exposes a conservative selector; unsupported shapes fall back to the mature FlashBridge path. Numerical parity tests run across a matrix of head_dim ∈ {32,64,128}, seq_len ∈ {64,256,1024} and show max relative error < 1e-6 in fp16 accumulation mode. A runtime flag REDWOOD_ENABLE_FLASHMOSAIC (default on) is provided so operators can toggle at runtime.

Notes on design tradeoffs: fusing rotary removes a memory pass but increases register pressure. The mosaic tiling prefers larger shared-memory allocations which can reduce occupancy on older GPUs; selector heuristics keep this limited to GPUs with sufficient SM/shared resources. KV hotset hints are advisory and will not cause eviction anomalies; they are additive metadata passed to the scheduler and respected when memory headroom exists.

Related work: conceptually similar to earlier Flash variants but differs by the mosaic tiling pattern and in-register fused rotary. See ENG-9123 for design doc and perf traces.

Motivation: In multi-GPU tensor-parallel workloads we observed recurring p99 spikes driven by (1) small allreduce latency on dozens of layer-level tensors and (2) KV cache serialization/deserialization overhead when checkpointing/sharing KV shards across ranks. This PR implements a pairwise rendezvous allreduce path with eager micro-fusion for small tensors, plus a lightweight on-wire KV serialization elimination for hot-path checkpoints to reduce CPU->GPU stall. Approach: 1) Introduce pairwise asynchronous rendezvous that groups tensor allreduces into stable peer pairs when topology and bandwidth permit, reducing NCCL launch overhead in small-message regimes. 2) Add an eager micro-fusion pass that merges consecutive small kernels (<= 64KB) into a single fused kernel when safe to do so. 3) Replace the baseline KV cache checkpoint format with an in-place delta shipping mode: small KV windows are exchanged via a direct GPU-to-GPU buffer without an intermediate host-serialized blob. 4) Integrate the new paths into continuous batching so that prefix KV warmup keeps the fused path primed and avoids first-request stalls. Compatibility: The pairwise rendezvous falls back to the legacy allreduce when topology changes, PCIe-only nodes, or when NCCL reports stream conflicts. The KV delta shipping is opt-in by config (kvcache.delta_mode=true) and guarded by runtime checks for pinned memory and CUDA IPC availability. Commits: "initial pairwise rendezvous implementation", "add eager micro-fusion kernelizers and tests", "kv delta shipping wire format and runtime guards", "continuous-batching integration and priming", "benchmark results and tuning knobs". Changed areas: runtime/tp/collectives.cc, runtime/tp/pairwise_rendezvous.h, runtime/kvcache/delta_ship.cc, runtime/kernels/fusion_pass.cc, runtime/serving/continuous_batcher.cc, tests/tp/collective_integration_test.cc, bench/benchmarks/tp_smallmsg_allreduce.py. Performance: On 8xA100-80GB pods with NVLink, synthetic TP passbench shows p50 token latency -3%, p95 -7%, p99 -10% for small message micro-batched workloads; end-to-end throughput for 4-token streaming scenarios improved +12% at equal SLO. KV checkpoint hot-path CPU time dropped ~65% for small window checkpoints (<=1MB) and median request CPU tail reduced by ~18%. Safety and testing: Added unit tests for rendezvous fallback, fusion correctness tests with random shapes, and integration tests exercising kvcache.delta_mode across mixed topologies. Bench harness: repeated runs across three nodes with network emulation to verify regressions. Rollback plan: feature gated by runtime flags and config; immediate rollback possible via flipping kvcache.delta_mode=false and disabling pairwise_rendezvous in cluster config. Impact and risk: Low risk when flags off. With flags on, risk surface includes corner NCCL stream ordering issues, which are mitigated by conservative stream-affinity checks and an emergency fallback that forces legacy path on NCCL errors. Related work: ENG-2314 (small-message collective perf), ENG-2389 (kvcache repartitioning).
Diego Park: 'Nice isolation between rendezvous selection and actual NCCL calls. Please add a test where a failing rank triggers fallback.' Author (Priya): 'Added integration test that injects a simulated NCCL error and verifies fallback to legacy allreduce.' Ava Moreno: 'Fusion looks correct but we need to avoid increased register pressure; can you share PTX sm_80 runs?' Author: 'Included PTX run artifacts and conservative codepath that disables fusion for kernels with >64 registers.' Liam Chen: 'KV delta approach looks promising; ensure IPC FD lifetimes are bounded.' Author: 'Added scoped IPC wrapper and additional CI coverage on shared-memory runners.' Approvals: Diego, Ava approved after fixes; Liam requested a follow-up for observability but approved merge.
Hardware: 8xA100-80GB NVLink, 3xDGX nodes. Workloads: micro-batched small message TP (avg tensor 16KB), continuous-batching streaming 4-token profile. Results: p99 latency reduced 10% (baseline 42ms -> 38ms), throughput +12% under load, KV checkpoint CPU time -65% for <=1MB shards. Repeatability: 5 runs, stdev <2% for throughput.
Introduce opt-in pairwise rendezvous path that reduces small-message allreduce latency and an opt-in KV delta shipping mode to reduce KV cache serialization CPU time. Feature is off by default and gated behind kvcache.delta_mode and pairwise_rendezvous flags. Recommended for TP workloads with many small tensors.

Motivation: Improve debuggability and metrics fidelity for streaming API calls and function/tool invocations while preserving OpenAI shim compatibility. Problem: when streaming tokens and invoking tools we were losing per-endpoint context and sequence information in logs and metrics (difficult to attribute errors and regressions). This PR introduces per-endpoint correlation ids, stream-fragment markers, and propagates trace+baggage into tool execution processes while mapping these fields into the OpenAI-compatible response surface.

What this change does (high level):
- Attach an endpoint-scoped correlation_id header (x-rw-correlation-id) to every API request and include it in structured access logs and JSONL streaming fragments.
- Emit stream fragment metadata with fields: fragment_id, seq_in_fragment, is_final, and fragment_offset to allow reassembly and per-fragment metrics.
- Propagate existing W3C traceparent and baggage headers into tool/function executor launches so tool logs include the same trace context.
- Add per-route metric labels (route_name, api_mode: streaming|non-streaming, compatibility: openai|native) so high-cardinality is controlled at metric emission layer.
- Maintain OpenAI shim compatibility: the OpenAI-compatible response still exposes id/request_id and the old headers (x-request-id) are populated from the new correlation id to avoid breaking downstream customers.

Checklist:
- [x] server: attach correlation id to request context and access logs
- [x] streaming: include fragment metadata in JSONL lines (prefixed with "rw-frag-" fields)
- [x] function/tool exec: set TRACECONTEXT and RW_BAGGAGE env vars before start
- [x] metrics: add per-route tags and a sanitizer to cap cardinality
- [x] tests: unit + integration test for reassembly and per-fragment metrics
- [x] docs: add small note to observability guide about fragment reassembly and header mapping

Commits summary: (high-level)
- feat(observability): add correlation_id middleware and header mapping
- feat(streaming): emit fragment metadata in streaming JSONL and update client shim
- feat(exec): propagate traceparent and baggage into tool subprocess env
- perf(metrics): add per-route label sanitizer and update metrics emitters
- test: add integration test for stream fragment ordering and metrics tagging
- docs: update observability guide and API compatibility section

Files changed (high-level):
- server/middleware/correlation.go (new middleware to generate/propagate correlation_id)
- api/streaming/fragment_emitter.go (stream fragment metadata attachment)
- adapters/openai/shim_response.go (map x-rw-correlation-id -> x-request-id and response.id)
- exec/launcher/launcher.go (inject tracing env into tool processes)
- metrics/route_labels.go (sanitizer for high-cardinality route tags)
- observability/docs/fragment-reassembly.md (docs)
- tests/integration/stream_fragments_test.go (integration tests)

Small illustrative example (what a streaming JSONL fragment now looks like):
{"rw_frag_fragment_id":"f0a9b2", "rw_frag_seq":1, "rw_frag_is_final":false, "content":"the quick brown"}
{"rw_frag_fragment_id":"f0a9b2", "rw_frag_seq":2, "rw_frag_is_final":true, "content":" fox jumps"}

Compatibility notes: the OpenAI shim will attach the following headers to preserve backwards compatibility: x-request-id (set from x-rw-correlation-id), and the response.id in non-streaming endpoints is set to correlation_id when an explicit request id is not present. No public API changes required for current customers using the OpenAI shim.

Testing and validation: added unit tests for correlation middleware, fragment ordering, and tool exec env propagation. Integration test runs a simulated streaming request with an invoked tool and asserts the logs emitted by the tool process contain the same traceparent and baggage.

Operational considerations:
- Per-route labels are sanitized to avoid explosion (we limit to well-known route_name set and fallback to 'custom' for unknown).
- Fragment IDs are UUID4-ish (short hash) and the fragment sequence numbers are small ints to avoid large telemetry cardinality.

Introduce a latency-bounded reservation allocator that ensures per-request tail-latency SLOs while making soft capacity reservations; add an incremental utilization reporter that streams summarized per-pool utilization metrics for efficient storage and real-time dashboards.
Motivation: Dedicated fleets need predictable tail latency for tenant requests while still allowing short bursts and efficient packing. Existing reservoir-style allocators optimize for long-term fairness but do not provide explicit bounds for p95/p99 tail latency during transient bursts. This change introduces a reservation allocator that trades small, short-lived soft reservations to keep queueing latency under explicit bounds and a companion incremental utilization reporter that emits compact deltas suitable for high-cardinality fleets.

Summary of changes: implement a latency-bounded reservation allocator in the autoscaler which: 1) continuously estimates per-pool service capacity and current queueing headroom; 2) creates short-duration soft reservations (configurable TTL and decay curves) when queueing delay prediction exceeds configured latency SLO; 3) honors proportional tenant shares to avoid long-term unfairness; 4) exposes decision diagnostics for tracing and debugging. Add a util reporter process that: 1) aggregates utilization at multiple timescales (10s/1m/5m) and emits incremental deltas rather than full snapshots to reduce ingestion costs; 2) tags records with origin (autoscaler vs. gateway) and reservation attribution; 3) surfaces percentiles and decay-weighted averages used by the allocator.

Design notes: the allocator is conservative by default (defaults tuned in charts/dedicated/values.yaml) and has three knobs: latency_slo_ms, reservation_ttl_s, and reservation_decay_factor. Reservation_credit accounting is soft—credits can be reclaimed early if headroom returns. The util reporter uses a windowed sampler with an exponentially weighted delta compressor; it includes backpressure when the telemetry pipeline is saturated.

Compatibility and rollout: implemented feature-flagging for both allocator and reporter. Default: disabled in hosted by default; enabled on Dedicated environments behind an opt-in config. Rollout plan includes canary in one pool, monitor p95/p99 latency, utilization deltas, and tenant throughput impact. Rollback: disable feature flag and drain outstanding soft reservations (immediate reclamation path included).

Testing: unit tests cover allocator decision logic and invariants (no negative credits, proportional fairness over 10k simulated ticks). Integration tests simulate bursty traffic across tenants and assert p95/p99 under configured SLOs. Bench harness included to measure CPU and memory of the reporter under 100k series.

Checklist: - [x] Implement allocator logic and unit tests - [x] Implement incremental util reporter and unit tests - [x] Add integration tests and smoke harness - [x] Add docs/design/reservation-allocator.md - [x] Add Helm defaults and migration notes - [x] Manual canary run and metrics validation

Related: ENG-9742 (autoscaler backpressure refactor), ENG-9801 (telemetry cost-reduction initiative).

Asha Kapoor: Fixed reclamation race by serializing reclamation through pool reconciler; added stress test in integration suite.

Motivation: prevent cross-operator credential surfacing and provide high-fidelity audit sampling for KMS consent decisions. This PR introduces an operator credential boundary that reduces the blast radius when operator credentials are used to interact with tenant-scoped KMS endpoints and folds in an audit sampling policy so we can observe tenant residency consent decisions without flooding the audit pipeline.

Changes in this PR (high-level):
- enforce operator token masking at the auth gateway for any request that touches 'kms:decrypt' or 'kms:wrap' APIs, ensuring operator->tenant credential transitions are explicit
- add a KMS consent probe service which performs non-blocking consent checks against the regional KMS allocator and exports a compact trace to the audit forwarder when consent is denied/ambiguous
- introduce audit sampling profiles (default, elevated, quarantine) configurable per-tenant to reduce noise while keeping coverage for high-risk tenants
- RBAC adjustments: new 'operator:limited-kms-proxy' role and a short-lived delegation flow that requires explicit consent-proof headers
- observability: new metrics (kms_consent_probe.latency, kms_consent_probe.denials, operator_token_masking.count) and a dashboard prototype

Canary monitors added to the console for 5% of traffic. If probe latency > 200ms for 3m, fallback to legacy path and emit an alert to SRE.

Backward compatibility: default behaviour unchanged unless the feature flag is enabled or tenant profile explicitly switched. Masking is additive: operators with older clients still succeed but are routed through proxy that injects consent headers (noop for non-KMS calls).

Motivation: Customers running diverse tenant workloads struggle to pick safe default batching, cache, and quantization profiles. Manual tuning is slow and error-prone, leading to suboptimal unit economics or regressions in tail latency. This PR introduces an automated preset curator that synthesizes tenant-aware defaults from telemetry snapshots and a small rulebook so teams can opt into conservative, balanced, or aggressive presets per tenant.

What this changes: adds a new controller (preset-curator) that consumes workload sketches and generates JSON presets for: batching (max_batch_size, microbatch_target, batch_timeout_ms), KV cache prefill thresholds, and quantization profiles (q8/q4 variants and fallback chains). Presets are exposed via the existing tenant-defaults API and are versioned so rollbacks/rollouts are safe. The curator ships with three starter strategies (conservative, balanced, aggressive) and a dry-run mode which emits telemetry comparing simulated token-cost and 95th latency against current defaults.

Key files touched (high level):
- services/preset-curator/{controller.go,simulator.go,policy_rules.md}
- pkg/telemetry/sketches/{workload_sketch.go,serializer.go}
- api/tenant_defaults/v1/handler.go (adds POST /tenants/:id/presets/dryrun)
- cli/presetctl (new subcommand: apply/dryrun/list)
- integrations/tests/preset-curator-integ.yaml (lightweight scenario harness)

Commits summary:
- 8f9a2dd: scaffold preset-curator service and API hooks
- b2c6f1a: implement workload sketch serializer and stable hashing
- d4e7c3f: add policy rule engine and starter strategies
- e11f9b0: add simulator that replays recent telemetry to estimate unit-econ impact
- f3a12b4: add CLI, docs, and integration test harness

Testing and validation: unit tests for serializer and policy engine, integration harness that simulates three tenant shapes (chatty short prompts, long-form generation, mixed embeddings+chat). Ran a staging dry-run across 50 tenants using one week of telemetry: median token-cost reduction 12% for balanced presets, median 95th latency change +2ms (conservative) and +12ms (aggressive). Dry-run reports included in artifact: ci/preset-curator/dryrun-report-20260228.json.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan: presets are additive and opt-in per-tenant. Disabled by default; operations can enable the service per environment. When enabled, default strategy is conservative. Rollout plan: canary 10 tenants -> 100 tenants -> all tenants, monitor unit-econ, errors, tail latency. A built-in safeguard automatically reverts applied presets if error rate or latency regressions exceed thresholds for 10 minutes.

Risks and mitigations: automatic quantization can cause rare regressions on small-sample workloads. Mitigation: quant profiles include immediate fallback chains to known-safe FP16/FP32 variants, and the simulator runs classifier heuristics to mark high regression risk tenants.

Related: ENG-8342, ENG-8410, PM-1201.

Release notes: adds tenant-aware preset curator (opt-in) for batching, KV cache, and quantization defaults. CLI support via presetctl. Dry-run mode for safety checks.

Context: We observe repeated short-duration contention across dedicated pools where static reservations cause nearby tenants to either starve or overrun resulting in amplified autoscaler churn. This PR introduces a proactive 'capacity shear' mechanism that gradually rebalances reserved capacity between pools ahead of predicted demand spikes and a tenant fairness index (TFI) to guide reallocation decisions. Motivation: Reduce oscillation and emergency cold-starts by using decorrelated utilization signals and a fairness objective that accounts for recent latency targets, percentiles, and committed throughput. Design summary: 1) Capacity shear controller: a continuous controller (provisioner/shear.go) that computes candidate reallocations using multi-window utilization deltas and headroom forecasts. Shear actions are constrained by safety knobs: min_reserve_floor, per-tenant cooldown, and a circuit-breaker preventing >10% cap movement in a 5m window. 2) Tenant Fairness Index (TFI): a composite score computed from normalized committed throughput, 95th latency violations, and historical utilization elasticity. TFI is used as a weight when distributing reclaimed capacity. 3) Utilization demultiplexer: telemetry/util_demuxer.go ingests aggregated pool metrics and emits tenant-level signals by probabilistic attribution when direct counters are missing. 4) Telemetry and debugging: new metrics (shear_attempts_total, shear_applied_bytes, tfi_distribution, demux_confidence) + an ops endpoint (/debug/shear/state) for dry-run inspection. Rollout plan: opt-in flag per-pool (provisioner.features.capacity_shear=true). Start in dry-run mode for 48h, then enable gradual apply with safe limits set conservatively for the first week. Backout is a simple feature flag toggle. Testing and validation: extensive unit tests for controller math, integration tests in perf-canary using synthetic multi-tenant traces, and a staged canary rollout across 3 clusters. Observability: dashboard updated with time-series of TFI and per-tenant headroom; alerts added for shear_applied_rate > expected thresholds. Checklist: [x] design doc linked || docs/design/capacity-shear.md [x] unit tests [x] integration canary harness [x] e2e perf validation [x] feature flag gating [x] ops runbook added. Impact and metrics to watch: decrease in emergency scaling events, reduction in median cold-start latency, and stable SLA compliance. Backwards compatibility: no breaking API changes. Cost: small steady-state controller CPU + increased metric cardinality; we measured <2% infra cost bump in canary clusters.

Summary This PR adds canonical v1 audit events for API key lifecycle actions in the control plane: creation, rotation (new key issued for an existing key record), and revocation. The events are emitted for both API and Console-backed workflows and follow the audit schema library introduced in pr-21984 and the event_type registry from pr-21991. Motivation API keys are a high-risk credential surface and are explicitly called out as “sensitive actions” for SOC2/ISO-aligned control evidence and customer investigations. Prior to this PR we had partial/legacy logging with inconsistent field names and (in one path) a debug log that could include a key prefix. This PR standardizes the audit semantics and hardens redaction so key material is never persisted to the audit stream. Event types added (registered in audit registry) - credential.api_key.created - credential.api_key.rotated - credential.api_key.revoked Actor / target semantics - actor.* is the authenticated principal performing the action (user/session, service account, or internal system actor). For Console-initiated actions, the actor is the human user; for API actions, actor is derived from the auth context (user vs service token). - target.* represents the API key record being modified. We intentionally avoid putting any API key secret material in either actor or target fields. Redaction / key material handling - The API key secret (full value) is NEVER included in the audit payload, logs, errors, or traces. - We emit: key_id (server-generated stable identifier) and key_fingerprint (sha256 of the secret, truncated to 12 hex chars) to support correlation without leaking the key. - We also emit key_prefix only in the response payload to the caller at creation time; it is explicitly prohibited in audit events and in application logs. - Added a lint guard that rejects attempted inclusion of fields matching /(api[_-]?key|secret|token)(_value|_raw|_plaintext)?/ in audit event builders for these event types. Payload fields (high-level) Each event includes: schema_version, event_id (ULID), occurred_at, event_type, tenant_id, project_id (if scoped), actor_type/actor_id/actor_email_hash (when available), source_ip, user_agent (capped), request_id, trace_id, target_type=api_key, target_id=key_id, and a small metadata block (flattened) with: api_key_name, api_key_scopes (sorted + allow-listed), expires_at, and for rotate/revoke: previous_state/new_state. Note: Per cardinality budget guidance we do not include arbitrary free-form descriptions; api_key_name is capped at 64 chars and normalized whitespace. Implementation details - Added AuditEmitter hooks in the API key service methods: CreateKey(), RotateKey(), RevokeKey(). - Ensured the emitter is called after DB commit but before response return so audit reflects a successful state transition. (Failures remain covered by standard error logs; we do not emit “attempted” events in v1.) - Added correlation propagation from request context into background tasks used by rotation/revoke for async cleanup, so audit events carry request_id/trace_id consistently. - Normalized legacy fields: where older code used audit_action or resource_uuid, we now use event_type and target_id. Testing - Unit tests: verify each action emits exactly one audit event with required fields; verify fingerprint generation is stable and does not equal any substring of the raw key. - Integration tests: exercise Console workflow paths (via console-backend calling control plane) and direct API calls; assert audit payload validates against v1 JSON schema. - Negative tests: assert audit builder rejects inclusion of api_key_value/secret/token-like fields (regression for near-miss reported in eng-security thread). Example (sanitized) {"schema_version":"1.0","event_id":"01JH8Q2V6K9Q6A7F8S6Y9G8M3D","occurred_at":"2026-02-02T18:41:09.552Z","event_type":"credential.api_key.created","tenant_id":"tnt_7f3...","project_id":"prj_a91...","actor_type":"user","actor_id":"usr_2c1...","actor_email_hash":"sha256:4b0d...","source_ip":"203.0.113.10","user_agent":"Mozilla/5.0 ...","request_id":"req_01JH8Q2...","trace_id":"4f2c0b...","target_type":"api_key","target_id":"key_9d2...","api_key_name":"vectorgrid-prod-ci","api_key_scopes":"inference.read,inference.write","api_key_fingerprint":"sha256:9f3a1c0b22e1","expires_at":"2026-08-01T00:00:00Z"} Rollout / compatibility - Gated behind AUDIT_SCHEMA_V1_ENABLED for one deploy cycle; once exporter normalization (ENG-4827) is fully rolled out, we’ll flip the flag by default. - Exporter can ingest these events as-is; no schema migration needed beyond existing v1 support. Follow-ups - Add “attempted/failed” variants for key operations once we finalize taxonomy for authz-denied actions (tracked in ENG-4822 discussion). - Ensure Private installer emits operator actions for offline key rotation where applicable (ENG-4826).
- Added v1 audit events for API key create/rotate/revoke across Hosted/Dedicated/Private control-plane.
- Enforced redaction: API key material is never logged; only key_id + fingerprint + metadata are emitted.
- Added unit + integration coverage for sensitive API key flows; ensured correlation IDs propagate into audit payloads.
Ethan Park (review): Good direction. Two asks: (1) ensure audit emission is strictly post-commit; I don’t want "created" events for rolled-back txns. (2) For rotate, please include reference to the prior key_id if it’s a new record, but don’t leak anything about the secret.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Updated to emit after commit hook (see CreateKey/RotateKey). For rotate: target_id is the new key_id; added rotated_from_key_id for correlation. No secret material included; fingerprint only for the new key.
Hanae Suzuki (review): Please remove user_agent from these events or cap it. It tends to be high-cardinality and occasionally contains weird strings.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Capped to 256 chars + normalized; also added allow-list for known UA prefixes per observability standard. If you still prefer removal, happy to follow up, but other sensitive events include it for investigations.
Allison Grant (review): Confirmed this aligns with audit logging standard. One nit: api_key_scopes should be stable ordering and constrained; don’t allow arbitrary scope strings.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Done. Scopes are validated against server allow-list, sorted, and joined. Added test to ensure ordering.
Sahana Iyer (review): CI failed on audit lint (new redaction guard flagged a debug log in routes.ts). Please fix and rerun.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Removed debug log statement and added a regression test. Re-ran CI; green.
Marcus Lin (review): Looks good. Make sure we document dedupe guidance for exporter retries (SUP-18510). Is event_id always unique per emit? Also ensure rotate/revoke are idempotent under retries.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): event_id is generated at emit time (ULID). For idempotency: rotate/revoke handlers are already idempotent on key state; audit will be at-least-once, so duplicates are possible. Added a note to internal doc: SIEM should dedupe on event_id; for customer pipelines that can’t, we also include request_id + event_type + target_id as a fallback composite key.
Marcus Lin (approval): Approved. Please coordinate flag rollout with exporter normalization timeline (ENG-4827).

Motivation: Canary/A-B promotions in multi-tenant services often react to single-signal thresholds (latency or error rate). That produces noisy rollbacks and opaque decisions for downstream SREs and product owners. This change introduces a lightweight consensus-driven failover controller that aggregates orthogonal signals (p50/p95 latency deltas, availability/error spikes, semantic drift via embedding distance, and synthetic smoke checks) across cohorts to make an explainable pass/fail decision for A/B promotions and canaries.

What this PR does (summary): Adds a new controller (consensus_ab_controller) that: collects metric shards from multiple telemetry sources, computes a configurable quorum using weighted voters, produces a deterministic decision (+trace) for promote/rollback/freeze, and exposes the decision trace to the rollout logs and the Console. Includes a rehearsal harness for shadow traffic that simulates failover decisions offline and an autotune adapter that suggests safe max traffic fractions based on historical variance. Also extends existing rollout API to accept a "decision_trace_url" and a short JSON-LD decision schema for auditability.

Why now: We observed two incidents where a single noisy p95 spike caused a broad rollback even though other signals were healthy. The consensus model reduces sensitivity while improving debuggability for postmortems.

Checklist: - [x] Controller implementation and unit tests - [x] Integration tests with simulated shadow traffic harness - [x] Instrumentation: decision traces + Console hookup - [x] Migration guide and API docs - [x] Performance bench (end-to-end latency impact < 4ms median)

Compatibility/Migration notes: The new controller is opt-in via rollout.policy.type = "consensus". Existing rollout behaviors remain unchanged unless a customer switches policy. Decision traces are stored as ephemeral queryable objects for 7 days by default (configurable per tenant).

Related: Linear ENG-4872 for design doc, SUP-1143 for customer incident follow-up.
Carlos Alvarez: Nice design. Two asks: (1) add a short-circuit for catastrophic downstream errors (e.g., DB outage) so we don't wait for quorum, (2) can we expose per-voter confidence scores in the trace?
Maya Chen (author): Implemented short-circuit rule in d4b1e84; confidence scores are now included in the trace proto and surface in Console (see e7b4a11).
Priya Singh: Unit tests look solid. Integration run failed in first CI due to a race in the rehearsal harness (flaky synthetic generator). Please add a deterministic seed and a retry; also add benchmarking to verify <4ms median overhead.
Maya Chen (author): Added deterministic seed and retry backoff in 9a8e112. Benchmarks attached to PR CI artifacts show median 2.7ms overhead for decision path on our staging fleet.
Ethan Park: Docs look good. One doc nit: clarify retention window for traces (default 7 days) and add example CLI to fetch traces. Also request a small e2e that shows promotion -> failover -> rollback sequence for auditability.
Maya Chen (author): Added retention note and CLI example; added a short e2e replay scenario in tests/integration/test_rehearsal_end2end.py.
Introduce opt-in 'consensus' rollout policy: aggregates multiple telemetry signals for robust promote/rollback decisions. Includes explainable decision traces and rehearsal harness for shadow testing. Opt-in only; existing rollouts unchanged.
Default decision trace retention is 7 days; heavy use (~>50 rollouts/day per tenant) may increase storage — see docs for retention config. Autotune suggestions are advisory; they do not change live traffic without explicit apply.
payload.title: Consensus-led A/B Failover with Explainable Decision Traces
