Context: production traffic patterns show intermittent starvation of small, latency-sensitive requests when the continuous-batcher aggregates large inflight KV-heavy requests. Motivation: reduce p95 tail and avoid unfair queuing without sacrificing batching efficiency or adding hard preemption. This PR introduces a soft-throttle queue-aging mechanism combined with per-request kernel-selection hints and an opportunistic KV prefetch path. Design summary: 1) Soft-throttle aging: requests accrue an aging score while queued; the admission controller uses a decaying soft-reservation that elevates aged requests' priority to break starvation while capping the extra reservation to avoid loss of batch efficiency. 2) Kernel-selection hints: the runtime exposes a lightweight hint (hint.kernel_preference) derived from predicted sequence-length distribution and token-type info. The scheduler uses this hint to preferentially co-locate requests with compatible kernel targets, reducing kernel-switch overhead inside a batch. 3) KV prefetch micro-path: for requests marked as KV-prefetchable, we add a non-blocking prefetch into the KV cache during queuing windows; prefetches are rate-limited by a token bucket per GPU to avoid cache thrash. Implementation notes: - Admission scorer updated in continuous-batcher/admission.cc to track per-request aging_score and soft_reserve_pct (defaults: 12% max uplift, half-life 8s). - Kernel hints flow added at the API layer (serving/proto/request.proto) and plumbed to the scheduler with minimal serialization overhead. - KV prefetch implemented in kv_cache/prefetch.h and invoked by the batcher when a request's hint.kv_prefetch==true. Prefetch uses existing kv-async interfaces and increments an internal prefetch-miss metric to detect ineffective prefetches. Default config changes (runtime flags): --batcher.soft_reserve_pct_max=12 --batcher.soft_reserve_half_life=8s --kv.prefetch_rate_per_gpu=20/s --scheduler.kernel_hint_merge_window=7ms Testing and results: - Unit & integration: added 12 unit tests and 4 integration flows covering aging score transitions, hint propagation, and prefetch backpressure. - Benchmarks (internal lab, A100, mixed toy workload): median latency for small chat requests (<=64 tokens) decreased by 6%, p95 decreased by 22% under mixed load, and overall token throughput was stable (+0.8% measured variance within noise). - Real traffic canary (10% of us-west-2 traffic for 48h): observed 19% fewer latency incidents (alerts crossing 200ms) and no KV cache churn increase beyond expected. Rollout plan: staged canary starting at 5% -> 10% -> 50% with automated rollback on >3% increase in 95th percentile or >1.5x prefetch-miss growth. Monitoring: new metrics emitted: batcher.soft_reserve_uplift, scheduler.kernel_hint_cohort_hits, kv.prefetch_miss_ratio. Backwards compatibility: kernel hint defaults to unset; behavior unchanged unless clients opt into hints or rollout toggles turned on. Risk analysis: main risk is over-prefetching causing KV cache eviction; mitigations: per-GPU rate limits, incremental canary, and metric-based rollback. Misc: added doc string comments in proto and runtime config; preserved feature flags for quick disable.
Liam: Can you justify the 12% default uplift? What was the sensitivity analysis?
Priya: 12% is conservative; we swept in lab from 0-25% and observed diminishing returns beyond 15% and batch efficiency drop >6% after 20% (bench numbers summarized in PR description). Chosen for safety during canary.
Ava: The kernel_hint enum looks fine but ensure forward compatibility if we add more kernel targets. Consider making it extensible (string-based) in the long term.
Priya: Agreed; added comment in proto and feature flag to make migration easier. We'll follow up with an RFC for string identifiers if we add >3 targets.
Diego: KV prefetch backpressure—what if prefetches themselves evict warm keys? How do we detect that?
Priya: We emit kv.prefetch_miss_ratio and kv.prefetch_eviction_delta; canary thresholds will alert on >1.5x. We also lower prefetch rate automatically if miss_ratio climbs beyond 0.2.
Liam: CI flaky on integration; please re-run after fix. (marked as required)
Priya: Re-ran CI after adjusting a timing assert; integration now stable.
Introduce soft-throttle queue-aging to reduce starvation for latency-sensitive requests, add kernel-selection hints to improve kernel co-location within batches, and optional opportunistic KV prefetching during queueing. Configurable flags allow tuning of uplift, half-life, merge window, and prefetch rate. Backwards compatible by default.
payload.title: Improve soft-throttle queue aging with kernel-selection hints and KV prefetch for continuous-batcher

Motivation: Production rollouts have complex failure modes when multi-metric canaries and shadow traffic are used together. Existing controllers could either silently swap traffic back or require manual intervention. This PR introduces a declarative rollback journal and a lightweight safety-probe that records deterministic rollback rationale and enables automated, auditable rollback/replay decisions across canary/A-B/shadow strategies. Design summary: 1) Rollback journal: an append-only, per-rollout record saved in the control plane that stores snapshoted metric windows, decision traces (why a checkpoint failed), and the set of fallback actions taken. Journal entries are immutable and include a deterministic decision-id so downstream automation (alerts, incident tooling) can correlate events. 2) Safety-probe: a small runtime agent that performs low-cost synthetic checks (probe sequences) against candidate model variants using the same routing and KV-cache behavior as production, and reports pass/fail with confidence scores to the rollout controller. 3) Declarative API: new fields on the Rollout CRD (rollbackJournal.enabled, rollbackJournal.retentionDays, safetyProbe.profile, safetyProbe.syntheticRequestsPerMinute) allow operators to opt-in and tune behavior. 4) Compatibility: default behaviour is opt-in; existing rollout flows remain unchanged unless the CR toggles the journal or probe. 5) Failure modes & remediation: journal entries include canonical rollback reasons (latency spike, perplexity regression, toxicity alert) and a suggested remedial action (pause, scale-up, pin-old-model). Implementation highlights: the controller writes journal entries via the existing control plane WAL subsystem and signals a short-lived rollout annotation when a journal entry is created. The safety-probe reuses the serving runtime's routing shim to produce realistic traffic shapes; probes are rate-limited and isolated to avoid perturbing production caches. Testing: added unit, integration, and e2e tests (rollout replay, journal replay, safety-probe edge cases). Rollout plan: staged rollouts across internal clusters for 48h with metric gates and canary percentages, then gradual opt-in for customers using Dedicated. Backwards compatibility: CRD changes are additive; default-off ensures safe upgrade. Open questions: retention policy defaults, and how the journal is surfaced in Console (followup UI PR planned). Related: ENG-1184 (safety automation) and SUP-332 (customer incident that motivated the journal).
Aisha Khan: Can you clarify how the journal is garbage-collected? Suggested retentionDays default to 30.
Evan Park: retentionDays default set to 30 in the CRD; added a config override for infra teams.
Diego Morales: Safety-probe looks good, but probe traffic could affect KV cache hit rates. Please add cache-isolation guard.
Evan Park: added cache isolation toggle and rate-limiter; updated tests to assert no >1% hit-rate change in probe runs.
Priya Nair: e2e flaky on the CI run — integration cluster timed out once, reran and passed. Approved after green e2e.
Samir Patel: lgtm, left minor nit about log verbosity and structured fields.
Added an opt-in rollback journal and safety-probe for rollout controllers. Operators can enable declarative journaling to capture auditable rollback decisions and enable automated safe rollbacks. Safety-probe provides synthetic, low-impact checks for candidate models to reduce false positives during canaries. Default is opt-in; see docs/rollouts/rollback-journal.md for operation and runbook.
If customers report unexpected rollbacks after upgrade, check rollout annotations for journal entries and examine the safety-probe logs. Journal retention defaults to 30 days; retention config is available on the Rollout CRD. If probe traffic affects cache hit rate, toggle safetyProbe.cacheIsolation to true and reopen a followup PR to tune the profile.
payload.title: Declarative rollback journal + safety-probe for automated canaries and shadowed traffic

Motivation: long-tail latency anomalies frequently correlate with kernel-level sparse execution paths that were not instrumented, making it hard to distinguish model-induced vs. runtime-induced latency. This PR adds a sparse-kernel latency mapper plus an invocation context enricher so token-level cost/latency breakdowns include kernel path attribution and prompt shape metadata. Scope: add new metric kernel.latency.sparse{kernel,device,seq_len} with histogram buckets optimized for tail analysis; enrich existing invocation traces with invocation.context.{prompt_shape,kv_cache_hit,quant_cfg,route_variant} tags; Grafana: add a Sparse Kernel Latency panel and a Kernel-Context join dashboard for fast triage; Alerting: introduce a route-aware p95 drift that subtracts baseline kernel-noise and a tunable quiet-window to reduce alert churn. Rollout plan: feature gated (telemetry.feature_flags.sparse_kernel=true) and staged by telemetry shard; start with internal canary -> customer canary -> full rollout. Backwards compat: original metrics retained; new metrics are additive. Checklist: - [x] Metric instrumentation and aggregation (telemetry service) - [x] Trace enrichment and span tagging - [x] Dashboard panels and links to invocation timelines - [x] Alert rules updated and tuned with quiet-window - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Migration notes and ops runbook Changeset summary: 3 logical commits, 23 files, focused on telemetry service, runtime agent, dashboard, and alert rules. Migration instructions: enable feature flag in canary pool; if customers depend on pre-specified label sets, follow ops note to map old -> new labels. Contact: @priya for rollout schedule and emergency rollback. This description contains no embedded diffs; see changed_files for a high-level list.
Ethan Brooks: Can we keep the default histogram buckets aligned with existing kernel latency to make rollups easier? I suggest adding a compatibility mapping layer.
Priya Nair: Added compatibility mapping in telemetry/service/aggregator/mapper.go; kept old buckets as a renormalization step during the first 24h of rollout.
María González: Alerting change looks good, but we need a runtime toggle to disable quiet-window per-tenant. Please add config and tests.
Priya Nair: Added telemetry.service.config.tenant_quiet_window_enabled flag and test coverage in tests/telemetry/test_sparse_kernel_metrics.py. Updated runbook with tenant toggle instructions.
Add kernel.latency.sparse metric and invocation.context tags for prompt_shape/kv_cache_hit; new Grafana dashboards for kernel-context correlation; tuned p95 drift alert with quiet-window to reduce false positives; opt-in via telemetry.feature_flags.sparse_kernel; migration script provided to map legacy labels.

Motivation: customers and internal security reviews highlighted two operational gaps: (1) inconsistent behavior when a service scoped RBACv2 policy referenced KMS keys in multiple regions (we need a deterministic enforcement mode for 'region pin' to avoid silent cross-region key usage), and (2) audit log entries for policy evaluation used non-deterministic IDs which made forensic replays and test harness comparisons brittle. This PR introduces a migration toolchain for RBACv2 policy templates, a conservative opt-in region-pinned KMS enforcement mode, and deterministic audit ID generation. Summary of changes: (a) migration tool: tooling/rbacv2/migrate_policy_templates.py - a CLI that validates legacy role bindings, emits a proposed RBACv2 manifest, and can apply a dry-run diff to a target namespace; it includes a --conservative flag that preserves implicit operator roles to reduce blast radius. (b) region-pinned KMS enforcement: auth/kms/region_pin_enforcer.go and config schema changes (api/v1/security.yaml) add enforcement.mode = [off|warn|enforce] and enforcement.kms_region_preference list. When set to 'enforce' the runtime rejects requests that attempt to use a KMS key outside the declared pinned regions; 'warn' logs an audit event and allows fallthrough to compatible local key variants. (c) audit: internal/audit/deterministic_ids.go replaces timestamp/random UUID mixing with a deterministic ID derived from sha256(namespace + request_id + policy_fingerprint) encoded as base62, ensuring stable IDs for identical evaluation traces (useful for tests and replays). (d) tests and dashboards: added unit + integration tests (tests/rbacv2/*, tests/integration/kms_region_pin) and a Grafana dashboard tile that surfaces 'kms_region_mismatch' audit count. Rollout plan and feature flags: region-pinned behavior is behind a feature flag security.region_pin.enforcement which defaults to off in main. Migration tool produces a Linear export and a suggested canary set of namespaces to opt into 'warn' first. We performed a staged rollout: opt-in with two internal tenants for 48h, observed no rejects, then switched those to 'enforce' with automatic fallback to region-local surrogate keys for specific legacy services. Safety and rollback: the enforcer records an audit event with action=reject/warn and includes the deterministic audit ID; operators can toggle enforcement.mode to off to immediately revert. For migrations that touch many bindings the CLI supports --batch-size and a dry-run CSV export to review. Backwards compatibility notes: when enforcement.mode is off we do not change runtime behavior. Migration tool will not auto-mutate production policies without explicit --apply. Testing and CI: initial CI run failed linting (go vet) on kms enforcer comment formatting; fixed in commit 0002. Integration test harness includes a synthetic KMS provider that simulates cross-region errors and validates that the enforcer surfaces consistent audit entries. Security review: SEC-204 requested explicit audit of fallback paths; added logs and a small counter metric (security_kms_pin_fallback_total). Observability: added tracing spans for policy evaluation fingerprinting and a per-request tag for pinned_region. Documentation: docs/security/rbacv2_migration.md and a short runbook for operators in docs/runbooks/kms_region_pin.md. See release notes for admin guidance.
Reviewer Alice Kim: 'Overall this looks good; two asks: a) can we provide a migration dry-run JSON output that includes suggested enforcement.mode per-namespace based on historical KMS usage? b) please add a short explanation why we use base62 for audit IDs instead of hex.'
Author Marina: 'a) added --export-json in 0001 that emits per-namespace suggestions using a simple heuristic (>=95% single-region usage -> suggest enforce). b) base62 reduces length and is URL-safe without punctuation; added comment and link to RFC in deterministic_ids.go.'
Reviewer Diego Morales: 'Can we avoid a hard reject for services that declare multiple allowed regions but reference a single-key tied to a different region? Suggest warn+metric first.'
Author Marina: 'Agreed. Implementation now checks configured allowed_regions and will only reject when enforcement.mode=enforce and request_key_region not in allowed_regions; otherwise it emits a kms_region_mismatch audit event and increments security_kms_pin_fallback_total. Added integration test to cover this case.'
Reviewer Ravi Shah: 'CI failed earlier; ensure go vet & lint are green and add a short performance note: enforcer should be O(1) per request aside from fingerprint calc.'
Author Marina: 'Addressed linting, and added documentation on expected CPU cost (<0.5% p95 request CPU on busiest path) backed by microbenchmarks in tests/integration. CI green after 0002.'
Approvals: Alice Kim (approved), Diego Morales (approved with one comment addressed), Ravi Shah (LGTM).
- Add RBACv2 migration CLI to generate and validate v2 templates and produce an opt-in enforcement suggestion per namespace.
- Introduce region-pinned KMS enforcement (off|warn|enforce) with safe rollout guidance and a runbook.
- Deterministic audit IDs for policy evaluation traces to improve replayability and forensic matching.
- New metrics: security_kms_pin_fallback_total, and audit events for kms_region_mismatch.
Operators: enable security.region_pin.enforcement=warn before enforce and use the migration CLI --export-json to verify suggested targets.
This PR intentionally keeps enforcement behind a feature flag. The migration CLI is written to be conservative by default (no auto-apply). We coordinated with SRE to schedule canaries and alert rules before wide rollout.
payload.title: Introduce RBACv2 migration toolchain, region-pinned KMS enforcement, and deterministic audit IDs

Motivation: production canary cutovers occasionally expose session-affinity regressions when a model swap drains existing sessions. This PR introduces a session-fenced rolling cutover executor that: 1) acquires a short-lived telemetry lock for a cohort during each step so metrics observed during a step cannot be overwritten by concurrent rollouts, 2) enforces session-fencing on swap so in-flight sessions are either pinned to the old model until completion or moved atomically to a warmed instance depending on policy, and 3) exposes a rewind handle for operator-driven fast revert (replayable snapshot of routing state). This reduces noisy telemetry and avoids mixing signals across overlapping rollouts. Changes included: - new orchestration executor (CutoverExecutor) that sequences cohort-level cutover with lock leases - session fencing mode (pin | migrate) with safe drain heuristics and KV-cache-aware handoff - telemetry lock on the metrics pipeline with lease and ownership tags - lightweight rewind journal that captures routing state + snapshot pointer for immediate revert - integration test harness for simulated multi-cohort traffic and smoke replay Checklist: - [x] CutoverExecutor implementation - [x] Session fence mechanics + migration path - [x] Telemetry lock integration and lease renewal - [x] Rewind journal and revert API - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs: rollout-runbook and operational playbook Notes: this is targeted at the hosted/dedicated control plane and is intentionally backwards-compatible by default; existing rollouts continue to use the previous executor unless customers opt-in via rollout.policy.cutover_strategy. Related linear: ENG-4321 (session fencing design), ENG-4380 (telemetry lock prototype). Rollout impact: opt-in only, no mandatory migration. See the runbook link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4321/session-fenced-cutover
Evan Garcia: Nice separation of concerns. Two requests: (1) add invariants to CutoverExecutor docs about lease expiry behavior; (2) can we make the default pin timeout configurable per cohort?
Maya Chen (author): Responding: added invariants in doc comments and exposed cohort.timeout.pin in rollout policy. Updated tests to exercise shorter lease windows.
Priya Kapoor: Integration test looks comprehensive but I saw a flake when running the migration path under high concurrency. Please add a retry in the handoff path and a comment explaining tradeoffs.
Maya Chen (author): Added exponential backoff retry to handoff and extended test run to cover the flake. Also added a TODO to consider bounded retries in future work.
Liam O'Neil: Approving pending CI. Minor nit: prefer 30s default telemetry lock vs 60s. Not blocking.
Introduces session-fenced rolling cutover executor (opt-in). Adds telemetry lock and rewind journal to allow safe cohort-level cutovers with operator-driven revert. Configuration: rollout.policy.cutover_strategy and rollout.policy.cohort.timeout.pin. See runbook for operational guidance.
payload.title: session-fenced-rolling-cutover-with-telemetry-lock-and-rewind

payload.body:
Motivation: Fleet-level utilization and latency signals conflate multi-tenant workloads. This makes autoscaler decisions noisy and leads to either overprovisioned warm pools or tenant-level SLA regressions. This PR introduces a windowed SLA deconvolution pipeline and a tenant fidelity curve that lets the autoscaler reason about how much enduring throughput a tenant contributes vs transient bursts. Design: 1) Streaming deconvolution operator: consumes per-host aggregated telemetry (p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, queue lengths) and tenant attribution logs to produce per-tenant time-windowed signals (window size configurable, default 60s). 2) Fidelity curve estimator: for each tenant we compute a compact curve mapping lookback window percentiles to an estimated sustainable throughput band. 3) BurstOvertime accountant: new metric that tracks the decay of burst credit usage for a tenant over a rolling 24h window; used to cap burst allocations during autoscaler decisions. 4) Offline warm-pool simulator: a deterministic simulator that replays traces and computes suggested warm-pool sizes and commit hedges given fidelity curves and target SLOs. Implementation highlights: - New package redwood/autoscaler/deconv that implements a fast exponentially-weighted deconvolution algorithm with C++ kernel and Go shim. - Fidelity estimator runs as a controller in the dedicated controller-manager and exposes Prometheus metrics and a small RPC for the autoscaler to query compact tenant curves. - Metrics: introduced rwd_tenant_fidelity_curve{tenant,quantile} and rwd_tenant_burst_overtime_ratio. Both are additive and labeled to be safe for existing dashboards. - Feature flagging: rollout behind feature flag autoscaler.deconv.enabled and autoscaler.fidelity.enabled with a two-stage enable (sim-only -> read-only -> read-write). Backwards compatibility: when deconv is disabled the autoscaler falls back to fleet-aggregated signals. Testing and validation: - Unit+integration tests for the deconvolution kernel and fidelity estimator. - Simulator validation: replayed two weeks of production traces (sanitized) and compared recommended warm-pool delta against historical capacity events; median recommendation error reduced from 24% to 8% in holdout sets. - Canary rollout plan: start with 5% of Dedicated clusters, monitor tenant_slo_violation_count and warm_pool_utilization_ratio for regressions. Observability and ops: added dashboards in grafana/autoscaler showing tenant fidelity heatmaps, burst_overtime per-tenant histograms, and simulator vs actual warm-pool utilization. Migration and safety: the fidelity curve data is stored in the existing time-series store as a namespaced series; retention defaults to 30d and can be increased per-tenant. Rollback plan: flipping feature flags off reverts autoscaler to legacy behavior with no state cleanup required. Related work and tickets: ENG-1982 (deconvolution design), ENG-2041 (simulator), SUP-5342 (customer incident highlighting noisy fleet signals).
Adds a fleet-level -> tenant-level deconvolution pipeline and a fidelity curve used by the autoscaler to recommend warm-pool sizing and burst allowances. Backwards compatible metrics and feature-flagged rollout.
Diego Alvarez: Can we bound memory usage of the C++ kernel under high-cardinality tenants? Suggested adding an LRU eviction for old tenant state.
Maya Chen: Added soft-LRU with configurable shard caps; updated tests to simulate 2M tenant events.
Priya Nandakumar: Metrics look good; one nit on label cardinality for fidelity_curve — suggest coarser quantile bucketing.
Maya Chen: Switched from raw percentiles to 5 fixed quantile buckets in the exporter; updated dashboard panels.
Liam O'Connor: Verified simulator determinism and replay results locally. Approving pending CI.
CI Bot: All checks passed after rerun (flaky network test was retried).
Release Manager: Merged and scheduled feature-flag rollout for 2026-02-25 clusters.
Key risks: cardinality explosion for per-tenant curves (mitigated via quantile bucketing), correctness of deconvolution under extreme multi-tenant colocation (mitigated via offline replay and synthetic stress tests), and potential for autoscaler oscillation when fidelity curves are noisy (mitigated with smoothing window and hysteresis). Please pay attention to memory caps and the RPC schema stability.
Unit: 92 new tests; Integration: replay harness validated on 14 sanitized clusters; Canary: started 5% cluster rollout with no SLO regressions after 48h; observed expected reduction in warm_pool overprovisioning in canary clusters.
Autoscaler: add tenant fidelity curves and burst-overtime accounting; adds simulator to recommend warm-pool sizes and reduces warm-pool overprovisioning.
payload.title: windowed-sla-deconvolution-and-fidelity-curve

payload.body:
Motivation: under mixed chat + embedding workloads we observed persistent KV cache fragmentation and frequent small-page spillovers that increase memory overhead and 95th percentile latency during bursts. This PR introduces an anchor-based prefetch + lease-based eviction windows strategy and an asynchronous anchor compactor to reduce fragmentation without blocking hot-path serving.

What this change does (single-string description): Implements a lightweight CacheAnchors table that tracks granular page anchors (page start addresses and occupancy metadata), a heatmap-driven prefetcher that favors reads around high-occupancy anchors, and a lease eviction window that soft-pins recently-accessed anchors for a decay period to avoid evicting working sets prematurely. Adds an async anchor compactor that performs low-priority page rewrites to defragment scattered entries and coalesce partially-filled pages back into full pages. The eviction logic now considers anchor age, occupancy ratio, and tenant affinity; it exposes runtime knobs for eviction aggressiveness, anchor decay interval, and compactor backoff. Kernel/runtime interaction: adds a small alignment hint to the kernel path to reduce copy overhead for compactor rewrites, and modifies the batching scheduler to allow cooperative compactor CPU time slices without impacting token-level latency.

Why now: recent customer workloads (tenants with thousands of short-lived sessions) showed >20% memory blowup and repeated spill I/O under queued bursts. This approach reduces tail work by avoiding aggressive per-request evictions and amortizing compaction.

Benchmarks: microbench harness (mixed chat+embedding synthetic trace) shows: 95th latency reduced by ~18% (from 210ms to 172ms) for small seqs under 16-GPU cluster; sustained throughput improved ~12% under steady-state load due to fewer spill IOs; resident KV memory usage reduced ~22% after 30 minutes of steady traffic versus current main. Perf tests attached in PR (perf/artifacts).

Compatibility and rollout: all new behaviors are behind runtime feature flags (kv.anchor_prefetch, kv.lease_evict_windows, kv.anchor_compactor). Defaults are disabled in main; tests enable them. Config can be toggled per-tenant in Dedicated/Private deployments.

Testing: unit tests for CacheAnchors and eviction heuristics added; integration test simulates heavy fragmentation and validates compactor eventually reduces page count and that hot-path latencies stay stable. Added telemetry metrics: kv.anchor_hits, kv.anchor_prefetch_count, kv.compactor_rewrites, kv.eviction_window_evictions.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked (ENG-4821) and reviewed by runtime team
- [x] Unit and integration tests added
- [x] Benchmarks run in perf lab and artifacts uploaded
- [x] Runtime knobs exposed and documented

Notes: this is intentionally conservative to avoid regressions in multi-tenant scenarios; compactor rate is capped per-node and backs off automatically on IO pressure.
Diego Marquez (reviewer): Great direction; can you add a small benchmark for cold-start (empty cache) to ensure prefetch doesn't harm startup latency?
Maya Chen (author): Added cold-start perf run and included results in perf/artifacts. Cold-start showed negligible latency change (<2ms median).
Asha Patel (reviewer): Nit: rename 'anchor_age' -> 'anchor_ttl' to be clearer and update godoc. Also please expose compactor rate as a knob.
Maya Chen (author): Renamed field and added kv.anchor_compactor_rate config; updated docs and tests.
Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Integration test flaked once on CI (race in compactor shutdown). Please ensure compactor stops cleanly on shutdown.
Maya Chen (author): Fixed shutdown ordering and added explicit join in tests. Re-ran CI.
Diego Marquez (reviewer): Approve after addressing comments.
payload.title: KV: anchor-based prefetch + lease eviction windows to reduce fragmentation and tail latency

Mitigation: EU-West B200 pool will not select the experimental B200 hardware tuning profile by default; nodes fall back to standard (non-profile / H100-aligned baseline) scheduling + kernel heuristics until the regression is triaged.
Context: During perf-canary + early staged rollout of the B200 experimental tuning profile, eu-west/b200-dedicated showed a repeatable p95 latency regression and elevated retry rate on streaming chat workloads. We are disabling the experimental profile selection in this pool as an immediate mitigation while Kernels/Scheduling dig into root cause. Incident linkage: Slack thread `#incidents` ts=1764395502 ("canary-regression-b200-eu-west-disable-request") and internal follow-up from SRE in `#eng-sre` (rollback criteria / comms). What this changes: (1) Forces `b200_experimental_profile_enabled=false` at the eu-west pool override layer. (2) Adds an explicit allowlist entry so other pools remain unaffected (do not globally disable B200 experimental). (3) Adds a startup log line when pool-level override disables a detected B200 profile, so oncall can quickly confirm effective config. (4) Updates the oncall mitigation playbook snippet (runbook link) with the exact toggle and expected runtime log/metric changes. Scope / safety: This is a hotfix limited to eu-west pool config + a small guardrail in selection logic to emit a structured reason tag. No schema changes. No behavior change for H100/L40S. Testing: Unit tests for override precedence are already present; this adds one focused regression test for "pool override disables experimental profile". CI ran full runtime unit/integration suite on the release branch. Rollout plan: Merge to release/runtime-1.18, deploy to eu-west canary pool first (10% of nodes), verify `runtime_profile_selected` metric drops the `b200-experimental/*` label to `none` or `default` and p95 returns to baseline, then expand to 100% of eu-west/b200-dedicated. Follow-ups: (a) root-cause analysis in ENG-4826 with perf traces and scheduler fairness knobs; (b) tighten perf-canary thresholds to reduce noise but keep this regression class caught; (c) ensure docs for B200 profile reference includes explicit maturity + region gating language.
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Please make sure this is pool-scoped only. We still want experimental enabled in the us-east sandbox pool for debugging. Also add a log/metric reason so oncall can confirm the override is active without SSHing.
Irene Choi (author): Yep — pool override only. I added a structured log line `profile_selection_override_reason=pool_disable_experimental` and an integration test to lock behavior.
Benji Okafor: Can you confirm precedence order? We should be disabling before hardware detection chooses the B200 profile, otherwise we might still end up applying partial defaults.
Irene Choi (author): Precedence is: explicit per-deployment override > pool override > fleet default > auto-detect. The disable happens after detection but before applying any knob set; the log shows detected SKU + suppressed profile name + override source.
Hiro Tanaka: Any chance this masks a kernel selection mismatch that we should keep visible? I'd prefer we keep the metric label for "detected b200" even if profile is suppressed.
Irene Choi (author): We keep `gpu_sku=b200` and emit `profile_selected=default` plus `profile_override_source=pool` and `profile_override_reason=disable_experimental` so we can still segment eu-west B200 performance while profile is off.
Neha Kapoor (SRE sponsor): Add rollback criteria in the PR description (what metrics and thresholds) and ensure docs mention expected impact (p95 drop back, retries normalize).
Irene Choi (author): Added rollout verification bullets + updated the mitigation runbook snippet with exact dashboards to check.
Vanessa Ortiz: Approved. This is the least risky mitigation; we can re-enable once ENG-4826 has a validated fix.
Sean Gallagher: Approved. Please ping #eng-oncall once the canary deploy is complete.
payload.title: Hotfix: disable B200 experimental hardware profile in eu-west pool

Background and motivation: several customers reported ambiguous operator-level access where service operator tokens could perform cross-tenant KMS lookups during a paging incident (SUP-711). This PR introduces two coordinated features: (1) an operator-boundary RBAC shim that enforces RBAC v2 constraints at operator scope (prevents operator-scoped principals from implicitly gaining tenant-scoped capabilities), and (2) a KMS region assertor that validates KMS key usage is compatible with the request's declared region and emits an immutable provenance entry into the audit pipeline. Additionally, an audit fanout path is added so KMS provenance and operator-claim metadata are forwarded to the long-term audit store and to an internal mini-index for fast residency queries. Design summary: - Operator-boundary RBAC shield: new RBAC middleware evaluates an incoming request's operator claim and enforces deny-by-default rules for any tenant-scoped actions. It plugs into RBAC v2 decision flow and exposes a lightweight allowlist for explicitly delegated operator actions. Configuration is via the existing RBAC policy bundles with two new annotations: "operator_scope: true" and "operator_allowed_actions". - KMS region assertor: at KMS call sites, we validate the key's declared region against the request's region/geo-claim. Failures are surfaced as a 403 with a machine-readable audit tag. For compatibility we add a non-blocking "warn" mode toggle controlled by feature-flag rbac.operator_kms_assert_mode (warn|enforce). - Audit fanout: the KMS assertor emits an immutable provenance record (kms_provenance_v1) to the audit writer. The writer has an option to fanout a summarized message to the compliance index (for fast residency checks) and to the long-term blob store. Rollout plan: feature gated behind rbac.operator_boundary flag. Start in warn mode for two weeks for telemetry collection, then opt-in rollouts by account for enforcement. Ops tasks: add alert (rbac.operator_assert_fail_rate > 0.5% per hour) and dashboard panels for "operator_assertions", "kms_provenance_skips", and "audit_fanout_latency_ms". Compatibility and migration: existing RBAC policies remain valid but bundles that intend operator delegation must add the operator_scope annotation. KMS providers that don't surface region metadata will be treated as unknown-region and will be logged; we provide a helper adapter to enrich provider responses. Testing and validation: unit tests for the RBAC decision path; integration tests exercising operator-scoped tokens against tenant actions; end-to-end e2e against local KMS stub verifying audit fanout. Security review: design reviewed by SEC/Privacy and includes threat scenarios for operator privilege escalation, replay attacks on KMS provenance, and audit tampering mitigations. Documentation: updated auth/rbac/README and added a short runbook for incident responders.
Lena Zhou: Can we avoid adding a second policy language? Keep annotations consistent. — Aisha: Operator annotations reuse the existing RBAC bundle syntax, documented in the README. Owen Gallagher: How will this interact with Dedicated/Private deployments where KMS is customer-managed? — Aisha: The assertor uses provider metadata; for customer-managed KMS we fall back to 'provider-declared-region' and the warn mode lets customers opt-in after validating provider metadata. Priya Menon: Request adding a metric for 'assert_mode_mismatches' and a log-level change for warn-mode hits. — Aisha: Added metrics and lowered log volume in warn mode. Lena: LGTM after tests. Owen: Approved after nit on error messages addressed. CI: one flaky e2e on first run, rerun succeeded. Merge: squashed and merged by Aisha on 2026-02-12.
Security: add operator-boundary RBAC guard to prevent operator-scoped principals from performing tenant-scoped KMS actions; KMS: introduce optional region assertor and provenance auditing; Ops: new feature flags and dashboards for operator/KMS assertion telemetry
Ops: enable rbac.operator_boundary in staging, monitor 'operator_assertions' and 'kms_provenance_skips' for two weeks before enforcement. Support: notify key enterprise customers with custom KMS setups about the warn->enforce rollout window.
payload.title: Introduce operator-boundary RBAC shield + KMS region assertor and audit fanout

Motivation: tri-SDK users repeatedly asked for a small, explicit surface to express reauthentication windows and retry profiles while keeping streaming ergonomics consistent across Python/TS/Go. This PR introduces a lightweight ReauthProfile abstraction, a StreamSampler adapter to reduce noisy heartbeats for low-throughput real-time consumers, and alignment changes so Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs present the same defaults and helper names. Key goals: 1) reduce auth-related 401s during long-lived streams by adding configurable preemptive refresh windows; 2) offer pluggable retry presets that map to the platform's circuit/retry guidance; 3) provide a StreamSampler observer that suppresses frequent keepalive emissions for samplers marked as low-volume and aggregates telemetry into periodic hearts instead of per-chunk pings. Summary of changes: - Core: Add ReauthProfile (fields: refresh_window_ms, max_concurrent_refresh, jitter_ms) and surface helpers (from_env, from_static) implemented in tri-shared package. - SDK surfaces: Python: new ReauthProfile class, stream.sampler factory helper, refined AsyncIterator backpressure defaults. TypeScript: exported types and builder functions, added sampler decorator for ReadableStream consumers. Go: compact ReauthProfile struct, helper constructors, and a StreamSampler interface with default implementation. - Retries: introduce named retry presets (default, aggressive, conservative) and adapters to map to platform retry hints; SDKs now include telemetry tags for which preset was used. - Telemetry & CI: added unit + integration tests for reauth timing, sampler suppression tests, and smoke across all three SDKs; CI matrix added a flaky test tolerance entry. - Docs/Changelog: update quickstarts for streams to show reauth usage and sampler example; bump SDK versions: py 1.13.0 -> 1.14.0, ts 2.9.1 -> 2.10.0, go 0.8.4 -> 0.8.5. Backwards compatibility: all new APIs are additive; defaults preserve previous behavior. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked and approved in ENG-1459; - [x] Implementations in Python/TS/Go; - [x] Unit + integration tests; - [x] Docs and examples updated; - [x] Version bumps and changelog entries. Why unique: Combines an auth-window primitive with a streaming-specific sampler to address two correlated real-world pain points (auth drift on long streams and noisy keepalives) with a compact cross-SDK surface. Rollout plan: release SDKs in coordinated minor bumps, notify customers via changelog, enable new StreamSampler in a feature-flagged sample in the console for early adopters.
Aisha Khan: Nice narrow surface; can we add an option to disable preemptive refresh entirely for very short-lived streams? Author: added from_static(None) to indicate disabled refresh and documented behavior.
Tomás Rivera: CI matrix shows one flaky streaming test on Node14. Action: pinned node image in CI and reran. Result: passed on rerun.
Marta Novak: Telemetry tag naming needs to align with existing SDK metric keys. Author: adjusted telemetry key to 'sdk.auth.reauth_profile' and added mapping tests.
Added ReauthProfile and StreamSampler across Python/TS/Go SDKs to improve robustness of long-lived streams and reduce noisy keepalive telemetry. Introduced named retry presets and bumped SDK versions: py 1.14.0, ts 2.10.0, go 0.8.5.
payload.title: tri-sdk: lightweight reauth profiles, stream-sampler adapter, and parity ergonomics

Motivation: customers operating under strict data residency constraints asked for a first-class "privacy zone" concept that ties RBAC claims, KMS usage, and audit metadata together. This PR implements a zone-scoped RBACv2 hard-guard (policy enforcement instead of best-effort tagging), anchors KMS operations to region-pinned CMKs, and emits a compact "audit delta" sink with zone + key provenance so downstream compliance tooling can prove residency and key-origin. The change is intentionally surgical: the new enforcer is pluggable and gated behind a feature flag (feature.privacy_zones.enabled) and a rolling rollout can be performed per cluster via operator config. Checklist: - Implement zone-aware policy evaluator (RBACv2) that denies requests if zone claim/key mismatch. - Add KMS anchoring middleware to annotates decrypt/encrypt calls with cmk-region and enforcement mode. - Add audit-delta sink that tags audit events with zone, cmk_origin, and enforcement_decision. - Surface policy editor in Console (read-only for GA; edit via YAML for now). - Add unit and integration tests, plus a small e2e scenario using test-kms emulator. Related: ENG-4198 (design doc), SEC-1224 (compliance signoff). Rollout notes: enable feature flag in canary region first; RBAC policy migration includes a one-time background scan that annotates tenants with inferred zone where available. For tenants without a zone, the enforcer defaults to "opt-in" behavior until tenant metadata is set. If the feature is turned on in enforcement mode, mismatches will be rejected and will surface QC alerts. Implementation details: - Enforcer lives in authorization/zone_enforcer.go and plugs into the existing RBACv2 path as an additional policy step; it evaluates the request's tenant_claims.zone, service_region and the configured policy matrix. - KMS anchoring is implemented as a proxy shim (infra/kms/anchor_proxy.py) that consults the configured cmk registry and rejects operations if the requested cmk is out-of-region for the request zone; it emits a KMS_PROVENANCE header consumed by the audit delta sink. - Audit delta sink (observability/audit_delta_sink.go) batches lightweight audit deltas (event_id, zone, cmk_origin, decision, timestamp) which are forwarded to the compliance indexer. - Console adds a new read-only "Privacy Zones" page with a per-tenant summary and policy preview. - Helm/installer additions: new values.privacyZones.* keys and operator RBAC changes for the background annotator. Migration: background annotator will run as a job (k8s) that is idempotent; rollback is safe (feature flag off => enforcement disabled). Security review notes: added extra checks in the KMS proxy to ensure authorization context is preserved; a lint-level security scanner flagged a potential header propagation gap which has been fixed. Testing: unit tests for policy behavior, integration with test-kms emulator, e2e scenario using a synthetic tenant with zone=eu-west. Signoffs: security, compliance, and infra.
Elliot Kim: Nice high-level design. Can you clarify the interaction with existing fallback routing? If a region-pinned CMK is unavailable we should fallback to a tenant-level policy rather than a blind reject.
Author (Dana Park): We explicitly do not allow silent fallback when enforcement=true. The background annotator tries to populate tenant zone metadata to avoid surprises; fallback can be enabled via 'enforcementMode: permissive' in the helm values for a controlled roll-out.
Mariana Silva: Tests look good overall, but I saw a flaky assertion in the e2e that was failing on CI (timeout). Please replace time.Sleep with an event wait and re-run.
Author (Dana Park): Replaced with event-driven wait; pushed a small fix. CI re-run addressed the flake.
Rajesh Patel: Please add a metric for 'zone_enforcer.denied_by_zone' and an audit-level histogram for audit-delta forwarding latency. Also ensure the KMS proxy logs cmk_id with redaction at debug level.
Author (Dana Park): Added prometheus counters and an audit-latency histogram; KMS proxy logs are now redacted by default and only expose cmk fingerprint at debug.
Mariana Silva (approving): Security review complete, checked header propagation and mitigations for header spoofing. Approving pending 1 doc tweak.
Elliot Kim (approved): Approve. Recommend canary enablement in eu-west only for first week.
Repo automation (merge-bot): All required approvals present and CI green. Ready to squash-merge.
payload.title: Privacy zones: RBACv2 hard-guard, KMS anchoring, and audit delta sink

Adds a Lag-Compensating Provision Oracle (LCPO) to reduce SLA violations caused by autoscaler headroom lag and introduces a burst diagnostic exporter that correlates utilization spikes with latency signals to help ops tune conservative headroom and soft-burst policies. Motivation: incidents in January showed short-duration microbursts that the existing warm-pool/autoscaler paths reacted to too slowly, creating transient latency spikes for dedicated tenants. LCPO uses short-horizon demand extrapolation, weighted recent-util deltas, and a lightweight speculative allocate path to create ephemeral buffer credits that bridge the autoscaler ramp-up window. The exporter emits compact correlation events (burst_event_id, tenant, pool, util_before, util_after, latency_p50/p95, decision_reason) to the telemetry pipeline for offline debugging and live dashboards. This PR contains controller logic, config knobs (speculative_credit_limit, compensation_decay_ms, signal_weighting), unit and integration tests, a performance test harness for end-to-end microburst replay, and docs for rollout and observability. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-3982) [x] unit tests [x] integration e2e harness [x] load/perf test [x] telemetry schema and Grafana dashboard prototype [x] upgrade-safe migration notes. Rollout plan: staged canary to 5% pools with feature flag; monitor burst_diagnostic.events and latency regressions for 3 days; increase to 25% then general availability if no regressions. Backout: disable feature flag and revoke speculative credits; rollback is safe because core autoscaler path unchanged. Risk: speculative credits can increase short-term GPU usage; mitigated by global speculative_credit_limit and tenant-level caps. Notes: this does not change billing semantics, credits are accounted in telemetry for future billing policy work.
Ethan Morales: Nice design and tests. Two concerns: (1) global speculative_credit_limit feels permissive — can we add a circuit-breaker that prevents speculative credits if cluster-wide GPU utilization > 85%? (2) add more comments on how credits affect actual slot allocation to avoid confusion in the allocator code.
Priya Nandakumar: Addressed both: added a circuit-breaker check in ledger.go (threshold default 85%) and added docstrings + README section describing how speculative credits map to allocation reservations. Updated tests to exercise high-cluster-util rejection.
Liang Chen: telemetry schema looks good but please include an enum for decision_reason and make burst_event_id deterministic (hash of tenant+window) for easier debugging across services.
Priya Nandakumar: Switched decision_reason to an enum and made burst_event_id a truncated SHA256 digest; added mapping doc to mappings.yaml and updated exporter tests.
Marisol Ortega: Integration perf run looks fine, but watch memory use in ledger when many tenants create ephemeral credits concurrently. Suggested a bounded LRU cache for stale entries.
Priya Nandakumar: Implemented bounded LRU with eviction after 1h idle; added metrics lcpo_ledger_entries and lcpo_evictions_total.
CI Bot: go vet and linters passed. Perf job (microburst_replay) completed: p95 latency improved by 12% for replayed bursts, speculative credit usage averaged 3.2% of dedicated capacity during 30s spike windows.
Release Manager: Approved for canary under feature flag; include rollout checklist in release notes.
Introduce LCPO (Lag-Compensating Provision Oracle) that can provide short-lived speculative buffer credits to reduce transient latency during microbursts. Adds burst diagnostic exporter for correlating utilization spikes with latency signals. Rollout behind feature flag. See docs/ops/lcpo-rollout.md for canary steps and operational playbook.
Feature is gated by feature flag feature.lcpo.enabled and additional knobs speculative_credit_limit (global), tenant_speculative_limit, compensation_decay_ms. Monitor metrics: lcpo_credits_allocated_total, lcpo_credits_rejected_total, lcpo_evictions_total, burstdiag_events_emitted, and existing latency SLO metrics. Backout by turning off the feature flag and clearing ephemeral credits via admin API.
Unit tests cover ledger accounting and extrapolator heuristics. Integration e2e harness replays recorded microburst traces against a canary cluster to validate latency wins and speculative credit safety. Perf job executed across 3 pool topologies; results in PR show median p95 latency reduction and <4% average extra capacity during spikes.
(1) Deploy telemetry mapping to staging ingest cluster (2) Add burstdiag events to dashboards and alert rules (3) Run 72-hour canary on 5% pools and collect LCPO metrics (4) Iterate on default compensation_decay_ms if eviction/oscillation observed
payload.title: Introduce lag-compensating provision oracle and burst diagnostic exporter

Motivation: under mixed latency and bursty workloads the paged KV cache showed high pin churn and repeated allocation/eviction thrashing. This PR introduces a transient 'shadow pool' that holds recently freed blocks for a short handoff window, plus a compacting handoff path that coalesces small free fragments to reduce allocator fragmentation. The change also adjusts allocator scheduling heuristics to prefer locality-aligned reuse and adds light kernel hints to avoid expensive scheduler wakeups during hot-path reuse.

What this PR does: - Adds a transient shadow pool that accepts unpinned blocks for a configurable grace period before they become globally reclaimable. Shadow pool entries can be handed off directly to new allocators with a lock-light queue to avoid full freelist ops. - Implements a compacting handoff routine: when a shadow entry is larger than a threshold and adjacent free segments exist, we coalesce them before exposing back to the global pool. Compaction is opportunistic and bounded by a CPU budget to avoid SLO impact. - Introduces a pin-handoff fastpath that lets the serving runtime transfer ownership of a block to a new request without a full unpin/pin cycle where safe, reducing atomic ops on high-contention pages. - Adds allocator scheduling tweaks: favor same-CPU locality bins for repeated prefixes, and a hysteresis timer to avoid oscillation between pools. - Adds unit and integration tests covering handoff races, compaction budget exhaustion, and metrics. - Documented new knobs in docs/ops/kv-cache.md and added a short explainer in CHANGELOG.

Compatibility and safety: The handoff fastpath is gated behind a runtime flag (kv.shadow_handoff_enabled=false by default) and a strict verification step that rejects handoff when there are any outstanding long-lived transactions. Compaction runs with a bounded work budget and will fallback to the previous fast free path if it cannot complete within the budget. No on-disk format changes.

Performance summary (local bench): - 95th percentile token latency improved by 12% under mixed read/write workloads with small working set churn. - End-to-end throughput improved by ~8% under high-concurrency synthetic workloads due to reduced allocator CAS contention. - Memory fragmentation metric (measured as external fragmentation ratio) decreased ~15% in long-running steady-state runs.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc and benchmarks attached (ENG-7721) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests (kv-cache stress harness) - [x] Feature gated behind runtime flag - [x] Docs updated - [x] Smoke-tested on canary cluster

Notes for reviewers: pay special attention to race handling in handoff_queue.{cc,h} and to the compaction budget enforcement in compactor.{cc}. The patch that touches scheduler hints is deliberately small; we're conservative there to avoid regressions.

References: ENG-7721 (design), ENG-7815 (bench harness), SUP-234 (customer incident that motivated change)
Introduces a transient shadow pool with lock-light handoff to reduce pin/unpin churn and improve reuse; reclaim/compact path added to reduce fragmentation under mixed workloads.
Lucas Chen (2026-02-11): Nice reduction in CAS noise. Please add stronger assertions around handoff queue ABA scenarios; I pushed a small test suggestion.
Maya Patel (2026-02-12): Added assertion and extended stress test to cover ABA case; test now reproduces previously-flaky scenario reliably.
Avery Singh (2026-02-14): Can we make compaction CPU budget a runtime knob? Concerned about tail latency on small machines.
Maya Patel (2026-02-15): Added budget knob and lowered default for small-instance bands; documented behavior in kv-cache.md.
Priya Nair (2026-02-16): CI flake on ubuntu-20 integration test; looks like a timing-dependent test, reworked to be less timing-sensitive.
Lucas Chen (2026-02-17): Approved after tests and comments addressed. Marking for squash-merge.
payload.title: Transient shadow pool: handoff-driven compacting & reduced pin churn for paged KV cache

payload.body:
Title: Fix benchmark regression/variance caused by decode-loop debug logging

Context
We traced the p95 jitter/throughput regression seen in the FP8/INT8 matrix runner (especially H100 decode-heavy cases) to a debug logging path that was accidentally left enabled in the “benchmark” execution mode. The logging was on the hot path (per-step / per-batch) and was also triggering extra string formatting + mutex contention in spdlog sinks. This perturbed kernel scheduling enough to show as benchmark variance and, in a few cases, flipped the apparent winner between baseline vs quantized paths.

This PR removes the hot-path debug logs from the decode loop and gates the remaining instrumentation behind an explicit opt-in flag that is OFF by default in all benchmark runners.

What changed
- Remove per-iteration debug logs in decode loop (token step) and prefill inner loop.
- Keep a small amount of high-level progress logging (once per request / once per batch) at INFO.
- Add an explicit runtime flag and env gate for verbose benchmark logging:
  - CLI: --bench_debug_logging (default: false)
  - Env: RW_BENCH_DEBUG_LOGGING=1 (only honored when --bench_debug_logging=true)
  - Rationale: accidental env-only enablement was too easy; we now require explicit CLI intent.
- Ensure benchmark harness forces these off:
  - benchmark runner now passes --bench_debug_logging=false explicitly
  - removed legacy RW_VERBOSE_BENCH_LOGS support (was enabling the path implicitly)
- Add a small guard macro around formatting-heavy debug code to avoid even evaluating fmt args when disabled.

Why this is safe
- Debug logging was not used for production runtime decisions; it was only intended for local troubleshooting.
- The new logging is opt-in and has a dedicated flag name to avoid collisions with existing --verbose / --log_level.
- No functional changes to kernel selection or scheduler behavior besides removing side effects.

Evidence / before & after
- Reproduced on H100 (decode-heavy workload: long generations, concurrency=32) using the matrix runner config from ENG-7428.
- Before:
  - tokens/s variance: ~9–13% run-to-run (same commit, same node)
  - p95 TPOT jitter spikes aligned with log sink backpressure
- After:
  - tokens/s variance: ~1.5–2.8% run-to-run
  - p95 TPOT stable; no spikes correlated with logging

Implementation notes
- We previously had a log statement inside the decode step loop that ran at DEBUG but the benchmark container set log_level=debug by default for an unrelated issue (trace collection). That effectively enabled the statement.
- The statement also used fmt::format with a couple of large structs (shape + scheduler state), which was costly even when the sink dropped messages.
- New code uses a fast boolean gate and avoids formatting work entirely unless explicitly enabled.

Changed areas (high level)
- runtime/scheduler/decode_loop.cc: remove per-step debug logging and guard remaining debug-only instrumentation
- runtime/bench/bench_flags.cc: add --bench_debug_logging flag and env validation
- tools/benchmark_runner/run_matrix.py: explicitly disable bench debug logging
- docs/internal/benchmarking.md: update “how to enable debug logs” section + note about perf impact

Illustrative snippet
Before:
  SPDLOG_DEBUG("decode step={} qdepth={} shapes={} ...", step, qdepth, shapes_to_string(...));
After:
  if (UNLIKELY(bench_debug_logging_enabled)) {
    SPDLOG_DEBUG("decode step={} qdepth={} shapes={} ...", step, qdepth, shapes_to_string(...));
  }

Commits
- runtime: remove decode hot-path debug logs
- runtime: add bench_debug_logging flag + env gate
- benchmark-runner: pass explicit default flags
- docs: update benchmarking debug logging guidance

Checklist
- [x] Reproduced variance regression on H100 and confirmed fix
- [x] Verified no change in outputs/correctness (same seeds, same prompts)
- [x] Confirmed matrix runner defaults keep logs OFF
- [x] Added note to internal benchmarking docs

Review conversation (highlights)

Motivation: Long conversational sessions and evolving prompt shapes have produced low-frequency but high-impact cost/latency tail events that escape uniform sampling and cause noisy SLO alerts. This PR introduces two complementary observability features: 1) an entropy-guided invocation sampler that biases trace sampling toward invocations with high token-level entropy, abrupt token-cost drift, or rare argument shapes; and 2) a session flamegraph summarizer that compacts long multi-turn invocations into stage-level frames (prompt, model-run, tool-calls, post-processing) with stacked token-cost/latency bars so humans can quickly scan where cost accumulates across a session. The description below lists changes, tests, reviewers' discussion, CI results, and deployment notes.

What this does (high level):
- Add entropy-based scoring to the invocation sampler (telemetry/sampler/*). Sampler computes a lightweight per-invocation entropy estimate and a delta token-cost drift metric; these are combined into a dynamic sampling weight so we retain more traces from noisy long-tail cases without increasing overall storage significantly.
- Add a session flamegraph summarizer (observability/flamegraph/*) that reduces long token streams into a compact JSON summary and a small set of representative spans for trace UI and alert links.
- Dashboard: new "Session Flamegraph" panel and a "Entropy Drift Explorer" heatmap in observability/dashboards/session-flamegraph.json.
- Alert tuning: new rule that warns only when entropy-weighted cost percentiles exceed baseline AND the session flamegraph indicates concentrated cost in the model-run stage (reduces false positives from client-side retries).
- Tests: unit tests for sampler heuristics, e2e replay bench to validate sampling budget, and a small perf microbench for summarizer latency.

Why this is different: existing sampling is mostly frequency- or cost-proportional which misses high-entropy failure modes (e.g., malformed prompts, adversarial inputs, or sudden prompt-shape drift). Entropy-guided sampling targets those rare but high-value traces. The session flamegraph focuses investigator attention on stage-level attribution rather than token-level noise so SREs and engineers can triage faster.

- [x] Summarizer proto and serializer with backwards-compatible metric labels

Context: We observed sporadic user reports where structured tool/function call outputs (tool call JSON objects) emitted over SSE could arrive with mismatched framing when upstream fragmentation produced skewed byte offsets. In practice this manifested as: (1) toolcall JSON emitted across multiple fragments with fragment offsets shifted by preceding heartbeat/event fragments, and (2) downstream OpenAI-compatible adapters sometimes reassembled fragments using a strict append order, producing truncated or duplicated JSON boundaries under backpressure. This PR introduces an offset-resynchronization layer and a toolcall-boundary mapper to make reassembly idempotent and order-agnostic.
fix(sse/parser): introduce fragment offset map and resync algorithm
feat(sse/handler): add toolcall_boundary_mapper to align JSON span start/end against resync table
chore(tests): add deterministic replay tests and new fixtures for interleaved heartbeats
docs: update CHANGELOG and observability notes
Samir: Can you explain how this interacts with the existing checkpoint/replay flow? Are there cases where we might drop a fragment due to a stale seq?
Author (Marina): The resync table is keyed by stream id + seq window. We never drop fragments on mismatch; instead we record an offset correction and replay locally. Only fragments that fail checksum validation after correction are dropped and surfaced to metrics.
Jordan: Tests look thorough; one nit around naming in offset_map.go (suggested an exported method rename). Also please add a short explanation to sse_metrics.md for the new 'sse.fragment_offset_corrections' counter.
Aisha: Verified that OpenAI adapter changes preserve function-call sentinel ordering. I ran the repro from SUP-7783 locally and saw consistent reconstruction across multiple client replay strategies.

Motivation: presubmit latency and toolchain image churn are major contributors to developer feedback time and CI cost on large PRs. This change splits the monolithic toolchain image into minimal language+tool bundles, wires a presubmit 'weight' selector so only relevant bundles are prepared for a change, and adds a release quiesce hook to reduce rollout churn during lockfile rotations.

What this PR does: 1) Introduces 'toolchain manifests' that declare minimal sets of binaries for each language bundle (node, python, go, rust). 2) Adds a lightweight image builder action (ci/actions/slim-toolchain) and small Dockerfiles for each language bundle. 3) Reworks presubmit workflow to select bundles based on path heuristics and an annotation on the PR (ci/presubmit/workflows/lint.yml). 4) Adds a release-side 'quiesce' hook (scripts/release/quiesce-hook.sh) that delays non-critical rollouts for up to 10 minutes during dependency rotation windows to avoid cascading redeploys. 5) Adds docs and a migration guide for infra and contributors.

Testing done: local action tests in a containerized runner, staged presubmit run on a fork with path heuristics, smoke deploy to staging with release quiesce toggled, and end-to-end CI run in the main pipeline (see CI checks).

Rollout plan: feature-gate enabled by default for main only after a 2-week dogfood period; a monitoring dashboard will track presubmit duration and image build count. If presubmit failures or significant regressions appear, the gate can be toggled off and we will revert the presubmit selector (rollback instructions documented).

Problem: sudden traffic handoffs from shadow verification to canary can cause flapping, cold-cache misses, and blind regressions when upstream models have stateful behavior or different KV cache warmup profiles. Goal: provide a conservative, observable, and automated handoff that requires transient stability before increasing live traffic. Changes: 1) Observation buffer: configurable time-window and minimum sample thresholds for key metrics (latency P95, error-rate, token-rejects, and quality regression score) collected from shadow runs. 2) Hysteresis gates: require metrics to remain within pass thresholds for N consecutive observation windows before each traffic step. 3) Circuit-breaker on regressions: immediate halt+roll-back to previous stable model variant when regression thresholds are exceeded; supports automated freeze and owner notification. 4) KV-cache warmup probe: background prefix-warm requests that run during low-traffic windows; reported as warmup progress in rollout state. 5) Phased traffic table: declarative phase definitions (percent, duration, min-samples) that the rollout controller enforces. 6) Simulation harness: offline simulator that replays shadow logs to validate config and estimate warmup time. 7) Observability: new rollout metrics (rollout_phase, obs_window_pass_rate, warmup_progress) and Grafana dashboards + alert rules. 8) Compatibility: fallback to existing canary flow if controller CRD absent. Motivation and rationale: this consolidates manual heuristics customers were using into a first-class policy that reduces incidents during model swaps and gives operators clear indicators and rollback guarantees. Design notes: observation windows are sliding with an exponential backoff if metrics oscillate; hysteresis windows are bounded to prevent indefinite stalls; circuit-breaker supports soft stop (hold traffic) and hard rollback. Rollout controller integrates with existing routing and model variant catalog so swaps are atomic at routing level. Implementation summary: added a new RolloutPhase controller module, a small in-memory state-machine for phase transitions, metrics exporters, warmup probe worker, and a simulator CLI. Tests: unit coverage for state transitions, integration test that spins up a minimal local routing stack and validates handoff behavior, and two e2e replay tests against historical shadow logs. How to review: focus on controller state machine correctness, metric thresholds wiring, and failure modes around datastore/network partitions. Related: references ENG-11234 for prior prototyping and SUP-4421 for a field incident that motivated hysteresis.

Context: We need a single controller that codifies staged promotions (canary/A-B), shadow rehearsals and predictable automated rollback behavior across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments. Motivation: disparate rollout implementations make cross-environment guarantees hard (different telemetry, different early-stop rules). This PR implements the "Orbit" rollout choreographer — a modular controller that composes: 1) cost-SLO cutpoints: dynamic holdpoints that evaluate both latency/error SLOs and per-token cost deltas; 2) synthetic shadow rehearsal: lightweight synthetic traffic runner that exercises new model paths with sampled inputs to detect regressions not visible in live mirrors; 3) counterfactual A/B gating: run A/B buckets with replayed sessions to estimate delta and bias-adjust results; 4) rollback playbook automation: deterministic steps for quarantine, snapshot restore, and staged traffic rewind if multiple gates fail.

Summary of changes (high-level commits):
- feat: controller core, state machine for Orbit (modular phases + holdpoint evaluation)
- feat: synthetic shadow runner + lightweight recorder and seed generator
- feat: cost-SLO evaluator and configurable thresholds per-customer/profile
- test: unit + integration harness for phased promotes and rollback scenarios
- infra: RBAC + Helm values to enable Orbit in Private installs
- docs: rollout reference and operator playbook

Commits: 6 commits (see abbreviated):

- Samira (review): "We should avoid automatically executing snapshot restores without human approval for enterprise tier; propose a tier-gated automaton."
- Priya: "Added tier gating in the policy parser and Helm value toggle; default behavior: auto-retain but require manual snapshot restore for enterprise (docs updated)."
- Evan (review): "CI showed a flaky replay test initially (timeout). Isolate and increase timeout for the slow path; also add a retry loop to the synthetic runner."

Observability/Telemetry:

Motivation: Improve stream lifecycle robustness in client disconnect/reconnect scenarios while preserving OpenAI-compatible semantics. We observed increased user-facing duplicate tool invocations and opaque stream terminations when a client rejoined after a network hiccup. This PR introduces a lightweight server lease/watchdog and a client heartbeat protocol plus small changes to the OpenAI compatibility adapter to handle soft cancels and resume semantics with explicit tool-call confirmation tokens.

What this PR does (single string): Adds a lease-based server watchdog that keeps a short-lived lease for active streaming sessions and enforces a soft-quarantine on abandoned sessions. Implements a client heartbeat (periodic ping tied to the session lease) so the server can distinguish short disconnects from abandoned streams. Introduces a confirmation token attached to tool/function call events: when the server emits a tool call to a downstream executor, it attaches a monotonically-increasing confirmation id; on reconnect the client and server reconcile outstanding confirmation ids to avoid duplicate retries. The OpenAI adapter maps the new internal soft-cancel event to the existing stop/abort codes and maintains the previous wire format for backwards compatibility. Adds configuration knobs: lease_ttl, heartbeat_interval, reconnect_grace_window, and fallback_routing_policy (how to route resumed sessions to alternate capacity pools). Includes unit and integration tests that simulate flaky connectivity, delayed reconnects, and tool call retries.

Commit summary: (high level)
- a1b3d2c: add lease manager and watchdog loop, TTL enforcement and metrics
- 7f4e1b0: implement client heartbeat handler and reconciler logic on reconnect
- 3c9b8a7: tool-call confirmation token plumbing through runtime and adapter layer
- ef5d2a1: openai_compat: map soft-cancel + resume semantics to existing streaming events
- d1a7cbb: tests: stream resume, orphaned lease reconciliation, toolcall idempotency harness
- c8b4f99: docs and examples: openai compat upgrade notes + migration guide

Files changed (high level):
- src/streaming/lease_manager.py (new): lease lifecycle, metrics, and TTL enforcement
- src/streaming/watchdog.py (new): background watchdog to detect orphaned sessions and trigger fallback
- src/streaming/heartbeat.py (modified): heartbeat handler + reconcilier
- src/openai_compat/stream_adapter.py (modified): map soft-cancel/resume and carry confirmation token in stream events
- tests/stream/test_resume_and_toolcall.py (new): deterministic harness for reconnect/toolcall idempotency
- examples/openai-streaming-migration.md (new): migration notes for SDKs
- docs/operational/lease_and_heartbeat.md (new): runbook and tuning guidance
- examples/benchmarks/lease-overhead.md (modified): small perf numbers and CI benchmark updates

Runtime behavior and compatibility notes: The server-side lease default TTL is conservative (20s) with a heartbeat_interval of 5s. Short disconnects less than reconnect_grace_window (config default 30s) are fast-reconciled and the runtime attempts to reuse the same backing execution slot. If the lease expires the watchdog marks the session quarantined and triggers fallback routing: either resume on warm standby or redirect to another region/pool depending on policy. Tool-call confirmation ids are opaque strings but deterministic per-session; clients that do not opt into the new confirmation flow continue to receive the same streaming payloads but may observe duplicate tool invocations in pathological reconnect cases. The OpenAI wire format remains compatible: we reuse the streaming "stop" and "done" events and add an optional "x-confirmation-id" field on tool-call structured events (adapter strips unknown fields for older clients).

Testing and CI: Initial runs surfaced a flaky race in the test harness where the watchdog TTL and artificial network pauses needed tighter coordination; addressed by adding deterministic clock mocking in tests. CI matrix: unit (pytest) / integration (docker-compose streaming harness) / lint (flake8) / type checks. First pipeline run: unit tests failed (reconciler race); fix pushed in commit 3c9b8a7 and CI re-run passed.

Review conversation highlights:
- Arjun Mehta (reviewer): "Please surface a metric for lease_reclaimed_count and ensure we emit a debug log with session id and reason when fallback routing triggers."
- Nina Park (author): "Added lease_reclaimed_count metric and the session debug log; log is gated behind DEBUG to avoid noise in prod by default."
- Claire Zhou (reviewer): "Edge case: if a tool call is long-running and client reconnects after TTL, do we risk sending stale completion events? Suggest attaching confirmation id to completion ack as well."
- Nina Park: "Good catch — completion ack already included a call_id but not the confirmation id. Updated stream_adapter to include confirmation id on completion acks, and added tests."
- Diego Ramos (reviewer): "Can the fallback routing cause cold-start spikes on dedicated pools? Add a soft ramp or circuit-breaker."
- Nina Park: "Added a simple token-bucket guard and a configurable ramp parameter; documented in docs/operational/lease_and_heartbeat.md."

Merging and operational rollout: Merged via squash on 2026-02-21 after approvals. Feature flags: the heartbeat + confirmation flow is behind a runtime feature flag (runtime.features.stream_lease_v1) and default-on for new accounts. Ops runbook includes SLO dashboard widgets for lease churn rate and confirmation-id mismatch rate, and an alert if fallback_routing_rate > 1% sustained over 5m.

Potential follow-ups: tighter telemetry for cross-region resume latency, SDK ergonomics for exposing confirm ids to function-call handlers, and a long-term plan to expose lease diagnostics via the Console.

Motivation: long-tail noisy alerts and expensive full-trace storage make SRE investigations slow and costly. This PR introduces a lightweight invocation-digest-exporter that captures a compact, fixed-size summary for every invocation (phase timing quantiles, token-cost estimate, KV-cache-hit-fingerprint, route tags) and a contextual alert-suppressor that uses digest scores and historical clustering to temporarily mute low-actionability alerts and reduce paging fatigue. Scope: implement exporter service (Go), streaming producer in the runtime, a consumer that writes digests to a compact index (time-series + Bloom-ish fingerprint store), a dashboard with digest sampling panels, an RBAC-safe toggle in the Console, unit + integration tests, and docs + runbook updates. Design notes: digests are intentionally lossy to bound storage and network overhead; we include a pluggable scorer for alert suppression so teams can tune aggressiveness per route; privacy: digests avoid user payloads and are pseudonymized before indexing. Testing: includes synthetic replay harness to validate retention/fidelity and an SLO test showing 42% reduction in alert noise in our staging traffic with negligible change to detection of actionable incidents. Rollout plan: feature-gated by runtime flag and Console toggle; staged canary (10% tenant sample) then 50% then global over two weeks; if digest fidelity regression is detected we automatically roll back to full traces.
