payload.body:
Context: Shadow traffic needs consistent comparisons across time windows and across control/shadow targets. The earlier routing mirror MVP used per-request RNG sampling which made deltas noisy and made it hard to correlate control vs shadow outputs for the same logical request. This PR adds a deterministic request fingerprint and a stable bucketing/assignment helper used by the data plane when deciding whether to mirror a request and which shadow target(s) to send it to.

What’s in this PR: 1) Request fingerprinting (fingerprint_v1): Computes a 256-bit fingerprint as HMAC-SHA256(tenant_shadow_secret, canonical_request_bytes). Canonical bytes are derived from a canonical JSON encoding of a strictly limited set of fields: route_id, request_kind (chat/completions/embeddings), model_group (logical), normalized generation params (temperature/top_p/max_tokens/etc), and the request content payload (messages/prompt) after canonicalization (stable key ordering, normalized whitespace for JSON tool args, and explicit UTF-8 encoding). The HMAC key is per-tenant (and per-environment) and is never emitted in telemetry. This ensures: (a) the same logical request maps to the same fingerprint across instances/regions; (b) fingerprints are not reversible without the secret; (c) we do not store raw prompt text to achieve determinism.

2) Bucketing + assignment: Adds helpers for (a) deterministic sampling: sample = (uint64(fingerprint[0:8]) / 2^64) < sample_rate; (b) stable variant selection: variant_index = uint64(fingerprint[8:16]) % num_variants; (c) optional multi-shadow fanout selection using independent lanes: lane_i uses bytes [16+8*i : 24+8*i] to avoid correlated selection when we add more than one shadow target.

3) Collision + privacy notes: Includes a short ADR note in-code and in docs about collision risk and privacy posture. Collision risk: We still treat the fingerprint as an identifier, not a cryptographic guarantee of uniqueness; we store both (fingerprint_prefix_64) and (fingerprint_full_256) internally, but only emit a truncated 96-bit form in telemetry events to reduce cardinality and avoid join keys that are too powerful. For collision math: probability is negligible at our expected sample sizes with 96 bits, but we still design joins to tolerate rare collisions (e.g., shadow pairing includes request_id + timestamp bucket as additional join constraints).

4) Guardrails: The canonicalization step caps included content to 16KB for fingerprinting (after UTF-8 bytes) and includes a fast-path for streaming requests: fingerprint is computed from the initial request envelope only (before any streamed tokens) so we do not block the user path on stream completion.

Why HMAC vs plain hash: A plain SHA256(prompt) can be dictionary-attacked for common prompts; HMAC with a per-tenant secret meaningfully raises the bar and prevents cross-tenant correlation of fingerprints.

Rollout plan: This PR wires the helper behind ShadowTrafficDeterministicBucketing (default off). Routing mirror code will start using this in pr-24833 once merged. No behavior change unless the flag is enabled.

Test plan: Unit tests for canonicalization stability (key ordering, whitespace), determinism across processes, sampling distribution sanity (chi-square vs expected), and variant selection stability. Added a microbenchmark to ensure fingerprinting stays < ~15µs p50 on typical chat payloads (1–4 messages).
Mina Haddad (review): Canonicalization worries me. What fields are we including exactly, and is there any chance we accidentally include request_id or timestamp and break determinism across retries/regions? Also, does including model_group mean we won’t be able to compare control model A vs shadow model B for the same prompt? 

Vikram Singh (author): Good callouts. We explicitly exclude request_id, trace_id, timestamp, headers, and any per-hop metadata. CanonicalRequest is constructed from the user-visible API payload + route_id + normalized params only. On model_group: we include the logical model group requested (e.g., "chat-default") rather than the resolved concrete model id. That way control vs shadow variants (different concrete ids) still share the same fingerprint.

Benji Okafor (review): Please include route_id (or route stable key) in the fingerprint; otherwise two different routes with identical prompts will collide and we’ll pair apples-to-oranges in dashboards. Also, can we ensure the per-tenant secret is not shared across Dedicated pools? 

Vikram Singh (author): Added route_id to the canonical set (it was in the draft but not plumbed through for all request types). Secret is sourced from tenant config; Dedicated pools will have a tenant-scoped secret in their control plane namespace. I also added a comment that secrets must be unique per tenant+env and should not be reused across stacks.

Marcus Lin (review): Privacy: emitting even truncated fingerprints can become a stable correlation handle across datasets. What’s the retention and how are we preventing cross-product joins? Also: how do we handle secret rotation without breaking longitudinal experiments? 

Vikram Singh (author): For telemetry we emit only a 96-bit truncation and we do not expose it via customer-facing APIs (internal-only). Pairing in the pipeline uses the full 256-bit value stored in the shadow artifacts table (with short retention per policy). On rotation: we add a key version prefix in the stored fingerprint metadata; when we rotate, we will still be able to pair within the same key-version window. Longitudinal experiments spanning rotations will show a discontinuity (documented). Follow-up: add dual-key support for a transition period (separate PR; Marcus requested).

Sean Gallagher (review): Performance: HMAC per request on the hot path is OK if bounded, but I want an explicit cap on canonical payload bytes. Also ensure any failure in canonicalization is fail-open (i.e., shadow disabled, user path unaffected). 

Vikram Singh (author): Added max 16KB cap (bytes) for content contribution; beyond that we hash only the first 16KB and include a "truncated" bit in the canonical bytes. Any canonicalization error returns (fingerprint="", sampled=false) and logs at debug with a counter; it never blocks the request.

Nadia Rahman (review): Telemetry note: if you emit 96-bit fingerprint, do not allow it as a dimension in high-cardinality metrics. Can you name the fields carefully (request_fingerprint_trunc) and mark as "join-only"? 

Vikram Singh (author): Done. Updated naming to request_fingerprint_trunc96 and added comments in the event schema docs. We also added a lint rule stub in our metrics emitter (TODO in ENG-5410) to prevent accidental tag emission.

Resolution: Approved after changes (route_id inclusion, payload cap, truncation naming, added key-version metadata).
CI: build (pass), unit tests (pass), gofmt (pass), lint (pass), security-scan (pass). Perf microbench: router/shadow BenchmarkFingerprintV1 p50 9.8µs (c6i.2xlarge), p99 17.1µs; no regression against main (±3%).
Internal: adds deterministic request fingerprinting and bucketing helpers for Shadow Traffic experiments (flagged off by default).
Uses per-tenant HMAC secret for non-reversible fingerprinting; avoids emitting full fingerprint to telemetry; caps canonicalized content bytes and excludes volatile identifiers (request_id/timestamp/headers).

payload.body: Summary: Adds an invocation-level 'decorator' pipeline that enriches spans and metrics at request entry/exit and introduces an Alert Synthesis Engine that coalesces noisy, per-token alerts into single actionable incidents. Motivation: alert fatigue from token-level and phase-level SLO fires makes triage slow; many noisy alerts stem from the same underlying invocation pattern (e.g. long-tail prompt shapes, cold-cache microbursts). This PR delivers two orthogonal pieces: 1) lightweight invocation decorators that attach stable invocation keys and canonicalized prompt-shape metadata to traces/metrics and 2) an offline/stream synthesis service that groups alert signals by invocation fingerprint and applies heuristic suppression/priority fusion before page routing. Changes: - inference/proxy/middleware/decorators.go: new middleware that computes invocation_fingerprint, prompt_shape_bucket and attaches them to OpenTelemetry spans and the request envelope. - observability/synthesis/engine.py: synthesis engine that consumes alert events, enriched spans, and rule configuration; outputs fused alerts and a short provenance blob used by the runbook UI. - observability/synthesis/config.yaml.example: operator editable rules for fusion thresholds, time-windows and priority escalation. - dashboards/observability/invocation-synthesis-panel.json: Grafana panel showing synthesis rate, fusion ratio, and top contributing invocation fingerprints. - tests/observability/test_synthesis_engine.py: unit + regression tests covering grouping heuristics, TTLs and priority escalation. - internal/metrics/labels.go: new stable labels (invocation_fingerprint, prompt_shape_bucket) and helper APIs. - ci/workflows/obs-integration.yml: adds staged integration job that runs synthesis smoke tests against sampled production traces. Commits (summary): - 1a2b3c4: add decorators middleware and label helpers - 4d5e6f7: initial synthesis engine + clustering heuristics - 7f8e9d0: add dashboards and CI integration job - ab12cd3: tests and docs; tweak fusion thresholds for stage Review notes: - Design rationale: Prefer deterministic fingerprint generation (sha1 over normalized prompt+client+route) to keep cardinality capped. We intentionally avoid adding new high-cardinality user identifiers. - Performance: decorator added ~120ns median overhead in hot path (benchmarked on canary infra). Batch tracing exporter unchanged. - Backwards compatibility: spans get new attributes but old consumers will ignore them; no schema migration required. Review conversation (high level): - Sanjay Patel (reviewer): "Can the fingerprint collide across tenants when prompt shapes are similar? Please add test asserting different tenant ids produce different fingerprints." -> Author: "Added tenant ID salt to fingerprint and a unit test (tests/observability/test_fingerprint_tenant_salt.py)." - Elliot Zhang (reviewer): "What happens if synthesis engine is down?" -> Author: "Engine runs best-effort; alerts are ingested into the canonical alert queue. Synthesis runs as a consumer with at-least-once semantics and includes a pass-through mode if disabled (config flag: enable_synthesis:false). Added runbook note." - Nora Mills (approver): "Please document how ops can tune fusion thresholds. Approved after docs update." CI summary: - go-build: pass - py-tests: initial run failed on edge TTL case, rerun passed - lint (golangci + flake8): pass - integration-tests: pass (staged job against sampled traces) Final CI status: pass Files changed (high level): - 18 files changed across middleware, observability synthesis, dashboards, tests and CI. Additions: 1243 deletions: 312 Release notes: "Introduces invocation decorators to enrich spans/metrics with stable invocation fingerprints and prompt-shape buckets; adds an Alert Synthesis Engine that groups related alert signals into single incidents to reduce alert fatigue. Ops can tune fusion thresholds via observability/synthesis/config.yaml.example." Merge: merged via squash, commit message: "invocation decorators + alert synthesis engine: reduce alert noise and add fusion controls"; merger: "Elliot Zhang"; merge date: 2026-03-02. Follow-ups & rollout plan: - Canary rollout: decorator enabled for 10% of traffic in us-west-2 for 48h, monitor fusion ratio and false positive suppression. - Metrics to watch: synthesis_fusion_ratio, synthesis_group_latency_ms, invocation_fingerprint_cardinality, alert_pager_count_by_rule. - Post-merge tasks: add synthetic-synth-runner to ops playbook, create runbook snippets linking fingerprint -> trace view. Related work items: ENG-1123, ENG-1189, PM-4561. Notes for oncall: synthesized alerts include the provenance blob (top 3 contributing spans) and a direct deeplink to invocation trace; operators can set enable_synthesis:false to bypass fusion if troubleshooting. This PR is conservative about cardinality and includes unit tests asserting stable fingerprinting.

Motivation: Over time the monorepo accumulated divergent lint/test helpers (multiple shell wrappers, duplicated plugin lists, and several transitive devDependencies). This PR reduces CI noise, speeds up lint runs in fast-feedback lanes, and reduces install surface area for ephemeral CI runners. It also reduces accidental transitive changes from dev-only deps that previously slipped into release automation.

Summary of changes: consolidated individual eslint/formatter plugin installs into a single composite Node Action (actions/ci-lint-compact) that performs install+cache+lint; migrated shell-based lint scripts in tools/ and .github/workflows/* to the new action; introduced a dep-pruner script + GitHub job that removes unused devDependencies from package.json files (heuristic + safe-guard and dry-run mode by default); updated release automation to skip triggering releases for devDependency-only bump PRs; added a small pre-merge fastpath that runs only changed-package lint/tests for quicker feedback.

Commits (high-level): - feat(ci): add actions/ci-lint-compact composite action and unit tests - refactor(monorepo): replace shell lint invocations with composite action - chore(deps): remove unused devDependencies discovered by dep-pruner dry-run - ci(workflows): add dep-pruner post-merge job and skip rule for release pipeline - test(ci): add matrix reduction for fast-feedback lane and smoke job for full-run

Files touched (high level): - .github/actions/ci-lint-compact/action.yml (new) - .github/workflows/ci-fastpath.yml (updated) - .github/workflows/release.yml (updated: add skip rules) - package.json (root) & package.json in packages/* (pruned devDeps) - tools/lint.sh -> removed, replaced by tools/lint.js wrapper - scripts/dep-pruner.js (new) - README.ci.md (updated docs for contributors)

Example replacement snippet (old -> new): "scripts": { "lint:all": "tools/lint.sh --ci" } -> "scripts": { "lint:all": "node tools/lint.js --ci" }

CI results: First CI run (2026-02-15) failed on flaky shell path in packages/cli where an environment assumption broke the new cache flow; addressed in commit 2 (refactor: make cache key path-agnostic) and rerun. Final CI status: all checks passed including: lint (fastpath, full), unit-tests (sharded), integration-smoke, e2e-nightly (was not run in fastpath), dep-pruner dry-run.

Review conversation (abridged, chronological): Jordan Lee (reviewer): "Nice consolidation. Can we keep the old shell wrapper for one release to give integrators time to switch?" Ava Martinez (author): "Can do — left a thin shim that logs a deprecation warning and maps flags to the new node wrapper; will remove in 1 release cycle." Priya Nambiar: "Dep-pruner heuristics look OK, but add a CI safety net to prevent accidental removal of build-time deps used by the native build image." Ava: "Added a whitelist check and explicit opt-in for packages with native-bindings. See scripts/dep-pruner.js lines 62-78." Omar Haddad: "Please add a note in release automation so that dependabot devDep bumps don't trigger a full release run." Ava: "Added skip rules and updated README.ci.md with examples." Approvals: Jordan Lee (approved), Priya Nambiar (approved after minor suggestions), Omar Haddad (approved). Merge method: squash and merge.

How to validate locally: 1) npm ci at repo root (or use the provided docker/dev image) 2) node tools/lint.js --changed-packages 3) run scripts/dep-pruner.js --dry-run to inspect suggested removals 4) run .github/actions/ci-lint-compact locally via act or against a small test repo

Rollout notes: we will keep the shim for one release (label: ci-deprecation), monitor fastpath latency and lint flakiness for two weeks, and run the dep-pruner in dry-run mode for one release before enabling auto-prune (will be configured via a repo-level boolean in repo settings). If PRs to release pipeline are skipped inadvertently, the repo bot will post a comment with the rationale and a link to the triggering diff.

Related workitems: Linear ENG-4219 (CI fastpath), ENG-4300 (dep hygiene), SUP-5123 (support ticket where devDep bump caused a release spike).

Notes: This PR intentionally errs on the conservative side for pruning — dep-pruner requires human approval to actually commit removals unless org-config enables auto-prune. The composite action is lightweight and written to be portable across runners to avoid future platform-specific breaks.
Consolidated lint/test infra for faster CI feedback; removed ~30 devDependencies across the monorepo; introduced a hermetic node-based lint action and a post-merge dep-pruner job. No customer-facing behavior change.

Context and motivation: Some tenants experience unexpectedly high token costs during cold-starts and microbursts because default prefill and batch shapes are generic. This PR introduces a lightweight sampling service (Prefill Sampler) that captures short-run traffic patterns and a Tiering Advisor that recommends quantization tiers and batch/caching defaults per-tenant. The goal is to automate conservative cost-optimization suggestions while preserving latency SLOs.

What this PR does (single contiguous description): Implements a Prefill Sampler that runs as a runtime-side sampling component: it records short histograms of sequence length, prefix reuse ratios, and cold-cache hit estimates (safely sampled at 0.1% by default). Adds a Tiering Advisor microservice that consumes sampler outputs and tenant-level telemetry (token-cost, latency P95, kv-cache hit rate) to recommend: quantization tier (none/8bit/4bit-int8), prefill batch shape (micro/small/standard), and cache durations for prefix caching. Introduces a new 'econ.prefill_advisor' feature flag and a TenantPrefillProfile CRD used only in Private/Dedicated deployments; hosted customers get recommendations surfaced in the Console but not persisted.

Checklist: - [x] Prefill Sampler runtime integration with request router - [x] Tiering Advisor API + basic rules engine - [x] Feature gate + config defaults - [x] Unit tests for sampler and advisor rules - [x] Integration test that simulates bursty traffic and asserts recommended profiles reduce projected token cost by >= 10% without increasing P95 > 5ms - [x] Telemetry: added sampling metrics and advisor decision event traces - [x] Docs snippets for Console UI and CLI dry-run

High-level commits summary: - Commit 1: initial sampler prototype and sampling API contract - Commit 2: add rules engine skeleton and simple heuristic rules (seq_len_based, prefix_reuse) - Commit 3: advisor gRPC API + HTTP translation layer for Console - Commit 4: feature flag wiring, config defaults, and CRD schema - Commit 5: unit & integration tests + mock telemetry generator - Commit 6: docs and examples for CLI --dry-run and Console preview - Commit 7: small followups addressing reviewer feedback (timeouts, metrics names)

Files touched (high level): - runtime/sampling/prefill_sampler.go: sampling logic and rate-limiter - runtime/sampling/prefill_sampler_test.go: unit tests - advisor/service/main.go: Tiering Advisor service entrypoint and rules engine - advisor/rules/basic_rules.go: simple heuristics used in this PR - advisor/api/proto/prefill.proto -> generated advisor/api/prefill.pb.go - api/tenant/crds/tenant_prefill_profile.yaml: CRD schema (Private/Dedicated only) - console/backend/econ_advisor_handler.go: HTTP proxy + preview endpoint - docs/guides/prefill_advisor.md: user guide and dry-run examples

Small illustrative diff snippets: - Added sampler config with conservative defaults (sampling_rate=0.001, max_buffer=512). - Rules: if median_seq_len < 32 and prefix_reuse > 0.6 -> recommend 'micro' batch shape; else if prefix_reuse > 0.85 and kv_cache_hit < 0.2 -> recommend longer cache durations.

Telemetry and CI expectations: CI initially had a flaky integration test (integration/prefill_burst_test) that timed out on first run in CI. I adjusted the test to use a mocked clock and reduced wall-clock dependencies; CI reran and all checks passed. The PR adds metrics: sampler.sampled_requests_total, sampler.buffer_overflows_total, advisor.recommendation_count, advisor.decision_duration_ms.

Review conversation (condensed): - Alyssa Chen (reviewer): "Nice separation between sampling and advising. A few nit comments: prefer context-based timeouts and clarify sampling rate config visibility to hosted users." - Diego (author): "Addressed timeouts; sampling rate now controlled by 'econ.prefill_sampling_rate' and defaults are lower for hosted tier." - Priya Nair (reviewer): "Concern about privacy: are we logging any PII?" - Diego: "No PII. Sampler records only aggregate stats and hashed tenant ids; added a note in telemetry policy docs." - Tomás Rivera: "Can we gate the CRD creation behind an installer flag?" - Diego: "Yes—CRD manifests are emitted only when 'private.enable_prefill_profiles' is true in installer values. Added to helm chart docs." - Alyssa: "Integration test still relied on real scheduler; switched to mocked scheduler. LGTM after green CI."

CI checks: - unit-tests: pass - linters: pass (golangci-lint) - integration-tests: pass (after rerun) - e2e: pass (smoke) - security-scan: pass

Backward compatibility and safety: The Tiering Advisor only produces recommendations; no automatic changes are applied to runtime unless tenant opts in or an admin applies recommendations. Defaults remain unchanged. Feature is disabled by default for hosted customers and enabled behind feature flag for private/dedicated tenants where an admin explicitly opts in.

Operational notes: - Advisor exposes a /preview endpoint that returns a sample recommended profile and projected 30-day cost delta. - Recommendations include a confidence score (low/medium/high). Low-confidence suggestions require manual review. - Added alert econ.advisor.sync_failures > 3 in 5m to platform SRE runbook.

Migration plan: No data migrations required. For Private installs that opt-in, CRD creation is performed during installer run. For Hosted customers, Console surfaces suggestions in a non-intrusive banner and a Console 'Recommendations' tab under the tenant page.

Performance validation: Load test setup used tenant traffic generator with bursty Poisson bursts; advisor recommendations produced projected token cost improvements between 12-28% in tests while keeping P95 within 3ms of baseline most frequently.

Follow-ups planned: - Add a machine-learned decision model (offline) to complement heuristic rules - Expose batch-shape tuning CLI for operators - Add automatic A/B rollout (opt-in) for high-confidence recommendations

Merge method and outcome: Squash and merge after two approving reviews and green CI. Merge commit message includes Linear links (ENG-1842, ENG-1909) and a concise summary of the feature.

Alyssa: prefer context-based timeouts and clarify sampling rate visibility
Priya: ensure no PII is emitted by sampler
Tomás: gate CRD creation behind installer flag
Diego: added config flag and docs, sampling rate defaulted lower for hosted
Alyssa: integration test flake fixed with mocked clock, LGTM
Adds a sampler-based prefill advisor and quantized-tier recommendation service to suggest cost-aware defaults for tenant warmups and batch shapes. Non-breaking; feature gated behind 'econ.prefill_advisor'.
Unit coverage added for sampler rules; integration simulates multi-burst traffic pattern; CI shows consistent timeouts fixed by test refactor; load tests demonstrate 12-28% projected cost improvement in simulated workloads.
Add Prefill Sampler and Tiering Advisor: opt-in cost-optimization recommendations for prefill/batch/cache and quantization tiering.
Feature gated; recommended to operators. Console will show recommendations for hosted read-only preview; Private/Dedicated admins can opt-in to apply profiles. Rollout staged: internal beta -> 10 tenants -> broad opt-in.
Sampler only collects aggregate counters and hashed tenant IDs. No raw prompts or PII are logged. Telemetry policy updated and privacy review completed.

payload.body:
Motivation: production workloads showed repeated small free regions inside the KV cache after tenant churn and background lease expirations. The existing compaction path relied on aggressive whole-segment compaction, which created IO spikes and unfair eviction across tenants. This PR introduces an "islanded fragment runner" plus a lazy page-rewrite batcher to reduce fragmentation without large synchronous compaction windows. High-level goals: (1) isolate tiny fragments into 'islands' that are eligible for low-priority rewrite rather than immediate eviction, (2) introduce a staged evictor with tenant-aware pacing and soft-quarantine hysteresis so recently demoted pages are not immediately re-evicted, (3) add a low-priority rewrite-batcher that performs small in-place page rewrites/defrag cycles to coalesce islands during steady-state, and (4) expose runtime knobs and metrics to monitor island counts, rewrite latency, and tenant fairness. Change summary: - New islanded fragment lifecycle and bookkeeping (island id per region, demotion timestamps). - Lazy rewrite-batcher daemon that groups small fragments into batches sized by target_rewrite_bytes and respects a global IO budget. - Staged evictor: fast-path evictor for hot pressure, slow-path for island rewrite candidates, with tenant-weighted pacing to avoid tenant starvation. - KV allocator hint changes to prefer page-aligned placements for rewrite-friendly coalescing. - Telemetry: island_count, rewrite_batches, rewrite_bytes, tenant_rewrite_backlog, staged_evictor_cycles. Compatibility and safety: feature gated behind runtime flag kv.enable_islanded_rewrite=false by default. All changes are opt-in and can be toggled per deployment. Rollout plan: enable for internal canary with 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% after two perf sweeps. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of islanded fragment tracker and allocator hints - [x] Lazy rewrite-batcher with IO budgeting and batch coalescer - [x] Staged evictor + tenant pacing loop - [x] Unit tests for island lifecycle and eviction paths - [x] Integration test harness simulating tenant churn and continuous batching - [x] Benchmarks against synthetic mixed-tenancy workload - [x] Documentation: runtime config docs and Console metric wiring Notes: description includes short rationale for design tradeoffs; see commit messages for micro design decisions and pointers to internal design doc (shared via Linear ENG-1842).
2024-11-18 Arjun Patel: Design looks promising; two asks - (1) add a hard upper bound on rewrite IO per tenant to avoid noisy neighbor, (2) add more defensive checks around island metadata lifecycle to avoid leaks.
2024-11-19 Sofia Chen: Addressed both: added tenant_rewrite_max_bytes and island tombstone sweep in islanded_tracker.cc; added unit tests for tombstone expiry.
2024-11-22 Evan Kim: Found a race in staged evictor where eviction token was not atomically transferred to slow-path. Requested an explicit CAS and test.
2024-11-24 Sofia Chen: Added CAS fix and a targeted multithreaded test simulating concurrent eviction + rewrite worker; CI flake observed and re-run passed.
2024-11-28 Marta Lopez: Verified telemetry and console widgets; left an approval after minor docs nit.
Add an opt-in KV islanded fragmentation handler and low-priority page rewrite batcher to reduce small-fragment eviction and long tail memory pressure. Disabled by default; runtime flag kv.enable_islanded_rewrite. Improves memory reclamation under multi-tenant churn with controlled IO budget.

Motivation: Mixed-length traffic produces inefficient GPU batches due to padding and kernel mismatch. This PR introduces an adaptive lane-based coalescer that groups concurrent requests into "lanes" based on sequence-length ranges and kernel alignment targets. The coalescer makes batching decisions that balance padding overhead, KV-cache locality, and kernel execution characteristics. Key ideas: 1) lane assignment uses a lightweight histogram maintained per-slot to pick lane bounds that align with the runtime's best-performing kernel sizes; 2) small lanes are opportunistically merged into adjacent lanes when kernel alignment and predicted padding cost indicate net win; 3) before merging, the coalescer evaluates KV-cache collision risk and prefers merges that preserve hot-cache entries to avoid cache thrash; 4) integrates with continuous batching: lanes are first-class scheduling units and can be flushed independently or coalesced by the slot scheduler based on pending volume and latency SLOs; 5) cost model uses profile data gathered by the kernel profiler (avg per-token kernel time by seqlen bucket) to estimate per-lane token cost and expected latency; 6) exposes two new runtime knobs: lane_target_utilization and kv_eviction_safety_margin, and a diagnostic endpoint (/debug/lane-coalescer) for live histograms and merge decisions. Implementation highlights: new coalescer and scheduler adaptor in serving/runtime/lanes, a lightweight in-memory histogram store, kernel-profile consumer hooks in serving/runtime/profiler, KV-cache-aware merge checks in serving/runtime/kv_cache_manager, and unit + integration tests for mixed workloads. Benchmarks: measured on a 8x A100 node with mixed GPT-like load (70% short <=64, 30% long <=1024) and steady QPS representative of production. Results: 12-18% P50 latency reduction across models tested, 22% reduction in wasted padding tokens (measured at the runtime batching boundary), and 8-11% lower end-to-end token cost for steady-state loads where KV-cache reuse is high. Compatibility: default behavior is opt-in via config flag lane_coalescer_enabled=false. Backwards-compatible when disabled. Rollout: feature gated behind runtime config and requires kernel profile data to be present for alignment benefits. Checklist: - [x] Design doc and cost model handwritten and linked in PR - [x] Unit tests for lane assignment and merge logic - [x] Integration test exercising KV-cache-aware merges - [x] Benchmarks and flamegraphs attached - [x] Docs entry for runtime knobs and diagnostic endpoint - [x] CI green and benchmarks validated in staging
Miguel Santos: Nice work. Please add a short explanation of the heuristic thresholds in the docs. How sensitive is lane_target_utilization to bursty traffic?
Aisha Patel: Added a paragraph in docs and added an autoscale-friendly mode that lowers merge aggressiveness under bursty conditions. See config sample in docs.
Rachel Lee: KV-cache awareness is critical. Two questions: 1) do we track per-model hot keys or per-slot? 2) how expensive is the cache-check on the hot path?
Aisha Patel: We track per-slot hot-key summaries (bloom filter + LRU counters) to keep the fast-path checks O(1). Expanded comments and tests to validate false-positive behavior.
Kenji Watanabe: CI had a flaky scheduling test on re-run. I suspect a race in slot flush; can you add a small jitter before forced flush in test?
Aisha Patel: Fixed test by introducing deterministic jitter and added a retry helper. Re-ran CI and benchmarks.
Rachel Lee: Approved after verifying benchmarks in staging and reviewing the diagnostic endpoint output.
Miguel Santos: Squash-merge ok after you address the one nit about log verbosity (reduce debug logs for production).
Initial CI: 7/8 checks passed; flaky scheduling-test failed. After fix and small test changes CI: all checks passed. Lint: pass. Unit tests: pass. Integration staging run: pass. Benchmark job: pass (benchmarks uploaded to tools/benchmarks/lane_coalescer/bench_results.md).
Introduces an opt-in lane-based coalescer that reduces padding waste and improves latency for mixed-length workloads. Exposes lane_target_utilization and kv_eviction_safety_margin runtime knobs and a diagnostic endpoint at /debug/lane-coalescer. Opt-in via runtime config lane_coalescer_enabled. Not enabled by default.
Staging rollout recommended. When enabling, ensure kernel-profile data is populated (runtime-profiling must have run for 24h or a minimum sample count). Watch /debug/lane-coalescer histograms and kv_eviction_metric. For high-burst traffic, use autoscale-friendly mode to reduce merge aggressiveness.

Context and motivation: Teams building long-lived streaming integrations have reported confusion about when SDK credentials are refreshed vs. when application code should trigger refresh. Simultaneously, our TypeScript ergonomic examples for typed async streams diverged from Python/Go patterns and caused portability questions. This PR unifies guidance, tightens docstrings, and adds small API ergonomics to reduce footguns. Summary of changes: 1) Python: introduce Session context manager (sdk/python/session.py) that centralizes credential acquisition, TTL semantics, and a lightweight background refresh probe. Docstrings and README were expanded to show three canonical patterns: short-lived interactive requests, long-lived streaming with periodic lease refresh, and delegated-credential fallbacks. Added unit tests (test_session_ttl.py) around TTL edge cases and race conditions. 2) TypeScript: provide a typed async-iterator example (examples/typed-pullstream.ts) that demonstrates backpressure hints, retry-policy combinators (policies.ts), and a recommended shape for consumer code to interoperate with Redwood servers. The example intentionally uses an exported RetryPolicy builder to demonstrate composition (exponential backoff + jitter + max-window). 3) Go: rename internal Receiver interface to StreamConsumer to better reflect cross-language naming; provide a small compatibility shim (consumer.go / receiver_shim.go) so downstream users see a deprecation warning instead of breakage. 4) Docs: unify the credential lifecycle documentation (docs/reference/sdk-auth.md) with explicit TTL definitions, examples of safe refresh windows (e.g. refresh when remaining_ttl < 0.2 * lease_duration), and migration notes (docs/migration/2026-02-sdk-parity.md). 5) Tests & CI: added invariant tests for credential tombstoning, TTL refresh probe, and typed-stream examples run under TS checker. Checklist: - [x] Add Session context manager and tests (Python) - [x] Add typed TS streaming example and RetryPolicy combinators - [x] Add Go rename + shim + tests - [x] Update docs and migration notes - [x] Update changelogs and bump SDK versions (py 0.14.0rc1, ts 2.8.0-rc, go 1.6.0-rc) Compatibility and migration notes: - Python: new Session is opt-in; existing low-level TokenProvider APIs are unchanged. Customers using custom keepalive loops will see no forced behavior, but we recommend adopting Session for shorter code and fewer edgecases. - TypeScript: example introduces a small helper export RetryPolicy.compose(...). Motivation: Some tenants experience oscillating latency/cost patterns when competing for shared batching windows; static batch shapes plus coarse quantization tiers cause either wasted GPU cycles or degraded P75 latency. This PR introduces a tenant-aware 'jittered' batching policy that spreads micro-batch alignment to reduce hot-spot bursts, and pairs it with an adaptive quantization scaler that nudges model quant levels per-tenant within a safety budget to keep unit-econ targets without violating latency SLOs. Scope: server/runtime patch (batch scheduler), policy engine changes (tenant policy translation), and a new lightweight telemetry probe + decision logic for safe quant adjustments. Key design points: 1) Jittered batcher: each tenant gets a small randomized offset window (configurable, deterministic for deduplication) to avoid synchronized microbursts across tenants while preserving max batch fill for throughput. 2) Adaptive quant scaler: takes tenant-level recent unit-econ and p95/p75 latency signals and proposes quant nudges (int8->int4 or FP16 variants) constrained by an SLA-derived safety budget and a quality gate using recent evals/held-out prompts. Changes are opt-in via tenant defaults; safe fallbacks route to tenant baseline model when probes fail. Checklist: - [x] Implement jitter offset generator and integrate into batch planner - [x] Add tenant policy schema to console and defaults service - [x] Telemetry probe and rollout circuit-breaker - [x] Decision engine with conservative ramp schedule and rollback hooks - [x] Unit tests for scheduler heuristics - [x] Integration tests for rollback/fallback behavior Rollout plan: feature gated behind tenant opt-in flag; staged rollout starting with internal test tenants, then low-traffic customers, followed by a two-week shadow run with telemetry-only mode. If regressions detected (latency p95 up > 10% or quality drift flagged), scaler automatically reverts to baseline and triggers an incident annotation. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged for tenants that do not opt in. New policy fields are additive and validated by the defaults service. Security/privacy: no customer payloads leave the cluster for probing; quality gate uses cached evaluation sets only. Risks and mitigations: risk of over-quantization hurting hallucination rates -> mitigation: quality gate rejects changes with token-level divergence above threshold and forces manual review; risk of jitter causing micro-latency variance -> mitigation: jitter magnitude bounded and throttled under high-latency conditions. Related: referenced ENG-1984 (tenant batch fairness) and ENG-2010 (unit-econ autosuggest).
Rafael J. Ortega: Nice isolation approach. Two asks: (1) ensure jitter window is bounded by per-tenant latency SLO and (2) add a metric for 'jitter-induced fill-loss' so we can detect when offsets harm throughput.
Author (Maya): Added bound check against tenant.slo.ms and instrumented a new prometheus metric runtime_batch_jitter_fill_loss_total in the telemetry probe. See latest commit f1b8c55.
Priya Sinha: For the quant scaler, can you add a deterministic dry-run mode that emits proposed changes to the audit log without applying? We'll want to run this across a few tenants first.
Author (Maya): Added dry-run flag and audit log emitter (ops/telemetry/audit_emitter.go) in commit f1b8c55; dry-run enabled during shadow stage in rollout plan.
Daniel H. Lee: Integration tests look solid. One small nit: make the rollback delay configurable; sometimes we want faster reverts for critical tenants.
Author (Maya): Exposed rollback.delay_ms in tenant policy and defaults; updated console handler to surface it.
Add tenant-jitter-batcher and an adaptive quant scaler with safety budgets. Opt-in feature; provides reduced tenant batch contention, improved unit-econ tuning with safe rollbacks and audit logging. See console for tenant policy fields and rollout options.

Motivation: during a short-lived regional surge we observed repeated node rejoin/evac cycles that amplified downstream SLO violations and caused KV-cache churn. This PR introduces a Temporal Isolation Gate (TIG) and a soft tombstone marker to break oscillation loops and allow graceful backfill without immediate re-admission. Summary of changes: 1) core: add TemporalIsolationGate in the routing layer to delay re-admit attempts for nodes/tenants within a configurable SLO window; 2) eviction: introduce 'soft tombstone' metadata on connections and KV leases that marks ephemeral quarantine without full eviction, reducing KV drain churn; 3) controlplane: surface tombstone/quiet-window state in the health API and add a TTL-backed tombstone reconciler to ensure automatic clear after the configured window; 4) telemetry: emit new metrics and structured spans (tombstone.count, tombstone.reason, tig.window_ms, tenant.quiet_window) and add corresponding SLO alert hooks; 5) helm/ops: expose the TIG feature flag and default quiet-window config (canary-friendly defaults). Rollout plan: gated by the feature flag 'runtime.tig_enabled' and a per-region canary set via fleet labels; start with us-west-2 for 1 hour at low traffic then expand; observability dashboards added to monitor tombstone churn and rejoin rate. Backout: flip feature flag off and cleanup reconciler; tombstones are TTL-backed so state will clear automatically. Testing: unit tests for gate logic, integration test simulating rapid rejoin (tests/integration/regional_tombstone_flow.py), k8s smoke deploy with helm chart tweak. Checklist: - [x] design review (ENG-3421) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] telemetry and alert hooks - [x] canary rollout plan - [x] docs updates for operators (docs/operations/graceful_degradation.md). Technical notes: the TIG uses token-bucket logic scoped per-tenant and per-node to avoid global head-of-line blocking; tombstone is a lightweight lease annotation persisted in the controlplane with eventual consistency to edge proxies to avoid blocking request paths. This is intended as a safety mitigation for short spikes and should not replace longer-term capacity/autoscale actions.
Marco Ruiz (reviewer): Concerned about race between tombstone TTL and in-flight KV drains — can we ensure tombstone clearance doesn't cause duplicate re-admits?
Sofia Nguyen (author): TIG defers re-admit by a randomized jittered window after TTL expiry; reconciler performs a compare-and-set based clear to avoid races. Added unit tests to prove behavior in edge cases.
Anya Patel (reviewer): Telemetry looks good; request to add a histogram for tombstone durations to help tune defaults.
Sofia Nguyen: Added tombstone.duration histogram and a Grafana panel in the ops dashboard.
Liam Chen (reviewer): CI initially failed on an integration flake (timing). After adjusting wait semantics in test harness the job passed. Approve-by: Anya, Marco. Merge: squash-and-merge after canary smoke passed on us-west-2.
- Hotpatch: add Temporal Isolation Gate to prevent rejoin/evac oscillation under short regional surges.
- Add soft tombstone marker to reduce KV-cache churn during transient quarantines.
- New telemetry metrics and dashboards to help tune quiet-window defaults.

payload.body:
Summary: This PR adds a small suite of staging-only safety smoke tests for Hosted canary rollouts. The goal is to catch two classes of beta issues before they reach customers: (1) cohorting / split enforcement regressions (e.g., observed split mismatch per region) and (2) stop-condition wiring regressions (e.g., SLO breach evaluates but orchestrator doesn’t pause/rollback, or rollout step stalls on metric timeouts). These tests are intentionally narrow, deterministic, and cleanup-safe so they can be run as part of GA change management.

Motivation / context: During beta we saw an incident-like split mismatch in us-east (SUP-48377) and a separate class of failures where metric evaluation timeouts could stall progress (see follow-ups in ENG-9158 / pr-28895). We already have E2E coverage in the monorepo (ENG-9164), but we wanted a lightweight “canary of the canary” that runs against staging infrastructure end-to-end (routing + telemetry aggregation + orchestrator actions) without needing full Console UI flows.

What’s included: 1) Cohorting correctness smoke: Creates a temporary Hosted route + rollout with baseline/canary config, sets split to 20% canary, and sends N=2,000 synthetic requests with a fixed cohorting key distribution. Validates: (a) per-request cohort assignment is stable for the same key across retries, (b) overall split converges to expected bounds (20% ± 3% at N=2,000), (c) split is consistent across regions when the same key is used (us-east-1 + eu-west-1), and (d) streaming requests retain cohort stickiness across reconnect within the allowed retry window.

2) Stop-condition wiring smoke: Starts a rollout step and intentionally injects failures into the canary cohort only (via the staging failure-injection header understood by the Hosted gateway) to exceed the default stop threshold for 5xx within a short window. Validates: (a) telemetry tags include rollout_id and cohort and are queryable via the staging metrics API, (b) stop-condition evaluator fires and emits an action event, (c) orchestrator transitions the rollout into PAUSED or ROLLED_BACK per policy (configurable per test), and (d) no orphaned rollouts remain after test completion.

3) Anti-cardinality + safety rails: Tests do not create unbounded (rollout_id, route, region) series. The suite uses a single route per run with a unique suffix, but aggregates assertions via the orchestrator + a single metrics query path. Added guardrails that hard-fail if route names exceed a maximum length or if run attempts to create more than 2 rollouts.

4) Cleanup and time-bounding: Every test uses a strict max runtime with deferred cleanup. If a run times out, we still attempt to rollback/delete the rollout and delete the staging route. Cleanup is idempotent and safe to re-run.

Implementation details: - Uses the perf-canary harness to call control-plane and orchestrator endpoints directly (no Console dependency). - Adds a small wrapper for deterministic key generation to validate hash cohorting behavior. - Adds a metrics polling helper with exponential backoff and a hard cap; avoids busy-waiting. - Uses a single staging-only feature flag gate so the job is a no-op in non-staging environments.

Changed areas (high level): - tests/rollouts/test_rollout_split_accuracy.ts: new split validation test and cohort stickiness assertions - tests/rollouts/test_rollout_stop_condition.ts: new stop-condition wiring test with failure injection - lib/staging/orchestrator_client.ts: helper for rollout create/start/pause/rollback + state polling - lib/staging/metrics_client.ts: helper for cohort-tagged metrics queries with bounded polling - lib/staging/cleanup.ts: idempotent cleanup for routes + rollouts - ci/nightly.yml and ci/on_demand.yml: new job definition + required secrets

Illustrative snippet (cohort stickiness assertion): The test tracks (cohort, request_id) for a stable key and asserts that retries do not flip cohorts unless the rollout config changed. This mirrors the ADR decision for deterministic cohorting and protects against accidental inclusion of unstable fields in the hash input.

How to run: - On demand (staging): ./scripts/run_smoke_tests.sh --suite rollouts --env staging - CI: job “staging-rollout-smoke” (nightly) and optional manual dispatch

Rollout / risk: Low risk to production since this is perf-canary only. Risk to staging is mitigated via strict cleanup and caps. If staging is degraded, the suite is expected to fail fast and page nobody (non-paging); it will file a CI failure for visibility.

Follow-ups: - Consider adding a latency regression stop-condition test once default thresholds are finalized (ENG-9158). - Consider adding a “split mismatch per AZ” probe once we have better visibility into the per-AZ routing logs.

Checklist: - [x] Tests are time-bounded and cleanup-safe - [x] Does not increase metrics cardinality unboundedly - [x] Validates both routing enforcement and telemetry stop-condition wiring - [x] Documented required staging secrets - [x] Linked to relevant Linear + support ticket
Adds staging smoke tests that validate deterministic rollout cohort assignment and split accuracy.
Adds staging smoke tests that validate auto-stop/rollback signals are emitted and consumed by the rollout orchestrator without stalling.
Adds CI job wiring to run smoke tests on demand and nightly with automatic cleanup.
Mina Haddad: The split bounds seem tight at N=2,000. Can we justify ±3% or make it configurable? Also please make sure the hash key input matches the data plane implementation (no request_id leakage).
Leila Farouk (author): Good call. I bumped N from 1,000 -> 2,000 and made the tolerance configurable per env with a staging default of ±3%. Also added an explicit assertion that the cohorting key is derived only from (tenant_id, route_id, stable_user_key) and not request_id. Added a comment linking back to the cohorting ADR.
Aisha Bello: For the stop-condition test: please ensure it doesn’t create paging alerts. Also we should validate the orchestrator transition, not just that metrics exceeded threshold.
Leila Farouk (author): Updated: the test uses the non-paging staging alert policy and only asserts via orchestrator API state transitions + action events. No pager integration is touched. Also added a guard to skip if the staging alerting backend is in maintenance mode.
Sean Gallagher: Cleanup needs to be bulletproof. What happens if the rollout is mid-step and rollback fails? We’ve had stuck rollouts in staging before and they’re annoying.
Leila Farouk (author): Added cleanup retry logic with jitter and a hard cap. If rollback fails after retries, we force-delete the rollout and route as a last resort (staging-only admin path). Also added a post-run sweeper that detects leftover resources with the test prefix and removes them.
Dylan Brooks: Can we align naming with Console/Platform? ‘pause’ vs ‘auto-stop’ semantics are easy to confuse.
Leila Farouk (author): Renamed the test cases to match product wording: ‘auto-stop (pause)’ and ‘auto-rollback’. Also updated the README and job output to print the final state using the orchestrator enums.
Logan Wright: Please be careful with metrics queries. Querying raw series per route+rollout can still be expensive. Can we query a pre-aggregated endpoint or enforce a single rollout_id filter?
Leila Farouk (author): Done. All metrics calls include rollout_id and cohort filter, and we use the staging cohort comparison endpoint rather than raw series. Added a hard fail if the query attempts to pull unfiltered route-level series.

Context: The presubmit pipeline has grown noisy and slow due to full toolchain fetches, overly conservative devdep pinning, and repeated cold-start overheads in ephemeral CI runners. Motivation: Reduce pretest latency and flakiness by introducing a lightweight presubmit prober that warms an ephemeral 'shadow' artifact cache, a sparse-fetch wrapper to avoid pulling full toolchains for quick presubmit lanes, and a small dependency-cleanser (Oxide) that flags / optionally prunes devdeps causing large install graphs. This PR bundles a tooling + workflow refactor to give teams an opt-in fast lane for quick feedback and a hygiene tool to keep CI images and lockfiles lean. Summary of changes: - tools/presubmit-prober/: new Go binary (small, dependency-free) that probes common package registries, exercises cache layers, and warms a shadow cache on the runner prior to heavy installs. It exits 0 on successful warm, non-zero on registries unavailable (used to gate slow lanes). - tools/oxide-dep-cleanser/: Python script + policy rules that detect devdeps larger than XMB or with >N transitive deps; emits a suggested devdep rollback or a Linear ticket. Has a --dry-run mode used in CI. - .github/workflows/presubmit.yml: adds a 'quick-lint' lane that runs the prober + sparse-fetch + lint/test smoke subset for changed packages. Quick lane is opt-in via PR label "quick-feedback" and automatically triggers when change size < 200 LOC and files_changed_count < 10. - ci/ci-setup/sparse-fetch.sh: new wrapper around package managers (npm/pip/go) that uses registry list hints and fetches only declared direct deps for quick lanes. - Docker/ci: small tweaks to the CI image entrypoint to expose shadow-cache dir and make cache permissions deterministic. - docs/dev/ci-guides.md: documents opt-in criteria, observability signals, how to interpret Oxide reports, and rollout plan. Design notes: - The shadow cache is kept in the runner's ephemeral workspace and does not change upstream artifacts; it's purely advisory to reduce network and cold cache penalty. - Oxide deliberately does not edit lockfiles in CI by default; we run it with --dry-run and surface structured findings in presubmit comments. Teams can flip a repo-level config to allow automated patch PRs after manual review. - Quick-lint lane preserves strict unit/integration lanes for main pipeline; fast lane is additive and gated so it cannot replace full checks. Testing done: - Local unit tests for presubmit-prober (registry mocking), oxide (policy fuzzing) - End-to-end smoke on a canary repo with 30 sample PRs: median presubmit setup time reduced from ~125s to ~62s on quick lanes. - Integration: ran full main pipeline twice with the new hooks to ensure no regressions; a flakey integration test surfaced (test/db/timeout) which was unrelated and filed as SUP-2123. Rollout plan: - Start as opt-in for 20% of repos via repo-config opt-in label and selective enabling in .github. - Monitor presubmit latency, flake rate, and Oxide false-positive rate for 2 weeks. - Follow-up: enable auto PR creation for low-risk devdeps after product review. Checklist: - [x] Add presubmit-prober binary and tests - [x] Add Oxide script + policy rules - [x] Wire quick-lint lane and sparse-fetch wrapper - [x] Add docs and observability hooks - [x] Add reviewer feedback fixes (timeouts/logging/metrics) Related work: builds on ENG-4020 (ci sparse-fetch research) and pairs with ENG-4231 (presubmit cost telemetry).
Initial add of presubmit-prober and oxide tools; add sparse-fetch wrapper; update presubmit workflow with quick-lint lane; docs and CI-image tweaks; follow-up commit reduces prober logging and shortens timeouts per reviewer feedback; final commit bumps presubmit workflow to gate by label and change-size heuristics.
Liam O'Connor: Nice approach. Please reduce prober log noise and add a single prom metric for warm_duration_ms.
Ava Chen: Addressed — reduced log level and added warm_duration_ms histogram (promclient). PTAL.
Sofia Martinez: Oxide looks useful but I'm worried about false positives on monorepos. Can we add a repo whitelist and a dry-run default?
Ava Chen: Added repo-level opt-in in policies.yaml and made dry-run the default in CI. Also surfaced findings to presubmit comments rather than auto-fixing.
Ravi Iyer: Quick-lint gating looks sane; please ensure the heuristic doesn't run for release/* branches.
Ava Chen: Added explicit branch guard and unit test showing the guard behaviour.
SRE (automated): integration tests had 1 transient DB timeout during runs; reran and passed. Logged SUP-2123 for follow-up.
- Add opt-in quick-lint presubmit lane that reduces setup time for small PRs
- Introduce presubmit-prober to warm runner caches and reduce cold-start latency
- Introduce Oxide dep cleanser for devdep hygiene (dry-run by default)
- Sparse-fetch wrapper for faster installs in quick lanes
Ops: monitor presubmit-latency and oxide false-positive rate. Backstop: quick-lint is opt-in and cannot block merges unless repo config is changed.

Context: During a recent incident we observed cascade eviction behavior when the SLO enforcer moved tenants to hard-evict state aggressively under transient overloads (see SUP-987). This PR introduces a tenant lease preserver that temporarily converts hard-evict decisions into 'preserve-lease' windows and an incremental SLO backoff algorithm that lengthens backoff windows per tenant to avoid oscillation.

Motivation: prevent noisy evictions that amplify regional failover and reduce tail latency spiking when capacity flaps.

High level:
- Add tenant_lease_preserver component in serving/controlplane that records short-lived preserves and emits telemetry
- Change SLO enforcer decision path: hard-evict -> preserve-lease (short) -> escalate only if preserve window expires without improvement
- Introduce incremental backoff state machine that grows preserve windows with repeated infra failures and decays them on sustained healthy signals
- Expose rollout flags and percent-based gating via feature flags to allow staged enablement across regions

Description checklist:

- [x] Integration test exercising preserve -> escalate path
- [x] Metrics and tracing events added
- [x] Config flags + runtime documentation
- [x] Canary rollout plan in PR description

Observability and alerts:

Testing:

Rollout plan:

2) Enable for 5% tenants in us-west via flag

Review conversation (selected):

- Sofia: "Prefer to move decay constants to config file for on-the-fly tuning." Maya: "Done; moved to featureflags/config.yaml and added runtime knobs."

Hotfix considerations: This change aims to reduce blast radius; however it touches the eviction hot path so rollout is conservative. For urgent customer impact we also added a temporary safety bypass (featureflags.slo_preserver_bypass) to revert to previous behavior without code rollback.

Related work: ENG-6123 (design), SUP-987 (incident), PRs referenced during review: #2143577 (heartbeat sanitizer)

Backwards compatibility: configuration defaults preserve current behavior (preserver disabled) and is opt-in. Telemetry is additive.

Context and motivation: Our current rollout controllers focus on instantaneous metrics (latency/err-rate) and cohort partitioning. That makes short-lived signal spikes (traffic bursts, transient infra flakiness) cause noisy rollbacks or overly conservative holds. This PR introduces a Temporal Signal Horizon Swap Controller: a rollout orchestration component that smooths short-lived metric spikes across a configurable decay horizon and gates model swaps by a time-weighted anomaly budget. The goal is to reduce noisy rollbacks while preserving quick safety responses for sustained degradations.

What this PR changes (high level):
- New controller: pkg/rollouts/temporal_horizon_controller.go implementing the horizon window and decay weighting.
- Decay policy library: pkg/rollouts/decay_policy.go + tests, exposes configurable half-life and weighting functions.
- Swap executor updates: services/orchestrator/swap_executor.go updated to consult horizon controller decisions and produce safe swap transactions with checkpointed rollback markers.
- Safety journal: deployments/rollback_journal/entry.go — lightweight append-only log for post-mortem playback and deterministic rollback.
- E2E tests: deployments/e2e/temporal_horizon_swap_test.go (simulates transient spikes vs sustained regressions).
- Docs: docs/runbooks/temporal-signal-swap.md and examples/rollouts/temporal_horizon.yaml.

Key design points:
- Time-weighting: recent observations are decayed with an exponential half-life so a single short spike contributes less to the aggregate anomaly score than sustained regressions.
- Two-stage gating: the controller exposes a fast-fail gate (immediate severe-signal abort) and a smoothed gate (time-weighted score must exceed threshold for t_window).
- Safety budget: rollouts are allocated a small anomaly budget per cohort. If the budget is exhausted, the controller triggers an automated rollback and escalates telemetry.
- Deterministic rollback markers: swap_executor writes a checkpoint to the rollback journal before switching traffic. Rollback replays are deterministic and recorded for audits.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation of controller and decay policy
- [x] Unit tests for weighting functions (pkg/rollouts/decay_policy_test.go)
- [x] Integration tests simulating noise vs sustained errors
- [x] Runbook and example usage
- [x] Performance microbench for controller loop (benchmarks added under pkg/rollouts/bench)
- [x] Metrics and tracing hooks added (metrics: rollout.horizon_score, rollout.budget_remaining; traces: rollout.swap_attempt)

- 1d2e3f4: integrate with swap executor and add rollback journal checkpointing
- 2f3g4h5: add unit tests and benchmark; tune half-life defaults to 60s
- 3h4i5j6: add e2e simulation harness and CI job; hook up metrics and traces
- 4k5l6m7: docs and example manifest; address review comments

@@ services/orchestrator/swap_executor.go +72, -12
-   if !safetyOk(r) { return errors.New("safety check failed") }
+   // consult temporal horizon controller before committing swap
+   decision, err := horizon.Controller.Evaluate(ctx, r.Cohort, currentMetrics)
+   if err != nil { return err }
+   if decision.Abort { return fmt.Errorf("horizon abort: %s", decision.Reason) }
+   // write checkpoint and proceed
+   journal.WriteCheckpoint(ctx, decision.Checkpoint)",

Motivation: during recent regional pressure incidents we saw abrupt circuit flips that caused cascading hard-deny behavior for mid-tier tenants. This PR introduces a lightweight soft-fail gatekeeper inside the routing layer that applies gradual shedding (token-rate reduction + soft-deny responses) per-tenant and per-region before tripping a circuit. The goal is to preserve tail latency SLOs while avoiding wholesale tenant blackouts and large-scale reconnections.

Design summary: the gatekeeper implements a two-stage approach: (1) a fast region-aware estimator computes short-window load pressure and maps it to a shed score; (2) a tenant policy engine maps shed scores + tenant SLO priority to a soft action: prefix caching encouragement, reduced concurrency tokens, or a graceful 'degraded' response envelope (trimmed output, explicit 2xx-with-warning). Only when soft measures cannot stabilize does the existing circuit breaker engage. Key properties: hysteresis windows, exponential cool-down on reopen, k-v cache preservation hints, and telemetry anchors for post-incident analysis.

What changed (high level): added a new routing component (soft_gatekeeper) that hooks into request admission; expanded the tenant policy model to include 'soft_priority' and 'degrade_profile'; instrumented telemetry and traces for decision points; added feature flag + runtime config; tests and docs.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of region estimator and soft action engine
- [x] Unit tests for policy evaluation and hysteresis logic
- [x] Integration tests in benchmark-lab (canary) with simulated regional pressure
- [x] Observability: metrics + traces + dashboards added
- [x] Feature flag gated rollout config added to console
- [x] Rollback plan documented

Testing & validation: ran benchmark-lab scenarios (sustained 60% oversubscription for 3m, bursty 10x spikes) and measured a 3.1x reduction in tenant hard-trips and a 22% improvement in P99 tail latency under load compared to baseline. Integration canary in us-west-2 for 5% traffic ran for 48h with no regressions. All CI checks passed (lint, unit, integration).

Rollout plan: 1) Enable feature flag for 1% traffic in us-west-2 for 24h; verify metrics (slo.soft_fail.trigger_count, slo.circuit.opens) and latency P95/P99; 2) Increase to 10% if stable for 24h; 3) Global canary at 30% then full rollout. Canary opt-out available per-tenant via control-plane toggle.

Rollback & mitigations: the feature is behind a runtime feature flag and operator-safe toggle. If increased error rates are observed we will disable the flag and the system will revert to previous circuit behavior. A hotfix branch is prepared (hotfix/soft-fail-rollback) that reverts the gatekeeper wiring for targeted regions.

Related: SUP-1289 (tenant outages investigation), ENG-4523 (soft degrade design doc), ENG-4599 (policy model extension).

Notes: this change is intentionally conservative in default behavior (soft_priority defaults to 0). To avoid customer surprise the console shows an annotation when a tenant is affected by the gatekeeper and logs a human-readable reason with trace id for support flows.
Leah Kim (review): small nit - please add a comment explaining the magic '0.7' threshold in region estimator. Also suggest moving the cooldown config out of code into config defaults.
Maya Chen (reply): moved threshold to named const and added config override in soft_fail_defaults.yaml. responded inline with performance numbers that drove the threshold choice.
Arjun Rao (review): we need a clear telemetry anchor to show when soft actions are used vs circuits open; added slo.soft_fail.action_count and trace tags. please ensure sampling doesn't overwhelm existing traces.
Tomás Alvarez (approval): tested locally and in benchmark-lab scenario; safe to squash-merge once CI green and docs link is added to console release notes.
Adds an opt-in 'soft-fail gatekeeper' that attenuates hard circuit tripping by applying region-aware, tenant-scoped shedding and a temporary degraded response path. Feature-flagged; rollout via canary. No public API changes.

Summary: Add a new CLI tool (prefill-discover) and service library that scans recent inference traces to synthesize candidate prefill/batching defaults and a lightweight 'quant skeleton' profile to jumpstart quantization trials.
Motivation: many customers delay enabling quantization and batching optimizations because building safe, conservative defaults requires manual profiling and tuning. This PR automates the discovery step, letting tenant admins generate suggested prefill shapes, batch curves and a skeleton quant profile (per-layer candidates, quant bit hints, and fallback-safe flags) along with a simulated unit-econ impact report.
Changes include:
- New binary cmd/prefill-discover (Go) implementing a tenant-scoped discovery pipeline with sampling, fingerprinting, and dry-run simulation.
- Prefill discovery library pkg/prefill/discover.go containing traffic summarizers, batch-shape heuristics, and a candidate scoring function that balances latency SLO risk against cost savings.
- Quant skeletonizer tool tools/quant/skeletonizer.py (Python) that consumes a distilled model signature and token-distribution heatmap to emit an opinionated minimal quant profile (layer groups, target bits, per-layer safe-guard flags).
- Telemetry: added telemetry events (prefill.suggest, quant.skeleton.generated, prefill.simulation.report) with aggregated metrics to console/templates/prefill (dashboard snippets) and new tracing hooks in internal/tracing/prefill.go.
- CLI UX: supports --dry-run, --simulate-traffic, --tenant-id, --seed-profiles and outputs JSON suggestions compatible with the existing policy/importer.
- Safe-apply flow: a simulated apply path that runs microbenchmarks against a shadow pool (if available) and returns a unit-econ delta estimate (tokens/second, estimated $/1M tokens).
- Tests: unit tests and integration tests under test/prefill/* with a small synthetic-trace corpus and a CI smoke test that runs in 2m.
Why this approach: We want to reduce the time-to-first-savings for customers by delivering conservative but actionable defaults. The skeletonizer intentionally produces small, explainable quant steps (e.g., group-to-8bit on dense attention matrices, per-layer fallback path) so that the runtime can gracefully fall back on failure.

Adds a capacity-aware temporary SLO relaxation policy and a regional soft-eviction safeguard to avoid noisy mass-evictions during transient capacity pressure. No user-visible API changes; operational knob under feature flag.
Context: We saw repeated cascade evictions during multi-region capacity spikes where strict SLO enforcement triggered aggressive circuit breakers, causing higher tail latency and customer throttles (SUP-9812). This PR introduces a capacity-aware, timebound SLO relaxation layer plus a regional soft-eviction safeguard that stages evictions to avoid synchronized mass-drains. What changed: 1) control/allocator: add 'capacity-aware slo_relaxation' policy that dynamically relaxes non-critical SLOs by a configurable percentage when sustained node-utilization exceeds a threshold for a hold window; 2) routing/eviction: introduce 'soft-eviction' state where instances are marked for probabilistic eviction over a decay window instead of immediate hard drain, enabling load to bleed off while respecting per-tenant priority buckets; 3) telemetry: new metrics (slo_relaxation.active, soft_eviction.pending, soft_eviction.success_rate) and traces for decision points; 4) ops: feature flag rts.slo_relaxation_v1 and runtime knobs for threshold/decay; 5) tests: end-to-end canary harness and unit coverage for decision logic. Motivation: allow graceful degradation that is both capacity- and cost-aware: we prefer slight SLO slack for low-priority requests over wholesale region failovers or bulk evictions which amplify disruption. Implementation notes: the relaxation algorithm is conservative by default (5% token latency budget increase, 2-minute hold window) and respects tenant-priority masks; the soft-eviction uses jittered timers and a token-bucket backoff to limit eviction rate per-region. Operation guidance: defaults are safe for most clusters; ops can tune threshold and relaxation_pct per-capacity class. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (internal design doc: https://linear.app/ENG/1428/capacity-aware-slo-relaxation) - [x] unit tests - [x] integration canary in perf-lab - [x] metrics + dashboard patches - [x] feature-flag gating - [x] rollout playbook attached (see PR artifacts) Commits: 3 commits (initial implementation, metrics + tests, docs + rollback hooks). High-level changed files: control/allocator/policy_manager.go, control/allocator/slo_relaxation.go, routing/eviction/soft_eviction.go, routing/eviction/soft_eviction_test.go, telemetry/metrics_definitions.yaml, ops/feature_flags.yaml, docs/ops/slo-relaxation.md, examples/perf-canary/config.yml. Review conversation summary: Marcus Lin: "Can we make tenant-priority mask evaluation O(1) to avoid runtime cost?" — Author: "Updated mask cache to constant-time lookup and added microbenchmark (see commit 2)." Aisha Patel: "How do we avoid oscillation between relaxed and strict states under flapping load?" — Author: "Added hold window and exponential backoff on relaxation decay; documented rationale and added unit tests for flapping scenario." Ethan Zhao: "Suggest lowering default relaxation_pct to 3% for small regions." — Author: "Left default at 5% but exposed knob and wrote guidance; lowered default for regions with <8 GPUs in ops playbook." CI history: Initial run failed lint due to unused import in soft_eviction_test.go; fixed in commit 3. Integration perf canary showed reduced peak eviction rate in staging (40% -> 7%) with 1.8% median latency increase on low-priority traffic. Rollout plan: enable feature flag in staging for 24h, enable in one EU region with canary traffic split 5%, monitor slo_relaxation.active, soft_eviction.success_rate, region_eviction_rate and rollback in 30m if region_eviction_rate increases. Merge: squashed and merged after approvals from all reviewers and green CI. Post-merge actions: deploy to dedicated canary clusters, coordinate on-call rotation for first 48h, add alert thresholds to SLO dashboard. Notes: This is an operationally-sensitive change; although not a breaking API change, treat rollout as a minor incident risk and follow ops playbook.

Context: Multiple teams requested consistent streaming ergonomics and auth/reauth behavior across the three official SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go). This PR implements a lightweight compatibility layer in the monorepo to centralize retry profiles, stream consumer semantics, and signal/shutdown handling so SDKs can converge without duplicating policy logic. Motivation: parity gaps were causing subtle production regressions (different backoff curves, resume semantics, and platform shutdown behavior). Goals: 1) provide a single source of truth for retry/backoff presets used by all SDKs, 2) standardize streaming consumer APIs (async iterator in Python, async generator / AsyncIterable in TS, context-aware streamer in Go) and 3) add platform-specific shutdown handling (improved Windows Ctrl-C/signal handling) and a small set of batching presets for low-latency / high-throughput workloads. Summary of work: - New compat module: sdk/compat/retry_presets.go / retry_presets.py / retryPresets.ts which define named retry bundles (conservative, balanced, aggressive) and serialization hooks so SDKs can embed them at build time. - Streaming API harmonization: Python: introduced StreamClient.iter_lines() typed async iterator and StreamConsumer helper for backpressure hooks; TypeScript: added AsyncGenerator-based consumer helpers plus small adapter for Node/Browser differences; Go: added StreamCursor interface that accepts context.Context for clean cancellation and a StreamAdapter that mirrors TS/Py semantics. - Auth & reauth: centralized token refresh policy and heartbeat hint protocol so SDKs can exchange short lease tokens and run the same refresh jitter logic. - Batching presets: server + client hints to encourage smaller/larger batch windows depending on latency budget; clients surface an ergonomic batchingHint option. - Windows and signal handling: previously the Go SDK's interrupt logic was Linux-first; added a small cross-platform signal shim and e2e test to validate graceful KV cache flush on Ctrl-C on Windows runners. - Docs and examples: updated docs/sdk/streaming.md with cross-language examples and migration notes, added examples/streaming/prefix_cache.py and examples/ts/streaming_demo.ts. - Tests: unit tests in each SDK package for parity cases, integration smoke tests in ci/workflows/sdk-integration.yml. Checklist: - [x] compat/retry_presets implemented and exported - [x] Python async iterator facade added and documented - [x] TypeScript async generator helpers added and documented - [x] Go context-aware StreamCursor implemented - [x] Token refresh policy centralized and validated - [x] BatchingHint option surfaced in client constructors - [x] Windows signal shim + e2e test added - [x] CI matrix updated to run py/ts/go streaming suites - [x] Version bumps for all three SDKs Local testing: ran unit tests across SDKs and the integration smoke suite locally and on CI windows-latest, ubuntu-latest, macos-latest. Observability: added short-lived telemetry hooks so the platform can measure retry counts and reauth latencies (opt-in by default to protect privacy). Rollout plan: merged to main behind feature gate; SDKs will publish subsequent releases once the compatibility package lands in the build artifacts. Breaking changes: none by default; new ergonomic APIs are additive and migration notes are in the docs. Related: references ENG-2345 (streaming parity), ENG-4512 (token lease refactor), SUP-987 (customer-reported reconnects).
Introduces a cross-SDK compatibility shim for streaming auth/reauth and a consumer-friendly stream API across Python/TypeScript/Go. Bumps SDK versions: py 2.3.0, ts 1.13.0, go v1.9.0. Adds batching-friendly retry presets and Windows signal handling for graceful shutdowns.
Miguel Santos: Can we avoid importing the entire compat package into the runtime hot path? Suggest lazy load + serializing presets into a small JSON blob included in builds.
Evelyn Park: Good point; switched to serialized presets embedded at build time in build/release/manifest.json to keep runtime footprint minimal.
Priya Natarajan: In Python, the async iterator surface looks good but please add an example for handling backpressure when consumers are slow.
Evelyn Park: Added consumer_helpers.py with documented usage and included example in docs and examples/streaming/prefix_cache.py.
Connor O'Reilly: Windows runner e2e is flaky on first run due to timing; recommend adding a small retry or longer timeout to the ctrl-c validation.
Evelyn Park: Increased timeout and added one retry attempt in the windows job; re-ran CI and verified stability.
Follow-up: publish SDK packages after release job includes the compat manifest. Plan to cut python 2.3.0, typescript 1.13.0, go v1.9.0 in the next release window. Monitor new telemetry for retry spikes for two weeks; rollback plan is to flip feature gate in the platform and republish SDKs with previous default presets if needed.

Add a lightweight auditing tool that scans tenant prefill and batching defaults and emits safe quantization fallback rules. Includes a small CLI and telemetry events to integrate with Console alerts.
Motivation: Some tenants with low qps and narrow request distributions were picking aggressive default batch shapes and quant profiles that regressed latency and occasionally broke low-memory hosts. This PR adds a lightweight auditor and runtime adapter that (1) statically lints tenant prefill/batching defaults against observed shape histograms, (2) synthesizes conservative quantization safety fallbacks for affected tenants, and (3) surfaces deterministic telemetry so Console can create alerts and automated rollbacks. What changed: added a new CLI 'prefill-lint' under cmd/prefill-lint for offline checks; implemented runtime adapter in serving/prefill/safety_adapter.go that applies conservative quant/shape overrides when memory headroom is low; added a small telemetry bridge (observability/prefill_audit_bridge.go) that emits audit findings as events; extended the defaults manifest schema with an optional safety_profile block; unit/integration tests and docs. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4921) - [x] Unit tests for linter and adapter - [x] Integration smoke against a small local cluster - [x] Telemetry hooks added to Console-compatible channel - [x] Backwards compatible: new safety_profile is optional Rollout plan: Canary rollout on dedicated pools for 48h; observe telemetry and Console alerts; if we see >5% latency regression on pinned tenants revert adapter via feature flag. Related: SUP-879 incident postmortem influenced the heuristics in the linter. The description below lists commits, changed areas, review comments, CI summary, and merge details.
Samantha Liu: Can you clarify the memory headroom threshold used by safety_adapter? Is it per-GPU or aggregate?
Arjun Patel: The threshold is per-device and derived from the device memory reporting plus a safety margin constant (see safety_adapter.go constants). I added comments and a short note in the docs.
