This PR introduces the first cut of multi-window, multi-burn-rate alerting for tiered SLOs (Hosted vs Dedicated) using Prometheus recording rules + Alertmanager alerts. The goal is to standardize burn-rate paging across endpoint classes (chat/completions, embeddings, streaming) and regions without blowing up cardinality. This is the alerting layer for the tiered SLO + error budget program; budget computation/enforcement gates are tracked separately.

What’s included: (1) Recording rules to compute request success rate and burn rate from gateway/routing SLIs with consistent label sets (tier, region, route_class, protocol). (2) Alert queries implementing multi-window burn-rate alerts (fast + slow) per tier/endpoint/region with initial thresholds aligned to a 30d budget window. (3) Alert annotations with runbook + dashboard links and incident-bot-friendly fields. (4) Guardrails to avoid per-model/per-customer label expansion (we intentionally do NOT include model_id or customer_id in the core paging alerts).

Key design points: (a) Alerts page on burn rate (error budget consumption) rather than raw error rate to normalize across SLO targets. (b) Multi-window alerts reduce flapping and catch both sharp regressions and slow leaks. (c) Tier-aware labeling is required at ingest (see tier-tagging PR); this PR assumes the tier label is present on the underlying SLI metrics.

Initial thresholds (subject to tuning during rollout): For 30d SLO windows, we page when burn_rate_1h > 14.4 AND burn_rate_5m > 14.4 (fast burn), or burn_rate_6h > 6 AND burn_rate_30m > 6 (slow burn). These are standard Google SRE-style burn alerts and correspond to spending a material fraction of the monthly budget quickly. We emit warning (Slack only) at half thresholds to support the warn-only enforcement phase.

Runbooks / dashboards: Runbook: confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/error-budget-breach-mitigation-runbook. Dashboard: grafana/d/tiered-slo/tiered-slo-burn-rate (linked in annotations). Incident process: confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/error-budget-breach-incident-process.

Notes / follow-ups: (1) Streaming disconnect SLI semantics are still being finalized; current alerting uses the existing stream_error_total / stream_sessions_total series with client-abort exclusions applied upstream. (2) Dedicated account-level alerts are out of scope here; this PR only covers tier/region/route_class aggregates. (3) Once enforcement gates move beyond warn-only, we’ll revisit severities + paging routes per tier.

Test plan: Validated rule evaluation in promtool; verified generated series names/labels in staging; manually triggered an error-rate spike in staging gateway to confirm fast-burn paging + annotation links; validated Alertmanager routing to eng-sre-oncall for Dedicated and eng-platform-oncall for Hosted (as configured in alertmanager routes).

Risk: Moderate. Recording rules are additive but can increase TSDB load if label sets drift; we included explicit labeldrop/labelkeep in rule templates and limited dimensions to tier/region/route_class/protocol only.
Core metric inputs assumed (post-exclusion): redwood_api_requests_total{result="success"|"error",error_class!="invalid_request"|"rate_limited",tier,region,route_class,protocol}
Burn rate definition: burn_rate = (1 - success_rate) / (1 - slo_target). For streaming: burn_rate = stream_failure_rate / allowed_failure_rate (target varies by tier).
We use recording rules to normalize names: redwood:sli_success_rate:<window> and redwood:slo_burn_rate:<window> with a stable label set.
Fast burn (page): (redwood:slo_burn_rate:5m{tier="dedicated"} > 14.4) and (redwood:slo_burn_rate:1h{tier="dedicated"} > 14.4)
Slow burn (page): (redwood:slo_burn_rate:30m{tier="hosted"} > 6) and (redwood:slo_burn_rate:6h{tier="hosted"} > 6)
Warning (slack): same queries with thresholds /2 and severity=warning
Allison Grant: Can we confirm the label set won’t accidentally include model_id after the routing layer adds tags? I want this to be safe-by-default.
Sergio Costa: Yep—recording rules explicitly use by(tier, region, route_class, protocol). Even if upstream adds model_id/customer_id, it won’t be preserved in the aggregate series. I also added a template helper to labeldrop everything except the allowlist for the final series name.
Thomas Baird: These recording rules will create a lot of series if route_class is too granular. What values do we expect here? Please document the allowlist.
Sergio Costa: Good call. Updated docs to define route_class as one of {chat, completions, embeddings, rerank, streaming} and added a prom rule test that fails if new classes appear without updating the allowlist.
Aisha Bello: Thresholds look reasonable, but for Hosted we may need to start with warning-only paging during rollout. Can we set severity=page only for Dedicated and warning for Hosted for the first week?
Sergio Costa: I wired severity mapping by tier behind a single variable in the alert config. Default is page for both, but I added a staged override file (disabled by default) we can enable in prod during rollout.
Connor O'Brien: Please add runbook link + dashboard link in annotations; incident-bot depends on consistent annotation keys.
Sergio Costa: Added annotations: runbook_url, dashboard_url, slo_tier, route_class, region, and a short 'impact' string. Also aligned summary formatting with incident-bot expectations.
Logan Wright: Any concerns about scraping/evaluation load? Also, do we have promtool coverage for these rules?
Sergio Costa: Added promtool rule tests for recording + alert rules (synthetic fixtures) and confirmed CPU impact is within limits in staging (<3% evaluator CPU increase).

alerts: add burn-rate recording rules (5m/30m/1h/6h) for availability + streaming reliability
alerts: add multi-window burn-rate alerts with severities + routing labels
dashboards: add deploy/incident annotations hook fields used by burn alerts

Summary: Adds a GPU-backed load test harness (burstbench) that exercises Dedicated baseline + burst behavior with a paired “neighbor” tenant and fails the run when neighbor tail latency regresses beyond configured thresholds. The harness produces a structured report (JSON) and JUnit output for CI consumption, and optionally uploads run artifacts (latency histograms + admission/denial breakdown) to GCS for SRE review. Motivation: During burst beta we had a couple near-misses where burst admission was “correct” but non-burst neighbors saw measurable p99 tail amplification under certain batching/telemetry conditions. We need an automated, repeatable test that detects noisy-neighbor regressions before GA tuning/rollouts. This PR implements the core scenarios + an analyzer/gate that can be used in nightly and pre-GA release qualification runs. What’s included: (1) New tool `tools/burstbench/` (Go) that can generate two-tenant traffic against a staging or perf cluster using Redwood gateway APIs, with deterministic request shapes and seeded randomness. (2) Scenario library for `baseline_only`, `burst_window`, and `burst_with_cooldown` with knobs for request rate ramps, max concurrency, streaming/non-streaming mix, and token distributions. (3) Analyzer that computes p50/p95/p99 per tenant, plus “neighbor delta” metrics: `neighbor_p95_delta_ms`, `neighbor_p99_delta_ms`, and `tail_amplification_ratio` (p99/p50) before vs during burst window. (4) Regression gate config (`tools/burstbench/configs/guardrails.yaml`) with defaults aligned to Dedicated non-burst SLO protection: fail run if neighbor p95 increases by > 40ms or neighbor p99 increases by > 120ms for >= 3 consecutive 1m buckets; warn-only thresholds are also emitted. (5) Buildkite step + documentation for running in nightly on `perf-us-east-h100` (gated behind a flag; does not run on every PR by default due to GPU cost). (6) Prometheus query snapshots embedded in the report (best-effort) to correlate admission controller denials/queueing and router fallback events during the test window. Notes/assumptions: - This uses real staging/perf infra with Dedicated + burst pool enabled; it does not attempt to fully emulate kernel-level contention in unit tests. The only “fast” CI coverage is the analyzer unit tests + report formatting. - Tenant IDs are passed explicitly; we do not create tenants as part of the test (avoids control-plane flakiness). - The harness labels are constrained to avoid high cardinality in metrics; per Allison’s guidance, we only tag `scenario`, `run_id`, `region`, and `hardware_class` (no tenant names in metrics). How to run: `bazel run //tools/burstbench:burstbench -- --config tools/burstbench/configs/burst_window_us_east_h100.yaml --run_id local-<ts> --target https://gateway.perf.us-east.redwood.ai` (see README for required auth + allowlist). Outputs: - `artifacts/report.json` (full run) - `artifacts/junit.xml` (gating) - `artifacts/summary.txt` (human readable) - Optional upload to `gs://redwood-perf-artifacts/burstbench/<run_id>/` when `--upload_artifacts` is set. Rollout: Start with nightly + manual pre-release qualification. Once stable (2 weeks) we can consider enabling the analyzer gate on release branches for burst-related changes only (label-driven).
Sean Gallagher (review): Can we make the failure criteria explicit in the PR description and ensure they map to “non-burst protection” rather than “burst customer success”? I want to avoid a test that silently incentivizes loosening guardrails. Also: please add a note about bucket duration and consecutive-bucket logic (we’ve been bitten by flappy gates). Peter Holtz (author): Updated README + PR description; guardrails are explicitly neighbor-protection oriented. Added `--bucket_duration` and documented default 60s with a 3-bucket consecutive requirement to fail. Allison Grant (review): Please do not emit tenant IDs/names as metric labels. Also, make sure the report includes the exact query window boundaries so we can correlate in Grafana. Peter Holtz (author): Removed tenant label entirely; metrics now only include scenario/run_id/region/hwclass. Added report fields `window_start_rfc3339` and `window_end_rfc3339` plus per-phase boundaries. Keiko Yamamoto (review): The p95/p99 delta thresholds look plausible, but can we make them config-only (no constants) and add a warn band? Also, does cooldown scenario verify that denials drop after cooldown? Peter Holtz (author): Thresholds moved to `guardrails.yaml`, and analyzer emits WARN vs FAIL states. Cooldown scenario now asserts that `BURST_COOLDOWN_ACTIVE` denials dominate for the configured cooldown duration and then decrease once cooldown expires (reported as a check, not a gate yet). Mina Haddad (review): For the router correlation, do we rely on log scraping or Prometheus? Prefer Prometheus queries. Also ensure we record fallback rate (baseline vs burst admitted). Peter Holtz (author): Switched to Prometheus query snapshotting via the internal query API (best-effort, non-fatal). Added fallback counters to the report: `router_fallback_rate` and `admission_denial_rate` for the burst window. Ravi Menon (review): Minor: rename “neighbor” to “non_burst_neighbor” in the report to make semantics clear. Also, can we add a scenario knob for streaming vs non-streaming? Peter Holtz (author): Renamed fields and added `streaming_mix` to scenario config. Final approvals: Sean Gallagher (approved), Allison Grant (approved), Keiko Yamamoto (approved), Mina Haddad (approved).
Merged via squash into main after approvals; nightly perf step enabled behind `PERF_NIGHTLY_BURSTBENCH=1` on the perf pipeline only.
Internal: Added burstbench load test harness + neighbor latency regression gate (nightly/perf only). No customer-facing changes.
payload.title: Load test harness for burst pools + neighbor tail-latency regression checks

Summary: This PR adds two related pieces of automation for cost optimization: 1) an Economic Fallthrough Engine (EFE) that makes request-level routing decisions to fall back to cheaper quantized model variants when unit economy checks indicate acceptable risk, and 2) a Quant Cohort Linter that statically and dynamically flags inconsistent quantization profiles across model cohorts.
Motivation: Customers want predictable unit economics without regressing quality. We frequently see manual ad-hoc fallbacks that either regress accuracy or fail to capture cost wins. EFE codifies a conservative policy allowing safe fallthrough to smaller/quantized variants when workload signatures and eval-driven thresholds are satisfied.
Design:
- EFE evaluates three signals at request time: workload cohort, live quality estimate (fast embedding similarity + sketch of rerank delta), and unit-econ delta (expected tokens * cost-per-token delta). The policy DSL supports hard thresholds (e.g. max-allowed-quality-delta) and soft gates (budget-weighted scoring).
- Quant Cohort Linter runs on model manifests and CI to detect mismatched quant settings (e.g. a 4-bit profile missing KV cache-friendly layout), and flags runtime incompatibilities that would make fallthrough unsafe.
- Batch/cache defaults: Introduce cohort-aware defaults for batching (target_microbatch / preferred_batch_window_ms) and KV cache retention. These defaults are conservative; they can be overridden per-tenant.
Implementation:
- runtime/fallthrough/engine.go: core policy evaluation + metrics hooks.
- runtime/fallthrough/policy_dsl.go: small DSL with unit-econ expressions and fallthrough scoring.
- optimizer/quant/linter.py: static validators + dynamic test harness to replay small batches and check output distributions.
- infra/telemetry/metrics.yaml: new metrics (econ_fallthrough_attempts, econ_fallthrough_accepts, quant_linter_issues) and dashboard templates.
- docs/operational/econ-fallthrough.md: design doc, rollout playbook, rollback steps, and example policy snippets.
Safety & mitigations:
- Conservative defaults: EFE is off by default for tenants; it can be enabled via tenant feature flag.
- Canary rollout plan below: start at 1% traffic, monitor quality delta and fallback ratio, escalate to 5/25/100% only on green.
- Automatic auto-revert if sliding-window quality regression > 0.75% or if error rate increases by > 0.5% over baseline.
Testing:
- unit tests for policy evaluation and DSL parsing.
- integration test that runs 500 synthetic requests across synthetic cohorts to assert that fallthrough occurs only when unit-econ delta > threshold and quality proxies are within tolerance.
- CI harness runs the Quant Cohort Linter against the model registry (snapshot) and fails if new models introduce incompatible quant layouts.
Measured results from internal experiment (toy tenant):
- Average per-token cost reduction for targeted baseline: 8.3%
- Median latency change: +7ms (within SLA)
- Quality proxy regression (similarity sketch): 0.3% (below threshold)
Rollout plan:
1) Enable EFE in staging + run linter for entire model catalog.
2) Canary 1% of traffic (48h) -> 5% (72h) -> 25% (7d) -> 100% if no regressions.
3) Expose safe-config presets via Console and a dry-run mode that logs potential savings without applying fallthroughs.
Related work items: Linear ENG-784 (fallthrough engine prototype), ENG-810 (quant linting + CI).
Checklist:
- [x] Core runtime + policy DSL
- [x] Quant Cohort Linter + CI integration
- [x] Metrics + dashboards
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Docs and rollout playbook
- [x] Feature flag gating for tenants
Add Economic Fallthrough Engine to route eligible requests to cheaper quantized model variants under unit-econ guarantees; include Quant Cohort Linter to validate quant profile consistency; introduce workload cohort defaults for batching and KV cache. Rollout with canary and metrics guardrails.
Priya Desai: Can you walk through how cohort identification works for traffic with mixed patterns?
Ethan Liu: Cohorts are generated by sampling recent requests and clustering on short signatures (prompt length, prompt embedding centroid, route). We use a sliding window to adapt.
Miguel Santos: Linter flagged two registry entries with incompatible KV layouts; are we auto-blocking publish?
Ethan Liu: Linter fails CI by default for protected branches; for model-publish pipeline we added a suppressible warning mode for experimental channels.
Harriet Cole: Suggest adding a flag to make the canary duration configurable as a tenant-level policy.
Ethan Liu: Added tenant.canary.duration in config/defaults/cohort-batch-presets.yaml and added docs.
Priya Desai: Two minor nits on logging verbosity in engine.go.
Ethan Liu: Addressed (removed noisy debug logs behind feature flag).
Miguel Santos: CI flakes on the quant-linter job intermittently; can we add retry?
Ethan Liu: Added 3x retry on transient linter jobs and hardened an environment var.
Approved-by: Priya Desai, Miguel Santos

Context and motivation: Customers with regulatory requirements have asked for higher-fidelity, queryable proofs that a request was served under a particular jurisdiction and that encryption keys used were consistent with the tenant's region pin. This PR implements a lightweight jurisdictional audit indexer (compact per-tenant shard), a KMS-proof collector that batches and anchors KMS usage proofs into audit envelopes, and a temporal RBAC lock abstraction that prevents short-lived elevation across jurisdiction boundaries. Scope: this change touches the audit pipeline, authz middleware, and the KMS integration layer. It is designed to be backward-compatible for hosted users and opt-in for Private deployments (installer flag: --enable-jurisdictional-audit). Checklist: - [x] Implement audit indexer and storage schema (compact shards + retention knobs) - [x] Add KMS-proof collector that emits verifiable per-batch proofs into envelope v2 - [x] Introduce temporal RBAC lock with TTL and region-bound constraints - [x] Expose token hint header X-Region-Pin for downstream routing and policy evaluation - [x] Add unit + integration tests for indexer, proof collector, and auth path - [x] Update docs & ops runbook for rollout/rollback - [x] Add opt-in installer toggle for Private installs Compatibility notes: Audit envelope v2 is interpreted by the indexer; hosted migration will enable a read-only bridge for existing envelopes for 30 days before enabling full indexing. Private installer will keep the feature disabled by default and expose a migration command. Security considerations: KMS proofs are HMAC-signed with a rotation-aware key; indexer data is stored encrypted-at-rest and tagged with residency metadata. No plaintext keys are stored. Performance: indexer runs asynchronously and uses a bounded in-memory buffer; typical CPU/IO overhead observed in load testing is <3% at p95 traffic patterns. See testing section for numbers. Implementation summary: - services/audit/indexer.go: new indexer service with shard manager and compaction - services/audit/envelope_v2.go: envelope v2 decoder and proof unpacker - pkg/kms/proof_collector.go: KMS batching + signer interface - pkg/rbac/temporal_lock.go: RBAC temporal lock + policy evaluation hooks - middleware/auth/region_pin.go: reads X-Region-Pin and annotates context - migrations/2026_02_jurisdictional_index.sql: DB schema for index metadata - ci/integration/audit-indexer-e2e.yaml: integration pipeline for the indexer and KMS proofs Migration and rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind a feature flag. 2) Enable feature flag in staging; run indexer against a replay window to validate envelope v2 compatibility. 3) Run canary in a single region for 48 hours with sampling enabled. 4) For hosted customers, enable read-only indexing for 30 days to surface any parsing gaps; run automated recovery for malformed envelopes. 5) For Private customers, operator runs migration command which validates DB schema and enables the indexer. 6) Roll forward to full indexing and enable temporal RBAC locks cluster-wide. Rollback: feature flag off will stop indexing and collector; index metadata remains but will be ignored by API. Related work: builds on ENG-1201 (audit-envelopes) and ENG-2980 (kms-usage-telemetry).
Ethan Park: Can you clarify how the indexer handles malformed envelope v1 payloads? Suggested adding defensive parse logic and metrics.
Maya Singh: Added defensive parse path which emits audit.indexer.parse_errors and falls back to raw envelope retention for manual inspection.
Lina Fernandez: The RBAC temporal lock needs a TTL jitter to avoid stampedes; also please document admin override flow.
Maya Singh: Added jittered backoff on TTL refresh and documented the operator override (rbacctl unlock --reason).
Arjun Patel: CI flaked on kms integration test, re-run required. Also ensure HMAC key rotates without gaps.
Maya Singh: Fixed test flake by increasing test harness timeouts; implemented key rotation grace window and unit tests.
Lina Fernandez: Please add a smoke test for region-pin header propagation across proxies.
Maya Singh: Added middleware test and updated proxy docs to include X-Region-Pin forwarding rules.

Hotfix: Add soft-quantile SLO throttler to reduce circuit flip oscillations; introduce egress fence to isolate aggressive global egress cuts from cold regions; tweak inflight hedging backoff. Improves stability during regional egress spikes and reduces tenant impact.
Context: During the outage on 2026-02-10 (Linear ENG-2145) we observed repeated circuit flips driven by an aggressive egress cap that applied globally and a hard percentile cut at the SLO boundary. Cold regions with low KV cache pressure were being forced into slowpaths which then tripped regional circuits and cascaded. This PR introduces a soft-quantile SLO throttler that smooths enforcement around the target percentile and an egress fence policy that prevents aggressive global egress reductions from immediately affecting regions with divergent capacity profiles.

What this PR does (single-string description): Implements a soft quantile throttler in services/scheduler that uses a sigmoid-based smoothing window around configured SLO percentiles, adds an egress fence layer in services/egress that marks region eligibility for global egress reductions and enforces staged application, tunes inflight hedging backoff to use exponential backoff with jitter to avoid herd replays, and surfaces additional telemetry (slo_trim_count, egress_fence_denied, inflight_replay_rate) for post-deploy analysis. Includes unit and integration tests, a small canary rollout plan, and a rollback toggle.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2145/soft-quantile-slo-throttler (high-level design and math) - [x] Unit tests for throttler smoothing behavior and egress fence acceptance logic - [x] Integration test for staged egress application in staging cluster - [x] Canary deployment (10% regional routes) observed for 24h with no regression - [x] Added telemetry and dashboards for quick triage - [x] Rollback toggle added (feature flag: slo.soft_trimmer.enabled)

Performance expectations: smoothing reduces spike-induced throttle variance by ~40% in internal microbenchmarks and reduces circuit reopen frequency under synthetic egress bursts. Egress fence should prevent 70% of global egress policy applications from touching cold regions immediately (measured in synthetic staging run). See bench results in commits.

Rollback and safety: feature flag can disable new throttler and egress fence immediately; implementation defaults to fallthrough mode that preserves current behavior if the flag is off. No datastore migrations. Metric-backed abort: if slo_trim_count or inflight_replay_rate exceed safety thresholds we will automatically disable via the feature-flag operator.

Commits summary: - Add soft-quantile throttler core algorithm and tests (author) - Add egress fence policy with staged-apply logic and tests (author) - Tune inflight hedging backoff and add jitter (author) - Add telemetry counters and Grafana dashboard snippets (author) - Canary rollout scripts and config (ops)

Changed areas (high-level): services/scheduler/throttler.go -> new smoothing algorithm and config options; services/egress/policy.go -> egress fence acceptance and staged apply; runtime/kv/cache_manager.go -> small guard to avoid triggering egress fence during KV drain; observability/metrics/registry.go -> new counters and tags; infra/canary/deploy.yaml -> canary rollout config; tests/integration/egress_staged_apply_test.go -> integration test for staged policy.

Why this is different from prior work: Existing SLO enforcement applied a hard percentile cutoff which produced brittle transitions when load and egress quotas were noisy. This change pushes enforcement to a soft window and complements it with a policy-level fence to keep cold regions insulated from large global adjustments. It is intended as an operational stability improvement rather than a new feature.

Related: Linear ENG-2145 (incident), SRE-671 (postmortem follow-up), SUP-982 (customer report about regional flapping).
Maya Chen: Please add microbench numbers — how does smoothing affect p50/p95 under bursty egress?
Evan Patel: Added microbench numbers in commit b2c3d4e and included smoke graphs in the PR description. p95 reduced by ~30% in the synthetic scenario.
Lena Ortiz: The egress fence looks good but we need to ensure the staged apply respects per-tenant isolation; add unit tests for tenant-scoped fence decisions.
Evan Patel: Added tenant-scoped unit tests and a guard in policy.go so tenant-override flags are respected (commit c3d4e5f).
Arjun Rao: Minor nit on log verbosity and a suggestion to tag telemetry with 'canary=true' during rollout. Approved after fix.
Evan Patel: Reduced log verbosity and added canary tag via deploy.yaml. Marking as ready to merge.

Motivation: on-call responders need a fast, low-noise diagnostic snapshot that fits in a notification card and a single-click playbook chooser. This PR ships 'LightProbe' — a compact telemetry sampler that produces a prioritized diagnostic digest — and the 'playbook fuse' UX that attaches contextual playbook suggestions to the probe. Goals: 1) reduce on-call cognitive load by surfacing 3–5 highest-confidence remediation hints; 2) make playbooks actionable from a single commute (copy/paste-free) step; 3) keep the probe size and collection time bounded (~5s, <256KB payload). Summary of changes: - Implementation of LightProbe sampler (agent library + CLI glue) with deterministic snapshot prioritization and optional anonymization hooks. - Playbook fusion algorithm that ranks candidate playbooks by signal-match score (alert fingerprint × recent telemetry delta × historical success). - New /api/v1/probes endpoint and a PlaybookSuggestion sidebar component used by the oncall UI. - Small UX flow and accessibility tweaks so suggestions are keyboard-navigable and copy-safe. - Backwards-compatible telemetry schema v1.1 (probe.metadata.* added). Compatibility & safety: probe runs at user-trigger or incident-initiated and respects redwood RBAC + scrub rules; default anonymization enabled for external/Slack exports. Performance: local microbenchmark under dev cluster shows median probe generation 3.8s (p95 5.1s) and 180KB median payload. See release notes.

payload.body: Motivation: tail latency for mixed-length requests (short chat turns interleaved with long completions) remains a significant pain point in production. Large prefill windows create kernel inefficiencies and cause KV cache churn when multiple long-prefix requests arrive concurrently. This PR introduces a stage-tiling model for the prefill stage plus an opt-in KV warmup hints channel to improve kernel reuse, reduce KV cache thrash, and overlap prefill and decode more efficiently. Changes: 1) Stage tiling: prefill work is split into fixed-size "tiles" (configurable per-model, default 64 tokens). Prefill tiles are scheduled as independent units enabling kernel microbatch fusion across tiles from different requests while preserving per-request ordering guarantees. 2) Asynchronous tile handoff: tiles are queued into a lightweight stage-tiling dispatcher that performs size-aware batching and forwards completed tiles to the decode stage with a small re-order buffer to tolerate out-of-order tile completion. 3) KV warmup hints: service-level metadata header allows the router to attach predicted future tile IDs and token ranges; runtime uses hints to prefetch KV pages and bias kernel selection (fp16 vs q4) for the next tiles. Hints are advisory and gated behind a feature flag. 4) Kernel hinting and eviction policy: add a tile-aware eviction score that prefers keeping KV state for active tiles and for hinted tile ranges; the policy uses a small LRU-with-weight heuristic computed by the serving runtime. 5) Config and observability: new runtime flags (tile_size, tile_reorder_window_ms, kv_hint_enabled) and metrics (tile_fusion_count, tile_out_of_order_pct, kv_hint_hit_rate). Motivation and rationale: tiling reduces stragglers caused by oversized prefill kernels and increases opportunities for microkernel fusion across short bursts. Warmup hints are low-cost metadata piggybacking useful in hybrid workloads where the client can provide next-token distribution shape or approximate token counts. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-1243) - [x] Unit and integration tests for tile dispatcher and reorder buffer - [x] End-to-end benchmarking harness added to perf-canary - [x] Feature flag and runtime config added - [x] Backwards compatibility tests for requests without hints - [x] Observability dashboards and alerts added Summary of commits: ["add stage-tiling dispatcher and tile abstraction","implement tile-aware kernel selection and eviction heuristics","add KV warmup hint parsing and prefetch hooks","tests: tile reorder buffer unit tests","perf: end-to-end benchmarks and harness updates","docs: runtime flags and telemetry notes","minor: lint and typing fixes"] Files changed (high level): ["core/serving/tiling/dispatcher.py","core/serving/tiling/tile.py","core/serving/tiling/reorder_buffer.py","core/serving/kv/prefetcher.cc","core/serving/kv/eviction_policy.cc","core/serving/kernel_selector.cc","runtime/config/runtime_flags.yaml","observability/metrics/tiling.prom","perf-canary/benchmarks/tiling_mixed_length.yaml","docs/runtime/tiling.md","tests/serving/test_tiling_dispatcher.py","tests/serving/test_kv_hint_integration.py"] Review conversation highlights: ["Ethan Park: Nice approach; can you quantify memory overhead for keeping additional tile metadata?","Marisol Nguyen: Measured ~3% additional GPU memory at default tile_size on our 24GB benchmark model; added a flag to lower tile_size to 32 tokens to reduce overhead","Saira Malik: Concern about out-of-order semantics impacting user-visible streaming; how do you ensure deterministic streaming?","Marisol Nguyen: Reorder buffer guarantees per-request token ordering and will only forward contiguous tile prefixes to streaming sockets; added tests covering streaming interleaving","Jonas Becker: Suggest adding a small microbenchmark to the kernel selector to avoid regressing fp32 vs q4 selection; addressed and added tests","Ethan Park: CI flake on one test fixed by increasing retry timeout; re-ran pipeline and all checks passed"] CI summary: "all checks passed after a single pipeline re-run; unit, integration, and perf Canary run green; lint shows two minor warnings fixed in last commit" Benchmarks summary: ["p95 latency reduction on mixed-length trace: 12% median across 10 runs","p99 latency reduction: 9%","aggregate throughput increase under 75% utilization: 8%","KV hint hit rate on synthetic workload: 67% with default hinting enabled","GPU memory overhead: +3% at tile_size=64, +1.5% at tile_size=32","observed token-per-second regression on long-serial workloads: -0.7% (investigation flagged; opt-in flag advises caution)"] Backwards compatibility: "Requests without KV hints behave the same; tiling is safe and controlled by feature flag; existing decode-only pipelines unaffected until feature flag is enabled for a deployment." Release notes: "Introduces stage tiling (configurable tile_size) and an opt-in KV warmup hint header to improve tail latency for mixed-length workloads. Enabled behind a runtime feature flag. Expect lower p95/p99 latencies for chat-like interleaved traffic; monitor kv_hint_hit_rate and tile_out_of_order_pct after rollout." Follow-ups and TODOs: ["ENG-2107: autotune tile_size per-model distribution (next sprint)","Add runtime telemetry for hint-sourced prefetch latency","Investigate small regression on long-serial workloads and add opt-out heuristics for strictly long-run workloads","Add language/SDK examples to redwood-sdk-* repos showing how to emit KV warmup hints"] Notes on testing and rollout: "Feature gated rollout with canary in perf-canary, followed by gradual enable on Dedicated pools. Operators warned via console alert when tile_out_of_order_pct exceeds 5% or kv_hint_hit_rate falls below 25%. All changes covered by unit/integration tests and end-to-end perf runs."

Motivation: Operators and cross-service tooling can amplify residency and KMS risk if delegated credentials are used without a residency-aware guard. This PR introduces an Opaque Residency Proxy (ORP) that centralizes residency-assertion verification, attaches region-bound residency proofs to downstream requests, and enforces KMS usage locality. It also adds an RBACv2 'operator throttle' layer that rate-limits and time-bounds delegated operator grants to reduce lateral blast radius. The change is intended for customers using Private and Dedicated deployments to strengthen data-residency guarantees and auditability while minimizing false positives for normal control-plane operations. Implementation summary: 1) New service components: ORP service (go) and ORP-enforcer sidecar (small wasm filter) that validates incoming operator claims against the residency policy engine and requests a short-lived residency proof token from the KMS-assertor. 2) KMS integration: extended kmspolicy client to support region-anchored key wraps and an 'assert-and-wrap' call that emits a signed residency-proof header (residency-proof:v1) bound to the key manifest and operator claim. 3) RBACv2 extension: operator_throttle policy type and enforcement hook in the policy-evaluator to apply per-operator ephemeral grant limits and cooldown windows. 4) Audit: audit-proxy now accepts an opaque provenance envelope that contains residency-proof metadata and a hash of the original operator token; the envelope is signed and stored in the immutable audit store while PII fields are redacted. 5) Migration: dual-write to audit-v1 and audit-v2 during the rollout; ORP runs in permissive mode by default and flips to enforce after telemetry validation. Checklist: - [x] Design doc and security review (ENG-4219) - [x] Unit tests for ORP and kmspolicy client - [x] Integration test harness for operator_throttle behavior - [x] e2e smoke in staging with permissive mode - [x] Gradual rollout plan with canary and telemetry gating - [x] Docs: operator/residency and KMS integration pages Notes: This description intentionally avoids including raw token samples. See design doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4219 for full diagrams and threat model.
Evan Park: Can we ensure the ORP handles clock skew between regions? Suggest adding monotonic TTL checks on residency proofs.
Priya (author): Added monotonic TTL validation and a clock-drift tolerance flag (configurable by region) in the latest patch.
Lena Ortiz: Audit envelope needs to be searchable for compliance queries. Can we keep an indexed minimal fingerprint?
Priya (author): We add a canonical fingerprint (sha256) to the envelope metadata and index it in the compliance table; value is non-PII.
Arjun Patel: How does this affect Dedicated customers using external KMS providers?
Priya (author): ORP supports a KMS-provider adapter interface; we ship adapters for AWS and GCP. For external KMS we fall back to a blinded-assertor path that records provider provenance without exporting raw keys.
Evan Park: CI flaked once on the wasm build, re-run passed.
Lena Ortiz: Approve after a small doc tweak.

Motivation: Continuous-batcher suffers occasional tail spikes when small numbers of late-arriving requests repeatedly preempt in-flight coalesced batches or re-acquire hot KV cache pins, causing starvation of other lanes. This PR introduces a late-arrival debouncer and a timebound arbiter to smooth admission decisions and a soft-lease decay for slot leases to reduce repeated re-grabs. Goals: (1) reduce 95/99p tail latency under mixed arrival jitter without losing throughput, (2) avoid KV cache pin churn on micro-hot keys, (3) preserve fairness across priority lanes with a small bounded added latency for highly-jittered arrivals. Summary of changes: - scheduler/arbiter: add TimeboundArbiter which assigns a short, configurable admission window (debounce_window_ms) per batch slot; late arrivals that fall inside the window are coalesced rather than treated as fresh high-priority arrivals. - scheduler/leases: implement soft-lease-decay that reduces the effective priority of repeated immediate lease re-acquisitions by the same client for a short cooldown period, implemented as a probabilistic decay counter so behavior is smooth across scale. - kvcache: introduce shadow-pin accounting to detect churny keys; shadow pins don't block eviction immediately but track touch frequency to recommend prefetch/repin thresholds to the allocator. - batching heuristics: arrival-jitter-dampener which adds small, randomized jitter to waiting agents to avoid pathological synchrony. - metrics: new metrics (debounce.window_hits, soft_lease.decays, kv.shadow_pin_rate) and dashboards for per-queue hit/miss and fairness indices. - tests: added deterministic unit tests for debouncer logic and an integration benchmark harness that simulates mixed jitter workloads. Backwards compatibility and config: all features default to off/opt-in via runtime flags and rollout config; conservative defaults enabled for internal perf canaries. Perf results (canary): local perf lab with mixed microburst + jitter workload: 95p latency reduced by ~9% and 99p by ~14% on p50 routing; throughput unchanged within 0.5%. On a KV-heavy churn scenario (hot key fanout), observed ~30% reduction in shadow pin churn and a 7% reduction in token cost due to fewer cache repins. Checklist: - [x] Design doc + benchmark plan in ENG ticket ENG-7482 - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Canary run against perf-lab - [x] Dashboard panels added - [x] Feature flag and rollout plan included Risk notes: soft-lease-decay may slightly increase latency for repeated short requests from same client; exposed via feature flag and gated behind rollout. Rollout plan: enable for internal canary pool -> expand to Dedicated regions with telemetry -> full rollout once fairness index stable for 48h. References: ENG-7482, ENG-7520, related PRs on queue fairness and lease reclaiming.
Diego Ramos: Nice focused change. Concern: how does the TimeboundArbiter interact with existing lane preemption rules? Please add unit tests covering a high-priority request arriving mid-window.
Maya Patel (author): Added targeted unit test 'TestArbiter_PreemptDuringWindow' and documented preemption override rules in docs; arbiter yields to critical lanes if explicit override flag is set.
Anika Singh: The soft-lease-decay logic looks probabilistic; can we make the decay parameters observable (counters/histogram) so SRE can tune without code changes?
Maya Patel: Exposed counters soft_lease.decays and a decay_attempts histogram; added dashboard tile and instructions for tuning via rollout config.
Liam O'Connor: Integration test shows one flaky where debounce window boundary is off by 1ms on some runners. Can we tolerate +-2ms?
Maya Patel: Relaxed boundary checks in TestArbiter_TimingEdge and added jitter in test harness to avoid machine-clock artifacts. Verified in CI.
SRE Bot: Perf canary results uploaded to infra/perf-canaries/late-arrival-debouncer/ (thresholds met).
Introduce TimeboundArbiter (late-arrival debouncing), soft-lease-decay to reduce repeated lease re-acquisitions, and shadow-pin tracking to mitigate KV cache churn. Config flags provided for staged rollout. Expected benefit: lower 95/99p latencies under arrival jitter and reduced KV repin costs.

Hotfix: Stabilizes tenant graceful unplug flow and prevents spurious regional circuit tripping under short maintenance windows. Backported to v2026.02-release.
Motivation: production incidents in the past 48 hours revealed two correlated failure modes during tenant unplug (customer-initiated detach and scheduled maintenance): 1) abrupt KV cache eviction left in-flight requests failing with 503s; 2) regional circuit state machines could flip to OPEN due to transient health probe flaps and then remain sticky, causing cascading regional failover and load oscillation. This PR provides a minimal, low-risk hotfix that introduces a ’graceful shepherd’ flow for tenant unplug and hardens the circuit state transition logic to tolerate transient probe failures. Summary of changes: - Introduces a tenant-unplug coordinator that drains inflight shared KV cache sessions and transitions tenant routing into a ’soft-standby’ window (configurable ttl) before full detach. This avoids dropping requests and allows in-progress batches to complete. - Adds a transient-probe debounce layer and bounded reopen backoff to the regional circuit breaker so a sequence of short probe failures does not permanently open circuits. - Adds explicit telemetry and audit events for unplug start/finish and for circuit soft-deny transitions to aid post-incident analysis. Rollout strategy: - Deploy as a hotfix to main, then staggered rollout to release branches: v2026.02-release and v2025.12-legacy. - Feature gate for graceful-shepherd enabled by default for dedicated and private customers; can be toggled per-customer via tenant flags for additional vetting. Testing and validation: - Unit tests for coordinator state transitions (drain -> soft-standby -> detached) and for circuit debounce paths. - Integration test harness simulating concurrent request streams during unplug; validated no 5xx spike in local perf lab. - Canary deployment to a subset of regions (us-west-2 then eu-west-1) with streaming telemetry checks and automatic rollback on error-rate delta > +1.5% over baseline. Backport and urgency: This is a hotfix tied to customer-impacting incidents (SUP-4312). Targeted for immediate merge and backport. Risk: Low-medium. Changes are conservative, mostly additive control logic and feature-guarded. KV drain uses existing eviction APIs and respects current SLO prioritization. Notes: This PR is intentionally small and focused to minimize blast radius; follow-up PRs will (a) add a formal visibility page in Console and (b) provide an admin tool to trigger manual shepherd windows. References: Linear ENG-1952, incident notes SUP-4312.
Carlos Ramirez: Left a request for clarification on drain timeout semantics — why 60s vs 30s?
Nina Patel: Reply: 60s chosen after local lab runs with 99th perc request completion ~38s under heavy batch; documented as configurable via tenant flag. Will add note to runbook.
Eve Singh: Integration tests look good but canary config needs explicit rollback threshold; suggested adding automated rollback to the canary manifests.
Nina Patel: Added automated rollback in deploy manifests and re-ran canary smoke. CI showed transient lint failure which I fixed.
Jordan Blake: Approved after one nit on log message formatting; non-blocking.
SRE-bot: CI rerun requested due to flaky integration test; all checks green on rerun.

- Internal: emit lightweight counters for streaming disconnects and partial tool-call args to make example smoke tests regression-resistant.
- No API behavior changes; metrics are additive and behind the existing metrics export.
Context: The examples refresh work (ENG-4821/4822) is adding golden transcripts + smoke tests that exercise streaming, tool calling, and structured output. We’ve had a few regressions slip through because the test harness could only assert on final text (or brittle event ordering) and didn’t have a stable signal when certain edge cases occurred (disconnect mid-stream, partial tool args emitted across multiple chunks, etc.). This PR adds a small set of counters in the API gateway streaming path and tool-call assembly code so smoke tests can assert “did we observe the expected condition?” without coupling to internal event serialization.

What’s included: (1) New Prometheus counters (namespaced under redwood_api_*) emitted from the streaming SSE/WebSocket handlers and tool-call delta assembler: redwood_api_stream_disconnect_total{reason}, redwood_api_stream_reconnect_total{success}, redwood_api_tool_call_partial_args_total{tool_name}, redwood_api_stream_parse_error_total{stage}, redwood_api_stream_final_message_assembled_total{mode}. (2) A tiny test-only “metrics snapshot” helper used by the examples smoke tests to read counter deltas between test phases (no dependency on internal tracing; works in local + CI). (3) Documentation in the smoke test README on how to interpret these metrics when debugging flakes.

Design notes / constraints: Metrics are intentionally low-cardinality. tool_name is capped to a short allowlist in the example runner (unknown tools bucket to tool_name="other"). We only increment tool_call_partial_args when we see arguments delivered over >1 delta chunk for a single call_id (this directly targets SUP-18421 confusion). The disconnect counter is best-effort and increments on any transport close before the terminal event is emitted; it should not be used as a billing/usage signal.

Testing: Added unit tests around the delta assembler to ensure partial-args detection increments once per call_id. Added integration coverage in the example smoke test harness to assert counters change as expected during a forced disconnect/retry scenario. Ran existing gateway tests + examples suite.

Impact: No user-facing API changes. Adds a few counters to the existing metrics endpoint. Helps catch regressions earlier (especially around the known pitfalls section in the refreshed docs).
Ibrahim Khan: Can we keep label cardinality low? tool_name could explode if customers define arbitrary tools.
Sahana Iyer (author): Yep — tool_name label is only used by the examples runner. In gateway/runtime we only emit tool_name for known example tools; everything else buckets to "other". Added a note + guard in the helper.
Brian Murphy: For stream_disconnect, do we risk double-counting when the client cancels after completion but before we flush the terminal event?
Sahana Iyer (author): Good call. I changed the increment to only happen when we have not emitted terminal_event=true for that request context. Added a unit test for “graceful finish then close” to ensure no increment.
Sabrina James: Smoke test expectation: should we assert exact counts or just >0? Concerned about retries changing counts.
Sahana Iyer (author): Updated the smoke tests to assert minimum deltas (>=1) for disconnect/reconnect and exact-once for partial_args per call_id. That should be stable even with additional retries.
Connor O'Brien: Any rollout concerns for metrics dashboards/alerts?
Sahana Iyer (author): No alerts added. These are purely counters; we can decide later if SRE wants alerting. Documented them under “example validation metrics” only.

Context: Production customers observed increased tail latency for short tool/function-calling requests when the gateway was co-located with large batched generation workloads. This PR updates routing and proxy buffer policies so small payload, low-token-rate requests (typical in fncall workflows) are prioritized onto low-latency routes and are protected from head-of-line blocking.

What I changed: - Added a route-priority rule that scores requests by (payload_bytes, expected_stream_rate, route_health) and prefers nodes with low existing KV-cache pressure. - Introduced a soft payload limit (route-specific soft_limit_bytes) enforced at the gateway with a backoff policy; requests exceeding the soft limit get a 413-soft response header suggesting chunking, and are forwarded to larger-capacity routes instead of being dropped. - Streaming proxy: replaced fixed 256KB per-client in-memory buffer with an adaptive low-water/high-water window that keeps at most 32KB of eager buffer for low-rate streams and allows opportunistic burst buffering for large streams up to route hard limit. This reduces memory pressure and reduces blocking of small fncall streams. - Fncall/OpenAI-compat handshake: tightened the initial stream-framing timeout to 7s (was 15s) with an opt-out flag for customers on high-latency links. This prevents stuck handshakes from tying up proxy resources. - Added compatibility shim so OpenAI-compatible requests that use structured toolcall semantics get routed to nodes with structured-output validators enabled. - Instrumentation: added metrics (gateway.small_payload_route_hit, streaming.buffer_window_ms, stream.handshake_timeouts) and dashboards, plus an alert on small_payload_route_miss_rate > 2%.

Why: Fixes multiple customer incidents where quick tool calls experienced 3-10x higher p95 latency under mixed workloads. The new behavior preserves OpenAI-compatible surface semantics while improving median and tail latency for short synchronous tool calls.

Rollout: Feature guarded behind gateway feature-flag (gate.priority_small_payloads). Default off for dedicated/private until validated. Gradual rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% in hosted over 72 hours with monitoring gating.

Notes: This is focused on surface-level routing and proxy buffer behavior only; no model-serving runtime changes.
Ava Liu: Can you add a guard so this doesn't trigger for private deployments by default? (requested change)
Author (Priya Menon): Added feature flag and updated docs to mark default off for private/dedicated. PTAL.
Diego Martinez: The new handshake timeout seems aggressive; can we make it configurable per-region? (requested change)
Author: Made timeout configurable via route_schema.yaml with per-region override and added integration test for handshake opt-out flag.
Sasha Ivanov: Approve. Verified metrics and dashboard look reasonable in staging.
Ava Liu: Approve after flag and docs update.

Summary: Reduce developer CI image size and presubmit runtime by replacing monolithic dev toolchains with a slim multi-stage container and introduce an idempotent release hook runner that guarantees once-only execution for release automation. Motivation: Presubmit builds have grown slow due to heavy container layers and duplicated toolchain installs; release automation occasionally triggered duplicate hooks in edge cases (race on tag creation and webhook retries). Goals: (1) Provide a hermetic slim Dockerfile with explicit bootstrap and a light runtime image for tests so local dev + CI reuse layers; (2) Move expensive setup steps to a cacheable build-stage and use a small runtime image for presubmit; (3) Implement an idempotent release hook runner (go) that persists run-state to the control-plane API and retries safely; (4) Add a shallow preflight dry-run gate to the release workflow to catch common failures earlier. Changes: Added tools/ci/docker/Dockerfile.slim and tools/ci/docker/entrypoint-slim.sh; refactored .github/workflows/presubmit.yml to use the slim image and to parallelize lint/unit shards; created ci/release-hooks/runner.go and ci/release-hooks/README.md describing the idempotency model; updated scripts/release/preflight.sh to perform a lightweight checksum and tag-existence probe before invoking hooks; bumped action versions for setup-go and actions/cache to reduce transitive deps; added a small integration test harness ci/harness/test_release_hooks.sh that simulates webhook retries. Testing: local build of slim image (image size reduced by ~420MB), CI presubmit matrix runtime reduced 22% on average in smoke buckets, end-to-end simulation for release hooks validated against retries and network blips. Deploy: rollout is safe-by-default; feature flag ci.slots.release_hook_idempotency = on for 48 hours, followed by gradual enable. Notes: This PR intentionally avoids touching the main runtime images used for Dedicated; it only optimizes CI/dev toolchains and release hook runner behavior.
Liam Patel: Nice reduction in image size. Two asks: 1) can we limit the slim image to only what presubmit needs (node + go runtime?) 2) decrease default hook retry backoff to 30s with jitter so release waits aren't excessive. (commented inline on runner.go)
Maya Chen (author): Addressed both; split out node runtime and moved go toolchain to build-stage; reduced backoff and added jitter. Added comment in runner.go explaining the backoff rationale.
Nora Singh: Tests look good. Small nit: preflight.sh should exit non-zero on non-HTTP-200 from tag-probe to be clearer. Also prefer using the existing control-plane client lib instead of raw curl for the probe if available.
Maya Chen (author): Switched to control-plane client lib for tag probe and updated exit codes. Added unit tests for probe failure cases.
Aaron Gold: Approved after verifying the presubmit runtime numbers in the smoke bucket and confirming there are no increased flakes in the nightly job. (APPROVED)
Continuous Integration: initial presubmit run failed lint in runner.go (unused var). Author pushed fix, reran checks.
Maya Chen: pushed g0d12ef fixing lint and adding small docs for ops to flip the feature flag.
- Introduced a slim CI toolchain image to reduce presubmit runtime and developer image bloat; average presubmit time reduced ~22% in smoke tests. - Added an idempotent release-hook runner to prevent duplicate hook executions on webhook retries or racey tag events; safe-by-default behind a 48-hour feature flag. - Bumped several GitHub Actions to newer minor versions to reduce transitive dependencies and speed up setup.

Motivation: debugging the fat-tail of token-latency has been time-consuming because sampled traces miss the small subset of invocations that exercise rarely-hit kernel paths (prefetch contention, KV cache cold misses, and model quantization fallbacks). This PR introduces a prioritized "hotpath" sampler that boosts sampling probability for invocations that exhibit early indicators of tail behavior and an annotated log-joiner that attaches compact enrichment metadata to traces for faster root-cause grouping. Design summary: (1) Hotpath sampler lives in telemetry/samplers and runs a lightweight rule engine over request metadata and early model-stage signals (kernel-time-estimates, kv_cache_miss_hint, prefix-shape). Sampling is priority-weighted by a configurable score; weights resolve deterministically to keep sampling stable across retries. (2) Annotated log-joiner is a small service/agent that performs signal extraction from structured logs and attaches 128-bit stable anchors to traces (implemented as polyglot library with Go+Python bindings). Anchors allow compact joins in the observability backend without shipping full logs. (3) Rollout plan: feature flag gate feature.hotpath_sampler, canary 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with dashboard and alert quieting during ramp. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for score heuristics - [x] integration tests with trace backend - [x] dashboard & alerts - [x] e2e throughput bench in perf-lab - [x] docs and config example Files changed: telemetry/samplers/hotpath_sampler.go, pkg/logjoiner/annotated_joiner.py, observability/dashboards/hotpath-sampler-dashboard.json, console/alerts/hotpath-tail-slo.yaml, telemetry/README.md, test/integration/hotpath_sampler_test.go, scripts/ramp_hotpath_flag.sh, deploy/featureflags/hotpath.yaml. Impact and safety: scoring is conservative by default (base-sample-rate left unchanged) and only increases sampling probability for invocations with score > 0.4; the service is rate-limited and uses reservoir caps to ensure observability ingestion cost stays bounded. Migration notes: ops can opt to emit anchors as trace attributes or as log metadata; we added a toggle in telemetry/README.md. Backwards compatibility: no breaking API changes; the annotated joiner provides a compatibility shim for backends that don't consume anchors. Monitoring: added a hotpath-sampler dashboard (per-model share, score distribution, sampled vs unsampled ratio), a compact anchor-sparsity panel, and an alert hotpath-tail-slo which is cohort-aware and will auto-suppress for low-volume tenants. Ops runbook included in telemetry/README.md. CI: flaky integration test flaked once and was re-run in CI; final status PASS. Merge: squash-merged after approvals and CI green.
Miguel Santos (review): please make the scoring function deterministic across restarts; otherwise sampling weight changes will bias comparisons. Author: switched to a stable seed derived from tenant+route hash.
Priya Desai (request changes): need a cap on daily sampling cost per-tenant. Author: added reservoir cap and a config knob per tenant in deploy/featureflags/hotpath.yaml.
Liam O'Connor (approval): code/lgtm, dashboard panels are helpful; recommend we add a collapsed timeline view for anchor joins in a follow-up.
CI Bot: integration test suite flaky: TestHotpathSamplerScore; rerun resolved the transient GPU kernel timing dependency.
Introduces a prioritized hotpath sampler to increase trace coverage of tail invocations and an annotated log-joiner to attach compact anchors for fast trace-log joins. Includes dashboards and cohort-aware alert tuning. Feature gated and opt-in by default.
This PR complements existing tail-sampling work but targets early indicators and introduces compact anchors to reduce storage and join cost; follow-up PR will add a small UI in Console to inspect anchor joins.

Context & motivation: We need a safer way to perform short-lived handoffs between model revisions during canary/AB workflows and shadow-to-active promotions where session affinity and transient state can complicate rollback. Current promote/drain paths can lose causal information required to deterministically revert or replay traffic for forensics. This PR implements an ephemeral handoff controller that attaches a minimal "scribe" (compacted event sketch) to promotions; the scribe captures revision boundaries, cohort assignment, and key telemetry anchors to drive deterministic rollback and accelerated replay.
Introduces a revision-aware ephemeral handoff controller that records a compact rollback scribe for deterministic revert and replay; adds supporting telemetry and a runbook. Backward compatible with existing rollout policies.

1d3c2e5 - telemetry: add scribe proto + compact serializer and producer to rollout pipeline
2b7e9d0 - console: visualize handoff timelines and expose scribe download on rollout detail
3c9a1f2 - charts: optional helm flag rollout.ephemeralHandoff.enabled = true
4f6b2c9 - tests: integration and unit tests for deterministic revert and replay
5a8b0e1 - docs: runbook and operator playbook for scribe-based rollback
Claire Ng: Great overall design. Two questions: 1) How does the scribe size behave under high QPS? 2) Are there any privacy/PII risks when recording cohort keys?
Author (Asha): Scribe is a compact sketch (HyperLogLog-like summary) limited to 1KB by default; full payloads are not captured. Cohort keys are hashed and salted per-customer; docs updated with privacy notes.
Diego Morales: Request change - add a circuit-breaker that stops scribe emission if latency impacted (seen in perf smoke).
Author (Asha): Added backpressure + rate-limiter to scribe emitter (new commit 3c9a1f2) and perf tests. See integration test for latency guard.
Samir Kapoor: Minor nit - helm flag naming inconsistent with other controllers. Suggest rollout.ephemeralHandoff.enabled -> rollout.ephemeralHandoff.enabled (kept for parity).
Author (Asha): Kept the flag to match existing convention; added comment in values.yaml to clarify.
Claire Ng: Approved after code changes and documentation updates. Diego approved on second pass.
Unit + integration coverage added for state transitions and deterministic revert; synthetic e2e validated canary->promote->replay path with session-affine traffic and verified fidelity within 0.4% of baseline. Load test included 10K RPS ephemeral handoffs with scribe rate-limited and no user-visible latency regression after backpressure enabled.
Feature is behind helm flag rollout.ephemeralHandoff.enabled=false by default. Initial rollout: enable on non-prod clusters for 48h, enable on a small cohort (1% traffic) in staging for 24h with smoke checks, then enable for selective customers under dedicated capacity. If metrics breach: auto-backout policy triggers (see runbook) and scribe provides deterministic replay to reproduce issue.
New metrics: rollout.scribe.emitted_count, rollout.scribe.overlimit, rollout.handoff.latency_p99. Alerts added: ScribeErrorRate > 0.1% for 5m, HandoffLatencyP99 > 200ms for 3m. Dashboards added to Console rollout detail + service-level tracing linked.
No DB schema migrations. Controller persists lightweight markers in existing rollout ledger; it is backward compatible with older controllers (they will ignore scribe blobs). Operators should ensure helm values are synchronized across clusters before enabling.
Added docs/runbooks/rollback-scribe.md with operator playbook, example curl commands to download scribe artifacts, and forensic replay steps. Console changes expose a 'Download scribe' button on rollout details.
Scribe payloads are compact, hashed, and stored with customer scoping. Added KMS encryption at rest for scribe artifacts when stored beyond retention window. Privacy review completed and documented in docs/privacy/rollout-telemetry.md.
If a promotion causes regression: 1) Use Console to 'Pause rollout' (holdpoint). 2) Download scribe and run replay tool (scripts/replay/replay_from_scribe.py) in dry-run mode. 3) If replay reproduces issue, execute 'rollback via scribe' which replays traffic against previous revision and automates swap. Follow runbook steps to notify customer success for affected cohorts.
This PR aims to improve determinism for fast promotes and automated rollbacks. It does not change existing routing or session affinity semantics. Future work: expose scribe-based automated bisect tooling and long-term archival options.
Added EphemeralHandoffController, scribe serializer/emitter, Console visualization, helm toggle, integration tests, and operator runbook.

Motivation: Multiple customers and internal workloads observed intermittent auth races during credential rotation under high-throughput streaming workloads. Existing SDKs used slightly different fallback behaviors which made incident diagnosis hard and caused subtle resume failures during token swap. This PR introduces a unified "credential fallback mosaic" -- a small, deterministic chain that attempts delegated token fetch -> cached lease -> orchestrated refresh -> ephemeral token from local agent. It also adds a minimal StreamProgress adapter (emit progress events and checkpoints) to make streaming ergonomics consistent across Python/TS/Go. Implementation notes: - Core credential chain implemented in redwood-core/sdk-common/cred/mosaic.go (Go canonical implementation) and mirrored with idiomatic facades in redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript. - StreamProgress adapter added as a thin cross-language surface: progress events are simple JSON envelopes emitted on stream frames (progress, checkpoint, final). Each SDK exposes a small listener callback / async iterator helper to consume these without changing the primary chunking API. - Backoff/retry alignment: introduced a RetryProfile named "streaming-foreground" tuned for low-latency short-circuits and weaker exponential floors to avoid excessive token churn. - Version bumps: python -> 0.27.3, typescript -> 1.9.0, go -> 1.5.2. Compatibility and opt-in: Default behaviour is backward compatible. The mosaic is enabled by default for new clients but preserves previous token lookup order when a legacy config flag (legacyCredOrder=true) is set. StreamProgress is opt-in via a client option (enable_stream_progress=true) to avoid spamming existing applications. Testing: - Unit tests: 86 new unit tests across the three SDKs exercising token failover and progress envelope parsing. - Integration: added a smoke matrix that runs on CI against a staging auth proxy to validate rotation handoffs and stream resume scenarios. - Load canary: a small canary run against Dedicated in us-west-2 with synthetic streams sustained for 4 hours (no auth races observed). Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature gate; 2) Deploy SDK releases to package registries; 3) Canary opt-in with internal repo owners and a handful of early enterprise customers; 4) Full rollout after 2 weeks observation. See linked Linear ENG-981 and ENG-1050 for rollout checklists and postmortem references.
Adds multi-SDK credential fallback chain and a lightweight stream progress adapter; bumps Python/TS/Go SDK versions. Backwards compatible: default behaviour unchanged unless opt-in. Recommended for early rollout to Dedicated/private customers before wide release.

Motivation: different SDK teams have drifted in retry configuration semantics and telemetry emission. This causes operational surprises when services switch SDKs or when a single app uses multiple SDKs.

What this PR does (high level): introduce an atomic RetryPolicyRegistry in the platform core and provide lightweight, shimless adapters in Python/TS/Go SDKs that read and apply policies consistently. Telemetry hooks are standardized so a single retry decision across languages emits the same metric tags. The registry supports composition (e.g., default + tenant overrides) and deterministic precedence; policies are immutable once installed to avoid races.

Checklist: - [x] Core retry registry implementation (platform/runtime) - [x] Python adapter and tests - [x] TypeScript adapter and tests - [x] Go adapter and tests - [x] End-to-end CI matrix (py/ts/go) - [x] Docs and changelog entry - [x] Telemetry tag parity verified

Compatibility notes: default behavior is unchanged for existing consumers. New behavior (policy composition and atomic installs) is behind an opt-in flag in each SDK (enable_atomic_retry_registry = true). The registry API is intentionally small: register_policy(id, spec), get_policy(id), install_atomic_batch(list_of_policies).

Dev notes: see inline code snippets below for the minimal adapter surface used by each SDK. The adapters are intentionally thin—no language-side reimplementation of decision logic—so most of the logic lives in the registry (platform).

References: Linear ENG-2145 (retry harmonization), internal doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2145/retry-harmonization, previous PRs touching retry RFCs: #214007, #110010.

Adds a centralized, atomic retry policy registry and cross-language shims to improve parity between Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Backwards-compatible defaults preserved; opt-in for advanced policy composition. Includes documentation and test coverage across SDKs.
Diego Morales (review): This is a big win for parity. Two asks: 1) ensure the immutability contract is enforced across concurrent installs (we should avoid a window where half-installed batches are visible). 2) add a defensive TTL on registry cache entries in SDKs so a long-closed connection doesn't hold stale policy forever.
Anika Shah (author): Implemented atomic batch installs with a version token returned by install_atomic_batch; SDKs must fetch policy by version to avoid seeing partially-installed batches. Added optional TTL param in SDK adapters; default is 24h. See commits b3e4c7a and f4b8a66.
Liam Chen (review): Code + tests look good. Minor: in the TypeScript client please avoid Promise<any> in the public surface — prefer well-typed PolicySpec.
Anika Shah: Addressed typing in TS (policySpec typed in registryClient.ts). Expanded unit tests to cover typed round-trip. See commit d9f2c11.
Anika Shah: Added integration test for concurrent installs (tests/interop/test_retry_policy_matrix.py) and CI matrix entry to run it across py/ts/go.
Anika Shah: Left migration guidance in docs/sdk/retry.md showing how to opt-in and roll back safely.
payload.title: Introduce atomic retry policy registry and shimless cross-SDK interoperability

Context and motivation: customer teams reported a set of interrelated SDK ergonomics problems when long-running streams encounter credential rotations and transient infra errors: (1) duplicate reauth attempts from parallel consumers, (2) inconsistent cursor/resume behavior between Python/TS/Go, and (3) differing retry presets that made service-level parity testing brittle. This PR introduces a small cross-SDK surface called the 'credential concierge' (a thin, opinionated orchestrator for credential lookups + telemetry) plus a compact stream facade that normalizes resume semantics and reduces boilerplate for application code. Work completed: - Implement credential concierge in each SDK (Python/TS/Go) with a consistent public API and pluggable provider chain. - Add adaptive retry profiles (idle-window, short-burst, long-tail) and ensure the same defaults across SDKs. - Replace low-level stream consumer helpers with a compact pull-stream facade that exposes a stable async iterator/async generator contract and a lightweight resume token. - Fix edge-case race where token refresh and stream reconnect could cause duplicate request bodies to be replayed. - Add end-to-end parity tests (matrix py/ts/go) and update docs + changelogs. Checklist: [x] API design doc reviewed (ENG-4521) [x] All unit + e2e tests added [x] Docs updated and sample snippets included [x] Version bumps applied to packaging and changelogs Notes: description intentionally concise; implementation keeps runtime allocations minimal and avoids cross-process state.
Adds a lightweight 'credential concierge' abstraction that centralizes credential lookup/fallback and telemetry across SDKs; introduces a compact, ergonomic stream facade (pull-stream friendly) with improved resume semantics; fixes cross-language parity issues around stream cursor iteration and token-refresh races; bumps Python/TS/Go SDK minor versions.
Evan Li: Overall looks good. Two asks: add a short timeout for concierge lookups to prevent blocking in sync clients, and please add a note about observability keys emitted.
Maya Thompson: Added timeouts to the concierge client and emitted 'concierge.lookup' span attributes. PTAL.
Priya Desai: TS lint flagged an unused import in compactFacade; also the iterator close path needs to ensure KV cache is released.
Maya Thompson: Fixed tslint import, added explicit close() on facade and ensured KV cache release in all codepaths. Added unit that simulates abrupt consumer cancel.
Carlos Mendez: Tests look good. One behavior question: when the concierge falls back to the local provider, do we still emit the same telemetry? We should mark source=local in the event.
Maya Thompson: Good catch — added 'credential.source' tag (local|remote|fallback) to telemetry and updated docs.
Priya Desai: CI flake on e2e matrix previously; re-run passes now. Approving pending squash commit message clean-up.
Evan Li: Approve. Recommend mention in release notes about migration steps for advanced custom credential providers.
