payload.body:
Context
We have a repeated hang/timeout signature in TP replicas under sustained mixed prefill/decode load where collectives become ready but never get scheduled promptly because the scheduler keeps selecting prefill-heavy work that maximizes token throughput. When one rank gets delayed on a collective boundary while others enter the collective path, NCCL ordering diverges and we end up in a silent stall (or downstream request timeouts).

This PR adds a narrow scheduler guardrail: when a TP group has collective-ready work pending beyond a bounded window, we temporarily bias scheduling decisions to ensure the collective boundary is reached and executed across ranks. The goal is correctness/stability first, with minimal perf impact.

What changed (high level)
- Introduce the concept of "collective-ready" work items in the runtime scheduler for TP replicas.
- Track a per-TP-group "collective_ready_age_ms" and "collective_ready_depth" (how many steps are waiting at a collective boundary).
- Add a fairness rule: if collective_ready_age_ms exceeds a threshold OR collective_ready_depth exceeds a small limit, we throttle selecting additional prefill-heavy batches and instead drain collective-ready items until the TP group is back in a healthy state.
- Ensure the policy is deterministic across ranks by basing the decision on rank-0 broadcast state (same inputs => same ordering decisions).
- Add metrics + structured logs to make this visible in production and in repro harnesses.

Why this is safe
- The guardrail is behind a feature flag: `runtime.scheduler.tp_collective_fairness_guardrail`.
- Default behavior remains unchanged unless enabled.
- The policy only activates when we are already in a high-risk state (collective-ready work aging / queueing).

Implementation details
- New scheduler hook `TpCollectiveFairnessController` evaluates TP group health on each tick.
- Added a bounded "prefill_budget" when fairness is active. Prefill work can still proceed, but it cannot indefinitely starve collective-ready work.
- Added a deterministic state propagation: rank 0 computes `fairness_mode` and the current budget, then shares it as part of the TP control-plane message. Non-zero ranks treat the state as authoritative.
- Added a small jitter tolerance to avoid flapping when workloads hover around the threshold.

Perf comparison (benchmark-lab)
Environment
- HW: A100 80GB, TP=4, 1 replica unless specified
- Models: 70B-class decoder-only (internal build; see benchmark sheet link in ENG-4824)
- Workload: mixed prefill/decode with long tail prompt lengths, streaming enabled

Key results (median of 5 runs; higher is better for throughput, lower is better for latency)
1) Mixed workload (prefill-heavy, high concurrency)
- Baseline (flag off): p50 65 ms/token, p99 310 ms/token, throughput 1.00x, hang repro rate 2/5 runs
- Guardrail (flag on): p50 67 ms/token (+3.1%), p99 235 ms/token (-24.2%), throughput 0.98x (-2.0%), hang repro rate 0/5 runs

2) Decode-biased workload (short prompts, steady decode)
- Baseline: throughput 1.00x, p99 stable
- Guardrail: throughput 1.00x (no measurable change), fairness activation ~0 (as expected)

3) Worst-case long-context bursts (burst concurrency + long prompts)
- Baseline: occasional large p99 spikes and one stall in 3 runs
- Guardrail: p99 spikes reduced; no stalls in 3 runs; fairness activation correlated with burst windows

Notes:
- The p50 regression is expected when the guardrail activates because we stop greedily stuffing prefill. Given the stability gain and p99 improvement, this tradeoff is acceptable for Dedicated canary. We can tune thresholds per model/hardware after we have more production data.

Metrics added
- `runtime_scheduler_tp_collective_ready_age_ms{tp_group_id,model,cluster}` (histogram)
- `runtime_scheduler_tp_fairness_mode_active{tp_group_id}` (gauge)
- `runtime_scheduler_tp_prefill_throttle_total{reason}` (counter; reason = collective_age|collective_depth)
- Log: `tp_fairness_decision` structured event (includes budgets and queue summary; sampled)

Testing
- Unit tests for fairness controller state machine and determinism across ranks.
- Integration test using the TP hang repro harness config (ENG-4822) updated to assert fairness-mode triggers and that the scheduler drains collective-ready items within bounded time.

Rollout plan
- Land behind feature flag (this PR).
- Enable in perf-canary TP stress scenarios once ENG-4828 thresholds are updated.
- Dedicated-first canary for affected accounts (see PM-911 + SUP-48344) before broad Hosted enablement.

Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Make thresholds dynamic based on observed seq length distribution (could reduce p50 impact).
- Add a "stall reason" correlation in tracing spans (ENG-4823 / PR-21872).

Refs
- Linear: ENG-4824 (scheduler ordering/fairness), ENG-4821 (initiative)
- Support: SUP-48344 (streaming timeouts during peak load), SUP-48321 (Dedicated A100 hangs)
- Related PRs: PR-21834 (heartbeat metrics), PR-21853 (NCCL stream sync hardening)

Checklist
- [x] Feature-flagged
- [x] Metrics added + documented in code comments
- [x] Unit + integration coverage
- [x] Benchmark results attached in ENG-4824
- [x] Rollback: disable flag (no migration)

Signed-off-by: Lena Fischer
- Reduces probability of TP hangs/timeouts in mixed prefill/decode by preventing collective work from being starved by large prefill batches.
- Adds scheduler metrics for collective-ready age and fairness throttle activations.
- No API changes; rollout behind feature flag `runtime.scheduler.tp_collective_fairness_guardrail` (default off).
Sofia Ivanova (review): The intent makes sense. Two concerns: (1) determinism across ranks—can you confirm non-rank0 doesn’t independently flip fairness_mode based on local queue state? (2) The threshold values feel aggressive; can we make them config-driven and start conservative?
Lena Fischer (author): (1) Non-rank0 treats the rank0 fairness_mode + budget as authoritative. Local queue signals are still computed for metrics, but not used for decisions. Added a comment + assertion in `ApplyFairnessStateFromRank0()` to make this explicit. (2) Thresholds are now config-driven under the flag: `collective_ready_age_ms` and `collective_ready_depth`. Defaults match what’s in the repro harness; we can tune per model in canary.
Noah Patel (review): I like that this stays surgical. Request: add a guard to avoid flapping when hovering around the boundary, and please include the fairness decision in the structured event so we can correlate to stalls. Also: any risk that we starve prefill too hard and hurt throughput for small prompt bursts?
Lena Fischer (author): Added hysteresis: once fairness activates it stays on for `min_active_ms` and deactivates only after age/depth are below thresholds for `cooldown_ms`. Structured event now includes: mode, budget, age_ms, depth, and selected queue id. Re throughput: prefill isn’t blocked, it’s budgeted. In my decode-biased runs it never triggers; in prefill-heavy it triggers only when age/depth grows, and throughput drop was ~2%.
Rafael Mendes (review): From SRE perspective: can we ensure the new metrics are cheap and labeled sanely? Please avoid tp_group_id cardinality explosion in Hosted.
Lena Fischer (author): Good catch. I changed tp_group_id to a low-cardinality `tp_group_hash` (stable per replica lifetime) and added a separate `replica_id` only in sampled logs. Metrics keep model/cluster and do not include request ids.
Julian Moore (review): The integration test looks good, but it’s currently asserting exact ordering in one step which may be brittle. Can we assert bounded drain and fairness activation count instead of exact sequence?
Lena Fischer (author): Updated test: asserts fairness mode activates at least once under the workload, and that `collective_ready_age_ms` does not exceed 2x threshold for more than N ticks. Removed strict ordering assertions.
Marcus Reed (review): Can you attach perf numbers in the PR too (not just Linear)? Also add a note about potential p50 regression when fairness activates so release managers aren’t surprised.
Lena Fischer (author): Added a perf section in the description with p50/p99/throughput deltas and notes on expected tradeoff. Also added release notes entry.
Sofia Ivanova (approval): Looks good with the determinism + hysteresis changes. Approved.
Noah Patel (approval): Approved. Let’s keep the flag default-off until we have canary data.
Rafael Mendes (approval): Approved with the label-cardinality fix. Please coordinate enablement via ENG-4829.
Connor O'Brien to coordinate flag enablement for Dedicated canary as part of ENG-4829. Aisha Bello to add alerts after the dashboard PR lands (observability-pack PR-412).
payload.title: Scheduler: guardrail to prevent TP collective starvation under prefill-heavy load

Context: Customers saw ephemeral post-swap latency spikes when a new model warmed up under real traffic. Motivation: provide a deterministic, observable, and reversible policy that smooths traffic shifts (the "traffic thermostat") and schedules a planned failback window if quality regressions are detected. Goals: 1) Avoid large instantaneous traffic jumps that overload caches/GPUs; 2) Provide a scheduled, auditable failback plan with automatic graceful rollback that preserves session-affinity; 3) Integrate with existing shadow-replay plumbing so we can validate candidate model outputs against baseline without impacting users. Summary of changes: Implements a traffic thermostat controller that phases traffic according to an adaptive temperature curve derived from latency, token-efficiency, and model-confidence signals. Adds a "planned failback" subcontroller which can register a future failback window (timeboxed) tied to a model swap; during the window the system monitors quality regressions against a user-supplied metric set and, if a run rate of violations exceeds the configured failure budget, triggers a graceful roll-back with preflight drain and snapshotting of in-flight sessions. The controller integrates with shadow-replay to build an ongoing disagreement histogram and with the console rollout timeline for visualization and operator overrides. API changes: new rollout policy fields (thermostat_profile, failback_window_minutes, confidence_thresholds, replay_sample_rate). Backwards compatibility: defaults are conservative and no change for existing rollout configs. Migration: CLI helper to annotate existing active swaps with a default thermostat_profile. Testing and safety: unit tests for scheduler logic, e2e test against the perf canary harness, and a short-term synthetic shadow-replay run in the benchmark-lab. Observability: adds two new metrics (rollout_thermostat_temperature and planned_failback_violation_count), plus dashboards and alerting playbooks. Rollout plan: staged canary in dev -> beta -> prod with a 6-hour observation window and manual approval gates after beta. Related: references ENG-1345 for thermostat tuning experiments, SUP-7823 incident postmortem. Docs: console rollout reference and a new runbook for planned failbacks. Merge notes: squash-merged after sign-off. This PR is targeted at production-safe defaults and includes opt-in knobs for aggressive rollouters.
Diego Ramirez: Overall looks solid. Two concerns: 1) how thermostat interacts with autoscaler when temperature stays high for long periods; 2) snapshot size when failing back with many in-flight sessions. Please add documentation and a small test for both.
Author (Asha): Added autoscaler backpressure hook and documented snapshot retention. Snapshot size limited to metadata + causal checkpoints to avoid full state blowup.
Claire Ng: I'm worried about the default confidence thresholds being too permissive for multimodal models. Recommend lowering default and adding a checklist for teams to opt-in with overrides.
Author (Asha): Lowered default confidence threshold from 0.6 to 0.75 for multimodal model family and added CLI flag to revert if needed.
Michael O'Connor: CI flaked on e2e (timeout). Reran and passed; please monitor for flakiness in benchmark-lab harness.
Reviewer (Diego): Approved pending one minor log message change.
Author (Asha): Addressed log change and added structured log fields for rollout_id and thermostat_step.
payload.title: Planned failback and traffic thermostat for model swap

Context and motivation: We observed defects when promoting micro-cohorts to A/B variants where concurrent cohort joins could step on each other (session skew and transient mismatch of user splits). This PR adds a synchronized MicroCohort Join Controller that serializes cohort join work by session-lease and a staged commit protocol to ensure session-consistent join behavior across the mesh. The goal is to enable deterministic A/B join operations for small cohorts and staged canary promotions while preserving the existing rollback/failforward semantics used by the rollout runtime.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a new controller component rollout/microcohort/controller.go implementing a lease-backed queue and a three-phase join protocol (prepare, validate, commit).
- Implements session affinity enforcement in rollout/microcohort/affinity.go to guarantee that sessions do not observe partial joins mid-transaction.
- Introduces a graceful failforward mode: if validation fails but the error is non-safety-critical (e.g., perf regression within tolerance), controller can mark cohort as degraded and reduce traffic fraction instead of immediate rollback.
- Adds new telemetry counters and histograms (microcohort.join.duration_ms, microcohort.join.validation_failures, microcohort.join.failforward_events) and tracing spans (join.prepare -> join.validate -> join.commit).
- Adds thorough unit and integration tests (tests/microcohort/*) and an e2e smoke harness to exercise session continuity under join and rollback scenarios.
- Updates docs runbooks and rollout design notes (docs/rollouts/microcohort-join.md).

Commits included:
- Add microcohort join controller and basic protocol (mch-controller init) — 4 commits aggregated: core controller + lease client wiring.
- Add session affinity enforcement and tests (affinity + tests).
- Add telemetry, tracing, and e2e smoke (telemetry + e2e).

Files changed (high level):
- rollout/microcohort/controller.go (new) — core orchestration logic.
- rollout/microcohort/affinity.go (new) — session stickiness checks and deterministic hashing helpers.
- rollout/registry/lease_client.go (small changes) — expose lease API used by controller.
- internal/telemetry/microcohort_metrics.go (new) — counters and histograms.
- tests/microcohort/ (new) — unit/integration harnesses, deterministic replay fixtures.
- docs/rollouts/microcohort-join.md (new) — design and operational runbook.
- pkg/api/rollout.proto (tweak) — optional enum for FailforwardMode.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests: added ~45 unit tests, focused on state transitions and race conditions.
- Integration: a 3-node integration harness simulates lease leader election and persistent state across controller restarts.
- E2E smoke: runs against dev cluster, validates session affinity across traffic split changes.
- CI: all checks passed after a lint fix and a test flake retry.

Rollout plan (ops):
- Feature gated behind rollout.experimental.microcohort_join=false by default.
- Gradual enablement: start with internal canaries (0.5% traffic) for 48h with telemetry alerting.
- Safety gates: validation failure rate > 0.5% or average join.duration_ms > configured SLO triggers an automatic traffic reduction or rollback depending on failforward policy.

Operational considerations:
- The controller holds short-lived leases per cohort; lease TTL defaults to 30s and is configurable. Watch for lease starvation in overloaded control planes; telemetry includes lease.acquire.duration_ms.
- Session affinity requires a deterministic hashing seed shared across routers; this PR adds a compatibility mode that falls back to current hashing when the seed is not available.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc and runbook updated.
- [x] Unit tests added and passing.
- [x] Integration and e2e smoke passing on dev cluster.
- [x] Telemetry and alerts wired to console dashboards.
- [x] Migration paths for older rollout specs documented.

Related work: ENG-3241 (design spike), ENG-3308 (affinity refactor), SUP-8821 (customer incident that motivated deterministic joins).

Notes for reviewers: Focus on race conditions in controller.go (prepared a small concurrency diagram in the doc), validation thresholds and the semantics of failforward versus rollback. There's a deliberate conservative default (failforward=false) to preserve existing rollback-first behavior.
Erik Johnson (2026-02-18): Overall design looks sound. Two immediate asks: (1) make lease TTL configurable via runtime config not a compile constant; (2) add a bounded retry backoff when leader fails to acquire lock to avoid hot-looping.

Maya Chen (2026-02-18): Done — pushed change to expose TTL via config and added jittered backoff in the leader acquisition path (see controller.go + tests).
Priya Nair (2026-02-20): Tests caught a race where session affinity seed could be nil during coordinator handoff. Can you add a fallback and unit test?

Maya Chen (2026-02-21): Added a compatibility fallback and new unit tests (tests/microcohort/affinity_fallback_test.go). Also added a note in docs about rolling upgrade ordering.
Owen Park (2026-02-23): Small nit on telemetry naming: prefer microcohort.join.validation_failures_total for prometheus style. Also, can we emit a debug span that includes cohort id for easier trace search?

Maya Chen (2026-02-24): Renamed metric to validation_failures_total and added cohort_id tag on debug span. Updated dashboards.
Introduces a controller to coordinate timeboxed micro-cohort joins for A/B experiments and canaries. Adds session-consistent join orchestration, new telemetry, and rollout guard checks. Backwards compatible with existing rollout policies.

Motivation: reduce presubmit latency and developer cycle time by decomposing the monolithic lint runner and introducing tiny developer images for fast local iteration. This change partitions lint plugins by language/runtime and introduces a release-narrowing premerge gate to avoid running expensive downstream checks when the change is unrelated to release-critical paths. Scope: refactors the presubmit runner to load plugin bundles per-path, adds devcontainer and thin CI images optimized for quick installs, and wires a conditional release-narrowing check that consults a lightweight path classifier. Checklist: 1) extract lint-plugin registry and partition loader; 2) add thin dev image Dockerfiles and minimal toolchain bundles; 3) add path classifier (heuristic-based) and premerge gating; 4) update presubmit docs and dev-runner flags; 5) preserve legacy runner as opt-in via PRESERVE_LEGACY_RUNNER env flag. Testing: local smoke runs for python/ts/rust lint shards, CI pipeline run in feature branch with staged presubmit lanes, canary merge to staging repo, and manual validation by reviewers. Rollout plan: merge to main behind feature flag, enable on 10% of PRs via CI fastpath, monitor presubmit latency and false-positive rate for 2 weeks, then promote to 100% and deprecate legacy runner. Risk/mitigation: path classifier may underclassify, which would skip some expensive checks; mitigated by conservative defaults (treat unknown paths as release-critical) and a manual fallback that forces full presubmit. Migration notes: minimal changes required for devs—devcontainer images exposed as .devcontainer/quick-{py,ts,rust} and new make targets make dev-fast and make ci-thin. Related: ENG-2142 (presubmit partitioning), ENG-2207 (dev experience images). Release notes: presubmit latency improvements and new developer fast images; default presubmit behavior unchanged until rollout completes. CI details: initial run showed two flaky tests in ts-lint-shard fixed in follow-up commit. This PR retains all existing linters but changes the runtime loader and the CI orchestration to conditionally enqueue shards. Documentation: updated docs/presubmit.md and docs/devcontainers.md. Merge outcome: squash merged to main after final approval and green CI. For operational observability, added telemetry counters presubmit.partition.* and devimage.pull_latency.* to the CI telemetry namespace.
refactor: add plugin partition loader (m. lin); feat(ci): add thin dev images and make targets; ci: wire path-classifier premerge gate; fix(ts): address flaky-lint test exposed by partitioning; docs: update presubmit and devcontainer guides
Reviewer Omar: Please add a short description of the path classification heuristics and a fallback. Author Maya: added heuristics doc string and conservative fallback. Reviewer Priya: noted the devimage size could be reduced further; tracked as a follow-up task. Reviewer Luca: requested telemetry counters; added metrics_registry registration. CI note: initial CI failed lint in ts-shard due to new loader ordering; fixed in commit 'fix(ts): address flaky-lint test exposed by partitioning'. All reviewers approved after fixes.
- Presubmit: partitioned lint plugins to reduce average presubmit latency. - Developer: new lightweight devcontainer images for fast iteration (make dev-fast). - CI: release-narrowing premerge gate reduces unnecessary expensive checks.
This PR aims for minimal disruption: legacy runner can be re-enabled via PRESERVE_LEGACY_RUNNER=true. We will monitor telemetry presubmit.partition.latency and presubmit.partition.false_suppression_rate and revert gating if false suppression exceeds 0.5%. Follow-up work tracked in ENG-2299 to shrink devimage layer counts and ENG-2314 to add ML-based path classifier.

Motivation: We observed a recurring tradeoff between continuous-batching efficiency and p99 latency for mixed-sequence workloads. The existing monolithic attention path either prioritized throughput (large batches) or latency (small batches) but could not achieve both without wasting KV cache or performing redundant KV writes. This PR implements a split-stage attention pipeline that separates token dispatching, kernel execution, and KV commit into clear stages connected by minimal synchronization. Key pieces: (1) a small dispatch worker that merges short requests into micro-batches while maintaining latency SLOs; (2) a lightweight kernel launcher that runs a compact 'compute-only' attention kernel optimized for tiled QK compute (no commit side-effects); (3) an asynchronous KV commit stage that deduplicates KV entries and performs batched writes to the cache with ordered guarantees. The approach reduces redundant KV writes for similar prefix requests and allows more aggressive batching without lengthening commit latency. Detailed changes and why: - Split-stage pipeline: adds runtime/attn/split_stage_orchestrator.cpp + header and a new state machine for request lifecycle. The orchestrator exposes two knobs: pipeline_mode (off|latency|throughput) and commit_window_ms; default remains backward-compatible. - Compute-only kernel: introduce runtime/attn/split_compute_kernel.cu implementing a compact tiled qk kernel that omits KV store ops and exposes a small per-thread scratch for rotary precomputation. Kernel selection logic in kernel_selector.cpp now prefers split_compute_kernel for short-to-mid sequence cases when pipeline_mode!=off. - KV deduplication: cache_manager.cpp gains a lightweight fingerprint table (small LRU with fast 64-bit hashes) to coalesce identical KV entries within the commit window; this reduces redundant memory churn for many chat-based workloads that re-emit similar prefixes. Dedup is opt-in via config and keys are stable across model versions. - Async commit: commit_worker.cpp applies commits in background worker(s) with commit-grouping and backpressure signals to the orchestrator. Worker employs single-producer multiple-consumer patterns to avoid locks on the hot path. - Continuous batching integration: the dispatcher now supports micro-batch formation while respecting per-request latency budgets; continuous_batcher.cpp got a heuristic for preferring micro-batches vs immediate dispatch. - Tests and benchmarks: added tests/benchmarks/attn_splitstage_bench.py and unit tests for dedup, correctness under race conditions, and backward-compatibility asserts. Performance: bench runs on p4d-like instance (fp16) show: - Mixed-length conversational workload: throughput +22% (tokens/s) vs main, p99 latency -12% - Long-context (8k) workloads: KV memory reduction ~35% due to dedup and delayed commit grouping - Small single-request latencies: median change <1% regression (goal met) Compatibility and safety: default behavior is conservative; pipeline_mode defaults to 'off' to avoid surprising behavior in older deployments. Migration steps are documented in docs/perf/split_stage_attn.md. Checklist: - [x] Kernel implementation and selector - [x] KV dedup LRU and tests - [x] Async commit worker and backpressure API - [x] Bench harness and baseline comparisons - [x] Documentation and config knobs - [x] Internal canary on Dedicated cluster (small rollout) Related work: builds on ideas from recent continuous-batching improvements (ENG-7122) and cache eviction instrumentation (ENG-7309). There is a companion experiment branch on redwood-examples that demonstrates switching pipeline_mode at runtime. Release notes: see release_notes field. Merge notes: squashed merge; post-merge immediate canary rollout; monitoring dashboards added under Console -> Attn Split-Stage.
Adds a split-stage attention pipeline with compute-only kernels and async KV commit that allows safer aggressive batching, reduces redundant KV writes via deduplication, and yields measurable throughput and latency improvements for mixed workloads. Opt-in via pipeline_mode and controlled rollout enabled.
Introduce split-stage attention pipeline with KV deduplication and async commit: +22% tail throughput on mixed-length workloads, p99 latency down ~12%, and KV memory footprint reduced ~35% for long-context models. Backward-compatible runtime switch; opt-in via attn.pipeline_mode.
Trevor Hammond (2025-11-20): Can you explain the dedup fingerprint collision risk and what happens if we get a false positive?
Lena Rodriguez (2025-11-21): We use 64-bit fingerprints with a policy of fallback full-key compare in boundary cases. Collision probability is negligible; added unit test that forces collision path via test harness and verifies correctness. Answered inline with pointer to tests/unit/test_kv_dedup.cpp
Priya Nair (2025-11-24): The async commit backpressure API looks good but ensure that the orchestrator's latency budget is not starved when commit queue is full. Please add a metric and a graceful fallback to synchronous commit for high-priority requests.
Lena Rodriguez (2025-11-25): Added metric attn.commit.queue_wait_ms and implemented synchronous fallback for requests with priority==high. See commit a11c9f0. Added tests covering fallback path.
Owen Brooks (2025-11-28): Suggest adding a flag in defaults so customers can opt into dedup only for models known to be stable across versions.
Lena Rodriguez (2025-11-28): Added config entry configs/defaults/attn_config.yaml: kv_dedup_enabled_by_default: false and documented model-stability requirements in docs/perf/split_stage_attn.md

Added conservative runtime defaults for cache tiers, a safety wrapper for automatic low-bit quantization rollouts, and a unit-econ delta report generator. No behavioral breaking changes for existing tenants; new opt-ins available for aggressive optimization.
Motivation: customers increasingly enable aggressive quantization and cache trimming via automated profiles; we observed regressions in perceptual-quality sensitive flows and noisy unit-econ signals when defaults allowed too-aggressive rollouts. This PR introduces conservative, production-friendly defaults for cache tiers and a quantization safety layer that prevents automatic low-bit rollouts in high-risk contexts.

What this changes (summary):
- Introduces a tiered cache defaults module (packages/runtime/src/cache/defaults.ts) with conservative TTLs, explicit warmup thresholds, and a tenant opt-in flag for more aggressive caching. Defaults are chosen to reduce tail-latency variance while preserving unit-econ improvement potential.
- Adds a quantization safety wrapper (packages/runtime/src/quantization/safety-layer.ts) which annotates model variants with a safety_score (string label + float) and blocks auto-rollout to <8-bit quantized variants for inputs flagged as quality-sensitive (e.g., code generation, long-form summarization). The safety policy is configurable via the optimization-settings UI.
- Console UI: new control in tenant optimization settings to opt into aggressive defaults, and a visual indicator showing quantization risk (packages/console/src/components/tenants/optimization-settings.tsx).
- CLI: unit-econ diff command (packages/cli/src/commands/unit-econ-diff.ts) which produces a compact report comparing token-level cost deltas and sample-quality regressions between a baseline and a candidate config. This helps SREs and PMs validate that default changes produce net-positive unit economics.
- Tests: added integration e2e tests that simulate a high-quality workload and verify the safety-layer blocks unsafe rollouts (integration-tests/e2e/quant-safety.spec.ts) and caching fixture (integration-tests/fixtures/tenant-scenarios/caching.json).
- Docs: operations guide describing new defaults and rollout guidance (docs/ops/cost-optimization-guides.md).

Commits (high level):
- 9f3a2b1: initial cache defaults and config plumbing
- d7b4c88: quantization safety-layer implementation and unit tests
- 3c2d1f4: console settings and CLI unit-econ-diff command
- b8e7a9c: integration tests and docs

Files changed (high level):
- runtime cache defaults and interfaces; low-risk change with clear feature gates.
- new quant safety module; inserted into model rollout path with short-circuit for tenants that opted for legacy behavior.
- console UI additions and minor UX copy.
- small CLI tool to generate unit-econ delta reports used by SRE/PM.

Testing & CI:
- Local unit tests: all new unit tests pass (coverage maintained).
- Integration: e2e quant-safety and caching fixtures added; CI runs these as part of the perf-e2e job.
- CI status: passing in this PR (perf-e2e flake fixed on second run).

Review conversation (high level):
- Ethan Park: "Thanks — can we make the default warmup window configurable per-tenant? For tenants with low QPS, the warmup threshold might be hit too slowly."
  - Author reply: "Added tenant-level override and documented expected tradeoffs in the ops doc; default remains conservative to protect quality."
- Luca Morales: "The safety_score is useful, but can we ensure we surface an actionable reason in logs when a rollout is blocked?"
  - Author reply: "Yes — telemetry event added: quant.safety.blocked with reason code and tenant id (see safety-layer). Also surfaced in console as a tooltip."
- Ava Chen: "Integration tests look good; please add a smoke check that the CLI report returns non-zero delta when candidate uses 4-bit vs baseline 16-bit."

Rollout plan:

- Gradually open opt-in flag for internal tenants and SRE-run experiments.
- After 2 weeks of monitoring unit-econ deltas and QoQ metrics, consider promoting opt-in to tenant default for low-risk classes.

Backward compatibility:
- Existing tenants keep previous behavior unless they opt in to the new aggressive caching/quant controls. The quant safety-layer defaults to permissive legacy behavior if a tenant explicitly set legacy_rollout=true in their optimization profile.

Merge details: squashed and merged after final sign-off from reviewers. CI green.

Notes for on-call: if you observe sudden QoL regressions in production streams after enabling aggressive opt-ins, run the CLI unit-econ-diff against the last-known-good config and the opt-in config; the diff includes tokenized sample comparisons and cost delta scores to aid rollback decisions.

Motivation: Continuous batching under mixed-priority workloads occasionally allowed persistent low-priority starvation and mid-tail latency spikes when KV cache pins and kernel selection conspired to form micro-pipelines of long-running requests. This PR introduces the 'latent harmonizer', a lightweight queue-damping and timeout orchestration layer that smooths admission bursts, enforces soft fairness credits, and moves a small set of KV-cache pin heuristics into the scheduler to reduce cross-request interference. Changes: 1) scheduler: add soft-fairness credit accounting with exponential decay and a configurable damping factor to prevent bursty priority inversion; 2) queueing: introduce per-cohort enqueue jitter and time-horizon backoff to spread arrival peaks and reduce coalescer monopolization; 3) timeouts: tighten soft-reservation timeouts and add a probe lease that opportunistically preempts stalled slots when backlog and age thresholds are exceeded; 4) KV cache: add pin-eligibility window tracking and a lightweight sampler-driven demotion path to avoid long-term KV pin starvation; 5) kernels: add hints to kernel selector for short-seq fast-path preference when harmonizer detects high churn; 6) observability: new metrics for harmonizer_credit, cohort_damping, kv_pin_age_buckets and an internal histogram for preempted_slot_age. Performance: in internal bench runs with mixed chat+embedding workload the harmonizer reduced 99th percentile generation latency by 18-28% in contention scenarios and lowered effective token cost by 6% due to fewer wasted kernel warmups. Testing: unit tests for credit decay and enqueue jitter, e2e contention tests and KV pin demotion tests added; canary rollout plan described below. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.harmonizer.enabled=false by default; staged rollout to Dedicated then Hosted with automatic fallback; add console knobs for damping_factor and probe_threshold. Risk and mitigation: risk of over-preemption causing throughput regression fixed by conservative defaults and a safety circuit that disables harmonizer when preemption_rate > 0.5% for 5m; added alerts and automatic rollback in console. See linked Linear tickets for experimental traces and benchmark dashboards. Checklist: code, unit tests, integration tests, docs, bench results, ops runbook, canary plan. 
2026-02-20 Arjun Patel: Nice approach, can you explain how the decay constant was chosen and whether it's per-cohort adjustable? Maya Chen: We picked the decay via controlled bench sweeps across 0.2-0.9; defaults are 0.6 and exposed as damping_factor per-cohort in runtime config.
2026-02-21 Lucia Romero: We should be conservative with preemption in Hosted initial rollout; add a safety circuit that disables harmonizer if regressions appear. Maya Chen: Added safety circuit that monitors preemption_rate and a rollout plan in the PR description.
2026-02-24 Evan Gray: Observability looks good but please add a percentile for preempted_slot_age in the dashboard. Maya Chen: Added histogram and example dashboard tiles in docs and benchboard.
2026-02-26 Arjun Patel: Small nit: prefer explicit unit tests for enqueue jitter distribution. Maya Chen: Added deterministic jitter unit tests using seeded RNG.
2026-03-01 Lucia Romero: CI flaked once on bench harness, reran, all green. Lucia Romero: Approved and queued for merge.
Operational: New runtime feature 'latent harmonizer' to reduce continuous-batcher tail latency and prevent starvation; default disabled. Operators: damping_factor and probe_threshold knobs added to runtime config; recommended conservative defaults documented. Observability: new metrics harmonizer_credit, cohort_damping, kv_pin_age_buckets. Rollout: staged canary with automatic rollback conditions described in ops runbook.
1) Enable runtime.harmonizer.enabled=false->true in 10% of nodes. 2) Monitor harmonizer_credit and preemption_rate for 15m. 3) If preemption_rate > 0.5% or 99p latency regresses >5% rollback automatically. 4) Tune damping_factor down if throughput drops. 5) For KV-heavy services increase pin_eligibility_window_ms cautiously.

Motivation: Structured-output use cases (JSON/CSV/DSL responses) remain fragile in partial/streaming modes when tokenizer boundaries or control characters are emitted mid-response. This PR introduces a conservative output sanitizer and a set of tokenizer-boundary heuristics to reduce malformed structured responses, improves OpenAI-compatibility behavior for function/tool calls during streaming, and exposes a short-circuit backend toggle for constrained decoding fallbacks.

What this changes (single-string summary): Adds a streaming sanitizer that performs low-latency, token-aware escapes and soft-truncation hints; implements a deferred-close-token heuristic to avoid emitting closing braces/quotes until an end-of-structure token is confidently produced; augments regex/CFG backends with a tokenizer-aware fallback that aligns regex anchors with token boundaries; patches the OpenAI-compat layer so function call hints are preserved and rehydrated if a streaming interruption occurs; introduces an environment toggle (OPENAI_COMPAT_CONSTRAINT_BACKEND) to prefer "token-aware-fallback" for high-integrity structured outputs.

Checklist:
- [x] Sanitizer: streaming token-level sanitizer with minimal buffering
- [x] Token boundary heuristics: conservative opening/closing emission, surrogate pair handling
- [x] Regex/CFG fallback: tokenizer-aware anchor alignment and percent-escape mapping
- [x] OpenAI compat: persist function-call hints across partial responses and replay on reconnect
- [x] Backwards-compatible defaults: feature off for older deployment profiles, opt-in via env/route config
- [x] Tests: unit + e2e streaming harness + compatibility fuzzing against existing examples

Why unique: Previous PRs addressed grammar or regex backend bugs; this work focuses on the surface between tokenizer semantics and structured output stability in streaming/function-call scenarios and ties to OpenAI compatibility behaviors. It intentionally errs on the conservative side to prioritize correctness over token throughput in affected routes.

Testing notes: Added new e2e tests run in the streaming harness (tests/streaming_structured_scenarios) that simulate mid-stream disconnects and racey token emissions. CI includes fuzz runs for token-boundary edge cases (surrogate pairs, combining marks) and regression asserts against the real-world prompt corpus used by ENG-8721.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind OPENAI_COMPAT_CONSTRAINT_BACKEND=token-aware-fallback and route-level config in console. Start with canary on dedicated cluster, monitor structured-output regressions and latency P50/P95.

Marco: Can you summarize the expected latency impact on high-throughput chat routes? Please include a P50/P95 delta from the benchmark harness.
Ava: Conservative heuristics add a small buffering window (~1-3 tokens) in streaming hotpath; measured P50 unchanged, P95 +6ms for 2048-token typical sequences (benchmarks added).
Sofie: Edge case: surrogate pair split across token boundary still produced malformed JSON in local run. Is the joiner logic handling UTF-16 surrogate pairs?
Ava: Added explicit surrogate-pair reassembly in token_boundary.rs and a fuzz test that reproduces the issue; pushed that commit.
Devon: LGTm but please add an explicit opt-out in route config for low-latency chat endpoints where strict structure is not required.
Ava: Added route-level flag preserve_structured_integrity=false and documented behavior; default remains true for OpenAI-compat constrained routes.
Adds an opt-in token-aware streaming sanitizer and tokenizer boundary heuristics to improve stability of structured outputs in streaming and function-call scenarios. Default gated behind OPENAI_COMPAT_CONSTRAINT_BACKEND; see console docs for rollout.

Impact: reduces malformed JSON/CSV outputs during mid-stream disconnects and tokenizer-edge cases; small P95 latency increase on affected routes.

Action: Enable in canary, monitor structured-output error rate and latency P95.
New route-level flag: preserve_structured_integrity (default true for compat routes)
New env toggle: OPENAI_COMPAT_CONSTRAINT_BACKEND=token-aware-fallback
Improved stability for streamed JSON/CSV/DSL outputs when using constrained decoding or function calls
This PR avoids wholesale changes to the constrained decoding API and focuses on runtime heuristics and short-term fallbacks. Future work includes a configurable integrity/latency knob surfaced in the console and tighter integration with Optimize recommendations.

Motivation: ensure cryptographic provenance and tenant attributes flow end-to-end for auditability and access control. This PR implements immutable crypto-tag propagation in request headers and audit records, exposes those tags as first-class attributes in the RBAC v2 evaluation pipeline, and ships a small policy-matrix generator to help security teams validate tenant scoping policies. Summary: 1) carry X-Redwood-Crypto-Tag through the API gateway, internal RPCs, and eventual audit forwarder without allowing mutation by downstream services; 2) enrich audit events with crypto_tag and signer_fingerprint fields and persist them to the audit index; 3) add crypto_tag and tenant_attribute predicates to the RBAC v2 engine and wire them into policy evaluation; 4) include a tool (scripts/policy-matrix-generator) that expands high-level policy rules into a matrix with example tenants and crypto tags for reviewers; 5) provide a migration/rollout path behind feature flag security.crypto_tag.enabled. Implementation notes: header validation happens at the JWT introspection layer (authn) and at the gateway ingress. The header is canonicalized to a hashed form to avoid PII leakage and is signed with the platform key before being forwarded to internal services. The rbac evaluator receives an attributes bag that includes crypto_tag and tenant_attrs which can be referenced from policy expressions. The audit forwarder now appends crypto provenance fields and exposes an opt-in index mapping in the private deployment installer. Migration and rollout: feature flag default is off; rollout plan is staged: enable in dev -> enable in staging for all tenants -> opt-in for enterprise customers -> globally on after 2 weeks and metric stability checks. Backwards compatibility: services that don't understand the new attributes will safely ignore them; audit indices will be populated only when the feature flag is enabled for a control group. Testing: unit tests for header parsing and policy predicates, integration tests covering gateway->service->audit path, and end-to-end smoke with a sample tenant. Docs and ops: added runbook entry, upgrade notes for private installer, and sample policies. Checklist: [x] header propagation and signing implemented [x] rbac attribute plumbing implemented [x] audit enrichment implemented [x] policy-matrix generator added [x] unit/integration tests added [x] docs and upgrade notes added

Anika Bose: Added TTL check to the signer and included a unit test to assert replay rejection for stale tags.
Priya Nair: We need stronger guarantees that downstream services cannot overwrite the canonical crypto tag. Suggest rejecting requests with X-Redwood-Crypto-Tag when the service writes a different tag to downstream calls.
Anika Bose: Implemented gateway-level mutation protection and added a lint rule to fail builds if services attempt to set the header in outbound clients. Documented expected behavior in the migration notes.
Lucas Park: Integration tests are failing intermittently in CI due to timing in the signer; can we make the signer deterministic in tests or mock the clock?

Exposes crypto_tag and tenant_attribute predicates in RBAC v2 so policies can reference cryptographic provenance and tenant metadata.
Adds audit enrichment for crypto provenance fields; private installer includes optional index mappings for search/alerts.

Adds a Throughput Sentinel controller that smooths scale decisions by anchoring elasticity to observed tail-utilization and latency, introduces per-tenant microburst insulation tokens, and publishes new telemetry for utilization ratcheting and burst accounting.
Motivation: Dedicated fleet autoscalers at scale have repeatedly oscillated on short workload shifts and microbursts. Scale-up reactions are generally fine, but scale-down decisions occasionally evict capacity too aggressively and fail to reserve microburst headroom for tenants with bursty traffic, causing transient SLA slippage. This PR introduces a small, conservative control-plane component — the Throughput Sentinel — which provides an elasticity anchoring layer that biases autoscaler decisions using a ratcheted utilization view and a microburst insulation budget per tenant.

Design summary: The Throughput Sentinel is an opt-in controller that sits between the utilization sampler and the scale decision engine. Key concepts:
- Ratcheted utilization: maintain a short-term percentile (P90/P95 by config) utilization envelope per tenant/pool and never drop below the envelope for scale-down decisions until a configurable decay window passes.
- Elasticity anchoring: compute an anchoring factor (0..1) that dampens scale-down velocity based on recent utilization delta, tail latency, and warm-pool occupancy.
- Microburst insulation tokens: lightweight credit tokens allocated per tenant that represent reserved headroom for microbursts; tokens are consumed on accepted bursts and replenished over longer windows. Tokens prevent aggressive preemption of spare slots needed for short-lived spikes.
- Telemetry: expose new metrics (throughput_sentinel.ratchet_util, throughput_sentinel.anchor_factor, throughput_sentinel.tokens_remaining) and an aggregated microburst_accounting histogram to help diagnose burst-related throttles.

Checklist:
- [x] Controller implementation + unit tests
- [x] Autoscaler integration (hooks for anchor factor)
- [x] Telemetry + Prometheus rules and Grafana dashboard draft
- [x] E2E scenario tests (scale-down oscillation + synthetic microburst)
- [x] Feature flag gated (default OFF for existing customers)

- a9bf22e: autoscaler integration: apply anchor factor and token checks during proposed scale-down

Behaviour and safety notes:
- Feature flag & rollout: the sentinel is disabled by default. A runtime flag can enable it per-cluster; rollout plan recommended: stage in non-prod -> subset of Dedicated pools -> all Dedicated pools.
- Fail-open: if sentinel cannot retrieve sufficient telemetry (e.g. aggregator outage) it will skip anchoring and let autoscaler behave as before to avoid global risk.
- Tunables: ratchet percentile, decay window, anchor_strength, token_replenish_window and per-tenant max_tokens are configurable via the existing autoscaler config map.

CI summary:

- Lint: passed (go vet/golangci-lint)

- Performance bench: lightweight local bench shows <3% extra CPU overhead on control-plane leader and negligible latency to scale decisions (~4ms median additional).

Review conversation (summary):

- Priya Nair: requested clearer invariants to ensure the anchor doesn't prevent necessary scale-down after sustained idle periods. Added decay window and a conservative default anchor_strength=0.25; documented invariants in docs/ops/throughput-sentinel.md.
- Luca Bianchi: raised concern about cross-tenant fairness when tokens are scarce; proposed a weighted token allocation based on tenant commitment tier. Implemented a simple weight multiplier and left hooks for future policy modules.

Merge: Squash-merged by Samir Patel on 2025-11-21 after approvals from Ethan and Priya. Release note drafted and included in release_notes field above.

Maya Chen: Added fail-open path and per-pool enable flag. Benchmarks attached in artifacts/throughput-sentinel/bench-20251114.txt showing ~3% cpu at leader under test load.

payload.body:
Motivation:
High spill frequency and fragmented free space in the KV cache increase disk/network IO and amplify tail latency for token-generating requests. This change introduces a hybrid approach to reduce fragmentation-driven spills and the volume of spilled bytes.

What this PR does (single-string description):
- Adds a Hybrid Tail Coalescer: a background compaction agent that identifies small "micro-holes" (free fragments under a threshold) at the tail of allocation arenas and coalesces them into contiguous spans when doing so minimizes copy work. The algorithm prefers tail-biased coalescing to avoid disrupting warm pages in the middle of arenas.
- Introduces a Spill Compression Pipeline: when eviction is necessary, pages eligible for spill are routed through an inline compression pipeline (lz4 fast, fallback to zstd for higher ratio when CPU slack is available). Compressed spill records are tagged with a compression header for backwards compatibility with existing spill readers.
- Eviction gating integrated with continuous batching: eviction decision now considers pending batch size and KV "recently-accessed" hints to avoid preemptive evictions that force immediate cache re-reads for requests in-flight. This reduces churn during busy tails.
- Kernel and scheduler hints: cache allocator exposes a small set of kernel hints (COLD/COLD_COMPRESS/CANDIDATE) to steer the runtime's kernel selection and IO batching heuristics.
- Telemetry and safety toggles: added metrics (spill_bytes_compressed, spill_compression_ratio, microhole_coalesce_runs, microhole_coalesce_bytes, eviction_gate_hold_ms) and config flags to control coalescer aggressiveness and enable compression per-tenant.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- The coalescer operates opportunistically and is bounded by a per-arena compaction budget to avoid CPU interference with inference. We tuned default budget to <2% CPU on a typical dedicated worker in our canary fleet.
- Compression reduces network egress and S3 object sizes for hosted spills but introduces CPU cost; we apply it selectively based on measured compressibility and runtime headroom.
- Backwards compatibility: spill readers accept both compressed and uncompressed formats; migration is opt-in via config to avoid step-change for large deployments.

Benchmarks (micro-bench on internal perf harness):
- p50 generation latency: ~0.6% improvement (noise), p95 generation latency: -9% on heavy-eviction scenario (50% cache pressure).
- Spill bytes written: -23% (lz4 fast baseline), observed zstd paths yield up to -42% bytes in high-compressibility workloads.
- Eviction frequency: -18% (fewer eviction events per minute in synthetic mixed workload).
- End-to-end cost projection: estimated 7–12% unit-cost reduction in cache-heavy workloads when compression enabled.

Rollout plan:
- Feature behind two-stage toggle: coalescer.enabled and spill.compression.enabled (tenant-level flags).
- Canary: enable coalescer without compression on 5 dedicated workers for 48h, monitor eviction and latency metrics.
- Stage rollout for compression on tenants with low CPU utilization or high spill bandwidth; monitor CPU and request SLOs.
- Full rollout after 14-day canary and a controlled canary expansion.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for coalescer (fragment identification and merge correctness).
- [x] Integration test for compressed spill roundtrip and backward compatibility.
- [x] Telemetry and dashboards (cost/latency/regression alerts).
- [x] Canary rollout plan documented.

Notes for reviewers: please focus on the coalescer budget interaction with our scheduler and the correctness of the compressed spill headers. I included a small compatibility shim to keep old spill readers functional; if we want to avoid the shim we can gate a short migration window in the control plane.

Benji Liao (review): Can the coalescer's budget be adjusted at runtime? We should be able to throttle if CPU climbs during peak.
Author: yes, it's a dynamic config and we default to conservative values. Added a note in ops config and a runbook entry.
Marta Kovac (review): I'm worried about interaction with existing defragmenter. How do they coordinate?
Author: Coalescer prefers tail regions and has a lease-based coordination token with the global defrag agent; added comments and a small unit test to validate non-overlap.
Diego Alvarez (review): Compression header looks fine but please add a version field to avoid future ambiguity.
Author: Added version byte and tests for reader fallback.
CI system: Build failed on first run due to flake in allocator test; reproducer added and fixed.
Author: fixed allocator race by adding a test-only barrier.

Motivation: Rollouts that rely solely on passive telemetry and long-running A/B experiments often detect regressions too late for low-latency LLM inference workloads. This change introduces the Rewind Adjudicator, an operator-side component that orchestrates short-lived staged shadow rehearsals using a synthetic smoke runner to accelerate regression signal and provide an actionable rollback suggestion. Design summary: The adjudicator is a stateful controller that can be enabled per rollout via helm values or the rollout spec. It coordinates three phases: 1) Dry rehearsal where a bounded subset of traffic is shadowed and replayed deterministically against a candidate revision; 2) Synthetic smoke where generated prompts (user-provided or default prompt bank) exercise known SLO-sensitive slices and produce a compact metrics digest; 3) Decision adjudication where telemetry anchors (latency P95, token-cost delta, accuracy proxy via eval hooks) are compared against configured fidelity gates and historical baselines to compute a risk score and suggested action. Key behaviors: - Non-blocking: when the adjudicator is experimental it only attaches suggestions to the rollout decision; when promoted it can block promotion until gates pass. - Deterministic replay seeding ensures reproducible smoke runs for postmortem. - Graceful fallback: if the adjudicator or replay runner fails the orchestrator continues with existing staged rollout policy and records the failure as an event for triage. API and surface changes: - rollout.spec.adjudicator.{enabled,mode,probeSet} new fields to opt-in and configure synthetic smoke parameters. - rdctl adjudicator subcommand: rdctl rollout adjudicator status|replay|force-rollback. - Console panel to visualize adjudicator decisions and replay traces. Testing and rollout plan: Unit coverage for the decision logic and telemetry extraction. E2E suite triggers a short staged shadow rehearsal and asserts the adjudicator suggests rollback under injected regression signals. Feature gated behind helm.values.rollouts.adjudicator.enabled=false by default. Observability: added Prometheus rules and tracing annotations for adjudicator-run.{start,success,fail} and a compact decision event schema emitted to the event bus for easier SLO backfills. Security and compliance: replayed inputs are masked by default using existing PII redaction hooks; customers can opt into raw replays via Private deployments and KMS-wrapped storage. Backwards compatibility: no changes to the public runtime API. Migration: operators can enable the adjudicator per-rollout incrementally and tune probe sets with the new rdctl CLI. Impact: expected to reduce mean time to detect latent regressions in canary/promote flows by surfacing actionable signals within minutes rather than hours. Related work: builds on ENG-7201 (staged-shadow plumbing) and complements ENG-7920 (telemetry anchors). Linear: ENG-8421 and ENG-8479. CI matrix: flaky test adjusted and stabilized in e2e harness. Merge notes: squad validated on dedicated staging cluster for three days with controlled traffic and synthetic regressions applied.
Adds a Rewind Adjudicator that coordinates staged shadow rehearsals and automatic rollback suggestions based on synthetic smoke results and user-configured fidelity gates. No breaking API changes.
Jordan Kim (reviewer): This is a significant addition to the rollout surface. Please ensure the decision algorithm is explainable and add logging that records the contributing metrics for a suggestion.
Asha Patel (author): Added a decisionTrace payload that records the metric deltas and gate thresholds used; see pkg/orchestrator/adjudicator.go line 210. We also emit the compact decision event to the event bus for postmortem queries.
Priya Shah (reviewer): The default probe bank might leak personal data if customers supply arbitrary prompts. Can we ensure redaction is applied to both replay and synthetic buckets by default?
Asha Patel (author): Default behavior now applies redactPipeline to all replay inputs. Added docs in cmd/rdctl/rollback_adjudicator.md and a helm toggle to opt into raw replays for Private installs.
Mateo Rivera (reviewer): CI e2e was flaky once. Can we add retry logic to the synthetic smoke runner and make the harness deterministic?
Asha Patel (author): Added exponential backoff with bounded retries and deterministic seeding; updated tests to use replay fixture with timeouts tightened. CI flakiness resolved.
Jordan Kim (approver): Code review complete. Approving after docs updates.
Enable feature via helm: rollouts.adjudicator.enabled=true and supply optional probe set via rollouts.adjudicator.probeSet. Start with mode=observe to gather decision traces before enforcing gate blocks. Monitor adjudicator_run_success_rate and decision_risk_score. If adjudicator causes unexpected blocking, disable by setting rollouts.adjudicator.enabled=false and trigger rdctl rollout adjudicator force-rollback to revert suggestions.

Motivation: developer feedback and CI flakiness showed the monolithic lint runner was slowing presubmit feedback and making dependency churn risky. This PR breaks the lint pipeline into explicit language plugin adapters, introduces a small plugin contract, and adds an automated dependency-rotation scheduler to safely roll forward low-risk devdeps. Changes include a new plugin loader, language adapters for python/ts/go, a lightweight dep-rotator service that opens PRs against our repos with tests run by the existing CI lanes, and a migration path that keeps the old pipeline as a feature-flagged fallback. Checklist: [x] plugin contract and loader implemented [x] python/typescript/go adapters added [x] dep-rotator worker + scheduler added [x] migration feature flag and docs updated [x] existing CI matrix integrated with new jobs [x] release notes drafted. Why now: presubmit latency has regressed for large monorepo changes and dependency drift is causing urgent follow-ups. Design highlights: language plugins are small binaries or scripts executed under the same hermetic runner, they declare lint-target patterns and provide a normalized exitcode+report JSON. The loader picks plugins by file globs and runs them in parallel per-changed-file batches. The dep-rotator runs weekly in a lightweight k8s CronJob, clones the repo, runs the dependency bump strategy (pin-to-latest-minor, run tests, open PR with changelog and CI link), and annotates PRs for staged rollout. Rollout plan: enable plugin loader behind feature flag (default off) for two weeks, mirror CI results in a staging branch, then flip on progressively for service owners. Backout: fall back to legacy runner by disabling flag. Risk: new scheduler requires RBAC for creating PRs and a robot token; token is scoped and rotated by the secrets team. Related: builds on ENG-2417 (presubmit decomposition) and ENG-2432 (lint telemetry). Docs: added CONDUCT and docs/ci/lint-plugins.md. Testing: unit tests for plugin contract, e2e presubmit smoke on a staging branch, integration tests for dep rotation executing on a fork with dry-run mode. Known issues: initial TS adapter has one noisy rule that is being tuned, and one flaky integration test was quarantined with a linked ticket. Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2417/lint-pipeline-plugin-design, scheduler diagram https://company.internal/diagrams/dep-rotator. Merge: squashed and merged after final approval. Timeline: work started 2025-10-01, first review 2025-10-20, last review 2025-11-02. Summary of commits: 10 commits squashed into one merge commit capturing plugin loader, three adapters, dep-rotator service, CI job definitions, and docs updates.
Refactor: Lint pipeline modularized into language plugin adapters. Feature: Automated dependency rotation service added to open and test dependency update PRs on a weekly cadence. Ops: Deprecated legacy makefile lint targets. No runtime behaviour changes expected.
Ethan Zhao: The plugin contract looks clean. Small ask to document loader timeouts and concurrency defaults. Author: Added default concurrency=8 and timeout=60s in loader, updated docs.
Priya Nair: Can we gate the dep-rotator so it starts in dry-run mode for 2 weeks? Author: Dep-rotator supports dry-run via --dry flag; scheduler set to dry-run for first 2 runs, added runbook.
Samir Gupta: CI matrix may increase overall presubmit time; suggest slicing by changed-file groups. Author: Implemented per-file batching and parallel plugin execution; updated presubmit job to slice into 4 shards.

Motivation: We see a recurring tradeoff where aggressive fast-path kernel selection and low-precision variants reduce p99 latency but occasionally produce small numerical regressions on a narrow set of prompts (rare long-tail token distributions). This PR introduces the "Correctness-Latency Controller" (CLC): a runtime component that continuously balances correctness and latency targets by (1) adaptively toggling precision modes on per-model/route windows, (2) soft-throttling fast-path usage under detected correctness drift, and (3) adjusting batching windows and KV cache staleness heuristics to reduce false-positive regressions from cache evictions.

Goals: (a) keep p99 and p95 within existing SLO tiers while reducing end-to-end correctness regressions (measured by our eval harness) by >60% on canary traffic; (b) do not increase median latency by more than 6% for high-throughput routes.

What changed:
- New component runtime/clc_controller.{cc,h}: controller loop, state machine, and pluggable policies (latency-first, correctness-first, balanced). The controller consumes lightweight telemetry (per-route output-diff signal, kernel-fallback counts, kv-eviction rates, batching window occupancy) and emits decisions: precision_hint, fastpath_allowance (0..100), batching_window_ms_override, kv_staleness_grace_ms.
- Scheduler integration runtime/scheduler.cc: scheduler now queries CLC when making fast-path vs compatibility-path dispatch decisions; a soft-throttle token bucket is applied before selecting optimistic kernels.
- KV cache manager runtime/kv_cache_manager.cc: supports staleness grace window and exposes eviction surge metrics.
- Adaptive testing harness tests/clc_integration_test.py: synthetic correctness perturbations and latency SLO simulation; reproduces past regression scenarios found by ENG-8453.
- Docs and runbook docs/operational/clc.md: operational knobs, how to promote policies, rollback steps.
- Benchmarks benchmarks/clc_canary_report.md and benchmark scripts for automated canary runs.

Backwards compatibility: Controller defaults to a no-op (pass-through) policy unless enabled via feature flag service.flags.enable_clc on a route or deployment; safe-mode flag forces compatibility path and disables precision upgrades.

Tests and validation:
- Unit tests for controller state transitions and policy evaluation.
- Integration test that replays historical regression traces (from SUP-3124) and verifies controller suppresses the fast-path for offending traces.
- Canary job: 5% traffic for 48h with shadowed metrics and automatic rollback if eval-regression > 3% relative.

Benchmarks:
- Internal microbench (measured on p3.8xlarge equivalent): baseline (no CLC): median=28ms, p95=72ms, p99=130ms, tokens/s=480K. With default balanced policy: median=29.5ms (+5%), p95=74ms (+2.8%), p99=96ms (-26%); tokens/s=455K (-5%). With correctness-first: median=31ms (+10%), p99=88ms (-32%). Eval-harness (10K prompts targeted at edge cases): baseline correctness-failure-rate=8.4%, balanced policy=2.9% (-65%), correctness-first=1.6% (-81%).

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag gated.
- Start with internal dedicated clusters, then 5% canary on Hosted API for 48h.
- If canary metrics good, 50% for 24h, then full rollout.
- Automatic rollback on canary if eval regressions or latency SLO violations (+p99 > 20% absolute).

Checklist:

- [x] Integration replay tests
- [x] Docs and runbook
- [x] Benchmarks attached

- [x] Security review (no new surface)

- 9d4c8b1: kv_cache staleness grace windows + metrics
- b2a9e0c: integration tests + replay harness
- c3f7f55: docs and canary manifests

Files changed (high level):

Merge outcome: "Merged via squash on main by Miguel Torres on 2025-02-08. Canary rollout configuration added to deployment manifests. No breaking API changes; default behavior is opt-in behind feature flag."

Known limitations and follow-ups: "1) The current output-diff signal is syntactic (token-level divergence) and can produce false positives for harmless rearrangements; follow-up ENG-8602 will add semantic eval sniffers. 2) We do not yet persist controller state across restarts; follow-up ENG-8603 will add lightweight state checkpointing. 3) Need dashboards for policy_flip_rate and fastpath_denied_ratio (ENG-8610)."

Context: Optimization config changes (batching/caching/quantization profiles) are production-impacting and must be traceable and reviewable. We’ve had gaps reported by enterprise customers (SUP-18544) and internal operators (INT-3390) where rollback actions were not consistently visible in audit exports, and some lifecycle steps were only logged in app logs. This PR standardizes and emits structured audit events for the full Optimization Config lifecycle and updates the audit schema registry accordingly. What’s included: (1) New/standardized event names under the "optimization_config" namespace: optimization_config.version_created, optimization_config.version_validated, optimization_config.apply_requested, optimization_config.rollout_started, optimization_config.rollout_paused, optimization_config.rollout_resumed, optimization_config.rollout_step_completed, optimization_config.rollout_failed, optimization_config.version_promoted, optimization_config.rollback_requested, optimization_config.rollback_completed, optimization_config.rollback_failed. (2) Consistent required fields across events: event_id, occurred_at, actor_type (user|service), actor_id, actor_email (when actor_type=user), actor_roles (best-effort snapshot), source (console|api|controller), request_id, trace_id (if present), tenant_id, scope (tenant/model/region; serialized as strings), optimization_config_id, optimization_config_version_id, from_version_id/to_version_id (when applicable), rollout_id (for staged apply), canary_percent (when applicable), reason (free-form operator reason; required for rollback_requested), gate_summary (serialized compact string: "latency_p95:pass;5xx:fail" etc.), eval_run_id (only for quantization-related applies where eval gating was invoked), and outcome (success|failure) with error_code/error_message when failure. (3) Explicit PII/secret handling: the audit payload does NOT include raw config bodies, prompt data, or customer inputs; the only config-related identifiers are config_id/version_id and a small "diff_fingerprint" (sha256 of normalized diff) for correlation. (4) Event emission points: service-layer emission in Optimization Config Service for create/validate/apply/promote/rollback API endpoints; rollout controller emits step/progression and gate evaluation results; rollback controller emits completion/failure. (5) Schema updates: updated audit schema registry entries for all new events, plus tightened validation rules for required fields and enums; added forward-compatible optional fields for private deployments (cluster_id, deployment_id) without making them required. (6) Backfill/compat: kept prior legacy event names as aliases for 30 days (emitting both) behind feature flag AUDIT_OPT_CONFIG_DUAL_EMIT; Console and downstream export pipelines continue to function. Example payload (redacted): {"event_name":"optimization_config.rollback_requested","actor_type":"user","actor_id":"u_7f...","actor_email":"oncall@redwoodinference.com","source":"console","tenant_id":"t_123","scope":"model=llama-3.1-70b;region=us-east-1","optimization_config_id":"ocfg_91...","optimization_config_version_id":"v_42","from_version_id":"v_43","to_version_id":"v_42","reason":"p95 regression during canary","request_id":"req_...","trace_id":"tr_..."}. Testing/verification: unit tests for event construction and schema validation; integration tests asserting audit emission on each endpoint; controller tests verifying pause/resume and failure paths emit the right events; manual verification in staging that events appear in SIEM-export sink with correct field names. Rollout plan: ship behind AUDIT_OPT_CONFIG_EVENTS_V1 (default off); enable for internal beta tenants first; after 1 week with no schema errors in export, disable dual-emit and remove aliases in follow-up PR. Checklist: [x] event taxonomy reviewed with Security (Marcus) [x] fields aligned with RBAC expectations (Jordan) [x] no raw config bodies logged [x] added docs snippet to internal audit-event catalog [x] added dashboard annotation hooks is tracked separately (observability-pack PR).
Marcus Lin: Please ensure we capture actor context consistently (actor_type/actor_id/actor_email) and include request_id + trace_id where available. Also confirm we’re not logging the raw config or any customer prompt data.
Kevin Osei: Added actor_type + actor_email (when present) across all events and plumbed request_id/trace_id from middleware. Confirmed payload only includes ids + diff_fingerprint; no raw configs/prompts are emitted. Added tests to prevent accidentally attaching config JSON.
Jordan Lee: Two asks: (1) Align field naming with RBAC bundle conventions (tenant_id, scope) and (2) ensure rollback is blocked unless reason is provided, since that’s required for auditability in enterprise change management.
Kevin Osei: Updated to tenant_id + scope string format (model=...;region=...). Rollback handler now requires reason (400 if missing) and we carry it into rollback_requested. Added a migration note that older clients must include reason (Console already does).
Benji Okafor: For staged rollout events, can we avoid emitting on every minor progress tick? We don’t want to spam audit sinks at high volume.
Kevin Osei: Good call. We emit rollout_step_completed only on shard boundary transitions and gate checkpoints (not per worker). Added a rate-limit guard to avoid duplicate step events when controllers retry.
Sean Gallagher: Make sure the outcome/failure events include a stable error_code so alerts/runbooks can key off it, and include rollout_id so SRE can correlate to dashboard annotations.
Kevin Osei: Added error_code enum (SCHEMA_VALIDATION_FAILED, SEMANTIC_VALIDATION_FAILED, GATE_FAILED, APPLY_TIMEOUT, RBAC_DENIED, CONFLICT) and ensured rollout_id is present for rollout/rollback controller events. Follow-up for dashboard annotations is in observability-pack; linking there.
Chloe Martin: Console relies on the audit feed to show "who did what" in history. Can we include source=console/api/controller consistently?
Kevin Osei: Yes—source is now set from request origin (console/api) and controllers use source=controller. Added a small helper to standardize it.
Audit log coverage added for optimization config lifecycle actions; events now include config_version + scope fields to support enterprise audit trails and incident forensics.

Motivation: in low-latency continuous-batching workloads we observed tail regressions when late-arriving KV-heavy requests starved smaller fast requests. This PR introduces the "flow-control conservator", a set of complementary scheduler heuristics to reduce starvation and stabilize p99 without sacrificing throughput. Key ideas: 1) late-queue guard: detect request cohorts that arrive near batch deadlines and limit their ability to evict ready slots unless they improve aggregate utilization; 2) soft-timeout amplification: when a request nears a soft timeout we accelerate slot admission and reduce coalescing for that cohort to preserve application-level SLOs; 3) aging score rebalance: incorporate an age/tokens composite score so small, latency-sensitive requests gain admission priority over long, KV-locked requests after a bounded wait; 4) KV-pin backoff: when a request holds a pinned KV cache entry and has already consumed multiple slots across retries, apply a probabilistic backoff to avoid repeated preemption of other work; 5) telemetry hooks and canary gating: new counters and traces allow gradual rollout and automatic rollback if throughput or e2e latency regress. Implementation summary: modified scheduler admission path to compute a conservative admission delta for late cohort members; added a soft-timeout fast-path that bypasses batching heuristics for at-most-N tokens when amplification conditions are met; added a token-aware age weight to the fairscore function; introduced a KV pin lease counter persisted on work descriptors and used by the admission filter to apply exponential backoff; wired feature flags and console metrics for rollout. Checklist: - [x] design doc (ENG-4821) updated - [x] unit tests for admission filter - [x] bench harness updated with KV-heavy and mixed profiles - [x] telemetry + dashboard wiring - [x] canary gating config - [x] upgrade notes and feature flag default off on stable clusters Deployment plan: land behind feature flag, enable for canary pool, observe p95/p99 and throughput for 48h, widen to 30% then full rollout. Rollback: flip feature flag; automated canary monitor will close flag on regressions. Why this is different from previous changes: rather than changing batch sizes or global timeouts, flow-control conservator focuses on per-request admission decisions and KV-aware backoffs so we avoid global throughput oscillations while removing starvation hotspots. Bench results (local perf-lab): mixed KV/short workload at 256-concurrency: baseline p99=210ms, mean=24ms; with conservator p99=150ms, mean=26ms; throughput delta -1.8% (within noise). Safety: defaults disabled in production; added regression tests that run in CI; feature flag named runtime.flow_control_conservator. Related: touches scheduling, kv cache behaviour, and batching flow; referenced prior thread on queue fairness (ENG-3120).
Marcus Chen: Nice direction. Two immediate asks: 1) can we avoid a potential oscillation when the soft-timeout fast-path repeatedly bypasses coalescing? Add a cooldown. 2) please spell out the safety/rollback steps in the PR body.
Ivy Navarro: Added a per-cohort cooldown and documented rollback steps in the description and deploy plan. Cooldown default 2s and gated via feature flag. Updated tests to cover cooldown behavior.
Lena Ortega: Please include a unit test that simulates repeated KV pin renewals to ensure backoff triggers. Also note that the metrics emit a new tag 'flow_control_cohort' which may have high cardinality; consider bucketing.
Ivy Navarro: Added the unit test and changed the tag to a low-cardinality bucketed tag (short|medium|long) as requested.
Ravi Malhotra: Bench numbers look promising. Request one more integration run at 4x concurrency to ensure no hidden tail. Also suggest an e2e smoke in canary.
Ivy Navarro: Queued the integration run and added canary smoke steps to the deployment plan.
a1b2c3d: initial implementation of admission filter and late-queue guard
d4e5f6a: add soft-timeout amplification fast-path and tests
b7c8d9e: KV pin lease counter and probabilistic backoff logic
f1e2d3c: telemetry hooks, console metrics, and feature flag wiring
c4b5a6d: bench harness scenarios and perf baseline updates
Merged after canary gating and second integration run passed. Feature flag off by default. Squash-merged to main.
Introduce flow-control conservator: late-queue guard, soft-timeout amplification, KV-pin backoff, and telemetry. Disabled by default; enable via runtime.flow_control_conservator feature flag.
1) enable feature on canary pool; 2) run mixed KV/short workload bench for 48h; 3) verify p99 improves and throughput within 5% of baseline; 4) monitor kv.pin_lease_backoff and flow_control_cohort bucket metrics; 5) rollback by disabling feature flag if regressions observed
