Motivation: We're seeing duplicated workflow logic across repos and inconsistent behavior for dependency bumps and license checks. This PR introduces a set of reusable CI workflow templates plus a lightweight policy-as-code gate using OPA to (a) enforce allowed dependency upgrades, (b) validate license/CLA metadata on dependency manifests, and (c) ensure lint/test matrices match supported runtimes. The goal is to reduce per-repo CI drift, centralize dependency policy, and make release automation safer via a post-merge canary run. What changed: - Added .github/workflow-templates/ci-template.yaml and release-template.yaml (reusable templates for presubmit/build/test and post-merge release checks). - Added .github/actions/opa-policy-check/ (composite action) which runs an opa eval against a bundled rego policy set and a small python helper to extract dependency candidates from package.json/Pipfile/requirements.txt. The action returns a non-zero exit and a structured message when policy violations are found. - Introduced policy rules: disallow deps with unknown licenses, prevent minor/major bumps for pinned security flagged packages without manual approval, and require dependency bump Linear reference in PR body. - Updated repo-specific workflows to use templates (redwood monorepo: .github/workflows/ci.yaml now instantiates ci-template and passes matrix parameters). - Simplified the test matrix: removed legacy Node 12/14 jobs, standardized to node 16/18 and python 3.9/3.11 where applicable. - Added a new release-phase job "post-merge-canary" to the release template that performs a smoke-run against staging endpoints with canary model routing enabled; failures trigger automatic rollback steps documented in the template. - Minor hygiene: CODEOWNERS additions for infra/*, updated .gitignore, and docs/policies/ci-dependency-policy.md documenting the rego rules and upgrade workflow. Migration notes: existing repos should switch to the templates by referencing the two files; a short migration script (scripts/migrate-to-templates.sh) is included to automate basic replacement. Tests and CI: Several CI runs initially failed due to the policy gate rejecting an unlicensed transitive dependency from a vendor package; I adjusted the rule to allow curated exceptions via policies/allowlist.json with comments pointing to the responsible team. All tests and e2e smoke checks passed on the final run. Related work: ENG-845 (CI consolidation), ENG-1290 (dependency policy).
Samir Kohli: This is a useful consolidation — can we ensure the opa composite action runs in an ephemeral container and doesn't leak credentials? Please add a note to the action README explaining inputs/outputs and required secrets.
Asha Patel: Added entrypoint.sh to run OPA eval in a minimal alpine container and documented required secrets (GITHUB_TOKEN only). Updated action README in this PR.
Maya Liu: The matrix change is good but a repo like redwood-model-registry still needs Node 14 for a legacy tool. Can we add an opt-in flag to the template so subsystems can opt into legacy runtimes?
Asha Patel: Added 'legacy-runtimes' template input and adjusted migration script to preserve explicit legacy matrix entries when present.
Jared Thompson: I saw a transient CI failure where the canary job hit a rate limit on staging; recommend retry/backoff logic in the smoke-run step.
Asha Patel: Added retry with exponential backoff and a 3-attempt limit for the post-merge canary step.
Introduce reusable CI workflow templates and an OPA-based dependency policy gate. Standardize test matrices (drop legacy Node 12/14 by default), add post-merge canary release job, and provide migration script and docs. Impact: improved CI consistency and automated policy enforcement for dependency updates.
When rolling out to other repos: 1) run scripts/migrate-to-templates.sh in a branch, 2) review policies/allowlist.json for repo-specific exceptions, 3) add infra owners to CODEOWNERS to handle policy exceptions. For incidents where OPA blocks an urgent security bump, toggle the policy by creating a small PR to policies/allowlist.json and reference ENG-1290.
Manual QA: ran migration script on redwood-examples and redwood-model-registry, executed template-driven CI in a feature branch, exercised post-merge canary against staging with model routing toggled. Automated: unit and integration tests included in template. No regressions observed.

Motivation: We continue to see downstream partial-JSON churn and fncall reordering when small SSE fragments arrive out-of-order or are interleaved with heartbeat delimiters. This causes user-visible truncated structured outputs and toolcall boundary mispairings in edge network conditions (mobile/poor NAT). This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: 1) offset compaction: a lightweight compaction ledger that coalesces adjacent tiny fragments in the in-memory fragment store before attempting final JSON reassembly, reducing reassembly thrash for high-fragmentation traces; 2) toolcall affinity heuristics: a pairing affinity window so function-call sentinel tokens are held and reassembled with preferred fragments rather than flushed when ambiguity exists. Additionally this change tightens delimiter anchoring rules so the parser prefers explicit sentinel anchors over ambiguous heartbeat delimiters during contention and introduces an idempotent reconnect checkpoint token emitted at a stable point in the stream to speed client resumption. Changes: - runtime/sse/framereader.go: add offset compaction map and compaction pruning based on configurable hysteresis (default 35ms) and size threshold to avoid waiting on long stalls. - runtime/sse/parser.go: introduce delimiter anchor preference ordering and affinity-aware reassembly path for fncall sentinels; add unit tests for ambiguous-delimiter sequences. - pkg/openai/compat/handler.go: emit reconnect checkpoint token and handle client resume requests; ensure compatibility with existing replay semantics. - internal/protocol/checkpoint.go: new idempotent token format and validation helpers. - tests/e2e/sse_stream_partial_json_test.go: new randomized fuzz cases that simulate interleaved heartbeats, reordered fragments, and mid-json splits; added deterministic seeds used in CI. - docs/streaming.md: document new hysteresis config and checkpoint semantics, and migration notes for Private deployments. Backwards compatibility: the reconnect checkpoint is opt-in via a small negotiation header to avoid surprising older clients; the default hysteresis is conservative to avoid added latency for well-behaved streams. Performance: microbenchmarks show a 28% reduction in reassembly retries and a 12% reduction in median tail latency for highly-fragmented traces in our lab harness. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for parser reassembly and delimiter anchoring - [x] e2e fuzz scenarios and deterministic seeds - [x] compatibility negotiation for checkpoint token - [x] documentation updates - [x] canary rollout plan in release notes Testing and rollout: CI runs include unit, integration, and the new e2e fuzz suite. We will ship as a staged canary: 5% hosted traffic for 24h, 25% for 48h, then 100% with automatic rollback on regression. Related work: builds on ENG-2142 (sse-cohesion-hysteresis) and ENG-2267 (fncall-order-preservation); incident SUP-9081 motivated the initial triage. Merge method: squash and merge with small follow-up hotfix expected for telemetry label normalization.
Diego Ramos: The hysteresis default (35ms) looks reasonable, but we need a flag for Dedicated customers to lower it — added a TODO for config path.
Aisha Patel: Can we avoid copying payloads in offset compaction hot path? Suggest using slice references with reference counting; author responded that a follow-up will add zero-copy path once the allocator refactor lands.
Lars Henriksen: Add telemetry counters for compaction hits/misses and affinity evictions. Author updated PR to emit compaction.{hit,miss} and affinity.evictions.
Security review (R. Nguyen): checkpoint token is signed and short-lived; confirm KMS use — author added validation and deterministic replay guards.
Introduce SSE offset compaction and toolcall affinity to reduce partial-JSON truncations and preserve function-call ordering under high-fragmentation networks. Opt-in reconnect checkpoint token for faster client resumption. Backwards-compatible by default. Configurable hysteresis (default 35ms) available for tailoring to customer needs.
Canary rollout scheduled; telemetry dashboard created in observability-pack to track compaction.* and affinity.evictions. Follow-up ticket ENG-2399 created to add zero-copy compaction path and Dedicated-tunable hysteresis.

Motivation: We need better visibility into high-cardinality token-level latency outliers that are currently masked by per-invocation aggregates. This PR introduces two complementary observability pieces: (1) token-latency-facet, a compact per-invocation histogram-rollup that captures token-phase latencies (prefix, decode, kv-lookup, kernel, network) with keyed facets for prompt-shape and model-variant; and (2) log-condenser, a lightweight event coalescer that attaches condensed log snippets and span anchors for the top-k slow tokens per invocation to reduce cardinality and noise while preserving debug context. Goals: enable SRE and runtime engineers to diagnose long-tail latency regressions quickly, surface token-level cost/latency correlations, and provide actionable alerting signals without exploding metric cardinality. What changed: - telemetry: added token_latency_facet histogram metric (labels: tenant_id, model_family, prompt_shape_bucket, token_phase) with compressed quantile rollups; added token_tail_count gauge to track number of tokens above phase-specific thresholds per invocation - tracing: span enrichment that attaches token_phase and facet_bucket tags to existing model-io spans and emits a compact token_anchor span for the slowest token per invocation - logging: log-condenser service that subscribes to the invocation event stream, samples top-k slow tokens, and produces a condensed payload (max 2 log lines + 3 surrounding tokens) written to a bounded artifact store; payloads are cross-referenced by token_anchor_id in traces - dashboards/alerts: new Token Latency Facet dashboard with phase heatmap, tenant-level top-k tails, and a Cost vs Latency scatter; alert rule updated to add token_tail_rate (auto-muted for low-volume tenants) and an adaptive dampener that uses sessionization to avoid alerting on single noisy invocations Backwards compatibility and performance: metric additions are additive; histograms use reservoir sampling and exponential decimation to keep cardinality and storage bounded. The log-condenser runs as an independently scaled service to avoid impacting request path. Rollout plan: staged feature-flag rollout (off by default) to 20% of tenants for 48 hours, evaluate token_tail_rate signal, then 100% with a 7-day quiet window. We will enable span enrichment for Dedicated clusters only during initial rollout. Testing: unit tests for histogram encoding and span tag propagation; integration run against synthetic heavy-invocation harness to validate throughput; e2e smoke on staging with sample dashboard panels. Motivation: Customers consistently ship suboptimal batching/cache/quant defaults per-route which increases per-token unit economics and causes unpredictable latency spikes. This PR introduces a lightweight, declarative 'Cost Broker' service and a quantization-profile linter to provide safe, auditable defaults and automated checks before rollout.

What this PR does (high level): Adds a Cost Broker component that consumes a small YAML policy (per-tenant/per-route selectors) and synthesizes recommended runtime defaults (batch size targets, KV-cache TTL/prefix heuristics, and quant profile hints). The broker is purely advisory by default and exposes: 1) rictl preview CLI (dry-run) 2) a control-plane API for safe-preview and apply 3) telemetry hooks for per-route unit-econ estimates. Also adds a standalone quant-profile linter that validates candidate quantization settings against service-level loss budgets (per-model tolerances) and rejects profiles likely to regress BLEU/QA metrics beyond configured thresholds.

Design notes: Policies are intentionally terse: selector + worklet. Selector matches by route regex, model family, and traffic class. Worklets are ordered and can emit overrides for batching, cache, and quant recommendations. Runtime respects that Cost Broker recommendations are tagged as 'advisory' until an operator flips 'applyMode' for a tenant. The linter runs as part of CI for quant-profile PRs and as part of the control-plane preview endpoint.

APIs and config: - pkg/costbroker/policy_schema.go: YAML schema and validator - cmd/rictl/cost-broker.go: preview/apply CLI - api/controlplane/costbroker/v1: preview/apply endpoints - infra/helm/cost-broker-values.yaml: defaults for installation

Telemetry and safety: Adds metrics (costbroker.recommendation.applied, costbroker.preview.estimate_usd_per_1k_tokens, quant.linter.rejects) and tracing spans. Recommendations include a delta estimate (expected USD change) and risk score (0-100). The linter emits a compact report with per-check violations and an aggregated risk score.

Testing and rollout plan: Unit tests for policy matcher and linter. E2E harness runs a synthetic workload against the preview endpoint and verifies that 'applyMode=false' leaves runtime unchanged. Rollout plan: feature-gate = off by default; gradual enabling via console + Linear task for first 5 tenants. Backout: Cost Broker changes are control-plane only and reversible; no runtime-breaking migrations.

Related: ENG-2543 implements the policy matcher proto; PM-87 defines the UX for preview/apply in Console.

Notes: Kept runtime surface minimal — runtime only reads final overrides from standard config path. Changes are designed to be conservative and operator-driven.

1) Add policy schema and parser (pkg/costbroker) 2) Implement preview/apply endpoints + CLI (cmd/rictl) 3) Add quant-profile linter and unit tests (tools/linter) 4) Hook telemetry and tracing (internal/telemetry) 5) Docs and example policies (docs/operations/cost-broker.md, examples/cost-broker) 6) Helm values and chart tweaks for optional install

Motivation: client sockets can silently drop (TCP RST, NAT timeouts, mobile backgrounding) which leads to duplicate tool/function calls or lost structured output when clients attempt an immediate reconnect. This PR introduces a server-side silent-disconnect detector, a short-lived rejoin token protocol for safe resume, and defenses to ensure tool/function calls remain idempotent across reconnects. Key behaviors: 1) Heartbeat/keepalive: server now tracks per-session last-activity and emits a 'quiesce' state after configurable grace_window (default 18s). 2) Rejoin token: on session creation the server issues a short-lived rejoin token bound to a session_id and lease; clients reconnecting present Rejoin-Token + Last-Event-ID to resume stream without reexecuting completed tool calls. 3) Tool idempotency ledger: function/tool calls now carry an Idempotency-Key; server persists call results for the token lease window and fences duplicate execution. 4) Buffered event replay: the server persists the final structured output envelope and last N events to replay to reconnecting clients, with integrity markers (sequence numbers + crc32) to detect mismatch. 5) Compatibility: OpenAI compatibility layer accepts Rejoin-Token via 'x-openai-rejoin-token' header and maps legacy 'last-event-id' query param. 6) Config: per-route conservative/aggressive reconnection policies and a feature-flag for rolling this out. The description below summarizes changes, tests, and rollout plan.
Diego: Please add a test that simulates rapid connect/disconnect to catch race window between quiesce and ledger eviction. Meera: We should not make the default lease > 30s without perf justification. Security: ensure token entropy and bind to session origin.
Author (Ava): Added a stress test in test_rejoin_idempotency.py and reduced default lease to 18s; reworked token to include origin fingerprint.
Diego: LGTM after addressing the stress test flake and a small refactor to the ledger removal path. Meera: approving, couple of doc nits fixed.
First CI run failed due to a timing-dependent e2e flake in test_rejoin_idempotency; increased test wait and added deterministic clock in the test harness; rerun passed.
Added graceful session quiesce detection and a Rejoin Token protocol for safer reconnects; clients can present x-openai-rejoin-token and last-event-id to resume streams without causing duplicate tool/function calls. Default rejoin lease is 18s and per-route policy controls are available. This reduces duplicated tool calls on flaky networks and improves streaming resilience.
Default off for 24h canary on prod, enable for 20% of traffic in region-us-west for 72h, monitor session.quiesced, toolcall.duplicate_rate, and reconnect.latency then proceed to 100% over one week; SDK releases provide opt-in helpers.

Summary: Adds a small, auditable decision-tree based suggester service that consumes recent tenant telemetry and workload shapes to recommend safe defaults for batching, prefix/KV cache window, and quantization profile tiers. Motivation: customers frequently ask for one-click recommendations that reduce token cost without regressing latency or quality. The heuristic presets in Optimize are useful but brittle for mixed workloads; this PR introduces an explainable decision tree that maps telemetry signatures (median seq length, 95th latency, KV hit rate, model family, CPU/GPU footprint) to conservative default profiles. Key design goals: 1) deterministic and auditable recommendations, 2) low-cost inference (rules only reference aggregated telemetry, no raw prompts), 3) safe fallbacks and explicit human-readable rationale, 4) incremental rollout and A/B telemetry. What changed (high level): new service under /services/econ-suggester, a small rules engine with exported rationale strings, a CLI dry-run mode for operators, and a set of unit tests and integration harness scenarios. The decision tree is intentionally shallow (max depth 4) and implemented as data (yaml nodes) to allow future non-destructive updates via config. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked - [x] unit tests for tree evaluation - [x] integration test that runs the suggester against replayed tenant traces - [x] telemetry metrics (suggester.recommendations, suggester.rationale_hash) - [x] CLI dry-run and export to JSON - [x] e2e smoke run on staging - [ ] docs: user-facing guidance and Console integration (follow-up PR) Related: Linear ENG-13023, ENG-13590, infra/ops runbook entry https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-13023 Decision rationale export (example): "tenant: acme-corp, model: rw-1-mt, median_seq: 128 -> recommend: small-batch(8, 32ms-prefill), cache_window: 16kb, quant: q4_0; rationale: 'median_seq between 64-256 and KV hit < 5% suggests short-context batchable calls; choose conservative quant with no red-team to avoid quality regressions'" Commits (summary): - add [econ-suggester] lightweight decision tree evaluator and config loader - add CLI dry-run + replay adapter for trace-based evaluation - export suggester metrics and rationale hash for telemetry - add unit + integration tests - add initial YAML configuration (shallow trees) - add ci matrix job for suggester tests Changed files (high level): - services/econ-suggester/{main.go, tree_evaluator.go, config.yaml} - pkg/telemetry/suggester_metrics.go - tools/suggester-cli/{main.go, README.md} - tests/integration/econ-suggester/{replay_fixtures, smoke_test.go} - deployment/staging/suggester.yaml - Makefile: add suggester test target Review summary: The approach intentionally avoids ML-in-the-loop for the first iteration and focuses on explainability and safe defaults. The output is a JSON recommendation plus an English rationale string suitable for Console display. CI: initial runs flagged a flaky replay test that depended on timing; fixed by adding a deterministic clock to the replay harness. CI status at merge: pass. Merge: squash and merge. Migration/rollout: staged rollout via feature flag (econ.suggester.enabled) and dry-run telemetry to measure uplift before enabling automatic adoption.

Motivation: Many tenants exhibit bimodal latency/cost tradeoffs where aggressive batching reduces unit cost but spikes tail latency for interactive routes. This PR implements an "efficiency-lattice" batch shaper that maintains per-tenant batch shape profiles (sequence-length distribution, prefilling ratio, tail-latency percentile targets) and performs a runtime handoff to tenant-specific quantized model variants when throughput vs quality/latency tradeoffs cross configured thresholds.

What changed (high level): - Introduces efficiency-lattice controller (runtime) to compute and apply batch shaping heuristics per-tenant. - Adds tenant-quantization handoff gating with safety checks (accuracy smoke checks, fallback window). - CLI tool redwood-econ-dryrun to simulate traffic traces against candidate batch/quant configs and produce unit-econ estimates and risk profiles. - Telemetry: new metrics (shaper.applied_profile, handoff.attempt, handoff.fallback_count, econ.estimated_cost_tokens) and dashboards in console. - Tests & infra: end-to-end smoke harness, deterministic simulator for CI, feature flag gating.

Why this is unique: Instead of a single global default the lattice supports multiple stable operating points and a decision boundary that chooses conservative vs aggressive shapes by workload signature. The quantization handoff is tenant-scoped and gated by short A/B validation and a warmstart period to limit regressions.

Checklist: - [x] Runtime: scheduling and batcher integration - [x] Safety: fallback path and revert logic - [x] CLI: dry-run mode and summary report - [x] Telemetry: metrics + dashboard skeleton - [x] Tests: simulator unit tests + e2e smoke - [x] Docs: developer guide + ops runbook

Testing performed: Ran redwood-econ-dryrun on three production-sampled traces (chat, search, summarization). Simulated 48-hour traffic windows with and without handoff. Observed median unit cost reduction 12%-18% on aggressive profiles with tail-latency P99 increase < 10ms for interactive tenants in conservative lattice bands. CI flake fixed (simulator seed handling).

Rollout plan: Feature-flagged rollout; step 1: internal beta (canary tenants), step 2: opt-in tenants via console, step 3: automated advisor recommends profiles for eligible tenants after 72h of stable telemetry. Manual rollback via feature flag or immediate fallback if handoff.fallback_count > 5 within 10m.

Related: Linear ENG-2930 (efficiency lattice design), ENG-3001 (economics CLI).

Motivation: Tenant KV memory pressure spikes and micro-fragmentation were causing noisy eviction storms and unpredictable tail latency. This PR introduces a clustered page-rewrite path plus an eviction-smoothing controller and a budgeted background compaction worker to reduce fragmentation and smooth spillover. Approach: 1) Add a clustered page-rewrite that groups small hot pages by tenant and rewrites them into contiguous slots to improve locality and reduce free-fragmentation; 2) Implement eviction-smoothing: instead of issuing large synchronous evictions under pressure, the controller issues paced eviction batches with tenant-aware watermarks and backpressure tokens to downstream spillers; 3) Introduce a budgeted-background-compaction worker that runs low-priority compaction (rewrite+free coalescing) during idle CPU/GPU windows and honors a configurable per-tenant IO/cpu budget; 4) Integrate hooks in the scheduler to prefer rewritten contiguous pages for kernel dispatch and KV cache lookups; 5) Expose runtime flags and per-tenant knobs for rollout. Benchmark summary: mixed generation workload (seq=512, batch=16) observed median token latency improvement ~7% and P95 improvement ~12% for high-fragmentation synthetic traces; background IO overhead capped at configured 5% by default. Migration & rollout: feature gated by "kv.clustered_rewrite" and "kv.evict_smoothing" flags; rollout plan uses canary on dedicated pools then gradual ramp. Risks & mitigations: background compaction may increase IO during peak—mitigated by budget throttle and tenant elevation; rollback via feature flag. Related: ENG-1248, ENG-1302. Checklist: [x] design doc updated; [x] unit and integration tests added; [x] perf bench harness updated; [x] feature flags added; [x] docs note added.

## Context
We’re refreshing AWS + GCP marketplace listings and moving to a new SKU catalog (Hosted/Dedicated/Private + add-ons). To support clean procurement paths and reduce onboarding/billing friction, the core billing catalog needs stable marketplace-facing SKU identifiers and an explicit mapping from marketplace dimensions -> internal meters.

This PR adds first-class `marketplace_sku_id` entries to the billing catalog and defines the authoritative mapping to internal meter keys used by the usage pipeline.

## What changed
- Adds `marketplace_sku_id` to billing catalog entries for all marketplace-eligible products (Hosted, Dedicated, Private, and add-ons).
- Introduces a `marketplace_dimension_mapping` table that maps:
  - provider (`aws` | `gcp`)
  - marketplace dimension name/id
  - Redwood `marketplace_sku_id`
  - internal meter key (what we actually record against)
- Adds validation to prevent:
  - duplicate `marketplace_sku_id`
  - dimension mapping referencing unknown catalog items
  - dimension mapping referencing non-metered catalog items
  - mismatched provider constraints (AWS uses dimension strings; GCP uses SKU/billing dimension pairs)
- Ensures backwards compatibility for existing direct-billed plans: no behavior change unless `billing_source == marketplace`.

## Why
- Avoids the class of issues where marketplace dimension names drift from internal meter keys (see SUP-4829).
- Makes metering reconciliation deterministic for Finance/RevRec (one place to audit).
- Unblocks docs + onboarding work that needs stable identifiers for “what did you buy?” and “what limits apply?”

## Rollout / operational notes
1) Deploy to staging with marketplace sandbox subscriptions enabled.
2) Validate end-to-end metering in staging using the entitlement verification endpoints (ENG-22110/PR-19875) and confirm the expected dimensions hit the correct internal meters.
3) Deploy to prod behind existing marketplace gating (no new customer impact unless subscription is marketplace).
4) Post-deploy: run the reconciliation job for 24h and confirm there are no unknown/uncategorized marketplace dimensions.

## Testing
- Unit tests for catalog schema validation and mapping validation.
- Integration test that loads the full catalog and asserts all marketplace SKUs have an internal meter mapping.

## Notes for reviewers
- Naming follows the guidance from Partnerships: stable, provider-agnostic IDs in the catalog, provider-specific mapping tables.
- If we need to rename any `marketplace_sku_id`, please call it out now—these IDs are meant to be durable across listing copy iterations.

Refs:
- Linear: ENG-22111, PM-1844
- Support: SUP-4829
- Related PRs: PR-19875 (entitlement verification), PR-19877 (telemetry events)
Nadia Rahman: Can we guarantee we won’t silently accept an unmapped marketplace dimension? That’s how we got into the mismatch issue last time.
Cole Summers (author): Updated `reconcile/marketplace-dimensions.ts` to emit `marketplace.dimension_unmapped` metric + error log with provider + dimension. Also added a test case that fails validation if mapping references an unknown meter key.
Priya Natarajan: Please keep marketplace IDs provider-agnostic. Don’t bake AWS/GCP into the SKU IDs; put provider-specific details only in the mapping files.
Cole Summers (author): Done. `marketplace_sku_id` is now `ri.hosted.payg`, `ri.dedicated.reserved`, etc. Provider-specific dimension strings moved to `dimension-mapping.*` files only.
Laura Bennett: From a finance perspective, can we export a single authoritative table for reconciliation? Ideally something deterministic for audit.
Cole Summers (author): Added `scripts/validate-billing-catalog.ts --print-marketplace-map` which prints a stable CSV view (provider, dimension, marketplace_sku_id, meter_key).
Emily Stone: Any change to revenue recognition treatment? Just confirming this is identifier/mapping only and not changing the underlying performance obligation definition.
Cole Summers (author): Correct—no pricing/terms changes, and no change to the internal meter semantics. This is a mapping + validation change to ensure marketplace dimensions resolve deterministically.

Motivation: We frequently onboard tenants with custom budget constraints and workload samples. Operators repeatedly hand-edit presets which leads to inconsistent defaults and unexpected unit-econ regressions. This PR adds a lightweight CLI and library that imports preset bundles, validates them, and produces deterministic tenant defaults and compact quant profiles to seed Redwood defaults for Dedicated/Private deployments.

What this PR does: adds a new CLI (redwood-econ-import) and a small library module (redwood.econ.importer) that: 1) accepts preset bundles as YAML/JSON; 2) validates against the econ-presets schema; 3) computes deterministic defaults by combining historical workload signatures (sample weights) with tenant budget constraints; 4) synthesizes compact quantization profile templates (float16/8-bit presets) tuned for target tail latency; 5) emits a migration-ready JSON bundle and optionally applies to a tenant via an admin API.

Design notes and constraints: deterministic defaults are produced using a seeded weighted sampler so repeated runs with the same inputs are reproducible; the quant templates are small (<= 6 entries) and purposely conservative to avoid quality regressions; telemetry events are emitted at import/time-of-apply for auditing and rollback. CLI includes a --dry-run and --explain flags to aid reviews.

Checklist:
- [x] CLI and library implementation
- [x] Schema and validator tests
- [x] Unit tests for weighted sampler determinism
- [x] Integration test (dry-run) against staging API
- [x] Docs and quickstart in /docs/econ-importer.md
- [x] Telemetry hooks and feature flag gating

payload.body:
Motivation: We observed that real-world request lengths and prompt distributions at scale are highly asymmetric (many short queries interleaved with occasional long contexts). Existing tiled attention kernels assume symmetric tiling or fall back to a slower generic path when shapes are irregular, which hurts p99 latency and throughput for mixed workloads. This PR introduces a new microstrip attention pipeline that supports asymmetric tile sizes, combined with a fused rope/rotary optimizer to reduce operator overhead and memory traffic. The patch also adds scheduler hints for continuous batching and a KV cache eviction heuristic that prefers compacting hot prefixes ahead of eviction to reduce cache misses.

What changed (high-level):
- New kernel: runtime/attn/microstrip_kernel.cu implements the microstrip attention path. It tiles Q/K/V in variable-width microstrips, enabling efficient vector loads for short and medium sequences without paying the cost for full-tile padding.
- Fused rope/rotary: runtime/attn/fused_rope.cpp and fused_rope.cu implement a single fused CUDA kernel that applies rotary embedding, rope remapping for legacy models that use 'rope swap' patterns, and a precision-aware accumulation stage to maintain fp16 stability at long sequences.
- Prefetch scheduler: runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.cc adds a prefetch hint generator that informs the microstrip kernel about likely next-prefix lengths to reduce KV cache latency on continuous streams. The scheduler integrates with existing autoscaling hints and has a config knob to opt in per-model.
- KV eviction heuristic: runtime/kv_cache/evict_policy.cc updates the eviction logic to attempt hot-prefix compaction before evicting whole shards; adds metrics (kv.evictions.compactions, kv.evictions.fallbacks).
- API/test/benchmarks: benches/bench_microstrip.py and tests/attn_microstrip_test.cpp with deterministic microbench harness for typical Redwood workloads. Performance regression guard added to CI.

Compatibility and fallbacks:
- The microstrip path is guarded behind device capability checks and a runtime flag (ATTN_MICROSTRIP_ENABLED). On unsupported devices we automatically route to the existing tiled path. A runtime assertion ensures behavioral parity for short sequences in debug builds.

Benchmarks (summary):
- Mixed short/long workload (80% <= 128 tokens, 20% up to 2k tokens) on A100-40GB: throughput +28% for generation throughput (tokens/sec) at median latency, p99 latency down by 14% compared to mainline fused-flash kernel; cost-per-token reduction ~9% due to fewer wasted loads and better KV locality.
- Long-only workloads (>1k tokens): parity with existing fused-flash kernel (within 2%).

Checklist:
- [x] Kernel correctness tests (unit + randomized)
- [x] Numerical stability tests (accumulation checks vs baseline)
- [x] Benchmarks and perf dashboards updated
- [x] CI regression guard
- [x] Documentation comment blocks in critical files

References: Linear ENG-1482 (microstrip kernel), ENG-1620 (continuous batching hints). Related PRs: earlier rope/rotary fusion efforts (see PRs in the repo history) but this is a distinct microstrip design and introduces the KV compaction heuristic.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the memory model in microstrip_kernel.cu (comments explain data layout) and the interaction between the scheduler hints and eviction policy. I left the tuning constants (MICROSTRIP_MIN_WIDTH, PREFETCH_LOOKAHEAD) as config flags in runtime/config/attn_flags.h for easier experimentation.

Migration notes: default behavior unchanged. Operators who want to enable the new path can set the runtime flag or allow the autotuner to enable it when device caps match.

Risks: the most likely risk is subtle differences in fp16 accumulation for extremely long sequences; extensive tests were added and a debug parity check is enabled in dev builds.

Diego Ruiz (2026-02-16): Interesting approach, can you clarify how microstrip aligns with warp-bound loads? Request: add comments on coalescing strategy.

Ava Morgan (2026-02-16): Added detailed comments in microstrip_kernel.cu and included a small microbenchmark that measures coalescing efficiency (bench_microstrip.py).

Leah Patel (2026-02-19): CI failed on Windows GPU runner (link to CI). Looks like build flag missing for fused_rope.cu.

Ava Morgan (2026-02-20): Fixed build flags in CMakeLists.txt and added an ifdef to guard host-only compilation. Reran CI.

Mina Chen (2026-02-23): Requested a fallback test demonstrating parity for sequences < 256 tokens.

Ava Morgan (2026-02-24): Added parity unit that runs in debug builds and an automated randomized check in tests/attn_microstrip_test.cpp.

Diego Ruiz (2026-02-26): Approved after a final run of perf benchmarks.

Leah Patel (2026-02-27): Approved.

- Added microstrip attention kernel for asymmetric tiling and improved mixed-workload throughput
- Fused rope/rotary kernel to reduce operator overhead and improve fp16 stability
- Scheduler prefetch hints for continuous batching and KV cache compaction heuristic
- No behavioral breaking changes; feature is opt-in via ATTN_MICROSTRIP_ENABLED
payload.title: Introduce microstrip-attn pipeline with asymmetric-tile prefetch and fused-rope optimizer

Context and motivation: We continue to see rare but high-impact partial promotions during multi-stage rollouts where in-flight sessions or transient backpressure cause a promoted cohort to observe diverging behavior. Earlier mitigations (shorter hold windows, noisy-metric smoothing) reduced incidence but did not provide a deterministic handoff path for sessions already in-flight. This PR introduces a traffic-fencing handoff state and a replay safeguard so that staged promotes either complete deterministically or can be rolled back and replayed to validate correctness before full promotion.

What this changes (summary): Adds a fencing state machine and a replay buffer adapter to the rollout conductor, wiring to metrics and tracing, test coverage, and a conservative default policy. The change is intentionally opt-in via rollout.policy.fencing.enabled=false to avoid altering current production rollouts until staged adoption. Key user-visible behaviors: 1) During a phased handoff, cohorts are fenced (new sessions routed using fence tokens), 2) in-flight sessions are tracked and quiesced to a consistent snapshot, 3) if anomaly gates trigger, the fence can be closed and the replay buffer used to simulate promotion offline before retry.

Implementation notes (high level): - New state: FENCE_OPEN -> FENCE_HOLD -> PROMOTE/REPLAY/ROLLBACK. - Fence token generation and propagation added to the API gateway routing layer (redwood-gateway) and the routing table. - Lightweight replay buffer persists ids + request prefixes + KV-cache footprints for up to 30 minutes; a replay adapter can replay traffic against a candidate model in a sandboxed backend. - Added metrics: rollout.fence.open_count, rollout.fence.quiesced_sessions, rollout.replay.success_rate, replay.latency_p95. - Safety defaults: fencing requires canary_success_ratio >= 0.98 for auto-promotion; otherwise operator-driven promote after manual verification.

Files changed (high level): - services/conductor/rollout_state_machine.go (adds fencing states and transition guards) - gateway/routing/fence_tokens.go (token lifecycle, propagation) - sandbox/replay/adapter.go (sandbox replay runner + KV footprint handling) - console/rollouts_ui/fence_modal.tsx (console control to inspect fence state + replays) - metrics/registrations.go (new metrics) - test/integration/fence_replay_test.go (end-to-end test covering quiesce+replay paths) - charts/values.yaml (flag to enable fencing and default TTLs)

Commits (summary): - 8f3b2d1: introduce fencing state machine and guard logic - 2d7c4a9: gateway token propagation and routing changes - b1f6e03: replay buffer implementation and sandbox runner - 4caa9e0: console UI for fence inspection and replay controls - 9eab447: metrics and tests + config flags - dff12a6: docblocks and rollout policy defaults

Review thread (condensed): - Connor Li (reviewer): "Overall strong. Please ensure the replay buffer cannot leak PII; add an explicit scrub step and a proof-of-concept scrub unit test." - Author (Maya): "Added request scrub hook and unit test (test/scrub_test.go). The scrub is pluggable and defaults to header and body key whitelist." - Priya Natarajan (SRE): "How does fencing interact with autoscaling? If we quiesce sessions for 30s we might spike memory on the host." - Author: "Fencing keeps only request prefixes and KV-cache footprints (not full responses). We also added a TTL and a memory cap per-host; when cap is reached the conductor will prioritize replay to disk and signal a 'deferred_replay' metric. Notes added to design doc." - Jasper Holt (SEC): "Confirm replay runs in a sandboxed network namespace with no egress to prod resources." - Author: "Replay runner is an isolated sandbox with strict egress rules. Added network isolation integration test in sandbox/replay/sandbox_test.go."

CI and test results: - Unit tests: pass - Integration tests (fence_replay_test) initially flaky on CI runner; rerun succeeded. - E2E smoke in staging: pass with two manual promotons. - Lint/format: pass. Overall ci_status: pass.

Backward compatibility and rollout: - Backwards compatible: fence tokens are optional; older gateways ignore unknown token headers. - Default is disabled; rollout via feature flag; we recommend enabling in a single region per-customer and monitoring rollout.fence.* metrics for 72h before global enabling.

Performance and cost: Replay buffer is bounded and uses an LRU spill-to-s3 path when per-host in-memory cap is reached. We measured a median additional memory of ~3.4MB/host for a 5-minute fence TTL in internal load test (see bench/notes).

Related work and Linear tickets: ENG-2140 (design), ENG-2311 (sandbox replay runner), ENG-2367 (gateway token work).

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals from Connor and Priya and an explicit security signoff from Jasper. Post-merge tasks: ship rollout policy docs and notify Platform SRE about the feature flag window.

Checklist: - [x] Design documentation updated - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Metrics and alerts added - [x] Console controls wired - [x] Security review

If you want to try this locally: enable rollout.policy.fencing.enabled=true in charts/values.local.yaml, deploy conductor + gateway, and run test/integration/fence_replay_test.go.

Add opt-in traffic-fencing handoff with replay safeguard to improve deterministic promotions. Disabled by default; see rollout.policy.fencing.enabled.

payload.body:
Motivation: We observed intermittent SLO violations during short-lived multi-region traffic spikes where existing load-shedding and circuit-breaker heuristics either over-ejected tenants or caused thrashing when capacity returned. This PR introduces a TemporalSurgeArbiter: a conservative, time-aware request prioritizer that smooths transient spikes using weighted fairness and exposes a safe rollback path when sustained SLO pressure is detected.

What this changes (single-string summary): Adds a new runtime component (TemporalSurgeArbiter) that sits between the router and node scheduler. It maintains per-tenant ephemeral tokens (surge credits) that decay over a configurable window, applies a weighted-fairness algorithm that combines tenant priority and recent acceptance rate, and attaches a graceful rollback hook that triggers progressive relaxations to avoid mass evictions. The arbiter integrates with the existing SLO enforcer and circuit manager so it can shift from conservative throttling to soft-relaxation (grace window) when health probes indicate recovery.

Key features: 1) Weighted fairness by tenant token budgets and recent latency/errored-token feedback. 2) Temporal decay of surge credits (configurable half-life) to prevent long-term state accumulation after spikes. 3) Soft-rollback path: when SLO violations persist beyond a configured window, the arbiter progressively relaxes thresholds and signals the circuit manager to increase retry headroom instead of immediately widening routes. 4) Backpressure-safe: the arbiter returns clear Retry-After semantics and integrates with client hedging policies. 5) Config-gated rollout behind feature flag surge_arbiter_v1 and runtime config in /etc/redwood/arbiter.yaml.

Compatibility and migration: Backwards compatible by default; the arbiter is disabled unless the feature flag is enabled. Migration steps in the console: enable feature flag for a pilot tenant, monitor slo:request_p99_latency and slo:served_ratio, then enable at region-level. If rollback is needed, disable the feature flag to revert to previous behavior.

Implementation notes: TemporalSurgeArbiter is implemented as a lightweight in-memory controller in serving/runtime/arbiter. It uses a fixed-size LRU for tenant entries to bound memory and a lock-free sampling queue for fairness scoring to minimize added latency. We added telemetry (metrics: arbiter.accepted, arbiter.rejected, arbiter.rollback_steps, arbiter.token_decay_rate) and traces in the request path (span:arbiter.evaluate). The arbiter exposes a gRPC health endpoint for cross-region probes.

Performance results (benchmark-lab): On synthetic spikes (2x baseline QPS for 45s) in the lab we saw p99 latency improvements of ~18% for high-priority tenants and net reduction in eviction events by ~42% versus current soft-evict policy. Cost overhead measured at ~0.9% CPU on serving nodes and sub-0.5ms median added latency in critical path.

Hotfix included: race condition fix in circuit-manager state transitions (fixes a double-commit on fast-reconnect) and a metrics naming bug that hid rollback step counts in older dashboards.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for scoring and decay (serving/runtime/arbiter/*_test.go). Integration tests: staged canary in perf-canary with 3 regions, automated chaos run (simulated node drains) passed. Manual runbook validated rollback path and failure mode (see testing/arbiter-canary-runbook.md).

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-482 linked)
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] Telemetry added and dashboards draft updated
- [x] Feature flag gating and runtime config present
- [x] Compatibility/migration notes written
- [x] Hotfix race condition verified

Rollout plan: 1) Enable for 5 pilot tenants in us-west with observability alerting on slo:served_ratio drop >1% over baseline. 2) Monitor 48 hours, adjust token half-life. 3) Gradual region-by-region enablement with automatic rollback on persistent SLO degradation.

Asha Raman: Overall this is promising. Two requests: can we make the token decay half-life configurable per-tenant (or at least per-tenant-class)? Also add a short note about memory bounds for the LRU in the design doc.
Evan Park (author): Good point — added tenant-tier multiplier and documented LRU sizing. Implemented limit to 10k tenant entries by default and added config entry for override.
Luca Meyer: The scoring math looks fine but please add a small comment explaining the tie-breaker (use timestamp) so future maintainers understand determinism.
Evan Park: Added comments and unit tests asserting deterministic ordering for equal scores.
Priya Kapoor: CI flaked on the first run due to test timeout in the perf harness; re-ran and all checks passed. Approving pending minor doc tweak on rollout steps.
Evan Park: Updated the rollout in docs to include explicit Saga-style rollback triggers and monitoring thresholds.
payload.title: Temporal surge arbiter with weighted fairness and rollback path

Motivation: CI feedback time has regressed as the monolithic workflow runs more heavy integration tests for every PR. This PR introduces a layered/staged CI model: very fast path-aware lanes for lint + unit tests that run on push and PRs (fast-feedback), a medium lane (integration smoke) that runs on PRs but can be cached/queued, and heavy/nightly lanes for long-running end-to-end suites. Additionally, this adds a small tool (DepCurator) that scans workspace dependency graphs to propose candidate removals, flag oversized transitive deps, and annotate PRs with potential savings. The goal is to speed developer feedback, reduce CI resource waste, and give engineering teams automated guidance for dependency pruning. Changes in this PR include: - New .github/workflows/ci-fastpath.yml: path-aware triggers and targeted job matrix. - New .github/workflows/ci-staged.yml: staged lane orchestration with gates and artifact annotations. - tools/dep-curator/: TypeScript scanner action + CLI for local runs. - scripts/ci/affected-packages.ts: faster change detection vs previous workspace scan. - docs/ci/README.md: guidance for adding new modules to fast-lanes and running DepCurator locally. - Dockerfile.ci: small build image tuned for the TS actions to reduce cold-starts. Migration plan: fast-lanes enabled by default for packages in /packages/* and service directories that include a CI fastpath tag in package.json; teams can opt-in/out via .ci-config.yml. DepCurator runs as an optional check and will initially report suggestions (no automated removals). Follow-ups planned: (1) wire DepCurator suggestions to an internal RFC pipeline for safe removals, (2) add license/size gating for release lanes, (3) expose fast-lane metrics in the console. Checklist: - [x] Implement path-aware fast-lane action - [x] Implement staged orchestration and annotated caches - [x] Add DepCurator action and CLI - [x] Update docs and runbook - [x] Run internal dogfood for 48h and iterate Observability: the CI changes produce annotations with estimated tokenized cache sizes and a new metric ci.fastlane.latency in telemetry (sampled) to help tune thresholds. Rollout: merged to main behind feature flag CI_LAYERED_FASTLANES=on.
Maya Rangan: Nice separation — can you clarify how flakes in the medium lane bubble back to the PR author?
Diego Morales: We added an annotation on the PR and a retry job link; medium lane failures produce a single condensed trace and a re-run button in the workflow to avoid noise.
Ethan Brooks: DepCurator looks promising — how do we avoid false positives for optional peer deps?
Diego Morales: DepCurator currently checks package.json/requirements.txt and the lockfile; it marks candidates as 'suggested' and includes context (import counts) to reduce noise. We will add a peer-deps heuristics follow-up.
Sofia Ivanov: CI image bump seems safe but please include the smaller Dockerfile.ci note in the release notes.
Maya Rangan: Approving after nitfixes to action inputs (verified) — LGTM.
Introduce layered CI (fast/medium/nightly) with path-aware fast-lanes and an initial DepCurator dependency suggestion tool. Improves PR feedback latency and surfaces dependency pruning candidates. No behavioral changes to runtime; opt-in controls available via .ci-config.yml.
This PR intentionally keeps DepCurator non-blocking for the first rollout. Teams will receive annotations and can run the CLI locally. The follow-up will wire safe removal automation behind an approval workflow and add stricter gating for release lanes.
payload.title: Introduce staged CI fast-lanes and DepCurator dependency scan

payload.body:
## Context
Support and customers currently see the same 429 for multiple distinct conditions (quota exceeded, per-minute rate limiting, and new overload shedding / admission control paths). During incidents/bursts this makes it hard to: (a) give correct retry guidance, (b) separate "expected" best-effort shedding from true quota misconfig, and (c) correlate customer complaints with fleet protection triggers.

This PR standardizes 429 semantics (headers + error payload fields) so clients, Support, and on-call can distinguish:
- Quota window exhaustion (account/org quota)
- Rate limit (token bucket / rps) enforcement
- Overload shedding / admission control (capacity protection)

Related: ENG-4922 (tier-aware rate limiter), ENG-4924 (routing admission control). This PR is intentionally scoped to response/reporting so we can ship reason-code clarity ahead of the full GA rollout.

## What changed
### 1) Standard 429 reason taxonomy
Introduces a small, versioned set of reason codes:
- `quota_exceeded` (quota window exceeded)
- `rate_limited` (token bucket / request rate limit)
- `overload_shed` (request rejected due to fleet pressure / admission control)
- `route_budget_exhausted` (per-route budget for the tier depleted)
- `tier_throttled` (best-effort tier throttled due to priority protection)

### 2) Response headers
Adds the following headers to all gateway-generated 429s (and normalizes when upstream returns a 429 without them):
- `x-redwood-error-code`: always `rate_limited` for HTTP 429 (consistent top-level code)
- `x-redwood-429-reason`: one of the reasons above
- `retry-after`: set when we have a meaningful value (quota window remaining, or configured min backoff for overload)
- `x-redwood-request-id`: ensured to be present for all 429 paths (some early-return paths skipped this)

We continue to emit existing `x-ratelimit-*` headers where applicable (no removal).

### 3) Error payload normalization
Ensures the JSON error body includes a stable `code` and a human-readable message that matches the reason:

Example:
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate_limit_error",
    "code": "overload_shed",
    "message": "Request was throttled due to temporary capacity protection. Retry with exponential backoff.",
    "request_id": "req_..."
  }
}

Notes:
- We did not change the HTTP status code (still 429).
- We did not change which requests are admitted or rejected; only classification + messaging.

### 4) Deterministic logging for support escalation
Adds a structured gateway log field `throttle.reason` and `throttle.retry_after_s` so on-call can quickly answer: "is this quota, or overload?" without reading free-form strings.

## Files / areas touched (high level)
- `services/api-gateway/middleware/throttle_response.ts`: new reason mapping + header writer
- `services/api-gateway/middleware/quota.ts`: propagate quota window retry-after into normalized response
- `services/api-gateway/middleware/admission_control.ts`: set `overload_shed` / `tier_throttled` on reject paths
- `services/api-gateway/openapi/error_schemas.yaml`: updated 429 error code docs + examples
- `services/api-gateway/tests/integration/throttle_reasons.spec.ts`: coverage for each reason + headers

## Test plan
- Added integration tests for each reason that assert:
  - HTTP 429
  - `x-redwood-429-reason` is set and correct
  - `x-redwood-request-id` always present
  - `retry-after` present when applicable
- Manually verified in staging:
  - quota exhaustion path via forced small test quota
  - overload path via admission control test flag (internal only)

## Rollout / compatibility
- Backwards compatible: clients that only look at 429 continue to work.
- New behavior is additive (new headers + stable code strings).
- Docs updates for customers will land in a separate docs PR (Wei/Elliot are tracking in ENG-4930).

## Follow-ups
- Wire `route_budget_exhausted` reason from routing service (currently only gateway-originated budgets emit it).
- Ensure Console surfaces these reasons in internal operator view (tracked separately).

Refs:
- Jira: SUP-18421 (customer confusion during rollout), SUP-18462 (streaming termination confusion; separate fix PR)
- Project: Hot-route capacity protection
- Hosted API: 429 responses now include standardized reason codes and headers that distinguish quota limits from overload shedding.
- No behavior change to enforcement in this PR; this is response semantics + logging only.
Jordan Lee (requested changes): Can we keep the top-level `x-redwood-error-code` stable and put the detailed classification in a separate header? Some internal tooling keys off `rate_limited` today.
Amara Diallo (author): Yep—updated to always use `x-redwood-error-code=rate_limited` for HTTP 429 and added `x-redwood-429-reason` for the detailed code. Also ensured JSON payload `error.code` matches the reason.
Dev Patel: Please make sure Support can tell customers exactly what to do. Can we include explicit retry guidance in the message for overload vs quota?
Amara Diallo (author): Added reason-specific messages (quota: "increase quota or wait", overload: "retry with exponential backoff"). Also ensured `retry-after` is set when we have a concrete value.
Logan Wright: Any risk of high-cardinality logging here? Please avoid logging tenant IDs in the throttle log line.
Amara Diallo (author): Logs only include reason + retry_after_s + request_id and route group; tenant/account identifiers remain in existing auth log context (unchanged). No new high-cardinality dimensions added.
Kaitlyn Nguyen: Header naming: prefer `x-redwood-429-reason` vs `x-redwood-throttle-reason`? Consistency with other error headers matters.
Amara Diallo (author): Settled on `x-redwood-429-reason` to be explicit and avoid ambiguity with non-429 throttling. OpenAPI examples updated accordingly.

payload.body:
## Summary
This PR adds the backend API powering the Console “Optimization Config History” / timeline UI. It exposes a stable, paginated feed of optimization config lifecycle events (create/validate/apply/pause/promote/rollback) with filtering by scope (tenant, model, region), actor, and status.

Primary goals:
- Enable the Console timeline view + diff navigation to reliably load for large tenants.
- Keep queries predictable and fast (keyset pagination, stable ordering, sensible indexes).
- Ensure auditability (all entries link back to audit events / request IDs) without requiring Console to query the audit log service directly.

## API
### New endpoint
`GET /internal/console/optimization-config/history`

Query params:
- `tenant_id` (required)
- `model` (optional)
- `region` (optional)
- `scope` (optional; one of `tenant|model|region|deployment`) — used by UI for grouping
- `action` (optional; e.g. `APPLY|PROMOTE|ROLLBACK|VALIDATE|CREATE`)
- `status` (optional; `STARTED|SUCCEEDED|FAILED|PAUSED`)
- `actor` (optional; partial match on email/subject)
- `from` / `to` (optional; RFC3339)
- `limit` (optional; default 50, max 200)
- `cursor` (optional; opaque)

Response shape:
- Items are returned in descending time order.
- Pagination uses keyset pagination with `(occurred_at, id)` to ensure deterministic ordering under concurrent writes.
- Each item includes: `history_id`, `occurred_at`, `action`, `status`, `config_id`, `config_version`, `previous_config_version` (when applicable), `scope` + `scope_ref`, `actor_subject`, `actor_email` (if available), `request_id`, `rollout_id` (if applicable), and `summary`.

Notes:
- This is currently an *internal* endpoint behind Console auth and RBAC checks. A public customer-facing history endpoint is tracked separately (PM-903 follow-up for exposure/field redaction).

## Implementation details
### Data source
We aggregate from `optimization_config_change_log` (control plane) which is already emitted by the apply controller + rollback endpoint. Console needs a timeline across actions with minimal joins.

### Pagination
- Implemented as keyset pagination rather than offset pagination to avoid O(n) scans for large datasets.
- Cursor encodes: `occurred_at` + `id` + filters hash to prevent cursor reuse across mismatched filters.

### Filters
- All filters are optional except `tenant_id`.
- `model` and `region` filters are applied as exact matches.
- `actor` filter is a case-insensitive search against `actor_email` and `actor_subject` (bounded to prefix match for index friendliness; see below).

### Performance tuning
- Added covering indexes to keep the common paths fast:
  - `(tenant_id, occurred_at DESC, id DESC)`
  - `(tenant_id, model, occurred_at DESC, id DESC)`

Motivation: During a cross-region capacity crunch we observed coordinated drain+failover waves that amplified latency SLO violations. This change introduces a 'soft evacuation' orchestrator that performs a windowed, priority-aware drain of traffic from impacted nodes/regions instead of hard preemptive evictions. The orchestrator cooperates with an updated priority-windowed shedder that applies gradual, time-boxed shedding to low-priority routes/tenants while preserving higher SLO buckets. Goals: reduce cascading failovers, keep higher-priority customers within SLO, and provide measurable recovery telemetry during evacuation windows. Changes in this PR: 1) Add soft evacuation controller (control-plane) that signals a staged drain with adjustable window, ramp and cooldown parameters. 2) Implement priority-windowed-shedder in serving runtime to apply graceful degradation per-request based on tenant priority, recent error budget, and evacuation state. 3) Telemetry: new evacuation.span and shedder.window metrics and traces; automated alerts for window overrun. 4) Safety: fail-open config and an emergency-bypass to disable soft-evacuation per region. 5) Docs and runbook: operational guide for triggering soft-evacuation and interpreting telemetry. Related: ENG-7842 (post-incident mitigation), ENG-7901 (shedder design doc), SUP-4128 (customer incident). This description includes implementation rationale, rollout plan, and validation notes. Rollout plan: staged Canary -> regional opt-in -> global rollout, with a feature flag and default off for existing clusters. Validation: synthetic load tests and real-world canary showed 35-60% fewer cross-region handoffs and reduced p90 latency spikes by ~22% under simulated degradation. Backwards compatibility: control plane will ignore older agents; serving runtime gracefully no-ops when feature flag is off. Manual rollback: disable flag and trigger immediate graceful stop. See release notes for operator-visible changes.
Maya Chen: Nice design. Two asks: (1) Add a hard guard that aborts windowed shedding if critical health markers increase (CPU, queue length) beyond X; (2) please include unit tests covering concurrent policy refresh.
Arjun Patel: Addressed both. Added a health-guard check in controller.go and new concurrency tests in policy_eval_test.go (see commit f0d1a2b).
Luis Ortega: Concern about telemetry cardinality from per-tenant windows. Suggest aggregating per-priority-bucket and sampling per-tenant only when windowed-shedder escalates.
Arjun Patel: Updated evacuation_metrics.go to emit priority_bucket aggregates by default and rare per-tenant samplers behind a flag.
Priya Raman: Can we make the default window conservative (30s ramp, 2m hold, 1m cooldown)? Also request a short e2e showing rollback path.
Arjun Patel: Default parameters set to 30s/2m/1m. Added an e2e script and CI job to simulate canary rollback; documented in runbook.
Operator-visible: adds a feature-flagged soft-evacuation controller and a priority-windowed shedder. Default behavior is disabled. When enabled, soft-evacuation performs staged, priority-aware traffic shedding to prevent cascading region failovers. New metrics: evacuation.span, shedder.window, shedder.priority_aggregates. Rollback: disable feature flag for the region to stop new windows and let existing windows cooldown. See docs/ops/soft-evacuation-runbook.md for playbook.

Motivation: Continuous-batcher workloads have exhibited intermittent KV-pin starvation where long-lived KV-heavy requests repeatedly preempt short requests due to deterministic dequeue ordering. This causes tail latency spikes for small requests and degrades 95th/99th percentile SLOs. This PR introduces an adaptive dequeue backoff algorithm and a lightweight starvation score metric to smooth fairness without sacrificing throughput.

What this PR does: Adds an adaptive 'dequeue backoff' policy that injects a variable delay/jitter when a queue has consumed consecutive slots beyond an expectation threshold. The backoff duration is proportional to a starvation_score computed from queue hold-time, recent slot usage, and KV-pin weight. The policy is kernel-aware (hints to the runtime when large kv- pinned workloads are present) so the scheduler can prefer low-KV lanes under tight latency SLOs.

Design summary: - starvation_score: rolling counter decayed over 10s window combining (consecutive_slots, avg_exec_ms, kv_pin_weight) - backoff calculation: min_backoff + log(1 + starvation_score) * scale, jittered to avoid synchronization - kernel hints: continuous_batcher exposes light/heavy hints; the kernel scheduler can favor different execution kernels or quantized paths for heavy requests - config: new config block continuousBatcher.adaptiveBackoff with tunables and a safety cap to avoid starving throughput-critical lanes.

Testing & validation: Unit tests for backoff math and starvation score decay. Integration test that replays real production traces (small/large mix) showing reduced 99th latency for short requests. Benchmarks on p4d: baseline vs this change with mixed workload (75% small, 25% kv-heavy): 99th latency for small requests reduced from 312ms -> 188ms (40% improvement) with <2% throughput regression.

Rollout plan: Feature-flag gated, gradual canary by region: 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Observability added: continuous.batcher.backoff_ms, continuous.batcher.starvation_score, continuous.batcher.backoff_count. Alert added to SLO dashboard to detect regressions (increase in mean backoff_ms > 20% on canary).

Related: Implements ENG-4822 (scheduling fairness workstream). References in-code tickets and design doc at docs/design/continuous-batcher-backoff.md.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the default backoff conservative to avoid oscillation; future work includes auto-tuning scale per-tenant and integrating with autoscaler signals.
Tomás Ortega: Please add a safety cap to the backoff calculation so we never introduce unbounded delays. Also add a short explanation for the jitter choice in the doc.
Aisha Verma: Added safety cap (max_backoff_ms) and documented jitter rationale in docs/design/continuous-batcher-backoff.md; pushed another commit.
Lena Cho: Can you add a small benchmark that exercises a very small-request heavy tail? We should ensure no regression when >90% small requests.
Aisha Verma: Added bench config for 95/5 small/large mix and included results in PR description. Inline comments on thresholds are in tests/batcher_starvation_test.rs.
Marcus Bell: CI initially failed lint on formatting in continuous_batcher.rs (rustfmt). Reran and now clean. Approving change.
Tomás Ortega: Approved after verifying metrics and rollout guard.

Merge notes: squash-merged after approvals and green CI.
Introduce adaptive dequeue backoff in continuous batcher to reduce tail latency for short requests in mixed KV workloads. Feature-flag gated and conservatively enabled by default. Observability and rollout guidance included.

Motivation: tenants frequently ask for assistance tuning batch/cache defaults and quant profiles. Existing workflows are manual and produce heavyweight presets. This PR introduces 'cost-knockout', a small CLI + runtime probe that runs controlled micro-synth workloads against live telemetry snapshots to isolate token-level cost contributors and synthesizes compact batch/quant presets that are safe to roll out.

What this PR does: implements a cost-knockout CLI (python), a runtime probe harness (go) that can be invoked in 'shadow' mode against live traffic, a compact preset serializer (yaml/json), and an opinionated rollout helper that generates canary policies for the Console. The tool: 1) samples a tenant workload profile; 2) runs a set of micro-synth experiments (batch shapes, kv-prefill thresholds, quant tiers) in a bounded sandbox; 3) measures per-token latencies/costs and quality proxies; 4) emits prioritized presets and safe-fallbacks.

User-facing changes: a new CLI under tools/cost-knockout, docs in docs/ops/cost-knockout.md, and a demo workflow in examples/cost-knockout/demo.yaml. Admins can run the CLI locally (dry-run) or submit a proposal to the Console for automatic canary rollout.

Backward compatibility & safety: generated presets include automatic guardrails (max latency uplift, quality delta thresholds). All rollouts are produced as Console-friendly policy fragments; by default the system requires approval for nontrivial latency/quality tradeoffs.

Context: Users and downstream adapters (OpenAI-compatible SDKs and function-call bridges) have been tripping over rigid schema enforcement when responses arrive incrementally or when tool-calls interleave with the model stream. This PR introduces a small, opt-in runtime handshake and a human-friendly error surface to reduce developer friction while preserving strict validation when customers opt in. Summary of changes: Introduces a lightweight response_format metadata handshake that is exchanged at stream start and allows the runtime to advertise support for: 1) schema versions (json-schema-v3), 2) adaptive_strictness levels (per-request hint: permissive|warn|strict), 3) snapshot markers for resumable streams, and 4) tool_call fencing tokens to anchor tool call boundaries. Streaming stability: add a SnapshotMarker token sequence that the stream injector emits at safe checkpoints and a deterministic resume flow that replays minimal context to regenerate the KV cache when a reconnection happens. Tool/function calling: add explicit fencing metadata so functions invoked by adapters are only executed after a complete tool_call block has been received; partial tool payloads now surface as structured warnings rather than immediate failures. Validation and errors: implement human-readable validation errors mapped to an actionable error taxonomy (error_code, user_hint, recovery_hint) surfaced in the API and in the OpenAI-compat shim. The runtime will emit structured error frames on the stream (with an escape token) allowing clients to handle retries or fallbacks without breaking streaming parsers. OpenAI compatibility layer: add a translator that maps common function_call shapes to the new schema-handshake and back to legacy function_call when necessary; this preserves existing SDK behaviour while enabling the new validation features. Backwards compatibility: default behaviour remains unchanged; customers must set response_format or an adapter flag to enable adaptive_strictness and snapshotting. Tests and telemetry: add unit tests for handshake negotiation, fuzz tests for interleaved tool calls, and metrics (handshake_success, resume_rate, schema_violation_rate). Docs: update API reference, add a migration guide for SDK authors and a troubleshooting page with common error scenarios and recommended remediation steps. Implementation notes: no on-disk migration required; changes are mostly runtime/kafka message schema and small SDK adapters. Rollout: feature gated behind feature flag response_format_v3 and controlled rollout for Dedicated accounts for 2 weeks before global flip. Related: builds on previous schema work but intentionally exposes a smaller, developer-friendly surface for early adopter feedback.
Sasha Nguyen: Requested that the handshake include an explicit backward-compatibility flag so older SDKs can decide whether to attempt translation. Also asked for more integration tests around function_call edge cases.
Author (Amira Patel): Added a backward_compat flag and expanded the translator to stub legacy function_call shapes when requested. Added two integration tests to cover partial payload interleaving.
Diego Ramos: Noted a potential race in resume_manager when multiple reconnects happen concurrently; suggested deferring resume attempts via a single-run worker per session_id.
Author (Amira Patel): Implemented single-run worker and added a comment with reasoning; added a unit test for concurrent reconnects.
Luca Moretti: Approved after addressing race and after CI green. Observability notes: please expose handshake_success and resume_rate at 1m granularity.
CI Bot: One flaky test (resume_fuzz_test) failed on first run; reran and passed. All checks green.
Introduce opt-in response_format v3 handshake: adaptive strictness levels, snapshot markers for stream resume, tool_call fencing, and human-readable validation errors. Backwards compatible by default; feature-flagged rollout. Includes SDK adapters and migration guide.

Context: We observed two incidents in the last month where large regional maintenance windows caused SLO enforcement to aggressively circuit dozens of tenant requests simultaneously, producing cascading failovers and elevated error rates in downstream systems. This PR introduces an "ambulance mode" SLO attenuator + rolling fallback safety net to reduce cascade risk during emergency conditions.

Goals:
1) Provide a fast, auditable emergency toggle for SRE to relax non-critical SLO enforcement thresholds for a short window.
2) Ensure fallbacks are applied in a rolling, paced manner across nodes/regions to avoid synchronized re-routing spikes.
3) Emit clear telemetry and audit events so post-incident analysis can attribute decisions and quantify residual impact.

Summary of changes:
- runtime/serving/attenuator.go: new Attenuator service that evaluates per-tenant SLO attenuation policies and exposes a lightweight API for the control plane to request temporary attenuation. Includes an in-memory short-lived lease mechanism and a conservative decay timer to avoid rapid flip-flopping.
- controlplane/handlers/slo_attenuator.go: control plane endpoint which SRE and the console can call to enable/disable ambulance mode; validates RBAC and writes audit entries to the existing audit log.
- orchestrator/fallback/rolling_fallback.go: implements rolling fallback orchestration: when a fallback is required the coordinator assigns phased fallback windows to nodes and tracks progress to minimize instantaneous load shifts.
- console/api/v1/attenuator_toggle.go and console/ui/alerts: UI and API enablement for operators; toggles show a clear TTL, scope (tenant/global/region), and a link to the suppressible alert rule.
- telemetry/metrics/attenuator_metrics.prom and telemetry/events/attacks_audit.log: new metrics and structured audit events for attenuation actions, fallback phases, and rollback triggers.
- tests/integration/attenuator_e2e_test.go: canary-style integration test that simulates a regional maintenance and asserts that fallbacks are rolled out without >10% spike in QPS to any single target.
- docs/ops/ambulance-mode.md: runbook describing when to enable, guardrails, and postmortem steps.

Rollout and safety:
- Feature gated behind a cluster feature flag (default: disabled).
- Must be enabled via Console or CLI and requires an approval step in Linear for production clusters.
- Default attenuation only relaxes non-critical SLO buckets (e.g., best-effort token deadlines/latency SLOs) and never disables critical correctness/authorization checks.
- All attenuation actions create audit events and a linked Linear ticket suggestion for follow-up.

CI: unit tests and linters run on initial push; integration e2e initially failed intermittently in CI (flaky timing in the test harness), fixed by adding a more deterministic clock stub and retry backoff in the test. See commit history for fixes.

Checklist:
- [x] Attenuator runtime implementation
- [x] Control plane toggle + RBAC
- [x] Rolling fallback coordinator
- [x] Telemetry + audit events
- [x] Integration tests and runbook
- [x] Safety feature flag and TTL guard

Related: Builds on prior work for staged failover orchestration (ENG-0821) and ties into the SRE incident responder flows (SRE-210).
Introduces an emergency SLO attenuator (ambulance mode) to allow controlled temporary relaxation of non-critical SLOs and an automated rolling fallback safety net that performs staggered model/region fallback with strong telemetry and audit logs. Backward-compatible toggle; safe by default.
Priya Nair: This looks good overall. Request: tighten the default TTL to 15 minutes instead of 30 to reduce operator blast radius. Also add a canary-only mode for non-prod clusters.
Maya Chen (author): TTL changed to 15m and added canary-only flag; pushed a follow-up commit. The coordinator still enforces a minimum 5m stabilization window per phase.
Jacob Kline: Suggest adding an opt-in metric that reports "attenuation_pressure" per tenant so SRE can surface which customers are affected. Also asked for clarity on which SLO buckets are considered "non-critical" in docs.
Maya Chen (author): Added attenuator_pressure metric and expanded runbook section enumerating SLO buckets that are eligible for attenuation.
Alejandro Ruiz: Ran a quick load run; controller behavior looks sane. Approving pending CI green. Left a comment about adding a short audit field for operator-justification text (freeform) so we can later correlate operator reasoning with impact.
Maya Chen (author): Added optional justification field to controlplane toggle and ensured it's sanitized in audit logs.
