Context: Multiple teams reported inconsistent streaming ergonomics and frequent reconnects for low-throughput long-lived streams. This PR introduces a small, lightweight StreamAdapter abstraction in the redwood monorepo that standardizes backpressure and reauth/reauth-shim behavior across SDKs, plus a set of adaptive retry profiles aimed at reducing noisy reconnects for typical PLG and enterprise workloads.

Summary of changes and rationale (single continuous description): Commits: - Add core/stream/adapter with StreamAdapter interface, TTL-based idle heartbeat, and adaptive retry profile registry (commit: add-stream-adapter-core) - Implement compatibility shim that proxies previously-exported session_shim API to StreamAdapter while emitting deprecation warnings (commit: compat/deprecate-session-shim) - Python SDK: replace legacy SessionShim with PyStreamAdapter, expose ergonomic async iterator for chunked streaming, add tests and type hints, bump version to 2.8.0 (commit: sdk-python/adapter-and-iterator) - TypeScript SDK: implement StreamAdapter facade, normalize backpressure signals to a shared set of events, update stream consumer docs and examples, bump patch to 1.13.0 (commit: sdk-ts/stream-facade) - Go SDK: introduce small stream connector and SessionFactory to reduce token handoff complexity, add integration tests, bump module to 1.6.2 (commit: sdk-go/connector-sessionfactory) - Docs and changelog: update streaming guide, migration notes, and SDK release notes (commit: docs/streaming-migration) - Tests: add e2e scenario that simulates low tokens-per-minute long-lived consumers, unit tests for adaptive profiles and heartbeat (commit: test/stream-adapter-e2e)

Files touched (high level): - core/stream/adapter.py (new) - core/stream/compat_shim.py (new) - sdk/python/redwood/streaming/adapter.py (updated) - sdk/python/tests/test_stream_adapter.py (new) - sdk/typescript/src/stream/adapter.ts (new) - sdk/typescript/examples/stream-heartbeat.md (new) - sdk/go/stream/connector.go (new) - sdk/go/session/factory.go (new) - docs/streaming/migration.md (updated) - sdk/*/CHANGELOG.md (updated)

Motivation: The effort unifies a number of small behavioral differences that caused callers to implement bespoke retry and reconnect logic. Standardizing reduces duplicated code in customer applications and makes telemetry meaningful across languages.

Key design points: - StreamAdapter centralizes three responsibilities: backpressure normalization (pause/resume semantics), token lifecycle/reauth hooks, and an optional idle heartbeat to keep long-lived KV caches warm. - Adaptive retry profiles are pluggable and tuned for three workload buckets (interactive low-latency, batch high-throughput, long-lived low-volume). Profiles are conservative by default to avoid aggressive reconnect storms. - The compat shim provides a deprecation window (two releases) with telemetry so customers can migrate at their cadence without outages.

Review summary and conversation highlights: - Diego: "Nice consolidation. Please add a small benchmark showing end-to-end token-per-second reduction for long-lived streams." Author reply: "Added a micro-benchmark in test/bench/stream_heartbeat_bench.py and included results in the PR description; numbers show ~22% fewer reconnects in the long-lived profile." - Priya (request changes): "The TypeScript backpressure signal mapping needs clearer docs; also ensure that pause() is idempotent across consumers." Author reply: "Clarified adapter.ts comments, added a unit test ensuring idempotency, and included a short example in examples/stream-heartbeat.md." - Evan: "Can we avoid changing the public constructor signature for the Go connector?" Author reply: "We introduced a SessionFactory to preserve the older signature; updated README and left a TODO for the next major where we'll consider a cleaner API."

CI and checks: - Unit tests: pass (python/ts/go) - Integration e2e: pass on linux-amd64 - Lint: ts/py linters pass, go vet clean - Flaky test rerun: one intermittent TS test flaked on first run, re-run succeeded

Outcome: - Merge method: squash and merge - Changelog: SDK versions bumped (python 2.8.0, typescript 1.13.0, go 1.6.2) - Migration: Added docs/streaming/migration.md with a 2-step migration path and example code in each SDK - Rollout: feature toggled via STREAM_ADAPTER=true for 3 weeks before defaulting to true

Notes for maintainers: - Deprecation telemetry emits event: stream.session_shim.deprecated; monitor for adoption. - The compat shim logs a single WARN per process on construction to surface older usages. - If teams want to revert, flip STREAM_ADAPTER=false and roll back the SDK consumer to prior pinned versions.

Related work: ENG-1764 (streaming observability), ENG-1820 (kv-cache keepalive), SUP-874 (customer-reported reconnect storms).
Introduce a single StreamAdapter abstraction across Python/TypeScript/Go; deprecate legacy session shim with a compatibility layer; add adaptive retry profiles and a default idle heartbeat to reduce reconnect churn. SDKs bumped: python 2.8.0, typescript 1.13.0, go 1.6.2.

Context: presubmit CI latency and noisy dependency churn have been slowing developer feedback and increasing dependency drift. This PR introduces a two-part approach: (1) a lightweight presubmit bootstrap path that minimizes setup time for small edits and fast-check lanes, and (2) an automated constraint-bumping heuristic that keeps dependency constraint pins within the acceptable compatibility window while avoiding mass upgrades during low-bandwidth presubmit runs.

Goals: speed up iteration for quick changes, reduce full-matrix CI invocations for low-risk edits, and reduce manual dependency churn by surfacing & optionally applying safe constraint bumps.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces a small presubmit bootstrap image (toolchain/mini-bootstrap) that contains only the runtime/tooling needed for lint + unit fast checks. Full toolchain images are used only for heavy integration tests.
- Adds a staged presubmit router: quickpath -> fastlint -> optional full-presubmit. Quickpath runs in ~30s for typical doc or small TS/py changes.
- Implements dep-constraint-bump worker: a deterministic heuristic that reads dependency constraints (package.json/pyproject.lock), queries a curated constraint index, and proposes minimal non-breaking constraint widenings on a separate branch. The worker can open draft PRs with diffs and a short evaluation report.
- Adds gating rules: constraint-bump PRs are set as draft and require explicit approval; they are not auto-merged. Constraint proposals are excluded from quickpath to avoid noise during rapid iteration.
- Adds metrics and telemetry: presubmit-setup-time, quickpath-duration, constraint-bump-proposals, and constraint-bump-false-positive-rate.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implement mini-bootstrap Dockerfile and minimal runtime image
- [x] Implement presubmit router logic and fastlane config
- [x] Add dep-constraint-bump worker and draft PR flow
- [x] Add unit + integration tests for router and worker
- [x] Add telemetry emitters and dashboards (skeleton)
- [x] Add docs: docs/ci/presubmit-fastpath.md and docs/ci/constraint-bump.md

Rollout plan: staged rollout. Default org-level CI keeps legacy path enabled. Start routing trivial PRs (<5 files, no package manifest changes) to quickpath for a beta cohort (team infra, team sdk) for one week, monitor presubmit-setup-time and false negatives. After 2 weeks expand to wider org and enable constraint-bump worker in dry-run mode (opens draft PRs only). After a month evaluate automation quality before recommending manual approve/merge.

Why unique: unlike earlier 'split presubmit' PRs, this change ties bootstrap reduction to an automated, conservative constraint-bumping flow with explicit telemetry so we can quantify both developer velocity gains and dependency safety.

Related: Linear ENG-9876 (presubmit fast lanes), ENG-9988 (dep automation), incident SUP-4321 (slow CI incident on 2026-01-21).
Ethan Wright (2026-02-20): LGTM overall. Two requests: add explicit timeouts for the worker network calls and ensure draft PR titles include 'constraint-proposal' prefix.
Maya Chen (2026-02-20): Thanks — added timeouts and changed draft PR title format (see commit b7c8d9e).
Sofia Alvarez (2026-02-22): Please add a health-check endpoint to mini-bootstrap so our staging runner can probe image readiness.
Maya Chen (2026-02-22): Added /healthz probe and a readiness script (commit c0ffee1).
Rahul Patel (2026-02-25): Verified telemetry events; suggest a dashboard panel showing quickpath ratio over time. Marking approved pending CI green.
CI Bot (2026-02-26): build: passed; unit-tests: passed; integration-smoke: flaky — rerun required.
CI Bot (2026-02-27): integration-smoke: passed on rerun. All checks green.
Presubmit: Introduced a fast 'quickpath' presubmit lane and mini-bootstrap image to reduce developer feedback time. Added an automated constraint-bump worker that opens draft PRs proposing minimal, non-breaking constraint updates for maintainers to review. No automatic merges enabled. Monitor presubmit-setup-time and constraint-bump proposals in infra dashboards.
- To enable quickpath for additional teams, add their org/team ids to .github/presubmit-fastpath-allowlist.json.
- Constraint bump worker uses SECRET_INDEX_API_KEY; provision in org secrets before enabling auto-run.
- Telemetry names: infra.presubmit.setup_time_ms, infra.presubmit.quickpath_ratio, infra.dep.bump_proposals.
- If you see many false positives from constraint proposals, toggle worker dry-run in ci/config.yaml -> dep_bumper.dry_run = true
Presubmit median setup time improved from ~95s to ~34s for quickpath PRs in beta. Overall presubmit CPU consumption reduced by approximately 18% in early pilot. Constraint-bump created 12 draft proposals in dry-run over 48 hours; maintainers accepted 5 of them manually after review. No regressions observed in integration smoke runs post-merge.
1) Roll out quickpath in beta (infra, sdk teams) using feature flag ci.quickpath.beta=true.
2) Monitor metrics for one week; collect feedback and iterate.
3) Enable constraint-bump dry-run across org before making it active.
4) Follow up: expand dashboard panels and schedule retro with ENG-9876 owners.

Background and motivation: A recent support escalation (SUP-442) and an internal incident showed intermittent KMS calls routed outside the tenant's allowed region when requests were proxied through legacy gateways that dropped the tenant-region claim. This change adds a lightweight propagator that ensures a cryptographically signed region assertion (region-assertion and audit-proof) travels with requests from the API gateway through service mesh to the KMS plugin and audit-forwarder. The goal is to make KMS region checks and audit evidence verification robust even when intermediate proxies sanitize standard headers.

What this PR does:
- Introduces a RegionAssertionPropagator component in the api-gateway that signs a compact assertion (tenant_id, region, issued_at, nonce, signature) using the platform signing key and attaches it as X-Redwood-AuditProof.
- Extends the auth-service to surface canonical tenant claims (tenant_id, allowed_regions) in a machine-readable JSON Web Claim (not a JWT) consumed by downstream services.
- Adds validation hooks in the kms-plugin to prefer region information from X-Redwood-AuditProof if present, falling back to the existing tenant claim only when the header is absent.
- Enhances audit-forwarder to store the audit-proof header alongside existing envelopes for tamper-evident retention and debugability.
- Adds a small translation layer in rbac-policy-compiler that maps older region-label policies to the new assertion model during a rollout window.
- End-to-end test coverage: new e2e scenario that simulates a proxy scrubbing standard headers but preserving the audit-proof header to verify KMS calls remain region-locked.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed by Security and Infra (ENG-8373)
- [x] Unit tests for propagator signing and verification
- [x] Integration tests for gateway->service->kms path
- [x] e2e test for proxy-scrub scenario
- [x] Feature gate implemented (rbac.v2.region_propagation) and config defaults to off for Dedicated tenants
- [x] Rolling rollout plan and monitoring dashboards updated

Changes (high-level):
Commits:
- feat(region): add RegionAssertionPropagator to api-gateway (Asha K)
- feat(auth): expose canonical tenant claims endpoint and library (Mateo A)
- fix(kms-plugin): prefer audit-proof header for region enforcement (Evan C)
- feat(audit): persist audit-proof header in forwarder envelopes (Lena P)
- feat(rbac-compiler): add translation shim for legacy region labels (Asha K)
- test(e2e): add proxy-scrub scenario to canary suite (QA)
- test(e2e): add proxy-scrub scenario to canary suite (QA)
- chore: gofmt and minor lint fixes (QA)

Files touched (high level):
- services/api-gateway/src/propagator/region_propagator.go
- services/auth-service/src/claims/canonical_claims.go
- infra/kms-plugin/src/region_enforcer.go
- infra/audit-forwarder/src/envelope_store.go
- infra/rbac-compiler/src/translator/region_shim.go
- tests/e2e/proxy_scrub_scenario.yaml
- docs/security/region-propagation.md (new)

Notable implementation details:
- The audit-proof header is intentionally compact (base64 of JSON + ed25519 signature) to avoid hitting header size limits and to be resilient across proxies.
- Signing keys are read from the existing platform KMS with a transient ephemeral signing key cached per process. No long-lived private keys are introduced.
- The propagator runs as a filter in api-gateway and only emits the header if the tenant has allowed_regions configured; otherwise it omits it to avoid leakage.
- Validation in kms-plugin includes nonce replay protection backed by a short-lived in-memory cache and a secondary async dedupe check in Dynamo for cross-process safety.

Review conversation (highlights):

Summary: Introduces a canonical permission registry for RBAC v2 in the redwood monorepo. This adds a typed Permission enum (backed by stable string IDs), a registry with required metadata (description, owning team, sensitivity tier, allowed scopes), and CI validation to enforce uniqueness + naming conventions. Motivation: We need a single source of truth for "what permissions exist" before we can (a) annotate endpoints/jobs consistently, (b) generate role templates/policy bundles, and (c) provide audit/evidence artifacts for enterprise customers. This PR intentionally includes only an initial catalog covering the first critical workflows (org/user/role management, API key management, audit log export, routing policy edits) so downstream adoption work can proceed in parallel. Design notes: Permission IDs follow ADR-014 conventions (namespaced dot-separated strings, no implicit wildcards, no environment-specific IDs; scoping is handled in bindings). Metadata is intentionally strict and required for every permission to avoid future "mystery permissions". The registry is compile-time accessible for services and is also exportable as JSON for docs/Console. Implementation details: Added rbac/permissions/Permission.ts (enum), rbac/permissions/registry.ts (PermissionDefinition map), a registry export command (prints machine-readable catalog), and a CI linter step (permissions-lint) that checks: (1) unique IDs, (2) regex match for allowed format, (3) required metadata fields present, (4) no duplicate descriptions with different IDs, (5) deprecated permissions must include replacement + sunset date. Also added unit tests around the linter and registry export. Follow-ups: Endpoint annotations (ENG-18305) will reference Permission enum values directly; Gateway middleware (ENG-18277) will use the registry to populate denial reason context; Docs (redwood-docs PR) will consume the exported catalog. Checklist: [x] Permission ID naming matches ADR-014; [x] Initial inventory reviewed w/ Security Eng; [x] CI enforcement added; [x] Export format documented; [ ] Backfill remaining permissions (tracked in ENG-18241). Risk: Low. This is additive and not yet wired into enforcement paths. CI: New step added to buildkite pipeline; should run <2s.
Marcus Lin (Security Eng) — Comment: Love the direction. A couple of asks: (1) Can we require an owning team / oncall field? This is always needed when we get a questionnaire asking "who approves changes to permissions". (2) For "audit.export" can you confirm this covers both Console export and SIEM exporter? I want to avoid split-brain permissions. Also, ensure the naming matches ADR-014 exactly (no underscores).
Jordan Lee — Reply: Added required owner field ("owner_team") to PermissionDefinition and updated lint + existing entries. On audit export: I split into two actions because the data paths differ: "audit.logs.export" (user-initiated export/download) vs "audit.siem.configure" (configure exporter destinations + tokens). Both are in this PR. Also fixed "api_keys.rotate" -> "api_keys.rotate" stays but removed an underscore in one draft entry (now "api_keys.create" etc).
Kaitlyn Nguyen (Authn/Authz) — Comment: Please make sure the enum values are the stable string IDs, not numeric. We’ve been burned by reordering enums. Also would be good to have a function like getPermissionDefinition(id) that throws a typed error if missing, so service middleware can fail closed.
Jordan Lee — Reply: Enum is string-valued. Added getPermissionDefinition() which throws MissingPermissionDefinitionError; callers can treat missing definitions as config error and deny by default. Added tests that the registry covers every enum entry.
Ethan Park (Control Plane) — Comment: For control-plane endpoint annotations we’ll import from this package. Can we keep the API surface dead simple? I’d prefer: Permission.<NAME> and registry lookup internal. Also: please add a short section in README with examples for endpoint annotations + jobs.
Jordan Lee — Reply: Kept exports limited: Permission enum + PermissionId type + getPermissionDefinition + listPermissions. Added README examples for: control-plane endpoint annotation, async job permission mapping, and exporting the catalog for docs/Console.
Amara Diallo (API Gateway) — Comment: The lint rule about deprecation requiring a sunset date is good. Can we also require a replacement permission if deprecated? And can the linter output a clear failure message (actionable) in CI logs?
Jordan Lee — Reply: Updated linter: deprecated requires both replacement_id and sunset_date. CI output now prints a short, greppable line per failure (e.g., PERM_LINT[E003] permission id invalid: ...).
Marcus Lin — Approval: Approved. This is a key building block for the rest of the v2 work. Please ensure follow-up PRs don’t add permissions without sensitivity tiers; CI should catch it now.
Kaitlyn Nguyen — Approval: Approved.
Internal-only (no customer behavior change): adds canonical permission registry + CI validation to unblock RBAC v2 endpoint annotation and policy bundle generation.

Motivation: We observed tail latency spikes when mixing INT8 and FP8 model variants with dynamic KV-cache reuse. Root cause traced to microstalling during per-token dequantization when the kernel scheduler switched execution lanes and the KV window prefetcher tripped an extra serialization point. This PR introduces a lightweight per-token affine-merge pass in the kernel pipeline coupled with a windowed KV-prefetch scheduler to coalesce dequant work and remove serialization across microbatches.

What this changes: Adds a new kernel fusion step (affine_merge_pass) that merges the tiny affine rescale + requant (dequant-affine-requant common pattern for smoothquant) into a single vectorized microkernel for INT8/FP8 hybrid paths. The scheduler changes introduce a KV-prefetch window (default 8 tokens) that aligns prefetching with affinity windows from the batcher to avoid cross-lane cache thrash.

Goals: Reduce per-token latency jitter on mixed-precision workloads, improve throughput in small-microbatch scenarios (1-8 tokens), and keep steady-state token/sec at parity or better with prior fused paths.

Design summary: - New pass: affine_merge_pass applied after layout normalization and before attention kernel selection. - Kernel: socalled "affine_merge_v2" implements fused dequant (INT8->FP32), affine scale/bias, and optional requant to FP8 in a single loop with prefetch hints. - Scheduler: kv_window_prefetcher schedules KV reads in aligned windows and defers cross-lane prefetches until the window completes. - Batcher integration: microbatcher includes affinity hints (affinity_id) which scheduler uses to avoid prefetching KV for lanes that will be drained soon. - Configuration: runtime flags (env and per-deployment config) to tune window size and enable/disable fused kernel.

Performance results (internal e2e bench): - Testbed: A100x4, Llama-3-8B variants (fp32 baseline / int8-smoothquant / fp8-heuristic), synthetic chat trace of 12k tokens. - Median latency (1-token microbatch): - baseline: 23.4ms, with this PR: 17.6ms (-24.8%) - P95: baseline 61.0ms -> 38.2ms (-37.4%) - Throughput (tokens/sec steady): baseline 9.8k -> 10.9k (+11.2%) - Cost proxy (GPU utilization): +3% steady util, net decrease in wasted stalls measured by scheduler traces. Regression tests show no quality delta on output when requant path used; we added opt-in param to bypass requant for strict FP8 fidelity.

Backward/compatibility: No API changes to the public inference API. Runtime flags are opt-in; deployments can gate rollout. Default is enabled for dedicated and private clusters with GPU >= Ampere.

Checklist (high level): - [x] Design doc link: Linear ENG-4821 (see linked_linear) - [x] Unit tests for affine_merge_v2 microkernel - [x] Integration tests for KV window alignment - [x] Perf harness run and numbers recorded - [x] Feature-flag gated rollout plan - [x] Observability: added metrics for prefetch_window_misses and affine_merge_fallback_count

Commits summary:
- feat(kernel): add affine_merge_pass + vectorized kernel implementation
- perf(scheduler): kv_window_prefetcher + affinity_id plumbing to microbatcher
- test: unit and integration tests for fused path and prefetch alignment
- ci: enable perf harness workflow for this PR

Files changed (high-level):
- runtime/kernel/passes/affine_merge_pass.cc (new)
- runtime/kernel/kernels/affine_merge_v2.s / .cc (new microkernel + wrapper)
- runtime/scheduler/kv_window_prefetcher.cc (new)
- runtime/batcher/microbatcher.cc (affinity hint plumbing)
- tests/kernel/affine_merge_test.cc
- tests/scheduler/kv_window_integration_test.cc
- docs/notes/affine-merge-prefetch.md (internal rollout notes)

Review conversation (high level, chronological):
- Diego Ramirez (reviewer): "Nice consolidation — can we avoid additional memory pressure when vectorizing? Please add explicit checks for register spilling and a fallback to normalized path."
- Author (Maya): "Added runtime heuristics to limit vector width based on reported L1/L2 size; added fallback counter metric for tracing."
- Sofia Patel (perf reviewer): "Benchmarks look good; please add microbench for mixed-precision 4-way batching and verify P95 regression under load."
- Author: "Added 4-way mixed microbatch perf job and included results in PR description. Also added canary rollout instructions."
- Carlos Alvarez (SRE): "Observability looks sufficient; add alert for high affine_merge_fallback_count."
- Author: "Alert added to redwood/observability alert deck; linked in rollout notes."

CI summary: Initial CI run had lint + test failures on string formatting (fixed), second run succeeded; perf harness ran in separate workflow and passed internal thresholds. Overall ci_status: pass.

Merge: Squash-merged after approvals. Merge method: squash.

Rollout plan: Canary on dedicated capacity pools (10% traffic) for 48h, monitor prefetch_window_misses, affine_merge_fallback_count, P95 latency, and output diff regression on eval set. If fallback_count > 100 in 48h or P95 degrades by >10% revert.

Risks & mitigations: The main risk is register pressure causing slowdowns on older GPUs; mitigated via runtime heuristics that lower vector width and fall back to the safe path. Another risk is KV-prefetch misalignment under unpredictable request interleaving; the scheduler keeps a small conservative backoff and exposes tuning params for platform teams.

Related: references Linear ENG-4821 (design), ENG-4906 (perf harness), and prior PR pr-370456 (hierarchical-dequant-kv-prefetch-adapter) for historical context.
Improves INT8/FP8 hybrid path latency and P95; introduces affine_merge kernel and KV prefetch scheduler; opt-in via runtime flags; canary rollout recommended.
payload.title: Per-token affine merge and KV-prefetch scheduler to reduce INT8/FP8 dequant stalls

Motivation: We've seen persistent noisy token-cost alerts correlated with prefix warmups and edge retries in regional proxies. This PR adds an Observability Edge Proxy (OEP) that normalizes metric/tag ingestion (metrics/traces/logs) at the edge and a Token Decay Calibrator (TDC) component that applies a short-lived decay weight to tokens attributable to warmup/retry semantics. Goals: 1) Reduce alert churn by de-emphasizing transient warmup cost spikes; 2) Improve trace/metric coalescing at the edge to lower cardinality and improve downstream rollups; 3) Provide a consistent tag set for downstream dashboards and SLOs. What this changes: - New service: observability/edge-proxy: Go-based sidecar that accepts OTLP/HTTP telemetry, normalizes routing tags (tenant, route, model_variant, region), and emits compacted spans with consistent invocation ids. - New library: telemetry/decay_calibrator: deterministic decay function based on prefix length and retry counts; implemented as a configurable filter in edge-proxy and as a webhook for ingest pipelines. - Dashboard updates: dashboards/token-cost-overview and dashboards/edge-invocations now show pre/post-calibrator series and a decay-adjusted cost band. - Alerts: token-cost long-tail alert rule now uses decay-adjusted aggregation and an adaptive quiet-window (configurable per-tenant). - Tests: unit tests for decay math, integration tests simulating warmup/retry traffic, and e2e for metrics roundtrip. Backwards compatibility: the edge-proxy honors existing tags and can operate in passthrough mode; default decay coefficients match historical baselines, and the feature is gated behind a runtime flag. Rollout plan: canary in a single region for 48h (5% of traffic with decay enabled), metric comparison (pre/post cost percentiles), then ramp to all regions with automatic rollback if token-cost SLO degrades by >5%. Related: ENG-2027 (alert reduction), ENG-2105 (edge telemetry unification).
Add Observability Edge Proxy to centralize telemetry ingestion and a token-decay-calibrator that reduces warmup-derived noise in token-cost signals; alert tuning to reduce noisy token-cost alerts

Motivation: OpenAI-style function/tool calling is flexible but fragile in streaming scenarios and through proxies (edge load balancers, gateways, SDK shims). We observed two classes of problems: (1) tool selection ambiguity when multiple compatible tool schemas exist (tool_choice semantics), and (2) stream fragmentation where tool-invoke frames are split or reordered, causing downstream tool agents to misinterpret or drop messages. This PR introduces a lightweight provenance handshake and an explicit stream-level ACK frame to make tool invocation deterministic and resilient across proxies and partial streams.

Design summary: single-line description: introduce a pre-invoke provenance handshake header and an in-stream ACK frame with idempotency tokens. Key behaviors implemented: 1) At dispatch, the router includes an x-rw-tool-provenance header encoding {tool_id, schema_id, schema_version, provenance_score} (base64-encoded JSON). This gives downstream workers an authoritative schema mapping and a provenance score used by deterministic tiebreakers. 2) We add a new framed streaming control message "tool_ack" that worker runtimes send back as soon as they accept the invocation and validate the inbound schema. The ack includes an idempotency token and a schema fingerprint. 3) If an ack is not observed within the configured ack_timeout, the caller receives a structured fallback event and the router can either (a) re-route to a pre-registered compatible tool, or (b) fall back to non-tool textual output per customer policy. 4) Fragment preservation: workers coalesce adjacent framed tool messages until the invocation is complete (terminal "tool_frag_end" frame). We added heuristics to reassemble fragmented JSON payloads and to signal a "fragment_repair" event if a fragment is missing after repair_timeout.

Compatibility and semantics: The changes are additive and opt-in: hosted OpenAI-compat adapter will emit x-rw-tool-provenance only when the call is detected as a tool/function invocation. Existing clients that ignore headers are unaffected; tool runtimes that haven’t been upgraded will still receive the original invoke envelope but will not emit tool_ack which triggers fallback behavior after ack_timeout. To preserve OpenAI compatibility, we do not change the visible JSON function schema in the final payload; the provenance header and tool_ack are transport-level signals only. The tool_choice tiebreak uses provenance_score + deterministic tie hash (request_id + elapsed_ms) to avoid non-deterministic selection under load.

Telemetry and observability: new metrics: rw_tool.ack.latency, rw_tool.ack.missing, rw_tool.fragment.repaired, rw_tool.choice.tiebreak.count. We added trace spans around handshake serialization and ack handling; these are surfaced in the Console per-route timeline and in the per-token breakdown for auditing.

Testing: unit tests for header encoding/decoding, ack frame serialization, and multiple fragment reassembly were added. Integration tests cover (a) proxy that strips and reorders frames, (b) worker that validates schema mismatch and returns an explicit reject ack, (c) rollback to fallback tool when ack missing. E2E staging runs simulated 1000 concurrent toolcalls with 50ms median ack latency and verified 99.95% success within ack_timeout.

Rollout plan: staged rollout: 1) internal canary on dedicated infra (1% of traffic) for 48h with enhanced telemetry, 2) opt-in customer beta for Hosted API, 3) default on for new OpenAI-compat v2 adapter and opt-out flag for customers needing older behavior. Migration notes: customers implementing custom tool runtimes should read the SDK guide; minimal change required: emit tool_ack on successful validation (SDKs updated in this PR to include helpers).

Checklist:
- [x] Header format spec added (docs/compat/tool-provenance.md)
- [x] Runtime ack frame implemented (runtime/streaming/ack.go)
- [x] SDK helper added (redwood-sdk-python/tool_ack.py)
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Telemetry + Console surfaces

Related: ENG-1123 (tool reliability), ENG-1178 (streaming fragmentation).
Evelyn Li: Nice incremental design. Two asks: add a short explanation for the deterministic tie hash and make ack_timeout configurable per-customer (not just global).
Author (Asha): Added configurable ack_timeout per-customer via routing config and documented deterministic tie hash in the spec (hash = sha256(request_id || schema_id) % 10000).
Marco Ruiz: Can we avoid the base64 JSON header to reduce header size? Consider compact binary fingerprinting.
Author (Asha): Switched to a compact fingerprint for schema_id and keep a short provenance byte mask; still include a base64 reference for debug mode. See runtime/streaming/ack.go changes.
Priya Nair: Tests look good. Please add a sanity test that asserts behavior when an older worker doesn't emit ack (fallback path).
Author (Asha): Added integration test proxy-old-worker-fallback.test and verified behavior in staging.
Added a transport-level tool provenance header and an in-stream tool_ack frame to improve determinism and robustness of OpenAI-compatible tool/function calls. Enables deterministic tool_choice tiebreaking and fragment repair. Opt-in rollout; SDK helpers added.
payload.title: Tool provenance handshake and stream ACK protocol for OpenAI-compatible toolcalls

Motivation: burst and steady-state allocation decisions in Dedicated fleets show pathological oscillation when tenant occupancy distributions stray from the assumed homogeneous model. This results in noisy headroom estimates, unnecessary prewarming, and occasional SLA blips for tail latency-sensitive tenants. This PR introduces an occupancy-entropy-based allocator and a complementary lease-granularity tuner to stabilize allocations and improve throughput guarantees without increasing overall capacity.

refactor(lease): extract lease granularity config and tuner scaffold
perf(autoscaler): integrate entropy bias into provision-decider pipeline
test(autoscaler): add deterministic harness for mixed occupancy patterns
ci: add telemetry panel snapshot for entropy metrics
+ func ComputeEntropy(samples []float64) float64 { /* uses log2 and small-sample bias correction */ }
+ // occupancy score = base_score * (1 - alpha * normalized_entropy)
- oldLease := s.LeaseDuration // removed fixed 30s assumption

Added a short benchmark in tests to demonstrate cases where variance misleads (see tests/integration/entropy_harness_test.go).

Rajat Mehra: Approved after small nits fixed about metric names and unit tests passing.
Introduce occupancy-entropy allocator and lease granularity tuner to improve allocation stability and reduce unnecessary prewarming. Adds new telemetry: occupancy_entropy, lease_granularity_histogram, allocation_rebalance_events. Gated behind feature flag occupancy_entropy_alloc_v1.

Context and motivation: We continue to see integration friction when customers attempt to use session/lease semantics across product SDKs. Different names (SessionFacade vs SessionProxy vs SessionHandle), subtle differences in retry defaults, and streaming resume hooks cause support churn (SUP-342) and subtle regressions in production integration tests. This PR introduces a minimal, ergonomic SessionProxy abstraction and aligns the default retry profiles for auth and streaming across the three SDKs so teams can rely on consistent behavior across language boundaries.

What this PR changes (high-level):
- Introduces SessionProxy (language-specific implementations) as a lightweight, well-documented facade around credential refresh + heartbeat + optional lease semantics. The goal is parity in surface and predictable lifecycle but with language-idiomatic ergonomics.
- Unifies retry presets: auth window, reauth backoff and circuit-fail fast profiles now live in a single cross-sdk spec under /docs/retry-presets.md and have been wired into each SDK.
- Streaming ergonomics: standardizes resume-token handling and exposes a pullstream-friendly cancel hook. TypeScript and Python expose async iterators with a resume(token) helper; Go exposes a StreamCursor with Resume(token) to match semantics.
- Minor parity fixes: bugfixes to Python's token rotation path when a streaming resume occurs mid-KV-cache restore; TypeScript fix for backpressure hint propagation; Go fixes around session shutdown ordering.
- Version bumps: python 1.15.0, typescript 2.9.0, go 1.6.3 (packaged in SDK meta manifests).

I increased the test timeout and added a targeted retry in the test harness.

payload.body:
Improves continuous batcher fairness and reduces KV miss tail latency by introducing lease smoothing and a proactive KV prefetch policy. Backward compatible runtime config with default off for private deployments.
Motivation: Continuous batching can suffer starvation and tail latency spikes when a small number of long-running KV-heavy requests repeatedly seize batch slots. This PR introduces a lease-smoothing admission layer and a lightweight proactive KV prefetch policy to reduce starvation and lower p95/p99 latency without increasing average token cost.

Summary of changes: Added a lease-smoothing coordinator that softens immediate slot reclamation by introducing a short, jittered secondary lease window. Implemented a two-tier queue (fast-path / steady-path) to prefer short requests while ensuring long requests make progress. Added heuristics-based proactive KV prefetch: when a request is admitted and the model indicates KV-dependency (cacheable context patterns), we issue a low-overhead async prefetch for top-k KV shards to warm the cache before generation proceeds.

Key behaviors and knobs: - lease_smoothing_window_ms (default 12ms): small grace window applied after primary lease expiry; jitter added to avoid synchrony. - two_tier_threshold_tokens (default 64): requests under this length are routed to fast-path queue. - kv_prefetch_mode: off|heuristic|aggressive (default heuristic). - prefetch_shard_budget: number of KV shards to prefetch (default 3). - backpressure_decay_ms: controls how quickly soft reservations decay when reshuffling.

Why this is different: Rather than hard preemption or strict priority which can starve long requests, lease-smoothing preserves forward progress with minimal latency cost. Proactive KV warming is conservative: it only prefetches when a high-probability KV dependency is detected (pattern-based and model-provided hints) to avoid unnecessary IO.

Performance: Microbenchmarks on a 4-GPU staging cluster (gpus with 32GB) with mixed workload (60% short interactive, 40% long KV-heavy streaming): - median request latency: +1% (negligible) - p95 generation latency: -12% - p99 generation latency: -18% - observed KV miss penalty (measured as additional per-request stall ms): -35% - sustained throughput under 90th percentile latency SLO improved by ~8% in steady-state.

Safety and rollout: Feature gated by config flags, default enabled on hosted main but disabled in the private installer until customers opt in. Backwards-compatible defaults chosen to avoid regressions. Rolling deploy plan: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with health checks on p99 and KV miss rate.

Testing: - Unit tests for lease expiry/jitter logic and queue routing. - Integration test harness that simulates mixture of KV-heavy and short requests with an emulated KV store. - Load tests against benchmark-lab with and without prefetch to validate throughput and cost impact. - Nightly perf regression alert added to catch delta >5% on p95.

Related: builds on ideas in ENG-7321 (fairness rebalancer) and ENG-7409 (kv warmup hints). Also references perf canary scripts updated in this PR.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Benchmark runs and numbers attached - [x] Docs: runtime config pages updated - [x] Migration notes added for private installer

Notes for reviewers: focus on the lease jitter distribution (exponential backoff vs uniform jitter), the heuristic condition for issuing KV prefetch, and performance cost trade-offs in aggressive prefetch mode.
Unit and integration tests added. Load tests in benchmark-lab reproduced latency improvements and safe throughput gains. Nightly perf regression monitor added to tools/perf_alerts/p99_guard.yml.
Default behavior enabled on hosted only. Private installer keeps kv_prefetch_mode=off. If customers see increased KV store load after enabling aggressive prefetch, reduce prefetch_shard_budget to 1 or set kv_prefetch_mode=heuristic. Canary script provided at examples/deploy/canary-rollout.sh.
No DB schema changes. To enable in private deployments modify serving.runtime kv_prefetch_mode and lease_smoothing_window_ms in runtime_config.yaml then restart runtime service. Recommended gradual ramp: 1%, 10%, 50% over 24h windows.
Ravi Kapoor (2025-11-13): Please add unit coverage for jitter distribution edge cases. Also what happens under KV store overload?
Maya Chen (2025-11-14): Added tests for jitter tails and introduced prefetch backoff to avoid storming; see commit e9f8a6b.
Elena Gomez (2025-11-16): Left a minor comment on naming of 'steady-path' vs 'slow-path' — prefer explicit term. Verified perf numbers on staging cluster and they match claims.
Samir Das (2025-11-18): Approved after verifying canary logs and ensuring no regression on token cost; recommended adding rollout steps to docs.
CI Bot (2025-11-19): All checks passed on squash-merge branch.

Adds a synth-based SLO generator that produces burst-resilient alert thresholds and a dashboard for coldstart latency profiling; non-breaking, opt-in via config flag.
Motivation: production SLOs were over-sensitive to short-lived token bursts and coldstart spikes from prefetch/backpressure. This PR implements a synthesis-based SLO engine that combines short-window burst-normalization, coldstart-aware percentile smoothing, and an exportable coldstart latency profile that teams can attach to alerting rules. Goals: 1) reduce noisy pager incidents caused by transient token surges 2) preserve sensitivity to real regressions 3) provide a compact dashboard and examples for teams to adopt. Design: the SLO synthesizer ingests per-route token-latency histograms and a short-term burst detector, computes a blended baseline from exponential-decayed percentiles and a coldstart correction curve, and emits threshold candidates with metadata (weight, expected false-positive rate, confidence). The coldstart profile is a small timeseries that summarizes latency decay in the first N seconds after container/model warmup, computed per model-version and region. Implementation: core synthesizer in obs/slo/synthesizer.go; a lightweight daemon obs/slo/collector that binds to the existing metrics pipeline and exposes a Prom-compatible endpoint; a dashboard JSON under observability/dashboards/coldstart-slo.json and an alerting recipe in observability/alerts/slo-synthesized-rules.yml. Opt-in: feature flag OBS_SLO_SYNTH=true toggles the new pipeline; default remains legacy SLOs until 2025-03-01. Backwards compatibility: synthesizer reads existing token-latency histogram buckets and uses same labels; emits new metrics prefixed with redwood_slo_synth_ to avoid collisions. Tests & validation: unit tests for the blending heuristic and coldstart curve generator (obs/slo/synthesizer_test.go), integration test that replays synthetic traffic and asserts stable alert counts, and a small loadbench verifying <1% CPU overhead at production sampling rates. Migration & rollout: staged rollout: feature-flagged canary (10% of routes) -> 50% -> 100% with a 24h monitor window and automatic rollback if alert volume increases >15% relative to baseline. Observability artifacts: the dashboard shows: coldstart decay panel (per-model-version), synthesized threshold ribbon overlay on per-route p95/p99 charts, and a regression explainer panel that links back to raw spans. Checklist: [x] core synthesizer implementation [x] collector + Prom export [x] unit + integration tests [x] dashboard + alert recipe [x] feature flag and rollout plan [x] runbook snippets for oncall. Related: ENG-3312 (SLO noisy-pager reduction), SRE-110 (coldstart mitigation). Documentation: docs/observability/slo-synthesizer.md with examples for teams and a short migration guide. Caveats: the blended heuristic uses a tunable alpha and requires representative histogram ingestion; teams with extremely sparse traffic may need to seed with synthetic warmups. Next steps: add quantized model-cost awareness to prefer lower-cost fallbacks for non-critical routes and extend the synthesizer to produce per-tenant suggested thresholds.
To enable: set OBS_SLO_SYNTH=true in observability helm values or env. Watch new metrics: redwood_slo_synth_threshold{route,model,region} and redwood_slo_coldstart_profile_duration_seconds. If alert volume increases after enabling, rollback the feature flag and run 'make slo-synth-test' locally with the replay harness to reproduce. Runbook snippets are in observability/runbooks/slo-synth-runbook.md.
payload.title: Introduce SLO synthesizer and coldstart latency profiles for burst-resilient alerts

Context and motivation: Operating teams continue to hit a tradeoff between low tail latency and unit cost when serving long-context transformer workloads. Existing FlashAttention variants we onboarded earlier reduce compute but require multiple fallbacks across rotary/rope variants and separate KV eviction policies. This PR introduces 'attn-harmony', a single fused attention kernel plus a lightweight coordinator that unifies rope/rotary offsets, fuses softmax+reduction for reduced memory hops, and integrates with a new shadow-KV scheduler to prewarm likely-to-be-used KV shards. Goals: reduce p50/p95 latency, improve throughput under continuous batching, and simplify runtime fallbacks so routing can favor a single optimized path for most models. Design highlights: 1) Harmony kernel implements a fused qk->softmax->attn*V path with an optional fused rotary application step; the kernel exposes a fastpath when rotary embeddings are contiguous or stride-1, and a generic path for legacy layouts. 2) Coordinator: small CPU-side shim that canonicalizes rotary/rope offsets across model variants, rewrites per-request metadata to align KV indexing, and calculates per-request tiling hints for the batcher. 3) Shadow-KV scheduler: runs alongside the real KV cache and simulates warmups using low-priority prefetch requests driven by the coordinator's access predictions; scheduler supports soft eviction scores and sequence-aware aging. 4) Continuous batching: the batcher consumes coordinator tiling hints to create tighter-preserving batches (minimizing padding) and to decide when to opportunistically fuse short sequences into micro-batches to keep GPU pipelines full. Implementation notes: - Harmony kernel written in CUDA with templated FP16/FP32 paths and explicit FP16 accumulation where beneficial. - Uses per-warp tile transposes to avoid global transpose passes for many common layouts. - Rotary normalization step implemented inline with minimal kernel divergence; when stride-1 rotary is detected the kernel takes a specialized vectorized path. - Coordinator is intentionally lightweight (single-threaded control loop per worker) to avoid adding scheduling jitter. - Shadow-KV scheduler operates with capped bandwidth and backpressure so it cannot starve user requests. Benchmarks (on p4d-like instance, sequence lengths 512/2048/8192, batch sizes tuned per test): - 512: p50 latency -10% vs baseline, p99 -6%, throughput +8% - 2048: p50 -18%, p99 -12%, throughput +22% - 8192 (long context): p50 -25%, p99 -18%, throughput +30% - Under continuous batching microbench (mixed seq distribution), cost per token reduced ~14% while maintaining target p95 SLO. Compatibility and fallbacks: - Kernel registers itself under existing kernel registry and advertises capabilities; the runtime will prefer harmony when model flags for rotary/rope are set or when coordinator canonicalization can be applied. - For models with bespoke rotary layouts, runtime falls back to the generic harmony path or the legacy kernel. Testing and CI: - Added unit coverage for rotary normalization and tiled transpose. - Integration tests exercise streaming, long-context KV prewarm, and canary can run with scripts/canary_rollout_attn.sh. - Perf CI job added that runs longseq_microbench.py and uploads trace artifacts. Rollout plan: 1) Canary in staging fleet for 48h using low percentage traffic with shadow-KV enabled. 2) Monitor p50/p95 and cost per token metrics; rollback if p99 regresses >5% or error rates increase. 3) Gradually increase to 25% then 100% if stable. Risk and mitigations: - Numerical regressions: added golden-model evals against reference kernels; nightly regression alerts in Optimize linked to prompt sets. - Scheduler bandwidth could induce pressure; we cap shadow prefetch and include dynamic backoff. - Edge-case rotary layouts: coordinator logs and auto-falls back to legacy kernel with telemetry to prioritize additional layout support. Checklist: - [x] Kernel correctness tests - [x] Integration tests for streaming and KV warmup - [x] Perf benchmarks run and reviewed - [x] Docs updated (ops/harmony_kernel.md) - [x] Canary rollout script included Related Linear tickets: ENG-3218 (kernel work), ENG-3302 (kv scheduler), ENG-3375 (perf CI).
Aisha Patel: Please add a p99 breakdown by GPU utilization and kernel occupancy for the 2048/8192 runs; also ensure the FP16 accumulation path has stochastic rounding disabled by default.
Liam Chen: Added perf artifacts under perf/trace and verified FP16 path uses deterministic rounding; updated CI to capture occupancy metrics.
Marcus Li: Concerned about coordinator adding scheduling jitter; can we confirm single-threaded loop introduces <200us variance at 1000 RPS?
Liam Chen: Measured end-to-end variance with synthetic load; coordinator adds ~80us median and ~170us 95th at 1000 RPS on our staging VMs, added numbers to benchmark notes.
Sofia Ramirez: Shadow-KV scheduler could be noisy; request a circuit-breaker if prefetch error rate increases or if total cache spill grows beyond threshold.
Liam Chen: Implemented breaker that disables shadow prefetch for 5m if any of the safety heuristics trip; added telemetry counters.
Evan Brooks: Approve after seeing the long-seq integration tests and canary rollout plan.
Introduce attn-harmony: a fused attention kernel with integrated rotary/rope coordinator and a shadow-KV scheduler that reduces latency and improves throughput on long-context workloads. Opt-in via runtime kernel flags; canary rollout required. Provides ~15-30% throughput improvements and 10-25% p50 reductions across tested sequence lengths.
payload.title: attn-harmony: fused attention kernel with rope/rotary coordinator and shadow-KV scheduler

Problem: we are double-counting burst usage when the same customer request is retried (client retries, gateway retries after 5xx/timeout, and some 429 backoff paths). In beta, this showed up as duplicate burst usage line items for the same request window and was flagged in SUP-28488 and during reconciliation sampling. Root cause: the burst metering emitter currently treats each attempt as billable because we do not have a stable request-scoped idempotency key carried end-to-end into the metering aggregation stage; request_id/trace_id are not consistently preserved across retry code paths. Fix: introduce a request-scoped idempotency key that is generated at the gateway if missing, propagated to the data plane and metering emitter, and used to dedupe burst billable events before exporting to billing. Also add a reconciliation guard that detects duplicates that slip through (e.g., telemetry lag / partial outages) and blocks export with an alert. Details: 1) API/gateway: accept and forward X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key; if absent, generate a ULID per incoming request and reuse it across internal retry attempts. 2) Metering: include idempotency_key on burst usage events; dedupe in the burst_usage_aggregator on (tenant_id, region, hw_class, pool_id, idempotency_key) with a bounded TTL and hashed storage to avoid high-cardinality raw keys. 3) Billing export: export a deduped_usage_count and dropped_duplicate_attempts metric; add a hard reconciliation check that fails the export batch if duplicate keys exceed a small threshold (defaults to 0.01%) and pages on-call for billing pipeline. 4) Tests: add integration test for retry paths to ensure only one billable burst event per idempotency key; add unit tests for dedupe window behavior and hash collisions (expected negligible; we still include tenant/pool scoping). Rollout: behind feature flag billing.burst_idempotency_dedupe_enabled (default off). Plan is to enable in staging immediately, then 10% of Dedicated burst tenants in us-east for 24h, then ramp. Risk: incorrect dedupe could under-bill if keys are reused incorrectly; mitigated by scoping on tenant+pool and generating server-side keys when absent. Note: this PR does not change customer-visible request semantics; it only makes billing/metering idempotent across retries.
Cole Summers: Can you confirm we’re deduping at the right layer? If we dedupe at emission we might still get duplicates due to retries from different processes. Nadia Rahman: Agreed; dedupe is in the aggregator (central path before export), not at the emitter. Emitter always emits per-attempt but includes idempotency_key so we can attribute retries and track dropped duplicates. Ethan Park: Please make sure the header is documented and that control plane schema doesn’t accidentally treat it as a stable customer identifier. Also, what’s the validation story? Nadia Rahman: Updated OpenAPI to mark header as optional, max length 128, allowed charset [A-Za-z0-9-_]. Internally we hash it (xxh3_128) and store only the hash; raw header is not persisted. Rishi Malhotra: Reconciliation behavior: failing a batch blocks invoicing—what’s the expected frequency and who gets paged? Nadia Rahman: Threshold default 0.01% duplicates per batch; in normal behavior it should be 0. The job pages billing pipeline on-call (rotation includes me + Cole) and posts to #eng-platform with tenant and batch id. We also emit a metric so finance can spot anomalies before invoice close. Sean Gallagher: Any chance this creates noisy alerts during telemetry lag incidents? Nadia Rahman: The check uses a sliding window and ignores known-degraded states when metering ingestion lag > 2m (existing metering_lag gate). Added a runbook note and ensured we don’t flap by requiring 3 consecutive failing batches before paging. Cole Summers (requested changes): Please add an integration test that simulates 429 retry and ensure we don’t charge twice. Nadia Rahman: Added burst_retry_billing_idempotency_test covering 429 backoff and a synthetic gateway retry on 5xx. Cole Summers: Approved. Ethan Park: Approved. Sean Gallagher: Approved after runbook link added. Merge: Squash + merge.
Billing/metering: Burst usage is now idempotent across retries via request-scoped idempotency keys. Added reconciliation guardrails and metrics to detect duplicate charging attempts. No API behavior change; customers may optionally provide X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key, otherwise Redwood generates one.
payload.title: Fix billing double-counting on Dedicated burst retries (idempotency + reconciliation)

Context and motivation: builds on ENG-9472 to further reduce wasted CI cycles and prevent unsafe dependency upgrades reaching main. We observed repeated flaps where dependabot PRs passed unit tests but caused flaky integration test reruns and occasional broken releases. This PR introduces a premerge viability check that runs a lightweight, deterministic set of validations and a dep-safety gate for automated dependency updates.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a new GitHub Action 'premerge-viability' that runs early in the PR lifecycle; it performs quick static checks, a minimal lint (fast mode), and a targeted smoke test matrix against a pinned integration fixture. The intent is to fail fast and avoid starting heavy integration shards.
- Integrates a dependency-safety check (based on the internal dep-curator script) that verifies pinned transitive deps, checks for removed exports via a small static analyzer, and blocks merges from dependabot if risk > low.
- Refactors CI workflows so linters and typechecks are run as composite actions (python/ts), de-duplicating setup and reducing avg CI wall time for multi-language changes.
- Introduces a lightweight 'ci-dedupe' manifest that prevents duplicate test suites across staged lanes (fast feedback lanes will no longer start redundant integration shards already reserved for nightly runs).
- Small repo hygiene changes: cleans stale .gitignore entries, normalizes pre-commit hooks, and enforces 'signed-commits' for release-* branches via branch protection config snippets in workflows.

Commits (high level):
- feat(ci): add premerge-viability action and workflow (aisha)
- feat(dep): dep-safety integration + risk scoring hook (aisha)
- refactor(ci): convert python/ts linters to composite actions and consolidate setup steps (chen)
- chore(repo): tidy .gitignore and pre-commit config (sofia)
- fix(ci): dedupe test lanes and add manifest-based guard (aisha)

Changed areas / files (high-level):
- .github/workflows/premerge-viability.yaml (new)
- .github/actions/composite/fast-lint-action/action.yml (new/refactor)
- .github/actions/dep-safety-check/run.sh (new)
- .github/workflows/ci-staged-lanes.yaml (modified)
- infra/ci/ci-dedupe-manifest.yaml (new)
- tools/dep-curator/score.py (modified)
- scripts/release/generate-draft.sh (small tweak to emit draft metadata)
- package.json, pyproject.toml (pin cleanup hints)

Notable implementation details:
- premerge-viability is intentionally conservative: it uses short timeouts and a small prebuilt fixture image so it remains cheap. The action matrix runs against node/python runtimes we support and returns a structured status (ok/warn/fail). The action emits annotations to the PR and adds a status check named 'premerge/viability'.
- dep-safety-check computes a heuristic risk score (0-100) using: semantic version delta, changed export set size, downstream usage count (best-effort), and a small AST diff to detect deleted/renamed exports. The threshold for blocking dependabot is configurable via repo-level .dep-safety.yaml. Example config: "block_threshold: 30".
- Composite lint actions factor out expensive language setup (toolchain install/caching) so multiple lint jobs in a matrix share cached toolchains and avoid repeated installs. The composite action also surfaces a 'fast' mode which runs a subset of linters when the PR touches <= 10 files.
- ci-dedupe-manifest is a human-editable YAML file that enumerates canonical shards; the workflow uses it to short-circuit duplicate shard launches. This prevents two workflows from booting the same heavy integration job.

Review conversation (summary):
- Liam O'Connor: requested tighter timeouts on the premerge fixtures and an explicit opt-out label for long-running test PRs. Action: added 'ci/skip-fastpath' label handling.
- Chen Wei: asked for metrics exports from the dep-safety-check (histogram of scores). Action: added a minimal Prometheus push gateway report and a trace id in the action logs.
- Sofia Martinez: flagged the release script change and requested compatibility with our changelog generator. Action: release/generate-draft.sh was updated to include changelog fragments and to create annotated draft release instead of auto-publishing.
- Security review (brief): verified that dep-safety runs in a read-only sandbox and that any credentials used for downstream heuristics are optional and default to offline heuristics.
- Author replies: updated timeouts, added metrics, documented opt-out label and .dep-safety.yaml, wrote unit tests for the risk scorer.

CI and testing:
- Local unit tests: pass (new unit tests for score.py).
- GitHub Actions: premerge and main CI lanes passed on the final run. Notable transient failure during iteration: flakiness in the old integration shard that motivated the ci-dedupe guard; fixed by dedupe manifest and a backoff in the scheduler.

Risk and rollout plan:
- Feature toggles are used: premerge-viability is enabled for selected repos only via .github/enable-premerge.yaml. We will enable for core repos for 2 weeks then roll org-wide.
- Dep-safety default is non-blocking for human-authored PRs; it is blocking only for dependabot/automated update PRs initially.

Merge outcome: squash and merge. Changelog entry created under 'ci improvements' with a short summary and rollout notes.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-9601: expand risk heuristics with runtime test coverage mapping.
- ENG-9622: dashboard for premerge-viability pass/fail trends and dep-safety scores.

If you want to test locally: see tools/dep-curator/README.md (includes a small docker-compose fixture used by the premerge action) and run: 
- ./tools/dep-curator/score.py --old-rev HEAD~1 --new-rev HEAD --output json
- act -P ubuntu-latest=nektos/act-environments-ubuntu:18.04 -j premerge-viability

Thanks to Chen and Sofia for the review and to infra for help with action runner quotas.
Adds a premerge viability gate and integrates a dependency-safety check into CI; refactors lint/test runners to avoid duplicate work; small repo hygiene cleanups.

Motivation: We have persistent gaps when attributing kernel- and queue-level costs back to the original API invocation. This makes it hard to detect regressions that only appear after retries, fast-fail routing, or multi-stage models. This PR introduces a lightweight 'invocation edge anchor' that tags the first externally-observed span for an invocation and threads that anchor id through downstream kernel and batching spans. The anchor enables deterministic per-invocation cost attribution, improved grouping for long-tail token-cost analysis, and simpler joins between logs, traces, and billing events.

What this changes (summary): 1) New anchor header propagation: runtime sets X-Inv-Anchor on ingress and preserves it across retries and internal requeueing. 2) Tracing integration: span enrichment to include inv_anchor_id and phase labels (parse, kv_cache, decode, send). 3) Metrics rollups: cohort-backed rollups by anchor-phase that power per-invocation token-cost and latency histograms. 4) Dashboard: new invocation-edge Anchors dashboard with sparkline cost-by-phase, cohort breakdown, and a tie-out panel to billing events. 5) Alert tuning: new adaptive alert rules that use anchor-cohorts to suppress noisy token-cost alerts from known heavy prompt cohorts. 6) E2E tests and a small util for reconciling anchor -> billing join keys.

Why this PR is different: rather than changing sampling rates or adding more aggregation jobs, the anchor provides a single join key that dramatically reduces downstream cardinality when doing per-invocation joins. This accelerates our ability to run deterministic regressions on token cost and latency across retries and fallbacks.

Checklist: [x] Propagate anchor header in runtime ingress [x] Add anchor to spans at kernel/batcher layers [x] Emit per-anchor phase counters and histograms [x] Dashboard JSON and panels added [x] Unit + integration tests for anchor propagation [x] Rollout plan in PR description (staged: beta tenants -> 10% roll -> 100%)

Rollout plan (short): stage to stable-tenants (opt-in) for 48h to validate billing joins and traffic behavior; enable at 10% across regions for 24h; full release if no cost regressions or token-attribution mismatches.

References: Linear ENG-1982 (anchor design), ENG-2037 (dashboard panels), Jira INT-3241 (support case where tenant billing mismatch observed).
Diego Alvarez: Nice approach — I like a single join key. Question: what happens to anchors for streamed, chunked responses?
Asha Menon (author): For streaming we set the anchor on the first request frame and include it in the chunk metadata header. Kernel/batcher code reads and ignores if absent (backcompat).
Priya Shah: Need to ensure the anchor doesn't inflate cardinality when callers mutate prompts per-retry. Suggest adding a bounded LRU for anchor->prompt hashes in rollup job.
Asha Menon (author): Added an LRU-backed deduper in telemetry/rollups to limit cardinality — see anchor_cohorts_job.yaml and commit c9d2ea0.
Liam O'Connor: CI flakes on telemetry e2e, please make tests idempotent and add a retry wrapper.
Asha Menon (author): Added retry wrapper and expanded test timeouts; reran CI.
Add invocation-edge anchors to enable deterministic per-invocation cost and latency attribution, new dashboard panels for anchor-phase rollups, and alert tuning to reduce churn from heavy prompt cohorts.
Enable rollout by feature-flag: observability.inv_anchor.enable. Monitor billing join error rate and anchor propagation failure metric (telemetry.anchor.propagation.failures) during rollout.
1) Backpopulate anchor ids for 24h of recent traces for customers who opt-in to historical joins (job scheduled), 2) Add runbook entry for anchor propagation mismatch (docs/observability/runbooks/anchor_mismatch.md).
Anchor id is a random 128-bit value, no PII. We avoid embedding prompt text in anchor metadata; only a stable hash is used for deduping in rollups.
1) Start a local runtime with feature flag enabled, 2) Send a request that triggers a retry and verify X-Inv-Anchor header across retries, 3) Check traces in APM for inv_anchor_id on kernel spans, 4) Verify dashboard shows a sample anchor cohort and costs map back to billing events.
Follow-up PR will add an opt-out sampling mode and a compact anchor alias to reduce label cardinality further.

payload.body:
Motivation: streaming requests under mixed workloads exhibited spiky first-byte latency (TTFB) and poor tail behavior when KV prefetches and microbatch drains collided with kernel selection. This PR introduces an autotuned coordinator that couples per-stream throttle windows with probabilistic KV prefetch warming and drain prioritization, aiming to reduce median and tail TTFB without regressing throughput. Key ideas: 1) Per-stream latency budgets derived from SLA config and recent percentiles drive a soft throttle that caps emission window size and dynamically stretches inter-token yield points. 2) A lightweight prefetch score uses recent KV cache hit/miss ratios, token generation velocity, and kernel warm indicators to trigger prefetches earlier for likely-follow prefixes. 3) Cooperative microbatch drain ordering: streams with tighter budgets and active prefetches are prioritized for kernel allocation and KV reheating. 4) Autotuner observes background load signals (device utilization, kernel queue depth, histogram of token latencies) and adjusts throttle aggressiveness and prefetch lead-time using exponential moving averages. This was implemented with low-overhead data structures and fast-path checks to avoid impacting the hot token loop. The description below outlines changes, benchmarks, tests and rollout plan.
feat(streaming): add StreamAutotuner and ThrottleWindow manager
perf(kv): introduce probabilistic prefetch scorer and async prefetch queue
sched: cooperative drain priority and budget-aware microbatch sorter
core(runtime): fast-path checks in token emission loop to consult throttle window
tests: add e2e perf job and synthetic concurrency harness
docs: streaming tuning guide and observability dashboard tiles
Synthetic mixed-workload (chat+completion) with 256 concurrent streams on g4dn-like nodes: median TTFB -18%, p95 TTFB -35%, p99 -20% under constrained GPU kernel capacity. Throughput unchanged within +/-3% under steady load. In low-load scenarios p50 improved ~10ms. Benchmarks include cold-KV, warm-KV and interleaved arrivals.
Verified no regression on throughput and memory; memory allocations for autotuner are bounded per-stream (~1.2KB). Kernel selection latency unaffected on average. Unit and integration perf monitors added.
Canary -> 10% of traffic (observability flags) 24h -> 50% 48h -> full roll when p95 TTFB improvement stable. Feature gated behind runtime.flags.streaming_autotune and kv.prefetch_async. Fallback to previous scheduler on error or SLO breach.
unit tests for throttle window edge cases, property tests for prefetch scorer, e2e perf job in CI that runs nightly, integration scenario to validate kv warmup ordering
New doc 'streaming-tuning.md' explains throttle window semantics, recommended per-customer SLA mappings, and knobs: autotune aggressiveness, prefetch lead-time, microbatch priority weights. Added dashboard tiles for per-stream budget burn, prefetch hit-rate, and kernel queue latencies.
Ava Chen: Nice approach. Can we bound the autotuner adjustments to avoid oscillation under highly bursty traffic? Please add a small dampening factor and document expected oscillation behaviour.
Diego Morales: I saw a minor allocation spike in the preload path during the first synthetic run. Is the prefetch queue zero-copy across interop? Let's ensure we don't introduce per-token allocs in the hot path.
Samir Patel: Requesting a flag to disable probabilistic prefetch for Dedicated customers who prefer deterministic behavior. Also add a short note on telemetry cost (ingest cardinality).
Ava Chen: Tests look good but please add a regression threshold to the nightly perf job to catch accidental TTFB regressions in future PRs.
Lina Ortega: Added dampening factor (0.75) to the autotuner and a configurable max step-size. Updated docs to explain trade-offs.
Lina Ortega: Prefetch queue now reuses a preallocated slab and uses pointer handoff; removed hot-path allocations. Alloc overhead verified in perf test.
Lina Ortega: Added runtime flag runtime.flags.kv_prefetch_probabilistic=false and documented telemetry cardinality.
Introduce streaming autotuner that couples per-stream soft throttles with probabilistic KV prefetching and budget-aware microbatch ordering to reduce TTFB and smoothing tail latency. Feature is feature-gated and rolled out gradually. See docs/streaming-tuning.md for details and tuning guidance.
Ops: enable runtime.flags.streaming_autotune in staging and monitor dashboards/streaming-ttfb. Watch kernel queue depth and per-device util to avoid overload. Fallback via runtime.flags.streaming_autotune=false if SLO regressions are observed.
Added StreamAutotuner, ThrottleWindow, PrefetchScorer, microbatch sorter priority, observability tiles, tests and docs. Backwards compatible by default behind flags.

payload.body:
Motivation: Continuous canary signals are great at detecting regressions but often leave engineers blind about why a regression happened. This PR adds an "Explainable Regression Inspector" to the perf-canary pipeline: a lightweight, streaming attribution layer that produces cohort- and feature-level attributions alongside existing latency/throughput detectors, plus an adaptive stratified sampler that preserves rare but high-risk cohorts. The goal is faster RCA and safer automated rollouts.

What this change introduces: 1) Streaming attribution processor that ingests perf events and emits per-cohort attribution vectors (approximate SHAP-style contributions using a fast linear-interaction sketch). 2) Adaptive stratified sampler that decides which requests to keep for detailed tracing/kv-capture based on attribution uncertainty and recent cohort volatility. 3) New "deferred cutover" rollout guard: a canary gate that requires attribution weights for top-N contributing features to stabilize (moving window) before completing a cutover. 4) Telemetry and dashboards: new metrics (inspector.attribution_entropy, inspector.top_feature_shift, inspector.sampler_retention_pct) and a correlation heatmap UI under Observability -> Perf Canary. 5) Backward-compatible event schema v2 extension (perf_event.v2) with optional attribution blob. 6) End-to-end canary job and smoke tests added to CI.

Implementation notes: The inspector is implemented as a streaming service (inspector-worker) colocated with canary aggregators; it uses feature hashing and a lightweight online interaction estimator to bound memory usage. Sampling decisions are soft (tagged) so downstream systems can ignore them if they don't understand the tag. Attribution computation is tunable (fast-mode vs. accurate-mode) via the canary policy YAML. The deferred cutover gate plugs into the existing rollout orchestration by subscribing to canary evaluation events and rejecting completes until stabilization criteria pass.

Testing and verification: Unit tests for the estimator and sampler (coverage added). Integration tests that run against the local canary harness (perf-canary/test/harness) with synthetic traffic profiles to validate attribution correctness and sampler retention targets. An e2e canary run was executed in the staging cluster (see CI run perf-canary-e2e/824159). Memory and CPU profile runs included to ensure inspector_worker stays below the cluster resource SLOs.

Runbook / Rollout: Default rollout is disabled; operators can opt-in by setting canary.policy.inspector.enabled: true. When enabled, the default deferred-cutover window is 30 minutes with a conservative entropy threshold. The PR adds a runbook at docs/runbooks/explainable_inspector.md with troubleshooting steps for noisy attributions and guidance for tuning the sampler.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] e2e canary smoke - [x] Docs and runbook - [x] Observability dashboards - [x] Backwards-compatible schema extension

Related: ENG-1289 ties to the global canary observability effort; SUP-4821 is a customer-reported case where cohort attribution would have sped RCA.
Anika Rao: The estimator looks promising but memory usage needs a hard cap; please add a circuit breaker or an LRU eviction for the hash buckets.
Maya Chen: Added a soft-LRU and a max_buckets config with sane defaults; included stress test results in the PR description.
Jonas Keller: Can we ensure the sampler tags are optional so older services don't break? request: add backwards compatibility note.
Maya Chen: Sampler tags are optional and ignored by downstream if unknown; added explicit doc and comment in proto.
Priya Nair: Approved after e2e pass and addressing the memory cap comment.
CI: unit-tests — pass
Lint: gofmt/golangci-lint — pass
Integration: inspector_integration — pass
e2e: perf-canary-e2e (staging) — pass after one rerun (flake in harness)
Perf regression CV: within threshold (0.3%)
Adds a new Explainable Regression Inspector to perf-canary: streaming attributions, adaptive stratified sampling, and a deferred-cutover rollout guard. Default off; enables richer RCA and safer automated rollouts when turned on.
Default configuration keeps inspector disabled. To enable in an existing canary policy set canary.policy.inspector.enabled=true and tune inspector.window_mins / inspector.entropy_threshold. If operator sees high attribution entropy for many cohorts, increase sampler retention_pct or reduce feature hashing resolution.

payload.body:
Motivation: customers using response_format with strict JSON schema validation saw production regressions when upstream models emitted small structural drift mid-stream or emitted toolcall boundaries that were split across stream frames. We need a runtime that can validate streaming output without aborting useful partial responses, provide actionable diagnostics, and keep OpenAI-compat behavior clear for strict vs lenient modes. Summary: Introduces a streaming-aware response validator with checkpoint tokens and automatic lightweight repairs for minor JSON-schema violations (configurable via response_format.strict_mode: 'strict'|'lenient'|'auto-repair'). Adds a 'partial_json' event type to streaming output for OpenAI adapter when lenient repair occurs and a structured error mapping for strict failures. Design highlights: 1) Streaming checkpoints: validator emits stable checkpoint tokens (opaque resume_token) at schema-consistent boundaries to allow the service to request a resume from the model or client; 2) Auto-repair heuristics: for common issues (trailing commas, single-quoted strings, missing closing braces), the runtime attempts deterministic corrections and appends a repair_metadata object to the final response in lenient/auto-repair modes; 3) Tool/function-call fencing: validator recognizes toolcall spans and will not apply repairs inside fence blocks; instead it emits a tool_fence_violation event for operator review; 4) OpenAI adapter behavior: when response_format.strict_mode is 'strict' we return a structured 400 with error.code = "E_SCHEMA_STRICT" and a machine-readable error_hints array; when 'lenient' the stream emits partial_json events followed by a final patched object and a telemetry tag. Rollout and compatibility: default remains 'lenient' for hosted API to avoid breaking existing users; strict is opt-in and documented in API changelog. Added feature flag runtime.streaming_schema_validator.v1 to enable canary on Dedicated and Private. Telemetry: new metrics schema.repair_count, repair_types, resume_token_issued, and schema_violation_rate. Backwards compatibility: clients that expect raw OpenAI stream chunks may see new partial_json/repair events when using lenient mode—we added adapter docs and SDK unpack helpers. Testing: unit tests for 38 heuristics, end-to-end tests with toy models that emit fragmentation, and an integration test that exercises function/tool call fencing. Checklist: [x] design doc linked to ENG-2147 [x] tests added [x] telemetry wired [x] docs updated [x] canary flag added.
feat(runtime): introduce streaming schema validator and checkpoint tokens
feat(api): add response_format.strict_mode enum and parsing logic
chore(openai-adapter): emit partial_json event and map strict errors to structured codes
fix(runtime/repair): make auto-repair deterministic and record repair metadata
test: add unit/e2e tests for fragmented toolcall and repair heuristics
docs: API docs and SDK unpack helper examples
Eliot Barnes (2026-02-19): Looks great overall. Concern: auto-repair heuristics risk masking model regressions. Can we emit a flag in trace/span that shows the exact repair delta?
Priya Nair (2026-02-19): Yes — added repair_metadata with before/after diff and repair_type. It's included in spans and in the final response when lenient/auto-repair is enabled.
Marco Ruiz (2026-02-20): Tests failing on CI for a race between resume_token expiration and client reconnect. Suggest adding token TTL + renew path.
Priya Nair (2026-02-21): Added TTL and token_renew endpoint; updated tests to simulate reconnect and token refresh.
Zoe Kim (2026-02-24): Small nit: rename 'heuristics.py' to 'repair_rules.py' to avoid misspelling — not blocking.
Priya Nair (2026-02-25): Renamed file and updated imports; pushing final fix. CI now green. Approving for squash merge.
Adds streaming-aware JSON schema validator with optional auto-repair and resume tokens. OpenAI-compat adapter now emits partial_json events for lenient repairs and structured error codes for strict failures. Feature gated for canary rollouts.
