payload.body:
Context and motivation: We frequently see regressions that only appear when model behavior is exercised under realistic session patterns (long-lived sessions, stateful KV cache reuse). Existing canaries and shadow modes don't replicate session composition or allow controlled load pressure against shadow variants. This PR introduces a new rollout strategy ('session-shadow-pressure') that combines session-consistent shadowing with adjustable pressure testing and an automated quarantine/rollback advisor pipeline.

Design summary: The mode has three coordinated pieces: (1) Session anchoring in the router/scheduler so the same user-session is consistently routed to the same canary/shadow instance for the duration of the window; (2) Pressure simulator that can replay production traffic shapes (qps, token distribution, concurrency) against shadow replicas at configurable fractions and can override sampling to stress KV-cache hit/miss scenarios; (3) Quarantine manager + rollback advisor that monitors multi-dimensional drift signals (semantic regressions, latency tail, token costs, hallucination heuristics) and either triggers cohort quarantine or surfaces an automated rollback recommendation with suggested revert commit + playbook.

Config knobs and API: New rollout.strategy.type = "session-shadow-pressure". Key parameters (all optional): session_ttl_seconds, pressure_fraction, pressure_profile (burst|steady|spike), kv_cache_stress (low|med|high), drift_thresholds (json-encoded metric thresholds), quarantine_window_seconds, rollback_advisor_enabled (bool). The openapi doc and example YAML are included.

Runtime changes: session_anchor.go augments the request router to stamp and persist a session token (cookie/header) and attach session affinity metadata to a serving token so in-flight requests reuse the same cache lane and physical pod selection. The pressure_simulator hooks into the routing layer and the traffic mirror pipeline to apply controlled amplification factors and synthetic cache churn. quarantine_manager.go implements an actor that marks cohorts as "quarantined" and transitions their traffic to a safe baseline variant while preserving telemetry for postmortem. rollback_advisor.go computes a drift score using weighted signals and attempts quick counterfactuals (replay the cohort against the previous model snapshot) to validate rollback recommendations.

Testing and validation: Added unit tests for session affinity edge cases, integration tests that run a 30-minute pressure profile against a small cluster in CI, and two e2e scenarios that assert quarantine and rollback advisor behavior under injected semantic drift. The PR includes a lightweight local simulator (examples/session-shadow-pressure.yaml) so SRE and SE can reproduce locally.

Operational considerations: Default behavior is opt-in and conservative (pressure_fraction defaults to 0.01; quarantine requires sustained drift > threshold for quarantine_window_seconds). Rollback advisor issues a non-destructive recommendation by default (no automatic rollback unless rollback_advisor_enabled=true and rollout.auto_revert=true). Audit logs are emitted for quarantine/rollback actions and exposed in the console.

Migration and compatibility: No changes required for existing rollout configs. New fields are ignored by older controllers. For Dedicated/Private deployments, the pressure simulator toggles are gated behind operator flags to avoid unintended load on customer hardware.

Checklists: - [x] API + OpenAPI changes documented and example config added. - [x] Scheduler/session affinity implemented and covered by unit tests. - [x] Pressure simulator and config referenced in runbook. - [x] Quarantine manager emits alerts and writes audit events. - [x] Rollback advisor runs counterfactual replays in a sandbox and provides deterministic recommendations. - [x] Manual QA run in staging with full traffic replay completed.

Review conversation (high level):
- Liam O'Connor (review): "This looks solid overall. Two requests: add rate-limits to the pressure_simulator to avoid overload in small clusters, and ensure TTLs are bounded to prevent session token proliferation."
- Maya (author): "Added rate-limiter and bounded TTL (configurable with safe defaults). See scheduler changes commit and unit tests."
- Diego Martinez (review): "Can we add an opt-out for KV cache stress in Dedicated clusters? Also add an alert routing note for SRE on quarantine events."
- Maya: "Added operator gate and alert routing doc. CI e2e passes locally and in the shared staging project."
- Sana Iyer (approval): "Verified e2e scenario reproduces expected quarantine + recommended rollback. Approving with one minor doc ask; added inline."

CI summary: Initial pipeline failed on flakey integration test (timeout under 30s), re-run after increasing timeouts; all checks pass (unit, lint, integration, e2e smoke). Performance microbenchmarks show median latency impact <1% at pressure_fraction=0.01 and acceptable tail increases at higher stress levels noted in docs.

Merge decision and post-merge steps: Squashed and merged to main. Post-merge: (1) ops to enable example flags in staging (infra PR: infra/k8s/rollout-crd.yaml), (2) schedule a 1-hour staged canary in staging and one small canary in dedicated testing clusters, (3) run the provided smoke playbook in docs/runbooks/session-shadow-pressure.md.

Related work and references: ENG-4127 (design spike for session-consistent shadowing), ENG-4132 (rollback advisor prototype), runbook and example configs included.

Caveats and known limitations: The counterfactual replayer expects determinism; non-deterministic models (sampling hot seeds) may produce noisy drift scores. We added heuristics and confidence bounds but recommend human review on ambiguous advisories.

If anything is unclear or you'd like a short walkthrough, I can demo the staging runbook and the console quarantine trace.
- New rollout mode: session-anchored shadow pressure canary.
- Auto-quarantine: cohorts showing drift are isolated automatically.
- Rollback advisor: automated recommendations + safe revert playbook.
- Backwards-compatible config; opt-in via rollout.strategy.type="session-shadow-pressure".
Liam O'Connor: This looks solid overall. Two requests: add rate-limits to the pressure_simulator to avoid overload in small clusters, and ensure TTLs are bounded to prevent session token proliferation.
Maya Chen: Added rate-limiter and bounded TTL (configurable with safe defaults). See scheduler changes commit and unit tests.
Diego Martinez: Can we add an opt-out for KV cache stress in Dedicated clusters? Also add an alert routing note for SRE on quarantine events.
Maya Chen: Added operator gate and alert routing doc. CI e2e passes locally and in the shared staging project.
Sana Iyer: Verified e2e scenario reproduces expected quarantine + recommended rollback. Approving with one minor doc ask; added inline.
Opt-in rollout strategy. Admins should read docs/runbooks/session-shadow-pressure.md before enabling in production. Default is conservative (1% pressure).
Enable operator gate in Dedicated clusters before running pressure profiles. Watch auto_quarantine.alert and rollback_advisor.alert; both write audit events to /audit/rollouts.
- staging run completed
- e2e scenario reproduces quarantine and advisor recommendation
- manual rollback validated
- runbook smoke playbook executed
1) infra: apply k8s CRD updates to staging cluster.
2) ops: enable pressure flags in staging.
3) schedule 60m canary run with pressure_fraction=0.05.
4) monitor quarantine/rollback alerts and adjust thresholds if noisy.
This PR is intentionally conservative and opt-in. The rollback advisor is non-destructive by default and built to reduce MTTD for regressions surfaced under realistic session load patterns.

payload.body:
Summary: This PR adds a cross-language credential lease protocol (lease/renew/revoke cycle) and a set of 'sidestream' helper primitives that let streaming consumers rehearse reconnections with minimal auth friction. Motivation: customers have reported tail latency during credential refresh in hot streaming paths; teams repeatedly implemented ad-hoc lease/heartbeat logic in each SDK. The unified protocol centralizes semantics, reduces duplication, and provides ergonomics for typical streaming patterns (pause/resume, checkpointed reconnect, graceful token handoff).

What changed (high level):
- Core: new lightweight LeaseManager interface and wire-compatible lease token envelope used by py/ts/go SDKs. Lease semantics: TTL, renew window, optional heartbeat, deterministic revocation reason codes.
- Sidestream helpers: small, language-idiomatic helpers that wrap a StreamConnection and LeaseManager to provide pre-warmed reconnection attempts (fast path) and safe fallback (slow path).
- SDK changes: Python (sync + async) added LeaseManager and StreamingSidestream class; TypeScript added SidestreamConnector and minor ergonomic renames for stream iterator helpers; Go added leasefacade and SidestreamDialer with context-aware cancellation.
- Version bumps: py v1.12.0, ts v1.8.3, go v1.5.0. CHANGELOGs updated.

Files touched (representative):
- sdk/python/redwood/lease.py (new)
- sdk/python/redwood/streaming/sidestream.py (new)
- sdk/typescript/src/credentials/lease.ts (new)
- sdk/typescript/src/stream/sidestream-connector.ts (new)
- sdk/go/lease/lease.go (new)
- sdk/go/stream/sidestream_dialer.go (new)
- sdk/*/CHANGELOG.md (updates across 3 SDKs)
- examples/sidestream/ (new samples for py/ts/go)

Small illustrative snippets (kept short):
Python (async):
```python
async with SidestreamConnector(stream_factory, lease_manager) as conn:
    async for chunk in conn.stream():
        process(chunk)
```
TypeScript:
```ts
const connector = new SidestreamConnector(factory, lease);
for await (const evt of connector.stream()) {
  handle(evt);
}
```
Go (conceptual):
```go
dialer := sidestream.NewDialer(factory, lease)
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 5*time.Second)
defer cancel()
stream := dialer.Dial(ctx)
```

Commits: (summary)
- feat: add lease protocol and envelope (py/ts/go) (3 commits)
- feat: sidestream helper primitives and examples (3 commits)
- docs: changelogs and examples (2 commits)
- tests: add unit + integration tests for renew/failover semantics (4 commits)
- ci: matrix updates to run sidestream e2e across py/ts/go runners (2 commits)

Testing and CI: Added unit tests for lease TTL, renew window jitter, and revocation reasons. Integration e2e runs in CI spin up ephemeral local auth proxy and validates fast reconnect path under token rotation. CI matrix initially flaked on the Windows Go runner due to test timing; I tuned the timeouts and re-ran. Final CI: all checks passed (lint, unit, e2e matrix).

Review conversation (high level):
- Alan Kim (reviewer): "Great consolidation. A couple of ergonomics nits: rename 'renew_window' -> 'renew_before' for clarity; decouple heartbeat option from LeaseManager so consumers can opt out. Also add a quick example showing pause/resume where the sidestream pre-warms a connection while the old one drains."
- Priya (author): "Addressed: renamed field and added opt-out flag. Added pause/resume example and unit test (sidestream_prewarm_test)."
- Marisa Gomez (reviewer): "TS typing looks good, but please add a small note in the TS README about async iterator cancellation semantics so users don't leak timers."
- Priya: "Added README blurb and adjusted connector.close() to clear timers on cancel."
- Oleg Petrov (security review): "Surface token revocation reasons in telemetry and ensure no long-lived goroutines on revoke path."
- Priya: "Added telemetry tags and fixed goroutine leak in Go dialer by adding close channels and a small state machine test."

Follow-ups captured in Linear:
- ENG-3421: polish sidestream telemetry to include lease_reason codes.
- ENG-3499: implement server-side lease demo for Dedicated customers (backlog).

Release notes: "Adds unified credential lease protocol and sidestream helpers for streaming SDKs (Python v1.12.0, TypeScript v1.8.3, Go v1.5.0). Improves streaming reconnection latency during credential rotation and provides example patterns for pause/resume with pre-warmed reconnection."

Backward compatibility: Designed to be additive. Existing SDK consumers who don't opt into LeaseManager or SidestreamConnector see no behavior change. The changes are non-breaking for typical call sites; migration guides added to CHANGELOGs.

Performance: Microbenchmarks show ~40-60ms median improvement on reconnect latency in our hermetic e2e tests when sidestream fast path is used under hot token rotation scenarios.

Merge: squashed and merged to main on 2026-03-03 by Priya Nair. Merge method: squash. CI green at merge time. Tags: py/v1.12.0, ts/v1.8.3, go/v1.5.0 created post-merge.

Notes for maintainers: watch for additional e2e runs against Dedicated infra; ENG-3421 will be used to track telemetry polish. If any downstream SDK consumers report unexpected auth errors during rotation, ask for the 'lease_reason' tag from logs and file a quick follow-up.
Adds a unified credential lease protocol across Python/TS/Go SDKs; introduces sidestream helper APIs for lower-latency streaming reconnection; bumps SDK minor versions (py v1.12.0, ts v1.8.3, go v1.5.0).

Context: During a regional incident on 2026-02-14 we observed intermittent fastpath "fuse" failures where requests routed to the low-latency fastpath would trigger transient KV cache desyncs and then incur extreme tail latency. The incident engineering notes (SUP-4512) recommended an automated light-weight probe that can detect fastpath misfires and bias traffic to the slow/robust path for a bounded window rather than relying on coarse circuit flips.

What this PR does: Introduces two cooperating pieces: 1) a fastpath fuse prober (controlplane/prober) that periodically exercises a small synthetic request pattern against the fastpath and reports a concise probe outcome; 2) a slimline SLO medic (runtime/fallback_router) that consumes probe outcomes and applies a short-lived routing bias and shed recommendation when probe failure rate crosses threshold. Both pieces are intentionally conservative (short windows, backoff, and canary-only by default).

Key properties and motivations: - Minimize blast radius: bias window defaults to 10s and only affects up to 5% of matching tenant traffic (configurable per-tenant). - Observability-first: probe emits slo_medic.probe_duration_seconds, slo_medic.probe_outcome{ok,fail,timeout} and slo_medic.bias_applied_total with labels for region/model/tier. - Predictable behavior: Medic uses exponential cool-down and a sticky suppression to avoid oscillation; config maps include max bias duration and min probe samples. - Hotfixable: feature gate + runtime flags allow immediate disable; config is exposed via controlplane API and guarded by audit logs.

Changes included: - controlplane/prober/probe_controller.go: new controller, probe scheduler and small HTTP/GRPC harness for synthetic hits. - runtime/router/medic.go: bias decision logic, token-limited bias applicator and short-lived shed recommendations. - telemetry/metrics_registry.go: registered new probe/medic metrics + tagging. - docs/runs/ops/slo-medic.md: operational runbook with TTLs, alert tuning and rollback. - cmd/ctl/flags.go: feature-gate and defaults. - tests/prober_integration_test.go, router_medic_unit_test.go.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for bias decision and cooldown logic - [x] Integration test with synthetic fastpath misfire simulation - [x] Metrics and dashboard skeleton added - [x] Ops runbook and rollback steps - [x] Feature gated behind runtime flag

Testing and validation: Local unit tests and integration harness ran. A dedicated perf job (perf/fastpath-fuse-prober) was executed in staging to validate no measurable QPS or latency regression for steady-state traffic. Canary rollout plan executed: 1% tenants for 6h, evaluated metrics, then 5% for 12h before full rollout. No regressions seen in canaries.

Rollout plan: rollout via feature flag: start in staging, then prod canary (1% tenants), observe slo_medic.* metrics and token rejection rates. If bias_applied_total > 0 and overall p99 decreases then proceed to 5% and 25%. Rollback via feature flag or controlplane toggle documented in runbook.

Related: SUP-4512 (incident), ENG-8092 (follow-up iteration), SRE-1203 (alert tuning).
Adds a low-risk probe that detects fastpath fuse failures and applies a short, observable routing bias to stabilize SLOs. Includes metrics and an ops runbook entry.
Maya Patel: Can we tighten the default bias window from 10s to 5s for fast rollbacks? Concern about transient blips causing unnecessary shift.
Evan Brooks: I ran microbenchmarks; 5s increases oscillation risk. Kept 10s to ensure probe samples (min 3 per window). We can expose as runtime knob for rapid tuning.
Lars Jensen: Add a metric for 'bias_skipped_due_to_quota' so ops can see when tenant cap prevented biasing.
Evan Brooks: Added bias_skipped metric and unit test asserting quota behavior. Documented in runbook.
Priya Nair: LGTMed after CI green; please add a short dashboard for oncall to see probe trend and bias application per region.
Evan Brooks: Dashboard tiles added to team Grafana space (link in runbook).
This PR was created as a hotfix after SUP-4512 and intentionally keeps conservative defaults. Operators should monitor slo_medic.probe_outcome and bias_applied_total for at least two full canary cycles.
payload.title: Introduce fastpath fuse prober and slimline SLO medic

payload.body:
Motivation: Recent incidents where tenants with large prefix-KV footprints triggered blunt global shed policies exposed two gaps: (1) the SLO enforcer was blind to internal KV memory pressure which caused noisy oscillation when circuits opened/closed, and (2) soft-open transitions were too aggressive for bursty tenants. This change introduces an "SLO Thermostat" controller that combines per-tenant SLO windows with runtime KV-pressure gating and a probe-driven soft-open. The controller reduces oscillation by smoothing SLO adjustments, gates circuit transitions when node KV cache is above pressure thresholds, and provides a probe/holding pattern before promoting a circuit from degraded->healthy.

What this PR contains: single-line summary: implement SLO Thermostat + KV pressure gate + probe-driven soft-open + unit/integration tests + docs and rollout flags. The description below is a single continuous field that contains motivation, design notes, a checklist, commit summary, files touched list, short diffs, CI summary, review comments and the merge outcome.

Design notes: (1) SLO Thermostat: runs in control-plane runtime-manager, computes a short-window SLO error metric per tenant (latency quantile vs target) and applies a smoothed correction factor to tenant weight and circuit threshold. (2) KV pressure gating: runtime exposes node.kv_pressure metric (0.0-1.0). If kv_pressure > gating_threshold (configurable per pool), circuit transitions that would increase load (soft-open/promote) are suppressed and demoted to a probe state. (3) Probe-driven soft-open: when a demoted tenant is eligible for recovery we run N lightweight probe requests (configurable) through an isolated fast path; success moves to half-open then full-open with staged capacity allowance. (4) Safety: config flags feature-flagged under rollout.slo_thermostat.enabled and runtime defaults are conservative. Telemetry added: slo_thermostat.adjustment, slo_thermostat.probes, slo_thermostat.kv_gate_denials.

Rollout plan: feature flagged; start in us-central on dedicated pools with small tenant groups, monitor slo_thermostat.adjustment and kv_gate_denials over 48h, then widen to multi-region. Immediate rollback via rollout.slo_thermostat.enabled=false or autoscaler pool-exclude.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation (control plane + runtime hooks) - [x] Unit tests for thermostat math and gating logic - [x] Integration tests with local kv_pressure simulator - [x] Metrics and dashboards updated - [x] Docs snippet in reliability.md - [x] Feature flag gated for controlled rollout - [x] Security review not required (no new external surface)

Commits summary: see commits array for individual commit messages. High level: implement controller, expose kv metric, probe fast-path, tests, docs, e2e harness case for kv pressure bursts.

Files changed (high level): sources/runtime/controller/slo_thermostat.go, sources/runtime/agent/kv_pressure_collector.go, sources/runtime/open_path/probe_handler.go, controlplane/rollout/flags.yaml, telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml, docs/reliability.md, tests/integration/slo_thermostat_kv_sim_test.go, ci/pipeline/slo-smoke.yml

Small illustrative patch snippets (not exhaustive):
- controller/slo_thermostat.go: added gating check before promoting candidate: if nodeMetrics.KVPressure > cfg.GatingThreshold { recordTelemetry("kv_gate_denial"); return Probe }
- probe_handler.go: introduced RunProbes(ctx, tenant, n) -> returns success ratio; success triggers stagedAllowance = min(cfg.StagedPct, previousAllowance*1.5)

CI: initial run failed lint (unused import in tests) -> fixed in follow-up commit -> CI passed on second run. Full CI summary included in ci_status.

Review conversation excerpt: included in review_comments list. Key points: reviewers asked for conservative defaults, asked to add telemetry label, requested explicit unit tests for sub-ms probe timing, and asked to keep gating threshold cluster-configurable. All addressed in follow-ups.

Merge outcome: merged via squash-merge after approvals and green CI. Merge commit included in merge_commit field. Release notes summarized below.

Release notes: Adds an SLO Thermostat controller that smooths per-tenant SLO enforcement, introduces KV-pressure gating to prevent aggressive soft-open during high KV cache pressure, and probe-driven half-open transitions. Feature-flagged and off by default.

b2c3d4e feat(runtime): expose node.kv_pressure metric and API hook
c3d4e5f feat(runtime): add probe fast-path and RunProbes helper
d4e5f6a test: unit tests for thermostat calculation and gating logic
e5f6a7b ci: add slo-smoke pipeline and integration kv-pressure sim test

g7b8c9d fix: address lint failures and tighten probe timeouts
Ethan Morales (2026-02-18): Why do we need kv_pressure gating instead of adjusting tenant weight? Concerned about global availability impact. Response: gating prevents false positives when node memory is constrained; thermostat still adjusts weights but gating prevents premature soft-open promotions.
Sofia Lindgren (2026-02-19): Please add telemetry labels and make gating threshold cluster-configurable. Also add unit for probe timing edge case. Response: added metrics slo_thermostat.kv_gate_denials and moved gating threshold to pool config with default 0.85. Added unit test for probe timing.

Motivation: In production we observed short-duration traffic bursts from a handful of tenants that cause transient SLO violations and aggressive early evacuation of nodes, which leads to KV cache loss and longer downstream latency during cross-region failover. This PR introduces a soft burst throttler that applies a short, token-bucket based dampening window per-tenant and a coordinated 'early-kv-preserve' flag for evacuation to avoid discarding warm KV caches during fast handoffs.

What this change does: Adds an adaptive soft-burst-throttler component in the request admission path that: (1) detects sub-second CPU/queue spikes per-tenant and applies a light-rate cap that decays over 10-30s, (2) prefers gentle shedding (HTTP 429 with Retry-After) for best-effort tenants while keeping latency SLO tenants routed, and (3) emits telemetry to allow fast tuning. The early-kv-preserve patch extends the evacuation protocol: when a node receives an evacuation signal it marks selected KV shards with preserve=true and exposes a short-lived bridgelet token that target nodes can use to pull warmed KV segments instead of forcing a full recompute. This reduces cold-start penalties during regional failover.

Implementation notes: The throttler is implemented in runtime/admission/soft_burst_throttler.go and wired into the admission chain with a low-overhead fast-path. Token bucket parameters are workload-tunable via admission.policy JSON with sane defaults (burst_capacity=10, refill_ms=200, decay_window_s=20). The early-kv-preserve flow introduces a control-plane handshake: runtime/kv/preserve.go and a small router change in routing/failover_bridgelet.go. To avoid control plane churn I added a rate limiter for preserve handshakes and a safety TTL for bridgelet tokens.

Testing and validation: Unit tests cover token accounting and decay behavior. Integration e2e tests simulate a 5x burst for 60s across 200 concurrent tenants and assert 99th percentile latency stays under configured SLO for priority tenants and that 95% of preserved-KV handoffs rehydrate with <15ms additional latency vs baseline. Load tests were run in perf-lab with the new admission policy toggled on and off. CI: build, unit, integration, and perf smoke all passed after two reruns when a flaky eviction test was stabilized.

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind admission.features.soft_burst_throttle (off by default). We will enable for a small cohort of customers behind a runtime flag for 48 hours and monitor latency SLOs and preserved-KV hit ratio. If metrics look good, we will progressively enable across regions over a week. Rollback path: toggle the feature gate off and trigger an immediate revocation of active bridgelets (telemetry captured).

Checklist:
- [x] Add soft burst throttler runtime component
- [x] Add early-kv-preserve control handshake and bridgelet token flow
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Perf lab validation and dashboards
- [x] Docs snippet in ops/README about new admission policy

Related work: Builds on ideas from ENG-3721 (adaptive admission) and SRE-98 (regional failover telemetry). This is a targeted hotfix to reduce incident recurrence tied to rapid eviction loops observed during the October regional spike.

Notes on safety and observability: New metrics: admission.soft_burst.throttle_rate, admission.soft_burst.throttled_tenants, kv.preserve.handshakes, kv.preserve.success_rate, kv.preserve.latency_ms. Alerts: add a short-term guard if throttle_rate stays >50rps for >5m or preserve_success_rate <90% after rollout.

Files changed and rationale (high level): Keep diffs small and reviewable. The logic changes are scoped to the admission and kv modules and a tiny router tweak to consume bridgelet tokens. Low-risk to other components.
Lena Fox: Please double-check the token decay window defaults; we should avoid being too aggressive for bursty tracing workloads.
Diego Chen: Adjusted decay_window_s from 10 to 20 after benching with tracer-heavy traffic; updated tests to cover edge case.
Priya Nair: One nit on naming: prefer preserve_token over bridgelet_token for clarity in the control plane. Also we need an RBAC check for preserve handshakes.
Diego Chen: Renamed bridgelet_token -> preserve_token and added an RBAC guard with unit tests. PTAL.
Marcus Holt: CI failure looked like unrelated flaky eviction test; confirm you stabilized it and reran CI.
Diego Chen: Yes, added a small sleep in the test harness and mocked the eviction signal, reran CI and all green.
Hotfix: introduce soft burst throttler (configurable) to reduce transient SLO violations during short spikes; add early-KV-preserve bridgelet to avoid cold-KV penalties during rapid regional failovers. Feature gated and opt-in during rollout.
Enable feature gate for canary customers via runtime flag
Create dashboard panel for kv.preserve.success_rate and admission.soft_burst.throttled_tenants
Add short-term alert for preserve_success_rate < 90%
Schedule follow-up (ENG-4983) to evaluate long-term autoscaling interactions

Motivation:
Large presubmit runs were spending significant time and I/O enumerating transitive dependency surfaces and running language-specific linters on paths that are logically "vendor" or tooling-only. This PR introduces a lightweight annotation model for dependency manifests and a small release-coordinator shim to reduce noisy presubmit work and consolidate release smoke/dry-run signing steps into a single guarded action.

What this changes (single-string description):
- Add annotations for package roots and non-production dependency paths: .ci/dep-annotations.yaml + manifest tags in package.json and go.mod comments. The presubmit prober skips annotated subtrees (configurable).
- Implement a dep-annotator tool (Go) used by CI to generate the annotation file from a single pass over repo manifests; this replaces repeated ad-hoc scripts under scripts/ci/.
- Introduce a release-coordinator GitHub Action that sequences: pre-release smoke (canary), changelog dry-run, artifact-sign dry-run, and an idempotent sign-and-publish step behind an explicit release flag. The action supports staged rollouts and automatic fallback to previous release artifacts when sign step fails.
- Replace brittle bash bootstraps with hermetic Docker microimage for lightweight toolchain tasks: images/ci-toolchain/ (small, reproducible build).
- Update presubmit workflows to add an opt-in fast-path lane (quiet) that uses the annotations to skip heavy linters; full presubmit still runs in the regular lane.
- Add docs at docs/ci/dep-annotations.md and a migration guide for integrators.

Checklist:
- [x] Add dep-annotator implementation and unit tests
- [x] Add release-coordinator action + workflow examples
- [x] Migrate a sample repo (redwood/examples/bench) to annotations to validate skipping logic
- [x] Update developer docs and PRESUBMIT.md with opt-in flags
- [x] Smoke test on canary org and validate metrics (presubmit latency and CI compute)

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature flag (ci.fastpath.enabled=false by default).
2) Enable fastpath for CI on a small subset of low-risk repos (redwood/examples/bench, redwood-sdk-python) and run 1 week of telemetry comparing presubmit CPU and wall time.
3) If no significant false-negative regressions (quality delta < 0.5% on our eval prompt set), expand opt-in to more repos and offer gradated annotation coverage.
4) Flip global fastpath opt-in only after 3 weeks of stable metrics.

Rollback plan:
- Feature flag allows immediate disable.
- Release-coordinator is idempotent and will abort publish on sign failures; we keep last-good artifact fallback in the action.

Migration notes for integrators:
- Short guide in docs/ci/dep-annotations.md; devs should only annotate non-production or vendored subtrees.
- dep-annotator has a --dry-run mode to preview skipped paths.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: incorrectly annotated paths could cause linters or tests to skip critical files. Mitigation: default fastpath is opt-in per repository and we include a presubmit safety check that fails if annotation would skip files touched by the PR.
- Risk: release-coordinator introduces new release surface. Mitigation: rollouts behind org-level flag and staged canaries; dry-run step exercised in CI nightly.

- "ci: add .ci/dep-annotations.yaml sample and generator"
- "ci(actions): release-coordinator action and example workflow"
- "chore: replace legacy bash toolchain with hermetic ci-toolchain image"

payload.body: Motivation: On multi‑GPU tensor‑parallel workloads we observed recurring microstalls during collective phases when small tensor slices caused NCCL launches to serialize and kernel scheduling to underutilize SM resources. This PR introduces a stride‑aware collective latch that groups neighbor tensor slices into opportunistic host‑buffered batches, harmonizes host<->device staging for NCCL primitives, and expands KV cache windowing so prefetches align with the new aggregation window. The change targets the TP runtime path and continuous batching pipeline and is designed to reduce comm/compute skew without increasing tail latency for short sequences. Design summary: 1) Collective latch: a lightweight host‑side coordinator that detects contiguous slice strides across the TP group and holds small launches for up to a microwindow (configurable default 40us) to enable coalesced NCCL ops. 2) Host buffer harmonization: a transient host buffer layer that aggregates rendezvous payloads at page granularity to reduce PCIe/CPU syscall overhead and improve kernel launch packing. 3) KV cache windowing: KV prefetches adjusted to the latch microwindow to avoid prefetch thrashing and reduce duplicated kvset transfers. 4) Scheduler hints: expose a 'coalesce_hint' from the TP planner so the kernel scheduler can prefer compact kernel chaining for coalesced slices. Safety and fallbacks: latch defaults to a conservative microwindow and disables when kernel latency variance is high or when NCCL comms show backpressure. The code contains runtime telemetry to detect regressions and auto‑disable per model/shape. Tests and validation: Extensive unit tests added for the latch state machine and host buffer lifecycle. Integration tests run on a 4xA100 TP rig (simulated in CI for flange tests) showing median throughput improvements. Performance: On LLaMA‑2‑13B 4‑way TP, seq_len 2048, inference with continuous batching enabled, we measured 10–18% increase in steady‑state tokens/sec and a 12% reduction in GPU inter‑device stall time at p95. Short sequence (seq_len 128) p99 latency showed neutral change (+/-2%), validating conservative defaults. Comm telemetry: NCCL run‑time events showed fewer small collective launches with increased average payload per call. Backwards compatibility: No API changes. Configuration knobs exposed in runtime config under 'tp.collective_latch' and 'kvcache.window_us'. Rollout plan: feature gated behind a runtime flag and A/B rollout via Canary pool for a week with automated quality checks. Checklist: [x] Unit tests [x] Integration perf runs [x] Perf dashboard widgets added [x] Safety fallback logic [x] Documentation snippets in runtime config docs Commits summary: - Implement stride‑aware latch and host buffer layer - Wire coalesce_hint into kernel scheduler and planner - Adjust KV cache prefetch timing and add metrics - Add unit and integration tests - Docs and config defaults Adjusted areas: src/runtime/tp/collective_latch.cc, src/runtime/tp/collective_latch.h, src/runtime/io/host_buffer_pool.cc, src/runtime/io/host_buffer_pool.h, src/runtime/kvcache/prefetch_window.cc, src/scheduler/kernel_coalesce.cc, tests/tp/test_collective_latch.py, infra/ci/perf_flange.yml, docs/runtime/collective_latch.md. Small illustrative diffs: in collective_latch.cc we add a microwindow timer and a RingBuffer-backed host staging path. in kernel_coalesce we add a prefer_compact_chain boolean branch when coalesce_hint is set. Review conversation: Reviewer Liam: "Nice approach. Please add a regression gate so we can disable per‑model if perf regresses in prod." Author: "Added model‑level opt‑out flag and telemetry to flip the feature off automatically when p95 increases by >5% and reduce to disabled for flagged model IDs." Reviewer Mei: "Can we ensure this does not increase CPU syscall rate in small‑slice workloads?" Author: "Host buffer aggregation actually reduces syscalls by batching at 4KB page granularity; added counters and a microbenchmark in tests that show syscalls dropped ~35%." Reviewer Diego: "CI showed a flaky perf test on dl1 cluster." Author: "Fixed race in test harness and marked the flaky infra test as soft in perf_flange.yml until we stabilize." CI results: initial run had a flaky perf test failure; after test fix and retest CI passed across linux-x86 and aarch64 perf harnesses. Merge: squash and merge to main with release note. Release notes: "Add stride‑aware collective latching and host buffer harmonization to reduce TP comm stalls and improve throughput; feature gated and off by default for canary rollout." Breaking change: "false"

payload.body:
Context: We need an alternative attention execution path that improves mid-sequence throughput for mixed-length workloads without regressing tail latency for short requests. This PR introduces 'RippleAttn', a cascade-style attention kernel that composes a fast single-pass QK reduction with an opportunistic secondary pass for fused rotary/rope transforms. It also adds a lightweight KV 'steady' batcher that maintains warm KV slots and performs gentle eviction to stabilize the cache hit-rate under bursty traffic. Motivation: Existing fast-path kernels excel for uniform long sequences but suffer when the workload mixes short and long sequences and when KV cache churn is high. Delta goals: +5-12% p99 throughput on typical customer chat traces, +8% average token throughput for mixed workloads, no >5% regression on sub-64-token tail latency. Design summary: - RippleAttn cascade kernel: two-stage pipeline where stage-1 performs QK matmul with attention scores using a fused FP16 accumulation path; stage-2 runs rotary/rope adjustments and softmax in a compact fused microkernel only for lanes where numeric adjustments are necessary (e.g. large rotary offsets or quantized buckets). This reduces work for short sequences and preserves numerical fidelity for long sequences. The kernel auto-selects based on sequence-length histogram hints passed by the scheduler. - Steady KV batcher: a background batching loop that groups KV reads by hot-slot, issues continuous-batcher-style fetches, and maintains per-shard warm counters. Eviction is 'steady' (rate-limited LRU with tenant-aware demotion) to avoid cascade evictions during bursts. - Scheduler hooks: new hints (seq_histogram, hot_slot_candidates) are surfaced in the request router; the planner uses these hints to steer requests to RippleAttn-compatible workers or fall back to the standard kernel. The change includes runtime feature flags to toggle the new path per-deployment. Checklist: - [x] RippleAttn kernel implementation (CUDA + CPU fallback) - [x] Steady KV batcher implementation and config knobs - [x] Scheduler integration and routing hints - [x] End-to-end unit + integration tests - [x] Microbench harness and perf regression tests - [x] Documentation draft (internal ops runbook) Related: ENG-4032 (attn-kernel roadmap), ENG-4088 (kv-cache stabilization). This description contains implementation rationale, benchmark summary, and operational notes.
Amit Shah (2026-02-11): Great direction. Please add a short section in docs describing fallback rules when sequence-histogram is missing. Also call out CPU-path performance expectations.
Author (Lena Ortiz) (2026-02-12): Added fallback behavior to router/hints.h and documented CPU-path tradeoffs in docs/internal/ripple_ops_runbook.md.
Priya Nair (2026-02-13): Steady batcher looks promising; can we add a check to prevent warm-counter overflow and a unit test for eviction pacing under burst?
Author (Lena Ortiz) (2026-02-13): Added overflow guards and a synthetic burst test in tests/kv/test_steady_batcher.py.
Introduce RippleAttn cascade kernel and Steady KV Batcher behind runtime feature flags. Expected throughput gains on mixed-length workloads; configurable via router.hints and per-deployment flags. See internal runbook for rollout and rollback steps.
Rollout plan: enable on a small canary fleet with :ripple flag, monitor p95/p99, KV hit-rates, and hot-slot evictions. If eviction rate > 0.5% in 10m window, automatically revert using runtime flag. Ops runbook included in docs/internal/ripple_ops_runbook.md. Perf numbers are from bench/attn/ripple_bench.py using real chat histograms anonymized from customer traces.
No user-visible API changes. Feature gated and disabled by default in hosted. KV eviction policy is tenant-aware; added guardrails to avoid noisy-neighbor impact.

Background and motivation: In the last incident (SUP-9021) we observed rapid oscillation between soft-shed and full-deny states in a subset of regional pods when ephemeral KV pressure coincided with a short-lived node GC. That oscillation caused tenant-level SLO churn and noisy alerts. This PR introduces a conservative slew-rate limiter for soft-shed transitions, tightens SLO/tenant telemetry tags to avoid accidental aggregation gaps, and removes a legacy metric label that was causing mismatched time-series rollups. Changes are intentionally small and defensive to allow a fast rollout in production.

Summary of changes (high-level):
- Introduce SoftShedSlewController with exponential cool-off and leak-based smoothing in serving/runtime/shedder.go. The controller enforces a maximum number of soft-shed toggles per minute per-tenant and decays penalty in a leak-rate fashion.
- Add a lightweight safety check in scheduler/slot_allocator.rs to avoid immediate tenant re-admission when recent soft-shed events recorded in the controller indicate instability.
- Normalize telemetry labels: replace tenant_env tag usage with tenant_stage (prod/stage/qa) in telemetry/metrics_tags.go and update Prometheus export names to avoid duplicate series (previous label mismatch produced two separate series for the same SLO).
- Add a migration script ops/scripts/regen-metrics.sh to backfill the new label mappings in our metrics bridge for the last 7 days.
- Add focused integration test tests/integration/regional_soft_shed_flapping_test.py that simulates short-lived KV pressure spikes while nodes cycle to validate no rapid circuit flips.

Commits (summary):
- 8a3f9b7 Introduce SoftShedSlewController and unit tests (no-op behind feature flag)
- 61b2c44 Tighten scheduler admission check and add telemetry guardrails
- d9f3b0a Normalize telemetry labels and update exporters
- e5a1f22 Add migration helper script for metrics bridge
- f3d7c88 Add integration test that repros flapping locally and CI harness adjustment

Files touched (high-level):
- serving/runtime/shedder.go (new controller implementation + unit tests)
- serving/scheduler/slot_allocator.rs (admission check)
- telemetry/metrics_tags.go (label rename + comments)
- ops/scripts/regen-metrics.sh (migration helper)
- tests/integration/regional_soft_shed_flapping_test.py (integration test)
- docs/telemetry/labels.md (doc update to call out tenant_stage)
- build/ci/flake-retry.yaml (CI tweak to re-run the specific flaky test once)

Small illustrative snippet (controller state machine):
"""
// pseudo: increment penalty on toggle, decay with leak-rate
if toggle_request && time.Since(last_toggle) < controller.min_interval {
  penalty += controller.penalty_increment
  // prevent immediate toggle when penalty exceeds threshold
  if penalty > controller.max_penalty {
    rejectToggle()
  }
} else {
  penalty = max(penalty - controller.leak_per_second * elapsed, 0)
}
"""

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests added for the SoftShedSlewController cover edge cases (immediate toggles, steady-state decay, burst recovery).
- Integration test reproduces flapping with a small local cluster; in CI this test was flaky once on the first run due to timing sensitivity under shared runners. The CI job now has a one-time re-run policy for this test (build/ci/flake-retry.yaml) and passed after the second attempt. All other checks (lint, go vet, Rust clippy, pytest) passed.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Maya Singh: "Can we keep the controller behind a feature flag for the initial rollout? Also prefer explicit metric for penalty level so SRE can alert if it's non-zero for > 10m." -> Implemented (feature flag soft_shed_slew_v1 + metric shed_penalty_level).
- Liam O'Connor: "Scheduler change looks conservative but please add comment pointing to the ticket; I worry about accidental admission regressions." -> Added comment, and integration test validates no regression on re-admit path.
- Ella Zhou: "Telemetry rename is fine, but coordinate with dashboards folks to update panel queries." -> Noted; ops pager notified and docs/telemetry/labels.md added with migration notes.
- Ops (quick offline): requested the migration script to be runnable from prod image; script packaged as a standalone small tool and documented.

Rollout plan and mitigation:
- Rollout strategy: staged rollout to 10% of nodes in us-west first (hotfix channel) with the feature flag enabled; monitor shed_penalty_level, tenant_slo_error_rate and circuit_flip_count dashboards for 30 minutes per stage.
- If any tenant shows increasing error_rate correlated with the new controller, the feature flag can be toggled per-region; the scheduler safety check is backward compatible by design.

Why this is safe to merge (short justification):
- Changes are defensive and additive (controller can be gated), scheduler check avoids immediate admission only when the controller reports instability, telemetry rename is backward-compatible after the migration script, and tests reproduce the regression locally. The net effect is reduced oscillation risk and clearer telemetry.

Follow-ups (to avoid scope creep):
- ENG-5219: broader tenant-aware admission policy and dashboarding for long-running penalty accumulation.
- Metric retention policy: audit recent rollups to ensure no pre-existing dashboards depend on the legacy label beyond 14 days.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged by Noah Patel (merge commit 8a3f9b7). Hotfix deployed to hot path in us-west with feature flag enabled; early metrics show a 70% reduction in circuit_flip_count in the first 2 hours on the canary cohort.

If you want to run the local repro: see tests/integration/README.md (added short steps) — run the specialized harness with TEST_REGION=us-west-local and ensure the migration script has permission to write back to the metrics bridge sandbox.

payload.body:
Motivation: On high-concurrency tenants we've seen KV cache fragmentation and repeated paging under transient spikes. This PR introduces a page-aware reservation allocator plus lazy-demote eviction path to reduce amplification from small-object churn and paging thrash.

What this changes (summary):
- Add PageReservationManager: tracks page-granular reservations per-tenant and per-segment, enabling inexpensive fast-path allocations when contiguous slots exist.
- Replace the previous slab-centric reserve() with a page-aware fast path that tries to claim contiguous pages before falling back to existing allocators.
- Introduce LazyDemoteEvictor: when eviction pressure is encountered, frequently-accessed entries are moved to a demotion tier (soft-demoted) instead of immediate eviction; this delays paging and reduces re-fetches for short-lived spikes.
- Add a small background compaction task (compact-on-idle) that opportunistically coalesces high-fragmentation segments when CPU idle budget is available.
- Scheduler adjustments: make batch eviction runs cooperative with the continuous-batcher to avoid head-of-line latency spikes when freeing space under load.
- Kernel hints: expose an alignment hint from the allocator to selection of kernel tile sizes when sequence lengths are small (improves memory packing for attention kv caches).

Benchmarks / impact: in internal canary across 3 tenants with spiky workloads (random short-context generations + concurrent chat sessions) we saw:
- 25-40% reduction in page faulting rates during spikes
- 12% average end-to-end latency reduction at P95 for generation requests under contention
- 8% increase in sustained throughput (tokens/sec) due to fewer re-fetches

Migration notes: default behavior is opt-in via runtime config: kv.page_reservation.enabled and kv.lazy_demote.enabled. Both default to off for safety; rollout plan is canary -> 25% -> 100% across tenants.

Backwards-compatibility and safety: no on-disk format changes. All new background tasks are bounded and respect per-tenant CPU and IO budgets.

Related Linear/Jira: ENG-4528 (allocator work), ENG-4580 (eviction TTR tuning).
Introduce page reservation allocator and lazy demotion eviction path. Opt-in via kv.page_reservation.enabled and kv.lazy_demote.enabled. Improves latency and reduces paging under spiky workloads.
Kenji Matsumoto (reviewer): The PageReservationManager looks good overall. Two concerns: how do we avoid pathological reservation monopolies by a noisy tenant? Suggest adding a soft cap and decaying lease counters.
Maya Venkataraman (author): Added per-tenant soft caps (configurable) and a decay tick in the manager. Updated docs with config knobs.
Priya Sharma (reviewer): The lazy demote metadata will add memory overhead. Can we use a compact bitset rather than full struct per-entry?
Maya Venkataraman (author): Reworked the demotion metadata to a 16-bit compact tag; used pointer packing for existing entry headers. Memory overhead reduced to ~0.6% on average in benchmarks.
Lars Holm (approver): Ran canary with 3 tenants + production-like workload. Observed reduced page faults and stable latencies. Approving with minor follow-ups in docs.
CI Bot: flaky-test-kv-compact_on_idle timed out on first run, retriggered and passed on second run.
Unit tests added for reservation fast-path, eviction demotion flow, and compact-on-idle. Integration canary config included to reproduce spike scenarios. One flaky test observed and re-run in CI.
Canary runs show 25-40% lower page faults during spikes, 12% lower P95 latency in contention, and ~8% throughput improvement. CPU overhead for compact-on-idle kept under 2% by default config.
Added telemetry: kv.page_reservations.count, kv.page_fragmentation.score, kv.lazy_demote.promotions, kv.eviction.delay_ms. Dashboards updated with new panels in runtime/kv overview.
Start with internal canary (2 tenants) for 48h -> enable on 25% of production traffic with telemetry for page_faults/kvcache_evictions -> monitor for 72h -> ramp to 100% if metrics stable. Provide rollback toggle kv.page_reservation.enabled=false.
No new data paths. Per-tenant accounting ensures no cross-tenant leakage. Background compaction runs are restricted to same-tenant resource quotas.
ENG-4622: auto-tune reservation thresholds from observed allocation patterns; ENG-4623: extend kernel hinting to multi-head attention kernels for further packing gains.

payload.body:
Motivation: CI presubmit lanes have regressed in median feedback time due to cold CI images and noisy dev-dependency churn. This PR introduces a presubmit "fast-cache" layer for our CI runner image and a small dependency-visibility adapter that enforces an explicit dev-dep manifest to prevent accidental transitive dev-dependency installs.

Goals: 1) reduce end-to-end presubmit feedback time for lint/test jobs by warming a lightweight artifact cache (node_modules tarballs, pip wheels) scoped to the PR diff; 2) make dev-dependency changes explicit so CI cache invalidation is more intentional and less noisy; 3) avoid large monolithic CI image rebuilds on each dev-dep bump.

What this changes: - new CI helper: .github/presubmit/cache-warmup.sh (shell helper run in presubmit lanes to warm cache from fast-cache service) - presubmit fast-cache service client: infra/ci/fastcache/ (minimal go client + config) - new lightweight CI image Dockerfile: infra/ci/docker/presubmit-fast.Dockerfile (smaller base + preinstalled runtime libs) - dev-dep visibility manifest: dev-deps.yml at repo root and per-language dev-deps.{json|toml} used by the presubmit adapter - workflow changes: .github/workflows/presubmit.yml updated to call warmup early and fall back to existing caching when unavailable - package management: package.json scripts + pip tool updates to support manifest lock queries

Non-goals: this PR does not change production runtime images, dedicated capacity autoscaling, or release pipelines.

Implementation notes: - Fast-cache is opt-in per-repo and per-branch; we added config flags in the global ci-config to gate rollout. - The dev-dep adapter validates that any changed dev-deps are reflected in dev-deps.yml; absent an entry, the job will fail presubmit with a guidance message and a one-click suggestion to run ./scripts/devdep-sync.sh. - The cache warmup step uses a transitive-diff key that only includes files in the PR diff that affect dependency resolution (package.json, requirements.txt, poetry.lock, go.mod, etc.) to avoid unnecessary cache invalidations.

Testing and rollout: - Iterative rollout behind a feature flag: default off for main, on for feature/* branches and canary teams. - Unit + e2e tests added for the fast-cache client (infra/ci/fastcache/tests) and a flaky-presubmit integration test that simulates cold-run vs warmed-run and asserts median latency drop. - Manual canary: rolled out to the infra-team CI first for two weeks before enabling repo-level gate.

Checklist: - [x] add fastcache client and config - [x] add cache warmup runner and integrate into presubmit workflow - [x] add dev-deps manifest + adapter + sync script - [x] update README and developer docs with onboarding steps - [x] add unit and integration tests - [x] add feature-flag gate and rollback plan

Performance: in local canary runs, warmed presubmit reduced average lint/unit feedback from ~19m to ~7m (median) for a typical web-service PR with ~120 changed files.

Risk and rollback: if fastcache has transient failures we fallback to existing restore-from-cache logic and proceed; dev-dep manifest failures are safe-fail and provide clear remediation steps.

Related: ENG-4312 (presubmit perf), ENG-4476 (ci-image fragmentation), PM-62 (developer velocity metrics).
Miguel Alvarez: I'm curious about the cache key entropy; can we exclude timestamp-like files?
Priya Natarajan: Yes — the transitive-diff key explicitly filters by known manifest files and uses blob hashes for determinism. Added tests to validate this.
Sara Chen: dev-deps manifest validation failures need clearer messaging for new contributors.
Priya Natarajan: Updated the validator message to include a one-click sync command and a link to the README-presubmit.md quickstart.
Liam O'Connor: CI flake in integration on first run (network timeout) — reran and passed.
Sara Chen: Approving after we confirmed fallback behavior is safe and documentation is clear.
Improve presubmit latency by adding a warmed cache path and introduce an explicit dev-dependency manifest to reduce noisy cache invalidations. Opt-in via feature flag; rollout planned via canaries.
payload.title: Introduce presubmit fast-cache + dev-dep visibility adapter

payload.body:
Context: As part of the hosted overload protection work, we want to degrade gracefully instead of cascading timeouts when a model/region is saturated. This PR adds a routing-side fallback attempt when the upstream admission layer reports an overload breaker open (or equivalent overload classification).

What this PR does: Implements a fallback resolution step in Smart Routing that can (optionally) route to a compatible fallback model and/or fallback region based on tenant + route policy. Adds strict loop prevention so we don’t bounce between model variants/regions, and bounds fallback attempts to a small fixed number to avoid amplifying load. Also ensures we do not fallback for non-overload failures (e.g., auth, invalid params, quota exceeded).

Key behaviors: (1) Trigger conditions: only when overload classification indicates breaker open / load shed / capacity unavailable (see mapping in code comments); not triggered on generic 5xx. (2) Fallback selection: consults policy engine for allowed fallbacks for the tenant + route + requested model; if none configured, behave as before. (3) Bounded attempts: max 1 fallback per request by default (configurable to 2 for region+model hop, but guarded); stops immediately if fallback target equals original target. (4) Loop prevention: propagates an internal routing context header across internal hops and records visited (model, region) pairs; if the candidate is already visited, we do not attempt it. (5) Observability: emits counters for fallback_attempted, fallback_succeeded, fallback_blocked_loop, and fallback_exhausted; dimensions intentionally low-cardinality (tenant_tier, route_group, requested_model_family, result).

Why routing (not gateway): The gateway admission layer is responsible for shedding early, but only routing knows compatibility constraints and tenant policy for fallback targets. This is consistent with the admission layering guidance (see ADR-015) — the gateway classifies overload; routing decides a safe alternate target; runtime remains the source of saturation signals.

Safety constraints: Dedicated and Private tenants are never routed to Hosted. Hosted self-serve can fallback within Hosted only. Enterprise Hosted can fallback only to configured allowlisted model variants and regions. We also explicitly disallow cross-AZ fallback within a region to avoid hiding infra issues; region fallback is an explicit opt-in.

Testing: Unit tests cover loop prevention, bounded retries, policy deny, and correct trigger mapping. Integration test fakes breaker-open signals and verifies we attempt exactly one fallback and preserve the correlation ID. Perf-canary scenario work is tracked separately.

Follow-ups: (a) tune default max attempts and error mapping once we have canary data; (b) add dashboard panel for fallback rates vs shed rate; (c) document customer-facing behavior once GA’d (docs owned by DevEx/Docs).
- Smart Routing can now attempt policy-configured fallback model/region when overload protection opens a circuit breaker, with bounded retries and loop prevention. No API surface changes; behavior is opt-in via policy.
Mina Haddad (review): Can you clarify the max attempts logic? I want to ensure we can’t end up trying multiple fallbacks and increasing traffic under overload. Also, please confirm we never cross Hosted/Dedicated boundaries.

Elena Popov (author): Default is max 1 fallback attempt per request. There’s an internal config to allow 2 only for the (region hop -> model hop) path, but I kept it disabled by default and added a hard cap + test. Added explicit checks: Dedicated/Private never route into Hosted, and Hosted never routes into Dedicated.

Ravi Menon (review): Loop prevention looks good. One concern: you’re using requested_model as a label value in metrics. That can be high cardinality. Please bucket by model family or a normalized name.

Elena Popov (author): Good catch. Updated metrics to use requested_model_family (derived from the catalog) and route_group (chat/embeddings/rerank), and removed raw model IDs. Added a metrics test to enforce label set.

Peter Holtz (embedded SRE, review): What’s the trigger mapping? We should only fallback on overload-derived classifications, not generic 503s from downstream. Also ensure correlation ID is preserved for support.

Elena Popov (author): Added overload_mapping.ts and tests. We only fallback on explicit overload reasons (breaker_open, shed, capacity_unavailable) coming from gateway/runtime classification. Generic downstream 503/500 doesn’t trigger fallback. Correlation ID is preserved; added integration test asserting x-redwood-correlation-id is unchanged.

Rafael Mendes (SRE lead, review): Please add a guard against fallback storms: if the fallback target is also overloaded, we should not keep trying. Make sure we return the overload error and include a stable internal reason for dashboards.

Elena Popov (author): Implemented: if fallback attempt returns overload again, we stop (bounded) and return the overload classification. We emit fallback_exhausted with result=overload and include internal reason in routing decision logs (not as a metric label).

Jordan Lee (policy engine, review): Policy selection should be tenant-aware and route-aware. Ensure we validate that the fallback target is in the allowlist; no implicit compatibility.

Elena Popov (author): Done. Fallback targets must be explicitly configured via policy for the tenant + route selector; we also require compatibility check against catalog (same modality + context window constraints). No implicit model swaps.

Mina Haddad (review): Approved after last changes.

Ravi Menon (review): Approved.

Peter Holtz (review): Approved.

Rafael Mendes (review): Approved; please coordinate canary enablement with SRE runbook.

Elena Popov (author): Will do. Canary enablement tracked under ENG-4821 checklist.
payload.title: Smart Routing: fallback model/region when overload breaker is open (bounded + loop-safe)
