Context: During a regional KV pressure incident we observed a pathological interaction where the lightweight per-tenant load-shedder would aggressively trim inflight requests while the region-level circuit manager simultaneously flipped routes to a cold fallback path, causing amplified latency spikes and client-facing 5xxs. This PR introduces a small, conservative 'load stencil' window that smooths decision signals across the shedder and the circuit manager so they make coordinated, non-overlapping transitions; it also hardens the degenerate fallback path so requests routed there are replay-safe and don't trigger additional cross-region cold-path escalations. Changes include: 1) new load-stencil sampling + decay in runtime/shedder to avoid step changes under short spikes; 2) an explicit coordination handshake between shedder and circuit_manager via a transient token to avoid double-shedding; 3) safe-mode guards for the degenerate fallback route that force KV-drain-first semantics and short-circuit certain retries; 4) telemetry additions (metrics and tags) to track stencil window occupancy and handshake failures; 5) an opt-in canary gate and rollout script for Dedicated customers. Motivation: prevent cascade reroutes and reduce observed 5xxs during short-lived KV pressure events while preserving latency SLOs for best-effort tenants. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-9254) [x] unit tests for stencil decay and handshake [x] e2e repro in benchmark-lab [x] telemetry events + Grafana dashboard panel added [x] rollout script with feature-flag and canary percentage. Testing: unit + integration tests added; synthetic load test run in benchmark-lab reproduces previous failure and demonstrates >70% reduction in transient 5xxs and stable P95 latency under the same spike. Rollout plan: deploy to staging cluster behind feature flag, canary 5% in us-west, monitor the new metrics for 24h, then 25%/50%/100% over 3-6 hours with automatic rollback if handshake-failure-rate > 1% or P95 delta > 25ms. Related: SUP-4312 incident notes and postmortem fragment included. Notes: this is intentionally conservative (small stencil windows, handshake TTLs) to avoid long-lived tenant unfairness; future follow-ups will explore dynamic stencil sizing and per-tenant tuning.
Arjun: Can you clarify the handshake TTL and failure mode? The doc implies 30s TTL but code has 10s; please align.
Author (Priya): Updated TTL to 30s; added comments and unit tests to cover expiry path.
Maya: Is there any risk of the stencil smoothing masking a real capacity problem? Add a telemetry spike flagized metric.
Author: Added 'stencil_masked_spike' metric and Grafana panel; added alert rule to surface when stencils suppress >30% of decisions for >5m.
Liam: CI flake on tests/test_stencil_handshake.py on first run; looks like timing nondeterminism. Suggest test harness use fixed clock.
Author: switched to deterministic clock in tests and re-ran CI.
Reviewer (Maya): LGTM after TTL and metrics changes. Arjun approved with minor comments addressed.
QA: Ran benchmark-lab scenario against canary and verified reduced 5xxs and stable P95; approving for merge.
Ops: Added rollout script and verified permission bits; recommend squash merge to keep history compact.
payload.title: Introduce load-stencil smoothing and degenerate-fallback coordination to prevent cascade reroutes

payload.body:
Problem: Tenant throughput guarantees currently rely on coarse concurrency targets and headroom heuristics which overreact to transient bursts or noisy utilization signals. This causes oscillation in Dedicated pools and uneven latency for tenants that have steady-rate workloads.

What this PR does: Implements a new 'rate-match' autoscaler mode for Dedicated capacity that focuses on matching observed served RPS to tenant-declared throughput targets (or inferred targets from historical steady-state windows). The controller adjusts two knobs: effective concurrency cap and burst-window allowance. It uses a short-term PID-like reconciling loop combined with a decay-based safety to avoid rapid oscillation.

Key features and rationale:
- Rate-matching policy: target_rps -> compute desired concurrency via adaptive estimator that accounts for median token-per-request and observed latency percentiles. This reduces unnecessary scale-ups when token costs fluctuate.
- Burst window control: instead of outright granting large static burst credits, tenants get a moving burst-window quota proportional to sustained utilization; soft-revert restores baseline over a configurable half-life.
- Utilization fingerprint: a compact 64-bit hash-like fingerprint (stable across short replays) that summarizes workload shape (median seq len, concurrency distribution, long-tail latency buckets). Fingerprint is exported to TSDB as a tag to group telemetry by workload-shape, making long-term regressions and model changes easier to detect.
- Signal smoothing: introduces an exponential smoothing layer and util-fingerprint-aware dampening so scale decisions weigh persistent shifts more than single-window spikes.
- Config: opt-in via fleet.autoscaler.mode="rate-match"; flags for burst_half_life, smoothing_alpha, and max_concurrency_delta_per_min. Default is conservative (off) and enabled gradually.

Files changed (high-level):
- pkg/autoscaler/controller/rate_match_controller.go (primary controller loop, reconciler)
- pkg/autoscaler/estimator/throughput_estimator.go (estimator functions and tests)
- pkg/telemetry/util_fp/agent.go (fingerprint builder + unit tests)
- internal/config/defaults.yaml (new defaults and flags)
- deploy/dedicated/helm/values-rate-match.yaml (example rollout config)
- test/integration/autoscaler_rate_match_test.go (integration tests with simulated tenants)
- docs/ops/autoscaler-rate-match.md (operator doc + rollback steps)
- scripts/bench/provision_small_cluster.sh (bench harness tweak)
- observability/dashboards/rate-match-overview.json (dashboard panels)

Testing and results:
- Unit tests: added for estimator corner cases, burst-window decay and fingerprint stability (coverage +6%).
- Integration: simulated 120 tenants with mixed steady / bursty profiles; rate-match reduced scale oscillation by 48% vs baseline step-autoscaler and improved median P95 latency by ~12ms for steady tenants under mixed load.
- Bench: small cluster stress run (30m) to validate no token-cache starvation.

Rollout plan: staged rollout across Dedicated fleets: canary (5% traffic) -> pool-wide (50%) -> full. Helm values provided for safe defaults. Auto rollback if P95 latency for any tenant increases by >20% for 15m and reconciler logs show >10 rapid adjustments per minute.

Backward compatibility and migration notes:
- Existing autoscaler modes unchanged; rate-match is opt-in.
- Telemetry backward compatible: util_fingerprint introduced as optional metric tag; missing tag is treated as "unknown-fp" in dashboards.

Operational concerns:
- The fingerprint computation is cheap (O(1) per aggregate window) but we added CPU budget checks to avoid overhead at very high fleet cardinality.
- Safety nets: max_concurrency_delta_per_min prevents runaway concurrency changes; we retained existing emergency-fallback: fallback to step-autoscaler if reconciliation errors exceed threshold for 3 consecutive cycles.

Related work: ENG-9271 (autoscaler smoothing), ENG-9432 (observability gaps for tenant shaping).

Author notes: this PR is intentionally conservative: defaults keep behavior identical until operators enable rate-match. The code is contained to autoscaler and telemetry subsystems with minimal cross-cutting changes.
Miguel Ortega: Nice approach. Two asks: (1) can we add a debug endpoint that emits current fingerprint + raw histograms for a tenant to speed triage? (2) please add a small comment in estimator describing how median tokens-per-request is estimated under truncated traces.
Evelyn Brooks (reply): Added a /debug/tenant/:id/fp endpoint in controller and expanded estimator docs; also added a unit test for truncated traces.
Aisha Kaur: Telemetry looks good; make sure tag cardinality stays constrained. Suggest we bucket fingerprints into stable families in the dashboard rather than raw-fingerprints everywhere.
Samir Patel: Tested canary on staging. Observed one tenant that saw 2 rapid deltas due to very spiky traffic; recommend lowering default max_concurrency_delta_per_min to 5 for conservative rollout.
Evelyn Brooks (reply): Lowered default to 5 and documented the rationale in ops doc.
Added a new rate-matching autoscaler mode that dynamically reconciles tenant throughput targets with observed request pacing; introduces a lightweight utilization fingerprint metric for more stable telemetry-driven decisions.
payload.title: introduce-rate-match-autoscaler-and-util-fingerprint-telemetry

payload.body:
Background & motivation: during a regional preemption event we observed abrupt tenant evictions that caused downstream KV cache loss and a spike in cold-start latency for high-priority customers. This PR introduces a coordinated 'demotion handoff' protocol that (1) soft-demotes tenants on impacted nodes, (2) conserves KV/cache state during handoff windows, and (3) sanitizes control-plane signals so transient flaps don't trigger hard evictions. Design summary: - Introduces a short-lived tenant demotion state (DEMOTED_PENDING) with an epoched handshake to the control plane. DEMOTED_PENDING signals the runtime to stop accepting new long-lived sessions while preserving KV cache and inflight prefix caches for a configurable warmup window. - Adds a SignalSanitizer middleware in the control plane that coalesces rapid health flips and applies a rate-limited reopen backoff. This reduces oscillation and prevents noisy probes from accelerating evictions. - Implements a KV conservation helper that tags critical keys with a transient retention hint enabling fast rehydration on the target node (metadata-only snapshot + async rehydrate). - Adds telemetry anchors: new metrics for demotion transitions, kv_preserve_hit/miss, sanitizer_coalesce_count, and demotion_handoff_duration. - Backoff & rollback: demotion windows are configurable by tenant weight and can be rolled back by the control plane if the region stabilizes; this PR wires an emergency rollback API for operators. Checklist: - [x] Protocol definitions and protobufs for handshake - [x] Runtime demotion state + eviction guards - [x] SignalSanitizer implementation with unit tests - [x] KV conservation metadata tagging and rehydrate path - [x] Integration test that reproduces race between health flap and preemption - [x] Telemetry and dashboard dashboards reference file - [x] Canary rollout plan in rollout notes What changed (high level): - runtime/eviction/tenant_demote.go: new demotion state machine and graceful drain paths - controlplane/signals/sanitizer.go: coalescer, rate limiter, and sanitizer rules - controlplane/handshake/handshake.proto: handshake definitions and state enums - kv/preservation/marker.go: tagging helpers + retention hint API - telemetry/metrics/demotion_metrics.yaml: metric definitions and alert rules - tests/integration/demotion_flow_test.go: end-to-end scenario reproducing race - docs/operational/tenant-demote.md: operator runbook and rollback steps Backwards compatibility & safety: default values keep behavior unchanged (demotion disabled per-tenant unless opt-in or above SLA tier). The SignalSanitizer defaults to conservative thresholds to avoid masking real failures. Rollout plan: canary on dedicated clusters first (5% traffic), monitor demotion_handoff_duration and kv_preserve_hit ratio for 24h; widen on stable signals. If adverse effects detected, rollout can be reverted via feature flag or use emergency rollback API. Testing: unit tests cover sanitizer rules, handshake state transitions, and KV tag lifecycle. Integration tests simulate flaky region heartbeats and assert no hard-eviction occurred and KV rehydrate path triggers within the warmup window. Observability: dashboards and alerting rules added; key alerts: demotion_handoff_duration > 30s (warning), kv_preserve_miss > 1% (warning), sanitizer_coalesce_count spike (info). Risk & mitigation: risk of prolonged DEMOTED_PENDING causing capacity pressure; mitigated by tenant-weighted admission and an auto-escalation to hard-evict after configurable maximum hold time. Also added a telemetry-driven auto-rollback. Notes: ties to ENG-2287 (regional preemption postmortem). This PR is intentionally conservative in defaults; further optimizations (adaptive demotion window by tenant behavior) are planned as followups.
Evan Brooks (2026-02-11): Can you quantify the extra memory pressure from preserving KV metadata? We should ensure we won't OOM small nodes.
Priya Raman (2026-02-11): Added conservative limit per-node and a tenant-weighted admission cap; link to design notes in the PR description.
Lena Martin (2026-02-12): Please add an integration that asserts sanitizer_coalesce_count prevents a flap from causing a hard-evict within 10s. Also request a unit test for the sanitizer backoff timer.
Priya Raman (2026-02-13): Added the integration and unit tests; CI initially showed a flaky integration, I stabilized the timing by using a clock mock.
Carlos Vega (2026-02-14): Verified metrics and load on canary cluster; small regression in cold-start p95 (1.6% increase) expected and within threshold. Approving.
Evan Brooks (2026-02-14): Approve after confirming emergency rollback works and no telemetry gaps.
payload.title: Tenant demotion handoff and signal sanitizer for graceful regional preemption

payload.body:
Motivation: Presubmit pipelines have grown costly and noisy — a large fraction of lint and heavyweight test shards run for tiny surface-area changes. This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: (1) a lint-weight trimmer that computes a per-change weight and selectively runs lighter lint shards for small changes, and (2) a release-window prober that defers/re-schedules heavyweight gating tasks to controlled windows and proactively checks for release collisions.

What this change does (single-string summary): Adds a lightweight Go CI shim and a deterministic 'lint weight' heuristic, configures presubmit workflow to opt into trimmed lint paths via a 'ci:trim' label and change-size thresholds, introduces a 'deferred-heavy' tagging flow for tests that can be run on nightly/release windows, and adds a small release-window prober that validates mergeability and dependency drift during release windows. Also adds migration tooling to backfill historical file-surface metadata for accurate weight computation.

Why now: We observed median presubmit runtime increasing 28% year-over-year and SRE/infra costs up ~12% attributable to redundant lint/test runs on low-risk changes (docs, README edits, vendor updates). This is a low-risk opt-in mechanism that yields immediate CI cost and latency improvements.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement lint-weight compute algorithm (deterministic, language-aware, cached per-commit)
- [x] Replace targeted bash flows with a small Go shim for stability and observability (ci-shim)
- [x] Integrate trimmed lint path into .github/workflows/presubmit.yml with safe opt-in label and change thresholds
- [x] Add release-window prober that runs during configured release hours and posts status to the PR and release dashboard
- [x] Add migration script to backfill file-metrics (scripts/ci/migrate-lint-weights.go)
- [x] Add telemetry hooks (statsd/datadog) and opt-out env var for Private deployments
- [x] Unit and integration tests for weight calc and shim behavior
- [x] Docs for contributors and runbook for SRE

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag (CI env: CI_LINT_TRIMMER=off by default).
2) Enable in opt-in mode: contributors can add 'ci:trim' label or maintainers can rely on automatic thresholds for non-critical paths.
3) Monitor Telemetry: presubmit latency, shard counts, false-negative rate for lint and test coverage delta.
4) Gradual tightening of thresholds over 3 weeks with fallback to full-run on any coverage regression.

Rollback plan: revert feature flag to off, or remove 'ci:trim' label from merges; migration/backfill script is non-destructive. Release-window prober is read-only by default and can be disabled via RELEASE_PROBER_ENABLED=false.

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: missed lint finding because trimmed lint skipped an important rule. Mitigation: trimmed path still runs a core rule set; any failure in post-merge nightly job triggers an auto-rollout-block and alerts the author.
- Risk: hidden test regressions. Mitigation: heavy tests are scheduled to run in the next release-window and a short-circuit fallback runs full test on push-to-release branches.

Notes on CI cost impact (internal projection): expected presubmit runner-time reduction ~34% for small PRs, cluster CPU savings ~20% across working set.

Marcus Chen: Please add an integration test that exercises a multi-language change (TS + GO) to validate weighting across mixed diffs. Also suggest renaming 'weight' to 'lint_score' to be explicit.
Ava Martinez (author): Added tests under tests/ci/weight_calc_test.go and kept 'weight' name after discussion — we standardize on 'lint_weight' in code and map to 'lint_score' in external metrics. Added a comment explaining the naming.
Priya Nair: CI shim logs look good. Request: add retry/backoff on remote cache fetches and surface cache hit ratio in telemetry. Also can we scope Datadog tags by repo (repo:redwood) and environment?
Ava Martinez: Added backoff and cache metrics (internal/telemetry/metrics.go). Datadog tags now include repo and env. See last commit.
Ethan Cole: Verified release-window prober logic. One nit: the prober should not block merges if it cannot reach external dependency registry — made it read-only and log a warning instead. Approved after change.
Introduce lint-weight trimming and a release-window prober to reduce presubmit cost and schedule heavy tests. Opt-in via 'ci:trim' label; rollout behind CI_LINT_TRIMMER flag. See docs/ci/README.md for contributor guidance.
Run 'make ci-shim-test' for local shim integration. To simulate trimmed lint path: add label 'ci:trim' to a PR or set CI_LINT_TRIMMER=on in CI. Use scripts/ci/migrate-lint-weights.go to populate historical cache.
If presubmit regressions occur after enabling, flip CI_LINT_TRIMMER=false. Nightly backstop jobs will run heavy tests — check statsd.lint_trim.false_negatives and ci.release_prober.alerts. Migration script is idempotent.
payload.title: Introduce lint-weight trimmer and release-window prober to reduce presubmit footprint

payload.body:
Summary: Hotfix to reduce region-wide KV eviction storms that were causing transient SLO breaches during metadata-thrashing incidents. Root cause: under high regional egress the KV sticky-preserve heuristic allowed aggressive KV retention eviction loops that amplified load; eviction churn caused higher CPU on the serving runtime and led to regional retry storms. This PR introduces a defensive 'regional KV pause' gate and an exponential soft-backoff for sticky eviction decisions, plus extra telemetry and an emergency runbook link. Motivation and context: after incident SUP-9012 on 2026-02-18 we observed repeated reopen cycles tied to KV pressure; prior mitigations (short-term drain) prevented immediate outage but did not stop churn. The fix is intentionally conservative and primarily runtime-side so it can be backported to release branches. Changes in this PR: 1) runtime/eviction.go: introduce RegionKVPauseManager (lightweight gate) that rate-limits eviction churn for nodes within the same region and enforces a short circuit that prefers soft-eviction (drop non-hot prefixes) before full tenant eviction; 2) runtime/eviction_policy.go: add exponential soft-backoff state machine for sticky-preserve toggles (max backoff 30s with jitter); 3) controller/region_probe.go: expose a probe that surfaces kv_pressure_ratio and kv_eviction_churn metrics and a new API endpoint used by the control plane to annotate affected nodes; 4) telemetry/metrics.yaml: add kv_eviction_churn, kv_pause_events, kv_backoff_state metrics and Grafana dashboard fragment; 5) tests/regression_kv_shedding_test.go: deterministic regression that reproduces the pressure->churn loop and validates the pause/backoff suppresses oscillation; 6) docs/runbooks.md: emergency runbook entry "Regional KV pause and soft-backoff" and rollback instructions. Checklist: - [x] Reproduced churn in local benchmark harness - [x] Unit tests added and passing - [x] Integration scenario validated in benchlab (staging) - [x] Runbook written and reviewed - [x] Backport PRs prepared for release/2026-02-hotfix Notes on design tradeoffs: the RegionKVPauseManager is intentionally coarse-grained (region-level) to avoid per-tenant state bloat; we chose a soft-eviction-first approach to preserve hot KV prefixes whenever possible. This reduces tail-latency regressions at the cost of slightly longer memory residency for low-activity prefixes during the pause window. Follow-ups: - Consider adaptive backoff bounds driven by observed CPU/egress signals (ENG-4290) - Add per-tenant telemetry tagging for disputed prefixes (work item ENG-4354) Links: Incident SUP-9012 heatmap: https://redwood.internal/incidents/SUP-9012; Linear tasks: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4281.
Ethan Zhang: Please clarify lifecycle of the pause token—what ensures it doesn't remain sticky across long partitions?; Priya: The pause token is tied to a TTL (default 30s) and persisted only in-memory on each region coordinator; we intentionally avoid cross-region persistence to prevent split-brain persistence.
Maya Cortez: Can we gate the default max backoff to an operator-configurable value?; Priya: Added operator flag --kv-backoff-max and documented in ops/flags.md; default remains 30s.
Oliver Schmidt: Observability looks good, but add an indicator metric for 'eviction_suppressed_count' so we can alert on persistent suppression; Priya: added kv_pause_events and eviction_suppressed_count in metrics.yaml and dashboard fragment.
Hotfix: Introduced regional KV pause gate and exponential soft-backoff for sticky eviction to prevent eviction-churn storms and reduce SLO breaches under heavy regional egress. Added telemetry and runbook. Backported to release/2026-02-hotfix.
Backport PRs: release/2026-02-hotfix already prepared. Operator flag --kv-backoff-max (default 30s) and --kv-pause-threshold (default 0.75 kv_pressure_ratio) introduced. If incidents recur, escalate to runtime on-call and follow runbook section 'regional-kv-pause' to force-disable via control-plane annotation.
Risk: soft-backoff may increase memory residency for cold prefixes leading to temporary memory pressure on small nodes. Mitigation: pause is region-scoped and limited by TTL; we have a fail-open path that will revert to previous hard-eviction behavior if node memory exceeds emergency threshold (configured via --kv-emergency-memory-percent).
1) Cherry-pick to release/2026-02-hotfix and 2026-01-maintenance branches (done). 2) Monitor kv_eviction_churn and eviction_suppressed_count dashboards for 72 hours. 3) If suppression rate exceeds threshold, revert via admin flag --kv-pause-enabled=false and open ENG follow-up.
payload.title: regional-kv-pause-and-softbackoff-guard-hotfix

payload.body: Context and motivation: We have seen intermittent customer reports where long-running streaming sessions with fncall/tool calls produce corrupted structured-output boundaries or stall during the handshake when routed through busy gateway instances. Root cause analysis pointed to two contributing factors: (1) aggressive route-level payload allowances that allowed oversized control frames to bypass stream backpressure logic, and (2) a proxy coalescing window that could over-aggregate small fragments causing the fncall newline/JSON boundary detector to miss delimiters under head-of-line conditions. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a per-route soft-clamp for declared payloads and an enforced hard-cap at the gateway ingress. Soft-clamp emits telemetry and reduces credit assignment; hard-cap returns a clear 413-like OpenAI-compat error with structured JSON error body to preserve clients expecting OpenAI semantics. 2) Add a streaming proxy buffer TTL and minimum flush thresholds so fragments are not held indefinitely to wait for aggregation; this reduces boundary-detection stalls for function/toolcall handshakes. 3) Modify routing rules: small-payload preferential steering sends sub-4KB control/tool frames to low-latency worker pools; large payloads follow capacity-aware routing paths. 4) Update OpenAI compatibility layer adapter to normalize error shape for the new hard-cap and to retry a single-time route fallback to a compatible model variant (if available) when a payload is blocked due to capacity gating. 5) Add an explicit structured-output delimiter verifier that runs on stream flush to detect truncated JSON/NDJSON and surface clearer evalable errors. Implementation notes and trade-offs: The soft-clamp emits a new metric gateway.route_payload_soft_clamp{route,customer} which is used by Optimize suggestions; we kept the soft behavior conservative to avoid false positives. The hard-cap is intentionally strict to make client behavior deterministic and to enable backend autoscaling signals when customers repeatedly hit the cap. Buffer TTL is default 75ms (configurable) with an opt-out per-route for legacy customers who require maximal merge coalescing. Routing heuristics use request metadata (content-length hints, control-frame flag, and prior tail-latency samples) to pick a target worker pool; this adds an extra routing decision but reduces end-to-end fncall latency on observed workloads. Tests and safety: Unit and integration tests added: gateway/router_test.go (route selection and clamp enforcement), gateway/stream_proxy_test.go (buffer TTL and flush thresholds), compat/openai/adapter_test.go (error normalization and retry path). We exercised a canary rollout: 10% of traffic in us-west1 for 48 hours with synthetic fncall scenarios and incremental increase to 50% after observing no regressions. Backwards compatibility and rollout plan: Default behavior is backward compatible due to soft-clamp telemetry enabling and the hard-cap only triggering on oversized payloads. Customers who relied on previous implicit coalescing can opt out with a per-route annotation to restore previous buffer behavior for 30 days while they migrate. Docs and observability: Added docs/compatibility/openai.md section documenting the new 413 structured error and suggested client retry/backoff behavior. New Grafana panels for route_payload_soft_clamp and proxy_fragment_ttl_expiry were introduced and wired to the Console. Commit summary: - commit 1: gateway: add per-route soft-clamp and hard-cap enforcement with metrics emission - commit 2: stream proxy: implement TTL and min-flush threshold, add unit tests - commit 3: openai-compat: normalize hard-cap error shape and implement single-fallback routing - commit 4: sdk/python: update streaming client docstring to mention structured error handling - commit 5: docs: add compatibility notes and rollout instructions Files changed (high level): - gateway/router.go: routing decision heuristics and route annotation parsing - gateway/payload_limits.go: soft-clamp/hard-cap logic and metrics - gateway/stream_proxy.go: buffer TTL, flush thresholds, and fragment coalescer tuning - compat/openai/adapter.go: error normalization and fallback routing - sdk/python/redwood/streaming.py: client handling note and small compatibility helper - docs/compatibility/openai.md: docs for new behavior - tests/integration/streaming_toolcall_test.go: e2e scenarios and regression checks Review conversation summary: - Ethan Morales (reviewer): "Please add a short circuit for health-check traffic so the new routing heuristics don't add latency to probes." Author reply: "Added a navigator health-check bypass in router.go; updated tests to assert zero added latency." - Lina Gupta: "Can the buffer TTL be exposed as a per-customer override in the Console?" Author reply: "Planned: added backlog task in ENG-4321 to wire Console toggle; default behavior stays server-side for safety." - Marcus Lee: "OpenAI error shape change may break older clients; ensure we include a clear migration note in release notes." Author reply: "Added compatibility docs and included an example of runtime-decoding that falls back to the older shape if needed." CI and validation: - CI: build: passed - CI: unit tests: initial run failed (flaky coalescer test); rerun passed - CI: integration (streaming): passed - Load test: local run against staging clusters showed 1.8% p95 latency improvement for fncall scenarios and a 0.7% increase in gateway CPU due to lightweight routing heuristics Observability notes: - New metrics: gateway.route_payload_soft_clamp (counter), gateway.route_payload_hard_cap (counter), proxy.fragment_ttl_expiry (counter) - Alerts: created a warning alert for repeated hard-cap hits per customer (linked to support playbook) Merge and rollout outcome: Squash-merged to main on 2026-02-20 after approvals from all reviewers and green CI. Gradual rollout to production with canary gates at 10%, 25%, 50%, and 100% over 72 hours. Release notes: - Improve streaming stability for function/toolcall handshakes by reducing fragment aggregation stalls and adding explicit structured-output verification. - Add per-route payload soft-clamp telemetry and a hard-cap that returns OpenAI-compatible structured errors for oversized payloads. - Introduce buffer TTL on the streaming proxy to reduce boundary detection stalls. - Prefer low-latency worker pools for small control/tool frames to reduce fncall tail latency. - New metrics and console panels for monitoring route payloads and proxy TTL expiries.
payload.title: tighten-ingress-routing-payload-clamping-and-stream-buffer-safeguards

payload.body:
Context: alert noise from per-invocation token cost and latency spikes is creating high pager fatigue and long MTTR for long-tail cases. Motivation: reduce alert storming by grouping invocations into operationally useful buckets and provide a lightweight cross-tenant SLO explorer for root-cause and impact analysis without expensive full-trace hydration. What this PR does: 1) adds an invocation bucketizer that groups invocations by prompt-shape fingerprint, initial KV-warm state, model-variant tag, and inferred phase composition (generation vs rerank). Buckets are emitted as low-cardinality labels (invocation_bucket_id, bucket_reason) suitable for rollup counters and histograms; 2) instruments a compact bucket histogram metric (invocation_bucket_histogram) and a sampled bucket exemplar anchor that links to a short trace id for deep-dive; 3) introduces a new SLO Explorer dashboard JSON (observability/slo-explorer) with cross-tenant selectors, bucket-level aggregation, burn-rate overlays, and a lightweight diff mode to compare two time ranges or two tenants; 4) tightens sampling: we add a bucket-aware reservoir sampler that increases retention probability for underrepresented buckets to avoid masking rare but high-cost shapes; 5) adds docs and a migration guide for downstream alert rules to use bucketed rollups and avoid cardinality blowups. Rollout plan: feature flags are gated per-tenant; initial rollout to internal staging then 10 pilot tenants for 2 weeks; enable UI via feature-flagged console toggle; alert rule migration guidance provided in docs. Backwards compatibility: labels are additive; no change to existing per-invocation metrics. Performance: bucketizer code runs in the telemetry subservice, optimized for O(1) processing path with lock-free map for bucket table and async exemplar enrichment. Testing: unit tests for bucket mapping, e2e config in perf-canary, and a small replay bench to validate histogram semantics across sequence lengths. Risks and mitigations: cardinality spike — mitigated by explicit TTL and cardinality cap on bucket table; sampling bias — mitigated by reservoir uplift for low-volume buckets and a calibration job. Observability: new metrics emitted: telemetry.invocation_bucket_count, telemetry.invocation_bucket_histogram, telemetry.bucket_exemplar_trace, telemetry.bucket_warm_rate. Dashboards: slo-explorer.json, bucket-rollup-metrics.json. Migration notes: existing alerting playbooks updated to prefer bucketed 95/99p rollups with fallthrough to invocation-level when necessary. Related work: builds on ENG-1203 (adaptive sampling) and references PM-210 for tenant SLO UX. Deployment: automated helm chart patch (redwood-helm-charts) and feature flag in console. Merge method: squash.
Ethan Park: overall looks solid. Please add a brief benchmark of per-invocation tail latency overhead when bucketizer is enabled; worried about p99 on hot paths.
Maya (author): added lightweight microbench in bucket_table_test.go showing ~200ns/op overhead in optimized path, included results in PR description.
Lucia Moreno: cardinality safety is critical. Can we add a hard cap metric for number of active buckets and an alert when exceeded?
Maya (author): added telemetry.bucket_table_active_gauge and a dashboard alert that triggers at 80% of cap, included migration note to throttle new bucket creation for noisy tenants.
Samir Patel: sampling uplift approach is interesting; please document bias implications and add a calibration job as a cron in perf-canary.
Maya (author): added perf-canary replay and a calibration job script under perf-canary/replays, tests show uplift reduces false-negative rate on rare heavy-cost shapes by ~45%.
Ethan Park: CI failed initially due to a vet error; re-ran and green after fix. Approving for squash-merge.
Lucia Moreno: small nits in console component (prop typing) fixed in follow-up commit. Approved.
payload.title: Introduce invocation bucketizer and cross-tenant SLO explorer

payload.body:
Context: Intermittent user reports and internal load tests showed that long-lived SSE connections occasionally emitted fragments that, when consumed by OpenAI-compatible clients, produced partial JSON objects for function/tool call payloads. Root cause: the previous coalescing strategy favored throughput by merging fragments eagerly, and the streaming parser could flush partial JSON tokens when a function-call sentinel spanned a fragmentation boundary. This caused downstream consumers that assume atomic JSON frames to throw parse errors and led to retries and duplicated tool calls.

Motivation: We need a conservative, low-risk change to the SSE emission pipeline that prevents partial JSON emission for tool/function call boundaries while preserving overall throughput and backpressure characteristics. This PR implements a lockstep windowing approach: event fragments that may contain function-call sentinels are fenced with a small serialization handshake so reassembly is deterministic and ordering is preserved across retries and reconnects.

What this change does (high level):
- Introduces a lightweight window-state machine in runtime/sse/coalescer.go that tracks event edges and defers flush when a window contains a potential function-call boundary.
- Adds a serialization fence token ("--rf") that is omitted from the delivered SSE payload but used internally to ensure coalescer and parser agree on flush points. The fence is never exposed in the public API or to users.
- Enhances the OpenAI-compat stream parser to treat the fence as a synchronization marker: when a fence is present, the parser holds partial JSON until the matching fence/flush pair is seen.
- Adds targeted unit and integration tests that simulate interleaved tokens, reconnects, and partial-delivery scenarios.
- Provides a gradual rollout plan: feature-flagged on the coalescer and enabled by default for main, with an opt-out for Dedicated/Private customers if required for compatibility.

Checklist:
- [x] Design review with runtime and api teams (ENG-9142)
- [x] Unit tests covering edge cases (fragment split in UTF-8 boundary, split within string, split inside function-call args)
- [x] Integration test against openai-compat parser harness
- [x] E2E load test demonstrating <5% p99 token latency regression under typical traffic (verified)
- [x] Documentation PR (docs link) for rollout notes and rollback steps

Backward compatibility: The internal fence token is never emitted to clients and the OpenAI-compatible streaming endpoint continues to present the same SSE wire format. Consumers that already tolerate partial tokens will be unaffected; consumers that previously observed partial JSON parse errors should see fewer failures.

Rollout notes: Feature gated for 72 hours with monitoring dashboards in Console (SSE-parse-errors, toolcall-retries). If any significant increase in latency or user-visible regressions occur, we will toggle the flag and revert the change.

Related: ENG-9142 (coalescer redesign), ENG-9299 (openai-compat stability), SUP-445 (support ticket capturing production incidents).
Diego Martinez: This looks solid. Two asks: (1) can we avoid altering existing wire tokens in case some internal components rely on literal markers? (2) please add a perf benchmark showing the latency tail impact under 95th/99th percentiles.
Author (Ava Chen): Answered: the fence is internal-only (never emitted), added an explicit test asserting no fence bytes in final payloads; added p95/p99 slab microbench in coalescer_test.go and linked results in the PR description.
Priya Kapoor: Concern: Dedicated customers might run on slightly older parsers. Can we gate the feature by config and document the opt-out?
Author (Ava Chen): Done. Feature flag added and rollout notes updated. Also added telemetry to report if customers opt-out so we can track adoption.
Liam O'Neill: Minor: please add a comment explaining why the fence token uses the chosen sentinel and a reference to the state machine diagram. Also, consider renaming fence->serialization_fence for clarity in code.
Author (Ava Chen): Renamed internal identifier to serialization_fence and added diagram link in coalescer.go docstring.
Fixes partial-JSON parse failures over long-lived SSE streams by introducing a lockstep windowing/coalesce strategy and an internal serialization fence to guarantee function-call boundary atomicity. Rollout is feature-flagged and monitored; opt-out available for Dedicated/Private customers.
payload.title: Lockstep SSE windowing and function-call handoff to prevent partial JSON emission

Context: We are observing long presubmit runtime spikes and noisy dependency churn which cause slower feedback and occasional release regressions. This PR introduces two coordinated interventions: 1) a 'quickcheck' presubmit lane that runs a tiny, fast smoke subset of lint+unit checks for rapid developer feedback, dynamically escalating to full presubmit on larger diffs; 2) a Dependency Entropy Mitigator (DE-Mitigator), a policy + CI job that detects high-velocity transitive changes and applies conservative auto-fix suggestions (lockfile pinning, devdep pruning), plus a dry-run bot that submits candidate fixes for approval.

What I changed (high level): Consolidated presubmit orchestration into an explicit stage graph (presubmit.quickcheck -> presubmit.full -> presubmit.post-merge), added a tiny Node/Go lint shard runner and a lightweight python test-sandbox for fast isolation, implemented the DE-Mitigator analyzer (go-based), introduced new CI annotations for upward escalation thresholds, and updated release hooks to tolerate transient dep-refresh windows.

Why: Reduce median feedback time from ~7m to ~90s for small changes; reduce noisy human triage from rolling dependency churn; prevent release automation failures caused by simultaneous transitive updates.

Checklist:
- [x] New quickcheck lane + docs
- [x] DE-Mitigator prototype and CI integration (dry-run mode)
- [x] Backwards-compatible release hook changes and graceful fallback
- [x] Unit + smoke integration tests
- [x] Rollout plan: opt-in for 1 week then default-on for teams with >50% presubmit hits

Testing & rollout: Local unit tests and presubmit smoke on forked runs; staged rollout enabled via feature flag in ci-config (default off for first 48h). Monitored via presubmit-latency dashboard and dep-refresh alert (SLO: <20% false positives for DE-Mitigator dry-runs). Related work: ENG-1423, ENG-1428, SUP-210.
Ava Chen: Nice separation — can we make the quickcheck time budget configurable per-repo? (requested changes)
Lina Thompson: Added ci-flags.yaml field quickcheck.time_budget_secs with default 90s and per-repo override (reply)
Diego Ramirez: DE-Mitigator looks promising; add integration test to ensure no autopush when vulnerability score > 7 (requested changes)
Lina Thompson: Added vuln-score gating and updated tests (reply)
Samir Patel: Approving after small nits (approve)
a1b2c3d: orchestrate presubmit stages and add quickcheck runner
b2c3d4e: implement DE-Mitigator analyzer and dry-run endpoint
c3d4e5f: add escalation thresholds and CI annotations
d4e5f6a: integrate quickcheck into GitHub actions and update docs
e5f6a7b: fix flakiness observed in sandboxed python runner
Introduces a fast presubmit quickcheck lane (opt-in, default roll-out after 1 week) and a Dependency Entropy Mitigator that proposes conservative lockfile/devdep fixes. Improves median presubmit feedback time; adds CI feature flags and docs.
payload.title: Introduce slim presubmit quickcheck and dependency entropy mitigator

payload.body:
Motivation: Dedicated customers have observed oscillations when long-lived traffic patterns interact with burst credits: short sharp bursts are consumed correctly, but long tails cause over-allocation followed by aggressive decommit that violates throughput agreements and spikes latency. This PR introduces a time-windowed guarantee allocator that enforces contractual throughput over configurable windows and a burst reconciliation controller that decays burst credits with hysteresis to avoid ping-pong decommits.

Summary of changes: commits: - introduce windowed throughput allocator algorithm and integration (allocator/windowed_allocator.go) - implement burst-credit reconciler with hysteresis and decay curve (controllers/burst_reconciler.go) - add telemetry exporter for reservation utilization (pkg/telemetry/reservation_reporter.go) - configuration: new throughput contract schema and knobs (config/throughput_contracts.yaml) - unit + integration tests (alloc_test.go, burst_reconciler_integration_test.go) - docs: operations guide and migration notes (docs/dedicated/throughput-windows.md)

What it does: - Enforces contractual throughput guarantees by computing a moving budget over a configurable sliding window (default 5m) rather than a single instantary rate. Requests are admitted against the window budget to preserve long-term guarantees while allowing short bursts. - Keeps a separate burst-credit ledger per-tenant that decays via a two-stage hysteresis function: soft decay (exponential smoothing) and hard decay (linear floor) to prevent immediate credit evaporation when utilization drops. - Reconciliation loop checks for outstanding 'commitment debt' and applies proportional backpressure when headroom is insufficient, with a prioritized fallback to compatible model variants. - Emits telemetry: p50/p90/p99 for reservation utilization, windowed commit fulfillment ratio, credit inflow/outflow counters, and reconciliation events for alerting.

Files changed (high level): - allocator/windowed_allocator.go: core algorithm, admission checks, unit tests. - controllers/burst_reconciler.go: reconciliation loop, hysteresis implementation, mocks for testing. - pkg/telemetry/reservation_reporter.go: aggregator that computes percentile sketches and exposes Prometheus metrics and a compact JSON line for the backend. - config/throughput_contracts.yaml: new schema (window_size, smoothing_factor, min_credit_floor, priority_weights). - e2e/canary/reservation_simulator.go: synthetic workload generator used by integration tests to validate stability under bursty long-tail traffic. - docs/dedicated/throughput-windows.md: operator guide and recommended defaults for migration. - helm/values-dedicated.yaml: adds knobs for window_size and telemetry sampling rate.

Testing summary: - Unit tests cover admission logic, window budget roll-up, and hysteresis math. - Integration canary (local) simulates 100 tenants across three pools; validated that long-tail traffic no longer causes >20% oscillation in reservation utilization across 10 windows. - Load test in benchmark-lab shows median latency improvement during reconcilation windows (p50 down 12ms) and reduction in tail oscillation events. CI: all jobs passed (lint, unit, integration-canary, benchmark-smoke).

Review conversation (high level): - Priya: requested clearer separation between 'window budget' and 'instant quota' to avoid double-counting; author updated allocator to hold separate counters and added explicit comment blocks. - Diego: asked for telemetry cardinality controls; added sampling with configurable rate and an aggregated sketch for high-cardinality tenants. - Liam: flagged potential race in credit decay; added mutex and a small benchmark showing <1% overhead at 10k req/s per pool. - Security review: no customer data surfaced in telemetry, metrics are aggregated; noted in docs.

Migration & rollout plan: - Default behavior behind a feature flag (config: enable_windowed_alloc = false). - Stage rollout: dev -> canary -> production with 10% traffic for 24h, check telemetry: window fulfillment ratio, credit drift, and latency SLOs. - Recommended default knobs: window_size=5m, smoothing_factor=0.12, min_credit_floor=5%. Operators can tune per-tenant via Dedicated Console.

Observability & Alerts added: - alert: WindowedCommitFulfillment < 90% for 3 windows -> Investigate undersupply or misconfiguration. - alert: BurstCreditRunrate > 200% sustained -> Possible misuse or runaway jobs. - dashboard: dedicated/reservations/windowed-overview showing utilization percentiles and credit balances.

Backward compatibility: - New config fields are additive; the prior instant-rate allocator is still available and remains the default until feature flag flip. No breaking API or on-disk format changes.

Risk and mitigations: - Risk: misconfigured window_size could delay reaction to genuine capacity shortfalls. Mitigation: conservative defaults and canary rollout. - Risk: added telemetry may increase cardinality/ingestion. Mitigation: sampling knobs and sketch-based aggregation.

Merge: Squash-merged on 2025-09-18 after two approving reviews. Release note: see release_notes field.

Related: references ENG-1729 (throughput budgeting RFC), SUP-3421 (customer support case describing oscillation), and internal benchmarking doc link: https://redwood-internal/benchmarks/window-allocator-2025-09 (internal).
Introduce a time-windowed throughput allocator that enforces contractual guarantees while smoothly reconciling burst credits; adds telemetry for reservation utilization percentiles and a migration guide for Dedicated customers.
payload.title: Time-windowed guarantee allocator and burst reconciliation

payload.body:
Motivation: Customers operating in regulated jurisdictions need stronger guarantees that KMS usage and audit records respect tenant region pins while avoiding noise from benign audit failures. This PR wires a lightweight "residency-enforcer" shim into the request path and introduces an encryption mapper that selects a region-scoped KMS alias before key-wrap, plus an audit-exception handler that classifies and deduplicates expected vs. unexpected audit write errors.

What this changes (summary):
- Add a residency assertion extension to RBAC v2: services can now declare and verify tenant.residency.claims before KMS calls. The verifier supports explicit geozone and soft-affinity modes.
- Introduce kms.EncryptionMapper (small, testable component) that maps service/tenant claims + scope policy -> region-prefixed alias (e.g., alias/redwood/eu-west/tenant-abc) and records a mapping hint in request metadata.
- Add audit/exception handler that: (a) tags audit writes with residency provenance, (b) suppresses duplicate transient audit errors (with configurable window), and (c) surfaces high-severity audit policy violations as SLO alerts.
- Wire residency-enforcer as a middleware in the internal request router (runs before KMS calls and after auth).
- Add config flags to allow conservative rollout: rbacv2.residency.enabled (per-cluster), kms.mapper.mode = [strict|affinity|fallback], audit.handler.dedupe_window_ms.

Why not reuse existing residency middleware? The existing region-pin middleware handled routing but did not participate in RBAC decisions or provide KMS alias mapping; this PR complements it by making KMS choice policy-aware and making audit behavior deterministic during transient KMS errors.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc: linear ENG-3411 (link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3411/residency-enforcer-kms-mapper)
- [x] Unit tests for EncryptionMapper and ResidencyVerifier (new test package)
- [x] Integration test that replays tenant request with conflicting region claim (eu vs us) and verifies mapper picks KMS alias per policy
- [x] E2E scenario on staging (manual): simulated KMS throttling + audit sink flaps, validated dedupe and SLO alerting
- [x] Console flag added for controlled rollout

Compatibility and rollout plan: Start with kms.mapper.mode=affinity in staging for two weeks, enable RBAC residency checks in shadow mode (log-only) for 48 hours, then flip to enforced for clients that have opted in. If audit dedupe suppresses true positives, the dedupe window can be lowered; default set conservatively to 1000ms.

Security considerations: The ResidencyVerifier adds decision telemetry but does not persist keys or sensitive contexts; KMS alias selection happens server-side only. A secondary audit step records the alias hint but redacts tenant identifiers in exported telemetry.

Notes on tests and observability: 
- Added per-request telemetry tags: residency.reason, kms.alias.hint, audit.suppressed=true/false.
- New dashboard tile (Console) tracking "Residency enforcement rejections" and "Audit dedupe rate".

Files changed (high-level): added residency verifier and mapper packages, small changes in request router, new unit/integration tests, console feature flag wiring, and dashboards.

References: design doc + linear ENG-3411, related work ENG-2971 (geo-routing refactor).
Maya Patel: Nice design. Two main asks: ensure the mapper can't be spoofed by crafted headers and add a unit test for the redaction path when telemetry export is enabled.
Sofia Martinez: Addressed — mapper now validates tenant claim against the auth token signature and we added telemetry redaction unit tests (verifier_test.go).
Owen Li: Found a race in the dedupe window counter during heavy parallel writes — suggested use of an atomic slab.
Sofia Martinez: Switched to a sharded atomic counter (audit/exception_handler.go). Added comment and bench for worst-case concurrency.
Sofia Martinez: Also added console feature flag for emergency kill-switch as requested by platform ops.
payload.title: Introduce region-pin encryption mapper, RBAC v2 residency-assertions, and audit-exception handler

payload.body:
Motivation: Customers observed transient 503/stream resets when large numbers of small streaming requests arrive in short bursts (spiky PLG traffic). Root cause is short-term headroom exhaustion in route credit accounting combined with lingering per-connection write buffers that block proxy writers and prevent fast recovery. This PR introduces a conservative "burst debt recovery" mechanism plus a lightweight toolcall sanity layer to reduce malformed fncall handshake aborts and provide a compatibility fallback for older OpenAI-style tool call sequences.

What this changes (high level):
- Route credit recovery: after a short burst that temporarily drives a route into negative credit, we now allow controlled recovery credits that replenish at a higher rate for the first N seconds to avoid extended quarantine. Recovery parameters are tunable per-route.
- Transient buffer trimming: proxy writer now enforces a soft egress queue TTL that will drop/aggregate stale fragments older than configured window to prevent write stalls from building up under bursty ingress.
- Toolcall sanity layer: added strict pre-flight validation for structured fncall payloads, with fast-fail and normalized handshake for older OpenAI-compatible payload shapes. This reduces stateful retry thrashing between gateway and backend runtimes.
- Compatibility fallback: when a legacy OpenAI-style fncall pattern is detected, gateway temporarily routes to the compat shim which performs normalization and preserves streaming envelopes. This path is rate-limited and opt-in via feature flag to avoid unexpected perf regressions.
- Observability and metrics: new metrics for burst debt events, recovery credits granted, trimmed fragments, and compat fallback invocations; added alert tuning suggestions in docs.

Motivation: We need predictable, auditable canary outcomes that are reproducible for postmortems and actionable when things go wrong. This PR introduces a small deterministic smoke-simulator and a "contracted canary" controller that evaluates canaries against user-defined contracts (latency, error-rate, model-confidence regressions). When a contract is violated the controller will automatically enact rollback policies and create a Linear incident (optionally tag and escalate) to reduce manual toil.

What this changes (summary): 1) A smoke-simulator service (tools/smoke-sim) that generates deterministic synthetic sessions matching customer session shapes; it seeds KV cache and simulates model/sidecar interactions. 2) A "canary contract" DSL (config/canary_contracts/{.yaml}) and parser that allows teams to express pass/fail gates (e.g. p95_latency < 220ms, top1_confidence_delta < -0.03, embedding_cosine_drop < 0.02). 3) A controller extension in services/rollout that evaluates live traffic and simulator probes against the contract, computes an explainable failure rationale (why a contract failed), and triggers rollback or graduated traffic adjustments. 4) Linear integration: when an auto-rollback occurs the controller creates a Linear issue with an attached failure summary and reproducible smoke-sim job spec; optionally includes links to replay artifacts stored in object storage. 5) Small CLI and runbook additions for SREs to run the smoke-sim locally and to replay failing sessions for bisect.

Checklist: - [x] smoke-simulator core and deterministic RNG seed support - [x] contract DSL + parser + schema validation - [x] controller integration + telemetry (telemetry includes contract_evaluations, contract_fail_reasons, simulator_match_rate) - [x] Linear autocreate + configurable escalation mapping - [x] Unit tests for parser and controller logic - [x] End-to-end integration test that spins a minimal controller + simulator in CI - [x] docs and quickstart example in redwood-quickstarts/canary-contracts

Backward compatibility and opt-in: This is non-breaking by default. Canary contracts are behind rollout.experimental.canary_contracts. Linear autocreate requires onboarding and API key configuration per org. Existing rollout behaviors are unchanged unless a contract is attached to a rollout resource.

Related Linear/Jira: ENG-11234 defines canonical contract semantics; SUP-4021 requested autocreate for expedited incident creation during customer-facing regressions. Also references design notes: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-11234/contracted-canary-design

Risk and mitigation: The simulator intentionally uses low load and well-scoped session shapes to avoid capacity interference. Controller has rate limits on automatic rollbacks and requires two independent contract failures in a 5-minute window (configurable) before a hard rollback. Autocreate has a dry-run mode for orgs to evaluate behavior without noise.
Adds a deterministic smoke-simulator and a contract-driven canary orchestrator. Enables automatic Linear ticket creation on rollback triggers. Non-breaking: opt-in feature behind rollout.experimental.canary_contracts flag.
Daniel Kim: Can you clarify the failure aggregation window? What if we see a short spike that triggers a rollback but stabilizes after one minute?
Aisha Patel: Response: controller requires two independent contract failures across the configured window (default 5m). Added unit tests for 1- and 2-failure scenarios and documented the window in docs/canary-contracts.md.
Mohamed El-Sayed: Linear autocreate looks powerful but noisy — can we add an org-level opt-out and a dry-run toggle?

Aisha Patel: Added a concurrency-limited worker and a test harness that asserts production controllers remain within their memory budget. See tests/integration/canary_contracts/worker_throttle_test.go.

Context: As part of the Reliability Program “Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping”, we’re making incident_type/subtype and owner explicit/required in incident tooling. Motivation: existing canary detectors were sensitive to transient spikes when request rates differed significantly between control and candidate; this led to noisy alerts during A/B traffic shifts. This PR introduces a rate-normalized detector that weights latency/throughput signals by per-window QPS and explicit degradation profiles to better surface true regressions. What changed: 1) a new detector implementation (canary/detectors/rate_normalized_detector.py) that computes rate-weighted deltas for P50/P95 and request success-rate, 2) a degradation profile DSL (canary/profiles/) to encode multi-metric degradation patterns (e.g., latency-only, throughput-degen, combined), 3) staged rollback hooks and an operator-facing config (console: Rollout -> Canary -> Detector) to tune sensitivity and rollback granularity, 4) end-to-end integration tests and a synthetic traffic harness for CI. How it works: the detector computes per-bin metrics for control and candidate, scales the contribution of each bin by observed QPS and a configurable smoothing window, then applies profile-defined thresholds across metrics and a composite score with hysteresis to avoid flip-flop. If composite score crosses the profile's failure threshold for N consecutive windows the rollout guard transitions to 'soft-fail' and can optionally trigger staged rollback hooks (candidate->10%->0%). Config and rollout: new config keys under perf_canary.detectors.rate_normalized: window_seconds, smoothing_alpha, min_qps_per_bin, profile_name, consecutive_windows, rollback_strategy (none|soft|hard), staged_weights (comma-separated list). Default settings are conservative to avoid surprising behavior. Testing: we added a synthetic harness that replays production-like QPS patterns to validate noise resistance and a small collection of historical regressions to assert detection and rollback behavior. Docs and migration: console docs updated with examples and recommended defaults; feature is behind perf-canary.rate-normalized feature flag and does not change existing detectors unless explicitly enabled. Rollout plan: merge to main can be toggled for internal Canary experiments; monitor for two weeks with dashboards perf/canary/rate-normalized and a rollback cooldown. Related work: ENG-1987 (canary false positives investigation), ENG-2041 (staged rollback automation).
Introduces a rate-normalized canary detector and degradation profile primitives. Enables safer staged rollbacks based on combined latency and throughput regressions; configurable defaults are non-breaking and behind the perf-canary feature flag.

Context: We’re standardizing audit logging across Hosted/Dedicated/Private with a canonical v1 schema. RBAC is a top-tier sensitive surface (role definitions, role bindings, membership changes), and we’ve had customer reports of missing RBAC change events in Private (SUP-18421). This PR instruments the control plane RBAC service (and the HTTP layer that fronts it) to emit v1 audit events for RBAC CRUD actions with consistent actor attribution, safe diff summaries, and correlation IDs (request_id/trace_id/admin_action_id) for investigations. What’s included: (1) v1 audit event emission for RBAC endpoints: role.create, role.update, role.delete; role_binding.create/update/delete; membership add/remove; project/tenant-scoped permission bundle updates. (2) Actor identity + impersonation support: actor.type (user|service_account|service), actor.id, actor.email (when available), actor.session_id, actor.impersonated_by.* (when admin impersonation is used), and source_ip/user_agent pulled from request context. (3) Diff summaries for update operations: we generate a constrained JSON Patch-style diff (ops limited + size capped) and also include a human-friendly summary string for common RBAC changes (“added permission: models.use”, “removed member: user:abc”). (4) Correlation: request_id + trace_id propagated from gateway headers, plus admin_action_id generated for Console-initiated workflows and included in both the HTTP response and emitted audit events. (5) Safety + operability: audit emission is best-effort (does not block RBAC writes on sink failure) but increments metrics and logs structured errors; payload fields are classified and redacted (no secrets; free-form strings truncated; role descriptions not included in diffs). Testing: unit tests for diff generator + actor extraction; integration tests that exercise RBAC endpoints and assert a schema-valid v1 audit event is emitted via the in-memory audit sink. Example emitted event (redacted): {"schema_version":"1.0","event_type":"rbac.role.update","event_id":"01HRQ0...","occurred_at":"2026-02-03T19:22:11.482Z","tenant_id":"tnt_9f3...","project_id":"prj_12a...","actor.type":"user","actor.id":"usr_3c1...","actor.email":"admin@customer.com","actor.ip":"203.0.113.10","actor.impersonated_by.id":"usr_8aa...","request_id":"req_7b1...","trace_id":"9b2f...","admin_action_id":"admact_17c...","target.type":"rbac.role","target.id":"role_29d...","change.summary":"added permission: routing.policy.write","change.diff":"[{\"op\":\"add\",\"path\":\"/permissions/4\",\"value\":\"routing.policy.write\"}]"}. Rollout notes: guarded behind feature flag AUDIT_V1_RBAC_ENABLED (default on in staging, off in prod until exporter normalization is deployed); legacy audit events (pre-v1) are left unchanged for now (ENG-4833 handles normalization/deprecation). Follow-ups: Console needs to pass admin_action_id consistently for all RBAC admin flows; Private parity tracked in the installer/exporter workstreams. Checklist: - [x] Event types registered in taxonomy registry - [x] Required fields present per schema v1 - [x] No PII/secrets logged; diff capped and validated - [x] Metrics for emit failures added - [x] Integration tests added and running in CI
Ethan Park (review): Can we guarantee request_id/trace_id are always set for internal callers (e.g., migrations / cron)? If missing, what do we emit?
Benji Okafor (author): Added defaults in AuditContext: request_id generated when absent; trace_id optional (empty string omitted). For internal jobs, actor.type=service and actor.id set to the job name; added tests for missing incoming headers.
Hanae Suzuki (review): Diff payload looks like it could include role descriptions (free text). We should avoid emitting arbitrary strings to SIEMs; also ensure truncation is enforced.
Benji Okafor (author): Agreed. Removed role.description from diff inputs entirely; only include permissions + bindings + members. Diff generator now hard-caps at 25 ops and 4KB, truncates values, and falls back to change.summary when over budget.
Allison Grant (review): Please tag audit emit failures with service + event_type but avoid high-cardinality labels (tenant_id/project_id). Also confirm best-effort behavior won’t break RBAC writes.
Benji Okafor (author): Updated metrics labels to {service,event_type,result}. No tenant/project labels. Emission errors are logged + metered but do not block handler execution; tests cover sink failure path.
Marcus Lin (review): This references SUP-18421. Are we covering the specific missing events (role binding changes) and do we have a way to correlate Console actions across multiple calls?
Benji Okafor (author): Yes—role_binding create/update/delete and membership add/remove included. admin_action_id is generated for Console-initiated flows and returned as a response header so subsequent calls can reuse it; Console follow-up tracked separately but control plane supports it now.
Ethan Park (review): Ship it after the diff cap change. Approved.
Hanae Suzuki (review): Approved after redaction changes; thanks.
Marcus Lin (review): Approved.

Motivation: Several production incidents and bench runs showed that CUDA graph capture/replay can regress tail latency and correctness for mixed-length traffic. Root causes we observed: (1) captures taken on a short, unrepresentative sequence can pick kernels and shape guards that later fail or trigger expensive fallbacks; (2) the kernel selection scoring ignores sparsity and dtype compatibility which leads to suboptimal kernel mappings during replay; (3) a subtle KV-cache offset alignment bug causes token duplication when a capture primes partial KV pages. This PR adds a lightweight priming buffer, a kernel compatibility scoring function used at capture-time, and a scheduler gate to avoid capturing until sufficient priming samples are collected. The PR also fixes the KV-cache alignment issue and wires telemetry for diagnosing capture health.

What this changes (high level):
- runtime/cudagraphs/priming_buffer.*: new priming buffer that conservatively stores short sequence samples per device and route. Buffer exposes an API to query representative shapes and average sparsity.
- runtime/kernels/compatibility_score.*: new scoring function that returns a compact compatibility score for (kernel, shape, dtype, sparsity). Scoring biases toward kernels with robust fallback semantics and lesser sensitivity to small sequence length drift.
- scheduler/capture_gate.*: capture gating logic that prevents starting a cudagraph capture until priming buffer reach a configurable threshold (defaults: 8 samples or 5s). Also supports force-capture CLI flag for debugging.
- runtime/kv_cache/align_fix.*: fix for KV cache offset calculation to ensure page alignment when reusing primed KV segments. Adds regression test that reproduces prior duplication.
- telemetry/capture_health.*: emits priming buffer hit/miss, capture_decision, chosen_kernel_score, and kv_alignment_events.
- tests/cudagraphs/*: unit and integration tests covering gating, scoring boundary cases, and an end-to-end replay correctness test under mixed-length traffic.

Design notes and rationale: The idea is to decouple capture priming from production traffic as little as possible while still collecting representative samples. The priming buffer is intentionally bounded and per-device to avoid OOM pressure. The compatibility score is a simple integer (0-100) computed from binary compatibility flags (dtype/sparsity/kernel-stability) and a small penalty for narrow shape margins. During capture we compute the score for potential kernel mappings and prefer the highest scoring mapping that meets a minimum threshold. If no mapping meets the threshold and gating is enabled, we delay capture until more priming data arrives; otherwise we fall back to the non-cuda-graph path. The scoring logic is kept deterministic and cached keyed by model+op so replay decisions are reproducible.

Commits (summary):
- a1b8d2c: add priming buffer implementation and unit tests
- b3f7e21: implement kernel compatibility scoring + benchmarks
- c2d9f74: add capture gate and config knobs (env + console)
- d4e2a13: fix kv cache alignment + add catch regression test
- e5a0e9b: telemetry and tracing for capture decisions
- f6b3c5d: wire integration tests and CI GPU job update

Files changed (selected):
- runtime/cudagraphs/priming_buffer.cpp (new), priming_buffer.h (new), priming_buffer_test.cpp (new)
- runtime/kernels/compatibility_score.cpp (new), compatibility_score.h (new), compatibility_score_test.cpp (new)
- scheduler/capture_gate.cpp (new), capture_gate.h (new)
- runtime/kv_cache/align_fix.cpp (mod), kv_cache.cpp (mod), kv_cache_test.cpp (mod)
- telemetry/capture_health.cpp (new)
- tests/integration/cudagraph_replay_mixed_lengths.py (new)

Small code excerpt (illustrative only):
- compatibility_score.h: int computeScore(const KernelMeta& k, const Shape& s, float sparsity);
- priming_buffer.h: bool shouldDelayCapture(const RouteKey& r); // checks sample count + diversity

Review conversation (high level, chronological):
- Marcus Lee (review): "This looks promising — can you explain why we chose 8 samples as default? Also add a test that simulates high-sparsity kernel mismatch so we don't regress again."
- Author (Asha): "8 was chosen empirically from bench runs across 3 models (chat, code, summarization). Added comment and made it configurable via REDWOOD_CUDAGRAPH_PRIMING_SAMPLES. Added a high-sparsity test (compatibility_score_test covers this)."
- Elena Gomez (review): "Nit: telemetry key names should follow existing naming conventions (camelCase). Also we need to ensure privacy-safe content never enters priming buffer."
- Author: "Renamed keys to captureHealth.* and added redaction in priming buffer to strip token content; only shapes/sparsity stored. See priming_buffer_test for validation."
- Tomoya Saito (review): "KV alignment fix looks correct but please add a microbenchmark to show no perf regression for large KV reuse cases."
- Author: "Added microbench and included results in PR description; <1% throughput regression in worst case, often a win due to fewer fallbacks."
- Marcus (approve): "LGTM after CI green and one nit about log level for capture gating."
- Author: "Adjusted log level to debug for frequent events and info for state transitions."

CI & testing:
- CI initially failed on azure-gpu-integration: deterministic-seed test flaked (randomized scheduling produced a non-deterministic ordering). Reproducer added and fixed by seeding the scheduler's collector; rerun passed.
- GPU perf smoke job included microbench; results attached to CI artifacts.
- All unit tests and Linux GPU integration jobs passed on rerun. ci_status marked as pass.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan:
- Default gating enabled on main for a gradual rollout. We will monitor captureHealth metrics and only enable force-capture for select canaries.
- Console exposes a per-route override to tune priming sample threshold and minimum compatibility score.
- If customers see captures delayed too long, support can increase maxWaitMs or lower score threshold.

Potential follow-ups (tracked in ENG-1382):
- Adaptive thresholding: make sample counts depend on model variance detected at runtime.
- Persist priming buffer snapshots across restarts for hot routes.
- Backfill samplers for cold-start routes using synthetic sequences.

Merge details: squash-and-merge. Commit message includes a short summary and links to ENG-1382 and ENG-1399.

Notes for on-call / SRE: The captureHealth.telemetry stream will be the primary signal for regressions. Alert if captureDelay > 30s or captureFallbackRate > 5% for a route during a 5m window. The patch includes a dashboard tile in observability/ that teams can add to their service view.

QA checklist (completed): [x] unit tests added [x] integration tests for mixed-length replay [x] kv-cache regression reproduced and fixed [x] telemetry wired [x] perf microbench attached

If you want to exercise locally: export REDWOOD_CUDAGRAPH_PRIMING_SAMPLES=4 to lower the gating threshold and run tests/tests/integration/cudagraph_replay_mixed_lengths.py.

This PR is intentionally conservative: it prefers delaying capture over taking brittle captures, and adds fallbacks so we can iterate after collecting telemetry in prod.
- Improve CUDA graph capture/replay stability by introducing a priming buffer and kernel compatibility scoring.
- Reduce warmup regressions for mixed sequence-length workloads.
- Fix KV-cache alignment bug that caused occasional token duplication under primed captures.
- No user-visible API changes; runtime internal behavior only.

Background and motivation: We continue to see customer telemetry showing bursts of near-simultaneous credential refreshes from multi-threaded clients and short-lived connections. Those refresh bursts increase load spikes against the auth service, and in edge cases can cause transient stream drops while SDKs independently backoff and retry. This PR introduces a lightweight, compact credential scheduler (a small local coordinator in each SDK) plus a synchronized set of streaming retry profiles that reduce reconnect churn and improve cross-language parity. The goal is better out-of-the-box stability for short-lived streams and more predictable unit economics for high-concurrency clients.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds compact credential scheduler implementations in Python/TypeScript/Go (sdk helpers only). The scheduler batches/defers refreshes, applies jitter windows, and exposes a minimal contract for external credential providers to implement (observe/refresh).
- Standardizes streaming retry profiles across SDKs: short, balanced, and conservative presets with explicit default values for: initial_delay, max_delay, multiplier, max_retries, and heartbeat_window.
- Updates streaming connection handshake to consult the SDK-level scheduler for credential validity before attempting reconnects (reduces back-to-back auth failures).
- Backfills unit tests and e2e smoke tests that exercise cross-language behavior under load via the existing harness.
- Adds a short migration guide in docs/sdk-migration/credential_scheduler.md and updates the TypeScript and Python changelogs.

Design notes:
- The credential scheduler is intentionally minimal: it does not centralize network calls across processes, only within an SDK instance. It is safe to use in multi-threaded and event-loop contexts. The API surface is one small trait/interface (observe, refresh_if_needed) plus an optional background wake hook.
- Retry presets were chosen after analyzing production disconnect histograms; they aim to reduce rapid reconnect storms while keeping recovery latency acceptable for interactive apps.

Checklist:
- [x] Feature in Python SDK: compact scheduler and tests (redwood-sdk-python/src/redwood/cred_scheduler.py).
- [x] Feature in TypeScript SDK: compact scheduler and tests (redwood-sdk-typescript/src/cred/scheduler.ts).
- [x] Feature in Go SDK: compact scheduler and tests (redwood-sdk-go/cred/scheduler.go).
- [x] Cross-language docs and migration guide.
- [x] E2E smoke tests added to benchmark-lab/e2e/cred-burst.test.
- [x] CI green and manual canary run on staging.

Commits (high level):
- feat(sdk): add compact credential scheduler interface and Python implementation

- docs: add migration guide and changelog entries

Context: Multiple SDK teams have independently evolved auth and stream retry ergonomics which caused subtle surface mismatches and test flakiness for cross-language examples. This PR aligns token/session shapes, provides production-oriented retry presets, and ships explanatory docs + a CI matrix that runs representative auth+stream integration tests across Python/TypeScript/Go.

Motivation: reduce cognitive overhead for integrators, remove accidental incompatibilities when clients switch languages, and reduce production incidents caused by inconsistent default backoffs.
