Adds an adaptive holdoff controller that smooths regional backpressure signals and reduces oscillatory failover; no behavioral changes to public API. Recommended rollout to Canary before global rollout.
Summary: Implement a telemetry-backed 'Kinetic Backpressure Holdoff Controller' to smooth transient overload signals from regional health probes and avoid aggressive failovers. Motivation: During several incidents we observed oscillatory regional failovers driven by short-lived probe bursts and abrupt circuit flips. This PR introduces a lightweight signal normalizer + warmup window that dynamically prolongs holdoff when a region is exhibiting high variance, reducing wasteful failovers and improving overall SLO stability.

What this changes (single-string description): The change introduces a new controller in runtime/eviction that consumes existing region health metrics (p50/p95 latency, error-rate derivative) and computes a kinetic score. The holdoff duration for regional failover/circuit-open transitions is adjusted by a smoothing factor proportional to recent signal kinetic energy so that noisy spikes lead to gentle, time-decayed extensions rather than immediate eviction. The controller is policy-driven: default policy is conservative for production but can be tuned per-customer in Dedicated/Private deployments.

Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-4321) - [x] unit tests for smoothing math and boundary cases - [x] integration test for simulated burst -> no oscillatory failover - [x] telemetry/metrics added for kinetic_score, holdoff_extension_ms - [x] e2e canary run (small fleet) completed

Commits summary: - feat(holdoff): add kinetic score calculator and policy bindings (priya/kinetic-score) - feat(holdoff): integrate kinetic controller into region state machine and expose metrics (priya/holdoff-integration) - test: add unit/integration tests and a load simulation harness (priya/tests)

Files changed (high-level): - runtime/eviction/kinetic_controller.go (new) - runtime/eviction/holdoff_policy.go (modified) - runtime/eviction/holdoff_policy_test.go (new) - observability/metrics/registry.go (modified to register kinetic_score, holdoff_extension_ms) - integration/simulators/regional_burst_sim.go (new test harness) - docs/operational/holdoff-controller.md (new) - scripts/deploy/canary.yaml (updated canary rollout config)

Code snippets (small illustrative): - kinetic score core: "func kineticEnergy(samples []float64) float64 { /* compute variance-weighted derivative */ }" - policy usage: "holdoff = baseHoldoff + policy.SmoothingFactor*kineticEnergy(history)"

Testing and CI: - CI matrix: unit (go test ./...), linters (golangci-lint), integration (small simulation) - Initial CI run: one flaky integration test (integration/simulators/regional_burst_sim.go) failed on first run due to timing race; reran integration job, passed. Final CI state: pass.

Review conversation (high level): - Evan Lu (reviewer): "Nice approach, I like the kinetic metaphor. Two questions: 1) how do we guarantee this won't indefinitely prolong holdoff on a partially recovered region? 2) can we expose the saturation cap for holdoff extension?" - Priya (author): "Answered: controller decays kinetic energy with exponential half-life (configurable); added a max_extension_ms cap and a telemetry alert if cap is hit. See holdoff_policy.go changes lines ~120-160." - Sofia Martinez: "Please add an integration test that simulates repeated small bursts — verify no cumulative drift." - Priya: "Added repeated-burst scenario in regional_burst_sim.go; included assertions on no cumulative growth beyond cap." - Oliver Grant: "Suggest adding an opt-out flag for dedicated/private installs for early adopters; otherwise looks good." - Priya: "Added install-time flag and updated docs/operational/holdoff-controller.md with instructions." - Evan Lu: "Approval: LGTM after addressing comments." 

Operational notes: - Metrics added: telemetry/kinetic_score (histogram), telemetry/holdoff_extension_ms (gauge), telemetry/holdoff_cap_hit (counter). - Dashboard: new panel added under runtime > regional-failover to visualize kinetic_score vs regional_ejects. - Canary guidance: enable controller in canary region for 48h, monitor holdoff_cap_hit and regional_ejects. If cap_hit rate > 1% over 24h, lower smoothing_factor by 25%.

Rollout & rollback: - Rollout method: gradual canary in canary.yaml -> 10% -> 50% -> global. - Rollback path: flip feature flag runtime.features.kinetic_holdoff=false and redeploy controllers.

Merge outcome: squashed merge into main on 2026-02-14 after CI passed and approvals. Changelog entry created under docs/operational/CHANGELOG.md.

Notes on uniqueness/compatibility: This implementation focuses on smoothing high-frequency variance (kinetic energy) of telemetry signals rather than absolute thresholds; it complements existing SLO enforcement and circuit logic by avoiding oscillations under noisy probes. No API breaking changes; policy knobs are additive and disabled by default for Dedicated/Private until customer opt-in.

Context: A recent incident (SUP-4032) exposed cases where short-lived node flaps in a region caused the local health-probe to mark large swathes of nodes as unhealthy, triggering aggressive degraded-route failovers and cascading capacity spikes in adjacent regions. This PR introduces a conservative override mechanism at the health-probe layer that prevents transient flaps from causing an immediate routed-degradation for multi-tenant customers while retaining fast failover semantics for sustained outages.
Motivation: We need to reduce noisy regional failovers and avoid expensive cross-region ramping while preserving our SLO-driven failover behavior for real outages.
Goals implemented: 1) Introduce a "degraded-route override" decision that can be set by the probe manager for a tenant-region pair to suppress immediate routed degradation for a short bounded window when flapping is detected. 2) Add dampening logic (exponential backoff with jitter) to extend override windows for repeated flaps and expire them quickly after stability. 3) Ensure override decisions are tenant-scoped and cannot suppress manual operator-initiated failovers or critical circuit-breaker actions. 4) Expose operator-visible metrics and an alert threshold so SREs can tune sensitivity.
Description of changes: - services/health-probe: new override API, dampening state machine, and conservative default config (see health-probe-config.yaml). The probe manager now computes an "override_decision" with fields {tenant_id, region, expires_at, reason} and surfaces it via the probe-status stream. - runtime/router: policy_override.go consumes override_decisions and applies a precedence rule: operator/manual > circuit-breaker > override > automatic-slo-enforced-degrade. This avoids override masking an operator outage directive. - Tests: policy_override_test.go includes scenarios for single-flap, repeated-flap with increasing override windows, and expiry behavior under restored health. - Observability: new metrics (health_probe.override_count, health_probe.override_window_seconds) and an alert that fires if override windows exceed 5 minutes for more than 2 tenants in 10m.
Migration and rollout: defaults are conservative (initial override window 8s, max 3 backoffs). This was behind a feature flag defaulted ON for regions with rolling probe versions >= 1.14. Operators can adjust via deploy/manifests/health-probe-config.yaml. CI: unit tests + integration harness for probe->router flow ran in CI; all checks passed (see ci checks summary below).
Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear ENG-7891 - [x] Feature flag gated - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Observability and alert added - [x] Rollout plan in docs/ops/regional-failover.md
Rollout plan: staged to low-traffic regions for 24h, monitor health_probe.override_count and cross-region capacity spikes, then expand to remaining regions over 48h.
Risk assessment: low — does not change circuit-breaker threshold behavior and cannot suppress operator/manual failovers. However, a misconfigured long override could delay legitimate failover; alerting mitigates this.
CI checks summary: - unit-tests: pass - integration-probe-router: pass - lint: pass - static-analysis: pass - e2e-simulated-failover: pass
Review conversation (high level): - Diego Alvarez: "Please add explicit invariants that prevent override from suppressing operator-initiated failovers and document the tenant-scoping." (addressed in second commit and docs) - Priya Natarajan: "Can you make the initial window configurable via configmap and add a test that simulates clock skew?" (added configmap and a mocked-clock test) - Liam O'Connor: "Metrics look good; add an alert for runaway overrides." (added alert) - Maya Chen (author): "Addressed comments, added tests and docs; moved defaults to conservative values and gated behind the probe version check." Merge: squashed and merged to main after approvals from Diego and Priya.
Release notes: "Health-probe: add transient-flap override to reduce noisy regional failovers; conservative defaults enabled by probe-version gating. Operators can tune windows via config. See docs/ops/regional-failover.md for rollout guidance." Links: Linear ENG-7891, SUP-4032 incident writeup, internal runbook updated in docs/ops/regional-failover.md

Summary: Introduce a classification-aware enforcement shim that carries data-classification labels from ingress through policy evaluation and audit enrichment, and influences KMS key selection. Motivation: customers in regulated industries require per-object handling guarantees (e.g., 'restricted' vs 'public'); prior work enforced tenant+region constraints but lacked classification-aware access controls. This PR implements a light-weight, opt-in path that ties classification to RBAC v2 predicates, audit metadata, and CMK selection.||What this changes: 1) frontproxy now accepts/normalizes X-Data-Classification and validation metadata; 2) a classification predicate for the RBAC v2 evaluator (policy DSL extension) that supports allow/deny by classification and legal_basis; 3) audit pipeline enrichment includes classification, classifier_version and legal_basis with an append-only envelope; 4) KMS allocator update to prefer classification-bound keys and respect region pinning when classification requires residency; 5) a migration shim for older tenants (falls back to preexisting behavior) and an operator-facing rollout flag; 6) new unit/integration/e2e tests and docs.||Design notes: Policies are evaluated after tenant/role checks but before side-effecting operations; classification is treated as an attribute (subject/resource) available to predicates. We keep the shim opt-in via feature.guard.classification_rbac (default: off); when disabled the system behavior is unchanged. KMS selection uses a soft-preference model: if a classification-mapped key exists in the requested region it is selected, otherwise we fall back to tenant-default key and emit an audit flag for operator review.||Testing and rollout: Added exhaustive unit tests around the predicate evaluator, integration tests that assert audit enrichment and KMS selection in multi-region scenarios, and an e2e that simulates cross-border datasets. Canary rollout plan: enable for internal customers, monitor audit volume and false-positive access denials, then progressively enable for opt-in tenants. Rollback: flip feature.guard.classification_rbac to false, which removes predicate enforcement but preserves enriched audit logs.||Commits: See commits list below.||Files changed summary: policy engine + predicate, gateway middleware, audit enricher, kms allocator, helm values, docs, and tests.||Operational considerations: We publish a short migration runbook (docs/compliance/classification-guidelines.md) and a monitoring dashboard with the top N denied requests by classification. Expected performance impact: negligible for common paths (classification header parse + predicate check ~ sub-ms); KMS allocator adds a small consistent lookup (cached).||Security review: encryption of the classification header is recommended for external clients; we added validators and size limits to avoid header injection.||Related: ENG-4821 (classification policy framework), SEC-314 (compliance gating), SUP-8901 (customer support case driving scope)
Add classification-driven RBAC predicates and audit enrichment. New KMS key selector honors classification and region pinning. Rollout gated by feature flag; no immediate breaking changes. Backwards-compatible shim included.

Context: Long-tail cost regressions and noisy token-level signals make it hard to triage why an invocation became expensive. We instrument a lightweight 'span fanout' sampler that, when an invocation exceeds a configurable cost threshold, opportunistically increases tracing sampling for its child spans and records token-level cost deltas and cache-effect annotations. Motivation: give SREs and on-call engineers an end-to-end view of per-invocation token cost and where the cost amplifies across the serving pipeline without permanently increasing global sampling rates. What this PR does: 1) runtime: add telemetry/span_fanout.go implementing a bounded fanout sampler that tags sampled spans with token_cost_delta, kv_cache_hits, model_variant and invocation_stage. The sampler respects per-tenant and per-route budgets and decays after the critical window. 2) metrics: introduce a token_cost_delta Prometheus metric and a compact histogram for per-invocation token timelines. 3) console: add a new dashboard JSON (Invocation Cost Explorer) that surfaces invocation timeline, span fanout tree, cumulative cost waterfall, and a sortable table of top contributing spans. 4) alerts: introduce tuned alert invocation-cost-regression which uses route-weighted thresholds and an exponential backoff to avoid noisy pages for known bursty routes. 5) docs + tests: add a docs page that explains the sampler knobs and a test harness to simulate fanout under quota constraints. Backwards compatibility: fanout is off by default and sampling respects existing global sampling settings. Rollout plan: staged enablement by tenant via feature flag and a 2-week canary with enhanced retention for fanout traces. Checklist:
- [x] implement fanout sampler and tagging
- [x] export token_cost_delta and histogram metrics
- [x] add dashboard JSON and panels
- [x] add alert with suppressions for bursty routes
- [x] unit + integration tests
- [x] docs and runbook entry

Notes on design decisions: the fanout sampler is intentionally conservative: it only amplifies sampling for direct child spans of a high-cost root invocation, has a strict max-per-invocation cap, and records an opaque fanout_id for cross-join in downstream systems. Token-level cost deltas are stored as delta-per-stage to make comparisons across model variants easier. The dashboard is intentionally focused on forensics (single-invocation deep-dive) rather than rollup aggregates; rollups will be a follow-up. Related work: builds on prior token-span-attribution work (see ENG-1310) and complements the Invocation Fingerprint panels. Migration & ops: new config keys added to telemetry config; default shown in docs; ops should monitor the fanout_sampler.total_samples metric during rollout.

tests: add span_fanout test harness and synthetic invocation generator
docs: add observability/invocation-explorer.md and runbook notes
fix: address flaky integration test by adding deterministic clock mock

Summary: This PR completes the permissioning work for the tenant-aware config diff endpoint by wiring AuthN/AuthZ roles + OAuth scopes into the handler and adding a time-bounded break-glass path for on-call responders during Sev0/Sev1 incidents. The intent is to make incident-bot v2 and Console diagnostics safe-by-default (least privilege, customer-safe output) while still enabling responders to unblock themselves in emergencies with explicit audit trails.

Context: We introduced the config diff endpoint in PR-29112 with redaction hooks and basic authorization plumbing, but we were still relying on coarse environment allowlists. During the 2025-02-07 Hosted API incident followups and INT-3312 we identified gaps: (a) bot lacked a narrowly-scoped permission to call diff in prod, (b) SREs needed a documented break-glass procedure for Sev0/Sev1, and (c) Security required auditable, severity-gated access.

What’s included: 1) Scope + role enforcement: The config service now requires BOTH (i) a service identity scope for machine calls and (ii) a user role for interactive calls. Service-to-service (incident-bot): new scope `configdiff:read_redacted` for customer-safe diffs (redacted + allowlisted fields only). Interactive (Console / CLI): new permission `config.diff.read_redacted` gated by role `platform-oncall` or `sre-oncall` (via Policy Engine). No path returns unredacted diffs via this endpoint. 2) Break-glass for Sev0/Sev1: Added endpoint path `POST /v1/config/diff:breakglass` which returns the same redacted diff but allows bypassing the normal role check when ALL of the following are true: request includes `incident_id`, `severity` in {SEV0, SEV1}, `oncall_user` (from OIDC), and `slack_channel_id` + `slack_thread_ts` for correlation; caller has base scope `breakglass:request` (limited to SRE tooling identities) and is in the on-call group (Pager duty group sync) OR is a member of `sre` org team; break-glass grant is time-bounded (15 minutes) and rate-limited per incident/user. The handler writes a dedicated audit event (see below) and includes a response banner field `breakglass_grant_expires_at` for downstream UI warnings. 3) Policy Engine wiring: Added policy bundle rules to express “standard access” vs “break-glass access” explicitly. This removes the previous env-based branching and makes reviews easier for Security. 4) Audit logging: Emits `audit.config_diff.access` on every request and `audit.breakglass.grant` when break-glass is used (fields: incident_id, severity, tenant_id_hash, actor, client_id, reason, slack_channel_id, slack_thread_ts, grant_ttl_seconds, decision). These align with the audit event schema added in PR-29133. 5) Guardrails: Added per-tenant + per-actor QPS limits for diff reads to prevent incident-bot bursts from amplifying outages. Added a “deny by default” behavior if severity is missing or malformed (no implicit downgrade). All responses include `redaction_applied=true` and omit any raw secret-bearing keys even if present in config state.

Implementation notes: - Auth: Uses Gatekeeper-issued OIDC claims for `actor` and `groups`, plus mTLS client identity for service calls. Bot uses service identity only; user identity is required for interactive. - Tenant handling: Tenant identifier is hashed in audit logs; raw tenant id remains in service logs (restricted) but not in audit event payload. - Redaction: Break-glass does NOT change redaction behavior; it only changes who can retrieve the redacted diff. (Unredacted diff remains an internal-only admin workflow outside of Slack/incident-bot.) - Backwards compat: `GET /v1/config/diff` behavior remains but now enforces policy; callers without the new scope/role will receive `403` with a remediation hint.

Motivation: engineers building multiplexed streaming features and long-lived session flows were repeatedly re-implementing small pieces (per-call heartbeat timing, credential refresh windows, demultiplexing logical streams on a single connection, and ad-hoc hedged retries). This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) session-profiles: a lightweight, declarative profile for per-client session tuning (auth refresh window, heartbeat cadence, prefetch hints) surfaced in Python/TS/Go SDKs; 2) stream-demux operator: a transport-agnostic operator that lets the client demultiplex multiple logical streams over one websocket/HTTP2 stream while preserving typed cursor semantics; 3) hedged-retry-simplifier: a pragmatic preset that replaces the previous complex hedging knobs with a small, well-documented policy that matches common production patterns. Implementation notes: session-profiles are implemented as a tiny JSON schema plus SDK-friendly builders; profile resolution is performed client-side with explicit override precedence (env -> constructor arg -> Linear-linked default); stream-demux is implemented as a composable operator layer that plugs into existing PullStream/AsyncGenerator surfaces (no runtime dependency changes); hedged-retry-simplifier provides a default policy and a small, documented API for advanced customizations. Cross-SDK changes: python: new session_profiles module and convenience factory, stream demux context manager, tests and examples, bumped to v1.28.4; typescript: new SessionProfile builder, demux operator exported from streaming package, and public types, bumped to v1.27.0; go: SessionProfile struct and StreamDemux helper with minimal GC allocations, bumped to v1.9.2. Backwards compatibility: defaults are no-op for users who don't opt into session-profiles or demux; hedged-retry-simplifier replaces the default hedged behavior but preserves surface; migration notes added to SDK changelogs. Testing: unit tests for profile resolution matrix, integration tests that exercise demux over ws and http2, fuzzed retry policy validator, and cross-sdk e2e that verifies credential refresh and stream reconnection across simulated auth flaps. Benchmarks: microbenchmarks show demux adds ~1.5ms median overhead to the happy-path per multiplexed frame but reduces connection counts by ~70% in the multiplexed scenario; hedged-retry-simplifier reduced spurious duplicate hedged requests by 30% in synthetic tail-latency tests. Rollout: feature flags enabled, staged rollout to internal Dedicated customers for two weeks, then full platform merge. Related work: builds on ENG-2979 (stream checkpoints) and ENG-3120 (credential lease), references SUP-7012 for an incident that triggered this effort. Checklist: [x] design doc linked in Linear ENG-3245; [x] unit + integration tests; [x] changelog entries; [x] SDK version bumps; [x] docs PR in redwood-docs queued.
Adds session-profiles and a stream demux operator to unify multiplexed stream handling; introduces a simplified hedged-retry preset and bumps SDK versions (python v1.28.4, typescript v1.27.0, go v1.9.2).

Context and motivation: production inference workloads show large variation in decoded sequence lengths (short responses for embeddings/intent classification, long for summarization). Existing autoscaling uses request-count and aggregate token rates which underprovisions for long-decoding tails and overprovisions for short bursts. This PR introduces a sequence-length-aware window autoscaler (seqlen-window-autoscaler) that tracks token-decoding distributions per pool and per tenant and makes scale decisions on a time-windowed, p95 token-decoding budget. It also introduces a tenant burst degrade limiter: a soft admission controller that intentionally degrades non-critical bursts from a tenant when observed utilization cross-couples with other tenants and risks latency SLOs.

Changes in this PR (summary): - New autoscaler component: seqlen_window_autoscaler that computes decodelength histograms, estimates per-request token costs, and converts short/long mix into an effective concurrency target. - Tenant burst degrade limiter: admission policy that applies graceful tail-drop (drop-to-limited-concurrency) for bursty behavioral patterns while recording decline reason and offering automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant. - Telemetry: per-pool and per-tenant metrics for seq_len_p50/p95/p99, token_rate_by_seqbucket, effective_concurrency_estimate, and degrade_limiter_events. - API: config knobs under dedicated/autoscaling: window_size_seconds, seq_buckets (bins), pctl_target, degrade_thresholds, degrade_duration_seconds, fallback_policy. - Safety: integrate with existing provision-safety-checks to avoid decommitting capacity during sustained long-tail decoders; add a back-pressure signal to gateway routing to prefer fast-compatible model variants during degrades. - Tests: unit tests for histogram merging, end-to-end simulation in benchmark-lab with synthetic seq distributions, and integration smoke with dedicated fleet in staging.

Detailed usage notes (single-line config example): {"autoscaling":{"type":"seqlen-window","window_size_seconds":60,"seq_buckets":[0,32,128,512,2048],"pctl_target":95,"scale_up_multiplier":1.25,"degrade_thresholds":{"p95_cpu":0.85,"p95_latency_ms":1200},"degrade_duration_seconds":30}} (actual config lives under dedicated/config/autoscalers.yaml). The autoscaler operates as a replacement policy for pools that opt-in; default remains the existing token-rate autoscaler.

Commits (high-level): - a1b2c3d: initial seqlen_window_autoscaler implementation + histogram proto and merge logic - b4c5d6e: integrate autoscaler into provisioner API and add configuration plumbing - c7d8e9f: tenant burst degrade limiter + admission API and gateway backpressure hook - d0e1f2a: telemetry labels, metrics, and dashboards + unit tests - e3f4g5h: simulation harness and integration test fixes

Files changed (high-level): - dedicated/autoscaler/seqlen_window_autoscaler.go: core logic for windowing and histogram-based concurrency target - dedicated/autoscaler/histogram.proto: compact histogram message and merge helpers - gateway/admission/degrade_limiter.go: tenant burst limiter and policy enforcement - telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml: new metrics definitions and tag keys - console/dashboards/seqlen-utilization.json: new observability dashboard - benchmark-lab/simulations/seqlen_mixture_test.py: synthetic workload and validation harness - tests/autoscaler/seqlen_window_test.go: unit test matrix

Small illustrative snippet (autoscaler decision, pseudo-code): "if p95_estimated_token_rate > provision_capacity * safety_margin then signal_scale_up() else if bursty_tenant && degrade_limiter.ShouldDegrade(tenant) then apply_graceful_degrade(tenant)". This is intentionally high-level; see dedicated/autoscaler/seqlen_window_autoscaler.go for exact thresholds and smoothing constants.

Review timeline and conversation (highlights): - Miguel Soto (2026-02-11): "Nice design — can you clarify how histograms are merged across pools? Concerned about memory usage at high cardinality." - Ava Chen (2026-02-11): "We use fixed bins (configurable) and only store counts + sample moments; per-tenant histograms are sharded and TTL'd after inactivity to bound memory. Added comments and a benchmark in sim harness." - Priya Nair (2026-02-13): "Need to ensure degrade events are rate-limited to avoid flip-flopping; also add observability that ties degrade events to fallback model choice." - Ava Chen (2026-02-14): "Added a token-bucket rate limiter for degrade events and expanded telemetry with degrade_reason and fallback_model tags." - Liam O'Connor (2026-02-15): "Integration tests look good, but failing flakily under high synthetic variance." - Ava Chen (2026-02-16): "Tuned smoothing window from 30->60s and added jitter in sim to validate. Reran CI and repros are stable."

CI checks and status: - build: passed - unit-tests: passed (coverage +0.4%) - integration-smoke: passed in staging - lint: passed - benchmark-regression: baseline within 1% - e2e-dedicated: passed after stability fix

Edge cases and limitations: - This autoscaler assumes requests report expected output token estimation; for models that perform variable decoding strategies (e.g., sampling with early stop heuristics) observed lengths can still be noisy — the policy uses conservative smoothing. - Per-tenant histogram labels introduce extra cardinality; disabled by default for tenants with <1000 reqs/day. - The degrade limiter is soft: it opts for graceful capacity shedding or fallback to fast variants; we do not unilaterally kill in-flight requests.

Operational notes for SRE: - When enabling for a pool, monitor metrics: seqlen_effective_concurrency, seqlen_bucket_counts, degrade_limiter_events and fallback_model_uses. - Recommended rollout: canary two pools with traffic mirroring enabled, watch for p95 latency regressions and increase window_size_seconds if noisy. - Rollback: switch pool autoscaler config back to "token-rate" and clear degraded_tenants cache.

Merge outcome: squashed and merged into main (merge method: squash). Backported a small hotfix to release/2026-02 for an off-by-one in bucket indexing.

Related work: links to design doc and Linear tickets: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1429/seqlen-aware-autoscaler-design (reference), internal runbook: docs/internal/autoscaling-seqlen.md.

Checklist (task list): - [x] Proto and merge semantics implemented - [x] Autoscaler core logic with smoothing and target conversion - [x] Degrade limiter with rate limiting and gateway hook - [x] Telemetry and dashboards added - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Simulation harness for varied seq distributions - [x] Docs and operational runbook updated
Miguel Soto: Can you clarify histogram merge and memory bounds?
Priya Nair: Add rate limiting for degrade events and telemetry tying degrade->fallback
Liam O'Connor: Integration tests flaky under synthetic variance; increased smoothing window

payload.body:
Problem: During a regional overload incident on 2026-02-22 we observed aggressive circuit flips and tenant thrashing when regional nodes attempted to rejoin after transient KV pressure. That led to repeated SLO violations at p95 and p99 for conversational routes. The existing regional circuit state machine was too eager to reopen and lacked coordination across nodes, which amplified token-cost storms and caused cascading backpressure. Goal: Introduce a small, low-risk coordinator and a conservative fallback mode that (1) prevents rapid-open/rapid-close loops across a region (Rapid Regen Fallback), (2) enforces a soft SLO invariant at the admission layer (SLO Invariant Keeper) to prevent global SLO regressions, and (3) provide telemetry + a one-button rollback. This PR is a targeted hotpatch (branch hotfix/rapid-regen-slo-keeper) intended to be applied quickly to release and staging and then merged to main after verification. Design summary: - Regional Circuit Coordinator (new component) maintains ephemeral region-level state: recent reopen_attempts, probation windows, and a token budget for reopens. Coordinator exposes a REST/gRPC probe and integrates with the existing circuit manager via a lightweight lease (backed by existing coordination KV). - Rapid Regen Fallback: when a node attempts to reopen a circuit, the coordinator evaluates reopen_budget and recent_failures. If the budget is exhausted the node is placed into a rapid-regen fallback state: reject reopen, keep serving existing cached responses (fastpath), and begin a longer, randomized backoff with telemetry. - SLO Invariant Keeper: admission controller consults regional SLO metrics (rolling p95 proxy latency, failed_responses) and will gracefully degrade admission (soft-deny new long-run requests and route them to a lower-cost model variant or a queued fastpath) when the invariant is under pressure. Degradation is rank-preserving (preserves highest-priority tenants first). - Safety and rollback: feature gated behind runtime flag enable_rapid_regen and a canary rollout policy. There is a manual revert script included. All new behavior has opt-outs via per-tenant config. What changed (high level): - pkg/coordination/regional_circuit_coordinator.go (new): coordinator logic and lease handling. - internal/admission/slo_invariant_keeper.go (new): admission rules and degradation policies. - runtime/config/flags.go: new flags for gating and thresholds. - api/telemetry/metrics.yaml: added metrics definitions and dashboard pointers. - cmd/ops/revert_hotpatch.sh: rollback helper. - tests/*: unit + e2e scenarios for circuit stability and graceful degrade. Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to staging with canary=false for 4 hours, watch slo_invariant.violation_count and circuit_coordinator.reopen_rate. 2) Canary exact 10% of production traffic for region-eu-west for 1 hour. 3) Expand to 50% then 100% if no regressions. Metrics to watch: slo_invariant.violation_count, circuit_coordinator.reopen_attempts, route.p95_token_latency, tenant.priority_failures. Rollback plan: run cmd/ops/revert_hotpatch.sh or disable enable_rapid_regen via runtime config and ensure coordinator drains. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for coordinator state transitions - [x] Integration test simulating KV pressure rejoin pattern - [x] Metrics and dashboards updated - [x] Can be toggled off per-tenant - [x] Ops revert script included Risks and mitigations: - If coordinator lease cannot be acquired (KV partition), nodes fall back to local conservative behavior (no reopen for configured ttl). This is explicitly tested. - Potential for increased latency for low-priority tenants; mitigated by tiered degrade and observability. Reference: incident SUP-8742, related design note ENG-3421.
Jonas Kline: Looks good overall; please add a short note in docs/ops about expected reopen_rate baselines for our top 10 tenants.
Maya Chen (author): Added baseline note and a dashboard link in metrics.yaml; re-ran tests.
Priya Singh: Ensure we have a safe default for enable_rapid_regen (disabled) and that the canary policy is explicit in release notes.
Maya Chen (author): Default is off; updated release notes and canary instructions in revert_hotpatch.sh.
Ethan Ramirez: Small nit: prefer randomized jitter in backoff to be drawn from exp distribution; can we add in follow-up? Approving now.
Hotpatch: add regional circuit coordinator and SLO Invariant Keeper. Enables safe, coordinated reopen backoff and admission-based graceful degradation to protect global SLOs. Feature gated, default off. Ops: canary rollout instructions and revert script included.
If you observe an increase in slo_invariant.violation_count after enabling, disable enable_rapid_regen immediately. If coordinator lease errors surface, the nodes will fallback to local conservative ttl-based no-reopen behavior; watch circuit_coordinator.lease_errors metric and escalate to infra-team if >5/min for >5m.

Context: customer signals and internal SDK parity work showed divergence in how Python/TS/Go SDKs express credential presets (refresh window, fallback chains) and a number of ergonomics gaps for streaming consumers (pull vs push primitives, cancel semantics). Motivation: converge on a compact, language-idiomatic 'CredentialPreset' surface plus a small 'stream primitive' layer that gives each SDK a stable, minimal contract for retries, heartbeat/keepalive, and cancel semantics rather than re-implementing rights/refresh logic per SDK. This reduces duplication, improves telemetry uniformity, and enables cross-SDK samples to behave identically. Changes (summary): introduced CredentialPreset model and presets registry with three modes (ephemeral-lease, rotating-fallback, delegated-pass-through) implemented in Python/TS/Go clients; added a StreamPrimitive interface/facade implemented as PullStream (py/ts) and StreamHandle (go) with identical observable semantics; centralized retry profiles used by streaming reconnect into a small shared spec and adapted each SDK to map to it; bumped SDK version pins: python->1.12.0, typescript->2.4.0, go->1.5.3; updated examples and migration guide. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-9876), [x] unit tests for each SDK, [x] integration tests for streaming handshake and reconnect, [x] sample app updated, [x] changelogs and migration notes. Commits: "add credential preset registry and spec (initial)"; "py: implement CredentialPreset + PullStream adapter + tests"; "ts: CredentialPreset + PullStream facade and examples"; "go: CredentialPreset mapping + StreamHandle + compat layer"; "align retry profiles and wire into streaming reconnect"; "bump versions and update changelogs". Files changed (high level): "sdks/python/redwood/credentials.py"; "sdks/python/redwood/streaming/pullstream.py"; "sdks/python/tests/test_credential_presets.py"; "sdks/typescript/src/cred/presets.ts"; "sdks/typescript/src/stream/pullStream.ts"; "sdks/typescript/test/stream-reconnect.spec.ts"; "sdks/go/cred/presets.go"; "sdks/go/stream/stream_handle.go"; "examples/credential-presets-migration.md"; "docs/sdk-migration/credential-presets.md"; "changelogs/python-1.12.0.md"; "changelogs/ts-2.4.0.md"; "changelogs/go-1.5.3.md". Testing & CI: unit-tests passed for all three SDKs; integration tests that exercise a simulated token refresh and reconnect passed after two iterations; linting applied in TS (prettier/eslint) and py (ruff/black) with a single style fix commit; e2e benchmarks flagged a transient latency regression on high-concurrency pullstream reconnect which was addressed by a small batching tweak and re-run. Review thread (high level): Miguel: requested clearer separation between CredentialPreset semantics and transport-level heartbeats; response: split the transport heartbeat into StreamPrimitive and left CredentialPreset pure (auth only) in second commit; Emily: asked for clearer migration docs and a shake-out of degenerate fallback chains; response: added examples and migration guide with recommended presets; Jordan: raised a concern about Go ergonomics around context cancellation mapping to PullStream cancel semantics, addressed by adding StreamHandle.Cancel and backing it with context.WithCancel under the hood. CI Checks: ["unit-tests (py): pass", "unit-tests (ts): pass", "unit-tests (go): pass", "integration/streaming: pass", "lint (ts): pass", "style (py): pass", "benchmarks: pass after fix"]. Jordan Lee: Go cancel semantics look leaky — how does StreamHandle.Cancel map to context? Asha: Implemented Cancel backed by context.WithCancel and added unit tests in sdks/go/tests.

payload.body:
Motivation: When aggressive speculative prefill and chunked prefill are enabled we observed KV-cache write hot spots and contention on a subset of worker shards. This manifests as elevated p99 decode latency during high-concurrency prefill bursts. This PR introduces two coordinated changes: 1) an overlap-aware KV-cache routing layer that routes prefill writes to a rotatable set of shards to avoid single-shard hotspots, and 2) a prefill throttling token-bucket that smooths bursty prefill scheduling while still allowing decode overlap. Design: - KV routing: annotate prefill chunks with a routing token derived from request id + chunk index; use lightweight consistent-rotor that prefers local shard but rotates under load. This is implemented as a pluggable Router trait so future strategies (e.g., model-aware hashing) can be added. - Prefill throttling: per-worker token bucket with adjustable refill rate and burst capacity. Prefill scheduler consults token bucket before scheduling chunk prefill; decode stage has a higher priority lane and can borrow tokens for immediate low-latency decode when necessary. - Overlap heuristics: a short-lived 'overlap window' (ms configurable) allows prefill and decode to run concurrently; if the token bucket is exhausted the scheduler will fall back to staggered prefill that prioritizes decode continuity. Implementation summary: - runtime/scheduler/prefill_router.rs: new Router trait and Rotor implementation (approx 180 LOC). - runtime/scheduler/prefill_throttle.rs: token-bucket + metrics hooks (120 LOC). - runtime/kv_cache/shard_writer.rs: minor changes to accept routing token and perform non-blocking handoff. - runtime/executor/overlap_controller.rs: integration glue and configuration flags. - tests/runtime/bench_overlap.rs: microbench harness for p50/p95/p99 under synthetic load. - e2e/ci/prefill_integration.test: integration asserts for correctness and no cache corruption. Backwards compatibility: router defaults to previous behavior when disabled; default config keeps prefill enabled but conservative throttle parameters. Rollout plan: staged feature flag enabled on canary pool then ramp to production over 72 hours with metrics monitoring (kv_write_conflicts, prefill_retries, p99_decode_latency). Checklist: - [x] unit tests for routing and token-bucket - [x] integration tests for decode correctness - [x] microbench numbers attached - [x] docs: config knobs documented in ops/configs.md - [x] metrics and dashboard PR queued
Introduce overlap-aware KV cache routing and a prefill throttling mechanism to reduce hotspot contention and improve tail latency under high concurrent prefill loads. No API changes.
Arjun: Can you justify why rotor-based routing is better than deterministic hashing in high churn? Response: rotor keeps affinity but rotates under pressure; deterministic hashing caused permanent hot shards on skewed request ids.
Lena: Suggest adding a metric for token-bucket drained events. Response: added prefill_throttle.drained_count and export in metrics.
Diego: Concern about additional allocations in hot path. Response: optimized Router to use stack-allocated small buffer and re-used rotor state; microbench shows minimal overhead.
Arjun: Please add a short runbook entry in ops for throttle tuning. Response: added to ops/configs.md with recommended knobs for small/medium/large clusters.
Synthetic concurrent prefill workload (2000 concurrent streams): p50 latency improved 8%, p95 improved 12%, p99 improved 22% after enabling rotor routing + throttle (throttle conservative config).
Hotspot test (single-request-id skew): prior p99 spikes to 1.2s, new routing reduces peak to 420ms with same hardware and kernel versions.
Throughput: end-to-end token/sec unchanged (+/- 2%) under sustained load; decode tail improved due to less prefill contention.
Feature gated behind runtime.feature.overlap_prefill (default enabled on canary).
Ops knobs: prefill_throttle.refill_rate, prefill_throttle.burst, overlap_window_ms. Start with recommended values in ops/configs.md.
Rollback: feature flag off or throttle refilled to high value to mimic legacy behaviour. No schema changes to persisted cache layout.
Follow-ups: explore model-aware routing and estimate-driven token allocation per model size.

Motivation: In high-concurrency mixed workloads we observed recurring tail latency spikes when prefill chunk boundaries synchronized poorly with decode work and kernel launches were fragmented across tiny micro-batches. This PR introduces an interleaving scheduler and a kernel coalescing layer that let decode start earlier and group adjacent kernel invocations to amortize launch overhead. Goals: reduce p99/p999 latency, improve throughput for short and medium sequence workloads, and avoid regressions on long-form generation. Summary of changes: 1) stage-interleaver scheduler: schedules prefill and decode tasks on the same GPU worker in a fine-grained round-robin when prefill progress crosses a configurable watermark (prefill_watermark_ms). This allows decode to begin as soon as the first chunk arrives rather than waiting for full prefill completion. 2) kernel coalescer: runtime/kernel_coalescer.cpp groups compatible kernel calls (same op, compatible dtypes and seq lengths) originating from different pipeline stages within the same dispatch tick; coalescing is conservative and respects memory headroom heuristics. 3) prefill chunk metadata: prefill chunks now carry a compact token-range watermark and KV signatures so the decode stage can perform safe speculative KV reads and early KV cache lookups. 4) KV shard-awareness: KV cache eviction and soft-evict heuristics were updated to avoid evicting shards currently used by in-flight interleaved decodes. 5) Batching policy updates: continuous batching now maintains micro-batch windows per stage to allow bounded cross-stage coalescing without increasing tail latency. 6) Observability: new metrics (runtime.prefill_watermark_latency, runtime.kernel_coalesce_count, runtime.interleave_slices) and a small dashboard patch. Tests & bench: unit tests for the coalescer, scheduler integration tests in tests/runtime_interleave_test.py, and microbench harness updates in tools/benchmarks/prefill_decode. Benchmarks (internal mixed-short workload): median token latency -6.1%, p95 -9.8%, p99 -12.3%, throughput +29% when kernel coalescing enabled; worst-case memory overhead <3% for our test matrix. Rollout: feature flag runtime.enable_interleaved_prefill (default off). Canary rollout to dedicated pool followed by gradual percentage ramp. Backwards compatibility: no API changes, KV cache format unchanged; flag-controlled. Checklist: - [x] scheduler + coalescer design doc linked in Linear - [x] unit/integration tests - [x] benchmark harness updates - [x] feature flag + fallback path - [x] observability & dashboards - [x] small canary and SLA watchlist Commits summary: see commits list below. Changed files (high level): runtime/scheduler/stage_interleaver.cpp, runtime/kernel/kernel_coalescer.cpp, runtime/kv/kv_shard_manager.cpp, runtime/kv/prefill_metadata.h, tools/benchmarks/prefill_decode_bench.py, tests/runtime_interleave_test.py, docs/perf/prefill_decode_interleave.md, scripts/canary_rollout.sh, build/meson.build (runtime entries), ci/runtime_integration.yml. Review notes: initial CI run flagged a flaky integration test (interleave timing); fixed by adding deterministic tick injection in test harness. Memory safety and race conditions were carefully audited; sanitizer runs were clean on our CI hardware. Merge: squash and merge after approvers signed off.
Marcus Reed: Overall this is promising; main concern is memory pressure when coalescing in worst-case burst traffic. Can we bound coalescing by a soft memory budget?
Leah Kim: We implemented a soft headroom budget that refuses coalescing beyond a percentage of free GPU memory; fallback is immediate dispatch. See kernel_coalescer.cpp heuristics and the new metric runtime.kernel_coalesce_skipped_by_mem.
Priya Nair: How does this interact with KV cache eviction? I worry about thrashing on small KV shards.

Motivation: Dedicated fleets must avoid brittle capacity spikes and cross-pool overload during transient surges. This PR introduces a transient headroom allocator plus a spillover backpressure calculator to improve graceful degradation and fairness when capacity is constrained.

What it does (summary):
- Adds a transient headroom allocator that computes short-term headroom budgets per-tenant using a decaying forecast window (exponential decay over 30s by default). Headroom is expressed as a prioritized budget vector (steady, burst, emergency) so we can differentiate sustained commits from true bursts.
- Implements a spillover backpressure calculator used by the gateway/router to compute an orthogonal "spill score" when a pool is near saturation; the score drives either soft-rejects or cross-pool forwarding according to policy.
- Exposes new telemetry: per-tenant utilization histograms (P50/P90/P99), headroom consumption traces, and spill events as structured logs so Optimize can recommend warm-pool sizing.
- Adds a fairness window applied to burst grants to prevent repeated micro-burst monopolization (sliding-window token decay).

Design notes: The allocator runs every 250ms and uses an internal lightweight forecaster built on EWMA+variance to avoid O(n) per-request overhead. The spillover calculator uses occupancy and recent ingress gradient to compute a probabilistic spill probability; this reduces thrashing compared to hard thresholds. Policies are pluggable so Dedicated customers can opt into strict throughput guarantees or latency-first burst modes.

Backward compatibility: Default policy preserves existing SLOs; new settings are behind a feature flag (dedicated.transientHeadroom.enabled = false by default) and do not change current autoscaler contracts unless explicitly enabled.

Testing: Unit tests for allocator math, integration test that replays synthetic burst traces against a local fleet (included), and a small load test in perf-canary which verifies 12% lower 95th percentile tail amplification during controlled bursts.

Deployment plan: Gradual rollout behind flag, staged to non-production fleets for 48h, then canary to 3 production pools, followed by full rollout if no regressions.

Related: ENG-4321 (burst fairness), ENG-4367 (spillover telemetry), incident INT-21983 noted an event where cross-pool spill generated oscillation which this PR addresses.
Maya Chen (review): Nice separation of concerns. Question: why EWMA and not a tiny AR(1)? Can you add a short justification and link to the microbenchmarks?
Sofia Ramirez (reply): EWMA chosen for computational simplicity and bounded memory; added microbenchmarks in allocator_test.go and commentary in docs/operators/transient_headroom.md.
Arjun Patel (review): Spill probability looks promising, but I saw a small oscillation in the integration replay when combined with the existing warm-pool autoscaler. Request: add a damping term or minimum hysteresis window.
Sofia Ramirez (reply): Added a minimum hysteresis of 500ms and a damping coefficient in spillover_calculator.go; integration replay now shows stable convergence.
Introduce transient headroom allocator and spillover backpressure calculator behind feature flag. Adds tenant-level utilization histograms and spill_event logs. Optional policy knobs for throughput-first vs latency-first behavior.

Motivation: Under high write-heavy inference workloads the KV cache shows repeated small spill events and high fragmentation which increases device-to-host paging and amplifies downstream latency spikes. This PR introduces a two-part mitigation: a pressure-driven partial compaction pass that opportunistically coalesces adjacent freelist segments without doing full in-place compaction, and a spill-smoothing controller that rate-limits spillback by applying a moving-average based backpressure signal to the request scheduler. Design summary: 1) Partial compactor: a lightweight, incremental compaction routine that runs per-tenant when fragmentation_ratio > configurable_threshold. It scans small contiguous free ranges (configurable max_range_bytes) and merges them into larger slabs by doing local pointer adjustments and an optional small memcpy for adjacent live slots. The pass is bounded by budget (time_slices_per_epoch, bytes_moved_per_epoch) to keep p99 latency impact minimal. 2) Pressure-driven reservation: when device resident memory pressure exceeds a high watermark the allocator reserves a small eviction buffer per-tenant to avoid thrashing; the buffer size is adaptive (feedback loop tied to recent spill bytes and request QPS). 3) Spill-smoothing controller: computes an exponential moving average of spill_rate and uses a PID-inspired dampener to produce a spill_budget token rate consumed by the scheduler. When budget is exhausted the scheduler shifts requests to non-blocking paths or short-circuits to a lower-capacity model variant. 4) Telemetry and knobs: added kv.cache.fragmentation_ratio, kv.cache.partial_compact_runs, kv.cache.spill_budget_ratio, and a feature flag kv.partial_compact.enabled. Rollout plan: feature guarded behind runtime flag, staged rollout to internal canaries (10% traffic) for 48h, followed by 50% then full. Checklist: - [x] design doc reviewed (ENG-4621) - [x] unit tests for compactor/allocator - [x] integration test with simulated fragmentation - [x] canary run and perf observations - [x] CI green and load-tested on perf-lab Results: On perf-lab synthetic mixed read/write workload (80% read, 20% write) with heavy hotspotting, spill frequency reduced by ~34% and host paging bytes decreased by ~1.6x. End-to-end p99 generation latency improved ~12% under 95th percentile memory pressure scenarios. Caveats: partial compaction moves small amounts of memory and does not replace a full defragmentation for extreme fragmentation cases; the spill-smoothing tradeoff may route some requests to lower-quality variants under sustained pressure. References: Linear ENG-4621 (partial compactor), ENG-4702 (spill smoothing), linked incident SUP-3121 for root cause analysis.
Synthetic perf-lab (mixed workload, hotspotting): spill events reduced by 34%
Host paging bytes decreased by 1.6x during peak
End-to-end p99 generation latency improved by 12% under high memory pressure
CPU cost increase: +2% median (compaction work amortized), GPU unaffected

Config knobs: kv.partial_compact.enabled, kv.partial_compact.max_range_bytes, kv.spill_smoothing.window_ms. Default is disabled for older clusters; enabled in new deployments.
To enable on a cluster: set kv.partial_compact.enabled=true in runtime config and monitor kv.cache.fragmentation_ratio and kv.cache.spill_budget_ratio.
If you observe increased CPU without spill reduction, reduce kv.partial_compact.time_slices_per_epoch or increase max_range_bytes.
Fallback: feature can be toggled off without restarting serving processes; graceful drain of compactor state occurs within configured epoch windows.

Context: High-concurrency continuous-batching workloads expose two related sources of tail-latency and throughput loss in the paged KV cache: (1) contention and fragmentation in the block allocator when many small requests allocate and release slots concurrently, and (2) reactive prefetching that either overfetches cold blocks or stalls hot-path allocations while waiting on reclamation. Motivation: Reduce allocator lock contention, improve reuse of hot blocks across tenants, and ensure prefetching does not induce stalls. This PR implements a prefetchable shared-reservation allocator combined with a hysteresis-driven slab reclaimer and tenant-aware reservation hints. Summary of changes: - Introduce SharedReservation token: callers can acquire a lightweight reservation token that guarantees a best-effort slot will be available for the next N allocations. The token abstracts a reservation window to allow callers to prefetch or warm KV ranges without immediate blocking. - Prefetchable allocator path: new fast-path in block_allocator that consumes SharedReservation tokens; when a token is present the allocator will attempt to allocate from a reserved mini-pool before taking global locks. This reduces cross-core contention during continuous-batching. - Hysteresis slab reclaimer: slab_reclaimer now uses dual-threshold hysteresis per-slab (low/high watermarks) to avoid thundering reclaims under oscillating load; background reclaims are rate-limited and may defer to on-path eviction when latency SLO allows. - Tenant-aware reservation hints: scheduler exposes tenant access patterns to allocator via a small hints API so the allocator can bias reservations to tenants with tight latency budgets. - Kernel selection hint plumbing: added a small opt-in hint so the serving runtime can prefer quantized kernels when allocation pressure is high to reduce memory footprint and speed eviction. - Metrics and tracing: new metrics for reservation token usage, reservation miss rate, prefetch hit rate, and hysteresis-triggered reclaim counts. Added traces on allocation hot-path for post-mortem analysis. - Tests & benchmarks: unit tests for SharedReservation semantics, stress test to reproduce prior contention, and end-to-end benchmarks showing improvements in 99th percentile latency under continuous batching. Commits (high-level): - commit 1: add SharedReservation token type, token pool, and API surface
- commit 2: implement prefetchable fast-path in block_allocator and fallback logic
- commit 3: add hysteresis-based slab_reclaimer with rate limits and metrics
- commit 4: tenant hint plumbing, kernel selection hint integration, docs and tests
- commit 5: benchmark rig, CI tuning, and minor fixes Review summary: Initial implementation accepted by reviewers after two rounds of iteration. Main reviewer concerns were correctness under failure paths (token cleanup on panic), ensuring no unbounded memory growth with reservations, and clarity around tenant hint privacy/safety. All concerns addressed: tokens are tied to request lifetimes and reconciled in allocator shutdown paths; reservation pools are capacity-limited and observable via metrics; tenant hints are opt-in per-tenant and sanitized before use. Performance: On our continuous-batching benchmark (64 clients, batch size 8, mixed read/write, seq_len=512) this change reduced allocation median time by ~38% and 99th percentile tail allocation latency by ~54% compared to baseline. End-to-end 99th percentile generation latency improved by ~22% at peak load with no regression in throughput. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated (kv.reservation_prefetch.enabled=false by default). Gradual rollout to prod: enable for canary fleet (10%) for 48h, collect reservation miss metrics and prefetch hit rate, then 50% for 72h before full rollout. Operator docs: added tuning guidance in docs/ops/kv-tuning.md describing reservation window sizing and hysteresis thresholds. Migration notes: none required for on-disk format; runtime-only behavior change. Related work: This complements the recent KV hotprefix pinning work (see ENG-3110) by focusing on allocator-level smoothing and prefetch coordination.

Aisha: tokens are tied to RequestContext and we added a drop handler; added unit test that simulates panic via assert panic in test_reservation.rs.
Linnea: Hysteresis thresholds look reasonable, but we should expose them as ops tunables and document tradeoffs.
Aisha: thresholds exposed in docs and values.yaml; added examples for conservative/aggressive profiles.

Unit tests for token semantics, stress tests reproducing prior contention, and end-to-end continuous-batching benchmarks. Canary rollout plan and metrics to observe reservation misses and prefetch hit rate.

Recommended operators to tune reservation window and hysteresis thresholds for their workload.
If seeing migration of memory usage or unexpected reservation growth: check kv.reservation_prefetch.enabled, reservation_miss_rate, reservation_pool_size and per-tenant caps. Feature flag can be disabled dynamically to revert to baseline allocator behavior.

Motivation: Improve our model promotion story by running high-fidelity shadow traffic comparisons and progressively promoting models from shadow -> canary -> full based on both fidelity and operational metrics. This PR introduces a lightweight 'fidelity gate' service that scores shadow responses against production baselines, new wiring in the servegraph to support hybrid shadow+canary lanes, and a promotion controller that performs staged ramping with automatic rollback when fidelity or SLO gates fail. Key constraints: non-disruptive to existing traffic routing, minimal added latency to the control plane, and clear observability for on-call. Changes include: 1) fidelity-gate service and scoring adapters; 2) servegraph route extensions to attach shadow lanes with sampling and response capture; 3) promotion-controller that drives staged weight increases, evaluates fidelity/latency/error budgets, and triggers rollback snapshots; 4) e2e smoke harness and replay simulator for local validation; 5) instrumentation and new telemetry buckets (fidelity.score, fidelity.delta_histogram). Checklist: - [x] fidelity service prototype and unit tests - [x] servegraph integration and backwards-compatible config flags - [x] promotion controller with canary holdpoints and rollback snapshots - [x] end-to-end smoke and replay tests (simulated production traces) - [x] dashboards and alert rules added - [x] documentation draft for runbooks and Linear tickets. Related: ENG-4521 (promotion controller design), ENG-4590 (servegraph shadow plumbing), SUP-203 (customer-driven shadow request). Rollout plan: deploy fidelity-gate as opt-in behind feature flag; enable hybrid shadow lanes for a small cohort; run comparative replay for 48 hours before auto-promotion opt-in. Testing: unit, integration, synthetic traffic replay, and a limited staged rollout to a dogfood account. Risks and mitigations: transient false positives from scoring are smoothed by an annealing window and require sustained degradation for rollback; added control-plane load is bounded by a sampling quota and cache layers. Merge method: squash and merge.

Context: During a recent incident (INC-2026-02-high-kv-pressure) we observed aggressive tenant eviction and immediate circuit flips for tenants with marginal SLO violations. Root cause analysis showed a lack of machine-readable justification attached to SLO enforcement decisions and a hard circuit unwind that did not account for transient KV pressure spikes. Motivation: Provide operators and SREs better observability into why a request was shed or a tenant downgraded, and soften abrupt rejections with a short-lived graceful-unwind path that gives recovery-friendly signals and reduces customer-facing errors. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) a SLO Decision Inspector (runtime telemetry component) that emits structured rationale for shedding/circuit transitions, and 2) a Graceful Unwind polyfill that implements a short, probabilistic slow-path acceptance window instead of a binary reject during short-lived SLO overages. Summary of changes: - runtime/inspector: add decision_inspector.go which produces compact decision records (json-lines) with reason, inputs (slo_score, kv_pressure, inflight, tenant_weight), and suggested_action (shed/queue-accept/defer). Records are emitted to the local telemetry buffer and to the decision-audit log stream when configured. - runtime/shedder: introduce graceful_unwind.go which implements a tokenized slow-path that accepts a small fraction of requests for a configurable window when SLO breach is detected. Slow-path uses exponential backoff on acceptance rate when errors persist. - orchestration: small feature flag (feature.slo_decision_inspector) and runtime config knobs (graceful_unwind.window_ms, graceful_unwind.initial_accept_pct, graceful_unwind.cooldown_ms) added to config schema and console defaults. - tests: unit + integration tests that simulate KV pressure spikes and assert no customer-visible 5xx increase while keeping SLO error budget accounting intact. - docs: new troubleshooting section in docs/observability/slo-decision-inspector.md with sample queries and Kibana dashboards. Implementation notes: - Decision records are intentionally compact and redact tenant identifiers by default; when tenant opt-in is present (via org-config) full context can be emitted to the audit stream. - The graceful unwind is conservative by default: 5% initial acceptance for 5s window, halving acceptance on each error, and full revert to normal policy after cooldown. - We preserved existing metric names; new metrics: slo_decision.recorded, graceful_unwind.accepted, graceful_unwind.rejected, graceful_unwind.window_entered. Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind feature.slo_decision_inspector and gradual rollout via console controls. - Step 1: enable telemetry recording only in staging for 24h, validate record volume. - Step 2: enable decision-audit stream for a small set of tenants (canary) and validate operator dashboards. - Step 3: enable graceful_unwind at 1% of clusters, monitor 5xx, latency, and slo_decision.* metrics. - Backout: revert feature flag or set initial_accept_pct to 0 to disable graceful path immediately. - Ops runbook entries added (docs link). Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests against kv-pressure harness - [x] docs updated - [x] feature flag and config validated - [x] telemetry (record sampling) implemented - [x] runbook and rollback steps documented Commits summary: - Add decision inspector and serializers - Implement graceful unwind slow-path and integrate with shedder - Add feature flag, config, and console defaults - Tests and telemetry dashboards - Docs and runbook Changes (high level): - src/runtime/inspector/decision_inspector.go - src/runtime/shedder/graceful_unwind.go - src/config/feature_flags.go (add flag) - src/config/graceful_unwind.yaml (defaults) - telemetry/dashboards/slo_decision_inspector.json - tests/integration/kv_pressure_unwind_test.go - docs/observability/slo-decision-inspector.md Review notes: reviewers asked for a tight retention policy for decision records and assurance that no PII leaks into the default stream. I added redaction by default and a per-tenant opt-in documented in the runbook. CI: full unit suite and integration harness were run on linux-amd64 and linux-arm64; small lint fixes applied after initial run. Expected impact: reduce noisy tenant evictions, surface actionable telemetry for SRE/engineers, and lower customer-visible 5xx at marginal slowdowns without increasing overall SLO cost materially.

Introduce a lightweight "log_heft_index" metric and an interactive Cost Provenance Playground to help SREs and engineers correlate verbose logging with unexpected token-level inference cost. Motivation: while we have token-cost and span telemetry, teams struggle to attribute cost spikes to excessive logging or chat-system debug output that inflates prompt/response sizes. This PR adds: 1) a runtime-exposed metric (redwood_runtime.log_heft) that weights log lines by verbosity and semantic size; 2) trace/span enrichment to annotate invocation traces with log_heft and primary provenance keys so traces can be joined with log shards; 3) a Console dashboard (Cost Provenance Playground) with panels: log-heft scatter vs token-cost, session provenance sankey, provenance query builder, and an interactive sample explorer that links to a sampled trace and compact log excerpt; 4) an alert tuning change: new alert rule heavy-log-cost-drift that triggers only when log_heft > P95 and cost-delta exceeds a dynamic window, plus a suppressor to reduce noisy alerts from known high-verbosity clients; 5) sampling adjustment: span sampler gets a small prioritization boost for invocations with high log_heft so we preserve observability for potential cost-root causes; 6) tests and a small synthetic replaybench to validate provenance joins at scale. Backwards compatibility: metric addition is additive-only; no breaking API changes. Implementation notes: log_heft is computed at log-emit time in the runtime library using a heuristic combining token-estimate, structured field count, and message nesting depth; the trace enricher attaches these as tags and emits a compact provenance key derived from the invocation fingerprint and KV-cache-id. The Console JSON is intentionally lightweight to allow iterative refinement by SREs. See linked Linear tasks for follow-up instrumentation and threshold tuning.

Summary: This PR adds an explicit "--mode=lts" (aka "LTS mode") to the runtime release notes generator. LTS notes are intentionally slower-change and enterprise-friendly: they include curated summaries, a compatibility matrix, and a known-issues block with workarounds. Motivation: Dedicated/Private customers are asking for patch notes that are auditable and predictable (less noisy than mainline changelogs), while still capturing security fixes and operational guidance. This is a prerequisite for cutting the first 1.18.x LTS patch notes from labeled PRs + a small curated input file. Scope: This change is limited to formatting/output + data ingestion for known issues/compat sections. It does not change release tagging, publishing, or any branching logic. Design notes: (1) Input sources: (a) merged PR metadata (title, number, labels, author, merge SHA), (b) a per-release curated YAML file for human-approved summaries (optional overrides), (c) a compatibility matrix YAML (runtime<->driver/cuda/helm/installer), and (d) a known-issues YAML that is maintained by Runtime/SRE. (2) Output: emits both Markdown (customer-facing) and a JSON sidecar used by Console to link sections and render a compact summary. (3) Taxonomy: LTS mode uses a stricter category set (Security, Reliability/Correctness, Performance, Ops/Tooling, Documentation) and suppresses low-signal buckets ("Refactors", "Chores") unless explicitly curated. (4) Safety: generator fails hard if required metadata is missing for Security entries (CVE id or "CVE-PENDING" + tracking link) or if compatibility YAML is inconsistent (unknown GPU/CUDA tuple). Usage: ./tools/release_notes/gen.py --mode=lts --version 1.18.1-lts --base runtime-1.18-lts --since-tag 1.18.0-lts --curation tools/release_notes/curation/1.18.1-lts.yaml --known-issues tools/release_notes/known_issues/lts.yaml --compat tools/release_notes/compat/lts-1.18.yaml. Output files: dist/release-notes/runtime-1.18.1-lts.md and dist/release-notes/runtime-1.18.1-lts.json. Testing: adds golden tests for LTS markdown + JSON output, schema validation for known issues/compat inputs, and unit tests for categorization + gating rules. Follow-ups: (a) wire generator into the release runbook and CI workflow for release/* branches, (b) add an "Upgrade notes" curated section for Private-specific sequencing, (c) allow known issues to be filtered by deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) in JSON sidecar.
Adds LTS-specific release notes templates (Markdown + JSON sidecar)
Supports curated Highlights + per-entry summary overrides for enterprise-friendly notes
Renders Compatibility matrix (CUDA/driver + Private installer + Helm chart expectations)
Renders Known issues block with affected versions, symptoms, workarounds, and deployment modes
Enforces stricter validation for Security entries and schema validation for inputs

payload.body:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets observed recurring short-duration spike patterns that cause repeated cold allocations and transient SLO violations for small-to-medium tenants. Existing autoscaler reacts late and either overprovisions long tails or allows brief latency spikes. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) an anticipatory buffered autoscaler (ABA) that maintains a small, decaying warm buffer based on short-term workload forecasts and headroom signals, and (2) a utilization-reporting agent that aggregates per-tenant utilization into percentile buckets and sampled histograms to reduce cardinality while preserving signal quality.

Design summary: ABA runs as an autoscaler policy extension that watches the existing demand predictor (short-window EWMA + burst detector) and keeps a configurable buffer of N warm slots per-tenant class. Buffer sizing uses a probabilistic safety margin: buffer = ceil(P50_predicted_concurrency * alpha + min_fixed)) with decay half-life to release unused warm slots over a configurable window. The buffer is subject to a global safety cap and uses soft-decommit (graceful drain) so in-flight requests complete before returning capacity. The utilization-reporting agent samples per-device and per-tenant utilization at low frequency and reports aggregated percentiles (p50/p90/p95) and a small, fixed histogram (5 buckets) to the control plane. Aggregation keys are low-cardinality (region, tenant_class, slot_type) to avoid metrics explosion.

Implementation details: - New autoscaler plugin in autoscaler/plugin/buffered_autoscaler.go with a light state machine for buffered slots and decay timers. - Predictor hook points added to autoscaler/dispatcher so ABA can observe short-window forecasts without copying core logic. - Soft-decommit implemented as graceful-eviction in orchestrator/evict.go with a 30s default drain window and immediate preemption override for hard safety events. - Util-report agent implemented in telemetry/agent/util_reporter.go; uses local reservoir sampling and per-period aggregation; flushes to control plane via existing telemetry client with a new compact proto. - Feature flag: feature/aba_enabled (defaults to off). Cluster-wide knobs available in config/dedicated.yaml.

Config knobs (defaults): - aba_enabled: false - aba_per_tenant_min_buffer: 1 - aba_alpha: 0.25 - aba_decay_half_life_s: 300 - aba_global_cap_percent: 0.03 - aba_drain_window_s: 30 - util_report_period_s: 60 - util_sample_rate: 0.05

Test plan and results: Unit tests added for buffer math and decay (autoscaler/plugin/buffered_autoscaler_test.go), soft-decommit lifecycle, and telemetry aggregation. Integration tests in perf-canary simulate rapid 10s spikes and validate that ABA reduces cold allocations. In staging runs with a mix of 120 tenants: - Cold allocation events reduced by ~34% compared to baseline autoscaler. - 95th token-start latency for small tenants dropped from median 220ms -> 155ms on staging workload. - Median cluster idle capacity changed by +0.8% (within target). Telemetry bandwidth measured at +2.1% due to util_reporter; cardinality remained stable.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag. 2) Enable ABA in a single region (us-west-2) for test clusters for 48h. 3) Enable for a small tenant-class (non-critical). 4) Monitor eviction/cold-start and p95 latency. 5) Gradual ramp with canary to all dedicated clusters. If regressions observed: flip aba_enabled=false and let buffers decay, or reduce aba_alpha and aba_per_tenant_min_buffer.

Related: Linear ENG-4921 (anticipatory autoscaling investigation), ENG-5002 (reduce cold allocations for SMB tenants).

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration perf canary - [x] Feature-flagged roll out - [x] Observability dashboards updated

Upgrade notes: No DB migrations. Config defaults keep feature off. Operators should pre-seed config with aba_global_cap_percent if operating close to capacity.

Security: telemetry payload uses existing encrypted channel; payload size limited. No tenant secrets added.

Ops note: The util_reporter runs on control-plane-adjacent agents; it may add a small CPU percent to telemetry agent (~1-2%). This is configurable via util_sample_rate.
Adds a new anticipatory buffered autoscaler that keeps a small warm buffer for predicted short spikes and a low-cardinality utilization-reporting agent to improve tenant telemetry without inflating metrics cardinality. No customer-visible API changes; rollout controlled via feature flag.
Ava Chen: Please clarify global cap interaction with dedicated reservations. Are we allowed to exceed tenant reservations temporarily?
Jordan Park: Reply: ABA never exceeds tenant reservation limits; global cap is a safety layer to avoid cluster-wide warm buffers consuming more than X% of total capacity. Added explicit assertion and unit test.
Carlos Mendez: Code looks good, but the decay math seems aggressive for very bursty tenants. Can we expose half-life per-tenant class?
Jordan Park: Reply: Added aba_decay_half_life_s override per tenant_class and updated config docs. Kept default conservative (300s).
Riley Patel: CI flaked on telemetry proto generation; reran and passed. Please add a canary dashboard tile before merging.
Jordan Park: Reply: Added dashboard JSON and a short runbook for interpreting p50/p95 util signals.

Adds a tenant-level prefetch coalescer (Cost Sentinel) and a conservative quantization-tier selector with CLI tooling. Backwards-compatible; new feature gated behind feature flag 'cost_sentinel_v1'.
Context: Customers with mixed bursty and steady traffic were seeing suboptimal unit economics from 'eager' prefetch defaults and a single global quantization policy. This change introduces a cost-aware prefetch coalescer (Cost Sentinel) that builds a lightweight tenant prefetch catalog and a Quant Tier Optimizer that selects conservative quant profiles at rollout time. Motivation: reduce per-token cost on mid-size tenants while preserving latency SLOs and preventing quality regressions during quant rollouts. Key changes: 1) server/prefetch/cost_sentinel.py — new coalescer that synthesizes tenant prefetch catalogs from short-window request traces, implements an eviction heuristic (LRU by last-use + size score) and exposes a bounded catalog API; 2) service/econ/quant_selector.go — runtime policy to map tenant catalogs + workload shape to a quant tier (fp16 / int8-safe / int8-aggressive) with safety gates based on eval-set regressions and token loss thresholds; 3) cli/econ-inspect/main.go — developer CLI to inspect tenant prefetch catalog, simulate cost delta for candidate quant tiers, and produce a dry-run report; 4) docs/operator/prefetch.md — operational guidance on feature flagging, rollout windows, and recommended observation queries; 5) tests/e2e/prefetch_cost_test.py and unit tests for quant stability. Rollout plan: feature flag default off; enable on a small cohort (10 tenants) with shadow-prefetch mode for 48h, then canary with 1% traffic shift; automatic rollback if token-loss delta > 0.6% or latency P99 increases by >10ms. Related: closes ENG-3456 (prefetch defaults), references SUP-4123 (customer incident with cold-prefetch thrash).
Diego Morales (2024-11-06): Nice design. A couple of questions: 1) how do we bound memory usage of tenant catalogs when there are many low-volume tenants? 2) can the quant_selector depend on offline evals only, or do we allow lightweight online probes?
Author (Samira) (2024-11-06): Catalogs are bounded per-tenant (default 128 entries) and overall memory is protected by a global low-memory eviction path that compacts cold tenants every 5m (configurable). Quant selector supports both offline eval-set checks and an online 'probe' mode gated behind a tenant opt-in and the feature flag — added to docs.
Ava Chen (2024-11-08): Tests look good. Suggestion: make the default safety threshold more conservative (token-loss delta 0.6% -> 0.4%) for the initial canary. Also add an alert playbook entry for false-positive regressions.
Author (Samira) (2024-11-09): Lowered default to 0.4% and added alert playbook snippet to docs. Addressed minor nits in CLI help text.
Liam O'Connor (2024-11-11): CI flaked once due to lint rule; reran and green. Approving — please squash when merging.
