payload.body:
Motivation: large fleets pay a measurable tax for conservative cold-prefill and conservative quant choices. This change introduces the 'Econ Sparker' — a lightweight dynamic prefill controller plus a companion set of lightweight quantization profiles and telemetry hooks to reduce per-token cost while keeping latency SLOs intact. Design summary: a probe-driven, budget-aware prefill loop that samples a small number of requests (probe samples) to estimate effective warmup benefit, applies a compact micro-prefill when beneficial, and chooses a lightweight quant profile (int4-lite / 4-bit-perf) only for the prefilling execution path. The controller is latency-SLO-aware and will back off to full-safe prefill when p99 or cpu/gpu utilization signals are near configured thresholds. Implementation details: added serve/prefill/sparker.py which contains the probe scheduler, budget estimator, and a simple state machine; a new policy schema serve/prefill/policy_config.yaml to express microbudgets and SLO knobs; lightweight quant presets in serve/quant/light_profiles.json that are intentionally conservative and intended only for prefill passes; metrics in telemetry/prefill_metrics.md and instrumentation in runtime/telemetry/prefill_emitter.go. Safety and rollout: default state is opt-in; the console exposes a canary toggle and budget sliders; canary policy deployed to a small dedicated pool (canary:d-prefill-1). We included unit/integration tests and a perf smoke that gates obvious regressions. Expected impact: for chat-like workloads with prefix reuse we expect 6–18% reduction in token-unit cost on average for cold-cold flows and a negligible change in p95 latency when canaried correctly. Follow-ups: auto-tuning heuristics, richer confidence intervals for the probe estimator (ENG-1293), and a dashboard query bundle for the Console. Links: Linear ENG-1293, internal RFC: /docs/rfcs/econ-sparker.md. How to test locally: run tools/bench/prefill_smoke.py against local minimal runtime; toggle feature via console and observe telemetry.prefill.prefill_success_rate and telemetry.prefill.sampler_cost_estimate. Rollout notes: squash-merge, canary for two weeks, then evaluate cost-savings telemetry and expand.
Diego Ramos (reviewer): The probe sampling rate looks reasonable but can we expose a conservative lower bound so very spiky workloads never under-prefill? Requested: add max_probe_delay and a unit test that simulates bursty arrivals.
Author (Aisha): Added max_probe_delay with default 1200ms and unit test bursty_probe in tests/prefill/test_sparker.py — see commit 'probe: add max_probe_delay'.
Lina Patel (reviewer): Need clearer telemetry around fallback events (when we decide to bail to safe prefill). Please add an enumerated metric for fallback_reason and a label for current_quant_profile.
Author (Aisha): Added telemetry.prefill.fallback_reason and telemetry.prefill.quant_profile label; updated telemetry doc with sample queries.
Samir Chen (approver): Verified canary run for 72h on d-prefill-1, cost delta looks promising and p95 remained within 0.6% of baseline. Approving for merge after small lint fix (done).
CI Bot: perf-benchmark reported a minor p99 regression on small-roberta. We gated with a perf threshold and author added a config to run full prefill for that model as exception.
Release Manager: Please include release notes about opt-in nature and the canary toggle.
- Added Econ Sparker: opt-in dynamic prefill controller that reduces cold-prefill cost using probe-driven micro-prefills.
- Introduced conservative lightweight quant profiles used only during prefill paths.
- New telemetry: telemetry.prefill.* and dashboard bundle.
- Opt-in canary (deploy/canaries/prefill-canary.yaml); default off for all tenants.

Motivation: Customers building replication and replay systems asked for a deterministic way to capture/restore session state across restarts and to pre-warm credentials for short-lived tokens. This PR adds a lightweight SnapshotResolver abstraction (pluggable per-SDK) plus a 'staged' retry profile that aggressively fast-fails on transient auth errors while preserving a longer fallback profile for backend retries. The change spans py/ts/go SDKs and the redwood SDK bridge to keep cross-language ergonomics consistent.

What I changed (summary): - Introduced SnapshotResolver interface and reference implementations (memory + file-backed) in each SDK. - Added staged retry presets: fast-fail -> short backoff -> fallback policy. - Plumbed SnapshotResolver through session creation (optional param) so server-side mgrs can persist snapshots. - Improved generator/async iterator ergonomics in TS/Py: explicit close() and resume_from_snapshot() helpers. - Go: added typed iterator safety wrappers and idempotent resume helper. - Centralized small docstrings/README snippets to show cross-SDK examples. - Minor version bumps: py-sdk 1.9.0 -> 1.10.0, ts-sdk 2.4.3 -> 2.5.0, go-sdk v0.8.7 -> v0.9.0.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc and Linear linked (ENG-3092) - [x] Unit tests added for resolver behavior and retry composition - [x] End-to-end smoke test in benchmark-lab to validate resume semantics - [x] Updated SDK READMEs with examples - [x] Version bumps and changelogs updated

Notes: This is intended to be non-breaking for existing users: SnapshotResolver is optional and default behavior preserves current in-memory session semantics. The staged retry presets are additive; existing retry profiles remain available. For pinned customers we will coordinate the minor SDK bumps with the respective account owners.
Diego: Can you clarify why the file-backed implementation chooses JSON.gz instead of protobuf?
Amina: JSON.gz was chosen for readability during debug and to avoid adding proto deps to reference impl; we can provide a proto-backed example in a follow-up if needed.

Priya: TS API ergonomics look good, but the close()/resume_from_snapshot() names feel ad-hoc vs existing Stream.close() naming. Could we align names?
Amina: Renamed stream.close() -> closeStream() in the TS helper and added deprecation note for the alias to keep ergonomics consistent.

Ethan: Tests flaked on CI (py flaky test_snapshot_resolver_timeout).
Amina: Root cause was a timing assumption; switched to a deterministic fake clock in tests and added a retry window. Reran CI and tests passed.

Diego: Approval pending small docs nit about error codes returned by staged retry.
Amina: Addressed - clarified mapping and added example table in docs. Diego approved on 2026-02-22. Priya approved on 2026-02-22. Ethan approved after rerun on 2026-02-23.

payload.body:
Background and motivation: We continue to see production incidents where SSE consumers receive concatenated delimiter bytes or truncated JSON payloads when chunk boundaries split multi-byte UTF-8 sequences or when upstream buffering coalesces multiple events. Previous fixes addressed ordering heuristics and heartbeat coalescing, but we observed a replay class of failures in which the final bytes of a span contain delimiter-like sequences that later get interpreted as event separators after network reassembly, causing partial-JSON errors and downstream tool-calling misfires.

This PR introduces two coordinated, low-risk mitigations: 1) an escaper applied at the span tail that encodes any trailing bytes which could be mistaken for event delimiters ("span-tail-escaper"); and 2) a compact, human-readable resynchronization marker emitted opportunistically when the server detects a boundary anomaly during reassembly ("[[RSYNC:<hex>] ]"). The resync marker is designed to be easy for clients to detect and ignore, and it helps clients recover without requiring a full connection reset. Both changes are backward compatible and guarded by an opt-in Accept header so we can cut over incrementally.

What this changes (high level):
- Implemented span-tail-escaper in the streaming encoder to escape sequences that match the SSE delimiter pattern at the end of an emitted span. The encoder chooses a 1-3 byte escape prefix that is unlikely to appear in normal payloads.
- Inserted lightweight resync marker on the next flush when a boundary checksum mismatch is detected in the reassembly window. The marker uses ASCII-friendly delimiters so legacy clients simply ignore it.
- Added server-side heuristics to only emit markers when a tolerance threshold (configurable in runtime flags) is exceeded to avoid noise.
- Client-side parser additions: a permissive resync-marker skip path and a small escape-unwrapping step in the final reassembly phase. Parser changes are guarded by Accept: application/x-rw-sse-resume.
- Added unit tests (encoding/decoding), integration streaming tests simulating TCP reassembly, and an e2e test with the OpenAI-compat layer validating function-call JSON remains intact across chunk splits.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implement span-tail-escaper in runtime encoder.
- [x] Add resync marker emission and threshold knobs.
- [x] Add decoding path for clients behind Accept header.
- [x] Add unit and integration tests.
- [x] Run perf microbenchmarks to ensure <2% P99 encoding latency regression.
- [x] Coordinate rollout plan with SDK teams (Python/TS) for Accept header opt-in.

Commits (summary):
- 3a2f7b1: add span-tail-escaper utility and encoder hook (runtime/streaming/encoder.rs)
- 8d11c5f: emit resync marker when reassembly checksum mismatch detected (runtime/streaming/reassembler.rs)
- 4b0e2d3: add Accept header gating and feature flag (api/gateway/compat.rs)
- ec7a9f0: client parser relax: ignore RSYNC markers and unescape tails (sdk/js/sse-parser.ts, sdk/py/streaming.py)
- b59f4d2: integration tests for reassembly scenarios and function-call preservation (tests/streaming/reassembly_integration_test.go)
- f0c3a11: docs and migration notes (docs/platform/sse.md)

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/streaming/encoder.rs: new escaper plus unit tests
- runtime/streaming/reassembler.rs: marker emission logic, window checksum, and counters
- api/gateway/compat.rs: Accept header parsing, backward compatibility gating
- sdk/js/sse-parser.ts: skip RSYNC markers and unescape tails behind opt-in
- sdk/py/streaming.py: symmetric changes for Python SDK
- tests/streaming/reassembly_integration_test.go: new test harness for simulated TCP splits
- docs/platform/sse.md: migration and runtime flag docs
- ci/presubmit/streaming.yml: added reassembly integration job to presubmit
- charts/templates/configmap.yaml: new runtime flags for resync threshholds

Review conversation (highlights):
- Diego Alvarez (review): "Nice, this addresses a class of production issues we've chased during incident INC-1128. Two requests: 1) add an opt-out metric so we can measure marker emission rate across customers; 2) please double-check UTF-8 edge cases for 4-byte sequences at span boundaries."
- Author (Maya): "Added emission counter metric runtime.sse.resync_emitted (prometheus) and extended tests to include 4-byte UTF-8 emoji edge case. PTAL."
- Priya Nair (review): "Client changes look fine but we should avoid any parse-time allocations in the hot path. Can we keep the unescape operation allocation-free when possible?"
- Author (Maya): "Reworked JS parser to do in-place unwrapping for ArrayBuffer-backed chunks; Python path uses memoryview to avoid copies. Benchmarks attached to the PR show negligible allocation impact."
- Evan Cho (approval): "Approach looks safe and incremental. I approve after Diego's metric request is included."

CI / checks: 
- presubmit/unit: pass
- presubmit/integration: fail (flake in unrelated test), rerun -> pass
- presubmit/lint: pass (minor formatting fixed in follow-up commit)
- presubmit/perf: pass (encoding P99 +1.3% at default span size)

Rollout plan and compatibility: 
- Gate server encoder behavior behind runtime flag streaming.resync.enable (false by default).
- Gate client parsing behind Accept: application/x-rw-sse-resume; SDK teams will add this header to the default streaming client in the next minor release after server flag flip.
- Start with internal canary for 10% traffic for two days, observe runtime.sse.resync_emitted and client-side recovery metrics, then expand to 50% and finally 100% for customers with opt-in header.

Follow-ups: 
- Add telemetry to map resync markers to connection metadata (region, model, route) to root cause frequent emitters.
- Explore a shorter binary escape variant to reduce bandwidth for very small spans.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals. Backfilled a short changelog entry and added the new runtime flags to Helm chart values.

References: issue INC-1128, linear ENG-2104, previous PRs addressing SSE coalescing and delimiter heuristics.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: Customers integrating streamed tool/function outputs reported two recurring failure modes: 1) opaque stream failures with inconsistent retry guidance, and 2) difficulty reconciling idempotency across multiplexed HTTP/2 and SSE sessions. This made it hard for language agents to reliably retry or resume work without risking duplicate tool-effects. Goal: provide a small surface that (a) gives clients a stable, machine-readable error envelope at stream end-frames, (b) surfaces a lightweight session-level idempotency artifact that survives reconnects (Idempotency-Cookie), and (c) map legacy OpenAI-style HTTP errors into the same envelope so the OpenAI shim gets predictable semantics.

What this PR does (high level): Introduces an "Idempotency-Cookie" header and server-side cookie token emitted on stream start; implements a normalized error envelope emitted as a final control frame (type: "error_envelope") for all stream terminations that are not clean 200/OK end-of-streams; extends the OpenAI compatibility adapter to translate 4xx/5xx responses into the same envelope; and adds conservative retry/reconnect hooks in the router to prefer session-resume when the Idempotency-Cookie is present. The change intentionally keeps ephemeral tokens opaque to clients — they can send back the cookie on reconnect but cannot parse its internals.

Compatibility and contract: The error envelope is a JSON object with fields: code (string), message (string), retry_after (milliseconds or null), scope (string: 'session'|'request'), and hint (optional string). For streaming transports that don't support explicit end frames, the adapter will send a final chunk prefixed with "__RW_ERR__" followed by the envelope JSON to preserve compatibility. Existing clients that ignore the envelope will see a normal stream close; well-behaved clients should parse the envelope and act on retry_after and scope.

Key implementation notes: - Added server/streaming/idempotency_cookie.go: generates short-lived opaque tokens, stores mapping in in-memory session store with optional Redis backing controlled by configuration. - Added server/streaming/error_envelope.go: canonical error envelope builder and serializer, plus streaming-framing helper for transports (SSE, chunked, HTTP/2). - Router changes (server/router/streaming_router.go): on transient failures, if Idempotency-Cookie present and session state compatible, respond with 409 + envelope with scope=session and retry_after hint; if not present, return 429/503 mapping depending on upstream hint. - OpenAI adapter updates (openai/adapter/stream_shim.go): translate legacy Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* headers into retry_after in envelope; map model-specific transient codes into canonical codes ("rate_limit", "server_unavailable", "kv_cache_miss"). - SDK updates: added lightweight parser helpers in redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript to extract Idempotency-Cookie and envelope when present.

Testing and validation: Added unit tests for envelope serialization and parsing (tests/streaming/error_envelope_test.go), integration tests that simulate reconnect/resume flows against a fake backend (tests/streaming/idempotency_cookie_integration_test.go), and end-to-end smoke tests against the OpenAI shim to ensure header->envelope mapping. CI: lint, unit, integration, and canary benchting were run. Observability: new metrics: streaming.error_envelope.emitted, streaming.idempotency_resume.success, streaming.idempotency_resume.conflict.

Rollback and feature toggles: Feature guarded behind config flag `features.streaming_idempotency_cookie` (off by default for on-prem until Redis session-backed store is enabled). Backwards compatibility: default behavior for clients remains unchanged (streams close as before); envelope is additive. Operators can opt-out by disabling the feature flag.

Checklist: - [x] Implemented token generator + in-memory store with Redis option - [x] Implemented envelope framing for SSE/HTTP chunked/H2 - [x] Adapter mappings for OpenAI shim - [x] Tests: unit + integration + e2e smoke - [x] Docs: added docs/api/streaming-error-envelope.md and examples in quickstarts - [x] Benchmarked overhead (0.4% median p99 token latency increase under synthetic load) - [x] Security review pass (cookie is opaque, signed, short TTL)

Release notes: Adds Idempotency-Cookie header for session resume and a normalized streaming error envelope that provides retry_after and canonical error codes. Default behavior unchanged for clients that do not parse the envelope. See docs/api/streaming-error-envelope.md for migration guidance.
Liam O'Connor: Can we avoid storing full session state in memory for hosted tier? Suggest pluggable Redis and bounded LRU fallback.
Maya Patel: Implemented pluggable store with Redis-backed config and an in-memory LRU fallback; documented TTL and eviction behaviour.
Ruth Chen: The 409 vs 429 semantics were unclear. Recommend explicit mapping in the router.
Maya Patel: Clarified router logic: 409 used when resume conflict detected with existing session, 429 used for rate limit with retry_after present, 503 for backend transient failures. Added tests.
Diego Alvarez: Need to ensure OpenAI shim mapping doesn't expose internal error codes. Suggest whitelist.
Maya Patel: Added canonical code whitelist and mapping table; shim emits only canonical codes and a human hint.
Liam O'Connor: Approve after minor comment about metric naming
Ruth Chen: Approve
Adds an opaque Idempotency-Cookie for stream session resumption and a normalized streaming error envelope (code, message, retry_after, scope). OpenAI adapter maps legacy headers into the envelope. Feature is behind a config flag for gradual rollout.
payload.title: Introduce Idempotency-Cookie and normalized error envelope for graceful stream fallbacks

payload.body:
Motivation: customers using response_format="schema" together with the OpenAI compatibility layer reported confusing errors during streaming responses and tool calls; some errors were opaque (generic 500-style messages) and made retry/rollback logic brittle. This PR introduces a clearer error taxonomy and small behavioral changes so clients can make deterministic decisions in strict vs permissive modes. Summary of changes: 1) Define a concise error taxonomy returned in the inference response envelope when response_format="schema" is used (keys: structure.mismatch, schema.partial, stream.truncation, toolcall.fenced, compat.narrowing). 2) When running in openai_compat mode we map legacy error shapes (old openai-like error.body) to the new taxonomy and include a compat_hint header for clients migrating from the OpenAI shape. 3) Streaming path: introduced a finalization signal ("schema_finalized": true/false) in the non-streaming envelope and a stream footer event in streaming mode that gives a deterministic schema validation result; this avoids ambiguous client-side timeouts deciding whether to attempt a resume. 4) Tool/function-calling: we add an explicit fence error (toolcall.fenced) when the model returns a tool invocation that violates the declared tool contract (missing required fields or wrong return type) and include a recommended action (retry_with_prompt_fix / abort) to help orchestration layers. 5) Backwards compatibility: default behavior in permissive mode remains unchanged; strict mode flips on both runtime enforcement and the new error codes.

Checklist: - [x] Define error code strings and schema for envelope (docs + enum). - [x] Implement mapping layer in openai adapter. - [x] Add stream footer event and resume hint implementation. - [x] Add tests for strict/permissive behavior and toolcall fencing. - [x] Update SDK error docs and quickstart example.

Design notes: - Error envelope lives at inference response top-level under "schema_validation" and carries: code, message, details (array of short strings), and hint (retry, abort, fallback-model). To keep JSON response small during streaming we emit a compact footer event: {event: "schema_result", code:..., hint:...}. - For OpenAI compatibility we continue to accept legacy error responses but always emit a compat_hint header that includes the new code equivalent. This avoids client breakages while nudging teams to adopt the richer codes.

Migration guide: clients should prefer the new codes when present. For streaming clients, wait for the final footer event before marking schema check success/failure; if the connection drops before the footer is received, the client may reconnect using the provided resume_token (if present) or fall back to the permissive path.

Security and performance considerations: schema validation runs in a lightweight sandbox and is guarded by a short-circuiting fast-path (prefix checks) to avoid full validation on common OK responses. The added validation accounts for ~2% median CPU increase on our canary but reduces downstream error churn.

Risks: clients that depended on parsing human-readable error messages in the past will need to migrate to the structured codes; the PR includes a compat mapping to reduce disruption.
Jordan Patel: Please clarify how stream.truncation differs from partial schema failures. In particular, when clients reconnect do they need to re-run validation from scratch?
Maya Chen (author): stream.truncation is reserved for when the streaming connection closed without a footer event. We include a resume_token; reconnecting with the token jumps to validation continuation so clients do not need to re-run from scratch in most cases.
Lena Sørensen: Can we avoid extra latency in the hot path? The perf numbers look OK but please add a percentile breakdown and a stress test for long sequences.

Motivation: teams increasingly want a low-risk sandbox to evaluate tenant-level unit economics changes (batching, cache defaults, and aggressive quantization) before applying them to production. This PR introduces a lightweight "Cost Lab" runner service plus an experimental Quant Safeguard Advisor designed to run isolated what-if experiments, score end-to-end token/unit cost impacts, and produce safe fallback-presets. High-level summary: add a new microservice (cmd/cost-lab-runner) that orchestrates tenant-specific synthetic workloads, a simulator library (pkg/econ/simulator) that replays request traces with configurable batching and cache policies, and a quant sensitivity probe (pkg/quant/safeguard) that performs operator-level pruning experiments and synthesizes robust quantization ladders constrained by latency SLOs and fallthrough quality thresholds. The PR also exposes a small CLI (tools/costlab-cli) for offline dry-runs and a console toggle (web/console/src/components/CostLabToggle.tsx) to seed canary experiments. Key behavior: experiments run against a sandboxed runtime instance with prefix/KV caching disabled by default; the runner supports multi-tenant trace slices, deterministic random seeds for repeatability, and automated scoring metrics (token-cost delta, P95 latency delta, model-quality proxy using saved prompt/eval pairs). Safety & rollout: generated presets are annotated with confidence scores and suggested rollout policies (canary fraction, warmup duration). The advisor will never auto-apply presets; it emits a diffs-as-code artifact that can be reviewed and applied by operators. Implementation notes: most of the heavy work is encapsulated in pkg/econ/simulator and pkg/quant/safeguard so the change surface for the serving runtime is minimal (a small agent hook at internal/runtime/experiment_agent.go to shadow traffic). Telemetry: new metrics and tags added under telemetry.econ.* and telemetry.quant.*; we included sample Grafana dashboard JSON under observability/dashboards/cost-lab.json. Testing: unit tests for simulator determinism and quant probe stability included (pkg/econ/simulator/sim_test.go, pkg/quant/safeguard/safeguard_test.go). An e2e smoke harness (tests/e2e/costlab_smoke.sh) runs in CI. Performance: microbenchmarks show the simulation harness runs 6-8x faster than a naive replayer due to batched trace replay and compiled kernel selection toggles; we include a perf-run report in docs/perf/costlab_run_2026-01.pdf. Backwards compatibility: all defaults are conservative; no changes to user-facing inference defaults without opt-in. Followups: integrate the advisor with Optimize to propose one-click preset migrations and add a model-quality regression detector for high-risk quant ladders. Why different from previous work: this change packages simulation + quant pruning into a discoverable, sandbox-first developer flow (Cost Lab) rather than a purely autosuggesting default generator. It is intended for advanced SRE/ML-ops experimentation workflows.
Liam O'Connor: Overall design looks solid. Two requests: (1) ensure experiment_agent cannot leak tensors to prod caches, (2) add a CLI flag to force deterministic seed. Reply (Maya): both addressed in latest commits; agent sanitizes all KV writes and seed flag added.
Priya Patel: Can you add a short section to the runbook describing how to validate model-quality proxies? Reply (Maya): added 'validating-proxies' section in docs/runbooks/cost-lab-runbook.md.
Diego Marquez: Suggest adding a fallback policy when quant ladder leads to >5% P95 regression. Reply (Maya): added confidence score and a suggested 'auto-fallback' policy in the diff artifact; it remains opt-in for operators.

Context and motivation: CI runtime and noisy dependency churn have been adding 20–30% latency to developer feedback in the monorepo. This PR compacts the CI surface to prioritize fast feedback for common edit paths, extracts a small dep-curation tool to reduce transitive upgrade noise, and adds minimal observability hooks for CI performance. Commits summary: 3 commits — 1) refactor(ci): split lint+unit into fast-lint & slow-lint lanes and introduce fast-test profile; 2) feat(deps): add tools/dep-curator with heuristic-suggest and lockfile-diff commands; 3) chore(ci): add lightweight metrics emitter for job duration and cache hit rates. Changed areas (high level): ".github/workflows/ci-fast.yml" (new fast pipeline), ".github/workflows/ci-slow.yml" (trimmed slow matrix), "tools/dep-curator/curator.py" (new; Python 3.11, small heuristic engine), "scripts/fast-lint.sh" (wrapper that lints changed files only), "pkg/build/cache-keys.go" (compact cache key logic), "docs/ci-observability.md" (how to read CI metrics), minor updates to "redwood/Makefile" and several package.json devDependency pin bumps. Example change snippet: tools/dep-curator now exposes "curator suggest --pr=1234" which outputs a short list of suspect transitive upgrades and a recommended pin list. Review conversation: Elena: "Nice separation — will fast-lint cover staged files only?" Author reply: "fast-lint uses git diff against main by default; added an option to pass a file list for CI containers." Samir: "Can the dep-curator be run as a bot on PR open?" Author: "Yes, added a follow-up Linear task ENG-3499 to wire the GitHub action; curator exposes machine-friendly JSON output." Ravi (security review): "Ensure dep-curator does not execute package scripts during analysis." Author: "Tool uses safe parsing only; documented in README and sandboxed in CI run." Requested changes: adjust cache key to include node-modules metadata hash (addressed in cache-keys.go), add unit tests for curator heuristics (added). Approvals: Elena approved on 2026-02-21, Samir approved on 2026-02-22. CI summary: initial run — fast pipeline green, slow matrix had a flaky integration test (redis-session) which was quarantined and rerun; all checks passing after rerun. Checks: lint (pass), unit (pass), integration (pass after rerun), build (pass), dep-scan (pass). Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2026-02-22; commit message consolidates the above. Migration/ops notes: Ops should watch the new CI metrics dashboard for first 48 hours; added alert docs in docs/ci-observability.md. Follow-ups: wire dep-curator to a lightweight PR bot (ENG-3499), iterate cache-key entropy reduction if cache hit rates drop below 70% in 2 weeks.
Improves CI feedback loop by splitting fast/slow test lanes, introduces dependency curation helper for PRs, and adds lightweight CI observability; no breaking changes

Motivation: Customers with strict regulatory boundaries repeatedly request a) curated RBACv2 policy presets for common compliance postures (SOC2, GDPR data-local operators, restricted-operator), b) a stable plugin surface for KMS provider integrations (so private deployments can add internal HSM/KMS implementations without forking core), and c) better audit telemetry that reduces PII exposure while keeping forensic fidelity. This PR implements three coordinated changes: 1) policy-presets: a set of validated, parameterizable RBACv2 policy templates and a small CLI to materialize them for tenant bootstrapping; 2) kms-plugin: a lightweight provider interface and shim layer with two example adapters (aws-kms-compatible shim for Hosted tests, and a local hsm-mock used by our private-installer tests); 3) audit-sampling: adaptive audit sampling and content redaction rules driven by policy labels and risk tiers so we can sample full payloads only for sensitive operator actions and otherwise store compact event signatures.

Scope and user-visible behavior: The API, runtime, and console behavior is unchanged by default. Admins can opt into the presets via the new admin CLI (bin/rbac-presets apply --preset=restricted-operator --tenant=acme). The KMS plugin is an opt-in dependency for Private install and Dedicated operator-hosted deployments: a new extension point (plugins/kms/v1) accepts a go plugin or a containerized adapter (see docs/integrations/kms/README.md). Audit sampling is controlled by the new policy annotation audit.sampling: {mode: adaptive|always|none, sample_rate: 0.01}.

Design highlights: - Policy-presets are authored as parameterized YAML with constraints validated against the policy-compiler; templates live in policy/presets/*.yaml and include tests under policy/presets/testdata. - KMS plugin surface defines three operations (Wrap, Unwrap, Sign) and a minimal config schema; the runtime loads adapters at startup when configured and falls back to default internal KMS for hosted. - Adaptive audit-sampling computes event risk score using operator role, resource sensitivity label, and KMS provider confidence; high-risk events are stored with full payloads, low-risk events use deterministic hashes and compact metadata.

Backward compatibility and migration: Existing tenants see no change unless admins apply presets or configure a plugin. The policy-compiler validates imported presets and will reject incompatible templates; a migration helper (bin/rbac-presets lint --in=old-policy.yaml) is provided. The KMS plugin uses a strict versioned interface; older adapters must implement a compatibility shim.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests added for policy compilation, plugin loader, and audit sampler. End-to-end smoke tests added to redwood-private-installer CI (integration/kms/e2e). We ran a canary rollout to Dedicated where audit sampling was enabled for 10% of operator actions for two weeks; no regressions observed.

Checklist: - [x] Policy templates with tests - [x] CLI helper and linting - [x] KMS plugin interface + two adapters (aws-test shim, hsm-mock) - [x] Audit sampler + redaction rules - [x] Documentation updates (docs/integrations/kms/ and docs/operator/rbac-presets.md) - [x] E2E integration tests for private-installer

Related: ENG-2319 implements the admin UX follow-up; SUP-4421 captured a customer incident that motivated adaptive sampling. For discussion and design rationale see internal doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2319/rbac-presets-and-kms-plugin (internal).
Diego Torres (reviewer): Please add a migration note for tenants with custom role templates; their role IDs may collide with preset names.
Author (Aisha Malik): Added lint step and explicit name-spacing to templates to avoid collisions; updated description.
Maya Chen (reviewer): The plugin loader looks fine, but we should fail fast on version mismatch rather than falling back silently.
Author: Loader now validates semantic version and returns a startup error if configured plugin is incompatible. Added unit test.
Omar Rahman (security reviewer): Audit redaction looks good but add a short-term override to force full capture for incident investigations.
Author: Added admin API endpoint: POST /admin/audit/override with TTL; documented in docs/operator/rbac-presets.md.
Maya Chen: Approved overall after requested changes.
Diego Torres: Approved.
Omar Rahman: Approved with comment on monitoring (see release notes).
Add policy-presets for quick tenant bootstrapping, a pluggable KMS provider interface with example adapters, and adaptive audit-sampling with configurable redaction policies. Opt-in features for Private/Dedicated. Admin CLI and migration helpers included.

payload.body:
Summary: Integrates fleet/runtime capacity signals into the routing service to drive tier-aware admission control. Under pressure, we preserve enterprise route budgets by gating best-effort traffic first (throttle/queue/deny depending on configured policy). This is the core routing-side change for Hot-route capacity protection (ENG-4924).

Context: We’ve seen fleet-wide tail latency cascades when one or two high-traffic routes (often best-effort/self-serve) push shared pools into high queue depth, causing p99 latency and 5xx across unrelated enterprise workloads. The gateway limiter (ENG-4922) helps, but we need routing to react to real-time capacity and make tier-aware decisions consistently across regions/pools.

What’s in this PR:
- New capacity signal client in routing (fleet-signal service + runtime aggregate metrics): pulls a low-cardinality “pool pressure” snapshot per (region, model-family, pool) and caches it (default TTL 250ms, bounded jitter).
- Admission control policy evaluation in routing request path:
  - Computes an AdmissionDecision = {allow, allow_degraded, queue, deny} with tier attribution (enterprise vs best-effort) and route_group attribution.
  - Applies “gate best-effort first” rules when pool pressure crosses thresholds: best-effort is denied/queued before enterprise is impacted.
  - Enterprise behavior is budget-based: enterprise requests are admitted until an explicit per-route_group budget is exhausted (budget source is policy engine route budgets; this PR only consumes policy output).
- Deterministic decision logging (structured, sampled): emits a stable decision record including inputs (pressure level, tier, route_group, model-family) and the policy version hash. Intended for auditability during enterprise escalations.
- Backpressure integration: when AdmissionDecision=queue, routing returns a retryable response to gateway with explicit backoff hints (no new customer-facing schema changes in this PR; gateway controls final 429 semantics).
- Feature flags + rollout guardrails:
  - routing.admission_control.enabled (default off)
  - routing.admission_control.allowlist_accounts (empty)
  - routing.admission_control.regions (empty)
  - Safe fallback: if signals are stale/unavailable, routing uses “no-signal” mode (allows traffic) but emits a metric for signal gaps.
- Metrics (low cardinality):
  - routing_admission_decisions_total{decision,tier,route_group,region}
  - routing_capacity_snapshot_age_ms{region,pool}
  - routing_capacity_signal_errors_total{region,source}
  - routing_best_effort_denied_ratio{route_group,region}

Not in scope / follow-ups:
- Gateway 429 reason codes & headers live in ENG-4922 / pr-27441.
- Runtime metrics export lives in ENG-4925 / pr-27435.
- Policy schema changes for budgets/priority classes live in ENG-4923 / pr-27418.
- Global fairness changes (scheduler rewrite) explicitly out of scope.

Implementation notes:
- Signal sources: primary is fleet-signal aggregator (preferred), secondary fallback is runtime aggregate endpoint when aggregator is degraded.
- Pressure model: we treat pressure as a normalized scalar [0..1] computed by fleet-signal service; routing uses configured cutoffs:
  - pressure >= 0.75 => start gating best-effort (queue then deny)
  - pressure >= 0.90 => deny best-effort immediately; enterprise remains allow until budget exhaustion
  - pressure >= 0.97 => allow_degraded for enterprise only if policy permits (routing returns ‘degraded’ marker to downstream; no automatic model fallback in this PR)
- Performance: policy evaluation + signal lookup is designed to add <200µs p50 overhead on routing nodes. Signal cache is in-memory, lock-free read path.

Testing:
- Unit tests: pressure threshold behavior, stale signal handling, decision determinism, allowlist/flag behavior.
- Integration tests (local): routing <-> fleet-signal mock; verifies decision metrics and logs.
- Load test (staging): burst traffic on /v1/chat/completions with best-effort accounts; confirmed enterprise latency preserved while best-effort gets queued/denied.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge with flags off.
2) Enable in us-east for allowlisted enterprise accounts + synthetic best-effort load (game day).
3) Expand allowlist, then regions, then remove allowlist once SRE signs off on dashboards/alerts.

Risk assessment:
- Main risk is incorrect gating due to bad signals or unexpected staleness. Mitigations: TTL bounds, signal-gap metrics, and safe allow fallback when signals are missing (no hard deny without a current snapshot).

Links:
- Linear: ENG-4924
- Related PRs: pr-27435 (runtime metrics), pr-27418 (policy budgets), pr-27411 (gateway tier limiter)
- Incident reference: 2025-11-03 Sev1 fleetwide latency cascade (postmortem linked in Confluence)

Screenshots / dashboards: None included here (dashboards are in observability-pack PR).
Mina Haddad (review): The overall flow looks right. Two questions: (1) how do we ensure we never deny enterprise due to missing signals, and (2) can we avoid tagging metrics by model id (cardinality)?
Elena Popov (author): (1) In no-signal mode we force decision=allow and emit routing_capacity_signal_errors_total; deny paths require a fresh snapshot. (2) Metrics here use model-family + pool only; no model id tag. I’ll add an explicit assertion in the metric helper to prevent model ids.
Peter Holtz (review): For queue vs deny: returning a retryable response to gateway is fine, but please ensure we don’t accidentally “queue” for streaming requests forever. Can we cap queue duration / add a max retry hint?
Elena Popov (author): Good call. Added max_backoff_ms=2000 and a header for gateway to translate into Retry-After / jitter. Also added test for streaming routes to default to deny when pressure>=0.90 (avoids indefinite queueing).
Vanessa Ortiz (review): On the signal client: please add circuit breaker when fleet-signal service starts timing out so routing doesn’t amplify overload. Also please use bounded jitter on refresh to avoid herd behavior.
Elena Popov (author): Implemented per-region circuit breaker (opens after 10 consecutive timeouts; half-open after 5s) and added +/-50ms jitter to refresh scheduling.
Logan Wright (review): Decision logging: ensure the policy hash and route_group are included, but avoid customer_id in logs by default. If needed, sample + restricted path only.
Elena Popov (author): Updated logger to omit customer_id and request_id by default. Added optional debug logging behind routing.admission_control.debug_logging (off) and documented it as restricted/on-call use only.
Mina Haddad (approval): Looks good. Please follow up with SRE to confirm dashboard panels match the new metric names; otherwise OK to merge.
Robert King (approval): Approved. Thanks for keeping cache read path lock-free; perf looks fine.

Summary: Adds a small CI-side telemetry proxy and a 'smallfoot' dependency reshaper that rewrites devcontainer/CI dependency sets to remove unnecessary transitive dev deps. This reduces presubmit flakiness, lowers container image sizes for runners, and centralizes CI telemetry sampling so we can measure presubmit latency and cache hit rates without spamming production observability.
Added a lightweight CI telemetry proxy to centralize and reduce noise for premerge runs; introduced a dependency reshaper that trims dev/test-only transitive deps for faster CI start and smaller images. No user-facing API changes.
Arjun Patel (reviewer): Nice approach to centralizing telemetry. A few nits: 1) Can we limit the proxy sampling rate to 1% by default to avoid initial noise? 2) Add a circuit-breaker so if the proxy fails we don't block presubmit runs.
Maya Chen (author): Added sample_rate config with default 0.01 and a local fallback mode. Implemented a simple in-memory circuit breaker that switches to passthrough after 3 consecutive failures; documented behavior in infra/ci/telemetry-proxy/README.md.
Lena Müller (reviewer): smallfoot heuristics look promising. Request: add a quick benchmark showing cold-start time before/after reshaper on a representative fastpath image. Also ensure we don't prune deps listed explicitly in workspace manifests.

payload.body:
Motivation: We observed recurring incidents where aggressive regional failover would trigger a cascade: requests were routed to fallback model variants before the in-flight KV cache was drained, causing higher tail-latency and quality regressions. The symptoms included repeated circuit flips and tenant-level SLO breaches during regional egress throttles. This PR implements two complementary mitigations: (1) an "opaque fallback bridge" that intercepts candidate fallback routing decisions and applies a short-lived, topology-aware holdoff while allowing in-flight KV drains to complete; (2) an early KV-drain heuristic that biases drain ordering and batch size to reduce tail amplification when a region is about to hand off traffic. The design aims to reduce oscillation between fallback targets and lower 99th-percentile latency spikes without adding significant routing latency during steady-state.

Summary of changes: single continuous description string covering functional changes, testing, rollout, and rollback. Key changes include:
- runtime/fallback/opaque_bridge.rs: new module that evaluates fallback candidates and adds a small, per-tenant opaque holdoff window (configurable). The bridge keeps fallback decisions idempotent so repeat opens don't cause duplicate model handoffs.
- runtime/kv_cache/drain_scheduler.rs: early-drain heuristic added; batches inflight KV flushes with priority for requests belonging to soon-to-be-rerouted tenants.
- controlplane/policies/surge_governor.rs & controlplane/config/defaults.yaml: new governor knobs: governor.window_ms (defaults to 300ms), quarantine.batch_size (defaults to 16), max_quarantine_duration_ms.
- observability/metrics/registry.yaml: added metrics fallback_decision{outcome}, kv_drain_latency_ms, kv_drain_batch_size.
- tests/integration/fallback_quarantine_test.rs: synthetic region-failure harness that asserts no repeated reopens and that 99p latency regression is < 15% under the test load.
- docs/operational/kv-drain-and-fallback.md: runbook for on-call, rollout steps, and emergency rollback.

Testing and benchmarks: Unit tests added for bridge predicate logic and drain ordering. Integration canary executed via scripts/canary_run.sh across two regions simulated in CI (local cluster). Benchmarks on a small internal cluster (g4-equivalent) show the following: steady-state P50/P95 latency unchanged (+/-1%), P99 reduced from 640ms to 420ms for the synthetic failover scenario; the number of cross-region re-routes per minute dropped ~42% in stress tests. Memory and CPU overhead measured as <2% on the pilot footprint.

Operational notes / rollout plan: This was deployed as a hotfix to Dedicated pilot tenants first. Rollout strategy:
1) feature-flagged rollout to 10% of traffic in pilot region for 24h
2) monitor metrics: fallback_decision{outcome=held,executed}, kv_drain_latency_ms, tenant_slo_error_rate
3) if no regressions and P99 improves, ramp to 100% of pilot region then gradually to all regions over 3 days

Emergency rollback: flip feature flag off and trigger immediate drain cancellation path (controlplane/cancel_drain) which will re-enable previous fallback behavior. docs/operational/kv-drain-and-fallback.md contains the exact commands and playbook for on-call.

Review summary & discussion: Reviewer Marcus Nguyen requested tightening the default governor.window_ms from 500ms to 300ms (accepted) because experiments showed lower holdoffs reduced visible failover blur without reintroducing oscillation. Elena asked for explicit metrics to detect opaque bridge being a bottleneck; added fallback_decision timing and unit tests around it. Tomoko ran canary and reported an intermittent race in the drain_scheduler; fixed by adding a per-batch mutex and added more integration assertions.

CI: all unit and integration tests passed in CI. Lint and fmt checks passed. Canary runs completed successfully post-merge in staging.

Related work: addresses Linear tickets ENG-4521 (regional failover oscillation) and ENG-4598 (KV cache handoff tail latency). Also referenced SUP-1287 where customer incident traces motivated prioritizing KV drain ordering.

Merge: merged via squash on 2026-02-25 after approvals from reviewers and green CI. Release notes: "Hotfix: improve regional failover stability by introducing opaque fallback bridge and early KV-drain biasing; reduces P99 latency spikes during failover scenarios." No API breaking changes. Breaking_change: false.
Marcus Nguyen: Can we reduce the default holdoff from 500ms? Experiments show 300ms keeps benefit while lowering visible blurring. (requested change)
Aisha Patel: Updated governor.default in defaults.yaml to 300ms and added a comment with rationale. PTAL. (author)
Elena Rodriguez: Add a metric to ensure the opaque bridge doesn't become a new hot path. (requested change)
Aisha Patel: Added fallback_decision_timing metric and unit test coverage. (author)
Tomoko Saito: Canary reveals a rare race in the drain scheduler when batch_size==1. Please add a mutex around batch commits. (requested change)
Aisha Patel: Mutex added and integration test extended to cover single-batch drains. Re-ran canary. (author)
Marcus Nguyen: Approving — changes look good and canary is stable. (approved)
Elena Rodriguez: Approved. (approved)
Tomoko Saito: Approved after canary pass. (approved)
Hotfix: improved regional failover stability through an opaque fallback bridge and prioritized KV drain ordering. Reduces 99th percentile latency spikes during failover scenarios. No breaking changes.

Context: recent audits highlighted gaps in operator-level telemetry for cryptographic KMS activity (key wrap/unwrap, transient key leases) and inconsistent region-pin assertions emitted by upstream services. This change adds an operator crypto audit playbook, an adapter that injects and validates region-assertion headers for KMS calls, and RBACv2 templates to surface per-operator retention and attestation obligations. Motivation: give security/compliance teams deterministic evidence during post-incident reviews and make operator-scoped crypto usage auditable without changing customer-facing APIs. What this PR does: 1) runtime/adapter: introduce region-assertion-adapter that decorates KMS requests with signed region claims, validates responses' provenance, and emits structured audit events to the audit pipeline; 2) policy: add rbacv2/operator-retention-templates that map operator roles to audit retention classes and consent scopes; 3) playbook: add docs/playbooks/crypto-operator-audit.md with step-by-step runbook for triage, artifacts to collect, and checklists for legal/regulatory handoff; 4) telemetry: add metrics and traces (kms.region_assertion.{validate,failed}, audit.playbook.run_count) and link to Console dashboards; 5) tests: unit tests for adapter signing/verification and integration test that simulates cross-region KMS failover; 6) rollout: feature-flag gated (feature.flags.crypto_audit_adapter) with staged rollout to 10% then 100% and synthetic monitoring for latency/99p token path. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for adapter signing/verification; - [x] Integration test for KMS failover + assertion fallback; - [x] RBAC templates reviewed by compliance; - [x] Playbook reviewed by Legal; - [x] Feature flag and metric hooks added; Related: ENG-9842 for platform telemetry and SUP-4321 for a customer support escalation that surfaced missing operator audit trails. Testing notes: synthetic test harness added under benchmark-lab/testdata/crypto-assertion to simulate signed region claims and stale-token scenarios. Operational considerations: adapter verifies that region claims are signed by an operator-attestor service (new microservice stubbed here), a CA rotation path was added to docs, and a mitigation path triggers KMS local fallback when assertion validation fails to avoid hard outages. Security review: encryption signing keys are stored in tenant-scoped keystores and never emitted in plaintext to logs. Migration and backward compatibility: adapter is opt-in behind feature flag; RBAC templates are additive and do not alter existing policies. Rollout plan: 10% -> monitor error budget for 72h -> 50% -> 100% after no anomalies. Followups: add automated audit summarizer and Legal retention exporter (separate PR).
Adds an operator-focused crypto audit runbook, region-assertion middleware for KMS calls, and RBAC policy templates for storing audit retention windows. Backwards-compatible rollout with feature flag. Not visible to end users.
Diego Alvarez: Can the adapter fall back to non-asserted KMS calls when the attestor service is unreachable? We should avoid hard outages for customer traffic.
Priya Malhotra (author): Adapter is configured to fallback to local KMS path; fallback is controlled by feature flags and emits a high-severity audit event so SRE/Compliance can trace the window.
Marta Chen: Please add a small note in the playbook about evidence preservation (where to snapshot KV-cache/memory artifacts). Also consider expiring the audit retention mapping after policy rotation.
Priya Malhotra (author): Added explicit snapshot locations and an automated retention expirer hook in legal/retention/retention_mapping.md; explained rotation story in the playbook.
Ravi Patel: Lint and go vet flagged a race in adapter_test; please fix before merging.
Priya Malhotra (author): Fixed race by using a test harness mutex; re-ran CI and verified tests are stable.
Marta Chen: Approved after verifying that the retention templates align with compliance matrix.
Diego Alvarez: Approve (tested locally with synthetic harness).

payload.body:
Motivation: Customers asked for unambiguous billing provenance for KMS operations and stronger guarantees that audit records survive cross-region failovers without misattribution. This PR implements a lightweight KMS usage provenance tagger plus an opt-in Audit Consistency Proxy that enforces ordered, idempotent audit writes and emits signed checkpoints. Key changes: 1) services/kms: introduce an annotator that emits X-Redwood-KMS-Tag header with canonical tuple (service_id|region|purpose|nonce) derived from tenant claims and routing decisions; the nonce is HMAC(service_signing_key, timestamp|tenant_id) to prevent replay and spoofing; 2) audit/proxy: new service that buffers per-tenant audit envelopes, verifies monotonic sequence windows, signs checkpoints to an audit index, and exposes a health/metrics endpoint for backpressure monitoring; 3) pkg/rbac: add residency.kms-controller role and RBAC v2 mappings preventing non-region-anchored operators from modifying tagger or proxy configuration; 4) infra/terraform: optional module to deploy the proxy behind a regional gateway; 5) web/console: admin toggle and rollout controls for audit.consistency.enabled. Backwards compatibility: the tagging header is additive and ignored by legacy components; the proxy is disabled by default for gradual rollout. Rollout plan: enable in a single region for canary tenants, monitor checkpoint latency and audit sink throughput, then expand regions. Rollback: flip audit.consistency.enabled to false to bypass proxy and restore best-effort forwarding. Security considerations: tags are signed at the perimeter to prevent operator spoofing; proxy verifies signatures before accepting envelopes. payload.body:
- Adds migration safety guardrails used during Private upgrades: advisory locks, lock/statement timeouts, idempotency validation, and "safe default" patterns for schema changes.
- Improves migration logging and surfaces actionable errors to upgrade tooling.
- No user-facing API changes; behavior change is limited to migration execution and failure mode (fail-fast with clearer remediation).
Title: DB migrations: add guardrails (idempotency checks, lock timeouts, safer defaults) for Private upgrades

Context
We’ve had multiple upgrade-related incidents/near-misses where a migration either (a) blocked application traffic for longer than expected due to long lock waits, (b) partially applied and then re-ran in an unsafe way, or (c) took a non-backward-compatible path that required perfect ordering across control-plane/data-plane rollouts. The most recent customer-visible case is SUP-18421 (upgrade failed during DB migration; required manual intervention and extended downtime).

This PR adds a set of guardrails to make migrations safer by default in Private environments:
- predictable lock acquisition behavior (timeouts + fail-fast)
- explicit idempotency checks (detect partial/duplicate application earlier)
- safer schema patterns (additive/expand-then-contract defaults, avoid non-null without backfill, avoid table rewrites)
- better structured logging so installer can present actionable remediation and so SRE can correlate upgrade windows

Goals
- Reduce upgrade-induced outages by preventing migrations from waiting indefinitely on locks.
- Make reruns safe and detectable (idempotency validation + consistent bookkeeping).
- Encourage backward-compatible schema evolution so CP/DP phase separation remains valid.
- Keep changes compatible with existing migration tooling and deployment modes.

Non-goals
- Rewriting existing historical migrations.
- Introducing multi-hop migration automation across many majors.

What changed
1) Migration execution guardrails (Postgres)
- Enforce lock timeout and statement timeout for all migration sessions.
  - Default lock_timeout: 5s
  - Default statement_timeout: 15m
  - Both are configurable via env/config for Private deployments.
- Acquire an advisory lock keyed by (service, schema) before applying any migrations to prevent concurrent migration runners during rollouts.
- Ensure all migration steps run in a controlled transaction mode (transactional where possible; explicit non-transactional allow-list).

2) Idempotency & partial-apply detection
- Validate migration history before applying:
  - Detect duplicate version entries.
  - Detect checksum mismatch for already-applied migrations (when a migration file changed between builds).
  - Detect “dirty” state from interrupted runs and fail with explicit remediation steps.
- Add a small helper that marks a migration as "started" and "completed" with timestamps for better debugging, while remaining compatible with the existing schema_migrations table (no breaking schema change).

3) Backward-compatible schema defaults
- New helpers/patterns used by upcoming Private upgrade work:
  - Add columns as nullable + backfill + set default + then (optionally) enforce NOT NULL in a later release.
  - Avoid blocking index creation (use CONCURRENTLY where supported and safe).
  - Prefer additive enums/polymorphic refs rather than destructive renames.
- Update a handful of existing in-tree migrations that were in-flight (unreleased) to follow the safer patterns (no changes to already-shipped migration versions).

4) Observability & operator UX
- Structured logs emitted per migration:
  - migration_version, migration_name, phase (acquire_lock/apply/verify), duration_ms
  - lock_timeout_ms, statement_timeout_ms
  - blocked_by_pid (when available) for lock timeouts
- Errors are categorized with remediation text intended for installer surface area:
  - LOCK_TIMEOUT: "retry after clearing blocking transaction; see query to identify blocker"
  - DIRTY_STATE: "manual verification required; see steps"
  - CHECKSUM_MISMATCH: "artifact mismatch; verify bundle/version pin"

Implementation details
- Config keys
  - REDWOOD_DB_MIGRATIONS_LOCK_TIMEOUT (default: 5s)
  - REDWOOD_DB_MIGRATIONS_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT (default: 15m)
  - REDWOOD_DB_MIGRATIONS_ADVISORY_LOCK (default: enabled)
- Advisory lock key is derived from a stable hash of (db_name + schema_name + service_name) to avoid collisions across services sharing a cluster.
- Lock timeout handling
  - We set local session settings at the start of each migration transaction.
  - On lock timeout, we emit the blocker info when obtainable and abort without retrying in-process (retry is handled by upgrade orchestration to keep behavior deterministic).

Files / areas touched (high level)
- services/control-plane/db/migrate/*
- services/common/db/migrations_runner/*
- services/common/db/postgres/lock_helpers.*
- docs/internal/private-upgrades/migration-guardrails.md
- tests/db/migrations_guardrails_test.*

Commits (summary)
- db: add advisory lock + timeout config for migration runner
- db: add migration history validation + dirty state detection
- db: structured logs + categorized errors for upgrade surfaces
- migrations: refactor unreleased migrations to use safe additive patterns
- tests: add integration tests for lock timeout and checksum mismatch cases
- docs: add "Migration guardrails" guidance for Private upgrade runbook

Testing
- Unit tests for history validation, checksum mismatch detection, and advisory lock behavior.
- Integration test (Postgres) that simulates:
  - long-running transaction holding an exclusive lock -> migration fails with LOCK_TIMEOUT and prints blocker pid query
  - dirty state -> fails with DIRTY_STATE and remediation text
  - checksum mismatch -> fails with CHECKSUM_MISMATCH (useful for air-gapped bundle mismatch debugging)
- Manual: applied on staging Private environment with synthetic traffic during upgrade window; verified CP/DP phased rollout does not deadlock.

Rollout / risk
- Low-to-medium risk: touches migration execution path. Mitigated by:
  - conservative timeouts + config overrides
  - fail-fast behavior (previous behavior was indefinite waiting)
  - additional logging for quick diagnosis
- Intended to be a prerequisite for the Private upgrade + rollback mechanism work (installer will treat these error categories as deterministic failure modes).

Reviewer notes / requests
- SRE asked that failure modes be explicit and that we don’t auto-retry inside the runner.
- Security asked that we avoid logging query contents or sensitive data; this PR only logs metadata and pids.

Review conversation (highlights)
- Sean Gallagher (SRE): "Can we ensure we never wait forever on locks? Also want the blocker PID surfaced so oncall can act quickly." Author: "Yes; lock_timeout is enforced via SET LOCAL; on timeout we attempt to query pg_locks/pg_stat_activity and include a suggested query with the blocker pid when available. No auto-retry in runner." Requested changes: add docs snippet to SRE runbook and ensure log fields are stable. Addressed in commit 4/6.
- Ethan Park: "Advisory lock keying: make sure multi-tenant DBs don’t collide and that services with separate schemas don’t block each other." Author: "Key includes db + schema + service; also added a unit test for key derivation stability." Approved after changes.
- Irene Choi: "Timeout defaults feel aggressive for large customers. Can we make them configurable and document recommended overrides?" Author: "Added env/config + docs table with guidance. Default statement timeout 15m; lock timeout 5s." Approved.
- Naomi Feldman: "Double-check logs don’t include SQL text or customer identifiers." Author: "Confirmed; only versions/names/timeouts/pids." Approved.
- Rafael Mendes: "How does this interact with installer rollback?" Author: "Fail-fast allows installer to stop before DP rollouts proceed; categorized errors map to planned remediation. This PR doesn’t implement rollback but is a dependency for deterministic upgrade state." Approved.

CI
- build-and-unit-tests: pass
- db-integration-tests: pass (added ~3m)
- lint: pass
- security-scan: pass

Merge
Merged via squash on 2025-06-07 by Connor O’Brien after approvals from Platform + SRE + Security. Follow-ups tracked in ENG-4844 to align installer surfaces with the new categorized errors and to ensure support bundles collect migration logs during upgrade windows.
payload.title: DB migrations: add guardrails (idempotency checks, lock timeouts, safer defaults) for Private upgrades

Motivation: our premerge lint stage runs the monolithic linter across the whole monorepo which causes noisy failures and slow feedback for small changes. Release instrumentation currently uses a hard quiesce period that is difficult to rollback during incidents. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) an Atomic Lint Adapter that shards lint invocation by package and by changed-file footprint, plus a lightweight action wrapper so teams can opt-in per-directory; (2) a Rollbackable Release Quiesce controller that implements a release annotation and a short-circuit API so on-call can cancel or shorten quiesce windows without rolling back the deploy.

Changeset summary: single continuous description below with checklist, commits summary, changed areas, reviews and CI notes. See related Linear ENG-1267 for rollout plan and SUP-412 for incident follow-up notes.

Checklist:
- [x] design doc attached and discussed with infra (link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1267/atomic-lint-design)
- [x] add action composite and publish ephemeral image tag for testing
- [x] add feature flags for adapter and quiesce controller (off by default)
- [x] unit + e2e for quiesce controller and adapter shim
- [x] docs: docs/ci/atomic-lint.md and docs/ci/release-quiesce.md
- [x] roll-forward plan and telemetry hooks added for 1-week canary

Commits (high-level):
- feat(ci): add atomic-lint composite action and per-package runner shim
- feat(release): add quiesce controller + short-circuit API + controller tests
- chore(ci): bump actions/setup-node + cache action pins for compatibility
- refactor(cache): introduce v2 build-cache protocol negotiation (backward compatible)
- docs: add operational runbook and rollout steps

Files changed (high level):
- .github/actions/atomic-lint/action.yml - composite action and entrypoint wrapper
- ci/lint/adapter/runner.go - logic to compute changed-file footprint and shard jobs
- ci/cache/protocol/v2.proto - cache protocol negotiation (keeps v1 server support)
- release/controller/quiesce_controller.go - controller + API ext
- docs/ci/atomic-lint.md - usage and opt-in guide
- docs/ci/release-quiesce.md - runbook and short-circuit playbook
- Dockerfile.ci-image, images/ci/BUILD.bazel - small image bump for setup
- tests/ci/atomic_lint_integration_test.go - new e2e harness

Testing and rollout:
- Local unit tests: go test ./ci/... (green)
- Integration: atomic-lint was exercised in a canary repo (redwood-examples) with flaky file detection disabled; two minor fixes pushed after initial run
- Quiesce controller tested end-to-end against staging controller; added a short-circuit endpoint and RBAC guard
- Canary window: enabled for team/platform/* routes for 72 hours; telemetry keyed under telemetry.ci.atomic_lint.* and telemetry.release.quiesce.*

Review conversation (thread summary):
- Ravi Kapoor (review): "Nice separation. A few questions on concurrency: will the atomic adapter ever hit the coordinator with >100 shards for a single PR? How do we limit executor fanout?" — Author reply: "Adapter groups by package and has a max_shards config default 12; added a coordinator-side rate limiter and a fallback to run monolithic lint if shard budget exceeded. See ci/lint/adapter/runner.go lines flagged." 
- Aisha Parker (request changes): "Cache protocol negotiation looks okay but make sure v2 falls back cleanly to v1 servers. Add an integration test that mocks v1 behavior." — Author reply: "Added v1 mock server in tests/ci/cache_mock_v1_test.go and included compat test in CI matrix."
- Leo Martinez (approval): "Approach is sensible and deployable. Suggest adding a small audit metric for quiesce short-circuits (who invoked)." — Author reply: "Added audit metric and associated tag in quiesce_controller.go; included in telemetry registration."
- Final /commit: after a small CI flake on the integration job we reran the job; fixed a test ordering race in atomic_lint_integration_test.go. Approvals: Ravi Kapoor approved 2024-11-04, Leo Martinez approved 2024-11-05.

CI status details: initial run had one failing integration (flaky test), rerun succeeded. Checks: build (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-canary (pass after rerun), lint (pass), security-scan (pass). GitHub Actions matrix included linux/go1.20 and linux/go1.22 lanes.

Merge and post-merge actions: merged via squash on 2024-11-06 by Ravi Kapoor. Post-merge: created rollout Linear task ENG-1291 to stagger enabling and to add quota for shard limits. Feature gates default to off; rollout window captured in docs/ci/release-quiesce.md.
Ravi Kapoor: Asked about shard fanout and rate limiting. Author added max_shards=12 and coordinator rate limiter.
Aisha Parker: Requested v1 fallback tests for cache protocol. Author added cache_mock_v1_test.go and CI matrix entry.

Ravi Kapoor: Approved and merged on 2024-11-06.

Add atomic lint adapter (opt-in) to shard lint runs by changed-file footprint; add a rollbackable release quiesce controller with short-circuit API; backward-compatible v2 build-cache protocol negotiation; CI action pin bumps and docs. Feature gated off by default; rollout under ENG-1291.
This PR touches CI tooling and release infra; operations should monitor telemetry.ci.atomic_lint.* and telemetry.release.quiesce.* during rollout. If on-call needs to abort quiesce, call POST /api/v1/quiesce/short-circuit with audit header.

payload.body:
Motivation: We need a lightweight mechanism to capture a tenant-aware cost snapshot at decision points (model rollout, autoscale events, prefills) and to register compact quantization bundles that can be referenced by routing/policy rules. This PR introduces two cooperating subsystems: (1) Cost Snapshotter - a runtime hook that records short-lived unit-econ signals (per-tenant token mix, batch shapes, cache hit ratio, recently selected quant profile) to a compact, queryable store; (2) Quant Bundle Registrar - a small metadata service that validates, fingerprints, and publishes quantization bundles (quant configs + safety tags) to be used by the routing layer and Optimize recommendations.

What changed (high level):
- Cost Snapshotter: new runtime hook integrated into the request router; emits a compact protobuf to the snapshots store for sampling-enabled tenants. Snapshots are TTL'd and indexed by tenant, model, and request time-bucket.
- Snapshot ingestion pipeline: lightweight consumer that enriches snapshots with recent telemetry and persists derived unit-cost estimates to the cost-store used by the optimizer.
- Quant Bundle Registrar: CLI + HTTP endpoints to publish quant bundles, validate compatibility, and attach safety labels (loss-estimate, fallthrough-policy). Bundles are versioned and fingerprinted.
- Policy integration: routing policy logic extended to consult latest snapshot and registered bundle metadata when selecting model/quant variants for a request.
- Tests and docs: unit tests for the registrar, runtime smoke tests for snapshot emission, and an ops runbook for enabling sampling and bundle rollouts.

Design notes:
- Snapshots are intentionally compact (<= 1KB) and emitted at request-tail to avoid blocking.
- Registrar validates bundles by running a dry-run quant check on a small synthetic prompt set to approximate compatibility; expensive checks are gated behind a flag.
- By default sampling is off; rollout plan recommends enabling 1% tenant sampling then ramping.

Checklist:
- [x] Snapshot proto and migrations
- [x] Runtime hook + gated feature flag
- [x] Registrar API + CLI
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Docs: ops runbook + API docs

Backward compatibility: Registrations are additive. If routing cannot find a compatible registered bundle, it falls back to the existing quant selection logic.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy registrar in read-only mode and smoke test publishing CLI to staging.
2) Enable snapshot sampling for internal tenants (alice/dev) at 1%.
3) Validate cost estimates and ensure no perf regression under low sampling.
4) Gradually enable sampling on more tenants and flip on registrar-driven routing for canary tenants.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: extra write amplification on hot paths. Mitigation: snapshots are emitted asynchronously to an in-memory buffer with backpressure; when buffer is full we drop non-critical snapshots and record a metric.
- Risk: incorrect quant bundle causing quality regressions. Mitigation: safety labels and a staged rollout (dry-run compatibility checks + canary routing with automatic fallback).

Related: ENG-4238 (unit-econ hooks), SUP-1082 (customer report influencing sampling needs).
Ravi Menon: The async buffer size looks small for certain tenants that burst; can we expose this as a tenant-level override?
Aisha Patel: Added a tenant-level override via config and documented it in the runbook (see commit 0a1b2c3).
Jonas Bergstrom: Registrar should surface a compatibility score instead of a binary pass/fail to assist manual reviews.
Aisha Patel: Added compatibility_score to the registrar response and included threshold config (dry-run gated).
Marta Flores: Add alerting for high snapshot drop rates so SRE can troubleshoot before enabling sampling broadly.
Aisha Patel: Alert added to ops runbook and metric exposed (snapshots dropped / emitted).
Introduce Cost Snapshotter (tenant sampling of compact runtime cost signals) and Quant Bundle Registrar (publish/validate versioned quant profiles). Feature is gated and off by default; follow ops runbook to enable sampling and registrar-driven routing.

payload.body:
Motivation: We need finer-grained, tenant-aware allocation decisions that trade latency SLOs against unit cost in a predictable way, and a companion mechanism to prioritize quantization candidate lanes when capacity is constrained. This PR introduces two coordinated components: 1) alloc-decision-graph (ADG) — a small, deterministic decision-graph runtime that consumes tenant profiles, recent latency/cost telemetry, and policy rules to select allocation tiers (dedicated/d burst/cold-shed) and batching hints per request cohort; 2) quant-priority-synthesizer (QPS) — a lightweight ranking engine that scores quantization profiles by expected unit-cost reduction and estimated regression risk (based on eval-snapshots) to drive graceful prioritization and staged rollouts. What this changes: - New runtime module: src/econ/alloc_graph.py (decision-graph evaluator, policy compiler, deterministic fallback path). - Quantization ranking: src/compiler/quant_priority.py (scoring models, snapshot ingestion, drift detection hooks). - Runtime bindings: src/runtime/route_allocator.cc and src/runtime/route_allocator_test.py (integrates ADG into routing path with a fast cache for per-tenant decision results). - Telemetry and dashboards: docs/observability/alloc-telemetry.md and dashboards/alloc-decision-board.jsonnet (new metrics and tracing spans). - Operator UX: docs/operators/quant-priority-playbook.md (how to interpret QPS scores, safe rollout steps). Compatibility and safety: - ADG runs in read-only mode by default; a feature flag enable_alloc_graph=true is required to apply decisions in production. - QPS exposes conservative defaults and a safety gate that prevents a quant profile from being auto-applied unless weekly regression rate < 0.5% on a controlled eval set. - Both components include explicit fallbacks to current behavior (round-robin allocation and static quant tiers) when telemetry is insufficient. Tests and validation: - Unit tests for ADG node evaluation and policy compilation added under tests/econ/test_alloc_graph.py. - Synthetic integration harness in benchmark-lab/synthetic/alloc_graph_runner.py that simulates tenant mixture and reports unit-cost and 95p latency. - End-to-end smoke in CI that runs a small local runner against sample profiles. Performance: - In the synthetic harness, enabling ADG reduced per-token unit-cost by ~7.2% on mixed workloads while keeping 95p latency within SLO bounds in 94% of runs. QPS prioritized 3x fewer aggressive quant candidates compared to the previous naive ranking and avoided 2 regression incidents during the rollout simulation. Rollout plan: - Stage 1 (canary): enable_alloc_graph for internal tenant ID=redwood-ci for two weeks. - Stage 2: opt-in for beta tenants via console flag. - Stage 3: gradual ramp to tiered allocation until telemetry confirms <1% latency regressions. Documentation: - Added README sections and operator playbooks (see docs/). Related work: builds on ENG-1429 tenant profiling work and PM-321 cost-heuristics initiative. Notes: this PR is intended to be conservative and operator-driven; no automatic tenant-wide enforcement is enabled without explicit opt-in.
1) add initial alloc-decision-graph evaluator and unit tests
2) introduce quant-priority scoring module and ingestion path
3) wire ADG into route allocator with caching and feature flag
4) add telemetry spans and dashboard manifest
5) docs: operator playbook and rollout guidance
6) tests: synthetic harness & CI smoke
--- a/src/runtime/route_allocator.cc
+++ b/src/runtime/route_allocator.cc
@@ -128,6 +128,24 @@
+// consult alloc-decision-graph for tenant-aware allocation hints
+if (feature_flags.enable_alloc_graph) {
+  auto hint = alloc_graph_->Evaluate(tenant_profile);
+  ApplyHintToBatching(hint);
+}

--- a/src/compiler/quant_priority.py
+def score_profile(profile, eval_snapshot):
+    # simple risk-adjusted estimate: benefit * (1 - regression_risk)
+    return profile.estimated_savings * (1.0 - eval_snapshot.regression_prob)

Liam O'Neill: Could we add a quick circuit-breaker that disables ADG when critical p99 latency climbs > 20%? Request adding integration smoke to assert this behavior.
Maya Kapoor: Added a circuit-breaker hook and test in route_allocator_test.py; by default it is set to 20% and operator-adjustable via alloc_circuit_config.
Sofia Ramos: Telemetry looks good. Please include a short rollback playbook and ensure dashboards expose decision distribution per-tenant.
Maya Kapoor: Added dashboard manifest and rollback playbook (docs/operators). Also added per-tenant decision metric (alloc.decision.count by decision_label).
Anand Patel: Nit: move quant-priority configuration to compiler config file rather than hardcoding thresholds. Also see one minor threading issue in route_allocator.cc.
Maya Kapoor: Moved thresholds to /etc/redwood/compiler/quant_priority.yaml and fixed the threading race by using platform::AtomicGuard.
Sofia Ramos: Approved after changes.
Liam O'Neill: Approved. Recommend squash merge to keep history compact.
Adds a tenant-aware allocation decision graph to improve unit-costs and a quantization priority synthesizer to safely rank quant profiles. Feature gated; no automatic tenant-wide enforcement. Operators: see docs/operators/quant-priority-playbook.md for rollout and rollback steps.
Enable canary for internal tenant redwood-ci via feature flag toggles
Monitor alloc.decision.* metrics and cost/latency dashboards over two weeks
Collect QPS scoring telemetry and evaluate false positives vs eval-snapshots
