payload.body:
Context: As part of the Cloud Marketplace Listing Refresh, we need reliable, provider-consistent instrumentation to measure the subscription → entitlement → org provisioning → first API key/usage funnel and identify drop-offs. Today we have partial logs and a few ad-hoc metrics, but no stable analytics taxonomy and no standard error/latency dimensions to support Partnerships + Growth reporting. This PR introduces a small set of canonical marketplace onboarding telemetry events emitted by the console + control-plane API, plus a metrics bridge so we can build dashboards/alerts without scraping logs.

Summary of changes: (1) Adds canonical analytics events for marketplace onboarding across AWS/GCP flows. (2) Adds latency + error code dimensions for entitlement verification and org linking steps. (3) Adds a lightweight server-side aggregator that emits Prometheus counters/histograms to support operational dashboards ("entitlement check failure rate", "entitlement check p95") while keeping product analytics in RudderStack/warehouse. (4) Adds dashboard hook definitions (Grafana JSON + Looker explore notes) and updates the event catalog docs.

Event taxonomy (new): All events are emitted as "track" events to telemetry with a stable schema. Event names are provider-agnostic; provider is a property.
- marketplace.onboarding_entrypoint_viewed (when user enters marketplace-specific console flow)
- marketplace.entitlement_check_started
- marketplace.entitlement_check_succeeded
- marketplace.entitlement_check_failed
- marketplace.org_link_started
- marketplace.org_link_succeeded
- marketplace.org_link_failed
- marketplace.api_key_create_started
- marketplace.api_key_create_succeeded
- marketplace.api_key_create_failed
- marketplace.first_request_succeeded (first successful request made with a marketplace-provisioned key)
- marketplace.provisioning_waiting_shown (UI state when entitlement exists but org provisioning not yet completed)

Common properties (all events): provider (aws|gcp), provider_account_id_hash (sha256, salted), marketplace_product_code (string, where available), marketplace_sku_id (Redwood marketplace SKU id), marketplace_offer_type (public|private|unknown), region (control plane region), environment (prod|staging), redwood_org_id (uuid), redwood_user_id (uuid), session_id, request_id (if server-side), error_code (if failed), error_stage (entitlement|org_link|api_key|first_request), latency_ms (when applicable). We intentionally do NOT send raw cloud account IDs, emails, API keys, or full error messages. Error details are bucketed by code.

Operational metrics (Prometheus):
- marketplace_entitlement_check_total{provider,result,error_code}
- marketplace_entitlement_check_latency_ms_bucket{provider,result}
- marketplace_org_link_total{provider,result,error_code}
- marketplace_org_link_latency_ms_bucket{provider,result}
- marketplace_api_key_create_total{provider,result,error_code}
- marketplace_first_request_total{provider}

Dashboards/hooks: Adds Grafana dashboard skeleton "Marketplace Onboarding Funnel (Ops)" with panels for p50/p95 entitlement check latency, error-rate by code, and time-in-waiting-state distribution. Looker/warehouse note added for funnel chart using events marketplace.onboarding_entrypoint_viewed → marketplace.entitlement_check_succeeded → marketplace.org_link_succeeded → marketplace.api_key_create_succeeded → marketplace.first_request_succeeded.

Implementation notes:
- Console now emits client-side events on key steps, but all success/failure completion events are confirmed from server responses so the funnel is not inflated by navigation abandons.
- Control-plane emits server-side events for entitlement verification endpoints (ENG-22110) and org linking endpoints; these are used for authoritative latency/error metrics.
- Adds a shared error mapping table (MarketplaceOnboardingErrorCode) to keep error codes consistent across UI + API.
- Rate limiting: server-side telemetry emission uses a bounded async queue; drops are counted in marketplace_telemetry_dropped_total.

Testing:
- Unit tests for event payload construction and redaction (no raw provider account id).
- Integration tests for entitlement check endpoint instrumentation (ensures error_code mapping on common failures).
- Manual: validated staging flow for AWS and GCP subscription linking, including "entitlement propagation delay" UI state.

Rollout:
- Behind feature flag telemetry.marketplace_onboarding_v1 (default ON in staging, OFF in prod).
- After merge: enable in prod at 25% for 24h, then 100% if no telemetry drop spikes and no PII violations in warehouse sampling.

Follow-ups (not in this PR):
- Add client-side retry reason fields for entitlement propagation delay (ENG-22116 / sync job hardening) once final error codes are agreed.
- Wire dashboards to SRE alert thresholds after baseline is collected for ~7 days.

Checklist: [x] Reviewed with Growth (Ben) for funnel semantics [x] Reviewed with Console owner (Chloe) for UX coverage [x] Reviewed with Billing/Metering (Cole) for SKU id properties [x] Security review for PII/redaction (Marcus to follow up in separate security docs PR) [x] Added docs to internal event catalog
Ben Carter (review): The funnel definition looks right, but we need a way to distinguish "entitlement not yet propagated" vs "hard failure". Can we add a specific error_code for the waiting state and make sure it doesn't count as a failed entitlement check? Nadia (author): Added marketplace.provisioning_waiting_shown as a UI event and ensured entitlement_check_failed only fires on terminal error responses (4xx/5xx with known codes). Waiting state is tracked separately.

Chloe Martin (review): Please avoid double-firing success events when users refresh the page mid-flow. Also want request_id included for server-side events so we can correlate traces when debugging. Nadia: Added idempotency guard in console emitter keyed by (session_id,event_name,org_id). Server-side now includes request_id; console includes request_id from response headers when present.

Cole Summers (review): Make sure marketplace_sku_id matches the new catalog IDs (pr-19874). Right now I see "hosted_api" in a couple payload examples. Nadia: Updated to use billing catalog mapping and added a test fixture wired to the new marketplace SKU ids; examples corrected.

Ethan Park (review): Metrics bridge is good, but the histogram buckets are too fine (will create high-cardinality series). Suggest standard buckets and ensure provider/result/error_code labels are bounded. Introduce a lightweight Telemetry Deduper service and a Token Collapse Visualizer dashboard to reduce noisy duplicate spans and surface redundant token-level cost patterns. Motivation: during several incidents and routine SLO tuning we observed high cardinality and alert fatigue caused by duplicated spans emitted from the serving runtime (frontend retries, duplicate instrumentation points, and batched replays). This PR implements a deterministic fingerprinting pipeline that collapses semantically-identical spans early in the observability ingestion path and a dashboard that helps engineers understand when token costs are dominated by collapsed/duplicate traffic. The change includes a TTL-backed fingerprint cache, session-aware collapse heuristics, an orthogonal latency decomposition helper ("orthogonalizer") that attributes latency to queue/io/model phases for collapsed invocations, alert tuning rules to avoid duplicate alert storms, end-to-end tests with synthetic replay, and a Grafana dashboard with an interactive token-collapse Sankey and cost-savings calculator. Backwards compatibility: original spans are still retained in sampled snapshots; deduped counts are emitted as both raw_count and deduped_count so downstream consumers can opt-in. This description includes: design rationale, implementation summary, QA notes, rollout plan, and linked Linear/Jira items.
Ben Carter: Nice design; double-check that fingerprinting is stable across SDK versions. If the SDK changes field ordering we might get different fingerprints. Can we canonicalize JSON fields before hashing?
Aisha Rahman: Good point — we canonicalize by using a deterministic field ordering and a trimmed key set (service, span_name, callsite_id, token_span_hash). Added unit to test canonicalization.
Lara Kim: Question on retention: you collapse early — where do engineers look when they need raw traces? Are we losing fidelity?
Aisha Rahman: We emit sampled raw spans at a configurable sample rate and keep a 'recent_raw_snapshot' buffer for 1 hour. Deduped_count is emitted as a metric and the raw sample includes an "original_spans" array when sampled. Documented in ops runbook.
Mateo Alvarez: The orthogonalizer code looks promising but the math should be commented — hard to review. Add a short note explaining the decomposition and assumptions.
Aisha Rahman: Added docstring and a design paragraph in docs/observability/README.md; moved linear algebra helpers to a util module and included a reproducible example.
CI Bot: Unit tests failed on first run (integration e2e timeout).
Aisha Rahman: Increased timeout for synthetic replay and added retry backoff; re-ran CI, tests passed.
Adds a telemetry deduplication stage to the ingest pipeline that reduces duplicate spans and lowers alert noise; introduces a Token Collapse Visualizer dashboard to inspect redundant token-level cost and a latency orthogonalizer to attribute latency by phase. Default behavior preserves sampled raw spans. See docs/observability/README.md for rollout and tuning.
Canary deploy under flags: deduper.enabled=true and deduper.canary_tenants=[internal-*]. If alerts spike after canary, set deduper.mode=passthrough to disable collapse and keep metrics intact. Runbook: ops/monitoring/runbooks/token-collapse-runbook.md

Context and motivation:
We maintain three SDK implementations (Python/TS/Go) that each had slightly different credential wiring, retry presets, and streaming consumer ergonomics. That caused recurrent bugs during rollouts where a token refresh behavior in one SDK didn't match the behavior in the others and made cross-language examples brittle.

This PR introduces a lightweight, language-agnostic 'auth profile' concept (credentials + retry profile + telemetry tags) and companion async consumer helper utilities for streaming endpoints. The goal is to: (1) unify token refresh semantics, (2) centralize retry presets so customers get consistent SLO behavior across SDKs, and (3) provide ergonomic async/iterable helpers for common streaming patterns.

- Added AuthProfile class/factory in each SDK that encapsulates: credential source, rotation window, retry preset name, and telemetry tags.
- Introduced AsyncStreamConsumer helpers: a small set of convenience functions to iterate, pause/resume, and run timebound consumers with built-in backoff hints and graceful cancelation.

Summary: Add a tenant 'shelving' path that temporarily reduces feature surface when a tenant repeatedly breaches SLOs instead of instant eviction; add a cross-zone circuit 'hold' (hysteresis) controller to reduce flip-flopping of circuit breakers during regional pressure events; fix a KV-drain race observed during a canary incident that caused brief 5xx spikes.
Motivation: during the last incident we saw two negative effects: (1) tenants hitting soft SLO thresholds were immediately escalated to hard eviction which caused cascading retries and higher tail latency across nodes; (2) circuit states were oscillating across zones, triggering repeated rejoin/drain cycles. Shelving provides a graduated, observable degradation that preserves core functionality (reads and short prompts) while shedding expensive paths (batch-heavy routes, long-context generations). The hysteresis controller enforces a small, configurable cool-down window across regions before allowing a circuit re-open; combined with a lightweight telemetry-backed quorum check this reduces oscillation and regional thrashing.
Hotfix: KV drain procedure could race with shelf transition leading to stale cache pointers and occasional 500s for a small fraction of requests; this PR serializes the transition and adds a short safety checkpoint to guarantee KV eviction completion before route switch.
Changes (high level):
- runtime/tenant_manager: add shelving state machine, shelve/unshelve transitions, API hooks for route selectors
- runtime/circuit/coordinator: introduce crosszone_hysteresis controller and quorum probe

- api/gateway: route selector updates to honor 'shelved' routes with degraded config

payload.body:
Problem: under mixed tenant workloads we observed oscillatory spill behavior and long tail GC/compaction pauses when the KV cache hit a high fragmentation state. Existing slab and segment allocators used fixed reservation heuristics which either over-reserved space for noisy tenants or under-provisioned hot lanes, causing repeated spill waves that increased p99 latency and IO churn.

Proposal and approach: introduce a new 'slot-lane reservoir' allocator that separates cache residency into lightweight lanes per-tenant and a small shared reservoir. Key ideas: 1) lane reservations are elastic and decay over time based on access patterns (soft-threshold allocator), 2) a deferred spill controller (spill deferrer) batches spill operations and applies tenant-level pacing when downstream IO is saturated, 3) a compact-on-evict hook triggers opportunistic in-place compaction for highly fragmented lanes before spilling, and 4) metrics and trace points added to observe lane occupancy, reservoir pressure, and deferred-spill queue length. The design favors graceful degradation: when reservoir pressure rises we throttle low-priority lanes and avoid synchronized large spills via randomized jitter.

What this PR does: implements the slot-lane reservoir (pkg/kv/cache/reservoir.go, pkg/kv/allocator/slot_lane.go), adds unit and deterministic concurrency tests (pkg/kv/cache/reservoir_test.go), integrates a deferred-spill controller with tenant pacing (pkg/kv/spill/deferrer.go), exposes observability (metrics + span annotations), and updates the perf harness and Helm values for ramp testing.

Testing and benchmarks: microbenchmarks show a 35% reduction in spill events under synthetic mixed-tenancy load and a 22% improvement in p99 token-generation latency for latency-sensitive routes at 95th percentile reservoir pressure. CI includes unit tests, integration (small cluster) validation, and a benchmark job that ran twice to stabilize noisy results.

Upgrade/compat notes: no API changes. Configuration knobs are additive (reservoir_size, lane_decay_window_ms, spill_deferrer_max_batch) and default to off/low for safety. Operators can opt-in via Helm values or Redwood Console toggles.

Related work: follows ENG-1609 for fragmentation telemetry and ENG-1610 for spillback pacing heuristics.

Summary: this PR reduces noisy spill amplification and improves tail latency by combining elastic per-lane reservations with a deferred, paced spill controller and opportunistic compaction before eviction.
Arjun: Please clarify how lane decay interacts with high-frequency bursts — recommend adding a bounded hysteresis to avoid thrashing.
Author (Elena): Added lane_decay_hysteresis in second commit and updated tests to cover burst scenarios.
Priya: Observability looks good but we should add an alert for deferred-spill queue length > 1000.
Author: Added alert rule and doc entry; default threshold set to 500 for cloud-managed clusters.
Samir: Minor nit: rename reservoir.pressure -> reservoir.utilization for clarity.
Author: Renamed and updated metrics export in commit 5.
Samir: Approve after CI stabilization.
Under mixed workload (10 tenants, skewed hotset), spill count reduced from 1580 -> 1025 over 10 minutes; p99 latency for small-chat route reduced from 312ms -> 244ms. Bench harness details in bench/perf/kv_reservoir_bench.go.
Unit tests cover allocator invariants, decay window, and deferred spill scheduling. Integration test deploys a 3-node small cluster and runs a mixed-tenancy synthetic driver for 15 minutes verifying no more than 2 sustained spill waves. Bench harness run for statistical significance (n=5).
Risk: new allocator paths could regress memory accounting and trigger unexpected OOMs in unusual cluster configurations. Mitigations: conservative default reservoir size, extensive unit tests, a feature gate and runtime flags to disable deferred spill controller, and extra prometheus metrics to detect anomalies quickly.
Introduce slot-lane reservoir allocator to reduce spill amplification and improve tail latency under mixed-tenancy workloads. Add deferred spill controller with tenant pacing and compact-on-evict optimization. No user-facing API changes; configurable via Helm/Console.
Deployed to canary cluster for 48h post-merge with telemetry indicating expected pressure behavior; plan to roll to wider fleet after 1 week of stability metrics.

payload.body:
Title: Runtime: safer TP defaults (concurrency + batch guardrails) behind feature flag

Context
We have repeated reports of TP replicas hanging under sustained mixed prefill/decode + bursty concurrency (see SUP-48321, SUP-48344; also linked to ongoing ENG-4821/ENG-4824 work). While root-cause fixes are landing (scheduler ordering, NCCL stream sync, watchdog), we still need a low-risk operational mitigation we can roll out quickly to Dedicated canaries.

This PR introduces a feature-flagged guardrail set for TP replicas that reduces the probability of starvation / collective mismatch scenarios by:
- capping concurrent decode microbatches per TP replica
- limiting prefill batch tokens under mixed workloads
- bounding prefill queue depth / admission to avoid long prefill bursts starving decode + collectives

The intent is NOT to "solve" TP hangs, but to reduce incidence while deeper fixes roll through canary and to provide an easy on/off lever for SRE during incidents.

What changed
- New feature flag: runtime.tp.guardrails.v1
  - default: OFF globally
  - intended rollout: Dedicated canary clusters first (release plan tracked in ENG-4829)
- When enabled for TP replicas, apply guardrail defaults unless explicitly overridden by cluster config:
  - max_decode_concurrency_per_replica: 2 (was effectively unbounded aside from global worker limits)
  - max_inflight_prefills_per_replica: 1 (new; prevents prefill pileups)
  - max_prefill_batch_tokens: 16384 (new; tuned for A100/H100 mixed prompt distributions)
  - prefill_queue_soft_limit: 8 (new; admission control backpressure)
  - prefer_decode_on_mixed_load: true (new; small bias to keep decode iterations progressing)
- Adds structured log event at replica init: tp_guardrails_applied=true/false + the resolved values (so we can correlate outcomes in incident review).
- Adds metrics:
  - runtime_tp_guardrails_enabled{cluster,replica}
  - runtime_tp_admission_rejections_total{reason}
- Updates docs in code comments + config schema with "do not enable for non-TP replicas" guidance.

Why these numbers
These values came out of repro runs from benchmark-lab mixed-workload harness (see ENG-4822 / benchmark-lab PR-97) and align with what oncall has been doing manually during incidents (reduce concurrency; constrain batch sizes). The goal is to keep TP replicas from entering long prefill-only regimes where decode collectives get delayed long enough to trigger downstream timeouts and eventually a stall.

Risk / performance impact
- Expected: throughput reduction on prefill-heavy workloads when flag enabled (admission control). This is considered acceptable for the canary window because the failure mode we’re trading off against is replica wedging + autoscaling thrash.
- Decode latency should improve at p95/p99 under bursty concurrency due to reduced queueing.
- Flag is OFF by default; enabling is per-environment/per-cluster.

Rollout plan (high level)
1) Land behind flag.
2) Enable in one Dedicated canary cluster for affected account(s) during a low-risk window with SRE support.
3) Watch: request timeout rate, TP heartbeat gaps, admission rejection rate, and customer-perceived streaming stability.
4) If stable, expand to additional Dedicated clusters as part of runtime 1.19 canary (ENG-4829).

Testing
- Unit tests for config resolution precedence (global defaults < guardrails defaults < cluster overrides < per-model overrides)
- Integration test in runtime config loader for "flag on only for TP" behavior
- Manual validation in staging: enabling flag yields expected structured log + metrics

Changelog / commits
- 0d4c3c2 runtime/config: add runtime.tp.guardrails.v1 feature flag + schema
- 4a9bf11 runtime/scheduler: apply tp guardrail defaults to admission control
- 7c1ae88 runtime/metrics: add guardrails enabled + rejection counters
- 19d0a6d tests: config precedence coverage + TP-only guardrail test
- bbe12c9 docs: inline config docs + oncall notes (internal)

Files / areas touched (high level)
- runtime/config/schema.yaml
- runtime/config/loader.cc
- runtime/scheduler/admission_control.cc
- runtime/scheduler/replica_limits.h
- runtime/observability/metrics_runtime_tp.cc
- runtime/logging/structured_events.cc
- runtime/tests/config_resolution_test.cc

Reviewer notes
- This PR intentionally keeps guardrails minimal and reversible. We should avoid embedding long-term policy here; once ENG-4824/ENG-4826 land broadly, we can revisit whether any of these should become defaults (or be removed).

---
Conversation (selected)

Sofia Ivanova (review): I like the direction. Two concerns: (1) make sure prefill_queue_soft_limit doesn’t affect non-TP replicas; (2) please document precedence when both per-model and per-cluster overrides exist.

Julian Moore (author): Good call. I’ve gated the entire block on tp_world_size > 1 and added a precedence test + comment in loader.cc.

Rafael Mendes (review): From SRE perspective, can we get a metric that tells us the flag is actually active on the replica? Also, can we include a log line with resolved values so oncall doesn’t have to grep config dumps.

Julian Moore (author): Added runtime_tp_guardrails_enabled gauge and a structured init event with resolved caps.

Noah Patel (review): The max_prefill_batch_tokens default might be too aggressive for long-context customers. Can we (a) make it explicit that this is a canary mitigation and (b) allow an override without disabling the rest of the guardrails?

Julian Moore (author): Yes—each cap is overrideable independently. The guardrails defaults only apply when the value is unset. Added config docs and an example.

Aisha Bello (review): Please include label(s) or tag(s) in metrics to break down rejections by reason so we can alert on pathological rejection loops.

Julian Moore (author): Added reason label (queue_full, prefill_tokens_cap, decode_concurrency_cap).

Connor O'Brien (release): Once merged, I’ll wire this into the runtime 1.19 canary checklist and ensure we have a rollback step (disable flag) in the runbook.

---
CI
- build-and-unit (linux) ✅
- runtime-integration-tests ✅
- lint/config-schema ✅
- perf-smoke (staging) ✅

Merge
Merged via squash on 2025-03-03.

Follow-ups
- Coordinate enablement window + cluster list with SRE (ENG-4829)
- Validate impact in perf-canary TP stress scenarios (ENG-4828)
- If rejection rate is high, consider dynamic caps keyed off observed queueing/heartbeat (out of scope here)
Adds feature-flagged TP guardrails that cap prefill/decode concurrency and batch sizing to reduce likelihood of TP stalls during rollout of deeper scheduler/NCCL fixes. No behavior change unless enabled via runtime.tp.guardrails.v1 or per-cluster overrides.

payload.body:
Motivation: As part of the FP8/INT8 benchmarking sprint (ENG-7424), we need deterministic and safe selection of the INT8 GEMM path. Prior to this PR, INT8 could be requested via quantization config, but dispatch was overly optimistic and would attempt INT8 kernels for shapes/alignments that the backend can’t handle reliably across SKUs, leading to either correctness failures (rare) or silent perf cliffs due to internal reformatting.

What this PR does: Implements explicit INT8 matmul dispatch rules, shape constraints, and a transparent fallback to baseline kernels when the INT8 path is unsupported. This is intentionally conservative; we can widen support after the benchmark matrix validates additional regimes.

Dispatch rules (high level): (1) Only consider INT8 GEMM on supported GPU arch (sm80+). (2) Require weight-only INT8 layout to be present (prepacked/registered) and runtime activation to be INT8-enabled via quantization profile. (3) Enforce shape/alignment guardrails: K must be a multiple of 32, N must be a multiple of 8, and the activation/weight pointers must be 16B-aligned (to avoid slow paths). (4) Enforce a minimum tile utilization threshold (avoid INT8 for tiny GEMMs where packing/launch overhead dominates); default threshold is (M*N) >= 4096, configurable via an internal knob for benchmarking.

Fallback behavior: If any guardrail fails, we fall back to the existing baseline GEMM (fp16/bf16 as previously selected) and record a structured fallback reason for benchmarking and later heuristics work. Fallback is non-fatal and does not change numerics relative to current behavior.

New metadata/debugging: Adds a small, structured annotation to the benchmark artifact metadata to help interpret “INT8 requested but not used” cases. This includes kernel_mode_selected={int8|baseline} and fallback_reason={arch_unsupported|shape_k|shape_n|alignment|missing_prepack|too_small}.

Correctness/testing: Adds unit tests that compare INT8 GEMM outputs against the baseline reference for a shape sweep that includes both supported and intentionally-unsupported shapes. For supported shapes, we validate within INT8 expected tolerance (and explicitly validate we don’t NaN/Inf). For unsupported shapes, tests assert that we take the fallback path and match baseline bit-for-bit (since INT8 is not executed).

Illustrative snippet (dispatch guardrails):
- can_use_int8 = (sm >= 80) && (K % 32 == 0) && (N % 8 == 0) && aligned16(activations) && aligned16(weights) && has_prepacked_int8(weights_id) && (M*N >= min_mn_threshold)
- if !can_use_int8: return baseline_gemm(fallback_reason)

Performance notes: This PR does not claim a speedup by itself; it makes benchmark runs interpretable and prevents outliers caused by accidental slow paths. Early spot checks on H100 show reduced variance when sweeping common hidden sizes because unsupported shapes no longer attempt INT8 and then internally repack.

Rollout/compatibility: No default behavior change unless INT8 mode is enabled via quantization profile/flags. The fallback path is designed to be safe for production rollout behind the existing kernel-mode gating.

Links: Linear ENG-7424 (INT8 matmul integration + correctness fallbacks), ENG-7422 (harness updates). Related PRs in the sprint: pr-19827 (FP8 attention integration behind flag), pr-19863 (kernel autoselect heuristics).
Hiro Tanaka (review): Guardrails look good. Can we make the fallback reason visible in perf artifacts? Otherwise matrix triage will be painful when INT8 silently drops to baseline.
Grace Kim (author): Added fallback_reason + kernel_mode_selected to artifact metadata (see runtime/bench/artifacts/metadata_writer.cc) and included in JSON output. Also added a counter dimensioned by fallback_reason for internal runs (not exported to customer metrics).
Rina Kobayashi (review): The alignment requirement is correct, but please make sure we don’t hard-fail when activation pointers aren’t aligned (some callers might not guarantee it).
Grace Kim (author): Yep—alignment is a guardrail only; we fall back to baseline and record fallback_reason=alignment. Added a unit test that forces misalignment and asserts baseline is used.
Noah Patel (review): The min (M*N) threshold seems arbitrary; can we at least make it configurable for bench so we can explore? Also please add comments explaining why 4096.
Grace Kim (author): Added an internal config knob runtime.int8_gemm_min_mn (default 4096) with a comment referencing launch/packing overhead from microbench. Bench harness can override via config file/env.
Claire Dubois (review): Correctness tests: please include K%32 edge and N%8 edge cases, and verify we don’t accidentally run INT8 for those shapes.
Grace Kim (author): Added explicit test cases for (K=...+16) and (N=...+4) and assertions that fallback_reason matches shape_k/shape_n and baseline path is taken.
Hiro Tanaka (approval): Approved. This should unblock clean matrix runs for INT8 while we refine heuristics.
Internal-only: Adds INT8 GEMM dispatch guardrails + safe fallback to baseline kernels when unsupported (shape/alignment/arch). No behavior change unless INT8 mode enabled via existing quantization config/flags.
payload.title: INT8 matmul dispatch rules + shape guardrails with baseline fallback

payload.body:
Motivation: We see repeated bursts and predictable weekly/diurnal patterns per-route that make static SLO thresholds noisy (false positives during predictable peaks, and missed regressions during troughs). Existing per-route percentiles don't account for seasonality and multimodal request shapes (short prompts vs long multi-turn sessions), which leads to noisy alerts and manual tuning. This PR introduces a lightweight baseline generator that decomposes per-route token-cost and latency time series into seasonal + trend + residual components, and a complementary request-shape clustering pipeline so we compute baselines and alert thresholds per route x shape instead of a single global route threshold.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds a seasonal-trend decomposition service (stl-lite) that runs incremental updates on per-route per-hour rollups and emits a stable baseline median and a seasonal amplitude metric. The algorithm is a compact STL-inspired decomposition optimized for streaming rollups (low memory, O(n) incremental).
- Introduces request-shape fingerprinting (prompt_length_bucket, kv_cache_hit_rate_bucket, streaming_tokens_flag, model_variant) and a clustering stage that assigns a route request to a small integer cluster id (0..N-1). Clustering is done by mini-batch k-means on compact sketch features with daily re-fit.
- Calibrator component that computes adaptive alert thresholds per (route,shape_cluster) using robust quantiles of the residual distribution combined with a sigmoid smoothing factor that prevents alerts on short, transient spikes. Calibration parameters are stored in the config store and surfaced to Alerting and Console.
- Low-cardinality metric exports and trace enrichment: emits aggregated histograms keyed by route and cluster id (rwi.route.shape.histogram) and annotates top-level spans with shape tags (rwi.route.shape_cluster) for downstream joins. To avoid cardinality explosion we keep cluster ids dense and only enable shape tags for routes with >100 requests/day by default.
- Console additions: new dashboard panels (Route Shape Explorer, Clustered Baseline Overview, Residual Anomaly Streams) and an alert tuning UI that exposes the calibrator's sigmoid and quantile parameters per route.

Why this is different: Rather than raising global per-route thresholds or trying to tune many static alerts, this approach models predictable seasonality and the multimodal structure of traffic so alerts can be both more sensitive to true regressions and less noisy. The design intentionally minimizes cardinality and CPU overhead so it is safe to roll out as a tenant-facing feature.

Implementation notes:
- New service: observations/calibrator (go). Uses a streaming rollup input (hourly route x cluster rollups) and writes baseline rows to telemetry.baselines (compact protobuf payload).
- New metrics: rwi_route_shape_bucket (histogram labels: route, cluster_id), rwi_baseline_median_tokens (gauge), rwi_baseline_seasonal_amp (gauge), rwi_calibrator_score (gauge).
- Tracing: top-level server span now includes tags: route.shape_cluster (int), route.shape_signature (hash). Only added when route sampling flag is enabled to protect cardinality.
- Safe defaults and feature flags: feature gate observability.route_shape_clustering=false by default. Canary rollout configured in infra/defaults.yaml (10% tenants, 4-hour ramp).

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for the STL-lite decomposition (edge cases: sparse hours, daylight savings transitions) and for clustering stability (minibatch seed determinism).
- Integration tests: simulated workloads with two synthetic routes (short-chat vs long-batch) validate per-cluster baselines and expected alert suppression on seasonal peaks.
- Performance: local profiling shows the calibrator service uses <5% CPU on a c4-large equivalent with the default 10k-route config. Metric cardinality increases were measured <2.3% in a 2-week canary.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag.
2) Enable for 10% tenants (canary group) for 72 hours and monitor rwi_calibrator_score distributions and SLO alert counts.
3) If stable, ramp to 50% and enable dashboard UI in read-only mode.
4) After 2 weeks of stable behavior, flip write-enable so calibrator can update alert thresholds and expose full UI.

Backward compat and migration:
- No breaking API changes. Baseline rows are additive and ignored by older services.
- Migration job included (tools/migrate/compact_baselines) to backfill 30 days of baseline statistics for existing routes. Backfill is optional but recommended for teams enabling the calibrator.

Related work: Linear: ENG-2049, SRE-778. See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2049/route-shape-clustering-and-seasonal-baselines (internal link).

Checklist: implemented code, unit + integration tests, migration script, console panels, feature flag, changelog entry, performance safety review signed off.

Arjun Patel: Nice end-to-end. A few nitpicks: can we cap seasonal amplitude so a runaway route doesn't push thresholds too high? Also please add more metrics around calibration failure/retries.
Maya Chen (author): Added amplitude cap and two new health metrics (calibrator.up and calibrator.recent_backfills). Updated tests to cover amplitude cap.
Leah Kim: Please document how cluster ids are stable across daily refits. Concerned about alert churn if cluster mapping flips frequently.
Maya Chen: Cluster assignment stabilized via hashed seed + drift smoothing; added explanation and an instrumented metric cluster.reassign_rate.
Diego Morales: Verified console panels render correctly in chrome and firefox. Approving once CI is green. 
(approved)

Context: Recent incident analysis (ENG-2219) showed replay windows and header leakage allowed cross-operator correlation of residency assertions. This PR implements two complementary defenses: 1) nonce-bound service authentication: session- and request-level nonces are bound into KMS envelopes and RBAC v2 decision checks so any replayed KMS token or operator lease that does not present a matching nonce is rejected; 2) residency-opaque headers: residency assertions are encoded as opaque, peppered hashes when forwarded to downstream services to avoid exposing raw region identifiers in logs or telemetry while preserving verifiability at the gateway.

Goals: reduce auditable replay risk, limit residency attribute exposure in transit, and add minimal compatibility shims for Private/VPC deployments.

What this PR does: - Implements a nonce middleware that issues, validates, and caches short-lived nonces tied to a service session. Nonces are emitted into KMS envelope metadata and into a per-request audit token. - Extends KMS proxy to include nonce in encryption context and validate nonce signature on unwrap as an additional gate. - Adds an RBAC v2 policy check (opt-in per-role) that requires nonce binding for operator leases and ephemeral roles. This prevents elevation via replayed operator tokens. - Introduces a ResidencyOpaqueHeader generator (X-Residency-Opaque) that produces a peppered HMAC over the residency claim; the raw claim remains available to the policy engine in the control plane but downstream routes only see the opaque value. - Adds audit-replay-detector that records nonce sequence numbers in an append-only index and rejects duplicates within a configured window; metrics exported: audit.replay.detected, nonce.cache.hits/misses, residency.header.generated. - Updates docs and migration notes for operators running Private installer: toggles to enable/disable header obfuscation and the RBAC-Nonce requirement are in configuration with safe defaults (disabled for older clusters).

Checklist: - [x] Nonce middleware implementation and unit tests - [x] KMS envelope changes and integration tests - [x] RBAC v2 opt-in validator and policy examples - [x] Audit replay detector and metrics - [x] Docs and migration guide - [x] Backward compatibility gates for older control planes

Compatibility/migration: Enabled behind feature flag `security.nonce_binding.v1` and `security.residency_opaque_headers`. Operators upgrading from <2024.8 should coordinate: turn on flags in canary first. Migration docs: docs/security/nonce-auth.md.

Related: ENG-2219, SEC-104, SUP-342.

Notes: design intentionally avoids changing user-visible API payloads except for adding an optional X-Residency-Opaque header (downstream compatible); nonces are internal tokens and never exposed to customer request bodies.

Kara Nguyen: Please add metrics for nonce issuance rate and an opt-out config at the namespace level — otherwise we risk noisy defaults in multi-tenant control planes.
Ethan Patel: Added metrics (audit.nonce.issued) and added namespace opt-out in the second patch — see auth/middleware/nonce_auth.go lines 120-153.
Jamal Rivers: Can we ensure that the KMS providers that don't support arbitrary encryption context keys degrade gracefully? Suggest a compatibility shim in kms/proxy.
Ethan Patel: KMS shim added — it falls back to signed assertion header when encryption context is unsupported. Documented in migration notes.
Sofie Martin: Tests are failing intermittently on CI e2e with Private installer; looks like timing on cache eviction. Please add deterministic sleeps or configurable TTL for tests.
Ethan Patel: Fixed flakiness by making test TTL configurable and reducing reliance on wall-clock sleeps; added deterministic clock in tests.
Kara Nguyen: LGTM after minor doc nits resolved.
Sofie Martin: Approved (+1)

payload.body:
Motivation:
High-throughput short-sequence workloads show suboptimal utilization due to misaligned memory access patterns and KV-cache fragmentation when using small per-request prefixes. This PR introduces a SIMD-friendly transpose microkernel and a dynamic KV-tiling allocator that cooperates with the continuous batcher to reduce per-token latency and improve GPU occupancy.

What this changes (single continuous description):
- Add a unified simd_transpose kernel (CUDA+AVX fallback) optimized for small-head-count Q/K/V layouts. The kernel packs Q/K into transposed tiles to enable contiguous loads for the subsequent fused attention path.
- Implement dynamic_kv_tiler: runtime component that reserves contiguous KV slabs when requests share prefix shapes, allows coalesced KV writes, and prefers in-place appends to reduce copying. The tiler exposes a reservation API to the scheduler.
- Update continuous_batcher to consult the tiler when forming batches; prefer grouping requests by prefix-length and head-width to maximize tiling benefits without violating per-request latency SLOs.
- Add kernel_registry heuristics to select the simd_transpose+fused-attn path when sequence length <= 256 and head_dim <= 64.
- Tests and benchmarks: microbenchmarks for the transpose kernel, integration benchmark comparing end-to-end per-token latency for chat workloads, and new unit tests for the tiler reservation edge cases.

Checklist:
- [x] Kernel implementation and CPU fallback
- [x] Runtime tiler with reservation/eviction policy
- [x] Scheduler integration and guardrails for SLOs
- [x] Benchmarks and unit tests
- [x] Documentation: performance note + guidance in docs/perf/kv-tiling.md

Performance highlights (internal microbench):
- Short-seq chat (avg seq 32, head_dim 64): 13-18% p99 latency reduction; 25% increase in token throughput under steady-state small-batch workloads.
- Long-seq cases unchanged due to kernel selection heuristics.
- Memory overhead: tiler increases peak GPU allocation by ~3-5% for workloads that heavily coalesce, but reduces overall memcpy overhead significantly.

Compatibility and safety:
- Feature gated behind kernel registry flags; default behavior preserves previous scheduling unless heuristics active.
- No changes to on-disk model artifacts.
- The tiler uses a soft reservation model with timeouts to avoid starvation; eviction stats are exposed to metrics.

Related: ENG-1973 (kv-coalescing-performance), ENG-2011 (continuous-batcher-upgrades), SUP-4421 (customer report of high p99 on short-chat).

Notes for reviewers: please focus on eviction correctness under concurrent reservations and the registry heuristic thresholds.

Diego Ramirez: Please add more comments describing the eviction heuristics; it's not obvious what happens when reservations overlap and memory is tight.

Aisha Kapoor: Added inline comments and an explanatory section in docs/perf/kv-tiling.md; eviction policy is LRU-ish with time-based fallback, and we expose stats for monitoring.

Marta Novak: Bench numbers look promising. Can we add a regression test that simulates frequent short prefixes to catch allocation thrash?

Aisha Kapoor: Added a unit benchmark test that runs a synthetic chat pattern with randomized short prefixes (tests/attn/transposed_kernel_bench.py). Also added an integration job to the CI bench matrix.

Elliot Chen: CI had one flaky bench timeout on initial run; re-ran and green. I approve pending a small nit about header include order.

Aisha Kapoor: Fixed header order and squashed the commits. Diego approved the final patch.

Lower p99 latency and higher token throughput for short-sequence chat workloads via a SIMD-friendly transpose kernel and dynamic KV tiling; opt-in via kernel registry heuristics. See docs/perf/kv-tiling.md for guidance.

Adds a token chronicle aggregator service that produces compact per-invocation token rollups and a proactive alert conductor that dampens noisy token-cost/latency alerts by applying adaptive suppression and guided fallback rules.
What: Introduces a new token chronicle aggregator that creates compact, time-bucketed per-invocation token rollups (chronicles) and a Proactive Alert Conductor (PAC) that consumes those chronicles to apply dynamic alert suppression, escalation scoring, and automated fallback recommendations. Why: Long-tail token-cost and microburst latency alerts were generating noisy paging and obscuring genuine regressions. Rather than simply coarsening sampling, this PR builds a server-side rollup layer that preserves important signal (phase breakdowns, kv-hydration events) while enabling deterministic alert orchestration. Design: chronicle-aggregator service ingests sampled spans + token-phase annotations and emits per-invocation chronicle keys, a compact delta-encoding of token counts by phase, and an embedding of prompt-shape fingerprint. The PAC subscribes to the chronicle topic and maintains a short-term history per route/tenant to compute an alert score and suppression token using exponential decay and seasonality smoothing. The PAC also produces fallback recommendations (route to cheaper model variant, adjust batching window, or pin KV-cache warmup) via an action API consumed by the routing policy engine. Backwards compatibility: Chronicle records are produced alongside existing spans; no upstream agent changes required. Rollout: 1) deploy aggregator behind a feature flag; 2) enable PAC in read-only mode (record-only) for two days to validate signals; 3) enable suppression with conservative thresholds, then incrementally increase aggressiveness by route. Testing: unit tests for rollup correctness, e2e synthetic replay tests to validate suppression behavior, canary on staging with live traffic. Monitoring: dashboards added for chronicle ingestion latency, chronicle size distribution, PAC suppression ratio, and false-suppression sampler. Security: chronicles are pseudonymized for non-admin teams and respect tenant scoping. Linked work: ENG-8273. Checklist: [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] dashboard panels [x] docs update [x] migration/rollout plan. Commits summary: "init: add chronicle aggregator service and proto schema", "add: chronicle writer and delta-encoder", "add: PAC engine and suppression policy DSL", "test: synthetic replay harness for chronicle->PAC", "infra: topic + RBAC + helm chart updates", "docs: observability/chronicle and PAC guide". Changed areas: server/observability/chronicle_aggregator/*, server/observability/pac/*, infra/helm/observability-charts/*, webapp/dashboards/chronicle-overview.json, tests/observability/replaybench/*, docs/observability/chronicle.md. Review conversation highlights: "Liam Chen: Can we ensure chronicle payload remains <= 2KB for the 99.9th percentile?" "Aisha: yes, delta-encoder + shard-level truncation keeps the payload under 1.6KB in our synthetic worst case; added a unit to enforce size" "Priya Menon: PAC suppression must be explainable to oncall; include action trace and reason codes" "Aisha: added human-readable reason codes and a UI link to the chronicle for each suppression event" "Diego Alvarez: verify no signal loss for phase boundaries when using delta encoding" "Aisha: added a phase-boundary-preserving tag and test coverage" CI summary: build (pass), unit tests (pass), integration replay (pass), lint (pass), e2e-canary (pass). Merge: merged via squash on 2024-11-14 after approvals from all reviewers. Rollout notes: initial rollout to staging on 2024-11-10, read-only PAC observed on 2024-11-12, suppression enabled 2024-11-13 for 10% of traffic, global enable 2024-11-14. Post-merge actions: monitor suppression false-positive rate, iterate suppression thresholds, add model-variant auto-fallback tuning to Redwood Optimize as follow-up.

Aisha Kapoor: yes, delta-encoder + shard-level truncation keeps the payload under 1.6KB in our synthetic worst case; added a unit to enforce size
Priya Menon: PAC suppression must be explainable to oncall; include action trace and reason codes
Aisha Kapoor: added human-readable reason codes and a UI link to the chronicle for each suppression event
Diego Alvarez: verify no signal loss for phase boundaries when using delta encoding
Aisha Kapoor: added a phase-boundary-preserving tag and test coverage

Summary: Add a lightweight per-model backpressure collector and a compact 'peek latency' sparkline for route dashboards to surface transient queueing without exploding cardinality. Motivation: operators are seeing noisy SLOs from short-lived queue spikes that correlate with heavy fanout prompts and prefetch bursts. Existing token-latency rollups miss microbursts and existing queue metrics are too coarse at model level. This change introduces: 1) a per-model queue-depth meter exposed as a histogram with device-level tags (model,region,instance_type); 2) a peek-latency sampler that collects sub-100ms percentiles for the head-of-line request path and exposes a compact sparkline JSON panel for dashboards; 3) alert attenuation and a 30s quiet-window policy that reduces pager churn for bursts under configured throughput thresholds. What changed (high level): - observability/collector/backpressure_collector.go: new collector with bounded in-memory reservoir to avoid cardinality explosion - observability/metrics/schema.yml: new metric definitions (model_queue_depth, peek_latency_ms_count, peek_latency_ms_sum) - observability/dashboards/peek-latency-sparklines.json: dashboard panel definition (compact, sparkline + lightweight tooltip linking to trace) - observability/alerting/attenuation_rules.yaml: staged attenuation rules and quiet-window configuration - telemetry/testing/synthetic_prefetch_replay.go: synthetic runner used to validate attenuation logic under bursty workloads Implementation notes: - The collector attaches to the request router's admission path and samples the head request of every 1 in N windows (configurable via env REDWOOD_PEEK_SAMPLE_RATE). Sampled items include minimal context (route, model, queue_depth, seq_len_bin) and are kept in a 2048-entry ring to bound memory. - Metrics use OTel histograms with explicit bucket set optimized for short-lived queue depths (0-64, powers of two) to avoid high-cardinality tagging. - The sparkline panel renders a compact 60-point series (1s resolution by default) and includes an action link that opens the sampled trace in the trace UI for deeper inspection. - The attenuation rules implement a two-stage suppressor: first a low-sensitivity suppression for bursts < 5x baseline and <30s, then an auto-escalate path if the burst sustains or correlates with increased error-rate. Testing performed: - Unit tests for collector boundary conditions and sample eviction (observability/collector/backpressure_collector_test.go) - End-to-end synthetic replay validation (telemetry/testing/replaybench) that exercises 10k requests/sec for 60s with prefetch patterns - Load bench in perf-canary with YAML config used to calibrate quiet-window thresholds Rollout plan: - Canary on staging and one small prod shard for 48h - Monitor: model_queue_depth p50/p99, peek_latency spike count, alert firing rate - Gradual rollout across regions with feature flag REDWOOD_OBS_BACKPRESSURE=on Related: Linear ENG-4621 (reduce alert churn from microbursts), ENG-4710 (dashboard compact units). Checklist: - [x] Collector implementation - [x] Dashboard panels - [x] Attenuation rules + tests - [x] Documentation snippets in docs/observability/backpressure.md - [x] Perf canary run and threshold calibration Manual verification steps: 1) Deploy with feature flag set on a single shard. 2) Run telemetry/testing/synthetic_prefetch_replay with short bursts and confirm peek_latency sparkline shows sub-second spikes. 3) Trigger a sustained load to verify attenuation step-up opens normal alert path. Links: - Dashboards: observability/dashboards/peek-latency-sparklines.json - Playbook: docs/ops/alert-attenuation-playbook.md
Added per-model backpressure and queue-depth metrics; new compact dashboard panels (peek latency sparklines); alert attenuation rules to reduce churn for transient bursts.
Daniel Kim (2026-02-22): Please add a note about cardinality limits — good to see you capped the reservoir. - replied: added config note and test for eviction.
Luis Fernandez (2026-02-24): Attenuation logic looks sensible; please ensure SLI owners are aware of quiet-window defaults. - replied: added docs/ops/alert-attenuation-playbook.md and notified SLI owners.
Maya Chen (2026-02-27): Sparkline panel is compact and loads fast in staging. approved (LGTM).
If you see suppressed alerts after rollout, check attenuation_rules.yaml and the attenuation meter (observability/attenuation/suppressor_status). Use the replaybench to reproduce transient bursts.

Context: Customers frequently have mixed traffic shapes (short prompts vs long mult-turn chats) which single global defaults struggle to optimize. This PR adds a lightweight shape-aware defaults engine plus a safe CLI-driven quantization rollout/rollback flow that ties into unit-econ simulation and canary routing. Motivation: reduce per-token cost and tail latency regressions by automatically selecting batch and cache presets based on observed request shape, while making quantized rollouts reversible and observable. Summary of changes: 1) Shape classifier that derives request shape fingerprints (short/medium/long, seq-delta distribution) and maps them to recommended batch sizes, cache TTL, and KV prefill heuristics. 2) Presets-as-code: a new tenant-level config schema (yaml) allowing shape->preset mappings and an import CLI to seed tenant defaults. 3) Quant rollout CLI: `rw quant promote|canary|rollback` that stages quantized model variants with traffic weights, automatically creates a canary route, and wires unit-econ simulator runs to validate cost/latency tradeoffs before ramp. 4) Safety controls: automatic regression detector (simple latency + quality thresholds) that will rollback a canary if SLOs or unit-econ deltas exceed thresholds. 5) Observability hooks: emits new telemetry namespaces (prefill.presets, quant.rollout) and a short-lived debug trace for canaries. 6) Tests: unit tests for the classifier, e2e smoke test for CLI flow, and a simulated workload test that exercises the canary rollback path. Backwards compatibility: defaults are opt-in; existing tenant configs remain unchanged until an operator imports presets. Linear/jira: ENG-4219 (shape-aware defaults), ENG-4301 (quant-rollout CLI), SUP-9821 (customer support follow-up). Checklist: - [x] Shape classifier implementation and docs - [x] Presets-as-code schema + import CLI - [x] Quant rollout + rollback implementation - [x] Unit-econ simulation hookup for canary validation - [x] CI tests added - [x] Integration tests for rollback path - [x] Docs snippet in console runbook (deferred to a follow-up PR for full docs)
Add shape-aware tenant presets for batching/caching; introduce `rw quant rollback` CLI and safe canary rollout for quantized model variants. No behavioral API changes; opt-in via tenant defaults or CLI.
Ethan Liu: Nice separation of concerns. Two asks: (1) make the fingerprint deterministic across SDK versions (add schema version), (2) ensure telemetry keys are low-cardinality. Please add tests for schema versioning.
Priya Shah: Added schema version field and unit tests for fingerprint stability. Telemetry keys moved under prefill.presets.{bucket}. Kept cardinality to 3 buckets.
Mariana Costa: CLI UX looks good. Request: expose a dry-run that only runs the unit-econ sim and prints summary without touching routing. Also add clearer error messages if canary creation fails due to quota.

payload.body:
Motivation: In the last two oncall incidents (SUP-1182) we saw eviction+fallback-induced oscillations when a regional overload triggered aggressive tenant evictions and immediate rejoin attempts. That interaction caused repeated circuit flips and elevated 95th P50/P95 latency for affected tenants.

This PR introduces two complementary changes to reduce oscillation and provide smoother degradation behavior: 1) an Adaptive Eviction Smoother in the runtime scheduler which low-pass filters short-lived eviction pressure spikes and spaces eviction actions across a configurable window; 2) a Probabilistic Fallback Heuristic in the control plane which gates immediate regional failover by probabilistically delaying fallbacks for low-priority routes and gradually ramping fallback probability based on sustained error/latency signals.

What changed: single continuous description of design + checklist below. Key goals: preserve SLO enforcement semantics for critical tenants, reduce oscillations for medium/low priority tenants, avoid global fail-open.

Design summary: - Eviction smoother: exponential moving average over eviction pressure (evict_score) with tunable alpha, plus an eviction budget token bucket to ensure we never starve necessary evictions. The smoother adds hysteresis to node-level decisions so short spikes don't cause mass drains. - Probabilistic fallback: new control-plane decision layer that takes current SLO breach signal, regional capacity state, and route priority to compute a fallback probability p(t). For p < 1 we introduce a randomized short delay before triggering fallback, and we back off probability if the target region is itself at capacity. - Operator knobs: smoothing window, token refill rate, min/max fallback probability per priority class, and emergency override for oncall.

Checklist: - [x] Add smoother implementation in runtime scheduler - [x] Wire smoother into SLO enforcer path - [x] Implement probabilistic fallback heuristic in control plane - [x] Add unit and deterministic integration tests for hysteresis + probability ramping - [x] Add a small ops doc describing knobs and recommended defaults - [x] Hotfix migration plan: default to conservative smoothing (safe by default) and enable rollback via feature flag.

Testing: unit tests for statistical properties (moving average behavior) and deterministic integration tests that simulate node pressure ramps. QA ran 1h soak in staging with synthetic spike load; observed 48% fewer full-node drains and 30% lower rejoin churn. Telemetry updates added to track evict_score, smoother_value, fallback_probability.

Risk and rollback: conservative defaults minimize risk; feature flag gate added at control plane and runtime. Rollback is immediate by toggling flags and a reversion patch is ready.

Related: addresses SUP-1182 and reduces noise observed in ENG-3412.

Priya Menon (reviewer): Can we prove that the smoothing window won't unreasonably delay required evictions for high-priority tenants? Please add a token bucket that guarantees minimal eviction rate.
Marco Alvarez (author): Added eviction token bucket (runtime/scheduler/eviction_smoother.go). Token refill is configurable and defaults to 1 eviction per 30s for critical classes. See added unit tests that verify the bound.
Samir Gupta (reviewer): The probabilistic fallback introduces nondeterminism; ensure tests are deterministic and add telemetry for probability decisions so we can debug in prod.
Marco Alvarez (author): deterministic tests added using fixed RNG seed and a test-only injector. Telemetry counters: fallback_probability_histogram, fallback_decision_sample (route_id, p, result).
Jae Park (reviewer): Suggest tightening default fallback probability ramp for medium routes; current default seemed aggressive in staging runs.
Marco Alvarez (author): Lowered medium priority ramp slope and updated docs/ops recommendations. Re-ran staging soak; improved churn metrics.
Priya Menon (approval): Approving after token-bucket and telemetry additions. Observability looks adequate.
Samir Gupta (approval): LGTM. CI reruns clean.
payload.title: Adaptive eviction smoother and probabilistic fallback heuristic to reduce oscillation during regional overloads

payload.body:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets need predictable throughput guarantees while allowing short-lived surges without destabilizing headroom. Current soft-burst banks react too aggressively and produce oscillations across tenants under correlated spikes. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: 1) a FlightReservationScheduler (FRS) that staggers short-term reservation windows and softly enforces watermarks to smooth admission; 2) a CommitmentTracer telemetry pipeline that records reservation lifecycles and observed fulfillment ratios for per-tenant SLAs.

Design summary: The FRS implements a lightweight slotting layer that converts burst requests into time-boxed reservations (flights). Each flight carries a requested throughput and an expected duration. The scheduler uses a reservoir smoothing algorithm to allocate flights into the existing warm pool and reserved headroom, prioritizing long-running commitments but allowing short flights to be slotted opportunistically. When capacity is tight, the FRS will downscale newly scheduled flights by an adaptive factor and emit a suggested fallback model variant via routing metadata. The CommitmentTracer is a non-blocking collector that annotates tenant traces with: reservation_id, scheduled_slots, actual_tokens_served, fulfillment_ratio, and backoff_reason if any. This ties directly into console dashboards and alert rules.

Checklist: - [x] Scheduler core algorithm and unit tests - [x] Non-blocking telemetry collector + protobuf schema - [x] Integration test for a 200-tenant synthetic workload with correlated spikes - [x] Console dashboard draft panels (PR to redwood-docs coming next) - [x] Graceful rollback path: feature flag + conservative default (disabled for 1 week in prod while we monitor)

Backward compatibility and rollout: The feature is guarded behind runtime.feature.flight_reservations (off by default). Existing reservation APIs are unchanged; the scheduler consumes the same reservation objects and annotates them. If the scheduler rejects a flight due to lack of capacity, it returns an HTTP 429 with a structured JSON payload containing fallback.suggested_variant and fallback.retry_after_seconds. Gradual rollout plan: enable in staging for 48h, then 10% traffic in prod, 50% after verification, full enable.

Benchmarks and results: On a 64-GPU dedicated cluster running our synthetic spike profile, median p95 tail latency for high-priority tenants improved by 18% compared to the current soft-burst bank (from 310ms -> 255ms) while overall average utilization increased by 6%. Worst-case fairness deviation (measured as 95th percentile of per-tenant throughput delta) dropped from 22% to 9%. See commit messages for raw numbers.

Security & audit: CommitmentTracer events are sanitized; only hashed tenant identifiers are emitted in non-prod telemetry. No new secrets introduced.

Related work: Links to Linear tickets: ENG-4982 (autoscaler smoothing follow-up), ENG-5077 (commitment telemetry roadmap). Jira SUP-229 notes an incident where correlated spikes caused cascading warm pool depletions — this PR addresses that class of failure.

Migration notes: Operators can opt-out by setting runtime.feature.flight_reservations=false. If enabled, monitor console -> Reservations -> Tracer Fulfillment panel.

Files changed (high level): additions to autoscaler service, scheduler module, a small change to routing metadata, new telemetry protobufs, and unit/integration tests.

This PR is intentionally conservative: the core algorithm is optimized for predictability and observability over aggressive packing. Future follow-ups will add probabilistic preemption and inter-cluster spillover.
Evan Brooks (2025-01-13): Can we clarify how the adaptive downscale factor is computed? The math in flight_scheduler.go is hard to follow. Suggest adding a short docstring and a unit test for a degenerate case.
Maya Patel (2025-01-13): Reply: Added docstring and expanded unit tests to cover degenerate reservoir sizes. The formula is now broken into two helper functions with descriptive names.
Lin Zhou (2025-01-15): Regarding telemetry volume: will CommitmentTracer create a high-cardinality explosion during multi-tenant load? We should sample or aggregate before emitting to external pipelines.
Maya Patel (2025-01-15): Reply: CommitmentTracer emits aggregated fulfillment buckets by default and falls back to sampling for debug mode. Added comments and a flagized config (telemetry.commitment_tracer.aggregation=true).
Priya Nair (2025-01-17): Safety question: if FRS schedules flights that cannot be satisfied because of a sudden GPU eviction, do we attempt retries or immediately emit a rejection? Need to ensure we don't double-charge reserved tokens.
Maya Patel (2025-01-17): Reply: On sudden node eviction we mark flights as failed with backoff_reason=node_eviction. We do not re-charge tenant credits; instead we surface a compensation ticket in the console for operator review. Added tests to assert no double-charge behavior.

Motivation: We frequently see tenants override defaults in a way that regresses unit economics (higher per-token cost or latency spikes) after model/quant rollouts. This PR introduces a small, auditable path to import 'unit-econ templates' as code and a lightweight quant sanity checker that runs as part of CI and as an on-demand validation step in the Console. The goal is to reduce manual error when applying tenant defaults and to catch quantization-induced quality drift before rollouts.

What this PR adds (high level):
- CLI importer: `redwood unit-econ import <yaml>` which merges template YAML into the tenant-defaults store with validation and dry-run support.
- Template schema: a validated YAML schema (examples under cfg/defaults/unit_econ_templates.yaml) for batching, cache hints, and quant modality suggestions.
- Quant sanity checker: a small Go service (server/quant/sanity_checker.go) that executes a bounded simulation (synthetic micro-inference) comparing FP32 baseline outputs to candidate quantized model outputs using configurable tolerances; reports a quality score and known-failure fingerprints. The checker is plumbed into CI and can be invoked by product rules during a tenant rollout.
- Docs: developer guide for the importer and the sanity checker (docs/unit-econ-importer.md) with examples and recommended thresholds.
- Tests: unit tests for importer validation and an integration smoke harness that exercises the quant checker in a mocked runtime.

Files of note (high level):
- cli/unit_econ/importer.py: CLI entrypoint, validations, and dry-run code path.
- cfg/defaults/unit_econ_templates.yaml: curated seed templates for sandbox and production tiers.
- server/quant/sanity_checker.go: quant comparison runner and summary exporter.
- docs/unit-econ-importer.md: usage and rollout recommendations.
- tests/unit/test_importer.py, tests/integration/test_quant_sanity.py: coverage for core flows.

Checklist: 
- [x] Schema and validator for templates
- [x] CLI import/dry-run path
- [x] Quant sanity checker with pluggable thresholds
- [x] CI integration (see pipeline changes)
- [x] Developer docs and sample templates
- [x] Unit + integration tests

Testing notes and CI: The first CI run surfaced a flaky assertion in the mocked inference harness (tests/integration/test_quant_sanity.py). I tightened the timeout and added a retry around the harness startup; second pipeline run passed. CI checks included: lint, unit-tests (py/go), integration-smoke, telemetry-schema-check. Artifacts contain the sanity_checker report (json) on success.

Migration and rollout plan: The importer is additive and requires opt-in via Console or CLI. Seed templates are non-authoritative—importing writes a tenant-level template draft which must be applied by an operator. The sanity checker is enabled in 'preflight' mode for early rollouts and will block a rollout only if the configured quality score drops below the tenant's safety threshold. We will monitor Console telemetry for template adoption and any denied rollouts for 2 weeks post-merge.

Related: This complements ENG-1734 (unit-econ audits) and ENG-1901 (tenant defaults UI work).
Ethan Park: Can we add telemetry metrics for template import failures and sanity-check scores? We should be able to answer 'how many imports failed validation' and 'distribution of quality scores' before enabling blocking mode.
Priya Ramesh: Added metrics (metrics.import.validation_failures, metrics.quant.sanity_score) and exported them to the telemetry bridge. See server/quant/sanity_checker.go lines ~120 for the exporter.
Maya Lind: The quant checker is great — please make thresholds configurable per-tenant and not hard-coded in cfg. Also add a clear fallback that does NOT block rollouts for tenants with 'non-blocking' mode.
Priya Ramesh: Thresholds are pluggable via tenant defaults now; importer schema includes 'safety.mode = {blocking | advisory}' and 'safety.threshold'. Default is 'advisory' until we flip the Console toggle.
Daniel Ortiz: Tests look good — one nit: reduce the seed template verbosity to avoid leaking internal notes into public docs. Also add a short README in cfg/defaults explaining purpose.
Priya Ramesh: Removed internal notes and added cfg/defaults/README.md explaining template usage and intended audience.

Motivation: Current SLO alert baselines are static and tuned at org-level heuristics which leads to frequent noisy paging for tenants with differing request shapes. This PR implements a historical-weighted baseline recalibration that computes per-tenant SLO baselines by combining short-term signal with an exponential-decayed historical profile (watermarking). It also introduces a low-cost alert fallback: when a high-cardinality metric triggers, we automatically attempt a cheap synthetic SLO replay and lightweight span-sampling probe before escalating to full alerting. The goal is to reduce noise and infra cost while preserving correctness and time-to-detect for genuine regressions. Implementation summary: 1) New baseline engine (observability/slo/baseline_engine.go) that ingests token-latency and per-invocation cost rollups and produces a tenant baseline using configurable decay and weight parameters. 2) Drift correction module (observability/slo/drift_correction.go) that detects systematic baseline shifts and applies a conservative correction factor so that we don't overfit to transient spikes. 3) Low-cost fallback controller (observability/alerts/fallback_controller.py) that, upon threshold crossings, triggers a synthetic replay queue and a sampled KV-warmup trace probe; only if both probes indicate degradation do we open full-investigation alerts. 4) Dashboard for operators (dashboards/slo-recalibration-overview.json) and a small docs page (docs/observability/baseline-tuning.md) describing knobs and recommended presets. 5) Integration test harness (tests/slo_replay_integration_test.go) that runs synthetic replays against the staged baseline. Backwards compatibility: Baseline engine exposes a config flag to opt-in per-tenant recalibration; default rollout is off. Rollout plan: 1) Canary tenants via feature flag for three days with tight telemetry and cost limits. 2) Expand to 20% of tenants and collect alert reduction/loss-of-detection metrics. 3) Global enable if false negative rate < 0.3% and alert volume reduced >= 18%. Testing: unit tests for baseline math and drift correction; integration test for replay-based fallback; local perf bench showing <1.5% latency overhead for sampling probes. Monitoring and observability: new metrics slo.baseline.absolute, slo.baseline.delta, slo.fallback.invocations, slo.fallback.probe_success, slo.drift.detected_count; traces instrumented for fallback decision path with span tags fallback.probe.type and fallback.probe.duration. Configuration knobs: decay.window_days, decay.weight_alpha, fallback.probe_timeout_ms, fallback.probe_sample_rate, synthetic_replay_batch. Security/ops: fallback controller runs under observability service account and respects tenant data-scoping; synthetic replay uses masked prompts to avoid PII egress. Related: ENG-3421 (SLO baseline initiative), ENG-3489 (alert volume reduction).
Ethan Rivera: Nice approach; please add an explicit circuit-breaker to the fallback probe so we don't DDoS model infra during a cascading incident.
Maya Zhang: Added a probe backoff and global rate-limit in fallback_controller.py and updated docs to call out the rate cap.
Priya Desai: Can you quantify expected alert suppression vs false-negative risk in the PR description? Let's add an integration metric.
Maya Zhang: Added integration metrics and updated rollout gating thresholds in the description. See tests/slo_replay_integration_test.go for synthetic replay assertions.
Liam O'Connor: Unit tests look good. CI flaked once on the replay pipeline; reran and all green. Approving.
Release Manager (automation): Please include release_notes file snippet — added as part of this PR.
Introduce per-tenant historical-weighted SLO baselines and a low-cost alert fallback probe. Default off; rollouts gated by feature flag and detection metrics. Reduces noisy alerts and high-cardinality escalation costs.

Motivation: Some customers reported large p99 latency spikes and throughput cliffs on models with irregular head layouts (mixed MQA/GQA variants, non-uniform dim packing) especially under mixed short/long request workloads. Root causes include lane contention in the scheduler and suboptimal kernel selection when attention head dimensions don't align to the chosen implementation. This PR introduces two complementary runtime features: 1) dynamic lane throttling — a lightweight runtime scheduler extension that measures per-lane activation density and throttles long-running lanes to prevent starvation of low-latency short requests; 2) kernel polymorphing — a polymorphic kernel selection layer that chooses between packed/planar/striped attention kernels at call-time using a compact heuristic that accounts for head stride, dim alignment, and per-model quirks. Design summary: Implement a per-device lane scoreboard that tracks recent token counts, head-density histogram, and eviction pressure; the throttler applies soft caps to in-flight tokens per-lane and dynamically rebalances available slots across lanes when variance is high. Kernel polymorphing is implemented as a thin dispatch wrapper in runtime/kernel_dispatch.cpp that probes model metadata (model_head_layout, dim_alignment_hint) and runtime counters (current_batch_shape) and chooses the best kernel variant. To avoid runtime cost we cache decisions per model+shape and invalidate on quantization profile changes. Model-specific quirk table: include entries for Llama (prefer planar at head_dim%64!=0), Mistral (prefer striped kernel for head counts > 32 due to its block attention layout), and Qwen (prefer packed kernel unless MQA detected). KV cache compaction: when throttling triggers, the compactor is invoked to trim inactive KV slabs with conservative heuristics to free memory and reduce eviction churn. Safeguards: feature gated (runtime flags lane_throttle.enabled, kernel_polymorph.enabled); max throttle is configurable and disabled for pinned-capacity Dedicated instances by default. Testing and benchmarking: unit tests for scheduler invariants and kernel selection logic; added perf harness scripts (bench/mixed_short_long.py) that produce the included benchmark outputs. Benchmarks: mixed workload (70% short <32 tokens, 30% long 512 tokens) on g5.12xlarge: Llama-MQA profile: p99 latency reduced from 210ms to 186ms (~11.4%); steady-state throughput up by 15% for MQA-heavy runs; Mistral-8B with mixed heads: p99 reduced 12.2%, throughput +10%. Observability: new metrics lane.throttle.active, lane.eviction_pressure, kernel.decision.cache_hit_rate; added dashboard panels and alerts for throttle activation rate and kernel fallback percent. Rollout plan: 1) land behind feature flags; 2) enable in hosted canary region for redwood and select Dedicated clusters; 3) monitor metrics for 48h; 4) ramp to all-hosted customers. Checklist: - [x] Design doc and perf plan linked in Linear ENG-1824; - [x] Unit + integration tests; - [x] Bench results attached; - [x] Feature flags and config knobs; - [x] Docs stub updated (runtime/flags.md). Known limitations: rare extra kernel dispatch latency when cache miss occurs (cached decision warms within 10 calls); may need tuning for extremely skewed workloads (>95% long). Related: this complements prior KV prefetch work but uses a different mitigation vector aimed at scheduling and kernel selection.
Diego Morales (reviewer): Can you clarify how the throttle interacts with continuous batching? I'm worried about oscillation when short requests arrive in bursts.
Priya Patel (author): The throttler uses exponential smoothing on recent token counts and only adjusts throttle windows every 50ms; continuous batching is given a top-priority slot allocation so short requests see minimal added latency — added a test (scheduler_test.cpp) that simulates bursts to validate stability.
Ava Chen (reviewer): Kernel decision cache looks like it could grow unbounded for exotic shapes; please add an eviction policy.
Priya Patel (author): Added an LRU with max 256 entries per-device and metrics to track cache hit/miss. Also added a size knob kernel.decision.cache_size; see commit b2c9d44.
Samir Gupta (reviewer): Please run the perf harness on the Dedicated config (reserved) as behaviour is different when autoscaling isn't present.
Priya Patel (author): Ran bench on a Dedicated-like cluster and included results in bench output; noted in the body that default is off for pinned Dedicated clusters and added a config to enable it.
Diego Morales (reviewer): Approving pending small nits in comments (variable names and a missing header).
Ava Chen (reviewer): Approved — the perf gains look solid and the rollout plan is conservative.
payload.title: Dynamic lane throttling and kernel polymorphing to mitigate irregular-head performance cliffs
