Motivation: Constrained decoding (CFG/regex backends) and the OpenAI compatibility layer were observing spurious mismatches when streaming responses contained multi-codepoint graphemes (emoji sequences, regional indicators, zero-width-joiner ligatures) or when deterministic Unicode normalization differed between constraint preprocessors and the runtime tokenizer. This caused structured-output validators and tool/function-calling to incorrectly reject partial or final outputs in production.

What I changed: Implemented a Unicode-aware \"lexer proxy\" that sits between the constraint backends (CFG, regex) and the tokenizer/streaming emitter. The proxy normalizes input sequences, exposes grapheme-boundary-aware token spans to the constraint engines, and adds a streaming-safe framing layer so we never emit a partial grapheme that could break a live constraint check. Key behaviors: NFKC normalization option (configurable), grapheme cluster segmentation using the Unicode Grapheme Cluster Boundary algorithm, mapping of grapheme spans to tokenizer token indices, and a small on-the-fly rewrite table for common emoji modifier/ZWJ sequences to maintain stable regex anchors. The proxy is pluggable so existing constraint backends can opt-in with minimal changes.

Why this is different from previous work: Prior PRs focused on tokenizer fallback heuristics and token-edge stitching. This PR resolves correctness at the grapheme/Unicode layer (pre-tokenization), preventing subtle mismatches when clients use regex/CFG constraints that assume character boundaries rather than BPE subtokens. It also improves streaming safety by ensuring constraint evaluation sees only whole grapheme units.

Files touched (high level): runtime/constraint/lexer_proxy.py, runtime/constraint/profiles/emoji_rewrites.json, runtime/constraint/tests/test_lexer_proxy.py, sdk/compat/openai_compat.ts (adjusted framing shim), docs/structured_output/unicode_compat.md, examples/structured-output/emoji-toolcall-example.json, infra/ci/constraint-integration.yml (added integration stage).

Commits (summary):
- Add Unicode-aware lexer proxy and grapheme segmentation utils
- Wire lexer proxy into CFG and regex backends behind feature flag
- Add rewrite table and normalization config; document behavior
- Add unit/integration tests covering emoji, ZWJ, regional indicators, and streaming truncation cases
- Fix openai_compat streaming shim to reject partial-grapheme frames
- CI: add constraint integration job and flake guard for tokenizer tests

Tests and CI: Local unit tests cover ~120 new cases for grapheme/token mapping and constraint satisfaction. Integration job runs a simulated streaming scenario with a tiny model (mock runtime) to ensure canary constraints don't regress. One unit test was flaky on first CI run (tokenizer fixture race); re-ran and marked as flake-guard with a short backoff — final CI status is green.

Usage notes and migration: This is enabled by default for new structured-output routes, but can be toggled via the \"unicode_lexer_proxy\" boolean in model constraint profiles for backwards compatibility. We added guidance in docs/structured_output/unicode_compat.md explaining interactions with regex anchors and recommended NFKC for user-supplied constraint grammars.

Rollout plan: Feature-flag gated across runtimes; Canary (10%) on hosted API for 48h, monitor structured-output rejection rate and streaming latency. No expected perf regression beyond a ~0.5–1ms per-request CPU cost for grapheme segmentation on short prompts; batching amortizes cost.

Related: ENG-3291 (structured-output stability), ENG-3410 (openai-compat framing issues).
Miguel Torres: Nice, this addresses the root cause we saw in ENG-3291. Can you quantify worst-case CPU impact for long sequences?
Asha Patel: Added a microbenchmark in docs/structured_output/unicode_compat.md — worst-case single-request cost for 1k chars is ~6ms on a 4-core small instance; typical prompts are <200 chars so we expect ~0.5–1ms overhead. Batching and caching of segment maps reduces repeated work.
Leah Kim: I see potential interaction with existing token-prefix caching. Did you validate KV cache lookups still align when grapheme mapping changes token boundaries?
Asha Patel: Yes — we added deterministic mapping that is stable for tokenization changes if normalization mode is constant. There's a small note in the README about pinning normalization mode for long-lived caches.
Evan Ross: Tests look good. One nits: move the emoji rewrite table to profiles and load via existing profile loader. Also please add a short example to examples/structured-output showing a tool call with an emoji param.
Asha Patel: Done — moved the table and added example. Thanks.
Miguel Torres: Approved after the flake guard was added to CI. Verified canary metrics in staging show no spike in latency or rejection rate.

Motivation: Several regulators and large customers require demonstrable tenant-scoped key rotation and server-side proof that data keys were rewrapped with the tenant's active CMK. This PR adds enforcement hooks to the KMS layer to ensure tenant key rotation policies are honored and introduces an immutable audit-proxy that signs and stores rotation proof envelopes to a write-once audit bucket. Summary of changes: 1) KMS: new "rotation_enforcer" middleware that validates rotation requests, enforces tenant CMK scoping, and rejects cross-region or public-key rotations when tenant policy forbids them; 2) Rewrap flow: server-side atomic rewrap operation with fallback to region-affine CMK when primary CMK is unavailable, with detailed failure reasons surfaced to callers; 3) Audit proxy: new stateless service (audit-proxy) that accepts signed rotation envelopes, appends a signature and monotonic sequence number, and forwards to immutable storage (S3 WORM + signed manifests); 4) RBAC v2 policy: new permission "kms:force-rotate" and mapping changes so only authorized platform service accounts and tenant admins (with explicit grant) can trigger forced rotations; 5) Migration: a safe migration script that detects keys out of compliance and schedules background rewrap jobs under a controlled feature-flag rollout; 6) Tests and docs: end-to-end tests for rotation and audit proofs, updated compliance docs and runbook. Rollout plan: gated behind feature flag "rbac_v2_key_rotation_enforcer"; start canary on internal/test tenants, monitor rotation latency and audit-proxy throughput for 48h, then expand to steady-state. Backout: feature-flag off returns system to previous behavior; we also include an emergency admin endpoint to abort in-flight rewrap batches. Checklist: [x] KMS middleware implemented and unit tested [x] Rewrap atomic operation implemented and e2e-tested in perf-canary harness [x] Audit proxy implemented with signature and monotonic sequencing [x] RBAC policy schema changes and mapping test vectors included [x] Migration script with dry-run mode [x] Runbook and release notes drafted [x] Security review completed. Impact: introduces new small latency on forced-rotation calls (projected +50ms median) and audit-proxy adds write bandwidth; no plaintext key material leaves the KMS. Notes: we opted for signed rotation envelopes (PKI) rather than storing raw CMK identifiers in the audit log to reduce exposure and to allow later re-validation; rotation failures are retried with exponential backoff and recorded in the audit proxy. Related: ENG-5124 (key-management roadmap), SEC-210 (audit-chain requirements).
Ethan Huang: Can you clarify the failure semantics when the tenant CMK is temporarily unavailable? Please document the retry/backoff and the observable error codes.
Riya Patel: Reply: rotation_enforcer surfaces canonical error codes: KMS_UNAVAILABLE, POLICY_VIOLATION, REWRAP_FAILED. Retry is exponential up to 5 attempts with Jitter. I added details to the runbook and integration tests that assert retry semantics.
Marta Lopez: Request changes: Audit-proxy should include a monotonic sequence id to prevent reorder attacks; also ensure manifests are signed with platform key.
Riya Patel: Reply: added monotonic seq and manifest signing; included safety checks in proxy and unit tests for manifest verification.
Owen Park: Approved: security review looks good, small nits around logging level for rotation failures; prefer WARN not ERROR for transient network errors.
Riya Patel: Fixed: adjusted logging and added a metrics counter for transient failures.
CI: Integration tests flaked on first run (timeout in e2e), re-ran pipeline, all checks green.
Enforce tenant-scoped KMS rotation policies by introducing a rotation enforcement middleware, atomic rewrap flow with region-affine fallback, and an immutable signed audit-proxy to record rotation proofs. RBAC adds kms:force-rotate for authorized principals. Rollout via feature-flag. See docs/compliance/key-rotation-runbook.md for migration steps and monitoring guidance.

Motivation: Introduce a conservative tenant-level "geo quarantine" mode and a KMS usage blacklist check to reduce blast radius when cross-region consent or KMS provenance anomalies are detected. The feature bundles three coordinated pieces: 1) a tenant quarantine state that can be set by policy or triggered automatically from anomaly detectors, which routes all inference requests into a restricted execution path; 2) a KMS blacklist validator that denies use of tenant-bound keys originating from disallowed regions or providers; and 3) hardened audit envelopes for quarantined operations to ensure immutable provenance and faster downstream forensic queries. Design summary: - TenantQuarantine: new RBAC-like flag attached to tenant records, surfaced to request handlers via request context and enforced by the routing layer. While quarantined requests are allowed read-only access to diagnostics endpoints, they cannot use write-affecting KMS operations or access dedicated capacity pools. - KMSBlacklistChecker: pluggable validator that inspects encryption context and key metadata; a denylist can be configured per-organization or via global policy. The checker integrates with the existing KMS abstraction and returns structured denial reasons for audit. - AuditHardening: quarantined requests are written into a separate append-only audit stream with additional signed metadata (operator id, trigger rule id, decision trace). This stream uses existing audit sink but tags entries for fast queries and retention overrides. Changes made: - service/routing/quarantine_middleware.go: new middleware to short-circuit handlers and inject quarantine metadata. - service/rbac/v2/policy_engine.go: policy evaluation hook to consider quarantine state for role decisions. - pkg/kms/blacklist_checker.go: core denylist logic and provider adapters. - service/audit/envelope_writer.go: envelope v2 writer with signature and extra fields for quarantined flows. - api/swagger.yaml: new admin endpoints POST /admin/tenants/{id}/quarantine and GET /admin/tenants/{id}/quarantine-status, and admin KMS denylist endpoints. - migrations/20241106_add_tenant_quarantine_flag.sql: schema migration adding tenant.quarantine_state, quarantine_reason, and quarantined_at. - tests/integration/quarantine_e2e_test.go and unit tests across modules. Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind feature flag security.quarantine_v1. - Deploy code to staging and run the anomaly -> auto-quarantine e2e. - Enable admin APIs for internal operators only, run shadow mode for KMS blacklist for 2 weeks (denylist logs only). - After monitoring, flip enforcement and progressively add protected tenants. Backwards compatibility and data migration: - Migration is additive; default quarantine_state = "none". Policies not referencing quarantine behave unchanged. - KMS blacklist defaults to empty; administrators must opt-in entries. Tests and validation: - Unit tests for policy engine, KMS adapters, and audit envelope signer. - Integration tests for middleware routing and admin APIs. - Load test to validate that quarantined stream tagging does not affect core write throughput (observed <2% p99 increase in staging). Security review notes: - Threat model updated to include denial amplification if attackers attempt mass-quarantine; mitigations include operator-only API permissions, rate limits, and audit alerting. - KMS provider adapters validate signed key metadata before decision. Follow-ups: - Add Linear ticket ENG-4302 to expose quarantine metrics in the Console and link to runbooks. - Post rollout: add canary rules for automated un-quarantine with step-down cooldown. Checklist: [x] migrations added [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] docs (admin) updated [x] security review done
Miguel Torres: Please ensure the middleware does not add synchronous remote calls that can amplify tail latency. Consider deferring KMS metadata fetches to the KMS adapter cache. // Aisha: moved metadata fetch into adapter init and added in-memory TTL cache.
Claire Huang: Audit envelope signing looks good but we should rotate the envelope signing key and add key version to entries. // Aisha: added envelope_kv with version header and rotation doc.
Jordan Lee: Can we expose a metric for number of quarantined tenants and avg quarantine duration? // Aisha: added metrics.quarantine.count and metrics.quarantine.duration_seconds to the PR.
Security bot: static-scan flagged hardcoded admin route; removed default credentials and added a policy to fetch admin ACL from secrets manager.
Added tenant-level quarantine and KMS denylist enforcement. Admins can quarantine tenants and configure KMS denylists via new admin APIs. Quarantine is feature-gated and initially disabled. Enables hardened auditing for quarantined flows.
Observed <2% p99 write latency increase in staging when quarantine tagging enabled; recommended monitoring dashboards updated by ENG-ops.

Motivation: our CI pipeline has grown heavier over time as dependency checks and full validator runs are gated on every push. This PR introduces an incremental dependency validation step that runs cheap checks on changed dependency metadata and a post-submit stability validator for the full graph. It also refactors the CI runner image into a lightweight 'runner-lite' variant used for fast checks, reducing startup time and image size for ephemeral CI jobs.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a new CI composite action 'ci/actions/incremental-validate.yml' that inspects lockfile diffs, package manifests, and a cached dependency fingerprint to run focused validations instead of full graph resolution on every PR.
- Adds a post-submit job (nightly and post-merge) that runs the heavyweight dependency-stability validator against the full dependency graph and publishes a report artifact.
- Introduces a small Go-based helper 'tools/dep-validator' (single binary) used in both incremental and post-submit flows for reproducible resolution checks and simple heuristics (license, checksum drift, registry mismatch).
- Refactors our CI runner image into 'ci/actions/runner-lite' (smaller base image, removed optional language runtimes, moved heavy tooling into remote step caches) and updates Makefile.ci to support image variants.
- Adds a TTL-based ephemeral build cache pruner script 'scripts/build-cache-ttl.sh' to avoid unbounded cache growth and reduce long-tail CI flakiness.
- Updates docs with a migration guide 'docs/ci/runner-migration.md' and adds a short dev-facing FAQ about the new incremental checks.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design and acceptance criteria documented in ENG-4281
- [x] Unit tests for the dep-validator helper (basic resolution + checksum checks)
- [x] Integration smoke in a feature pipeline (small repo fixture)
- [x] Migration docs + runbook for rollbacks
- [x] Post-merge nightly job configured and tested

Commits (high level):
- feat(ci): add incremental-validate composite action and small wrapper
- feat(tools): add dep-validator v0.1 with checksum and license checks
- refactor(ci): introduce runner-lite image + Makefile.ci targets
- chore(scripts): add build-cache-ttl.sh and documentation
- docs: ci/runner-migration.md and faq

Files/areas changed (high level):
- ci/actions/incremental-validate.yml
- ci/actions/postsubmit-dep-stability.yml
- ci/actions/runner-lite/Dockerfile
- Makefile.ci
- tools/dep-validator/*.go
- scripts/build-cache-ttl.sh
- docs/ci/runner-migration.md
- pkg/ci/runner/entrypoint.ts (adjusted to detect runner variant)

Testing notes: 
- Local unit tests for dep-validator run in ~8s.
- End-to-end smoke for incremental flow executed against a small monorepo fixture in CI.
- Postsubmit nightly job validated by running once on a staging branch; result artifact uploaded to artifacts/redwood-dep-stability/2026-02-18.

Review conversation (high level):
- Aisha (review): "Love the idea of incremental checks — two asks: can we make the fingerprint algorithm stable across platforms and ensure the cache key accounts for node/yarn/pnpm differences? Also please add a short explanation of false-positive modes in the docs."
- Maya (author): "Addressed: fingerprint normalized by sorting manifests and canonicalizing macOS / Linux line endings; added explicit cache-key sections in the action and expanded the FAQ about false positives and how to trigger a full run."
- Daniel (review): "Runner image looks much smaller, but we need to be careful about missing runtime pieces when a job intentionally wants the full image. Suggest Makefile.ci provide a clear target to build the full runner."
- Maya: "Added Makefile.ci 'runner:full' and 'runner:lite' targets and documented expected tradeoffs in runner-migration.md."
- Luca (approval): "Verified postsubmit run and artifacts; good to go after CI green."

Motivation: Regional tail latency spikes (mostly in noisy EU/Beta zones) cause downstream SLO violations and frequent fallback oscillation. Current failover logic is purely reactive and global, which leads to cross-region thrash and unnecessary cold-starts. This PR introduces a locality-aware fail-fast gate combined with a sticky fallback reconciler to reduce oscillation and improve SLO stability without increasing overall error budgets.

Summary of changes: 1) locality fail-fast gate: a lightweight per-locality admission gate that evaluates short-window tail latency (p95/p99) and error rates, and triggers a fast-fail decision for requests that are likely to miss the SLO. The gate uses an exponential moving average with configurable hysteresis to avoid flip-flops. 2) sticky fallback reconciler: when a locality decides to fallback to a pre-warmed compatible model variant or remote region, the reconciler records a short sticky decision per-tenant (default 30s) and coordinates backfills of KV/cache where applicable. Sticky decisions are opportunistically refreshed or allowed to expire based on health probes. 3) speculative regional fallback: for requests routed from latency-sensitive tenants, we introduce speculative fallback attempts to warm remote replicas asynchronously while continuing local servicing; this reduces cold-start impact on the first fallback. 4) Observability: new telemetry (locality_failfast_decisions, sticky_fallback_events, speculative_warmup_success) and annotated traces for decision paths. 5) Feature flag + knob surface: runtime flags and per-tenant override (console + API) to tune thresholds, sticky TTL, and speculative concurrency.

Why this is different: instead of global thresholds we track locality characteristics and apply hysteresis with sticky decisioning so the system degrades gracefully and remains predictable. The reconciler coordinates KV preservation during short fallbacks so client-level caches see fewer regressions.

Testing & results: Unit tests added for gate logic, hysteresis transitions, reconciler state machine. Integration tests exercise cross-region fallback and speculative warm path. Canary in us-west with synthetic tail spike showed 38% reduction in fallback flip rate and 22% fewer cold-start latencies on first fallback attempt. p99 latency for affected tenants improved by ~120ms during injected noisy-driver tests.

Rollout plan: 1) feature-flagged rollout to 10% of requests (per-tenant sampling) for two days; 2) progressive increase to 50% with close telemetry monitoring; 3) enable per-tenant sticky TTL tuning for enterprise tenants only during phase 2. Rollback path: disable feature flag or reduce sampled tenants to 0; reconciler state timeouts ensure no long-lived inconsistent state.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for gate and reconciler - [x] Integration test for speculative warm path - [x] Added metrics and dashboard proposals - [x] Feature flag gating + console controls - [x] Run canary with synthetic spike harness - [x] Security review (auth boundary unchanged)

Related: Linear ENG-1345 (regional tail stabilization), ENG-2109 (sticky fallback design). Support ticket SUP-4421 was the immediate trigger for the investigation.

Notes: this PR intentionally keeps decision logic deterministic and small—no ML-based heuristics—to reduce risk during rollout. Future work: cost-aware fallback ranking and automated TTL tuning based on tenant historical stability.
Ethan: Can you clarify how the hysteresis window reacts to sustained but slowly improving latency? Suggest adding an exponential fallback to decay the threshold.
Author (Priya): Hysteresis uses an EMA with configurable alpha; added comments and test cases covering slow decay. We decided against exponential fallback for now to keep behavior predictable.
Marta: Sticky TTL defaults to 30s — is that empirically derived? Could be short for some enterprise flows.
Author: Default 30s chosen from canary tuning; made TTL configurable per-tenant and added console knob. Documented recommended values in ops guide.
Noah: One unit test flaky on CI (TestReconcilerBackoff) — looks timing sensitive.
Author: Increased test tolerance and replaced real time.Sleep with a controllable clock in the reconciler tests. Re-ran CI.
Ethan: Approved pending CI green and a short ops runbook addition.
Marta: LGTM.

Implements CRUD for Dedicated staged rollout plans in the control plane service, including server-side validation and basic RBAC enforcement.

Context
- This builds on pr-28411 (DB schema + migrations). This PR wires the schema into the service and exposes initial endpoints so Console + operators can create/update/get/list plans.
- Promote/abort + audit events are intentionally out of scope here (tracked in pr-28458).

What’s included
- API surface (internal + Console backend use)
  - POST /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans
  - GET  /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans/{plan_id}
  - GET  /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans (supports filtering by status + pagination)
  - PATCH /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans/{plan_id} (draft-only updates)
- Validation rules (enforced on create + update)
  - stage monotonicity: stages must be strictly increasing by allocation (traffic_pct or replica_count depending on stage.mode)
  - uniqueness: stage IDs + names unique within a plan
  - minimum headroom guardrail: ensure smallest stage alloc does not violate pool-level min canary size and headroom requirements
  - multi-region constraint: if pool has multiple regions, stage definitions must be compatible across regions (no per-region allocation yet)
  - draft immutability rules: once a plan is RUNNING, stage definitions are immutable (only metadata fields allowed)
- Basic RBAC
  - Read access: any principal with pool read access (customer admin + internal)
  - Write access (create/update): requires dedicated_pool_rollout:write permission
  - Enforcement is via authz middleware + explicit permission checks at handler level (defense-in-depth).
  - Adds temporary feature flag guard (dedicated_staged_rollouts) to block plan creation unless enabled for the account/pool.

Not included / follow-ups
- promote/abort/hold state machine actions and idempotency keys (pr-28458)
- audit event emission for CRUD actions (security requested; we’ll add once the audit schema lands; tracked under ENG-5932 subtasks)
- gate evaluation / policy engine integration (pr-28476)

Testing
- Unit tests for validation edge cases: decreasing stages, zero/negative allocations, duplicate IDs, and draft-only update enforcement
- API handler tests: RBAC deny cases, feature flag deny, pagination/filters
- Manual: used dev console to create a plan against a staging Dedicated pool; verified list/get responses and update constraints

Docs
- Added OpenAPI snippets + examples for Console backend integration

Rollout
- Safe to ship behind dedicated_staged_rollouts flag. No behavior changes for existing customers without the flag.

Screenshots/Examples
- Example create request:
  { "name": "mistral-7b-v2 rollout", "stages": [{"id":"canary","mode":"traffic_pct","allocation":1},{"id":"ramp","mode":"traffic_pct","allocation":10},{"id":"full","mode":"traffic_pct","allocation":100}] }
- Example validation error:
  "stages must be strictly increasing: stage 'ramp' allocation=10 must be > previous stage 'canary' allocation=10"
2025-02-19 Ethan Park: Looks good overall. Two concerns: (1) update endpoint should be draft-only, and (2) list endpoint needs pagination to avoid huge payloads for noisy customers. Can we enforce both now?

Motivation: Chat and low-latency completion workloads show high tail latency when models consist of many small compute layers (short sequence lengths or small microbatches) due to per-kernel launch overhead and blocking synchronization between compute kernels and NCCL collectives. This PR introduces a compact, stride-aware kernel-chaining runtime path plus a lightweight async-CUDA-event overlap mechanism to reduce per-token latency and improve utilization for multi-GPU tensor-parallel inference. Approach: 1) Add a kernel-chaining ABI that allows consecutive small ops within the same inference step to be launched as a single chained launch path when they meet stride and memory-hint heuristics; the ABI exposes a 'chainable' hint at operator registration time and a compact launch planner that produces merged kernel groups. 2) Use non-blocking CUDA events and a per-device 'handoff' stream to decouple kernel launch ordering from NCCL collective dispatch, enabling overlap of local compute and inter-GPU communication without introducing busy-waiting. 3) KV cache prefetch adjustments: the cache prefetcher now recognizes chained regions and postpones aggressive eviction while chained launches are in-flight to reduce redundant reloads; it also inserts small prefetch windows between chained groups to keep memory pressure bounded. 4) Scheduler integration: the chain scheduler is a lightweight policy in the runtime scheduler that prefers chaining when anticipated savings (launch overhead + extra latency from cache thrash) exceed a tunable threshold. Back-compat and safety: Chain path is opt-in via per-model config (runtime.chain.enabled) and is guarded by runtime checks for deterministic ordering. Fallback to existing launch path retains identical semantics. Testing & results: microbench (small-batch chat with 8 token responses) shows 15-28% p95 reduction across our internal TPU-equivalent and multi-GPU setups for medium models (7B-30B) and a 7-12% tokens/sec cost reduction on typical continuous-batching traffic. Stress tests run for 72 hours without deterministic correctness regressions; KV cache metrics show 4-6% less eviction churn for chained workloads. This change also reduces overall kernel-launch counts by ~22% in observed traces. Implementation notes: new header runtime/kernel_chain.h, CUDA core in runtime/kernel_chain.cu, scheduler integration in runtime/scheduler/chain_scheduler.cpp, KV prefetcher updates in runtime/kv_cache/prefetcher.cpp, lightweight python bindings for toggling in bindings/python/chain_api.py, new perf harness tests, and docs. See release notes for config knobs and recommended thresholds.
Commit 1: add kernel_chain ABI and minimal planner; Commit 2: implement chained launch path and event-based overlap; Commit 3: integrate chain scheduler policy and heuristics; Commit 4: KV cache prefetcher awareness and metrics; Commit 5: perf tests, docs, and python bindings; Commit 6: followup fixes from reviewers (ordering, corner-case evictions); Commit 7: CI perf tuning and stability fixes.
p95 latency reduction: 15-28% on small-batch chat; tokens/sec improvement: 7-12% on continuous batching; kernel-launches reduced by ~22%; KV eviction churn reduced by 4-6% for chained workloads.
Arjun: 'Nice approach — can you quantify memory overhead for chaining in worst-case (largest model segment)?' Author: 'Added microbench and worst-case numbers to perf doc; chaining adds a small staging buffer per-device (typ. <8MB) and we abort chain if staging would exceed memory budget.' Sofia: 'Be careful with NCCL ordering; tests should exercise stress with peer drops.' Author: 'Added deterministic ordering tests and simulated peer drop scenarios; chain falls back to canonical path on peer error.' Diego: 'We need telemetry for chain on/off and reasons for aborts.' Author: 'Added runtime metrics: chain_attempts, chain_comm_overlap_ms, chain_abort_reasons.' Reviewers: approved after follow-ups and CI-green.
CI: linux-build (pass), unit-tests (pass), gpu-integration (pass), perf-regression (pass after second run), lint (pass), flake8 (pass). One flaky microbench re-run required; green on re-run.
- Introduces compact stride-aware kernel chaining to reduce kernel-launch overhead for workloads with many small ops. - Adds async CUDA event overlap to overlap local compute and NCCL collectives. - KV cache prefetcher is aware of chained regions to reduce eviction churn. - Config knobs: runtime.chain.enabled (bool), runtime.chain.min_stride (int), runtime.chain.memory_budget_mb (int), runtime.chain.overlap_threshold_ms (float). - Behavior is opt-in and falls back to the original launch path.
Recommend enabling on staging with runtime.chain.memory_budget_mb=128 and runtime.chain.min_stride=3; monitor chain_abort_reasons and chain_comm_overlap_ms; roll out via canary on 10% traffic before full rollout.

Motivation: We need a safe, tenant-aware rollout guard to prevent automated econ/autotune systems from regressing latency or cost SLOs during canary and staged rollouts. This PR implements a frugal rollout guard plus a quantile-based autotuner that adjusts per-tenant quantization profiles (and optionally batch/caching defaults) by observing latency and unit-econ signals at P50/P95/P99. The goals are: 1) block/auto-rollback a rollout that increases P95 latency beyond tenant thresholds or causes unit-cost above configured budgets, 2) provide a conservative autotuner that recommends quantization tiers and prefill/batch hints per tenant using statistically-significant quantile signals, and 3) expose safe-fallback policies and operator controls in the Console and CLI. What changed (high-level): added rollout guard runtime hooks that evaluate live telemetry and apply canary gates; added quantile_autotuner service that samples per-tenant request traces and produces candidate profiles; added redwoodctl/econ CLI knobs to run dry-runs and import suggestions; added Console controls to set tenant budget/latency tolerances and to view autotuner recommendations; added telemetry metrics and a small e2e smoketest. Rollout plan: feature flag gated (feature_econ_frugal_rollout) behind an opt-in tenant flag; start with dry-run suggestions on tenant groups, followed by canary gating configured at 5/20/50 percent. Backwards compatibility: default is no-op until flag is enabled; fallbacks always route to non-quantized or previous model variant. Checklist: - [x] runtime guard and gate evaluation - [x] autotuner algorithm + CLI import/export - [x] Console UI controls + telemetry dashboard - [x] unit + e2e tests - [x] docs and changelog entry - [x] safety: fallback to previous model when thresholds violated Related: builds on work in ENG-3142 (prefill telemetry) and complements ENG-1874 (tenant warmstart). Linear/Jira: ENG-4521, PM-881, SUP-1204

Maya Chen: Added a bootstrap-resample unit test to cover noisy signal and updated docs to recommend minimum sample sizes.

Summary: This PR adds a soft-threshold slab partitioner to the runtime batcher that groups incoming requests into variable-width slabs by sequence length distribution. The goal is to reduce padding overhead while avoiding brittle hard bucket boundaries and to surface lightweight kernel-selection hints for packed lane execution. Motivation: Existing fixed bucketing either over-fragments or forces heavy padding at the tail of mixed-length workloads. We observed customer workloads with bimodal distributions (short chat queries + long document summarizations) where worst-case padding accounted for 12-18% of token cost. Design: The slab partitioner forms contiguous length ranges (slabs) with an adaptive soft threshold: each slab has a target max-pad ratio (configurable, default 0.12). Incoming requests are first routed to an active slab based on length; slabs accept small overflows for a short time window (soft threshold) before creating a new slab, which reduces churn for lengths near boundaries. Key behaviors: 1) soft thresholds avoid frequent slab creation on noisy length borders; 2) each slab tracks average length and pad ratio and emits kernel-selection hints for packed kernels (e.g., prefer lane-packed conv kernels when >60% lanes above the slab median); 3) a lightweight prefill probe queries KV-cache prefetch priority for high-length slabs to avoid pop-and-wait on first-token cold paths. Configuration: runtime/batcher/slab_partitioner: enabled=false (default), max_pad_ratio=0.12, soft_threshold_ms=30, min_slab_size=8. API: no surface changes to public inference API; config exposed via console and runtime flags. Benchmarks: MixedChatDocs workload (60% short seq <=64, 35% mid 128-512, 5% long >1024) on p4d.24xlarge: - Token-cost (estimated per-100k tokens): -9.1% vs mainline fixed-quantile bucketing - P95 latency at 1000 QPS: -7.4% (from 223ms -> 206ms) - Median latency: -5.8% - Throughput (sustained tokens/sec): +6.3% Notes: improvements concentrated where mid/long tail intermix; pure-short workloads see neutral change. Backwards compatibility: feature off by default; KV-keying unchanged. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear ENG-8421 - [x] Unit tests for slab lifecycle and soft-threshold timers - [x] Integration perf test added (ci/perf/slab-partitioner) - [x] Console flag + runtime flag - [x] Added metrics: slab_count, slab_rebalance_count, slab_pad_ratio_histogram Commits: - 7 commits: initial partitioner skeleton, slab lifecycle, lane-packing hints, kv-prefetch probe, metrics + tests, perf harness, docs Changes (high-level): - runtime/batcher/slab_partitioner.{rs,mod} (new) - runtime/batcher/slot_scheduler.rs (update: slab-aware slot allocation) - runtime/kv_cache/prefetch.rs (add probe + priority heuristic) - inference/kernels/packed_lane_selector.cc (hint plumbing) - perf/benchmarks/mixed_chat_docs.yaml (new harness) - docs/runbooks/slab_partitioner.md (new) - tests/unit/test_slab_partitioner.rs (new) - ci/perf/slab-partitioner (new job) Small illustrative snippet (config): "runtime.batcher.slab_partitioner.max_pad_ratio=0.12; runtime.batcher.slab_partitioner.soft_threshold_ms=30" Review thread: - Owen Martinez (reviewer) 2026-02-19: "Nice approach; soft thresholds should reduce oscillation. Two asks: (1) can we make the slab creation backoff exponential to limit pathological bursts? (2) add a metric for 'slab_creation_rate' per minute." - Maya Patel (author) 2026-02-19: "Added exponential backoff and slab_creation_rate metric in latest commit. Backoff default: base_ms=50, multiplier=2, max_ms=1000." - Eliot Chen (reviewer) 2026-02-20: "KV prefetch probe looks good; ensure it respects privacy: only prefetch keys for requests in dedicated/datasafe mode. Please gate it behind existing KMS flag." - Maya Patel 2026-02-20: "Gated probe behind datasafe flag and added explicit unit test to assert no prefetch when datasafe=true." - Priya Kapoor (reviewer) 2026-02-21: "Microbench shows the packed kernel hint can regress small-batch short sequences by ~2% median; please add a safety threshold to only emit hints when slab occupancy > min_slab_size." - Maya Patel 2026-02-21: "Added min_slab_size and adjusted hint thresholds. Updated perf numbers in PR description."
Introduces a soft-threshold slab partitioner for sequence-length-driven batching that reduces padding tokens and improves p95 latency on mixed-length workloads. Backwards-compatible config flag (disabled by default).

Eliot Chen: 'Gate KV prefetch behind datasafe flag to avoid privacy risk'
Priya Kapoor: 'Add safety thresholds so packed-kernel hints don't hurt small-batch short sequences'

Motivation: SDK users across Python/TypeScript/Go reported inconsistent credential resolution ordering and awkward ergonomics for streaming consumers. This PR centralizes credential lookup precedence for all SDKs (explicit config -> env vars -> shared OS credential cache -> platform delegated token) and introduces a lightweight async-iterable facade / sync-generator adapter to improve ergonomics for common streaming patterns. The change is intentionally conservative: no breaking changes to existing method names, but we add a small opt-in compatibility shim and bump SDK minor versions. Key changes: unify credential lookup precedence in client factory and document it; implement implicit credential fallthrough with deterministic logging and telemetry tag so operators can see which source won; introduce `AsyncIterableFacade` in TS that normalizes chunk framing, backpressure hints, and reconnect metadata; add `sync_stream()` helper in Python that wraps async iterators with a stable generator-based API for sync code paths; add a Go `streamer` helper that returns a context-aware channel iterator with explicit Cancel semantics and a small connection-warmup path; add a new retry preset `balanced` for streaming idempotency trade-offs and map it into all SDKs; small telemetry/trace tag harmonization so streaming spans include `cred_source` and `retry_preset`; update tests and examples; bump SDK versions. Testing/CI: unit tests (py/ts/go) and cross-language integration test harness run in CI; a flaky TS chunking test failed initially and was fixed by increasing a short debounce window and adding deterministic stub for chunk boundaries in tests. Commits are organized as small, reviewable pieces (credential lookup, TS facade, Python helper, Go streamer, tests & docs, version bumps). Backwards compatibility: opt-in facade and helpers; existing streaming APIs remain supported. Merge: squash and merge after approvals and a green CI run.

Motivation: We see recurring small-cost spikes that produce noisy SLO alerts despite being semantically benign. Root cause is often downstream model switching or short-lived prompt-shape changes that current alerting attributes to tenants incorrectly. This PR introduces 'invocation shadow profiles' that capture compact summaries of invocation execution shape (prefix length, kv-cache hit ratio estimate, model-variant fingerprint) and a causalized alerting layer that attributes cost/latency drift to the most likely driver rather than the tenant by default. Summary of changes: added shadow profile generator in the serving runtime, introduced a lightweight causal attribution scorer that runs in the observability service, added a new dashboard and alert rule templates, and wired end-to-end tests and benchmarks. Commits (high-level): 1) Add shadow profile proto and serializer; 2) Instrument runtime to emit shadow-profile sidecar for sampled invocations; 3) Build causal attribution service with noise-aware priors and event windowing; 4) Update observability ingestion pipeline to join shadow profiles and metrics; 5) Add dashboard panels and new alerting rules; 6) Tests and infra: add unit tests for scorer, integration test using replaybench, add e2e smoke. Files changed (high level): src/runtime/shadow_profile.rs added summary serializer and sampling knobs; src/observe/attribution/scorer.py added causal scoring model and CI-configured thresholds; observability/ingest/pipeline.go updated to perform 1:1 join on sampled invocation ids; dashboards/causal-cost-explorer.json new Grafana panels showing per-model and per-tenant causal attribution; alerts/retrospective-cost-alerts.yaml new templated alert; tests/replaybench/shadow_capture.yaml test replay gestures. Runtime knobs: sampling_ratio default 0.002 (configurable per-tenant), max_profile_size 512 bytes, and a privacy-safe hashing pipeline for model and prompt fingerprints. Review conversation summary: Ethan requested deterministic sampling for integration tests and tighter defaults on retention; author replied that tests now inject deterministic seed and retention is capped to 7 days for shadow-profile raw payloads; Priya asked for clarification on attribution priors and whether they bias against recent model rollouts; author added a linear-decay prior and documented fallback to tenant-anchored alerts in low-confidence cases; Marcus requested perf microbenchmarks for emit overhead, author added a benchmark showing median 28us extra per-invocation at 8k seq and 99th 120us under synthetic load. Comments and change requests: - make sampling_ratio configurable via tenant flags (addressed) - add opt-out for enterprise private installs (addressed, KMS key gating documented) - confirm no sensitive prompt text is persisted (addressed, only 64-bit hashed shape signatures stored). Approvals: Ethan approved after second iteration, Priya approved, Marcus approved with no further changes. CI: initial run had one flaky test in replaybench, rerun passed; lint and type checks pass; integration e2e in staging passed. Canary notes: deployed to staging for 48 hours, observed 43% reduction in low-confidence alerts on a noisy customer and no regressions in throughput. Rollout plan: staged rollout by tenant percentage: 0%, 5%, 25%, 100% with metrics validation gates at each step; automatic mute to tenant-anchored alerts if attribution confidence < 0.6 for more than 10 minutes. Backwards compatibility: shadow profiles are emitted only when sampling is enabled and join keys are optional; ingestion side can ignore new fields. Operational notes: dashboard includes a causal attribution heatmap, per-model impact table, and a retrospective alert queue that surfaces suspected misattributions for operator review. Migration: no customer data migration required. Post-merge actions: 1) coordinate with SRE to create alerting playbook entries, 2) add retention policy to tenant docs and compliance, 3) schedule a 1-hour runbook review with support. Related work and references: builds on ENG-7029 (prefetch tracing) and ENG-7182 (invocation coalescing); relates to SUP-1193 investigating noisy alerts for tenant X. Why unique: unlike previous token-level attributions this PR attaches compact execution fingerprints and applies a lightweight causal model that can retroactively re-attribute alerts and mute noisy signals, enabling quieter SLOs without losing signal for true regressions.
Introduce invocation shadow profiles and causalized token-cost alerting. Provides per-tenant retrospective scoring to reduce noisy alerts and surface true regressions. No user-facing API changes.

Context and motivation: Over time presubmit runners accumulated near-duplicate lint/test setup code across JS/Go/Python pipelines. This increases flakiness and slows iteration when bootstrapping toolchains or rotating devdeps. This PR introduces a thin "lint-bridge" abstraction and a minimal toolchain curator binary that centralizes devtool snapshots, normalizes env bootstrapping, and provides a lightweight caching layer for presubmit images. Goals: reduce presubmit setup churn, remove duplicate setup scripts, shrink CI image surface area, and provide an opt-in compatibility adapter for legacy jobs.

What this change does (single-pass summary):
- Adds a Go-based toolchain-curator (cmd/curator) that discovers workspace language targets and emits a stable toolchain manifest.
- Introduces lint-bridge shim that exposes a small, consistent CLI (lint-bridge run --profile) used by presubmit workflows.
- Reworks CI workflows to call the curator once per matrix and pass a manifest path into runners rather than running ad-hoc install scripts.
- Adds a minimal Docker light-image for fastest-presubmit path and a fallthrough path for full images.
- Plumbs dep-curation metadata into existing dep-snapshot reports to make aggressive pruning safe.

Checklist:
- [x] Add curator CLI and tests for manifest generation (unit + small integration).
- [x] Replace three ad-hoc presubmit scripts in .github/workflows with lint-bridge entries.
- [x] Add documented migration steps for teams with custom presubmit logic.
- [x] Smoke test on staging with fastpath lanes and nightly full-matrix.
- [x] Update devcontainers and local dev scripts to consume curator manifest.

Commits summary: 
- feat(curator): initial curator binary that emits JSON/YAML manifest (4 commits)
- perf(ci): wire lint-bridge into js/python/go presubmit matrices
- refactor(scripts): remove legacy bootstrap scripts and move helpers into /internal/ci
- test(ci): add integration test that validates manifest-driven toolchain equality

Changed areas (high-level):
- cmd/curator/* (new)
- tools/lint-bridge/* (new)
- .github/workflows/presubmit-fastpath.yml (modified)
- .github/workflows/presubmit-full.yml (modified)
- internal/ci/bootstrap_helpers.go (refactored)
- devcontainer.json and docs/dev-tooling.md (docs updated)

Testing and migration notes:
- Staged rollout adopted: lint-bridge enabled on the fastpath lanes first (small repos), then nightly full-matrix observed for three days before enabling across the org.
- Rollback is a one-line toggle in workflow templates to call legacy bootstrap scripts; we retained those scripts under scripts/legacy-bootstrap for emergency use.
- Observability: added probe metrics (curator.manifest_generation_time_ms) and a presubmit cache hit gauge to the CI metrics exporter.

Related work and references: Linear ENG-4821 tracks the devdep rotation plan; ENG-4824 is the ci-telemetry task. See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4821/toolchain-curation-design (internal).

Why this is safe: curator is additive and emits deterministic manifests; presubmit fastpath still falls back to a full-image path if a cache miss or manifest validation fails. We run both in staging for three days before merging.

Release notes: Adds lint-bridge CLI and toolchain-curator to centralize presubmit toolchain snapshots and reduce duplication in CI. Migration instructions added to docs/dev-tooling.md.

Alexei: Nice cleanup. Two comments: (1) ensure curator binary honors XDG_CONFIG_HOME for local dev; (2) can we gate the fast-image rollout by repo size?
Priya: Thanks Alexei — curator now reads XDG config with fallback. I added a repo-size predicate to presubmit-fastpath to opt-in only repos < 5MB by default.
June: Integration tests look good; request to add a small note to docs about how to opt-out if your repo needs custom deps.
Priya: Added docs/dev-tooling.md section 'Opting out & custom presubmit' and kept legacy-bootstrap scripts for emergency fallbacks.
Miguel: CI metrics look stable on staging. Approving pending minor CI flakiness fix in the windows runner (separate patch).

Motivation: SRE runbooks show a high volume of noisy alert triggers driven by microbursty token-cost spikes from long conversational tails. This PR introduces a streamed rollup pipeline that computes lightweight per-invocation cost summaries (decibel-weighted rollups) in the telemetry ingest path and an alert-fuzz controller that applies hysteresis + probabilistic smoothing to alert evaluation to reduce churn. Key goals: 1) preserve signal for real regressions 2) suppress transient burst noise without dropping visibility 3) keep rollup compute < 2% of telemetry budget. Changes: adds a streaming aggregator service that builds three compact rollup artifacts per invocation (total_tokens, decibel_cost, tail_entropy) and attaches a rollup-hash to the trace; introduces an AlertFuzzController that hooks into the alert pipeline and rewrites thresholds by applying time-decayed fuzz envelopes and cohort-aware suppression; wires rollup metadata into the observability query layer and dashboard panels. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-4211) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] E2E synthetic replay with noisy tails - [x] Backwards-compatible schema migration for rollup tags - [x] Alert playground run and tuning notes Commits are small/iterative to aid review. Related: SUP-3321 incident notes, OBS-88 spike analysis. TODO: follow-up to add tenant-level opt-out and tighten memory bounds for high-cardinality tenants.
Priya: Can we avoid adding high-cardinality tags for tenants by default? Suggest adding an allowlist and defaulting to a hashed tenant id.
Author (Asha): Good catch. switched rollup_hash to tenant-hashed index and added opt-out flag. See ingest/transform_pipeline.go commit b3f9e21 for implementation notes.
Diego: The AlertFuzzController looks promising; request: add a short circuit for SLO-critical alerts so we never suppress those. Also please add a dashboard slice showing suppressed vs fired alerts over time.
Author (Asha): Added SLO-critical bypass and dashboard slice (ui/dashboards/rollup_insights.json). Updated tests to assert bypass behavior.
Noah: integration tests failed once due to replaybench timeout; reran CI and it passed on second run. Approving after CI green.
Priya: Approve - small nits addressed in follow-up commit.
Add lightweight streamed per-invocation cost rollups (decibel-weighted cost, tail entropy) and an AlertFuzzController to reduce noisy long-tail alert churn. Rollups are opt-out per-tenant and attached to traces as rollup_hash tags. Includes dashboard panels and replaybench scenarios for tuning.
Deploy order: rollup aggregator binary -> feature flag on ingest -> enable AlertFuzzController in alerting config. Monitor 'rollup_ingest_error_rate' and 'alert_suppression_rate' dashboards during canary. Memory watch recommended for tenants with > 10k concurrent invocations.

payload.body:
Fixes intermittent partial-JSON emissions in SSE caused by UTF-8 multi-byte split across chunks; improves determinism of function-call/event ordering during stream handoff; no API changes.
Motivation: Customers reported sporadic partial JSON objects arriving in the SSE stream when a multi-byte UTF-8 character is split across network chunks; additionally, high-concurrency tool/function call flows could produce out-of-order fncall boundaries in rare interleaving windows. This PR introduces a small stream-lexer component in the streaming path that reserves trailing bytes to avoid splitting UTF-8 codepoints at chunk boundaries and adds an ordered handoff gate for fncall/toolcall events to preserve logical ordering across internal buffering and backpressure events. This is intended to be a minimal, low-latency change that prevents user-facing partial JSON and tool/function call reordering without changing existing stream framing or client behavior. Changes made: 1) stream/lexer/byte_reserve.go: new lexer that inspects outgoing chunks and ensures the last up-to-4 bytes (configurable) are held until the next chunk arrives if they form an incomplete UTF-8 sequence; emits a safe boundary marker when the sequence completes to aid downstream parsers. 2) stream/handshake/ordered_handoff.go: introduces a small gate that sequences fncall/toolcall terminal events by assigning a monotonic stream-epoch and only allowing the epoch to advance once the previous epoch has observed its terminal sentinel (reduces rare races when KV cache flushes + rebuffering cause swapped call boundaries). 3) integrations/openai_compat/sse_adapter.go: wires lexer and handoff into the OpenAI compatibility adapter so hosted and compatible routing paths benefit. 4) unit and integration tests: new tests that fuzz-chunk UTF-8 splits, simulate backpressure pause/resume, and assert JSON recomposition and call ordering invariants. Checklist: - [x] Design doc sketched in ENG-1428 - [x] Unit tests for byte-reserve lexer - [x] Integration test for fncall ordered handoff - [x] Load smoke to validate latency impact < 2% p50 - [x] Backcompat: no changes to API surface - [x] Added metrics: stream.byte_reserve_events, stream.handoff_latency Summary of commits: - c1a2b3 introduce stream lexer and byte reservation algorithm - d4e5f6 add ordered handoff gate and epoch sequencing - f7a8b9 wire components into openai_compat adapter and add metrics - a1b2c3 add unit/integration fuzz tests and fixes - b2c3d4 tidy up logging and add feature flag (alpha) Files changed (high-level): - stream/lexer/byte_reserve.go: new - stream/lexer/byte_reserve_test.go: new - stream/handshake/ordered_handoff.go: new - stream/handshake/ordered_handoff_test.go: new - integrations/openai_compat/sse_adapter.go: modified (hooked lexer/handoff, added metrics) - integrations/openai_compat/sse_adapter_test.go: modified (updated test vectors) - metrics/registry.go: added two counters/gauges - docs/streaming.md: note about byte-reserve behavior and troubleshooting (small section) Review conversation: - Diego Ramirez (reviewer): "Overall this looks reasonable; only concern is the feature flag gating for the lexer — can we make it opt-in for now and enable by default in nightly? Also add benchmarks for p99." - Elena Park (author): "Added feature flag (alpha) and benchmark entry; default enabled in nightly runs only. Bench numbers included in the PR comments." - Asha Menon: "Ordered handoff looks correct but please add a comment describing why we choose monotonic epoch vs sequence number in the code - helps future debuggers." - Elena Park: "Added code comment and a short note in streaming.md explaining the epoch choice (avoids gaps when ephemeral replays occur)." - Samir Gupta: "Two test flakes observed in CI on first run (integration/timeouts) — I retriggered CI." CI checks: - unit: pass - integration: flaky on first run, passed on rerun - lint: pass - bench-nightly: recorded (p50 +1.4%, p99 +0.7%) Observed behavior and mitigation: - Partial JSON: prior to this change we observed ~1 in 50k streams encountering a truncated multi-byte sequence that would cause JSON decode errors on the client. With byte-reserve enabled in nightly, we saw zero reproductions in a 48-hour fuzz run. - Fncall reordering: repro requires a tight interleaving of toolcall terminal flush + rebuffer + resend; the ordered handoff prevents the epoch from advancing until the previous terminal is observed, eliminating the reordering window in integration fuzz. Performance: microbenchmarks show negligible p50 latency impact (+1.4%) and p99 increase under worst-case backpressure scenarios of ~0.7% which is acceptable for the hosted workload and can be toggled with the feature flag. Rollout plan: enable feature flag in nightly for 48 hours, run extended fuzz and canary in us-east-1 traffic at 5% for 72 hours, monitor stream.json_decode_errors, stream.byte_reserve_events, and stream.handoff_latency. If stable, promote to full rollout over 7 days. Merge details: merged by Diego Ramirez using squash on 2026-02-28 after approvals. Notes: this change is focused on stability and compatibility; it is intentionally conservative and guarded behind a feature flag to allow quick rollback if any anomaly is observed. Related: ENG-1428 design doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1428/stream-lexer-byte-reserve. Logs and bench artifacts attached to the PR for auditors.
payload.title: stream lexer: trailing-byte-reserve and ordered handoff to prevent partial-json and fncall reordering

payload.body:
Add templated RBAC roles scoped to geo-fence claims; attach KMS usage metadata tags for audit correlation; introduce tokenization layer to redact sensitive claim values in audit logs. Backwards compatible: existing role bindings continue to work.
Motivation: Customers operating across multiple jurisdictions need fine-grained operator permissions that automatically adapt to a tenant's geo-claims, without proliferating dozens of static role definitions. At the same time we must ensure KMS usage is attributed with minimal PII in audit logs for compliance teams and regulators. This PR introduces a templating mechanism for RBAC v2 role definitions keyed by geo-claims (geozone, country_code, region_bucket) and a lightweight KMS usage metadata tagging scheme combined with an audit tokenization layer to strip or token-format sensitive claim values before they hit long-term audit storage.

Changes in this PR: 1) Role templating engine: a new role-templater service and a set of YAML templates under internal/rbac/templates/geo-templates/ that allow templates to be expanded into RBAC v2 roles at bind-time. Templates support conditional blocks (e.g., is_eu, is_us_region) and annotation-derived constraints. 2) RBAC admission hook updates: the admission webhook now resolves template placeholders to runtime claims and emits the resolved role fingerprint to a decision cache. This avoids storing cleartext geo-claims in role bindings. 3) KMS usage metadata tagging: when a request uses a customer CMK, the request path now attaches an opaque kms_meta tag (kms_meta.{env,zone_hash,usage_class}) propagated to downstream billing/audit systems. 4) Audit tokenization layer: an extraction and replacement step added to the audit forwarder that replaces raw claim values (email, tenant_geo_id) with reversible tokens (short hash + version) when forwarding to long-term storage while keeping full values in short-lived debugging traces retained in internal logs only. 5) Migration tooling: a small migration that converts a subset of staged role-bindings using the new templating syntax and backfills kms_meta tags for the last 30 days of audit traffic in a best-effort mode.

Testing & CI: unit tests for the templater and admission-hook logic were added (internal/rbac/templater_test.go, internal/webhooks/admission_templater_test.go). End-to-end smoke tests were added to the perf-canary suite to validate token round-trip and KMS tag propagation. The CI pipeline had one flaky integration test (AuditForwarder::deliver_with_retry) that failed once and was retried automatically; the final status is green.

Rollout plan: staged rollout using a feature flag (rbac.geo_templates.enabled) across Dedicated clusters for 2 weeks, monitored by a new observability dashboard (Console -> Security -> Geo RBAC) that tracks template expansion failure rate, decision cache hit rate, and kms_meta propagation. If error rate > 0.1% for 30 minutes we will rollback the flag.

Backwards compatibility: templates do not replace existing static role definitions; if a binding references a static role it is unchanged. The templater will only operate on role-binding files that include the "template:" key.

Migration notes: the included migration script (scripts/migrate_bindings_geo_template.sh) must be run in the operator console with the migration flag enabled and will produce a dry-run report.

Security review: the tokenization design was reviewed by Security (SEC-44) and includes HSM-backed token seeds stored in the key-management service; tokens are reversible only by the audit-token-service which requires a special operator role.

Known limitations: template language does not yet support nested arrays in conditions (to be added in a follow-up), kms_meta currently supports a fixed set of keys; adding new keys requires a small schema bump and downstream mapping updates.

Related work: this PR complements ENG-2081 (decision-cache TTL tuning) and ENG-2130 (audit-forwarder batching improvements).
Priya Nair: Please confirm the tokenization format and escape properties; we need to ensure downstream ELK ingestion won't treat tokens as failed JSON. Response: token format is v1:<short-b64-hash>, added unit test that simulates ELK pipeline and escapes special chars.
Ethan Cho: Can the templater be used by operator scripts (yes/no)? Concern about privilege escalation if templates reference arbitrary annotations. Response: templater restricts placeholders to a safe whitelist (geozone, country_code, region_bucket, tenant_tier) and this is enforced by the admission hook.
Marisol Ruiz: Suggest adding a feature-flagged debug endpoint that returns expanded templates for a given binding for easier troubleshooting. Response: added console endpoint /api/debug/templater/expand under feature flag rbac.geo_templates.debug_endpoint; locked to SRE and security roles.
Security (SEC-44): Reviewed HSM-backed seed storage, recommended rotating the audit token seed quarterly and limiting the audit-token-service to read-only in staging. Action: added rotation_note to docs and scheduled quarterly job in infra-runbooks repository.
QA: Found flaky AuditForwarder::deliver_with_retry test; flaked once due to timing issue. We added exponential backoff and increased the mock latency tolerance. CI retried and passed.
payload.title: Introduce geo-fence role templating and KMS usage metadata tagging with audit tokenization

payload.body:
Motivation: Customers operating under regional data residency and custodial key constraints need guarantees that (1) audit metadata cannot be injected or replayed by downstream services and (2) KMS key usage is provably tied to allowed key origins. This PR introduces two complementary controls: (A) sealed-audit-headers: an immutable header envelope added at the edge (gateway) and verified by services and the audit-forwarder before logs are persisted or exported; (B) kms-origin-policy-evaluator: a policy plugin in the request-authorizer that rejects crypto-ops when the requested key origin region is not allowed for the tenant. Together these reduce risk of accidental cross-region key usage and audit tampering. Changes: 1) gateway: add sealing middleware that computes a signature over canonical audit headers and a request nonce, emits X-Redwood-Audit-Seal and X-Redwood-Audit-Seal-V:1 and rejects requests that present non-matching unsealed audit headers. 2) authorizer: new kms_origin_policy evaluator consulted by RBAC v2 policy engine; policy predicate 'kms_origin in allowed_regions' implemented and configurable per-tenant. 3) audit-forwarder: extended to validate sealed headers before forwarding to external SIEM and to include origin verification metadata in exported envelopes. 4) rbac-mapping: new service-account -> tenant binding validator to prevent service accounts from being used across tenant boundaries for KMS ops. 5) docs and console: admin UI surfaces to view tenants' allowed KMS regions and compliance status. Implementation notes: sealed header uses HMAC-SHA256 with tenant-scoped signing key stored in KMS; signature computed on a deterministic ordering of audit headers plus request id and timestamp window to prevent replay. Policy evaluator consults tenant metadata and falls back to explicit deny when metadata missing; rollout flag 'security.kms_enforce_origin' gate controls evaluator. Tests: unit tests for header canonicalization, property-based tests for canonical ordering, integration test harness exercising gateway->authorizer->audit-forwarder path with both permitted and denied key origins, e2e smoke in staging using synthetic tenant configs. Backwards compatibility: if gate is off, system behaves as before; gateway accepts requests without seals but emits advisory log so operators can estimate impact. Migration: a lightweight migration adds tenant.allowed_kms_regions string array and a signing_key_reference to the tenants table; an offline job (scripts/migrations/73199-populate-tenant-kms) prepared to backfill likely values from billing metadata but requires manual review for ambiguous tenants. Security review: SEC reviewed the design and requested sealed header TTL of 90s and replay nonce store eviction policy; these are implemented. Rollout plan: enable in canary region for 48h, monitor audit-forwarder rejects metric and application 403 spikes, then progressively enable with config locks per-account. Related: ENG-1157 explains the policy schema, SUP-934 contains a customer support case that motivated origin enforcement.
Diego Ramos: Nice design. Please add explicit tests for header ordering; I want to be sure no accidental canonicalization drift occurs.
Author (Nora Patel): Added property-based tests and a test vector file with canonical ordering examples.
Li Wei: What is the performance impact on p99 for the authorizer path? Can we cache policy decisions per-request-id?
Author (Nora Patel): Benchmarked in perf-canary: median auth path +1.8ms, p99 +3.2ms at 10k rps due to HMAC; added a short in-memory cache with 15s TTL to mitigate repeated header rechecks behind LB.
Ava Thompson: We need a migration rollback plan if tenant backfill assigns a wrong region. Add a manual remediation doc.
Author (Nora Patel): Added remediation steps in docs and a dry-run flag for the backfill script.

Add immutable sealed audit headers to protect audit metadata from injection and a KMS origin policy evaluator to enforce tenant allowed key regions. Configurable via feature gate security.kms_enforce_origin. Requires tenant metadata migration (tenant.allowed_kms_regions).
Canary plan: enable in us-west-2 for 48h before wider rollout
Monitor metrics: audit.seal.rejects, kms_origin.denied_count, tenant.kms_missing_metadata
Rollback: flip security.kms_enforce_origin=false and disable gateway seal enforcement if needed

payload.body:
Context and motivation: We continue to see production incidents where long-lived streaming connections are interrupted during token refresh windows or due to transient network blips. Existing SDKs had ad-hoc reconnection code and differing token fallback behaviors. This PR introduces a lightweight, consistent credential swapping/fallback pipeline (CredentialSwapper) and a resumable line-buffered streaming iterator (LineBufferedAsyncIterator) implemented in Python/TypeScript/Go so application code can rely on identical semantics across languages.

What this PR does (single summary): Adds CredentialSwapper as an injectable strategy that 1) tries the active token, 2) transparently falls back to a delegated refresh token, and 3) invokes a user-provided tokenProvider callback as last resort. Adds a stream iterator that reassembles chunked text using line delimiters (\n) into logical messages, preserves an opaque resumeToken, and supports manual or automatic resume on reconnect. Also bumps SDK versions (py 1.13.0, ts 1.9.1, go v0.7.4) and updates a selection of examples and docs.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed by ENG-9981
- [x] Implementations for Python, TypeScript, and Go
- [x] Unit tests for credential fallback order and edge cases
- [x] Integration tests (local e2e harness) for stream resume semantics
- [x] Updated quickstart snippets and CHANGELOG entries
- [x] Backwards-compatible by default (opt-in features documented)

Commits (high level):
- feat(auth): add CredentialSwapper core interface (multi-sdk scaffold)
- feat(python): python sdk CredentialSwapper implementation + unit tests
- feat(ts): typescript sdk CredentialSwapper + typed tokenProvider hooks
- feat(go): go sdk credential cascade and context-aware refresh
- feat(stream): add LineBufferedAsyncIterator and resumeToken plumbing across sdks
- docs: quickstart examples and migration guide
- tests: e2e harness additions for flaky-network simulation
- chore: bump versions and changelogs

Files / areas changed (high level):
- sdk/python/redwood/auth/credential_swapper.py (new)
- sdk/python/redwood/stream/line_buffer_iterator.py (new)
- sdk/python/tests/test_credential_swapper.py (new)
- sdk/typescript/src/auth/credentialSwapper.ts (new)
- sdk/typescript/src/stream/lineBufferedIterator.ts (new)
- sdk/typescript/test/stream-resume.spec.ts (new)
- sdk/go/auth/swapper.go (new)
- sdk/go/stream/linebuffer.go (new)
- docs/quickstarts/streaming-resume.md (updated)
- examples/stream-resume/py/README.md (updated)
- ci/e2e/network-sim.yml (updated)

Testing notes: Unit coverage added for primary code paths: token present, delegated refresh success, provider callback invoked, and resumeToken replay resulting in duplicate suppression. E2E harness runs the new flaky-network scenario that simulates TCP resets mid-chunk and ensures resume occurs without duplication or deadlock. Performance microbenchmarks show <2% overhead on steady-state token checks (cached path), a ~5-8% increase in allocation during active resume sequences (acceptable for resumed sessions).

Review conversation (selected highlights):
- Lucas Chen (review): "CredentialSwapper looks solid. Two asks: (1) make the tokenProvider callback optional by default and (2) add a short-circuit path when token TTL > 30s to avoid unnecessary refreshes."
- Priya (author): "Implemented optional tokenProvider default; added TTL short-circuit and tests. See commit 7af3d2a."
- Sofia Petrova (review): "LineBufferedAsyncIterator is a good ergonomics win. Can we expose a MaxBufferBytes option so users can avoid OOM on pathological streams?"
- Priya: "Added max_buffer_bytes option with safe default 64KiB; iterator returns explicit BufferOverflowError when exceeded. Updated docs and examples."
- Hiro Tanaka (review): "Go implementation: prefer context cancellation propagation — add ctx checks on each chunk assemble path."
- Priya: "Go changes updated to propagate ctx cancellation; added test that cancels mid-resume and verifies cleanup."
- CI / infra note: an intermittent flake in the TS stream-resume test was resolved by increasing the test harness timeout and adding deterministic sequence IDs.

Decision notes and tradeoffs: We purposely made CredentialSwapper an abstraction rather than changing existing token stores to retain backward compatibility and allow gradual opt-in for clients that want explicit delegated fallback. LineBufferedAsyncIterator targets line-delimited protocols (the most common for our streaming outputs) — future work may add delimited-by-token or JSON-aware reassembly.

Migration guidance: Existing client code continues to work unchanged. To opt-in: instantiate SDK client with credentialSwapper option and/or use the new stream.iterator = LineBufferedAsyncIterator.fromResponse(resp) helper. Examples in docs/quickstarts show migration steps and code samples for Python/TS/Go.

CI / Checks summary:
- Linux unit tests (python/ts/go): pass
- e2e flaky-network: pass (after transient rerun)
- Lint: pass (TS/Go linting autoformat applied)
- Security scan: pass (no new high-risk deps)

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main on 2025-11-09 after approvals from Lucas, Sofia, and Hiro. CHANGELOG entries added for each SDK and the main repo.

Follow-ups (tracked in ENG-10012):
- Add JSON-aware stream reassembly for cases where logical messages may span arbitrary chunk boundaries.
- Consider adding a shared telemetry event for resume attempts to correlate server-side logs.
- Evaluate making CredentialSwapper the default behavior for dedicated/private deployments later this quarter.
Adds a CredentialSwapper abstraction and a resumable LineBufferedAsyncIterator across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Improves robustness for interrupted streams and provides a delegated token fallback order. Patches include small ergonomic surface wins (simpler stream resumption, clearer error classes) and minor version bumps for each SDK. Non-breaking to existing public APIs by default, opt-in behaviors documented.
payload.title: Introduce credential-swapper and resumable line-buffered streams (cross-SDK)

payload.body:
Motivation: We observed tail latency and throughput regressions on mixed-head models (MQA/GQA hybrids) and select Mistral variants when the kernel selector encountered too many head-stride polymorphisms. The runtime was spending CPU cycles in kernel dispatch, plus the GPU kernels saw suboptimal memory coalescing for attention key/value matrices encoded in the default layout. This PR introduces two complementary runtime optimizations: (1) a row-major attention repack pass that transforms KV/attn buffers into a coalesced-friendly layout for affected models, and (2) a lane harmonization preprocessor that groups attention heads into small homogeneous lanes to reduce kernel polymorphism and enable larger fused kernels. Both are gated by model metadata and a runtime probe to avoid regressions on models that are already optimal.

What I changed (high level):
- Added a new model onboarding hook that computes a per-model "repack map" and head-lane plan based on config (max heads per lane, head strides, and quantization footprint). The map is stored in model metadata and used by the serving runtime at first request to trigger an in-place repack when beneficial.
- Implemented a lightweight row-major repack routine in runtime/kernel/layout_repack.cc with careful pinned-memory staging to avoid extra GPU synchronizations. The routine supports both float32 and int8/quantized weight encodings and preserves KV cache compatibility by storing an indirection table in the model manifest.
- Implemented lane harmonization in runtime/scheduler/lane_harmonizer.cc which groups heads by stride/width and emits a lane descriptor that the kernel router can match to fewer kernel variants. The harmonizer also exposes a conservative fallback that keeps original head groupings if repack cost exceeds a runtime ROI threshold.
- Kernel selector updates in runtime/kernel/router.cc to prefer fused row-major kernels when a lane descriptor is present. I added a new kernel variant: fused_fwd_attn_rowmaj_{float32|int8} that assumes coalesced loads and uses a different shared-memory tiling strategy.
- Added unit and integration tests for the repack pass (tests/runtime/test_repack.py) and a small GPU benchmark harness (bench/gpu/attn_repack_bench.cc) used in CI perf sampling.

Commits (summary):
- 1a2b3f4: initial lane harmonizer prototype and unit tests
- 2b3c4d5: row-major repack implementation + pinned staging buffers
- 3c4d5e6: kernel router matching and fused kernel hooks + small kernel implementation
- 4d5e6f7: perf harness + docs + model metadata glue

Files touched (representative):
- runtime/kernel/layout_repack.cc
- runtime/scheduler/lane_harmonizer.cc
- runtime/kernel/router.cc
- kernel/kernels/fused_fwd_attn_rowmaj.cu
- bench/gpu/attn_repack_bench.cc
- tests/runtime/test_repack.py
- models/manifests/mistral-variants/repack-metadata.json

Key design notes and tradeoffs:
- Repacking is done lazily on first warm request to avoid extra prep work for cold models. The repack operation uses pinned staging buffers and a short-lived CUDA stream to write the coalesced layout; we avoid a blocking synchronize by using an event that gates the first inference that relies on the new layout. This reduces cold-start penalty to ~18-30ms on Mistral-7B families (measured on p4d-like instances).
- Lane harmonization reduces kernel selector branching at the cost of slight head-level padding. We tuned the max padding to 6-8% in the default plan to keep quality and per-token cost stable. Operators that rely on exact head indexing (rare) are supported via an indirection map so correctness is preserved.
- The fused row-major kernel is intentionally conservative in register pressure and uses a smaller tile when int8 quantization is detected. We found a 12-22% throughput uplift for MQA workloads on Mistral-7B variants and a 7-11% improvement for Llama-13B when lane harmonization matched heads to 4-head lanes. P95 latency improved by ~8-14% on continuous-batching workloads in our internal bench harness.

Safety and rollout plan:
- Feature gated via model metadata flag "enable_repack_lane_harmony" and a runtime probe that checks expected ROI. Default for existing manifests is off; new model onboarding can opt-in after offline analysis.
- Canary rollout: staged to 5% of traffic on dedicated clusters, with trace-level metrics for repack_time_ms, repack_roi_estimate, and lane_pad_pct. Added alerts if repack_time_ms > 3x estimate or if token-level token_cost increases > 5% post-repack.

Review summary and conversation (high level):
- Arjun: requested a clear fallback path for models with side-effecting layers that assume head ordering. I added an indirection table and tests exercising those cases.
- Lena: asked for quantized path validation; I added an int8 kernel and bench numbers including int8 variations.
- Diego: suggested avoiding repack at scale when GPU memory is highly utilized; I added a quick probe that checks free device memory and will delay repack under pressure.
- Author replies addressed all comments; small follow-up commit reduced staging buffer size and added more asserts in the lane harmonizer unit tests.
- Final status: reviewed and approved by reviewers above; perf engineering gave a thumbs-up after bench runs.

CI and perf checks:
- Linux unit tests: pass
- GPU bench job: flaky on first run (OOM on a crowded runner), re-run passed with baseline/perf numbers attached in CI artifact (see bench-results/attn_repack/2026-02-18).
- Lint and static analysis: pass
- Integration tests (models): pass on mainline nightly harness with Mistral/Llama/Qwen smoke tests.

Merge and follow-ups:
- Merged via squash to main on 2026-02-20.
- Follow-ups tracked in ENG-4450: add automatic model onboarding tool to produce repack metadata and a small telemetry job to surface models that would benefit most.

Release notes: 
- Added optional row-major attention repacking and lane harmonization to improve throughput on MQA/GQA and mixed-head Llama/Mistral models. Expected impact: 10-20% throughput improvement on targeted models and reduced P95 in continuous-batching scenarios. Opt-in by model manifest flag and staged rollout to prevent regressions.

If you want to run the perf harness locally: 
- See bench/gpu/attn_repack_bench.cc; example run: ./attn_repack_bench --model mistral-7b --batch 8 --seq 1024 --quant int8

Notes for release engineering: This change touches kernel selector and low-level CUDA paths; coordinate with infra upgrades for new kernel artifacts and ensure canary traffic includes both hosted and dedicated clusters to validate memory-pressure heuristics.
Optional row-major attention repacking + lane harmonization for MQA/GQA and mixed-head models. 10-20% throughput uplift on targeted models; opt-in via model manifest flag; staged rollout and telemetry added.
