Background: We've seen repeated scale-churn in Dedicated fleets when short spikes cause the autoscaler to open capacity aggressively and then quickly scale down, which degrades tail latency and burns commitments. This PR implements a thresholded elasticity limiter that gates scale actions with a temporal margin and a sampled utilization stream so the autoscaler can make decisions from a low-cardinality but statistically representative signal.

Motivation: reduce oscillation and cost while preserving throughput SLAs for tenants.

Design summary: 1) Elasticity limiter: a compact controller (pkg/autoscaler/elasticity_limiter.go) that computes a dynamic headroom threshold based on recent p50/p95 utilization and a configurable margin. Scale-up events are delayed for a short window_ms if the signal is near the threshold; repeated hits escalate to a graceful fast-path. Scale-downs are damped using the same margin but with longer hold-off to avoid premature decommits. 2) Sampled utilization reporting: a lightweight sampling pipeline (pkg/telemetry/sampler.go) subscribes to per-pool utilization heartbeats, performs reservoir sampling per-tenancy window, and emits aggregated percentiles to the controller. Sampling reduces ingest costs in the control plane and avoids full-cardinality telemetry for very large fleets. 3) Configuration and safety: feature flags and per-pool overrides are plumbed (internal/config/autoscaler.yaml) to allow staged rollout and emergency disable. The limiter uses a safe-fallback: if sampled data is missing, the autoscaler falls back to the legacy moving-average estimator.

Checklist:
- [x] Core limiter + unit tests
- [x] Sampling pipeline + integration test harness
- [x] Metrics and dashboards (docs/observability/metrics.md)
- [x] Controlled rollout via feature flag
- [x] Backwards-compatible fallbacks
- [x] Load tests against perf-canary and dedicated-staging (see pipeline results)

Commits summary: * 8d2f3c4 - initial limiter scaffolding and interfaces * f3b9aa1 - implement threshold heuristics and gating * 1b4c2e9 - reservoir sampler and publish path * 5c7d2a0 - wiring: config + feature-flag + e2e test * 2a1f0b7 - docs, dashboards, and runbook updates

Testing and CI: unit tests (pkg/autoscaler/*) cover threshold computation, backoff timers, and fallback semantics. Integration tests (e2e/tests/autoscale_scenarios_test.go) exercise short spike and sustained load scenarios against a local controller; perf-canary runs validated reduced scale churn (median scale events per minute dropped ~45% in synthetic 60s-spike test). CI: lint, unit, integration, and chart validation passed; a flakey e2e test was retried once and succeeded.

Files changed (high level): pkg/autoscaler/elasticity_limiter.go, pkg/autoscaler/elasticity_limiter_test.go, pkg/telemetry/sampler.go, pkg/telemetry/sampler_test.go, internal/config/autoscaler.yaml, internal/api/v1/autoscale.proto, cmd/controller/main.go (feature flag wiring), charts/dedicated/values.yaml, docs/observability/metrics.md, e2e/tests/autoscale_scenarios_test.go, scripts/perf/scale_scenarios.yaml, Makefile updates.

Rollout plan: staged canary on two small dedicated pools (canary-1, canary-2) for 48h with sampler at 10% sample_fraction, then expand to 30% and wider pools after monitoring p95 latency and scale event rate. Backout: flip feature flag to off; sampler publishes a tombstone to signal absence.

Observability: new metrics exported: limiter_decision{pool,tenant,decision}, sampled_util_p50/p95{pool,tenant}, sampler_sample_rate and sampler_dropped_count. Dashboards added and alert tuned to fire on limiter_decision == blocked AND p95_latency_increase > 15% for 10m.

Related work: follow-up ticket ENG-2080 to expose per-tenant recommender for threshold_margin, and SUP-4121 incident references where oscillation caused SLA miss.

Security & compliance: no new secrets; telemetry uses existing auth path.

Migration notes: config keys default to previous behavior; no required migrations.

Known limitations: reservoir sampling may underrepresent very small tenants; we enforce min_sample_size to mitigate.

Attribution: Priya Natarajan implemented the limiter and sampler; Samir Patel wrote the e2e harness; Marco Alvarez reviewed safety boundaries; Evelyn Cho owned dashboards and alerts.
Introduce a thresholded elasticity limiter to prevent oscillatory scale-ups during short-lived surges.
Add sampled utilization telemetry to reduce cardinality while preserving percentile signals for autoscaler tuning.
New config knobs: window_ms, threshold_margin, sample_fraction, min_sample_size.
Behavioral change: default sampler fraction is conservative; teams can opt-in to higher fidelity for dedicated pools.
Marco Alvarez: Can we avoid adding another timer if the controller already has a backoff queue? Suggest integrating with existing backoff to reduce churn.
Priya Natarajan: We investigated integrating with the backoff queue; the limiter needs a separate short-window gate to compute decisions without mutating the global backoff state. Added an adapter that reads backoff state but keeps limiter timers locally.
Evelyn Cho: Dashboard queries look good; please add an example alert query for on-call runbook. Also confirm SLI thresholds used in perf tests.
Priya Natarajan: Added alert query + runbook snippet to docs/observability/metrics.md and included SLI thresholds used in perf-canary in the PR description.

Priya Natarajan: Marked the e2e as Serial; CI run now passes consistently.

Summary: Introduces a separable-rotary microkernel that isolates rotary application from q/k/v transforms and a KV-adaptive continuous batcher that widens batching windows when prefix-hit probability is high. Motivation: production p99 latency for short chat turns; profiling showed general-purpose kernels and static batching were inefficient. Key changes: new CUDA microkernel with lane-aligned loads and small unrolls for common head sizes; deterministic rotary offset clamps; cache_manager API extension to report ring hit estimates; batcher policy that adapts per-route based on observed KV prefix-hit-rate and sequence variance; microbench harness and regression tests. Benchmarks: short sequences (8-32 tokens) throughput +24% and p99 -18%; medium (64-128) throughput +12% and p99 -9%; long sequences (512) negligible change. CI: unit and integration pass; perf microbench passed after pinning GPU CI image. Merge: squashed into main on 2026-02-22. Rollout notes: enable in Dedicated pools at 25% traffic first; dashboards and alerts added for batcher.window_size and kv.cache.prefix_hit_rate. Risks: rotary/rope mixing edge-cases handled with defensive clamps and tests; adaptive batching affects scheduling so rollout gating recommended.
Adds a separable rotary attention microkernel and an adaptive continuous batcher that uses KV prefix-hit heuristics. Improves short-turn throughput and p99 latency; no API changes.

Adds a modular presubmit 'ghostworker' process that prefetches toolchains and third-party deps in a separate, low-priority lane and a dep-harvester that snapshots transitive dependency metadata for lightweight presubmit validation. Motivation: reduce noisy presubmit failures from network/timeouts and shrink the main presubmit runtime by decoupling long I/O from lint/test runners. This PR introduces a new presubmit service (ci/ghostworker) with a containerized prefetcher, a dep-harvester binary (tools/dep-harvester) that emits a dep-manifest, and a presubmit router that routes PRs into fast/slow lanes based on a heuristic. Also adds a staged lint holdback to preserve a short fast-path for quick feedback and a migration script to populate initial dep snapshots. Includes docs, unit tests for the harvester, and telemetry for queueing latency.
3 commits: 1) Add ghostworker service and prefetch container image (ci: add ghostworker, Dockerfile, k8s job spec). 2) Implement dep-harvester binary and manifest schema (tools/dep-harvester, tests). 3) Presubmit router + migration script + docs and telemetry hooks. Each commit annotated with short msgs and signed off by author.
Reviewer Marco Alvarez: Please add retries around network fetch in the harvester; observed a transient failure in integration run. Author reply: Added exponential backoff and circuit-breaker, pushed a follow-up commit. Reviewer Leila Rahman: The presubmit-router heuristic needs a clear opt-out for teams that want deterministic runs. Author reply: Added PR label opt-out 'presubmit:force-fast' and a per-repo config in ci/presubmit-config.yaml. Reviewer Tom Brewer: Can we ensure the ghostworker respects quota and avoids prefetching private packages without creds? Author reply: Ghostworker will only prefetch public registries by default and reads per-repo credentials from a sealed secret; documented behavior updated.
CI checks initially: presubmit/fast-lint failed due to a flaky test (timeout on external registry fetch). Reran ghostworker job to seed cache; subsequent CI run passed: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, lint: pass, integration-smoke: pass, e2e-nightly: skipped. Coverage delta: -0.1%.
Merged by squash on 2026-02-23 by Leila Rahman after 2 approvals. Merge commit message summarizes ghostworker + dep-harvester and notes follow-up tickets for infra scaling and RBAC for secrets. Changelog: presubmit: introduce ghostworker prefetch lane and dep-harvester; infra: add presubmit-router; docs updated. Post-merge notes: rollout to canary orgs for 48h then full enablement.
presubmit: introduce ghostworker prefetch service; tools: add dep-harvester to snapshot transitive deps; ci: presubmit routing into fast/slow lanes and opt-out label; infra: telemetry for presubmit queueing; migration: scripts to seed initial dep snapshots.
Follow-ups: ENG-3523 (scale ghostworker to handle repo surge), ENG-3524 (RBAC for credentialed prefetch), ENG-3525 (add UI in Console to view dep-manifests and presubmit queue).

Motivation: In recent incidents we observed rapid circuit reopen/close oscillations when regional capacity fluctuated, which led to cascading SLO degradations. This PR introduces a Tiered Circuit Entropy Stabilizer: a lightweight state machine that applies probabilistic cooloff, tiered reopen windows, and jittered reopen attempts to prevent synchronized flips across nodes. Design: 1) Introduce three tiers for circuits: healthy, guarded, quarantined. 2) On transition to guarded/quarantined, attach a randomized cooloff window derived from a configurable entropy seed to avoid herd reopen. 3) Reopen attempts use exponentially increasing jitter and a capped backoff to avoid saturating downstream capacity. 4) Penalize circuits that reopen too frequently by increasing their tier severity. 5) Emit new telemetry: circuit_entropy.seed, circuit_tier.transition, circuit_reopen.attempts, circuit_reopen.jitter_ms. Backwards compatibility: feature gated behind runtime flag "tiered_circuit_entropy" defaulting to true for release; config bump in values-stability.yaml included for Dedicated and Private installs. Migration and rollout: deploy to canary zone for 24h with synthetic replay (scripts/loadtest/oscillation-replay.yaml), monitor the new metrics and SLO regression alerts, then promote. Testing: unit tests for state transitions, fuzz test harness added to reproducer, and an integration scenario that simulates regional KV drain and verifies no more than 2 rapid reopen cycles within 5 minutes. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of stabilizer state machine - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Telemetry hooks + metric names - [x] Helm values and feature flag - [x] Canary loadtest playbook - [x] Docs: upgrade guide and operational notes Impact: reduces probability of synchronized reopen by introducing entropy and tiered backoff; expected to lower incident recurrence frequency and SLO violation blast radius. Rollback plan: disable feature flag or revert to previous binary; metrics allow quick detection of regressions. Related: Linear ENG-1987, support ticket SUP-4123.
Asha: This looks promising. Two concerns: are entropy seeds per-node stable across restarts? Also please ensure metrics have cardinality controls. | Elliot: Entropy seed persists in local node metadata, we fall back to env-seed on fresh nodes. Added cardinality notes to metrics.yaml and bound the seed space. | Diego: Can we avoid any heavy locks on hot paths? The stabilizer uses atomics and per-circuit sharded timers, minimized locking; added microbenchmarks in stabilizer_test.go. | Priya: Add more observability for tier transitions so SRE can tune thresholds. | Elliot: Added circuit_tier.transition and a dashboard snippet in docs/upgrade/circuit-stabilizer.md. | Asha: CI flaked on one integration; reran and it passed. Approving now.
payload.title: Tiered circuit entropy stabilizer to reduce repeated reopen oscillations

Motivation: Streaming responses that must satisfy a JSON Schema present a challenge when mid-stream validation fails or downstream tool-calls are triggered. Existing approaches either abruptly terminate the stream (breaking client parsers) or attempt heavy-weight rollbacks. This PR introduces a lightweight 'response_offramp' mechanism plus an OpenAI-compatibility shim to ensure predictable, client-friendly behavior for schema violations and function-call boundaries.

What it does (high level): Adds a new response_format variant (response_format="json_offramp") and a runtime offramp code path that emits a compact final envelope when schema enforcement fails in streaming mode. The envelope contains a concise error_code, user-facing message, and minimal diagnostic hints (schema_path and validation_summary). OpenAI-compat adapter maps the envelope to a final chunk with finish_reason set to "schema_error_offramp" and a small, parsable metadata payload so existing OpenAI-based clients can detect and handle schema failures without crashing.

Key user-facing changes: - New response_format option: json_offramp (fallback semantics documented) - New SDK surface: `Stream.onOfframp()` (Python/TS/Go SDKs updated) - OpenAI-compat shim will translate offramp envelopes into a single final SSE/event payload with explicit finish_reason for backward compatibility - A non-strict path is still available: strict_mode="off" (previous default), strict_mode="error" (current strict), strict_mode="offramp" (new; emits envelope and marks generation complete).

Implementation notes: - Runtime: added an offramp emission stage in streaming state machine; when validator detects an unrecoverable schema mismatch after the streaming commit point, it switches to the offramp stage instead of hard-closing the stream. - Validator: lightweight incremental validator now tracks schema_path of first failing token and composes a short validation_summary rather than full diff to keep wire payload small. - Toolcall anchoring: when a tool call is in-flight, the offramp includes a tool_anchor field so callers can deterministically decide whether to retry, abort, or invoke the tool with partial context. - OpenAI-compat adapter: implements deterministic mapping of offramp envelope to an SSE final chunk compatible with common OpenAI client expectations. - Telemetry: new metrics (offramp.count, offramp.latency, offramp.by_schema) and an example dashboard were added.

Backward compatibility and migration: Existing clients are unaffected by default. The new behavior is opt-in via response_format or strict_mode. OpenAI-compat clients receive a clear finish_reason so existing parsers can detect and surface user-friendly messages instead of failing with truncated JSON.

Testing and rollout: Unit and integration tests added for streaming validator, offramp envelope composition, SDK callbacks, and OpenAI-compat mapping. Canary rollout on Dedicated region eu-west-1 for 48 hours followed by global rollout.

Related work: complements ENG-8470 (stream-snapshot-repair) and PM-431 (structured-output-ux), addresses several incidents where client parsers crashed due to abrupt stream termination (SUP-1291).
Connor Liu: Please ensure offramp envelopes are under 1KB — clients in low-bandwidth mobile scenarios need a small payload. Suggest truncating validation_summary and sending a link to verbose diagnostics in the console.
Aisha Patel: Implemented size cap and added telemetry link for verbose diagnostics (see telemetry change).
María Gomez: Can we make the default strict_mode remain unchanged? We should not surprise users. Also request explicit doc note for SDK de-serialization behavior.
Aisha Patel: Kept default unchanged and added migration guide + SDK behavior notes.
Added opt-in response_format="json_offramp" and strict_mode="offramp" to emit compact schema-error envelopes for streaming responses; OpenAI-compat adapter maps these to finish_reason="schema_error_offramp". SDKs expose onOfframp/on_offramp hooks. Opt-in only; default behavior unchanged.
payload.title: Introduce response_offramp for graceful schema failures and OpenAI-compat shim

Motivation: We've observed oscillatory circuit flips and repeated cross-region handoffs during transient overloads which amplify downstream tail latency and cause regional instability. This PR introduces a "circuit dampener" layer that applies a sticky backoff window to circuits entering a degraded state and performs proactive in-flight queue trimming when initiating a regional handoff. The goal is to reduce flip-flop behavior, smooth traffic redistribution, and avoid cascading evictions while preserving SLOs. Changes: 1) runtime/slo/dampener: new dampener controller that records recent circuit events and enforces a sticky backoff period (configurable) before allowing circuit to transition back to healthy. 2) routing/region_handoff: integrate dampener checks into handoff path; when a handoff is triggered the router trims low-priority requests from the local queue and annotates traces with dampener decisions. 3) config: add circuit_dampener.{yaml,example} with parameters (backoff_ms, max_trims_per_window, priority_cutoff). 4) observability: metrics (dampener.suppressed_transitions, handoff.queue_trims, dampener.backoff_seconds) and traces for decision points; dashboards updated in docs/ops/region-dampener-dashboard.md. 5) tests: unit and integration tests for dampener state machine and an end-to-end canary scenario that simulates a burst and cross-region failover. Rollout plan: feature gate redwood.runtime.circuit_dampener is default-off in main, enabled in a single canary region for 24h with synthetic load tests and SLO monitoring. If stable, expand to 30% of traffic, then full rollout. Fallback: if dampener causes unexpected regressions we include an automated kill-switch (redwood.runtime.circuit_dampener=false) and a short-circuit route that forces legacy behavior per-tenant. Config knobs: backoff_ms (default 15000), max_trims_per_window (default 8), sticky_threshold (ratio of degraded events). Observability & validation: new Grafana panels and alerts tied to dampener.suppressed_transitions and handoff.queue_trims; added smoke scripts in observability-pack for canary validation. Security and perf: changes are read-only to routing decision paths except queue-trim code which requires careful CPU allocation; microbenchmarks show <1% additional tail CPU under high load. Related work: builds on ENG-1045 (regional handoff refactor) and complements recent SLO enforcer improvements. Testing: unit tests and integration tests passed; CI initially flaked on a timing-sensitive test which was hardened and re-run. Merge: squash merge to main after approvals.
Adds a circuit dampener that reduces oscillation during cross-region failover by applying a sticky backoff window and queue trimming heuristics. Default behaviour is conservative and gated behind flags; rollout to production will be canary-first.
Eleni Ward: Can we make the default backoff shorter for canary to reduce risk? Answer: kept conservative (15s) after perf tests showed 10s was still too noisy.
Marcus Li: queue trimming might affect low-latency customers — added a priority_cutoff and tenant opt-out documented in the config.
Devon Kapoor: please add an alert to detect population mismatch during handoff. Added dampener.population_mismatch alert in docs and example rules.
payload.title: introduce-circuit-dampener-with-sticky-backoff-for-cross-region-handoff

Motivation:
Reducing developer fatigue from noisy presubmit runs while keeping fast feedback for regressions. This PR introduces a lightweight "preflight-sideline" workflow that runs fast static checks and targeted smoke tests in parallel with the existing presubmit lanes, plus a ci-hygiene-sweeper tool that identifies stale devdeps, unused workflows, and expired runner labels. It also separates the monolithic 'toolchain bootstrap' manifest into stable runtime and ephemeral dev toolchain manifests so CI can fetch smaller images for presubmit fastpath.

What this PR does (summary):
- Add .github/workflows/preflight-sideline.yml: a fast, low-cost job that runs TypeScript typecheck, python-flake/black quick checks, and a small smoke harness against a cached toolchain image. Designed to run on push and PR concurrently but with lower concurrency and quiet notifications.
- Add tools/ci/sweeper.py: a scheduled script (weekly) that collects package.json/pipfile snapshots, flags devdeps not referenced in any package or scripts, and makes a maintenance report in Linear. The script supports a --dry-run mode and an enterprise flag to disable auto-suggestion edits.
- Split ci/toolchains/toolchain-manifests.yaml into ci/toolchains/runtime-manifest.yaml and ci/toolchains/devtools-manifest.yaml. The runtime manifest is used by nightly/integration pipelines; the devtools manifest is smaller and prioritized for presubmit.
- Minimal refactor of scripts/presubmit-wrapper.sh to honor PRELIGHT_FAST=true and early-exit for long-running steps when preflight-sideline already passed.
- Update docs/ci.md with rationale, opt-out flags, and examples for on-call/SE teams.
- Bump a handful of CI action pins (actions/checkout@v4 -> v4.1 pinned commit) and add an integration test that asserts preflight job completes within 120s on typical runner.

Checklist:
- [x] Add preflight-sideline workflow and runner labels
- [x] Implement ci-hygiene-sweeper with dry-run and report modes
- [x] Split toolchain manifests and update presubmit wrapper to prefer devtools manifest
- [x] Update docs and RELEASE_NOTES
- [x] Add unit tests for sweeper logic and a lightweight integration smoke test for preflight

Commits (high level):
- feat(ci): add preflight-sideline workflow and job templates
- feat(ci): introduce ci-hygiene-sweeper script and scheduler
- refactor(ci): split toolchain manifest into runtime/devtools
- chore(ci): pin actions and update bootstrap helper
- test(ci): add unit tests for sweeper and preflight smoke harness
- docs: document new workflow and opt-out flags in ci.md

Files touched (high level):
- .github/workflows/preflight-sideline.yml
- .github/workflows/ci-scheduler.yml (added weekly trigger for sweeper)
- tools/ci/sweeper.py (+ tests tools/ci/test_sweeper.py)

- .github/actions/pinned-versions.json (minor pins)

Testing and CI behavior:
- Local unit tests: all passing (python pytest for sweeper; ts typecheck for preflight harness)
- CI: initial run showed build-image job failing due to stale base image tag. Updated manifest and re-ran; subsequent run passed.
- Preflight job is gated to quiet notifications: failed preflight will not send noise to #dev-notifications, it will create a single aggregated thread comment on the PR.

Review notes and decisions:
- Sweeper requires explicit opt-in (default dry-run). We debated auto-PR creation for devdep removals; decided against it for now to avoid churn. See comment thread below.
- The toolchain split intentionally keeps the runtime manifest stable to reduce image churn for longtests and integration pipelines. Devtools manifest is re-generated by the existing toolchain generation pipeline.
- Presubmit-wrapper early-exit behavior is conservative: it only skips long linters when PRELIGHT_FAST succeeded and the changed paths are limited to codegen/docs/infra files.

Migration plan:
- Roll out preflight-sideline as opt-in to teams for 1 week, then enable org-wide with a 48h rollback window controlled by feature flag in .github/ci-flags.yml.
- Schedule ci-hygiene-sweeper in the next maintenance window; start with dry-run reports to team leads for 2 weeks before enabling suggestions.

Related work:

Potential risks and mitigations:

- Risk: sweeper suggestions remove needed devdeps. Mitigation: dry-run default and owner review required before edits.

The CI toolchain manifests are split to reduce presubmit image size. These changes reduce developer notifications and improve presubmit turnaround time."

Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally hit transient short-duration demand spikes that cannot be satisfied by the normal reservation allocator without over-provisioning. Large allocations for these very short events pump cost and destabilize fairness. This PR introduces a deferred reservation proxy layer that accepts short-duration admission requests, settles reservations asynchronously against the main ledger, and exposes a lightweight gating signal (shortburst-gate) that upstream routers and admission controllers can consult to make fast local decisions. Design: 1) deferred_proxy component runs as an independent actor in the autoscaler with a small memory-only ledger for tentative admits; it uses optimistic admission and then attempts to commit to the primary reservation store with bounded retries. 2) shortburst-gate signal summarizes recent tentative admit density, commit success ratio, and time-to-commit distribution; it is emitted at 5s granularity. 3) a sentinel reporter aggregates gate metrics into the observability stack and triggers an SLO degradation alert if commit-ratio<80% for a sustained window. 4) a feature flag (dedicated.deferred_proxy.enabled) controls rollout and a safe-mode path falls back to immediate reservation semantics. Implementation notes: added circuit-breaker to limit concurrency against reservation store, exponential backoff on commits, and strict idempotency keys to avoid double-commit. API: no user-facing API changes; config knobs in configs/dedicated/defaults.yaml and operator-facing flags for rollout. Tests: unit tests for optimistic admit logic, integration test that simulates commit contention and verifies fallback. Deployment: staged rollout behind feature flag, start with 5% of fleets for 48h then 25% then 100% if metrics stable. Related work: builds on prior autoscaler improvements (ENG-4210) but focuses on ephemeral admission smoothing rather than long-term credits.
Arjun: Can we tighten the concurrency ceiling on commit_client to avoid an N+1 storm during global restores? Suggest default 32 -> 8.
Maya: lowered default to 8, added circuit-breaker tests and a runtime knob dedicated.deferred_proxy.commit_concurrency
Sofia: CI flaked on e2e sim, can you add a deterministic seed?
Maya: added deterministic seed and simplified timing in simulator; re-ran CI, green
Devon: please add a clear rollout plan in the PR description and a kill-switch path for operators
Maya: added rollout plan (5%->25%->100%) and explicit feature-flag off path; documented kill-switch in configs/dedicated/defaults.yaml
Sofia: approved after minor comments (LGTM)
Arjun: approved (code-reviewed)
Adds a deferred reservation proxy and shortburst gating signal to allow lightweight, optimistic admission for short-lived demand spikes. Helps reduce over-provisioning and smooth transient surges while preserving fairness. Rollout behind feature flag; requires no customer API change.
Unit tests added for commit idempotency, concurrency ceilings, and backoff. Integration sim reproduces commit contention and validates fallback to immediate reservation. E2E fixture exercises the feature flag path. Manual canary: enable on small fleet subset, validate commit_success_ratio>90% and queue latency impact <10ms p95 before scaling rollout.
Synthetic load test against a 200-node dedicated fleet: with deferred proxy enabled p50 admission latency unchanged, p95 admission latency increased by 4ms on accepted path, overall reservation store QPS reduced by ~18%, and measured cost simulations show ~3.5% lower transient allocation cost during bursty workloads. Short-term tail instability observed when commit_ratio dropped below 60% which triggered sentinel and immediate fallback; this was addressed by lowering commit concurrency and adding backoff.
No breaking changes. Feature behind flag. Operators should monitor dedicated.deferred_proxy.commit_success_ratio and dedicated.shortburst.gate_open_ratio during rollout.
payload.title: Deferred reservation proxy + shortburst-gating SLO sentinel

payload.body:
Background and motivation: We observed multiple production incidents where streaming tool calls retried incorrectly due to ambiguous Retry-After semantics and lack of a per-session idempotency context. OpenAI-compatible clients expect simple Retry-After behavior, but multiplexed streams and function/tool calls need richer signals so that SDKs and proxies can make correct retrying decisions without accidental double-execution. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) a machine-readable, opaque Retry-Advice header (X-Redwood-Retry-Advice) that encodes backoff windows and optional short-term lease tokens for idempotency coordination; and (2) an Idempotency-Session token surfaced in stream init frames and the HTTP layer to tie retries to a single logical session across reconnects.

Summary of changes:
- API layer: add X-Redwood-Retry-Advice header generator and parser, documented encoding (base64 JSON envelope) and fallback rules.
- Stream protocol: include idempotency_session_id in the initial handshake frame (and as an HTTP header for non-streamed endpoints).
- SDK compat: OpenAI-compat adapter maps Retry-Advice to Retry-After when possible and logs advisory reasons.
- Server runtime: produce Retry-Advice on capacity-related 429s and transient worker errors; conservative advice when admission control is uncertain.
- Tests: unit tests for header encoding/decoding, integration tests with reconnect+retry scenarios, and a small load test demonstrating reduced duplicate tool invocations.
- Docs: API surface doc updates and migration guidance for SDKs and proxies.

Checklist:
- [x] API design review (ENG-8432)
- [x] Backwards compatible: existing clients still see Retry-After or 429 as today
- [x] Add unit and integration tests
- [x] Observability: metrics + tracing for retry-advice issued
- [x] Rollout plan included
- [x] Docs & migration notes

Commits summary:
- a1f3c9b add retry-advice encoder/decoder and tests
- b5d2e10 surface idempotency_session_id in stream handshake
- c3f4a88 openai-compat: map retry-advice to retry-after header when possible
- d9b7e1f server: emit retry-advice for admission-control 429s
- e4c1027 integration tests: reconnect + idempotency session scenarios
- f671b3e docs: migration and examples

Files changed (high-level):
- server/api/retry_advice.go (new)
- server/streams/handshake.go (handshake frame changes)
- sdk/compat/openai_adapter.go (mapping logic + logging)
- sdk/types/protocol.md (doc)
- tests/integration/retry_advice_reconnect_test.go (new)
- docs/guides/retry_advice.md (new)
- telemetry/metrics/retry_advice_metrics.prom (new)
- CHANGELOG.md

Compatibility and semantics:
- The Retry-Advice header is opaque to clients: it encodes a JSON envelope with fields (advice_ttl_seconds, recommended_backoff_ms, lease_token_optional, reason). The header is base64(json) and intended for SDKs and proxies that can parse it.
- Fallback precedence: 1) If Retry-After header is present and the server explicitly set it, clients SHOULD honor it. 2) If X-Redwood-Retry-Advice is present, clients MAY use its recommended_backoff_ms as an advisory. 3) If neither is present, clients follow existing exponential backoff heuristics.
- Idempotency-session: when present, it is a server-side ephemeral opaque token (UUIDv4-like) that ties the logical tool/function invocation session across reconnects; clients include it on reconnect attempts so the server can associate retries with prior state and avoid duplicate function invocations.

Observability and rollout:
- New metrics: retry_advice_emitted{reason}, idempotency_session_reused, duplicate_tool_invocations_blocked
- Create dashboards for retriable-errors, percent of streaming reconnects using idempotency_session
- Rollout plan: staged on Canary (10%), then Dedicated, then Hosted. Feature flag gated for first 2 weeks.

Migration guidance for SDKs:
- Parse X-Redwood-Retry-Advice when available and prefer its numeric fields for backoff decisions.
- On reconnect, include previous idempotency_session_id if network error occurred within TTL.
- OpenAI-compat adapter continues to expose Retry-After for simplicity but logs the presence of Retry-Advice for future migration.

Tests and CI:
- Unit tests added for encoder/decoder and handshake behavior
- Integration test simulates reconnect with a tool call: server returns retry-advice and subsequent reconnect includes idempotency_session -> server suppresses duplicate invocation
- Load test with 1000 concurrent short streams shows duplicate tool invocations drop by ~72% vs. baseline with naive retries.
- CI initially failed on lint (openapi spec mismatch), fixed in follow-up commit and all checks passed.

Review thread (highlights):
"Jonas Rivera (reviewer): The envelope looks fine but we should avoid leaking actionable tokens to user logs — ensure lease_token is redacted in telemetry." — Author reply: "Agreed; lease_token is marked sensitive and only hashed before emitting to logs; updated telemetry code in b5d2e10." "Priya Shah (reviewer): How does this interact with long-tail client libraries that only look at Retry-After?" — Author reply: "OpenAI-compat maps the numeric recommended_backoff_ms to Retry-After seconds when present; docs added to guide SDKs on gradual migration (see docs/guides/retry_advice.md)." "Samir Kulkarni: Can we avoid adding a new header if Retry-After already suffices?" — Author reply: "We emit Retry-Advice only when richer context is available (e.g., lease_token or precise backoff_window) or when we anticipate reconnection attempts; otherwise we keep current Retry-After behavior." "QA: Found a race in session reuse on reconnect when two reconnects happen concurrently; fixed by session compare-and-set in stream manager (commit e4c1027)." "OPS: Please add metric for 'retry_advice_issued' tagged by region — added telemetry change and dashboard sample."

CI timeline:
- Initial run (2026-01-20): unit tests pass, integration tests flaky (2/4), lint failed (openapi docs)
- Fixes applied (2026-01-24): bump openapi schema and stabilize integration, re-run CI
- Final run (2026-01-29): all checks green (unit+integration+lint+e2e), canary load test executed in staging with expected reduction in duplicate tool calls.

Merge rationale and outcome: This change improves robustness of streamed tool/function calls by giving richer, machine-readable guidance for backoff and a mechanism to reliably identify retry sessions. It is backwards compatible with clients that only observe Retry-After. After approvals from reviewers and successful staging canary, the branch was squashed and merged into main on 2026-02-02.

Notes and future work:
- Proposal to standardize Retry-Advice envelope across other Redwood services (follow-up ENG-8699).
- Consider exposing a lightweight, non-sensitive 'retry_hint' JSON in a future minor release for non-SDK proxies.
- SDK changes (python/ts/go) will land in separate PRs that consume the header and implement session reuse logic.

Summary: Introduce a small, ergonomic surface across the Python/TypeScript/Go SDK packages that makes credential hints and stream consumer wiring simpler for application code. Motivation: customers repeatedly ask for clearer token lifecycle guidance and helper hooks that let applications opt-in to lightweight session leases and prefetch heartbeat semantics without embedding runtime-specific logic. This PR implements: 1) A CredentialHints struct/option (Python: CredentialHints, TS: CredentialHintsOptions, Go: CredentialHints) that allows callers to provide non-sensitive metadata (e.g., 'product', 'purpose', 'session_ttl_hint') that the connector and orchestrator can use to improve warmup/route decisions. 2) A StreamHelpers module with a small set of helpers: auto_retry_iterable (py), streamReconnectHelper (ts), and StreamGuard (go) to centralize backoff/coalesce behavior, expose a typed on_reconnect callback, and standardize graceful shutdown semantics across SDKs. 3) A session lease helper (opt-in) that surfaces lease_acquired/lease_revoked callbacks and a light-weight heartbeat utility used by Redwood Private deployments; it's documented as opt-in and off by default. 4) Version bumps for the SDK package artifacts in the monorepo: python 0.9.3 -> 0.9.4, typescript 1.6.1 -> 1.6.2, go 1.5.2 -> 1.5.3. payload.body:
Motivation: We routinely see noisy long-tail cost and latency signals that are hard to attribute to a small set of invocation characteristics (prompt shape, model variant, routing policy, KV cache hit pattern). Existing rollups and token histograms capture macro trends but fail to isolate correlated spectral patterns that indicate systemic regressions (e.g., a specific prompt family that triggers elevated per-token cost during particular time windows). This PR introduces an end-to-end feature set: Invocation Scenario Profiling + Spectral Cost Anchors.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a lightweight invocation "scenario" fingerprint computed at ingress which captures a compact signature of: prompt-shape bucket, caller-client, model variant tag, first-k token entropy bucket, and observed KV cache hit class. The fingerprint is intentionally low-cardinality (target: < 10k active cohorts) and stable across retries.
- Emits two new metrics per invocation: scenario_id (label), per_invocation_token_cost_us (microseconds-per-token equivalent), and spectral_cost_vector (a small 4-bin spectrum that summarizes token-cost distribution across the first N tokens). Metrics are emitted via our existing telemetry pipeline (metric name prefixes telemetry.inv.scenario.*) with aggregation-friendly labels.
- Implements a sampling service (spectral-anchor-sampler) in observability/ingest that performs reservoir sampling on scenario cohorts to store representative spectral vectors and a short example trace per cohort. This enables low-cost storage of cohort exemplars for dive-in analysis.
- Adds a Grafana dashboard (dashboards/observability/invocation_scenarios.json) with: scenario cohort heatmap, spectral anchor gallery (exemplar traces), per-scenario P50/P95 cost lines, and a cohort drift sparkline.
- Adds an adaptive alert: if a scenario's spectral centroid shifts by more than a configured threshold AND its per-invocation cost increases by > 15% for a rolling hour and the scenario frequency > 0.05% of traffic, open a Severity-2 incident for investigation (tuning defaults provided).
- Documentation: new docs/observability/invocation-scenarios.md describing how to interpret cohorts, tuning knobs, and migration notes.

Implementation notes and constraints:
- The scenario fingerprint code lives in runtime/ingress/profile.py and is feature-flag guarded with config: observability.scenario_profiling.enabled (default: off for private deployments; on for hosted beta).
- To avoid high-cardinality issues we cap unique scenario labels via hashing into a fixed bucket space and expose a telemetry.inv.scenario.bucket label. High-cardinality clients will see collisions but sampling retains exemplar traces for dominant traffic shapes.
- spectral_cost_vector is a compact string-encoded histogram (base64 of 4 bytes) to keep metric cardinality low; downstream processing decodes it into a 4-bin vector. The choice of 4 bins was an empirical tradeoff between expressiveness and metric cardinality.
- Storage for exemplar traces is limited to one exemplar per cohort per 24h by the sampler; retention is driven by observability.sampler.retention_days (default 7).

Commits (summary):
- Add scenario fingerprint generator and unit tests (runtime/ingress/profile.py) (+58/-3)
- Emit scenario metrics at ingress and enrich span tags (telemetry/emitter.py) (+104/-12)
- Add spectral-anchor-sampler microservice and reservoir implementation (observability/sampler/) (+168/-24)
- Grafana dashboard and small dashboard utils (dashboards/observability/invocation_scenarios.json, dashboards/utils) (+42/-0)
- Docs and runbook (docs/observability/invocation-scenarios.md) (+49/-3)

Changed areas (high-level):
- runtime/ingress/profile.py: new profiler and unit tests
- telemetry/emitter.py: metric emission points and labels
- observability/sampler/: new service that runs alongside metric ingest processors
- dashboards/observability/invocation_scenarios.json: dashboard panels and layout
- docs/observability/invocation-scenarios.md: user guide and alert tuning notes

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for fingerprint stability across small perturbations to prompts.
- Integration test that simulates 10k synthetic scenarios and verifies sampler retains exemplars for top-k cohorts and falls back cleanly when bucket collisions occur.
- E2E in staging: load test with 100k invocations/hour to validate that metric cardinality growth is bounded and that the sampler memory footprint remains stable (observed < 150MB).
- Dashboard smoke tests added to ci/grafana-smoke.sh to assert panel JSON loads and basic queries return non-empty results.

Review conversation (high level):
- Mateo Ruiz: "Nice approach. Two asks: (1) add an operator-friendly circuit-breaker so the sampler can be torn down if it starts to thrash; (2) make alert thresholds configurable via cluster-level config maps."
- Asha Patel (author): "Added sampler.enable circuit breaker and configmap-driven thresholds. Put defaults in config/observability.yaml; documented in the runbook."
- Grace Li: "Can we avoid base64 string for spectral vector — tough to query in sub-second dashboards?"
- Asha: "We keep the base64 for metric emission to avoid cardinality explosion; the sampler stores decoded vectors in exemplars which the dashboard queries separately. Added note to docs explaining the two-step decode flow."
- Oliver Bennett: "Please add a short hotfix plan if a cohort alert floods SRE."
- Asha: "Added runbook section and a quick CLI to mute a scenario cohort via 'rbacctl obs mute-scenario <bucket>' which SRE can use."

CI status: CI initially failed on lint (line length in docs) and one flaky grafana-smoke test. After fixes: lint and grafana smoke pass, unit & integration tests pass, e2e staging validated.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature gated rollout: enable for 10% of hosted traffic for one week, monitor SLI for metric ingestion lag and sampler memory.
2) Gradually increase to 50% and then full rollout if no regressions.
3) For Dedicated/Private customers the feature is off by default; on request we enable in a controlled beta with config guidance.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- All changes are additive; no schema changes to existing metrics. Dashboards are optional. If the sampler is not enabled, nothing is stored beyond emitted metrics.

Operational notes:
- Expected steady-state metric cardinality increase: +0.8% in medium clusters (measured in staging).
- Sampler memory usage: ~1–2MB per active cohort. Defaults limit cohorts to the top 2k by frequency to bound memory.
- If an alert floods, operators can mute by cohort bucket via rbacctl or scale down sampler replicas.

Why this is valuable:
This PR gives SRE and Product teams a practical way to find actionable cohorts driving cost and latency regressions — not just signal on aggregate percentiles. The spectral anchors provide compact exemplars that make investigating root cause (prompt shape, model variant, or routing policy) much faster than chasing noisy percentiles.

Follow-ups:
- Add lightweight per-cohort A/B comparison panels to measure quality regressions aligned with cost drift (ENG-2214).
- Explore automated remediation playbooks that propose route-policy fallbacks when a high-frequency scenario becomes expensive.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main by Asha Patel on 2026-02-25 after green CI and successful staging validation.
Adds invocation scenario profiling metrics, a new spectral cost anchor sampler, Grafana dashboard panels for scenario cohorts, and tuned alerts for spectral anomaly windows. Backwards compatible; opt-in via config flag.

payload.body:
Context: production traffic exposed noisy tail latency for Llama and Mistral MQA models where small micro-batches scatter KV cache lookups across GPU kernels causing suboptimal kernel dispatch and extra device-to-host synchronization. This PR introduces two complementary runtime techniques: 1) lookup coalescing — group KV read requests across micro-batches within a scheduling window so a single contiguous GPU memread services multiple tokens; 2) batch-stitching/token-stitching — align and stitch adjacent micro-batches with compatible shapes so subsequent attention kernels see larger steady work units. Motivation: reduce per-token overhead, increase kernel throughput, and avoid pathological kernel launches for mixed MQA/GQA sequences. What changed (high level): implemented a coalescing layer in the KV cache read path that accumulates small read ranges for up to configurable micro-window milliseconds and issues coalesced device reads; added micro-batch alignment logic in the batcher that optionally merges compatible requests if their rotary/position offset ranges match policy; introduced a KV-slab heuristic table per-model for MQA to select slab sizes and spill thresholds (with safety caps to prevent OOM behavior on small GPUs); added a fallback path that preserves latency SLOs by falling back to uncoalesced reads when cross-model conflicts are detected; extended tracing and metrics to surface coalesce hit/miss, stitched-batch counts, and micro-window wait times. Commits: ["Init lookup coalescing layer and tests", "Batcher: batch-stitching implementation and policy flags", "Per-model KV slab heuristic + config table", "Tracing/metrics and perf lab harness updates", "Canary rollout gating and rollback hooks", "Fix: alignment bug for rotary embeddings with odd token offsets"]. Files changed (high level): ["runtime/batcher/coalesce_batcher.cpp", "runtime/kv/kv_coalesce.cpp", "runtime/kv/kv_slab_heuristics.yaml", "runtime/kernels/dispatch_router.cpp", "sdk/benchmarks/microbench/mqa_coalesce_bench.cc", "observability/metrics/kv_coalesce.promql", "perf-canary/configs/mqa-canary.json", "tests/runtime/test_kv_coalesce.py", "docs/perf/mqa_coalescing.md"]. Tests and CI: unit tests added for coalesce boundary conditions and rotary alignment; microbench harness updated to simulate MQA conditions. CI run initially flagged a flake in the perf-canary integration test due to timing sensitivity; fixed by tightening the canary client timing and reran. Final CI status: pass on main (linux, macOS, perf-canary). Benchmarks: on our perf lab (A10g, batcher policy=aggressive, sequence len distribution sampled from customer workload) we observe median latency ~3% change, p90 ~8% reduction, p99 ~12% reduction, and sustained throughput improvement of ~18% for mixed-length MQA workloads versus baseline. Observed small regression (1.6% p50 increase) on extremely short sequences due to extra micro-window wait — mitigated by per-model policy defaults that disable stitching for seq_len<=4. Review convo highlights: Amit: asked for safety caps and rollback plan; requested additional logs for canary failure modes. Author (Sofia): added slab caps and canary gates; replied with implementation details and load-tested rollback. Priya: requested benchmark reproducibility; author added harness config and seed details. Liam: approved after nit on metric naming and one small memory-leak fix. Rollout plan: staged canary in perf-canary for 72h, then 50% traffic on Dedicated clusters with monitoring dashboards for kv_coalesce_hit_rate, stitched_batch_ratio, and p99 token latency; automatic rollback if p99 regresses >5% or memory pressure spikes >10% above baseline. Backout: feature flag at runtime to disable coalescing and stitching with immediate effect; configuration stored per-deployment. Risks and mitigations: risk of memory pressure on tiny GPUs addressed via slab heuristic caps and immediate fallbacks; risk of increased latency for very short sequences mitigated by default policy to skip stitching for short requests. Related: touches scheduling and kernel routing logic; coordinated with ENG-10021 to avoid overlapping kernel-router changes. Conclusion: merged to main via squash; shipping metrics/observability and canary gating in place to monitor impact across fleets.
Improves MQA latency by coalescing KV lookups and aligning micro-batches; reduces p99 by ~12% and increases throughput by ~18% for Llama and Mistral on tested GPU profiles. Includes heuristics for spill-to-CPU thresholds and safer fallbacks for rotary embedding misalignment.
Amit Shah: Please add safety caps for slab sizing and outline rollback plan.
Sofia Kaplan: Added slab caps and runtime feature flag; added rollback/gating steps to PR description.
Priya Desai: Can you add seed and harness config so benchmarks are reproducible?
Sofia Kaplan: Added harness config and deterministic seeds used for perf lab runs.
Liam O'Connor: Approve after small metric name cleanup and memory leak fix.

payload.body:
Context: Several tenants reported noisy alert storms during transient kernel queue spikes where token-level cost variance caused many per-route SLO alerts to fire simultaneously. Root cause analysis showed (1) high-cardinality trace fanout from per-shard sampling, (2) duplicated trace fragments across ingest, and (3) lack of tenant-priority weighting in alert scoring. This PR introduces a delegated trace aggregator service plus an SLA-aware alert coordinator to reduce alert churn and provide deterministic cost/latency attribution. Summary of changes: - Add delegated_trace_aggregator service (go) that consumes sampled spans from the observability ingestion stream, performs idempotent coalescing of trace fragments across shards, computes compact fingerprints, and emits aggregated trace rollups at a configurable cadence. The aggregator uses a two-tier reservoir (fast LRU + epoch sketch) to bound memory and prioritize recent, high-cost traces. - Add sla_alert_coordinator (python) that subscribes to aggregated rollups, computes per-invocation alert scores by combining token-cost, latency percentile deltas, and tenant SLA weight, and emits suppression or escalate decisions via the alerting bus. It implements a decay window to avoid repeated re-alerting on the same root cause. - Telemetry: new metrics (delegated_trace_coalesced_count, delegated_trace_rollup_latency_ms, sla_alert_score, sla_alert_suppressed_total, rollup_memory_pressure_gauge) + tags for tenant_id, route, model_family, kernel_bucket. - Dashboards: add compact rollup panel (rollup velocity / coalesced ratio), SLA score heatmap by tenant and route, and alert-suppression timeline. - Alert tuning: new rule templates that consult sla_alert_score and suppress low-priority alerts when a correlated cluster is already open; added knob for per-tenant override (SRE console). - Deployment and ops: helm chart changes to observability-pack, k8s HPA hints for aggregator, and a feature flag `observability.delegated_aggregator.enabled` with canary rollout strategy. Motivation: coalescing reduces cardinality and query cost while providing a single source of truth for invocation-level cost attribution; SLA-aware scoring reduces alert noise and helps oncall focus on meaningful regressions. Rollout plan: 1) Internal canary in staging with 5 tenants for 48h, monitor rollup latency and memory pressure; 2) opt-in beta for high-volume tenants; 3) gradual default-on rollout with runtime knob. Backwards compatibility: aggregator emits rollups alongside raw spans; consumers can opt-in. Tests & benchmarks: - Unit tests for coalescing logic and fingerprint stability - Integration test that simulates cross-shard fragment duplication (passes) - Load bench: aggregated rollups reduced trace cardinality by ~73% on a production-shaped replay and increased CPU on aggregator by ~12% (within SLO). Related: ENG-4827 (ticket), SRE-231 on alert fatigue. Links: design doc (internal/observability/delegated-aggregator.md), dashboard JSONs in dashboards/observability/rollups/*.
Evan Carter: Please add a short-circuit for tenants with <100 invocations/min to avoid noise — otherwise LGTM.
Maya Singh: Added threshold config and made it a runtime knob; updated tests to cover small-tenant path.
Sofia Martinez: Can we add more sampling invariants in the coalescer docs? Specifically how fingerprints handle reordered spans.
Maya Singh: Expanded doc section and added a deterministic reordering tolerance test in test_integration_rollup.py.
Liam O'Connor: CI failure on lint in aggregator; needs gofmt and a smaller exported symbol surface.
Maya Singh: Fixed formatting, reduced exported API; reran CI.
SRE rotation note (auto): Manual verification of alert suppression behavior required during staging canary.

Problem: Customers operating under regulatory constraints needed stronger guarantees that KMS operations are routed to regionally-appropriate key providers and that audit streams carry a stable watermark for cross-region ingestion. Additionally, on-call and operator workflows were requesting time-limited RBAC elevations but we lacked a uniform enforcement layer that prevents stale grants from persisting.

Design summary: This PR implements three coordinated features: (1) a jurisdiction-aware KMS router that matches tenant/residency assertions to KMS provider endpoints with a fallback policy and decision logging; (2) audit watermarking that attaches a monotonic per-tenant watermark header to outgoing persistence events and an ingest-side verifier that rejects out-of-order or duplicate batches; and (3) an RBAC TTL enforcement component that validates and enforces expiration on transient grants issued by the operator escalation service. Each component is gated behind feature flags and defaulted off for existing clusters.

What changed (high level): Added a new KMS routing policy engine (service/kms/router.go + pkg/kms/policy/*), a lightweight decision cache with TTLs to avoid excessive policy evals, an audit watermark generator and verifier (service/audit/watermark.go, service/audit/verifier.go), an RBAC TTL enforcer integrated into the policy evaluation pipeline (pkg/rbac/ttl_enforcer.go), operator-facing migration steps and a k8s overlay for gradual rollout (deploy/k8s/overlays/compliance.yaml). Documentation and API contract notes are under docs/security/kms-routing.md and docs/security/audit-watermarks.md.

Testing: Unit tests added for routing decisions and TTL expiry logic. Integration tests simulate cross-region replay and verify that audit verifier rejects duplicates and that the KMS router falls back to secondary providers when primary is unavailable. Load tests indicate median routing decision latency ~0.7ms under a 1000QPS synthetic policy cache warmup. Security scan coverage added for decision payload serialization.

Rollout plan: Feature flags are controlled through the console and can be enabled per-tenant. Default rollout: internal staging -> select enterprise tenants with consent flag -> global. A migration job is included to backfill recent audit watermark anchors for eligible tenants; job is safe to re-run. In case of routing regressions, there is an automated fallback to legacy KMS behavior controlled by a cluster-level override and monitoring alerts on >0.1% KMS error uplift.

Checklist:
- [x] API + routing policy implementation
- [x] Audit watermark generation + verifier
- [x] RBAC TTL enforcer and integration tests
- [x] Docs and rollout k8s overlays
- [x] Security review and threat-model notes

Related work: This builds on prior policy-compiler changes (ENG-2011) and complements the operator session attestation work (SEC-21).
Add jurisdiction-aware routing for KMS operations to respect tenant residency claims.
Emit stable audit watermark headers for cross-region request ordering and replay detection.
Introduce RBAC TTL enforcer to allow time-limited elevated operator roles for emergency workflows.
Priya Nair: Can we avoid a synchronous policy fetch on the hot path? Suggest adding a bounded async refresh and a cache hit fallback.
Maya Chen (author): Added a decision cache with 200ms async refresh and bounded staleness; updated router.go to prefer cache and fall back to last-known policy.
Liam O'Connor: The watermark header name needs to be stable across services — suggest X-Redwood-Watermark-V1; watch for proxy stripping.
Maya Chen (author): Renamed header to X-Redwood-Watermark-V1 and added tests for proxy passthrough in ingress simulation.
Arjun Rao: Need a plan for zero-downtime rollback if TTL enforcer blocks an existing long-lived grant; please add an operator override and audit log entry.
Maya Chen (author): Added an operator-override flag and explicit audit entry when a grant is rejected by TTL check. Documented in the operator runbook.

payload.body:
Summary: This PR introduces a small, focused hotpatch that centralizes circuit state transitions into a 'circuit lifecycle harmonizer' to reduce flapping across regional routers and to make rollbacks safe and well-instrumented. The change is intentionally scoped to the serving path and the KV-drain coordination plumbing so we can ship a mitigation for an incident we observed on 2026-02-10 where multiple regions briefly oscillated into slowpath due to competing reopen timers.

Motivation: We observed repeated rapid circuit open/reopen sequences when (a) staggered KV-drain events raced with probe-driven reopen, and (b) temporary high-latency probes triggered per-tenant downgrade heuristics. That behavior amplified load shedding and caused higher than expected soft-degradation rates for a small subset of tenants. The harmonizer introduces an explicit epoched lifecycle per circuit with three goals: (1) avoid rapid reopen/open flips by applying a short jittered grace window, (2) ensure a single authoritative drain/reopen decision across the region for a tenant route, and (3) emit high-cardinality telemetry for postmortem and rollback decisions.

What changed: - Add pkg/shedder/circuit_lifecycle.go: a compact state machine that sequences open->draining->closed transitions with epoch anchors and jittered timers. - Add pkg/telemetry/circuit_events.go: structured events (JSON) emitted for open/drain/reopen decisions and reason codes. - Modify internal/allocator/kv_drain.go: elect a coordinator for KV-drain epochs and consult the harmonizer before claiming drain ownership. - Introduce a small rollout-toggle in charts/redwood/templates/circuit-config.yaml to gate the harmonizer per-cluster. - Tests: tests/stability/circuit_lifecycle_test.go covers timing behavior (deterministic timers via test clock). - docs: deploy/hotpatch/README.md documents the rollback path and emergency toggle.

Commit summary: - 3e9b4f2: initial harmonizer implementation and tests - f1a2c3d: wire telemetry events and reason codes - 7b8e9f0: KV-drain coordinator hook and gating flag - 0a1b2c3: docs + chart toggle + defensive checks for nil coordinator

Testing: - Unit tests added for state transitions and timer jitter (CI). - Integration load run on staging with a 5k-tenant synthetic spike showing a 43% reduction in reopen cycles vs baseline. - Canary rollout plan executed in us-west-2 with the chart toggle enabled for <1% of capacity initially; telemetry was monitored for two hours. - One flaky integration test failed on first CI run (stability/test_runner) due to test clock mis-sync; re-run passed and is included below.

Rollout & rollback: - Rollout method: gradual chart toggle (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with 30m observation windows per step. - Abort criteria: increase in soft-degrades > 2x baseline or >1.5x reopen rate. - Immediate rollback: flip chart toggle to disabled and restart sidecar; harmonizer is stateless (epoch metadata kept in existing KV) so rollback restores previous behavior without data loss. - Emergency patch: deploy hotfix branch with harmonizer disabled but telemetry still emitted (this was used in staging validation).

Follow-ups: - Propagate harmonizer events into Console SLO dashboard (ENG-2197). - Consider merging epoch election into allocator leader module to reduce cross-component calls (refactor ticket ENG-2203).

Notes: This PR intentionally avoids changing tenant prioritization logic or global SLO thresholds. The goal is to stabilize circuit lifecycles and provide better observability to make subsequent SLO tuning safer.
Liam O'Connor: Nice focused scope. Two asks: (1) can we make the grace window configurable per-cluster (not just chart-level)? (2) add a low-sample-rate dump to help postmortem tenant-level traces.
Author (Maya Patel): Addressed both — added chart toggle and cluster override in router_proxy.go, and added a 0.1% sample dump for tenant traces behind the same toggle.
Ethan Chen: Unit tests look good; integration run shows improvement. One nit: reason code strings should be enumerated in telemetry to avoid drifting labels. Please add a small enum in circuit_events.go.
Author (Maya Patel): Added telemetry enum and updated tests to assert enum values rather than free strings.
Sofia Martinez: CI flaky test observed on first run. Confirmed re-run fixed. Please note in changelog that test harness depends on test clock alignment. Approved after re-run.
Infra Bot: Lint passed; go vet flagged a nil-check that was fixed in 0a1b2c3 commit. All green now.
Fix: stabilize rapid circuit flips by introducing a lifecycle harmonizer and safer rollback; includes telemetry for diagnosing misattributed evictions.

payload.body:
Motivation: Multiple customer integrations observed subtle races between token refresh heartbeats and stream reconnect logic across our SDKs. The work unifies a lightweight credential synchronizer, introduces a small DSL for declarative retry profiles, and polishes async streaming ergonomics (cancellation semantics, typed stream guards, and clearer session priming). Summary of changes: 1) credential synchronizer: a cross-language thin coordinator that serializes credential refreshes, emits telemetry hooks (cred.refresh.start/stop/failure) and exposes an opt-in prefetch window to reduce hot-path latency on reconnect; 2) unified retry DSL: a compact, declarative retry profile language (backoff caps, jitter classes, idempotency predicates) compiled to per-SDK presets—used to standardize behavior for stream reconnects and the token refresh backoff; 3) streaming ergonomics: explicit cancel() semantics for pull/push streams, a StreamGuard type that enforces single-consumer and typed chunk envelopes, and improved handshake timeout defaults; 4) version bumps: python-sdk v2.8.0, typescript-sdk v1.27.0, go-sdk v1.4.2 to align APIs; 5) tests & docs: e2e sims for credential contention, new examples in quickstarts, and updated changelogs. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-1122) - [x] Backwards-compatible API (opt-in synchronizer) - [x] Unit tests added for all SDKs - [x] E2E stability test added to perf-canary harness - [x] Updated quickstart examples and CHANGELOGs How to exercise locally: follow the README in sdk-integration/test-harness: run `make multi-sdk-stream-e2e` which spins lightweight local servers and a token-mint stub. Rollout plan: feature gated; default off for existing customers. Staged rollout: enable for internal canary -> beta customers -> GA. payload.body:
Problem: Recent staged promotions showed noisy spikes from background traffic (batch retries and health checks) that contaminated canary signal windows. Small canaries would pass locally but later regress in production because our observation windows were polluted and rollback playbooks were brittle.

Goal: introduce a 'quiet-window' promotion primitive that temporarily mutes low-value noise traffic and pins a telemetry baseline (telemetry-lock) for the duration of a canary sampling window, combined with resumable rollback snapshots so a promotion can be reverted deterministically if signals cross thresholds. Deliver a developer-facing config + runtime enforcement inside the rollout controller.

What this PR does (single-contiguous description): Adds a QuietWindow step to the rollout graph and a telemetry-lock mechanism that freezes baseline aggregations for selected metrics for the sampling window; implements a lightweight traffic-labeling injector to mark noise sources (healthchecks, batch-retries, internal probes) and gate them out of canary cohorts; captures a resumable rollback snapshot that includes routing map + KV snapshot of model version metadata so reversion is instant and idempotent. Includes end-to-end tests in the rollout-sim harness and a canary smoke job that validates both forward promote and resume rollback paths.

Checklist: - [x] rollout-controller: add QuietWindow node type and graph semantics - [x] telemetry: telemetry-lock implementation + baseline snapshot API - [x] ingress: traffic-label injector and noise-policy config - [x] resume-rollback: snapshot creation and apply path with idempotency checks - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs: rollout reference and operator playbook - [x] e2e smoke in perf lab

Impact: Enables more deterministic canary assessments by reducing signal contamination and reducing human intervention during reverts. The snapshot-based rollback reduces mean-time-to-recover for bad promotes from minutes (manual) to < 30s in most test scenarios.

Backward compatibility: All new behavior is opt-in via rollout spec fields (quietWindow, noiseLabels, telemetryLock). Default rollout behavior unchanged.

Notes and rationale: We experimented with adaptive filtering inside metrics ingestion but found it brittle across tenants; pushing noise-labeling to the edge (ingress) with a small policy language keeps semantics explicit and auditable. Telemetry-lock stores a short-lived baseline vector and a hash so rollouts compare live windows to the locked baseline (instead of re-computing a moving baseline that drifts during a promote). Resume rollback takes a snapshot of the model routing map and the KV cache pointers to avoid cache-warmup inconsistencies on revert.

Tests & validation: Added 12 unit tests, 3 integration tests, and an e2e smoke job that runs in the benchmark-lab environment. Benchmarks in perf lab show quiet-window has negligible CPU overhead (<2%) and reduces false-positive canary alerts by ~78% in our synthetic noisy workload.

Migration/playbook (SUMMARY): 1) Append quietWindow block in rollout spec, optionally set noiseLabels to known probes. 2) Start small (1% traffic), monitor telemetry-lock stability. 3) If rollback trigger fires, operator can run `rw rollout resume-rollback <id>` which uses stored snapshot to revert routing map and KV pointers. 4) If issues persist, follow documented operator playbook to escalate (linked in PR docs).

Related: ENG-2345 (design doc), PM-4120 (product acceptance criteria), SUP-87 (support case that motivated this).

Asha Patel: Added ttlSeconds to rollout spec and made server-side cap so operators can override via tenancy policy.
Priya Nair: Request small refactor in resume-rollback to validate cache pointer checks before applying routing map.
Asha Patel: Refactored resume-rollback apply path, added idempotency guard and extra unit test.
Evan Brooks: Verified e2e smoke and perf numbers in benchmark-lab, left an approval.
Release lead (Sophie Grant): Please ensure operator runbook includes instructions for on-call during first 48h post-rollout.

payload.body:
Context: Interactive workloads continue to show bimodal latency tails when we treat prefill and decode as a single undifferentiated pipeline. Motivation: reduce tail latency and KV cache amplification while keeping high throughput for background/throughput traffic. This PR introduces a lightweight prefill-decode demultiplexer that classifies requests at enqueue-time using a low-cost latency provenance signal and routes them into specialized pipeline lanes with stage-smoothing and adaptive thresholds. Summary of changes: - New demux stage (runtime/scheduling/prefill_demux.cc/.h): samples token-level provenance (prefill size, cache hit heuristic, observed kernel queue depth) and assigns one of three lanes: fast-speculative, conservative-prefill, or decode-only. - Lossy prefill aggregation (runtime/prefill/aggregator.*): aggregates small concurrent prefill chunks destined for the same KV shard using a lossy coalescer that keeps representative KV primes to reduce duplicate warms. The coalescer has tunable fidelity and falls back to exact prefill when quality drop is detected. - Stage smoothing controller (runtime/scheduling/stage_smoother.*): per-lane leaky-bucket concurrency limiter that smooths burstiness between prefill and decode handoff, reducing kernel scheduling jitter and tail amplification. - Latency provenance tracing (observability/tracing/prefill_provenance_events.md + tags): new trace tags and sampling logic so we can attribute p95/p99 latency to demux decisions and coalescing. - Rollback and conservative fallback (runtime/scheduling/fallback_policy.*): when the demux lane shows regression in quality (measured via sample evals), traffic is automatically rolled back to the conservative lane. - Tests and benchmarks (tests/prefill_demux_unit.cc, perf/benchmarks/prefill_demux_bench.py): unit tests for demux classifier thresholds and microbenchmarks showing tail improvements. Motivation and behavior notes: - The demux uses a tiny per-request fixed-size probe (4 bytes of provenance) to avoid adding allocs. - Lossy aggregation is conservative: it merges only when KV affinity and token-range overlap exceed a tunable threshold. - Stage smoothing uses a token-bucket that prefers keeping prefill throughput up to configured SLO, then limits burst transfer to decode to avoid sudden kernel queue spikes. Checklist: - [x] Demux classifier implementation and unit tests - [x] Aggregator with fidelity knob and fallback - [x] Stage smoother with configurable SLOs - [x] End-to-end perf harness added - [x] Tracing/instrumentation and sampling - [x] Rollback policy and smoke tests - [x] Docs + release notes Perf summary (internal perf harness against llama-13b-like workload): - p50 end-to-end latency: -2% (neutral) - p95: -18% - p99: -27% - GPU kernel queue jitter (stddev): -33% - Token-level KV duplications (measured via synthetic overlap load): -42% Notes on tradeoffs and mitigation: - Small accuracy regressions can occur when lossy aggregation merges disjoint token prefixes; to mitigate we only enable it when sample-eval pass rate >= 99.5% on a held-out eval set. - The demux introduces a small classification overhead (~40ns median); overall improvement outweighs cost for interactive SLOs. Related work: builds on prior prefill/decode handoff PRs but takes a routing-first approach rather than kernel-level preemption. Releases: opt-in feature flag: runtime.experimental.prefill_demux default off for 2 weeks, then gradual rollout. Follow-ups: - automatic threshold tuning via Optimize; - extend demux signals with model-architecture-aware features; - add a bounded shared warm cache lane for multi-tenant affinity. Links: Linear ENG-4567 (design doc), benchmark harness in perf/benchmarks/prefill_demux_bench.py, tracing guide: observability/tracing/prefill_provenance_events.md
Priya Nair: Could you add a failsafe counter for the coalescer so it doesn't starve fringe ranges? Requesting a test for the counter behavior.
Maya Chen (author): Added a coalescer eviction counter and unit test (see aggregator.cc). It enforces a max-merge-per-shard per-second and is covered in tests.
Diego Alvarez: Nice metrics — can you add a dashboard query example for attributing p99 to demux lanes?
Maya Chen: Added observability queries and a minimal dashboard JSON in perf/benchmarks dir for review.
Connor Blake: I saw slight regressions in a long-sequence gen e2e test when aggregation fidelity > 0.6. Can we gate default to 0.5?
Maya Chen: Default fidelity set to 0.45 and a runtime flag to adjust in prod. Added note to release notes.
Introduces a prefill-decode demultiplexer that reduces tail latency and KV duplication by routing requests into specialized pipeline lanes and applying lossy prefill aggregation with stage smoothing. Opt-in feature flag: runtime.experimental.prefill_demux. Expect p95 improvements for interactive workloads; enable behind flag and monitor pref-fill provenance metrics.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: Customers and internal teams have repeatedly asked for better attribution of long-tail token cost and tail latency to concrete lifecycle events (allocation, reuse, eviction) and for a way to identify causally related spans in dense microservice graphs. Static threshold alerts were generating noise during gradual traffic shifts. This PR introduces three complementary capabilities: 1) token lifecycle event instrumentation (lifecycle tags and structured event stream), 2) a collapsed span-dependency graph that synthesizes repeated RPC edges into a single dependency with counts, and 3) an SLO slope detector alerting rule that triggers on sustained upward slope in 95th-token-cost or token-latency over a sliding window.

What I changed (high level):
- telemetry: emit telemetry.token_lifecycle_events (structured events with life_stage: allocated|reused|evicted, reason tags for eviction/coldstart, and token_cost_micros). Also emit telemetry.token_entropy and telemetry.kv_cache_hotness.
- tracing: add span dependency synthesizer that produces tracing.span_dependency.edges_count and tracing.span_dependency.collapse_reason. Collapses repeated RPC edges within a session to reduce cardinality and make graphs readable in the UI.
- dashboards: new dashboard panels under Observability > Token Economics: "Token Lifecycle Sankey" (flows from allocation -> reuse -> eviction, grouped by model and route), "Dependency Collapse Explorer" (collapsed graph with counts), and "SLO Slope Detector" widget showing fitted slope and alert window.
- alerting: introduce slo-slope-detector rule that compares rolling-window linear fit on p95 token cost and token-latency and fires when slope > threshold and R^2 > 0.6 for N consecutive windows. This replaces two noisy static thresholds for the hosted API routes.
- logging: structured log enrichment with event_type and lifecycle_id to correlate logs / traces / metrics more easily in joins.
- docs: added a HOWTO for using the Token Sankey and best practices for slope thresholds.

Checklist:
- [x] Instrumentation added with feature flag (telemetry.token.lifecycle.enabled)
- [x] Unit tests for event serialization and small integration harness for collapsed dependency generation
- [x] Dashboard panels and JSON exports
- [x] Alert rule with runbook and sample Linear alert for oncall
- [x] Docs and example queries

Why this is different: The lifecycle events give a first-class primitive for attributing per-token cost/latency to actual runtime lifecycle stages rather than just route/model. The dependency collapse reduces noise from chat/chain workloads where the same RPCs are repeated in a session. The slope detector is tuned for gradual regressions (e.g., model drift, quantization regressions, infra degradation) rather than transient spikes. Together these reduce alert noise and accelerate root cause discovery.
Priya Singh: Nice end-to-end. A couple asks: (1) can we keep the event schema minimal and avoid embedding large route metadata in every event? (2) add a short TTL for lifecycle_id to avoid storage blowup.
Maya Patel (author): Addressed — event now references route_id instead of embedding full route metadata and lifecycle_id TTL added; updated tests to assert TTL semantics.
Liam O'Connor: The collapse heuristic is clever but could hide low-frequency but high-latency edges. Suggest adding a 'collapse_exceptions' list for edges with cost variance > X.
Maya Patel (author): Added collapse_exceptions config and documented tradeoffs. Also added a small integration test that validates exceptions are preserved.
Noah Chen: CI failed on lint initially (line length) and one flaky e2e. Please re-run CI and add a flake whitelist entry if needed.
Maya Patel (author): Fixed lint and added whitelist entry. Re-ran CI; integration flake was unrelated and rerun passed.
New telemetry: token lifecycle events and token_entropy metric; new dashboards (Token Lifecycle Sankey, Dependency Collapse Explorer); SLO slope detector alert rule for gradual regressions; docs and runbook for tuning slope thresholds.
Enable feature flag telemetry.token.lifecycle.enabled in staging to validate dashboards before enabling in production.
Recommended initial slope thresholds: p95_token_cost slope > 0.0005 per minute over 3 windows, with R^2 > 0.6 (see runbook).
Legacy static thresholds have been preserved but disabled by default; teams must migrate to slope detector for noisy routes.
