Motivation: We need a lightweight, low-cost way to surface intermittently occurring regressions (tail quality and tail latency) that are missed by steady shadow mirroring and typical canaries. This PR implements an "intermittent shadow peeker" mode plus session-coherent cutover semantics and a deterministic rollback/replay path for reproducible remediation.

Summary of changes: introduces an intermittent sampling controller (configurable cadence and burst window) that temporarily mirrors a small fraction of traffic to candidate variants with tightened telemetry (percentile stratification, session-level correlation) and preserves session affinity and KV-cache continuity during cutover phases. Adds an input-snapshotting facility that records deterministic request vectors and minimal state needed to replay sessions on a reference infra for rollback validation. Exposes rollout policies to the orchestration layer so automated rollback can invoke replay checks before finalizing a revert.

Key user-visible behavior:
- "peeker" sampling windows: short-lived high-fidelity shadow bursts (default 30s every 15min) that increase sensitivity to transient regressions without continuous cost.
- Session-coherent cutover: when promoting a variant from peeker/canary to live, the controller migrates session affinity and checkpoints KV-cache keys referenced during peeker windows to avoid cold-cache regressions.
- Replayable rollback: on a rollback trigger, the system can perform deterministic replay of recorded sessions against the to-be-restored variant and produce a traceable diff artifact (response deltas, latency histogram deltas, token-level divergence).

Design notes: The intermittent peeker leverages our existing router token to divert a configurable traffic shard and attaches a short-lived mirror session tag. Peeker telemetry enriches spans with sample-tier labels and computes 50/90/95/99 tail deltas. The rollback replay engine is deliberately minimal — it captures request inputs, model version, K/V dependencies (keys touched), and sequence seeds to allow deterministic re-execution on the same model binary. This avoids shipping full recordings of payloads beyond what is necessary for verification (privacy conscious config).

Compatibility and safety: Default config is opt-in per-route. Peeker windows are rate-limited and subject to existing tenant quotas. Replay recordings are encrypted at rest and access-controlled by RBAC. No change to default routing semantics for routes that do not opt into peeker.

Testing: added unit tests for sampling controller, end-to-end integ test that simulates a tail-latency spike during peeker bursts, and a replay smoke test that validates deterministic replays on toy models. Also ran canary on infra (dedicated test cluster) for 48 hours.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of intermittent peeker controller and policy bindings
- [x] Session-coherent cutover logic and KV checkpointing
- [x] Deterministic replay capture format and minimal replay engine
- [x] Unit/integration tests and basic canary run
- [x] Docs (console toggle + rollout recipe)

Notes for reviewers: focus on safety boundaries (quota enforcement, privacy knobs), replay determinism guarantees, and any implications for autoscaling during burst windows. Related: ENG-3142 describes evaluation criteria; SUP-7812 was filed after a customer incident where transient tail regressions escaped detection.
Diego Alvarez: overall this looks good; two questions: how do we guarantee no extra cost leak to shared routing components? can we add telemetry for peeker admission failures?
Maya Chen: reply: peeker admission is enforced at router edge and we've added admission counters and a peeker_admit_failure metric (see mirroring_tags.go); added test to assert quota enforcement.
Priya Nair: please ensure replay captures are privacy-filtered and include a retention TTL default. Also would like a knob to disable storing K/V snapshots at customer request.
Maya Chen: reply: added privacy filter hook and retention TTL config (default 7d). K/V snapshotting can be disabled per-tenant via rollout policy (see session_checkpoint.go).
Liam O'Connor: minor: prefer 'burst_window' naming consistency (we had 'burstWindow' in some places). Also can we add a quick chart to the console docs showing expected cost vs sensitivity?
Maya Chen: reply: normalized naming to 'burst_window' across controller and console, and added a cost/sensitivity chart to docs.
Unit coverage added for controller and replay capture; integration test simulates transient latency/payload shifts and validates detection during peeker bursts; canary run on dedicated test infra for 48h confirmed no regressions in default traffic paths.
Adds an opt-in 'intermittent shadow peeker' sampling mode that surfaces transient regressions with low continuous cost, session-coherent cutover to avoid cold-cache regressions during promotions, and a minimal deterministic replay path for reproducible rollback verification. Opt-in per-route; privacy and quota controls included.
Monitor metrics: peeker.admit_count, peeker.admit_failures, peeker.tail_delta_p95/p99, replay.verification_pass_rate. Default cost exposure is low but watch burst_window concurrently with autoscaler settings. If replay runs fail due to non-determinism, buffer and alert to oncall for manual review.

Problem: short lived overload spikes (bursts of 1-3s) cause immediate tenant eviction when the SLO enforcer aggressively reclaims slots, which produces request loss and oscillating re-admits. Motivation: avoid overreacting to transient bursts while still enforcing SLOs for prolonged overloads. Goal: introduce a short, deterministic reservation window for slots (deferred slot reservation) and a complementary Fadeout SLO Controller that decays allowance over a configurable grace period; provide region-aware coordination so handoffs do not create double-counting and so that failovers remain conservative. Changes: 1) slot manager: add reservation token bucket and reservation lease with TTL; reservation allows a tenant to temporarily exceed strict allocation by N slots for up to T milliseconds; expired reservations are automatically reclaimed. 2) fadeout SLO controller: when a tenant crosses its SLO we no longer instant-evict; instead we move the tenant into a fadeout state where throughput is reduced gradually using a per-tenant penalty curve; the controller integrates with existing penalty decay code and emits explicit audit events for observability. 3) regional synchronizer shim: lightweight lease synchronizer to prevent simultaneous reservation acceptance for the same logical tenant across regions during failover windows. 4) telemetry: new metrics (reservation_attempts_total, reservation_success_total, fadeout_entries_total, fadeout_exit_latency_ms) and dashboards + alert on reservation_rejection_ratio > 5% for 2m. 5) config: feature flag (runtime.feature.deferred_reservations) default off, tuning knobs exposed via console and operator config. Testing & validation: unit and integration tests simulate micro-bursts and long sustained overloads; e2e run in perf-lab with canary traffic showed 48% reduction in immediate evictions and stable latency tail. Rollout: gated canary in 2 regions for 72h, followed by staged rollout with dark traffic validation; automatic kill-switch via feature flag if eviction_delta > 10% or error_rate increases > 0.5%. Backwards compatibility: behavior is opt-in while flag is off; no model/schema changes. Related: ENG-1982 describes production incidents motivating this work; SUP-4421 is a customer incident that required a hotfix for sudden tenant dropouts. Merge notes: squash-merged after addressing reviewers' comments.
add reservation token bucket and TTL handling in slot_manager
implement fadeout controller + penalty curve and attach to slo enforcer
introduce regional lease synchronizer shim and tests
add metrics, dashboards, and alert rules
integration tests for burst vs sustained overload behaviour
docs ops guidance and a console toggle
Carlos: Please decouple the reservation TTL from the penalty decay constant; make it configurable and document recommended values. Author reply: TTL is exposed via configmap and console toggle; updated docs with recommended defaults (500ms reservation, 10s fadeout window).
Ethan: Integration test flaked on race between regional sync and eviction path; can you add a deterministic barrier? Author reply: added deterministic barrier in tests and reworked sync_shim to use lease compare-and-swap semantics; tests now stable.
Olivia: Add a rollout guard to automatically disable the feature flag if eviction_delta grows. Author reply: added a guard that watches eviction_delta and will flip the flag via operator API if threshold breached; documented rollback steps.
Introduces a deferred slot reservation window to tolerate short spikes without immediate eviction.

Includes telemetry and alerting to monitor reservation health and rollout safety.

Add a lightweight presubmit shim for lint plugins to reduce startup time; introduce a dependency rotation optimizer that schedules staged devdependency upgrades and provides telemetry; add a release-slimmer hook to trim redundant artifacts from release bundles.
Context: presubmit latency and noisy devdependency churn slowed developer feedback loops. Goal: introduce a lightweight presubmit shim that pulls and runs only the lint plugins relevant to changed files, add a dependency rotation optimizer that stages devdep updates to small cohorts and emits telemetry for risk scoring, and add a release-slimmer hook to reduce release artifact size. Changes include a new .github workflow, a small Go-based presubmit shim binary with a cached plugin loader, a dep-rotation scheduler script, and documentation and tests. Checklist: - Add presubmit shim and workflow; - Implement plugin cache+warm strategy; - Add dep rotation scheduler and dashboard hooks; - Add release-slimmer hook and artifact prune step; - Add unit and integration tests; - Update docs and quickstart. Motivation: presubmit startup for large monorepo caused >8s median overhead for lint setups; dependency churn caused noisy CI and frequent rollbacks. This PR reduces presubmit cold-start to ~1.2s for changed-file-only runs and lays groundwork for safer, gradual devdep upgrades. Rollout plan: staged opt-in via repo-level flag, enable for 20% of teams for 2 weeks, monitor presubmit latency and dep-rotation regressions, then full rollout. Related: ENG-4218, ENG-4321, SUP-1054.
Initial presubmit-shim prototype: add shim/main.go and plugin cache interface
Add GitHub workflow: .github/workflows/presubmit-shim.yml and integration tests
Implement dep-rotation scheduler and simple cohort selection algorithm
Add release-slimmer hook and unit tests; wire into release job
Docs: presubmit-shim.md and dep-rotation-runbook; small test fixes and CI flake fixes
Kenji Sakamoto: Left a couple small nits around error wrapping in main.go; please return wrapped errors so stack traces show provenance.
Aditi Rao: Addressed in commit 'wrap-errors-presubmit-shim', also added a small test to assert error message format.
Marta Lopez: Can the dep-rotation scheduler record a per-cohort risk score rather than only a binary pass/fail? Suggest adding a histogram metric.
Aditi Rao: Added metrics.dco.cohort_risk histogram and documented its interpretation in dep-rotation README.
Evan Chu: CI was flaky on the presubmit integration on macOS runner; appears to be a timing issue in plugin fetch. Suggest a short backoff/retry and deterministic temp dir.
Aditi Rao: Switched to deterministic temp dir and added exponential backoff; reran CI and green.
Kenji Sakamoto: Approved after addressing comments.
Marta Lopez: Approved.
CI: All checks passed; presubmit and integration jobs green after rerun.
Presubmit workflow initially failed on plugin download flakiness, fixed by retry/backoff; full CI passed on final run. Tests: unit 523 passed, integration 12/12 passed, flake rate reduced.
Risk: introducing a new presubmit shim may hide plugin regressions; Mitigation: opt-in rollout and telemetry with automatic rollback on error rate >1% for two consecutive days. Dep-rotation risk: cohort selection could surface incompatible devdeps; Mitigation: small cohorts, canary tooling and automatic rollback, linear tasks ENG-4218 to enact stricter compatibility checks.
This is intentionally conservative: shim does not change lint rules, only the plugin loading path. Teams that rely on global devcontainer boot will not be impacted until opt-in. The toolchain-lease integration reduces noisy global tool installs by leasing ephemeral toolchains per presubmit job.

Added intermittent sample reconciler service and compact telemetry pipeline; new dashboard panels and tuned alerts to reduce noise from sparse sampling.
Motivation: we observed noisy alert churn and missing token-attribution in low-traffic tenants due to aggressive sampling and periodic exporter gaps. This PR adds an intermittent-sample reconciler service and a 'telemetry slimline' ingest path to stitch intermittent metric/tracing samples, reconstruct missing token-level attributions, and emit compact rollups for low-cardinality routes. Goals: reduce alert noise from sparse samples, provide better cost/latency attribution for long-tail invocations, and keep overhead sub-2% CPU for the observability pipeline. Summary of changes: 1) telemetry/reconciler: new service that consumes sampled traces and metric windows, applies a sliding reconciliation window to infer missing token-attribution events, and outputs compacted span anchors and delta-cost rollups. The reconciliation algorithm uses a best-effort prefix-matching heuristic with confidence weights and retains provenance tags for auditability. 2) telemetry/sidecar: lightweight sidecar that tags sampled logs with reconciler-correlation IDs and emits heartbeat markers so the reconciler can detect exporter gaps. 3) observability/dashboards: new Telemetry Reconciler dashboard with panels for "stitch rate", "reconciler confidence distribution", compacted token-cost per-route, and reconciler induced-suppressed-alerts. 4) alerts: introduced a noise-aware alert adapter that uses reconciler confidence and sample density to suppress low-confidence anomalies for the first N windows, reducing pager fatigue. 5) tests/docs: unit and integration tests for the reconciliation logic, loadbench results in docs showing <2% CPU overhead at production sampling rates. Backwards compatibility: reconciler emits both legacy and compact rollups; downstream consumers default to legacy until opt-in. Rollout plan: start with internal telemetry namespace for 48 hours, gated ramp to prod 20% tenants -> 50% -> 100% with feature flag. Why unique: this approach stitches sparse telemetry across exporter gaps rather than only downsampling or increasing sampling rate, preserving signal for long-tail token-level cost attribution without increasing sampling cost. Link to issue: SUP-7123.
Liam Chen: 'Can you clarify how the reconciler avoids false positives when prefix matches are ambiguous? Please add a metric for ambiguous_match_rate.' -- Maya: 'Added ambiguous_match_rate and confidence bucket metric; reconciler suppresses matches below 0.25 confidence by default and tags them for audit.' -- Noah Singh: 'Load result looks good but add an integration test with exporter gap simulation.' -- Maya: 'Added exporter-gap simulation test and included results in docs showing stitch recall/precision at 1%, 5%, 10% sampling.' -- Elena Korobkina: 'We need a gradual rollout plan and opt-out for regulatory tenants.' -- Maya: 'Rollout plan added to PR description and feature flag with tenant-level opt-out implemented.' -- Liam Chen: 'CI flaky test on dashboard import, re-run CI.' -- CI: 'rerun passed.' -- Final: reviewers approved and requested squash-merge.'

payload.body:
Context and motivation: our KV cache has seen increased fragmentation and unpredictable tail latency in multi-tenant workloads where ephemeral tenants produce many small allocations followed by bursts of reads. Existing eviction paths aggressively reclaim by LRU-like metrics which can cause unnecessary paging and I/O spikes as small dead fragments accumulate. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) a background 'memory harvester' that compacts low-utility fragments without blocking hot token lookups, and (2) a pluggable 'priority fallback adapter' which lets the routing/scheduling layer downgrade low-priority tenant allocations before resorting to global spillovers.

Design summary: the memory harvester runs as a background actor with tenant-aware work queues. It uses a fragmentation score computed from per-segment live density, recent access heatmap, and KV object pin counts to select candidate segments for asynchronous compaction. Compaction is copy-on-write: a harvester thread copies live slots into a compacted segment, updates segment metadata atomically, and releases the old segment via a deferred free path that respects in-flight KV references. The priority fallback adapter implements a small interface (RegisterPolicy, ShouldDowngrade, ApplyFallback) that allows policies to be swapped at runtime — the default policy is conservative: it downgrades only tenant-scoped caches marked best-effort and uses a token-bucket shaped grace window to avoid cascading reclaim storms.

Implementation notes: major changes are in cache/harvester/* and runtime/scheduler/fallback_adapter.{h,cc}. Harvester maintains a sharded priority queue keyed by (tenant, fragmentation_score, last_compacted_at). Fragmentation_score = (1 - live_slots/total_slots) * log(1 + cold_touch_count) + small_age_penalty. Compaction is rate-limited by a configurable cpu_budget_ms and io_budget_bytes to avoid impacting inference kernels; default is 4ms/cycle and 4MB/s per shard. The adapter hooks into request admission: when capacity pressure is detected (pressure > threshold), ShouldDowngrade consults tenant annotations and recent SLA violations, then issues ApplyFallback which can either mark allocations as 'evict-first' or instruct the harvester to prioritize that tenant's segments.

Testing and validation: unit tests for compaction correctness (pointer safety and deferred free) included. Integration tests simulate mixed workloads: 60% read-heavy high-priority tenants, 40% churny ephemeral tenants. Canary run in us-west-2 on dedicated infra with 3 GPU nodes: median latency unchanged, 95th reduced by ~18%, 99th reduced by ~12%, and peak spillover bytes decreased by ~28% over 24h. Detailed benchmark artifacts attached in the CI artifacts (harvester_bench_20250227.tar.gz).

Rollout and safety: feature gate redwood.runtime.harvester.enabled=false by default. We included canary-targeting flags allowing policy opt-in per-customer. Rollout plan: enable on 5% of traffic for 48h, then 20% for 72h, monitor tokens-per-second, spillover rate, and tail P99 latency; abort if any of these regress beyond configured thresholds. We also added an emergency-kill switch that stops harvester threads and flushes pending compaction work to avoid stuck defers.

Operational observability: new metrics exported: harvester.compactions_started, compactions_succeeded, compaction_cpu_ms, compaction_bytes_moved, tenant.compaction_score_histogram, fallback_adapter.downgrades_applied. Added Grafana dashboard panels and two alertrules: (1) harvester.failure_rate > 1% for 15m, (2) fallback_adapter.downgrade_rate spike > 3x baseline.

Related work and references: follows ideas from ENG-3129 (priority fallback RFC) and extends the allocator work in previous PRs by focusing on background compaction vs immediate eviction. Does not replace slab refactors; designed to interoperate with future slab/segment alloc changes.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked (ENG-3129: priority fallback + harvester)
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Canary benchmark run and artifacts attached
- [x] Feature flag and emergency kill switch
- [x] Observability (metrics + dashboards)

Known limitations: compaction currently avoids migrating very-large objects > 256KB to limit copy overhead; this means some fragmentation from large objects can persist. Also, the heuristic parameters (cpu_budget_ms, io_budget_bytes, fragmentation scoring) are conservative defaults and may need tuning per workload.

If reviewers approve I will follow up with a small RFC for adding a 'deprioritize' admission endpoint used by platform teams to mark tenants as low-impact for aggressive reclaim.
Introduces a background memory harvester that performs targeted compaction and a pluggable priority-fallback adapter for per-tenant reclaim heuristics. Reduces steady-state fragmentation and improves tail latency under cross-tenant pressure.
Evan McIntyre: Can we ensure deferred free path cannot starve the allocator? Suggest adding a bounded backlog metric and a hard cap on deferred_frees.
Aditi Rao (author): Added deferred_free_backlog gauge and hard cap; compaction will stop if backlog > 10k entries.
Sofia Patel: The fragmentation scoring seems heavy; can we do a cheaper approximate score for hot paths?
Aditi Rao (author): We added a fast-path heuristic for hot segments using sampled counters; full score computed in background only when candidate probability > 0.6.
Jules Moreno: CI flaked on one integration run (timeout). Re-run tests and confirm stability before merge.
Aditi Rao (author): Re-ran the flaky job with increased timeout; all integration tests passed on 2nd run. Added a small test harness timeout increase to avoid CI flakes.
Matrix: unit (pass), integration (pass after 1 rerun), lint (pass), benchmarks (pass). One flaky integration rerun due to timeout resolved by extending test harness timeout. Artifacts include bench bundles and canary logs.
Merged into main via squash after approvals from all reviewers. No post-merge hotfix required during canary staging.
Tuning pass for fragmentation_score weights per workload (ENG-3195)
Optional: pluggable policy for IO-prioritized compaction to coexist with dedicated infra (ENG-3210)
Prototype slab-aware compaction that cooperates with upcoming slab allocator refactor

Motivation: we observed multiple incidents where operator actions could not be correlated reliably with operator intent during post-incident reviews because request metadata lacked a structured, signed justification. This PR introduces: 1) a lightweight operator-justification header (X-Operator-Justification) that carries a short rationale tokenized for auditing; 2) server-side middleware that requires and validates a KMS-backed HMAC signature for justification headers when the caller is an operator principal; 3) an audit blindspot detector that scans historical audit streams and flags entries missing signed justifications; and 4) an RBAC epoch revoker daemon that enforces short-lived operator grants by revoking elevated bindings after configured epochs to reduce blast radius.

Scope & non-goals: This is focused on telemetry and enforcement at the API gateway and control-plane layers. It does not introduce new user-facing RBAC primitives or change existing operator UX (authorization flows remain the same); instead it layers ephemeral revocation and signed intent capture for tighter compliance. This does not ship a KMS migration — it uses existing KMS provider interfaces already onboarded.

Checklist implemented: - [x] Add justification header middleware with validation and structured parsing - [x] Integrate with existing KMS signer adapter and caching - [x] Implement audit blindspot detector and backfill report generator - [x] Add RBAC epoch revoker service and a small CLI to schedule revocations - [x] Unit + integration tests for happy/failure paths - [x] Helm templates and RBAC manifests for deployment - [x] Docs: security playbook snippet and operational runbook

Operational notes: default enforcement is opt-in via feature flag security.justification.enforce. When enabled in a cluster, operator principals missing signed justification will receive 403 with an explanatory error and link to the runbook. The epoch revoker runs as a cron-style job; default epoch for elevated bindings set to 24h in the release, configurable per-tenant.
3 commits: \n- Add middleware to capture and validate X-Operator-Justification header and wire to auth context (Priya Raman)\n- KMS signer adapter + caching + e2e test harness (Priya Raman)\n- Audit detector, epoch revoker service, helm changes, and docs (Maya Chen)
Evan Brooks: Overall looks good. Two high-level asks: (1) ensure low-latency path for signed header verification (cache KMS HMAC keys), (2) add clear metrics for 'justification_missing' and 'justification_invalid'.
Author (Priya Raman): Addressed — added an in-memory per-region key cache with TTL and added prometheus metrics justification_missing_total and justification_invalid_total. See commit 2.
Maya Chen: Audit detector is great. Request: include a CSV backfill export with counts per-tenant and sample IDs so compliance team can triage. Also, please add guidance in runbook for rolling the feature on/off.
Author (Priya Raman): Added csv exporter and runbook snippet; included sample Linear task references in docs.
Diego Alvarez: Small nit — ensure the revoker CLI supports dry-run and rate limits (we don't want mass revokes during testing).
Author (Priya Raman): Added --dry-run and --rate-limit flags to epoch-revoker; integration tests include a dry-run scenario.
Merged via squash by Evan Brooks on 2025-11-19 after green CI and 2 approvals. Release will be included in v2.13.0. The PR body includes a short migration guide; feature default is opt-in. Rolling deployment recommended: enable audit detector in read-only mode for 48h, evaluate blindspot report, then enable enforcement flag and deploy revoker in dry-run prior to active mode.
Security: add support for signed operator justification headers (X-Operator-Justification) validated with KMS; audit tool can detect historical blindspots; epoch revoker enforces short-lived elevated RBAC bindings. Opt-in via feature flag security.justification.enforce. See security runbook for rollout steps.

Motivation: During the Feb regional surge incident we observed aggressive tenant drains that caused cascading retries and KV cache inconsistencies when traffic returned. This PR introduces a coordinated 'Gentle Drain and Transparent Restore Conductor' that reduces noisy failovers by doing two things: (1) a tenant-aware gentle-drain algorithm that imposes a soft ramp-down with token-limited acceptance windows, and (2) a transparent-restore flow that preserves per-tenant KV snapshot markers and allows safe replay/rehydration on node rejoin. Design summary: - Gentle drain: tenant scoring is extended with a decay-aware backoff that reduces abrupt evictions; new parameters allow configurable ramp-duration, token-cap-per-window, and weight hysteresis so high-priority tenants do not suffer unnecessary SLO relaxation. - Transparent restore: on node demotion or planned drain we create compact KV snapshots with an idempotent replay marker; nodes rejoining will perform a checksum-validated state-sync and only accept replayed requests up to the last stable marker to avoid double-processing. - Circuit harmonizer: we add short-term circuit strobing protection so neighbouring regional circuits do not flip state in lockstep (prevents resonance). - Canary/rollout: the feature is gated behind a runtime flag and a per-region canary that primes with low-rate production traffic using token-limited warmup. Backwards compatibility: runtime flags keep original behavior intact. For Private deployments the restore flow falls back to current KV-drain path if state-sync is disabled. Testing: unit tests added for the scoring decay and token window; integration harness simulates a three-region failover with staggered drains and verifies no duplicate outputs for idempotent requests; a soak job ran for 48 hours in staging with mixed tenant weights. Rollout plan: 1) merge to main behind feature flag, 2) enable in a single low-traffic region for 24h canary, 3) expand to additional regions with telemetry checks, 4) enable auto-fallback to legacy drain if rollback signal observed. Checklist: - [x] design doc updated (RFC-DR-631) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] telemetry hooks and histograms added - [x] graceful rollback path implemented - [x] documented runtime config in ops wiki Observability/metrics added: tenant_drain_rate{region}, drain_token_utilization, restore_replay_success, restore_replay_conflicts, circuit_resync_count. Operational playbook: added instructions to the SRE runbook for forced-restore, manual marker prune, and emergency-disable flag. Related: follows up on ENG-1987 and SUP-4391 incident notes. Notes: this PR intentionally keeps the throttle knobs conservative (default ramp-duration = 60s, token-cap = 250 r/s) to avoid surprise on high-throughput tenants. The team will adjust after canary telemetry.
Elena Kuznetsova: Nice approach. Two quick asks: (1) describe how markers behave across shard resizes, (2) please ensure restore_replay_conflicts is a counter not a gauge.
Avery Patel (author): Markers are stable per-tenant per-shard id; on resize we write a tombstone marker and the restore flow merges by last-writer-with-epoch. I'll change the metric to a counter and add comments explaining the shard-resize merge semantics.
Marcus Lee: Can we add a short-circuit for very small tenants so they don't pay the extra snapshot cost? Also add a safety net that disables transparent restore if the snapshot store latency exceeds threshold.
Avery Patel (author): Added small-tenant bypass with configurable threshold and a snapshot-store-latency health check that flips the fallback flag. See configs/ops_runtime.yaml for knobs.
Samira Thompson: CI flaked on integration initially (race in rehydration). After fix I re-ran and tests passed. Approving pending telemetry names standardized.
Samira Thompson: Approve (comment)
Implements a tenant-aware gentle drain plus transparent restore conductor to reduce noisy failovers during regional capacity shifts; improves SLO stability and KV-replay safety; backport to 2026.2 recommended for critical regions.

payload.body:
Motivation: existing canary probes run at fixed rates across slices which can over- or under-probe under heterogeneous traffic. This causes noisy regression alerts and either wasted probe budget or blind spots during production rollouts. This PR introduces a traffic-conditioned probe mixer (TCM) that adaptively allocates probe budget to traffic cohorts using a lightweight stochastic scheduler, and a multi-signal rollback oracle (MSRO) that fuses latency percentiles, throughput deltas, and error-rate trends with a de-glitching stage to avoid spurious rollbacks.

What this changes: single-line summary: add TCM scheduling service, probe weighting heuristics, MSRO fusion engine, metrics adapters, unit+integration tests, and docs/runbook.

Details: the TCM observes per-route traffic histograms (shape, concurrency, recent QPS) and produces a probe mix vector per-cohort. The mixer uses a softmax-weighted reservoir sampler that favors under-observed slices and high-variance slices. The probe sampler is shape-aware: short-paths receive higher frequency but smaller batch probes; long-paths get fewer but deeper probes that exercise KV cache and long-context kernels. The MSRO ingests three signal streams: latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), throughput delta (relative to baseline), and error-rate trend. Signals are normalized by rolling robust statistics (median-of-means for variance estimation) then fed into a small logistic fusion model with an explicit deglitch stage: short transients (under configured half-life) are suppressed unless corroborated across two signals or persisted across two probe windows.

Deglitch algorithm: median-of-means on sliding windows + Bayesian change-point detector tuned for low false alarm rate. When a potential regression is detected, MSRO computes a composite risk score (0.0-1.0). Score > 0.85 triggers immediate canary pause + automated narrow rollback; 0.6-0.85 opens an investigation ticket and reduces canary weight by configurable fraction. Configs are exposed in canary.yaml under spec.probes.mixer and spec.probes.rollback.

Backward compatibility & rollout: TCM/MSRO are opt-in on canary resources. Default behavior unchanged. We provide a migration guide and example canary manifests in docs/runbooks/perf-canary-tcm.md.

Testing and validation: unit tests for mixer heuristics and deglitch logic; integration tests that run synthetic traffic shapes (stepped, bursted, long-tail) against a canary controller in a local kind cluster. Also added a replay-based regression test that replays a known noisy incident trace; MSRO reduces false-positive alerts by ~72% in the replay compared to the legacy detector (benchmarks in docs/benchmarks/tcm-replay.md).

Operational concerns: added observability hooks: per-cohort probe allocation metrics, composite risk_score metric (tagged by canary_id), and a debug endpoint to fetch current probe mix. Default probe budget limits are conservative to avoid additional load.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc and runbook added - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Backwards-compatible opt-in config - [x] Benchmarks and replay artifacts - [x] CI green (rerun after flaky test fix)

Related work: builds on ENG-2146 (probe reservoir refactor) and ENG-2210 (canary telemetry harmonization). Incident SUP-4321 motivated the deglitch thresholds and replay harness.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the deglitch thresholds (pkg/canary/deglitch.go) and the mixer fairness heuristics (pkg/canary/mixer.go). The fusion model is intentionally lightweight (no external dependencies) to keep the canary controller footprint small.

Links: design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/doc/TCM-MSRO-design, replay artifacts: docs/benchmarks/tcm-replay.md
Adds traffic-conditioned probe scheduling and a multi-signal rollback oracle that fuses latency, throughput, and error signals to reduce false positives in canary rollouts. Backwards-compatible; opt-in via canary config.
Samir Patel (2026-02-19): Can you explain why we chose median-of-means vs winsorized mean for deglitching? Priya Shah: median-of-means gives better robustness to heavy tails in our perf signals; added benchmarks in docs/benchmarks/tcm-replay.md.
Leah Wong (2026-02-20): The default thresholds look conservative; can we expose them as feature flags? Priya Shah: thresholds exposed under spec.probes.rollback.thresholds, documented defaults and recommended ranges in runbook.
Marcus Li (2026-02-21): test flake on integration test tcm_integration_test.go — intermittent race with metrics endpoint. Priya Shah: fixed a lock in mixer.go and reran CI; flake resolved.
Samir Patel (2026-02-22): LGTM after minor nits; approving. Leah Wong (2026-02-22): Approved. Marcus Li (2026-02-23): Approved and requested squash merge to keep history tidy.

Summary
- Adds hard validation + enforcement guardrails for high-cardinality tag dimensions used by the Unit Economics pipeline (model_id/model_version, region, customer_tier, quantization_profile, route_group, streaming).
- Prevents accidental explosions in metrics cardinality (e.g. route_id, raw customer identifiers, arbitrary quantization profile strings) that have previously caused ingestion lag and warehouse view instability.
- Emits explicit counters for dropped/rewritten tags so we can alert before dashboard coverage degrades.

Context
The internal Unit Economics dashboard depends on stable metering dimensions (see Confluence: token-metering-dimensions-and-cardinality). Over the last few weeks we’ve seen several near-misses where a single deploy introduced unbounded values in a tag (route id with embedded customer UUID; quantization profile leaking experiment run ids), which then:
- increased metrics series count significantly,
- delayed downstream rollups, and
- made hourly aggregates partially missing.

This PR implements guardrails at the telemetry emission boundary for the economics-related meter so we fail “safe” (map to canonical buckets) rather than “fail noisy” (explode series / drop ingestion).

Design (what changed)
1) Central TagPolicy and enforcement library
- Introduces telemetry/tag_guardrails (shared lib used by gateway + runtime meter emitter).
- Policy applied per dimension key:
  - max_value_length (truncate + mark)
  - allowed_values allowlist (optional)
  - allowed_regex (optional)
  - max_unique_values_per_window (per-process unique tracker; enforces using LRU+TTL)
  - fallback_value (what we emit when invalid / over limit)

2) Canonicalization changes for known offenders
- route_id is no longer emitted as a metric tag for unit economics. We emit route_group instead.
  - route_group is derived from route metadata (stable, low cardinality) and defaults to "unknown".
  - For debugging, the full route_id is still available in traces/logs (NOT as a metrics tag).
- quantization_profile is validated against a fixed set of allowed values (from model metadata config) and normalized (e.g. "int4-awq" and "INT4_AWQ" -> "int4_awq"). Unknown values map to "unknown".

3) Visibility / safety knobs
- New metrics:
  - telemetry.tag_guardrails.rewritten_total{meter,dimension,reason}
  - telemetry.tag_guardrails.dropped_total{meter,dimension,reason}
  - telemetry.tag_guardrails.unique_limit_exceeded_total{meter,dimension}
- New feature flag:
  - telemetry.tag_guardrails.unit_econ_v1
    - off: no guardrails
    - shadow: validate + emit counters, but do not rewrite/drop
    - enforce: rewrite/drop per policy

4) Aggregation compatibility
- Warehouse rollups already treat "unknown" as a valid bucket. This PR standardizes the fallback values and updates the dimension dictionary in-code comments.

Rollout plan
- Land behind feature flag in shadow mode (24h) in prod.
- SRE/Observability to review rewritten/dropped counters and confirm no unexpected churn.
- Flip to enforce during a low-traffic window.

Testing
- Unit tests for TagPolicy (regex/allowlist/length/unique-window behavior).
- Integration-style tests for the unit-econ meter emitter (ensures we never emit disallowed dimensions; ensures stable fallback values).

Notes / follow-ups
- Follow-up PR will wire guardrail counters into the unit econ pipeline Grafana pack and add an alert when rewritten_total exceeds threshold for >15m (tracked in ENG-8429).

Risk assessment
- Low product risk: only affects internal unit-econ metering tags.
- Moderate observability risk if we incorrectly bucket a tag; mitigated via shadow-mode + metrics.

Screenshots
- N/A (backend only)

Changelog
- Internal-only telemetry behavior change; no external API impact.
Nadia Rahman (requested changes): Unique value limiter should be windowed/TTL-based; a permanent seen-set will eventually drop everything on long-running pods. Also please confirm behavior for streaming vs non-streaming meter paths.
Caleb Johnson (author): Good call. Switched to LRU+TTL (default 60m) and added tests for eviction. Streaming/non-streaming both go through the same unit_econ meter emitter; added an integration test to assert parity.

Allison Grant (comment): +1 on removing route_id. Can you add explicit counters for rewritten vs dropped so we can tune thresholds + alert before aggregates are impacted?
Caleb Johnson: Added telemetry.tag_guardrails.{rewritten_total,dropped_total,unique_limit_exceeded_total} with dimension+reason labels. Also added "shadow" mode so we can observe in prod before enforcement.

Logan Wright (comment): Please make sure fallback buckets are stable and finance-friendly ("unknown" > "other"), and that we don’t introduce a new value that breaks existing hourly rollups.
Caleb Johnson: Standardized fallbacks to "unknown" (and "invalid" only as a reason, not as a dimension value). Mei confirmed the warehouse views already include unknown bucket handling.

Sean Gallagher (comment): Perf concerns—does the unique limiter allocate per request? Also want to avoid logging spam.
Caleb Johnson: Unique limiter uses a lock-free fast path for known values; LRU mutation only on new values. No per-request allocations in steady state (verified via benchmark). No per-request logs; only counters.

Mei Lin (approval): Looks good. Thanks for keeping fallback buckets consistent with the rollup views.

Final approvals: Nadia Rahman, Allison Grant, Logan Wright, Sean Gallagher.
payload.title: Telemetry: cardinality guardrails for unit economics tags

payload.body:
Motivation: constrained-decoding backends (CFG + regex) have been brittle when tokenizers split grammar terminals across byte/word boundaries; this caused streaming truncation and malformed tool/function call frames observed in customer incidents (SUP-887). This PR introduces a priority-driven grammar fallback chain and a tokenizer-aware boundary resolver that normalizes constraint matching against tokenized streams. It also updates the OpenAI-compat function-calling framing to be more resilient to partial streaming boundaries. Design summary: 1) GrammarPriorityResolver: assigns priority to CFG nodes and exposes deterministic fallback semantics when a token boundary prevents a direct match. 2) TokenBoundaryResolver: canonicalizes token sequences into boundary-safe fragments and synthesizes soft-boundary tokens for constrained samplers to consider (without changing model inputs). 3) Streaming Frame Guard: when streaming function/tool outputs, we buffer up to N tokens (configurable, default 6) to confirm boundary integrity before emitting function-call start/stop events; falls back to chunked continuation if ambiguity remains. 4) OpenAI-compat shim: retains existing API surface but adjusts the streaming chunk framing wire format when constraints are active to avoid premature function call termination. Compatibility & risk: backward-compatible at API level; internal sampling path changes may affect deterministic outputs in corner cases — added canary tests and a staged rollout. Test plan: unit tests for CFG fallback permutations, tokenizer fixtures for 6 common tokenizers (BPE, SentencePiece variants), integration e2e that simulates a slow streaming client to validate frame guards, and perf regression benchmarks. Rollout: feature flag rollout by account tier (dev flag -> Canary -> 25% -> 100%) and metric monitoring for service-level latencies and malformed function-call rates. Related: ties to ENG-1423 (constraint stability) and ENG-1568 (streaming tool/frame resilience).
Marco Gutierrez (reviewer): The grammar fallback approach looks sane; two questions — how do we guarantee termination on pathological CFGs, and can we bound memory on the resolver?
Author (Priya Raman): We limit fallback depth to 8 by default and add a circuit-breaker that converts to a permissive match if depth exceeded; added tests for intentionally ambiguous CFGs.
Elaine Zhou (reviewer): The streaming buffering could increase tail latency. Can we make boundaries adaptive based on downstream latency SLOs?
Author (Priya Raman): Added STREAM_GUARD_ADAPTIVE flag and heuristic: default horizon 6 tokens, reduces to 2 when p95 tail latency > SLA, documented in rollout notes.
Jonah Patel (approver): Verified unit + e2e on staging with BPE SentencePiece fixtures. Observed no measurable tokenization regressions. Approving to merge after addressing lint error in stream_shim.
CI Bot: lint check failed on compat/openai/stream_shim.py (line 231) — fixed in commit e5c21bf.
Improves robustness of constrained decoding (CFG & regex) by handling tokenizer boundary splits and reducing malformed function/tool call frames during streaming. Adds a streaming frame guard to reduce premature tool-call termination. Rollout behind feature flag; no API changes.

Introduce Throttle Fade Controller: gradual decay of tenant-level throttles with anticipatory offsets to reduce hard cutoffs during transient demand drops. New telemetry metrics and operator flags. Backwards compatible; opt-in via operator config.
Motivation: Dedicated fleets currently apply abrupt tenant throttles when utilization crosses hard thresholds which causes short-lived request loss and poor tail latency for bursty tenants. This PR adds a Throttle Fade Controller that replaces instant hard-throttle transitions with a controlled exponential decay (fade) and pairs it with an Anticipatory Offset Orchestrator that nudges per-tenant headroom ahead of predicted demand drops using a short-term demand slope detector. The goal is to preserve throughput guarantees while reducing churn/evictions during noisy signals.Technical summary: 1) New controller pkg/autoscaler/throttle_fade_controller.go implements a per-tenant state machine that tracks throttle_level, last_scale_time, fade_factor, and a hold window. Throttles are decayed using an exponential schedule tuned by operator-configurable fade_half_life and min_floor. 2) The anticipatory orchestrator (pkg/autoscaler/anticipatory_offset.go) computes a 30s and 5min slope on admitted requests and emits an anticipatory_offset_gain per tenant which temporarily increases the soft headroom budget to avoid over-aggressive decommit. 3) Telemetry: new metrics decayed_throttle_rate, anticipatory_offset_gain, request_slope_30s and request_slope_5m are registered in observability/metrics_registry.yaml and emitted via pkg/telemetry/metrics_collector.go. 4) Operator config flags and a values.yaml snippet allow ops to opt in and tune behavior (deploy/dedicated/operator/values.yaml and pkg/cli/operator_flags.go). 5) A conservative rollout path: controller is off by default; can be enabled per-pool; includes canary policy changes for 10% of traffic implemented in pkg/rollout/canary_policy.go.Rollout and safety: default fade_half_life is large (30s) and min_floor = 0.05 to avoid starving tenants. There is an automatic safety circuit that reverts to previous hard-throttle if the controller observes sustained SLA violations (pkg/autoscaler/safety_circuit.go). Tests and benchmarks: unit tests for the decay math and slope detector in test/unit/throttle_fade_unit_test.go; an integration test that replays real production traces with synthetic bursts in test/integration/throttle_fade_test.go; benchmark harness in benchmark-lab/benchmarks/throttle_fade_bench.go. Docs: a short design doc and operator guidance added to docs/dedicated/throttle-fade.md and examples/dedicated/anticipatory-offset-config.yaml.Migration notes: feature is opt-in, no DB schema changes. Operator operators should enable on a small pool and observe decayed_throttle_rate and request_slope metrics before broad rollout.Checklist: [x] design review (ENG-2142) [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] telemetry registered [x] operator flags [x] docs and example config [x] canary rollout policy [x] perf benchmark. Related: references ENG-2190 for fairness constraints and SUP-341 for a customer incident motivating smoother throttles.
Ethan Park: Can we clarify how fade_half_life interacts with autoscaler cooldown? Suggest exposing a cooldown_multiplier rather than coupling to absolute timers.
Maya Chen: Good point, added cooldown_multiplier to operator flags; default 1.0 keeps current behavior. Updated unit test to assert interaction.
Ravi Patel: Telemetry names look fine; please add a compact dashboard JSON with thresholds for the new metrics.
Maya Chen: Added observability dashboard snippet to docs and a recommended alert in metrics_registry.yaml.
Claire Dubois: Integration ran for 4h against replay trace, saw a 28% reduction in eviction spikes and tail latency improved at p99 for the noisy tenant. Approving after minor nits.
Automated CI: Integration flaky test fixed in f0d2e3c
Default disabled. To enable: set dedicated.operator.throttleFade.enabled=true and tune fade_half_life, cooldown_multiplier, and min_floor. Watch decayed_throttle_rate, anticipatory_offset_gain, request_slope_30s, and request_slope_5m. Enable on a small canary pool first.
Low-risk opt-in change. No client-visible API changes. Risk is potential under-throttling in pathological high-slope scenarios; mitigated by safety_circuit that reverts to hard-throttle when SLA regressions exceed configured thresholds.
payload.title: Throttle Fade Controller and Anticipatory Offset Orchestrator

Motivation: tenants with spiky but high-value traffic waste unit-econ when cold (cache misses) or when non-optimal quant tiers are chosen conservatively. This PR adds two cooperating components: (1) a tenant-adaptive warming policy that schedules short prefill requests and targeted KV cache warmups for tenants that cross a value threshold, and (2) a hindsight quant calibrator that processes recent request traces offline to suggest tenant-specific quantization tier assignments and safe rollback thresholds.

Goals: reduce tail per-token cost while keeping latency SLOs and avoiding perceptible quality regressions. Make recommendations auditable and reversible. Integrate into existing policy engine and Optimize telemetry.

What this PR changes: single continuous description string that includes the planned changes, diagrams referenced in docs, and migration notes. See changed_files for details.

Implementation highlights: - New tenant_warmer service (runtime component) that submits controlled prefill requests, tracks prefill success, and exposes metrics for cost/benefit per tenant. - HindsightQuantCalibrator (offline worker) that consumes recent traces, computes delta estimates for quality vs token-cost across quant tiers, and produces recommended quant tiers with confidence scores and rollback thresholds. - Policy glue in policy-engine to accept calibrator proposals and schedule canaries at percent-of-traffic with automatic rollback on quality drift. - Safe defaults and a global kill-switch to disable warming/calibrator per-organization. - New SDK endpoint for tenants to opt-out or pin quant tiers.

Backward compatibility & safety: default behavior is inert for tenants that do not opt in or do not meet the value threshold. All calibrator proposals are tagged with expected unit-econ delta and a confidence score; the rollout engine requires at least two high-confidence proposals and a successful canary before applying at scale.

Migration notes: Add a short migration step to the Private installer to enable the hindsight worker and grant it read access to recent trace buckets and cost telemetry. The terraform changes are optional and guarded by feature flags.

Related work: builds on ENG-7122 (batching-credit-meter) and ties into the prefilling primitives from ENG-6561. Supports SUP-3291 customer incident followups for tenant-specific cost spikes.
Diego Alvarez: Can we gate the prefill frequency at the tenant-level so noisy tenants don't flood capacity? (requested change)
Maya Chen: Added tenant-level burst limiter with leaky-bucket enforcement and a global circuit breaker; updated tests.
Priya Natarajan: The confidence scoring looks good but add a small validation that the calibrator doesn't recommend quant tiers that increase average latency beyond target. (requested change)
Maya Chen: Calibrator now computes expected latency delta and rejects proposals that exceed tenant SLO by >5%; added unit tests.
Jonah Blake: Observability panels are helpful; approve after minor doc wording fix.
Maya Chen: Addressed wording and added a short runbook for rollback steps.
Introduce tenant warming policy and hindsight quant calibrator. Adds tenant-level prefill to reduce cold-miss cost, and an offline calibrator that suggests tenant-specific quant tiers with safe canary rollouts. Feature disabled by default; opt-in via SDK or policy. Observability panels and runbooks included.
payload.title: tenant warming policy + hindsight quant calibrator for adaptive unit-econ

payload.body:
Problem: Small, concurrent KV cache reservations for short-context workloads generate many tiny allocations and scheduler handoffs, which increases per-request CPU overhead and creates noisy eviction churn. On high-concurrency generation workloads (many short prompts with streaming), we observed ~18% p50 latency regression and higher tail jitter due to reservation contention and immediate prefetches for marginally useful slots.

Goals: Reduce per-reservation overhead, aggregate small reservations to amortize synchronization, and provide lightweight steering hints to the prefetcher so it focuses on likely hot slots. All changes must be backward compatible with existing slot ownership semantics and respect existing pin/eviction guarantees.

What this PR does:
- Introduces a ReserveAdapter abstraction that sits between caller code (kv_cache::reserve_path) and the underlying block/slot allocator. The adapter performs short-lived aggregation of reservation requests into SlotBatches, holding reservations in a cheap local pool for O(1-5ms) to improve reuse and coalescing.
- Adds a SlotBatcher implementation (slot_batcher.rs) that groups reservations by affinity key (model+request bucket) and sequence length bucket to maximize locality. Batches are size-capped and flushed on a combination of time and backpressure thresholds.
- Adds prefetch steering hooks: the adapter emits lightweight, best-effort steering hints to the prefetcher (prefetcher.rs) so the prefetcher prioritizes batches with higher reuse probability. Hints are advisory; no correctness depends on them.
- Soft-lease counters: rather than hard-pinning on reservation, we introduce a soft-lease counter that allows the eviction fastpath to be aware of recent adapter activity and avoid immediately reclaiming freshly-batched slots. This avoids eviction ping-pong on workloads with rapid reuse.
- Scheduler integration: hint_router.rs consumes adapter hints and maps them to scheduler priorities when routing requests to serving pools. This reduces head-of-line blocking for high-locality batches.
- Tests and microbench: added a microbench harness that simulates 1000 concurrent short prompts to validate latency and throughput improvements and new unit tests for the adapter lifecycle.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- The ReserveAdapter is intentionally lightweight: it retains reservations only for a short dwell period to increase reuse without violating observable semantics. If a reservation is not reused within the dwell window, it's flushed to the allocator as before. This avoids long-lived implicit pins.
- Batching uses affinity keys to maintain strong locality; affinity keys are coarse (model + bucket) to avoid over-sharding.
- Steering hints are lossy and non-authoritative: they only influence prefetch ordering. If the prefetcher is disabled the system still functions identically to today.
- We intentionally avoid adding additional persistent metadata to the block header to keep on-disk compatibility intact. All adapter state is in-memory and ephemeral.

Benchmark results (local perf lab, p95 runs):
- Baseline: 1000 concurrent short-stream requests, p50 latency 18.4ms, throughput 9.4k tokens/s, CPU 78%
- With ReserveAdapter: p50 latency 15.1ms (-18%), throughput 10.8k tokens/s (+15%), CPU 66% (-15% CPU), tail jitter reduced (p99 / p50 ratio improved ~22%)
- Memory: transient adapter overhead ~1.5MB per serving worker under test config; configurable via adapter.max_memory_bytes.

Checklist (both checked in code where applicable):
- [x] Unit tests for adapter lifecycle and batch flush semantics
- [x] Microbench harness reproducing high-concurrency short-context workload
- [x] CI integration: lint, unit, integration microbench step
- [x] Config knobs and defaults exposed via runtime config with safe conservative defaults
- [x] Design doc: docs/design/kv-slot-batcher.md

Files changed (high-level):
- src/runtime/kv_cache/reserve_adapter.rs: new core. Contains ReserveAdapter, lightweight timing wheel, and metrics emission.
- src/runtime/block_manager/slot_batcher.rs: new batching policy, capacity accounting, and flush logic.
- src/runtime/prefetch/prefetcher.rs: accept optional advisory steering hints; small reordering logic.
- src/runtime/scheduler/hint_router.rs: minor router extension to map hints to priority lanes.
- src/runtime/kv_cache/mod.rs: wiring into existing reserve_path entrypoint and config knobs.
- tests/microbench/kv_slot_batcher.rs: harness and reproducible scenarios.
- docs/design/kv-slot-batcher.md: rationale, knobs, and perf numbers.
- Cargo.toml: added small dev-dep for bench harness.

Review conversation (high-level chronology):
- Ravi: "Nice clean separation. Two requests: (1) can we make the dwell window configurable per-pool? (2) please add a metric for 'batched_reserve_hit_rate' so we can SLO on expected reuse."
  - Maya: "Added pool-level dwell window (config + safe default) and a new metric 'kv.reserve_adapter.batch_hit_ratio' exposed via metrics crate. See last commit e4a1d07."
- Sofia: "Concern about eviction interaction: if batches keep slots alive, will this starve other tenants?"
  - Maya: "Adapter uses soft-lease counters with max_soft_lease_ms; eviction code checks combined hard pins + soft_lease and falls back to reclamation under memory pressure. I added comments and a unit test validating reclamation under forced pressure."
- Liam: "Microbench was convincing. Can we add a short integration test that runs the hint path through the scheduler to ensure no regressions?"
  - Maya: "Added a scheduler routing smoke test in microbench. It exercises hint->router->pool path."
- Ravi (approve): "LGTM after docs update"
- Sofia (approve): "Verified on perf lab, merging after CI passes"

CI: All checks passed (lint, unit, integration microbench using perf-canary harness). No flaky runs in the observed CI window.

Follow-ups and future work:
- Explore adaptive dwell window based on measured reuse heat (ENG-2334).
- Consider exposing per-model affinity tuning via config center for large customers.
- Longer-term: merge steering hints with predictive prefetch models in prefetcher v2.

Notes: This change targets runtime performance and is safe for release without customer-facing API changes. Ops: rollout plan is a staged flag rollout (off by default), enable for a subset of serving pools, validate metrics, then flip globally if stable.

Related resources: Linear ENG-2217 (kv reservation batching), ENG-2334 (prefetch steering followup). Design doc: docs/design/kv-slot-batcher.md (included in this PR).
Introduce a lightweight reserve adapter that batches small KV slot reservations and supplies prefetch steering hints to the prefetcher. Improves median latency under high-concurrency workloads and reduces per-token CPU overhead. No API/compatibility changes.
payload.title: kv-slot-batcher: reserve adapter for lightweight slot batching and prefetch steering

payload.body:
Context: We need a safer, deterministic way to promote model variants across time-ordered cohorts (e.g., night->morning->day) while being able to rehearse and validate rollback strategies offline. Current canary controllers focus on traffic fraction and random sampling; they make it hard to reproduce incidents tied to temporal cohort ordering and session-anchored users. Motivation: support product requests for time-windowed rollouts and to reduce noise in SLO regressions by deterministic cohort assignment. This PR introduces a chronological cohort release controller plus a rollback simulation harness that can (1) simulate policy-driven failures, (2) run micro-bisect scenarios across cohorts, and (3) produce deterministic traces for postmortem and automated rollback policy tuning. Summary of changes: - controller/chronological_cohort_controller.py: new controller implementing time-window cohort phases, cohort fencing, and session affinity preservation. - sim/rollback_harness.go: a lightweight simulator that replays traces and injects policy failures (latency, error spike, partial degradations) and computes candidate rollback points. - policies/rollback_policy_v2.yaml: new policy document that maps multi-metric gates (latency, error, quality eval) to rollback decision types (gradual-drain, immediate-swap, staged-revert). - docs/rollouts/chronological-cohort.md: design doc and operator playbook for running offline rehearse and live promotions. - tests/e2e/chron-cohort-e2e.py: end-to-end smoke tests that run a simulated 3-cohort promotion with a forced late cohort regression and validate rollback decisions. - infra/helm/values-rollout.yaml: optional Helm knobs for enabling deterministic replay mode in Private deployments. Design highlights: - Deterministic cohort assignment: users are deterministically hashed into chronological cohorts with a TTL-aware binder so a user's cohort remains stable for the rollout window. - Time-window phases: cohorts are gated by absolute wall-clock windows and can be paused/resumed by operator or automated SLO gates. - Rollback rehearsal: the harness can run a replay of live traces with synthetic degradations and evaluate how the configured policy would have behaved, producing a replay report and recommended policy adjustments. - Micro-bisect mode: the harness supports a binary-search-like simulation to find minimal cohort sets required to reproduce an SLO regression, enabling targeted rollbacks without full revert. Compatibility and migration: - No breaking user-facing APIs. - Helm flag rollout.deterministicReplay=false by default. Operators can opt-in per-cluster. Testing and verification: - Added unit tests for cohort hash stability and TTL rebind behavior. - E2E smoke covers a full promotion + mid-progress rollback path. - Simulator comes with deterministic seed option to make runs reproducible. Checklist: - [x] Design doc and playbook added - [x] Implementation of controller and simulation harness - [x] Unit tests and smoke e2e - [x] Helm values and docs - [x] Perf baseline: controller adds ~2.6% CPU on control-plane pod under synthetic load - [x] Security review: no new secrets stored; harness runs with cluster-reader role - [x] Manual staging rollout validated on staging cluster (2026-02-10) Commits: - "init: chronological cohort controller and API surface" - "sim: rollback harness prototype with deterministic seed" - "policies: add rollback_policy_v2 and mapping docs" - "docs: chronological cohort operator playbook" - "tests: add e2e smoke and unit tests for TTL binder" - "infra/helm/values-rollout.yaml: optional Helm knobs for enabling deterministic replay mode in Private deployments." - "Makefile (targets to run harness and e2e)" CI summary: - CI run #1: unit tests failed (timing-sensitive test flakiness in cohort TTL binder) - investigation: non-deterministic sleep in test harness; replaced with deterministic clock stub - CI run #2: all checks passed (lint, unit, integration, e2e-smoke with mocked sim) - Size/perf checks: control-plane pod CPU delta measured in staging; dashboard link: https://internal.redwood/reports/rollout/cpu-delta/545210 (internal) Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2026-02-18 after approvals. Migration plan: ops will enable rollout.deterministicReplay on staging for 48 hours and run a suite of historical replays for the last 30 days of traffic. Known limitations and follow-ups: - The harness does not simulate KV cache warm starts; follow-up ticket ENG-4489 scheduled to add model-stateful replay. - Does not yet integrate with Optimize's quantization recommendations; follow-up ENG-4522. - We observed a small CPU increase in the controller; plan to optimize the binder to avoid repeated hash computations. Contact: Priya Nair (author) and Ethan Ross (owner for production rollout).
Adds a deterministic chronological-cohort release controller with an independent rollback simulation harness. No API changes for customers. Enables scheduled cohort promotions and offline rollback rehearsal for safety validation.
Ethan Ross: Important work — controller looks clean. One request: can the cohort binder expose a metrics tag for cohort_id to make SLO drilldowns easier?
Priya Nair: Added cohort_id tag to metrics in next commit and instrumented trace-id -> cohort mapping in logs.
Sofia Martinez: The micro-bisect API looks powerful but I'm worried about operator safety. Can we add a dry-run flag so the harness never issues writes in rehearsal mode?
Priya Nair: Dry-run flag added in sim harness; it runs in read-only trace replay by default. Documented in playbook.
Liam Zhang: CI caught a flaky test — good catch. After fix, e2e smoke passed locally. Approving pending squash.
CI Bot: unit tests passed, integration passed, e2e-smoke (mocked) passed.

Summary: This PR instruments the API Gateway admin/control endpoints to emit canonical Audit Log Schema v1 events for sensitive actions (quota overrides, rate-limit/quota policy updates, key validation / key-policy configuration changes), and standardizes actor attribution by deriving actor fields from auth context consistently. The goal is parity with Control Plane/Console audit events and to remove the current drift where some gateway-emitted events lack stable actor/source fields, which has shown up as inconsistent SIEM exports (ref SUP-18477). Context: As part of audit logging standardization (ENG-4824), we need 100% coverage for sensitive actions across the platform with consistent actor/target semantics and correlation IDs. Gateway is a key gap because it sits in front of several admin surfaces and also owns enforcement knobs (quota overrides, validation policies) that should be auditable. What changed: (1) Added Audit v1 emission to Gateway admin routes: POST/PUT /admin/quotas/overrides (create/update/delete override), PUT /admin/key-policy (allowed issuers, token validation flags, audience config), PUT /admin/rate-limits (tier config updates), and PUT /admin/quotas/defaults (tenant defaults). (2) Normalized actor attribution: implemented a single "ActorFromAuthContext" mapping used by all audit producers in gateway so actor_type/actor_id/actor_display_name/source_ip/user_agent/auth_method are consistently populated. Includes support for service-to-service calls (mTLS/JWT) and Console/admin UI calls (OIDC). (3) Correlation + idempotency: ensures request_id and trace_id are present on all emitted events; adds gateway_admin_action_id derived from request_id for internal correlation; event_id generated as ULID at emission time. (4) Cardinality and redaction: event payload includes bounded/summarized diffs (no raw policy JSON), and explicitly avoids emitting secrets/credentials. The only free-form strings are capped and allow-listed where applicable (e.g., quota_tier). (5) Tests: Added unit tests for actor mapping, diff summarization, and required-fields validation against schema v1; added integration test coverage for representative admin calls in gateway test harness. Event types introduced/used (registered in centralized registry already): - gateway.quota_override.created - gateway.quota_override.updated - gateway.quota_override.deleted - gateway.quota_defaults.updated - gateway.rate_limit_policy.updated - gateway.key_validation_policy.updated Example event (trimmed): {"schema_version":"1.0","event_id":"01JH8Y4J9K6R8E9P7YH5WQ8B9S","event_type":"gateway.quota_override.updated","occurred_at":"2026-02-01T19:22:11.481Z","environment":"prod","deployment_mode":"hosted","tenant_id":"tnt_9b7...","project_id":"prj_4a1...","actor_type":"user","actor_id":"usr_2c1...","actor_display_name":"chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com","auth_method":"oidc","source_ip":"203.0.113.10","user_agent":"Mozilla/5.0 ...","request_id":"req_7f6...","trace_id":"5d2c...","target_type":"tenant","target_id":"tnt_9b7...","resource_type":"quota_override","resource_id":"qov_13f...","action":"update","result":"success","changes_summary":"max_rps: 200 -> 500; expires_at: null -> 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z"} Notes on behavior/failure modes: Audit emission is best-effort and must not break the admin workflow if the audit sink is degraded; we still log structured gateway errors and increment audit_emit_failed counter. (Delivery guarantees tracked in separate ADR/ENG-4829; this PR only aligns gateway with the platform standard.) Rollout/compatibility: This only adds new v1 events; does not remove legacy gateway logs. Exporter normalization is handled in audit-log-exporter (ENG-4827). Checklist: - [x] Event payloads validate against schema v1 - [x] Actor/source fields populated for user + service actors - [x] request_id + trace_id present - [x] No secrets/PII beyond policy-approved fields - [x] Tests added (unit + integration) - [x] Updated gateway admin endpoint docs (internal) Links: ENG-4824 (Gateway coverage), ENG-4830 (correlation IDs), PR #21984 (schema lib/validator), PR #21991 (event type registry)
gateway/audit: add v1 audit emitter helpers and schema validation hook
gateway/auth: implement ActorFromAuthContext mapping (user/service/impersonation-safe)
gateway/admin: emit audit events for quota override CRUD
gateway/admin: emit audit events for key validation + rate limit/quota policy updates
tests: add actor mapping fixtures + schema required-field tests
tests: add gateway admin integration tests asserting audit event shape
Allison Grant (review): Can we ensure source_ip is pulled from the same trusted header set we use for request logging? Also please confirm we cap user_agent length to avoid cardinality / ingestion issues.
Amara Diallo (author): Yep. Switched to the existing "clientIpFromTrustedProxyChain" helper (same as access logs) and added a 256-char cap + "<truncated>" suffix for user_agent. Added a unit test for both.
Kevin Osei (review): For SIEM export dedupe, we should be explicit that event_id is stable per emission, but retries may cause duplicates. Do we include any idempotency key (e.g., request_id + event_type)?
Amara Diallo (author): Added gateway_admin_action_id = request_id and ensured request_id is always present. Export guidance will recommend de-dupe on (event_type, request_id) when present. event_id remains ULID per emission (consistent with platform direction in eng-security thread).
Ethan Park (review): Changes_summary should avoid embedding raw JSON blobs. For key_policy updates, can we summarize only the changed fields and keep allow-lists?
Amara Diallo (author): Updated diff builder to allow-list: issuers_count, audiences_count, "jwks_refresh_enabled" boolean, and "token_leeway_seconds". No raw issuer URLs or audience strings are logged (counts only). Added tests.
Sahana Iyer (review): CI lint is passing but can we add a compile-time check that every admin handler uses the AuditAdminAction wrapper? Otherwise future endpoints may skip emission.
Amara Diallo (author): Added a shared wrapper and refactored all admin handlers in this PR to use it. Follow-up ticket is in ENG-4831 for cross-service enforcement; within gateway I added an eslint rule scoped to /admin routes to prevent direct handler exports without wrapper (see last commit).
Marcus Lin (review): Looks good. Please confirm behavior when audit sink is down: admin action still succeeds but metrics and structured logs are emitted. Also add a short note in release notes for internal rollout.
Amara Diallo (author): Confirmed: emitter failure increments audit_emit_failed and logs a structured error with request_id/trace_id; no exception bubbles to handler. Added internal release note line.
Marcus Lin: Approved.
Allison Grant: Approved.
Kevin Osei: Approved.
Internal: API Gateway now emits canonical audit events for quota overrides and key/rate-limit policy changes with normalized actor attribution (v1 schema).
Post-merge: coordinate with Logan Wright/Nadia Rahman to ensure coverage dashboard picks up new gateway event types; verify sampling in prod once enabled for enterprise tenants.

payload.body:
Motivation: customers need per-tenant serving defaults that balance latency SLOs and unit economics without manual tuning. This PR adds a small, opinionated microservice (slate-concierge) that synthesizes tenant-specific batch/cache defaults and candidate quantization 'slates' by combining sample-weighted traffic signals, recent telemetry, and safe heuristic fallbacks. The service emits human-readable slate recommendations plus a machine-consumable JSON manifest that can be applied via the existing defaults-as-code CLI. Key design goals: non-destructive (read-only by default), simulation-first (dry-run and cost/latency estimate modes), conservative fallbacks for tail latency, and explainability for audit/SME review. What changed: implemented a new service at services/slate_concierge with a lightweight HTTP API and a CLI integration; added a quant-slate generator module that produces candidate quant profiles (FP16/INT8 mixed presets and knob suggestions) along with estimated token cost deltas and simulated latency curves; introduced a small latency/cost simulator to validate recommendations against historical slices; added unit and integration tests and a telemetry adapter that reads recent token-latency histograms from observability. Checklist: - [x] Core concierge service and API - [x] Quant slate generation and scoring - [x] Dry-run CLI + simulate mode - [x] Unit tests and e2e harness - [x] Telemetry adapter for 90-day windows - [x] Docs and sample defaults-as-code manifest - [x] Migration and safe-apply flow (opt-in). Risk profile and mitigations: defaults are not applied automatically; the CLI requires --apply and a tenant-owner signoff. Simulations include headroom margins for tail latency and will annotate confidence levels. Performance: in synthetic tenant tests across three traffic shapes we saw median cost improvement 17-26% with <3% median latency increase and 95th percentile latency within configured SLA for the conservative slate. Observability: added a new dashboard tile and alert rule for slate-apply failures. Related work: builds on ENG-1024 and reuses parts of the prefill telemetry pipeline from ENG-2587. Release/rollout: feature gated behind slate_concierge.enabled, staged rollout to internal tenants then to opt-in customers. Followups: automated A/B rollout, CI scenario for tenant-history regression, extended quant-profile library. See commits and changed files for details.

payload.body:
Motivation: We’ve had multiple investigations where KV/prefix cache hit-rate dropped, but we couldn’t quantify the *cost impact* on prefill. This PR introduces a first-pass metric for “wasted prefill”: prefill tokens that were computed but did not contribute to subsequent decode reuse because we missed/evicted/disabled caching. The goal is a privacy-safe, low-overhead signal we can correlate with cache pressure to (a) triage regressions and (b) power recommendations (e.g., increase max_prefix_cache_bytes, adjust TTL/eviction policy, fix version mismatch, or change routing locality).

Definition (per ADR-in-progress / sprint alignment):
- Wasted prefill tokens are counted per request at the end of prefill.
- For a given request, we compute: wasted_prefill_tokens = prefill_tokens - reused_tokens_observed.
- reused_tokens_observed is the number of prefill tokens that are attributable to prefix/KV reuse for the subsequent decode path of the same request.
- We intentionally bucket this at request-level and aggregate to avoid logging prompts or adding high-cardinality dimensions.

Implementation notes:
- Adds a new histogram: runtime.cache.wasted_prefill_tokens (buckets aligned to prompt-length bucket policy).
- Adds a companion counter: runtime.cache.wasted_prefill_requests_total with a miss_reason label (enum) to help separate “real misses” vs “cache disabled” vs “evicted/pressure”.
- Emits lightweight correlation counters when eviction/pressure is active during prefill: runtime.cache.wasted_prefill_eviction_correlated_total and runtime.cache.wasted_prefill_pressure_correlated_total (both low-cardinality, no per-tenant labels).
- Sampling: the histogram is sampled using the existing cache telemetry sampling knobs (default unchanged); counters remain unsampled but are kept low-cardinality.
- Avoids per-tenant, per-prompt hash, or request-id labels; uses allowlisted route/model/version tags via request context plumbing already in-flight.

Operational impact:
- Overhead: adds a couple of integer accumulators per request + single emission at prefill end; no per-token events.
- Can be used in dashboards to show wasted prefill alongside hit-rate and eviction/pressure, especially useful when workload mix changes make hit-rate alone ambiguous.

Testing:
- Unit tests for token accounting under (1) full miss, (2) partial reuse, (3) policy disabled, (4) eviction during prefill.
- Integration test extends the cache-metrics harness to assert wasted prefill > 0 on forced misses and ~0 on stable cache reuse.
- Perf: validated in perf-canary locally; no measurable p95 regression at default sampling.

Follow-ups (not in this PR):
- Fold this into the canonical metrics naming PR and dashboard panels (separate PRs).
- Improve semantics for streaming retries and batched prefill attribution (tracked separately).
Omar El-Sayed (review): Definition question: reused_tokens_observed — are we counting prefix cache reuse only, or KV cache reuse too? For multi-turn chat, this can be tricky if we extend the KV across turns.

Samir Qureshi (author): Counting both prefix cache and KV cache reuse, but only as observed/attributed during prefill->decode planning for the *same request*. I’m avoiding cross-request attribution in v1. For multi-turn chat, each turn is its own request; reuse is captured if the runtime reuses cached prefix/KV for that turn.

Noah Patel (review): The correlation counters seem a bit hand-wavy. Can we ensure they don’t become “always on” under high utilization and lose meaning? Also please confirm they don’t have route/model tags.

Samir Qureshi (author): Good point. I’m scoping correlation as “eviction occurred during this request’s prefill window” and “pressure gauge exceeded threshold during prefill window”. Tags are intentionally restricted to {deployment_mode, region} only. Added comments + tests asserting tag set.

Nadia Rahman (review): Naming: please align with our cache metrics naming conventions (runtime.cache.*). Also ensure histogram buckets match the prompt-length bucket policy.

Samir Qureshi (author): Updated names to runtime.cache.wasted_prefill_tokens + runtime.cache.wasted_prefill_requests_total. Histogram buckets now reuse the same bucket boundaries as prompt_len_bucket definitions; included in registry.

Marcus Reed (review): Perf: can you add a micro benchmark or at least a note about allocations? Observing histogram per request can allocate if tags aren’t stable.

Samir Qureshi (author): Verified tags come from a cached/arena-backed tag set; no per-request allocations beyond integer math. Added a perf note + ensured the tags are built once per request context.

Allison Grant (review): For dashboards, we’ll want to compare wasted prefill with eviction pressure. Can you include an explicit miss_reason for policy_disabled vs version_mismatch? That will help triage.

Samir Qureshi (author): Added miss_reason propagation in the counter path. Currently supports: capacity, ttl_expired, policy_disabled, hash_mismatch, version_mismatch, unknown. (Enum already shared with other cache metrics PRs.)

Omar El-Sayed (final approval): Looks good for v1. Please file a follow-up to reconcile semantics under streaming retries (we’ve seen double counting elsewhere).

Samir Qureshi (author): Filed follow-up and added a TODO with a link to the retry semantics ticket.
payload.title: runtime/telemetry: add wasted prefill metric + correlate with eviction/pressure
