Motivation: Our lint and preflight coverage has grown ad-hoc: language-specific runners, duplicated init logic across devcontainers, and a couple of fragile GitHub Action jobs that required frequent pin updates. This PR introduces a small, opinionated "plugboard" for the lint harness (lightweight adapter layer so new linters/runners can be added without forking pipeline logic) and consolidates the release automation's quiet-window handling into a single, observable step. The goals are: 1) reduce repeated CI YAML and bootstrapping, 2) make lint plugins discoverable and versioned, 3) reduce release flakiness during rollouts and simplify merge windows. Summary of changes (high level): - Add tools/ci/lint-plugboard: a tiny shim (Go) that enumerates configured plugins, runs them with standardized environment and exit codes, and emits structured JSON diagnostics to stdout. This lets the GH Action job call a single entrypoint regardless of language. - Replace three separate lint GH jobs with a single job that delegates to the plugboard; keep language-specific containers but unify setup steps. - Consolidate release automation quiet-window logic into .github/actions/quiet-window (JS action wrapper) so the window is enforced consistently across scheduled and manual releases. - Bump a few GH Action pins to reduce flakes and add a lightweight dep-scan step that reports stale pins to CI telemetry (does not fail merges). - Small devcontainer cleanup and README for plugin authors. Checklist: - [x] Implement plugboard shim + README - [x] Update GitHub workflows to use unified job - [x] Add quiet-window action and migrate existing release workflows - [x] Pin critical actions and add dep-scan reporter - [x] Smoke test local runner + nightly on staging - [x] Add migration notes for platform teams Rollout plan: - Merge to main behind a staged rollout flag. - Enable plugboard for lint:fastpath lane first (low impact). - Monitor CI latency/queue metrics and lint failure rate in Console. - If any language plugin misbehaves, the plugboard is designed to fall back to the previous behavior via feature flag. Backwards-compatibility notes: The plugboard supports a compatibility mode that preserves prior job contracts (exit codes and artifact names). Existing devcontainers continue to work unchanged unless teams opt in to the discovery mechanism. Testing performed: - Unit tests for plugboard command parsing and plugin lifecycle mocks. - Nightly integration on staging with matrix of node/go/python containers. - Manual dry run of release quiet-window (simulated conflicts) to verify enforcement and logs. CI history: first run failed due to one pinned action requiring a minor refactor (eslint action version mismatch); author iterated and bumped only the required action instead of blanket upgrades. Final runs: all checks green. Impact on deps: bumped eslint to 8.38.x, actions/checkout pinned to v4@sha256..., setup-go minor patch, added small dep-scan tool (non-blocking). Migration notes for integrators: - To add a new language linter: add a new plugin entry under tools/ci/lint-plugboard/plugins.yaml and provide a small wrapper that conforms to the plugboard interface (exit codes + JSON minimal schema). - If you depend on previous artifact names, set CI_LINT_COMPAT=1 in your job. Related work: ENG-4589 (lint runway), ENG-4620 (release automation stability).
Diego Marquez (2026-02-21): Nice consolidation. A few questions: can we guarantee the plugboard won't add >100ms to job startup? Also please add a small telemetry ping that records plugin version so we can triage flaky linters.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-21): Reply: startup cost is ~20ms based on local profiling; added optional telemetry ping behind PLUGBOARD_TELEMETRY=false by default. See commit e3c7b55.
Lin Zhao (2026-02-23): Found an edge case where a python plugin swallows stderr and returns 0. Request: add stricter validation on JSON diagnostics. Marked as changes requested.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-24): Addressed: plugboard now validates JSON schema and fails fast if diagnostics are malformed. Added unit tests.
Marcus Nguyen (2026-02-26): Verified release quiet-window logs. Suggest adding a short explanation in the release handbook about expected behavior when merges land during a window. Small nit: document default timeout.
Marcus Nguyen (2026-02-27): Approved after text tweak.
CI Bot (2026-02-28): ESLint job failed on first run (plugin version mismatch). Rerun with pinned action passed.
Add a unified lint plugboard to simplify adding new language linters; consolidate release quiet-window into a single action for consistent enforcement; pin a small set of critical GH Actions to reduce flakes and add a non-blocking dep-scan reporter. No breaking API changes for pipelines; opt-in discovery mode available.

payload.body: Motivation: During a recent regional overload incident we observed rapid oscillation between failover and reopen states for a subset of tenants when KV pressure and short-lived traffic spikes coincided. This caused noisy fallbacks and unnecessary cross-region egress. This PR introduces two coordinated mechanisms to make degradation behavior more stable and predictable: 1) an Ephemeral Fallback Limiter (EFL) that rate-limits transient fallback decisions using a lease-backed admission window, with hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping; 2) a Priority Calibrator that adjusts tenant evict/holdoff weights based on recent SLO burn and tokenized latency percentiles to preserve fairness across cohorts. Key design points: EFL uses a lightweight distributed lease (existing ring-based lease store) so decisions survive restarts but expire quickly; limiter accepts short bursts but enforces a decaying allowance when repeated fallbacks occur; Priority Calibrator runs per-routing cohort and translates observed P95/P99 latency deltas into small, timeboxed weight nudges rather than large immediate reassignments. Scope: runtime admission controller, a new calibration controller in controlplane, observability additions (metrics and traces), config knobs in console defaults, and a small compatibility shim so Dedicated pools with older agents fall back to a safe default. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-3621) - [x] unit tests for limiter logic - [x] integration test with simulated KV pressure - [x] e2e canary rollout (10% traffic) - [x] console flag and README snippet - [x] telemetry dashboards updated - [x] feature gated behind runtime flag for safe rollback Rollout plan: staged rollout to canary clusters for 48h, monitor SLO burn, P99 tail latency, cross-region egress. If SLO burn increases >10% relative to baseline revert flag. Backwards compatibility: if controlplane calibration fails or RPC times out, runtime falls back to a stable-weight method; Dedicated agents without lease support use a local in-memory limiter with stricter thresholds. Why different from previous approaches: this implementation explicitly ties short-term fallback allowances to a rapidly expiring lease and couples it to observed SLO deltas to avoid permanent demotions for transient noise. Commits summary: - add ephemeral fallback limiter core + unit tests - implement priority calibrator controller + integration tests - add metrics/traces and console feature flag - compatibility shim for old dedicated agents - update docs and rollout script Changed files (high-level): - runtime/admission/efl_limiter.go - controlplane/calibrator/controller.go - controlplane/calibrator/calibrator_test.go - observability/metrics/efl_metrics.md - console/feature_flags.yaml - ci/canary-rollout/efl_rollout.sh - tests/integration/kv_pressure_simulator.go - docs/runbooks/ephemeral-fallback.md - charts/dedicated/compat-shim.yaml Impacted areas: runtime admission path (hot), controlplane calibration loop (medium), console defaults (low), Dedicated agent compatibility handling (small).

Motivation: CI feedback latency has been increasing as dependency upgrades, monorepo-wide lint runs, and full integration tests run for small focused changes. This PR introduces a lightweight 'dependency-coordinator' job that centralizes dependency-bump orchestration and a fastpath lint lane to give engineers quick feedback for localized edits. Goals: 1) reduce developer wall-time for common changes, 2) make dependency upgrades non-blocking by separating coordination and artifact creation, 3) improve signal-to-noise for lint failures by scoping fast failures to touched packages and running the full lint in a slower gated lane, and 4) tighten action pinning for release hooks.

What this PR does: - Add a new CI job workflow: .github/workflows/ci-dep-coordinator.yml that runs weekly and on demand to batch compatible dependency upgrades, create curated PRs, and publish a coordination manifest picked up by downstream CI lanes. The coordinator does not merge but posts a Linear ticket suggestion and a release-note draft. - Introduce fastpath lint lane: .github/workflows/lint-fastpath.yml which runs for changes limited by path filters (packages/*, sdk/*, docs/*). It runs eslint/ruff/format-checks and a lightweight type-checker. - Update existing lint workflow to run as lint-full.yml (nightly and pre-merge for high-risk PRs) that includes exhaustive checks and cross-package rules. - Change release automation: release-annotator action pinned to a specific sha with an updater that reads the coordination manifest to reduce false-positive release notes generated during batched upgrades. - Add caching/warmers: small prebuild job to fetch prebuilt toolchain artifacts and restore node/python caches earlier in the pipeline to reduce redundant installs for shard jobs. - Add documentation: docs/ci/README.md with contributor-facing guidance on when the coordinator will create PRs and how to opt out for single-package hotfixes. - Pin a handful of actions (setup-node, actions/cache, release-annotator) to SHAs and update lockfiles for the hermetic builder image.

Important notes: - No runtime code changes to product binaries. All edits are CI and tooling only. - The coordinator introduces a curated manifest under .ci/dep-coordinator/manifest.json; downstream jobs read it through a single artifact download step to minimize repeated network calls. - This PR intentionally narrows the fastpath lint to produce earlier, high-value feedback; teams touching multiple packages will still get the full lint. - There was one flaky integration test during validation; tests were rerun and all checks passed prior to merge.

Summary: Introduce a tenant-scoped PrefillAllocator that derives conservative prefill budgets, microbatch sizes, and transient burst lanes from tenant profile histograms; add econ-sim CLI that replays exported traces to estimate token-cost, median and tail latencies, and effective tokens-per-dollar for candidate defaults; include an interactive quantization profile wizard that generates three suggested qprofiles (safe, balanced, aggressive) with estimated quality delta and fallback rules. Motivation: Global defaults are brittle across tenant traffic shapes and lead to uneven unit economics. By simulating tenant-level outcomes and producing tenant-aware prefill and quant defaults, operators can reduce cost while containing regression risk. What changed: 1) runtime: pkg/prefill implements PrefillAllocator, tenant policy engine, and conservative safety multiplier; 2) cli: cmd/econ-sim provides replay tooling with S3/CSV inputs and outputs JSON/CSV summaries and suggested defaults; 3) tools: tools/quant-wizard generates qprofile artifacts and a small exportable manifest; 4) web: console preview page to review and apply tenant defaults behind feature flag; 5) telemetry: new sim events and metrics to track simulated cost and estimated quality delta; 6) db: migration adds tenant_profile defaults and a backfill job. Rollout: Feature-flagged under tenant_prefill_allocator_v1. Start internal alpha for 10 tenants, enable opt-in in Console, then staged rollout to opt-in customers. Safety: automatic fallback to global defaults if observed quality delta exceeds 3%; CLI and wizard default to conservative profile unless --allow-aggressive is specified. Tests: unit tests for allocator heuristics, integration tests for econ-sim replay, e2e smoke tests for console apply flow. Notes: Offline sim runs on representative traces showed balanced profiles reduce token-cost by ~12% with <1% simulated latency increase; aggressive profiles can approach ~20% saving but require manual review. CI: initial flaky integration test fixed (deterministic sort); final CI passed. Merge: squash-merged to main. Follow-ups: ENG-2499 to add Bayesian estimator for quality delta and additional telemetry dashboards.

Context: Token-level telemetry and sampled logs have become a major driver of metrics cardinality and dashboard noise for long-tail customers. Frequent short-lived token spikes (e.g., multi-token bursts from streaming clients) were triggering noisy paging and masking real regressions. Motivation: Reduce ingestion and dashboard noise while preserving investigatability: compact frequently-repeating event sequences into an indexable compact snapshot, surface token-phase sparklines on per-route panels, and add an alert quiescer that automatically suppresses repeated short-lived spikes for a configurable window. This PR implements a compact event indexer service, a lightweight per-invocation snapshot format, dashboard panels, and an alert quiescer + rollout plan. Key changes (high level): - Introduce compact event indexer microservice (telemetry/compact-index) that consumes sampled spans and log fragments, performs deduplication of recurring token-phase sequences, and emits compact snapshots keyed by (tenant, route, token_phase_hash). - Add an invocation-level snapshot format (span.attributes.compact_snapshot_ref) that stores a 128-bit stable ref and small metadata (seq_count, top_tokens, estimated_cost_cents) to avoid embedding full token sequences in traces. Snapshots are retained in a TTL-backed store for 7 days by default. - Emit a new span attribute request.token_cost_cents and request.token_phase_map to improve per-span cost and phase decomposition for downstream rollups. - Dashboard: new "Token Phase Sparklines" row on per-route dashboard that uses compact snapshot refs to render per-phase small-multiples and a compact noise metric. - Alert quiescer: an alert middleware that detects repeated bursts from the same token_phase_hash and suppresses firing if bursts are < 5s and occur within a 60s window (configurable per-tenant). - Telemetry: histograms for compact_index_hit_rate, snapshot_store_size_bytes, quiescer_suppressed_count added to prometheus exporters and per-tenant rollups. Why this is different: instead of increasing sampling or broad downsampling (which loses fidelity), the indexer preserves the ability to inspect exact example sequences via snapshot refs while dramatically lowering cardinality in primary telemetry paths. Backwards compatibility: Old spans without compact_snapshot_ref are still fully supported; compaction is opt-in per-tenant during rollout. Rollout plan: 1) Canary deployment in telemetry/canary (48h) with quiescer off and sampling at 1% for snapshots. 2) Enable compact snapshots for 5 pilot tenants, monitor compact_index_hit_rate and snapshot retrieval latencies. 3) Gradually increase snapshot sampling to 10% and enable quiescer with default thresholds. Migration notes: - Snapshot references are opaque; UI and on-call runbooks updated to resolve a snapshot via the compact-index service when a user clicks a sparkline. - Short-term storage cost (~+2-3% telemetry storage) expected during ramp; long-term cardinality reduction reduces downstream storage by ~10-20% for heavy-tail routes. Testing: - Unit tests for compaction/dedup logic and hash stability across CPU endianness. - Integration tests that verify span attribute injection, snapshot store retrieval, and per-route dashboard rendering in storybook. - Load bench: simulated 10k/s sampled spans with 20% repeated sequences; compaction reduced exported sample count to telemetry backend by ~58% and decreased Grafana panel query times by ~22%. Rollback: disable compaction in config and backfill spans remain unaffected. Observability & alerting: added ephemeral SLOs to monitor snapshot store latency (p50 < 30ms), hit_rate > 0.6 after pilot, and quiescer suppression rate. Security & privacy: snapshots redact PII following existing redact pipeline; snapshot store enforces tenant-scoped ACLs and KMS encryption at rest. Checklist: - [x] Compact indexer service implemented - [x] Snapshot format v1 defined and gated - [x] Dashboard rows + panels added - [x] Quiescer middleware wired into alerts - [x] Tests and load bench results attached - [x] Rollout plan documented in PR body Related work: ENG-4721 (telemetry cardinality), PM-198 (product request: quieter alerts).
Evan Brooks (2026-03-01): Can we make the quiescer window tenant-configurable via feature flag? Also please ensure metrics expose the raw suppressed events count.
Author reply (2026-03-01): Added a per-tenant config with feature-flag gating and exposed quiescer_suppressed_count.
Lina Chen (2026-03-01): Snapshot retrieval latency needs a hard SLA; consider async prefetch for UI flows.
Author reply (2026-03-01): Added p50/p95 latency metrics and a prefetch hook in the UI integration; documented fallbacks if prefetch fails.
Marco Silva (2026-03-02): Load bench looks promising; include memory profiling for snapshot store under churn.
Author reply (2026-03-02): Added memory profiles and GC tuning notes to infra manifest comments.
Adds compact event snapshot indexing to reduce telemetry cardinality for repeated token-phase sequences, a per-invocation compact_snapshot_ref attribute, and an alert quiescer to suppress short noisy token bursts. Dashboards updated with Token Phase Sparklines. Opt-in rollout and tenant configuration provided.
If rollout causes missing context in traces, disable compact snapshots via the observability feature flag for the tenant and query snapshot-store directly to retrieve snapshot by ref. Monitor compact_index_hit_rate and quiescer_suppressed_count for unexpected drops or spikes.

payload.body:
Adds retention policy change history and a customer-admin export endpoint used by the Compliance Reporting Pack generator (MVP). Export includes effective policy + defaults + change log summary and is scoped/authorized for enterprise evidence workflows.
Context: The Compliance Reporting Pack MVP needs a deterministic, customer-ready artifact that captures (a) the tenant’s effective retention settings across supported data classes and (b) the auditability of retention changes over time. Today we can fetch the current policy, but we don’t retain a first-class change history nor provide a stable export payload suitable for report generation. This PR adds: (1) retention policy change history persisted in the control plane with immutability guarantees, and (2) a new export endpoint that produces a versioned export (JSON) used by the report pack generator and audit-log-exporter attachment bundling. Scope: control plane only; does not change TTL enforcement in data plane stores. What’s included: 1) Change history: new table retention_policy_change_events with append-only rows capturing actor, source, diff summary, previous_policy_hash, new_policy_hash, request_id, and effective_at. History is written on every successful policy create/update/patch as part of the same transaction as the policy write. Includes backfill for existing tenants: we create a single seed event “imported_current_state” with actor=system and previous hash=null. 2) Export endpoint: GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention/export?format=json&include=history_summary&window_days=90. This returns the tenant’s effective retention config (post-validation, post-defaulting, post-tier constraints) plus an optional bounded history summary. The response is versioned via export_schema_version and is intended to be stable for external evidence packages (see ADR-018). 3) Authorization/RBAC: export requires role=SecurityAdmin or ComplianceAuditor (new permission RETENTION_EXPORT_READ). Endpoint is tenant-scoped; cross-tenant access is blocked at the router layer + DB query layer. All exports emit an audit log event retention.exported with tenant_id, actor_id, and export_schema_version (no policy contents logged). 4) Redaction: Export payload intentionally excludes free-form notes fields and internal-only evaluator debug fields. Actor email is replaced with actor_display_name + actor_type + actor_id. 5) Rate limiting + caching: export response supports If-None-Match via an ETag computed from (effective_policy_hash + latest_change_event_id + query params) to reduce repeated generation during report pack assembly. 6) Tests: unit tests for diff summarization and hash stability; integration tests for RBAC and ETag behavior; snapshot test for export v1.0 payload shape. API details: Response (format=json) includes: export_schema_version (e.g., "1.0"), generated_at, tenant_id, tier, region_scope, effective_policy (data_class -> ttl_days, purge_semantics, legal_hold_supported flag), defaults_applied (per class), constraints (min/max per tier), and history_summary (bounded list with event_id, occurred_at, actor_type, action, affected_classes, previous_hash, new_hash). Example snippet: { "export_schema_version": "1.0", "generated_at": "2025-02-14T19:22:10Z", "tenant_id": "tnt_1g8...", "tier": "Dedicated", "effective_policy": { "audit_logs": { "ttl_days": 365, "purge_semantics": "hard_delete" }, "request_response_logs": { "ttl_days": 30, "purge_semantics": "hard_delete" } }, "history_summary": [ { "event_id": 4812, "occurred_at": "2025-02-14T18:01:00Z", "actor_type": "user", "action": "update", "affected_classes": "audit_logs", "previous_hash": "rp_7f9...", "new_hash": "rp_8a1..." } ] } Notes/decisions: - We store both a normalized policy hash and a small diff summary (affected data classes + ttl deltas) so audits can see what changed without reconstructing the full prior policy from logs. - History_summary is bounded to prevent accidental large exports; default window_days=90 with max=365. Full history export is intentionally deferred (non-goal) until we validate customer needs + storage costs. - This is designed to integrate with ENG-18441 (report generator) and audit-log-exporter PR-627 (attachment bundling). Rollout: Behind feature flag retention_exports_v1 for 1 week; enabled for internal tenants + 2 design partners; then GA. DB migration is safe and backward compatible. No changes to existing retention CRUD endpoints besides writing change events. Risks/mitigations: - PII leakage in change events: actor is stored as IDs; display name is resolved at export time via directory service, and can be disabled in Private deployments. - DB growth: events are small; we will apply a long TTL (7y) only for Dedicated/Private tenants by default, else 1y for Hosted (configurable later). - Consistency: policy write and change event write are in one transaction; export reads at REPEATABLE READ to avoid mismatched policy/hash. Screenshots: none (API-only).
Marcus Lin (Security): Please confirm export payload doesn’t include prompt/completion contents or request bodies. Also, ensure audit event doesn’t log the export body.
Kevin Osei (author): Confirmed. Export only includes retention config + bounded history summary; no request bodies. Audit event is metadata-only (tenant_id, actor_id, schema version, request_id). Added a test asserting audit payload keys.
Olga Petrov (GRC): Can we make the schema version explicit and stable for customer evidence, and include a generated_at timestamp + window_days used? This will help with audit trails.

Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally hit transient utilization spikes that deterministic headroom policies either over-provision for or react to too late. This PR introduces a Quantile Headroom Orchestrator (QHO) that maintains headroom budgets using tail-aware quantiles derived from short and medium windows, and a Spillover Smoothing Adapter that gracefully redirects excess load to compatible fallback capacity tiers with controlled ramping. The change aims to reduce wasted reserved capacity while keeping throughput guarantees during short, heavy tails. Scope: - New controller implementing dual-window quantile estimation and safe headroom allocations. - Smoothing adapter that exposes a BufferAllowance signal to the scheduler and a SpilloverRamp policy to the fleet router. - Lightweight telemetry hooks, histograms and HDR sketches for per-pool quantile reporting. - API additions: small protobuf update to autoscaler.proto to surface QuantilePolicy and BufferAllowance. - New unit and e2e tests including synthetic spike scenarios and rollback safety checks. Checklist: - [x] Design doc + simulation results attached (linear ENG-3421) - [x] Unit tests for quantile estimator and allocator - [x] E2E spike test in perf-canary harness - [x] Telemetry dashboards (draft) - [x] Backward-compatible protobuf evolution Notes: This PR is intended to be non-breaking for existing resource configs; the default autoscaler policy remains unchanged unless QuantilePolicy is enabled on a pool. See linked Linear tickets for tuning knobs and simulation traces: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3421/quantile-headroom-orchestrator and relatedSUP ticket SUP-9123 for customer incident context.
Marco Li: Can you explain why we need dual windows vs exponential decay? The simulator shows better tail sensitivity but we need explanation in comments.
Asha Patel: Dual windows separate short spikes from sustained drift. Short window picks up microbursts; medium window prevents thrashing when traffic trends. Added inline comment and updated design doc.
Sofia Nguyen: Telemetry looks good; please add the per-pool 99.9th quantile to the allocation UI so SREs can observe headroom pressure.
Asha Patel: Added hdr sketch exporter and a dashboard JSON draft under docs/; left follow-up (ENG-3478) to iterate on UI surface.
Ethan Brooks: Integration tests flaky on arm64 CI (timing-sensitive). Suggest using deterministic clocks or increased tolerances in e2e.
Asha Patel: Replaced a time.Sleep with a controlled clock in tests and increased tolerances where simulation variance was expected.
Marco Li: Approved after small nits fixed (comments and a logging level adjustment).
- Introduce Quantile Headroom Orchestrator: tail-aware headroom allocations to reduce over-reservation and improve responsiveness to microbursts.
- Add Spillover Smoothing Adapter: controlled redirection to fallback capacity with ramp policies to preserve throughput guarantees.
- New telemetry: per-pool HDR sketches and quantile exports for monitoring headroom pressure.

Problem: our current presubmit runner is a monolithic bash/python combo that schedules lint and test jobs by coarse repo paths. This causes redundant work (same linters run across many subpackages), long feedback loops for language-specific changes, and brittle ad-hoc dependency bootstrapping.

Goal: introduce a language-aware CI orchestrator (Go) that: (1) inspects changed files and constructs a minimal presubmit plan per-language, (2) delegates to existing language runner plugins (py, ts, go, docker), (3) integrates the dependency-minimizer (dep-minimizer) to skip unnecessary package installs, and (4) exposes a dry-run preflight mode for release automation. The change should reduce CI runtime for common PRs and make presubmit behavior predictable.

What this PR does (summary):
- Add a go-based orchestrator cmd/ci/orchestrator that computes a language-aware presubmit graph and emits a compact job manifest.
- Replace the single presubmit.sh entrypoint with orchestrator invocations in .github/workflows/presubmit.yml while keeping backwards compatibility flags for local dev.
- Add dep-minimizer integration: the orchestrator asks dep-minimizer for a minimal dependency snapshot per job (uses existing lockfiles; no new lockfile format).
- Introduce a --dry-run=preflight mode used by release automation to validate staged releases without full artifact builds.
- Add lightweight telemetry events (ci.plan_size, ci.job_estimate_ms) and coarse retry/backoff knobs for flaky integration shards.
- Update docs: docs/dev/ci-orchestrator.md and quickstart snippets in devcontainers.

Checklist:
- [x] Architect review and design doc (Linear ENG-2534 attached in description)
- [x] Implement orchestrator + plugins with unit tests
- [x] Migrate presubmit workflow; keep feature flag for 2 weeks rollout
- [x] Add release preflight dry-run hook and document usage
- [x] Monitor CI impact via one-week canary

Commits (high-level):
- 7efb1ac add go orchestrator scaffolding and basic language detector
- a1d4c2b implement dep-minimizer client + caching layer for job snapshots
- 34b7e9a refactor: replace presubmit.sh with orchestrator invocation in workflow
- d2c9efa tests: add unit tests for plan generator and plugin interface
- b5f8d22 docs: add dev guide and dry-run examples

Files changed (high-level):
- cmd/ci/orchestrator/main.go (new)
- internal/ci/plan.go (new)
- tools/dep-minimizer/client.go (new)
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yml (modified)
- scripts/presubmit.sh (deprecated - wrapper kept for local)
- docs/dev/ci-orchestrator.md (new)
- go.mod / go.sum (adds new deps: cobra, semver, prometheus-client)

Why this is safe to roll out incrementally:
- The workflow change is gated by a repository-level feature flag CI_ORCHESTRATOR_ENABLED. The default remains off for two weeks while the canary team (engineers listed below) validates results. The old presubmit wrapper remains and can be re-enabled by unsetting the flag.

Metrics we will track (post-merge):
- median presubmit latency by change size (goal: -25% for small changes)
- CI compute minutes used per PR (goal: -20% for typical docs/TS changes)
- false-negative presubmit failures vs. monolith baseline (goal: <= 1%)

Related Linear tickets: ENG-2534, ENG-2598, PM-388

Notes on compatibility and tradeoffs:
- The orchestrator relies on existing language runner plugins rather than reimplementing linters/test harnesses; this keeps behavior stable.
- Dep-minimizer is conservative by default; it will only trim installs when lockfiles are unchanged. We added a cache to avoid repeated resolution overhead.
- The Go orchestrator adds a small binary to CI images; image size increased ~4MB. We measured no measurable cold-start impact on ephemeral runners.

Testing and CI: unit tests run locally via go test and we have an integration workflow presubmit-canary that exercises the orchestrator with a sampled subset of PRs. During the first run one flaky integration shard failed (npm-install on windows-late) and was retriggered; see review thread.
Alex Garcia: Nice separation — can we make the plugin interface smaller? Suggest reduce Plugin.Run args to ctx+job to simplify mocking.
Priya Menon: I trimmed the interface and added a PluginTest harness; updated tests in d2c9efa.
Maya Chen: CI telemetry looks good. One request: expose an env var to disable dep-minimizer for debugging.
Priya Menon: Added MINIMIZER_DISABLED env var and documented in docs/dev/ci-orchestrator.md
Jonah Rivera: observed flaky npm-install on windows-late during canary; reran the job and it passed. Leaving approval pending until canary completes.

Introduce the "FlashWeave" attention path: a compact FlashAttention-inspired microkernel that fuses rotary/rope rematerialization with a windowed KV prefetch strategy and scheduler hints for continuous batching. Motivation: reduce hot-path allocations and KV cache pressure for long-context streaming workloads while preserving low tail latency for short requests. This PR contains kernel, scheduler, and runtime fallbacks needed to safely deploy the path behind ops flags and model annotations. Key changes are summarized below and in the commit log. Benchmarks and compatibility notes, as well as rollout steps, are included.
c1a4f2d: add flashweave microkernel and operator abstraction
d3b9e71: implement windowed-KV prefetcher and eviction hinting
f7e2b6a: fuse rope/rotary rematerialization into attention compute path
2ab9c4e: scheduler hooks for continuous batching and priority lanes
9f0d5e7: add feature flag, config schema, and runtime fallbacks
b6c8a12: unit tests for remat correctness and KV window boundaries
e0f3b19: perf tests and microbenchmark harness integration
Diego Alvarez: Please add a short note in the scheduler doc about how priority lanes interact with reserved capacity to avoid double-counting latency budgets.
Maya Chen: Added section and clarified the runtime heuristic for lane promotion (see docs/ops/rollout-playbook.md).
Priya Nair: Can we add a regression test that simulates intermittent long-context streaming to validate KV window boundaries?
Maya Chen: Added tests/perf/flashweave_microbench.py and a unit test that covers a 64k token rolling window; CI perf runs included.
Evan Park: I see fallback paths for when the kernel cannot compile on older drivers. Confirmed with docker image matrix and added a CI job to avoid silent degradation.
SecurityBot: Flagged use of new shared memory allocation; author responded with rationale and added bounds checks and OOM-safe fallbacks.
Microbench (A100, fp16, sequence=1k): throughput +12% vs baseline flashbridge (continuous batching enabled).
End-to-end p95 latency (streaming, mixed payload, 40 concurrent): -8% tail latency vs baseline path (median improvement ~5%).
KV memory pressure (64k rolling window): -22% resident set size due to windowed prefetch and early eviction hints.
Quality: numerically identical outputs within floating error for standard rotary-enabled models; unit remat tests validate token-level equivalence for 99.99% of cases.
Default is opt-in via feature flag 'flashweave_enabled' and model annotation 'attn.path=flashweave'.
Fallback to existing flashbridge path when kernel JIT fails, driver older than CUDA 11.8, or when quantized kernels are selected.
Config knobs expose KV window size, prefetch lookahead, and eviction aggression for per-model tuning.
No changes to REST API surface. Changes are runtime-only and covered by rollout playbook.
1) Enable feature flag in staging for a single canary tenant with low RPS.
2) Monitor token-level latency, KV hit rate, and memory RSS for 24h.
3) Gradually expand to production canaries using priority lanes, watch autoscaler behavior.
4) If p95 regresses >10% for a tenant, flip runtime annotation to fallback and collect traces for investigation.
5) Promote to GA when 72h of stable metrics observed across three regions.
Introduce FlashWeave attention path: fused rotary rematerialization and windowed KV prefetcher for improved throughput and reduced KV memory usage. Opt-in behind feature flag and model annotation. See docs/ops/rollout-playbook.md for safe rollout steps.

Summary: This PR extends the route configuration schema to include an optional quantization_profile_ref field. When the field is unset (or explicitly set to "default"), behavior is unchanged and the serving stack will continue to use the baseline (non-profile) execution path. Motivation: The Quantization Profile Library workstream needs a control-plane surface area to opt in per route (and later by region/tier) without changing tenant defaults. This PR is intentionally limited to route config wiring + compatibility-safe defaults; policy evaluation and runtime application are handled in follow-up PRs. Design notes: - New field: quantization_profile_ref (string). Allowed values in this PR are: unset/null, "default", or a concrete profile ref string (format validation in control plane comes later). - Default behavior: treat unset and "default" identically; downstream resolution returns "disabled" state for profile application. - Backwards compatibility: Existing routes deserialize cleanly; API responses omit the field unless explicitly set (to avoid unexpected diffs for customers mirroring config). - Serialization: Both REST JSON and internal protobuf/struct tags updated. - Audit/change tracking: This PR adds explicit diff output for the new field in route config change logs, but does not introduce new audit event types yet. Migration: Adds a schema migration to persist the new field in route_config storage with a NULL default. Includes a safe backfill job that is a no-op (leaves NULL) and can be rolled forward/back without rewriting large tables. API docs: Added inline docs in the route config API structs (Go) describing semantics, default handling, and examples. Testing: - Unit tests for (1) decode/encode stability, (2) patch semantics (field clearing vs unset), and (3) default equivalence between unset and "default". - Golden tests updated for route config snapshots. Rollout plan: Ship behind existing server-side feature gate (RouteConfigQuantizationRefWrite) for write paths only; read paths are safe because the field is optional and omitted by default. Once policy engine guardrails are merged, we can enable writes for internal accounts + design partners.
Ethan Park (review): The default/omission behavior is key. Can we make sure responses omit quantization_profile_ref unless the user set it? This avoids noisy diffs for customers who sync config via IaC.
Benji Okafor (author): Yep. Updated serializer: when field is nil or "default" we omit in JSON responses. Added a golden test covering omission for both cases.
Mina Haddad (review): Patch semantics: how do we distinguish clearing the field vs leaving it unchanged? If a user sends an empty string, do we treat it as clear or invalid?
Benji Okafor (author): Treat empty string as invalid. Clearing is done via explicit patch op "clear" or setting value to "default". I added a test that empty string returns 400 with a message pointing to allowed values.
Jordan Lee (review): Re: determinism, I know compatibility checks are later, but we should avoid accepting arbitrary refs that could create hidden behavior changes once runtime support lands. Can we at least validate format (e.g., max len + allowed chars) now?
Benji Okafor (author): Added basic format validation (len <= 128, [A-Za-z0-9._:/-]). No allowlist yet; that comes with policy engine checks (ENG-5815).
Michael Nguyen (review): Migration looks fine. Please make sure the down migration is safe and doesn’t drop data unexpectedly if we roll back the app after some writes.
Benji Okafor (author): Good call. Updated down migration to keep column but ignore reads (documented) since dropping could lose data. Also gated writes behind RouteConfigQuantizationRefWrite flag so prod won’t write until we’re ready.
Naomi Feldman (review): RBAC/audit: Even if you’re not adding new event types, we need confidence that diffs are visible for change reviews. Can you include the new field in the route diff output?
Benji Okafor (author): Added to route_diff.go output and updated tests. This should show up in existing audit/change-history pipeline once the event emitter includes diffs (already does for route updates).
Ethan Park (approve): Approving with the omission behavior + patch semantics change. Please coordinate with policy engine PR so writes don’t get enabled prematurely.
Mina Haddad (approve): LGTM. Thanks for clarifying empty string behavior.
Jordan Lee (approve): LGTM. Format validation is enough for this layer.
Michael Nguyen (approve): Approved after migration tweak.
Naomi Feldman (approve): Approved.

Context: Customers and internal SRE runs showed recurring tenant cost regressions due to inconsistent batch and cache defaults + risky quantization rollouts. This PR introduces 'Autocraft Econ Prescriptor' — a service and CLI that auto-generates tenant-scoped default profiles for batching, KV/prefix cache, and quantization candidate tiers by analyzing sample traffic traces and tenant unit-economic constraints.
Motivation: reduce manual playbook work, prevent regressions during model/quant rollouts, and give platform engineers a safe dry-run path before applying defaults.
Scope:
- New standalone service (services/econ-prescriptor) exposing a primary /v1/prescribe endpoint and a dry-run mode; accepts sampled profile and tenant budget targets and returns candidate defaults.
- CLI integration (cli/autocraft) to run against local or remote prescriptor with CSV/JSON export.
- Migration helper script to export/import tenant defaults to the centralized defaults store (no automatic writes in this PR).
- Telemetry and gating: prescriptor emits selection_reason metrics and a safety_score; decisions require passing a minimal safety_score and an opt-in flag for automated apply.
Design notes:
- Prescriptor uses a two-stage pipeline: workload summarizer (sampled sequence length distributions, concurrency histogram, prefix-hit rates) then rule synthesizer (heuristics + unit-econ evaluator). The synthesizer prefers conservative presets for cold/warm traffic and proposes quant candidates annotated with expected latency delta and cost delta.
- Safety model: each candidate is scored against latency SLO impact (simulated using cached microbenchmarks) and unit cost delta; candidates below configured safety thresholds are flagged for manual review.
- Dry-run mode: CLI can run with --dry-run which returns the candidate set and a risk report but does not apply anything.
- Backward compatibility: the defaults store format was extended with a new optional "source" and "safety_score" fields; reads remain compatible.
Checklist:
- [x] Prototype heuristics and unit-econ library
- [x] Service + API + CLI dry-run
- [x] Integration tests for cold/warm traces
- [x] Telemetry metrics and dashboard skeleton
- [x] Docs and rollout guide
- [x] Migration script (manual apply only)
Security & compliance: service runs with tenant-scoped RBAC; migration script requires a service-account with defaults-write permission.
Tests & CI: Initial CI failed due to flaky prescriptor integration test (timing around microbenchmark mock). Fixed by adding deterministic mock responses and tighter assertions. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, lint, integration).
Review conversation summary:
- Marco Liu requested clearer telemetry labels and a compact metric for "prescriptor_decisions_total"; addressed in commit 3.
- Priya Desai asked to add one more e2e case simulating a heavy cold-start tenant; addressed by adding tests/e2e/prescriptor_integration.test.ts.
- Ethan Park asked to gate any automatic apply behavior behind a feature flag (SRE/ops opt-in); added config PRESCRIPTOR_AUTO_APPLY=false by default and documented rollout steps.
- Discussion about on-prem installer: added a note in docs/operations/prescriptor.md about packaging the prescriptor in the Private Installer.
Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature flag (PRESCRIPTOR_ENABLED=false).
2) Deploy to staging and exercise CLI dry-run on sampled tenants.
3) Open a small pilot with two internal tenants using manual apply.
4) After 2 weeks of stable telemetry and no negative-regressions, consider enabling automated-apply opt-in for a limited tenant cohort.
Migration notes: the migrate-defaults script generates a CSV of candidate defaults and a JSON risk-report; manual review required. No destructive migration performed in this PR.
Related items: ENG-5781 (unit-econ evaluator), ENG-5790 (prescriptor telemetry), SUP-1123 (customer report referencing noisy quant rollouts).
Merge outcome: squash-merged into main on 2026-02-15.
Follow-ups (tracked in Linear):
- Add model-driven quant simulation harness (ENG-5840)
- Add user-facing Console control to preview prescriptor recommendations (DES-901)
Marco Liu: please add a metric that counts decisions and tags by reason (latency|cost|conservative). I added a TODO; updated in commit 3.
Priya Desai: can we add an e2e trace for a cold-start heavy tenant? Added test and fixed flake.
Ethan Park: block any automatic apply behind a clear feature flag and RBAC. Implemented PRESCRIPTOR_AUTO_APPLY=false and documented in rollout guide.

Context: Dedicated fleet tail latency and cost efficiency are sensitive to coarse-grained autoscaling signals and centralized decision bottlenecks. Motivation: introduce a decentralized slab-based autoscaler that reconciles tenant commitments with local pod-level signals to reduce orchestration churn while preserving throughput guarantees. Summary: this PR implements a decentralized slab autoscaling algorithm and a lightweight commitment reconciliation layer. Key ideas: 1) Slabs: time-bounded capacity slabs (e.g., 30s windows) are advertised cluster-wide with soft guarantees; nodes independently accept slab allocations based on local occupancy and heuristic headroom; 2) Commitment reconciliation: a background reconciler streams commitment deltas (commit, revoke) from the control plane and uses an idempotent, monotonic ledger to converge state without centralized locks; 3) Safety fences: local conservative allocator prevents oversubscription by reserving a minimal safety margin, with a burst-fallback path that uses short-lived soft credits; 4) Telemetry and observability: per-slab util histograms, convergence lag gauges, and commit delta counters are emitted; 5) Rollout plan: feature gated by runtime flag slab_autoscaler_v1, canary to 5% of clusters, experiments to compare per-tenant tail latency. Design notes: the reconciler uses vector-timestamped deltas and tombstones to achieve eventual consistency; node-level allocation prefers minimizing slab fragmentation to improve batching efficiency; slabs expire with lease-driven TTL and are auto-refreshed by nodes that serve as slab-anchors. Backwards compatibility: legacy reservation endpoints remain supported; the reconciler will only activate when the feature flag is set. Tests and results: unit tests for ledger convergence, integration tests with simulated 10k-tenant workloads, and a perf bench showing a 7.8% reduction in mean cost-per-token under bursty traffic and a 12% reduction in tail-latency violations in the canary run. Migration: a migration job converts legacy reservations to slab commitments in-place under the control plane; a fallback toggle allows rolling back instantly. This description includes implementation rationale, configuration knobs (slab_window_sec, safety_margin_pct, anchor_selector), testing summary, and rollout strategy.
Luca Moretti: High-level: this looks promising but the reconciler complexity worries me for edge cases during network partitions. Can you expand on tombstone semantics and monotonicity guarantees?
Priya Desai: Reply: added detailed comments in monotonic_ledger.go and implemented tombstone vector timestamps to ensure idempotency. The reconciler tolerates transient partitions; leases and TTLs bound misallocation windows.
Anika Rao: Please add more unit tests for a double-apply scenario where deltas arrive out of order. Also add an e2e canary check for slab expiry behavior.
Priya Desai: Added tests (slab_simulator_test.go) and an e2e check in the canary harness. Fixed an ordering bug which caused a 10% over-reservation in a synthetic partition test.
Marcus Chen: LGTm pending CI. Recommend limiting default slab_window_sec to 30s for GA and documenting cost/latency tradeoffs in the runbook.
QA: Found minor race in tombstone cleanup path under heavy reconciler restarts; confirmed fix in commit f6a7b8c.

Motivation: production Dedicated pools experience short-lived microbursts that exhaust ephemeral burst credits and cause downstream latency spikes and fairness regressions. This PR adds a consumption-window based allocator plus a lightweight burst sanity guard to make per-tenant burst admission both time-aware and safety‑constrained. High level: (1) consumption-window allocator calculates per-tenant consumption over a configurable sliding window (default 60s) using an efficient EWMA sketch to avoid storing per-request history. This lets the autoscaler and admission layers reason about short-term sustained load rather than instantaneous spikes. (2) burst sanity guard enforces a soft gate that denies or delays ephemeral burst consumption when doing so would violate longer-term throughput guarantees; it prefers deferred warmup/batching instead of hard evictions. Implementation details: added pkg/autoscaler/consumption_window.go implementing the sliding-window EWMA and budget decayer; controllers/warmup_scheduler.go implements deferred warmup heuristics and a probabilistic prefill when utilization is predicted to trend up; internal/telemetry/metrics_exporter.go emits consumption_window_utilization, burst_guard_denials, warmup_prefill_attempts and burst_credit_reclaim_count. The allocator is plumbed into the admission path via controllers/admission_middleware.go and is compatible with the existing reservation ledger and burst-bank layers. Testing: unit tests for EWMA edge cases and budget roll-off (tests/autoscaler/consumption_window_test.go), integration test that simulates microburst patterns vs. sustained load (integration/dedicated/consumption_window_integration_test.go). Rollout: behind feature flag dedicated.consumption_window.enabled=false by default; staged canary to 10% of infra pools, with a 24h telemetry window and an automated rollback if burst_guard_denials > 1% and tail latency regressions exceed 5th percentile threshold. Backwards compatibility: does not change storage layout; configuration defaults preserve prior behavior. Checklist: [x] design doc linked; [x] unit + integration tests; [x] metrics and dashboards added; [x] feature flagged rollout plan included. Related: complements ENG-2201 (reservoirized warm pool tuning) and addresses SUP-1456 customer incident where transient microbursts degraded throughput guarantees.
Luca Romero: Can we lower the default window to 30s? 60s felt slow in local sims. Also please ensure the EWMA alpha is configurable.
Priya Desai: Reply: I ran sims with both 30s and 60s; 60s reduced oscillation in multi-tenant bursts. Made window configurable and exposed alpha via config with a sane default.
Ethan Park: Nit: add a short note in the admission path comment explaining why we prefer delaying vs denying in some cases.
Priya Desai: Reply: added comment and extended unit tests to cover delay path.
Introduce consumption-window allocator and burst sanity guard behind a feature flag. Adds new telemetry metrics (consumption_window_utilization, burst_guard_denials, warmup_prefill_attempts). Default behavior unchanged until feature is enabled. Recommended canary rollout and dashboards updated.
Operators: enable feature via dedicated.consumption_window.enabled=true and tune dedicated.consumption_window.window_seconds (default 60) and dedicated.consumption_window.alpha. Watch metrics: consumption_window_utilization and burst_guard_denials. If warmup_prefill_attempts spike without corresponding utilization, revert flag for diagnostic investigation.
Added Grafana panel 'Ded: Consumption Window Utilization' and alert 'Ded: Burst Guard Denials > 0.5%'
Unit tests exercise EWMA decay and budget refill; integration test runs synthetic microburst/sustained scenarios and validates that steady-state throughput meets pre-change baselines while reducing evictions during bursts.

Motivation: Dedicated fleets were experiencing repeated short congestion spikes during cold starts and burst handoffs which caused transient 95th latency regressions. This PR adds a congestion-aware warmup prober together with a soft-shedder policy that temporarily reduces admission for non-critical low-priority tenants while the fleet warms. Design summary: introduce a lightweight probe that samples tail latency and queue depth during warmup windows, compute a congestion score (0-100) with exponential smoothing, and expose signals to the autoscaler and admission controller. When score > threshold the soft-shedder applies a probabilistic reject/backoff on best-effort classes and reduces allowed concurrency for speculative tenants. Configuration: new runtime config under /pkg/autoscaler/config that supports window_ms, smoothing_alpha, congestion_threshold, shed_probability_curve and critical_classes. Telemetry: new metrics redwood_fleet_congestion_score, redwood_warmup_probe_latency_p50/p95, and redwood_soft_shed_rate_by_tier; all exported to Datadog and Prometheus exporters. Rollout: staged rollout with canary pool, default disabled for existing customers; opt-in via dedicated config or Redwood Console toggle. Tests: unit tests for score calculation and shedder logic, integration test that verifies admission behavior against synthetic spike generator, and a small e2e on perf-canary harness. Backwards compatibility: non-breaking by default; configuration flags keep previous behavior unless enabled. Related work: builds on ENG-2134 (warmup telemetry refactor) and ENG-2199 (admission controller refactor).

Add a congestion-aware warmup probe and soft-shedder policy for Dedicated fleets. Context: customer integrations and internal examples exposed small mismatches between SDK credential cache TTLs and streaming consumer ergonomics (Python async iterators, TS async generators, Go pull/push stream helpers). Those mismatches caused edge-case double-refreshes under bursty traffic and made cross-language examples diverge. This PR synchronizes the credential TTL/resync heuristics, tightens default retry windows for auth failures, and polishes ergonomic surfaces for async iterables across the three SDKs. Motivation: reduce spurious token refreshes, avoid duplicate background refreshes when a consumer drains and reconnects, and provide idiomatic, consistent examples for docs and Quickstarts. Changes: 1) Introduce unified credential TTL configuration: default TTL window set to 55s of token lifetime for prefetch heuristics with a per-SDK override knob (env/config). 2) Align reauth backoff preset for transient 401/403 to a shared 'sdk-auth' retry bundle (5s, 15s, 45s) with jitter. 3) Python: add AsyncStream.peek() helper and explicit close semantics to avoid implicit refresh race on garbage collection; update session manager to coalesce concurrent refreshes. 4) TypeScript: expose generator.buffered() for line-buffered consumers and ensure reauth is idempotent across repeated pull calls; add small ergonomic rename for clarity (pull -> nextChunk kept as alias for backward compat). 5) Go: implement cred debounce layer in credcache.go to collapse rapid refresh requests and add lightweight ConnPool. 6) Tests: cross-lang e2e harness updated to simulate burst reconnects and assert single refresh per token window. 7) Docs/Examples: update three quickstarts to use new helpers and call out the config knobs. Compatibility notes: backward-compatible surface maintained; TS alias preserves old API names, Python changes are additive (peek/close) and do not remove existing methods, Go adds a new small package for pool management. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for token coalescing and retry backoff - [x] Integration e2e harness against local devserver simulating short-lived tokens - [x] Docs updated and example snippets tested - [x] Benchmarked under 10k req/s simulated bursts (no additional spurious refreshes observed) - [x] Security review for credential caching (no secrets persisted to disk) Testing instructions: run sdk-e2e/harness/run_local.sh then run three SDK clients in the harness directory; see README in e2e for assertions. Impact: reduces token refresh churn under bursty traffic and reduces 401 cascades during short token lifetimes. Related: ENG-3479 (streaming stability), ENG-3301 (auth backoff consistency).
Alex Rivera (reviewer): Nice consolidation. Question: why 55s for TTL window? Can we derive from token lifetime instead of hardcoding a number?
Priya Nair (author): We compute window as max(ceil(lifetime*0.1),55) for short-lived tokens; 55s was chosen from empirical tests with 60s lifetimes to avoid immediate refresh storms. Added comment in code and docs to explain formula.
Jinsoo Park (reviewer): In Go, ConnPool looks good but watch the mutex on borrow/return for hot paths. Could you add a microbenchmark?
Priya Nair (author): Added go microbench in conn/pool_bench_test.go and tuned the borrow path to use sync.Pool for light-weight cases; results appended in the PR CI artifact.
Maria Gomez (reviewer): TS rename 'pull -> nextChunk' concerns me for semver. Is aliasing sufficient to avoid breakage for frameworks?
Priya Nair (author): We keep pull as an exported alias to nextChunk and added deprecation comment with a one-minor bump note in changelog; tests cover both names.
CI Bot: e2e harness failed first run due to race in Python session coalescer under heavy concurrent refresh attempts; reworked lock-free path and retriggered; tests now pass.
Security Team: quick scan looks good, no secrets written to logs or disk; well documented TTL knobs.
SDKs: aligned credential prefetch TTL heuristics and added ergonomic async iterable helpers. Python: AsyncStream.peek and explicit close to avoid refresh races. TypeScript: buffered() helper and nextChunk alias; auth retry presets unified. Go: credential debounce and ConnPool added. No breaking changes; minor API aliasing note for TS.
Unit+integration+bench: unit coverage increased for auth modules, e2e burst tests confirm single refresh per token window in >95% of runs, minor flakiness fixed and re-run.

Summary: This PR aligns credential payload shapes and streaming call signatures in the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs to reduce cross-language friction for customers and internal examples. Motivation: multiple docs and examples were diverging (camelCase vs snake_case credential fields; different async/iterator ergonomics for streaming). The change set standardizes on a compact, explicit credential shape and adds lightweight compatibility shims so existing call sites continue to work.

Goals:
- Standardize on a superset credential object with stable aliases (clientId, client_id, token, api_key)
- Provide identical streaming entrypoints: pull_stream / pullStream / StreamPull with consistent semantics across SDKs
- Keep runtime behavior backward-compatible; emit deprecation warnings rather than hard errors
- Keep changes small in surface area; prefer shims and adapters over mass API renames

What changed (high level):
- Python: redwood-sdk-python/src/redwood/credentials.py: introduce CredentialSpec class, add from_mapping helper, add deprecated alias properties for camelCase fields. Update streaming client in streaming.py to accept both generator/callable and async iterator payloads; add pull_stream alias.
- TypeScript: packages/redwood-sdk-typescript/src/credentials.ts: export CredentialLike type, create normalizeCredential() helper. streaming.ts: expose pullStream function and async iterator compatibility layer; update JSDoc to show normalized examples.
- Go: sdk/go/credentials/cred.go: introduce Credential struct with json tags for both camelCase and snake_case; normalize in NewCredentialFromMap. stream/client.go: add StreamPull convenience wrapper that returns a channel-based consumer and implements io.Closer for ergonomic shutdown.
- Tests: unit tests added for normalization, streaming adapters, and cross-language example snippets ported to each SDK's test suite.
- Docs: update quickstart snippets in redwood-examples/docs/ to use normalized credential fields and demonstrate both alias forms.

Commit summary:
- feat(cred): add CredentialSpec and normalization helpers in py/ts/go
- feat(stream): add pull_stream/pullStream/StreamPull ergonomic wrappers
- test: add unit tests for credential aliases and streaming adapters
- docs: update quickstarts and examples
- ci: fix go vet and regenerate lockfile for ts SDK

Changed files (representative):
- redwood-sdk-python/src/redwood/credentials.py
- redwood-sdk-python/src/redwood/streaming.py
- redwood-sdk-python/tests/test_credentials_normalize.py

# cred.client_id and cred.clientId both available (clientId is deprecated alias)

TypeScript example:
const cred = normalizeCredential({ client_id: 'abc', api_key: 'xyz' });
for await (const chunk of pullStream(model, request, cred)) { console.log(chunk); }

Review conversation (highlights):
- Arjun Patel (reviewer): "Please ensure the deprecation warnings are rate-limited and not noisy in high-throughput services. Also add a clear migration note for customers using direct dict-style creds in python."
  - Maya Chen (author): "Agreed — added a DeprecationLogger singleton that emits one warning per process per deprecated field; updated py docs with migration section."

- Sonia Lopez (reviewer): "Go wrapper looks good but go vet complained about unused imports in client.go on the first CI run. Also request explicit Close() guidance in docs to avoid goroutine leaks."
  - Maya Chen: "Addressed: removed unused imports, added Close() example in go/README.md, and added a test that verifies no goroutines leak on stream Close()."

- Ethan Brooks (reviewer): "TypeScript: please ensure types keep backward compatibility — adding a CredentialLike union is better than replacing the type entirely."
  - Maya Chen: "Done — CredentialLike union added and exported; existing code paths compile without changes."

CI runs: 
- Initial run: typescript lint + python unit tests passed; go build failed (unused import in client.go)
- Follow-up run: fixed imports, initial failing Go test added more strictness; adjusted test harness, all checks passed
- Final CI: all checks (lint/test/build) passed, coverage delta +0.2%

Compatibility notes and migration guidance: 
- Existing code using client_id or clientId will continue to work; the SDK will log a single deprecation warning per process for the deprecated key.
- Streaming: old streaming helpers still present but the preferred ergonomic interfaces are the new pull_stream / pullStream wrappers — they are thin adapters over existing code.
- Version bumps: this PR also includes coordinated version bumps for the three SDKs to make the release easier for downstream dependents.

Merge details: squashed and merged to main after reviewers approved; changelog entry added to releases/notes. Merged by Sonia Lopez on 2025-06-18 (merge method: squash).

Notes for release engineers: tag python v1.14.0, typescript v1.28.0, go v1.9.3. Coordinate minor advisory e-mail for customers who pinned older SDK versions and rely on raw dict credential shapes.

If follow-ups are needed I recommend:
- a small telemetry PR to capture how many customers still use deprecated fields (low-overhead sampling),
- a docs-only PR to add side-by-side examples for every major language, and
- consider a major deprecation policy doc to make eventual removal less surprising.
- Harmonized credential object fields across SDKs (client_id -> clientId alias added)
- Unified streaming call signatures and ergonomic aliases (pullStream / streamAsync)
- Minor version bumps: python v1.14.0, typescript v1.28.0, go v1.9.3

payload.body:
## Summary
This PR adds a consistent PR labeling taxonomy for Runtime LTS/backports/security fixes and wires the release notes generator to categorize changes based on those labels.

This is a prerequisite for:
- automated backport workflows (cherry-pick helper + bots)
- slower-change LTS release notes generation (curated summaries + stable categories)
- Support/CS visibility into whether a fix is expected to land in an LTS patch

## Motivation
We currently rely on free-form PR titles and ad-hoc labels ("bug", "perf", "security") to decide what gets cherry-picked and how it shows up in release notes. For LTS we need:
1) explicit intent (is this a backport candidate?)
2) explicit approval (is it cleared for LTS?)
3) a deterministic mapping into release note buckets
4) a lightweight schema that works across repos but is owned in the monorepo

## Label taxonomy (proposed)
### Backport/LTS flow labels
- `backport-candidate` — author signals the change may be eligible for backport (mainline PR)
- `lts-approved` — Runtime + Release Eng approved for backport to the active LTS line
- `lts-blocked` — requested for LTS but blocked pending risk/test/perf gates, or needs conflict resolution

### Security labels
- `security` — security-relevant fix (may or may not be customer-facing)
- `security-hotfix` — expedited process; use only when we are cutting an out-of-band patch (release manager adds)

### Release notes categorization labels (one required when `release-notes` is present)
- `release-notes:bugfix`
- `release-notes:performance`
- `release-notes:stability`
- `release-notes:security`
- `release-notes:build`
- `release-notes:docs`
- `release-notes:deprecation`

Notes:
- We intentionally separate "security" from the release note bucket; a security fix can land with `security` + `release-notes:security` (or omit release notes entirely if not customer-facing / embargoed).
- `lts-approved` is separate from `backport-candidate` to avoid auto-cherry-picking based solely on author intent.

## Tooling changes
- Updates the release notes generator label mapping to:
  - recognize the `release-notes:*` taxonomy
  - treat `security-hotfix` as a high-priority flag (but not required)
  - include an "LTS Backport" marker in the generated notes when the PR has `lts-approved`
- Adds a small validation step in CI for PRs labeled `release-notes` to ensure exactly one `release-notes:*` bucket is present (prevents "uncategorized" entries)

## Operational guidance
- For Runtime PRs that should appear in customer release notes, add:
  - `release-notes` + one `release-notes:*`
  - a 1–3 sentence human-written summary in the PR description under "Release notes blurb" (template added below)
- For fixes requested by Support to go into LTS, Support will reference the mainline PR and request `backport-candidate`; Runtime oncall/release manager will apply `lts-approved` after rubric review.

## Files changed (high level)
- `.github/labels.yml` — adds/normalizes labels with descriptions + colors
- `.github/pull_request_template.md` — adds "Release notes blurb" section and guidance
- `tools/release_notes/label_map.yaml` — new mapping for LTS + release note categories
- `tools/release_notes/generate.py` — uses `release-notes:*` buckets; includes LTS marker
- `tools/release_notes/validate_labels.py` — ensures category presence when `release-notes` is set
- `.github/workflows/pr-label-validation.yml` — runs validation script on labeled PRs

## Example
If a PR fixes a Sev1 crash and we want it in LTS:
- On mainline PR: `backport-candidate`, `release-notes`, `release-notes:stability`
- After review: add `lts-approved`
Generated notes will:
- include the change under "Stability"
- annotate that it is part of an LTS backport set

## Checklist
- [x] Labels defined in repo with descriptions and stable names
- [x] Release notes generator recognizes new labels
- [x] CI validation prevents missing/multiple categories
- [x] PR template updated
- [x] Documented intended use in label descriptions

## Rollout
Once merged, Release Eng will sync labels in GitHub (labels.yml is the source of truth). Existing PRs are unaffected unless labeled `release-notes` without a category.

Related:
- ENG-4823 (backport labels + automation)
- ENG-4826 (LTS release notes generator)
- SUP-18544 (request to backport KV cache crash fix into LTS)
Connor O'Brien (review): This is the right direction. Two asks: (1) please clarify that `lts-approved` is applied by release manager/runtime lead, not authors, (2) ensure generator behavior is deterministic when multiple release-notes labels are present (fail fast).
Devon Price (author): Updated label descriptions to specify ownership (release manager/runtime lead). Added validate_labels.py and workflow to fail if `release-notes` exists without exactly one `release-notes:*` label.
Dr. Aisha Rahman (review): Naming: I prefer we keep `security` and `security-hotfix` distinct, but make sure we don’t force `release-notes:security` for embargoed items. Add a note in README about allowed combinations.
Devon Price (author): Added guidance: security fixes may omit release notes label entirely for embargoed/internal-only changes; `security-hotfix` is an expedited-process marker.
Elliot Price (review): PR template section looks good. Minor: call it “Release notes blurb” and explicitly note it can be “N/A” for non-customer-facing changes.
Devon Price (author): Done. Template updated with “N/A” guidance and examples.
Samir Qureshi (review): Can we add `release-notes:performance` vs `release-notes:stability` separation? We’ll need this for LTS to differentiate perf regressions vs correctness.
Devon Price (author): Added both `release-notes:performance` and `release-notes:stability` buckets; generator updated to render those as separate headings.
Connor O'Brien (approval): Approved. This unblocks ENG-4823/4826. Please ping #eng-releases once merged so we can sync labels and update contributor guidance.
Elliot Price (approval): Approved.

Motivation: observed 95th/99th tail spikes during mixed interactive workloads when prefill stages completed early but decode stage was starved waiting on kernel availability or KV priming. This PR introduces a lightweight 'prefill heartbeat' to surface readiness and a lazy-decode graft that opportunistically attaches decode work to adjacent warm kernels, reducing handover stall windows. Summary of changes: 1) Prefill heartbeat: periodic, low-overhead readiness pings emitted from prefill workers to the scheduler to avoid hard barriers and enable soft-fence handovers; 2) Lazy-decode grafting: when a decode kernel becomes available within a heartbeat window, short decode slices from pending prefill sequences can be grafted into that kernel to avoid a full pipeline restart; 3) KV priming hints: prefill now emits sparse KV priming hints for head tokens which decoder kernels consume to reduce first-token decode latency; 4) Scheduling changes: replace strict stage barrier with 'soft fence' ordering and heartbeat-driven admission, including backpressure smoothing to prevent oscillation; 5) Kernels: minor kernel adapter that enables decode slices to accept partial KV contexts and continue seamlessly. Key benefits: reduces 95th latency by ~12% and 99th by ~8% on our interactive bench with mixed short/long sequences; reduces wasted kernel idle time by ~15%; small memory overhead for short-lived primed KV buckets. Checklist: [x] design doc linked [x] unit tests [x] perf harness run [x] telemetry added [x] no breaking API changes. Rollout plan: canary on Dedicated then staged rollout with metrics guardrails (tail-latency and kernel-utilization).
Introduces prefill heartbeat and lazy-decode grafting to reduce tail latency by improving stage handover and KV priming; no user-facing API changes; recommended rollout on Dedicated first.
Jun Park: Nice approach, I like the soft-fence idea, left a few nit comments around naming and a race in the scheduler admission path. Sofia Rivera: addressed namings and added atomic fence in second commit. Lena Hoff: Please add an explicit test for KV hint correctness across evictions. Sofia Rivera: added test_integrations that simulates eviction; results included in CI. Marcus Green: performance numbers look good, one question on memory overhead when many parallel sessions create priming hints. Sofia Rivera: priming hints are capped per-session and garbage collected after 2 heartbeats; added telemetry and a guard to avoid unbounded growth. Jun Park: LGTM after CI pass. Marcus Green: approved. Merge: squash and merge after CI green.
CI pipeline: unit tests passed (100/100), integration tests passed (12/12), lint ok, perf-bench initial run: flaky on 99th latency due to infra noise then rerun stabilized; final run shows 12% 95th reduction and 8% 99th reduction on canary nodes. All checks passed before merge.

Summary: Introduces a new command-line tool 'redwood cost-suggester' and a safe 'recommendation dry-run' flow for tenant cost optimization (batching/caching defaults, suggested quant profiles, and unit-econ impact estimates). Motivation: teams repeatedly ask for a low-friction way to get deterministic, tenant-scoped cost suggestions without applying changes. This PR delivers a preview-first UX, a small presets format, and instrumentation so product can measure suggestion uptake and accuracy.

What this PR does (single-string description): Adds CLI subcommands: 'redwood cost-suggester preview --tenant-id <id> [--simulate] [--output preview.yaml]' and 'redwood cost-suggester apply --tenant-id <id> --preset <name>' (apply gated behind feature flag). By default preview is a dry-run and emits telemetry event cost.suggester.recommendation.preview containing suggestion fingerprint and unit-econ delta. The CLI consults historical telemetry (sampled token/latency distributions) and runs an internal unit-econ estimator to produce ranked suggestions (batch size, prefix-cache hint, quant profile). Suggestions include a conservative safety score and a migration path.

Checklist: [x] CLI and library implementation; [x] unit tests for estimator and safety scoring; [x] integration test for dry-run end-to-end; [x] telemetry events + schema; [x] docs page and quickstart; [x] feature-flag gating and server-side opt-in settings.

Commits (high level): 1) init: add CLI scaffolding and command docs; 2) impl: unit-econ estimator and suggester core + presets parser; 3) telemetry: add preview event and schema; 4) tests: unit + integration dry-run; 5) docs: ops + examples; 6) fix: handle missing tenant history fallback.

Changed files (high level): cmd/cost-suggester/main.go (new CLI wiring), internal/econ/suggester.go (core algorithm), internal/econ/estimator_test.go (unit tests), pkg/telemetry/events.go (new event), deploy/presets/cost-presets-v1.yaml (new starter presets), docs/ops/cost-suggester.md (operator docs), tests/integration/cost_suggester_dryrun_test.go (integration), internal/config/flags.go (feature flag config). Small illustrative snippet (CLI help): "$ redwood cost-suggester preview --tenant-id t-12345 --output preview.yaml" -> generates a preview YAML with fields: suggested_batch, suggested_cache_policy, quant_profile, estimated_monthly_savings_usd, safety_score.

Implementation notes: - Estimator uses sampled per-tenant latency/token histograms (10% sample) and a small econometric model trained on synthetic microbenchmarks; defaults back to global profile if tenant history is sparse. - Suggestions are conservative by default (safety_score >= 0.6) and include a fallback route that keeps original model/route in place for canarying. - Telemetry is GDPR-friendly: previews emit only fingerprints/hashes for suggestions and aggregated numeric deltas; no raw prompts or user content. - Feature flag: redwood.cost.suggester.enable (default false for new clusters; enabled for pilot tenants).

Review conversation summary (single-string): Ethan: "Nice separation between CLI and estimator; please add more tests around sparse-tenant fallback and edge-case histograms." Marta: "Added sparse-tenant unit test and amended estimator to clamp quant suggestions when latency skew > 3x." Priya: "Telemetry schema LGTM, confirm events are sampled at 1% by default." Marta: "Yes, sampling handled by pkg/telemetry with config default 0.01; added note in docs." Jordan: "Docs need an example of reading preview.yaml and running a 'safe apply' CI job." Marta: "Added a short CI snippet in docs/ops/cost-suggester.md showing how to parse preview.yaml and call 'apply --confirm' from a gated pipeline." Final reviewers approved after fixes.

CI summary: CI pipeline initially failed on a flaky integration test 'TestDryrunConvergence' (timeout in CI env). Reproduced locally on slow runner, reduced test timeout and added deterministic seeding to the synthetic load generator; re-ran CI -> all checks passed (unit, integration, lint, build). Checks: build: pass; unit-tests: pass; integration-tests: pass (rerun); lint: pass; docs-linkcheck: pass.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main by Priya Nair on 2026-02-21. Follow-ups: ENG-2102 (UX: web-console preview panel), ENG-2115 (policy: auto-apply guardrails + rollout automation), ENG-2150 (pilot telemetry analysis to validate unit-econ estimator).

Operational impact: Low-risk. New presets YAML added to deploy/presets is optional; operators can opt-in tenants. The default behavior is preview-only, so no immediate changes to tenant serving behavior unless 'apply' is invoked.

Notes for release: Ship as part of 2026.02.3 minor release; include short blog post for pilot customers and run a targeted pilot with three tenants to validate estimator accuracy.
