Context: During the Quantization Profile Library beta, Applied ML flagged a statistically significant regression on the Redwood internal prompt set ("support_summaries_v2") when enabling profile `qp_int8_calib_v3` on model variant `x1` (model id `rw-lm/atlas-7b`, variant `x1`). This aligns with a design partner report of output drift after enablement (see SUP-27411). We performed an immediate operational rollback by disabling the profile at the affected route(s) and verified recovery, but we also need a hard guardrail to prevent re-enable while we recalibrate/re-evaluate.

Incident references: Slack #incidents thread 1741684000 (quality regression alert during beta) and #eng-ml thread 1740068833 (bench + regression notes). This PR implements a targeted hotfix in the control-plane/policy layer so the profile cannot be applied for `atlas-7b:x1` even if referenced in route config. Runtime remains unchanged; behavior is deterministic: resolution returns baseline precision with an explicit blocked reason.

What changed: (1) Add a known-bad block entry for `model_id=rw-lm/atlas-7b`, `variant=x1`, `quant_profile_id=qp_int8_calib_v3` in the quantization profile constraints/allowlist used by the policy engine. (2) Update compatibility evaluation to treat "blocked" as a distinct outcome from "incompatible" so we can alert/observe separately (metrics tag + audit trail). (3) Add an operator note in the returned compatibility error message surfaced to Console/API (human-readable remediation: "Profile blocked due to quality regression; use default precision or select qp_int8_calib_v2").

Why this approach: Route-level disable is necessary but not sufficient (humans/automation can re-enable). A global kill-switch is too blunt; this is a surgical block with clear observability. This follows the fallback standard: baseline precision is always the safe default.

Risk/rollout notes: This is intended for the release train `release/2025.03` and should be cherry-picked to main after merge. No schema changes. Default behavior unchanged for all other models/variants/profiles. Existing routes that reference `qp_int8_calib_v3` on `atlas-7b:x1` will deterministically fall back to baseline on next config cache refresh.

Rollback notes: If we need to revert this hotfix, revert commit `b3f7c4a` ("block qp_int8_calib_v3 for atlas-7b:x1") and redeploy control-plane. Operationally, the fastest mitigation remains (a) disable profile at route level, and (b) if multiple routes are impacted unexpectedly, use the global kill-switch (ENG-5819 runbook).

Testing: Added unit tests for policy resolution outcomes: applied vs fallback(incompatible) vs fallback(blocked). Verified Console error copy via API snapshot tests. Ran staging smoke: create route config referencing blocked profile -> resolved profile outcome is baseline, metrics emit `quant_profile_resolution=blocked`.

Checklist: [x] Linked incident/support context. [x] Added tests. [x] Release manager sign-off for release/2025.03. [x] Post-merge: notify #eng-ml and #eng-sre; update beta design partner comms (PM-643).

Commits: 1) policy: add known-bad profile blocklist and resolution outcome 2) api: improve compatibility response message for blocked profile 3) tests: coverage for blocked vs incompatible outcome 4) ops: add dashboard tag note + runbook snippet update.

Changed areas (high-level): control-plane policy engine (quant profile constraints), route resolution response shaping, metrics tags, unit tests.

Review conversation (highlights): Arjun requested we scope the block to (model_id, variant, profile_id, profile_version) to avoid future unintended blocks; updated to include explicit `profile_version=3` match. Selene asked for explicit mention of the eval signal that triggered the block and to keep messaging consistent with regression thresholds doc; added note and standardized remediation text. Mina requested we ensure routing doesn't loop on fallback; confirmed we return baseline directly and included regression test from pr-18531 coverage. Connor requested a release note and a clear cherry-pick instruction; added to description and release_notes.

CI: Initially failed on `policy-engine-tests` due to a missing fixture update; fixed in follow-up commit. Final checks: build (pass), unit (pass), integration (pass), lint (pass).

Merge: Squash merged into `release/2025.03` by Connor O'Brien on 2025-03-15.
Prevents enabling quantization profile qp_int8_calib_v3 on model variant x1 via route settings (compatibility guardrail).
Improves operator-facing log/event when a profile is blocked due to known regression (includes remediation text).
payload.title: Hotfix: disable INT8 profile on model variant x1 after quality regression

payload.body:
Motivation: Production workloads at Redwood show a bimodal sequence length distribution (many short streaming requests interleaved with occasional long completions). Existing kernels either favor short requests (low setup overhead) or long requests (amortized compute) but we observe increased tail latency and suboptimal KV cache pressure when both are colocated. This PR introduces a combined approach: 1) a fused QKV kernel that applies rotary/rope as a deferred step during the attention compute path (reducing redundant memory shuffles); 2) a 'hyperbatch' scheduler that continuously batches compatible requests but prioritizes low-latency streaming tails and defers rope rematerialization for batched long sequences; 3) priority-aware KV cache admission/eviction policies so short high-qps sessions retain hot prefixes.

What changed (high-level):
- New fused kernel: runtime/attn/fused_deferred_rope.cu and runtime/attn/fused_deferred_rope.h implement a CUDA kernel that fuses q/k/v transpose, qkv interleave, and rotary application into a single pass when the runtime flag enable_fused_deferred_rope=true. The kernel applies rope by streaming position indices in-band so we avoid a separate pre-transform buffer for rotary keys when sequence optics permit.
- Hyperbatch scheduler: runtime/scheduler/hyperbatch_scheduler.cpp adds continuous-batching logic that groups requests by model variant, dtype, and effective rope-offset compatibility. The scheduler maintains a fast-path for <64-token streaming requests with strict latency SLOs and a deferred path for long sequences where rope application is delayed until the kernel's final combine stage.
- KV cache priorities: runtime/kv/priority_cache.cc implements a scored admission policy (recency + request_priority tag) and a spill strategy that prefers evicting low-priority long-session shards before short-session prefixes.
- API/flags: runtime/config/flags.h and docs/ops/flags.md add enable_fused_deferred_rope & scheduler.hyperbatch.enable toggles. Feature is opt-in and off by default for safety.
- Metrics and tracing: observability/metrics/attn_metrics.cc adds attn.kernel.fused_deferred_rope.invocations and scheduler.hyperbatch.batch_size histogram. Added traces for 'deferred_rope' decision points to the RPC trace context.
- Tests and harness changes: perf/bench/hyperbatch_end2end.yaml and tests/attn/test_fused_deferred_rope.cpp with unit and integration tests validating numeric parity with current pipeline and coverage for rope edge-cases (odd/even rotary dims, variable base indices).

Benchmarks: (internal perf harness on p4d.24xlarge, mixed workload: 80% short(<=64) streaming, 20% long(>512))
- Baseline (main): median latency p50=18.6ms, p95=210ms, throughput=14.2k tokens/s, GPU mem usage 24.8GB
- This PR (opt-in flags both enabled): median latency p50=14.2ms (-23%), p95=132ms (-37%), throughput=17.3k tokens/s (+22%), GPU mem usage 22.1GB (-11%)
- Long-only workloads show parity in token throughput (+1-3%) and slightly improved memory locality.

Correctness: Kernel reuses existing attention math and matches reference fp32 and fp16 outputs within numerical tolerance (L2 delta < 1e-5 on sampled tensors). Unit tests cover rotary edgecases and continuous-batching boundary conditions. Numeric tests run on CI and on a small nightly GPU matrix.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind two runtime flags and an operator-visible toggle in the console. Start with internal canary on dedicated pools, then staged rollout to hosted clusters with gradual traffic ramp and automatic rollback on regression alerts.
- Observability: new metrics and trace spans are included; Canary dashboards added in docs/ops/canaries.md.

Why this is different: Earlier PRs introduced fused QKV or rotary optimizations or scheduler tweaks independently. This PR focuses on integrating a deferred-rope strategy into a fused kernel specifically to reduce memory shuffles during continuous batching and pairs it with a scheduler and KV policy that prioritizes short low-latency sessions. The combined effect reduces tail latency under mixed workloads and lowers per-token overhead for streaming-heavy applications.
Jinsoo Park requested changes: Please add a small fallback path for older GPUs with limited shared memory; the kernel currently assumes 64KB per CTA. Suggested to check SM capability at runtime and fallback to two-pass rope application.
Avery Chen (author) replied: Added a capability check and a two-pass fallback that keeps semantics identical. See fused_deferred_rope.cu: fallback_two_pass_apply_rope().
Maria Gonzales asked: Can we track how often deferred_rope was chosen vs. immediate rope in the first 10M requests? Add a counter.
Avery Chen: Added metric attn.deferred_rope.selection_count and a trace tag. Also added a perf harness flag to emit selection rates.
Liam O'Neill: Approves with comment: Nice work — please coordinate with release engineering for a staged rollout. Also ensure the priority scores are documented for SRE teams.
Release Engineering (comment): Confirmed gating flags and rollout timeline; requested a short postmortem runbook be added to docs/ops/canaries.md (done).
Introduces an opt-in fused QKV+deferred-rope attention kernel and a priority-aware hyperbatch scheduler. Default behavior unchanged; opt-in via runtime flag. Improves median latency and tail for mixed small/long seq workloads and reduces per-token GPU memory pressure for streaming requests.
payload.title: Hyperbatch attention: deferred-rope fused QKV kernel and priority-aware scheduler

payload.body:
Context: As part of “workload-aware batching defaults” we need per-tier visibility (fast/standard/cost-efficient) for latency/cost. Naively adding `tier` (plus other dimensions like `route`, `model`, `region`, `tenant`) to existing high-volume histograms explodes series count and increases telemetry cost. This PR adds tier labeling in a controlled way and introduces runtime-side cardinality controls so we can safely roll out tiered metrics in Hosted/Dedicated canaries. Summary of changes: (1) Adds `batching_tier` label to a curated set of runtime metrics: request latency histograms, queue/wait metrics, batch size distributions, and token-cost attribution counters. (2) Implements a metrics label policy (allowlist + hashing/normalization + sampling) so high-cardinality dimensions don’t propagate into hot-path metrics. (3) Adds guardrails: metric emission fallback mode (“cardinality clamp”) and self-observability counters that report when labels were dropped/normalized/sampled. (4) Updates tracing spans to include tier as a low-cardinality attribute (not a tag on every child span) to avoid backend blowups. Metrics impacted (new/updated): `runtime.request_latency_ms` (histogram) now optionally includes `batching_tier` with controlled roll-out, `runtime.decode_latency_ms` and `runtime.prefill_latency_ms` similarly updated, `runtime.batch.size_tokens` and `runtime.batch.size_requests` now include `batching_tier`, `runtime.scheduler.queue_depth` includes `batching_tier` only when queue is per-tier (Dedicated), `metering.tokens_generated_total` includes `batching_tier` (counter) for cost views, new: `runtime.metrics.cardinality_clamp_total{metric,reason}` and `runtime.metrics.labels_dropped_total{label,metric}` for diagnosing clamp behavior, new: `runtime.metrics.emission_sample_rate{metric}` (gauge) for backend cost accounting. Cardinality control policy: Tier is always allowed (fixed enum: `fast|standard|cost_efficient|unknown`). Region is allowed (bounded set). Model is allowed only via `model_family` (e.g., llama3, qwen2, mistral) in runtime hot-path; full model id remains in low-rate debug metrics and traces. Route is never emitted on histograms; route-level breakdown is handled in the gateway / control plane metrics. Tenant/customer is never emitted from runtime. When a metric would exceed the configured series budget, we clamp by dropping the highest-risk label(s) (route/model_id/tenant) and increment `cardinality_clamp_total` with a reason code. Config / rollout: Adds `metrics.cardinality_controls.*` runtime config (default enabled in canary env only): `series_budget_per_metric` (default 20k), `hotpath_label_allowlist`, `model_id_mode` (`family|id|off`, default `family`), `debug_metrics_sample_rate` (default 0.01), `clamp_mode` (`drop_labels|disable_metric`, default `drop_labels`). Backwards compatibility: No dashboards depend on tier labels yet; existing metric names are unchanged. New labels are additive and behind `features.tiered_batching_metrics_labels`. Notes: The intent is to let observability-pack dashboards slice by tier without having to ship new metric names, while ensuring we don’t reintroduce past high-cardinality incidents. Testing: Unit tests cover label policy evaluation, clamp reason codes, and ensuring tier label enums are normalized. Load test in staging shows <2% overhead in metrics serialization at p95 CPU for the telemetry exporter. Linked work: ENG-18429 (dashboards/alerts) and ENG-18426 (reason codes) consume these labels; INT-33012 tracks missing tier breakdown in dashboards and should be unblocked once observability-pack is updated.
Allison Grant: Can we guarantee tier stays low-cardinality even when unknown / experimental tiers show up? Also please document clamp semantics; we’ve been burned by silent label drops. Logan Wright: Added strict normalization to `fast|standard|cost_efficient|unknown` and will reject anything else at parse time; also added `labels_dropped_total` and `cardinality_clamp_total{reason}` so drops are visible. Aisha Bello: For dashboards, we need tier on request latency + queue depth, but route is required for some triage. Are we sure route must be excluded? Logan Wright: Route on histograms is the biggest risk; proposing to keep route breakdown in gateway/control-plane metrics and use traces for drilldown. Added comment + doc note; happy to revisit once series budgets are stable. Julian Moore: The hotpath exporter allocates on each label normalization; can we avoid string copies? Logan Wright: Switched normalization to interned enum strings and precomputed label sets; allocator profile improved in staging run. Nadia Rahman: Metering counters with tier are OK, but please ensure we don’t create `model_id`+`tier` cross product in billing metrics. Logan Wright: Confirmed billing path uses `model_family` only; full `model_id` is limited to debug metrics at 1% sample. Caleb Johnson: Tracing change looks good; please add a note about span attribute placement to avoid future churn. Logan Wright: Added to internal doc and a guard unit test ensuring tier is only on root span. Approvals: Allison Grant ✅, Aisha Bello ✅, Julian Moore ✅, Nadia Rahman ✅.
Internal: Tiered batching metrics now support `batching_tier` label (fast/standard/cost_efficient) with runtime-side cardinality controls; canary-only flag `features.tiered_batching_metrics_labels` enables emission. Adds clamp visibility counters to detect label drops and series budget enforcement.
payload.title: Runtime: add batching tier labels to metrics + cardinality controls

payload.body:
Summary: Add a lightweight presubmit prober ('presubmit-differ') that detects scope of dependency and toolchain changes to reduce install IO, and wire it into our presubmit workflow to route costly installs to staged lanes. Motivation: CI spend and noisy presubmit runs remain the largest drag on dev feedback cycles for infra-heavy changes. This PR implements a fast heuristic that compares lockfile deltas, package manifest deltas, and a small toolchain manifest to determine if a full toolchain bootstrap is required or if a cached partial layer suffices. Goals: - Reduce average presubmit install time for non-dep commits. - Prevent unnecessary full toolchain pulls on shallow changes (docs, tests, small code edits). - Provide observability (metrics) so SRE can tune thresholds. High level changes: - Introduce .github/actions/presubmit-differ/action.yml: composite action encapsulating the detection logic and exit codes for routing. - Add scripts/toolchain-bootstrap.sh: idempotent bootstrap that supports partial layer fetch by tag. - Add scripts/ci/cache-warmup.go: a small Go utility to probe remote cache and surface warm/cold state to CI. - Update .github/workflows/presubmit.yml: early presubmit step runs presubmit-differ and sets outputs to route to 'fastpath' or 'full' lanes. - Add docs/dev/presubmit.md with usage, metrics to watch, and rollback steps. - Minor Makefile/README tweaks to document new targets. Checklist: - [x] implement lightweight differ and composite action - [x] wire to presubmit workflow and staged lanes - [x] add cache probe utility and metrics emission to CI logs - [x] add docs and rollback plan - [x] performance validation on internal canary CI (see CI summary below) Performance observations (canary): - Median install time on fastpath reduced from ~42s to ~9s for non-dep commits. - Full-lane runs unaffected. - Cache probe reduces unnecessary full downloads by ~62% for the sampled week. Related: ENG-2048 (presubmit performance), SUP-912 (support ticket reporting flaky installs). Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag (this PR toggles flag via workflow inputs) 2) Canary: route 10% of PRs to the new router for 72 hours 3) Monitor presubmit latency and false-negative rate on cache detection 4) Gradual ramp to 100% and kill switch available in workflows Docs: docs/dev/presubmit.md includes both operator playbook and developer-facing notes. Backwards compatibility: If the differ action fails, workflow falls back to 'full' lane to be safe. No current breaking changes expected.
Ethan Liu (reviewer): Can the differ be gamed by maliciously updating lockfile comments or reordering entries? Response: The action hashes canonicalized lockfile contents (sorted keys + deterministic serialization) and normalizes ordering; minor reordering won't change the computed fingerprint. We also TTL signatures in the probe so an attacker would need to push a full change to affect routing.

Sofia Ramirez (reviewer): How do we observe false negatives (i.e., we route fastpath but the job actually needed full bootstrap)? Response: The probe emits a 'bootstrap_required' boolean and a 'confidence' float to workflow logs. We added metrics that increment on downstream install failures that trigger the 'fallback_full' path; dashboards are included in docs/dev/presubmit.md.

Liam O'Neal (reviewer): Are we adding any privileged network calls in the action? Security note: The composite action runs the probe and calls our internal cache API with a short-lived runner token scoped to cache:read; no credentials are persisted. Security reviewed by infra team (see SUP-912).

Author (Maya Patel): Addressed review comments: - improved canonicalization logic and added unit test (tests/presubmit/differ_test.go) - limited probe tokens to cache:read and added rotation instructions in docs - added conservative default: confidence threshold defaults to 0.9 to minimize false fastpath routing.

CI Maintainer (automation): First run failed due to flaky network to cache backend; reran job and all checks passed. CI summary: lint: pass; unit-tests: pass; integration-presubmit: pass after rerun; e2e-canary: pass; security-scan: pass with low-severity notice (token scope checked).

Merge decision: After two approving reviews and successful canary smoke runs, approved for squash merge. Rollout toggled on 10% canary for 72h post-merge. If presubmit latency regresses or install failure rate climbs >1% absolute, we will roll back the router flag.
Introduce presubmit-differ that reduces unnecessary full toolchain bootstraps by routing safe PRs to a fastpath; adds cache probe utility and documentation. Improves median presubmit install time for non-dependency changes.
Unit tests for differ logic added (tests/presubmit/differ_test.go). Ran 3-day internal canary across ~1.2k PRs: fastpath hit-rate 58%, median presubmit time for fastpath 9s, regression none observed on full lane. Manual negative tests verified fallback when probe returns low confidence.
Canary enabled: 10% of PRs for 72h. Monitor metrics: ci.presubmit.latency.p50, ci.presubmit.full_bootstrap_rate, ci.presubmit.fallbacks. Hook to alert: SRE oncall if fallback rate > 1% for 1h.
- Extend differ to consider transient devdeps via heuristics - Add de-duplication across monorepo packages to reduce repeated installs - Integrate with presubmit cost dashboard to show per-PR savings
If an incident occurs related to presubmit routing, use rollback: flip presubmit-differ.enabled=false in .github/workflows/presubmit.yml and re-run CI.
payload.title: light-presubmit-prober-and-dependency-differ

payload.body:
Motivation: Long-tail cost/latency incidents often arise from ineffective prefetch or background warmup strategies and from which SKU (model variant / quantization tier / hardware class) paid for the tokens. Existing observability surfaces show token-level cost and latency but do not connect synthetic prefetch effectiveness to SKU-level charge attribution. This PR adds a shadow-prefetch probe that issues lightweight synthetic invocations alongside production traffic (opt-in per-deployment) and stitches their traces into the real invocation graph to measure warmup effectiveness and per-SKU cost origins.

Design summary: - Shadow-prefetch probe service (telemetry/shadow_probe) that generates controlled mini-invocations matching recent prompt shapes; results are emitted as synthetic spans and a compact summary event. - SKU-aware tagging: spans created by the runtime now include a compact "sku.id" tag (string) and an inferred "sku.reason" label when fallbacks/quantization happen. These tags are propagated through the trace envelope and included in cost-attribution rollups. - Trace stitching: a new lightweight indexer joins synthetic spans to production traces via a shared correlation token (X-Trace-Anchor) without exposing user payloads. The join is privacy-preserving: only span metadata and aggregated counters are emitted to observability backends. - Dashboard: new panels under Observability -> Prefetch Effectiveness showing: synthetic warmup success rate, delta in first-token latency when warmup succeeded vs not, SKU cost slices, and a microbudget sparkline per-tenant. - Alerts: add a tuned SLO alert rule that triggers when the synthetic warmup success rate drops >20% for a tenant or when SKU-cost-per-token shifts by +30% relative to a trailing baseline. Alerts use a 5m lookback with a 3x hysteresis to avoid churn.

Backward compatibility and opt-in: Shadow-prefetch probe is disabled by default; customers enable per-deployment via the existing observability config (observe.prefetch.enable=true). SKU tags are additive string labels that do not change existing metric names. The trace-stitching indexer can be deployed in the private control plane for Private customers; default behaviour in hosted is to emit aggregated counters only.

Testing and validation: Unit tests added for trace tag propagation and synthetic span generation. End-to-end harness (tests/e2e/prefetch_harness) simulates varying prompt shapes and hardware fallbacks; we ran the harness against a dedicated staging pool for 48h. Performance bench: shadow probe adds <1% request overhead on a 1k RPS staging cluster when enabled. Privacy review: design reviewed by Security (Priya) to ensure no user payloads are leaked; probe emits only aggregated summaries and synthetic span metadata.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag, 2) Enable for internal staging and SRE tenants for 2 weeks, 3) Gradual opt-in to Hosted customers via console toggle + doc update.

Related: references ENG-8142 (linear) for the initial post-incident analysis and SUP-412 for the customer request.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation and unit tests - [x] E2E harness + perf run - [x] Security review - [x] Dashboard and alert rules - [x] Docs stub and console feature flag
Liam O'Connor: Nice end-to-end. Two asks: (1) make the probe opt-in at deployment level, (2) add a rate-limiter so we don't create synthetic bursts that distort autoscaling. Please add tests for rate-limiting behavior.
Maya Chen (author): added rate limiter to probe (token-bucket) and wired a deployment-level opt-in flag. Added unit test covering limiter edge cases.
Priya Nair: Security review done. Confirmed no payload leak; recommend explicit doc note about privacy guarantees. Added doc note in docs/observability/prefetch-probe.md.
Diego Ramos: Observability nit - the SKU tag cardinality looks bounded but add an allowlist config for hosted. Author updated to include sku.allowlist in config and fallthrough to 'unknown' for unknown SKUs.
Liam O'Connor: CI flakes on unit-tests re-run; reran and all checks green. Approving in comments.
Add opt-in shadow-prefetch probe that generates synthetic warmup invocations, SKU-aware trace tags for cost attribution, new Observability dashboard panels for prefetch effectiveness, and tuned alerts for warmup failure and SKU cost shifts.
payload.title: Introduce shadow-prefetch probe and SKU-aware trace attribution

payload.body:
Context and motivation: Several production incidents (SUP-1198) and internal load tests showed intermittent stalls in the API gateway when serving OpenAI-compat streaming routes under mixed workloads. Root causes were: (1) unbounded route payloads causing oversized request processing, (2) lack of an explicit streaming handshake for compatibility layers resulting in partial frames being forwarded, and (3) suboptimal proxy buffer high/low watermarks causing head-of-line blocking when a large sync request arrived. Goal: apply conservative, non-disruptive changes to reduce latency spikes and make streaming behavior deterministic while preserving compatibility with existing OpenAI-style clients.

Summary of changes (high-level commits):
- Commit 1: gateway: add per-route payload cap enforcement and graceful 413 handler (ENG-4821)
- Commit 2: compat: explicit stream handshake header and handshake fallback logic for clients that do not send it (ENG-4910)
- Commit 3: proxy: lower buffer high watermark and introduce a low watermark to trigger internal flush (reduce H/O-L stalls)
- Commit 4: tests: unit + integration tests for 413 scenarios and flaky streaming reassembly
- Commit 5: docs: console help text for route payload limits + migration notes

Files changed (summary):
- gateway/src/http/route_limits.rs (new checks + telemetry)
- gateway/src/proxy/stream_proxy.rs (handshake, buffering, backpressure logic)
- compat/openai/adapter.rs (compat handshake header handling and fallback)
- proxy/config/defaults.yaml (buffer watermark defaults)
- integration-tests/gateway/streaming_handshake.test (new tests)
- docs/notes/route-payload-limits.md (operational guidance)

Small illustrative snippet (handshake header check):
- If "X-Redwood-Stream-Handshake: v1" present -> proceed with framed streaming path
- Else -> advertise handshake in 101-like early header and fall back to line-delimited frames; if client continues to send large single-frame bodies, apply payload cap and return 413.

Runtime behavior and compatibility guarantees:
- Default per-route payload cap set to 4MB (configurable per-route). Caps are enforced at the gateway input layer; large multipart/tool-calling payloads are accepted via long-polling routes configured for the workload (see docs). The change aims to be opt-in per-route for teams with known large single-request needs.
- Streaming handshake is additive and backward-compatible: clients without the handshake continue to be served via the fallback reassembly path, but with stricter buffering semantics to avoid large RAM usage.
- Proxy buffers: default high watermark lowered to 256KB, low watermark introduced at 64KB. These settings reduce head-of-line stalls while keeping throughput for bursty traffic. Operators can tune via proxy config.

Testing and CI:
- Added integration tests that simulate: partial frame arrival, missing handshake header, oversized request mid-stream and ensured the gateway returns a deterministic 413 or graceful stream termination.
- Local perf runs: 10k concurrent short-streams with 1% large sync requests reduced median p95 latency by ~18% and reduced OOM/lag incidents in the repro harness.
- CI: initial lint/test pass failed on a race in the proxy reassembly; added a mutex around the reassembly queue and re-ran CI which passed. Final status: pass.

Review conversation highlights:
- Diego: "Can we avoid hardcoding 4MB in defaults? Ops teams will want smaller caps." -> Updated to make default 4MB but clearly documented as configurable per-route; added console UI note.
- Priya: "The handshake header introduces a new surface; how do we avoid breaking middleboxes?" -> We added a conservative header name (X-Redwood-Stream-Handshake) and fallback path; verified with e2e through our proxy test harness.
- Owen: "Need metrics for drop/413 counts and buffering churn." -> Added metrics: gateway.route.payload.rejected, proxy.buffer.highwater.triggers, proxy.buffer.lowwater.flushes.
- Diego (after updates): Approve. Priya: Approve. Owen: Approve with one nit about log level for the handshake fallback (fixed).

Rollback and mitigation plan:
- This change is small-surface and behind a feature flag for the first week post-deploy. If regressions are observed, ops can: (1) toggle handshake feature flag for the compat layer, (2) relax per-route caps via console, (3) revert proxy watermarks via config. Alerting added to detect >0.5% 413 rate across routes in a five-minute window.

Operational notes for SRE and customers:
- Console shows a new per-route card: "Payload cap" with current usage and recent rejected counts.
- Migration: teams that rely on very large single-request payloads should set a route override or use the dedicated long-poll route template.

Merge and rollout:
- Merged via squash on 2024-10-24 after approvals and CI green. Rollout started as a staged feature-flag rollout to 10% of gateway nodes, increasing to 100% over 48 hours while monitoring the new metrics. No customer-impacting regressions observed during rollout window.

Notes for future work:
- Consider dynamic payload caps using request-signature sampling to auto-increase caps for authenticated clients with historical behavior.
- Evaluate switching to structured binary stream frames to simplify reassembly and decrease buffer churn (long-term).
Stabilizes streaming for OpenAI-compat routes: adds explicit stream handshake, enforces per-route payload caps with graceful 413 responses, and tunes proxy buffer watermarks to reduce H/O-L stalls.
gateway: enforce configurable per-route payload caps; add OpenAI-compat streaming handshake and proxy buffer watermark tuning (non-breaking, opt-in per-route).
Run integration-tests/gateway/streaming_handshake.test locally; simulate large single-frame bodies and confirm 413 returned. Verify metrics emitted: gateway.route.payload.rejected and proxy.buffer.highwater.triggers.

Summary: This PR introduces a latency-drift compensator into the continuous-batcher scheduler. The compensator monitors per-queue running latency and recent service shortfalls, dynamically adjusts admission weights and per-request jittered timeouts, and coordinates with a light KV-cache pinning fallback to avoid long-lived starvation in co-located KV-heavy workloads. Motivation: Recent customer workloads with mixed short/long sequences exposed cases where continuous batching heuristics could allow sustained starvation of low-throughput, latency-sensitive lanes when long KV-miss requests dominate batch composition. Existing mitigations (static priority boosts, simple TTL-based preemption) reduced tail latency but caused oscillation and expensive cache thrashing. Design: The compensator implements three cooperating mechanisms: 1) Drift estimator: a running estimator per-lane that computes 'latency drift' = observed P95 - expected SLO; it uses an EWMA with bias correction to avoid overreacting to single spikes. 2) Admission rebalancer: when drift for a lane exceeds a threshold, the compensator increases that lane's admission weight by a bounded factor and schedules soft backoffs on competing lanes. Adjustments decay with an adaptive half-life proportional to current load to prevent oscillation. 3) Jittered soft-timeouts: requests from lanes with high drift receive a small randomized timeout budget (10-50ms) added to their scheduling window to prioritize completion without hard-preemptions. KV-cache pinning fallback: when a lane is identified as KV-heavy and repeatedly starved, the compensator coordinates with the KV-cache layer to pin hot keys for a short duration (configurable) to avoid repeated long fetches; pins are conservative and evicted preferentially when memory pressure increases. Telemetry & tuning: new metrics: scheduler.latency_drift{lane}, scheduler.weight_adjustment{lane}, scheduler.timeout_jitter_ms{lane}, kv_cache.pinned_keys_count, kv_cache.pin_evictions. Defaults chosen from offline benches (see bench/bench_compensator.go). Testing: unit tests for estimator/backoff logic (pkg/scheduler/compensator_test.go), integration fixture simulating KV-miss storms, and small-scale bench harness to assert non-regression on median and 95/99 latency for mixed loads. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag --enable-drift-compensator (default off), staged rollout via canary percentage and automatic rollback on regressions detected in SLO monitors. After two weeks of canary and manual verification we enabled default-on for dedicated clusters. Backwards compatibility: no API or protobuf changes. Config knobs added to runtime config and console UI for operator tuning. Related work: follows recommendations from ENG-3421 (continuous-batcher fairness review) and uses heuristics from ENG-3489 (kv pinning guidelines).
1) initial compensator implementation + estimator (pkg/scheduler/continuous_compensator.go)
2) tests and bench harness (pkg/scheduler/compensator_test.go, cmd/bench/bench_compensator.go)
3) KV-cache pinning hook and conservative eviction policy (pkg/runtime/kv_cache/pinning.go)
4) flags and config plumbing (internal/config/flags.go)
5) telemetry and docs (pkg/scheduler/metrics.go, docs/design/continuous-batcher-compensator.md)
6) small fixes after review (bounds tightening, extra unit-tests)
Ravi Shah: Can you clarify how the EWMA bias-correction constant was chosen? Looks like a potential tuning footgun for low-traffic lanes.
Ava Martinez: Added comment and unit test demonstrating estimator behavior at low sample counts; default alpha=0.12 matches bench-derived stability curve.
Lena Petrov: The KV pinning integration looks risky for memory; can you make pin duration and memory threshold operator-configurable?
Ava Martinez: Exposed two settings (kv_pin_duration_ms, kv_pin_memory_threshold_pct) and added defensive checks to avoid pinning under pressure; updated docs.
Marcus O'Connor: CI showed a flake in bench harness; please make bench tolerance deterministic or skip on CI.
Ava Martinez: Bench harness now has deterministic RNG seed in CI path; flakiness went away.
Lena Petrov: Request small comment in continuous_compensator.go about why we choose jittered soft-timeouts vs hard-preemptions.
Ava Martinez: Added explanatory comment and referenced design doc.
Ravi Shah: Approving pending one more integration run against a KV-heavy scenario.
CI: integration run passed (flaky rerun 1).
Ravi Shah: Approved.
Lena Petrov: Approved.
Marcus O'Connor: Approved and merged.
Introduce latency-drift compensator for the continuous-batcher scheduler. Reduces prolonged starvation of latency-sensitive lanes under KV-heavy or long-sequence mixes by adaptive admission rebalancing, jittered soft-timeouts, and conservative KV-cache pinning. Metrics and operator knobs added. No public API changes.
Feature initially gated behind --enable-drift-compensator. Recommended canary: 5% traffic for 72h, monitor scheduler.latency_drift and kv_cache.pinned_keys_count. Default conservative knobs: drift_threshold_ms=40, max_weight_boost=1.5, kv_pin_duration_ms=5000, kv_pin_memory_threshold_pct=20. If kv_pin_memory_threshold_pct is exceeded, pinning is disabled until pressure subsides.
Risk: mis-tuned expectations could over-prioritize low-volume lanes and increase overall throughput tail. Mitigations: bounded weight multipliers, adaptive decay proportional to load, opt-out flag for critical workloads, and progressive rollout with SLO-based automatic rollback. Added additional telemetry to detect oscillation and a dashboard in Redwood Console docs/design/continuous-batcher-compensator.md.
Bench scripts and a small recorded workload are included in cmd/bench; see docs for how to reproduce the KV-starvation scenario.
payload.title: scheduler: latency-drift compensator for continuous-batcher to reduce starvation

Adds an opt-in span-edge indexer that emits path-anchored cost/latency rollups and a dashboard + alert to surface long-tail cost regressions by application path.
Motivation: long-tail token cost and latency are often hard to attribute when spans are sparse or work is shared across services; this change introduces a compact span-edge indexer and path-anchored rollups so SREs and engineers can quickly attribute cost/latency to an application path (route+handler+model-variant). What this does: adds an OTLP processor that synthesizes directed span edges at ingest time and emits edge tuples, a lightweight indexer service that materializes path_key -> {token_count_ms_cost} rollups, a small schema addition (edge_id and path_key tags), and a new console dashboard with per-path cost/latency heatmap and an alert tuned for persistent 95th-percentile cost drift per-path. Backwards compatibility and rollout: indexer is opt-in via telemetry.config.enabled=false by default, legacy traces remain unchanged, and the rollout is feature-flag gated across regions with a canary population; no customer-facing breaking changes. Performance: added ~5% ingestion CPU at peak in our bench but yields ~25% faster root-cause detection on canary traffic due to pre-aggregated paths. Testing and validation: unit tests for extractor and aggregator, integration test harness with synthetic routes, e2e canary in us-west-2 with staged traffic, manual SLO guardrails during rollout. Checklist: run schema migration for new tags, update Prometheus scrape jobs to include span-edge metrics, update ops runbook, add console dashboard to release bundle. Related tasks: ENG-1129 (indexer implementation) and ENG-1194 (console and alerts).

Summary: Introduce a lightweight client-visible error taxonomy for JSON schema mismatches and a backpressure handshake for streaming responses that improves stability when using response_format/schema validation and tool/function calling. Motivation: Customers integrating structured outputs were seeing opaque parse failures and silent stream truncations when the model deviates from the schema. That made debugging hard in hosted and private deployments and produced noisy support tickets. This PR addresses three things: 1) a set of human-friendly error codes and actionable hints returned inline with stream/terminal responses for schema issues, 2) a transient backpressure/handshake signal that allows callers to request the server to pause/resume stream emission while the client attempts to reconcile partial output (useful for large tool calls and KV cache warmups), and 3) OpenAI-compat mapping for function_call/response_format interactions so existing clients have predictable behavior. Design highlights: - New error codes: SCHEMA_MISMATCH_HINT, SCHEMA_TYPE_COERCE_ATTEMPTED, SCHEMA_TRUNCATED_CHUNK, STREAM_PAUSED_FOR_RETRY. Each code contains a short, user-facing message and a concise debug_hint string (example: "expected field 'items' to be array but got string; try wrapping single object in [ ] or enable response_format=coerce"). - Streaming markers: we add a control-signal frame type "control.handshake" that is emitted as a JSON-LD-like control envelope on the stream. Control frames are only emitted on explicit streaming connections where response_format is set and streaming is enabled; they are ignored by non-aware clients. - Backpressure API: client can send control.resume or control.pause messages over the same websocket/HTTP2 stream to allow server to temporarily hold token emission for up to a configurable window (default 5s). This is intended for short reconciliations, not long polling. - OpenAI compatibility: function_call responses that previously relied on post-stream assembly now include a final control.frame with "function_schema_verified":true/false and the error code when verification failed. This avoids silent mis-parses by wrappers. - Opt-in: the new strictness toggle remains opt-in via response_format.mode={permissive,coerce,strict}; default remains permissive for backward compatibility. Implementation notes: runtime: add a new control frame serializer and lightweight state machine to the streaming agent. API: extend response_format schema with an optional "client_handshake":true field. OpenAI-compat shim: post-process function_call object before final frame, emit verification result. Console/Docs: document handshake semantics and show client examples for WebSocket and SSE. Tests: unit tests cover error code creation and mapping; integration tests simulate a streaming model that emits malformed JSON and verify correct control frames and pause/resume behavior; e2e tests with Python SDK sample. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind rollout.feature.schema_handshake. Step 1: Canary on internal beta accounts for 48 hours. Step 2: Ramp to 10% hosted traffic for 24h while monitoring schema-error rates and stream disconnects. Step 3: Full rollout with a 7-day monitor window. Migration notes: No required changes for most clients. To observe pause/resume and richer errors, clients should opt-in by setting response_format.client_handshake=true and handling control frames. For OpenAI-compat clients using function_call, the shim is backward compatible but exposes verification boolean in the final frame. Related work: follows up on previous schema negotiator and stream-snapshot work. See Linear ENG-2345 for original incident. Checklist: - [x] Runtime control frame implemented - [x] Error taxonomy and messages in localization pipeline - [x] SDK examples updated (Python/TS) - [x] Docs page on structured streaming updated - [x] Canary plan and alerting configured
Liam O'Connor: Can we avoid adding an additional websocket sub-protocol? I like the control frame approach but prefer reusing existing framing if possible.
Ava Martinez: Responding, we intentionally keep framing as a lightweight JSON control envelope to avoid incompatibilities with SSE parsers; it's feature-flagged and ignored by older clients.
Priya Desai: The default 5s pause window seems arbitrary; can we make it configurable via tenant config?
Ava Martinez: Yes, added tenant-level rollout.feature.schema_handshake.pause_window_seconds with default 5; documented.
Marco Ruiz: Suggest adding more graceful fallback telemetry so SRE can distinguish client-triggered pauses from model stalls.
Ava Martinez: Added observability events and an alert that surfaces pause/resume counts per tenant. Also included a debug_hint field in all error frames.
Introduce optional streaming handshake and human-friendly schema error codes. Clients can opt-in to pause/resume streaming to allow client-side reconciliation of partial structured outputs. Adds OpenAI-compat verification frame for function_call responses. Backwards compatible by default.
Enable rollout.feature.schema_handshake for internal beta. Monitor schema-error-rate and pause-resume metrics. Publish docs and SDK snippets. Follow-up: telemetry dashboard to show top schema_hint values.
payload.title: Humane schema error codes and backpressure handshake for streaming structured output

Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and uncontrolled spillover during tenant backfills were causing multi-tenant tail latency spikes and elevated egress to cold storage. This PR introduces a coordinated backfill-aware evictor and a lightweight page-mending handoff protocol that reduces fragmentation and smooths spillback during sustained background writes. Summary of changes: 1) evictor: new gradient-based eviction policy that weights fragmentation score, tenant priority, and backfill intensity; 2) backfill coordinator: exposes a soft-lock contract so long-running backfills advertise working sets and receive eviction leeway; 3) handoff protocol: compacting swaps and page-mend operations that attempt in-place remerge before spill-to-disk; 4) scheduler hooks: add preemption-safe window for continuous-batching to drain KV write bursts without defeating latency SLOs; 5) metrics and knobs: new metrics kv.backfill_score, kv.fragmentation_ratio, kv.handoff_attempts and associated config for backfill_throttle and mend_retries. Implementation notes: eviction policy implemented in runtime/kv/evictor with a small state machine and async io-safe recovery path; backfill coordinator runs in a per-tenant actor and negotiates with evictor via shared SI queues; handoff uses preallocated temporary pages to avoid allocation stalls. Testing and validation: unit tests for eviction heuristics and handoff correctness; end-to-end bench harness that runs mixed load with synthetic backfills to measure tail-latency and spill volume; staged rollout to Dedicated with canary and automatic rollback on >5% tail-latency regression. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-2145) [x] unit tests added [x] bench added [x] docs/ops updated [x] feature-flag guarded and on-by-default in canary. Risks: handoff retries can increase short-term CPU; mitigated by exponential backoff + mend_retries cap. Rollout plan: deploy to canary cluster for 72 hours, analyze kv.handoff_attempts and kv.spill_bytes, then enable global rollout if spill volume drops >40% and p99 latency unchanged or improved. Related: references to prior compaction PRs for allocator stability.
Tomás Alvarez: Please add a short doc comment on the eviction weight formula and how tenant priority interacts with fragmentation score. Author reply: Added comment and unit test that validates weight ordering under synthetic conditions.
Priya Nair: Can mend_retries be made configurable per-tenant? Concern about noisy tenants. Author reply: Added per-tenant override and default global cap; updated config surface in docs.
Evan Li: Benchmark shows 2% CPU increase at 95th; can we gate CPU-heavy compaction to low-load windows? Author reply: Added low-load gating heuristic and adaptive backoff; re-ran bench and p99 tail improved while CPU delta reduced to 0.4%.
Alex (SRE): Confirmed metrics emitted and alert threshold suggestions; requested a transient spike window in runbook. Author reply: Runbook updated and added canary dashboard tiles.
Consensus reached that a coordinated backfill contract is preferable to unilateral eviction tuning. SRE requested runbook updates and thresholds. Implementation favors incremental rollout behind config flags. Bench improvements validated after adaptive gating added.
Unit tests covering eviction weight ordering and mend success rates, integration mixed-backfill harness demonstrating 45% drop in spill bytes and 8% improvement in p99 under test load, and canary run with no degraded SLOs over 72h.
Feature is behind feature flag 'kv.backfill_handoff_v1'. Default canary config: backfill_throttle=0.25, mend_retries=3, low_load_window_ms=2000. Watch kv.spill_bytes, kv.handoff_attempts, kv.fragmentation_ratio. Rollback if p99 increases >5% or spill_bytes increases.
Introduce backfill-aware eviction and page-mend handoff to reduce KV spillover during tenant backfills. Adds new metrics and knobs for ops tuning. Improves p99 under mixed backfill workloads.
payload.title: Introduce orchestrated backfill-aware evictor and page-mending handoff

payload.body:
## Context
We’re landing the cache telemetry suite (hit/miss, reuse depth, evictions, wasted prefill). For the signals to be actionable in dashboards and in the recommendations MVP, we need consistent slicing keys that match how Redwood operates: route, model, model version, deployment mode, and region.

This PR wires request-scoped context from the gateway/control plane into the runtime metrics emitter and applies strict allowlists/coercion so we don’t accidentally create per-tenant/per-request label explosions.

Related: ENG-4823 (route/model context joinability), ENG-4821 (metric defs + tags).

## What this changes
- Adds `TelemetryContext` (derived from `RequestContext`) to runtime metric emission sites for cache metrics.
- Adds the following metric labels (when enabled):
  - `rw_route`: stable route identifier (normalized, allowlisted; NOT tenant-specific)
  - `rw_model`: model identifier (allowlisted)
  - `rw_model_version`: model version identifier (allowlisted, stable across regions)
  - `rw_deployment_mode`: `hosted|dedicated|private`
  - `rw_region`: coarse region (existing tag in some metrics; now consistent for cache metrics)
- Enforces allowlists + coercion:
  - If a value is missing or not in the allowlist, we emit `other` and increment a debug counter.
  - No tenant IDs, no project IDs, no raw route paths, no prompt hashes.
- Adds debug/health counters:
  - `rw_runtime_telemetry_label_coercions_total{label_name=..., reason=...}`
  - `rw_runtime_telemetry_context_missing_total{field=...}`
  These are intended for internal validation only and are not broken down by route/model.

## Cardinality policy (implementation details)
The runtime receives context values from the gateway as already-normalized strings (e.g., `route_key`, `model_key`, `model_version_id`). Runtime does not attempt to “compute” route keys from paths.

Allowlist sources:
- Static allowlist shipped via config (initial rollout)
- Optional dynamic allowlist refresh (follow-up; stubbed interface included)

Coercion behavior:
- Empty/unknown values → `other`
- Over-length values (defense-in-depth) → `other` with reason `too_long`

Example:
- `rw_route = chat_support_prod` (allowlisted)
- `rw_route = /v1/chat/completions?customer=foo` (NOT allowed; would be coerced)

## Flags
- `telemetry.cache_metrics.enable_context_labels` (default: true in staging/canary, false in prod until rollout gate)
- `telemetry.cache_metrics.route_allowlist_path`
- `telemetry.cache_metrics.model_allowlist_path`
- `telemetry.cache_metrics.model_version_allowlist_path`

## Tests
- Unit tests for allowlist + coercion reasons.
- Regression test asserting that when context labels are disabled, the cache metric label set remains unchanged.
- Integration-level handler tests validate that context is plumbed for chat/generate/embeddings/rerank.

## Notes / Follow-ups
- Ingestion-side guards still apply (observability-pack PR adds drop rules for forbidden label combos); runtime coercion is defense-in-depth.
- Next PR will turn on `enable_context_labels` in prod behind the rollout checklist once allowlists are populated for top routes/models.

## Checklist
- [x] No raw prompts / no request IDs added to labels
- [x] Label values are allowlisted + bounded
- [x] Added internal counters to validate coercion rates
- [x] Added tests
- [x] Updated internal docs for join keys

---
### Implementation snippet (illustrative)
`cache_metrics.cc` now takes a `TelemetryContext` and merges it into the label set:

```cc
MetricLabels labels = base_labels;
if (flags.enable_context_labels) {
  labels["rw_route"] = allowlists.route.CoerceOrOther(ctx.route_key);
  labels["rw_model"] = allowlists.model.CoerceOrOther(ctx.model_key);
  labels["rw_model_version"] = allowlists.model_version.CoerceOrOther(ctx.model_version_id);
  labels["rw_deployment_mode"] = DeploymentModeToString(ctx.deployment_mode);
  labels["rw_region"] = ctx.region.empty() ? "other" : ctx.region;
}
metrics::Counter("rw_runtime_cache_kv_hits_total", labels).Increment(hits);
```

---
## Review conversation (highlights)
**Omar El-Sayed (Runtime):** “Make sure we don’t accidentally tag retries with different context; the labels must be stable across the request lifecycle.”

**Ethan Park (author):** “Yep — context is attached to the top-level RequestContext and copied into the per-attempt telemetry context. We also keep the label injection in one place (metrics emitter) so retries don’t ‘drift’ based on handler code paths.”

**Nadia Rahman (Telemetry schema):** “Can we keep the label names aligned with the naming policy (`rw_route`, `rw_model`, `rw_model_version`)? Also prefer `deployment_mode` values to be a fixed enum.”

**Ethan Park:** “Updated to `rw_*` label names and hard-coded enum strings (`hosted|dedicated|private`). Added a unit test to prevent new deployment mode strings without updating the allowlist policy doc.”

**Caleb Johnson (Cardinality controls):** “I’m worried about `rw_region` exploding via AZ or private cluster names. Please bound it (coarse region only) or coerce unknowns.”

**Ethan Park:** “Good catch. `rw_region` comes from the existing region enum we use in gateway metrics (e.g., `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`). Added a length guard + `other` fallback, and a `context_missing_total{field=region}` counter.”

**Noah Patel (Runtime architecture):** “Do we need `rw_model_version` vs `rw_model_revision`? Consistency matters for joins.”

**Ethan Park:** “Using `model_version_id` per the control-plane contract and Slack thread on joinability. Added `platform/contracts/telemetry_context.md` with examples and a note that ‘version’ is the stable join key.”

Approvals:
- Omar El-Sayed: ✅ Approved
- Nadia Rahman: ✅ Approved (after label rename)
- Caleb Johnson: ✅ Approved (after region bounding + coercion counter)
- Logan Wright: ✅ Approved

---
## CI
- buildkite/runtime-linux: PASS
- buildkite/runtime-tests: PASS
- buildkite/lint: PASS
- sanitizer-smoke: PASS

Merged via squash to `main`.
payload.title: Propagate route + model version context into runtime cache metrics (with cardinality allowlists)

payload.body:
Motivation: following a partial network partition incident in us-west-2 we observed an 'islanded region' pattern where a subset of nodes continued accepting requests but lost connectivity to our global control plane and downstream KV cache. Two issues made this worse: 1) the region-level circuit breaker failed to open quickly when loss of heartbeats coincided with aggressive KV cache eviction, and 2) tenant-level SLO budgets were not being re-provisioned to reflect sudden capacity loss, causing high-priority traffic to be starved by background low-priority workloads. This PR implements a fast-path isolation policy that: (a) detects islanded-region semantics (heartbeat delta + cache-thrash signal) and flips an emergency backpressure marker; (b) triggers prioritized eviction of best-effort requests and request-level early-exit with HTTP 429 for low-priority routes; (c) updates the SLO enforcer to re-weight token budgets immediately under emergency backpressure; and (d) fixes a race in the region circuit-breaker where repeated KV cache invalidations could prevent Open->Closed transitions. Changes are conservative and opt-in behind a feature flag `islanded_fastpath_v1` for staged rollout. Design notes: - Detection: combine node heartbeat loss (>3s missed) with cache-thrash metric (kv_evictions_per_sec > threshold) to avoid false positives during short control-plane jitter. - Eviction semantics: best-effort routes are drained first; streaming/chat sessions are checkpointed and offered a graceful close signal; high-priority inference (reserved/dedicated customers) keep their token budgets but may experience slightly higher latency due to FQ backpressure. - SLO enforcer: when backpressure marker is set, tenant token allocations are scaled by emergency_factor (default 0.5) except for pinned tenants (matches dedicated/reserved mapping). - Circuit-breaker fix: avoid a missed-open path by making state transitions idempotent and introducing an in-memory 'pending_open' set persisted to raft-config for 10s to survive quick flaps. Testing & rollout: - Unit tests for detector heuristics and SLO re-weighting added. - Local chaos tests simulate control-plane partition with simulated KV thrash. - Canary rollout: start feature flag on staging, then route 5% of us-west-2 traffic to the new path; increase to 50% if metrics show reduced P95 degradation. Observability: new metrics exported: islanded_backpressure_active (0/1), islanded_evict_rate, islanded_slo_scale_factor; dashboards and alerting rules added in observability-pack. Risk & mitigation: false positives could evict unnecessarily; mitigated by dual-signal detection and feature flag. Rollback via disabling `islanded_fastpath_v1` or setting emergency_factor=1. Related: incident SUP-987, ENG-2120.
Diego Alvarez: Can we avoid dropping streaming sessions mid-response? Suggest we emit a graceful-close event and allow 10s drain window.
Maya Chen (author): Implemented graceful-close handshake for streams; added 10s drain window and test coverage (integration/chaos).
Priya Nair: The detector threshold for kv_evictions_per_sec seems low for prod; propose 2x multiplier behind a runtime knob.
Maya Chen: Added runtime knob `detector.kv_eviction_multiplier` and updated docs to recommend conservative defaults during early rollout.
Evan Thompson: LGTM overall; please add unit test asserting circuit-breaker doesn't oscillate when kv invalidations spike for <5s.
Maya Chen: Added unit test `region_cb_stable_under_spike` and a small comment explaining the pending_open set semantics.
- Fix: region circuit-breaker missed-open race causing islanded regions to continue accepting traffic under control-plane partition; now durable for short flaps. - Feature: emergency backpressure path that prioritizes eviction of best-effort requests and reweights tenant SLO budgets under islanded-region conditions. - Telemetry: new islanded_backpressure_active, islanded_evict_rate, islanded_slo_scale_factor metrics
If you see islanded_backpressure_active=1 in us-west-2: check detector thresholds and kv_evictions_per_sec; quick mitigation is to disable feature flag `islanded_fastpath_v1` or set emergency_factor=1. For persistent control-plane instability, escalate SUP-987.

payload.body:
Motivation: Reduce risk when rolling out RBAC v2 policy changes and KMS residency mappings by providing a deterministic dry-run and local simulation path plus an immutable audit artifact bundler. This PR adds three coordinated developer-facing tools: 1) an RBACv2 policy simulator that evaluates policy changes against a configurable set of tenant/operator scenarios (including nested role templates, temporal grants, and operator-scoped exceptions), 2) a KMS dry-run validator which resolves KMS selection heuristics, affinity fallbacks and quota checks without touching production KMS keys, and 3) an Audit Proof Bundler that packages policy change inputs, simulator output, and a signed checksum so infra teams can store verifiable evidence alongside deploys. Summary of changes: new CLI service (rctl simulate) and internal library redwood/security/simulator with a lightweight scenario DSL; kms/dryrun that wire-frames KMS provider selection and upstream compatibility checks; audit/proof-bundler that emits an immutable JSON+sig artifact and S3 uploader with retention metadata. Checklist: [x] unit tests for simulator decision paths, [x] e2e harness against staged policy DB snapshot, [x] docs (console + CLI usage), [x] feature-flag gated (rbac.simulator.enabled=false by default), [x] telemetry events and per-scenario latency histograms. Backwards compatibility: no runtime path changes—simulator and dry-run code paths are read-only by default. Rollout plan: land behind feature flag, opt-in for early enterprise customers via console toggle, run a one-week pilot on redwood-dedicated, iterate based on false-positive/negative policy diffs. Security review: KMS dry-run intentionally prevents key material or credential exchange; it uses cached provider metadata and quota/region heuristics. Audit artifacts are signed with the platform's signing key (rotation-aware) and stored in the immutables bucket; access to artifacts requires org-level RBAC perms. Testing: comprehensive unit coverage added, integration tests run in CI against a mocked KMS cluster and a snapshot of policy-catalog; manual validation performed with three customers in staging. Related work: ties into ENG-4122 (policy rollout safety) and ENG-4231 (tenant residency tooling). Migration notes: operators should run `rctl simulate apply-scan --snapshot <id>` on policy snapshots before large rollouts; artifact bundle IDs are compatible with the Console's policy diff view. CI notes: some flaky integration tests required mocking timeouts; we added retries and a small delay param. Merge: squash merged by Marina Gómez on 2025-09-19. Release notes: Adds RBACv2 policy simulator CLI, KMS dry-run validator, and audit proof bundler to help safely validate cross-tenant policy and KMS changes before rollout.
Ethan Cole: Nice toolset—can the simulator ingest live operator sessions for accuracy? Author: We intentionally kept ingestion to snapshots to avoid PII and to keep runs deterministic; we may add an optional sanitized ingestion later behind a flag.
Marina Gómez: Audit bundles need TTL metadata. Author: Added retention and vault-key annotation to the bundler; docs updated.

Motivation: observed recurring thrash on multi-tenant nodes when low-frequency keys are promoted back into hot segments and trigger premature spillovers. This PR introduces a temporal retention-decay model and a margined spill scheduler that cooperates with the scheduler and the kernel hinting path to keep spill bursts bounded.

What this does (high level): implements a decaying retention score (time-decay + access recency) for KV entries, exposes a per-tenant soft-margin which reserves a small buffer of pages to reduce immediate spill pressure, and schedules spill work in a paced fashion (margined spill scheduler) instead of draining aggressively. Adds kernel-level page hinting (MADV_DONTNEED-like signals) for cooled pages to accelerate reclaim without full spill when safe.

Design notes: the temporal score is computed as score = alpha * recency + beta * (1 - e^{-age/tau}) where alpha/beta/tau are tunables exposed in config. The soft-margin is a tenant-level reservation (percentage of cache) that prevents a tenant's low-priority allocations from triggering global spill until global pressure crosses a threshold. The margined spill scheduler groups candidate pages into bounded batches and enforces a backoff window to smooth IO. Interacts with continuous batching: the batcher now tags requests with 'cache-affinity' hints so eviction can avoid hot prefixes currently being actively batched.

Checklist: [x] unit tests for score computation, [x] integration tests for margin behavior, [x] end-to-end perf job, [x] feature-flag gating, [x] docs update stub.

Commits summary: single-feature branch squashed into logical commits: initial temporal-decay model, margin reservation plumbing, margined spill scheduler, kernel hinting integration, tests and perf tuning.

Files touched (high-level): kv/cache/retention.h, kv/cache/retention.cc, kv/scheduler/spill_scheduler.cc, kv/scheduler/spill_scheduler.h, infra/config/kv_flags.yaml, runtimes/linux/page_hints.cc, tests/kv/temporal_decay_test.cc

Testing and perf: locally ran mixed workload A (80% small requests, 20% cold scans) against staging fleet: cache hit rate improved +3.7% and sustained throughput +4.2% at same provision; p99 token latency reduced by 6.1% under spike conditions. Extended soak for 72h on dedicated canaries with feature flag enabled — no regressions observed in memory usage patterns.

Rollout plan: gate under kv.temporal_decay_v2 (default off for existing clusters). Start with 5% of dedicated clusters, monitor hit-rate, p99, and spill IO. If stable after 48h, increase to 25% then full rollout. Fallback: feature flag off and scheduler reverts to legacy immediate-spill path.

Related: follows up on ENG-1142 (tenant-aware quota work) and complements recent spill pacing experiments in ENG-1298.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps migration conservative — we do not change on-disk formats or persisted metadata. The kernel hinting path on some older kernels is a no-op; code guards are in place.
Introduce a tenant-aware temporal decay policy and a margined spill scheduler to reduce fragmentation-related thrash; improves tail latency and cache utilization for mixed workloads. Rollout via feature flag `kv.temporal_decay_v2` with canary on dedicated clusters.
Anya Kovalenko: Can you explain the default values chosen for tau/alpha/beta? Have we considered workload-specific autotuning?
Samir Patel: Reply: defaults picked from microbench runs on mixed-traffic; added a follow-up TODO to hook autotuning into the Optimize service. See comment in retention.cc
Priya Nair: Please ensure kernel hinting is a no-op on kernels <5.10 to avoid unexpected behavior. Also request a short doc for operators.
Samir Patel: Reply: added kernel check branch and a small operators doc in infra/config/kv_flags.yaml. Marked for docs-owner to expand.
Marcus Reid: Observed one flaky test on PR CI due to timing window in spill_scheduler test. Suggest increasing backoff tolerance in test harness.
Samir Patel: Reply: widened tolerance and reran tests; CI green now.

Motivation: We see repeated noisy alerts driven by small cohorts of invocations (odd prompt shapes or very long KV cache cold starts). Teams need a way to attribute cost/latency anomalies to invocation cohorts and to visualize how kernel latency evolves across the first N tokens as kernels and KV caches warm up. This PR introduces: 1) a lightweight per-invocation cohorting tag (invocation_cohort_id) based on prompt-shape and context-warmth heuristics; 2) a kernel-warmup heatmap that aggregates kernel-level latency for the first 32 tokens vs KV-warmth buckets and exposes a Grafana dashboard; 3) an adaptive alert-backoff rule that quiets alerts for cohorts that show high variance but low long-term impact, and increases sampling and digesting instead of immediate paging. Checklist: - [x] Add cohort id generation and propagation into traces and metrics - [x] Emit cohort-level rollup counters and histograms (latency, tokens, cost-est) - [x] Instrument kernel-level per-token timings and KV-warmth tag - [x] Grafana dashboard JSON and panels for heatmap + cohort explorer - [x] Alert rule: adaptive backoff with cohort decay window and prioritization - [x] Unit tests and integration test for cohort assignment - [x] Docs: observability guide section + example query snippets Design summary: - Cohorting: we compute a compact prompt-shape fingerprint = hash(num_tokens, avg_token_length, normalized_prompt_embedding_bucket) and combine with a KV-warmth score (0..3) to form invocation_cohort_id = fingerprint:vwarm. This is intentionally coarse to bound cardinality while grouping meaningful shapes. Cohort id is attached as a trace tag and a metric label for rollups. - Kernel warmup heatmap: the collector records per-kernel micro-latency for token positions 0..31 and emits a histogram keyed by (kernel_name, token_pos_bucket, kv_warmth). We downsample high-frequency kernels with reservoir sampling for storage cost. - Adaptive alert backoff: new alert logic uses cohort-level variance + recent impact to decide whether an alert should escalate to paging or be converted into a digest entry. This reduces churn for cohorts with spiky behavior but small aggregate cost. Commits (high-level): - commit 1: "observability: add invocation cohort id and cohort propagation" - introduces cohort fingerprinting code, tagging in request tracer, and metric label plumbing. - commit 2: "collector: kernel warmup timing and kv-warmth tag" - records per-token kernel latencies, adds reservations for high-cardinality limits, and backfills unit tests. - commit 3: "monitoring: grafana kernel-warmup heatmap + cohort explorer" - adds dashboard JSON + example queries. - commit 4: "alerting: adaptive cohort backoff rule and playbook" - updates alert rules and runbook guidance. Files changed (high level): - src/observability/cohorting.rs: new fingerprinting and tag propagation logic - src/collector/kernel_timer.cc: per-token kernel timers and kv-warmth extraction - src/collector/rollups.rs: cohort rollup counters and histograms - deploy/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/kernel_warmup_heatmap.json: new dashboard (heatmap + cohort explorer panels) - infra/alerts/alert_rules.yaml: adaptive backoff rule and new labels - sdk/python/redwood/observability.py: helper to surface cohort id in SDK traces - docs/observability/cohorting.md: design/queries and runbook - tests/observability/test_cohorting.py: unit tests for fingerprint boundaries - examples/observability/query_examples.md: example PromQL / Flux queries Migration notes: - Cohort id is an additive label; existing metrics are unchanged but rollups gain a new label. We add default cardinality caps to collectors (default 5k cohorts per shard) to avoid explosion; teams with high cardinality can opt-in for higher caps via config. Observability queries (examples included in docs): - Top cohorts by token-cost: sum(token_cost) by (invocation_cohort_id) - Kernel warmup heatmap: heatmap of p95 kernel_latency per token_pos_bucket grouped by kv_warmth - Cohort stability metric: delta of p95 over 5h-window and 1h-window Review summary: - Diego found an edge-case where trivial prompt shapes collided; we widened the hash input to include a small fingerprint of the first non-empty token. - Priya suggested lowering reservoir sample size for the hottest kernels; adjusted to 10k -> 5k to cap storage. - Liam requested an explicit opt-out flag for compliance-sensitive customers; added config flag and test. Backwards compatibility: additive only. Telemetry and cost: added a small instrumentation overhead (~0.7% sampling equivalent) when heatmap enabled; default is off for low-traffic tiers. Merge: Squashed and merged to main on 2026-02-24.
Add new per-invocation cohorting metadata, a Grafana kernel-warmup heatmap dashboard, and an adaptive alert backoff policy to reduce noisy alert churn for long-tail cohorts.
Diego Alvarez: Nice approach on bounding cardinality. One concern: two very different prompts with identical token counts and avg_token_length might collide. Can we include a tiny prefix fingerprint?
Maya Chen (author): Good catch — added first-nonempty-token fingerprint (8-bit) into the prompt-shape hash to reduce that class of collisions. Updated tests accordingly.
Priya Natarajan: Reservoir sampling tune looks fine but storage hit still non-trivial for high-throughput kernels. Suggest exposing sample_limit per-kernel via config and a safe default of 5k.
Maya Chen (author): Exposed kernel_sample_limit in collector config; default 5k. Added integration test to simulate high-frequency kernel and assert retention bound.
Liam O'Connor: For enterprise/private installs we need an opt-out to avoid sending cohort fingerprints to hosted telemetry. Add config and docs.
Maya Chen (author): Added 'observability.cohorting.enabled' config toggle and doc section for compliance. The toggle disables cohort label emission while keeping internal behavior for on-prem aggregation.

Motivation: Customers and internal SOC reviews called out two gaps for high-assurance tenants: (1) operators and runbooks must be constrained to region-scoped duties (operator cannot act outside their assigned region), and (2) audit records stored for some jurisdictions require PII-obfuscation before leaving the region. This PR implements a policy-level 'operator.scope' assertion for RBAC v2 and a pluggable audit obfuscation writer that applies region-aware masks and removes sensitive fields when required.

What this changes: Implements an attribute-driven entitlement check and audit middleware. Key components: 
- rbac/attribute_assertor.go: new attribute evaluator that checks the caller's operator.scope claim (e.g., "eu-west-1", "us-east-1") against resource locality/route annotations. Supports wildcard scopes ("eu-*") and timebound assertions. 
- authz/policy_compiler.v2: small extension to policy DSL to declare 'operator_scope' enforcement points. Compiler emits an extra decision hook when policies include 'scope: region-bound'. 
- audit/obfuscator/region_policy.yaml: declarative rules for per-region fields to obfuscate (email, phone, ssi, raw_prompt). Rules are overridable by tenant flags. 
- audit/writers/obfuscating_writer.go: middleware writer that inspects request metadata (tenant region, kms_key_location) and applies the obfuscation pipeline before handing logs to the storage backend. Supports streaming and batch modes used by the hosted ingestion path. 
- kms/residency_enforcer.go: lightweight check that ensures the CMK referenced in request headers matches the tenant region assertion before allowing write operations; integrates with attribute_assertor and returns structured audit annotations on mismatch. 
- tests/*: unit and integration tests covering assertion evaluation, wildcard matching, obfuscation rules, and failure modes (deny + audit annotation). 

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind 'operator_scope_enforcement' and 'region_audit_obfuscation' runtime flags. Default off for existing tenants. Gradual rollout: enable for internal test tenants, then pilot with 3 EU customers for 2 weeks, followed by org-wide opt-in for tenants with data_residency requirement. 

Backward compatibility and migration: The policy DSL extension is additive; policies without 'scope:' behave as before. Existing audit writers remain available; this PR wires the obfuscating writer as an option behind the feature flag. Derived audit indices and downstream pipelines must be verified by the observability team before wide rollout. 

Testing notes: Ran the internal compliance harness (SEC-211) and the region end-to-end suite. Simulated operator tokens with differing operator.scope claims and verified expected allow/deny decisions and annotated audit entries. Performed a failure-mode test where KMS region mismatches are logged as 'kms_residency_violation' with masking applied and the write rejected. 

Security considerations: Obfuscation uses deterministic hashing for identity fields with tenant-specific salt stored in KMS-protected secret. Never stores raw PII in long-term logs for protected regions. The enforcement path returns structured audit metadata (non-PII) for debugging in the control plane. 

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests for attribute_assertor and obfuscating_writer 
- [x] Integration test for KMS residency enforcement 
- [x] Feature flags added and documented in ops/flags.md 
- [x] Release note drafted for compliance channel 
- [x] Reviewed by security and privacy teams

Commits summary: 
- feat(rbac): add operator.scope attribute evaluator and tests 
- feat(audit): add obfuscating writer and region policy config 
- feat(kms): residency enforcer sync with attribute_assertor 
- docs: ops flags and rollout notes 
- test: e2e for region-bound operator flows

Changed files (high level): 
- rbac/attribute_assertor.go 
- authz/policy_compiler.go 
- audit/writers/obfuscating_writer.go 
- audit/obfuscator/region_policy.yaml 
- kms/residency_enforcer.go 
- ops/flags.md 
- pkg/telemetry/audit_annotations.go 
- tests/rbac/operator_scope_test.go 
- tests/audit/obfuscation_integration_test.go 

Related work: This complements ENG-2982 (policy instrumentation) and reuses the key-claim wiring from ENG-2711. It is a smaller-surface alternative to earlier geo-fencing proposals, focusing on operator-scoped assertions rather than global routing changes.

Release notes: Adds operator-scoped RBAC v2 assertions and an optional region-aware audit obfuscation writer. Feature is off by default and must be enabled via runtime flags. See compliance/notes/region-obfuscation.md for tenant onboarding steps.

Priya Menon (author): Added wildcard tests in tests/rbac/operator_scope_test.go. For obfuscation failures we log an audit_annotation and reject the write for protected regions; added comment explaining this is required by policy (privacy-first), but the behavior is behind a flag and can be relaxed in emergency by ops.
