Context: The new internal Unit Economics dashboard surfaces sensitive cost data (blended $/1M output tokens, drilldowns by model/region/tier). We need to ensure access is restricted to a small internal allowlist initially and that all access is auditable for Finance and Security sign-off. This PR adds (1) a server-side feature flag gate and (2) RBAC policy updates + enforcement in the Console backend so that the Unit Economics endpoints and UI route are not reachable unless explicitly granted. Changes: - Feature flag: add `console.internal_unit_economics_dashboard` (server-side, env-scoped). Default OFF in all environments; can be enabled in prod only for the internal allowlist group. - RBAC: introduce permission `console:unit_economics:read` and require it for all unit economics API endpoints + the console route loader. - Enforcement points: apply gating at the HTTP router layer and again at the service layer (defense-in-depth) so future endpoints don’t accidentally bypass checks. - Audit logging: emit an audit event on successful access and on denied access (includes actor, org, reason: missing_flag vs missing_permission). - Admin tooling: add a small helper to map the initial allowlist group to the permission for dogfood rollout. Notes: - The UI still renders behind the flag, but if the backend gate denies access, the page shows the standard “Permission denied” state (UI work in PR-19378). - This intentionally does not add any customer-level permissions; v1 is internal-only (no customer exposure). Testing: unit tests cover flag off -> 404/403 behavior, permission missing -> 403, both enabled -> success, and audit event emission. Follow-ups: - Once Finance signs off on metric definitions, we can expand the allowlist and/or move to role-based groups (Finance, Platform Eng, SRE) instead of named individuals. - Consider adding a “redacted mode” for broader internal visibility if needed (out of v1 scope).
Marcus Lin (Security): Can we make this deny-by-default even if the UI route is hit directly? I’d prefer the backend returns 404 (not found) when the feature flag is off to avoid hinting the endpoint exists. Also want an audit event for denied attempts (flag off / permission missing) so we can track accidental exposure attempts. Kaitlyn Nguyen (Author): Updated. Router now returns 404 when flag is off; permission missing still 403. Added audit events for both denied cases with a `deny_reason` field. Chloe Martin: Please ensure we’re checking both flag and permission on every endpoint, not just the top-level route. We’ve had regressions where new drilldown endpoints forgot authz. Kaitlyn Nguyen (Author): Added `requireUnitEconAccess()` helper and applied to all unit economics routes; also added a service-layer assertion so even if a route forgets the middleware, it fails closed. Added a test that enumerates the router paths and validates the middleware is attached. Sean Gallagher (SRE): The audit log volume might be high if people bookmark the page; make sure denied access is sampled or at least not going to page oncall. Kaitlyn Nguyen (Author): Denied audit events are logged at INFO (not alerting) and rate-limited per actor/org (60/min). Successful access logs at INFO once per session (24h) to reduce noise. Allison Grant: Can we include the feature flag state in the response headers for debugging? Kaitlyn Nguyen (Author): Added `x-rw-unit-econ-flag: on|off` and `x-rw-unit-econ-permission: allowed|denied` headers only for internal staff requests (employee SSO), not for external traffic. Marcus Lin: Approved with the header restriction; thanks. Chloe Martin: Approved. Dylan Brooks: Looks good; aligns with rollout plan. Merge it once CI is green.
Merged via squash into `main` after approvals from Security + Console Eng; rollout behind flag remains OFF by default. Enabling in prod will be done via internal change management once Finance confirms allowlist (tracked in PM-487).
Internal-only: Unit Economics dashboard is now gated behind a server-side feature flag and RBAC permission; access is deny-by-default and audited.

Motivation: continuous-batcher tail latency instability has been observed under mixed KV-heavy workloads where long-lived, cache-pin-heavy requests block slot reuse and cause starvation for small low-latency requests; this PR introduces a slot-watchdog mechanism that bounds per-slot hold time, adapts admission priorities, and surfaces kernel hints to reduce preemption cost. Design summary: 1) slot_watchdog tracks an approximate per-slot timestamp and enforced soft_deadline which is jittered to avoid synchronized expiries; when a slot's soft_deadline is exceeded we switch the request to a hedged admission path or preemption-friendly kernel path instead of a hard kill; 2) admission reshaper: a lightweight token-bucket is placed in front of the batcher admission queue to smooth bursts and preserve proportional fairness across request classes (small/short, medium, KV-heavy); 3) kv_pin_lifetime extension policy: long-running KV-pinned requests can be voluntarily demoted to a pinned-cache-hint mode which reduces pinned set inflation while maintaining hit-rate for warm prefixes; 4) kernel-hint API: the runtime exposes a hint to the lower-level exec engine allowing it to select a lower-latency memory access kernel when preemption is imminent. Implementation notes: new files add slot_watchdog.cc/h and slot_watchdog_metrics.cc, small admission reshaper in admission/token_bucket.cc, kv_pin_manager adjustments, tests and a perf harness that drives mixed traffic. Backwards compatibility: feature gated behind runtime config flag "slot_watchdog.enabled" default=false in this change so rollout can be toggled per-cluster. Benchmarks: on the 8-GPU p99 P95 test we see 28% p99 reduction for small requests under KV-heavy background load and 12% lower mean latency; tail variance reduced by ~35%; cost impact measured negligible due to adaptive demotion. Safety and degradation paths: when disabled the behavior is unchanged; rollout plan uses canary cohort then global flip. Ops: new console dashboard (batcher.slot_watchdog.* metrics) added for debugging and Sentry tags for preemption events. Related: references ENG-4219 (investigation) and ENG-4280 (admission reshaper exploration). Rollback: set slot_watchdog.enabled=false and revert canary if regressions in throughput are observed. Testing: unit tests for deadline logic and integration perf harness included. CI notes: unstable test fixed by increasing simulation horizon and adding deterministic jitter seed. See changed_files for details.
Maya Chen: Nice approach; can you clarify the invariants of the soft_deadline vs hard timeout? I want to ensure we don't leak pinned state when a slot is demoted.
Noah Ramirez: The soft_deadline only triggers a mode change (demotion or kernel hint) and does not unpin; pinned entries are aged by the kv_pin_manager demotion routine which is run asynchronously. Hard timeouts still exist and are only used as last-resort safety nets.
Liam O'Connor: Please add a microbenchmark that simulates preemption cost of the hint path vs full preemption so we can justify the extra branch.
Noah Ramirez: Added mixed_kv_tail_test and included the preemption microbenchmark results in the PR description; numbers show <3% throughput delta for hint-path vs baseline with much improved p99.
Priya Desai: We should expose the token-bucket parameters in the console as a hidden advanced config so SRE can tune on-call without redeploys.
Noah Ramirez: Exposed token_bucket.rate and token_bucket.burst in the runtime config and added console UI hook; documented in docs/ops/continuous-batcher-tuning.md.
Ethan Park: CI flake on the jittered deadline test; looks nondeterministic in presubmit. Recommend seeding RNG in test harness.
Noah Ramirez: Fixed by deterministic_seed for test harness; updated test to assert stable ordering.
Introduce slot-watchdog for continuous batcher: reduces p99 tail latency under mixed KV workloads by bounding slot hold times and adaptive demotion; adds admission token-bucket for smoother fairness; feature off by default and gated via runtime flag.
payload.title: slot-watchdog: latency stabilizer and starvation protection for continuous batcher

payload.body:
Motivation: existing seqlen bucketing approaches reduce padding but can create hard bin boundaries that underutilize batch capacity when workloads have heavy-tail length distributions or bursty short/long mixes. This PR introduces a 'spillover' batching heuristic that treats buckets as soft-capacity containers: short sequences preferentially join short-length buckets, but when a bucket is near capacity we allow low-cost spillover into adjacent buckets if the incremental padding cost is below a computed threshold. The goal is to reduce wasted token work while keeping per-request latency SLOs stable. Key changes: 1) Soft-capacity buckets: each bucket has a target capacity and a spill tolerance ratio. If accepting an extra request increases total padded-tokens by less than tolerance*expected_gain, the scheduler will allow spillover. 2) Padding-cost estimator: a lightweight estimator that computes incremental padded tokens for merging two sequences into a bucket; uses sequence length histogram + recent-runtime kernel efficiency model to convert padded tokens into an expected GPU-time cost (so we account for kernel selection and sequence-length-specific kernel scaling). 3) Kernel-aware routing: the runtime now tags candidate batches with preferred kernel flavor (fp16/quantized/packed attention) based on the highest-common-capability of included sequences; the scheduler prefers batch compositions that map to a single efficient kernel instead of mixing incompatible sequences. 4) KV-cache affinity hinting: when a request has a warm KV-cache (prefix match), it gets an affinity score that biases the scheduler to group it with others sharing the prefix to reuse KV memory and reduce duplicate KV loads. 5) Partial-flush thresholds for continuous batching: introduces a sliding flush threshold that permits earlier flushes for buckets with high variance to avoid p95 spikes while still allowing longer accumulation for low-variance buckets. 6) Config flags and observability controls: new runtime flags (spillover_enabled, spill_tolerance, kernel_affinity_weight, kv_affinity_weight, bucket_flush_sensitivity) and metrics (spillovers/second, padded_tokens_saved, kernel_switch_penalties, kv_affinity_hits). Implementation notes: this change touches the batcher, scheduler, and the kernel selection contract but keeps the public API unchanged. The algorithm is conservative by default (spillover_enabled=false) and gated behind a feature flag. Testing: unit tests for the padding estimator and bucket scoring, integration tests that simulate mixed-length workloads with mock kernels, and end-to-end CI runs on a small GPU harness. Performance: in internal perf lab tests on g4dn.12xlarge with a mixed workload (40% <64, 40% 64-512, 20% >512) we observed a 12.7% mean throughput increase and a 9.3% reduction in padded tokens for steady-state traffic; p95 latency improved by 6ms in steady-state and remained within SLO under burst scenarios. Rollout plan: feature gated + gradual rollout on Dedicated clusters: Canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback on increased p95 or error rate. Backcompat: scheduler config is additive; no customer-facing changes unless flags are enabled. Follow-ups: 1) tune spill tolerance per model using Optimize heuristics, 2) expose a per-deployment dashboard for spillover metrics, 3) explore machine-learned cost model to replace the current estimator.
Ethan Park: Overall looks solid; main concern is the cost-estimator accuracy under quantized kernels — can we add a calibration job?
Author (Priya): Added calibration harness in benchmarks/ci and a follow-up entry in the PR description; estimator exposes a calibration hook.
María Gonzalez: Suggest lowering default spill_tolerance to 0.05 for canary; also please add metrics for spillover-caused kernel switches.
Author (Priya): Set default to 0.05 and added kernel_switch_penalties metric, updated tests to assert the metric emits on switches.
Leo Zhang: KV affinity looks promising; risk is memory churn if we co-locate very large prefix caches. Can we cap affinity bonus by KV memory impact?
Author (Priya): Added kv_affinity_memory_penalty and unit tests that simulate large prefix cache scenarios; kept conservative defaults.
Squashed and merged after approval from reviewers and CI green. Feature is behind a default-off flag and will be rolled out to Dedicated via canary as described in the PR. Changelog entry added.
Introduce an opt-in spillover batcher that reduces padding and improves throughput for mixed-length workloads. Default disabled; enable via runtime flag 'spillover_enabled'.
payload.title: Seqlen spillover batcher: soft-capacity bucketing and padding-aware scheduling

Context: production teams are seeing noisy SLO alerts driven by rare high-cost tokens and prompt-shape oscillations. This PR introduces a two-piece observability feature: 1) alert anchoring — a policy layer that computes per-route, per-tenant baseline windows and suggests threshold adjustments (and can apply auto-proposals for SRE review); and 2) fidelity_shepherd — a small continuous analyzer that monitors token-level fidelity metrics (token_fidelity_score) and surfaces correlated cost/latency drift with a suggested mitigation (canary rollback, increase batching, or quantize model variant).

What changed (high level):
- telemetry: emit token_fidelity_score (0..1) on invocation spans and as a structured log field when available; add token_cost_component tag to span (cpu,gpu,kv_cache).
- fidelity_shepherd service: new microservice in telemetry/ with a simple rule engine that identifies drift windows, computes anchor candidates, and writes proposals to an Anchors API. Runs with low QPS and has a safe read-only mode.
- alert anchoring: added a controller that reads anchor proposals and pairs them with existing SLO rules, exposing an interactive suggestion in the Observability Console.
- dashboards: new dashboard panels (fidelity sparkline, anchored-threshold overlay, drift heatmap) and a compact explainer panel for suggested actions.
- tests: unit tests + integration test harness simulating token-fidelity regressions.

Checklist (checked):
- [x] Emit token_fidelity_score in traces and structured logs (opt-in config flag: telemetry.emit_token_fidelity).
- [x] fidelity_shepherd service with metrics and health endpoints.
- [x] Anchors API and UI panel in console (read-only by default).
- [x] Prometheus recording rules for anchor metrics and Grafana dashboard JSON.
- [x] E2E test that simulates fidelity drop and verifies proposal creation.
- [x] Documentation draft and runbook entries included.

Commits (summary):
- add: token_fidelity_score field to tracer instrumentation (sdk/python and runtime instrumenter).
- feat: fidelity_shepherd service + rule engine + health checks.
- feat: alert anchoring controller + Anchors API.
- ui: console panels for fidelity sparkline and anchoring suggestions.
- infra: recording rules + alertmanager template for anchored alerts.
- test: e2e fidelity regression test harness.

Files changed (selected):
- telemetry/fidelity_shepherd/main.go (new) — shepherd service with rule engine and proposal writer.
- telemetry/proposals/api.go (new) — Anchors API (read/write for proposals, currently RBAC-protected).
- runtime/instrumentation/token_tags.go — emits token_fidelity_score and token_cost_component.
- sdk/python/redwood/telemetry.py — optional helper to compute token_fidelity_score on-client prompt quality hooks.
- console/dashboards/fidelity_sparkline.json — dashboard panels and templated variables.

- tests/e2e/fidelity_proposal_test.go — integrates shepherd with telemetry simulator.
- docs/observability/fidelity_shepherd.md — design and runbook.

Testing and CI: initial CI run failed with lint on console JSON (naming convention). Fixes applied in second commit; full CI passed (unit tests, integration harness, lint). Prometheus rules validated with promtool. Load test of fidelity_shepherd done in staging with synthetic traces at 50rps for 20 minutes — shepherd CPU < 1 vCPU and memory stable.

Rollout plan:
- Merge to main behind feature flag (observability.feature_fidelity_shepherd).
- Enable telemetry.emit_token_fidelity default=false; dev tenants opt-in.
- Stage shepherd as read-only and surface UI suggestions to SREs. After 2 weeks of stable data, enable auto-proposals in a canary subset.

Migration notes:
- No db migrations. Anchors API uses existing proposals store (append-only). If telemetry.emit_token_fidelity=false no extra tags are emitted. Older traces remain compatible.

Review conversation (high-level excerpt):
- Asha Patel (reviewer): "Nice end-to-end. Two asks: (1) can the shepherd back off aggressively under high cardinality tenants? (2) please ensure the Anchors API has RBAC checks so only SRE/service owners can apply auto-proposals."
- Author reply (Sofia): "(1) shepherd has tenant backoff rules and a per-tenant sampling cap (configurable). I added unit tests demonstrating backoff. (2) Anchors API enforces RBAC via existing auth middleware; added test coverage."
- Liam O'Connor: "Dashboard looks good; minor comment on color contrast for the heatmap. Also suggest calling out expected cost of running shepherd in the runbook."
- Sofia: "Adjusted palette and added staging cost estimate to runbook (approx. $0.12/hr at 50rps in staging)."
- Marcus Chen: "Left a nit on naming in telemetry tags (token_cost_component -> token_cost_source). I kept current name for now to match historical code; added compatibility mapping in the tracer to accept both tags."
- Marcus (approval): "Looks good after fixes."

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after all approvals and passing CI. Release notes added to the changelog and docs updated. Console feature gated behind observability.feature_fidelity_shepherd and telemetry.emit_token_fidelity.

Why this is different: Anchoring ties alert thresholds to real fidelity baselines (not just token counts or raw percentiles) and provides human-readable proposals rather than automatic threshold changes; fidelity_shepherd focuses on surfacing cause (e.g., prompt-shape drift, model variant changes) with low-cost continuous sampling. This complements existing token-cost and latency telemetry by adding a quality-aware observability layer.
Adds an adaptive alert anchoring component that ties alert thresholds to token-fidelity baselines, a lightweight fidelity_shepherd service for per-route drift detection and recommendations, new dashboard panels (fidelity sparkline, anchoring suggestions), and instrumentation to emit token_fidelity_score for traces and logs. Backwards-compatible; runtime emits additional optional tags.
Asha: Can shepherd back off aggressively under high-cardinality tenants? Added backoff tests.
Liam: Dashboard color contrast nit and staging cost ask — fixed and documented.
Marcus: Naming nit for token_cost_component -> kept for compatibility and added mapping.

payload.body:
Motivation: We are seeing two recurring problems in production telemetry: (1) invocation logs frequently contain high-cardinality or sensitive fields that increase storage cost and complicate searches, and (2) rare long-tail invocations contribute disproportionate token cost noise which destabilizes alerting and SLOs. This PR introduces an adaptive, tenant-aware log sanitizer and a span-key indexer that together reduce telemetry cardinality, protect PII, and enable fast lookups for heavy-cost invocations. Design summary: - LogSanitizer: a pipeline stage that applies tenant-configurable masking rules (regex + allowlist), numeric bucketing for high-cardinality IDs, and an optional stable signature hash for invocation identity (salted per-tenant with rotation support). The sanitizer emits metrics (sanitizer.masked, sanitizer.dropped, sanitizer.signature_assigned) to track effectiveness. - Token-weighted reservoir sampler: a lightweight sampler that prefers sampling invocations with higher estimated token-cost (configurable weight function). This keeps a small, high-signal trace corpus for debugging cost/quality regressions without exploding storage. Emits sampler.token_weight_total and sampler.sampled_count. - SpanKeyIndexer: a compact index of synthesized span keys (stable low-cardinality identifiers derived from span edge patterns). Implemented as an LSM-backed shard with bloom-filter quick checks, optimized for append-heavy workloads and low-memory tail. Exposes a query API for the Invocation Explorer dashboard. - Dashboard + alerts: new dashboard (Observability / Invocation Explorer) with panels for per-invocation token cost breakdown, model-stage latency waterfall, and sampled trace links. Alert tuning changes: the token-cost spike alert now uses a decayed baseline and an adaptive dampener keyed by invocation_signature to reduce noisy duplicates. Backwards compatibility: sanitizer defaults are conservative and off by default per-tenant; sampling and indexing are opt-in. Migration/rollout: gradual rollout by tenant flag with canary telemetry enabled. Checklist: - [x] core sanitizer implementation and unit tests - [x] span-key indexer and index query API - [x] token-weighted sampler + integration tests - [x] dashboard JSON + panels - [x] docs: docs/observability/adaptive-sampling.md - [x] perf bench: small load test showing <5% additional CPU at 1000 rps - [x] security review by SRE (SRE-404) Testing: local unit and integration tests, e2e with synthetic high-cardinality payloads, manual canary verification on staging for 3 tenants. Monitoring: added metrics and traced slow paths; main SLOs to watch during rollout are telemetry-ingest-latency, sanitizer.cpu_percent, sampler.sampled_rate, and spanindex.write_latency. Related: builds on earlier work in ENG-1879 around token attribution. This PR intentionally does not change public generation APIs; it focuses on server-side telemetry and observability.
Adds a privacy-aware log sanitizer, token-weighted sampling for traces, and a span-key indexer + new dashboard panels for per-invocation cost/latency breakdowns. No customer-facing API changes.
Alexei: Great work. Two nits: use sync.Pool for temporary buffers in scrubber to reduce GC pressure; and please add a knob to fully disable signature hashing per-tenant.
Maya (author): Added sync.Pool and tenant-level feature flag. Also exposed rotate_salt endpoint for ops. PTAL.
Priya: Could we add a safety limit to the span index shard size? If an attacker floods with synthetic span patterns we can OOM. Suggest shard-level eviction and a hard cap.
Maya: Added LRU-style compaction with configurable shard_max_segments; included metrics for eviction.count.
Jordan: Verified integration tests and approved. Noted one flake in e2e that was due to jitter; marked as flake and reran CI.
Alexei: Approving after addressing buffer reuse and adding documentation on privacy knobs.
Release Manager: Chose squash merge to keep history compact. Deployed to staging canaries 2/19, full rollout complete 2/22.

Motivation: A recent internal incident showed a risky pattern where a large RBAC policy rollback (mass deny) could be applied by accident during fast rollouts. At the same time we need better visibility into KMS usage at the operator and service level for billing and compliance, and a compact residency-decision auditor to help debug residency pinning decisions. This PR introduces three coordinated changes: 1) RBAC rollback-safety compiler pass that detects and blocks high-impact policy diffs unless an explicit multi-approver override is present; 2) lightweight KMS usage metrics exporter for the control plane (per-tenant, per-key/provider counters and sampled latencies); 3) residency-decision auditor that samples decision traces, attaches a signed lightweight proof (claim + decision hash) to the audit envelope, and emits an audit event for offline replay.
Adds an RBAC rollback-safety compiler pass (prevents large accidental denies), KMS usage telemetry for billing/audit, and a sampled residency-decision auditor that attaches proof metadata to audit logs. No user-facing API changes.
a1b2c3d: rbac/compiler: add rollback_safety pass that computes impact ratio and requires multi-approver override
b2c3d4e: controlplane/metrics: add kms_usage exporter (kmssvc.kms_requests_total, kmssvc.kms_request_latency_seconds)
c3d4e5f: audit/residency: add decision sampler and proof encoder (compact signed claim)
d4e5f6a: tests: unit + integration tests for rollback safety, metrics labels, and residency proof roundtrip
e5f6a7b: docs: extend RBAC changelog with rollout guidance and add observability page for kms_usage metrics
Miguel Ortega (reviewer): Requested a clearer failure mode in the CLI — don't block, but mark the change as "high-impact" and require 2 approvals for automated merges. Also asked for unit tests around empty-policy edge case.
Author (Aisha): Implemented — CLI now annotates high-impact PRs and pipeline will fail automated merge until approvals are present; added unit tests for empty-policy and no-op diffs in rbac/compiler tests.
Samantha Klein (reviewer): Asked to ensure KMS exporter labels include provider and tenant_id and to avoid cardinality explosion. Suggested using an optional dimension set for top-level tenants only.
Author (Aisha): Updated exporter to emit provider and tenant_id as labels only for aggregated metrics; per-key counters are bucketed by key_type (CMK/DEK) to limit cardinality. Added a note in docs about label cardinality and best practices.
Leon Wu (reviewer): Called out that residency proofs need crypto housekeeping; requested a rotation strategy for the proof signer keys and a fallback when signing fails.
Author (Aisha): Added key rotation hooks to proof_signer and an opt-out: when signing fails we still emit an unsigned decision with `proof_present=false` in the audit envelope and surface an internal alert. Tests added to simulate signer failure.
QA (comment): Flaky e2e initially due to test clock drift; fixed by using monotonic timers in tests. CI rerun passed.
Feature is guarded behind two runtime flags: --rbac-rollback-safety (enabled by default for control plane) and --residency-audit-sampler (default sample rate = 0.01). KMS metrics endpoint is wired into the control-plane metrics stack and is safe for 10k TPS control-plane load due to internal aggregation. Operators should monitor `rbac.rollback_high_impact_detected_total` and `kmssvc.kms_requests_total` when enabling in prod. Backport PR for release branch will flip the rollout-safety to opt-in until ops completes a manual audit run.
Unit tests: added 18 new tests covering impact calculation, approvals gating, proof signing and signer-failure fallback. Integration tests: e2e simulating a staged policy rollback with approval flow; metrics smoke test for label cardinality. Load validation: local perf run (control plane) at simulated 5k req/s to validate metrics aggregation. QA notes included in the PR checklist.

payload.body:
- Adds release notes for new prefix/KV cache telemetry metrics (hit-rate, miss reasons, evictions/pressure, wasted prefill) and trace annotations.
- Documents feature flags + sampling knobs for safe rollout.
- Calls out early-rollout limitations (cardinality allowlists, sampling effects, model/version pinning impacts) and links to dashboards/runbook.
## Summary
This PR updates the runtime release notes to document the new prefix/KV cache telemetry landing in this train, including:
- What new metrics exist and how to interpret them at a high level
- The config/feature flags required to enable the new signals safely
- Known limitations / caveats for the first production rollout

This is intended to reduce confusion during staged enablement (staging -> canary -> prod) and to make it clear which dashboards/alerts are expected to move when these flags are flipped.

## Context
Cache telemetry work has been landing across multiple PRs (counters, histograms, miss reasons, evictions/pressure, wasted prefill, sampling/guards, trace annotations, naming reconciliation). We’ve had multiple internal questions during canary setup about:
- whether hit-rate is expected to move immediately (and how sampling affects it)
- what labels should/shouldn’t be present (cardinality allowlists)
- what counts as a miss (e.g., version mismatch vs policy disabled)

This PR centralizes those notes in release notes so operators don’t have to piece it together from Slack threads.

## What’s included in the release notes
### New cache telemetry (high-level)
- KV cache hit/miss counters and derived hit-rate
- Prefix cache reuse histograms (reused token depth / reused tokens)
- Miss reason breakdown (capacity, ttl_expired, policy_disabled, hash_mismatch, version_mismatch)
- Eviction counts + eviction reason taxonomy, plus memory pressure indicators
- Wasted prefill (prefill tokens that did not contribute to subsequent decode due to misses/evictions)
- Trace span annotations for cache events (to correlate cache behavior with request latency without high-cardinality metrics)

### Flags / knobs (documented with defaults + rollout guidance)
- `runtime.cache_telemetry.enabled` (default: false in prod at time of this release; true in staging)
- `runtime.cache_telemetry.metrics_sampling_rate` (default: 0.05 in prod when enabled; 1.0 in staging)
- `runtime.cache_telemetry.event_rate_limit_per_sec` (protects against bursts on high-QPS routes)
- `runtime.cache_telemetry.labels_allowlist` (explicitly calls out that per-tenant / per-request labels are not emitted)
- `runtime.cache_telemetry.emit_trace_annotations` (default: true when tracing enabled; independent sampling)

### Known limitations / caveats (first rollout)
- Sampling: hit-rate should be stable in expectation, but low-volume routes will look noisy; guidance included for minimum traffic thresholds before acting on changes.
- Cardinality controls: some dimensions are intentionally bucketed/normalized (prompt-length buckets / token bins) and some are dropped at ingestion if misconfigured; notes include symptoms (e.g., “zero hits” due to label-drop) and where to look.
- Model/version rollouts: version mismatch misses can spike during canaries or when mixing versions across pools; recommendation is to verify routing/pinning policy when investigating sudden cost increases.
- Streaming retries: release notes point to the semantic change that retries should not double-count hits/misses once the retry-fix is present in this train.
- Continuous batching: notes clarify that hit attribution is per-request (not per-batch) and that extremely short prompts can show counter-intuitive reuse distributions.

### Pointers to operational docs
- Dashboards: Cache hit-rate + eviction pressure + wasted prefill
- Runbook: “Cache telemetry pipeline incident runbook” (what to do if metrics stop flowing / show zeros)

## Files changed
- `docs/release-notes/runtime/2025-03-xx.md`
  - Adds a “Cache telemetry (prefix/KV)” section with the above details
- `docs/ops/feature-flags.md`
  - Adds cache telemetry flags and short descriptions
- `docs/observability/metric-names.md`
  - Adds links to the canonical cache metric names and label policy

## Example snippet (as added)
Added to the runtime release note section:
"Cache telemetry is behind a feature flag. When enabled, expect new `cache.*` metrics to appear within ~5 minutes. Hit-rate and reuse histograms are sampled by default in production to limit overhead and cardinality. Investigate sudden hit-rate drops by first checking miss reason breakdown (version_mismatch, policy_disabled, capacity) and eviction pressure before adjusting cache knobs."

## Testing
- Doc-only changes.
- Verified links resolve in internal docs preview.

## Rollout notes
- Release notes explicitly state: do not flip `runtime.cache_telemetry.enabled` globally without confirming ingestion-side cardinality guards are deployed for the target region.

## Related
- ENG-4821 (definitions/tags)
- ENG-4824 (dashboards/alerts)
- PRs: #18421, #18422, #18423, #18424, #18425, #18426, #18428, #18430, #18431, #18432, #18433, #18434

---

## Conversation highlights
Allison Grant (review): Please add a short “If you see zero hits” troubleshooting note and link to the pipeline incident runbook. We’ve already had one canary where ingestion dropped labels and the dashboard looked flat.

Connor O'Brien (author): Added a troubleshooting callout under limitations + linked the runbook.

Logan Wright (review): Can we be explicit that per-tenant labels are not emitted (and will be dropped if someone tries to add them)? Also call out sampling making low-volume routes noisy.

Connor O'Brien (author): Done — added a “Cardinality + sampling” subsection with concrete symptoms.

Omar El-Sayed (review): Mention version_mismatch misses during rollouts. We saw that in SUP-3912 style investigations and it’s an easy misread as ‘cache broken’.

Connor O'Brien (author): Added a bullet under limitations plus guidance to check routing/pinning.

Sean Gallagher (review): Please avoid telling oncall to page on hit-rate changes; position as guardrail and link to alert policy.

Connor O'Brien (author): Updated wording to “guardrail” and removed paging language; added link to the SRE dashboard/alert policy doc.

Paula Mendes (PM): Looks good. This is sufficient for the MVP rollout; we can refine copy once Console surfaces the recommendations.

- Buildkite / `unit`: PASS (no-op)
- Link checker: PASS

payload.body:
Motivation: The KV cache was showing oscillatory spill behaviour under mixed tenant workloads: hot tenants would momentarily exhaust reservation windows causing aggressive spill followed by immediate refill and repeated churn. This amplified fragmentation and increased tail latency for token-serving requests. This PR introduces a shadow-threshold mechanism with hysteresis and a lightweight predictive spill mitigator that smooths eviction decisions, reduces micro-spill events, and proactively consolidates cold fragments to reduce paging overhead.

Design summary: Implement a shadow reservation vector per tenant that tracks short-term access intensity (exponentially-weighted histogram over 1s/10s/60s windows). Eviction decisions consult both the live occupancy and the shadow vector: when the live occupancy crosses a threshold, the hysteresis band prevents immediate spill unless the shadow signal indicates sustained pressure. The predictive spill mitigator uses the access histogram to rank candidate segments by short-term read/write intensity and expected reclaimability, preferring to consolidate cold segments before spilling hot-but-fragmented segments. We also add an opportunistic micro-consolidation pass that runs inline with normal eviction and is budgeted to the current serving kernel to avoid CPU interference.

Interactions with batching and scheduler: To avoid increasing serving latency, the micro-consolidation work is throttled by a scheduler token bucket that ties its budget to observed continuous-batching latency SLOs. When batching pressure is high (lots of small sequences), consolidation backoff is enforced and we rely on hysteresis to avoid reactive spill storms. The change includes a kernel hint API so the planner can deprioritize consolidation on latency-sensitive kernels and favor it on background kernels.

Implementation notes: - new modules: kv/shadow_reservoir.*, kv/predictive_spill.*, kv/consolidator_worker.* - kept the public eviction API stable; behavior is opt-in via config flags (default enabled in main builds after canary). - metrics: added kv.shadow_pressure, kv.spill_candidates_ranked, kv.consolidation_time_ms (p80/p95). - telemetry tags are tenant-aware for downstream cost attribution.

Testing and validation: single-node microbenchmarks (mix of 80/10/10 hot/warm/cold key distributions) show a 28% reduction in spill events, 18% lower fragmentation score (measured by live-region-coalescence metric), and 7-11% lower 99th-percentile token latency under mixed-tenancy stress compared to baseline. Cluster canary runs (3x machines, region eu-west-1) observed stable tail latencies and no increase in CPU beyond a 3% median. Load tests include synthetic tenant bursts and real-production trace replay for 1 hour.

Risk and rollout plan: staged rollout via feature flag + tenant whitelist. Initial canary in eu-west-1 with 10% traffic, monitor kv.shadow_pressure and spill rates for 48h, then expand. In case of regressions the system falls back to the previous eviction path (config toggle) and aborts consolidation jobs.

Checklist: - [x] design doc linked in Linear (ENG-4512) - [x] unit tests for histogram decay and scoring logic - [x] integration tests with eviction simulation harness - [x] canary run and perf numbers collected - [x] metrics wired to console dashboards

Notes: This is intentionally conservative in CPU usage; consolidation is small and idempotent. Future follow-ups planned: tenant-aware global compaction scheduler and optional background rewriter that operates off-peak to perform larger defragmentation sweeps.
Aisha Patel: architecture looks sound; please clarify thread-safety around the reservoir update path.
Marco Delgado: updated implementation to use atomic snapshots and added comment; new unit tests cover concurrent updates.
Linnea Sørensen: can you add a flag to disable consolidation per-tenant? some customers may want to opt-out.
Marco Delgado: added per-tenant opt-out config and doc note in ops guide.
Thomas Nguyen: ran perf job; initial kv-unit-tests failed due to a timing assumption. Reran and green. Approve.
Aisha Patel: approved after confirming metrics and canary thresholds.
Introduce a shadow-reservation based hysteresis and predictive spill ranking to reduce KV spill churn, lower fragmentation, and smooth eviction behaviour under mixed-tenant workloads. Enabled behind feature flag; opt-out per-tenant. Improves spill event rate and 99p latency in mixed workloads.
Canary microbench: -28% spill events, -18% fragmentation score, 7-11% lower 99p token latency under mixed-tenancy stress. CPU median increase ~+3% during consolidation windows.
Flip feature flag off and drain consolidator worker via graceful shutdown; evictor logic reverts to baseline. Automated rollback script located in deploy/scripts/rollback_kv_shadow.sh
Requires metrics consumer to include new kv.shadow_pressure and kv.consolidation_time_ms. Add config toggles to tenant config template. Can be toggled off via tenant config key: kv.consolidation.enabled=false

payload.body:
Motivation: many tenants exhibit bursty request patterns where cold KV/cache misses and conservative batch sizing cause disproportionate per-token cost spikes. This change introduces a tenant-aware warmstart cost forecaster service and a compact quantization policy layer that together reduce unit economics for peaky workloads while preserving latency SLOs.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a lightweight forecasting service (forecasterd) that consumes tenant request histograms and predicts short-horizon load to proactively seed KV caches and adjust prefill/microbatch windows.
- Introduces a compact quantization policy DSL and a default policy pack that maps workload signatures to conservative quant profiles (int8/int4+gemm knobs) with safety fallbacks.
- Wires the forecaster output into serving runtime heuristics: prefill size, rolling microbatch window, and cache TTL tuning.
- Safety & observability: adds guardrails that prevent warmstart when tail latency budgets are threatened; extensive telemetry for cost delta, latency, cache hit-rate, and quantization-induced model divergence.

Changes included:
- A new service: infra/forecasterd (golang service, small in-memory sliding windows + protobuf API).
- A policy registry and compact DSL under runtime/quant/policies with default tenant mappings.
- Runtime hooks to read forecaster decisions in runtime/allocator and runtime/cache.
- End-to-end e2e integration tests and a smoke runner in infra/ci/prefill-smoke.
- Console and metrics: dashboards and new telemetry metrics (prefill.prediction_accuracy, prefill.cost_delta, quant.policy_applied, forecast.window_size).

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc (ENG-6821) linked
- [x] Unit tests for forecaster logic and DSL parser
- [x] E2E smoke tests for warmstart behavior
- [x] Telemetry and dashboard definitions
- [x] Canary rollout plan documented

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy forecasterd in staging and enable dry-run mode (decisions logged, not applied). Monitor prediction_accuracy and false positive warmstarts for 72h.
2) Canary apply for 5% tenant cohort with conservative defaults (small prefill, TTL 30s, quant fallback to fp16 if divergence > threshold). Monitor prefill.cost_delta and 99p latency.
3) Gradual ramp to 25% after 24h if metrics stable, then 100% with step-down safety triggers.

Operational notes:
- The default policy pack targets inference families (chat, completion, embeddings) and is intentionally conservative for chat workloads.
- Breaking changes: none to public API. Forecaster runs behind feature flag (runtime.feature.warmstart_forecaster).
- Risk: quant policy may increase model drift; mitigation includes sample-based quality checks and automatic rollback if eval loss crosses threshold.

Related: Linear ENG-6821, ENG-7043; discussion thread: internal link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-6821/tenant-warmstart-forecaster

Noah Chen: Can we make the forecaster windowing configurable per-tenant? Author: Yes — added tenant.window_size with global default; we can expose later via Console.
Priya Raman: Quant policies look sensible but add an explicit automatic rollback on eval divergence. Author: Added sample-based eval checks and policy_applied metrics; rollback triggers if sample_loss delta > 2x baseline.
Luca Ferraro: CI flakes in the prefill-smoke on AMD instances. Author: Adjusted smoke runner to skip on AMD until runtime kernel parity is verified.
Noah Chen: Approving after nit fixes. (APPROVED)

payload.body:
Context and motivation:
This PR implements a runtime check that validates a tenant-level KMS residency proof attached to requests that perform cross-region key unwrap/wrap operations. The goal is to provide cryptographic proof (signed assertion) that a CMK is resident in an allowed jurisdiction before the request is allowed to use that key. This complements existing geo-routing and audit pipelines by preventing accidental cross-border crypto operations for tenants with residency constraints.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds a KMS residency proof validator component (pkg/security/residency/validator) that verifies signed proofs against a local trust bundle and returns an enum: VALID | EXPIRED | INVALID | MISSING.
- Introduces new RBAC predicate attributes (rbac.residency_allowed and rbac.residency_denied) and wiring in the policy evaluator to short-circuit evaluates based on residency checks.
- Extends audit logs with a residency_verification field (enum) and a compact proof reference (sha256) instead of embedding entire provenance. Audit records include residency outcome and validator version to enable post-hoc compliance audits without leaking full keys.
- Feature gated behind runtime flag 'residency_proofs' and default-off for older clusters.

Implementation notes / commits summary:
- Commit 1: scaffold residency validator, minimal interface, unit tests for proof parsing and signature verification using mocked trust bundle.
- Commit 2: integrate validator into KMS request admission path (kms/handler.go). Add RBAC predicate hooks to policy evaluator and a small policy compiler update to accept new predicates.
- Commit 3: audit enrichment and logging changes, add end-to-end tests simulating tenant with EU-only residency. Update docs and add a migration note for operators.

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/security/residency/validator.go (new) - implements proof parsing, TTL validation, and signature verification against trust bundle
- pkg/security/residency/validator_test.go (new) - unit tests covering VALID/EXPIRED/INVALID/MISSING cases
- internal/kms/handler.go - wire residency validator into KMS API admission flow (early reject + metrics)
- internal/rbac/predicate.go - add residency predicates and short-circuit logic
- observability/audit/encoder.go - append residency_verification metadata and compact proof reference
- deploy/feature-gates.yaml - add 'residency_proofs' gate and documentation
- docs/security/residency-proofs.md - new operator-facing doc describing proof format, trust bundle rotation, and rollback guidance

Illustrative snippets (small):
- validator.Verify(proofBytes) -> (Outcome, proofRef)
- policy: allow: kms:wrap_key where rbac.residency_allowed == true

Review conversation (highlights, condensed into single thread):
- Leah Kim (reviewer): "This is the right long-term direction. A couple of requests: 1) can we reduce the surface area of the trust bundle API so installers can't accidentally replace it without operator intent? 2) add unit tests for expired proofs with clock skew tolerance."
- Author (Ravi): "Addressed both in commit 2: trust bundle is now provisioned via KMS key manager with an explicit 'trust-bundle' ConfigMap name; added skew tolerance tests (±2m)."
- Anya Sokolov (security): "Please ensure we don't log full proof payloads in any case. The audit encoder looks good but add a unit that asserts sensitive fields are redacted."
- Author: "Added assertions and updated audit encoder to emit only 'proof_ref' and 'validator_version'."
- Diego Martinez (approver): "Verified end-to-end with an EU-only tenant test; performance microbenchmark shows ~0.6ms median overhead on hot-path when proof is cached. Approve pending CI."

CI and flaky runs:
- Initial run: build/presubmit failed on a lint rule (golangci: error on exported doc comment). Fixed in follow-up commit.
- E2E test run: one flaky test in audit-forwarder, rerun passed. Final status: all green.

Operational considerations / rollout plan:
- Feature is behind 'residency_proofs' gate. Operators should enable in canary clusters first. When enabled, the validator will return MISSING for requests without proofs — policy default is to allow, so behavior is non-blocking unless admins explicitly write residency_denied predicates.
- For strict enforcement, customers must: 1) enable feature gate; 2) update RBAC policies to include residency predicates; 3) supply tenant trust bundle via the documented ConfigMap/Secret flow.
- Metrics added: residency_verification_total{outcome=VALID|INVALID|EXPIRED|MISSING} and latency histogram residency_verification_latency_seconds.

Security review notes:
- Signature verification uses tenant-supplied X.509 assertion signed by approved issuers from the trust bundle. Trust bundle rotation is supported and documented.
- We intentionally avoid including full proofs in audit logs to limit exposure. Proof references are sha256(proofBytes) so auditors can request the full proof from the tenant if necessary (out-of-band).

Related work / references:
- ENG-4127: Residency proof design RFC
- SEC-908: KMS geography policy spike
- SUP-2214: Customer ticket for cross-region key usages that motivated this work

Testing performed:
- Unit tests for validator edge cases (malformed, expired, bad signature)
Adds a validator that enforces KMS key residency proofs on tenant-scoped requests and plumbs new RBAC predicates for residency-aware role checks. No behavioral changes by default; feature gated behind 'residency_proofs' feature flag.
Operator docs and a short migration guide are included in docs/security/residency-proofs.md. This PR is intentionally conservative: no enforcement by default and operator-controlled policy required to block requests.
Added KMS residency proof validator and residency-aware RBAC predicates behind a feature gate. Operators must opt-in to enforce residency.

Summary: This PR introduces a canonical tool/function signature normalizer for the OpenAI-compatibility layer and adds fragment-tolerance logic to the streaming framer so interleaved tool output (partial fragments, out-of-order frames, and repeated tool_choice hints) do not corrupt the upstream message envelope.

Motivation: Customers saw flaky behavior when tool_call payloads were split across streaming fragments or when LLMs emitted tool_choice hints multiple times during a response. In practice this manifested as duplicate invocations, truncated schemas, and frequent retries that degraded latency and user experience.

Goals:
1) Normalize incoming tool/function schemas to a predictable internal representation (canonical argument names, explicit optional/required markers, and stable ordering for equality checks).
2) Make the streaming framer idempotent when reassembling tool messages across fragments and robust to duplicated tool_choice tokens.
3) Emit deterministic telemetry and a small migration guide for downstream consumers.

Design:
- Signature normalizer (pkg/compat/openai/signature_normalizer.go) parses OpenAI-style function/tool schema objects and produces a compact canonical form: name, ordered args (name:type:required), and a checksum label used for fast equality checks. The normalizer tolerates synonyms (e.g., "params", "arguments"), coerces primitive JSON Schema variants, and drops non-serializable examples.
- Framer changes (pkg/serving/stream/framer.go): introduce a fragment buffer keyed by request-id + tool-call-id checksum; fragments are validated against the canonical signature before commit. Duplicate tool_choice hints are treated as idempotent votes — the first full message wins, later duplicates are logged but ignored.
- Message envelope tagging: add a light-weight tag on tool output frames (X-Tool-Canon: <checksum>) so downstream routers can match partials to canonical signatures without reparsing full schemas.
- Backwards compatibility: for any input that does not match canonicalization rules, the system falls back to the previous loose-envelope behavior and emits a compatibility metric (compat.signature_fallback).

Migration notes: No client changes required; however customers relying on exact byte-level tool payloads should pin to older SDK versions until they adopt checksum-based matching. The change is gated by a feature flag (compat_tool_normalizer=true) and will be rolled out in canary first.

Testing and observability:
- Unit tests: signature normalizer has exhaustive cases for nullable/optional fields and synonym maps.
- Integration tests: tests/integration/toolcall_replay_test.go simulates out-of-order fragments, duplicate tool_choice emissions, and interleaved non-tool text; all replay cases assert a single invocation and conserved schema.
- Telemetry: new counters (compat.signature_normalized, compat.signature_fallback) and a histogram for fragment_reassembly_latency.

Security: sanitization removes example/snippet fields from canonical payloads before any logs.

Checklist:
- [x] Parser implemented and tested
- [x] Framer accepts partial interleaved fragments
- [x] Telemetry added
- [x] Feature flag implemented
- [x] Docs and migration notes added
- [x] End-to-end test with live streaming harness

Commits summary:
- feat(compat): add signature normalizer and checksum generator
- feat(stream): fragment buffer keyed by request+checksum
- fix(stream): idempotent tool_choice handling on duplicate hints
- perf: avoid reparsing by caching canonical forms for 30s
- docs: note migration and feature-flag behavior

CI notes: initial CI run failed on a flaky integration asserting order; I reworked the test harness to use deterministic clock injection and re-ran. Final CI is green.

Merge strategy: squash and merge after approvals.
Aisha Patel: Can we avoid checksum collisions by including schema version + arg order? Please add a short rationale for the checksum algorithm.
Sofia Martinez: Added schema version as part of the checksum input; included tests for collision simulation.
Marcelo Ortega: The framer buffer keyed by request-id may grow under adversarial streams — consider an eviction policy.
Sofia Martinez: Implemented a TTL eviction and max-buffer-bytes with metrics for evicted entries.
Lina Zhou: Approve after one small nit: move the compat metric name to namespace "compat.v1" to ease future migrations.
feat(compat): add signature normalizer and checksum generator\n\n- add parsing for openai-style function objects\n- canonical form serializer\n- unit tests
feat(stream): fragment buffer keyed by request+checksum\n\n- add in-memory reassembly buffer\n- unit tests for interleaved fragments
fix(stream): idempotent tool_choice handling on duplicate hints\n\n- treat repeated tool_choice as votes\n- update integration test harness
perf: cache canonical forms for 30s
docs(migration): add migration notes and feature flag docs
Improves OpenAI-compat tool/function calling by normalizing tool signatures for deterministic matching and fixes streaming fragment reassembly to tolerate interleaved and duplicated fragments. Adds feature flag and telemetry for rollout.

payload.body:
Motivation: Long, high-cardinality traces make it hard for oncall and SREs to get a quick signal about whether an invocation is a broad systemic issue or a localized expensive callsite. Existing dashboards surface per-route aggregates, but they lack a compact, at-a-glance representation that highlights hot callsites and per-token cost concentration across a single invocation. This PR introduces the 'callchain-minimap' concept: a compact, single-line visual summary for an invocation plus a lightweight backend compactor that produces per-invocation rollups suitable for dashboard sparklines and drilldown.

What this change contains: backend - a dedicated small service (trace-compactor) that subscribes to sampled trace events, builds a compact callchain digest, computes a minimap score (weighted by token-cost and latency), and emits two new metrics (invocation_minimap_score and invocation_compact_digest_id) along with optional sampled log anchors. The compactor uses a reservoir sampler keyed by tenant+route with token-cost and latency weighting to prioritise expensive/slow invocations. UI - a new React component CallchainMinimap that renders a compact SVG timeline and per-phase token-cost sparklines with hover tooltips and a one-click 'open-full-trace' action. Dashboard - a templated panel (Grafana/Chronicle compatible) that shows a sortable list of recent minimap rows for a route, with top-k token contributors.

Compatibility and opt-in: The compactor is behind a runtime feature-flag (telemetry.compactor.enabled=false by default). For Hosted tenants, the feature is off until a rollout window; Dedicated customers can enable via cluster-config. No existing trace schema is mutated; the compactor consumes existing spans and emits derived metrics.

Operational notes: compactor instances are horizontally scalable and memory-bounded (configurable reservoir size, default 1024 per shard). Emitted compact digests are stored in a small Redis-backed cache with 24h TTL by default; the dashboard fetches expanded context on demand to keep storage costs low. Alerts were tuned: a new alert rule minimap_high_entropy_trigger will fire only when minimap_score exceeds 0.85 and the token-cost concentration (top-3 tokens) exceeds 70% for more than 3m to reduce noise.

Why this is different: Instead of shipping heavier sampling or full trace persistence increases, this change introduces a compact, attribution-first signal that surfaces likely root causes quickly and directs engineers to full trace when necessary. It targets the long-tail investigative workflow: rapid scannability, low storage cost, and per-token explainability.

Checklist:
- [x] Backend service and deployment manifests
- [x] Metrics and registry entries
- [x] UI component and dashboard panel template
- [x] Unit and e2e tests for compactor and UI
- [x] Documentation and runbook entry

Related: ENG-6721 (compactor design), ENG-6882 (dashboard UX), PM-421 (product signal prioritization).
Marcus Nguyen: Nice idea — can we make the reservoir sampler deterministic per shard to improve reproducibility during incident replay?
Sofia Patel: Responded that sampler now seeds with shard id + epoch; added unit test to assert deterministic ordering under same inputs.
Elena Gomez: The minimap_score threshold seems aggressive; worried about alert noise at 0.6 for busy tenants.
Sofia Patel: Tuned alert to require both minimap_score > 0.85 and token concentration > 70% for 3m; added smoke tests for the rule.
Ravi Kapoor: backend Redis cache TTL should be configurable via ENV; also request that we emit a telemetry tag for compactor_version.
Sofia Patel: Added REDIS_TTL config and compactor_version tag; updated deployment manifest and docs.
Marcus Nguyen: CI flake on e2e fixed in follow-up commit; approving change.
Elena Gomez: LGTM — approving after small docs nits fixed.
Add compact 'callchain-minimap' trace summary and per-invocation token attribution probe. Opt-in via feature flag; improves triage and reduces full-trace noise for long-tail invocations.

Motivation:
As customers adopt mixed deployment strategies (canary + A/B + shadow), the orchestration layer must support convergent routing where multiple validation modes (shadow verification, staggered A/B slices, and canary traffic) cooperate and automatically trigger safe rewind/rollback when cross-signal regressions appear. This PR introduces the "Convergent Shadow Funnel" controller plus a staged A/B scheduler and an operational rewind playbook to reduce manual intervention during rollouts.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a Convergent Shadow Funnel controller that can consume multiple telemetry anchors (latency, top-k disagreement, hallucination rate, token-level perplexity) and compute a single safety score used by rollout policies.
- Implements a staged A/B scheduler that supports timeboxed slices, entropy seeding to avoid cohort bias, and deterministic replayable slice assignments for reproducible rollbacks/bisects.
- Introduces a Rewind Playbook subsystem: snapshot-backed checkpointing for rollout state, fast-rehearsal mode (replay captured traffic against candidate snapshots), and automated rollback steps with human-notify hooks.
- Extends telemetry schema to include per-cohort drift counters and a lightweight provenance header so promoted requests can be traced back through the funnel.
- Adds unit and integration tests for safety gate logic, and a simulation harness (pkg/simulator) to run stochastic rollouts offline.

Why this approach: 
- Many regressions are multi-signal (slight latency increase + falls in answer-value agreement). By fusing signals into a convergent safety score we reduce false positives while still surfacing compound failures.
- Deterministic slice assignment and snapshotting let us perform reproducible bisects and rehearse candidate rollbacks without touching production traffic.

Design highlights: 
- Safety score is a weighted composite (configurable via rollout policy). Default anchors: latency_p99, payload_disagreement_rate, hallucination_rate, generated_token_entropy_change. Each anchor has an independent threshold and burn-in period.
- The staged A/B scheduler supports progressive slice expansion: initial micro-slices (0.1% cohorts), warmup (1%), validation (5%), ramp (10-50%). Expansion is gated on the safety score and custom metric predicates.
- Shadow fusion accepts multiple model variants and performs lossy sampling for high-throughput workloads (configurable sampling ratio). Shadow traffic is mirrored asynchronously; result diffs are scored and fed back into the funnel.
- Rewind Playbook: on trigger, the controller creates a freeze snapshot (routing table + cohort mapping + model variant pointers), attempts a dry-run rehearse using captured sample traffic, then executes rollback with sticky session preservation. Hooks notify the on-call channel with automatic postmortem starters.

Checklist (what landed):
- [x] Controller: pkg/controller/convergent_funnel_controller.go
- [x] Scheduler: pkg/orchestrator/ab_scheduler.go
- [x] Snapshot & playbook: pkg/playbook/rewind_playbook.go + state snapshots in pkg/state
- [x] Telemetry: telemetry/schema/anchors.proto and telemetry/aggregator adapters
- [x] Simulation harness and smoke scenarios: pkg/simulator/*
- [x] Docs: docs/runbooks/rewind-playbook.md and docs/rollouts/convergent-funnel.md
- [x] Tests: unit + integration + simulation scenarios

Testing and validation notes: 
- Ran sim harness with 10k synthetic sessions for 50 random seeds; median safety false-positive < 1.2% for default thresholds.
- Staging deploy validated with a live shadow run across two canary cohorts; observed expected scoring behavior and deterministic replayable slices.
- Perf bench shows additional ~2% CPU overhead on routing path for mirrored requests when sampling ratio=1.0; recommended default sampling=0.25 for production.

Migration notes: 
- The rollout policy schema is backward compatible. New anchors are opt-in; existing policies keep previous behavior unless updated.
- Customers using custom rollout tooling that rely on raw mirror payloads may need to adapt to the new provenance header. Migration docs included.

Operational playbook (short):
1) If safety score crosses threshold, controller pauses expansion and emits an incident with snapshot ID.
2) Run "rw rehearse <snapshot-id>" in staging using captured traffic from the snapshot; compare safety score deltas.
3) If rehearsals confirm regression, run "rw rollback <snapshot-id> --preserve-sessions" which applies snapshot routing and backs out head pointers.
4) Post-rollback: schedule bisect using deterministic slice seed from snapshot metadata.

Related: ENG-3241 (convergent rollouts), PM-842 (telemetry anchors), SUP-1182 (customer incident that motivated deterministic replay).

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus on safety score semantics and default weightings in config/defaults.go; weight choices are conservative but we should validate at scale.
- Scheduler expansion windows are intentionally conservative; we can tune based on telemetry after launch.
- Performance knobs for shadow sampling are in orchestration config; recommended production defaults are documented in docs/rollouts/convergent-funnel.md.

Require approvals from SRE and Reliability before merge.

Ajay Menon: Can we expose individual anchor deltas in the dashboard? Also requested stronger unit tests for the p99 latency anchor - addressed in follow-up commit
Claire Liu: Concern about deterministic slice seeding collisions across parallel rollouts; suggested a namespace prefix. Author replied: added deterministic prefixing and tests.
Diego Ramos: Asked for failure-mode diagrams in docs and clarified session-preservation semantics; docs updated.
CI Bot: integration tests flaky on first run, retriggered by Marina, second run passed
Ajay Menon: Approved after small nits fixed
Claire Liu: Approved
Diego Ramos: Approved with follow-up ticket created for telemetry dashboarding

Summary: This PR adds an 'operator endorsement' layer to RBAC v2 that lets operator-scoped actions require an endorsement token (short-lived attestation) before sensitive KMS operations or cross-region resource bindings proceed. It also introduces a region-pin assertor middleware that canonicalizes claimed region headers and produces a provenance token consumed by downstream KMS-routing, and an access-provenance bridge that ties RBAC decisions to audit entries for traceable post-hoc review.
Motivation: We observed ambiguity when operator sessions performed elevated actions across tenants/regions which made post-incident forensics difficult. Existing RBACv2 allowed operator roles but lacked an endorsement handshake and a standard provenance artifact to correlate with KMS usage and audit logs. This PR aims to reduce blast radius, make policy decisions auditable, and enable conservative rollouts of region-pin enforcement.
Design highlights:
- operator endorsement: a new claim on operator sessions (endorsement_id) that must be presented when the scope crosses a guarded resource. Endorsements are minted by the operator-endorser service after policy checks and MFA confirmation; the runtime validates the endorsement signature and TTL.
- region-pin assertor middleware: intercepts inbound requests, normalizes region headers (X-Redwood-Claimed-Region), looks up tenant residency policy, emits X-Redwood-Region-Proof token (HMACed with service key) and attaches a human-readable reason in X-Redwood-Region-Note for observability.
- KMS-consent cache hooks: runtime now consults a small in-memory consent cache (LRU) to short-circuit repeated consent checks for the same (tenant, operator, key) tuple for a configurable window. Misses invoke existing KMS consent flow.
- access-provenance bridge: audit writer now includes a provenance blob (base64 JSON) with rbac_decision, endorsement_id, region_proof, and route_fingerprint. This enables downstream auditors to verify which endorsement authorized an operation and which KMS key owner saw the request.
Rollout plan: guarded behind feature flag security.operator_endorsement.enabled defaulting to off. Initial rollout will enable generation and validation only in staging, with read-only provenance in production before enforcing denies.

- [x] Add region-pin assertor middleware and unit tests

- [x] Add canary configs and feature flag gating

- [x] E2E smoke tests for cross-region KMS flows

Changed files (high level):

Small illustrative snippet (endorsement validation path): "if endorsement == nil || !endorsement.VerifySignature(endorserPubKey) || endorsement.Expired() { return denyWithAudit(r, \"endorsement_invalid\") }"
Review conversation summary:
- Liam O'Connor: "High level: good separation of concerns. Two asks: (1) add an opt-out for tenants on provenance collection (privacy/legal), and (2) confirm KMS consent cache TTL defaults and observable evictions."
- Maya Patel (author): "Addressed both: added tenant_provenance_collection opt-in in tenant config (default true), and set consent cache TTL to 5m with configurable env var REDWOOD_CONSENT_CACHE_TTL. Added eviction metrics and tests."
- Elena Ruiz: "Please add a short circuit that returns 400 instead of 500 for malformed endorsements; otherwise lgtm."
- Maya Patel: "Changed validation to return 400 and added unit tests covering malformed endorsements and replay attempts."
- Chao Wang: "Suggest to log provenance blob only at INFO for operator events and redact sensitive KMS key ids in the blob. Also asked to run perf canary."
- Maya Patel: "Redaction implemented for key ids (keep fingerprint only). Perf canary job was added and passed with a 3% median latency overhead in the staging profile."
CI status: initial CI failed on lint (max-line-length in docs), fixed in follow-up commit. Unit tests pass, e2e smoke passed in staging. Perf canary: staging median latency +3%, p95 +7% — within SLO for non-enforced rollout.
Security review: security-runbook noted change; SRE requested an alert for consent_cache_miss_rate spike.
Merge outcome: merged to main via squash on 2026-02-25 after approvals from Liam and Elena; merge commit message includes summary and Linear links.
Notes for operators:
- Feature flag security.operator_endorsement.enabled must be toggled in console for production enforcement.
- Tenant opt-in for provenance configured via tenant API (tenant.provenance.enabled).
- Watch metrics: security_endorsement_validation_failures, consent_cache_hit_ratio, audit_provenance_size_bytes.
Backwards compatibility: The added headers are optional and systems that do not understand them will be ignored; provenance blob writing is opt-in per tenant and does not change public API shapes.
Follow-ups tracked: ENG-3301 implement operator-endorser service autoscaling and HSM-backed signing; ENG-3310 policy-sim tests for large tenant rolls.
Adds operator-endorsement RBAC assertions, a lightweight region-pin assertor middleware, KMS-consent cache hooks, and an access-provenance audit bridge. Backwards-compatible rollout behind feature flag; no API changes.

Summary: Adds an 'Event Trellis' small-multiples dashboard, implements a lightweight token-cost fallback suggester service that annotates traces with candidate fallback model hints, and wires kernel warmup logs into invocation trace links. Motivation: production customers were hitting unexpected token-cost spikes during specific event types (batch ingestion, conversational streaming handoffs). Existing dashboards show per-route aggregates but make it hard to visually compare behavior across event types and warmup epochs. This change provides: 1) a trellis view (rows=event type, columns=hour buckets) showing median/95p token cost, median latency, and kernel-warmup-signal sparklines; 2) a background suggester that runs in the observability ingest path to attach recommended fallback variants when per-invocation token-cost exceeds a configurable threshold; 3) trace enrichment to attach the most-recent kernel warmup log pointer for quick debugging. Checklist: - [x] Trellis dashboard JSON and panels - [x] small backend service: observability/fallback_suggester.py - [x] trace enrichment in span-enricher.go - [x] docs: docs/observability/event_trellis.md - [x] unit tests for suggester heuristic - [x] e2e smoke run against staging dashboards

Commits (high-level): - 9bd3f2c: add dashboard definition and test fixtures - c4a7b0e: implement suggester service and configuration - f1e5a12: span enrichment: attach warmup-log link & fallback hint - ab7d55f: add dashboard docs and runbook section - 3c9a0d1: unit + integration tests; lint fixes

Changed areas (high level): - webapp/dashboards/event_trellis.json: new dashboard with 12 panels (median token cost, 95p token cost, median latency, kernel-warmup-sparkline). - observability/fallback_suggester.py: a small async service that inspects incoming metric envelopes and emits a lightweight annotation to the trace store when trigger conditions are met. - rpc/telemetry/span_enricher.go: enriches spans with 'fallback_hint' and 'warmup_log_url' fields when present. - docs/observability/event_trellis.md: runbook + how to interpret trellis rows/columns. - scripts/bench/warmup-replay.sh: helper for synthetic warmup logs to validate warmup linking.

Testing/CI: - Unit tests: fallback_suggester tests cover heuristic tuning and thresholding. - Integration: smoke test renders dashboard panels in staging and verifies panel queries return non-empty series. - CI checks: go vet + golangci-lint, python pytest, frontend linting. All checks passed on the final run (two flaky graphQL snapshot tests were retried and resolved).

Review conversation (selected): - Diego Ruiz (review): "Nice visualization idea. Two asks: (1) can we make the suggester idempotent and throttle annotations to avoid span spam? (2) please add a short TTL for warmup_log_url links to avoid stale pointers." - Maya Chen (author): "Addressed both: suggester now dedups on invocation id and rate-limits to 1 annotation per-invocation; warmup URLs are tombstoned after 7 days (configurable). PTAL." - Asha Patel (review): "Please add a note in the runbook for oncall about interpreting the 95p token-cost delta column and recommended mitigation steps (scale, fallback, prompt trim)." - Maya Chen: "Added runbook section and an automated quick-link in the dashboard that opens the suggester log for the selected cell." - Liam O'Connor: "Approvals pending a small nit on metric labels (use 'tokens_cost' instead of 'token_costs')." - Maya Chen: "Renamed the metric alias in the panel queries and pushed commit." - Diego Ruiz: "LGTM, tested on staging. Approving." - PR merged by Maya Chen via squash merge.

Operational notes & rollout: - Default threshold for the suggester is conservative (750 token-cost units per invocation); config is in infra/config/observability.yaml under 'fallback_suggester.threshold'. - We deliberately keep the suggester out of the main ingest hot path by running it as an async sidecar; deployment will start as 10% of observability ingestion workers for 48 hours, then scale up if no noise. - Dashboards are namespaced under 'Observability / Event Trellis' and the runbook link points to the docs page. - No schema migrations required for trace store; the enrichment is optional and stored as tags.

Release notes: - New 'Event Trellis' dashboard for rapid cross-event comparison of token-cost and latency. - Suggester annotates traces with recommended fallback model variants when token-cost spikes are detected. - Kernel warmup logs are linked in traces to speed root-cause for warmup-related latency.
Diego Ruiz: Nice visualization idea. Two asks: (1) can we make the suggester idempotent and throttle annotations to avoid span spam? (2) please add a short TTL for warmup_log_url links to avoid stale pointers.
Maya Chen: Addressed both: suggester now dedups on invocation id and rate-limits to 1 annotation per-invocation; warmup URLs are tombstoned after 7 days (configurable). PTAL.
Asha Patel: Please add a note in the runbook for oncall about interpreting the 95p token-cost delta column and recommended mitigation steps (scale, fallback, prompt trim).
Maya Chen: Added runbook section and an automated quick-link in the dashboard that opens the suggester log for the selected cell.
Liam O'Connor: Approvals pending a small nit on metric labels (use 'tokens_cost' instead of 'token_costs').

Diego Ruiz: LGTM, tested on staging. Approving.

If the trellis shows recurring 95p token-cost spikes for an event type, first check fallback_suggester annotations on the upper-right cell; suggested mitigations: enable fallback variants, increase burst capacity, or apply prompt trimming. Motivation: we keep seeing noisy token-level cost spikes that cluster by callsite (the user-facing API path / prompt template) rather than by model or tenant. Existing token histograms and per-route aggregates miss cross-token fallout patterns that indicate latent tail risk (e.g., a single prompt variant producing occasional long continuations that spike cost and latency). This PR introduces a callsite-aligned token fallout matrix: a compact N x M summary that maps token-phase buckets to callsite cohorts, enabling fast UI drilldowns and smarter alert suppression. Design: (1) an aggregator that consumes per-invocation token-phase counters and emits a fixed-size matrix keyed by callsite id and day/hour window; (2) a compact encoding for storage and transport (run-length + epoch sketch) to keep cardinality low; (3) an alert-priority-suppression engine that de-escalates alerts when a callsite shows historically bursty fallout patterns (configurable half-life + churn threshold); (4) a Grafana dashboard panel and an observability playbook to interpret fallout matrices and tune SLOs. Implementation highlights: - src/observability/fallout/aggregator.go: new aggregator service with streaming ingestion and early-aggregation hooks into the telemetry pipeline. - src/observability/encoding/compact_matrix.go: serialization helpers (RLE+sketch) and forward-compat versioning. - dashboards/grafana/fallout-matrix-panel.json: new dashboard panel with tile and flame-sparkline rendering. - tools/telemetry/canary_playbook.md: playbook for on-call to investigate fallout-driven alerts and recommended suppression settings. - config/observability.yml: new keys fallout_matrix.enabled, sampling.global_rate, suppression.half_life_minutes. Rollout plan: rollout is staged: canary on prod-observability for 3 days with sampling.global_rate=0.005, then traffic scale to 0.02 after metrics confirm no ingestion/backpressure. Alerts default to add low-priority tag for callsites with >70% churn over 72h; ops can opt-in to auto-suppress for callsites marked experimental. Backwards compatibility: fallback emits legacy per-token histograms if the compact matrix flag is disabled. Testing: unit tests for serializer/decoder and aggregator edge-cases; integration test that ingests synthetic invocation traces and asserts correct matrix shape, downstream indexing, and UI rendering. Linear references: ENG-2890 (fallout-matrix), ENG-2901 (alert-suppression playbook). Checklist: [x] aggregator impl [x] encoding test coverage [x] dashboard panel [x] playbook [x] canary rollout config [x] changelog notes.
src/observability/fallout/aggregator.go: added StreamIngest loop with batching and early-aggregate -> EmitMatrix(callsite, window, matrix)
src/observability/encoding/compact_matrix.go: new EncodeMatrix() / DecodeMatrix() using RLE+uint16 epochs
pkg/alerting/suppression_engine.go: Add SuppressIfChurny(callsite, window) with exponential decay state store
Ravi: Can we be more conservative with sampling initially? I asked for 0.1% default and a canary plan. Maya: set initial sampling.global_rate=0.005 for canary window and documented scale-up criteria in the playbook. Sana: please add an escape hatch for when the encoding causes index size blow-up. Maya: added forward-compat versioning and a feature flag to fallback to legacy histograms; added unit tests that assert matrix size bounds. Ethan: minor nits on naming and a request to expose suppression thresholds in the Console UI. Maya: added console flag in config and filed ENG-2950 to track Console integration. Final: approved-by Ravi, merged after green CI and one post-merge smoke run on canary cluster.
Introduce callsite-aligned token fallout matrix (compact encoding) and an alert-priority suppression mechanism. Adds Grafana panel and on-call playbook. Rollout is canaryed; default sampling is low. See ENG-2890/ENG-2901 for tuning guidance.
1) If an alert is suppressed, check tools/telemetry/canary_playbook.md -> guidance for manual re-escalation. 2) To increase sensitivity, raise sampling.global_rate and re-evaluate matrix churn. 3) To opt out, set fallout_matrix.enabled=false.
This PR focuses on observability and alert quality. Performance: aggregator uses bounded memory and early-aggregation to avoid OOM; encoding keeps per-callsite payloads <2KB in typical workloads. Storage impact monitored under rollout.
