Motivation: Intermittent production incidents showed truncated JSON objects in streamed responses when delimiters and UTF-8 token boundaries aligned poorly across transport chunks. This surfaced in OpenAI-compatible streams and caused downstream JSON parsers to fail or drop function-call frames. This PR introduces a conservative delimiter heuristic and an atomic-span repair pass in the SSE coalescer so partial JSON objects are never emitted without an explicit repair boundary. Summary of changes: 1) Add a delimiter-heuristic layer that marks potential mid-object delimiter splits and delays emission until a short lookahead window confirms boundary integrity. 2) Implement an atomic-json-span-repair step that reconstructs and resynchronizes incomplete object fragments by using lightweight checksum and sentinel markers when available. 3) Preserve original event ordering by tagging tentative fragments and enforcing deterministic replay order when repair is applied. 4) Tighten OpenAI-compat rules for function call sentinel handling so function_call/finish events cannot be interleaved with partial JSON emits. Compatibility: backward compatible with existing client integrations; behavior toggled by feature flag sse.atomic_span_repair (defaults to on for hosted). Testing: unit tests for corner splits, fuzz harness runs against random chunking, integration tests with openai-compat streaming harness, and end-to-end smoke in staging. Rollout: staged rollout to canaries, then gradual region rollout with metric gating (json_repair_rate, sse_latency_p50/p95).
parser: add delimiter heuristic and unit tests
coalescer: implement atomic-json-span-repair and sentinel tagging
compat: tighten function_call delimiter rules for openai layer
tests: add fuzz harness and new e2e scenario for truncated object
ci: add metrics gating config for rollout
Marco Diaz commented: Can we simplify the lookahead window heuristic to avoid an extra allocation? The current impl clones fragments; prefer zero-copy where possible.
Priya Kannan replied: Updated coalescer to use a borrowing slice for lookahead and removed one allocation; benchmark unchanged for p50 and improved p99 slightly.
Li Wei commented: The checksum heuristic sounds good but could collide on tiny fragments. Please add a defensive fallback to byte-wise resync.
Priya Kannan replied: Added a two-tier fallback: checksum+length then deterministic byte-resync for <16 byte fragments; added tests.
Samantha Ortiz requested changes: add a feature flag to toggle behavior in private installs and document operational impacts.
Priya Kannan replied: Added deploy/feature_flags.yaml entry and expanded docs/compatibility/streaming.md to describe flag and rollout plan.
Marco Diaz approved: lgtm after allocation fix and tests.
Li Wei approved: Verified fuzz harness results in staging.
Samantha Ortiz approved: Docs and flags look good.
Fixes: Prevents emission of truncated JSON objects in SSE streams by adding a delimiter heuristic and atomic-json-span repair. Improves function_call sentinel ordering in OpenAI compatibility layer. Operational: feature flag sse.atomic_span_repair controls behavior for Private installs. Monitoring: new metrics json_repair_rate and sse_repair_latency.

Motivation: Multiple customers reported production instability for long-lived streaming tool calls routed through intermediate proxies and gateway layers. When combined with scoped project keys and browser CORS preflight behavior, signed stream handshakes were either blocked or expired mid-stream, causing expensive reconnections. This PR introduces an ephemeral per-route signature token, a lightweight stream keepalive header, and an OpenAI-compat mapping so existing integrations keep working.

What this changes: 1) Introduces the X-RDW-Ephemeral-Token header (opaque, short TTL ~30s) that is minted by the control plane during initial handshake for streaming/tool-call sessions. The token is bound to a specific route+method and is micro-rotated on reconnects. 2) Adds X-RDW-Stream-Pulse: a keepalive pingable header that clients can emit periodically to prevent proxy idle timeouts without extending the main auth TTL. 3) Implements per-route signed-allowlist metadata stored in route config (allowlisted tool endpoints that accept ephemeral tokens) and a fallback mapping layer for OpenAI-compatible Authorization: Bearer semantics (ephemeral token presented as Bearer for compat if requested). 4) Refines CORS preflight behavior: control plane replies to OPTIONS with X-RDW-Allow-Ephemeral and exposes X-RDW-Ephemeral-Token in Access-Control-Expose-Headers when a handshake is expected from browser contexts. 5) Adds server-side validation hooks that check nonce replays and small KV entry to track ephemeral token rotations for up to 60s to support short reconnect windows.

Compatibility notes: - Default behavior is backward compatible: existing long-lived API keys/Project tokens continue to work; ephemeral tokens are optional and preferred for streaming/browser tool-calls. - OpenAI-compat: when clients use Authorization: Bearer <token> for streaming endpoints, the gateway will accept ephemeral tokens presented as Bearer and transparently mark the session as ephemeral for routing decisions. - For Dedicated/Private deployments, ephemeral token minting is disabled by default but can be toggled via config:enable_ephemeral_handshake.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for token minting, rotation, and expiry (90% coverage for handshake modules). - Integration tests covering browser OPTIONS preflight -> ephemeral token exchange -> streaming reconnect. - Load test (benchmark-lab) shows <3% added p99 latency on handshake paths and no measurable change on steady-state token-bearing streams. - Added new e2e scenario to perf-canary to simulate proxy-induced mid-stream reconnects; regression prevented in 95% of runs.

Security considerations: ephemeral tokens are short-lived and single-route-scoped; the server enforces strict nonce reuse checks so tokens cannot be replayed across routes. We log handshake failures and surface an alert when token mint rate exceeds expected traffic patterns (possible replay or abuse).

Deployment plan: staged rollout on Canary -> blue/green in Hosted -> opt-in for Dedicated/Private with feature flag. Config defaults off for Private. Gate: metrics for handshake success rate and p95 handshake latency must be within SLOs before wide rollout.

This description includes links to the design doc and Linear tasks in the commits section and CI logs below.
Introduce ephemeral per-route handshake tokens (X-RDW-Ephemeral-Token) for more resilient browser and proxy streaming.
Add X-RDW-Stream-Pulse keepalive header to reduce proxy-induced reconnects.
OpenAI-compat: accept ephemeral tokens presented as Bearer headers for streaming endpoints.
New console flag: enable_ephemeral_handshake (off by default for Private).
Aisha Patel: Overall this looks good. A couple of questions: how do we surface ephemeral token mint failures to customers? Can we add a counter metric?
Maya Chen: Added rdw.handshake.mint_fail counter in the latest commit and an alert rule draft in docs/handshake/alerts.md. Also included a console UI note in docs so SREs can toggle the flag.
Marco Li: Why not use long-lived signed cookies for browser flows to avoid repeated OPTIONS calls?
Maya Chen: We considered cookies but they don't map cleanly to our gateway routing model and introduce CSRF surface; ephemeral token in header allows consistent routing and simple CORS expose. Added a short section to the design doc explaining the tradeoffs.
Sofia Ramos (approval): Verified integration tests and perf-canary output; approving pending small nits about log text (addressed).
payload.title: Ephemeral per-route handshake tokens + streaming keepalive for more stable tool calls and browser flows

Motivation: Our presubmit lane has grown heavy as we added per-language lint/test shards and dependency scans. That increases feedback latency and CI cost. This PR introduces three coordinated changes: 1) lightweight runtime instrumentation for the repository build graph so we can prioritize hot paths and avoid running expensive checks for low-impact edits; 2) a presubmit-condenser that coalesces fast sanity checks into a compact fastpath and defers expensive/long-running checks to staged lanes; 3) an opt-in CLI 'dep-escort' that authors can run locally to compute a minimal dependency delta and generate a compact shrinkwrap suggestion to reduce noisy dep churn. Summary: - Add build-graph instrumentation (tracepoints + annotation) to ci/graph and build scripts. Instrumentation emits per-target weight and last-run duration metrics to the CI telemetry pipeline (datapoint keys: buildgraph.target_weight, buildgraph.last_duration_ms). - Implement presubmit-condenser in ci/presubmit which detects the change footprint (via build-graph) and routes the PR to one of three fastpaths: tiny (quick lint/spec smoke), focused (language-specific fast tests), and full-stage (deferred deeper tests). The condenser is opt-in via PR label "presubmit:condenser" or auto-enabled for small-footprint edits. - Add dep-escort under tools/dep-escort: a local Python CLI that computes transitive dep deltas, identifies minimal package.json/pyproject updates, and produces a proposed shrinkwrap diff that authors can include. It also annotates the PR with a dependency-signal comment (used by the presubmit-condenser). - Update docs/dev/presubmit.md with workflow and developer guidance. - Split large monolithic CI jobs into smaller tasklets referenced by the new condenser; this reduces warm setup time when only a subset of checks are required. Checklist: [x] build graph proto + metrics emission implemented; [x] presubmit-condenser core routing + label gating; [x] dep-escort CLI with unit tests; [x] docs updated and quickstart added; [x] smaller CI tasklets wired into workflows; [x] end-to-end smoke on main branch. Backwards compatibility: All changes are opt-in by label or controlled by the auto heuristics; existing PRs without labels see the same behaviour unless the auto heuristics consider them "small" edits. Rollout plan: merge to main behind a short feature flag in ci config; enable auto heuristics after 48 hours of telemetry collection and a short opt-out period. Related: ENG-3219 (ci cost reduction), ENG-3220 (dep churn reduction), SUP-1812 (support ticket describing noisy dependency updates).
Ethan Walker: Nice direction. Please split the large presubmit YAML into tasklets before merging so rollbacks are localized.
Priya Shah: Split into separate commits and added the tasklets directory; condenser now references tasklet entrypoints. PTAL.
Leah Morris: Can we make dep-escort language-agnostic (JS/Python) from day one? The current implementation is Python-first.
Priya Shah: Dep-escort core is language-agnostic; the first implementation includes heuristics for npm/poetry. Added tests and docs clarifying scope.
Diego Ramirez: CI telemetry bridge failed on first run (flake in target-weight emission). Rerun after small timeout.
Priya Shah: Adjusted emitter backoff and added a unit test for intermittent telemetry timeouts. Reran CI and green.
Add build-graph instrumentation and presubmit-condenser to reduce CI cost and speed feedback for small edits. Introduce dep-escort CLI to compute minimal dependency deltas and reduce noisy dependency updates. Opt-in via label 'presubmit:condenser' or auto-enable for small footprints. Backward-compatible and feature-flagged.

Context: presubmit CI has been a major source of noisy failures and slow feedback for mixed-language changes. Our current single presubmit matrix runs broad rust+go test profiles and a monolithic dependency install step that invalidates caches frequently. This PR splits language-specific presubmit profiles, tightens cache keying, and adds a lightweight 'dep-freeze-adapter' that produces minimal, per-profile lock overlays to reduce transitive churn. Goal: faster, more stable presubmit runs with clearer failure attribution and fewer full-cache evictions. Changes in this PR: 1) Introduce two separate presubmit workflows: .github/workflows/presubmit-rust.yml and .github/workflows/presubmit-go.yml. Each workflow exposes narrow profiles (quick, integration, full) instead of a single combined job matrix. 2) Add tooling/presubmit/profiles.yaml which declares canonical testprofiles and their resource buckets; used by workflow generation and local dev shim. 3) Implement ci/scripts/dep-freeze-adapter.go: a small Go binary that inspects workspace manifests, computes a minimal freeze file for the requested profile (pins top-level deps, prunes optional transitive sets), and emits layered lockfiles that are cached by CI. 4) Change CI cache keying logic in ci/cache/keying.go to include profile:name and language hash (not the full lockfile hash) to avoid unnecessary invalidation when unrelated language changes land. 5) Add a lightweight presubmit bootstrap script scripts/ci-bootstrap.sh that coordinates fetch+freeze+setup in <60s for quick profiles. 6) Docs: docs/ci/presubmit.md updated with examples and local reproduction steps. Motivation and tradeoffs: the dep-freeze-adapter favors deterministic presubmit installs and faster cache warmups at the cost of maintaining a small compatibility shim. It does not replace canonical dependency locks for releases; it only produces ephemeral overlays for CI profiles. Migration plan: workflows added in this PR run in parallel with the existing combined presubmit for two weeks (opt-in via toggles). After monitoring (SLAs: 30% median runtime reduction target for quick profiles, 50% fewer cache-miss full installs), we'll flip the default and remove the monolithic workflow. Checklist: - [x] Add separate presubmit workflow files - [x] Implement dep-freeze-adapter prototype and unit tests - [x] Update cache keying and bootstrap script - [x] Update docs and local dev shim - [x] Run dogfood against redwood/* and redwood-sdk-python for two days - [x] Add metrics to presubmit dashboards (runtime, cache-hit) Related: ENG-2653 (reduce-rust-presubmit-flakiness), infra notes in Linear ENG-2874.
Miguel Ortega (2026-02-19): Nice separation — can we avoid adding another long-running binary to maintain? Please add a short integration test that runs the adapter against the testdata overlay.

Aisha Patel (2026-02-19): Added minimal unit/integration tests and sample overlay in testdata. The adapter is intentionally small (~220 LOC) and only used in CI; we vendor it under ci/scripts to keep ownership clear.

Priya Shah (2026-02-20): Request: add metrics for cache-hit / cache-miss labels so SRE can measure improvement. Also, ensure the adapter fails fast (exit 1) on checksum mismatch.

Aisha Patel (2026-02-20): Added Prometheus counters in ci/scripts/dep-freeze-adapter.go and updated bootstrap to emit a synthetic metric on success/failure. Also added stricter checksum handling. Reran CI.

Evan Li (2026-02-21): Verified reduced runtime on quick profiles in staging (median reduced from 3m10s to 1m55s). Approving pending squash and brief changelog entry.

CI (2026-02-21): presubmit-rust quick: passed; presubmit-go quick: passed; full integration: flaky on a separate package (unrelated). Final run after fixes: all checks green.
Staged CI changes: split Rust/Go presubmit workflows, introduce dep-freeze-adapter for profile-specific minimal lock overlays, improved cache keying and a faster bootstrap script. This should reduce presubmit runtime for quick profiles and lower noisy cache evictions.
Ops: the new presubmit workflows are behind a temporary feature toggle controlled by org-level repo secret CI_PROFILE_ROLLOUT. Monitor presubmit/cache-hit and runtime dashboards (dashboards/presubmit-runtime). If cache-hit drops by >10% after 24h, revert the rollout toggle. The adapter emits metrics prefixed ci_presubmit_freeze_*.

Context: Large customer deployments exposed a race in session-affine canary cutovers where user sessions were split between old and new models during a multi-step promote, causing degraded UX and noisy SLO alerts. This PR implements a coordinated, transactional cutover 'saga' that preserves session affinity, stages user cohort handshakes, and provides an autocorrect rollback pathway when safety checks fail. Motivation: Reduce user-visible flapping during promotions, make rollbacks fast and explainable, and provide operators a deterministic playbook for cross-region cutovers. Design highlights: 1) AtomicCutoverSaga controller — a new orchestration primitive that sequences probe -> handshake -> promote -> verification steps with checkpointed progress so rollbacks are deterministic. Each step emits provenance metadata for audit and replay. 2) UserAffinityProxy — lightweight routing layer that pins active sessions to the pre-cutover model until the handshake completes; supports sticky cookies and token-based leases for API clients. 3) AutocorrectRollback policy — rule engine that evaluates multi-metric windows (latency, error-rate, semantic-drift score) and triggers a staged rollback which can be automatically promoted to a fast revert if thresholds are still breached. 4) Telemetry signals and human-in-the-loop hooks — emits a 'cutover.trace' span with decision reasons to the tracing backend and surfaces a single-click abort/rollback action in the Console. Backwards compatibility: New defaults are opt-in for Dedicated/Private customers; Hosted uses gradual rollout for the first 30 days. Checklist: - [x] Implement AtomicCutoverSaga controller and unit tests - [x] Add UserAffinityProxy and integration test harness - [x] AutocorrectRollback policy + policy params in rollout CRD - [x] Tracing + Console button wiring - [x] E2E smoke tests against canary harness - [x] Docs: playbook and runbook snippets - [x] Release notes Draft Changeset summary: - New CRD: RolloutSaga (spec for staged cutover steps, metrics, abort windows) - Controller: controllers/rollout_saga.go (core logic, checkpointing) - Router: router/user_affinity_proxy.go (session pinning, lease renewal) - Policy: rollback/autocorrect_engine.go (multi-metric evaluator) - Console: ui/rollouts/atomic-cutover-button.tsx (abort/promote actions) - Telemetry: tracing/cutover_traces.go (span enrichment) - Tests: integration/atomic_cutover_test.go, e2e/cutover_smoke.sh Security & privacy: affinity token is TTL-bound and encrypted; no user PII is logged. Operational notes: - Default autopilot is disabled for tenants with strict change control (can be toggled in Console). - Operators can opt into 'strict verification' mode which requires manual approval between handshake and promote. Rollout plan: staged rollout for Hosted customers starting with 5% of traffic for 24h, escalate to 25% if verification passes, final promote after 72h. Dedicated customers can enable immediately after scheduling a maintenance window. Related work: builds on the checkpointed promote model from ENG-1910 and shadow handoff work in SUP-992. Testing & validation: ran 3 production-like canary rehearsals in benchmark-lab; autocorrect rollback triggered correctly on injected latency and semantic-drift faults. Known limitations: - Cross-region session stickiness requires sticky token propagation (future work: distributed lease coordinator). - Very large burst traffic patterns may require additional pre-warming of caches; documented as mitigation.
Maya Patel: Please split the large method in controllers/rollout_saga.go into smaller steps — makes the checkpointing logic easier to reason about.
Jordan Kim: Split out reconcileStep() and added unit tests for the checkpoint transitions (see second commit).
Luca Moretti: Suggest tightening the default metric windows in autocorrect_engine.go; 5m aggregation hides transient regressions.
Jordan Kim: Reduced the default window to 90s for latency and 3m for semantic-drift, added config knobs in the CRD.
Ariana Chen: Security review — ensure affinity token rotation works when a backend restarts; also add metrics for tokens expired vs renewed.
Jordan Kim: Added token renewal metrics and a fallback path that rebinds sessions to the older model for clients that fail renewal.
CI Bot: build/linux-unit-tests failed on first run (flake in scheduler test)
Jordan Kim: Re-ran CI after fixing test ordering; all checks passed on re-run.
Introduces RolloutSaga (atomic cutover orchestration) with session affinity proxy and an autocorrect rollback policy. Admins can opt into automatic rollback or require manual verification. See docs/playbooks/atomic-cutover.md for runbook and Console operator actions.
Operators: monitor cutover.trace spans and the new metrics rollout.saga.step_duration_seconds and rollback.autocorrect.triggers. Use Console single-click abort if the automated rollback is disabled. For Dedicated clusters, schedule a maintenance window when enabling strict verification.
1) Start RolloutSaga in dry-run mode for a small cohort. 2) Verify handshake metrics (handshake.latency < 200ms, handshake.failures == 0). 3) Promote to 25% and monitor grouped metrics for 2h. 4) If autocorrect triggers, follow audit log to replay decision and escalate to manual abort if needed.

Fixes intermittent SLO watchdog stalls that could leave tenant queues frozen under sustained egress throttling. Adds a bounded 'priority warmup' token dispenser to avoid sudden cold-start floods during graceful reinstate. No customer-facing API changes.
Context: During a prolonged egress-capacity event we observed the SLO enforcement watchdog enter a pathological state where some tenant queues would never recover (stall) despite capacity returning. Root cause analysis pointed to the interaction between exponential backoff in the watchdog, the tenant penalty ledger, and the reinstate path: a race allowed an almost-zero token allotment to persist and prevented the normal warmup window from progressing. Motivation: This is a production-impacting hotfix for multi-tenant regions; symptoms included persistent 503s for affected tenants and unusually long tail latencies after regional capacity reclaimed.

What this PR does: 1) Introduces an adaptive stall resolver in the watchdog: periodic detection of progress stalls (no token increase for N cycles) triggers a bounded reset of the warmup gradient for affected tenants instead of full penalty wipe. 2) Implements a 'priority warmup' token dispenser that ramps tokens for reinstated tenants in priority-ordered buckets (fast-path for tier-1, measured ramp for lower tiers). 3) Adds additional guardrails to the egress throttle controller to surface early telemetry when backpressure patterns deviate from expected shapes (spike vs sustained). 4) Adds conservative circuit-state persistence to avoid oscillation during short flaps.

Behavioral guarantees: - Stall resolver only relaxes the warmup slope by a bounded factor and records an audit event; it cannot fully bypass SLO limits. - Priority warmup uses tenant metadata (reserved tiers) to allocate initial tokens; non-reserved tenants get a slower ramp. - All changes are opt-in via runtime flags for 24h push rollout and monitored rollback.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for stall detection heuristics and token ramp math. - Integration in perf-canary: simulated egress stress test with tenant mix (70/20/10 production/staging/test) validates recovery times reduced by ~60% on median and eliminates permanent stalls in synthetic repro. - End-to-end validation on a regional canary for 6 hours with gradual traffic restore. - Observability: new metrics (slo_watchdog.stall_detected, priority_warmup.ramp_step) and logs added; dashboards updated.

Risk and mitigation: - Risk: warmup could temporarily increase tail latency if too aggressive; mitigations: bounded ramp, feature flags, canary rollout, and immediate rollback path. - Risk: telemetry noise; added counters and sampling to avoid metric storms.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main + enable flags in staging (immediate). 2) Enable in 1 non-critical region for 2 hours, monitor. 3) Progressive enable across regions over 24 hours. Contingency: switch flags off or trigger automated rollback if slo_violation_count increases beyond threshold.

Related: Linear ENG-2109 (SLO watchdog improvements), ENG-2203 (regional egress hardening), incident SUP-984.

Title: Make quality gating policy configurable per-route and account tier

Context
Today, quality gates are effectively “one size fits all” once the feature flag is enabled. This creates friction for:
- Self-serve routes where we want a fast smoke gate by default (DX) and escalated full gates for higher-risk diffs.
- Enterprise / regulated routes where we want stricter defaults (full gates always, tighter override rules) and explicit auditability.

This PR introduces a first-class gating policy object that can be resolved by (route_id, account_tier, model_family) with sane defaults. Enforcement remains defense-in-depth (Optimize apply boundary + rollout promotion), but now reads a consistent policy source.

What’s in this PR
1) Policy model + resolution
- Adds GatePolicy and GatePolicyBinding data model.
- Resolution order:
  1. Route override (route_id)
  2. Tier default (account_tier)
  3. Global default
- Optional predicates for model_family and change_type (batching/cache/quant_profile).

2) Default policies (MVP)
- global_default: smoke gate required for apply; full gate required for canary promotion.
- tier:self_serve: smoke required; full required only for quant_profile changes.
- tier:enterprise: full required for all in-scope change types.

3) Enforcement wiring
- Optimize ApplyConfig endpoint now loads effective policy and enforces required gate tier(s).
- Rollout controller promotion check reads the same effective policy for the route/tier.
- Override flow unchanged but now validates against policy (e.g., enterprise requires explicit approver role).

4) Console/Optimize API surface
- Gate run summary endpoints now include "effective_policy" metadata (id + human-readable summary + resolved_from).
- Allows UI to explain “why you’re blocked” and what gate tier is required.

5) Migration/backfill
- Introduces a migration to create global_default and tier defaults.
- Backfills existing gating-enabled routes to a route binding matching the prior behavior to avoid surprise changes.

Out of scope
- Private/on-prem automation policy distribution (this will be design-only for now).
- Per-account custom policies beyond tier (we can add account_id bindings later if needed).

Testing
- Unit tests for policy resolution ordering and fallbacks.
- Integration tests for apply boundary enforcement by tier.
- Added a small e2e fixture to ensure rollout promotion is blocked when policy requires full gates.

Example (sanitized)
- Policy summary string shown in API responses:
  "tier=enterprise -> require_full_gate_for=[batching,cache,quant_profile], require_smoke_gate_for=[batching,cache,quant_profile], overrides=admin_or_enterprise_approver"

Rollout plan
- Ship policy plumbing + defaults behind existing gating feature flag.
- For limited production rollout, only apply tier defaults for newly created routes; existing routes remain pinned via backfill bindings.

Follow-ups
- Add account_id bindings once we have a stable enterprise exceptions workflow (see PM-482).
- Add policy observability counters (policy_resolution_source, required_tier) once ENG-3926 lands.

Refs
- Related PRs: pr-19531 (block apply when gate fails), pr-19544 (rollout controller respects gate), pr-19537 (override flow)
- Linear: ENG-3921, ENG-3928; PM: PM-481

Aditya Rao (Product) — 2026-02-10
Can we make sure existing customers don’t see behavior changes on rollout? I’m worried enterprise routes might suddenly require full gates and block planned changes.

Jordan Lee (Author) — 2026-02-10
Yep. The backfill migration creates route-level bindings for any route that previously had gating enabled, mapping to the old behavior. Tier defaults will only apply to new routes unless we explicitly migrate them.

Paula Mendes — 2026-02-10
For rollout coupling: does the rollout controller use the same resolver or are we duplicating logic?

Jordan Lee — 2026-02-10
Same resolver logic, shared contract via a lightweight policy summary record fetched from Optimize. For now rollout controller calls Optimize’s policy endpoint (with caching) to avoid drift.

Noah Patel — 2026-02-11
Request: add static validation so a policy can’t require “full” without “smoke” (or define what that means). Also ensure quant_profile always forces at least smoke even on global default.

Jordan Lee — 2026-02-11
Added validation: required_full implies required_smoke for the same change types (enforced at write + migration seed). Also added a guardrail: quant_profile change types always require >= smoke even if misconfigured.

Benji Okafor — 2026-02-11
DB review: do we need an index on (route_id, account_tier, model_family)? Resolver will run per apply.

Jordan Lee — 2026-02-11
Added composite indexes on bindings: (route_id, precedence), (account_tier, precedence) and (model_family, change_type). Also caching in Optimize for 30s with invalidation on policy write.

Dylan Brooks — 2026-02-12
Console needs to show a clear human-readable explanation. Can you include “resolved_from” so UI can say “Route override” vs “Enterprise default”?

Jordan Lee — 2026-02-12
Done. Response now includes resolved_from in {route_override|tier_default|global_default} and a summary string (kept stable for UI copy).

Sean Gallagher — 2026-02-12
SRE ask: please emit a counter for policy resolution failures / fallbacks. If Optimize can’t resolve, we should fail closed for enterprise, but not for self-serve?

Jordan Lee — 2026-02-12
Implemented fail-closed across all tiers when gating is enabled (consistent with guardrails goal). Added structured logs for resolution failures and a metric stub behind the existing gating metrics feature flag (full dashboards in ENG-3926).

Paula Mendes — 2026-02-13
Looks good. One more: rollout controller should treat “policy endpoint unavailable” as promotion blocked (not allowed).

Jordan Lee — 2026-02-13
Confirmed: promotion check returns BLOCKED with reason QUALITY_GATE_POLICY_UNAVAILABLE and surfaces it in the rollout event.

Approvals
- Aditya Rao: Approved (2026-02-13)
- Paula Mendes: Approved (2026-02-13)
- Noah Patel: Approved (2026-02-13)
- Benji Okafor: Approved (2026-02-13)

Merge
Squashed and merged by Jordan Lee on 2026-02-13.

Gating enforcement can now vary by route and account tier (self-serve vs enterprise). New default policy introduced; existing routes are backfilled to preserve current behavior. Console/Optimize APIs expose the effective policy used for a recommendation/change.

Context and motivation: High-volume low-value requests (status checks, short-answers, autosuggest pings) account for a disproportionate share of prefill and KV cache churn while contributing minimal product value. This PR introduces a 'hush sampler' — a budget-aware, low-priority prefill sampler that reduces prefill frequency for low-value request cohorts and surfaces lightweight quantization-profile hints so downstream serving can select cheaper execution paths when safe. Goals: reduce token-level unit cost for noisy workloads, avoid user-visible regressions for high-value traffic, provide safe fallback and observability for ops. Summary of changes: 1) New hush sampler orchestrator (pkg/prefill/hush_sampler.go) that groups incoming requests into budget lanes (gold/silver/bronze) based on tenant heuristics and recent value signals. Each lane has an independently configurable 'quiet_rate' controlling the fraction of requests that skip expensive prefill but still receive a fast degraded path. 2) Quant hinting module (pkg/quant/hinting.go) that attaches a stable hint token to requests that pass through hush lanes. Hints are interpreted by the runtime to prefer lower-precision kernels or compact cache allocations; the runtime will fall back to full precision if quality triggers detect degradation. 3) CLI helpers and export (cmd/cli/econctl/hush_profile.go) to generate and apply hush profiles per tenant. 4) Telemetry: new prefill metrics and histograms (telemetry/prefill_metrics.yaml) and a canary workload (e2e/canaries/hush_sampler_workload.yaml) that tests economic and latency impacts. 5) Documentation and ops runbook (docs/ops/hush-sampler-runbook.md, docs/dev/quant-hinting.md) explaining configuration, safe rollouts, and playbooks for incidents. 6) Tests: unit and integration — a targeted integration (tests/integration/hush_sampler_test.go) that exercises warm/cold prefills and validation hooks. Design notes: - The hush sampler is conservative by default: quiet_rate defaults to 0.05 for bronze lanes and is tenant-scoped. - Hints are advisory and require runtime opt-in via a new capability flag. - Quality monitoring watches for hallucination and embedding drift; if diagnostic probes cross thresholds the control plane auto-elevates the lane to normal prefill behavior. Rollout plan and safety: - Feature gated behind tenant-level flags and runtime capability toggles. - Start with a shadow mode that emits metrics without changing behavior for one week (telemetry validated). - Canary on dedicated staging on region us-west-2 with a synthetic workload simulating 30% bronze traffic. - Gradual ramp: 1% tenants -> 10% -> 50% with automated rollback on metric regressions. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of hush sampler orchestrator and policy proto. - [x] Quant hinting API and runtime opt-in hooks (runtime patch submitted in separate PR). - [x] CLI and profile export/import. - [x] Telemetry and canary workloads. - [x] Docs and runbook. - [x] Unit and integration tests. Commits summary: feat(prefill): add hush sampler + policy proto; feat(quant): hinting attach/parse; test(ci): add hush canary smoke test; docs: ops runbook. Files changed (high-level): pkg/prefill/*, pkg/quant/*, cmd/cli/econctl/*, telemetry/*, docs/*, tests/integration/*. Review notes and conversation summary: - Priya Shah: "Can we ensure quiet_rate is tenant-admin controllable and visible in Console UI?" -> Response: "Yes — CLI exposes it and the Console work item (ENG-2104) is tracking the UI surface; added a note in docs." - Luca Moretti: "How do we measure downstream quality impact from quant hints?" -> Response: "Added quality probes: per-tenant hallucination-rate and embedding-similarity hooks. If probes exceed thresholds the sampler auto-escalates; thresholds are in telemetry/prefill_metrics.yaml." - Jordan Kim: "CI flake observed on integration 02, looks timing-related." -> Author: "Tightened test timeouts and restructured canary to use stable synthetic seed; reran CI — green." - Ops (feedback): "Runbook needs a command for emergency disable" -> Added `econctl hush disable --tenant <id>` in cmd/cli and documented rollback steps. CI and checks: - Unit: pass - Integration (staging): pass after one re-run - Lint: pass - Benchmarks: baseline microbenchmark shows ~12% token-cost reduction for bronze-lane workloads with <1% latency 95th percentile increase in synthetic canary. Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after reviewers approved and canary metrics validated in staging. Related work items: ENG-1890 (sampling platform), ENG-2104 (Console visibility). Follow-ups: - Runtime patch to honor quant hints and implement fallback kernel selection (PR linked in description). - UX work to expose hush profiles in Console (tracked by ENG-2104).
Priya Shah: Please make quiet_rate tenant-controllable and expose in Console UI. (resolved)
Luca Moretti: Add explicit quality probes for quant hinting and auto-escalation. (addressed)
Jordan Kim: Integration flake — tightened timeouts and fixed synthetic seed. (verified)
Ops: Add emergency disable command to econctl and document rollback. (added)
Add hush-sampler: budgeted low-priority prefill lanes and quantization hinting. Reduces prefill churn for noisy low-value workloads; feature is gated and opt-in. Includes CLI, telemetry, docs, and canary. Requires runtime opt-in to use quant hints.
To exercise: enable hush sampler for a test tenant, apply default bronze profile via econctl, run the hush canary workload, and validate telemetry signals. QA should verify auto-escalation behavior by artificially tripping quality probes.

Motivation: observed tail spikes when aggressive length bucketing created narrow bins that oscillated in occupancy across seconds, causing padding variability and kernel inefficiencies. This PR introduces a "smooth-bucket regulator" heuristic that (1) adds temporal smoothing to bucket boundaries to avoid rapid oscillation, (2) integrates a lightweight kernel-affinity estimator so cohorts favor kernels with better throughput for the predominant sequence lengths, and (3) biases placement for requests with warm KV cache to stay in the same cohort (sticky KV affinity) to reduce KV cache churn. The changes are implemented inside the continuous batch composer and scheduling layer; the feature is opt-in behind runtime config 'smooth_bucket_regulator=true' and a guardrail param 'max_boundary_shift_ms'. Implementation summary: we add a BucketRegulator object that maintains per-batcher histogram windows, computes smoothed boundary deltas with an exponential moving average, then rebalances requests into neighbor buckets only when smoothed benefit outweighs reallocation cost (estimated padding reduction minus kernel-switch overhead). Kernel affinity scores are derived from a mini cost-table populated by microbenchmarks run at boot and periodically updated; KV-stickiness adds a small positive score when request metadata indicates a populated KV handle. Benchmarks: internal perf run on c6g.4xlarge-equivalent with Llama2-7B-quantized profile; workloads: mixed chat (50%), short queries (30%), RAG retrieval+answer (20%) simulated from production traces. Results: median token throughput +3.8%, average token cost -6.7%, p95 latency improvement 12% on heavy RAG mixes, padding tokens reduced by ~18% overall for the trace set. Safety & fallbacks: when kernel-affinity table is stale or reports high variance we fallback to classic fixed bucketing; regulator exposes diagnostic metrics (regulator.bucket_shifts, regulator.kernel_mismatch_rate, regulator.kv_stick_hits) surfaced to the console. Tests and CI: unit tests for regulator boundary math and score composition, e2e smoke with continuous batch composer harness and a new micro-benchmark that asserts no regression in cold-start latency. Rolling strategy: merge to main with feature gate off by default; enable in canary pool #5 then progressively to Dedicated pools. Related: this complements ENG-6210 (KV cache eviction smoothing) and supersedes some ad-hoc heuristics introduced in earlier PRs. See commits for implementation notes and small refactors of the batch composer module.
Mateo: Can you quantify the kernel-switch overhead used in the scoring? Author: we measured ~0.6-1.2ms overhead for model variants on our quantized kernels and use a conservative 1.5ms penalty (configurable).
Priya: I see potential for inflating bucket counts in pathological traces; suggest a hard cap per-bucket size. Author: added max_bucket_capacity and fallback to merge with neighbor when exceeded.
Jordan: tests are good but the e2e perf run had one flaky seed; re-ran and included deterministic seeding in tests.
Ops: please ensure metrics names here follow the console convention; updated registrations.yaml accordingly.
Introduces a smooth-bucket regulator that reduces padding-induced waste and prefers kernel-aligned cohorts; improves cost and p95 latency for typical RAG and chat workloads.
Feature gate off by default. To try in canary set runtime.smooth_bucket_regulator=true and adjust runtime.sbr.max_boundary_shift_ms=200. Monitor regulator.bucket_shifts and kernel_mismatch_rate for first 24h.
Unit tests for regulator math, integration test against continuous composer harness, perf regression gated via benchmark job. Deterministic seeding in tests to avoid flakiness.

Motivation: CI sensitivity to transient dependency resolution and a proliferation of small gateway wrappers has increased presubmit latency and made build caches less reproducible. This PR consolidates the CI gateway surface, introduces an inline dependency snapshotter that records resolved transitive pins at presubmit time, and replaces several composite GitHub actions with light-weight, first-class binaries to reduce flakiness and startup overhead.

What I changed: consolidated pkg/ci/gateway* into a single gateway implementation with a pluggable hook for snapshotting; added tools/dep-snapshot (Go) which can emit a deterministic snapshot.json from the resolver used in CI; updated .github/workflows/ci.yaml to call the snapshot tool as an explicit step and to publish the snapshot artifact; removed two composite actions (actions/ci-prepare and actions/deps-collector) and replaced them with direct invocations to tools/dep-snapshot and scripts/presubmit-prober.sh; added Makefile targets for local dev and a minimal shim for the release pipeline to consume snapshots for staged rollouts.

Rollout plan: staged rollout to main CI lanes over 3 days. Step 1: enable snapshot recording on presubmit (this PR). Step 2: enable snapshot validation in the 'fastpath' lane (follow-up toggled by flag). Step 3: set CI to fail on snapshot drift for release branches after one week of telemetry.

Testing done: unit tests for gateway and snapshot logic (pkg/ci/gateway_test.go), e2e smoke in benchmark-lab using a canned resolver fixture, manual local runs using Makefile targets, and CI run with flaky retry reduced to 2.

Compatibility notes: snapshots are additive and do not change runtime model artifacts. Existing releases consume snapshots only if release pipeline flag is enabled. The gateway refactor preserves the public API used by Dedicated/Private installers; I added compatibility shims where necessary.

Motivation: We observed oscillatory scaling during rapid tenant commit churn where short-lived commitments trigger immediate provisioning and then decommit shortly after, causing thrashing and elevated unit costs. This PR introduces a Deferred Capacity Orchestrator (DCO) plus a Commitment Replay Adapter (CRA) that treats recent commitment events as an event stream and replays them into a smoothed planning window to produce less reactive provision decisions.

Summary: Implement an event-sourced replay layer that ingests reservation/commit events (create/extend/release) and emits aggregated delta plans on a configurable horizon. The DCO uses those plans with temporal damping and a cost-weighted headroom objective to decide elastic provisioning actions. The CRA translates legacy commitment records into the event stream so existing commitment writers do not need modification.

What changed (high level): - New event ingestion pipeline and small in-memory event journal (bounded retention). - Commitment Replay Adapter that serializes/deserializes legacy commitment records and emits normalized events. - Deferred Capacity Orchestrator that consumes the replay stream and outputs provision intents (scaleUp/scaleDown) with an adjustable lookahead and hysteresis. - Telemetry: new metrics for replay_lag_seconds, plan_variance, and predicted_headroom. - Tests: unit + integration harness that simulates bursty commit patterns and validates stability and cost regressions versus current autoscaler. - Docs: design doc and operator runbook describing tuning knobs and operational alerts.

Behavioral notes: The orchestrator will not immediately act on single short-lived commits unless the replay window indicates sustained contention above tenant SLO thresholds. The controller respects existing reservation priorities and burst credits; it produces intents that the existing provisioning reconciler will consume.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc added (docs/design/deferred_capacity.md) - [x] Unit tests for replay adapter and orchestrator decision logic - [x] Integration scenario harness and golden baseline comparison - [x] Metrics and dashboard snippets for ops - [x] Backwards-compatible adapter for older commitment writers

Migration/compatibility: CRA runs side-by-side and can be toggled per-cluster via a feature flag. No database schema changes required. Operators should enable the replay journal and monitor replay_lag_seconds during the first 24h.

Related work: builds on autoscaler research (ENG-4721) and ties into tenant budgeting improvements (ENG-4888). See docs/design for decision formulas and examples.

Detailed commit summary: see commits field.

Files changed (high level): see changed_files field.

Testing: Local unit tests and the integration harness were run; we also deployed a canary to the staging fleet for 48h under synthetic churn and saw a 23% reduction in ephemeral provisioning events and ~7% lower GPU-hour cost for the scenario used in the harness.

Operational concerns: Operators should watch plan_variance and predicted_headroom. If plan_variance spikes it indicates noisy commit traffic and operators can increase damping or widen the replay horizon.

feat(orchestrator): implement deferred capacity planner with horizon smoothing
perf(orchestrator): optimize plan aggregation and reduce GC pressure
test(integration): add bursty-commit harness and golden baseline

Motivation: We see frequent small regressions during progressive traffic shifts when probes (synthetic and live) are correlated and bursty. This PR introduces two coordinated mechanisms to reduce rollout flakiness: a staggered cutover lock that gates traffic shift steps until probe ensembles reach convergence, and an ensemble probe throttle that adaptively jitters and paces probes across cohorts to avoid correlated probe bursts.

What this implements: 1) rollout.cutover_lock: a stateful guard that holds progression when the probe ensemble's statistical convergence metric (ensemble_convergence_score) is below threshold. The lock is staggered by cohort so rollouts across multiple regions/replica pools progress independently rather than in lockstep. 2) probe.ensemble_throttle: a low-latency throttle controller that applies jittered pacing and priority smoothing for high-frequency probes (tail probes, KV-primed probes) to reduce probe-induced amplification of transient service pressure.

Behavioral guarantees and safety: - By default the cutover lock is opt-in for canaries; we wire it into the default canary policy with conservative defaults (min_convergence=0.85, min_samples=200). - The throttle operates in permissive mode for 72 hours post-merge in hosted test clusters to validate behavior before we flip enforcement for production rollouts. - We add a fallback policy: if the lock is held longer than max_hold_time (configurable), the orchestrator will continue with a limited-step slow-roll that caps traffic delta per minute to avoid indefinite stalls.

Testing and verification: - Unit tests for lock state transitions and throttle factor calculation. - Integration tests with the synthetic-canary harness that simulate correlated probe storms; added deterministic scenarios where throttle reduces probe amplification and cutover lock prevents 30%+ regression spikes during shift. - Canary experiments in 'staging-usa' for 48h: observed 2.7x reduction in rollout-related 95p latency spikes across three runs.

Upgrade and rollout plan: 1) Merge to main. 2) Deploy to staging clusters with enforcement disabled (telemetry only) for 72h. 3) Enable enforcement in a single region canary for production (traffic cap 5%) for 6 hours. 4) Gradual enable by region with monitoring playbook if ensemble_convergence_score trends downward.

Related work items and references: Linear: ENG-12841 (canary orchestration improvements), ENG-12902 (probe stabilization). Design doc: internal link https://linear.app/redwood/notes/cutover-lock-design.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation (code + tests) - [x] Unit/integration tests - [x] Canary verification in staging - [x] Observability (metrics, dashboards, alerts) - [x] Documentation in runbooks
Asha: Can you explain how the ensemble_convergence_score is computed and whether it's sensitive to sample skew?
Evelyn: The score is a weighted similarity metric combining rolling-window KS divergence across cohorts and a stabilization factor that downweights short-lived spikes; weights are configurable in rollout_policy.yaml. We added unit tests that simulate skewed probe distributions.
Miguel: We saw one flaky integration run where the throttle factor overshot during a burst. Is there a safety clamp?
Evelyn: Yes — throttle factor is clamped [0.1, 1.0] and we added a leaky-integrator decay to prevent overshoot. Added integration case that reproduced the previous overshoot and confirmed clamp behavior.
Samir: Approve after two nits on docs (minor wording) were addressed.
Asha: Approved. Miguel: Approved after re-run on staging passed. Merge-by-squash requested.
Introduce staggered cutover lock (opt-in) and ensemble probe throttle. Adds new metrics: ensemble_convergence_score, cutover_lock_state, probe_throttle_factor. Config knobs: rollout.cutover_lock.enabled, rollout.cutover_lock.min_convergence, rollout.cutover_lock.max_hold_time, probe.ensemble_throttle.enabled. Default is telemetry-only enforcement for 72h post-merge.

Motivation: Customers adopting the newer OpenAI Responses variants expect two things from our OpenAI-compatibility proxy: (1) streaming stability across fragmented chunks from v11-style responses and (2) transparent propagation of client-provided determinism hints and request metadata. This PR implements a compact proxy layer and mapping rules to preserve the behavior users rely on while avoiding coupling to internal response framing.

What this PR does: implements a responses-v11 compatibility shim that: 1) consolidates streaming fragments into deterministic application events (message/choice/segment) with reassembly metadata so SDKs can rehydrate partial streams without losing token alignment; 2) forwards client-side determinism hints (client_seed and rng_hint) supplied via the OpenAI 'seed' and 'determinism' fields into our internal request context and downstream runtime so that sampling remains reproducible across retries and logs; 3) preserves and exposes user_request_metadata (arbitrary JSON payloads) by mapping them to the x-rw-user-metadata header and including them in response events for auditing and downstream tool calls; 4) adds structured-output attribute mapping so that responses with the new "structured" payload type map to our existing structured-output contract instead of being folded into free-text.

Scope and exclusions: the proxy focuses on behavior required for API compatibility and streaming stability. It does not change model selection or scheduling heuristics; follow-up PRs will add routing policies for quantized model variants that require different seed semantics.

Testing and rollout: included unit tests for chunk reassembly, CI e2e for the streaming path against a synthetic responses-v11 server, and a small perf microbenchmark to verify CPU overhead of the mapper is <2% at typical payload sizes. payload.body:
Motivation: Production traffic has visible oscillation between aggressive spill cycles and immediate refill for small-object-heavy tenants. This causes repeated paging, short-lived memory pressure spikes, and tail-latency regressions during bursty workloads. Existing eviction policies favor simple LRU or slab-based heuristics which do not encode per-tenant reuse locality nor dampen rapid pressure signals from the IO/spill subsystem.

Summary: Introduces two complementary mechanisms to reduce fragmentation-driven spill churn and improve steady-state token-serving latency: 1) a Granular Reuse Map (GRM) — a compact, per-tenant map that tracks slot-level reuse heat and preferred free-slot candidates for fast allocation without triggering global compaction; 2) a Spill Signal Dampener — a small, configurable controller in the KV pressure path that accumulates and smooths spill demand signals (with hysteresis and rate limits) so that spill/compaction work is scheduled less reactively and with fewer oscillations. The change includes metrics, a limited-capacity background compact worker, a scheduler tweak to prefer local slot reclamation tasks, and an opt-in config flag for gradual rollout.

Implementation details: - GRM is implemented as a bounded, lock-sharded structure attached to tenant descriptors (src/serving/kv/grm_allocator.go). It maintains a lightweight bloom-like recency fingerprint plus a free-slot candidate ring; allocations consult GRM first to find reuse-friendly slots. - The Spill Signal Dampener (src/serving/kv/spill_dampener.go) converts instantaneous pressure events into an exponentially-weighted accumulator with a cooldown window; only when accumulated pressure crosses a tenant-specific threshold does it schedule a bounded compact job. Dampener parameters are tunable via tenant config and default to conservative values. - compact_worker.go implements a rate-limited background compactor that performs local slot coalescing (scoped to tenant and slab class) and returns reclaimed slots to the GRM. Compaction uses short windows to avoid CPU spikes. - Scheduler integration (pkg/scheduler/compact_policy.go) prioritizes compact jobs that are likely to reduce fragmentation without triggering remote spill. - Metrics added under internal/metrics/kv_frag_metrics.go: grm_hit_ratio, dampener_pressure, scheduled_compactions, compaction_duration_ms, and spill_cycles_prevented. - Tests: microbenchmarks and e2e scenarios added in tests/kv/grm_bench_test.go that simulate small-object churn and bursty writes.

Rollout plan: Feature is gated behind kv.grm_enabled and kv.spill_dampener_enabled tenant flags. Default rollout: enable in canary region for 24 hours, monitor grm_hit_ratio and spill_cycles_prevented, then expand to 20% of tenants, then to all. There is an emergency opt-out via tenant-scoped toggle and an operator-level override to disable background compactor immediately.

Benchmarks & results: On our synthetic small-object churn suite (10k tenants, median object size 176B, burst windows 200ms), observed results after enabling GRM + Dampener: - median P95 token latency improved by ~6.8% under burst (service layer); - number of spill cycles reduced by 71% in steady state; - cumulative CPU used by background compaction stayed under configured budget (default 4 cores across nodes) and did not materially affect serving throughput; - memory residency improved (fewer transient allocations) leading to 12% lower peak host memory usage during bursts. Full benchmark logs attached in PR artifacts.

Testing: Unit tests for GRM invariants and dampener behavior added. Integration tests simulate Tenants A/B under mixed read/write and confirm no regression in eviction correctness. CI runs include new microbench harness; added automated smoke test that toggles tenant flags to validate safe opt-out.

Compatibility & safety: Changes are backward-compatible: when flags are off, behaviour is unchanged. Parameters are conservative by default. Compaction is rate-limited and scoped to avoid cross-tenant interference. There are additional telemetry alerts (alert rule names included in docs) to surface unexpected compaction or spill patterns.

Docs/RFC: New design doc and rollout instructions at docs/rfc/2025-07-grm-spill-dampener.md. The PR includes guidance for SRE on dashboards to watch and suggested thresholds for the dampener.

Why this is different from past approaches: Prior PRs focused on monolithic slab compaction or eviction heuristics that react immediately to pressure. GRM changes allocation-time locality behavior to reduce fragmentation at the source, while the Dampener avoids oscillatory compaction/ spill scheduling — together they yield lower spill churn without centralizing compaction or increasing worst-case CPU.

Requested action: review for algorithmic edge cases around concurrent slot reclamation and correctness of the dampener thresholds; suggestions on metric naming and alert thresholds welcome.

Liam O'Connor: Can we bound the worst-case CPU the compactor will consume per node? Please add an abort condition when host CPU > 70%.
Author (Sophia Martinez): Added a soft budget and an immediate abort hook when host-level CPU exceeds configured threshold; documented in the compactor code and RFC.
Ravi Singh: The dampener threshold feels tenant-sensitive. Can we make it proportional to tenant steady-state allocation rather than absolute bytes?
Author: Dampener now uses tenant-resident-window-normalized pressure (configured by tenant_weight). Added tests to validate behavior across small and large tenants.
Mei Chen: Unit test failure on race in GRM with concurrent frees + scans; please ensure proper sharding/locks.
Author: Fixed by converting the candidate ring to lock-sharded segments with compare-and-swap updates; re-ran tests and added deterministic concurrency test.
Liam O'Connor: Approving after minor nits on metric names; leaving final approval for Ravi.
Ravi Singh: Approving. Observability looks good; recommend enabling for canary immediately.
Introduce opt-in GRM (Granular Reuse Map) and Spill Signal Dampener to reduce fragmentation-driven spill churn and improve latency under small-object churn; gated by tenant flags kv.grm_enabled and kv.spill_dampener_enabled. Includes metrics and a controlled background compactor. Non-breaking; disabled by default.

Motivation: Our monolithic presubmit runner spins up heavy language-specific linters and long-running integration checks for every push which increases CI latency and cost. Goals: reduce cold-start and aggregate runner CPU hours, cut median presubmit time for small changes by ~40%, and provide a smooth migration path for teams to opt-in. What I changed: 1) Added ci/presubmit/prober.go, a Go-based standalone probe that inspects diff heuristics, touched files, and cached fingerprint hints to return a compact decision token. 2) Decomposed internal lint entrypoint into language adapters under tools/lint/adapters/{python,ts,go,java} with a shared adapter ABI and smaller container images. 3) Updated .github/workflows/presubmit.yaml to run the prober as a very fast presubmit step and conditionally trigger the full adapter matrix via repository_dispatch when the prober signals. 4) Added scripts/toolchain-manifest-sync.sh and docs/presubmit-migration.md to document migration steps and how to produce a small toolchain profile for each adapter. 5) Added a lightweight shim to the release automation that honors presubmit decision tokens so that automated staging merges avoid redundant checks. Context and motivation: Our continuous-batching runtime has intermittent request starvation and high tail latency for low-volume, KV-heavy traffic. Earlier work introduced static linger and simple fairness knobs, but real traffic mixes (short, KV-heavy, and long requests) cause harmful oscillation: small requests wait too long for batch fill, while large/slow requests pin slots and starve short ones. This PR introduces two cooperating runtime components: (1) soft-linger-adapter, a dynamic per-queue linger controller that adjusts hold time based on short-request hit-rate and recent kernel execution profile; and (2) fairshare-rescuer, a lightweight admission-time rebalancer that detects KV-cache pinned lanes and hedges timeouts to reschedule/rescue short requests.

Design summary: soft-linger-adapter computes a rolling short-request fraction and effective kernel tail estimate, then gently increases or decreases the linger window (within configured min/max bounds) using an exponential-decay controller so changes are smooth. This reduces batch fill waits for bursty short traffic while still enabling batching for throughput. fairshare-rescuer attaches a small credit budget to each priority cohort; when KV-cache pinning or long-running kernels are detected (via kernel-exec-duration histograms and cache-miss signals), rescuer temporarily raises short-request admission priority and issues a non-blocking hedged probe to an alternate slot/worker to reduce observed starvation. The rescuer is conservative: hedging uses a brief jittered timeout and cancels duplicate work when the primary completes. Both components are KV-aware: hints from the KV cache (pin counts, warmup status) influence rescuer thresholds and linger decay rates.

Compatibility and config: New config knobs (soft_linger.min_ms, soft_linger.max_ms, soft_linger.decay_tau_ms, rescuer.credit_window, rescuer.hedge_timeout_ms, rescuer.kv_pin_threshold) are exposed with reasonable defaults tuned for our production mix. Feature flags allow incremental rollout per-cluster. No API changes.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc: docs/design/batcher_dynamic_linger.md
- [x] Unit tests for adapter and rescuer modules
- [x] Integration tests that reproduce starvation scenarios
- [x] Benchmarks comparing tail p99/p999 before/after
- [x] Telemetry hooks for new metrics

Commits summary: [1/3] introduce soft-linger-adapter core loop, config and metrics; [2/3] add fairshare-rescuer admission-time logic, KV-cache hint plumbing and cancellation plumbing for hedged probes; [3/3] tests, integration harness updates, docs and benchmark results.

Changed areas (high level): src/serving/batcher/soft_linger_adapter.rs - new controller and API; src/serving/scheduler/fairshare_rescuer.rs - admission-time rescuer & hedging; src/serving/kv_cache/prefetch_hint.rs - light-weight pin counters and hint surface; runtime/config/batcher.toml - configs; tests/integration/batcher_starvation_test.py - reproducer; benchmarks/batcher_tail/continuous_bench.py - benchmark harness additions; docs/design/batcher_dynamic_linger.md - design rationale; metrics/observability/metrics_registry.rs - new metrics (batcher.linger_ms, rescuer.hedge_count, rescuer.rescue_rate); examples/ops/continuous_batching_rollout.yaml - rollout procedure.

Testing and results: On the internal benchmark harness that mixes 80% short (<=64 tokens) KV-heavy requests and 20% long-form requests we observe: median latency: +2% (due to slightly increased probe activity), p95: -18%, p99: -32%, p999: -41% for short requests. Starvation incidents (measured as requests waiting > configured timeout without progress) dropped by ~85% in the simulated spike runs. CPU/GPU utilization remained within acceptable bounds; hedging contributes ~1.7% additional request work at peak.

Telemetry and rollout: New metrics were added and wired into the console dashboards (batcher.linger_ms, batcher.short_fraction, rescuer.hedge_count, rescuer.rescue_rate, kv.pin_count). Recommended rollout: enable feature-flag on a non-critical region for 24h, monitor rescue_rate and p99; if rescuer.hedge_count spikes > threshold consider backing off or increasing hedge_timeout.

Backward/forward compatibility: No protocol or API changes; config defaults preserve current behavior. The rescuer and adapter are opt-in via feature flags for gradual adoption.

Followups: (a) kernel-level hints to preemptively migrate KV-warm kernels off hot lanes; (b) tighten autoscaling integration so batcher linger adapts to observed node capacity; (c) distributed coordination experiment for global fairsharing across machines.

Motivation: In practice we observe pathological latency/throughput regressions for mixed-quality-attention (MQA/GQA) model variants when a single universal kernel choice and naive KV caching are applied. This PR introduces two complementary runtime mechanisms: (1) attention contracts, a lightweight per-request contract that encodes sparsity/stride hints and preferred kernel families (dense-fused, sparse-fused, fallback attention), and (2) KV cache slot scaling, a dynamic slot allocation and soft-eviction policy that reduces memory amplification for MQA shards while preserving prefix reuse. Design: attention contracts are produced by model introspection + sequence-length heuristics at the front of request processing and carried as a 1-byte mask + 1-byte profile id; the kernel selector consults the contract before performing cost-model scoring, biasing toward a sparse-fused kernel for MQA-style layout when sequence_length <= 1024 and head_count matches known Qwen/Mistral patterns. KV slot scaler monitors per-request unique-prefix ratio over a 1k-sample sliding window and adjusts per-shard slot_multiplier (0.5x..2.0x) with hysteresis to avoid thrash. We also add a compact slot-allocator that groups small prefixes to adjacent slots to improve locality. Implementation: changes to runtime/kernel_selector.cpp implement the contract pesos and backoff; new runtime/kv_cache/slot_scaler.rs contains the scaler state machine and eviction hooks; lightweight ABI changes add contract header propagation in runtime/transport.h; unit tests and a microbench harness were added under tests/microbench; docs and rollout notes added to docs/perf. Backwards compatibility: contracts are opt-in behind runtime flag "enable_attn_contracts" and fall back to legacy selector when not present. KV slot scaler also defaults to disabled; a controlled canary rollout is documented. Benchmarks: on internal MQA Llama-70B microbench with synthetic chat load (p95 tokens_per_second, seq len 128..512) we measured median throughput uplift of 18% and p95 latency reduction of 12-16% when both mechanisms are enabled, with memory savings of ~22% for KV allocations on mixed-prefix workloads. On Qwen-R50 tests we saw 8-10% throughput gains at mid/long sequences due to reduced kernel mis-selection. Tests and CI: full unit test coverage added for selector heuristics, scaler transitions, and eviction invariants; microbench harness runs on GPU CI tier with deterministic seeds. Rollout: gated by feature flags, stepwise canary to 10%/50%/100% of traffic with runtime metrics monitored (token latency by model, p95, kv_alloc_bytes, kernel-selection-distribution). If regression threshold exceeded (>5% p95 regression) feature flag auto-rolls back. Risks and mitigations: wrong contract bias can increase compute cost for some models; mitigated by conservative default weights and a fallback to cost-model scoring. Edge cases: models with mixed head sizes (custom Llama forks) will bypass contract bias and still use cost model. Related: references ENG-1987 (MQA regression incident), ENG-2040 (kernel selector refactor). Request: review kernel correctness on MQA head splitting and KV eviction invariants, sanity-check perf numbers and rollout gating. This is intended as an incremental, opt-in improvement to reduce operator tuning burden for MQA/GQA workloads.
Lorenzo Diaz: Please add a short comment on the cost-model weight math in kernel_selector.cpp so future readers understand the fallback behavior. Request change.
Author (Maya Patel): Added inline math comment and a unit test demonstrating fallback path.
Kris Nguyen: KV scaler seems susceptible to oscillation for bursty traffic; can we increase hysteresis and add a cooldown? Request change.
Author: Increased hysteresis from 3->6 windows and added a 30s cooldown; added tests for cooldown behavior.
Priya Shah: microbench numbers look strong but add a smaller end-to-end chat test with real prompts to ensure quality of generated tokens is unchanged.
Author: Added an e2e quality smoke check using standard prompts and BLEU/ROUGE-like heuristics; no regression observed.
Add runtime opt-in: attention contracts and KV slot scaling to improve MQA/GQA model throughput and reduce KV memory amplification. Opt-in behind feature flags: enable_attn_contracts, enable_kv_slot_scaler. Expected p95 latency improvements 12-16% and KV memory reduction ~22% on mixed-prefix workloads.
Canary plan attached in docs/perf/attn_contracts.md. No breaking API changes; transport header extension is backwards compatible.

Motivation: The repo has accumulated several generations of build entrypoints (legacy-make, legacy-scripts/ci.sh, and ad-hoc node wrappers). These lead to brittle local dev bootstraps, duplicated logic across presubmit flows, and divergence between CI and release behavior. This PR introduces a compact 'toolchain-bridge' adapter that provides a single runtime facade to incrementally migrate callers off legacy scripts and standardize tool installation and feature flags. Goals: (1) deprecate legacy top-level scripts with a clear shim/backcompat layer; (2) centralize toolchain boot (node/pnpm/rust/go) into typed.yml manifests consumed by the bridge; (3) make presubmit/lint/test runners consume the bridge so CI and local dev share the same boot semantics; (4) remove duplicated linter and formatter invocations spread across scripts. Migration plan: - Add toolchain-bridge binary (go) that reads manifests/.toolchain/*.yml and exposes a deterministic env + exec behavior. - Replace direct calls to npm/pnpm/setup-toolchain in presubmit runners with bridge invocations. - Add a deprecation shim for legacy scripts that forwards to the bridge but emits a deprecation warning and telemetry event. - Provide a devcontainer quickpath and lightweight dev image to accelerate local onboarding. We will remove the shims after two release cycles once telemetry shows <1% usage. Summary: Add a permission-aware audit annotator and a lightweight KMS multi-region fence to enforce region pinning during cryptographic operations. This PR introduces a short-lived middleware in the request flow that annotates audit events with the effective permission delta (what changed compared to the caller's base role) and verifies the KMS key used for encryption/decryption is eligible for the tenant's configured geozone. Motivation: Customers operating under regional data residency rules and strict audit requirements asked for clearer permission provenance in audit logs and stronger enforcement when keys are selected by routing/fallback logic. The annotator helps post-hoc forensics and alerting, while the KMS fence prevents accidental use of a key outside the tenant's permitted set.

Design and scope: - PermissionAuditAnnotator (rbac/audit): inspects PDP decision + request context and emits four new audit fields: auth.principal_id, auth.principal_role, auth.effective_permissions_delta, audit.permission_change_kind (added/removed/unchanged). The annotator runs immediately after PDP returns to avoid changing decision latency profile. - KMSRegionFence (kms/fence): a policy evaluator consulted by the kms-allocator. It is a fast allow/deny check that compares resolved key.location (region tag) against tenant.residency.allowed_geozones. If key fails check, the allocator falls back to an explicitly configured regional keyset; if none available, request is denied with 4xx and logged as policy_denied.kms_region. - Config: new tenant flag residency.enforce_kms_region (false by default) and a fallback keyset pointer residency.kms_fallback_keyset to preserve availability. - Observability: add two new metrics: audit.annotator.latency_ms and kms.fence.denied_count and a structured log field audit.context.permission_delta for use in Console queries. - Backwards compatibility: the annotator is additive (no contract changes to API). The KMS fence is opt-in per tenant to avoid breaking existing customers. A rollout will start with internal tenants and opt-in beta customers.

Li: 1) Introduce PermissionAuditAnnotator and tests 2) Wire annotator into auth pipeline 3) Add KMSRegionFence and allocator integration 4) Tenant config + migration guidance 5) Metrics and log schema 6) Integration tests (simulated multi-region tenant) 7) Docs and examples for console + linear references

Elena: "We intentionally run right after PDP to avoid latency in tokenization/generation phases. Added an adaptive fast-path: if request.token_count > 4096 and tenant.analytics.low_sensitivity == true, annotator tags 'skipped_for_latency' instead of full delta. See annotator.go:fastpath comment." - M. O'Connor (security): "What about cross-tenant operator leases — could an operator grant cause a delta that's misleading?" Elena: "We added operator.origin to the audit context and a cross-check in extractPermissionDelta to detect leases; when present we mark permission_change_kind='operator_elevated' and include lease_id in auth.trace." - R. Gupta (SRE): "If KMS denies a request due to missing fallback keyset, what's our incident escalation path?" Elena: "Denies are recorded as policy_denied.kms_region with tenant_id and request_id. The allocator emits metrics and an alert rule was added to SLO/alerting for >1% denies over 5m for production tenants. Docs include runbook playbook.")

Release notes: "Add permission provenance annotations to audit logs and an opt-in KMS multi-region fence to enforce residency constraints. See docs/residency-kms-fence.md for configuration and migration steps."

payload.body:
Background and motivation: We observed repeated headroom thrashing during moderate sustained bursts where deterministic backfill caused oscillation between warm and cold pools (see SUP-4123 incident notes). This PR implements two coordinated features: 1) an epochal randomized backfiller that staggers warm-pool replenishment across epochs to reduce correlated allocation spikes; and 2) a stochastic headroom controller that computes per-tenant probabilistic headroom allocations based on recent utilization jitter and a configurable confidence parameter. Together these reduce momentary oversubscription and improve fairness for small tenants while preserving throughput guarantees for committed capacity.

What changed (high level):
- autoscaler/epoch_backfill.go: new epochal backfill controller with randomized jitter and backoff windows.
- autoscaler/headroom_controller.go: new stochastic allocation engine that emits allocation proposals with an attached confidence score and TTL.
- autoscaler/hooks.go: integration points for the warm-pool reconciler to accept epochal backfill proposals.
- telemetry/utilization_fairness.md: documentation for the new fairness metrics and labels added to metrics emission.
- metrics/exporter.go: new metrics endpoints: redwood_autoscaler_headroom_proposal{tenant,confidence}, redwood_backfill_epoch_active, and a percentile sampler redwood_utilization_jitter_p50/p90.
- config/defaults.yaml: added knobs: epoch_backfill.window_ms, epoch_backfill.jitter_seed, headroom.confidence_default, headroom.max_ttl_ms.
- e2e/autoscale_backfill_test.go: deterministic test harness with synthetic tenants exercising staggered replenishment.
- docs/design/epochal-backfill.md: design rationale, failure modes, and rollout plan.

Implementation notes: The backfiller runs on an epoch boundary (default 10s) and computes a target set of warmlets to prewarm. Instead of issuing all prewarm requests immediately, it samples a shuffle offset derived from a tenant-scoped PRNG seeded by epoch_id xor jitter_seed. This ensures consistent but desynchronized replenishment across minutes without global coordination. The headroom controller ingests sliding-window utilization deltas and fits a lightweight asymmetric quantile estimator to produce a conservative proposal at the requested confidence. Proposals are advisory; the admission controller still validates hard reservation constraints.

Testing and CI: Unit tests cover PRNG behavior, headroom proposal math, and edge cases (empty history, sudden drop to zero). e2e tests simulate 100 tenants with mixed commit levels and assert that 95th-percentile cold-starts are reduced by ~25% in the synthetic workload. Initial CI run showed a flaky e2e related to timing; fixed by replacing time.Sleep-based synchronization with epoch barrier signals. All CI checks are green on the final push.

Rollout and safety: Feature-gated by config.features.epochal_backfill and headroom.enabled. Default is off for existing clusters. Rollout plan: canary on low-traffic pool for 24h, then incremental ramp to 25% of warm pools, monitor redwood_autoscaler_headroom_rejects and redwood_cold_start_95. If regressions are observed revert via runtime flag or return to previous commit.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for PRNG and headroom math
- [x] e2e reproducible harness
- [x] Metrics and dashboards updated
- [x] Docs and rollout plan included
- [x] Feature gate behind config flag

Related work and notes: This is complementary to the warm-pool smoothing work (see ENG-1983) but focuses on de-correlation rather than smoothing heuristics. Linear items: ENG-2147 (design), ENG-2204 (telemetry). Support ticket SUP-4123 provided incident traces that motivated desynchronization.

Commits summary: "epochal backfill controller initial implementation"; "stochastic headroom controller and proposer interface"; "metrics: headroom proposal and jitter percentiles"; "tests: deterministic epoch harness + e2e scenarios"; "docs: design + telemetry".

Changed areas/files (high level):
- pkg/autoscaler/epoch_backfill.go
- pkg/autoscaler/headroom_controller.go
- pkg/autoscaler/hooks.go
- pkg/telemetry/utilization_fairness.md
- pkg/metrics/exporter.go
- config/defaults.yaml
- test/e2e/autoscale_backfill_test.go
- docs/design/epochal-backfill.md

Review conversation (summary):
- Raj Patel (comment): "The PRNG seeding looks good but we should ensure reproducible results for replay tests — can we expose the jitter_seed as a test-only override?"
- Lena Park (reply): "Added jitter_seed override in config and test harness; updated tests to set a deterministic seed."
- Marta Alvarez (request_changes): "The headroom proposal includes a confidence float; we need a defensive clamp to avoid NaN when history is zero-length. Also add a metric for proposals rejected by admission controller so we can monitor mismatch between advisory and enforced constraints."
- Lena Park (reply): "Added clamp logic and proposed_rejects metric. Extended unit tests to cover zero-length windows and admission rejects."
- Owen Chen (approve): "Code looks clean, and tests exercise both happy-path and edge cases. I like the epoch barrier approach for e2e stability."
- Raj Patel (approve): "Verified canary run on staging for 6h; no regressions observed. Metrics show improved 95th cold-start latency under synthetic churn."

CI details: Build: passed; Unit tests: passed; Linters: passed; e2e: passed (after fix); Re-run of flaky job was manual with timestamped barrier.

Merge: merged via squash on 2026-03-01 by Lena Park. Merge commit message prefixed with "feat(autoscaler): epochal randomized backfill + stochastic headroom".

Notes for on-call: Watch metrics redwood_cold_start_95, redwood_autoscaler_headroom_proposal_rejects, redwood_backfill_epoch_active. If warm-pool oversubscription is observed, flip config.features.epochal_backfill=false and allow the autoscaler to reconcile.
