Motivation: developer feedback loops on lint and lightweight regressions were costing time. This PR introduces a two-stage lint pipeline that provides near-instant feedback for changed files and shifts full lint and formatting checks to later pipeline stages. It also adds a 'release-smoke' gating step to release automation so releases must pass a small, fast e2e smoke battery before a draft is published.

What this changes (summary):
- New workflow: .github/workflows/lint-staged.yml — runs quick linters (flake8/ruff/tsc-check) only on changed paths detected by git diff against base branch; returns early on trivial changes.
- Keep the existing full lint job but move to a slower pipeline stage with a longer timeout and isolation: .github/workflows/lint-full.yml.
- CI cache TTLs: adjusted cache key patterns and introduced short-lived TTL for per-branch fast caches and longer TTL for shared artifacts (see .github/cache/policies.md). This reduces stale cache hits and avoids large cache growth in the monorepo.
- Release automation: .github/workflows/release.yml updated to require jobs.release-smoke to pass before creating/publishing a release draft. The smoke job performs a minimal set of integration checks (health endpoint, basic model inference path using a small test model, and infra provisioning smoke tasks) to catch obvious regressions earlier.
- Repo hygiene: removed legacy scripts/prepare-commit-hook.sh and replaced with a lightweight staged pre-commit that only runs on developer machines if configured. CI enforces lint-format checks so local hooks are advisory.

Why staged lint?
- Fast feedback for PR authors: changed-file detection reduces the typical lint job from ~6m to <45s for most small PRs.
- Keeps full lint coverage for merging to ensure repo stability.

Checklist (all run/validated):
- [x] Add lint-staged workflow and unit tests for changed-file detection logic.
- [x] Update docs: dev-infra/ci-lint.md with new developer guidance.
- [x] Add cache policy file and update cache keying to include TTL metadata.
- [x] Wire release-smoke into release workflow and verify gating in a dry run.
- [x] Remove legacy pre-commit script and update CONTRIBUTING.md.

How to test locally:
- Run: ./dev/ci-scripts/run-staged-lint.sh --base main --paths src/redwood-client/*.py
- Emulate release smoke: ./dev/ci-scripts/run-release-smoke.sh --env test

Notes and trade-offs:
- Staged lint relies on git-diff heuristics; we added unit tests and a small fallback to run full lint if detection fails.
- Cache TTLs are conservative; we may longitudinally tune them if cache churn is high.
- Release-smoke intentionally keeps scope narrow to avoid blocking legitimate releases; broader e2e coverage remains in nightly pipelines.

Related: Linear ENG-1421 (fast lint pipeline) and ENG-1422 (release smoke automation).
Arjun: Left a note about caching key collision when branch names contain slashes — added a hash-based sanitizer. Lena: Requested a guard in release-smoke to skip for emergency hotfix branches; implemented a skip flag. Noah: Verified staged-lint reduces runtime on sample PRs and approved. CI initially failed a flaky integration test 'integration/db-connection' in run #3; test was re-run and passed; we added a follow-up item to stabilize the test (ENG-1489).
Introduce staged lint fast-feedback job and release-smoke gating for release automation; adjust CI cache TTLs and remove deprecated pre-commit hook. Improves dev feedback and reduces CI cost for small PRs.
Smoke gate runs a small battery (health check, minimal inference, provision check). QA should verify release workflow is blocked if smoke fails and allowed when smoke passes. See dev-infra/ci-lint.md for local reproduction steps.
ENG-1489 Stabilize integration/db-connection test; ENG-1510 Tune cache TTLS after 2 weeks of telemetry; add optional local pre-commit installer UX improvement
Merged after approvals and green CI. Rollout: the staged-lint workflow is enabled for all repo pushes; release-smoke gating will initially be enabled for release/* branches and then widened after one week of telemetry.
payload.title: Introduce staged lint fast-feedback slices and release-smoke gating

Motivation: We frequently need a low-cost sampling path to discover tenant prefill shapes and cold-start ratios for better default batching/caching and quantization recommendations. Larger profilers add cost and complexity during onboarding. This PR introduces a slimline prefill prober (sidecar) plus a conservative 'soft-guard' layer for quant profile rollouts to reduce unit-econ regressions while allowing aggressive trialing in canaries.

Summary of changes: single continuous description with commits, file-level summary, tests and review threads.

What this does: adds a minimal sidecar that samples a configurable percentage of incoming requests' token-length distribution and prefix reuse heuristics; emits compact telemetry and local sketches (count-min + histograms) for the optimizer. Adds a quant soft-guard that: 1) evaluates candidate quant profiles server-side in a low-fidelity simulator, 2) assigns a risk score, and 3) blocks automatic tenant-wide promotion if risk > threshold (with a telemetry-driven override). Also wires a canary flow to allow restricted rollout and an automatic safe-rollback when quality regressions are detected.

Design notes: the prober intentionally avoids full KV cache capture to reduce storage and privacy scope; all sketches are kept per-tenant and TTL'd. Metrics are labeled for model, tenant, route, and observed sequence-length bucket. The soft-guard uses sampled outputs + a lightweight quality fingerprint (BLEU-like delta for deterministic evals, token-entropy delta for generative paths) to detect regressions.

Commits: - b1f4c2a: add slim prober sidecar and config knobs - a9d44f7: telemetry schema and compact histogram encoder - 0c3be11: quant soft-guard runtime check + risk calculator - 7f2d992: canary/rollback controller and CLI flags - 2a8b5ef: TS SDK hooks and small example for console - e1f0c3d: unit/integration tests and benchmarks

Files changed (high-level): - pkg/prefill/prober.go: sidecar worker, sampling logic, sketch encoder - runtime/quant/softguard.go: risk scoring and rollout gating - telemetry/schemas/prefill_metrics.yaml: compact metric shapes - console/examples/prefill-demo.md: usage and config snippets - sdk/typescript/hooks/prefill.ts: hook to expose sampled stats to the Console - tools/canary-controller/canary.go: lightweight canary controller and rollback path - tests/prefill/prober_test.go, tests/quant/softguard_test.go - charts/prefill-sidecar/values.yaml: helm defaults for Private/Dedicated installs

Small code excerpt (illustrative): "func SampleAndSketch(req Request) { if rand.Float32() > cfg.SampleRate { return } sketch.Add(req.Tokens.Len()) emitCompactMetric(sketch.Flush()) }"

Benchmarks & results (local microbench): - prefiller CPU overhead: ~0.6% at 1% sample rate - telemetry payload: ~1.3KB per minute per 10k reqs (compressed) - quant soft-guard simulation: 8-15ms per candidate profile on a 4-vCPU test harness - end-to-end unit-econ impact in tests: median per-token CPU down 3.2% after safe rollouts, max observed quality delta within configured thresholds.

Testing: unit tests for sampling/sketch correctness, integration tests for soft-guard gating, end-to-end simulation with synthetic workloads. Added smoke test to CI that runs a tiny canary flow (30s).

Review conversation (highlights): 
- Maya Chen (reviewer): "Can we guarantee prober telemetry doesn't include any user PII?"
  - Arjun: "Yes — prober only records token-lengths, prefix-hash (one-way salted), and sequence buckets. No text copied. Added unit tests to validate no raw_text fields are emitted."
- Liam O'Connor: "Risk scoring looks good; can we expose the threshold as a tenant opt-in?"
  - Arjun: "Added tenant-level override in the helm values and Console toggle; default remains platform-controlled."
- Sofia Alvarez: "Concerned about the extra 15ms simulation time for large candidate sets."
  - Arjun: "We limit simulations to the top-3 candidate profiles in canary; added an adaptive timeout and a circuit-breaker if simulation exceeds 50ms per-request flow."

CI: All checks passed after two reruns. One flaky unit test (quant_sim_test) was flapping; fixed by replacing a time-dependent seed with deterministic fixture. CI summary: build (pass), unit (pass), integration (pass), e2e-smoke (pass), lint (pass).

Backward compatibility & upgrade notes: this is additive; sidecar can be deployed independently. Helm chart defaults keep the prober disabled for air-gapped installs by default. No breaking API changes.

Merging: Squash merge after signoff. Merged by Maya Chen on 2024-11-20; merge method: squash.

Follow-ups / TODOs: - Add an opt-in dashboard in Console for prefill heatmaps (ENG-3187) - Export compact sketches to the unit-econ simulator for long-run profiling - Add privacy review ticket for EU deployments (PM-513).
Adds a lightweight prefill prober sidecar to collect compact workload signals and a conservative quantization soft-guard that enables safe rollbacks during canary. No user-facing API changes.
Related: ENG-3129 (sampling requirements)
Canary flow tested against staging tenant 'acme-corp'

Motivation: reduce noisy user-visible regressions during canary promotions by ensuring session-affine traffic stays pinned while enabling deterministic shadow replay for offline verification before promotion. This PR implements a session-pinned canary lane that pins user sessions to the incumbent variant until a session-safe handoff completes and introduces a deterministic shadow replay path that replays sampled live requests into candidate models with preserved session state. Key goals: maintain session consistency for stateful flows, provide reproducible shadow results for automated regression detectors, and support graceful drain with end-to-end idempotency guarantees. Design summary: 1) Session affinity tokens: requests now carry a stable session token used by the canary conductor to decide pinning eligibility. 2) Handoff protocol: a three-phase handshake (prepare, verify, commit) that verifies KV-cache compatibility and replay parity before committing session transfers. 3) Deterministic shadow replay: captured request + session KV is replayed through the candidate in a deterministic executor that disables non-deterministic hooks and seeds RNGs. Replays are recorded to the shadow-results store for batch evaluation. 4) Graceful drain and rewind: if a safety gate trips, affected sessions are rewound to incumbent within the same flow using snapshot checkpointing. 5) Metrics and telemetry: new histograms for replay-latency, replay-diff-score, and session-handoff-duration; integrated into console rollout dashboard. Checklist: - [x] core conductor protocol and handshake implementation - [x] deterministic executor and replay capture - [x] session snapshotting and rewind hooks - [x] telemetry, tracing spans, and dashboard wiring - [x] unit and e2e smoke tests - [x] rollout playbook and runbook entry Backwards compatibility: falls back to existing stateless canaries when session tokens are absent. Migration notes: to enable session-pinned canaries an operator flag must be set and a short config migration on Dedicated clusters performed to enable checkpoint storage. Security: session tokens are treated as opaque identifiers and not logged; replay store encrypted with existing KMS keys. Commit summary: small focused commits for protocol and tests followed by a squash for release. See commits below. CI: flaky integration test (replay-suite) retried once; all checks passed on final run. Merge strategy: squash and merge. Impact: primarily rollout conductor and runtime executor changes; rollout safety gates tightened. Release notes: Adds session-aware canaries and deterministic shadow replay for safer model promotions, enabled via operator flag. No breaking API changes.
Diego Alvarez: The handshake looks solid but we need to ensure the prepare phase has a timeout so we don't block on stuck sessions. Can we also add an audit span for prepare/verify/commit?
Maya Chen: Added prepare timeout with configurable default 30s. Added tracing spans for each phase and surfaced them in console. See commit d9910ff and f3a8a11.
Priya Natarajan: The deterministic executor disables a few runtime optimizations. We should document the performance tradeoffs and ensure replay sampling rate is conservative by default.
Maya Chen: Documented tradeoffs in protocol.md and set default replay sampling to 0.5% with operator override. Added dashboard alert if replay backlog grows > 5k requests.
Jonah Brooks: Tests are thorough; one nit — snapshot_store restore should validate checksum before applying to runtime to avoid corrupt KV states.
Maya Chen: Added checksum validation and test coverage for snapshot restore paths.
payload.title: Session-pinned canary with deterministic shadow replay and graceful drain

payload.body:
Context and motivation:
We keep seeing customer production failures where naive client retries (especially across streaming tool-invocations) either trigger duplicate side-effects or fail to respect per-customer transient capacity limits. Previous effort focused on clarifying 429 semantics and idempotency key formats, but two pain points remain: (1) idempotency keys are long-lived and encourage reuse across logically distinct operations, and (2) the server's "Retry-After" hints are either too sparse or ambiguous for streaming/tool-call flows.

This PR implements two coordinated server-side changes in the OpenAI compatibility layer and the toolkit used by tool-calling/runbook integrations: (A) lease-based idempotency tokens (short-lived, single-use leases that carry scope and validation metadata), and (B) an adaptive retry-window envelope returned in a structured response header/frame to guide client backoff with finer granularity and jitter hints. Together these reduce duplicate side-effects while giving clients better signals to avoid hot retries during capacity pressure.

What this changes (high level):
- New header: X-Idempotency-Lease: a short opaque lease token issued on request acceptance when idempotency is requested via the existing Idempotency-Key. Leases are single-use and time-bound (default TTL 60s, configurable per route).
- New structured retry envelope header: Retry-Hint: base64url(JSON) where JSON = {"retry_after_ms": int, "jitter_ms": int, "lease_backoff": "boolean", "scope": "string", "hint_version": "v1"}. The header is attached to non-success responses (429/503/504) and to a final control frame for streamed failures.
- Streaming contract: for streamed responses we add a final control SSE frame (event:control, data: <base64url JSON error envelope>) when an in-stream error occurs; the envelope includes the same fields as Retry-Hint plus an error_code and ephemeral_lease (if applicable).
- Idempotency refinement: the adapter now issues ephemeral leases when the incoming Idempotency-Key is detected but we need a bounded scope to protect internal retries. Clients may present either an Idempotency-Key (legacy) or the X-Idempotency-Lease (preferred after initial acceptance). Leases are validated atomically with the operation and revoked on completion.
- Error normalization: unify error_code strings to the format namespace.action.error (e.g., "rate_limit.write.exceeded", "tool.execution.timeout"). We also return a top-level canonical message and an errors[] list for richer clients.

Design notes and rationale:
- Lease model avoids reuse across disconnected operations: a long-lived API token (Idempotency-Key) is still honored to derive intent, but any actual deduplication uses the short-lived lease which guarantees bounded state and simpler revocation semantics for retries/failover.
- Retry-Hint carries a jitter_ms value so SDKs can implement randomized backoff within server-specified bounds; lease_backoff=true indicates clients should renew/obtain a fresh lease before retrying tool-invocations that have side-effects.
- Streaming control frame ensures that streamed tool-call failures are surfaced with the same structured guidance as regular responses and that intermediate frames are not misinterpreted as retriable success.

API compatibility and client guidance:
- Backwards compatible: existing clients that only look at HTTP 429/Retry-After will continue to work. New clients can prefer Retry-Hint/X-Idempotency-Lease. If both Idempotency-Key and X-Idempotency-Lease are supplied, lease wins for deduplication semantics.
- SDK changes (separate PRs ongoing for python/ts): SDKs should automatically parse Retry-Hint, honor jitter_ms, and only retry tool-calls when lease_backoff=false OR after acquiring a fresh lease. Streaming clients should listen for control frames and follow the envelope rather than heuristics like connection close times.

Implementation summary (files changed):
- src/openai_adapter/handler.go: add header parsing and lease issuance/validation, attach Retry-Hint on error paths.
- src/openai_adapter/streaming_control.go: new helper to emit final control frames for streaming failures.
- internal/idempotency/lease_store.go: implement in-memory + redis-backed lease store with TTL and revocation.
- internal/errors/normalize.go: map internal error categories to canonical error_code strings.
- tests/integration/openai_adapter_retry_test.go: add tests for lease lifecycle, header parsing, streaming control frames.
- docs/openai_adapter.md: document header formats, example sequences, and migration guidance.
- sdk-adapters/compat/README.md: short note for SDK maintainers.

Commits (summary):
- 7e2f1b2: introduce lease store interface and redis implementation
- 9a4d3c8: wire lease issuance into request acceptance path in adapter handler
- a63f9e1: emit Retry-Hint header for 429/503 and populate structured envelope for streaming failures
- b2c4d69: normalize error codes and update tests for canonical messages
- c4d5e8a: docs + migration guidance + small refactor of existing idempotency unit tests

Testing and CI:
- Added unit tests for lease TTL/renewal/reject semantics.
- Integration tests cover: (1) client retries using Idempotency-Key results in unused lease; (2) client uses lease and server rejects second use; (3) Retry-Hint header contains jitter_ms and sensible bounds; (4) streaming flow includes final control frame when a tool-call errors mid-stream.
- CI initially failed on a flaky timing test in integration (intermittent sleep races). I adjusted the test harness to use deterministic fake clock for lease TTLs and re-ran CI. Final run: all checks green (lint / unit / integration / e2e).

Security and operational considerations:
- Leases are opaque tokens and rotate regularly; we intentionally keep leases single-use and short TTL to reduce blast radius if leaked.
- Redis-backed lease store offers eventual consistency trade-offs; we added an atomic compare-and-revoke step to avoid double-accepts on concurrent requests. For weaker backends we fall back to a best-effort strategy and emit metrics when collisions are observed.
- Monitoring: new metrics lease.issued, lease.used, lease.rejected, retry_hint.emitted. Added dashboard to SLO team for early detection.

Review conversation (high level):
- Diego Ramos: "Nice approach. Two asks: add a test for concurrent lease race on our redis cluster emulator and ensure the lease size is limited (no enormous headers)."
- Maya (author): "Added concurrent race test using the emulator and capped lease token size to 128 bytes, storing longer entropy server-side."
- Priya Natarajan: "Can we avoid clients having to parse base64 headers? Would an alt header be better?"
- Maya: "We considered JSON header but some proxies strip complex headers; base64url(JSON) keeps a single header safe-cross-proxy. SDKs will expose helpers to decode. Documented in docs/openai_adapter.md."
- Samir Goyal: "Streaming control frame payload: confirm we don't expose secrets in envelopes and that they are signed if we later allow cross-service retries."
- Maya: "Control frames contain only non-sensitive fields and ephemeral_lease tokens. We validated with security — if we later enable cross-service lease handoff we'll add HMAC signatures and audit logs."

Merge outcome:
- Merge method: squash and merge.
- Post-merge actions: SDK teams were pinged (PR references in python/ts SDK repos) with migration checklist and example code for parsing Retry-Hint and using X-Idempotency-Lease. Ops scheduled a 24h canary rollout for high-throughput routes to monitor lease collision rates.

Risk and next steps:
- Risk: client adoption lag may lead to mixed behavior during rollout; mitigated by backwards compatibility and conservative default TTLs.
- Next steps: follow-up PRs to add HMAC-signed leases for inter-service handoff, SDK updates to expose helpers, and optional telemetry headers for per-request sampling of retry decisions.

If you'd like, I can split the lease store implementation into a standalone package and open a follow-up to add signed lease tokens.
Introduce lease-scoped idempotency tokens and a structured adaptive retry-window envelope returned by the OpenAI adapter; clients should prefer new headers but fall back to existing semantics.
payload.title: lease-based-idempotency-and-adaptive-retry-window-in-openai-adapter

payload.body:
Introduces ephemeral scale allocator and lane synchronizer which reduce per-token allocation overhead on INT8 hotpaths; fuses dequant+transpose+requant microkernel; KV cache coalescer improves continuous-batching throughput. Measured p50 latency down 8-12% and throughput up ~18% on typical INT8 workloads. No user-facing API changes.
Context and motivation:
We identified two runtime inefficiencies on our INT8/FP8 serving paths that disproportionately affect short-lived hotpath allocations and continuous batching with KV cache traffic: 1) per-token temporary scale buffers are allocated/freed frequently across lanes, increasing allocator pressure and jitter; 2) KV cache prefetches and continuous batching introduce cross-lane contention during slot alignment which prevents optimal coalescing of microbatches.

This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: an ephemeral scale allocator and a lock-free lane synchronizer. The ephemeral allocator reuses small per-request scale buffers from a per-worker ring with epoch-based reclamation (no central locks). The lane synchronizer provides a light-weight rendezvous primitive that aligns KV-prefetch windows across active lanes so the continuous batcher can merge token batches with lower overhead. In addition, we add a compact fused microkernel (fused_deq_transpose_requant) for the common path INT8->FP16 compute->INT8/FP8 fallback to eliminate intermediate copies.

What changed (single-string description with checklist):
- Implement ephemeral scale allocator with epoch reclamation and config flag: runtime.ephemeral_scale.enabled (default true)
- Add lane synchronizer primitive and integrate with continuous-batcher and kv-prefetch coordinator
- Implement fused_deq_transpose_requant microkernel (C++ + CUDA) with integer scaling LUT path for INT8
- Scheduler hints: allow scheduler to prefer "lane_coalesced" bundles when synchronizer is active
- Small API: expose internal metric keys: runtime.ephemeral_scale.reuse_rate, runtime.lane_sync.wait_ms, runtime.kv_coalesce.merge_ratio
- Unit tests for allocator and synchronizer, integration test for continuous-batcher correctness
- Bench harness updates and a perf job that collects p50/p95 latency and token throughput for INT8 workloads

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc attached (link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2042/ephemeral-scale-allocator-design)
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] Perf benchmarks run in benchmark-lab (job id: bench/2026-01-25/ephemeral-scale)
- [x] Feature gated behind runtime.ephemeral_scale.enabled and can be disabled via env var
- [x] No public API breaking changes

Commits (summary):
- 7c3a9d1 Implement ephemeral scale allocator with epoch reclamation and tests
- b1f7e44 Add lane synchronizer primitive and continuous-batcher integration
- d2e4f20 fused_deq_transpose_requant microkernel and CUDA launch wrapper
- a9f5b33 Scheduler hint plumbing + metrics export for reuse/merge ratios
- f0c8a66 Fix race in epoch reclamation under high concurrency (addressed review)
- e6b1f12 Bench harness: add INT8 hotpath scenario and perf report script

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/alloc/ephemeral_scale_allocator.{h,cpp}  (allocator core + tests)
- runtime/kv/lane_synchronizer.{h,cpp}  (rendezvous primitive)
- runtime/batching/continuous_batcher.cpp  (use lane synchronizer when enabled)
- runtime/kernels/fused_deq_transpose_requant.cu  (new microkernel)
- runtime/kernels/launcher.cpp  (kernel registration and fallback path)
- runtime/scheduler/scheduler_hints.cpp  (new enum and preference code)
- bench/benchmarks/int8_hotpath.yaml  (bench job definition)
- tests/integration/kv_coalesce_integration.test  (integration test)
- docs/ops/feature_flags.md  (document runtime.ephemeral_scale flag)

Small code excerpt (allocator usage in continuous_batcher, illustrative):
``
// reuse scale buffer from local ring; falls back to stack if disabled
auto* buf = allocator->acquire(scale_size);
apply_scale_inplace(buf, tokens);
allocator->release(buf);
```

Benchmarks (benchmark-lab; single-run median numbers):
- Workload: 2048-token long-chained chat, INT8 quantized model (gpt-like)
- Baseline (main, no allocator/sync): p50 = 42.1ms, tokens/sec = 23.4k, cost/token = 1.00x
- With changes: p50 = 37.6ms (-10.7%), tokens/sec = 27.6k (+17.9%), cost/token ~= 0.86x (-14%)
- p95 improved modestly (~6-8ms) due to reduced allocation jitter

Correctness and safety notes:
- Ephemeral allocator uses epoch-based reclamation to avoid ABA/free-after-free while remaining lock-free for the common path. Fallback path uses thread-local stack allocation for very small sizes (<64B) to avoid cross-lane contention in microbench workloads.
- The fused kernel contains a fallback path to the prior dequant->transpose->requant sequence when input shapes or alignment are not supported. A config flag runtime.kernels.fused_deq.enabled controls usage.

Review thread (high-level):
- Liam O'Connor (reviewer) 2026-01-19: "Nice microkernel. Concern: epoch reclamation loop may spin under heavy stall; prefer exponential backoff and metric for active stalls."
- Maya Chen (author) 2026-01-20: "Added backoff and a metric runtime.ephemeral_scale.backoff_count. Also added tighter unit tests that simulate stalls."
- Priya Desai (reviewer) 2026-01-21: "Please add a smoke test that runs fused kernel with FP8 fallback on CPU CI runner."
- Maya Chen 2026-01-22: "Added CPU fallback smoke test and CI job entry. Also fixed a UB on misaligned 4-byte loads reported by sanitizer."
- Diego Morales (reviewer) 2026-01-24: "Run results look good; request to add a scheduler opt-out when pod-level latency SLO is tight."
- Maya Chen 2026-01-24: "Added scheduler opt-out config runtime.scheduler.allow_lane_coalesce (default true) and surfaced note in docs."
- CI history: initial push failed lint (clang-format) and a flaky test `kv_cache_eviction.test`; both addressed in follow-up commits and all checks passed on 2026-01-27.

Performance experiments and follow-ups:
- Bench run attached: bench/2026-01-25/ephemeral-scale/report.json (internal artifact). Summary above.
- Follow-up work: extend fused kernel to support per-head quantization scale LUT (ENG-2101) and evaluate FP8-only fastpath in a subsequent PR.

Merge outcome:
- Approvals: Liam O'Connor, Priya Desai, Diego Morales
- Merge method: squash-and-merge on 2026-01-29 by Maya Chen
- Post-merge: Canary rollout to dedicated cluster pool with eps=0.1; monitored metric runtime.ephemeral_scale.reuse_rate and runtime.kv_coalesce.merge_ratio for one week; no regressions observed.

Notes for operators:
- Default is safe-on: ephemeral allocator on, fused kernel enabled only for supported shapes. To disable: set RUNTIME_EPHEMERAL_SCALE=0 and RUNTIME_KERNELS_FUSED_DEQ=0 in the agent config.

If there are any questions about interaction with Dedicated autoscaling or Private installer, ping me (Maya) or ENG-2042 in Linear.
payload.title: Ephemeral scale allocator + lane synchronizer for compact INT8 hotpath

payload.body:
Motivation: customers reported sporadic 401s during long pull/stream sessions and awkward ergonomics for checking stream liveness. This PR introduces a lightweight credential 'sliding window' that normalizes prefetch timing across SDKs, plus two small stream ergonomics helpers (peek_end and wait_for_end) and instrumentation to correlate reauth events with stream traces. Changes span Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs and docs. What changed: 1) Credential sliding window: add a tunable lease_window and prefetch_margin to SDK credential providers so refresh is deterministic across clock skew and latency. Default profile keeps behavior identical but allows operators to reduce reauth jitter for long-lived streams. 2) Stream ergonomics: add Stream.peek_end() to poll if the upstream finished without consuming tokens, and Stream.wait_for_end(timeout) as a convenience awaitable. Implementations are fully non-blocking and optimized for the host runtime (asyncio/promises/goroutines). 3) Telemetry: emit stream.reauth.attempt and stream.reauth.success spans and attach credential_window arg for easier debugging in Console. 4) Cross-SDK parity work: align arg names and defaults across py/ts/go, bump versions (py 0.12.4 -> 0.12.5, ts 1.6.2 -> 1.6.3, go v1.5.1 -> v1.5.2). 5) Tests and docs: add unit and integration tests to cover the window edge cases and update quickstart examples and changelog. Rollout plan: feature guarded behind SDK feature flag (CRED_WINDOW_ALPHA); default is off in existing published builds so behavior is opt-in for early adopters. Impact: reduces observed 401 spikes during sustained streams, clarifies telemetry for SRE, and gives app authors ergonomic primitives for stream lifecycle. Checklist: - [x] API signatures reviewed across SDKs - [x] Telemetry schema bump registered - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration test with dedicated runtime - [x] Docs/quickstart updated - [x] Version bumps staged

Ava Chen: Discussed offline with Diego; added margin_mode config (absolute_seconds | percentage) and left default as absolute_seconds for backward compatibility. Added docs to explain tradeoffs.
Priya Kapoor: In TS, peek_end currently allocates an extra promise on each poll; can we reuse an internal pending promise to reduce churn?
Ava Chen: Updated TS implementation to reuse a single deferred promise for the peek path, added benchmark microtest, results show ~10% fewer allocations under steady polling.
Liam O'Neill: CI showed flakey TestStreamTimeout in Go initially — root cause was a race on context cancellation. Please ensure context teardown ordering is deterministic.
Ava Chen: Fixed Go test by moving cancel after pipeline drain; reran CI and test stabilized.
a1f4d2b: introduce credential sliding window primitive (py/ts/go)
b2c8f91: add Stream.peek_end() and Stream.wait_for_end(timeout) helpers (py/ts/go)
c3d9ea0: emit stream.reauth.* telemetry and attach credential_window tags
d4e1f77: tests: add window edge cases and stream lifecycle integration tests
e5f2b33: docs: quickstart and changelog updates; version bumps

Behavior is opt-in by default. We plan to monitor stream.reauth.* events for two weeks post-release before recommending enabling globally for customers with high-volume long-lived streams.

payload.body:
## Context
We’ve had intermittent marketplace onboarding/provisioning delays where a customer subscribes in AWS/GCP Marketplace but Redwood does not reflect entitlement quickly enough (or at all) due to transient upstream errors and non-idempotent reprocessing. This has shown up as:
- SUP-4821: entitlement/provisioning delay after subscription (support escalation)
- SUP-4829: confusion from partial sync + billing dimension mismatch during replays

Root cause in recent cases: the entitlement sync worker treats some partner/API failures as terminal, and on retry/replay can double-emit "entitlement_granted" side effects (email/webhook + provisioning steps), leading to noisy logs and occasional inconsistent state.

## What’s in this PR
1) **Retries + backoff for upstream calls**
- Adds bounded exponential backoff with jitter for marketplace provider fetches (AWS entitlement lookup + GCP entitlement listing).
- Retries only on retryable classes (timeouts, 429, 5xx, connection resets). Does *not* retry on 4xx validation errors.
- Enforces a max wall-clock budget per job run to avoid thundering herds.

2) **Idempotency keys for entitlement processing**
- Introduces an idempotency key per (provider, account, subscription_id, entitlement_version) for:
  - entitlement upsert
  - event emission (provisioning + audit/event bus)
- Ensures that reruns (manual or scheduled) do not create duplicate side effects.
- Adds a DB uniqueness constraint and a best-effort "already processed" fast-path.

3) **SRE hooks: metrics + alerting signals**
- Emits explicit metrics for:
  - `marketplace_entitlement_sync_attempts_total{provider, outcome}`
  - `marketplace_entitlement_sync_duration_ms{provider}`
  - `marketplace_entitlement_sync_retryable_failures_total{provider}`
  - `marketplace_entitlement_sync_backlog_depth`
- Adds alert conditions (wired to existing alert manager routing):
  - sustained retryable failures > threshold (10m)
  - p95 sync duration regression (30m)
  - backlog depth not draining (15m)
- Includes runbook link + dashboard panel IDs in the alert annotations.

4) **Safer job semantics**
- Makes sync job processing idempotent across restarts by persisting a per-run `sync_run_id` and using it only for tracing (not for state transitions).
- Adds explicit "partial failure" outcome codes so we can distinguish: upstream failures vs internal DB deadlocks vs provider throttling.

## How to test
- Unit tests:
  - retry classification matrix (timeouts/429/5xx vs 4xx)
  - idempotency key generation stability
  - event emission dedupe
- Integration tests (uses the existing marketplace stub server):
  - simulate 2x transient 503 then 200; verify eventual success with single entitlement record + single event
  - simulate provider throttling (429); verify backoff + job budget
  - replay same subscription sync; verify no duplicate side effects

## Operational notes
- Default retry policy: max 6 attempts, base delay 250ms, max delay 5s, full jitter.
- A single run is capped at 45s wall-clock to prevent overlap with the next scheduled invocation.
- This should reduce time-to-entitlement for marketplace customers and prevent duplicate provisioning steps when support triggers manual reruns.

## Follow-ups
- (ENG-22114) add funnel instrumentation to correlate entitlement sync latency with onboarding drop-off.
- Move alert thresholds to config once we have 2 weeks of baseline after launch.

CC: @Cole Summers for billing/metering semantics; @Nadia Rahman for metrics naming consistency.

Cole Summers: Can we confirm the idempotency key includes the provider subscription version (or equivalent) so upgrades/downgrades aren’t accidentally deduped? Also, please document how this interacts with metering dimension mapping to avoid SUP-4829 repeats.
Ethan Park (author): Yep — key is (provider, provider_account_id, subscription_id, entitlement_version). For AWS we use the entitlement "Revision"/"Version" field; for GCP we use entitlement updateTime (rounded to ms) + planId. Added a short note in entitlement_events.ts docs and a test that verifies upgrade emits a new side-effect record.
Nadia Rahman: Metric names look good. Can we add `provider` label cardinality guardrails and ensure we don’t label on customer/org id? Also, what’s the expected baseline for backlog_depth alert threshold?
Ethan Park (author): No customer/org labels — only provider + outcome. I added a lint check in marketplace_metrics.ts to block org-scoped labels. For backlog threshold, I set initial warn at >200 for 15m based on the last incident peak; we can tune after 2 weeks of data as noted in follow-ups.
Priya Natarajan: Wall-clock budget at 45s — any risk of starving large accounts? We don’t want perpetual partial runs.
Ethan Park (author): Good call. We process in batches ordered by oldest `last_synced_at` first; we persist a cursor and resume next run. Added an info log + metric when we hit budget so we can see if we’re consistently truncating. If it shows up, we can bump concurrency or split by provider.
Leila Farouk: Integration tests pass locally. Please add one more case for DB deadlock retry (we’ve seen it under load).
Ethan Park (author): Added a test that injects a simulated serialization failure and verifies we retry the transaction once with jittered delay. Pushed in latest commit.
Priya Natarajan: Approved after last test addition. Let’s make sure SRE has the runbook link before merge.
Ethan Park (author): Runbook link added to alert annotations + posted in #eng-platform thread. Merging.
payload.title: Hardening: entitlement sync job retries, idempotency keys, and SRE alert hooks

Context: On-call teams frequently spend the first 10-30 minutes of an incident assembling what 'normal' looks like for the impacted route and then hunting for the earliest divergence. We built a lightweight Golden-Run diff flow and an oncall triage hub to compress that work into a few clicks.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Adds an 'obs-triage-hub' microservice that ingests golden-run artifacts (serialized invocation profiles produced by our synthetic-runner), computes per-route delta rollups (latency percentiles, token-cost, kernel queue indicators, KV cache hit rate), and stores compact diff summaries for fast query. Exposes a small HTTP API for: (1) registerGoldenRun, (2) computeDiffAgainstBaseline, (3) fetchRepresentativeSnippets for a route/time-window. Adds a weighted-log-sampler that scores candidate log lines by a combination of severity, uniqueness, and token-density to return 3–5 representative snippets per diff that are surfaced in Console.

In Console: introduces a new 'Golden Run diff' dashboard (console/dashboards/golden_run_diff.json) and a timeline component (diff_timeline.tsx) that overlays current metric stream against baseline percentiles and highlights the first divergent segment. Each diff tile includes direct links to: the runbook (runbooks/golden_run_triage.md), the triage hub API trace, and a pre-populated PagerDuty annotation template.

Operational safeguards: added a noise gate that ignores diffs driven by low-volume routes (threshold configured via feature flag) and a cardinality guard to downsample routes with high tag cardinality prior to diff computation.

Checklist:
- [x] design doc + Linear: ENG-4218
- [x] triage hub service with ingestion API and diff runner
- [x] console dashboard + timeline widget
- [x] weighted log sampler and snippet extractor
- [x] runbook with triage steps and PagerDuty templates
- [x] e2e test harness and fixture data (ci/e2e/golden_run)
- [x] CI passes and manual smoke test on staging

Commits (high-level): d4b9f3f adds the hub skeleton and API; a7c0e2b wires dashboard panels and console plumbing; f1e7bad implements the heuristic sampler and snippet extraction; 8b2c114 adds an e2e fixture and test asserting diff outputs remain stable for the canonical golden run.

Files changed (high level): see changed_files list — notable additions are the diff runner (observability/triage-hub/internal/diff/runner.go), the snippet extractor (telemetry/logsampler/snippet_extractor.go), and the console JSON dashboard. The dashboard layout is intentionally compact to avoid query explosion; it uses precomputed compact diff summaries served by the triage hub instead of joining raw timeseries in the browser.

Review conversation summary: 
- Tom Barlow (review): requested that the diff payload include the model variant and quantization tag to help explain cost deltas. Action: added those metadata fields to the ingest API (d4b9f3f).
- Evelyn Zhang (review): observed high tag cardinality in early runs; asked for a fallback to coarse-grained route buckets and a sampling cap. Action: implemented route-bucket hashing and a per-tenant cap with an opt-in precise mode (f1e7bad). Evelyn approved after smoke tests.
- Marcus Holt (review): asked for a test covering the snippet extractor's dedup heuristic to avoid surfacing repeated log frames; author added unit tests and an e2e that asserts non-duplicated snippets in the returned set (8b2c114).

CI summary: Initial run failed in linters (gofmt) and a flaky e2e (timing-dependent). Fixes: applied formatting and hardened e2e timing to use deterministic fixture timestamps. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, integration, e2e).

Operational notes & rollout: feature gated behind 'golden_run_diff' feature flag. Staged rollout: enabled for staging tenants on 2025-11-05, small cohort of production tenants 2025-11-09, full rollout 2025-11-11. Monitored: per-route diff compute latency, diff queue length, and sampler error rate. Added alert: obs.triage.diff.compute.latency.p95 > 2s for 5m -> page SRE.

Runbook excerpt (runbooks/golden_run_triage.md): first step: fetch golden-run diff for route -> if diff shows latency increase >20 ppoints and token-cost > 15% -> fetch representative snippets -> check kernel queue and kv cache hit rate panels -> if kernel queue elevated, escalate to infra; otherwise continue model/config/traffic RCA.

Merge: approved by Evelyn Zhang and Marcus Holt. Squashed and merged into main on 2025-11-12.

Notes for follow-ups (future PRs):
- persistence compaction for multi-day golden-run archives (ENG-4270)
- UI: enable side-by-side prompt-level diff view if customers opt-in
- Telemetry: add a token-weighted delta to better surface cost regressions originating from prompt growth rather than model behavior

If you want to exercise the flow locally: see observability/triage-hub/README.md for quickstart and the e2e fixture at ci/e2e/golden_run/fixture.yaml.
Adds a Golden-Run diff layer to the Console and an oncall triage hub service to speed SLO RCA for per-route latency/cost regressions. Includes runbook links and weighted log snippets to accelerate incident response.

Introduces a sustained reserve allocator to provide predictable throughput floors for Dedicated fleets; adds a linearized utilization probe to improve telemetry quality and alerting for burst events. Backwards-compatible config flags added to dedicated fleet values. No user-facing API changes.
Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally experience long low-utilization tails followed by sudden bursts that invalidate short-window autoscaler signals. Customers need stronger 'sustained throughput' guarantees for service classes (e.g. search-heavy tenants) while preserving overall fleet efficiency. This PR introduces two cooperating mechanisms: 1) a Slot Stabilizer Reservoir (sustained reserve allocator) that keeps transient capacity earmarked for tenants that have recent sustained demand patterns; and 2) a Utilization Lucidity Probe (linearized-util telemetry exporter) that emits smoothed, commit-keyed utilization snapshots and HDR-backed burst samples to improve autoscaler decisions and SLA reporting. Summary of changes: - New allocator implementation (pkg/autoscaler/sustained_reserve_allocator.go) implementing a reservoir that tracks sustained demand by exponential foothold windows and awards soft-slot reservations that can be reclaimed under strict overcommit. - Soft-decline controller (pkg/autoscaler/proportional_decline.go) that gently scales back reservations when global pressure rises, with hysteresis and decay-factor controls. - Telemetry probe (telemetry/linearized_util_lucidity.go) that normalizes multi-window utilization into linearized percentiles and emits HDR sketches for burst rates; integrates with metrics exporter and disk-backed transient buffer for outage resilience. - Helm values and config knobs (deploy/helm/values/dedicated.yaml) to enable/disable feature gates per pool and tune window/decay parameters. - Observability (observability/dashboards/sustained_reserve.json) with per-tenant reservation heatmap, reservation reclaim events, and burst HDR percentiles. - CLI tooling (cmd/ctl/reserve_inspect.go) to inspect current reservoir state and simulate reservation grants. - Tests: unit and integration tests covering allocator safety bounds, reclamation paths, and telemetry invariants. Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag default=false. 2) Canary in a single Dedicated pool for 72h with detailed telemetry enabled. 3) Gradual opt-in for customers requiring sustained throughput guarantees with opt-out path. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (docs/design/sustained-reserve.md) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests for reclaim behavior - [x] Telemetry integration and dashboard - [x] Helm chart values and migration notes - [x] Backwards compatibility validated - [x] Manual canary run plan documented (Linear: ENG-9244) Related: ENG-9312 (autoscaler signal fidelity work), SUP-4472 (customer support case for search tenant burst regressions). Migration notes: existing Dedicated fleets will not be affected until feature flag enabled in values.dedicated.reservoir.enabled. When enabled, there is a brief reconciliation window (up to 30s) while the allocator backfills soft reservations; this is safe but may temporarily increase observed unused slots in dashboards. Implementation details and knobs are documented in docs/design/sustained-reserve.md.
Noah Chen (reviewer): The allocator looks good overall; please call out the worst-case runtime complexity for reconciliation loops and add a comment about potential O(n^2) behaviors when many tenants are in probation.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Good catch — added reconciliation bucketization and updated comments in sustained_reserve_allocator.go to document O(n) amortized behavior.
Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Can we avoid emitting HDR sketches for every small sample during high QPS? Suggest switching to adaptive sampling threshold.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Implemented adaptive_sampler with epsilon threshold; tests added to ensure sampling saturation remains <1% of emission bandwidth.
Marta Reyes (reviewer): Observability note — reservation reclaim events should include tenant tags for downstream chargeback. Please add tag enrichment.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Enriched events with tenant_id and service_class tags and updated dashboard panels accordingly.
CI (integration-tests-dedicated): Initial run failed on reservoir reconciliation flaky test, reran after adding test guard and it passed.
Noah Chen (approver): Approving pending small nit on comment wording, which is non-blocking.
Liam O'Connor (approver): Approved.

payload.body:
Motivation: In production we continue to see tail latency variability and increased SSD paging under multi-tenant KV workloads when fragmentation and uncoordinated evictions drive uneven residency. This PR introduces the 'memory plumber' (a cross-tenant memory coordination layer) and an 'eviction orchestrator' that jointly reduce fragmentation, avoid synchronous paging spikes, and make eviction decisions aware of runtime scheduling and continuous batching.

What this changes (high level): Implement a lightweight cross-shard coordinator (memory plumber) that tracks coarse-grained residency windows and issues tenant-level soft-reservation hints; add an eviction orchestrator which computes an adaptive eviction score that mixes access heat, recency, kernel-latency-sensitivity (per-route SLO tag), and fragmentation penalty; introduce a spill-log micro-paging path that serializes low-priority cold objects to SSD in append-only chunks to reduce random synchronous writes; add an opportunistic background compactor that coalesces small free slabs during low-load windows; integrate hot-reserve markers with the continuous batching pipeline so keys participating in in-flight batches are transiently protected from eviction.

Design notes and tradeoffs: The memory plumber is intentionally coarse: it operates on ranges and resident heuristics instead of per-key locking to avoid global contention. The orchestrator uses a weighted scoring vector with runtime-tunable coefficients exposed as flags and runtime-config to allow ops to tune behavior per cluster/class of workloads. Spill-log is not a full-blown object store; it is a ring of write segments used strictly for eviction-backed cold pages. This reduces latency amplification from random paging at the cost of modest background read amplification at cold-read time. The compactor runs opportunistically and is gated by CPU and GPU latency budgets so it yields aggressively if serving latency creeps.

Behavioral changes and safety: Default behavior is backwards compatible: if the memory plumber is off, eviction falls back to existing LRU/age-based evictor. New behavior is behind feature flags and rollout knobs (feature.memory_plumber_enabled, eviction.orchestrator_profile). Canary rollout plan described below.

Benchmarks (summary): Micro-bench with mixed read/write + long-tail hotset churn: P99 latency reduced by ~22% (from 84ms to 65ms) under a 30% write churn scenario. End-to-end hosting experiment with continuous batching showed 18% fewer synchronous SSD page faults and 12% lower per-request CPU overhead for eviction work. For a batch-heavy conversational workload the hot-reserve integration reduced batch tail amplification, improving aggregate throughput by ~9% at 95th percentile.

Testing and validation: Unit and integration tests cover the scoring logic and fallback fast-paths; an e2e canary harness simulates multi-tenant churn with cold-read spikes. Added stress tests that force heavy fragmentation to validate compactor behavior. CI pipeline includes a canary run that exercises the spill-log under emulated slow SSD latencies.

Rollout and ops: Ship behind feature flag. Canary in prod for dedicated clusters only for 48h, with the following monitors: kv.page-fault-rate, kv.eviction-rate, kv.fragmentation-score (new metric), kv.spill-log-throughput, serving.p99. Auto-rollback threshold: >10% increase in P99 or >3x spike in page fault rate over baseline.

Migration notes: No data migration; spill-log segments have an on-disk footer version. When feature is disabled, objects in spill-log are rehydrated lazily on access and the segments are reclaimed by background GC.

Related: complements previous slab/evictor work (ENG-3900, ENG-4012) but focuses on cross-tenant coordination and runtime-awareness (scheduling + continuous batching).
Marco Lin: Overall design looks solid. A couple of concerns: (1) scoring vector normalization across tenants — ensure scores are comparable; (2) important to clarify compactor backpressure to serving loops.
Author (Anya): Scoped normalization to tenant capacity buckets and added a normalization step in eviction_orchestrator.rs (see commit 'kv: implement adaptive eviction scorer and unit tests'). Compactor now exposes cpu_budget_pct and latency_backoff flags, documented in docs/ops/kv_memory_plumber.md.
Priya Sethi: Can we quantify worst-case read amplification from spill-log? Also please add metrics for spill-log read-latency histogram.
Author (Anya): Added read-amplification microbenchmark in scripts/benchmark and added metrics kv.spill_log_read_latency_histogram. Updated CI to run a slow-ssd scenario.
Diego Alvarez: I requested a small refactor to ensure hot-reserve markers do not prolong memory leak windows in rare error paths.
Author (Anya): Addressed in commit 'scheduler: annotate batch contexts with hot-reserve markers' with proper scope destruction; added regression test test_hot_reserve_scoped_release.
Marco Lin: Approve after nits; verified canary results in staging (P99 improvement reported).
Priya Sethi: Approved. Diego: Approved.
- Introduces memory-plumber: cross-tenant residency coordination to reduce fragmentation and synchronized paging.
- Adds eviction-orchestrator: adaptive scoring combining heat, recency, fragmentation and route SLO sensitivity.
- Spill-log: append-only micro-paging path to serialize cold object writes and reduce random SSD stalls.
- Background compactor: opportunistic slab coalescing during low-load windows.
- Feature gated behind feature.memory_plumber_enabled; default off for existing clusters.
payload.title: kv: memory plumber and eviction orchestrator to reduce fragmentation and paging

payload.body:
Motivation: We have good per-invocation token cost telemetry but it's coarse — teams frequently need to know which part of a prompt/response (system prompt, user prompt, instruction blocks, model-generated continuation) drives token cost and latency regressions. This PR introduces a token-cost decomposition pipeline and end-to-end UX: 1) runtime emits per-segment token counters and cumulative latency tags; 2) trace enrichment synthesizes 'stage' spans (system/user/instruction/generation) for each invocation; 3) metrics rollup produces per-tenant and per-model per-stage cost histograms and a compact cohort index used by alerting. In addition, we observed alert fatigue from tenants with noisy dev traffic. This PR adds an auto-mute policy for alerts where >80% of noise is from a small set of callers for a short window, and a manual-unmute flow in the Console.

What changed (high level): - Runtime span enrichment: small change to request wrapper that emits stage boundaries and token deltas (instrumentation guarded behind a feature flag). - Trace-sidecar enrichment job: lightweight sampler that merges prefix metadata (client-side stage markers) into spans and tags high-cost prefixes for retention. - Metrics rollups: new per-stage token_cost_* metrics (sum, p50/p95/p99 histograms) and per-stage latency histograms. - Alerting: new SLO attenuation rule and an auto-mute controller that can suppress noisy alerts with audit trail and suggested escalation. - Dashboards: new Observability > Cost > Per-stage Cost Breakdown dashboard with cohort selectors (model, tenant, route, prompt-stage) and a compact waterfall panel for per-invocation stage latency. - Tests and migration: migration adds compact histogram series and a lightweight index for prefix fingerprints; migration is backwards-compatible and small storage delta.

Checklist:
- [x] Runtime instrumentation behind feature flag
- [x] Trace enrichment service + integration tests
- [x] Metric rollup + histogram unit tests
- [x] Alert auto-mute controller + audit logging
- [x] Dashboard panels + Console toggle
- [x] Docs: observability/per-stage-cost.md (docs PR will follow, linked in linear)

Commits (summary): - 0a1b2c3: add span-stage markers to runtime request path; feature flag infra
- 1b2c3d4: implement trace enrichment sampler and prefix fingerprinting
- 2c3d4e5: rollup pipeline: per-stage histograms and aggregate keys
- 3d4e5f6: alert controller: auto-mute policy and audit trail records
- 4e5f6g7: dashboard JSON, compact waterfall renderer component, unit tests
- 5f6g7h8: add migration script for histogram-series and index updater

Changed files (high level): - runtime/instrumentation/stage_markers.go (new, small)
- trace/enricher/prefix_sampler.go (new)
- telemetry/rollups/per_stage_rollup.go (new)
- telemetry/histogram_migration/001_add_stage_histograms.sql (new migration)
- alerting/auto_mute/controller.go (new)
- console/dashboards/per_stage_cost.json (new dashboard)
- console/components/waterfall_panel.tsx (new component)
- docs/placeholder_observability/per-stage-cost.md (placeholder linked to Linear)
- tests/integration/observability_stage_integration_test.go

Review notes and tradeoffs: - Accuracy vs overhead: per-stage counters are emitted as deltas; we kept per-token instrumentation coarse-grained (per-chunk) to avoid per-token RPC overhead. Sampling is keyed to cost density so we keep retention budget focused on expensive prefixes. - Storage: histograms add modest cardinality. We aggregate into fixed cardinality cohort keys (tenant, model, stage, route hash) to avoid explosion. - Rollout plan: feature flag default off for hosted customers. Enable in a canary cluster, run nightly cohort reports to validate distribution, then flip on for more tenants. - Security/PII: stage markers are metadata only; we do not ship prompt text to metrics or index unless tenant opt-in; trace retention for payloads follows existing PII rules.

Review conversation (summary): Arjun: "Nice incremental approach — can we tighten the sampling threshold defaults?" — reply: "Lowered defaults in config and added per-tenant override. Included tests." Lucie: "Dashboard looks great; can we add a quick link from invocation detail to the waterfall?" — reply: "Added Console link generation and tests." Ben: "Auto-mute auditor needs to surface rationale to SRE playbooks." — reply: "Audit events now include rule fingerprint and top-3 callers; added to event schema." QA: "E2E flakes in the first run due to query timeout; reran and green." Merge decision: squash-and-merge after green CI and final doc stub added. Deployed to canary on 2025-12-01; monitored for 48h; no regression in P95 latency or token-cost budgets.
Adds per-stage (system/user/instruction) token-cost breakdowns, a new dashboard with cohort panels, and an adaptive alert muting rule for noisy tenants. Backwards compatible; no API changes.
Arjun Patel: tighten sampling defaults; added per-tenant overrides
Lucie Morales: Console link to waterfall added
Ben Thompson: audit events include top-3 callers and rule fingerprint
QA: initial e2e flake fixed and rerun, passed
Feature flag: observability.per_stage_cost = off by default for all hosted clusters. Canary enablement steps included in deploy/README. Migration: run 001_add_stage_histograms.sql during a low-traffic window; rollup job can backfill limited window (configurable). Auto-mute policy defaults: window=10m, noise_threshold=80%, mute_ttl=30m. Manual unmute via Console with audit log entry required.

ENG-1410: docs PR with sample dashboards and interpretation guide

Motivation: Customers require fine-grained service-level RBAC that can be mapped from onboarding metadata (service tags) into RBAC v2 bindings, and a non-intrusive enforcement layer that enforces data residency/region pinning for KMS usage while keeping audit trails intact. This PR introduces a 'Gatekeeper' proxy and an RBAC transformer pipeline that together provide: 1) deterministic translation of service tags -> RBAC v2 subject/role bindings, 2) region-pin enforcement at the service ingress with safe fallbacks, 3) a KMS routing shim that selects the tenant-backed CMK provider based on residency rules, and 4) audit header enrichment and signed provenance for downstream long-term storage.

High level changes: - new service-tag-to-rbac transformer (service/integration/transformer) that consumes onboarding claims and emits RBAC v2 delta patches; supports multiple mapping profiles and an allowlist mode for gradual rollout. - gatekeeper proxy (service/gatekeeper) that intercepts internal API calls, validates region assertions, enforces tenancy pinning, resolves KMS target using a configurable resolver, and injects canonical audit headers (x-rw-audit-provenance, x-rw-region-assertion). - kms-routing shim (service/kms-resolver) that implements affinity scoring for preferred KMS providers and falls back to multi-provider wrap/unwrap when strict residency is not met. - migration tooling and a linear task to backfill existing services with tags (scripts/migrations/backfill-service-tags). - unit + integration tests and a simple canary rollout orchestration script for Redwood Dedicated.

Design notes: The transformer uses a small declarative mapping language (YAML profiles) so security owners can express tag -> role mappings without code changes. RBAC patches are additive and annotated; we also emit a migration report to detect potential privilege escalations. The gatekeeper enforces region pinning using an assertion matcher that supports regex patterns and explicit lists; enforcement modes: monitor (log-only), audit-fail (deny and emit structured audit), strict (deny and require manual approval). KMS routing honors the tenant residency policy; if a strict residency mismatch occurs and strict mode is enabled, the request returns a 403 with a structured audit entry and an operator alert.

Context: Customers frequently need to retire model variants (old quantizations, interim checkpoints) without surprising production traffic. Existing rollout primitives handle promotion and canarying but lack an automated safe deprecation path for models that must be swept out of the serving fleet.
Motivation: eliminate manual deletion scripts, reduce orphaned snapshots, and provide predictable drain windows and recovery playbooks. This PR introduces a Model Deprecation Sweep Controller: design goals are safe gradual drain, snapshot-backed rollback capability during sweep, cohort-aware eviction to preserve sticky sessions, and timeline recovery for interrupted sweeps.
Key behaviors: 1) Controller understands deprecation annotations on ServeGraphs/model-versions and converts them into a staged drain plan. 2) It applies cohort-aware traffic fractions so sessions tied to older models get gradually remapped with priority for long-lived sessions. 3) Before a model node is removed, we capture a replay snapshot (lightweight KV-cache + recent-request-metadata) to support fast reinstate within the recovery window. 4) Safety gates: SLO/latency metric check, recent-error-rate threshold, and a minimum healthy instance count. 5) Config knobs: drain_window (default 10m), replay_retention (default 30m), cohort_sample_pct, fail_open boolean for emergency retention.
Implementation: adds a new controller under controllers/lifecycle with three main components: planner (generates timeboxed drain plans), coordinator (orchestrates per-pool eviction with batching and backoff), and snapshotter (compact snapshot format stored in objectstore). We extended the servegraph API surface with a deprecation_reason and deprecate_at timestamp; deprecated models are visible in the console UI and CLI.
Migration: existing ServeGraphs are unaffected until annotated.
Operator flow: 1) annotate model version and optionally set drain_window/replay_retention 2) controller schedules plan and emits events to audit-log 3) console shows per-cohort progress and allows manual pause/resume 4) if recovery invoked, controller reinstates the snapshot and resumes traffic.
Testing: unit tests for planner heuristics, e2e integration on perf-canary infra with synthetic cohorts, and chaos test that simulates controller crash-and-restart to validate timeline recovery.
Checklist: - [x] planner + coordinator implementation - [x] snapshot format + store adapter - [x] API surface and console flags - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs + playbook - [x] migration e2e on staging - [x] safety gate metric hooks - [x] confirm no default automatic deprecation (opt-in)
Commits summary: - initial planner scaffolding and tests - cohort-aware traffic allocator and sticky session support - snapshotter + compact KV dump + objectstore adapter - audit events and console wiring - safety gate integrations and smoke tests - docs + playbook and upgrade notes
Files changed (high level): controllers/lifecycle/deprecation_planner.go, controllers/lifecycle/coordinator.go, controllers/lifecycle/snapshotter.go, api/servegraph/v1alpha/model_annotations.go, console/ui/components/deprecation-panel.tsx, docs/ops/deprecation-playbook.md, integration/tests/deprecation_flow_test.go, e2e/perf-canary/simulated-cohort.yaml
Review conversation summary: - Diego Morales (2026-01-21): "Planner looks solid; we should make drain_window a cluster-level cap too so users cannot set an arbitrarily long drain that starves capacity." Author (Asha): "Ack; added cluster.level.max_drain_window config and validated with unit tests." - Riley Chen (2026-01-25): "Snapshot size might be large for some models; can we make snapshotter skip heavy KV entries and favor recent request headers?" Author: "Added retention filter and gzip+delta encoding; documented tradeoffs in snapshotter README." - Maya Kapoor (2026-01-28): "How does this interact with canary rollbacks? If a canary is promoted then deprecated quickly, we need to avoid thundering replays." Author: "Coordinator respects active rollout locks; if model is in promotion window we defer deprecation and emit a warning event to audit-log. Added integration test that simulates rapid promote->deprecate race."

Rollout plan: deploy controller as default off in staging, enable feature flag for select customers, run a small scheduled sweep on staging models, run two-week canary with monitoring alerts for latency and error regressions, then enable wider rollout.

Context and motivation: In production incident SUP-4821 we observed repeated circuit reopen/reclose oscillations during KV-sync jitter and transient region saturation. Those flips caused cascading tenant churn and made automated failovers amplify load instead of absorbing it. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) an SLO Umbrella controller that can apply short-lived, controlled SLO relaxations grouped by region/cohort to reduce admission pressure and allow graceful routing fallbacks; (2) a Circuit Snooze mechanism that temporarily freezes circuit state transitions for a configurable window when KV-sync variance or bursty telemetry is detected. Both are designed to be conservative defaults (short windows, telemetry-driven) and fully overridable by operator policies.

Summary of changes / checklist: - Add slo_umbrella controller in control-plane/slo (controller, API handlers, unit tests). - Add circuit_snooze logic inside runtime/circuit (state machine pause + metrics). - Add KV-sync jitter detector (runtime/kv/jitter_detector) and hook into snooze decision. - Wire a new admin flag: controlplane.slo_umbrella.enabled (default true) and runtime.circuit_snooze.window_ms (default 1500). - Export new telemetry: slo_umbrella.decisions, circuit_snooze.activations, kv.jitter_score. - Add e2e scenario to perf-canary (simulated regional saturation + kv jitter). - Hotfix: change to kv-sync backoff logic to avoid immediate reopen on out-of-order ACKs.

Implementation notes and rationale: The SLO Umbrella is implemented as a best-effort coordinator: it observes per-tenant SLO breach risk signals and issues ephemeral 'umbrella' tokens that the serving edge uses to (a) temporarily widen latency targets for low-priority routes, and (b) prefer local cached responses or smaller model variants. The umbrella token TTLs are small (default 5s) and issuance is rate-limited per-region. Circuit Snooze takes a conservative approach: when jitter_detector detects > threshold variance in KV sync latency or missing heartbeat bursts, it transitions the circuit state machine to an "aligned" pause state where reopen attempts are suppressed for window_ms. Snoozes are recorded in telemetry and count toward failure budgets so behavior is auditable.

Commits (high-level): - c1a9f04: initial slo_umbrella controller + API + unit tests - 7f2d3bb: runtime hook to consume umbrella token at admission and route decisions - 33bfa99: circuit_snooze state machine and metrics - 8bc4d11: kv jitter detector + tuning - a4e3c22: perf-canary e2e scenario and fixture updates - d0e9b18: hotfix to kv sync backoff (address SUP-4821 symptom)

Files changed (representative): - control-plane/slo/umbrella_controller.go - control-plane/slo/README.md - runtime/circuit/snooze.go - runtime/circuit/snooze_test.go - runtime/kv/jitter_detector.go - runtime/kv/sync_backoff.go - serving/edge/admission_umbrella.go - perf-canary/scenarios/umbrella_kv_jitter.yaml - telemetry/metrics_definitions.yaml - docs/operations/slo-umbrella.md

Testing and CI: - Unit tests: added for controller and snooze machine (coverage + boundary cases). - Integration: local integration run against mini-cluster passes. - Perf-canary: new scenario added and validated in staging (simulated kv jitter + regional saturation). - CI: build & lint & unit tests passed on first run; flaky e2e in earlier iteration fixed by reducing default TTLs.

Review conversation (high-level): - Riya: "Can we make the default umbrella TTL smaller? I'm worried about masking real SLO degradation for too long." - Ava: "Agreed; reduced default from 10s to 5s and added rate-limits per-region. Added telemetry to show duration distribution." - Diego: "Snooze looks good but needs a circuit-level audit event for every transition." - Ava: "Added audit events and a lightweight trace span for snooze activations." - Liam: "What's the operator story to opt out?" - Ava: "controlplane.slo_umbrella.enabled=false and runtime flag runtime.circuit_snooze.enabled=false; documented in ops guide." - Diego (approval): "LGTM pending one nit on metric name; approved after rename." - Riya (approval): "Approved. Verified staging canary metrics show reduced reopen churn."

Motivation: our presubmit lint/test lanes have grown uneven: a small set of files cause huge lint jobs while other PRs run many trivial linters. This increases CI queue time and raises flake surface area. Separately, dependency roll PRs were frequently failing due to lockfile churn and noisy CI; locks were updated piecemeal which created transient regressions. This PR introduces two coordinated changes: 1) weighted-lint-allocator: a scheduler component that assigns presubmit lint workers by historical file-cost weights (measured by average lint runtime and rule density). The allocator creates lightweight fast-lanes for small-surface changes and reserves heavy-lane slots for large or high-cost patches, enabling faster feedback for most PRs. 2) lockfile-gardener: a small orchestration service that performs atomic lock rotations for grouped dependency updates. It stages changes in a temporary branch, runs the CI matrix with a deterministic job ordering and retries only the failing matrix targets before opening the final roll PR. The gardener reduces non-deterministic lock churn and makes dep rotators (dependabot-like bots) more robust. Changes: - new package ci/allocator with: - weighting model (historical sampling + decay) - fast/normal/heavy lane selector - integration shim for GitHub Actions presubmit router - small opt-in config per repo in .github/ci-lanes.yaml - new package infra/lockfile-gardener with: - batch rotation runner - deterministic job ordering and selective retry logic - test harness that simulates the matrix and lockfile merge conflicts - new GH Action composite steps: ci/allocator-action and gardener-check - updates to main presubmit workflow to call allocator before lint shards and to gate dep-rolls through gardener - tests: unit tests for weighting functions, integration smoke tests that run a trimmed CI matrix using mocked runners - docs: README describing config knobs, migration guide, and operational runbook Checklist: - [x] design doc: ENG-1987 (linked) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] migration guide + config schema - [x] smoke deployment to staging CI cluster - [x] rollout plan with canary on small repos Rollout plan: stage behind a feature flag set in .github/ci-lanes.yaml. Start with two low-traffic repos, monitor average presubmit latency (SLO target: 75th percentile +15% improvement) and flakiness rate. For lockfile-gardener, run in dry-run mode for two weeks before enabling automatic PR creation. Related: ENG-1999 (release automation improvements), SUP-4421 (customer dep-rotation incident). Links: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1987 https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1999 Implementation notes: - The allocator stores lightweight per-path statistics in an internal Redis namespace; stats have TTL and decay to avoid stale weights. - We intentionally keep the initial weighting model simple (exponential moving average of observed lint runtimes per file, plus a per-rule penalty) to avoid RL-style complexity during rollout. - The gardener uses a two-step commit approach: create a staging branch, run the matrix, perform targeted retries for failures, then squash-merge the lock updates when the matrix stabilizes. Observability: Added metrics and dashboards: ci.allocator.job_latency_bucket, ci.allocator.shard_size, gardener.rolls.created, gardener.rolls.success_rate. Alerts: gardener:err_rate > 3% over 1h, allocator:queue_latency_p50 > 30s on presubmit lane. Security: gardener accesses repo tokens with limited scope (contents:write, checks:write) and records all operations to audit logs. Migration: repository owners opt-in by adding .github/ci-lanes.yaml with minimal config. Compatibility: backward compatible; default behavior if config absent remains current presubmit routing. Backwards impact: none.
Adds a weighted lint scheduling layer for presubmit lanes and a lockfile gardener that stages seed rotations for dependency updates. No public API changes. Improves CI feedback latency and reduces flakiness caused by oversized lint shards.
Diego Morales (requested changes): The allocator looks promising but I worry about cold-start skew for new files. Please add a fallback that keeps file weight bounded until we observe at least N samples (N=3). Also add a unit test that validates decay behavior.
Maya Chen (author): Added bounded-initialization with N=3 and added decay unit tests in weights_test.go. Pushed commit 5 to address this.
Priya Singh (comment): The gardener's token scope should be minimal. Please confirm tokens don't grant admin rights and add a note to the runbook.
Maya Chen (author): Confirmed and updated runbook; gardener uses a deploy key with only contents:write and checks:write. See runbook section Operational Security.
Evelyn Hart (approval): Verified staging runs. Observed ~22% reduction in median lint job latency for the two pilot repos. Approve after small Windows runner fix.
Maya Chen (author): Fixed Windows runner shell escaping and re-ran staging; CI green. Pushed final squash commit for merge.
This PR intentionally keeps the ML/complex weighting for a later phase; current approach is deterministic and easy to reason about. We expect to iterate on lane thresholds during the canary. Also added a small CLI helper for backfilling historical weights when migrating large repos.

Adds scoped project API keys (proj_* tokens), canonicalized Authorization header precedence, X-Redwood-Signature/X-Redwood-Nonce request signing headers with deterministic verification, and CORS improvements for browser clients. OpenAI-compat layer now maps legacy headers and preserves streaming semantics. Feature is opt-in for Private/Dedicated via config flags.
Motivation: We have multiple client integrations that rely on different ways of passing credentials (Authorization: Bearer, X-Redwood-Api-Key, project-scoped tokens). This PR unifies header precedence, introduces scoped project keys, and adds simple request-signing primitives to mitigate replay attacks for sensitive admin endpoints. It also fixes several browser CORS issues that caused streaming connections to be preflighted incorrectly and updates the OpenAI-compatibility layer to accept both legacy and canonical headers.

What this changes: 1) Canonical header precedence: Authorization: Bearer (token) > X-Redwood-Api-Key > X-Redwood-Project-Key. Servers now normalize input into a single internal credential object at the earliest request-auth stage. 2) Scoped project keys: new token prefix 'proj_' and minimal JWT-like format (header.payload.sig) carrying project_id and allowlist metadata. Tokens are compatible with existing account tokens but can be scoped and revoked independently. 3) Request signing: optional headers X-Redwood-Nonce and X-Redwood-Signature (HMAC-SHA256 over canonicalized request line + headers + body) plus a deterministic canonicalization routine. Verified in the auth middleware with strict replay-window configurable via env. 4) OpenAI-compat: map Authorization and X-Redwood-Api-Key into the same flow; preserve existing streaming chunking for SSE and streaming HTTP so third-party tools (curl, openai SDKs) behave as before. 5) CORS: add Access-Control-Allow-Headers entries for X-Redwood-Signature and X-Redwood-Nonce, ensure preflight early-return for streaming endpoints to avoid buffering. 6) Observability: add telemetry flags for which credential type was used (account/scoped/project), and metrics when request-signing verification fails.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-2394) - [x] Unit tests for token parsing and precedence - [x] Integration tests for CORS and streaming - [x] Compatibility tests against OpenAI-compat shim - [x] Docs update and migration notes - [x] Security review (SEC-112)

Compatibility notes: The change is non-breaking by default. Existing account tokens continue to work. Scoped project tokens are opt-in; customers can create proj_* tokens in Console. Request-signing is opt-in per-route; default replay-window is 2 minutes. Operators on Private/Dedicated can toggle canonicalization lenience for older clients.

Backwards-compatibility mapping examples: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" remains canonical. Older clients sending X-Redwood-Api-Key will be accepted and logged as legacy-header usage. The OpenAI-compat endpoint accepts both Authorization and Api-Key headers and translates them to the normalized credential.

Risks and mitigations: - If operators enable strict signing without rolling out client changes, legitimate requests will be rejected; mitigated with a permissive flag and verbose logs for rollout. - Token format change is additive; ensure no leaking of project metadata in logs. All new tokens are audited at issuance time.

References: linear:ENG-2394, security:SEC-112, support:SUP-721. Design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2394/auth-header-precedence-and-scoped-keys.

Initial review from Ethan noted a potential race in nonce cleanup; added Redis-based TTL and deterministic nonce bucket key. Priya requested clearer telemetry for legacy header usage which was added (auth.credential_source metric). Alex requested an explicit migration section in docs for operators; docs expanded and example curl commands added. After two CI reruns (streaming test flaky) reviewers approved and marked as security-reviewed. Final sign-off from Priya and Alex before merge.
Operators: to enable scoped tokens set AUTH_ENABLE_SCOPED_KEYS=true and configure token issuer key in secrets (AUTH_SCOPED_ISSUER_KEY). To enable strict signing set AUTH_STRICT_SIGNING=true and SIGNING_REPLAY_WINDOW_SECONDS=120. For Private installs, older clients can be allowed by setting AUTH_CANONICALIZER_LENIENCE=1. Monitor auth.signing_failure metric for rollout.
Publish migration docs to docs.redwood.ai (docs/source/auth.md) - assigned to docs team
Add Console UI for proj_* token creation with allowlist settings - follow-up ticket PM-512
Perf: add cache for parsed scoped-token claims in gateway to reduce crypto cost under high QPS - ENG-2407
