Motivation: We have continuing drift in how each language SDK handles short-lived credentials and retry backoff defaults for streaming calls. Customers using multi-language stacks see inconsistent reconnect behavior and duplicate connection attempts during auth refresh windows. This PR coordinates a cross-SDK implementation to: 1) introduce a small credential TTL prefetch window (configurable, default 15s) that triggers a non-blocking refresh; 2) expose adaptive retry presets (fast/steady/conservative) which surface the same parameters across Python, TypeScript, and Go; 3) add a lightweight resumable async-iterable helper for streaming consumers that supports checkpointing and resume-after-refresh without duplicating payloads. Implementation notes: - Python: added redwood.streaming.resume.AsyncResumableIterator and a small CredentialsWatcher that emits non-blocking refresh signals; integrated with existing retry profiles via new retry_presets enum. Backcompat: existing StreamClient iterators now opt into resumable behavior via resume_on_auth_refresh=True. - TypeScript: added resumeStreamForAuth() helper and exported RetryPresets type with same numeric params as other SDKs; ensured async-generator ergonomics and backpressure hint passthrough. - Go: introduced stream.CheckpointIterator and a CredentialPrefetcher that runs alongside existing session renewal logic; provided examples for context-aware iteration using contexts for cancellation. Cross-cutting: unified telemetry tags for auth_refresh events (sdk.auth.refresh.*) and added small e2e streaming tests that exercise auth near expiry and verify at-most-once semantics for resumed streams. This description includes the checklist and examples below. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked in Linear ENG-1182 - [x] python + ts + go tests added - [x] docs updated with migration guidance - [x] define default prefetch window and make configurable - [x] bump SDK versions and changelogs - [x] add telemetry events for refresh/retry decisions Related: SUP-4521 (customer reported double-reconnect during token rotation).
Small SDK surface changes: unify credential TTL handling, introduce adaptive retry presets, add resumable async-iterable helpers for streaming and bump SDK versions (py 3.9.5 -> 3.10.0, ts 1.27.3 -> 1.28.0, go v1.5.2 -> v1.6.0). No breaking API changes for typical callers; migration notes included.
Daniel Kim (reviewer): Can we avoid allocating a goroutine per stream for the credential prefetcher? Suggest using a shared prefetch ticker per client instance.
Monica Reyes (author): Good point — switched to client-scoped prefetcher with per-stream subscription; updated go implementation and tests.
Asha Patel (reviewer): On TS helper, ensure backpressure hints are forwarded to underlying socket. Also add an example that shows resuming from a numeric offset checkpoint.
Monica Reyes (author): Added backpressure passthrough and offset-based example in resume.ts; updated tests.
Luca Moretti (security review): Verify that credential prefetch does not leak tokens to logs and that telemetry only emits obfuscated token metadata.
Monica Reyes (author): Verified in code and added assertion to e2e test to ensure no raw token strings are present in logs; telemetry emits boolean flags and token age only.

payload.body:
## Context
During the 2026-01-15 controlled regional failover (us-east → eu-west), we had to manually reconstruct the key milestones (trigger time, policy flip, drain start, rollback, steady-state) across multiple sources (routing audit logs, controller logs, Slack timeline notes). This PR integrates failover automation events into the incident timeline tooling so that postmortems can auto-populate those milestones and on-call can see a consistent view during an event.

This is part of the Regional Failover Automation Upgrade program and complements the new structured failover audit events (recommendation/execution/rollback) emitted by routing/control plane.

## What this changes
- Adds a new incident-timeline ingest adapter for `failover.audit_event` records emitted by the failover controller/policy engine.
- Normalizes audit events into timeline entries with stable, low-cardinality fields.
- Adds a computed “Failover summary” block to the incident timeline view that groups related events by `failover_id` and renders:
  - Trigger / corroboration signals
  - Decision outcome (recommended vs executed)
  - Policy flip details (source region, target region, tier/route scope)
  - Rollback reason + hold-down/anti-flap context (when present)
- Auto-creates postmortem milestone candidates (timestamps) for:
  - `failover_triggered_at`
  - `failover_executed_at`
  - `traffic_shift_started_at`
  - `traffic_shift_completed_at` (best-effort, derived from final execution event or “steady-state” marker)
  - `rollback_initiated_at` and `rollback_completed_at` (when applicable)
- Adds timeline annotations for dashboards via existing incident annotations pipeline (addresses INT-1149: missing annotations during test).

## Event schema expectations
This PR expects audit events shaped like the controller output from recent work:
- `event_type`: one of `failover.recommendation`, `failover.execution`, `failover.rollback`
- `failover_id`: stable id across the workflow
- `reason`: normalized enum (e.g., `reachability_loss`, `error_burn`, `capacity_exhaustion`, `manual_operator`, `hold_down_timer`)
- `source_region`, `target_region`
- `scope`: string summary (route/model/tier), not exploded labels
- `actor`: `automation` | `oncall:<handle>` (string)
- `evidence`: summarized string (no high-cardinality raw metrics)

If any fields are missing, we still emit a timeline entry with a degraded rendering and a warning badge to prevent ingest failures.

## Implementation notes
- Uses the existing timeline event bus (no new infra) and adds a dedicated parser with strict validation + best-effort fallback.
- Uses a bounded in-memory grouping window keyed by `failover_id` to generate the summary block; also stores summary text as a first-class timeline event so it’s visible even if grouping state is lost.
- Adds a small test fixture from the 2026-01-15 controlled failover (sanitized) to validate rendering and milestone extraction.
- Adds annotation emission for the key milestones so dashboards can show vertical markers (trigger/execution/rollback) aligned to the incident timeline.

## Files/areas changed (high level)
- `services/incident-timeline/ingest/failover_audit_adapter.ts` (new)
- `services/incident-timeline/model/timeline_entry.ts` (new entry kind: `FAILOVER_EVENT`)
- `services/incident-timeline/renderers/failover_summary.ts` (new)
- `services/incident-timeline/postmortem/milestone_candidates.ts` (extract failover milestones)
- `services/incident-timeline/annotations/emit.ts` (emit markers for failover milestones)
- `packages/audit-events/schemas/failover.ts` (tightened validation + enums; no new labels)

## Tests
- Unit: adapter parses all supported event types and tolerates missing optional fields.
- Unit: milestone extraction produces deterministic timestamps given an ordered set of events.
- Snapshot: summary rendering is stable and doesn’t leak high-cardinality evidence.

- Added metrics:

  - `incident_timeline_failover_events_dropped_total{reason}`

- Add links from timeline entries to the failover dashboards panel and/or runbook section (pending final dashboard URLs).

- Postmortem draft auto-populates milestones and includes the failover summary block.

Checklist

Related

Notes for on-call
If you don’t see failover events in the incident timeline during a regional event, verify the feature flag is enabled for the incident tooling environment and check `incident_timeline_failover_events_dropped_total` in the incident-timeline service dashboard.

payload.body:
Motivation: we have seen two related issues in high-concurrency production workloads: (1) intermittent starvation of small, latency-sensitive requests caused by long-lived KV-heavy sequences that pin slots, and (2) oscillatory shifts in the batching frontier when per-tenant burst patterns change rapidly, which increased P99 token latency. This PR introduces a windowed arbiter for the continuous batcher that enforces short, rolling fairness windows and an expiry-based decay for KV priority marks so that heavy requests do not permanently dominate scheduling decisions. Design summary: - Windowed arbiter: requests are admitted into discrete, overlapping micro-windows (configurable window_ms, default 25ms). Within a window, the arbiter computes fair shares using normalized weights, then applies a small randomized jitter to admission deadlines to avoid synchronization-induced oscillation between queues. - KV priority expiry: requests tagged as KV-heavy receive a transient priority boost; that mark now decays after expiry_ms (configurable, default 200ms) instead of being sticky. Expiry is stored as an epoch token in the request descriptor; when the KV cache hits are replenished, the token is refreshed only up to a configurable cap to avoid re-entrancy amplification. - Oscillation damper: a token-based soft-preemption mechanism prevents repeated preemption of the same queue within a short horizon (damper_ms, default 75ms). If a queue gets preempted, its eviction penalty decays linearly, limiting oscillatory thrashing. - Adaptive timeouts with jitter: per-request soft-timeouts are derived from observed tail latencies per route. We attach a small randomized jitter to timeouts to de-correlate client retry patterns when fallbacks trigger. - Kernel hinting: the arbiter exposes a short-lived kernel hint with expected sequence length and kv_hint flag to the compilation/kernel-selection layer so that the runtime can favor tiled attention kernels or different KV cache eviction policies for anticipated long-running sequences. - Backpressure probe: when free slots are low, the arbiter injects low-priority probe admits (hedging) to measure real capacity; probes are rate-limited and labeled for observability. Implementation notes: - New module: runtime/batcher/windowed_arbiter.rs (Rust) handles window state, fairness calculation, and jittered deadlines. - New module: runtime/scheduler/kv_priority.rs implements the expiry token and KV-mark lifecycle. - Minor changes in runtime/alloc/slot_manager.go to add soft-preemption tokens and expose an API for the damper state. - Integrations in runtime/metrics to emit window occupancy, expiration_rate, damper_evictions and probe_success_rate for dashboards. Tests and validation: - Unit tests for fairness math (edge cases with skewed weights), expiry token lifecycle, and damper time-decay were added. - A synthetic load test harness (bench/continuous_bench.py) validates P50/P95/P99 behavior across mixed KV/plain traffic. - Canary in staging: we ran a 48-hour canary across three machines with production-like traffic and observed a 12% P99 reduction for latency-sensitive routes and a 7% improvement in throughput for mixed workloads. Rollout plan: - Feature guarded behind runtime config: enable_windowed_arbiter, kv_priority_expiry_ms, damper_ms. - Canary: staged rollout with 5% -> 25% -> 100% traffic gating tied to observed SLOs. - Metrics to watch: p99_latency_routeA, window_occupancy, expiry_reapply_rate, damper_evictions. Backout plan: disable feature flag and revert head if regressions observed for more than two consecutive deployment windows. Migration considerations: - No schema changes to stored models or persistent KV; all state is in-memory and epoch-based. - Default flags remain off for Dedicated regions until QA sign-off. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear (ENG-2193) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration bench validated - [x] CI passing - [x] Docs: runtime tuning notes updated in docs/perf/batcher.md - [x] Rollout plan documented in PR description Observability updates: dashboards for expiry_reapply_rate and damper_evictions were added; new traces tag window_id included in batcher traces. Related work: this complements prior fair-share and lease-based work (see ENG-1503) and replaces the earlier TTL-based KV-deprioritization experiment which caused abrupt fairness shifts. 
Introduces a windowed arbiter and KV-priority expiry to reduce starvation and oscillation in the continuous batcher; rollout guarded by canary and config flags.
Ava Chandra: Can you clarify how the expiry token interacts with KV cache refill events? Might user flows with interleaved prefetching reapply priority repeatedly?
Marcus Li: We cap token refresh to once per token_lifetime window (configurable). Refill events can refresh but only up to the cap to prevent amplification; added unit test to validate behavior.
Priya Nair: The damper_ms default seems conservative; can we make it tenant-configurable and add a safety upper-bound?
Marcus Li: Damper is tenant-configurable in the new config map with an upper-bound (500ms). Documented in runtime tuning notes.
Diego Ramos: CI flake on test_kv_priority on first run; looks like a timing assumption in test harness. Please make assertions tolerant to jitter.
Marcus Li: Adjusted tests to use eventual assertions with 200ms slack; CI re-ran and passed.
Initial CI hit a timing flake on test_kv_priority (fixed by using eventual assertions). Full suite now passes on Linux amd64 and macos-latest. Bench harness run completed in staging with expected improvements.
This change is intentionally conservative: defaults are feature-flagged and off for Dedicated until product QA signs off. Operators can tune window_ms, kv_priority_expiry_ms and damper_ms per deployment.

payload.body:
Fix urgent regression: mitigate rapid circuit flips during tenant bursts by introducing burst tranching fallback and a graduated circuit coastdown. Improves availability and reduces tail-error spikes under short-lived traffic surges.
Motivation: In recent incidents we observed short, high-amplitude tenant bursts driving immediate circuit flips and wide tenant impact. The root cause is an all-or-nothing shed decision combined with an aggressive circuit reopen policy that amplifies oscillation. This change introduces two related controls: 1) Burst tranching fallback: when a tenant exceeds its burst rate, requests are amortized across small timed tranches that allow partial acceptance and progressive backoff instead of a single large shed event. 2) Circuit coastdown: when a circuit transitions from tripped->closed we now apply a configurable coastdown window that gradually ramps full capacity back to the tenant rather than restoring it instantly. Design decisions: - Tranching uses an in-memory window per tenant with micro-buckets (250ms) and a weighted acceptivity score computed from recent error rate, kv pressure, and SLO debt. - Coastdown is implemented as a multiplicative ramp factor applied to the per-tenant token allowance over a short epoch (default 10s) with exponential smoothing to avoid sharp rebounds. - Both features are guarded behind feature flags and an operator-visible metric set (burst_tranche_accept, coastdown_multiplier, tranche_reject_rate). Checklist: - [x] Feature design doc linked (ENG-1345) - [x] Unit tests for tranche window and coastdown ramp - [x] Integration test in perf-canary that replays historical incident traces - [x] Canary rollout plan and rollback steps - [x] Telemetry and dashboards added. Commits: 1) "hotfix: introduce burst tranching sampler and accept/reject logic" - initial implementation and tests 2) "sre: add coastdown ramp and server-side config + metrics" - coastdown algorithm and observability 3) "telemetry: dashboard and alerts for tranche rejection spikes" - grafana and alert rules 4) "ops: feature flags and canary rollout script" - rollout automation and kill switch Changed areas (high level): - serving/runtime/soft_shed/tranche_controller.go - serving/runtime/circuit/coastdown.go - serving/runtime/config/flags.go - telemetry/dashboards/burst_tranche.jsonnet - ci/canaries/replay_burst_traces.yaml - docs/operational/tranche_and_coastdown.md - tests/integration/burst_tranche_test.go Testing summary: - Unit tests cover boundary cases for bucket alignment and aggregate scoring. - Integration canary replays 30 historical burst incidents in perf-canary, comparing circuit flip rate and 95th percentile latency. - CI was flaky once due to clock drift in a test; added clock stub and reran. Review conversation (high level): - Aisha Kaur: "Can we tune the default coastdown window down for small tenants?" Author: "Added small_tenant_coastdown_seconds override; default remains 10s but configurable per-tenant." - Diego Morales: "Is tranche state memory bounded? Need eviction to avoid unbounded growth." Author: "Yes, tranche_controller uses LRU with max entries=100k and per-tenant TTL; documented in config." - Emily Chen (approval): "Verified canary replay; metrics show 3x fewer circuit flips and no latency regression." CI checks: ["unit-tests: pass (with rerun)", "integration-canary: pass", "lint: pass", "telemetry-schema-check: pass"] Rollout and mitigation: - Canary ramped in us-west-2 with 2% of traffic for 4h, then 10% for 2h, then 50% for 1h before full rollout. - Observed drop in circuit flips from 18/min -> 5/min during canary. - Rollback plan: feature flags allow immediate disable; operator runbook updated. Follow-ups and operational notes: - Follow-up ticket ENG-1402 to add adaptive tranche sizing based on long-term tenant footprint. - Add end-to-end tracing for tranche decisions (low overhead) to aid post-incident debugging. Merge outcome: merged via squash, commit message consolidated to "hotfix: burst tranching fallback + coastdown; fixes circuit oscillation under bursty tenants".
Aisha Kaur: Can we tune the default coastdown window down for small tenants?
Marcus Li: Added small_tenant_coastdown_seconds override and documented it.
Diego Morales: Is tranche state memory bounded? Need eviction to avoid unbounded growth.
Marcus Li: Implemented LRU with TTL; added tests to assert eviction.
Emily Chen: Verified canary replay; metrics show reduced flips and stable latency. Approving.
This hotfix addresses a high-severity production regression observed during weekend traffic bursts. Operators should monitor tranche_reject_rate and coastdown_multiplier; if tranche_reject_rate climbs >5% system-wide, consider further throttling upstream or engage SRE on-call.

payload.body:
Motivation: Customers repeatedly ask for safe, opinionated defaults that improve per-token unit economics without surprising latency regressions. This PR adds a new service (cost-symphony) that synthesizes tenant-level batching, KV-cache, and quantization defaults from sampled workload signatures and runtime telemetry. Goals: 1) provide deterministic, auditable defaults for new tenants and rolloutable updates for existing tenants; 2) reduce typical token cost on common web workloads by ~12% without increasing p99 tail latency beyond SLA; 3) expose a dry-run mode and a human-review path for safety-critical accounts. Summary of changes: - New service: redwood/cost_symphony/ with a small runtime that ingests sampled traces and computes a prioritized list of defaults (batch_shape, cache_prefill_policy, quant_profile). Defaults are represented as JSON profiles and versioned in the defaults registry. - Defaults-as-code: introduce a CLI redwood-cli defaults synth that can produce deterministic presets from a captured workload snapshot and upload them as a draft profile. - Safe rollout: server-side rollout controller that supports canary -> tiered rollout across tenant cohorts with automatic rollback on cost/quality regressions. - Offline prober: a synthetic prober that runs simulated inference with candidate defaults against a small, representative sample and computes delta metrics (cost/token, avg latency, p95/p99). - Telemetry and evals: new telemetry keys (symphony.profile_id, symphony.sim.delta_cost, symphony.sim.quality_change) and a lightweight evaluator for detecting hallucination/regression against a canonical prompt set. - Console integration: expose generated draft profiles in the Console defaults UI under "Cost automation -> Suggested defaults" and allow a one-click approve/apply. - Tests and CI: unit + integration tests for the synth algorithm; a deterministic snapshot-based integration test that runs prober comparisons on CI. Checklist: - [x] Design doc: Linear ENG-5421 linked and reviewed - [x] Implementation: core synth, registry, rollout controller - [x] CLI: redwood-cli defaults synth + dry-run - [x] Telemetry + metrics: added to metrics schema - [x] Console surface: draft UI card + apply flow - [x] E2E: prober-based smoke tests - [x] Documentation: docs/ defaults automation guide is included Breaking considerations: Profiles are opt-in by default for existing tenants; new tenants receive a recommended profile but can opt out. Rollouts run with conservative thresholds by default and require explicit enablement for high-SLA tenants. Performance summary: On an internal web-chat workload sample, the synthesized default reduced median cost/token by 12.3% and 95th-percentile token cost by 9.4%; avg latency increased 1.8ms and p99 was unchanged within noise. Rollout plan: squash-merge to main, enable draft uploads to staging for two weeks, run prober sweeps, then gradual canary to 5% of tenants. Related work: builds on tenant-warmstart/tenant-prefill work and reuses portions of the sample-cataloger. Links: Linear ENG-5421, ENG-6120 (prober enhancements).
Marco Li: Did you consider restricting quant-profile suggestions to only LLM families that we have validated quantizers for? I worry about applying 4-bit suggestions to models not tested.
Priya Desai: Good point — synth now tags profiles with 'validated_model_families' and the rollout controller refuses apply if tenant runs an unsupported model. Added tests for the guard.
Rafael Gomez: The prober should include a tiny canonical prompt set to catch quality regressions; please add a signal for hallucination rate change.
Priya Desai: Added symphony.sim.quality_change and a lightweight BLEU-ish matcher for template-based prompts; documented false-positive modes in the docs.
Anika Schultz: CLI UX: dry-run output should show expected delta metrics and the JSON profile; done, and user can --approve to upload draft.
Jamie Park: Console card looks good but needs tooltip copy on 'expected cost savings' explaining simulation assumptions; updated copy in the last commit.
Adds 'Cost Symphony' defaults orchestrator: automated synthesis of batching, cache prefill and quantization presets; CLI synth + dry-run; console UI for suggested profiles; safe rollout/controller with telemetry and prober-based validations. New metrics: symphony.profile_id, symphony.sim.delta_cost, symphony.sim.quality_change.
No immediate oncall changes required. Default rollouts are disabled by default; if enabling for production tenants, monitor symphony.sim.delta_cost and symphony.sim.quality_change for spikes. If quality_change > 0.02 for any canary cohort, rollback the rollout controller for that profile.

payload.body:
Introduce a new sparse-length quantizer batch allocator that reduces padding overhead and schedules KV-prefill-heavy requests earlier. Config flags are behind runtime.feature.sparse_length_quantizer and default to off for a controlled rollout.
Motivation: production workload traces show a long-tailed sequence length distribution where naive fixed bucketing or uniform-width buckets cause excessive padding and poor kernel fit. Additionally, KV-prefill bursts (requests that attach large cached context) were causing spikes in prefill latency and unexpected KV cache thrashing. This PR implements a sparse-length quantizer allocator that (1) computes non-uniform bucket boundaries from recent traffic quantiles, (2) combines kernel-fit heuristics to prefer bucket boundaries aligned with efficient kernel shapes (e.g. 64/128 multiples for TensorCore lanes), and (3) integrates a lightweight KV-prefill awareness to prioritize or reserve prefill slots so continuous batching doesn't starve prefill-bound requests.

Implementation summary:
- allocator/service/runtime/sparse_length_quantizer.{cpp,h}: new allocator that maintains a sliding quantile summary (t-digest inspired) of sequence lengths with an EWMA window for drift. Quantiles are used to place incoming requests into a small number (configurable, default 8) of variable-width buckets.
- scheduler/kv_prefill_reservoir.{rs,cpp}: small reservation mechanism that marks N slots per batch for requests flagged as KV-prefill-heavy; integrates with continuous batching so prefill slots can be filled within a prefill_timeout window before normal batch composition proceeds.
- scheduler/batch_cost_model.{py,cpp}: extended cost model that estimates padding token overhead vs inferred kernel throughput; allocator chooses the bucket composition that minimizes expected cost = cpu+gpu_token_cost + padding_penalty.
- runtime/config.yaml: feature flag runtime.feature.sparse_length_quantizer and tuning knobs (num_buckets, quantile_decay_alpha, prefill_reserve_pct, prefill_timeout_ms).
- tests/unit/test_sparse_quantizer.py and tests/integration/test_prefill_reservation.py: exercise edge cases for skewed distributions and KV-prefill bursts.
- docs/running/allocators.md: operational notes and rollout steps.

Commits (high level): 1) add quantile summary and allocator core; 2) integrate with scheduler and cost model; 3) add KV-prefill reservoir and wiring; 4) unit + integration tests; 5) docs and feature flag. Changed areas: runtime/allocator, scheduler, runtime/kv_cache, runtime/config, tests, docs.

Example code snippet (high-level, illustrative): "if (is_prefill_heavy(req)) { reserve_slot = prefill_reservoir.claim(); if (reserve_slot) route_to_prefill_bucket(); } else { bucket = quantizer.assign(req.len); queue(bucket); }"

Performance results:
- Synthetic replay of customer trace A: 22% token-padding reduction vs current length-bucketing baseline, 9% lower p95 latency at 512-token tail workloads.
- End-to-end throughput improvement of 6-12% on p3dn-24 across mixed workloads due to better kernel fit.

Observability additions: new metrics: allocator.bucket_boundaries, allocator.padding_tokens_saved, prefill.reservations.used, prefill.wait_time_ms; dashboard panel in runtime -> batching to show quantile drift.

Backwards compatibility & rollout: feature is behind default-off flag and guarded; when enabled, allocator gracefully falls back to legacy fixed buckets on OOM or if quantile window insufficient.

Tests & CI: initial CI run failed (flake in integration prefill test due to timing), added deterministic timing hook and expanded wait time tolerance; all CI now passing.

Review thread (condensed):
- Owen Patel: "Great approach — concern about contention on quantile structure and GC pressure from per-request recording." Maya: "Quantile uses a compact reservoir sketch with batched updates every 50ms to avoid per-request allocations; added benchmarks showing <2% CPU. See commit 3 for batched_ingest optimization."
- Diego Alvarez: "What if kernel alignment heuristics cause worse packing for small models?" Maya: "Added cost model weighting to fall back to padding-minimizing composition when kernel throughput delta is small; added config knob kernel_alignment_weight (default 1.2)."
- Rina Sato: "Need to ensure prefill reservation can't be abused to starve normal traffic." Maya: "Prefill_reserve_pct defaults to 10% and is per-worker; reservations timeout (prefill_timeout_ms, default 30ms) and expire. Added metric prefill.reservations.expired and a test demonstrating fairness under burst."
- Requested changes were implemented in subsequent commits (batched quantile ingest, timeout guard, additional tests). Merge decision: after a short dogfood in staging for 48 hours and no regressions observed, approved and squashed.

CI summary: unit tests: pass, integration tests: pass, lint: pass, performance regression check: pass (no regression on p50/p95 for baseline scenarios).

Related: references ENG-8219 (dynamic batching improvements) and SUP-4191 (customer incident where KV-prefill bursts caused p95 spikes).

Notes for SRE: enable feature flag on canary pool using config runtime.feature.sparse_length_quantizer=true and monitor allocator.padding_tokens_saved and prefill.reservations.expired for 2 hours before wider roll-out.

Additional: included a small backwards-compatible API bump to scheduler metrics (added optional field "reservation_hint" to BatchEntry) — guarded in consumer code with feature flag.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation - core allocator and scheduler wiring
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Performance benching
- [x] Docs and rollout instructions
- [x] Security review (no sensitive data in quantile sketch)
- [x] Canaries and rollout plan
This PR is intentionally conservative: feature is off by default and includes multiple observability hooks and toggles to allow careful rollout across Dedicated and Private deployments.
payload.title: Sparse-length quantizer batch allocator with KV-prefill awareness

payload.body:
Summary: This PR wires the serving runtime to (1) consume the resolved quantization profile reference from routing metadata, (2) fetch and validate the corresponding profile metadata + artifacts from the model registry, (3) apply quantization mode deterministically for the request/model shard, and (4) emit metrics + structured events so rollouts can be observed and debugged. Motivation: The Quantization Profile Library is opt-in and route-scoped. For v1 we need deterministic selection, safe fallback, and clear signals for SRE and customers to verify whether a profile was applied for a given request. This PR is scoped to runtime behavior only; control plane resolution/compatibility checks are handled upstream (see related PRs). Design overview: - Input contract: router attaches quantization selection metadata to the request context (grpc metadata + internal request proto field). Runtime treats this as advisory and re-validates profile/model compatibility against the local model + GPU runtime capabilities. - Profile loading: new QuantProfileManager loads profile metadata via registry client (cached), then downloads artifact bundle (signed) to a local content-addressed cache. Artifacts are keyed by (profile_id, artifact_sha256) to guarantee determinism and avoid alias drift. - Deterministic application: on each request, runtime resolves outcome = {disabled|applied|fallback} with a single pass decision. If artifacts are missing/invalid/incompatible, runtime falls back to baseline precision for that model variant and records the reason code. No retry loops. - Runtime integration: ModelExecutor now accepts an optional QuantizationModeSpec derived from the profile. Kernel selection remains in kernel auto-selector; runtime passes a constrained spec and relies on kernel guardrails to reject unsupported mixes. - Observability: Adds counters and histograms for enablement outcome, artifact cache behavior, load latencies, and per-request annotations (logs + traces) including quant_profile_id and resolution outcome. Metrics are low-cardinality by design; profile_id is recorded in logs/traces but not as a metrics label. Metrics/events added: - Counter: runtime.quant_profile.requests_total{outcome=applied|fallback|disabled, reason=...} - Counter: runtime.quant_profile.artifact_fetch_total{result=success|error, source=cache|registry} - Histogram: runtime.quant_profile.artifact_fetch_latency_ms - Histogram: runtime.quant_profile.profile_resolve_latency_us - Gauge: runtime.quant_profile.cache_entries (debug-only, exported behind internal flag) - Structured event (json log): quant_profile_resolution with fields {request_id, route_id, model_id, model_variant, quant_profile_id, outcome, reason, artifact_sha256} - Trace attribute: redwood.quant_profile.id, redwood.quant_profile.outcome, redwood.quant_profile.reason Safety/guardrails: - Default behavior unchanged when routing metadata is absent or explicitly indicates "default". - Fallback is always baseline precision; never attempts to select an alternate quant profile in-runtime. - All profile fetches are rate-limited and cached; failures do not fail the request unless the request explicitly mandates a profile (not supported in v1; we treat all as best-effort). - Validates artifact signature + sha256 match before loading. - Adds circuit-breaker style suppression: repeated registry errors degrade to fallback without spamming registry. Testing: - Unit tests: profile parsing/validation, artifact cache keying, determinism invariants, reason code coverage. - Integration test: fake registry + runtime exec path ensures a quant_profile_id flows through request context -> applied -> annotated logs. - Perf smoke: decode path overhead measured to be <0.3% in microbench; artifact load occurs on first hit only. Rollout plan: This lands behind the existing feature gate in runtime config (QuantProfileRuntimeEnabled). When disabled, all new code paths short-circuit at the request boundary. Observability will be used in perf-canary and early beta routes to verify applied/fallback rates and to correlate latency/cost deltas. Related: - ENG-5816 runtime integration - ENG-5817 dashboards/metrics follow-up - pr-18427 policy compatibility guardrails (upstream) - pr-18445 control plane endpoints (upstream) Notes: This PR intentionally does not implement the global kill-switch (tracked separately). It also does not add profile_id as a metric label to avoid cardinality issues; profile granularity is available via logs/traces and audit events upstream.
- Runtime now consumes resolved quantization profile selection metadata and deterministically applies an approved profile when enabled.
- Added metrics/log annotations for quantization profile applied/fallback/disabled outcomes and artifact load/cache behavior.
Hiro Tanaka (review): Can we ensure the quant spec we pass cannot trigger a mixed FP8/INT8 path on unsupported GPUs? Suggest explicitly constraining allowed kernel families in the spec instead of relying only on selector rejection.
Noah Patel (author): Updated QuantizationModeSpec to include allowed_kernel_families derived from profile + local GPU caps. Selector still validates, but runtime no longer proposes mixed modes when caps don’t include them.
Omar El-Sayed (review): Any interaction with KV cache layout? Specifically, does enabling INT8 weights change KV precision assumptions or cache keying?
Noah Patel (author): KV cache stays in the baseline path for v1 (same precision/layout). Quant profile only affects weights/compute mode. Added a comment + a unit test asserting KV cache keying ignores quant_profile_id to avoid cache fragmentation.
Logan Wright (review): Please don’t add quant_profile_id as a metrics label; cardinality will be unbounded. Can we keep it to logs/traces and add a stable reason taxonomy for metrics?
Noah Patel (author): Agreed. Metrics now label only outcome + reason (bounded enum). quant_profile_id is in structured logs + traces only.
Nadia Rahman (review): For cost attribution, can we guarantee every request logs the resolved outcome even when disabled? Otherwise we can’t compute enabled-rate from sampled traces.
Noah Patel (author): Added a lightweight counter emitted on every request (disabled/applied/fallback). Trace attrs remain sampled; logs are available on-demand by request_id.
Mateo Alvarez (review): Determinism: ensure we never resolve an alias at runtime. Must be pinned to an immutable profile_id + artifact hash.
Noah Patel (author): Runtime only accepts explicit profile_id + artifact_sha256. If metadata contains alias fields they are ignored; also added a safeguard that rejects missing sha256 and falls back.
Sofia Ivanova (review): The error path currently retries registry fetch twice. This could amplify load during an incident. Prefer single attempt + cache negative results briefly.
Noah Patel (author): Removed retries; added a 30s negative cache for registry errors (bounded) and a suppression counter.
payload.title: Runtime: load quantization profile artifacts, apply mode, and emit observability signals

payload.body:
Background and motivation: Customers and compliance teams have asked for better visibility into when requests fall back to alternative KMS providers or when operator-scoped RBAC rules would have blocked operations in a future RBAC v2 rollout. This PR adds two complementary pieces: (1) structured KMS consent telemetry emitted whenever a KMS routing decision or consent check is taken, and (2) a non-enforcing RBAC shadow checker that replays live decisions (and historical audit samples) against RBAC v2 policies to surface policy deltas, false positives, and drift before we flip the enforcement bit.

Design summary: The telemetry layer emits a new schema (consent_event.v1) with fields: request_id, tenant_id, service_zone, kms_provider, consent_decision (allow/deny/fallback), decision_reason, latency_ms, operator_claims (list), and a consent_entropy bucket (computed per-tennant window). Events are coalesced by the audit coalescer to reduce noise for noisy paths (e.g., orchestration heartbeats). The RBAC shadow checker runs inline as a sidecar-enabled library call in the auth path when the feature flag rbac_shadow_enabled=true, and also as an offline migrator CLI that consumes audit logs and writes diffs to rbac-shadow/{date} index for analysis.

Commits (high level):
- add: pkg/kms/consent_telemetry.go + api schema for consent_event.v1
- add: internal/audit/coalescer.go to group low-value events
- add: cmd/rbac-shadow-runner for offline replay against RBAC v2 rules
- add: auth/shadow_checker.go integrating dry-run RBAC evaluation
- docs: docs/security/kms-consent-telemetry.md and migration guide
- infra: helm values and dashboard jsonnet for consent-entropy

Changed areas (high level):
- pkg/kms/ (telemetry hooks and minor refactors)
- internal/auth/ (shadow checker implementation and unit tests)
- internal/audit/ (coalescer and event sink registration)
- cmd/ (new migration tool to run shadow checks in bulk)
- observability/ (dashboards and alerts)
- docs/ (security and migration guide)

Testing and CI: Unit tests added for consent_event serialization and for the shadow checker decision engine. Integration test that spins up a minimal auth + fake-kms backend and asserts both emitted telemetry and shadow diffs. A small e2e run was executed against the staging audit stream with 10k events (sampled) to validate memory and disk footprint of the coalescer. Initial CI run failed due to a flaky clock-dependent test (auth/tokens_test). Flaky assertion fixed by using a deterministic clock stub; full CI re-run passed (all checks green).

Performance: Microbenchmarks show ~1.8% median added latency on the critical auth path when the inline shadow checker is enabled; due to this we gate the inline checker behind a per-cluster feature flag and recommend starting with the offline runner for large tenants. The consent telemetry path is async and uses buffered batching to keep tail latency impact negligible.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Step 1 (canary): Deploy to staging and two small production clusters with rbac_shadow_enabled=false and telemetry enabled for KMS service routes only.
- Step 2 (shadow): Enable rbac_shadow_enabled=true in a canary cluster; run the offline runner against 30d of audit samples to build a baseline.
- Step 3 (policy review): Use the rbac-shadow index and the generated deltas dashboard to triage policy false positives; update policy templates as needed.
- Step 4 (enforce): Targeted gradual enforcement after 2 weeks of no-high-risk deltas.

Operational notes and backward compatibility: The new event schema is versioned (v1) and emitted under the existing audit topic. Coalescer reduces event volume for high-cardinality tenants; customers can opt-out via tenant config (audit_coalesce=false). RBAC shadow checker does not change enforcement behavior unless the rollout flag rbac_enforce_v2=true. The offline runner includes a dry-run mode and outputs a signed report for compliance teams.

Security considerations: Consent events include operator claims and service_zone but redact raw PII; the telemetry pipeline is integrated with KMS usage tagging so event retention follows tenant retention policies. The offline runner accesses historical audit logs and requires the new role: role:rbac_shadow_runner (documented in the migration guide).

Related work and references: Linear ENG-8194 (RBAC shadowing MVP) and ENG-8271 (KMS consent telemetry). See docs/security/kms-consent-telemetry.md for schema and example queries.

This description is intentionally condensed; refer to changed files for implementation details and the migration guide for step-by-step instructions.

- Add RBAC v2 shadow checker that evaluates policy diffs without enforcing to detect regression risks.
- New dashboards: consent-entropy and shadow-checker-delta.

Fixes rare cases where SSE chunk boundaries split JSON tokens or tool-call markers, causing partial JSON emissions and fncall ordering issues. Adds a fragment inspector and deterministic mux serialization to improve stream stability.
Context: We still observed customer incidents where SSE streams emitted partial JSON objects when TCP/chunk boundaries bisected UTF-8 sequences or JSON tokens, and in edge cases interleaved tool/function-call sentinel frames were reordered by the mux during concurrent writes. Motivation: reduce customer-facing partial-json errors and fncall ordering regressions without large changes to the public streaming API. Changes: 1) Introduce a lightweight fragment_inspector component in the serving runtime that classifies incoming byte slices for safe emission: UTF-8 tail-finding, JSON token boundary hints, and a small checksum to detect replays. 2) Add a serialization shim in the sse_mux that serializes fragments using an ordinal stamped at the sender and enforces per-stream in-order flush guarantees for fncall/tool sentinel frames. 3) When a mid-json split is detected, the inspector will coalesce contiguous pending fragments up to a safe window or emit an escaped placeholder and enqueue a soft-resume marker; this avoids spurious partial JSON objects. 4) OpenAI-compat layer updates: ensure function-call sentinel objects are emitted as atomic events with a trailing zero-length field when serialized to SSE to make downstream parsers deterministic. 5) Add unit and integration tests including a deterministic replay harness and a small fuzz runner that simulates network chunking patterns encountered in production. Checklist: - [x] Add fragment_inspector implementation and tests; - [x] Add sse_mux serialization shim and tests; - [x] Update openai_compat emitter to append atomic sentinel framing; - [x] Add integration test that reproduces previously-reported mid-json incident; - [x] Run existing SSE compatibility suite and fix fallout. Commits: summary of 5 commits included: "fragment inspector + unit tests", "sse mux serializer and ordering enforcement", "openai_compat: atomic sentinel framing", "integration reproducer and regression test", "test harness and CI config for chunk-fuzzing". Files touched (high level): runtime/sse/fragment_inspector.rs, runtime/sse/mux_serializer.rs, openai_compat/stream_emitter.go, sdk/python/streaming_client.py, tests/integration/sse_midjson_repro.test, tests/fuzz/chunk_harness.go, ci/flakeguard.yml, docs/streaming_stability.md. Risk/regressions: small latency increase (microseconds) under extreme write fanout due to ordinal stamping; mitigated by batching path and configurable window. Performance: added microbenchmarks show median tail-latency unchanged for normal workloads and 0.6-1.4% increased CPU in worst-case synthetic stress tests. Why this approach: prior heuristic fixes addressed many delimiter issues but left a class of boundary/ordering races; explicit inspection + deterministic serialization is simpler to reason about and is easier to test and reason about during canary rollouts. Migration: default enabled; runtime flag sse.fragment_inspector=on to disable in emergencies. Merge: approved by reviewers after 2 rounds of small fixes; CI green; merged by squash.
Rajesh Menon: Good overall approach; please add a microbenchmark for mux path latency and ensure no lock convoy on high fanout. Request: expose window size as config.
Sofia Patel: Added microbench in commit 4 and made window tunable via runtime config. Benchmarks attached in CI run #4823.
Claire Zhou: Found a race in the inspector when streams close while coalesce is in-flight; please add test to cover close+coalesce.
Sofia Patel: Added test 'close_during_coalesce' and fixed ordering by holding ephemeral token until flush completes in commit 3.
Diego Alvarez: Verified openai_compat sentinel change is backward-compatible with existing parsers; approved after nit on docs.
Claire Zhou: Approve after tests and bench updates.

Motivation: long-tail tenant-level cost attribution and routing decisions are hard to reason about from point metrics alone. We prototype a Sankey-style invocation-flow visualization that links per-invocation stages (ingest->routing->model->postprocess) to sampled KV cache hit/miss patterns so product, SRE and billing teams can quickly surface which stage and tenant-shard combinations drive disproportionate token cost. Summary: adds an opt-in runtime flag to sample invocation flows and correlated KV cache signals; a low-overhead exporter that emits aggregated Sankey edges with weight and cost buckets; a Grafana dashboard with a Sankey panel and a complementary KV hitmap heatmap; alerting guidance and a staged rollout plan. Implementation details: 1) telemetry/exporter/kv_sampler.go implements a reservoir-based sampler keyed by (tenant_id,invocation_role,tenant_shard) and emits edge tuples (src_stage,dst_stage,weight,cost_tokens,kv_hit_mode) to the metrics pipeline with cardinality controls; 2) runtime/flags.go adds enable_observability_sankey and sankey_sample_rate (default off, 0.001 sample rate) with per-tenant override hooks; 3) metrics/transformer normalizes edge labels and buckets costs into [tiny,small,medium,large] to keep metrics cardinality bounded; 4) grafana/dashboards/tenant_sankey.json defines the Sankey panel with drilldown links to traces and a KV hitmap heatmap panel; 5) docs/observability/multi-tenant-sankey.md documents signal semantics, sampling lottery, and alert tuning recommendations. Rollout: feature gated; start with 25% of tenants for 48h, evaluate exporter CPU/ingest, increase to 100% after SLO verification. Backward compatibility: metrics are emitted under new metric namespaces (redwood.sankey.edge, redwood.sankey.kv_heat) and default sampling is off so no impact to existing dashboards. Checklist: ( ) unit tests added for sampler reservoir; (x) integration test asserting downstream aggregation; (x) grafana dashboard created and stored as code; (x) docs updated; (x) CI green; (x) rollout plan included. Observability impact: estimated additional exporter CPU ~+2% when enabled for sampled tenants; ingestion volume increase estimated at +0.5% of metrics cardinality at 0.1% global sampling. Related: follows ENG-1589 ideas about attribution; complements existing token-cost rollups by providing a flow-based view of where tokens are consumed and whether KV behavior correlates with cost spikes.
High-level changed files: telemetry/exporter/kv_sampler.go (new), runtime/flags.go (mod), metrics/transformer.go (mod), grafana/dashboards/tenant_sankey.json (new), docs/observability/multi-tenant-sankey.md (new), tests/integration/sankey_integration_test.go (new), ci/workflows/observability.yml (mod)
Ethan Zhao: 'Can we bound the cardinality of tenant_shard to avoid prometheus explosion?' Author reply: 'Yes, transformer buckets shard -> shard_group (16 groups) and we documented it; added unit test covering bucket mapping.' Marta Ruiz: 'Need explicit guidance on alert tuning for Sankey-derived attributions; someone might double count cost if they create alerts on both edge weight and token buckets.' Author reply: 'Added Alerting section in docs: recommend using composite SLOs and stable-signature thresholds, and suggested suppression window of 30m for transient bursts.' Samir Patel: 'CI flaky: sankey_integration_test failed on first run due to race in sampler reservoir; please add deterministic seed for test.' Author reply: 'Added seeding and retry in test; re-ran CI.' Reviewer approvals: Ethan approved after comments addressed; Marta approved; Samir approved after test fix.
Add optional multi-tenant invocation Sankey visualization and sampled KV hitmap to improve cost attribution and debugging. Feature is off-by-default and controlled via runtime flags. Provides a low-overhead path for teams to surface stage-level cost drivers and KV behavior. Rollout plan included.
If exporter CPU or metrics ingest spikes above threshold during rollout: 1) disable enable_observability_sankey globally, 2) revert to previous exporter image, 3) re-evaluate sample rate and shard bucketing, 4) contact telemetry-oncall (pager duty), 5) post-mortem if incident caused customer impact.
Unit tests for sampler reservoir and bucketing; deterministic seeding for integration; local grafana schema validation; manual e2e run against staging cluster with 10k synthetic invocations to verify Sankey edge distribution and heatmap coherence.

payload.body:
Context: Dedicated fleets occasionally experience short-lived microbursts that lead to aggressive provisioning and subsequent thrashing between scale-up and scale-down windows. Those events increase cost and transiently degrade tail latency. This change introduces two cooperating components: (1) an Elasticity Sentinel controller that inspects headroom, recent burst signature, and inter-fleet spillover signals to provide an admission recommendation (Allow/Hold/Reject) for new burst commitments; and (2) a Provisioning Guard that mediates autoscaler-triggered grow decisions with short-term decay and a credits-based backoff to avoid oscillation.

Motivation: Current autoscaling reacts to instantaneous util spikes and a short smoothing window. That pattern can cause repetitive warm pool churn when several tenants emit correlated bursts. We want predictable throughput guarantees for paying tenants while avoiding constant cluster churn and excessive spot/reservation churn.

What this PR does (high level): Adds a sentinel-based admission path that checks a tenant's requested burst against a short-term modeled headroom and historical burst acceptance rate. If the sentinel returns Hold, the Provisioning Guard will defer autoscaler-triggered provisioning for an exponential backoff window and attempt an opportunistic warmlet reuse path instead. The guard also exposes metrics and decision traces so SRE and product teams can tune thresholds without code changes.

Checklist:
- [x] Sentinel controller and decision API
- [x] Provisioning guard with credits and backoff state
- [x] Metrics: sentinel_decision, guard_backoff_duration, guard_credit_balance, sentinel_rejection_rate
- [x] Unit + integration tests covering acceptance, hold, and reject paths
- [x] Documentation for operators and runbook entries
- [x] E2E throughput benchmark harness and artifacts

Design notes: The sentinel evaluates three signals: static reservation (committed capacity), ephemeral headroom estimate (5s median of available warmlets), and a burst shape fingerprint (recent burstiness score). The decision is advisory for soft SLAs and is implemented as a short-circuit in the admission path so existing autoscalers only consult it; we do not hard-block allocations by default. The Provisioning Guard retains a per-fleet credit counter; credits are consumed on provisioning and slowly replenish. If credits are exhausted, the guard prefers warmlet reuse and queued admission with best-effort TTL.

Telemetry and observability: New Prometheus metrics, relevant labels (fleet_id, tenant_id, decision), and traces propagated through tracing headers. Added a small console page under Dedicated -> Fleet Health to display sentinel history and active backoffs.

Testing and rollout: Feature gated behind --enable-elasticity-sentinel. Rolling canary applied to two low-traffic Dedicated pools for 72 hours, followed by staged ramp to broader pools once regression-free. Benchmarks included: synthetic-surge-5s, correlated-tenants-30m, and denial-backoff-replay.

Risks and mitigations: Incorrect thresholds could increase request queuing and increase apparent latency. To mitigate: conservative defaults, telemetry-driven thresholds, and an automatic bypass if average queue time exceeds SLA thresholds.

Related: ENG-2147 (fleet burst stability), ENG-2230 (warmlet lifecycle improvements), SUP-1023 (customer incident that motivated the change).
Adds a non-breaking elasticity sentinel controller and provisioning guard to improve burst admission stability and reduce over-provisioning for Dedicated fleets.
Ava Martinez: Can we document how sentinel decisions impact billing visibility? Suggest adding a debug metric for expected vs actual capacity allocated.
Evelyn Park (author): Added sentinel_expected_alloc metric and a short section in the operator doc explaining billing behavior. The sentinel is advisory and will not change committed billing unless explicit override flag is enabled.
Rohit Patel: The exponential backoff parameters look aggressive for multi-tenant spikes. Recommend softer defaults and a configurable fast-path for SLA-tier tenants.
Evelyn Park: Made backoff base configurable and added a fast-path whitelist by tenant tier. Updated tests to cover whitelist behavior.
Linus Ng: Can we add more state reconciliation safety for controller restarts? The credit ledger is in-memory in the first patch.
Evelyn Park: Persist ledger to existing fleet metadata store with an atomic update; added idempotent reconcile and tests for restart scenarios.
Ava Martinez (LGTM): Behavior looks good in canary; metrics are sufficient to tune. Approved for squash-merge after a small lint fix.
Squash-merged by Ava Martinez after canary validation. Commit message condensed to key changes and metrics. Post-merge steps: enable feature-flag on canary clusters, schedule telemetry dashboard review in 48h.

payload.body:
Motivation: Large fleets show sustained token cost drift from a small fraction of tenants whose coldstart and microburst patterns defeat current batching and prefill defaults. This PR introduces two cooperating features: Cost Pulse Regulator (a tenant-level warmup and transient-budget controller) and Quant Pruner (a conservative quantization profile shrinker that trims non-impactful low-importance weights for warm tenants). The goal is to reduce unit cost on high-variance traffic while preserving tail latency and quality SLOs.

Design summary: The Cost Pulse Regulator attaches to the request routing layer and maintains a short-lived per-tenant pulse budget. It smooths bursts by: 1) coordinating short prefills for tenants flagged as burst-prone, 2) dynamically lowering preferred batch target for cold windows, and 3) gating optimistic cache reuse when latency headroom is tight. The Quant Pruner runs as a background job in the model profile pipeline: it takes an existing quant profile, evaluates a low-cost sensitivity scan on a sampled prompt set, and applies small, conservative pruning steps (per-channel thresholds) that have measured <0.5% BLEU-like quality drift on the sampled eval.

Implementation notes: - New package: pkg/econ/pulse_regulator.go implements the regulator state machine and exposes a lean API used by the router. - New package: pkg/quant/pruner.go implements the prune-and-simulate loop, with dry-run and apply modes. - API: costctl suggest now includes --pulse and --prune flags; Console shows a new CostPulse heatmap and a quant-prune preview. - Telemetry: added econ.pulse.{allocated,consumed,throttled}, quant.prune.{candidate_count,applied_count,estimated_risk}. - Safety: all prune actions are staged as suggested changes and require tenant opt-in for Private Dedicated customers; Hosted gets an opt-out list.

Checklist: - [x] Core regulator state machine and API wired to router. - [x] Quant pruner prototype with sensitivity scan. - [x] E2E smoke that simulates tenant microbursts and verifies no >5% latency tail regressions. - [x] Telemetry dashboards + alert thresholds added. - [x] Documentation and console UI stub.

Testing: Unit tests for state transitions and prune heuristics added. E2E synthetic run against prefiller with a 10k request trace shows ~12-18% cost reduction on bursty tenants and median tail latency increase <2%. CI included simulated load tests.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to canary tenants in staging (2/25), 2) run 48h cost/quality canary with traffic shadowing, 3) enable auto-suggest for high-variance tenants (opt-in) while keeping apply locked. Full rollout contingent on telemetry signal.

Rollback: regulator runs behind a feature flag; pruner applies changes as candidate diffs until explicitly accepted. Remove flag or revoke tenant opt-in to revert impact.
Lars Becker: Please add a metric for 'pulse_rejected' so we can track how often we deny a prefill. Also call out expected memory overhead per tenant.
Aisha Kapoor: Added pulse_rejected metric; regulator stores only 128B of state per tenant in memory on average (updated docs).
Maya Chen: Quant pruning looks promising — include an explicit guard to prevent pruning when eval diversity score is below threshold; otherwise we risk overfitting to small samples.
Aisha Kapoor: Implemented diversity guard and added integration test to exercise low-diversity failure mode; documented opt-in requirement for production apply.
Diego Alvarez: CI flaky on synthetic e2e — tracked to timing in router; suggested increasing test timeouts and backing off non-deterministic sleep. Fixed and re-ran.
Lars Becker: approved after telemetry and safety comments addressed.
Introduced Cost Pulse Regulator to smooth tenant microbursts and Quant Pruner to suggest conservative quant-profile trims. Early canary saw cost reductions for bursty tenants; features are gated behind flags and require tenant opt-in for apply. No breaking changes to public API.
Enable feature flag 'econ.pulse.enabled' in staging for canary tenants. Watch econ.pulse.throttled and quant.prune.estimated_risk dashboards. Set alert: >2% SLA tail regression for 1h to trigger automatic rollback.

payload.body:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets currently use a single headroom target per pool which causes oscillation when tenants with bursty traffic compete for transient capacity. This PR introduces two coordinated features: a weighted headroom harmonizer (an autoscaler policy that allocates headroom proportionally to tenant importance and observed tail-utilization) and an independent utilization sentry service that produces smoothed per-tenant utilization fingerprints for the harmonizer to consume. Key benefits: smoother scaling decisions, fewer micro-scale provisioning churns, improved throughput guarantees during transient spikes, and clearer telemetry for SLA debugging. Design summary: 1) Weighted Headroom Harmonizer: policy evaluates per-tenant effective weight = config.weight * max(1, percentile_util/target_util); desired_headroom = base_headroom * normalized_weight; uses multi-window smoothing (5s, 30s, 5m) to avoid reacting to short spikes; respects pool-level max_headroom_pct and cluster budget constraints; supports manual overrides and canary tiers. 2) Utilization Sentry: lightweight collector deployed per-pool that computes HDR sketches and percentile deltas on rolling windows and exports aggregated 50/90/99 utilization and burstiness score to the orchestrator via a compact protobuf. It also emits change-points to accelerate harmonizer when a true workload shift is detected. Compatibility and safety: harmonizer is opt-in per-pool and defaults to passthrough behavior; when enabled, autoscaler fallback rules ensure we never reduce reserved capacity below existing commitments; the harmonizer can be configured with conservative gain and cooldown settings for gradual rollout. Telemetry and observability: new metrics: redwood.harmonizer.effective_weight, redwood.harmonizer.desired_headroom_pct, redwood.sentry.burstiness_score, redwood.sentry.delta_pctiles, and event logs for change-point triggers. Dashboard: added a harmonizer panel to Dedicated -> Pools showing headroom allocation per-tenant and predicted provisioning delta. Tests and validation: unit tests for weight normalization, simulated cluster-level integration tests with synthetic tenants (steady, periodic burst, random microbursts), and two-night canary on a small dedicated pool. Performance: sentry uses O(1) per-request amortized CPU and keeps memory at <2MB per-pool by using compact sketches; harmonizer computation runs on the control-plane cadence (default 5s) and is horizontally sharded. Migration and rollout: feature gated behind pool config.enable_weighted_headroom; rollout plan: 1) dry-run mode (0%) with metrics only; 2) canary on non-critical dedicated pools for 48-72h; 3) gradual ramp to 25/50/100% across regions in 1-2 weeks if there are no regressions. Related work items: ENG-2489, ENG-2620; support follow-up SUP-342. Implementation notes: avoid tight coupling with the existing reservation ledger; harmonizer emits desired headroom signals that the existing provisioner reconciler consumes; added idempotent tests to ensure reconciler tolerates transient conflicting signals. Security and perf review: no new network surface besides internal control plane RPCs; protobuf message is versioned. Rollback: harmonizer supports immediate disable flag and a fast-fail-safe which falls back to legacy allocation on mismatch thresholds. Checklist: [x] design doc; [x] unit tests; [x] e2e simulations; [x] telemetry dashboards; [x] canary run configured; [x] docs. Potential follow-ups: integrate tenant-priority SLA scores into weight calculation; add machine-learning based burst predictors as an optional plugin.
Liam: Please clarify how this interacts with existing reservation decay; suggestion: add explicit unit test for negative headroom flows || Maya: Added test and explicit guard to not touch committed reservations; clarified in description and tests. || Priya: Can we surface tenant weight changes in audit logs? requested change: add audit event for manual weight updates || Maya: Added audit event and small-change log; backed by e2e assertion. || Diego: Small nit: rename burstiness_score -> burst_index to match telemetry naming; asked for a rename to keep dashboards consistent || Maya: Renamed metric and kept compatibility alias for 2 weeks; updated docs. || Priya: Approved after audit logs and small docs updates. || Diego: Approved. || Liam: Approved with canary follow-up noted.
Added weighted headroom harmonizer to dedicated autoscaler; Introduced Utilization Sentry for per-tenant percentile reporting; New metrics and dashboard panels for headroom allocations; Opt-in rollout and conservative defaults; No breaking changes by default (feature-gated).

payload.body:
Stabilizes continuous batching under KV-heavy loads by introducing a priority-credit reflow mechanism and adaptive soft timeouts. Reduces starvation of KV-pinned requests and smooths tail latency. No public API changes.
Motivation: In long-running continuous-batcher workloads with a mix of small KV-pinned requests and large model-generating requests, we observed starvation of pinned requests and amplified tail latencies when the batcher filled with long-running tokens. Existing preemption heuristics are brittle under bursty KV traffic.

This PR introduces a priority-credit reflow mechanism that: (1) maintains a lightweight per-priority credit budget, (2) triggers a reflow window when soft-timeouts/jitter indicate a slot is held too long, (3) gracefully reclaims or reassigns credits from low-impact/low-priority slots to satisfy pinned short requests, and (4) adapts refill rates based on occupancy and KV pin statistics.

Design notes: The reflow controller is intentionally decoupled from kernel execution paths; it emits hints to the scheduler so kernel hot paths remain minimal. A new credit_reflow component keeps short histograms for slot hold times and uses EWMA to avoid reacting to single outliers. Soft timeouts are jittered to avoid synchronized drains across replicas.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation: credit accounting, reflow controller, scheduler hook
- [x] Tests: unit coverage for credit logic, deterministic integration replay for KV scenarios
- [x] Benchmarks: real-trace perf harness added and baseline recorded
- [x] Docs: operator tuning guide and recommended presets
- [x] Safety: feature gated behind runtime flag 'batcher.priority_credit_reflow' (off by default in release channel)

Testing and roll-out: Feature gated and shipped behind a config flag. Rolling canary to Dedicated then Hosted; default remains off for customers until we validate in production canaries. If regressions observed, we auto-disable via runtime gate and fallback to previous scheduler behavior.
Key changes across batcher and KV subsystems:
- src/runtime/batcher/scheduler.go: add priority-credit accounting, reflow loop and heuristics to drain credits from low-priority slots.
- src/runtime/batcher/credit_reflow.go: new component implementing credit decay, reflow windows and adaptive refill on soft timeouts.
- src/runtime/kv/cache_manager.go: expose pin-aware stats and per-slot weight hints used by the scheduler.
- src/runtime/batcher/timeouts.go: adjustable jittered soft-timeout logic tied to occupancy signals.
- integration-tests/batcher/kv_replay_test.go: new deterministic replay harness for KV-pin heavy traces.
- perf/benchmarks/continuous_batcher_real_trace.yaml: benchmark config and helper script.
- docs/ops/continuous-batcher-tuning.md: operator-facing knobs and recommended presets.
- examples/quickstart/batcher-tuning.ipynb: notebook walkthrough for reproducing perf numbers.
- Unit tests for credit accounting and scheduler hook.
- Integration replay: 10-minute KV-heavy trace run comparing main vs this branch using deterministic seed.
- Perf benchmark: real-client trace over 100k requests measuring p50/p95/p99 latency and token throughput.
- Canary rollout: enable flag on 2 dedicated pools (staging), monitor P99 and error rates for 24h before enabling broader fleet.
Staging perf runs (real-trace):
- Baseline (main): p50=22ms p95=110ms p99=340ms throughput=13.5k rps
- This PR (flag=true): p50=24ms p95=95ms p99=210ms throughput=13.1k rps
Notes: small p50 regression (due to occasional preemptive credit moves) but substantial p95/p99 improvement for KV-heavy tails; end-to-end token cost delta ~+0.8% under this trace. Under mixed workloads (50/50 KV/generation) throughput within 3% of baseline.
Risks: aggressive reflow could harm throughput if credits are reclaimed too eagerly; per-tenant fairness complications; potential interaction with existing hedging logic.
Mitigations: runtime gate and operator knob to cap controller CPU, EWMA smoothing to prevent oscillation, integration tests that run under synthetic heavy load, canary rollout with automatic rollback on P99 regressions, interaction tests with hedging and kv-pin logic added.
Operator knobs (docs/ops/continuous-batcher-tuning.md):
- batcher.priority_credit_reflow (bool)
- batcher.reflow_window_ms (int, default 60)
- batcher.reflow_jitter_pct (int, default 15)
- batcher.controller_cpu_budget_pct (int, default 2)
- batcher.per_tenant_credit_override (map in tuning config)
Recommended initial preset: "balanced-kv" (enabled on dedicated staging only).
Arjun: 'Nice separation of concerns. Two asks: reduce allocations in hot path and add a safety timeout that never lets reflow run more than X% CPU.'
Maya: 'Addressed: credit accounting uses pre-allocated ring buffer and atomic ops; added a controller_cpu_budget config with default 2% per scheduler thread.'
Lena: 'Integration test is solid. Can we get a deterministic failure scenario where reflow misbehaves?'
Maya: 'Added replay harness that can inject synthetic KV spikes and assert no starvation beyond configured SLA.'
Diego: 'Consider exposing per-tenant knobs at Dedicated scale.'
Maya: 'Added per-tenant override and documented caveat about potential cross-tenant fairness impacts.'
Pull request approved by Arjun and Lena after two rounds of feedback. Diego approved with comment about ops rollout steps.

payload.body:
Context: This PR implements the v1 hourly aggregation job for the internal Unit Economics dashboard. It introduces warehouse schema migrations, a scheduled aggregator (hourly) that joins token metering with cost inputs (GPU rate card + allocation factors), and initial materialized views to power cost/$ per 1M output tokens drilldowns by model, region, and customer tier. This is the first production path for the canonical metric (blended $/1M output tokens) and is intended to be finance-aligned while still allowing iteration via versioned logic. Scope: (1) New warehouse tables for hourly aggregates and reconciliation-friendly rollups, (2) A job that runs hourly with late-arrival handling and idempotent upserts, (3) Materialized views for dashboard queries (time series + top-N breakdowns), (4) Data validation checks to fail fast on missing dimensions and prevent silent drops. Non-goals: Streaming output token parity is handled in a separate PR; this assumes output_tokens is present and accurate in metering. Implementation details: The aggregator reads from `metering.request_tokens_hourly` (or equivalent staged fact) and joins against `finance.gpu_rate_card_hourly` via normalized region + provider + capacity_type. We allocate shared/idle components using the current v1 allocation factors table (owned by Finance), then compute blended cost per output token. All cost computations are stored in USD with 6 decimals; dashboard views scale to $/1M output tokens. Key tables: `analytics.unit_econ_hourly_fact_v1` (grain: hour x model_id x model_version x quant_profile x region_norm x customer_tier), `analytics.unit_econ_hourly_rollup_v1` (grain: hour x region_norm x customer_tier; used for reconciliation), `analytics.unit_econ_job_runs` (job run audit / late data tracking). Key MVs: `analytics.mv_unit_econ_ts_by_model_region_tier_v1` (time series), `analytics.mv_unit_econ_topn_models_7d_v1`, `analytics.mv_unit_econ_topn_regions_7d_v1`, `analytics.mv_unit_econ_topn_tiers_7d_v1`. Idempotency / late data: We reprocess a sliding window (default 36h) each run to incorporate late-arriving metering, then upsert by primary key (hour + dims + version). We also persist `processed_through_hour` and row counts per run for oncall visibility. Performance: Hourly fact table is partitioned by day(hour_ts) and clustered by (region_norm, model_id, customer_tier). MVs use pre-aggregated measures to keep dashboard query latency <2s for common groupings. Illustrative snippet (aggregation core): `blended_cost_usd = (gpu_compute_cost_usd + gpu_idle_alloc_usd + shared_overhead_alloc_usd)` and `blended_usd_per_1m_output_tokens = (blended_cost_usd / nullif(output_tokens,0)) * 1e6`. Validation: The job asserts non-null for required dims (model_id, region_norm, customer_tier) and records a `dropped_rows_reason` metric when input facts are excluded (e.g., unknown region mapping). Follow-ups: (a) streaming output token parity (ENG-8421), (b) region normalization table productionized (ENG-8424), (c) quantization_profile tagging (ENG-8425). Test plan: `bin/unit_econ_agg --dry-run --start 2025-01-28T00:00Z --end 2025-01-28T06:00Z` against staging; compare rollup totals to billing exports for the same window (within tolerance).
Logan Wright (review): Can we confirm the grain includes quant_profile and model_version, even if v1 UI doesn’t expose them yet? If not, we’ll regret it for regressions. Also, what’s the strategy for late metering arrivals (we’ve seen >12h delays during incidents). Mei Lin (author): Yes—fact table grain includes both `model_version` and `quantization_profile` (nullable until ENG-8425 lands), UI can ignore for now. For late arrivals: I set the sliding reprocess window to 36h by default and made it configurable. We upsert into the partitioned fact table keyed by (hour_ts, model_id, model_version, quant_profile, region_norm, customer_tier). Nadia Rahman (review): The job currently filters out rows with missing output_tokens; can we surface that in metrics (otherwise we’ll hide the streaming undercount issue). Also, please ensure we don’t accidentally include input tokens in the denominator. Mei Lin (author): Added counters: `unit_econ_agg.dropped_rows_missing_output_tokens` and `unit_econ_agg.dropped_rows_missing_dims`. Denominator is explicitly `output_tokens` only (see compute_hourly_fact.sql). Caleb Johnson (review): A couple of concerns: 1) null region mapping currently becomes 'unknown' and is included—Finance may not want that in blended KPI. 2) We should add a run audit row even on failure so oncall can see the gap. Mei Lin (author): Addressed (1) by excluding unknown from KPI MVs (still stored in fact for debugging) and adding `unknown_region_tokens` to rollup so reconciliation can explain deltas; (2) job now writes a `job_runs` row at start and updates with status=failed + error summary on exception. Cole Summers (review): Rate card join: I think capacity_type mismatch (reserved vs on-demand) will bite us. Can we default to blended rate by region if capacity_type is null, but also track how often we fall back? Mei Lin (author): Implemented `rate_card_fallback_used` boolean + counter. Join order: exact (region, provider, capacity_type) -> fallback (region, provider, 'blended') -> fallback (region, 'any', 'blended') for staging only (prod will require provider). Added a hard failure if we can’t find a rate for a prod region/provider. Logan Wright (review): Looks good; last request: add a note to docs about versioning (v1) and how we’ll roll v2 without breaking dashboards. Mei Lin (author): Added doc section: schema has `_v1` suffix; future versions write parallel tables/views, with a `analytics.unit_econ_active_version` pointer used by API layer. Logan approved. Nadia approved after re-run. Caleb approved with minor nits. Cole approved.

Summary: Add a lightweight slab-level acknowledgement and ordered-event siloing mechanism to harden our HTTP EventStream (text/event-stream) ingestion path against chunked-transfer reordering, partial JSON emissions, and tool-call interleaving. Motivation: production incidents (see ENG-3142) showed rare but exploitable windows where a sequence of small chunks caused partial JSON to be delivered out-of-order to downstream JSON framers and the OpenAI-compat layer, producing malformed function-call payloads or dropped events. This PR introduces an in-protocol slab ACK ledger and an ordered event silo that: 1) assigns small incremental slab IDs to contiguous chunk groups, 2) buffers slab payloads until slab-level completeness heuristics are satisfied, and 3) emits an ordered, atomic JSON span to the existing SSE coalescer so function-call sentinels and structured output remain intact. Approach: implement a compact ACK/slot ledger in pkg/streaming/acknowledger, add a slab-aware reader wrapper to pkg/streaming/reader, and extend api/openai/compat/stream_framer.go to prefer slab-anchored boundaries when reassembling events. This is backwards-compatible: the ledger is only used intra-proxy; clients are unaffected. Changes include conservative in-memory limits and an opt-in config flag (REDWOOD_STREAM_SLAB_ACK_ENABLED) to allow staged rollout. Tests & validation: new unit tests for slab edge-cases, an integration scenario that replays recorded incident traces, and a canary deployment to a subset of streaming prod routes. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (linked) and Linear tickets created - [x] Unit tests covering partial JSON spans and tool-call interleaving - [x] Integration replay against incident trace - [x] Canary rollout plan and telemetry (latency/correctness) - [x] Post-merge rollback instructions and feature flagging Rollout: start with canary (5%) for client-facing streaming routes for 48h, validate JSON fidelity and tool-call success rates, then 25% for 24h before full rollout. Related: ENG-3142 (incident), ENG-3187 (streaming perf followup).
Julian Soto (2026-01-15): Can we bound the slab buffer memory per connection? Suggest adding a hard cap and LRU eviction for long-hanging slabs.
Priya Nair (2026-01-15): Added cap and eviction policy; documented in internal/config/streaming_flags.go and added metrics for eviction counts.
Maya Chen (2026-01-20): Integration test passes, but saw a small latency bump under synthetic bursts. Can we add a histogram for slab assembly time?
Priya Nair (2026-01-21): Added prometheus histogram (stream_slab_assembly_seconds) and adjusted heuristics to favor early flush when assembly time exceeds threshold.
Ethan Brooks (2026-02-03): LGTMs on core code, left a minor nit on variable naming in reader.go (slot -> slabSlot).
Priya Nair (2026-02-03): Renamed variable and pushed follow-up commit.
Fix: reduce malformed partial JSON and tool-call interleaving by introducing slab-level ACKing and ordered event siloing for streaming ingestion. Rollout behind feature flag; canary first. Impact: improves streaming JSON fidelity at very low latency cost.
