Adds a lightweight multi-sdk credential bridge with tracing metadata and retry-presets. Bumps TS/Go/Python SDKs minor versions. No public API breaking changes.
Context: Multiple SDKs had divergent credential helpers and retry defaults, causing inconsistent streaming reconnection behavior and absent cross-sdk tracing for auth events. Motivation: provide a single lightweight bridge in the redwood control plane that standardizes (1) credential fetch/fallback semantics, (2) streaming reconnect presets, and (3) attach explicit tracing/telemetry markers for auth lifecycle events across Python, TypeScript and Go SDKs. This PR implements: - a small 'credential-orchestra' shim that lives in each SDK and delegates to a shared policy surface (pluggable) - explicit RetryProfile presets exposed as ergonomics-friendly factories (latency-first, cost-first, steady-load) - stream handshake telemetry points (auth.requested, auth.succeeded, auth.refresh, auth.failed) to aid SRE/Debugging - minor API ergonomics: simplified session factory signatures and single-arg stream helpers - version bumps: python-sdk v3.8.1, typescript-sdk v1.28.3, go-sdk v1.6.2 Checklist: [x] implement credential-orchestra adapter in TS/Py/Go [x] add RetryProfile factories and tests [x] add telemetry spans and event markers [x] docs + examples updated [x] QA run and canary on dedicated infra [x] release notes drafted Scope of changes: Commits: - feat(credential): add credential-orchestra adapter and fallback chain (d2f4a6c) - feat(retry): introduce RetryProfile factories and presets (b9c1f2d) - perf(stream): wire auth lifecycle telemetry into stream handshake (3e11b77) - chore(sdk): bump versions across py/ts/go and update changelogs (e5a2b88) - test: add cross-sdk integration tests for reconnect and auth-fallthrough (7f4d3e1) Changed areas (high level): - sdks/typescript/src/credential-orchestra.ts (+ adapter tests) - sdks/typescript/src/stream/handshake.ts (+ telemetry markers) - sdks/typescript/package.json - sdks/python/redwood/credential_orchestra.py (+ session_factory) - sdks/python/redwood/streaming/handshake.py (+trace integration) - sdks/python/setup.cfg - sdks/go/credentials/orchestra.go (+retry presets) - sdks/go/stream/handshake.go - docs/sdk/auth.md (new section) - examples/multi-sdk/credential-fallback/ (new samples) - tests/integration/mock_auth_server.go - ci/fixtures/go_auth_fixture.sh Test strategy: unit tests per SDK (credential fallback, preset selection), integration tests that run a mock auth server and exercise refresh and failover, and an end-to-end canary against Dedicated staging. Observability: new metrics auth.event.count{kind=..}, auth.latency_ms, and span attributes redwood.cred.mode and redwood.retry.preset. CI: initial CI run failed on the Go integration job due to missing test fixture; the fixture was added in commit 7f4d3e1 and CI rerun passed. Review summary: Reviewers requested API clarity, telemetry naming, and docs. See review_comments for details. Backwards compatibility: adapter is additive. Existing SDK auth helpers are preserved; customers can opt-in to the new default via minor SDK upgrade. Rollout plan: - cut SDK minors, publish packages - enable bridge by default in Hosted infra canary cohort - monitor auth.event.* and retry metrics for regressions - rollback by toggling opt-in flag in console if regressions observed.
Miguel Alvarez (requested changes): Please clarify the RetryProfile naming - 'latency-first' vs 'fast-path' may be confusing across SDKs. Also confirm whether the presets are tunable per-tenant.
Priya Patel (author reply): Renamed presets to latency-first/cost-conscious/steady-load and added tenant override hook. See commit b9c1f2d.
Zoe Chen: Would like the telemetry attributes names to follow 'redwood.auth.*' instead of 'auth.*' for consistency with other spans.
Priya Patel: Updated span attributes to redwood.auth.event and redwood.auth.latency_ms in 3e11b77.
Daniel Kim (approved): Verified Go fixture and integration tests on my laptop, metrics emitted as expected, minor nits fixed.
CI Bot: initial go-integration failed (missing fixture). After fix and rerun, CI green.

Motivation: tenant workloads show correlated cold-start patterns that the current prefetch heuristics miss, and static quant profiles are suboptimal for transient miniburst traffic. This PR introduces a coordinated 'frugal-fusion' prefetch optimizer that synthesizes cross-tenant heat signals, a small ruleset language for safe warmup decisions, and a telemetry bridge that exports anonymized cost/latency signals to the econ services. Goals: reduce token-unit cost by shifting warmups to low-cost windows, avoid over-warming, and dynamically select quantization profiles for warm batches without exposing tenant data. This change is additive and behind the feature flag 'frugal_fusion_v1'. Summary of changes: 1) new service module prefetch/fusion orchestrator that aggregates prefills and emits safe warmup plans, 2) lightweight rules DSL and policy engine for warmup gating and budget limits, 3) quant-profile selector that recommends int8/int4 fallbacks tied to batch shape and perf guardrails, 4) telemetry bridge that pumps cost/latency histograms and policy decisions to the econ pipeline, 5) CLI tool redwoodctl prefetch simulate + dry-run export for operator validation, 6) unit and integration tests and a small perf benchmark harness. Backwards compatibility: config defaults preserve existing prefetch behavior unless the feature flag is enabled; migration notes below. Tests & performance: local simulations using synthetic traces (mixed chat/complete) show median per-token cost reduction of 12-16% for tenants with >15% cold-start traffic and average latency impact of +3ms tail in worst-case windows. Canary on small set of tenants (5 tenants) produced 14% cost saving and zero customer-facing errors over 72h. Safety: budget guardrails enforce a maximum warmup budget per tenant per hour and allow automatic rollback on SLO degradation. Telemetry is anonymized and sampled to avoid PII leakage; KMS encryption used for bridge credentials. Rollout plan: canary (feature flag + 5 tenants) -> expand to 20% traffic over 1 week -> full roll when metrics stable for 7 days. Operators can revert by disabling frugal_fusion_v1. Related work: builds on ENG-1211 (prefill telemetry schema), reuses parts of the batch-cache coordinator. Linear tickets: ENG-4321 (prefetch optimizer) and ENG-4333 (quant profile selector). Checklist: [x] design doc linked, [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] perf harness, [x] e2e canary, [x] docs/console UI for toggling flag, [x] RBAC for telemetry bridge. Migration: default remains unchanged; to adopt, set tenant_policy.prefetch.strategy = "frugal_fusion": run redwoodctl prefetch simulate --tenant <id> and review dry-run report; optionally enable frugal_fusion_v1. Observability: new dashboards: Prefetch/Fusion Plans, Prefetch/Policy Matches, FrugalFusion-Cost-Delta; alerts: FFusion:BudgetExceeded, FFusion:SLORegression. Implementation notes: the fusion orchestrator keeps a compact sliding window (max 1h) of tenant sampling signatures and uses a bloom-filter-backed coalescer to propose shared warmups; quant selector samples batch shapes and consults an offline oracle for quality prediction before recommending lower precision. Runtime path changes are guarded and asynchronous to avoid blocking the main serving pipeline.
Diego Morales: The bloom coalescer looks promising but we should bound memory. Please add an eviction strategy and a max-cardinality test.
Ava Chen: Added eviction and a max-card test; adjusted sliding window cardinality to 10k per shard (configurable).
Priya Patel: Quant selector needs a guard to avoid switching profiles mid-request; ensure recommendations only apply to new batches.
Ava Chen: Quant changes now apply only at batch-creation time; added docstring and an integration test to verify no mid-request mutation.
Ethan Walker: CI flake observed in perf harness; can you stabilize the synthetic trace seed?
Ava Chen: Fixed seeds and improved harness warmup; reran canary reports.
Security review (Sofia Martinez): Telemetry payload looks OK but add sampling and retention policy to telemetry/bridge/README.md
Ava Chen: Added sampling description and default retention of 7 days; bridge uses KMS for creds as noted.
Add a configurable frugal-fusion prefetch optimizer that reduces cold-start-driven token costs by dynamically coordinating warmups and recommending quantization profiles; disabled by default and gated by frugal_fusion_v1 feature flag.
Enable via feature flag and validate with redwoodctl prefetch simulate dry-run output. Monitor Prefetch/Fusion Plans and FrugalFusion-Cost-Delta dashboards; watch FFusion:BudgetExceeded and FFusion:SLORegression alerts. Rollback by disabling frugal_fusion_v1.

Context: Customers using structured output with streaming have experienced silent schema drift and partial tool invocations being forwarded when the model output is invalid. This PR implements a verifiable response protocol (VRP) and schema handshake to give callers deterministic behavior for structured outputs, plus safer tool/function calling semantics and improved OpenAI-compat error mapping. Motivation: reduce customer incidents caused by malformed streaming JSON and ensure tool calls are only executed after an explicit handshake when schema constraints apply. Goals: 1) Provide a wire-level handshake that lets the server accept/convert/decline a requested response_format/schema; 2) Validate streams incrementally with lightweight checkpoints to allow mid-stream recovery/resume; 3) Fence tool/function calls until the model output has passed a minimal schema gate; 4) Expose clear error codes for API consumers and map them to OpenAI-compat shapes when using the compatibility layer; 5) Make strict validation opt-in per-route so we can rollout safely.

What changed (high level): - Introduces a VRP layer that negotiates response_format + schema version at request start. The server can respond with an accepted schema variant or an explicit negotiation rejection with reasons. - Adds incremental validation checkpoints in the streaming path. Each checkpoint emits a small signed resume token that the client can use to resume validation-aware streams when transient failures occur. Checkpoints are lightweight and intended not to increase per-token latency significantly. - Adds a toolcall fencing mechanism: tool invocation events are withheld from the tool-executor until the VRP gate for the required structured fields reaches a configurable minimal confidence/validation state. This prevents partial/malformed payloads from reaching backend tooling. - Extends OpenAI compatibility mapper to translate VRP-specific errors into OpenAI-compatible error objects (error.type, error.code, error.param) so clients using the OpenAI shape get meaningful, actionable diagnostics. - Config and rollout: a new per-route config vrp.strict_mode: off|permissive|strict. By default routes remain permissive; strict must be enabled by customer or rolled out by feature flag. - Metrics/tracing: new metrics vrp.validation.ok, vrp.validation.fail, vrp.stream.resume_count, vrp.tool.fenced_count and tracing spans for handshake/validation checkpoints. - Documentation: docs/openapi/response_format.md and examples/strict-mode-rollout.md added.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4527) - [x] Unit tests for handshake and checkpoint parsing - [x] Integration test for toolcall fencing - [x] OpenAI-compat mappings covered by contract tests - [x] Feature flag and rollout plan in examples/strict-mode-rollout.md - [x] Observability events emitted

Commits summary: - feat(vrp): add VRP handshake and negotiation state machine - feat(api/stream): emit validation checkpoints and resume-token structure - feat(tooling): implement toolcall fence and executor gating - feat(compat): map VRP errors to openai-compatible error shapes - test(vrp): add unit + integration tests for handshake and fencing - docs: response_format spec + rollout example - fix: edge-case resume-token truncation in low-memory paths

Files changed (high level): [
  "src/api/response/vrp_handler.rs",
  "src/runtime/streaming/checkpoint.rs",
  "src/api/compat/openai_mapper.rs",
  "runtime/config/vrp_config.yaml",
  "docs/openapi/response_format.md",
  "examples/strict-mode-rollout.md",
  "tests/vrp_integration.test"
],

Small snippets (illustrative): - vrp handshake response shape (pseudo): {"vrp_accepted":true,"schema_variant":"v3-coerce-permissive","resume_token":"rTkn:eyJ..."} - error example: {"error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"schema mismatch","code":"VRP_SCHEMA_MISMATCH","param":"response_format"}}

Review conversation:
- Diego Morales: "Can we make the checkpoint signature size configurable? I worry about payload bloat for short lived sessions." (requested change)
- Aisha (author): "Added config.max_checkpoint_sig_bytes to vrp_config.yaml and made default small (96 bytes). Tests updated to simulate truncation." (author reply)
- Rina Sato: "Toolcall fence looks good but we should bubble a non-500 error to callers when a tool is intentionally withheld." (requested change)
- Aisha: "Changed fence behavior: it now returns a VRP_TOOL_FENCED user-visible error (4xx-like in OpenAI-compat) and emits a trace span so operator tooling can correlate." (author reply)
- Evan Liu: "Performance baseline looked acceptable in local canary; please include a rollout note about CPU footprint." (comment)
- Aisha: "Added perf numbers to examples/strict-mode-rollout.md and added a disabled perf test that can be re-enabled during canaries." (author reply)
- Diego Morales: "Approving pending CI green and small nit about variable name in checkpoint.rs" (approved after nit fixed)

CI summary:
- unit (linux) : pass (flaky test retried once)
- integration (docker): pass
- e2e (canary harness): pass
- lint: pass
- perf-check (opt-in): skipped in CI
Overall status: pass

Observability and rollout notes: - Default behavior is permissive; customers won't see changes unless they enable vrp.strict_mode or request strict via API. - Recommend staged rollout: enable on 1% traffic with onboarding test prompts, then 10%, then full. - Watch vrp.validation.fail and vrp.tool.fenced_count; set alert if fenced_count grows unexpectedly after enabling strict.

Backward compatibility: - Non-VRP clients (no response_format/schema) are unaffected. - OpenAI-compat mapping preserves existing shapes for existing errors; new error codes are added but mapped to OpenAI type/param so clients can handle them.

Merge: merged by Rina Sato using squash and merge. See changelog entry for VRP handshake in release notes.
Adds a verifiable response protocol (VRP) that negotiates a schema handshake for streamed responses and tool calls. Introduces incremental validation checkpoints, new error codes for schema/stream/tool failures, and a per-route strictness toggle (opt-in rollout).

Context: Multiple teams reported fragile credential fallbacks and repeated boilerplate when wiring streaming consumers with refreshable tokens. The SDKs had asymmetrical helper surfaces which made cross-language parity and onboarding harder. Goal: Provide a small, well-documented credential registry abstraction (CredentialRegistry) that composes sources (env, file, delegated, cache) with deterministic fallthrough semantics, plus a tiny ergonomic helper PullStream.simplify() that normalizes async/pull streaming patterns across Python/TS/Go. This PR implements the registry and helpers in all three SDKs, updates tests and docs, and bumps SDK patch versions. Changes here are intentionally additive and opt-in.
Add CredentialRegistry (fallthrough credential sources) and a lightweight PullStream.simplify() helper across Python/TS/Go SDKs. No behavioral breaking changes; opt-in ergonomics improvements and a minor SDK version bump.
Migration: no mandatory code changes for existing users. Teams can opt into CredentialRegistry by importing and composing sources. The docs include a small migration recipe for teams that previously scattered credential logic across app bootstrapping. Monitoring: added a telemetry event when the registry falls through more than one source in a single lifetime (helps detect misconfigurations).
Liam O'Connor: Nice separation of concerns on the registry. Can we make the fallthrough order explicit in the docstring? Also request an example showing KMS-backed source with env fallback.
Maya Chen: Added explicit ordering to docstrings and included a KMS+env example in docs/ and examples/; tests added to validate ordering under failure injection.
Priya Nair: TS typings look good but please ensure PullStream.simplify preserves cancel semantics. The test harness caught a leak in the earlier patch.
Maya Chen: Addressed cancellation propagation in TS and Go; added a test that asserts the consumer cancel path triggers underlying connection close.
Evan Brooks: Go adapter uses context correctly; consider adding a small benchmark to check no allocation regressions on hot paths.
Maya Chen: Added a micro-benchmark and verified allocations are stable; results briefly summarized in the PR description.

Context: Hosted canary rollouts GA requires enforceable guardrails on *actions* (create/start/progress/pause/resume/rollback) so customers can’t accidentally (or maliciously) exceed approved step sizes, skip minimum soak times, or bypass required approvals. This PR adds rollout-specific policy checks to the policy engine and wires them into the Console backend error contract (human-readable messages + stable error codes). Scope: (1) step size guardrails: max traffic jump per step (e.g., 1%→25% disallowed if max_step_increase_pct=10) with special-case handling for rollback; (2) soak time guardrails: minimum soak duration between step changes, with explicit override only when the actor has a higher-privilege permission; (3) approval gates: per-action approvals (e.g., requiring rollout_approver for start and/or step changes past N%) with consistent denial semantics; (4) error mapping: policy denials return structured errors that Console can render as inline validation + blocking modal errors; (5) auditability hooks: include policy decision context in the denial payload so orchestrator/Console can log why an action was denied (note: audit event emission itself is in a separate PR). Implementation notes: - Added new resource type `rollout_action` to policy engine with `action_type`, `route_id`, `rollout_id`, `from_canary_pct`, `to_canary_pct`, `time_since_last_step_seconds`, and `requires_approval` as inputs. - Guardrails are computed from effective policy (tenant defaults + route overrides) resolved via existing config layering. - Approval checks integrate with RBAC: `rollouts.approve` permission gates actions when approval_required=true, and also gates override paths (e.g., early step progression before min soak). - Deny reasons are normalized into `POLICY_DENIED` with subcodes: `ROLLOUT_MAX_STEP_EXCEEDED`, `ROLLOUT_MIN_SOAK_NOT_MET`, `ROLLOUT_APPROVAL_REQUIRED`, `ROLLOUT_OVERRIDE_NOT_PERMITTED`, `ROLLOUT_ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED_IN_STATE`. - Added test matrix covering: small jumps, large jumps, rollback to 0, step changes at/over boundary, soak timers, and approver vs non-approver actors. - Console backend integration: updated policy client to pass full rollout action context; maps denial subcodes to the existing Console contract (rendered as “You can’t increase traffic by more than 10% per step” etc.). Out of scope: quality gates, dynamic traffic optimization, and Dedicated/Private behavior (schema remains compatible, but enforcement here is Hosted action policy only). Risk/rollout: policy evaluation is behind `hosted_rollouts_policy_guardrails` flag; when disabled, engine falls back to existing coarse allow/deny behavior. Follow-ups: align defaults with SRE recommended beta thresholds (tracked in ENG-9158/ENG-9152) and wire denial payload into audit events (ENG-9171).
Ethan Park: Can you clarify precedence when both tenant default and route override specify max_step_increase_pct? Also, how are we handling action attempts while rollout is paused?
Jordan Lee (author): Precedence matches existing config layering: route override wins over tenant default; if unset on route, tenant default applies. For paused rollouts, `ROLLOUT_ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED_IN_STATE` denies progress, but allows rollback and resume (resume requires approval if configured). Added explicit state matrix tests in guardrails.test.ts.
Chloe Martin: Console needs stable subcodes. Please avoid embedding numbers in the code (e.g., MAX_STEP_10). Also make sure the denial message is actionable for end users and includes next allowed step.
Jordan Lee (author): Updated to fixed subcodes only (no numeric variants). Message template now includes computed next_allowed_canary_pct and min_soak_remaining_seconds so Console can show “Next allowed: 15%” and “Try again in ~8m” where relevant.
Marcus Lin: For overrides (skip soak / exceed step), are we checking a distinct permission vs rollouts.approve? I’d prefer least privilege: approval != override.
Jordan Lee (author): Agreed. Split permissions: approvals use `rollouts.approve`; overrides require `rollouts.override_guardrails`. Wired both through RBAC and added tests. Default bundles do not grant override to rollout-approver.
Benji Okafor: Concern about policy evaluation cost. We’re adding new inputs and more logic. Any perf impact measured?
Jordan Lee (author): Added a micro-benchmark in policy-engine (eval 10k actions). Δ ~2.1% p95 eval time due to extra branching, within budget. Also cached effective guardrail config per route_id for the request lifetime to avoid repeated YAML resolution.
Chloe Martin: One more: Console currently surfaces only one error. If multiple guardrails fail, which one do we show?
Jordan Lee (author): Deterministic ordering: state validity -> approval required -> max step -> min soak. Rationale: approvals/state are the primary blockers; step/soak are secondary. Documented in `guardrails.ts` header and added a test to lock ordering.
Ethan Park: Looks good. Please add a short note in defaults file about recommended values for beta vs GA (even if we keep GA defaults conservative).
Jordan Lee (author): Added comments in `config/policy/defaults/hosted_rollouts.yaml` referencing PM-1851 and that SRE tuning is tracked in ENG-9158.
Added policy engine guardrails for Hosted rollout actions: max step increase, minimum soak time, and approval gates.
Console backend now displays actionable validation messages when a rollout action is denied by policy.
Introduced distinct permission for guardrail overrides (separate from rollout approvals).

Motivation: Many tenants ship with conservative prefill and quantization defaults which are safe but expensive. This PR introduces 'Cost Caddy', a lightweight prefill-heuristics controller that applies tenant-aware default batching/caching presets and a safe quantization fallback policy to reduce unit token cost while preserving quality SLOs. Goals: 1) Provide deterministic, explainable defaults for prefill and micro-batching tuned to observed traffic affinity. 2) Add a safety-first quantization fallback so tenants automatically degrade to a compatible, higher-precision variant only when quality or latency regressions are detected. 3) Surface prefilling telemetry so ops teams can validate cost/latency tradeoffs. Summary of changes:
- New runtime controller "cost_caddy" that computes an allocation hint (micro-batch shape, prefill window, cache TTL) per tenant based on short-term traffic profile and tenant tier.
- A quant-fallback policy engine that attaches a graded fallback chain to model variants (e.g. q4->q5->fp16) with configurable thresholds for quality drift and token-latency.
- Telemetry tags and histograms for prefill hit-rate, prefilling cost delta, and fallback triggers; added debug traces for the decision path.
- CLI tool (redwood cli prefill-sim) to dry-run candidate defaults using replayed request traces.
- Defaults file under config/defaults/cost_caddy.yaml with conservative seed profiles and human-readable rationale. Rollout plan: Start as an opt-in feature under feature flag redwood.prefill.cost_caddy; run for 3 tenants in staging and 10 low-traffic tenants in canary for one week; collect prefilling telemetry and run the automated quality regressions. On successful validation, enable for all free-tier tenants to capture early cost gains before expanding to enterprise tenants with opt-out. Testing: unit tests for the decision logic, integration test that validates quant-fallback invocation on simulated degradation, load test showing median token-cost reduction of 11% on a representative small-batch workload, and cli replay verifications. Backwards compatibility: all defaults are applied only when a tenant has not set explicit overrides; quant-fallback is non-destructive and keeps the original model pinned unless thresholds are crossed. Related work: references ENG-2389 (prefill telemetry schema) and ENG-2401 (quant fallback design doc).
Ethan Park: overall this reads well; can we make decision thresholds per-tenant overrides and not global?
Maya Ortega: addressed in commit d2a671f, added tenant-level overrides and documented precedence in config comment
Laila Gupta: tests look good but add a regression test that simulates an LLM quality drop (BLEU-like signal) to ensure fallback fires
Maya Ortega: added integration test cc442e0 which synthesizes a quality drop and asserts fallback chain selection
Jonah Kim: minor nit - telemetry tag names should match schema ENG-2389; changed metrics proto accordingly
Maya Ortega: updated telemetry schema and re-ran unit tests

Context: During a partial regional recovery on 2026-02-14 we observed repeated circuit flips and large-scale tenant evictions when a previously degraded region began accepting traffic. These oscillations amplified transient latency spikes and violated short-term SLO budgets for multiple customers. Motivation: introduce a coordinated, conservative reopen flow to avoid mass preemption and provide an automated safe rollback path. Changes: 1) runtime/failover/regional_orchestrator: new lightweight orchestrator that manages reopen epochs and issues transient 'soft-reopen' tokens to nodes in a region; tokens constrain allowed parallel rejoin rate and expose an observed-health window. 2) controller/circuit: CircuitController now respects a telemetry_gate which requires k consistent healthy samples (configurable) before upgrading a soft reopen to full open. 3) eviction/service: eviction queue uses a sliding-window penalty-decay and an emergency dampener that defers aggressive preemptions during a reopen epoch. 4) feature flag: regional_throttle_v2 feature-flag guarding behavior; defaults off. 5) scripts/revert-regional-throttle.sh: one-command revert to previous rollout and flag state. Design notes: orchestrator is intentionally single-shard per-region and communicates via existing control-plane pubsub; tokens carry an epoch id and a suggested concurrency cap. The telemetry_gate aggregates latency and error-rate histograms from local probes rather than raw counters to reduce reactivity to noisy samples. Rollout plan: (a) merge behind feature-flag, (b) enable for 10% of clusters in us-west-2 for 6h, monitor eviction-rate, circuit flip rate, and token exhaustion metrics, (c) expand to 50% then 100% if stable. Revert: run scripts/revert-regional-throttle.sh and monitor for immediate restoration of prior behavior. Testing: unit tests for state transitions, integration harness that simulates region flap with controlled RTT and error spike, canary run in staging with 3 clusters. Observability: new metrics regional_orchestrator.epoch_duration, regional_orchestrator.token_grants, circuit.telemetry_gate_samples, eviction.dampener_deferrals added to dashboard and log keys prefixed with rto:. Backwards compat: when flag is off or orchestrator unreachable system falls back to existing per-node reopen logic. Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] e2e canary in staging, [x] docs + rollout notes, [x] revert script, [x] security scan. Rationale: this balances safety and liveness during region recoveries and reduces tenant-impacting evictions while keeping the control plane in charge of reopen pacing.
Hotfix: introduce regional throttle orchestrator, soft reopen gating, eviction dampener, telemetry-gated circuit reopen. Feature-flagged rollout and immediate revert script included.
Diego Ramirez: Design LGTM. Two questions: (1) can we avoid additional control plane load during large-scale reopens? (2) what's the failure mode if orchestrator loses quorum?
Maya Chen (reply): Orchestrator is single-shard per-region and uses existing pubsub; token grants are rate-limited and cached to minimize chatter. If orchestrator becomes unreachable we fallback to per-node local reopen with a conservative backoff (documented).
Priya Nair: Please add a metric that counts 'soft-reopen to full-open transitions' and expose it to SLO dashboard — I want to watch conversion rate during canary.
Maya Chen (reply): Added metric circuit.telemetry_gate_samples and a derived metric rto.soft_to_full_transitions; dashboard updated.
Lars Petersen: Found a race in the token expiry path, flagged a small fix in last commit — re-running tests now.

Motivation: Production apps require both high fidelity structured outputs and resilient streaming behavior when the model deviates from a schema. This PR introduces a schema-first output mode (typed contracts) with a graduated strictness model and a streaming recovery path that preserves partial results instead of hard aborts. Key ideas: 1) response_format supports 'typed_schema' with a 'strictness' param that ranges from lenient->strict; 2) streaming path adds a soft-fallback branch which emits a best-effort 'repair_hint' event and continues with a canonicalized payload; 3) when validation fails during a tool/function call, the runtime attempts a single automatic repair pass before invoking tool failure handlers; 4) OpenAI-compat layer maps these contract failures into structured error objects and 'function_call' adjustments per spec compatibility. Changes include API surface, runtime streaming changes, SDK mappings, console UX, and metrics.

What changed (high-level): implemented typed contract parsing and schema registry lookup; added heuristic_repair module that can fix common issues (missing keys, type coercion, truncated arrays); added stream_recovery path that queues last-good tokens and emits repair_hint + contract_violation events instead of closing stream; exposed response_format: {"type":"typed_schema","schema_id":"<id>","strictness":"lenient|balanced|strict"} in server API; SDK changes in openai_compat to translate old 'function_call' behaviors into tool_call + contract_failure semantics.

Checklist: - [x] API design doc in linear (ENG-4721) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] integration with console viewer - [x] metrics and alerts added - [x] docs draft in repo - [x] backwards compatibility gate guarded behind feature flag

Related: Linear ENG-4721, ENG-4803. Links: design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4721/typed-contracts; spec: docs/api/response_format_v2.md

Commits: feat(schema): add typed_contracts registry and parser; feat(validation): heuristic_repair and strict toggle; fix(stream): preserve-token-queue on validation-fail; feat(sdk): openai_compat mapping for contract errors; docs: response_format v2 and examples; test: contract streaming integration tests.

Files touched (high level): API contract layer, runtime stream handler, validation heuristics, SDK compatibility layer, console schema viewer, tests, docs.

Review conversation summary: Reviewer Lucas asked for clearer failure codes and to avoid failing user streams for recoverable problems; author implemented contract violation events and improved error code taxonomy (CONTRACT_VIOLATION_RECOVERED, CONTRACT_VIOLATION_HARD). Samira requested additional unit tests around function/tool calling when the model returns JSON-like but with wrong types; added test harness and a flaky-model simulator. Evan pointed out potential perf regression on high QPS due to extra validation; we added a fast-path that bypasses heuristic repair for strict=true and added batching for validation to amortize cost. QA ran integration tests and reported one intermittent failure on low-memory nodes; fixed by moving small buffer to disk-backed queue in edge case. Final approvals from Lucas and Evan before merge.

CI summary: 12/12 checks passed in final run. Flaky lint failure earlier addressed in commit 5. Integration suite reported one transient failure in earlier run; rerun was green.

Runtime behavior/compat notes: Feature is behind feature flag 'typed_contracts_v1'; default strictness is 'lenient' for existing customers. OpenAI compatibility: SDK's openai_compat layer will translate contract events into older 'function_call' error shapes for older clients. New telemetry: schema.validation.result, schema.validation.repair.count, schema.validation.latency_ms, stream.recovery.count.

Release notes: - New 'typed_schema' response_format with lenient|balanced|strict modes; - Streaming now preserves partial outputs and emits repair_hint events rather than abruptly closing for recoverable schema violations; - Automatic one-shot heuristic repair for common JSON issues before tool invocation; - OpenAI-compat mapping preserves backwards behavior while exposing richer error taxonomy; - Feature behind flag and not enabled by default.
Lucas Tran: Please avoid aborting streams for recoverable schema mismatches; prefer eventing so apps can surface partial results. -- addressed in stream_recovery.go and added repair_hint event.
Samira Patel: Add unit tests for tool/function calls failing due to type coercion; include a simulated model that returns string where array expected. -- added integration test and simulator harness.
Evan Brooks: Concerned about perf impact at high QPS; propose fast-path bypass when strict=true and batch validation. -- implemented validation batching and strict fast-path.
QA (Marina Chen): Found intermittent failure on low-memory CI node; moved small queue to disk-backed buffer to mitigate. -- fixed and added CI test.

lenient->strict modes
streaming repair_hint events
automatic heuristic repair before tool invocation
openai-compat mapping for contract errors
Feature flag typed_contracts_v1 gate must be enabled per-tenant via admin console
Watch metrics: schema.validation.repair.count and stream.recovery.count during rollout

Motivation: A production incident (see ENG-3421) showed repeated regional failover flip-flopping when control-plane heartbeats exhibited transient jitter. This resulted in elevated SLO violations and noisy rollbacks. This PR introduces a lightweight prioritizer that factors in a heartbeat stability score and a temporal quarantine window when a regional circuit is tripped so we avoid lockstep re-evictions that amplify instability. Changes: 1) runtime/slo/heartbeat_prioritizer.go: new prioritizer that computes a heartbeat_stability_score (0..100) based on median inter-arrival and variance, and incorporates it into allocation scoring. 2) routing/regional_quarantine.go: temporal quarantine controller that prevents re-eviction for a configurable cooldown period (default 45s) and tracks quarantine origins (manual vs automatic). 3) telemetry/metrics.go: new metrics: redwood.slo.quarantine_initiated_total, redwood.slo.quarantine_duration_seconds, redwood.slo.heartbeat_stability_gauge and a trace span for quarantine decisions. 4) config/feature_flags.yaml: runtime flag "enable_temporal_quarantine" (opt-in for canary clusters, on for Dedicated by default). 5) docs/runbooks/regional-failover.md: update with guidance and CLI commands to inspect and override quarantines. 6) tests: unit tests for prioritizer logic, integration test that simulates jittering heartbeats and asserts no repeated re-eviction within the quarantine window. Checklist: - [x] Design doc & ops runbook updated - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration test added (simulated jitter) - [x] Telemetry dashboards prototyped - [x] Feature flagged for gradual rollout Commits (high-level): - "add heartbeat stability prioritizer and tests" - "implement temporal quarantine controller and CLI hooks" - "add telemetry counters and trace spans" - "enable feature flag and docs" Files changed (high-level): - runtime/slo/heartbeat_prioritizer.go (new) - routing/regional_quarantine.go (new) - telemetry/metrics.go (modified) - config/feature_flags.yaml (modified) - docs/runbooks/regional-failover.md (modified) - tests/integration/jitter_quarantine_test.go (new) - cli/quarantine_inspect.go (small addition) Review convo summary: - Evan Cho: "Nice minimal surface area. Two asks: expose quarantine TTL per-region in admin API and add a unit test for TTL override." Author(Maya): "Added admin endpoint /admin/quarantine/{region}/ttl and unit test; pushed." - Priya Nair: "Concern: could we accidentally hide real capacity problems under quarantine? Suggest adding a quarantine_reason label and a health check that escalates if SLOs keep accumulating during quarantine." Author: "Added quarantine_reason label, wired metric redwood.slo.quarantine_reason_count and added note in runbook to escalate after three consecutive quarantines in 5m." - Luca Moretti: "CI flake observed on integration test under high CPU; recommend retry-and-backoff in test harness." Author: "Test harness updated to use exponential backoff; CI flake addressed." CI: - unit tests: pass - integration tests: pass (after harness fix) - linters: pass - e2e canary: queued during rollout Merge: Merged via squash on 2026-02-03 after approvals from Evan and Priya. Post-merge actions: - Rollout plan: enable on canary Dedicated clusters (internal tag) for 24h, monitor redwood.slo.quarantine_initiated_total and latency p95; if stable, flip flag for all Dedicated and then gradually for Hosted. - Dashboard: added quarantine panel under "SLO Enforcement" dashboard. Operational notes: - Default quarantine TTL is 45s; operator can change via admin API or cluster config. - Quarantine counters are exported to Prometheus with labels (region, reason, origin). - If a region is quarantined 3x within 5m, Alert SRE-119 page and create a P1 investigation. Why this is different from previous mitigations: Instead of only throttling or widening SLO windows, this approach uses a short, observable quarantine period coupled with a heartbeat stability score so we avoid both noisy re-eviction cascades and hiding persistent capacity issues. This is intentionally conservative: short TTLs, opt-in flag, and clear escalation paths.
Introduces a temporal quarantine and heartbeat-stability prioritizer to reduce region flap and noisy regional failovers. Adds telemetry for quarantine events and SLO impact tracing. Default quarantine enabled for Dedicated clusters; flaggable via runtime feature toggle.

payload.body:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally scale down too aggressively during short quiet windows, which leaves insufficient headroom for tenant microbursts and causes transient SLA violations. This PR introduces a configurable provisioning safety margin and a lightweight utilization-delta observer that feeds into autoscaler decisions and reporting. Goals: (1) prevent aggressive decommitment when short bursts are likely; (2) expose a sampled utilization-delta metric per-pool for post-hoc analysis and alerting; (3) keep runtime impact minimal and opt-in by config/feature-flag. What this change does: - Adds a ProvisionSafetyMargin that can be configured per-fleet and per-pool; default is 10% of committed capacity. The margin is applied as extra headroom during scale-down decisions and when computing warm-pool targets. - Adds a UtilizationDeltaObserver that samples utilization deltas across short windows (5s/30s/5m) and reports HDR-sketch-ready histograms. The observer runs with a bounded memory footprint and is off by default. - Wiring: autoscaler uses safety margin in its scale-down scoring and in the decommit cooldown calculation. The observer produces new metrics (util_delta_p50/p90/p99, util_regex_sample_rate) under the dedicated namespace. - Config and rollout: feature gated under dedicated.safety_margin.enabled and dedicated.util_observer.enabled. Cluster-wide defaults are in helm values; per-tenant overrides via FleetSpec. - Tests & validation: unit tests for margin arithmetic and observer sampling; integration test that simulates short burst followed by quiet window to validate no premature decommit; e2e gating on the Dedicated staging cluster. Migration notes: default behavior unchanged until cluster operator enables the feature; recommended gradual rollout on fleets with historical microburst patterns. Ops: expose new dashboard tiles (util-delta heatmap) and an alert recipe for sustained util_delta_p90 > 0.25 for 10m. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-4721) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] metrics + dashboards instrumented - [x] feature flags + helm values - [x] docs stub in /docs/dedicated/provisioning-safety.md Related: this PR is complementary to recent warm-pool smoothing work but is intentionally orthogonal: warm-pool sizing reduces cold-starts; safety margin prevents capacity undershoot during scale decisions.
Maya Singh: high-level LGTM — I left two questions inline: (1) can we make the observer aggregation window configurable for shorter experiments, and (2) the default 10% margin: do we have telemetry to justify that as a starting point?
Aisha Kumar: replied: made window values configurable via dedicated.util_observer.windows and added a note about choosing the default in the design doc (empirical, 95th percentile of historical short bursts across fleets).
Carlos Viteri: nit: prefer explicit constant names for the histogram tags so we don't get mismatched dashboards later. Also asked for a quick perf microbenchmark on observer CPU.
Aisha Kumar: replied: extracted histogram tag constants and added a microbench that shows <0.6% CPU on a 2k qps synthetic stream at sample_rate=0.01; results appended to the design doc.
Tomás O'Leary: requested change: make safety margin applied only to scale-down path (not scale-up). Concern: locking headroom reduces capacity for short sustained growth.
Aisha Kumar: applied change and updated tests: margin now only impacts decommit and cooldown calculations; scale-up path unaffected. Added a feature flag to enable full-path margin if operator chooses.
- Added configurable provisioning safety margin for Dedicated fleets to reduce risk of premature decommit during short quiet windows.
- Added Utilization-Delta observer (opt-in) to surface short-window utilization spikes for alerting and analysis.
- Feature is disabled by default; operators must enable via helm/values or FleetSpec override.
Default off. To enable: set dedicated.safety_margin.enabled=true and optionally tune dedicated.safety_margin.default_percent. For util observer: dedicated.util_observer.enabled=true and set sample_rate (e.g., 0.01). New metrics: dedicated.util_delta.p50/p90/p99 and dedicated.util_delta.sample_rate. Dashboard templates added under docs/dedicated/dashboard-templates.json
Plan: run a 2-week canary on a subset of fleets (canary tag = safety-margin-canary) and collect util_delta histograms + SLA incidents. Next PR will add automatic recommended margin sizing based on fleet historical delta profile (ENG-4800).

payload.body:
Context and motivation: We observed customer workloads where token quota bursts and rate limiting created poor tail latency and spurious retries across SDKs. Separately, deploys and autoscale events produced abrupt stream cancellations that surfaced as confusing errors in end-user apps. This PR implements a coordinated cross-SDK change: (1) rate-aware retry windows that scale backoff slopes and jitter based on observed success-rate and throttle signals, and (2) a graceful stream-drain/quiesce helper that allows long-lived streaming consumers to finish inflight messages before reconnecting. The goal is parity across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs with minimal ergonomics changes for integrators.

What changed (high level):
- Added "RateAwareRetryProfile" and default presets (conservative/throughput/aggressive). Profiles adjust maxRetryWindow, baseBackoff and jitter envelope based on recent 1m success/rate signals.
- Added streaming client method quiesce(drain_timeout_ms) + signal-based shutdown hook (client.quiesce or env REDWOOD_SDK_QUIESCE). Implemented polite shutdown handshake with server support: sends QUIT_HINT, waits for server ACK or timeout before closing the underlying transport.
- Aligned typed SDK error classes: SDKRateLimitedError, SDKStreamDrainedError, SDKTransientError with stable error.code strings ("rate_limited", "stream_drained", "transient").
- Telemetry: emit new metric sdk.retry.profile and sdk.stream.quiesce.duration to help teams tune policies.
- Bumped SDK versions and changelogs for py/ts/go.

Commits (summary):
- 0a1b2c3: add rate-aware retry library and presets (shared runtime lib)
- 1d2e3f4: implement quiesce API fo r python sdk; tests + docs
- 2f3g4h5: implement quiesce API for ts sdk; add sample in examples/streaming-quiesce
- 3h4i5j6: implement go sdk quiesce + graceful shutdown; update CI matrix
- 4j5k6l7: telemetry counters and profiling hooks; add e2e test simulator for throttles
- 5m6n7o8: bump versions and update changelogs across SDK packages

Files touched (select):
- sdk/common/retry/rate_aware_profile.go (core algorithm, small)
- sdk/python/redwood/sdk/retry.py (new RateAwareRetryProfile + mapping to client)
- sdk/python/redwood/sdk/stream.py (add Client.quiesce, tests/test_quiesce.py)
- sdk/typescript/src/retry/rateAware.ts (profile and presets)
- sdk/typescript/src/stream/quiesce.ts (client API + docs snippet)
- sdk/go/retry/profile.go (Go port + unit tests)
- examples/streaming/quiesce-demo/* (small example and README)
- docs/sdk/streaming.md (quiesce usage, best-practices)
- CHANGELOGs for py/ts/go updated

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We implemented rate-awareness as a lightweight sliding success-rate window; it is intentionally conservative (1m default) to avoid rapid oscillation. Teams can opt into more aggressive profiles via explicit RateAwareRetryProfile presets.
- The quiesce handshake is a best-effort signal: if server does not ACK within drain_timeout_ms, the client falls back to immediate close. This behavior was chosen to avoid blocking shutdown progress in noisy environments.
- To keep the PR approachable, the core rate-aware algorithm lives in a small shared runtime library (sdk/common/retry) and language bindings call into that when present. When the shared lib is not available (older installs), SDKs fall back to the previous fixed-profile behavior.

Review conversation (high level):
- Ava Chen: "This is a great direction — can we make the default conservative for GA? I'd rather avoid surprising customers on high-throughput workloads."
- Author (Ethan): "Agree; defaults are conservative (see presets). Added explicit test that validates no behavior change under 10 QPS unless 'throughput' preset is selected."
- Diego Morales: "Can we ensure the telemetry tags include 'profile_name' and 'active_rate_bucket' so infra teams can filter?"
- Author: "Added sdk.retry.profile tag and active_rate_bucket labels; unit tests updated to validate metric emission."
- Priya Kapoor: "One flaky e2e failed in CI on the first run (stream reconnect test). Looks like a race in the example harness."
- Author: "Yes — failure was due to the example harness not awaiting the server ACK properly. Fixed and added a short backoff in the harness. CI re-run green."
- Ava Chen: "Approved after minor doc tweak and test name clarification."

CI summary: initial CI run (linux/py38, linux/ts-node14, linux/go1.20) showed a single flaky test failure in examples/streaming (test_stream_reconnect) — root cause: harness race. We fixed the harness and re-ran. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, integration, lint).

Compatibility and rollout:
- Default behavior is backward compatible; existing apps see no change unless they upgrade SDK version.
- For Hosted customers we coordinated a server-side small flag flip to honor QUIT_HINT; rollout will be gradual in the next two weeks.
- We added a short migration note in docs and the changelog explaining the new error codes and quiesce behavior.

Backports and follow-ups (planned):
- Backport conservative preset to the 1.x maintenance branches for py/ts.
- Add an example showing how to combine quiesce with autoscaler lifecycle hooks (Kubernetes preStop).
- Explore server-side per-tenant rate signals to refine client rate buckets.

Decision/Outcome: Merged via squash on 2026-02-10 after final approvals. Version bumps included in the squash commit.

Related tickets: ENG-4219 (rate-aware retry), ENG-4220 (stream quiesce ergonomics), DOC-198 (quiesce doc updates).

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation for Python, TypeScript, Go
- [x] Unit tests and integration tests
- [x] Telemetry and metrics instrumentation
- [x] Changelogs and docs updated
- [x] CI green after re-run

Notes for reviewers of future changes: When tuning presets, prioritize stability over raw throughput; small changes to backoff slopes can have outsized effects at scale.
Introduce rate-aware retry profiles and graceful stream-drain behavior across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Default retry windows now adjust under high QPS; streaming clients get a quiesce/drain API to avoid mid-flight cancelation on redeploys. Minor ergonomics and typed error surface parity across SDKs. Version bumps: py 3.12.0, ts 2.8.0, go 1.6.1.

payload.body: Motivation: our observability pipeline has grown high-cardinality and leaks customer-identifying fields into downstream metric labels and logs, increasing storage costs and complicating alerting. This PR introduces two cooperating subsystems: 1) telemetry-scrub-runner: a small, pluggable service that applies configurable scrubbing/transformation rules to metric labels and structured logs before they reach long-term storage; 2) deferred-metric-compressor: an aggregator that identifies low-value, high-cardinality metrics and compresses them into compact sketches or time-bucket rollups with an attached fidelity tag so downstream dashboards/alerts can opt into reduced-resolution data. Key features: configurable scrubbing rules (regex + allowlist), annotation tags for provenance, on-the-fly privacy-safe hashing for identifiers, retention-aware compression policies, and a stability-simulator to run replayed traffic and estimate alert impact prior to rollout. Changeset summary: implements the runner service, adds compression adapters for Prometheus/StatsD ingestion, wires a new sidecar for the telemetry ingesters, updates observability dashboards and alerting recipes, and documents the config in the operator charts. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is no-op unless an org enables a rule-set in the Console; compression is opt-in per metric prefix. Rollout plan: staged canary (10% tenants) -> 25% -> 100% over two weeks with automated rollback on fidelity regression. Testing: unit tests for scrub rules and compressor logic, integration tests against a small replaybench with synthetic tenant traffic, and a canary-run in perf-lab. Related work: ENG-2345 (privacy observability), ENG-2398 (cost reduction sprint). Checklist: [x] telemetry-scrub-runner service and API; [x] compressor library with sketch and rollup adapters; [x] Console UI for rule toggles; [x] operator Helm changes and migration notes; [x] integration + load tests; [x] runbook for rollback and fidelity diagnostics. Impact: expected to reduce high-cardinality metric ingestion by ~35% for customers that enable default rules and cut cost for long tail tenants. Monitoring: added an internal fidelity-metric (telemetry.fidelity.score) and a compressor-drop-rate metric to track potential data loss from compression.
payload.title: Introduce telemetry-scrub-runner and deferred-metric-compressor for cardinality and privacy control

payload.body:
Motivation: In high-concurrency streaming and sampling workloads we observed excessive KV block churn when multiple small sequences triggered evictions that fragmented the paged block arena. This increases tail latency and the number of block reclaims per token, hurting both latency SLOs and per-token cost. This PR implements a reshuffle-aware allocation fast-path and an eviction coalescer that reduces fragmentation and amortizes writeback/eviction work. Summary of changes: 1) New coalescer layer in the block manager that groups adjacent eviction candidates into a single work unit (src/kv/block_coalescer.rs). 2) Fast-path allocator that attempts a reshuffle (in-place movement) before falling back to full eviction; this avoids unnecessary writeback for hot-vs-warm KB patterns. 3) Scheduler hints to prefer coalescer-friendly allocation windows (src/runtime/scheduler.rs) so that continuous-batching doesn't interleave many small evictions. 4) New metrics and tracing (kv.coalescer.evictions_coalesced, kv.alloc.fastpath_hit_rate, kv.coalescer.work_units) and dashboards updates (docs/perf/kv-cache-metrics.md). 5) A feature flag (kv.ec_coalescer_enabled) gated behind a canary rollout and off by default. Implementation notes: The coalescer uses the existing paged allocator's metadata to identify contiguous-to-logical blocks and collapses them into a single eviction task submitted to the background reclaimer. The fast-path performs a bounded reshuffle (copy within GPU/CPU page) when source and target blocks are colocated and no outstanding readers hold KV snapshots; otherwise it falls back to the safe eviction + writeback path. Care was taken to keep kernel selection stable: allocator fast-path nudges runtime to prefer copy kernels when reshuffle is in-use; no new kernels were added. Testing: unit tests for block_coalescer and fast-path (tests/kv/block_coalescer_unit.rs), integration test that exercises reshuffle under continuous-batching (tests/kv/reshuffle_integration.rs), and new benchmarks (bench/kv/bench_reshuffle.py) that simulate heavy parallel streaming. CI: initial CI run revealed a flaky test (reshuffle race in debug-mode), fixed by adding a lightweight snapshot fence and re-ran checks. Rollout plan: feature flag off by default, enable on canary hosts for 48h and monitor kv.alloc.fastpath_hit_rate, p99 allocation latency, and kv.coalescer.evictions_coalesced. If regressions observed, fallback to old allocator via flag. Related work: builds on prior paged-KV reuse efforts (ENG-7398) and scheduling hints from CONTINUOUS-BATCHING-II (ENG-7223). Checklist: - [x] Design and implementation - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Benchmarks and results - [x] Docs update - [x] Canary rollout plan
Marco DeLuca: Can you clarify the invariants that allow an in-place reshuffle? The comment in block_allocator.rs was helpful but I want explicit conditions for readers/writer snapshots.
Author (Evelyn): The allocator checks snapshot_epoch == current_epoch and reader_count == 0 for the source page before attempting in-place copy; added documentation and assertions in block_allocator.rs to make this explicit.
Priya Nair: Bench numbers look great, but please gate coalescer behind a flag and add a simple fallback path for older clusters.
Author (Evelyn): Added kv.ec_coalescer_enabled feature flag and command-line override; documented rollout plan in PR description.
Jonah Miller: There was a flaky reshuffle test on CI - after the fence fix the test passed locally and on rerun. Recommend adding a stress job in CI for 48h canary.
Author (Evelyn): Added stress bench in ci/workflows/kv.yml and addressed race by introducing snapshot fence and small backoff in allocator fast-path.
Introduces an eviction coalescer and a reshuffle-aware allocation fast-path to reduce KV block churn. Expected benefits: lower tail allocation latency, fewer writebacks, and reduced per-token cost in high-concurrency streaming workloads. Feature is behind a feature flag and rolled out via canary.

payload.body:
Context: Several customers running multi-region deployments observed spiky SLO breaches during short-lived regional network storms. The existing regional circuit breaker aggressively tripped and tenant-level SLO quotas caused cascading evictions when a region briefly underperformed. Motivation: Reduce user-visible errors while keeping global capacity protections intact. This PR introduces a two-part mechanism: 1) Slipstream SLO relaxation: transient, time-windowed softening of tenant SLO enforcement based on short-term regional health signals (slipstream windows). 2) Circuit Escort: an escorting path that keeps a minimal number of warm requests routed through a secondary region while the primary circuit transitions, preventing rapid cold-start thrashing and losing all in-flight KV cache benefit. Design summary: - Slipstream windows: when regional upstream health indicates >=2x baseline tail latency or increased error rate, tenants with recent successful requests get a short-lived SLO relaxation token (configurable TTL, default 15s) that increases their eviction threshold by a fractional budget (default +10%). Tokens are per-tenant-per-region and decay linearly. - Circuit Escort: when a regional circuit moves from healthy->degraded or degraded->open, select N escort slots per tenant (configurable; default 2) to route shadowed requests to an adjacent healthy region with warm KV hinting and priority lane so they do not contend with cold traffic. Escorted requests are rate-limited and excluded from standard eviction accounting; they are used to keep per-tenant KV slices warm during transient regional disruptions. Implementation notes: - Runtime: added slipstream token generator in region-monitor service. Tokens are signed ephemeral keys stored in Redis with TTL and a histogram eviction key for decay. - Router: enhanced route decision to consult slipstream token and escort table; added escort path that sets X-Escort: true and attaches KV-hint header. - Policy: new SLOPolicy flags and fallbacks; default conservative values kept; feature gated behind runtime flag "slipstream_enabled" for staged rollout. - Observability: new metrics: slipstream.tokens_issued, slipstream.token_hit_ratio, escort.active_slots, escort.kv_hint_success_rate; added dashboard panels and SLO regression alert. Testing & QA: - Unit tests cover token lifecycle, decode/validation in router, and escort flow selection. - Integration: local multi-region integration harness (benchmark-lab) simulated 30s region latency spikes and validated that the slipstream window reduced tenant-level evictions by ~78% in the experiment and overall error budget burn by ~62%. - Load test: perf-canary run with 2k concurrent tenants showed escort slots did not increase p95 server CPU. Rollout plan: 1) Canary enable on a small set of internal tenants for 48 hours. 2) Gradual ramp on non-production regions for 72 hours. 3) Controlled exposure to customers with a feature flag opt-in. Rollback: runtime flag and gate allow immediate disable; Redis token TTLs ensure full revert within TTL window (default 15s) after disable. Risk and mitigation: - Risk: misconfiguration could allow a noisy tenant to consume extra capacity; mitigated with per-tenant caps and cross-tenant usage metrics + alerting. - Risk: escort path could add tail latency if the secondary region is not actually healthy; mitigated by health checks and KV-hint success gating before escorting. Related work: follows ENG-1928 (regional failover playbook) and builds on router changes from ENG-1973. Notes: This is intentionally conservative — token amounts and escort slots are small by default to avoid changing global behavior until we validate telemetry in canary.
Ethan Chen: Can we make the default token TTL configurable per-tenant? Concerned about long-lived tokens during prolonged incidents.
Maya Patel (author): Answered: added per-tenant TTL cap and a hard global maximum of 2 minutes; noted in runtime defaults.
Introduces Slipstream SLO relaxation windows and Circuit Escort path to reduce tenant-level evictions during short regional degradations. Opt-in via runtime flag; safe defaults applied.
payload.title: Slipstream SLO relaxation and regional circuit escort

## Summary
This PR enforces RBAC checks on all route experiment *mutation* endpoints exposed by the Console backend (create/update/start/stop/delete, plus traffic split updates). Read-only endpoints (list/get/results) remain unchanged.

Motivation: route-level experiments change request routing behavior and can impact latency/cost/reliability. For enterprise accounts we need consistent authz semantics with Rollouts and audit logging requirements.

## What changed
- Added explicit permission gates to experiment mutation handlers using the existing Console authz middleware.
- Introduced a small permission mapping for experiment operations (fine-grained but aligned with existing admin roles).
- Added integration tests covering:
  - 403 on mutation attempts without required permissions
  - 200/201 with the correct permissions
  - error payload includes a stable `error_code` to drive UX copy in Console
- Added docs stubs for the permissions required by route experiments (to be expanded in ENG-9032).

## Permissions
We’re using existing role primitives and adding new action strings in the policy bundle:
- `route_experiments:write` — create + update config
- `route_experiments:start` — start/resume
- `route_experiments:stop` — stop (includes soft-stop and hard-stop paths)
- `route_experiments:delete` — delete experiment

Default role mapping (unchanged from existing policy bundle behavior):
- Project Admin: allowed all
- Project Operator: allowed start/stop, not delete
- Read Only: none

## Implementation notes
- Mutations go through `requirePermission(...)` at the handler boundary (before validation / state machine transitions).
- For stop semantics: we gate both `POST /experiments/:id/stop` and any mutation that changes the state to STOPPING/STOPPED.
- Error payload shape matches other Console APIs:
  - HTTP 403
  - `error_code=RBAC_FORBIDDEN`
  - `details` includes `required_permission` and `resource_scope`

Illustrative snippet (not exhaustive):
```ts
// console-backend/src/experiments/routes.ts
router.post("/v1/experiments/:id/stop", authn, requirePermission("route_experiments:stop"), async (req, res) => {
  return stopExperimentHandler(req, res)
})
```

## Security / compliance
- Confirmed the deny path does not leak experiment config; it returns only the required permission string.
- Works with existing audit logging: mutation attempts that fail RBAC do not emit experiment audit events (intentional; audit events are reserved for accepted state changes). Access logs still capture actor + endpoint.

## Testing
- Added integration tests in `console-backend/test/integration/experiments_rbac.spec.ts`.
- Local:
  - `pnpm test -F console-backend -- experiments_rbac`
  - `pnpm lint -F console-backend`

## Rollout
No config changes required; policy bundle update is included. Feature is behind the existing route experiments feature flag (PR-28673) for beta accounts.

## Follow-ups
- Expand docs to include examples of least-privilege roles and troubleshooting guidance (ENG-9032).
- Align UI affordances (disable/hide buttons) with these permission checks (Console UX work; tracked separately).
Marcus Lin: Please confirm deny responses don’t include any experiment metadata. Also ensure we’re using consistent permission strings with other Rollouts actions.
Kaitlyn Nguyen: Confirmed: 403 includes only `required_permission` + `resource_scope` (project_id). No experiment_id/config returned. I also aligned naming with existing `rollouts:*` conventions by using `route_experiments:*` (see latest push).
Chloe Martin: Can we gate the traffic-split PATCH endpoint too? It wasn’t listed in the summary but it’s a mutation.
Kaitlyn Nguyen: Good catch — added `requirePermission("route_experiments:write")` to PATCH /allocations and added a test that it 403s without write.
Kevin Osei: For policy bundle updates, do we have any concern about export/retention formats? (I know audit export is a separate PR, just checking scope.)
Kaitlyn Nguyen: No changes to audit export here; RBAC gating happens before audit emission. This PR only updates policy bundle action strings + checks.
Dylan Brooks: Are we returning an error code that UI can map to a friendly message? Support asked for something consistent.
Kaitlyn Nguyen: Yes, `error_code=RBAC_FORBIDDEN` and we include `required_permission` so Console can show a targeted prompt. Added to integration assertions.
Marcus Lin: Approved. Thanks for tightening the handler boundary checks and adding tests.
payload.title: RBAC: gate route experiment mutations in Console APIs

payload.body: Context: During a multi-region degradation last week we observed a rapid 'tailspin' where aggressive SLO-driven tenant eviction in Region-A amplified cross-region failover traffic into Region-B, triggering a cascade and KV-cache churn that impacted warm standby readiness. This change introduces a conservative emergency hedging path ("tailspin-hedge") that temporarily alters QoS decisions and warms failover targets with a lightweight probe before bulk re-routing. Goals: 1) prevent cascade amplification by soft-shelving noisy tenants instead of eviction; 2) preserve KV cache prefixes for in-flight failovers; 3) add a short warmup probe and throttled warm-reject window for candidate regions; 4) provide a single toggle for rapid rollback and a phased canary sequence. Summary of changes: 1) runtime/shedder: add TailspinHedge controller - holds tenant eviction for X seconds, marks tenants as 'soft-shelved' and routes reduced-weight hedged requests; 2) routing: introduce regional-warmup-prober that issues 5 lightweight KV-preserve probes to standby region before re-route; 3) kvsync: guard to snapshot hot prefixes to mirrored cache on candidate region (best-effort); 4) telemetry: add hedging metrics (hedge.entered/hedge.exited/hedge.probe_latency) and an 'amplification_detected' signal; 5) config: hotpatch feature flag redwood.experimental.tailspin_hedge with status, initial timeouts, and max-shelve-percentage; 6) migration script: add opt-in rollout that flips feature flag on Canary pool; 7) docs: operational runbook snippet and rollback steps. Testing: unit tests for controller decision logic, integration test that simulates region-A overload and asserts no >10% amplification to region-B, e2e canary in perf-canary infra with synthetic tenant spikes. Checklist: [x] unit tests added and passing [x] integration test updated [x] telemetry dashboards stubbed [x] canary plan included [x] runbook + rollback documented Links: Linear ENG-4281 (root cause), SUP-912 (support incident), runbook: https://linear.app/redwood/board/ENG-4281 || Commits: listed separately below. Merge notes: squash-merged to main; feature gated behind config and enabled only for Canary pool for 24h before wider rollout. Rollback: flip redwood.experimental.tailspin_hedge=false and trigger kvsync revert hook to stop mirroring.

Context: We need a safe, reproducible way to seed shadow traffic to new model variants while preserving a bounded surface for automated rollbacks. Current shadow workflows flood a target cluster and can cause noisy telemetry; promoting shadows to canary requires manual validation and replay. This PR implements a 'reservoired' shadow seeding pattern and a dry-run promote command that simulates promote semantics without mutating live routing.

Summary: Adds a reservoir controller that applies a per-cohort budget to shadow traffic, gradual reservoir refill rules, and session-reservation to keep user sessions sticky during a seed. Also implements a dry-run promote operation that performs the promotion decision logic and emits an audit playbook (replay steps, expected traffic fractions, and rollback checklist) but does not change routing. The feature is intended to: 1) reduce blast radius for initial shadow staging, 2) make promote decisions sound and reproducible, and 3) provide an operator-facing playbook for safe manual promotes.

What changed (high level): - New controller: controllers/reservoir_seed_controller.go — owns Reservoir CRD and orchestration logic. - New CLI subcommands: redwoodctl rollout dry-run-promote and redwoodctl rollout apply-reservoir. - Reservoir CRD: api/v1alpha1/reservoir.yaml and typed client scaffolding. - Telemetry: added reservoir.{budget,used,refill_rate} metrics and events for dry-run-audit. - Simulator harness: test/sim/reservoir_sim_test.go for deterministic validation. - Docs: docs/concepts/reservoir-seeding.md and runbooks/rollout-dry-run-playbook.md.

Rollout plan and safety: - Default reservoir budget is 0.5% of cohort traffic and throttle window is 10m. - Session-reservation pins session keys to the shadow variant for up to 5m to maintain fidelity in short interactions. - Dry-run promotes are gated by a metrics gate (latency P95 and failure-rate) and produce an audit artifact stored in the rollout history index (read-only in dry-run). - We added safety checks to refuse direct promote if the reservoir controller detects refill pressure > 85% for > 3 intervals.

Testing: - Unit tests cover controller reconciliation, CRD validation, and CLI flag parsing. - Integration tests run against local kind clusters: the canary-sim pipeline verifies traffic fractions and rollback triggers. - Load bench: we exercised seeding logic under a 10k qps synthetic trace; memory/KV cache behavior verified. - Observability: Grafana dashboard snippets and an alert rule template provided.

Backwards compatibility and migration: - Reservoirs are an opt-in CRD; no change to default routing. - Controllers tolerate older routing objects; feature flag rollout_reservoir seeds off by default. - Migration notes in docs explain how to convert ad-hoc shadow configs to reservoir CRs.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration simulation added - [x] Docs and runbooks added - [x] QA smoke run against staging - [x] Performance bench (10k qps microtrace)

Why this is different: Existing shadow patterns mirror all traffic or rely on ad-hoc throttles. Reservoir seeding treats shadowing as a first-class deterministic primitive with bookkeeping (budget, refill, session-reservation) and a reproducible dry-run promote that lets operators validate the promote decision before changing routing.

Related: Linear ENG-3940, ENG-4021. Jira SUP-721 describes a customer incident where a full shadow swamped a private deployment during a model onboarding window.
Maya Singh: Overall this is promising. A few questions on how refill interacts with autoscaling — can refill cause oscillation?
Avery Cole: Refill is capped and uses a leaky-bucket token model; I added notes in reservoir_manager.go and unit tests to show bounded behavior.
Diego Ramos: We should avoid session pinning for >5m by default; customers with long sessions could skew metrics.
Avery Cole: Agreed; changed default to 5m and made it configurable per reservoir CR. Updated docs.
Priya Nair: Observability looks good but add a synthetic smoke alert if reservoir.used grows > 75% for 3 intervals.
Avery Cole: Added alert template and test for alert firing in sim harness.
Maya Singh: CI flake on integration-canary-sim — rerun and passing now. Approved pending one doc nits fix.
Priya Nair: Docs nits addressed, approving.
Introduces Reservoir CRD and reservoired shadow seeding with a dry-run promote command. Opt-in feature behind feature flag rollout_reservoir=false by default. Adds metrics reservoir.{budget,used,refill_rate} and a runbook for dry-run promotes.
1) To try: enable feature flag rollout_reservoir in staging, create a Reservoir CR with budget 0.005 (0.5%). 2) Use 'redwoodctl rollout dry-run-promote <reservoir>' to generate an audit artifact and validation summary. 3) If validation passes, run 'redwoodctl rollout apply-reservoir' to perform live promote. See runbook path in docs for rollback steps.

Background: streaming token emission occasionally sees tail first-byte latency spikes under bursty traffic due to cold KV cache misses and abrupt credit bursts from the emitter. This PR introduces two coordinated runtime mechanisms: 1) an adaptive KV windup that proactively probes and warms likely KV cache entries for in-flight streams based on a short predictive window, and 2) a smooth-credit emitter that applies a low-latency smoothing filter to emission credits to prevent large instantaneous bursts that trigger kernel thrash. Motivation: reduce median and tail TTFB for streaming RPCs without increasing steady-state cost or impacting throughput. Design summary: - KV windup: small predictive sampler runs inline when a stream opens and during early tokens; it computes a probability distribution of upcoming key ranges from recent prefix profiles and issues lightweight prefetch hints to the KV cache layer. Prefetches are rate-limited and cancellable; no synchronous blocking on prefetch completion is performed. - Smooth-credit emitter: replaces the binary token-flush gating with a damped-credit integrator that holds a small rolling credit reserve and releases credits at a controlled rate tuned per-model and per-seq-length bucket. The integrator uses an adaptive time-constant based on measured inter-arrival gaps to balance latency and batching efficiency. - Coordination: when windup detects a predicted KV miss above threshold it transiently increases emitter smoothness to avoid exposing downstream kernel coldness to the client. Implementation notes: - Runtime: added runtime/emitter/credit_integrator.rs and runtime/kv/predictive_windup.rs with C-FFI hooks for Go-based server loop. - Scheduler: scheduler/latency_tuner.go provides per-route time-constant selection using recent windowed stats and Braess-style heuristics to avoid oscillation. - Kernels: small kernel-friendly prefetch hint path in serving/kernels/kv_iface.c that tags prefetches as low-priority. - Config: new route configs (console & API) to opt-in per-tenant: kv_windup:{enabled,aggressiveness}, emitter_smoothing:{enabled,base_tau_ms}. Backwards compatible defaults preserve existing behavior. Testing & results: - Unit tests added for credit integrator and windup sampler. - Perf lab: measured using perf-canary harness across 3 models (small/med/large) and two hardware types (A100, T4). Results: median TTFB -9% to -15% across profiles; p95 improved by 8-22ms; p99 improved up to 50ms on bursty mixes where KV churn existed. Cost impact: steady-state token throughput unchanged within noise; prefetch bandwidth increase <2% in worst-case; heatmaps show fewer 200-300ms TTFB tail events. Rollout plan: staged canary -> 10% fleet -> 50% -> global. Feature guarded behind per-route flag and disabled by default for older tenants. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (link: https://linear.app/redwood/ENG-4872-kv-windup-design) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration perf runs - [x] Console controls wired - [x] Docs note (docs/notes/latency-tuning.md) - [x] Feature flag gated - [x] Load-tested under Dedicated config Known limitations: - Extremely high-entropy prompts with zero prefix similarity will not benefit; windup overhead is bounded but non-zero. - Some very old kernels may ignore prefetch hints; we skip windup for those kernels. Related: builds on prior emitter and prefetch work but intentionally uses a smoothing integrator rather than aggressive flush heuristics to avoid oscillation (see ENG-3121).
Connor McBride: Can we ensure the integrator avoids long tails under sustained high-QPS? Please add a circuit-breaker.
Asha Patel: Added a scheduler circuit-breaker that decays integrator reserve after sustained drops, see scheduler/latency_tuner.go commit.
Marta Gonzalez: Verified per-route flags and default off for older tenants. Left one comment about telemetry (see below).
Marta Gonzalez: Please emit a 'windup.prefetch_count' gauge and tag by route.
Asha Patel: Added gauge and tests (metrics prefixed windup.*).
Evan Liu: CI failure on initial run was a flaky integrator test on macOS runner. Reproduced locally, fixed race and re-ran CI.
Connor McBride: Approving after nit fixed.
Merge Bot: Merged by squash on 2026-02-18 (merge method: squash)
Introduce adaptive KV windup (predictive prefetch hints) and smooth-credit emitter to reduce streaming first-byte latency, opt-in via per-route flags. Median TTFB reduced up to ~15% in benchmarked workloads; p99 tail improved in bursty KV churn scenarios. No breaking API changes.
