Motivation: production workloads have been showing repeated cascade evictions during bursty multi-tenant traffic and large sequence requests. Pure LRU-based evictors trigger long-tail spikes in CPU (due to compaction) and increased paging to disk for large models. This PR introduces a low-risk, incremental orchestration layer for KV cache relinquish behaviors plus a tenant-aware prioritizer that reduces fragmentation and avoids mass spillovers.

What this PR does: introduces the 'relinquish orchestrator' — a thin stateful controller that coordinates: soft relinquish windows, tenant priority scoring, and an adaptive rollback window to prevent cascade evictions. The orchestrator emits gentle signals to slab allocators and the background compactor instead of immediate hard evictions. It also surfaces light-weight kernel-hint metadata (allocation_stride_hint, hot_contiguous_hint) from the runtime that lets the allocator prefer contiguous regions for cached keys likely to be scanned in long generations.

Design highlights and safety: - Soft relinquish: tenants are asked to relinquish least-recently-used slots in micro-windows (5-50ms) with backoff, allowing KV consumers (e.g. streaming decoders) to complete without immediate eviction hits. - Tenant-aware scoring: eviction score = base_lru + tenant_priority_penalty + frag_penalty + recent_scan_bonus; tenant tiers and lease tokens bias scoring so latency-sensitive tenants avoid spillovers. - Adaptive rollback window: if an eviction wave causes a sustained increase in upstream latency or paging, the orchestrator aborts the current relinquish phase and reclaims a small fraction of previously freed slots to stabilize throughput. - Kernel hints: allocator accepts optional allocation_stride_hint, which influences selection of compact vs. scatter allocator paths; helps reduce fragmentation for bursty sequential access.

Compatibility & rollout: implemented as an opt-in config flag (kv.relinquish_orchestrator.enabled) and a canary route that targets 2% of traffic. No changes to public API. Config defaults to disabled for on-prem/private installs until customer opts in.

Benchmarks (canary): measured on a mixed-tenant test harness with synthetic tail-heavy sequences and three tenant tiers. Baseline: 99th percentile latency 420ms, spill rate 7.2% of requests under 30s test. With orchestrator enabled: 99th percentile latency 320ms (-24%), spill rate 3.1% (-57%), average token CPU per request -12%. Memory fragmentation score (internal metric) reduced by ~18% across runs.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc and safety review (ENG-2134) - [x] Unit tests for score calculation and rollback logic - [x] Integration tests in bench-lab for canary cohort - [x] Metrics (per-tenant spill_rate, relinquish_events, rollback_count) - [x] Feature flag and canary rollout plan - [x] Docs: runtime config and migration notes

Files touching major components: small changes to allocator interfaces to accept optional hints, new orchestrator control plane module, metric hooks, unit/integration tests, and config. See files_changed for details.

Why unique: instead of changing eviction math globally we provide an orchestrator that coordinates the cache ecosystem (allocators, compactor, scheduler) and gracefully orchestrates memory relinquish across tenants to reduce cascading failure modes. It is intentionally conservative and reversible (rollback).
Diego Alvarez: high level LGTM — can we prove rollback won't flip-flop during GC-heavy windows? Add safety thresholds.
Priya Narayanan: added hysteresis to rollback (min_stable_window=2s) and safety thresholds tied to paging rate; updated tests to simulate GC pulses.
Samir Patel: please add unit test that verifies allocation_stride_hint preference is honored for contiguous allocations.
Priya Narayanan: added allocator unit test and small benchmark that shows contiguous allocations reduce fragmentation on seq workloads.
Liu Chen: can we expose per-tenant metrics for relinquish latency? Ops wants that for SLO tracking.
Priya Narayanan: added relinquish_latency_histogram and per-tenant counters to telemetry dashboard. Verified in bench-lab.
Samir Patel: approved (2/2) after CI green
Diego Alvarez: approved and requested squash merge
Introduces an opt-in KV relinquish orchestrator and tenant-aware eviction prioritizer to reduce cascade evictions and memory fragmentation. Feature is disabled by default and available behind kv.relinquish_orchestrator.enabled. Provides metrics and a canary rollout guide.
payload.title: Gentle KV memory relinquish orchestrator and tenant-aware eviction prioritizer

Context: Our monolithic CI bootstrap logic made adding lightweight presubmit lanes and language-specific toolchains brittle; transitive devdeps caused noise in presubmit flakiness and made dep updates risky. This PR unbundles the ci bootstrap into smaller, composable toolchain adapters and introduces a small 'dep-clarifier' utility that emits a normalized dependency manifest used by presubmit guards and the dep-refresh pipeline. What changed: 1) move heavy bootstrap scripts out of ci/bootstrap.sh into ci/adapters/<language>-adapter.{sh,ts} and a slim ci/bootstrap.light that loads adapters on demand; 2) add tools/dep-clarifier written in Go to produce a deterministic dep-manifest.json and a small CLI to surface why a dep was included; 3) introduce a presubmit-step that checks the dep-manifest against lockfiles and flags unexpected transitive additions; 4) documentation under docs/dev/ci-tooling.md and quickstart snippets for adding new adapters. Motivation: reduce presubmit setup time for small changes, make dep-surface auditable, and avoid accidental release regressions when dep refresh PRs land. Checklist: - [x] introduce adapters and lightweight bootstrap - [x] implement dep-clarifier CLI and unit tests - [x] wire presubmit manifest check into staged lint lane - [x] update docs and onboarding snippet - [x] verify on ephemeral runners and CI flakes triaged. Risk/compatibility: adapters live alongside old scripts; bootstrap.light is opt-in via a new env CI_LIGHT_BOOTSTRAP=true so existing pipelines continue to work until rollout. Rollout plan: enable CI_LIGHT_BOOTSTRAP for dev and nightly lanes for 2 weeks, adjust presubmit gate to warn-only, then flip to fail if stable. Related: ENG-7123 (ci perf), ENG-1999 (dep hygiene), minor follow-up planned to add telemetry for adapter load times.
Jonah Park: Can we keep a migration toggle so current release lanes are unaffected? Recommended adding CI_LIGHT_BOOTSTRAP env to workflow - implemented.
Ravi Patel: Suggest clarifier also emit a compact 'blame' map for use by dep-refresh bot; responded that we'll add in follow-up to avoid bumping PR size.
Marta Kuznetsov: Unit tests look good but add an integration smoke test against a real lockfile; added a minimal smoke test harness in tools/dep-clarifier/tests/.
CI Bot: initial run failed on lint (shellcheck) for node-adapter.sh; lint fixes pushed in second commit and re-run passed.
Introduce modular CI adapters and a dep-clarifier utility to produce deterministic dep manifests for presubmit checks; opt-in light bootstrap reduces presubmit setup time and improves dep hygiene visibility.

payload.body:
Context
This PR wires up progressive rollout controls for Hot-route capacity protection (tier-aware admission control / priority routing) and performs the first canary enablement in us-east.

We already have the core enforcement plumbing landing in:
- Gateway tier-aware rate limiting + 429 semantics: pr-27411 / pr-27441
- Policy engine priority classes + route budgets: pr-27418
- Routing admission control using capacity signals: pr-27427
- Runtime metrics export: pr-27435

What this PR adds is the rollout substrate: feature flags, allowlists, and a repeatable enable/disable workflow with guardrails.

Goals
- Default safe: all protection behavior OFF unless explicitly enabled for a region + account allowlist.
- Canary first: enable for a small set of enterprise accounts and the protected route group in us-east.
- Reversible: provide one-command rollback that disables protection at gateway + routing consistently.
- Auditable: log flag evaluations and canary activations (low-cardinality) for on-call.

Rollout model (high level)
- Flags are evaluated in control-plane config service and cached in data plane.
- Two gates must pass before protection activates:
  1) region gate: hot_route_protection.enabled_regions contains current region (e.g., us-east)
  2) account gate: request tenant_id is in hot_route_protection.allowlisted_tenants (or allowlist group)
- Optional third gate for route group: hot_route_protection.allowlisted_route_groups (default: protected_enterprise_hot_routes)

Flags introduced
- hot_route_protection.enabled (global master kill switch; default false)
- hot_route_protection.enabled_regions (default empty)
- hot_route_protection.allowlisted_tenants (default empty)
- hot_route_protection.allowlisted_route_groups (default empty)
- hot_route_protection.debug_headers (default false; when true, adds X-Redwood-Admission-Debug: <reason> for allowlisted internal tenants only)

Canary enablement in us-east
- Config seeded with:
  - enabled=false globally
  - enabled_regions=["us-east"]
  - allowlisted_route_groups=["protected_enterprise_hot_routes"]
  - allowlisted_tenants=[REDACTED: 6 enterprise tenant IDs tracked in ENG-4928]
- Note: we intentionally do NOT flip hot_route_protection.enabled in this PR. The enable step is in the release runbook window (see rollout instructions below). This PR only ensures the us-east canary config is present and validated.

Rollback updates
- Updates scripts/ops/hot_route_protection_{enable,disable}.sh to:
  - atomically set hot_route_protection.enabled=false
  - clear enabled_regions and allowlists (belt + suspenders)
  - verify propagation by polling config version + checking sample gateway/routing flag eval logs
- Adds scripts/ops/hot_route_protection_status.sh to print current config and last-applied change (from audit log)

Observability
- Adds two low-cardinality metrics:
  - controlplane.feature_flag_eval_total{flag_name, result}
  - dataplane.hot_route_protection_active_total{region, route_group, tier}
- Adds structured log line when protection becomes active per process: "hot_route_protection_active": true/false with {region, route_group_count}

Testing
- Unit tests for flag evaluation gates (region/account/route-group)
- Integration test (mocked config service) to ensure default-off behavior and correct activation for allowlisted tenant

Rollout instructions (for release owner)
1) Merge this PR
2) During scheduled window, run scripts/ops/hot_route_protection_enable.sh --region us-east --tenants <allowlist_file>
3) Monitor dashboards (ENG-4926) and incident-bot notifications (ENG-4927)
4) If any unexpected behavior, run scripts/ops/hot_route_protection_disable.sh immediately (target <2 min)

Notes / follow-ups
- INT-3302: Access provisioning for the (future) admission decision debug endpoint remains separate; this PR only adds internal-only debug header toggle.
- We should keep allowlisted_tenants list in config, not in code, to avoid redeploys for canary adjustments.

Refs
- Linear: ENG-4928, ENG-4926, ENG-4927
- Postmortem driver: 2025-11-03 Sev1 hot route cascade

Canary enablement plumbing for hot-route capacity protection in us-east behind feature flags. Adds region/account allowlists, safe defaults (off), and updated rollback scripts for rapid disable during incidents.
Rafael Mendes (SRE lead): The rollback script needs to be safe under partial propagation. Can we verify the config version made it to both gateway + routing before declaring success?
Benji Okafor (author): Yep. Added polling to configctl.sh to fetch the audit-log version and then query /internal/config/version on one gateway pod and one routing pod per zone (best-effort). If either check fails after timeout, script exits non-zero with guidance to page on-call.
Ethan Park (Platform): Please ensure we don't accidentally enable protection globally due to us-east overrides. I want master switch to remain false by default.
Benji Okafor (author): Confirmed. hot_route_protection.enabled defaults false in schema; the us-east override file only sets enabled_regions/allowlists. Enable requires explicit script execution which flips enabled=true in config store.
Mina Haddad (Routing): For the dataplane.hot_route_protection_active_total metric, can we keep route_group bounded? Route group names should be from a fixed enum.
Benji Okafor (author): Agreed. I enforced validation on allowlisted_route_groups against the route_groups registry, and the metric labels only include the canonical name (no free-form).
Kaitlyn Nguyen (Authn/Authz): Any concerns about debug headers leaking? I'd prefer they only be present for internal tenants.
Benji Okafor (author): Implemented: debug_headers flag gates the header, and the header is only emitted if tenant is in internal_tenants allowlist (existing config) AND request has admin auth context. Also added a test to ensure external tenants never receive it.
Allison Grant (Observability standards): The controlplane.feature_flag_eval_total metric might be high-volume. Is it sampled and is flag_name cardinality bounded?
Benji Okafor (author): It's emitted at 1% sampling in control plane (config service) only, and flag_name is a fixed constant per evaluator call site. No tenant_id / route in tags. Updated to include result={hit,miss,error}.
Rafael Mendes (SRE lead): Requesting change: the disable script should also clear allowlisted_tenants to prevent accidental re-enable with stale canary list.
Benji Okafor (author): Done. disable now sets enabled=false and empties enabled_regions, allowlisted_tenants, allowlisted_route_groups. Added status script output to confirm empties.
Rafael Mendes (SRE lead): Approved.
Ethan Park (Platform): Approved.
Mina Haddad (Routing): Approved.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (Authn/Authz): Approved.
Allison Grant (Observability standards): Approved.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: In the recent regional instability incident we observed rapid open/close cycles for tenant connections which amplified evictions and caused an egress stampede when regions recovered. This PR introduces two coordinated mitigations: 1) a Connection Quarantine slow-backoff state that progressively increases connection admission for quarantined peers instead of immediate reopen, and 2) an Egress Habituation controller that ramps egress token allotments for a region over a configurable window after health recovery. The intent is to reduce SLO oscillation, prevent KV-cache churn, and avoid simultaneous high-egress bursts after failover.

What this change does (single-line summary): Adds logic and configuration for quarantined connection slow-backoff, a controller to warm egress capacity, updated telemetry, unit/integration tests, and a hotpatchable runtime flag to disable/adjust behavior for emergency rollbacks.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement slow-backoff quarantine state and admission policy
- [x] Add Egress Habituation controller with configurable ramp window
- [x] Emit metrics: quarantine_backoff_state, quarantine_reopen_attempts, egress_habituation_progress
- [x] Unit tests for quarantine transitions and habituation ramping
- [x] Integration test simulating region recovery blast
- [x] Runtime flag and operator docs for immediate reconfiguration
- [x] Monitoring alert tuning guidance in release notes

Commits (summary):
- 1a2b3c4: runtime: introduce QuarantineState enum and slow-backoff admission logic (runtime/connection/quarantine.go, runtime/connection/quarantine_test.go)
- 5d6e7f8: controlplane: add egress habituation controller and config (controlplane/egress/habituation_controller.go, controlplane/egress/config.go)
- 9a0b1c2: telemetry: add metrics and Grafana snippet; update alert thresholds (telemetry/metrics.yaml, docs/observability/egress-habituation.md)
- 3d4e5f6: helm/values: expose emergency runtime flag and default tuning (helm/redwood/values.yaml)
- 7f8g9h0: tests: add integration scenario and fix flakiness in quarantine test (tests/integration/recovery_blast_test.go)

Files changed (high-level):
- runtime/connection/quarantine.go (new logic)
- runtime/connection/quarantine_test.go (unit tests)
- controlplane/egress/habituation_controller.go (new controller)
- controlplane/egress/config.go (config knobs)
- telemetry/metrics.yaml (metrics definitions)
- docs/observability/egress-habituation.md (operational guidance)
- helm/redwood/values.yaml (runtime flag)
- tests/integration/recovery_blast_test.go (integration test)
- Makefile (integration target adjustments)

Design notes and decisions:
- Quarantine slow-backoff: when a connection is quarantined due to repeated failures or eviction, it enters a timed backoff with an internal multiplier instead of being placed back immediately. The backoff is exponential but capped with a jitter window; we expose max_backoff_ms and initial_backoff_ms knobs via config. This avoids rapid reconnect storms.
- Egress Habituation: after a region health indicator flips from degraded->healthy, the controller issues staged egress token grants that gradually increase from 10% -> 100% over 'habituation_window' (default 2 minutes). Token granting is tenant-aware and weighted by historical egress share to avoid small tenants getting disproportionate capacity early.
- Observability: key metrics and debug traces added to allow SRE to validate ramp profiles in real time. We also added a one-click dashboard snippet that overlays quarantine transitions with egress throughput.
- Rollout: hotpatch flagged and defaulted conservatively. We will roll to 25% of regions first (canary) via A/B routing in controlplane, observe the SLOs for 30m, then proceed to global if stable.

Testing performed:
- Unit tests for state machine transitions (quarantine_test) covering normal, rapid-fail, and jittered reopen scenarios.
- Integration test simulating a region that becomes healthy and triggers habituation (recovery_blast_test). The test asserts that peak egress at t=0 is <= 1.2x normal and reaches steady-state by habituation_window.
- Local load bench with 3 tenants to validate reduced KV cache invalidation frequency (bench/local_quarantine_bench.go, results attached in PR comment as CI artifact).

Review conversation (excerpts):
- Arun Patel (reviewer): "Can you add a small micro-benchmark to measure KV cache churn before/after? Also prefer making default habituation window shorter (90s) to minimize customer impact."
- Maya Chen (author): "Added bench and results; kept default 120s after talking with SRE because we saw better stability in the 2-minute window. Exposed config so ops can tune to 90s if desired."
- Lucia Gomez (reviewer): "Unit test flake observed in quarantine_test on CI — looks like timing assumptions. Suggest switching to wall-clock tolerant asserts or increase jitter bounds."
- Maya Chen: "Adjusted tests to use monotonic time abstraction; pushed fix in commit 7f8g9h0."
- Tomás Rivera (approver): "Telemetry looks reasonable; please ensure alerts won't fire during canary. Approving pending CI green."

CI summary and timeline:
- Initial CI run (linux/unit): fail on quarantine_test timing (flaky). Reran with test fix commit 7f8g9h0.
- Second CI run (linux/unit + integration): unit and integration passed; coverage unchanged within tolerance. E2E staging run passed with integration harness.
- Lint and security checks passed. A subsequent canary deployment job noted a transient -1% regression in 99th p50 for the canary region; after reducing initial token allotment the regression resolved — change included as a small config tweak in 5d6e7f8.

Rollout and rollback plan:
- Rollout path: canary to 1 region (25% traffic) -> monitor SLOs for 30m -> 3 regions (50%) -> global. Feature gated by helm.runtime.flags.enable_quarantine_backoff and enable_egress_habituation.
- Rollback: toggle helm flag false and trigger controlplane route rollback; quarantine state machine will honor an immediate 'drain' command that reverts quarantined connections to previous behavior. This reversion is designed to be safe within 30s.

Operational guidance added in docs/observability/egress-habituation.md: recommended dashboards, alert thresholds (temporary_surge > 1.5x baseline during first 30s), and steps for emergency disable.

Merge & post-merge actions:
- Merge method: squash and merge
- Post-merge: create canary deployment (ops ticket) and run bench against two traffic patterns: sudden recovery and slow recovery. SRE to validate quarantine_reopen_attempts metric and habituation_progress.
- Follow-up: add a Linear ticket to add tenant-level overrides and better historical weighting algorithm (ENG-2477).

Why this is different from prior approaches: previous hotfixes used hard-deny windows or immediate global dampening which protected SLOs but caused long tails for some tenants. The slow-backoff + habituation approach aims for smoother transitions, preserving fairness while preventing concentrated egress bursts.

If anything, this is intentionally conservative: defaults are mild and operator-configurable. We want telemetry-driven adjustments before increasing aggressiveness.
Hotpatch: reduce circuit flip churn by introducing a slow-backoff quarantine state for connections and a staged egress habituation controller to warm egress capacity after regional recovery. Adds telemetry and a runtime flag for emergency tuning.
payload.title: Introduce Connection Quarantine Slow-Backoff and Egress Habituation Hotpatch

payload.body:
Background: streaming stability incidents in November showed a pattern where certain invocations produced interleaved or duplicated chunks that triggered retries and inflight reassembly logic, inflating token cost and tail latency for a subset of models and routes. This PR introduces two observability primitives to make that behavior visible and actionable: 1) a chunk-stability metric family that quantifies per-route and per-model chunk jitter, duplication and reordering; 2) a model-hotspot Sankey dashboard that attributes token cost and latency to model routing/fallback paths and surface persistent hotspots across tenants. Motivation: current dashboards surface per-token cost and per-invocation latency distributions, but they do not make streaming chunk instability or cross-model fallback flows explicit. The lack of these signals delays mitigations (rate-limit adjustments, streaming retry fixups, and targeted model pinning). Changes: - Add metrics/chunk_stability.go: exporter that emits three new counters/gauges per invocation: chunk_jitter_ms_p90, chunk_dup_rate, chunk_reorder_rate. These are computed in the stream reassembler with a light-weight reservoir for p90 estimations. - Instrument streaming runtime (stream/reassembler) to increment and tag the new metrics with route, model_variant, tenant_id (hashed), and sequence_shape (single-chunk, multi-chunk-short, multi-chunk-long). - Add histogram labels for chunk_size_bytes to help spot fragmentation patterns. - Add dashboards/model_hotspot_sankey.json: Grafana panel set that renders a Sankey-style flow from ingress route -> model variant -> fallback model -> post-processing stage, weighted by aggregated token-cost and median rendering latency. Includes link-outs to sample traces filtered by the top 3 flows. - Add dashboards/streaming_chunk_troubleshooter.json: troubleshooting page with sparkline of chunk_dup_rate over time + top contributing routes and the first-seen example trace id column for quick drill-in. - Add tests/observability/test_chunk_stability_exporter.go: unit and integration tests validating metric labels and aggregation behavior under synthetic reorder/dup scenarios. - Add docs/obs/chunk-stability.md: usage doc describing the metric semantics, suggested alerts (see below), and remediation steps. - Add small change to telemetry/rollups to preserve chunk labels for 7 days (configurable). Implementation notes: - The chunk-stability metrics are intentionally aggregated at the exporter edge to avoid per-token cardinality explosion. We hash tenant IDs and trim route/model labels for high-cardinality routes. - p90 reservoir is bounded to 1024 samples per minute window; we experimented with reservoir sizes and chose this tradeoff based on a replay of the canary workload. - The Sankey dashboard uses a precomputed daily rollup index to drive the flows; real-time panels pull from the 5m window when available. Testing and CI: - Local unit tests added and passing. - Integration run on staging with a replay of synthetic streaming anomalies showed the chunk_dup_rate rising in the expected routes and the Sankey highlighting the retry->fallback->postproc path. - CI: all checks passed after a lint cleanup iteration (flake8/golangci-lint) and a small timeout adjustment to an existing telemetry integration test. Alerts (recommended): - Alert: streaming.chunk_dup_rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m on production routes (sev-2) - Alert: chunk_jitter_ms_p90 > 250ms for any paid tier route for 5m (investigate network vs runtime scheduling) - Auto-suppression: exclude synthetic/replay traffic via the new "replay_source" label. Rollout plan: - Feature flagged off by default. - Enable in staging and run synthetic anomaly replay for 48h. - Enable for 10% of production routes (internal flag) for one week; monitor top flows and adjust reservoir sizing if needed. - Full rollout after one-week validation. Backwards compatibility and perf: - The extra instrumentation in the reassembler is micro-optimized to use a lock-free ring buffer and a per-shard aggregator so expected latency impact is <0.2ms p50 on the hot path in our microbenchmarks. - Metrics cardinality controls are conservative; if teams need higher fidelity we provide a per-tenant opt-in. Related work: draws on ideas from ENG-3121 (streaming retry visibility) and ENG-2987 (per-route cost attribution). See linked Linear items.
Diego Ramos: Left a couple of nits around label cardinality — can we prefix hashed_tenant to make queries clearer?
Asha Menon: Updated hashing prefix and pushed a follow-up commit to normalize tenant label length.
Maya Chen: Could we add a short-circuit to skip reservoir sampling for single-chunk invocations? That would reduce noise for small requests.
Asha Menon: Added check to bypass reservoir for sequence_shape == single-chunk; re-ran staging replay, results unchanged besides reduced metric churn.
Oliver Grant (approval): Verified staging replay and CI; performance microbenchmarks look good. Approving for gradual rollout.
SRE oncall (comment): Please include an example Alertmanager rule snippet in docs so we can onboard paging quickly.
Asha Menon: Added Alertmanager examples in docs and a recommended mute rule for synthetic replays.
Added streaming chunk-stability metrics and two dashboards: model-hotspot Sankey and streaming chunk troubleshooter. Introduces alerts for chunk duplication and 90th percentile chunk jitter. Feature is behind a flag and rolled out gradually.
If chunk_dup_rate is high but traces show network layer problems, consider enabling the network-probe profiler in the reassembler. We may also add an optional per-tenant full-fidelity mode for debugging.

payload.body:
Context: We need a lightweight, deterministic way to validate candidate model variants against production traffic without committing user-visible traffic immediately. Existing shadowing proved noisy for cohorted traffic and lacked a compact mechanism for deterministic rollback when regressions were detected. This PR introduces a Cohorted Shadow Replay controller: it samples production cohorts, replays them to candidate variants under configurable fidelity, and attaches heuristic safety latches (latency/cost/error gates + time-windowed anomaly detectors) that can trigger an automated deterministic rollback AND create a snapshot for forensic replay.

What this PR does (summary): adds a new rollout controller (cohorted-shadow-replay-controller) that: 1) defines cohort selectors and sampling profiles; 2) streams sampled requests (optionally anonymized) to shadow targets with consistent session-affinity; 3) performs batched deterministic replays to avoid interference with live throughput; 4) evaluates compare metrics (latency P95, token-level divergence score, error-rate, cost-per-token) over sliding windows; 5) exposes policy hooks for automatic rollback, pause, or escalate to on-call; 6) writes compact snapshots for failed cohorts to S3-compatible storage for offline bisect and replay.

Key design notes: - Cohort selectors accept boolean predicates based on route, header flags, user segments, or synthetic tags. - Replay fidelity modes: dry-run (no response compare), sample-compare (compare summaries), and full-compare (token-level alignment). - Safety latches combine threshold gates with short-term anomaly detectors (EWMA + robust outlier trimming) and require quorum across multiple metrics before auto-rollback. - Rollback is implemented as a transactional operation: controller writes a rollback marker and issues an atomic traffic swap via existing promote/swap API; if swap fails, controller falls back to a soft-quarantine (shadow-only) and alerts. - Snapshots are compact (request metadata + hash + minimal context) and encrypted with KMS keys when Private deployment is enabled.

Files changed (high level): added controller implementation in rollout/controller/cohorted_shadow_replay.go, new protobuf messages in proto/rollout/v1/replay.proto, CRD/schema updates in deploy/k8s/rollout-crd.yaml, a new e2e test harness under test/rollout/cohort_replay_test.go, migration docs in docs/rollouts/cohorted_replay.md, and console wiring for a Replays tab in console/src/components/Rollouts/ReplayPanel.tsx. Small changes to the promote API to accept a signature token for transactional rollback.

Test plan: unit tests for core controller logic and gate evaluation (added ~40 unit tests), integration tests that run a synthetic cohort against a canary candidate in CI harness (simulated traffic, deterministic assertions on metrics), e2e in the benchmark-lab to validate mutexing with hot paths. Local smoke steps included in docs; CI added two new checks: rollout-unit and rollout-integration.

Backward compatibility & migration: existing rollout CRs are unchanged unless they opt into the new Replay profile. The new CRD field 'replayPolicy' is optional with sane defaults (sampling: 1%, fidelity: sample-compare, autoRollback: false). For Dedicated/Private customers with stricter privacy requirements, snapshot encryption and in-cluster-only replay are available via flags in the CR.

Operational notes & rollout plan: feature gated behind rollout.experimental=true. We'll enable gradually: (1) internal canaries for platform teams, (2) small external beta with two customers (opt-in), (3) wider availability after 3 weeks of telemetry. Metrics surfaced: replay_request_count, replay_error_count, replay_token_divergence, replay_auto_rollback_count.

Why this is different: unlike prior shadowing approaches which mirrored 100% of traffic and relied on ad-hoc analysis, this controller focuses on reproducible, cohort-localized replays with deterministic rollback and compact forensic artifacts, improving both operator confidence and cost efficiency.

Related: ENG-3421 (cohort sampling service), ENG-3987 (rollback transaction semantics), SUP-2123 (customer incident that motivated deterministic snapshots).
Connor Blake: This looks promising. Two questions: how do we guarantee session affinity across replay vs live for stateful models?
Maya Chen: We attach a deterministic session-hash to the replay stream and pin it to the same model shard key used in production routing. Added details in cohorted_shadow_replay.go comments.
Anika Shah: Need clear SLO impacts and backpressure behavior if replay queue grows. Add quotas and backpressure hooks.
Maya Chen: Implemented queue-size soft-limit and backpressure signal to throttle sampling rate; documented in docs/rollouts/cohorted_replay.md. CI integration tests simulate queue pressure.
Luis Ortega: Gate evaluation looks susceptible to false positives on transient cloud noise; consider requiring a 2-period confirmation.
Maya Chen: Safety latches now require metric quorum plus a stable-window confirmation (configurable, default 2 windows).
Connor Blake: Approving pending one small nit on proto naming (ReplaySnapshot -> SnapshotRecord).
Maya Chen: Renamed ReplaySnapshot to SnapshotRecord and updated consumers.
payload.title: Cohorted shadow replay with heuristic safety latches and deterministic rollback

Motivation: reserve-heavy tenants and uneven cluster packing are causing long periods of underutilized Dedicated capacity while other clusters experience microburst shortages. This PR introduces a conservative, safety-first mechanism to opportunistically redistribute soft headroom (unused burst credits and pre-warmed slot budgets) across compatible clusters and a cross-cluster warm-queue that proactively pre-warms warmlets on low-utilization racks. Goals: (1) reduce wasted reserved dollars, (2) improve tail throughput for tenants that experience transient surges, (3) maintain strict isolation and safety so no tenant's committed capacity is violated.

Summary of changes: (single continuous description) Implemented HeadroomRedistributor controller that periodically samples per-cluster headroom signals and offers redistributable credit parcels. Added CrossClusterWarmQueue that enqueues warm tasks with affinity and rack-safety rules; warmlets are scheduled with a capped evictable token so they yield under pressure. Updated autoscaler decision path to consult redistributor signals before making scale-down/scale-up choices. New telemetry: redistributable_headroom_bytes, redistributed_parcels_count, warmqueue_pending, warmlet_prewarms_succeeded, warmlet_evictions. Introduced a conservative 3-stage safety check: (a) commitment-guard ensures tenant-commitment watermark isn't affected, (b) locality-guard prevents cross-region redistribution, (c) reclaim-policy ensures distributed headroom is recalled within configured windows.

Testing and rollout plan: added unit tests around the redistributor state machine and warm-queue backpressure. Added an integration test harness that spins a 3-cluster simulator with synthetic burst traffic; this is gated behind a slow-integration CI job. Rollout strategy: feature-flagged off by default, enable for internal staging clusters for 2 weeks (traffic experiments), then enable for low-risk customers with canary ratio 5% -> 25% -> 100%. Metrics dashboards and alerts are included.

Notes: this PR purposefully decouples the redistributor from the primary autoscaler to keep operational boundaries clear; operators can disable redistribution without changing scaling rules. See linked Linear items for experiment tracking and acceptance criteria.

Checklist: - [x] design doc updated (ENG-3211) - [x] unit tests added - [x] integration test added (slow) - [x] telemetry wired to metrics pipeline - [x] feature flag gating the controllers

Related: ENG-3211, ENG-3287, incident SUP-78 referenced for burst hotspot investigation.
Daniel Kim (2026-02-09): This looks promising. Two concerns: race between recall window and autoscaler ramp-down, and how redistributor offers interact with preemption on spot nodes. Please add a unit test that simulates a recall during a scale-down decision.
Priya Shah (2026-02-10): Added a recall-unit test and a recall hook that is consulted by the autoscaler. Spot preemption is handled by the reclaim-policy which tags parcels as evictable; updated docs to clarify. PTAL.
Ruth Alvarez (2026-02-11): Please ensure telemetry cardinality is bounded; the current reporter emits one metric per tenant+cluster. Suggest aggregating to cluster-level and tagging by tenant percentile. Also add an alert for sustained recall cycles.
Priya Shah (2026-02-12): Aggregated metrics to cluster-level and added percentile tagging. Added alert rule: 'redistributor.recall_cycles > 3 over 5m -> page'.
Samir Nair (2026-02-13): Left one nit in the warmlet scheduler regarding exponential backoff defaults. Also requested a brief canary playbook for operations.
Priya Shah (2026-02-14): Addressed nit, added canary playbook to runbook. Tests passing locally; pushing CI fix for a flake in integration harness.
Introduce a feature-flagged soft headroom redistributor and cross-cluster warm-queue to improve utilization across Dedicated clusters. Operators can enable via deploy/featureflags/soft_headroom.yaml. New metrics: redistributable_headroom_bytes, redistributed_parcels_count, warmqueue_pending, warmlet_prewarms_succeeded. Safeguards include commitment-guard, locality-guard, and a reclaim-policy. Rollout: staged canary; disabled by default.

Introduces tiered capacity commitments (soft/firm) with a new burst-pacing adapter to smooth commitment drain during spikes. Adds telemetry for commitment percentile utilization and admin-facing docs/config samples. Backwards-compatible config migration provided.
Motivation: Customers with Reserved/Dedicated pools want finer-grained guarantees: long-running firm commitments for steady throughput, and short-duration soft allocations for bursty traffic. Current reservoir-style credits lead to sharp depletion during microbursts and cascaded throttling that breaks SLAs for steady tenants. This PR implements a tiered commitment model and a burst-pacing adapter that actively shapes burst consumption to preserve firm commitments.

What this changes (high level):
- New commit model: firm (guaranteed baseline) and soft (ephemeral burst allowance). Each tenant can hold multiple soft tranches with expiry windows.
- Burst-pacing adapter: in the serving path, a lightweight pacing controller limits instantaneous token burn by borrowing from soft tranches gradually and enforcing per-window smoothing parameters. This is configurable per-tenant and per-commitment-tier.
- Accounting: a reworked commitment ledger with percentile-based retention reporting (p50/p90/p99 for firm vs soft consumption) for use by SLO evaluators and billing.
- Config/migration: config schema extensions (config/commitments.yaml) include backward-compatible defaults; operators can opt-in to tiered mode.
- Observability: new metrics (commitment_consumption{tenant, tier}, pacing_backpressure_count, soft_tranche_expiry) and dashboards (docs/ops/tiered-commitments.md).

Design notes: pacing is implemented as a leaky-bucket overlay on top of the allocator; it does not change core scheduler semantics but applies short-term rate windows before token allocation reaches the runtime. The implementation prioritizes low overhead on hot paths (fast path is a two-atomic-update check) and degrades gracefully: if pacing is disabled or config omitted, behavior is identical to current commit ledger.

Backward compatibility & rollout: default is disabled for all tenants. Rollout plan: canary (10 tenants) -> staggered (per-customer opt-in) -> global enable. A migration script (tools/migrate_commitments.py) converts single-line commitments into firm baseline + a soft tranche with the previous quantity and a 24h expiry. Operators who rely on precise billing should coordinate enablement with billing team (linked_linear ENG-4921).

Testing: unit tests cover pacing logic and ledger transitions; integration tests simulate mixed steady+bursty traffic to validate non-regression of firm SLOs. Load bench shows 3-5% p99 latency impact in worst-case serving path but reduces firm-commitment breach rate by ~78% under synthetic microbursts (details in bench/README.md).

Related: supersedes parts of ENG-4300 (soft-reserve experiments) and complements ENG-4872 (commitment visibility).
Aisha Kumar: Overall this looks promising. Can you clarify how pacing interacts with the gateway backpressure? We should avoid double-throttling tenants.
Omar Singh: Pacing sits upstream of gateway backpressure. The adapter aims to smooth immediate token burn; if pacing still cannot satisfy the request it returns a soft throttle signal which gateway treats as advisory. Gateway enforcement happens only on hard throttle from allocator.
Diego Martinez: We need a migration safety net for tenants that depend on precise baseline matching. Suggest a feature-flag per-customer in the DB and a dry-run telemetry mode.
Omar Singh: Added a per-tenant enable flag and a dry-run telemetry mode in the follow-up commit (see commit 'chore: migration script and helm value examples').
Rachel Cho: The new metrics are great. Can we add a tag to tie percentiles back to reservation ids for billing queries?
Omar Singh: Added reservation_id label on commitment_consumption and retention percentiles in commit 'telemetry: add commitment percentile metrics'.
Merged after Aisha and Diego approvals. Metric names validated by telemetry team; ops docs added. Can be toggled via helm values-dedicated.yaml and per-tenant flag.
1) Apply helm values include: commitments.enabled=true and configure tiers. 2) Run tools/migrate_commitments.py --dry-run first. 3) Enable tenant flag via PATCH /api/v1/tenant/{id}/commitment_mode. 4) Monitor metrics: commitment_consumption and pacing_backpressure_count for first 24h.
Billing should not be switched to tiered model automatically. Soft tranches are not billed at full unit price by default; coordinate with billing (PM-214) before enabling billing changes.
payload.title: Tiered capacity commitments and burst-pacing adapter

Context: Customer workloads show an uneven arrival pattern causing expensive cold K/V cache misses and frequent cold-start token overhead for low-traffic tenants. This PR implements a budget-aware coldstart prefetch operator and ships a compact quantization profile library and a small CLI to generate tenant-level unit-econ presets. Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost for sparse tenants without regressing tail latency for high-throughput tenants. Scope: - Introduce a budgeted prefetch controller that enforces per-tenant coldstart budgets and selects a small set of seed KV prefixes to prefill based on recent arrival distribution. - Add tenant warmup profiles (sensible defaults) that are applied automatically when a tenant crosses an activity threshold; profiles are versioned and can be rolled back. - Ship a compact quant bundle format (.qbundle) containing pre-validated 4-bit and 8-bit calibration matrices for common decoder-only families; runtime picks the best compatible bundle using a checksum match. - Expose a small CLI (redwood econ-init) to synthesize unit-econ presets by sampling traces or using dry-run simulator outputs. Design decisions: - Prefetch strategy prioritizes prefix coverage over token depth for cold starts to maximize cache hits with limited budget. - Budget is expressed in microcredits per minute (configurable per tenant); controller will prefer cheaper prefill choices when budgets are tight. - Quant bundles are immutable artifacts stored in model registry; validating metadata includes expected input length distributions and kernel compatibility. - Default warmup profile is conservative (small prefetch set + slow ramp) to avoid sudden capacity spikes. Checklist: - [x] Budgeted prefetch controller implementation and internal API glue. - [x] Warmup profile definitions and proto-to-config mappers. - [x] Compact quant bundle schema, packer/unpacker, and registry upload flow. - [x] econ-init CLI with trace/dry-run input modes and dry-run report. - [x] Unit tests for prefetch decision logic and quant bundle verifier. - [x] Integration test: simulated tenant arriving pattern -> warmup applied -> cold miss rate reduction validated. - [x] Documentation: console UI knobs, CLI usage, and release notes. Backcompat & safety: Default behavior is opt-in for tenants under trial tier; enterprise tenants can enable via tenant policy. A runtime feature flag (prefetch.v2) gates rollout; the controller falls back to legacy prefill when disabled. Related: builds on work from ENG-2160 (hot-path prefill) and reuses parts of the sample-synth framework. Migration path: - Existing prefill configs are translated on upgrade using a migration script included in this PR. - Bundles uploaded to registry will not be used until tenant opts-in or admin toggles rollout. Monitoring: added new metrics: prefetch.budget_spent, prefetch.seed_coverage, quant.bundle_match_rate, econ-cli.dryrun_delta. Rolling plan: staged rollout to 10% of tenants for 48h, observe cold-miss and tail-latency signals, then expand.
Arjun Patel: Overall 👍. Two questions: 1) How does the controller avoid thundering-prefetch when a tenant crosses the threshold? 2) Have you measured the additional memory overhead for storing qbundles in registry?
Maya Chen (author): For 1) controller enforces soft ramping + randomized staggered prefill windows; details in controller docstring and integration test sim. For 2) qbundles are compact (avg 1.6MB per model) and stored in compressed blobs; added metrics and a hard cap per-tenant registry quota.
Lucia Gomez: Need a follow-up: add e2e test against Dedicated nodes with limited GPU memory — prefetch behavior interacts with shard placement. Can we add a smoke test?
Maya Chen: Added integration test and opened follow-up task ENG-2215 to broaden Dedicated-node e2e coverage.
Merged after two rounds of review. CI green after rerun of flaky e2e. Migration script included. Feature gated behind runtime flag for safe rollout.
Introduce budgeted coldstart prefetch controller, tenant warmup profiles, compact quant bundles (.qbundle) and econ-init CLI. Default opt-in behavior for non-enterprise tenants. Monitor prefetch.* and quant.* metrics. See docs for rollout instructions.
Enable feature via runtime flag prefetch.v2. Apply migration script during maintenance window. Watch metrics prefetch.budget_spent and prefetch.seed_coverage for first 48h of rollout. If budget burn is high, reduce tenant default budget via central policy.
Medium. Prefetch reduces cold misses but can increase short-term load if misconfigured. Mitigations: feature flag, budget caps, conservative defaults, staged rollout and telemetry alerting.

Adds a new tenant buffer pool rebalancer that reduces oscillation when tenants compete for reserved capacity; exposes utilization damping metrics and a fairness gate configurable via Dedicated feature flag.
Motivation: tenants with bursty traffic were observed to induce oscillatory reassignments of reserved buffer credits during contention windows which degraded P99 latency for mid-tier customers. This PR introduces a conservative, proportional rebalancer for tenant buffer pools combined with a utilization-signal mediation layer that smooths short-term noise and applies a fairness gate to protect latency-sensitive SLOs. The change is opt-in behind a feature flag and includes backward-compatible fallbacks to the existing allocation ledger. Implementation summary: 1) controller: tenant_buffer_rebalancer - samples per-tenant occupancy and in-flight rates, computes target deltas using a damped proportional allocator, and emits reassignments via the existing reservation API; 2) util-signal-mediator: lightweight EWMA smoothing with configurable half-life and an outlier clamp that prevents a single spike from triggering rebalances; 3) fairness gate: when a tenant's latency SLO metric cross-check fails, rebalancer reduces reclamation aggressiveness for that tenant; 4) telemetry: new prometheus metrics (rb_rebalance_attempts_total, rb_rebalance_succeeded_total, rb_util_ewma, rb_fairness_skips_total) and structured tracing spans to link rebalances to tenant traces; 5) migration: small idempotent background job to reconcile existing reservation ledgers to the new buffer accounting (no data loss). The description below enumerates commits, changed paths, CI results, and the review thread. This PR is targeted to Dedicated capacity and fleet management improvements and aims to decrease P99 tail latency regressions under multi-tenant contention while keeping burst capacity utilization high.
5 commits: initial controller scaffold; add EWMA util mediator and config; implement fairness gate & unit tests; prometheus metrics and tracing; migration job and integration tests; final polish and doc strings.
Controller and mediator implementation in reservation-controller, tests, metrics/tracing, feature flag, migration job, and operator docs + demo script.
Miguel Ortega: 'Please add a unit test for the outlier clamp behavior when a tenant spikes to 10x normal qps.'
Asha Patel: 'Added rebalancer_test with synthetic spike scenario and asserted no aggressive reclamation within configured clamp window.'
Lena Fischer: 'Can we make the EWMA half-life configurable per-pool? For now ok as a cluster flag, but we may want per-tenant tuning later.'
Asha Patel: 'Exposed half_life_seconds at pool-level in config; default preserved. Documented in operator docs.'
Ben Carter: 'CI lint failed on import grouping; small fix pushed.'
CI bot: 'lint failed -> new commit fixes import ordering and dead code.'
Miguel Ortega: 'Approving after metrics naming tweak (rb_util_ewma -> rb_util_ewma_seconds) which was applied.'
Presubmit: lint (initially failed, fixed), unit-tests (all pass), integration-e2e (flaky on first run due to harness timeout, retried and passed), security-scan (no findings), chart-lint (pass). Final CI state: pass.
Adds new Prometheus counters/gauges and tracing spans. Updated the console dashboard JSON to include a rebalancer panel and P99 guardrail alerts; operator docs include suggested alert thresholds.
Benchmarking on a 40-tenant synthetic workload showed a 22% reduction in median rebalancer-induced churn and a 12% improvement in 99th-percentile latency for medium-tier tenants under sustained contention; warmup costs are minor due to damped deltas.
Idempotent reconcile_buffer_ledgers job runs with a dry-run mode; operators should run dry-run during maintenance window and then switch to apply mode. Backwards compatibility preserved; there is a feature flag to disable the rebalancer if unexpected behavior occurs.
Squash and merge to main. Merge commit message: 'tenant buffer pool rebalancer + util-signal mediator (ENG-3174): introduce damped proportional reserve rebalancer, EWMA util smoothing, fairness gate, metrics, and migration job.'
Deployed to staging behind feature flag on 2025-01-23; scheduled progressive ramp to production with canary pool on 2025-01-28. Ops runbook entry created referencing SUP-4421.
This PR is intentionally conservative: rebalancer only reassigns from warm spare pools first and never reduces hard reservation guarantees below safety floor. Future follow-ups planned for fine-grained per-tenant half-life autotuning and cross-cluster spillover policies.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: The KV cache is showing higher-than-expected fragmentation under mixed tenant workloads and bursty loads that trigger large spill waves. Existing evictors reduce residency but often produce large contiguous spill bursts that overload the paging pipeline and cause tail-latency regressions for interactive tenants. This PR introduces two coordinated subsystems: a lightweight memory tessellator (re-segments large sparse extents into small, defragmentation-friendly tiles) and a late-writeback/soft-spillback smoother (staggers spill I/O and reorders writeback to minimize peak throughput). Together they reduce fragmentation score, smooth spillback traffic, and keep hot prefixes resident for continuous-batching workloads.

Design summary: 1) Tessellator: a background sampler that scans large KV segments and emits small 'tiles' (configurable: default 4KB-64KB) for preferential retention and compact-on-rewrite. The tessellator produces a fragmentation score per segment using a stochastic histogram; scores feed into the evictor priority queue so we bias against evicting tiles that reduce downstream KV lookups. Tessellator is non-blocking and restart-safe (state stored in per-tenant checkpoints).

2) Late-writeback & Spillback smoother: when eviction decides to spill, we attach spill candidates to a smoothing window controlled by an adaptive leaky-bucket. The window reshapes output into smaller, more frequent batches rather than large coalesced writes. A backpressure hook integrates with the scheduler so that when paging IO saturates, the smoother increases in-memory demotion and defers low-priority tiles.

3) Integration with continuous batching: the tessellator marks tiles as 'batch-friendly' when their access patterns indicate frequent prefix reuse. The request router and batcher use this hint to preferentially colocate requests to nodes with those tiles cached, increasing per-batch cache hit-rate.

What changed (high level files): - src/kv/cache/tessellator.cpp (new) - include/kv/tessellator.h (new) - src/kv/evictor/spill_smoother.cpp (new) - src/kv/evictor/evictor_integration.cpp (modifications to accept tile-priority hints) - tests/kv/tessellator_test.cpp (unit + microbench) - tests/kv/spill_smoother_integration_test.cpp - docs/ops/kv-memory-tuning.md (new section + examples) - examples/benchmarks/fragbench.yaml (added scenario)

Commits (summary): - Add tessellator core loop, sampling heuristics and checkpointing (Maya Chen) - Implement spillback smoother and leaky-bucket controller (Maya Chen) - Wire tile-priority into evictor and scheduler hooks (Ben Rodriguez) - Add unit and integration tests + basic perf bench (Priya Nair) - Docs and ops notes; tuning defaults (Liam O'Connor)

Checklist (manual & automated): - [x] Unit tests for tessellator sampling and checkpointing - [x] Integration test for spill smoothing under synthetic IO saturation - [x] Microbenchmark comparing fragmentation score before/after - [x] Docs describing tuning knobs and safety defaults - [x] Feature gated behind runtime flag (kv.tessellator_enabled = false by default for canary rollout)

Testing and validation: Local microbenchmarks on fragbench scenario show a 28% reduction in measured fragmentation score and a 15% reduction in 99th-percentile tail latency under bursty writes on a 4-tenant mixed workload. End-to-end CI included unit tests and an integration scenario that simulates sustained spillback. A flaky paging test failed on first CI run due to timing; rerun passed and full CI is green.

Review conversation (high level): - Priya: "Nice work. Can we avoid additional lock contention in the tessellator when checkpoints are emitted?"  Author reply: "Tessellator uses per-tenant RCU-style buffers; checkpointing is off the hot path and emits only delta positions to the checkpoint store. I added a unit test that asserts locking time < 200us on 8-thread stress." - Ben: "Integration looks clean but rebalancer may starve low-priority tenants if smoothing defers too aggressively."  Author reply: "Added adaptive priority decay and a tenant-sla knob; default keeps fairness unchanged. See tests/spill_smoother_integration_test for enforcement." - Liam: "Docs are essential here for on-call tuning — good that you added examples."  Author reply: "Expanded ops doc with recommended defaults and a rollback recipe."

CI: Initial run - paging_flaky_test timed out (flake) -> rerun -> all checks passed. Summaries: unit (pass), integration (pass), perf-bench (pass, CI-simulated), lint (pass), docs-build (pass).

Rollback and safety: Feature is behind kv.tessellator_enabled flag and the smoother behind kv.spill_smoother_enabled. Rolling back is safe by toggling flags and forcing an immediate soft-eviction of pending tiles. Migration notes included in docs/ops/kv-memory-tuning.md.

Risks: - New background scanner uses CPU cycles; defaults tuned conservatively (0.5% CPU budget per node). We measured negligible scheduler interference in staging. - Incorrect priority heuristics could keep cold tiles; mitigated by ephemeral sampling window and eviction fallback heuristics.

Release notes: "Memory: introduce a tessellator that reduces KV cache fragmentation and a spillback smoother that staggers writeback to reduce paging spikes. Feature is disabled by default and can be enabled per-cluster via kv.tessellator_enabled and kv.spill_smoother_enabled. See docs/ops/kv-memory-tuning.md for guidance."

Related work and links: Linear: ENG-4821 (fragmentation investigation), ENG-4890 (paging spike mitigation). Internal perf graphs and fragbench scenarios are attached in the PR (perf/fragbench-2025-10-30/).
Canary to Dedicated clusters for Nov 2025; ops runbook added.

Motivation: multiple production workloads show a tail of small-sequence requests that trigger a suboptimal code path: separate rotary application and KV cache maintenance cause additional memory copies and synchronization between the continuous-batcher and the attention microkernel. This PR introduces an inline "attn-orchestrator" that performs in-place rotary/rope application fused with the attention kernel entry points and emits lightweight KV-maintenance hints for the continuous-batcher. Goals: 1) eliminate an allocation+memcpy for rotary application on the common fp16 path; 2) let the batcher preemptively place/reuse KV storage slots via hints instead of reactive eviction; 3) provide a safe quantized fallback path for int8/4 FlashAttention variants when the fused path is not supported on a device.

What changed (high level): implemented an in-place rotary applier that integrates directly into the FlashAttention entry sequence, added a small ABI for KV-hint emission (kv_hint_t) used by the continuous-batcher, extended the kernel-selection logic to prefer the fused path for sequences <= 512 and batch sizes >= 4, and added an int8-compatible kernel shim that delegates to quantized flash when AVX/SM-specific intrinsics are present. Also updated tests, bench harness, and runtime metrics to capture hint utilization and fused-path hit-rate.
Diego Alvarez: Overall this looks promising. Can you justify the heuristics for seq_len <= 512? Bench numbers would be helpful across 128/256/512/1024 to ensure no regressions.
Asha Menon: Added bench results in bench/micro/attn_fused_bench.py and included a table in docs/perf/fused-attn-orchestrator.md showing 15-28% p99 latency reduction and ~12% token cost improvement in the 128-512 range. For 1024 there is a small regression on some card types due to register pressure; we fall back to standard flash in that case.
Priya Shah: The kv_hint ABI seems lightweight, but I'm concerned about thread-safety when the batcher reuses slots. Can we document lock ordering and provide an assert in debug builds?
Asha Menon: Added assert and a brief doc section. The hint is advisory — batcher validates slot ownership with an epoch check before reuse. Documented in scheduler/continuous_batcher/kv_hints.h comments.
Liam O'Connor: Are there memory-safety implications for in-place rotary on pinned buffers used by async GPU copies?
Asha Menon: We added a pinned-buffer guard: if buffer->is_pinned() we fall back to the copy-path. This is guarded in orchestrator.cpp and tested in tests/attn/test_inplace_rotary.py.
Diego Alvarez: CI flake on windows build; looks like a path issue in quant_shim - reran and passed.
CI Bot: All checks passed on rerun.
Unit tests added for inplace_rotary edge cases (pinned buffer fallback, seq boundary). Microbench harness run against production traces; integration tests exercised quantized fallback on an Ampere A10 and an older T4 (validated no correctness regression).
Performance: Introduce inline-attn-orchestrator that fuses in-place rotary application with the attention kernel and provides KV hints to the continuous-batcher. Typical improvements: 12% token-cost reduction and 15-28% p99 latency reductions for 128-512 sequence workloads in fp16 on supported hardware. Fallbacks ensure correctness for larger sequences and pinned buffers.
Operators: To enable fused path on Dedicated clusters, ensure runtime flag --enable-inline-attn is set (off by default until v1.18 rollout). Quantized shim requires the quantized runtime package (quant-runtime) to be present on nodes. Telemetry emits attn.fused_path_hit_rate and attn.kv_hint_utilization; recommend adding alarms for fused_path_hit_rate drop > 30% during rollout.
ENG-2154: tune heuristics for small batch sizes (1-3) where overhead differs
ENG-2161: add hardware capability probe to advertise fused path support in node registry
ENG-2202: expose kv_hint metrics at route-level in Console
payload.title: inline-attn-orchestrator: in-place rotary fusion + KV-hinting for continuous-batcher

payload.body: Context: We observed a partial outage last quarter when a regional KMS provider experienced intermittent availability, which caused tenant requests pinned to that provider to fail rather than failover. Motivation: provide a deterministic, auditable fallback for KMS selection while preserving tenant data-residency constraints and minimizing blast radius. This PR implements a residency-aware KMS selector with per-tenant provider allowlists and a prioritized fallback plan, an RBAC v2 probing endpoint for simulating policy decisions before rollout, and audit integrity chaining to prove key-selection decisions. High-level changes: 1) residency/kms: add residency-aware KMS allocator that consults tenant residency profile, provider health, and policy allowlists; supports multi-step fallback (primary -> regional partners -> staged emergency escrow) with TTL-bound ephemeral wrapping keys. 2) rbac/v2: add /internal/rbac/simulate endpoint that accepts an assertion payload and returns the PDP decision trace to preview how a change to role bindings would evaluate. 3) audit: append per-request KMS-signature pointers and an integrity HMAC of the KMS decision envelope to audit logs so audits can prove which KMS was selected and why. 4) migration/ops: add migration to extend tenant metadata schema with kms_allowlist and residency_tier; CLI tooling to backfill from policy engine and to run dry-run simulation. Security considerations: fallback respects tenant allowlists and tenant-level emergency consent flag; emergency escrow path requires explicit operator approval and is recorded in the immutable audit envelope. Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains unchanged unless tenant metadata is populated or feature-flag enabled. Rollout: feature-flag gated, staged canary to 5% of traffic, followed by region-by-region expansion with a 48h observation window per region. Linear/Jira: ENG-9123 implement selector, SEC-441 add audit-proofing. Checklist: - [x] selector prototype and unit tests - [x] RBAC simulate endpoint and integration tests - [x] audit envelope schema changes and log wiring - [x] migration and backfill CLI - [x] docs and runbook updates - [x] canary plan and rollout playbook - [x] add metrics (kms.selection.count, kms.fallback.count, rbac.simulate.latency) Related: policy linter changes in /tools/policy-lint to catch allowlist omissions. Risks & mitigations: KMS provider churn may increase latency during fallback; mitigated via optimistic async wrapping and cached ephemeral keys. Emergency escrow path limited by operator gating and additional HSM signing.
payload.title: residency-aware-kms-fallback-and-rbac-probing-tooling

payload.body:
Motivation: During gradual rollout canaries we sometimes see transient tail-latency spikes caused by bursty background traffic or long-tailed user flows. These spikes increase noise for detectors and can cause unnecessary rollbacks or user-visible SLA violations. This PR adds an adaptive, SLA-aware traffic corking guard that temporarily reduces (corks) low-priority traffic fraction when the canary signals tail-latency pressure, preserving capacity for high-priority requests and stabilizing canary signals.

Design summary: corking is an automated, short-lived traffic shaping action performed by the perf-canary controller. The guard monitors per-route 95/99/99.9 latency, in-flight concurrency, and SLA budget (error budget / latency SLO burn rate). When the guard detects sustained tail-latency elevation above configured thresholds AND the estimated SLA burn suggests user-facing impact, it computes a cork fraction in [0.0, 0.9] to reduce non-critical traffic classes. Corking is adaptive: fraction depends on severity and remaining SLA budget; duration is bounded and decays automatically. The controller uses exponential backoff for repeated corks to avoid oscillation.

Key configuration knobs (defaults included): policy.sla_window_seconds=60, policy.tail_latency_ms_thresholds={p95:150,p99:400,p999:1200}, policy.min_cork_fraction=0.1, policy.max_cork_fraction=0.6, policy.cooldown_seconds=120, policy.priority_classes=["user","interactive","batch","background"], policy.cork_targets=["background","batch"]. These are mounted as CRD fields for Redwood Private and as remote flags in hosted.

Implementation notes: - New controller: perf-canary/controllers/traffic_corker.py implements the temporal decision logic and exposes a TrialCork CRD used internally by the controller manager. The cork action translates to a traffic-shaping directive in the router (via existing traffic-mutation API) that temporarily drops or deprioritizes a percentage of requests in the targeted priority classes. - Integration with canary pipeline: the corker subscribes to canary health streams (latency histograms and throughput) and emits events consumed by the rollout manager so the rollout can pause or continue based on combined signal. - Observability: added metrics corker.actions_total, corker.current_fraction, corker.cooldowns, and a dedicated dashboard and alert rule to detect repeated cork storms. - Safety: default policy only corks non-user-facing classes and requires a linear ticket (ENG-) opt-in to extend to higher priority classes.

Testing and benchmarks: added unit tests for decision heuristics and a small integration harness that simulates mixed traffic (80% background/batch, 20% user) with injected tail events. Benchmarks against a baseline canary run show a 5-9% reduction in p99-p999 tail spikes under identical synthetic bursts and reduced false-positive rate for the canary detector in our replay tests.

Rollout plan: gated by feature flag perf.corker.enabled. Start with internal SRE on dedicated clusters: 0% -> 10% of routes (1 week) -> 50% (observability window) -> 100%. We also added a kill-switch in the control plane to immediately disable corking globally.

Security & compliance: corker does not touch request payloads or logs, only traffic metadata and routing weights. All actions are audited and appear in existing audit logs.

What this PR contains: - controller, tests, CRD stubs, router adapter, docs, dashboard changes, quickstart policy example.

Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration replay, [x] dashboard + alerts, [x] docs, [x] release notes, [x] feature-flag gating.
Diego Ramos (reviewer): Can the corker accidentally mask a real regression in the canary by hiding bad behavior? Please add rationale and a telemetry signal to detect masking.
Maya Patel (author): Added a masking-detection metric (corker.masking_risk) and a conservative rule that increases cork only if masking_risk is below 0.2. Documented in docs/operator/corker.md.
Leah Kim (reviewer): The cooldown/backoff logic looks reasonable but needs an explicit unit test for repeated corks across windows.
Maya Patel (author): Added test 'test_corker_repeated_cork_backoff' in perf-canary/tests/test_corker.py and extended integration replay.
Evan Cho (approver): Verified dashboards and alerts. Approved pending CI green and small nits in docs formatting.
CI Bot: integration-replay failed on first run due to synthetic harness timeout; rerun succeeded after extending duration.
New feature: adaptive SLA-aware traffic corking guard. Helps stabilize canary signals by temporarily reducing non-critical traffic when tail-latency threatens SLAs. Gated by feature flag perf.corker.enabled; operator opt-in required for private clusters.
Operators should watch corker.actions_total and corker.masking_risk during rollout. Use control-plane kill-switch if unexpected user impact observed. Default policy only targets background/batch classes.
ENG-4921 follow-up: add multi-route correlation to avoid simultaneous corks across dependent routes; SRE-230: tune thresholds based on customer traffic shapes.
payload.title: Add adaptive SLA-aware traffic corking guard for performance canaries

Motivation: Improve resilience of multi-stage rollouts by adding a lightweight deferred-cutover safety net and an independent telemetry witness that can veto or pause cutovers when drift or metric anomalies are detected. This change is targeted at complex fanout rollouts (A/B + shadow lanes) where downstream stabilization is latent and automated rollback or holdpoints are required. Design summary: 1) Introduce a Telemetry Witness component that subscribes to rollout events and emits a signed verdict (allow|pause|veto) based on sliding-window metric heuristics and anomaly detectors. 2) Add a Deferred Cutover controller that delays final traffic shift until the witness returns a positive verdict or a timeout elapses; supports operator-configured holdpoints and manual override. 3) Persist a immutable Decision Journal for each rollout with timestamps, witness verdicts, triggering metrics, and the operator who performed any manual override. 4) Provide a packaged rollback playbook and a minimal API for external audit/forensics. Backwards compatibility: witness is opt-in per-rollout via rollout.spec.safety.witness.enabled=false by default; controller falls back to existing immediate-cutover behavior when disabled. Tests: unit tests for verdict logic and timeout behavior, integration e2e test which simulates a drift by introducing synthetic latency and ensuring rollout pauses, and a smoke upgrade test for private deployments. Checklist: - [x] Add witness component and gRPC contract - [x] Implement deferred cutover controller + decision journal - [x] Expose manual override endpoints with RBAC checks - [x] Add e2e integration test and add to CI matrix - [x] Add runbook and rollback playbook docs - [x] Perf sanity: witness runs in separate lightweight goroutine and limits to 50ms latency budget per verdict Related linear tasks: ENG-2145 (telemetry witness PoC), ENG-2210 (deferred cutover design). Rollout lifecycle impact: decision journal enables post-mortem playback for canary/A-B experiments; automated veto reduces blast radius for accidental regressions. Migration notes: existing rollout CRs keep current semantics; to opt-in set spec.safety.witness.enabled: true and configure spec.safety.witness.policyRef. Security: verdicts are signed with controller identity; manual override requires escalation role. CI notes: initial run failed a flaky integration test, fixed by rate-limiting synthetic load in the test harness. Merge: squash and merge after final approval. Release notes: "Add opt-in Telemetry Witness and Deferred Cutover safety-net for rollouts; adds decision journal and a packaged rollback playbook."
Marcus Li (reviewer): Nice design, can you clarify failure modes when the witness is partitioned?
Asha Patel (author): If witness cannot reach metrics backend within verdict timeout we treat as 'pause' to minimize blast radius; added decision journal entry marking 'witness_unreachable' and an operator alert. See deferred_cutover_controller.go:handleWitnessTimeout
Sofia Martinez (reviewer): Please ensure manual override requires escalate role and is audited.
Asha Patel (author): Manual override now requires role 'rollout.operator.escalate' and writes an audited event to the decision journal. Added integration test for override flow.
Jun Park (approver): Integration e2e passes in CI and manual playbook looks good. Approving.
CI system: initial integration run failed on synthetic load flake; rerun after test harness rate-limit patch => all checks passing.

Title: Decompose test profiles and add dependency triage bot

Description: This PR refactors CI test sharding into small, profile-aware shards and introduces an automated dependency triage bot that opens recommended bump PRs and labels candidate repos for manual review. Motivation: long CI queues and noisy full-suite runs made iteration expensive. By splitting test shards by runtime characteristics (fast/unit, medium/integration, slow/e2e) and making the dependency update workflow proactive we reduce queue contention and accelerate dependency hygiene.

What this changes (high level):
- CI: introduce three explicit shard profiles (fast/unit, medium/integration, slow/e2e) and a lightweight profile selector that picks a shard subset based on changed paths and heuristics.
- CI: add path-aware test runner so lint and unit tests only run for affected packages when the change is scoped.
- CI: add cache-rotation policy (TTL + LRU hint) to avoid stale docker layer re-use across node-version bumps.
- Automation: add a dependency-triage bot (scripts/dep-triage/) which runs weekly, scans package manifests (go.mod, package.json, pyproject.toml), and opens candidate PRs with owners + labels (deps/minor, deps/patch) for non-breaking upgrades. The bot integrates with our internal Linear tags and a lightweight risk scoring to avoid noisy upgrades for transitive major bumps.
- Tooling: introduce a slim builder image and split Dockerfile into build/runtime stages to shave ~220MB off the CI image and reduce upload time to the runner cache.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implement shard profiles and selector
- [x] Implement path-aware test gating
- [x] Add cache rotation and TTL for docker/build caches
- [x] Add dep-triage bot and basic scoring
- [x] Update CI docs and add troubleshooting notes
- [x] Manual dogfood run on the staging pipeline

Commits (summary):
- feat(ci): add test-profile selector and profile definitions
- feat(ci): implement path-aware test gating for unit/lint runs
- perf(ci): introduce cache-rotation TTL and LRU hinting for runner caches
- feat(automation): add dep-triage bot scaffolding and weekly workflow
- refactor(docker): split Dockerfile into slim builder + runtime
- docs(ci): update CONTRIBUTING.md and ci/README with new shard guidance

Files changed (high level):
- .github/workflows/ci.yml (rewritten to call profile selector and conditional jobs)
- .github/workflows/dep-triage.yml (new weekly workflow for bot)
- ci/profile-selector.py (new helper used by CI)
- ci/path-gate.py (path-based gating logic)
- scripts/dep-triage/* (bot code, templates, scoring rules)
- images/ci/Dockerfile (split into multi-stage)
- docs/ci/README.md (update)
- CONTRIBUTING.md (ci iteration section)

Small snippet examples included in PR: a condensed selector rule used by the workflow: paths matching src/python/ or sdk/python/ trigger "fast+medium" profile; changes to infra/ or e2e/ trigger slow profile. The path-gate implements a cheap git-diff parse and a file-type map to map changed files to test suites.

Review conversation (high level):
- Ethan Park (reviewer): "Nice decomposition. Two requests: 1) add metrics for profile selection decisions so we can audit why a shard was picked; 2) make the dep-triage PR body include an opt-out label so platform owners can pause automation per package."
- Maya Chen (author): "Added telemetry events (ci.profile.selected reason tag) and added the opt-out label mechanism (deps/automation-paused) to the bot. See commit feat(ci): telemetry + dep-triage optout in second push."
- Rhea Kapoor: "Please add a smoke job that runs the medium shard against the staging cluster on a cron to catch regressions we may miss when only unit tests run."
- Maya Chen: "Added a staging-smoke job to .github/workflows/ci.yml; it runs nightly and is gated by a flag in ci/config.yaml."
- Samir Patel: "Security scan step should still run for dependency bot PRs — we can't auto-merge without a security check."
- Maya Chen: "Dep-triage opens PRs as draft and CI runs the security-scan job; the merge automation waits for a maintainer to approve after checks pass. Documented in the workflow comments."
- Approval summary: Ethan approved after telemetry added; Rhea approved after adding staging smoke; Samir approved after explicit security gating added.

CI run history on this PR:
- Initial push (2026-02-18): integration runner timed out on one slow e2e test (flaky infra teardown). job rerun was scheduled.
- Second push (2026-02-20): fixed a minor timing issue in e2e teardown, triggered full CI; fast and medium shards passed; slow shard had a single flaky test which was quarantined (skipped with ticket ENG-8270).
- Final push (2026-02-22): all shards green, security-scan passed, dep-scan reported two low-severity transitive issues (documented in dep-triage output).

CI checks summary: build: pass; unit-tests (fast): pass; integration (medium): pass; e2e (slow): pass (after quarantine); lint: pass; security-scan: pass; dep-scan: pass; docker-build: pass; cache-priming: pass.

Performance impact measured in dogfood runs: median CI runtime for changes touching single packages decreased from ~24m to ~9m when path-gating correctly selected the fast profile. Full-suite runtimes for cross-cutting changes are unchanged but now run on dedicated slow runners to avoid head-of-line blocking. Runner queue wait times dropped ~37% during a 48h experiment window.

Rollout plan:
- Step 1: merge to main behind a feature flag; enable path-aware selection for a subset of repos (sdk-* and examples) for 48h.
- Step 2: expand to monorepo packages incrementally and monitor ci.profile.selected metrics and fail rates for 7 days.
- Step 3: enable dep-triage bot in draft mode org-wide (no auto-merge) and collect maintainer feedback.

Post-merge notes and follow-ups:
- OWNERS mapping needs a small update for several legacy packages (tracked in ENG-8288).
- Add alerting for the staging-smoke job failing more than twice in 24h (follow up ENG-8299).
- Consider adding an opt-in auto-merge path for patch bumps after 48h and successful security passes (future work).

Merge: This PR was rebased and merged to main on 2026-02-23 after all reviewers approved and CI was green.

Related: ENG-8123 (CI scalability), ENG-8270 (e2e flaky teardown quarantine), ENG-8288 (owners cleanup).

Notes for release: include a bullet in the next platform changelog about faster CI for scoped changes and the dependency triage bot (non-breaking, targeted automation to improve dependency hygiene).


Split test-shard profiles to reduce tail latency in CI runners; add a dependency triage bot that files labeled PRs for minor/patch bumps and suggests owners. Improve build cache rotation policy to reduce stale layers.
