Context: This is an out-of-band security hotfix for the Runtime LTS line (runtime-1.18-lts). We received a private report that our model artifact cache extraction path could be abused if a malicious/compromised artifact contains symlinks or path traversal entries ("../") that escape the intended extraction directory. This primarily impacts Private deployments that use customer-provided artifact registries and any environment where artifacts can be injected into the cache layer. This PR hardens archive extraction and adds explicit deny rules + tests. It also includes the tightened approval + CI + comms checklist we agreed to for LTS security patches.

Severity / tracking: High (customer-controlled input path + potential file overwrite). CVE request in progress (internal tracking: SEC-2025-019); will update with CVE/GHSA once assigned. No customer exploit observed; patch is being cut under embargo.

What changed (code): 1) Hardened tar/zip extraction in runtime artifact cache: reject entries with absolute paths, parent directory traversal, or Windows drive prefixes; do not follow symlinks/hardlinks; enforce maximum file count and per-file size caps; require all extracted paths to remain within the target directory after realpath normalization. 2) Added a "safe_extract" helper with centralized validation and audit logging (log-only in debug builds; redacted paths in production logs). 3) Added unit tests covering traversal, symlink escape, and archive bombs. 4) Added a targeted integration test that runs in release-branch CI (fast) to ensure the cache directory remains unchanged outside extraction root.

Operational notes: No perf impact expected; extraction is not on token-critical path. The stricter validation can cause artifact download failures if a customer artifact is malformed; error message includes a stable error code (RUNTIME_ARTIFACT_EXTRACT_VALIDATION_FAILED) for Support triage.

Release intent: Cut runtime-1.18.1-lts+security.1 (tag format per ADR-027 draft; final tag to be created by release manager). This patch should be made available to Dedicated and Private customers on the LTS channel as "recommended" and may be escalated to "mandatory" based on Security review.

Expedited LTS security patch checklist (must be completed before merge): [x] Security sign-off (Dr. Aisha Rahman delegate / Hanae Suzuki) [x] Runtime sign-off (Noah Patel + Mateo Alvarez or delegate) [x] Release Eng sign-off (Connor O'Brien) [x] SRE sign-off for rollout/alerting (Sean Gallagher) [x] CI: release-branch unit + integration suite green [x] CI: scheduler smoke tests green [x] CI: container build + vulnerability scan green [x] Perf gates: waive full perf-canary; run "perf-smoke" set and document results (see below) [x] Artifact provenance: generate checksums + provenance metadata (handled in release pipeline; verified in staging) [x] Comms: draft internal Support/CS heads-up and customer advisory stub (without exploit details) [x] Backport notes: confirm no additional cherry-picks required

Perf-smoke results (A100, H100; 5 runs; p95): Within noise vs baseline (+0.2% to +0.6% p95 latency), throughput unchanged. Full perf-canary will run post-tag as informational.

Files / areas touched: - runtime/artifacts/safe_extract.{cc,h} (new helper) - runtime/artifacts/model_cache.cc (use safe_extract + error codes) - runtime/tests/artifacts/safe_extract_test.cc (new) - ci/workflows/release-branch.yml (add extraction integration test) - docs/internal/security/lts-hotfix-comms-checklist.md (new internal doc for on-call/release manager)

Rollout / comms plan: 1) Publish artifacts to LTS channel with signed checksums. 2) Notify Support/CS in #support and #customer-success with patch availability + error code mapping + recommended next steps. 3) For Private customers, provide advisory + upgrade guidance (pin to patch, verify checksums, rollback steps). 4) Dedicated: phased rollout per region with elevated alerting; rollback on elevated 5xx/latency anomalies.

Notes for reviewers: Please focus on (a) path normalization correctness across platforms, (b) symlink/hardlink handling, (c) error messages not leaking sensitive paths, and (d) CI gating coverage.

Follow-ups (not in this hotfix): - Add SBOM attestation to LTS artifacts (tracked in PR-23402) - Expand safe_extract to support additional archive formats we may introduce later - Wire Support playbook to include the new error code mapping

Refs: ENG-4829 (security patch SLA for LTS), ENG-4821 (LTS initiative epic), SUP-18506 (Private customer asks for checksums/pinning), INT-3302 (release branch secrets/permissions).
Hanae Suzuki: Can we guarantee we never follow symlinks created inside the extraction root? Some tar implementations will materialize symlinks before later entries reference them.
Connor O'Brien: Yes. We reject any symlink/hardlink entries outright (typeflag) and we also open output files with O_NOFOLLOW where supported; added a test where an archive first creates a symlink then writes through it — now fails validation.
Noah Patel: realpath() behavior differs if the file doesn't exist yet. How are we preventing '../' without relying on realpath of a non-existent path?
Connor O'Brien: We normalize the entry path syntactically first (clean + reject '..' segments) and then join against extraction root; after creating parent dirs we validate the parent directory realpath is under root. Added comments + a unit test for the non-existent path case.
Sahana Iyer: CI change looks fine, but for hotfixes we should keep the workflow additions minimal. Can we ensure this test runs only on runtime-*-lts and release branches?
Connor O'Brien: Updated the workflow filter to only run the new extraction integration test on runtime-*-lts and release/* branches. Main branch continues to run the broader suite.
Sean Gallagher: For Dedicated rollout, add a note about what metrics we watch and what constitutes rollback criteria.
Connor O'Brien: Added to body under rollout plan: elevated alerting on artifact download/extract failures + standard latency/5xx; rollback on sustained SLO violation or elevated RUNTIME_ARTIFACT_EXTRACT_VALIDATION_FAILED rates after confirming not customer artifacts.
Mateo Alvarez: Approving. Please ensure the error code is stable across patches and added to the internal support mapping.
Connor O'Brien: Done. Added to errors.h and internal doc template. Support mapping will be referenced in the Support playbook follow-up.

runtime/artifacts: enforce extraction caps and stable error codes for validation failures
tests: add unit tests for traversal/symlink/hardlink/archive bomb cases
ci: add fast extraction integration test to release-branch workflow
docs(internal): add LTS security hotfix comms checklist + sign-off requirements

Reliability: Added stable error code RUNTIME_ARTIFACT_EXTRACT_VALIDATION_FAILED for Support triage.
CI/Process: Added expedited LTS security hotfix checklist and a fast extraction integration test for release branches.

Motivation: We observed intermittent streaming stalls and truncated structured outputs from the OpenAI-compat gateway under sustained concurrent streaming traffic, especially when requests included tool/function-calling and large JSON structured-output payloads. Root cause analysis pointed at oversized proxy buffer headroom plus lack of per-route payload quota enforcement which allowed some long-poll requests to exhaust upstream connection resources and cause head-of-line blocking. Changes: 1) Reduce default proxy write/read headroom from 1MB to 256KB and make it configurable per-route. 2) Introduce per-route payload byte quota and hard limit enforcement for sync (non-streaming) requests; requests over quota are rejected with 413 or 429 depending on route config and provide a Retry-After header. 3) Adjust streaming proxy chunk flush thresholds to favor more frequent smaller flushes for function/tool-calling streams so structured output arrives earlier and is less likely to be dropped. 4) Add a lightweight in-memory per-connection backpressure counter to deprioritize new large non-streaming requests when streaming sessions are active. 5) Extend OpenAI-compat layer to include a compatibility shim that maps oversized completion responses to a streaming fallback when route allows streaming, preserving function-call markers and structured JSON chunks. 6) Add metrics: gateway.proxy.buffer_headroom_bytes, gateway.route.payload_quota_exceeded, gateway.stream.flush_count and an alert to detect sustained per-route 413/429 spikes. Tests: added unit tests for headroom config parsing and quota logic, integration tests simulating concurrent streaming plus large sync requests, and a perf canary harness that validates stable p95 latency under 1000 concurrent streaming clients. Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag gateway.buffering.v2 and staged canary at 5%->25%->100% with monitoring queries for errors and alloc spikes. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is conservative and non-breaking; routes that depend on previous large single-request semantics can opt out by setting route.payload_quota_bytes to 0. Motivation: Some operator and cross-tenant paths were able to surface KMS-wrapped artifacts and audit records without an explicit tenant binding, increasing blast radius during operator escalation. This PR implements a small, composable enforcement surface that performs three coordinated tasks: (1) aggregate and normalize tenant assertions at the edge, (2) allocate a short-lived KMS escrow key tied to the tenant claim for cryptographic operations that require strict locality, and (3) emit audit envelopes through an immutable audit bridge which signs and seals events before delivery to long-term storage. Design summary: The claim-aggregator service collects claims from auth headers, session tokens and upstream directories; it produces a canonical tenant assertion that is cached per-request with a TTL and HMAC fingerprint. The kms-escrow allocator returns a tenant-scoped transient CMK handle (wrapped key material) and records a minimal provenance record. The immutable audit bridge converts internal audit records into a sealed protobuf envelope, signs with the escrowed key and forwards to audit-plane; envelopes include a region and residency tag to aid downstream retention. Operational considerations: default behavior is shadow mode where assertions, KMS allocations and sealed envelopes are emitted to a separate shadow stream; enforcement gates are feature-flagged and can be turned on per-cluster. Rollout plan: 1) deploy aggregator and bridge in shadow mode; 2) enable KMS escrow allocation for sampling traffic; 3) enable enforcement for internal operator flows; 4) full enforcement by tenant cohort. Backout plan: flip feature flag off and run the revert script. Checklist: implement aggregator and tests; add OPA v2 policy and unit tests; create integration tests covering KMS fallback and audit sealing; update Helm chart and rollout docs; run soak for 72h in canary cluster. Related: ENG-1327 and SEC-48. No API changes expected for customers.
Adds tenant-boundary claim aggregator, KMS escrow path for tenant-scoped keys, and an immutable audit bridge that signs and seals audit envelopes. Default rollout is shadow mode with gradual enforcement; no customer-visible API changes.
introduce tenant claim aggregator service; wire aggregator into auth pipeline; add kms-escrow allocator and tests; implement immutable-audit-bridge and signing agent; add integration tests for residency and fallback; fix race in claim cache; update docs and rollout script
Miguel Santos: Can you clarify the TTL and cache invalidation semantics for the aggregator? I saw a TODO in aggregator.go referencing stale claims.
Aisha Kumar: TTL default is 30s and we invalidate on token rotation events; added explicit cache eviction in latest commit.
Priya Desai: The KMS escrow path looks good but we need to ensure the allocator honors key-provider quotas to avoid throttling during high churn.
Aisha Kumar: Added a simple token-bucket in allocator and instrumentation to surface throttle rates. See kms/escrow/allocator.go + metrics.
Kenji Watanabe: Audit envelope format looks stable; please add migration script for audit-consumers that currently expect flat JSON.
Aisha Kumar: Added docs and a shim in audit/bridge for transitional consumers; will follow-up with ops to migrate sinks.
medium. Introduces new crypto path and caching surface which increases attack/operational surface; mitigations include shadow-mode rollout, rate-limiting on KMS escrow allocations, scoped IAM roles for allocator, and automated health checks. Monitoring includes per-tenant KMS allocation rates, envelope signing errors, and increased latency SLO alerts.

Motivation: customers with strict data residency requirements and complex key management setups asked for stronger runtime enforcement and better visibility into per-tenant KMS usage. This PR introduces a lightweight Residency Shield middleware that validates request claims and enforces region pinning policies early in the request path, a per-tenant KMS telemetry exporter to surface key selection and provider fallback events to the console, and an RBACv2 assertion sanitizer that strips unsafe claim combinations before policy evaluation. Changes are targeted at hosted and private control planes with opt-in gating for Dedicated until rollout is verified. Implementation summary: Residency Shield validates x-tenant-region and service-geo claims, consults the residency-policy cache and returns a 403 with structured audit tags if the request violates policy; it also attaches an immutable residency.verdict header for downstream components. KMS telemetry records selected provider, key-id hash, fallback_reason (if any), and latency buckets; metrics are emitted to the existing telemetry pipeline and a new tag residency_cohort. RBACv2 sanitizer normalizes attribute keys, removes cross-tenant impersonation attributes, and converts legacy role strings into canonical role IDs. Rollout plan: behind feature flag feature.residency_shield; gradual canary to 5% of traffic for 48h, monitor audit-error-rate and request-latency P95; if regressions observed, auto-fallback to policy-simulation mode that logs but does not enforce. Backwards compatibility: requests without residency claims default to existing routing behavior; sanitizer is conservative and only drops attributes that match denylist patterns. Testing: unit tests for middleware and sanitizer, integration tests exercising KMS provider fallback (mocked AWS/GCP/az), e2e in staging with synthetic tenants in three geozones. Security review: includes threat model doc and IAC changes to add new telemetry IAM roles. Docs: admin console addition documenting telemetry fields, new alert runbook for residency.verdict violations. Why different from prior karma: this PR focuses on observability + non-destructive enforcement and bridges KMS telemetry with residency policy decisions to aid auditability and incident reasoning.
Evan Liu: Can the residency verdict be forged by clients? Make sure header is immutable and only set by gateway. Author: Residency header is set server-side and validated by an HMAC signed attestation when crossing internal proxies.
Marissa Gomez: How do we avoid noisy alerts during rollout? Author: We include a simulation mode that logs as audit events and a sampling knob to avoid alert storms; added runbook that describes thresholds and step-down plan.
Owen Park: KMS telemetry contains key-id hashes—ensure hashing is salted and non-reversible. Author: We use tenant-scoped salt from KMS config; added unit tests to verify truncation and hashing.
Security Review (Anika Rao): Confirmed threat model and added remediation for header replay; recommended adding telemetry ACLs. Author: ACLs added in infra/iam/telemetry-role.tf and documented in ops runbook.
Marissa Gomez: observed a transient p95 spike in canary during integration run, suggested increasing cache TTL. Author: Increased residency cache TTL to 2s and added cache-miss metric to track impact.
Add Residency Shield middleware to validate tenant-region claims and apply policy-driven enforcement; introduce per-tenant KMS telemetry with residency_cohort tagging; add RBACv2 attribute sanitizer to prevent unsafe attributes from reaching policy engine. Rollout is gated by feature flag. Operators: review new telemetry panels and update alert thresholds.
Disable feature.residency_shield flag and re-deploy gateway config; telemetry exporter removal is non-blocking but should be disabled if immediate rollback required. For Dedicated customers use the console to switch to policy-simulation mode to avoid enforcement.

Motivation: Multiple SDK teams (Python/TypeScript/Go) have drifted in credential APIs and streaming ergonomics: mismatch in session factory shapes, differing retry preset names, and inconsistent stream iterator behaviour caused duplicated adaptation logic in upstream services. This PR coordinates a minimal, backwards-compatible convergence across the three SDKs by introducing a small cross-language contract (documented in sdk/README/SESSION.md), consolidating retry preset names, and adding a lightweight token-warmup hook for stream-first requests.

What this PR does (high level): 1) Introduces SessionFactory v2 surface (polyglot contract) and a thin compatibility shim on top of existing SessionFactory implementations to avoid mass migrations. 2) Adds a RetryProfile alias map so "default"/"standard"/"balanced" map to a canonical engine preset at runtime and surfaces the mapping in SDK logs. 3) Stabilizes stream consumer ergonomics: async generator/pull-stream implementations now expose a canonical .checkpoint() method and consistent error wrapping for transient auth/IO failures. 4) Adds a token_warmup hook that allows SDKs to prefetch tokens for zero-first-byte latency on long-running streams. 5) Bumps SDK versions: python-sdk 1.12.0, typescript-sdk 0.9.7, go-sdk v1.5.3 and updates changelogs.

Compatibility and migration notes: The SessionFactory v2 is opt-in via the configuration flag "enable_session_v2". The compatibility shim will log a single deprecation warning when enabled against older server-side contracts. Retry preset aliases are additive (no removed names). The only behavioural change that could affect callers is the standardized stream error envelope (wraps transient errors as StreamTransientError). A migration doc with examples and copy/paste fixes is included and linked in release notes.

Testing and verification: Unit tests added across all three SDK test suites (python: tests/test_session_v2.py, ts: test/stream-checkpoint.spec.ts, go: session/factory_test.go). End-to-end smoke runs performed in the staging cluster: stream warmup reduced median TTFB by ~7% on synthetic workloads; no increased error rate on 48-hour soak.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc updated (sdk/README/SESSION.md) - [x] Unit tests for new surfaces - [x] E2E smoke on staging - [x] Changelog and version bumps - [x] Release notes draft - [x] Harmony with SDK owners (see reviewers)

Related: ENG-2134 (credential parity), ENG-2139 (stream ergonomics), PM-501 (release coordination). Links: design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2134/session-v2-cross-sdk, staging run summary: https://internal.ci/redwood/stage/178945/run-summary
Ava Chen: Please clarify lifecycle of objects returned by SessionFactory v2; can we avoid additional goroutines in Go impl?
Sofia Ramos: Reply - v2 returns a light wrapper with explicit Close() and does not spawn background goroutines by default; warmup can opt-in to background refresh.
Marcus Holt: Suggestion - unify the RetryProfile enum names in telemetry to avoid fragmentation across users. Updated alias map accordingly.
Leah Patel: Small nit on TS typings for checkpoint - prefer optional generics to keep backward compatibility. Fixed in c4b7de2.
Owen Garcia: Verified Go unit tests and suggested a small benchmark; added benchmark results to staging run summary.
Ava Chen: Approve after small doc wording change. Marcus Holt: Approve. Leah Patel: Approve. Owen Garcia: Approve.
Cross-SDK: Introduce opt-in SessionFactory v2, standardize retry preset aliases, unify streaming checkpoint API, and add token warmup hook. SDKs bumped: python 1.12.0, typescript 0.9.7, go v1.5.3. Backwards-compatible with a single opt-in flag; see docs/sdk/SESSION.md for migration.

payload.body:
Motivation: Users running streaming and function-calling workloads need reliable correlation across gateway, runtime and SDKs to tie partial streams and tool invocations back to a single request. Existing observability was sparse for streaming slices and tool/function calls.
Goals: 1) propagate a stable correlation id (header: X-Correlation-ID) across the OpenAI compatibility shim and runtime, 2) attach endpoint and variant dimensions to HTTP metrics and Prometheus labels so per-route cost/latency is visible, 3) emit structured JSONL logs for streaming chunks and tool call boundaries so log ingestion can reconstruct full interactions, 4) avoid changing public user-facing API semantics but provide compatibility mappings for common OpenAI headers.
What changed:
- Gateway: map incoming OpenAI style request headers (e.g. OpenAI-Client-Request-Id) to X-Correlation-ID if present; if none found, generate a v4 UUID early in the request path. Ensure header is passed to downstream runtime and to internal async event bus.
- Runtime: attach correlation_id to all emitted span tags and to streaming chunk events. Streaming fragment logs now include fields: correlation_id, stream_offset, partial_text, model_variant, route_name, and sequence_token when available. Logs are emitted as newline-delimited JSON to the structured logger.
- Metrics: per-endpoint metrics include new label endpoint=/<route> and variant=<model-variant>. Added a lightweight mapping in metrics exporter to avoid cardinality explosion: only include variant for routes marked as high_variance in route config.
- SDK shim (OpenAI-compat): expose correlation id in response metadata under top-level "correlation_id" for quick access in SDKs and examples. Also preserve compatibility headers for downstream user code.
- E2E tests: added deterministic test for correlation propagation across gateway->runtime->function-hook cycle, and an integration test that asserts JSONL structure for streaming partials.
- Docs: updated observability.md with examples for searching logs by correlation_id and configuring endpoint dimensions.
Implementation notes: conservative approach to labels to prevent high tag cardinality. UUID generated once per inbound HTTP request. When requests are retried by the client via the compatibility shim, the shim preserves the original correlation id unless explicitly overridden.
Backwards compatibility: no request body semantics were changed; header mapping is additive.
Rollout plan: feature gated behind FF_TELEMETRY_CORRELATION (default on for staging, opt-in for production rollout).
Evan Liu: Nice work. Question: are we sure we won't accidentally increase Prometheus cardinality when variant changes per request? Please add guard logic or sampling.
Priya Shah: Added guard. exporter now checks route config high_variance flag and only labels variant when true. Also added unit test to ensure labels length bounded.
Marco Diaz: The JSONL schema looks good but add an explicit timestamp and sequence number for each chunk to make reassembly deterministic.
Priya Shah: Added timestamp and sequence_token. Updated tests accordingly.
Ava Thompson: Can we document how this interacts with existing request IDs in downstream services? It confused our SREs in dev.
Priya Shah: Added a note in observability.md recommending using correlation_id as the canonical trace key; included a migration snippet for downstream services to read X-Correlation-ID.
Priya Shah: Feature flag added to configs/feature_flags.yaml to control rollout.
New tests cover gateway mapping, runtime propagation, JSONL log schema, and metrics exporter label safeguards. Manual verification performed on staging with a streaming demo: search by correlation_id returned the full session and associated tool call logs.
When enabling FF_TELEMETRY_CORRELATION in production, monitor Prometheus series count for the first 24h. If series growth > 5% for endpoints, flip flag for the affected service and file ENG-1989.
Correlation IDs are UUID4 and do not contain PII. We avoid echoing user-supplied headers verbatim in logs — OpenAI-compat mapped headers are normalized and validated before emission.
cURL example: curl -H 'X-Correlation-ID: abc-123' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -d '{...}'
SDK note: response.metadata.correlation_id is available in Python and TS SDKs under response.metadata['correlation_id']
Logs: jq filter: jq -c 'select(.correlation_id=="abc-123")' logs.jsonl

Context and motivation:
This PR aligns three SDK codepaths (Python, TypeScript, Go) for credential rotation, backoff presets, and streaming ergonomics. Teams reported subtle mismatches in reauth handshake timing and retry semantics across languages leading to spurious reconnects and metric noise (see ENG-8921). The goal here is to provide a small, well-documented surface (RetryProfile + CredentialHint) that is behaviorally consistent across SDKs while preserving idiomatic APIs for each language.

Summary of changes (one-liner):
Consolidate auth/backoff config, add compact RetryProfile API, introduce cancelable pullstream helpers and stream resume hints, and bump SDK versions to ship the unified surface.

Review conversation (high-level):

Summary: This hotfix addresses a regression observed during a multi-region failover drill where the quarantine controller's instantaneous eviction score could spike and trigger bulk node/slot evictions in the affected region. The root cause was a mismatch between the quarantine scoring window and the decay logic in the eviction policy: short-lived latency spikes were amplified instead of being attenuated, which cascaded into capacity loss and higher latencies for remaining requests. This PR introduces a 'dynamic eviction attenuator' that applies a time-decayed smoothing factor to quarantine scores and a region-level 'quarantine stabilizer' that enforces a soft cap on simultaneous evictions and provides a controlled retry/backoff for drain actions.

Motivation and impact: During the incident the platform lost 18% of serving capacity in the region, causing end-to-end latency SLO breaches for several high-throughput tenants. The change is intended to: 1) prevent mass evictions from transient spikes, 2) preserve KV cache locality where possible, and 3) allow the existing circuit breaker and SLO enforcer to take corrective action without compounding failures. This is a targeted hotfix with a feature flag (runtime.feature.degradation.stabilizer) to allow phased rollout and measured rollback if needed.

What I changed (high level):
- Add attenuation layer (src/runtime/eviction/attenuator.rs) that smooths quarantine scores using exponential decay based on per-tenant and per-slot metrics.
- Add regional stabilizer (src/infra/region_quarantine/controller.go) implementing a soft-concurrency cap for evictions and a jittered exponential backoff for drains.
- Wire feature flag gating and metrics (pkg/config/featureflags.go, observability/metrics/eviction_metrics.prom).
- Add unit and integration tests that simulate transient spikes and assert no more than N concurrent evictions per region (tests/eviction/attenuator_test.go, tests/region_quarantine/flow_integration_test.go).
- Update rollout notes and a short mitigation playbook (docs/runbooks/region_quarantine.md).

Commits (summary):
- commit 1: initial attenuator implementation + unit tests (attenuator.rs, attenuator_test.go)
- commit 2: region stabilizer + controller wiring + feature flag checks (controller.go, featureflags.go)
- commit 3: add metrics, dashboards, and alerts adjustments (eviction_metrics.prom, dashboards/eviction.json)
- commit 4: test hardening and race-condition fix after reviewer feedback (tests/..., controller.go small fix)

Files changed (high level snippets):
- src/runtime/eviction/attenuator.rs: new file, core function compute_attenuated_score(score, age_ms, decay_half_life_ms) with comments describing expected behavior and complexity O(1).
- src/infra/region_quarantine/controller.go: introduces stabilizer struct with fields {maxConcurrentEvictions, backoffBaseMs} and a small state machine to track in-flight drains.
- pkg/config/featureflags.go: adds runtime.feature.degradation.stabilizer flag (default false for canary).
- observability/metrics/eviction_metrics.prom: adds eviction_in_flight_count and eviction_attenuation_ratio metrics.
- tests/region_quarantine/flow_integration_test.go: simulates 10s spike and asserts < 3 concurrent evictions and no capacity loss >5%.
- docs/runbooks/region_quarantine.md: runbook entry with playbook steps to toggle feature flag and manual rollback.

Checklist (internal):
- [x] Reproduced issue with unit/integration tests
- [x] Added attenuator + stabilizer implementation
- [x] Added metrics and dashboards for observability
- [x] Feature-flagged rollout path documented
- [x] Coordinator + SRE runbook updated
- [x] Post-merge canary plan (10% traffic in eu-west-1 for 30m)

Review conversation (condensed):
- Ravi Kumar: "High level LGTM. Two asks: (1) add clearer comments around the decay half-life choice and how it maps to observed spike durations, (2) ensure backoff doesn't starve the SLA for queued requests."
- Aisha (author): "Addressed both: added math comments in attenuator.rs and added a peripheral queue budget used by stabilizer so evictions don't starve queued requests (see controller.go lines ~180-220)."
- Elena Morales: "Can you add an e2e shot with a longer tail (60s) to validate we don't slowly bleed capacity?"
- Aisha: "Added extended e2e in flow_integration_test.go and tuned backoffBaseMs to 2000ms for better recovery."
- Samir Gupta (SRE): "CI flaked on one race in tests; after the test hardening commit, re-ran CI and all green. Approving for hotfix backport to release/2026-02."

CI and checks:
- build: pass
- unit-tests: pass (attenuator tests added)
- integration-tests: pass (regional flow tests)
- e2e: pass (short + extended scenarios)
- lint: pass (small gofmt/fix in controller.go)
- canary-smoke (post-merge): pending (run by ops after merge)

Risk and mitigation: This changes eviction behavior and could mask pathological load if coupled with other policy changes; mitigation includes the feature flag for gradual rollout, additional metrics to detect attenuator miscalibration (eviction_attenuation_ratio > 0.9) and an immediate rollback path (toggle runtime.feature.degradation.stabilizer=false) plus runbook steps to manually trigger regional circuit-breaker if needed.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after approvals from Ravi, Elena, and Samir. Backported to release/2026-02 as hotfix/attenuator-regional-quarantine-stabilizer-backport. Post-merge ops plan: 1) enable on 10% EU-WEST-1 traffic for 30 minutes, monitor eviction_in_flight_count and p95 latency, 2) ramp to 50% for 1 hour, 3) full enable if no regressions.

Notes for follow-up: Evaluate different decay_half_life_ms per-tenant profiles (ENG-8910) and consider exposing a per-tenant override via Dedicated config in a future PR. Logs/metrics from the canary are collected under infra/canary/82463/ and will be used to tune defaults.
Fixes an over-aggressive regional quarantine eviction path: adds a decay-aware attenuation layer and a feature-flagged stabilizer to prevent mass evictions during transient cross-region failovers. Backported as hotfix.

payload.body:
This PR introduces an incremental dependency-refresh coordinator and refactors the presubmit routing layer so CI gives faster, more targeted feedback for dependency updates and small change sets. Motivation: our full repository dependency refresh runs are expensive and frequently trigger broad presubmit pipelines; this work reduces waste by 1) tracking a minimal transitive delta per dep-bump via a lightweight 'dep-diff' fingerprint, 2) routing presubmit lanes based on path-aware impact maps (only run runtime-heavy integration suites when the change touches core runtime or infra directories), and 3) adding an opt-in change set annotation for automated dep-rolls so maintainers can request full-sweep validation if desired. High level: - Add dep-refresh-coordinator service (lightweight Go binary) that consumes dep bump events, computes a small set of impacted targets (via dependency-graph queries and the dep-diff fingerprint), and writes a presubmit routing hint to the PR as a GitHub check. - Refactor presubmit-router to accept routing-hints from the coordinator and a new path-aware matcher; previous hardcoded routing matrix replaced by YAML policies under .github/presubmit-policies/. - Small UX: PR check shows an actionable summary (why certain suites were skipped, and a one-click button to 'run full validation'). - Backwards compat: if coordinator is unavailable we fall back to current matrix to avoid blocking. Includes security posture: dep-scan step is still inserted for all dep bumps regardless of routing. Checklist in PR body and inline build artifacts for maintainers. Related: ENG-4523 (reduce CI waste for dep automation), ENG-4599 (presubmit routing policy engine).

feat: implement dep-diff fingerprinting and minimal impact set computation
refactor: presubmit-router to consume routing-hints and policy YAML
chore: add presubmit policy examples and docs
tests: add unit tests for dep-diff and integration test for routing flow

.github/presubmit-policies/runtime.yml: paths: ["runtime/**", "serving/**"] suites: [integration-runtime, perf-canary]
Arjun Patel: Nice work — can we make the fingerprint stable across Go versions? Request: add a golden-file test for the fingerprint function. (requested changes)

Add a lightweight telemetry sidecar that runs alongside inference workers to emit compact per-invocation telemetry and prefetch effectiveness metrics, plus a seasonal alert gating mechanism that reduces noisy paging during predictable diurnal traffic patterns. Motivation: customers are experiencing noisy alert churn tied to predictable daily token-usage seasonality and prefetch warmup bursts; we need a low-latency, low-cost way to (1) surface per-invocation kernel-queue-depth, prefetch-hit/miss signals, and estimated energy/token proxies, and (2) apply context-aware alert gating so SREs can focus on non-seasonal anomalies. This PR implements: 1) sidecar binary and a tiny protobuf-over-UDP wire format optimized for 1kB/second telemetry per worker, 2) per-invocation prefetched-prefix metrics (prefetch_hit, prefetch_latency_ms, kv_prefetch_age_ms) and kernel_queue_depth sampled at entry/exit, 3) a new histogram metric token_energy_estimate_bytes that uses a compact bucketing scheme to approximate GPU work per-token for coarse cost attribution, 4) an alert-gate policy engine that ingests seasonal baseline windows (hour-of-day, day-of-week) and mutes low-severity token-cost alerts within expected bands while allowing bursts above a configurable multiplier, 5) DB migration to add telemetry_sidecar_config and seasonal_windows tables, 6) console dashboard: "Sidecar Prefetch Overview" and a lightweight "Seasonal Alert Gate" playbook panel. Backwards compatibility: sidecar is optional; servers without sidecar fall back to existing runtime metrics with a small compatibility shim that synthesizes kernel_queue_depth as -1 and prefetch_* as unknown. Tests: unit tests for sidecar encoder/decoder, integration test that spins a local worker+sidecar and validates emitted metrics reach the metrics-relay, and an end-to-end staging run with sample seasonal windows to verify alert suppression. Rollout plan: 1) deploy sidecar to staging and run for 48h, 2) enable seasonal-window read-only mode in prod to validate no missed critical alerts for 7 days, 3) flip suppression to active with conservative multipliers, monitor for 14 days, 4) iterate on buckets and multipliers by observation. Related: ENG-4412 (prefetch telemetry exploration), ENG-4470 (alert noisefloor initiative).
Diego Alvarez (2024-11-08): Can we guarantee the sidecar's failure mode is crash-only and won't block the worker? Maya Chen: Yes, sidecar communicates over UDP and the shim uses a 50ms deadline; worker proceeds if ack not received.
Priya Nair (2024-11-09): The seasonal windows schema looks flexible but do we need timezone normalization? Maya Chen: Windows are stored in UTC and UI converts by tenant timezone; added UTC note to migration comment.
Ruth Kim (2024-11-10): Prefer exponential histogram for token_energy_estimate, but I see compact manual buckets—can we revisit? Maya Chen: Chose manual small set to keep cardinality low; added an adapter to convert to exponential histograms downstream for analysis.
Ruth Kim (2024-11-11): LGTM pending one nit on migration idempotency. Maya Chen: fixed migration to be idempotent and added test.
Diego Alvarez (2024-11-12): CI flaked on lint; re-run looks clean. Diego Alvarez: Approved.

Introduce seasonal alert gate to suppress predictable low-severity alert noise

payload.body:
Motivation: Continuous batching has periodic p99 spikes and occasional KV-cache starvation when many short requests interleave with a few long ones. This PR adds a smoothing layer for prefetch window sizes, an admission hysteresis gate to reduce oscillation under bursty load, and a lightweight KV-weighted aging heuristic to prevent pin-starvation. The change is intentionally conservative: we add configurable knobs with safe defaults to avoid accidental throughput regressions.

Design summary: (1) Prefetch window smoothing keeps a moving exponential average of the effective prefetch size per slot and limits instantaneous growth by a configurable growth_clamp factor. (2) Admission hysteresis introduces two thresholds: admit_threshold and release_threshold (release_threshold < admit_threshold) so we only shrink prefetch windows after sustained low-utilization, avoiding thrash. (3) KV-weighted aging biases slot reclamation away from slots with large KV pin counts by assigning an "effective age" that scales inversely with pinned_kv_count, preventing eviction storms for KV-heavy requests. (4) Timeout micro-tuning: we shift from a uniform hard timeout to a jittered soft-timeout that lets a small fraction of near-deadline requests run to completion before preemption, which reduces tail amplification for conversational workloads.

Implementation notes: Changes are primarily in runtime/batcher/continuous_scheduler.{cc,h}, runtime/kv/kv_pin_tracker.{cc,h} and runtime/config/defaults.go. New feature flags: batcher.prefetch.smoothing.enabled, batcher.admission.hysteresis.{admit,release}, batcher.kv_age.weight. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve existing behavior unless smoothing or hysteresis flags are toggled; config validation rejects obviously unsafe values.

Benchmarks and testing: Microbench harness (perf/bench/continuous_bench) shows a 7% reduction in p99 latency and a 3% increase in median throughput on our mixed short+long synthetic workload (50k requests, 90/10 short/long split). KV-heavy regression suite (perf/kv_starvation_suite) shows elimination of recurring slot reclamation for pinned workloads in 95% of runs. Unit tests and integration tests added for hysteresis transitions, smoothing window boundary conditions, and KV aging math.

Rollout plan: Merge to main, enable feature flags off by default. Canary rollout to dedicated/intra-team redwood clusters for 48 hours with telemetry gates: p99 latency, batching efficiency, slot churn rate, and KV eviction events. If telemetry remains stable, flip smoothing.enabled=true and hysteresis to conservative values across hosted rows over 7 days.

Risks and mitigations: Overly-aggressive smoothing could reduce responsiveness to persistent load shifts — mitigated by growth_clamp and per-tenant overrides. Admission hysteresis can delay capacity reductions; thresholds chosen to be conservative and runtime metrics expose hysteresis dwell time. KV-weighted aging is intentionally gentle to avoid starving short stateless requests; can be disabled per-deployment.

Related: ENG-4107 (batcher tuning epic), ENG-4210 (kv pinning observability), SUP-1201 incident postmortem referenced in the description.

This description is intentionally compact but covers motivation, design, tests, and rollout instructions.
Liam O'Connor (2026-02-16): Please add a note in defaults.go explaining why growth_clamp defaults to 1.5 — helps reviewers understand risk profile.
Asha Patel (2026-02-16): Added comment and unit test for clamp boundary in continuous_scheduler_test.cc
Maya Ruiz (2026-02-18): Can you run the KV-heavy suite with higher concurrency? The initial run had only 8 workers — starvation happens at 32+.
Asha Patel (2026-02-18): Re-ran KV suite at 32 and 64 workers; results attached to perf run. No recurring reclamation observed at 64 workers for 1000 iterations.
Ethan Zhao (2026-02-20): Suggest adding a telemetry gauge for hysteresis dwell time — added dashboard patch in a follow-up commit.
Liam O'Connor (2026-02-21): Approving after verifying perf-smoke and reviewing tests.
Maya Ruiz (2026-02-21): Approved — small runtime nit resolved.
Adds conservative prefetch window smoothing and admission hysteresis to the continuous batcher to reduce p99 spikes and prevent KV-pin starvation. Feature flags and defaults provided; enabled via canary before full rollout.

Context: Optimize recommendations can change serving behavior (batching / caching / quantization profiles). We already persist gate runs and compute pass/fail, but there were still paths where an operator (or automation) could call the apply endpoint even if the gate was failed or still running. This PR enforces quality gating at the final boundary: the ApplyConfig operation.

What this PR does: (1) Adds a mandatory precondition check in OptimizeService ApplyConfig: if the target route/policy requires gating, the request must reference a gate_run_id and that gate run must be in PASSED or OVERRIDDEN state at time of apply. (2) Returns explicit, structured failure reasons (reason_code + human message) and stable identifiers for the UI/automation to link to the gate artifacts. (3) Adds a Console deep-link URL and API field to allow the Console to render “Blocked by quality gate” with one click to inspect the run.

Key behavior changes: - If gate is FAILED => ApplyConfig returns HTTP 409 with code QUALITY_GATE_FAILED, includes gate_run_id, gate_status=FAILED, failing_metrics summary (top 3), and a console_url. - If gate is RUNNING/PENDING => ApplyConfig returns HTTP 409 with code QUALITY_GATE_PENDING and includes a recommended retry_after_seconds. - If gate is missing but required => ApplyConfig returns HTTP 400 with code QUALITY_GATE_REQUIRED (this is the "safe by default" behavior). - If policy does not require gating (legacy/internal routes in staging) => unchanged behavior.

Non-goals: This PR does not implement override approval flows (handled in pr-19537) and does not add per-route policy configurability (handled in pr-19588). It does include forward-compatible fields in the error response to avoid another API churn when those land.

Testing: Added unit tests for gate status transitions and ApplyConfig error mapping; added integration tests to ensure ApplyConfig blocks on FAILED and PENDING gates, and allows PASSED.

Rollout plan: This is guarded behind feature flag optimize.quality_gates.enforce_apply=true (default off). We will enable in staging first, then for internal dogfood routes, then limited beta. Flag will be flipped on alongside Console UI work.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] OpenAPI updated - [x] Error codes documented - [x] Structured log added for blocked applies (for audit + debugging)

Refs: ENG-3921 (state machine), ENG-3927 (audit log events), related PRs: pr-19523 (eval-harness wiring), pr-19537 (overrides).
Noah Patel (review): We should be careful about the “missing gate_run_id but required” path. If someone is doing a manual apply during incident response, do we want a hard block? Also, please confirm there’s no way to bypass by using an older PASSED gate.

Jordan Lee (author): Agree on incident response, but we’re keeping bypass out of band (admin-only override flow lands in pr-19537). For now, safe-by-default means hard block if gating is required. Re older gate: this PR enforces that gate_run.config_diff_hash matches the apply request’s config diff hash (and model_family/hardware_sku when present). So you can’t “reuse” a prior PASSED gate for a different diff.

Chloe Martin (review): API response shape: the Console needs a stable code + a user-safe message. Please avoid leaking metric internals (prompt ids, raw examples) in the error payload.

Jordan Lee (author): Updated. Error payload now includes: reason_code, summary_message, gate_run_id, gate_status, failing_metrics=[{metric_name, delta, threshold}] and console_url. No prompt ids, no raw artifacts. Full details remain behind gate run artifacts.

Benji Okafor (review): Where does policy come from? I see OptimizePolicy.requiresQualityGate() defaulting to true for “Optimize-generated” diffs but false for “manual”. That seems risky.

Jordan Lee (author): Good catch. I removed the manual/optimize heuristic. Policy lookup is now route-scoped with a fallback default. In this PR fallback is conservative for production routes: requires gate unless explicitly allowlisted (staging/internal). Per-route configurability lands in pr-19588; here we use the existing policy bundle with a temporary default.

Yara Haddad (review): Can we make the 409 errors retryable? Our recommender pipeline will hammer apply if it doesn’t know it’s a transient PENDING.

Jordan Lee (author): Added retry_after_seconds on QUALITY_GATE_PENDING and set an explicit “is_retryable: true”. QUALITY_GATE_FAILED is “is_retryable: false” unless a new gate is run.

Marcus Lin (review): Please add an audit-friendly log event when apply is blocked (who attempted, route, gate_run_id, reason_code). Also ensure the event doesn’t include request payloads.

Jordan Lee (author): Added structured log optimize.apply.blocked_by_quality_gate with actor_id, account_id, route_id, gate_run_id, reason_code, and request_id only.

CI note: First integration run failed due to a test assuming 400 for pending gates; updated to 409 and added retry_after_seconds assertion. Re-run passed.

Final: Approved (Noah, Chloe, Marcus).
Optimize: Applying a cost optimization config now enforces quality gate outcomes. Applies will be blocked if the gate is pending/failed, and the API returns explicit failure reasons plus a link to gate run results for debugging.
payload.title: Block Optimize config apply when quality gate fails + surface failure reasons

Motivation: reduce repetitive session handshake and streaming boilerplate across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs while giving consumers an ergonomic generator/streaming experience. This change introduces a lightweight session signal adaptor concept and idiomatic wrappers for each SDK plus a compact shared retry preset to make streaming auth/retries predictable and tunable. The adaptor surfaces heartbeat, reauth_hint, chunk, and end signals so users can handle token rotation and graceful shutdown without erroring the stream by default. Changes include language native shims, tests, docs, and synchronized package version bumps for downstream stability.

Motivation: new customers frequently hit suboptimal unit economics when they first start using Redwood due to conservative defaults for batching, caching and quantization. This PR introduces a tenant-focused 'Prefill Advisor' that provides safe, telemetry-backed onboarding defaults and a lightweight dry-run evaluator so we can suggest tenant-specific batch/cache/qprofile presets from day one without risking latency SLOs.

What this PR does (single-line description): implements advisor service, CLI dry-run mode, console suggestions UI hook, and runtime safeguards for suggested defaults.

Key pieces: 1) advisor service that ingests short tenant workload profiles and returns ranked presets (batch shape, cache TTL, kv-prefill window, quant profile) with confidence scores and rollback safety metadata; 2) a dry-run simulator that runs in the control plane to estimate unit-econ delta and P95 latency impact for a given preset; 3) Console integration endpoints to surface suggestions under "Onboarding -> Cost suggestions"; 4) a safe-apply flow that only enables presets in shaded canary for 5% of traffic and auto-rolls back on latency regressions; 5) telemetry hooks and new telemetry views for us to evaluate real-world impact.

Checklist: 
- [x] Advisor core algorithm and schema (proto + validation)
- [x] Dry-run simulator with synthetic warmup and KV-cache model
- [x] Console endpoint and minimal UI payload (front-end wired as placeholder)
- [x] CLI "redwood prefill --dry-run" command and --apply-safe flag
- [x] Unit, integration and e2e smoke tests for core flows
- [x] Telemetry metrics and dashboards (telemetry IDs included)
- [x] Migration doc and runbook for SRE to manage safe apply

Safety notes: the advisor never auto-applies a preset to >5% traffic by default. All applied presets include a revert TTL and automatic latency/regression guardrails (P95 increase > 15ms triggers revert). See docs/runbooks/prefill-advisor.md for operational details.

Performance/telemetry: early synthetic runs show median token-cost reduction 8-14% for onboarding workloads with no measurable P99 regressions in our mini-benchmark harness. Workload sampling and anonymization are applied; no customer prompt text is stored.

Related tickets: ENG-1842 (prefill advisor design), SUP-4123 (customer reported onboarding cost spike).

Migration / rollout plan: feature gating via feature flag "prefill.advisor". We will start with internal tenants + 3 pilot customers, ramp to general availability over 4 weeks with daily telemetry review and rollback windows.
Arjun Kapoor: Nice direction — I like the conservative default flow. Two main asks: 1) prove the dry-run estimator under a few bursty workloads (simulate 1k rps/tenant) and 2) ensure the kv-cache TTL proposals don't step on existing tenant cache policies.
Samantha Chen (author): Added a synthetic burst scenario to the simulator and a TTL-compatibility check that marks presets 'incompatible' if tenant policy restricts cache TTL. See commit b3d9f14.
Liam O'Connor: Can we add an integration test that exercises safe-apply -> revert path? We had an incident last quarter where revert didn't fully remove the batch-shape change.
Samantha Chen: Added integration smoke test tests/integration/prefill_dryrun_smoke_test.py and an extra cleanup hook in runtime/guards/prefill_safe_apply.go. Tests included in CI.
Marisol Vega: Security question: advisor collects short workload fingerprints — please confirm no PII or text is persisted. Recommend an extra audit log entry when a preset is applied for a tenant.
Samantha Chen: Confirmed: only histogram/sketch metrics and length/shape metadata stored. Added audit log write on safe-apply and documented retention in runbook. See docs/runbooks/prefill-advisor.md.

Context: During the Feb 14 incident response, multiple Console dashboards (Saturation Overview + Routing/Fallback drilldowns) slowed to a crawl and some alerts stopped evaluating on time. The root cause was a time series explosion on routing/fallback metrics after we started emitting per-request fallback detail labels in the serving/control-plane pipeline. Those labels included values that are effectively unbounded (e.g., fallback_target_model, fallback_reason_detail, source_pool_id, and an occasionally-unique route_override_id). On busy regions this pushed cardinality high enough to cause query latency spikes and ingestion pressure.

This PR is a hotfix to immediately bound metric cardinality without losing the ability to answer the question responders actually need: "Are we falling back? Where? And is it capacity-driven or policy-driven?".

Changes: 1) Remove unbounded labels from fallback metrics: dropped fallback_target_model, route_override_id, source_pool_id, and fallback_reason_detail from the primary counters and histograms. 2) Introduce a bounded fallback_class label (enum): {"none", "capacity", "policy", "compat", "error"} derived from existing routing decision fields. 3) Keep a single low-cardinality fallback_to_family label for coarse attribution (e.g., "llama", "mistral", "other"), only when fallback_class != "none". 4) Add guardrails in the metrics emitter: hard cap on allowed label keys for fallback metrics; if additional keys are attempted, they are ignored and a single internal counter routing_metrics_label_drop_total{metric="fallback"} is incremented. 5) Update dashboard queries to use fallback_class + region + service rather than fallback_target_model.

Why this is safe: This is limited to internal metrics emission and dashboard wiring; the routing behavior is unchanged. The only behavior change is which labels are exported. Existing alerts that depended on fallback_target_model will need to be updated (included in this PR for the standard pack). We validated the new time series counts in staging (peak QPS replay) and saw >95% reduction in series for fallback metrics.

Rollout/ops: - This should be deployed ASAP to production control-plane + metrics sidecars. - If responders need deep attribution (exact fallback target), they should use traces/logs for now; we still log full routing decisions with sampling and will follow up with a safe aggregated view.

Follow-ups (not in this hotfix): - Re-introduce richer attribution via logs-to-metrics aggregation (bounded) or exemplars. - Add automated cardinality budget tests in CI for metrics PRs touching routing tags. - Align incident-bot cards to use fallback_class instead of target-model labels.

Testing: - Unit tests for label allowlist + fallback_class mapping. - Local prom scrape sanity test. - Staging load replay (notes in comment).

Incident reference: internal thread "telemetry query latency spike during incident" and the hotfix request from SRE to unbreak dashboards/alerts quickly.
Logan Wright (review): Can you confirm which labels were the major contributors? Also want to ensure we still have a way to correlate capacity-driven fallback vs policy-driven. Nadia Rahman (author): Biggest offenders were fallback_target_model + route_override_id; combined they were effectively unbounded due to per-tenant overrides and experimentation. Added fallback_class so on-call can still bucket by cause. Full detail remains in routing decision logs/traces.

Allison Grant (review): Please update the alert queries in observability-pack to stop grouping by fallback_target_model; otherwise we’ll silently page-break. Also add a comment in the metric definition about cardinality budget. Nadia Rahman: Updated standard alerts/dashboards in this PR and added a doc note + emitter allowlist.

Mina Haddad (review): Concern: fallback_to_family could still be high if we ever include fine-grained families. Is that list bounded somewhere? Nadia Rahman: Yes—implemented as a fixed mapping for current catalog families with default "other"; no dynamic model string. Unit test included.

Aisha Bello (review): Any risk that changing labels will break existing SLO burn dashboards? Nadia Rahman: SLO dashboards use request_success/latency series, not fallback series. Only routing/fallback dashboards were impacted; updated here.

CI: first run failed due to jsonnet formatting (dashboards). Re-ran after fixing. Final checks green.

Approval: 4 approvals. Merged via squash. Deployment note added for on-call to prioritize shipping to prod today.
payload.title: Hotfix: reduce metrics cardinality from fallback routing labels

Motivation:
We see a recurring pattern where SRE and oncall engineers spend time hunting long-tail incidents that are noisy because traces lack compact contextual anchors. Full log payloads increase cardinality in downstream indices and make alert grouping brittle. This PR introduces a compact, path-aware context anchor service that produces bloom-filter based context summaries (compact anchors) for invocations and attaches them to traces, metrics, and synthetic telemetry. The anchors enable lightweight contextual joins in dashboards and reduce alert noise by enabling fuzzy grouping and de-duplication.

What this PR does (high-level):
- New component: observability-context-bridge (Go microservice) that consumes span events, generates a 128-bit bloom-ish anchor and a short context digest (max 128 bytes) using deterministic keying of sanitized prompt tokens and route path.
- Runtime: a small sidecar integration for the serving runtime to emit context-hash headers; fallbacks to async enrichment when sidecar is disabled.
- Telemetry: Metrics for anchor generation latency, anchor collision rate estimate, enrichment success ratio, and index join hit-rate.
- Tracing: span attribute rwd.context_anchor added; sampled span enrichment joins now use anchor predicates to backfill logs without pushing whole request payloads.
- Dashboards: new dashboard panels (Context Anchor Heatmap, Anchor Collision Trend, Alert-Group Stabilization) plus a compact sparkline for per-route anchor join success.
- Alerts: an adaptive alert curator that uses anchor join fidelity and group stability to de-duplicate noisy alerts; tunable knobs in the Console.

Why bloom-ish anchors?
- Compact: small footprint in traces/metrics and indexes.
- Probabilistic joins are acceptable for our use-case (we only need high-precision low-cost joins for debugging).
- Deterministic keying across service boundaries enables cross-stage correlation without shipping PII.

Backward compatibility and privacy:
- Anchors are deterministic hashes computed over sanitized token fingerprints and route metadata; no raw prompt or PII is stored or transmitted.
- Feature is opt-in per-tenant and disabled by default for Private installs.
- When disabled, spans still carry a minimal flag so the backend can attempt async enrichment if available.

Testing and CI:

- CI: full test matrix passed on Go 1.21 and 1.22; lint fixed.

Review conversation (summary):

Priya Natarajan (2025-11-10): Please add a helm values flag and mention Private deployment constraints; also include a migration note for customers that have strict index budgets.

payload.body:
Summary: Introduce a dynamic credit-based backpressure mechanism for streaming connections plus an inline KV prefetcher that reduces first-token and p99 tail latency for common prefixes.

Motivation: We observed intermittent p99 spikes on hosted streaming when a few connections generated long sequences causing kernel queues and KV miss penalties to cascade. Fixed window throttles (tokens-per-interval) are too coarse and either add latency or drop throughput.

Design: Replace the global fixed flush windows with a per-stream credit allocator. Each active stream receives credits proportional to an adaptive budget computed from: kernel queue length, recent token service time, and observed KV hit-rate. Credits are consumed per-token generation; when credits are low we request rapid async refill or apply lightweight pacing. To address cold-start KV misses, the inline KV prefetcher tracks hot prefixes at scheduler time and performs a non-blocking prefetch into the local KV cache prior to first-token generation for predicted prefixes.

Key behaviors:
- Credit allocator is in runtime/streaming/credit_scheduler.* and exposes a small API for stream_controller to request credits; it uses EWMA of service times and a configurable headroom factor.
- Prefetcher lives in runtime/kv and exposes `prefetch_for_prefix(stream_id, prefix_hash)`; it's non-blocking and has a bounded concurrency counter to avoid overloading the KV backend.
- Scheduler hook (policy_hooks.h) uses kernel queue depth metric to temporarily boost credits for latency-sensitive streams and deprioritize long-batch microjobs.
- Fallbacks: if prefetch fails or KV hit-rate is low, streams fall back to existing async KV fetch path; if credit allocator is disabled via config, behavior reverts to previous fixed-window flush cadence.

Commits & changes: See commits array for high-level commit summary. Files changed include new credit scheduler, inline prefetcher, tests, perf harness, and a small kernel pacing patch to smoother enqueue bursts.

Performance results (bench/perf_stream_latency.py):
- In our internal benchmark with mixed short-chat and long-generation workloads: median first-token latency improved ~18%, p95 improved ~30%, p99 improved ~42% on hosts with heavy contention.
- On dedicated hardware (no KV network), improvements were smaller for median but p99 still ~25% due to reduced kernel queue amplification.

Tests: added unit tests for credit math and concurrency invariants, integration tests for prefetcher correctness and end-to-end perf harness.

CI: initial CI run failed due to a flaky test `credit_model_test::handles_underflow` on macOS builders; fixed by tightening timer stubbing and re-ran CI.

Review discussion (summary):
- Rafiq: asked for observability (per-stream credit metrics, prefetch success/failure counters). Author: added metrics and tracing spans, documented in docs/notes/streaming_credit_design.md.
- Sofia: requested safe opt-out and config knobs for enterprise/private (we added `streaming.credit_allocator.enabled=false` and `kv.inline_prefetch.enabled=false`).
- Theo: flagged potential for KV overfetch at scale; we added bounded concurrent prefetch counters and backoff policy.
- Also discussed how this interacts with existing prefix/KV caching; we added explicit compatibility notes.

Backwards compatibility and rollout: feature is behind two config flags and gateable via rollout service in Redwood Console. Default rollout set to 20% of hosted traffic for 72h with aggressive monitoring (token latency, kernel queue depth, KV QPS).

Release notes: "Streaming: dynamic credit-based backpressure and inline KV prefetch to cut first-byte and p99 token latencies; gated rollout and config tunables."

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: prefetcher could increase KV QPS; mitigation: bounded concurrency and adaptive backoff, and monitored dashboards added.
- Risk: mis-calibrated credits causing starvation; mitigation: headroom defaults conservative and circuit-breaker to revert to fixed window.

Follow-ups:
- Tweak EWMA windows and headroom after 72h ramp (ENG-3229).
- Expand prefetcher heuristics to include recent user prompts and telemetry-driven hot-prefix mining.
- Evaluate moving credit allocator to a centralized heuristic service for cross-host coordination.

Merge: Squash-merged after approvals and green CI.

JIRA/SUPPORT: linked SUP-4421 for customer reports that motivated part of this work.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps algorithm parameters configurable and instruments new metrics to allow iterative tuning in production. Change log and docs updated.

payload.body:
Motivation: We need a low-risk way to change tenant RBAC/KMS mappings and residency constraints without surprising production behavior. This PR delivers three coordinated components: (1) kms-usage-evaluator: daily/adhoc job that attributes KMS calls to tenants, operators, and routes; (2) policy-simulator: a local/CI tool to simulate proposed RBAC v2 policy edits against historical auth events to estimate denial rates and KMS call deltas; (3) audit-reconciler: a reconciler to backfill and canonicalize audit entries when policy migrations cause reattachment of KMS claims. The single-string description below covers design, usage, tests, and rollout checklist.
Design summary: kms-usage-evaluator computes tenant-level KMS metrics (calls, key-ids used, average latency, region affinity) and writes a time-bucketed report to /metrics/kms_tenant_usage/{tenant}/{yyyy-mm-dd}. policy-simulator consumes a policy diff (yaml) and a historical auth event sample (ndjson) and produces a scored report: predicted_denials, predicted_kms_delta_percent, affected_routes, confidence_score. audit-reconciler consumes evaluator output + simulator plan and replays canonical audit envelopes for a configured window to ensure downstream compliance systems see consistent KMS provenance after a migration.
Usage examples:
- Run a local simulation: ./tools/policy-sim --policy-proposed example/policy-proposed.yaml --events sample/events-2025-01-*.ndjson --out report.json
- Inspect tenant KMS usage for tenant-42: ./bin/kms-eval query --tenant tenant-42 --start 2025-01-01 --end 2025-01-31
- Backfill audits for tenant-42 after migration: ./bin/audit-reconcile apply --tenant tenant-42 --window 2025-01-01:2025-01-15
Key constraints & safety: reads-only by default; audit-reconciler has a dry-run mode and requires explicit allowlist for mutate mode (ENV: AUDIT_RECONCILE_ALLOWLIST). The reconciler signs generated audit envelopes with a rotated reconciliation key and emits reconciliation metrics to metrics/reconciler/{tenant}.
Checklist:
- [x] design doc linked (ENG-1976)
- [x] unit + integration tests
- [x] end-to-end dry-run against staging (ran 2025-01-24)
- [x] security review by SEC (Renee)
- [x] migration playbook added in docs/tools/policy-sim/README.md
Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main (feature flags off).
2) Run kms-usage-evaluator in observation mode for 2 weeks, compare with existing KMS telemetry.
3) Run policy-simulator for upcoming RBAC changes before scheduling enforce window.
4) Execute audit-reconciler in dry-run for target tenants, review reconciliation diff, then enable apply for small cohort.
5) Gradual ramp to 100% tenants; monitor reconciler.errors and kms.tenants.delta metrics.
Testing: Added unit tests for evaluator aggregation logic (edge-case: multi-key per-request), simulator fidelity tests (sample dataset with injected denies), reconciler idempotency tests. CI: policy-scan, unit, integration, e2e-staging run; addressed flaky step in e2e by adding a retry backoff.
Migration notes: This PR includes a small migration that adds two DB tables (kms_tenant_usage and audit_reconcile_jobs). Migration adds an index on (tenant_id, date) and is reversible. Rollback plan: disable reconciler apply, delete reconciliation jobs created by the job-runner, and run compensating audit canonicalizer.
Logging and observability: new dashboards added at Observability -> Security -> KMS Usage; reconciler exposes reconciliation.duration, reconciliation.applied_count, reconciliation.dryrun_diff_count, simulator.predicted_denial_rate histograms.
Security review summary: threat model considered malicious operator spoofing KMS key IDS in events; evaluator cross-checks with signed KMS response headers and drops suspicious events, flagged to security. The reconciler signs backfilled audits with reconciliation-key and tags metadata.reconciled_by = "reconciler/v1".
Related work: builds on ENG-1452 (policy dry-run infra) and leverages the existing audit-envelope format introduced in PR pr-73199.
Migration controls: policy-simulator has a confidence threshold (default 0.75) before recommending enforcement; teams must opt into lower thresholds.
Documentation: docs/tools/policy-sim/README.md and docs/ops/audit-reconcile-playbook.md included in the change set. This description string is intentionally compact and single-block for PR metadata export.
Markus: Could the simulator be expensive on large event sets? Aisha: We included sampling and a streaming estimator; default sample rate is 0.1 but configurable. Renee: I reviewed the threat model; we need to make reconciler-key rotation explicit in docs. Aisha: Added rotation docs and config (docs/ops/audit-reconcile-playbook.md). Samir: Please add an integration test that verifies reconciliation is idempotent. Aisha: Added idempotency test and a second run condition in reconciler. Markus: Approving after tests green. Renee: Security approve. Merge-by: squash. Post-merge: schedule observation run for the evaluator on staging.
Added a tenant-level KMS usage evaluator, a policy simulator to estimate RBAC/KMS impact before policy changes, and an audit reconciler to backfill canonical audit envelopes post-migration. Includes DB migrations, dashboards, and operator playbook. No breaking changes when feature flags off.
Unit + integration + e2e staging dry-run. Run evaluator in observation mode for two weeks, verify metrics parity, then run reconciler dry-run for pilot tenants and validate diffs with compliance before enabling apply.
Disable reconciler apply, remove reconciliation jobs, and run compensating canonicalizer to restore audit view. DB migrations are reversible via the included down migration.
Evaluator adds a daily aggregation job (CPU + IO). Policy-simulator is offline/CI only. Reconciler apply can be rate-limited; default rate is 10 reconciles/min per worker. Expected steady-state RPS impact: negligible when feature off.
Security reviewed by Renee Alvarez; concerns addressed include signed KMS response validation, reconciler signing, allowlist for apply mode, and key rotation docs. SEC sign-off obtained 2025-01-28.
Ops: enable feature flag 'kms_eval_enabled' in staging, set AUDIT_RECONCILE_ALLOWLIST for pilot tenants, monitor metrics security.reconciler.errors and security.kms.tenant_delta. Follow playbook in docs/ops/audit-reconcile-playbook.md for apply.
