payload.body:
Context: Under TP load, we’ve had multiple incidents/support escalations where replicas wedge in a NCCL collective (or watchdog aborts the step), but the request surfaces upstream as a generic deadline exceeded / internal error. That prevents (a) smart routing/fallback from kicking in quickly, (b) customers from getting actionable diagnostics, and (c) on-call from correlating API timeouts to a specific NCCL failure mode. This PR wires the runtime’s NCCL/TP failure signals (including watchdog-triggered aborts) through the internal RPC boundary to the API layer and normalizes them into stable error codes + routing hints.

What changed: 1) Introduced stable RuntimeErrorCode values for TP/NCCL failure modes (kept intentionally small + versionable): RWD_TP_NCCL_TIMEOUT, RWD_TP_NCCL_ABORTED, RWD_TP_NCCL_COLLECTIVE_MISMATCH, RWD_TP_NCCL_UNHANDLED, RWD_TP_REPLICA_DRAINED. 2) Runtime now captures NCCL failures at the comms boundary and wraps them as a typed RuntimeError (instead of a generic Status::Internal) with safe context fields: tp_rank, tp_world_size, collective_seq (monotonic), last_collective (enum), watchdog_fired (bool), and a redacted nccl_error_string (guarded behind existing debug flag; default off in Hosted). 3) API gateway maps RuntimeErrorCode -> customer error response with consistent shape and HTTP status: - Timeout/Abort/Mismatch: HTTP 503 (service unavailable) with error.type="runtime_stall" and error.code set to the stable code. - Replica drained: HTTP 503 with error.type="replica_unavailable" and retry_after_ms populated when known. 4) Added RoutingHint to internal response metadata: retryable (bool), fallback_allowed (bool), and preferred_action (RETRY_SAME_MODEL | FALLBACK_COMPAT_MODEL | REROUTE_REGION). Initial policy: NCCL_TIMEOUT / NCCL_ABORTED => retryable=true, fallback_allowed=true; COLLECTIVE_MISMATCH => retryable=false (to avoid hot-looping) but fallback_allowed=true; REPLICA_DRAINED => retryable=true. 5) Streaming path: ensure we terminate the stream with the structured error payload (previously some paths hung until client timeout when the backend died mid-stream). We now emit a final error frame and close the stream.

Why this is safe: - Codes are derived from a narrow set of runtime conditions we already detect (NCCL error return, watchdog abort reason). - Context fields are intentionally limited and do not include prompts/outputs; rank/world_size/collective sequence are non-sensitive. - Customer-visible strings are generic; detailed NCCL strings remain behind the existing diagnostic flag and are intended for controlled canary windows (see INT-2219).

Illustrative payload: {"error": {"type": "runtime_stall", "code": "RWD_TP_NCCL_ABORTED", "message": "Tensor-parallel execution aborted due to a stalled collective.", "retryable": true, "fallback_allowed": true, "request_id": "..."}}

Files/areas touched (high level): - runtime/comms/nccl_wrapper.*: map NCCL return values + watchdog abort reason -> RuntimeErrorCode - runtime/tp/executor.*: plumb typed errors through TP step boundaries (prefill/decode) - rpc/runtime_service.proto + generated clients: add RuntimeError + RoutingHint to response envelope - gateway/api_error_mapping.*: normalize to customer payload + http status - streaming/bridge.*: ensure mid-stream backend failure yields a final structured error frame - tracing/spans.*: attach error.code and (when debug enabled) tp_rank/collective_seq tags

Test plan: - Unit tests: mapping coverage for NCCL errors and watchdog abort reasons; API error mapping snapshot tests. - Integration tests: simulated NCCL abort injected in TP executor -> API response contains RWD_TP_NCCL_ABORTED and retryable=true; streaming test verifies final error frame and stream closure. - Manual: ran benchmark-lab repro harness (mixed prefill/decode) with injected abort path; confirmed Dedicated canary correctly falls back to compatible single-GPU model when enabled.

Rollout notes: - No behavior change unless a NCCL/TP failure occurs; normal success path unaffected. - RoutingHint consumption is gated behind an existing runtime routing feature flag (on for Dedicated canary only per ENG-4829). - Follow-up: dashboard/alerts will key off these codes (tracked in observability pack PR-412).

Checklist: - [x] Added stable error codes and docs in code comments - [x] Ensured no customer payload includes sensitive model inputs/outputs - [x] Added tests for streaming + non-streaming - [x] Validated with SRE (paging/alertability) and Support (actionable customer messaging)

Links: Linear ENG-4826 (watchdog), ENG-4825 (NCCL hardening), ENG-4823 (instrumentation), Support SUP-48377. Incident context: 2025-02-17 Sev1 (TP decode hang).
- Runtime now maps NCCL abort/timeout/stall conditions to stable, customer-visible error codes.
- API layer emits structured error payloads with routing hints (retryable/fallbackable) instead of generic 500/timeout.
- Traces/logs include rank + collective context when safe, improving support diagnostics for TP stalls.
Hiro Tanaka: Can we ensure COLLECTIVE_MISMATCH never retries on the same replica? We’ve seen this hot-loop when ranks diverge. Omar El-Sayed: Good call—set retryable=false for COLLECTIVE_MISMATCH and include preferred_action=FALLBACK_COMPAT_MODEL. Added unit test and updated mapping.

Sofia Ivanova: Does adding RoutingHint change any scheduling behavior? Omar: No—purely metadata in the response envelope. Consumption is behind the routing flag in the gateway and only used when a request fails.

Rafael Mendes: Please confirm we’re not leaking NCCL debug strings to customers by default. Omar: Confirmed. nccl_error_string is redacted unless runtime.debug.nccl_strings_enabled is true; gateway does not serialize it into customer payload at all. Added explicit test asserting absence.

Allison Grant: Can we attach error.code to spans for correlation? Omar: Added error.code tag to request span and (when enabled) tp_rank/collective_seq tags. Kept rank tags behind the same debug flag to avoid cardinality surprises.

Rafael Mendes: Approving with note: follow up to update runbook to reference these codes. Omar: Ack—will coordinate with runbook owner; tracking via ENG-4829 checklist.

Summary: Introduces a staged handover protocol and controller improvements to support deferred canary activations and a surge-fallback routing mode. This PR enables a handover window where: (1) a canary is created but traffic is not immediately shifted; (2) observational checks run on mirrored traffic; (3) on explicit handover the controller performs a coordinated swap with a graceful ramp; (4) if capacity pressure or latency regressions are detected, traffic is routed to pre-configured surge variants until remediation. Motivation: Customers asked for a way to perform canaries that collect live shadow metrics before affecting production traffic and to have a predictable fallback path when capacity or latency regressions happen during rollouts (see ENG-1987). Key changes: new CRD fields for RolloutSpec.stagedHandover (graceWindowSeconds, deferredActivation, surgeVariants, maxSurgePct), a handoff protocol implemented in controllers/handover/handshake.go, a surge-aware router in scheduler/surge_router.go, updates to the simulation harness and integration test cases. Checklist: - [x] API: CRD + validation - [x] Controller: staged handover state machine + leader election guards - [x] Router: surge fallback path and capacity probing - [x] Tests: unit tests for state transitions, integration tests exercising deferred activation and surge fallback - [x] Docs: rollout CRD examples and console doc strings - [x] Migration notes and compatibility checks Behavior notes: - Deferred canary: when deferredActivation=true, controller will create the canary ReplicaSet and mirror traffic but will not increase live traffic until an explicit Handover event (via API or Linear-triggered automation). - Handover arbitration: a three-way handshake ensures only one controller instance completes the final swap (prevents split-brain). - Surge fallback: on sustained latency regressions or soft OOM/queue pressure the scheduler will divert a configurable percentage of traffic to a higher-capacity variant or a pre-warmed fallback pool. - Observability: emits rollout.handover.* and scheduler.surge.* metrics; exposes handover.trace_id in traces. Backwards compatibility: CRD fields are additive and default to conservative behavior (deferredActivation=false, maxSurgePct=0). Migration: existing rollouts unaffected until customers opt-in. Rollout runbooks updated in docs/rollouts/staged-handover.md.
Arjun Patel (2026-02-20): Overall approach LGTM. One open question: should we expose a health-check window separate from graceWindowSeconds? Concern about noisy metrics during cold starts.
Maya Chen (2026-02-21): Reply: added healthProbeWindowSeconds with conservative default (30s) and a note in the CRD docs; updated validation to ensure healthProbeWindow <= graceWindowSeconds.
Sofia Martinez (2026-02-24): Request changes: tighten leader election guard and add a unit test for race where two controllers attempt handover concurrently.
Maya Chen (2026-02-25): Addressed: added leader token handshake and unit test in handshake_test.go. Also added logs for transition reasons.
Liam O'Neill (2026-02-27): Approved pending CI. Verified integration test run locally with a small cluster and observed expected metrics emitted.

Motivation: tenant workloads vary widely and static defaults for batching, prefill/caching, and quantization cause either excessive cost or regressions in output quality. This PR ships a runtime 'batch crawler' that continuously samples tenant request shapes and synthesizes conservative batch/cache/quant profiles; it also introduces a short-circuit "quant rollback" mechanism to automatically relax aggressive quantization when quality or eval signals deteriorate. High-level summary: 1) crawler service that samples traffic, builds workload histograms and candidate batch shapes; 2) policy engine that proposes tenant-level defaults (microbatch size, prefill window, cache TTL, quant profile) and exposes them as opt-in staged rollouts; 3) quant rollback controller that watches quality signals (loss spikes, eval regression, exemplar divergence) and swaps back to safer quant tiers for affected routes; 4) telemetry changes to emit prefill hit/miss histograms, per-prefill unit-econ metrics, quant stability score, and audit events for automatic rollbacks; 5) safe guards: cooldowns, rate-limited changes, tenant isolation and canary rollout mode. Checklist: [x] unit tests for crawler sampling logic; [x] integration test harness simulating tenant workload shapes; [x] metrics and dashboards wired to observability; [x] docs and runbook for operators; [x] feature flag and canary rollout. Rollout plan: enable crawler in dry-run per-tenant for 1 week, then pilot on 5 low-latency tenants; observe unit-econ delta and quality regressions for two weeks before broad opt-in. Backwards compatibility: defaults are only suggested until tenant accepts or rollout is global; rollback is automatic and conservative. Related: ENG-2245 for crawler design, ENG-2298 for quant rollback heuristics. Impact: expected 6-12% token cost reduction for sampled pilot tenants without measurable end-user quality degradation in pilot. Monitoring: new alerts on quant stability falling below thresholds and rollback rate spikes.
Arjun Patel: Requested more explicit metric names and a histogram bucket review for prefill latency; suggested making the crawler sampling window configurable per-tenant. Author response: adjusted metric names to prefex 'econ_' and added tenant_window configuration with sane defaults, pushed new commit b6f4e90. Leah Soto: Asked to add guardrail that prevents quant rollback from happening more than once per 10 minutes per route; asked for a small e2e demonstrating rollback under a synthetic quality drop. Author response: added cooldown logic to quant_rollback controller and an e2e test that flips an eval signal; pushed commit ef4b221. Diego Morales: Concerned about persistence schema for workload histograms at scale; requested retention strategy and compaction. Author response: added compaction policy and TTL configuration, documented expected storage growth; Diego approved after verifying compaction unit tests. Final status: two approvals and CI green, ready to merge.
Unit tests cover histogram aggregation, candidate profile selection, and rollback cooldown logic. Integration harness simulates variable sequence-length traffic and verifies recommended batch shapes reduce avg token cost in dry-run mode by ~9% in synthetic workloads. Added e2e that triggers rollback via synthetic eval regression and verifies safe fallback within configured cooldown. Load tests show crawler overhead <1% p95 latency impact when sampling at configured default rate.
Feature flag: econ.autonomize.enabled default false. Helm value: econ.autonomize.sample_rate (default 0.02) and cooldown_ms for rollback (default 600000). Recommended pilot steps and dashboard links documented in runbook. If rollback rate exceeds 5% of routes in pilot, disable auto-apply and investigate via quant_stability metric.
Introduce an opt-in runtimes feature: 'Autonomize batch crawler' to recommend tenant-level batching/caching/quant defaults and an automatic quant rollback controller that reverts aggressive quant profiles on detected quality regressions. Includes telemetry and dashboards. Rollout gated behind feature-flag and tenant opt-in.

Introduces a regional spillover admission gateway and an SLO Anticipator that proactively reserves token budgets and warms KV cache. Improves regional failover smoothness and reduces noisy circuit flips. No customer-facing API changes.
Context: During a recent multi-region pressure incident we observed fast cascade failovers when a region hit transient GPU KV pressure. Root causes included bursty egress and late detection of SLO drift, which triggered aggressive circuit flips and mass tenant rebalancing. This PR implements two orthogonal mitigations: a lightweight Spillover Gateway that provides controlled regional spill routing, and an SLO Anticipator that uses short-window telemetry to preemptively apply smoothing actions. Motivation: Reduce noisy circuit transitions, keep hot KV cached where possible, and avoid wholesale tenant migrations that amplify load spikes. Goals: 1) Provide a low-latency path to route overflow requests to neighboring regions when local SLOs are at risk, honoring tenant affinity and KV preservation heuristics. 2) Predict imminent SLO violations (latency and error rate) with a short look-ahead model and trigger token-budget reservation, prefetch of KV prefixes, and adaptive batch relaxation. 3) Keep behavioral controls per-tenant and per-route so enterprise customers can opt-in to spillover or pin to local-only behavior. Summary of changes: - runtime/spillover/gateway.go: new Spillover Gateway component that exposes an internal route decision API and integrates with the smart routing layer. Adds circuit-aware pacing and KV-preserve hint headers. - routing/policy/spillover_policy.yaml: default policy config (region adjacency weights, per-tenant opt-in, max spill ratio). - telemetry/anticipator/service.py: lightweight anticipator service (stateless window aggregator + simple exponential smoothing model) and a REST hook to the control plane. - runtime/kv/prefetch_manager.go: prefetch hot prefixes on anticipator signal and hold a short-lived soft lock to reduce cold-KV penalties. - orchestration/helm/spillover-values.yaml: gating flags and tunables for Dedicated/Private installs. - tests/integration/spillover_e2e_test.go: deterministic e2e that simulates KV pressure and verifies no noisy mass failovers. - docs/ops/spillover.md: operational runbook, thresholds, and rollback steps. Commits: ["init: implement gateway skeleton and route decision API", "feat(anticipator): add short-window SLO predictor and REST hook", "feat(kv): prefetch manager and soft-lock semantics", "ops: add helm values and runbook", "test: add integration e2e for spillover scenario", "ci: fix flakey e2e by increasing synthetic timing slack"]. Review conversation highlights: ["Evan: 'Can we ensure spill routing preserves KV affinity for active sessions? Add tests to validate sticky KV behavior.'", "Author (Maya): 'Added soft-lock semantics to prefetch manager and extended e2e to validate sticky KV under spillover.'", "Priya: 'Anticipator thresholds look aggressive in staging — can we expose a conservative default and an auto-tune flag?'", "Author: 'Added tunable \"anticipator.sensitivity\" with conservative default and documented auto-tune behavior; added telemetry hook for feedback loop.'", "Lucas: 'Concerns around inter-region cost — ensure we respect per-tenant egress caps and have clear opt-out.'", "Author: 'Policy includes max_spill_ratio and tenant opt-out; helm values expose egress budget guardrails.'", "Priya (after fixes): 'LGTM — recommend squash merge after a final CI run.'", "Evan: 'approved'"] CI summary: ["unit-tests: pass", "integration-tests/spillover-e2e: flakey on first run (timeout), re-run fixed; pass", "lint: pass", "security-scan: pass", "canary-deploy-preview: pass"]. Post-merge notes: Merged via squash on main; changelog entry added. No rollback required during canary. Post-merge actions: monitor anticipator firing rate and per-tenant spill ratio in the next 48h; watch metrics spelling: regional.spill.count, anticipator.fired, kv.prefetch.hit_rate.

Context: Customers and SDKs reported intermittent JSON parse errors and duplicate function-call events when using the OpenAI-compat streaming endpoint across unstable networks. Root cause analysis showed three related issues: (1) event delimiter heuristics relied on a strict "double-newline" boundary which could be split across TCP/chunk boundaries, producing empty events or merged tokens; (2) function-call/structured-output sentinels (short special markers inside data fields) could be cut mid-token and then re-emitted in a subsequent SSE event, resulting in partial JSON fragments that the client attempted to parse prematurely; (3) older clients that relied solely on delimiter-based reassembly made unsafe assumptions about event atomicity. Solution summary: introduce a compact stream-sentinel header and sequence scheme in the SSE event meta that is backwards-compatible and adds deterministic reassembly at the compatibility layer. Each SSE event now includes a small ASCII header line: "X-RW-SEQ:<seq_id>|<frag_index>|<total_frags>|<crc8>" (when fragmentation is possible). The compatibility layer uses these headers to: (a) buffer and reassemble partial data by seq_id, honoring frag_index ordering; (b) validate fragment integrity via crc8 and drop/mark corrupted fragments; (c) emit only fully reconstructed, canonical events to downstream SDKs; (d) preserve legacy delimiter behavior when header is absent so older clients continue to work. Implementation details: - Added stream-sentinel encoder/decoder in the compatibility proxy (pkg/sse/sentinel.go). The decoder maintains a small in-memory window keyed by seq_id and uses frag_index to detect reordering; out-of-window fragments are marked and logged. - For untrusted/large streams we cap reassembly buffer to 128kb per seq_id and a max 64 concurrently open seq_ids to bound memory. - Added crc8 checks for quick corruption detection; on mismatch the fragment is dropped and a lightweight diagnostic event is emitted (internal only). - Fixed edge-case where a trailing delimiter at chunk boundary created a zero-length event: explicit suppression for zero-length data unless a header indicates a true zero-length fragment. - Ensured that function-call sentinels are always reassembled before JSON parsing and added stricter parsing at the boundary for structured output to avoid early parse attempts. Testing and validation: - Unit tests for sentinel encoding/decoding and crc mismatches (tests/sse/sentinel_test.go). - Integration tests that replay recorded faulty chunk sequences from real incidents (tests/integration/sse/replays/) including replays that previously produced JSON parse exceptions. - End-to-end smoke tests with Python/TS SDKs to verify fallback behavior for clients that do not understand the header. Performance: microbenchmarks show ~0.2% median CPU overhead on the compatibility proxy under representative streaming workloads; memory bounding prevents OOM at scale. Rollout plan: canary to us-west-2 (5% traffic) for 24 hours, monitor parse-error-rate, client-latency histogram, and new debug metric rw.sse.reassembly_failures. If stable, ramp to 50% then 100% over 48 hours. If reassembly_failures exceed 0.1% or latency p99 increases >10%, automatic rollback to the previous proxy image will trigger. Migration notes: - No action required by customers. - SDKs updated to log and expose rw-seq metadata for advanced debugging (redwood-sdk-python v1.12.3, redwood-sdk-typescript v0.9.7). Related: fixes ENG-4582, addresses parts of ENG-4620. Checklist: [x] unit tests added [x] integration replays added [x] canary plan documented [x] release notes included
Ethan Rivera: Can we avoid allocating ephemeral buffers per-fragment? Consider using a pooled buffer for the 128kb window.
Maya Chen (author): Switched to sync.Pool-backed buffers for hot-path allocation in sentinel.go; benchmark shows reduced GC pressure.
Priya Kapoor: Add more conservative defaults for the reassembly limits in cloud-managed plans. Suggest lowering to 64kb for free-tier.
Maya Chen: Added plan-aware caps and feature flags; default remains 128kb for enterprise-managed proxies, 64kb for free/self-serve.
Noah Kim: Need a metric for dropped fragments and an automated debug dump endpoint guarded by feature flag.
Maya Chen: Added rw.sse.reassembly_drops and a gated debug dump at /_debug/sse/reassembly (requires admin token).
Fix: SSE streaming compatibility layer now reassembles partial JSON fragments deterministically using a compact X-RW-SEQ header. Resolves intermittent JSON parse errors and duplicate function-call events for streaming clients. Backwards-compatible with older SDKs.
Canary 5% us-west-2 -> 50% -> 100%. Watch rw.sse.reassembly_failures, rw.sse.reassembly_drops, and parse-error-rate. Automatic rollback threshold: reassembly_failures > 0.1% or p99 latency +10%.

Motivation: Dedicated fleets currently rely on hard reservations and long-lived commitments to guarantee tenant throughput. This leads to headroom waste when tenants have bursty behavior and to conservative sizing.

This PR introduces the Soft Grant Orchestrator (SGO): a transient-grant mechanism that allows the autoscaler to issue short-lived capacity grants to tenants for burst windows, together with an anticipatory decommit path that gently reduces long-lived reservations when sustained underutilization is detected. The goal is to preserve percentile throughput guarantees while reducing committed GPU hours.

What changed (high-level):
- New controller: controllers/soft_grant_orchestrator.go — issues grants with TTL and backoff, tracks grant health and fallbacks.
- Reservation reconciler: modified to respect soft grants and to annotate reservations with "grant-origin" for observability.
- Anticipatory decommit module: heuristics that analyze a rolling 1h utilization window and schedule step-downs with a safety fence and cooldown.
- Telemetry pipeline: exporters/tenant_grant_telemetry.go publishes granted_vs_used, grant_ttl, and anticipated_decommit_reason into the existing metrics pipeline and a compact one-minute histogram for Console.
- Tests: unit + e2e harness changes to simulate bursty traffic and verify SLA preservation under grant/trim cycles.

Design notes and safety:
- Grants are additive and ephemeral; the orchestrator never revokes hard reservations. If capacity pressure is detected the scheduler will automatically fall back to hard-reserved capacity.
- Anticipatory decommit only trims up to 25% of a tenant's reservation per step and requires a 30m low-utilization confirmation window before enacting. A short safety hold (10m) prevents immediate re-provisioning churn.
- We added an emergency opt-out label (dedicated.sgo/opt-out=true) for tenants that want deterministic reservation behavior.

Migration / rollout plan:
1) Deploy SGO disabled by feature flag. Monitor telemetry for false positives.
2) Enable SGO for a small cohort (internal "pilot" tenants) for 48h and validate no SLA regressions.
3) Gradually scale to controlled percentage of fleets.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for orchestrator state machine and decommit gating.
- Synthetic load canaries included in perf-canary to exercise grant issuance and backstop fallback.
- Benchmarks show <3% additional scheduler latency on grant decision path under 95th percentile load.

Related: Linear ENG-2145 implements the product acceptance criteria; SUP-4432 captured customer request to reduce overcommit in monthly billings.
- Introduces Soft Grant Orchestrator to allow temporary capacity grants for tenants, reducing long-running reservations.
- Adds anticipatory decommit logic to trim excess reservations during sustained underutilization.
- New telemetry stream for per-tenant granted vs used capacity exposed to Console.
Arjun Patel: Can we make the 25% step configurable per-fleet? Some enterprise customers have tighter burst constraints.
Maya Chen (author): Added FleetConfig.SGO.StepMaxPct with a default of 25%. Updated docs to surface the knob.
Ravi Kumar: The 1h rolling window seems aggressive for tenants with diurnal patterns. Suggest an adaptive window or minimum sample count.
Maya Chen: Switched gating to require at least 3 low-utilization windows in the last 2 hours (configurable) before action. Added tests to cover diurnal mock traces.
Elena Sokolov: Telemetry will double-count when grants overlap with autoscaler actions; confirm metrics alignment with existing reservation gauge.
Maya Chen: Exporter now emits a grant_delta metric and uses reservation UID to dedupe; updated mapping to Console charts.
Ravi Kumar (approval): Ran canary against internal fleets, behavior within expectations. Approve.
Arjun Patel (approval): Minor nits fixed, approve.
Operators: to enable SGO set flags sgo.enabled=true and configure FleetConfig.SGO.StepMaxPct or use tenant opt-out label. Watch metrics: tenant_grant_delta, tenant_grant_ttl, anticipated_decommit_reason. There is an emergency toggle in the console to disable SGO cluster-wide.
Merged via squash on 2026-02-03 after approvals from Ravi Kumar and Arjun Patel. Feature gated and disabled by default. Release note added. No rollback required.
Monitor tenant_grant_delta and 95th latency for 72h after pilot expansion
Add an alert if >5% of grants incur backstop fallbacks in 1h
Schedule doc walkthrough with SRE and support teams

Introduces a delegated soft-throttle that defers eviction decisions to a regional coordinator and a heartbeat grace latch to prevent double-eviction during transient partitioning. Off by default behind feature flag. Minor telemetry and e2e tests added.
Context and motivation: In recent partial-region partition incidents we observed rapid back-to-back eviction decisions leading to tenant hard-failovers and prolonged KV cache loss. This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: 1) Delegated soft-throttle: a lightweight regional coordinator that receives eviction-suggestion votes from local nodes and issues a short-lived soft throttle decision that is cheaper and less aggressive than full eviction. This prevents simultaneous hard-evict actions while preserving SLOs. 2) Heartbeat grace latch: when nodes detect a transient heartbeat jitter (flapping < 5s), they enter a grace-latch window that suppresses duplicate eviction attempts for that tenant-key-range. Implementation notes: - The feature is guarded by feature flag runtime.delegated_soft_throttle.enabled (default=false) and a runtime.slo_threshold override for canary. - Coordinator is implemented as a probabilistic, gossip-backed leader hint (no single point of failure) and uses existing lease metadata channel; it is intentionally lightweight to avoid adding new long-lived RPC surfaces. - Added metric tags: telemetry.evictions.source (local|delegated), telemetry.evictions.suppressed (true|false), telemetry.heartbeat.flap_count. - Added small e2e scenario in the perf harness that simulates partial regional partition and asserts no tenant experiences >2 consecutive hard evicts within 30s. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of delegated coordinator with fallback to local decision - [x] Heartbeat grace latch algorithm with configurable window - [x] Unit tests for latch edge cases - [x] Integration tests in e2e/regional_failover_test.go - [x] Telemetry and dashboards: updated metrics.yaml and alert hint - [x] Feature flag gating and rollout docs - [x] Smoke tested in canary region (us-west-2a) Summary of commits: - Initial coordinator scaffolding and interface (runtime/eviction/coordinator.go) - Soft-throttle ballot flow and local vote aggregation (runtime/eviction/delegated_throttle.go) - Heartbeat latch algorithm + unit tests (runtime/heartbeat/grace_latch.go, runtime/heartbeat/grace_latch_test.go) - Telemetry + prometheus metrics registration (telemetry/metrics.yaml, telemetry/metrics.go) - E2E test and minor harness changes (e2e/regional_failover_test.go) - Rollout docs and feature flag (docs/ops/feature_flags.md) Notes on backwards compatibility and safety: - Default-off feature flag ensures no impact to users unless enabled. - Coordinator failures fall back to local hard decisions; logic prefers safety over availability when leases are stale (explicitly documented). - Added guards to limit throttle lifetime to 8s to avoid long-term degraded throughput. CI summary: - Initial CI run: unit tests failed due to race in grace_latch_test.go (flaky timer); fixed by switching to a virtual clock in test harness. - Second CI run: all checks passed (unit, integration, linters, go vet). Review discussion highlights: - Riya: "Can we avoid any extra RPC dimension for large clusters?" — Answered: design uses existing lease gossip and an ephemeral ballot carried in existing metadata to avoid new RPCs; added comment in coordinator.go. - Lars: "What happens if the coordinator becomes partitioned alongside a node?" — Clarified: local nodes will time out and run local hard decision; added metrics and an alarm for coordinator ballot saturation. - Chen: requested a shorter default throttle lifetime; lowered from 12s to 8s and added as configurable parameter. Deployment plan: - Gate feature flag behind canary in us-west-2a for 48 hours. - Monitor telemetry.evictions.suppressed and slo.latency.p50/p95 for promoted tenants. - Roll forward to region if no anomalies; otherwise revert flag. Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2026-02-20 by Riya Patel with merge commit 4f6d2c8c. Related tickets: Linear ENG-2142 (investigate double-eviction), SRE-93 (production incident RCA).

Context: Release pipelines have intermittent flakiness during canary/smoke windows, and engineering teams need a low-friction, reproducible pre-merge snapshot to validate release artifacts before cutting stable releases. This PR introduces an 'atomic release checkpoint' workflow plus a quiet staging guard to reduce noisy premerge churn and a minimal toolchain image to speed preflight checks. What changed: Added .github/workflows/release-checkpoint.yml which creates a deterministic build snapshot, uploads a compact artifact, and runs a thin smoke suite; introduced build/toolchain/Dockerfile.min (alpine-based, trimmed toolchain) for preflight use; added tools/ci/keeper.go, a small Go helper that exposes artifact signing hooks and exponential backoff for flaky infra; added scripts/release-smoke.sh and README.ci.md documenting usage and rollout steps; minor updates to go.mod and Makefile to wire the minimal image into the preflight flow. Motivation: Reduce time-to-feedback for release engineers, make canary smoke deterministic and retry-safe, reduce CI image pull times, and provide a single checkpoint artifact teams can pin during rollback. Testing: Local smoke runs (scripts/release-smoke.sh) and full workflow runs on forked branch; CI flaky steps observed early were addressed by adding an idempotent artifact retrier and bumping timeouts for integration network calls. The GitHub Actions run passed on the final run: unit/lint/build -> pass, smoke -> pass, publish-checkpoint -> pass. Rollout: Gradual opt-in by release-manager teams via a feature flag in README.ci.md; the workflow is opt-in (comment trigger) until two release cycles have run. The keeper helper is feature-gated and defaults to no-op unless a GITHUB_TOKEN and SIGN_KEY are provided.

Priya Ramakrishnan: Keeper helper looks useful but add more unit tests around backoff and transient 5xx handling. Asha: Added retrier_test.go with 3 cases and updated go.mod.
Jordan Lee: Please lightweight the Dockerfile (remove apt and use alpine) to cut image pull time. Asha: Switched to alpine-based Dockerfile.min and trimmed build deps.

Context: During the Dedicated predictive autoscaling pilot we observed an unsafe downscale to 0 replicas when the forecast provider returned `null` for `predicted_replicas` (provider was up, but returned no value for the window due to insufficient history / timezone mismatch). In the current arbitration code path we treat `null` as `0` (via defaulting), then apply dampening/cooldown and clamp to bounds. For pilot deployments with `min_replicas` unset (legacy default 0) this allowed scale-to-zero, which is explicitly disallowed for Dedicated inference pools and caused queue build-up + increased p95 latency. This PR adds a guard: when predictive mode is enabled but the predictor returns `null`/missing, we treat it as "prediction unavailable" and fall back to the reactive desired (or keep last desired when reactive is also missing), never generating a new desired from a null prediction. We also emit an explicit reason code + metric so we can alert on predictor quality without impacting safety. Fix is scoped, low risk, and intended as an immediate pilot hotfix.

Changes:
- Autoscaler: treat `prediction == null` as unavailable and skip predictive arbitration for that tick.
- Autoscaler: ensure we never compute desired=0 solely from null prediction; decision reason becomes `predictive_unavailable_fallback_reactive`.
- Metrics: increment `dedicated_autoscaler_predictor_null_total{region,deployment_id}` and add decision log field `prediction_present=false`.
- Tests: add unit test covering null forecast with legacy bounds (min unset) asserting desired stays >= 1 for Dedicated (using existing "dedicated floor" safety invariant) and does not downscale compared to reactive.

Rollout:
- Ship as hotfix behind existing per-account pilot flag (no config changes).
- SRE to monitor bound-hit + queue depth + `predictor_null_total` for the pilot accounts for 48h.

Incident reference:
- Related to pilot oscillation / latency report and on-call thread; see SUP-28479 for customer impact details.

Checklist:
- [x] Added unit coverage
- [x] Verified no behavior change when predictor returns a valid value
- [x] Verified fallback is deterministic (audit fields set)
- [x] SRE sign-off for pilot hotfix
Vanessa Ortiz (review): Can we confirm we are not changing behavior when the predictor is temporarily stale vs null? I want stale to still be treated as unavailable.
Keiko Yamamoto (author): Yep — stale continues to be handled in the provider wrapper (returns unavailable). This PR only fixes the "present but null" case that was slipping through as 0.
Rafael Mendes (review): Please add an explicit metric for nulls so we can see if this is happening often; also ensure decision logs include a boolean for prediction presence for auditability.
Keiko Yamamoto (author): Added `dedicated_autoscaler_predictor_null_total` and `prediction_present=false` in the decision payload. Updated the regression test to assert reason code.
Jordan Lee (review): For the test, can we assert we fall back to reactive desired rather than pinning to last desired? Otherwise we might hide a separate reactive pipeline failure.
Keiko Yamamoto (author): Updated test to include a reactive desired and assert we follow it. If reactive is missing, we still preserve last desired (existing behavior) and set reason accordingly.
Vanessa Ortiz (approval): Approved. This is minimal and addresses the safety invariant. Please coordinate with SRE to roll to pilot accounts today.
Rafael Mendes (approval): Approved; hotfix is good to go. On-call will monitor `predictor_null_total` and queue depth panels during the next ramp.
Dedicated: fixed an issue in predictive autoscaling where a null forecast could trigger an unsafe downscale; autoscaler now falls back to reactive scaling when predictions are unavailable.

Motivation: Customers frequently ask why some invocations are expensive even when model latency is OK. We previously had only token-level aggregate cost estimates that lumped CPU and GPU together. This PR adds explicit per-token hardware attribution (CPU vs GPU execution time and token-level I/O overhead) and a synthetic replaybench that replays sampled traces with hardware routing flags to estimate cost splits across deployments.

What this change does:
- Adds new metrics exported by runtime workers: invocation_token_cpu_ms_total, invocation_token_gpu_ms_total, invocation_token_io_ms_total, token_hardware_fraction{hw="cpu"|"gpu"}. Metrics are aggregated per-invocation and exposed with per-tenant labels.
- Introduces a lightweight sampling/opt-in hook (runtime config flag runtime.metrics.hw_split_enabled) so customers can enable measurements without global perf impact.
- Implements a synthetic replaybench service (observability/replaybench) that consumes sampled invocation traces, replays them against the runtime with controlled hardware routing and collects hardware-split metrics to build cost attribution profiles. The replaybench accepts a date range and sampling seed for reproducible runs.
- Adds Grafana dashboard panels and a small explorer to visualize per-route and per-model hardware split, token-rate stacked bars, and an alert panel that triggers when token_hardware_fraction{hw="cpu"} rises above a configured threshold for a route.
- Adjusts alerting: new alert rule (SRE-HW-SPLIT-01) uses a 60m rolling window and de-duplicates noisy spikes by looking at replaybench-confirmed regressions.
- Documentation: runtime flag, SDK tagging (invocation.metadata.hw_hint), and a short howto for running the replaybench locally.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- We measure CPU time using a per-worker lightweight timer (no sampling of syscalls) and correlate with GPU timestamps from the batch execution path. Because GPU timestamps are coarse across batches, we add a per-token attribution heuristic: GPU time is divided by token emission count in the batch, and CPU time is attributed from worker-side work. This is intentionally conservative and documented.
- The runtime flag ensures zero default overhead; the code paths are behind fast checks. We intentionally avoid fine-grained per-token kernel probes to keep this safe for shared environments.

Commits:
- 1) init: add hw split metric collectors and basic exporter hooks
- 2) replaybench: synthetic replaybench service + trace consumer
- 3) dashboards: grafana panels + alert rule + docs
- 4) tests/lint: unit tests for metrics + fix lint failures

Changed files (high level):
- services/runtime/metrics/hw_token_metrics.go
- services/runtime/metrics/hw_token_metrics_test.go
- services/replaybench/main.go
- observability/grafana/dashboards/hw_token_split.json
- observability/alerts/hw_split_alerts.yaml
- docs/observability/hw_token_attribution.md
- infra/helm/templates/runtime-configmap.yaml (hook for flag)
- sdk/python/redwood/telemetry_tags.py (invocation hw_hint tagging)
- tools/replaybench/dockerfile

Review thread summary: 
- Evan Liu: asked for opt-in runtime flag and confirmation that default path is zero-cost; requested unit tests covering label explosion.
- Priya (author): implemented the flag, added fast-path guard and reduced label cardinality by limiting label values to {cpu,gpu,io} and adding sampling_rate label only when >0.
- Samira Khatri: requested an architectural note on how GPU timestamps are correlated; requested that the dashboard include a baseline historical view and a replay-confirmation toggle.
- Priya: updated the dashboard JSON with a baseline row and added a replaybench badge to panels so operators can mark a spike as replay-confirmed.
- Diego Marquez: asked to gate alert firing on replaybench confirmation for the first rollout to avoid noisy alerts; we settled on a 48-hour delayed auto-enable for the gating.

CI history: initial run failed lint (golangci) due to unused import in hw_token_metrics.go; second run: tests flaked in replaybench E2E due to a missing env var in CI container; fixed and final run: all checks passed (unit, integration-replay smoke, lint).

Motivation: Customers with strict data residency controls asked for a lightweight, auditable enforcement point that can accept requests from the serving runtime and assert KMS usage + tenant residency without changing existing request paths. This PR introduces 'Policy Sanctuary' — a small, high-availability service that validates per-request residency constraints, selects an allowed KMS provider/region, and issues a short-lived operator lease token used by downstream services to access tenant-scoped keys. The service also emits immutable residency audit headers that are appended to the audit pipeline to improve forensic traceability.

What changed (single-string description): - New service 'policy-sanctuary' with a compact policy DSL for residency rules (services/policy-sanctuary/policy/engine.go). - KMS allocator that chooses a CMK endpoint based on tenant claims, configured geofences, and configured provider preference; falls back to a configurable soft-fail policy that triggers controlled audit-only mode. - RBAC v2 'operator-lease' flow implemented: operator requests short-lived leases with limited scopes; leases are minted with proof-of-residency assertions and TTL enforcement (services/policy-sanctuary/rbac/lease_handler.go). - Audit enricher that attaches immutable X-Residency-Assertion and X-KMS-Provenance headers; these headers are HMAC-signed using the platform audit signing key to prevent tampering (internal/audit/enricher/enricher.go). - Integration tests exercising residency matches, KMS fallback, and lease revocation (tests/integration/policy-sanctuary/residency_e2e_test.go). - Private installer / Helm charts and docs to allow opt-in deployment in VPC/on-prem installs (deploy/private-installer/*, helm/policy-sanctuary/*). - Feature flag and rollout plan in pkg/config/feature_flags.yaml so the service can be enabled via staged rollout.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed in ENG-4821 - [x] Unit tests added for policy engine - [x] Integration tests for end-to-end residency flow - [x] Helm chart and private-installer manifest included - [x] Docs and playbook for incident runbooks included - [x] Security review requested and completed (Sofia Martinez)

Files changed: See changed_files list above for highlights; no changes to public API surfaces of the serving runtime. The runtime calls remain behind a feature flag and use the new operator-lease token when enabled.

Testing and CI: CI run green for unit and integration matrix on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. Load-smoke test simulating 200rps ran in a k3s environment — acceptable P95 latency impact under controlled batch sizes. A single flake in the cache eviction test was traced to test timing and fixed.

Review conversation (high-level): - Liam Patel: "The residency DSL looks compact — can we add a lint that rejects overly-broad allow rules?" — Author: "Added rule-linter and unit tests; linter runs in CI." - Sofia Martinez: "Audit header signing needs key rotation considerations." — Author: "Added key identifier header and rotation test; documented KMS signing key rotation in docs." - Igor Volkov: "Operator lease revocation path isn't clear on race with in-flight requests." — Author: "Added lease revocation callback and TTL check in allocator; documented best-effort rollback semantics in playbook." - Security approves after clarifications; SRE requested a soft-fail mode for partial outages which was implemented.

Rollout plan: Feature flag default off. Staged rollout with canary in a single region, followed by 24h telemetry review (audit header rates, lease minting rate, allocation errors). If residency mismatches exceed 0.1% or latency impact at P95 > 50ms, rollback.

Backward compatibility: The serving runtime continues to operate without the sanctuary service. When enabled, requests include an operator lease token; services that do not recognize the token will ignore it. The audit enricher emits additional headers that downstream consumers can opt into.

Operational notes: - Responsible oncall: security-infra rotation week of rollout. - Telemetry: meters for lease_minted, lease_revoked, kms_allocation_hits, kms_allocation_fallbacks, residency_audit_headers_emitted. - Alerting: high fallback rate (>0.5%) and increased audit rejections.

Related work: ENG-4822 tracks RBAC v2 policy templates for operator leases; SUP-1192 is a partner request case.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after two approvals and green CI.

Add Policy Sanctuary service: enforces tenant KMS residency constraints, attaches immutable residency audit headers, and introduces operator-lease RBAC v2 flow. Backwards-compatible; opt-in gate via feature flag.

Motivation: customers requested a non-blocking KMS consent flow for tenant onboarding and cross-region failover that preserves auditability without impacting tail latency. This PR implements a deferred consent handshake for KMS-bound operations and couples it with an audit-forward sampler to reduce load on the audit pipeline while guaranteeing eventual proof-of-consent. Design summary: (1) A consent-handshake middleware that returns an immediate 202 Accepted for operations when tenant consent is configurable-asynchronous, emits a consent-token header to downstream services, and enqueues a consent verification task for background processing. (2) A KMS affinity gate that consults RBAC v2 temporal grants to decide if a synchronous KMS operation is still required, otherwise defers and routes to a helper queuer. (3) An audit-forward sampler which buffers high-frequency audit events from deferred flows and forwards deterministic, sampled envelopes to the main audit sink with provenance headers to reconstruct the full sequence if needed. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is unchanged; the feature is behind a per-tenant flag (tenant.features.deferred_kms_consent) and an env toggle (KMS_CONSENT_DEFER_ENABLED=false). Rollout plan: enable in internal staging, run with 10% of production tenants for 48h, validate no increase in P99 latency or token leakage, then staged 25/50/100% rollout with canary keys. Testing: unit tests for middleware and sampler state machine, integration tests emulate KMS provider delays and verify audit envelope reconstruction in tests/integration/test_kms_consent.py, end-to-end manual verification checklist included. Security review: includes threat model and mitigation section in docs/security/residency-consent.md describing attacker vectors for consent token replay and how TTL+nonce and signed provenance headers prevent misuse. Performance: added benchmarks in benchmark-lab/kms-consent/ showing <1ms median added latency for synchronous path and bounded queue tail under burst. Checklist: [x] Design doc linked [x] Unit tests added [x] Integration tests added [x] Docs updated [x] Security reviewed [x] Smoke tested. Release notes: Adds an opt-in deferred KMS consent mode and an audit-forward sampler to reduce audit ingestion load for deferred flows. Related: ENG-5932 covers UX for tenant whitelisting. Merge method: squash. CI notes: initial lint failure due to goimports ordering; fixed in follow-up commit. Production monitoring: added metrics kms.consent.deferred.count, kms.consent.reconcile.failures, audit.sampler.forwarded_envelopes. Deploy notes: helm toggle chart value redwood.kms.deferConsent.enabled=false by default.

Context: We see occasional tenant cost blowups when aggressive prefetch/prefill heuristics combine with sudden bursty traffic and conservative KV-cache reuse. This PR implements a budget-conscious prefetch operator plus a small policy engine for quant-tiered fallbacks so that inference remains available while respecting tenant budget and unit-econ constraints. Motivation: reduce tail cost spikes, make safe automatic fallback to cheaper quantized variants when budget signals or latency tolerance allow, and instrument unit-econ metrics so the ops team and the cost advisor can validate behavior in production. What this PR does: 1) Introduces a new prefill operator (pkg/prefill/budget_operator.go) that tracks an adaptive budget window per-tenant and throttles speculative prefetching during burst windows. The operator uses a short predictive window (exponential decay counter) to avoid cold-prefetch storms. 2) Adds a quant-tier policy adaptor (runtime/quant/policy.go) that can fall back from fp16->int8->sparse-4bit variants based on combined signals: tenant budget headroom, latency SLO headroom, and recent model-quality checks. 3) Hooks unit-econ telemetry into the control loop (telemetry/unit_econ/*) emitting tokens_per_dollar, prefetch_efficiency, fallback_count and cost_delta_by_tier metrics. 4) Provides a CLI dry-run and simulator (tools/prefill-sim) to validate policies against replayed traffic traces. 5) Adds canary rollouts with gradual risk gating and a per-tenant override API (api/v1/prefill-override). Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag `budget_prefill_v1` and enabled by default for staging. Contains a simulator mode for offline testing. Backwards compatibility: All operator changes are additive; defaults are conservative and fallbacks require both budget and SLO signals. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (Linear ENG-4983) - [x] Unit tests for operator and policy - [x] Integration tests in perf canary harness - [x] Telemetry dashboards smoke tests - [x] CLI dry-run and simulator smoke tests - [x] Docs: README + rollout playbook Not included: quality-regression detector (separate follow-up ENG-5021) Single-string description: this entire block is the continuous description; please see commits for granular diffs and review comments for followups.

Motivation: Customers need safer, resumable promotions from shadow to canary that preserve session affinity and allow automated, explainable rollback suggestions when regression signals appear. This change introduces the 'Chronicle' rollout orchestrator: a deferred, gate-driven promote controller that combines session-coherent shadow draining, synthetic dry-run replays, and an autorepair rollback advisor that surfaces prioritized rollback actions.

What this PR does (single-string description): Adds a new orchestration runtime (chronicle-controller) and associated API surface for declarative deferred promotes. Chronicle implements: deferred promote windows (start/hold/commit phases), gate predicates (latency/error/quality thresholds), session-coherent handoff (keeps user sessions sticky until safe promote point), synthetic dry-run (replay a sample of live traffic through candidate model variants without affecting live responses), rollout telemetry anchors (time-series anchors for counterfactual comparison), and the Autorepair rollback advisor which synthesizes a ranked list of rollback playbooks with a confidence score. The description includes a short checklist: [x] controller runtime and CRD definitions, [x] controller unit + integration tests, [x] synthetic-replay harness (v0), [x] observability wiring (metrics/traces/logs), [x] migration docs and playbook.

Implementation notes: The controller is written in Go, uses the existing servegraph APIs for traffic routing, and introduces a lightweight playback worker that taps sampled requests (configurable sample rate) and replays them to candidate pools with deterministic session keys. We extended the promote API with three new fields: deferredWindow (start/hold/commit timestamps), gateProfiles (list of metric predicates with tolerances), and repairPolicy (auto|suggest|manual). The Autorepair advisor subscribes to the controller's telemetry stream, runs diff diagnostics (latency P50/P95, token-level quality regressions from eval hooks, error-rate deltas), and emits a ranked set of rollback actions (e.g., instant-swap revert, staged-drain to shadow, model-variant fallback) together with a recommended explanation string.

Backward compatibility and migration: Chronicle is opt-in; existing rollout CRs are unchanged. We added a migration guide under docs/runbooks/chronicle-migration.md and a console flag to enable the UI promote flow.

Risks & mitigations: Risk: synthetic replay could increase cost. Mitigation: sample rate defaults to 0.1% and is configurable per rollout. Risk: mis-ranked rollback suggestions. Mitigation: initial advisor run is suggest-only; we surface confidence and require two reviewers to enable auto mode.

Related work: builds on prior rollout work (see ENG-1427 for canary gating ideas, ENG-2131 for session affinity improvements). Links: linear/ENG-2147, design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2147/chronicle-rollout-design, runbook draft: docs/runbooks/chronicle-migration.md.

Notes for reviewers: focus on controller reconciliation correctness, telemetry anchors calculation, and the advisor’s ranking heuristic. I included unit and integration test summaries further down.
Aaron Chen (2024-11-06): Question - how does the playback worker guarantee deterministic ordering for session-affine replays? Can we avoid adding latency to the serving path when sampling?
Nina Alvarez (2024-11-06): Reply - playback uses an async tap; we only capture headers + body snapshot. Determinism is achieved via a stable session hash (user-id || cookie) and a per-rollout replay queue. No sync blocking on request path. Added notes in playback/worker.go comments.
Priya Rao (2024-11-08): Request changes - the advisor ranking currently favors latency regressions over token-level quality; please make weighting configurable and add unit tests for rank stability.
Nina Alvarez (2024-11-09): Update - added advisor weight config (advisor.weighting.latency, .quality, .error) with defaults and unit tests for stability under small signal noise.
Lucas Green (2024-11-10): Suggestion - add an opt-in dry-run flag that emits the rollback suggestion to the audit log only (no auto actions). This will help SRE validate suggestions during initial rollout.
Nina Alvarez (2024-11-10): Done - added repairPolicy 'suggest' which writes advisor decisions to audit logs and surfaces them in the console. Updated runbook with verification steps.
Priya Rao (2024-11-11): Approved - tests look good, minor nits addressed.
Aaron Chen (2024-11-12): Approved - verified e2e smoke on staging cluster. CI green.
Introduces 'Chronicle' rollout orchestrator (opt-in). Features: deferred gated promotes, session-coherent handoff, synthetic dry-run replays, and an Autorepair rollback advisor (suggest-only by default). See docs/runbooks/chronicle-migration.md for migration steps and console enablement.
Default playback sample rate is conservative (0.1%). Advisor auto-mode disabled by default; to enable, set helm value 'chronicle.advisor.mode=auto' and require two reviewer approvals in policy. Monitor metrics 'chronicle_gate_failures' and 'chronicle_advisor_confidence'.
Unit tests added for gate predicate engine and advisor ranking. Integration test validates full deferred window lifecycle including commit and staged rollback. Manual staging smoke run performed on staging cluster with 1000 sampled replays.

Motivation: We repeatedly see tenants shipping with suboptimal batching and quantization defaults that increase unit cost by 10-40% before an engineer tunes them. This PR adds a lightweight "heuristic coach" service and a dry-run CLI that suggests tenant-specific batching, cache and quantization defaults based on recent workload samples and unit-econ heuristics.

What this PR does: Adds a heuristics engine that synthesizes tenant signals (request shape distribution, cold-start ratio, latency SLO profile, model family) and emits a ranked set of recommended defaults: batch shapes, cache TTLs/prefixing rules, and quantization fallback tiers. It also provides a CLI mode to run simulated dry-runs against historical traces (no live traffic) and output expected cost/latency delta for each candidate preset. The feature is conservative by default and exposes a safe-apply mode that writes presets as tenant proposals for ops review.

Scope: runtime recommendations (batching/cache), quant profiles (fp16/int8/quant-ffn), a CLI dry-run tool (cli/econ/dryrun), telemetry hooks, unit tests, docs and a small migration of tenant-defaults storage to support proposal metadata.

Checklist: - [x] heuristics engine implementation (services/econ/coach.py) - [x] dry-run CLI with simulate & report subcommands (cli/econ/dryrun.py) - [x] YAML presets format and validation (configs/defaults/cost_presets.yaml, schema) - [x] telemetry events for decision explainability (telemetry/econ_events.proto) - [x] unit and integration tests (tests/test_coach.py, tests/test_dryrun_integration.py) - [x] docs (docs/decisions/heuristic-coach.md) - [x] e2e cost-sim smoke test added to CI

Safety posture: Recommendations are gated behind a "proposal" lifecycle; the coach never overwrites live tenant defaults without explicit apply-by-operator. The dry-run CLI is read-only by default. Quantization fallbacks include an accuracy-estimate field and require an opt-in fast-eval threshold before automated rollouts.

How to review: Start with services/econ/coach.py for the algorithm and heuristics, then the CLI for reproduction steps, and finally the tiny schema changes for tenant-defaults persistence. Note the new telemetry events used by the Optimize UI; adding consumers is behind a feature flag.

Related: ENG-1249 (tenant defaults automation), PM-88 (prefill cost-playbooks), and a previous spike PR that collected traces (ref: pr-731122).

Rosa Martínez: The telemetry proto needs a version bump. We saw a transient failure in e2e cost-sim when the event shape changed. Please add a compatibility test for live pipelines.
Theo Alvarez: Suggest exposing an explicit --force-apply flag in the CLI and gating it behind an ops role. Also add a note about rate-limiting proposals to avoid churn.
Asha Patel (author): Addressed comments: added doc paragraph on conservative thresholds, bumped telemetry proto and added compatibility unit test, added --force-apply CLI flag behind a config gate, and implemented a proposal rate limiter with a default of 1 proposal per tenant per 24h.
Liam Chen: Approving after tests pass and docs updated.

Adds a conservative heuristics-based coach that generates tenant-specific batching, cache and quantization default proposals. Includes a dry-run CLI to simulate cost/latency impact. Feature is opt-in and requires operator approval to apply defaults.

Context: During a recent regional egress incident we observed large swings in per-tenant SLOs when the control plane applied blunt egress-deny rules. That oscillation caused unnecessary failovers and increased downstream retries. This PR implements a tenant-aware, incremental egress reduction controller and an SLO oscillation mitigator to smooth control actions and avoid thrashing.
Motivation: Reduce unnecessary failovers and customer-visible latency spikes by shaping egress at finer granularity rather than hard denies.
Goals: 1) Apply graded egress attenuation per-tenant based on a short moving-average of error/latency signals. 2) Introduce escalation windows and minimum hold times so decisions are not flipped rapidly. 3) Provide a soft-deny probe endpoint that can confirm degraded-but-acceptable paths. 4) Expose telemetry and per-tenant audit events to help SREs debug.
Design summary:
- Controller core implemented in infra/egress/controller.go: maintains per-tenant rolling windows for latency, error-rate, and egress-cost signals. Uses exponential smoothing (alpha=0.2 default) to compute a degradation score.
- Attenuation policy in serving/slo/egress_shaper.py: maps degradation score to a three-step attenuation {nominal, partial-shape, soft-deny} with hysteresis timers.
- Probe architecture: a short-circuit probe endpoint (/internal/probe/egress-check) implemented in serving/handlers/probe.go that verifies an egress path before applying soft-deny.
- Telemetry: new metrics (egress_shaper_score, egress_shaper_action, tenant_slo_drift) and structured audit events sent to otel collector.
- Config: feature gated via deploy/helm/values.yaml and a runtime flag for dedicated/private installs.
- Docs: operations playbook at docs/operations/egress-strategy.md with rollout and rollback guidance.
Tests and validation:
- Unit tests in tests/unit/test_egress_shaper.py cover policy mapping and hysteresis.
- Integration tests in tests/integration/test_egress_mitigator.py simulate synthetic latency/error spikes and assert no >2 flips/min for decisions.
- A small load soak was run in perf-canary (internal run id pc-20241108-03) showing reduced failovers in a 2-hour spike window.
Rollout plan: 1) Feature flag off in hosted by default. 2) Canary on 5% of traffic for 48h with traffic shadowing enabled. 3) Increase to 25% for 72h and monitor tenant_slo_drift. 4) Gradual global enable if stable.
Emergency rollback: flip helm flag to disable controller and the system reverts to legacy circuit semantics. Backout steps listed in docs/operations/egress-strategy.md.
Checklist: - [x] Implementation - infra and serving changes - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Telemetry events - [x] Docs and runbook - [x] Canary plan
Commits summary: - "initial egress mitigator controller and moving-average scoring" - "policy mapping and hysteresis timers; probe endpoint" - "tests, telemetry and docs; helm feature flag"
Changed files (high level): - infra/egress/controller.go: new controller, smoothing logic, per-tenant state machine. - serving/slo/egress_shaper.py: attenuation policy and configuration. - serving/handlers/probe.go: short-circuit probe endpoint and test harness. - tests/integration/test_egress_mitigator.py: multi-tenant integration scenario. - docs/operations/egress-strategy.md: rollout/rollback procedures and runbook. - deploy/helm/values.yaml: feature flag and sane defaults.
Review conversation: 1) Diego: "Controller looks reasonable; can you add a guard to prevent scoring from taking effect for tenants with <100 requests/min? We saw noisy tenants before."  - Priya: "Added a min-rate guard (configurable min_requests_per_min) and updated tests to exercise the path." 2) Marta: "Telemetry tags look good but please standardize tenant_id as 'tenant.id' in events and add an example to the docs."  - Priya: "Fixed telemetry keys and added an example JSON event in docs." 3) Owen: "Concern: rolling-average alpha selection might be too aggressive for long tails. Suggest making it configurable and adding an integration test for alpha=0.05."  - Priya: "Alpha made configurable and a test added; canary will default to 0.2 but ops can tune per-region." 4) Diego (approval): "Works for me after fixes. CI flakes were rerun."
CI summary: - unit tests: pass - lint: pass - integration: initially failed on a timing assertion, rerun passed - e2e: pass (two flaky tests quarantined)

Follow-ups: - Telemetry alert thresholds to be configured in observability-pack (ENG-2007). - Run an SRE post-mortem if canary shows >5% tenant SLO regressions. - Consider per-tenant learning in v2 (ticket ENG-2109).
Notes: This is intentionally conservative — algorithm is simple and feature-gated so we can iterate quickly in the wild. The hotfix nature of the change is that the controller contains a short circuit to neutral mode if it detects control-plane instability, minimizing risk during rollout.

payload.body:
Context: We observed intermittent memory spikes and increased tail latency when many concurrent function/tool calls arrived as large initial payloads (tool params + long messages) on the gateway ingress. These events were correlated with long-lived streaming connections where the proxy would buffer large chunks while waiting for downstream runtime availability.

Motivation: Reduce gateway memory amplification and improve tail latency without breaking existing OpenAI-compatible streaming semantics. We need to limit per-connection and per-route buffered bytes, apply a small sliding "window" for ingress chunk acceptance, and surface clear backpressure behavior to callers and runtimes for graceful degradation.

Design summary: 1) ingress window: implement a sliding byte window per connection that caps buffered, unconsumed bytes to route-configurable max_payload_bytes and a new streaming_window_bytes (defaults: max_payload_bytes=1MB, streaming_window_bytes=128KB for OpenAI-compat routes). The window allows a few small chunks to stream through while preventing a single large upload from inflating memory. 2) fncall streaming bounds: when function/tool calling is detected (via content flags in the OpenAI-compat adapter), the gateway keeps a tighter default window and switches to chunk-prioritization: small chunks (<4KB) are preferred and put through immediately; large chunks are acknowledged with a 429-like backoff signal (X-Stream-Accept: delayed) and reflowed when capacity frees. 3) route-level overrides: new fields in route_defaults.yaml and per-route config to tune both limits and prioritization behavior. 4) observable signals: new metrics (gateway.ingress.windowed_bytes, gateway.ingress.backpressure_count) and a short human-readable reason code in responses when chunks are deferred. 5) compatibility: openai_adapter updated to interpret and emit the new small-chunk prioritization header and to surface a stable fncall handshake when chunks are deferred so SDKs can retry with smaller chunks.

Checklist: - [x] ingress window primitives and tests - [x] route config + defaults - [x] fncall prioritization logic - [x] adapter compatibility changes + unit tests - [x] integration test that simulates many concurrent fncall streams with mixed chunk sizes - [x] docs and release notes

Testing: Added gateway/tests/streaming_integ_test.go that spins up a simulated runtime and opens 300 concurrent streams mixing small/large payloads. Verified memory usage under the new defaults is stable and tail P99 latency drops ~35% in our stress harness. CI initially failed the integration flakily due to a timing assumption; fixed by adding backpressure delay jitter handling and reran checks.

Rollout plan: feature flag gated under "gateway.ingress.windowing.v2". Default enabled on staging, will flip in prod after 48h of staging telemetry. If early signals show increased client errors we will lower streaming_window_bytes for OpenAI-compat routes and push a hotfix to relax prioritization.

Backward compatibility: No breaking API changes. OpenAI-compatible streaming still follows same framing; we add advisory headers and observable reason codes. SDKs are recommended but not required to honor the backpressure headers. Documented behavior in docs/gateway/payload-policies.md.
Diego: Can we make the 4KB small-chunk threshold configurable at route-level? I think mobile clients may prefer 8KB. (resolved: added route override)
Lina: The metric names look fine but add a tag for route.id so we can filter noisy tenants. (resolved)
Samir: Integration test flaked on 2nd CI run, I saw a flakiness because of tight timing; ask authors to add jitter. (resolved)
Asha: responded with implementation notes and added jitter + route tag in metrics
Gateway: add ingress streaming window and fncall prioritization to reduce memory amplification and improve tail latency for streaming function/tool calls. Defaults tuned for OpenAI-compatible routes; route overrides available.

payload.body:
Introduce ephemeral tenant-aware transient rate cap (accordion) and a soft-evictor with cooldown windows to smooth regional rampdowns and provide an emergency unwind path. No breaking changes. Recommended rollout: staged canary -> 25% -> 100% with automatic metrics gating.
Context: We observed two related problems during the recent surge incidents: (1) sudden per-tenant bursts caused regional controller thrashing and rapid circuit flips, and (2) emergency operator unwind requests could produce hard evictions that caused downstream quality regressions. This PR implements a tenant-aware ephemeral rate-cap "accordion" that dynamically compresses burstable capacity across tenants during regional rampdown, and a "soft-evictor" that performs staged eviction with a cooldown and graceful fallback to cached/low-fidelity responses. Motivation: reduce cascading circuit breaker flips and give operators a low-risk emergency unwind that does not immediately hard-evict in-flight work. Design summary: - Ephemeral rate-cap accordion: transient token buckets per-tenant that can be compressed by the regional sequencer when a region is ramping down (capacity contraction). Compression is proportional to tenant priority and recent SLO history. - Soft-evictor: instead of immediately marking requests as evicted, we mark them as candidate-evicted and begin a short TTL-based drain (default 3s) during which requests may be retried, redirected to a read-only KV cache, or compacted to a lower-cost model. After the TTL, candidates are converted to evicted. - Emergency unwind endpoint: operator API to request an unwind for a region with a staged mode (observe -> soft-unwind -> hard-unwind). This gives time to ramp evictions and observe impacts. - SLO enforcement hooks: the accordion consults SLO credit windows and can preferentially preserve capacity for tenants below error budget thresholds. - Observability: new metrics (accordion.compress_ratio, evictor.candidate_count, unwind.stage) and tracing spans for decision points. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of token compression and tenant priority weighting - [x] Soft-evictor state machine and cooldown timer - [x] Emergency unwind operator API and RBAC gating - [x] Unit tests for compression math and state transitions - [x] Integration test in perf-canary with synthetic spike and regional rampdown - [x] Dashboard panels and alerts for regressions Rollout plan: 1) Deploy canary to perf-canary cluster behind feature flag 2) Monitor compress_ratio and candidate_count during synthetic and real traffic 3) Gradually enable in a single region (25%) with automatic rollback on SLO regressions 4) If stable, enable global. Backwards compatibility: operator API is additive; default behavior remains unchanged unless feature flag enabled. Related: ENG-1249 (tenancy SLO policies), SRE-88 (regional rampdown postmortem). Merge notes: squash-merged after CI re-run; no DB migrations or client surface changes.
Marcus Liu: Nice approach. Two asks: (1) add a safety timer to avoid indefinitely delaying hard-evict in pathological cases, and (2) include an escape hatch metric we can alert on.
Author (Asha Patel): Added max_safety_window config (default 30s) and emit evictor.hard_escape_count. Updated tests.
Eleni Vass: Compression math looks good; can we ensure we do not penalize tenants currently under error budget? Please add a unit test for that path.
Author: Added unit test 'TestCompressionPreservesLowBudgetTenants' and adjusted weighting to clip at min_preserve_ratio for low-budget tenants.
Tomás García: Security: RBAC change looks fine, but ensure the unwind endpoint logs operator identity for audit.
Author: now writing operator identity to controlplane audit logs and added an E2E check in integration test.
Marcus Liu: CI flake on windows AMI; re-ran. All green. Approved.

payload.body:
Motivation: We observed repeated regional oscillations during transient overloads where immediate evacuation + aggressive circuit flips caused thrash and slow recovery. This PR introduces two coordinated mechanisms that reduce oscillation risk and make regional failovers softer: (1) a proactive circuit prober that continuously probes candidate fallback regions and updates circuit state with probabilistic confidence scoring, and (2) a gradual evacuation stabilizer that moves traffic out of an overloaded region in bounded steps with hysteresis windows.

Design summary: the circuit prober runs as a lightweight probe runner inside the serving control-plane with configurable probe types (health, short-path latency, a minimal inference request) and per-region confidence decay. Probes feed into an updated circuit-state machine: instead of immediate open/close flips, circuits transition to a PROBING state where decisions are weighted by a rolling confidence score. The evacuation stabilizer subscribes to circuit state + SLO telemetry and, when evacuation is triggered, ramps egress percentage in discrete ticks (default: 5% steps every 30s) until either the target region returns to healthy or a maximum egress cap is reached. Hysteresis prevents rejoin until multiple consecutive healthy probe windows succeed.

Configuration and knobs: feature flag (evac-stabilizer-enabled) for staged rollout; probe_interval_seconds (default 10s); probe_window_seconds (default 60s); probe_confidence_threshold (default 0.85); evac_step_percent (default 5); evac_step_interval_seconds (default 30); evac_max_percent (default 80); rejoin_required_good_windows (default 3). All knobs live in serving/config/evac_config and can be overridden per-tenant in dedicated deployments.

Telemetry and observability: new metrics emitted: prober.probe_latency_ms{region,type}, prober.probe_success_rate{region}, circuit.confidence_score{region}, evac.progress_percent{region}, evac.step_events_total{region,result}. Added structured traces for probe sequences and a dashboard prototype (dashboards/evac_stabilizer.json) that surfaces probe timelines and evacuation steps for on-call.

Safety and rollout: implemented canary rollout (10% traffic regionally) gated by feature flag and Linear tasks ENG-1842/ENG-1899. Added circuit probe dry-run mode so we can exercise logic without performing actual egress. Backout: setting evac-stabilizer-enabled=false or forcing evac_max_percent=0 disables evacuation and returns circuit machine to existing behavior.

Testing and validation: unit tests for confidence aggregation and hysteresis logic; integration test that simulates a noisy region with intermittent latency spikes and verifies no >2 toggles in a 10-minute window. Load test in benchmark-lab showed a 37% reduction in rejoin oscillations and a 12% improvement in downstream tail latency during overload windows.

Migration notes: no customer-facing API changes. Default behavior is behind feature flag; recommend enabling in staging for 72 hours, then canary to 5% of production traffic before progressive rollout.

Why this is different: previous solutions attempted aggressive immediate failover or depended solely on SLO breaches. This approach explicitly measures candidate fallback health, smooths evacuation, and ties rejoin policies to multiple good windows to reduce flip-flopping.
Marco Ruiz: Overall looks good. Two asks: 1) make probe payload size configurable and small by default, 2) add a slowpath circuit metric so SRE can detect when probes are missing. Response: obrigado — probe payload is now configurable (probe_types.go) and prober emits probe_missing_total metric.
Priya Patel: Can we avoid tenant-wide config change? Suggest per-tenant opt-in. Response: added per-tenant override via serving/config/evac_config and documented how to set in Dedicated clusters; default remains off for tenants.
Ethan Cole: Concerned about DAG ordering when multiple regions are evacuated concurrently. Response: stabilizer serializes evacuation per-tenant and records causality in traces; added unit test to validate ordering and added a small backoff jitter to reduce thundering herd.
Adds a proactive circuit prober and a gradual evacuation stabilizer to reduce regional failover oscillations. Behind feature flag evac-stabilizer-enabled. New telemetry and dashboard available for on-call. Default off for tenants; can be enabled per-tenant in Dedicated deployments.
If you see repeated rapid evacuation/rejoin events after enabling, disable evac-stabilizer-enabled and set evac_max_percent=0; check prober.probe_success_rate and circuit.confidence_score for probe anomalies. See docs/ops/evacuation-runbook.md for steps.
Unit tests cover confidence decay and rejoin hysteresis. Integration simulation demonstrates reduction in oscillations under noisy latency profiles. Benchmark-lab shows improved tail latency during controlled overloads.
Low to medium. Changes are control-plane only and behind feature flag; misconfiguration could cause slower evacuation (traffic stays longer in degraded region) but not data loss. Added safety caps (evac_max_percent) and rapid disable path.
Set EVAC_STABILIZER_ENABLED=false in control plane config, restart control-plane, or set evac_max_percent=0 via config API. Reversions available in main if immediate rollback required.
