payload.body:
Motivation: teams need fine-grained, privacy-preserving cohorting for multi-arm experiments and phased promotes without leaking slice identities across services. This PR introduces the 'Opaque Slice Orchestrator'—a rollout layer that assigns opaque slice tokens to user cohorts, schedules time-windowed promotes, and enforces rollback windows driven by telemetry safepoints. Key goals: (1) session-consistent routing for promoted clients, (2) rollback windowing so automatic reversions respect a minimum quarantine period before re-promote, (3) telemetry-driven safepoints so automated rollback triggers are only evaluated at stable aggregation boundaries, and (4) A/B pairing support for paired metric diffs and counterfactual capture.

What this PR does: implements a new orchestrator component in the rollout controller, adds a lightweight tokenization layer to generate opaque slice IDs (no user PII retained), extends the rollout API to accept 'sliceAffinity' and 'rollbackWindow' parameters, instruments telemetry hooks for safepoint flushes, and adds a controller-level simulation harness to validate failure-mode behavior. The description below is a continuous narrative that includes checklist, test surface, and merge notes.

Checklist: - [x] design doc (ENG-4829) linked - [x] unit + integration tests for token lifecycle - [x] e2e staged deployment in canary cluster - [x] migration path for existing cohort rules - [x] docs and API changelog - [x] security review (no user id persistence)

Behavioral highlights: - Opaque slice tokens are stable per-cohort across 72h by default (configurable) but rotate on manual remap to avoid long-lived correlations. - RollbackWindow: a minimum time an experiment must remain in quarantine before attempting automatic re-promotion; prevents churn loops on noisy metrics. - Telemetry safepoints: the orchestrator evaluates metric gates only after configured aggregation windows (e.g., 5m/1h buckets) to avoid acting on transient spikes. - A/B pairing: when enabled the router maintains paired user-to-variant mapping to ensure within-subject comparisons for metrics like CTR and latency.

Compatibility and migration: - Backwards compatible with existing cohort rules: if 'sliceAffinity' absent, behaviour is unchanged. - Admins can opt-in per-rollout via the console or API. - The feature flags allow gradual ramp of tokenization and safepoint enforcement.

Commit summary: see commits field for short messages. Files changed: rollout controller, router shard, telemetry aggregator hooks, API contract, migration script, and test harness. Small illustrative snippet added in rollout_controller.go to show time-window guard:

if now.Sub(rollout.LastQuarantineStart) < rollout.RollbackWindow {
    // hold promotion until window expires
    return ErrQuarantineWindow
}

Tests and CI: initial CI run showed a flaky aggregator test; test fixed by introducing time-simulated aggregator in tests and adding deterministic clocks to the harness. Final CI run: pass. Load test: canary cluster exercises 20k concurrent sessions with <=5% overhead on routing compared to baseline.

Operational playbook (short): - Default rollout in beta cluster for 48h. - Monitor 'orchestrator.slice_rotate' and 'orchestrator.rollback_evaluations' metrics. - If rollback oscillation observed, increase RollbackWindow and widen telemetry aggregation window. - Emergency stop available via console -> rollouts -> abort and snapshot.

Related work: builds on ENG-3911 (traffic fencing) and ENG-4522 (session affinity), pairs with SUP-1304 support runbook for incident rollback. This PR is intended to reduce false-positive automated rollbacks and enable privacy-safe paired A/B experiments.

Merge notes: squash merge; migration script will be run as a background job during the next maintenance window. No DB schema breaking changes.
Ethan Zhao: Design looks solid; can you clarify slice token entropy and rotation window?
Priya Nair: Tokens are HMAC-based with a server-only secret; rotation default 72h, configurable per-org.
Marina Lopez: Concern about metric alignment when safepoint windows mismatch upstream aggregators; suggestion to add an adapter.
Priya Nair: Added a safepoint adapter and deterministic clock for tests in the follow-up commit.
Grace Kim: Minor: please add an audit log entry when admin remaps slices (security) — added in migration commit.
Ethan Zhao: CI flake on aggregator fixed; verified load numbers in canary cluster. Approving.
New rollout feature: Opaque Slice Orchestrator with telemetry-backed rollback windows and paired A/B support. Opt-in via API/Console. Provides safer automatic rollbacks and privacy-preserving cohort tokens. Migration script seeds tokens for legacy cohorts.
Enable feature flag 'opaque_slice_orchestrator' in beta before enabling in prod. Watch metrics: orchestrator.slice_rotate.count, orchestrator.rollback_evals.count, rollout.promotion_latency.p50. Migration script is idempotent; run during low-traffic window.
Run migrations/2026_02_seed_opaque_slices.sql in staging then prod
Flip feature flag in beta cluster
Schedule 1h post-deploy smoke test and telemetry validation

payload.body:
- Adds TP heartbeat + in-flight collective metrics to improve stall detection/diagnostics.
- Adds stall_reason codes and structured logs on suspected TP stalls.
- No API behavior changes; metrics are low-cardinality and gated by config where appropriate.
Context: Under sustained TP load we’ve seen “silent stalls” where requests hang (often streaming decode) but the only visible symptom is downstream timeouts and eventual replica churn. This PR adds low-cardinality TP liveness + progress metrics and a standardized stall reason taxonomy so SRE/on-call can quickly answer: is it compute, comms/NCCL, or scheduler starvation? Scope in this PR is instrumentation only (no scheduling/comms correctness changes). Related: ENG-4823 (instrumentation), ENG-4821 (initiative umbrella). What’s included: (1) Per-rank heartbeat metrics: a monotonic heartbeat updated at key progress points (prefill start/end, decode step start/end, before/after collective calls). Exported as both a counter and “seconds since last heartbeat” gauge so alerting is straightforward. (2) In-flight collective counters: increments/decrements around NCCL collectives and exposes last seen collective sequence per TP group to help identify mismatched ordering vs global stalls. (3) Stall reason codes: introduces a shared enum used by scheduler/runtime to tag suspected stall sites (compute, comms collective, scheduler starvation/backpressure, kv cache compaction, cancellation path, unknown). This is deliberately small + stable; we can extend later but want to avoid high churn and label cardinality explosions. (4) Structured logs on stall suspicion: when heartbeat gaps exceed a threshold (see below) or when a step crosses the “soft stall” deadline, we emit a single structured log entry with enough context to correlate across ranks. (5) Unit tests: fake-clock tests validate heartbeat progression, ensure we do not emit high-frequency logs under normal operation, and verify reason codes map to expected metric labels. Metric names (agreed w/ SRE in Slack thread 1739897721): - redwood_runtime_tp_rank_heartbeat_total{model,cluster,replica,tp_rank,tp_world_size,phase} - redwood_runtime_tp_rank_heartbeat_age_seconds{model,cluster,replica,tp_rank,tp_world_size} - redwood_runtime_tp_inflight_collectives{collective,model,cluster,replica,tp_group_id} - redwood_runtime_tp_last_collective_seq{collective,model,cluster,replica,tp_group_id} - redwood_runtime_tp_stall_suspected_total{reason,model,cluster,replica,tp_group_id} Stall reason taxonomy (initial): - STALL_REASON_UNSPECIFIED - STALL_REASON_COMPUTE (kernel/compute step didn’t advance) - STALL_REASON_NCCL_COLLECTIVE (in-flight collective didn’t complete) - STALL_REASON_SCHEDULER_STARVATION (no scheduling progress / queue fairness) - STALL_REASON_KV_COMPACTION (compaction/eviction path blocking) - STALL_REASON_CANCELLATION_PATH (client disconnect / cancellation leaving ranks waiting) - STALL_REASON_UNKNOWN Structured log fields (sample): event=tp_stall_suspected request_id=<uuid> replica_id=<id> model=<name> tp_group_id=<id> tp_world_size=<n> tp_rank=<r> phase=<prefill|decode> stall_reason=<enum> heartbeat_age_ms=<ms> inflight_collectives=<n> last_collective_seq=<seq> scheduler_queue_depth=<n> stream_id=<cuda stream int> note=<short> Config/overhead notes: - Heartbeat updates are intentionally lightweight (atomic + timestamp). We avoid per-request labels; replica_id/model are already present in our standard metric dimensions. - redwood_runtime_tp_rank_heartbeat_age_seconds is updated once per scrape (computed from last heartbeat timestamp) and does not require timers per request. - Structured stall logs are rate limited per (replica,tp_group_id,reason) to 1/min by default to avoid log storms during incident conditions. - A “soft suspicion” threshold is currently 5s heartbeat age; this is not paging by itself. Alert rules/paging thresholds will be implemented in observability-pack PR-412 after we get a few days of baseline. Dashboards: - Draft panels are referenced here (Grafana): https://grafana.redwoodinference.internal/d/tp-stalls/tp-stall-and-timeout (WIP; final panels/alerts tracked in observability-pack PR-412) - Confluence dashboard doc: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/tp-stall-and-timeout-dashboard.json (linked in ENG-4823) Validation: - benchmark-lab mixed workload repro: heartbeat progresses under normal load; when forced to block a mocked collective, inflight_collectives stays >0 and heartbeat_age_seconds increases and emits a single structured stall log per minute. - Local tests: runtime_unit_tests pass; added coverage for stall reason mapping + rate limiter. Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Add trace span attributes for collective counters/rank IDs (tracked in PR-21872). - Wire in scheduler queue depth (we included a placeholder hook; scheduler team will fill real signal in ENG-4824/PR-21841). - Alert rules + paging policy (observability-pack PR-412 + SRE thread 1740071202).
Julian Moore (review): Can we confirm we’re not adding request_id / prompt_id as metric labels anywhere? We can’t afford cardinality spikes during incidents. Omar El-Sayed (author): Confirmed. request_id only in structured logs (rate limited). Metrics labels are restricted to the standard runtime dimensions (model/cluster/replica + tp_rank/world_size/group_id + reason/phase/collective). Aisha Bello (review): Naming looks good. For alerting, I’d prefer a gauge like “heartbeat age seconds” rather than having to do PromQL math off a counter. Looks like you added that — thanks. Can you add a note on scrape-time computation to avoid per-request timers? Omar El-Sayed (author): Added to PR description + docs: heartbeat_age_seconds computed from last_heartbeat_ns and exported at scrape. Allison Grant (review): Please align stall reason strings with trace attribute naming conventions (snake_case). Right now the log emits “STALL_REASON_NCCL_COLLECTIVE”; could we also emit a lowercase variant for easier querying? Omar El-Sayed (author): Updated log schema to emit stall_reason="nccl_collective" while keeping enum constant internally; added unit test for mapping stability. Noah Patel (review): +1. Minor: the “soft suspicion threshold” default (5s) seems aggressive for long-context prefill. Can we make it phase-aware or just call it “debug threshold” for now? Omar El-Sayed (author): Renamed to “soft suspicion threshold (debug)” and made it configurable per phase with conservative defaults: prefill=15s, decode=5s. Default values are intentionally non-paging; SRE will tune alerting separately. Sofia Ivanova (review): Good. I’d like to ensure scheduler starvation reason is not used until scheduler actually sets it; otherwise it’ll bias incidents. Omar El-Sayed (author): Agreed—by default we emit UNKNOWN unless explicit reason is set by caller. Added comment + guard in the helper. Approvals: Julian Moore (APPROVED), Aisha Bello (APPROVED), Allison Grant (APPROVED), Noah Patel (APPROVED).
payload.title: TP: add per-rank heartbeat metrics, stall reason codes, and structured stall logs

payload.body:
Motivation: We continue to see production incidents where interleaved or truncated SSE fragments lead to partial JSON emissions or reordered tool/function-call events in the OpenAI compatibility layer. Root causes are (1) late-arriving tail bytes that look like delimiters, (2) ambiguous fragment ordinal assignment across concurrent streams, and (3) heuristic resyncs that sometimes drop fncall ordering metadata. This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: a lightweight tailguard that holds a soft buffer for trailing bytes and a deterministic ordinal resolver that assigns and reconciles fragment ordinals across patch/replay windows. The changeset aims to reduce partial-JSON emission and guarantee deterministic ordering of function/tool call handoffs across retries and replays. Implementation notes and checklist: - Introduce sse.tailguard: soft-timeout buffer (configurable per-tenant) that delays final flush for up to N ms when trailing delimiter-like bytes are detected. - Add sse.ordinal_resolver: monotonic per-stream ordinal tag plus reconciliation policy for out-of-order fragments during reassembly. - Emit explicit "watermark" events in the openai-compat layer when ordinals are advanced so downstream SDKs can safely order fncalls. - Improve the stream sanitizer to prefer fence-tokens produced by the ordinal resolver over naive delimiter heuristics. - Add unit/e2e tests that simulate split-utf8, delimiter-spill, interleaved fncalls, and replay scenarios. - Docs: add API note for the public streaming contract changes and new per-tenant tailguard config. Checklist: [x] Tests added/updated [x] Benchmarks (micro) for latency impact [x] Migration note in docs [x] Back-compat notes (watermark events are additive) Related work: Linear ENG-3214, ENG-2987. This description is a single continuous string containing motivation, design summary, and checklist.
Jordan Lee: Can you explain the decision to use a soft buffer instead of adding an explicit frame terminator? We risk added p50 latency.
Author (Priya Kaur): Soft buffer is opt-in (per-tenant) and we observed that an explicit terminator would require protocol bump and break many clients. Tailguard keeps latency impact minimal and is tunable; see microbench results in the PR.
Marisol Alvarez: The ordinal reconciliation looks complex — how does it behave across reconnects and replay?
Author: Ordinals are monotonic tokens attached to each fragment. On reconnect we exchange the last-seen ordinal via the preface and the resolver stitches missing ordinals using deterministic fill rules; duplicate fragments are dropped based on ordinal and checksum. Added tests that simulate the exact reconnect sequence.
Hank O'Neill: We should ensure SDKs ignore watermark events if they are not adopting ordering guarantees yet.
Author: Watermarks are additive and carry a version header. SDKs that do not recognize the header will ignore them; added a note to the streaming contract doc and SDK compatibility test.
Jordan Lee requested a configurable max-tail-delay default of 4ms rather than 10ms for critical low-latency tenants
Marisol asked for stronger assertions in e2e for duplicate-ordinal suppression
Changed default max-tail-delay to 4ms for low-latency tier; made config overridable by tenant
Added stronger assertions and a randomized e2e matrix to exercise duplicate suppression
Fix streaming partial-JSON and fncall ordering issues by adding tailguard buffering and a deterministic fragment ordinal resolver. Backwards-compatible watermark events added to the OpenAI compatibility layer. Configurable tail delay per-tenant to balance latency vs safety.
OpenAI-compat: watermark events are additive and optional. SDKs that wish to rely on deterministic fncall ordering must opt into watermark handling. Existing clients remain functional without changes.
Microbench: enabling tailguard at 4ms increased p50 by 1.2ms on medium load; tailguard at 10ms added ~3.7ms p50. Reassembly success rate improved from 98.1% -> 99.98% on synthetic interleaved stream tests.
Rollout plan: feature gated behind tenant config. Default rollout to staging for 72h health check, then progressive enablement to GA. Monitor stream_error_rate, fncall-misorder, and p50 latency. Alert if fncall-misorder > 0.01% or stream_error_rate increases by 50%.
payload.title: Add tailguard and ordinal resolver to rescue fragmented SSE payloads and preserve fncall ordering

payload.body:
Context and motivation: Our presubmit pipelines are a major contributor to long CI cycles and noisy builds for trivial changes. Multiple teams reported that small README/docs/infra tweaks still trigger full lint/test matrices and expensive toolchain installs. This PR implements two coordinated improvements: (1) a presubmit-minifier that computes a change fingerprint and narrows the set of lint/test shards and the set of tools required for the change, and (2) a toolchain fingerprint file that records the computed toolchain signature per workspace so runners can conditionally reuse cached tool images rather than reinstalling devdeps on every job. The goals are: faster feedback for small diffs, fewer spurious dep installs, and clearer CI cost accounting.

What this PR changes (high level):
- New presubmit-minifier binary (cmd/presubmit-minifier) with a small decision engine that maps changed paths, file globs, and heuristics to a presubmit profile. The profile controls which lint plugins and test groups run.
- Toolchain fingerprinting: a deterministic SHA256-based fingerprint written to .toolchain/fingerprint.json (human-readable) when CI bootstraps. Runners and local devcontainer helpers read this to skip reinstallation if the fingerprint matches cached images.
- CI workflow updates: main/.github/workflows/presubmit.yml updated to call presubmit-minifier and pass profile tags to job matrices; added a lightweight matrix fallback for cases where heuristics are disabled.
- Presubmit daemon unit tests and e2e harnesses under infra/presubmit/tests.
- Docs: docs/dev/presubmit-minifier.md and docs/dev/toolchain-fingerprinting.md.

Commits summary (top-level, chronological):
- feat(presubmit): add presubmit-minifier command and core heuristics
- chore(ci): wire presubmit-minifier into presubmit workflow and matrix expansion
- feat(toolchain): add deterministic fingerprint generator and caching helpers
- test(presubmit): add unit tests and e2e harness for minifier
- docs(ci): add developer docs and rollout plan
- fix(ci): handle edge-case for binary changes affecting fingerprinting

Note: commits were squashed on merge to a single consolidated commit describing the feature.

Files / areas touched (representative):
- cmd/presubmit-minifier/* (new)
- internal/presubmit/heuristics.go
- internal/presubmit/profile_map.yaml
- .toolchain/fingerprint.go
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yml
- infra/presubmit/tests/*
- docs/dev/presubmit-minifier.md
- docs/dev/toolchain-fingerprinting.md
- devcontainer/scripts/cache-toolchain.sh
- scripts/ci/cache-check.sh

Behavior and heuristics detail: The minifier inspects the git diff for the PR (base..head) and assigns tags: docs-only, infra-only, service-api, runtime, cross-repo. Each tag maps to a presubmit profile defined in profile_map.yaml. Profiles specify a whitelist of lint plugins and test groups. Heuristics include path-based rules (e.g., docs/** => docs-only), filetype rules (.md, .rst), and a small opt-out annotation "[ci full]" in PR body to force a full run. The fingerprint generator canonicalizes tool versions declared in devcontainer.json and known tool-lock files, sorts entries, and computes a SHA256; the fingerprint is compared against the runner-side cached-image manifest.

Rollout plan and safety net:
- Feature gate enabled in main for all repos but defaults to conservative profiles (i.e., only skip heavyweight jobs for docs-only/infra-only).
- Added a staged rollout: dev teams opt-in by setting presubmit: fast in repo settings; after two weeks of telemetary validation we broaden to default-on for small PRs.
- A fallback matrix job runs in parallel for a sparse sample (5% of PRs) to validate correctness and catch false-negatives in heuristics.
- Opt-out: PR body can include "[ci full]" to force full presubmit.

Review conversation (abridged, inline):
- Claire: "Can heuristics accidentally skip required integration tests when only manifest changes are present?" Author reply: "Good catch — we added a manifest rule to map changes to 'service-api' if CHANGELOG or api/manifest.yaml changes are present, and we keep a conservative default that retains integration tests unless it's docs-only or infra-only."
- Diego: "Toolchain fingerprint files in the repo — will they cause churn?" Author reply: "Fingerprint is written to .toolchain/fingerprint.json but only updated via an explicit `./dev-toolchain regenerate` flow described in docs. CI sets an env guard so it doesn't auto-commit changes. The fingerprint is intended to be human-managed in tandem with devcontainer/tooling upgrades."
- Samir: "How do we validate runner caches aren't stale across cloud images?" Author reply: "Added cache-check.sh that cross-validates stored manifest entries and the artifact registry. We also added telemetry if cache reuses happen more than 3x without observed tests — it will surface as a warning in the presubmit console."
- Claire (after review): "LGTM after small nits (doc clarifications)."
- Diego: "Approved."

CI and validation notes:
- First CI run failed two long-running integration shards due to a flaky infra test; those were retried individually via the rerun action and passed.
- Lint and unit tests passed on first run.
- E2E harness required a minor time adjustment (increased tunable waiter to 30s) to stabilize on slower runner types; that change is in the final commit.

Observability and telemetry:
- Added lightweight presubmit telemetry events: presubmit.profile_assigned and presubmit.fingerprint_mismatch. These are routed to internal metrics and are visible in the presubmit dashboard.
- Telemetry will be sampled initially (10%) to limit noisy dashboards.

Risk assessment:
- False-negatives (skipping required jobs) are the primary risk; mitigations include conservative default profiles, a 5% parallel validation fallback, opt-out override, and telemetry alerts.
- Toolchain fingerprint churn is mitigated by an explicit regenerate flow and docs to guide teams.

Post-merge tasks and follow-ups:
- ENG-1245: sweep repos in the org to add lightweight profile hints for monorepos with many generated files.
- ENG-2208: add an autosuggest feature in the PR UI to propose profile tags when presubmit-minifier produces low confidence.

Merge outcome and method: Squash-and-merge to main with a single consolidated commit titled "presubmit: introduce minifier + toolchain fingerprinting (ENG-1245, ENG-2208)".

Additional notes: This PR was designed to be minimally invasive: when presubmit-minifier is disabled (feature-flag off), the CI behaves exactly as before. We kept the default conservative to avoid regressions. The docs include a rollback procedure and diagnostics for any team that wants to disable local minification in their repo.
Adds a lightweight presubmit minifier that narrows test/lint jobs for small changes; introduces deterministic toolchain fingerprinting to avoid unnecessary dependency installs. No user-facing API changes.
payload.title: Introduce presubmit-minifier and toolchain fingerprinting to reduce CI noise

payload.body:
Motivation: we observed tenant churn and cascading regional rejoin oscillations during a partial-e2 region degradation in staging; this caused repeated KV cache warm drains and SLO spikes. This PR introduces a tenant probation fuse component (lightweight, in-server token-bucket-like probation state) combined with a region stability probe that informs the probation time constants. The goal is to reduce rapid tenant re-admittance and prevent repeated warm-drain cycles while keeping degradation observable and reversible. Design summary: probation_fuse is implemented as a compact Rust module in the runtime that tags tenant sessions with a probation score and an exponential decay window; the probe (Go) runs as an opt-in controller per-region and emits a stability score via the control plane; routing picks up the score and raises probation thresholds when region instability is detected. Key changes: runtime admission logic, a small control-loop probe, telemetry counters and histograms, integration test harness, and a helm values toggle for staged rollout. Testing: unit tests for probation decay and admission thresholds; integration harness simulates rapid tenant disconnect/rejoin and confirms a ~40% reduction in warm-drain events; manual canary in staging passed for 24h. Rollout plan: enable feature-flag off by default, enable for 10% of tenants in staging for 24h, then ramp to 100% in region beta if no regressions. Rollback: flip helm flag to false or revert main config; probation state expires naturally. Checklist: [x] unit tests; [x] integration test; [x] metrics and tracing; [x] docs and helm values; [x] staging canary. Related: ENG-4123 for telemetry work, SUP-889 for incident context.

Summary: Introduces a coordinated failover choreographer that sequences node drains, KV-cache safe handoffs, and per-tenant SLO fences to perform regional failovers and graceful degradation with bounded latency impact. Motivation: Recent incidents showed that parallel region failovers and uncoordinated kv-evacuation caused token spikes and client-visible latency regressions. This PR implements a staged choreography layer that reduces bursty reconnections and avoids violating tenant SLOs during emergency evacuations.

What this change does: Implements a small orchestration layer in the runtime scheduler that: 1) establishes an SLO 'harbor' window for affected tenants (timeboxed preserve of latency SLAs), 2) sequences KV cache preservation and handoff with a short-lived lease so slowpath clients are gracefully redirected, 3) limits concurrent node-drain operations via a global throttle and per-zone concurrency budget, 4) provides a telemetry contract surface (events: choreo.start, choreo.step, choreo.finish, choreo.abort) for observability and automated paging, 5) automatic rollback/fast-reopen if KV handoff fails within a detection window, and 6) optional emergency fast-path that preserves highest-priority tenant tokens by temporarily freezing lower-priority queues.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-7190), [x] unit + integration tests for choreography transitions, [x] end-to-end canary in perf-lab region, [x] console dashboard tiles for choreo events, [x] migration/rollout plan for Dedicated and Private.

Backwards compatibility and gating: The choreography is feature-flagged by config.runtime.failover_choreographer (off by default for existing clusters). When enabled, the system advertises the choreographer capability in node metadata so control-plane rollouts can be performed gradually. The default policy is conservative: 2 concurrent drains per zone, 30s KV handoff lease, 60s harbor window. These defaults can be tuned per deployment.

Testing and canary notes: Deployed to perf-canary (eu-west-1) for a 48h soak. Observed a 37% reduction in token replays and no SLO violations in the canary tenant cohort. CI: full unit suite + runtime integration on k8s overlay.

Deployment plan: Feature-flag rollout (canary -> staged regional ramp -> global), enable observability for 72h at each step, automatic rollback via console if choreo.abort rate > 0.5% over 10m.

Risks and mitigations: Risk: choreography can slow emergency evacuation if misconfigured; mitigation: default conservative timeboxes and an emergency 'fast-unwind' override for operator use. Risk: stale KV leases on network partitions; mitigation: TTL-based lease and fast reclaim path on disconnect.

Related work: builds on the KV-preserve mechanics introduced in ENG-6531 and integrates with the SLO-metering hooks from ENG-6822.

Samir Patel: Can you confirm the failure modes for KV handoff? What happens to in-flight requests if the lease cannot be acquired?
Maya Chen (author): If the lease fails we trigger a fast-unwind: we stop additional drains, mark the node as quarantined, and increment a choreo.abort counter so operators are paged. In-flight requests are retried on the local node while quarantine is active to avoid mass replays.
Lina Gomez: Large change — please ensure the observability labels are present on all choreo.* events; we need team dashboards to filter by tenant and region.
Maya Chen (author): Added tenant and region labels to all event emissions in telemetry commit, updated dashboard definition.
Theo Rivera: Tests look good; can we add a targeted stress test that simulates N+1 region outage with slow network so we validate lease TTL reclaim behavior?
Maya Chen (author): Added an integration scenario in perf-lab that runs a slow-network simulation with lease TTL asserts; results included in canary notes.
Introduce controlled failover choreographer (opt-in) to sequence node drains and KV handoffs with SLO-preserving windows. Feature gated; default conservative params. See docs/ops/failover_choreographer.md for rollout steps and tuning.

Motivation: Recent audits and a support incident (SUP-1123) showed a gap in how operator sessions were attributed when requests traversed region-linked proxies. That made post-incident forensics and residency claims brittle. This PR introduces three coordinated changes: 1) entitlement fingerprinting: compute a stable, short-lived fingerprint for operator sessions that binds operator identity, session nonce, source geozone, and service boundary to prevent silent operator impersonation or replay across regions; 2) audit-fencekeeper: a gate that ensures audit logs for jurisdiction-sensitive operations are written with canonical metadata and blocks a request path unless an immutable audit envelope is produced; 3) KMS geo-fanout router: when multiple KMS providers are available, route encryption operations with an affinity score based on tenant residency, operator geozone, and cost heuristics with safe fallbacks. Design notes: Entitlement fingerprinting is generated at the auth proxy layer and propagated as X-Ent-Fingerprint header. Fingerprints are HMAC-SHA256 over (operator_id|session_id|source_zone|service_scope|timestamp_window) with a short TTL and rotation at the proxy. The fencekeeper intercepts audit writes and verifies the presence of the fingerprint and a signed audit-seal before allowing side-effects for region-pinned resources. KMS geo-fanout uses a policy engine: candidate providers are scored by residency match (+100), low-latency bump (+30), and cost delta penalty (-cost_weight*delta). The router falls back deterministically to the next available provider while annotating audit metadata with the decision vector. Implementation summary: commits: - create entitlement fingerprint generator and validation hooks in auth-proxy (auth-proxy/*) - add audit-fencekeeper service with gRPC ingress and enforcement middleware (audit/fencekeeper/*) - wire fencekeeper checks into resource controllers for tenancy-sensitive writes (controllers/tenancy/*) - add KMS routing layer and policy config (kms/router.go, config/kms-policies.yaml) - add unit and integration tests and a small e2e harness that simulates cross-region operator hops (tests/e2e/geo-ops) Files changed (high level): auth-proxy/pkg/fingerprint.go (new), auth-proxy/middleware.go (hook), audit/fencekeeper/service.go (new), audit/fencekeeper/middleware.go (new), controllers/tenancy/handler.go (patch), kms/router.go (new), config/kms-policies.yaml (new), tests/e2e/geo-ops/test_geo_handoff.go (new), ci/workflows/audit-fencekeeper-integration.yaml (new), docs/security/entitlement-fingerprint.md (new). Small illustrative snippet: in auth-proxy/pkg/fingerprint.go we compute the fingerprint as: hmac := HMAC_SHA256(master_key, fmt.Sprintf("%s|%s|%s|%s|%d", operatorID, sessionID, zone, scope, window)) The fencekeeper API is light-weight: VerifyEnvelope(request_id, fingerprint, envelope) returns (ok,bool, reason,string). Rollout and migration: guarded behind feature flag feature.entitlement_fingerprint. Default off for all prod clusters. Rollout plan: stage 1 - land feature flag and non-blocking fencekeeper that emits metrics and logs only (canary namespace) 2 weeks. stage 2 - enable fencekeeper enforcement for a small cohort of tenants (10%) and monitor audit write latency and error rates. stage 3 - broad enforcement once we see stable metrics and no regression in latency SLOs. Metrics and alarms: new grafana dashboards and alerts included for: audit_fencekeeper_reject_rate, entitlement_fp_generation_failures, kms_router_fallback_rate, audit_write_latency_p50/p95. Thresholds: reject_rate > 0.1% for 1h triggers paging. Testing: unit tests added for HMAC edge cases and spoof attempts; integration test simulates operator hop from eu-west to us-east and verifies envelope rejection when fingerprint mismatches. Security review notes: keying material for HMAC uses the existing operator master key stored in KMS and rotates via the key-rotation pipeline; fencekeeper stores minimal envelope metadata and leverages existing audit-retention pipes to avoid duplication. Performance: benchmark of fingerprint generation adds ~120μs at auth-proxy median; fencekeeper adds ~2ms to audit-call path in our canary cluster. These numbers are within SLO but we'll watch after ramp. Review conversation (abridged): Nina Gupta: "Can we ensure the fingerprint doesn't leak PII and that it's deterministic across proxies?" Aisha: "Yes the fingerprint is derived from IDs and a time window; no raw user names or emails are included. Documentation updated to call this out." Thomas Wang: "What happens if KMS routing fails for all providers?" Aisha: "Router will return a deterministic 5xx and fencekeeper will block the side-effect. We document fallback and add a retry/backoff in router; incident runbook updated." Liam O'Connor: "Suggest adding a metric for the decision vector histogram." Aisha: "Done - added kms_router_decision_vector metric and tagged logs for replay." CI: go unit tests pass, integration workflow ran against staging and passed with one transient flake retried. Lint and security-scanner flagged a missing input validation in controllers/tenancy/handler.go which was fixed in a follow-up commit. Backwards compatibility and opt-out: existing clients that do not send X-Ent-Fingerprint are compatible while fencekeeper runs in observation mode. When enforcement is enabled, operator sessions without a valid fingerprint will be rejected with 403 and an explicit error code (ERR_AUDIT_FINGERPRINT_MISSING) with guidance to rotate clients. Related work: ENG-3219 (operator session hardening), ENG-4987 (kms router policy engine) Linear tickets mentioned above. Merge notes: feature gated, merged via squash, and feature flag default off. Post-merge actions: - schedule canary rollout in nimbus-prod cluster starting 2026-03-02 - add dashboard panels to incident book and notify security on the 10% cohort flip - run a small compliance validation against tenants in EU region to verify residency enforcement. Known limitations and follow-ups: - current fingerprint window is conservative; future work may permit per-tenant TTL tuning - we do not yet export a global audit-proof index; planned follow-up ENG-4041 - additional KMS cost tuning to be addressed by finance pairing on ENG-5232.
Adds operator entitlement fingerprinting to prevent lateral privilege expansion, deploys an audit-fencekeeper service that enforces log consistency for jurisdictional events, and introduces a KMS geo-fanout router with affinity scoring. Backwards-compatible; opt-in via feature flag and gradual rollout to prod clusters.

Introduces locality-aware RBACv2 templates and a lightweight KMS residency proxy; harmonizes audit sampling for cross-region flows. Default behavior is opt-in behind the 'locality-policy' feature flag. No customer-facing API changes. Admins should review RBAC templates before enabling.
Motivation: Customers operating across multiple regions require both RBAC constraints that can express geography-bound roles and a safe way to pin encryption to region-scoped KMS keys while preserving audit fidelity. Existing rule sets were ad-hoc and caused operator confusion when KMS fallbacks happened in a different geozone. This PR introduces three cooperating components: 1) a compact RBACv2 policy template DSL (rbac/templates) that can express locality constraints and inheritance; 2) a lightweight KMS residency proxy (pkg/kms/residency-proxy) which validates requested key regions and emits provenance headers; and 3) an audit harmonizer (telemetry/audit/harmonizer) that normalizes and samples residency-related events to reduce noise while preserving compliance proof points. Summary of changes: - rbac/templates: new template language, examples for 'tenant-region-restricted' and 'operator-cross-zone-read' templates, template compiler and unit tests. - pkg/kms/residency-proxy: authorization checks to ensure CMK usage matches request residency claim, region affinity caching, and explicit denial path on mismatch. - telemetry/audit/harmonizer: layered sampler that groups similar residency-deny events and emits canonical compliance records suitable for export. - sdk hooks: minor additions to Python/TS SDKs to pass the new residency headers for private deployments. - docs: operator guide and migration notes under docs/security/residency-and-rbac.md Design notes: - Policy templates are intentionally compact (YAML-first) and compile to the existing RBACv2 JSON model to avoid runtime changes to the enforcer. - Residency proxy is implemented as a transparent gRPC middleware for Dedicated/Private deployments and as an optional sidecar for on-prem installers. - Audit harmonizer retains full raw payloads for 90 days (configurable retention) but reduces long-term export volume via deterministic sampling and canonical event stitching. Compatibility & rollout: - Feature gated under 'locality-policy' feature flag. - Default: disabled for hosted customers; opt-in via console or env var for Dedicated/Private. - Migration path: admin tool 'rbacctl compile --validate' added to validate templates against tenant metadata. Testing & CI: - Unit + integration tests cover template compilation, residency assertion matching, and audit sampling correctness. - Benchmarked residency-proxy latency ~0.7ms median added to tokenized requests (see bench results in PR artifacts). Checklist: - [x] Template language spec and examples - [x] Residency proxy core logic + caching - [x] Audit harmonizer deterministic sampler - [x] End-to-end integration test (synth tenant, kms mock, audit sink) - [x] Docs and operator migration notes - [x] SDK header passthrough - [x] Backward compatibility: templates compile to RBACv2 JSON - [x] Feature flag gating Rollback plan: flip feature flag off; residency-proxy responds in permissive passthrough mode that emits a deprecation warning header; compiled templates not applied if flag is off. Security considerations: - Residency proxy enforces KMS principal mapping and performs strict validation of encryption-context to mitigate key misuse. - All provenance headers are HMAC-signed before insertion into audit stream. - Audit harmonizer preserves raw events for compliance audits. Observability: new per-tenant metrics: residency_denies_total, residency_proxy_p95_latency_ms, audit_harmonizer_stitched_events_total. Migration notes for operators: run 'rbacctl dry-run --templates ./my-templates.yml' to see impacts; enable flag in staging first. Related: ENG-2314 (template compiler), SEC-89 (audit sampling policy).
Jordan Kim: Nice isolation between compiler and runtime. A few nits on error messages in compiler.go — please include template name and line. (requested_changes)
Priya Rao: Updated compiler error formatting to include template name and line numbers, added unit tests for malformed templates. (author_reply)
Sven Müller: Residency proxy looks solid; can we add a metric for cache hit-rate? Also prefer configurable TTL via env var rather than hardcoded 30s. (requested_changes)
Priya Rao: Added residency_proxy_cache_hit_total and residency_proxy_cache_miss_total metrics; made TTL configurable via RESIDENCY_PROXY_CACHE_TTL. (author_reply)
Aisha Patel: Audit harmonizer deterministic grouping is good; ensure we keep raw payload export path for compliance audits. Also confirm HMAC key rotation semantics. (comment)
Priya Rao: Harmonizer keeps raw event store for 90 days by default and exposes an admin endpoint to export raw events. Documented key rotation: rotate KMS signing key via admin flow, harmonizer will accept both old/new for 24h window. (author_reply)

Motivation: After the outage on 2026-02-16 we observed repeated oscillations when tenants were force-evicted and then rapidly reinstated. Cold KV misses + global rehydration spikes triggered cascading soft-evictions and SLO blips. This hotfix implements a two-part mitigation: (1) a 'gentle rewind' SLO limiter that applies a time-limited, decaying backoff to aggressive reopen attempts for recently-evicted tenants; and (2) a Prefetch Coordinator that attaches an optional lightweight prefetch intent to a tenant reinstatement to warm KV prefixes and reduce cold-path latency. Goals: reduce oscillation count, avoid rapid reopen/evict churn, and improve tail latency during tenant warmups.

Adds a new stateful cohort hedged rollout controller that stores checkpointed snapshots for safe, session-consistent rollback. New APIs for snapshot inspection and manual rollback; console UI; instrumentation for SLOs and rollback metrics.
Context: We need safer progressive rollouts for model variants that preserve session affinity and allow fast rollback without violating in-flight session consistency. Current canary/shadow controllers are stateless and either drop affinity or rely on ad-hoc cache invalidation which causes inconsistent user experiences and risk during rollbacks.

What this PR does: Implements a stateful 'Hedged Cohort Rollout Controller' that: (1) tracks cohorts and binds session anchors to a persistent snapshot record, (2) creates lightweight transactional rollback snapshots at configurable checkpoints, (3) supports hedged routing (send duplicate low-priority requests to candidate variants) for cold-start smoothing, and (4) exposes inspection and manual rollback APIs. The controller integrates with the serving runtime to invalidate KV caches deterministically during snapshot application.

Design notes: Snapshots are append-only records (migration id rollout_snapshots) with a compact diff encoding to minimize storage. Rollout policies are expressed as a single controller config (percent/phased/cohort map) with optional hedging window and snapshot cadence. To preserve session consistency we record anchor identifiers for active sessions and resolve them to the appropriate model revision during reads.

Files and surface changes: Adds orchestration/controller/hedged_rollout.go, orchestration/transactional_anchor.go, apis/v1/rollout_types.go, migrations/2026_02_26_add_rollout_snapshots.sql, console/pages/rollouts/snapshot_view.tsx, tests/e2e/hedged_rollout_flow.test.ts, docs/rollouts/hedged-controller.md, charts/templates/rollout-controller-deployment.yaml plus small changes to serving/runtime/cache_invalidator.go and prometheus metrics registration.

Testing: Unit coverage for controller decision graph (controller unit tests), integration tests between the controller and runtime cache invalidation (integration/rollout_cache_test), and an e2e scenario that simulates a live cohort with 30k requests and a mid-rollout manual rollback. Load tests run locally with the perf lab harness; results attached in PR comments.

Migration: Adds a backward-compatible DB migration (2026_02_26) that creates rollout_snapshots and snapshot_index tables. Migration includes a cleanup TTL for snapshots older than configurable retention.

Operational concerns & flags: Feature gated behind rollout.hedged_controller.enabled and rollout.snapshot_retention_days (default 7). We added metrics: rollout_snapshot_create_total, rollout_snapshot_apply_duration_seconds, hedged_traffic_ratio, hedged_failure_retries_total.

Checklist: [x] Controller implementation, [x] DB migration, [x] Unit tests, [x] Integration tests, [x] Console UI, [x] Docs, [x] Perf run, [x] SRE review.

Caveats: Snapshot diffs are not currently compacted across model family boundaries — we avoid cross-family compaction in this iteration. Future work: TTL compaction, snapshot delta compression, and RBAC controls for manual rollback APIs.

Control plane: add inflight health-signal debouncer and soft-fail autorepair. Improves regional stability by reducing transient circuit flips and automating warmup of replacement nodes. Backwards compatible; rollout behind feature flag.
Context: Recent incidents (SUP-1245) revealed that short-lived probe flapping and transient KV-cache drain notifications cause cascading circuit transitions and aggressive tenant evictions during regional hiccups. This causes unnecessary soft-fail handoffs and customer-visible latency spikes. Motivation: reduce sensitivity to short-lived signals while retaining fast detection for real degraded nodes. Approach: introduce an "inflight signal debouncer" in the control plane health aggregator plus a complementary "soft-fail autorepair" that can warm standby capacity and pre-warm KV caches when a node shows ephemeral badness. The PR contains: - Debouncer: aggregates node-level signals (probe success/fail, drain markers, connection errors) on an event timeline, applies configurable hysteresis, and emits a single debounced health state change only after observation windows and weighted votes. - Soft-fail autorepair: when a debounced soft-fail is detected (transient but repeated within a short epoch), the orchestrator creates a micro-warmup plan: pre-warm a spare replica, populate prefix cache for top-ten tenants for that node, and hold eviction decisions for a short cooldown to avoid oscillation. - Telemetry/observability: new metrics (controlplane.debounce.window_ms, controlplane.debounce.vote_count, controlplane.softfail.warmups, controlplane.softfail.cooldown_s), structured tracing events for debouncer decisions, and dashboard panels in SLO console for warmup success rate. - Safety: feature-flagged rollout (featureflags.inflight_debouncer) with an escape hatch that forces immediate legacy behavior. Includes rate limits on warmup operations to protect capacity. - Tests/benchmarks: unit tests for debouncer logic, integration test simulating flapping probes, and a small perf microbenchmark showing <1% avg latency added to control plane decision path under 5000 events/sec. Checklist: - [x] Debouncer core algorithm implemented and covered by unit tests - [x] Orchestrator integration and warmup plan plumbing - [x] Telemetry + dashboards instrumented - [x] Feature flag and rollout plan documented - [x] E2E integration test simulating SUP-1245 repro - [x] Load perf benchmark run and results attached Link: Linear ticket https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4312 "Debounce inflight health signals and soften soft-fail behavior". Notes on config: defaults tuned conservatively (window_ms=1000, vote_threshold=3, warmup_cooldown_s=120). Operators can tune in runtime config if needed. Migration and compatibility: API contract unchanged. Debouncer lives inside control plane aggregator; upstream consumers receive the same health state events but with less churn. Rollout strategy: staged in canary region -> 25% -> 50% -> global, with telemetry checks at each stage to ensure no increased mean-time-to-detect for true failures.

Context and motivation:
We frequently see token-level alert storms when upstream clients send short bursts of high-concurrency requests. These surges produce noisy SLO alerts (p50/p95 oscillation) and generate many redundant PagerDuty incidents. Additionally, late-arriving tracing spans (collector batching / network jitter) were creating disconnected traces which made root-cause diffs harder for oncall. This PR introduces a two-part observability solution: 1) an adaptive token-surge dampener that gates alerting sensitivity during transient bursts, and 2) a span-reconciliation engine that joins late spans back to their original invocation and emits reconciliation metrics for debugging.

What changed (high level):
- telemetry/surge_dampener: new service implementing exponential decay windowing + adaptive hysteresis to suppress transient token SLO alerts and emit dampening metrics (dampener.active, dampener.suppressed_alerts, dampener.reason).

Motivation: Customers operating under strict data residency and regulated-key controls asked for an auditable, compact proof that a request used a region-anchored KMS key and that any operator-delegated actions were filtered by per-route policy. This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) a resident 'attest wallet' abstraction that binds service requests to a signed KMS-derived residency proof (compact hash chain), 2) a per-route delegation filter that projects RBAC v2 grants into least-privilege delegations and prevents operator escalation across geozones, and 3) an in-memory audit-seal cache that reduces KMS signature load while preserving non-repudiable audit chains for forwarding.

Summary of changes:
- service/attest-wallet: new package implementing ResidencyAttestWallet (creates short-lived attestations signed with region-scoped CMKs, exposes Verify/Embed APIs used at gateway and routing layers)
- gateway/middleware: add AttestWalletMiddleware which attaches attest payload to outbound responses and validates inbound claims (fallback to online verification if cache miss)
- auth/delegation: DelegationFilter that evaluates RBAC v2 decisions and emits scoped operator delegations; rejects delegations that would broaden residency scope or add cross-region service roles
- audit/forwarder: AuditSealCache which caches signed seals (KMS wrappers) for recently seen operation digests and provides TTL-based cache invalidation plus cryptographic replay-resistant proof (nonce chaining)
- integration tests and e2e harness updated to simulate multi-region KMS and operator delegation scenarios
- docs: architecture note and API surface doc for public SDK use

Checklist:
- [x] Implement ResidencyAttestWallet prototype
- [x] Implement DelegationFilter and wire into auth pipeline
- [x] Add AuditSealCache with configurable TTLs and eviction metrics
- [x] Unit tests for wallet, filter, cache
- [x] Integration tests for KMS fallback path and cache miss/rehydration
- [x] Update console schema to display attest status per-request
- [x] Add migration note for operators using legacy delegation header

Compatibility notes:
- The new wallet uses an additional header X-Redwood-Attest in internal service-to-service calls; backward compatible when header absent (wallet will attempt transparent verification via token proof).
- DelegationFilter is opt-in behind feature flag auth.delegation_projection (default: off for 72 hours rollout).

CI: initial run failed on lint (golangci) due to naming in attest-wallet; fixed in commit 3; integration flakes observed in KMS simulator (transient), added retry and a KMS simulator seed.

Migrations/deployment:
- Feature flag gate + canary rollout: start with 5% of traffic for tenant-scoped CMKs, then 25/50/100 once metrics stable
- Observability: new metrics added (attest.cache_hit_rate, delegation.filter_rejects, audit.seal_sign_rate, audit.seal_cache_ttl_evictions) and tracing spans (attest.wallet.verify, delegation.filter.eval)

Security rationale:
- Minimizes KMS usage by caching small sealed hashes rather than signing full payloads on every request
- DelegationFilter enforces residency invariants: an operator delegation cannot expand the region set for a request and cannot add roles not derivable from the base RBAC grant
- The attest proof includes a KMS signature + monotonic nonce so auditors can validate forward-only progression of attestations

Commits summary:
- a1b2c3: initial attest-wallet skeleton, tests
- d4e5f6: wire middleware into gateway and add header plumbing
- 7a8b9c: implement DelegationFilter + RBAC projection logic
- 0f1e2d: add AuditSealCache, eviction policy, metrics
- 3c4b5a: fix lint naming and add integration retry for KMS simulator
- 6d7e8f: docs and migration notes, console panel change

Files changed (high level): ["service/attest-wallet/wallet.go", "service/attest-wallet/wallet_test.go", "gateway/middleware/attest_middleware.go", "auth/delegation/filter.go", "audit/forwarder/seal_cache.go", "audit/forwarder/seal_cache_test.go", "integrations/tests/residency_e2e.yml", "docs/arch/residency-attest-wallet.md", "console/schema/requests_attest.json"]

Review thread and timeline:
- 2026-02-10 (PR opened by Aisha Tan): initial description and prototype attached
- 2026-02-11 (Connor Li): "High level looks good. Two asks: 1) add explicit TTL and staleness metric, 2) show a sample signed attestation format in docs." (author reply: implemented sample in docs and exposed attest.cache_ttl_seconds metric)
- 2026-02-12 (Marisol Vega): "Concern: how does the DelegationFilter interact with existing operator escalation whitelist? Please add unit test that simulates operator with multi-zone privilege." (author reply: added filter unit tests and guard to consult operator-whitelist; if operator is on whitelist, delegation is allowed but we emit strong audit tag)
- 2026-02-13 (Ethan Park): "CI flakes on KMS sim, consider deterministic seeds for tests and exponential backoff for signer." (author reply: added deterministic seed option and retry backoff)
- 2026-02-15 (Connor Li, approved): "Approvals from security side, minor nits addressed."
- 2026-02-16 (Merge queue): CI green, canary gating config added to deployment manifest

Notes from reviewers:
- Added suggestion to surface per-tenant attestation age in Console request inspector (implemented)
- Suggested audit retention policy: keep attest seals 90 days by default; made TTL configurable via audit.seal_cache.ttl_days

Release notes: "Added Residency Attest Wallet to produce compact KMS-backed residency proofs, a DelegationFilter for RBAC v2 projection to prevent cross-region operator escalation, and an Audit Seal Cache to reduce signing load while preserving non-repudiable audit chains. Opt-in via feature flag auth.delegation_projection; see docs for migration and console support."

Risk and mitigation:
- Risk: misconfigured TTL could allow stale attestations to be accepted. Mitigation: default conservative TTL (60s for cache hits, 90d for offline sealed proofs), observable alerts on attest.cache_hit_rate drops and delegation.filter_rejects spikes.
- Risk: operator whitelist could bypass residency guard. Mitigation: whitelist changes require APPROVAL queue and are surfaced to audit with elevated retention.

Conclusion: This change provides a practical balance between cryptographic assurance for regional KMS usage and operational cost by caching short sealed proofs. It is feature-flagged and rolled out in controlled canaries. Everything merged with squash once CI passed.

payload.body:
Context: KV cache compaction/eviction is rolling out behind flags. During canaries we need a deterministic, oncall-friendly way to disable compaction immediately (or gate it to a safe minimum) without requiring a full runtime restart, while preserving allocator invariants and avoiding relocation-in-progress hazards.

This PR adds the config/feature-flag plumbing and a safe-disable path (“kill switch”) for KV compaction + related relocation behavior. It also wires metrics/tracing so oncall can validate that the disable took effect, and links to the runtime runbook + rollout guardrails.

What changed: (1) Introduced runtime config keys under `kv.compaction.*` with sane defaults for release/runtime-1.22: `kv.compaction.enabled` (bool), `kv.compaction.kill_switch` (bool, higher priority than enabled), `kv.compaction.budget_ms_per_tick` (int), `kv.compaction.budget_bytes_per_tick` (int), `kv.compaction.min_fragmentation_ratio` (float), and `kv.compaction.force_background_worker_off` (bool). (2) Added control-plane config subscription wiring to the runtime config registry so these keys can be flipped via existing rollout tooling; includes “last applied config version” and “last applied timestamp” tracking. (3) Implemented safe-disable semantics: kill-switch causes (a) scheduler to stop granting compaction budget immediately, (b) background worker to stop accepting new relocation tasks, and (c) relocation state machine to transition to a quiescent point (finish current page move if already in a copy/commit section, then stop). The goal is to avoid leaving partially-relocated blocks or dangling references; correctness is preferred over instantly aborting mid-copy. (4) Added oncall-exposed counters + gauges: `kv_compaction_config_kill_switch{}` (0/1), `kv_compaction_config_enabled{}` (0/1), `kv_compaction_config_version` (gauge), `kv_compaction_disable_inflight_moves_total` (counter), and `kv_compaction_disable_wait_ms` (histogram) so we can see whether we were blocked waiting to reach a safe point. (5) Tracing: added a lightweight span event `kv_compaction.kill_switch_applied` with config version + node id to correlate with any tail-latency spikes around a disable. (6) Docs pointers: updated internal docs links in code comments to `sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/runtime-kv-cache-compaction-runbook.json` and `hosted-api-tail-latency-guardrails.json` (SRE guardrails). No user-facing docs.

Operational behavior (intended): - If `kill_switch=true`, compaction does not run regardless of `enabled`. - If `enabled=false` (kill_switch false), compaction is disabled but we still export config metrics; relocation state machine remains loaded but idle. - If config propagation is delayed, nodes continue with previous config; metrics include applied version so rollout system can detect stragglers. - On shutdown/restart, persisted config is re-read at boot, so kill-switch is sticky across restarts.

Notes on safety: Kill-switch does not hard-cancel a relocation that is already in a critical section. Instead we wait for a “commit boundary” (copy -> pointer swap -> free old) and then stop. This avoids a correctness class where we’d lose KV pages or leave allocator free-list inconsistent. Oncall expectation: disable should apply within <100ms under normal load; we record if it takes longer.

Files/areas touched (high level): - `runtime/config/kv_compaction_config.{h,cc}` new config keys + validation - `runtime/control_plane/config_subscriber.cc` registry wiring + version tracking - `runtime/kv/compaction/compaction_worker.cc` kill-switch checks + quiesce - `runtime/kv/compaction/relocation_state_machine.cc` quiescent boundary handling - `runtime/scheduler/scheduler_loop.cc` compaction budget gating on kill-switch - `runtime/observability/metrics_kv_compaction.cc` config + disable metrics - `runtime/tracing/kv_compaction_spans.cc` event emission - tests: `runtime/kv/compaction/test_kill_switch.cc`, `runtime/config/test_kv_config_validation.cc`

Small illustrative snippet: `if (cfg.kv.compaction.kill_switch) { budget = 0; worker->RequestQuiesce("kill_switch"); }`

Testing: - Unit: config validation, kill-switch override ordering, quiesce boundary behavior - Integration: scheduler loop doesn’t grant budget with kill-switch on, even with fragmentation trigger - Soak: repeated flip enabled/disabled/kill_switch under synthetic churn; asserts no allocator invariant violations - Manual: verified config flip via rollout tool updates metrics within propagation window

Rollout plan: This is a prerequisite for canarying compaction allocator changes (PR-19357/19371). Landed in release/runtime-1.22 so we can use it during canary expansions. Kill-switch authority remains SRE oncall (per guardrails doc), with runtime TL as escalation.

Links: - Linear: ENG-4826 (kill-switch/config), ENG-4829 (release plan) - Jira: INT-11904 (dashboard standards follow-up), SUP-28433 (OOM/high churn mitigation path) - Related PRs: pr-19357 (allocator changes), pr-19371 (scheduler budgeting), pr-19405 (tracing spans)

Review conversation (highlights): - Sean Gallagher: asked for explicit metrics proving kill-switch applied + a bound on “time to quiesce.” Added `disable_wait_ms` histogram and documented expected behavior in comments. - Rafael Mendes: requested oncall steps + clarity on whether kill-switch persists across restart. Updated config boot path and added a note in runtime runbook link comment; verified sticky behavior. - Omar El-Sayed: questioned whether we should abort mid-move to reduce tail latency during incident. We chose correctness-first and added the counter `disable_inflight_moves_total` so we can see when we had to wait. - Allison Grant: asked to align metric naming with standards; renamed gauges to `kv_compaction_config_*` and added labels consistent with other runtime configs.

CI: First run failed `cfg-lint` due to missing docs link in new config file; fixed and reran. Final checks green: build (linux), unit tests, integration tests, sanitizer, config-lint.

Merge: Squash-merged into release/runtime-1.22. Backport not required (feature is new).

payload.body:
Motivation: Close remaining parity gaps between Redwood's /v1/chat.completions adapter and OpenAI semantics around stop heuristics, streaming sentinel resolution, and function/tool output shaping. Users observed edge cases where: 1) stream fragments could emit duplicate sentinel indicators (partial stop tokens) leading to downstream parsers seeing multiple 'stop' events; 2) function/tool responses in framed JSON envelopes did not always include the canonical metadata keys OpenAI clients expect (name, arguments, parsed_args) causing client-side deserialization errors; 3) logprob reconciliation for partial deltas produced inconsistent scores for final tokens when stop tokens were synthesized by the adapter.

What this PR does (high level): Implements a deterministic sentinel coalescer for stream fragments, upgrades the framed JSON tool envelope to include a stable signature and secondary metadata fields for backwards compatibility, and normalizes logprob fallback logic so token-level probabilities agree with the non-streaming path. The changes are additive and gated under the existing v1 adapter flag; default behavior for customers is unchanged unless they opt into the stricter OpenAI-parity mode via the compatibility toggle.

Checklist:
- [x] Add stream sentinel coalescer that merges adjacent partial stop deltas into a single sentinel emission
- [x] Ensure final chunk emits a single canonical stop event with normalized index mapping
- [x] Extend toolcall envelope: include "tool_name", "tool_args_raw", "tool_args_parsed" and keep legacy "name"/"arguments" keys for older clients
- [x] Reconcile streaming logprob deltas with batch logprob computation for identical prompt+model seed
- [x] Add unit tests for parser edge cases and an end-to-end e2e test using mock client
- [x] Update docs/openai_compat.md with expected framed envelope shape and migration notes

Compatibility/rollback: All code paths are behind the v1 compatibility toggle. If downstream issues are reported, ops can flip the adapter flag to revert to prior behavior without restarting serving instances. No customer-visible new API surface; only response envelope additions (backwards compatible).

Testing performed: Local unit tests, e2e harness with mock OpenAI client, CI run (lint, go tests, python sdk smoke) — CI initially failed on a flaky fragment test which was fixed by increasing inter-fragment buffer tolerance and adding a strict coalescer test. See commits for details.
Diego Martinez: I like the sentinel coalescer but can you add a short comment describing why we choose to merge on byte-boundary vs token-boundary? (clients observed UTF-8 split edgecases)
Asha Patel: Added explanation + a test that fakes UTF-8 split fragments to ensure we don't generate invalid JSON. See coalescer_test.go: TestUtf8SplitSentinel
Karen Li: The tool envelope change is safe, but we should preserve exact key names for legacy clients. Suggest keeping both "arguments" and "tool_args_raw". Also request a changelog entry for the SDK team.
Asha Patel: Preserved legacy keys and added the SDK smoke test. Changelog note added to docs/openai_compat.md under Migration -> SDK updates.
Omar Rahman: Observed a small perf regression on the canary (p95 token latency +1.8ms). Can we micro-opt the coalescer to avoid extra allocations?
Asha Patel: Optimized buffer reuse in coalescer (replaced a temporary slice allocation with a pooled buffer). Re-ran canary, p95 delta reduced to +0.4ms and accepted.
Diego Martinez: Approving after Buffer reuse optimization and test green. +1
Karen Li: LGTM
Omar Rahman: Approved

Motivation: we see frequent short-lived bursts (1-10s) that spike per-invocation percentiles and cause noisy alerts even though downstream client perceived latency remains acceptable. This makes SRE triage expensive and obscures real regressions. Summary: add an Invocation Stabilizer service (runtime-side aggregator) plus a fidelity-aware metric gating layer that prevents percentile/alert updates until a configurable minimum of high-fidelity samples are available. The stabilizer computes lightweight per-invocation EWMAs and emits stabilized metrics (invocation.stabilized.{p50,p95,p99}, invocation.stabilized.count) and fidelity tags (fidelity=low|medium|high). The gating layer in PromQL/Alertmanager uses those fidelity tags to mute or route noisy alerts to a lower priority channel until fidelity stabilizes. This PR includes: - the stabilizer implementation in the serving runtime (stateless worker that consumes invocation probes, computes EWMA aggregates, and annotates traces/metrics) - Prometheus rule changes and new recording rules for stabilized series - Alertmanager rule templates and an adjusted SLO alert that is fidelity-gated - Grafana dashboard (dashboard/json) for the stabilizer: time series, fidelity distribution, noise window histogram, and alert-suppression heatmap - playbook (docs/playbooks/invocation-stabilizer.md) with rollout, verification, and rollback steps - unit and integration tests + an observability CI job to validate recording rule correctness Checkout notes: this description contains the checklist, rollout plan, and links. Checklist: - [x] Stabilizer core implementation (src/observability/stabilizer.go) - [x] Recording rules and gating templates (monitoring/prometheus/rules/stabilizer.rules.yml) - [x] Dashboard (grafana/dashboards/invocation-stabilizer.json) - [x] Playbook and runbook (docs/playbooks/invocation-stabilizer.md) - [x] Unit + integration tests (pkg/observability/stabilizer_test.go, tests/integration/stabilizer_e2e.yaml) - [x] CI job (ci/observability-stabilizer.yml) - [x] Backwards-compatible metric names and opt-in feature flag (env: OBS_INVOCATION_STABILIZER=true) Links: - Linear: ENG-1149 - Support ticket: SUP-4021 - Design doc: internal/notes/invocation-stabilizer-design.md (internal link) Rollout plan summary: 1) Deploy stabilizer behind feature flag to a small subset of serving nodes (canary) and emit stabilized metrics alongside raw metrics. 2) Observe fidelity distribution over 48h. 3) Flip Prometheus gating in read-only mode (no alert suppression) and run the CI recording-rule validation. 4) Enable gating for a small set of non-critical SLOs for 24h. 5) Gradually expand gating scope to critical SLOs and all regions. Rollback: flip OBS_INVOCATION_STABILIZER=false or revert Prometheus gating rules. Why this is safe: stabilized metrics are emitted in parallel and metric names are opt-in; alerts are gated rather than deleted. Backwards compatibility preserved for any consumer of raw series. Performance: the stabilizer runs per-invocation in a lightweight path (1-2 allocations); measured overhead ~0.2ms per invocation in microbenchmarks (see design doc).
Miguel Santos: noted that EWMA alpha should be configurable per-tenant; added tenant override support and tests.
Danielle Cruz: requested clearer dashboard panels for fidelity distribution; updated graphs with cohort breakdown and tooltip docs.
Omar Khalid: asked for Prometheus rule labels to avoid high-cardinality explosion; scoped fidelity tag cardinality and added production-smokecheck.
Priya Nair (author): responded to all comments, pushed fixes in f1e2d3c, and added a short benchmark report to the design doc.
Adds an opt-in Invocation Stabilizer that emits stabilized latency percentiles and fidelity tags; introduces fidelity-aware alert gating to reduce noisy SRE alerts. Requires updating Prometheus recording rules during rollout. Backwards compatible and opt-in via OBS_INVOCATION_STABILIZER.
If noise increases after gating disable Prometheus gating templates and flip OBS_INVOCATION_STABILIZER=false. Look for sudden drop in raw metric cardinality or missing stabilized series in the first 10 minutes after deployment.

Summary: Introduces the initial version of the changelog generator used to produce customer-visible model release notes (Console + docs) and internal audit-focused notes from model metadata change events. This adds (1) an event ingestion layer (with idempotency), (2) category mapping + severity normalization, (3) a templating system aligned to the customer release notes taxonomy/style guide, and (4) strict public vs internal field filtering/redaction. Motivation: Today model/version changes are visible inconsistently across model registry, runtime config, and ad-hoc docs. Support escalations (e.g., SUP-28411) show we need a single, consistent change artifact generated from the same events that drive rollouts. This PR is the first end-to-end piece: given a stream of ModelMetadataChanged/ModelVersionPromoted events, produce deterministic changelog entries and expose them via an internal API consumed by Console and docs build. Scope: In scope: generator library + small service wrapper, templates, category mapping rules, redaction/publication rules, and test fixtures. Out of scope: full docs-site integration (tracked separately) and subscription notifications.

Key design points: Event-driven generation (per ADR-0143) with deterministic output. We generate an entry keyed by (model_id, model_version, event_id) and write it to ChangelogEntry storage. Reprocessing is safe (idempotent) and does not create duplicates. Public vs internal fields: The generator takes a ReleaseNoteVisibility policy (PUBLIC | INTERNAL) and filters fields accordingly. We default to PUBLIC for anything leaving the control plane boundary. Internal entries may include oncall hints and infra-only details, but MUST never be returned to non-admin Console roles. Category mapping: Maps raw changes into the standardized taxonomy: security, breaking, perf, quality, bugfix, deprecation, and other. Severity language is normalized (low/medium/high) and constrained for public notes (no unreviewed claims about quality improvements). Templates: Templating uses a small DSL (Go templates with a restricted function set) so we can update phrasing without code changes, while still keeping outputs structured (title, summary, impact, guidance links, metadata block).

Implementation details: New package: internal/changelog (core generation engine + mapping). New service: services/changelog-generator (HTTP + queue worker wrapper around the engine). Storage: adds changelog_entries table (or equivalent backing store) with fields for model_id, model_version, visibility, category, severity, rendered_markdown, rendered_json, source_event_id, and created_at. API: Internal endpoints: GET /internal/changelog/v1/entries?model_id=...&visibility=public|internal&limit=... and GET /internal/changelog/v1/entries/{entry_id}. These are intentionally internal-only; Console uses a separate backend-for-frontend endpoint that enforces RBAC (added in subsequent PR). Redaction: Applies allowlist-based field selection for PUBLIC output. Any unknown/internal-only fields are dropped. Additionally, we redact freeform strings if they match banned patterns (e.g., internal hostnames, incident links, ticket references) using a conservative sanitizer. Tests: Adds fixtures for common change events: version promotion, tokenizer/runtime bump, quantization profile change, deprecation window change, and security patch. Includes golden tests for rendered outputs to prevent template drift.

Review/rollout notes: This PR is intended to land behind an internal feature flag changelog_generator_v1. After merge, we will dogfood by generating entries for a small subset of models in staging, then enable writes in prod with READ-only consumers initially. Follow-ups will wire Console UI and docs generation to the API, and add CI checks for preview artifacts.

Manual testing: Ran worker locally with recorded events from staging; verified deterministic output and redaction behavior. Verified that PUBLIC output contains no internal links/tickets and that INTERNAL output preserves operator notes.

Docs: Template wording and categories align with the customer release notes taxonomy/style guide; any future wording changes should occur in template files + golden tests.

Risk: Primary risk is accidentally leaking internal information in PUBLIC output. Mitigations: strict allowlist, sanitizer, golden tests, and a required security review on template changes.

Screenshots: N/A (service/library).
2025-10-10 (Jada Williams): The overall flow looks good. Two concerns: (1) idempotency key should include visibility; otherwise you can overwrite internal vs public accidentally, and (2) category mapping for tokenizer/runtime changes might be breaking depending on compatibility constraints. Can we make the mapping consult metadata.compatibility? 2025-10-10 (Michael Nguyen): Good catch. Updated idempotency key to (model_id, model_version, visibility, source_event_id). Also updated mapping to treat tokenizer/runtime bumps as breaking only when compatibility_constraints change or min_runtime_version increases across the pinned major. Added tests. 2025-10-11 (Connor O'Brien): Template updates need to be safe to change without accidentally altering meaning. Please add golden tests for at least security + breaking + perf and enforce restricted template functions. 2025-10-11 (Michael Nguyen): Added restricted function map (no arbitrary eval/exec). Added goldens for security/breaking/perf + a deprecation example. 2025-10-11 (Marcus Lin): Public redaction: allowlist is good, but the sanitizer pattern list is risky and brittle.
