Problem: The fleet provisioner occasionally oscillates (fast scale up followed by rapid scale down) when tenants concurrently change committed capacity or when burst requests cluster. Root cause analysis shows two interacting feedback loops: short-window utilization spikes trigger immediate reservation adjustments, while downstream allocator eager preemption produces downstream utilization dips that feed back into the controller, causing a wobble. This PR adds a "provisioning wobble attenuator" that reduces reactivity for short-lived utilization spikes while preserving throughput guarantees. It also introduces a utilization report normalizer to remove sampling artefacts from the percentile reports used by commitment reconciler.

Summary of changes:
- New stabilizer package (pkg/provisioner/stabilizer.go) implementing a two-stage smoothing: reservoir smoothing + asymmetric hysteresis. The controller uses a rate-limited apply path to avoid thrash.
- Introduce CommitWobbleIndex metric and promql extractor (pkg/metrics/commit_wobble_index.promql) used by alerting and dashboards.
- Utilization normalizer (pkg/telemetry/utilization_normalizer.go) that debounces shard-level sampling noise and tags stabilized series for downstream consumers.
- Autoscaler config knobs (configs/autoscaler/stabilizer.yaml) to tune short-burst damping and steady-state aggressiveness per pool.
- Integration tests (e2e/provisioner/stability_test.go) that replay historical spike traces and assert SLA adherence and absence of oscillation.
- Docs and dashboard updates (docs/observability/provisioner-metrics.md, dashboard/provisioner-wobble.json).

Behavior and safety notes:
- Defaults are conservative: wobble attenuator disabled for pools with >99.99% uptime SLAs unless explicitly enabled by ops.
- All changes behind a feature flag: feature.provisioner.wobble_attenuator.
- The new code path is covered by unit+integration tests; e2e uses recorded traces from incidents/2026-01-22 to validate regression.

Testing:
- Unit suite: 84 new unit tests, local run passes.
- e2e: stability tests added; CI replay harness ran on a 3-node test fleet in seat-labs.
- Prometheus rules updated and verified in staging dashboards.

Related work: ENG-4210 (wobble detection), ENG-4211 (telemetry normalization), SUP-3345 (post-incident follow-up), and previous autoscaler smoothing PRs.

Checklist:
- [x] Code compiles and unit tests pass
- [x] Integration / e2e tests for stability
- [x] Feature flag controlled
- [x] Docs updated
- [x] Telemetry / dashboards updated
Diego Ramos (2026-03-01): Can we avoid double-counting when normalizer tags series? If normalizer emits both raw and normalized series downstream it might inflate quota evaluation. Request: add a clear contract in telemetry README and an opt-in tag for consumers.
Asha Patel (2026-03-01 reply): Good point, I added an explicit tag 'normalized=true' and updated docs to indicate downstream consumers should prefer normalized series. Also gated emission behind feature flag for staging only.
Nina Kapoor (2026-03-02): Tests look solid. Please add an integration-level assert that the CommitWobbleIndex stays < 0.02 for 95th percentile of the replayed trace; otherwise LGTM.
Asha Patel (2026-03-03 reply): Added assertion and updated replay trace to include a longer tail. CI e2e passes now.
Liam O'Connor (2026-03-04): Small nits on comments and a suggestion to expose knob via Console UI rather than only YAML. Not blocking.
Asha Patel (2026-03-04 reply): Filed ENG-4228 for Console knob work and added a TODO in configs comment.

## Summary
Implements the first end-to-end console UI for the Usage Insights breakdown view (Route × Model) with filter state, drill-down navigation, loading/error/empty states, and basic table UX.

This PR is intentionally scoped to the interactive breakdown table + related page chrome. It assumes the query API exists (see pr-23135) and wires up the request/response to the UI. Export and Top Drivers are handled in separate PRs.

## User-facing behavior
- New Console section: **Usage → Cost Insights (Beta)** → **Breakdown**.
- Table supports:
  - Time range (7d / 30d / custom)
  - Project/workspace selector (existing Console control)
  - Deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) when available
  - Region filter when available
  - Route (normalized) and Model (family/version bucket) filters
- Drilldowns:
  - Clicking a row navigates to a detail view pre-filtered to that route+model combination (keeps time range + project).
  - Breadcrumb and "Back to breakdown" preserves filter state.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: We currently surface token-level cost and latency breakdowns and long-tail alerts, but we lack a compact, query-efficient signal that captures the delta between streamed/committed tokens and final generator decision sequences across invocations. This causes noisy alerts for streaming-heavy routes and makes it hard to prioritize log capture for expensive anomalies. This PR introduces two orthogonal improvements: (1) a compact-delta aggregator (stream-delta-meter) that computes a lightweight fingerprint and byte/ token delta histogram per invocation, suitable for rollups; and (2) a span-primer sampler that prefetches higher-fidelity logs and span context for invocations whose compact-delta signatures match configured entropy or pattern thresholds. On top of those we add a contextual alert gating policy (quiet_gate) that reduces alert churn by conditioning alerts on delta stability and recent run-rate of similar fingerprints. Summary of changes: - Introduce stream-delta-meter: a runtime-side metric that emits per-invocation compact hashes, token delta counts (prefetch vs commit), and a small entropy score. Aggregates are designed for rollup storage (low cardinality keys + reservoir histograms). - Add span-primer sampler: a lightweight pre-sampler integrated into the observability sidecar which, given a fingerprint and entropy, will pre-attach a small log buffer and request span enrichment only for candidates above a configurable threshold. The sampler is tunable per-tenant and per-route. - Add quiet_gate alert conditioning: a filter that subscribes to compact-delta rollups and SLO state; alerts are muted for short windows when matched fingerprints have stable low-entropy behavior, and re-enabled when variance increases. - Dashboard additions: new panels in observability/default-invocations.json showing compact-delta heatmap, delta-to-cost scatter, and primer hit-rate. - Tests and benchmarks: unit tests for aggregator, e2e system test with synthetic streaming traces, and a small perf benchmark to ensure meter adds <1% p99 overhead under 1000req/s on local bench. Design notes and rationale: - Compact deltas are intentionally lossy: we trade exact reconstruction for low-cardinality signal useful at scale. The hash + histogram allows joining to traces when we escalate only for interesting patterns. - Span-primer reduces log storage and rate of expensive span hydration by steering enrichment to likely-high-value invocations. - quiet_gate is a pragmatic middle-ground between strict suppression and noisy alerts; tuned conservatively by default. Checklist: - [x] runtime metric implementation and unit tests - [x] sidecar sampler + integration tests - [x] dashboard panels and example queries - [x] alert rule + default gating policy - [x] perf benchmark and basic throughput test Deployment plan: staged rollout by tenant: 1) feature off by default in main; 2) enable for internal telemetry-qa tenant and observe primer hit-rate; 3) ramp to canary for <10% of traffic on observability namespace with quiet_gate in monitoring-only mode; 4) flip gating to active after 48h stable canary. Rollback: feature flags at runtime for both stream-delta-meter and span-primer; quiet_gate can be disabled centrally. Backwards compatibility: metric schema adds a v2 tag; aggregators fall back to v1 path when v2 not present. Related work: this complements existing prefetch-warmup-metrics (pr-577890) but focuses on compact fingerprints and gating rather than prefetch efficiency. Also ties into token-cost-atlas efforts for downstream attribution. Review notes: reviewers asked for clear cardinality constraints and privacy review for hashing; hashing scheme uses HMAC with tenant key and is documented in SECURITY.md. Performance testing and CI: CI run passed (unit/integration/linters). Benchmarks included microbench script results in /observability/bench/compact_delta/bench.md. Post-merge action items: (1) add a telemetry dashboard to SLO-runbook linking primer hits to alert history, (2) schedule a short playbook with oncall to observe quiet_gate behavior for first week.
Lina Park: Please add estimated cardinality upper-bounds for the compact hash and verify tenant isolation. Author reply: Added HMAC scheme and cardinality notes in docs; hash space limited to 64-bit and bucketed by route. Mateo Alvarez: Can we ensure the sampler won't increase p99? Requested perf test. Author reply: Added microbench and CI perf check, verified <1% p99 increase at 1k rps. Ruth Brenner: Suggest default quiet_gate thresholds be conservative. Author reply: lowered default sensitivity and added feature flag for aggressive gating.
Added compact-delta aggregator and a context-aware span primer sampler to reduce observability noise and improve targeted log capture. Includes new dashboard panels and an alert gating policy to reduce churn. Disabled by default; staged rollout required.
payload.title: Introduce compact-delta aggregator and span-primer sampling with contextual alert gating

payload.body:
Motivation: In high-fragmentation workloads we observed oscillation between aggressive eviction and immediate rehydration of recently-evicted pages, causing elevated I/O and CPU under moderate memory pressure. This PR introduces a lightweight page lifecycle (active -> stashed -> soft-quarantined -> released) to reduce churn, plus a backpressure-aware release path that defers low-value releases during transient pressure spikes.

Summary: Implement a 'soft-quarantine' state for KV pages that have been candidate-evicted but are kept in a compact, compressed slab for a configurable grace period. While in soft-quarantine pages consume less resident memory accounting but can be restored without full spill-reload. The eviction path now signals the scheduler about transient pressure via a ReleaseFence token; release decisions use hysteresis windows and tenant-fairness weights so we avoid repeated evict/rehydrate cycles for hot tails.

Key changes: - page lifecycle state machine and in-memory compact store (server/kv/cache/soft_quarantine.go) - eviction hysteresis in the evictor; introduces short-term holdback and time-decay scoring (server/kv/evictor/evictor.go) - backpressure-aware release router that uses metrics from the scheduler and autoscaler to throttle bulk releases (pkg/schedulers/backpressure_router.go) - metrics and traces for quarantine lifecycle and backpressure signals (server/kv/metrics/metrics.go) - unit + integration tests and a microbenchmark exercising oscillatory workloads (tests/kv/quarantine_test.go, benchmarks/kv/page_lifecycle_bench.go) - docs explaining configuration knobs and rollout guidance (docs/kv/quarantine.md)

Behavioral guarantees: - default config preserves existing memory accounting; quarantine is opt-in by cluster config. - under steady pressure the soft-quarantine reduces load by keeping recently-evicted pages cheap to restore (lower I/O). - under sustained pressure quarantined pages are progressively compacted and finally released once grace periods and tenant priorities allow.

Testing and results: Microbenchmarks on p3.xlarge-like nodes show a 22% reduction in average eviction-induced disk reads for our mixed chat+search workload and latency P95 improvements of ~8ms during eviction storms. CI includes unit tests, an integration test that simulates tenant skew, and a perf canary run.

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind 'kv_soft_quarantine' flag. Start on staging for 48 hours with default short grace, enable for canary tenants, then gradually increase grace period if metrics are favorable.

Related: ENG-1842 (eviction feedback loop), ENG-1907 (tenant fairness scheduling).
Samir Patel: Can you clarify memory accounting while a page is in soft-quarantine? The change in flags should not affect existing reserved memory calculations.
Author (Maya Chen): Soft-quarantined pages are tracked via a separate compact-resident counter and do not count toward the 'active_resident_bytes' metric by default. We added an opt-in toggle to include them in accounting for legacy customers.
Lena Ortiz: The hysteresis windows look sensible but we should make tenant weights pluggable for dedicated clusters.
Author (Maya Chen): Added TenantWeight hook and documented configuration; default weights preserve previous behavior.
Diego Alvarez: CI flaked on the canary perf run; re-ran and the perf canary now passes. Approving change.
Samir Patel: Verified metrics and traces on staging; overall looks good. Approved and squash-merge recommended.
Introduce optional 'soft-quarantine' page lifecycle for KV cache to reduce evict/rehydrate churn under transient memory pressure; adds eviction hysteresis and backpressure-aware release router. Feature is gated and off by default.
Enable 'kv_soft_quarantine' in cluster config. Start with short grace period (5s) and monitor 'kv.quarantine.restore_rate' and 'kv.eviction.hysteresis_misses' metrics. See docs/kv/quarantine.md for step-by-step rollout.
This PR focuses on reducing churn for workloads with frequent temporal locality flips. It is intentionally conservative: quarantine durations and memory accounting are configurable so we can tune per-cluster behavior during rollout.
payload.title: KV: soft-quarantine page lifecycle with backpressure-aware release and eviction hysteresis

payload.body:
This change updates the OpenAI compatibility adapter to support the latest Responses API variant semantics (responses/v21) and fixes several edge cases we saw in production around streaming reassembly, client-specified randomness hints, and metadata passthrough. Motivation: customers using mixed toolcall/streaming workloads saw corrupted interleaved chunks when a retry or connection hiccup caused fragments to arrive out-of-order; at the same time the new responses endpoint exposes a client_seed/rng_hint header and a top-level metadata map that must be preserved through our bridge to avoid breaking ordered sampling and downstream telemetry. Goals: 1) reliably preserve client-provided seed/rng_hint and advertise it through our internal tracing and rerunnable request token so deterministic behaviors are reproducible; 2) introduce per-stream fragment IDs and a small reassembly window to safely reorder/recombine chunked frames without harmful buffering latency; 3) ensure top-level metadata and user_tags are passed unchanged through the OpenAI adapter and surface in fulfillment logs and observability; 4) add schema-strict mode for structured-output use-cases to fail-fast on malformed JSON payloads instead of producing silent parsing errors. Summary of changes: core adapter: accept and forward X-OpenAI-Client-Seed / X-OpenAI-RNG-Hint headers into the responses envelope; wire seed into request trace and into the deterministic key used by the runtime caching layer. Streaming layer: attach fragment_id + sequence_index to each outbound chunk; accept incoming chunks that include those attributes and reassemble using a small out-of-order buffer with a 200ms adaptive timeout (configurable). Toolcalls and structured output: add an escape prefix for toolcall boundaries to prevent accidental merging when fragments split JSON boundaries; add a schema-strict flag that uses the JSON schema returned by the model to validate top-level structured responses and return a 422 to callers if strict validation fails. Observability & testing: add unit + integration coverage for reassembly, seed propagation, and metadata passthrough; new e2e playbook 'responses-v21-tear-up' simulates flaky connections and interleaved toolcalls. Backwards compatibility: adapter falls back to old behavior when fragment metadata is missing; client-seed is optional and will not affect existing RNG behavior unless provided. Risks / compatibility notes: small behavioral change when schema_strict=true could cause callers that previously tolerated malformed JSON to receive 422; marked label "breaking-change-candidate" for product review.
Omar Singh: This overall approach makes sense but we should avoid using a hard-coded 200ms window; can you expose an adaptive config breakpoint and document performance tradeoffs?
Maya Patel (author): Agree, made the timeout configurable via fragment_reassembly_timeout_ms and added a note in the docs about latency vs safety tradeoffs
Elena Ruiz: The toolcall escape prefix looks fragile if model output itself includes the sequence. Can we instead add an explicit toolcall marker field on chunk frames?
Maya Patel: Switched to an explicit chunk-level 'toolcall_marker' boolean on frames; fallback remains the textual escape for older bridges; added tests for both paths
Kai Nakamura: Unit tests look good. Integration run failed once due to a flakey CI network simulation; re-ran and passed. Approving after minor nits fixed.
Product-Manager (FYI): Marked as breaking-change-candidate; please surface to the release notes and notify SRE teams before rollout.
Add OpenAI responses/v21 compatibility: preserve client seed and RNG hints, robust streaming fragment reassembly with configurable timeout, metadata/user_tags passthrough, and optional schema_strict validation for structured outputs. NOTE: schema_strict=true may cause 422 on malformed model JSON.
Ops: rollout gate: enable fragment reassembly by default in staged regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1), notify SRE to watch fulfillment parsing error alerts and latency. SDK: bump HTTP client to include X-OpenAI-Client-Seed when caller sets deterministic sampling.
payload.title: OpenAI adapter: preserve client-seed, robust stream fragment reassembly, and metadata tag passthrough

payload.body:
Motivation: Customers in regulated environments asked for stronger guarantees that operator actions (operator service accounts, platform operators, human ops) cannot be used to access keys or data outside of an explicitly pinned region. Existing RBAC v2 rules cover role bindings but do not prevent an operator token minted in one region from being used with a different CMK or from being routed through a cross-region KMS proxy. This PR implements a layered guardrail: (1) session-scoped operator tokens that encode the origin region and permitted service-bound KMS scope; (2) a KMS wrapping validator which rejects key-unwrapping requests that violate the token's declared region; (3) RBAC enforcer adjustments to treat session token attributes as first-class predicates; and (4) audit header middleware to emit immutable provenance headers for downstream indexing.

Summary of changes (high level):
- Add session token generator (api/middleware/session_scope.go) that issues short-lived JWT-like tokens with region, service, operator_id and scope claims; tokens are non-refreshable and bound to a single operator action window.
- Introduce kms/wrap/validator.go which implements server-side checks for unwrap/wrap calls; enforces a policy allowlist per-region and returns structured error codes (KMS_REGION_VIOLATION) when violated.
- Extend rbac/enforcer to consult session token claims for attribute-based decisions (rbac/enforcer.go). This allows policy like "allow operator:scale-deploy if session.region == service.region".
- Add audit/middleware/provenance_injector.go that sets X-Redwood-Provenance (signed) and X-Redwood-Region headers and marks them immutable for downstream processors.
- Add compliance doc: docs/compliance/region-token-workflow.md with example flows and threat model.
- Helm chart tweak for private installs: charts/private/values-region-pin.yaml to surface the KMS wrapping allowlist as a configurable block.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc approved by Security & Compliance (linked in Linear ENG-3321)
- [x] Unit tests for token validator and kms/wrap checks
- [x] Integration test that simulates cross-region unwrap and asserts rejection
- [x] Backwards-compatible to existing token formats (we fallback to legacy tokens if no region claim present)
- [x] Docs updated
- [x] Migration plan included in docs for private installer

Commits included:
- "add: session token generator and middleware (Nadia Park)"
- "feat: kms wrapping validator and error codes (Samir Patel)"
- "refactor: rbac enforcer to accept attribute predicates (Evan Liu)"
- "chore: add docs and helm values for region pinning (Priya Raman)"

Files changed (illustrative):
- api/middleware/session_scope.go
- kms/wrap/validator.go
- rbac/enforcer.go
- audit/middleware/provenance_injector.go
- docs/compliance/region-token-workflow.md
- charts/private/values-region-pin.yaml
- test/integration/region_kms_unwrap_test.go

Review conversation (abridged, chronological):
- Evan Liu (Reviewer): "Overall looks solid. Two concerns: token size (we need to keep header small for streaming gateways) and whether the validator will add measurable latency for high-throughput unwrap calls. Can we micro-benchmark?"
- Nadia Park (Author): "Agree on both points. Token uses compact claims and is gzipped in transit for streaming; added benchmark harness in test/perf/kms_wrap_bench.go and attached numbers to the PR description (median +1.8ms on unwrap path under 95th percentile)."

- Priya Raman (Reviewer): "Policy semantics LGTM, but we should expose a debug metric for denied unwraps and a flag to opt-out in emergencies. Please add a metric and an operator override path with audit."
- Nadia Park (Author): "Added metrics.kms.unwrap.denied and an emergency flag kms.wrap.allow_cross_region (defaults to false for private installs). Documented emergency procedure in the compliance doc."

- Samir Patel (Reviewer): "Nit: suggest using structured audit reason codes so downstream can aggregate (e.g., reason=kms_region_violation). Also add unit tests for legacy token fallback."
- Nadia Park (Author): "Added reason codes and unit tests for legacy token path."

CI & checks:
- Unit tests: pass (coverage for changed modules >= 88%)
- Integration tests: pass (region_kms_unwrap_test simulated cross-region unwrap and returned expected denial)
- Linter: pass (golangci-lint)
- Helm lint: pass
- Security scan: informational warnings about token entropy; addressed in design doc

Performance note: micro-benchmarks (test/perf/kms_wrap_bench.go) show an additional ~1.5-3ms median latency on KMS unwrap when the validator is enabled (mostly due to claim parsing and HMAC verification). We added caching for token verification keyed by token hash with a 30s TTL which reduces impact for repeated operations.

Migration and rollout plan (ops):
1) Deploy middleware and validator in shadow mode for 48h in staging; collect metrics.kms.unwrap.denied and provenance header coverage.
2) Enable enforcement behind feature-flag for 10% of traffic in production (canary) and monitor for false positives.
3) After 72h stable canary, enable 100% and publish compliance note to accounts.

Backward compatibility: Legacy client tokens without region claims are accepted but cause the validator to fall back to a conservative deny-for-cross-region behavior (i.e., deny unwrap if target CMK region differs from request origin when no explicit consent is present). This protects customers during rollout but requires accounts to rotate to region-scoped tokens for full functionality.

Security considerations: The design minimizes risk by making tokens short-lived, non-refreshable, and tied to operator_id + action nonce. All provenance headers are signed with a server key (rotated via KMS) and cannot be overwritten by upstream. Emergency override requires a signed operator action and is auditable.

Merge outcome: PR was approved by all reviewers, CI green on green build, and merged via squash. Change log entry created and docs published to the compliance space. The private-installer chart change is gated behind a release flag and will be included in the next private release train.
Add operator session tokens bound to region and service; enforce KMS wrapping policy for cross-region key usage; middleware injects immutable audit headers for session provenance. No user-facing API change.
payload.title: Location-scoped operator tokens and KMS wrapping guardrail

Summary: Implements an operator shielding layer that enforces RBAC v2 constraints at the operator graph level and validates KMS-origin proofs for service-submitted encryption envelopes. Also introduces a sealed-audit gateway which normalizes, tags, and signs audit records with region and origin metadata before they are emitted to downstream sinks. This is an opt-in safety control intended for Dedicated and Private deployments that require strong operator isolation and cryptographic provenance of KMS usage.

Motivation & context: Several customers and internal audits identified two related risks: (1) operator principals with broad operator-like permissions being able to escalate across tenant boundaries via ephemeral admin flows, and (2) ambiguous KMS-origin metadata making it hard to prove that a given ciphertext was produced by an allowed provider/region. This PR addresses both by adding a graph-based RBAC enforcement layer that evaluates operator reachability and by validating KMS-origin assertions embedded in envelopes at ingress. Paired with the sealed-audit gateway, we get a tamper-evident, region-aware audit trail that improves compliance posture.

What I changed (high level):
- rbac/graph: new enforcement engine that computes operator reachability, supports time-bound grants, and denies paths that cross tenant isolation boundaries unless explicitly permitted.
- kms/attestor: component that verifies envelope provenance claims (KMS provider ID, region tag, attestation signature) and rejects envelopes with missing or invalid proofs.
- audit/sealed_gateway: HTTP service that accepts internal audit events, enriches with region/operator provenance, signs the payload with a host-managed audit key, and forwards to configured sinks (S3, BigQuery, Kafka).
- config: new feature flags (operator_shielding.enabled, kms_origin_proof.required, audit.sealed_gateway.enabled) with default off for existing hosted tenants.
- tests: unit and integration tests for graph evaluation, a KMS attestation fixture, and end-to-end flow tests for audit signing and sink delivery.
- docs: design doc and runbook additions under docs/security/operator-shielding.md and deploy notes in private-installer/README.md.

Commits (summary):
- 9d1a7f0: add rbac graph evaluator + unit tests
- 1c7b3e2: introduce kms origin attestor + envelope schema changes
- 7f4b2a9: sealed-audit gateway initial implementation + signer interface
- a0c6f88: wire feature flags and config knobs; add gating checks in request pipeline
- 5b2ff11: integration tests and fixture updates
- 8d3e9b4: docs + runbook + upgrade notes

Files/areas touched (representative):
- rbac/graph/evaluator.go
- rbac/graph/README.md
- api/middleware/operator_shield.go (new middleware in request pipeline)
- kms/attestor/attestor.go
- kms/attestor/testdata/envelope-proofs.json
- audit/sealed_gateway/main.go
- audit/sealed_gateway/signer.go
- audit/sealed_gateway/README.md
- config/features.yaml
- private-installer/README.md (deploy note)
- docs/security/operator-shielding.md
- tests/integration/operator_shield_flow_test.go

Small illustrative snippets (kept minimal):
- rbac graph check (pseudo):
  if evaluator.PathCrossesIsolation(subject, target) && !policy.AllowCrossTenant(subject, target) {
      return deny("cross-tenant operator path")
  }

- KMS attestor validation (pseudo):
  valid := attestor.VerifyEnvelope(envelope)
  if !valid { return reject("invalid kms provenance") }

Review conversation (condensed, chronological):
- Lukas Chen (requested changes, 2024-11-20): "Please add a unit test covering timebound grants where the grant expires mid-flight — we had a similar edge-case in ENG-5123."
- Maya (author, 2024-11-21): "Added timebound grant tests and clarified evaluator semantics; left a comment on design doc about eventual refactor to use WASM for policy expressions."
- Priya Rao (comment, 2024-11-23): "We should gate the registries for audit signing keys behind KMS-backed HSM keys in Private installs. Also add a metrics counter for attestation failures."
- Maya (2024-11-24): "Wired metrics.counter.kms_attest_failures and added config checks for requiring HSM-backed signing in private-install docs."
- Adrian Gomez (approval with comment, 2024-11-28): "Approving — one small nit on log verbosity in graph evaluator (reduced); see inline."

CI history: initial CI run (2024-11-19) failed on a flaky integration test (operator_shield_flow_test.go), reran after adding a small wait fix in the test harness; subsequent runs passed (all checks green: unit, linters, integration-on-docker, e2e-smoke). Final CI status: pass.

Backward compatibility & migration notes:
- This change is opt-in via feature flags; default is off for hosted tenants to avoid unexpected rejects.
- For Dedicated/Private customers who enable kms_origin_proof.required, they must ensure their envelope-producing KMS (CMKs) attach the new provenance headers (provider-id, region, attestor-signature). We added a small helper library (kms/attestor/client.go) to help partners emit compliant envelopes.
- Audit gateway can be deployed sidecar or as a central service; deploy notes included. The gateway signs with a local key and publishes key metadata for offline verification; operators should rotate signing keys via documented procedure.

Security review & compliance impact:
- SEC performed a security review on 2024-11-26 and signed off on the design provided the HSM-backed signing requirement is followed for regulated customers.
- The feature enables stronger evidence collection for KMS usage and reduces operator blast radius by preventing implicit operator escalation paths.

Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2024-12-03 after all approvals and green CI. Changelog entry created under CHANGELOG.md and release notes prepared for the next patch release.

Follow-ups / future work:
- Replace expression evaluator with sandboxed WASM policy expressions (ENG-9002).
- Add telemetry-driven policy simulation mode to measure the impact before turning on enforcement.
- Implement tokenized audit export format for long-term archival to meet retention and zero-knowledge audit scenarios.

If you want to try it locally: see docs/security/operator-shielding.md and run tests with TEST_KMS_ATTEST_FIXTURE=1 make test-integration."
Adds operator-scoped RBAC graph enforcement, a KMS origin attestor for incoming envelopes, and a sealed-audit gateway that tags and signs region-bound audit entries. Backwards-compatible; opt-in via config flags for Private/Dedicated installs.

payload.body:
Motivation: current canary and shadow controllers support linear phased rollouts but lack expressive policy primitives to represent non-monotonic cohort promotions and resumable recovery after partial failures. This PR adds a decision-lattice execution model, a deferred-promote policy (time- and metric-gated delayed promotions), and snapshot-based resumable recovery for in-flight cohorts. Summary: implements a compact decision-lattice runtime, new rollout policy CRD fields (deferWindow, quorumExpression, snapshotRetention), snapshot capture and restore hooks, and operator-level reconciliation for resumable promote/abort. Backwards compatibility: existing rollout specs are unchanged and map to the lattice's default path. Main changes: new controller and reconciler, policy validation and migration script, operator metrics and tracing, e2e tests for pause/resume and snapshot restore, and CLI tooling to inspect lattice state. How it works: rollout is translated into a directed acyclic lattice of states where nodes represent cohort states and edges represent labeled transitions with guard expressions. A deferred-promote policy attaches a time-window and metric expression to promote transitions; if the guard evaluates false during the window the transition is re-evaluated at a configurable cadence. Snapshot-based resumable recovery captures minimal cohort state (traffic positions, KV cache markers, evaluation buckets) before risky transitions and stores them in the rollout namespace with lifecycle TTL. On controller restart or partial failure the reconciler can restore the last snapshot and resume the lattice execution, or fall back to a safety rollback path if snapshot integrity fails. Config examples: rollout.spec.policy: {"type":"deferred-promote","deferWindow":"10m","quorumExpression":"p95.latency<120&&errorRate<0.005","recheckInterval":"30s","snapshotRetention":"1h"} Implementation notes: optimized snapshot format uses compressed protobufs; snapshots are stored as k8s secrets encrypted with cluster KMS when available. We added unit tests covering guard parsing, checkpointing, and snapshot GC, plus integration scenarios with heterogeneous cohort quorums (latency-sensitive cohorts promoted independently). Testing: local canary e2e (kind cluster), a scaled simulation harness validating lattice topologies under injected failures, and benchmark runs measuring reconcilation tail-latency (no measurable regressions). Rollout of this feature will be gated behind a feature flag in the console and an opt-in annotation on rollout objects. Checklist: implement controller and reconcile loop, add CRD validation and conversion webhook, add snapshot store with KMS integration, add metrics and traces, add CLI inspect command, add e2e tests, update docs and examples, add migration script for existing staged rollouts. Risks and mitigations: snapshot size explosion mitigated by incremental checkpoints and TTL; snapshot restore safety validated by checksum and schema version; deferred-promote can cause extended partial exposure — we added global safety TTL and automatic rollback if total exposure exceeds budget. Related: Linear ENG-4127, ENG-4450.
Evan Morales: Please add a short-circuit path for the lattice when the rollout annotation `redwood.io/skip-lattice` is set; otherwise operator will do unnecessary work.
Author (Aisha Patel): Added skip-lattice check and unit tests in a1b2c3e. Also added CLI flag to force evaluation even when skipped.
Priya Singh: Can we ensure snapshot encryption falls back gracefully when KMS is not configured? edge clusters should not fail the whole reconcile.
Author: Yes, snapshots default to namespace secrets unencrypted but flagged with audit metadata; when KMS is available controller uses envelope encryption. see snapshot/store.go for logic.
Luca Romano: Minor nit on metrics cardinality for lattice node labels; prefer coarser labels to avoid high cardinality in long-lived clusters.
Author: Reduced label dimensions and added aggregated gauges.
Added decision-lattice rollout engine with deferred-promote policy and resumable snapshots. Feature is behind a feature flag and requires opt-in via rollout annotation. See docs for CLI inspection and migration steps.
payload.title: Decision-lattice for staged cohort promote with deferred-promote policy and resumable snapshot recovery

payload.body:
Problem: RBAC v2 policy rollouts and subsequent policy drift are currently hard to correlate with historical audit records. Multiple teams asked for an auditable, tamper-evident way to bind served access decisions to the exact policy that produced them. This PR introduces two related pieces: 1) a deterministic policy fingerprint (hash + stable normalization) computed at policy compile time and embedded in the policy bundle metadata; 2) an audit canonicalizer that enriches and normalizes audit events with that fingerprint plus compact KMS key metadata (provider, region, key-id-hash) to make retention/forensics queries precise. Motivation: enable post-hoc verification that a given allowed/denied event was evaluated against the same policy snapshot operators expect, and reduce false-positive drift alerts during policy rollouts. Changes: - Add policy fingerprint generator and validator in the RBAC compiler pipeline. Fingerprints are computed using canonical JSON (stable key ordering, type coercion rules) and SHA-256, base64-url encoded. - Embed fingerprint into policy bundle manifest and service discovery so runtime decision caches and authorizers include the fingerprint in decision traces. - Add audit canonicalizer service that: normalizes timestamp formats to RFC3339-UTC, ensures stable header keys (x-rw-audit-...), attaches policy_fingerprint, a short kms_key_meta (provider:aws|gcp|azure, region, key_hash), and a canonical request-id -> hashed operator mapping for privacy-preserving operator attribution. - Enforce on-accept path: when enforcement mode is enabled, the authorizer rejects a decision if the runtime policy fingerprint does not match the bundle fingerprint declared by the control plane (prevents silent drift from out-of-band changes). - Migrations: backfill script to compute fingerprints for historical policy bundles and re-run canonicalizer over the last 30d of audit events to produce enriched records in the audit-s3/forwarder path (non-destructive). - Feature flag gating and staged rollout: default is "report-only" with a canary group (5% tenants) for enforcement. Ops runbook and console indicators added to track enforcement rejections. Checklist: - [x] fingerprinter implementation + unit tests - [x] runtime authorizer integration + integration tests - [x] audit canonicalizer service + e2e test harness - [x] backfill script + dry-run mode - [x] console UI badge + docs - [x] CI gating job to prevent accidental fingerprint regeneration - [x] rollout plan and runbook attached to Linear tickets
Marco: Can you explain collision surface and why SHA-256+B64 is sufficient?
Priya: SHA-256 with canonical JSON normalization is our threat model; collisions are considered infeasible for our retention and audit window. We also include a 6-char human-readable short-id for quick lookups.
Anya: Is there an operator privacy concern with attaching policy fingerprints to decision traces?
Priya: We only include the policy fingerprint and a hashed operator id (HMAC with a per-tenant salt stored in the secrets store) to allow attribution without leaking raw operator identifiers. See audit canonicalizer docs for the privacy design.
Samir: Rollout: how do we handle mismatch spikes during canary?
Priya: We start in report-only mode for 7 days and surface mismatch metrics to console + alert to sec-oncall if mismatch rate > 0.5% for canary tenants. Enforcement can be toggled per-namespace via feature flag.
Anya: CI check to prevent accidental fingerprint churn looks good; please add a clear error message.
Priya: Added better error message and a link to docs in the CI job.
Marco: LGTM after two small nits (naming + comment); approved.
Merge: squash and merge after green CI.
Add deterministic RBAC V2 policy fingerprints and an audit canonicalizer which enriches audit events with policy_fingerprint and compact KMS metadata. Backfill tool provided to reprocess recent audit events. Default: report-only; enforcement can be enabled via feature flag.
payload.title: Declare policy fingerprints and audit canonicalizer for tenant anchoring

payload.body:
Motivation: On multi-GPU tensor-parallel (TP) workloads we observed periodic stalls and poor tail latency due to inefficient interleaving of collective operations (NCCL) and compute kernels. The runtime was launching kernels with a naive round-robin stream assignment which caused kernel/comm contention, suboptimal kernel placement, and missed opportunities to prefetch KV cache entries in time for subsequent microbatches. This PR introduces a heuristic-driven kernel affinity scheduler and a small KV-window prefetcher that together increase overlap between comm and compute and reduce context-switch overheads.

What this PR changes: 1) A lightweight affinity heuristic (runtime/scheduler/affinity_scheduler.cpp) that classifies kernels by predicted device memory working set, comm participation (collective vs local), and expected duration. Affinity rules prefer assigning high-comm kernels to isolated comm streams while GPU-heavy compute kernels land on compute-optimized streams. 2) Kernel bundling: adjacent small kernels are grouped to reduce kernel launch overhead for short-lived ops. 3) KV-windowed prefetcher (kvcache/prefetcher.cpp) which issues early KV prefetches for the next N microbatches when the affinity heuristic predicts a contended comm phase. The window size is tunable per deployment and conservatively defaults to 2 microbatches. 4) NCCL adapter updates to annotate collective launches with affinity hints and to expose a lightweight async progress hint for host-side pacing (nccl/adapter.cpp). 5) New telemetry and histograms (observability/tp_affinity_metrics.*) to track comm/compute overlap, kernel stream distribution, and KV-prefetch hit rate. 6) Feature flag tp_affinity_v2 (config/feature_flags.yaml) - opt-in by default for safety.

Benchmarks: Microbenchmarks run on 8xA100, sequence length 1024, synthetic batching with mixed prompt lengths. Results: p50 ~ +3% throughput, p95 latency -12%, overall token/sec +9% for typical real-world mixes (documented in tests/integration/tp_affinity_bench.py). Gains are most pronounced at p95 and under mixed-size request distributions.

Compatibility and safety: The scheduler is conservative by default and the feature is gated behind tp_affinity_v2. When disabled behavior is identical to baseline. The KV-window prefetcher includes memory safety checks and refuses to expand the window if device memory headroom is below a configured threshold.

Testing and CI: Added unit tests for the affinity rules and prefetch heuristics (tests/unit/test_affinity_scheduler.cpp, tests/unit/test_kv_prefetcher.cpp) and an integration benchmark used in perf CI (tests/integration/tp_affinity_bench.py). CI initially flagged a flaky allreduce deadlock during the first integration run; root cause was a missing barrier in the nccl adapter when a prefetch completed concurrently with stream reordering. Extra synchronization and a retry path were added to fix the flake.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-1824) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration perf bench - [x] Feature flag and safe defaults - [x] Observability metrics - [x] Release notes entry

Notes: This change touches the kernel scheduler and NCCL integration path; recommend a staged rollout with canary on Dedicated before enabling broadly. The heuristics are intentionally lightweight; future follow-ups can add topology-aware optimizations and ML-driven affinity estimation.

Introduce a heuristic kernel affinity scheduler and KV-windowed prefetch to improve overlap between NCCL collectives and compute for tensor-parallel workloads. Default disabled behind tp_affinity_v2 feature flag. Expected improvement: p95 latency -12%, throughput +9% on 8xA100 for seq=1024 workloads.
Maya Chen: Please add accounting for transient device allocations in the affinity heuristic; without that we risk overcommitting when kernels allocate temporary buffers. Also add unit test that simulates a small headroom scenario.
Arjun Patel (author): Added transient alloc tracking and a unit test that triggers the memory-guard behavior when headroom < 10%. See tests/unit/test_kv_prefetcher.cpp commit c54d21f.
Lena Torres: Strong preference to keep the feature off by default in hosted for at least one release cycle. Please ensure the flag default is false and document rollback steps.
Arjun Patel (author): Confirmed tp_affinity_v2 defaults to false in config/feature_flags.yaml and added a rollback paragraph to docs/release_notes/tp_affinity_v2.md.
Omar Haddad: How does this behave on heterogeneous topologies (NVLink vs PCIe)? We should avoid worse-than-baseline cases. Consider falling back to baseline when detected cross-node bandwidth is low.
Arjun Patel (author): Added topology-weighted affinity multiplier and a safe fallback to baseline when measured link bandwidth between peers falls below configured threshold. See affinity_scheduler.cpp update.
Maya Chen: CI integration bench flagged an allreduce hang on first run, please describe the mitigation.
Arjun Patel (author): Root cause was a race between host-side prefetch callback and stream reorder; added a lightweight barrier in nccl adapter and a retry path for in-flight collectives. Covered by integration test enhancements.
Merged by Maya Chen via squash merge. Squash commit message: 'tp: heuristic-driven comm/compute kernel affinity + KV-window prefetch (ENG-1824)'. Deploy gated behind tp_affinity_v2=false by default; follow rollout plan in docs/release_notes/tp_affinity_v2.md.
Follow-ups: 1) topology-aware cost model (ENG-1902) 2) automatic window tuning via light-weight sampling 3) extended metrics for per-model affinity auditing. Recommended canary on Dedicated for 48h before enabling hosted customers.

Motivation: production customers asked for a compact, declarative way to express retry, hedging and reconnect decisions that can be compiled once and consumed by all SDKs and the serving runtime. This PR introduces a small opinionated rules language (Resilience Rules Language, .rrl) and an accompanying compiler that emits a portable policy manifest. We ship lightweight bindings for Python / TypeScript / Go so SDKs can consume the manifest and expose ergonomic helpers for streaming reconnection and hedged requests.

What changed (high level):
- Add a rules compiler (pkg/resilience/compiler) that validates and compiles .rrl -> JSON policy manifest with deterministic evaluation order and simple predicates.
- Add a runtime evaluator (pkg/resilience/eval) used by the serving runtime and by SDK test harnesses.
- Python SDK: add redwood.resilience.PolicyLoader and async helpers (async with PolicyLoader.from_manifest(...)) plus streaming RetrySession wrapper that resumes pulls with checkpoint hints.
- TypeScript SDK: add ResilienceManager, typed policy manifest client, and a reconnect decorator for async iterables.
- Go SDK: add resilience.Policy and Resumer interfaces, small helper for hedged requests.
- Docs: new docs/resilience-rules.md with examples and migration guide.
- Tests: end-to-end tests that compile example rules and exercise SDK bindings against a local runtime shim.

Checklist: 
- [x] Compiler + manifest schema, with unit tests
- [x] SDK bindings (py/ts/go) + integration tests
- [x] Docs + migration guide
- [x] CI passing (one flaky test retried)

Backward compatibility: the manifest reader is additive and old SDKs ignore unknown attributes; no mandatory runtime change required to adopt. We did make one small surface simplification: the previous streaming helper name stream.resume_token was deprecated in favor of stream.checkpoint_token. A compat shim is provided for one release cycle.

How to adopt: compile your rule files using pkg/resilience/compiler into a manifest and distribute that manifest alongside your service config. SDKs can load the manifest at startup (PolicyLoader.from_manifest(path)) and optionally attach a Policy to streaming calls or request decorators. See docs/resilience-rules.md for examples that cover simple retry windows, hedging with jittered offsets, and opt-in fast-fail-on-429 policies.

Performance note: the compiler output is intentionally compact; the manifest evaluation is microsecond-class per decision in the Go evaluator and introduces negligible overhead in hot-paths. In our load tests (see benchmark-lab samples linked in the doc) applying a typical 3-rule manifest added ~0.6% median CPU and reduced incidentous cold-retry churn by ~21%.

Related: ENG-3245, ENG-3301, SUP-78.
Evan Park: Compiler looks solid; two nits on error messages in compiler.go to make line numbers clearer (see inline). Also suggest adding a fuzz test for malformed predicates.
Maya Thompson: Addressed both nits; added line-aware errors and a small fuzz harness under pkg/resilience/fuzz_test.go. Pushed a follow-up commit.
Linh Nguyen: TypeScript API ergonomic question: can we expose a smaller 'wrap' helper instead of requiring direct manager usage?
Maya Thompson: Added ResilienceManager.wrap(asyncIterable) sugar and updated examples in docs. Kept advanced APIs for advanced users.
Samir Patel: Integration tests fine, but one flaky test 'TestHedgingTiming' failed twice on CI before passing locally. CI rerun green; added extra jitter in test to stabilize.
Introduce Resilience Rules Language (.rrl) and cross-SDK bindings. Adds a compiler that outputs a portable policy manifest and lightweight SDK helpers to apply reconnect, retry and hedging policies in streaming and request code paths. Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs receive new ergonomics for policy loading and streaming resume. See docs/resilience-rules.md for migration steps.

Motivation: During sustained latency SLO pressure some tenants experience hard failures or abrupt degradation. This change implements a thresholded SLO relay that (1) enforces soft per-tenant delegation when local SLOs cross configured thresholds and (2) bridges requests to a lower-cost, lower-QoS "soft" circuit rather than immediately tripping a hard circuit breaker. The relay is conservative by default and is controlled by a runtime flag (runtime.slo_relay.enabled).

Design summary: The SLO relay runs inside the request router and maintains an exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) of observed tail latency and error rate per tenant-window. When metrics cross a configured threshold (tenant_slo.window_ms and tenant_slo.error_rate_pct), the relay starts steering a configurable percentage of new requests to an attached soft circuit (soft-circuit reduces concurrency and uses a degraded model variant). The soft circuit responds with an explicit header indicating degraded path. The relay supports graceful un-winding: if the SLO metrics return below the release threshold for a cooldown period, traffic is phased back to normal.

Key characteristics: single request-level plugin with no model change, feature flag gated, tenant-configurable thresholds, hysteresis and cooldown windows to prevent flip-flopping, integrated telemetry and traces (relay.decision and relay.reason tags). The relay complements the existing circuit-breaker by deferring hard tripping until soft-circuit saturation is reached.

Implementation notes: - New module: src/runtime/slo_relay.go implements EWMA windows and routing decisions. - Soft circuit abstraction: src/runtime/soft_circuit.go encapsulates degraded model selection, reduced concurrency pools, and circuit health counters. - Router integration: router/mux.go updated to consult SloRelay.Decide(ctx, tenant) and tag routed requests. - Configuration: ops/helm/values-shedding.yaml adds flags and sane defaults used in CI tests. - Observability: metrics added (relay_decisions_total, relay_rollbacks_total, relay_duration_ms), tracing span "slo_relay.decision" and structured logs for auditability.

Testing & validation: Unit tests added for decision logic and hysteresis: tests/unit/slo_relay_test.go. Integration tests simulate tenant latency spikes and verify phased delegation and rollback: tests/integration/relay_integration_test.go. Canary run: deployed to staging and 10% of production traffic for 48 hours with synthetic spike generator. Observed behavior: relay took effect when tail p95 crossed configured threshold, soft-circuit served 18% of traffic with no client-visible errors, system CPU increased by ~2% under test.

Rollout plan: Feature is behind runtime flag runtime.slo_relay.enabled. Rollout schedule: 10% traffic for 24-48h (monitor relay_decisions_total, svc_p95 and errors), 50% for 48h, full rollout. Abort criteria: sustained increase in client 5xx > 0.5 percentage points or p95 regression > 15% compared to baseline.

Migration and compatibility: No schema or API changes. Soft circuit adds a response header X-Redwood-Degraded: true when used. Customers may opt out by tenant config (tenant.slo_relay.mode=off).

Risks & mitigations: - Risk of double-routing causing increased cost: mitigated by conservative default delegation percent (10%) and global budget cap. - Risk of oscillation: mitigated by hysteresis windows and exponential cooldown. - Observability blind spots: added metrics and a dashboard to surface relay activity and tenant-level outcomes.

Follow-ups: - ENG-3003: add automated rollout canary gating to Console. - ENG-2240: enable per-model degradation profiles for better quality tuning.

References: Linear ENG-2145, manual runbook updates in docs/ops/graceful-relay.md.

Adds a thresholded SLO relay that delegates excess load to lower-cost soft circuits and introduces observability for relay decisions. Feature guarded behind runtime flag. Rolling rollout planned to 10% -> 50% -> 100% traffic. No breaking changes.

Samir Kapoor: Added comments next to the constants in slo_relay.go, and included rationale in docs/ops/graceful-relay.md. PTAL. (author reply)
Marcus Bell: Integration test was flaky locally — found a race on soft circuit counters, pushed a fix to use atomic increments. Re-running CI. (requested changes)
Samir Kapoor: Fixed atomic counter and added an extra integration assertion to prevent regression. (author reply)
Priya Deshpande: Observability looks solid; please ensure dashboard has tenant drilldowns. Approving after CI passes. (approved)
Lina Huang: Verified canary telemetry in staging; approving. (approved)

Motivation: Customers need safer, automated defaults for prefill/batching/caching and conservative quantization recommendations that preserve unit economics while minimizing latency and token cost. This PR introduces a lightweight Prefill Optimizer CLI and an interactive Quant Prober that produce tenant-specific default profiles (batch shapes, cache TTLs, quant tiers) from sampled traces and synthetic probes.

What this change does: introduces a new CLI command (redwood econ prefill-scan) that ingests a small trace or runs a synthetic sampler against a tenant workload, runs a constrained search over batch/cache/quant configurations, and emits: 1) a ranked set of default profiles for tenant deployment, 2) deterministic cost/latency estimates, and 3) a dry-run policy that can be applied as a prefill-policy via the existing policy API. The Quant Prober runs in two modes: safe-probe (low Q aggression for production sampling) and fast-probe (higher aggression for lab sims).

Design notes: the optimizer uses a constrained hill-climb with simulated KV-cache and microbatch costs (cost model pluggable). The prober includes a small microbenchmark harness that executes model micro-batches with representative sequence lengths to measure token latency deltas for fp16/int8/4-bit-like runtimes. Outputs are compact JSON profiles plus an human-readable summary.

Checklist: 
- [x] CLI scaffolding and help text
- [x] Prefill optimizer kernel + cost model integration
- [x] Quant prober harness + safe-probe mode
- [x] Unit tests and integration test with synthetic traces
- [x] Telemetry events for generated profiles
- [x] Docs stub and example output included

Rollout plan: merged behind feature flag econ.prefill_optimizer; staged rollout 10% tenants for 48h, monitor unit_econ.delta and latency.p95; fallback path included in CLI to revert policy.

Follow-ups (future PRs): add auto-apply heuristics, tenant GQL export, and a lightweight UI in Console for profile diffs.

Notes: this is intentionally conservative in quant aggressiveness — default profiles prefer batching + cache over aggressive quantization unless safe-probe metrics show minimal quality/latency regressions.
Liam: please add a guard to prevent applying profiles with >25% estimated quality delta. Rana: can we add an integration e2e that runs in the CI matrix? Diego: approve after unit tests and telemetry added. Author reply: added the guard and a small synthetic integration job, expanded unit tests to cover prober edge-cases. Final: 2 approvals, 1 comment resolved, CI green.
Add CLI 'redwood econ prefill-scan' to generate tenant prefill+batching+quantization profiles. Feature guarded behind econ.prefill_optimizer; view generated profiles in logs or export to policy API.

Motivation: We frequently need a lightweight, reproducible way to evaluate tenant workloads for affordability before applying global defaults (batching/caching/quant). This PR adds a synthetic-slate cost annotator that: 1) synthesizes small representative request slates from replay traces, 2) annotates candidate batch/cache/quant presets with an affordability score and delta unit-econ estimate, and 3) exports a compact 'quant exemplar' — a single representative quantization profile per tenant that can be used for dry-run validation and fast canaries. This enables safer defaults rollouts and an automated dry-run step in the defaults-as-code workflow. Summary of changes: Added a new service (pkg/econ/annotator) which ingests sample traces or synthetic slates, runs a fast simulation of batching/cache hit heuristics, and applies quantization simulation using the runtime's cost models. Introduced a CLI (tools/econctl) with a `annotate` subcommand for offline runs and a `dry-run --exemplar` flow which uploads results to telemetry. Integrated annotator with the defaults-import pipeline to surface exemplar suggestions in the Console. Tests, docs, and a light e2e smoke test were added. Motivation: Our presubmit pipelines have grown ad-hoc annotations for dependency lifecycle and readonly metadata in package manifests which makes automated tooling brittle and release automation noisy. This PR introduces a small, opt-in dependency lifecycle annotator service and a lightweight lint proxy to centralize presubmit-only rules. The annotator tags package manifests with machine-readable lifecycle metadata (stable/unsupported/experimental) and writes an annotations file under .ci/annotations.json for downstream stages to consume. The lint proxy provides a stable adapter between team-level lint configs and the monorepo presubmit runner so we can standardize lint exit codes and reduce duplicate rule ownership friction. A compatibility shim adapts legacy makefile targets and older release hooks to the new presubmit loader; this reduces bursty failures during rollout.

What this changes: single-line summary of changes (full list below): 1) New tool: tools/dep_lifecycle/annotator.py — inspects package manifests, consults the dep policy, emits annotations and a small caching layer. 2) Presubmit loader: ci/presubmit/loader.go — now reads .ci/annotations.json and exposes a lightweight API for other presubmit stages (fast path for unchanged modules). 3) Lint proxy: ci/lint/proxy.ts — a shim that normalizes different lint runners' outputs and maps to standardized presubmit severity levels. 4) Workflows: .github/workflows/presubmit.yml updated with an annotation-loading step and a new quick-lint job used for fast feedback. 5) Backwards-compatible shim: tools/compat/release-shadow.sh and make/compat.mk with guarded targets to preserve old developer flows.

Commits summary: - Add annotator implementation and tests - Wire annotator into presubmit bootstrap - Add lint proxy and couple of adapter modules for eslint/golangci-lint - Update presubmit workflow and add quick-lint job - Add compat shim and integration smoke tests - Fix flakiness in presubmit loader using a small exponential backoff for remote cache

Files changed (high level): ["tools/dep_lifecycle/annotator.py", "tools/dep_lifecycle/README.md", "ci/presubmit/loader.go", "ci/presubmit/loader_test.go", "ci/lint/proxy.ts", "ci/lint/adapters/eslint_adapter.ts", "ci/lint/adapters/golangci_adapter.ts", "make/compat.mk", "tools/compat/release-shadow.sh", ".github/workflows/presubmit.yml", ".ci/annotations-template.json", "docs/ci/annotator.md"].

Testing and CI notes: The PR initially failed the integration-smoke job because the annotator's cache path defaulted to /tmp and the integration runner ran with a noexec mount. I pushed a follow-up commit to honor CI provided TMPDIR and added a check to fallback to a repo-local cache under .ci/cache. After the fix, full CI passed: lint (pass after adapter updates), unit (pass), integration-smoke (pass on second run), e2e-release-smoke (pass), security-scan (pass). A limited rollout was done in staged presubmit lanes to validate that the quick-lint job reduced feedback latency by ~45% on typical PRs.

Migration plan and rollout: The annotator is opt-in per-package via a new field in package.yaml: ci.dependency_lifecycle: true|false. Teams can opt-in immediately; default behavior remains unchanged until the annotator runs as a presubmit step in all lanes. The lint proxy is behind a feature flag in the presubmit config: presubmit.lint_proxy.enabled. We communicated the rollout window on the internal #ci-tooling slack channel and provided a one-week grace period for team-level config updates. The compatibility shim guards are annotated and the old targets remain available for two weeks before we flip defaults.

Related work: ENG-7642 (dep taxonomy), ENG-7701 (presubmit fastpath), SUP-3412 (customer-reported flaky releases). Links to docs: docs/ci/annotator.md and tools/dep_lifecycle/README.md.

Ava Martinez (author): Good catch, added a manifest-only filter and exported a prometheus counter in the annotator. See commit 3.
Liam O'Connor: The lint proxy maps some eslint error codes to 'error' severity today; can we reduce that mapping to 'warn' for non-blocking stylistic rules to preserve fastpath throughput? Also, please add a short migration FAQ for teams that have custom eslint rules.
Ava Martinez: Adjusted mapping and added docs/ci/annotator.md + tools/dep_lifecycle/README.md with FAQ and a sample migrate.sh snippet.

Motivation: We observed a recurring class of incidents where localized backend instability causes a cascade of autoscaler reactions across tenant pools, amplifying latency spikes and causing swingy utilization signals. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) an Adaptive Fleet Degradation Shield (AFDS) — a lightweight controller that detects pool-level degradation patterns and applies short-lived isolation + soft-fallback policies to prevent noisy thrashing; and (2) a Throughput Telemetry Unifier (TTU) — a sidecar-style signal aggregator that reconciles token-level, request-level, and allocation-level metrics into a single smoothed throughput series fed to autoscalers and accounting. Together these reduce false positive scale-ups, keep tail latency bounded, and improve tenant fairness during transient failures.

Context: The perf-canary service (see perf-canary repo PRs) needs to call internal inference endpoints continuously from prod. We do not want to reuse broad internal scopes (or customer-style API keys) because (a) blast radius is too large, (b) auditing is noisy, and (c) it complicates incident response when we need to quickly disable only canary traffic. This PR introduces a restricted auth scope + service account intended solely for synthetic canary inference reads.

What’s in this PR:
- New auth scope: `inference.canary:read` (internal-only). This scope can only be minted for service accounts (not user tokens) and is denied in external auth flows.
- New service account type + default policy bundle: `svc-perf-canary` (control-plane managed). The policy allows:
  - POST `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions` against internal inference gateways
  - streaming responses
  - read-only access to model metadata needed for request normalization (canonical model + version)
  And explicitly denies:
  - any admin/control-plane routes
  - any write/update routes (model registry writes, routing config, quotas)
  - any endpoint that could return customer prompts/logs
- Gateway enforcement: inference gateway now recognizes `inference.canary:read` and applies additional constraints:
  - requires `X-Redwood-Canary: true` header (prevents accidental reuse)
  - requires `X-Redwood-Caller: perf-canary` (auditing/dedupe key)
  - enforces per-request caps: `max_tokens <= 512`, `n == 1`, `logprobs == false`, `store == false`
  - disables tool/function calling for canary scope (reduces surface area + variance)
- Audit logging: adds structured auth/audit fields `caller_type=service_account`, `service_account=svc-perf-canary`, `auth_scope=inference.canary:read` on inference gateway logs so we can correlate canary-driven load and quickly validate that the canary is not calling broader routes.
- Documentation: updates internal auth scope registry docs with ownership + rotation expectations for this scope.

Why this design:
- Least privilege: canary needs “generate tokens” but should not be able to mutate config or read any customer data.
- Fast kill-switch: we can revoke the service account or deny-list the scope at the gateway without impacting other internal tooling.
- Predictable observability: dedicated scope + headers make it easy to filter canary traffic from production dashboards and to attach clear attribution during incidents.

Operational notes:
- This PR does not create the service account secret/IAM bindings; that is wired in terraform (tracked under INT-2213 and ENG-4879). This PR only adds the scope, gateway enforcement, and policy plumbing.
- Backwards compatibility: existing internal inference callers are unchanged. The new scope is additive.

Test plan:
- Unit: added auth policy evaluation tests ensuring `svc-perf-canary` cannot access denied routes and cannot exceed request caps.
- Integration (staging): exercised canary token against internal gateway with synthetic requests; verified 200s on allowed routes and 403s/422s on denied/invalid requests.
- Observability: verified audit log fields present and that `X-Redwood-Canary` traffic is filterable in log explorer.

Rollout:
1) Merge this PR.
2) Apply terraform to create `svc-perf-canary` and mint a token restricted to `inference.canary:read`.
3) Deploy perf-canary with new token + required headers.
4) Monitor `inference_gateway_authz_denied_total{scope="inference.canary:read"}` and request volume for 24h.

Notes for reviewers:
- Policy lives under `authz/policies/service_accounts/perf_canary.yaml`.
- Gateway constraints are intentionally conservative to reduce both variance and abuse potential. If we need tool calling later for coverage, we should add a separate scope rather than expanding this one.

Related:
- perf-canary service skeleton: sources/github/perf-canary/pr-19201-bootstrap-perf-canary-service-skeleton.json
- Control plane config surface for canary targets: PR-19203
- Service account + secrets wiring (terraform): tracked under INT-2213 / ENG-4879
Sean Gallagher: Can we ensure this scope can’t accidentally be used from a laptop / user token flow?
Caleb Johnson: Yes — scope minting is restricted to service accounts only; added an explicit deny in the token issuer for user principals and a unit test covering it.
Logan Wright: Please add a stable audit field so we can filter canary traffic in metrics/logs without relying only on headers.
Caleb Johnson: Added `service_account` and `auth_scope` fields to inference gateway audit logs; headers are still required but audit is now authoritative for filtering.
Nadia Rahman: Request caps look good, but why hard-disable tool calling? That might reduce representativeness later.
Caleb Johnson: Two reasons: reduces variance for perf signals and removes a larger surface area for unintended side effects. If we need it, we should introduce a separate scope with explicit review.
Omar El-Sayed: Can we ensure the canary can’t set `store=true` / log prompts anywhere?
Caleb Johnson: Enforced `store==false` for canary scope at gateway validation. Also verified we don’t emit request bodies in logs for this scope.
Sean Gallagher: Approved after the service-account-only restriction + audit fields.
authz: register new internal scope inference.canary:read
authz: add svc-perf-canary service account policy bundle (allow inference generate routes only)
gateway: enforce canary scope constraints (headers, request caps, disable tool calling)
logging: add structured audit fields for canary service account traffic
tests: add authz evaluation + gateway request validation tests
Internal: add restricted `inference.canary:read` scope and `svc-perf-canary` policy bundle for safe production perf-canary inference calls.

Motivation: Tighten tenant-bound CMK usage assertions in the service-side KMS allocator and eliminate duplicate audit entries emitted by the log-forwarder when requests are retried. This change reduces the risk of cross-tenant key misuse and significantly lowers audit noise that has been confusing SREs and compliance reviewers.

What this PR does (high level):
- Enforces a tenant-scoped check in the runtime KMS allocator: requests that carry a tenant claim must be bound to the tenant's CMK alias or be explicitly allowed via a tenant-level exception list.
- Adds a deterministic CMK resolution path that prefers explicit tenant bindings, then tenant-affine regional fallbacks; misbindings now return a 403 with audit tag metadata.
- Implements an idempotent audit deduplication layer in the audit-forwarder: audit envelopes carry a new stable event_id derived from request UUID, tenant_id, and authorization version to prevent duplicate entries from retries.
- Adds e2e integration tests that simulate retries, regional failovers, and mixed-tenant traffic to validate both enforcement and dedup semantics.

Design notes:
- KMS assertion lives in runtime/kms/allocator and is gated behind feature flag feature.tenant_cmk_assertion (off by default for rollout). When enabled, allocator performs two checks: (1) tenant CMK alias matches request claim; (2) the CMK's region matches request's region pin when present.
- Audit dedupe is implemented as an idempotent envelope filter in observability/audit-forwarder. New audit_envelope.event_id is HMAC-SHA256(key=service-audit-key, data=tenant_id||request_uuid||auth_version). Envelopes with the same event_id within a 5m sliding window are collapsed. A metrics counter audit.dedupe.filtered is exposed.
- To preserve backwards compatibility we add a compatibility header X-Redwood-Audit-Event-V1 and a migration flag audit.forwarder.v2 (controlled via config).

Checklist:
- [x] Runtime allocator check with unit tests
- [x] Audit-forwarder dedupe with integration tests
- [x] Feature flag gating and rollout plan in README
- [x] Documentation updates (security playbook + console notes)
- [x] Linear/Jira links added to PR

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature flag off.
2) Deploy audit-forwarder with dedupe enabled in staging only; monitor audit.dedupe.filtered and audit.latency.
3) Enable runtime assertion in canary region for small subset of tenants with manual opt-in.
4) Gradually increase canary %, then globally enable after two maintenance windows with no elevated alerts.

Risk considerations:
- Misconfigured tenant aliases will lead to 403s; we added clear error codes and a console listing to help operators map aliases to tenants.
- Dedupe window trades off eventual de-duplication vs. potential suppression of legitimate replays; window default 5m is conservative and configurable.

Related: ENG-6234, PM-190, SUP-8121.

Owen Park: Can you explain how the HMAC key is rotated without invalidating the event_id window?
Priya Malhotra: Good question — the forwarder keeps a small grace list of previous keys (currently prev-1) and will accept event_ids computed with either the current or the preceding key for the duration of the window. Rotation steps are documented in docs/ops/rollout-playbooks.
Liu Zhang: There are a couple of places where we read tenant claims from headers; please ensure we prefer authenticated token claims not headers.
Priya Malhotra: Fixed in allocator.go — token claims are now canonical source, headers used only as fallback during ingress-layer compatibility. Updated unit tests to cover both flows.
Rana Singh: Needs an audit log schema bump? We should version envelopes so older consumers keep parsing.
Priya Malhotra: Added X-Redwood-Audit-Event-V1 header and migration flag as discussed.
Owen Park: CI flake on integration (timeout) — rerunning.

Enforce tenant-scoped CMK bindings in KMS allocator (feature-flagged). Add idempotent audit deduplication in audit-forwarder with metrics audit.dedupe.filtered. Admins should review tenant CMK mappings in Console before enabling. See docs/security/tenant-cmk-assertion.md for details.
If enabling feature.tenant_cmk_assertion, pre-populate tenant CMK alias mapping using console or the /admin/tenant-keys API. Monitor audit.dedupe.filtered and audit.forwarder.latency for first 24h. Key rotation must include prev-1 grace key as documented.
