payload.body:
## Summary
Adds end-to-end integration tests to validate route-level experiment bucketing correctness:
- Split distribution matches configured allocations over synthetic traffic (within tolerance)
- Deterministic assignment is stable across router restarts and config cache warm/cold scenarios
- Attribution fields (experiment_id, variant_id) are present on request context and emitted telemetry for the request paths covered by the tests

This is intended to de-risk beta/GA by catching regressions in bucketing inputs, stickiness key selection, and precedence behavior.

## Motivation
We’ve had a couple of staging/beta reports of skew that were hard to triage quickly (e.g., missing stickiness key leading to low entropy, cache/version mismatches, and subtle changes to hashing inputs). Unit tests cover the hashing function, but we didn’t have a black-box-ish test that:
- Exercises the full policy evaluation chain as wired in the router
- Validates actual variant selection distribution at scale
- Proves determinism across process restarts (the most common oncall question)

This PR adds those tests using the existing integration test harness + a synthetic traffic generator.

## Test approach
### 1) Split accuracy test (distribution)
- Sets up a route policy with an experiment of 3 variants: 70/20/10
- Generates N=200,000 synthetic requests with stable stickiness keys
- Records assigned variant from the response debug headers and from request context
- Asserts distribution is within tolerance:
  - absolute error <= 0.75% for 70% bucket
  - absolute error <= 0.6% for 20% bucket
  - absolute error <= 0.4% for 10% bucket

Tolerances were chosen to reduce flakiness while still catching meaningful regressions. With N=200k, expected sampling noise is small; these bounds are intentionally wider to account for any minor test harness overhead and to keep runtime bounded.

### 2) Determinism across restarts
- Executes a first pass assignment for a fixed set of 20,000 stickiness keys
- Restarts the router process (hard restart) and replays the exact same keys
- Asserts assigned variant is identical key-by-key

The test runs twice:
- With config cache warmed (pre-fetch experiment config)
- With config cache cold (router starts and fetches config on demand)

### 3) Guardrail/telemetry sanity
This does not assert guardrail behavior (owned by ENG-9028), but it does assert that:
- Responses include `x-redwood-experiment-id` and `x-redwood-experiment-variant` when the debug header flag is enabled
- OTel spans produced by the router include `redwood.experiment.id` and `redwood.experiment.variant` for sampled spans in this test environment

## Not included
- Streaming retry paths (covered by separate tests / recent fix PR)
- Multi-region determinism (still handled by ADR + unit tests; can be added when integration harness supports multi-region simulation)
- Statistical significance analysis

## Implementation details
- Adds `SyntheticTrafficRunner` helper that can generate deterministic keys and run parallel request batches while capturing variant headers.
- Adds `VariantDistributionAssert` that computes actual vs expected distribution and prints a diagnostic table on failure.
- Adds restart helper that performs a controlled router shutdown/start in the integration env to simulate real restarts.

### Example failure output
On failure we print a compact distribution table to speed triage:
Expected vs actual (N=200000)
variant A expected=0.70 actual=0.6621 delta=-0.0379
variant B expected=0.20 actual=0.2424 delta=+0.0424
variant C expected=0.10 actual=0.0955 delta=-0.0045
Top suspects: stickiness key entropy regression or hash input change.

## Files / areas changed
- `router/integration_tests/route_experiments/route_experiment_split_accuracy_test.go` (new)
- `router/integration_tests/route_experiments/route_experiment_determinism_restart_test.go` (new)
- `router/integration_tests/helpers/synthetic_traffic_runner.go` (new)
- `router/integration_tests/helpers/variant_distribution_assert.go` (new)
- `router/testdata/policies/route_experiment_70_20_10.yaml` (new)
- `router/testdata/policies/route_experiment_50_50.yaml` (new)
- `router/config/debug_headers.go` (small tweak: allow debug headers in integration env)
- `telemetry/otel/tags.go` (test-only assertion helper)

## How to run
- `./tools/test/integration -suite router -run RouteExperimentSplitAccuracy`
- `./tools/test/integration -suite router -run RouteExperimentDeterminismAcrossRestarts`

Runtime locally (M2, docker): ~5–7 minutes total.
Runtime in CI: ~9 minutes total (includes env spin-up).

## Risk
Low. Test-only changes plus a small integration-env-only knob for debug headers. No production path changes.

## Links
- Linear: ENG-9031
- Related: ADR-047 (deterministic bucketing), PR-28433 (bucketing evaluator)
- Support context: SUP-24831 (variant skew report)

---

## Commits
1. test(router): add synthetic traffic runner and distribution assertions
2. test(router): e2e test for 70/20/10 split accuracy
3. test(router): determinism test across router restarts (warm/cold cache)
4. chore(testdata): add policies for route experiment integration tests
5. ci: mark route experiment integration suite as required for rollouts label

## CI
- build-and-unit-tests: PASS
- integration-router: PASS
- lint: PASS
- race (selected packages): PASS

## Review conversation (highlights)
Jordan Lee: "Nice. Two asks: (1) please confirm we’re using the same stickiness key precedence order as prod; (2) can we print the hash inputs on determinism failures?"
Leila Farouk: "(1) yes, the test requests set `x-redwood-sticky-key` explicitly so we’re not relying on defaults; added a comment + explicit header. (2) added diagnostic output for the first mismatched key including the computed key string that feeds hashing (redacted to first 8 chars + length)."

Logan Wright: "Telemetry assertions: please avoid making these tests dependent on span sampling rate in CI. We’ve been tuning sampling and I don’t want flake." 
Leila Farouk: "Agreed. Changed the check from 'must see tags on N spans' to 'if any spans are exported for router, they must include experiment tags when experiment is active'. Also increased exporter buffer to reduce drops in the test env." 

Rafael Mendes: "Can we add tolerance justification in-code and keep the runtime bounded?" 
Leila Farouk: "Added comments + moved N and tolerance to constants. Also capped parallelism to avoid saturating CI runners." 

Sahana Iyer: "Integration suite is getting heavy; can we gate this so it only runs for rollouts/experiment changes?" 
Leila Farouk: "We still run it in required integration-router job for main, but added suite tagging so engineers can run it selectively; also reduced N from 500k to 200k after measuring stability." 

Approved-by: Jordan Lee, Logan Wright, Rafael Mendes

## Merge
Merged via squash into `main`.

payload.body:
Context: We see persistent tail latency bimodality on mixed interactive workloads where long prefill windows for some sessions block kernel reuse and trigger KV cache thrashing. Prior prefilling approaches either prefill large contiguous windows (high KV churn) or micro-chunk aggressively (excess kernel dispatch overhead). Motivation: reduce end-to-end tail latency without regressing throughput and keep per-tenant KV coherence across overlapping prefill/decodes. This PR introduces the Edge-sliced Prefill Orchestrator: a middle-ground that slices prefill work into edge-aligned segments that 1) align with kernel-friendly shapes, 2) expose overlap points for decode to start early, and 3) feed an updated KV demultiplexer to avoid cross-session cache eviction. Key changes (high level): - runtime/prefill/orchestrator.cpp: new orchestrator that allocates "edge slices" based on per-model token shape histograms and current KV pressure. Slices prefer ends of sequences (edges) first to maximize early decode overlap. - runtime/scheduler/slice_allocator.cc: slice-aware resource allocator that schedules slices with priority buckets (hot-slices, neutral, background) and integrates with the pre-existing token-bucket admission controller. - runtime/kv/cache_demux.cc & runtime/kv/cache_demux.h: KV demultiplexer that shards KV cache entries by affinity vectors (tenant, model-variant, slice-hash) and includes soft-eviction hints to the scheduler. - runtime/kernels/kernel_hint.h & user-facing hints: a small interface so orchestrator can pass kernel-friendly shapes (seq_len, microbatch) and preferred compute backend (f16/quantized path). - runtime/decode/handshake_refactor.{cc,h}: decouple the previous monolithic handshake into two phases: RSVP (locks necessary KV pages) and START_DECODE (kick off decode kernels as slices arrive). This reduces blocked prefill time and makes decode start opportunistically. - tests/perf/prefill_overlap_bench.py: new harness that reproduces mixed interactive workload and measures tail P50/P95/P99 end-to-end latency and per-token cost. - docs/architecture/prefill-edge-slicing.md: design doc and rollout notes. Commits: - Add edge-sliced orchestrator and slice allocator (Maya Chen) - Implement KV demultiplexer and eviction hints (Maya Chen) - Kernel hint API and small kernel-side consumer stub (Tom Becker) - Refactor decode handshake into RSVP/START_DECODE phases (Priya Natarajan) - Add perf harness, CI benchmarks, and docs (Maya Chen) Implementation notes: - The orchestrator samples model sequence-length distributions from recent request histograms to pick slice boundaries that are likely to be kernel-friendly (powers-of-two or multiples of 16 where kernels are optimized). - Edge-first slicing: for most user prompts the tail tokens are more latency-sensitive; we create small slices at the edges (<=16 tokens) and schedule them at higher priority so decode can begin earlier while the rest of the prefill continues. - KV demultiplexing: instead of a global LRU causing eviction across unrelated traffic, demux shards by affinity vectors and maintains per-shard age metrics. The scheduler consults these metrics to avoid scheduling slices that would immediately thrash a hot shard. - Handshake refactor: RSVP acquires soft locks on KV pages and returns immediately if decode can start; START_DECODE is idempotent and will no-op if kernels already started. This reduces head-of-line blocking when multiple slices are queued. Benchmarks (summary): - Mixed interactive benchmark (50% short chats, 50% long-prefill queries): end-to-end P95 latency improved from 432ms -> 318ms (26% improvement). P99 improved from 1142ms -> 832ms (27% improvement). - Throughput at 95% tail SLO: unchanged within noise (+/-2%). - Token cost: per-token GPU hours decreased by 7% due to increased kernel reuse and fewer cold KV misses. CI and testing: - Unit tests added for slice allocator and KV demux paths. - Perf harness runs in CI as an optional benchmark check; initial run failed on a flaky race in RSVP which was fixed in commit 3. - E2E integration tests for private deployments added to validate KV affinity semantics. Review conversation (high level): - Diego: asked for a clearer invariant on when slices can be merged back; requested explicit metrics for 'slice churn' in the console. Response: added merge heuristic (if two neighbor slices remain unscheduled after 200ms they are merged) and wired a slice_churn counter to the console. - Priya: requested that the KV demux fallback to global LRU for very small clusters. Response: implemented a config flag (kv.demux.enabled) with sane default true and cluster-size threshold to fall back. - Tom: requested a minimal kernel hint API to avoid coupling; provided kernel_hint.h with consumer-fastpath in kernels and a lightweight fallback path. - Security review: no new privileged surfaces; KV demux uses existing tenant isolation vectors. Rollout plan: - Canary on Dedicated region us-west-2 with 10% traffic for 48 hours. - Monitor slice_churn, kv_shard_evictions, end-to-end P95/P99, kernel_invocation_count and per-token cost. - If regressions observed, automatic rollback to main branch via rollout policy. Backwards compatibility and migrations: - Default behavior is backward compatible; orchestrator can be toggled with runtime flag runtime.prefill.orchestrator=edge-sliced. - The KV demultiplexer can be toggled and ships with conservative defaults to avoid warmup regressions. Notes and related work: - Related Linear tasks: ENG-1981 (prefill latency reduction), ENG-2043 (kv eviction debugging). - Related PRs: earlier experiments on slice-friendly batching are in PRs linked in the commit message (internal). Potential follow-ups: - Adaptive slice sizing based on live CPU/GPU telemetry. - Cross-tenant cooperative caching hints for multi-tenant noisy-neighbor mitigation. Merge: squash-merged after reviewers approved and CI passed. Release notes: - runtime: introduce edge-sliced prefill orchestrator and KV demultiplexer to reduce tail latency on mixed interactive workloads. Metrics: P95/P99 tail latency reduced ~25% in our benchmark. Troubleshooting: - If you see increased small-kernel overhead, toggle orchestrator off and open ENG-XXXX with perf traces attached. Attached files changed (high level): - runtime/prefill/orchestrator.cpp (+624/-132) - runtime/scheduler/slice_allocator.cc (+232/-48) - runtime/kv/cache_demux.cc (+214/-86) - runtime/kv/cache_demux.h (+42/-0) - runtime/decode/handshake_refactor.cc (+98/-26) - runtime/kernels/kernel_hint.h (+12/-0) - tests/perf/prefill_overlap_bench.py (+38/-6) - docs/architecture/prefill-edge-slicing.md (+22/-4) - tools/ci/bench_runner.yaml (+0/-30)
Introduce edge-sliced prefill orchestrator and KV demultiplexer to reduce tail latency on mixed interactive workloads (P95/P99 improvements). Toggleable via runtime.prefill.orchestrator.

payload.body:
Motivation:
The monolithic presubmit lint runner is fragile and slow to evolve for language-specific rules. We want a maintainable path forward that: 1) allows per-language lint/test adapters, 2) reduces CI time by fanout + targeted shards, and 3) surfaces dependency metadata to make dep-updates and dep-bot decisions safer.

Summary of changes (single-pass description):
- Introduces a small presubmit dispatcher (ci/presubmit/dispatcher.py) that reads ci/presubmit/shards.yaml and fans a single GitHub workflow run into a set of targeted lightweight presubmit jobs. The dispatcher is intentionally side-effect-minimal and designed to run as a step in the existing presubmit workflow.
- Replaces the single monolithic lint step with a plugin interface (scripts/lint_plugins/__init__.py) and two initial language plugins (js_plugin.py, py_plugin.py). Each plugin is responsible for selecting files and invoking the existing lint/test tooling in a hermetic way.
- Adds tools/dep_index, a small dependency metadata indexer and lightweight CLI that produces a canonical JSON index used by depbots/integrations. The index captures package name, lockfile location, dependency type (direct/transitive), and last-updated hint. This reduces blind upgrades and makes rollback decisions deterministic.
- Updates .github/workflows/presubmit.yaml to run an initial dispatcher step which then spawns language-specific job shards (via workflow_dispatch hooks). The workflow now uses smaller Docker images (docker/presubmit/Dockerfile.small) to reduce startup latency for these short-lived jobs.
- Adds ci/cache/priming.sh to warm common caches when a shard set is large; the dispatcher decides whether to prime caches based on changed file sizes and aggregate shard count.
- Small CI and developer-facing docs (docs/dev/presubmit-fanout.md) and an example shard config in examples/presubmit.

Implementation notes and rationale:
- Plugin interface: minimal, synchronous API (select_files(changed_paths) -> list_of_targets; run(targets) -> exit_code, output). This keeps language-specific logic decoupled from the dispatcher and avoids huge cross-language dependencies in the core CI runner.
- Presubmit shards manifest: ci/presubmit/shards.yaml is declarative and supports rules like: include when path matches, minimum job weight, and preferred runner label. This lets teams opt-in to language shards without repo-wide rewrites.
- Dep metadata index: the index is intentionally conservative (only metadata) so it's safe for on-prem/private deployments; no telemetry is sent by default. The indexer supports a --local-only flag for air-gapped installs.
- Backward compatibility: For repos that rely on the old monolith, the dispatcher includes a fallback mode (legacy_shard) that runs the previous runner if no plugins match. This was key to an incremental rollout.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests added for the dispatcher and adapters (pkg/ci/runner/*_test.go). Integration smoke runs executed in ephemeral runners to validate workflow dispatch and job creation.
- Added a small e2e harness in Makefile.ci that simulates a change set and validates expected shard creation.
- CI outcomes: the branch passed the full presubmit matrix after three reruns to warm caches. Final CI status: pass.

Review notes (conversation highlights captured here):
- Diego Rivera: "Nice separation. Two asks: 1) make shard weighting explicit in the manifest so we can tune cost vs latency per language; 2) add a short-circuit if no changed files match to avoid unnecessary workflow_dispatch spikes."
  - Author response (Ava): "Added weight and no-op early exit in shards.yaml and dispatcher; see commit 'ci: shard no-op guard'."
- Priya Shah: "Can dep-index run in the builder image and emit a deterministic artifact? We want reproducible indexes for CI audits."
  - Author response: "Indexer now has --stamp option to write a reproducible artifact and a small note in tools/dep_index/README.md describing how to reproduce."
- Connor Lee: "Small nit: Dockerfile.small should pin the base image digest to avoid flakiness in the short term."
  - Author response: "Pinned digest and added a CI gate to detect unexpected base-image changes."
- Marie Dubois: "Will this increase noise for small PRs? Fans of small PRs may suffer if we spawn too many runners."
  - Author response: "Dispatcher only creates shards that match changed files and will collapse to a single lightweight shard for tiny changes; added test coverage to validate collapse behavior."

Rollout plan and safety:
- Merged behind a feature flag (ci.presubmit.fanout.enabled) defaulting to off. We enabled for two teams and monitored presubmit cost and latency. After two weeks of stability, we enabled org-wide.
- If the dispatcher or any plugin fails, the dispatcher will fall back to legacy_shard mode and post a diagnostic comment on the PR with a YAML snippet for quick reproduction. This fallback path was tested during the staged rollout.

Observability and follow-ups:
- Added metrics emitted by the dispatcher: presubmit.shard.count, presubmit.shard.duration, presubmit.fallback.count. These integrate with existing presubmit dashboards.
- Follow-up work items: ENG-2101 (add Go plugin), ENG-2102 (presubmit cost exporter per-PR), ENG-2110 (make dep-index available to dep-bot for safe auto-upgrades).

Files changed (high-level):
- ci/presubmit/*: dispatcher, shard manifest, cache priming script.
- scripts/lint_plugins/*: plugin interface and initial language plugins.
- tools/dep_index/*: indexer, README, packaging.
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yaml: converted to dispatcher-first flow.
- docker/presubmit/Dockerfile.small: smaller runtime image for shards.

Merge notes:
- Addressed requested changes from reviewers; squashed commits and merged via squash merge on 2026-02-20. Post-merge: a small hotfix (PR 102338) fixed a race where the dispatcher attempted workflow_dispatch for already-closed PRs.

Impact:
- Median presubmit feedback time for non-monolithic changes dropped by ~28% in early rollout teams. CI cost per-PR dropped by ~14% due to smaller images and targeted shards. Dep upgrade rollover velocity improved with dep-index metadata available to the depbot integration.

If you need to revert: flip ci.presubmit.fanout.enabled=false in repo settings and revert the small dispatcher step in .github/workflows/presubmit.yaml.

Diego Rivera: Please make shard weighting explicit and add a no-op spike guard.
Priya Shah: Reproducible dep-index artifacts would be ideal for auditing.
Connor Lee: Pin Docker base digest to reduce image drift flakiness.
Marie Dubois: Ensure we don't spawn shards for tiny changes (noise concern).
Introduce presubmit fanout dispatcher, language-aware lint plugins, and a dep-metadata indexer. Improves presubmit latency and reduces CI cost by targeting shards. Backwards compatible fallback included.
payload.title: decompose-presubmit-lint-into-language-aware-fanout-and-add-dep-metadata-index

payload.body:
Motivation: We need safer, session-coherent A/B experiments that can expand gradually without violating user session affinity or causing noisy transients that invalidate metric comparisons. This PR implements a holdpoint allocator and an integrated auto-bisect helper that narrows down problematic traffic slices when a safety gate trips. It also bundles a human-readable rollback playbook so SREs can recover quickly. The description below covers design, how to exercise the feature, and operational guidance. Design summary: - Holdpoint allocator: allocates traffic fractions to candidate and control lanes while preserving session affinity via a lease token. Holdpoints are annotated with causal anchors (request metadata + session fingerprint) so we can deterministically replay affected slices. - Expansion policy: timeboxed gradual growth with entropy smoothing to avoid bursty jumps; supports step, linear, and sigmoid ramps. - Auto-bisect helper: when an SLO gate trips (latency or error budget), we can run an automated bisect that isolates cohorts by decreasing the holdpoint allocation and running short A/Bs across shard subsets; results are surfaced as ranked suspects. - Rollback playbook: prioritizes stepwise drain (shadow-to-control replay where possible), lease recall, and atomic traffic quiesce; includes CLI recipes and a Console runbook. Backwards compatibility: integrates with existing rollout controller; default behavior is off and must be opted in by a new rollout policy flag (holdpoint.enabled=true). Tests & validation: added unit tests for allocator maths, end-to-end simulation with synthetic traffic traces, and smoke runs against the staging rollout controller harness. Security & privacy: session lease tokens are ephemeral and rotated; no new user PII is stored. How to test locally: 1) enable feature flag in staging config, 2) create a rollout with holdpoint policy and a 5-step linear ramp, 3) trigger synthetic traffic with sticky session cookies and watch fidelity metrics in Console. Ops runbook highlights: - When a gate trips, run `redwoodctl bisect --rollout-id <id>` to produce a suspect list. - If metric delta > threshold, run `redwoodctl rollback --id <id> --strategy drain` for controlled rollback. - For emergency revert, use `redwoodctl swap --instant --id <id>` (falls back to atomic swap). Context and related work: follows on ENG-1970 (session affinity refactor) and pairs with the telemetry hooks added in ENG-2043. Commit summary: - 7 commits: allocator core, auto-bisect worker, rollout controller integration, CLI bindings, tests, docs, and gating flag. Changed areas: - pkg/rollout/allocator.go (new holdpoint allocator) - pkg/rollout/bisect_worker.go (new worker) - cmd/redwoodctl/rollback.go (new CLI helpers) - internal/telemetry/hooks.go (added holdpoint metrics) - deploy/staging/rollout_policy.yaml (example) - docs/runbooks/holdpoint_playbook.md (new runbook) - test/harness/allocator_sim_test.go (simulation tests) Review notes: This is a medium-large change but architected to be opt-in and feature-flag guarded. We focused on making the allocator deterministic and observable so operators can reason about suspect cohorts. The description string above also doubles as the top-level runbook blurb to ship with the docs.
Introduce a holdpoint allocator that enforces session-coherent A/B traffic slices, provides an automated bisect path for regressions observed during gradual promotes, and ships a documented rollback playbook for operator-driven interventions.
7 commits: 1) allocator: deterministic holdpoint maths and lease handling; 2) bisect worker prototype and suspect scorer; 3) rollout controller hooks + policy parsing; 4) CLI: redwoodctl bisect/rollback commands; 5) telemetry: holdpoint metrics and traces; 6) docs: playbook + examples; 7) tests: unit + sim harness.
Arjun Patel (2025-11-03): Left a couple of nit comments on allocator edge cases. We need to ensure session lease expiry is conservative so stuck sessions don't flip lanes unexpectedly.
Priya Nair (2025-11-03): Reply: adjusted lease expiry to 30s in default policy and added a unit test that simulates sudden client disconnects.
Samantha Liu (2025-11-04): Can we make the bisect worker emit candidate-by-candidate flamegraphs to help humans triage? Also requested an e2e smoke scenario in the staging pipeline.
Priya Nair (2025-11-04): Reply: added a telemetry hook that emits top-k flame metrics and extended the staging pipeline to run the smoke scenario as part of the rollout e2e job.
Marco Reyes (2025-11-05): Approved after quibbles addressed. Asked for a short docs docblock in Console showing the holdpoint UI state machine.
Priya Nair (2025-11-05): Follow-up: added docs/runbooks/holdpoint_playbook.md and a Console mockup image reference.
This feature is behind holdpoint.enabled=false by default. Release engineers should coordinate with SRE before enabling for production traffic. When toggling the flag, use staged ramp (10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) and ensure the bisect worker is configured with the same telemetry retention as staging.
If an SLO gate trips during a holdpoint promote: 1) run 'redwoodctl bisect --rollout-id <id>' and inspect top suspects; 2) if suspects point to a single variant, run 'redwoodctl rollback --id <id> --strategy drain' to minimize impact; 3) collect deterministic replay trace via 'redwoodctl export-replay --rollout-id <id> --slice <suspect>' and escalate to the on-call owner if necessary.
Merged to main via squash-merge after approvals. No post-merge hotfixes required; staged rollout first in staging then gradual in prod per rollout policy.
payload.title: Gradual holdpoint allocator for session-coherent A/B tests with auto-bisect and rollback playbook

payload.body:
Motivation: We frequently surface latency/cost SLOs but lack a clear signal for invocation-level bandwidth (payload + generated bytes) which drives egress costs and can cause tail latency when responses are large. This PR introduces a compact per-invocation bandwidth allocator and a privacy-conscious sampled log snapshotter so SRE and product teams can correlate bandwidth spikes with model behavior and customer payloads without shipping PII to observability backends.

What this does (high level):
- Introduces metrics emitted per invocation: invocation.request_bytes, invocation.generated_bytes, invocation.total_bytes, invocation.kv_cache_delta_bytes. These are tagged by route, model_version, tenant_id (hashed), and warmup_tag.
- Adds a small allocator in the runtime that accounts for buffered chunks (streaming) to avoid double-counting while keeping memory overhead bounded. The allocator is careful to account for partial chunking and retries.
- Implements a sampled log snapshotter (reservoir sampler) that captures a scrubbed payload + truncated response for a configurable fraction of high-bandwidth or erroring invocations. Snapshots are PII-scrubbed using the existing prompt-sanitizer pipeline and optionally hashed for tenant correlation. Snapshots are emitted to the observability pipeline as compact JSON blobs with strict size caps.
- Adds an Invocation Bandwidth dashboard (observability/dashboards/invocation-bandwidth.json) showing per-route bytes distribution, 99/95/50 quantiles, bandwidth vs latency scatter, and example sampled snapshots linked by trace id.
- Adds alert rules for sustained bandwidth SLO breach: monitoring/alerts/bandwidth_slo.yaml. Policy: if 99th percentile of invocation.total_bytes exceeds configured threshold for 10m with increased rate of errors, trigger P1 runbook.
- Exposes an API toggle for tenants to opt out of snapshot collection; snapshot metadata (size, sampler_reason) is always recorded even when snapshots are disabled.

Why this is different from existing metrics: Many of our current observability changes focus on token or cost decomposition; bandwidth is orthogonal and necessary for egress cost attribution and for diagnosing slow tails caused by large outputs, streaming backpressure, or network stalls. The allocator prevents double-counting between streaming chunks and the final aggregation which avoided a ~30% overcount in our internal perf test.

Commits summary:
- feat(runtime): add invocation bandwidth allocator and metric hooks (5 commits merged into one)
- feat(obs): dashboard + alert rules for invocation bandwidth
- feat(logging): sampled log snapshotter with sanitizer integration and opt-out flag
- test: unit + integration tests for allocator accounting and sampler
- docs: developer notes and runbook updates for bandwidth SLOs

Files changed (high level):
- src/runtime/metrics/bandwidth_allocator.go - new allocator and accounting helpers
- src/runtime/metrics/bandwidth_test.go - unit tests for chunk accounting and retries
- src/runtime/tracing/trace_enricher.go - attach bandwidth tags to traces
- src/observability/dashboards/invocation-bandwidth.json - new dashboard panels and links to snapshots
- monitoring/alerts/bandwidth_slo.yaml - new alerting policy with runbook reference
- src/logging/snapshotter/reservoir_sampler.go - sampled snapshot implementation with sanitizer hook
- src/logging/snapshotter/snapshot_store.go - upload/size cap + encryption metadata
- pkg/config/feature_flags.go - tenant opt-out toggle and sampling config
- scripts/observability/seed_dashboards.sh - add dashboard to staging and prod orgs
- docs/runbooks/bandwidth_slo.md - runbook and triage steps

Review conversation (high level excerpts):
- Samir Patel (reviewer): "This looks reasonable. Two asks: 1) add e2e test with real streaming chunks + retry to ensure no double-counting; 2) make sure the default sampler rate is conservative for GA (0.1%). Also please add an opt-out in the tenant UI flows."
- Author (Anika): "Added integration test in bandwidth_integration_test.go that replays chunked responses with injected retry; sampler default lowered to 0.1% in config and opt-out flag exposed via tenant feature_flags. UI work tracked separately (ENG-5490)."
- Evelyn Chu (reviewer): "Privacy check: does snapshot sanitizer use the same regex/PII rules as request-logging? We must ensure no hashing errors leak variable-length secrets."
- Author (Anika): "Yes, snapshotter reuses the prompt-sanitizer pipeline (src/logging/sanitizer/). We added an additional post-scrub length cap and ensure deterministic hashing uses HKDF with tenant-scoped salt. See snapshot_store.go for details and unit tests covering edge cases."
- Diego Morales (approver): "CI initially failed on a flaky allocator test; fixed with a minor timing tolerance increase and deterministic RNG seed in the sampler test. Approving now."

CI:
- Checks run: unit-tests (linux), integration-tests (staging infra flap), lint, gosec, dashboard-validation.
- First run: unit-tests failed (allocator race), rerun after fix -> all checks pass.

Performance and cost notes:
- Microbenchmarks show allocator adds ~0.6% CPU on the hot path and ~1.4KB memory per concurrent streaming invocation under stress; metric emission is batched to reduce cardinality pressure.
- Snapshot uploads are capped to 8KB and use gzip; expected observability retention cost estimated at <0.02% of current logs spend at default sampler rate (0.1%).

Rollout plan:
1) Canary on staging and a subset of low-traffic tenants with snapshots disabled by default (config flag off).
2) Enable metrics only for all prod tenants (no snapshots) to populate dashboard and alert baselines.
3) Enable sampled snapshots for internal tenants and opt-in customers; monitor cost/PII metrics for one week.
4) Gradually increase sampler as needed after operations review.

Runbook pointers: docs/runbooks/bandwidth_slo.md includes triage steps, dashboards to examine, and remediation (throttle, model fallback to smaller variants, apply response truncation policy).

Merge: Squash-and-merge. Changelog message included (see release_notes).
Adds per-invocation bandwidth metrics (request/response bytes, embedding payload size, kv-cache-delta) and a sampled, scrubbed log snapshotter for high-bandwidth/failed invocations; new dashboard and alert rules for bandwidth SLOs; runtime hooks for tagging and trace enrichment.
Samir: add e2e test with chunked streaming + retry; lower default sampler rate to 0.1%
Anika: added integration test and lowered default sampler; opt-out flag exposed; UI tracked in ENG-5490
Evelyn: ensure sanitizer matches request-logging rules and prevent hashing leaks
Anika: snapshotter reuses prompt-sanitizer; added post-scrub length cap and deterministic hashing with tenant salt
Diego: allocator test flaky on CI; increased timing tolerance and seeded RNG - approving
payload.title: Introduce per-invocation bandwidth metrics and contextual log snapshotter

payload.body:
Context & motivation: Customers with regional compliance requirements ask for stronger guarantees that KMS usage and operator RBAC decisions are evaluated against tenant-specific obligations (e.g., allowed provider list, region pinning). Existing enforcement paths were scattered: some checks lived in the KMS allocator, some in the policy-enforcer, and audit records varied by component, making post-hoc compliance proofs brittle. This PR introduces a centralized Tenant KMS Obligation Mapper (TKOM) plus an Audit Normalizer that standardizes provenance metadata across services. Goal: make decisions deterministic, auditable, and easier to reason about during audits without large surface-area changes to runtime.

Summary of changes: Implements TKOM service/interface (inference and private branches) that consumes tenant profiles and compiles a normalized obligations object (allowed_providers, region_pin, soft_restrictions). Adds an enforcement shim used by the KMS allocator and policy-enforcer that consults TKOM results. Introduces an audit-normalizer pipeline that transforms existing audit events into a canonical schema with KMS_obligation_id, decision_reason, and operator_scope fields. Adds a lightweight migration assistant that backfills obligation IDs for existing tenants and a feature-flag to gate rollout.

Checklist (implemented): - Add TKOM API + in-memory cache with TTL and refresh metrics. - Integrate shim into kms-allocator and policy-enforcer with fallbacks. - Audit normalizer: schema, transformer, and retention hooks. - Migration assistant: dry-run mode + backfill. - Feature flag: config.features.tk_obligation_mapper (off by default) - Unit + integration tests for policy-enforcer and audit pipeline. - Security review and threat model update.

Commits (high level): - 3d8a9f2: bootstrap tenant obligation mapper service and core types. - b7f21c1: add cache adapter + metrics and config toggles. - a12f4e7: integrate enforcement shim into kms-allocator (use obligation id and provider whitelist). - f9e2b33: audit-normalizer transformer + schema migration and tests. - c1b4d0a: migration assistant and dry-run tooling. - 4b7c9ae: docs, rollout playbook, and e2e tests for private deployer.

Changed areas/files (high level): - services/tkom/* (new service, API, cache, tests) - services/kms-allocator/shim.go (enforcement shim and integrations) - services/policy-enforcer/obligation_adapter.go (adapter to consult TKOM) - observability/audit/normalizer/* (transformer, schema v2) - infra/feature-flags.yaml (feature gating) - tools/migration-assistant/* (backfill + dry-run) - docs/security/tkom.md and runbook/rollout-tkom.md

Testing & CI: Initial CI run showed a flaky integration test in policy-enforcer (race on cache refresh). Fixed by adding a mutex and a retry backoff (commits b7f21c1 -> a12f4e7). Final CI: linux-unit (pass), linux-integration (pass after rerun), lint (pass), go-vet (pass). Performance: obligation lookup latency added ~0.9ms median when cache cold; negligible when warm. Measured end-to-end add of ~1-2ms tail for KMS allocation path in our perf-canary harness under synthetic load. Included microbenchmarks in services/tkom/bench.

Backward compatibility & migration: Feature-gated rollout with migration assistant to compute obligation ids and validate no tenants are left without obligations. Default behaviour when feature off: system behaves as today. When on: enforcement shim treats unknown obligation as permissive (configurable) for a 48h soft-enforcement window, then strict. Migration assistant dry-run produced no tenants that would move to strict deny in our staging sample.

Security review & threat model: Conducted with Priya Raman. Major findings: ensure TKOM caches don't leak cross-tenant data; we added tenant-scoped cache keys and telemetry scrubbing. Audit-normalizer includes hashed operator identifiers to support non-repudiation while minimizing PII in long-term retention. Threat mitigations and design notes are in docs/security/tkom.md.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy TKOM in staging with feature flag off. 2) Run migration assistant dry-run and reconcile. 3) Enable feature for internal tenants (canary). 4) Monitor metrics (obligation_hits, obligation_misses, audit_normalizer_errors) and SLOs for KMS latency. 5) Expand to >80% tenants, then strict enforcement after 48h window. Rollback plan: flip feature flag off and flush caches.

Follow-ups: - Formal evaluation to surface obligation diffs in Console (ENG-5378). - Add per-operator attribute mapping to aid operator-scoped RBAC (design doc linked). - Consider moving obligation compilation into policy-compiler for offline verification.
Jared Alvarez: Can you clarify the fallback semantics if TKOM is unavailable? The PR description says permissive by default but the code reads as strict in one path.
Maya Chen (reply): Good catch. Updated the shim logic to centralize fallback semantics in shim.go and added unit tests. Permissive by default is now enforced via config.features.tk_obligation_mapper.default_mode.
Priya Raman: Please add a note to the threat model about cache key entropy and operator identifier hashing.
Maya Chen (reply): Added section in docs/security/tkom.md and a short unit test that verifies operator id hashing is stable across restarts.
Eleanor Wu: Audit normalizer should include a version field to allow roll-forward parsing; add schema v2 header.
Maya Chen (reply): Included schema_version on all normalized events and migration tooling to backfill older records.
Add tenant-level KMS obligation mapping and an audit-normalizer pipeline. No public API changes. Operational flag gate and automated migration helper included.
payload.title: Introduce tenant KMS obligation mapper and audit normalizer

payload.body:
Summary: This PR introduces a small set of 'pipeline' stream helper utilities intended to make composing streaming transforms, warmup sequencing, and credential handoffs ergonomic across our tri-SDK surface (Python, TypeScript, Go). It also adds a shared 'retry template' set (lightweight presets) stored in devtools so that SDKs can converge on consistent backoff profiles (fast/normal/conservative) for streaming and short-lived RPCs. Motivation: multiple customers and internal product teams hit subtle differences in backoff and stream warmup behavior across SDKs which made cross-service debugging and incident rollouts slow. This PR aims to reduce the cognitive load for integrators by providing small, well-documented helpers and documented presets while keeping default behavior unchanged. Changes: - SDK surface additions: pipeline helpers (map_stream, windowed_batch, staged_warmup) implemented in Python/TS/Go with identical semantics and typed signatures. - Retry templates: introducing devtools/retry_templates/(fast|normal|conservative).yaml and a lightweight generator used by SDK build steps to embed defaults. - Auth/cred: small credential handoff helper (credential_fanout) that attaches a short-lived lease during stream warmup to reduce reauth races. - Telemetry: added lightweight telemetry hooks for warmup and retry categories (no PII). - Version bumps: python sdk 0.19.2 -> 0.20.0 (minor), ts sdk 1.6.0 -> 1.7.0, go sdk v1.5.3 -> v1.6.0. Migration notes: For existing consumers nothing breaks — new helpers are additive. Consumers wanting consistent backoff should switch to using the RetryTemplate enum or import the presets. Checklist: - [x] Implement pipeline helpers in all SDKs - [x] Add retry template YAMLs and generator - [x] Add tests (unit + quick integration smoke) - [x] Update SDK changelogs and bump versions - [x] Add docs snippets and examples - [x] Run perf canary on staging and validate 99th/50th latency regressions Context/related: See Linear ENG-2801 for design conversation and SUP-1178 for customer repro. Also follows work in pkgs/devtools#43 (retry-presets). Summary: Adds an opt-in Client-Compatibility-Mode request header that signals the API gateway and the OpenAI-compat layer to employ a conservative response shape and streaming fallback strategy for older clients and third-party tool callers. Motivation: some downstream integrators observed breaking changes in structured-output envelopes and streaming chunk formats after the recent schema evolution rollouts. This patch provides a lightweight, observable, opt-in shim so customers can migrate on their cadence without sacrificing streaming stability for newer clients. Key behaviors: when Client-Compatibility-Mode: v0 is present the runtime will: 1) coerce structured/tool-call envelopes to legacy field names (tool_name => name, tool_args => args) and drop unknown typed metadata; 2) disable chunked type-framing for streaming responses and fall back to newline-delimited 'data:' event frames compatible with older SDK stream parsers; 3) emit compatibility telemetry tag compat_mode=v0 for per-client SLO tracking; 4) enable a per-request permissive schema-coercion path that attempts best-effort conversion of typed tool-call payloads into the legacy format. Non-goals: this PR does not change default behavior for new clients, nor does it change persisted model outputs or eval scoring. Checklist: - [x] design doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2461/compat-header-design - [x] add header parsing and gateway routing - [x] implement coercion utilities and unit tests - [x] update python and typescript SDK stubs to include header constant - [x] telemetry + alerting for compatibility fallbacks - [x] documentation + migration guide - [x] integration test against legacy stream parser (test_legacy_stream_parser) Testing & validation: included unit tests for coercion utilities, integration test that simulates an older SDK consumer, end-to-end run in perf-canary cluster to validate no regression to 99th percentile p50 latency under light load. Rollout plan: feature gated behind a rollout flag (server.config.compatibility_mode.enabled) with canary to 10% requests for 48h, then gradual ramp to 100% for clients that opt-in. Will deprecate v0 after a 6 month window with Linear ticket ENG-3012 tracking removal. Related: references SUP-7901 support case and aligns with recent schema deprecation guidance.
Evan Brooks: Can we ensure KV cache keys remain stable when coercion changes field names? Suggest adding a deterministic mapping function to avoid cache fragmentation.
Author (Aisha): Agreed, added deterministic mapping in coercion util and unit tests to verify cache-key stability.
Lena Fischer: lgtm overall. Please add an explicit opt-out example in the SDK docs for customers that want strict schema enforcement.
Author (Aisha): Added opt-out snippet to SDK and docs. Also added e2e test that asserts strict mode rejects legacy-typed payloads.
Rahul Mehta: CI flake on integration test during first run (race in stream parser). Marked flaky and added simple backoff+retry; re-ran CI.
Evan Brooks: Approve after resolving KV cache mapping and addressing integration flake.
- Introduce Client-Compatibility-Mode header for opt-in backcompat behavior. - Adds streaming fallback framing compatible with legacy SDKs. - Coercion utilities for legacy tool-call envelopes. - New alerts for compatibility fallbacks exceeding threshold.
1) Clients opt in by setting header 'Client-Compatibility-Mode: v0' on requests. 2) Test parsing against legacy SDKs using tests/integration/test_compat_mode.py. 3) Follow docs/openai-compat/compatibility_mode.md for examples and notes about eventual deprecation. 4) Track removal via ENG-3012.
Enable server.config.compatibility_mode.enabled=true rollout flag to begin canary. Watch observability/alerts/streaming_compat_fallback.rule and dashboard: 'compat.mode.rate' and 'streaming.fallback.latency' during ramp.
Unit + integration + canary perf covered. Manual validation against known legacy client (internal test harness) passed. Observability tags added to trace and metrics for post-deploy monitoring.

Context: We see persistent p99 tail latency in continuous-batcher when a small number of KV-heavy 'pin' requests occupy long-lived slots; existing deadline heuristics either favour throughput (allowing starvation) or favour fairness (reducing throughput). Motivation: reduce long-tail latency without large throughput regressions and provide an operationally-safe rollout path. What this PR does: 1) Introduces an adaptive slack sampler that computes a per-cohort 'slack' budget based on recent slot occupancy percentiles and request duration histograms, using an exponentially weighted percentile estimator. Slack is the additional time a request may linger in the active window before being considered for eviction or preemption. 2) Adds a timebox gating layer that enforces an upper bound on how long a request may be allowed to persist in the head of the continuous batcher queue; the timebox is dynamically adjusted by the sampler but clamped to safe min/max values. 3) Integrates prefetch hints into KV pipeline: requests that declare KV-prefetch intent can be sampled more conservatively to avoid mass prefetch churn. 4) Telemetry: new metrics batcher.sampler.effective_slack, batcher.sampler.percentile_estimate, batcher.timebox.duration_ms, and cohort_size; these are surfaced in existing dashboards and used for alerts. Design details: - Slack calculation: use the 90th/95th percentile of observed slot hold times with EWMA smoothing (configurable alpha) and apply a decay hysteresis to avoid rapid swings. - Timebox gating: when head request hold time > effective_slack, we start soft-preemption probes with jittered backoff; if a request exceeds timebox hard-limit, it is demoted to background queue for fairness. - Safety: feature-flagged behind batcher.feature.adaptive_slack in helm values; default off for clusters >= prod; enabled in canary envs. - Rollout: staged canary: 5 hosts (1%) -> 20 hosts (5%) -> 100 hosts (20%) -> full. Automated rollback if error_budget > 5% or p50 latency degrades by >5% and p99 does not improve. Tests and validation: - Unit tests for percentile estimator, slack decay hysteresis, and zero-occupancy guard. - Integration tests in integration/batcher/kv_tail_test.go simulating mixed KV/non-KV traffic. - Perf harness: synthetic KV tail workloads run on benchmark-lab with 3 seeds; results: p99 reduced by 12% (median across seeds), p95 reduced by 7%, overall throughput change -2% under heavy KV scenario. - Observability: new dashboard panels and alerts for effective_slack and cohort_size; added logs at debug level for sampling decisions. Files changed (high level): - pkg/batcher/continuous_sampler.go: new sampler implementation, including EWMA percentile estimator and config options. - pkg/batcher/timebox_gate.go: gating logic and demotion hooks. - runtime/scheduler/cohort.go: cohort metadata tracking and slot occupancy sampling. - runtime/kv/cache.go: prefetch hint plumbing and lightweight token to inform sampler. - pkg/telemetry/metrics.go: metrics registration and tags. - integration tests and docs. Review notes and iterations: - First CI run failed due to an edge-case where hosts with transient zero-occupancy produced negative slack; fixed by clamping and unit test added. - Ethan requested autoscaling oscillation tests; added decay hysteresis and bench to prove stability. - Lina requested extra telemetry for cohort sizes; added metric and dashboard snippet. Operational impact and rollback: - Backward compatible and disabled by default. Helm flag in helm/values/batcher-featureflags.yaml toggles the sampler. - Rollout includes canary gating and automated metric checks; rollback documented in docs/operational/batcher.md. Known limitations: - In extremely bursty workloads with very short sequences, the estimator needs longer windows to converge—this will be addressed in a follow-up that adds adaptive windowing. - Prefetch hinting requires callers to opt-in; without hints the sampler conservatively assumes worst-case. Merge: Squash-merged into main after approvals and successful canary. Summary: This PR provides a practical middle path between strict deadline enforcement and throughput-first behavior by adaptively computing slack and enforcing a timebox. Benchmarks show meaningful p99 improvements for KV-heavy tails with minimal throughput cost.
Ethan Morris: This looks promising; main concern is the interaction between slack decay window and autoscaling. Can we prove it doesn't create oscillation?
Author (Asha Patel): Added a decay hysteresis and a max-step limiter; bench harness shows no oscillation across 0/20/100% KV mixes. See metrics added under batcher.sampler.*
Lina Zhou: Please add a guard for zero-slot hosts to avoid fractional slack -> negative gating; also ensure telemetry exposes cohort sizes.
Author (Asha Patel): Fixed zero-occupancy edge and added cohort_size and effective_slack metrics. Unit test included.
Owen Park: Approved after seeing integration results and canary rollout plan.
Introduce an adaptive slack sampler and timebox gating for the continuous batcher to reduce p99 latency in KV-heavy workloads. Backward compatible behind feature flag; rollout via canary. Improves p99 by ~12% in internal benchmarks with minimal throughput impact.
payload.title: Adaptive slack sampler with timebox gating for continuous batcher

Summary
This PR flips the GA defaults for route-level experiments (Console Rollouts) and tightens validations across the control plane + policy evaluator, plus wires up release notes + rollout checklist for the 2025.04 train.

Context
During beta we saw two recurring issues:
1) Variant skew when a stable stickiness key was missing or low-entropy (SUP-24831, see also follow-up fixes in pr-28705).
2) Customers accidentally creating configs that were "valid" structurally but unsafe operationally (overlapping experiments, impossible allocations, incompatible model variants, and confusing stop semantics).

This PR is intentionally not adding statistical significance analysis (explicit non-goal for GA per PM-482). It focuses on making the defaults safe and predictable.

What changed (high level)
- GA enablement defaults:
  - Route experiments are enabled by default for eligible orgs behind a staged rollout gate (see "Rollout plan" below).
  - New orgs created after GA gate automatically get the capability (no manual flag required), but actions remain RBAC-gated.
  - Existing orgs are enabled in waves by region/account tier with an immediate rollback lever.

- Deterministic assignment defaults (safe handling of missing identifiers):
  - Stickiness key precedence updated to:
    1) Explicit customer-provided header: x-redwood-sticky-key (if present)
    2) customer_id (authenticated requests)
    3) api_key_id (fallback for service-to-service)
    4) If none are present: assign to "control" variant only (no split) and emit a structured warning event + Console validation warning
  - This prevents low-entropy defaults that caused skew and makes the "missing id" behavior visible.
  - Debug endpoint output updated to show which key path was used (ties into pr-28596) without leaking raw identifiers (redacted).

- Validation hardening (control plane + Console API):
  - Allocation rules:
    - Enforce allocations sum to 1.0 (within epsilon), no negative values, and max N variants (GA default: 5).
    - Enforce minimum non-zero split (GA default: 1%) unless experiment is in "draft".
  - Route overlap rules:
    - Block multiple ACTIVE experiments targeting the same normalized route_id.
    - Allow an ACTIVE + DRAFT overlap for editing, but DRAFT cannot be started until the active one is stopped.
    - Error messages include the conflicting experiment id and a deep link to Console.
  - Variant compatibility:
    - Validate variant model compatibility with route schema (chat vs completions, tool calling enablement, structured output requirements).
    - Validate fallback interactions: experiments apply before fallback evaluation (consistent with pr-28457); config that would "mask" variant selection via fallback is rejected with a remediation hint.
  - Stop semantics:
    - GA default remains soft-stop on guardrail breach (mark degraded + notify). Optional hard-stop remains opt-in and is protected by a kill switch (see below).

- Guardrail defaults (GA):
  - Default thresholds applied on creation (editable):
    - p99 latency regression: +25% vs control (warning), +50% (eligible for auto-stop if hard-stop enabled)
    - error rate: +0.5% absolute vs control (warning)
    - cost/token: +15% vs control (warning)
  - Console copy updated to clarify that guardrails evaluate on aggregated windows and may lag during backfills.

- Release notes + operational readiness:
  - Added 2025.04 release note entry and internal rollout checklist (feature flag, dashboards, runbooks, support macros).
  - Added runbook links in the guardrail banners + alert payload wiring (consistent with pr-28734).

Rollout plan (staged)
- Phase A (Day 0): Enable for internal + existing beta allowlist accounts in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Monitor:
  - config propagation lag p95
  - attribution drop rate
  - split accuracy monitors
  - DB query cost for results endpoint
- Phase B (Day 2-3): Expand to remaining regions for allowlisted accounts.
- Phase C (Week 1): Enable for all "Pro" tier accounts.
- Phase D (Week 2): Enable for all remaining eligible accounts.

Roll-back plan
- Immediate: global kill switch to revert "enabled by default" back to explicit opt-in (keeps APIs functional for already running experiments, but blocks new starts).
- If routing anomalies: force evaluator to route 100% to control for all experiments (separate emergency flag), preserving attribution headers for debugging.
- If metrics pipeline issues: disable high-cardinality expansions; keep minimal dimensions only (see ADR-048 + pr-28741 follow-ups).

Files / areas touched
- control-plane/experiment-service:
  - GA validation rules, improved error messages, and audit payload change-diff summary fields
- policy-engine / router:
  - stickiness key precedence + missing-id behavior; additional metrics for warning rate
- console-api:
  - surface validation errors consistently; enforce RBAC on new defaults (no permission changes, but safer gating)
- docs/release-notes:
  - 2025.04 notes and rollout checklist section

Commit summary
- feat(experiments): default-enable route experiments w/ staged rollout gate
- fix(assignment): safe missing-id behavior (force control) + warning events
- chore(validation): block overlapping ACTIVE experiments + tighten allocation constraints
- feat(console): improve validation error mapping + GA default guardrails
- docs(release): add 2025.04 route experiments GA notes + runbook links

Testing
- Unit: experiment schema validation, overlap rules, stickiness precedence
- Integration: deterministic bucketing stability across restarts, split distribution simulation, stop/start state transitions
- E2E (smoke): create experiment -> start -> observe attribution headers -> stop (drain)

Checklist
- [x] GA defaults approved by Product (Marissa Cole)
- [x] SRE review for rollout + kill switches (Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes)
- [x] Telemetry reviewed for cardinality risk (Logan Wright)
- [x] Security review for debug output redaction + audit fields (Marcus Lin)
- [x] Release notes updated for 2025.04

Notable review discussion (captured here for posterity)
- SRE requested that "missing stickiness key" never silently hashes low-entropy attributes; we now force control and emit a warning event.
- Telemetry requested keeping experiment dimensions minimal by default; this PR does not change the tagging strategy beyond adding a warning counter.
- Product requested clearer Console copy around soft-stop vs hard-stop; updated in the wizard + details page tooltips.

Related PRs / references
- pr-28673 (feature flag gates for beta enablement)
- pr-28692 (config versioning/migrations)
- pr-28705 (skew fix when sticky key missing)
- pr-28741 (metrics cardinality reduction)

CI
- build: passed
- lint: passed
- unit tests: passed
- integration tests: passed
- e2e-smoke: passed (reran once due to transient env timeout)

Merge
Squash merged into main for the 2025.04 release train. Release coordinator: Connor O'Brien.
- Route experiments are GA and enabled by default for eligible accounts (staged rollout).
- Stronger server-side validation for allocations, variant compatibility, and overlapping experiments on the same route.
- Safer GA defaults for stickiness key selection and missing-identifier behavior (prevents skew).
- Console now surfaces clearer validation errors + guardrail defaults in the creation wizard.
- Added explicit runbook links and rollout guardrails to release notes.
payload.title: GA: enable route experiments by default + tighten validations + release notes

Context: This change implements a tenant-scoped operator allowlist and an epoched append-only audit lock to improve compliance guarantees when operator-scoped credentials are used with region/KMS constraints. Motivation: customers in regulated environments asked for stricter guarantees that operator-initiated actions are scoped to tenant-allowlisted operators and that audit records for those actions are immutable within a time epoch to prevent accidental rewrites during bulk reingestion or migration.

What this PR does (single-line description + what to expect):
- Add a tenant-scoped operator allowlist that gates operator tokens by (tenant_id, operator_fingerprint, region_hint). This is enforced at the policy-evaluation boundary and in the operator-auth middleware.
- Introduce an "audit epoch lock": a lightweight append-only marker for tenant audit streams that prevents in-place edits for events assigned to a closed epoch. Epochs are short-lived (configurable per-tenant) and allow safe bulk replays without risking historical mutation.
- Wire KMS-origin verification into the operator allowlist checker: operator entries carry an optional KMS binding (kms_provider:kms_keyid) checked at run-time for service accounts that delegate wrapping keys.
- Migration tooling and docs: an examples/migrations/README and a db migration script to add operator_allowlist and audit_epoch tables.

Why this approach: The allowlist gives an explicit, compact representation of allowed operator bindings and makes it simple to reason about cross-region operator delegation. The epoch model is intentionally append-only and not a full WORM store; it prevents accidental in-place modification while keeping operational recovery straightforward.

Compatibility and rollout plan:
1) Feature is behind feature flags: rbac.allowlist.enabled and audit.epoch_lock.enabled. Flags default to off.
2) Backwards compatible reads: services that do not opt in will continue to use current policy flow.
3) We recommend a staged rollout: enable allowlist enforcement in shadow/dry-run mode for 7 days, reconcile denylist hits, then flip enforcement; enable epoch lock in audit-ingesters first (regionally) and monitor ingestion latencies for 72 hours.

Checklist:
- [x] Core allowlist implementation (policy + middleware)
- [x] Audit epoch lock write-path and sanity-checks
- [x] Migration script and example SQL
- [x] Unit and integration tests for typical and edge cases
- [x] Docs and runbook additions (operator-affinity.md, migrations README)
- [x] KMS-origin verification for allowlist entries

Notes on security review: This PR integrates with the KMS client to surface key origin data. We intentionally do not modify KMS key permissions; we only assert provider:key metadata presented by the KMS client. Operators without a KMS binding still work but must be explicitly allowlisted.

Release notes (short): Introduces tenant-scoped operator allowlist and epoched audit-locks to improve audit immutability and operator scoping controls. Opt-in via feature flags. See docs/operator-affinity.md for migration steps.

Related: ENG-3421 implements the backend schema; SEC-178 tracked the compliance ask; SUP-4021 is a support case that motivated the runbook additions.
Maya Chen (2025-11-04): Can we ensure the allowlist lookup has an LRU-backed cache with TTL to avoid a DB hit on every auth check? Suggested adding metrics for cache hit/miss. Response: added a small in-memory cache with configurable TTL and metrics in allowlist.go (see commit 6e2d89f).
Ethan Ruiz (2025-11-06): The audit epoch lock write path needs an idempotency token to tolerate duplicate deliveries from the ingest path. Also asked for more aggressive testing around partial epoch closure. Response: added idempotency checks and added an integration test for double-post idempotency (tests/integration/tenant_affinity_test.go).
Priya Nambiar (2025-11-07): Security review - please clarify KMS-origin trust boundary and what to do if KMS provider metadata is absent. Response: clarified in docs and code: if KMS metadata is absent we only allow operator entries that do not require a KMS binding; enforcement mode can block non-bound operators per-tenant policy. We also added a feature flag to disable KMS-origin enforcement globally.
Maya Chen (2025-11-10): Approved after minor nits fixed in docs and a test flake addressed (CI rerun passed).
- Feature: tenant-scoped operator allowlist (opt-in behind rbac.allowlist.enabled)
- Feature: epoched append-only audit locks to protect historical audit immutability (opt-in behind audit.epoch_lock.enabled)
- Migration: new DB tables operator_allowlist, audit_epoch; see migrations/20251103_add_operator_allowlist.sql and docs/operator-affinity.md for steps.
Added a runbook section in docs/operator-affinity.md covering shadow mode rollout, reconciling denylist hits, and rollback steps for audit epoch lock. Key steps: enable shadow mode, monitor allowlist hits metric, follow migration order: DB migration -> enable shadow allowlist -> reconcile hits -> flip enforcement. If ingestion latency spikes after epoch lock, disable audit.epoch_lock.enabled per-region and re-run ingest in backlog mode.
payload.title: Introduce tenant-scoped operator allowlist and epoched append-only audit lock

Context: multiple SDK integrations (Python/TypeScript/Go) have diverged in how they handle credential rotation, ephemeral fallbacks, and streaming consumer ergonomics. This PR centralizes the auth fallback logic into a small, portable contract and ships a lightweight 'generator sugar' helper that makes streaming responses ergonomic and idiomatic in each language without leaking transport details.

Motivation: reduce duplicate retry/fallback logic across SDKs, remove observed race conditions during token swap on intermittent auth errors, and provide a single-pattern streaming example for docs and quickstarts.

Summary of changes:
- Introduce AuthFallback (interface + default implementation) that composes primary credential provider with optional delegated fallback providers; provides explicit backoff and 'shouldRetryOnAuth' predicate.
- Add GeneratorSugar helper (polyglot concept implemented for Python runtime and TS shim; Go receives the lightweight iterator adapter) that converts raw streaming frames into typed async generators/iterators with built-in error mapping & retry hints.
- Harmonize token-refresh timing: prefer TTL-based jittered prefetch; explicit heartbeat hook added for long-lived streams.
- Bump SDK versions: py-sdk v1.31.0, ts-sdk v1.27.2, go-sdk v1.8.4.
- Add cross-SDK examples and update existing quickstarts.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement core auth fallback contract
- [x] Add generator sugar helpers in Python/TS and iterator adapter in Go
- [x] Unit tests for auth fallback decision paths
- [x] Integration test that simulates token rotation during active stream
- [x] Update docs and examples
- [x] Version bumps and changelogs

Commits summary: squash of 7 commits: "init: auth fallback contract and default impl", "feat(gen-sugar): python generator sugar + examples", "chore(ts): add shim + types for generator sugar", "fix(go): iterator adapter edge-case for EOF+auth", "test: simulate token rotation during streaming", "docs: update streaming quickstart and samples", "chore: bump sdk versions and changelogs".

Files changed (high level): sources/sdk/python/redwood/streaming.py, sources/sdk/python/redwood/auth.py, sources/sdk/python/tests/test_stream_rotation.py, sources/sdk/typescript/src/generatorSugar.ts, sources/sdk/typescript/test/stream-rotation.spec.ts, sources/sdk/go/stream/iterator_adapter.go, sources/sdk/go/auth/fallback.go, website/docs/streaming-auth.md, examples/streaming/auth-fallback-examples/*, packaging/py-sdk/setup.cfg, packaging/ts-sdk/package.json, packaging/go-sdk/go.mod.

Testing & CI: Initial CI run: build (pass), unit (pass), lint (fail on TS new helper style rules). Author fixed lint and force-pushed; second CI run: all checks passed except a flaky e2e in nightly-integration (timeout on simulated network jitter). Flaky test was quarantined and retried; final CI status is passing.

Observability: added lightweight telemetry tags on fallback usage and stream-retry reasons.

Review conversation (high level):
- Miguel Alvarez: "Question: how does the fallback affect cold-start latency when primary provider is slow?" Reply (author): "Fallback decision is lazy: we do not contact fallback providers until primary returns a 401/403 or the 'shouldRetryOnAuth' predicate triggers; added a unit to assert no extra calls on happy path."
- Priya Shah: "TS types feel a bit loose around the generator envelope." Reply (author): "Added stricter types and a test that asserts runtime mapping; kept a small any<> in a narrow shim to avoid duplicating transport types across packages."
- Asha Kumar (design): "Please add a short note in console explaining when fallback was used (for audit)." Reply (author): "Added an opt-in telemetry flag and console note in examples; not enabled by default to avoid noise."
- Daniel Kim (SRE): "Observed 2x increase in retry attempts during the first run against staging; is that expected?" Reply (author): "That was the flaky e2e's artifact; we lowered the default retry ceiling for streamed auth to prevent aggressive retry storms and documented the knob in runtime configs."

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after approvals. Merge commit: 4b8f6d9c1e5b2a7f3d9c1b0a6d8f9e2c3f4a5b6c. Rollout notes: shipped as coordinated SDK micro-release; serverside compatibility retained via runtime feature flag. Rollback plan: revert the squash merge and pin SDK clients to previous versions; server-side flag to disable fallback if unexpected behaviors surface.
Miguel Alvarez: Question: how does the fallback affect cold-start latency when primary provider is slow?
Liam O'Connor: Reply: Fallback is lazy; no calls to fallback providers on happy path; added unit test to assert zero extra calls.
Priya Shah: TS types feel a bit loose around the generator envelope.
Liam O'Connor: Reply: tightened types and added runtime mapping test; left a minimal shim to avoid cross-package type coupling.
Asha Kumar: Please add a short note in console explaining when fallback was used (for audit).
Liam O'Connor: Reply: Added opt-in telemetry flag and example console note; disabled by default.
Daniel Kim: Observed 2x increase in retry attempts during the first run against staging; is that expected?
Liam O'Connor: Reply: That was a flaky e2e artifact; lowered default retry ceiling for streamed auth and documented config knob.
- Add AuthFallback contract to unify multi-provider auth flows across SDKs.
- Introduce GeneratorSugar helpers to make streaming responses ergonomic in Python/TypeScript and add iterator adapter for Go.

Summary: Introduces a latency-floor fanout scheduler that reduces tail latency for heterogeneous request sizes while preventing KV-cache starvation via a per-key warmup hint. Motivation: Continuous-batching pressure and high fanout can starve low-frequency keys and inflate tail latency when large requests monopolize slots. This PR provides a scheduler that enforces a soft latency floor to bias small/latency-sensitive requests toward earlier dispatch, while still preserving throughput for batch-friendly workloads. Key design points: 1) Latency floor token: requests below a configurable expected latency are eligible for fast-path fanout up to a small window to keep tail latency bounded. 2) Per-key KV warmup hinting: request issuers may attach an optional kv_warm_hint tag; scheduler maintains a tiny in-memory last-access sketch and will preemptively reserve warmup slots for keys that have warmed-up recently or have an explicit hint. 3) Fanout capping by bucket: fanout is bounded per priority bucket to limit slot monopolization. 4) Graceful degradation: when capacity is constrained, scheduler decay ramps down fanout and shifts to prioritized leaky-window admission rather than abrupt drops. Behavioral changes: default latency_floor=15ms for text-gen short prompts, fanout_cap=8 per bucket, kv_warmup_reserve=2 slots per hot-key. Configuration is fully runtime-controllable via operator flags and Console feature toggle. Implementation notes: scheduler changes are implemented in runtime/scheduler/fanout_scheduler.cc with a compact policy engine. KV warmup hint tracking sits in runtime/cache/kv_warmup_tracker.{cc,h}. The admission path and continuous-batcher hooks were updated to consult the scheduler policy and KV tracker before building the dispatch bundle. There is instrumentation added to expose fanout_decisions, kv_warm_reserve_hits/misses, and latency_floor_evicts as Prometheus metrics. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind a feature flag. Start in canary region for 48 hours with traffic shaping to 5% of traffic, observe fanout_decisions and kv_warm_reserve_hits, then 25% and global after SLA confirmation. Backout is a feature-flag toggle. Testing: unit tests for decision logic, integration test with simulated request mixes (kv-hot, kv-cold, large-burst), and an end-to-end perf job that validates P99 reduction on mixed workloads. Backwards compatibility: honors existing batcher contracts and will not change external API surface. See linked Linear tasks for evaluation prompt sets and perf dashboards.
Devon Liu: Concern about unbounded memory if every key attaches kv_warm_hint; asked for an LFU cap and eviction policy. Author: Added a fixed-size sketch with exponential decay and clarified limits in kv_warmup_tracker.h; updated tests. Devon: Requested additional unit test for eviction behavior; added. Priya Anand: Asked for clearer observability (how to tell if warmup is helping). Author: Exposed kv_warm_reserve_hits/misses and added Grafana example to docs. Marco Ruiz: Ran perf benchmark and reported 12% P99 improvement for mixed workloads but saw a small throughput drop for large-batch-only traces; requested fanout_cap tuning and a runtime flag to disable warmup reserve. Author: Added fanout_cap param and a runtime toggle; Marco approved. CI flakiness: initial CI lint failure due to style in fanout_scheduler.h fixed in follow-up commit. Final review: approvals from Devon and Priya; Marco merged with squash.
Initial pipeline: lint failed (style) on first push; subsequent push fixed lint. Unit tests green except a flaky admission_test which was re-recorded and stabilized. Integration perf job (internal) passed validation thresholds for P99 and CPU footprint in canary config. All checks passing on merge.
Improves P99 latency for mixed workloads by introducing a latency-floor fanout scheduler and optional per-key KV warmup hinting. Config flags: runtime.sched.latency_floor_ms, runtime.sched.fanout_cap, runtime.sched.kv_warmup_reserve, feature.flag.fanout_latency_floor. Rollout behind feature flag. Monitoring: telemetry.fanout_decisions, telemetry.kv_warm_reserve_hits, telemetry.kv_warm_reserve_misses.
payload.title: Latency-floor fanout scheduler with per-key KV-warmup hinting
