Problem: multiple SDKs independently were doing cred pre-warm, heartbeat, and streamed telemetry which caused duplicated requests, token churn, and mismatched heartbeat intervals across languages. This led to spiky auth calls under bursty workloads and noisy telemetry. Goal: provide a single lightweight in-repo "stream-proxy" primitive that centralizes preflight credential priming, lightweight heartbeat publishers for long-lived streams, and a compact telemetry envelope for streamed metrics. The change harmonizes behavior across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs, reduces auth thundering, and enables a safer default for session lifetime handling. Summary of changes: - Add a small in-repo stream-proxy component (lib/stream_proxy/) that exposes an opinionated REST-compatible boundary used by SDK adapters. The proxy supports: cred-priming (pre-warm token and short-lived lease), heartbeat publisher (periodic keepalive events with exponential backoff on failure), and streamed_metrics envelope (compact binary/JSON variant selectable by SDK). - SDK adapters: python/ts/go subpackages updated to call the proxy during session open, to subscribe/unsubscribe heartbeat publishers when streams start/stop, and to emit streamed_metrics via the proxy rather than directly to the telemetry backend. - Ergonomics: simplified client API surface for streaming to a single method on the sdk client: start_stream(options) with opt-in advanced hooks for custom heartbeat intervals and preflight scope. This reduces ceremony for the common case. - Backwards compatibility: when the proxy is not available (older deployments), SDKs fall back to previous per-language behavior; we added a detection and a conservative retry/jitter profile so behavior remains stable. - Version bumps: synchronized minor bumps for SDK packages to make the new ergonomics available: python 0.12.4 -> 0.12.5, typescript 1.6.0 -> 1.6.1, go 1.8.2 -> 1.8.3; changelogs included. Migration notes: - Existing consumers need not change immediately. To opt in to the proxy behavior, set client.start_stream({enable_proxy: true}) or set REDWOOD_STREAM_PROXY=1 in environment. - If you manage a Private deployment, see deployments/stream_proxy/README.md for install/compat notes; the proxy is optional but recommended for high-throughput stream workloads. Testing and verification: unit tests for proxy logic, adapter integration tests for Py/TS/Go, and a lightweight throughput canary in perf-canary/stream-proxy-test. We ran canary traffic for 72h across regions (us-west1/eu-west1) with telemetry validated and auth calls reduced by ~65% under synthetic bursts. Rollout: staged rollout on hosted API with feature-flag gate; automatic fallback on proxy error conditions. Why this is different: rather than adding per-SDK heuristics we provide a thin, deployable coordinator that keeps language ergonomics simple while centralizing auth/heartbeat behavior.
Diego: could we avoid a sync call on warm path? Author: switched to async preflight with best-effort fallback and adjusted tests. Priya: telemetry envelope needs version marker to support future schema changes. Author: added 'v' field and document. Liam: minor nit on CLI installation docs; addressed. Diego approved after async preflight change, Priya approved after envelope version, Liam approved. Final :tada: merge by squash.
- Added optional in-repo stream-proxy to centralize credential priming and heartbeat publishing across SDKs; opt-in via enable_proxy or env var. - SDKs (Python/TS/Go) updated with lightweight stream adapter and simplified start_stream API. - Reduced auth churn and duplicated telemetry under bursty workloads. - Minor SDK version bumps: py->0.12.5, ts->1.6.1, go->1.8.3.
This PR coordinates code across SDKs and the deployable proxy. Operations should coordinate a staged rollout if you host the private control plane. If deploying the proxy in private clusters, ensure KMS keys are configured for the token-lease path.
payload.title: Introduce stream-proxy: preflight cred-priming, heartbeat publishers, and tri-SDK version bumps

payload.body:
Introduces a rate-decoupler and ephemeral failfast probe to reduce regional SLO churn during transient egress pressure. Configurable via runtime flags and defaults disabled for Dedicated/Private until validated.
Motivation: We observed repeated SLO thrash during intermittent egress constraints in EU-west, where the controller oscillates between full routing and aggressive regional fallbacks. This PR adds a rate-decoupler layer and a short-lived failfast probe to reduce noisy circuit flips and provide a predictable soft-degradation window. Summary of changes: 1) Rate-decoupler: an admission adapter that maintains a small token buffer decoupling incoming request rate from the backend dispatch rate for up to configured headroom (defaults: 200ms burst, 1s smoothing window). This allows brief upstream surges to burst through without triggering immediate tenant-level circuit actions. 2) Ephemeral failfast probe: a lightweight probe that runs a fast path health check against the region's egress mesh; if the probe detects transient egress saturation it will open an ephemeral failfast (30s by default) which signals dependent components to enter short soft-degrade mode instead of firing long-lived circuit breakers. 3) Telemetry and safeties: new metrics (rate_decoupler.* and ephemeral_probe.*), a debug-only trace hook for request lineage through the decoupler, and automatic escalation to existing SLO enforcer after repeated ephemeral failfasts. 4) Config & rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag "enable_rate_decoupler" (default: false in hosted main), and added canary rollout knobs in the console to enable per-region and per-tenant overrides. Compatibility: No API changes. This is purely a serving runtime adapter. Why this is different: previous mitigations relied on immediate tenant-circuit flips which caused collateral degradation for unaffected tenants; the decoupler tolerates millisecond bursts and the ephemeral probe provides a short, auditable degradation window so the system prefers soft degrade over wholesale circuiting. Metrics to watch: p99 latency, rate_decoupler.buffer_fill, ephemeral_probe.failures, slo_enforcer.invocations. Rollout plan: canary 1% EU-west for 24h -> 10% with autoscaled monitoring -> full region. If metrics indicate increased p99 or error rates, roll back feature flag and disable automatic escalation. Related tickets: ENG-2230 implements the adapter, ENG-2247 contains integration tests, SUP-9812 traced customer incident where oscillations were observed.
Ops: enable feature gate via runtime flag rather than cluster restart. For hosted canary use console -> feature flags -> enable_rate_decoupler for eu-west-1 at 1%. Watch metrics: rate_decoupler.buffer_fill, ephemeral_probe.open_count, slo_enforcer.escalations. If buffer_fill remains >90% for >10m, disable immediately to avoid backlog.
Unit tests added for token buffer semantics. Integration harness simulates egress saturation and asserts ephemeral probe opens for <60s and then closes. Manual smoke: deploy to dev region with flag on, inject short 2x normal egress latency spike and confirm soft degrade signals observed but no tenant circuit flips. Metrics validated in the stress harness (see test/probe_integration.sh).
Flip runtime flag enable_rate_decoupler=false in console; disable per-region overrides if set. If rollback fails to stop degradation, revert the merged commit in main and redeploy. Record incident and escalate to runtime team.
Diego Alvarez: Can we bound the memory impact of the token buffer under heavy tenant churn? Suggest adding a hard cap per node.
Maya Chen: Added per-node hard cap and eviction policy; described limits in config comments. See decoupler.go lines 120-145.
Priya Nair: We need to ensure the ephemeral failfast doesn't suppress important 5xx signals used by SLO enforcer. Please add an escalation path.
Maya Chen: Added automatic escalation that converts three ephemeral failfasts within 5 minutes to a standard SLO enforcer invocation (configurable).
Samuel Ortiz: CI flake on probe integration -- looks like test harness port conflict. Re-ran CI after changing ephemeral port selection.
Maya Chen: Confirmed; made probe port selection randomized in test harness and added retry logic.
payload.title: Introduce rate-decoupler and ephemeral failfast probe for graceful regional downgrades

payload.body:
Motivation: In high-churn tenant fleets we observed many small, short-lived reservations that fragment pool capacity and inflate headroom estimates. This leads to unstable autoscaler decisions (frequent scale ups followed by rapid scale downs) and noisy utilization metrics. This PR introduces two cooperating pieces: (1) a Gradual Reserve Unifier controller that periodically coalesces adjacent or rapidly renewing micro-reservations into a single logical reservation to reduce fragmentation and smooth headroom; and (2) a lightweight per-pool Utilization Heartbeat emitter that samples and reports reservoir-level utilization percentile snapshots at a configurable cadence. The goal is to improve autoscaler stability and give SREs more reliable percentile-based signals for throughput guarantees.

What this changes (summary):
- controller/gradual_unifier.go: new controller that scans pool reservations and merges candidates according to time-window and affinity rules. It exposes config knobs: unify_window_ms, min_reservation_age_ms, max_merge_factor.
- telemetry/pool_heartbeat.go: new emitter that publishes a small telemetry event (utilization_p50/p90/p99, active_reservations, reserved_capacity) every heartbeat. Events are routed to the existing telemetry pipeline with a new metric namespace dedicated.pool_heartbeat.
- config/defaults.yaml: defaults for the unifier and heartbeat (disabled in Private by default; can be enabled via dedicated.features.unifier=true).
- charts/dedicated/values.yaml: Helm flags for operators to opt-in and tune parameters per deployment class.
- docs/ops/gradual-reserve-unifier.md: operational runbook, rollout steps, observability dashboard examples and rollback guidance.
- tests/unifier_e2e.go: synthetic e2e harness that exercises fragmentation and verifies autoscaler stability improvements (asserts decrease in scale-flap frequency).

Design notes: The unifier only touches reservations with compatible affinity labels and only merges when merge factor results in >=10% reduction in active reservations for the same capacity footprint (configurable). We intentionally avoid global locking: merges are append-only transforms that create a new unified reservation and mark old reservations for graceful expiry to prevent mid-flight eviction of tailing requests. The heartbeat emitter samples internal ringbuffers rather than full KV scans to keep overhead under 0.2% CPU for large pools.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature gated off by default in cloud-hosted; enable in internal canary clusters for 48h.
2) Run telemetry-only (heartbeat enabled, unifier disabled) for 72h to validate metric signal stability.
3) Enable unifier in a single low-traffic pool with conservative params (unify_window_ms=30000, max_merge_factor=4).
4) Gradually increase rollout if scaling flaps reduce and service-level throughput remains within 0.5% of baseline.

Benchmarks and results: Local perf lab simulated 50k reservations with median lifetime 12s. With unifier+heartbeat enabled we saw: 45% drop in reservation count variance, tail autoscale events reduced by ~60%, controller CPU overhead +0.15% at 99th percentile. E2E harness shows median request latency unchanged; 95th percentile improved by ~3% under high churn.

Security and config: No secret material. Operators can opt out. The unifier respects tenant isolation labels and cannot merge reservations across tenant boundaries (enforced in code and tested).

Related work: builds on ENG-1678 (reservation lifecycle rewrite) and complements ENG-7692 (stabilized-autoscaler). See SUP-3421 for customer-reported fragmentation incident that motivated the work.

Notes for reviewers: key safety checks are in tests/unifier_e2e.go and unit tests around affinity matching. Pay attention to edge cases around reservation expiry races; I added a small jitter to the expiry window to avoid thundering merges.

Maya Ivanov: This looks promising — please double-check tenant isolation and race windows; the merge path must be idempotent.

S. Ramos (author): Answered: unifier marks old reservations as 'deprecated' and we expire them via the normal lifecycle; added tests to cover idempotency.

Ravi Singh: CI e2e flaked once under high concurrency — can you add a retry to the harness and make failure deterministic?

S. Ramos: Added retry + tightened timing in tests; CI rerun passed.

Elena Gomez: Request: add a dashboard tile showing 'merged_reservations/sec' and a rollback playbook.

S. Ramos: Added dashboard snippet to docs and an operator rollback section (docs/ops/gradual-reserve-unifier.md).

Maya Ivanov: Approved after address comments.

Automated CI: initial unit tests pass, integration tests failed on first run (timeout), integration re-run pass, e2e passed in synthetic harness. Linter: pass. Security scan: no findings.
Add optional 'Gradual Reserve Unifier' to coalesce short-lived reservations and a low-overhead 'per-pool utilization heartbeat' metric to improve autoscaler stability and utilization visibility. Feature is disabled by default and must be enabled by operators in dedicated.features.unifier. Rollout guidance provided in docs/ops/gradual-reserve-unifier.md.
Latency: no client-visible changes expected. Cost: minor controller CPU +0.1-0.3% in large pools. Risk: medium-low; potential for unexpected reservation consolidation if misconfigured; safeguards included (tenant boundaries, affinity checks, opt-out).
payload.title: Introduce gradual reserve unifier and per-pool utilization heartbeat

payload.body:
Motivation: On long-lived workloads with variable sequence lengths we observed sustained small-object allocations inside the KV arena that caused increased page faults, allocator metadata churn, and elevated tail latency during traffic spikes. This PR introduces a low-risk two-part approach: (1) a page-consolidation pass that coalesces small adjacent KV entries into contiguous pages to reduce fragmentation and the number of page table entries; (2) a proactive rebalancer that migrates underutilized slab regions between arenas during idle windows to keep hot entries collocated and free large contiguous ranges for future large-key allocations. Both changes are designed to be conservative by default (config flags + safe thresholds) and opt-in for Dedicated/Private customers before we flip to default in hosted environments.

What this PR does: Implements a background page-consolidation job in runtime/kv that runs opportunistically when CPU and memory headroom are available, and a proactive rebalancer in runtime/kv/rebalancer that uses a lightweight access-frequency sketch to move cold regions. The consolidation pass uses a compacting writer that preserves existing stable pointers for readers via a short-lived epoch grace period (readers observe old pages until consolidation completes). The rebalancer integrates with scheduler to request small maintenance windows (micro-backoff) so migration does not interfere with latency SLOs.

Compatibility and safety: All behavior gated behind config flags (kvc.page_consolidation.enabled, kvc.rebalancer.enabled) with thresholds and a rollout knob (max_migrations_per_minute). The data movement maintains checksums and uses write-ahead markers so we can resume interrupted consolidations after process restart. No on-disk format changes.

Benchmarks: On a synthetic chat workload (p50 token latency-sensitive, mixed short/long sequences) we measured: - 9-12% reduction in page-faults per-minute; - 6% improvement in sustained throughput at SLO latency windows under high concurrency; - 18% reduction in tail latency spikes attributable to paging-related stalls. Overhead when idle is <1% CPU; consolidation triggered ~2x per hour on the test fixture.

Testing and rollout: Unit + integration tests added for consolidation correctness and rebalancer anti-starvation. End-to-end perf lab runs and canary on internal Dedicated cluster for 48h before broader rollout. Feature flags will be used to gradually enable across tenant tiers.

Related: ENG-5801 (KV reliability epic), ENG-6020 (scheduler maintenance windows), PERF-128 (bench harness updates).
Jordan Li (2025-11-12): Can we ensure the consolidation pass never blocks eviction? Suggest adding an explicit max_time slice per run. — responded: added max_migration_window and scheduler-cooperative yielding
Marta Gomez (2025-11-18): Added note about resume safety and checksum verification, looks good. Small nit: extract thresholds to config module. — responded: thresholds moved to runtime/kv/config.rs
Ravi Sinha (2025-11-22): Verified bench harness and observed lower tail latencies in 48h canary. Recommend gradual rollout. — acked by author
Introduces an opt-in KV page consolidation pass and proactive rebalancer to reduce fragmentation and paging. Expected to reduce page-fault related tail latency and improve throughput for mixed-length workloads. Disabled by default for Hosted; enable via kvc.page_consolidation.enabled and kvc.rebalancer.enabled in Dedicated/Private deployments.
This PR intentionally avoids changing on-disk formats and keeps all behavior behind flags. Follow-up work: automated tuning of thresholds via Optimize recommendations and a telemetry signal to auto-suggest enabling to tenants that show high small-object churn.
payload.title: KV: page-consolidation and proactive rebalancer to reduce paging and slot churn

payload.body:
Motivation: In production workloads we observed tail-latency spikes and high OOM churn when large KV items caused allocator fragmentation and reactive spillover flooded the disk/remote store. This PR introduces a two-pronged approach: (1) priority segmentation of the KV cache to isolate large/pinned entries from latency-sensitive small entries, and (2) a hybrid evictor that combines lightweight size-aware LRU with a background compaction/defragmentation pass and a rate-limited spill scheduler to avoid 'spill storms'.

Summary of changes: Adds a new KV segment abstraction (priority, transient, general), implements a hybrid evictor that prefers evicting from the transient/general segments by size and recency and only triggers spill operations when the spill_budget token bucket allows it, and a background compactor that coalesces free blocks to reduce fragmentation. Also exposes a handful of tunables (segment thresholds, spill_rate_limit, compaction_window) and a health metric set for monitoring fragmentation and spillbackpressure.

Design notes: The segmentation is implemented as a thin wrapper around the existing arena allocator; items are tagged at allocation time based on size and origin (pinned requests mark priority). The hybrid evictor keeps per-segment candidate lists and uses a two-stage decision: first try reclaim within-segment via reclaim windows and local compaction; if insufficient and spill budget remains, schedule a spill request. The compactor runs at low priority and uses epoch marking to avoid stalling fast-path allocations.

Upgrade and rollout plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag kv.hybrid_evictor.enabled with default off for 48h canary. Start with conservative spill_rate_limit=50MB/s and compaction_window=5s, monitor new metrics kv.fragmentation_ratio and kv.spill_backpressure. Rollout steps in checklist.

Checklist: - [x] implement segmentation and allocator hooks - [x] hybrid evictor and token-bucket spill throttling - [x] background compactor with non-blocking epochs - [x] unit + integration tests for eviction ordering and compaction safety - [x] benchmarks (micro and e2e) - [x] metrics and Console dashboard tiles - [x] feature flag for staged rollout

Benchmarks: Microbench against synthetic mixed-size workload (75% small tokens, 25% large KV blobs) shows 30-45% reduction in 95th-percentile allocation latency and 2.1x fewer spill operations under sustained pressure when hybrid evictor is enabled. End-to-end inference tests show 8-12% lower p95 latency for interactive small-token workloads when large cache objects are present.

Related: ENG-5241 (KV reliability), PRs that worked on eviction heuristics and paging, and a follow-up ticket to add eviction visualization in the Console.
Arjun Patel: Can we make the spill_rate_limit a runtime-configurable metric so SRE can tune without deploy? Suggests adding a /metrics endpoint export.
Maya Chen (author): Added runtime flag and metrics export in metrics.rs; verified SRE can change via dynamic config in canary.
Lena Sørensen: The compactor epoch logic looks solid, but please add a safety timeout to avoid stuck epochs during GC thrash.
Maya Chen (author): Added compaction_epoch_timeout and unit test for stuck epoch scenario.
Diego Morales: Approved after confirming no regressions on small-allocation p95 in perf lab. Left a nit on logging verbosity in compactor.
Maya Chen (author): Reduced compactor info logs to debug and left a comment with instrumentation guidance.
Introduces KV priority segmentation and a hybrid evictor to reduce fragmentation-driven latency spikes and prevent large spill storms. Exposes kv.hybrid_evictor.enabled, kv.spill_rate_limit, and kv.compaction_window for tuning. Benchmarked to reduce p95 allocation latency and spill count under mixed workloads.
payload.title: kv: priority segmentation and hybrid evictor to mitigate fragmentation and spill storms

payload.body:
Title: Tune backpressure thresholds for long prefill workloads

Context
Long-context summarization / retrieval-augmented prompts (large prefill, modest decode) are a top variance driver in the Q1 2026 perf suite (ENG-4824). In baseline sweeps we repeatedly see p99 TTFT spikes correlated with scheduler backpressure entering “hard stop” mode too aggressively once prefill token-in-flight crosses the global watermark. This PR retunes the default thresholds and adds guardrails to protect overall throughput under mixed traffic.

What changed (high level)
- Retune scheduler backpressure thresholds to reduce p99 TTFT specifically in the long-prefill cohort while keeping tokens/s within expected noise for chat/embeddings.
- Split the single prefill watermark into a two-stage (soft/hard) admission control:
  - Soft stage: slows acceptance by applying a small queue delay and preferentially assembling smaller prefill batches.
  - Hard stage: rejects/defers new long-prefill admissions only when the in-flight prefill budget is truly saturated.
- Add a “decode reservation” floor so we don’t starve decode during a prefill-heavy burst (prevents TPOT regressions for streaming chat).
- Emit new metrics tags for backpressure transitions so dashboards can explain TTFT tails (ties into ENG-4826 instrumentation work).

Detailed changes
- scheduler/backpressure:
  - Increase `prefill_inflight_soft_limit_tokens` (default) to reduce premature throttling.
  - Lower `prefill_inflight_hard_limit_tokens` only slightly; keep hard stop available for overload.
  - Change `backpressure_soft_wait_ms` from a flat wait to a capped jittered delay (reduces synchronization artifacts when many workers cross the watermark at once).
  - Add `decode_reservation_ratio` (default 0.15) to keep decode from being starved by large prefills.
  - Tighten the “long-prefill” classifier threshold to better match representative suite bins (>= 8k prefill tokens).
- scheduler/batch assembly:
  - When in soft backpressure, bias toward forming smaller prefill batches to reduce head-of-line blocking and shorten TTFT tails.
- observability:
  - New counters: `scheduler_backpressure_soft_enter_total`, `scheduler_backpressure_hard_enter_total`.
  - New histogram: `scheduler_backpressure_soft_delay_ms`.
  - Tagging: `workload_class={chat_streaming,long_prefill,embeddings}` and `reason={prefill_inflight,queue_depth,decode_reservation}`.

Before/after (perf suite)
Method
- Benchmark harness: representative workload suite v1 long-prefill test (ENG-4824) + mixed traffic smoke (chat streaming + embeddings) to validate no obvious throughput regressions.
- Environment: A100-80GB (us-east), driver 550.54, CUDA 12.4, runtime build redwood@9c3f6e1 (before) vs redwood@c4b0a2d (after).
- Runs: 5x per scenario, discard first run (warmup), report median of remaining 4 runs. Cold and warm cache reported separately; this PR targets cold-path TTFT.

Results summary
Long-prefill cohort (prefill ~ 12k–16k tokens, decode 256)
- TTFT p50: 1.42s -> 1.36s (-4.2%)
- TTFT p95: 3.98s -> 3.21s (-19.3%)
- TTFT p99: 6.87s -> 4.78s (-30.4%)
- Prefill tokens/s (aggregate): 100% baseline -> 98.9% (within noise; see notes)

Mixed traffic smoke (chat streaming + embeddings)
- Chat streaming TTFT p99: +1.1% (noise; no consistent trend across runs)
- Chat streaming TPOT p95: -0.8% (noise)
- Embeddings req/s: -0.4% (noise)

Notes
- The soft-stage delay introduced small increases in queue time at p50 during saturation, but materially reduced p99 by avoiding hard stop oscillations.
- In traces, the “thundering herd” pattern (many workers hitting the watermark simultaneously) is reduced due to jittered delay + smaller prefill batch bias.
- Throughput delta is not statistically significant in our current noise model; see reviewer thread below for rationale.

Risk & rollout
- This changes scheduler defaults. Guardrails:
  - Hard limit remains in place; we are not increasing max in-flight prefill without bound.
  - `decode_reservation_ratio` prevents decode starvation.
  - All knobs are config-driven and can be reverted via fleet config without a rebuild.
- Proposed rollout:
  - Land behind config defaults for benchmark environments first (perf suite + canary).
  - After 48h canary stability, roll out to 10% hosted clusters in us-east only.

Checklist
- [x] Added/updated unit tests for backpressure state transitions
- [x] Added metrics for backpressure enter/exit + delay distribution
- [x] Ran representative suite long-prefill workload (cold + warm)
- [x] Ran mixed traffic smoke (chat streaming + embeddings)
- [x] Added notes to scheduler defaults doc (follow-up PR to confluence planned)

Screenshots / artifacts
- Baseline run IDs: perf-suite/a100-us-east/long-prefill/2026-01-22T03:14Z (before), 2026-01-23T05:02Z (after)
- Trace links (internal): go/trace/sched-bp-longprefill-21541 (before/after pair)

Related
- ENG-4824 (long-context prefill workload)
- ENG-4826 (scheduler instrumentation)
- Slack thread: eng-runtime/1763608899 (p99 regression triage; decision to adjust backpressure)

Noah Patel (review): The before/after looks good for long-prefill TTFT. Two questions: (1) Why is soft limit increasing but hard limit only slightly changed? (2) Can we prove we’re not just pushing latency into queue time? Please add a metric that attributes TTFT tail to queue wait vs prefill compute.
Sofia Ivanova (author): (1) Soft limit was the main culprit for oscillation; hard limit is still a safety valve for overload so I kept it conservative. (2) Agree — added `scheduler_backpressure_soft_delay_ms` histogram and tagged `scheduler_queue_wait_ms` in the perf harness export. In the after traces, queue wait increases slightly at p50 under saturation, but p99 TTFT drops because we avoid hard stop + re-admission cycles.
Lena Fischer (review): `decode_reservation_ratio=0.15` seems arbitrary. Did you test 0.10 vs 0.20? Also please document the rationale inline in config defaults.
Sofia Ivanova (author): Ran a quick sweep on A100 for 0.10/0.15/0.20. 0.10 occasionally allowed decode starvation during prefill bursts (TPOT p99 up ~6% in one run). 0.20 started to hurt long-prefill throughput more consistently (~3%). 0.15 was stable across runs. Added an inline comment + links to run IDs in `config_defaults.yaml`.
Sean Gallagher (SRE review): Concerned about default changes landing without a canary plan. Please add a note about fleet-config rollback and ensure metrics are low cardinality. Also, are the new tags safe for prod?
Sofia Ivanova (author): Added rollout notes to the PR body and confirmed tags are bounded (`workload_class` enum + `reason` enum). No request IDs. Cardinality should be stable. Rollback is via scheduler config defaults in fleet config; no binary rollback needed.
Omar El-Sayed (review): Any interaction with KV cache / warm runs? We should ensure warm cache numbers don’t regress unexpectedly.
Sofia Ivanova (author): Warm runs are neutral; p99 TTFT warm changes were within +/-2%. The code paths that change behavior are mainly admission gating for large prefills; warm cache reduces prefill compute so it hits backpressure less frequently.
Noah Patel (review): Requested changes: please add a unit test that reproduces the oscillation by crossing soft limit repeatedly; and ensure backpressure state transitions are logged at debug level for perf runs only.
Sofia Ivanova (author): Added `TestBackpressureSoftLimitOscillationDoesNotTriggerHardStop` and gated debug logs behind `SCHED_DEBUG=1` (already only enabled in benchmark harness).
Noah Patel (review): Approved.
Sean Gallagher (review): Approved (SRE).
Lena Fischer (review): Approved.

payload.body:
Motivation: We've seen recurring short-lived tail-latency spikes on cold prefix/cache misses and during client-driven prompt shapes (very long system prompts or unusual instruction formatting). These spikes generate noisy SLO alerts and obscure genuine regressions. This change introduces explicit 'prefix_warmup' annotated spans, a small histogram metric keyed by prompt_shape (a lightweight fingerprint of prompt structure), and a dashboard panel to visualize tail-latency by prompt_shape and warmup state.

What this PR does: - Adds span annotations for prefix warmup start/finish and tags spans with a boolean warmup=true/false and a lightweight prompt_shape key. - Emits prefix_warmup_duration_ms histogram and increments a warmup_miss counter so we can correlate cost and latency. - Adds a Prompt Shape Tail Latency dashboard (heatmap + percentile ridgeline) to help SREs and ML infra teams identify prompt shapes that cause persistent tails. - Introduces an alert tuning rule that dampens SLO alerts when the signal originates from warmup-only spans and requires persistence across N windows before firing. - Adds docs with guidance on interpreting the panel and recommended mitigations (prefetch, batching, model variant).

Checklist:
- [x] Instrument spans and metrics
- [x] Add dashboard JSON and snapshot
- [x] Add alert tuning and unit tests for rule logic
- [x] Add integration test for warmup span emission
- [x] Docs for oncall and SRE

Related: ENG-3241 (reduce warmup alert noise), SUP-812 (customer report of tail latency on long prompts). This is intentionally conservative: warmup spans are low-cardinality (prompt_shape is compact hashed string) and sampling is configurable via the existing telemetry sampler.

Notes on rollout: feature flag telemetry.prefix_warmup.enabled defaults to false in production; enabled in staging for 24h before opt-in on main. Metric cardinality guard added to prefix_warmup_metrics.go to cap new label counts to 200 per tenant.

Luca Alvarez (2026-02-16): Nicely scoped. Please add an explicit cardinality guard and document the prompt_shape hashing function so support engineers don't leak raw prompts.
Maya Chen (2026-02-16): Added a 200-per-tenant cap and expanded docs; prompt_shape is an sha1 of structural tokens (see docs).
Priya Nair (2026-02-17): Can we make the alert require 3 windows of 5m instead of 1 to reduce churn? Also add a test covering the suppressed-alert path.
Maya Chen (2026-02-17): Updated alert rule, added unit test for suppression logic. CI flaked once on lint (line length) — fixed.
Omar Williams (2026-02-19): LGTM after addressing one nits in comments. Approving for merge.
Added prefix warmup tracing and a prompt-shape tail latency dashboard; introduced alert tuning to reduce warmup-driven SLO noise. Rollout behind feature flag. See docs/observability/prefix-warmup.md for guidance.

payload.body:
Motivation: multiplexed streaming and tool/function calls expose subtle race conditions around retries and idempotency when requests are concurrently routed, retried, or partially acknowledged. Existing behavior relied on opaque Retry-After hints and an ad-hoc idempotency key semantics that caused duplicate side effects in rare failure windows. This PR introduces two interoperable primitives and related server-side controls: 1) a machine-readable Retry-Watermark header that carries a bounded, monotonic token describing the server's current retry window and partial-ACK state; 2) an Idempotency-Context header that scopes idempotency to a tool-call session (session id + optional call index) and allows the bridge to reconcile retries across multiplexed frames.

What this changes:
- API contract: clients can send Idempotency-Context to declare the logical tool-call session; servers will include Retry-Watermark on 429/503/retryable frames when stateful partial progress exists.
- Error envelopes: adds explicit machine-readable error codes in the structured error envelope (code: rate_limited | retry_window | session_mismatch | capacity_degraded) and a consistent retry_hint object with fields (preferred_wait_seconds, watermark_token).
- Runtime: server-side enforcement of a bounded retry window per model-pool (default 30s) and an optional conservative fallback policy to a stateless variant when watermark indicates session mismatch.
- Backwards compatibility: servers still honor Retry-After and legacy idempotency-key headers. Retry-Watermark is additive: clients/SDKs are encouraged to prefer Retry-Watermark when present for deterministic retry orchestration.

Implementation summary:
- API layer: add parsing/validation for Idempotency-Context and generation of Retry-Watermark tokens (base64 HMAC over pool-id, monotonic counter, expiry).
- Runtime: attach per-request watermark state to streaming multiplexers and tool-call sessions; introduce graceful fallback to stateless model variant when watermark mismatch detected.
- OpenAI-compat shim: map Retry-Watermark + structured error codes into OpenAI-style 429 with a machine-readable JSON body under "error.meta.retry_hint" for SDKs that consume only the body.
- SDK changes (python/ts): small handling code to propagate Idempotency-Context and surface retry_hint to callers; tests added.
- Docs: new API section documenting the headers, example retry loops, and migration guidance for existing idempotency-key usage.

Checklist:
- [x] Add Retry-Watermark header generation and validation
- [x] Implement Idempotency-Context parsing and session scoping
- [x] Add structured error codes and retry_hint mapping
- [x] Add unit tests for watermark token expiry and session reconciliation
- [x] Add E2E test for multiplexed stream retry scenario
- [x] Update openai-compat adapter to include retry_hint mapping
- [x] Update python and typescript SDKs with propagation helpers
- [x] Add docs and upgrade notes

Backwards-incompatible notes: default retry window shortened from 60s to 30s for model pools where Retry-Watermark is enabled (configurable). Migration guidance included in docs.

Linkages: this work is a follow-up to ENG-7420 and touches run-time batching and stream framing components. Design doc: internal/notes/retry-watermark.md (linked in PR comments).
Marcus Li: Please clarify the semantics around watermark expiry. Is it safe for clients to retry after expiry or must they start a new session?
Elena Rivera: Watermark expiry indicates server can no longer reconcile partial state. Clients may retry but will get a session_mismatch code; recommended flow is to start a fresh session id when session_mismatch is returned. Added docs and tests to cover this.
Sofia Patel: Concerned about token size and privacy (pool id leakage). Can we HMAC with server-only key?
Elena Rivera: Yes — tokens are HMACed with an internal signing key; docs updated to note tokens are opaque and must not be interpreted by clients beyond equality/expiry.
Jonah Brooks: CI flake in e2e occurred due to timing of watermark expiry; suggested making tests less timing-sensitive.
Elena Rivera: Adjusted test to use deterministic clock injection and re-ran CI. CI initially failed on lint step (tslint rule) then passed after formatting fix.
Sofia Patel: Approving pending one small doc wording change. Doc wording updated. Marcus Li: Approved. Merge done via squash.
- Add Retry-Watermark header and Idempotency-Context to improve deterministic retries for multiplexed streams and tool calls.
- Introduce structured error codes and retry_hint object for machine-readable retry instructions.
- Shorten default retry window for watermark-enabled pools to 30s (configurable).

payload.body:
Motivation: KV cache fragmentation from variable-sized entries and incremental spills was causing increased resident set size and p95 latency spikes under mixed workloads. Small free holes accumulate and cause frequent paging/spillovers despite overall available capacity. This PR introduces a tenant-aware background defragmenter ("mosaic rechunker") plus a controlled spillback policy to an asynchronous compressed spill pool to lower fragmentation and reduce tail latencies while keeping steady-state throughput. Summary of changes: 1) mosaic rechunker: a background worker that identifies small adjacent free slots and coalesces live objects into compact segments, using a lightweight pinning protocol to avoid KV reads during relocation. The worker uses tenant affinity and request-rate heuristics to prioritize cold tenants and minimize user impact. 2) spillback manager: when memory pressure is sustained above a configurable threshold, large cold segments are asynchronously compressed and written to the spill pool (on-disk/remote SSD) with eviction tickets. Spillback is rate-limited and can be configured per-tenant; the runtime can transparently fetch and rehydrate segments on demand. 3) scheduler integration: the serving scheduler receives new kernel hints so hot-path token-generation requests avoid nodes with active rehousing operations; background rechunker and spill tasks are throttled by runtime SLO tokens to limit tail impact. 4) observability and safety: added telemetry events for rechunk steps, spillback latencies, and per-tenant reclaimed bytes; added graceful shutdown and abort semantics for in-flight relocations. Checklist: - [x] mosaic rechunker prototype and unit tests - [x] spillback manager and integration tests with simulated remote pool - [x] scheduler kernel hints and integration with continuous batching - [x] perf harness and benchmarks showing improvements - [x] ops doc with tuning knobs and recommended thresholds Results (perf harness, mixed RW with realistic doc sizes): - Median latency for small gen requests: ~2.8ms -> 2.6ms (3.6% improvement) - P95 latency for mixed workload: 44ms -> 31ms (29.5% improvement) - Resident set memory fragmentation reduced by ~28% across tenants - Steady-state throughput unchanged within 1-2% (no regression) Backwards compatibility and flags: feature gated behind runtime flag kv.rechunk.enabled=false by default; spillback requires kv.spillback.enabled=false to opt-in. Migration: non-disruptive. See docs/ops/kv-rechunker.md for tuning guidance and recommended defaults. Motivation references: ENG-2345 (fragmentation incidents), SUP-891 (support ticket describing tenant OOM while node had free holes).
Ethan Cole: The relocation protocol looks solid but we need a stronger invariant around multi-threaded pin/unpin to avoid ABA; please add a stress test for concurrent relocations.
Marta Lopez: Can we add a per-tenant hard cap on concurrent spillback streams? A single noisy tenant shouldn't saturate the remote pool.
Samir Gupta: The scheduler hint interface is small and safe, but please ensure hint propagation doesn't add RPC overhead on the hot path; consider caching decisions for 100ms.
Priya Nair (author): Added stress test and fixed pin/unpin ABA window; implemented tenant-level concurrent spillback cap. Scheduler hint now cached for 150ms by default and feature-gated.
Introduces an experimental kv.rechunk background defragmenter and kv.spillback remote compressed spill policy. Reduces KV cache fragmentation and p95 tail latencies for mixed workloads. Feature-gated; see docs/ops/kv-rechunker.md for tuning.

payload.body:
Motivation: recent incidents showed rapid, correlated circuit state flips across regional proxies when noisy tenants triggered transient downstream latency. That oscillation caused unnecessary regional failovers and SLO remediation thrash. This hotpatch introduces a deferred circuit coalescer that smooths circuit transitions, applies a short SLO-cooling window to reduce aggressive failover actions, and provides explicit telemetry for post-incident analysis.

What this PR does (summary): adds a lightweight coalescer component that groups circuit-open signals over a configurable time window, computes an aggregated severity score, and only triggers a full regional circuit transition if the score crosses thresholds. Meanwhile, for intermediate severities the system applies an SLO-cooling policy: temporarily relax per-tenant SLO enforcement thresholds and convert immediate failover actions into staged degraded routes (soft-evict -> rate-limit -> failover). The patch also exposes new Prometheus metrics and tracing spans to help investigate coalescing decisions.

Key design points: single-file coalescer state is sharded by region and by tenant-priority-bucket to minimize lock contention. The coalescer keeps a short event ring buffer per shard, computes an exponential backoff for repeated opens, and emits a coalesced_event with reason, weight, and suggested action. SLO-cooling is timeboxed and conservative: nominal relaxed_margin defaults to 10% for 30s and is downgraded if errors continue. All defaults are tunable via config flags and a feature-gate for progressive rollout.

Rollback and safety: feature-gate defaults to off. For the hotpatch we enable the gate in canary (us-east-1 small cohort) and have a fast revert path (toggle feature-gate) plus a dedicated emergency endpoint to force immediate circuit resets if needed. No persistent migrations.

Testing and verification: added unit tests for coalescer scoring, integration test that simulates bursty tenant events to assert no more than one immediate region-wide failover in the window, and a synthetic load canary harness run in perf-canary that validated latency tail improvement and reduced flip count under noise.

Operational notes / rollout: enable feature-gate "deferred_circuit_coalescer" in canary region for 48h, monitor new metrics (coalescer_coalesced_events_total, coalescer_decision_latency_seconds, slo_cooling_applied_total). If flip-rate decreases and application error SLOs remain acceptable, expand to 3 regions over one week.

Files changed: small changes in circuit manager (Go), config, telemetry collector, and a new coalescer package. No changes to customer-facing API.

Why unique: rather than lowering thresholds globally or making longer cooldowns (which harmed healthy tenants), the coalescer defers action and uses aggregated signals so that transient correlated noise is handled as a group without aggressive per-tenant penalties.
2026-02-21 Leah Martinez: Nice approach. Two asks: (1) please add a metric for "coalescer_suppressed_open_total" so we can quantify suppression, (2) ensure the ring buffer has an upper bound to avoid OOM under pathological signal storms.
2026-02-22 Jin Park: Thanks — added coalescer_suppressed_open_total and cap the ring buffer to 1024 events per shard. Updated unit tests for the cap.
2026-02-23 Marco Santoro: Safety nit — can we make the default feature-gate OFF in config.yaml and document the manual enable procedure in the runbook? Also add a short-circuit in manager to bypass coalescer for admin-forced resets.
2026-02-24 Jin Park: Done. Feature-gate default set to false and runbook updated. Added admin bypass endpoint with auth checks.
2026-02-25 Ethan Cole: Ran perf-canary smoke. Observed 42% reduction in flip-rate and tail latency improved by ~6th percentile. Approving to merge after CI green.
2026-02-27 CI: All checks passed — merging with squash.
Hotpatch: Add deferred circuit coalescer and timeboxed SLO-cooling to smooth regional failovers and reduce circuit flip thrash. Feature gated, canary rollout recommended. Metrics and runbook included.
If observing unexpected broad degradation after enabling, toggle feature-gate 'deferred_circuit_coalescer' to false to revert. Emergency endpoint /admin/circuits/reset?force=true exists with RBAC checks. Monitor coalescer_suppressed_open_total and slo_cooling_applied_total to ensure expected behavior.
Unit tests for scoring and buffer cap added. Integration tests simulate bursty tenants, verifying no more than one regional failover per 60s window in the canary scenario. Perf-canary run validated stability under noise and reduced flip-rate.

payload.body:
Motivation: Our existing canary probes surface regressions but noisy traffic and transient microbursts cause false positives and unnecessary rollbacks. This PR introduces a traffic curation layer and probe-scaling levers that reduce noise while preserving sensitivity for real regressions. It also adds a staged throttle rollout guard that gracefully applies backpressure during sustained degradation instead of immediate failover.

What this changes (high level):
- perf-canary/orchestrator: new TrafficCurator component that stratifies live traffic into cohorts by request shape (seq_len buckets), origin, and synthetic probe budget. It exposes a lightweight API used by the probe scheduler to decide which traffic to sample for canary comparisons.
- perf-canary/probes: probe-scaling configuration (probe_credit_budget, burst_resilience, temporal_strata) and logic for adaptive probe placement across replicas. Probes now use reservoir sampling with per-cohort weights so low-volume but important slices still get coverage.
- perf-canary/guards: StagedThrottleGuard implements a three-stage response to detected throughput/latency deltas: 1) soft-attenuation (reduce new canary traffic by fraction), 2) adaptive backpressure (increase probe density + throttle non-critical background routes), 3) circuit-escrow (hold critical traffic on safe model variant while rollouts pause). Each stage has configurable thresholds and cooldown windows.
- metrics/tracing: additional tags emitted for curator decisions (cohort, reason, probe_id) and guard decisions (stage, anchor_metric, confidence). These feed into console dashboards and the canary-runbook.
- tests: unit + integration harness: synthetic microburst generator, cohort replay tests, and a new e2e canary scenario that simulates slow memory-pressure-induced tail latency plus throughput drop.

Implementation notes:
- Baselines are estimated via an online quantile sketch per cohort (T-Digest variant) to keep memory bounded for high cardinality slices. The curator periodically compacts sketches and computes delta z-scores used by the guard.
- Probe scaling respects a global probe_credit_budget. Credits accrue on a per-window basis and are consumed by probes; when budget is low the curator prioritizes high-SLO cohorts using a priority function.
- StagedThrottleGuard uses a hysteresis-aware cooldown: each escalation stage has a soft deadline; if metrics recover within deadline the guard de-escalates without rollback.
- Safety: defaults are conservative to avoid customer-visible impact; the guard is opt-in per deployment until one week of canary metrics collection after rollout.

Related work: replaces ad-hoc heuristics from ENG-1920 and complements the rollout-sentinel in ENG-1805 by focusing on sample quality and controlled throttling rather than immediate cutoff.

Checklist:
- [x] Traffic curation algorithm and API
- [x] Probe scaling config + scheduler integration
- [x] StagedThrottleGuard implementation + unit tests
- [x] E2E harness scenario and CI jobs
- [x] Metrics/tags wired to console panels

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: misprioritization of cohorts could under-sample important traffic. Mitigation: default priority function favors low-volume auth/enterprise routes; manual overrides per-tenant are supported.
- Risk: sketch drift during traffic shifts. Mitigation: periodic full-window compaction and a fallback to rolling-window histograms when drift detected.

Rollout plan:
1) merge to main behind feature flag off
2) enable on perf-canary staging for two days, collect telemetry
3) smoke enable on 10% of canaries, monitor for false positives
4) full opt-in for all perf-canary runs after 7 days if stable

This PR is focused on production safety and reducing noisy rollbacks; it does not change model routing logic or model artifacts.
Miguel Santos: Nice approach to cohorting — can we add a simple regression test that verifies prioritization under extreme cardinality?
Aisha Patel: Added a priority stress test in perf-canary/tests/test_curator.py and a comment describing the priority function
Jordan Lee: The T-Digest compaction frequency looks like it may add CPU overhead at high QPS; can we make compaction adaptive?
Aisha Patel: Made compaction adaptive based on QPS and sketch error threshold; added benchmarks to the unit tests
Priya Desai: CI shows a flaky e2e failure on the first run; seems related to test timing — can we stabilize?
Aisha Patel: Increased timeouts in harness and switched generator seeds to deterministic stream; reran CI
Introduce traffic curation and staged throttle rollout guard for perf canaries; opt-in behind feature flag. Reduces false-positive rollbacks by improving probe sampling and adding a gradual backpressure policy.

- Adds Console backend APIs for viewing and updating route-level quantization profile settings (opt-in, feature-flagged).
- Adds server-side compatibility validation and user-facing warning/error mapping.
- Emits structured audit events for enable/disable and profile ref changes.
Summary: Adds the Console backend surface area needed for route-level Quantization Profile Library enablement. Specifically: (1) endpoints to display available profile options for a route/model, (2) a server-side compatibility/guardrail validation path that mirrors policy engine rules (with explicit dry-run support for UI previews), and (3) write endpoints that persist changes via the control plane config service and emit audit records with diffs. Motivation: Console needs a single backend façade that can (a) call into control-plane resolution/validation, (b) map errors into UX-friendly messages, and (c) ensure RBAC + auditable change history. This PR does not change serving defaults; routes remain baseline precision unless explicitly configured. API details: GET /console/v1/routes/{route_id}/quantization-settings -> returns current effective setting (disabled|default|profile_ref), global kill-switch state (read-only), and last-change metadata (actor + timestamp when available). GET /console/v1/routes/{route_id}/quantization-profiles/options?region=&deployment_tier= -> returns list of eligible profiles for the route’s pinned model version, including profile_id, label (stable/experimental), expected savings fields when available, and compatibility status. POST /console/v1/routes/{route_id}/quantization-settings -> accepts quantization_profile_ref (or "default"), enabled boolean, optional region/deployment_tier selectors, and dry_run=true to return validation warnings without persisting. Guardrails/validation: Validation is performed by calling the control plane quantization config service (single request) which evaluates compatibility (model family/variant, GPU SKU class, max context constraints) and returns either OK, OK_WITH_WARNINGS, or INCOMPATIBLE with machine codes; backend maps to UI-safe messages and includes remediation hints (e.g., "select baseline" or "choose a profile compatible with L4 class"). RBAC: Adds permission gate console.routes.write_quantization (requires routes:write + quantization:manage). Read endpoints require routes:read. Audit: Write path emits QUANT_PROFILE_SETTINGS_CHANGED audit events including actor, route_id, old/new setting, and selectors (region/tier). Audit emission is best-effort but failure to write audit fails the request (per security review guidance) to avoid untracked changes. Performance: Options endpoint caches resolved profile option metadata for 30s per (route_id, selectors) to avoid thundering herds on model registry reads during Console refreshes. Tests: Adds unit tests for request validation and error mapping; adds integration tests with mocked control-plane responses (OK / warning / incompatible / kill-switch). Notes: Console UI work in ENG-5818 will consume these endpoints. Related: PR-18445 (control plane CRUD) and PR-18488 (kill-switch propagation).
Ethan Park: Can we guarantee we’re not duplicating policy-engine compatibility logic here? I’d prefer the Console backend call the control-plane validation endpoint and not re-implement SKU/model checks in this repo.
Chloe Martin (author): Yep—no local compatibility rules. The backend calls the control-plane validate/resolve endpoint and only maps machine codes -> UI copy + remediation. Added a test asserting we don’t branch on gpu_sku/model fields beyond pass-through.
Jada Williams: Audit diff needs to include old/new quantization_profile_ref *and* enabled flag. Also please include selectors in the diff (region/deployment tier) since those affect blast radius.
Chloe Martin (author): Updated audit payload to include old/new for enabled + profile_ref + selectors. Also switched to failing the write if audit emission fails to avoid untracked changes (aligned with Naomi’s note below).
Naomi Feldman: RBAC: read endpoints can be routes:read but write must require an explicit quantization permission. We’ve been burned by broad routes:write before.
Chloe Martin (author): Added console.routes.write_quantization gate (routes:write + quantization:manage). Updated error response to return 403 with a stable error_code for the Console UI.
Dylan Brooks: For the options endpoint, we should support dry-run previews the UI can call before the confirmation modal. Does POST dry_run cover this? Also please ensure the response includes warnings in a structured way.
Chloe Martin (author): Yes—POST supports dry_run=true and returns warnings[] + warning_codes[]. Also added GET options to include per-profile compatibility status so the dropdown can gray out incompatible items without an extra call.
Benji Okafor: Please ensure caching doesn’t bypass kill-switch updates. If kill-switch flips, UI should immediately reflect "disabled" and block writes.
Chloe Martin (author): Cache key now includes kill_switch_version from control plane; if it changes, cache is bypassed. Write path always checks kill-switch live and returns 409 error_code=QUANT_PROFILES_GLOBALLY_DISABLED.
CI (openapi-schema-lint): failed on missing response schema for 409; author added schema + examples; re-run passed.
Approvals: Ethan Park approved after validation path confirmed; Naomi Feldman approved after RBAC changes; Jada Williams approved after audit diff update; Dylan Brooks approved.
Feature-flagged behind console.quant_profiles_route_settings (default off). No DB migrations in Console backend. Requires control plane quantization config service endpoints from PR-18445 to be deployed first. Verify in staging: (1) GET settings returns disabled by default, (2) POST dry_run returns warning/incompatible codes, (3) POST write emits audit event and the change is visible in audit log explorer, (4) toggling global kill-switch causes POST to return 409 with QUANT_PROFILES_GLOBALLY_DISABLED and GET settings reflects disabled state.

payload.body:
Motivation: We observed a pattern during regional failovers where a large fraction of short-lived connections rejoined immediately after a brief outage which caused a cascading spike in payloads, rehydration KV loads, and tokenized work that briefly violated per-tenant SLO windows. This PR introduces a connection warmup hedge and a soft-deny window to smooth rejoin traffic and give the serving pool time to restore caches and prefix/KV warm state.

What this changes: Adds a tenant-aware connection warmup state machine that tags reconnections with a low-priority warmup flag for a configurable window (default 8s). During warmup, requests are subject to a soft-deny gate: lightweight requests (probes, health pings) are allowed, but heavy requests that trigger KV-prefetch or large-batch execution are rate-limited and demoted into a background warm queue. We also add an adaptive warmup multiplier that reduces the warm window if the region shows stable health signals.

Design notes: warmup decisions are made at the regional connection proxy and propagated in a short-lived header (x-rw-warmup: {flag, window, priority}). The runtime respects that header when deciding to inline or enqueue. To prevent tenant starvation we cap the per-tenant warm queue to a soft fraction of the node (configurable). Telemetry includes new histograms for warmup-duration, warm-queue-latency, rejoin-spike-rate, and per-tenant warm-drop-rate.

Safety and rollback: Feature is behind a runtime flag and an operator toggle in the Console. Default rollout is off; this PR enables the flag in the staging cluster for soak tests. If we observe higher than expected client errors or SLO regressions we revert by flipping the flag or cherry-picking the revert commit.

Checklist: [x] unit tests for state machine transitions; [x] integration test for soft-deny behavior under simulated rejoin storm; [x] telemetry dashboards and alert queries; [x] Console toggle + docs; [x] migration note for older proxies that ignore the header (they will treat it as no-warmup).

Related: ENG-9876 (regional failover smoothing), SUP-4123 (customer report of cascading rejoin), ENG-9901 (warm cache telemetry).
Diego Morales: Can we make the default warm window shorter for on-prem clusters? Suggest exposing cluster-level default. (addressed)
Priya Desai: The soft-deny path needs explicit test coverage for large-batch payloads; existing test targeted small requests only. (added integration vectors)
Ethan Liu: Watch out for header spoofing from older clients; added validation and ignore-by-default semantics. (implemented)
Aisha Kapoor (author): Replied with details on multiplier heuristics and included a short note on expected telemetry thresholds for rollout.
Introduce tenant-aware connection warmup and soft-deny window to smooth rejoin spikes. Default disabled; operator toggle in Console. Improves stability during regional failovers by reducing abrupt KV-prefetch and heavy work bursts.
payload.title: Connection warmup hedge and soft-deny window to reduce failure cascades

payload.body:
Background: customers integrating via the OpenAI-compatible shim need clearer, machine-readable guidance for retry/backoff and consistent error payloads across both streaming and non-streaming endpoints. Motivation: avoid brittle client heuristics (parsing Retry-After heuristically), reduce duplicated logic in SDKs, and make function/tool-calling failure modes explicit so callers can safely decide whether to retry or surface errors to users. What this PR does: 1) Adds a stable response header X-Redwood-Retry-Hint that encodes a short, opaque backoff hint (RFC-safe token) and an optional suggested backoff in seconds (e.g. "t=10;token=abc123"). 2) Introduces a compact, machine-readable error envelope for OpenAI-compat routes: top-level fields error.code, error.message, error.retryable (boolean), error.hints (array of strings). This is emitted for 4xx/5xx and runtime tool-call failures. 3) Normalizes 429/503 classification: 429 => quota/rate-window, 503 => transient capacity/maintenance; both can include the header but different retryable flags. 4) Adds a streaming preamble event for streamed function/tool-call errors so clients receive a structured terminal frame ("event": "error", payload: error envelope) before the stream closes. 5) Updates SDK compatibility notes and docs with examples and guidance (Python/TS snippets) and a migration guide. Checklist: - [x] RFC implemented (link: https://linear.app/ENG/issue/ENG-1481/retry-hint-header-rfc) - [x] Unit + integration tests for header parsing and error envelope - [x] SDK examples updated - [x] E2E smoke on hosted API - [x] Docs + changelog entry Compatibility notes: header is additive and optional; existing clients will continue to work but can opt in to reading X-Redwood-Retry-Hint and the structured error body. See linked linear tasks for further rollout automation.
Lena Fischer (2024-11-09): Overall looks good. Need to confirm header format won't conflict with proxies. Suggest switching to an ABNF-safe token and adding validation at ingress.
Ethan Chen (2024-11-09): Responded—using token base64url without padding; added validation in handler and unit tests.
Ravi Kumar (2024-11-10): Can you clarify semantics of error.retryable for streamed tool failures? If a function call fails due to user code, should retryable be false?
Ethan Chen (2024-11-10): Answered—function runtime errors (user code) are not retryable; infrastructure timeouts are retryable. Added mapping table in comments and tests.
Asha Romero (2024-11-12): Please add a short note in the console docs about how retry-hint tokens are rotated/invalidated when capacity changes.
Ethan Chen (2024-11-12): Added docs section and metric to track token churn as requested.
Added X-Redwood-Retry-Hint header (opaque token + suggested backoff) and a machine-readable error envelope (error.code, error.message, error.retryable, error.hints). Streaming now emits a terminal structured error frame for tool/function-call failures. This enables SDKs and clients to make deterministic retry decisions.

payload.body:
Motivation: improve end-to-end observability for the API surface (both OpenAI-compatible adapter and native Redwood endpoints) with three concrete goals: 1) ensure request/trace propagation and per-request metadata flows through streaming paths; 2) emit structured JSON logs with stable fields for downstream analysis and SLI calculation (including tool/function-calling events); 3) tag metrics per-route and per-compatibility-path to make latency/cost SLOs actionable. Scope: middleware and adapter layers, logger v2, metric tagging, small streaming protocol additions, tests and docs. Major points: - Request ID and trace propagation: unify headers (X-Request-Id, X-Redwood-Trace, Traceparent) at the edge, persist request_id on streaming sessions, and include request_id/trace_id in all emitted metric labels and structured logs; non-breaking fallback for older clients. - Streaming resilience signals: add periodic keepalive marker events and chunk-level health tags (stream_chunk.seq, stream_chunk.checksum, stream_chunk.type) so consumers and observability can detect mid-stream truncation and replays. - Structured logging: introduce json logger with stable schema: timestamp, level, request_id, trace_id, route, model, user_id (if available), op (e.g., inference.start, inference.chunk, tool.invoke), tool_invocation_id, duration_ms, token_count, error_code. Tool/function calling: emit explicit tool.invoke/return events with tool-specific metadata and route labels. - Per-route metric tagging: middleware adds route and compatibility labels (openai_compat=true/false; adapter_variant=classic/v2) to histogram and counter buckets so dashboards can split traffic easily. - OpenAI compatibility adapter changes: map openai's x-request-id and openai-client-metadata into Redwood trace fields, preserve streaming chunk framing but add minimal compat-preserving markers for observability; maintain same response framing for existing clients. - Rollout and feature flagging: feature-flagged via ff_obs_streaming; rollout ramp 10/30/60/100 over 48h with a kill-switch. Tests: unit + integration streaming tests added; added synthetic workload for streaming truncation detection. Backwards compatibility: header mapping is additive; clients that don't send trace headers work as before. Migration: analytics teams should pivot dashboards to use route and adapter tags. Related: ENG-9143 (per-route SLOs), ENG-9210 (streaming resiliency). Checklist: - [x] middleware to attach request/trace IDs - [x] json logger implementation - [x] per-route metric tags - [x] streaming chunk metadata and keepalive events - [x] openai adapter header mapping - [x] integration tests and docs - [x] feature flag and rollout plan
Priya: Overall looks good. Please add a short note on cardinality limits for route tags and ensure we aren't exploding metric label cardinality. Ava: Added a tag whitelist with rate-limited fallback and documented it in pkg/metrics/README.
Diego: Can we avoid changes in client-visible framing? The keepalive markers need to be no-op for existing parsers. Ava: keepalive is sent as a zero-length metadata frame with type=keepalive; adapter strips it for legacy frames. Added explicit tests.
Jordan: integration flakiness on Windows CI; suggest increasing the socket timeout in test harness. Ava: bumped timeout and added retry - tests stable now.
Priya: approve after addressing metric cardinality note. Diego: approved. Jordan: approved. Merge comment: squashed and merged by Ava after passing CI.
Add request/trace propagation across streaming sessions; request_id and trace_id included in structured logs and metrics
Emit streaming keepalive markers and chunk metadata for stream health monitoring
Introduce structured JSON logs with stable schema for API handlers and tool invocation events
Attach per-route and adapter tags to metrics for easier SLO dashboarding
OpenAI adapter maps OpenAI headers into Redwood tracing fields; backward compatible
Feature-flagged rollout (ff_obs_streaming). Start 10% traffic for first 6h, 30% next 12h, 60% next 24h, full rollout after 48h if no regressions. Watch per-route latency histograms, streaming error-rate, and token throughput. Immediate rollback by disabling ff_obs_streaming.
Dashboard owners: replace raw /api/* histograms with route-tagged histograms
Client teams: no action required unless you rely on raw log text; JSON logger fields are additive
Observe the new streaming metric stream_chunk.truncation_count and alert if >0.1% for 1h

payload.body:
Problem:
Clients observed occasionally truncated/unterminated JSON blobs when SSE events were split across network frames and the reassembly heuristics emitted duplicate delimiters or dropped the trailing token. This caused structured output parsing (tool/function call handoff) to fail intermittently in high-latency paths and during churned streaming (keep-alive heartbeats interleaving).

Root causes identified:
- The streamer emitted event delimiters aggressively which could produce duplicate trailing delimiters when a fragment replay occurred; duplicate delimiters confuse downstream JSON assemblers and some OpenAI-compat clients.
- Reassembly preferred the first-arrived fragment instead of a later, more-complete fragment when seq windowing jitter occurred. That led to truncated JSON being forwarded instead of waiting a short, configurable grace window.
- There was no lightweight in-stream marker that operators or the client SDK could use to checkpoint a safely-closed JSON scope when the model emits structured output (objects/arrays) across frames.

What this PR does (high level):
1) Introduces a flushable-checkpoint marker emitted by the producer when it detects a closed JSON value boundary (internal heuristic documented in code). This marker is an opaque SSE event ("x-rw-checkpoint") that does not change user-facing payloads but allows reassembly to commit a fragment as "complete" before advertising to higher layers.
2) Adds sentinel debouncing: the SSE emitter now suppresses emitting duplicate trailing newline/delimiter events for the same logical token when a replay or retransmit is detected within a small time window. The debounce is conservative and configurable via STREAM_SSE_DEBOUNCE_MS.
3) Updates the reassembly logic to prefer a later fragment if a seq-id mismatch occurs within a small lookahead window (150ms by default). This reduces stale-first selection in jittery networks. There is also an explicit max-hold budget so we never stall beyond the configured latency SLO.
4) Adds integration tests that simulate interleaved heartbeats, delayed fragments, and replayed frames from a TCP simulator to ensure structured output (tool calls) are always either delivered complete or clearly marked as incomplete to the consumer.
5) Adds an adapter fallback in openai_compat that recognizes the new checkpoint event and uses it to validate structured outputs before invoking toolcall logic. If a checkpoint is missing but the fragment is older than max-hold, the adapter will perform a conservative retry path rather than invoking incomplete tool calls.

Files changed (summary):
- sse/emitter.py: add checkpoint emission and debounce timer, config knobs for debounce/ms.
- sse/reassembler.rs: rework seq-window selection, add max_hold budget, expose checkpoint recognition.
- openai_compat/adapter.go: understand x-rw-checkpoint and conservative fallback.
- integration_tests/sse_fragmenting_test.py: new deterministic test harness for replay/heartbeat scenarios.
- docs/sse-checkpoints.md: design note and opt-in configuration.
- api/compat/CHANGELOG.md: entry.
- pkg/metrics/streaming_metrics.go: add checkpoint and debounce counters for observability.

Why this is safe:
- The checkpoint event is an internal marker and is ignored by existing clients (SSE consumers that only parse data events). It is not surfaced as part of the generated model text.
- Debounce defaults are conservative (30ms) and guarded by feature-flagging; behavior can be toggled via env vars for canary rollout.
- Reassembly changes fall back to previous behavior if the lookahead window is zero; the max-hold budget prevents pathological head-of-line blocking.

Testing performed:
- Unit tests for emitter debounce logic and checkpoint insertion heuristics.
- Rust-level unit tests for reassembler selection with simulated seq jitter and partial frames.
- End-to-end integration test using the fragmenting_test harness that reproduces the customer-reported failure mode; validated both with and without the openai_compat adapter.
- Benchmark smoke to ensure no measurable increase in median latency (95th percentile unchanged within noise).

Release notes: "Fix intermittent malformed/partial JSON emission in SSE streams by introducing flushable checkpoints, sentinel debounce, and jitter-aware reassembly. Improves stability of structured output and tool/function calling under network jitter."

Risks and followups:
- Some third-party clients that introspect SSE event names might observe the new x-rw-checkpoint event; we documented it as internal and will monitor telemetry for adoption or unexpected behavior.
- Follow-up work: expose a per-route opt-out for checkpoints for extreme ultra-low-latency customers and add an observability dashboard for checkpoint hit/miss rates (ENG-1473).

Checklist included in description (single string):
- [x] Add emitter checkpoint and debounce
- [x] Update reassembler to use lookahead preference
- [x] Add integration tests for replay/heartbeat scenarios
- [x] Update openai_compat adapter to read checkpoint marker
- [x] Add docs and changelog entry
- [x] Feature-flag + env config for rollout

Asha Patel (reviewer): Can you explain how the checkpoint heuristic decides a JSON value is closed? We should avoid false positives with multi-step toolcall payloads.
Jonas Meyer (author): The heuristic looks for balancing of object/array braces at the event boundary and a short lookahead to ensure no immediate continuation token follows. It's conservative and only emits a checkpoint when braces balance and the next token is not a continuation indicator. I'll add comments and a unit test to show behavior on nested structured outputs.
Marcelo Ruiz (reviewer): The new lookahead preference is reasonable but we need an integration test that simulates the exact jitter pattern reported by SRE (retransmit on second fragment). Please add test and telemetry counters.
Jonas Meyer (author): Added deterministic jitter scenario in integration_tests and exported debounce/checkpoint counters to streaming_metrics. Also added a feature-flag env var STREAM_SSE_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED.
Evelyn Cho (reviewer): Small nit: expose the debounce ms via config rather than hard-coding. Also please add a changelog entry and short docs for operators.
Jonas Meyer (author): Switched to env config STREAM_SSE_DEBOUNCE_MS and added docs/changelog per request.
Asha Patel (approver): Verified integration test reproduces the failure pre-change and is fixed post-change. Approving for squash-merge.
Marcelo Ruiz (approver): Ran canary in staging with feature-flag and saw checkpoint hit-rate ~98% for the reproducer without latency regression. Approving.
Merge bot: CI passed on re-run and changelog entry lint OK. Merging via squash.
Fix intermittent partial/unterminated JSON in SSE streams by adding internal flushable checkpoints, debouncing duplicate delimiters, and making reassembly jitter-aware. Improves reliability of structured output and toolcall handoffs under network churn.
