payload.body:
Motivation: during cross-region surge events we observe rapid fan-in of connections causing transient KV cache pressure and SLO breaches. This PR adds an adaptive connection pacing layer in the serving runtime plus a regional holdoff coordinator in the control plane to smooth open connection ramps and provide a graceful short-term holdoff when regional ingress spikes are detected. Key goals: avoid wholesale circuit trips, maintain tenant fairness, and keep latency SLOs for high-priority routes. Changes include: pacing algorithm (EWMA-based rate limiter with per-tenant weights), a leaky-window admission smoother for inflight requests, a regional holdoff lease with softbackoff and telemetry-anchored decay, an operator-configurable safety toggle for immediate disable, end-to-end unit+integration tests, and docs for operators. Rollout plan: enabled behind feature flag, gradual canary to 10% of traffic then 50%; metric thresholds documented. Rollback plan: feature flag off or revert the holdoff coordinator; and a targeted emergency circuit unstick script included. Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration scenario harness, [x] telemetry dashboards and alerting playbook, [x] k8s helm values, [x] operator docs. Related: ENG-2841 (holdoff design), ENG-2990 (pacing spec).
7 commits: initial pacing core and interfaces; add telemetry counters and histograms; implement regional holdoff coordinator and lease logic; add e2e harness and stress tests; helm and values for rollout; operator docs and runbook; fix CI flake in pacing_test by reducing timing dependence.
Marco Rivera: I like the EWMA approach. Two asks: (1) can we expose a per-tenant max window to avoid cold-start starvation? (2) add a safety clamp when kv-pressure > threshold so we don't amplify congestion.
Aisha Patel: Answered: added tenant_max_window config and a kv_pressure clamp that forces immediate softbackoff. See region_holdoff.go lines 82-110 and new helm value pacing.tenantMaxWindow.
Elena Kim: CI flaked on pacer_test when run under race detector; add a small jitter in test to avoid deterministic timing. Also request a metrics tag for route priority.
Aisha Patel: Addressed: introduced test jitter and added metrics label route_priority to histograms. CI now green.
Trevor Huang: Are we confident this won't create additional request reordering during hedged-retries? Can we opt-out hedging for paced routes?
Aisha Patel: Added opt-out flag hedging.enabledPerRoute=false for paced routes and added a short note in docs explaining tradeoffs.
CI run: build passed, unit tests passed, integration stress scenario passed after fix; one transient lint failure on first run which was fixed in commit 4.
Added adaptive connection pacing and a regional holdoff coordinator to mitigate transient inbound surge fan-in. Feature is behind a feature flag and off by default. Operators can enable gradual rollout via helm values. New telemetry: pacing.request_rate, pacing.window_size, holdoff.leases_active. See docs/operational/regional-holdoff.md for runbook.
Low-medium: runtime changes are guarded by feature flag and per-tenant clamps. Integration stress tests in CI replicate fan-in scenarios. Emergency toggle and rollback documented. Observability added to detect regressions quickly.
During initial CI runs a timing-sensitive test caused a transient failure under race detector; fixed by adding controlled jitter and a tighter condition in pacer_test. No customer-facing rollback required during merge window.
payload.title: Adaptive connection pacing and graceful regional holdoff for surge fan-in

payload.body:
Motivation: Our CI has been spending increasing time on full dependency audits and heavy integration test runs for every dependency bump and small tooling change. This PR introduces a new lightweight 'quick-verify' mode for the dependency validator and a minimal CI test stub runner that gives fast feedback for infra/CI-only changes. The goals are: reduce turnaround for repo hygiene PRs, lower CI compute cost for dependency churn, and provide a safer incremental path for rolling out stricter dependency gates.

Implementation: 1) dep-validate: add a --quick-verify flag which performs checksum/manifest checks and a targeted transitive-safety probe instead of the full graph resolution. This is implemented in scripts/dep-validate with feature-flag gating (ENV: DEP_VALIDATE_QUICK=true) and returns structured exit codes documented in docs/ci/dependency-validation.md. 2) ci-stubber: add a new job template .github/workflows/ci-stub.yml and a small Go binary tools/ci-stubber that runs a configurable subset of smoke checks (lint-shard header, small unit test subset, and install/build dry-run) in memory without launching containers. The stub runner is intentionally conservative: it cannot replace full integration tests but detects common infra regressions early. 3) CI orchestration: add a conditional premerge lane that picks the stub runner for PRs touching only non-runtime paths (scripts/, .github/, build/) using a path-aware matcher. 4) Telemetry and rollback: emit metrics to observability when quick-verify is used and add a transparent opt-out via PR label 'ci:full' that forces the full CI path.

Files changed: workflow templates, a ~700 line script refactor for dep validator with unit tests, the small Go stub binary (approx 150 LOC), and docs updates describing usage and failure modes.

Testing: Local unit tests for dep-validate quick mode and e2e smoke in a constrained ephemeral runner were added. CI matrix includes the new ci-stub job and a staged rollout where the quick-verify job runs alongside full CI for the first 48 hours for telemetry validation. Manual canary on the redwood repo integration team was performed.

Rollout and risks: Quick-verify is opt-in via env and annotated in PR checks. Risk: false negatives where quick-verify misses a deep transitive issue. Mitigation: keep quick-verify as a fast pre-merge gate only; full CI remains the final blocker. Observability alerts added to detect divergence between quick-verify and full CI.

Related work: builds on design notes from ENG-1409 and complements the staged CI lanes introduced in ENG-2871. Linear: ENG-5212.

Checklist: - [x] Add --quick-verify implementation and docs. - [x] Add ci-stub job + binary. - [x] Add path matcher rules. - [x] Add telemetry hooks and opt-out label. - [x] Unit and smoke tests + staged rollout plan.
Arjun: Please add explicit fallback behavior when DEP_VALIDATE_QUICK is unset. Response: implemented default to full validation unless env is set to true.
Sofia: Could quick-verify produce a false sense of safety? Suggest telemetry. Response: added metric emission and 48h dual-run rollout plan.
Liam: Can the stub runner accidentally mask container-level failures? Response: documented limitations in docs/ci/ci-stub-runner.md and added opt-out label 'ci:full'.
Introduce a lightweight dependency quick-verify mode and a CI stub runner to speed feedback for infra changes. This is opt-in and intended as a pre-merge gate; full CI remains required. See docs/ci/* for usage.
payload.title: Introduce dependency-validate quick-verify mode and lightweight CI test stub runner

payload.body:
Introduce a lightweight load sentinel that detects short-lived KV pressure spikes and routes affected requests to a transparent readonly fallback to preserve SLOs and reduce error amplification. Backwards compatible config flags and a conservative default ensure safe rollout.
Context: We observed a pattern of transient KV backpressure spikes causing cascading retries and SLO violations during short regional pressure events. This change introduces a surgical load sentinel that detects short-lived KV pressure and routes affected requests to a transparent readonly fallback when safe. Motivation: Preserve tail latency and reduce amplified error/latency cascades without wholesale throttling of tenants. Keep changes conservative to avoid behavioral surprises. Design summary: 1) Load sentinel in controlplane monitors kvPressure, inflightPerTenant and recent error-rate histograms and computes a lightweight score. 2) When score exceeds a configured short window threshold the sentinel marks traffic for an incremental readonly fallback using a routing hint. 3) The readonly fallback path in route-mux preserves identity headers and KV snapshot tokens and returns best-effort read-only responses; write requests receive a soft-deny with clear error code to clients. 4) Circuit cooldown and penalty decay prevent flapping. 5) Feature gated and rollouts via sentinel-config with conservative defaults. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for sentinel heuristics and cooldown - [x] Integration tests for fallback routing and trace propagation - [x] Metrics and alerting for sentinel trips - [x] Runbook drafted and linked - [x] Staged rollout config included Commits summary: a1f4b8c initial sentinel prototype and tests; b2d9e3f integrate readonly fallback path into route-mux and preserve trace headers; c3f7a11 add metrics, alerts and runbook entries; d4e2b20 CI checks and threshold tweaks. Files changed (high level): services/controlplane/src/sentinel/load_sentinel.rs added core detection logic, comments, and Prometheus hooks; route-mux fallback path updates add readonly routing and header passthrough; runbook and staging k8s overlay for gated rollout; CI and console flag. Small snippet: `if kv_pressure.window(3s) > threshold && inflight_per_tenant > tenant_cap {mark_readonly_hint(tx)}` Review thread: Ethan Park: "Nice focused approach. Two asks: expose the cooldown as a config and add an e2e that simulates KV spike to assert no double-counting across tenants." Sonia Patel (author): "Added cooldown config and unit tests that exercise decay; e2e simulated in staging overlay, see staging config. Addressed double-counting by scoping metrics to tenant-id." Maya Singh: "We should be explicit about error codes for writes when in readonly fallback; will this surface to SDKs?" Sonia Patel: "Writes return a 409 with `x-redwood-fallback=readonly`; SDKs will map to a Retryable=false error; console flag documents UX." Julien Moreau: "Metrics look good, consider a low-cardinality 'sentinel_reason' tag for easier rollups." Sonia Patel: "Added sentinel_reason tag with values 'kv_pressure'|'inflight'|'err_rate' and tests updated." CI notes: All pipeline stages passed after second run. Unit tests 142/142, integration smoke passed, lint warnings fixed in second commit. Performance bench: synthetic kv spike test in benchmark-lab shows 28% reduction in 99p tail latency for impacted tenants with <3% cost overhead. Merge notes: Squash-merged into main after approvals from Ethan and Maya. Deployed to staging with feature-flag off for production; gradual rollout plan in runbook. Post-merge actions: monitor sentinel.trip_rate, sentinel.duration_p95, and readonly-fallback.rate for 48h; be ready to revert via feature flag.
payload.title: surgical-load-sentinel-and-transparent-readonly-fallback

payload.body:
Context: We’re rolling out the new onboarding / “first production launch” checklist in Console behind a feature flag, with progressive exposure by cohort. This PR introduces the first-cut flag definition, deterministic cohort assignment, and an emergency kill-switch path that Support/SRE can use if we see regressions during dogfood or cohort rollout. Summary of changes: (1) Adds flag definition `console.onboarding_checklist` with structured config: `enabled`, `mode`, `allowlist_tenants`, `denylist_tenants`, `rollout_percentage`, `cohort_seed`, and `kill_switch` (server-side hard disable). (2) Implements deterministic cohort assignment using stable hashing on `tenant_id` + `cohort_seed` to avoid cohort “flapping” between requests and across regions. (3) Adds a small policy layer to compute exposure in the control plane so Console can request “shouldShowChecklist” with a single API call (rather than duplicating logic client-side). (4) Adds operational guardrails: kill-switch can be toggled via config service and also via `ONBOARDING_CHECKLIST_KILL_SWITCH=1` env var override for emergency response. (5) Adds telemetry events for exposure decisions (aggregated, low-cardinality) to support rollout monitoring: `onboarding_checklist.exposure_evaluated` with fields `{tenant_id_hash, decision, reason, rollout_percentage, mode}`. (Tenant ID is hashed server-side; no org name/email/etc.) Rollout modes: `off` (default), `dogfood` (employee + internal tenants only), `cohort` (percentage-based), `allowlist` (explicit tenants only). Precedence (highest to lowest): kill_switch -> denylist -> allowlist -> mode/percentage. Notes / non-goals: This PR does not include checklist UI (ENG-5814) or progress tracking service changes (ENG-5813). It only provides a consistent mechanism for exposure + safe rollback. Related: PM-768 (Rollout plan and feature flag strategy). Testing: Added unit tests for cohort determinism, precedence ordering, and env-var kill switch. Added integration test to validate consistent exposure decision across regions when config is replicated. Follow-ups: (a) Hook Console UI gating to the new `GET /console/feature-flags` endpoint (tracked in ENG-5814). (b) Add an admin “force enable for tenant” override path for Support (separate PR / ENG-5852).
control-plane: add onboarding checklist feature flag definition + schema validation
control-plane: implement deterministic cohorting (stable hash) + precedence rules
console-api: expose /console/feature-flags endpoint for checklist gating
telemetry: emit exposure_evaluated metric with low-cardinality reason codes
tests: add cohort determinism + env kill switch coverage
Dylan Brooks: Can we avoid any client-side cohort math? We’ve had issues where Console and backend diverge and customers see inconsistent UI states across refreshes.
Ethan Park (author): Yep — cohorting is 100% server-side in control plane. Console will call `GET /console/feature-flags` and receive `onboarding_checklist: {enabled: true/false, reason}`. I added reason codes so we can debug “why” without exposing tenant identifiers.
Logan Wright: Telemetry event includes `tenant_id_hash` — can we confirm hashing is stable per tenant but not reversible, and that we’re not emitting raw tenant IDs anywhere?
Ethan Park (author): Good call. Updated to use the existing `hashTenantIdForAnalytics()` helper (salted, non-reversible). Also added a test that fails if raw tenant_id is present in payload serialization.
Aisha Bello: For kill switch, I’d like a path that works even if config propagation is lagging. Env var override is good, but is it wired in all regions and in the right process?
Ethan Park (author): Wired into the control-plane evaluator (the source of truth for the Console endpoint). If we need to hard-disable regionally, we can toggle via deploy-time env var immediately; config kill switch remains the normal path.
Ben Carter: Rollout percentage — are we guaranteed determinism when `rollout_percentage` changes? We should avoid the same tenant bouncing in/out within a day.
Ethan Park (author): Determinism is stable for a given percentage and seed. When percentage increases, only additional tenants get enabled (monotonic). When percentage decreases, some tenants will lose exposure. That’s expected but we should avoid toggling percentages frequently; I added this as a note to the runbook.
Chloe Martin: Precedence looks right. Minor nit: can we rename `mode=dogfood` to make it explicit it’s internal-only? Might be confusing later.
Ethan Park (author): Renamed display string in docs/runbook to “internal_dogfood” but kept wire value as `dogfood` for now to avoid churn across services. Happy to change wire value in a follow-up if we want stricter naming before GA.
Internal: Introduced server-side feature flag and cohorting rules for Console onboarding checklist rollout, including emergency kill switch support.
payload.title: Add feature flag + cohorting rules for Console onboarding checklist (with kill switch)

Context: customers operating in regulated jurisdictions asked for stronger operator-level accountability and a way to prove which operator actions triggered KMS usage without leaking sensitive key material. This change introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) credential watermarking for operator-issued API tokens (non-secret stamp embedded in token metadata and audit-trace), 2) a per-operator KMS governor that enforces soft quotas and emits KMS usage provenance headers for downstream audit, and 3) a consolidated residency audit pipeline that stitches RBAC v2 decisions, KMS provenance, and region pin metadata into a single exportable audit artifact. Motivation: improves non-repudiation, makes post-incident forensic queries simpler, and helps meet regulatory audit requests without adding operator-visible latency. Changes: - credential watermarking: new token issuance flow adds a deterministic watermark id (HMAC over operator id + issuance ts, keyed with deployment-local secret) stored as token metadata and emitted as x-operator-watermark in internal audit messages only. Token payloads are unchanged for customers; watermark is only present in internal audit and ephemeral logs. - per-operator KMS governor: lightweight middleware in pkg/kms/governor that tracks per-operator KMS call rates (local cache + distributed counters fallback) and enforces configurable soft thresholds; when thresholds hit, metrics and audit events are emitted and optional throttling can be enabled per-tenant. - residency audit consolidation: new audit exporter (cmd/audit-exporter/residency-consolidator) that consumes rbac-decision-stream, kms-provenance stream, and region-assertion events and writes canonical residency-audit objects for compliance ingestion. Migration/compatibility: new features are opt-in via config flags (feature.credential_watermark, feature.kms_governor, audit.residency_consolidation). Default off for existing clusters. Security considerations: watermark key is stored in KMS-wrapped secret and rotated monthly; watermark values are one-way HMACs to prevent reverse engineering of operator ids. Audit artifacts are TTL'd and can be configured to redact sensitive fields before export. Tests & rollout: unit + e2e tests added; staged rollout plan uses a shadow-mode where the governor only observes for two weeks before optional enforcement. Linear tasks: ENG-1298 broken into incremental work items for rollout. Checklist: - [x] design review (SEC-442) - [x] unit tests - [x] e2e shadow-mode test - [x] integration with audit exporter - [x] docs and runbook updates - [x] staged rollout notes (canary then global)
Daniel Ortiz: Nice direction. Request: make watermark HMAC key KMS-wrapped; don't rely on plaintext config in-cluster. Also can we ensure the watermark is not returned to customer-facing logs?
Maya Chen (author): Agree, switched to KMS-wrapped key and added a code path that strips watermark headers before any response written to public logs. Added unit test verifying header redaction.
Priya Nair: KMS governor looks good. Two requests: 1) add metrics histogram for time-to-enforce and 2) document the failure modes when counter store is unavailable.
Maya Chen: Added prometheus histogram and fallback doc section; governor runs in observe-only mode when counter store is degraded by default.
Greg Shah: Audit consolidator needs stable canonical schema. Please add schema versioning and a migration path.
Maya Chen: Added schema.v field and versioned exporter config; wrote migration helper to synthesize v1 artifacts from older audit fragments.
Initial implementation of watermark generator and token metadata plumbing
Add KMS governor middleware and per-operator counter store with Redis fallback
Implement residency-audit consolidator and streaming ingest adapters
Add unit tests, e2e shadow-mode harness, and docs/runbook updates
Address reviewer feedback: make watermark HMAC key KMS-wrapped and add redaction hooks
Add opt-in credential watermarking for operator tokens, a per-operator KMS governor (observe then enforce), and a residency audit consolidator. Opt-in via feature flags; see docs/security/credential-watermarking.md and docs/runbooks/kms-governor-canary.md for rollout guidance.
payload.title: Introduce credential watermarking, per-operator KMS governor, and consolidated residency audit

payload.body:
Context: We continue to see oscillation when regional SLOs are under transient pressure: the in-memory circuit breaker opens, traffic is shed, the region drains, the breaker quickly closes on restart and traffic surges back leading to another open event. This PR introduces two coordinated changes: 1) a localized SLO hysteresis controller that computes a slow-decaying penalty and staged thresholds for load-shedding decisions (tiered degrade fast-path); 2) persistence of circuit state to the cluster KV (etcd) so breaker open/half-open state survives controller restarts and node failovers. Motivation: reduce oscillation, avoid repeated cold-open/down cycles during transient spikes, and improve graceful degradation while keeping outages predictable. What this changes: - runtime/degrader: adds HysteresisController that applies per-region SLO windowing, a tiered threshold that ramps degrade severity slowly, and a TTL-based decay of penalty scores. - runtime/circuit: moves primary circuit state to a small persisted store backed by etcd with a local in-memory cache and write-through; state includes open/half-open/last-opened-at/penalty-score. - routing/policy: updates fast-path routing so requests consult the persisted circuit state first and fall back to local heuristics if the KV is temporarily unavailable. - observability: new metrics (region_hysteresis_penalty, circuit_persistent_write_latency, circuit_state_transitions) and dashboards added. - tests: unit tests for hysteresis math and integration test that simulates coordinator restart while circuit is open. Rollout plan: - feature-flagged (runtime.flag.enable_persistent_circuit + runtime.flag.enable_hysteresis) - Canary rollout to two non-critical regions for 48hrs with synthetic SLO load (see runbook snippets) - If anomalies in client latency or error-rate (>5% increase sustained over 15min), rollback flags via ops console. Backwards compatibility: if etcd persistence is unavailable, the code gracefully degrades to purely-local breakers with additional telemetry and a warn log. See compatibility section in the body below. Testing: unit/integration tests were added, and a small perf microbenchmark shows <1ms median added p95 of 2.5ms for circuit path when persistence enabled. Related: addresses oscillation investigated in ENG-4521 and is preparatory work for ENG-4700 (regional prefetch scheduling). Linear: ENG-4521. Checklist:
- [x] Hysteresis controller implementation
- [x] Persistent circuit state + write-through cache
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Feature flags and environment gating
- [x] Observability and dashboard PR linked
- [x] Runbook / rollback notes included

Compatibility notes: Persistence uses the existing cluster KV abstraction (etcd cluster used by control-plane). On older private deployments that do not expose the control-plane KV, persistence is disabled automatically and the runtime emits a metric circuit_persistence_disabled=true. Fallthroughs are audited in logs and surfaced in the console. Performance note: the write path is write-through but batched small writes (coalesced every 50ms) to keep tail latency low. Security: persisted state contains no customer data; state schema is limited to enums, timestamps, and small numeric penalty values.

Merge rationale: reduces incident blast radius from rapid open/close cycles and makes graceful degradation behavior auditable across restarts.

Maya Chen: Reply: yes, implemented coalescing and jitter to avoid thundering writes; wrote small microbenchmark demonstrating tail impact under synthetic load.
Sofia Martinez: Please make sure the feature flag default is off for older private installs. Also request a short note in the upgrade guide for on-prem customers.
Maya Chen: Reply: added upgrade note and a runtime detection path that emits circuit_persistence_disabled=true when KV not available.
Lars Becker: Approve with comments: small nits on logging and a suggestion to increase integration test time window to capture TTL decay. I left one small comment inline about a nil check in manager.go which I handled in follow-up commit.

Motivation: customers frequently need safe, automatic defaults for batching/prefill (prefix caching), and quantization profiles that respect a per-customer cost SLO. Manual tuning is time-consuming and error-prone, leading to regressions or overconservative defaults. This change introduces the 'econ-autocalibrator' subsystem: a simulation-backed suggestion engine that synthesizes safe batching/prefill/quant profiles given a workload fingerprint and a target unit-econ constraint. Key goals: 1) provide immediate out-of-the-box defaults that reduce token cost without violating latency SLOs; 2) offer a canary-safe rollout path (suggestions applied as config overlays with shadow simulation); 3) integrate telemetry and conservative safety checks to avoid regressions in quality or tail latency. The description below covers components, testing, rollout plan, and known limitations. Components: - service/econ-autocalibrator: main Go service implementing workload fingerprint ingestion, simulation runner (cost+latency model), and suggestion scoring with safety heuristics (max tail-latency multiplier, quality regression budget). - cli/bin/econctl: lightweight CLI to generate suggestions from local traces or stored workloads (used by SEs and SREs). - runtime integration: a new SuggestionConfig type, plus an adapter in the routing layer to apply suggested overrides as staged config (shadow, canary, apply). - default profiles: curated prefill/batch/quant presets generated by the simulator and validated against common benchmarks. - telemetry: metrics for suggestion accept rate, simulated vs. actual delta, suggestion age, and safety violations. Checklist (all items in this single paragraph per repo conventions): - [x] design doc: ENG-4187 linked - [x] unit tests for scoring and safety heuristics - [x] end-to-end integration test in perf-canary harness - [x] docs: console and CLI usage - [x] migration: SuggestionConfig is additive and defaults to no-op - [x] observability: add tracing spans and metrics - [x] canary rollout plan documented. Limitations and future work: current simulator uses a conservative latency model; quantization acceptance checks are heuristic and will be replaced by a lightweight regression eval in a follow-up; policy zoning for tenant-level hard caps needs product alignment. Usage notes: operators can run econctl against traces or request suggestions via the Console UI (new 'Econ suggestions' card). Suggestions are returned with a confidence score and a recommended rollout policy (shadow -> canary -> apply).

Maya Chen (author): I split the proto into a non-breaking additive change in commit 2 (api.proto) and adapter handles unknown fields. Updated description to call out additive migration.
Lena García: Safety heuristics look reasonable; add a unit test that covers the multiplier edge-case (high variance workloads).

Motivation: In long-running nodes we observed slow memory growth and suboptimal eviction choices caused by fragmentation and size-skewed items. This PR implements a fragmentation-aware reclamation strategy plus a prioritized spill policy to reduce tail latency when the KV cache needs to free pages. Summary of changes: 1) Add a lightweight arena fragmentation estimator that tracks free-run histograms per arena and exposes a fragmentation_score metric used by the reclaim path. 2) Implement a cooperative defragmenter that runs in small time-sliced windows on an IO-worker thread to coalesce free extents without blocking allocation hot paths. 3) Replace the single FIFO spill queue with a priority spill queue that orders candidates by a combined LRU-weight and size_score so that small high-hit items are preferred to remain in-memory while large cold objects are spilled first. 4) Introduce reclaim hints to the kernel selection logic so allocations for short-lived KV entries favor compact arenas, reducing cross-arena fragmentation. 5) Add telemetry: fragmentation_score, spill_priority_distribution, defrag_duration_buckets, and eviction_jank_rate. Backwards compatibility: on-by-default behind feature-flag "kv_frag_reclaim_v2"; existing customers continue on current algorithm until opt-in. Checklist: - [x] Fragmentation estimator + metrics - [x] Cooperative defragmenter with bounded CPU budget - [x] Priority spill queue and policy - [x] Integration with kernel allocation hints - [x] Unit tests for allocator heuristics and spill ordering - [x] End-to-end perf canary run and dashboard entries How to validate: 1) Run bench/kv-reclaim with long-lived mixed-size workload (scripts/bench/kv_reclaim.sh) and observe reduced memory high-water and lower eviction_jank_rate. 2) Use perf-canary preset "kv-frag" to validate latency p95/p99 under steady-state traffic. Related: builds on ideas from ENG-1742 (arena compaction) and addresses incidents SUP-2145 (out-of-memory due to fragmentation).
Ethan Zhang: I like the histogram approach; please add an upper bound on estimator memory and avoid per-allocation atomics.
Priya Menon (author): switched estimator to per-thread scratch + periodic aggregation to reduce atomic pressure (see allocator.cc).
Lena Kovacs: can defrag windows trigger GC-like pauses on low-powered instances? Add a knob to reduce budget.
Priya Menon: added feature flag and per-node budget percentage (default 0.5%) with integration test in perf-canary.
Marcus Hale: CI flaky on macOS build target; reran and logs look clean. Approved pending addressing allocator_test timeout.
Priya Menon: increased test timeout and optimized test setup to use in-memory backing store; all tests passing locally.

Summary: This PR adds end-to-end integration tests for the Dedicated staged rollouts path using a simulated Dedicated pool + fake telemetry backend. The goal is to validate that control-plane state transitions, routing partition selection, stage-tagged telemetry, gate evaluation semantics, and rollback behavior work together (and stay working as we iterate). Context: We’ve had early beta regressions where canary partitions effectively reduced capacity and triggered 429s (SUP-28522) and where gate evidence panels were empty due to telemetry tag mismatch (SUP-28605). These tests are intended to catch those classes of failures before changes land in main. What’s included: (1) Happy path rollout: create DedicatedPoolRolloutPlan -> start running -> promote through stages -> complete, with assertions on audit events and deterministic stage selection. (2) Gate failure scenario: simulate elevated 5xx + p99 latency in stage=canary and confirm policy engine returns FAIL, control plane auto-aborts (when configured), traffic split reverts to baseline, and rollout is marked aborted with correct audit trail. (3) Missing/stale metrics behavior: simulate telemetry lag and validate gate evaluation returns UNKNOWN (and is treated as fail-closed) unless an admin override is used (override actions are validated in separate unit coverage, but this suite asserts the end-to-end behavior that promotion is blocked). (4) Capacity starvation / 429 regression test: simulate small pool partitions + queue depth increase; assert routing selects baseline partition for overflow when stage partition is saturated (protects against the early beta failure mode). (5) Idempotency + concurrency: repeated promote/abort requests with the same idempotency key do not advance state twice; conflicting promotes are rejected via optimistic concurrency. (6) Rollback validation for streaming: test uses a simulated streaming request pinned to the selected partition at request start; on abort/rollback we do NOT migrate in-flight streams, but we do ensure new requests route to baseline immediately after the rollback commits. Test harness notes: These tests run in CI using the existing integration runner with a simulated Dedicated pool scheduler and in-memory telemetry backend. Gate evaluation is exercised through the policy engine path (not mocked) but telemetry queries are backed by the fake backend with deterministic timestamps to avoid flakiness. To keep runtime reasonable, we use short windows (e.g., 30s) and force sufficient sample counts. Gate thresholds in tests are intentionally low/explicit to avoid coupling to prod defaults. Files/areas changed (high level): - test/integration/dedicated_rollouts/*: new staged rollout integration suite and fixtures - test/integration/helpers/sim_dedicated_pool*: simulated pool + partitioning model (replica-based) - test/integration/helpers/fake_telemetry_backend*: deterministic metrics store + query helpers - control_plane/test_support/audit_capture*: capture + assert audit events emitted during integration runs - routing/test_support/partition_assertions*: assertions for stage partition selection and fallback behavior - ci/integration-test-manifest.yml: registers new suite, marks as required for rollouts label Notes on determinism and flake control: The suite runs with seeded randomness (SEED env) and uses monotonic time under the test clock. We also added a guard that fails the test if any telemetry series uses unbounded label sets (protects cardinality regressions). Checklist: - [x] Covers create -> promote -> complete - [x] Covers gate fail -> abort -> rollback - [x] Covers missing metrics behavior (fail-closed) - [x] Covers 429 regression scenario with fallback - [x] Validates audit events for promote/abort - [x] Validates idempotency/retry semantics - [x] CI integration job added (required for rollouts PRs) Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Expand quality regression gate coverage once eval harness integration is wired into the integration runner (Selene/Olivia). - Add multi-region impairment scenario (region down mid-stage) once routing multi-region simulator is in the test harness.
Ethan Park: The rollback test looks good, but please assert the rollout plan state machine fields (held/aborted/completed) rather than just the HTTP response. Also, can we assert the audit event includes old_stage/new_stage and idempotency key? Leila Farouk: Added explicit assertions on plan.state, plan.current_stage_index, and captured audit events. Also asserted audit payload contains old_stage, new_stage, override=false, and idempotency_key. Jordan Lee: On missing metrics test: we agreed fail-closed, but the test currently treats UNKNOWN as pass for stage 0. That’s risky. Please align with policy engine semantics: UNKNOWN should block promotion unless force-promote. Leila Farouk: Updated: UNKNOWN now blocks promotion for all non-terminal stages. Added a separate assertion that an admin-only override path exists (but not exercised end-to-end here). Mina Haddad: Re: 429 regression test—can we make it more representative of the beta incident? Specifically, simulate a small pool where canary has 1 replica and gets a burst; routing should fallback to baseline when queue depth breaches threshold. Leila Farouk: Updated the simulator to model queue depth per partition and to trip fallback once queue_depth > threshold. Test now asserts initial requests go to canary then new requests route to baseline when saturated. Rafael Mendes: Please ensure the suite is stable and won’t flap on CI. The window lengths and sample counts need to be deterministic. Also, mark the suite required only for rollouts-related changes to avoid slowing unrelated PRs. Leila Farouk: Added test clock + seeded RNG; removed reliance on wall clock. CI manifest now scopes the required suite behind labels/path filters (dedicated/rollouts/control_plane/routing). Connor O’Brien: Looks ready. Please add a note in the CI job description on how to re-run locally and how to set SEED when debugging. Leila Farouk: Added to ci/integration-test-manifest.yml and test/README.md section for integration runner. Approved.

Motivation: Provide a lightweight forecasting layer that automatically derives per-workload batcher curves and suggests conservative cost/latency defaults for batching, prefill, and quantization profiles. This PR introduces a new 'cost-horizon' component that ingests short-term telemetry (30m-6h) and synthesizes expected token throughput vs tail-latency curves for a given model+route. Goals: 1) reduce time-to-safe-defaults when onboarding new routes; 2) provide explainable fallback defaults for Dedicated/Private deployments; 3) feed the Optimize recommendations UI with a compact curve summary. Motivation: customers using the /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer reported inconsistent stop handling and truncated toolcall exchanges when streaming responses and falling back across model variants. This PR unifies parameter normalization for stop arrays/sentinels, ensures logprobs and stop signals are propagated deterministically through streaming envelopes, and introduces a resilient tool-call handshake/resume protocol to avoid lost tool outputs in intermediate reconnections.

What this changes (single continuous description): canonicalize v1 chat params: introduce a single param-normalizer that accepts legacy stop formats (string, array, special tokens) and produces an internal stop-set representation used by both batch and streaming paths; coerce role aliases and preserve role metadata when mapping between adapter layers; implement stop-propagation: stops are now evaluated at token-generation and stream-framing layers with consistent precedence (explicit stop list > stop weight heuristics > model-inferred EOS) so clients see matching stop points between sync and streaming responses; logprobs envelope: add compact logprob delta messages emitted on the stream with clear token indices and an explicit final logprob frame for non-streamed fallback; tool-call handshake/resume: new two-way preflight step in the stream (TOOL_HANDSHAKE / TOOL_ACK) plus a resume token so downstream tool runners can rehydrate partial tool outputs after connection blips; streaming stability: introduce heartbeat sentinel frames and backoff-aware fragment coalescing to reduce duplicate fragments and improve reassembly across proxies.

Files changed (high level): api/compat/v1/param_normalizer.py (new) — canonicalization and migration shims; serving/streaming/framer.go — stop evaluation and heartbeat frames; runtime/tooling/handshake.go — tool handshake and resume token state machine; tests/compat/test_chat_stops.py — coverage for stop formats and streaming parity; tests/streaming/test_resume_reassembly.js — fuzz tests simulating partial reconnects; docs/openapi/v1_chat_compat.md — updated compatibility notes and migration guidance.

Commits (summary):
- 4f92d5d: add param normalizer and adapter glue;
- 9c1b3a7: implement streaming stop evaluation + heartbeat frames;
- a6e4b2f: tool handshake/resume protocol and runtime state;
- 2b7f113: tests, docs and CI flakiness fixes.

Backward compatibility and migration notes: existing clients should continue to work unchanged. Edge cases fixed: stop arrays passed as comma-separated single strings (legacy client bug) are normalized; stop handling differences between non-streamed and streamed codepaths are eliminated. Tool runners that rely on implicit stream termination should adopt the new handshake ACK semantics to avoid missing final fragments — see docs/openapi/v1_chat_compat.md for example pseudocode. No breaking API changes were made; developers wanting to opt into stricter stop-prioritization can set the new parameter "stop_mode=strict" (opt-in).

Tests and CI: added unit and integration tests that exercise mixed-mode streaming and reconnects; included a small synthetic latencies harness that revealed an off-by-one stop fence which was fixed. CI: build/test/lint all pass on main matrix except a transient macOS flake that required a rerun. Final CI status: pass.

Review thread (condensed): Reviewer Liam asked for clearer separation between param-normalizer side effects and request telemetry; I split the telemetry emission into a separate tracing hook as requested. Sofia requested an additional fuzz test for tool reassembly under packet reorder; added test case in tests/streaming/test_resume_reassembly.js. Eliot flagged a potential race in the resume token garbage collection; I added a bounded TTL and unit test. After two rounds of changes reviewers approved and marked ready.

Deployment notes: staged to canary and exercised against dedicated workloads; observed 0.4% p99 latency increase under large stop lists but 18% reduction in duplicate stream fragments. No rollout blockers.

Related work: references ENG-9384 (streaming parity effort) and ENG-9422 (tool-runner reliability). Links: internal design doc at /docs/design/chatv1-stop-tool-handshake.md and migration examples in docs/openapi/v1_chat_compat.md.

Release notes: "Improve v1 chat compatibility: consistent stop handling for streamed and sync responses; robust tool-call handshake with resume support to avoid lost tool outputs during reconnects; streaming stability improvements (heartbeat, fragment coalescing) and logprob envelope frames for clearer token-level diagnostics."
Liam Chen: clarify telemetry side-effects -> moved telemetry to tracing hook; Sofia Rodriguez: add fuzz case for packet reorder -> added; Eliot Brooks: race on resume GC -> added TTL and tests; approvals after changes (LGTM x3).
Improve v1 chat compatibility: deterministic stop propagation across streaming and sync paths; resilient tool-call handshake with resume tokens; streaming stability fixes and compact logprob frames.

Motivation: Customers operating in regulated zones requested stronger, append-only audit artifacts that carry compact, verifiable sealing information per request attachment (payloads, model outputs, and routing metadata). At the same time, repeated KMS selector calls across region boundaries were a measurable contributor to latency and billing spikes for multi-tenant workloads. This PR implements two coordinated features: 1) an attachment-stamped audit proxy that signs a compact attachment fingerprint using tenant-scoped KMS keys and emits a sealed audit envelope with provenance headers; 2) a KMS constraint optimizer service that pre-computes region-aware key candidate sets and caches selection decisions for short TTLs, falling back to strict validation when constraints change. Changes include server-side runtime hooks, a small client-side SDK helper for generating attachment fingerprints, policy updates for RBAC v2 to allow temporal sealer grants, and migration steps for audit ingesters. Scope: - runtime/service: new attachment sealer middleware and audit-envelope composer - kms service: constraint optimizer + metrics and decision cache - authz: RBAC v2 role template for 'sealer.grant' with timebound allowance - sdk: helper function in redwood-sdk-go and redwood-sdk-python to compute attachment stamps - infra: migration task that backfills audit index entries with new headers Backwards compatibility: Audit messages without attachment stamps are accepted; when stamped messages are present ingesters verify stamp signatures if the tenant flag is enabled. Rollout plan: 1) Feature flag off by default. 2) Canary deploy proxy in us-west-2 with a single high-volume tenant. 3) Monitor audit verification error rates and KMS constraint cache hit ratio. 4) Gradual enablement per-tenant via Console. Checklist: - [x] implement sealer middleware and envelope composer - [x] implement KMS constraint optimizer + decision cache - [x] SDK helpers for Go and Python (TS planned in follow-up) - [x] RBAC v2 role template and admission validator - [x] unit and integration tests for verification workflow - [x] add tracing and perf metrics for KMS selector path - [x] migration plan + one-time backfill script Links: Linear ENG-4021 (design), SEC-119 (threat-model); design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4021/attachment-stamped-audit-proxy; smoke dashboards: grafana/dashboard/attach-seal-canary.
Diego Alvarez: This looks solid; two questions: (1) can you quantify the expected extra per-request latency for the sealing step? (2) what's the failure mode if KMS is not reachable?
Author (Priya): Latency: median +2.3ms when using cached decision; cold path +15-25ms depending on KMS provider. Failure mode: we emit an unsigned envelope with a 'seal-missing' header and the ingestion path treats it as non-stamped. The migration uses a strict-mode gate for tenants that require stamped artifacts.
Maya Chen: Concern about RBAC risk surface — granting sealer privileges could be abused for replay attacks. Suggest timebound + operator-approval required for long-lived grants.
Author: Added timebound TTL on sealer role and updated admission validator to require operator approval for >1h grants. Documented in templates and Console UX notes.
Luca Romano: KMS constraint optimizer uses Redis decision cache; ensure the eviction policy won't cause inconsistent key selections during operator scale-up. Also please add telemetry for cache eviction reasons.
Author: Added eviction_reason tag and a prewarming step during replica scale events. Added unit tests simulating eviction and forced re-election.
Diego Alvarez: CI flake on e2e-deploy — rerun fixed it. Approving now.
Maya Chen: LGTM after RBAC tweak and tests pass.
Introduces an attachment-stamped audit proxy to embed non-repudiable seals in audit envelopes and a KMS constraint optimizer that reduces cross-region KMS calls by coalescing candidate key selections.

Context: Customers with strict residency and operator segregation requirements asked for a light-weight enforcement layer that prevents cross-geozone operator actions while preserving existing RBACv2 decision flow. This PR introduces three coordinated components: 1) operator-silo enforcer: a middleware that enforces operator-scoped bindings (silo tag + role) and short-circuits unsafe operator operations; 2) KMS metadata propagator: attaches minimal, signed KMS residency and provider metadata to outbound calls so downstream services can make region-aware decisions without extra RPCs; 3) audit-stitcher: a background worker that collects per-hop audit fragments and emits a canonical audit envelope with provenance and non-repudiation HMACs. Motivation: reduce customer risk when operator tokens or service accounts span regions, decrease policy evaluation complexity downstream, and provide an auditable compact envelope for compliance reviews. Compatibility: all components are feature-flagged and default to no-op; existing RBACv2 policies continue to operate when the flag is off. Design highlights: operator-silo enforcer uses attribute-driven RBAC (silo_id claim) and consults the existing policy cache; KMS propagator attaches a signed metadata header (X-RW-KMS-META) that contains region, key-alias-hash, and a short-lived signature derived from the local KMS attestor; audit-stitcher subscribes to the audit fragment topic, validates HMACs, deduplicates, and emits a single envelope to the audit sink with a provenance index. Security considerations: metadata header is minimized and HMAC-protected; we avoid embedding plaintext keys. Rollout plan: 1) unit + integration tests in CI, 2) shadow rollout in staging (operator_silo=shadow), 3) canary on 5% of namespaces with observability dashboards added, 4) full rollout after 2 weeks with no regression. Related work: references ENG-2047 for operator claims standardization and SUP-6421 incident follow-up. Checklist: - [x] RFC reviewed by security - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests against mock KMS and policy cache - [x] E2E smoke tests in staging - [x] Observability (metrics/traces) added - [x] Feature flag gating implemented
Introduces an operator-silo enforcement layer (opt-in), propagates KMS residency metadata through service boundaries, and stitches distributed audit fragments into a single canonical audit envelope. Backwards compatible; feature gated under 'operator_silo' feature flag and rollout via canary namespaces.

Improves /v1/chat.completions parity: introduces configurable soft-stop matching, deterministic logprob backoff for truncated streams, streaming resume checkpoints, and improved function-call continuity across stream reconnects. No public API surface breaking changes.
Motivation: Customers integrating with OpenAI-style /v1/chat.completions reported two classes of reliability issues in production: (1) fragile stop-token matching when downstream truncation or tokenization differences occur, and (2) stream reconnects causing function-call (fn_call/tool) sequences to be lost or duplicated. This PR implements a compatibility layer that: (A) supports 'soft' stop matching (suffix-aware and token-boundary tolerant) with configurable sensitivity per request, (B) adds a streaming resume protocol that replays minimal context and reconciles partial deltas, and (C) preserves function-call continuity across reconnects by persisting call fragments to an ephemeral resume store and emitting deterministic end-of-call markers.

Summary of changes:
- OpenAI compat: add opt-in param v1.softmax_stop and v1.stop_tolerance to the chat param normalizer; map legacy 'stop' semantics into tolerant matching for streaming and non-streaming flows.
- Streaming runtime: introduce fragment checkpoints (streaming/fragmenter.go) and a resume API surface (streaming/resume.go) used by the gateway to resume interrupted client streams.
- Fncall continuity: persist partial fn_call payloads to an in-memory resume buffer keyed by session_id + sequence, with best-effort dedupe on resume.
- Logprobs/backoff: when stream truncation is detected we emit a synthetic final delta with deterministic logprob backoff instead of dropping probability metadata.
- SDK adapters: add small adapter changes in TS/py SDKs to surface new param names and to optionally enable resume handshake.
- Tests and docs: add integration tests that simulate staggered reconnects, tokenization mismatches, and function-call fragment loss; update compatibility docs.

Backwards compatibility: v1.softmax_stop and v1.stop_tolerance default to off/zero; existing behavior is unchanged unless the customer opts in. The streaming resume handshake is backwards-compatible: older clients will ignore the handshake field and receive the previous behavior.

Rollout: feature gated behind runtime feature flag "soft_stop_resume"; will be enabled for beta customers first and rolled out to general availability after one week of monitoring.

Checklist:
- [x] Parameter mappings implemented
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] SDK adapter tests
- [x] Docs note and migration guidance
- [x] Performance baseline validated (no regression >2% p99 latency)

Related: Linear ENG-2589 (soft-stop prototype), ENG-2691 (stream resume design), SUP-4421 customer report.
Marco Lin: High level — this addresses the core issue from SUP-4421, nice to see the resume handshake. Two questions: what's the memory bound of fncall_resume_buffer and how do we evict?
Aisha Kapoor: Response — buffer is an LRU with configurable max_entries (defaults to 5000 fragments) and TTL of 10m. Eviction is by sequence age; documented and exposed as runtime config.
Derek Chen: Requested change — make the soft-stop matcher deterministic across tokenizers; prefer implementing at token-id level instead of substring heuristics to avoid parity drift. Also add a fuzz test against GPT-like tokenizers.
Aisha Kapoor: Addressed — switched matcher to use token-bigram anchor points when tokenizer metadata available; added fuzz harness (internal/tests/fuzz/stop_fuzz.go) and unit coverage across tokenizers.
Sofia Martinez: Approve after CI: please ensure we log a metric for resumed_streams per customer so we can monitor adoption and failure rates.
Aisha Kapoor: Added metric streaming.resume_attempts and streaming.resume_success in stream_coordinator.go; updated dashboard docs.

Motivation: Customers need predictable failure modes when asking the runtime to emit structured JSON. Existing JSON schema validation is brittle for streaming outputs and offers little control over whether validation problems fail the request or are surfaced as warnings. This PR introduces a lightweight per-request and per-route strictness control (response_format.strict_level) and a standard error-mapping produced when schema validation fails in streaming or non-streaming modes.

Summary of changes: adds response_format.strict_level with values (off|warn|error); implements streaming-aware partial validation that can buffer and attempt recovery for warn mode; defines a canonical structured error report (error_code, location, token_snippet, suggestion, transient) that the OpenAI-compat layer emits on schema issues; maps schema failures to HTTP 400/422 when strict_level=error.

Design notes: the strict_level flag is evaluated in this order: explicit request param > route config > org default. warn mode attempts streaming-friendly heuristics (buffer up to N tokens, attempt incremental re-parse, if still invalid emit structured error record to the metadata channel and continue if possible). error mode will abort the stream and surface the structured error as the final message in the error channel. off preserves current behavior (best-effort, may emit textual hints in the stream). The structured error format is intentionally compact and platform-neutral to support SDKs and downstream tracing.

Compatibility: default remains off; no user-visible changes for callers who don't set strict_level. OpenAI-compat layer supports the new fields under the "response_format" envelope (backwards compatible). SDKs updated to expose the enum and helper utilities to decode the structured error payload.

Testing & rollout: unit tests for validator edge cases and integration tests for streaming scenarios are included. Feature will be rolled out behind a runtime flag and enabled for a small percentage of traffic for two weeks before full release. Documentation was added and linked in the files_changed list.

Files changed (high level): new validator and policy integration + compatibility glue in the API gateway; SDK updates in Python and TypeScript; docs and changelog.

Related: ENG-1124 (structured-output roadmap), ENG-1187 (streaming stability work). See inline commits for details.
feat(api): accept response_format.strict_level in request parsing and validation
feat(stream): implement partial/streaming-aware jsonschema validator with buffer window
chore(openai-compat): emit structured schema errors on validation failures
feat(sdk): expose StrictLevel enum and structured error helper in python + ts sdks
test: add integration tests for warn/error/off modes and streaming fallback
docs: document response_format.strict_level and migration guidance
Marco: Can you clarify how route-level defaults are configured? Response: added policy integration and config examples in strictness_policy.go and docs.
Priya: Concern about increased latency in warn mode due to buffering. Response: buffer window limited to 256 tokens and bounded by time (50ms); added perf tests and benchmark results to bench/stream_validator_bench.go.
Evan: SDK ergonomics - prefer enum helpers. Response: added StrictLevel helpers and a convenience decoder in both python and ts sdks.
Introduces response_format.strict_level (off, warn, error) to control JSON schema enforcement behavior. Adds a canonical structured error payload for schema validation failures that SDKs can decode. Streaming validator will attempt recoveries in warn mode and will abort with clear structured errors in error mode. Default behavior unchanged (off).
payload.title: introduce response_format.strict_level and structured error mapping for schema failures

Context: during beta testing we’ve had multiple instances where customers interpreted route/model breakdown swings as “real spend changes” when the underlying issue was ingestion lag / late events / partial rollups for a region. This PR adds explicit freshness metadata to the Usage Insights API and renders a banner + inline status on the console breakdown pages when results may be incomplete. The goal is to make data trust issues obvious, reduce support load, and give users an action (narrow time range / wait for backfill) rather than silently showing partial totals.

What this PR does:
- API: extends v1 usage-insights responses to include `data_freshness` metadata (latest_complete_bucket_end, observed_lag_seconds, completeness, and a human-readable status reason). This metadata is computed per query based on the requested time range and the dataset watermark.
- Console: shows a dismissible banner at the top of Usage → Cost Insights pages when `completeness != complete` or when lag exceeds threshold; adds a smaller “Data freshness” pill next to the time range selector for non-blocking warnings.
- UX details: banner copy is intentionally specific (“Data through 14:00 UTC; newer data still processing”) and links to the help article section on freshness/late events.
- Telemetry: emits a `console.usage_insights.freshness_banner_shown` event with the reason code so we can measure how often users hit lag/partial states.

Thresholds / semantics:
- `completeness` is `complete` if requested_end <= latest_complete_bucket_end.
- `completeness` is `partial` if requested_end > latest_complete_bucket_end.
- `completeness` is `unknown` if the watermark lookup fails (we default to no banner, but show a small pill tooltip indicating we couldn’t confirm freshness).
- Banner is shown for `partial` always; for `complete` we show only if observed_lag_seconds > 900 (15m) to catch edge cases where buckets are “complete” but significantly delayed.

API example (abridged):
- `data_freshness.completeness`: complete | partial | unknown
- `data_freshness.latest_complete_bucket_end`: RFC3339 timestamp
- `data_freshness.observed_lag_seconds`: integer
- `data_freshness.reason`: enum (LATE_EVENTS, AGGREGATION_LAG, WATERMARK_UNAVAILABLE)

Notes:
- This is backwards compatible for existing clients; the new field is additive.
- The freshness metadata is explicitly excluded from response cache keys (it’s computed post-query from the same watermark source), but the watermark lookup itself is cached for 30s in the query service to avoid thundering herds.

Testing:
- Unit tests for freshness computation across time ranges + watermark states.
- Frontend tests for banner rendering/copy and dismissal persistence.
- Manual: verified in staging by forcing a low watermark and querying “Last 24h”.

Rollout:
- Guarded behind existing usage-insights beta flag; banner can be disabled via `console_usage_insights_freshness_banner` kill switch if copy/threshold needs rapid iteration.

Refs:
- Linear: ENG-3824
- Related: PR #23135 (query API v1), PR #23114 (aggregation dataset)
- Support signal: SUP-24863 (timeouts/long ranges often correlating with partial data); this should reduce confusion when users narrow ranges.

Checklist:
- [x] Add API contract + changelog entry for additive field
- [x] Console banner + pill states (partial/lag/unknown)
- [x] Events + dashboards hook (follow-up: add alert if watermark unavailable > 5m)
- [x] Copy reviewed by Design + DevEx (lightweight) and aligned with help center wording

Chloe Martin (requested changes): Can we make sure the watermark lookup failure doesn’t flip the whole request to 500? I’d prefer the query still succeeds and freshness is `unknown`.
Felix Schneider (author): Yep — updated to catch watermark errors and set `completeness=unknown` + `reason=WATERMARK_UNAVAILABLE`. Query response remains 200 and we don’t show the big banner by default (only pill tooltip). Added test coverage.
Allison Grant: The reason codes look good, but we should be careful about calling it “late events” vs “aggregation lag”. Can we ensure `LATE_EVENTS` is only used when the late-event counter is non-zero for the window?
Felix Schneider (author): Good call. I split it: if `late_event_rate > 0.5%` for the trailing hour, reason is `LATE_EVENTS`; otherwise `AGGREGATION_LAG`. If we can’t fetch the metric, we default to `AGGREGATION_LAG` to avoid over-claiming. Tests updated.
Tessa Morgan (requested changes): Banner copy feels too generic. Can we include a concrete “Data through <time>” and avoid “may be incomplete” if it definitely is incomplete?
Felix Schneider (author): Updated copy to: “Showing partial data. Complete data through {timestamp} (UTC). Newer usage is still processing.” and only uses “may” for `unknown` (pill tooltip).
Kaitlyn Nguyen: RBAC question — are we leaking anything about other projects/workspaces via watermark? This should be scoped to workspace/project filter.
Felix Schneider (author): Watermark query is computed on the same dataset partition keys as the request (workspace_id + project_id when provided). No cross-scope access. Added an auth regression test to ensure watermark lookup uses the caller’s scoped filter set.
Dylan Brooks: Looks solid. One perf nit: avoid an extra warehouse roundtrip for watermark when the request is cached.
Felix Schneider (author): Implemented 30s in-process cache for watermark keyed by (workspace, project, dataset, bucket). Also ensured we compute freshness after retrieving cached breakdown results so we don’t invalidate existing caches.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved after changes. Please make sure we track watermark-unavailable rate post-merge.
Dylan Brooks (approval): Approved.
payload.title: Usage insights: add data freshness metadata + console banner for partial/lagging data

Motivation: During a recent regional incident we observed frequent churn when standby nodes came back online: idle capacity would be immediately re-allocated, triggering cascading KV-sync and causing short-lived capacity oscillations that pushed SLO-sensitive tenants into circuit states. This PR introduces a telemetry-driven fallback prioritizer plus a predictive node hibernation controller to reduce churn and make regional failovers calmer. Goals: 1) Prioritize fallback and shed decisions using recent per-tenant request shape and success-rate deltas instead of simple token-rate thresholds. 2) Temporarily mark underutilized nodes as 'hibernating' during controlled warmup windows to avoid immediate re-inclusion in load balancing. 3) Emit observability signals and rollout knobs so SRE can tune behavior without code changes. Summary of changes: runtime/scheduler: new fallback_prioritizer.go with prioritization rules driven by sliding-window aggregates; orchestration/hibernate: predictive_hibernator.go controller that recommends hibernate/unhibernate actions based on predicted ramp and probe latency; telemetry: added two new histograms (fallback.priority_score, node.hibernate_probability) and a new composite metric fallback.regional_pressure; console: dashboard updates + a feature flag toggle; tests: unit tests for prioritizer, integration tests simulating cross-region restarts, e2e: synthetic scenario that reproduces the incident pattern. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind rollout.defer.prioritizer; staged canary to 10% of regions for 24h, then 50% for 12h, then global. Backport: cherrypick to release/1.12 (hotfix) included. Checklist: - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Telemetry and dashboard panels - [x] SLO regression tests run locally - [x] Ops runbook entry added (docs/ops/node-hibernate.md) - [x] Backport PR created to release/1.12 Links: Linear ENG-4621 (fallback prioritizer spec), SUP-345 (incident ticket).
Luca Marin: 'Can you explain how we avoid a long-term bias where low-priority tenants are always hibernated?' -- Asha: 'Prioritizer includes a decay window and minimum serve quota per-tenant; added tests to ensure no permanent starvation.'; Priya Nadar: 'Feature flag makes sense, but add throttling on hibernate transitions to avoid oscillation.' -- Asha: 'Added transition cooldown and exponential backoff in predictive_hibernator.'; Ethan Zhang: 'Metrics look good; please ensure dashboards show both probability and actual events.' -- Asha: 'Adjusted dashboards to include event overlays and trace links.'
Introduce telemetry-driven fallback prioritizer and predictive node hibernation to reduce regional failover churn and improve SLO stability during node restarts. Feature-flagged. Backported to release/1.12.
Ops playbook (docs/ops/node-hibernate.md) added: how to toggle rollout.defer.prioritizer flag, how to read fallback.priority_score and node.hibernate_probability histograms, manual unhibernate steps, and rollback guidance. Recommended alert: fallback.regional_pressure > 0.6 for 5m triggers investigation.
1) Monitor fallback.regional_pressure and node.hibernate_probability for 48h in canary regions; 2) If SLO regressions observed, flip feature flag off and roll back cherrypick; 3) Follow up with a retrospective and potential tuning RFC (ENG-4689).

Add a lightweight CI Gatekeeper service and a lazy dependency sync agent to reduce presubmit noise and speed feedback. Gatekeeper is a small Go binary that sits as a pre-merge policy check, performing deterministic rule evaluation (changelist size, dependency category, license flags) and making a pass/fail/soft-fail decision that can route PRs into fastpath lanes or require full presubmit lanes. The lazy dep sync agent defers expensive dependency resolution and lockfile churn to an async reconciler that populates a dep-snapshot artifact used by the presubmit fastpath to avoid reinstalling devdeps for trivial edits. This PR refactors existing presubmit wiring to a plugin model, migrates the presubmit workflow to a two-lane flow (fastpath vs full), introduces a small state machine for gate decisions, and adds operational observability (metrics and event logs). Motivation: long-running lint/test jobs caused noisy flakes and slow merges for low-risk PRs; repository-wide dependency churn from repeated lockfile updates increased CI time. Checklist: [x] gatekeeper service and config schema implemented, [x] presubmit router integrated into workflows, [x] lazy dep-sync agent implemented and reconciler cron job added, [x] metrics and traces added to Redwood observability-pack, [x] migration guide and docs/ci/fastpath.md, [x] smoke-tested on staging org. Rollout: staged rollout using feature flagging in presubmit router; enable fastpath for low-risk teams first, monitor errors for two days, then widen the cohort. Backout plan: disable presubmit fastpath flag and revert presubmit workflow to previous single-lane by removing the router step and dropping the gatekeeper check. Impact: reduces average presubmit runtime by up to 45% for trivial changes and decreases devdep rebuild frequency. See release_notes for more details.
Asha: The gate decision logic is compact but please add an explicit unit test for license-blocking rules (we had a regression last quarter).
Omar: Added license rule unit tests and a small e2e that runs gatekeeper against a sample manifest (see ci/testdata).
Michael: Two nits on logging levels and an edge-case in the reconciler when network is flaky; recommend retry backoff. Omar: addressed the logging nits and added an exponential backoff with jitter in the reconciler (last commit).
Lena: Approving after smoke runs on staging. Left a suggestion to add a dashboard tile for fastpath ratio — will follow up in a separate PR.
Introduces a presubmit gatekeeper that routes low-risk PRs to a fastpath and adds a lazy dependency sync to reduce devdep rebuilds. Admins can toggle fastpath via feature flags. Expect faster presubmit feedback for non-dep-touching changes and less lockfile churn. See docs/ci/fastpath.md for migration steps.
payload.title: introduce-ci-gatekeeper-and-lazy-dep-sync

Motivation: presubmit jobs were spending a large portion of wall-clock time waiting on remote package registries and shared artifact stores; cold CI runner startup and network IO contribute to slow feedback and flakiness. This PR introduces three coordinated changes: (1) a presubmit cache-proxy that runs as a short-lived sidecar on ephemeral CI runners to serve cached package artifacts and proxy registry requests; (2) a slim CI bootloader image (minimal toolchain + fast init) to reduce runner boot time and image pull size; (3) a release signaler utility that posts a compact smoke-run summary to the release automation pipeline so we can gate releases on an explicit lightweight acceptance check. High-level goals: reduce presubmit latency (esp. for JS/Python installs), reduce flakiness caused by transient registry errors, and attach automated smoke-run context to release notes for observability.

Description of changes:
- tools/ci/presubmit-cache-proxy/: new Go-based cache-proxy with HTTP/HTTPS proxying, local on-disk cache, LRU eviction, and simple /health and /metrics endpoints for Prometheus scraping. Configured to cache npm tarballs, pip wheels, and container layers.
- ci/bootloader/Dockerfile.{slim,helpers}: new multi-stage slim Dockerfile that installs only the runtime pieces used in fast presubmits (git, curl, tar, node/pip shim); legacy heavy boot images moved to ci/bootloader/legacy/ and retained for nightly/integration lanes.
- tools/release/signal.py: small Python script invoked by release pipeline that collects the last presubmit smoke-run status, test coverage quick snapshot, and artifact hashes; posts a structured message to Linear/release-notes webhook and adds a release annotation in the release metadata.
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yml: updated to include a presubmit-proxy step that spins up the cache-proxy container via docker-in-docker, runs fast-installs against it, and tears it down.
- ci/runner-init.sh: wrapper that prefers slim bootloader images for fast lanes and falls back to legacy for full tests.
- docs/ci/cache-proxy.md: operational runbook, metrics to watch, and cost/retention guidance.

Commits (summary):
- add presubmit cache-proxy initial implementation and tests; wire up metrics
- add slim bootloader Dockerfile + helper scripts; provide migration notes
- integrate cache-proxy into presubmit workflow and runner-init
- add release signaler script and release workflow hook
- update docs and add runbook
- fix flaky test by extending network timeouts in proxy integration tests

Changed files (high level): .github/workflows/presubmit.yml; ci/bootloader/Dockerfile.slim; ci/bootloader/helpers/*.sh; tools/ci/presubmit-cache-proxy/{main.go,proxy.go,cache.go,go.mod}; tools/release/signal.py; ci/runner-init.sh; docs/ci/cache-proxy.md; tests/integration/test_proxy.go; Makefile (added targets: ci-cache-proxy-start/stop).

Checklist:
- [x] Basic unit + integration tests for cache-proxy (mock registry)
- [x] Presubmit flow validated on a subset of repos (sdk-python, redwood-docs)
- [x] Bootloader image size reduced ~45% vs legacy image
- [x] Release signaler posts to staging release webhook and attaches metadata
- [x] Operational docs + runbook included

Known limitations & tradeoffs:
- The proxy doesn't currently support authenticated private registries (will follow up in ENG-2257). For private registries the proxy can be run behind a short-lived credential forwarder (documented in runbook).
- This PR prioritizes fast presubmits; full integration lanes still use legacy images and full caches.

Review & CI notes: initial CI run failed on integration tests due to a flaky network assertion in test_proxy.go (intermittent DNS timeouts in runner images). I pushed a fix to increase DNS timeout and added retry logic in the integration harness. CI was rerun and then passed on the second run.

Review conversation (summary):
- Priya: asked for explicit eviction policy configuration and a safe default; requested an option to cap disk usage per-runner. Response: added LRU eviction + max-disk setting with default 2GB and documented how to tune per-runner via workflow inputs.
- Marcus: asked whether the release signaler could accidentally leak internal test artifact URLs; asked for structured redact rules. Response: added a sanitizer in tools/release/signal.py to strip auth tokens and S3 presigned URLs; tests added.
- Elena: requested a clearer migration plan for repos that depend on the legacy boot image; provided ci/bootloader/legacy/ with migration notes and a Makefile target to rebuild legacy images.
- Security review (quick): validated that proxy does not persist credentials and that traffic is restricted to ephemeral runners; added e2e smoke to assert no credentials written to disk.

CI matrix behavior and results:
- presubmit unit: pass
- proxy integration: initial fail (test_proxy.go flaky DNS), rerun pass
- lint: pass
- e2e-smoke (slim): pass
- release-signal unit: pass

Observability and SLOs:
- New metrics: ci_cache_proxy.requests_total, ci_cache_proxy.hit_ratio, ci_cache_proxy.evictions_total. Dashboards added in docs runbook and a Grafana panel suggested for SRE.
- Expected presubmit median reduction: 18-28% on sampled repositories (measured with a 2-week A/B on a staging project).

Rollout plan: deploy cache-proxy to presubmit lanes for low-risk repos (sdk-python, docs, examples) for 2 weeks, monitor hit ratio and eviction behavior; then gradually opt-in other repos. Release signaler initially enabled only for staging releases; require opt-in for production releases until we confirm sanitized payloads.

Post-merge tasks (tracked in ENG-2201):
- add private registry auth passthrough (ENG-2257)
- add auto-scaling for cache-proxy sidecars for larger runners
- backport slim bootloader to release-branches if approved by release owners

Merge: squashed and merged to main (squash commit message included perf numbers and link to runbook). No service-facing breaking changes. If we see unexpected cache stomping or disk pressure, ops can flip presubmit cache off via repository workflow input.
Added a lightweight presubmit cache proxy to reduce CI network IO; small bootloader images for faster startup; release signaler that attaches smoke-run results to release notes. No behavioral changes to public APIs.
payload.title: Introduce presubmit cache-proxy, slim CI bootloader, and release signaler

Motivation: intermittent, slowly accumulating latency regressions in mixed-traffic environments were frequently masked by aggregated canary signals. This PR introduces a deconvolutional drift prober that separates correlated traffic covariates (request size, concurrency, model variant mix, and input modality) from true per-replica latency drift and pairs it with a soft-failover policy that reduces blast radius without an immediate hard rollback. Approach: add a canary evaluator plugin (deconv_drift_prober) that runs lightweight deconvolution on streaming telemetry, computes per-covariate residuals, and emits a probabilistic drift score. The soft-failover policy uses a hysteresis-backed traffic-weighted throttling action that progressively shifts traffic away from affected replicas and falls back to a compatible model variant only after a sustained confidence threshold. Configuration: new canary config fields deconv_window_seconds, covariate_list, residual_threshold, soft_failover_grace_seconds, and max_shift_pct. The feature is guarded behind runtime flag canary.deconv_prober.enabled and is off by default. Tests: unit tests for the deconvolutional estimator, integration tests in perf-canary harness with synthetic traffic patterns (burst, diurnal, phased model skew), and a canary E2E job that validates no false-positive rollbacks on 10k-sample windows. Rollout plan: opt-in in staging for two weeks using traffic shadowing, then gradual enable on canaries for low-traffic namespaces with observability dashboards; monitor false-positive rate and rollback frequency via new metric canary.deconv.false_positives. Related work: builds on ENG-3629 (covariate-normalized canary baseline) and complements ENG-3680 (traffic-aware probe scheduler). Checklist: ensure feature flag gating, docs updated, metrics exported, perf unit tests added, runbook note written. Backwards compatibility: no changes to existing canary schemas when feature flag off. 
add deconvolutional prober implementation and public interface
implement soft-failover scheduler and traffic-shift controller
add unit & integration tests and perf harness scripts
docs: add configuration guide and runbook notes
Alex Ruiz: Nice approach. Can you justify the choice of deconvolution algorithm and its O(n) runtime under high concurrency? Suggest adding a microbenchmark in perf_harness.
Maya S. Park: Added a microbenchmark and included its results in perf_harness.yml. The algorithm uses incremental least-squares with L2 regularization to be streaming-friendly.
Priya Nambiar: We should ensure this doesn't increase tail latency by running the prober on a dedicated worker pool. Please add option to run in-process vs out-of-process.
Maya S. Park: Added config flag prober.execution_mode with choices inproc|worker-pool and updated docs; default is worker-pool for production.
Evan Cho: CI flaked on the integration test due to timing; reran CI and all checks passed. Approve after addressing minor logging message formatting.
Maya S. Park: Fixed logging format and pushed the change. CI green.
Initial CI run: tests failed due to a flaky integration timing assumption; updated harness and reran. Final CI: all unit, integration, lint, and perf smoke checks passed. Coverage delta: +1.8% in canary package.
Add deconvolutional canary prober to improve detection of covariate-driven latency drift
Introduce soft-failover policy that gradually shifts traffic to limit blast radius
New config fields: deconv_window_seconds, residual_threshold, soft_failover_grace_seconds, prober.execution_mode
Feature is behind runtime flag canary.deconv_prober.enabled (off by default)
Schedule staged rollout in staging cluster and shadow 5% production traffic for two weeks
Add dashboard panels for canary.deconv.* metrics and false-positive tracking
Coordinate with SRE to add automated alert on sustained shift > 30%
