Motivation: During recent maintenance windows and rolling kernel upgrades we observed tenant-level eviction storms triggered by simultaneous circuit transitions and aggressive prioritizer heuristics. This caused fragile tenants to be repeatedly evicted, increasing tail-latency and recovery time. This PR introduces a 'maintenance holdoff' that temporarily softens eviction aggression for tenants that have been recently moved into maintenance mode, plus two complementary flood-protection measures (rate-bounding for circuit transitions and a short-lived tenant grace lease) to prevent cascade failures.

What this changes: 1) Maintenance holdoff: when an operator marks a node or shard as 'maintenance', affected tenants enter a 30s holdoff during which the prioritizer reduces eviction weights and avoids hard preemption. 2) Transition rate-bounding: a cluster-wide leaky-bucket limits circuit transition events to a configurable burst (default 5 transitions / 10s) to avoid simultaneous rebalances. 3) Tenant grace lease: a short-lived lease (default 45s) allows in-flight requests to finish without being forcibly evicted; the lease is observable and audited. 4) Telemetry: new metrics and debug traces for holdoff starts/ends, rate-bucket fills, and lease expiration reasons. 5) Rollout-safe: feature gated behind runtime flag "maintenance_holdoff_v1" with default enabled for safety team; can be toggled per-region.

Implementation notes: changes touch the prioritizer, circuit orchestrator, operator CLI, and observability hooks. Logic added in prioritizer/holdoff.go, orchestrator/rate_limiter.go, operator/commands.go, and telemetry/metrics_registry.go. Tests: unit tests for holdoff state machine and leaky bucket; integration test that simulates a rolling maintenance with 100 tenants to validate no mass-evictions.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-1987) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration test added - [x] Metrics and traces wired - [x] Runtime flag and CLI hook - [x] Docs blurb for maintenance runbook (internal) - [x] Observability dashboard tile prototype

Rollout plan: 1) Canary on non-prod regions (2/20) 2) Monitor new metrics for two maintenance cycles 3) Gradual enable for production regions 4) Enable cluster-wide by config after SRE signoff. Rollback: runtime flag off or change leaky-bucket thresholds; revert is safe since state machine tolerates stale holdoff entries.

Related work: touches codepaths from ENG-1223 (tenant prioritizer refactor) and ENG-1544 (operator CLI improvements). Support ticket SUP-9142 reported repeated evictions during a kernel upgrade and motivated the flood-protection rate-bucket.

Notes on safety: The holdoff only reduces eviction aggressiveness; it never disables critical safety evictions (e.g., overloaded GPU OOM conditions). We included a safety bypass when node health drops below critical thresholds.

Commits summary: - c1a7d9b: add maintenance holdoff state machine and tests - 0f3e2a1: implement cluster-wide leaky-bucket rate limiter for circuit transitions - 9b4c8f2: add tenant grace lease and audit events - 7d0f11e: wire metrics and add dashboard tile stub - a2b3c4d: add operator flag and CLI integration - 4e5f6a7: integration test for rolling maintenance scenario and flake fixes

Changed files (high-level): - prioritizer/holdoff.go (new) - orchestrator/rate_limiter.go (new) - orchestrator/transition_manager.go (updated) - operator/commands.go (updated) - telemetry/metrics_registry.go (updated) - tests/unit/holdoff_test.go (new) - tests/integration/maintenance_rollout_test.go (new) - docs/internal/maintenance-runbook.md (updated) - dashboards/maintenance_holdoff.json (new) - ci/config.yml (tweaked to add integration stage) - pkg/lease/grace_lease.go (new)

CI and checks: initial CI run failed on integration stage (transient race in test harness: TestMaintenanceRollout flake). I reproduced locally and added deterministic timing controls in integration harness (commit a2b3c4d). Final CI run: unit tests pass, integration suite pass, lint pass, e2e smoke pass. Post-merge: we will keep an eye on integration flakiness metric.

Review thread (high-level): see review comments below. The PR was iterated twice to address concerns about tenant fairness scoring and to add additional observability for lease expirations. After addressing those comments the change received approvals and was squashed and merged.

Merge decision: Squash-and-merge after CI green and SRE approval. Merged by Lina Chen on 2026-02-20.
Stability: Add tenant maintenance holdoff window and flood-protection heuristics to circuit maintenance mode; reduces churn during multi-tenant node maintenance and prevents tenant-level eviction storms.
Samir Gupta (2026-02-16): Can we ensure the holdoff doesn't bias tenant fairness permanently? Suggest adding a decay so weights return to normal after 2 minutes. - Response: added decay in holdoff.go and unit test (commit c1a7d9b).
Lina Chen (2026-02-17): We need better observability for lease expirations (reason codes). Please add audit events and a metric. - Response: added audit events and metrics (commit 9b4c8f2).
Diego Ruiz (2026-02-18): Integration test flaked locally; reproducible race in test harness. Add deterministic timers or mocks. - Response: updated integration harness and made timers deterministic (commit 4e5f6a7).
Samir Gupta (2026-02-19): Approved after verifying integration run on canary region; recommend watching 'maintenance_holdoff.evictions_avoided' metric for first 48h. - Response: noted in rollout plan.

Context: A small but observed class of incidents showed short multi-region thundering spikes where the fastpath stayed healthy but egress saturation (downstream model IO) created tail latency cascades and then aggressive circuit flips. Motivation: provide a soft 'ventilation' path that gently siphons a configurable fraction of low-priority requests to a controlled slowpath/egress-trim pipeline while deferring hard circuit flips until telemetry confirms persistent degradation. This reduces noisy circuit churn and prevents mass failovers during transient egress pressure. What this PR does: 1) Introduces an EgressSiphon controller that can be attached to existing admission and routing layers to probabilistically divert or slow low-priority requests based on recent egress queue depth and token-level telemetry. 2) Adds a DeferredCircuit state machine that delays full circuit tripping for a short hysteresis window and requires both metrics and sampled trace evidence before moving to OPEN. 3) Adds telemetry guards: lightweight sampling rules that emit a preflight event for siphoned requests so we can correlate siphon volume with downstream error budget usage. 4) Runtime knobs: per-tenant weight, min-siphon-fraction, max-siphon-fraction, egress-queue-threshold, defer-window-ms. 5) Minimal operator docs and a small k8s CRD and rollout recipe for safe enablement. Rollout plan: feature-flagged off by default; staged rollout in canary region -> regional ramp -> global. Hotfix rationale: accelerated to a hotfix because it prevents an immediate class of circuit storms that were contributing to 3rd-party throttles. Testing: unit tests for state transitions, integration test that simulates egress pressure and validates reduced circuit flips, and a short e2e in staging with synthetic load. Ops: added telemetry tags (siphon.variant, siphon.reason) and a dashboard snapshot for the first 72 hours. Related: hooks into ENG-4198 for long-term admission shaping and SRE-702 for incident runbook updates. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration test - [x] Load test in staging - [x] Docs + CRD - [x] Telemetry dashboards and alerts - [x] Rollout plan and rollback steps Notes: This is intentionally conservative: siphon fraction starts at 1% and will auto-scale up to configured max only when egress queue > threshold for > defer-window. The deferred circuit requires both metric and sampled trace error correlation to prevent flipping on noisy single-metric spikes.
Implemented EgressSiphon (~320 lines), DeferredCircuit (~140 lines), small telemetry tagging and CRD YAML. Tests added ~200 lines across unit and integration harness. Docs and CI script additions.
Marco Liu: Can we avoid adding an extra goroutine per tenant in the hot path? Suggest using shared sampler with tenant tags — responded: switched to shared sampled emitter, updated implementation to the pooled emitter
Nina Gomez: How will this interact with existing KV cache warmups? Concern that siphoned slowpath might miss cached KV leading to work amplification — responded: siphon respects cache presence; fastpath cache hits bypass siphon (added test).
Daniel Reiss: CI flaky on integration run (timeout) — addressed by increasing harness timeouts and splitting the heavy scenario into a separate job.
Initial CI run failed on integration timeout; retried integration job with extended timeout. Lint and unit tests passed on first run. Full pipeline passed on rerun.
Unit: state transitions, sampling rules. Integration: simulated egress saturation with synthetic model latency — verified 60-70% reduction in circuit flips and stable request success for high-priority traffic. Staging e2e: no regressions in latency p95 for fastpath; observed siphon traffic at configured 1-5% window.
Gate: feature flag 'egress_siphon_v1' default=false. Phase 1: enable in canary region at 1% siphon fraction for 2 hours, monitor 'siphon.error_rate' and 'circuit.flip_rate'. Phase 2: ramp to 5% in canary, 0.5% in 2 additional regions. Phase 3: conditional global ramp to configured defaults if circuit_flip_rate falls >30% vs baseline. Rollback: flip feature flag off and wait one defer-window for circuits to settle. Operators: follow SRE-702 runbook for incident triage.
Added a conservative egress siphon (soft vent) and deferred circuit logic to reduce noisy circuit storms under transient egress pressure. Feature-flagged and off by default. Operators can enable per-tenant with CRD. Improves stability during short-lived downstream saturation.
Backport to release/2026-02 branch if urgent; a minimal backport patch is prepared in branch release/2026-02/egress-siphon-hotfix. Coordinate with on-call SRE if enabling on older clusters.
No model artifacts changed. Runtime change only. Operators must update helm chart to include CRD when enabling the feature.

Motivation: reduce repeated rotary/rope rematerialization and scheduling stalls when continuous batching crosses KV-cache boundaries. This PR introduces a lightweight "rope handshake" protocol between the attention microkernel and the KV cache manager plus a virtual-pipeline (vPipe) continuous batching runtime that keeps micro-batches in flight across CUDA streams. The change consolidates the rotary application and QK pre-softmax path into a single fused kernel that performs rotary embedding application, QK dot product, and scaled-softmax in-stream to reduce DRAM traffic and intermediate allocations. Goals: 1) reduce per-token memory bandwidth and kernel launch overhead for long-context workloads, 2) remove extra rotary recompute when a hot KV segment is spilled/reshuffled, 3) keep GPUs saturated with small interactive micro-batches using vPipe. What changed (high level): implemented a rope handshake ABI that attaches a small metadata header to KV segments (rope-base, rope-offset, handshake-version); modified kernel launcher to propagate handshake metadata; added fused-kernel attn_rope_handshake.cu implementing rotary+qk+softmax path with stream-aware loop unrolling; runtime changes in continuous_batcher to maintain vPipe slots and coordinate cross-stream fence points; KV manager updated to honor handshake hints and avoid rematerializing rotary embeddings when possible. Backwards compatibility: handshake metadata is optional — old kernels and KV stores ignore unknown headers; runtime falls back to legacy path when handshake version mismatch is detected. Checklist: [x] design doc and perf plan attached, [x] microbenchmark harness added, [x] integration tests for handshake ABI, [x] manual validation against existing perf canary, [x] doc updates to kernel interface. Performance: end-to-end throughput gains versus current mainline flash-attn baseline: +18% throughput for seq_len=8192 with batch-size=1 real-time inference profile; +11% for seq_len=4096; 95th-percentile tail latency reduced 7% for interactive sampling workloads. Microbench single-GPU kernel-level comparisons: fused rope-handshake kernel shows 1.12x effective tokens/sec compared to flash-attn-v4 for fp16 experiments on A100-40GB. Cost tradeoffs: slightly higher register pressure on some GPU SMs (resolved with a small vectorization fallback path), small increase in binary size due to handshake metadata helpers. Testing: unit tests for ABI, CUDA unit tests for fused kernel numerics (fp16/fp32) with randomized rotary offsets, integration perf runs in benchmark-lab, canary on perf-canary repository for 48h. Rollout plan: feature-flagged on mainline, enable vPipe on dedicated pools for 2 weeks monitoring through Redwood Console, gradual traffic ramp with automatic fallback to legacy kernel on increased error rate. Commits summary: "add rope handshake ABI and metadata helpers", "implement fused attn_rope_handshake kernel", "runtime: vpipe continuous batcher and slot allocator", "kv: handshake-aware segment manager and heuristics", "tests and perf harness updates". CI summary: initial CI failed on flaky trace test (GPU timing); fixed with fence ordering change and re-run; final CI status green. Merge: squash merge after two approvals and post-merge routine canary deployment. Related work: follows on ideas in ENG-2476 and complements previous async-prefetch and pipeline batching PRs; references design notes in docs/attn/rope-handshake.md. Release notes: Introduces an optional 'rope handshake' attention kernel and vPipe continuous batching for improved throughput on long-context workloads. Metrics and observability: emits new metrics continuous_batcher.inflight_slots, kv.handshake_misses, kernel.rope_handshake_latency for Console dashboards and alerting. Known limitations: handshake overhead can be slightly negative for tiny sequences (seq_len<=64) so the runtime disables vPipe by default for those cases. Deployment: feature gated under runtime.experimental.vpipe and kernel.experimental.rope_handshake. Merge method: squash and merge.
Devon Nguyen (2025-11-24): Nice design. Two concerns: 1) register pressure on smaller SM GPUs could regress per-SM throughput; please add a vectorized fallback path. 2) Ensure handshake metadata doesn't inflate network copy size for multi-host KV replication.
Aria Patel (2025-11-25): Added vectorized fallback path and compacted handshake header to 16 bytes. KV replication now strips handshake hints across the wire and reattaches at host boundary; added tests.
Samir Rao (2025-11-27): Verified numerics against flash-attn across fp16/fp32 random seeds. Minor nits in logging format. Approving pending CI green.
Lina Chen (2025-12-01): Manual canary results look good; +15-20% throughput on long tail. Approved.
Optional rope-handshake attention kernel and vPipe continuous batching added behind experimental flags. Improves throughput on long-context workloads; enabled via runtime.experimental.vpipe and kernel.experimental.rope_handshake.

Adds an experimental "lanes" orchestrator that formalizes multi-lane rollouts (canary / A-B / shadow) with an emphasis on explainable automated rollback decisions and a deadman fallback path. Motivation: customers need a single control plane primitive to express complex multi-lane experiments while preserving predictable safety behavior under partial telemetry loss or control-plane latency. This PR implements: 1) lanes coordinator: new in-memory and persisted state machine for lanes (primary/candidate/shadow) with explicit lane transitions and timestamped shadow captures; 2) deadman fallback: if the controller cannot acquire stable telemetry for a configurable window (deadman_timeout), traffic is routed to a predetermined safe lane and an incident signal is emitted; 3) shadow-timestamping: shadow traffic is captured with request/response timestamps and trace-ids to enable precise offline replay and fidelity scoring; 4) rollback rationale: automated rollback decisions are recorded with human-readable reasons (metric anchors, drift magnitude, latency spike) and a provenance blob linking commits and rollout policy; 5) small API additions: rollout lanes extend the RolloutPolicy proto (new enum LaneType, shadow_capture_time) and rwctl gets new commands (rwctl rollout lanes status|promote|abort); 6) DB migration: rollout_lanes table to persist lane epochs, holdpoints, and last-known-reason; 7) tests and docs: integration e2e harness, unit tests for arbitration, and docs/experimental-lanes.md with examples and safety playbook. Checklist: - [x] implement lanes state machine and persistence - [x] add deadman fallback and incident hooks - [x] extend API protos and CLI - [x] migration script and backwards compatibility checks - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs and example configs Notes: This is gated behind the feature flag rollout.lanes.experimental. The changes are designed to be fully backward compatible when the flag is off. See ENG-2147 for design notes and SUP-8892 for a customer reproduction that motivated the deadman behavior.
Ravi Patel: Overall nice shape. A few concerns: 1) deadman_timeout default seems long (10m) — prefer 2m for hosted tiers, 2) need clearer circuit-breaker semantics when downstream timeouts increase, and 3) add metrics for 'fallback_invocations' and 'shadow_capture_rate'.
Evelyn Chen: Thanks Ravi — lowered default to 2m for hosted and introduced tiered default via config with explicit note in docs. Added fallback_invocations and shadow_capture_rate metrics in runtime. PTAL.
Nina Gomez: API change looks good. Please ensure backward-compatible wire format for rollout.proto; clients should ignore unknown enums. Also request a small compatibility test in CI that loads older rollout records.
Evelyn Chen: Added ignore-unknown-enum handling and a compatibility CI job that replays pre-migration rows against a new binary (scripts/ci/compat_rollout_test.sh).
Liam O'Connor: e2e flake observed locally — test harness replays traced requests but ordering varied; suggest deterministic seeding and a 'wait-for-metrics' helper. Also prefer the rollback rationale to include the exact metric thresholds and the sliding window used for detection.
Evelyn Chen: Introduced deterministic seed for traffic generator. Rollback rationale now includes metric window and threshold snapshot in the provenance blob (human-readable plus JSON in DB).
Ravi Patel: Approved after changes. Nina: Approved. Liam: Approved.
Experimental: rollout lanes — multi-lane orchestrator with canary/A-B/shadow semantics, deadman fallback for telemetry loss, shadow timestamping for replay, and automated rollback rationale. Feature gated behind rollout.lanes.experimental. See docs/rollouts/experimental-lanes.md for examples and playbook.
Run DB migration script on staging and then production (scripts/upgrade/20260218_add_rollout_lanes.sql). Enable rollout.lanes.experimental behind a gradual adoption plan. Notify SRE on-call about new fallback alerts 'lanes.deadman.triggered'.
This PR focuses on the control-plane orchestration and safety wiring; runtime sampling/efficiency improvements for shadow capture are planned in a follow-up PR (ENG-2189). The migration was designed to be idempotent and safe for rolling upgrades.

Context: A customer incident exposed a rapid connection-flood scenario that caused local circuit flip-flopping and a cascade of tenant-level SLO violations. This PR introduces a lightweight "blackout guard" and a progressive SLO rearm policy to reduce oscillation and give regional failover time to stabilize. Motivation: keep user-facing latency SLOs stable during short congestion spikes, avoid aggressive tenant eviction, and ensure repairability without manual intervention. Summary of changes: || 1) runtime: add connection_blackout_detector that tracks short-lived burst profiles per route/tenant and emits a local 'blackout' status to the node-level circuit manager. Blackout state prevents immediate circuit reopen for a configurable cooloff window and increases local prioritization thresholds. || 2) slo_rearm: replace binary rearm with progressive rearm stages (probe -> soft-rearm -> full-rearm). Each stage has telemetry gates and backoff timers so we avoid full reopens on transient success. || 3) telemetry: new metrics (runtime.blackout_events_total, runtime.blackout_duration_seconds, slo.rearm_stage_total, slo.rearm_probe_success_rate) and tracing spans to help incident diagnosis. || 4) config: expose new per-tenant knobs in runtime config (blackout_threshold_per_minute, blackout_cooloff_seconds, rearm_probe_ttl, rearm_stage_backoffs) and sensible defaults that preserve existing behavior for customers who don't opt in. || 5) tests: unit tests for blackout detector logic and integration tests that simulate connection bursts and validate rearm hysteresis. Also added a quick canary script used by SRE to exercise the flow in staging. Changeset summary, commits and high-level file diffs are below.
Maya Kapoor: Overall looks good; two concerns: ensure default cooloff is not too long for low-volume tenants and add a unit test that asserts we don't block reopen forever.
Author (Ethan Li): Addressed. Shortened default cooloff to 30s for tenants below 20 rps and added TestBlackoutNotPermanent in blackout_detector_test.go. See commit d9a8c77.
Nina Patel: Telemetry looks useful, but add an open / close event tag to the blackout metric to make dashboards easier.
Author (Ethan Li): Added event_type label for open/close to runtime.blackout_events_total; updated docs and alerts accordingly.
Carlos Gomez: Can we gate the rearm probe traffic so it doesn't magnify the burst? Suggest probe rate limit tied to circuit weight.
Author (Ethan Li): Implemented probe rate limiting with a token-bucket sized by circuit weight. Added integration test to validate behavior under bursty probe scenarios.

payload.body:
Motivation: We continue to see edge cases where short-term tenant bursts starve longer-running commitments because reservations are reconciled only at coarse intervals and burst credits are consumed without a soft leash. This change introduces a windowed reservation reconciler that reasons about recent allocation windows (sliding time buckets) and applies a configurable burst leash that gradually reduces burst allowance when a tenant's short-term consumption threatens group-level throughput guarantees.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Adds a new reservation reconciler component (windowed_reservation_reconciler) that maintains lightweight sliding windows per-tenant and per-fleet partition. The reconciler exposes two knobs: window_length and decay_slope. The reconciler computes an expected committed utilization over the window, compares against contracted reservation and the fleet-level safety headroom, and emits soft adjustments to tenant burst allowances rather than hard preemption. To enforce fairness during contention, the reconciler introduces a burst_leash module that attaches to the existing credit bank and implements a slope-based reduction: when recent windowed utilization exceeds the committed percentile, burst allowance is reduced according to decay_slope over a configurable leash_duration. The leash is cooperative: it emits recommendations that the admission controller and slot allocator consume; hard enforcement happens only when safety thresholds are crossed.

Changes included: 1) runtime/controller: new sliding-window reconciler (go/service/reservation/windowed_reconciler.go) and unit tests; 2) controller API: new metrics and debug endpoint at /debug/reservations/windowed that returns LIS (list of compacted windows) and last action; 3) credit-bank: hooks to accept leash recommendations and apply soft caps for tentative allocations; 4) allocator: minor changes to accept tentative caps and prefer long-running reservations over recent bursts; 5) telemetry: new metrics (windowed_commit_pct, leash_invocations_total, leash_reduction_bytes) and dashboards + alert rule for leash_invocations spike; 6) integration tests: synthetic workload that reproduces the regression observed in ENG-1482; 7) docs: short design note in docs/ops/reservations.md.

Implementation notes: The reconciler keeps O(1) state per active tenant by compacting windows into 4-point summaries (count, sum, max, last_ts) to limit memory overhead. Window compaction and reconciliation run on a staggered schedule to avoid thundering herd. The leash uses a sigmoid-like clamp expressed as linear decay for simplicity and predictability; we can swap to a non-linear curve later if needed. All new knobs are feature-flagged behind ff.windowed_reservations to enable staged rollout to dedicated clusters.

Why this approach: We want to minimize hard preemptions and customer-visible failures while preserving hard throughput SLAs for committed tenants. The windowed approach captures recent bursty behavior without reacting to single-sample noise, and the leash provides a graceful, reversible lever for the allocator.

Backwards compatibility and rollout: Default behavior is unchanged when the feature flag is off. With the flag on, the reconciler defaults to conservative windows (60s) and gentle decay_slope (0.2) to avoid regressions. We added a smoke test to the deploy pipeline that flips the flag on a canary dedicated cluster and validates baseline throughput.

Benchmarks: In our synthetic scenario (50 tenants, 10% high-burst tenants), the reconciler reduced short-term SLA violations by ~72% with a 4.3% median increase in average latency for bursty requests (tradeoff due to soft-reductions). Memory overhead measured at +2.1MB per 1000 active tenants with compaction.

Security and cost: No new permissions. The debug endpoint is behind admin-only auth and respects audit logging. Additional metrics increase cardinality slightly; telemetry aggregator was updated to drop low-cardinality debug labels.

Open questions: whether to make leash curve configurable per-tenant and how this interacts with warm-pool warmups. A follow-up will add per-tenant profiles and a machine-learned slope suggestion service.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for reconciler logic - [x] Integration test reproducing ENG-1482 - [x] Telemetry + dashboard patch - [x] Docs note and rollout plan - [x] Feature-flag gating and smoke canary

References: ENG-1482 (regression), ENG-1560 (telemetry spike analysis), design doc /docs/design/windowed-reservations.md (attached).
Arjun Patel: Can we avoid adding per-tenant timers? Stagger reconciliation to a jittered cron or use the existing tick shard. Also please add memory accounting when compaction is enabled.
Maya Chen: Addressed by using the existing tick-shard and compacted 4-point summary; added mem accounting in windowed_reconciler.go and tests.
Lina Rodriguez: The leash feels too aggressive for small tenants that occasionally burst; can we make leash a function of reservation size (absolute) not just percentage?
Maya Chen: Updated algorithm to apply a min_absolute_threshold so leases don't reduce allowances below a small fixed byte/token floor for tiny reservations; updated tests and docs.
Noah Kim: CI integration test flakes on low-rps mode; I see a race in the test harness where the reconciler tick runs before synthetic traffic starts. Please add a warmup phase in the test.
Maya Chen: Added warmup phase to the integration test and a retry loop for the harness; flakiness gone in local runs.
Arjun Patel: Approve after minor nit on metric name (windowed_commit_pct -> windowed_commit_percentile).
Maya Chen: Renamed metric and updated dashboard and alert rule.

payload.body:
Introduce a sliding SLO gatekeeper that attenuates strict SLO enforcement under transient load and an evacuation buffer to smooth regional failovers. Backwards-compatible; gated behind feature flag. Recommended rollout: canary -> gradual ramp -> full release.
Motivation: In recent incidents we observed aggressive circuit flips during short bursts which escalated into regional cascade evictions. This PR introduces a 'Sliding SLO Gatekeeper' that softens immediate SLO enforcement for short-lived bursts and an 'Evacuation Buffer' that reserves transient capacity to absorb rejoin traffic, reducing oscillation.

What this changes (high-level):
- Sliding SLO Gatekeeper: a controller that converts strict SLO violations into a proportional attenuation signal based on the violation magnitude and exposure duration. Instead of immediate tenant eviction or hard circuit trip, the gatekeeper applies graded admission penalties and records a probationary circuit state.
- Evacuation Buffer: a regional soft-reserve of capacity (timeboxed) to accept reconnecting KV-bearing requests during controlled drains. The buffer is sized by recent KV-preserve metrics and tenant churn heuristics.
- Probation state for circuits: newly-introduced transient state to allow a graceful rejoin window (configurable TTL) where requests are admitted at a reduced weight and prioritized into the evacuation buffer.
- Telemetry: new metrics (slo_gatekeeper.attenuation_ratio, evacuation_buffer.usage, circuit.probation_count) and traces for gate decisions. Event logs include decision_reason and source_signal for post-incident analysis.
- Feature flag: runtime.feature.flags.slo_gatekeeper (off by default). Emergency bypass for on-call: slo_gatekeeper.mode = emergency_bypass.

Design notes:
- Attenuation curve: cubic easing mapped from 0..1 intensity where intensity = normalized_slo_excess * min(1, duration / D). We cap attenuation to prevent starving fast-exit tenants.
- Buffer sizing: moving-window percentile of reconnecting token counts + 20% headroom. Buffer decays if unused to avoid orphaning capacity.
- Safety: when region-wide critical thresholds (latency or node pressure) are crossed, gatekeeper escalates to existing circuit breaker behavior rather than blocking it. We do not change hard-eviction heuristics, only insert an intermediate step.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for attenuation math and probation TTL logic.
- Integration tests simulate short spikes and long sustained overload; assert fewer circuit flips and improved p95 stability.
- Chaos test (local lab): introduce a 60s spike and measure rejoin throughput and KV-preserve miss rate.

Rollout plan:
1) Enable in canary region (one small cluster) with feature flag off-by-default; monitor new metrics.
2) After 48h of stable telemetry and no regression: enable in 25% of traffic (weighted routing).
3) Ramp to 100% over 72h with automated rollback if circuit flip rate or SLO breach increases > 15%.

Follow-ups / TODOs:
- Add an opt-in per-tenant policy to prefer immediate eviction for low-latency critical tenants.
- Dashboard and alert playbook for new metrics (ENG-2025).
- Explore integrating gatekeeper signals into autoscaler heuristics.

Notes for reviewers: This touches admission logic and routing weights. I've kept changes isolated to a new gatekeeper service with clear interfaces and backward-compatible protobuf changes. Small changes were added to the core admission path to consult the gatekeeper. Please pay attention to edge cases around probation TTL when a tenant repeatedly cycles (commented inline).
Marina Chen: Please add more telemetry around decision latency. Also we should ensure the buffer cannot be hijacked by low-cardinality tenants.
Samira Patel: Added evacuation_buffer.decisions_lat_ms and throttling per-tenant weight limits. See buffer.rs lines ~120-170.
Diego Alvarez: Concern about protobuf change compatibility. Is the gatekeeper API backward compatible with older sidecars?
Samira Patel: API is additive; older sidecars will just ignore the new optional field. Proto changes used optional fields and we added compat tests.
Owen Brooks: Integration test failed in first CI run; saw intermittent race on probation TTL. Please address.
Samira Patel: Fixed race by synchronizing probation update path and added a stress test. CI rerun green.
Marina Chen: Approved after the telemetry addition and the TTL fix.
Diego Alvarez: LGTM. Marking for merge.

Motivation: When the fleet experiences simultaneous transient pressure (node failures, region congestion, or unexpected warmpool exhaustion) the current burst admission policy aggressively rejects or hard-throttles burst requests which causes capacity cliffs for many tenants and regresses soft throughput guarantees for committed customers. This PR introduces a Proportional Burst-Degradation Controller (PBDC) that gracefully degrades best-effort burst capacity across eligible tenants in proportion to their recent burst consumption and SLA class, preserving committed throughput for high-tier tenants while avoiding binary hard-failures for everyone else.

What this changes: Adds a controller in the autoscaler plane that watches fleet utilization, warmpool headroom, and per-tenant burst ledgers. When the controller detects a rapid decline in available burst capacity it computes a proportional degradation vector that: 1) honors per-tenant minimum committed throughput (reservation floor), 2) uses a time-decayed recent-burst score to distribute remaining burst capacity, and 3) enforces a global safety floor to avoid starving system-critical background jobs. The controller publishes a compact policy blob to the gateway/allocator that is evaluated at request admission time.

Key behaviours: - Smooth decay: Degradation is applied over a short smoothing window (configurable, default 30s) to avoid sudden cliffing. - Tier-aware weighting: Tenants with higher reservation tiers get multiplicative priority but never exceed configured headroom caps. - Backfill safety: Opportunistic backfill requests (best-effort) are reduced proportionally before impacting reserved throughput. - Telemetry hooks: Emits proportional_degrader.summary, per-tenant.degraded_fraction_pct, and headroom_repartition events for downstream dashboards and alerts.

Tests and validation: Unit tests for the degradation allocator, scheduler integration tests exercising the gateway admission code path, and an e2e scenario that simulates a 25% sudden warmpool loss with 50 concurrent tenants. Performance microbench: controller loop 2.3ms median CPU time, and policy blob serialization < 1ms at 2000 tenants.

Operational notes: Feature gated behind runtime feature flag "proportionalBurstDegrader" and enabled in canary only. Default config conservative: smoothing_window=30s, min_committed_floor_pct=90, safety_floor=5% of global capacity. Runbook doc added.

Related: builds on prior utilization reporting work ENG-1680 (telemetry sampling) and coordinates with SUP-4123 incident postmortem to avoid repeated cliff events.

+}

+    // scale down best-effort tokens, preserve reserved path
+}

Ethan Cole: Overall direction looks good. Please add a test that asserts fairness across tenants with identical weights when global headroom is <10% (edge-case).
Mariana Ruiz: Need clarity on how this interacts with the per-route concurrency floor — can we guarantee isolation between low-latency routes and background bulk routes?
Liam O'Connor: Telemetry names look fine but prefer histograms for degraded_fraction_pct to capture distribution. Also add a dashboard panel for headroom_repartition events.
Priya Menon: Added the requested fairness test (tests/e2e/proportional_burst_degradation_test.go) and a unit test for the allocation normalization path.
Priya Menon: Updated admission_policy docs and explicitly excluded routes with low_latency=true from proportional backfill truncation; added config flag 'apply_to_background_only' (default true).
Priya Menon: Switched degraded_fraction to both gauge + histogram and hooked up new dashboard query in docs.
Introduce Proportional Burst-Degradation Controller: adds graceful, tier-aware reduction of best-effort burst capacity under fleet pressure. Feature gated; canary only by default. See docs/ops/proportional-burst-degrader.md for config and runbook.
Risk: misconfiguration may under-allocate opportunistic traffic causing higher p99 for some background endpoints. Mitigation: conservative defaults, canary rollout, quick toggle via feature flag, and an automatic rollback hook if headroom_repartition crosses alert threshold.
Schedule canary rollout to two regions next week
Create dashboard for proportional_degrader.summary and headroom_repartition
Hook metric to automatic rollback runbook

Context: Developers have asked for a less opinionated credential lifecycle inside the SDKs so embedding token rotation and stream surface concerns in one place is easier to reason about and test. This PR extracts a lightweight Credential Orchestrator, introduces small per-language adapters, and trims blocking points in streaming consumers to improve ergonomics and parity across Python, TypeScript, and Go. Changes are intentionally conservative: the public top-level client surface remains stable where possible and a compatibility shim is provided for legacy TokenProvider shapes. Motivation: reduce duplication of token refresh logic across SDKs, make stream iteration non-blocking during reauth windows, and give ops teams telemetry hooks to attribute auth-induced latencies. Summary of changes: 1) Introduced credentials/orchestrator module (core): centralizes refresh policy, backoff profiles, jittering, and metrics tagging. 2) Added per-sdk adapters: python/adapters/credential_adapter.py, typescript/src/credentialOrchestrator.ts, go/cred/orchestrator.go. Adapters implement a small well-documented interface and are wired to each SDK's session manager. 3) Streaming ergonomics: made generator/async iterator resume non-blocking during credential renewal by allowing an in-flight request to complete while a background refresh is performed; added explicit ResumeAfterRefresh hint for clients that need deterministic ordering. 4) Backoff/retry alignment: consolidated retry presets used for auth failures across SDKs and added telemetry counters for reauth attempts and durations. 5) Shims and migration helpers: legacy TokenProvider adapter for backward compatibility and migration notes. 6) Tests and CI: added cross-sdk unit tests (mocked token server) and e2e smoke tests for streaming reconnect scenarios. 7) Version bumps: Python SDK -> 1.12.0, TypeScript SDK -> 1.28.0, Go SDK -> 1.8.3. Files changed (high level): - python/sdk/session.py (refactor: delegate token lifecycle to orchestrator) - python/sdk/adapters/credential_adapter.py (new) - python/tests/test_stream_reauth.py (new) - typescript/src/client.ts (hook in orchestrator) - typescript/src/credentialOrchestrator.ts (new) - typescript/test/stream.spec.ts (new) - go/sdk/session.go (wiring) - go/cred/orchestrator.go (new) - docs/migrations/credential-orchestrator.md (new) - examples/streaming/reauth-demo/* (updated example flow) - scripts/ci/mock-token-server/* (test helper) Design notes and rationale: The orchestrator exposes a minimal surface: getActiveToken(), leaseToken(durationHintMs), onReauth hook registration. SDK clients call leaseToken before starting long-running streams or can subscribe to onReauth to get fine-grained signals. We intentionally did not introduce a global blocking refresh on every request to avoid adding per-request latency. The ResumeAfterRefresh hint is optional: runtimes that require strict ordering can opt-in. Telemetry: every reauth attempt emits credential.renew.* metrics (count, duration_ms, result). This surfaces when auth is a dominant contributor to tail latency. Backwards compatibility: legacy TokenProvider objects are accepted by the adapter; a console deprecation notice will be emitted (30 days) when the adapter is used. Migration: docs/migrations/credential-orchestrator.md contains a short recipe: 1) Replace TokenProvider with CredentialOrchestrator adapter 2) Call leaseToken before starting persistent streams 3) Optionally wire onReauth for in-application state reconciliation. Checklist: - [x] Core orchestrator impl and adapters for py/ts/go - [x] Unit tests for adapter logic - [x] Streaming non-blocking reauth smoke tests - [x] Telemetry hooks and metrics naming - [x] Docs and migration guide - [x] Version bumps and changelogs Compatibility notes: No forced API rename for top-level client methods. Some internal session manager method names were changed (session.acquire_token -> session.lease_token) and shims are present for two release cycles. Rollout plan: staged rollout (feature flag) to internal dogfood org for two weeks, then enable by default for GA. Related: ENG-7123 (auth stability), ENG-7190 (streaming ergonomics). Impact on running services: low risk; added tests and canarying recommended. CI: all checks passed except one flaky TS test that required an additional retry; retried and green. Merge: squash-merged to main. Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the shims (python/sdk/compat_legacy_token.py) and the handshake semantics in TS/Go adapters. If you are an integrator maintainers for a downstream embedder, follow the migration guide in docs/migrations/credential-orchestrator.md.
Miguel Santos: can we avoid leaking the orchestrator type into the public client surface? Suggest exposing an opaque factory and keep concrete type internal.
Aisha Kapoor: agreed, adapted—exposed only a CredentialProvider interface and kept the concrete orchestrator in internal modules. Updated docs to show factory usage.
Hannah Lee: TS test fails on Node 14 with async iterator ordering—suggest a small delay in the mock server; also add an explicit test for ordering when ResumeAfterRefresh is used.
Aisha Kapoor: added ordering test and adjusted mock server to be deterministic under Node 14; CI re-run green.
Raj Patel: telemetry metric names look good. Please document the tag sets for attribution (sdk.language, transport, op=reauth).
Aisha Kapoor: added telemetry tagging to implementation and docs.
Performance team (automated): microbenchmark shows 2-3% lower median latency on streaming happy path due to reduced per-request checks.
Introduce Credential Orchestrator to centralize token refresh and retry logic. Streaming consumers can opt into non-blocking reauth behavior via leaseToken/ResumeAfterRefresh. SDK versions bumped: py 1.12.0, ts 1.28.0, go 1.8.3. Backwards-compatible shims provided. See docs/migrations/credential-orchestrator.md for migration steps.
Enable feature flag 'orchestrator-experimental' for 2 weeks in dogfood org. Watch metric credential.renew.count and credential.renew.duration_ms for spike; threshold alert if renew duration 95th percentile > 1000ms.

payload.body: Background and motivation: our presubmit lanes have grown organically and incur a large fanout of lint/test runners for every PR. This increases queue times and makes fast feedback unpredictable for small changes. This PR introduces a lightweight CI proxy (go-based) that centralizes presubmit routing decisions, performs change-aware fanout, and exposes a compact presubmit graph to downstream runners. Primary goals: (1) reduce unnecessary runner fanout for doc/style-only changes; (2) provide a single place to implement staged lanes (fast, medium, full); (3) make release hooks (signing, artifact tagging) easier to attach to an orchestration point. What this PR does: - Adds cmd/ci-proxy: a small Go binary (~600 LOC) that ingests GitHub check-run webhooks or simulated presubmit events and computes a presubmit graph based on changed paths, labels, and a new manifest (ci/presubmit-manifest.yaml). The proxy emits a compact request (route) to runner agents instead of fanout-ing to all jobs. - Introduces ci/presubmit-manifest.yaml: declarative mapping of path globs to presubmit lanes (fast/medium/full), with metadata for dependency groups and required release hooks. - Reworks GitHub workflow templates: .github/workflows/presubmit-proxy-dispatch.yml (dispatches events to the proxy) and updates to several composite actions to accept the proxy route. - Adds a lightweight Go-based runner shim (tools/runner-shim) that understands the proxy route and maps it to existing GH actions or remote executors. - Updates docs: docs/ci/README-presubmit-proxy.md and examples in redwood-quickstarts/ci-example. - Small dependency bumps in go.mod for github.com/google/go-github and sigs.k8s.io/yaml to support webhook parsing and manifest handling. Compatibility and safety: - Proxy respects existing skip conditions (ci skip, label-based skips) and defaults to conservative fanout (full) when in doubt. - No change to protected branch policies; workflow permissions unchanged. - All changes are behind the feature flag CI_PROXY_ENABLED and the proxy is disabled by default for production until rollout. Rollout plan (brief): 1) Deploy proxy in staging and run against nightly PRs for a week (no effect on real checks). 2) Enable proxy for opt-in repos/groups via a repo setting; collect telemetry (fanout reduction, queue time). 3) Flip default to enabled for small repos after 2 weeks, then expand. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for manifest parsing and route resolution - [x] Integration test harness for proxy -> runner-shim roundtrip - [x] Updated workflow templates and docs - [x] Telemetry hooks (fanout.count, presubmit.latency) - [x] Backwards-compat shim so runners that don't support proxy still receive full fanout Commits summary: - feat(ci-proxy): initial proxy command and manifest model - feat(runner-shim): implement route consumer and GH actions adapter - chore(ci): add presubmit-manifest and update workflow templates - refactor(workflows): reduce duplicated composite inputs, wire proxy route - deps(go): bump go-github and sigs.k8s.io/yaml for webhook and manifest handling - test(ci): add unit and integration tests, add test fixtures Files changed (high level): ["cmd/ci-proxy/main.go", "internal/manifest/manifest.go", "tools/runner-shim/main.go", "ci/presubmit-manifest.yaml", ".github/workflows/presubmit-proxy-dispatch.yml", ".github/workflow-templates/presubmit-template.yml", "docs/ci/README-presubmit-proxy.md", "redwood-quickstarts/ci-example/.github/workflows/ci-example.yml", "go.mod", "go.sum", "scripts/telemetry-emit.sh"]

payload.body:
Motivation:
We observe noisy tenant-level signals and brittle dashboard comparisons during rollouts of runtime changes. Alert thresholds tuned to absolute token-cost or latency buckets don't translate across tenants with different invocation shapes. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) a lightweight cross-tenant metric normalizer service that produces stable, per-tenant normalization scores (z-like and rank-based percentiles) for core token/latency/cost metrics; (2) a synthetic-token playback generator that replays deterministic token-shaped invocations to validate dashboards and simulate alerts under controlled conditions.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds observability/metric-normalizer: a service that consumes routed metrics, maintains sliding-window summaries, and emits normalized time series (tenant_norm_{metric}) plus normalization metadata (sample_count, shard_version).
- Adds synth_playback CLI and library to generate deterministic token traces from recorded prompt shapes and replay them into the ingest pipeline for dashboard replay and alert simulation.
- Wires the normalizer into the metric ingest proxy so dashboards and alerts can opt into normalized series without changing collectors.
- Adds a set of Grafana dashboards and a simulation page (dashboards/normalized-metrics.json + dashboards/synthetic-playback.json) and a small alert-simulation harness (tests/alert_simulator.py) used by SRE to estimate expected alert noise per tenant.
- Adds unit + e2e tests and a Helm values change to gate rollout with a feature-flag.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Normalization semantics: the service emits two streams per metric: a rank_percentile (P0-100) using an approximate t-digest and a z_score computed against a rolling mean+std over a 6-hour window. For low-sample tenants (<200 invocations in window) we emit a sparse flag and fall back to global percentiles to avoid volatility.
- Storage: we keep sketches per tenant with aggressive TTL + compacting to bound memory. We chose t-digest for percentiles because it compresses heavy tails well and supports merge.
- Performance: normalizer runs as a horizontally scalable service with sharding by tenant hash; ingestion cost added ~2-3% CPU in benchmarks with 1k tenants per shard. The synth_playback is intentionally single-threaded for deterministic replay; a parallel mode exists behind a flag for load testing.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for normalization math and sketch merges (tests/normalizer_test.py).
- Integration smoke: replayed 10k synthetic invocations representing three customer shapes; validated normalized dashboards match expected rank ordering and z-scores move consistently when we inject latency shifts.
- Alert sim: tests/alert_simulator.py runs replay and computes FPR/TPR estimates for current alert rules; included a short report that influenced an alert tuning change for token-cost-95 alert.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flagged behind helm values.observability.enableMetricNormalizer = false by default.
- Canary rollout to 2 internal tenants for 48h, then opt-in for more tenants using route-level annotation.
- Monitoring: added internal dashboards and health checks; will watch sample_count_sparse rate and normalized series deviation.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration replay tests
- [x] Dashboards added and linked in docs
- [x] Feature flag + Helm values
- [x] Load bench (small) and memory caps

Notes for reviewers: please focus on the low-sample fallback semantics, the memory TTL choices, and the API shape for consumers (tenant_norm_{metric} + tenant_norm_meta labels). The PR contains a migration note in docs/observability/metric-normalization.md describing backwards compatibility and consumer adoption steps.
Samir: Can you clarify the fallback when tenant sample_count < 200? It was noisy in local runs - suggest exposing the threshold via config.
Ava: Addressed - threshold is now configurable via ENV and helm values; added docs section 'low-sample fallback' and tests showing behavior.
Lena: t-digest merge correctness looks good but we should cap bucket growth under pathological distributions. Request: add compaction pass every 5m.
Ava: Added compaction loop and a unit test (compaction_test). Memory bounded in bench runs.
Diego: Please add a feature-flag and an opt-in header so we can roll out incrementally; also include metrics for 'sparse_fallback_rate'.
Ava: Implemented X-Use-Norm opt-in header and added 'normalizer.sparse_fallback_rate' metric. Updated dashboards to visualize it.
Samir: Approve after small lint fix (line length) and a note on TLS cert rotation in helm values.
Ava: Fixed lint and added cert rotation note to docs.
Adds a tenant-aware metric normalizer and a deterministic synthetic token playback tool to enable reproducible dashboard replays and alert simulations. Feature-flagged rollout and dashboards included. Impact: observability teams can compare normalized metrics across tenants and run deterministic alert noise simulations.
Use tools/replay/fixtures to run synth_playback against a staging ingest endpoint; enable helm value observability.enableMetricNormalizer=true for validation. Watch normalizer.sparse_fallback_rate and heap under load.

payload.body:
Fix: Add transient heartbeat smoothing and controlled fallback timer to reduce noisy regional failovers during short probe storms. No customer-facing API changes.
Motivation: We observed an increase in short heartbeat spikes (1-5s) from probe jitter and transient network blips which triggered regional fallback and aggressive egress shed behavior. This caused cascading capacity shifts and customer-visible tail latency spikes. This hotpatch introduces two cooperating pieces: a transparent fallback timer in the routing/failover layer and a heartbeat surge mender that smooths ephemeral probe bursts. Design: 1) Transparent fallback timer: adds a per-route ephemeral timer (default 3s) that delays triggering a hard fallback/circuit trip for transient degradations while still recording candidate degraded events. If the degradation persists past the timer, existing fallback logic runs unchanged. The timer is feature-flagged and can be tuned per-tenant. 2) Heartbeat surge mender: a lightweight smoothing stage sitting between health probes and the failover decision engine. It applies a sliding-window median+decay correction to heartbeat latency samples and emits a corrected health score. This reduces sensitivity to 1-5s probe noise without masking real regressions. Changes included: - Routing: route/fallback/timer.go (new) — implements timer lifecycle and tenant override. - Health: probes/surge_mender.go (new) — smoothing algorithm, metrics, and tests. - Config: config/flags.yaml — feature flag and per-tenant defaults. - Telemetry: telemetry/heartbeat_metrics.go — new metrics: heartbeat_mender_adjustments, fallback_timer_skips, fallback_timer_triggers. - Tests: unit tests for timer and mender logic, integration harness extension to simulate probe storms. Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to staging and run synthetic probe-storm scenarios (completed). 2) Canary in production traffic: 10% of routing planes for 24h (observed reduction in rollback events by ~68%). 3) Gradual rollout to 50% then 100% over 48h each with automated guardrail checks. Feature flag allows immediate rollback. Backout plan: flip feature flag off; routing will immediately stop using the timer and smoothing stage and fall back to previous behavior. Also revert is a single-service config change, no DB migrations. Observability: added dashboards under "Routing / Fallback" for the new metrics and an alert if fallback_timer_triggers exceeds historical baseline by 3x in a sliding 5m window. Compatibility: fully backwards compatible — the fallback path after the timer is identical to prior logic. Tests: unit (coverage 91% for new modules), integration (probe storm simulations), e2e scripted canary that validated SLO preservation. Security: no secrets or permissions changes. Impact: reduces noisy short-lived cross-region failovers and lowers tail latency during transient network events; small added memory for per-route timer state (~<1MB per plane). Related: SUP-4372 documented customer incident reproduced in test harness. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in ENG-5782 - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Telemetry and dashboards - [x] Feature flag - [x] Canary rollout - [x] Post-merge monitoring on-call runbook Notes: tuned default timer to 3s after testing on three representative customers. Longer defaults delayed legitimate failovers in stress tests; shorter defaults did not sufficiently suppress churn. We allow per-tenant override for edge cases.
Diego Morales: Could the timer hide real partial outages? Request adding a guard that increments a counter if failures occur while timer active. Aisha: Added fallback_timer_triggers metric and unit that records events when the timer expires — included in telemetry section.
Priya Raman: Suggest lowering default to 2s for small customers. Aisha: We tested 2s and it didn't sufficiently reduce churn for our mid-market cohort; added tenant override and documented tradeoffs in docs/runbooks/fallback_timer.md.
James O'Connor: Please add an e2e assert that ensures requests during a timer window are counted as degraded for SLO reckoning. Aisha: Integration harness updated to mark candidate degraded events and emitted metrics for SLO evaluation.
SRE: Verified canary results in us-east-1 and saw no missed real outages in 72h noisy-wire tests. Approved for merge.
QA: Found a race in timer shutdown when route deleted; fix added in commit 3 (timer goroutine shutdown and waitgroup).
Squash-merged into main after successful canary and CI green. Post-merge: on-call observed reduced regional failovers; no rollbacks required.
payload.title: Transparent fallback timer and heartbeat surge mender (hotpatch)

payload.body:
Context and motivation: We observed repeated oscillation in tenant-level circuit states during regional egress spikes: regional circuits would open/close rapidly, causing cascading failovers and repeated SLO blips across tenants. This is most visible for tenants with bursty traffic spanning multiple regions (see ENG-1482). The change: Introduce two cooperating components: 1) circuit-conciliator (a lightweight cross-region reconciler) that maintains a small consistent view of circuit buckets and enforces a damped decision window so circuits do not flip faster than a tuned hysteresis period; 2) soft-shed ETA harmonizer which augments load-shedding percentages with an estimated time-to-clear (ETA) signal derived from queue backlog and recent processing rate. Together they produce a gradual, probabilistic soft-shed that ramps down traffic instead of immediate binary circuit transitions. Implementation notes: - circuit-conciliator runs as part of the runtime control-plane. It exposes a reconciliation API and a local policy engine that prefers the highest-safety (more-shed) state but will respect a short keepalive to avoid re-opening until ETA improves. - ETA harmonizer computes a per-slot ETA using exponential smoothing over backlog and tokens/sec and exposes a confidence score used to modulate shed strength. - We added a compact protobuf for cross-region conciliator messages and a small persistence layer to retain transient circuit epochs for up to the configured hysteresis window. - Default tuning is conservative off-by-default for Dedicated customers; hosted rollout will be gradual and behind a feature flag. Risks and mitigations: - New cross-region messages increase control-plane chatter: we limit fanout to bucket-summary deltas and compress updates. - Mis-tuning could over-shed traffic; we ship with telemetry (see metrics/conciliator_* and harmonizer_*), end-to-end e2e test coverage, and a rollback toggle in the config. The description below includes a small illustrative snippet (not the full diff) to show the reconciliation loop logic. Reconciliation snippet: "for each bucket: if remote_state.consensus_shed > local_shed and time_since_change > min_hysteresis: adopt remote_shed else keep local with decay" Related work items: ENG-1482 (investigation), ENG-1501 (SLO-stability epic), SUP-4321 (customer incident that triggered hotfix).
Adds a new circuit conciliator service to coordinate circuit state across regions and a soft-shed ETA harmonizer that smooths load-shedding decisions to avoid rapid oscillation. Improves regional failover stability and reduces customer-visible SLO blips under transient overloads.
Luca Fernandez (reviewer): Nice approach. Two questions: 1) can you clarify how the conciliator chooses tie-breaks when regions disagree? 2) we should ensure the persistence window doesn't exceed our leader-election TTLs.
Asha Menon (author): Tie-breaks favor the more-conservative state (higher shed). The proto includes an epoch counter; conciliator picks higher epoch unless both epochs are within hysteresis window, then picks conservative. Persistence window default set to 120s and is bounded by leader-election TTL - documented in defaults.yaml.
Maya Patel (reviewer): Integration tests look good. One nit: can we add a small e2e test covering an alternating spike pattern (region A spike then region B) to validate no reopen flip-flopping?
Asha Menon (author): Added tests/integration/test_conciliator_end_to_end.py which simulates alternating spikes and asserts at-most-one state transition per hysteresis window. Also added bench to reproduce scenario.
Evan Leung (approver): Verified on staging. Observed 3x reduction in reopen frequency during simulated cross-region bursts. CI perf bench had a flaky test that I reran; passing now. Approving for merge.
Security (comment): throttling decisions use bucket ids only; no tenant PII is transmitted. Confirmed encryption is applied for control-plane proto in transit.
QA (comment): added two minor test failures that were fixed in commit c3d01aa; all passing now.

Motivation: customers need easier correlation between token-level cost signals, prefetch/warmup events, and downstream alert routing to reduce oncall noise and speed RCA. This PR introduces an invocation-context telemetry hub that normalizes invocation metadata, emits a small set of canonical tags for cost/latency traces, and exposes a topology mapping used by alerting rules to route incidents to the appropriate SLO domain. Changes include a lightweight context serializer, a new observability index service, dashboards for context-cohort heatmaps and prefetch effectiveness, and an alert topology that de-duplicates noisy token-level alerts. The description below summarizes the work, tests, and rollout plan. Work items: 1) add invocation context schema and serializer with backwards-safe defaulting; 2) instrument runtime to attach context-id and warmup flags to spans and metrics; 3) add observability-index service that ingests context tags and produces cohort rollups used by dashboards and alert rules; 4) add three Grafana dashboards: invocation-context-cohort, prefetch-warmup-effectiveness, and alert-topology-insights; 5) provide migration script and compatibility shim so older agents continue to report without schema changes; 6) add E2E replay test and unit coverage for index service. Rollout plan: deploy index service to staging behind a feature flag for one week, enable telemetry consumers in read-only mode, validate cohort alignment with synthetic replay, then flip feature flag and enable alert topology for a subset of tenants, monitor noisiness for 72 hours and iterate. Related: Linear ENG-3221, ENG-3302. Links: internal runbook https://linear.app/redwood/ENG-3221, dashboard proto https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/ctx-cohort. This description contains the full context and checklist.
feat(telemetry): add invocation-context schema and serializer
chore(runtime): attach context-id to trace/span metadata
feat(index): implement lightweight observability-index service and HTTP ingestion endpoint
docs: add dashboard definitions and runbook notes
test: add e2e replay test and unit coverage for index service
ci: update integration pipeline to start index service in tests
Oliver Shaw: Nice consolidation. A couple of nits: can we avoid adding new top-level envs; prefer feature flags via configmap. Also request stronger validation on context schema versions.
Nina Patel: Thanks, addressed in commits feat(index): add schema validation and moved feature flag to helm values. PTAL.
Priya Menon: Index API looks clean. Two questions: (1) can the cohort rollups be downsampled to reduce memory footprint? and (2) how do we handle index rehydration after restarts?
Nina Patel: Answered inline: rollups use reservoir sampling with tunable window and rehydration uses a compact snapshot via S3 with incremental replay. Added tests for snapshot restore.
Ethan Ross: CI showed a flaky integration failure on first run (timeout against index ingestion). Retriggered and passed. Approving pending small docs tweak.
Ethan Ross: docs tweak resolved. Approving.
Add invocation-context telemetry hub that normalizes and indexes invocation tags for better correlation between token cost, warmup/prefetch signals and alert routing. New dashboards and an alert topology reduce noisy token-level alerts. Rollout gated behind feature flag.
Added unit tests for serializer and index, integration e2e replay against synthetic traffic, and staging shadow run for 72h. Observability smoke tests included. No customer-facing API changes when flag is off.
Risk: increased cardinality if clients send arbitrary context keys. Mitigation: serializer enforces canonical tag whitelist and truncation, index enforces TTL and reservoir sampling, and feature flag allows quick rollback.
1) Enable index service in staging behind feature flag for 7d. 2) Validate cohort rollups using synthetic replay and compare to baseline telemetry. 3) Flip read-only mode off for a 10% tenant sample. 4) Monitor alert noise and token-cost attribution for 72h. 5) Gradually expand to 100% and remove compatibility shim after 30d.

Motivation: progressive canaries + A/B experiments at Redwood currently use stepwise traffic increments with static holdpoints. For workloads where signal-to-noise ratio decays slowly we saw either long rollouts or too-frequent rollbacks. This PR adds an "annealed traffic-gradient controller" that adjusts traffic ramp rate per-cohort based on an online confidence estimate and a short 'cohort smoke' validation phase before integrating traffic metrics into SLO gates.

Design summary: the controller exposes a new rollout strategy type (strategy: 'annealed_gradient') that: 1) assigns target cohorts (percent buckets) and a per-cohort initial ramp_rate; 2) runs a lightweight cohort smoke validation (synthetic queries or small real-traffic shadowing) for a configurable window (default 30s) to bootstrap a confidence score; 3) uses an exponential decay on the confidence signal while ramping traffic so that early instability yields slower ramps but stable cohorts accelerate automatically; 4) integrates with existing safety gates (latency, error-rate, quality regression) and supports immediate drain/rollback if thresholds are breached.

Config changes and API: added RolloutStrategy schema extension: "annealed_gradient": {"initial_step_pct","min_step_pct","max_step_pct","cohort_smoke": {"enabled","duration_s","synthetic_profile"},"confidence_decay_half_life_s"}. Exposed via the same rollout CRD and Redwood Console UI. Backwards compatible: existing strategies unaffected.

Implementation notes: core logic implemented in rollout/controller/annealed_gradient_controller.go with a separate confidence estimator module (rollout/estimator/confidence.go). Lightweight smoke harness implemented in rollout/smoke/runner.go which can be toggled to only shadow traffic for Private deployments. New observability metrics: rollout_cohort_confidence{rollout_id,cohort}, rollout_smoke_pass_ratio, rollout_ramp_rate_pct. Added tracing spans for smoke->gate evaluation path.

Testing: unit tests for estimator and smoke harness (rollout/estimator/*, rollout/smoke/*), integration test that runs an end-to-end simulated A/B with a flaky latency generator to verify ramp deceleration and rollback detection (integration/annealed_gradient_sim_test.go). Manual QA: staged on dedicated QA cluster using an experimental rollout (linear ENG-4823 test plan).

Migration and rollout: feature-flagged under "annealedGradient". Default off for production customers; set to on for internal canaries and opt-in customers. No migration steps required for existing rollout records.

Checklist:
- [x] Controller implementation
- [x] Config schema + API surface
- [x] Unit & integration tests
- [x] Console UI stub + docs note
- [x] Metrics & tracing
- [x] Feature flag gating

Related work: builds on prior cohort-aware controllers and safe-holdpoint logic (see ENG-2712 and PRs for staged-rollouts). See linked Linear ENG-4823 for experiment matrix and expected SLO behavior.

Risk notes: the smoke harness performs short synthetic traffic; if customers opt into synthetic profiles without rate limits it could add noise — defaults are conservative. Confidence estimator uses rolling windows so there is potential for slow adaptation on very low-traffic cohorts; documented in release notes.

How to exercise locally: makefile target 'make test-integration-rollout' runs harness + local simulator; console toggles available on feature flags page.

Merge notes: squash-merge, update release notes with an example rollout YAML and a migration paragraph.
Arjun Patel: Nice addition — can you add a short comment on why exponential decay was chosen vs 1/t? Also add a unit test for the half-life behavior.
Maya Lopez: Reply: exponential decay chosen to give tunable memory (half-life) and simpler parameterization for operators. Added test half_life_test.go covering expected behavior.
Lena Fischer: Request change: surface a max_synthetic_qps cap in smoke harness config to avoid accidental load.
Maya Lopez: ACK, added max_smoke_qps with default 5 and a validation check in API layer.
Diego Marquez: Approve after CI passes and docs updated.
Introduce 'annealed_gradient' rollout strategy: supports cohort smoke validation and confidence-decay-driven ramping to reduce unnecessary rollouts/rollbacks. Feature-flagged behind 'annealedGradient' and disabled by default. See docs/rollouts/annealed-gradient.md for examples.
Feature is disabled by default; enable per-cluster via feature-flag. Watch rollout_cohort_confidence and rollout_smoke_pass_ratio metrics for initial deployments. Ensure cluster allows smoke harness qps (default cap 5).

Motivation: We see a recurring class of incidents where downstream model hosts or network egress introduce transient stalls that cause the gateway streaming proxy to retry/choke, which in turn amplifies tail latency and leads to degraded fncall/tool-call behavior in OpenAI-compat mode. This PR introduces a lightweight congestion-pacing layer in the streaming proxy plus a structured fncall failsafe that gracefully degrades tool call sequences when streaming is unstable. Summary of changes: 1) Add a congestion pacer (egress pacing token bucket + adaptive holdback) that smooths bursty egress from the proxy and prevents immediate retransmit storms; pacing parameters are workload-aware and derived from route profiles. 2) Add a fncall failsafe path: when the stream stalls beyond a configurable threshold, the gateway will atomically complete the structured function call with a best-effort buffered payload and mark the stream degraded via X-Redwood-Stream-Status header to allow clients to fallback. 3) Tighten route-level payload quotas and move per-route in-memory buffers into a capped slab allocator to avoid head-of-line OOMs. 4) Add observability: streaming pacing metrics, per-route degrade counters, and structured-fncall fallback histogram. 5) Tests: add unit and integration tests for pacing behavior, fncall fallback semantics, and OpenAI-compat regression tests. Backwards compatibility: The OpenAI-compat read/write semantics are preserved; clients will see a new response header when a fallback occurred. This is opt-in via route flag route_config.enable_stream_pacing (defaults to true for safety). Rollout plan: merge to main, canary to region-us-east-1 with routing weight 2% for 24h, monitor pacing_* metrics and structured_fncall_fallback_rate. If fallback_rate > 0.5% sustained for 1h, auto-rollback flag will be triggered. Implementation notes: the pacer lives in gateway/proxy/egress_pacer.rs and is invoked by the stream buffer loop; we selected an exponentially-smoothed target rate using recent egress success latency. The fncall failsafe reuses the existing structured-output serializer but forces a close-of-stream marker and emits a synthetic function-complete event to ensure downstream consumers (and SDKs) receive a final consistent payload. Testing summary: unit tests cover edge cases (zero-sized payloads, rapid connect/disconnect), e2e integration runs against a model simulator that flips egress stalls; local perf lab shows 18-34% reduction in tail retry storms. CI: all checks passed after two reruns of the flaky e2e streaming test. Docs: brief entry added to docs/openai_compat.md explaining the header and route flag. Related work: follows up on ENG-1304 (streaming robustness) and pairs with the canary autoscaler circuit from ENG-1421. If anything is unclear reach out to @priya for design walkthrough.
Gateway: add congestion pacing to streaming proxy and a structured-function-call failsafe. Improves stability for long-lived OpenAI-compat streams and reduces noisy retries. No public API contract changes; internal routing and buffering knobs added.
Ethan Brooks: The pacer looks good overall, can we add a small benchmark showing CPU overhead? Also please ensure the default pacing values don't throttle small latency-sensitive routes.
Priya Nair (author): Added microbench in integration/perf and ensured pacing is disabled for routes with max_latency_sla < 50ms. See latest commit b3c7a81.
Maya Chen: The fncall failsafe header is helpful. Please document the exact header semantics and the SDK behavior we expect so clients can handle fallback deterministically.
Priya Nair: Docs added to docs/openai_compat.md and added a test asserting the header is present for fallback cases.
Diego Alvarez: Verified metrics emission and added a suggestion to emit a sampled payload size distribution for paced streams. Approved after CI passes.
CI Bot: e2e/streaming failed on first run (timeout); rerun succeeded. All checks green.
payload.title: Introduce congestion-pacing and structured fncall failsafe in gateway to stabilize streaming and OpenAI-compat
