Summary: Introduces a canonical node readiness state model in the control plane and exposes internal (operator-only) APIs to read and mutate readiness for a fleet node. This is the first control-plane building block for provision-to-ready automation (Allocated -> Provisioning -> Validating -> Ready / Quarantined) as defined in ADR-017. The API is intentionally scoped to internal tooling + orchestrators; it is not customer-facing.

Motivation: Today, readiness is inferred indirectly from a mix of kube/node condition signals and ad-hoc fleet scripts. That makes it difficult to enforce gating (e.g. “don’t add nodes to serving pools until validations pass”) and to surface actionable failure reasons. This PR makes readiness explicit, durable, and auditable in the control plane.

What’s in this PR: (1) Data model + migration: Adds fleet_readiness_nodes and fleet_readiness_events tables. Nodes store current_state, last_transition_at, last_heartbeat_at, and a small set of normalized fields for failure_reason_code + failure_reason_message. Events are append-only transition records to support debugging/SLI calculations later. (2) State machine + transitions: Adds a small state transition helper that enforces allowed transitions (Allocated -> Provisioning -> Validating -> Ready; any state -> Quarantined; Quarantined -> Provisioning only via explicit override). Transition validation is done in the control plane; clients cannot write arbitrary states. (3) Internal APIs: Adds REST endpoints under /internal/fleet/readiness: GET /nodes?pool_id=&region=&state= for listing, GET /nodes/{node_id} for detail, POST /nodes/{node_id}/transition for state transitions, and POST /nodes/{node_id}/heartbeat to record agent/orchestrator heartbeats. These endpoints are behind internal authz and require the fleet-operator role. (4) Authz + auditability: Adds authorization checks for all mutate endpoints; read endpoints require fleet-readonly or fleet-operator. Emits structured audit logs for transition actions (actor, node_id, old_state, new_state, reason_code). (5) Basic integration tests: Adds request/response contract tests for the internal API and migration coverage for the new tables.

Not included / follow-ups: This PR does not yet store validation artifacts or per-step durations (coming in a follow-up PR). It also doesn’t enforce readiness gates for joining serving pools (separate PR). Metric emission is minimal here; observability hooks land after API stabilization.

Risk/rollout: Low-risk in production because the new tables and endpoints are additive and unused by default. We will enable write traffic only from the provisioning orchestrator behind a feature flag once downstream is ready. Migration is backwards compatible and safe to run online.

References: ADR-017 (readiness state machine), ENG-4822 (implementation), Slack thread: eng-platform alignment on naming + fields. Tested locally with Postgres + integration test suite; verified authz behavior with internal roles.

Checklist: - [x] DB migration is additive + reversible - [x] Authz checks for all endpoints - [x] Integration tests for transition constraints - [x] Audit log fields reviewed with SRE - [x] OpenAPI updated for internal endpoints
Ethan Park (review): Can we make sure only the orchestrator can call transition, not any internal service with a generic token? Also, naming: prefer current_state over readiness_state to avoid confusion with k8s readiness.
Benji Okafor (author): Updated authz to require fleet-operator for transitions; read-only role can list/detail. Renamed column + API field to current_state throughout.

Jordan Lee (review): Transition rules: should Quarantined -> Provisioning be allowed only with an explicit override flag + actor recorded. Also, allow any -> Quarantined is OK, but ensure we prevent Ready -> Validating regressions unless forced.
Benji Okafor (author): Implemented override_required for Quarantined -> Provisioning and blocked Ready -> Validating without override. Transition endpoint now requires {"override": true} for those cases and logs it in audit.

Rafael Mendes (SRE): Please add an audit log entry for all state changes including old/new and actor. Also, avoid storing long failure blobs; keep it short and link to external logs later.
Benji Okafor (author): Added structured audit logger call on every transition. failure_reason_message capped at 512 chars; longer details should live in validation artifacts (follow-up).

Allison Grant (observability): Future-proof: include last_transition_at and last_heartbeat_at as timestamps for SLIs. Also index by pool_id/region/current_state for dashboards.
Benji Okafor (author): Added timestamps and composite index (pool_id, region, current_state).
payload.title: Control plane: add fleet readiness states + internal API

Motivation: Reduce cross-language friction when wiring credentials into streaming flows and make small ergonomic wins for consumers that iterate over incremental chunks. This PR flattens the credential input shapes across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs, introduces a small set of variadic stream helper primitives (chunked_iter/streamBatch/StreamChunks) to simplify common chunking and backpressure patterns, and harmonizes retry defaults for auth-adjacent transient failures. Design summary: 1) Credential shape flattened: replace the nested {credentials: {token: ..., source: ...}} envelope with top-level fields (api_key, token_provider_hint, refresh_scope) in all SDK constructors and callsites for streaming helpers. The change is implemented as a thin compatibility shim that prefers the new flat fields while accepting the old envelope for one release cycle. 2) Variadic stream helpers: added chunked_iter(chunk_size, max_pending) in Python, streamBatch(batchSize, maxInflight) in TypeScript, and StreamChunks(ctx, size) in Go. These helpers encapsulate simple buffering + backpressure hints and return the same typed streaming envelope across languages to make cross-language examples consistent. 3) Retry parity: tuned the auth retry policy to be latency-aware (short default hedging window for streams, tighter backoff for one-off requests) and aligned telemetry tags across SDKS so server-side routing and canarying can be coordinated. Compatibility & migration: existing callsites will continue to work because constructors accept the legacy envelope; a deprecation warning is emitted at runtime. Consumers are encouraged to migrate to the flat parameters to remove ambiguity when composing credential providers. To migrate: - Python: replace Client(credentials=...) with Client(api_key=..., token_provider_hint=...) - TypeScript: new ApiClient({ apiKey, tokenHint }) - Go: NewClient(ctx, ClientOptions{APIKey: "...", TokenHint: "..."}). API snippets: Python: client = Client(api_key="${REDWOOD_KEY}") for chunk in chunked_iter(stream, 512): process(chunk) TypeScript: const c = new ApiClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY }); for await (const batch of streamBatch(resp, 4)) { /* ... */ } Go: cl, _ := newClient(ctx, ClientOptions{APIKey: key}) for ch := range StreamChunks(ctx, resp, 256) { // handle ch } Rollout plan: staged deploy. Server accepts both old and new shapes. SDKs ship with deprecation warnings for one major release and docs updated with migration examples. Canary: internal telemetry flagged for 72h and two customer tenants opt-in for early rollout. Telemetry: added tag sdk.cred_shape=flat/legacy and stream.helper=variadic to trace spans. Why this is unique: previous PRs converge on retry and stream ergonomics; this one focuses on unifying the argument surface shape (flattening) and adding small helpers that deliberately keep the runtime surface minimal while improving parity in examples and docs. Risks & mitigations: risk of accidental key collisions when both envelope and flat args are supplied; mitigated with explicit precedence rules and validation error when both fields populated. Minor compatibility risk covered by runtime warning + one-release shim. CI & canary coverage described below.
a1b3c4d: flatten constructor shapes and add compatibility shim
d4e5f6a: introduce chunked_iter/streamBatch/StreamChunks implementations and tests
b7c8d9e: align retry presets and telemetry tags across SDK bindings
f1e2d3c: docs, migration examples and version bumps
Luis: Can we keep the compatibility shim opt-in via an env flag for the first 48h? — Author: We decided to emit warnings instead and gate server-side acceptance; opt-in flag adds complexity for customers.
Priya: TypeScript helper should accept async iterables and plain arrays; please add a small adapter — Author: added adapter and tests in second commit.
Omar: Add telemetry tag for sdk.cred_shape so infra can track adoption — Author: added tag and test for the span metadata.
SDKs: flattened credential constructor args for Python/TypeScript/Go; added lightweight variadic stream helpers (chunked_iter/streamBatch/StreamChunks) to simplify buffering/backpressure; harmonized auth retry defaults. Backwards-compatible shim included; deprecation warnings emitted. Version bumps: py 1.11.0, ts 2.7.0, go v1.8.1.
One-line: pass api_key/token_provider_hint directly to the SDK constructors instead of the nested credentials envelope. Example replacements provided in docs/sdk-migration/flatten-credentials.md. The legacy envelope remains accepted for one release with runtime warnings; remove legacy usage by next minor release.
Local unit + integration streaming tests added for all languages. e2e canary executed against two customer tenants with telemetry gated for 72 hours. Load profile simulated 5k RPS for batching semantics; no regression observed in tail latency. Observability added to track sdk.cred_shape adoption.
payload.title: flatten SDK credential surface and variadic stream helpers

Summary: Introduces a staged token coordinator (STC) and a KV coalescer to enable tighter overlap between token prefetch (prefill) and decode stages without increasing worst-case latency. The STC moves from a coarse stage-boundary handshake to a token-window-driven handoff that lets small chunks of KV state be streamed earlier. The KV coalescer batches and deduplicates overlapping KV prefetch requests across concurrent inflight prefills, reducing redundant GPU kernel invocations and improving token throughput under medium-length sequences.

Motivation & context: Ongoing work around overlapped prefill/decode showed good p50 improvements but left tail latency and redundant kernel launches when many similar prefill windows were requested concurrently (see ENG-4821). This change is a lighter-weight alternative to full speculative-chunking: it aims for predictable SLOs while recovering batching opportunity lost by strict stage boundaries.

What this changes:
- Adds staged_token_coordinator that slices prefill windows into small token-windows (configurable, default 32 tokens) and provides a single subscription interface for decode to consume early-ready KV shards.
- Implements kv_coalescer that merges KV prefetch intents from multiple requests within a short coalescing window (default 6ms) and deduplicates identical keys.
- Introduces a soft backpressure policy to avoid overwhelming the decode side: STC tracks in-flight kv-shards and delays prefetch extension when soft_limit exceeded.
- Runtime knobs exposed via redwood/config/runtime.yaml: token_window_size, kv_coalesce_ms, stc_soft_limit.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc linked in Linear (ENG-4821)
- [x] Unit tests for coordinator and coalescer
- [x] End-to-end microbench that compares baseline vs STC on local bench lab
- [x] Feature-flag gating (stc_enabled) for gradual rollout

Commits (summary):
- feat(stc): initial staged token coordinator, windowing and subscription API
- perf(kv): implement kv_coalescer with dedupe and merge strategies
- fix(runtime): soft backpressure and metrics for stc
- test: add unit + integration tests for coalescer/stc
- docs: runtime knobs and rollout notes

Files touched (high-level):
- serving/runtime/staged_token_coordinator.rs (new)  -- core STC implementation
- serving/runtime/kv_coalescer.rs (new) -- merges prefetch intents and dedupe
- serving/runtime/handshake.rs -- replace coarse handshake with STC subscription points (small adapt)
- serving/bench/bench_stc.py -- microbench harness and plotting script
- config/runtime.yaml -- knobs and defaults
- tests/stc_unit.rs, tests/kv_coalescer_integration.rs
- docs/ops/stc_rollout.md

Patch excerpt (illustrative):
// staged_token_coordinator.rs (simplified)
impl StagedTokenCoordinator {
    fn extend_prefill(&self, req_id: RequestId, token_range: Range) {
        // slice range into windows and publish ready kv-shards as they resolve
        for window in token_range.windows(self.window_size) {
            self.publish_shard(req_id, window.start, window.end);
        }
    }
}

Review conversation (highlights):
- Brian Chen (review): "Nice targeted approach. My main concern is metric coverage for when we dedupe keys across different model versions (we need to avoid cross-version contamination). Please add strict version tagging on coalescer entries."
- Asha (author): "Added model_version tag to coalescer keys and unit tests that simulate version skew. See second commit."
- Omar Farouk (review): "Can we avoid adding a new full async queue per request? The current impl had a queue in Stc per-request which looked heavy."
- Asha: "Reworked STC to use a shared slab of subscriptions with lightweight tokens instead of per-request heap allocations; updated bench results (see bench_stc.py)."
- Lena Rodriguez (review, approval): "Bench looks convincing for medium-length sequences; approved for gradual rollout behind flag. Please watch p99 during canary."

CI / checks summary: 
- linux-unit-tests: pass
- bench-lab-smoke: pass
- lint: pass (one clippy suggestion addressed)
- integration: pass
- upgrade-checks: pass

Bench results (short):
- Baseline: p50 token latency 7.8ms, p95 34ms, throughput 1200 tokens/s
- With STC+coalescer (default knobs): p50 6.1ms (22% improvement), p95 28ms (17% improvement), throughput 1375 tokens/s (14% uplift).
- Memory/CPU overhead: +2% CPU, +0.8% GPU kernel invocations (reduced overall kernel invocations by ~9% due to dedupe)

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag stc_enabled=false by default
- Canary on dedicated pool with 5% traffic for 48h, monitor p50/p95/p99, kernel invocation rate, kv-prefetch queue depth, and cross-version key hits.
- If stable, increase to 25% then full rollout over one week.

Release notes (short):
- runtime: staged token coordinator + KV coalescer improve token-level overlap between prefill and decode; reduces redundant KV prefetch work and improves p50/p95 latency for medium-length sequences. Controlled by stc_enabled flag.

Follow-ups / known limitations: 
- Does not yet implement speculative eviction of coalesced shards for extremely long sequences; follow-up ENG-4899 tracks an aggressive eviction policy.
- May not yield visible gains on very short (<16 token) prefills; runtime defaults keep token_window_size configurable.

Merge outcome: squashed and merged by Lena Rodriguez on 2026-02-24. Feature gated and documented.

runtime: staged token coordinator + KV coalescer improve prefill/decode overlap and reduce redundant KV prefetch work; feature-flagged behind stc_enabled
Brian Chen: Add model_version tag to coalescer keys to prevent cross-version contamination.
Asha Menon: Added model_version tagging and tests in second commit.
Omar Farouk: Avoid per-request async queues; please rework to shared slab.
Asha Menon: Reworked STC to use shared slab of subscriptions; bench updated.
Lena Rodriguez: Approved for gradual rollout behind flag; monitor p99 during canary.

Summary: This PR adds telemetry for kernel auto-selection v2 decisions so we can debug mis-selections, quantify selection distribution shifts during canary, and correlate tail latency with selector features. Telemetry is PII-safe (no prompts, no tool args, no user identifiers), cardinality-limited, and behind config gates with sampling.

Context: Kernel auto-selection v2 introduces SKU- and seq-regime-aware decision logic. During rollout we need (1) per-request explainability (why a kernel was chosen / why we fell back), (2) low-overhead sampling controls to avoid cost regressions, and (3) stable field semantics for replay/determinism investigations. This implements the telemetry portion of ENG-4824 and unblocks dashboards in observability-pack.

What’s included: (1) New structured event `runtime.kernel_selection.decision` emitted after selector evaluation, before kernel launch; (2) Sampling + gating: off by default, with environment/model/GPU overrides; (3) PII/capability constraints: explicit allowlist of fields, no request payload; (4) Cardinality controls: candidate kernels are emitted as a bounded list + a stable signature; (5) Light unit/integration tests validating redaction, truncation, and event determinism.

Event schema (stable fields): selector_version=v2; decision_id (uuidv4); timestamp; model_id (internal canonical id); model_family (llama/mistral/qwen/gemma/unknown); model_revision (serving rev string); gpu_sku (normalized, e.g. H100-SXM, A100-80GB, L40S; no device UUIDs); cuda_version + driver_version (coarse buckets); seq_bucket (short/medium/long/xlong); prefill_tokens_bucket + decode_tokens_bucket (bucketed, not exact); observed_regime_hint (from scheduler if present); chosen_kernel (string id); candidate_kernels (bounded list, max 6); candidate_set_sig (stable hash over sorted candidate ids); fallback_reason (enum: none|missing_kernel|denylisted|unstable_driver_guardrail|compile_cache_miss|perf_guardrail|unknown); denylist_rule_id (string, optional); gate_state (enabled/disabled + source); selection_time_us (integer); compile_cache_hit (bool); selector_cache_hit (bool); error (optional enum if selector encountered recoverable error).

Sampling and overhead: Default sampling is 0.1% (`kernel_selection.telemetry.sample_rate=0.001`) with an additional “burst” mode for canaries (up to 2% for specific {model_id,gpu_sku,region} tuples). Sampling decisions are made once per request, early, and reused across all telemetry writes for that request. Emission uses the existing async telemetry queue; at 2% on our perf-canary profiles the added CPU overhead was within noise (< ~3µs p95 in microbench; see selector perf counter logs in test output).

PII / privacy considerations: No prompt text, completions, user ids, IPs, headers, or tool payloads are recorded. The only request-linked identifier is `decision_id` and a short-lived `request_trace_id` that is already present in tracing and is not customer-provided. GPU identity uses normalized SKU only; removed raw PCIe device ids and GPU UUIDs. Token counts are bucketed to avoid leaking precise lengths for unusually structured workloads.

Operational notes: New config keys under `runtime.kernel_selection.telemetry.*` with hot-reload support. SRE can temporarily increase sampling for a model/GPU combo during incidents. This PR does not add new dashboards; it provides the underlying events/metrics that dashboard panels will query.

Testing: Added unit tests for redaction/truncation and a deterministic snapshot test for schema stability. Ran `runtime_e2e_gpu_smoke` on A100 and H100 lanes (hosted canary). CI includes lint + schema validation.

Follow-ups: Observability-pack PR will add dashboard panels keyed on `chosen_kernel`, `seq_bucket`, `gpu_sku`, and `fallback_reason`. We may also add a rate limiter on telemetry queue in a separate PR if we see backpressure at higher sampling in Dedicated pools.
Omar El-Sayed (review): Please ensure we never emit raw device identifiers. I see `gpu_uuid` in the initial draft payload—this is a hard no for both privacy and cardinality. Also: bucket token counts; exact prefill length can be sensitive for some enterprise workloads.
Logan Wright (author): Ack. Removed gpu_uuid + device_id entirely; switched to `gpu_sku_norm` only. Token counts are now bucketed (powers-of-two buckets up to 32k, then 64k). Added tests that fail if any raw ids are present in payload.
Allison Grant (review): Metrics/event naming: we should keep event fields stable and versioned. Can we add `selector_version` and avoid changing field names between v1/v2? Also please cap candidate list length; otherwise dashboards will explode.
Logan Wright (author): Added `selector_version` (v1/v2) and kept field names generic (`chosen_kernel`, `candidate_kernels`). Candidate list now capped at 6 with an additional `candidate_set_sig` hash for complete set correlation. Added schema snapshot test to catch accidental field changes.
Caleb Johnson (review): Telemetry ingestion will choke if candidate_kernels is unbounded or high-cardinality strings. Can you confirm kernel ids are from a finite registry and not include build paths? Also I’d prefer truncating any unexpected string fields at source.
Logan Wright (author): Kernel ids are registry keys (e.g. `flashattn_v3_fp16`, `xformers_mha_int8`), not paths. Added a `sanitize_string()` helper with a max length (64) applied to all string fields including rule ids/fallback reasons; unknown values are coerced to `unknown`.
Jordan Lee (review): Determinism: sampling should not affect selection outcomes. Please confirm the sampling decision is computed after selector evaluation or at least not used by selector inputs. Also, do we log any non-deterministic ordering (candidate list)?
Logan Wright (author): Sampling is computed independently and only gates telemetry emission; selector inputs untouched. Candidate list is emitted in deterministic order (stable sort by kernel id) and we log a hash over the sorted set. Added a test asserting ordering determinism.
Yuki Sato (review): Nice. One more: add `fallback_reason` enum and include denylist rule id when applicable. This will help when we disable kernels per SKU/driver.
Logan Wright (author): Done. Added `fallback_reason` enum and optional `denylist_rule_id` (string). Also added `unstable_driver_guardrail` as a specific reason.
Buildkite (bot): runtime-lint failed (clang-format) in decision_event.cc
Logan Wright (author): Fixed formatting + reran lint.
Omar El-Sayed (approval): Approved. Thanks for removing gpu_uuid and bucketing token counts. This should be safe to enable at low sample rates during canary.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved with the schema snapshot test + candidate cap.
Caleb Johnson (approval): Approved. Sanitization + bounded fields look good.
Merge (squash): Merged by Logan Wright into main. Squash commit message: 'Kernel selection v2: emit per-request telemetry events with sampling + PII-safe fields' (ENG-4824).
payload.title: Kernel selection v2: emit per-request telemetry events with sampling + PII-safe fields

Summary: This PR breaks the monolithic CI dependency graph into a small, declarative catalog (tools/deps/catalog.yml) and implements a lightweight presubmit warmup agent that pre-fetches language runtimes and primes the toolcache on ephemeral runners.

Motivation: CI flakiness and long first-run latencies were traced to a large, tightly coupled dependency bootstrap path. Teams saw 20-40s variance on initial lint/test job starts and noisy network bursts when many jobs bootstrapped toolchains simultaneously. By decomposing the dependency topology and adding a thin warmup path, we reduce noise, make caching more explicit, and make future selective prefetch strategies possible.

Approach:
- Introduce tools/deps/catalog.yml: a small manifest that captures logical dep groups (node, python, go, docker) and their minimal bootstrap steps.
- Add ci/presubmit/warmup-agent: a tiny Go binary and systemd-style service that runs on ephemeral runners to pre-pull images, restore small tool caches, and perform quick validations of environment variables.
- Refactor CI workflows (ci/workflows/presubmit.yml) to call the warmup-agent when runner labels include warmup=true and to use the catalog when resolving which dep groups to prepare.
- Add a new fastpath lint shard (ci/workflows/lint-fastpath.yml) that only runs a subset of linters for quick feedback.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement catalog manifest and loader
- [x] Implement warmup-agent binary and unit tests
- [x] Wire workflows to call warmup where applicable
- [x] Add smoke nightly to validate warmup behavior
- [x] Update docs/ci/dep-management.md
- [x] Run cross-repo canary on redwood-examples

Changes (high level):
- added: tools/deps/catalog.yml (manifest format, schema v1)
- added: ci/presubmit/warmup-agent/main.go + Dockerfile + unit tests
- modified: ci/workflows/presubmit.yml (calls warmup step conditionally)
- added: ci/workflows/lint-fastpath.yml (fast lint lane)
- modified: scripts/toolcache/restore.sh (split restore into group-aware restore)
- modified: docs/ci/dep-management.md (explains catalog and migration)
- modified: Makefile and CI entrypoint to accept --dep-group flags

Commits (summary):
- 1a3e4d2: add catalog manifest and loader + schema tests
- 2b4f6a1: implement warmup-agent, Dockerfile and small unit tests
- 7c8d9ab: wire presubmit workflow to call warmup agent and add lint-fastpath
- 9f0b1c3: split toolcache restore by dep-group and add feature flag
- d4e5f6b: docs and release notes update

Review conversation (selected excerpts):
- Ethan Zhao (review): "Nice decomposition — can we keep the catalog schema intentionally tiny? worried about coupling later."
- Author (Aisha): "Agreed; kept schema to 3 top-level fields (id, groups, commands). I added schema tests to prevent creeping."
- Marina Kovacs (review): "Warmup agent LGTM; please add a conservative timeout so it never blocks the runner startup."
- Author: "Added 30s default timeout and a DEBUG env var to skip warmup for debugging."
- Liam O'Connor (approval): "Approach looks safe for canary; recommend rolling to fastpath first then broad rollout."
- Comment thread (post-merge): "Observed ~18% reduction in average presubmit wall clock for first-run jobs during canary window. Need to track network egress reduction metric."

CI status and checks:
- GitHub Actions: build matrix (linux/go, linux/python, docker image) — passed
- Unit tests: go test (warmup-agent) — passed
- Integration: smoke-presubmit (canary on redwood-examples) — passed
- Lint: go vet + staticcheck — passed
- E2E (nightly smoke): pending on merge but gated for next night

Merge outcome: merged via squash-merge into main on 2026-02-22 by Aisha Raman. Merge commit message kept a short changelog and referenced ENG-3142.

Notes for operators:
- To opt out for a runner set label warmup=false; default behavior remains unchanged for older runners.

Hotfix: introduce ephemeral quiet-window and weighted-evictor to reduce SLO breaches during transient KV stalls; backported to release/2026-02 for affected customers.
Motivation: Following a regional incident (SUP-9876) where short-lived KV-stalls amplified into tenant SLO violations, we need a fast, low-risk mitigation that prevents circuit thrash and evens tenant fairness without a heavy config rollout. This PR adds a lightweight 'fail-shepherd' controller that gates transient circuit flips using a short, adjustable quiet-window and couples it with a weighted-evictor that preferentially trims noisy tenants under egress pressure. Design summary: 1) Quiet-window: newly added per-region ephemeral timer (default 8s) that suppresses immediate reopen attempts after a circuit trip to avoid rapid flip cycles; 2) Adaptive reopen pacing: reopen attempts are backoff-capped and attempt counts are recorded in ephemeral metrics for telemetry-driven tuning; 3) Weighted evictor: eviction decisions now consider tenant weight and recent token-rate variance to avoid evicting small fair tenants when a noisy tenant spikes; weights default to usage but can be overridden by tenant config; 4) KV-coalescer soft-handoff: when a node drains KV pressure, we wait for a short grace window to preserve prefix cache affinity for hottenants; 5) Telemetry hooks: emit quiet_window.* and evictor.* metrics and an incident log marker for correlation with trace ids. Checklist: - [x] implement quiet-window timer and secure expiration path; - [x] integrate weighted evictor into admission pipeline; - [x] emit metrics for SLO dashboards; - [x] add unit tests for timer semantics and eviction scoring; - [x] run staged canary in us-west-2 on dedicated dev fleet; - [x] backport to release/2026-02. Risk: low surface area change (control-plane gating + small admission path hook). No model-serving code changes. Rollout: staged canary -> 10% -> 50% -> full; automatic rollback if SLO regressions exceed 0.5 p50 latency or 2% error-rate bump in canary windows. Related: ENG-4521 explains long-term plan to replace static thresholds with learned reopen schedules.
Diego Morales: Looks good overall. Two requests: (1) make quiet-window default configurable via feature flag for canary; (2) add a short note on metric cardinality for quiet_window.* - replied and added flag and metric tag (Marina)
Claire Nguyen: Verified unit tests and added an integration smoke-run on the dev fleet. Observed no circuit thrash during simulated KV spikes. Approved pending CI green.
Ravi Singh: Please add a short note in ops runbook about when to increase quiet-window for persistent cross-region flapping — added section in docs/ops/incident-mitigations.md (Marina)
Marina Chen (author): Addressed comments; enabled feature-flag guard and added metric tags. Deployed to canary (us-west-2); monitoring looks stable.

Motivation: We see frequent short-lived, cross-tenant error spikes that trigger noisy SLO alerts. These often come from fanout edges, transient infra glitches, or misrouted retries. Existing per-invocation error counts produce high false positive rates and high paging overhead for on-call. This PR introduces two complementary observability pieces: (1) a correlated-error-aggregator that computes probabilistic co-occurrence scores across dimensions (tenant, route, model_variant, region) and emits a compact correlation metric used by alerting to prioritize coherent incidents, and (2) a synthetic-invocation-reporter that issues low-rate synthetic requests across routing surfaces to exercise fallbacks, collect reproducible traces, and validate routing/kv-prefetch health without affecting customer quota.

What this changes: - telemetry/correlated_aggregator: new service that subscribes to sampled error spans and invocation events, computes a time-decayed co-occurrence score (exponential decay window), and emits a single correlation_metric{tenant,route,model_variant,region} per minute. The score is normalized to [0,100]. - runtime/hooks/synthetic_reporter: opt-in reporter (feature-flagged) in the request mux which issues 0.01 invocations/sec per region target surface (configurable per deployment) and attaches a synthetic-tag so it is excluded from billing pipelines. When the reporter observes a non-200 or exception it buffers a compact log bundle and emits a synthetic_failure_metric and a compressed log reference to the aggregator. - alerts/alerting_rules.yaml: new alert rule "HighCorrelatedErrorScore" that triggers only when correlation_metric>40 for 3m and sustained by synthetic_failure_metric or error_rate>2% over same window; includes a two-step hysteresis: mute for 10m on single-tenant flares, escalate after cross-tenant correlation. - dashboards/observability/correlated_error_overview.json: A Grafana panel showing correlation heatmap, synthetic failure timeline, and representative sampled traces. - config/telemetry_sampling.yaml: sampling knobs exposed to ops to tune reservoir size and synthetic reporter rate.

Checklist: - [x] implement aggregator and reporter - [x] unit + integration tests for aggregator logic - [x] dashboards + alert rule - [x] feature flag gating and default off in private installs - [x] rolling rollout plan and runbook notes

Linear / Context: ENG-2123 tracks alert fatigue reduction; SRE-987 is follow-up to tune hysteresis and eviction thresholds. This PR is intentionally opt-in behind feature flag; rollout plan included in runbook.
Added a correlated error aggregation pipeline and a low-volume synthetic invocation reporter to improve signal-to-noise for tenant SLO alerts; new dashboards and alert hysteresis settings included; runtime hook is opt-in behind feature flag.
Liam Chen (review): Nice approach. A few asks: 1) add idempotency guard for synthetic reporter to avoid double-invocation during retries, 2) prove that correlation scores don't degenerate with sparse tenants, add unit tests for decay math.
Maya Patel (reply): Added idempotency token and expanded unit tests to include sparse tenant cases. Updated docs to call out rate limits and feature-flag default off.

Motivation: TP inference workloads were observing frequent short-lived stalls caused by misaligned prefetches across tensor shards and suboptimal kernel launch ordering under mixed microbatch sizes. This PR introduces a two-part runtime optimization: (1) a waterfall prefetch aggregator that coalesces KV cache prefetch intents from concurrent microbatches into prioritized multi-shard prefetch waves, and (2) a kernel coordinator that schedules compute launches based on predicted prefetch completion windows and NCCL transfer bandwidth estimates. Changes are gated behind runtime flags and default-off for Dedicated/Private until canary metrics validate behavior. Summary of changes: waterfall prefetch aggregation logic (runtime/kvcache/waterfall_aggregator.cc/.h), a lightweight shard-level prefetch metadata cache for cross-request coordination (runtime/kvcache/shard_prefetch_index.*), kernel coordinator and priority queue (runtime/scheduler/kernel_coordinator.*), an NCCL bandwidth estimator used to compute expected prefetch completion (runtime/comm/nccl_bandwidth_estimator.*), and CI + unit tests plus a small perf harness under perf/bench/tp_waterfall_test.py. Key behaviors: - Prefetch intents are collected for a short aggregation window (default 200us) and batched into ordered waves to maximize intra-node multi-shard coalescing while keeping latency SLOs. - The coordinator computes per-shard expected transfer end-times and delays/advances kernel launches to reduce compute waiting on outstanding transfers. - Aggressive local combining of adjacent KV prefetch ranges reduces NCCL launch counts for small KV segments. - Backoff and fast-fail paths added for heterogeneous hardware when bandwidth estimates are poor. Performance: internal canary on 8xA100-40GB TP jobs with typical short-context conversational workload shows median latency unchanged, p95 down ~6%, p99 down ~8%, sustained throughput up ~12% for batch size 16 microbatches, and NCCL host-to-host stall time reduced ~22% in traces. Implementation notes: to avoid cross-tenant contamination, the shard_prefetch_index is scoped to allocation pools and cleared on allocation release. Feature is enabled by feature flag runtime.prefetch_waterfall and runtime.kernel_coordinator with three rollout phases: off -> canary (10% of traffic) -> on. Testing: unit tests cover aggregation correctness, bandwidth estimator sanity, and coordinator hysteresis. Perf tests exercise mixed microbatch size patterns. A small integration test with NCCL antiques runs in perf CI. Rollout plan: canary on internal infra, monitor p99 latency, NCCL stall metric, and error rates for two weeks; expand to Dedicated customers with opt-in before global enablement. Related work: intersects with ENG-4923 (kvcache prefetch heuristics) and ENG-4988 (scheduler microbatch priorities).
Introduce a waterfall prefetch aggregator and kernel coordinator that reduces comm stalls on tensor-parallel inference. Improves p99 latency and throughput for multi-GPU TP workloads; safe rollout behind runtime feature flag.
Diego Morales (reviewer): The aggregation window is sensitive; can we make the 200us tunable per-pool and add telemetry for drops?
Priya Shah (author): Yes — exposed runtime.prefetch_aggregation_window_us and added telemetry metrics waterfall.aggregate_waves and waterfall.prefetch_drops. Updated tests to assert window override.
Mei Chen (reviewer): Re: coordinator delaying kernels: how do we ensure we don't violate strict latency SLOs for single-shard small requests?
Priya Shah (author): Coordinator uses conservative slack defaults and a fast-path bypass for single-shard tiny requests (<= 32 tokens). See scheduler/kernel_coordinator.cc lines 120-148. Added e2e test for single-shard latency.
Liam O'Connor (approver): Verified perf harness numbers on internal cluster. One nit: add more logs when estimator calibration fails.
Priya Shah (author): Added estimator_calibration.warn logs and a unit test for calibration fallback behavior.

Context: Tenants with short, high-amplitude spikes were incurring disproportionate token costs because default batching and quant defaults were tuned for steady-state throughput. Motivation: provide an automated, low-risk path to align per-tenant batch shapes and quant presets to observed traffic "trajectories" without requiring manual profile ops. What this PR does: introduces a new Cost Path Synchronizer (Syncer) that coordinates a miniature prefill/mini-batcher with the serving scheduler and a Quant-Horizon Probe that periodically evaluates candidate quantization presets over short sliding windows and reports expected token-cost vs quality tradeoffs. The Syncer computes tenant-specific horizon windows, groups incoming requests into micro-batches when beneficial, and enforces budget-aware deadlines to avoid violating latency SLOs. The Quant-Horizon Probe runs ephemeral evaluation jobs (1-3s windows) using lightweight sampling and a shadow-compare against the tenant's pinned model variant; results are surfaced to the Console and used to suggest safe quant presets. Key implementation notes: a new src/scheduler/cost_syncer.go implements a cost-aware batching policy and KV-cache hints; src/batcher/mini_prefill.go contains the mini-batcher and prefill heuristics; tools/quant_horizon/* implements the probe harness and the probe-runner service; console: ui/tenant_defaults/cost_syncer_panel.tsx and api routes for toggling flags; CLI: rwdctl cost-scan --tenant <id> --dryrun to run the probe on demand. Summary of commits: (1) scaffold Syncer + config and integration with scheduler; (2) mini-batcher implementation + prefill policies; (3) quant-horizon probe + probe runner; (4) telemetry/metrics hooks and unit_econ metrics; (5) Console UI and API; (6) CLI command and docs; (7) tests and lint fixes. Representative changed files: src/scheduler/cost_syncer.go, src/batcher/mini_prefill.go, tools/quant_horizon/probe_runner.go, ui/tenant_defaults/cost_syncer_panel.tsx, cli/rwdctl/cost_scan.go, tests/integration/tenant_sync_burst_test.go, tests/integration/quant_horizon_smoke_test.go, charts/featureflags.yaml, docs/ops/cost-sync-runbook.md. Small illustrative diff snippet: "@@ src/scheduler/cost_syncer.go @@ func chooseBatchWindow() { // new heuristic uses tenantTrafficSlope and budgetDeadline }". Performance & cost signal: internal simulator (based on traces from three seed tenants) shows token-cost reduction of 6-18% for bursty workloads and p99 latency improvements of 10-25% when mini-batcher is allowed to aggregate short windows; median latency impact is <3% in steady state. Safety & fallback: Syncer defaults to conservative thresholds; if Quant-Horizon probe fails or reports quality degradation >1.5% on our eval metrics the runtime automatically reverts to pinned model/quant configuration. A new flag redwood.enable_cost_sync (default: false) and per-tenant override controls rollout. Rollout plan: feature flagged, canary to 10 tenants for 48h, expand to 25% after telemetry verification, then global; monitor unit_econ.delta, tenant.error_rate, and p99 latency dashboards. Review conversation highlights: Kai Chen: "Need an explicit CPU/IO budget for the probe runner to avoid noisy neighbor effects; prefer cgroup-based limit." Author reply (Ava): "Added probe CPU cap (0.1 core by default) and probe PID isolation; documented in charts/featureflags.yaml." Jordan Patel: "Add a CLI dry-run and ensure no persisted state is written for probe-only runs." Author: "Implemented rwdctl cost-scan --dryrun, added integration test to assert no DB writes." Riley Thompson: "Expand telemetry to track tenant_unit_cost_delta and probe_quality_score over time." Author: "Added tenant_metric.unit_cost_delta and probe_quality.score; updated Console panel to visualize them." CI & testing: CI passed (build/test/lint) after one flaky integration test (quant_horizon_smoke_test) failed on first run due to timing; rerun succeeded. Files changed count small and focused to core scheduler, batcher, tools, console and docs. Merge: squashed and merged to main on 2026-02-20 by Ava Martinez. Migration / operational steps: operators should enable redwood.enable_cost_sync=false by default, flip for selected tenants using Console or rwdctl, watch the new unit_econ.alert (threshold configurable) and revert if unit cost increases unexpectedly. Related work: ENG-4021 (mini-batcher design), ENG-4090 (quant probe harness). No breaking changes. Notes: this PR intentionally ships as experimental with feature flag and conservative defaults; follow-up work planned: automated per-tenant rollout recommendations and integration with Optimize suggestions engine.

Background: We see intermittent availability issues for long-running streaming sessions when clients disconnect briefly (mobile flapping, NAT churn). Existing long-lived leases both tie up worker slots and create noisy reclaim logic. This PR introduces an ephemeral handoff + time-slicing model: short-lived server leases (default 30s) that capture a lightweight session snapshot checkpoint; a resumable client workflow that attempts soft resume using a one-time resume token; and a preemption/time-slice reclaim policy to allow high-priority requests to evict inactive long tails without killing resumable work.

Goals: 1) reduce orphaned GPU slot retention caused by client disconnects, 2) keep tool/function-call idempotency intact across resume, 3) maintain OpenAI-streaming compatibility for clients that expect a continuous SSE/ws stream.

What changed:
- New ephemeral lease controller that issues short TTLe leases and stores compact checkpoints (KV of model position + pending toolcall markers) in in-memory indexed storage with optional persistence to Redis for private deployments.
- Resume token construction: single-use, scope-limited token tied to session id, last-seen token version, and a replay-cap window to prevent double-execution of tool calls. Tokens are intentionally opaque and rotate on every snapshot.
- Client-suggested checkpoint points: clients can request a checkpoint at safe boundaries (post-toolcall, at top-level narrative turns) via a small protocol extension to streaming events; server still snapshots automatically on disconnect.
- Time-slice preemption: long-running sessions paved into 1s slices; if a worker needs capacity, inactive slices are checkpointed and evicted; active slices get grace-run for spans up to a configured soft-run window.
- Backoff and reconnect flow: clients attempting resume follow a hedged strategy (fast rejoin -> bind resume token -> server validates and rehydrates checkpoint) with a short escrow window to accept late rebinds while preventing split-brain.
- OpenAI compat: streaming SSE frame semantics preserved; we add a streaming-control event "x-resume-hint" that falls back to existing behaviors for clients that ignore it.
- Tool/function-call safety: we add per-toolcall confirmation markers in the checkpoint and make tool calls idempotent by replaying only unconfirmed calls on resume.

Tests & rollout:
- Unit tests for checkpoint serialization, token rotation, resume validation, and tool-call replay logic.
- Integration tests that simulate NAT churn, flaky clients, and worker preemption; flaky e2e surfaced once and was rerun in CI.
- Canary rollout toggles: feature gated behind runtime flag that defaults off for older clusters; automatic telemetry captures resume success rate, mismatch errors, and average slot reclaim latency.

Backwards compatibility & migration notes:
- Clients that do not opt into the checkpoint hints will continue to behave as before; they get the server-initiated ephemeral leases but will not benefit from client-initiated lower-latency resumes.
- Resume window configurable per deployment; default conservative values chosen to avoid double-run of toolcalls.

Security: ephemeral resume tokens are HMAC-signed with rotating keys (KMS integration for Private installs).

Privacy: checkpoints avoid storing user prompt text by default; only model position and toolcall metadata are persisted unless customer opts in.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-4907: expose resume metrics in Console and add a retry budget per API-key.
- ENG-4958: opt-in durability tier that persists full snapshots to object store for very long resumes.
Ethan Shaw: Please add a diagram showing token lifecycle and race scenarios (addressed in docs update).
María Gómez: Concern about Redis persistence overhead for Private; added config toggles and KMS notes (ack).
Liam O'Connor: Suggested stricter default resume-window to reduce potential double-exec; reduced default to 30s (done).
CI Robot: flaky integration test 'client-flap-e2e' failed on first run; rerun passed.
Adds an ephemeral lease + checkpoint resume flow to improve streaming resilience on brief client disconnects. Backwards compatible; disabled by default via runtime flag. See docs/streaming-resume.md for migration steps and console metrics (ENG-4907).

Motivation: customers using structured response_format wanted a way to gradually opt into strict JSON Schema validation without disrupting streaming-first workloads or tool-invoking flows. This PR adds a runtime-controlled strictness toggle, a prioritized stream-fallback mapping, and OpenAI-compat error-code translation so that callers receive consistent signals across compatibility layers. Design summary: 1) response_format.strictness boolean (runtime-config + per-request header override) toggles between permissive and strict validation modes. 2) When strict mode is enabled, final-block validation enforces the configured JSON Schema. If stream chunks are malformed, the runtime will attempt two recovery strategies in order: prefix-coercion attempts minimal corrective edits to reconstitute a well-formed JSON object; checkpoint-rewind falls back to the last validated checkpoint and continues generation with a softer schema profile. 3) A new stream_fallback_map lets operators prefer "coerce-first" or "rewind-first" and set maximum recovery attempts. 4) Tool/function-calling paths are fenced: when a tool call is emitted the output is validated against the declared tool-schema; if strictness rejects a tool payload it converts the rejection into a structured tool-error event instead of dropping the invocation. 5) OpenAI compatibility adapter maps internal validation error classes into stable OpenAI-style error codes and includes an error_hint payload for developer tooling. Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains permissive (strictness off) unless opt-in via config or request flag. Streaming semantics: added lightweight checkpoints every N tokens (configurable) to bound rewind cost. The implementation touches the response_format negotiation layer, the runtime validator, stream checkpointing, and the openai compatibility shim. Tests and rollout: added unit and integration tests that exercise coerce-first and rewind-first strategies, toolcall fencing, and compatibility mapping. Feature toggles and telemetry allow a staged rollout starting with canary accounts. Related work: references ENG-2148 for schema negotiation design, SUP-4132 incident notes motivating clearer error codes. Checklist: - implementation and tests added - docs updated with config and semantics - SDK surface updated (python/ts) - canary rollout plan attached. See release_notes for operational guidance.
Lucas Grant: Please add an explicit limit on recovery attempts to avoid cost blowups. Addressed in infra/config/defaults.yaml and documented.
Priya Nair: Tool calls can be stateful; ensure fencing doesn't swallow retryable errors. Response: we convert strict rejects to a structured tool-error event with retryable flag when appropriate.
Omar Haddad: Can we preserve token-aligned telemetry for billing? Response: added lightweight token checkpointing metric and separate telemetry tag for recovery events.
Lucas Grant: nit - prefer 'coerce-first' naming in config, updated in all places.
Added a per-request and runtime toggle for structured-output strictness, stream recovery strategies (coerce-first and rewind-first), tool-call fencing behavior under strict validation, and OpenAI compatibility error mapping. Default remains permissive; operators can opt into strict mode for higher schema guarantees. See docs/operational/stream_recovery.md for rollout guidance and telemetry to monitor recovery events.
Canary rollout steps included in examples/strictness_toggle/canary_playbook.md. Watch metrics 'stream.recovery.attempts' and 'stream.recovery.success_rate'. Set stream_fallback_map.max_attempts to 3 for initial rollout.

payload.body:
Motivation: We need a consistent, machine-consumable signal when Optimization Config versions change (apply/promote/rollback) so internal tooling can annotate dashboards, kick off automated checks, and attach context during incidents. Today, the source of truth is audit logs + DB state, which is not ideal for near-real-time integrations and requires each consumer to poll. This PR adds (1) an internal event stream publisher for Optimization Config lifecycle changes and (2) a webhook delivery mechanism for internal service integrations, with reliability guarantees and security guardrails. Scope: Events are emitted for Optimization Config actions: VALIDATE (success/failure), APPLY (staged start/pause/resume/complete/fail), PROMOTE, and ROLLBACK. Events use a stable schema (v1) modeled after CloudEvents-like envelope and include the minimum fields required for correlation (event_id, occurred_at, actor_type/actor_id, request_id, correlation_id, tenant_id, model, region, scope, config_version_id, previous_config_version_id (when applicable), rollout_id, and action/status). Implementation details: We introduce an outbox table (optimization_config_event_outbox) written in the same transaction as the config state transition to ensure we never publish an event that doesn’t correspond to persisted state (and we don’t miss events). A lightweight publisher worker drains the outbox, publishes to the internal event bus topic redwood.controlplane.optimization_config.v1, and (optionally) fans out to registered webhook subscriptions. Webhook subscriptions are internal-only for now: created/managed via internal endpoints guarded by service-to-service auth + RBAC permission optimization.config.webhook.manage, and secrets are stored via the existing secrets provider (no plaintext secrets in DB). Delivery: Webhook deliveries are signed with HMAC-SHA256 (X-Redwood-Signature, X-Redwood-Event-Id) and retried with exponential backoff + jitter. We enforce idempotency on the receiver side by documenting X-Redwood-Event-Id, and on the sender side by tracking delivery attempts keyed by (event_id, subscription_id) to avoid duplicates on worker restarts. Observability: Adds metrics for publish latency, delivery latency, attempts, and failure rate tagged with action/status, plus structured logs with event_id/request_id for easy joins with audit logs. Tests: Unit tests for schema validation and signature generation; integration tests for outbox draining + retry behavior using a fake HTTP server; and a regression test to ensure config apply/rollback continues to emit audit events (ENG-4826) even if webhook publishing is temporarily unavailable. Rollout plan: Ship behind feature flag optimization_config_change_events_enabled (default off). Enable in staging for incident-bot + dashboard annotations, then progressively enable in production for internal consumers. Related: Follow-on PR in incident-bot adds a shortcut command and uses these events for auto-linking rollback UI/runbook (see incident-bot PR-20081). Notes/Non-goals: This does not expose a customer-configurable webhook feature; it’s explicitly internal for now. We also do not implement guaranteed ordering across tenants/regions beyond per-rollout ordering best-effort; consumers must handle out-of-order events using occurred_at + state reconciliation.
Jordan Lee (review): Outbox approach makes sense. Two asks: (1) Can we ensure the event is written in the same transaction as the config state transition? (2) Please document the consumer contract for out-of-order delivery and retries; consumers will treat these as at-least-once.
Benji Okafor (author): Yep on (1) — I refactored the state transition to accept a tx handle and write outbox rows before commit. Added integration coverage that fails if the outbox write is outside the transaction. On (2) I added a doc section + a note in the schema: delivery is at-least-once; consumers should de-dupe by event_id and reconcile by comparing config_version_id to current active pointer.
Kevin Osei (review): Security: please avoid storing any webhook secret material in DB. Also add a signature timestamp header or include occurred_at in the signed payload to reduce replay risk. Finally: ensure internal endpoints require service auth and are not reachable from customer-facing gateway.
Benji Okafor (author): Updated: DB now stores only secret_ref (Vault path) and a key_id. Dispatcher fetches secret at send-time with caching. For replay: signature is over canonical JSON payload including occurred_at plus subscription_id; added X-Redwood-Signature-Timestamp set to occurred_at. Internal endpoints moved under /internal/control-plane/* and require mTLS service identity + RBAC permission optimization.config.webhook.manage.
Allison Grant (review): Metrics tags look good. Can you add a gauge for outbox backlog size and a histogram for (occurred_at -> publish_time) to detect worker lag? Also please ensure config_version tag is present for delivery failures; we want to correlate with rollout health dashboard annotations.
Benji Okafor (author): Added outbox_backlog_total and publish_lag_seconds histogram. Delivery failure counter now tags tenant_id/model/region/config_version_id/action/status/subscription_id (with cardinality guardrails: subscription_id only in logs, not metrics). Config version is always included.
Jada Williams (review): For Console integration later, please confirm the event payload includes previous_config_version_id so we can generate a useful human diff link. Also: naming—can we use 'ROLLBACK' action with status 'COMPLETED' rather than a separate action 'ROLLED_BACK'?

Context and motivation: This hotfix addresses a production incident (INC-2026-02-17) where a subset of requests entered a slow-path admission queue and failed to make forward progress when regional egress saturated. Root cause analysis pointed to two contributing issues: (1) admission controller thresholds were static and tuned for steady-state load, not surge transitions; (2) tenant-aware rebalancing logic did not preemptively nudge long-running KV drains, leading to longer-than-expected stall times for some lanes. The regression surfaced in late-night traffic spike and caused degraded p99 tail latency for a handful of tenants.

Summary of changes (single continuous description): Implement an adaptive slow-path admission controller that tracks moving-window service-time distributions and adjusts admission cutoffs dynamically; introduce a tenant rebalancer that detects sticky drains and issues light-weight eviction hints to accelerate KV cache handoff for affected tenants; add a soft-eviction decay that gradually reduces penalties for tenants after successful graceful retries to avoid permanent demotion; wire additional telemetry (runtime.slowpath.admissions, runtime.tenant.rebalance_attempts, runtime.slowpath.drain_time_histogram) and a Console dashboard snapshot for on-call triage; include an integration test harness and a focused load test to reproduce the stall pattern seen in INC-2026-02-17. This PR is intended as a hotfix with minimal behavioral change outside surge scenarios.

Checklist:
- [x] Reproduced issue in local integration harness and unit tests
- [x] Implemented adaptive admission controller and tenant rebalancer
- [x] Added observability (metrics + dashboard) for on-call
- [x] Back-compat ensured (soft-eviction decay is opt-in via flag until rollout)
- [x] Release notes and changelog entry added

Commits (high-level):
- commit 1: runtime: add moving-window estimator and adaptive admission thresholds (m. thompson)
- commit 2: runtime: tenant rebalancer that issues soft eviction hints (m. thompson)
- commit 3: monitoring: add slowpath metrics + prometheus exporters (e. park)
- commit 4: console: dashboard snapshot for slowpath triage (j. lee)
- commit 5: tests: integration harness + deterministic stall scenario (s. gupta)
- commit 6: docs: ops runbook + quick rollback steps (m. thompson)

Changed areas / representative files:
- runtime/admission/slowpath_controller.go — new: moving-window estimator, adaptive threshold logic
- runtime/rebalance/tenant_rebalancer.go — new: heuristic to detect sticky drains and issue soft eviction hints
- monitoring/collectors/slowpath_metrics.go — new metrics and exporters
- console/dashboards/ops/slowpath-triage.json — dashboard snapshot used by on-call
- tests/integration/slowpath_repro_test.go — harness to simulate KV drain and verify recovery
- deployment/helm/values-prod.yaml — add feature flag and rollout knob
- docs/ops/load_trimmer.md — operational runbook and rollback steps

Design notes / reasoning: The adaptive admission controller uses an exponential moving window over service times and recent drain events to avoid reacting to single outliers; thresholds are bumped conservatively and include a minimum holdoff to prevent oscillation. Tenant rebalancer is intentionally lightweight: it only emits a soft eviction hint (idempotent and advisory) which the runtime uses to prioritize background KV handoff; it does not forcibly evict or drop in-flight requests. Soft-eviction decay avoids permanently lowering tenant priority after transient problems.

Testing: Added deterministic unit tests for estimator math and simulated integration tests that reproduce the original stall pattern with a controlled egress choke. CI matrix included linux/amd64 unit+integration. During CI we observed a flaky network test unrelated to changes; test was retried and passed on second run. All checks green at merge time.

Review discussion (selected):
- Jordan Lee (review): "Adaptive thresholds look reasonable but we should add an explicit cooldown metric to detect oscillation." — Author reply: "Added runtime.slowpath.cooldown_count and a brief doc comment explaining cooldown semantics (commit 3)."
- Samir Gupta (review): "Tenant rebalancer needs to be non-blocking and should not introduce extra scheduling latency." — Author reply: "Rebalancer runs as background coroutine with bounded work per tick; added benchmarks (bench results in PR) showing <1% CPU impact under 10k qps." 
- Elena Park (review): "Prometheus labels need to include tenant_id fingerprinting policy." — Author reply: "Metrics will use tenant hash (non-reversible) to avoid PII; updated collector and tests."
- Jordan Lee (requested change): "Please gate the new behavior behind a feature flag for gradual rollout." — Author reply: "Done; flag exposed in helm values and default OFF for canary until rollout plan completed."
- Final approvals: Jordan Lee (approved), Samir Gupta (approved), Elena Park (approved).

CI summary: build: pass; unit tests: pass; integration: pass after 1 flake retry; lint: pass; e2e: skipped (hotfix, limited scope). Artifacts: integration logs and benchmark outputs attached to build #1229.

Merge decision: Hotfix approved by SRE and runtime leads. Merged via squash by Maya Thompson on 2026-02-20 after gating the feature flag false-by-default in production values. Post-merge actions: (1) deploy to canary region for 4 hours with enhanced telemetry; (2) run targeted load test to validate stall reduction; (3) if stable, flip rollout flag over 2 regional waves. Runbook and rollback steps included in docs/ops/load_trimmer.md. Link to incident summary: https://linear.app/redwood/incident/INC-2026-02-17-stall-pattern (internal).

Notes for future: Consider a coarse-grained global controller that can coordinate admission thresholds across regions for synchronous failures; add automated alert that correlates slowpath.admissions spike with region egress saturation to auto-trigger mitigation runbook.

Motivation: Customers with heterogeneous workloads still have to manually tune batching, cache defaults and quantization choices. This PR adds an offline analyzer (Cost Hint Scorer) that produces ranked configuration hints per tenant/workload and a companion Quant Clustering Runner that groups model signatures to suggest candidate quantization profiles.

What this PR changes: the change is intentionally split into two cooperating components: 1) services/cost_hint_scorer - a stateless offline scorer that ingests workload telemetry snapshots and replay traces to compute per-tenant cost/latency tradeoff curves and produce a small set of ranked 'hints' (batch_size, kv_cache_ttl, quant_profile_id) with estimated unit cost and expected P95 impact; 2) tools/quant_cluster - a CLI and pipeline that clusters model activation signatures (sequence length distribution, attention pattern fingerprints, activation histograms) and emits quant profile candidates (8-bit symmetric, 4-bit groupwise, mixed-int8) along with a compact regression estimator for expected accuracy loss.

Design notes: the scorer is conservative by default: it prefers safer defaults (smaller batch, longer cache retention) when telemetry indicates high cold-start variance. Hints are exported as JSONL and can be loaded by the defaults-as-code service. The quant clustering step is independent of tenant routing; it outputs labeled clusters that map to recommended baseline quant profiles and associated safety scores. Both components are feature-flagged and run as offline jobs in the econ tooling pipeline.

Backward compatibility & rollout: runtime behavior is unchanged until a tenant opts into experiments. We added a dry-run exporter and a small API endpoint to preview suggested defaults in the Console (feature flag: econ.hint-preview). The feature is gated behind a rollout flag and will be enabled for small cohorts only; there's no automatic enforcement.

Testing & validation: unit tests for scorer heuristics, integration tests that run a 10k-sample replay against a staging runtime image and compare predicted vs observed P95 deltas, and an end-to-end simulation that replays tenant traces through suggested defaults and validates cost delta within a tolerance. Performance tests ensure the offline scorer completes a tenant snapshot (100k requests) within ~3 minutes on a 4-CPU job.

Operational notes: added lightweight telemetry (histogram metrics) and traces to the scorer; alerts configured for pipeline failures and for divergence between predicted and observed metrics beyond 15%. Documentation: new RFC and Console preview docs under docs/rfc/cost-hint-scorer.md and docs/console/econ-hints.md.

Files touched (high level): src/services/cost_hint_scorer.py, tools/quant_cluster/runner.py, tools/quant_cluster/README.md, infra/jobs/cost-hint-pipeline.yaml, docs/rfc/cost-hint-scorer.md, docs/console/econ-hints.md, tests/unit/test_cost_hint.py, tests/integration/test_quant_cluster_e2e.py, small runtime integration shim at runtime/defaults_loader.py.
Introduce Cost Hint Scorer service (offline) that produces tenant-aware recommended defaults for batching, cache TTLs, and quantization profiles. Add Quant Clustering Runner to group model variants and generate candidate quant profiles for evaluation.

Motivation: We continue to see tail latency and token-cost inefficiency for real-time small-batch workloads (chat UX and streaming). Previous kernel upgrades focused on bulk throughput; this change optimizes the hot path for small to medium sequence lengths while improving KV cache locality across continuous batching windows.

Summary of changes: Introduces a new "attn-concierge" microkernel and a runtime component called the Continuous KV Synchronizer. The concierge kernel consolidates small-op fusion: inline transposition for 64/128 heads, a compact rotary/rope fusion path that avoids extra re-layouts for common rotary sizes, and a shadow-prefetch lane that issues lightweight prefetches for K/V memory used by the next N micro-batches. The Continuous KV Synchronizer is a scheduling + background worker that keeps cold KV segments warm by re-registering frequently accessed KV ranges with the serving allocator and coordinating warmup I/O during idle gaps between continuous batches.

Key points: - Concierge kernel implements a fastpath for (seq_len <= 512, head_dim <= 128) with fused QK and rotary application to reduce memory traffic. - Shadow-prefetch lane is non-blocking and backpressure-aware; it can be disabled per-model via runtime flags. - KV Synchronizer uses a lightweight LRU+heatmap per-model to prioritize segments to warm; it integrates with existing KV eviction to avoid overcommit. - Scheduler hints: new per-request hint "kv_priority" that bumps KV synchronizer attention for critical/latency-sensitive routes. - New unit/driver tests + perf harness scenarios added to the benchmark-lab suite.

Design notes and motivations: Small-batch workloads suffered from repeated micro-transposes and redundant rotary multiplications when serving many short tokens. Prior solutions reduced kernel latency asymptotically but left a gap where memory movement dominated. By fusing steps commonly seen in our telemetry and adding a staged, cooperative prefetcher (shadow lane) we reduce per-token memory overhead while preserving numerics and FP16/FP32 accumulation paths. The KV synchronizer addresses the problem where continuous batching leaves KV shards cold when requests switch between lanes or models. Keeping these shards warm reduces first-token latency and avoids synchronous spill/reload windows that create latency spikes.

Testing and validation: - Perf microbenchmarks (benchmark-lab) show 8-14% median latency reduction and 18-30% improvement in token/sec for small clients (1-8 concurrent connections, seq_len 32–256) on T4/RTX6000-class hardware. - End-to-end chat demo workload shows 10% lower p99 in Canary traffic. - CI: added integration tests exercising scheduler hints and KV synchronizer toggles. - Safety: numeric parity tests for rotary/rope paths with 1e-6 tolerance.

Migration and rollout: Feature gated behind runtime flag "attn_concierge_enabled" and model annotation opt-in. Rollout plan: start with canary on Dedicated pools (low-rpm) -> expand to burst pools -> default on hosted after 2 weeks of stable telemetry.

Notes: This PR bundles kernel changes and small runtime pieces. Production toggle and observability hooks added (console metrics: concierge_hits, concierge_fallbacks, kv_sync_warmups).
Ethan Cole: Can we add a fallback path that avoids the fused rotary when head_dim % 32 != 0? (Addressed in commit 3, added conditional path)

Jun Park: Suggest exposing kv_priority as a float in addition to bool; accepted and added to scheduler hints

Context: alert noise from long-tail token-cost spikes has been creating a high-volume of low-actionable incidents. Several customers reported alerts triggered by rare prompt shapes that skew token-cost percentiles for short windows. Motivation: provide an efficient, queryable aggregation that preserves per-token cost fidelity for high-volume prefixes while allowing alert systems to mute spurious long-tail signals. What this PR does: 1) Adds a new 'token slab index' that buckets token-cost contributions into fixed slabs (e.g. 1-4,5-8,9-16 tokens) and maintains per-route + per-model slab rollups. This is implemented as a compact in-memory aggregator with periodic checkpointing to the metrics store. 2) Introduces an 'alert attenuator' integration which consumes slab histograms to calculate an attenuation score (probabilistic dampening) used by the alerting pipeline to reduce noisy alerts coming from low-support slabs. 3) Adds a dashboard (token-slab-explorer) with drilldowns from slabs to sampled log anchors (queryable links to stored log snippets), enabling on-call to inspect representative examples for an attenuated alert. 4) Updates ingestion and query paths: ingest side emits slab proto, query layer exposes a slab_index SQL function for efficient aggregation. 5) Adds docs, examples, and unit + integration tests. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of slab aggregator (telemetry/ingest) - [x] Query surface (slab_index function) - [x] Alert attenuator rule and CI gate - [x] Dashboard JSON and UX review - [x] Sampling hooks for log anchoring - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs and runbook snippets Roadmap notes: this is intentionally conservative (fixed slab boundaries) so we can iterate with production telemetry first. If adoption is strong we will add adaptive slab tuning and compression in a follow-up (ENG-7490).

Priya Natarajan (2026-01-29): Reply: kept 'slab' for now (internal term) but added an alias 'band' in the SQL function docs and expanded checkpointing section in docs/observability/token_slab_index.md.
Sofia Martinez (2026-01-30): Request changes: unit tests were flaky on windows runner — please make the temp directory deterministic and add a teardown to avoid port conflicts.
Priya Natarajan (2026-01-31): Addressed: made tests deterministic and added CI-only teardown step; pushed tests fix in commit f0e1d2c.
Liam O'Connor (2026-01-31): Approval with comment: the attenuator math looks reasonable; make sure ops can opt-out per-tenant (added a config flag), and include a short playbook for false-negatives.
Priya Natarajan (2026-02-01): Added tenant-level opt-out flag and playbook section in README-observability-runbook.md.
Added token slab index (compact slab histograms) and alert attenuator to reduce long-tail alert noise. New dashboard 'Token Slab Explorer' and a slab_index SQL function for querying slab rollups. Opt-out flag per tenant and runbook guidance included. (ENG-7421)
Config knobs: telemetry.slab.enabled (default true), telemetry.slab.checkpoint_interval (default 60s), alerts.attenuator.enabled (default true), alerts.attenuator.min_support_threshold (default 25). If you see legitimate alerts attenuated, set alerts.attenuator.min_support_threshold=1 for the tenant and contact telemetry@redwood.ai.

payload.body: Summary: Add an adaptive lint fence that dynamically gates heavy linters based on change-surface heuristics and lightweight fastpath presubmit prober to reduce CI noise; add a configurable release 'gentle drain' window that quiesces noncritical rollouts, migrates in-flight jobs, and emits clearer telemetry for release health. Motivation: large monorepo CI runtime and noisy long linters slow developer feedback and cause frequent merge blockers; releases sometimes spike transient errors when many canaries roll simultaneously. This PR introduces two complementary features to improve feedback velocity and stability. What changed: 1) CI presubmit: new lightweight prober (tools/presubmit/prober.go + .github/workflows/presubmit-prober.yml) pings impacted language shards and marks PRs eligible for fastpath when only metadata/docs/json changes are detected. 2) Adaptive lint fence: a new gating layer (tools/lint/fence/) that calculates a change-cost score (lines, files, languages, transitive dep churn) and selectively runs heavy linters/formatters only when cost exceeds thresholds. 3) Release gentle drain: release agents/scripts (scripts/release/drain.sh and infra/release/config.yml) implement a configurable window during which canary traffic is gradually reduced, flaky retry budgets are increased, and a 'release.quiesce' metric is emitted. 4) Toolchain and actions: updated GitHub Actions pinned versions and slimmed toolchain images (infra/ci/toolchain-manifests.json); bumped actions/checkout and setup-go, and upgraded the eslint plugin used by JS teams. 5) Docs and onboarding: ci/guide.md and docs/ci/release-gentle-drain.md added with examples and troubleshooting. Context: We observed two recent incidents where a rapid burst of requests in a single region led to a cascade of slowpath fallbacks and repeated circuit flips, causing increased tail latency and tenant impact. This PR introduces two small, orthogonal defenses: (1) surge-sanitizer, a short-window admission controller that applies a graceful 'soft-drop' with weighted tenant drain to smooth bursts without hard-deny, and (2) ephemeral-circuit-lock, a short-lived circuit state that prevents immediate reopen attempts for recently failed circuits while allowing gradual reheating. Motivation: previous mitigations either overreacted (hard-deny) or allowed rapid reopen/flapping that amplified load. The goal here is to reduce tail amplification during region-localized spikes while minimizing false positives and preserving throughput for healthy tenants. Changes: implemented a lightweight token-bucket window in the regional ingress path (surge-sanitizer) with per-tenant weight profiles; added a short-lived circuit lock (default 5s) that records a minimal recovery score and enforces exponential re-open backoff with jitter; added KV-prefetch gating to avoid expensive slowpath prefetches for tenants in the soft-drop window; instruments: new histograms and labeled counters for sanitize_decisions, circuit_lock_events, and tenant_weighted_drop_rate. Backwards-compat: all features are opt-in by feature-flag and default to conservative thresholds; no protocol changes to client-facing APIs. Rollout plan: feature-flagged on main; staged rollout to us-west-2, eu-west-1 with canary traffic (2% -> 20% -> 100%) and live SLO watch; automatic fallback to previous behavior if error rate rises beyond threshold. Commits summary: - 1f3b9d4: add surge-sanitizer admission controller and tests - 7a2c1b0: add ephemeral-circuit-lock state machine and backoff strategy - 4c9e2a7: gate KV-prefetch behind sanitizer and add defensive checks - 9b8f7a1: telemetry: counters, histograms, dashboards + unit tests Review notes: requested more unit tests around jitter correctness and a tighter metric label set. I adjusted and added deterministic tests that validate the backoff jitter distribution and the weight decay behavior for tenant drain. Observability: dashboards added include a per-region 'surge_sanitizer' panel, circuit_lock heatmap, and tenant-level drop-rate flashcards. CI: full test suite green; perf benchmark run on synthetic spike workload shows 42% reduction in 99.9th tail latency under moderate bursts and 11% throughput drop at extreme overload compared to hard-deny baseline. Safety: added a kill-switch that disables KV-prefetch gating in case of unexpected latency regressions. Related work: references incident SUP-3421, prior soft-shed experiments ENG-1987, and convo in #sre-ops.

Motivation: customers need a safer way to request structured output (JSON schema) in streaming scenarios while keeping OpenAI-compatible fallbacks. This PR implements a negotiation layer that surfaces validation hints in the response metadata, emits granular telemetry for validation failures, and ensures tool/function calls are fenced so partial JSON errors don't lead to unsafe executions.

What this does: adds a small response_contract negotiator that sits between the API surface and the runtime. The negotiator: 1) negotiates an effective response_format (strict|soft|hint-only) with explicit headers and an OpenAI-compatibility fallback, 2) exposes X-Response-Validation hint headers that the runtime uses to apply best-effort coercion during streaming, 3) attaches a validation error map to telemetry (validation.stage -> error.code -> token_offset) for classification, 4) wraps tool/function calls with a two-phase commit-like fencing: tool intents are buffered until a schema checkpoint confirms safe structure, 5) provides a streaming checkpoint API so client libraries can request a resume token when partial validation errors occur.

Backward compatibility: default behavior remains the same unless a caller opts into a response_format that requests schema negotiation. OpenAI compatibility mode (response_format=openai_compat) maps the negotiator to a 'soft' mode that attempts best-effort coercion and surface a single top-level meta error rather than failing the stream.

Checklist:
- [x] core negotiator implementation in runtime/response layer
- [x] hint header + proto definitions and JS/Go SDK plumbing
- [x] integration tests for streaming resume and toolcall fencing
- [x] docs and API examples for response_format and OpenAI mapping
- [x] telemetry events, dashboard query and alert for validation regressions

Related: linear ENG-7842 (response contract telemetry), ENG-7990 (toolcall safety). Also references design notes: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-7842/response-contract-telemetry and internal RFC: /docs/rfc/response-negotiator.md

Notes for reviewers: the negotiator is intentionally conservative with changes to execution: it only changes toolcall timing when schema checkpoints are present, and it never suppresses user-visible content unless strict mode is selected. The PR contains a short shim in the OpenAI compatibility adapter so SDKs that set the old openai response_mode get mapped to response_format=openai_compat.

Priya Nair: added negotiation_mode tag and bump to metric v2; updated dashboard query.

Owen Gallagher: noted a potential race in checkpoint ack handling when streams interleave; requested a small locking refactor.

Priya Nair: applied locking refactor and added a targeted integration test that repros the interleaving case; test now passes in CI.

Liam Park: approved after the changes. Owen: approved. Mei: approved.

Merge notes: squashed commits and merged via squash-merge on 2026-02-22 by Priya Nair.

Motivation and summary:
This PR introduces two small, linked pieces of work aimed at lowering presubmit CI costs and improving signal for flaky or misconfigured jobs: 1) a presubmit cost exporter that emits per-job time and resource estimates to our telemetry pipeline, and 2) a compact CI prober that runs a thin subset of smoke checks (fast lint + unit-test surface) to give quicker feedback for devs and to exercise release hooks for automation.
