Motivation: High-client-load experiments revealed that large sparse allocations and partial page lifetimes were driving elevated fragmentation and increasing spill pressure during bursty workloads. Existing eviction heuristics were reactive and operated at a per-slot granularity, which produced noisy eviction churn and tail latency spikes under multi-tenant mixes. This PR introduces a holistic 'residency controller' to reason about page residency at page and tenant scopes, plus an adaptive background 'page trimmer' that safely collapses underutilized partial pages to improve compactness without synchronous eviction storms.

What this changes (high level): residency controller: computes a composite residency_score per page combining: occupancy_ratio, fragmentation_factor, recent_access_weight (LFU window), tenant_priority, and bounce_rate (re-pinned after trim). Scores drive eviction preference buckets (hot/warm/cold) and per-tenant soft quotas. The controller emits new metrics and exposes a dynamic evictor hook for policy experiments. page trimmer: background worker that periodically scans low-residency candidates and atomically compacts live slots into contiguous pages, freeing trailing partial pages. The trimmer uses adaptive pacing based on in-flight IO, KV writeback pressure, and a conservative max_trims_per_cycle derived from observed latency erosion. Trimming is strictly cooperative: if eviction/backpressure signals are active the trimmer backs off.

Implementation notes: - residency controller implemented in src/kv/residency_controller.rs; algorithm heavily commented and isolated behind a feature gate. - page trimmer implemented in src/kv/page_trimmer.cc with a small shim in src/kv/trimmer_adapter.go to integrate with the Go runtime scheduler used by the server. - New on-disk page metadata version bump (+migration path) is transparent: a lightweight upgrade path migrates metadata lazily during trimmer runs; no offline migration required. - Metrics added: kv.residency.score, kv.page.trim.count, kv.page.trim.latency_ms, kv.fragmentation.p50/p90, kv.residency.evictions_by_bucket. - Admin flags in config: kv.residency.enabled, kv.residency.safe_mode (start with safe heuristics), kv.trimmer.max_ops_per_cycle, kv.trimmer.backoff_threshold.

Testing and benchmarks: Unit tests and property tests validate score monotonicity and that trimming never drops live key references. Integration test harness simulates tenant mixes with skewed hot keys and short-lived bursts. Microbenchmarks against the existing master show: 6.1% reduction in average working set size for mixed tenant workloads, 9% reduction in total spill bytes during bursty tails, and 3–7% improvement in p99 generation latency under sustained heavy load when safe_mode=false. CI: flaky kernel binding test failed on first run (linux-kernel-bind-check) but was rerun and passed; full CI green at merge.

Migration and rollout plan: feature gated off by default (kv.residency.enabled=false). Staged rollout: canary in Dedicated -> monitor kv.fragmentation.* and kv.page.trim.*; enable safe_mode=true for first 48h, then safe_mode=false if metrics stable. Rollback: disable kv.residency.enabled.

Risks and mitigations: trimming is IO-intensive if misconfigured; mitigated by dynamic pacing and backpressure signals from the IO path. Potential for eviction policy regressions on pathological synthetic workloads; mitigated by A/B experiments, and the residency controller ships with a tunable decay window and conservative default thresholds.

Related: ENG-1719 (fragmentation telemetry), ENG-1802 (tenant-aware eviction).
Ethan Russo: Nice isolation of the score computation. Question: have you tried moving the bounce_rate into the decay term instead of the score? Might stabilize churn.
Priya Nair: considered that; we experimented and found it made hot->cold transitions too slow for our bursty demos. Leaving bounce_rate as a penalty in the score gives more direct control and is easier to expose for tuning.
Marisol Ortega: request: add a knob to cap memory reclaimed per second to limit latency impact during compaction cycles.
Priya Nair: added kv.trimmer.max_ops_per_cycle and pacing; documented the knob and default in config/defaults.yaml.
Liam Patel: CI hit on linux-kernel-bind-check; looks unrelated but please re-run. Also add a short section in ops docs about rollout signals.
Priya Nair: re-ran CI, fixed a race in the mmap path that surfaced on the kernel-bind CI node, added docs/ops/kv-residency.md with rollout guidance.
Marisol Ortega: approving after documentation and the pacing knob were added.
Ethan Russo: approved - perf numbers look reasonable; recommend canary and 72h observation window for Dedicated.
Introduce residency controller and adaptive page trimmer to reduce KV cache fragmentation, reduce spill bytes under bursty load, and improve tail latency. Feature gated and off by default; can be enabled via kv.residency.enabled and configured via kv.trimmer.* flags.

Summary: Add a conditional lint cache priming step that only populates lint/test caches for affected subtrees, plus a release-sweep job to clean stale release artifacts from the release bucket and GitHub Releases.

Motivation: CI latency and cache churn have been increasing; many presubmit runs re-populate caches for unrelated folders which slows feedback. We also accumulate stale artifacts in the release bucket when release workflows are retried or aborted; that increases storage and complicates audits.

This PR introduces a lightweight toolchain-adapter pattern: a small shim that computes change-aware cache keys and primes caches only for impacted toolchains, and a release-sweep action that runs post-release in a best-effort, idempotent manner.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement conditional cache priming script (tools/ci/prime_lint_cache.sh)
- [x] Add new workflow .github/workflows/conditional-lint.yml
- [x] Introduce release sweep composite action .github/actions/release-sweep
- [x] Add docs to docs/ci/CHANGELOG.md (short note + how it works)
- [x] Add unit tests for the cache-key computation (tools/ci/tests/test_cache_key.py)
- [x] Run canary in staging and validate reduced warmup times

Context and design: The cache priming step runs early in presubmit pipelines. It calculates which "toolchains" (lint, gofmt, tsserver, python) need warm caches based on a git diff against main. Instead of a single global cache key, we build per-toolchain keys under prefix: ci/cache/<toolchain>/<short-key>. The priming script then attempts to fetch each relevant cache and, if missing, primes only that toolchain by running a minimal warm runner (lint dry-run or type-only build). The priming is best-effort and timeboxed (default 45s) so it cannot block fast feedback.

Release sweep: a composite action invoked by release workflows (after successful publish OR on workflow failure) that will: a) list objects with a release tag prefix and remove objects older than retention threshold (configurable via workflow inputs), b) close stale GitHub draft releases that are orphaned, c) emit telemetry events to our release-ops topic.

Safety: all destructive steps are gated by a dry-run by default and require explicit confirm input for production runs.

Implementation notes and changed areas (high level):
- .github/workflows/conditional-lint.yml: new presubmit path that runs for push/pull_request and includes the priming step before lint job.
- .github/actions/release-sweep/action.yml: composite action with awscli, gh cli invocations and safe dry-run toggles.
- tools/ci/prime_lint_cache.sh: shell shim that produces a newline-separated list of cache keys; small python helper tools/ci/cache_key.py for robust path matching.
- tools/ci/tests/test_cache_key.py: pytest unit tests asserting mapping heuristics for go/, node/, python/ changes.
- docs/ci/CHANGELOG.md: short entry describing behavior and config.

Commits (summary):
- 556677a: add conditional lint workflow and priming script
- 6b8d2c: add cache key library and tests
- 2d4f91: introduce release-sweep composite action with dry-run
- 9c1a0e: docs and cleanup
- f3b4ae: fix shell quoting and make priming timebox configurable

Reviews and conversation:
- Diego Ramos: "This is a great direction — reduces unnecessary cache churn. Two asks: 1) can we make the timebox configurable via workflow input for team owners? 2) add a smoke job that ensures the priming itself doesn't exceed 60s in CI."
- Author (Aisha): "Done — added timebox input with default 45s and a smoke job in conditional-lint.yml. See second commit 2d4f91 for the smoke job."
- Priya Nair: "Please add a small note about how the cache key maps to our paid cache tier to avoid surprises in billing."
- Author: "Added a section in docs/ci/CHANGELOG.md describing mapping and suggested cost thresholds."
- Jonah Keenan: "Release sweep looks fine but make sure dry-run is strict by default; do not run deletes without explicit confirm."
- Author: "Dry-run is default. Deletes require confirm=true in production workflows; added guard."

CI / checks:
- presubmit lint (golang, python, ts): pass (initial run had gofmt failure, fixed in f3b4ae)
- unit tests (pytest): pass
- integration smoke (conditional-lint smoke job): pass
- release-sweep action dry-run run in staging: pass

Metrics observed in staging canary (3/2 runs):
- average warmup time reduced from ~62s to ~18s for changed toolchain subsets
- per-pr cache writes reduced by ~55%

Issues and follow-ups:
- Follow-up task: ENG-2504 to wire release-ops telemetry into observability pipeline (now emits to release-ops topic but not yet surfaced)
- Follow-up: add similar priming to nightly matrix to populate long-lived caches (ENG-2505)

Merge and rollout: Merged to main via squash-merge after approvals from Diego and Priya. Rollout will be gradual: enable conditional-lint for core repos first (redwood, redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-typescript) then expand.

Release notes:
- Reduced presubmit feedback latency by avoiding full cache populates for unrelated changes
- Idempotent release-sweep that removes stale release artifacts when enabled
- New docs: docs/ci/CHANGELOG.md

How to revert: Revert the workflow file and tools/ci/* changes if we observe any regressions. The release-sweep composite action is non-destructive by default (dry-run), so immediate risk is low.

Motivation: CI feedback latency and flakiness have been steadily impacting developer velocity. This PR consolidates the CI 'boot sequence' steps into a deterministic, idempotent initializer, removes duplicated setup logic across multiple workflows, and introduces a conservative automated dependency pruning pass that removes unused top-level dev deps and surfaces suspects for manual review. Changes are limited to CI orchestration, small helpers, and the dep-rotator tool; no runtime application code is touched. Summary of changes: 1) Introduced ci/boot/bootstrap.sh and consolidated environment/credentials setup into a single entrypoint that is executed by lint, unit, and integration workflows; this reduces duplicated shell logic and lowers presubmit flake by standardizing PATH/KUBECONFIG handling. 2) Reworked ci/workflows/lint.yml and ci/workflows/test-matrix.yml to call the new bootstrap step and to expose a light-weight 'fastpath' lane for small PRs based on changed paths detection. 3) Added a minimal Go-based dep-rotator in tools/dep-rotator/ that runs static analysis against package manifests (go.mod, package.json) and outputs a proposed prune list; the rotator runs in dry-run mode by default and is gated behind a new label 'dep-approve' for auto-apply. 4) Added Makefile.ci with typed targets for common CI operations and documented the new flow in docs/ci/dep-policy.md and README.ci.md. 5) Small hygiene edits: removed obsolete helpers in scripts/ci-legacy-setup.sh, trimmed duplicated env vars in infra/helm/ci-values.yaml, and updated test runner docker image tag to reduce image-pull flakiness. Backwards compatibility and safety: bootstrap.sh has a strict dry-run / apply mode flag; workflows default to dry-run for dep-rotator; the fastpath triggers are conservative and require at least one approving reviewer for release branches. Rollout plan: roll out on canary for the monorepo (team-redwood/*) for 48 hours, then opt-in teams can flip 'fastpath' label for faster feedback. If any presubmit flake increases by >3% over baseline we will revert the fastpath lane while keeping the bootstrap consolidation. Checklist: [x] consolidated shell logic into single bootstrap entrypoint; [x] added Makefile.ci and docs; [x] dep-rotator initial implementation with dry-run; [x] added tests for boot sequence idempotency; [x] manual smoke run on staging CI; [x] coordinated with infra for image tag bump. Known limitations: dep-rotator is conservative and does not auto-edit transitive lockfiles yet; future iteration will include language-specific heuristics and a vetting dashboard. CI summary: initial run had a lint flake on macOS runner, fixed by pinning a brew package; subsequent runs passed full matrix. Related: ENG-1924 tracks the ci velocity improvements target, ENG-2001 captures repo-level dep hygiene initiative.
Aisha Patel: Can you add a feature-flag env var so infra can opt-out of fastpath on release branches?
Evan Turner: Added CI_FASTPATH_OPT_OUT and documented it in README.ci.md; workflows check for it before enabling fastpath.
Diego Ramos: Dep-rotator looks promising but I worry about false-positives on monorepo globs; can we restrict to explicit manifests per repo?
Evan Turner: Rotator now detects repository root and falls back to per-submodule manifest discovery; dry-run results are posted to the PR as an artifact.
Morgan Lee: Approving after smoke runs; please squash commits and ensure release pipeline is unchanged for release/* branches.
Evan Turner: Will squash on merge; release/* workflows are explicitly unchanged and call the bootstrap in apply=false mode.
consolidate: move shared env setup to ci/boot/bootstrap.sh
ci: wire lint/test workflows to bootstrap entrypoint
tools(dep-rotator): add initial analyzer with dry-run mode
docs: add README.ci and dep policy notes
chore: Makefile.ci and small image tag bump

This PR targeted decreased presubmit flakiness and shorter feedback loops. Post-merge monitoring: runbook created in docs/ci/post-merge-monitoring.md and will be observed for 72 hours. No breaking changes to runtime code. If dep-rotator identifies high-risk removals, a follow-up PR will surface a one-click rollback plan.

Context: Incident-bot v2 needs consistent “recent deploy context” during the first 5 minutes of an incident (service, image SHA, rollout phase, canary results, links). Today responders manually cross-reference Spinnaker/Argo + GitHub + our internal service registry, which increases MTTR (see #incidents thread 1739058123 and postmortem 2025-02-07 hosted API 503s). This PR adds a small internal export surface in the redwood control plane so incident-bot (and later Console) can query deploy metadata in a stable, machine-readable format. What’s in this PR: (1) New internal endpoint `GET /internal/deploy-metadata/recent` backed by the deploy controller’s rollout state store. Supports filters: `service`, `region`, `environment`, `limit`, and optional `since` (RFC3339). Response includes: service name (canonical registry key), image tag + image SHA, rollout phase (canary|ramp|full|rollback), rollout id, started_at, last_updated_at, and canary health summary (pass/fail/unknown + gate names). (2) Optional event stream emitter (`DeployMetadataExported`) behind a flag for consumers that prefer push (incident-bot currently will poll; event stream is for follow-up work to reduce query load). (3) Normalization logic to join rollout records to the canonical service registry (fixes “missing service mapping” issues seen in eng-releases 1740086015). (4) Guardrails: endpoint is restricted to service identities with `deploy-metadata:read` scope; response excludes tenant/customer identifiers by design; adds request logging with request_id + caller identity for auditability (detailed audit event wiring is handled in PR-29133). (5) Documentation: internal README for the schema, examples, and stability/versioning notes (`v1` schema with additive-only promise). Notes/decisions: The endpoint is intentionally not tenant-scoped; incident-bot uses it to show “what changed recently in this service/region” independent of tenant. If/when we need tenant-correlation, that should happen in the incident-bot telemetry/config collectors where we have stronger redaction/audit controls. The canary status is derived from the deploy controller’s gate results. When gates aren’t configured, canary_health will be `unknown` rather than failing the request. Rollout phase mapping is based on controller state machine; see `RolloutPhaseMapper` notes in code. Testing: Unit tests cover phase mapping, schema serialization, and service-registry join edge cases (unknown service -> omitted record + metric). Integration test spins up controller + registry fakes and exercises `GET /internal/deploy-metadata/recent?service=hosted-api&region=us-east-1`. Metrics: Adds `deploy_metadata_export_requests_total{status,caller}` and `deploy_metadata_export_join_failures_total{reason}` plus request duration histogram. Rollout: Endpoint is shipped dark behind `deploy_metadata_export_enabled` (default false). Release eng will enable in staging, then prod for incident-bot service identity only. Follow-ups (not in this PR): (a) add Console deep-link generator into response (owned by Chloe), (b) wire audit events to central SIEM (PR-29133), (c) incident-bot card rendering + link-out (incident-bot repo PR-1842).
Miles Thornton (review): Can we guarantee the service naming matches what incident-bot expects? We’ve had incidents where deploy events used a display name and responders couldn’t correlate.
Connor O'Brien (author): Yep — this uses the canonical service registry key (`service_registry_id`). If the rollout record can’t be joined, we drop it and emit `deploy_metadata_export_join_failures_total{reason="unknown_service"}` so we can catch drift. Added an example to the docs as well.
Sahana Iyer (review): Request: keep the response stable. Can we version the schema and promise additive changes only? Also please ensure we don’t accidentally include tenant/environment variables from the deploy spec.
Connor O'Brien (author): Added `schema_version: "v1"` to the response and documented additive-only promise. The handler uses a dedicated DTO that only includes the allowlisted fields; we don’t serialize the underlying deploy spec. Also added a unit test asserting no `tenant_id`-like keys exist in JSON.
Rafael Mendes (review): On failure modes: if the deploy controller store is degraded during an incident, we need fast timeouts. What are the defaults?
Connor O'Brien (author): Good call. Set handler timeout to 750ms and hard cap to `limit<=20`. If store query exceeds timeout, we return 200 with `partial=true` and `errors=["timeout_querying_rollout_store"]` (incident-bot will render the card with a warning + links).
Ethan Park (review): Authz: please ensure this is service-identity only and not user sessions. Also avoid making it accessible via the general internal gateway without scopes.
Connor O'Brien (author): Implemented `requireServiceIdentity()` middleware + scope check `deploy-metadata:read`. User sessions will get 403. Route is under internal service mesh only (no public gateway).
Miles Thornton (review): Can we add a quick example response for the bot team to code against?
Connor O'Brien (author): Added to docs/internal/deploy-metadata-export.md with fields: service, region, rollout_phase, canary_health, image_sha, started_at, rollout_id.
Sahana Iyer (review): Approving once CI is green.
System: CI was failing: integration-tests (control-plane) — fail (flaky clock dependency).
Connor O'Brien (author): Fixed by injecting a fake clock into the handler test; reran CI.
System: All checks passed.
Sahana Iyer (review): Approved.
Miles Thornton (review): Approved — bot team can start integrating.

Motivation: Many tenants have predictable budget envelopes but heterogeneous traffic shapes. Default batching/caching and quantization profiles were static and either underutilized budget (too conservative) or violated latency SLOs (too aggressive). This PR introduces 'Pulse' — a lightweight prefill sampler + quant prioritizer that dynamically suggests tenant-scoped defaults and exposes a dry-run CLI for conservative rollout.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a telemetry adapter that translates per-tenant cost/latency traces into candidate prefill/batching defaults and a ranked set of quantization profiles. The adapter publishes suggestions to the prefill engine via the existing defaults API.
- Implements a Pulse sampler daemon (prefill/pulse_sampler) that runs short synthetic samples against model variants to estimate latency/quality tradeoffs for candidate quant profiles. Sampling is workload-weighted (recent traffic sketches) to avoid noisy signals from tiny routes.
- Adds a prioritizer: a simple scoring function combining unit-econ delta, 99p latency delta, and measured quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE-like or model-specific regression metric) to rank quant candidates.
- Introduces a CLI (rb-pulse dry-run) that operators can use to run deterministic dry-runs against a tenant, producing a report and a suggested defaults bundle. The CLI supports a --simulate flag to run in simulation mode using historical traces.
- Adds end-to-end integration tests and new telemetry dashboards (docs/reference/pulse) and a short playbook for rolling changes.

Why different: Prior PRs autotuned defaults from long-running batch signals. Pulse focuses on rapid, safe exploration: sample small micro-batches across a compact quant grid and present ranked options, not automatic rollouts. It lowers human review overhead with a deterministic report and promotes safe manual adoption.

Design notes:
- Score = w_cost * normalized_cost_savings + w_latency * normalized_99p_latency_change + w_quality * normalized_quality_change. Weights default to (0.5, 0.3, 0.2) but are tenant-configurable.
- Sampling uses shadow-mode requests and does not touch live KV caches. Any candidate that increases 99p latency by >20% is filtered by default.
- Quant profiles tested: [fp16, int8-qweight, int8-qkv, int4-mixed] with fallback to fp16 if quality regressions >2% on the tenant's eval set.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests for scorer, adapter translation logic, and CLI parsing.
- Integration tests that spin up a small local runtime and run 50-sample sketches to validate latency/quality signals.
- E2E smoke on staging that simulates tenant traces using the simulate flag.

Files changed (high level):
- prefill/pulse_sampler/*.py: main sampler, scheduler, local cache of sketches
- telemetry/adapters/pulse_adapter.go: translates spans/metrics into suggestion payloads
- cli/rb_pulse/main.rs: dry-run CLI and simulate flag
- prefill/service_defaults_api.proto: small API addition (SuggestBundle message)
- docs/reference/pulse.md: operator guide and interpretation of reports
- tests/integration/test_pulse_endtoend.py, tests/unit/test_pulse_scorer.py

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy telemetry adapter to staging and enable for a handful of low-risk tenants (opt-in).
2) Run CLI dry-runs and gather operator feedback for 2 weeks.
3) Publish suggested defaults to internal defaults-staging for manual canary adopters.
4) If metrics stable, promote suggestions to defaults-prod as manual commits (no automatic apply).

Backward compatibility: The adapter and CLI are additive. Existing defaults API remains unchanged for consumers. Pulse suggestions are advisory by default (no automatic apply).

Security/privilege: Pulse requires read-only access to tenant traces and read-only access to model eval harness. The CLI requires operator privileges to produce suggestions for other tenants.

Open items / future follow-ups:
- Add soft-automatic-apply mode behind a feature flag for tenants that opt into 'aggressive-econ' experiments.
- Expand quant grid and integrate hardware-backed latency models for faster estimates.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration smoke added
- [x] Docs: operator guide + example report
- [x] Telemetry dashboards (staging)
- [x] Security review (read-only)

Related Linear: ENG-1287 prioritizer design, ENG-1314 CLI and telemetry plumbing.

Supporting artifacts: sample dry-run report for tenant 'acme-pay' is attached to the Linear ticket (ENG-1287).
Diego Ramos (2025-11-04): Can you add an integration test that validates the 99p filter behavior? I want to see a failing case where a candidate spikes 99p latency and gets rejected.
Maya Patel (2025-11-05): Added tests/integration/test_pulse_endtoend.py and a failing fixture to assert the 99p filter. Also included a small synthetic harness to reproduce the regression locally.
Priya Singh (2025-11-06): The scoring weights default look reasonable, but we should expose tenant-level overrides in the config. Can you add a config fallback chain (tenant -> team -> global)?
Maya Patel (2025-11-07): Added pkg/config/pulse_defaults.toml and wired the fallback chain. Documented in docs/reference/pulse.md.
Ethan Cole (2025-11-09): CI initially failed on linting for telemetry adapter (unused import). Once fixed, can we run a longer smoke on staging to validate no KV cache leakage?
Maya Patel (2025-11-10): Fixed lint and added additional assertions to ensure sampler runs in shadow mode without modifying KV cache. CI green after rerun.
Diego Ramos (2025-11-11): Approved after verifying tests + running a manual dry-run for tenant 'alpha-inc' on staging. All good.
Introduce Pulse: a prefill sampler and quant prioritizer that generates tenant-scoped default suggestions via a dry-run CLI. Advisory-only suggestions, safe-by-default filters (99p latency guard). Adds telemetry adapter, sampler daemon, scorer, integration tests, and operator docs.

Summary
This PR introduces an SLO evaluation hook into the rollout controller state machine. The controller can now consult an external SLO evaluator for the exact rollout scope (service/route + model version + region + customer tier) and take a conservative automatic action.

MVP behavior in this PR is pause-only (no rollback execution). If an SLO breach is confirmed, the rollout is paused at the current step and an audit event is emitted. When SLO data is missing/stale/insufficient, we do not pause (fail-open) but we record a structured reason for visibility.

Motivation
We’ve had multiple latency/error regressions during canary/A-B rollouts where the window between detection and manual intervention is too large. This adds the wiring point so follow-on PRs can plug in:
- policy/config evaluation (thresholds, windows, debounce)
- the monitor provider adapter (burn rate + sample size)
- rollback executor (traffic shift back to baseline)

Key changes
- Adds a RolloutSloEvaluator interface and wires it into the controller loop.
- Adds a feature flag gate: rollouts.auto_slo_eval.enabled (default: false).
- Adds pause-only action outcome:
  - If evaluator returns BREACH_CONFIRMED => controller transitions to PAUSED with reason AUTO_PAUSE_SLO_BREACH.
  - If evaluator returns OK => no change.
  - If evaluator returns INSUFFICIENT_DATA / MONITOR_MISSING / MONITOR_STALE / EVAL_ERROR => no change, emit structured log + audit event w/ suppression_reason.
- Adds unit tests covering state transitions and idempotency.

Notes / non-goals
- No rollback action is executed in this PR (follow-up: rollback executor + safe traffic shift).
- No burn-rate window/debounce logic lives here; this PR only introduces the hook and the contract.
- No Console API changes here; audit event is emitted but not yet surfaced.

Implementation details
- The hook is invoked after a step has been applied (i.e., traffic split update committed) and before advancing to the next step.
- Evaluator input is a RolloutScope derived from rollout metadata:
  - service_id, route_id
  - model_id + candidate_version_id
  - region
  - customer_tier
- Controller behavior is explicitly idempotent:
  - If already PAUSED, repeated BREACH_CONFIRMED responses do not re-emit the pause action.

Testing
- Added controller unit tests:
  - pauses rollout when evaluator reports breach
  - does not pause on missing/stale/insufficient data
  - does not pause when flag disabled
  - evaluator error is treated as fail-open (no pause)
  - idempotent pause (no duplicate events)

Rollout plan
- Land behind flag (off by default).
- Enable in dev/staging for internal canaries after monitor adapter PR is ready.

Related
- Linear: ENG-4821
- Design/PRD: Auto-rollback on SLO breach integration (see Confluence)

Checklist
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Flag default is disabled
- [x] Logging does not include customer prompt content
- [x] Controller remains functional when evaluator is unset (no-op evaluator)

Ethan Park (review): Can we confirm the hook is invoked after the traffic split change is persisted? If called before, we might pause based on SLOs that reflect the *previous* step.
Jada Williams (author): Good catch. Updated to invoke after ApplyStep() returns success and we have the new step_index committed. Added a unit test that asserts ordering around ApplyStep vs Evaluate().

Jordan Lee (review): The feature flag key name should match the convention used by policy engine flags (dot-separated). Also please ensure the evaluator contract makes it explicit that debounce/windows are not implemented here.
Jada Williams (author): Renamed flag to rollouts.auto_slo_eval.enabled and added docstrings in the interface clarifying controller only consumes a pre-evaluated decision.

Sean Gallagher (review): For MVP, I agree with pause-only, but I strongly prefer fail-open on monitor missing/stale to avoid accidental pauses during telemetry outages. Please add a structured audit/log reason so we can see when we’re blind.
Jada Williams (author): Implemented fail-open for MONITOR_MISSING / MONITOR_STALE / INSUFFICIENT_DATA / EVAL_ERROR and emit an audit event with suppression_reason=<reason>. No paging yet; that will come with dashboards.

Chloe Martin (review): Minor: the pause reason enum should be stable for Console. Also avoid putting rollout name strings in logs; use rollout_id.
Jada Williams (author): Updated to log rollout_id + scope fields only, and made AUTO_PAUSE_SLO_BREACH a stable string constant in audit schema.

Approvals
- Ethan Park: Approved
- Jordan Lee: Approved
- Sean Gallagher: Approved
- Chloe Martin: Approved

Adds a lightweight session-stabilizer and replayable-shadow safeguard to the rollout controller to improve canary/A-B promotions for sessionful workloads. Motivation: our current staged-promote flow can prematurely promote model variants that break user sessions under slow KV-cache warming and transient routing skew; this PR introduces a non-blocking session quiesce probe, compact session checkpoints (snapshots), and a replayable shadow rehearsal mode that runs a sampled, synthetic replay of live traffic against the candidate model before commit. Key behaviors: (1) stabilizer enforces a minimum session-cohort consistency window during ramp-up to avoid split-affinity anomalies; (2) snapshots are compact (delta encoded) and stored in the rollout ledger so staged rollback can rewind to a known good session mapping; (3) replayable shadow runs on a fraction of traffic with deterministic seeding and preserves ordering to exercise session paths; (4) telemetry gates (latency, user-facing error rate, session-drop metric) are evaluated by the rollout engine and can trigger automatic backout with rewindable snapshots; (5) dry-run mode allows ops to preview snapshot generation and replay without altering routing. Implementation notes: added a new stabilizer plugin (stabilizers/session_stabilizer.go) and a compact snapshot serializer (snapshot/delta_serializer.go); extended the rollout ledger schema with snapshot metadata and retention hints; added a controlled shadow-replay worker pool with deterministic sampling and kv-cache warmup stalls to better surface regressions. Tests and validation: unit tests for snapshot compacting and stabilizer heuristics; integration harness that spins up a mini_shadow_rehearsal job and asserts deterministic replay traces against golden prompts; load-smoke e2e in perf-canary demonstrates no >1% additional p95 token latency overhead when shadow replay is enabled at 5% traffic. Backwards compatibility and rollout safety: the feature is off by default and gated behind rollout policy flags; snapshots use a new namespaced ledger bucket to avoid collisions; we included migration code that will be no-op for customers who do not enable the policy. Checklist: [x] design doc linked ENG-4021; [x] unit + integration tests added; [x] docs page and quickstart updated; [x] feature-flag gating; [x] added rollback playbook snippet. Related: ENG-4127 (telemetry gate tuning), SUP-221 (customer incident that motivated session regressions).
Jonah Park: Nice approach; can you clarify the cost tradeoff for retained snapshots? Suggest retention defaults and a TTL policy.
Ayesha Malik: Reply: snapshots are delta-encoded and capped; default retention is 3 revisions per rollout with 7d TTL; added config and doc note.
Diego Ramos: Request changes: ensure deterministic sampler uses global seed derived from rollout id to avoid cross-run variance.
Ayesha Malik: Reply: addressed, sampler seed now rollout-scoped; added unit and integration tests to assert determinism.
Priya Singhal: Approve after minor docs nits fixed.
CI Bot: All green after rerun of flaky e2e; merging when ready.
Introduce session-stabilizer plugin to reduce session affinity regressions during staged rollouts.
Add replayable shadow rehearsal mode to run deterministic, sampled replays before promotion.
Snapshots (delta-encoded) enable rewindable rollbacks for sessionful workloads.
payload.title: Lightweight session stabilizer with replayable shadow safeguard

payload.body:
Title: Add missing region dimension to usage events (Hosted API + OpenAI-compat)

Context
We found a non-trivial % of Hosted API usage_events in Snowflake with region = NULL or an incorrect value (notably for OpenAI-compatible endpoints, some streaming paths, and retry/fallback routing). This breaks pricing attribution (region-based price books), distorts gross margin reporting, and creates reconciliation noise between ledger aggregates and customer usage exports.

Root cause
- The API gateway request context has a canonical region (edge_region / compute_region depending on route), but the usage event builder was reading region from an optional field that isn’t populated for all ingress paths.
- OpenAI-compat handler was bypassing the standard request_context plumbing for a subset of endpoints.
- Streaming retries/fallback could emit a usage event from a path where region wasn’t re-attached after request replay.

What this PR changes
1) Canonicalize region selection in the telemetry layer
- Introduces a single helper to compute usage_event.region with priority:
  (a) request_context.compute_region (preferred when available)
  (b) request_context.edge_region
  (c) resolved region from routing decision (when request_context is missing)
- Ensures we never emit NULL for region; if we cannot resolve, we emit "unknown" and increment a counter (see Metrics).

2) Wire region into OpenAI-compatible endpoints
- OpenAI-compat request handlers now pass through the same RequestContext used by Redwood-native endpoints.
- Ensures streaming and non-streaming OpenAI-compat responses share the same telemetry envelope.

3) Make region required in the usage event schema (soft enforcement)
- We do not hard-fail requests if region resolution fails; instead we set region="unknown" and flag it.
- Adds a validation step in the event emitter that logs structured warnings when emitting unknown.

4) Tests
- Unit tests for region resolution priority order.
- Integration test covering OpenAI-compat chat.completions streaming with simulated fallback retry path.
- Regression test for “region missing => unknown + metric increment” behavior.

5) Observability
- New counters:
  - usage_events_region_unknown_total{route, endpoint_family}
  - usage_events_region_mismatch_total{expected_source, actual_source}
- Adds region null-rate to the metering sanity checks query pack (used by Finance/Eng) (note: alert wiring tracked separately).

Data impact / billing safety
- This change does not affect billed token computation or request counting. It only fixes a missing/incorrect dimension.
- Downstream: pricing attribution and margin dashboards become correct for affected traffic.
- We are not retroactively changing invoices via this PR. If Finance wants a backfill for internal analytics / exports, we should do that as a separate, controlled job with a documented freeze window and sign-off.

Rollout plan
- Deploy behind feature flag telemetry.region_dimension_v1 (default ON in staging, 10% prod for 24h, then 100%).
- During rollout, monitor:
  - region_unknown rate (target < 0.01% overall)
  - drift vs ledger by region should decrease (no new drift introduced)
  - OpenAI-compat endpoints: region_null should go to ~0

Testing
- buildkite: unit + integration suite
- staging: manually exercised:
  - /v1/chat/completions (streaming + non-streaming)
  - /v1/completions
  - /v1/embeddings (batch)
  - fallback routing simulation (forced capacity constraint)

Screenshots / evidence
- Before: region null-rate for openai_compat endpoints spiked to 8–12% depending on day.
- After (staging): region null-rate 0%, unknown-rate ~0.003% (expected from synthetic tests missing routing metadata).

Changed areas (high-level)
- services/api-gateway/request_context.ts
- services/openai-compat/handlers/chat_completions.ts
- services/telemetry/usage_event_builder.ts
- services/telemetry/schema/usage_event.avsc
- services/telemetry/tests/region_dimension.test.ts
- services/telemetry/tests/openai_compat_streaming_retry_region.test.ts

Commits (summary)
- telemetry: canonicalize region resolution + add unknown fallback
- openai-compat: plumb request context into usage event builder
- schema/tests: add region field validation + regression coverage
- metrics: add unknown/mismatch counters + log sampling

Review conversation (selected)
Logan Wright (EM Telemetry): Can we guarantee we’re not writing nulls anymore? Also please confirm the routing decision is available on the retry path.
Caleb Johnson (author): Yes, builder now sets "unknown" if it can’t resolve. Retry path now rehydrates RequestContext from the original attempt and falls back to routing decision only if missing.

Nadia Rahman (Staff Telemetry): Please document precedence (compute vs edge) and make sure Dedicated isn’t accidentally using edge_region.
Caleb Johnson: Added precedence comment + unit tests; Dedicated paths use pool_region and do not hit this code path.

Mei Lin (Recon datasets): Any schema compat risk for the Snowflake export? I want to avoid breaking the reconciliation export job.
Caleb Johnson: Kept the field name consistent (region already existed as nullable in the downstream table, but ingestion was not populating it). Schema change is “soft required” at emitter only; export schema remains compatible.

Aisha Bello (SLO/Alerts): Can you add a metric for unknown and an easy panel dimension suggestion?
Caleb Johnson: Added usage_events_region_unknown_total and tagged by endpoint_family; will follow up in the dashboard PR to add the panel.

Follow-ups
- (Separate PR) Optional backfill for analytics/exports with Finance sign-off + freeze window.
- (ENG-4421) Alert on region_unknown rate and drift-by-region after we have a stable baseline.

Merge
- Squash merged to main after approvals and green CI.
Usage events now consistently include `region` for Hosted API requests (including OpenAI-compatible endpoints and streaming). This improves pricing/margin attribution and reduces invoice/export discrepancies without changing token counting.
payload.title: Add missing region dimension to usage events (Hosted API + OpenAI-compat)

payload.body:
Motivation: Users integrating structured outputs (JSON schema via response_format) with tool/function calling reported brittle behavior when streamed tool outputs diverged from client-provided schemas. This PR introduces a lightweight contract-metadata layer that travels in-stream so the runtime and client can reach a consensus about which schema variant applies, plus an opt-in strict enforcement mode for tool call results. Goals: 1) Stabilize streaming behavior during tool/function calling so partial tool responses do not cause inconsistent validation errors; 2) Provide clear, machine-friendly error IDs and diagnostic hints when strict validation fails; 3) Maintain OpenAI-compatibility as a default by keeping behavior permissive unless strict mode is enabled. Design summary: We add a new contract-metadata header to the stream envelope (x-contract-schema-id, x-contract-source) which is emitted by the model adapter and echoed by the tool runner when a tool is invoked. The runtime now performs a two-step consensus check: prefer client-specified schema_id, fall back to model-declared schema if the client did not supply one, and in ambiguous cases emit a contract-disagreement event but continue streaming in permissive mode. Strict mode (enabled via response_format.strict = true or response header X-Response-Strict: true) causes the runtime to buffer the final tool payload, run JSONSchema v2020 validation, and if it fails emit a structured error object with fields {error_id, path, expected, received_snippet, severity_hint}. To keep streaming stable for latency-sensitive paths, when strict validation is enabled we allow a short resumable buffering window (200ms default) and do not abort the stream early; when validation ultimately fails we append a terminal validation event and a human-readable suggestion string. Implementation highlights: - Streaming protocol changes: small additions to the stream envelope so existing clients ignore unknown headers; implementation guarded by feature flag 'contract-metadata' for rollout. - Tool runner changes: echo x-contract-schema-id and annotate emitted stdout/stderr chunks with chunk-level schema anchors when available. - Runtime validator: pluggable validator that supports schema version negotiation (v4/v7/v2020) and returns standardized error IDs; validation runs in worker pool to avoid blocking the main recv loop. - SDKs: python and typescript SDKs updated to surface the final validation event and translate error_id into typed exceptions for convenience. - OpenAI-compat shim: when the request includes openai_compat: true, we map our validation event to an openai-style finish_reason and include the structured error in the last chunk under 'metadata' so most existing clients can continue to parse streams. Testing and rollout: unit tests for streaming envelope parsing (server and client), integration tests that simulate divergent schemas between model/tool/client, e2e canary in staging that enables 'contract-metadata' for 5% of traffic, and live traffic monitoring dashboards for contract_disagreement_count and strict_validation_fail_rate. Checklist: - [x] schema header and envelope format defined and documented; - [x] runtime dispatching and buffering implemented; - [x] validator worker and error ID mappings added; - [x] tool-runner echoing implemented; - [x] python and ts SDK hooks implemented; - [x] OpenAI compatibility shim verified; - [x] canary rollout plan created. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is permissive if no strict flag provided; unknown stream headers are ignored by older clients. Risks and mitigations: risk of added latency when strict mode enabled; mitigated by buffered window + worker pool and a per-tenant throttle; risk of increased error noise during early rollout; mitigated via canary and metrics gating. Related work: builds on prior schema checkpointing work (see ENG-6233) and improves on the 'resume token' approach by adding explicit contract metadata to stream events. Docs: updated redwood docs with examples for response_format.strict and SDK mapping for error_id. Rollout: feature-flag rollout over two weeks with observability thresholds for rollback.
Adds contract metadata headers for streaming events; introduces opt-in strict schema enforcement for tool/function-call results with standardized error IDs; backward-compatible by default; rollout via flag and canary.
Ethan Li: Can we avoid blocking the main streamer on validation? The worker pool approach looks good but add quotas per-tenant.
Maya Chen (author): Added per-tenant quota and metrics; validation queue depth exposed as metric.
Sofia Ramirez: SDK error_id string format should be stable. Please include semantic versioning for error catalogue.
Maya Chen (author): Added error_catalog_version header and updated SDK mapping code to include catalog_version in exceptions.
Victor Huang: What about non-json tool outputs (plain text)? Shouldn't validation be best-effort only?
Maya Chen (author): We skip validation for non-json content-types; added detection and clear audit log lines for skipped validations.
QA (automated): integration test test_toolcall_schema_mismatch.py failed initially due to race; fixed by extending buffering window to 200ms and adding retry in test harness.
SRE: please ensure Alert runbook includes steps to disable strict mode per-tenant. Added to ops runbook under docs/ops/strict-mode-rollbacks.md.
payload.title: introduce-contract-metadata-and-strict-schema-handling-for-streamed-tool-calls

Context: During the last two incidents we observed oscillatory behavior when nodes briefly lost capacity and the global circuit opened aggressively, which caused downstream cold-start cascades and client errors. This PR implements a probationary fallback coordinator: a lightweight controller that mediates soft fallbacks (temporarily reducing token budgets and trimming request load) in a bounded window before escalating to full circuit open. Motivation: reduce noisy, immediate circuit openings while preserving SLO protection and preventing capacity thrash. Goals: 1) Give transient hotspots a short probationary period (configurable window 10-60s) where we apply conservative load trimming and tenant-specific token budgets. 2) Emit rich audit events and metrics so SRE can validate that probationary windows reduce full-circuit opens. 3) Integrate with regional routing so fallout is limited to affected zones rather than global. Major changes: - New probationary coordinator component that subscribes to SLO violation signals and maintains ephemeral per-tenant/per-route windows. - Windowed Load Trimming policy that drops or short-circuits low-value tokens according to a token-weight heuristic (configurable thresholds). - SLO Enforcer integration: coordinator can request a soft-shed action first; only if probationary windows expire or re-trigger does the enforcer escalate to deprio/circuit. - Regional router updates to prefer local probationary decisions and to fall back to cross-region only when probationary windows are saturated. - Observability: fallback_metrics and tracing for window lifecycle, decisions, and reason codes. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-8934) - [x] unit tests for coordinator logic - [x] integration smoke test for regional failover path - [x] metrics and tracing added - [x] config knobs and sensible defaults - [x] add migration notes for configmap and defaults Testing notes: ran the full serving unit test suite; created a local canary with synthetic traffic bursts to validate that probationary windows reduce circuit opens by ~62% in our simulation. Benchmarks: median p99 latency under burst was reduced by ~120ms compared to immediate circuit approach at equivalent throughput. Files changed (high level): added coordinator and policy implementations under src/serving/fallback, small surface changes to regional_router to accept probationary hints, added tests under pkg/slo and src/serving, added a Kubernetes configmap with knobs. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: mis-tuned window might delay necessary full-circuit opens for real sustained overloads. Mitigation: windows are opt-in per-tenant and default to short durations (15s) with immediate escalation if error rates exceed a hard threshold. - Risk: added complexity to routing decision path. Mitigation: minimal on-path logic; coordinator runs as separate goroutine and communicates via existing enforcer RPC with stable protobufs. Operational playbook: on rollout, enable probationary coordinator in a small subset of regions and monitor fallback_metrics.probationary.window_succeeded and .escalated counters. If we see sustained escalations or increased errors, revert configmap to disable. Release notes: Soft probationary fallback coordinator and windowed load trimming to reduce noisy full-circuit opens during transient capacity loss. How to review: focus on coordinator correctness, the token-weight heuristic, and the SLO-enforcer integration test. Related work: builds on ENG-7612 (regional routing improvements) and complements ENG-9050 (SLO enforcement hardening).
Samir Patel: Quick note — please ensure the token-weight heuristic includes a per-tenant decay so a single burst doesn't permanently bias decisions.
Ava Chen (author): Added exponential decay with 30s half-life; documented in windowed_trim_policy.go comments.
Lina Rodriguez: Can you add a short-circuit test where probationary window and immediate-error threshold both trigger? We should verify escalation correctness.
Ava Chen (author): Added enforcer_integration_test to simulate simultaneous triggers and validated escalation path.
Marta Green: Observability looks good. Can we add a Grafana panel recipe to the metrics doc for quick SRE oncall checks?
Ava Chen (author): Added a /observability/metrics/fallback_metrics.md section with suggested panels and alert thresholds.
CI pipeline: unit-tests -> lint -> integration-smoke (regional) -> e2e-canary. Initial run: lint failed for trailing whitespace; fixed in follow-up commit. Integration smoke flaked once on the regional router test (timeout) and was re-run; final status: all checks pass. Full CI log links: (internal) ci/build/998776/units, ci/build/998776/integration, ci/build/998776/e2e; timestamps included in the internal runbook.
Merged to main via squash after approvals from Samir, Lina, and Marta. No conflicts. Post-merge action: rolled out configmap to canary regions and created a dashboard for probationary windows. Included a follow-up ticket ENG-9102 to add a runtime flag for emergency disable.
Add probationary fallback coordinator with windowed load trimming to reduce noisy circuit openings and improve p99 latency under transient capacity loss. Default enabled only in canary regions. Config knobs available in fallback-configmap.yaml.
Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to staging for 24h, validate metrics (fallback_metrics.probationary.window_succeeded ratio > 0.5 and circuit.opens decreased), 2) Enable in two canary regions for 48h, monitor error budget burn and escalations, 3) Gradual global rollout if stable. Emergency rollback: set fallback-configmap.disable_probationary = true and restart coordinator pods.
This PR prioritizes soft recovery strategies that reduce global impact of transient overloaded nodes. It is intentionally conservative: opt-in per tenant and short default windows. Follow-up work will include a machine-learned token-value estimator (ENG-9102) and a canary alert to auto-disable if escalation rate increases beyond baseline.
payload.title: probationary-fallback-coordinator-and-windowed-load-trim

Motivation: Our monolithic lint workflow has grown slow and noisy; small frontend or SDK changes often wait ~12-15 minutes for irrelevant lint shards, and dependency churn in lockfiles frequently triggers full CI runs and noisy alerts. This PR splits the lint matrix by package ownership, adds a lightweight dependency-stability scanner that surfaces transitive churn risk, and wires a ‘release lightprobe’ smoke job for release automation to validate runtime-critical paths quickly.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces a package ownership map and a partitioned lint workflow so only owners' lint/test shards run for small, ownership-scoped changes.
- Adds a dep-stability scanner job that computes a stability score for modified lockfiles / package manifests and uploads a small JSON artifact to the PR (used by release gating).
- Adds a release lightprobe job that runs a minimal end-to-end smoke script against a staging runtime to catch regressions that lint/unit tests miss.
- Updates developer docs and the devtooling Make targets to generate the owner map automatically from CODEOWNERS and manifest tags.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Partitioning approach: Owner-map driven partitioning keeps the job matrix small and stable. Default behavior falls back to 'global' shard when ownership cannot be determined. We opted for JSON-based owner map generated from CODEOWNERS to avoid duplicating metadata.
- Dep-stability scanner: conservative heuristics (major version bumps, new transitive hosts, binary-native deps) are used. The scanner is intentionally permissive and emits warnings rather than blocking; the release gating can be configured to escalate.
- Release lightprobe: a short (~45s) smoke script that validates basic model-serving flows and the token billing path. Runs only on release candidates or when the release pipeline opts into lightprobe.

Checklist: 
- [x] Partitioned lint workflow with owner-map lookup
- [x] dep-stability scanner implemented (Go small utility under tools/)
- [x] release lightprobe smoke script and workflow job
- [x] docs: CONTRIBUTING.md update + dev/owner-map README
- [x] tests for ownership heuristics + unit tests for the Go scanner
- [x] CI integration and artifact publishing for scanner results

Commits (summary):
- initial: add owner-map generator and partitioned-lint workflow
- tools: add dep-stability scanner (tools/dep-stability/main.go) + unit tests
- ci: add .github/workflows/dep-stability-scan.yaml and release-lightprobe.yaml
- scripts: add scripts/lightprobe-smoke.sh and Makefile targets for dev tooling
- docs: update CONTRIBUTING.md and add dev/owner-map/README.md
- fix: ownership lookup fallback and flake guard in scanner tests

Changed areas (high level):
- .github/workflows/partitioned-lint.yaml (new): matrix computed at runtime using owner-map artifact; fallback to full-lint when necessary
- .github/workflows/dep-stability-scan.yaml (new): run scanner for PRs touching lockfiles/manifests; uploads artifact to PR
- .github/workflows/release-lightprobe.yaml (new): opt-in smoke for release candidates + manual trigger
- tools/dep-stability/main.go (new): lightweight scanner that outputs stability-summary.json
- dev/owner-map/generate_owner_map.go (new): generator and tests that pull CODEOWNERS + manifest tags
- scripts/lightprobe-smoke.sh (new): minimal E2E smoke shell script used by release jobs
- CONTRIBUTING.md (updated): guidelines for owner tags and dev workflow
- Makefile (updated): new targets: make owner-map, make dep-scan-local
- pkg/ci/owner_map.json (new generated artifact placeholder)

Review conversation (highlights):
- Amit Patel (review): "Nice reduction in CI surface. A couple of questions: how do we ensure we don't gate critical cross-cutting infra changes behind an owner map? Also please add metrics to understand what % of PRs get fast feedback."
- Maya (author): "Added a fallback 'global' shard for any path touching infra/ci or top-level directories and an annotation to always run global-lint on PRs that modify .github or tools/. Also added a telemetry counter step that emits 'ci.fast_feedback.v1' metric; can be toggled off via env."
- Sofia Martins (review): "Dep scanner looks useful, but the heuristic for native deps flagged some false positives in my local run. Can we add an allowlist config?"
- Maya: "Added a small allowlist under tools/dep-stability/allowlist.yaml and a unit test for the previous false positive case. Marked the scanner job non-blocking by default. We can promote it to a hard gate after another 2 weeks of traffic."
- Lucas Rivera (approval): "Approach looks good; please squash the last nit fix commit and we can merge. Confirmed CI green after rerun."

CI summary and notable events: 
- matrix: lint-fast (targeted shards) — pass on first run for most shards
- lint-full (fallback global) — skipped for ownership-scoped PRs; ran once for infra-touching paths
- unit-tests — pass (2 reruns to stabilize a flaky db test; rerun successful)
- dep-stability-scan — pass, artifact uploaded (stability-summary.json)
- release-lightprobe — pass in staged run (manual trigger in test)
- e2e-nightly — not run for PRs
- Overall run: green after re-run of unit-tests; CI status set to pass and gating checks updated accordingly

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after approvals and green CI. Merge performed by Lucas Rivera. The squashed commit message includes a short summary and the most relevant checklist items.

How to validate locally (dev notes):
- make owner-map  # generates dev/owner-map/owner_map.json from CODEOWNERS
- go test ./tools/dep-stability -run TestScanner -v
- ./scripts/lightprobe-smoke.sh --local-staging  # runs minimal smoke against local dev runtime

Follow-ups and rollout plan: 
- Monitor ci.fast_feedback.v1 telemetry for 2 weeks; revert owner mappings causing excessive global falls back.
- Add a GitHub App hook to annotate PRs with stability-summary badges (UX follow-up).
- Consider promoting dep-stability-scan to blocking for lockfile PRs after 30 days if false positive rate < 5%.

Notes for on-call and SRE: The release lightprobe should be considered an additional safety net but not a replacement for full release smoke. The lightprobe will be gated by the same RBAC token used by the release pipeline; ensure the token has read-only access and the minimum required scopes.

References: Linear tickets ENG-4287 (partition lint rollout) and ENG-4300 (dep-stability scanner), internal doc dev/owner-map/README.md and tools/dep-stability/README.md.
payload.title: Partition lint pipelines by package ownership; add dependency-stability scanner and release lightprobe

Context / motivation: customers and SREs have surfaced incidents where token-cost spikes correlate with rapid retry loops and downstream errors, but our current token-level telemetry and logs make it hard to attribute cost to a causal error surface. This PR introduces two complementary observability features: (1) a Token Credit Meter that tracks per-invocation 'credit' consumption per token phase and exposes rate-normalized delta metrics for short and long tails, and (2) Contextual Error Tags that attach lightweight error-class fingerprints to spans/logs so traces and dashboards can quickly group cost spikes by error mode. Goals: reduce mean time to detect cost-causing errors, enable alert rules that target cost-anomalies with contextual grouping (so noisy long-tail errors don't trigger noisy pages), and provide dashboard panels that let product and SRE teams explore token cost by error cluster. Summary of changes: - Runtime metrics: new counter/gauge set under observations.token_credit.{issued,consumed,expired} with labels: tenant_id, model_name, invocation_stage (prefill, decode, finalize), error_class (optional). Added normalized per-second and per-invocation rate variants. - Trace/log instrumentation: attach contextual_error_tag to spans and emitted logs when downstream adapters return specific error classes (timeout, rate-limit, invalid-response, precondition-failure). Motivation: Provide a defensible, auditable mapping from a service-level 'owner' claim to RBAC v2 role bindings and ensure KMS operations carry provenance tied to that owner. This change introduces a lightweight operator-side claim propagation path and a gatekeeper component that validates KMS requests against a provenance assertion before allowing key-wrap/unwrap operations. The goal is to improve incident forensics, reduce accidental cross-tenant KMS usage, and make region-pin decisions deterministic when an explicit owner claim is present. Summary of changes: 1) Add an ownership-claim extractor that reads service identity, explicit owner annotations, and fallback tenant metadata; normalizes claim format and emits a signed claim token used by downstream services. 2) RBAC v2 adapter: map ownership claim -> temporary derivative roles (read-only, crypto-op) and attach TTL-limited grants via the policy engine. 3) KMS provenance gatekeeper: middleware in the KMS proxy that validates the signed claim, checks residency constraints (region pin and locality policies), and stamps audit envelopes with origin provenance. 4) Audit enrichment: include owner.id, owner.role, and claim-hash in the immutable audit headers to help post-incident attribution and sampling-based retention. 5) Tests and docs: integration tests that simulate cross-region fallback, and a security doc with configuration knobs and recommended rollouts. Impact and rollout: default behavior is opt-in via a feature flag (auth.ownership_claims.enabled=false). During rollout we plan a shadow mode that logs provenance validation results (auth.ownership_claims.mode=shadow) and an automated Linear evaluation run (ENG-4281) for quality/regression checks. See linked Linear ticket ENG-4281 and security task SEC-102 for acceptance criteria. Checklist: - [x] Claim extractor implementation and unit tests - [x] RBAC v2 mapping plugin and policy templates - [x] KMS gatekeeper middleware and integration tests - [x] Audit header augmentation and retention guidance - [x] Feature flag + shadow mode - [x] Docs: docs/security/owner-claims.md - [x] End-to-end test in CI that verifies region-pin fallback when claim missing Known limitations: - Current implementation relies on the existing operator token exchange; we plan a follow-up to decouple operator token issuance (see linked_linear ENG-5120). - Edge case: services using legacy metadata that do not surface owner annotations will fallback to tenant metadata, which may be less precise for attribution. Operational notes: - Default audit retention for provenance-enriched events is increased to 90 days under the compliance package; operator can override via organizational policy. - KMS gatekeeper introduces an additional 6-12ms median p99 overhead for wrapped requests (measured in bench harness); included a perf knob to bypass validation for high-throughput internal-only keys. Documentation: docs/security/owner-claims.md explains configuration, rollout guide, and example policy templates for RBAC v2.
Evan Chen: Can you clarify how the signed claim token is rotated? We should avoid long-lived assertions. (requested changes)
Priya Nandakumar: The extractor issues a TTL-limited claim (default 15m) and relies on the operator token refresh path; added unit tests and a config field auth.ownership_claims.token_ttl. I also added a follow-up in ENG-5120 to surface token exchange improvements.
Lena Ortiz: Approve after you add an integration test for cross-region key unwrap when claim is missing and the region-pin fallback triggers. (changes requested)
Priya Nandakumar: Added ownership_kms_test.go which covers cross-region fallback and a shadow-mode run. Tests pass locally and in CI.

Priya Nandakumar: Moved header names and added runbook entry describing retention defaults under ops/runbooks/provenance-rollout.md. Ready for final review.
Evan Chen: Approved. Verified policy template and local end-to-end. No blocking comments.

When enabling in production consider starting in shadow mode for 48-72 hours and inspect audit.provenance.* metrics. Watch KMS proxy p99 latency; perf knob available to skip validation for internal keys. Coordinate with infra for helm value auth.ownership_claims.enabled=true rollout.

Problem: Multiple constrained-decoding backends (CFG/grammar, regex, and the legacy token-mask backend) behave inconsistently in two problem areas: 1) the adapter layer that translates a top-level constraint spec into backend-specific inputs had divergent semantics (e.g. inclusive vs exclusive anchors), which caused structured-output regressions when falling back between backends; 2) tokenizer edge-cases—multibyte tokens, surrogate pairs, and custom tokenizer merges—were producing partial-token cutoffs when streaming and when performing function/tool call framing, leading to invalid JSON or truncated tool arguments in some streams.

What this PR does: Adds a unified ConstraintAdapter that normalizes high-level constraint specs into a canonical intermediate representation and then emits backend-specific payloads (CFG, regex, token-mask). It also introduces a TokenBoundaryPolisher that post-processes streaming token chunks to avoid emitting partial tokens and to maintain deterministic cursor positions for the KV cache. The adapter is intentionally conservative to preserve semantics when falling back between backends and when using openai-compat streaming.

Key design points (summary):
- Canonical intermediate model: a small, well-documented IR (ConstraintIR) that represents sequences, alternations, optional groups, and anchors. This IR is plain data (no engine code) and is the single source of truth for translation rules.
- Backend translators: thin, fully-tested translators for CFG, regex, and token-mask. Each translator preserves optional group semantics and emits explicit token-boundary hints where possible.
- TokenBoundaryPolisher: during streaming we buffer up to N bytes (configurable, default 32) to detect incomplete token boundaries (multibyte or merged tokens) and only forward full tokens to the stream sink. This reduces latency by average 3% for long sequences while eliminating malformed JSON/tool-call edgecases.
- OpenAI-compat framing: the adapter respects function/tool calling framing rules and reframes constraint payloads to ensure deterministic framing in the OpenAI-compat stream shim. This fixes cases where tools were receiving truncated args in compatibility mode.
- Backward compatibility: defaults preserve previous behavior; a feature-flag
--enable-canonical-constraints (off in stable) gates the new adapter. Rollout plan uses a gradual flag ramp to Dedicated tenants before enabling globally.

Checklist:
- [x] Add ConstraintIR and translators (CFG/regex/token-mask)
- [x] Implement TokenBoundaryPolisher and integrate with streaming layer
- [x] Add unit tests for tokenizer edge cases (emoji, surrogates, BPE merges)
- [x] Add integration tests for OpenAI-compat tool framing with fallbacks
- [x] Update docs and SDK contract notes (docstrings + short changelog entry)

Testing notes and results:
- Unit test bundle added: runtime/tests/test_constraint_adapter.py (60 cases) and tokenizer/tests/test_boundary_polisher.py (48 edge cases).
- Integration: ran openai-compat integration pipeline against sample tool-calling harness. First CI run surfaced a flaky streaming test due to an unrelated socket timeout; fixed by adding better drain logic in stream_sink. Final CI: all green.
- Performance: microbenchmarks on a p3.2xlarge-like shape show median additional CPU cost of ~0.6% for constraint translation and an average 3% token throughput improvement in stable streaming due to reduced reassembly work downstream.

Migration / rollout:
- The change is behind --enable-canonical-constraints; will be enabled only for 3 internal Dedicated tenants for two weeks, then rolled to beta customers, and then to default-on. We added a telemetry flag to record fallsbacks and any serialization errors to monitor regressions.

Files changed (high-level): see changed_files list.

Notes for reviewers: pay special attention to tokenizer boundary heuristics (tokenizer/token_boundary.pyi and tokenizer/boundary_polisher.cc) and to the translator unit tests which include aggressive negative cases. The ConstraintIR is intentionally tiny to keep the attack surface small.

Release notes:
- Add canonical constraint adapter and streaming token boundary fixes to improve structured-output stability and OpenAI-compat tool calling. Feature-gated rollout.
1) add constraint IR and initial CFG/regex translators (A. Chen)
2) token-mask translator + translators tests (A. Chen)
3) streaming boundary polisher implementation + tests (A. Chen)
4) openai-compat framing glue + integration tests (A. Chen)
5) docs/changelog and small refactors after CI feedback (A. Chen)
Diego Morales: Left nits on cfg_translator edge-case handling (see inline). Please add a small comment explaining why we prefer inclusive anchors.
Priya Natarajan: Question about memory budget for the buffer in TokenBoundaryPolisher; suggested a max cap and a hard cutoff. Updated to cap 128 bytes with a fallback policy.
Julien Lefevre: Verified openai-compat integration tests locally; suggested adding a negative test for overlapping lookahead in regex translator (added).
Feature-gated canonical constraint adapter plus streaming token boundary fixes to improve structured-output and OpenAI-compat tool framing. Default off; opt-in via --enable-canonical-constraints. Monitor constraint_serialize_errors telemetry.

Motivation: On high-variance production traffic some canary detectors produce noisy signals because synthetic probes either flood the system or are too sparse to catch transient regressions. This PR implements an interleaved synthetic probe scheduler that mixes lightweight background probes with targeted burst probes keyed to observed traffic phases, reducing probe-induced noise while preserving detection sensitivity. Summary of changes: 1) New scheduler module perf-canary/scheduler/interleaved_scheduler.py implementing a two-tier schedule: low-rate continuous probes and phase-triggered burst probes; smart jitter and backoff to avoid synchronized bursts across instances; probe prioritization by route SLO weight. 2) Autotune logic in perf-canary/autotune/phase_detector.py that infers phase boundaries from short-term throughput and concurrency fingerprints and adjusts burst window size. 3) Canary evaluation adapter perf-canary/evaluator/interleaved_adapter.py that consumes mixed probe streams and feeds an updated detector that weights probe samples differently depending on probe class. 4) Small change to the traffic generator used in canary lab perf-canary/tests/traffic_fixtures.py to support hybrid traffic shaping and deterministic replay for unit tests. 5) New integration tests perf-canary/tests/test_interleaved_scheduler.py that simulate common phase-shift scenarios and assert reduced false-positive rate and comparable detection latency. 6) Docs update docs/perf/canary-scheduler.md with configuration knobs and recommended defaults. Why this approach: interleaving keeps a baseline signal for long-tail regressions while burst probes provide concentrated sensitivity during suspected phase transitions. The autotune limits operator overhead and the scheduler includes a global-rate cap to prevent probe stomping during incidents. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind perf.canary.interleaved_scheduler, default off for all clusters. Canary on a single canary-controller pool for two weeks, measure false-positive rate, detection latency, and probe-cost uplift. If metrics are within thresholds we will enable for Stage and then gradually to Prod, with an immediate opt-out via runtime flag. Checklist: - [x] design doc reviewed by SRE and Applied ML - [x] unit and integration tests added - [x] performance microbenchmarks (see bench/README.md) - [x] docs updated - [x] feature flag gating in config - [x] linear tickets created for rollout and dashboards Details about detection model changes: the evaluator now applies a hierarchical sample weight: baseline probes are downweighted for short-window detectors to avoid washout, burst probes have higher weight for change-point detectors; combined score computes posterior using a small Bayesian smoothing term to avoid single-probe amplification. Impact on metrics: expected probe token uplift ~0.8% at default settings, probe CPU additional 0.3% on canary controllers during bursts; false positive rate reduced by ~35% in our synthetic phase-shift tests while median detection latency remained within 5-10% of baseline. Backwards compatibility: existing detectors continue to run unchanged unless the feature flag is enabled. Migration notes and config knobs are documented. Related work: builds on ENG-2145 phase fingerprint work and complements recent anomaly fusion changes in perf-canary. Risks and mitigations: risk of probe cascades across controllers mitigated by the global-rate cap and randomized jitter; risk of overfitting phase detection mitigated by conservative default knobs and a training cooldown window. Monitoring and dashboards: added canary_scheduler.{probe_rate,burst_rate,burst_count,phase_inference_confidence} metrics and dashboard templates in dashboards/canary-scheduler.json. Rollback safety: runtime flag immediate disable, and abort-on-anomaly if false-positive rate exceeds threshold for 1h. Merge outcome and rationale: after addressing initial review comments around concurrency in the scheduler and adding a safety cap to the burst backoff, the PR passed CI and was squash-merged into main to simplify revert.
Linus Park: The burst scheduler looks promising but I'm concerned about lock contention when multiple controllers schedule bursts simultaneously. Can you add a global rate limiter and ensure async-friendly backoff?
Aisha Raman: Added a token-bucket global limiter shared via controller config and switched to non-blocking asyncio timers for backoff; included tests that stress concurrency.
Evelyn Cho: Tests are thorough, but please add a canary lab scenario replay that demonstrates the 35% FPR reduction claim with seed values so it's reproducible.
Aisha Raman: Added deterministic traffic fixture seeds and documented how to reproduce benchmark numbers in bench/README.md.
Mateo Alvarez: CI flake on python37 linting; re-ran and cleared; approvable after squash commit to cleanup print statements.
Add interleaved scheduler core loop and unit tests
Implement phase detector autotune and integration adapter
Add docs and dashboard templates
Fix concurrency bug in burst scheduling (review feedback)
Update config defaults and feature flag gating
Introduce interleaved synthetic probe scheduler behind feature flag; reduces false positives in phase-shift scenarios and limits probe noise; opt-in via perf.canary.interleaved_scheduler; new metrics exported for observability.

Motivation: continuous batching in the runtime needs better cost-aware grouping to reduce padding waste while preserving kernel-friendly shapes and KV cache locality. Prior bucketing approaches reduced padding but treated every bucket as independent, which caused kernel underutilization and KV cache churn for mixed-length workloads. This PR implements a min-cost sequence clustering batcher that jointly optimizes for (1) padded-token cost, (2) kernel shape efficiency (selected kernel cost per batch shape), and (3) KV cache locality score to favor co-locating prefix-contiguous requests. The change is backward compatible: runtime batching policy is pluggable and defaults to previous bucketed batcher. Key pieces implemented: 1) Cost model module that combines padding penalty, kernel selection latency estimator, and a KV-locality penalty; weights are tunable via config. 2) New clustering-based batch composer that runs a lightweight greedy min-cost merge on the active queue every scheduling tick; it considers sequence-length centroids and merges neighboring clusters when cost(delta) < merge_threshold. 3) Kernel-aware batch shaping: after clusters are chosen the composer queries the kernel registry to pick an execution kernel optimized for the resulting max sequence length and batch size; cluster merges that would force a kernel downgrade are penalized. 4) KV cache affinity: requests with overlapping prefixes are annotated by the router and assigned a KV affinity token; the batcher prefers grouping identical affinity tokens to avoid cross-device KV synchronization. 5) Continuous batching tweaks: adaptive timer that backs off when clustering yield is low and aggressive coalescing for tail latencies. 6) Extensive unit and integration tests simulating mixed-length traffic and cold KV scenarios. Performance summary (brief): in internal synthetic workloads with bimodal seqlen (8/1024) we measured 22-28% token-cost reduction vs baseline bucketed batching at equivalent 95th percentile latency target; in a production trace sample with mixed web chat traffic we observed 11% reduction in GPU time and 14% fewer KV cache misses. Rollout plan: feature gated via runtime config; staged rollout to Dedicated clusters then Redwood-hosted starting with non-critical models. This PR also includes a small telemetry addition exposing batch cost breakdown per schedule tick for offline analysis.
Sophia Lin: Nice decomposition. Two asks: (1) add safety cap so merge loop can't starve the scheduler on high-concurrency queues, (2) add a simple A/B metric emitted when gating to compare cluster vs bucket for 1 week.
Response (Riley): added a hard cap on number of merges per tick and added 'batching.strategy_evaluation' telemetry event.
Mateo Ruiz: Kernel penalty weights look large in defaults and cause preference for tiny batches. Can you add auto-tune that nudges weights based on recent kernel throughput?
Response (Riley): added a light-weight exponential moving average tuner in cost_model with config switches (disabled by default).
Aria Chen: KV affinity token serialization in router is fine but ensure forward compatibility with on-prem affinity stores.
Response (Riley): switched token to a 128-bit stable hash and added compatibility shim in runtime/kv/affinity.rs.
Synthetic bimodal seqlen test: 22-28% token reduction vs bucketed baseline under same latency target. Production chat trace sample: 11% GPU time reduction, 14% fewer KV misses. Tail latency change within SLA (95th +3-6ms, within rollback window).
Introduces a new min-cost clustering batcher that reduces padding and KV cache churn for mixed-length workloads; feature off by default and gated for staged rollout. See docs/runtime/batching.md for config. Performance gains vary by workload.
Feature gated via 'batcher.strategy' config. Revert by switching to 'bucketed' strategy at runtime and optional restart of composer process. Emergency flag 'disable_clustering=true' added to config service.
payload.title: Min-cost sequence clustering batcher: kernel-aware, KV-local continuous batching
