payload.body:
## Context
Hosted canary rollouts need baseline vs canary comparisons for key SLO signals (5xx, timeouts, p95 latency) and throughput/cost signals (tokens/sec, in/out token counts). The routing/data plane work (ENG-9123) can split traffic, but without consistent request tagging we can’t build accurate cohort dashboards or auto-stop conditions.

A hard constraint here is metrics cardinality: emitting `rollout_id` on all request metrics will explode series count and degrade dashboards/alerting, especially on high-QPS tenants.

This PR implements request tagging and aggregation hooks that make cohort comparison possible while keeping the default metrics surface cardinality-safe.

## What’s included
1) Request context tagging
- Adds `rollout_id` (string) and `rollout_cohort` (enum: `baseline|canary|none`) to the shared request context.
- Tags are set by the router when a rollout split is applied (baseline path and canary path).
- Propagates tags through:
  - gateway -> data plane request context
  - internal tracing attributes
  - structured request logs

2) Metrics strategy (cardinality-safe)
- Core request metrics keep their existing low-cardinality label set (route, region, status class, etc.).
- We emit `rollout_cohort` as a label ONLY on a small, explicitly scoped set of “rollout cohort” metrics (new namespace), not on the global request metrics.
- `rollout_id` is NOT emitted as a label on the global request metrics.
- Instead, `rollout_id` is:
  - attached to traces/logs (for debugging)
  - used by a rollouts-specific aggregation path that is allowlisted + TTL bounded

3) Rollouts metrics aggregation hooks
- Introduces a rollouts-only metrics namespace where `rollout_id` is an allowed dimension, but only for rollouts in an “active allowlist”.
- Adds an in-process allowlist cache keyed by `rollout_id` with TTL refresh from control plane (default 5 minutes). If the allowlist entry expires, we stop emitting the rollout_id series.
- Metrics emitted under this namespace include:
  - `rollouts.requests_total{rollout_id, cohort, route, region}`
  - `rollouts.errors_total{rollout_id, cohort, route, region, error_class}`
  - `rollouts.latency_ms_bucket{rollout_id, cohort, route, region}` (histogram)
  - `rollouts.timeouts_total{rollout_id, cohort, route, region}`
  - `rollouts.tokens_in_total` / `rollouts.tokens_out_total` (where available)

4) Naming / schema notes
- Uses the prefix `rollouts.*` for the new metrics namespace.
- Tracing attributes use `rw.rollout.id` and `rw.rollout.cohort`.
- Log fields use `rollout_id` and `rollout_cohort` (matching existing structured log conventions).

## Why this approach
- `cohort` is low cardinality and safe to use broadly, but even cohort + route + region is still manageable only if we scope where it’s emitted.
- `rollout_id` is inherently high cardinality. Restricting it to an allowlisted metrics namespace ensures:
  - dashboards/alerts can query per-rollout during the soak window
  - series disappear after the rollout is complete (or after TTL), preventing long-tail series buildup
  - we can set explicit budgets and instrumentation ownership for this feature

## Implementation details
- Router sets tags using the existing rollout evaluation result (from the split primitive) and injects into `RequestContext`.
- Telemetry layer reads from `RequestContext` and:
  - always attaches tags to tracing span attributes
  - always attaches tags to structured logs
  - conditionally emits rollouts metrics when `rollout_id` is present AND allowlisted
- Allowlist provider (control plane) is called on cache miss and periodically refreshed; errors fall back to “not allowlisted” to protect metrics systems.

## Tests
- Unit tests:
  - RequestContext serialization/deserialization includes rollout tags.
  - Allowlist TTL behavior (refresh, expire -> stop emitting).
  - Metrics emission only under allowlisted conditions.
- Integration-ish test (mocked allowlist):
  - baseline vs canary requests increment separate `rollouts.*` series.

## Operational notes / limitations
- If control plane is degraded, we bias toward NOT emitting rollout_id metrics (still keep trace/log tags).
- For streaming retries: tags stay stable across internal retries because cohort assignment happens before request execution and is copied into context; we don’t re-roll cohort on retry.
- This PR does not add dashboards; it only provides the tagging + metric hooks. Dashboards/alerts are tracked in follow-ups (ENG-9152 and PR-28910).

## Follow-ups
- Wire allowlist membership to orchestrator state transitions (start/stop rollout) so series appear/disappear deterministically (tracked under ENG-9152).
- Add explicit cardinality budgeting + alerts for rollouts namespace (tracked under ENG-9152).

## Screenshots
N/A (server-side telemetry changes)

## Checklist
- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] No rollout_id labels added to core request metrics
- [x] Metrics naming reviewed with Observability
- [x] Rollout tags propagated to traces/logs for debugging

## Linked
- Linear: ENG-9152, PM-1843
- Related: ENG-9123 (traffic splitting), ENG-9158 (auto-stop/rollback)

---

### Commits (squash merged)
1. telemetry: add rollout tags to RequestContext and tracing attributes
2. telemetry: introduce allowlisted rollouts metrics namespace
3. telemetry: TTL cache + control plane allowlist provider
4. tests: rollout tags propagation + allowlist gating
5. cleanup: naming consistency + docs on cardinality constraints

### Files / areas changed (high level)
- `services/router/request_context.*`
- `services/telemetry/emitters/metrics_emitter.*`
- `services/telemetry/emitters/tracing_emitter.*`
- `services/telemetry/rollouts/allowlist_cache.*`
- `services/control_plane_client/rollouts_allowlist_client.*`
- `services/telemetry/tests/*`

### Review discussion (highlights)
- Logan Wright: Requested we avoid adding `rollout_id` to any existing `requests_total` style metrics; suggested a separate namespace with a strict allowlist and TTL. Addressed by moving all `rollout_id`-dimensioned metrics under `rollouts.*` and gating emission.
- Thomas Baird: Asked for explicit safeguards around series lifetime and cache behavior under control plane failure. Added TTL expiration behavior and fail-closed emission; added tests.
- Aisha Bello: Requested consistent naming across logs/traces/metrics and to ensure timeouts are broken out for stop-conditions work. Added `timeouts_total` and aligned attribute names.
- Mina Haddad: Confirmed cohort stickiness behavior for retries/streaming. Added notes and ensured context copy is stable across retries.

### CI
- `build-and-unit-tests`: pass
- `lint`: pass
- `telemetry-integration-tests`: pass
- `perf-smoke (staging)`: pass

### Merge
Merged via squash on 2025-03-26.
Adds cohort tagging (baseline/canary) and rollout-aware aggregation hooks to enable baseline vs canary metric comparisons in Console.
Rollout ID is propagated through request context and traces/logs, but is not emitted as a default label on core request metrics to avoid cardinality blowups.
Introduces an allowlisted, TTL-bounded rollouts metrics namespace keyed by rollout_id for active rollouts only.
payload.title: Telemetry: tag requests with rollout_id + cohort for Hosted canary comparisons (cardinality-safe)

payload.body:
Context and motivation:
We run continuous performance canaries across production-like traffic to detect regressions early. Existing probes are either static (fixed qps) or full-traffic shadows which can misrepresent load or add cost. We also observed noisy rollbacks during short transient degradations. This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: (1) a proportional stress sampler that injects probe traffic proportionally to recent load patterns (keeps probe representativeness across traffic modes), and (2) a degradation-credit sentinel that requires sustained regression credit accumulation before triggering an automatic rollback, reducing flapping during transient spikes.

What this change does (summary):
- Implement proportional-stress sampler in perf-canary/prober: schedules probes that scale probe volume relative to a traffic fingerprint (by percentile buckets).
- Add degradation-credit sentinel in canary-evaluator: a credit ledger that increments on detected degradation signals and decays over time; only when credits exceed a threshold does it mark a canary as failing.
- Expose config knobs in canary policy YAML: probe.scale_strategy = "proportional", sentinel.credit_window_ms, sentinel.decay_rate
- Add integration tests that simulate traffic mode changes (steady, bursty, low-qps) and validate probe representativeness and sentinel hysteresis behavior.
- Observatory: dashboard panels and alert rule for "sentinel_credit_balance" and a new histogram for probe qps distribution.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Proportional sampler uses an exponential moving average of recent requests grouped by percentile traffic fingerprints to decide probe multiplier. This keeps the probe mix small in low-traffic tenants but increases probe frequency in heavy-traffic scenarios to preserve statistical power.
- Degradation-credit sentinel intentionally biases towards hysteresis: short regressions add limited credit which decays quickly; sustained regressions accumulate faster. This dampens rollbacks for noisy metrics while still enabling response to true sustained regressions.
- Both features are opt-in and default to off for existing customers. They are exposed as canary policy fields and default values are conservative.

Checklist (what I changed):
- [x] Implementation in prober scheduler and canary-evaluator core
- [x] Unit tests for credit ledger and sampler heuristics
- [x] Integration test harness with synthetic traffic patterns
- [x] Docs: canary policy reference and runbook note
- [x] Dashboard panels and Grafana queries + example thresholds
- [x] Feature flag gating + migration note

Commits included (high-level):
- 9f7a2b1: add proportional stress sampler core loop and configuration parsing
- c3d4e8f: implement degradation-credit ledger and evaluation hook
- b12f44a: integration tests: traffic-mode simulator and synth driver
- e9a0b7e: dashboard queries and grafana JSON export (trimmed)
- f4512c0: docs: canary policy reference and runbook guidance

Files changed (high-level):
- perf-canary/prober/sampler.go (new): proportional sampler implementation and unit tests in sampler_test.go
- perf-canary/evaluator/sentinel.go (new): credit ledger + evaluation policy
- perf-canary/config/policy_schema.go (mod): add fields for sampler and sentinel
- perf-canary/integration/traffic_simulator.go (new): synthetic traffic modes for tests
- docs/canary_policy.md (mod): reference and examples
- observability/grafana/canary_panels.json (mod): new panels and queries
- .github/workflows/perf-integration.yml (mod): add matrix entry for new integration test runs

Review conversation (high level, single thread):
- Diego Ramirez (requested changes, 2026-02-11): "Nice approach. Two asks: (1) please add a deterministic seed option for the sampler for test reproducibility, (2) I think we should add an upper cap on probe multiplier to avoid accidental runaway in extraordinary spikes."
- Maya Patel (author reply, 2026-02-12): "Thanks Diego — added deterministic seed config and a hard upper bound (default 10x). Also added a safety circuit in the scheduler that rejects >1000 probes/sec for an entire deployment as an emergency cap."
- Hannah Cho (comment, 2026-02-13): "Integration tests look good. One note on metric names: recommend using 'canary/sentinel/credit_balance' to align with existing naming conventions."
- Maya Patel (author reply, 2026-02-14): "Renamed metric and updated dashboards."
- Samir Kumar (approval, 2026-02-15): "Approach validated, tests cover critical cases; LGTM after CI green."

CI and validation details:
- Unit tests: pass (local and CI)
- Integration tests (matrix): initially one flaky test failed under the k8s ephemeral runner (traffic_simulator timing); fixed by adding deterministic seed and extending timeouts in the harness. Final CI run: all checks passed.
- Performance baseline: synthetic run shows median probe CPU overhead increase ~1.8% for heavy tenants, within budget; cost trade-offs documented in the canary policy doc.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind canary.policy.experimental.enable_proportional_sampler (default false)
- Rollout plan: enable for internal perf lab tenants first, monitor sentinel_credit_balance and rollback events for 72h, then opt-in for customers with dedicated capacity.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: misconfigured multipliers could overload clusters. Mitigation: hard caps, safety circuit, config validation at admission time.
- Risk: sentinel threshold tuning might be conservative or too permissive. Mitigation: default conservative thresholds, canary-specific overrides, dashboards and alerting for tuning.

Merge details:
- Merge method: squash
- After merging, I kicked off the internal perf lab job to validate a 24h window across three traffic modes; results were as expected and no rollbacks were auto-triggered in the presence of transient spikes.

Notes for reviewers and ops: the canary runbook section at docs/canary_policy.md contains sample YAML snippets and monitoring queries. If you want to exercise the feature locally: perf-canary/integration/README.md includes a short guide to run the traffic simulator with deterministic seeds.
Adds a proportional traffic sampler for stress probing and a degradation-credit sentinel to reduce noisy rollback flapping; opt-in via canary config

Adds a lightweight presubmit snapshotter (opt-in) and a quiet-merge mode for release windows; no API changes.
Context and motivation: We have recurring noisy presubmit runs that make it hard to reason about regressions during staged releases. Teams have asked for a lower-cost presubmit option that produces reproducible artifact snapshots for fast triage, plus a merge mode that reduces churn during release quiet windows. This PR introduces a stage-aware presubmit snapshotter and a quiet-merge mode that defers non-essential CI shards in release windows.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a presubmit snapshot step that captures deterministic toolchain manifests, lockfile hashes, and a minimal set of test seeds so infra can reproduce failures without running full integration shards. Snapshots are stored as short-lived build artifacts and indexed by commit and stage.
- Introduces "quiet-merge" pipeline semantics: when a release window label is present, non-blocking/slow CI lanes are soft-snoozed and results annotated on the merge commit rather than gating the merge.
- Implements a lightweight lint runner wrapper (node -> Go shim) to reduce cold-starts and memory footprint for small PRs.
- Adds telemetry hooks that tag presubmit snapshots with stage (dev/canary/release) and sample rates, enabling stage-aware dependency telemetry and aggregated presubmit cost metrics.

Commit summary: 5 commits (squash target)
- Add presubmit snapshotter service and CLI wrapper
- Integrate snapshot publish step into presubmit composite action
- Implement quiet-merge detection and pipeline router change
- Replace node lint entrypoint with go shim for fastpath linting
- Tests, docs, and changelog for CI behavior

Files changed (high level):
- .github/actions/presubmit-snapshot/* (new) — CLI, action.yml, publisher
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yaml (modified) — stage routing, snapshot step insertion
- .github/workflows/release-window.yaml (modified) — quiet-merge annotations
- infra/ci/router.go (modified) — stage detection and lane throttling
- tools/lint/entrypoint.go (new) — lightweight lint wrapper
- docs/ci/presubmits.md (modified) — usage and opt-in guidance
- test/ci/snapshotter_test.go (new) — unit tests for snapshot behavior

Testing and CI: All CI lanes pass on the final branch. Initial run showed a flaky integration collector test (test/ci/collector_test.go) which was fixed by reducing parallelism and adding a small sleep in the fixture; re-ran twice. Lint and go vet pass. Nightly longtests unaffected because quiet-merge only applies during labeled windows.

Review feedback and threads (summary):
- Diego: requested stronger guarantees on snapshot determinism; asked for explicit lockfile stamps and a note about ephemeral artifact TTL (accepted).
- Jian: asked to gate quiet-merge to only apply when repo-level release window flag is set; implemented an opt-in repo setting and added docs.
- Priya: asked to keep non-blocking lanes observable; added a new dashboard tile and exported a presubmit-snapshot metric.
- Author replies: clarified snapshot contents and added a small CLI mode to allow local reproduction (presubmit-snapshot --replay).

Backward compatibility and opt-in behavior: The snapshotter is opt-in per-team (presubmit config key). Quiet-merge must be explicitly enabled via repo settings or PR label (release/quiet-merge). Default behavior is unchanged. No public API changes.

Performance and cost implications: Early internal trials reduced total presubmit CPU time by ~28% for small PRs (<10 files changed) by diverting heavy lanes into snapshot-only flows. Snapshot artifacts are small (~300KB) and TTL is 6 hours by default to limit storage costs.

Operational notes and rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature-flag gate (ci.feature.presubmit_snapshot = false).
2) Enable for a small team (platform infra) for 1 week and monitor presubmit-cost and false-negative rates.
3) Gradually opt in additional teams while adjusting sample rates.
4) After 4 weeks, consider enabling quiet-merge for scheduled release windows.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals (Diego, Jian, Priya). Created a follow-up Linear to track dashboard polish and sampling rate tuning.

Related work and references: Linear ENG-1421 (presubmit cost profiling), ENG-1488 (release window process improvements), SUP-431 (customer incident where CI flakiness delayed a release).

Notes for reviewers/maintainers: Snapshot artifacts should not be used for long-term forensic needs; they are intended for quick repro and triage. If you need persistent recording, request a longer TTL via infra support.

Checklist: [x] Unit tests added for snapshotter core [x] Integration test for pipeline router [x] Docs updated [x] Feature-flagged rollout plan [x] Telemetry exported

If there are concerns about silencing too much during quiet windows we can relax the quiet-merge criteria to only deflect known-expensive lanes rather than all non-blocking lanes.

payload.body:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally see short, unpredicted microbursts that cause transient SLA slippage for customers with tight throughput guarantees. Existing warm pools and burst tokens absorb many cases, but we lack a coordinated short-horizon reservation that (1) is cheap to maintain, (2) can be sized per-tenant according to contract, and (3) emits clear accounting signals for downstream billing and autoscaler decisions. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: SafetyWindowProvisioner (a low-cost short-horizon capacity reservation layer) and TenantQoSAccountant (per-tenant obligation/debt accounting and telemetry).

What this change does (single-string summary): Adds a SafetyWindowProvisioner controller that holds small, time-bounded slot reservations per pool to cover microbursts; a TenantQoSAccountant that tracks committed throughput vs observed throughput and exposes an SLO-debt metric and replenishment recommendation; wire-ups into the autoscaler to prefer using safety windows before triggering expensive provisioning; and a small observability surface (metrics, dashboards, docs, unit and integration tests).

Design notes: SafetyWindowProvisioner maintains sliding-window reservations of slots expressed as "safety-units" (abstract token representing N requests or X tokens). Each safety-unit has a TTL (configurable, defaults to 45s) and a lease weight mapped from tenant contractual priority. The provisioner opportunistically fills windows from underutilized pools and drains them when headroom is needed for long-running scale-ups. TenantQoSAccountant consumes per-tenant sampling from request routers and the pool occupancy exporter to compute three time-series: committed_rate, observed_rate, and slo_debt (committed - observed over a rolling 5m window). QoS accountant publishes a recommended safety-window size and an urgency flag used by the autoscaler to accelerate a minimal reactive scale (fast-path) or fallback to full provisioning (slow-path).

Compatibility and fallbacks: Default behavior is disabled for existing clusters; enabled via configmap flag dedicated.safetyWindow.enabled=true. When enabled, provisioner is conservative: safety units cannot exceed 5% of a pool's allocatable capacity unless tenant has a high-priority contract. On failure modes (controller crash, API unreachability) the provisioner gracefully releases reservations; autoscaler and request path have a deterministic fallback path unchanged from prior behavior.

Checklist (follow-ups and CI): - unit tests for provisioner lease lifecycle added - integration test in perf-canary harness added (simulates 3s microbursts) - dashboards: added example Grafana panels and alert rule for slo_debt > 5% sustained - docs: operator guide + flags - Linear: ENG-4321 (design/impl), ENG-5600 (telemetry/dashboards)

Commits (high-level): ["a1f4d3c: safety-window controller skeleton and CRD", "b2d7f91: provisioner reconcile loop and lease allocator", "c3e9ab2: tenant QoS accountant metrics and sampler", "d4a1b7f: autoscaler integration hooks (fast-path) and config knobs", "e5b2c33: tests: unit + perf-canary integration scenario", "f6c3d44: docs and grafana snippets"].

Key changed files (high-level list): ["services/provisioner/safetywindow/controller.go", "services/provisioner/safetywindow/api/v1alpha1/safetywindow_types.go", "pkg/qos/accountant/accountant.go", "pkg/autoscaler/fastpath/fastpath.go", "deploy/manifests/dedicated/safetywindow-config.yaml", "test/integration/perf-canary/safetywindow_microburst_test.go", "docs/operators/safetywindow.md", "docs/observability/slo-debt-dashboards.json"].

Review conversation (condensed): - Marco: "Nice separation. Two asks: clarify how we unit-size safety-units vs real request token counts, and make TTL config per-pool." -> Response: clarified sizing math in code comments and added per-pool TTL config (pool annotation) in commit b2d7f91. - Evelyn: "Concerned about double-counting capacity when safety windows overlap with warm pools." -> Response: added allocation reconciler so safety units account for warm-pool reservations; added tests to assert no overcommit in commit d4a1b7f. - Tomas: "Prefer exposed metrics to include label 'commit_source' (api|manual|linear-recommendation)." -> Response: added label on metric series in c3e9ab2. - Code owners: minor nits on naming and comments addressed in follow-up commits.

CI and stability notes: First CI run flagged a flaky integ test in perf-canary that simulates 10x burst patterns; reran with increased timeouts and it passed. Lint and unit tests green. E2E smoke in a dedicated QA cluster passed (observed reduced 95p latency for microbursts when safety-window was active).

Telemetry and dashboards: New metrics published under redwood.qos.slo_debt (gauge) and redwood.safetywindow.allocations (counter/gauge with labels pool/tenant/commit_source). Added a Grafana dashboard JSON with panels for per-tenant slo_debt, safetywindow fill ratio, and fastpath activation rate. An example alert: slo_debt > 0.05 for 10m triggers a warn and recommends linear-issue ENG-5600 follow-up.

Operational playbook (short): - To enable: set dedicated.safetyWindow.enabled=true, tune per-tenant contract multiplier in tenant-profile config, observe dashboards. - To troubleshoot: use /debug/safetywindow/leases and accountant diagnostic endpoint which returns recent commit/observed windows. - Rollback: flip the flag and the provisioner will release leases within TTL + reconciliation window.

Merge: Squash-merged to main after approvals. No migration scripts required; CRD installed as part of manifests (safe to apply).
Marco Rossi: Clarify unit sizing math and make TTL per-pool.
Sana Iqbal: Added per-pool TTL and documented sizing in comments (b2d7f91).
Evelyn Chen: How do safety windows interact with warm pools? Risk of overcommit.
Sana Iqbal: Added allocation reconciler and tests to prevent double-counting (d4a1b7f).
Tomas Ortega: Add commit_source label to metrics.
Sana Iqbal: commit_source label added to slo_debt and allocations (c3e9ab2).
CI Bot: Integration test flaky on first run; rerun passed.
Release Manager: Recommend enabling behind feature flag, include operator note in 1.8 release notes.
Added SafetyWindowProvisioner (opt-in) to reduce latency during short microbursts and TenantQoSAccountant for per-tenant SLO debt reporting. Defaults off; operator flag dedicated.safetyWindow.enabled=true to opt-in. See docs/operators/safetywindow.md for tuning guidance.
This PR is focused on short-horizon capacity smoothing; follow-ups planned to integrate billing signals and longer horizon predictive resizing (ENG-5600).

- Control Plane endpoints now declare RBAC v2 permissions for org/user/role + routing policy actions.
- Added CI guardrail to prevent shipping new sensitive endpoints without permission annotations.
- No behavior change unless RBAC v2 enforcement is enabled (feature-flagged).
Context: As part of RBAC v2, we need a canonical mapping from Control Plane API actions to permission strings and a mechanical way to ensure new endpoints can’t ship without being categorized. This PR adds explicit permission annotations to the most security-relevant Control Plane routes (org/user/role management and routing policy updates) and introduces unit tests that fail if a sensitive endpoint is missing a permission. This is intended to support deny-by-default enforcement in the gateway/service middleware (separate PRs), and to improve auditability by guaranteeing an action string exists for every sensitive operation. Scope: (1) Add @RequiresPermission(...) annotations for org/user/role CRUD, API key admin surfaces that live in the Control Plane, and routing policy create/update/delete + rollout/pinning operations. (2) Introduce an endpoint coverage test that enumerates registered routes and asserts that any route tagged as "sensitive" is annotated with a permission and resource scope mapping. (3) Normalize a handful of legacy endpoints to use consistent "resource" extraction (org_id/project_id/env_id) so the evaluator can be called with the correct scope. Non-goals: This PR does not enable enforcement by itself; enforcement remains behind rbac.v2.enforce_control_plane and rbac.v2.enforce_gateway. It also does not finalize role templates or migration mappings; those are handled in the policy bundle repo. Implementation notes: Permission strings follow ADR-014 conventions (e.g., org.users.create, org.roles.update, routing.policies.update, routing.rollouts.manage). Each handler now declares a permission + a resource scope extractor (OrgScope / ProjectScope / EnvScope). The coverage test relies on the router registry metadata rather than reflection on handler code, so it stays stable as we refactor handler wiring. Testing: Added unit tests for the router registry: (a) all sensitive endpoints have permissions, (b) permission strings are unique within the Control Plane module, (c) scope extractor returns non-empty IDs for endpoints that claim org/project/env scoping. Verified locally with rbac.v2.enforce_control_plane disabled (no functional changes) and enabled in a dev environment (expected 403s when calling admin endpoints with insufficient roles). Rollout: Merge is safe independent of feature flags. Once gateway/service enforcement PRs land, this ensures coverage for the core admin surface area and blocks regressions where we add a sensitive endpoint without a permission mapping. Follow-ups: (1) add remaining annotations for billing/admin and data-retention endpoints (tracked in ENG-18241), (2) wire "denial reason" detail into Control Plane error mapping (PR-28241), (3) add integration tests for key user journeys (PR-28344).
Ethan Park (review): Good direction. Two asks: (1) make sure routing rollouts are scoped to env (not project) since rollouts are env-specific in the data model; (2) the coverage test should fail on any endpoint tagged sensitive, even if it’s internal-only, otherwise we’ll forget when we flip flags in Private.
Benji Okafor (author): Updated rollouts to EnvScope (env_id extracted from /projects/{project_id}/envs/{env_id}/rollouts). Also changed the coverage test to include internal routes with sensitive=true. Added a short comment in RouteMetadata explaining why internal is included.
Jordan Lee (review): Permission names: I see org.role_bindings.* and org.roles.*. Per ADR-014 we should keep plural resource segments stable; role_bindings is OK, but can we avoid mixing underscore and dot semantics? Recommend org.roleBindings.* or org.role_bindings.* everywhere. Also we need a unique stable action string for routing policy edits: routing.policies.update is fine; rollout should be routing.rollouts.manage (or create/update/delete).
Benji Okafor (author): Normalized to org.role_bindings.* everywhere (kept underscore per existing permission registry style in PR-28134). For rollouts, split into routing.rollouts.create/update/delete to match handler granularity; kept routing.rollouts.read separate for GET endpoints. Added uniqueness assertion in the test module to catch accidental duplicates.
Marcus Lin (review): Please ensure we are not accidentally exposing permission strings to non-admin clients in error bodies. Also can we add a test for at least one endpoint to assert missing permission annotation fails registration? Guardrails are great, but we should test the guardrail.
Benji Okafor (author): Error bodies unchanged in this PR; no enforcement here. Added a negative test that constructs a RouteRegistry with a synthetic sensitive route missing permission metadata and asserts registry.validate() throws with a clear message. That should cover the guardrail behavior.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): Minor: In ScopeExtractors, return a typed error / sentinel rather than empty string for missing IDs; empty IDs can become "global" by mistake later. Even if enforcement isn’t wired, we should make failures loud.
Benji Okafor (author): Good call. Updated extractors to return Result<Scope, ScopeError> and made registry validation fail if a sensitive route’s scope extractor can’t produce an ID from the path params. Updated tests accordingly.
Ethan Park (approval): Approved. The scope fix + coverage test looks solid. Please keep follow-up for billing/data-retention endpoints tracked; those are common enterprise questionnaire items.
Jordan Lee (approval): Approved after naming normalization. Thanks for adding uniqueness and negative tests—this will prevent a lot of drift.
Marcus Lin (approval): Approved. Please link this PR in ENG-18305 and ensure we call out in the rollout runbook that annotations alone don’t mean enforcement is active.
Benji Okafor (author): Linked in ENG-18305 and added a note in the Linear ticket with the flag names.
payload.title: Control Plane: annotate sensitive endpoints with RBAC v2 permissions + coverage tests

Context: Our monolithic ci/build.sh and ci/test.sh have become difficult to maintain across multiple packages in the monorepo. This PR splits the scripts into small, composable steps (setup, toolchain-bootstrap, install, build, lint, test, collect-coverage), introduces a hermetic test shim (tools/hermetic-test-shim) that wraps test execution with deterministic environment and cache control, and migrates the GitHub Actions workflows to call the new scripts. Motivation: reduce flakiness, make local debugging faster, and enable per-package cached artifacts for incremental CI runs. Summary of changes (high level): 1) New scripts under scripts/ci/{setup.sh,bootstrap-toolchain.sh,install-packages.sh,build-package.sh,run-lint.sh,run-tests.sh,collect-artifacts.sh}. 2) tools/hermetic-test-shim: a small Go binary (single source file) that sets up isolated TMPDIR, pins environment variables, enforces node/yarn/npm path isolation for JS packages, and coordinates ephemeral sqlite-based test-db seeds for integration tests. 3) .github/workflows/ci.yml: replaced monolithic job steps with calls to the modular scripts and introduced a lightweight caching key strategy that separates npm/go/cache to reduce cross-contamination. 4) package.json and workspace tooling: bumped devDependencies for eslint, jest, and turbo to mitigate known flakiness with older runners. 5) Dockerfile.ci: minor change to install the hermetic shim's binary into the runner image. 6) Makefile: added targets to run pieces of the pipeline locally with the same env used in CI. Checklist: - [x] Split monolithic scripts into modular steps - [x] Add hermetic test shim and unit tests for shim - [x] Update GitHub Actions and runner images - [x] Bump devDependencies with changelog review - [x] Validate against full CI matrix in staging - [x] Add docs/updating-ci.md and usage examples Rationale and notes: - The hermetic shim is intentionally minimal and is implemented as a single-file Go program to avoid additional runtime deps; it is built as part of the ci image. - Caching changes aim to reduce cross-package invalidation while keeping cache keys stable across runner OS updates. We fall back to a conservative key if cache restore fails. - We reduced the matrix dimension for node versions from 3 to 2 for faster CI turnaround while preserving coverage on the oldest supported and latest stable. - This PR does not change runtime code or public API surface. See linked Linear tasks ENG-4215 and ENG-4321 for perf goals and rollout plan. Related: previous work on ci templates and cache-keying (see PRs: #31287, #36890).
Refactors CI build and test scripts into modular workspace-aware scripts, adds a hermetic test shim to improve test determinism and reduce flakiness, and bumps several developer tool dependencies. No user-facing behavior changes expected.
Priya Kaur: Requested that hermetic-test-shim log a short trace id for each test run so we can correlate infra flakes — addressed in commit 3 and tests added.
Daniel Ortiz: Asked to surface cache hit/miss metrics as action step outputs; added basic metrics and documented them in docs/updating-ci.md.
Mei Chen: Raised concern about increasing image size; we moved the shim to be built as a tiny static binary and only added ~2.1MB to Dockerfile.ci, measured in staging.
Jordan Reyes: Replied that we will monitor first three weeks for latency regressions and added a Linear follow-up ENG-4380.
Priya Kaur: Approved after minor nits were fixed (script exit code handling, added defensive set -euo pipefail).
Initial run: lint failed on an upstream eslint rule (CI run 1). After bumping eslint and applying autofix changes CI rerun passed. A single test flake was reproduced locally and fixed by the hermetic shim seed isolation. All jobs passing on final run.
Deployed updated Dockerfile.ci to staging runners on 2026-02-26, added monitoring dashboards for cache hit ratio and test-run variance, and scheduled a follow-up linear task to evaluate rollout impact after two weeks (ENG-4380).
See docs/updating-ci.md for example Makefile targets. Typical local run: make ci-bootstrap && make ci-install && SCOPE=packages/auth make ci-run-tests. The hermetic shim is invoked automatically by run-tests.sh; pass --shim-disable to opt out for debugging.
Low. The hermetic shim runs as unprivileged user in CI and does not introduce networked services. We added a short audit of the Go code for unsafe syscalls and verified none present.

payload.body:
Motivation: Several high-throughput streaming customers observed CPU pressure and extra memory churn from repeated token handoffs and per-chunk byte copies. This PR introduces two focused changes to reduce client-side cost and improve cross-SDK ergonomics: 1) a compact CredentialLease adapter that standardizes short-lived token leases and proactive refresh logic across SDKs, and 2) a zero-copy stream handle layer that exposes buffer views to avoid per-chunk allocations.

Summary of changes: - New compact credential lease adapter (sdk/shared/lease): a tiny, dependency-free lease interface and producer that SDKs can opt into. It supports lease.acquire(timeout_ms) -> LeaseHandle (id, expiry, token), proactive refresh callback registration, and a light metrics hook. The adapter is intentionally minimal so it can be embedded into hosted or private deployments without heavy runtime coupling. - Python: adds sdk/python/redwood/auth/lease.py (memoryview-based streaming token appender), integrates lease warmup in the session factory, adjusts retry backoff presets for short-lived tokens. - TypeScript: introduces src/stream/zero_copy_handle.ts that returns Uint8Array views referencing the underlying stream buffer; adds a thin Lease binding in src/auth/compactLease.ts. - Go: adds compact lease types in pkg/auth/compact_lease.go and a zero-copy io.Reader wrapper used by the stream consumer. - Tests: unit and integration tests for lease refresh behavior; streaming throughput microbenchmarks show a ~16% CPU reduction on medium payload workloads.

Compatibility and migration notes: - Default behavior is unchanged. The compact lease adapter is behind an opt-in flag (client config: auth.compact_lease: true). - Zero-copy handles are opt-in at client construction for languages where exposing raw buffer views is safe (python: stream_zero_copy=True, ts/go: same). Enabling zero-copy may affect code that assumed owned copies of chunks; we documented usage patterns and provided helpers to copy when required. - No server-side contract changes.

Testing and rollout: - CI: unit-tests, integration-tests, typechecks, linting all green after two reruns. - Internal canary: rolled out the opt-in flags to internal staging and to 3 beta customers for 2 weeks. Observed no regressions in end-to-end behavior and consistent CPU decreases. - Rollout plan: start as opt-in in the next SDK minor release; collect telemetry and then enable automatic suggestions in Optimize for eligible customers.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-1329) - [x] Cross-SDK API surface minimal and documented - [x] Unit/integration tests - [x] Benchmark microbenchmarks included - [x] Release notes drafted - [x] Version bumps for each SDK package
Diego Alvarez: Can you clarify lifetime semantics for a LeaseHandle if the underlying token is rotated mid-stream? How should consumers detect invalidation?
Author (Maya Chen): LeaseHandle includes an expiry timestamp and lease.id; adapters will emit a 'lease_invalidation' metric and the handle.owner should check expiry before sending chunk. Added note in docs and added unit test that simulates mid-stream rotation.
Priya Nair: Zero-copy on TS looks great but I worry about user code that mutates the view. Can we add a helper to get an owned copy?
Author (Maya Chen): Added toZeroCopyCopy(bufferView) helper and documented common pitfall. Also added a terse comment in zero_copy_handle.ts.
Ethan Liu: CI flaked on streaming e2e the first run; was the failure related to environment noise?
Author (Maya Chen): Flake was due to a test that assumed non-deterministic chunk boundaries; updated test to be tolerant and retriggered CI. All checks green on rerun.
Adds a cross-SDK compact credential lease adapter (opt-in) and zero-copy stream handle primitives for higher-throughput streaming. Tweaks retry profiles and bumps Python/TS/Go SDK minor versions.

payload.body:
Motivation: During the 2024-09-18 regional surge incident we observed rapid tenant-level thrashing when circuit breakers and eviction policies ran independently: tenants repeatedly entered eviction, released, and were re-evicted within short windows causing wasted work and instability. This PR introduces a cohort-aware 'soft respite' orchestration layer that (1) groups tenants into short-lived cohorts for SLO relaxation windows, (2) provides a token-based respite lease extension to avoid rapid eviction/reinstate cycles, and (3) transitions the circuit breaker into a low-impact 'lull' state for cohorts meeting stability criteria instead of a full open. Approach: implement a RespiteOrchestrator in control plane that tracks ephemeral cohort membership (shuffle-once per 30s) and issues short respite leases (default 10s) using the existing lease API. Add heuristics to the circuit state machine to accept 'lull' transitions when cohort-level error rate is below a threshold and individual tenant token buckets indicate transient overloads. Feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.feature.respite_orchestrator (off by default). Rollout plan: behind feature flag -> unit and integration tests -> dogfood in canary region for 48h -> staged roll to US regions -> enable for EU with opt-in. Observability: new telemetry emitted under metric names respite.cohort_size, respite.granted_count, circuit.lull_entries, and debug logs emitted at TRACE only when runtime.debug.respite is enabled. Backwards compatibility: the orchestrator uses existing lease primitives and fallbacks to standard eviction machinery if the orchestrator fails. Reverts are supported by disabling the feature flag and removing orchestrator assignments from the control plane. Changes included: code (control plane orchestrator + circuit state machine updates), unit/integration tests, small additions to telemetry dashboard JSON, and an entry in ops/rollout.md. Risk: medium — logic touches eviction and circuit transitions; tests and dogfood period required. Linear/Jira: ENG-4921, SUP-7123. CI: initial run surfaced a flaky integration test around lease expiry (fixed by commit 3), full CI green after fix.
Jonah Kim: Can we avoid cohort oscillation when membership churn is high? Suggest adding a minimum residence TTL or jitter - see comment on respite_orchestrator.go:line 78.
Asha Patel: Added minResidenceTTL=8s and randomized cohort assignment jitter in commit a1f3b2b; updated tests to validate jitter behavior.
Priya Deshmukh: The lull transition reduces eviction aggressiveness but may hide genuine degradations. Please make metrics for suppressed evictions visible and add a dashboard panel. (request change)
Asha Patel: Added respite.granted_count and circuit.lull_entries counters and added panel to respite-dashboard.json in commit c7a9d8e.
Luca Moretti: Integration test was flaky locally; the lease expiry fix looks correct. Approving pending CI.
CI Bot: All checks passed on rerun (lint, unit, integration, e2e-canary).
Unit tests for orchestrator and state transitions; deterministic integration test that simulates cohort churn and lease expiry; canary run for 48h with detailed telemetry and alerting on eviction suppression > 5% of baseline.
When enabling in canary: set runtime.feature.respite_orchestrator=true and runtime.debug.respite=true for first 2 hours. Watch respite.granted_count and circuit.lull_entries; if queueing latency increases or error-rate drift > 0.5% for 5m, toggle off and capture logs with trace id prefix 'respite-run/'.
Merged to main via squash. Feature flag default remains off; ops runbook updated with steps to enable and monitor. Can be reverted by toggling runtime.feature.respite_orchestrator=false and allowing existing eviction flow to reclaim control. Telemetry panels are in telemetry/dashboards and will be added to the canary Grafana shortly.
Add cohort-aware soft-respite orchestration to reduce tenant eviction/reinstate thrashing under transient overloads. Feature disabled by default; enable behind runtime.feature.respite_orchestrator. Monitor respite.cohort_size, respite.granted_count, and circuit.lull_entries.
This change was motivated by incident SUP-7123 (2024-09-18) where short-cycle evictions amplified regional instability. The orchestrator aims to reduce rework and improve SLO stability during transient surges.
Addressed reviewer concerns: added minResidenceTTL and jitter to prevent cohort oscillation, added telemetry for suppressed evictions, stabilized flaky test, and documented rollout. CI green and PR approved by all reviewers.
payload.title: Tenant cohort fairing and soft-respite orchestrator

payload.body:
Motivation: customers operating across regulated geographies require enforced region pinning for KMS usage and stronger tamper-evidence on audit logs while keeping RBAC v2 decision flow simple for platform teams. This PR implements a region-bound service-account attestation hook and an audit-hash-bridge that generates compact, verifiable audit digests and forwards them into the existing audit pipeline. The attestor enforces that service-account tokens contain an immutable region claim (region_hint) or are mapped via a tenant_region binding; when a mismatch is detected the attestor returns a DENY decision upstream in the RBAC v2 pipeline. The audit-hash-bridge computes incremental HMACs over serialized audit events using tenant-scoped keys; the bridge signs events and emits both the original event and a small audit-proof record to the centralized audit topic. KMS affinity enforcer: a small policy shim chooses the tenant CMK by region tag and rejects cross-region CMK selection when the tenant policy forbids it. Migration and rollout: feature-gated (security.region_attestor + audit.hash_bridge) and rollout plan includes canary in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 with traffic split and automatic fallback to preexisting behavior. Backwards compatibility: attestor is optional; when disabled it is a no-op shim. Testing: unit tests for attestor logic, integration tests that run full RBAC v2 decision flow, e2e test that validates audit-proof roundtrip and reconcile with the audit-consumer. Performance: local benchmark shows median decision latency +1.8% at 95th percentile under synthetic token workloads; bridge throughput 6k events/s per instance. Checklist: [x] spec and design doc added; [x] unit and integration tests; [x] security review requested; [x] helm chart changes for private installer; [x] migration runbook. Related work: ENG-4582, ENG-4699 (policy-mapper), PM-88. This PR touches runtime policy path, audit forwarding, and the helm values used by private deploys; please validate the rollout plan with SRE before merging.
Luca Moretti: Please add a diagram to the docs showing where the attestor sits in the RBAC v2 decision flow and clarify whether attestation failures are audited (answer: yes, failures emit an audit event prior to deny).
Author(Aisha Patel): Added a diagram and clarified failure semantics in docs/security/region-attestation-and-audit-hash-bridge.md; failures produce a minimal audit record and the bridge signs it.
Priya Sharma: The helm values expose kms.affinityPolicy as a freeform string; can we make enums and validate at chart-render time to avoid accidental misconfiguration?
Author: Converted affinityPolicy into an enum in values-security.yaml and added validation for legacy installs; included migration note in runbook.
Rafael Gomez: Integration tests flake on CI (timeout on audit consumer). Can we increase wait time and add a deterministic reconcile check?
Author: Increased the consumer wait timeout and added a deterministic reconcile step; re-ran CI which passed all suites.
Priya Sharma: Security review complete; please ensure keys used for HMAC are rotated and stored in KMS as per runbook. Approved pending one small doc tweak.
Luca Moretti: Approved. Rafael Gomez: Approved and merged via squash by release manager after smoke verified in canary clusters.
Add region-bound service-account attestor enforcing region claims and a tenant-scoped audit-hash-bridge that signs audit events; new helm flags for KMS affinity and feature flags for gradual rollout; opt-in via feature gates; migration runbook included.

payload.body:
Add burst-aware transient reservation to paged KV block allocator and a cooperative eviction scheduler that preserves batch hotpaths; reduces 95th/99th tail latency under bursty request patterns. No API changes; runtime flags for tuning.
Motivation: We see recurring tail-latency spikes in production when short-lived bursts (traffic spikes or long-tail model calls) coincide with KV cache reclamation work. Current paged KV allocator does not distinguish transient bursts from steady-state pressure: it starts aggressive eviction on detection of low free blocks and sometimes runs eviction work on the hot path which lengthens batch latencies. This PR introduces a burst-aware transient reservation and a cooperative eviction scheduler that defers/pauses reclamation during latency-sensitive windows and performs targeted background reclaiming when the runtime signals quieter windows (e.g., between batching flushes).

Implementation summary: Single continuous string below to preserve GitHub PR body style. We add a lightweight burst sensor (kv::BurstSensor) that tracks allocation rate and detects short-lived spikes by maintaining short sliding windows of allocation events and recent batch completion markers. The block allocator now exposes a transient_reserve counter: when a burst is detected we reserve a small headroom of blocks per-pool to avoid immediate eviction. Eviction work is moved out of synchronous allocation slow-path into eviction_scheduler, a cooperative component that subscribes to runtime batching events via a new low-overhead hook in continuous_batching (on_batch_flush/on_batch_idle). The scheduler runs reclamation tasks only when signaled idle or when free memory drops below a critical hysteresis threshold; it also accepts per-pool eviction hints (victim_ranges) from the allocator to focus work and minimize scanning.

Key behavioral changes:
- Allocator fast-path remains lock-free for common-case allocations.
- On allocation pressure, instead of immediately walking long freelists and evicting multiple pages, allocator first consults transient_reserve and attempts local reuse strategies (LRU-like local candidate reuse) up to the reserve.
- Eviction work that requires I/O or heavy compaction is enqueued to eviction_scheduler which respects a latency fence: if batch hotpath is active, eviction is throttled or paused for tunable window_ms.
- Scheduler uses per-thread backoff counters and prioritizes small, high-impact evictions (sparse victims) to recover capacity quickly with minimal cache churn.

Performance: Benchmarks in benches/kv/burst_bench.rs show the following on a 8-GPU host with representative Llama-derived model workloads and a synthetic burst pattern (1000 rps steady, 5x bursts for 2s every 20s): - 95th latency reduced by ~28% compared to main with the previous allocator strategy. - 99th latency reduced by ~41% during bursts. - End-to-end throughput unchanged or slightly improved due to fewer batch stalls. Microbenchmarks: background eviction CPU utilization dropped 33% by focusing work and avoiding full-scan passes.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for allocator behavior and BurstSensor (tests/kv/burst_allocator_test.rs) cover reserve logic and corner cases. Integration tests wire eviction_scheduler into continuous_batching simulation; CI included a simulated burst scenario (integration-kv) that was flaky initially due to a race which is fixed in commit 3. Benchmarks run on perf-lab and results attached in PR artifacts. We also ran a staged rollout to a subset of dedicated clusters: no regression signals; observability dashboards updated to show burst events and scheduler decisions.

Operational / rollout notes: New runtime flags (config/runtime_flags.toml documented and ops examples provided) allow teams to tune reserve size, detection window, and eviction_fence_ms. Defaults were chosen conservative to avoid regressions. The feature is guarded behind a runtime flag (kv.burst_reserve.enabled=true) and can be disabled at boot if needed. No schema changes; no model-serving API changes.

Review conversation summary:
- Maya: requested clarifications on reserve sizing algorithm and impact on long-lived high-pressure workloads; asked for config knobs and autoscaling guidance. Response: added reserve sizing doc and autoscaling note; default reserve is a small fraction (0.5-2% of pool) with adaptive decay.
- Priya: suggested to add metrics for "eviction_deferred_during_batch" and a histogram for eviction latency; addressed by adding eviction_{deferred,count} metrics and histograms in src/kv/metrics.rs.
- Liam: flagged a potential race between scheduler shutdown and allocator teardown in hot-swap flows; fixed by adding a graceful cancellation token and unit test.
- Reviewers approved after second pass; CI green on merge.

CI: build: pass; unit-tests: pass; integration-kv: flaky on first run (race reproduction) -> fixed -> rerun -> pass; bench pipeline: artifacts uploaded (perf/burst_run_2026-03-01). Final ci_status: pass.

Merge: squashed merge; commit message: "burst-aware block allocator + eviction scheduler: reduce KV cache tail latency under bursts". Rollout: enabled on canary dedicated clusters for 72 hours and then global rollout.
Maya Patel: Please include guidance for reserve sizing and how this interacts with Dedicated autoscaling. — addressed in docs/allocator/burst-aware-design.md
Priya Raman: Add metrics to show when eviction is deferred to ease debugging — added eviction_deferred_count and eviction_latency histogram
Liam O'Connor: Found a race on shutdown between scheduler and allocator teardown; proposed using cancellation tokens — fixed and added unit test
payload.title: burst-aware-block-allocator-and-eviction-scheduler-to-reduce-kv-cache-tail-latency

Summary: This PR implements a hybrid headroom autoscaler that combines predictive headroom (short-term demand forecasting) with contract-aware allocation. The goal is to reduce SLA violations during rapid surges while limiting overprovisioning for Dedicated customers with explicit throughput commitments. The change introduces a soft-eviction path that gracefully degrades non-contract traffic (best-effort) before affecting committed throughput. Motivation: multiple customers experienced transient SLA blips during microburst patterns; existing heuristics either over-provision or cause abrupt evictions. This PR balances cost and guarantees by adding an allocator that respects per-tenant contracts and a fallback pathway that applies graded throttles and reroutes to compatible model variants when necessary. Design highlights: - New allocator component: contract-allocator. It pulls per-tenant commitment metadata and current utilization, computes a desired headroom budget using an autoregressive short-horizon predictor, and issues reservations to the fleet headroom manager. - Soft-eviction flow: a three-step degrade path (throttle -> model-variant fallback -> enqueue-with-deadline) that is applied only to non-contract (best-effort) traffic and signals via a new header X-Redwood-Degrade-Reason for observability. - Telemetry & reporting: new metrics (contract_utilization_ratio, headroom_projection_ms, degrade_reason_counts) and a per-tenant daily compliance report (s3 export hook). - Config / flags: feature.hybrid_headroom.enabled (opt-in), allocator.lookback_ms, allocator.forecast_horizon_ms, degrade.window_seconds, degrade.priority_threshold. - Backwards compat: if feature flag is off, no behavior change. Contracts are read from existing tenant metadata store; defaults to 0 for tenants without commitments. - Performance: allocator runs in a lightweight event loop co-located with fleet-controller; forecasting uses an online linear model with bounded CPU. The runtime impact measured in local perf harness: median scheduling latency +1.8ms under steady state, tail +3.2ms at 99th (acceptably under SLO). Changes included: - service/autoscaler/contract_allocator.go: new allocator implementation and unit tests. - runtime/scheduler/headroom_manager.go: headroom reservation APIs and reconciliation loop. - runtime/scheduler/soft_eviction.go: degrade flows and decision engine. - telemetry/metrics_contracts.yaml: metric definitions and dashboards. - examples/ops/configs/hybrid-headroom.yaml: sample rollout config. - docs/operational/headroom.md: operational runbook and rollout checklist. - test/e2e/hybrid_headroom_test.go: end-to-end test harness simulating microbursts and contractual mixes. Commits: - 7f3d4b1: initial contract-allocator scaffold and interfaces. - 8a12d2c: implement short-horizon predictor and headroom reconciliation. - ae93b11: add soft-eviction decision engine and degrade pathways. - b44f0e5: telemetry hooks and dashboards (metrics + Grafana). - c1b9a9d: e2e tests and perf harness adjustments. - d2257aa: docs, feature flags, and rollout config. Tests & CI: Initial CI run had a flaky e2e that timed out under the nightly integration cluster (test harness timed out at 10m). Root cause: the test's mock backend used a fixed response delay; increased the harness timeout and added jitter to the mock to reduce coupling. After the fix, CI passed (unit, integration, lint, e2e). Review notes and conversation captured below. Rollout plan: - Stage 1 (canary): enable feature.hybrid_headroom.enabled=true for 1% of Dedicated nodes with no contract tenants; observe metrics for 72 hours. - Stage 2 (contracted tenants small cohort): enable for 5% of nodes serving pledged-tenants only; validate contract_utilization_ratio and no increase in committed-latency. - Stage 3: gradual ramp with automated rollback if contract_utilization_ratio falls below 98% or if degrade_reason_counts spike beyond thresholds. Monitoring / Alerts: - New alerts: ContractUtilizationDrop (P2), ExcessDegrades (P3). Both have playbooks in docs/operational/headroom.md. Known limitations: - Forecast model is short-horizon and will not capture multi-minute sustained ramps; for long ramps, normal autoscaler path remains primary. - Soft-eviction currently only degrades non-committed text-generation traffic; embeddings and synchronous admin routes are excluded. - Further tuning required for multi-region spillover heuristics. Related work: builds on ENG-1124 predictive-headroom prototype and reuses portions of throttle-orchestration (ENG-1421). Changelog & migration: no DB migrations; feature flag gateway ensures safe rollback. Merge: squash merge after approvals.
Omar Rivera (requested changes, 2026-02-23): The allocator looks good but we should avoid calling the tenant metadata store synchronously on every reconciliation. Can we cache TTLs and instrument cache-miss metrics?
Maya Chen (author reply, 2026-02-24): Added an in-memory TTL cache with cache_misses metric; see allocator/cache.go (unit tested).
Tina Gupta (comment, 2026-02-25): Soft-eviction path needs stronger logging at the decision point to aid postmortems. Please add a structured event with tenant_id, reason, and pre/post utilization snapshot.
Maya Chen (author reply, 2026-02-26): Added structured_event emission and included it in the telemetry schema; updated docs with example logs.
Ethan Brooks (approved, 2026-03-01): Verified e2e on staging with 50% synthetic microbursts. CPU is within budget and contract SLAs held. Approving for merge.
CI (auto, 2026-02-28): Flaky e2e timed out; fixed by increasing harness timeout and adding jitter to mock backend. Rerun passed.
Introduces a hybrid headroom autoscaler that is contract-aware (per-tenant throughput commitments), exposes soft-eviction pathways to preserve SLAs, and adds telemetry hooks for utilization and contract compliance. Opt-in via feature flag; safe rollback path included.
payload.title: Hybrid headroom autoscaler: contract-aware allocation and soft-eviction

Adds a background ‘Cost Janitor’ service that applies workload-derived prefill and quantization hints to reduce unit costs while preserving latency SLOs. Tunable via Redwood Console and disabled-by-default for existing clusters.
Summary: Introduces 'Cost Janitor', a lightweight controller that synthesizes workload signals (prefix hit rates, request sparsity, and latency percentiles) into safe default prefill policies and quantization hints for model variants. The controller emits recommendations, can apply non-breaking config seeds to Dedicated/Private clusters, and exposes audit events for all changes. Motivation: Many customers underutilize prefill and conservative quantization defaults, leaving 10-30% unit-economy on the table. This PR provides an automated, auditable path to surface and optionally apply low-risk adjustments so teams can safely converge to better cost/latency tradeoffs.

What changed (high level):
- New component: services/cost_janitor (controller + reconciler + lightweight ML heuristic library)
- API: /v1/admin/cost-jobs (create/list/react) and console hooks to preview recommendations
- Runtime: new prefill_policy hint metadata on model variants; quant_hint profile metadata for quantization tiers
- Telemetry: audit events, recommendation traces, and a new metric redwood_cost_janitor_recommendation{result}
- Tests: unit tests for heuristics + an integration smoketest that runs controller against a local dev workload sample

Commits (high level):
- 0a7c3d1: initial controller scaffolding, CRD-like config and scheduler
- 2f9b1aa: heuristics: prefix-hit decay, tail-latency guard, cold-prefill threshold
- 5d4a2b8: API endpoints and console preview payloads
- 7f6e8c4: telemetry and audit event wiring; add metrics and tracing spans
- 9b1f3e0: tests and CI flake fix (retries for smoketest)

Files changed (not exhaustive):
- services/cost_janitor/controller.go (new)
- services/cost_janitor/heuristics.go (new)
- api/admin/cost_jobs.go (new endpoints)
- models/variant_metadata.go (adds PrefillPolicy & QuantHint fields)
- console/src/components/CostJanitorPreview.tsx (console preview UI)
- metrics/metrics_defs.yaml (new metric)
- tests/cost_janitor_smoketest.sh (integration smoke test)

Design notes and safety:
- Recommendations are tagged with a safety score (0-1). Only scores >= 0.75 are auto-applied when 'auto_apply' is enabled for a cluster.
- Janitor never lowers model precision on variants that are pinned or marked 'no-auto-quant'.
- Prefill policy changes begin as shadow/apply-preview by default; customers must opt into auto-apply.
- All changes generate audit logs and offer a 24h rollback window (configurable per cluster).

Performance and cost expectations:
- Internal benchmarking on three sample workloads showed 8-18% reduction in token cost for conversational traffic and 4-9% for single-turn generation without SLO regression.
- Benchmarks were run on p4d and a16 hardware; results are included in the PR artifact (benchmarks/README.md).

CI and validation:
- CI run summary: build ✓, unit tests ✓, lint ✓, integration-smoketest initially failed (timeout on smoketest step), retried and passed on rerun. Full CI attached in checks panel.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Ethan Clarke (reviewer): "This looks promising. Two concerns: 1) semantic tests around quant hints — how do we validate output quality? 2) metrics cardinality if we emit per-variant recommendation traces?"
- Author (Sofia): "Added a small qual-check harness that runs a delta-bleu/embedding-similarity test on a 100-example QA set for any candidate quant hint. It is lightweight and only runs in prerelease mode. For metrics, we aggregate by model_family + cluster to avoid high cardinality; per-variant traces are sampled (1%)."
- Priya Nair: "Would like a knob in Console to preview cumulative delta on cost and p95 before applying — is that possible?"
- Sofia: "Console preview now shows an estimated cost delta and p95 impact based on historical samples. See console preview UI changes and backend budget estimator in heuristics.go."
- Jordan Li: "Nit: rename 'auto_apply' in config to 'apply_mode' with explicit enum (disabled, preview, auto). Also prefer the default to be 'preview' for safety."
- Sofia: "Addressed: config renamed, default set to 'preview', tests updated."

Manual testing and rollout:
- Deployed to staging Dedicated cluster (staging-dedicated-03) for 72h with auto_apply=preview and sampled traffic. Observed expected reduction in inferred unit cost and no p95 SLA violations.
- Runbook updated: docs/runbooks/cost_janitor.md with steps to audit, roll back, and tune thresholds.

Merge details:
- Merge method: squash and merge
- Merge commit: "Introduce Cost Janitor controller, admin API, and console preview"

Follow-ups / TODOs (tracked in Linear):
- ENG-1304: Add drift detection that re-evaluates recommendations weekly
- ENG-1317: Add experiment channel to run A/B application of recommended prefill policies
- ENG-1350: Add richer qual checks (LLM-specific evals) to the quant hint pipeline

Why this is different from previous econ PRs: Cost Janitor emphasizes small, auditable, incremental changes surfaced as recommendations first (preview path) with a focus on safe auto-apply gating. It blends low-cost heuristics with lightweight qual checks and conservative rollout mechanics rather than a fully automatic autotuner. This lowers risk for customers who want gradual cost improvements and clear rollback paths.
Console preview added with cost/p95 estimate
Default apply_mode set to 'preview'
Audit logs included for every automated change

Context: Usage Insights breakdown queries (route + model) were timing out for larger ranges (esp. 30d) and causing elevated warehouse spend due to repeated full scans. This PR introduces a materialized view + clustering strategy for the route/model aggregates, updates the query builder to hit the MV when filters are compatible, and adds perf benchmarks + p95 targets that match the Console interactive budget.

What changed (high level): 1) Materialized view for interactive breakdowns: Added a warehouse MV on top of telemetry.usage_route_model_agg_hourly that pre-joins model bucketing + normalized routes and precomputes the common metrics used by the Console table (tokens_in/out, billed_tokens, cache_hit_tokens, retry_count, fallback_count, req_count, latency_ms_p50/p95, cost_usd). The MV is keyed by (workspace_id, project_id, time_bucket_hour, route_canonical, model_family, model_version_bucket, region, deployment_mode) and is clustered to optimize the top access pattern: (workspace_id, project_id, time_bucket_hour) + selective dimensions (route_canonical, model_family).

2) Partition/clustering tweaks on base aggregates: Adjusted clustering/partition hints on telemetry.usage_route_model_agg_hourly to reduce spill in range scans and to improve pruning for common filters. Also added a small “hot window” optimization for the last 48h, which is the dominant interactive range for most Console usage.

3) Query planner and guardrails: Updated the usage insights query service SQL builder to route queries to the MV when: time grain is hourly or daily, requested dimensions are a subset of [route, model, region, deployment_mode], and the time range <= 31 days. For requests that include unsupported dimensions or very large ranges, we keep the existing path but apply stricter limits (max rows, required workspace filter) and return a clearer error message with guidance.

4) Benchmarks + targets: Added benchmark harness and documented p95 targets for interactive queries. Benchmarks include (a) 24h, (b) 7d, (c) 30d, and (d) 30d + route filter (selective) across representative workspaces (small/medium/large cardinality). Results are checked in as fixtures so we can track regressions.

5) Observability: Added query-level tracing attributes for: warehouse_path=(mv|base), scanned_bytes_estimate, result_row_count, and pruning_ratio, and a counter for “fell back to base path” with reason codes.

Performance summary (Snowflake, prod-like dataset; measured from query service, excluding auth but including warehouse execution time): Before: 24h breakdown p95 1.6s; 7d p95 5.9s; 30d p95 14.2s (frequent timeouts at 20s gateway limit). After: 24h breakdown p95 430ms; 7d p95 820ms; 30d p95 1.9s (no timeouts in 50-run sample). Warehouse cost impact: scanned bytes reduced ~68% for 7d and ~74% for 30d in the benchmark suite. Note: numbers vary by workspace cardinality; worst-case (very high distinct routes) still improves materially but can exceed 2s for 30d; see “Known limitations”.

Targets (for beta): p95 (server-side) <= 600ms for 24h, <= 1.0s for 7d, <= 2.5s for 30d (breakdown table). Availability handled by upstream service SLO; this PR only sets latency budgets and emits metrics.

Files/areas changed: - services/usage-insights-query/sql/: MV-aware SQL builder + fallback logic - services/usage-insights-query/benchmarks/: benchmark runner + fixtures + README - telemetry/warehouse/migrations/: MV definition + clustering changes - telemetry/warehouse/ddl/: base agg clustering tweaks - observability/tracing/: new attributes + metrics

Illustrative snippet (MV routing): IF requested_dimensions ⊆ supported_mv_dims AND range_days <= 31 AND grain IN ('hour','day') THEN use telemetry.mv_usage_route_model_breakdown ELSE use telemetry.usage_route_model_agg_hourly.

Test plan: - Unit: SQL builder snapshots for MV path and base path; guardrail error messages - Integration: ran benchmark harness in staging warehouse against a 30d backfilled dataset; validated no correctness drift on totals vs base query within rounding tolerance - Manual: Console breakdown table load for 24h/7d/30d on 3 internal workspaces; verified filters (route/model/region) and pagination - Observability: verified new traces show warehouse_path and scanned_bytes_estimate populated

Correctness notes: MV uses the same rounding rules as base query (cost_usd rounded to 1e-6 internally, display rounding elsewhere). No changes to attribution semantics; this is a pure performance change.

Known limitations / follow-ups: - MV does not currently support arbitrary “top-N by cost with nested dims” beyond the supported set; the service falls back to base query and may be slower. - For workspaces with extreme route cardinality, 30d queries can still be >2.5s if no selective filters are applied; we should consider a daily rollup MV for 30d+ once we see real beta traffic. - Backfill: MV relies on existing hourly aggregate freshness; it doesn’t change lag behavior.

Rollout: Safe to deploy behind the existing query service; MV creation is additive. If the MV causes warehouse instability, we can flip USE_MV_USAGE_INSIGHTS=false to force base path (config flag included).

Review notes / conversation highlights: Logan Wright: “Can we guarantee the MV won’t change totals vs billing?” Author: “MV is a projection of the same aggregated dataset; validated against base query results over 30d; no semantic changes; added integration check in benchmark harness comparing sums.” Mei Lin: “Clustering keys: do we really want model_version_bucket before route?” Author: “Swapped order to prioritize route/model filters; also added workspace/time first for pruning; see updated DDL in latest push.” Chloe Martin: “Guardrail error copy should mention recommended range.” Author: “Updated: suggests <= 7d for unfiltered large workspaces + recommends adding route/model filter.” Allison Grant: “Please emit a metric for MV fallback reasons so we can alert.” Author: “Added counter usage_insights_mv_fallback_total{reason=…} and included in tracing attributes.” Felix Schneider: “Console uses daily grain in one view; will it hit MV?” Author: “Yes; MV supports hour/day; verified in staging traces.”

CI: build/test/lint passed. Benchmark job is informational for now (does not gate merge) but produces artifacts in CI logs; we can gate once we have stable baseline numbers.
Add MV definition for usage insights route/model breakdown
Adjust clustering/partitioning on hourly aggregate table
Route query builder to MV for supported filters + add fallback reasons
Add benchmark harness + baseline fixtures for 24h/7d/30d workloads
Add tracing attributes and metrics for scanned bytes + MV usage

payload.body:
Context: We continue to see customer-visible flakiness when SSE chunks drop bytes at network boundaries or when intermediary proxies truncate payloads, leading to partial JSON objects and delimiter loss. Motivation: Existing heuristics attempted to patch by gluing fragments heuristically but introduced duplicate delimiters and out-of-order function-call events for long-lived streams. This change introduces a checkpointed-span backfill mechanism paired with an escape-normalizer to make fragment resynchronization deterministic and safe. Approach: 1) Checkpointed spans: the stream encoder now emits lightweight span checkpoints (opaque short tokens) at configurable intervals; receivers can request backfill for any detected gap by referencing the last known checkpoint id. The server keeps a short replay buffer of tokenized events between checkpoints to allow efficient backfill without replaying the full session. 2) Escape-normalizer: we canonicalize escape sequences across chunk boundaries so multi-byte UTF-8 or JSON escapes cannot be split into invalid sequences; this prevents mid-escape truncation leading to recoverability loss. 3) Deterministic delimiter repair: when a delimiter (

 or SSE event separator) is missing, the resynchronizer consults checkpoint ids, token boundaries, and quoted-string state to insert repair delimiters only when unambiguous. 4) Tool/function call ordering: handoff semantics adjusted so function-call sentinel events include epoch and relative sequence ids; the receiver uses these to reorder/hold toolcall boundaries until a contiguous sequence is reconstructed or backfill times out. Implementation highlights: added sse_resync.go with a small state machine and replay buffer, a Rust adapter change that surfaces checkpoint tokens to the compatibility layer, end-to-end tests, and a small CLI inspector to debug real traces. Backwards compatibility: checkpoints are optional and encoded as meta-events compatible with the OpenAI-compat layer; older clients will ignore them. Rollout plan: feature flag off by default; staged rollout to 10% of streaming traffic for two days, then 50% with canary metrics for partial-json errors and function-call order regressions, then 100% if stable. Metrics and alerts: introduce streaming.checkpoint.backfills, streaming.resync.success_rate, streaming.escape.normalize_rate; alarms on >1% partial-json error rate regression. Checklist: [x] unit tests; [x] integration tests with proxy truncation scenarios; [x] e2e replay harness; [x] docs and quickstart; [x] metrics and dashboards; [x] rollout playbook. Related: ENG-8942 work on stream stability and SUP-4821 customer report.
Connor Lee (2025-01-30): Please expand on memory bounds for the replay buffer; in high-throughput sessions we need an LRU fallback. Also request a microbenchmark comparing latency impact when checkpoints are enabled. Aisha replied the buffer is capped at 256KB per session with LRU trimming and linked a benchmark result (see ci).
María Gómez (2025-02-01): Concern about introducing new meta-events into the OpenAI compat stream — asked for clear failure mode docs for older clients. Aisha updated description and docs section explaining graceful ignore semantics and provided example of backward-compatible marker format.
Evan Chen (2025-02-03): Suggested minor naming change for 'checkpoint id' to 'span_token' to avoid confusion with DB checkpoints; approved after rename. Also requested an additional test where a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence is split across three chunks; added in sse_resync_test.go.
Connor Lee (2025-02-04): Approved and noted CI flake resolved by bumping retry timeout in e2e harness.
Introduce optional SSE span checkpoints and escape-normalizer to improve recovery from truncated stream fragments; adds configurable replay buffer, deterministic delimiter repair heuristics, and safer function-call ordering across backfills. Rollout gated behind feature flag. Metrics and alerts added.
Unit tests cover resync state transitions and canonicalization of split escapes. Integration tests simulate proxy truncation and interleaved function-call events. E2E uses the stream-inspector to validate deterministic recovery. Performance microbenchmarks included in CI; feature is off by default and enabled via feature flag for canary traffic as described in the rollout plan.
payload.title: SSE backfill: checkpointed span recovery and escape-normalizer to repair truncated JSON splices
