Summary: This PR refactors the CI build graph and introduces an opt-in lightweight runner (QuickCI) plus a per-file linting mode to dramatically reduce CI latency for small changes. It also reorganizes build targets into smaller, cache-friendly units and pins a small set of GH Actions to SHAs for reproducibility. Motivation: Our full CI run averages ~22m for small README/typo PRs. This work targets fast feedback for iterative developer work while preserving full CI coverage for merge commits. Changes are gated behind an opt-in flag (QUICK_CI=true) so teams can adopt incrementally.

What I changed (high level):
- Add .github/workflows/quickci.yml: a lightweight pipeline that runs fast-path jobs (per-file lint, unit smoke subset, quick-typecheck).
- Update .github/workflows/ci.yml: split the large build target into smaller jobs (core-lib, serving-runtime, sdk-python, sdk-ts, docs), and add explicit cache-keying per-target.
- Implement per-file linting utility scripts/tools/perfile_lint.sh that detect changed paths (git diff --name-only) and invoke ESLint/ruff/clang-format only for impacted packages.
- Pin critical actions (actions/checkout, actions/cache, setup-python) to SHAs and add short pointer to lockfile in .github/actions-pins.md.
- Bump eslint -> 8.40.0 and pytest -> 7.4.1; update pre-commit hooks accordingly.
- Small edits to Makefile and BUILD_* entries to support targeted builds (make build-TARGET).
- Add docs: docs/dev/ci-quickci.md describing opt-in, expected latency, and how to override.

Commits (high-level):
- feat(ci): add quickci workflow and per-file linting script
- refactor(ci): split build matrix into labeled targets and per-target caches
- chore(ci): pin actions to SHAs and add actions-pins.md
- chore(deps): bump eslint, pytest, pre-commit hooks
- docs: add quickci opt-in guide and upgrade notes

Files changed (high level):
- .github/workflows/quickci.yml (new)
- .github/workflows/ci.yml (modified)
- .github/actions-pins.md (new)
- tools/perfile_lint.sh (new)
- scripts/ci_util.sh (modified)
- BUILD_TARGETS/ (new small target descriptors, 4 files)
- package.json / pyproject.toml (deps bumped)
- docs/dev/ci-quickci.md (new)
- Makefile (small changes)

Testing & CI:
- Initial CI run (first push) failed the full lint job due to a stricter ESLint rule in 8.40.0 catching a few legacy patterns in examples/; those were fixed in the follow-up commit by adding overrides for examples/* and a small code cleanup.
- After fixes, QuickCI run median latency on a sample of 50 small PRs dropped from ~22m to ~3m (per-file lint + smoke tests). Full CI runs remain unchanged in coverage; full CI median is ~28m but now split into parallelized smaller jobs which improved tail latency by ~12%.
- Cache hit rates improved by changing keys to include target-version and git-shas of deps; observed ~46% faster restore on average.

Review thread (condensed):
- Luca: "Nice ergonomics. Two asks: document opt-in and add telemetry for QuickCI adoption (percent of PRs using QUICK_CI)."
- Priya: "Added docs and a simple telemetry event in scripts/ci_telemetry.sh that emits to internal metrics when QUICK_CI=true; added note in docs/dev/ci-quickci.md."
- Rachel: "We should ensure pinning action SHAs is resurfaced in release notes and a maintenance checklist."
- Priya: "Added .github/actions-pins.md and a short section in docs/dev/ci-quickci.md about how/when to update pins; flagged ENG-2099 for rotation cadence."
- Samir: "Per-file linting looks good. Please ensure that test-only changes (tests/) still run unit tests. Also add an explicit fallback to full lint when detection fails."
- Priya: "Added detection fallback and forced full-lint for changes that touch the top-level CI configs or BUILD_TARGETS/ directory."
- Review approvals: Luca (approve), Rachel (approve after docs update), Samir (approve).

Notable implementation details and caveats:
- QuickCI is opt-in via the QUICK_CI pipeline dispatch or by setting QUICK_CI=true in a branch. The workflow is intentionally conservative: it will run only per-file lint + a small smoke test matrix. A lightweight feature flag in scripts/ci_util.sh will force full CI for branches matching release/* or when BUILD_TARGETS/ or .github/ files are modified.
- Per-file linting uses a path->tool map in tools/perfile_lint.sh. We keep a short whitelist of directories where per-file linting is safe; touching other directories triggers full-lint.
- Action SHAs pinned for reproducibility; see .github/actions-pins.md for the list and rationale. Pin maintenance will be tracked under ENG-2099.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge this PR to main behind an env toggle (QUICK_CI opt-in).
2) Infra/Platform teams can enable QUICK_CI for high-frequency test repos and pilot teams.
3) After 2 weeks of telemetry and any follow-ups, enable as default for PRs that are small (<= 10 files changed) and do not touch CI configs.

Follow-ups (tracked in Linear/JIRA):
- ENG-1245: Add telemetry dashboards and adoption metrics for QuickCI.
- ENG-2099: Quarterly rotation plan for pinned GH Action SHAs.
- SUP-8921: Support request to enable QuickCI for some customer-facing repos; included as linked_jira.

Merge notes: Squash-and-merge. After merge, I ran a smoke of 10 internal PRs to validate the probability of false negatives in per-file lint detection; none of the smoke PRs missed necessary checks but we left the fallback to full-lint as a safety net.

Why this is different than prior CI refactors: Earlier PRs focused on matrix pruning and cache key standardization. This change prioritizes developer feedback time (fast-path) with a conservative, auditable opt-in approach. It also introduces a minimal maintenance burden (pins + small scripts) and clear docs for teams to adopt.

If you want to test locally: see docs/dev/ci-quickci.md for the workflow dispatch steps and quick debug commands (tools/perfile_lint.sh --dry-run).

Acknowledgements: Thanks to the infra team (Luca), SDK owners (Rachel, Samir), and SRE for helping validate cache changes and test sharding.
Introduces QuickCI (opt-in lightweight CI), per-file linting to reduce job runtime, and splits monolithic build targets into smaller, cache-friendly units. No runtime behavior changes.

Motivation: large tenant mix shows divergent batch shapes that cause suboptimal batching and quant fallback thrashing. This PR adds a light-weight batch-shape-classifier that tags incoming request streams with a compact signature, feeds signals into the econ-orbiter to select safe quant profiles, and emits new telemetry to validate unit-econ impact. Goals: 1) reduce quant fallback oscillation for mid-size sequences, 2) pick more cost-effective quant profiles earlier without increasing tail latency, 3) provide observability hooks for post-merge validation and automatic rollback. Changes are conservative by default: classifier runs at admission and can be toggled per-tenant; quant profile selection only changes when the confidence score crosses a high threshold and when KV cache hit ratios are stable. Checklist: - [x] implement batch-shape-classifier (fast, <200ns per request path) - [x] integrate econ-orbiter decision hook with quant profile selector - [x] add toggle + tenant-scoped opt-in config - [x] telemetry: econ_signals, batch_shape_hist, quant_compat_events - [x] unit + integration tests for classifier + policy decision - [x] perf benchmarks (synthetic) and safety gating in CI - [x] docs: admin toggle + operator runbook How it works (short): classifier computes a 32-bit signature based on token-length histogram, request metadata, and prefix stability heuristics; signature is compared to a lightweight in-memory sketch to classify as 'steady', 'bursty', or 'fragmented'. The econ-orbiter consumes the label and historic cost/latency counters to pick a quant profile from the tenant's allowed set. A safety gate enforces TTL-based probation and forces reversion if tail p99 increases >10% over baseline. Rollout plan: feature flagged off by default; staged rollout to internal tenants, then opt-in beta for self-serve tenants, monitor econ_signals and quant_compat_events for 72 hours each stage. Related: ENG-3921 (batch telemetry), SUP-1212 (customer incident that motivated classifier).
Miles Chen (reviewer): Can the classifier state be sharded per-GPU to avoid hot locks? Suggest using per-worker ring buffer and eventual merge.
Ava Patel (author): Good point — switched to per-worker ring buffer and merged metrics via async flush. See batch_shape_classifier.go line 112 for comment.
Priya Nair (reviewer): We should avoid making quant changes for tenants with <10k requests/day in this release. Please add tenant-threshold check.
Ava Patel (author): Added tenant-min-traffic check and flagged in config (deploy/feature_flags/feature_flags.yaml).
Jonah Reed (reviewer): CI flagged a perf regression on a synthetic warmup; test harness shows +2% CPU in one scenario. Can we add an opt-out switch at admission?
Ava Patel (author): Added early-exit fast-path when classifier confidence < 0.25 to avoid additional CPU on cold paths. Reran benchmarks — perf regression resolved.
Miles Chen (approver): LGTM after the perf run and tenant-threshold check. Approving for merge.
- Add batch-shape-classifier to tag request patterns and enable safer quant profile selection.
- New telemetry: econ_signals, batch_shape_hist, quant_compat_events.
- Feature-flagged rollout with tenant opt-in and operator runbook.
- Safety gates: tenant-min-traffic and confidence thresholds to prevent oscillation.

Context and motivation: Our presubmit lane has two pain points: 1) developers hit long lint feedback times because lint shards are pinned to heavyweight runners; 2) dependency visibility is poor in presubmit which creates noisy failures and blocked merges. This PR introduces a light-weight 'fastpath' presubmit router, augments dependency visibility telemetry, and performs a small audit of top-level deps to reduce spurious infra noise. Summary of changes: - Introduce a presubmit router that routes small lint-only PRs to lightweight ephemeral runners (fastpath) and leaves heavier integration flows untouched. - Add dependency-visibility telemetry hooks (dep fingerprinting and top-level dep list) to CI traces and to the local dev lint script. - Replace the monolithic .github/presubmit.yml with two focused workflows: presubmit-fastpath.yml and presubmit-standard.yml. - Add a small dep-audit utility under tools/dep-audit to build a top-level manifest used by the router and for telemetry. - Update dev docs with quickstart for fastpath and fallback flows. Checklist: - [x] Fastpath router implementation and unit tests - [x] CI workflow split and smoke runs - [x] Dep-audit utility and packaging script - [x] Docs + migration notes - [x] Feature gated behind repo-level flag (default: enabled for files < 200 LOC and changes restricted to src/, pkg/, docs/) Rollout plan: 1) Feature enabled in main for all internal builds behind a repo flag. 2) Observe telemetry for one week; measure median lint feedback latency and presubmit success rate. 3) If no regressions, enable by default for all fastpath-eligible PRs. Backwards compatibility / migration: Existing presubmit logic stays in presubmit-standard.yml and is the default for non-eligible PRs. Dep-audit can be run locally (tools/dep-audit scan) to generate the manifest for a developer; CI will regenerate on every run. Testing and validation: Ran full CI matrix in ephemeral environment (see CI notes). Manually validated that lint responses for small PRs dropped from ~7m to ~90s median in the canary org. Related linear: ENG-1245 implements telemetry contract; ENG-2033 tracks router heuristics and rollout. Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the router decision heuristic conservative; if the heuristics are too restrictive we'll relax them in a follow-up. For incident mitigation, presubmit-standard.yml remains the clear fallback.
Priya Nair: Please add a brief note in the router unit test describing the heuristic edge cases (e.g. binary proto changes).
Sofia Martinez: Can you add CI budget telemetry for fastpath vs standard so SRE can track cost variance?
Liam O'Connor: Minor nits in shellscript quoting; also prefer a smaller docker image for fastpath runner — suggested alpine + busybox.
Ethan Wang (author): Addressed Priya's test note and added a unit that simulates proto delta detection. Added telemetry metrics as requested by Sofia (ci.fastpath.count, ci.fastpath.median_latency). Switched fastpath runner image to slim-builder:alpine-3.19. Ready for final review.

Summary: This PR addresses two related classes of v1/chat compatibility issues surfaced in production and by customers: (1) 'param-echo' where the streaming path could emit fragments that duplicated system/instruction text into the final assembled completion, and (2) fragile fncall/structured-output streaming frames that could leave the client with partial JSON or missing function-call metadata after transient network disconnects.
Motivation: Customers migrating to the v1/chat compatibility layer observed occasional duplicated instructions in the final completion and incorrect fncall objects after reconnects; both reduce reliability for production apps (especially tool-calling and structured-output use cases). This change reduces duplication and makes streaming frame reassembly deterministic on reconnect and partial replays.
What changed (high level):
- Introduced a streaming "echo filter" at the param-negotiation boundary that identifies tokens/segments highly-correlated with pinned system/instruction parameters and suppresses them from the final merge unless there is model-confirmed divergence. The filter uses a lightweight prefix-match heuristic and confidence threshold derived from the runtime token scorer to avoid false positives.
- Reworked fncall streaming framing: fragments now include a 2-byte frame header (version + frag-index) and an end-sentinel marker. A heartbeat/ack sequence allows servers to mark frames as committed; clients reconnecting in the middle of a stream can request the last-committed index.
- Added final-payload reconciler that aggregates streaming logprobs and stop hints with the non-streamed completion generation step. This prevents the streaming path from overwriting canonical stop/logprob state.
- Tests and observability: added deterministic unit tests for param-echo heuristic, integration tests that simulate reconnect/failure during fncall streaming, and new metrics: streaming.frame_reassembly_failures, streaming.echo_suppressed_count.
Commits (summary):
- 1a3f2e9: add param-echo filter and unit tests
- 2b9e4c1: implement fncall frame header + sentinel, add frame commit/ack handshake
- 7c5d113: reconcile streaming logprob aggregation with final payload
- 9ae5b2f: integration tests for reconnect / partial frame replay
- c4d8f07: docs: console notes on heartbeat/compat
- f5b1a22: fix linting and race in frame ack path
Changed files (illustrative):
- server/streaming/echo_filter.go (new) — implements prefix similarity heuristic and integration with token scorer
- server/streaming/frame_protocol.go (modified) — adds headers, frag-index, and ack handling
- server/streaming/handler_test.go (modified/added) — tests for reconnect scenarios and fncall reassembly
- sdk/python/redwood/v1/chat_stream.py (modified) — client-side support for reconnect and committed-index request
- sdk/typescript/stream-client.ts (modified) — small compat helpers for browsers
- docs/compat/v1-chat-streaming.md (modified) — added section about heartbeat and canary rollout notes
Small snippet (illustrative) included in server/streaming/frame_protocol.go: "// frame header: version(1) | fragIndex(1) - allows deterministic reassembly across reconnects"
Tests:
- Unit: echo_filter_test.go covers prefix-collision cases, threshold tuning and false positive regression.
- Integration: simulated 3 reconnect scenarios with random drops; fncall object reassembled successfully in 98/100 runs locally; CI runs are deterministic via mocked runtime.
CI:
- Pre-merge pipeline: lint, unit, integration, e2e-candidate.
- Current run: all checks passed (lint warnings auto-fixed), integration harness passed 28/28 scenarios.
- Flaky tests noticed initially (integration: reconnect-flaky) were stabilized by increasing frame timeout from 100ms->250ms.
Review thread (highlights):
- Owen Patel (reviewer): "Please ensure we don't silently drop legitimate repeated text when model actually re-states an instruction intentionally (e.g., role-reflection). The heuristic needs an escape hatch." Maya: "Added an escape: if final-generation logprob mass on the prefix exceeds 0.6 we bypass suppression and mark as explicit-repeat in telemetry."
- Priya Singh: "Add e2e that runs a small tool-calling example through the python and TS clients to validate fncall JSON shape end-to-end." Maya: "Added python/ts e2e callers and wired them into the integration job; added OP-level assertion on fncall.name and args."
- Luis Fernandez: "Risk: consumers of the streaming format may not be able to handle the 2-byte header. Need a compatibility flag." Maya: "Default frame version is backward compatible: legacy clients ignore the header and server emits a compat fallback for older agent-headers. Documented in compat notes."
- Owen (approve after fixes): "LGTM — tests look good, metrics added. Please watch canary closely."
Release notes (in PR body): "Fixes param-echo duplication in v1/chat streaming path and improves fncall frame recovery on reconnects; no API change for callers, minor client-side updates available in SDKs for better reconnect handling."
Deployment plan and canary:
- Canary rollout to 10% of hosted v1-chat traffic for 48 hours; streaming.frame_reassembly_failures and streaming.echo_suppressed_count monitored with alert thresholds.
- If any regression >0.5% error rate in fncall shape, automatic rollback will be triggered.
Backwards compatibility:
- Server emits header but will continue to stream compat frames when client advertises legacy agent via User-Agent/Handshake.
- SDK updates (python/ts) are optional but recommended for deterministic reconnect behavior.
Follow-ups:
- ENG-2071: telemetry dashboards for echo suppression across customers.
- ENG-2104: explore ML-based prefix de-duplication using scoring model (longer-term).
Merge: Squash-merged into main on 2026-02-03 after approvals from Priya and Owen. Canary started immediately; initial canary metrics show reduced duplication events (telemetry drop ~78% on sample customers).
Known limitations:
- Very adversarial prompts that intentionally echo instruction tokens may still appear in final output when model logprob supports it (we preserve these via escape hatch).
- There is a small increase in server-side CPU for the echo heuristic (~1.8% at 95th), measured and included in the release notes for capacity planning.
If you want to test locally:
- Run `make integration` under server/streaming with MOCK_RUNTIME=1
- Python example: examples/streaming_fncall.py (calls new client reconnect helper)
Fix streaming duplication where system/instruction content could be echoed in final completions; improved fncall streaming frame reassembly and heartbeat recovery to reduce client-visible truncation and malformed structured outputs.
Canary metrics to be reviewed by SRE and Product on 2026-02-05; docs updated to include migration guidance for older clients.

Context and motivation: Tenant teams frequently hit tradeoffs between latency SLOs and unit cost because current batch/cache defaults are static and reactive. This PR introduces a new CLI-driven workflow and small runtime hook that converts short-term tenant workload forecasts into tuned batching, cache and quantization presets. The goal is to automate safe, measurable saving suggestions and enable rapid dry-runs in sandbox before any rollout.

What this PR delivers: rwd-econ-shaper CLI (Go): consumes historical telemetry + 7-day forecast (CSV/JSON), simulates continuous-batching and prefix-cache efficiency, and produces an ordered list of recommended presets (batch shapes, cache TTLs, quantization profile hints) with an estimated delta on per-token cost and 95th latency. The CLI also emits a compact policy bundle that can be uploaded as a tenant override via the existing admin API.

Key design notes: 1) Forecast-first: simulator accepts per-tenant arrival-rate forecasts (per-minute) and uses the same service-side batching model to estimate microburst impact. 2) Conservative fallbacks: recommendations include a safe baseline and a risk score; operator must opt-in to aggressive profiles. 3) Quant profiles are suggested, not forced — the runtime will only apply quantization variants if tenant policy permits. 4) Unit economics: the estimator reports delta in cost/token and projected monthly savings at current traffic. 5) Telemetry and audit: every generated bundle is accompanied by a deterministic signature and simulation snapshot for reproducibility.

Files and surface changes (high level): - cmd/rwd-econ-shaper/main.go: new CLI, help/man pages, JSON/CSV parsers. - internal/econ/simulator/*: simulator core (traffic model, batching estimator, cache model). - internal/econ/quant_hints.go: quant profile heuristics and safety checks. - runtime/config/tenant_overrides.go: small hook to accept safe bundle metadata (no runtime enforcement change). - api/admin/v1/tenant_overrides.go: endpoint to validate and stage bundles. - docs/cli/econ-shaper.md: usage examples and rollback guidance. - tests/econ: unit tests for simulator, integration test harness with local runtime stub.

Commits (summary): - feat(cli): initial rwd-econ-shaper skeleton and argument parsing - feat(sim): implementation of forecast-driven batching simulator - feat(econ): quantization hint generator and risk scoring - feat(api): extend tenant overrides validation endpoint - test: add unit and integration tests and CI workflows - docs: usage guide and template forecast files - ci: add Github Actions workflow for CLI build and smoke test

Checklist: [x] Unit tests for simulator core [x] Integration test that validates bundle upload [x] Doc entry with example forecast [x] Telemetry events instrumented for simulation runs [x] Linear tickets referenced: ENG-1515 (simulator), PM-213 (UX/workflow)

Testing and CI: The new GH Actions job runs cross-platform builds, unit tests, and a quick end-to-end that runs the CLI against a local runtime stub. CI initially flagged a flaky test (TestBatchShapeEdgeCases) — fixed by increasing timeout and adding tighter deterministic seed. Final CI status: pass.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag econ.shaper.enabled=false. 2) Internal dry-run: engineering can run CLI in staging to generate bundles and validate telemetry; no live tenant changes. 3) Tenant opt-in by admins: admin API accepts staged bundles and applies them in a canary group (10% of traffic) with automated rollback if 95th latency regresses > 10%. 4) Monitor: create dashboards (prefill:dash/econ-shaper) and alerts (SLO regression, cache hit rate delta).

Backward compatibility and safety: The runtime default behavior unchanged. Bundles are advisory until an admin uploads and promotes them. Quantization hints are gated by tenant policy and require explicit acknowledgement for aggressive profiles.

Telemetry and observability: Emitted events: econ.shaper.run (success/failure), econ.shaper.simulation_snapshot_id, econ.shaper.recommendation_bundle_id. Dashboards and alert runbooks included in docs/cli/econ-shaper.md.

Related work: complements tenant-warmstart and prefill automations; design intentionally avoids automatic application without explicit opt-in.

Known limitations and future work: - Forecast quality sensitive: next PR will add an optional forecast quality estimator. - Auto-apply alpha guarded: we plan an experimental auto-apply pipeline with manual guardrails after additional experimentation.

Merge notes: Squash-merging after approvals. Change set kept intentionally scoped to CLI + validation hook; no automatic runtime application included in this PR.
Benji Huang: Nice end-to-end. Two asks: 1) please add a smoke test verifying bundle signature is stable across runs, 2) clarify risk scoring math (percentiles vs. stddev).
Aisha Patel: Addressed both — added deterministic snapshot signature and expanded doc on risk scoring (now percentile+tail penalty).
Marta O'Neill: Could we gate the CLI so it only runs when forecast file has >= 7 days? Also request to include an example of tenant override JSON.
Aisha Patel: Added validation for minimum forecast horizon and included example override in docs/fixtures. Also added clearer errors for malformed forecasts.
Devon Park: CI showed flakiness in TestBatchShapeEdgeCases; increase seed determinism and timeout looked good. Approving pending squash and changelog entry.
Benji Huang: Approved. Verified E2E against staging runtime stub and reviewed simulated cost deltas (savings estimates conservative).

Context: We've had ongoing divergence across the Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs for credential fallbacks, retry presets, and the pullstream (streaming) ergonomics. Teams reported brittle reauth interactions during long-lived streams and inconsistent retry defaults across SDKs leading to different production behavior. This PR centralizes the credential profile definitions, introduces an ergonomic PullStreamBridge to harmonize consumer-facing streaming patterns, and bumps tri-SDK versions to align expectations.

Motivation: 1) Make credential fallback behavior predictable across languages (delegated, cascade, and local-cache modes). 2) Provide clear retry presets (latency-sensitive, throughput-optimized, and conservative) that map to runtime policies. 3) Offer a small, opt-in PullStreamBridge API that simplifies checkpointing/resume, peek semantics, and a cancelable iterator pattern that matches the new credential lease/heartbeat semantics.

What this PR does (summary): - New shared credential profile catalog (internal/cred/profile_catalog.go + language bindings) describing TTLs, refresh windows, and fallback order. - DelegatedFallback credential mode: prefer delegated tokens, then fall back to cached service token, then to refresh. - Retry presets: latency-sensitive (single fast reauth attempt, short backoff), throughput-optimized (aggressive batching-friendly backoff), conservative (safer but higher tail latency). Presets are serialized in a small JSON schema used to drive SDK defaults. - PullStreamBridge: small facade implemented in each SDK that provides peek(), next(), and resume_from(checkpoint) semantics; attaches credential lease heartbeats when streams stay idle for >30s. - Telemetry tags added to all streaming requests: sdk.language, cred.profile, retry.preset, stream.bridge=true. - Tests and integration harness updates for session handoff scenarios and long-lived streams. - Version bumps: python 0.14.4, typescript 1.6.3, go 1.5.1 (changelogs included).

Files changed (high-level): see files_changed list below; notable changes include SDK public surface additions (peekable/resume methods), internal credential orchestrator, JSON presets, and docs/upgrade-guides/sdk-credential-orchestrator.md.

Important design notes: - The credential profile catalog is intentionally small and serializable so the control plane can propose presets in the future; SDKs read the local defaults but accept a remote override object. - PullStreamBridge is opt-in: existing streaming semantics are preserved unless consumers import the bridge facade. This keeps the PR safe for large dependent codebases. - Retry presets intentionally map to route/runtime hints; the runtime already understands the preset names and can route requests to different capacity tiers when needed.

Testing: - Unit tests added for all SDKs (python tests/unit/test_retry_profiles.py, ts tests/stream/pullstream_bridge.spec.ts, go stream/facade_test.go). - Integration scenario in perf-canary updated to run a long-lived stream with delegated credential rotation. - CI matrix ran py/ts/go, linting, and e2e harness; one flaky TS test was stabilized by adding a short jitter to timing expectations.

How to try locally: - python: pip install -e sdk/python && run examples/streaming/pullstream_example.py --use-bridge
- typescript: yarn install && yarn test:stream --bridge
- go: go test ./... -run PullStreamBridge; example in examples/go/pullstream/README.md

Rollout plan: feature gated behind environment variable REDWOOD_SDK_USE_PULLSTREAM_BRIDGE for initial weeks. We coordinated with infra (ENG-1951) to ensure runtime preset semantics are honored.

Related work: references ENG-1951 (credential orchestration), ENG-2022 (streaming ergonomics spike), and SUP-4123 (customer incident describing token rotation mid-stream).

Release notes: added to changelogs for each SDK; see release_notes field below.

Merge: squash merge after final approval and successful CI rerun.

Aisha Kapoor: Yes — it's opt-in behind REDWOOD_SDK_USE_PULLSTREAM_BRIDGE (documented in upgrade guide).

Context: Customers in regulated regions require per-tenant enforcement that incoming requests are pinned to an allowed geo zone and that any KMS operations use an ephemeral operator lease tied to the asserted zone. This PR implements a lightweight "zone-locker" middleware to normalize/respect tenant zone assertions, an operator KMS lease shim to create short-lived operator-scoped credentials for cross-tenant KMS orchestration, and an "audit-stripper" profile that redacts sensitive context from high-volume logs while preserving compliance anchors. Motivation: reduce blast radius for cross-region operator actions, make KMS usage auditable and proofable, and lower PII exposure in high-cardinality audit streams. Changes include: 1) request-time zone assertor that enforces tenant zone from token/headers with configurable soft/hard modes; 2) operator KMS lease flow that leverages existing CMK allocator but issues ephemeral operator leases with signed residency assertions; 3) pluggable audit-stripper pipeline stage with configurable redaction profiles per-route. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked: internal/doc/tenant-zone-locker.md - [x] unit & integration tests added - [x] staged rollout flags (feature gate) - [x] documented runtime knobs in CLI and Helm - [x] linear tasks closed: ENG-4182, ENG-4190 Notes: This is intentionally conservative in scope (does not change default enforcement behavior). See internal runbook for rollback and emergency disable of zone-locker and operator-lease feature gates. For more details see https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4182 and internal doc at docs/security/tenant-zone-locking.md
Rafael Ortiz (reviewer): Please add a unit test for the token-without-zone case showing soft vs hard enforcement behavior. Also add metrics for denied-by-zone counts.
Maya Chen (author): Added tests and a metric zone_enforcement_denied_total; updated PR with those commits.
Priya Nair (reviewer): Operator lease looks good but surface the lease TTL as a knob; teams may need 5m vs 1m depending on cross-region latency.
Maya Chen (author): Exposed operatorLease.ttl in helm values and runtime flags; documented recommended defaults in the design doc.
Jordan Blake (reviewer): Audit-stripper redaction profile needs a compliance note — ensure GDPR/CCPA mapping retained via audit anchors.
Maya Chen (author): Added anchoring fields (residency_assertion_id and audit_hash) to the stripped payload; added docs to explain retention requirements.
Add tenant zone-locker middleware (feature-gated) to assert tenant geo; Introduce operator-scoped ephemeral KMS lease for operator orchestrator flows; Add audit-stripper pipeline with configurable redaction profiles to reduce PII in high-volume logs; Helm chart knobs for enabling/disabling features; No default behavioral change unless feature gates are turned on.
Risk: misconfiguration could block legitimate cross-region operator tasks or over-redact audit data. Mitigations: defaults are non-enforcing (soft mode), feature gates and kill-switch route in ingress, rollout to 10% then 100% with monitoring, added metrics zone_enforcement_denied_total and operator_lease_failures_total, and a rollback plan documented in the runbook.
Follow-up work: add RBAC v2 policy generator that emits per-tenant zone allowlists (ENG-4201), and a telemetry dashboard for operator lease usage. This PR intentionally avoids touching the policy compiler to reduce blast radius.

Context: Presubmit latency and noisy CI cache misses were causing long developer feedback loops and elevated flakiness on language/toolchain-heavy jobs. This PR reduces cold start time for developer CI by optimizing toolchain bootstrap and adds a deterministic dependency eviction policy for CI caches to reduce transitive bloat and stale devdeps. Motivation: shorten 'git -> green' for common PRs, lower CI costs by reducing redundant downloads, and make cache contents more predictable so presubmit sharding and path-aware caching are more effective. What I changed (high level): 1) toolchain microimages: created a thin bootstrap image (ci/images/toolchain-micro:sha) that contains only the minimal runtime + package manager credentials; full toolchain layers are lazily populated. 2) shallow-restore logic: presubmit workflow will perform a shallow cache restore (metadata-first) to populate environment variables and steer which layers to hydrate, avoiding expensive full restores for small changes. 3) dependency eviction policy: new deterministic eviction algorithm (LRU-with-ttl + package-type prioritization) implemented in ci/cache/evictor.go and wired to the cache-gateway so caches do not accumulate cold transitive deps indefinitely. 4) toolchain bootstrap shim: replace bash-heavy bootstrap with a small Go binary (ci/bootstrap/fastboot) to parallelize installs and report structured timing metrics. 5) presubmit workflows: split the presubmit lane into 'fast-feedback' and 'full' lanes. Fast-feedback runs lint, unit tests, and lightweight type checks using microimage; full runs in nightly or gated merges. 6) release hooks: decoupled release trigger step so small presubmit jobs don't block release scans; added safety gate to ensure full lane completed on release branches. Implementation notes: changes are additive and gated by a feature flag (ci.features.fast_boot) toggled for the repo default and a canary org. The eviction policy persists metadata in the existing cache index; no external DB required. The fastboot binary is intentionally small (~150KB) with no new runtime deps. Rollout plan: 1) canary on small repos for 48 hours with telemetry (cache-hit rate, bootstrap time, job duration) 2) expand to redwood/* repos 3) default-on after 2 weeks if metrics show >=25% reduction in median presubmit duration. Testing: unit tests added for eviction heuristics, integration harness for microimage restores, and end-to-end smoke on a small cohort of PRs. Perf numbers from canary: median presubmit boot reduced from 42s -> 18s; median lint stage reduced 34% on fast lane. Risks & mitigations: 1) evictions could remove rare but required artifacts -> mitigated by TTL overrides and manual pinning via a cache-allowlist. 2) flakiness due to lazy hydration -> preserved full restore as fallback and added validation that rehydration completes before test shards requiring binaries run. Rollback: flip ci.features.fast_boot = false to revert fastpath; eviction policy can be paused via cache-gateway flag. Checklist: [x] unit tests [x] integ tests [x] perf telemetry [x] feature-flag gating [x] docs updated (ci/README.md) Related: builds on work in ENG-7240 that introduced path-aware cache keys.
Evan Liu: 'Great reduction in noise; please add a test for eviction boundary when TTL==0.' Author (Aisha): 'Added eviction TTL boundary unit test and updated docs to cover manual pinning.' Sofia Kim: 'Can we expose a metric for eviction-induced misses to watch regressions?' Author: 'Added metric cache.eviction.misses and a dashboard stub; will iterate.' Marco Diaz: 'Approvals pending green CI and perf dashboard; I'm comfortable with squash merge after canary.' Approvals: Evan Liu (approve), Marco Diaz (approve), Sofia Kim (approve after metrics added). CI: initial run failed (lint) due to gofmt; fixed in commit 2; subsequent runs passed.
Presubmit performance improvements: faster toolchain bootstrap via microimages and fastboot shim; deterministic CI cache eviction to reduce stale transitive deps. Feature gated; rollout started with canary. Expect ~25-40% faster presubmit feedback for typical PRs.

Summary: Implements a reusable, feature-flagged console nudge component used by the Lifecycle Growth Experiments sprint. Adds (1) a generic <NudgeCard/> UI with consistent layout, accessibility, and CTA patterns, (2) targeting rules for which nudge to show based on user activation state + page placement + experiment cohort, (3) dismissal persistence (server-backed with a local fallback) so users don’t see the same nudge repeatedly, and (4) basic analytics hooks for impressions/clicks/dismissals to support experiment readouts. Motivation: We need a lightweight in-console “next best action” system to reduce time-to-first-request and guide new users through API key creation → first request → enable streaming → view usage. This PR focuses on a minimal framework (not a full onboarding checklist). It’s designed to be iterated on via config + feature flags. Scope / notable behavior: - New NudgeCard component (title/body/CTA, optional secondary link, icon slot, compact vs default density). - Placements supported: dashboard header, api-keys empty state, quickstart panel. - Targeting model: given (userId, workspaceId, placement, currentRoute, activationState, cohortAssignment), pick a single nudge (highest priority) or none. - Dismissal persistence: Dismissals are stored as (user_id, nudge_id, nudge_version, placement) with a timestamp; server returns dismissed list for the user; client also caches to localStorage to avoid flicker before the server response arrives. Changing nudge_version will resurface the nudge (intended for copy/UX iterations). - Feature flags: gated behind lifecycle_growth_console_nudges_v1; cohort assignment read from existing experiment assignment service; includes explicit holdout behavior (do not render any nudges). - Analytics: emits product events for impression/click/dismiss; events include nudge_id, nudge_version, placement, route, cohort, and activation_state. No PII beyond internal IDs already present in standard console telemetry. Out of scope: complex multi-step checklist UI, personalization beyond activation state, or backend campaign management. Related: pairs with activation funnel eventing work (ENG-10492 / PR #28431) and the experiment flag rollouts (PR #28477).
console/ui: add NudgeCard component + styles + a11y
console/nudges: add nudge registry + selection/prioritization logic
console/nudges: add dismissal persistence (API + local cache) + versioning
console/flags: gate nudge rendering behind lifecycle_growth_console_nudges_v1 + holdout
telemetry: add console_nudge_* analytics hooks (impression/click/dismiss) + tests
qa: add Playwright coverage for dismissal + holdout cohort behavior
Marissa Cole: Can we ensure only ONE nudge shows at a time? I don’t want competing CTAs on dashboard. Also please confirm dismissal doesn’t block API key creation (we had issues with gating in the past). Dylan Brooks: Yep — selector returns a single nudge per placement; added a hard cap of 1 per page render and a priority table. Dismiss only hides the nudge card; it never disables underlying UI. Kenji Nakamura: Spacing/typography looks good but the “Dismiss” affordance is too subtle on mobile. Also CTA should be the only prominent button. Dylan Brooks: Updated to icon-button with tooltip and increased hitbox; secondary link now renders as text link (not a button) to avoid dual primaries. Nadia Rahman: Event names should align with the lifecycle taxonomy; please include nudge_version and placement and ensure impressions dedupe per page view. Dylan Brooks: Updated events to console_nudge_impression/click/dismiss and included required props. Added a per-render guard to avoid double-impression when React re-renders. Jada Williams: How does holdout work? We need deterministic assignment. Dylan Brooks: Uses the experiment assignment service (same as email). If cohort == holdout, selector returns null early and we do not emit impression events. Leila Farouk: Playwright test should cover refresh persistence and version bump. Dylan Brooks: Added both cases; also added a regression test for the api-keys empty state placement. Chloe Martin: Migration looks fine; please add an index on (user_id, placement). Dylan Brooks: Added composite index + updated query plan notes. Approvals: Marissa ✅, Kenji ✅, Nadia ✅, Jada ✅, Leila ✅, Chloe ✅.
Unit: yarn test console-nudges + telemetry-events. E2E: Playwright spec covers (a) nudge renders for eligible cohort, (b) dismiss hides immediately and remains hidden after refresh, (c) holdout cohort renders nothing, (d) version bump causes resurface. Manual: verified on staging with test users in each activation state (no_api_key, has_key_no_request, has_request_no_streaming) and validated event emission in the debug telemetry panel.
Keep feature flag OFF by default. Enable for internal dogfood first (25%) on staging, then 5% production for new signups only (signup_date >= 2026-01-20), then ramp to 50% if no UX regressions/support tickets. Holdout cohort (~10%) enforced at assignment layer. If issues: disable lifecycle_growth_console_nudges_v1 and/or force holdout for all cohorts; dismissal persistence is safe to leave in place (no user-visible surface without flag).
Console now supports a feature-flagged onboarding nudge card with targeting + dismissal persistence and telemetry hooks (internal use for Lifecycle Growth experiments).

payload.body:
- Adds a global (fleet-safety) circuit breaker for shared burst pools per (region, hardware_class) that automatically disables burst admission when safety caps are exceeded.
- Adds Prometheus metrics and alert annotations to explain when/why burst was disabled and when it recovered.
- Adds runbook links and structured reason codes surfaced to routing/support tooling.
Why: As we enable Dedicated burst in more regions/hardware classes, we need a hard backstop that prevents burst demand from consuming too much of the managed fleet and impacting non-burst tenants. We already have per-tenant caps and fairness, but we were missing a global safety limiter that can shut off burst admission quickly under fleet saturation or telemetry anomalies.

What: Introduces a global circuit breaker in the burst admission controller that opens when fleet-safety caps are exceeded for a given (region, hardware_class, pool_id). When open, burst requests are denied immediately with a deterministic denial reason and a suggested retry-after. The breaker automatically closes after a configurable cool-down + recovery threshold.

Behavior / semantics:
- Scope: breaker is evaluated per (region, hardware_class, pool_id). No cross-region behavior.
- Inputs: (a) fleet telemetry: burst_pool_allocated_gpus, burst_pool_target_gpus, burst_pool_saturation_ratio, and telemetry freshness; (b) config thresholds in policy engine.
- Open conditions (all must be true unless noted):
  - saturation_ratio >= burst.global_breaker.open_saturation_ratio (default 0.92)
  - allocated_gpus >= burst.global_breaker.open_allocated_gpus_floor (prevents flapping on tiny pools)
  - telemetry_age_seconds <= burst.global_breaker.max_telemetry_age_seconds (if telemetry is stale, we fail closed for burst: open breaker)
- Close conditions:
  - saturation_ratio <= burst.global_breaker.close_saturation_ratio (default 0.85)
  - breaker has been open for at least burst.global_breaker.min_open_seconds (default 30s) to avoid oscillation
- Denial semantics: breaker-open is an immediate denial (no queuing) and is evaluated before fairness token buckets.
- Determinism: given the same snapshot (telemetry + config), the decision is deterministic; we include the breaker state and evaluated thresholds in the internal debug payload (redacted externally).

API / surfaces:
- Admission response includes: deny_reason=GLOBAL_CIRCUIT_OPEN, retry_after_ms (bounded), and a short message suitable for logs.
- Adds internal debug fields (behind internal auth) to explain: breaker_state, open_reason, telemetry_age, saturation_ratio.

Observability:
- New metrics:
  - redwood_burst_global_breaker_open{region,hardware_class,pool_id} (gauge 0/1)
  - redwood_burst_global_breaker_open_total{region,hardware_class,pool_id,reason} (counter)
  - redwood_burst_admission_denied_total{region,hardware_class,pool_id,deny_reason} includes GLOBAL_CIRCUIT_OPEN
- Alert updates:
  - Adds annotations to BurstPoolSaturation and BurstAdmissionDenials alerts with the breaker status and thresholds (open/close ratios, telemetry age) so on-call can quickly tell if denials are expected.
  - Adds a new warning-level alert: BurstGlobalCircuitBreakerOpen (pages only if open > N minutes AND non-burst p95 latency is regressing, handled by SLO gate elsewhere).

Safety / rollout:
- Default config is disabled until explicitly enabled per region/hardware allowlist (ties into existing feature-flag and rollout gating).
- The breaker can be forced open via emergency config override (same pathway as other burst kill switches) but there is no new manual toggle endpoint in this PR.

Test plan:
- Unit tests: breaker open/close transitions, telemetry-stale behavior, hysteresis, and retry-after bounds.
- Integration tests: simulated saturation spikes; verifies burst denials flip to GLOBAL_CIRCUIT_OPEN while non-burst routing remains unchanged.
- Staging: replayed a recorded burst spike trace; confirmed breaker opens and alert annotations populate.

Notes / follow-ups:
- We should tune default thresholds per hardware class once we have more beta data (H100 vs L40S behave differently under partial saturation).
- The Grafana panel for breaker state is added in a separate observability-pack PR; this PR only emits metrics and annotations.

Refs:
- Linear: ENG-4902
- Related: pr-23822 (burst metrics baseline), pr-23837 (feature flags / kill switch), pr-23988 (SLO-based gating)
- Runbook: Burst pool overload mitigation (Confluence) to be updated with breaker-specific guidance after merge.
Keiko Yamamoto: Can we confirm we fail closed for burst when telemetry is stale? I'd rather deny burst than risk over-admitting based on an old low utilization snapshot.
Peter Holtz (author): Yep. In this PR, telemetry_age_seconds > max_telemetry_age_seconds forces breaker open with reason=TELEMETRY_STALE. Added a unit test and included telemetry age in the debug payload + alert annotations.
Vanessa Ortiz: Thresholds: 0.92 open / 0.85 close seem reasonable for H100 but L40S pools have been smaller. Do we have an allocated_gpus floor to avoid flapping on tiny pools?
Peter Holtz (author): Added open_allocated_gpus_floor (default 8) to prevent flapping on small pools. Configurable per pool via policy engine; defaults are conservative and disabled by default until allowlisted.
Jordan Lee: Determinism concern: saturation_ratio is coming from telemetry which can change between retries. That's fine, but the decision should be deterministic for a single evaluation. Are we snapshotting telemetry once per request?
Peter Holtz (author): Yes—telemetry snapshot is fetched once at request start and passed through the decision pipeline; we don't re-read mid-evaluation. Added a comment and made the snapshot struct immutable after creation.
Mina Haddad: How is retry-after computed? We should avoid synchronized retry storms when breaker opens.
Peter Holtz (author): retry_after_ms is randomized (jitter) within bounds based on min_open_seconds; also capped at 2s for now. We can revisit once we see client behavior. Included in response only for breaker-open and tenant-cap denials.
Sean Gallagher: Alerting: please add annotations that explain the evaluated thresholds and telemetry age so on-call can quickly assess. Also make sure this doesn't page by itself unless sustained + correlated with SLO regression.
Peter Holtz (author): Added annotations for open/close thresholds + current saturation + telemetry age. The new alert is warning-only and doesn't page; paging remains gated by SLO regression policies handled separately.
Keiko Yamamoto: Requesting changes: please add a small integration test that verifies GLOBAL_CIRCUIT_OPEN is returned ahead of fairness logic, otherwise we could burn tokens unnecessarily.
Peter Holtz (author): Done. Added integration scenario 'breaker_preempts_fairness' and adjusted ordering so breaker evaluation happens before token consumption. Pushed update.
Keiko Yamamoto: Approved.
Vanessa Ortiz: Approved (ship it; we'll tune thresholds during beta).
Sean Gallagher: Approved. Please link the runbook update PR once it's ready.
payload.title: Global circuit breaker for burst pools (fleet safety cap)

payload.body:
Context: We see intermittent flapping of SLO alerts driven by very short-lived invocation spikes (typically <250ms) that inflate token latency percentiles for a tiny subset of requests. These spikes often correlate with transient infra hiccups (node preemption, brief cold starts) and create alert noise that distracts on-call.

Problem: Existing per-route percentiles and token-level rollups are valuable but noisy for very short bursts; SLO alerts fire even when the bulk of traffic is healthy. We need a low-risk server-side approach to (1) surface per-invocation liveness for diagnostic correlation and (2) debounce alerts so short bursts don't immediately escalate.

Proposal: 1) Add a per-invocation liveness counter that increments at key lifecycle checkpoints (accept->start->first-token->complete). These counters are exported as low-cardinality metrics that can be correlated with traces and token cost metrics. 2) Introduce an alert debouncing layer that can be configured per-SLO: short grace window (default 45s) + rolling evaluation of sustained breach. Debouncer is configurable via Helm/values and the Console.

Implementation summary: - instrumentation: pkg/serving/liveness.go implements counters and tags (route_id, model, tenant_tier) with lightweight cardinality controls; uses existing metrics emitter (metrics/v2). - debouncer: observability/alerts/debouncer.go provides in-memory sliding window logic with optional persistent state using Redis when running in Dedicated/Private. - config: charts/redwood/values.yaml adds observability.alertDebouncer with sensible defaults (enabled: true, window_seconds: 45, min_breach_ratio: 0.6). - dashboards: observability/grafana/invocation_liveness_panel.json (new panel showing per-invocation state transitions, latched breach timeline). - tests: unit tests for counter transitions and debouncer policy; integration job that runs against a synthetic load generator that produces short spikes.

Testing and results: Unit tests: 34 new tests, all passing in CI. Integration: synthetic run (100k invocations with 1% short spikes) reduced alert count by 78% while preserving true positive firings in a controlled failure. CPU/memory increase negligible (~0.8% p95).

Rollout plan: - Canary: enable on staging and 10% of production routes for 24h, monitor invocation_liveness and alert counts. - Gradual ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 days with k-safety rollback if false negatives detected. - Console: add toggle in Alerts UI (behind feature flag) to allow SREs and tenants to tune local debouncer settings.

Rollback: Helm toggle to disable observability.alertDebouncer; remove debouncer state in Redis if used (script provided in observability/scripts/clear_debouncer_state.sh).

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps metrics low-cardinality by aggregating liveness states rather than per-invocation IDs. Trace correlation is added via a stable tag on the invocation to the existing tracing span (trace_id is unchanged).
Liam Chen: Asked for cardinality safeguards on tenant tags (addressed by adding tenant_tier only). Priya Nandakumar: Requested explicit unit tests for edge case where debouncer state thrashes after deploy; added test and adjusted backoff. Evan Brooks: Suggested a console toggle and documented it. Author (Maya): responded to comments, pushed 2 follow-up commits to fix tests and add Helm docs. PR approved by all reviewers on 2026-02-18. No unresolved comments.
Adds per-invocation liveness counters and a configurable alert debouncer to reduce SLO noise. Includes Grafana panels and an opt-in Helm flag. No breaking API changes.
payload.title: Add per-invocation liveness metrics and alert debouncing

Context: During runtime 1.21 canary we observed intermittent long-context tail spikes that correlated with a small subset of Dedicated pools running older NVIDIA driver + CUDA runtime combinations. Until we finish validation on those environments, we should hard-disable kernel auto-selection v2 (and fall back to v1) when the host driver/CUDA combo matches known-unstable pairs. This keeps determinism/correctness guarantees while reducing risk of tail latency regressions.

Summary of changes: Add a guardrail in the kernel selection v2 gate evaluation that checks (a) NVML-reported NVIDIA driver version and (b) CUDA runtime version, and forces v2=disabled when the combination matches an explicit denylist. Emit a structured telemetry reason so we can see how often the guardrail is firing and on which pools/SKUs. Provide an escape hatch override for oncall (explicit config opt-in) to re-enable v2 on a blocked combo for targeted testing.

Guardrail behavior: If kernel_auto_selection.v2_enabled is true AND the driver/CUDA combo is denylisted, v2 is disabled and we fall back to v1 selection path; we record selector_decision.v2_guardrail_applied=1 with reason_code=driver_cuda_denylist, along with normalized driver_version and cuda_runtime_version. If kernel_auto_selection.v2_force_enable_on_denylisted_combo is set (default false), we allow v2 but still emit telemetry with reason_code=driver_cuda_denylist_overridden.

Denylisted combos (initial): - NVIDIA driver 535.* with CUDA runtime 12.2 (observed on L40S pools) - NVIDIA driver 545.23.06 with CUDA runtime 12.3 (observed on one A100 MIG pool) Note: denylist is intentionally narrow and keyed to exact major/minor or explicit versions to avoid disabling v2 broadly; see code comments for rationale.

Implementation details: - Added DriverCudaGuardrail evaluator in runtime/config/gates that runs before per-model allow/deny rules so we can short-circuit and avoid emitting high-cardinality candidate telemetry when we already know v2 must be off. - Added version normalization helpers (strip distro suffixes, handle "535.104.05" vs "535.104") and unit tests around parsing edge cases. - Plumbed guardrail decision into selector context so deterministic replay tests remain stable (guardrail decision is a pure function of request-independent machine facts + config). - Updated docs: runtime 1.21 upgrade notes and oncall runbook to include the new guardrail + override flags.

Why here (release/1.21): This is intended as a safety patch for the release train and for Dedicated/Private customers with constrained driver upgrade paths.

Tests: - Unit: version parsing + guardrail matrix tests. - Integration: selector determinism replay test updated to include guardrail fields in the recorded environment snapshot.

Observability: - New metric: runtime.kernel_selector.v2_guardrail_applied (counter) with labels {gpu_sku_norm, driver_version_norm, cuda_runtime_version, reason_code} (driver/cuda labels are normalized and bucketed to reduce cardinality). - New event field on selector decision traces: guardrail_applied + guardrail_reason_code.

Docs/runbook updates: - Documented new config keys: kernel_auto_selection.v2_force_enable_on_denylisted_combo and kernel_auto_selection.v2_driver_cuda_denylist (optional explicit list override for Private). - Added troubleshooting section: how to confirm guardrail is firing using dashboards and how to capture the env snapshot for support escalations.

Commits (squash summary): 1) runtime: add driver/cuda guardrail evaluator + denylist plumbing 2) runtime: normalize driver versions + tests 3) obs: add guardrail metrics + trace fields (cardinality-safe) 4) docs: update runtime 1.21 notes + oncall runbook with guardrail/override

Changed areas/files (high level): - serving/runtime/kernel_selector/v2/gates/driver_cuda_guardrail.{cc,h} - serving/runtime/config/kernel_selection_flags.{cc,h} - serving/runtime/telemetry/selector_events.{proto,cc} - serving/runtime/tests/driver_cuda_guardrail_test.cc - docs/runtime/1.21/kernel-auto-selection-v2.md - docs/runbooks/kernel-selection-v2-override-and-rollback.md

Reviewer discussion (highlights): - Hiro Tanaka: Requested we keep the denylist narrow and avoid disabling across all 535.* unless we have evidence; suggested matching {535.104.*, 535.129.*} specifically. Resolution: kept wildcard at 535.* but constrained to CUDA 12.2 only and added a TODO with links to canary notes; also implemented a denylist override hook for Private to tune precisely. - Allison Grant: Flagged potential metric cardinality risk if driver versions are raw strings. Resolution: added normalization (major.minor) and explicit bucketing + reason_code enum; also documented in comments that raw host strings must not be emitted. - Omar El-Sayed: Asked for a clear reason_code so rollback automation can distinguish "guardrail disabled" from "allowlist disabled". Resolution: added guardrail_reason_code and ensured the gate decision path sets a separate boolean. - Connor O'Brien: Confirmed this is safe to land late in the 1.21 train; requested a release note blurb. Resolution: included a short note in runtime 1.21 docs and added a checklist item for canary monitoring.

CI checks: - buildkite/redwood-runtime (linux-gpu-smoke): PASS - buildkite/unit-tests: PASS - lint/clang-format: PASS - determinism-replay (selector): PASS (rerun once after updating env snapshot fixture)

Merge: Squash merged into release/1.21.

Follow-ups: - Expand denylist with confirmed versions once Dedicated fleet audit completes (owner: Omar / SRE). - Remove guardrail once CUDA/driver validation matrix is green for all supported SKUs (tracked under ENG-4821).
payload.title: Guardrail: disable kernel auto-selection v2 on known-unstable NVIDIA driver/CUDA combos

Motivation: automate tenant-safe application of batching, cache and quantization defaults to improve unit economics while preserving latency and quality SLOs. This PR introduces a cost pipeline orchestrator service that profiles tenant request shapes, simulates candidate batching/cache/quant combos, and applies conservative rollout policies with fallbacks and audit events. Includes a new 'quant-stitcher' policy that stitches multiple quant profiles by sequence-length bands to avoid quality cliffs. Checklist: 1) implement orchestrator service and CLI; 2) add quant profile v2 format and example presets; 3) add telemetry for per-tenant unit econ deltas and fallback rates; 4) add integration tests and e2e load smoke; 5) update helm values and operations runbook. Links: design doc: internal.link/cost-pipeline-design, Linear: ENG-4312. Migration note: defaults unchanged until rollout flag enabled; operators must preview diffs with the migration CLI before applying to production tenants.
We need an automated, auditable pipeline that composes batching, cache and quantization defaults per-tenant so that unit economics improvements can be rolled out safely and observed. Manual tuning is slow and error prone; this PR implements an orchestrator that reasons about tenant workload signatures, simulates expected cost/latency tradeoffs, and applies conservative quant-stitcher presets with pinch points and fallback gates.
The orchestrator has three stages: 1) profiler - samples request shapes and token distributions; 2) synthesizer - runs a lightweight simulator to estimate unit cost and latency for candidate batching/cache/quant combos; 3) applier - writes tenant overrides to the config-store with rollout metadata and safe fallback policies. Quant-stitcher is a new policy layer that stitches multiple quant profiles across sequence length bands to avoid quality cliffs. All decisions are logged as events for replay.
Defaults remain unchanged until rollout.percentage>0. A migration CLI is added (cmd/orchestrator/migrate_profiles.go) to preview diffs and apply per-tenant; ops should preview on a staging tenant group and increment rollout by 10% per day while monitoring unit_econ_delta and quality.alerts.
No model weights or PII are moved. The orchestrator requires RBAC permission cost:write; config-store writes are audited. All telemetry uses existing encryption at rest and in transit.
Local load tests show median latency unchanged, p95 increases by ~3-7ms for heavy-gen workloads depending on quant profile; estimated cost reduction 8-18% on the benchmark lab traces included in tests.
Run integration e2e with synthetic workload shapes in tests/integration/cost_pipeline_e2e_test.go; perform staged rollout using feature flag for 10% tenants, monitor metrics cost.unit_econ_delta, latency.p95, and fallback.rate over 24h; rollback via helm chart value revert.
Helm values: deploy.cost_pipeline.enabled=true and rollout.percentage=0-100; quant profile v2 defaults live under pkg/quant/profiles/v2.yaml; telemetry exposes new metrics prefixed cost_pipeline_*; add alert cost_pipeline_fallback_rate>0.5% for 1h.
Add cost pipeline orchestrator to compose batching/caching/quantization recommendations automatically;
Introduce quant-stitcher profiles v2 and safe rollout policy for tenants;
Add new telemetry for per-tenant unit-econ delta and fallback triggers;
Migration: default profiles will be applied gradually via service flags; see operations runbook.
Jordan Lee requested clearer migration path for tenants and an opt-out flag. Author added a migration CLI and updated docs. Sofia requested clearer unit tests around fallback behavior; tests added and flakey case fixed. Marcus approved after CI pass and a brief load run. Final approval by Marcus and merge after squashing.
Jordan Lee (2024-12-06): This looks promising. Please add a clear opt-out path for tenants and a preview CLI so ops can diff changes before applying. Also add a note on RBAC.
Priya Menon (2024-12-06): Added migrate_profiles CLI and RBAC notes, updated README; opt-out is supported via tenant.override=false and rollout.percentage=0. Updated description with migration guidance.
Sofia Rodriguez (2024-12-08): Can we add an integration test covering fallback when quant stitching produces a quality regression? The simulator helps, but I want an end-to-end assertion.
Priya Menon (2024-12-09): Added e2e test cost_pipeline_e2e_test.go that injects a synthetic quality regressor and asserts orchestrator triggers fallback and records audit event.
Marcus Chen (2024-12-10): Ran a short load run against staging tenants; p95 impact within expectations and fallback behaved as designed. Approving once CI green.

Adds a cohort-gated shadow quarantine controller and telemetry hooks to allow safe A/B tests and shadow traffic quarantining when regressions are detected. No public API change; opt-in via rollout config.
Context: We need a safe pattern for running A/B experiments and shadow traffic in production while automatically quarantining cohorts when regressions are detected by quality or latency signals. Motivation: ad-hoc shadowing created operational toil—on-call pages and noisy postmortems. This PR introduces a cohort-gated shadow quarantine orchestrator that detects per-cohort regressions, isolates shadow traffic into a quarantine lane, and automates rollback and notification flows. Design summary: - Cohort gating: rollouts can declare cohort selectors (user_id hash ranges, percentage buckets, request attributes). - Shadow quarantine lane: when metrics breach a configured threshold, matching cohort traffic is mirrored into an isolated quarantine pool rather than being routed to the primary candidate. Quarantine preserves request/response payloads for replay and offline debugging. - Safety gates: statistical and deterministic gates (SLO regression %, p-value threshold, upstream error increase). - Telemetry & audit: emits quarantine_open/quarantine_close events, cohort-level deltas (latency/quality/error), and a quarantine_reason field for forensic search. - Rollback automation: if quarantine persists beyond a configurable ttl or regression worsens, the orchestrator triggers a rollback to the previous stable model and closes the quarantine. Rollback is logged and emits an incident draft to the linear workspace (via ENG integration). Implementation highlights: - quarantine_controller.go implements a state machine: Idle -> Probing -> Quarantined -> RollbackPending -> Closed. - scheduler_integration adds backpressure-safe scheduling to the quarantine pool and keeps KV cache warm for candidate variants. - config_schema.go extends rollout spec: quarantine:{enabled, gates, ttl_seconds, sample_rate, mirror_ratio, notify_linear}. - Handlers expose a /rollouts/{id}/quarantine API to view state and perform manual interventions (force-close/open/rollback). - Telemetry: added protobufs and metric tags to correlate quarantine events with model versions and cohort ids. Testing & CI: - Unit tests for state transitions and gate evaluations. - e2e test that runs a synthetic cohort with injected latency and quality regression and validates quarantine opening, replay capture, and automated rollback. - Initial CI run had a flakey scheduler test; we fixed a timing assumption (see commit e1f3d44). Checks summary: - build: pass - unit-tests: pass (all rollout-controller tests) - e2e: pass (CI synthetic harness) - lint: pass - integration: pass (limited matrix) Backwards compatibility & migration: - Config is opt-in; existing rollouts are unaffected. - A migration script is provided to add defaults for older rollout specs if teams opt into quarantine by updating helm values. Operational runbook (docs/rollouts/cohort_quarantine.md): - How to enable for a rollout - Interpreting quarantine events and telemetry dashboards - Manual vs automated rollback flows - Recommended gates for common workloads Known limitations and future work: - Replay storage currently uses short-lived BLOB retention; plan to add configurable retention and replay export. - Statistical gates use a simplified delta test—will introduce more robust A/B analytics in a follow-up. Review summary and actions: - Lina requested clearer naming in the API and a small schema change to make notify_linear optional; addressed in commit c91a0f1 and docs. - Omar requested explicit tracing for replicated requests—added tracing tags and a short doc snippet. - Evan spotted race condition in transition from Probing->Quarantined under high concurrency; fixed by atomic state updates and added coverage (commit e1f3d44). Merge: squash merge after approvals.

Lina Martens (reviewer): Can we make notify_linear optional and include a default escalation policy? - Requested change
Priya Khanna (author): Made notify_linear optional, added default escalation to config and documented behavior in docs/rollouts/cohort_quarantine.md - Resolved
Omar Haddad (reviewer): We need trace propagation on mirrored requests so debugging uses the same trace id - Comment
Priya Khanna (author): Added tracing tags and propagation in scheduler_integration.go; added tests to ensure trace id is preserved - Resolved

payload.body:
Motivation: We have observed transient SLO oscillations during short-lived regional saturation events where aggressive admission and circuit resets cause noisy reopen cycles. This PR introduces a lightweight admission component (halt-attenuator) that smooths immediate hard halts by applying a short, decaying attenuation window to rate/admission decisions and a proactive region-hedger probe that detects imminent cross-region egress pressure and biases routing away from a fragile region before full failover is required. The goal is to reduce SLO oscillation, avoid circuit flapping, and preserve KV cache locality where possible so tail-latency and token-cost budgets remain stable.

What this changes (high-level):
- New runtime admission guard: HaltAttenuator (server/runtime/admission/halt_attenuator.go) which intercepts per-request admission decisions and applies a decaying attenuation factor for the first N seconds after a detected hard halt. The component does NOT replace the circuit breaker; it softens the immediate binary halt to a probabilistic attenuation for low-priority routes.
- RegionHedger probe (controlplane/hedger) that periodically samples regional egress metrics (egress_qps, local_kv_pressure, circuit_open_ratio) with a configurable window and emits a soft routing weight delta to the smart router. The hedger is conservative by default: it only nudges weights when multiple signals cross thresholds.
- Two feature flags and runtime knobs: runtime.feature.halt_attenuator (off|canary|on) and hedger.probe.window_ms and hedger.hedge_threshold. Canary defaults deploy to 5% traffic in selected regions.
- Telemetry: new metrics (halt_attenuator.attempts, halt_attenuator.allowed_ratio, hedger.weight_nudges, hedger.probe_latency_ms) and a new structured audit log when attenuation is applied so SRE can correlate attenuation events with SLO deltas.
- Tests: unit tests for attenuation decay math and integration test simulating short halts with synthetic KV pressure. Performance microbench for low-overhead path added.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- We intentionally keep attenuation probabilistic (sample/allow) rather than queueing requests to avoid head-of-line queuing in overloaded workers. That keeps latency bounds predictable for requests that are allowed through.
- The hedger is advisory only; routing decisions are ultimately decided by the router which now accepts a weight_delta from hedger. This separation keeps the hedger low-privilege and easy to toggle if we observe adverse effects.
- We do not change global circuit-breaker semantics; this is an intermediate smoothing layer meant to reduce oscillation frequency and improve graceful degradation UX.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main feature-flagged off.
2) Canary: enable runtime.feature.halt_attenuator=canary and hedger in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 at 5% for 48h with increased telemetry retention. Monitor halt_attenuator.allowed_ratio, hedger.weight_nudges and SLO 99th latency.
3) Gradually increase canary to 25% then 50% with staged regions.
4) If any region shows increased error_rate or SLO regressions, revert flag for that region and escalate.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for attenuation decay and hedger decision logic
- [x] Integration test simulating KV pressure and short halts
- [x] Bench microtest to validate <0.5% p99 overhead on hot path
- [x] Telemetry dashboards and alert runbook additions under observability-pack/dashboards/halt_attenuator.yaml
- [x] Linear tasks linked (ENG-4307)

Why this is different from previous soft-fallback attempts: Prior work focused on coarse-grained tenant quarantines or immediate failover. This PR targets the "in-between" window: the few seconds after a hard halt decision where a short smoothing action avoids triggering coordinated failovers or noisy reopen cycles. The hedger extends that by proactively steering away from regions showing early signs of instability rather than waiting for a full circuit open event.
Marcus Lee: Nice approach. Two immediate concerns: 1) Do we have any scenario where attenuation could worsen tail by letting through expensive slow requests? 2) Can hedger produce oscillation if multiple hedgers in sibling regions nudge weights against each other?
Author (Aisha Gupta): For (1) we limit attenuation to low-priority routes by default; metric halt_attenuator.allowed_ratio will be exposed per-route so SRE can inspect. For (2) hedger uses a conservative vote model (requires two signals) and adds a randomized backoff on nudges to avoid synchronized flips. Added a comment in region_hedger.go explaining the anti-oscillation backoff.
Evan Michaels: Add a fast opt-out flag scoped to deployment/unit-tests so we can flip the hedger quickly during canary. Also add more integration scenarios with mixed-priority traffic.
Author (Aisha Gupta): Added runtime.feature.hedger_opt_out and extended integration test to include mixed-priority driver. See tests/integration/short_halt_sim_test.go commit c3d4e5f.
Priya Nair: Telemetry looks good; request we add a composite SLO dashboard panel showing allowed_ratio vs 99p latency to simplify post-canny analysis.
Author (Aisha Gupta): Added panel to observability/dashboards/halt_attenuator.yaml and a short runbook step in docs/reliability/hedger.md.
Introduce HaltAttenuator admission smoothing and RegionHedger probe to reduce SLO oscillations during transient regional pressure. Feature-flagged, canary in selected regions. No breaking changes. See docs/reliability/hedger.md for rollout instructions.
payload.title: Add halt-attenuator admission and proactive region-hedger probe to reduce SLO oscillation

payload.body:
Context: Several enterprise customers requested stronger guardrails for operator-initiated cross-tenant and cross-region operations. The existing RBACv2 bindings and KMS usage controls lacked two features we need for compliance: (1) a rate-based operator claim throttler that prevents a single operator/service principal from performing high-frequency tenant-scoped actions across geozones, and (2) a delegated KMS path that lets per-tenant keys be used via a short-lived delegation token instead of long-lived operator credentials.

This PR implements a conservative, opt-in rollout of both features and wires a chained audit-check pipeline that computes incremental checksums on audit batches to detect missing or reordered audit envelopes. Motivation: reduce blast radius from operator automation bugs, provide a compliance-friendly KMS delegation flow for regulated tenants, and increase audit integrity visibility.

Changes in this PR (summary): adds a new operator claim throttler component (pkg/rbacv2/claim_throttler.go) with pluggable policies; implements a KMS delegation service (pkg/kms/delegator.go) that mints short-lived delegation tokens scoped to a tenant and operation; introduces an audit chaining writer (cmd/audit/chain_writer.go) which appends lightweight checksums to batched audit envelopes and verifies upstream sequencing; updates RBAC policy templates and role mappings to honor throttler verdicts; adds end-to-end integration tests and an operator-facing docs page.

Files of interest: pkg/rbacv2/claim_throttler.go, pkg/kms/delegator.go, internal/auth/claim_evaluator.go (hooked), cmd/audit/chain_writer.go, docs/operator/claim-throttler.md, tests/integration/test-kms-delegation.sh.

Rollout plan: feature-flag gated behind feature.operator_claim_throttle and feature.kms_delegation. Start with shadow mode for 2 weeks in prod (no enforcement, only metrics/audit entries), then opt-in enforcement for Dedicated customers on request. KMS delegation is opt-in per-tenant and requires IAM admin consent. Audit chaining will be enabled for all tenants once observed false-positive rate is below 0.5% over a 3-day sampling window.

Testing: unit tests for throttler policy evaluation and token issuance (pkg/*_test.go), integration tests exercise delegated KMS calls and verify audit chain checks (tests/integration/*). CI: added lint and static checks for new packages.

Backward compatibility and security notes: defaults are non-enforcing. Delegation tokens are short-lived (default 15m) and bound to operation and nonce. Throttler verdicts are computed deterministically from operator principal, tenant id, and policy bucket to avoid nondeterministic enforcement.

Related work: references ENG-5821 (operator rate controls) and ENG-5910 (kms per-tenant delegation). See SUP-3382 for a support ticket describing a customer incident that motivated the audit-chain checks.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration tests
- [x] Docs for operators/ent-admins
- [x] Feature flag gating
- [x] Security review (initial, follow-up scheduled)

Merge notes: squash-merged after approvals and green CI.

Noah Patel: Please add a circuit-breaker for the delegator in case of KMS provider latency spikes. Also add metrics for token issuance latency.
Maya Chen: Added a simple fallback circuit and Prometheus counters; moved token signing to a background worker to reduce hot-path latency (see commit 9d4f2c8 and e4f0a44).
Aisha Khan: Throttler looks good. Suggest tightening default policy for cross-region operator actions from 100/min to 20/min for the initial enforcement phase.
Maya Chen: Reduced default cross-region bucket to 20/min and documented in docs/operator/claim-throttler.md.
Luis Ortega: Audit chaining implementation is fine; can you ensure the checksum algorithm is stable across minor language versions? Prefer using SHA256 with explicit salt/version bytes.
Maya Chen: Switched to SHA256 with explicit version byte and added a migration path for older envelopes (chain_writer.go).
Aisha Khan: Approved after follow-ups. Noah: Approved. Luis: Approved.
Add opt-in operator claim throttling and per-tenant KMS delegation with chained audit checks. Feature gated and disabled by default. See docs/operator/claim-throttler.md for admin configuration.
Enable feature.operator_claim_throttle=shadow to validate for two weeks. For Dedicated customers requesting enforcement, set to enforcing per-tenant via admin UI and ensure KMS-delegation is provisioned with IAM consent. Monitor metric operator_claim_throttle.denied and audit.chain.checks_failed.
1) Deploy binary with feature flags off. 2) Enable shadow mode: feature.operator_claim_throttle=shadow, feature.kms_delegation=shadow. 3) After 14 days and acceptable metrics, opt-in tenants individually for enforcement.
Create a follow-up ticket to add RBAC policy generator templates for the new throttler buckets (ENG-5992). Schedule compliance comms for tenants that opt into enforced delegation.
Customers will see new audit-chain fields in audit envelopes when audit chaining is enabled; default flow is non-enforcing so no behavior change until opt-in.
