payload.body:
Motivation: Long-running incidents showed noisy alert storms when fallback/replicate paths triggered cascades and retries. Teams need per-request phase attribution (parse/routing/kernels/streaming) and trace-level stitching across retries to correctly attribute latency and token cost, plus a way to suppress alert storms that are a result of one upstream failure. This PR implements three coordinated changes: 1) request-phase attribution metricization: add phase timers and token-cost counters at each logical phase (ingest, routing, kv-cache, kernel-exec, streaming) emitted as low-cardinality labels that can be aggregated; 2) interleaved-span annotator: a tracing library component that synthesizes stable span anchors (synthetic_parent_id & phase_id) and stitches retry/fallback spans into a single logical request view for UI rollups; 3) cascade alert suppression: a server-side alert dampener that detects correlated spike patterns originating from the same upstream invocation fingerprint and suppresses secondary alerts for a bounded window (configurable per-tenant). The description below summarizes changes, testing, rollout, and follow-ups.
Changes: - serving/runtime/phase_attribution: new Go package that records phase start/stop timings and token counters. Exposes metrics via Prometheus histogram + OTLP span attributes. - tracing/annotator: interleaved-span annotator middleware (Go) that injects synthetic_parent_id and phase_id into spans and emits compact SpanAnchor events for the trace collector. - observability/metrics: new metric names (redwood_request_phase_seconds_bucket, redwood_request_phase_tokens_total, redwood_request_phase_error_count) and a migration doc mapping old token/latency metrics. - console/dashboards: added "Request Phase Waterfall" dashboard (JSON panel) with stacked latency and token-cost heatmap keyed by phase and model_variant. - alerts/cascade_suppressor: new component (Rust) that subscribes to alert events and enforces suppression policy using fingerprint indices with a TTL-backed bloom filter for memory efficiency. - docs: docs/observability/phase_attribution.md with recommended dashboards and SLO considerations. - tests: integration and e2e tests covering phase metrics under normal/fallback flows and a synthetic incident replay harness to validate suppression heuristics.
Implementation notes: - Metrics are emitted with low-cardinality labels: phase, model_variant, region, tenant_id (hashed for privacy). High-cardinality route and prompt tags are intentionally excluded from the base metrics; route-level rollups are handled by the console joiner. - Annotator uses a lightweight deterministic fingerprint (sha1 of first-3-kv cache keys + model hash + timestamp bucket) so it is stable across retries but inexpensive to compute. - Suppressor uses a windowed token-decay heuristic (suppression window default 90s) and a configurable aggressiveness score; default policy is conservative to avoid hiding unique failures.
Testing & CI: - Unit tests for phase timers, annotated spans, and suppression decision logic. - Integration tests run against local runtimes simulating fallback chains (primary -> model-fallback -> region-fallback). - Bench: microbench shows annotator adds ~120ns/span on p99 and metrics emission is batched to avoid syscall overhead. - CI: initial integration CI failed intermittently due to a flaky test (retry ordering); fixed by adding deterministic seed in test harness.
Rollout plan: - Canary: enable metrics+annotator for 5% of traffic for internal tenants for two weeks; monitor heatmap and trace stitching accuracy. - Suppressor: start in passive monitoring mode (no suppression) for one week to gather baseline correlations; then opt-in aggressive suppression for internal tenants, followed by gradual tenant rollout. - Feature flags to toggle per-tenant: phase_metrics, annotator_inject, cascade_suppressor_mode.
Review notes: reviewers asked for privacy constraints on tenant labels (hashing implemented), and for an escape hatch to disable suppression per-route (added). Related work: follow-up ENG-3478 to add UI controls for suppression tuning in Console, and ENG-3502 to surface phase-level cost at the token-aggregation API. Backwards compatibility: metric names are additive and the annotator preserves existing span ids; no breaking changes. Migration: small migration doc included recommending alert rule tweaks and new dashboard templates.
Arjun Patel: Please ensure tenant_id is hashed before emitting; avoid exposing PII in metrics. Added hashing as requested.
Sasha Ivanov: Can suppression hide real incidents? Add passive mode and per-route disable. Passive mode and route opt-out added.
Priya Nair: Need dashboard panel for token-cost percentile. Added 50/90/99 token cost sparkline in dashboard JSON.
Add per-request phase attribution metrics, interleaved span annotator for trace stitching, and a configurable cascade alert suppression mechanism. New dashboard 'Request Phase Waterfall' and feature flags for phased rollout.
payload.title: Introduce request-phase attribution, interleaved span annotator, and cascade alert suppression

Title: introduce region-anchored role hierarchy and audit immutability shim with KMS rate limiter

Motivation: Some enterprise customers require region-scoped administrative boundaries plus guarantees that audit records cannot be retroactively modified. We also observed tenant-level KMS request spikes impacting downstream HSM quotas during long-running ops; a lightweight quota enforcer prevents noisy tenants from impacting others. This PR implements three coordinated pieces: (1) an opt-in region-anchored RBAC role hierarchy that decorates role decisions with a region claim and enforces deny-if-region-mismatch semantics; (2) an audit immutability shim that writes signed audit envelopes to a write-once backing store (S3+object-lock or on-prem WORM equivalent) and emits proof digests to the audit ledger; (3) a tenant-scoped KMS usage rate limiter that exposes quota metrics and soft-fails with structured retryable errors to callers.

Summary of changes: - authz/region_hierarchy.go: new package implementing RegionBoundRoleEvaluator and a small policy-layer adapter that short-circuits decisions when region claims mismatch. The implementation is opt-in via config.security.region_role_hierarchy.enabled. - audit/immutability/shim.go: adds AuditImmutabilityShim that wraps existing audit forwarders, signs envelopes using the configured audit-signing key (KMS-backed), and writes to a durable WORM store. Includes retry/backoff and local buffering for transient outages. - kms/quota/quota_enforcer.go: tenant-scoped leaky-bucket enforcement with per-tenant burst allowance and a global safety cap; metrics exposed via prometheus: rbac.kms_quota.allowed, rbac.kms_quota.denied, rbac.kms_quota.remaining. - config/schema.yaml: flags for enabling the features and default quota values. - console: added read-only indicator and a tenant quota panel under Operations -> Security. - tests: unit + integration tests for the evaluator, shim (using a fakeWORMStore), and quota enforcer. - docs/security/region-rbac.md: operational notes and migration plan.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc: ENG-4928 (linked) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration test for shim write + verification - [x] E2E smoke test for quota path - [x] Console panel added - [x] Feature gated behind config flags - [x] Migration notes in docs

Commits summary: - 7a8c4d8: Add region-bound role evaluator and adapter (authz/region_hierarchy.go) - initial impl and unit tests - b2d49f1: Add audit immutability shim with signing and WORM write path (audit/immutability/shim.go) - c9e1f33: Tenant KMS quota enforcer and metrics + console widgets (kms/quota/*, console/ops)

Files changed (high-level): - authz/region_hierarchy.go (+120 lines) - new evaluator and docs comments - audit/immutability/shim.go (+230 lines) - core shim + envelope signing helper - kms/quota/quota_enforcer.go (+85 lines) - leaky bucket implementation - config/schema.yaml (+14 lines) - feature flags and defaults - console/ops/tenant_kms_quota_panel.tsx (+54 lines) - small read-only panel - docs/security/region-rbac.md (+400 lines) - migration and operator guidance - tests/authz/region_hierarchy_test.go (+80 lines) - tests/audit/immutability_integration_test.go (+180 lines)

Small illustrative snippet (authz adapter):
- if request.Region != role.AllowedRegion {
-     return DecisionDeny("region-mismatch")
- }

Runtime notes: - Feature is off by default. When enabled, the evaluator will add a deny decision if the request's region claim doesn't match the role's region binding; existing policies are otherwise honored. - Audit shim signs envelopes with the audit signing key; operators must configure the KMS key resource with usage permission for the service account. - KMS quota uses a combination of token refill and burst tokens; operator can tune via config.

Testing / CI: initial CI run showed a flaky integration test in audit shim (due to time skew in fakeWORMStore). Fixed by adding deterministic timestamping in test harness. Final CI summary: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration-tests: pass (one rerun), lint: pass, e2e-smoke: pass.

Review conversation (high level, chronological):
- Aisha Rahman (review): Please clarify how region claims are obtained for non-interactive service principal calls. Suggest adding fallback to instance-region on private deployments.
- Priya Menon (author): Reply: added fallback to instance-region via metadata service and documented behavior in docs/security/region-rbac.md.
- Daniel Ortiz (review): KMS quota should return a structured code so SDKs can expose retry-exponential backoff. Also please ensure metric labels include tenant_id and region.
- Priya Menon: Reply: changed error to KMS_QUOTA_EXCEEDED (http 429 with Retry-After), added tenant_id and region labels to metrics.
- Liang Zhou (review): Audit shim looks good; can you include an admin command to re-ingest proofs if the ledger becomes inconsistent?
- Priya Menon: Reply: added admin CLI reingest command (cli admin audit reingest --from <ts>) guarded by an RBAC role audit.reingest.
- Aisha Rahman: Approval after verifying tests and docs.

CI details: - GitHub Actions: build-and-test (matrix linux/go1.21, linux/go1.22), lint-step, integration (aws-mock), e2e-smoke - First run: integration flaky (audit shim test) -> reran single job -> passed - Final: all checks green

Backward compatibility and migration: - No breaking API changes. - Operators must explicitly enable security.region_role_hierarchy.enabled to opt into region anchoring. - Audit immutability requires configuring an object-lock enabled store or equivalent; when enabled, audit storage mode changes to append-only (operator action required and documented). - KMS quota defaults are conservative; can be raised via config.

Operational concerns and follow-ups: - Flag to temporarily disable quota enforcement via runtime admin (added). - Add alerting for rbac.kms_quota.denied > threshold (follow-up ENG-5012). - Consider making audit proofs exportable to external compliance systems (follow-up).

Merge outcome: squashed into a single commit and merged to main on 2026-02-25. Backport: none included in this PR; will prepare a small backport to the 2026.02 release branch in a follow-up.

Contact author: Priya Menon <priya@redwood.ai>.
Adds region-anchored role hierarchy (opt-in flag), immutable audit shim that seals audit records to a write-once store, and a tenant-scoped KMS usage rate limiter with metrics exposed under rbac.kms_quota.*. No public API changes; config flag behind 'security.region_role_hierarchy' and 'audit.immutability.enabled'.

payload.body:
Motivation: We have intermittent client-visible failures for streamed tool/function invocations when upstream rate-limit signals are ambiguous (mix of Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Reset-Ms, and vendor-specific headers) and when multiple tool streams are multiplexed over the same connection. This causes incorrect retry timing, duplicate tool execution, and opaque error surfaces in the OpenAI-compat adapter. This PR introduces an explicit "backoff envelope" parity layer and a clearer idempotency session surface for streamed tool calls, providing deterministic retry behavior and structured error codes that SDKs can rely on.

What this change does (summary):
- Adds a BackoffEnvelope: standardized parsing and canonicalization of rate/ retry signals from upstream responses (supports Retry-After, Retry-After-Ms, X-RateLimit-Reset-Ms, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Quota, and vendor backoff headers). The envelope yields: canonical_retry_after_ms, rate_window_ms, and priority_hint.
- Introduces Idempotency Session tokens for multiplexed streaming tool invocations. When a streaming request declares tool/function calls, the adapter issues/accepts an idempotency_session_id that scopes retries to the logical stream session (prevents duplicate tool side-effects across reconnects).
- Stream framing guards: stronger delimiters and sequence checks for partial-frame error payloads so SDKs can detect partial tool responses and trigger safe replays only when the session idempotency state permits it.
- Structured error codes: map common runtime cases into an explicit error_code field (examples: "rate_limited", "retryable_transient", "permanent", "partial_result"), plus backoff_hint_ms where applicable. This is surfaced in the OpenAI-compat adapter response envelope and in the runtime internal error model.
- SDK + doc updates: small changes in the Python/TS SDKs to consume idempotency_session_id, follow backoff_hint_ms, and expose structured errors to callers. Docs page added with migration guidance and examples.

Compatibility and policy:
- Backward compatible: adapter continues to accept existing headers; when no canonical signal is present we fall back to conservative defaults. New idempotency_session_id is optional for clients; if the client does not supply it, the adapter will assign one but will not change behaviour for single-shot non-streamed calls.
- Safety: idempotency_session_id semantics are conservative by default: only retries that the adapter can prove to be safe (no committed tool side-effects) will re-execute; otherwise the adapter returns a structured error with "partial_result" and a backoff_hint_ms.

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests for header parsing and canonicalization (header permutations, bad values, clock skew compensation).
- E2E streaming tests that simulate network reconnects, mixed 429/503 patterns, and vendor headers.
- Integration tests with the python SDK to verify session idempotency behaviour and correct error-code propagation.
- A small perf benchmark ensures no material change to steady-state latency for non-retry flows (observed ~0.2% median overhead in decode path under test).

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flagged behind runtime flag: runtime.openai_compat.backoff_envelope (default off for 48 hours in staging).
- Canary rollout to 10% of hosted traffic for 72 hours with alerts for: unexpected duplicate tool invocations, increased 5xx rate, and higher latency tail for streamed requests.
- If stable, flip default on and follow with SDK + docs announcement.

Files changed (high level):
- server/adapter/openai_compat/headers.go: new canonicalizer for backoff headers and utils for clock skew safe parsing.
- server/adapter/openai_compat/stream_decoder.go: framing guards and session rehydration hooks.
- server/adapter/openai_compat/idempotency.go: idempotency session lifecycle and safe-replay predicates.
- sdk/python/openai_compat_client.py: client opt-in for idempotency_session_id and helpers to honor backoff_hint_ms.
- docs/openai-compat/backoff-idempotency.md: migration guide and examples.
- test/e2e/streaming_tool_idempotency_test.go: new end-to-end test harness scenarios.

Checklist:
- [x] Header parsing robust against malformed inputs and clock skew
- [x] Idempotency session respects tool side-effect safety rules
- [x] SDKs consume new fields and expose structured errors
- [x] CI/E2E passing (flaky streaming tests stabilized)
- [x] Migration docs and rollout plan attached

Notes: This PR focuses on correctness and deterministic behavior for retries in multiplexed streamed workloads. Subsequent PRs will add telemetry counters to track idempotency session reuse and per-tool replay counts to refine automatic replay heuristics.
Diego Martinez: Can you clarify how we handle clock skew between upstream server and runtime? Response: headers.go applies a conservative floor of 250ms plus skew window (configurable); parsing normalizes to ms and rejects negative values.
Sara Chowdhury: Suggest making idempotency_session_id TTL configurable per-tenant; Response: added tenant-configurable TTL (defaults 10m) and documented in runtime config.
Evan Holt: Are there any perf implications for high QPS multiplexed streams? Response: bench shows ~0.2% decode overhead; added micro-optimizations to reuse buffer slices in decoder.
QA: Observed a flaky e2e case where partial frames returned without error_code; Response: updated framing guards to synthesize 'partial_result' with backoff_hint_ms when the stream ends unexpectedly.
Added a canonical backoff envelope and idempotency session tokens for streamed tool/function calls. SDKs can opt in to idempotency_session_id and should honor backoff_hint_ms and structured error_code fields. Rollout behind feature flag and canaried before full release.
payload.title: Explicit backoff envelope and idempotency surface for multiplexed tool streams

payload.body:
Motivation: Customers are adopting the new OpenAI Responses v20 variants which include connection-level semantics and explicit rng_seed/rng_mode fields that influence determinism. The existing OpenAI compatibility bridge did not fully preserve these semantics across the bridge -> runtime boundary and occasionally dropped or reordered streaming fragments for tool calls, causing partial tool payloads and downstream JSON schema breakage. This PR introduces a focused compatibility patch to: 1) surface a connection handshake to establish a stable conn-id and expected framing for long-lived streams, 2) implement a fragment reassembly layer that handles out-of-order and duplicated chunks for tool/function-call payloads, and 3) forward rng_seed and rng_mode through the bridge into the runtime RNG subsystem so customer-specified determinism is honored end-to-end. Summary of changes (high level): - responses_v20_adapter.go: add ConnectHandshake(conn-id) path and conn-level state tracking. Handshake negotiates expected chunk framing style (chunked/frag/line) and advertises supported fallback models if the selected model doesn't support the requested rng_mode. - stream/reassembler.go: new reassembler that maintains idempotent fragment sets per message id, applies checksum validation when provided, and exposes a compact API for callers to request "assembled message" with a timeout/partial fallback. This prevents truncated tool-call JSON objects from reaching the structured output decoder. - rng/seed_forwarder.go: small interface that carries rng_seed and rng_mode from the bridge to the runtime RNG provider. When rng_seed is present we pin the runtime PRNG seed prior to token sampling to make responses reproducible for the same prompt+seed+model. - headers/propagation.go: ensure x-redwood-conn-id and x-openai-rng-seed headers are mapped to internal context keys and carried on internal requests to dedicated/private deployments. - metadata_passthrough.json fixture and e2e test: assert that an arbitrary user_metadata blob (opaque JSON) submitted with the request is preserved in the final response envelope and also logged in tracing spans for auditability. - tests: add e2e for streaming stability under simulated packet reordering and unit tests for rng seed propagation. Performance note: reassembly has a small CPU cost for bookkeeping (per-fragment map) but avoids costly downstream retries and JSON reparsing. The code includes a bounded fragment map with TTL to limit memory under noisy clients. Backwards compatibility and safety: when rng_seed is not provided we follow existing behavior (runtime-managed nondeterministic sampling). The handshake is optional — older clients will fall back to line-chunking with the same compatibility shim as before. Edge cases & decisions: - We do not attempt to replay missing fragments from clients; instead we expose a partial-message fallback that can be configured to either error (default) or return the best-effort assembled chunk. - Checksums are optional; when present we validate and drop corrupted fragments (metrics emitted). Tests and CI: initial CI run showed a flaky e2e failure in resp_v20_streaming_test (simulated network jitter) — root cause was a 50ms ephemeral race in test harness timeouts; I increased the test harness timeout and added a jitter-tolerant assertion. Final CI: all unit and integration checks passed. Review notes: please focus review on the reassembler's concurrency model (mutexing + per-message queues) and the seed forwarding safety boundary (ensure seed isn't logged or exposed to telemetry). Backwards-incompatible risk: very low — new headers are additive and handshake is opt-in. Linear tasks: ENG-1412 implement bridge handshake; ENG-1428 add deterministic seed propagation. Related support ticket: SUP-9821 (customer reported partial toolcall payloads when using v20). Motivation: During an intermittent incident on 2026-02-12 we observed rapid oscillation between normal and soft-deny states in regional egress when transient backend latency spikes coincided with bursty tenant traffic. That interaction exposed two issues: (1) the token-based rate limiter emits sharp step changes that produce aggressive load-shedding decisions, and (2) the regional health probe lacked hysteresis causing frequent region failover toggles. This PR introduces three coordinated mitigations: a lightweight smoothing layer for rate limits (EMWA-based), an 'egress soft-deny probe' that allows a short probationary holding pattern before full soft-deny enforcement, and a telemetry guard that prevents automated failovers when we detect probe/metric oscillation patterns. Summary of changes: - runtime/shedder/smoother.go: new smoothing wrapper around the existing leaky-bucket limiter using an exponential moving weighted average (configurable alpha) to soften ramp-up/ramp-down. - runtime/egress/soft_deny_probe.go: probationary probe that tracks transient rejection rates and only flips soft-deny on sustained windows; supports configurable window and grace counters. - telemetry/region_guard.go: guard that computes oscillation score from region-probe and egress metrics and inhibits automated regional failover if score exceeds threshold; emits guard telemetry for SRE dashboards. - k8s/patches/egress-configmap.yaml: runtime defaults and feature flag toggles to stage rollout. - tests/integration/egress_smoothing_test.go: new integration and deterministic fuzz tests that simulate bursty tenants + backend hitches. - docs/ops/egress-smoothing.md: runbook, rollout, and rollback steps. Backwards compatibility: all features are behind feature flags and conservative defaults (alpha=0.25, probation window=30s, oscillation threshold high). Rollout plan: canary 25% (us-west-2) for 2 hours, then region-by-region rollout with a 2-hour observation window and a quick rollback playbook. Hotfix rationale: this was prioritized as an incident-driven hotfix (SUP-4523) because oscillation previously caused two small regional failovers within a 45m window. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for smoothing math and boundary conditions - [x] Integration test that reproduces previously-observed oscillation in CI fuzz harness - [x] Updated runbook and alert thresholds - [x] Telemetry events wired and dashboard updated - [x] Feature flag gating for progressive rollout Deploy notes: flip feature flag to canary, observe metrics: region.failover.count, egress.soft_deny.rate, shedder.smoothing.alpha; if regional oscillation returns, revert flag and tag incident for deeper root cause. Related: ENG-7891 (rate-limiter stability), SRE-141 (egress incident postmortem).
Daniel Kim: Could the smoothing delay increase latency for tiny requests? Please add microbenchmarks.
Asha Patel: Added microbenchmarks in runtime/shedder/smoother_test.go; observed <0.4ms median overhead at 2000 RPS.
Roxanne Liu: The oscillation guard threshold seems arbitrary. Can we emit a metric and tune from production?
Asha Patel: Guard emits region_guard.score and region_guard.blocked_count; default is high to avoid false positives. We'll tune after canary per SRE-141.
Mateo Alvarez: Integration test flaked once in CI; I re-ran the job and it passed. LGTM after tests green.

Reproduced prior oscillation locally with injected backend latency. Canary in us-west-2 showed no repeat of double-failover in 2 hours. Integration harness simulates 8 tenant classes and passed deterministic fuzzing.
Incident hotfix: soften rate-limiter transitions and add probationary egress probe to reduce regional failover oscillations. Feature behind flag; staged rollout. Follow-up tuning planned.

Summary: Introduces an SLO-driven node drain smoothing controller and cross-zone hedging policy to avoid latency spikes and bulk eviction storms when GPU nodes degrade or enter maintenance. This change reduces p99 latency regressions observed during abrupt node drains by allowing gradual eviction + short-term hedging to nearby healthy zones, with automatic fallbacks to smaller quantized model variants when capacity is constrained. Motivation: Recent incidents (SUP-4421) revealed that immediate eviction of pods on degraded GPU hosts caused transient head-of-line latency increases and cache warm-up penalties across many tenants. Our existing circuit-breaker/eviction logic is binary: evict now or not. This PR implements a middle path that honors SLO envelopes and keeps high-priority requests within budget while draining safely. Design highlights: 1) slo-drain-controller (new component in scheduler): observes node health, request SLO burn-rate (from metrics-exporter), and issues phased eviction directives: MARK_DRAIN_PRE (reduce new routing to node), PHASED_EVICT (evict low-priority pods first), FINAL_EVICT. 2) Cross-zone hedging policy: when draining a node in zone A, the router can optionally route a small percentage of new requests to compatible replicas in zone B/C for a bounded duration (configurable via runtime flag hedging.window_ms and hedging.weight_pct). Hedging stops automatically when the drain phase completes. 3) Temporary model fallback: when aggregate headroom across zones is insufficient, the controller can trigger a short-lived rollout to a compatible, smaller quantized model variant (e.g. 8-bit quantized) for affected routes to preserve latency SLOs. This uses the existing rollout infra with an emergency flag (emergencyModelFallback=true) scoped to customer/route. 4) KV-cache flush & rebind fix: addresses an observed race where pod eviction + near-instant recreate could cause stale KV cache references. The fix ensures an explicit KV cache checkpoint and a brief grace TTL before rebind. 5) Observability: adds metrics slo_drain_phase{phase="pre|phased|final"}, hedged_routes_count, hedging_traffic_pct, fallback_model_active, and a dashboard with p50/p90/p99 and error budget burn. Rollout plan: - Stage 1 (canary, 1% of clusters): enable slo-drain-controller in canary region with hedging.disabled=false but fallback disabled. Monitor error-budget and latency. - Stage 2 (10%): enable cross-zone hedging with hedging.weight_pct=5 and enable fallback for non-SLA tenants. - Stage 3 (global): ramp weight_pct up to 15 for high-priority routes; enable per-tenant tuning. Feature flags and operator docs included. Tests and validation: - Unit tests for controller decision logic and eviction ordering. - Integration tests (simulated node degradation) verifying gradual eviction ordering and hedging routing. - Chaos e2e run: simulated GPU host flapping showed p99 reduced by ~38% vs immediate-eviction baseline in internal perf runs. - KV-cache rebind unit + e2e validated under recreate race. Rollback: feature gates allow immediate disable (hedging.disabled=true, controller off) and automatic rollback of any emergencyModelFallback via rollout engine. If regression detected, operator doc includes steps to revert and to run a forced cache clear across affected nodes. Related changes: small API addition to routing layer (RouteHints.hedgeCandidates and hedgeWeight) and a new admin endpoint /admin/v1/drain_status for on-demand inspection. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed by SRE and Runtime teams - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Canary deployment in internal staging - [x] Observability dashboard and alert: EvictionRateSpike, HedgingErrorRatio - [x] Rollout playbook entry added Notes: This is intentionally conservative on hedging weight and fallback usage for the first public rollout. The goal is to prevent outage amplification during node-level degradations while limiting cross-zone traffic to a predictable budget.

Maya L. Chen (2026-02-23): Added a geo-constraint check in router; updated tests. See commit 9b8d7e5.
Sofia Martinez (2026-02-24): Please call out the operational cost estimate for hedging (eg egress between zones). Added suggestion to limit hedging to high-priority API keys.
Maya L. Chen (2026-02-24): Honor per-tenant hedging opt-in via tenant config; docs updated.
Evan Zhou (2026-02-25): perf bench looks good. One question: fallback rollout uses the same rollout controller - ensure it doesn't trigger canary alerts. Added approval pending small test addition.
Maya L. Chen (2026-02-26): Added test to ensure fallback rollouts are labeled emergency and do not count towards normal canary metrics. Ready for merge.

Introduce kernel-lane-aware bucketing scheduler to reduce padding overhead.
Add pad-savings estimator to prefer co-located requests that unlock kernel lane utilization.
No API changes; rollout flag gated behind runtime.feature.kernel_lane_bucketing.
Summary: This PR adds a kernel-lane-aware bucketing scheduler and a pad-savings estimator to the continuous batching pipeline. The goal is to reduce wasted padding across mixed sequence length workloads by preferring batch compositions that simultaneously align to kernel lane widths (vector lane / warp-like constraints) and maximize reuse of KV/prefix cache entries.

Motivation: On modern GPU runtimes we observed microsecond-level inefficiencies that multiply into meaningful token-costs for high QPS services. Two root causes: (1) padding to the longest sequence in a slot leads to wasted compute and memory traffic, and (2) kernels provide best throughput when sequence dimensions align to internal lane widths (e.g., multiples of 8/16 tokens for certain fused-attention kernels).

Design:
- Add a lightweight pad-savings estimator that computes a per-request expected padding penalty for candidate slot compositions. The estimator uses the request seqlen, recent seqlen distribution histograms, and model kernel lane parameters queried from kernel caps metadata.
- Implement a kernel-lane-aware bucketing step before the existing bucket scheduler. Buckets are annotated with preferred lane alignment (e.g., lane_mod = 8). When composing batches, the scheduler prefers combinations that achieve zero or minimal lane_mod remainder while also minimizing total padding.
- Integrate kernel-lane bucketing with the continuous batching window: the scheduler runs as a scoring pass over current cohort, scoring candidates by combined pad-savings + lane-alignment bonus + cache-reuse penalty. A tunable weighting parameter controls tradeoffs.
- KV cache / prefix interaction: to avoid extra cache churn we add a small affinity bonus when requests share identical or strongly overlapping prefix keys (same conversation id or cached embedding id). The scheduler will prefer coalescing these when it does not dramatically increase padding.

Implementation notes:
- New files: runtime/scheduler/kernel_lane_bucketer.rs, runtime/scheduler/pad_savings_estimator.rs, runtime/scheduler/integration.rs (glue), tests/bench/kernel_lane_bucketer_integ.test, docs/perf/notes/kernel-lane-bucketing.md
- The estimator is pure-C, no locks; it reads model kernel metadata from the existing runtime model manifest cache (no schema change).
- Added feature flag runtime.feature.kernel_lane_bucketing (off by default for gradual rollout).
- Configs: default lane weight = 0.75, cache affinity bonus = 0.5, pad weight = 1.0.

Benchmarks:
- Mixed seqlen synthetic workload (poisson arrival, seqlen mix 8/32/128): median latency at steady QPS improved by 6.8%, p99 down 9.2% for single-GPU runs.
- Token compute cost (measured as effective GPU token-seconds) reduced by 12–18% depending on cluster packing.
- Small uniform short-seq workloads unchanged (regression <= 1%).
- Kernel alignment wins were most pronounced on fused-attention kernels that favor 16-token multiples.

CI and validation:
- Unit tests for estimator math and bucketing decisions
- Integration bench harness added and run on perf-canary
- End-to-end e2e test with KV cache overlap scenarios
- CI checks: build, unit, integration, perf-smoke (all passing after two reruns)

Commits summary:
- "introduce pad-savings estimator and kernel lane bucketer" (core logic)
- "add integration glue to continuous batch composer" (integrate with existing window)
- "tests: unit + integration + perf-smoke harness"
- "docs: perf notes and rollout guide"

Changed areas (high level):
- runtime/scheduler/* (new files and small modifications to composer)
- runtime/model/manifest.rs (read-only metadata read path added)
- runtime/config/defaults.toml (feature flag + weights)
- docs/perf/*
- tests/bench/*
- CI workflow: .github/workflows/perf-canary.yml (hooked up to new bench)

Review conversation:
- Ava Chen: "Can you quantify cost of estimator itself? we don't want scheduler CPU to become bottleneck." Author response (Jordan Lin): "Estimator is O(n_candidates) with very cheap ops; in perf runs the added CPU was <2% of scheduler budget. Added microbench numbers to docs."
- Diego Morales: "How does this interact with existing slot-duration packing heuristics?" Author: "We run lane-aware bucketing as a pre-pass scoring step; slot-duration and burst packing remain unchanged. Added comments and a small refactor to keep separation."
- Priya Nambiar: "Feature flagging and rollout criteria? Need safe defaults for dedicated clusters." Author: "Flag off by default. Added a staged rollout doc with metrics to watch: pad_ratio, token_seconds_per_second, p99 latency. Added a kill-switch via runtime admin endpoint."
- Diego Morales (post-approve): "Approve after CI green and add docs about the model manifest field required." Author: "Acknowledged; manifest metadata addition is backward compatible and documented."

CI checks: - build: pass - unit: pass - integration: pass - perf-smoke: pass (two reruns after flakiness on perf harness)

Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2026-03-07.

Rollout notes:
- Start with 5% of requests on hosted clusters with low variance seqlen and monitor pad_ratio and token_seconds.
- Enable cache-affinity only after confirming low churn.
- If regressions appear, reduce lane weight or disable feature flag.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: estimator misweights short bursts, causing slight latency regressions for purely short-seq traffic. Mitigation: default weights tuned conservatively; feature flag.
- Risk: model manifest missing kernel lane metadata on older models. Mitigation: fallback to conservative lane_mod=8 default and emit a one-time warning metric.

Follow-ups (future PRs):
- Auto-tune lane weight using rolling pad_ratio signal
- Add GPU-side hints to kernels to accept soft-padding for fractional lanes
- Extend estimator to consider memory bandwidth impact for long-context models

payload.body:
Motivation: We observed persistent padding overhead on workloads with high variance in sequence length (chat + multimodal tokenizers). Existing bucketing strategies reduce padding but leave room for improvement where short-lived short sequences cluster with long sequences in shared slots, causing excess GPU work and KV cache churn. This PR introduces two coordinated heuristics: (1) a Variable Pad Trimmer that opportunistically trims trailing padding at slot boundaries by adjusting KV offsets and kernel work sizes, and (2) a Sequence Cohort Allocator that groups inflight requests into transient cohorts based on a lightweight sequence-length sketch and estimated token-density, prioritizing cohorts for coalesced kernel launches.

Summary of changes: added a new coordinator in the serving runtime (runtime/slot_cohort_allocator.cc/py bindings) that maintains per-slot cohort candidates and drives short-window cohort formation; implemented pad-trimmer code paths in the kernel dispatcher to emit smaller work ranges when trailing pad-only columns are detected; extended the scheduling policy to expose a cohort_hint that can be consumed by the GPU scheduler and packing layer; KV cache metadata now carries a trimmed-offset to allow coherent reuse of cache ranges without copying large tensors. The changes are conservative by default (feature-flagged) and fall back to existing bucketing when heuristics are disabled or not beneficial.

Benchmarks & results: end-to-end benchmarks on prod-like traces (conversation mix, token-density variance 0.18–0.47) show a median token-cost reduction of 9% and p95 latency improvement of 6% for the Canary cluster; synthetic extreme-variance workloads saw up to 14% throughput uplift. Microbenchmarks indicate the pad-trimmer adds ~0.3ms scheduler overhead per batch in worst-case but reduces per-token GPU FLOPs meaningfully for padded slots. Regression tests added to perf-canary and benchmark-lab reproducer scripts.

Compatibility & safety: The code is guarded behind runtime feature flags: cohort_allocator.enabled and pad_trimmer.enabled. KV cache trimming updates maintain backward-compatible metadata layout; we added a compatibility shim in KV cache loaders for older persisted traces. No API changes to the public Redwood API. We included a stress test simulating rapid sequence-length churn to validate correctness and KV coherence.

Why this is different from existing bucketers: Rather than statically bucketing by seqlen or using fixed padding policies, the cohort allocator is a transient, fast-path grouping mechanism that considers short temporal locality (requests arriving within the same slot window) and token-density. The pad-trimmer complements the allocator by reducing wasted compute when cohorts include a mix of short and long sequences that were historically padded to the longest in-slot request.
Marco Chen: Nice work. Concern: how do we reason about KV cache fragmentation over long-lived sessions? Can we add bucket-level compaction if fragmentation crosses threshold?
Aisha Patel (author): Fragmentation tracked in serving.pad_trimmer.fragmentation_ratio; added a compaction callback in the compat shim that schedules eviction for low-benefit ranges. Will follow up with an automated compaction PR if we see threshold crossings in canary.
Lena Garcia: Can we get numbers on p50/p95 for short-chat workloads? Also please add a flag to disable pad trimming per-queue for experiments.
Aisha Patel (author): p50/p95 added to description; added per-queue disable in config. Updated tests to cover queue-specific disable.
Tomás Ruiz: tests look good. Please confirm no behavioral change for private deployment (VPC) path.
Aisha Patel (author): Verified locally against private-installer dev image; no API or on-disk layout changes for private deployments beyond the shim. Noted in docs.
Merged by Marco Chen (squash merge). Changelog: added section 'cohort allocator & pad trimmer' under runtime performance improvements. Canary rollout started Feb 18.
Introducing an optional runtime optimization: Variable Pad Trimmer and Sequence Cohort Allocator. Reduces padding overhead in mixed-length workloads; expected token-cost savings 5–14% depending on variance. Feature flags: cohort_allocator.enabled, pad_trimmer.enabled. Monitor serving.pad_trimmer.* metrics during rollout.
Related linear tickets: ENG-4021 (cohort allocator proposal), ENG-4199 (pad trimming design). This PR intentionally keeps behavior behind flags to enable gradual rollout and A/B. Follow-up work: automatic compaction, adaptive cohort sizing, and kernel-level fused trim-and-dispatch path.

Context: Tenants exhibit wide variance in request size, burstiness, and acceptable latency/cost tradeoffs. Current global presets are either too conservative (high cost) or too aggressive (quality regressions for some tenants). This PR implements a tenant profile matcher that chooses a cost-aware defaults bundle (batching, prefill/caching hints, quantization profile preference) based on per-tenant telemetry signals, and a deterministic fallback chain for quant profiles to ensure graceful quality-first degradation. Motivation: reduce unit cost for conservative tenants while preserving output quality and providing predictable rollback behavior when telemetry indicates regressions.

What this PR changes: 1) pkg/econ/matcher.go: new matching engine that ingests a compact feature vector (median request tokens, 95th pct tail, burstiness, recent error-rate delta, embedding vs generation mix) and maps it to a named preset (e.g., "compact-latency-safe", "balanced-cost", "quality-first"). 2) configs/presets/tenant-presets.yaml: curated presets with explicit quantization fallback chains and batch/cache knobs. 3) telemetry/prefill_signals_ingest.py: lightweight transformer to compute tenant feature vectors and write to signal-store. 4) cmd/rwctl/profile-preview.go: CLI to preview which preset would be chosen for a tenant and to simulate fallback decisions given an observed degradation. 5) docs/tenant-profiles.md: doc + decision table and recommended rollout plan. 6) tests: unit + simulated workload integration test that replays sampled traces to verify fallback ordering and no silent regressions. 7) a feature flag (feature.tenant_profile_matcher) and migration notes to enable gradual rollout.

Checklist: - [x] Matcher algorithm + serialization format defined in code and docs - [x] Default presets added and reviewed by econ/ops - [x] Feature flag gating and rollout plan in docs - [x] Unit + integration tests, and a small bench comparing 95p latency and token-cost delta - [x] rwctl preview command and examples in docs - [x] Telemetry enrichment - [x] CI green (unit/integration/bench)

Linear/Jira: ENG-1421 covers the matcher implementation and tests; ENG-1422 covers presets and rollout. Support ticket SUP-9034 requested safer quant fallbacks for a high-cost tenant.

Notes on safety: The matcher returns a preset name only. All runtime controllers continue to validate that the selected quant profile is allowed per-tenant policy; if disallowed, the runtime will choose the next allowed profile from the fallback chain. The fallback chain prioritizes quality-preserving paths (e.g., int8->q4_0->q4_k_m) rather than immediate low-bit aggressive jumps.

Migration/rollout: Start with a small percentage (5%) of tenants behind feature flag plus rwctl dry-run preview reports. If telemetry shows >1% generation quality delta for any tenant, the runtime triggers an automatic opt-out and an alert to SRE.

Links: - RFC: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1421/tenant-profile-matcher - Design doc: docs/tenant-profiles.md
Maya Chen: Overall this looks good. Two items: please add a feature flag check in the matcher path (so we can toggle per-cluster), and confirm that fallback chain respects tenant deny-lists. Also can you add a small benchmark to ensure matcher latency is <1ms in the hot path?
Asha Patel (author): Added a feature flag gate and moved heavy serialization to an async precompute path. Benchmarks added under Makefile target 'bench-matcher' — median 0.6ms on dev machines. Registry consults tenant policies before finalizing selection.
Luca Romano: Suggest making the fallback chain prioritize 'no-quant-change' first (i.e., prefer batch/cache changes before quant if possible) — otherwise risk of unnecessary quant switching.
Asha Patel: Adjusted mapping to include 'prefers_cache_then_batch' ordering and updated docs with decision table. Added unit test that asserts fallback ordering in 4 scenarios.
Priya Singh: Accepted. Verified integration sim for three tenant traces; no regressions. Approving pending green CI.
CI Bot: All checks passed. Integration sim completed with <0.5% token-cost reduction and no regression in quality metrics in the simulated tenants.

Context: Production serving has increasing variance from mixed sequence-length workloads and multi-tenant continuous batching which creates suboptimal KV alignment and kernel selection. Motivation: reduce p99 latency and per-token cost without requiring model changes or new maintenance burden for ops. This PR introduces two orthogonal features: (1) a dynamic-shard attention microkernel (late-bound kernel selector and small-footprint microkernel implementations for skinny/short/long shards) and (2) rotary-offset stitching which fixes misaligned rotary/rope offsets when KV cache slices are split across continuous-batching boundaries. Summary of changes: added a late-bound kernel selector that picks optimized microkernels (small-tile, wide-tile, and wavefront microkernels) based on runtime shard shape; implemented a lightweight runtime registry for microkernels and a fast path for fused qkv->softmax->apply rotary for the small-tile microkernel; added a rotary-offset stitcher during KV assemble that recomputes per-shard rotary offsets and applies an O(1) remap for slices that straddle batch boundaries to avoid artifacts; updated continuous-batcher to emit shard-aligned KV slice metadata and a hint to the scheduler for prefetch alignment; improved the allocator to reserve KV padding when needed to maintain cache-line friendly alignment. API/compatibility: no API changes to the public inference REST/SDK surface; changes are internal to runtime and opt-in behind the flag runtime.dynamic_shard_attn=true. Performance: internal perf runs on c5g-like infra and NVidia A100 cluster show p99 latency improvements of 8-14% depending on mix, average token throughput improvements of 6-11% for mixed short/long workloads, and up to 9% token-cost reduction when continuous-batching is enabled because fewer fallback kernels are invoked. Safety/fallback: when runtime.dynamic_shard_attn is disabled or a microkernel fails feature checks, runtime falls back to current flashbridge kernel to guarantee correctness. Testing: unit tests for microkernels and rotary stitching added; integration perf harness with synthetic variable-length streams; CI includes determinism checks comparing output with baseline within L2 numerical tolerances. Rollout plan: staged rollout with canary on Dedicated for 24 hours, monitor p99 and correctness traces, then 25% traffic ramp to all dedicated clusters, fail-open to baseline kernel on anomaly. Related work/items: builds on earlier kernel registry work (ENG-8220) and continuous-batching scheduler heuristics (ENG-9120). Checklist: ensure changelog entry (done), add observability hooks for selected kernel (done), perf dashboard updated (done), security review completed (done).
Introduce a dynamic-shard microkernel that late-binds kernel selection to observed sequence-length/shard distribution and a rotary-offset stitching layer that aligns KV slices across continuous-batching boundaries; ~12% p99 latency reduction on long-context workloads and ~9% token-cost saving in continuous-batching scenarios.
Liam Chen: Can you explain the invariant that rotary-offset stitcher maintains across split slices? I worry about off-by-one artifacts when slices are not aligned to token boundaries.
Maya Patel: The stitcher computes a per-slice base_offset from original sequence absolute position and applies a modular remap using the model's rotary period; we added unit tests that compare against a monolithic KV write to ensure no drift. See tests/kv/test_rotary_stitcher.py for specifics.
Aisha Rahman: Microkernel selection looks good but the selector's cost model is simplistic. Can we include a learned or profile-driven threshold later?
Maya Patel: Agreed. This PR uses a heuristics-driven threshold tuned from our perf lab. Follow-up ENG-9680 will add profile-driven thresholds and online adaptation.
Diego Morales: Does this change alter memory accounting for RVs or KV caches? Need to ensure autoscaler alarms still work.
Maya Patel: We reserve worst-case padding in allocator and emit accounting events; I added a test for peak_memory reporting and updated autoscaler docs in docs/ops/rollout_notes/dynamic_shard_attn.md.
Liam Chen: Verified correctness on the canary cluster and re-ran perf bench; p99 improved and outputs match baseline within fp16 tolerances. Approving.
Aisha Rahman: Approved after confirming the fallback path covered by feature-flag gating.

payload.body:
Motivation: We observed recurring KV-cache starvation in mixed workloads where long-running KV-heavy requests would hold hot pins while short, latency-sensitive requests queued behind them. Existing epoch-based soft timeouts prioritized strict fairness and often caused tail latency regressions when a few long requests dominated a slot. This PR introduces Asymmetric Epoched Wait Admission (AEWA), a scheduler admission policy tuned for continuous batching workloads that reduces starvation without sacrificing batching efficiency.

Summary: AEWA groups incoming requests into short 'admission epochs' per logical queue (latency-sensitive, balanced, kv-heavy). Each epoch tracks an asymmetric budget: latency-sensitive epochs are given small, frequent admission windows to keep p99 stable, while kv-heavy epochs receive larger, less frequent windows but are subject to an epoch overflow preemption check to avoid long-term pin monopolies. The admission decision uses: epoch age, per-epoch backlog, per-request kv_pin_hint, and recent kernel alignment score (from kernel_hints) to prefer admissions that improve batch kernel utilization.

Design details (single continuous paragraph to keep description as one string): The core data structure is epoch_counters with monotonic epoch IDs + sliding-window backlog counters. When a request arrives we compute its target epoch and evaluate a weighted admission score: score = w_age * normalized_epoch_age + w_backlog * normalized_epoch_backlog + w_pin * pin_penalty + w_kernel * kernel_alignment_bonus. We tuned weights conservatively after load tests (defaults in config.rs). The "asymmetric" component is that latency-sensitive epochs use a negative pin_penalty (low tolerance for holding pins) and small max_epoch_admit; kv-heavy epochs have a positive pin_penalty tolerance but an epoch_overflow_threshold that triggers an immediate soft-preempt path: when overflow is detected, we drain at most N tokens from that epoch into a preemption buffer and allow short requests to be admitted with a small reservation. Admission is always try-fast then fall back to queued_wait where the request attaches a kv_pin_hint; when the request reaches the head of its epoch, the scheduler will re-evaluate admission using a jittered soft-timeout to reduce synchronized expiries. AEWA also emits metrics for epoch wait distribution and preemption events to aid ops tuning.

Implementation highlights: added pkg/serving/scheduler/aewa_admission.rs implementing the scoring, epoch lifecycle, and soft-preempt drain. epoch_counters.rs contains the compact counters and eviction policy used when many logical queues exist. kernel_hints.rs exposes a small API for runtime to report recent kernel batch sizes; admission consults this to slightly bias towards admissions that improve kernel packing. kv/cache_pin_hint.rs adds a hedged-unpin hint so callers (and SDKs) can flag when a request can tolerate temporary unpin (used by internal rerank workflows). Tests: added unit + integration tests in pkg/serving/scheduler/tests/aewa_integ.rs and a deterministic scheduler fuzzer to validate no-loss starvation invariants. Docs: design notes in docs/notes/aewa-design.md and an example loadtest profile.

Performance: microbench loadtests against a mixed traffic profile (60% short chat-like requests, 30% medium generation, 10% kv-heavy retrievals) show: p99 latency for short requests reduced by ~12% (from 210ms -> 185ms) under sustained load, p50 unchanged, overall throughput unchanged, and KV-pin hold-time 99th percentile reduced by ~34%. Observability: new metrics ae_epoch_wait_ms, ae_epoch_overflow_count, ae_preempt_drains emitted to the metrics backend.

Compatibility & rollout: default weights are conservative; the feature gate redwood.scheduler.aewa_enabled is off by default. We plan a canary rollout to Dedicated clusters with progressive ramping and a quick rollback key in Console. No API changes. The kv cache hint interface is additive and backwards compatible.

Checklist: - [x] Scheduler admission algorithm implemented - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Basic benchmarks and load profiles - [x] Metrics and dashboards (skeleton) - [x] Docs and rollout plan

Related: ENG-11234 (kv-starvation postmortem), ENG-11567 (kernel packing study).
Maya Chen: Nice work. Can you clarify how the preempt drain avoids hurting batch kernel shapes? We should prefer drains that preserve power-of-two or preferred kernel batch sizes.
Author (Samir Patel): We added kernel_alignment_bonus which biases selection toward preserved kernel shapes; drains try to move whole requests if that preserves alignment, otherwise they use micro-drains (at most 3 requests) to avoid breaking long-running batches.
Leah Ortiz: Please add a configuration knob for aggressive preemption for Dedicated customers (we may want to enable in some low-cost skews).
Author (Samir Patel): Added redwood.scheduler.aewa_aggressive_preempt boolean and documented the expected cost/latency tradeoff in docs/notes/aewa-design.md.
Diego Martinez: CI failed on the first run due to a flaky scheduler test; can you add a retry and a deterministic seed?
Author (Samir Patel): Added deterministic seed + increased timeouts for the flakier test; CI rerun passed.
Introduce AEWA admission policy for continuous batcher: reduces KV-pin starvation and lowers tail latency for latency-sensitive requests. Feature gated and off by default.
Canary rollout recommended; observe ae_epoch_overflow_count and ae_preempt_drains. Tuning may be required for very bursty KV workloads.

Motivation: customers using Redwood's OpenAI compatibility endpoint reported inconsistent behavior when mixing stop sequences, function calls, and role aliases across streams. This PR implements three orthogonal components to bring deterministic parity with common v1 expectations while keeping native runtime optimizations available.

Summary: implement a stop-sequence arbitrator (stop_precedence), a role-mapper to coalesce common role aliases (role_aliases + strict_role_mode opt-in), and a framed-JSON tool-handoff event so function calls in streaming mode are unambiguous and resilient to chunk boundaries. Also: normalize numeric/boolean param coercion for v1 requests and add e2e tests for overlapping stop/functioncall edge cases.

Key behavioral changes (enabled when request includes v1_compat_mode=true):
- stop_precedence (new request param): controls deterministic arbitration when multiple stop conditions occur in-flight (values: "first-token", "boundary-first", "function-priority"). Default for compatibility is "boundary-first" which prefers completed token boundaries and preserves OpenAI-like heuristics.
- Role-mapper: request-level role_aliases map common client roles (e.g., "user", "human", "end-user") to canonical roles. When strict_role_mode is true we return warnings for ambiguous role assignments and fall back to the mapper instead of failing.
- Framed-JSON tool-handoff: a small JSON envelope emitted as a discrete stream event when the model proposes a function call. Envelope fields are: event:"tool_handoff", tool:string, args:{...}, outgoing_signature:string. This avoids mid-chunk JSON parsing errors and provides a clear point for the runtime to execute tool calls or route to function execution layers.
- Logprobs and streaming offsets: logprob normalization was adjusted so per-token contributions are stable even when the stream fragments tokens across frames; a post-stream rebase step reconciles offsets and preserves reported token indices for v1 clients.

Files changed (high level): service/api/openai_compat/v1_handler.py, service/stream/framer.go, runtime/stop_arbiters/stop_arbiter.rs, docs/openai_compat.md, tests/integration/test_stop_function_interop.py, sdk/typescript/examples/v1_parity_chat.md, ci/compat_e2e.yml, tools/compat/role_aliases.yaml

Commits: See commits list below for granular change descriptions (squash merged).

Testing and rollout: added 10 new integration tests and 6 unit tests covering boundary-first vs function-priority arbitration, role alias collisions, and streaming handoff framing. This change is behind the HTTP compatibility flag v1_compat_mode to allow staged rollout; default behavior for non-v1 requests is unchanged.

Backward compatibility and migration notes: servers will accept both the old streaming envelope and the new framed-JSON event; SDKs updated to prefer framed events when v1_compat_mode is set. Documentation updates are included.

Merge notes: squash merge to main after CI green and two approvals.

Review conversation (condensed): see review_comments for threaded excerpts.

Diego Martinez (review): The stop_arbitrator looks clean. Two items: ensure we never drop a functioncall event when a stop sequence spans the same tokens; add a unit test that simulates mid-token boundary fragmentation.
Asha (reply): Added the boundary-first strategy and the mid-token fragmentation e2e. The arbiter exposes a resolve_trace for telemetry so we can see which rule fired.
Riley Chen (review): Role-mapper is useful, but please document how SDKs should indicate role_aliases. Also we need a WARN-level log if strict_role_mode sees an ambiguous role.
Asha (reply): role_aliases.yaml added to tools/compat and SDK example updated. We emit a compat.warn metric when strict_role_mode fallback occurs.
Samira Khan (security review): framer.go looks good but confirm the framed JSON event size is bounded and validated to avoid amplification attacks.
Asha (reply): added a 64KB cap and JSON-schema validation for the tool_handoff envelope; validation failures close the stream with a 400 and compat error code.
Diego Martinez (approval): CI green, tests added. Approving for merge after squash.
Riley Chen (approval): Approve. Verified e2e in staging with v1_compat_mode=true.

This PR introduces a small declarative manifest for CI stage weights and adds a lightweight dependency sanitizer that trims unused dev-deps during presubmit image builds. Motivation: long presubmit startup times and noisy dependency churn make premerge feedback slow for large surface changes. The change has three objectives: 1) make CI stage selection explicit and data-driven via ci/stages.yaml so teams can assign relative weight and target runners; 2) produce thinner presubmit images by running a dep-sanitizer step that reconciles package manifests against a curated allowlist and a simple reachability check; 3) wire a release-sanitizer hook that annotates release artifacts with a dep-sanity stamp so QA and release automation can gate on dependency hygiene. The description below includes commits, files changed, review thread highlights, CI summary, and merge notes.
init: add declarative ci stages manifest and loader (ci/stages.yaml)
feat(dep-sanitizer): add lightweight sanitizer binary and CLI (tools/dep-sanitizer)
ci: presubmit images: run dep-sanitizer during slim build path (scripts/presubmit/*)
docs: add dep-sanitizer README and migration notes
Diego Marquez: Nit: prefer explicit stage priorities as integers instead of floats to avoid rounding inconsistencies in the scheduler. Also can you add a link to the staging runner pool?
Samira Khan: Updated stages.yaml to use integers and added runner_pool field; pushed a follow-up commit. See commit 'ci: use integer stage weights'
Priya Nair: Security concern: dep-sanitizer currently runs a simple reachability check that spawns npm/pip inspect commands inside a builder image. Can we sandbox and timeout the check?
Samira Khan: Added timeout (45s per package) and moved checks into an ephemeral container performed by the existing presubmit runner; added note in README about how to opt out for legacy projects.
Tom Bennett: CI: presubmit pipeline flaked once on integration tests after slimming images; looks like a test relying on a dev-tool binary removed by the sanitizer. Can we add an opt-in allowlist file per-package?
Samira Khan: Added tools/dep-sanitizer/allowlist.txt support and per-project .presubmit-allowlist path; added migration guidance in docs/ci-migration.md
- Introduce declarative ci/stages.yaml to control stage weights and runner targeting.
- Add tools/dep-sanitizer: a fast, opt-in sanitizer for presubmit image builds to remove unused dev dependencies and shrink image size.
- Presubmit images now have a slim build path that runs the sanitizer; projects can opt out with .presubmit-allowlist.
- Release artifacts are annotated with a dep-sanity stamp to help release gating and audits.
1) Add a minimal .presubmit-allowlist at repo root if your build uses non-declared dev tooling. 2) Read docs/ci-migration.md for examples. 3) Teams that rely on legacy monorepo devdeps can opt-out by setting CI_PRESUBMIT_SLIM=false in their pipeline config.
After merge, monitor presubmit-image-build times and the presubmit queue length for 48 hours. If any team reports missing dev tooling in CI, advise adding entries to .presubmit-allowlist or to tools/dep-sanitizer/allowlist.txt. Watch presubmit failures tagged with 'dep-sanitizer' and revert the commit if wide breakage occurs.
Medium: changes are isolated to presubmit and release hooks but touch presubmit images and a new binary. Mitigations: opt-out flag, allowlist, and staged rollout via a canary label on teams with large custom toolchains.
1) Run ./scripts/presubmit/build-slim.sh locally for a sample repo. 2) Verify unit and smoke tests pass in presubmit. 3) Validate that release-sanitizer writes a stamp to release metadata. 4) Exercise opt-out by setting CI_PRESUBMIT_SLIM=false and confirm behavior matches previous build path.
Sanitizer supports npm, pip, and go modules in its first iteration. Yarn, poetry and other package managers will be added incrementally. Per-repo allowlist can override default behavior.
Added lightweight telemetry: counts of packages removed and time spent per repo. Telemetry keys: ci.dep_sanitizer.removed_count and ci.dep_sanitizer.duration_ms.
Thanks to Diego for scheduler feedback, Priya for security reviews, and infra guild for runner pool guidance.

Motivation: Continuous batching at high concurrency exhibits worst-case starvation and tail latency spikes for KV-heavy requests when long-lived pinned keys occupy slots. This PR introduces a decoupled queue-edge cutover and kernel slice hinting mechanism to reduce tail latency while preserving throughput. The design separates admission/queueing and execution handoff: a lightweight queue-edge reconciler performs fairness rebalancing and issues timed cutover windows to avoid head-of-line pinning; the execution handoff now accepts kernel slice hints that allow the runtime to schedule shorter preemptible slices for large attention kernels, improving cooperative fairness between KV-heavy and compute-heavy requests. Summary of changes: 1) runtime/batcher: add queue_edge_reconciler with priority buckets, soft-timeout windows, and probe-driven cutover triggers. 2) runtime/scheduler: implement kernel_slice_hints API and slice budget accounting; expose per-model hint profiles used during model-onboarding. 3) runtime/kvcache: improve pin-awareness by exposing key residency metrics and adding a transient pin-decay policy to reduce long tail for pinned keys. 4) telemetry: new metrics queue_edge_delay_seconds, slice_hint_utilization_ratio, kv_pin_decay_count; dashboards updated. 5) tests/benchmarks: microbench harness for mixed KV+compute workload and e2e perf job with 95th/99th tracking. Behavioral guarantees: soft timeouts are conservative by default and can be tuned via batcher_config.slo_steering; starvation monitor will escalate to emergency cutover that temporarily disables coalescing for offending keys. Backwards compatibility: kernel_slice_hints are optional; default hint profiles preserve current behavior. Performance: mixed workload benchmark on p4d-equivalent nodes shows median latency -6% and p99 tail -18% for KV-heavy routes at 80% load; overall throughput unchanged within 1.5%. Rollout plan: staged canary starting with 5% traffic, monitoring new telemetry for 48 hours, then 25% then global; can be reverted by toggling batcher.queue_edge.enabled. Why this is different: instead of solely adjusting admission timers or batch sizes, this change decouples the queuing semantics from execution slices and surfaces hints to kernel selection so the runtime can make informed preemption decisions, reducing harmful coupling between KV pin duration and large attention kernel runs.
Initial review requested changes around the default soft-timeout (Arjun asked to make default more conservative) and to add a telemetry counter for emergency cutovers (Sofia). I updated batcher/config.go to expose slo_steering.max_soft_timeout_ms and added queue_edge_emergency_cutovers_total metric. Liam suggested making kernel_slice_hints opt-in via model metadata which I implemented by checking model_profile.slice_hintable flag; this avoided changing default kernels for existing models. CI initially failed on the perf job due to an environment race; I fixed a test harness race by introducing deterministic seeds and re-ran CI; all checks passed. Reviewers approved after the fixes; approvals: Arjun (approve), Sofia (approve), Liam (approve). Author notes: included benchmark harness and runbook for ops to tune soft timeouts during canary.
Adds queue-edge reconciler and kernel slice hinting to reduce p99 for mixed KV+compute workloads; new telemetry (queue_edge_delay_seconds, slice_hint_utilization_ratio, kv_pin_decay_count); config knobs: batcher.queue_edge.enabled, batcher.slo_steering.max_soft_timeout_ms, model_profile.slice_hintable; rollout via canary; no behavior change unless enabled.

Motivation: During a multi-region load spike we observed repeated transient egress congestion that caused many in-flight requests to be re-routed, which magnified tail latency and triggered unnecessary regional failovers. This change introduces a lightweight transient route coalescer plus a graceful failover watchdog to reduce noisy re-routing and make SLO-driven failovers more deterministic.

What this PR does: - Adds a route coalescer that groups short-lived egress bursts within a tunable window so that routing decisions are evaluated on aggregated signals rather than per-request jitter. - Adds a failover watchdog that enforces a backoff+holdoff policy before initiating regional failover, driven by calibrated SLO breach heuristics. - Introduces telemetry hooks and a small in-memory smoothing buffer for egress metrics used by the coalescer. - Adds a new SRE-configurable feature flag (runtime) and a safe rollout plan (gradual enablement across regions).

Behavioral summary: - Short transients (default window: 500ms) are coalesced: routing retains the existing path while metrics accumulate; only sustained degradation triggers a failover candidate evaluation. - The watchdog requires a two-step confirmation (sustained metric, and KV-cache pressure or queue depth threshold) before promoting a failover. - Early exit on obvious catastrophic signals (node offline, disk threshold) remains immediate.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for coalescer logic and smoothing buffer with edge cases (burst only, long sustained spike, interleaved quiet/burst). - Integration test simulating regional egress spike with synthetic traffic to validate reduced failover rate and improved P99 latency. - Load test in perf-lab: when coalescer enabled, failover decisions dropped by ~62% on short spikes and application P99 improved by ~18ms under same load profile.

Rollout plan: - Feature flag default off. Stage 1: enable in staging and run perf harness for 48h (done). Stage 2: enable in canary region (eu-west-1) with 1% of traffic for 6h -> 10% for 12h -> 100% for region. Stage 3: enable global by region when canary metrics stable. SLO guardrails in console will auto-roll back if region-level error budget drains > 4% within an hour.

Operational notes: - New metrics: egress_coalescer.windowed_events, failover_watchdog.confirmations, route_coalesce_skipped_reasons. - Two new alert rules added: 'coalescer_rate_anomaly' and 'watchdog_confirmation_spike'. - Recommended tuning: window_ms, min_events_to_coalesce, confirmation_threshold.

Migration/backwards compatibility: - All changes are opt-in via runtime config. No data migrations required. Fallthrough logic ensures behavior is identical to current routing when the feature is disabled.

References: Linear ENG-4219 for design doc, SRE runbook SRE-88 updated with tuning guidance.
Maya Chen: Can you add a short note about worst-case added latency from the smoothing buffer? We need to ensure targets are clear for mobile customers.
Author (Ethan Park): Added comments and a microbenchmark section in docs that shows median added latency < 0.6ms for default window. Updated docs/sre/runbooks/egress-coalescer.md.
Priya Nair: The confirmation thresholds look conservative; please add toggles so SRE can adjust without deploy. Also please ensure metrics are high-cardinality safe.
Author (Ethan Park): Exposed min_events_to_coalesce and confirmation_threshold to runtime flags; metrics tagged at region+route but aggregated in low-cardinality roll-ups. Added tests for tag merging.
Liam O'Reilly: Tested in perf-lab — behavior looks stable. Only request: add a short circuit if the KV-cache pressure cannot be read (GRACEFUL fallback).
Author (Ethan Park): Implemented KV-cache read guard with conservative fallback (treat as negative confirmation). Added unit test.

payload.body:
Motivation: production traffic shows frequent short prefill bursts that cause decode-stage stalls and late tail latency spikes. Existing backpressure relies on coarse token credits and reactive KV eviction which either underutilizes kernels or thrashes the KV cache. This change introduces a token-flow-regulator subsystem that (1) exposes a lightweight admission controller for KV cache residency, (2) co-schedules prefill and decode kernel slices to avoid head-of-line bursts, and (3) introduces a pacing policy that converts microbursts into shaped windows that downstream decode kernels can absorb.

Design summary: the token-flow-regulator sits in the serving runtime pipeline between request intake and kernel dispatch. It tracks in-flight token windows, maintains a small moving-window estimator of per-request sequence progress, and emits two control signals: KV admission (allow/hold/evict-hint) and kernel-slot allocation hints (slice-size, priority). The regulator uses a credit refill algorithm with a burst-tolerance factor to allow short spikes without triggering KV admission evictions. Kernel co-scheduling uses those hints to place small prefill slices adjacent to pending decode slices on the same GPU when beneficial (reduces kernel launch overhead and warms KV cache).

What changed (high level): added runtime/scheduler/token_flow_regulator.cpp, runtime/scheduler/token_flow_regulator.h; implemented KV admission policy in runtime/kvcache/admission_controller.rs; extended kernel dispatcher to accept slice hints in runtime/worker/kernel_dispatcher.cpp; added integration tests and a microbenchmark harness in bench/token_flow_bench.py; updated docs and operator knobs in docs/perf/token_flow_regulator.md.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-4193) [x] unit tests added [x] integration perf harness + baseline numbers [x] feature flagged behind runtime.token_flow_regulator.enabled [ ] experimental metrics gated behind feature flag (follow-up patch)

Performance summary: in internal prefill-heavy traces the change reduces 99th-percentile completion latency for short conversations by ~14% and reduces KV cache churn measured as eviction rate by ~28%. End-to-end token/sec throughput on stable long conversations is neutral (-1% within variance). See bench/token_flow_report.md for detailed numbers and flamegraphs.

Operational notes: the feature is behind a feature flag and default-off for Dedicated clusters. Operators can tune runtime.token_flow_regulator.max_burst_tokens and .burst_tolerance. Rolling upgrade path: enable flag in canary subset, monitor kvcache.evictions and serving.tail_latency_99th. Rollback: flip feature flag or revert the feature gate; admission_controller changes do not change on-disk cache format.

Related: complements recent kernel slice optimizations; differs from speculative prefill in that this is admission and pacing-first (not speculative decode).
Arjun Patel: Nice direction. Two asks: (1) please add a clear invariant comment on when admission_controller may trigger eviction_hints vs hard evictions; (2) the kernel co-schedule path needs a fallback if GPU affinity doesn't match.
Author (Maya): added eviction_hints docs and implemented fallback to next-best GPU slot.
Sofia Martinez: Microbenchmark looks promising. Can you add a test that simulates sustained microbursts to ensure we don't starve long-running decodes?
Author: added prefill_burst_test with configurable burst patterns and threshold asserts.
Leo Wang: CI flagged a flake in perf harness that was caused by nondeterministic RNG seed; request deterministic seeds in harness.
Author: deterministic seeds added and re-ran benchmarks; attached updated report.
Infra Bot: integration/bench marked flaky on first run; re-run passed.
runtime: add token-flow-regulator to smooth prefill bursts and reduce KV cache churn; 99p tail latency improved for short conversations. Feature gated behind runtime.token_flow_regulator.enabled.
