How to run locally: 1) python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate 2) pip install -r quickstarts/guided-sprint/requirements.txt 3) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=<key> 4) python quickstarts/guided-sprint/probe/local_probe.py --seed 42 --count 10 5) Inspect JSON traces at /tmp/guided-sprint-traces and run quickstarts/guided-sprint/validate_traces.py for basic assertions.

Telemetry and expectations: traces are intentionally minimal: each step emits {"step": "retrieve|refine|tool", "lat_ms": <int>, "tokens": <int>, "status": "ok|warn|fail"} and an overall session summary. The README documents how to plug the traces into Console by uploading the JSON or using the small adapter script included.

Compatibility: the example agent uses the public Redwood SDK patterns (prompts -> structured JSON -> tool calling) but avoids any private APIs. The quickstart is suitable for hosted and local flow testing; it does not assume Dedicated or Private deployment.

Motivation: engineers frequently need a compact, reproducible environment to iterate on tool-calling behavior and regression test retrieval-augmented agents under synthetic but realistic user flows. This quickstart introduces a Replay Lab that records simulated sessions (prompt sequence + tool calls + tool responses) and a complementary tool-call fuzzer that injects network and tool-level edge conditions to surface robustness regressions. The goal is to give engineers a local-first loop for: 1) capturing a failing session from production or CI, 2) replaying it against new model/config variants, 3) running a deterministic fuzzer to exercise tool bindings and structured-output contracts, and 4) asserting invariants via lightweight contract tests and telemetry probes. What this PR adds: - quickstarts/replay-lab/README.md: walkthrough and concepts for recording, replaying, and writing assertions. - quickstarts/replay-lab/devcontainer/: VSCode devcontainer + docker-compose for local runners. - quickstarts/replay-lab/recorder: small Go-based session recorder that captures request/response envelopes and kv-cache warmup traces. - quickstarts/replay-lab/player: Node-based deterministic player that can run sessions in headless mode and emit structured-output diffs. - quickstarts/replay-lab/fuzzer: Python harness that mutates tool responses, simulates latencies, and toggles transient errors for tool-call paths. - quickstarts/replay-lab/tests/: playwright smoke e2e + contract assertions that run in CI. - quickstarts/replay-lab/example-corpus/: three curated example sessions (search-and-lookup, multi-tool itinerary, and invoice extraction) used by tests and demos. - CI workflow quickstarts/replay-lab/ci.yml: smoke runner job and matrix config for node/python versions. Developer checklist (included in README): - [x] Capture session via recorder - [x] Replay locally using player - [x] Run fuzzer against tool stubs - [x] Add contract assertions for structured output - [x] Run CI smoke job The description contains a short troubleshooting section and tips for pairing with Redwood Console telemetry (how to correlate session ids). Backwards compatibility: all added code is opt-in under the quickstarts path and does not change any platform API. The recorder/player work over the standard Redwood API surface and default auth; no changes to core runtime. Testing: local devcontainer smoke run + CI matrix. Performance: n/a for production runtime. Rollout: documents and quickstart merged to main and published to docs site via the docs pipeline. Related work: builds on ENG-1423 (replayability RFC) and ENG-1588 (tool-call contract spec).

Changed areas/files (representative): - quickstarts/rag-mosaic/README.md (new authoring guide and examples) - quickstarts/rag-mosaic/templates/*.yaml (retrieval/transform/tool/output stubs) - quickstarts/rag-mosaic/live-preview/server.py (SSE endpoints + example runner) - quickstarts/rag-mosaic/live-preview/static/index.html (mosaic UI) - quickstarts/rag-mosaic/devcontainer.json + .devcontainer/Dockerfile - quickstarts/rag-mosaic/telemetry/probes.yaml - .github/workflows/quickstart-e2e.yml (added smoke job) - docs/site/content/quickstarts/rag-mosaic.md (documentation and screenshots)

Usage and run instructions (short): 1) git checkout feature/rag-mosaic-authoring-live-preview 2) cd quickstarts/rag-mosaic 3) ./dev.sh start (boots local index, preview server, and sample index) 4) Open http://localhost:8080 to interact with mosaic editor and live preview The quickstart ships with a small seeded index (sqlite + json files) and an in-memory mock tool for safe local iteration.

Design notes and rationale: - Mosaic layout: each step emits a compact envelope {type, summary, tokens_used, result_preview}. The UI displays envelopes tiled so authors can quickly inspect how retrieval, rerank, transform, and tool calls interact. - Live preview uses SSE to avoid full-page polling; server-side runner replays a seeded conversation and emits step-level deltas to the UI. This mirrors production tracing while remaining lightweight for local runs. - Telemetry probes: small hooks are emitted from the runner with route and token-level metadata; default probes are no-op but wired to Redwood Console examples in telemetry/probes.yaml. - Templates: YAML-based step templates were chosen for readability and copy/paste ergonomics in docs and repos. Templates include sensible defaults for caching/batching hints and an example quantization/throughput note.

Testing and CI: - Added a headless CI job quickstart-e2e that launches the preview server, runs a scripted interaction via curl/WebSocket, and validates expected envelopes are emitted. - Initial runs flagged a flaky timing issue in the SSE client; fixed by adding a small backoff and a readiness probe in server.py. Current CI: pass (2026-02-12) — run summary: lint: pass, unit: pass, smoke-e2e: pass after 1 rerun.

Review conversation (highlights): - Chris Nguyen: "Nice UX—can we make the templates explicit about token budget guidance?" => Author: "Added 'token_budget' field and inline guidance in templates/README." - Maya Patel: "Telemetry probes look sensible; only ask is to keep them opt-in by default." => Author: "Probes are opt-in; default probes.yaml is commented with usage and a small snippet to hook to Redwood Console." - Jonah Reyes: "CI smoke job duplicated some logic from other quickstarts, consider extracting helpers." => Author: "Pulled common e2e helpers into .github/actions/quickstart-utils and updated workflow." - Maya: "Approve after CI green." - Chris: "Approve." Merge: squash-and-merge by Lena Morales on 2026-02-12.

Backwards compatibility and risks: - No breaking changes to existing APIs or docs. The quickstart is additive and isolated under quickstarts/rag-mosaic. - Risk: SSE behavior might differ across browsers; added guidance in README with fallback polling option and a small compatibility test in the e2e job.

Notes: kept the description intentionally compact and focused on developer onboarding, low-friction iteration, and telemetry safety. The quickstart intentionally avoids production-grade index setup and instead demonstrates wiring and UX patterns for teams to adapt to their infra.

payload.body:
## Context
We need a shared retrieval seam across templates so we can (a) swap local vs hosted vector stores without rewriting app code, (b) keep the “RAG baseline” consistent across Python and TS, and (c) emit consistent observability signals (retrieval latency, hit counts, empty results) for supportability. This PR introduces a small retriever abstraction, a default local adapter (FAISS-like behavior but lightweight for template use), and a hosted adapter placeholder that keeps vendor lock-in minimal.

## What’s in this PR
- `Retriever` interface (Python) + equivalent `Retriever` contract (TS stub for parity, used by shared docs/tests).
- `LocalVectorStoreRetriever` (default): simple embedding+ANN wrapper with a persistent store for dev; optimized for template ergonomics rather than maximum recall.
- `HostedVectorDbRetriever` (placeholder): a thin adapter with TODOs and clearly documented extension points (endpoint/auth/index name), intentionally not pulling a specific vendor SDK yet.
- Chunking defaults:
  - `CHUNK_SIZE_TOKENS=800`
  - `CHUNK_OVERLAP_TOKENS=120`
  - `MAX_CHUNKS_PER_DOC=200` (guardrail)
  - basic HTML/markdown stripping + whitespace normalization
- Retrieval result schema with explicit fields (`doc_id`, `chunk_id`, `text`, `score`, `source`, `metadata`) and redaction guidance.
- Observability:
  - span `rag.retrieve` with attributes `rag.retriever`, `rag.top_k`, `rag.query_length`, `rag.empty`, `rag.index_name` (if present)
  - logs include `retriever_type` and `result_count` (no raw query/doc text)

## Why these defaults
- Chunk size/overlap values are chosen to be safe for common doc-search workloads while avoiding unbounded token costs. We cap chunks per doc to prevent accidental ingestion blow-ups.
- Local adapter keeps onboarding simple (no external services) and makes evals reproducible.
- Hosted adapter placeholder is meant to be swapped by customers without changing the orchestration/agent loop.

## Files / high-level changes
- `python/rag_agent/retrieval/base.py`: introduces `Retriever` protocol + result dataclasses
- `python/rag_agent/retrieval/local_store.py`: local adapter implementation and persistence
- `python/rag_agent/retrieval/hosted_vector_db.py`: placeholder adapter (config + contract)
- `python/rag_agent/ingest/chunking.py`: token-aware chunking defaults + preprocessing
- `python/rag_agent/config.py`: env schema updates and validation
- `python/rag_agent/app/rag_pipeline.py`: pipeline now depends on `Retriever` interface
- `docs/retrieval.md`: explains how to choose/implement retrievers and what’s logged/observed
- `tests/test_retrieval_contract.py`: contract tests for empty results, top_k behavior, deterministic ordering

## Illustrative snippet
Python interface (trimmed):

```py
class Retriever(Protocol):
    def retrieve(self, query: str, *, top_k: int, filters: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> list[RetrievedChunk]:
        ...

@dataclass
class RetrievedChunk:
    doc_id: str
    chunk_id: str
    text: str
    score: float
    source: str
    metadata: dict[str, str]
```

Span naming:
- `rag.retrieve`
- nested under request span (existing `http.server`/`agent.run` depending on route)

## Security / privacy
- No raw query text is emitted as span attributes or logs.
- Metadata is whitelisted (string keys/values) and intended for non-PII tags only.
- Chunking pipeline includes a size cap and strips obvious HTML artifacts; does not attempt PII detection (documented as non-goal).

## Testing
- Added contract tests for retriever behavior and chunking determinism.
- Updated existing smoke tests to validate retrieval spans exist and include `rag.retriever`.

## Follow-ups
- Add real hosted adapter(s) after we decide which vendors to support in v1 (PM-913).
- Mirror retrieval contract + local adapter in TS template (Dana is tracking; this PR adds the shared interface notes but not the full TS implementation).
- Introduces a stable Retriever interface for RAG templates (query + optional metadata filters).
- Adds local vector store adapter as the default for dev (FAISS-like via sqlite/ann-lite implementation).
- Adds hosted vector DB adapter placeholder with a clean seam for provider-specific SDKs.
- Adds opinionated chunking defaults (size/overlap) and document preprocessing hooks.
- Adds retrieval spans + metrics tags consistent with template observability conventions.
Wei Chen: Can we justify the default chunk size/overlap? Some users will paste PDFs and we’ll over-chunk and blow up ingestion time.
Monica Patel (author): Added rationale in docs + hard cap `MAX_CHUNKS_PER_DOC` with a clear error message and remediation (increase cap or filter docs). Also added a progress log every N chunks to avoid “hung” perception.

Allison Grant: Please avoid putting `rag.query` or `rag.doc_preview` on spans; cardinality + privacy risk. Also ensure `rag.index_name` is optional and sanitized.
Monica Patel: Agree. Removed query/doc text from span attributes; only lengths/counts. Added sanitization for index name (alnum + `_`/`-`) and truncation to 64 chars.

Sabrina James: Contract test ordering looks flaky if scores tie; we should enforce deterministic sort.
Monica Patel: Updated local adapter to break ties by `(score desc, doc_id asc, chunk_id asc)` and asserted ordering in tests.

Brian Murphy: Hosted adapter placeholder: can we make sure it doesn’t import any vendor SDKs and that the config surface won’t clash with future providers?
Monica Patel: It’s a pure placeholder; no vendor deps. Config keys are namespaced (`VECTORDB_*`) and the adapter takes a `client` object so templates can wire any SDK without changing core code.

Wei Chen: Minor docs note—call it “hosted vector DB placeholder” explicitly so people don’t assume it’s supported.
Monica Patel: Updated docs and README callouts.

Allison Grant: One more request: add a span attribute for empty retrieval results (`rag.empty=true`) so dashboards can show ‘no context’ situations.
Monica Patel: Added `rag.empty` and a counter metric `rag.retrieval.empty_results` with low-cardinality labels.

Final: Approvals from Wei + Allison + Sabrina. Squash merge.

Summary: This PR adds a new quickstart that shows developers how to wire embedded debug probes into a small Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) agent. The quickstart covers local developer ergonomics (live probes, toggles), structured telemetry events (span names, severity levels), and an optional lightweight relay for shipping telemetry to hosted observability backends. Motivation: Teams building RAG agents often struggle to get actionable signals from fast-moving tool-calling paths and KV cache interactions. This quickstart provides an opinionated, minimal instrumented example that is easy to drop into existing RAG microservices and runs with the Redwood SDKs. It is intentionally small (single-node dev mode) and focuses on observability primitives rather than a full production collector. What changed (high level commits): 1) feat: add quickstart skeleton and README with setup and walkthrough (initial commit) 2) feat: embed debug-probe helpers in example agent (probe lifecycle, sampling toggle) 3) feat: add telemetry relayer example (file sink + optional HTTP forwarder) 4) docs: add architecture diagram and troubleshooting tips 5) tests: add smoke test for probe lifecycle and CI integration Notes on design: - Embedded probes are designed for low overhead: sampling rate defaults to 0.05 and can be bumped via environment variable for local debugging. - Probes emit structured JSON lines with fields: timestamp, probe_id, probe_type, duration_ms, tags, trace_id, span_id. - The optional relayer demonstrates how to convert probe lines to OTLP/Jaeger/Redwood Console events; it is intentionally separate from the agent to keep quickstart minimal. Files changed (high level): - quickstarts/rag-embedded-probes/README.md (new) - quickstarts/rag-embedded-probes/example-agent/main.py (new) - quickstarts/rag-embedded-probes/example-agent/probes.py (new) - quickstarts/rag-embedded-probes/relayer/README.md (new) - quickstarts/rag-embedded-probes/relayer/relayer.py (new) - quickstarts/rag-embedded-probes/test/test_probes.py (new) - docs/images/rag-probes-arch.svg (new) Short commit summaries: - a1f3c2e feat: quickstart scaffold and README with runbook - b7d9a11 feat: probes helper and context manager + sampling - c4e5f82 feat: relayer example and OTLP mapping - d91a7b0 test: add probe lifecycle smoke test and CI job CI/Checks: - GitHub Actions: python-unit-tests (pass) - Lint: ruff/black (pass) - Docs build: mkdocs (pass, warnings fixed in final commit) - Quickstart smoke matrix: local run & patch tests (pass) Testing performed: - Local end-to-end: executed the example agent in dev mode, toggled sampling to 1.0, verified probe lines written to file sink, and verified relayer converts to OTLP JSON envelope. - Unit: test_probes covers probe lifecycle, start/stop semantics, and sampling edge cases. - Manual: ran the quickstart against a small local vector store (sqlite) and validated cache-hit probe emission for prefix-cached responses. Review conversation (high level): - Riley Park: Requested clearer guidance for production vs dev usage and asked to lower default sampling in README. Response: lowered default sampling to 0.05 and added a prominent WARNING block in README. - Sofia Martinez: Asked for a one-click dev run command and CI smoke test. Response: added a github workflow quickstart-smoke that runs the example agent for 10s and asserts probes appear. - Liam O'Connor: Minor feedback on naming (probe -> debug_probe) and suggested tracing span_id presence; both addressed. Migration/rollout notes: - This is a docs/quickstart-only change; no runtime library changes. Safe to merge with docs cadence. - If teams adopt relayer in production, recommend routing to a buffered collector and enforcing backpressure; added a short paragraph to README. How to run locally (excerpt): - git checkout feature/rag-embedded-probes-qs - cd quickstarts/rag-embedded-probes - python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate - pip install -r example-agent/requirements.txt - env REDWOOD_PROBE_SAMPLING=1.0 python example-agent/main.py - tail -f /tmp/rag-probes.log to watch probe lines Observability guidance included: - Probe taxonomy and suggested naming conventions (e.g., probe_type:kv_cache_hit, probe_type:tool_invoke) - Mapping to Redwood Console event fields and suggested dashboards (latency P50/P95 by probe_type, cache hit ratio over request window) Security and privacy: - Probes intentionally avoid logging PII by default; README highlights fields that could contain user-provided strings and recommends scrubbing. - Relayer includes a configurable filter to drop high-cardinality tags. Documentation additions: - Step-by-step quickstart README with images and expanded troubleshooting - Architecture SVG and example dashboards screenshots - Troubleshooting: common causes for missing probes (sampling env, file permissions) Follow-ups (recommended): - Add TypeScript/Go versions of the same quickstart for SDK parity (tracked ENG-3042) - Add a small demo in the docs site that streams probe events to a live dashboard (opt-in) Related work: ENG-2983 (observability primitives for runtime), PM-1140 (RAG dev experience), SUP-8721 (customer request for debug tooling). Merge notes: - Squash-merged to main after green CI and approvals. - Changelog: docs(quickstarts): add rag embedded debug probes quickstart (release notes above).
Adds a new RAG quickstart that demonstrates embedding lightweight debug probes and telemetry hooks for local development and production observability. Recommended for teams instrumenting RAG workflows for latency, cache hits, and tool-calling traces.

Motivation: Provide a compact, reproducible RAG test harness and template set for product teams and examples authors to validate agent/tool-calling flows locally and in CI. This PR adds a lightweight 'schematic' template format plus runnable example stubs so engineers can create reproducible regressions for tool integrations and prompt/eval suites. References: Linear ENG-8321, internal testing playbook, and docs site quickstart section (docs link included below).

What this adds (single continuous description): The rag-harness folder contains a human-readable schematic.yaml that defines: - agents: logical agent names, supported tools, and expected tool signatures - flows: staged conversation traces (user -> agent -> tool -> agent) that serve as deterministic smoke tests - assertions: simple output/metadata checks to detect regressions (exact match, regex, and token-frequency heuristics) Alongside the schematic are two example artifacts: - examples/prompt-sets.json: canonical prompts used by CI to exercise common edge cases (context-window boundaries, streaming chunks, tool timeouts) - examples/tool-stubs.ts: a TypeScript dev shim that implements the tools declared in schematic.yaml; it logs call payloads and returns deterministic fixtures to make local runs stable.

Developer experience: Included devcontainer.json and a small runner script (ci/run-integration.sh) so contributors can: 1) Open the folder in VS Code with the devcontainer, 2) run ./scripts/run-harness locally to execute the flows against local Redwood CLI or remote endpoint (configurable via environment), 3) iterate on prompt-sets and tool stubs without spinning up infra. The quickstart page under site/content/quickstarts explains configuration variables, examples for Hosted vs. Private endpoints, and recommended checklist for turning a schematic into a production regression test.

CI and safety: Added a lightweight GitHub Actions job (.github/workflows/harness-ci.yml) that: - boots a matrix for node versions (18/20) - runs the harness runner against a mock endpoint (tool stubs) - lints prompt-sets for banned tokens and verifies assertions pass The job is intentionally fast (~30s per matrix) so it can gate docs/quickstart changes without adding heavy runtime cost. Secrets for hitting real endpoints are opt-in via repository secrets and not required for the fast path.

Checklist (what to review): - [x] schematic.yaml structure and examples cover common agent-tool patterns (sync, async, streaming) - [x] tool-stubs.ts exercises all declared tool signatures - [x] prompt-sets include failure/edge cases (timeouts, long-context) - [x] docs quickstart page clearly documents dev and CI flow - [x] CI workflow runs and passes on the repo (see CI status)

Review notes and conversation (excerpted inline in the PR body as a continuous narrative): Diego: "Can we make the schematic format compact enough to be hand-edited in PR comments? Also: please add an example for function-style tool return (structured JSON)." Maya: "Added a short example in schematic.yaml and expanded tool-stubs to emit structured JSON fixtures. Kept top-level keys minimal so it's easy to paste into issues." Harper: "CI should warn but not fail on flaky streaming checks; mark streaming assertions as advisory." Maya: "Streaming assertions are now opt-in per-flow; CI will emit a warning and continue for advisory checks." Rohan: "Docs page needs a short troubleshooting section for auth/timeouts." Maya: "Added troubleshooting and a short example for switching between hosted and private endpoints using REDWOOD_ENDPOINT env var."

Migration / rollout: This is additive and backwards-compatible: teams can adopt the harness by copying schematic.yaml into their repo, customizing tool stubs, and adding the CI workflow. The quickstart page links to a template PR checklist to help internal adoption.

How to validate locally: 1) git clone && cd redwood-quickstarts/rag-harness 2) code . (open devcontainer) 3) ./scripts/run-harness --schematic schematic.yaml --runner examples/tool-stubs.ts 4) inspect results under _harness-output/ for assertion reports

Release notes: Added a quickstart for an opinionated RAG test harness and schema-driven templates to help teams validate tool-calling and agent regressions locally and in CI.

Links: Docs quickstart draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/quickstarts/rag-harness  Linear: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-8321

Motivation: Teams building RAG-powered assistants frequently want to preserve short-term conversational context and anchor useful facts across a session without leaking state between users. This quickstart demonstrates a pragmatic pattern: a session-aware retrieval layer with explicit pinning and TTL, an LRU local cache for hot prefixes, and telemetry hooks to measure token cost and retrieval latency.

What this PR adds: - A new quickstart named 'retained-context-rag-workflow' with TypeScript and Python examples showing how to: 1) create ephemeral session IDs, 2) pin documents or embeddings to a session-scoped vector index, 3) configure TTL/expiry for pinned items, 4) fall back to global index when capacity is exceeded, and 5) emit telemetry (trace spans and cost events) for each retrieval+generation round trip. - Example harness to run small synthetic sessions and assert that pinned context persists across requests while obeying TTL and eviction. - Docs page under /quickstarts/rag/retained-context.md with architecture diagram (SVG), configuration knobs, and recommended cost/latency defaults. - A small interactive demo using the quickstart that runs locally (devcontainer) and exposes a /session-visualizer endpoint for debugging pinned items.

Checklist: - [x] Add quickstart code (TS + Python) - [x] Add docsite page and diagrams - [x] Add demo container + docker-compose dev flow - [x] Add unit tests for session pinning logic - [x] Add telemetry probes and CI smoke - [x] Docs review by platform docs owner - [x] Performance sanity run on benchmark-lab

Notes on behavior and tradeoffs: - Pinning is implemented as session-scoped keys stored in the vector store with a short TTL (default 1 hour) and an eviction policy triggered when per-session count > 200. This balances usefulness and storage/cost. - Local LRU cache keeps recently-seen prefix embeddings to reduce vector-store calls for high-frequency sessions; it is disabled in low-memory modes. - For regulated workloads, the quickstart documents how to enable encryption-at-rest and KMS keying for session indices in Private deployments. - The demo emphasizes observability: a trace shows retrieval, filtering, reranking, and generation spans; cost events include token counts and embedding requests.

How to review: Focus review on correctness of session isolation (no cross-session leakage), TTL/eviction defaults, and the telemetry events shape. The TS sample is the canonical reference; the Python sample is a one-to-one port. The docs site additions include copy and an architecture diagram — reviewers should verify wording and recommended knobs.

Related work: ENG-4321 (session-store work), ENG-3992 (vector-ttl feature), PM-112 (product ask for session-aware assistants).

Diff summary: small library additions (session store + pin API), two sample apps, docs page + diagram, and CI entries for quickstart smoke tests.
Introduce session-aware RAG quickstart: demonstrates context retention, per-session pinning, TTL policies, and telemetry probes for cost/latency tradeoffs.

Samira Kapoor: Updated default to 1h in code and doc, added config note for enterprise (KMS + encryption).
Luis Ortega: Please add an assertion in the unit tests that pinned items are not visible in other sessions.
Samira Kapoor: Added cross-session isolation tests and a small integration script used in benchmark-lab runs.
Maya Chen: Docs wording looks good; small nits on diagram labeling (fixed).
Ethan Zhao: CI smoke flake on first run, re-ran and passed. Approving.
Unit tests cover pin/unpin/ttl/eviction; integration smoke runs in CI exercise devcontainer flow; benchmark-lab profile shows median retrieval latency ~18ms for cached prefix and ~42ms for vector-store lookup on default small corpus.

This quickstart is intended as a pragmatic, production-oriented pattern rather than a one-size-fits-all solution. We included telemetry hooks so teams can tune TTL and pin counts against their token cost targets.

Problem: teams authoring RAG scenarios frequently need to iterate variations of prompts, tool bindings, and small index changes in isolation and then merge the best variants back into a canonical scenario. Existing quickstarts show single-file examples or full-playground runners but lack a lightweight, reproducible branching workflow for local authoring and telemetry-driven selection.

What this PR adds: a Snapshot-Branch Quickstart that provides a simple authoring loop: capture a snapshot of the current scenario, create a branch, run iterative edits (prompts, tool contracts, index seed), record deterministic telemetry for each run, and merge a chosen snapshot back into the main scenario. The quickstart is intentionally minimal: no server required, runs locally with the Redwood CLI and the quickstart runner, and includes a devcontainer for reproducible environments.

Key features: snapshot and branch metadata format (YAML + JSON), a tiny runner that replays scenarios deterministically (samples seeded), stepwise telemetry presets for comparing outputs, an example branching workflow (create/compare/merge), devcontainer + smoke CI for reproducibility, and docsite pages with guidance on evaluation criteria.

Usage summary: 1) git clone; 2) open devcontainer or run ./scripts/bootstrap.sh; 3) redwood quickstart run --snapshot create --name=baseline; 4) edit quickstarts/snap-branch/scenario.yaml to try a prompt variant; 5) redwood quickstart run --snapshot branch --from=baseline --name=variant-A; 6) run ./scripts/compare_snapshots.py --left=baseline --right=variant-A to produce a concise diff and telemetry summary; 7) merge with redwood quickstart snapshot merge --source=variant-A --target=baseline if chosen.

Compatibility: works with Redwood CLI (v1.8+), uses the local-hosted test runner (no cloud account required). The quickstart is designed to be safe for enterprise (no secret material stored); optional telemetry uploads are gated behind explicit consent.

Testing and CI: included small e2e smoke test that runs two snapshot branches and asserts stable determinism. CI workflow runs on push and verifies devcontainer build + smoke e2e.

Acceptance criteria: documentation page added, quickstart runner script with tests, devcontainer recipe, telemetry presets file, and a compact example scenario demonstrating branching.

Related: ENG-2104 (authoring UX), DOC-472 (quickstart doc site slot).
Ethan Park: Nice narrow surface area. Can we make sure the compare script handles tokenization differences across engines? Suggested adding a token-normalize flag.
Priya Shah (author): Good call — added a --normalize-tokens flag to compare_snapshots.py and documented engine compatibility in rag-authoring.md.
Lina Gomez: Telemetry looks fine but ensure no PII is collected by default. Add explicit opt-in and a README note about GDPR considerations.
Priya Shah (author): Telemetry uploads are now off by default; dev-mode preserves local files only and the README includes a privacy section.
John Wang: Devcontainer image is slightly heavy. Could we switch to the smaller node:18-slim base to make the startup faster?
Priya Shah (author): Switched to node:18-slim and trimmed unnecessary apt packages; image size reduced ~180MB.
Ethan Park: CI flake observed in e2e on first run due to RNG seed missing in one test. Please ensure seed is always set in runner.
Priya Shah (author): Fixed — seed propagated to all runner invocations and added a guard in tests to fail on missing seed.
Lina Gomez: Approving pending the small README grammar nit (line 42).
Priya Shah (author): Fixed the grammar nit.
John Wang: Approved.
Add snapshot-branch quickstart: local snapshot/branch/merge workflow for iterative RAG authoring; includes devcontainer, deterministic replayer, telemetry presets, and e2e smoke tests.
This quickstart is intentionally orthogonal to the full-playground offerings; it focuses on fast feedback loops for prompt and small-index iteration. We plan to add an optional UI to visualize snapshot diffs in a follow-up PR (ENG-2199).

Motivation: Customers building RAG-enabled products in field-deployed or intermittent-network contexts asked for a reference that demonstrates how to run Redwood inference and a retrieval layer when connectivity is poor or unavailable. This quickstart provides an opinionated, small-footprint sandbox that: 1) shows offline index building and a compact on-disk vector store, 2) demonstrates a local wasm retriever and optional local LLM runtime shim, 3) includes a step-through debugging UI for replaying sessions and inspecting prefix/KV cache behavior, and 4) instruments a telemetry shim that buffers and ships when the network reconnects.

Summary of changes: Added a new quickstart at quickstarts/offline-rag-sandbox with a guided README, sample dataset, a docker-compose + Makefile to bootstrap the sandbox, a tiny wasm retriever (demo code) and a local cache adapter, sample prompts and recorded session replays for the debug UI, and a telemetry shim that simulates backpressure and buffered uploads. The quickstart targets engineers who want a reproducible pattern to: prebuild compact indexes at CI or on-device, run retrieval+LLM in constrained environments, and record traces for postmortem analysis.

Why this is different: Existing quickstarts assume stable network and hosted telemetry. This project shows pragmatic knobs for narrowband (e.g., satellite, factory-floor) use: low-memory quantized embeddings, aggressive prefix/KV cache reuse, opportunistic background sync, and a developer-friendly replay tool for diagnosing mismatches between cached and live model outputs.

Files added: quickstarts/offline-rag-sandbox/README.md, quickstarts/offline-rag-sandbox/docker-compose.yml, quickstarts/offline-rag-sandbox/Makefile, quickstarts/offline-rag-sandbox/sample-data/mini-kb.jsonl, quickstarts/offline-rag-sandbox/retriever/README-wasm.md, quickstarts/offline-rag-sandbox/retriever/wasm-retriever-demo.ts, quickstarts/offline-rag-sandbox/debug-ui/README.md, quickstarts/offline-rag-sandbox/debug-ui/session-replayer.jsonl, quickstarts/offline-rag-sandbox/telemetry/offline-shim.js.

Usage (short): git clone && cd quickstarts/offline-rag-sandbox && make bootstrap && docker-compose up --build. The README contains step-by-step commands to index the sample-data, run the wasm retriever in dev mode, run the Redwood API shim configured to prefer local cache, and then drive the debug UI to replay a recorded session and inspect token-level cache reuse and model fallback logic.

Testing and CI: Added a lightweight smoke script run by CI that runs the indexer, starts the retriever container, and asserts that the sample query returns the expected top-k documents within a 500ms retrieval target on a small VM. CI pipeline shows build/lint/unit-smoke passing; synthetic e2e occasionally flaked on cold-cache startup which is mitigated by a retry in the bootstrap script.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add quickstart files and sample dataset
- [x] Add Makefile and docker-compose for reproducible local runs
- [x] Add debug UI session replay data and documentation
- [x] Add telemetry shim example and instructions for buffered uploads
- [x] Smoke CI test added
- [x] Docs reviewed by platform and runtime teams

Migration and rollout notes: This is additive, no platform changes required. The example references the Redwood-hosted API by default but includes instructions to run entirely offline using a local LLM shim (experimental). Recommend shipping to the docs site under Quickstarts > Offline & Edge RAG (docs staging), and announce to SDKs and solutions channels to collect early feedback.

Related: ENG-1412 (offline vector stores), PM-89 (customer ask from field trials).
Initial author commit with README and bootstrap scripts; add wasm retriever demo; add debug UI replay data; CI smoke test; follow-up commit fixes Makefile path and adds retry for flakey cold-indexing; documentation tweaks after reviewer feedback.

Maya Chen (author): Addressed — removed Rust variant, added security paragraph and explicit encryption-at-rest recommendation for the buffer file. Fixed in second commit.
Sofia Martinez (reviewer): CI smoke failure reproduced locally (cold-index race). Suggest adding an explicit wait/retry in bootstrap and marking the e2e as flaky in CI with rerun. Also asked for clearer guidance on when to use local LLM shim vs hosted API.
Maya Chen (author): Added retry loop to Makefile and updated README with decision criteria for local shim vs hosted API. Updated CI to allow one rerun on flaky e2e.
Add Offline RAG Debug Sandbox quickstart: reproducible local indexer, wasm retriever demo, session replayer UI, and telemetry buffering/shipping shim. Useful for low-connectivity and edge deployments.
Docs entry will go to staging docs site under Quickstarts > Offline & Edge RAG. No platform migration required. Recommend adding a short blog post with field notes from ENG-1412 after initial feedback.

Motivation: provide a minimal, production-ish quickstart that demonstrates async worker-based RAG pipelines in Python using Redwood's streaming API and a lightweight local background queue. This quickstart targets engineers who want to offload long-running retrieval + generation cycles from web request threads, keep streaming to clients, and run locally with minimal infra. Included patterns: 1) async worker that pulls retrieval jobs from an in-memory queue (easy to swap for Redis/RQ or RabbitMQ), 2) incremental streaming to a WebSocket client via a small proxy server, 3) prefix caching for repeated queries, and 4) a SQLite-backed vector store shim for offline examples. What changed: added quickstart folder with a Python async worker example, dev Docker Compose for local run, a short doc page with architecture diagram (ASCII) and API examples, unit tests for core helpers, and CI job to smoke-test the local runner. The README documents tradeoffs and recommended next steps.

Context and motivation: This PR adds a set of guided RAG walkthrough templates aimed at developer onboarding and reproducible local testing. The goal is to provide small, deterministic end-to-end scenarios (index -> retrieval -> agent/tool-calls -> final answer) that teams can run locally and in CI to validate routing, embeddings, tool binding, and structured-output assertions. These templates target both new users (guided step-by-step) and infra teams (deterministic eval hooks and telemetry presets for cost/latency probes).

What this PR includes: - Four new walkthrough templates under quickstarts/walkthroughs/: 'customer-support', 'policy-extractor', 'sales-summary', and 'local-qa' — each with a short README, a tiny synthetic corpus generator, and a one-command local runner. - A lightweight synthetic-corpus generator (scripts/generate_corpus.py) that produces seeded, small index files in JSONL. The generator supports size=small/medium and seed to ensure reproducible retrievals. - Deterministic eval hooks (walkthroughs/_eval/) that assert model outputs against golden prompts using a seeding strategy for any randomness (temperature=0 for CI, seeded RNG for local dev). - Playwright-based smoke scenarios (ci/smoke/walkthroughs.spec.ts) to run a headless quickstart flow in CI and assert telemetry emits. - Telemetry presets and probe docs (walkthroughs/telemetry-presets.md) that include examples for Redwood Console probes: token counts, per-request latency, and tool invocation counts. - Updated quickstarts index and docs nav entry so these templates appear under "Local authoring & quickstarts" on the docs site.

Design notes and trade-offs: - Synthetic corpora are intentionally tiny (~5-20 docs) to keep CI fast and low-cost. They include adversarial edge-cases (overlapping entities, short identical passages) to exercise reranker and retrieval heuristics. - Eval hooks are intentionally strict in CI (temperature=0, deterministic embeddings seed) which will fail if model or retrieval regressions occur. For local runs, authors can switch to temperature>0 to explore. - The Playwright smoke test checks end-to-end flow and the presence of telemetry events; it is intentionally minimal to avoid flakiness.

Checklist:
- [x] Add walkthrough templates and READMEs
- [x] Add synthetic corpus generator with seed support
- [x] Add deterministic eval hooks and golden outputs
- [x] Add telemetry preset documentation
- [x] Add CI smoke tests and Playwright scenarios
- [x] Update quickstarts index and docs nav
- [x] Add unit tests for corpus generator and eval harness

Commits summary: - a2f8b3c: initial walkthrough templates and generator stub - 6c4d2e9: flesh out customer-support and policy-extractor walkthroughs - 92b1f77: add deterministic eval hooks and golden outputs - d4e5a7a: add Playwright smoke tests and CI job - e8c9aa0: docs nav and telemetry presets

Files changed (high level): - quickstarts/walkthroughs/customer-support/README.md - quickstarts/walkthroughs/customer-support/run.sh - quickstarts/walkthroughs/policy-extractor/README.md - quickstarts/walkthroughs/local-qa/README.md - quickstarts/walkthroughs/sales-summary/README.md - quickstarts/walkthroughs/_eval/ (golden outputs and assertion harness) - scripts/generate_corpus.py - ci/smoke/walkthroughs.spec.ts - quickstarts/index.md (nav entry) - walkthroughs/telemetry-presets.md - tests/test_generate_corpus.py - examples/sample_corpora/*.jsonl

Small illustrative snippet (corpus generator seed usage):

# generate_corpus.py --seed 42 --size small --out examples/sample_corpora/customer_support_seed42.jsonl

The generator produces short JSONL docs with stable IDs so retrieval results are stable across runs when the same seed is used.

Review conversation snapshot: Miguel Torres (reviewer) - "Nice addition. Two things I'd like to see before merge: 1) clarify how the CI secrets are consumed by the Playwright smoke job; 2) reduce the Playwright timeout for the smoke check (it currently waits 30s which is too long for our fast CI)."

Asha (author) - "Thanks Miguel — addressing both: updated CI job to read REDWOOD_CLI_TOKEN from repo secrets and added a 10s explicit wait/timeout for the smoke assertion. PTAL."

Leah Kim (reviewer) - "Eval hooks are great. Suggest we add a short note in the README that these are intentionally strict in CI and how to relax them locally."

Asha (author) - "Added a 'Running locally' section to each README and examples showing temperature/seed override. Also added a note in telemetry-presets.md."

CI summary: - Initial run: lint + unit tests passed, Playwright smoke failed intermittently (timing issue). - Rerun after changes: all checks passed. CI artifacts: attached smoke run logs and trace files.

Performance and cost considerations: The smoke CI job targets a 40s wall-clock budget and the synthetic corpora keep token usage < 4k per run. Telemetry presets include token counts and a per-route cost estimate to help authors iterate on cost.

Migration and rollout: This is additive; no migration required. The docs nav update will surface these templates in the next docs site build.

Follow-ups planned: - ENG-1429: add examples that show cache warmup patterns with prefix caching. - PM-88: gather qualitative onboarding feedback from two internal teams and refine templates. - Add a periodic CI job to run walkthroughs against a dedicated lightweight model variant (low-cost) to detect regression without incurring high tokens.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main on 2026-02-20 after approvals from Miguel and Leah. CI green at merge.

Contact: If you have questions or want additional walkthroughs (e.g. multimodal examples), ping @asha or open an issue under quickstarts/walkthroughs.

Summary: This PR locks down dependency versions across the Python and TypeScript quickstart templates, adds automated vulnerability scanning in CI (PR-time + scheduled), and documents the upgrade process for template maintainers to reduce supply-chain risk. Motivation: Security review flagged unpinned transitive dependencies and lack of automated scanning (see ENG-4190 and template security review open items). We also want template repos to adhere to the Secure SDLC addendum for templates (dependency pinning, vulnerability scanning, and a repeatable upgrade story) without introducing noisy/flake-prone CI failures. Changes included: (1) Python template: move to fully pinned requirements (direct + transitive) via pip-tools, commit compiled requirements with hashes, and add a make target to regenerate; (2) TypeScript template: ensure package-lock.json is committed and consistent, add npm overrides for known vulnerable transitive packages where upstream hasn’t released yet; (3) CI: add a security scanning workflow that runs pip-audit + osv-scanner for Python and npm audit + osv-scanner for TS, with a nightly schedule and a lightweight PR check; (4) Docs: add docs/dependency-upgrades.md describing the approved upgrade cadence, how to regenerate lockfiles, how to handle false positives, and how to record remediation notes. Operational notes: The PR-time workflow is configured to avoid high-noise findings (dev-only packages in example tooling) and to fail only on high/critical CVEs by default; nightly runs are stricter and open an issue with a report artifact. Checklist: - [x] Pin Python deps with hashes - [x] Commit package-lock and align npm ci in CI - [x] Add vuln scanning workflow (PR + schedule) - [x] Document upgrade process + remediation guidelines - [x] Verify templates still install on macOS/Linux (python 3.11, node 20) - [x] No secrets in repo / no new external service tokens. Rollout: This is repo-only and should not impact Redwood API behavior. If CI noise is higher than expected, we can adjust severity thresholds or add targeted ignores with justification in docs/dependency-upgrades.md (no blanket allowlists).
Templates now pin dependencies by default and run scheduled + PR-time vulnerability scans (pip-audit/OSV for Python; npm audit/OSV for TS). Maintainers should follow docs/dependency-upgrades.md for safe upgrades and regenerating lockfiles.
Monica Patel (review): Love the direction. Two nits: (1) can we avoid pinning a pre-release for numpy/scipy equivalents if we don’t need them? (2) please ensure the template README still works with `pip install -r requirements.txt` without requiring pip-tools locally.
Sahana Iyer (author): Ack. Dropped the pre-release pin; the compiled set now stays on stable releases. README flow unchanged; pip-tools is only required for maintainers when regenerating via `make deps-update`.
Marcus Lin (review): For the scanning workflow, please avoid adding broad allowlists. If we need ignores, require a short justification + expiration date. Also: make sure scans run on forks without requiring secrets.
Sahana Iyer (author): Updated docs/dependency-upgrades.md with an ignore policy section (justification + expiry) and confirmed workflows use only GitHub-provided token permissions. Forks run PR checks without secrets; nightly issue creation is skipped on forks.
Hanae Suzuki (review): Please confirm we’re not printing env vars or token-like strings in scan output artifacts. Some tools dump environment context by default.
Sahana Iyer (author): Good catch—set `PIP_AUDIT_FORMAT=json` and upload only the JSON report; also redacted workflow step logs by default (no `set -x`). Added a note in SECURITY.md about artifact contents.
Christine Wong (review): Severity gating looks reasonable. Can we add a small note on what happens when nightly finds a vuln (who is on-call / how we triage)?
Sahana Iyer (author): Added a short triage section pointing to the DevEx rotation and linking ENG-4190 for remediation tracking; nightly workflow opens an issue with label `security` + `dependencies`.
Monica Patel (approval): Approved after latest changes. Thanks for adding the maintainers guide—this will reduce churn.
Marcus Lin (approval): Approved. Please keep the ignore mechanism strict as documented.

payload.body:
## Summary
This PR adds a first-pass region sweep runner to execute benchmark runs across a matrix of {model x region x workload} and emit a standardized run manifest (`manifest.v1.json`) for downstream validation + report generation.

Primary goals:
- Make it easy to run consistent sweeps across NA/EU/APAC regions with one CLI invocation
- Produce machine-readable manifests that capture configs, environment, and outputs for reproducibility + auditability
- Standardize artifact layout so we can later export a clean dataset to web/PDF pipelines

Out of scope:
- Changes to metric computation / normalization (handled in PR-4821)
- Redaction for public artifacts (tracked separately)

## Motivation / context
For the public-facing latency/$ report we need to run the same workload definition across multiple regions, repeat runs for stability gates, and retain sufficient metadata to explain and reproduce numbers. Prior tooling required manually invoking single-region runs and hand-tracking metadata in a sheet.

ENG-18442 calls for:
- region sweep automation
- reproducible manifests
- stable rerun rules integration (later)

This PR is the automation + manifest foundation.

## CLI changes
New command:
- `bench sweep`

Key flags:
- `--models <comma-separated>` e.g. `llama-3.1-8b-instruct,qwen2.5-14b-instruct`
- `--regions <comma-separated>` e.g. `us-east-1,eu-west-1,ap-southeast-1`
- `--workloads <comma-separated>` (defaults to `prod_mix_v3`)
- `--concurrency <int>` (default inherits workload preset)
- `--repeat <int>` number of repeats per matrix cell (default 3)
- `--out <path>` output root directory
- `--dry-run` prints the expanded matrix without executing

Example:
`bench sweep --models llama-3.1-8b-instruct,qwen2.5-14b-instruct --regions us-east-1,eu-west-1 --workloads prod_mix_v3 --repeat 5 --out s3://redwood-bench/runs/2025-06-12/`

## Manifest format (v1)
Each executed run writes:
- `manifest.v1.json` (single source of truth)
- `stdout.log` / `stderr.log`
- `metrics.json` (existing harness output)
- `runner.json` (runner-level timing + retry metadata)

Manifest highlights:
- `schema_version`: "1"
- `run_id`: stable ID derived from matrix inputs + timestamp
- `model`, `region`, `workload`
- `started_at`, `finished_at`, `duration_ms`
- `git`: `repo`, `commit_sha`, `dirty` (see review notes below)
- `runner`: `hostname`, `os`, `python_version`, `docker_image` (when applicable)
- `config`: resolved workload preset + explicit overrides
- `artifacts`: relative paths for outputs
- `status`: success/failure + failure reason

## Implementation notes
- Added `sweep_runner.py` that expands the matrix and executes runs sequentially by default.
- Added basic retry handling at the runner level for transient region failures:
  - retries only for known transient exit codes / network timeouts
  - records `attempts` and `retry_reasons` in `runner.json`
- Artifact directory layout:
  - `<out>/<date>/<run_id>/manifest.v1.json`
- Added `--max-inflight` as an internal flag (not documented yet) to experiment with limited parallelism; default 1 to avoid cross-run contention and confusing latency.

## Changed areas / files (high level)
- `bench/cli.py`: adds `sweep` subcommand + flags
- `bench/sweep_runner.py`: matrix expansion + execution loop
- `bench/manifest.py`: manifest writer + schema validation
- `schemas/manifest.v1.json`: JSON schema for validation
- `tests/test_manifest_v1.py`: unit tests for required fields + stable run_id generation
- `tests/test_sweep_matrix_expansion.py`: validates flag parsing/matrix behavior
- `README.md`: adds a "Region sweeps" section and example usage

Illustrative snippet (manifest writer):
- `manifest["git"]["commit_sha"] = git_rev_parse_head()`
- `manifest["runner"]["python_version"] = platform.python_version()`

## CI
Checks:
- `lint`: pass
- `unit`: pass
- `schema-validate`: pass

Initial CI run failed once due to a flaky integration test that still assumes `bench run` is the only entrypoint; updated to include `bench sweep --dry-run` coverage.

## Review discussion (key points)
### Claire Dubois (requested changes)
Comment: "Manifest is a good start, but we need stronger reproducibility guarantees for the report. Please capture more environment details and make the run_id deterministic across reruns (or explicitly encode randomness)."

Response: Updated `run_id` generation to be deterministic given (model, region, workload, concurrency, prompt_set_version, repetition_index) + an explicit `sweep_id`. Timestamp remains a separate field. Added prompt set version to `config` block.

### Jonas Weber (requested changes)
Comment: "We need to be able to rerun a specific published datapoint. Please include: git SHA, whether working tree is dirty, and the runner image digest when running in Docker. Also add a schema + validation step in CI."

Response: Added `git.commit_sha` + `git.dirty`. Added `runner.docker_image` (string). Added `schemas/manifest.v1.json` and a CI step to validate generated manifests in unit tests.

Follow-up: Jonas asked to record the *digest* not just tag.

Response: Runner now writes `runner.docker_image` as the full reference if provided (e.g., `ghcr.io/redwood/benchmark-runner@sha256:...`). If only a tag is passed, we record the tag and emit a warning in logs.

### Vanessa Ortiz (requested changes)
Comment: "From capacity planning perspective, region selection needs guardrails. Can the runner validate region names against a known allowlist and fail fast if a region is not reservable?"

Response: Added `regions.yaml` allowlist and a `--allow-unknown-regions` escape hatch (default false). Runner fails early with a clear message listing valid region IDs.

### Mei Lin (nit + data hygiene)
Comment: "Please ensure artifact paths are relative in the manifest so the dataset can move between S3 prefixes and local. Also include a stable `schema_version` string." 

Response: Artifact paths are now stored as relative paths from the run root; `schema_version` is a string "1".

## Open questions / follow-ups
- Parallel sweeps: leaving default as sequential until we have a contention-aware scheduler; track separately.
- Stability gates integration: will be layered on top of the manifest (PR-4855).
- Public redaction: not included here (PR-4873).

## Release notes
- Added `bench sweep` to run benchmark matrices across regions/models and emit `manifest.v1.json` per run.

## Checklist
- [x] Added schema + validation
- [x] Added unit tests
- [x] Updated README with usage
- [x] Captured reproducibility fields requested in review

Merge
- Merged via squash into `main`.
Claire Dubois: run_id currently depends on timestamp; we need deterministic IDs for reruns and to join to the master sheet. Also please capture prompt set version in the manifest.
Rina Kobayashi: agreed. I’ll add sweep_id + repetition_index and move timestamp out of run_id; also adding prompt_set_version + resolved preset fields.
Jonas Weber: please record docker image digest when using the container runner; tag alone is not reproducible. Also add a schema and validate in CI.
Rina Kobayashi: added schema + CI validation. runner.docker_image now records the full image reference; if only tag is provided we log a warning. In our runbooks we should pass digest.
Vanessa Ortiz: can we validate region values? We’ve had typos (eu-west vs eu-west-1) burn capacity windows.
Rina Kobayashi: added allowlist in regions.yaml and fail-fast validation; escape hatch flag included for dev environments.
Noah Patel: small nit—capture whether the git tree is dirty. We should not publish numbers from dirty builds.
Rina Kobayashi: added git.dirty and a warning. Runner will still run but marks manifest for review.
Jonas Weber: looks good now. Approving contingent on updated README and tests passing.
Claire Dubois: approved after run_id change; please make sure the schema_version is a string and stable.
payload.title: Region sweep runner + run manifest format for model/region matrices

Motivation: debugging RAG flows during authoring is painful for teams working offline and on CI. This PR adds a compact journey replayer CLI that records interactive RAG sessions, serializes them to a portable .jrny (JSONL+metadata) format, and replays them deterministically with configurable offline probes (tool stubs, latency fuzzers, deterministic RNG). The goal is a lightweight local-first workflow for reproducing issues, running smoke assertions, and generating telemetry snapshots for CI-based quality gates.

What this PR does:
- Add a new CLI 'jrny' (Rust + tiny node shim) under quickstarts/jrny-cli/ that can capture and replay sessions.
- Introduce session serializer format (compact JSONL with header metadata + deterministic seeds).
- Offline probe harness that lets authors register tool stubs, response fixtures, and latency profiles to emulate production toolchains.
- Examples: two templates (simple-qa and multi-tool-orch) and a CI job sample that runs a headless replay with assertions.
- Docs: quickstarts guide and step-by-step authoring tutorial in quickstarts/jrny-cli/README.md.

Checklist:
- [x] CLI binary + minimal Node shim for auth/credentials loading
- [x] Session serializer spec + examples
- [x] Probe harness + simple latency/failure profiles
- [x] Quickstart templates and README with screenshots of trace output
- [x] CI example workflow for offline replay smoke tests

Commits (summary):
- feat: initial jrny-cli scaffold and README (Maya Chen)
- feat: session serializer implementation and tests (Maya Chen)
- feat: probe harness and deterministic RNG seeding (Maya Chen)
- docs: add quickstart walkthrough and CI example (Maya Chen)
- fix: update CLI arg parsing and coverage gaps (Maya Chen)

Files changed (high level):
- quickstarts/jrny-cli/Cargo.toml (new)
- quickstarts/jrny-cli/src/main.rs (new) - lightweight recorder + replayer
- quickstarts/jrny-cli/node-shim/auth_loader.js (new) - small shim to load SDK creds
- quickstarts/jrny-cli/spec/session-serializer.md (new) - spec + examples
- quickstarts/jrny-cli/templates/simple-qa.jrny (new) - example serialized session
- quickstarts/jrny-cli/README.md (new) - full quickstart + CI snippet
- .github/workflows/jrny-replay-ci.yml (new) - example CI that runs replay and asserts non-regression

Small snippet (serializer header example):
{
  "version": "0.1",
  "created_by": "jrny-cli v0.1",
  "seed": 123456789
}

Review conversation (high level):
- Diego: "Nice ergonomic CLI. Two asks: make the seed deterministic in examples and add a minimal Python example for teams not using Rust/Node."
- Author (Maya): "Added deterministic seed in the serializer header and an additional template with a small Python shim that invokes the node-shim. See templates/python-proxy.jrny."
- Priya: "Docs are very clear. Can we add guidance about when to use replay vs live tests?"
- Maya: "Added a short section in README with guidelines and a recommended CI policy for smoke vs full integration runs."
- Evan: "CI flaked once on linux matrix because of a missing env var - reran, now green."

CI summary: initial run failed on lint in action (missing shellexec permission), fixed in follow-up commit; subsequent run passed all matrix jobs (unit tests, smoke replay, md lint). ci_status: pass.

Design notes and tradeoffs: chose a compact JSONL format to keep files human-inspectable and shippable as artifacts. The Rust binary was selected for small, dependency-free cross-compiled binaries; the Node shim limits auth surface area and reuses existing SDK credential loading. The probe harness intentionally focuses on deterministic tooling (fixtures + latency profiles) rather than full service emulation; that keeps CI runs fast and predictable.

2) ./target/release/jrny record --out examples/simple-qa.jrny --sdk-config ~/.config/redwood.json
3) ./target/release/jrny replay --in examples/simple-qa.jrny --probe latency:50 --assert \"final_answer contains \\\"Paris\\\"\"

Title: Playbook serialization, safe autopatch runner, and compact incident snapshot format

Summary: This PR introduces a compact, versioned serialization format for on-call playbooks and incident snapshots (ndjson-lite), a gated 'autopatch' runner that can apply recommended mitigations with dry-run and canary modes, and a small migration utility that backfills existing runbooks into the new snapshot format. The goal is to make handoffs and automated remediation faster and safer: snapshots are smaller on disk, deserialize faster in the UI/CLI, and autopatch requires configurable approval gates before affecting production resources.

Context & motivation: During post-incident reviews and regular on-call workflows we observed two recurring pain points: (1) large serialized playbooks (with full telemetry attachments) were slow to fetch and caused UI lag during handoff, and (2) teams wanted a safer path to attempt automated mitigations without risking blind writes in production. This change addresses both by providing a compact snapshot for fast handoff and a conservative autopatch runner with explicit dry-run/canary/approve semantics. Related Linear: ENG-1249 (playbook serialization), ENG-1350 (autopatch safety). Related support ticket: SUP-4421 (customer request for safer auto-remediation).

What changed (high level):
- New serialization module incident_bot.playbook.serialize implementing a compact NDJSON-like snapshot (versioned schema v2). Snapshots include compacted steps, pointer references to large attachments, and optionally inlined thumbnails.
- Autopatch runner incident_bot.autopatch that supports: dry-run mode (no writes), canary mode (apply to a subset of targets, default 1%), and production mode which requires 2 approvals for sensitive namespaces. The runner logs intent, a proposed patch diff, and emits a signed intent token.
- CLI flags: `ibctl snapshot export --compact` and `ibctl autopatch run --mode=canary` plus `--approvals=2` override.
- Migration script tools/migrate_playbooks_to_v2.py to backfill existing DB playbooks into v2 snapshots; this runs in batches and has idempotent checkpoints.
- Observability: new metrics incidentbot.playbook.serialize_ms, incidentbot.autopatch.attempts_total, incidentbot.autopatch.success_total, and associated tracing spans. Added Grafana dashboard snippets in observability/dashboards/playbook-autopatch.json.
- Tests: unit tests for serialization edge cases, integration test for autopatch dry-run and canary modes, and a local e2e test that exercises the CLI export/import flow.

Commits (summary):
- 0a3f9c3: add compact serializer and schema docs
- c71e2b1: implement autopatch runner with dry-run/canary/production modes
- e45b8f0: add CLI flags and short help text for snapshot/autopatch
- b92a5d4: migration utility and backfill job with checkpointing
- 8c3d2a7: add unit & integration tests, update CI config
- d14f0b2: dashboard snippets and metrics exporters

Files changed (high level):
- incident_bot/playbook/serialize.py (new)
- incident_bot/autopatch/runner.py (new)
- tools/migrate_playbooks_to_v2.py (new)
- cli/ibctl/commands/snapshot.py (modified)
- cli/ibctl/commands/autopatch.py (modified)
- observability/dashboards/playbook-autopatch.json (new)
- tests/unit/test_serialize.py (new)
- tests/integration/test_autopatch_canary.py (new)

Review thread (high level):
- Aisha Patel (review): Asked for clearer schema versioning and a migration rollback plan; flagged potential security concerns around signed intent tokens and token rotation.
  - Author response: Added schema version field and a migration checkpoint/rollback step in tools/migrate_playbooks_to_v2.py; rotated token signing keys to use KMS and required token TTL.
- Dmitri Volkov (review): Requested stricter default canary percentage (changed to 1% -> 0.5% for high-sensitivity namespaces), and asked to add a safelist for low-risk namespaces.
  - Author response: Implemented per-namespace risk profiles with default 0.5% for high-risk, 5% for low-risk; added config file autopatch/config.yaml to house safelist.
- Nora Kim (approver): Asked for CI evidence showing integration test flakiness addressed; requested a follow-up task to add chaos tests.
  - Author response: Fixed a race in test harness (sleep -> event wait), re-ran CI and added a follow-up Linear task ENG-1401 to add chaos testing to the autopatch pipeline.

CI summary:
- Initial CI run: lint=pass, unit tests=pass, integration tests=fail (flaky harness race discovered), e2e=not run by default; fixed in branch with test harness change.
- Subsequent CI run: lint=pass, unit tests=pass, integration tests=pass, e2e=pass (local e2e in CI matrix), coverage maintained (no regression). All checks green at merge.

Backward compatibility & safety notes:
- Snapshots are versioned; the system can read v1 and v2. The new serializer defaults to v2 for exports but import path will accept v1 and v2.
- Autopatch defaults to dry-run for all users; production application requires explicit approval flow (two approvers for sensitive namespaces). Admins can opt in to relax policies per workspace.
- Migration script is opt-in and includes idempotent checkpoints and a dry-run reporting mode.

Performance impact:
- Snapshot size reduced ~30% on median playbook (measured across 1200 samples); serialization time reduced ~40% in benchmark harness.
- Autopatch runner adds minimal overhead during plan creation; execution path optimized to batch target updates where supported by downstream providers.

Follow-ups / future work:
- ENG-1401: add chaos/resilience tests for autopatch pipeline.
- ENG-1418: integrate snapshot diff view into the Console incident handoff UX.
- Explore signed snapshot exchange protocol for cross-team handoffs (design doc in docs/handbook).

Merge outcome: Squashed and merged to main on 2026-02-26 after approvals from Nora Kim and Dmitri Volkov. All CI checks passing at the time of merge.

Notes for release: This change is non-breaking by default; operators should review the migration tool before running it in production. Recommend announcing the autopatch feature to SRE teams with a runbook that documents approval flows and safelist configuration.
Adds compact playbook snapshot format for faster on-call handoffs; implements a gated autopatch runner (dry-run, canary, production with approval); exposes metrics for playbook serialization and autopatch attempts; includes migration tool to backfill legacy runbooks.

Add a compact quickstart demonstrating offline/co-authoring RAG workflows: a small sandbox that shows local index sync, CRDT-based patching for concurrent edits, and a lightweight websocket relay to simulate intermittent connectivity. The quickstart contains an authoring README, a TypeScript client that runs in the browser (with a node shim for local dev), a sample replay harness for deterministic evals, and docs site updates in the Authoring Lab section. The goal is to give developers an end-to-end example they can run locally and extend for collaborative retrieval-augmented features without requiring a managed backend. Includes tests and CI checks to verify replay determinism and index merge correctness.
Context and motivation: Teams building retrieval-augmented collaborative features often need an example showing how to combine a local/offline-first authoring experience with RAG-style retrieval and a deterministic replay pipeline for tests and evals. This quickstart provides a minimal sandbox that demonstrates: 1) how to keep a small local index (chunked documents) on the client and synchronise it to a replay-friendly store; 2) a CRDT-based patch/merge primitive to reconcile concurrent edits and index diffs without losing token-level provenance; 3) a lightweight relay that simulates flaky connectivity so developers can test sync/resume behaviour; and 4) a deterministic replay harness that replays recorded events to validate retrieval stability and prompt/eval regression.

What changed: Added quickstarts/coauthoring-offline with an opinionated README and runnable steps; a browser client (example-client.ts) that can run headless with the node-shim or directly in modern browsers; lib/crdt-merge.ts implementing a small operational transform/CRDT merge util with tests; lib/indexer.ts for incremental chunking and fingerprints; replay/harness.ts to record and replay sessions; unit and smoke e2e tests under tests/; and docs/authoring-lab/coauthoring-offline.md which integrates into the docs site and includes UX guidance and suggested telemetry probes.

Testing and CI: Unit tests cover CRDT merge edge cases and index delta application; the replay harness is used in an e2e smoke job that runs with a deterministic seed to verify identical final index state across runs. CI added docs-build step and a quick smoke pipeline.

Backwards compatibility: Non-breaking. The quickstart is additive and does not change platform APIs.

How to try locally (short): 1) git clone && cd quickstarts/coauthoring-offline 2) pnpm install && pnpm dev:relay 3) open browser-client/index.html or run pnpm dev:client-headless 4) run pnpm test to validate replay smoke. Full instructions are in the README.

Motivation: We need a deterministic, auditable way to produce tenant-scoped default policies (batching, cache presize, quant tiers) that can be serialized, reviewed, and deployed across Dedicated and Private. Current heuristics are ad-hoc and encoded in multiple places; this PR introduces a policy defaults serializer and a synthetic-profile prober that generates deterministic example workloads so defaults can be validated in CI and by SRE.

Summary of changes: Introduces a small policy DSL and a serializer that emits canonical JSON policy bundles for tenants; implements a synthetic-profile prober that runs against the sampler and prefill subsystems to produce a compact profile used to pick batch/cache/quant defaults; provides a CLI (redwoodctl defaults serialize/probe) and a small REST endpoint for the policy service for on-demand probes; hooks into the defaults-as-code import pipeline so product can review generated bundles before applying.

What this enables: 1) deterministic defaults generation for tenant onboarding; 2) CI validation of defaults via synthetic-profile replay; 3) easier code review of default policies as serialized artifacts; 4) ability to snapshot and roll back defaults in the tenant defaults registry.

Compatibility and rollout: Backwards-compatible. The serializer produces bundles that match the existing policy schema; we added a v2 mime-type for the new compact profile artifacts but the previous pipeline still accepts them. Rollout plan: feature flagged behind feature/defaults-serializer; will enable for a small set of tenants and run for 48h before gradual enabling.

Testing: Unit tests for serializer and parser (coverage added for edge cases where workloads have heavy streaming tokens), integration tests that run the prober against a local prefiller/sampler mock, and an e2e smoke that verifies the imported bundle deploys to a dedicated tenant and returns the expected recommended batch/cache/quant selection.

Checklist: - [x] Policy DSL and serializer implementation - [x] Synthetic-profile prober + deterministic seed - [x] redwoodctl CLI commands + docs snippet - [x] REST probe endpoint gated by feature flag - [x] Unit/integration/e2e tests - [x] Migration/compatibility checks and release notes

Notes: This PR purposely keeps the prober lightweight (synthetic workloads, not full traffic replay) to avoid production load. The serializer includes metadata (probe seed, runtime heuristics, timestamp) for traceability. Future follow-ups will add exportable diffs and a UI reviewer in Console.
Marco Diaz (2026-02-16): This looks promising. Two notes: 1) can we guarantee the prober never hits production GPUs directly? Should route to the sampler mock by default. 2) serializer metadata should include the Linear/issue reference for auditing.
Aisha Kapoor (2026-02-16): Reply: Prober defaults to the mock harness in non-prod and we added logic to require an explicit --target=prod flag to run against live runner (also gated by flag). Serializer now includes linked_linear in metadata.
Ellen Park (2026-02-17): Nit: CLI help text could call out expected output dir and example usage. Also add a small timeout to the REST probe so it doesn't block dev deploys.
Aisha Kapoor (2026-02-17): Reply: Added detailed examples in docs and set REST probe timeout to 5s with a config override. Updated tests to cover timeout path.
Jonah Miller (2026-02-20): Approved after small safety changes; verified unit tests and integration job are green. Please squash commits on merge.
CI Bot (2026-02-20): CI run passed (unit + integration + e2e smoke).
- Introduce policy defaults serializer (produces auditable tenant policy bundles)
- Add synthetic-profile prober for deterministic workload probing
- redwoodctl support for serialize/probe commands
- Feature-flagged REST probe endpoint (disabled by default)
Key risk: running prober against live runners can spike prefiller activity; feature flag and explicit target guard mitigate this. Please verify the feature flag rollout in the deployment plan before enabling for production tenants.
Serializer unit tests: 42 assertions. Prober deterministic replay: identical profiles across 10 runs with same seed. E2E smoke: imported bundle applied and returned expected recommended batch=16, cache_presize=256KB, quant_tier=Q4MICRO for the test tenant.

Motivation: RAG workflows frequently need bounded tool execution (APIs, search calls, indexers) to avoid tail latency and to keep user-facing interactions responsive. This quickstart introduces an 'adaptive timebox' pattern: a canonical playbook and lightweight local tool-runner adapters (Node + Python) that demonstrate per-step timeouts, backoff policies, and graceful fallback behaviours.

What this PR adds (high level):
- A compact quickstart under quickstarts/adaptive-timebox that documents the pattern, trade-offs and recipe for instrumenting tool calls inside an agent-orchestrator flow.
- Two minimal example runners: a Node TypeScript runner that integrates with the RAG step payloads and a Python shim for teams wanting a quick serverless/local prototyping path. Both show a unified configuration for step timeouts and a small retry policy.
- A docs site page (docs/quickstarts/rag-adaptive-timebox.md) with step-by-step instructions, recommended defaults for production and a checklist for telemetry + chaos tests.
- A CI smoke job (ci/smoke-rag-quickstarts.yml) that runs the example runner end-to-end in CI with deterministic fixtures.
- Telemetry probes (telemetry/probes/timebox-probe.yaml) and tracing snippets to help validate SLOs during local runs.

Checklist: 
- [x] Quickstart content and examples implemented
- [x] Smoke CI added and passing on branch
- [x] Telemetry probe + docs included
- [x] Small unit + integration smoke tests
- [x] Reviewed and approved by eng + docs

Commits summary: Init scaffold with README and example stubs; Add node runner adapter and tooling; Add python runner shim; Docs: quickstart page + troubleshooting; CI: smoke job and fixtures; Tests: add deterministic fixture harness.

Testing notes: Run the Node runner locally: node examples/node-runner/start.js --fixture fixtures/sample-session.json. The runner supports a --timebox-ms override to exercise fallback behaviors. CI runs the same harness inside a container. The smoke CI is intentionally minimal to be fast (~90s).

Operational guidance: Default timebox recommendations are documented in the quickstart (100ms for non-critical enrichment calls, 300-500ms for primary retrieval, 1s for slow external APIs depending on SLA). The playbook includes a prescriptive fallback ladder (cached result -> short-summary -> safe-decline).

Related work: ENG-2124 (adaptive routing prototype), DOC-87 (docs backlog item for tooling quickstarts). This complements ongoing RAG session replay and structured-output examples.

Why unique: There are many RAG quickstarts; this one focuses specifically on runtime guardrails for tool execution and provides tiny runnable adapters to make the pattern adoptable without a heavy infra lift.

Author (Leah): Added fixtures/sample-session.json and updated CI to mount it; CI green locally.
Sofia Nguyen: Suggest lowering default timebox to 300ms for primary retrieval and document rationale. Updated docs accordingly.
Martin Voss: Approved after minor lint fixes and confirming smoke CI runtime (approx 90s).
- Add RAG adaptive timebox quickstart with runnable Node and Python examples
- Include CI smoke job and telemetry probes for timebox validation
- Docs: recommended defaults and operational fallbacks for tool timeouts

Context: Developers asked for a compact quickstart demonstrating low-latency RAG patterns where incremental retrieval (delta sync) and streaming deltas to the client reduce token costs and improve editor-like UX. This PR adds a new quickstart that wires: 1) a small TypeScript server that accepts query sessions and exposes a websocket delta-sync channel, 2) a minimal dev 'Replay Inspector' web UI that visualizes incoming retrieval deltas and embedding deltas, and 3) typed tool-contract stubs, a smoke e2e replay harness, and CI checks. Motivation: Many teams prototype RAG with full re-runs per message. For editor/assistant flows this causes repetitive retrieval and KV-work; delta-sync keeps KV/embedding state incremental and makes prefix caching obvious to engineers. The quickstart is intended as:
- Fast onboarding: clone, docker-compose up (or npm run dev)
- Clear examples: server stream -> client browser inspector -> replay harness
- Diagnostic-first: inspector surfaces retrieval hits, embedding similarity traces, and token/latency counters
Checklist: [x] add websocket delta-sync server and client library samples [x] add dev inspector UI and telemetry probes [x] add typed TS tool-contracts and schema examples [x] add CI smoke e2e & lint [x] document runbook and architecture diagram [x] add replay harness to reproduce incidents
How to run locally: 1) cd quickstarts/delta-sync 2) npm ci && npm run build 3) npm run start:dev (starts server + indexer) 4) open dev-inspector at http://localhost:8080 and connect a session 5) run examples/replay-harness to emit recorded user steps
Notes on design decisions:
- Websocket channel carries small JSON 'deltas' (retrieval-add, cache-hit, embedding-update, token-chunk) to keep messages idempotent and replayable.
- The indexer in this quickstart is intentionally in-process and keyed for clarity; production users should swap in Redwood's offline indexer or a managed vector DB.
- Typed tool-contracts are provided to show how structured tool-calling can interleave with deltas (see typed-contracts/tool-contracts.ts).
Related Linear: ["ENG-3412", "ENG-3480"]. Related docs: docs/devguides/delta-sync.md. Migration notes: no breaking API changes in Redwood; this is an additive set of samples and docs.
Liam Ortega: Nice compact design. Can we keep the delta protocol backwards-compatible by namespacing message types? Suggest prefixing types with 'rdw.' - addressed in commit 'protocol: namespace delta types'
Priya Rao: Dev inspector is very helpful; recommend adding a toggle to show only retrieval hits to reduce noise - added UI toggle and unit test
Owen Fitzgerald: Replay harness should seed a deterministic index to make CI stable; moved fixtures into examples/replay-harness/fixtures and added deterministic RNG
Maya Chen (author): responded with implementation notes and pushed fixes; addressed all review comments and asked for final pass
Priya Rao: Approved after fixes
Added 'delta-sync' quickstart demonstrating websocket-based incremental retrieval and a Replay Inspector developer UI. Includes typed tool-contract examples and a replay harness for deterministic e2e smoke tests. Useful for prototyping low-latency RAG flows and debugging retrieval/embedding behavior.
