payload.body:
Context: Customers running mixed-tenancy workloads asked for safer, automated defaults that trade unit cost for predictable SLOs. Existing autotuners target single knobs (batch size, quant) but do not reason jointly about tenant budget constraints, multi-shape request distributions, or cache warmup behavior. This PR introduces the 'economy navigator' — a small runtime planner + CLI that (1) surfaces tenant-level unit-econ constraints, (2) selects a microbatch lane for low-latency hot paths, and (3) generates candidate quantization footprints constrained by budget and acceptable delta in quality. Motivation: reduce operator effort and avoid blunt defaults that either overspend or risk regressions when quantization is too aggressive. What this change does: - Add a new microbatch lane type (CompactMicroLane) that enforces a tight max-batch-size and short stall-window; intended for latency-sensitive, low-token requests. - Implement a quant-footprint prescriptor that takes workload heatmap + quality budget and returns 1..3 candidate quant profiles (e.g., int8-llm, int4-hybrid with kv-preserve) with estimated token-cost and simulated quality delta. - New rwctl econ simulate and rwctl econ apply commands for dry-run and controlled rollout of suggested defaults across tenants. - Integrates with telemetry: emits econ.choice.*, econ.sim.* and ties suggestions to per-route SLO and token-cost metrics to enable dashboarding and alerts. - Safe rollout: suggestions are annotated with a safety_score; the runtime will only apply profiles when safety_score >= 0.7 for automated rollouts; otherwise suggestions land in the Console as a recommendation. - Unit-econ linter for CI that runs sample traces against the prescriptor and flags >10% cost regressions for routes marked 'budget-sensitive'. Key implementation notes: - The prescriptor is implemented under pkg/quant/prescriptor.go and uses a small heuristic solver that models cache-hit amplification and batch shaping. - Micro-lane is implemented under pkg/batcher/micro_lane.go and plugged into the dispatcher with a new lane selector that prefers CompactMicroLane for requests matching route_annotations: { "micro_latency": true }. - CLI changes under cmd/rwctl/econ.go with a dry-run mode that emits a JSON report and a human-readable suggestion table. - Telemetry hooks: telemetry/econ.go and metrics/registry additions. Testing: - Unit tests for prescriptor heuristics and microlane behavior (pkg/quant/*_test.go, pkg/batcher/*_test.go). - Integration in the e2e perf suite with synthetic mixed-shape workload to estimate cost delta and latency tails. - Manual validation against customer traces supplied in ENG-4789 (sanitized). Rollout plan: merged to main, gated by a feature flag fleet.econ.navigator. Fleet enablement will be gradual: first internal canary, then opt-in tenants, then automated suggestions for eligible tenants. Backout path: rwctl econ rollback and runtime checks will revert to previous quant profiles if latency or quality regress above configured thresholds. Related: builds on research prototypes from ENG-4920. Impact: provides automated, conservative defaults that lower unit costs for many mixed workloads while keeping safety gates to prevent user-visible regressions.
Miguel Torres: 'Nice decomposition. Two asks: can prescriptor include a simple guard for known-distortion-sensitive models (e.g., embeddings) and can the CLI output a machine-readable fingerprint so audits can track applied presets?'
Asha Patel: 'Added model-sensitivity whitelist and a fingerprint hash in the dry-run JSON output. See prescriptor.go lines ~120-150.'
Sophie Nguyen: 'Performance tests look good but please add a stress test for KV cache preservation when int4 hybrid is suggested.'
Asha Patel: 'Added a synthetic KV-heavy workload trace to the perf suite and an assertion to ensure >95% KV hit rates remain after suggestion application.'
Evan Brooks: 'Approve after addressing minor lint and documenting the feature-flag.'
Asha Patel: 'Addressed lint and added feature-flag docs. Squash-merged.'
Adds the 'economy navigator' feature: a conservative suggestion engine that proposes microbatch lanes and constrained quant profiles per-tenant. Includes rwctl econ CLI for dry-run and apply, telemetry for tracking suggestions, and CI linter to catch large cost regressions. Feature gated behind fleet.econ.navigator.
payload.title: Introduce econ-navigator microbatch lanes and quant-footprint prescriptor

payload.body:
Motivation: Private installs suffer from noisy preflight failures and brittle init hooks when tenants have heterogeneous network/topology constraints. This PR adds a small adaptive preflight framework plus a lightweight overlay mechanism for hook templates so operators can tune preflight probes and init-wave sequencing per-tenant without duplicating charts. Approach summary: 1) Add charts/private/values.schema.json extensions to validate overlay sections and per-tenant probe profiles; 2) Introduce charts/private/templates/hooks/_overlay.tpl and plumbing to render overlay parameters into existing init hook templates; 3) Implement an adaptive preflight controller stub (preflight probe CR template + explanatory README) that supports exponential backoff and a permissive-fallback mode; 4) Add values.example.yaml with tenantSandboxing and initWaveOrder examples; 5) Add helm-level unit/integration tests and a short upgrade script. Compatibility & safety: All new values are optional and default to current behavior; the overlay template is guarded by a feature flag values.private.init.enableOverlay=false by default. Migration: chart will accept existing values unchanged; operators who want per-tenant tuning can populate values.private.init.overlays.<tenant> entries as documented. Rollout plan: ship to Canary (dedicated) then gradual rollout to >=3 customer clusters before marking GA. Testing & validation: helm lint and unit tests added; integration job exercises three overlay permutations. Follow-ups: wire the adaptive controller into private-installer controller and add a metrics export for preflight probe histograms (tracked ENG-9021).
Luca Nguyen: Can we keep the default probe windows identical to current chart to avoid accidental regressions? I suggest explicit defaults in values.schema.json.
Author (Aisha Patel): Done, defaults added to values.schema.json and values.example.yaml. Kept feature flag disabled by default.
Priya Shah: The overlay logic looks sound but please add a unit test for template rendering when overlay contains unknown keys.
Author (Aisha Patel): Added a negative unit test that asserts unknown overlay fields are ignored with a lint warning, included in preflight-integration.test.sh.
Martin O'Connell: Integration flake observed on first CI run for slow clusters; recommend a retry wrapper around the helm test. Approved after CI rerun.
Introduce optional tenant-scoped hook overlay parameters to tune init jobs per-tenant
Add adaptive preflight probe template with backoff and permissive fallback mode
Values schema extended with tenantSandboxing and initWaveOrder examples
No behaviour change by default; feature gated behind values.private.init.enableOverlay=false
This release is backward-compatible. To enable per-tenant overlays populate values.private.init.overlays with tenant keys. See charts/private/values.example.yaml for examples. If you upgrade from a chart older than 2025-07 ensure your CI does not rely on implicit timing assumptions during init; recommended to run 'helm upgrade --install --dry-run' and then apply the preflight probe CR as described in README-upgrade.md.
1) Merge to main and publish chart-rc to Canary registry. 2) Deploy Canary to one dedicated customer cluster and monitor preflight probe metrics for 48h. 3) If stable, enable overlay in 2 additional clusters and run integration tests. 4) Promote to stable in 7 days after zero regressions. Rollback: revert values.private.init.enableOverlay or roll back chart revision via helm rollback.

payload.body:
Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private reported upgrade stalls when per-tenant migration jobs collide with init hooks during rolling upgrades. This PR provides a safer default by adding a deferred migration operator (helm-templated job + controller-side knob) and richer hook templating so operators can express priority and maintenance windows.

Goals: 1) allow tenant migrations to be scheduled after the critical init hooks finish and cluster stabilizes; 2) give Helm values to configure tenant probe templates so health checks are tenant-aware (namespace, annotation-based overrides); 3) introduce hook-priority annotations and sequencer helpers to order non-deterministic init jobs without hardcoding names.

What changed (high level):
- New templates/ deferred-migration/ operator-job.yaml: templated Job + RBAC snippets that are idempotent and keyed to tenant labels. Controlled by values.deferredMigration.enabled and values.deferredMigration.window.
- templates/_hook_helpers.tpl: added helper functions `hookPriority` and `maintenanceWindow` for composing annotations on jobs and cronjobs.
- values.schema.json: extended schema with `deferredMigration`, `tenantProbes`, and `hookPriority` sections; schema includes validation for cron expressions and duration strings.
- templates/tenant-probe.yaml: tenant-aware liveness/readiness probe templates with optional annotation overrides and nodeAffinity suggestions for on-prem node pools.
- NOTES.txt and values.example.yaml: documented operators on how to enable safe migrations and recommended window defaults for large clusters.

Files changed (illustrative):
- templates/deferred-migration/operator-job.yaml (+220 additions)
- templates/_hook_helpers.tpl (+48 additions)
- templates/tenant-probe.yaml (+120 additions)
- values.schema.json (+75 additions)
- values.example.yaml (+80 additions)
- charts/README.md (+12 additions)
- tests/helm/unit/deferred_migration_test.yaml (+40 additions)
- ci/helm-lint.yaml (updated to include schema validation)
- templates/NOTES.txt (+17 additions)

Commits:
- 7f3c1d0: add deferred migration operator and RBAC; initial tests
- 93b7a42: introduce hookPriority helper and annotation format docs
- a1e5bf0: add tenant probe templates and nodeAffinity knobs
- b4c2e88: extend values.schema.json and values.example.yaml; update helm-lint CI
- d2f909f: tweak templates after reviewer feedback; fix idempotency on Job names

Design notes:
- Deferred migration operator is intentionally thin: it's a templated Job that can optionally be deployed as a CronJob by operators. We expect larger installations to replace the Job with a controller (outside this chart) that watches for values.deferredMigration.enabled. The Job includes a guard that checks for `redwood.io/upgrade-in-progress` namespace annotation and respects `values.deferredMigration.window` before starting migrations.
- hookPriority uses numeric annotation `redwood.io/hook-priority` (0-100) to allow sequenced processing by init orchestrators; lower numbers run first. These values are advisory; chart consumers can implement leader-election watchers to enforce strict ordering.
- tenantProbes are rendered per-tenant via `{{ .Values.tenantProbes.template }}` and support annotation-based overrides so cluster-operators can opt into shorter probe timeouts for canary tenants.

Testing and CI:
- Added unit-style helm tests that render templates with different values sets: single-tenant, multi-tenant, and maintenance-window scenarios.
- CI changes: helm lint now runs schema validation; one flaky test (helm/render:deferred-migration job name collision) failed on first run; rerun succeeded. Integration tests run in the private CI pool where on-prem nodeAffinity examples are validated.

Security consideration: RBAC rules for the Job are minimal (Jobs can list/watch migrations in their tenant namespace only). Docs highlight that operators should run deferred-migration Job in a management namespace with cross-namespace RBAC if they want cluster-scoped migration orchestration.

Migration notes for operators:
- Default behavior unchanged. To enable: set values.deferredMigration.enabled=true and optionally tune values.deferredMigration.window (RFC3339 duration-like string).
- You can opt to render the Job as a CronJob by setting values.deferredMigration.cron="0 2 * * *" which will cause periodic non-blocking migration runs during off-hours.

Request for reviewers: please check the schema validation coverage and RBAC scope. Special ask to SRE: review the recommended default `window` value for clusters with >100 tenants.

Review conversation (high level):
- Jonas Park (reviewer): "Can the Job avoid naming collisions if multiple tenants request overlapping migrations?"
- Maya Kline (author): "Yes — Job name now includes tenant hash and a stable prefix; added tests to assert name length and uniqueness. See commit d2f909f."
- Arun Patel (reviewer): "We should not implicitly change nodeAffinity; operators must opt-in."
- Maya: "Agreed — nodeAffinity is off by default and the example shows how to enable it per-tenant. Updated values.example.yaml."
- Noah Chen (approver): "Schema looks good; validated helm lint locally. Approving pending CI pass."
- CI: first run failed a flaky render test; rerun passed.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after approvals and green CI. Backported as a non-breaking patch to the 1.12.x maintenance release in a follow-up PR (not included here).

Notes for docs/ops: follow-up PR planned to add an operator-runbook that shows recommended maintenance windows for different cluster sizes and how to integrate with cluster schedulers (K8s CronJob vs external controller).

Related work: addresses part of ENG-8421 (upgrade resiliency) and ENG-8473 (tenant-level observability). Also referenced in SUP-1297 where customer reported upgrade hang causing P0 incident.

Testing commands used locally: helm template ./charts/redwood-private -f values.example.yaml --set deferredMigration.enabled=true | kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f -

If any follow-ups are requested I will open small focused PRs: (1) chart-provided controller scaffolding; (2) runbook + examples for migrating existing clusters; (3) installer option to toggle render-as-cronjob during bootstrap.

Adds optional deferred migration operator to make tenant migrations non-blocking during upgrade windows; introduces configurable tenant-level liveness/ready probe templates and hook-priority annotations. No default behavior change unless values.enableDeferredMigration=true.
Added deferred migration Job templates, hook-priority helpers, tenant-level probe templates, and extended values.schema.json to validate maintenance windows and hook priorities.
This PR was intentionally authored as a minimal-behavior change with opt-in features. The deferral path is designed so operators can enable it per-customer without changing core upgrade semantics.
payload.title: introduce deferred-migration operator, tenant-level health probes, and hook-priority templates

payload.body:
Adds a deployment conductor that supports timeboxed experiments, enforceable latency budgets and automatic failover/rollback when experiment SLAs are violated. Backwards compatible with existing rollout CRDs; console gets a new 'Experiments' tab.
Summary: Adds a new controller component (deployment-conductor) and supporting CRD fields to enable timeboxed, SLA-driven experiments for model rollouts. The conductor coordinates A/B and shadow experiments that are bounded by a wall-clock duration and enforce safe failover when latency or error budgets are exceeded. Motivation: teams running short-lived experiments (e.g., 15m promos, timed feature flags, limited traffic load tests) need deterministic, auditable experiments that automatically stop or rollback when their SLOs degrade. Existing rollout controllers support progressive percentages and metric gates but lack a compact primitive for timeboxed experiments with a unified failover policy. Design: - New CRD field: experiment.window {duration, traffic_fraction, latency_budget_ms, error_rate_threshold, aggressive_failover:boolean, postmortem_tag} - DeploymentConductor: watches Rollout CRs and Experiment sub-specs, creates ephemeral TrafficMirror/Shadow resources, enforces traffic caps, and sets timers for window expiration. - SLA enforcement: conductor samples P99 and tail error rates from the observability plugin and triggers immediate failover/rollback if observed metrics cross configured thresholds for more than 2 consecutive buckets. - Safe state transitions: conductor implements a three-state lifecycle: Scheduled -> Running -> Concluded (Succeeded|Failed|TimedOut). If 'aggressive_failover' is true, the conductor will cut traffic to the experiment target and route to the primary model immediately on fail; otherwise it will reduce by half and observe for a cooldown period. - Audit & observability: conductor emits ExperimentEvents and annotates the rollout trace with experiment_id and reason codes. Console adds an Experiments timeline for quick debugging. Compatibility and migration: existing Rollout CRs are not affected. New optional Experiment fields are ignored by older controllers. The system defaults to passive mode until experiment fields are present. Implementation notes and files changed (high level): - cmd/deployment-conductor/main.go: new binary + health, leader election, config parsing. - api/v1alpha1/rollout_types.go: experiment window fields and validation webhooks. - controllers/experiment_controller.go: core logic (scheduling, timer, metric sampling, enforcement). - internal/metrics/sampler.go: bucketed sampling used for SLA checks. - observability/events.go: experiment event types and wire format. - ui/src/experiments/ExperimentsPanel.tsx: front-end timeline and controls (feature-flag gated). - e2e/experiments/timeboxed_flow.test.ts: integration harness simulating latency regressions and ensuring rollback triggers. - charts/deployment-conductor/Chart.yaml + values.yaml: helm addition for Private/Dedicated deployments. Commits (summary): - feat: scaffold deployment-conductor binary and basic reconcile loop - feat: add Experiment window CRD and validation - feat: implement sampling and SLA check pipeline - feat: console UI for experiments (feature-flag controlled) - test: e2e timeboxed experiment flows with injected latency - docs: rollout guide and API reference for experiment window - fix: tighten leader-election to avoid double-schedule in HA clusters Highlights of important diffs (small illustrative snippets): - api/v1alpha1/rollout_types.go added: `ExperimentWindow struct { Duration string `json:"duration"` TrafficFraction float32 `json:"trafficFraction"` LatencyBudgetMs int `json:"latencyBudgetMs"` ErrorRateThreshold float32 `json:"errorRateThreshold"` AggressiveFailover bool `json:"aggressiveFailover"` }` - controllers/experiment_controller.go: sampling loop pseudocode included in comments for reviewer clarity. Testing and CI: - Unit tests for sampler and decision logic added. - Integration test simulates a P99 spike and asserts rollback within the configured budget window. - Flaky test: e2e/experiments/timeboxed_flow.test.ts occasionally failed when the fake-metrics-server experienced a race; CI rerun passed. Review conversation (selected threads): - Liam O'Connor (reviewer): "Can we make the default cooldown window configurable cluster-wide rather than baked into the controller?" - Asha (author): "Added a top-level config value `experiment.cooldown_seconds` with a sensible default (60s). Documented in helm `values.yaml`." - Chen Li: "Sampling logic looks tight; verify memory use of sampler under high cardinality." - Asha: "Sampler uses fixed-size ring buffers per sample key (bounded by `sampler.max_keys` in config). Added tests to ensure GC behavior. See internal/metrics/sampler_test.go." - Morgan Reyes: "What guarantees do we provide for exactly-once scheduling in HA?" - Asha: "Leader election is enforced via the controller-runtime leader election built-in. I also added a lightweight scheduler lock in etcd (namespace-scoped) as a safety net if multiple controllers briefly think they're leader under partition. See controllers/scheduler_lock.go." - Reviewer approval flow: After two rounds of feedback (mainly configuration surface reductions and doc clarifications) Chen Li and Liam O'Connor approved. Motivation: Private deployments require flexible, composable preflight checks and safer migration/upgrade hooks that work across VPC and air-gapped on-prem installs. Current init hooks are monolithic for tenant bootstrap and make it hard to add environment-specific probes (e.g. restricted networks) without forking charts. This PR introduces a layered overlay approach to preflight and migration hook templates that (1) lets ops compose probes per-deployment, (2) surfaces a portable probe helper for air-gapped environments, and (3) adds a dry-run migration mode and safer rollback fence to reduce upgrade blast radius.

Summary of changes: added a new values overlay section (values.preflight.overlays) that composes a sequence of overlay fragments. Each fragment can inject templated initJobs, probeConfig, nodeAffinity/taints, and mount overlays. Introduced chart helpers/_probe-helpers.tpl and _overlay-merge.tpl to keep templates DRY; helper supports kube-probe wrapper for environments without external curl/hostnames. Added migration-hooks/migrate-dryrun Job template and a migration-fence-configmap that records migration phases for rollback safety. New values schema (values.schema.json) includes schema for overlays, minimumProbeConfig, and a new preflight.enabled flag.

Backward compatibility and safety: Default behavior is unchanged unless values.preflight.enableOverlay is set. Migration dry-run is opt-in via values.migration.dryRun=true. Hook templates include weightedHook annotations (hook-weight) and a preflight.gateConfig to allow orchestrators to gate upgrades (e.g. via private-installer controller). We added a feature toggle values.preflight.usePortableProbes to switch to the portable probe image for air-gapped installs.

Testing and rollout: unit/template tests added under templates/tests/preflight-overlay-test.yaml and a set of k8s manifest samples in examples/preflight-overlays/ that demonstrate tenant-mapping overlay (multi-tenant nodeAffinity), bare-metal probe (hostpath) and an airgapped scenario. CI runs lint, template unit-tests and smoke integration against KinD. We manually exercised a staged rollout in our staging cluster (redwood-staging) using canary releases and verified that the migration-dryrun writes the expected fence keys and does not mutate tenant data.

Docs and next steps: updated docs/helm/private/preflight.md with examples and recommended overlays for VPC vs on-prem. Filed a followup to add a private-installer controller hook to read gateConfig and coordinate tenant waves (ENG-15948). Also opened a small PR in redwood-private-installer to consume values.preflight.overlays by name.

Related: ENG-15932 (preflight overhaul), ENG-15948 (installer orchestration), SUP-983 (customer onprem upgrade fallout), and a docs task PM-4321.
Luca Moretti: Can we keep the default probe image unchanged for hosted deployments? I don't want change to leak into hosted path. -> Author: yes, the portable probe image is opt-in (preflight.usePortableProbes=false by default).
Nina Patel: The overlay merge logic looks complex; can we add more unit tests for conflicting keys? -> Author: added conflict-resolution tests and documented that later fragments override earlier ones, plus a validation precheck in values.schema.json.
Jorge Alvarez: Will migration-fence affect rollback time? We need to ensure small windows. -> Author: fence is a small ConfigMap write; documented expected latency and added retries/backoff to the hook template.

Motivation: Private installs (VPC/on-prem) have seen intermittent resource contention during tenant bootstrap and migration waves: dozens of init jobs and migration hooks spike API and storage load after upgrades. This PR introduces a lightweight, chart-driven quota and throttling facility for init/migration hooks plus templated hook wrappers so operators can opt into safe rollout pacing without modifying existing CI/orchestration.

Summary of changes: Introduce two complementary primitives in values.yaml and templates: 1) hookQuota: a declarative per-namespace limit for concurrent hook jobs (defaults to disabled to preserve backward compatibility). When enabled the chart renders a small controllerJob (CronJob-compatible) which acts as a leader-aware admission gate for init hooks. 2) initThrottle: a per-hook annotation + global chart setting to add a coordinated delay/slot allocation for heavy migration/seed jobs. 3) a templated hook wrapper (templates/hook-wrapper.yaml) that standardizes exit codes, idempotency annotations, and integrates with initThrottle slots. 4) values schema updates (values.schema.json) with strict type checks and allowed ranges and documentation.

Why this approach: We considered a full operator but chose a chart-first, opt-in controller to keep air-gapped installs simple. The wrapper is a minimal shim that can be used by existing hooks with a one-line change to the hook Job spec. The controller uses only RBAC and a ConfigMap-backed token ring so it remains lightweight for on-prem clusters.

What changed (high level): commits, templates, and docs. Key templates added: templates/hook-wrapper.yaml, templates/hook-quota-controller-deploy.yaml, templates/hook-quota-rbac.yaml, templates/_helpers.tpl (new helpers for annotations). values.yaml additions and values.schema.json schema expanded. README and docs/upgrade-notes.md updated with migration instructions and examples.

Migration notes and backwards compatibility: Default values keep previous behavior (quota disabled, throttle disabled). To opt-in operators set values.private.hookQuota.enabled: true and configure per-namespace quotas. A migration helper script (scripts/generate-quota-config.sh) is included to derive quotas from cluster capacity metrics free-form; this is provided as an optional utility for large fleets.

Checklist:
- [x] Values schema and chart linting
- [x] Unit-yaml rendering tests (helm template) across Kubernetes 1.21-1.27
- [x] Load-smoke test of quota controller in perf-canary cluster
- [x] Docs and upgrade notes
- [x] Add e2e gating to canary pipeline (follow-up pipeline change in perf-canary repo)

Commits (summary):
- Add hook quota controller deployment and RBAC, basic leader lock implementation
- Add hook-wrapper template and helper macros for deterministic annotations
- Expand values.schema.json with hookQuota and initThrottle sections and validation rules
- Add scripts/generate-quota-config.sh helper and README example
- Docs: upgrade-notes and example values for multi-tenant on-prem clusters
- Tests: add helm template smoke and basic rendering unit tests

Changed files (high level):
- values.schema.json (expanded)
- values.yaml (new options + docs)
- templates/hook-wrapper.yaml (new)
- templates/hook-quota-controller-deploy.yaml (new)
- templates/hook-quota-rbac.yaml (new)
- templates/_helpers.tpl (new helper funcs)
- charts/README.md (docs snippet)
- docs/upgrade-notes.md (new section)
- scripts/generate-quota-config.sh (new utility)
- tests/render-tests/hook-quota-values.yaml (new test fixture)

Example values snippet (in chart values.yaml):
private:
  hookQuota:
    enabled: false # disable by default, enable to gate init hooks per-namespace
    defaultConcurrent: 5 # max concurrent init hook Jobs per namespace
    namespaceOverrides:
      "tenant-a": 2
  initThrottle:
    enabled: false
    defaultSlotDelaySeconds: 6
    maxStaggerSeconds: 300

Review conversation (high level):
- Jonas Park: Asked for a plan to ensure the controller cannot become a single-point-of-failure. Resolution: added leader election (ConfigMap lock) and a no-op fallback that allows hooks to run after X minutes if controller unresponsive (configurable via hookQuota.unblockAfterSeconds).
- Marta Liu: Requested stricter schema validation for negative numbers and upper bounds. Resolution: added min/max bounds in values.schema.json and unit tests for invalid values.
- Evan Cho: Ran perf-canary with a synthetic tenant wave and reported a 42% reduction in API server QPS spike. Requested a small change to default delays; changed defaultSlotDelaySeconds from 10 -> 6 after discussion.
- CI bot: Initially flagged lint failure for long helper names, fixed by shortening template helper IDs and adding comments.

CI summary: GitHub Actions helm-lint, kubeval, and chart-testing passed after two iterations. Perf-canary job passed on the second run (first run had a flaky cluster provisioning issue unrelated to code).

Rollout and merge: Merged via squash on main. Ops follow-up: perf-canary pipeline will be updated to include the optional e2e scenario that enables private.hookQuota for one canary tenant (refer ENG-8214 follow-up). The feature is gated behind chart values so existing private installs are unaffected until operators opt in.

Notes for operators: See docs/upgrade-notes.md for example values and an FAQ on how to choose defaultConcurrent and unblockAfterSeconds. The helper script is intentionally non-opinionated: run it offline to generate per-namespace suggestions and validate against values.schema.json before applying.
Adds configurable hook quotas and an init-job concurrency throttle to the private Helm chart to reduce rollout-induced cluster contention; defaults preserve existing behaviour
Jonas: How do we avoid the quota controller becoming a single point of failure? Added leader election + unblock fallback.
Marta: schema allowed negative numbers in some paths. Fixed with min: 0 and tests.
Evan: observed improvement in perf-canary, requested smaller default slot delay. Adjusted to 6s.
CI bot: lint failures for helper name length; shortened helpers and added docstring comments.

Motivation: on air-gapped and multi-operator installs we observed multiple init/postupgrade hooks racing which caused duplicate migrations and transient secret reconciliation failures. This PR introduces a lightweight leader-elector pattern for Helm hook jobs, a checksum-based idempotency guard to short-circuit unchanged runs, and a configurable migration dry-run mode intended for safer private upgrades. Summary of changes: 1) templates/_hook_helpers.tpl - new leaderElector macro and checksum helpers; 2) templates/checksum-configmap.yaml - create a stable configmap with a computed checksum footprint for user-supplied migration/config; 3) templates/init-job.yaml and templates/migration-job.yaml - use leader election annotation and skip when checksum matches; 4) values.schema.json and values.yaml - add migrate.dryRun, hooks.leaderElector.enabled, hooks.leaderElector.lockTTL, hooks.checksum.enabled and externalLoadBalancer.annotations passthrough; 5) tests/integration/migration-dryrun.sh - CI integration test that validates dry-run no-op behavior. Design notes: leader-elector is implemented as a conservative ConfigMap-based lock annotation (no extra controller) so it works in air-gapped clusters without additional CRDs; lock TTL is configurable and defaults to 10m to avoid long stuck locks in failed runs. Checksum logic ties to a canonical set of keys (config, secrets, job templates) so trivial template re-renders do not re-trigger heavy migrations. The migrate.dryRun flag runs schema validation and a noop path for database migrations and reports a JSON summary to stdout for operator review. Testing and rollout: unit and chart-lint added; integration migration-dryrun test runs in CI; deployment plan is to enable the feature behind values defaults (leaderElector.enabled = true, migrate.dryRun = false) and rollout to internal canary clusters first. Backwards compatibility: all hooks remain functional if feature flags are disabled. See linked Linear tickets for rollout and post-merge follow-ups.
Ava Chen: Overall looks good — appreciate the conservative leader-elector approach. Please add a small unit template test to validate the ConfigMap lock keys and TTL logic.
Diego Morales: Added unit snapshot in tests/templates/leader-elector.test.yaml and a short explanation in the helmsman test harness. PTAL.
Lina Kaur: Can we make the default lockTTL shorter (e.g. 5m) for faster recovery in CI? Also request explicit ownerReferences on the checksum ConfigMap to avoid orphaned objects during uninstall.
Diego Morales: Lowered default to 10m after discussion (tradeoff for long-running migrations). Added ownerReferences when running under helm controller mode; documented behavior in README.
Marcus Lee: Integration test failure on first CI run showed a race condition — job pod started before lock ConfigMap was observed. Suggest adding a short readiness wait loop in the job entrypoint when leaderElector.enabled=true.
Diego Morales: Added a 3s backoff loop and retried CI. All checks green now. Marking as ready to merge.
Ava Chen: Approved. Verified manual canary on internal cluster and migration dry-run produced expected no-op logs.

Summary: This PR adds first-class Helm values to pin the active Optimization Config version for Redwood Private installs and documents an operator-friendly rollback flow (pin to prior version + apply). Motivation: In Hosted/Dedicated, the control plane manages versioning and rollback; for Private, operators need a deterministic way to (a) hold a known-good version during upgrades and (b) roll back quickly when an optimization change causes a latency/5xx regression. This change introduces an explicit chart-level mechanism to pass the pinned version to the control plane/runtime, making the procedure consistent with the Safe Apply + Rollback project. What’s included: (1) New values: optimize.optimizationConfig.versionPin (string, optional) and optimize.optimizationConfig.allowUnpinned (bool, default true). When versionPin is set, the deployment will request that version from the Optimization Config Service and treat it as the active version for the configured scope. (2) Templating: inject OPTIMIZATION_CONFIG_VERSION_PIN and OPTIMIZATION_CONFIG_ALLOW_UNPINNED into the control-plane and runtime components; add checksum annotations so updating values triggers rollouts. (3) Validation: fail chart rendering when versionPin is set but empty/whitespace; add a warning note in NOTES.txt when allowUnpinned=false and no pin is supplied. (4) Docs: add a dedicated “Rollback optimization config” section with a copy-paste example (helm upgrade --set optimize.optimizationConfig.versionPin=<prior_version>) and post-rollback verification steps (check rollout status, confirm config_version tag on metrics, confirm p95 recovery). Backwards compatibility: Existing installs that do not set versionPin behave as before (control plane uses the currently-promoted version / unpinned resolution). No changes to defaults that would impact current clusters. Testing: helm lint, helm template, and a minimal kind-based smoke deploy in CI to ensure env vars are present and rollouts happen on pin changes. Follow-ups: (a) In a separate PR we can add a small “pin status” panel to the Private operator docs to align with Console wording, (b) add a values.schema.json pattern restriction once we finalize the canonical version ID format (currently treated as opaque string).
Vivek Kulkarni: Can we make sure updating versionPin forces a rollout? We’ve been burned by config-only changes not triggering new pods. Bruno Silva: Added checksum annotation keyed off the rendered env var values; confirmed that helm upgrade changes ReplicaSet hash. Ethan Park: Naming question—can we avoid calling it “activeVersion” since runtime semantics treat it as a pin override rather than a promotion? Bruno Silva: Renamed to optimize.optimizationConfig.versionPin and updated docs to call it “pin”; promotion remains a control-plane concept. Kira Thompson: The rollback docs should include a clear verification checklist and mention where to look for the applied version. Bruno Silva: Added steps: kubectl describe pod env var, check metrics tag config_version, and validate p95/5xx stabilization window. Connor O'Brien: CI failed on the first run due to values.schema.json indentation; please rerun once fixed. Bruno Silva: Fixed schema formatting, re-ran CI, all green. Approvals: Vivek Kulkarni approved; Ethan Park approved; Kira Thompson approved; Connor O’Brien approved with note to reference GA checklist doc in follow-up.
Private (Helm): Operators can pin an Optimization Config version via values to support safe rollback and deterministic behavior during upgrades.
Docs: Added rollback procedure and verification checklist for optimization config changes.

payload.body:
## Summary
Adds a new Helm chart `node-validation-agent` that deploys the Provision-to-Ready node validation agent as a DaemonSet.

This chart is used by Fleet automation to run post-provision validation gates on GPU worker nodes before they are marked `Ready` in the control plane.

Key features:
- DaemonSet deployment with sane defaults for GPU nodes (tolerations/nodeSelector/priorityClass)
- Least-privilege RBAC (read-only access to Node + Events; optional Lease for heartbeat)
- Resource requests/limits and safe pod security context
- Configurable validation checks (enable/disable + per-check timeouts) via ConfigMap
- Optional OTLP export (disabled by default) + structured logs to stdout

## Why
Provision-to-ready automation needs a consistent, repeatable way to run the same validations on every node across regions and GPU SKUs. Shipping the agent as a chart lets us:
- pin versions alongside cluster config
- roll out by region/pool with existing Helm pipelines
- standardize security posture and RBAC

## What’s included
### Chart
- `charts/node-validation-agent/Chart.yaml`
- `charts/node-validation-agent/values.yaml`
- `charts/node-validation-agent/templates/{daemonset,serviceaccount,rbac,configmap}.yaml`
- `values.schema.json` for basic validation

### Default checks
Defaults are conservative (fast + actionable). NCCL smoke test remains off by default for now (flake tuning in progress).

Enabled by default:
- `gpu_health` (ECC/Xid scan, basic CUDA device enumeration)
- `driver_parity` (driver/CUDA/NCCL versions vs expected matrix)
- `network_smoke` (MTU + basic throughput probe to same-AZ endpoint)
- `storage_smoke` (disk layout + minimal IOPS sanity)
- `runtime_smoke` (container runtime + nvidia runtime presence)

Disabled by default:
- `nccl_smoke` (can be enabled per pool/region)

## Values (highlights)
```yaml
image:
  repository: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/node-validation-agent
  tag: "0.6.0"
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent

agent:
  checks:
    gpu_health:
      enabled: true
      timeoutSeconds: 60
    driver_parity:
      enabled: true
      timeoutSeconds: 60
    network_smoke:
      enabled: true
      timeoutSeconds: 45
    storage_smoke:
      enabled: true
      timeoutSeconds: 45
    runtime_smoke:
      enabled: true
      timeoutSeconds: 45
    nccl_smoke:
      enabled: false
      timeoutSeconds: 180

  expected:
    # populated by fleet automation per pool (values override)
    nvidiaDriverMajor: "550"
    cudaMinor: "12.4"

resources:
  requests:
    cpu: 100m
    memory: 128Mi
  limits:
    cpu: 500m
    memory: 512Mi

rbac:
  create: true
  # if true, allows agent to create/update a Lease for heartbeat in its namespace
  enableLeaseHeartbeat: false

telemetry:
  otlp:
    enabled: false
    endpoint: ""

nodeSelector:
  redwood.ai/node-type: gpu-worker

tolerations:
  - key: "nvidia.com/gpu"
    operator: "Exists"
    effect: "NoSchedule"

priorityClassName: "system-node-critical"
```

## Security / permissions
- Runs as non-root by default (`runAsUser: 65534`, `runAsNonRoot: true`).
- `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`.
- Drops all capabilities.
- No host networking.

GPU inspection notes:
- The agent executes `nvidia-smi` by mounting it from the host (`/usr/bin/nvidia-smi`) and mounts `/proc/driver/nvidia` read-only. This avoids bundling driver tooling in the container and keeps the container image small.
- Does not request `nvidia.com/gpu` resources (so it doesn’t reserve a GPU). It only reads health/driver state.

## Operational notes
- Uses a checksum annotation on the ConfigMap so edits trigger a rollout.
- DaemonSet update strategy is `RollingUpdate` with `maxUnavailable: 10%` (tuned in review).
- `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 10` to avoid hanging during drain.

## Testing
- `helm template` + `helm lint` in CI
- Rendered manifests applied to a dev GPU pool (us-east, A100) via staging pipeline
- Verified that pods schedule on tainted GPU nodes and emit expected JSON logs

## Rollout
This chart will be installed only in staging for now. Fleet automation will enable it behind the staged rollout flag per pool (separate PR in control plane/terraform).
Vanessa Ortiz: Can we make the check list explicitly configurable per pool, and ensure we can disable NCCL by default? Also please add a comment about why we’re mounting nvidia-smi from host.

Gabe Wilson (author): Updated values to be per-check enable/disable with timeouts. NCCL stays disabled by default. Added docs in values.yaml + README explaining host mount approach.

Rafael Mendes: RBAC looks a bit broad. Do we really need write permissions anywhere? Also RollingUpdate maxUnavailable=1 will take forever on large pools.

Gabe Wilson (author): RBAC is now read-only by default (get/list/watch nodes + create events removed). Added `rbac.enableLeaseHeartbeat` toggle; only when enabled does it grant Lease create/update in the release namespace. Updated updateStrategy to `maxUnavailable: 10%` (overrideable).

Fiona McCarthy: Please enforce `readOnlyRootFilesystem`, drop caps, and ensure we don’t run privileged. Also confirm the hostPath mounts are read-only.

Gabe Wilson (author): Added pod/container securityContext: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, allowPrivilegeEscalation=false, drop ALL, seccomp=RuntimeDefault. HostPath mounts are now explicitly `readOnly: true`.

Allison Grant: Telemetry: please don’t default OTLP on; also avoid adding high-cardinality labels/annotations.

Gabe Wilson (author): OTLP export remains disabled by default; config uses static keys only. No per-node IDs added to labels.

Approvals: Vanessa Ortiz approved; Rafael Mendes approved; Fiona McCarthy approved (security); Allison Grant approved (observability).

Motivation: Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) occasionally require tighter control over where init jobs land and better visibility when init sequences stall during upgrades. This PR adds a light-weight init-phase 'state tracing' hook and a conditional nodeAffinity/nodeSelector values subtree so operators can pin init jobs to specific node classes without forking templates per environment.

What this change does (summary): - Introduces charts/redwood-private/values.schema.json additions to validate .initJobs.enableTracing and .initJobs.nodeAffinity.* keys. - Adds a small helper template (templates/_init_helpers.tpl) with a 'renderInitAffinity' function that renders affinity/selector only when values are present. - Reworks templates/init-hooks.yaml to emit an annotated init Job that writes ephemeral traces to a Helm-managed ConfigMap (traces expire on subsequent upgrades) so we can inspect stage/state without requiring external logging. - Adds templates/tests/init-job-test.yaml to exercise the nodeAffinity rendering and the tracing toggle under helm test. - Updates README with configuration examples and upgrade guidance.

Config example included in README: one-liner examples for enabling tracing and pinning to nodeLabel: node-role.kubernetes.io/storage: "true". The values subtree is intentionally opt-in (defaults disabled) to avoid surface area for existing installs.

Upgrade notes: This is additive. When enabling nodeAffinity for init jobs operators should verify node capacity for init waves (see notes in README). Traces are stored in a small ConfigMap named redwood-private-init-traces-<release> and pruned by Helm hooks; no long-term retention is performed by default. If operators previously copied or templated custom init jobs, they should switch to the new helpers to avoid duplication.

Testing: Local helm lint/lint-values against values.schema.json, unit-style checks for helpers using helm template, and two CI runs: initial run failed on a flaky init-job helm test (timeout waiting for test pod), test re-run passed after bumping test timeout and changing test to use an ephemeral nodeSelector during CI.

Security: The tracing ConfigMap contains no secrets or PII; it's a plain status blob. RBAC added for the init Job ServiceAccount to create/patch the trace ConfigMap only in release namespace.

Related work: builds on ENG-1987 (init sequencing observability) and OPS-432 (onprem affinity profiles).

Checklist: - [x] values.schema.json updated - [x] templates updated and helper added - [x] README example and upgrade section - [x] unit/helm tests - [x] reviewers addressed comments

Merge: squash-merged into main after approvals and CI green.
Diego Alvarez: Can we avoid writing traces to a ConfigMap in very large clusters? This could cause churn—suggest a size cap and early prune.
Maya Chen: Addressed—added a maxTraceEntries value and GC logic in the job so it prunes to the latest N entries. Documented in README.
Priya Raman: NodeAffinity helper looks good; add unit tests for missing values path (should render nothing).
Maya Chen: Added helm-template snapshot in CI to assert the helper is a no-op when nodeAffinity is unset.
Lena Sørensen: rbac-init-job looks tight, please ensure the SA doesn't get broad permissions (lgtm otherwise).
Maya Chen: Restricted patch rights to ConfigMap only; removed generic edit role binding used in earlier draft.
Priya Raman: Approving after CI green.

payload.body:
Motivation: private installer deployments require an idempotent, auditable way to seed tenant-scoped RBAC without granting cluster-admin to the installer process. This PR adds a values-driven approach to enable tenant RBAC automation from Helm installs/upgrades and introduces a safe, cluster-side reconciliation job to pick up and apply curated policy bundles. Summary of changes: 1) New Helm values: "tenantRbac.enabled" (bool), "tenantRbac.bootstrapServiceAccount" (string), "tenantRbac.policyBundleConfigMap" (name) and a "tenantRbac.rollbackStrategy" option. Values can be toggled per-release or per-environment so operators can opt into automation. 2) Template: charts/redwood-private/templates/tenant-rbac-cronjob.yaml — a controllerless, namespaced CronJob that reads the configured ConfigMap with policy bundles and applies roles/rolebindings for tenants in a guarded/limited way (uses a dedicated SA with narrowly scoped permissions). 3) Hook templates: charts/redwood-private/templates/hooks/tenant-rbac-post-upgrade-hook.yaml and pre-upgrade validation job; these enable graceful rollouts and automatic idempotent reconciliation during upgrades. 4) Helper: charts/redwood-private/templates/_rbac-helpers.tpl — templated role manifests and a checksum annotation to trigger canary reconcilers only when policy changes. 5) Integration: small connector that exports a TenantPolicy CR name to a Secret so private-installer can drive tenant creation without cluster-admin. 6) Docs: expanded README values table and operator migration guide for private installs. Safety and rollout: the cronjob runs with a configurable schedule and supports a "dryRun" flag and a "maxConcurrentApplies" limiter. All cluster-facing actions are scoped to tenant namespaces and use least-privilege SAs created by the chart. There's a guarded rollback strategy: when "rollbackStrategy: conservative" the hook will remove only resources it created and leave tenant data untouched. Backwards compatibility: defaults are off — installing older helm releases will behave unchanged. Test plan and verification: - unit: helm template checks and kube-linting added to CI. - integration: e2e run in CI using kind with simulated multi-tenant namespace injection; verified idempotency by running the cronjob loop 5x and asserting no duplicate bindings. - manual: private-installer QA validated migration path in a staging VPC cluster. Related items: ENG-1921 (tenant onboarding automation), ENG-1983 (rbac least-privilege audit). Checklist: [x] Helm values docs updated, [x] unit tests added, [x] integration e2e, [x] safety flags and dry-run, [x] reviewer approvals. Rollout notes: enable tenantRbac.enabled=false initially; flip to true for staging and monitor the "redwood.rbac.apply_success_total" metric and audit logs. If any unexpected failures occur, use the post-upgrade-hook annotation "redwood.io/skip-rbac-reconcile=true" to freeze automation and follow the manual remediation doc.
Marcus Li (reviewer): Please ensure the SA used by the cronjob cannot escalate privileges (suggested binding only Role not ClusterRole).
Elena Park (author): Updated roles to use Role and bound to namespace; removed ClusterRole binding per Marcus suggestion (commit 9a11c5e).
Priya Kapoor (reviewer): Can we add a migration note for existing customers who previously used an external job?
Elena Park: Added migration section in PRIVATE_INSTALLER_RBAC_AUTOMATION.md and included a recommended dry-run cadence for the first 24 hours.
Ibrahim Khan (approver): Verified e2e and CI; approved with one follow-up to expose maxConcurrentApplies as a value.
Elena Park: Exposed maxConcurrentApplies and added helm values doc entry and test for concurrency limit.
Added opt-in Helm values to enable tenant-scoped RBAC automation for private deployments. Includes a guarded tenant-rbac CronJob, pre/post-upgrade hooks, dry-run and concurrency controls, and documentation for migration. Defaults are off to preserve backwards compatibility.

payload.body:
This PR adds first-class Helm support for scheduled backups in Redwood Private by introducing an optional Kubernetes CronJob and associated service account/RBAC wiring. This is the chart-side counterpart to the installer `backup create` command (ENG-9821) and the Day-2 backup/restore toolkit workstream. The CronJob is disabled by default and can be enabled via values. It is designed to be safe-by-default (concurrency policy, history limits, backoff limits), to run in restricted clusters (no cluster-wide RBAC required), and to support both VPC and on-prem installs where outbound egress may be limited.

What’s included: (1) New values under `backup.cronJob.*` to control scheduling and runtime behavior, including schedule, suspend, startingDeadlineSeconds, concurrencyPolicy, ttlSecondsAfterFinished, and history limits. (2) `backup.serviceAccount.*` and `backup.rbac.*` knobs to create or reuse a dedicated service account with minimal namespace-scoped permissions. (3) Resource requests/limits and pod-level controls (nodeSelector/tolerations/affinity, priorityClassName, securityContext, podSecurityContext) so SRE/customers can place the job on appropriate nodes and avoid starving the control plane. (4) A thin wrapper command that invokes the private installer backup flow with consistent flags, logs, and exit codes; backup artifacts are still written to the configured backend (e.g., S3/NFS) as defined elsewhere.

Security posture: the CronJob does not require cluster-admin. By default it does not request permissions to read Kubernetes Secrets; credentials are expected to be provided via mounted secret/environment (standard K8s volume mounts) rather than via API reads. The Role is namespace-scoped and only grants read access to selected configmaps used for identifying release metadata and environment configuration. The container is configured to run as non-root, drop Linux capabilities, and disallow privilege escalation.

Operational notes: Default schedule is unset (must be explicitly configured), and `backup.cronJob.enabled=false` by default. The job retries are bounded. Logs are structured and include a short summary line that can be scraped by log-based alerts until the metrics work lands (ENG-9826). This PR also documents common failure modes we’ve seen in staging (INT-612: missing RBAC permissions / running under the wrong service account) and provides a recommended minimal configuration.

Example values:
- backup:
  cronJob:
    enabled: true
    schedule: "0 */6 * * *"
    concurrencyPolicy: "Forbid"
    successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
    failedJobsHistoryLimit: 3
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: "100m"
        memory: "256Mi"
      limits:
        cpu: "500m"
        memory: "1Gi"
  serviceAccount:
    create: true
    name: "redwood-private-backup"
  rbac:
    create: true

Rollout/compatibility: This chart change is backward compatible. If enabled, it assumes the `redwood-private-installer` image tag referenced by the chart includes the `backup create` command; we fail fast with a clear error message if the binary is missing. Release notes included in chart README.
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Please make CronJob disabled by default and require schedule when enabled; also set concurrencyPolicy=Forbid and keep history limits low so clusters don’t accumulate job objects. Bruno Silva: Done. Added `required` on schedule when enabled, defaulted concurrencyPolicy to Forbid, and set successful/failed history defaults to 3.

Hanae Suzuki (Security): Can we avoid granting read permissions on Secrets? We’ve been trying to enforce “mount secrets, don’t read them via API” as a pattern for restricted clusters. Also please ensure container runs non-root and drops capabilities to satisfy PSA-restricted baselines. Bruno Silva: Updated Role to only read specific configmaps (no secrets) and added securityContext defaults: runAsNonRoot=true, allowPrivilegeEscalation=false, readOnlyRootFilesystem=true, capabilities.drop=["ALL"].

Connor O’Brien (Release): Please call out version compatibility: enabling this requires the installer image tag that contains `backup create`. Also please keep args/flags stable (we’ll reference this from internal runbooks). Bruno Silva: Added a README section and a fail-fast check in the wrapper command. Also pinned the default arg shape and documented overrides via `backup.cronJob.extraArgs`.

Ethan Park (Control Plane): The job name should be deterministic and include release name; also ensure it runs in the same namespace as the control plane so it can hit in-cluster endpoints without extra network rules. Bruno Silva: Updated naming to `{{ fullname }}-backup` and confirmed namespace-scoped templates; added note in README about network policies and in-cluster DNS target.

Follow-up requested changes: rename `backup.enabled` to `backup.cronJob.enabled` to avoid confusion with “backup feature”. Completed in latest commit; schema updated accordingly.

Approvals: Sean Gallagher approved after RBAC/securityContext changes; Hanae Suzuki approved after removing Secrets API permissions; Connor O’Brien approved after doc/compatibility notes.
Helm: add optional scheduled backup CronJob for Redwood Private with dedicated service account/RBAC and configurable resources. Disabled by default; requires setting backup.cronJob.schedule when enabled. No cluster-wide permissions required.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: Private deployments sometimes need fine-grained control over how init jobs and Helm hooks are sequenced across tenants and multi-AZ migrations. Current init hooks run in a single phase which makes long-running tenant migrations and staged DB migrations fragile: a subsequent Helm rollback can unintentionally interrupt an in-flight tenant migration. This PR introduces two orthogonal features to improve safety and flexibility for private installs: 1) init-wave annotations: a lightweight mechanism to assign init hooks to ordered waves (0..N) and have the chart render sequenced Job resources; 2) rollback-fence annotation: an opt-in guard that prevents chart-level rollback (Helm uninstall/rollback) from running if a tenant-level fence label is present and migrate-in-progress is detected.

What this PR changes (high level): - values.schema.json: updated to include new fields under .private.initWaves and .private.rollbackFence with validation and defaults. - templates/init-wave-job.yaml: new template that renders init jobs grouped by wave, uses annotation "redwood.io/init-wave" to choose ordering and adds readinessProbe-based gate for longer-running migrations. - templates/rollback-fence-hook.yaml: new pre-delete hook that checks for fence label and fails early with a clear message when rollbackFence.enabled = true. - templates/_helpers.tpl: helper functions for wave sorting and fence message. - .github/workflows/helm-lint.yaml: enable strict lint stage and run chart testing with the new schema. - charts/README.md: docs for the new opt-in flags and recommended patterns for multi-tenant migrations. - tests/preflight-waves.yaml: integration-style smoke test that exercises three-wave sequencing in CI.

Commits (summary): - 7f3a2d2: Add values.schema.json entries and defaults for initWaves and rollbackFence. - 84b1c6f: Implement init-wave job template and helpers for sorting. - a2d9b7a: Add rollback-fence pre-delete hook and exit messages. - c1e4f5b: CI: enable helm lint strict and add simple chart-testing. - e0f6b2c: Docs: expand README and add examples for tenant migrations and fences.

Files touched (representative): - values.schema.json (new fields, validation) - templates/init-wave-job.yaml (new) - templates/rollback-fence-hook.yaml (new) - templates/_helpers.tpl (updated) - charts/README.md (updated) - .github/workflows/helm-lint.yaml (updated) - tests/preflight-waves.yaml (new) - templates/NOTES.txt (updated) - Chart.yaml (patch bump)

Behavior and compatibility notes: - All features are opt-in. By default the chart behavior is unchanged: if private.initWaves is empty, existing init hook behavior is preserved. - rollbackFence.enabled defaults to false. When enabled, the pre-delete hook will run and will fail the delete if a fence label ("redwood.io/migration-in-progress=true") is detected on any namespace-scoped resource the hook inspects. This is intentionally conservative to prevent accidental disruption. - The init-wave implementation orders waves numerically and runs sequentially. Within a wave, jobs run concurrently (same as traditional hooks). - The pre-delete hook is a lightweight guard and advises operators to run a controlled migration rollback procedure; it does not attempt automatic resolution.

Review discussion (highlights, chronological): - Diego Alvarez (review): "Nice approach, I like the opt-in nature. Two asks: 1) can the fence check be toggled to only scan a tenant label set to avoid scanning too broadly? 2) add a short-circuit on the pre-delete hook so quick deletes for dev clusters aren't blocked." - Marisol Chen (author reply): "Addressed both: added rollbackFence.scanScope with values [namespace|tenant|cluster] (default namespace) and added an override rollbackFence.bypassForTags for dev buckets. Updated schema and README examples." - Priya Nair (review): "Can we add a Prometheus metric or event when a fence prevents a delete so SRE can alert?" - Marisol Chen: "Added a note in the docs recommending customers emit an Event in the hook; kept metric emission out of the chart to avoid coupling to any metrics stack. Also added example snippet showing how to emit a k8s Event from the hook job." - Samir Gupta (requested change): "Make the wave sorting deterministic when custom labels are used (pad numbers)." - Marisol Chen: "Updated helper to zero-pad and to treat absent values as wave 0. Added unit test in templates using helm-unittest pattern." - Priya Nair (approve): "Approved after the schema tests pass." - Diego Alvarez (approve): "LGTM. Verified the smoke test in CI."

CI and checks: - helm-lint (strict): pass - chart-tests (preflight-waves): pass - unit-template-tests: pass - integration smoke job (k8s kind): pass (flake-free on rerun) Summary: CI green after two iterations; minor lint tweaks fixed in second commit.

Merge details: Squash-and-merge chosen. Merge commit authored by Marisol Chen with message "Introduce init-wave annotations and optional rollback-fence for private installs — opt-in safety for tenant migrations". Deployed a dry-run of the chart to our internal staging environment and ran the preflight-waves test to validate sequencing.

Operational guidance (brief): - To enable init waves: set private.initWaves:
    enabled: true
    waves:
      - name: db-migrate
        annotations:
          - key: redwood.io/init-wave
            value: "1"
  See charts/README.md for full examples. - To enable rollback guard: set private.rollbackFence.enabled = true and choose scanScope per your tenancy model. - For on-prem customers with long-running migrations, combine waves with readinessProbe gating to reduce accidental concurrency.

Related work and follow-ups: - ENG-4591 will add an optional controller-based fence for clusters that prefer an operator rather than a hook-based guard. - A follow-up PR will add an optional Prometheus metric emission when fences trigger (team agreed to keep that separate from the chart change to avoid dependency churn).
Adds opt-in init-wave annotations, a rollback-fence annotation to protect tenant migrations, stricter Helm linting in CI, and extended values schema for private installs. No breaking changes by default; features are opt-in via values.yaml.
payload.title: Introduce init-wave annotations and optional rollback-fence for private Helm installs

payload.body:
Context: Dedicated + Private customers are asking to pin a stable Runtime LTS patch for 6–12+ months and to have a predictable way to discover “slower-change” release notes for the pinned version. This PR adds explicit Helm values to select the Runtime LTS channel/tag, surfaces the release notes URL via annotations, and documents expected pinning semantics for Private deployments.

What changed (high level): 1) New values to select the runtime image tag via an LTS-friendly interface (channel + version), while preserving existing explicit image.tag overrides. 2) Add standardized annotations on the runtime Deployment/StatefulSet (and optional Service) to expose the runtime version and release notes URL for operators/tools. 3) Docs: update chart README with examples and precedence rules (explicit tag override wins).

Values added: - runtime.channel: "stable" (default) | "lts" - runtime.lts.version: e.g. "1.18.1-lts" (required when channel=lts unless runtime.image.tag is set) - runtime.lts.releaseNotesUrl: optional explicit override; otherwise auto-constructed from runtime.lts.version - runtime.annotations.releaseNotes: true (default) to emit release notes annotation - runtime.annotations.version: true (default) to emit runtime version annotation

Annotation keys (new): - redwood.ai/runtime-version: "1.18.1-lts" - redwood.ai/runtime-release-notes: "https://docs.redwood.ai/runtime/lts/1.18.1-lts" These are intended to be machine-readable for fleet tooling and to match what Product is planning to surface in Console during LTS pinning.

Precedence rules (documented): 1) If runtime.image.tag is set, we use it as-is and set redwood.ai/runtime-version to that value (no parsing). 2) Else if runtime.channel=lts, require runtime.lts.version and use that as runtime.image.tag. 3) Else default behavior remains unchanged (stable channel uses Chart appVersion / values default).

Why annotations instead of ConfigMap only: Operators frequently inspect the rendered workload objects directly, and SRE tooling can scrape annotations without following references. This also gives Private customers an auditable “what version is running” signal that matches pinned artifacts.

Testing: - chart-testing (ct lint + install) - helm template snapshot checks for both stable and lts paths - verified annotations render on Deployment and are stable across upgrades

Rollout notes: This is backwards compatible for existing installs unless they were relying on an unset image.tag but a non-standard appVersion behavior. No runtime behavior changes; this is packaging-only.

Follow-ups: - Once Runtime LTS release notes generator output URL scheme is finalized, we may adjust the default releaseNotesUrl constructor (keeping explicit override). - Consider emitting the release notes annotation on Pods (via podTemplate annotations) as well; currently it’s on the owning workload and podTemplate to cover both kubectl get deploy and kubectl get pods use cases.
Connor O'Brien (Release Eng): Can we ensure the LTS values map 1:1 with runtime tag naming? We’re standardizing on 1.18.1-lts and runtime-1.18-lts branch. Also, please document precedence with explicit image.tag overrides since Private customers already pin images that way. — Bruno Silva: Updated README with precedence and clarified that runtime.lts.version is the tag string (e.g. 1.18.1-lts). Explicit image.tag continues to win.
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Please put the annotations on podTemplate as well; most of our scraping looks at pods not deployments. Also make sure the keys are stable and vendor-prefixed. — Bruno Silva: Added annotations to metadata.annotations and spec.template.metadata.annotations; keys are redwood.ai/* and documented as stable for LTS ops.
Elliot Price (Docs): Release notes URL construction: docs team is using /runtime/lts/<version> as the canonical path. If we can’t guarantee it, require an explicit value. — Bruno Silva: Implemented default constructor to /runtime/lts/<version> but kept runtime.lts.releaseNotesUrl override and noted in README that URL scheme may change during pilot; override recommended for early pilots.
Vivek Kulkarni (Private packaging): We need a clear error when channel=lts but version is empty; helm should fail fast. Also please confirm this doesn’t change defaults for stable channel. — Bruno Silva: Added required() in helper; stable path unchanged and tests cover stable render output.
Helm chart now supports selecting Runtime LTS channel via runtime.channel=lts and runtime.lts.version.
Rendered workloads include annotations for runtime version and release notes URL to support enterprise ops workflows.

Background: We want a safe, opinionated way to ship cluster-level defaults for batching/prefill, KV cache sizing, and quantization profiles so Managed/Private clusters can opt into Redwood Optimize presets at install time. This prevents teams from needing to hand-roll the same defaults across environments and ties chart installs into tenant-friendly unit-econ defaults.

What this PR does: Adds Helm chart-level defaults and a small templated ConfigMap that surfaces: 1) prefill/prefetch policy presets (hot/cold/tenant-weighted), 2) KV cache targets (percent-of-gpu-memory hints), 3) quantization profile stubs (fp16/int8/quant-acl presets) and 4) a small cost-mapping table used by the installer to seed tenant profiles. The values are conservative by default and documented.

Files touched (high level): updates to values.yaml (defaults block), new templates/configmap-cost-profiles.yaml, small changes to templates/deployment.yaml to expose env vars, README.md docs section and tests/values-tests.yaml.

Checklist: [x] Helm linted and fixed, [x] unit test harness for values, [x] docs updated in chart README, [x] CI smoke install on k3s cluster, [x] integration check: installer seeds tenant config.

Notes: these are installer-level defaults only; runtime still respects tenant-level overrides. This should be safe for upgrades because values are additive and the ConfigMap is created with labels that the installer can adopt. Referenced Linear: ENG-1534 (prefill defaults), ENG-1601 (quant profiles shipping).
Evan Morales: 'Can we keep the default KV cache as a percentage rather than absolute bytes to avoid surprises across SKU sizes?' -- Lina Ortega: 'Please add an explicit migration note for existing installs so adopters know they can opt-in.' -- Marcus Li: 'Consider adding a toggle to disable auto-seeding for stricter enterprise installs.' -- Author responses: Implemented % KV cache, added migration note to README, added values.install.seedCostProfiles: false flag and documented it. Addressed linter and naming nit. Final approval from Lina and Marcus after small fixes.
Installer: new optional cluster defaults for batching/prefill, cache sizing, and quantization profiles. Charts expose values.default.costProfiles and values.install.seedCostProfiles (default: false). Safe opt-in; no forced runtime changes.
To enable automatic seeding at install time set values.install.seedCostProfiles=true. For private installs, you can supply your own quant profile ConfigMap by setting values.default.costProfiles.sourceConfigMap. Defaults are intentionally conservative; review quant_profile entries before enabling in high-throughput clusters.
Local helm template checks + chart-tests validated schema. k3s smoke tested install and upgrade flows. Installer e2e verified that when seed flag is enabled, tenant gets seeded with a lightweight cost profile. Load-sensitive quant profiles were not enabled in e2e for safety; follow-up ENG-1628 is to add gated performance tests.

payload.body:
This PR wires the v1 "Private observability minimum pack" artifacts (Grafana dashboard bundle + Prometheus alert/recording rules) into the `redwood-private` Helm chart values, with customer-friendly toggles and sane defaults. Motivation: today Private installs often require manual copying of dashboards/rules, which makes upgrades brittle (e.g., empty dashboards after upgrade) and makes it harder for Support/SRE to assume a baseline. This change makes the minimum pack installable via `values.yaml` and version-pins the artifact bundle so air-gapped installs can package it reliably. What’s included: (1) Dashboards: ships a versioned dashboard bundle as ConfigMaps that work with the Grafana sidecar pattern. Customers can enable/disable per-category (runtime, control-plane, infra) and choose the label/key used by their Grafana sidecar. (2) Alerts/recording rules: ships `PrometheusRule` resources when the Prometheus Operator CRD is present; otherwise can optionally emit rules as a raw rules ConfigMap for non-operator Prometheus setups. (3) Exporter + retention toggles: adds values to enable/disable the recommended minimum exporters (kube-state-metrics, node-exporter, DCGM exporter) when customers choose to deploy the bundled stack, and exposes retention / storage knobs for Prometheus (and Grafana persistence when enabled). Non-goals: this does not introduce "premium" features (federation, long retention defaults, custom dashboards). It also does not force-install Prometheus/Grafana; by default we only ship artifacts and create ServiceMonitors/PrometheusRules when enabled. Values summary (new): `observability.enabled` (default true), `observability.dashboards.enabled` (default true), `observability.dashboards.sidecar.label` (default `grafana_dashboard`), `observability.dashboards.sidecar.folderAnnotation` (default `grafana_folder`), `observability.alerts.enabled` (default true), `observability.alerts.mode` = `prometheusOperator|configMap` (default `prometheusOperator`), `observability.alerts.runbookBaseUrl` (used to stamp alert annotations), `observability.stack.enabled` (default false; if true installs `kube-prometheus-stack` + exporters with bounded defaults), `observability.stack.prometheus.retention` (default `15d`), `observability.stack.prometheus.storage.size` (default `50Gi`), `observability.stack.exporters.kubeStateMetrics.enabled` (default true when stack enabled), `observability.stack.exporters.nodeExporter.enabled` (default true when stack enabled), `observability.stack.exporters.dcgmExporter.enabled` (default true when stack enabled). Implementation notes: dashboards and rules are imported from the `observability-pack` bundle (pinned by version in chart values) and rendered into templates via a small helper that keeps ConfigMaps under the Kubernetes size limits by splitting across multiple ConfigMaps. PrometheusRule creation is gated on both values and CRD presence (`monitoring.coreos.com/v1`). Alert annotations include: summary, description, severity, and `runbook_url` pointing to our internal runbooks (base URL configurable for customer docs mirrors in air-gapped environments). Testing: `helm template` on defaults; `ct lint` for chart schema; kind-based smoke deploy with Grafana sidecar and Prometheus Operator verifying dashboards appear and Prometheus loads rules. Related: ENG-19152 (chart wiring), PRs in `observability-pack` adding the bundles, and installer preflight work in `redwood-private-installer` (separate PR) to validate CRDs/storage prerequisites.
Dylan Brooks (review): Can we avoid assuming a specific Grafana sidecar label? Some customers use `grafana_dashboard` but others use `grafana_dashboard: "1"` patterns. Author (Diego): Added `observability.dashboards.sidecar.label` and `observability.dashboards.sidecar.labelValue` (default empty -> just key exists), plus `folderAnnotation` override; updated README comments. Logan Wright (review): PrometheusRule should be gated on CRD presence; we’ve seen installs without operator. Also we need a safe fallback. Author: Added `.Capabilities.APIVersions.Has "monitoring.coreos.com/v1"` gating; introduced `alerts.mode=configMap` that emits a rules ConfigMap (customer can mount into Prometheus) and documented it. Allison Grant (review): Please ensure alert severities map to our Private standards and include runbook URLs. Also recording rules should be separate so they can be disabled if cardinality is an issue. Author: Updated annotations to include `runbook_url` and clarified severity mapping in values comments; added `observability.recordingRules.enabled` toggle (default true) and grouped recording rules into a separate manifest section. Rafael Mendes (review): Default retention/storage for bundled Prometheus feels too low for some clusters and too high for others; can we document sizing guidance and keep defaults conservative? Author: Kept defaults at 15d/50Gi but added explicit values and comments; linked to infra sizing doc in README; also set CPU/mem requests for kube-prometheus-stack components behind the stack flag only. Chloe Martin (review): ConfigMaps can exceed size limits with dashboard JSON. How are we splitting? Author: Added helper to split by dashboard file and chunk by byte limit; validated template output < 900KiB per ConfigMap; added a chart-testing install job with stack enabled + dashboards enabled. Final: Approvals from Dylan, Logan, Allison; Rafael approved after re-run; merged via squash.
Private Helm chart now supports installing the minimum supported observability artifacts (Grafana dashboards + Prometheus alerts/recording rules) via values toggles.
Optional bundled Prometheus/Grafana stack can be enabled behind `observability.stack.enabled`, with configurable retention/storage and exporter toggles.
Alert resources include configurable runbook URLs to support customer doc mirrors in air-gapped environments.
payload.title: Wire Private observability minimum pack (dashboards + alerts) into Helm values

payload.body:
Motivation: On large private installs we still see unpredictable init ordering and a burst of tenant init jobs that competes for control-plane resources. This PR introduces a values-driven "timingPolicy" that lets operators express per-tenant init windows, soft backpressure windows, and jitter profiles, plus a Helm overlayTransformer helper that composes environment-specific overlays (airgap, single-az, high-density) without duplicating templates. The change is intended to be fully backwards compatible: when timingPolicy is omitted, behavior falls back to the current sequenced init job ordering. Work done: - Add values.schema.json extension for timingPolicy and overlayTransformer configuration with validation and examples. - Implement helm/_overlay_transformer.tpl helper and accompanying _init_timing.tpl to materialize ordered CronJobs/Jobs with calculated startDelay annotations. - Add init controller annotation hooks so the private-installer can coordinate with the init-sidecar and migrator when timingPolicy requests soft backpressure. - Introduce small migration patch (post-renderer hook) that backfills legacy init waves into timingPolicy for existing installs opting into the feature. - Update README and chart README sections with examples for airgapped and VPC multi-az deployments, including recommended timingPolicy profiles for low-CPU control planes. Checklist: - [x] values schema and readme examples - [x] templating helpers and unit tests - [x] small migration that is a no-op when feature not enabled - [x] e2e smoke validation in CI (chart test) - [x] documented upgrade notes and rollback guidance Notes: The overlayTransformer is intentionally conservative: it accepts a list of overlay names and a path-based overlay map in values, and composes them deterministically (order of overlays in the list defines precedence). The timingPolicy supports three modes: "sequential" (default), "staggered" (per-tenant window and jitter), and "backpressure" (soft concurrency limit via controller annotations). Related: ENG-4247 (tenant init stability), and a forthcoming small Terraform provider change to expose timingPolicy during private install bootstrapping. Rollout plan: feature gated behind values.enableTimingPolicy=false by default. Operators can opt in per-tenant or cluster-wide. Migration is additive and reversible by clearing timingPolicy values.
Mateo Ruiz (reviewer): Can the overlayTransformer preserve Helm hooks annotations? We rely on post-renderer hooks in some environments.
Lena Park (author): OverlayTransformer preserves annotations and merges hook lists; added a unit test to cover a hook-preservation case.
Riya Singh (reviewer): TimingPolicy looks useful, but we should avoid imposing default jitter that might hide underlying failures. Suggest making jitter opt-in per profile.
Lena Park (author): Good point — changed jitter to default 0ms for sequential and added profile-level jitter field. Updated examples and tests.
Samir Patel (reviewer): CI chart test failed initially on the migration hook flake (post-renderer order). I saw an intermittent where backfill replaced a label. Recommend idempotency re-check.
Lena Park (author): Fixed by making the migration use label-based existence check; re-ran CI and green. Added explicit idempotency assertion in the test.
Mateo Ruiz (approver): Approved — small nit about docs wording on rollback, but not blocking.
Riya Singh (approver): Approved after jitter opt-in change.
Merge: squashed and merged by Lena Park via squash merge.
Add optional timingPolicy to private-installer Helm chart for deterministic tenant init windows and a new overlayTransformer helper for composing environment overlays. Feature is opt-in and disabled by default; includes migration helper for existing installs. See docs/private-installer/upgrade-notes.md for migration and rollback guidance.
This PR was intentionally scoped to templating and small migration; it does not change runtime controllers beyond adding opt-in annotations. The companion controller work to implement soft backpressure behavior will be submitted as a follow-up and referenced in ENG-4247.
