Motivation: Private installations occasionally fail post-upgrade due to network connector misconfigurations (NAT/GW misroutes, egress rules). Current preflight hooks catch k8s resource readiness but not external connectivity assumptions. Separately, rapid automated rollbacks during a narrow failure window have caused repeated deploy flaps for tenants with slow controller reconciliation. This PR introduces two paired features: 1) a conditional external-connector-probe init job (opt-in via values) that runs small egress/connectivity checks against configured endpoints before pod handoff, and 2) a rollback timelock cronjob/lease that enforces a minimum delay window before automatic rollback pipelines can trigger again. Both are implemented as Helm primitives (templates + values.schema updates) so operators can toggle them per-tenant or cluster. Summary of changes: - values.schema.json: add new top-level properties.privateExternalProbes and privateRollbackTimelock (types, defaults, validation). Probes accept an array of probe definitions (name, image, timeout, endpoints, requiredHttpStatus, runOnInit boolean). Timelock accepts enabled, initialDelaySeconds, windowSeconds, and a namespace-scoped lockName. - templates/init-external-connector-probe.yaml: new templated Job that conditionally renders when privateExternalProbes.enabled and values.installMode != "hosted". It mounts a minimal busybox/curl-based probe container with RBAC to read ConfigMaps with probe endpoints. - templates/rollback-timelock-cronjob.yaml: new CronJob that periodically refreshes a ConfigMap lease and exposes an annotation consumed by the rollout controller (controller changes are out-of-scope for this PR; we include a small helper to set the annotation format). - templates/_helpers.tpl: helper functions for safe-to-slice probe lists, defaulting semantics, and name hashing to keep resource names stable during upgrades. - charts/README.md: documented operational guidance and example values for enabling probes only in preflight vs always-run init jobs. - examples/values-external-probes.yaml: example showing multi-endpoint probes and tenant-scoped enablement. - tests/helm/unit/test_schema.sh: added unit test that validates the schema against example values and a negative test where probe definition is missing required fields. Commits (high-level): - a1b3c7d: initial values.schema additions and plumbing for probe conditionals - 4f9d2b1: add init-external-connector-probe template and helper functions - 9c2b7f8: introduce rollback-timelock cronjob + example values - e7c1a5b: docs and README updates + examples - f2b4d9a: unit tests and CI fixups (lint/helm3 compatibility) Changed files (high-level): - charts/private/values.schema.json (new fields, docs) - charts/private/values.yaml (defaults: probes disabled, timelock disabled) - charts/private/templates/init-external-connector-probe.yaml (new) - charts/private/templates/rollback-timelock-cronjob.yaml (new) - charts/private/templates/_helpers.tpl (extended helpers) - charts/private/README.md (docs) - examples/values-external-probes.yaml (example) - tests/helm/unit/test_schema.sh (tests) - .github/workflows/helm-lint.yml (tweak: allow experimental hooks) Review thread (abridged): - Priya (reviewer): "Overall looks good; two asks: a) ensure probes are opt-in at both chart and tenant level, b) avoid creating rolebindings in cross-namespace contexts by default." - Ethan (author): "Agree. Added values.privateExternalProbes.installScope with choices [cluster, namespace] and default 'namespace'. RBAC now created only when installScope == 'namespace' or .Release.Namespace == values.probeNamespace." - Laura (reviewer): "Please add an e2e fixture or at least a smoke test in the canary pipeline to exercise the probe template; unit schema check is good but doesn't catch runtime container issues." - Ethan: "Added tests/helm/unit/test_schema.sh and a minimal smoke job in examples; requested follow-up to add e2e in perf-canary pipeline (ENG-8991)." - Omar (security): "Probe images must be image-pinned and must not run as privileged. Add image policy docs." - Ethan: "Pinned images and added securityContext dropCapabilities in template; documented in README." CI and iteration: - First CI run: helm lint failed due to helper function clash with another chart; fixed naming collisions in _helpers.tpl and re-ran. - Second CI run: unit schema test initially failed due to an incorrect JSON schema 'pattern' on endpoint URLs; fixed and re-ran. - Final CI: all checks pass (helm lint, kubeval, unit schema, docs spellcheck). Merging: - Approved by Priya and Laura after addressing comments. - Squash-merged to main on 2024-11-15 by Priya Nair with merge commit message summarizing feature, linear links ENG-8762 ENG-8991, and a pointer to follow-up work to add e2e canary tests and rollout-controller integration. Operational notes and migration guidance: - Backwards compatibility: All new behavior is disabled by default. Default values keep preflight behavior unchanged. - Recommended opt-in flow: operators should enable probes in a staging tenant for 1-2 releases before rolling out cluster-wide. - Rollback timelock defaults to 600s window; operators can tune per tenant. - Known limitations: the probe job depends on outbound DNS and basic network egress; for air-gapped installs define explicit probe endpoints that resolve locally. - Follow-ups: (ENG-8991) add canary pipeline fixture to execute the probe job in a representative cluster; (ENG-9023) wire rollout-controller to consume timelock annotation for automated rollbacks. Small example usage: helm upgrade --install redwood-private charts/private -f examples/values-external-probes.yaml NOTES: kept templates intentionally minimal and non-invasive so downstream operators can adopt incrementally. If you want a narrower change set, I can split the probe templates and timelock into two separate PRs, but the two features were implemented together because the operators requested both in the same incident post-mortem.
- Add opt-in external connector probe job for Private installs
- Add rollback timelock cronjob to reduce flapping during automated rollbacks
- Extend values.schema.json with probe and timelock fields
- Backwards compatible: probes disabled by default

Motivation: Day-to-day developer feedback loops are dominated by presubmit bootstrap time (container pulls + toolchain fetch). This PR implements an ambient (non-root) toolchain cache used by the presubmit runner and a slim bootstrap path for fast local iteration. The aim is to reduce cold-start latency for contributors and CI warmup cost while keeping the canonical full bootstrap for CI and release runs.

What this changes: - Add ambient toolchain cache daemon and a lightweight cache-warming step used by local presubmit and quick CI lanes. - Split bootstrap into 'slim' and 'full' modes; default presubmit uses slim. - Add integrity checks and a simple eviction policy to avoid stale toolchains. - Update .github/presubmit.yml to opt-in slim mode for fast lanes and avoid pulling the full toolchain image on small changes. - Provide a short migration shim for devcontainers and older scripts to fall back to full bootstrap if cache is unavailable.

Checklist (this PR): - [x] Implement ambient cache and slim bootstrap codepaths - [x] Add unit tests for cache metadata parsing and eviction logic - [x] Integrate slim mode into presubmit workflow and local dev script - [x] Document new env flags and migration steps in docs/dev-boot.md - [x] Run scalability smoke test on ephemeral runners (3 repeats)

Commits summary: 1) daemon: add ambient toolchain cache manager (entrypoint, metadata store, eviction) 2) bootstrap: introduce slim/full modes and fast fetcher 3) ci: update presubmit workflow and add fast-lane toggle 4) scripts: devcontainer/TODO shim + docs/dev-boot.md 5) tests: add unit tests for metadata parsing and cache eviction tuning

Testing performed: - Local smoke runs: slim bootstrap cold-start ~22s vs full ~2m24s across mac/linux devboxes. - CI fast-lane run (presubmit slim) executed against a representative change set; artifacts restored from cache successfully on second run. - Unit test suite: pass (ci/presubmit). - Integration tests (nightly): unchanged and green; slim mode gated to fast lanes only.

Rollout plan: merged to main behind feature flag; presubmit fast lanes enable slim mode immediately. Monitor: presubmit median startup latency, cache hit rate, CI image pull bytes. Fallback: runner will auto-fallback to full bootstrap on any integrity failure.

Notes on security and hygiene: cache metadata is stored locally under the runner user directory with file permissions 0700. Toolchain artifacts are verified by checksum and signed manifest. No secret material is cached.

Related: Linear ENG-4128 (reduce dev presubmit latency), ENG-4182 (ci cost: reduce image pulls), support SUP-782 (customer reported noisy CI stalls).

Reduce developer presubmit startup time by introducing an ambient toolchain cache and simplify bootstrap flow. No user-facing API changes.
Miguel Alvarez: Nice separation of slim/full. Two suggestions: make eviction threshold configurable via env and add a short explanation in the presubmit workflow about why we opt into slim mode.
Aisha Kapoor: Thanks — added env var TOOLCHAIN_CACHE_MAX_MB and documented the presubmit rationale in .github. Also added a small e2e smoke guard in the runner to avoid partial warms.
Riley Thompson: CI flake observed first run of integration job due to ephemeral runner image pull. Confirmed it's unrelated; re-ran integration suite and it passed. Approving pending one lint nit.
Jae Park: Left one nit on error wrapping in cache manager (return fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err)). Once fixed, happy to approve.
Aisha Kapoor: Fixed error wrapping and added brief comment referencing the integrity manifest format. Squashed and pushed fixup commit.

Motivation: upgrades from older private-installer chart versions often hit subtle breakages when tenants use customized connector init hooks or rely on legacy values. This PR splits connector/init job patterns into composable templates, introduces a values-transform shim to map legacy top-level fields into the new structured values shape, and adds guardrails for airgapped and dry-run flows. Summary of changes: 1) templates/_connector-init.tpl: extracted connector init job template that supports phased waves, leader election, and an optional quota-prober sidecar; 2) templates/_values-transform.yaml: a helm helper that normalizes legacy values at render-time and emits warnings when deprecated fields are used; 3) values.schema.json: extended schema with new connectors.* objects, initWave sequencing, and explicit backoff/retry settings; 4) templates/tenant-init-job.yaml: uses the new connector template and supports per-tenant concurrency and namespace-scoped images; 5) chart-tests and a lightweight test harness to exercise values transform for common upgrade patterns; 6) docs/upgrade-notes.md: guidance and example migration mapping. Checklist: - [x] Implement templating helpers with minimal behavioral changes - [x] Add values schema and JSON-schema-driven validation - [x] Provide migration shim and automated values mapping - [x] Add unit/helm-template tests for typical edge-cases (airgap, missing connectors) - [x] Manual dry-run upgrade verified on a 3-tenant dev cluster Breaking considerations and upgrade path: the old flat keys are still accepted but will be logged as deprecated; the values-transform helper attempts to map them to the new connectors.* shape during render to avoid requiring manual edits for most customers. For advanced customizations, migration examples are included in docs/upgrade-notes.md. Why this is different from previous init-hook work: previous PRs adjusted hook sequencing and timeouts; this change focuses on schema evolution and safe automated mapping so Private customers can upgrade without hand-editing tenant overlays. payload.body:
## Context
Private upgrades need deterministic ordering so we never roll data-plane changes (runtime/model-cache/agent pools) until the control plane is fully upgraded and stable (API/console/authn/z, migrations, webhook controllers).

We previously tried to approximate ordering inside a single Helm release via hook weights, but Helm still applies manifest changes as one transaction. This made it possible to partially roll DP resources even when CP was unhealthy (e.g., CP deployment stuck due to migration lock contention).

This PR introduces a clean separation:
- A **control-plane chart** installed/upgraded first
- A **data-plane chart** installed/upgraded second
- A lightweight **readiness gate** that blocks DP upgrades until CP health + migration state are OK

This matches the installer/orchestrator plan stages being implemented in redwood-private-installer (plan generation + phase execution).

## What changed
### 1) New charts
- `charts/redwood-private-control-plane/`
  - control-plane API, console, auth proxy, admission/webhook controllers, migration job, RBAC/ServiceAccounts, CP services
- `charts/redwood-private-data-plane/`
  - data-plane runtime deployments/daemonsets, model-cache, DP services, HPA/autoscaling primitives

### 2) Umbrella chart changes
- `charts/redwood-private/` is now an umbrella chart that pins versions and wires shared values. It no longer installs CP/DP resources directly.
- Values are split to avoid cross-phase coupling:
  - `controlPlane.*` (required for CP release)
  - `dataPlane.*` (required for DP release)
  - `global.*` remains for shared concerns (image registry overrides, TLS mode, common labels)

### 3) Readiness gate
We add a small job (shipped with the **data-plane** chart) that blocks upgrades/installs until the control plane reports ready and migrations are complete.
- Implemented as a `pre-install,pre-upgrade` hook Job `redwood-cp-readiness-gate`
- Gate checks:
  - Kubernetes readiness: CP deployments are available
  - HTTP readiness: `/readyz` on `control-plane-api` returns 200
  - Migration state: `redwood-migrator` job is complete OR `schema_version` is at/above target (when migrator is disabled)
- Timeouts are configurable via `dataPlane.upgradeGate.timeoutSeconds` (default: 900s)

### 4) Backwards compatibility + upgrade path
This is a packaging change that affects operators using helm directly.
- Installer-managed environments: the installer will now create two helm releases in the correct order.
- Helm-direct users: follow the migration steps in `charts/redwood-private/README.md`.

We keep old values as deprecated aliases where feasible (e.g., `api.*` -> `controlPlane.api.*`) for one release cycle, but release names and chart structure are intentionally changed to make ordering unambiguous.

## Why this approach
- Splitting CP/DP into separate releases is the only reliable way to guarantee ordering across helm upgrades.
- Makes rollbacks safer: rollback of DP can proceed without forcing CP rollback unless explicitly required.
- Enables independent readiness gating and different timeouts for CP vs DP.

## Testing
- `helm lint` on all charts
- `ct` chart-testing with kind
- Added an upgrade test scenario:
  - Install CP+DP at N-1
  - Upgrade CP to N
  - Verify CP ready/migrations complete
  - Upgrade DP to N
  - Inject a failure (CP deployment unavailable) and assert DP upgrade is blocked by readiness gate

## Notes for release engineering
- The installer should call:
  1) `helm upgrade --install redwood-private-cp charts/redwood-private-control-plane`
  2) `helm upgrade --install redwood-private-dp charts/redwood-private-data-plane`
- `charts/redwood-private` remains as the version pin + documentation entrypoint, but it is not intended to be installed as a single release for production Private.

## Follow-ups
- Add explicit "supported upgrade path" checks in installer plan generation to enforce CP then DP (tracked in ENG-4821)
- Expand gate checks for OIDC reachability and KMS (tracked in ENG-4829)

## Snippet (gate job)
The DP chart adds the following hook job:

apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: {{ include "redwood-private.fullname" . }}-cp-readiness-gate
  annotations:
    "helm.sh/hook": pre-install,pre-upgrade
    "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": before-hook-creation,hook-succeeded
spec:
  activeDeadlineSeconds: {{ .Values.dataPlane.upgradeGate.timeoutSeconds }}
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
        - name: gate
          image: {{ .Values.global.toolsImage }}
          command: ["/bin/sh","-c"]
          args:
            - >
              ./wait-for-deployments.sh -n {{ .Release.Namespace }} {{ join " " .Values.dataPlane.upgradeGate.controlPlaneDeployments }}
              && ./http-check.sh http://{{ .Values.dataPlane.upgradeGate.controlPlaneService }}:{{ .Values.dataPlane.upgradeGate.controlPlanePort }}/readyz
              && ./migration-check.sh

(Full implementation lives in `charts/redwood-private-data-plane/templates/hooks/cp-readiness-gate.yaml` + `files/` scripts.)
Connor O'Brien (Release Eng): Splitting into two releases makes sense. Can we add explicit docs for helm-direct users (names of the two releases + ordering) and call out that the umbrella chart isn't meant to be installed? Also please ensure we keep a deprecation window for old values where possible.
Irene Choi (author): Added `charts/redwood-private/README.md` migration section with exact commands + a value mapping table. Kept aliases for `api.*` and `runtime.*` under the new `controlPlane.*`/`dataPlane.*` blocks for one release cycle; warnings are emitted via NOTES.txt.
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Gate timeout default 900s feels high but ok. Can we make sure the hook job doesn't stick around on failure (cleanup policy) and that failures are actionable (log which CP deployment or endpoint failed)?
Irene Choi (author): Updated hook-delete-policy to `before-hook-creation` only; on failure the Job remains for inspection (standard helm behavior). Added explicit log lines for each check (deployment availability, /readyz status code, migration status) and the failing condition exits with a unique code.
Benji Okafor (Platform): For migration check, relying on Job completion is brittle if customers disable the migrator and run manual migrations. Can the gate fall back to checking schema_version in DB if configured?
Irene Choi (author): Yep. `migration-check.sh` now supports two modes: (1) migrator job completion (default) and (2) DB schema_version check when `dataPlane.upgradeGate.dbCheck.enabled=true`. Documented in values + README. Default remains job-based to avoid DB creds in the DP release unless explicitly enabled.
Victor Alvarez (Networking): The gate hits CP service over cluster DNS. For some locked-down installs, NetworkPolicies may block the hook job pod. Can we ensure the job uses the same labels/serviceaccount as DP so customers' policies cover it?
Irene Choi (author): Hook job now uses `data-plane` serviceAccount + labels consistent with DP pods (`app.kubernetes.io/component=data-plane`). README includes a note: allow egress from DP namespace pods to CP service on port 8080 (or your configured port).
Rafael Mendes (On-call): Please add a short "what to do when gate blocks" section to NOTES so operators don't just rerun helm blindly.
Irene Choi (author): Added NOTES.txt output: shows failing check category and points to `kubectl logs job/<...>-cp-readiness-gate` plus the runbook section (link placeholder for now; will be finalized with docs PR).
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Approved after the added logging + clarified failure retention. This should reduce partial-upgrade incidents.
Connor O'Brien (Release Eng): Approved. We'll align installer plan stages to match CP then DP in the release train.
Private Helm packaging now separates control-plane and data-plane into two charts/releases to guarantee upgrade ordering.
Data-plane installs/upgrades are gated on control-plane readiness + migration completion to prevent partial upgrades.
Umbrella `redwood-private` chart is now a documentation/version pin entrypoint; operators should install CP then DP as separate releases.
payload.title: Split Redwood Private chart into control-plane + data-plane rollout phases (with readiness gates)

payload.body:
Summary:
Introduce a lightweight stream fragment coordinator in the streaming runtime to make SSE/EventStream chunking resilient to partial JSON emissions, out-of-order delimiter painting, and race conditions around function/tool-call handoffs. This PR adds a coordinator that: (1) tags fragment boundaries with stable sequence anchors, (2) defers toolcall handshake until fragment completion when boundaries are ambiguous, and (3) emits compact checkpoint markers that help clients resync without re-requesting tokens.

Motivation:
We continue to see intermittent customer reports of partial JSON objects in streaming responses when backpressure, connection truncation, or multi-threaded flushes occur. Current heuristics occasionally paint delimiters in a different order than tokens arrive, leading to malformed JSON at the client or duplicated tool calls. A robust server-side coordinator reduces client-side heuristics and eliminates several edge-case workarounds.

What this changes (high level):
- Add FragmentCoordinator that maintains a small ledger (sequence anchor + pending fragments) per stream session.
- Introduce a deferred-toolcall mode: when a toolcall sentinel is emitted inside an unresolved fragment, the handshake is delayed until the fragment is closed or a short acknowledgement window expires.
- Emit compact "ckpt" SSE events (ckpt:<seq>) to let clients resync to last committed fragment when seeing truncated streams.
- Rework fragment flushing to use single-writer append with an epoch token to avoid interleaved delimiter slips.

Design notes / rationale:
- We chose an append-only fragment ledger (in-memory, per-session) to avoid global locks; typical session size is < 32 fragments, so memory overhead is bounded.
- Toolcall deferral is conservative: we only defer when fragment closure is ambiguous (interleaved writes, missing newline delimiter) to avoid unnecessary latency. There is a configurable window (default 50ms) for handoff.
- Checkpoints are intentionally compact strings (ckpt:<hex-seq>) to keep streaming bandwidth low and maintain OpenAI-compatible SSE event names for visibility.

Implementation details (single continuous description):
Commits: 4
- Add FragmentCoordinator and ledger implementation (streaming/fragment_coordinator.go)
- Integrate coordinator into event-emitter (streaming/emitter.go), add deferred handshake path
- Tests: unit and integration tests for fragmented JSON, toolcall deferral, checkpoint replay (streaming/*_test.go)
- Docs + changelog entry + migration note (docs/streaming-fragments.md, changelog/stream-fragment-coordinator.md)

Files changed (high level):
- services/streaming/fragment_coordinator.go (new)
- services/streaming/emitter.go (modified)
- services/streaming/fragment_coordinator_test.go (new)
- services/streaming/emitter_integration_test.go (modified)
- api/openai_compat/streaming_adapter.go (modified)
- docs/streaming-fragments.md (new)
- docs/notes/streaming-migration.md (new)
- pkg/metrics/streaming_metrics.go (modified)
- CHANGELOG.md (modified)

Behavioral changes for users:
- Clients should tolerate occasional "ckpt:<seq>" SSE events. These are informational and safe to ignore; they assist resyncing after truncation.
- Toolcall ordering guarantees are strengthened: in ambiguous fragment cases the server may delay toolcall completion until fragment closure (should be transparent for most SDKs).

Testing and QA:
- Added unit tests that simulate interleaved writes and assert the coordinator resolves fragment boundaries without producing partial JSON events.
- Streaming e2e test simulates connection truncation and verifies that clients can resync using the latest ckpt event.
- Load test: 1000 concurrent short-chat sessions; coordinator introduced <2% p90 latency increase for token emission but reduced malformed-stream incidents from ~0.7% to <0.02% in our harness.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag `enable_fragment_coordinator` and default-on for hosted API, optional for Dedicated/Private (toggleable via config).
- Canary rollout: 10% of streaming traffic for 48h, monitor malformed_streams, functioncall-duplicates, and streaming-latency metrics.
- Gradual rollout to 100% if metrics look stable.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- No protocol change required; ckpt events use SSE event names and a compact sequence id. SDKs can optionally read them for faster resync, but behavior remains compatible for clients that ignore them.

Known limitations and future work:
- The in-memory ledger doesn't persist across process restarts; in extremely long-lived sessions this could lead to a short window where resyncs are less helpful. A persisted ledger or durable checkpoint is a follow-up item.
- We intentionally set a conservative deferral window; for low-latency workloads we will expose knob tuning in the next PR.

Related tickets and prior art:
- ENG-9421: customer report of partial JSON for tool-enabled streams
- ENG-9487: internal incident postmortem recommending safer delimiter handling

Merge notes:
- Squash-merged into main after reviewer approvals and CI green. No manual conflict resolution was necessary.


Arielle Chen: Nice approach. A couple of questions: why in-memory ledger vs. ephemeral tokens on the emitter? Please add benchmarks for p90 comparisons.
Marcus Valdez: Replied - in-memory ledger avoids cross-goroutine contentions and keeps the write path single-writer; added microbenchmarks in fragment_coordinator_test.go with p50/p90/p99 results.
Priya Nair: Please make the default deferral window configurable via env var and add a note about Dedicated/Private opt-out.
Marcus Valdez: Added feature flag and config (runtime.flag.enable_fragment_coordinator, STREAM_FRAGMENT_DEFERRAL_MS), updated docs and tests.
Liam O'Hara: Integration test flaked once on CI (timing). Please add a small retry for the e2e connection tear-down to reduce non-determinism.
Marcus Valdez: Added deterministic retry and extended test timeout by 200ms; re-ran CI.
Arielle Chen: Approved after fixes. Priya approved. Liam approved.

payload.body:
Motivation: Private installs occasionally fail when init hooks run out-of-order across tenant slices in constrained clusters (observed in multiple customer upgrades). Existing hook sequencing is static and tied to job creation order; operators asked for a lightweight mechanism to express hook inter-dependencies and a values-driven gate that prevents prewarm/pvc claims from racing. This PR adds a terse annotation-based dependency template for Helm hook jobs and a new values schema section `initGates` that enables cluster- or tenant-scoped gating policies. Key goals: 1) allow chart consumers to express 'wait-for:<hook-id>' dependencies on hooks without adding a separate controller; 2) provide a declarative values surface to enable cautious prewarm/pvc claim ordering; 3) keep default behavior unchanged for existing installs.

What this PR contains (summary): - New templating helper `hook.dependencies.tpl` that resolves 'helm.redwood.ai/hook-depends-on' annotations into an init container check loop. - values.schema.json extended with `initGates` schema (max 3 gate profiles, optional gating TTLs, and per-tenant overrides). - Updated `templates/init-job.yaml` and `templates/tenant-seed-job.yaml` to consume the helper and short-circuit job start until dependencies are satisfied (idempotent wait loop). - Added `templates/_helpers.tpl` helpers to render safe annotation keys and gate labels. - README and docs/upgrade-notes describing migration, toggles, and troubleshooting steps. - Unit tests for helper rendering and a small e2e scenario (helm chart template tests) to cover gated startup.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed by infra and installability team (ENG-10342) - [x] Schema validated against Helm lint - [x] Unit tests added for template helpers - [x] Integration e2e rerun to validate gating in minimal k8s - [x] Docs and upgrade notes added - [x] Backwards-compatible defaults preserved

How the annotation-based dependency works (illustrative snippet): "annotations:\n  helm.redwood.ai/hook-id: tenant-seed\n  helm.redwood.ai/hook-depends-on: tenant-db-init,prewarm-claim"\nThe helper expands into an init container that polls for a ConfigMap-based token created by the referenced hooks. The referenced hook jobs, when successful, write a small stamped ConfigMap (name derived from hook-id) that unblocks dependents. This is intentionally light-weight and uses only Kubernetes primitives (ConfigMap + owner references) to avoid adding new controllers.

Values surface (new section): "initGates": {"profiles": [{"name":"conservative","maxParallel":2,"pvcClaimWaitSeconds":45}],"defaultProfile":"conservative","tenantOverrides": {"tenant-a":"aggressive"}}\nDefault is empty and has no gating; cluster operators can opt-in via values or use a global profile in the operator overlay.

Migration and rollout notes: - Default chart behavior is unchanged unless `initGates` is set or hooks annotate `helm.redwood.ai/hook-depends-on`. - For upgrades where existing hooks assume old ordering, enable the gating profile in a staged rollout (canary tenants first). - For air-gapped/private installs, the dependency mechanism uses in-cluster ConfigMaps and does not require external network access. - We ship an `upgrade-notes.md` section that calls out a 5-step canary process.

Security considerations: created ConfigMaps contain only small opaque tokens; we added RBAC snippets so install roles can create/read the token ConfigMaps and are namespaced-scoped by default. Operators who prefer stricter scopes can bind a patch to limit access.

Testing: - unit: template rendering tests (helm template assertions) - integration: scripted helm install/upgrade in KinD with two tenant namespaces showing gated ordering - e2e: flake observed on CI once; reran e2e, green. CI logs reference: build/helm-lint, test/templates, kind-integration (rerun), docs-check.
Maya Patel (reviewer): Can we avoid ConfigMaps and use annotations on Jobs? Reason: ConfigMap churn in very large clusters can be noisy.
Ethan Schultz (author): We considered annotations; however Jobs disappear on completion and we need a stable object to signal across namespaces and ensure idempotence. ConfigMaps are tiny and namespaced; we limited lifecycle and added TTL semantics.
Lina Ortega (reviewer): Please add explicit RBAC to values so operators can opt into least-privileged roles.
Ethan Schultz: Added a `rbacTokenConfig` toggle in values and documented the minimal Role/RoleBinding required.
Harold Kim (approver): Verified templates in KinD and the gating profile worked as expected for 2 tenant namespaces. Approving with suggestion to monitor configmap count in monitoring dashboards post-rollout.
Merge-bot: CI passed after re-run of kind-integration; merging via squash.
Add annotation-driven hook dependencies and optional init gating profiles for private installs. Operators can opt-in via `initGates` values. Backwards compatible unless enabled. See charts/private/docs/upgrade-notes.md for canary checklist and troubleshooting steps.
1) helm template to validate rendering: `helm template . -f values.yaml`
2) install in a test namespace with initGates set to conservative profile
3) create two tenant namespaces and run tenant seeding; observe that dependent hooks wait until their referenced tokens are present
4) rollback: revert values or remove hook annotations; old behavior restored immediately
Enable by setting charts.private.initGates.defaultProfile and apply incrementally. Watch for ConfigMap growth under namespace scope and monitor `helm_init_gate_unblocked_total` (added metric) to observe gating behavior.
This PR intentionally avoids a new controller to keep the installer footprint small. If we see widespread demand for cross-namespace orchestration we can iterate with an opt-in controller in a follow-up PR.

Add a configurable preflight validation job and an atomic rollback hook to the private Helm chart. Motivation: private deployments (VPC / on-prem) often fail during upgrades due to cluster-level preconditions (storageClass mismatches, missing CRDs, networkPolicy constraints) and we lacked a deterministic, observable rollback path when post-install health checks fail. This PR introduces: 1) charts/private/templates/preflight-job.yaml - a templated Job that runs as a pre-install/upgrade hook when values.hooks.preflight.enabled=true; it validates K8s resources, required Secrets, and optionally probes a set of service endpoints listed in values.hooks.preflight.endpoints. 2) charts/private/templates/hooks/rollback-atomic.yaml - a hook that runs on hook failure and attempts a best-effort cleanup and forces a rollback (uses Helm annotations and a short lived Pod with the helm rollback helper script). 3) values.schema.json additions to validate new hook values (timeouts, retries, endpoint list, runPolicy). 4) migration notes and a small helper template (charts/private/templates/_helpers-hooks.tpl) so downstream overlays can reuse the hook annotations. 5) docs: charts/private/README-hooks.md with examples and recommended preflight checks for common on-prem environments. 6) e2e smoke test harness update and a unit test for the template logic. Backwards compatibility: hooks are opt-in (default disabled) and will not change behavior for existing installs. The description below includes high-level commit summary, changed files, CI status and the review thread. NOTE: all explanatory content is contained in a single continuous string per repo policy.
Jun Park: Can we add a shorter default timeout for the preflight job in heavily constrained on-prem clusters? Suggest default 60s per endpoint and total job timeout of 5m.
Asha Patel: Updated defaults in values.yaml and adjusted schema to enforce maximum of 15m per job. Added note in README explaining tradeoffs between endpoint timeouts and overall job runtime.
Miguel Hernandez: The rollback hook looks helpful, but we should ensure it only triggers after a failed post-install hook and not on transient CI failures. Add guard using helm.sh/hook-delete-policy: hook-succeeded
Asha Patel: Added guard, and added a small backoff/retry loop inside the rollback helper script to avoid racing with kube-apiserver during large cluster upgrades.
Emily Chen: Can the preflight job be gated by a feature flag so operators can test without enabling automatic rollbacks? Also request a brief security review for the helper script execution context.
Asha Patel: Preflight is opt-in by default; added note and example for staged rollout. Security review: helper script runs as non-root and we documented required RBAC in README; Security scan CI added a warning for elevated privileges and we adjusted to minimize permissions.
Jun Park (approve): LGTM after defaults/guard changes and docs. Miguel Hernandez (approve): tested on lab cluster (k8s 1.26) and validated rollback path. Emily Chen (approve): Docs and security notes look good.
Add optional preflight validation job and an atomic rollback hook for Private Helm chart. Hooks are disabled by default. Operators can enable hooks.hooks.preflight and configure timeouts/endpoints. Improves upgrade safety for on-prem and VPC deployments.

payload.body:
Summary: Introduce LeaseKeeper (deterministic slot allocator) and a Utilization Smoother to reduce burst-induced jitter and produce stable per-tenant throughput signals for the fleet autoscaler. This change implements a slot lease model with deterministic assignment (no randomized slot shuffles), per-tenant locality buckets to favor cache locality, and a rolling exponential smoother that yields the new smeared_utilization metric for autoscaler / billing consumers.

Motivation: We observed variability in per-tenant utilization signals causing oscillatory autoscaling decisions in Dedicated clusters. The root causes were: nondeterministic slot assignment producing noisy short-lived bursts, and raw instantaneous utilization spikes that propagated into the autoscaler as false positives. The goals are: (1) stabilize utilization time-series, (2) keep short bursts bounded and predictable, (3) prefer locality to reduce KV cache misses.

Design: - LeaseKeeper: central allocator that issues deterministic slot leases for tenants. A slot is owned for a configurable lease_ms; assignments are computed via a deterministic hash+round-robin so that tenants map predictably across restarts (helps testing and debugging). - Locality buckets: tenants are bucketed by node locality tags (region/az/rack) and assigned a locality-weight to prefer slots that keep execution close to cached KV. The allocator falls back to cross-bucket assignment when locality capacity is exhausted. - Utilization Smoother: per-tenant rolling smoother that emits smeared_utilization and peak_tail_percentile metrics. The smoother uses two time constants (fast/slow) and a leakage term so that short spikes decay quickly while sustained load still surfaces. - Autoscaler integration: the fleet autoscaler consumes smeared_utilization instead of raw instantaneous util for scale decisions and exposes an override to fall back to raw util for emergency scaling.

Implementation notes: - New files: src/scheduler/leasekeeper.go, src/scheduler/leasekeeper_test.go, pkg/telemetry/utilization_smoother.go, pkg/telemetry/utilization_smoother_test.go, charts/dedicated/values.yaml (feature toggles), docs/ops/leasekeeper.md, docs/ops/utilization-metrics.md, tests/fixtures/dedicated-locality-buckets.yaml, scripts/measurement/compare-smoothed-vs-raw.py. - LeaseKeeper algorithm: deterministic assignment using tenant_id -> 64-bit hash, mod N_slots_per_node with round-robin offset per-lease-epoch to avoid long-term lockstep. LeaseKeeper maintains a light in-memory lease table and persists short-lived checkpoints to etcd for recovery. - Smoother details: implementation uses a two-pole IIR filter with configurable alpha_fast/alpha_slow and a hysteresis-based peak_tail to preserve tail behavior for SLA evaluation.

Testing: - Unit tests for allocator invariants and smoother edge cases added. - Integration tests simulate tenants with bursty poisson arrivals; validated that autoscaler does not oscillate under controlled synthetic load. - Load experiments on a 48-node dedicated staging cluster showing 22% reduction in autoscaler-triggered scale events and 9% reduction in average cold-KV miss rate for locality-enabled tenants. Test scripts are included under scripts/measurement.

Rollout plan: 1) Feature gate disabled by default. Deploy LeaseKeeper + Smoother as opt-in in staging. 2) Enable for a small set of non-critical tenants in canary mode (1% of production traffic) with observability dashboards. 3) Monitor smeared_utilization vs raw_utilization and autoscaler actions for 72 hours. 4) Gradually expand to 25%/50%/100% after validation.

Backwards compatibility: - Default behavior unchanged unless feature gate is enabled. - Metrics: smeared_utilization is additive to existing metrics; consumers can opt-in.

Metrics / telemetry added: - telemetry.smeared_utilization (gauge per-tenant) - telemetry.leasekeeper_assignments (gauge: slots assigned per-node) - telemetry.slot_lease_ms (histogram) - telemetry.locality_hit_ratio (gauge) - telemetry.autoscaler_input_source (tagged gauge: raw|smoothed) - smoke-test dashboards under console/dedicated/leasekeeper-panel.json

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Docs: ops runbook + metrics reference - [x] Feature gate + helm values entry - [x] Measurement scripts and staging run notes

Release notes: Introduces LeaseKeeper (deterministic slot allocator) and a Utilization Smoother that provide stable per-tenant utilization signals for the fleet autoscaler. Opt-in behind a feature gate; expected to reduce autoscaler oscillation and improve locality-related cache hit rates.

Related work: Addresses oscillation observed in ENG-2017 and SUP-4521 incident postmortem. Complements prior smoothing work in pr-103845 by adding deterministic slot leases and locality prioritization.
Jonas Kline: Please add more integration coverage for node failure scenarios (we need to ensure lease handoff is bounded).
Author (Aisha): Added a new test simulating node restart and documented expected handoff latency; kept lease checkpointing conservative to avoid split-brain.
Marta Ruiz: Suggest renaming smeared_utilization to smoothed_util_pct for consistency with existing metric names.
Author: Keeping smeared_utilization because it reflects the algorithm semantics; added alias metric smoothed_util_pct to ease adoption.
David Chen: Lint flagged a channel leak in early version; fixed and added test.
Approvals: Jonas Kline




Approved, Marta Ruiz




Approved (after renaming alias), David Chen




Approved.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: Private installs in heavily multi-tenant on-prem clusters continue to experience noisy-init storms during rolling upgrades and initial bootstrap. Existing init hooks can overwhelm control-plane and storage when many tenant seeds run concurrently. This PR introduces three complementary safety mechanisms: (1) tenant-scoped `concurrencyQuota` values in chart values to limit concurrent init workers per-tenant, (2) an `overlayGuard` toggle and lightweight admission overlay that gates large value overrides during upgrades (helpful for airgap/managed upgrades), and (3) a hook wrapper that uses a semaphore ConfigMap-based lock to serialize expensive init sub-steps across tenants.

This description is a single continuous string but includes a checklist, rollout notes, and testing steps.

What changed (high level): - Add new schema fields to values.schema.json for `tenantConcurrency.concurrencyQuota`, `tenantConcurrency.semaphoreConfigMapName`, and `overlayGuard.enabled/allowlist` - Add templates/init-quota-configmap.yaml: generates per-tenant quota ConfigMap when `tenantConcurrency.enabled` - Add templates/hooks/semaphore-runner.yaml: a shared wrapper for init hooks which acquires/retries a semaphore token in a central ConfigMap before running expensive substeps - Add helpers/_semaphore.tpl to render acquisition/release commands and backoff policy - Update README/UPGRADING.md with migration notes and recommended default values for on-prem clusters - Add tests/values-tenant-quota.yaml and CI helm unit tests to validate permissive/strict modes

Checklist: - [x] Add values.schema entries and validation - [x] Implement semaphore runner and helper template - [x] Add unit tests for templating and schema validations - [x] Manual integration run against local k3s with 50 simulated tenants - [x] Documentation and upgrade notes in UPGRADING.md - [x] Ensure default is conservative (feature disabled by default)

Testing and validation: I ran the chart template tests in CI and a local k3s harness. Integration steps: (1) deploy with `tenantConcurrency.enabled=false` (baseline) (2) enable `tenantConcurrency.enabled=true` and set `concurrencyQuota: 3` in a staging overlay for 50 tenants, observe init-wave spread and control-plane metrics (3) perform a simulated upgrade with `overlayGuard.enabled=true` to ensure large value overlays are refused unless listed in allowlist. Observed: steady-state CPU on control-plane improved ~38% vs uncontrolled init, no deadlocks during retries, and backoff prevented thundering retries.

Migration notes and rollout strategy: - Default behavior is no-op for existing users. To opt in, set `tenantConcurrency.enabled=true` in tenant overlays and configure `concurrencyQuota`. - For airgap customers, enable `overlayGuard.enabled=true` then populate `overlayGuard.allowlist` with fields you explicitly permit during upgrades. This prevents inadvertent large-scale overrides. - The semaphore uses a small ConfigMap to store token state; this is compatible with RBAC-restricted clusters but requires the chart to have permission to patch the ConfigMap range (documented in RBAC section). - If a cluster cannot support ConfigMap-based semaphores, customers can switch to `semaphoreConfigMapName: "off-cluster-semaphore"` and integrate a CRD-backed locker (operator work tracked in ENG-1307).

Related: ENG-1223 design doc (internal), prior init-rate controller PRs, and SUP-3421 support case for on-prem init storms.

Commit summary: listed below. Merge strategy: squash-merge into main after CI green and two approvals.
Added tenant-scoped init concurrencyQuota and a Helm overlay guard to reduce init storms during upgrades. Also introduces a semaphore-based hook wrapper to ensure safe parallelism across tenants. No breaking changes unless the new features are enabled.
Omar Rivera (reviewer) — 2025-11-05: Nice approach. Two quick asks: (1) can we make the semaphore acquisition exponential backoff configurable? (2) please add a note about RBAC requirements for the ConfigMap patch. 
Maya Chen (author) — 2025-11-06: Reply: added `semaphore.backoff` fields and documented RBAC in UPGRADING.md. Backoff default is conservative (linear then capped exponential).
Priya Nair (reviewer) — 2025-11-08: Security note: can the ConfigMap be used to DOS other tenants? Please ensure token rotation TTL and owner references are present. Also run the chart against an RBAC-restricted cluster in CI. 
Maya Chen (author) — 2025-11-09: Added token TTL, ownerRef for tenant-scoped ConfigMaps, and a CI job that deploys a minimal RBAC-restricted namespace. See ci/helm-unit-tests.yaml. 
Lucas Hoffman (approver) — 2025-11-12: Verified templating and tests. Approving for merge, please squash.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: Private deployments in heavily air-gapped environments often require a deterministic, controllable sequence for bootstrapping tenant data and pre-warming local registries. Existing init jobs were monolithic and could flood node pools (OOMs / image-pull storms) during large multi-tenant installs. This PR introduces an "init-slice" abstraction plus explicit airgap prewarm hooks and a namespace-compatibility guard to make installs safer, more predictable, and operator-friendly.

Summary of changes: 1) values.schema expansions: add `init.slice.enabled`, `init.slice.size`, `init.slice.mode` (tenant|global), and `airgap.prewarm.*` knobs (enabled, concurrency, pullPolicy, registrySecret). 2) templates: `init-slice.yaml` implements a slice iterator that creates N seed jobs per slice with backoff and optional leader-elector to serialize global slices. `hook-prewarm-image.yaml` is a conditional hook that runs before init-slices when `airgap.prewarm.enabled=true` and uses configured registry secrets. 3) `namespace-compatibility.yaml` is a small helper template that either creates tenant namespaces or maps to existing namespaces when `namespaceCompatibility.mode` is set to `legacy` (for clusters converted from older installers). 4) examples: `values.example.airgap.yaml` shows recommended defaults for on-prem installs with pre-pulled images and conservative slice sizes. 5) docs: update `charts/private/README.md` with operational guidance and migration notes for clusters previously using monolithic init jobs.

Commits (high level): - Add values.schema entries and examples: "add init.slice + airgap prewarm values" - Implement init-slice control loop template with leader-elector support: "init slice template + leader-elector" - Add prewarm hook and namespace compatibility helper + docs: "airgap prewarm hook + README"

Files changed (high level): - charts/private/values.schema.yaml: new schema blocks for init.slice and airgap.prewarm with descriptions, allowed values and defaults. - charts/private/templates/init-slice.yaml: new Job manifest with templated slice loop, `{{- if .Values.init.slice.enabled }}` guards, tolerations and resource queues for slice jobs. - charts/private/templates/hook-prewarm-image.yaml: annotated Helm hook for pre-install and pre-upgrade with optional concurrency and backoff. - charts/private/templates/namespace-compatibility.yaml: helper template to resolve namespace mapping. - charts/private/values.example.airgap.yaml: example prewarm registry secret and slice sizing for 50-tenant clusters. - charts/private/README.md: operations notes and migration checklist. - helmfile.d/airgap-prewarm.yaml: Helmfile entry for airgapped CI integration tests.

Testing and CI: Initial CI run flagged a linting error where the schema required `airgap.prewarm.concurrency` to be integer > 0; I fixed the schema and added unit-like template tests (helm template + `--values` smoke checks) into the existing chart test harness. On second run all checks passed: lint, template, kubeval (subset), and CI smoke tests for an example airgap values file.

Review conversation (summary, single-threaded): - Aisha: "Can we make slice.size a soft cap and ensure jobs don't all schedule at once? Also please add a template test that asserts the leader-elector annotations are present when mode=global." Author: "Added a preflight probe + leader-elector annotation check in the chart test harness and made slice scheduling respect `init.slice.maxConcurrent` (defaults to 2)." - Diego: "Tolerations look aggressive for some on-prem clusters — can you default to empty and allow cluster ops to opt-in? Also suggest a default backoff window." Author: "Changed tolerations to opt-in via `init.slice.tolerations` (empty by default) and set exponential backoff with jitter (initial 10s, max 5m). Updated README with recommended ops values for bare-metal." - Priya: "We need clear release notes and a migration path for clusters that relied on old init jobs." Author: "Added a migration section to README and a helper `namespaceCompatibility.mode=legacy` to preserve previous behavior. Also included a small helmfile entry for operators to dry-run the prewarm step."

Backward compatibility and migration: This change is additive and disabled by default (`init.slice.enabled=false`, `airgap.prewarm.enabled=false`). Migration steps are documented: operators can flip `init.slice.enabled=true` with conservative `slice.size` and `maxConcurrent` to ramp. For clusters that relied on previous implicit namespace creation, `namespaceCompatibility.mode=legacy` preserves behavior.

Operational notes: - For very large installs, set `init.slice.size` to number of tenants per slice (suggest 10-50 depending on node capacity). - Use `airgap.prewarm.concurrency` to limit simultaneous registry pulls (defaults to 3). - When using `mode=global` leader-elector will ensure only one slice performs global migration steps. - The prewarm hook is idempotent and annotated with a `pre-install` hook weight to run before any seed jobs.

Checklist: - [x] values.schema additions and validation - [x] template implementation with tests - [x] docs and examples - [x] CI green after fixes - [x] reviewers addressed comments

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into `main` after approvals from all reviewers.

Notes for release: see `release_notes` field for a short summary operators can include in their changelogs.
Add optional init-slice for bootstrapping, optional airgap image prewarm hook, and namespace compatibility helper. Disabled by default; see README for migration steps and recommended default values for on-prem installs.

payload.body:
Motivation: Private installs (airgap / on-prem) have accumulated multiple ad-hoc init jobs and templating overlays that are difficult to reason about during upgrades and rollbacks. This PR introduces a lightweight tenant bootstrap finite-state-machine (FSM) and an explicit 'bootstrap values contract' to: 1) sequence init steps deterministically, 2) expose safe knobs (timeouts, concurrency, backoff), and 3) provide a machine-readable values schema that CI and preflight checks can validate. This is opt-in: behavior is unchanged unless values.bootstrap.enabled = true.

What changed (high level):
- Add a bootstrap FSM implementation in templates/bootstrap-fsm.yaml that models phases: preflight -> image-prepull -> secret-sync -> db-migrate -> tenant-seed -> verify -> ready. Each phase maps to a Job with guarded transitions.
- Add values.bootstrap.* contract in values.schema.json and documented examples in values/bootstrap.example.yaml. Contract fields include: concurrencyLimit, phaseTimeouts, backoffStrategy, resumePolicy, maxRetries, and feature gates for airgap flows.
- New Helm helper templates (charts/_helpers.tpl) to render phase annotations and to inject rollback-fence annotations to prevent partial upgrades from leaving tenants in an inconsistent state.
- Add a lightweight preflight-check hook (templates/preflight-hook.yaml) wired to the FSM start phase to fail early on missing secrets/images in airgap mode.
- Add README section (charts/README-BOOTSTRAP.md) with recommended safe defaults for on-prem and an explanation of FSM states and failure modes.
- Conservative unit tests and a chart-testing workflow to validate the values contract and a small integration run in a KIND cluster for the happy-path.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc (linked in ENG-2217)
- [x] Helm lint and schema validations
- [x] Integration sanity run (KIND)
- [x] Docs and example values
- [x] Reviewed by infra/sre and charts teams

How to opt-in: set values.bootstrap.enabled = true and adjust values.bootstrap.phaseTimeouts and values.bootstrap.concurrencyLimit for your tenant scale. See charts/README-BOOTSTRAP.md for recommended profiles.

Notes on rollback safety: the FSM writes per-tenant bootstrap state to an init ConfigMap and attaches a rollback.fence annotation while a sequence is in-flight. The rollback guard prevents helm from performing a blind upgrade on resources that are mid-bootstrap unless the operator clears the fence or the resumePolicy allows automatic recovery. This avoids half-applied migrations and orphaned seed jobs.

Compatibility: The FSM is implemented using standard Kubernetes Job/ConfigMap primitives and follows existing RBAC scopes. No CRDs were introduced to keep the surface area minimal for airgapped customers.

References: ENG-2217 (design), tickets SUP-431 (customer-reported stuck-init) and INT-612 (upgrade flakiness during tenant seeding).
Introduce a tenant bootstrap state-machine and an explicit values contract to make airgapped/on-prem installs deterministic and easier to validate. No behavioral breaking changes when not enabled; opt-in via values.bootstrap.enabled.
Oliver Hayes: Can we make phase timeouts per-phase with sensible defaults? (Requested change)
Priya Menon: Addressed — added values.bootstrap.phaseTimeouts with defaults for preflight/image-prepull/migrate/seed/verify and documented rationale.
Rui Zhang: RBAC looks broad in the initial patch; can we ensure jobs only have namespace-scoped rights and follow least-privilege?
Priya Menon: Updated roles to use explicit verbs and only allow configmap/job/secret operations in the tenant namespace (see templates/rbac-tenant-bootstrap.yaml).
Marta Silva: Would like a way to mark a tenant bootstrap as manual resume in case of persistent external failures. (Suggestion)
Priya Menon: Added values.bootstrap.resumePolicy = [auto|manual|limited] and a small note in README describing operator actions for manual resumes.
Example enable snippet:

bootstrap:
  enabled: true
  concurrencyLimit: 6
  phaseTimeouts:
    preflight: 5m
    imagePrepull: 15m
    migrate: 20m
    seed: 10m
    verify: 3m
  resumePolicy: auto
  backoffStrategy: exponential

See charts/bootstrap/values/bootstrap.example.yaml for full profiles (onprem.small/onprem.large/cloud-default).
payload.title: Add tenant bootstrap FSM and values contract for safer airgap/on-prem installs

payload.body:
Motivation: Private/on-prem installs continue to surface flaky init sequencing and unclear values validation that lead to mid-upgrade failures. This PR compacts the init pipeline into three deterministic stages, centralizes values schema validation, and introduces a lightweight preflight probe to fail fast on common misconfiguration (networking, missing secrets, wrong CIDR). Changes here are focused on the Helm chart surface for the private installer and companion examples used by the terraform module.

Summary of changes: compact init pipeline (prepare -> connect -> finalise), strict values schema (OpenAPI-style JSONSchema for top-level values), templating helpers to reduce repeated conditionals, idempotent init-job wrappers, and a preflight hook that runs as a short-lived Job with clear diagnostics. Also adds example values for VPC and airgapped installs and documents required KMS/secret keys.

Migration notes: Charts that previously relied on per-component init hooks should move to the new three-stage lifecycle. Automatic mapping helpers are provided, but operators must verify custom hooks that assumed previous ordering. Values keys deprecated: init.oldSequence -> init.stages (migrator prints a warning). No automatic secret rotation is performed by this PR.

Implementation details: - values.schema.yaml: a concise JSONSchema that validates top-level keys (network, storage, init, secrets, upgrade). The schema intentionally keeps model-specific tuning out of the chart to avoid frequent churn. - templates/_init-helpers.tpl: helper templates for stage gating, backoff annotations, and leader-elector hints. - templates/init-job-compact.yaml: produces a single Job per stage with annotated fence ConfigMap to prevent overlapping runs. Jobs are idempotent and use a consistent checkpoint path in the tenant PVC. - templates/preflight-job.yaml: short Job that verifies DNS resolvability, KMS access (optional), and cluster resource requests; returns structured diagnostics in a pod log artifact stored on completion. - values/examples/*: added vpc-example.yaml and airgap-example.yaml with minimal required fields and notes.

Testing and rollout: Ran integration deploys in our internal staging environment across three topologies (single-tenant VPC, multi-az VPC, airgapped on-prem VM). Smoke tests for install/upgrade/rollback paths passed. CI: lint/chart tests + unit schema validation + e2e smoke job. Canary rollout plan: merge to release branch, cut a candidate bundle consumed by the private-installer job, and run tenant-scoped dryruns for 5 customers before wide rollout.

Checklist: - [x] values schema added and covered by unit tests - [x] init templates refactored and idempotency addressed - [x] preflight probe implemented - [x] updated examples and docs - [x] integration smoke runs in staging

Related work: this complements ENG-1171 (hook reconciliation improvements) and the private-installer terraform module updates in ENG-1304.
Evan Park: Nice consolidation. Two asks: (1) prove the fence ConfigMap is safe under concurrent upgrades, (2) can we keep the preflight probe optional via a values toggle?
Isabel Ramos: Addressed: fence now uses annotation-based mutex with exponential backoff; preflight job enabled by default but controlled by values.preflight.enabled. Added docs and tests.
Maya Kaur: The JSONSchema looks strict — raise a migration warning rather than failing older installs. Also suggest a clear example for KMS optional path.

Background: private installs of Redwood need safer upgrade and init paths when tenants are numerous or networking is constrained. This PR adds a compact set of Helm safety rails: a validated values.schema.json for tenant bootwave and init sequencing, optional graceful-prelude init job, and templated annotations to guard rollback/upgrade windows. Motivation: previous incidents showed opaque failures during multi-tenant preflight and seeding; automation must make implicit assumptions explicit and fail fast with actionable errors.

What this PR does: Adds a consolidated values schema (charts/private/values.schema.json) that documents and validates the new 'bootwave' config object: concurrency profiles, jitter windows, API preflight probes and quota hints. Introduces a lightweight templated 'prelude' init job (templates/init-prelude-job.yaml) that can optionally run pre-seed connectivity checks and emit step-level events to the hook controller. Adds hook annotations and a new 'safeRollout' template helper to ensure rollbacks are gated on a quorum of tenant seeds completing successfully. Also updates NOTES.txt and README with migration guidance and a short troubleshooting list.

Compatibility and migration: The schema is additive and defaulted to the current behavior. Clusters using stricter policy will get validation failures on helm install/upgrade unless they opt into the new values object or set 'bootwave.enabled=false'. Documented migration steps included. For on-prem customers using the Private installer, the PR also includes a small change to the installer overlay to map terraform-provided 'seed_concurrency' into the chart values.

Testing and rollout: unit tests for schema validation and helm template rendering were added (tests/helm-schema-test.sh). End-to-end canary performed in our staging tenant-slice with 120 tenants and a seeded jitter profile; the bootwave prelude prevented a mass seeding retry storm observed in previous runs. CI: lint -> template -> unit tests passed; e2e run was performed manually in staging.

Risks and mitigations: introducing user-visible validation can block installs; mitigated by conservative defaults, clear error messages and a single-step escape hatch 'bootwave.enabled=false'. Operational docs include sample values for common environments.

Related: ENG-4271 (tenant bootwave design), PRs that touched hooks and init sequencing.
Marcelo Ruiz: left a few nits on the schema messages — please make the validation errors actionable (include expected range and example).
Priya Patel: addressed the schema messages, added example snippets and a link to the troubleshooting section in README. PTAL.
Evelyn Wright: Canary looked good; I want to see a guard in the prelude job to avoid requeue storms if network flaps repeatedly. Suggested exponential backoff and a max-retries field.
Priya Patel: added 'prelude.retryPolicy' with backoff params and capped retries; updated tests to simulate transient failures.
Jonah Lee: CI flaked on the e2e provision step, reran and all checks green. Approving changes.
Marcelo Ruiz: approved — schema and templating look clean.
- Add bootwave values schema and tenant concurrency profiles
- Optional prelude init job for safe seeding and connectivity preflight
- Hook annotations and helper templates to gate rollbacks
- Installer overlay mapping for terraform seed concurrency
When upgrading clusters with many tenants, consider increasing the default 'bootwave.jitterWindow' to spread seed traffic; to bypass validation temporarily set 'bootwave.enabled=false' in values. For Private installer customers using Terraform, ensure the 'seed_concurrency' output is present in the overlay mapping.

Motivation: customers running Redwood Private in multi-AZ/on-prem topologies reported long manual windows when performing Postgres primary failovers across AZs (VIP moves, datastore fencing, and cache sync). This PR implements an opinionated, automatable quorum-shift workflow that can be invoked as part of DR drills and automated failovers. The goal is to reduce manual steps, provide safe rollbacks, and validate restores as code. High level: 1) Terraform module to atomically shift a virtual IP (VIP) and update firewall routes; 2) Ansible orchestrator playbook that coordinates operator actions (promote, demote, drain), runs pre/post checks, applies fencing if needed, and calls the Terraform VIP shift as a sub-step; 3) Helm chart updates to the postgres-operator that expose safe promotion hooks and a readiness probe to detect in-flight replication lag; 4) Runbooks-as-code (Markdown) that codify the drill steps and include automated checklists; 5) A restore-validation script and E2E test to exercise snapshot restore after quorum shift. Implementation notes: - Everything is feature-gated behind installer flag 'enable_dr_quorum_shift' to avoid changing behavior for existing installs. - Terraform module placed under terraform/modules/vip-shift with support for multiple providers (MetalLB, Keepalived). - Ansible playbook ansible/playbooks/quorum_shift.yml is idempotent and includes --check dry-run support as well as interactive mode. - Helm updates in helm/charts/postgres-operator/ add two new hooks: pre-promote and post-demote along with configurable wait timeouts. - docs/runbooks/dr_quorum_shift.md contains step-by-step, expected outcomes, mitigation steps, and automated rollback snippet. Testing: local unit tests for the Terraform module with terratest wrappers, Ansible linting and molecule scenarios (mocked), CI E2E that runs a simulated cluster using kind + containerized Postgres operator and invokes the playbook followed by restore-validation.sh. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module + docs - [x] Ansible orchestrator playbook - [x] Helm operator hooks + values - [x] Runbooks-as-code - [x] E2E validation test - [x] CI workflow to run the drill in sandbox Security considerations: the Terraform module requires change control for VIPs; the playbook enforces least-privilege service accounts when interacting with K8s APIs. Rollback strategy: the orchestrator supports an automatic rollback path (reverse steps) if post-checks fail; there is also a manual rollback section in the runbook that documents how to reassign VIP and re-declare the previous primary. Linear/Jira: related to ENG-5312, SRE-402, and SUP-1187. Links: internal runbook: docs/runbooks/dr_quorum_shift.md.
Adds automated quorum-shift tooling for on-prem Postgres clusters: Terraform VIP shift module, Ansible orchestrator playbook, Helm operator tweaks, runbooks-as-code, and end-to-end validation tests. Backwards compatible; feature gated behind installer flag.
Jordan Reyes: Overall looks solid. Two asks: (1) increase default promotion timeout to 5m to avoid flaky CI; (2) add explicit CRD readiness check before demotion. Please address and request another review.
Maya Chen: Thanks — bumped default to 5m and added CRD readiness check in ansible tasks. Also added a note about controlling pod disruption budgets in the runbook.
Priya Nair: CI flake observed on first run: terraform provider timeout when provider returned 409 on VIP create. Recommend adding retry with exponential backoff in module. Also confirm provider compatibility with Keepalived vs MetalLB.
Maya Chen: Added retry wrapper around provider calls and documented provider compatibility matrix in terraform/modules/vip-shift/README.md. CI re-run requested.
CI Bot: initial run failed (terraform apply timeout). Rerun triggered by @Maya Chen.
CI Bot: subsequent run succeeded (all checks green).
Tom Becker: Approved after verifying e2e passes in sandbox and reading runbook. +1 for runbooks-as-code format.
Initial pipeline failed on terraform apply timeout. Fixed by adding provider retries and increasing timeouts. Subsequent pipeline run passed all lint, unit tests, molecule, and e2e validations.
Local verification: molecule scenario 'dr_orchestrator' passed against containerized Postgres nodes. Terratest wrapper validates VIP shift for MetalLB and Keepalived providers. E2E run in CI exercised full converge -> promote -> VIP shift -> post-checks -> snapshot -> restore -> restore-validation.sh.
Feature is disabled by default. To enable set installer flag 'enable_dr_quorum_shift: true' and review terraform provider credentials. Run the included ansible playbook with --check for a dry-run. Ensure snapshots are available before promoting primary.
Merged via squash merge after sign-off from SRE and infra leads. No database schema changes; low risk but recommend scheduling non-business hours for initial rollout on customer clusters.
Added DR orchestration: automated Postgres quorum shift (Terraform VIP shift, Ansible orchestrator, Helm operator hooks, runbooks-as-code, e2e validation).

Add optional post-upgrade cleanup hook and explicit values.schema.json for Redwood Private Helm chart; refactor helpers for init/postupgrade hooks; add an integration test for upgrade scenarios.
Motivation: Private installs occasionally leave transient cluster objects (temp PVs, breadcrumb ConfigMaps) after upgrade paths that changed storage/retention policies. Operators need a safe, opt-in post-upgrade cleanup hook that can be enabled in values and validated by an explicit values.schema.json. This PR implements an optional post-upgrade cleanup Helm hook, adds a JSON schema for values validation, and refactors common helpers so init and post-upgrade hooks share templating primitives.

What I changed (summary): commits: 1) add values.schema.json and update values.yaml defaults; 2) introduce templates/hooks/post-upgrade-cleanup.yaml implementing a Job hook guarded by .Values.postUpgrade.cleanup.enabled; 3) refactor templates/_helpers.tpl to expose hook labels and common container/env helpers shared with init-job.yaml; 4) add a minimal integration test charts/private/tests/upgrade-scenario.sh that simulates a canary upgrade and asserts the cleanup job runs only when enabled; 5) small README update documenting the new flag and migration notes.

Key behaviors and decisions: - The cleanup hook is explicitly opt-in: values.postUpgrade.cleanup.enabled is false by default. When enabled the hook runs as a Helm post-upgrade hook with policy: hook-delete-policy:hook-succeeded. The job is namespaced and uses the same serviceAccount as the init-job when present. - The job is tolerant: uses exponential backoff and a --dry-run mode controlled via values.postUpgrade.cleanup.dryRun for safer rollouts. - To avoid breaking existing installs we added values.schema.json that marks all new keys as optional and provides deprecation notes for legacy top-level keys. This allows CI (helm lint --values) + custom validation to catch misconfigurations. - We refactored helpers into templates/_helpers.tpl to keep templates DRY and reduce divergence between init and post-upgrade hook logic.

Files changed (high-level): - charts/private/values.schema.json: explicit schema for postUpgrade.cleanup, initJob, and common hook controls. - charts/private/templates/hooks/post-upgrade-cleanup.yaml: CronJob->Job style post-upgrade hook (Job) that runs the cleanup container, reads retention rules from a ConfigMap and exits gracefully when nothing to clean. - charts/private/templates/init-job.yaml: small adjustments to use the shared helpers and to expose the existing sa name via helper. - charts/private/templates/_helpers.tpl: new helpers to render hook annotations, labels, and job container command composition. - charts/private/tests/upgrade-scenario.sh: basic e2e-ish script used in CI job input to validate that enabling flag causes job creation and successful completion. - charts/private/README.md: documentation for new values, examples to enable cleanup, and troubleshooting notes.

Review notes and conversation snapshot: - Diego Alvarez: requested stronger schema coverage for the dryRun field and suggested moving the default imagePullPolicy to values.global to match other charts. I addressed both and pushed a follow-up commit that updated values.schema.json and values.yaml. - Priya Natarajan: asked for an escape hatch when the cleanup job misbehaves (she requested a configurable backoffLimit and a toggle to restrict runtime). I added values.postUpgrade.cleanup.backoffLimit and a short note in README about controlling the job lifecycle. - Samir Gupta: ran the upgrade-scenario test in his dev cluster and reported a lint failure due to a missing helper; I fixed the _helpers.tpl order and re-ran CI.

CI: The pipeline originally failed one lint step due to a templating order (fixed in 2nd commit). Full CI run after fixes: helm/lint -> pass, unit/templates -> pass, integration/upgrade-scenario -> pass (the script runs in a mocked KinD job in CI and verifies job creation and logs).

Compatibility and migration: This is non-breaking by default; the cleanup job is disabled unless explicitly enabled. values.schema.json is additive and marks legacy keys as deprecated but not removed. Operators upgrading the chart can enable cleanup post-upgrade after confirming retention rules.

Testing performed: - Local helm template runs against k8s 1.26 and 1.27 manifests. - Integration script executed in CI with KinD cluster; tested both enabled and disabled states. - Manual run in a staging cluster to validate ServiceAccount permissions and RBAC scoping.

Merge outcome: Approved by reviewers after two rounds of feedback. CI green. Squash-merged into main on 2026-02-25 with a brief merge commit.

Notes for follow-ups: - Consider exposing a metrics endpoint for the cleanup job for observability (ENG-3820). - Add a safety-mode that requires a specific annotation on the release to permit cleanup in production environments.

Motivation: Teams reported that credential rotation and stream consumer ergonomics still required per-SDK boilerplate and fragile window-handling (time-based TTL checks + ad-hoc backoff). This PR introduces a small, well-documented runtime-agnostic credential swapper and a lightweight stream adapter that normalizes generator/pullstream ergonomics across Python, TypeScript, and Go. Goals: (1) Provide a single credential profile format (json/yaml doc + typed bindings) so SDKs can offer the same default behavior; (2) Offer an ergonomic token-swapper API that minimizes surface area (start/stop, lease callbacks, fallback chain); (3) Supply a generator-friendly stream facade that supports pause/resume, checkpointed resume tokens, and explicit heartbeat hints without changing underlying transport protocols; (4) Bump SDK minimums where needed and add compatibility tests. Changeset summary: - Added credentials/profile schema and docs at sdk/credentials/schema.md - Implemented a tiny `CredentialSwapper` shim in python/ts/go SDKs with the same semantic surface (Start(), RefreshIfNeeded(), Handoff()) - Introduced `stream-facade` helpers that wrap transport iterables and expose a small, language-idiomatic API: pause(), resume(), checkpoint() - Added end-to-end parity tests in internal/e2e/cred-stream-parity (matrix py/ts/go across node/python runner) - CI: expanded the matrix with a credential rotation stress job and reduced flakiness by adding deterministic time helpers - Docs: cross-SDK snippets and a migration guide under docs/sdk/migrations/cred-swapper.md Migration notes: existing consumers that implemented their own token rotation should continue to work; recommended path is to adopt the swapper by calling CredentialSwapper.wrap(existingProvider()) and opt into the new heartbeat hints. Checklist: - [x] Credential profile schema and examples - [x] Implementations for Python, TypeScript, Go - [x] Cross-SDK unit and e2e parity tests - [x] Docs and migration guide - [x] Version bumps: python v1.29.0, ts v1.27.3, go v1.8.0 - [x] CI matrix updated Tests and validation: described in test_plan below. Backwards compat: design preserves existing provider interfaces via adapter helpers; breaking_change=false. Related: ENG-3214 (auth-lease-stability), SDK-908 (stream-ergonomics).

Motivation: We need deterministic and auditable private control plane provisioning for customers deploying Redwood Private. This change pins external Terraform module versions via a repository-level lockfile, introduces a light Helm chart provisioner that the installer uses to create control-plane Kubernetes primitives, and wires end-to-end CI/e2e checks so module changes do not silently break subnet/endpoint creation. Summary: 1) Add terraform.lock.hcl at the installer root with exact provider/module checksums and update CI to validate lockfile consistency. 2) Introduce a small Helm chart (helm/controlplane-provisioner) used by the installer in the 'plan' stage to render Job manifests that run subnet assignment and endpoint creation logic. 3) Add migration helper scripts (scripts/migrate/controlplane-subnet-migrate.sh) to perform atomic subnet handoffs with pre/post DNS stamps and a safe rollback marker. 4) Update Terraform modules usage to a pinned source and bumped module inputs for conditional Privatelink provisioning. 5) Add a rollback-ready flag and a reconciliation worker toggle that can be enabled via installer config. Why this is different: prior PRs have focused on subnet allocation or DNS stitching in isolation; this PR ties module version management and chart-driven provisioning together so a module update cannot be applied without CI ensuring the corresponding Helm chart and migration path exist. Checklist: - [x] Add terraform.lock.hcl and CI check - [x] Add helm/controlplane-provisioner chart skeleton and simple templated Job - [x] Wire installer to use Helm chart during apply (chart rendered in dry-run for customers) - [x] Add migration script with idempotent mark-and-sweep step - [x] Add e2e smoke test that simulates a small subnet reallocation and DNS stamp validation - [x] Document operator-facing rollback steps in docs/installer/upgrade-readme.md How to validate locally: run ./scripts/dev/with-kind.sh then ./scripts/migrate/controlplane-subnet-migrate.sh --dry-run --stamp=ci-test; run terraform init && terraform validate --lockfile=readonly CI notes: The change adds a new pipeline stage 'lockfile-verify' that fails if terraform.lock.hcl is out of sync, and an e2e stage that deploys the helm chart into a ephemeral cluster. Tests flaked once on first run (helm timeout), fixed by increasing probe timeouts. Rollout plan: squash-merge into main, monitor canary customer namespaces for 48h (feature gated by toggle), then flip reconciliation worker to on by default after 72h if no regressions observed.
