Motivation: customers want lightweight per-invocation signals for alerting and perf triage without the overhead of full-span hydration. This PR adds a slimline metric set (compact counters/histograms) emitted at the invocation boundary together with a small log-anchoring protocol that lets sampled traces pull the most relevant log snippets for quick RCA. Goals: 1) provide low-cardinality, high-signal invocation metrics that fit retention/ingestion budgets; 2) enable cheap, deterministic linkage between a metric-level anomaly and a small, developer-friendly log excerpt; 3) preserve existing tracing semantics and sampling decisions. What is included: - invocation_slimline metrics: invocation.count, invocation.error_rate, invocation.latency_slab, invocation.token_delta (per-100-token buckets), invocation.hotpath_flag. Metrics are emitted by the serving runtime at the finalization step to avoid double-counting and to be robust to retries. - log anchoring protocol: lightweight anchor tokens are attached to metric emits and to a small log cache. When a metric indicates an anomaly, the UI can request anchored log excerpts for the failed invocation id. Anchors are short, reversible tokens (not secrets) and include minimal context (route, model_version, anchor_ts). - Sampling and retention: default sampler keeps 0.5% of invocations fully hydrated, with a burst window to 5% for detected anomalies. Slimline metrics are always emitted (low cardinality) and designed for long retention. - Dashboard assets: an invocation-timeline dashboard to visualize slimline histograms, hotpath markers, and anchored log excerpts. - Docs and runbook: README and runbook for oncall explaining how to interpret slimline signals and how to initiate an anchored log fetch. Design notes: - Kept metric labels minimal: tenant_id (sharded), model_family, route, stage. No free-form prompt content. - Anchors are stored in a bounded in-memory LRU cache on each arena for up to 60s; archival copies flow to the log-archiver for longer retention if requested by the user. - Backwards compatibility: if the anchoring module is disabled, only slimline metrics emit; no tracing changes required. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of slimline metric emissary in runtime finalizer - [x] Anchoring token generator and cache with eviction policy - [x] End-to-end integration test + unit tests for sampler thresholds - [x] Dashboard JSON and Grafana panels - [x] Docs and runbook - [x] Perf validation: <1% p95 latency add on microbench harness Migration/rollout: feature gated behind observability.feature_slimline. Default off for customers on Dedicated; rollout staged for hosted customers. Operational knobs exposed: slimline.sampling_rate, anchor.cache_size, anchor.ttl_seconds. Related: this PR complements ENG-2312 (contextual cost explorer) and ENG-2356 (alert-weighted sampling). The description of changed files, commits, and reviews below contain implementation details and rationale.
Connor Lee: Nice approach keeping label cardinality low. Two requests: can we avoid tenant_id on the hotpath flag and instead use tenant_shard? Also please add a sample of the metric protobuf used for ingestion.
Author (Aisha Patel): Reply: switched hotpath label to tenant_shard (implemented). Added metric protobuf example in runtime/telemetry/invocation_slimline.go comments.

Author (Aisha Patel): Reply: sanitize pipeline added; logs pass through redact.LogSanitize with default redact rules. Updated docs with sanitization behaviour.
Ethan Brooks: Suggest adding a feature flag for raising the sampler during incident playbooks. Also noted a potential race in anchor_cache eviction under burst -- added a mutex in latest commit.
Author (Aisha Patel): Reply: added observability.sampler.boost_window_seconds and fixed eviction race with mutex and tests.
Connor Lee (approve): LGTM after docs tweaks
María Gómez (approve): Approved
Ethan Brooks (approve): Approved

Unit tests cover sampler thresholds and eviction; e2e harness validates <1% latency overhead on p95 for a 1000qps workload. Integration tests exercised anchor fetch flow and UI panel rendering with mocked log excerpts.
Benchmarks (microbench harness) show median latency change <0.2ms and p95 change <1% with default sampling. Emitting slimline metrics increases cardinality by 4 labels but uses low-cardinality design and sharding to keep ingestion costs modest.
Oncall runbook: - If invocation.count spikes with error_rate increase, open anchored log for top routes; use sampler.boost to capture a wider window. - Use invocation.token_delta histogram to assess prompt/response token cost shifts. - Hotpath_flag marks requests that touched fallback models or retried KV cache misses. - If false positives observed, lower sampler.boost_window_seconds or increase anomaly threshold.

Motivation: continuous batching and kernel selection yield large perf wins but expose correctness risk when mixed-precision kernels and KV-cache corner cases interact. This PR introduces a fallback orchestrator that gates the fast path (optimized kernels + speculative scheduling) and gracefully falls back to a safe-mode execution when heuristics detect precision instability or KV cache mismatch. Summary of changes: 1) fastpath gating layer: lightweight runtime hook that evaluates a per-request heuristic (sequence length variance, kv-hit-ratio, requested precision) and routes to 'fast' or 'safe' execution. 2) kernel_selector: new scoring to prefer stable kernels for paths flagged as 'safe' and aggressive low-precision kernels for 'fast'. 3) kv_cache: additional validation pass and a compact mismatch detector that triggers safe-mode without invalidating the whole cache. 4) continuous_batcher: batching policy extension to allow heterogeneous batches where safe and fast items can co-reside with confined isolation; introduces a micro-batch spill to preserve latency SLOs. 5) config: precision_profile and runtime flags to tune gating sensitivity and to force safe-mode for debugging. Design tradeoffs: the gating heuristic is conservative by default (prioritizes correctness) but exposes a tunable curve for teams willing to trade correctness margins for throughput. Performance: on internal Llama-2-13B evaluation the fast-path increases throughput by ~28% and reduces p95 token latency by ~12% for homogeneous workloads; mixed workloads saw a 9-15% throughput gain with negligible correctness regressions when heuristics tuned. Testing: unit tests for selector and cache detector, integration tests that run end-to-end with BFloat16/FP16 toggles, and a stress bench that simulates cache churn. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind `runtime.fallback_orchestrator.enabled`; staged rollout to Dedicated pools then Hosted, with telemetry gating and a rollback switch. Related: ENG-1479, ENG-1534. This description is a single continuous string and includes design notes, tradeoffs, and rollout instructions.
Miguel Santos: Overall approach looks solid. Can we make the gating heuristic pluggable so teams can replace it with model-specific signals?
Author (Asha Patel): Yes, the orchestrator exposes a trait and a registration point; added an example in docs and tests to show swapping heuristics.
Olivia Chen: The heterogeneous micro-batching is clever but worried about head-of-line blocking under pathological mixes; do we have a backpressure strategy?
Author (Asha Patel): Added micro-batch spill and a per-queue token budget to bound latency impact; included stress bench results in perf tests.
Benji Kumar: kv_cache mismatch detector must not be a silent invalidation — add metrics and a non-destructive debug mode.
Author (Asha Patel): Implemented non-destructive validation and telemetry; added fallback_metrics for ops to trace incidents.
CI Bot: perf-regression check reported +3% on a narrow synthetic; please confirm this is acceptable for initial rollout.
Author (Asha Patel): Confirmed; added a tuning guide and default is conservative. We will gate by telemetry for Hosted rollout.
Introduce fallback orchestrator to gate fast-path kernels and provide a safe-mode fallback for continuous batching; add tunable precision profiles and KV cache validation; default conservative settings prioritize correctness; rollout behind feature flag and telemetry.

Motivation: Private installs often require tenant-specific connector profiles (region, network, pre-warm images) and a safe initialization flow that prevents concurrent snapshot/migration collisions during rolling upgrades. This PR adds a derived connectorProfiles values section and a phase-aware safe-snapshot init orchestration for the private Helm chart so operators can rely on declarative defaults while retaining overrides for on-prem and VPC deployments.

What this changes (high level):
- Adds a top-level values block `connectorProfiles` which allows schema-driven derived profiles for tenants (e.g. region-aware imagePullSecrets, networkPolicyHints, prewarmProfiles). The chart renders the final connector config by composing `global.defaultConnector` with per-profile overrides.
- Introduces `init.safeSnapshot` machinery: a helm template and init job that coordinates a lightweight lock (ConfigMap lease) to serialize snapshot/migration-critical steps across namespaces in a cluster. The job is optional and scoped by `connectorProfiles[].snapshotScope`.
- Phase-aware concurrency: init hooks now accept `phaseConcurrency` values (per-phase and per-zone jitter) and a backpressure window to avoid overloading on-prem storage or network during seed phases.
- New helpers and template functions in `_helpers.tpl` for deterministic profile merging and safe-lease naming.
- Updates values.schema.json with explicit types, defaults, and examples to make `helm install --validate` safer for operators.
- Adds unit Helm template tests and a simple integration harness for the init job using the existing canary lab framework.

Fixes a class of customer-facing streaming failures observed when clients disconnect mid-stream and then reconnect or retry. This PR centralizes stream teardown logic, adds an explicit session idempotency token for resume/reconnect, implements server-side exponential backoff for automatic retry attempts, and updates the OpenAI-compatibility adapter to preserve in-flight function/tool-call state across reconnects. Key goals: 1) avoid duplicate function/tool calls on client reconnect, 2) ensure server timeouts produce a deterministic terminal event that client SDKs can use for cleanup, 3) make streaming retries safe under load without amplifying downstream work. This is implemented as a small runtime change plus adapter and SDK patches and includes unit+integration tests and a controlled rollout plan. Migration notes: server behavior is backward-compatible for clients that don't use resume tokens; SDKs should be updated to take advantage of resume and idempotency tokens to prevent duplicate tool calls. Rollout: staged on Dedicated for 48h, monitor stream-error-rate and duplicate-tool-call metrics, then full rollout to hosted API.

Author (Jinsoo): Added reconnect_test.go that simulates a long tool and asserts single invocation; we also added a server-side in-progress marker to prevent dupes.

Author: Applied suggested defaults and exported retry_attempts metric; documented in console alert playbook.
Ethan Brooks: OpenAI adapter event naming changed from 'done' to 'complete' in one place; keep both for 2 releases for compatibility.
Author: Kept legacy 'done' event emission and added 'complete' alias with deprecation note in docs.
Stable streaming: deterministic teardown on disconnects; resume tokens to reconnect without duplicate tool/function calls; server-side retry/backoff to avoid thundering retries; OpenAI adapter preserves function call state across reconnects; SDK updates available for smoother migration.
Clients that want deduplicated reconnects should upgrade SDKs to the patched release and use the resume token exposed on stream start. Existing clients continue to work but will not benefit from resume semantics. Monitor metrics: streaming.duplicate_tool_calls and streaming.retry_attempts during rollout.

Context: customers observed malformed events and premature JSON parse errors when using the OpenAI-compat SSE shim in long-running streams (notably with tool/function-calling payloads). Symptoms included 'Unexpected end of JSON input' in the SDK adapter, spurious empty events due to trailing delimiters, and out-of-order token vs event propagation when partial objects were emitted across chunk boundaries. Repro: run a streaming function call that emits a large 'arguments' payload, interrupt network (simulate cell network) and resume; parsing fails reproducibly. Root cause: the compat layer relied on naive delimiter splitting (newline/data: heuristics) and attempted JSON.parse on individual chunks rather than buffering partial object text while respecting string/escape semantics. This produced parse errors for valid messages that were simply split mid-object. Additionally, the old code treated any empty 'data:' line as a no-op but that interacted badly with CRLF split sequences producing zero-length events. Fix: implement a stateful SSE framing buffer that accumulates incoming bytes until a complete event payload is detected. Event completeness is determined by a robust boundary detector: prefer explicit length-prefix when present; otherwise use JSON-aware bracket counting with string/escape awareness and a small safety timeout to avoid head-of-line blocking. Special-case handlers added for: 1) function/tool call JSON objects that may include nested braces and brackets; 2) 'data: [DONE]' canonical termination; 3) empty-data lines and stray CR/LF sequences. We also added an idempotent partial-replay mechanism: on reconnect, the client can request the last-event-id and the server will include a short replay token that the parser uses to dedupe already processed partial objects. Tests: unit tests cover mid-object chunk splits, CRLF edge cases, multi-event batches in a single TCP segment, and a simulated reconnect/replay flow. Performance: microbenchmarks show negligible (~1%) overhead for the buffering logic on typical 8k payloads; long-tail benefits due to reduced error retry. Migration notes: SDKs using the old shim should not need changes; the behavioral fix is backwards-compatible but fixes previously-observed parse failures. Checklist: - [x] Add robust SSE framing and buffered parser - [x] Add tests for partial JSON and delimiter edge cases - [x] Fix function-calling event ordering and replay dedupe - [x] Add TypeScript shim parity for browser client - [x] Update README/changelog entry - [x] Run perf microbench and e2e streaming smoke tests Release notes: Fixes streaming parse failures and delimiter bugs in the OpenAI-compat SSE shim; improves stability for function/tool-calling streams and reconnect replay. Related: Linear ENG-4821 (streaming regressions), ENG-4875 (compat shim reliability), SUP-1349 (customer incident) End of description.

payload.body:
Motivation: Intermittent partial-JSON emissions in our OpenAI-compatible SSE adapter were correlated with long tail fragments and late-arriving delimiters which caused downstream clients to receive non-atomic JSON objects. This PR adds a lightweight span-checkpointing mechanism inside the SSE parser and a sticky-tail suppression heuristic that defers emission of ambiguous trailing fragments for a short, configurable window. The intent is to reduce spurious partial JSON events while preserving low-latency streaming for well-formed events. Summary of changes: 1) Parser: introduce span checkpoints that record byte offsets and event boundaries; checkpoints are emitted as metadata events to the internal stream ledger to enable deterministic reassembly on reconnect or replay. 2) Sticky-tail suppression: when the parser sees a fragment that ends with a likely-truncated JSON token (heuristic based on trailing commas, open braces, unfinished string escapes, or cut-off numeric tokens) it holds emission for up to 120ms (configurable) awaiting completion; if completion does not arrive it emits a guarded partial object with a diagnostic field for downstream operators. 3) Compatibility shim: OpenAI-compat adapter now annotates checkpoint metadata using the existing sse-meta header (no protocol change for most clients); adapter will gracefully ignore checkpoints it's not able to apply. 4) Observability: add metrics for held_fragments_count, checkpoint_emitted, sticky_tail_timeouts and tracing spans for checkpoint lifecycle. 5) Tests: add unit and integration tests that simulate staggered fragment arrival, reconnect with ledger replay, and client-side reassembly. Backwards-compatibility note: default behavior keeps latency-sensitive streams unchanged for well-formed events; only streams with ambiguous tails get the short hold window and diagnostic partials if timed out. Rollout plan: feature gated by env SSE_SPAN_CHECKPOINT=true; staged rollout to canary, then 10% traffic for 48h with metrics alerting on sticky_tail_timeouts > 0.02% of events. Checklist: [x] Parser implementation and benchmarks; [x] Adapter compatibility shim; [x] Unit tests; [x] Integration tests with ledger replay; [x] Observability and dashboards; [x] Feature flag and rollout plan. Related: ENG-7321 (streaming stability), ENG-7550 (client-facing partial JSON incidents). See docs: docs/compatibility/sse-span-checkpointing.md for operator guidance and SDK changes required for advanced reassembly.
Marco Li: Important improvement. Two requests before approving: please reduce default hold window to 120ms from 200ms and add a small microbenchmark comparing latency P50/P95 with feature off vs on; also add an explicit opt-out env for high-frequency streams.
Aisha Patel (author): Reduced default to 120ms, added microbenchmark in tests/benchmarks/sse_hold_bench.go and implemented SSE_SPAN_SUPPRESS_DISABLE env flag to opt-out of holding; pushed fixes.
Ellen Rivera: Looks good, one nit on naming: suggest checkpoint->span_checkpoint to avoid collision with existing checkpoint metrics; please add migration note to docs for operators that parse sse-meta.
Aisha Patel (author): Renamed metric and added migration snippet and example in docs/compatibility/sse-span-checkpointing.md; updated dashboards.
Samir Doshi: Verified integration test behavior locally against the adapter; CI rerun passed. Approving.

payload.body:
Motivation: Close parity gaps with OpenAI /v1/chat.completions for production streaming and structured tool outputs while avoiding protocol bloat. This PR introduces a compact stream envelope (v2) to reduce event size and negotiation overhead, a logprob normalizer to provide consistent numeric semantics across float32/float16 backends, and a stop-token safety adapter to sanitize ambiguous stop sequences coming from third-party models. Changes include API adapters, runtime parsing, docs, and tests. Checklist: [x] compact envelope wire format and version negotiation; [x] stable streaming backpressure hooks; [x] deterministic logprob normalization and rounding; [x] stop-token sanitizer with whitelist/blacklist rules; [x] telemetry to track envelope fallbacks; [x] unit and integration tests; [x] docs and migration guide. Summary of behavior: 1) Stream envelope v2 collapses repeated metadata into a single header frame and encodes structured tool outputs with a content-type tag (example: "Content-Type: application/vnd.redwood+json; version=2"). Clients negotiate using a short handshake header ("X-RW-Stream: v2") and fallback to v1 if not present. 2) Logprob normalizer: server normalizes token logprobs to float32 precision then emits a stable rounding to 6 decimal places in JSON to avoid downstream diffs from float16 quantization. If client requests raw_logprobs=true we include the original float as an extra field raw_logprob_n32 for audit. 3) Stop-token safety adapter: sanitizes multi-byte and whitespace-only stops, strips zero-width chars, collapses repeated stop arrays, and enforces a max-stop-length policy configurable by the API. Compatibility and fallbacks: default behavior preserves current outputs unless client opts-in to compact envelope or logprob_normalize=true. For older clients we still emit v1 framing and legacy stop semantics. Performance: envelope v2 reduces per-frame overhead by ~18% in internal bench; the normalizer adds ~0.2ms per-response on p3-class hardware. Tests and CI: added unit tests for envelope handshake, fuzzing tests for stop sanitizer, and replay tests to assert stable logprob serialization. Deployment plan: feature-flagged rollout for two weeks, enable telemetry, and auto-fallback if >1% of requests encounter framing parse errors. Docs: migration guide added at /docs/api/migration/streaming-v2 (see PR link), and examples in SDKs updated.
Alex Chen (reviewer): Can you explain the decision to round to 6 decimal places for logprobs instead of emitting full float? Is there an opt-out?
Sofia Alvarez (author): Rationale: 6 decimals is enough to preserve ranking decisions while eliminating noisy diffs from float16 backends. There is an opt-in raw_logprobs=true which will include raw_logprob_n32 for auditing; we avoid sending full 32-bit binary blobs in the default path to keep response sizes small.
Marcus Bell (reviewer): stop sanitizer is conservative but we saw one model produce a control character stop sequence. How do we avoid accidentally stripping intentional markers?
Sofia Alvarez (author): We whitelist ASCII punctuation and alphanumerics by default; the config allows tenant-level overrides. The sanitizer logs anonymized samples to a secure bucket for review before policy changes.
Drew Patel (reviewer): CI flakes in the bench job on GPU allocation; can we make the benchmark job non-blocking?
Sofia Alvarez (author): Marked as non-blocking in ci config and added a gating job that runs only on weekly windows.
Introduce compact streaming envelope v2 with handshake and fallback; add stable logprob normalization (canonical JSON precision) and opt-in raw_logprobs for audits; add stop-token safety adapter with tenant-configurable policy; minor perf improvement for envelope framing; migration guide included.

payload.body:
Context: We need a less-disruptive path for rolling out the v2 request/response shape (structured outputs + richer function/tool calling) to OpenAI-compatible clients. Previously we relied on server-side feature flags and opt-in query params which made client routing and proxying brittle for streaming responses. This PR introduces a client-driven negotiation header plus a lightweight server backcompat shim and explicit streaming control header to make gradual adoption safer.

TL;DR: Add a Redwood-Schema header to let clients declare protocol intent (v1 | v2-beta | v2). Add Redwood-Stream-Mode to indicate how the server should stream structured tokens (raw-delta vs framed-json). Implement a server-side compatibility layer that inspects Redwood-Schema and falls back to canonical v1 envelopes when necessary.

Motivation:
- Reduce incidents where proxies or gateways rewrite streaming chunks in ways that break function-calling JSON frames.
- Give SDKs a predictable way to opt into beta behaviors behind a header rather than opaque feature flags.
- Ensure that older clients/third-party proxies continue to receive v1-compatible responses by default.

What changed (high-level):
- API surface: accept and validate two new headers: "Redwood-Schema" and "Redwood-Stream-Mode".
- Request parsing: server now normalizes incoming requests into an internal canonical model before invoking runtime.
- Response emission: streaming path picks a serializer based on the negotiated schema and stream mode.
- Backcompat shim: v1 serializer is preserved and used when header absent or explicitly v1.
- SDK changes: TS and Python SDKs updated to set Redwood-Schema when calling new helper methods (examples included in docs).
- Docs: migration section with example header usage and a troubleshooting checklist.
- Tests: added unit + integration coverage including a simulated HTTP proxy that rewrites chunk boundaries to validate resilience.

Checklist:
- [x] Header parsing and validation
- [x] v1 serializer unchanged
- [x] v2-beta serializer (structured framing) implemented
- [x] Streaming-control modes: raw-delta, framed-json
- [x] SDK examples and tests
- [x] Integration tests with chunk-rewriting proxy
- [x] Rollout gating in Console (feature flag hooks)

Commits (summary):
- core: negotiate-schema: add header parsing and canonicalization helpers
- streaming: serializer: add framed-json serializer and stream-mode switch
- openai-compat: translator: map OpenAI-style function_call to internal tool spec
- sdk-ts: expose setSchemaHeader helper and update streaming example
- sdk-py: add schema header option to client constructors
- docs: openai-compat: add migration guide and examples

Changed files (top-level view):
- server/src/http/headers.go (new header parsing/mapping)
- server/src/streaming/serializer.go (framed-json serializer)
- server/src/compat/backcompat_shim.go (shim for v1 behavior)
- server/src/compat/proxy_tests/proxy_rewrite_test.go (integration proxy test)
- sdk/typescript/src/client/schema.ts (helper to set header)
- sdk/python/redwood/client.py (constructor option)
- docs/openai-compat/migration.md (migration guide)
- docs/openai-compat/streaming.md (streaming modes)
- tests/integration/streaming_end_to_end.test.js
- ci/workflows/schema-negotiation.yml

Review notes and rationale:
- We intentionally keep v1 as the default: absence of Redwood-Schema results in v1-compatible behavior. This minimizes breakage for third-party proxies and older SDKs.
- v2-beta exposes a framed JSON stream where individual events are self-describing (type + payload) to make structured output robust over lossy intermediaries.
- Redwood-Stream-Mode supports two values: raw-delta (token deltas as before) and framed-json (self-contained JSON frames). Framed-json is the recommended mode for function-calling because it avoids partial-chunk decodes.
- We avoid embedding schema version into the URL to make CDNs and signed URLs simpler and avoid cache fragmentation.

Rollout plan (ops):
- Stage 1 (canary): enable header parsing in production and log occurrences; no change in behavior unless header present.
- Stage 2 (beta): opt-in clients set Redwood-Schema: v2-beta and Redwood-Stream-Mode: framed-json. Monitor for broken streams and parsing errors.
- Stage 3 (gradual): allow select customers to set Redwood-Schema: v2, enable minor rule relaxations in runtime (e.g., allow richer tool call bindings).
- Final: flip default to v2 only after 90 days of stability and customer migration docs.

Compatibility considerations and common pitfalls:
- Proxies that fold or coalesce chunk boundaries may still cause trouble for raw-delta streaming; framed-json solves most of these but requires clients to read by frame, not by raw bytes.
- Some HTTP libraries buffer until line endings; clients should use streaming body readers recommended in SDKs.
- WebSocket-based transports should mirror header negotiation at handshake time.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Ethan Park: "Can you add a metric that counts negotiation failures (malformed header / unsupported schema)?" — Maya: "Added redwood.net.schema.neg_fail metric and unit tests."
- Sofia Alvarez: "I'm worried about consumers accidentally opting into v2 in SDKs that default to v1. Make sure examples show explicit set." — Maya: "Examples updated, and SDKs expose explicit helpers; no default change."
- Ravi Menon: "Integration test looks brittle on CI due to timing; can we make chunk rewrites deterministic?" — Maya: "Test refactor to deterministic chunk sizes; CI flakiness addressed."

CI results and iteration:
- First CI run: lint pass, unit tests pass, integration flaky (streaming_end_to_end failed due to timing)
- After test fix: full CI pass, coverage +1.2%.

Documentation and examples included:
- docs/openai-compat/migration.md contains examples for curl, node, and python with explicit headers and fallback testing guidance.

Triage/incident notes:
- This PR was created after two incidents where function-calling responses were malformed when proxied through a third-party CDN (SUP-1123). The framed-json mode prevents those classes of failures.

Evaluation criteria for merge:
- No production behavior change without explicit headers
- Comprehensive tests for both streaming modes
- SDKs and docs updated
- Console rollout gating hooks in place
Introduce a client-driven negotiation header (Redwood-Schema) to opt into v2 behavior; add a streaming-control header (Redwood-Stream-Mode) to stabilize structured streaming and function-calling fallbacks. Backcompat shim keeps v1 parsing for servers that don't opt-in.
Ethan Park: Added metric request — implemented as redwood.net.schema.neg_fail with unit tests.
Sofia Alvarez: SDK default behavior — clarified in examples and left default as v1.
Ravi Menon: Flaky integration test — refactored to deterministic chunking sizes.
QA (Anika): Verified streaming_end_to_end with both modes behind a simulated CDN rewrite.
Security (Dmitri): Quick review, no sensitive header content; suggested logging rate limits for header abuse.

payload.body:
Motivation: clients integrating with the OpenAI-compatible shim have inconsistent behavior when faced with rate limits and transient overload during streaming responses. Reconnects often produce duplicate outputs or fail to resume, and clients don't have clear guidance whether to back off or reconnect. This PR makes three coordinated changes across the shim, stream proxy, and docs: 1) Normalize Retry-After handling and response codes: 429 remains primary for per-client rate limits; 503 is used to indicate transient server-side backpressure when the request reached the runtime but can't be scheduled. Both endpoints include Retry-After (seconds or HTTP-date) and a structured JSON error with a stable error_code (RWD_RATE_LIMIT | RWD_OVERLOAD). 2) Streaming resume / idempotency: introduce an optional X-Redwood-Resume-Token header emitted on partial/early termination and a guarantee that idempotency-key semantics persist across reconnects. Clients can reconnect with the same Idempotency-Key and Resume-Token to continue a stream without double-application of side effects (function/tool calls) and without re-executing completed steps. 3) Error mapping & compatibility: map legacy OpenAI error strings to consistent Redwood error codes and include an explanation mapping in the docs. The description below lists behavioral guarantees, developer migration notes, and test coverage summary.
src/shim/openai/errors.go: add canonical codes RWD_RATE_LIMIT, RWD_OVERLOAD, RWD_CLIENT_ERROR and map legacy OpenAI error 'rate_limit'/'insufficient_quota' -> RWD_RATE_LIMIT
src/shim/openai/stream_proxy.go: emit X-Redwood-Resume-Token when returning partial chunk with non-terminal status; accept Resume-Token+Idempotency-Key on reconnect and validate offset (new token format v1).
pkg/middleware/retry_after_parser.py: parse both integer-seconds and HTTP-date formats; clamp long Retry-After values to a server-configurable max_backoff to avoid DOS vectors.
pkg/middleware/idempotency_store.go: store resume offsets with idempotency-key namespace; on reconnect ensure previously completed tool-calls are not re-run, respond with 409+RWD_CONFLICT if client attempts conflicting replay.
src/runtime/scheduler/backpressure.go: expose explicit 503 path for runtime overload (RequestAcceptedButDelayed) that bubbles Retry-After and a short backoff suggestion; emit metrics runtime.backpressure.count and runtime.backpressure.avg_wait_ms.
docs/openai_compat/retry_idempotency.md: migration notes for clients, examples for reconnect flow in JS/Python, and recommended best practices for exponential backoff + jitter when Retry-After absent.
tests/integration/stream_resume.test.ts: simulate mid-stream 503 with Retry-After header and verify client can reconnect and resume tokens drive deterministic continuation.
examples/streams/resume-client.js: example reconnect logic that attaches Idempotency-Key and Resume-Token, validates server-supplied resume ranges, and sanity-checks final message deduplication.
tests/unit/retry_after_parsing_test.py: cover edge cases (HTTP-date in different timezones, negative values, very long durations).
Asha Patel (reviewer): Important work. Please clarify difference between 429 and 503 in the docs section; also ensure we don't leak internal queue state via headers. Requested change: hide internal queue_id; expose only opaque Resume-Token.
Evelyn Zhang (author): Addressed — replaced queue_id with opaque HMAC'd resume token and added docs note about token entropy. Added unit tests to assert token contains no plaintext metadata.
Diego Marquez (reviewer): Lgtm overall. Two nits: add additional coverage for reconnects with partial function-call side effects, and add an INFO-level metric when clients reconnect more than 3 times.
Evelyn Zhang (author): Added integration test that simulates function call idempotency; added metric runtime.stream.reconnects and hook for alerting on 3+ reconnects per 5m.
Samir Rao (approver): Approve after CI green and a follow-up to run load tests in benchmark lab.
Added unit tests for Retry-After parsing, idempotency token validation, and integration tests that run simulated reconnect scenarios (including function/tool-call deduplication). CI was flaky on initial run due to a timing-dependent test which was hardened and retried. Local load tests show ~1.2x increase in short-tail p95 while reducing duplicate tool calls to 0% in reconnect scenarios.
Clients: 1) When reconnecting, continue to supply the same Idempotency-Key header; if server returned X-Redwood-Resume-Token include it in Reconnect-Resume-Token header. 2) For backoff, prefer server Retry-After when present; otherwise use exponential backoff with jitter. 3) Update error handling to inspect error.code (RWD_RATE_LIMIT, RWD_OVERLOAD, RWD_CLIENT_ERROR) rather than string matching.
Improved streaming stability and error semantics: clients should see consistent Retry-After behavior for rate limits and runtime backpressure, be able to resume interrupted streams using server-issued resume tokens, and rely on canonical Redwood error codes for programmatic handling. See docs/openai_compat/retry_idempotency.md for migration steps and examples.

payload.body:
Motivation: We observed intermittent JSON parse errors in downstream OpenAI-compatible SSE clients when the server emitted partial JSON objects split across TCP frames and when a reconnect/replay path duplicated the SSE blank-line delimiter. Root cause: the emitter and compatibility layer used a naive line-oriented framing that treated any standalone LF/LFCR pair as an event separator without guarding for JSON payloads that include escaped/newline sequences. On reconnect, the replay path could re-emit the trailing blank-line delimiter in addition to the next event's leading 'data:' lines, resulting in an extra empty event or malformed parse in strict clients. This PR fixes reassembly, emitter, and replay logic to guarantee event atomicity and avoid duplicate delimiters. Changes (summary): 1) Implemented a robust SSE reassembly/parser that accumulates 'data:' lines until a true inter-event blank-line is reached, but also treats JSON string contents correctly by not naively splitting on newlines inside reconstructed JSON payloads. 2) Updated the emitter so payload lines are always prefixed with 'data: ' and we guarantee a single terminating blank-line per event; the emitter now escapes a minimal set of sequences and uses a stable boundary on replay. 3) Hardened replay logic: replay no longer re-emits the terminating blank-line from the prior stream; instead, the replay resumes from the next 'data:' token, and the server signals a 'stream-resume' control event when resumption occurs to aid clients that implement deduplication. 4) Added thorough tests: unit tests for the parser with intentionally split frames (embedded newlines, escaped sequences, long lines), integration tests that simulate immediate reconnects and partial write replays, and a fuzz test that runs 1000 randomized split scenarios. 5) Metrics and observability: new counters sse.reassembly_attempts, sse.reassembly_failures, sse.replay_duplicates_detected; emitted log lines include a trace-id for reassembly errors. 6) Backwards compatibility: default behavior is compatible with existing clients; an opt-in config flag openai_compat.sse_strict_mode enables the stricter resume control event for enterprise users wanting explicit resume signaling. Checklist: - [x] Parser implemented and unit-tested - [x] Emitter updated and regression-tested - [x] Replay logic patched and integration-tested - [x] Added metrics and dashboards (grafana panel ids in comments) - [x] Feature-flag gating and rollout plan drafted Testing: see test files (listed below). CI: initial run surfaced a flake8 formatting error in parser test; fixed in follow-up commit and CI passed. Rollout: staged rollout behind feature flag: 0->5% traffic for 48h, monitor sse.reassembly_failures and 2xx stream success; then 100% after stability window. Related: fixes a number of customer-reported incidents (SUP-8731) and should reduce errors in function-calling/tool outputs where clients previously failed to parse streaming structured JSON. Notes for reviewers: pay attention to parser edge cases around JSON strings containing '

' sequences and long-JSON streaming where KV cache dumps occurred in previous incidents. Conventions: emission keeps 'data: ' prefix on every line per SSE spec; control events use 'event:' header (e.g., 'event: stream-resume') and are documented in redwood-openai-compat/README_STREAMING.md.
Miguel Santos (review): please add a test that includes a JSON string containing literal '

' and confirm parser doesn't accidentally split; consider a metric tag for customer id.

payload.body:
Motivation: Streaming structured outputs sometimes emit partial or malformed JSON fragments before the model settles on a final schema-compliant payload. When tool/function calls are interleaved in the stream, we observed unrecoverable toolcall payload corruption at the SDK/adapter boundary. This PR implements a deferred-schema-commit protocol plus lightweight snapshotting around function call boundaries to enable runtime repair and deterministic resume without dropping the stream or silently returning invalid tool payloads.

Design summary: We separate the streaming lifecycle into three phases: provisional emit, in-flight toolcall snapshot, and final schema commit. Provisional emits are allowed to stream token-by-token with permissive validation; when a function/tool call boundary is detected we capture a compact snapshot of the KV-cache + pending tokens and fence the toolcall path so the tool invocation payload can be constructed deterministically from the snapshot. After the model finishes, we perform a final schema commit check against the full reconstructed output. If commit fails, the runtime will attempt localized repairs (coercion, partial re-run of last segment, or graceful rejection) depending on the configured strictness level. This preserves streaming latency while providing actionable errors for strict mode.

Implementation highlights: - New protocol handshake on the response_format negotiation layer: client indicates willingness to accept deferred commits via response_mode: "deferred_commit" (OpenAI-compat shim maps "response_format.deferred_commit"). - Streaming runtime: implement SnapshotManager to capture compact state at tool boundaries; snapshots are persisted in-memory for short TTL and also emitted to the tracing pipeline for debugging. - Toolcall fencing: added deterministic serializer at the adapter layer to rehydrate tool payloads from snapshots; tool invocations now include a snapshot id and sequence anchor. - Schema verification: final schema commit uses the existing JSONSchema validator but with staged checks (soft-validate provisional segments, hard-validate on commit). Validation failures map to structured error codes (SCHEMA_COMMIT_FAILED, TOOLCALL_MISMATCH, SNAPSHOT_EXPIRED). - Config: feature flag "deferred_schema_commit" (off by default), strictness profile via existing response_schema_mode (per-request override).

Files changed (high-level): runtime/streaming/manager.py, runtime/streaming/snapshot.py, api/response_format/negotiator.py, adapters/openai_compat/stream_adapter.py, sdk/python/redwood/response.py, tests/streaming/test_deferred_commit.py, docs/api/response_formats.md. Diffs are intentionally small per file; most complexity is in snapshot and adapter code paths.

Testing & rollout: Unit and integration tests covering snapshot capture/replay, toolcall fencing, and final commit failure modes. Added e2e canary against hosted OpenAI-compat endpoint to validate expected behavior with sample tool-calling prompts. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated, enable in staging for 48h, then gradual rollout to 10% of hosted traffic with monitoring for SNAPSHOT_EXPIRED and SCHEMA_COMMIT_FAILED rates; automatic rollback if error rates exceed thresholds.

Notes: This PR focuses on runtime and protocol; SDKs receive a minimal compatibility shim to surface structured error codes to callers. Followups will include telemetry dashboards for commit fidelity and UX improvements in the Console to surface snapshot traces for debugging.
Introduce deferred schema commit protocol for streaming responses to allow partial emits while preserving a final schema verification step; add compact snapshotting around function/tool calls so the runtime can replay and repair streamed tool-invocation payloads. No user-facing API breaking changes; default behavior behind feature flag 'deferred_schema_commit' and gated for OpenAI-compat mode.
Diego Marquez (2026-02-20): Can we avoid holding large KV caches in memory for long-running streams? Suggest bounding snapshot size and using a checksum to avoid reserializing identical state.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-20): Addressed — SnapshotManager now trims and stores diffs; added checksum-based dedupe and TTL of 60s by default. See runtime/streaming/snapshot.py changes.
Lena Hoffman (2026-02-22): If the final commit fails in strict mode, what's the recommended SDK behavior? Do we return a partial result or an error code?
Aisha Patel (2026-02-22): For strict mode we return a structured error (SCHEMA_COMMIT_FAILED) and include last good snapshot id; SDKs will surface this as an exception with repair hints. For permissive mode we coerce and return best-effort payload and emit telemetry.
Samir Gupta (2026-02-25): Nice tests. One nit: add a flakiness guard for the canary which depends on external model timing.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-25): Added time-budget guard and moved the canary to use a synthetic low-latency model to reduce CI flakiness.
Lena Hoffman (2026-03-01): Approved after followups were addressed.
Diego Marquez (2026-03-01): Approved — verified snapshot size bounds and TTL in staging logs.

payload.body:
Context and motivation:
We have inconsistent retry signals across the API surface when tool/function calls are streamed or multiplexed. Clients cannot reliably determine whether they should back off, fast-fail, or retry idempotently when a partial tool result is observed. This causes duplicated side-effects for third-party tools and poor UX during transient capacity or regional failovers.

Goals:
- Provide a compact, machine-readable Retry-Advice schema surface in responses and handshake frames so clients can make deterministic decisions without parsing freeform Retry-After text.
- Add an opt-in fail-fast mode for tool/function calls so latency-sensitive consumers can choose early termination when capacity is constrained.
- Clarify idempotency scoping for tool-session keys (session-scoped vs call-scoped) and document expected semantics for retries during multiplexed streams.
- Normalize error codes and a short error-class header so compatibility layers (OpenAI shim) map to consistent programmatic values.

What this PR does (high-level):
- Introduces a Retry-Advice header (Retry-Advice: token=<opaque>, retry_ms=<int>, scope=<call|session>, reason=<enum>) that can be returned on regular HTTP responses and as a control frame on streaming channels. The header is intentionally small and parseable without full JSON decoding.
- Adds a small handshake frame in the streaming protocol (control.advice) that mirrors the Retry-Advice header for in-band retries during long-running tool calls.
- Adds an opt-in fail-fast flag (X-Redwood-FailFast: true) at request level and a server-side backpressure path that returns 409+Retry-Advice when capacity is insufficient. Fail-fast is opt-in to avoid changing default behaviors.
- Documents idempotency scoping: idempotency-key: session:<uuid> and idempotency-key: call:<uuid>. Server treats session-scoped keys as safe to retry for non-destructive operations across stream reconnects; call-scoped keys are single-attempt-only by default.
- Normalizes structured error codes into X-Redwood-Err and a small textual code in the JSON body (error.code_short) to make OpenAI-compat layer mapping simple and deterministic.

Implementation notes:
- Runtime: change concentrated in rpc/streaming/control.go and rpc/http/headers.go. Added a lightweight parsing helper for Retry-Advice that avoids allocations on the hot path.
- OpenAI shim: map new X-Redwood-Err and Retry-Advice into OpenAI-friendly counterparts (x-openai-retry and retry_after_ms) in redwood-openai-compat adapter.
- SDKs: hooks implemented in redwood-sdk-python to expose a parsed RetryAdvice object and an experimental Client.fail_fast option. Typescript/Go SDKs receive follow-up patches to maintain small diffs.
- Tests: unit and integration tests added for backpressure, fail-fast, and idempotency-scope semantics; added a synthetic load test in perf-canary to validate behavior under constrained GPU pools.

Checklist:
- [x] Design and spec in Linear ENG-4321
- [x] Runtime parsing and control frame implementation
- [x] OpenAI-adapter mapping
- [x] SDK Python exposure and docs
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Observability: metrics for advice_emitted and advice_consumed
- [x] Rollout plan and feature gating behind feature flag (feature.retry_advice_v1)

Compatibility and rollout:
- This is backward-compatible by default: servers will only emit Retry-Advice when advantage is present; clients will ignore unknown headers. Fail-fast is opt-in. The OpenAI shim will translate fields to legacy retry_after semantics when clients expect them.
- Rollout plan: feature flag default off for 2 weeks in staging, controlled activation for select tenants, then global enable. We added metrics and tracing spans to detect any increase in client-side retries or side-effect duplication.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests: header parsing, handshake encoding/decoding, idempotency-scope transitions.
- Integration: simulated reconnects with session-scoped idempotency and multi-call interleaving.
- Load test: perf-canary scenario with a 30% capacity reduction validated that fail-fast reduces tail latency for high-priority routes while increasing 409+advice events (expected).
- Manual: exercised in staging against a small dedicated cluster and used the SDK to assert parsed retry advice fields.

Follow-ups and known limitations:
- TS/Go SDKs: follow-up PRs to provide the same convenience wrappers in the next week.
- We intentionally keep the Retry-Advice header small; future work may provide a richer JSON body for internal customers if necessary.
- Edge case: idempotent session semantics for multi-hop tool calls (tool -> external system -> callback) will require additional review; deferred to ENG-4507.

Summary of changes (single continuous string):
Adds Retry-Advice header + streaming control frame; introduces opt-in fail-fast request flag and server backpressure path; clarifies idempotency scoping for session vs call keys; normalizes short error code header for deterministic adapter mapping; implements Python SDK hooks and tests; adds rollout/feature-flagging and observability metrics.

Ethan Miller: Important improvement. Two asks: 1) add a short canonical example line for client parsers in docs/api/retry_advice.md, 2) ensure the header parser defers to a fastpath when header absent.
Marina Lopez: responded - added compact example and non-alloc fastpath; included benchmark in control_test.go that shows <1% overhead in hot path.
Priya Shah: question on idempotency - how do we expect external tool webhooks to treat session-scoped keys? Suggest adding a sentence to idempotency-scoping.md.
Marina Lopez: replied - added guidance: webhooks should validate the call_id and avoid re-applying side-effects for session-scoped retries unless tool explicitly declares idempotent behavior.
Leo Tan: CI flaked once on the perf-canary. Re-ran - green now. Approving with small docs nits addressed.
Vikram Rao (SRE): suggest emitting a metric advice_rate_per_route to help tune fail-fast thresholds — added in this PR.

payload.body:
Motivation:
We are rolling schema changes for tool/function call envelopes and streaming structured output (v1 -> v2). Customers running older clients observed breaking changes when servers started to emit v2 streaming frames. This PR adds a transient-schema-adapter middleware in the OpenAI-compat proxy to smooth deprecations with three goals: 1) preserve streaming stability for mixed client fleets, 2) avoid long-lived hacks in customer code by exposing an opt-in compatibility header, and 3) emit telemetry to measure client-side adoption so we can retire shims safely.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces pkg/compat/adapter: a middleware that performs request rewriting and incremental response coercion for streaming tool responses. The adapter can coerce field names, add missing envelope markers expected by v1 clients, and buffer small stream fragments to avoid mid-frame splits.
- Adds a header-driven opt-in: clients may send "Prefer-Schema-Compat: transient-v1" to enable the shim for their session. No behavior changes for clients that do not set the header.
- Implements a streaming sanitizer that detects v2 frames with new typed fields (e.g., "tool_output.v2") and emits a v1-compatible envelope sequence (progress, tool_call, result) while preserving chunked transfer semantics.
- Adds telemetry counters and gauges: compat.request.enabled, compat.response.coercions, compat.buffered_fragments, and compat.deprecation_signals. These are tagged by model, route, and compatibility value.
- Documentation updates: docs/compatibility/schema-migration.md documents recommended client opt-in flow and migration checklist.

Implementation notes:
- The adapter lives in redwood-openai-compat so that behavior is isolated from core runtime. It exposes a small interface to allow runtime teams to opt into a deployable config.
- To avoid latency regressions we only buffer up to 256KB or 50ms of stream data (whichever comes first) and fall back to pass-through under heavy load. Buffer thresholds are configurable via env and per-tenant flags.
- Coercions are implemented as reversible transforms with telemetry emitted on any non-noop transform. This makes it possible to measure real usage and test for accidental data loss.

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/compat/adapter/adapter.go - core middleware and transform pipeline
- pkg/compat/transformers/stream_coercion.go - rules for v2->v1 envelope translation
- cmd/compat-proxy/main.go - wiring and feature-flag handling for header opt-in
- docs/compatibility/schema-migration.md - migration guide and examples
- integration-tests/compat/streaming_coercion_test.go - end-to-end streaming tests (mock client + proxy + runtime)
- telemetry/metrics_registry.go - added compat.* metrics and tags
- helm/values-compat.yaml - new config knobs for buffer sizes and opt-in policy
- pkg/compat/README.md - internal notes and troubleshooting

Commits summary:
- feat(adapter): initial transform pipeline and middleware scaffolding
- feat(transformers): v2->v1 streaming coercion rules + unit tests
- docs: add migration guide and opt-in examples
- test(integration): add streaming canary and flaky-case harness
- ci: add compat integration job to pipeline

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests: all new unit tests pass locally and on CI.
- Integration tests: the compat integration job exercised canary streams and passed on the second run after we addressed a timing race in the test harness. The PR includes a small stability fix for the harness.
- Load: synthetic local load showed <0.8ms added median latency for small messages when buffering disabled; worst-case 18ms for buffered cases within thresholds.

Review conversation (summary):
- Evan: "Nice, this looks well scoped. Two asks: make buffer thresholds tenant-configurable and ensure we never convert structured tool errors into success envelopes."
- Sana: "Added tenant config via helm/values-compat.yaml and added an explicit error-preservation check in stream_coercion.go. Unit tests added (see commit 3)."
- Diego: "We should also emit a specific deprecation telemetry counter so we can track when v2-only frames are seen from clients that didn't opt-in."
- Sana: "Added compat.deprecation_signals and surfaced it in metrics_registry.go. Also added a short section in docs describing the signal thresholds for automated deprecation windowing."
- Lydia: "Please add a short rollout plan and a kill-switch for the middleware in case of unforeseen regressions."
- Sana: "Added the kill-switch (COMPAT_ADAPTER_ENABLED=false) and documented the rollouts: feature-gate on main, canary in production for 48h on 10% of traffic, then gradual ramp. Added Linear tickets for the ramp schedule."
- Approvals: Evan, Diego, Lydia approved the final changes.

Rollout and backwards-compat strategy:
- Default off: shim is opt-in by header for the initial rollout so we don't change behavior for existing clients.
- Canary: deploy to compatibility proxy canary ring with adapter_enabled=true for 10% of internal traffic and all requests that include a migration-test header. Monitor compat.response.coercions and error rates.
- Metrics-driven retirement: once compat.deprecation_signals drops below threshold for 90 days and we have adoption metrics from linked Linear tasks, we will schedule removal of the shim.

Potential risks and mitigations:
- Latency increase under heavy buffering loads: mitigated by strict buffer caps and fallback to pass-through. Added e2e tests to exercise this.
- Silent data loss if transforms are incorrect: mitigated by conservative reversible transforms and explicit telemetry on any coercion.
- Unexpected client behavior for partially upgraded clients: kept opt-in header flow and documented recommended client migration steps.

Merge details:
- Merge method: squash and merge by Lydia Chen on 2026-03-03. Merge commit: "squash: transient schema adapter for streaming tool compatibility".
- Linear links attached to merge: ENG-3147, PM-522.

Follow-ups (future work):
- Add server-side auto-opt-in for long-lived migrations once adoption metrics are clear (follow-up PR planned: feature/compat-auto-optin).
- Expand coercion rules to support typed-argument changes (planned).
- Add a small CLI tool to simulate v1 vs v2 streams for customer troubleshooting (RFC exists in PM-ldx).

If you want to run the adapter locally: see pkg/compat/README.md for an example curl invocation that sets the "Prefer-Schema-Compat: transient-v1" header and a small local runtime mock.

Adds a transient adapter middleware that rewrites incoming requests and outgoing streaming envelopes to maintain compatibility across schema deprecations. Ships behind opt-in header; no default behavior change.
payload.title: Introduce transient schema adapter to smooth schema deprecations for streaming tool-calls

Summary: Adds an operator-scoped KMS allowlist with RBAC-v2 integration and an audit consistency shim that stamps requests with a signed monotonic audit token. Motivation: customers in regulated regions require strict operator->KMS scoping and reliable audit evidence that requests were observed by the audit pipeline. This PR introduces a policy-enforced allowlist for operator service identities, ties the allowlist decision into the RBAC v2 decision flow, and attaches a lightweight audit-consistency stamp to KMS allocation requests to help downstream audit ingestion detect gaps. Changes are behind a feature flag and rolled out as a staged canary. Scope: - New RBAC hook to surface operator identity attributes into the KMS allocator. - Allowlist datastore (in-memory + persisted patch for operator-managed config) and CLI/operator-controller config. - Audit consistency shim: HMAC-signed monotonic stamp + optional proof header forwarded to audit-ingester. - Compatibility layer: non-enforced mode returns warnings and metrics; enforced mode rejects disallowed allocations. Checklist: - [x] RBAC hook added and unit tested - [x] Allowlist middleware and config docs - [x] Audit-stamp signing and verification tested in CI - [x] Canary rollout plan written and tested on staging - [x] Backwards-compatible when feature flag off Related tickets: Linear ENG-1209, ENG-1313; Support SUP-2110. Migration notes: Operators can add allowed KMS account IDs via the operator-config CRD (examples in docs/). Turning the feature flag to "enforce" will cause allocation failures for non-allowlisted operator identities; we recommend canary = 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 days while monitoring metric security.kms.allowlist.reject_rate and audit.ingest.missing_proof. Rollout: default is "warn" in 1.0.0. Monitoring & alerts: new alerts for reject_rate > 0.5% and audit-proofs-missing > 0.2% sustained for 15m. Security considerations: audit-stamp is HMAC keyed by the operator KMS signing key stored in cluster KMS; stamps are short-lived (TTL 5m) to limit replay surface. Implementation notes: RBAC v2 decision now exposes operator.zone and operator-residency-claims which the allowlist policy consults. The audit shim signs {request_id, operator_id, ts, seq} and returns X-REDWOOD-AUDIT-PROOF header; the ingest pipeline will validate HMAC and seq monotonicity per operator. Rollback: feature flag -> warn off; remove enforcement and clear reject metrics. CI/QA: end-to-end test added in perf-canary infra; manual canary run verified in us-west-2 staging.
Add operator-scoped KMS allowlist with RBAC v2 integration and an optional audit-consistency stamp. Feature gated; default mode 'warn'. Operators must update operator_config CRD to set allowed KMS accounts for enforcement. See docs/security/kms-allowlist.md for migration and rollout guidance.
If rollout shows reject_rate above expected, flip enforcement->warn and check operator-config for missing KMS account IDs. Audit-ingest logs will surface invalid stamps under audit.ingest.invalid_proof. Key recovery: use cluster KMS to rotate signing key and update operator-config accordingly.
Day 0: enable warn in staging; Day 1: canary 10% (1 cluster in prod fleet) monitor 4h; Day 2: 50% monitor 24h; Day 3: 100% enforce. Abort conditions: reject_rate > 0.5% or audit.ingest.missing_proof > 0.2% sustained 15m.
Unit tests for allowlist logic + stamp signer/verifier added. E2E run in perf-canary validated header flow and ingest verification. Load tests show <1ms median overhead on allocation path when stamp enabled.
Carlos Mendes (2024-11-10): Please add a migration note for operator-managed clusters that use third-party KMS providers. Response: Added docs/examples and a note about provider-specific mapping in docs/security/kms-allowlist.md.
Evelyn Park (2024-11-11): Suggest verifying audit-stamp TTL is configurable; risk of high clock skew in edge regions. Response: Exposed ttlSeconds in operator_config CRD and added skew tolerance in verifier (±30s max).
Jordan Kim (2024-11-12): Tests flaky in CI for seq monotonic checks; can we add a deterministic clock in unit tests? Response: Added deterministic clock to unit tests and a flaky test marker with retry for integration tests; re-ran CI and all green.

payload.body:
Background: Several customers reported corrupted JSON objects when streaming structured outputs through our OpenAI-compat SSE bridge. Symptoms included truncated object boundaries when the runtime split tokens in the middle of JSON tokens, double delimiters when the transport concatenated small chunks, and occasional reordering when backpressure caused coalescing of intermediate frames. Root cause: The compatibility shim blindly concatenated incoming bytes into 'events' without tracking explicit JSON parse boundaries or emitted delimiter state. When partial JSON fragments were emitted as separate SSE 'data:' lines the consumer's streaming JSON parser could see an unterminated object (e.g. '{"choices": [ {"index": 0,' ) followed by a closing chunk later; in between, the shim sometimes collapsed adjacent delimiters into a single empty event which clients treated as an explicit 'done' marker. Changes in this PR: 1) Introduces an explicit fragment buffer for SSE events in the compat layer that tracks JSON structural state (curly/array nesting depth, string escape state) so we only emit a 'data:' event when a syntactic JSON boundary or an SSE max-chunk size threshold is reached. 2) Add a delimiter coalescing guard: we now collapse consecutive empty events into a single heartbeat event instead of emitting multiple delimiters. 3) For function/tool call messages we add a soft-boundary marker so the function payload (which can be large JSON) is emitted as single logical event even if it crosses tokenization boundaries. This avoids partial-function JSON delivered to tool runners. 4) Expose a feature-flag (OPENAI_COMPAT_SSE_STRICT) to opt into strict-json-boundary emission while we rollout. 5) New metrics: sse.fragmentation_count and sse.coalesced_delimiters to help detect regressions. 6) Added unit and integration tests including a fuzz harness that simulates arbitrary chunk boundaries and transport coalescing patterns. Testing and verification: - Unit tests for fragmenter edge cases including escaped quotes, unicode and nested arrays/objects. - Integration tests that run the OpenAI compatibility e2e harness with streaming clients (python and node) verifying valid incremental JSON frames. - Added a long-running perf canary that runs under canary infra for 24 hours to check latency/regression. - CI initially showed a flaky test (compat_sse_fuzz) which we fixed by making the harness deterministic for seed reuse; final CI green. Rollout plan: - Merge to main behind the feature flag. - Enable OPENAI_COMPAT_SSE_STRICT for Canary customers for 48h. - Monitor sse.fragmentation_count and sse.coalesced_delimiters; if fragmentation spikes, revert flag. - Gradual enable for 10% of traffic, then 50%, then global. Follow-ups: - Integrate this logic into dedicated runtime path (ENG-5065) to avoid duplication. - Add server-side sampling of partial-frame payloads (PII-safe) to aid debugging. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Metrics emitted - [x] Feature flag gated - [x] Documentation note in compat README
Jonah Kim: Nice clarity in the buffer state machine. Two requests: make max_chunk configurable and add a short note on why we don't rely on tokenizer boundaries.
Maya Patel: responded - added configurable MAX_SSE_CHUNK_BYTES in feature_flags and expanded comment about tokenizer unreliability for cross-model differences.
Priya Nair: found a race in coalescing when multiple worker threads call emit_delimiter; requested atomic guard.
Maya Patel: fixed with an atomic flag and added a test 'test_delimiter_coalesce_race' to the fuzz harness.
Carlos Martinez: approved after CI fixed flaky fuzz seed; asked to add a metric tag for customer_id for easier triage.
Maya Patel: added metric tag and noted privacy considerations in docs.
Release lead (internal): please document rollout steps in release notes and gate behind OPENAI_COMPAT_SSE_STRICT by default off.
Maya Patel: done — release notes added and flag defaulted to false.
CI: initial run - compat_sse_fuzz (flaky) failed; reran with deterministic seed - pass.
preserve: add JSON-structure-aware sse fragmenter and coalescing guard
feat(tests): add fuzz harness and deterministic seeds for SSE fragmentation tests
docs: add OPENAI_COMPAT_SSE_STRICT feature flag note to compat README
chore: add sse.fragmentation_count and sse.coalesced_delimiters metrics and export hooks
Fix: Prevents streamed JSON fragments from producing invalid partial objects in OpenAI-compat SSE streams.
Fix: Avoids duplicate SSE delimiters caused by transport coalescing which previously caused some clients to treat streams as complete.
Feature: OPENAI_COMPAT_SSE_STRICT flag for strict JSON-boundary emission (off by default).
payload.title: Preserve JSON boundaries in SSE fragmentation and fix delimiter coalescing

payload.body:
Context: As part of the Safe apply + rollback workstream, we need an easy way (especially for Support/SRE and advanced customers) to confirm which Optimization Config Version (batching/caching/quant profile) was active for a given request. Today, customers can infer this indirectly via dashboards or internal tooling, but it’s not visible at the request boundary.

What this PR does: Add an opt-in response header in the OpenAI-compatible proxy that surfaces the active optimization config version ID when available. This is intentionally disabled by default to avoid leaking internal identifiers to all callers.

Header contract:
- Response header name: `x-redwood-optimization-config-version`
- Value: opaque version identifier (e.g., `ocv_01JH8V3K8XW2M6H9E8RZ0G4KQY`), stable for a given immutable config version
- Only emitted when opt-in is enabled AND the underlying execution path provides a config version

Opt-in / gating:
- If request header `x-redwood-debug: true` is present AND the caller is authenticated (standard Redwood auth; no anonymous traffic), emit the response header.
- Additionally, allow service-side enablement via env var `RW_OPENAI_COMPAT_EXPOSE_OPT_CONFIG_VERSION=1` for internal environments (staging, perf-canary). When this env var is set, the response header is emitted without requiring `x-redwood-debug`.
- If config version is unknown/unavailable, header is omitted (do not emit placeholder values).

Implementation notes:
- Pull config version from upstream response metadata when present:
  - For non-streaming responses: read `x-redwood-internal-opt-config-version` from the upstream Redwood API response and map it to the public header.
  - For streaming responses: capture upstream headers before streaming begins; emit the public header at the start of the stream.
- Adds `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: x-redwood-optimization-config-version` when the header is emitted to support browser debugging tools in Console/embedded clients.
- Ensures we do not vary cache keys or request routing on `x-redwood-debug` (header is handled in the response path only).

Testing:
- Unit tests for header emission behavior (default off, request opt-in, env var override)
- Integration tests for both /v1/chat/completions streaming + non-streaming flows
- Regression test for CORS expose-headers behavior only when the public header is present

Operational impact:
- Minimal. Header emission is conditional and cheap. No changes to request routing/behavior.

Follow-ups (not in scope):
- Consider surfacing a second header for "rollout stage" (canary vs promoted) once the rollout controller semantics settle.
- Docs update in customer-facing guide (tracked in docs repo).
- Adds opt-in response header exposing the active Optimization Config Version used for request execution (useful for debugging canaries/rollbacks and correlating with metrics tagged by config_version).
Felix Schneider (review): Can we align header naming with the Console/Control Plane terminology? I worry `x-redwood-config-version` is too generic if we later add model version headers. Suggest `x-redwood-optimization-config-version` and keep value opaque.
Benji Okafor (author): Good call. Updated to `x-redwood-optimization-config-version` and removed earlier `x-redwood-config-version` alias. Value remains opaque `ocv_*`.
Marcus Lin (security review): Please ensure this is not emitted by default. Also, avoid surfacing internal header names directly. Add explicit gating and confirm it doesn’t bypass auth in any mode.
Benji Okafor (author): Added default-off gating: either `x-redwood-debug: true` on an authenticated request, or env var override for internal clusters only. Also mapped from upstream internal header `x-redwood-internal-opt-config-version` to the public header; the internal name is never forwarded.
Sean Gallagher (SRE): For streaming, we can’t set headers after the body starts. Are we guaranteed to have the upstream headers before we write the first chunk?
Benji Okafor (author): Yes—updated streaming handler to wait for upstream response headers before writing the first SSE chunk. Added integration test to validate header presence on streaming responses.
Chloe Martin (console): Please expose via CORS headers when present; otherwise browser clients can’t read it. But don’t widen expose-headers unnecessarily on all responses.

payload.body:
Context: As part of the SDK parity initiative, we need consistent error shapes across all endpoint paths so Python/TS/Go can reliably classify retryability, surface request_id, and respect Retry-After. Today the OpenAI-compat layer returns a mix of OpenAI-style error bodies and legacy gateway bodies depending on route (/v1/chat/completions vs /v1/embeddings vs /v1/responses compatibility shims), which causes SDK mismatches (e.g., TS retry middleware classifies based on error.code; Python expects request_id always present; Go relies on retryable flag + status). This PR aligns OpenAI-compat error formatting to the shared SDK error taxonomy while preserving OpenAI-compatible top-level structure for clients that parse `error.message`.

What this changes (high level): 1) Normalizes error response envelope for all OpenAI-compat routes to include `error` + Redwood fields: `request_id` and `error.code` consistently. 2) Adds `error.retryable` derived from status code + platform error code (so SDKs can make deterministic decisions without duplicating classification heuristics). 3) Propagates `Retry-After` header (seconds or HTTP date) to the client unchanged; also mirrors a parsed value into `error.retry_after_ms` when present (non-authoritative; header remains source of truth). 4) Ensures `request_id` is present for non-streaming and streaming paths (including cases where upstream closes mid-stream and we only have partial context). 5) Unifies mapping from upstream Redwood error codes to OpenAI error `type` and `code` fields, documented in-code and covered by fixture tests.

Non-goals: This does not change gateway behavior or introduce new error codes. It also does not implement client-side retry logic; the intent is to provide stable signals consumed by SDKs and conformance fixtures.

Implementation notes: - Introduced a single `toSdkTaxonomyError()` helper that takes (status, upstream body, headers) and returns a normalized object. - Preserves OpenAI-style `error: { message, type, param, code }` while adding Redwood fields at the top level: `request_id`, and adding `retryable` + `retry_after_ms` inside `error` (additive). - For legacy upstream errors that already include `request_id` in a different location, we normalize and de-dupe. - For errors produced inside openai-compat (validation, unsupported params), we generate a synthetic Redwood-like code (e.g., `invalid_request`) but keep `retryable=false`.

Testing: - Added fixture-based tests used by the cross-language conformance suite: golden JSON bodies for 400/401/403/404/409/422/429/500/502/503 and for a simulated network upstream timeout mapped to 502. - Added streaming error regression tests ensuring that when a stream fails before first token we return a standard JSON error body; when it fails after emitting tokens we terminate the SSE stream with an `event: error` payload that includes `request_id` and `error.code` (SDKs treat this as non-retryable by default; docs cover idempotency). - Verified that existing OpenAI client libraries still parse `error.message`.

Follow-ups: - Once merged, SDK conformance fixtures can stop special-casing openai-compat paths and rely on the same golden error schema everywhere. - Platform PRs in `redwood` repo handle consistent `Retry-After` emission and request_id propagation; this PR assumes those headers/fields may or may not exist and normalizes accordingly.

Screenshots/log samples: - Example 429 response now includes headers `Retry-After: 2` and JSON: `{ "request_id": "req_01J...", "error": { "message": "Rate limit exceeded", "type": "rate_limit", "code": "rate_limited", "retryable": true, "retry_after_ms": 2000 } }`.

Risk: Low. Changes are additive and mostly unify fields; clients depending on legacy shapes should continue to work since `error.message` remains unchanged. Security note: no secrets are added; we explicitly redact upstream debug fields and avoid echoing auth headers.
Allison Grant (review): Can we ensure `retryable` is derived the same way as the SDK standard (429 + 5xx + certain network errors) and not just `status>=500`? Also please confirm `Retry-After` parsing supports both seconds + HTTP-date, and that we never treat missing/invalid Retry-After as 0ms (that can create tight loops).
Ethan Park (author): Yep. Updated `isRetryable()` to match the current SDK standard: 429, 500/502/503/504, and a small set of upstream transport categories (timeout, connection reset) mapped to 502/504 equivalents. For Retry-After: we keep the header as source of truth; `retry_after_ms` is only present when parse succeeds; otherwise omitted (not 0). Added fixtures for both formats and invalid values.
Marcus Lin (review): Please confirm we are not leaking upstream error `details` that may include internal hostnames or tokens. Also ensure we never include the raw Authorization header in logs when formatting errors.
Ethan Park (author): Good call. `toSdkTaxonomyError()` now whitelists fields from upstream body; we drop `details`, `debug`, and any non-string nested fields by default. No auth header logging here; the error handler only logs `request_id`, `status`, `error.code`, and a redacted message. Added an explicit test asserting debug fields are not present in the response.
Ibrahim Khan (review): This looks aligned with the SDK error taxonomy. One nit: `error.code` should be stable and match the enum used in conformance tests; can we map legacy `rate_limit_exceeded` to `rate_limited`? Also: for streaming mid-flight, are we sure emitting an SSE `event: error` is acceptable for our clients?
Ethan Park (author): Mapped legacy codes to the canonical enum (rate_limit_exceeded -> rate_limited; auth_error -> unauthorized; etc.) and documented the mapping table. On streaming: we already emit an error-like terminal chunk in some paths; this change makes it deterministic and includes request_id/code. Dana confirmed TS client can surface it; Go/Python treat it as a terminal error and do not auto-retry streaming by default.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): For 401/403, please ensure `retryable=false` always and that we don't include hints about which env var was missing (security).
Ethan Park (author): Updated: auth errors are always non-retryable. Message remains generic ("Unauthorized") and does not mention env vars / header names. SDKs can still show their own local auth-resolution guidance.
Allison Grant (review): Approving after the retryable logic update + fixtures. Please add one more fixture for 503 with Retry-After to validate we preserve the header.
Ethan Park (author): Added `test/fixtures/errors/503-retry-after-seconds.json` and assertion for header passthrough.
Allison Grant (review): Approved.
Marcus Lin (review): Approved.
Ibrahim Khan (review): Approved.

payload.body:
Motivation: In production we observed rare cases where small SSE fragments produced during backpressure replay would cause duplicate or dropped function-call sentinels and corrupt partial JSON payloads. This manifested as: 1) trailing sentinel markers emitted twice when a coalescing window boundary coincided with a replayed tail fragment, 2) partial JSON objects split across coalesced chunks with no robust boundary marker, and 3) occasional out-of-order emission of function-call/assistant->tool handoff tokens under aggressive requeue behavior. Changes: 1) Normalized the coalescing window: the coalescer now enforces a deterministic chunk-join policy that never merges a fragment that ends with an open JSON span with a following fragment that begins with an unmatched sentinel. 2) Introduced a "skip-sentinel" guard: when a replayed tail fragment would produce a sentinel duplicate, the guard drops the duplicate sentinel and records a reproducible marker in the connection state so downstream consumers can detect and recover if they missed the original sentinel. 3) Per-connection tail requeue logic updated to preserve explicit function-call boundaries: requeued fragments are stamped with a monotonic fragment-index and a boolean "boundary-anchored" flag to keep ordering stable across retransmit attempts. 4) UTF-8-aware fragment coalescer: ensures we never split multi-byte sequences across emission boundaries, preventing malformed JSON when a UTF-8 boundary falls on a chunk cut. 5) Added regression tests and an integration harness that replays production capture traces at different latency/backpressure profiles. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for coalescer and sentinel guard - [x] Integration replay harness reproduces previously observed failure trace - [x] Performance microbench to ensure <5% median latency regression - [x] Add compatibility shim for consumers that expect legacy sentinel duplication (feature-flagged off by default) Rollout: Feature gated behind compatibilityToggle.sseSkipSentinel; gradual rollout 5%->25%->100% with canary checks for structured-output regressions. Notes: this is targeted and low-risk; it addresses a long-standing edge-case affecting function-call semantics and partial JSON stability.
1) normalize: coalescer deterministic join and utf8 guards; 2) fix: skip-sentinel guard and fragment-index stamping; 3) test: add replay harness and new unit tests; 4) docs: describe compatibility toggle and rollout plan
Miguel: 'Can you explain how the skip-sentinel guard signals consumers to recover if they dropped the original marker?' Author: 'We write a reproducible marker in the per-connection state and emit a zero-length meta-event that downstream adapters can map to a missing sentinel and trigger a resync. This is documented in docs/sse-boundaries.md.' Sofia: 'Add more unit tests for the UTF-8 split cases (4/5 byte sequences).' Author: 'Added extra test vectors and an integration trace that covers multi-byte emoji and CJK sequences.' Ethan: 'CI flaked on the microbench; can you confirm no median latency regression?' Author: 'Bench numbers are included in the PR; median <2% change, p95 unaffected. CI rerun passed.' Reviewers approved after addressing tests and doc clarifications.
Fix SSE coalescing edge cases that could duplicate or drop function-call sentinels and corrupt partial JSON payloads under backpressure replay. Feature gated; enabled for all in next minor unless rollback criteria met.
