payload.body:
Background: We see two recurring customer problems: (1) clients that assume a single fixed schema version break when we roll forward small shape changes to structured responses; (2) long-lived streaming connections can silently degrade (slow heartbeats, partial frames) causing downstream tool-calling consumers to mis-parse envelopes. This PR implements a small, opt-in runtime probe plus a stability-driven fallback to make schema evolution safer and streaming more robust for OpenAI-compat clients.

What this change does (high level): 1) Introduces a client probe header (X-Rw-Schema-Probe: {version}) that the compat proxy will accept for a single preflight request and respond with a compact capability object in the X-Rw-Schema-Capabilities response header (capabilities include supported schema versions, streaming-stability flag, tool-envelope-format version, and deprecation warnings). 2) Adds a streaming slow-path detector in the compat proxy runtime: when per-connection heartbeat latency or chunk reassembly errors exceed configured thresholds we transition that stream to a buffered chunk fallback that preserves function/tool-call envelope markers as a JSON array of events. 3) Adds structured-output negotiation so clients can opt into strict typed envelopes (schema=v2-strict) or graceful coercion (schema=v2-coerce). 4) Adds docs and an integration test demonstrating client probe + fallback in a synthetic high-latency scenario.

Checklist:
- [x] Design and spec for probe/capabilities header and server response documented (docs/openapi/schema-probing.md)
- [x] Compat proxy: probe parsing, capability response, and server-side telemetry hooks implemented (src/proxy/schema_prober.go)
- [x] Streaming runtime: heartbeat monitor, slow-path transition, and envelope-preserving buffer implemented (pkg/streaming/slowpath_detector.go)
- [x] Tool/function calling: ensure tool envelope tokens are preserved when transitioning to buffered fallback (pkg/api/compat/tool_envelope.go)
- [x] Backwards compatibility: probe is opt-in; default behavior unchanged if header not present
- [x] Tests: unit + integration (tests/prober_integration_test.go)
- [x] Docs: migration guide and examples (docs/openapi/schema-probing.md)

Commits (summary):
- 9a7b2c1 add schema prober API surface and header parsing
- b3c0e4f implement capability header generation and telemetry counters
- d12f8ee add streaming slow-path detector and buffered fallback implementation
- 5f4a7bc preserve tool envelope markers in buffered output path
- 7c9e0d2 add integration test for probe + slow-path under artificial latency
- 114ef9a docs: add schema-probing migration guide and examples

Files changed (high level):
- src/proxy/schema_prober.go (new): parses X-Rw-Schema-Probe, validates client version, assembles X-Rw-Schema-Capabilities header, emits telemetry.
- pkg/streaming/slowpath_detector.go (new): heartbeat latency tracking, threshold-based transition logic, buffered chunk assembler.
- pkg/api/compat/tool_envelope.go (mod): marker constants and helper to serialize preserved envelopes when switching modes.
- docs/openapi/schema-probing.md (new): spec for probe header, capability header, examples for strict/coerce modes, migration notes.
- tests/prober_integration_test.go (new): simulates 200ms RTT + intermittent frame drops to exercise fallback.
- go.mod / go.sum: dependency bump for a small ringbuffer helper used in the buffered fallback.

Notable implementation details:
- Header shapes: the probe header is intentionally tiny ("X-Rw-Schema-Probe: v2") and the capability header is a base64-encoded compact JSON in "X-Rw-Schema-Capabilities" to avoid interfering with proxies that drop long headers. The server also adds a human-readable JSON to the first event of the fallback buffered stream for diagnostics.
- Streaming fallback behavior: on threshold breach we close the original SSE/time-based stream and open a buffered response that emits a single JSON array composed of the already-emitted events (best-effort) followed by subsequent events as array items. Each event carries an envelope type ("token", "tool-call", "meta"). Tool-call items keep their call_id to allow consumers to reconcile partial calls.
- Observability: added new prometheus counters: compat_probe_received, compat_probe_mismatch, streaming_slowpath_entered, streaming_slowpath_exited. Trace spans added around probe handling and stream-mode-transition.
- Security: probe parsing is read-only; no sensitive request content is echoed in capability headers. We log only capability fingerprints (hashes) in audit logs.

Compatibility notes and migration guidance (brief):
- Default: if clients do not send X-Rw-Schema-Probe nothing changes.
- Opt-in: clients that want smoother upgrades should send the probe header on an initial low-cost request and inspect X-Rw-Schema-Capabilities to learn server-supported schema versions and streaming stability.
- Tool callers: when upgrading to strict schema, clients should validate tool_call envelopes; use "v2-coerce" mode if you need automatic backwards-coercion.

QA and observed behavior:
- Local integration test simulating high latency caused streaming slow-path to be engaged and consumer reassembled the envelope array successfully.
- Load test (small cluster) shows <2% extra tail latency for affected streams; overall throughput unaffected.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag compat.enable_schema_probe (default true for compat tier).
- Stage rollout: nightly for internal tenants, gradual 48-hour ramp on hosted region-by-region with metric alarms on streaming_slowpath_entered > 0.5% of requests.

Follow-ups:
- Add a small client-side helper in SDKs to standardize the probe flow (follow-up PRs to redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript).
- Expose probe capabilities in Console per-token-level breakdown for customers opting in.

Adds an opt-in lightweight client schema probe header and server capability response. Introduces a streaming slow-path fallback that preserves tool/function call envelopes for clients that observe degraded streaming behavior.
Ethan Liu: nit - can we call the header X-Redwood-Schema-Probe instead of X-Rw-Schema-Probe? I worry about collisions. Also please add a unit test for malformed header values.
Priya Nair: replied - changed header name to X-Rw-Schema-Probe intentionally to keep length small for intermediary proxies; added validation and unit tests for malformed values (see tests/prober_unit_test.go). We can iterate on header naming in a follow-up if customers request a longer prefix.
Sofia Chen: please ensure tool_envelope.go change preserves call_id when chunked; otherwise LGTM after CI fixes.
Marcos Alvarez: ran perf smoke. Observability hooks look good. Approving pending green CI.

payload.body:
Motivation: We observed several incidents where long-running tool/function calls (especially those producing structured JSON arrays and large attachments) caused the gateway stream proxy to accumulate large in-flight buffers, which in turn increased tail latency and triggered compatibility fallbacks for OpenAI-compatible clients. This PR introduces two complementary mitigations: 1) credit-aware routing: a routing heuristic that factors in downstream proxy credit/backpressure and per-route buffer occupancy when selecting a target host/variant; 2) fragmented-chunk handshake: an explicit small handshake frame for fncall/structured-output flows that allows proxies to detect fragmented payloads and assemble them incrementally with bounded headroom before handing them to the compatibility layer. Summary of changes (commits): - commit 1: introduce credit tracker and routing policy hooks (gateway/router.go, routing/policy.md) - commit 2: implement fragmented-chunk handshake and reassembly in stream proxy (proxy/stream_proxy.go, proxy/handshake_test.go) - commit 3: extend OpenAI compatibility handler to honor incremental-assembly signals and avoid pessimistic framing (compat/openai/handler.go) - commit 4: add e2e regression tests and a small perf harness (tests/e2e/toolcall_fragmented.yaml, perf/tools/credit_routing_bench.go) - commit 5: docs and changelog updates (docs/gateway/route_policies.md, CHANGELOG.md) High-level changed areas/files: - gateway/router.go: new routing hook credit-aware route_score that penalizes targets with >X KB buffered fncall bytes - proxy/stream_proxy.go: introduce handshake frame type 0x7F (FRAG_HANDSHAKE); reassembly buffer limited to configurable headroom (default 64KB) - compat/openai/handler.go: read incremental-assembly flags and stream partial structured output to client while compatibility transformations run - tests/*: new deterministic tests reproducing the previous regression and asserting bounded buffer usage Small illustrative snippet: "if route.creditEstimatedBufferedBytes > route.maxBufferedKB*1024 { score -= 50 // deprioritize }" Review conversation (condensed into a single narrative): - Ravi: "Nice approach; two quick asks: make the default headroom conservative (64KB) and add telemetry for 'credit_rejections' so SRE can track how often routing avoids a host." - Maya: "Agreed on 64KB default; added metric gateway.routing.credit_rejections and exposed route.policy.headroom_kb to route config." - Elena: "Can the handshake be versioned? We need to avoid breaking older proxies in mixed clusters." - Maya: "Handshake frame includes a 1-byte version field; compatibility code ignores unknown versions and falls back to legacy chunking behavior." - Tom: "Saw a flaky test in proxy reassembly on first CI run. Did you root cause?" - Maya: "Yes — test assumed deterministic goroutine scheduling. Rewrote test to poll for condition and added a 50ms max-wait. Reran CI." CI and merge: - First CI run (linux-integration) failed on proxy/handshake_test.go due to timing flakiness; subsequent push fixed tests and all checks passed (unit, integration, lint, perf-smoke). - Metric checks and canary smoke were green in staging. - PR approved by Ravi and Elena; merged via squash. Operational notes and rollout: - This change is feature-flagged behind route.policy.enable_credit_aware_routing and route.policy.fragmented_handshake so we can rollout per-cluster. - Recommend enabling in staging for 48h and monitoring gateway.routing.credit_rejections, proxy.reassembly.headroom_allocs, and client.compatibility.fallback_rate. - If credit_rejections spike above 1% of routing decisions, consider increasing route.policy.headroom_kb or decreasing penalty weight. Rationale and impact: - Credit-aware routing reduces tail latency by preferring hosts with available headroom; it trades off slight routing imbalance for bounded buffer usage. - Fragmented-chunk handshake reduces worst-case proxy memory growth for very large structured outputs and stabilizes fncall handshakes for OpenAI-compatible streams. - No public client API changes; OpenAI compatibility layer behavior is relaxed to accept incremental assembly when handshake present. Related work and follow-ups: - Follow-up: add autoscaling signal based on aggregated buffered bytes across pool (ENG-6621). - Follow-up: expose per-route default headroom presets tuned for embeddings vs chat vs tooling (PM-121).
Gateway: introduce credit-aware routing to reduce proxy queueing on large toolcall streams; improve stream proxy resilience with fragmented-chunk handshake for fncall/tooling frames; no user-facing API changes, opt-in via route policy flag.

payload.body:
Motivation: Clients expect stable, documented semantics for rate limits and idempotency when talking to our OpenAI-compat adapter. Previous behavior left ambiguity around which headers/fields are authoritative (Retry-After vs X-RateLimit-Reset), how duplicated requests for streaming endpoints are handled, and how server errors map to OpenAI-style error objects. This change makes the adapter's behavior explicit, documents compatibility guarantees, and adds tests to prevent regressions.

Summary of changes: 1) Rate limit semantics: adapter now consistently prefers the standard Retry-After header (seconds) for upstream throttling and mirrors it into the OpenAI error body as error.retry_after_seconds (integer). We also surface X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset (when available) under the X-RW-Rate-* headers for internal telemetry, but these are not considered authoritative for client retry logic. 2) Error shape: All adapter errors returned to OpenAI-compatible clients follow a single canonical shape: {"error":{"message":string,"type":string,"code":string,"param":string|null,"retry_after_seconds":int|null}}. This replaces ad-hoc bodies and maps internal error categories to OpenAI-friendly codes (rate_limit -> rate_limit_exceeded, conflict -> duplicate_request, internal -> server_error, invalid -> invalid_request_error). 3) Idempotency behavior: adapter accepts Idempotency-Key (case-insensitive). When present we: - atomically record a request fingerprint + response pointer in the dedupe store (Redis) with TTL (configurable, default 24h). - If a duplicate arrives and the original completed successfully: return the same HTTP status + body as the original (including same error envelope). - If a duplicate arrives while the original is still in flight: return 409 with code duplicate_request_in_progress and include header X-RW-Idempotency-Status: in_progress. - If a duplicate is detected but the new request parameters differ: return 409 conflict with message 'idempotency key collision: differing payloads'. - For streaming endpoints, successful responses are persisted as a replayable stream reference; duplicates will stream the recorded bytes so clients receive the identical sequence of chunk events and closing sentinel. 4) Streaming and partial failures: if an original stream failed mid-flight, subsequent duplicates will receive a deterministic error (code incomplete_stream) and an indication whether the client can safely retry (field can_retry in the error body). 5) Downstream propagation: internal calls now receive X-RW-Idempotency header when Idempotency-Key is present; this allows downstream systems to participate in dedupe semantics. 6) Backwards compatibility: behavior is gated behind the OpenAI-Compat-Version header (>= 2026-02) or the adapter flag openai_compat_strict: true. Without that header/flag, legacy behavior is preserved.

Files changed (high level): openai_adapter/handler.py (idempotency and retry handling), openai_adapter/errors.py (canonical error shapes and mappers), openai_adapter/stream_replay.py (stream persistence + replay), docs/openai-compat.md (compatibility matrix + examples), tests/test_idempotency.py (unit), tests/e2e_stream_replay.py (integration), ci/fixtures/idempotency.json (examples).

Rollout plan: - Deploy to staging with strict flag enabled for a subset of routes. - Run e2e stream replay and idempotency tests against staging. - Gradually enable for customers who specify OpenAI-Compat-Version or opt-in via account flag. - Monitor metrics: idempotency_hits, idempotency_collisions, rate_limit_retry_after_distribution.

Testing: unit coverage added for error mapping and idempotency collision detection; integration test reproduces a duplicated streaming request and asserts identical chunk sequence and final event. Load test exercised Retry-After handling across Nginx + upstream to validate header precedence.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration test for stream replay - [x] Docs updated with examples and migration notes - [x] Rollout plan included - [x] Telemetry counters added

Backward compatibility notes: clients not opting into the new compat version will not observe the stricter semantics. We intentionally limit change-surface to prevent breaking existing integrations.

References: Linear ENG-4812 (idempotency design), ENG-4820 (stream replay), SUP-3321 (support case prompting clarifications).
Evan Park (requested changes): Can you include a short TTL rationale for the dedupe store? 24h seems generous for some customers. Also add a metric for dedupe ttl expiries.
Author (Priya Sinha): TTL made configurable with default 24h; added metric idempotency_ttl_expiries and documentation explaining tradeoffs. Suggested shorter TTLs for high-volume endpoints.
Miguel Alvarez (comment): For streaming replay, what guarantees do we provide around event ids and chunks? We should avoid leaking internal offsets.
Author (Priya Sinha): Stream replay now uses a stable event-id namespace derived from request fingerprint; we do not expose upstream offsets. Added tests to verify event-id determinism.
Zoe Chen (approved): Security + privacy note: ensure persisted stream blobs are encrypted at rest and honored by retention policy. Please add an ops runbook for manual revoke.
Author (Priya Sinha): Added encryption note and ops runbook link in docs.

Motivation:
Older customers and OpenAI-compat SDKs frequently send requests without the new Accept-Schema header and rely on legacy streaming event types (e.g., delta/text fragments vs. structured 'output' envelope). After rolling out structured-output v3 we observed a class of integration breakages where legacy clients either face silent parse errors or spike error rates when the server emits new enum tokens in streaming frames.

Summary of changes:
- Add an in-process compatibility proxy layer in the redwood-openai-compat service that rewrites legacy requests into the canonical v3 schema at the edge when Accept-Schema is missing or set to an older version. The proxy is opt-in via feature flag but enabled for the canary cohort.
- Translate streaming frames from v3 structured-event envelopes back into legacy streaming event shapes for clients that indicate legacy schema via Accept-Schema or a missing header. This includes mapping new enum values (e.g., structured_output/FINISHED -> "done", structured_output/DELTA -> "delta_text") and adding a small delta buffer to reorder frames that had changed semantics.
- Introduce a short-lived shim for tool/function-calling: older callers expect a flat `tool_call` field; the proxy will normalize v3 function_call objects into that shape.
- Add end-to-end integration tests that run both legacy and updated SDK fixtures against the proxy to validate no behavioral regressions.
- Observability: new metrics for `compat.proxy.rewrites_total`, `compat.proxy.stream_mapped_total`, and a trace span `compat.proxy.rewrite` to help identify rewrites in production.

Design notes / tradeoffs:
- We intentionally keep rewriting logic lightweight (string/enum maps and shallow object reshapes) rather than deep model-guided transformations to reduce latency impact and avoid semantic drift.
- Streaming mapping introduces a 1-2ms per-frame overhead on average (measured in canary) due to buffer/resequence logic; this is acceptable for canary and can be disabled per-tenant.
- The feature flag gate allows us to flip the proxy per-region or per-account during rollout.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flagged canary in prod (5% traffic) for 48h with strict alerting on any increase in 4xx/5xx for streaming endpoints.
- Expand to 25% for a week if no regressions; full enable after 2 weeks.
- Deprecation schedule for older SDKs will be communicated: we will advertise a soft deprecation of missing Accept-Schema header in 90 days giving customers time to upgrade.

Testing done:
- Unit tests for enum mapping and object reshaping (coverage ~95% on compat module).
- Integration tests using recorded legacy SDK sessions that previously failed against structured-output v3; all pass.
- Load-tested proxy under synthetic streaming workloads: median added latency 1.8ms/frame; p95 6ms/frame.

Files changed (high-level):
- cmd/compat-proxy/main.go: new proxy bootstrap and feature-flag config
- internal/compat/proxy.go: core rewrite logic and streaming mapper
- internal/compat/mappings.go: enum and object mapping tables + tests
- api/compatibility/accept_schema_middleware.go: header negotiation middleware
- integration/legacy-fixtures/*: new legacy client fixtures and golden recordings
- observability/metrics.yaml: new metric defs and dashboard snippets
- docs/compat/README.md: rollout instructions and behavior specs

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration tests with legacy fixtures
- [x] Metrics and traces added
- [x] Feature-flagged with default off for tenants
- [x] Docs and rollout plan

Related work:
- Follow-on work scheduled to add a telemetry ping from upgraded SDKs to help us target tenants during the 90-day deprecation window (ENG-8239).

Notes:
- This PR is designed to be a short-term compatibility layer; teams should still migrate to explicit Accept-Schema negotiation to avoid relying on server-side heuristics.

Casey Liu: Small nit: prefer explicit enum mapping table rather than switch chains in proxy.go — makes it easier to extend. Also request a short comment on the ordering buffer size rationale.
Author (Asha Patel): addressed — moved mappings into a dedicated file and documented buffer size rationale; added unit test for boundary behavior.
Emma Johansson: We saw a CI flake on integration/legacy-fixtures tests when run under race detector; can you add a deterministic timeout?
Author (Asha Patel): added 20s deterministic timeout and retried CI; race flake went away.
Miguel Torres: Approve after CI green. Left a suggestion to expose tenant-level opt-out via admin API later but not blocking.
Adds a temporary compatibility proxy that rewrites legacy requests and streaming frames to preserve behavior for older SDKs when Accept-Schema is missing. Feature-flagged and can be disabled per-tenant. New metrics added for monitoring.

payload.body:
Motivation: We are rolling out a tightened API contract that clarifies streaming chunk semantics, deterministic tool/function-calling payloads, and a more explicit structured-output framing. To avoid breaking existing customers and to enable staged opt-in, this PR introduces a runtime "fallback adapter" and an opt-in request header (Beta-Contract) that toggles the new contract behavior for a single request. The goal is to let client SDKs and downstream services validate the new contract in production traffic without forcing a global server-side switch.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a lightweight adapter layer in the OpenAI-compatibility route that performs request/response normalization when Beta-Contract is present. The adapter enforces stricter streaming delimiters, canonicalizes function-call payloads, and validates structured-output envelopes.
- Implements a Beta-Contract request header: "X-Redwood-Beta-Contract: v1-preview". Header is ignored for older clients. The header enables the adapter path and is logged for telemetry.
- Ensures streaming stability by adding an idempotent chunk reassembly pass that handles corner cases where partial delta tokens previously caused malformed JSON in structured outputs. This includes a backoff/retry for the streaming parser when it encounters non-terminal tokens.
- Provides compatibility hooks in the tool/function-calling layer so that invocation targets receive the canonicalized args shape (array-of-objects canonicalization) while still preserving original metadata in a "compat_meta" field for debugging.
- Adds a comprehensive test matrix (unit + integration) that asserts parity for legacy traffic and verifies contract behavior with Beta-Contract header enabled.

Commits (summary):
- 3a7b4c1: feat(adapter): add runtime fallback adapter and header parsing; basic telemetry events
- b8d9f02: fix(stream): robust chunk reassembly and streaming parser retry; add parser metrics
- c44211e: feat(tools): canonicalize function-call args and attach compat_meta; update tool runtime contract tests
- e1f90a6: test(ci): add integration matrix for old vs beta contract; include synthetic streaming edgecases
- f7550d3: docs: add header spec and migration guidance to openai-compat README

Changed files (high level):
- src/compat/adapter/fallback_adapter.py (new) - adapter implementation and header hook
- src/compat/middleware/header_middleware.py (mod) - parse and validate Beta-Contract header
- src/compat/streaming/parser.py (mod) - idempotent reassembly, retry logic, metrics hooks
- src/compat/tools/canonicalizer.py (new) - function-call args canonicalization + compat_meta
- tests/compat/test_beta_contract_matrix.py (new) - matrix test harness
- docs/openai-compat/contract-beta.md (new) - header spec, examples, telemetry notes
- ci/pipelines/compat-matrix.yml (mod) - run integration matrix in PR CI
- examples/compat-demo/client_preview.py (new) - sample client showing header usage

Notes on backward compatibility: The adapter is strictly opt-in. No change to default runtime for existing requests. The header is intentionally verbose to discourage accidental rollouts. Existing SDKs will continue to work; SDK maintainers can ship an opt-in toggle that sets the header during beta trials. There is an "adapter-telemetry" event that surfaces when a request uses the Beta-Contract and when the adapter falls back to legacy normalization due to an unparseable stream chunk.

Review conversation (selected excerpts):
- Ethan Cole (reviewer): "This looks good overall. Two asks: 1) add a small benchmark to measure adapter overhead in p95 for short requests, 2) ensure the compat_meta does not leak sensitive user data by default."
- Maya Liang (author): "Added the micro-benchmark; compat_meta is gated behind a debug flag and redacted by default. See tests and README notes."
- Rosa Alvarez (reviewer): "Streaming reassembly is the right call. Could we avoid introducing additional cross-process retries? I'm worried about head-of-line blocking in battched serving lanes."
- Daniel Kim (reviewer): "Confirmed CI matrix passed on my re-run. Verified the adapter adds ~1.8ms p95 on short text-gen requests in our lab; acceptable for beta trials."

CI summary: The PR runs the compat integration matrix (old vs beta), unit tests, packaging, lint, and the streaming-legitimacy suite. The first CI run had a flaky test in tests/streaming/test_fragmented_json.py which was fixed by increasing the parser buffer threshold; final CI status: all checks passed.

Operational considerations:
- Telemetry: new events: compat.adapter.used, compat.adapter.fallback, compat.parser.retry, compat.header.invalid. These are available in Console with a 24h default retention for the beta.
- Rollout plan: Beta usage is controlled client-side. After a two-week opt-in period and no regressions reported by the QA channel, we'll consider enabling a rolling opt-in for internal SDKs and feature flags. No forceful server-side flip is planned in this PR.
- Observability: Added dashboards for parser retry rates and adapter p95 cost. Alerting threshold suggested at 5% retry rate over 15m.

Merge decision: After reviews and CI green, PR was squashed and merged to main. No migration script required.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-2179: Add server-side feature-flag to apply adapter per-customer for controlled experiments (not included in this PR).
- PM-649: Draft customer-facing migration notes and SDK opt-in snippets for the next docs push.

This PR is intentionally conservative: it provides a path to test the new contract without breaking traffic and gives engineers a way to debug contract regressions with compat_meta and telemetry. The implementation emphasizes minimal latency overhead and explicit opt-in semantics.
Introduce a non-breaking runtime adapter and an opt-in Beta-Contract header to allow clients to exercise a new API contract for streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs. Existing clients unchanged unless they opt in.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: We observed two incidents where in-place private upgrades partially applied schema migrations and left clusters in an inconsistent state when failures happened mid-upgrade. Existing rollback relied on restoring full snapshots which is slow and error-prone for large on-prem datasets. This change implements a blue/green upgrade orchestrator for the private installer that creates application-consistent DB checkpoints and performs an atomic cutover between environments to enable fast, low-risk rollback.
Implementation summary: - installer/controller: add a new UpgradeOrchestrator CR workflow (stateless controller in the private installer operator) that drives blue/green lifecycle: preflight -> backup checkpoint -> apply changes to green -> verify -> traffic switch -> decommission old (with optional quarantine). Orchestrator uses tenant-aware fencing to avoid cross-tenant impact and records checkpoints with timestamped IDs. - DB checkpointing: introduce transactional checkpoint step for Postgres-based deployments using pg_start_backup/pg_stop_backup + coordinated WAL archival to S3/GCS-compatible buckets, plus an optional pglogical consistent snapshot path for multi-node clusters. For air-gapped customers we added an offline snapshot export format and a local filesystem staging flow. - Helm changes: add blue-green deployment hooks, pre-upgrade test hooks, configurable `cutoverStrategy` (immediate | canary | manual-confirm) and annotations to opt in per-namespace. The chart now exposes a `checkpointPolicy` that controls retention TTL and verification steps. - Terraform updates: add state_locking and backup_bucket modules, and a lightweight kms_integration optional resource to encrypt exported checkpoints. The terraform module also exposes a `quarantine_tenant` toggle used by the orchestrator. - CLI & docs: private-installer CLI gains `upgrade preview --dry-run` and `rollback to-checkpoint <id>` commands, plus a new runbook in docs/operator/runbooks/bluegreen-upgrade.md. - Tests: added e2e smoke tests that simulate partial-failure during migration and verify rollback behavior; unit tests cover orchestration state transitions and failure retry logic.
Commits (summary): - 1a3f9e5: operator: add UpgradeOrchestrator state machine and API surface - 2b6c0d2: db: implement transactional checkpoint exporter + offline format - 37f9b01: helm: blue-green hooks + cutoverStrategy + checkpointPolicy - 4d0a8b7: terraform: backup_bucket + state_locking + kms optional - 5c2fe14: cli/docs: dry-run/rollback commands + runbook - 6f8e0b3: tests: add e2e partial-failure simulations and unit coverage
Changed areas / high-level file list: - operator/: orchestrator controller, CRD, state machine - db/backup/: checkpoint exporter, WAL helper scripts - charts/private-installer/: templates, hooks, values.yaml additions - terraform/modules/backup_bucket/: new module + examples - cli/: upgrade preview and rollback commands - docs/: new runbook and upgrade guide - tests/e2e/: bluegreen scenarios and test harness
Reviewer conversation (high-level): - Seth Kim (comment, 2025-09-20): "The checkpoint flow looks solid but we need clear failure modes for partial WAL upload failures. Please add retries and documented operator retry policy." - Marina Alvarez (reply, 2025-09-21): "Added exponential backoff retry for WAL uploads and operator-level retry limit with reconciler-visible condition. See db/backup/retry_policy.go" - Anita Rao (request changes, 2025-09-22): "Helm values are powerful but add an escape hatch for air-gapped installs; make export path configurable via values as a filesystem path." - Marina Alvarez (update, 2025-09-23): "Added values.export.path and documented offline export flow in helm/README.md; added e2e test for local export." - Lars Mikkelson (approve, 2025-09-28): "Verified e2e failure injection and rollback within 90s on our test harness; small nits left in docs but not blocking."
CI history summary: - initial CI run: lint & unit: pass; integration/e2e: failed (WAL-upload flakiness) - second run after patch: all checks pass (integration rerun successful)
Rollout / merge notes: - This PR is merged to main via squash on 2025-10-02 after approvals. - Default behavior is opt-in: charts and installer keep blue/green disabled by default; operators must set cutoverStrategy and checkpointPolicy explicitly. - For customers upgrading to a release that includes this orchestrator: instruct to run `private-installer upgrade preview --dry-run` first; if opting in, recommended to set `checkpointPolicy.retentionDays >= 7`.
Rollback playbook (short): - If a migration fails on the green cluster, run `private-installer rollback to-checkpoint <checkpoint-id>` which will: 1) fence tenant traffic, 2) apply checkpoint restore (WAL replay or offline import), 3) re-point service mesh/ingress back to blue, 4) mark green for quarantine and alert SRE.
Related work: ENG-8421 (design doc), ENG-8475 (helm-value gating).
Security notes: - Checkpoints are encrypted at rest when using the terraform kms option; default S3-compatible buckets are private. - Added an audit log entry for `upgrade.start`, `upgrade.checkpoint.create`, `upgrade.cutover`, and `rollback.start`.
Migration compatibility / downgrade guards: - Orchestrator records a manifest hash tied to the installer release; rollback will refuse to restore checkpoints produced by newer major installer versions unless `force-allow-downgrade` is explicitly enabled (audit entry required). This prevents silent incompatibility in schema/manifest formats.
Known limitations and follow-ups: - MySQL connectors are currently out-of-scope; follow-up task added ENG-8609. - Large clusters with multi-TB datasets may still face long WAL upload windows; follow-up to support streaming WAL replication to backup endpoints planned. - UX: add console visualization of orchestrator state (follow-up ENG-8712).
CI / deploy notes for SRE: - Add the new terraform backup_bucket module when creating or upgrading a private deployment to ensure checkpoints have a durable store. - For air-gapped installs, ensure offline export path is writable and cluster has sufficient temporary storage. This PR bundles code, chart, terraform, docs, and tests to make private upgrades safe and fast with an opt-in blue/green model.
Add blue/green upgrade orchestrator to private installer with transactional DB checkpoint support, Helm hooks for safe cutover, and Terraform locking for state + backup resources. Included runbook and e2e smoke tests.
This PR intentionally keeps opt-in behavior to limit blast radius; ops required to enable in production. Follow-ups tracked in ENG-8609 and ENG-8712.

Motivation: debugging SLO regressions often requires stitching together fragments from frontend request IDs, gateway hops, router handoffs, and backend runtime spans. Current dashboards surface aggregate per-route latency and token cost but lack an easy way to answer: which execution stage contributed most to tail latency for a given session or user flow? This PR introduces a session reassembler that groups spans and logs into session-level traces, computes a latency contribution matrix per-stage, and surfaces the results in a new dashboard with drilldowns. Design: 1) Session reassembler: deterministic session keys are computed from request headers (x-session-id when present), fallback to hashed {client_ip,user_agent,first-7-chars-of-request_id} for best-effort reconstruction. The reassembler runs as a bounded streaming transformer in the tracing pipeline and emits enriched spans tagged with session_id and stage_ordinal. 2) Late-arrival span stitching: implement a 30s buffer window with eventual reconciliation to handle spans that arrive after initial aggregation. Reconciled sessions are exported as session_digests which include per-stage p50/p90/p99 latencies and token counts. 3) Latency contribution matrix: for each session_digest we compute a normalized contribution vector across stages (gateway, auth, preproc, router, runtime-queue, runtime-exec, postproc). Matrices are aggregated into reservoir sketches to keep cardinality bounded. 4) Dashboard and alerting: new dashboard panel "Session Latency Matrix" visualizes dominant contributors for recent sessions and supports filtering by customer, route, and model. Introduce an SLO smoothing policy that uses session-level p95 of contribution instead of raw endpoint p95 to reduce noisy alerts from noisy frontends. 5) Backwards compatibility and opt-in: the reassembler is behind a rollout flag in the observability config; default is disabled. Customers can opt-in per-tenant. Rollout plan: enable in staging for 48 hours, shadow in prod for 7 days, then enable for 10% of traffic with metric gates. Telemetry: we emit reassembler.metrics.{sessions_processed,stitch_reconciliations,session_digest_size} and tagging on traces with session.id and stage.rank. Rollout notes: this PR adds additional memory for the buffering stage; sizing guidance documented in observability/README. Security: session keys do not materialize raw client_ip in exported payloads unless tenant-level PII flag is set; by default keys are salted and one-way hashed. Related work: this complements ENG-1942 (sampling improvements) and OBS-73 (session-based alerting).
feat(observability): add session reassembler transformer and session_digest export; feat(tracing): late-arrival stitcher and reconciliation; perf(tracing): reservoir sketch for contribution matrices; ui(dashboards): session latency matrix and drilldowns; docs: rollout and sizing guidance; test: unit+integration for reassembler and reconciliation
Aidan Keller: Can you clarify the semantics of the fallback session key? Maya Chen: Fallback uses a salted hash of client_ip+user_agent+req_prefix; salted per-tenant and not reversible. Priya Nair: The 30s buffer seems small for some tenants with eventual log shipping; any plan? Maya Chen: We reconciled to make the window configurable and added a reconnect/reconciliation metric; default remains 30s to bound memory. Diego Ruiz: Reservoir sketches look good but please add a test for cardinality drift. Maya Chen: Added tests to integration suite and a benchmark in scripts/size_estimator. Priya Nair: Approve after CI pass. Aidan Keller: Left a small nit on the UI (color scale) — updated in follow-up commit. Diego Ruiz: Verified metrics emission and endorses merge.
Adds an opt-in session reassembler for reconstructing traces across hops, per-session latency contribution matrices, a new Session Latency Matrix dashboard with drilldowns, SLO smoothing policy using session-level contributions, and observability metrics for rollout and sizing. No breaking changes by default; opt-in per-tenant.
Sizing guidance added under docs/observability/README.md; may require observability team to coordinate with infra for buffer memory when enabling for high-cardinality tenants.

payload.body:
Motivation: several production workloads exhibit tail latency and throughput sensitivity when sequence lengths vary and when cold KV-cache misses occur. This change implements a pipelined attention kernel that overlaps QKV compute with async prefetch of KV slabs, adds a compact slab-based KV cache to reduce lookup overhead, and introduces a fused rotary/rope transformation pass at the kernel level. The implementation is opt-in behind a runtime feature flag (ATTN_PIPELINE=on) and includes a compatibility fallback to the existing attention path for models that rely on nonstandard rotary encodings. Highlights: 1) New pipelined kernel that splits the attention op into (a) gather + rotary-fuse compute for Q/K/V, (b) async DMA prefetch of KV slab pages based on predicted access windows, and (c) overlap of softmax/weighted-sum with next-token KV assembly. This reduces blocking on device memory stalls and improves token throughput for batched streaming. 2) KV-slab cache: a compact page-aligned slab cache with LRU eviction tuned for typical prefix reuse patterns and continuous-batching workloads. The cache exposes lightweight instrumentation hooks for hit/miss histograms and integrates with existing prefix-KV eviction policies. 3) Fused rotary pass: a compute-level fusion that applies rotary embeddings immediately after Q/K compute and before layout transposition to reduce memory traffic and kernel launches. 4) Scheduler hints for continuous batching: the runtime receives a short-lived hint from the kernel (prefetch latency and observed reuse window) which the scheduler uses to slightly bias batch formation and placement to improve coalesced KV usage. 5) Safety and fallbacks: if async prefetch is not supported on the device or if the slab cache pressure exceeds thresholds, the runtime falls back to the legacy attention kernel. Tests and validation: microbenchmarks (redwood/benchmarks/attn_pipeline) show median latency improvements of 18-26% and throughput +20-35% on production-like GPT-style models across sequence lengths 128..1024 with minimal memory overhead (+1-3%). CI and canary: added unit tests, end-to-end regression tests, and a staged perf-canary rollout plan (perf-canary config included) to gradually enable the flag for Dedicated customers. Related Linear issues: ENG-3421 (attention perf), ENG-3490 (kv cache telemetry). This PR bundles codegen patches, kernel implementations, runtime plumbing, and documentation for the runtime config. Context: we're rolling a new v2 request/response schema for the OpenAI compatibility layer that changes streaming chunk shapes and tool-call payloads. To avoid breaking existing clients immediately, this PR introduces a runtime shim that negotiates schema version via headers and provides a V2->legacy translation fallback. The shim recognizes an explicit preference header (Prefer-Schema-Version: 2) and a legacy beta header (X-OpenAI-Beta: schema-v2); when clients request v2 we serve native v2 responses. For clients that do not opt in, the shim will emit a deprecation warning header (Warning: 299 Deprecated legacy-response-mode) and translate v2 outputs back into the v1 wire shape so existing integrations remain functional. Motivation: gives customers time to migrate while enabling server-side V2 rollout and opt-in testing. What this PR changes: 1) adds a negotiator component that inspects incoming headers and routes through the v2 execution path or the compat translator; 2) implements the V2->V1 response translator for streaming chunks, function/tool-call structures, and structured-output envelopes; 3) exposes runtime config flags (compat.v2_fallback.enabled and RW_COMPAT_V2_FALLBACK env var) and a per-customer override in the control plane; 4) includes end-to-end integration tests that exercise streaming + translator and unit tests for header negotiation and warning emissions; 5) updates docs and adds a migration guide snippet to the compat README. Backward-incompatible notes: legacy mode is now deprecation-flagged but behavior preserved by the translator. Migration guidance: customers should start sending Prefer-Schema-Version: 2 or X-OpenAI-Beta: schema-v2 to opt into new schema, and update streaming handlers to accept the v2 chunk envelope (example in docs). Rollout plan: feature gate flipped off by default for a short canary cohort, then enabled globally after 2 weeks of monitoring. Checklist: - [x] negotiator + translator implementation - [x] unit tests - [x] integration (streaming) tests - [x] docs and migration guide - [x] console flag and env var - [x] monitoring and deprecation metrics. Risk/rollback: translator lives behind config flag; revert simply disables the translator and returns to previous routing. Related: ENG-2381 (schema rollout), SUP-5192 (support ticket about streaming mismatch).
Tomás: Please make the header name configurable via config; some customers prefer a namespaced header. Priya: added compat.header_name config and env RW_COMPAT_HEADER in follow-up commit.
Li: The streaming translator should preserve partial delta semantics for clients that rely on incremental tokens. Priya: fixed by keeping 'delta' in chunk payload and adding explicit continuation flag in translator.
Avery: How will metrics capture migrated vs legacy traffic? Priya: added a telemetry tag 'schema_version' emitted by negotiator and documented expected charts.
Add header-based schema negotiation: Prefer-Schema-Version and X-OpenAI-Beta
Introduce a V2->V1 translator to provide backward compatibility for streaming and tool-calls
Emit deprecation warning header for legacy clients; plan for full deprecation in 90 days
Runtime flag compat.v2_fallback.enabled and env RW_COMPAT_V2_FALLBACK to disable translator during rollback

payload.body:
Problem: intermittent mid-stream truncation and delimiter duplication in SSE streams caused downstream consumers to observe malformed JSON events or re-ordered tool/function-call boundaries when a chunk split cut inside a UTF-8 sequence or inside a JSON token. This surfaced in production as two classes of failures: (1) partial structured outputs becoming unparsable, and (2) function/tool-call sentinel events interleaving with regular token frames when a flushing boundary coincided with transport fragmentation.

Goal: make the OpenAI-compat SSE path resilient to arbitrarily split transport chunks while keeping latency and memory overhead bounded. Provide deterministic repair strategies so clients can rely on ordered event emission and a single authoritative function-call boundary.

What I changed: single continuous narrative of changes below.
- Introduced a "boundary-fence" reassembler: when the parser detects an unterminated JSON span (object/array/string) it will hold a bounded buffer and attempt reassembly across up to N successive chunks using a seq-window. The fence introduces an explicit lightweight SSE comment line of the form ":bseq=<seq>" emitted by the server-side gateway to tag chunk epochs; consumers can use this to resync after out-of-order arrival.
- Added seq-slack window metadata and conservative backpressure: the gateway assigns monotonic chunk epoch IDs and honors an in-flight window (configurable, default 8). This reduces reliance on heuristics during heavy concurrency and ensures ordering when multiple upstream shards may race.
- Call-drain ack handshake for function/tool-call frames: previously, a function-call sentinel ("]CALL\n" / "event: tool_call") could be split such that downstream saw call payload and then trailing tokens from the next completion. We introduced a two-phase emit for call-boundaries: the emitter marks the boundary with ":drain_ack=<id>" and will not emit subsequent completion frames until the drain is acknowledged by the local reassembler. This guarantees the function call is observed atomically by streaming clients.
- Trailing delimiter normalizer: normalize duplicate trailing delimiters produced by transport coalescing (e.g., multiple consecutive "\n\n" sequences) by collapsing to single canonical boundary while preserving a sentinel comment for observability.
- UTF-8 safe chunk splice prevention: we now detect split multi-byte sequences and defer decode until contiguous bytes are available; we avoid replacing invalid UTF bytes with U+FFFD in the streaming pipeline to prevent accidental JSON corruption.
- Tests & instrumentation: added a suite of targeted SSE fuzz tests and a small integration harness that emulates split-chunk delivery with random byte boundaries. Added metrics (compat.sse.reassembly.success, compat.sse.reassembly.fail, compat.sse.drain.latency) and Console dashboard docs.

Why this is different from previous approaches: instead of a large in-memory reassembler, the boundary-fence uses epoch markers plus a tiny sliding window to achieve deterministic repair without unbounded buffering; the call-drain handshake explicitly addresses function/tool-call atomicity rather than relying solely on JSON heuristics.

Compatibility notes: the new epoch markers are emitted as SSE comments (leading colon) so existing OpenAI-compat clients ignore them unless updated. The drain_ack marker is optional — the server can operate in a legacy-compat mode where it emits legacy boundaries, but we recommend enabling the handshake for production workloads that use function/tool calls.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add boundary-fence reassembler implementation (Go)
- [x] Add seq-epoch tagging in gateway emitter
- [x] Implement call-drain ack handshake and integration tests
- [x] Add unit & integration tests for mid-stream splits and UTF-8 boundary cases
- [x] Add metrics and Console docs snippets
- [x] Performance sanity: end-to-end p50 latency change < 4% for small completion workloads

Rollout plan: feature-flag behind "compat.stream.boundary_fence"; disabled by default for 48h canary, enable for GA after 7d of canary telemetry.

Related: ENG-4821 (streaming stability epic), ENG-4999 (function-call ordering), related PRs that touch parser internals.

Notes on operational behavior: if reassembly fails after the configured seq-window, we emit an actionable telemetry event and insert a minimal synthetic terminator event to avoid client hangs; this is opt-in and controlled by the feature flag.

Amit Rao: Can we bound the in-memory window size more aggressively? On large concurrent workloads this could still balloon if not capped. Suggest a hard cap + LRU eviction for very large events.
Priya Shah: Addressed — added a hard cap (maxBufferBytes=1MB per epoch) and an eviction policy that inserts a synthetic terminator when violated. Updated tests to assert synthetic terminator emission and telemetry path.
Sofia Kramer: The drain_ack handshake looks good, but we need to ensure legacy clients are not negatively affected. Add a feature flag and a compatibility regression test.
Priya Shah: Done — feature flag added and CI includes a legacy client emulation job that verifies pre-flag behavior remains unchanged.
Noah Bennett: CI flake on Windows due to line-ending handling in the fuzz harness; please normalize CRLF in the harness.
Priya Shah: Fixed the harness to normalize line endings and added platform matrix to CI config.
Stability: Harden SSE streaming in OpenAI-compat path — deterministic reassembly of split chunks, stable function/tool-call boundary semantics, and UTF-8 safe chunk handling. Opt-in via feature flag compat.stream.boundary_fence. Metrics added for reassembly and drain latency.
payload.title: stream-gate: introduce boundary-fence reassembler and call-drain ack for safer mid-stream cut

payload.body:
Motivation: We continue to see production incidents where streaming ingestion produces truncated JSON objects or mis-ordered function-call sentinel emissions when event fragments split across network frames and backpressure windows. These manifest as partial JSON payloads that downstream consumers treat as terminal, or as tool calls arriving before the final assistant delta, causing client-side parse failures. This PR rewrites the stream stitcher to anchor frame boundaries and adds a deterministic partial-JSON rescue path.

What changed (high level):
- New stitcher core: replaces the incremental buffer heuristic with an anchored-boundary protocol that maintains a small ledger of boundary anchors (sequence anchor tokens emitted by the runtime) and uses them to align fragments before attempting JSON reconstruction. Anchors are lightweight and flow with existing SSE comments to avoid protocol changes.
- Partial-JSON rescue: when a JSON object cannot be parsed after coalescing, we attempt a conservative rescue that trims trailing incomplete UTF-8 sequences and applies token-aware re-synchronization heuristics to preserve at least one valid JSON subtree (useful for structured outputs and tool call payloads).
- Function/tool-call ordering: we added an ordering gate that delays emitting function-call sentinel events until the stitcher confirms the surrounding JSON span is well-formed or after rescue succeeds. This reduces false-positive tool invocations for split frames.
- Delimiter normalization: normalize mixed delimiter sequences (0x0A, 0x0D0A variants) emitted by different clients and proxies so chunk boundaries are not treated as message boundaries by mistake.
- Strict mode flag: introduced feature flag stream.stitcher.strict (default: false for compatibility). When enabled the stitcher fails fast on ambiguous anchors and surfaces a metrics tag to drive rollouts.

Why this approach: Previous fixes focused on ad-hoc coalescing and UTF-8 repair in multiple places which evolved divergent heuristics across language bindings. Consolidating logic into a single stitcher reduces duplication, centralizes metrics and observability, and provides a single opt-in path to tighten semantics without breaking existing clients. Anchors provide a minimal, backward-compatible signal that improves alignment accuracy under packet-loss and proxy chunking scenarios.

Commits (summary):
- Rewrite: introduce StreamStitcher with anchor ledger and resync algorithms (core rewrite).
- Parser: add partial_json_rescue utility and UTF-8 tail trimmer.
- OpenAI compat: gate function-call emission behind stitcher confirmation.
- Tests: add deterministic fuzz vectors and integration tests that simulate TCP-level splits and HTTP/2 push chunking.
- Docs: document stream.stitcher.strict and troubleshooting guide.

Files changed (high level):
- src/streaming/stream_stitcher.rs (new core implementation)
- src/openai_compat/sse_parser.py (normalize delimiters, call gating)
- tests/test_sse_framing.py (unit + fuzz harness)
- docs/compatibility/streaming.md (operational notes and flag docs)
- examples/compatibility/streaming_playground.rs (manual repros)
- tools/compat/test_vectors.json (new test vectors for fragmented frames)
- ci/flake_fuzz.sh (harness integration)

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests cover UTF-8 tail trimming, anchor ledger edge cases, and ordering gate scenarios.
- Integration tests run a local HTTP/2 chunker against both the legacy and new stitcher; observed a 96% reduction in partial-JSON error rates on the supplied corpus.
- Fuzz harness produced no regressions after 3 CI reruns; CI passed on Linux x86_64 and macOS runners.
- Canary rollout in internal staging for 24h with stream.stitcher.strict disabled; Prometheus metrics show decreased sse_parse_error_count and fewer tool-call-duplicates.

Observability and signals:
- New metrics: stitcher.anchor_misses, stitcher.rescue_attempts, stitcher.rescue_success, stitcher.emit_delay_ms.
- Logs: increased visibility when rescue path runs (log level DEBUG by default) and an INFO event when strict mode blocks emission.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan:
- Default behavior is backward-compatible: anchors are optional and stitched only when present; if anchors are missing we fall back to previous coalescing heuristics.
- Feature flag stream.stitcher.strict must be enabled per deployment to activate hard failure behavior. We will roll strict to canaries, then a small percentage cohort, and observe tool-call duplication and consumer parse errors.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: strict mode could surface parse failures for clients that rely on prior lenient behavior. Mitigation: strict is off by default and includes a clear metric tag to track breakage.
- Risk: performance regressions from extra ledger bookkeeping. Mitigation: microbenchmarks show <1.6% CPU overhead at p95 QPS with anchors enabled; we will monitor in Dedicated pods.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4829)
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] Fuzzing applied and CI green
- [x] Docs updated
- [x] Metrics instrumented

Notes for reviewers: focus on the anchor lifetime semantics in stream_stitcher.rs and on the gating logic in sse_parser.py. In particular, check that the ledger never grows unbounded (we evict anchors older than 2x median RTT) and that the rescue heuristic only returns JSON subtrees when they can be safely parsed without inventing keys.

Merge notes: Squash-merged after approvals. Canary rollout initiated immediately after merge with stream.stitcher.strict=false by default.
Sven Petrov: Anchor eviction window looks right but please add a comment explaining the 2x RTT heuristic and the constant used.
Imani Okafor: Added inline comment and a unit test for anchor eviction behavior.
Lila Moreno: Rescue path is clever; please ensure we don't return malformed tool-call arguments — added a minor nit to the parser unit test.
Imani Okafor: Tightened parser validation and added an extra integration case where the tool-call contains nested arrays.
Arjun Suresh: Verified ordering gate on integration run; one suggestion to reduce temporary allocations in the ledger, marked as optional.
Imani Okafor: Applied allocation reduction in the ledger; benchmark regression removed.
SRE Bot: CI stress test reported 1 flaky on macOS runner, re-ran the job and it passed.
QA: Approved after end-to-end test against streaming_playground and downstream client SDKs.

payload.body:
Motivation: Several customers reported intermittent function/tool-calling failures and long tail latency when clients opened many concurrent streaming connections. Root cause analysis showed that the gateway's fixed per-connection proxy buffer window caused head-of-line backpressure and aggressive route-level payload enforcement caused sudden request drops under bursty tool-call fanout. This PR introduces an adaptive proxy windowing algorithm plus a token-rate smoothing layer for OpenAI-compat function/tool calls to reduce transient failures while keeping route payload limits enforced.

Summary of approach: 1) Adaptive proxy windowing: replace the static per-connection buffer with a sliding window that tracks recent token-forward throughput and dynamically adjusts the in-memory buffer and flush thresholds. The window is conservative for low-throughput connections (to minimize memory) and expands under sustained streaming to reduce fragmentation. 2) Tool-call rate smoothing: introduce a lightweight leaky-bucket per-route that smooths bursts of downstream tool/function calls originating from a single incoming request (helps when a single response triggers many parallel webhook/tool calls). 3) Graceful payload enforcement: move strict payload-size enforcement to a two-step check: a fast soft quota that allows short-lived overshoots (logged and meter-tagged) and a stricter hard quota which only triggers if the overshoot persists beyond a configurable time window. 4) OpenAI-compat shim updates: the compatibility layer now maps function-calling handshakes to the new smoothing API and translates the gateway's streaming frames into a stable JSONL framing when needed to avoid client-side parser errors. 5) Observability and experiments: new metrics, traces, and an A/B rollout to validate behavior under production traffic.

Key outcomes from internal canary (1 week, mixed traffic): - 95th percentile streaming latency reduced by ~18% for endpoints with heavy tool-call fanout. - Tool/function-call transient failures decreased by ~42% in end-to-end regression tests. - Memory usage per proxy worker increased by ~6% under steady-state high-concurrency workloads; we added a configurable hard cap.

Compatibility notes: The default behavior is opt-in via route flag "adaptive_proxy_window": true for routes. For OpenAI-compat routes we enable smoothing by default but keep a feature flag (compat_tool_smoothing) to toggle to previous behavior for quick rollback. No API contract changes for customers; the updates are internal gateway optimizations but can affect behavior at the margins (short-lived overshoot vs immediate 413 responses).

Testing and QA: - Unit and integration tests for window sizing heuristics and bucket refill semantics. - Added e2e scenario simulating a single chat response causing 40 parallel tool calls; validated rate smoothing and end-to-end correctness (function-call responses are aggregated into the stream without reordering). - Load testing showing improved 95p latency when aggregated across routes with high function-call density. - CI initially failed a flakey test (proxy window race) and was fixed by adding an ordering assertion and a deterministic timer in test harness.

Rollback and rollout plan: Gradual rollout over 3 days: 5% -> 25% -> 100% traffic for routes with the feature flag enabled. Automated canary checks validate error rate, 95p latency, and the new metric "proxy_window_fill_ratio". Fast rollback toggles the route flag to false and reverts to the previous stable windowing implementation.

Notes on operational tuning: - Default soft overshoot window: 200ms; hard quota enforcement: 5s. - Default per-route smoothing token refill: 50 tokens/sec with burst of 200 tokens. - New admin endpoints expose per-route buckets and current window sizes for debugging.

Related work and references: This PR builds on ENG-4921 (gateway buffering investigation) and ENG-4987 (fncall meltdown post-traffic spike). Related docs: updated compat docs and gateway operational runbook.
Liam O'Connor: Can we make the soft overshoot window configurable per-tenant? I worry enterprise customers will want tighter controls.
Maya Patel (reply): Added per-tenant override in the config; default continues to be route-level. See gateway/config/proxy_buffering.yaml.
Ravi Singh: The JSONL framing change is subtle for some older clients — did we add integration tests for legacy parsers?
Maya Patel (reply): Yes, added sdk/ts/tests/openai_compat_streaming.test.ts which exercises both legacy newline-delimited parsing and the JSONL frames. Also kept the old framing available behind a flag.
Sofia Martinez: CI was failing due to a race in the test harness; confirmed fix and reran CI. Approving after green builds.
Automated CI: Initial build failed (proxy_timer_harness.go flake); rerun passed. All checks green.
- Introduced adaptive proxy windowing to reduce head-of-line streaming latency; opt-in per-route flag.
- Added tool/function-call rate smoothing to reduce transient failures under high fanout.
- OpenAI-compat layer maps function-calling handshakes to the smoothing API and optionally uses stable JSONL framing to avoid parser errors.
- New observability metrics: proxy_window_fill_ratio, toolcall_smoothing_rate, proxy_buffer_overshoot_count.

Context & motivation: Customers running structured-output in production reported two classes of failures: (1) transient stream corruption during long-running streaming responses (partial JSON fragments that never reconcile), and (2) silent schema regressions when developers rely on soft validation. This PR introduces a small-but-impactful API surface + runtime changes to reduce both failure modes and to make OpenAI-compatible tool/function calling safer across streams.

What this change does (single sentence): Adds a validate_mode api option (off|warn|enforce) and a lightweight stream checkpointing protocol to enable resumable/repairable JSON-schema streaming with clearer error semantics and actionable telemetry.

Details (single continuous description): The new request-level parameter response_format.validate_mode controls runtime validation behavior. Mode semantics: 
- off: no validation at runtime (existing behavior).
- warn: runtime performs schema checks on streaming checkpoints and emits structured warnings in telemetry and the final response metadata; the model output is not rejected.
- enforce: runtime will attempt incremental correction using the last successful checkpoint, and if unrecoverable will terminate the stream early with a structured schema error payload (contract: status=invalid_schema, hint, checkpoint_cursor).

To support enforce/warn we introduce a compact checkpointing marker inserted into streaming chunks by the runtime when response_format.type == "json_schema" (configurable opt-in). Checkpoints are lightweight serialized deltas (SHA256 prefix + length + truncated fragment) and are never persisted to disk — they live in process in the serving worker's KV cache for up to 30s by default. On detection of parse failure the worker will rewind the stream to the last checkpoint and attempt one of: request a model retry (up to 2 attempts), coerce minor type mismatches (config-driven), or emit an enforce-mode structured error.

OpenAI-compat updates: function_call payloads in streaming now include an extra field function_call.arg_schema_hash to ensure tool arguments match expected schemas during incremental tool invocation. The compatibility shim will reject tool calls where arg_schema_hash != server-side registry hash unless validate_mode==off. This prevents silent mis-typed tool invocations observed during multi-stage streams.

Operational notes: Added telemetry tags response.validate_mode and stream.checkpoint_hit_count to Console so SRE can track enforcement rates and checkpoint efficacy. Default behavior remains warn for customers with response_format.schema specified; enforce must be enabled explicitly by the API client or via server-side policy on Dedicated/Private.

Checklist: 
- [x] API: add response_format.validate_mode to spec, update OpenAPI + TypeScript client generation. 
- [x] Runtime: implement checkpoint markers + rewind logic in serving worker. 
- [x] Compatibility: include arg_schema_hash in function_call shim and fallback mapping. 
- [x] Tests: unit + end-to-end streaming repro harness and integration against openai-compat mock. 
- [x] Docs: examples and migration guide added to redwood-docs (see related PR).

Backward compatibility and migration: validate_mode defaults to "warn" when response_format.schema is present to surface regressions without breaking running systems. Private/Dedicated customers can opt their clusters into enforce-by-default through a new cluster policy flag.

Risk & mitigations: enforce mode can cause early stream termination in presence of model hallucinations; mitigation: default to warn and expose retry budget + coercion toggles. We added a runtime metric for enforce-induced-terminations and a feature flag to turn off checkpoint insertion for latency-sensitive paths.

Related: This PR references a docs companion PR in redwood-docs and a small SDK change in redwood-sdk-python for the validate_mode parameter.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after two rounds of review and a flake rerun in streaming e2e tests.

Default _warn_ behaviour minimizes risk; enforce is opt-in. If you see a spike in enforce-induced-terminations after rollout, consider toggling cluster policy or increasing retry budget. Checkpoints are in-memory per-worker (30s) and do not affect disk persistence.

Context and motivation: Our presubmit lanes have grown costly and noisy: lint shards re-run the full toolchain bootstrap and re-download SDK artifacts even for trivial changes, and several teams have hit nondeterministic failures caused by partial bootstrap state. This PR introduces two coordinated improvements: (1) an incremental lint cache that keys on staged file fingerprint + lockfile fingerprint to skip unaffected lint shards, and (2) an idempotent toolchain bootstrap process (tiny microimage + deterministic install paths) so retries and parallel presubmit runners converge to identical state. Goals: faster feedback for small edits, fewer flaky premerge failures, less egress from CI, and clearer cache invalidation semantics.

What changed (high level):
- New lightweight cache layer: tools/presubmit/lint-cache/ with a content-addressed metadata index and eviction policy tuned for presubmit lifetimes.
- Deterministic bootstrap: scripts/bootstrap.go reworked to install toolchain under /opt/redwood-toolchain/<lockfile-hash>, uses package digests rather than timestamps.
- CI integration: .github/workflows/presubmit.yml updated with cache warm/restore steps and a new 'lint-fast' job that consults the lint-cache before running full linters.
- Tooling: docker/mini-toolchain.Dockerfile adds a microimage used for presubmit; Makefile targets for bootstrapping added.
- Docs: docs/dev/presubmit.md documents cache keys, invalidation, and how to run locally.

Single-line checklist:
- [x] Implement cache and bootstrap changes
- [x] Update presubmit workflow and tests
- [x] Add doc for local reproduction
- [x] Smoke-run presubmit in staging

Commit summary (high level):
- feat(presubmit): add incremental lint cache and index
- refactor(bootstrap): make toolchain bootstrap idempotent by hashing lockfile
- ci(presubmit): consult lint cache and add microimage restore steps
- test: add unit tests for cache key derivation and bootstrap path resolution
- docs: presubmit.md and quickstart for local dev

Changed areas and illustrative snippets (not a full diff):
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yml (added lint-fast job and cache steps)
- tools/presubmit/lint-cache/cache.go (content-addressed index API + eviction)
- scripts/bootstrap.go (now computes lockfile hash, installs to stable path)
- docker/mini-toolchain.Dockerfile (base image + pinned pkg hashes)
- Makefile (bootstrap-target, presubmit-local)
- docs/dev/presubmit.md (usage and troubleshooting)

Review conversation (summary):
- Marcus Patel (reviewer): "What's the invalidation story when the lockfile changes vs when only unrelated files are edited? Are we at risk of serving stale lint results?" Author reply: "Cache key is a two-tuple: staged-files-fingerprint + lockfile-hash. When the lockfile changes, the key changes and cached results are not used. We also added a TTL (48h) so long-lived branches don't grow cache cruft. See tools/presubmit/lint-cache/README in this PR for details." Marcus: "Please add an explicit unit test for lockfile-change invalidation." Author: "Added unit test commit 'test(presubmit): lockfile invalidation unit test'."

For self-hosted runners admins can opt out by setting REDWOOD_TOOLCHAIN_DIR; docs updated." Arielle: "Add a short troubleshooting section; otherwise LGTM." Author: "Added troubleshooting and a note about REDWOOD_TOOLCHAIN_DIR."

- Diego Alvarez: "Would like lightweight telemetry when fallback to full lint occurs (cache miss)." Author: "Added a small counter metric emitted to the existing presubmit telemetry bucket; instrumented in cache.go and presubmit workflow to surface in Console."

Links:

- Staging run (CI): https://ci.internal.redwood/reports/937401/staging

If anything breaks, revert guidance: revert the squash commit or set PRESUBMIT_LINT_CACHE=0 in CI to short-circuit the cache and fall back to baseline behavior.
Improves presubmit latency and reliability by adding an incremental lint cache and making the toolchain bootstrap idempotent; reduces CI wall-clock time for small changes.

payload.body:
Problem: On-call rehearsals and post-incident replay exercises are invaluable, but existing playback tooling either requires full prod access or produces raw traces that can leak credentials and overwhelm downstream services. Teams avoid realistic rehearsals because of safety and privacy risk.

This PR implements a three-part system to enable safe, realistic rehearsals: (1) a lightweight telemetry-mirror service that creates timebound, privacy-preserving mirrors of incident traces; (2) a sandboxed replay harness that can run mirrors against mock endpoints or a guarded staging proxy; and (3) a Rehearsal Guardian control plane that enforces throttles, quota accounting, and fidelity checks before a replay is allowed.

Design notes: mirrors are generated as compressed event streams with field-level scrubbers (configurable allowlists/denylists), sampling controls, and optional synthetic augmentation to reconstruct missing context. Mirrors are immutable and tracked with an internal provenance token to support chain-of-custody and auditability. The replay harness supports two execution modes: dry-run (validation-only, no outbound requests) and guarded-run (requests routed through an enforced staging proxy that rate-limits and strips sensitive headers). Guardian policies are tied to Linear tickets and can be scoped per-team.

Checklist implemented: 
- [x] Telemetry mirror producer (kafka -> mirror serializer with scrub rules)
- [x] Mirror storage index and provenance metadata
- [x] Sandboxed replay harness (dry-run and guarded-run modes)
- [x] Guardian policy engine with timeboxing and rate-limit enforcement
- [x] CLI and incident-bot command to create/preview/replay mirrors: `ib replay create|preview|run`
- [x] Unit and integration tests for scrubbers and replay safety gates
- [x] Documentation stub and an internal runbook describing safe rehearsal playbooks (link: https://linear.app/internal/ENG-4921/rehearsal-runbook)

Migration notes: existing `ib capture` snapshots can be converted to mirrors via `ib mirror convert`. Mirrors are backward compatible with earlier snapshot formats but add provenance headers; no customer-facing API changes.

Commits summary:
- 7b1d3b4: initial mirror producer and serializer, scrubber config glue
- d2c9a01: mirror storage index, provenance token implementation, migration tool
- 8f4a2c6: replay harness skeleton (dry-run/guarded-run) and cli commands
- f3e5b12: guardian policy engine and enforcement hooks in staging proxy
- 9c0a7b8: tests, docs, and CI integration

Changed files (high level):
- services/telemetry-mirror/producer.py (core mirror generation and scrub rules)
- services/telemetry-mirror/schema.py (mirror event schema + provenance headers)
- services/telemetry-mirror/storage_index.md (design doc for mirror indexing)
- tools/ib/replay.py (CLI commands: create/preview/run)
- harness/replay/runner.py (sandboxed replay harness)
- harness/replay/guarded_proxy.py (rate-limiting + header strip middleware)
- guardian/policy_engine.py (timeboxing and quota checks)
- tests/test_mirror_scrubbers.py (unit tests)
- tests/test_replay_guardian.py (integration tests)
- docs/internal/rehearsal-runbook.md (runbook draft)
- ci/incident-bot-pipeline.yml (added mirror unit/integration jobs)

Review conversation (chronological):
- Samir Gupta (requested changes): "Nice separation of concerns. Two asks: make scrubber configs pluggable at team-level and add a nonblocking safety warning when a mirror contains external hostnames. Also please add more unit tests around provenance token replay-mismatch cases."
- Maya Reyes (author reply): "Thanks Samir — pluggable scrubber registry added in producer.py (registry keyed by team id). Added a warning detector for external hostnames and added tests for provenance mismatch. See commits d2c9a01 & 9c0a7b8."
- Rhea Nair (comment): "Guardian looks good. Can you clarify policy escalation flow if a replay attempts >2x allowed RPS? Should the guardian auto-abort or scale down?"
- Maya Reyes (author reply): "Guardian will auto-throttle to safe RPS and then escalate to team on-call if repeated attempts occur within a 10m window. I've added this behavior to policy_engine.py and documented it in the runbook."
- Oliver Beck (approval): "Code looks solid, tests cover key paths. Left a minor nits comment about log formatting. Approving after the CI re-run."

CI timeline:
- Initial CI run: unit tests failed (missing provenance edge-case) -> addressed in f3e5b12
- Second CI run: integration flake on replay harness (timeout) -> increased harness timeout and mocked external host in tests -> subsequent runs passed
- Final CI status: pass (all checks green)

Merge outcome: squashed and merged to main on 2025-11-12 by Maya Reyes (merge method: squash). Post-merge actions: deployed mirror producer into staging for 72h canary and manual runbook rehearsals with platform SRE.

Notes for operators: 
- Mirrors are accessible via `ib mirror list` and require `replay:mirror` permission in RBAC to create or replay.
- Guardian policy files live under `guardian/policies/*.yaml`; editing them requires a Linear ticket.
- If you encounter a blocked replay, check `guardian/events` for the audit trail and provenance token mismatch reasons.

If reviewers want a separate follow-up: I plan to iterate on synthetic augmentation (filling gaps with inferred context) and tighter integration with the replay canary to automatically run one low-impact rehearsal per week for high-change services (follow-up: ENG-5037).
Adds a telemetry mirroring pipeline, sandboxed replay harness, and a rehearsal guardian enforcing timeboxed, rate-limited replays. No API breaking changes.
- Users can opt-in to create sanitized mirrors of incident telemetry for safe local or CI rehearsals.
- Rehearsal guardian prevents noisy replays from hitting prod backends and enforces credential redaction.
Samir Gupta: Requested changes — make scrubber configs pluggable; add external-hostname warning; add provenance mismatch tests.
Maya Reyes: Addressed — added scrubber registry, warning detector, and provenance tests (commits d2c9a01, 9c0a7b8).
Rhea Nair: Question — guardian behavior on >2x RPS attempts?
Maya Reyes: Answer — auto-throttle then escalate to on-call after repeat attempts; updated policy_engine.py and runbook.
Oliver Beck: Approval — minor log-format nit; approving after CI green.
