payload.body:
Motivation:
Users observed non-deterministic tool selection across retries and streaming fragments when the OpenAI compatibility layer synthesized tool_choice decisions. This caused duplicate tool invocations and confusing assistant/tool provenance in logs. The goal of this PR is to provide a deterministic, monotonic priority resolver for tool discovery, attach lightweight provenance to tool selection decisions, and preserve stream fragment boundaries and message metadata so clients can rehydrate continuous tool calls without ambiguity.

What this change does (single-line narrative): Adds a compatibility shim that maps OpenAI-style function/tool schemas into an internal priority-annotated catalog, enforces deterministic selection policy across retries/fallbacks, and ensures streaming fragments carry explicit fragment markers and provenance tags for tool messages.

Details/Approach:
- Tool priority mapping: introduce a stable priority vector derived from (explicit tool priority annotation if present, tool confidence heuristics, and deterministic tie-breaker based on tool_id canonical order). This ensures identical input + catalog state yields the same tool_choice.
- Provenance envelope: selected tool invocations now include a small provenance header (tool_selector_version, selection_score, selection_reason) that travels in both the stream meta and the non-streaming invoke envelope. This lets downstream consumers attribute outputs to a specific selection decision and facilitates replay.
- Streaming fragment preservation: framed streaming chunks now include fragment_id and fragment_index headers for tool messages. We preserve fragment boundary markers when coalescing or splitting fragments during network retransmit/rebuffer.
- Schema mapping changes: extend openai compat mapper to preserve optional param_aliases and required/optional field qualifiers in the translated internal schema to reduce accidental silent failures on strict tool runtimes.
- Retry/fallback semantics: when a fallback model or stub is used we attach selection_reason annotated as "fallback-route" and keep the original selection_score to make post-hoc analysis straightforward.

Files changed (high-level):
- src/compat/openai/tool_priority_resolver.rs: new deterministic priority logic and tie-breaker utilities.
- src/compat/openai/tool_provenance.rs: provenance envelope generator and serializer.
- src/serving/stream/framing.rs: add fragment_id, fragment_index headers and coalescing logic.
- api/openai_compat/README.md: spec notes on new provenance headers and fragment markers.
- tests/integration/tool_choice_replay.test.ts: deterministic replay + fragment reassembly tests.
- tests/unit/tool_priority.test.rs: coverage for tie-breakers and score stability.
- docs/release/notes/2026-02-26-tool-provenance.md: release notes.

Commits (summary):
- feat(compat): add deterministic tool priority resolver and utilities
- feat(compat): add provenance envelope and serializer
- fix(stream): preserve fragment headers during coalesce/split
- test: add integration tests for replay and fragment reassembly
- docs: update openai_compat README and release notes

Testing and validation:
- Unit test suite covers canonical tie-breaker ordering and selection stability across simulated catalog reorders.
- Integration tests replay the same request over a randomized catalog ordering and assert identical tool_choice and identical provenance headers.
- End-to-end streaming test validates fragment reassembly and idempotent-invoke behavior when client reconnects mid-stream.
- Ran internal performance benchmark: added ~0.6ms median overhead on selection path (within SLO), no measurable impact on token throughput for steady-state batched loads.

Backwards compatibility and migration notes:
- Compatibility: all old invocations still function; we only add extra metadata fields (provenance headers and fragment markers). Clients that ignore these will see no behavioral change.
- Migration: operators that relied on implicit nondeterminism should be aware that tool selection is now deterministic by default; an opt-out env var (OPENAI_COMPAT_ALLOW_UNORDERED) is provided for a short transitional window.

Checklist:
- [x] New unit tests
- [x] Integration tests (replay + streaming)
- [x] Docs and release notes
- [x] Perf smoke test

Related tickets: Linear ENG-2104 (deterministic tool routing), ENG-2147 (stream fragment metadata), SUP-7821 (support case: duplicate tool calls during reconnect)

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the tie-breaker logic in tool_priority_resolver.rs (stable sort is critical) and the fragment coalescer change — I added comments where we preserve original fragment boundaries.

Ravi Patel: Nice isolation between resolver and mapper. Please add a short comment explaining why we pick tool_id canonical order as the final tie-breaker.
Elena Soto: Can we add a debug flag to emit full selection_score breakdown in debug logs? It will help support investigations.
Marcus Li: Streaming reassembly looks good; one nit on off-by-one in fragment_index when coalescing two fragments.
Ava Moreno (author): Addressed Marcus' off-by-one nit and added a unit test; added a small comment about canonical order and flag to enable verbose selection logs behind a feature gate.
Added deterministic tool priority resolver and provenance headers for OpenAI compatibility layer. Streaming fragments for tool messages now include fragment_id/fragment_index. No behavioral breaking changes; opt-out available via OPENAI_COMPAT_ALLOW_UNORDERED.
Operators should roll forward without downtime. If you have custom tooling parsing tool_choice text blobs, update parsers to read the new provenance headers. Enable fallback logging for a day to verify selection stability in production.
This PR intentionally keeps selection math deterministic to make post-hoc analysis and auditing simpler; will follow up with a separate PR to expose selection telemetry to Redwood Console as per ENG-2210.

Motivation: onboarding engineers to RAG workflows often requires heavy scaffolding and manual test setup. This PR adds a compact "RAG Katas Lab" quickstart that bundles small, deterministic scenarios (katas), a lightweight CLI orchestrator (rk) for running and replaying sessions, and a typed-stub generator for tool contracts so teams can author tool mocks with TypeScript/Go/py typings. The goal is low-friction, repeatable developer exercises and CI-friendly scenario playback for early-stage integrations. What this PR contains: - three compact katas (intent-disambiguation, index-hiatus, streaming-tool-fallback) with preseeded corpora and minimal index configs - rk CLI: run, replay, record, and snapshot commands + a --seed flag for deterministic tokenization - typed-stubgen: scans a tool-contract.json and emits typed stubs (ts/go/py) and a tiny adapter shim for local testing - structured-output linter hooks: an eslint-like runner that validates schema/contract conformance against snapshoted outputs - docs: quickstart readme, workshop guide, and docs-site nav entry - small telemetry probes: optional probes that emit structured trace points for step boundaries (disabled by default) Usage (examples): 1) bootstrap: git clone ... && cd redwood-quickstarts/examples/rag-katas && make deps 2) run kata: rk run --kata intent-disambiguation --index local/sample.index --model redwood/ada-compat 3) record a session: rk record --kata streaming-tool-fallback --out ./snapshots/streaming-1.json 4) generate typed stubs: stubgen --contract examples/contracts/calc-tool-contract.json --lang ts --out examples/stubs/ The PR includes a compact checklist: - [x] kata scenarios and corpora - [x] rk CLI (run/replay/record) + README - [x] typed-stubgen + examples - [x] structured-output-lint integration for CI - [x] docs site entry and workshop guide - [x] basic unit tests and smoke CI compatibility Backwards compatibility and scope: everything is additive, feature-flagged by default (rk is in examples/ and not wired into production CI), and the typed stubs are opt-in. Related: ENG-1298 (developer onboarding), PM-402 (quickstart content plan).
Marco Alvarez: Nice compact katas. Two requests: make rk --seed reproducible across platforms (deterministic sort) and add a small e2e that runs in CI with a tiny mock model.
Author (Lena Zhao): Addressed. rk now hashes file list and applies deterministic sort; added a CI smoke job that uses the adapter-stub and a tiny sample index (ci/smokes/rag-katas-smoke.yml).

Evan Kim: Telemetry probes are fine as opt-in. Request: document how to disable probes in the README.
Author (Lena Zhao): README now documents REDWOOD_KATAS_TELEMETRY=0 to disable probes.
Marco Alvarez: Approved after smoke CI passed.
Priya Desai: Approved.
Evan Kim: Approved.

This adds a new end-to-end “Production Readiness” quickstart intended to mirror the Console onboarding / first production launch checklist. The quickstart walks a new Hosted API user from: API key setup → first request → streaming → retries/timeouts → usage visibility → quotas/budgets guardrails → basic observability hooks → model pinning + fallback (conceptual; uses config placeholders). Motivation: we keep seeing early prod launches fail on 401/403 setup mistakes, streaming disconnect confusion, and 429 surprises; the checklist in Console helps, but we need a canonical runnable path customers can copy/paste and deploy. Scope: adds a new quickstart directory with Python + TypeScript examples (Go is stubbed with TODO and links to the SDK guide), adds a minimal “healthcheck” endpoint pattern, structured logs, and a tiny dashboard note for usage-lag expectations. Includes guidance for where to configure quotas/budgets in Console and links out to Terraform sample budget alerts. Non-goals: full guided tour, Dedicated/Private specifics, deep integration with the checklist progress service (this is docs/examples only).
1) Local Python: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...; cd production-readiness/python; python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt; python app/main.py --non-streaming; python app/main.py --streaming. 2) Local TypeScript: cd production-readiness/typescript; npm ci; npm run start -- --non-streaming; npm run start -- --streaming. 3) Trigger 429 behavior: set low per-minute limit in Console (or use provided instructions to request temporary low quota), run load script in README, confirm exponential backoff and log output. 4) Observability: confirm logs include request_id + latency_ms; optionally set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT and run sample docker-compose from observability.md. 5) CI smoke: workflow runs dependency install + one non-streaming request behind a secret-less stub (mocked transport) to ensure compilation + basic execution paths don’t regress.
Monica Patel (review): Can we ensure we’re using the new recommended retry presets language from ENG-5820? Also please be explicit that streaming retries are tricky (non-idempotent).
Wei Chen (author): Updated both READMEs to reference the SDK preset names and added a dedicated “Streaming disconnects” section + guidance: do not automatically retry mid-stream unless the app is designed for it; do retry connect failures before first token; link to SDK guide.
Ibrahim Khan (review): In TS, you’re catching generic errors and retrying everything. Please gate retries to network/timeouts + 429/5xx only; do not retry 4xx other than 429.
Wei Chen (author): Updated retry.ts with status-code allowlist (429, 500, 502, 503, 504) and network errors; added note about 401/403 being config issues + link to troubleshooting.
Elliot Price (review): Please keep terminology consistent with Console: “Budgets & quotas” and “Usage dashboard (may lag ~X minutes)”. Also add a direct link placeholder that docs can redirect later.
Wei Chen (author): Copy updated to match the checklist naming; added canonical link placeholders under /docs/onboarding/production-launch and /docs/usage/usage-dashboard-latency (to be redirected by docs IA work).
Logan Wright (review): Observability section: can we make the minimal path “structured logs” first, and OTEL as optional? Also add a warning about high-cardinality labels if folks export metrics.
Wei Chen (author): Re-ordered observability.md to logs-first, OTEL optional; added note about avoiding user ids / prompts in metrics dimensions and keeping cardinality low.
Dev Patel (review): Support angle: please call out the top 3 failure modes up front (401/403, streaming disconnect, 429) and show what good logs look like for triage.
Wei Chen (author): Added “Common first-launch issues” section with example log lines and what to check in Console; also added link to support article placeholders.

payload.body:
Motivation: Large bursty workloads (e.g., chat fanout, high-concurrency embeddings) are causing auth fetch thundering and transient elevated latency/401s during cold Credential rotations. This PR adds a small, opt-in credential prefetcher using a leaky-bucket token schedule and a consumer-facing CredentialWarmup helper. It also exposes lightweight streaming backpressure hints so the SDK can signal downstream transports to slow or batch when the local leaky-bucket is drained.

Summary of changes: - core/credentials: add LeakyBucketPrefetcher (configurable rate, burst, jitter) and CredentialWarmup API. - streaming: add BackpressureHint enum and propagate hints through StreamContext so transports (http2/ws) can apply pacing. - auth: adaptive retry hooks that account for prefetched tokens. - ergonomics: convenient client.start_warmup(...) helper and retry presets (low/medium/high concurrency). - docs: usage section + migration notes. - tests: unit + integration harness exercising a simulated token endpoint and a high-concurrency streaming workload. - bump package version to 0.20.0 and add release notes.

Why leaky-bucket? A leaky-bucket prefetcher limits token fetch rate when many concurrent request paths trigger refresh simultaneously. It smooths bursts without changing token TTL semantics and is intentionally conservative (opt-in).

Developer checklist: - [x] Implement Prefetcher core and public helper. - [x] Wire backpressure hints into StreamContext. - [x] Add retry logic to prefer prefetched tokens when available. - [x] Unit tests for Prefetcher (edge cases: jitter, empty-bucket behavior). - [x] Integration tests with simulated auth server under concurrency. - [x] Docs and changelog. - [x] Version bump to 0.20.0.

Commits (high level): - 1a2b3c4: add leaky-bucket prefetcher + tests - 2b3c4d5: stream backpressure hints and plumbing into transports - 3c4d5e6: ergonomics: CredentialWarmup helper, client API surface, docs and changelog - 4d5e6f7: fix race in token handoff; adjust retry floor - 5e6f7g8: bump version, finalize release notes

Top-level changed files (illustrative): - core/credentials/prefetch.py - core/credentials/__init__.py - core/streaming/context.py - transports/http2/transport.py (apply_hint pacing) - transports/websocket/transport.py - sdk/client.py (start_warmup helper) - docs/guides/credential-prefetch.md - tests/integration/test_prefetch_concurrency.py - setup.cfg / pyproject.toml (version bump)

Testing and CI: CI run passed on first run (unit + integration on linux/py3.10, py3.11). Stress harness locally validated a 10k-rps simulated workload with backpressure hints enabled: 92% reduction in peak concurrent token fetches and elimination of 401 spikes in the harness. Bench script used is attached in tests/integration/bench_prefetch.py (small, non-blocking).

Compatibility and rollout: This is opt-in. Existing clients do not change behavior unless they call client.start_warmup(...) or configure prefetched=true in CredentialProvider. No changes to wire protocol or server-side contracts.

Documentation: docs/guides/credential-prefetch.md contains rationale, examples, and a recommended presets table. Recommend customers with bursty patterns enable warmup on client initialization: client.start_warmup(preset="high_concurrency").

Security/observability: Added metrics: sdk.auth.prefetch.attempts, sdk.auth.prefetch.successes, sdk.auth.prefetch.throttled. Also instrumented stream.hint.backpressure events so Console dashboards can correlate hints with increased latencies upstream.

Merge: Squash-merged to main. See merged_at metadata.

Known limitations and follow-ups: - Prefetcher assumes token endpoint scales; if token endpoint enforces strict per-account rate limits, operator should tune rate/burst. - Next PR: add server-side hint acceptance (server may return pacing advice to clients); tracking ENG-3490.

Arjun Patel: Nice, this addresses a long-standing cause of auth thundering in our on-prem customers. A few nits: (1) can we make the default preset safer for low-traffic apps? (2) add an opt-out env var to disable warmup entirely?
Maya Chen: Thanks — addressed both. Default preset renamed to 'conservative' and I added REDWOOD_SDK_PREFETCH=false that disables global warmup when set. Tests updated to include env var override.
Sofia Rivera: Left comments on the transport pacing granularity; transports should not sleep more than 10ms in tight loops to avoid head-of-line issues. Also please add a doc example showing how to monitor the new metrics.
Maya Chen: Adjusted pacing in http2 transport to batch at 5-10ms windows; added doc snippet and Grafana query examples for sdk.auth.prefetch.* metrics.
Daniel Kim: Observability question: will backpressure hints inflate metric cardinality? They look low-cardinality (enum) so fine. Approving pending a small race fix in token handoff.
Maya Chen: Fixed the race (commit 4d5e6f7) and added a unit that repros the previous failure mode. Marking ready-to-merge.
Arjun Patel: Approved. CI green. Merging with squash.
Introduces CredentialWarmup and a leaky-bucket prefetcher to smooth auth bursts; adds streaming backpressure hint API; ergonomic convenience wrappers; bump py SDK to v0.20.0. No breaking changes, opt-in behavior. Refer to upgrade notes for migration guidance.

Motivation: openai-style function/tool calling integration has subtle mismatches with Redwood's router and streaming layer. This PR defines a compact, backwards-compatible framing for partial tool messages so streamed invocations can be reassembled reliably by clients, aligns the tool schema mapping to Redwood's structured-output descriptors, and tightens tool_choice semantics to be deterministic when model signals are ambiguous. Changes include: 1) a specification for a minimal framing envelope inserted into streamed tool outputs so fragments contain tool_id, sequence_idx and a finality flag; 2) a router rule update that prefers explicit tool_id signals, falls back to schema-compatibility score if tool_choice is null/ambiguous, and exposes debug_reason on routed responses; 3) a mapping layer that converts OpenAI-style JSON-schema tool definitions into Redwood structured-output descriptors (type, required, constraints, example) and validates request/response against the mapped schema at call time; 4) new end-to-end tests for streaming reassembly, schema-validation failure modes, and ambiguous-tool fallbacks; 5) SDK helpers in python/ts to parse framed streams and surface partial tool payloads with progress events. Checklist: - [x] Spec document for framed tool messages included - [x] Implementation in openai_compat router + streaming codec - [x] Schema mapper and validation with clear error codes - [x] Unit/integration tests (including flaky test flake guard) - [x] SDK helpers and docs snippets - [x] Performance test to validate <2% p99 latency regression on small bursts Related: ENG-5234 (design), SUP-883 (support case exposing ambiguity in tool_choice), PM-112 (product acceptance criteria). This is intended to be non-breaking for existing customers: the framing defaults to an opt-in compatibility mode until a short feature flag rollout finishes and we run an automated migration to annotate live streams from the hosted fleet. See commits for implementation details.
OpenAI compatibility: clarify tool selection semantics and introduce framed tool-message protocol for streaming tool outputs. Backwards-compatible routing; mitigations for ambiguous tool_choice values.
Improves reliability of tool invocation streaming and structured output mapping.
Daniel Rivera: Overall looks good; only concern is edge-case where two tools share identical schemas. Please add deterministic tie-breaker and an opt-out for legacy routing.
Marta Liu (author): Added deterministic tie-breaker (prefer warmer model/route) and feature-flag opt-out; updated tests to exercise tie scenarios.
Aisha Khan: Can we avoid adding more bytes to every stream fragment? Suggest compact binary header; otherwise good.
Marta Liu: switched header to concise ASCII envelope (14-40 bytes typical) to keep existing stream compatibility and ease SDK parsing.
Samir Patel: CI failed on first run due to flaky test test_framed_tool_stream; I saw you added a flake guard. Confirmed rerun passed and added a retry decorator for the e2e test.
+++ codec.py: serialize fragment: 'FRAME_START|tool_id={tid};seq={i};final={f}|payload=<base64>'
router.py: if tool_choice is falsy: compute best_match = schema_score(candidate_tools, call_payload); if tie -> prefer lower-latency candidate; add response['debug_reason']=reason
mapper.py: map 'type: object' -> 'structured_output:type=object;fields=[...]' and preserve examples/tests
spec(openai-compat): add framed-tool-message spec and decision notes
feat(router): implement ambiguous-tool fallback and debug_reason in route response
feat(streaming): codec for framed tool messages and reassembly logic
feat(schema-mapper): convert openai json-schema to redwood descriptors + validation
test: add e2e streaming tooling tests and sdk parsing tests
docs: add API examples and migration steps

Title: Introduce RAG pipeline DSL quickstart with websocket tool-bridge and replay harness

Motivation and context: We have a lot of ad-hoc RAG quickstarts that show tool calling or stepwise orchestration, but teams keep asking for a compact, opinionated example that demonstrates: 1) expressing multi-step RAG flows as a readable pipeline DSL, 2) wiring external connectors via a lightweight websocket tool-bridge (simulates third-party APIs for local dev), 3) deterministic session replay for debugging/evals, and 4) idiomatic worker stubs in TypeScript and Go for integration testing. This PR provides a single quickstart that strings those pieces together so platform teams can onboard quickly and product teams can reproduce noisy production flows locally.

What this PR adds (summary): - A new quickstart directory: quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl/ with README, examples, and step templates. - A small pipeline DSL (YAML-first) that maps steps (retrieve -> call -> transform -> assert -> emit) to runtime hooks. The DSL is intentionally tiny (6 primitives) and designed for teaching. - Websocket tool-bridge: lightweight node server that accepts tool calls over websockets to emulate external connectors (search, payment, webhook sink). Includes a small harness to seed deterministic responses. - Replay harness: session serializer + deterministic RNG seeding for replaying a sequence of interactions (useful for CI-evals and debugging flaky prompts). - Two worker stubs: TypeScript (Node) and Go (lightweight HTTP shim) that implement the DSL hooks and demonstrate KV cache hotspots, streaming partial responses, and structured-output enforcement. - Devcontainer + sample k8s manifest for running the quickstart locally or in headless CI. - Telemetry probes: example OpenTelemetry spans and an instrumentation README showing how to add custom metrics to trace step latencies and token counts.

Files touched (high level): - quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl/README.md - quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl/pipeline-schema.yaml - quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl/examples/retail-recommendation.yaml - quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl/ws-tool-bridge/ (node websocket server, seeds) - quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl/workers/ts-worker/ (npm project with sample handlers) - quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl/workers/go-worker/ (go module with http shim) - quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl/replay/replay-cli.ts - quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl/devcontainer.json - quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl/k8s/quickstart.yaml - quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl/telemetry/otel-example.md

Commit summary: - 1a2b3c4: initial scaffold and README - 2b3c4d5: add pipeline schema + example flows - 3c4d5e6: websocket tool-bridge implementation + seeds - 4d5e6f7: add TS worker and CI smoke script - 5e6f7g8: add Go worker, k8s manifest, and replay harness - 6f7g8h9: add telemetry probes and docs; fix lint failures - 7g8h9i0: follow-up: update README with troubleshooting and merge prep

Testing and CI: - Unit: TS worker unit tests (Jest) and replay harness tests were added; Go worker has small integration checks. - Smoke: a headless smoke job in CI boots the websocket bridge, runs the dev pipeline against seeded responses, and verifies structured-output assertions pass. - Lint: Prettier/ESLint and gofmt checks.

CI run history on this PR: - Initial run: lint failure (missing gofmt and a couple of ESLint rules) - After fixes: one flaky Jest snapshot for streaming partial responses; reran tests with snapshot update and added an assertion to avoid nondeterministic ordering - Final run: all checks pass (lint/test/smoke)

Review conversation (high level, single thread): - Diego Morales (reviewer): "Nice compact DSL. Two asks: 1) make the structured-output contract explicit in the schema so teams can opt into strict validation, 2) clarify security implications of websocket bridge (seeds may contain secrets)." - Avery Chen (author): "Thanks — added a 'validation' boolean in pipeline-schema.yaml and moved seeds to a sample-only file under ws-tool-bridge/seeds.example.json; updated README with security guidance." - Priya Kapoor (reviewer): "Can we show a minimal example of migrating an existing step to a canary rollout? Suggest adding a short 'rollout' property in the DSL and a cookbook paragraph." - Avery Chen: "Added rollout property and a cookbook paragraph demonstrating a canary flag (percent-based). Also added a console screenshot for step metrics." - Samir Rao (reviewer): "Telemetry looks fine; please add token count metric per-step. Also, ensure replay harness runs deterministically on CI (seed RNG)." - Avery Chen: "Added token_count gauge example and deterministic RNG seeding in replay-cli; updated smoke job to set REPLAY_SEED. Ready for merge." - Diego Morales: "Approved" - Priya Kapoor: "Approved" - Samir Rao: "Approved with comment noting to monitor telemetry quotas after adoption."

Edge cases and notes: - The websocket tool-bridge is intentionally not production-grade; README warns to not expose it externally and to treat it as a local/dev-only shim. - The pipeline DSL is intentionally conservative and designed for teaching and fast iteration; it is not intended to replace production orchestrators but to act as an ergonomic onboarding artifact. - The replay harness serializes prompts, tool call transcripts, and final outputs; it does not currently record raw model latencies (future work).

Docs and onboarding: - README includes step-by-step guide to run the quickstart locally (devcontainer recommended), how to seed tool responses, and how to run replay and smoke checks. - A short 'migrating from ad-hoc scripts' cookbook paragraph helps platform engineers convert existing one-off scripts to the DSL.

Compatibility and backward compatibility: - Nonbreaking: all files are additive; no changes to runtime or core APIs. - Example flows use public SDK calls to Redwood API; developers will need an API key to run the flow against hosted models (instructions in README explain using sandbox mode with the websocket bridge).

Merge outcome: - Squash-merged to main on 2025-01-17 by Diego Morales. Commit message: "quickstarts(rag): add pipeline DSL quickstart + websocket tool-bridge + replay harness" Commit SHA (squash): 9a8b7c6d9f0e1a2b3c4d5e6f7g8h9i0j

Follow-ups (suggested): - ENG-2410: Integrate pipeline DSL examples into docs site as an interactive notebook. - ENG-2421: Add a 'live playback' web UI for replayed sessions (could extend websocket bridge). - PM-159: Track adoption in on-call rotations and sample teams for feedback.

Checklist (from PR description): - [x] Quickstart scaffolded and README - [x] Pipeline schema + sample flows - [x] Websocket tool-bridge + seeds - [x] TypeScript and Go worker stubs - [x] Replay harness and deterministic seed support - [x] Devcontainer + k8s manifest - [x] Telemetry probes and example docs - [x] CI smoke job and lint fixes

If you want to run locally: git clone .../redwood-quickstarts && cd quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl && ./dev/run-local.sh (devcontainer recommended).
Add new RAG quickstart demonstrating a lightweight pipeline DSL, websocket tool-bridge for external connectors, replayable session harness, TypeScript and Go worker examples, and devcontainer for local authoring.

Add a replayable evaluation checkpoint mechanism and a CI hook that compares checkpoints to baselines and triggers an automated rollback policy when regression thresholds are exceeded. Includes docs and tests.
Motivation: We need a deterministic, auditable way to snapshot eval runs so that regression checks can be replayed exactly (same seeds, tokenization, env) and so that CI can trigger an automated rollback when a model or config change causes a measurable quality regression. This PR adds a lightweight eval checkpoint format, a replay runner, persistent snapshot storage integration, and a CI hook that gates merges based on checkpoint comparisons.

What this changes: - eval_harness/checkpoints: new checkpoint format (metadata + compressed outputs) and a small Python API for writing/reading checkpoints. - eval_harness/replay: deterministic replay runner that restores RNG/seed, tokenizer state and KV cache stubs to replay model outputs for exact diffing. - storage/snapshot_store: pluggable S3/GCS local filesystem backend with retention and manifest. - ci/hooks/rollback_gate.yaml: CI configuration that downloads baseline checkpoint for the PR scope and runs a comparison using a configurable metric set (accuracy/F1/ROUGE and coverage). If regression exceeds thresholds for any primary metric, the hook annotates the PR and creates a Linear rollback task (ENG-5921) and, when configured, triggers the delivery pipeline to mark the candidate build as failed. - tests: unit + integration tests that simulate checkpoint creation and replay with seeded pseudo-models. - docs/eval_checkpoints.md: usage, storage cost considerations, and guidance on choosing metrics and thresholds.

Design notes: - Checkpoint format is JSONL header + gzipped protobuf payload for outputs; header has run_id, commit_sha, model_variant, seed, dataset_cohort, environment tags and metric summaries. This balances readability and compact storage. - Replay runner enforces seeded determinism and canonical tokenizer versioning to avoid false positives. It supports a 'light' replay mode for CI (skip heavy model steps using cached outputs) and a 'full' mode for local developer debugging. - To keep CI runtime reasonable, the hook compares aggregated metrics at cohort-level and only runs full per-example diffs when a metric is near-threshold. - Storage retention defaults to 90 days; older snapshots are pruned by manifest sweeper.

How to review: - Focus on the checkpoint header fields (eval_harness/checkpoints/schema.py) — missing or mis-typed metadata will make replays fragile. - Review the replay determinism tests (tests/test_checkpoint_replay.py) for edge-cases (tokenizer updates, padding changes). - CI hook config (ci/hooks/rollback_gate.yaml) should be safe: it runs in a sandboxed job with read-only access to snapshots.

Backwards compatibility: The checkpoint reader is versioned; older checkpoints are migrated on read where possible. No breaking API surface change expected for external callers.

Related: ENG-5921 (rollback automation), ENG-6010 (eval infra cost cap).
Ethan Zhao: Great direction. Two quick asks: 1) Can we add explicit tokenizer-version pinning in the header? I worried about tokenization drift causing spurious diffs. 2) Please add cost estimate per checkpoint (S3 size) so infra can set retention defaults.
Priya Menon: Addressed — tokenizer_version added to header and included in migration logic. Added a table in docs/eval_checkpoints.md with empirical sizes from small/medium/large evals and retention recommendations.
Carlos Ruiz: Tests look good; one nit on naming: replay_runner.run -> replay_runner.execute_for_ci to make intent clearer. Also please ensure the CI job runs under a restricted service account with read-only snapshot access.
Priya Menon: Renamed the method and updated the CI job to use the snapshot-readonly SA. Added a comment describing expected IAM role. Updated test harness to assert SA usage in CI config.
Maya Patel: Security review: confirm that checkpoints do not contain PII. We should add a scrub step for known PII patterns before upload.
Priya Menon: Added a scrubber pipeline hook and a test case. The upload step refuses to publish if scrubber flags potential PII and will surface a human review action.
Ethan Zhao: CI initially flaked due to a parallel download race; switching the manifest fetch to use a stable list fixed it. Verified CI job now passes locally and in remote runner.
payload.title: Introduce replayable eval checkpoints and automatic rollback CI hook

Motivation: During a recent incident we observed rapid accept/reject oscillation on tenant routes when node-level egress became constrained and SLO budgets dropped. This PR introduces a SLO Pacing Controller that applies a short-term, smoothly decaying acceptance window per-tenant to avoid rapid reopen cycles, plus an Egress Bottleneck Mitigator that tracks cluster egress credit pressure and proactively throttles egress-heavy request classes (model downloads, large-embedding exports, cross-region replication) so serving paths stay within SLOs. The two mechanisms are designed to operate together: pacing reduces traffic spikes at the request ingress while the egress mitigator prevents downstream piping from amplifying pressure. Key changes: 1) runtime/pacing: add slo_pacer module with adaptive window sizing, exponential decay on allowance, and metrics hooks (slo.pacer.pressure, slo.pacer.window_ms). 2) routing/egress: egress_credit_manager that aggregates per-zone egress usage and exposes per-route admission signals; a soft-deny path for high-cost egress requests with a tokenized retry hint. 3) telemetry: new Prometheus gauges and logs with structured reason codes to aid post-incident analysis. 4) safety hotfix: reconcile circuit-breaker reopen debounce to avoid double-reopening when pacing and CB both release simultaneously. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is opt-in via config flags (runtime.slo_pacer.enabled, routing.egress_mitigator.enabled) and safe defaults preserve existing flow when disabled. Migration: no DB schema changes. Feature gate and rollout: added rollout flag to Console (console rollout metadata included in docs). Checklist: - [x] design doc reviewed (ENG-2048) - [x] unit tests for slo_pacer core logic - [x] integration tests against mocked egress manager - [x] load test scenario showing reduction in reopen oscillations - [x] telemetry dashboards prototypes - [x] docs + console flag UI patch - [x] incident runbook entry updated Testing notes: local unit/integration, k8s staging soak (24h) with synthetic spike pattern, and canary on two low-traffic regions. Observed 45% reduction in rapid reopens and 30% lower cross-region egress bursts in staging. Known limitations: pacing currently operates on request-count windows, future work will add token-bucket per-tenant sizing using historical latency profiles. Related work: follows up on ENG-2101 (connection stabilization) and complements existing circuit logic from ENG-1783. Merge: squash-merged after addressing reviewer feedback and a single CI rerun for flaky e2e coverage.
Diego Alvarez: Nice direction. Please add a unit test that covers the exponential decay path when allowance is zero to prevent silent re-open loops.
Maya Chen: Added test covering decay and edge-case where tenant allowance flips from 0 to >0 within the same epoch; also added comment linking to ENG-2048 design notes.
Noah Patel: Telemetry looks good. Can you include a histogram for time-in-pacer-window so we can profile hotspots?
Maya Chen: Added slo.pacer.window_ms histogram and dashboard JSON in docs. Adjusted labels to include tenant_id for aggregation.
Priya Singh: e2e flakiness observed on arm64 runner. Please rerun e2e and confirm no perf regression on A100/GPU nodes.
Maya Chen: Reran e2e after narrowing the mocked egress burst timings; CI flake was unrelated (timeout on infra); rerun succeeded and I pushed a small sleep/timing tolerance in test harness.
payload.title: Introduce SLO Pacing Controller and Egress Bottleneck Mitigator

Motivation: Production rollouts show a class of slow, sustained latency drifts that evade percentile-based canaries and cause oscillatory cutovers when traffic patterns reverberate across cohorts. This PR adds a tempo-aware 'stablepoint' canary that tracks moving baselines across multiple horizons and a Traffic Reverberation Shield that quarantines traffic slices which amplify transient regressions. Key goals: 1) detect gradual upward trends before they breach SLO windows; 2) avoid noisy cutovers caused by reverberating traffic (e.g., users re-trying, fan-out amplification); 3) integrate with Redwood Console rollout policies for staged quarantine and measured fallback.

Summary of changes: Implements a multi-horizon confidence estimator that fuses rolling-window quantiles, exponentially-weighted mean shifts, and a bootstrap-derived trend score. Adds a probabilistic fingerprint sampler that groups requests by stable signal keys (user-agent + route + size bucket + subtle temporal bucketing) to isolate reverberant cohorts. Introduces a quarantine controller that marks cohorts for staged isolation and traffic throttling when they drive oscillatory signal amplification. Wires telemetry to existing perf-canary pipeline and adds dashboarding and alerts.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-4021) - [x] Unit tests for estimator and sampler - [x] Integration tests with canary orchestrator (simulated traffic fixture) - [x] E2E canary run in perf-lab namespace - [x] Redwood Console UI hooks for quarantine policy - [x] Documentation (docs/perf/canary-stablepoint.md)

Why unique: Unlike percentile-fence canaries, Stablepoint uses tempo-aware baselines and cohort-level fingerprinting to avoid false positives from short-lived bursts. The reverberation shield enforces a quarantine cooldown and decay credit to prevent repeated oscillatory cutovers across rollouts.
Jordan: Please add a short note on computational cost of bootstrap windows; addressed by limiting bootstrap samples and adding fast-path early exit. Priya: Can we tag telemetry with cohort_id and rollout_id? Updated metrics.go to include cohort_id and rollout_id labels. Liam: Minor nits on comments and error wrapping; fixed. Priya requested that quarantine policy be opt-in by default; updated CRD defaults to disabled and documented opt-in flow. All reviewers approved after fixes.
Add tempo-aware stablepoint canary with cohort fingerprinting and Traffic Reverberation Shield. Opt-in quarantine policies allow staged isolation of noisy cohorts to prevent oscillatory rollouts. Metrics: canary.stablepoint.trend_score, canary.cohort.reverberation_rate, canary.quarantine.active_cohorts.
payload.title: introduce-stablepoint-temporal-canary-and-traffic-reverberation-shield

Summary: Replace a patchwork of Makefile targets and ad-hoc bash release presubmit scripts with a compact Go-based presubmit/wrangler binary and introduce a small 'safe-dep-unlocker' helper to coordinate dependency rollouts. This reduces CI flakiness caused by long shell init sequences, centralizes telemetry for presubmit actions, and provides a safe path for batched dependency upgrades.

Motivation: Over time we've accumulated multiple Make targets and bash shims used at presubmit and release time (make release:prepare, scripts/ci-boot, scripts/release_sign). They are fragile (set -e traps, subtle env assumptions) and slow to startup. They also duplicate logging and exit semantics, making CI flakes hard to triage. This PR: (1) consolidates those behaviors into presubmit-wrangler (single binary invoked by CI job), (2) decomposes monolithic Makefile bits into small go packages used by the binary, and (3) adds safe-dep-unlocker — a lightweight coordinator that gates broad dependency bumps so we can stagger merges through canaries.

What changed (high level):
- New binary: tools/presubmit-wrangler (go cmd) — handles: workspace bootstrap, selective vendoring, env validation, artifact signing handshake, and structured JSON telemetry emitted to CI.
- New helper: tools/safe-dep-unlocker — REST-lite coordinator (file-backed lease) used by the dep-bot to get a temporary unlock token for repo-wide dependency rollouts.
- Makefile: reduced to minimal task map that delegates to the Go binary for heavy lifting (Makefile -> make phony targets now wrappers only).
- CI: workflow updates in .github/workflows/* to call presubmit-wrangler instead of scripts/* or inlined shell. Added a short-lived 'ci-presubmit-logger' step that consumes presubmit-wrangler structured output.
- Release automation: moved signing handshake (gpg/ossls wrapper) into presubmit-wrangler and added a retry/backoff for transient KMS failures.
- Tests: unit tests for new packages under tools/* and integration smoke under .github/workflows/ci-smoke.yml (fast path).
- Docs: updated CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/ci/README-presubmit.md to document the new flow.

Checklist (all completed):
- [x] Implement presubmit-wrangler and safe-dep-unlocker
- [x] Replace CI references to old scripts/make targets
- [x] Ship unit tests and a fast smoke CI lane
- [x] Update docs and quickstarts that referenced old Make targets
- [x] Coordinate with dep-bot config (stagger windows)
- [x] Run canary on infra repo and two SDK repos for one week

Commits (summary):
- a7c4f8c  introducer: add tools/presubmit-wrangler cmd and basic telemetry sink
- b3d2e2a  decompose: move make targets to small go packages (env, vendor, sign)
- c9f7b11  ci: update workflows to call presubmit-wrangler and attach JSON output
- d4e6a00  tooling: add safe-dep-unlocker with file-lease backend and lock TTL
- e5aee22  tests: add unit tests for env and sign packages; add ci-smoke workflow
- f11a99d  docs: update CONTRIBUTING.md and add presubmit README

Files touched (selective, representative):
- tools/presubmit-wrangler/main.go
- tools/presubmit-wrangler/{env.go,vendor.go,sign.go,telemetry.go}
- tools/safe-dep-unlocker/main.go
- Makefile (reduced wrappers)
- .github/workflows/ci.yml (call presubmit-wrangler step)
- .github/workflows/ci-smoke.yml (new fast lane)
- scripts/* (deleted: scripts/ci-boot, scripts/release_sign)

Testing and verification:
- Local: ran make smoke via presubmit-wrangler (dev mode) across macOS and Linux containers.
- CI: Introduced a canary label (ci.canary/true) and ran on infra and redwood-sdk-python repos. Observed 22% faster average boot (median 11s reduction) and 45% fewer flaky timeouts in the bootstrap phase.
- Dep unlocker: ran a simulated unlock across 3 repos and verified the TTL/lease semantics prevented two concurrent unlocks for the same org namespace.

Review discussion (important threads condensed):
- Liam Chen: "This looks sensible, biggest concern is user-facing error messages from the Go binary — can we preserve the same exit codes the CI expects?"
  - Response (Asha): "Yes — presubmit-wrangler maps common failures to existing exit codes. Added tests that assert exit code mapping for vendor/lock/sign failures (see tests/exitcode_test.go)."
- Noah Patel: "We should avoid introducing a network dependency for safe-dep-unlocker in CI. Is the file-lease backend robust across our ephemeral runners?"
  - Response (Asha): "safe-dep-unlocker defaults to file-lease for ephemeral runners and supports an optional gcs/kv backend via env vars. Added TTL and a fallback to heartbeat mode; documented in docs/ci/safe-dep-unlocker.md."
- Maya Rodriguez: "Telemetry looks great, but please ensure secrets are never logged. Confirm KMS errors don't dump keys."
  - Response (Asha): "Telemetry excludes any envs named *KEY* or *SECRET* by default. sign.go scrubs error blobs before emitting. CI tests exercise the KMS transient failure path without exposing secrets."
- Noah (follow-up): "Can the dep-bot be updated to use the unlocker?"
  - Response (Asha): "Yes — dep-bot config change is queued in a separate PR on the dep-bot repo; safe windows and unlock policy are included in linked Linear task ENG-1129."

CI checks: All required checks passed after one rerun of flaky integration test:
- unit-tests: pass
- go vet/staticcheck: pass
- integration-smoke (fast lane): pass
- release-signing-sim: pass
- e2e-long (optional nightly): pending (not required for merge)

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature flag (CI step name 'presubmit.mode' defaulting to 'legacy' unless repo opt-in).
2) Opt-in infra and SDK repos to canary lane for 7 days. Monitor presubmit error telemetry and boot-time.
3) Flip default after no regressions for two weeks; then deprecate old scripts/ and remove Make wrappers in a follow-up cleanup PR.

Merge details: Squash-merged to main after reviews and green CI. Author performed the merge to ensure signed commits trace to infra automation account for release signing changes.

Notes and follow-ups (separate PRs planned):
- dep-bot config PR to actually call safe-dep-unlocker with unlock windows (ENG-1129).
- Remove legacy scripts/ entirely after three-week grace period.
- Add optional central gcs/kv backend for safe-dep-unlocker for org-wide coordinated rollouts (design doc in INF-430).

If you want a focused walk-through I can demo the presubmit-wrangler flow and the unlocker in the rewired CI job — ping me and I will schedule a 30m session.

References: ENG-1129, INF-430, SUP-8812.

Replaces legacy Makefile/ bash presubmit and release shims with a single small Go binary (presubmit-wrangler). Adds safe-dep-unlocker tool to coordinate staggered dependency upgrades and avoid mass CI churn. Non-breaking; rollout via staged canary on the CI fast-path.
Mostly technical sign-off after minor adjustments: ensure exit code compatibility; avoid adding cloud deps for unlocker by default; redact secrets in telemetry. Dep-bot update is tracked separately.
Non-breaking. No action required from release manager beyond watching presubmit telemetry during canary. Signing flow has retry/backoff but preserves existing artifact format.

Adds a new 'circuit-respite' feature that phases tenants back into serving after circuit trips using a staggered rejoin schedule and tenant drain windows. Improves stability during region-wide recoveries and reduces mass-reopen spikes.
Motivation: During a recent region-wide transient (SUP-4021) we observed large clusters of circuits flipping open->closed simultaneously which caused a follow-on traffic spike and repeated KV thrash. This change introduces 'circuit-respite' — a controlled rejoin protocol that spaces tenant re-entry and optionally drains existing sessions to smooth load.

What this PR does: Implements a staggered rejoin scheduler plus tenant drain windows and a short probationary warmup for tenants coming out of circuit trips. The key pieces: 1) runtime/circuit_manager.go: adds a RespiteState machine that tracks 'respite_start', 'scheduled_rejoin', 'probation', and 'active' states and exposes admission gates for the serving runtime; 2) controller/rejoin_scheduler.go: global controller that creates weighted rejoin cohorts based on tenant weight and recent-error fingerprint and schedules rejoin windows with jitter; 3) controller/tenant_drain.go: utilities to mark live connections as 'drainable' with a TTL and soft-evict policy to reduce sudden pressure when cohorts rejoin; 4) telemetry updates (slo_anchors) to emit RejoinCohort, DrainWindow, and ProbationLatencySample metrics; 5) Helm values and a new runtime flag (respite.enabled, respite.cohort_size, respite.cooldown_ms) to control behavior per deployment.

Design notes: The scheduler uses probabilistic cohort selection to avoid correlated reopens and includes a randomized jitter to prevent alignment across regions. Cohort size is configurable and defaults to 5% of active tenants when running in hosted mode. Probation duration is adaptive: a fast path for low-latency tenants and a conservative path for heavy KV tenants. All defaults are conservative to avoid any production regressions.

Testing: Unit tests cover state transitions and admission gate semantics (runtime/circuit_manager_test.go). Added an e2e canary script (scripts/e2e/rejoin_canary.sh) that simulates a coordinated circuit trip and measures downstream SLOs under staggered v. immediate rejoin. Ran the canary against perf-canary infra and observed a 42% reduction in 95th percentile latency spike during warmup compared to immediate reopen. CI: ci/checks/rejoin-smoke.yml validates config parsing, scheduler dry-run, and telemetry emission.

Rollout plan: Feature off by default. Deploy helm values with respite.enabled=false, then enable in dedicated staging with respite.cohort_size=0.03 and respite.cooldown_ms=30000 for a 2-week soak. Next, enable canary route for 1% of traffic using weighted-rejoin canary in controller. If telemetry shows RejoinCohortDropRate < 0.5% and ProbationLatencySample stable, gradually increase to 100%. We also added a kill-switch (respite.enabled=false) and an operator endpoint /admin/respite/abort to immediately flush all scheduled rejoins.

Operational considerations: Documented runbook in docs/operational/circuit-respite.md including steps to abort, temporarily raise cohort jitter, and read key telemetry anchors. Telemetry anchors are wired into the SLO alerting playbook so that long probation latency triggers an SRE paging rule.

Review conversation summary: Ethan: asked for clarity on cohort selection and failure amplification risk; replied with additional tests and a simulation harness (included). Marta: requested stronger invariants around admission gates to prevent overlap with existing throttlers — added gate priority ordering and unit tests. Jun: suggested adding an operator abort endpoint and a Helm flag to control canary route size — both were added.

CI and merge: The PR initially hit a flaky telemetry test (telemetry/slo_anchors test) which caused one CI rerun; after fixing the mock timing the CI passed. Reviewed and approved by all reviewers on 2026-01-20. Merged by squash on 2026-01-21.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps default behavior conservative; we expect follow-ups to iterate on cohort heuristics and to expose richer routing controls for enterprise Dedicated flows.
Introduce circuit-respite: staggered tenant rejoin and drain windows to reduce reopen-induced surge. Off by default; opt-in via helm/runtime flags.
Feature introduces an operator endpoint /admin/respite/abort; endpoint requires existing operator RBAC role and a feature flag. No new data plane credentials or tenant secrets are exposed.
payload.title: introduce circuit-respite: staggered rejoin + tenant drain windows

payload.body:
Introduce dynamic escalation profiles and variable-driven runbook templates. Provides safe defaults and canary rollout. No breaking changes.
Context: On-call teams need flexible escalation policies that adapt to responder load and alert storm conditions. This PR introduces two features in the slo-toolkit: 1) dynamic escalation profiles — evaluable policies that adjust escalation timing and routing based on runtime signals (alert rate, average ack latency, oncall headcount); and 2) templated runbooks — parameterized YAML templates that incident-bot and on-call tooling can instantiate with live context.

Motivation: customers have asked for automatic hold-windows and progressive escalation that reduce noise during large-scale maintenance or cascading failures (ENG-2143). This change aims to reduce false escalations, speed up human response for high-severity incidents, and make runbooks reusable across teams.

What changed (high level):
- Add a new evaluation engine (slo-toolkit/policies/profile_engine.go) that evaluates profile rules against telemetry and responder load.
- Add runbook template files under templates/runbooks/*.yaml and a templating utility (slo-toolkit/templates/renderer.go) that supports variable interpolation, conditional steps, and preflight checks.
- Integrate with incident-bot by adding a lightweight HTTP hook (cli/escalate.go) that exports a preview endpoint for instantiated runbooks and suggested escalation adjustments.
- Add a CLI command `sloctl profile simulate` to run a deterministic simulation against historical alert traces for validation.
- Add unit and integration tests plus an e2e harness that runs a short alert storm simulation.

Checklist:
- [x] Add profile engine and tests
- [x] Add runbook template renderer and sample templates
- [x] Add CLI simulate command and docs
- [x] Add incident-bot hook and wiring
- [x] Add canary rollout (50% teams) config
- [x] Documentation and example templates in docs/runbooks.md

Commits summary:
- feat(profile): initial profile engine and rule evaluator
- feat(template): runbook templating and renderer
- feat(cli): add profile simulate command and integration
- fix(ci): mock telemetry sources for deterministic tests
- chore(docs): runbook examples and usage guide
- perf(profile): small optimization for evaluation hot path

Changed files (high level):

Motivation: Recent incidents showed oscillation during cross-region failovers when short-lived spikes triggered full circuit handoffs. Chronos is a small orchestrator that enforces timebound fallback windows and a coordinated recovery policy per-region to avoid repeated rapid circuit flips and egress thrashing.

This PR delivers: 1) a timebound fallback orchestrator (Chronos) that gates full failover for a configurable 'snooze' window; 2) a coordinated recovery probe sequence to reintroduce capacity gradually; 3) tighter egress cap smoothing during handoff to avoid transient egress storms; 4) tracing and metric hooks to make recovery windows and decisions visible in the Console; 5) a race-condition hotfix when two adjacent regions try to claim the same tenant lease during rapid handover.

Checklist:
- [x] core orchestrator loop implemented
- [x] policy config + Linear-driven defaults added
- [x] telemetry metrics & tracing added
- [x] unit tests for lease arbitration and window expiry
- [x] integration smoke against regional failover simulator
- [x] rollout gating and feature flagging
- [x] documentation notes for operators (Console + CLI)

Implementation notes: Chronos runs inside the control-plane failover coordinator and exposes a small policy struct (TimeboundWindow) used during SLO-triggered decisions. The orchestrator prefers soft-fallback first (prefix shedding / KV-preserve) and only escalates to full region handoff if the snooze window expires without observed improvement. During rejoin, Chronos uses a backoff ladder that increases allowed egress gradually over a window instead of an immediate cold restore. This avoids KV cache thrash and sudden downstream egress spikes.

Commit summary:
- 9f2b7c9: introduce chronos orchestrator scaffolding and policy config
- d2a3b4e: implement lease arbitration + timebound window state machine
- 7c5e1d2: add egress smoothing and staged reintroduce logic

Summary of behavioral changes:
- Default snooze window: 12s (configurable per-tenant/class)
- Staged reintroduce steps: 25% -> 50% -> 100% egress allowance over configurable intervals
- Preference order: soft-degrade -> staged reintroduce -> full region failover (last resort)

Context: Design partners and Support have hit confusing failures in the offline/air-gapped upgrade flow when bundles are incomplete, corrupted, or built against the wrong target version (see SUP-18510). Today the installer will often fail late (during image/chart pull) and the error doesn’t clearly tell the operator what’s missing or mismatched. This PR adds deterministic bundle verification up front: (1) a required SHA256 checksum manifest for all bundle artifacts, (2) optional signature verification for the manifest, and (3) clearer, actionable error messages that enumerate missing/incorrect artifacts before any cluster mutations. Behavior: - New required file inside bundle: bundle.manifest.json (list of artifacts + expected sha256 + size + logical type). - New required file inside bundle: bundle.manifest.sha256 (sha256sum of bundle.manifest.json) OR embedded sha256 in the manifest (we accept either; prefer sha256 file). - Optional files: bundle.manifest.sig + bundle.manifest.pub (ed25519). If present, installer verifies signature and prints signer fingerprint. (Signature is optional for this release to avoid breaking existing customers; we will gate to required in a future major). - Installer runs verification during upgrade plan generation and again immediately before apply (defense-in-depth if bundle is swapped between plan/apply). - Error messaging: missing artifact(s) are printed as a numbered list with expected paths; checksum mismatch prints expected vs actual sha256 and suggests re-download/re-mirror; version mismatch prints bundle target version vs requested version and points to the compatibility policy doc. - Adds break-glass flag: --skip-bundle-verification (hidden behind --i-understand-the-risks) for Support-only workflows. Security notes: No secrets are stored in the bundle verification metadata. Public key is optional and can be provided via file path or embedded in the bundle. Logging: verification results are included in the installer run summary and emitted as a structured event (bundle_verify_started / bundle_verify_failed / bundle_verify_succeeded). Testing: unit tests cover manifest parsing, sha validation, signature verification, and error formatting; integration test adds a corrupted bundle fixture and asserts failure before any k8s writes. Rollout: This is backward compatible for existing bundles (signature optional; checksum manifest required only when --airgapped-bundle is used). For online installs nothing changes. Checklist: - [x] Verify missing chart/image entries are surfaced preflight - [x] Verify corrupted tarball errors are actionable - [x] Add docs snippet to installer help output - [x] Add integration fixture + CI lane
Connor O'Brien: Can we fail before we even start k8s interactions? We had a case where the bundle was missing the chart tgz and it only showed up during Helm. Also please ensure the error includes the expected relative path so Support can tell customers exactly what to mirror.
Fatima Noor (author): Yes — verification now runs as part of plan generation (no k8s writes) and again right before apply. Error output enumerates expected paths from the manifest. Added a dedicated error formatter so it’s consistent with other preflight output.
Marcus Lin: Signature verification: what’s the trust model here? If signature is optional, we should at least strongly warn when a signature is present but invalid. Also, don’t allow arbitrary key fetch from network in airgapped mode.
Fatima Noor (author): Agreed. If .sig exists and verification fails, we hard-fail (no fallback). If no signature files, we proceed with sha validation only and print a warning that integrity is checked but provenance is not. Public key is only loaded from a local path or from bundle.manifest.pub if provided; no network access.
Irene Choi: For on-prem, operators will ask how to generate the sha/manifest. Are we providing a generator script or just validating? Also what about large bundles—streaming verification vs reading into memory?
Fatima Noor (author): This PR validates only; bundle creation is handled by the release pipeline (separate PR). Verification streams file hashing from disk (io.Copy to sha256) and does not load artifacts into memory. Added notes in help text describing required files and that they are produced by Redwood’s release tooling.
Victor Alvarez: Minor: the error for ‘missing registry mirror endpoint’ should not show up for offline bundles; it confused one of our staging tests.
Fatima Noor (author): Good catch. I scoped mirror endpoint checks to online mode only; airgapped verification now focuses strictly on bundle presence/integrity.
Connor O'Brien: Approved once the break-glass flag is behind a scary prompt / explicit acknowledgment.
Fatima Noor (author): Implemented --skip-bundle-verification only with --i-understand-the-risks, plus it prints a big warning and is excluded from normal help output.
Marcus Lin: Approved.
Connor O'Brien: Approved. Please add a note in release notes for Support.
Irene Choi: Approved.
Private/on-prem: Air-gapped upgrade bundles are now verified pre-upgrade via SHA256 manifest; optional manifest signature verification is supported.
Installer errors for missing/incorrect offline artifacts are now actionable and list the exact missing paths and checksum mismatches.
Support-only: Added break-glass flags to bypass verification with explicit risk acknowledgment.

Context: During canary we saw overload responses missing Retry-After on some routes (notably chat completions + a subset of streaming paths), which caused clients to implement ad-hoc retry behavior and in one case a retry storm. This PR standardizes how we emit Retry-After and correlation IDs for overload/load-shedding responses, and adds a short internal "client retry contract" comment block to keep behavior stable across gateway/routing/runtime.

What changes: 1) Retry-After is now set for all overload-class responses emitted by the API gateway (admission control + breaker open + dependency brownout mapping) and for propagated overload errors from downstream services when they bubble back through the gateway. 2) Correlation ID plumbing is tightened: we prefer an existing inbound X-Request-ID (if present), otherwise generate a Redwood request id, and we always return it to clients in both X-Request-ID and X-Redwood-Correlation-ID for a deprecation window. 3) Centralizes overload response construction into a shared helper that sets headers + JSON payload consistently (status, error.code, error.message, retry guidance, request_id). 4) Adds a code comment (internal contract) that documents semantics: when clients should retry, how to treat 429 vs 503 overload, and that Retry-After is in seconds.

Notes/constraints: - Retry-After is emitted as an integer number of seconds (RFC-compliant); we do not emit HTTP-date format. - For streaming (SSE) requests, we only attempt overload rejection before the response is committed; once headers have been sent, we cannot reliably add Retry-After. This PR ensures the admission decision happens before initiating the stream in gateway. - We do not change error codes/status mappings here (see ADR-014); this PR only enforces header + correlation id consistency.

Testing: - Unit tests for overload response helper (header presence, seconds formatting, correlation id behavior). - Integration test covering /v1/chat/completions streaming: overload rejection happens before stream start and includes Retry-After + request id. - Regression test for SUP-2860 reproduction (route missing header).

Rollout: Safe for dark launch; header additions are backwards compatible (additive). Client-visible change is improved consistency (some clients previously saw no Retry-After).
Ethan Park (review): Can we confirm Retry-After is always seconds (not date) and consistent across 429/503? Also please ensure we don't accidentally set it on non-overload 5xx.

Christine Wong (author): Yep. Helper only used by overload paths (breaker open, admission shed, downstream mapped overload). Added a guard test to ensure generic 5xx errors do not set Retry-After.

Aisha Bello (review): Please add a metric for missing Retry-After as a canary safety check. We should be able to alert if this regresses.

Christine Wong (author): Added api_gateway.overload.retry_after_missing counter (dimensions: route_group, region, status) and wired it into logging when helper isn't used (should stay at 0). No tenant_id dimension.

Ibrahim Khan (review): For SDKs we key off X-Request-ID today. Returning both X-Request-ID and X-Redwood-Correlation-ID is fine, but we should document the precedence and avoid breaking existing clients.

Christine Wong (author): Updated request_id.ts to prefer inbound X-Request-ID and always echo it back; X-Redwood-Correlation-ID is additive for now. Added comment in helper about deprecation window.

Mina Haddad (review): On routing fallback, we sometimes return an overload from routing with a retryable code. Are we certain Retry-After is preserved when routing returns its own error payload?

Christine Wong (author): Gateway now overwrites/sets Retry-After on mapped overload regardless of downstream body, but preserves downstream error.code/message. Also ensures request_id is our canonical id.

Nikhil Sharma (review): Please keep the "client retry contract" short and explicit. We should avoid promising exact backoff durations.

Christine Wong (author): Tightened language: we only promise Retry-After is present and in seconds; clients should add jitter and cap retries. No guarantees on exact window beyond header value.
Hosted API: overload/load-shedding responses now consistently include Retry-After (seconds) and return a stable correlation ID header for easier client retry/backoff and support debugging.
payload.title: Load shedding: consistent Retry-After + correlation IDs; document client retry contract

Motivation: New OpenAI Responses variants expose two practical features we need to support in the compatibility bridge: (1) determinism hints that affect rerolling/seeded inference (not always a raw numeric seed), and (2) an annotated metadata envelope that clients expect to be passed through back to their application layer. Without preserving these we see mismatch between Redwood responses and customer expectations (reproducibility and attribution).

What this PR does: Adds a compatibility layer in the OpenAI bridge that: 1) accepts the newer 'determinism_hint' top-level field (and the legacy 'seed' when present) and maps both into an internal safe representation (x-rdwd-determinism-hint) which is forwarded to the serving runtime and persisted with the response event. 2) accepts an 'annotations' / 'metadata' object from incoming Responses-style requests, validates it against a white-list (string keys, small scalar values) and forwards it as an opaque envelope into our response records and emitted events. 3) improves streaming reassembly by introducing "liveness anchors"—small sequence markers attached to partial events so the client can reconstitute ordered structured outputs even when chunks arrive out of order. 4) ensures tool/function calling headers (x-rdwd-toolcall-id, x-rdwd-toolcall-wrap) are carried through the bridge to the tool runtime and mapped back into the OpenAI-compatible "tool_call" frames so SDKs receive function call events as expected.

Compatibility and fallbacks: The bridge recognizes multiple Response variants via a 'response_variant' flag (v1/v2/v5). For older requests we fall back to prior behavior. For determinism, if both 'seed' and 'determinism_hint' are provided we prefer the explicit 'determinism_hint' and log an inspector warning. Customers using Redwood Dedicated with strict determinism can pin a deterministic profile; the bridge now surfaces the upstream hint for audit and replay.

Design notes (high level): - Minimal surface: use header translation (x-rdwd-*) rather than changing core request schemas. This keeps the runtime agnostic and limits blast radius. - Validation: annotations are size-limited (max 2KB serialised), keys must match ^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$, values must be strings or numbers. Invalid annotations are dropped and a warning returned in the response 'warnings' array. - Streaming anchors: binary-safe 8-byte anchor appended to the metadata of each partial event. Receiver reassembly uses anchor order, then sequence index. Anchor collisions are rare and cause a compact re-fetch of the missing shard. - Toolcall mapping: toolcall headers are stable strings; we generate a synthetic 'tool_origin' attribute that ties the function invocation back to the original request's metadata envelope.

Tests and CI: Added unit tests in bridge tests covering mapping and validation, integration tests that spin up the openai-compat harness and verify function-call roundtrips, and an e2e streaming test that simulates chunk reordering and validates reassembly. Also added a small dedicated load test that measures latency impact of anchor embedding (negligible in our quick runs).

Commits (summary): - Add compatibility translator for determinism_hint and seed -> bridge/header mapping - Validate and forward annotations envelope to events store - Implement liveness anchors for streaming reassembly and consumer helper - Propagate toolcall headers through bridge to tool runtime and back to OpenAI frames - Tests: unit + integration + streaming e2e harness - Docs: how-to and compatibility notes in docs/openai_compat.md

Files changed (high level): ["src/bridge/openai_compat.ts", "runtime/stream/anchor_reassembly.go", "api/handlers/toolcall_proxy.py", "docs/openai_compat.md", "tests/bridge/test_determinism.ts", "tests/integration/test_toolcall_roundtrip.py", "tests/e2e/test_stream_anchor_reassembly.sh", "pkg/events/annotations.go", "pkg/events/events_store_migration.sql", "ci/workflows/openai-compat.yml", "examples/openai/response-variant-samples.json", "README.md"]

Patch snippet (illustrative, kept tiny):
const mapped = {
  headers: {
    ...incoming.headers,
    'x-rdwd-determinism-hint': incoming.body.determinism_hint || incoming.body.seed || undefined
  },
  metadata: validatedAnnotations(incoming.body.annotations)
};

Review conversation (condensed):
- Arjun Patel: "Nice focused change. Two asks: (1) can we avoid adding anchors to every single token event by coalescing them when streaming rate is > 200 RPS? (2) add stronger unit tests for malformed annotations."
- Maya Singh (author): "Answer: we coalesce anchors when rate threshold hit (see runtime/stream/coalesce.go left-in). Added more tests for malformed keys and oversized payloads."
- Sofia Reyes: "Please confirm metrics emitted for dropped annotations and the inspector warning shape. Also check security review for arbitrary metadata size/keys."
- Maya Singh: "Metrics added: bridge.annotations.dropped and bridge.annotations.accepted. Security: white-list + size limit. I ran a short audit and added doc note."
- Ben Kwan: "Integration passed locally but CI hit a flakey test on macos runner (socket timeout). Rerun fixed it."
- Arjun Patel: "LGTM after semantics clarified on deterministic precedence. Approving now."

CI status history: initial CI run: lint pass, unit tests pass, integration tests fail (timeout on test_toolcall_roundtrip.py), rerun integration -> pass, workflow green. Coverage delta: +0.6%.

Notes for release: This change is non-breaking for the vast majority of users. Customers that depended on silently dropping unknown top-level fields should verify their clients if they rely on exact payload shapes. We added two documented headers (x-rdwd-determinism-hint, x-rdwd-toolcall-id) and the annotations envelope behavior to docs/openai_compat.md.

Related: ENG-1429 (compatibility with Responses v5), ENG-1587 (structured streaming reassembly).
Bridge: Add support for forwarding OpenAI-style determinism hints and annotated metadata from Responses variants. Improves streaming reassembly robustness and preserves toolcall headers for function/tool routing.

Added more tests for malformed keys and oversized payloads.' -- Sofia Reyes: 'Please confirm metrics emitted for dropped annotations and the inspector warning shape. Rerun fixed it.' -- Arjun Patel: 'LGTM after semantics clarified on deterministic precedence. Approving now.'

Summary: Adds a new benchmark runner (intermittent-sampler-sweep) and an Opportunistic Cache Auditor reporter to the benchmark-lab suite. The runner simulates bursty/intermittent traffic patterns with configurable sleep windows to exercise cold vs warm cache transitions; the auditor records KV cache hit/miss transitions and correlates them with per-request kernel samples to help diagnose transient thrash and warmup regressions.

Motivation: Several recent production incidents showed short-lived cache thrash during bursty ingress (p95 spikes for ~10s) that escaped our steady-state benchmarks. This PR provides a reproducible harness for those patterns and instrumentation to pinpoint whether regressions are scheduling-, batch-, or cache-related.

Key features:
1) Deterministic intermittent workload generator with phase scripting (pattern file format) and seeded RNG for reproducible runs.
2) Opportunistic Cache Auditor that attaches (non-invasively) to the benchmark runtime to capture KV cache evictions, prefix/hotpath counts, and short-lived miss bursts; outputs a delta-based audit stream suitable for our reporting pipeline.
3) Sampled kernel-stack annotator that emits a small stack capture per sampled request (configurable sampling rate) to correlate hot kernels with cache miss windows.
4) Phase-aware tail-latency heatmap reporter (per-phase p50/p95/p99 distributions and duration buckets).
5) CI benchmark job integration and a small local runner for dev iteration.

Description (detailed): The intermittent-sampler-sweep runner lives under benchmark-lab/runners/ and accepts a pattern.yaml that describes sequences of: {duration, qps, parallelism, sleep_ms, seed}. The default patterns include a short-burst-with-sleep scenario and a multi-burst staircase. The runner boots the workload, primes caches for a configurable window, then performs a sweep across phases while emitting standardized events to the bench-event bus. The Opportunistic Cache Auditor subscribes to that bus and tracks low-level KV events emitted by our test runtime (kvcache.eviction, kvcache.hit, kvcache.miss). When a transient miss burst is detected (miss-rate delta > configurable threshold within a sliding window), the auditor triggers a brief increased sampling rate for the kernel-stack annotator and tags the event with the active phase id and seed.

Implementation notes:
- Deterministic seeding is enforced across runner and reporters to make runs fully reproducible when run with the same pattern.yaml and seed.
- The auditor tracks per-model and global cache metrics and writes an audit stream in newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) under artifacts/audits/<run-id>.ndjson to be ingested by the reporting pipeline.
- The sampled-stack annotator uses a lightweight in-process signal-safe collector that collects at most one sample per request to minimize perturbation; sampling rate is adjustable (default 1%).
- The phase heatmap reporter produces both CSV and a condensed JSON summary for quick triage.

Commits:
- a1c3db2: runner: add intermittent-sampler-sweep implementation, pattern parsing and phase engine
- b4f7e90: reporter: add opportunistic cache auditor with ndjson audit stream
- c9d2f17: reporter: sampled kernel-stack annotator and per-phase heatmap exporter
- d2a9f41: tests: unit tests for pattern parsing and auditor detection thresholds
- e78b5c0: ci: add bench job and example pattern files

Files changed (high level):
- runners/intermittent_sweep.py (new)
- reporters/cache_auditor.py (new)
- reporters/stack_sampler.py (new)
- reporters/phase_heatmap.py (new)
- config/patterns/intermittent_default.yaml (new)
- tests/test_pattern_parser.py (new)
- ci/bench-workflow.yaml (modified)
- docs/bench/bench-guide.md (modified)

Small illustrative snippet (runner usage): ```yaml
pattern:
  - duration: 30s
    qps: 250
    parallelism: 16
    sleep_ms: 10000
    seed: 42
```

Integration notes:
- The new bench workflow (ci/bench-workflow.yaml) is gated behind a bench label to avoid running on every PR; it runs nightly for main and on-demand via workflow_dispatch.
- Local development: `python -m benchmark_lab.runners.intermittent_sweep --pattern config/patterns/intermittent_default.yaml --out artifacts/run-123`

Observability and outputs:
- artifacts/run-123/audits.ndjson (time-series of cache deltas and annotations)
- artifacts/run-123/heatmap.json (phase->quantile buckets)
- artifacts/run-123/stack-samples.ndjson (sampled kernel stacks)

Review conversation (high level, chronological):
- Ethan Cole (Reviewer) 2024-11-18: "Nice focused runner. Can we ensure the sampling collector doesn't skew latencies? Please include micro-benchmark numbers." Author (Priya) 2024-11-18: "Added a micro-benchmark in stack_sampler microbench and lowered default sampling to 1% — numbers added to docs."
- Marisa Flores (Reviewer) 2024-11-19: "Audit stream format looks good. Can you include model-id tag on each audit event so we can correlate multi-model Dedicated tests?" Author (Priya) 2024-11-19: "Done — auditor now emits model_id and route_id when available."
- Luca Romano (Reviewer) 2024-11-20: "CI bench job failed on first run due to missing workflow dispatch permission. Also saw a flake in test_pattern_parser on ~arm runners." Author (Priya) 2024-11-20: "Fixed CI YAML to use workflow_dispatch and relaxed timing in test to be tolerant on low-power runners. Re-ran CI."

CI and checks:
- build: pass
- lint: pass (minor style fixes applied)
- unit-tests: pass
- bench-smoke: fail on first run (missing permissions) -> fixed -> pass
- nightly-bench (manual run): pass

Merge: Squash and merge after approvals. Merge outcome: merged into main on 2024-11-21 via squash merge.

Post-merge follow-ups:
- ENG-4897: add a visualizer that consumes the heatmap JSON for quick on-call triage (tracked).
- ENG-4821: run the intermittent patterns against the Dedicated fleet in the staging cluster (scheduled).

Why this is different from existing suites: Existing bench-lab runners focus on steady-state sequences and phase-mixing; this PR intentionally targets short-lived intermittent bursts and transient cache behavior with tight correlation between cache deltas and kernel-level samples. That combination (opportunistic audit + phase-aware sampling) provides a new signal for diagnosing short-lived regressions that previously evaded our baseline benchmarks.

How to run locally:
1) pip install -e .[bench]
2) python -m benchmark_lab.runners.intermittent_sweep --pattern config/patterns/intermittent_default.yaml --out /tmp/bench-run
3) tail -n +1 /tmp/bench-run/audits.ndjson
4) python benchmark_lab.reporters.phase_heatmap --input /tmp/bench-run/audits.ndjson --out /tmp/heatmap.json

Notes:
- No behavioral changes to production code-paths; all instrumentation is opt-in and isolated to benchmark artifacts.
- Added tests to keep pattern parsing deterministic and to verify auditor detection thresholds.
- This PR is intentionally conservative on sampling defaults to avoid perturbing measurements.
New benchmark runner: intermittent-sampler-sweep. Adds opportunistic cache auditing to detect transient KV-cache thrash under bursty traffic patterns; new reporters for sampled kernel stacks and per-phase tail-latency heatmaps.
