Summary: Introduces two small, focused incident-response utilities inside incident-bot: a heuristics filer that ingests alert metadata and emits a 3-line on-call brief (mini-brief) prioritizing what to check first, and an ephemeral (sandboxed) remedier that can run read-only diagnostics and gated remediation suggestions in a safe environment. The intent is to reduce mean-time-to-first-action for oncall engineers and to provide a low-risk way to fast-run repeatable diagnostics during early investigation.

Motivation and context: On recent pager storms we observed that responders spend disproportionately long time finding the initial quick signal to validate whether a service is degraded vs an upstream problem (ENG-1284). Existing runbooks are often long and require manual scanning. We want a very small single-screen brief that highlights the top 3 heuristics and provides an immediately-runnable, read-only diagnostic harness that collects targeted artifacts (top traces, recent error counts, key metrics sample). This PR implements the core pieces used by our SRE rotation pilots.

What this change does:
- Adds heuristics-filer: a rule engine that maps alert labels, service ownership, SLO hit types, and recent deploy markers to a ranked list of three investigative heuristics (e.g., "check async queue depth", "validate upstream 3rd-party OK", "confirm KV cache hit-rate"). Each heuristic includes the rationale and one-line command suggestion.
- Adds ephemeral-remedier: a sandbox runner that executes a set of safe, read-only diagnostic commands (metrics snapshot, trace tail, log grep with size bounds) in an ephemeral container and returns an attachable bundle link. It is explicitly disabled for any remediation actions that mutate state; remediation suggestions are produced as plain-text guidance that require explicit confirmation via a separate secured workflow.
- Wire up a lightweight /oncall/mini-brief endpoint consumed by the web UI and Slack helper. The endpoint returns the mini-brief + a single ephemeral bundle URL when requested.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked in Linear (ENG-1284) [x] unit tests for rule scoring [x] integration tests for sandbox runner [x] basic UI integration (Slack button) [x] docs snippet in README / runbook snippets [ ] add SLO-based tuning (follow-up).

High level commits: 1) heuristics engine + test vectors; 2) ephemeral runner scaffold + sandbox container config; 3) integration adapter for alert payloads and Slack action; 4) docs and runbook examples; 5) fixer commit for CI flaky test.

Changed files (high-level):
- src/heuristics/filer.py - core rule engine and scorer
- src/heuristics/tests/test_filer.py - unit tests and edge cases
- src/ephemeral/runner.py - sandbox runner implementation and constraints
- src/ephemeral/sandbox/Dockerfile - minimal readonly image used in CI and staging
- integrations/slack/mini_brief_adapter.py - small adapter for Slack actions
- docs/oncall/mini-briefs.md - runbook + example queries
- ci/flake-fixes.yml - test timeout tuning to reduce false negatives
- pkg/ephemeral/README.md - operational notes and security model

Review conversation (high level):
- Marco Reyes (reviewer): "Nice focused surface area. A couple of questions: how do we prevent sensitive logs from leaking in the ephemeral bundles? Can the sandbox inadvertently escalate permissions?"
- Aisha (author): "Sandbox image is strictly read-only, runs under an unprivileged user and the collector has a whitelist of keys and size limits. I added pkg/ephemeral/README.md describing the guarantees. We also scrub PII from logs using the log-scrubber plugin before bundle upload."
- Priya Patel (reviewer): "Rule engine looks good but scoring feels too static. Suggest adding a small decay factor for deploy markers so that an older deploy doesn't dominate heuristics."
- Aisha: "Added a decay param and unit tests (test_filer decay cases). The decay is configurable via env so ops can tune per-service."
- Jonah Li (reviewer): "CI flake on the sandbox integration; re-run fixed it. Also requested clearer error surface when bundle upload fails."
- Aisha: "Added clearer error messages and retry logic for bundle upload. CI green after fix. See final commit message 'retry: clearer bundle upload error and timeout'."

CI summary: initial run failed due to a timeout in sandbox integration (test_ephemeral_integration). Timeout increased and test hardened in commit 5. Subsequent runs: build ✓, unit tests ✓, integration tests ✓, lint ✓, e2e flaky test retried once then passed. Overall status: pass.

Security and operational notes:
- Sandbox runs in a restricted namespace; network egress to external endpoints is blocked except to our artifact store.
- Bundle URLs expire after 24 hours and are signed with short-lived tokens.
- Audit events are emitted for all ephemeral runs (user, alert_id, heuristics chosen).
- No write actions are enabled by default; remediation suggestions are post-facto guidance that require a separate, audited workflow to execute.

Backwards compatibility and breaking changes: No public API changes to the alert payload schema. The new /oncall/mini-brief endpoint is additive. Breaking change: false.

Merge and rollout: Merged via squash-merge on 2026-02-15 after approvals from Marco and Priya. Feature gated behind a config flag INCIDENT_MINIBRIEF_ENABLED=false by default. Rollout plan: enable for SRE rotation cohort canary group first-week, monitor usage, then widen.

Follow-ups (post-merge):
- Add SLO-aware heuristics tuning (ENG-1302).
- Add signed printable one-pager for pagers on-call training.
- Add ability to attach user-provided safe scripts under a strict curations list.

Notes for reviewers: please see docs/oncall/mini-briefs.md for example payloads and sample heuristics. If any team wants early access to the canary, ping the SRE rotation list.
Adds a lightweight on-call brief generator and a sandboxed, read-only remediation runner. No end-user API changes.

Summary: Introduces a migration sandbox mode and operator eviction guard to reduce blast radius during private upgrades. Adds a tenant safelist (opt-in per-cluster) and a dry-run reporting pipeline for SQL/DDL migrations so operators can validate changes end-to-end before committing. Motivation: customers running Redwood Private have reported upgrade incidents where long-running schema migrations caused operator eviction/failover and tenant-impacting rollbacks. This PR provides a safe rehearsal path and automated rollback hooks to make upgrades incremental and observable.

What changed (high-level): \u2022 migration-sandbox controller: new controller that spins up ephemeral migration workers in a fenced namespace to run schema migrations against a writable but isolated sandbox DB (Postgres logical replica + rewrite rules). Outputs a detailed migration report (timings, locks, sample queries) to a ClusterReport custom resource. \u2022 operator-eviction guard: admission-style hook that blocks eviction or scaling down of critical operator/statefulset pods when an in-flight migration with a "lock-sensitive" label exists in the cluster. Guard can be overridden by explicit force-unblock from admins. \u2022 tenant-safelist: cluster-scoped config map + CRD allowing operators to mark tenants (namespaces/tenanted IDs) that are excluded from disruptive migration strategies during a rollout. \u2022 dry-run pipeline: SQL parser + preflight check stage that detects potential locking patterns (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, ALTER TABLE ...), estimates lock durations using sampling, and emits recommendations (CONCURRENTLY, chunked index build, background migration). \u2022 UX: console annotations and installer CLI flags: --enable-migration-sandbox, --migration-safelist-file, --dry-run-report-path.

Commits (summary): \u2022 1a2b3c4: scaffold migration-sandbox controller and CRDs\u2022 2b3c4d5: implement logical-replica executor + report generator\u2022 3c4d5e6: admission webhook for operator-eviction guard\u2022 4d5e6f7: tenant-safelist CRD and CLI wiring\u2022 5e6f7g8: dry-run SQL analysis engine and unit tests\u2022 6f7g8h9: e2e smoke tests and install docs

Files changed (representative): \u2022 charts/private-installer/templates/migration-sandbox.yaml (adds CRDs + controller deployment)\u2022 operator/controllers/migration_sandbox_controller.go (controller logic + reconcile loop)\u2022 operator/webhook/eviction_guard.go (admission webhook)\u2022 pkg/migration/dryrun/parser.go (SQL heuristics)\u2022 cli/install/migration_flags.go (installer flags)\u2022 docs/private-upgrades/migration-sandbox.md (operator runbook + playbook)

Small illustrative snippet (controller reconcile loop, simplified): \n```\n// reconcile: ensure sandbox job exists for the migration CR\nif !sandboxJobExists(cr) {\n  job := buildSandboxJob(cr)\n  r.client.Create(ctx, job)\n}\n// watch job status -> generate ClusterReport when finished\n```\n\nTesting and CI: The PR adds unit tests for the SQL heuristics, controller integration tests using KIND, and an e2e smoke job in the CI pipeline that validates CRD install/uninstall across supported K8s versions. CI initially failed on a flaky interaction between the webhook and the controller; fixed by adding a short backoff and idempotent admission response. Final CI status: pass (all checks green after rerun).

Review conversation (excerpt): \u2022 Jonas Becker (reviewer, 2025-11-18): "Nice isolation approach. Two asks: 1) add a TTL/garbage collection policy for sandbox DBs, and 2) ensure reports avoid PII in sample rows." \u2022 Maya Patel (author): "Added sandbox TTL config and implemented redaction hooks for sample rows (see pkg/migration/report_redact.go)." \u2022 Priya Singh (reviewer): "Eviction guard looks safe but we need an operator-level override for emergencies; suggest 'force-unblock' on the Operator CR." \u2022 Maya Patel: "Added operator.forceUnblock field and CLI admin command 'redwoodctl admin unblock-operator --reason'. Documented audit log entry." \u2022 Carlos Ramirez (approver): "E2E passed in my local cluster, and dry-run reports are useful for SRE teams. Approved with nits." \u2022 Post-merge note from SRE (internal): "Recommend enabling sandbox non-disruptively on staging clusters for 2 weeks before canarying to production. Added Linear ticket ENG-1610 for rollout plan." 

Backward compatibility and safety: The migration sandbox and safelist are opt-in behind installer flags and Operator CR fields. Default behavior of upgrades remains unchanged unless cluster admin enables the sandbox. The eviction guard only blocks automated eviction paths; manual admin overrides are available.

Operational runbook (short): \u2022 Stage: enable --enable-migration-sandbox on a staging cluster and run existing migration manifests with --dry-run-report-path set. Review ClusterReport for lock warnings. \u2022 Canary: enable safelist to exclude high-risk tenants, run migrations in sandbox for the rest. \u2022 Production: once reports are clean, flip migration-controller to 'apply' mode. If the eviction guard blocks a rollout, use 'redwoodctl admin unblock-operator' with a documented reason and follow rollback steps described in docs.

Why this is different from prior work: Earlier PRs focused on atomic rollback and snapshot restore; this PR focuses on preflight and rehearsal for schema changes and prevents operator-level disruption during migrations. It reduces human error during upgrades by giving teams a repeatable, observable dry-run and a mitigated path to production.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after approvals from Jonas, Priya, and Carlos. Changelog entry and upgrade notes added to docs site.

Follow-ups: ENG-1610 (rollout plan + monitoring), ENG-1623 (add anonymized cost-estimation for long-running migrations), DOC-78 (console integration for ClusterReport).
Adds a non-destructive DB migration sandbox and an admission-style eviction guard for the private installer operator. Enables a tenant safelist and dry-run reporting for schema migrations; no behavioral change by default unless flags enabled.
payload.title: Add DB migration sandbox, operator eviction guard, and tenant safelist for private upgrades

Motivation: Our CI pipeline has diverged over time: multiple workflow entrypoints, duplicated shell glue, and subtle differences between how lint and test run locally vs in CI. This makes it hard to reason about churn from dependency updates and causes flaky test coverage across runners. This PR centralizes the entrypoint logic for lint/test/build and introduces a lightweight dep-visibility audit plus a dep-curation-bot to automatically tag and annotate dependency PRs.

What I changed (high-level):
- .github/workflows/ci.yaml: Replaced three separate lint/test workflows with a single matrix-driven entry that delegates to scripts/ci/entrypoint.sh. Matrix preserves platform permutations (linux/arm, node/python).
- scripts/ci/entrypoint.sh: New canonical entrypoint for CI tasks. Accepts TASK=(lint|unit|integration|smoke) and loads common env/setup. Reduces ad-hoc shell fragments across repo.
- scripts/ci/README.md: Docs for local vs CI execution and how to add new tasks.
- tools/dep_visibility/audit.py: Small analyzer that inspects package-lock/yarn.lock and go.mod to surface transitive packages that appear in >1direct dependency version ranges (conflicts), and calculates a "visibility score" describing how widespread a transitive upgrade is likely to be. This is intentionally conservative (non-blocking).
- tools/dep_curator/bot.py + .github/workflows/dep-curator.yml: A GitHub Action wrapper that labels PRs from Renovate/Dependabot when the audit reports high-impact transitive changes. It also posts a short checklist in the PR body with recommended reviewers (platform, sdk, docs).
- renovate.json: small config tweaks to push monorepo-safe grouping and to add a label that dep-curation-bot recognizes.
- ci/shims/node-lint.sh and ci/shims/py-test.sh: Minimal shims that forward to canonical entrypoint for local dev ergonomics.

Commits (summary):
- 0c4a9b2: initial scaffold for entrypoint and CI workflow switch
- b7d3f11: implement dep_visibility audit and basic tests + sample lockfile fixtures
- 9a1e2ff: add dep-curation bot and action workflow + integration test harness
- 2f3c5d9: docs, README, and small fixes from review feedback

Changed files (representative):
- .github/workflows/ci.yaml
- .github/workflows/dep-curator.yml
- scripts/ci/entrypoint.sh
- scripts/ci/README.md
- tools/dep_visibility/audit.py
- tools/dep_curator/bot.py
- renovate.json
- ci/shims/node-lint.sh
- ci/shims/py-test.sh

Small illustrative snippets included inline in the patch: entrypoint.sh (stripped down):
"#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
TASK=${1:-unit}
case \"$TASK\" in
  lint) ./ci/shims/node-lint.sh ;;
  unit) pytest -q ;;
  integration) ./scripts/run_integration.sh ;;
  *) echo \"unknown task: $TASK\"; exit 2;;
esac
"

Why this is safe: The CI workflow change is additive: the matrix preserves current runner labels and only changes how jobs are invoked. The dep-visibility tool is read-only and non-blocking by default; the bot only annotates and labels PRs. Renovate grouping change tightens grouping but does not expand upgrade cadence.

Review notes and trade-offs:
- We deliberately avoid enforcing dep-visibility as a gate in this PR to keep adoption low friction. Next phase is to surface dashboards in Console and optionally add a soft-gate in a monitored repository.
- The audit currently supports npm/yarn and Go modules. Adding python/poetry/pip-tools will be follow-up (ENG-1399).

CI summary: Initial runs flagged a lint script that relied on an env var; fixed with a shim (b7d3f11). Final CI run: all checks passed (unit, integration-flaky allowed, lint, dep-curator smoke).

Merge: squashed and merged to main after approvals and a green CI run.

Related: ENG-1345 (monorepo CI consolidation), ENG-1399 (dep-visibility expansion).
- Consolidate CI entrypoints to reduce duplication and clarify lint/test semantics
- Add dep-visibility-audit tool and dep-curation-bot to surface risky transitive upgrades
- Small scripts to opt teams into incremental dependency ramping
Arjun Patel: Can we ensure the entrypoint preserves the runner's exit code so GitHub Actions job statuses remain accurate? Requested change: forward exit codes from tasks.
Sofia Park: Addressed in 9a1e2ff by explicitly capturing TASK_EXIT and exiting with that value; added unit test for exit code forwarding.
Maya Liu: The dep_visibility report is helpful, but can we avoid noise for low-impact transitive bumps? Requested change: introduce a visibility threshold and sample size check.
Sofia Park: Added threshold logic and an opt-out via DEP_VISIBILITY_THRESHOLD env var; updated README to document behavior.
Diego Ramos: Approve after CI green. Approved.

## Summary
Adds the Console UI for viewing Shadow Experiment results: quality deltas vs control, confidence intervals, segment breakdowns, and a drilldown drawer for scored examples.

This is explicitly *read-only* UI for the beta. Creation flow remains in the existing experiment wizard (DES-611 work), and the results page is linked from Rollouts timeline + the Shadow Experiments list.

Everything in this PR is gated behind `shadow_experiments_results_ui` (per tenant). When disabled, routes fall back to the existing placeholder/"Coming soon" page.

## Why
We have shadow traffic shipping in dogfood and early Dedicated beta, but teams can’t validate quality changes without an at-a-glance view of deltas and a way to inspect examples. This PR wires up the results UX to the new aggregates + examples endpoints from the Console backend (PR #24933) and renders:
- Quality delta charts (candidate vs control), with 95% CI bands and significance callout when applicable
- Segment filters (safe dimensions only) + time range picker
- "Top regressions" table and per-metric deep links
- Example drilldown drawer (prompt/response *redacted*) with rubric breakdowns and scorer metadata

## Feature flag
- Flag: `shadow_experiments_results_ui`
- Default: off
- Enabled for: internal dogfood tenant only (handled via INT-912 / config rollout)

## UX highlights
- Results header: Experiment name, route, control target, shadow target(s), sampling %, rubric version, data retention indicator
- Metric cards: e.g. `format_adherence_rate`, `refusal_rate`, `instruction_following_score_mean`, `safety_policy_violation_rate`
- Chart behavior:
  - Shows control and candidate series + delta band view toggle
  - Confidence band computed server-side; UI simply renders (no client stats)
  - Tooltips show sample size (n), window, and whether samples are shadow-sampled vs prompt-set
- Segment filters (cardinality-safe): `region`, `request_type`, `model_variant`, `status_class` (2xx/4xx/5xx), `token_bucket` (bucketed)
  - Explicitly *not* supported in UI: `prompt_id`, `customer_id`, raw `route_id` free text (route is chosen from context)

## API wiring
- GET `/console/v1/shadow-experiments/:id/aggregates?window=1h&range=24h&segment=region`
- GET `/console/v1/shadow-experiments/:id/examples?metric=format_adherence_rate&outcome=regression&limit=50&cursor=...`
- Error/empty states:
  - If scoring lag or no data: show "Waiting for scoring" with link to troubleshooting docs (internal)
  - If RBAC denies `shadow:read_examples`: hide examples tab and show callout

## Implementation details
- Adds `ShadowExperimentResultsPage` route + navigation entry under Observability → Shadow Experiments
- New components:
  - `QualityDeltaChart` (line + band)
  - `MetricDeltaCard` (delta, CI, sample size)
  - `SegmentFilterBar` (safe enum dims only)
  - `ScoredExampleDrawer` (prompt/response + rubric breakdown)
- Uses existing design system primitives (Panels, Callouts, Tables, Skeleton loaders)
- Maintains strict PII posture:
  - UI never renders raw prompt/response unless backend returns redacted text (expected)
  - Displays explicit "Redacted" markers when fields omitted

## Tests
- Unit tests:
  - chart toggle behavior (series vs delta)
  - segment filter param mapping + resets
  - flag gating renders placeholder when off
- Playwright:
  - loads results page, applies time range + segment, opens example drawer

## Screenshots (internal)
- Results overview: https://console-staging.redwood.internal/screens/24947-overview
- Segment breakdown: https://console-staging.redwood.internal/screens/24947-segments
- Example drawer: https://console-staging.redwood.internal/screens/24947-example

## Rollout plan
1) Merge behind flag (this PR)
2) Enable for internal tenant only (ENG-5416)
3) Enable for 2 Dedicated beta customers after SRE signoff on scoring lag dashboards (ENG-5409)

## Checklist
- [x] Feature flag gating added
- [x] RBAC checked before showing example drilldowns
- [x] Empty/scoring-lag states
- [x] Segment dimensions constrained to allowlist
- [x] Basic Playwright coverage

## Related
- Backend APIs: PR #24933
- Dashboards: observability-pack PR #391
- ADRs: adr-shadow-metrics-data-model-and-cardinality, quality-metrics-observability-standard

---

2. console: implement quality delta chart + metric cards

4. console: add scored examples table + drawer (RBAC gated)

### CI

### Review conversation (highlights)
Kenji Nakamura (requested changes): "Chart density is a bit high; can we default to 24h and keep 7d behind a secondary selector? Also the CI band needs a lighter tint to match the rest of the Console charts."

Dylan Brooks (author): "Updated defaults to 24h and moved 7d/30d into the time-range dropdown. Adjusted band opacity to 12% and used the `--chart-band` token. Pushed in 5f7c3b1."

Motivation: provide a compact, reproducible developer onboarding path for teams building retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) features that need both an interactive iteration surface and a minimal webhook adapter for tool-calling integration. Checklist: - [x] interactive shell prototype with replayable session recording - [x] webhook adapter with auth stub and structured tool-call contract - [x] example prompts and sample index (small synthetic corpus) - [x] docs site quickstart page and end-to-end walkthrough - [x] CI smoke tests and playground e2e smoke script Changes summary: adds a new quickstart under examples/rag-dev-shell and a webhook adapter under examples/rag-webhook-adapter, updates docs/quickstarts to include a walkthrough and adds a small set of telemetry probes in examples/common/telemetry. The interactive shell supports stepwise replay, streaming mock responses for token-by-token debugging and a --seeded mode for deterministic evals. The webhook adapter implements a minimal tool contract with JSON schema and includes a simulated external connector for calendar lookup and HTTP fetch tools. Commits: - Add initial rag-dev-shell prototype with TS CLI, replay recorder and example corpus - Wire up rag-webhook-adapter express scaffold, tool contract and auth stub - Docs: add quickstart guide, architecture diagram and troubleshooting notes - Tests: add smoke e2e script and CI pipeline job description Files changed (high level): - examples/rag-dev-shell/cli.ts - examples/rag-dev-shell/README.md - examples/rag-dev-shell/sample-index/*.json - examples/rag-webhook-adapter/server.js - examples/rag-webhook-adapter/tool-contracts/schema.json - examples/common/telemetry/probes.ts - docs/quickstarts/rag-dev-shell.md - .github/workflows/rag-dev-shell-smoke.yml CI notes: a new CI job (rag-dev-shell-smoke) was added to run the shell in a headless mode and exercise the webhook adapter; initial run surfaced a flaky network stub causing one rerun, resolved by adding a deterministic mock and a 2s backoff in the adapter. Motivation: Dedicated fleets see sudden, short-lived tenant spikes that existing synchronous autoscalers either overprovision for or respond too slowly. This PR introduces a new asynchronous, tiered autoscaler that separates long-running reservation decisions from short-term burst smoothing. It decouples the reservation ledger into a lightweight in-memory reservoir that can be tuned independently of the backing persistent commitments, reducing lock contention and improving decision latency.

What this PR does: Adds an AsyncTieredAutoscaler controller that runs two independent decision loops: (1) a slow, commitment allocator that manages backing reservations (commit window sizing, graceful decommit) and (2) a fast reservoir reconciler which issues ephemeral burst credits from a local in-memory pool. The reservoir uses a leaky-bucket estimator augmented with a time-weighted utilization drift reporter to smooth microbursts while preserving per-tenant throughput guarantees.

Key features and rationale: - Decoupled reservation reservoir: local, lock-free allocation to satisfy short bursts without writing to the central ledger for every microburst. Backing reservations are reconciled asynchronously to reduce high-frequency contention. - Tiered decision loops: slow loop handles policy-driven commitments and safety windows; fast loop serves immediate capacity requests and enforces short-term fairness. - Throughput guarantees: per-tenant SLA enforcement remains anchored to the backing commitments. The reservoir grants are conservative and honor minimum throughput floors. - Burst smoothing: leaky-bucket + exponential decay estimator reduces noisy oscillations when many tenants spike simultaneously. - Utilization telemetry exporter: new metrics for reservoir_fill_ratio, reservoir_drain_rate, drifted_utilization_percentile and commit_reconcile_lag to help SREs tune policies. - Fallback semantics: when the reservoir is exhausted, requests fall back to the legacy AdmissionController path which applies existing throttles and queued admission. This preserves graceful degradation. - Configuration: introduces a new AutoscalerPolicy CRD fields (asyncReservoirEnabled, reservoirSizeFraction, fastLoopIntervalMs, slowLoopIntervalSec, driftDecayAlpha) with sane defaults and per-tenant overrides.

Migration notes: Existing clusters will continue using the legacy synchronous autoscaler by default. Enabling the async tiered autoscaler is a feature-flagged rollout. We provide a migration tool (scripts/migration/commit-to-reservoir.sh) that safely seeds reservoirs from current commitments for canary pools.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for reservoir accounting and fast-loop invariants, integration tests in perf-canary harness simulating 1k tenants with randomized burst patterns, and cluster soak test on staging for 72 hours. Load tests show 32% reduction in commit-write rate under microburst workload and 12% lower 95th percentile tail latency for admission decisions.

Related: builds on earlier work for warm pools and tokenized burst banking but follows a different approach by avoiding synchronous ledger writes on microbursts. References: Linear ENG-4219, SUP-1132 (support incident that motivated quick response path).
init: add AsyncTieredAutoscaler controller skeleton; impl: reservoir allocator and leaky-bucket estimator; config: AutoscalerPolicy CRD fields and defaults; telemetry: add reservoir metrics and prometheus exporters; tests: unit tests for accounting and fast-loop; docs: design notes and migration guide; ci: pipeline changes for integration harness
Miguel: 'Can we bound the reservoir memory growth per pool? Also ensure we don't starve slow steady tenants.' Author (Asha): 'Added reservoirSizeFraction and per-pool caps, and ensured fast-loop honors minThroughputFloors by checking backing commitments before granting ephemeral credits.' Sven: 'Need clearer observability on reconcile lag and a dashboard suggestion.' Author: 'Added three new metrics and a Grafana dashboard draft in docs.' Lina: 'Unit tests look good but add a regression test that simulates ledger write failures.' Author: 'Added integration scenario that injects persistent store errors and verifies fallback semantics.' Miguel: 'Approve after CI passes.'
Introduce Async Tiered Autoscaler (opt-in). Adds per-pool in-memory reservoir for burst smoothing, new AutoscalerPolicy fields, and several reservoir/commit telemetry metrics. Defaults keep legacy autoscaler behavior unless enabled. See docs/autoscaler/async-tiered-design.md for tuning guidance.
Unit: 84 tests covering allocator invariants and accounting. Integration: perf-canary scenario with 1k tenants and stochastic bursts (72h soak). Regression: simulate datastore write failures and ensure fallback path preserves SLAs. Results: commit write rate -32%, admission decision p95 latency -12% under microburst load.
New metrics to watch: autoscaler_reservoir_fill_ratio{pool}, autoscaler_reservoir_drain_rate{pool}, autoscaler_commit_reconcile_lag_seconds. If reconcile_lag grows >5s, reduce reservoirSizeFraction or increase slowLoopIntervalSec. Grafana dashboard draft is in docs/.
1) Add cross-cluster reservoir synchronization prototype (ENG-4321). 2) Explore adaptive reservoir sizing driven by observed drift percentiles. 3) Add canary release automation to roll feature-flag per-pool.

Context and motivation: We have an increasing number of RBACv2 rule variants and per-tenant KMS residency constraints which are difficult to evaluate consistently in multiple runtimes. This PR adds an OPA-based policy bridge that centralizes policy evaluation for RBACv2 and emits structured metering events for KMS usage. The bridge is implemented as a light-weight policy server library that can be linked into the runtime or deployed as a sidecar; it supports Rego templates for common tenancy patterns and a small runtime cache to avoid repeated expensive evaluations.

What this PR does (single-string description with checklist): 1) Adds pkg/policy/opa_bridge.go: OPA client wrapper + evaluation API. 2) Adds Rego templates under policies/templates/ for tenant-scoped role assertions and kms-consent rules. 3) Adds internal/kms/meter.go and middleware to produce per-request KMS-meter events (tenant, key, op, region) and emit audit payloads. 4) Introduces evaluation metrics (pkg/policy/eval_metrics.go) for latency, cache hit rate, and policy size. 5) Adds integration test coverage and an example in examples/opa/. 6) Adds docs and a migration guide for policy authors and infra teams. 7) Helm values for enabling the bridge in the rbac-policy-bundle chart.

Checklist: [x] design doc referenced (ENG-2413), [x] unit tests added, [x] integration test for KMS metering added, [x] docs and migration guide, [x] observability and SLI hooks, [x] rollback plan included.

Commits (high level): 7 commits: initial OPA client and shim; add Rego templates and policy examples; implement KMS metering middleware; metrics and cache; integration tests; docs and helm chart values; fix flaky test and CI tweaks.

Changed areas and rationale: - Policy evaluation: centralizing via OPA reduces drift between services that previously had ad-hoc evaluation code. Rego templates make it easier for compliance to express residency rules. - KMS metering: a standardized meter makes it possible to attribute KMS calls to tenants and regions for audit and billing. - Performance: evaluation cache and short-lived partial-result cache were introduced to keep average eval latency < 2ms for common fast-paths. Benchmarks included in the PR show a cold-eval median of ~8ms on a single x86 dev box and warm-eval median ~0.9ms with cache enabled.

Footnotes on security controls and compliance: The bridge validates that Rego policies include explicit residency assertions when required by feature gates. Policy templates include deny-by-default principals for cross-region key usage. Audit events from the KMS meter are signed and contain an immutable policy_fingerprint field for post-hoc verification.

Staged rollout and migration: We will deploy the bridge as a sidecar behind a feature flag (rbac.opa_bridge.enabled) and progressively flip canaries: dev -> staging (50%) -> production (10% subset with low QPS) -> full rollout over 7 days. Migration guide in docs/rbac/migration-guide.md explains how to translate legacy role bindings to the Rego helpers and how to validate equivalence with the back-compat shim.

Testing and CI notes: Integration tests initially failed in CI due to a mocked KMS stub mismatch; the test harness was updated and the failing check was rerun (integration-kms: rerun passed). Load bench scripts are in tests/bench/ and were used to verify eval latency and cache behavior.

Rollback plan: Feature flag can be toggled off; the sidecar is backward compatible and falls back to legacy evaluation code on severe errors. If KMS-metering emits malformed events, a short-lived kill-switch (rbac.kms_meter.disabled) prevents emissions while preserving decision flows.

Related work and references: ENG-2413 (design), SEC-78 (compliance review), earlier policy bundle PRs for residency enforcement.

7 commits: add OPA bridge, Rego templates, KMS-meter middleware, metrics, integration tests, docs, CI fixes
Rohit Singh: Overall looks good. Please add a microbenchmark for evaluation cache hit-rate and include p95 numbers (requested change).
Ava Martinez: Added bench script and p95 numbers to eval_metrics.go comments and to the docs. See tests/bench/benchmark_eval.sh (reply).
Marie Chen: How do we ensure policy templates cannot introduce accidental allow rules for cross-region KMS usage? Suggest explicit deny-with-audit for unknown regions.
Ava Martinez: Rego templates now include a default deny-and-audit clause; added a new audit field policy_fingerprint for traceability (reply).
Diego Alvarez: Integration test failed in CI initially due to stub mismatch; re-ran and passed. Approving after green CI.
Rohit Singh: Approve. Left a minor nits comment about log level for policy failures.
Ava Martinez: Addressed nit, now using warn for transient OPA client errors and error for evaluation failures tied to deny decisions.
Unit tests: make test ./pkg/policy and ./internal/kms
Integration: make test-integration (requires local KMS stub)
Bench: tests/bench/benchmark_eval.sh to reproduce eval latency numbers
Manual: enable rbac.opa_bridge.enabled in staging values and verify policy_fingerprint appears in audit events
Adds OPA-based policy bridge for RBACv2 and standardized KMS-usage metering. Provides Rego templates to express tenant-scoped residency rules and denials for cross-region KMS usage. Opt-in via helm flag rbac.opa_bridge.enabled. Backwards compatible with legacy evaluation shims.
Enable feature flag in helm values and monitor new metrics policy.eval.latency, policy.cache.hit_ratio, rbac.kms_meter.events_emitted. Watch for integration-kms errors during the first 24h of rollout. Can toggle rbac.opa_bridge.enabled=false to rollback.

Context: Several tenants reported bursty traffic that caused head-of-line blocking in the continuous batching queue and unpredictable unit costs during surge windows. Independent investigation (ENG-8934) showed that aggressive batching plus cold KV cache misses amplified token cost during short spikes. Motivation: provide an automated runtime layer that (1) enforces tenant throughput targets to avoid catastrophic batch growth, (2) nudges cache prioritization for warmup-sensitive workloads, and (3) supplies a small CLI tool to produce tenant-specific quantization whitelists and compact quant profiles that respect quality budgets. This PR implements 'Throughput Conservator' (runtime controller) and a paired operator CLI 'quant-wrangler' (costctl subcommand) to generate safe quantization/priority defaults for tenants. Solution summary: - Runtime: introduce conservator module (infra/prefill/conservator.go) that observes request latency distribution and per-tenant unit-econ signals and applies a soft throttle that reshapes batch composition. Conservator exposes a small policy DSL (conservator.yaml) with: max_batch_growth, warmup_priority, and prefill_window_hint. It integrates with the existing batch allocator and KV cache scorer. - Cost tooling (CLI): add costctl quant-wrangler subcommand that: 1) ingests recent request traces and a small eval-set, 2) runs compact quant experiments (min-q -> high-q) with simulated unit-econ scoring, 3) emits a tenant-anchored whitelist.json (models + allowed quant levels) and a compact-profile.tar.gz for safe rollout. CLI supports --dry-run and --apply flags. - Defaults & rollout: provide a conservative defaults file shipped with the runtime (docs defaults/careful-presets.md) so newly onboarded tenants get a safe policy. The conservator will only enforce soft throttles for tenants above threshold (configurable). - Observability: add two new metrics: redwood.conservator.throttle_ratio and redwood.quantwrangler.safety_score and hooks for per-tenant unit_econ traces to appear in Console dashboards. - Tests: unit tests for conservator logic, integration smoke for CLI end-to-end local simulation, and a small load test that validates cost per token does not spike beyond configured SLAs. Commits: - "initial: conservator runtime scaffold + policy parsing" - "batch allocator hook and KV scorer integration" - "quant-wrangler CLI prototype + golden eval-set" - "e2e tests and telemetry + docs" Changed files (high level): - infra/prefill/conservator.go: new runtime controller integrating with allocator (approx 420 LOC). - cli/costctl/quant_wrangler.go: adds costctl subcommand with dry-run and apply flags. - defaults/conservator_presets.yaml: conservative policy shipped by default. - docs/cost-automation/throughput-conservator.md: user-facing guide and rollout instructions. - tests/prefill/conservator_test.go: unit tests covering throttle heuristics. - examples/quant-wrangler/sample_whitelist.json: sample output produced by CLI. Small code snippet (conservator decision heuristics): "if tenant.throttle_ratio > policy.max_batch_growth && unit_econ.delta > policy.cost_threshold { apply_soft_throttle(tenant, policy) }" Rollout plan: - Feature flagged behind runtime flag conserve_throughput (default off). - Gradual canary: enable 1% tenants -> 10% -> 50% with telemetry gating (look for no >10% regression in p95 latency and unit-econ). - CLI is opt-in; admin must run quant-wrangler and review whitelist before apply. Testing and results: - Local synthetic load: median token cost reduced 8% for spike-heavy workloads with negligible latency increase (+3ms median). - E2E staging: conservator reduced batch size variance by ~42% across synthetic surges. - CLI dry-run produced conservative whitelists that kept eval BLEU loss < 0.8% for most evaluated models. Risk & safety: - Conservative defaults and dry-run flow reduce blast radius. - Conservator uses soft throttles and falls back to policy-free routing if telemetry is missing. - Quant-wrangler includes a rollback marker in generated artifacts and integrates with rollouts/a-b. Related work: this PR builds on ideas from ENG-9021 (unit-econ instrumenter) and earlier prefill work (prefill heuristics). Links: Linear ENG-8934, ENG-9021, Support ticket SUP-7812. Merge notes: squashed commits and added final changelog entry.
Ben Fletcher (reviewer): Nice end-to-end. Can we avoid global locks in the conservator path? Looks like conservator.go uses a per-shard mutex but some calls still hit a global registry.
Ayesha Khan (author): Good catch. I refactored the registry access to use per-tenant shard maps and a RCU-style swap for policy updates. Updated in commit 3.
Marisol Ortega (reviewer): The CLI output should include a safety_score and the eval-set used. Also add a note about encryption of the whitelist when stored in S3.
Ayesha Khan (author): Added safety_score export and appended metadata to the artifact. Documented S3 encryption recommendation in docs.
Introduce Throughput Conservator: soft tenant throttling to stabilise batching during surges.
Add quant-wrangler CLI: generate tenant-safe quant whitelists and compact quant profiles.
New defaults and observability metrics for conservative rollout and cost telemetry.
Feature gated behind conserve_throughput runtime flag.
Ops: recommend enabling on a small percentage of tenants first and monitoring redwood.conservator.throttle_ratio and unit_econ.* metrics.
Follow-up: add UI in Console to visualize whitelist differences and to preview safety_score per tenant (tracked ENG-9145).

Motivation: oncall responders are overloaded with noisy context during incidents and often lack a safe, automated way to exercise likely failure modes against live stacks for faster triage. This PR introduces two coordinated features: a compact oncall context condenser that produces a sanitized, prioritized brief for the active responder, and an Active Failure Prober: a controlled synthetic probe runner that executes low-impact health checks and dependency sanity tests with safety gates and dry-run modes. Goals: 1) reduce time-to-first-action by surfacing the highest-confidence context and remediation hints; 2) enable safe, automated probes that can validate hypotheses without escalating blast radius; 3) provide observability hooks so every probe is tied to an incident ID and reversible. Changes include: new condenser engine (pkg/condenser) using weighted telemetry heuristics + fuzzy dedupe; probe orchestrator (pkg/prober) with policy-driven safety checks, rate limits, and canary targets; Slack and PagerDuty response templates that include condensed brief and probe runbook links; CLI extension for ops to trigger dry-run probes locally; integration tests and a small e2e harness. Checklist: - [x] condenser core implemented and unit tested - [x] prober orchestrator with safety policy engine and timeouts - [x] Slack responder attachment and brief link - [x] dry-run CLI mode and documentation - [x] CI tests and small-scale e2e simulation - [x] security review for K8s exec and network probes How this is intended to be used: incident-bot will append a condensed brief to the incident thread when an alert is created or on-demand via /brief; responders can optionally trigger the Active Failure Prober using the brief UI which runs only allowed probes (as configured per team) and returns structured results in the thread. Safety model: by default probes are dry-run and only run active checks if the incident severity is P0 and an approver label is present; all probes are logged, reversible where possible, and can be disabled via feature flags. Related work: builds on ENG-2156 (telemetry prioritization) and the prior incident-bot snapshotter PRs. Rollout plan: feature gated behind incident-bot.feature.condenser and prober feature flags with a controlled 10% rollout to SRE teams, monitor error-budget impact and false-positive probe runs for 2 weeks, then expand.
Aisha: Please add a clearer opt-out mechanism for teams that don’t want probes enabled. Reply: Added team-level feature flag and CLI opt-out flag.
Marco: The policy engine needs a max-duration safeguard per probe. Reply: Added per-probe timeout and global orchestrator hard cap.
Riley: Can we avoid storing sensitive telemetry in condensed briefs? Reply: Condenser now runs a sanitizer and redaction pass and records only abstracted hints.
Added oncall context condenser to produce concise incident briefs and an Active Failure Prober for safe, policy-driven synthetic checks. Feature behind flags with limited SRE canary. See docs/runbooks/oncall_condenser_and_prober.md for usage and security considerations.

Motivation: Private deployments require a reproducible, least-privilege bootstrap path that works for both cloud VPC and on-prem clusters and can survive installer upgrades and rollbacks. Current manual seeding leads to drift (duplicate RoleBindings, stale bootstrap secrets) and causes permission errors during automated upgrades. This PR introduces an idempotent tenant RBAC seeding flow that is safe to run multiple times and integrates with the installer Helm chart and Terraform modules used by the private deployment flow.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a new Terraform module (modules/tenant-bootstrap) that performs server-side apply via kubectl provider to create Namespaces, Roles, ClusterRoles, and RoleBindings required for tenant isolation. The module exposes a single variable `bootstrap_token_kms_key` to ensure the bootstrap secret can be KMS-wrapped for air-gapped/on-prem HSM setups.
- Updates the private-installer Helm chart to include a pre-install and post-upgrade hook (`templates/hooks/tenant-seed-hook.yaml`) that calls the tenant-bootstrap job. Hooks are implemented as a Job that runs `rbac-seed` container image (small Go binary) which reconciles desired RBAC objects using server-side apply and ownerReferences to ensure idempotency. Hooks are marked with `helm.sh/hook-weight` and `helm.sh/hook-delete-policy` so failed installs can be retried cleanly.
- Adds a `rbac-seed` controller image and job manifest that supports a dry-run mode and emits structured logs for tracing in the Console. The binary checks for pre-existing objects and only creates or updates when necessary; it is tolerant of transient API errors and retries with backoff.
- Terraform test coverage: integration test workspace (tests/terraform/tenant-bootstrap) that runs `terraform apply` against a KinD cluster in CI, verifies RoleBindings, and asserts that re-applying the module is a no-op (no additional diffs).
- Rollback support: the Helm hook records a stable ConfigMap checksum and the seed job sets ownerReferences so that when a release is rolled back the old RBAC objects are retained only if still referenced. We also add a lightweight cleanup job (templates/cleanup-hook.yaml) that runs on `post-delete` for releases that opt-in via values.x.cleanupOnDelete = true.
- Security: bootstrap token secret is created as a Kubernetes Secret with annotations linking to the KMS key; secret is short-lived by default (72h) and a rotation job is optionally installed by the Terraform module for managed setups.

Why this is different from prior work: existing RBAC bootstrap PRs focused on static role templates. This change introduces an orchestrated, idempotent seeding flow wired into both Terraform and Helm, supports KMS-backed secrets for Private, and explicitly handles upgrade/rollback semantics so CI/topology changes don't cause permission regressions.

Files changed (high level):
- modules/tenant-bootstrap/main.tf (new) - Terraform module implementing server-side apply and secret creation
- helm/private-installer/templates/hooks/tenant-seed-hook.yaml (new) - pre-install/post-upgrade hook Job
- helm/private-installer/templates/hooks/cleanup-hook.yaml (new) - optional post-delete cleanup Job
- images/rbac-seed/main.go (new) - small reconciler binary with server-side apply logic
- images/rbac-seed/Dockerfile (new)
- tests/terraform/tenant-bootstrap/ (new integration test workspace)
- docs/private/rbac-bootstrap.md (new) - operator-facing doc and manual troubleshooting steps

Minimal illustrative snippet (from rbac-seed reconciliation logic):
`kubectl apply --server-side -f <generated-yaml> --field-manager=rbac-seed`

Testing and CI:
- Added unit tests for the Go binary using fake clients and an integration Terraform test against KinD that runs in the `rbac-e2e` workflow.
- CI: initial runs showed intermittent KinD network flakiness (failing test `TestTerraformApply`) which we fixed by adding an exponential backoff and increasing KinD network readiness timeout. Current CI status: pass.

Upgrade plan / rollouts:
- Release the Terraform module as v0.1.0 in the private-installer chart repo.
- For existing customers we will ship a one-off runbook to create the bootstrap secret with their KMS key and run the terraform module in `plan` mode before applying.

Manual verification steps (for reviewers / SRE):
1) Deploy Helm chart with `values.rbac.enable=true` and `values.cleanupOnDelete=false` to a KinD cluster.
2) Confirm Job runs and exits 0, check the `rbac-seed` logs for `reconcile complete`.
3) Re-run `helm upgrade` (no changes) and assert that `rbac-seed` job is a no-op (log: `no changes`).
4) Inspect created Roles and RoleBindings to ensure they have the expected ownerReferences and KMS annotations on secrets.

Related: references ENG-2145 for the original design doc, SEC-108 for KMS secret pattern, and SUP-977 which was the support ticket motivating idempotent behavior during upgrades.

Checklist: 
- [x] Terraform module implemented and documented
- [x] Helm hooks added and tested
- [x] idempotent reconcile logic and ownerReferences implemented
- [x] CI integration test added and stabilized
- [x] Manual runbook and docs added

Notes: this change was kept conservative to avoid accidental privilege widening. The Terraform module requires an explicit `grant_admin` boolean to create any ClusterRoleBindings (default false). The `rbac-seed` binary runs as a low-privilege service account in the installer job and performs only the minimal operations defined in the module's outputs.
Ethan Zhang: request changes - use server-side apply with field-manager to avoid conflicts; also add unit tests for transient API errors.
Maya Patel: replied - switched to server-side apply and added retry/backoff unit tests (see images/rbac-seed/main.go).
Priya Rao: nit - prefer explicit annotation for KMS key on Secret; also ensure bootstrap token TTL is configurable.
Maya Patel: addressed - KMS annotation added and `bootstrap_token_ttl` exposed in module variables with default 72h.
Diego Alvarez: approved - verified Terraform no-op behavior in KinD test, CI green.
Added an idempotent tenant RBAC bootstrap flow for Private installer: new Terraform module (tenant-bootstrap), Helm pre-install/post-upgrade hooks for seeding RBAC, optional cleanup on delete, KMS-backed bootstrap secret support, and integration tests. No automatic ClusterRoleBinding creation unless `grant_admin=true`.

Adds a per-request KMS selection hook and an audit consistency checker. Backwards compatible, behind feature flag. Improves correct KMS routing for tenant-region constraints and provides stronger audit header validation and canonical audit hash chaining for dedupe and forensic integrity.
Motivation: Customers operating across multiple jurisdictions need deterministic KMS selection per-request so keys and providers respect data residency and tenant-scoped CMK constraints. In parallel, we have recurring incidents where audit headers are inconsistent after gateway routing changes; this makes cross-region deduplication and forensic reconstruction brittle. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: 1) a per-request KMS selection hook that evaluates tenant claims, requested region, and policy constraints (RBAC v2 attributes) to pick an appropriate key/provider or trigger an approved fallback, and 2) an audit consistency checker that validates incoming audit headers, normalizes provenance fields, and appends a small canonical hash chain (audit-hash) to the audit envelope to enable cross-system dedupe and tamper detection. Design: - Hook is implemented as a pluggable interceptor in the request routing layer (requests/runtime/kms_hook.go) and exposed behind feature flag security.per_request_kms. It consults the policy engine (rbac/v2 policy matcher) with a new attribute set (tenant.cmk_preference, tenant.data_residency, request.region_hint) and returns a KMS selection object (provider, key_id, provenance_token). - Audit consistency checker lives in the audit pipeline (audit/consistency_checker.go). It checks required headers (X-Audit-Tenant, X-Audit-Region, X-Audit-Origin), canonicalizes timestamp/nonce ordering, computes an incremental SHA256-based audit-hash, and writes the resulting metadata to the sealed audit envelope. - Fallbacks: if the hook cannot find a matching key subject to tenant policy, it returns a well-defined error code and optional esk (ephemeral signing key) fallback path that must be authorized by tenant policy (preventing silent cross-region key use). - RBAC v2 integration: a small policy fragment and a new policy template are added so operators can define which service principals can request cross-region key selection. A migration shim keeps existing binary policies until operators roll out the template. - Observability: added metrics (kms_selection.latency, kms_selection.hits_by_policy, audit.checksum_mismatch) and traces. - Tests: unit tests for policy matching, integration tests exercising a simulated multi-kms environment, e2e test that verifies audit envelope chain is preserved across routing and replay. Rollout plan: - Feature gated by security.per_request_kms; opt-in for Dedicated/Private tenants initially. - Canary on a small percentage of hosted traffic with runtime rollout via console. - Monitoring dashboards and alerts added for checksum_mismatch and unexpected fallback usage. Backwards compatibility: existing requests without feature flag behave identical to current code path. The audit checker is non-destructive and only appends audit-hash when all required headers present. Security review: design reviewed by security (Arjun Patel) and compliance (Leah Morgan); noted requirements for KMS provider proofs and tenant consent UI which are captured in ENG-4621 and follow-up ENG-4720. Documentation: updated operator docs and security runbook.
Arjun Patel: Strong overall. Please make sure provenance_token is constrained and cannot be forged by an upstream proxy — add signatures from the gateway's HSM.
Leah Morgan: Confirmed the audit-hash approach meets our eDiscovery retention requirements; include a config option to disable hash storage for tenants with limited retention policies.
Diego Alvarez: How does this interact with Dedicated reserved pools where local KMS is enforced? Need explicit deny in policy matcher rather than fallback.
SRE Bot: flakiness observed in integration test 'kms-selection-integration' — test sometimes times out on CI, please add deterministic timeouts and mocked providers.
Maya Chen: Added gateway HSM signature for provenance_token (see kms_hook.go lines 120-145), and added 'audit.hash_store' tenant-level flag to opt-out of persistent hash storage.
Maya Chen: Policy matcher now returns explicit DENY when tenant.enforce_local_kms == true; fallback path removed for those tenants.
Maya Chen: Increased determinism in integration tests by mocking KMS provider responses and tightening timeouts.
Squash-merged after security and SRE sign-off. Feature remains feature-flagged and gated to tenants. Operator docs and policy templates included. No backwards-incompatible API changes.
payload.title: Per-request KMS Selection Hook and Audit Consistency Checker

payload.body:
## Summary
Introduce a dedicated, least-privilege RBAC role for "release signing operators" who need to initiate and monitor offline bundle signing runs for Redwood Private releases.

This PR removes the current ad-hoc guidance of granting broad permissions in the release-tools cluster and replaces it with an explicit, reviewable policy bundle:
- New `ClusterRole` + namespace-scoped bindings for `release-signing-operator`
- Separation-of-duties: operator can create/approve signing requests and observe jobs, but cannot read signing key material (Secrets) or mutate trust roots
- Policy tests to prevent accidental wildcard RBAC in this area

Context: offline bundle signing pipeline workstream (ENG-4822) + trust store/key rotation migration (ENG-4825). This is intended to be deployed alongside the signing service rollout in the release-tools cluster.

## Motivation / background
As part of on-prem offline artifact signing, we’re introducing a signing service that produces detached signatures for offline bundles. The human/operator flow is: start a signing run, monitor status, and fetch resulting artifacts from the artifact store. Historically this has been done with elevated cluster access (sometimes effectively admin in `release-tools`), which is incompatible with our supply-chain threat model and the evidence expectations we’ve seen from air-gapped/regulated customers.

Threat model alignment:
- Reduce blast radius of compromised operator credentials
- Ensure operators cannot access private key material or modify signing configuration/trust roots
- Improve auditability: explicit role name and bindings show up cleanly in access reviews

## What changed
### New RBAC objects
- `clusters/production/release-tools/rbac/release-signing-operator.clusterrole.yaml`
- `clusters/production/release-tools/rbac/release-signing-operator.rolebinding.yaml`
- `clusters/production/release-tools/rbac/release-signing-operator.serviceaccount.yaml`

Permissions granted (high level):
- Create/update/get/list/watch `signingrequests.signing.redwood.ai` (CRD) in `release-signing` namespace
- Get/list/watch Jobs/Pods in `release-signing` namespace for run status
- Get/list Events in `release-signing` namespace
- Read ConfigMaps used for non-secret job parameters

Explicitly NOT granted:
- No `secrets` access (get/list/watch)
- No write access to ConfigMaps that define trust roots (`signing-trust-*`)
- No cluster-scoped writes beyond the specific CRD

### Removed/cleaned up
- Dropped legacy `release-operator` binding that included broad verbs over core resources in the namespace.

### Policy/CI guardrails
- Add `conftest` rules to fail on:
  - Wildcard resources/verbs in signing operator roles
  - Any Secrets access from roles matching `*signing*operator*`

## Example manifests (illustrative)
`release-signing-operator.clusterrole.yaml` (excerpt)
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: release-signing-operator
rules:
  - apiGroups: ["signing.redwood.ai"]
    resources: ["signingrequests"]
    verbs: ["create", "get", "list", "watch", "update", "patch"]
  - apiGroups: ["batch"]
    resources: ["jobs"]
    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["pods", "events", "configmaps"]
    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]

`release-signing-operator.rolebinding.yaml` (excerpt)
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: release-signing-operator
  namespace: release-signing
subjects:
  - kind: Group
    name: release-signing-operators
    apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
roleRef:

Motivation: Private deployments need an idempotent, auditable way to bootstrap tenant-scoped RBAC and generate policy bundles from Terraform during installer runs. This PR seeds a small, composable Terraform module and supporting Helm hooks so the private installer can: 1) create tenant ServiceAccounts and KMS-encrypted secrets, 2) apply namespaced Role and RoleBinding templates with unique tenant prefixes, 3) produce a policy-bundle JSON artifact that the private control plane consumes for offline audits.

What this PR changes: adds a terraform/priv-tenant-rbac module (variables + outputs + example), a helm chart hook (post-install job) that runs the policy renderer, a small go-based policy-generator used by the job, and unit/integration test scripts that run in the private-installer CI matrix. The renderer emphasizes idempotency (compare-and-patch behavior) and deterministic output for stable audits.

Checklist: - [x] Terraform module with input validation and outputs - [x] Helm post-install hook job + K8s job manifest template - [x] Policy generator binary (Go) with deterministic JSON output - [x] Integration test harness (kind) exercising tenant bootstrap and rollback - [x] Documentation and example in examples/terraform/priv-tenant-quickstart.md

Notes/constraints: this is intentionally a minimal seed to be extended by the installer team; it does not include multi-cluster sync (future work: ENG-1801). The KMS integration is pluggable (accepts an encrypted blob or plaintext secret depending on installer configuration). For high-assurance deployments the role templates are conservative (least privilege) and include opt-in flags for additional permissions.
Marco Ruiz: Please ensure the terraform module is idempotent when re-run against existing tenants. I see mergePatch logic in the generator but want a test case.
Aisha Patel: Added integration test that re-applies the module and asserts zero-diff on the generated policy bundle (see ci/integration).
Linnea Chen: KMS key rotation question: how will the installer perform secret re-encryption? Could be a follow-up ticket.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: Dedicated fleets have long-tail latency issues when multiple mid-priority tenants simultaneously issue bursty workloads that are too small to trigger warm-pool expansions but large enough to cause transient contention. Existing burst banks and warm-pool heuristics focus on peak bursts or reserved commitments; they leave a gap for midburst activity (short-lived 5–60s spikes) that increases cold-slot churn and causes p95/p99 latency regressions for affected tenants. This PR implements a "dynamic midburst slice reserver" and an associated utilization correlator to close that gap with minimal cost increase.

What this change does (single-string summary): Adds a controller that maintains soft "midburst slices" per-tenant that can be temporarily reserved for 30–90s using a decaying credit model; integrates the slice state with the fleet autoscaler so warm-pool prewarming is informed by midburst reservations; introduces a util_correlation metric to detect when midburst reservations are correlated across tenants (to avoid over-prewarming); exposes a runtime flag (feature.dynamic_midburst_reserver) and new telemetry for observability.

Design notes and algorithm summary: 1) Sliding-credit model: each tenant accrues midburst credits proportional to recent sustained throughput (30m window) and a short-term earn rate so healthy tenants can burst without immediate fleet changes. Credits decay with a half-life configurable per-pool (default 60s). 2) Soft slice reservation: when a request is assigned and the pool has transient headroom, the controller may attach a soft slice token to the tenant allowing immediate allocation of a warmlet for the duration of the slice. Slices are non-exclusive and have a configurable concurrency ceiling per-tenant to prevent monopolization. 3) Correlator: util_correlation is computed per-pool using a bounded-window cross-correlation of per-tenant instantaneous utilization to detect synchronized bursting; if correlation is high, the autoscaler biases toward warm-pool expansion instead of granting more soft slices. 4) Fallbacks: if pool-level capacity is insufficient, slices are demoted to pre-warming hints and requests fall back to the default admission path; no hard preemption of active requests is introduced.

Telemetry and observability: adds metrics (midburst.slice_grants, midburst.slice_evictions, midburst.credit_balance, midburst.util_correlation, midburst.slice_duration_seconds) and dashboards. Included tagging on existing per-tenant dashboards and new alert suggestions: sustained slice_evictions > 5/min, util_correlation > 0.6 for 3m, p95 latency growth > 15% post-rollout.

API / config surface: Dedicated pool config gains optional section "midburst": {enabled, max_slices_per_tenant, credit_half_life_seconds, correlate_threshold}. Default: disabled for legacy pools. The runtime flag allows safe canarying across 10% -> 50% -> 100% rollouts.

Implementation summary (commits): - initial controller scaffolding and CRD-free integration points with pool manager - sliding-credit state machine and in-memory windowed counter - slice lifecycle (grant, extend, revoke) and concurrency limits - util_correlation module (streaming correlation sketch) - autoscaler hook and prewarm hint pipeline - metrics/telemetry and dashboard snapshots - unit + integration test harness and sim workload for validation

Files changed (high level): services/fleet/controller/midburst_reserver.go, services/fleet/controller/midburst_credit.go, services/fleet/controller/util_correlation.go, services/fleet/autoscaler/prewarm_hints.go, services/fleet/api/pool_config.go, internal/telemetry/metrics_registry.go, observability/dashboards/midburst-overview.jsonnet, tests/integration/midburst_sim_test.go, tests/unit/midburst_credit_test.go, docs/operations/midburst.md, pkg/runtime/flags.go

Small illustrative snippet (midburst_reserver.go grant path): "if pool.HasTransientHeadroom() && tenant.CreditBalance >= sliceCost && tenant.ActiveSlices < cfg.MaxSlices { grantSlice(tenant, pool, cfg.DefaultSliceDuration) } else { recordPrewarmHint(tenant, pool) }". The implementation has been deliberately kept lock-light and relies on the pool's slot-allocator to enforce safety.

Testing and results: Using our sim harness (tests/integration/midburst_sim_test.go) we ran mixed-tenant workloads with injected synchronized midburst noise. Results on canary cluster: p95 latency for mid-priority tenants improved by 18% (baseline against current master) with a 3% increase in average warm-pool occupancy; cold-start rate for small bursts decreased 42%. The correlator prevented over-prewarming in a test where 30 tenants synchronized, reducing unwarranted node spin-ups by 28%.

Rollout plan and safety: Feature gated behind runtime flag and pool config; rollout sequence: developer canary (1 pool) -> 10% pools (gradual) -> 50% -> 100%; observability checklist: monitor midburst.slice_evictions, midburst.util_correlation, p95/p99 latency, warm-pool occupancy, provisioning events. In case of regressions, runtime flag off will immediately stop new grants and autoscaler reverts to baseline heuristics; a fast patch to revert prewarm hints path is included (hotfix branch ready).

Checklist (completed): - [x] Design doc and simulation (linked Linear ENG-4829) - [x] Unit tests for credit model - [x] Integration sim tests - [x] Telemetry and dashboard snapshots - [x] Backwards-compatible config - [x] Runtime feature flag and rollout guide - [x] Performance benchmarks on canary cluster

Open items / follow-ups: - Tune max_slices_per_tenant defaults per workload class (ENG-4991) - Add a persistent-but-ephemeral slice DB for multi-controller HA in a later change - Explore ML-based correlator for more accurate cross-tenant spike detection

Review conversation (abridged, single string): Jonas Becker: "Can you add a safety threshold that prevents granting slices if pool-level p95 latency is already degraded?" Author (Aisha): "Added a p95 check and unit tests around it in the latest commit; if pool.p95 > cfg.P95DisableThreshold we stop granting new slices." Priya Raman: "Preference is to keep the correlator cheap — let's ensure the sketch is bounded memory; also please add an integration assertion that correlation triggers autoscaler path." Author: "correlator uses a fixed-size ring buffer and streaming covariance sketch; added integration assertion and an extra sim scenario where correlation flips strategy." Marcus Lee: "CI flaked on one test initially, looks fixed after the flake guard." Reviewer approvals: Jonas Becker (approved), Priya Raman (approved), Marcus Lee (approved).

CI and merge: First CI run failed (tests/integration/midburst_sim_test flake due to timing assumptions). Fixed by replacing a timing race with an event-driven wait and updated tests (commit adds sim harness helper WaitForStableWindow). Final CI run: all checks green (unit, integration, linters, go vet, e2e smoke). Merge method: squash and merge. Change was merged to main and released behind the runtime flag for gradual rollout.

Notes on uniqueness and risk: This PR specifically targets the midburst size-class (5–60s), a gap not previously addressed by warm-pooling or burst banks. The correlator prevents system-wide prewarming when many tenants synchronize. No changes to billing or committed capacity semantics.

Contact: Aisha Malik (author) — linked Linear ENG-4829 for design, ENG-4991 for tuning; operations runbook added at docs/operations/midburst.md.
Introduce a midburst slicing/reserver controller to reduce cross-tenant tail latencies and stabilize utilization; new telemetry metrics and a rollout guarded by a runtime feature flag.
Canary metrics show p95 improvements with modest occupancy cost
Feature gated via runtime flag: feature.dynamic_midburst_reserver
Follow-up tasks tracked under ENG-4991

Motivation: onboarding teams iterate on mix-and-match retrieval+tooling patterns but often copy/paste glue code across repos. This PR adds a compact 'toolchain stitcher' example and a paired playground to demonstrate wiring multiple tool adapters (HTTP webhooks, DB lookups, schema-validated tool contracts) into an offline-first RAG session. The artifact set is intentionally small and opinionated: a TypeScript playground micro-app (browser + local dev server), a Go microservice tool-adapter (lightweight stub for simulated external APIs), an authoring README with step-by-step quickstart, and a docs site fragment that explains the pattern and telemetry knobs.

What this PR contains (high level):
- examples/rag-toolchain-stitcher/: new example workspace with an opinionated layout (src/, adapters/, fixtures/, telemetry/).
- examples/rag-toolchain-stitcher/playground-ts/: minimal React+Vite runner with local mock index and tool bindings; supports stepwise replay and deterministic seeds for e2e tests.
- examples/rag-toolchain-stitcher/tool-adapters/go-stub/: tiny Go HTTP adapter that demonstrates authenticated tool calls, backoff retry examples, and contract validation using JSON Schema.
- docs/snippets/rag-toolchain-patterns.md: short doc snippet intended for inclusion in the docs site; explains when to use stitcher pattern vs monolithic tool adapters.
- test/fixtures/*: authored prompts and small corpus used by CI smoke tests.

Checklist (manual & automated):
- [x] core quickstart README with start/stop and example commands
- [x] playground TS dev server + instructions
- [x] Go adapter with Dockerfile for Private deployment testing
- [x] unit-level smoke tests (sync e2e using local dev server)
- [x] telemetry probes (compact; opt-in via env VAR) and sample metrics emitted
- [x] docs snippet and architecture diagram (ASCII) included
- [x] license headers and CLA sign-off by author

Why unique: This PR focuses on the 'stitcher' design — a small runtime that composes independent tool adapters at runtime via a typed contract, rather than coupling tools into a single orchestrator. It surfaces practical tradeoffs: caching boundary placement, auth propagation, request routing by policy, and replay determinism for authoring/eval. The playground emphasizes reproducible authoring (seeded runs & step replay) so teams can write regression tests for prompt/tool interactions.

Risks & mitigations: The Go adapter is intentionally non-production (no DB). I added explicit README warnings and an example Docker Compose service that runs the adapter behind a simulated gateway. Telemetry is opt-in and disabled by default. The sample keys are ephemeral and documented.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: Customers operating under jurisdictional controls asked for stronger, auditable guarantees that (1) requests that claim a region-bound residency are actually served with region-anchored CMKs, (2) operator principles cannot bypass tenant-scoped RBAC policies, and (3) audit trails contain verifiable cryptographic markers tying requests to KMS commitments. This PR implements three coordinated pieces: (A) a lightweight Policy Contracts DSL and compiler that lets product and compliance own high-level contracts (e.g., "Tenant must use CMK in eu-west-1 for classification=restricted") and compiles into RBACv2 assertions and enforcer rules; (B) a KMS Commitment Ledger service that records authoritative, append-only KMS assignment decisions per request (signed by the enforcer) and surfaces a compact proof token that is attached to audit events; (C) a Residency Gate enforcement shim that runs in the mux layer to block/redirect requests that violate region pin constraints and surface clear error codes for callers. Implementation summary: - New package rbac-policy-bundle/policy_contracts: DSL spec (YAML first-class), compiler, and unit tests; includes example contracts for tenant residency, operator-scoped denylists, and service-level allowances. - Enforcer integration: authz/enforcer now consumes compiled policy contracts at startup (and supports runtime refresh). When the enforcer binds a KMS choice to a request it issues a KMS Commitment entry (ledger client) and returns a compact commitment token (base64url) which is attached to the request context. - Commitment ledger: services/commitment-ledger introduces a small append-only service with a signing key (rotatable via KMS). Entries include request_id, chosen_kms_key_id, region, policy_contract_id, signer_kid, and signature. Ledger exposes a read-only API for auditors and an expiry-based retention policy configured per-tenant. - Audit enrichment: audit/forwarder picks up commitment tokens and expands them into commitment metadata (last 8 chars of signer_kid, region, contract id hash) while preserving the original event. Enriched audit records pass through existing pipelines unchanged for consumers that don't need the extra fields. - Residency Gate: ingress/mux/residency_gate implements a fast path check for region assertions and KMS compatibility matrix. Failing checks return 403 with an explicit policy_violation code and a link to remediation docs. - Migration & rollout: feature flag rbac_policy_contracts.enabled with staged rollout; sticky migration script migrates a small cohort of tenants to the new enforcement path; compatibility shim ensures legacy bindings still resolve to prior KMS routing if the tenant is not migrated. Commits (high-level): - add(policy_contracts): DSL + compiler + examples - feat(enforcer): runtime contract loader + ledger client - feat(ledger): append-only commitment store + signer integration - feat(audit): enrich forwarder with commitment tokens - feat(mux): residency gate enforcement + error codes - docs: operator migration guide + consumer audit docs - tests: unit + integration + one flake-fix commit Tests and CI: - Unit test coverage added for DSL compiler, ledger signing and verification, and residency gate logic. - Integration tests include a simulated tenant migration with an in-memory ledger. - CI matrix: linux/amd64 unit, integration:e2e, lint, go-sec-scan. One flaky test (audit/forwarder TestBatchFlush) was fixed by replacing time.Sleep with a condition variable; CI green on rerun. Files changed (high-level): - rbac-policy-bundle/policy_contracts/{spec.md,schema.yaml,compiler.go,compiler_test.go,examples/tenant_residency.yaml} - authz/enforcer/{loader.go,binding_resolver.go,ledger_client.go} - services/commitment-ledger/{server.go,store.go,signer.go,api.md} - audit/forwarder/{enricher.go,enricher_test.go} - ingress/mux/{residency_gate.go,residency_gate_test.go} - docs/compliance/policy-contracts.md - installer/migrations/{migrate_policy_contracts.go} - charts/rbac-policy-bundle/values.yaml (feature flag) Review and feedback (selected): - Priya Rao (reviewer): "Can we avoid storing full key material in the ledger? auditors only need key id and region plus signed assertion." Author reply: "We only store key id + region + signed assertion; comments updated to clarify and added storage schema test." - Marta Alvarez: "We need explicit TTL and retention config per tenant for privacy/legal requests." Author reply: "Added tenant_retention_days in ledger config; added a migration that backfills TTL for existing tenants in the cohort." - Liam O'Connell: "How do we ensure operator-scoped roles can't escalate via policy contracts?" Author reply: "Policy contracts compile into RBACv2 constraints that are enforced in the PDP; operator roles are evaluated with a deny-first merge. Added unit tests covering operator override attempts." - Security review note (from sec-eng): "Signer key rotation must be audited; document added and rotation integrated into KMS provisioning flow." Author reply: "Rotation docs and a rotation e2e added; ledger exposes signer metadata in /v1/status." Billing/usage & telemetry: - Added metrics: policy_contracts.compiled, ledger.append.success, ledger.append.fail, residency_gate.denied, residency_gate.allowed. - Added trace spans for ledger-sign and commitment-attach with sampling tag policy_contract=true. Migration plan (operator-facing): - Phase 0: feature flag off. - Phase 1: enable read-only contract compilation and dry-run logging for 1% tenants. - Phase 2: enable enforcement for a small cohort; monitor metric residency_gate.denied and audit enrichment volume. - Phase 3: expand to 50% then 100% and deprecate legacy shim. Backout plan included. Observability: dashboards added in docs/dashboards/policy_contracts.json and alert policy: residency_gate.denied_rate > 0.1% sustained triggers P1. Security and compliance considerations: - Ledger entries are signed; access to ledger read API is restricted to compliance personas; retention configurable per-tenant; access logs forwarded to audit pipeline. - No plaintext key material stored. - Contract DSL reviewed for injection/resolution attack surfaces; compiler sandboxed. Docs and operator guide: - docs/compliance/policy-contracts.md with example workflows and remediation steps. - docs/upgrade/migration_steps.md with CLI helpers. Merge and rollout: - Merged via squash and merge after approvals. Merge commit: "Introduce policy contracts, commitment ledger, and residency gate (squash)". Notes and follow-ups: - Follow-up tasks added: ENG-8810 (policy-explain endpoint), SEC-345 (attestation of ledger signer), PM-402 enable customer-facing contract templates. - Suggested future work: compact zk-friendly proof for commitments; further KMS multi-provider cross-checks. Overall impact: This change centralizes compliance guardrails into an auditable, reviewable contract model that ties RBACv2 assertions to KMS choices and audit entries. It provides a clear, staged migration path and operator-facing controls required for region-pin and residency SLAs.
Introduces Policy Contracts DSL, a KMS Commitment Ledger for auditable per-request key provenance, and a Residency Gate to enforce region-pinned KMS usage. Backward-compatible rollout with feature flag and staged migration. See docs for operator steps.
