Summary: This PR adds first-class “Security Snippets” support to Internal Admin so we can centrally manage approved FAQ/RFP text blocks (and their versions) that Sales/SE tooling consumes. This is part of the Enterprise Security Enablement Kit refresh: we’ve had repeated drift between Drive/Confluence snippets, HubSpot templates, and ad-hoc copy/paste. The goal is a single source of truth with clear ownership, review metadata, and safe distribution semantics (no restricted evidence in snippets). Motivation / context: Enterprise security reviews are gating Dedicated/Private deals; field teams need fast, consistent answers without over-claiming. Today, approved language lives across Confluence + Drive and gets copied into various tools. This introduces: (1) a canonical snippet store; (2) an API for downstream consumption; (3) RBAC + audit log events for changes; (4) explicit versioning + “last reviewed” metadata to align with enablement kit governance. Scope (what’s included): - New snippet domain model + persistence: `security_snippets` table (Postgres) with: `key` (stable identifier), `title`, `category`, `deployment_modes` (Hosted/Dedicated/Private flags stored as text), `content_markdown`, `status` (draft|in_review|approved|deprecated), `version`, `last_reviewed_at`, `expires_at` (optional), `owner` (team/alias), `approver` (name), and `notes_internal` (e.g., references to evidence request playbook). - Versioning semantics: update creates a new version row (immutable content by version). “Approved” is per-version; deprecating a version does not delete it. - Internal Admin UI: new “Security & Compliance → Snippets” page with: list + filters (category, status, deployment mode), diff viewer between versions, and an “export” view (raw markdown or plaintext) for downstream tools. - Public/consumption API (internal): `GET /internal/snippets/security?status=approved` and `GET /internal/snippets/security/{key}`. The API returns only non-restricted fields; explicitly excludes `notes_internal` and any future evidence references. - Permissions: gated behind Internal Admin RBAC permission `admin.security_snippets.write` (write) and `admin.security_snippets.read` (read). Default: read for Sales Ops + Solutions Eng; write limited to Security/GRC + Product Security PM. (See reviewers’ notes below re: default grants.) - Audit logging: emits `security.snippet.created`, `security.snippet.updated`, `security.snippet.status_changed` with actor, snippet key, version, and timestamp. These show up in existing audit log pipelines for internal systems. - Seeded initial snippet keys: a small curated set to validate workflow (SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC granularity, audit log retention/export, data use/no-training language, encryption in transit/at rest, SOC 2 report request steps). The exact text was copied from the working GTM draft library and then reviewed in this PR; it is not intended to be a complete library in this change. Out of scope / explicit non-goals: - No new product features or promises; no roadmap language. - No restricted compliance evidence (SOC 2 report, pen test reports, vuln scan artifacts) is stored here. Snippets may include the approved process for requesting evidence under NDA, but not the evidence itself. - No direct HubSpot/CRM integration in this PR; the first consumer is the generic response tool (tracked separately) and manual use via export. Implementation details: - Backend: `internal-admin-api` adds `SecuritySnippetService` + repository; migrations in `migrations/2026_02_07_security_snippets.sql`. - Frontend: `internal-admin-ui` adds `SecuritySnippetsPage`, `SnippetEditor` (markdown), and `VersionDiffModal`. - API response includes `content_markdown` and `content_text` (server-side stripped markdown) to reduce divergence between tools that support rich text vs plain text. - All endpoints require admin auth; responses include `etag` and support `If-None-Match` to reduce polling load for downstream tooling. Changed areas (high level): - `services/internal-admin-api/src/security_snippets/*` - `services/internal-admin-api/src/routes/internal/snippets_security.ts` - `services/internal-admin-ui/src/pages/security/SecuritySnippetsPage.tsx` - `packages/rbac/policies/internal-admin.yaml` - `packages/audit-events/src/events/security_snippets.ts` - DB migration and seeds under `services/internal-admin-api/db/*` Example snippet (illustrative, shortened): Key: `sso_saml_scim_overview` Title: “SSO (SAML) + SCIM support” Category: “Access Controls” Content (excerpt): “Redwood supports SAML 2.0 SSO for the Redwood Console and supports SCIM 2.0 for user provisioning with supported IdPs. Role-based access control (RBAC) is enforced for console actions and API keys. For details on supported IdPs and RBAC roles, see the internal capability reference. If a requirement is not currently supported, follow the Security Questionnaire Exceptions Policy.” Test plan: - Unit tests: service + repository (create, new version on update, status transitions) - API tests: auth required; status filter; ETag behavior - UI smoke test: create draft (GRC/Sec role), request review, approve, view diff - Verified audit events appear in internal audit log stream for a status change - Manual: export approved snippets as plaintext and paste into a sample RFP questionnaire section (formatting preserved reasonably) Security / compliance considerations: - RBAC gating prevents broad write access; all mutations are audited. - “No evidence stored” is enforced by process + UI copy: editor includes a warning banner and blocks uploads/attachments. - PII: none expected; we added a lint check in editor that warns (non-blocking) if content appears to include email addresses or phone numbers. Review conversation (highlights): - Marcus Lin (Security Eng): requested audit event fields include `snippet_key` + `version` and that the update path is versioned (not in-place). Addressed in commit `a8b3f2c` (adds `version` and immutability). Approved after changes. - Olga Petrov (GRC): requested stronger do-not-say guardrails and explicit “evidence request under NDA” language in SOC 2 snippet; also requested that ISO language avoids implying certification. Updated seeded snippets and added an `approved_claims_tags` field (string list stored as comma-separated text) to support future reporting; tags are not yet exposed to consumers. Approved. - Naomi Feldman (Product Security PM): requested that deployment mode filters be explicit (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and that any roadmap mention be removed from seeded audit logging snippet. Updated copy and added deployment mode UI chips. Approved. - Camila Reyes (Product Marketing): requested consistency with security messaging pillars (terminology: “Hosted API / Dedicated / Private”) and removal of ambiguous “industry standard” claims in the generic encryption snippet. Updated snippet text accordingly. Approved. - Markus Klein (Solutions Eng): requested plaintext export option and that snippets be searchable by common questionnaire phrasing (“Do you train on customer data?”, “SIEM export”, “SCIM”). Added full-text search across title/content and `keywords` field (stored as text). Approved. Context and motivation: We saw an operational gap where operator credentials could be applied across tenant geozones when debugging live workloads. This made it hard to guarantee jurisdictional guarantees for KMS-backed keys and produced noisy audit trails during compliance reviews. This PR introduces two complementary controls: 1) an operator scope lock that binds operator elevation to a geographic jurisdiction claim (region), and 2) a KMS jurisdiction handoff middleware that attaches authoritative KMS origin metadata to encryption/decryption requests used by the runtime. Together these changes reduce cross-region operator blast radius and make KMS usage auditable for residency controls.

What this changes (summary):
- services/authz/operator_lock: add operator scope lock and enforcement logic. The lock is a guarded elevation path that validates operator request scopes against the tenant's pinned region claims.
- services/kms/jurisdiction_handoff: middleware that augments KMS requests with kms_origin, kms_region and proof_token when available. Supports multi-provider handshake for cross-account CMKs.
- middleware/audit/enrichers: add region_assertion and kms_origin fields into structured audit events, persisted in the audit forwarder.
- policy/opa/rbacv2: policy templates updated to include operator_scope bindings and a feature-flag gated check (feature.rbac.operator_scope_lock).
- helm/redwood-private-installer: add config toggles and RBAC seed job for operator-scoped roles (examples and migration job).
- tests: unit + integration tests for enforcement, and a small e2e scenario in eval-harness/fixtures to validate KMS handoff headers and audit entries.

Checklist: 
- [x] Feature gate: feature.rbac.operator_scope_lock (disabled by default)
- [x] OPA policy update + unit tests
- [x] Integration tests for KMS handoff (mock KMS provider)
- [x] Audit enrichment and retention smoke tests
- [x] Helm chart toggle and installer migration job
- [x] Security review and threat model completed (SEC-77)

Commits (summary):
- 7a2f9d9 add operator scope lock implementation and unit tests
- c3b4ea2 introduce kms jurisdiction handoff middleware
- d5f6b11 update audit forwarder to include region_assertion and kms_origin fields
- e8a1bdc opa policy: operator_scope binding and gate check
- f0c9aa1 helm: installer toggle and migration job
- a9d2f77 test: e2e scenario for multi-region operator request

Files changed (high-level):
- services/authz/operator_lock.go (+372/-84)
- services/kms/jurisdiction_handoff.go (+205/-12)
- middleware/audit/enricher.go (+92/-6)
- policy/opa/rbacv2/operator_scope.rego (+64/-0)
- helm/redwood-private-installer/values.yaml (+12/-4)

- eval-harness/fixtures/e2e/operator-kms-jurisdiction.yaml (+20/-10)
- tests/integration/kms_handoff_test.go (+-- see files)

Review thread (highlights, chronological):
- Arjun Patel (reviewer): "Nice separation of concerns. Two asks: (1) add a histogram for operator-elevation attempts by region in the metrics package; (2) ensure the migration job is idempotent if run twice during installer upgrades."
- Maya Chen (author): "Added op_elevation_attempts histogram and made migration job guarded by a JobConfigMap check. Pushed fix in c3b4ea2 -> f0c9aa1."
- Elena García (reviewer): "Policy looks good. Please add a short note to docs/ops/security.md explaining how to roll back if the gate accidentally blocks needed operator flows."
- Maya Chen: "Added rollback steps and a troubleshooting subsection to docs/ops/security.md. Highlighted the feature flag and ClusterRole binding to toggle behavior."
- Samir Venkataraman (approver): "Verified integration tests locally against mock KMS. Approving pending CI green."
- CI: initial run had a lint warning for a missing comment and a flaky test (integration timing). Fixed and re-ran. Final CI status: pass.

Security and compliance notes:
- Threat model update (SEC-77) attached: reduces cross-region operator risk by binding operator tokens to a claim asserted by the API gateway and validated against tenant metadata.
- Audit trail now records authoritative kms_origin and region_assertion tags for every KMS call made through runtime; these are exported to the audit-forwarder and available in the tenant audit UI.
- KMS jurisdiction handoff supports both AWS and GCP CMKs via a provider adapter; providers must opt-in via the installer values to enable cross-account proof tokens.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (canary): enable feature.rbac.operator_scope_lock for a single non-production tenant in us-east-1, validate operator elevation metrics and audit entries for two weeks.
- Stage 2: gradually enable for internal SRE and Platform teams across two regions after running migration job.
- Stage 3: enable by default when policy is marked stable (post 4 weeks of canary without issues).

Migration considerations:
- The migration job seeds operator-scoped ClusterRoles for known operator principals. The job is guarded and idempotent; it will not remove existing roles. Operators can roll back by removing the feature flag and running the provided rollback script in docs/ops/security.md.

Merge outcome: Squash-and-merge. Commit message: "operator: introduce operator scope lock and kms jurisdiction handoff; audit enrichment (SEC-77)". PR closed and merged on 2026-02-12 after approvals from Arjun, Elena, and Samir.

Notes for future work:
- Add a runtime sidecar to provide signed region assertions for on-prem deployments that cannot reach the central gateway.

If any post-merge issues are observed (audit gaps, installer errors) please tag ENG-1029 and SEC-77 in the incident ticket so we can prioritize a hotfix.

payload.body:
Context: customers and security reviews asked for better explainability for RBACv2 decisions and stronger correlation between RBAC decisions and audit logs. This PR adds a small, opt-in RBACv2 Explainability service that returns human-friendly decision traces, an audit correlator that links policy decisions to persisted audit events for incident investigation, and a lightweight in-memory KMS consent cache to accelerate residency/consent checks during policy evaluation. Design notes: the explainability service exposes a read-only HTTP endpoint used by the Console and CLI; it consumes the same policy decision trace emitted by the PDP and performs redaction of sensitive tokens before presentation. The audit correlator hooks into the audit pipeline and attaches a stable decision_id to audit events (UUID v7) so investigators can look up the exact policy evaluation that produced a grant/deny. KMS consent cache stores short-lived consent proofs (ttl=15s by default) keyed by (tenant, kms-key-hash) and is used strictly as a fast-path for residency/kms origin checks; it is feature-flagged and falls back to online verification. Migration/compatibility: all behavior is guarded behind the feature flag rbacv2_explainability and audit_correlation enabled via operator config; customers on Dedicated/Private can toggle independently. Security: explainability returns only redacted paths and never discloses full encryption context or raw KMS tokens. The KMS cache is ephemeral, encrypted at rest in-memory, and does not persist across restarts. Testing: unit and integration tests added for PDP traces, correlator durability under load, and KMS cache correctness under churn. Rollout plan: staged rollout -- enable behind flag in canary for 24h, smoke tests on policy-heavy tenants, then gradual ramp to 25%/50%/100%. Related work: replaces ad-hoc investigator tools and complements existing audit-signing work (see ENG-6117). Checklist: - [x] Feature flag gating - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests (audit pipeline) - [x] Docs: operator config and security notes - [x] Benchmarks: explainability endpoint median latency 2.6ms under load - [x] Readiness: fallback mode documented
Leo Nakamura: Nice separation of concerns. Two requests: 1) please add a short circuit to avoid building traces when feature flag is off, 2) ensure the request-level logs don't include raw encryption context. 
Ava Martinez: Addressed both in latest commit; short-circuit added in pdp/engine and redaction added to the explain handler. See commit feat(rbac): avoid trace build when flag=false.
Priya Shah: CI flaked once on the correlator integration test (timeout). Can we make the test more deterministic (use synchronous test harness)?
Ava Martinez: Switched to harness-based runner and increased default test timeouts; added an extra health check to prevent flakiness.
Tomás Ortega: Quick security review: the cache uses tenant-scoped hash keys which is good. Please add explicit eviction metrics so SRE can observe churn.
Ava Martinez: Added metrics.rbac.explain.cache_evictions and documented alert thresholds in docs/operator/rbac-explainability.md

payload.body:
Motivation: Several customers requested stricter enforcement that CMKs used for encrypting tenant data must be region-aligned with the tenant's residency setting. Previously we relied on best-effort checks in the private installer and operator docs; this PR introduces a policy + runtime guard to validate KMS claims at enforcement points and a background auditor to remove or flag audit records that reference retired or out-of-scope keys.

This PR includes: (1) policies/kms-usage-enforcer.yaml — an RBACv2 policy fragment that defines a kube-like admission-style guard for KMS claims: it validates the key's region attribute against tenant.residency and rejects requests where the key is outside the allowed zone unless the operator role is explicitly delegated and timebound; (2) policies/rbac-delegation-guard.yaml — a small policy that restricts cross-region operator delegation to short TTLs and requires an approval annotation; (3) tools/audit-cleaner — a small background worker (Go) that scans the audit ledger for entries pointing to KMS key ARNs in retired zones and either tags them as orphaned or prunes them after an admin retention window.

Design notes: We intentionally keep enforcement opt-in behind the feature flag "kms_residency_enforcement" so that Dedicated and Private customers can enable during a maintenance window. The enforcer runs synchronously at the final admission point for encryption requests (hosted path: encryption proxy; private path: installer hooks). When the policy would reject, the response surface returns a 403 with an error code X-KMS-REGION-MISMATCH and a remediation hint linking to the admin docs. For operator flows that require cross-region key use we support a delegation annotation (rbac.redwood.io/delegate-region) that must be accompanied by an operator-approved ticket id (Linear/Jira) and is limited to 4 hours by default.

Audit cleaner behavior: The cleaner uses the same residency rules to identify audit records that reference keys which are no longer in-scope (rotated/retired/region-changed). It writes a new audit tag "kms_orphaned: true" and increments a metric audit_orphan_count; after 30 days (configurable) orphaned records are pruned to satisfy retention and reduce exposure surface. Pruned entries are recorded in a tamper-evident prune log stored separately.

Testing: Unit tests added for policy rule edge cases (missing residency attribute, ambiguous region tags). Integration tests exercise a canary flow where enforcement is enabled for a single tenant and we assert the blocking and delegation paths. Local run: make test-integration passes, CI shows build/test/lint green after small lint fix to audit-cleaner imports.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag off. 2) Deploy audit-cleaner to staging and enable canary tenant via feature flag. 3) Monitor metrics: kms_enforcer_rejects, audit_orphan_count, rbac_delegation_grants. 4) If stable for 72h, toggle feature on for additional tenants in waves. We include a rollback script to disable the feature flag and re-run a pass that converts reject responses into warnings for 24h.

Security review: Reviewed by security and SRE (Michael Chen, Sofie Alvarez). We added rate limiting on the enforcer path to avoid amplification attacks and bounded the audit-cleaner worker concurrency. Key validation uses existing KMS metadata API with cached TTL to avoid per-request KMS calls.

Backward compatibility: When disabled, no behavior changes. Feature flag on may cause new 403 responses — documented in docs/security/kms-residency.md.

Related: ENG-4142 (residency policy backlog), SEC-88 (compliance remediation for EU tenant controls).

Checklist: - [x] Policy YAML and unit tests - [x] Enforcer implementation stubbed in admission point - [x] Background audit-cleaner and Dockerfile - [x] Integration tests for canary path - [x] Docs and rollout notes - [x] Security review sign-off

Manual steps for operators (high level): 1) Ensure feature flag is present in config and disabled by default. 2) Deploy audit-cleaner with k8s CronJob schedule or sidecar in Private installer. 3) For exceptional cross-region keys, create a delegation entry with a Linear ticket and set annotation rbac.redwood.io/delegate-region: <ticket>. 4) Monitor audit_orphan_count and run admin prune job if needed.

This PR is intentionally scoped to policy + tooling; it does not attempt to modify model-serving code paths directly — we will follow up with adapters in the encryption proxy and private installer to call the enforcer at the canonical point of encryption key selection.
Michael Chen: Looks good overall; please add a small circuit-breaker metric for the enforcer path so SRE can kill it quickly if we see a spike.
Anjali Rao: Added enforcer_circuit_breaker metric and patched the worker to respect it. Pushed commit b4d2c9e.
Sofie Alvarez: Can we narrow the default delegation TTL to 2 hours instead of 4? Risk of long-lived cross-region keys concerns me.
Anjali Rao: Updated default to 2h in rbac-delegation-guard.yaml and noted it in the docs. Pushed commit c3e9d11.
Ravi Patel: Integration tests flaked once on CI due to DB connection limits — increased concurrency cap to 3 and re-ran.

Title: Add break-glass verification override guardrails + required audit annotations. Context: As part of offline bundle signature verification, the installer now supports a policy-gated break-glass flag (see redwood-private-installer pr-24979). This PR adds cluster-side guardrails so that (1) break-glass cannot be enabled silently, (2) use is attributable and exportable via audit logs, and (3) only approved operators can authorize it. Summary of changes: (A) Adds a Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate + Constraint enforcing required annotations whenever break-glass is enabled via the Redwood Private install metadata ConfigMap (redwood-private/install-metadata) or Helm values rendered into that ConfigMap. Required annotations: redwood.ai/break-glass-ticket (SUP-/INT-/customer ticket id), redwood.ai/break-glass-reason (freeform, min 20 chars), redwood.ai/break-glass-approved-by (corporate email), redwood.ai/break-glass-approved-at (RFC3339 timestamp), redwood.ai/break-glass-expires-at (RFC3339; must be <= 72h from approved-at). Optional but recommended: redwood.ai/break-glass-approver-role (Security|ReleaseEng|SRE). (B) Adds a second constraint that denies enabling break-glass unless the requesting subject is in the allowlisted RBAC group (redwood:break-glass-approvers) or is a ServiceAccount with label redwood.ai/purpose=private-installer and bound to ClusterRole redwood-private-break-glass-approver. (C) Adds a policy exception mechanism for dev/test clusters only: if Namespace has label redwood.ai/environment=dev and redwood.ai/policy-exceptions contains break-glass-guardrails, constraints run in "warn" mode and include a warning message; default remains "deny" for all other environments. (D) Adds a small conftest test suite covering: missing annotations, malformed timestamps, expiry > 72h, approver not allowlisted, and the dev warn-only path. Why this approach: We want verification to fail closed by default but still support emergency installs when signatures cannot be verified due to environmental constraints (time skew, trust store mismatch, etc.). The installer already logs local audit markers; these policies ensure the cluster also has consistent, queryable attribution for any break-glass activation, and prevent accidental enablement by automation. Implementation notes: Policies target the install-metadata ConfigMap because it is the canonical place we already read for support bundles and audit export mapping. We intentionally avoid requiring outbound connectivity or external approvals (air-gapped), but we require the metadata fields that support and security will request during incident response and compliance evidence collection. Files / areas changed: policy/gatekeeper/templates/redwoodprivatebreakglass_annotations_template.yaml; policy/gatekeeper/constraints/redwoodprivatebreakglass_annotations_constraint.yaml; policy/gatekeeper/templates/redwoodprivatebreakglass_approver_template.yaml; policy/gatekeeper/constraints/redwoodprivatebreakglass_approver_constraint.yaml; rbac/clusterroles/redwood-private-break-glass-approver.yaml; rbac/clusterrolebindings/redwood-private-break-glass-approver-binding.yaml; tests/conftest/break_glass_annotations_test.rego; tests/fixtures/install-metadata-configmap.yaml; README.md (break-glass section). Illustrative snippet (ConstraintTemplate logic, shortened): "violation[{"msg": msg}] { input.review.kind.kind == "ConfigMap"; input.review.object.metadata.name == "install-metadata"; input.review.object.metadata.namespace == "redwood-private"; input.review.object.data["break_glass_enabled"] == "true"; missing := {"redwood.ai/break-glass-ticket", "redwood.ai/break-glass-reason", "redwood.ai/break-glass-approved-by", "redwood.ai/break-glass-approved-at", "redwood.ai/break-glass-expires-at"} - {k | input.review.object.metadata.annotations[k]}; count(missing) > 0; msg := sprintf("break-glass enabled but missing required annotations: %v", [missing]) }". Testing: make policy-lint; make test-conftest; validated against a local kind cluster with Gatekeeper v3.14. CI: gatekeeper-schema-check, conftest, yamllint all green. Rollout: This is a no-op unless Gatekeeper is installed (standard for regulated Private installs). For existing clusters, apply templates/constraints first (will only affect future changes to install metadata). Related: ENG-4824 (break-glass design), ENG-4829 (audit event schema), SUP-31977 (support guidance).
Marcus Lin (review): Can we tighten the schema so expires-at is always present and bounded? Also, confirm we’re not allowing arbitrary subjects to set these annotations (otherwise someone can self-approve). Kevin Osei (author): Updated template to require expires-at and added <=72h bound relative to approved-at. Added a separate approver constraint: deny unless user is in redwood:break-glass-approvers or installer SA bound to redwood-private-break-glass-approver. Allison Grant (review): Annotation names look good, but please align with logging redaction guidance (don’t force PII). Can we avoid requiring a full name? Kevin Osei: Using corporate email only; reason field is freeform but we recommend excluding customer identifiers; added README guidance. Ethan Park (review): Installer writes install-metadata—will this block initial install? We need a path where break-glass is off by default. Kevin Osei: Constraint only triggers when break_glass_enabled==true. Default install-metadata has it false; initial install unaffected. Connor O'Brien (review): Please add a warn-only mechanism for dev clusters. Kevin Osei: Added label-based exception for redwood.ai/environment=dev with enforcementAction=warn and explicit warning message; production remains deny. Final: Marcus approved after seeing tests for malformed timestamps and allowlist enforcement; Allison approved after README update. CI had one failure due to Gatekeeper schema mismatch; reran after fixing apiVersion and it passed.

Summary: Introduces explicit RBAC permissions for the Optimization Config lifecycle (create/validate/apply/promote/rollback) and adds two opinionated roles used by Console + control plane workflows. This is part of the Safe apply + rollback mechanism project to ensure rollback is both auditable and access-controlled. Motivation: Today, optimization config changes are implicitly covered by broad “platform operator” capabilities in some environments, and not consistently modeled in Private deployments. Enterprise customers and Security review require least-privilege roles with clear separation between “can propose” and “can execute rollback in prod.” Changes included: 1) New permissions: optimization_config.read, optimization_config.create_version, optimization_config.validate, optimization_config.diff, optimization_config.apply, optimization_config.promote, optimization_config.rollback, optimization_config.override_gates (break-glass), optimization_config.manage_rbac (internal only). 2) New roles: optimization_change_operator (intended for on-call + platform operators executing safe apply/rollback within an approved scope; includes read/diff/validate/apply/rollback; does NOT include promote-by-default to reduce accidental broad rollouts), optimization_change_admin (intended for senior operators; includes promote + override_gates; still does not include manage_rbac). 3) Updates to policy docs: clarified mapping from Console actions (“Rollback” button, “Promote to production”, “Override gates”) to permissions and recommended reviewer/approval process. 4) Tests: added rego/policy tests + golden snapshots covering allow/deny cases for Hosted/Dedicated/Private personas, including a regression test for INT-3390 (operator could not see rollback button due to missing permission). Backwards compatibility: No default widening of access; existing roles are unchanged except for documentation noting recommended migration. Control plane/Console will explicitly request these permissions when the feature flag is enabled. Rollout plan: Land policy bundle first; then enable in staging; then gate Console button visibility on optimization_config.rollback + server-side authz checks in control plane. Notes: “override_gates” is explicitly separate and intended for internal break-glass flows only (guarded by additional approval and audited separately).
Marcus Lin (review): Can we make sure rollback is not implicitly granted via promote? I’d prefer rollback to be in operator and promote to be in admin only. Also, “override_gates” should be separate and deny-by-default. Jordan Lee (author): Agreed. Updated role split: operator includes rollback but not promote; admin includes promote + override_gates. Added explicit denies + tests. Naomi Feldman (review): Please add a note in docs that Console must check BOTH the permission and server-side authz. We don’t want clients inferring from UI state. Also confirm audit events will include actor role/permission context (even if emitted elsewhere). Jordan Lee: Added doc section “UI visibility vs enforcement” and a pointer to audit requirements; audit payload fields are enforced in control plane, but we reference required fields and recommend including evaluated permissions in debug logs only (not audit events). Ethan Park (review): For Private deployments, do we have a clear mapping for customer-admin vs operator? Jordan Lee: Added guidance in docs/optimization-config-rbac.md: recommend customer define a limited operator group with optimization_change_operator and restrict by tenant/model/region scopes. Chloe Martin (review): Any impact on existing Console pages that list config history? Jordan Lee: Added optimization_config.read/diff to operator and admin; existing read-only views should map to read/diff. Benji Okafor (review): Please include a regression test for the exact permission check the rollback endpoint will use (optimization_config.rollback). Jordan Lee: Added test case “rollback_requires_permission” and updated golden snapshot. Marcus Lin (final): Looks good after the split + deny-by-default. Approving. Naomi Feldman (final): Approved with doc updates. Ethan Park (final): Approved. Chloe Martin (final): Approved.
RBAC: Added optimization config lifecycle permissions and new roles for safe apply/rollback. Console/control plane can now gate rollback/promote actions via explicit permissions.

payload.body:
Context: Customers are increasingly using structured output via response_format for tightly coupled tool/function calling. We observed two failure modes in production: 1) streaming validation failures mid-stream caused unsafe tool invocations or silent truncation, and 2) opaque errors returned by the OpenAI-compat layer that made automated retries and resume semantics hard for callers. This PR introduces a new explicit response_schema_mode (schema_mode) and a runtime 'resume token' anchoring mechanism that together make mid-stream schema failures actionable and enable safe toolcall fencing and resume flows.

Summary of changes (single-line description): Add response_format.schema_mode with options (strict, soft, resume-friendly), emit structured error payloads with error_code enum, add resume_token generation and validation, add runtime streaming checkpoints (anchoring) to fence tool/function calls when schema violations occur, and extend OpenAI-compat mapping to surface these semantics via function_call compatibility.

Design highlights: 1) response_format.schema_mode - new top-level field in the API: "strict" enforces immediate stream abort on validation failure, "soft" returns best-effort output with schema hints, "resume" produces a structured error (SCHEMA_VIOLATION) containing a resume_token when the generator detects a schema mismatch mid-stream. The resume_token can be sent back with a follow-up request to continue from the last validated checkpoint after prompt corrections or model fallback. 2) error_code enum - standardized codes (SCHEMA_VIOLATION, PARTIAL_OUTPUT, TOOLCALL_FENCED, STREAM_RESUME_HINT) so clients can programmatically handle outcomes. 3) Toolcall fencing - when tool/function call boundaries intersect with validation failures, runtime fences the attempted call, emits TOOLCALL_FENCED and the resume_token, and prevents execution until the resume flow is accepted. 4) OpenAI compatibility - the openai_compat layer now maps the resume_token into function_call metadata when present, and surfaces structured errors as top-level messages compatible with common SDKs.

Implementation notes: Changes touch the streaming validator, the request/response API layer, the OpenAI compatibility mapping, SDK adaptors (Python/TS), the docs page for response_format, and a set of integration tests that exercise race conditions between validation and function calling. The runtime now maintains lightweight per-request checkpoints (anchoring points) every N tokens; these are cryptographic hashes signed by the control plane so resume tokens cannot be forged. Resume flow validates token integrity, the model context that produced it, and enforces that the new prompt includes the user's correction/ack before un-fencing the toolcall.

Backward compatibility and opt-in: Default behavior remains unchanged for requests that do not specify response_format.schema_mode. OpenAI-compat callers get the old best-effort behavior unless they opt into the 'schema_mode' via the compatibility params (see docs).

Testing & rollout: Added unit tests for the validator, 3 integration tests simulating interleaved toolcalls and validation fails, and a non-blocking canary rollout config (10% of traffic) for 72 hours before enabling globally.

Related: Addresses ENG-8342 (streaming schema regressions) and ties to SUP-219 which described a customer incident where a mid-stream validation caused a downstream system to run an unwanted tool.

Checklist: - [x] API param schema and request validation - [x] Runtime streaming validator anchoring and resume_token signer - [x] OpenAI-compat mapping and SDK adaptors - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Docs update and release notes

Summary: Add a standalone Decision Proof Log (DPL) that records policy decisions (RBAC v2) with cryptographic provenance, and introduce a KMS Fidelity Gate that captures KMS call metadata (provider, region, key-id fingerprint, request-hash) for each decision that depended on KMS-backed keys. This PR wires the DPL into the auth pipeline, provides a compact audit-forwarding path, and adds a safe opt-in replay mode for incident investigation.

Motivation: Customers in regulated industries asked for tamper-evident decision records and an unambiguous link between resource access decisions and the KMS context used to satisfy them (ENG-1427, SEC-89).

Design goals:
1) Non-blocking: DPL writes are async with backpressure safeguards; 2) Tamper-evident: proof chain uses keyed HMAC with rotated audit keys; 3) Minimal latency impact on hot path; 4) Optional replay/export for compliance teams.

Changes included (high-level):
- New service: auth/decisionprover (go) — records decision entries, computes HMAC proofs, stores to durable audit-topic.
- KMS adapter: services/kms/fidelity_gate.go — captures KMS metadata and attaches fidelity assertions to decision payloads.
- Auth pipeline: middleware/authz/decision_logger.go — invokes DPL on allow/deny results and attaches trace ids.
- Telemetry: observability/metrics/decision_proofing.prom — counters and latency histograms.
- Infra: infra/helm/templates/audit-config.yaml — feature flags and retention defaults; infra/terraform/audit_topic.tf updates to add new pubsub topic.
- Docs: docs/security/decision-proofing.md — implementation notes and operational runbook.
- Tests: integration/authz_dpl_e2e_test.go and unit tests covering signature rotation and backpressure.

Commits:
- a2f9d3c: initial DPL service scaffolding and protobufs
- b7c8e34: integrate DPL into authz middleware; add async writer
- c3fd021: implement KMS fidelity gate and attachers
- d9e1b55: metrics, feature-flag configuration, helm template changes
- f4127a1: add integration tests and e2e CI job
- 0bb3c6f: docs and runbook, Linear links, changelog entry

Files changed (representative):
- src/auth/middleware/decision_logger.go
- src/auth/decisionprover/service.go
- src/auth/decisionprover/writer.go
- services/kms/fidelity_gate.go
- infra/helm/templates/audit-config.yaml
- infra/terraform/audit_topic.tf
- docs/security/decision-proofing.md
- tests/integration/authz_dpl_e2e_test.go
- observability/metrics/decision_proofing.prom
- Makefile (ci job)

Implementation notes:
- Decision entries contain: request_id, principal, resource, action, policy_version, decision, timestamp, proof_hmac (base64), kms_fidelity_block (optional JSON blob with provider, key_fingerprint, region, api_version, request_hash).
- Proof HMAC uses an audit-key injected from secret manager and rotated by the audit-ops job; rotation produces an envelope version number.
- DPL writes are batched and retried; when the audit topic is unreachable the middleware records a local diagnostic event and continues (opt-out via feature flag disables this fallback).
- The KMS Fidelity Gate is pluggable: adapters for aws/kms and gcp/kms included. The gate does not proxy secrets; it only records normalized metadata and a short request-hash (HMAC of request payload) so that replay is possible without exfiltrating sensitive plaintext.

Security review summary:
- Threat modeling completed in SEC-89; main risk is accidental inclusion of sensitive ciphertext in logs — mitigations: strict schema validation, scrubber in writer, and redaction policy enforced in infra.
- KMS adapters specifically avoid recording plaintext or encryption contexts in full.

Testing and CI:
- New e2e job authz-dpl-e2e runs against a local test KMS shim and the audit-topic emulator.
- Unit tests for signature verification and key rotation added.
- CI checks: go fmt, go vet, unit tests (pass), integration e2e (flaky in first run, rerun passed), lint, security-scan (terrascan policy for infra changes) — overall CI status: pass.

Review conversation (selected):
- Ruth Chen (reviewer): "Can we ensure the HMAC key is never exported via snapshot logs? Add a unit test that simulates rotation and verifies old proofs remain verifiable."
- Aisha (author): "Added verify_rotation_test.go and ensured the audit-key is marked as non-exportable in the secret manifest. Also tightened logging so key material is never printed."
- Luca Moretti (reviewer): "This looks good. One concern: what happens if the audit-topic retention exceeds allowed bounds? Add limits and an alert."
- Aisha: "Added retention default to 90d and configured an infra alert to fire when topic backlog > 100k messages in infra/monitoring — see infra/terraform/alerts.tf (follow-up PR planned to centralize alerts)."
- Priya Shah (security): "Please confirm that the KMS adapters cannot be used to exfiltrate on-demand key metadata."
- Aisha: "Adapters only record deterministic fingerprints and request-hash; added explicit schema validation and test 'kms_adapter_no_exfil_test.go'."
- Ruth Chen: "Approve after CI green and docs review."

Approval and merge:
- PR approved by Ruth Chen and Priya Shah.
- Docs reviewed by Platform Docs (content/ownership tracked).
- Merged via squash on 2025-11-26 by Ruth Chen.

Rollout and ops notes:
- Feature is behind helm feature-flag 'decisionProof.enabled' (default: false for existing clusters).
- For Hosted customers we will enable in a staggered rollout after informing compliance contacts; Dedicated/Private customers can opt-in via config.
- Operator runbook added in docs/security/decision-proofing.md with steps for key rotation, emergency disable, and replay guidance.

Follow-ups / Known limitations:
- Currently the fidelity gate adapters do not include Azure KMS; follow-up ticket ENG-1583 scheduled.
- Replay mode requires access to the request payload hashes and mapping to stored request bodies; we added a sentinel design doc and will ship a controlled export flow.
- The audit-topic backlog alerting needs centralization (see ENG-1532).

Checklist:

- [x] Unit & integration tests
- [x] CI jobs added and passing
- [x] Documentation and runbook
- [x] Infra changes applied to helm/terraform
- [x] Security review approval (Priya Shah)

Merge outcome: merged, squash.

Notes for release: no breaking changes; enable behind flag.

Linear/Jira: ENG-1427 (implementation), SEC-89 (security review), SUP-4123 (customer request).
Adds a decision proof log for RBAC v2 policy evaluations and a KMS fidelity gate that records and optionally replays KMS call metadata for compliance audits. No customer-facing API changes.

Motivation: reduce multi‑GPU stalls caused by head-of-line NCCL waits and KV cache prefetch serialization for tensor‑parallel workloads. This PR introduces a lightweight stream‑interleaving scheduler, a prefetch fence that decouples KV prefetch from blocking collective submission, and a small NCCL tuning pass that picks stream affinities per-rank. Changes are targeted to the TP runtime path only and include microbenchmarks and a fallback for older NCCL versions. Key benefits: fewer idle CUDA cycles during long decode sequences, improved overlap between communication and compute for per-layer allgather patterns, and more deterministic p99. Summary of changes follows in commits and files_changed. Notes: description is a single continuous string to preserve GitHub PR prose style and contains checklists and test notes inline.
scheduler: introduce StreamInterleaving policy and unit tests
gpu: add nccl_affinity tuner and version gate
kvcache: introduce prefetch_fence + nonblocking prefetch path
runtime: wire stream interleaving into tp dispatcher
bench: add long-seq tp microbench harness (8xA100)
Amelia Park: Can you add a small fallback path when NCCL < 2.14 is detected? Some on-prem clusters still use 2.12.
Ravi Patel: Added a version gate and a slower fallback that keeps the legacy submission ordering. See nccl_tuner.cc (second commit).
Zoe Kim: Bench numbers look promising; please add p95/p99 distributions and CI rerun to ensure stability.
Ravi Patel: Uploaded extended runs (8xA100, 4 seeds) and added p95/p99 charts to docs/perf. CI bench job re-ran and passed.
Marcus Liu: Approve after minor comment about a log level change for the tuner (suggest debug).
Runtime: added stream interleaving and nonblocking KV prefetch fence for tensor-parallel; improves overlap of comm/compute and reduces p99 on long decode workloads. Backwards-compatible with older NCCL via fallback.
8xA100-40GB, GPT-like 16k seq: throughput +18% end-to-end vs main (same batch size)
p99 latency reduced by 12% (median ~6%)
GPU utilization uplift: +9% sustained on TP layers with heavy allgather
Unit tests added for stream scheduler correctness; microbench harness integrated into CI bench stage. Manual verification performed on an internal 8xA100 cluster; regression tests for kvcache prefetch added.
Feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.tp_stream_interleave (default true for pools with NCCL>=2.14). Fallback enabled for NCCL<2.14; operators can disable via config if necessary.
Related work: builds on earlier TP scheduling PRs but uses a different approach: per-rank stream affinity + prefetch fence to prevent head-of-line blocking. See ENG-2184 for rollout plan and perf targets.

Introduce an automated policy-bundle generator and idempotent tenant bootstrap flow for Private deployments to simplify initial operator setup and tenant onboarding. Motivation: customers deploying Redwood Private currently perform manual RBAC wiring across cluster namespaces, service accounts, and cloud IAM + KMS roles; this is error-prone and causes onboarding delays during enterprise installs. This PR implements a deterministic policy bundle generator (Go tool), Helm chart templates for operator bootstrap, Terraform module updates to wire cloud IAM roles for KMS/HSM access, preflight checks to validate cluster RBAC and network reachability, and migration utilities to convert existing manual role mappings into managed bundles. High-level changes: 1) new tool private/installer/tools/policygen (Go) that outputs bundled YAML per-tenant with namespaced rolebindings, aggregated ClusterRoles for operator actions, and optional KMS IAM mapping annotations; 2) Helm templates under charts/private/templates/rbac-bootstrap.yaml implementing a two-phase bootstrap: operator-serviceaccount creation + cluster-level bootstrap job (runs once); 3) terraform/modules/private-rbac adds optional cloud_role_arn input and automates iam_policy attachment for KMS; 4) hack/preflight-rbac-check.sh validates required APIs, existing conflicting bindings, and idempotency; 5) docs/private/rbac-automation.md with recommended upgrade path and rollback steps. Backwards compatibility: generator recognizes legacy mappings (label selector and annotation based) and will emit a migration report; default behavior is non-destructive (does not delete existing bindings). Rollout plan: merge to main behind feature flag PRIVATE_RBAC_AUTOMATION=false, ship as opt-in in next Private release, and follow with an enablement blog + migration tool runbook. Testing: unit tests for generator, integration tests in perf-canary infra that exercise bootstrap job lifecycle, manual validation with on-prem test cluster. Related: referenced ENG-4821 for tracking rollout milestones and PM-205 for documentation and support tasks. Checklist: [x] generator + tests; [x] helm templates; [x] terraform wiring; [x] preflight checks; [x] docs + runbook; [x] migration utility and report. Merge note: squash merge after approvals.

Maya Patel: Added stable name algorithm (tenant prefix + truncated sha256) and unit tests in commit 3/5.
Sofia Ruiz: CI showed a failing integration test on the first run related to the bootstrap job imagePullPolicy; suggest forcing IfNotPresent to avoid flakes.

Automated RBAC policy bundle generator and tenant bootstrap for Private installer. Adds opt-in automation for creating operator service accounts, cluster-level bootstrap jobs, Terraform wiring for KMS IAM roles, and migration tooling for legacy bindings. Non-destructive by default.

Summary: This PR implements tenant-aware data residency controls (aka 'residency-guards'), scopes KMS key usage to tenant+region, and extends RBAC v2 role mappings to carry region annotations. Motivation: Several enterprise customers requested hard guarantees that keys and audit streams remain in-customer regions and that role grants cannot be used to bypass residency rules. This change closes gaps discovered during compliance reviews and a recent support investigation (SUP-7890). High level changes: 1) Residency guard middleware: routes requests by tenant geo-tag and enforces region pinning policies; rejects or routes to fallback when policy mismatch. 2) KMS scoping: KMS key references now require a tenant and region qualifier; server-side validation added to key lookup path and crypto plugins updated to reject cross-region key usage. 3) RBAC v2 mapping: role mappings accept an optional region_claim attribute which restricts tokens to the specified region; evaluation engine updated to intersect tenant region and role region. 4) Audit propagation: introduced X-Redwood-Audit-Region header enforcement and enriched audit log entries with region and key_id. 5) Migration tooling: included kms-region-migrate script that converts legacy key bindings and emits a report for customer review. 6) Tests & CI: new unit and integration tests including simulated multi-region tenants and negative tests for mis-scoped keys. Commits (high level): - 2a1f7bd: residency guard middleware and policy model - 7b4e2c1: KMS validation and plugin API changes - 9c2d5f8: RBAC v2 evaluator region handling and mapping docs - d45a8e3: audit header enforcement and log enrichment - f1b9c02: kms-region-migrate tool and migration tests - 0e3a91d: add e2e scenarios to private installer suite Changed areas/files (high level): - src/security/residency/guard.go: new middleware and policy loader - proto/policy/residency.proto: policy schema additions - internal/kms/provider.go: key scoping and validation logic (illustrative snippet: if key.Region != request.Region { return ErrRegionMismatch }) - services/authn/rbac/v2/mapping.go: region_claim checks and eval updates - cmd/kms-region-migrate/main.go: migration entrypoint and report exporter - infra/priv-installer/e2e/residency_test.go: e2e scenarios for on-prem installer - docs/security/data-residency.md: design and operator runbook Review notes and conversation: - Priya: "Can we ensure the middleware short-circuits before any key material is fetched?" Author reply: "Yes, guard checks run in the request admission path; added unit test and comment to make ordering explicit." - Luca: "Migration tool looks good, but add a dry-run mode and a CSV report." Author reply: "Added --dry-run and CSV output; report includes before/after key bindings." - Owen: "What happens if a region label is missing on older tenants?" Author reply: "Policy default is inbound: tenants without explicit region remain in 'unscoped' bucket and are blocked from KMS operations until migration; we added an operator-facing migration guide." - Priya requested a security review for crypto plugin changes, later approved after one minor naming nit. CI: initial runs failed on lint due to naming of a test variable; fixed in follow-up commit and all checks passed (unit, integration, e2e). Performance: small runtime overhead for residency checks (~0.6ms median per request in microbench), measured in tests and within SLO for targeted customers. Backwards compatibility: the KMS provider API introduces a non-breaking optional parameter for region; we included shims in legacy adapters. Migration: kms-region-migrate included and tested; migration has to be scheduled by operator and can be rolled back by restoring previous binding snapshot. Security considerations: added threat mitigation section to docs and required an ACL check prior to migration script execution. Merge details: PR approved by reviewers and merged via squash on 2026-03-02. Squash commit message: "security: add data-residency guards, KMS scoping, RBAC v2 region mapping" Follow-ups: - ENG-4821: rollout plan for Dedicated clusters and Private installer upgrades - SEC-134: audit rule to alert on any requests rejected by residency guard - PM-210: UI controls to show tenant region and migration status in console Known limitations: cross-region read-only audit streams are not migrated automatically; operator action required. Notes for release: this change should be rolled out to staging + canary before full prod; include operators on migration schedule. Related: references SUP-7890 and internal design doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/doc/RESIDENCY-DESIGN (internal).
Tenant-scoped KMS enforcement and data-residency guards; RBAC v2 mapping now honors region tags; audit header validation for routed requests; migration tool for existing customer KMS bindings.

payload.body:
Motivation: Our main CI pipeline provides strong coverage but slow feedback for small, iterative changes (median turnaround ~22m). This PR introduces a conservative 'fast-path' CI gate and companion dep-curation tooling to: (1) give developers quicker red/green on trivial edits, (2) keep heavy integration suites gated behind a staged smoke run, and (3) improve dependency hygiene with an automated curation snapshot.

Summary of changes: added a lightweight GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/ci-fastpath.yml) that runs lint, unit tests, and quick static checks in <10m for small diffs; modified ci/test-scheduler.go to classify PRs by changed paths and size; added scripts/dep_curate.py which generates dependency-snapshot.yaml (used by the pipeline to pin transitive ranges and skip noisy upgrades); adjusted existing lint/test workflows to accept the new fast-path gate as a pre-check; updated docs at docs/ci/fastpath.md describing gate behavior and escalation path.

Checklist: 
- [x] Fast-path workflow definition and runner labeling
- [x] Scheduler heuristics for path-based fast-path eligibility (docs updated)
- [x] Dep-curation script and sample snapshot committed
- [x] Integration tests for scheduler (unit-level)
- [x] Rollout plan included (gradual enablement via feature flag)

Rollout plan:
1) Stage: run fast-path on all PRs in opt-in mode (no gating) for 48h to collect metrics (latency, false negatives).
2) Gate: after metric validation, enable fast-path as a required check for small PRs (<10 changed files, only docs/ or pkg/ changes) with automatic fallback to full CI on mismatch.
3) Expand: incrementally relax size constraints and refine heuristics based on observed false-negative rate.

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: fast-path might miss failures that only surface in integration tests. Mitigation: staged smoke gate (full CI runs in parallel until we reach confidence thresholds) and automatic fallback configured in the scheduler.
- Risk: dependency-snapshot might become stale. Mitigation: add weekly job (not in this PR) to propose curated updates and alert on drift; snapshot will be validated by the heavy CI lane.

Operational notes: 
- dep_curate.py accepts a lockfile and a policy file; it emits dependency-snapshot.yaml with pinned transitive versions and a lightweight justification field. The CI step will abort and post a comment if the snapshot validation fails (prevents accidental uncurated upgrades landing in main).
- The test scheduler exposes a small HTTP endpoint for metrics and a feature flag toggle (default off) so SRE can flip the gate during rollout.

Commands to exercise locally: 
- scripts/dep_curate.py --lockfile=pnpm-lock.yaml --policy=ci/dep-policy.yaml --out=ci/dependency-snapshot.yaml
- go test ./ci -run TestSchedulerFastPath -v
- act -j fastpath (developer convenience, requires act config)

Related work: ENG-4219 (fast-feedback CI workstream), ENG-4228 (dependency hygiene initiative), SUP-1024 (customer incident that motivated faster triage).

Commit summary (high level):
- Add fast-path CI workflow and small-run runner config
- Implement path/size heuristics in test scheduler and expose feature flag
- Add dep_curate.py, policy schema, and sample dependency-snapshot.yaml
- Adjust lint and release workflows to respect the fast-path gate and snapshot validation
- Update CI docs and rollout notes

Merge notes: squash-merged to main after CI green and approvals. Post-merge tasks: enable opt-in mode for 48h, monitor metrics dashboard (ci/fastpath -> latency, fallback-rate).
- Add staged fast-path CI gate to speed feedback on small PRs
- Introduce dep-curation scripts and dependency-snapshot.yaml used by CI
- Adjust test scheduler to prefer lightweight lanes and reduce flakiness
Marcus Chen: overall looks good — can we add a short-circuit to force full CI when a PR touches infra/*?
Priya Nanduri: added exclusion for infra/* and updated scheduler tests to cover it
Elena García: nits on dep_curate.py logging format; prefer structured JSON logs — addressed in commit e7a1f49
Noah Patel: CI: observed intermittent flake in TestSchedulerFastPath on macOS runner, re-ran and added defensive nil-check
Marcus Chen: approved after changes — leaving a final +1

Summary: Introduces a holdpoint-driven 'carousel' promote strategy aimed at safe staged promotes across session-sensitive workloads. The feature combines (1) holdpoint anchors — deterministic traffic cut points keyed by session cohorts, (2) a rehearsal shadow runner that replays representative traffic for each holdpoint prior to live promotion, and (3) a rollback playbook that encodes automatic and manual abort semantics with quarantine lanes.

Motivation: Multiple incidents where incremental canaries passed aggregate metrics but failed for sticky-session cohorts motivated a promotion strategy that ensures session-coherent rehearsals before traffic cutover. This PR implements the orchestration primitives and a default rollback playbook that operators can tune.

Design:
- Holdpoint controller: computes holdpoints from cohort selectors and session affinity metadata, maintains per-holdpoint state and progress checkpoints.
- Rehearsal shadow runner: lightweight traffic replayer that runs sampled requests against candidate model variants with KV-cache warmup and smoke checks.
- Rollback playbook: policy-as-data YAML-driven playbook mapping failure classes (latency spike, token-error regression, model drift) to actions (quarantine, immediate revert, partial drain, human-latch).
- Integration with Console: exposes per-holdpoint timelines, rehearsal badges, and playbook-executed actions.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement controller state machine and progress checkpoints
- [x] Add rehearsal runner with deterministic replay seed
- [x] Provide default rollback playbook and validation harness
- [x] Unit tests for controller transitions
- [x] Integration tests (simulated sessions)
- [x] Console telemetry and holdpoint UI hooks
- [x] Docs and quickstart snippet

Backwards compatibility: The new promote strategy is opt-in via rollout_profile: "holdpoint-carousel". Existing rollout profiles are unchanged. Config changes are additive and safe for clusters that do not opt-in.

Testing:
- Local unit test suites under test/unit or test/orchestrator run with new mock session registry.
- Integration harness has a new scenario that simulates 10k session handoffs across 3 holdpoints and validates session affinity + KV prewarm.
- Ran canary smoke on staging with 2 rehearsal runs; CI flake fixed by increasing test harness timeouts.

Rollout plan: Stage to staging for 48h, enable feature flag for 5% of traffic (non-critical customers), run two rehearsal cycles and collect per-holdpoint smoke metrics, then raise to 20% with automatic rollback monitoring on the playbook thresholds.

Related: builds on ENG-4321 (session-affine routing) and follows the telemetry contract in ENG-4399.

Files changed (high level):
- src/orchestrator/holdpoint_controller.py: new state machine and API hooks
- src/orchestrator/rehearsal_runner.go: sample-driven replay engine with KV warmup
- src/orchestrator/playbooks/rollback_playbook.yaml: policy-as-data examples
- console/ui/holdpoint_timeline.tsx: UI badges and timeline
- docs/rollouts/holdpoint-carousel.md: design + quickstart
- test/integration/holdpoint_carousel_test.go: integration scenario
- cfg/rollout_profiles/defaults.yaml: new profile entry

Operational concerns & mitigation:
- Cost: rehearsal runs increase token spend; playbook includes a rehearsal_budget parameter and sampling controls.
- Latency: KV warmup performed in rehearsal; live cutover waits for warmup checkpoint.
- Observability: added per-holdpoint smoke histograms and replay diffs; console links to sample traces.

Rollback semantics: the playbook exposes three abort modes: fast-revert (squash), partial-drain (graceful rollback of subsequent holdpoints), and quarantine (isolate traffic, escalate to human-latch). See rollback_playbook.yaml for mappings and default thresholds.

Documentation: A new page docs/rollouts/holdpoint-carousel.md includes conceptual diagrams, playbook examples, and a quickstart.

Migration notes: none required for existing profiles; operators must opt-in to use the new profile.

Open items:
- Add CLI tooling to generate rehearsal seeds from production trace (follow-up PR)
- Add deterministic trace replay for embeddings-heavy workloads (research task)
Marco Ruiz: Please add a TTL on holdpoint state to avoid stale anchors in long-lived sessions. Also add an operator-visible metric for rehearsal success rate.
Ava Chen: Added holdpoint_ttl config and a per-holdpoint_rehearsal_success metric in the latest commit. See cfg/rollout_profiles/defaults.yaml for defaults.
Priya Anand: The integration test was flaky on CI; increased harness timeout and added deterministic seeds. approving with nit on docs wording.
Ethan Brooks: Left an inline comment about race conditions in progress_holdpoint; please add a Compare-And-Swap when updating the store.
Ava Chen: CAS implemented in progress_holdpoint and a unit test added to test/unit/holdpoint_state_test.py
Merged after addressing state TTL and CAS concerns; integration flakiness resolved by deterministic seeds. Feature gated and behind rollout_profile opt-in.
Adds holdpoint-carousel promotion strategy with rehearsal shadow replay and a configurable rollback playbook. Backwards compatible with existing rollout policies; new profiles opt-in.
Add: holdpoint-carousel rollout strategy (opt-in) with rehearsal shadow and rollback playbook.

Motivation: traces and token-level telemetry are critical for diagnosing cost spikes, but trace retention and query cost limit our ability to correlate long-tail token bursts across tenants, models, and hardware. This PR introduces a progressive span pruning policy to reduce storage and query noise while preserving signal for expensive invocations, and a new "cost resonance" Grafana dashboard that surfaces correlated token-phase bursts across dimensions (tenant, model, GPU pool, sequence-position).
Diego Morales (review): Nice approach. Two asks: (1) clarify invariant that preserves spans for invocations above X cost; (2) add an integration test that asserts pruned spans still allow computing per-token cost aggregates. Please add comments to pruner.go explaining the safety guarantee.
Author (Asha): Added explicit invariant checks and a new integration test under e2e/synthetic_replay.py that replays high-cost trace fragments and asserts token-level aggregates are unchanged. Also expanded comments in pruner.go to document the safety invariant.
Samantha Liu (review): Dashboard visual is useful. Request: make the tenant selector a multi-select and add a time-aligned token-position sparkline so oncall can quickly see token-phase alignment. Also please add a short note in the runbook about how to react when resonance_score > 0.7.
Author (Asha): Updated dashboard JSON to expose multi-select tenant filter and added per-token-position sparkline panel. Runbook updated with guided remediation steps and links to Dedicated autoscaler docs.
Ethan Zhang (approval): Verified metric names and labels follow conventions. Ran the perf bench — observed 18% reduction in trace index size for 30-day retention with <1% signal loss on top-10 cost queries. Approving to merge.
SRE (comment): When rolling out to production, consider ramping span-pruner threshold by percentage of traffic (10% -> 50% -> 100%) to validate alerting impact.
- Add progressive span pruning to reduce trace index size while preserving high-cost signals.
- Add cost resonance Grafana dashboard to correlate token-phase bursts across tenant, model, and hardware.
- Add metrics: telemetry.token_resonance_score, telemetry.span_prune_reason, telemetry.prune_score_quantile.
- Included runbook and rollout guidance for gradual enablement.
Local unit tests + integration tests passed. E2E synthetic replay validated token-level aggregates pre/post pruning for 10k synthetic invocations. Perf bench shows ~18% index reduction on a 30-day corpus with negligible signal loss for top-k cost queries.
1) Canary in staging cluster for 48h with 10% traffic. 2) Increase to 50% for 24h while monitoring alerts and prune_signal_loss metrics. 3) Full rollout. Dashboard accessible in Grafana under 'Observability/Cost Resonance'.

Motivation: during multi-tenant overloads we observe oscillation between full circuit trips and rapid reopen attempts for low-priority tenants which increases tail latency for everyone. This PR introduces a "tenant standby" SLO adapter and a staged circuit recovery mechanism to (1) proactively place low-priority tenants into a standby mode when cluster SLO headroom drops below configured thresholds, (2) apply a soft, exponentially-windowed backoff to circuit reopen attempts to avoid immediate flapping, and (3) expose operator-tunable controls for staging, warmup, and recovery windows. Design summary: - New SLO adapter component runs in the request-router and subscribes to the global SLO stream (derived from latency/availability aggregates) - When headroom < soft_threshold, non-critical tenants are demoted to standby: requests are routed to a lower-cost slowpath (batching + relaxed re-ranking) and token budgets are throttled down - Standby routing preserves correctness by still honoring request-level hints (priority overrides, emergency flags) - Staged circuit recovery uses a 3-phase policy: probed-reopen (single-probe), capped-reopen (limited concurrency), and fully-open (gradual concurrency ramp) with configurable backoff and jitter - Added metrics and events: standby_transitions, staged_reopen_attempts, staged_reopen_failures, reopen_cooldown_seconds - Operator console: new Liveview panel showing tenant states and recent staged reopen events This description includes implementation notes, tests, and rollout plan.
Miguel Ortega: Can we make the standby selector pluggable per-tenant annotation? I worry about special-casing - addressed by adding per-tenant opt-in flags and console toggle.
Sina Park: Need more visibility into reopen jitter distribution. Please expose percentiles and include example graphs. - added histograms for staged_reopen_latency and a sample Grafana panel in docs.
Ethan Cole: The e2e harness had a race; replace time.Sleep with a deterministic clock. - fixed and added a unit that simulates clock drift.
Miguel Ortega: Approve after nit for config naming (soft_threshold -> headroom_soft_pct) - renamed and updated docs.

Motivation: users report awkward ergonomics when combining credential prefetching with async generator based streaming in the TS SDK; parity gaps vs Go/Python lead to different failure modes under token rotation and transient network retries. This PR introduces a compact credential prefetch adaptor and ergonomic async-generator helpers that unify the lifecycle between TS/Go/Py SDKs while keeping backward-compatible call sites. Changes include: 1) CredentialPrefetcher: a small async factory that preloads short-lived tokens slightly early (configurable grace window) and exposes a lightweight lease object to the generator consumer so callers can opt into pinned credentials for critical sections. 2) AsyncGeneratorAdapter: two helpers (wrapAsyncGenerator and withPrefetch) that make it trivial to attach credential leases and deterministic retry hooks to existing streaming generators without changing upstream code shape. 3) Retry predicate enhancements: add a typed RetryHint returned by the adapter so callers can fine-tune backoff vs fast-fail semantics. 4) Cross-SDK parity shim: minimal API knobs added to the transport layer so Go/Py counterparts can match semantics in follow-up PRs. Compatibility: defaults preserve previous behavior; new helpers are opt-in. Testing: unit tests for lease lifecycle, simulated token rotation, and end-to-end integration using the local mock transport. Also includes updates to docs and a migration note. Impact: small bundle size increase (+2KB gzipped) but meaningful reduction in stream-level race conditions during reauth and fewer transient 401 surface errors in internal canaries.

Priya Nambiar 2026-02-16: Reply: lease is automatically released on generator finally path; adapter exposes onAbort hook for callers who want to take action earlier.

Summary: Adds a compact credential management abstraction ("credential garden") plus a lightweight streaming operator layer ("stream lattice") to improve cross-SDK ergonomic parity for long-lived streaming use cases and authenticated requests. Motivation: We have recurring issues where streamed connections fail mid-flight due to credential rotation or multi-provider fallbacks; SDK consumers also asked for a small, composable generator facade that works well with our token-retry strategies. This PR experiments with an opinionated but minimal surface that is easy to review and port to Py/Go.

What changed (high-level): credentialGarden - a tiny registry that composes credential providers, supports ordered fallback chains, prefetch hooks, soft-fencing (detect and mark failing providers), and a light lease API to surface TTLs without leaking implementation details. streamLattice - a typed generator facade with a few combinators (map, flatMap, merge) and pause/resume hints so the runtime can preemptively refresh tokens before long responses. The lattice operators are intentionally small: they orchestrate backpressure and provide explicit extension points for credential reharmonization.

Compatibility: No breaking public API changes. The new surfaces are additive. Consumers can opt-in by importing credentialGarden and streamLattice. A small version bump (1.17.0) was applied to signal added ergonomics. Parallel ports were scheduled for the Python and Go SDKs to keep parity; this PR updates docs and proposes a migration sketch for the other SDKs.

Files of interest: packages/sdk/src/auth/credentialGarden.ts (core), packages/sdk/src/streams/streamLattice.ts (operators + facade), packages/sdk/src/streams/types.ts (typed stream shapes), packages/sdk/tests/* (unit coverage), packages/docs/snippets/cred-garden.md (how-to).

Testing and CI: Unit tests added for provider failover and a simulated streaming scenario where the active provider returns transient 401s. Lint and typechecks were run. CI initially failed on an edge case in streamLattice when combined with strict tsconfig settings (map operator signature). Fix committed (8a7b3c0) and CI rerun passed. Checks summary: Typecheck: pass, Unit tests: pass (coverage +2%), E2E (integration smoke): pass, Lint: pass. Final CI status: pass.

Review thread (selected excerpts):
- Alex Chen (reviewer): "Great direction. I like the small API surface. Two asks: (1) clarify provider composition rules (what order fallbacks run in and how soft-fencing impacts selection), (2) can we avoid exposing raw Dates in the lease API?"
- Priya (author): "Reply: clarified ordering semantics in the docstring and implemented an opaque Lease type with ttlSeconds instead of raw Date. See commit b9e7f11 and docs snippet."
- Diego Alvarez (reviewer): "Stream combinators look good, but I'm worried about memory if merge is used on many producers. Can we add an explicit maxBufferedEvents config?"
- Priya: "Added optional config to merge (maxBuffered = 1024 default) and added tests that assert bounded buffering behavior."
- Marta Ruiz (reviewer): "Please add migration note for existing users of the old token helpers; also ensure Python/Go tracks the same semantics."
- Priya: "Added CHANGELOG section and a one-page migration guide in packages/docs/snippets/cred-garden.md; opened ENG-8234 for coordination with SDK leads."

Merge notes: After approvals from Alex and Diego and green CI, PR was merged via squash. Merge method: squash and merge. Squash commit message: "introduce compact credential garden and stream lattice; bump sdk to v1.17.0". Post-merge actions: created Linear task ENG-8234 to port APIs and run interop tests across Py/Go SDKs; raised a follow-up in the roadmap for telemetry metrics (credential selection counts, failover events).

Why this is unique: The metaphor of a "garden" (ordered, cultivable provider registry) and "lattice" (small composable operator set) helped constrain the scope to a portable, low-ceremony surface that is easy to replicate across languages. The implementation focuses on operational correctness (soft fencing, lease TTL exposure) and ergonomics for engineers building long-lived streaming integrations.

Notes for backport/release: because this is additive and non-breaking it can be included in the next minor release. The Python/Go SDK teams should coordinate on API names but match semantics (fallback order, opaque lease shape, default merge buffering).

Related: ENG-8234, PM-412, SUP-9981.
Introduce compact credential garden (provider registry + fallback chains) and stream lattice (lightweight combinators + typed generator facade). TS SDK + docs; minor version bumps for parity in Python/Go SDKs. No API breaking changes; improves ergonomic surface for long-running streams and token rotation.

Context and motivation: Several teams reported complexity and brittle behavior during long‑running streaming sessions when credentials expired mid‑stream and SDKs took different approaches (token swap, retry, or raising). This PR introduces a compact, deterministic 'reauth matrix' and a lightweight ergonomic stream facade to unify behavior across TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs. The goal is parity in observable behavior and a simpler consumer surface: automatic deterministic reauth attempts, clear failure semantics, and a single async/iterable-friendly facade for streaming consumers.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a reauth matrix that maps credential provider capabilities to a deterministic retry/handshake policy. Providers declare: canWarmSwap, supportsLease, supportsHeartbeats; the matrix yields an ordered strategy (warmSwap -> leaseRefresh -> failover) used by stream managers.
- Introduces StreamFacade (TypeScript) — a thin wrapper around existing push/pull stream implementations exposing async iteration with explicit .resume() and .shutdown() helpers and deterministic reauth hooks.
- Synchronizes protocol and test vectors with Python and Go SDKs (coordinated commits in their repos; see linked linear tasks).
- Bumps TypeScript SDK minor version to v1.28.0 and adds migration docs.

Commit summary:
- 7 commits, top-level:
  * Add reauth matrix implementation and tests (m: core/auth/reauth-matrix.ts, t: core/auth/reauth-matrix.test.ts)
  * StreamFacade implementation and example (m: streaming/facade.ts, examples/stream-facade.md)
  * Client-side integration hooks and telemetry (m: client/session.ts, observability/metrics.ts)
  * E2E test harness updates (tests/e2e/streaming-reauth.spec.ts)
  * Docs and changelog (docs/migration-1.28.0.md, CHANGELOG.md)
  * Bump version and package metadata (package.json, package-lock.json)
  * Cross-sdk coordination notes (scripts/coord-sync.md)

Files/areas changed (high level):
- core/auth/: reauth matrix, interfaces for credential capabilities
- streaming/: StreamFacade, small adapter changes to existing stream managers
- client/: hook points for deterministic reauth and graceful drain
- tests/: unit and e2e vectors for TTL expiry mid‑stream and simulated provider failures
- docs/: migration guide and examples for stream consumers

Small illustrative snippet (StreamFacade usage):
const stream = client.stream(request);
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  // application logic
}
// explicit shutdown when done
await stream.shutdown();

Design notes and rationale:
- Deterministic reauth: Rather than racey concurrent token swaps across retries, the matrix encodes a priority order. Providers can opt into warm swaps to allow zero‑gap KV cache resumes; otherwise we fallback to lease refresh or explicit failover to a fallback provider. This keeps latency regressions predictable.
- Ergonomics: the StreamFacade flattens multiple internal callbacks into a single async iterator plus explicit lifecycle helpers (.resume(), .shutdown(), .heartbeat()). This reduces application level plumbing and aligns TS ergonomics with the recently adopted Python async iterator surface.
- Observability: each reauth decision emits a small event with reason and latency bucketed into existing streaming metrics so customers can see reauth frequency and whether warm swaps succeed.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Luca Perrin (review): "Nice cleanup. Two asks: make reauth priorities config‑overridable for enterprise (we'll wire from console) and add a unit test for a provider that reports inconsistent capability flags."
- Maya Chen (author): "Addressed — introduced ReauthPolicy.fromConfig and added inconsistent‑capability test; left a follow up Linear to wire console flags (ENG-2073)."
- Amir Patel (review): "Can we avoid extra allocations on hot path in stream pump? The microbench shows +3% allocations in tight loops."
- Maya Chen (author): "Optimized the pump to reuse a small buffer and removed an extra Promise.resolve in the helper; microbench now within 0.5% of baseline."
- Sofia Martinez (approval): "Docs and migration guide are clear; approved pending CI green."

CI and stability notes:
- Initial CI run: failed lint in examples directory (prettier mismatch) — fixed in second commit.
- Unit tests: all pass locally; pipeline flake in linux/e2e one test timed out (retriggered).
- Final CI status: pass across node 16/18, E2E harness on CI stable after timeout fix.

Cross‑SDK coordination:
- This change required small adapter changes in Python and Go SDKs to implement the same reauth matrix semantics and expose a compatible stream facade. Python PR (linked in Linear) implements StreamFacade as an async generator with .shutdown() and .resume() helpers. Go PR adapts the Reader abstraction and adds a small interface for reauth hooks. The TypeScript PR includes a scripts/coord-sync.md with the commit SHAs to check for sync during release.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- Default behavior preserves existing semantics when providers do not declare capabilities. The reauth matrix is opt‑in via provider metadata; if a provider is unannotated we fall back to the preexisting behavior. Migration guide explains how to annotate providers and toggle policies.

Testing and QA:
- Added unit tests for 6 edge cases: token expiry mid‑chunk, provider warmSwap success, warmSwap failure -> leaseRefresh, duplicate reauth attempts suppressed, consumer shutdown during reauth, and heartbeat failure recovery.
- Added E2E test exercising long running stream with simulated token rotations at high frequency.
- Manual cross‑sdk verification performed against local dev cluster for parity.

Follow ups:
- ENG-2073: Console flagging and runtime config for enterprise override.
- SDK-309: Add explicit metrics dashboard and an alert recipe for elevated reauth rate.
- Minor: implement an optional optimistic prefetch token path for ultra‑low latency workloads (tracked).

Merge outcome: Squash‑merged into main. Release PR will be created to publish v1.28.0 packages once downstream Python/Go parity PRs are in.

If you want to try the new facade quickly: see examples/stream-facade.md (included in this PR) for a copy‑paste example and migration snippets.
Minor: Introduce reauth matrix and stream facade improvements; bump TS SDK to v1.28.0. No API surface breaking changes.
