payload.body:
Motivation: onboarding pipelines are ingesting model metadata from multiple sources (manual manifests, partner CSVs, third-party registries). We observed drift in canonical fields (alias vs canonical_name, hw_affinity tags, license canonicalization) which causes noisy diffs in changelogs and makes automated release notes brittle. This PR introduces a small, focused intake pipeline component (intake-canonicalizer) that normalizes and fingerprints key metadata fields and a complementary 'release-notes mosaic' generator that aggregates small, per-model deltas into a human-readable mosaic for release drafts.

Goals: 1) Reduce churn in changelogs by normalizing semantically-equivalent metadata variants (e.g. "MIT" vs "MIT License", gpu_affinity vs hw_affinity) prior to profile diffing. 2) Attach an affinity fingerprint to intake manifests so downstream variant selection and scheduling hints are stable. 3) Produce compact release-note mosaics that group small metadata-only changes across many models into a single digestible section for release managers.

What changed (high level): - New module: services/intake/canonicalizer.py and CLI wrapper tools/bin/intake-normalize. The canonicalizer implements rule-based normalization + a compact deterministic hashing strategy for canonical keys. - New module: tools/release/mosaic_builder.py which consumes normalized intake snapshots and compact per-model deltas to assemble a multi-model mosaic summary (with provenance links). - Onboard hook: a lightweight preflight hook was added to the intake HTTP handler (api/intake/handler.py) to run canonicalization and attach metadata_fingerprint. - Tests: unit tests and a small integration test that runs a representative CSV -> intake -> registry flow. - Docs: docs/onboard/canonicalization.md and a usage example in quickstarts/onboard-mosaic-example.md.

Checklist: - [x] Canonicalization rules implemented for name, license, tags, and hw_affinity. - [x] Deterministic fingerprint algorithm documented and tested. - [x] Release mosaic generator produces grouped human-readable summary for UI and email drafts. - [x] CI integration (unit + smoke) passing. - [x] Backwards-compatible: existing registry records keep original raw_manifest field for audit.

Usage notes: After deployment, existing intake items will be backfilled by a one-off job (scripts/backfill/normalize_snapshots.py). New intake submissions will receive a metadata_fingerprint in the registry response. The mosaic generator is available as tools/release/mosaic_builder.py --input <delta-dir> --output mosaic.md and emits links to intake snapshots for each tile.

Related work and constraints: This design intentionally keeps canonicalization rule-based and deterministic instead of using an ML normalizer to keep transparency for compliance teams. We avoided touching semver/versioning logic; the mosaic groups metadata-only changes and flags any profile/perf changes for separate rollout notes.

Commits summary:
- a1b3d9f: initial canonicalizer module and simple rule set
- b27f4c2: add CLI + ingestion hook, attach metadata_fingerprint
- c8d1aee: mosaic_builder and presentation renderer (markdown + json-lines)
- d4f87bc: tests, docs, and backfill script
- e5a09db: fix edge cases for empty-affinity tags and add CI flakiness guard

Changed areas (high-level paths):
- services/intake/canonicalizer.py
- tools/release/mosaic_builder.py
- api/intake/handler.py (preflight hook)
- scripts/backfill/normalize_snapshots.py
- docs/onboard/canonicalization.md
- quickstarts/onboard-mosaic-example.md
- tests/intake/test_canonicalizer.py

Small code example (CLI):
> tools/bin/intake-normalize --source path/to/raw.csv --dry-run

Testing and CI: Unit tests added for canonicalization edge cases (null tags, multi-aliases) and deterministic fingerprinting. CI matrix runs canonicalizer tests on Python 3.10/3.11, quick smoke integration on a small local sqlite registry. The mosaic generation step is covered by an integration test that asserts grouping behavior for 50 synthetic deltas.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag intakes.canonicalize.enabled = false. 2) Enable for 10% of new intakes and run the backfill job in parallel. 3) Monitor registries and release-mosaic output for diffs for two weeks. 4) Ramp to 100% and deprecate legacy post-processing that attempted to merge aliases.

Open questions: - Should we add a mapping table for corporate-partner license synonyms beyond the current compact heuristics? (follow-up ENG-3241) - Do we want to extend the mosaic renderer to produce structured release note objects for the Release Notes API? (PM follow-up)

This PR is intended to be low-risk and reversible: the canonicalizer writes normalized fields to a separate canonical_manifest and preserves raw_manifest for audits. The mosaic generator is an off-line tool and does not change registry state.

Ethan Rivera: Nice clean separation. One question: how do we avoid collisions in metadata_fingerprint for multi-tenant hosts? Suggest we prefix by tenant id in the hash domain.
Maya Chen: Good point — updated the canonicalizer to include tenant_id salt when present; added tests.
Priya Nair: Will the canonicalizer cause unexpected churn in existing downstream release automation? We should ensure the mosaic only consumes canonical_manifest when feature flag is on.
Maya Chen: Mosaic reads from diffs produced by the reconcile pipeline which respects the feature flag. Added explicit guard in mosaic_builder to ignore canonicalized-only deltas unless flag is set.
Luca Moretti: Small nit: prefer shorter fingerprint (10 bytes) for human-friendly URLs. Is there risk to collision?
Maya Chen: We keep a 16-byte truncated blake2b by default; exposed as config to shrink to 10 bytes with a warning in docs.
payload.title: Introduce intake metadata canonicalizer and release-notes mosaic generator

payload.body:
Motivation: When multiple intake profiles for the same model arrive from different partners/environments we need a deterministic, usage-weighted reconciliation so the registry surface (performance profiles, recommended quantization, changelog blurb) reflects real customer signal rather than noisy probes. This PR introduces a usage-aware 'profile stitcher' that merges incoming onboarding profiles using per-sample weights derived from telemetry and dataset provenance. It also adds an autobrief generator that drafts concise release notes summarizing changes between the active profile and the new stitched profile.

What this PR does (high level):
- Add profile stitcher implementation that: deduplicates metrics, normalizes latency/throughput histograms, applies per-field weighting, and resolves conflicting knobs (quantization/affordances) via configurable heuristics.
- Add autobrief generator that summarizes: top metric deltas, notable config drift (e.g., sequence length, batchability), recommended rollout safety notes, and suggested canary thresholds.
- Add DB migration: profile_stitch_runs table + indexing to support audit and rollback.
- Add CLI and API hooks to invoke stitching as part of onboard pipeline (on-demand and scheduled).
- Add unit/integration tests and small e2e fixture to validate summaries and determinism.
- Update onboarding docs with configuration knobs and migration notes.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of stitcher core algorithm and config
- [x] Autobrief text templates + examples
- [x] DB migration and rollback path
- [x] Tests for deterministic output with fixed seed
- [x] Docs and example CLI usage
- [x] Performance microbench harness for stitcher (latency under typical payload sizes)

Impact and safety: The new stitcher is opt-in by default for existing models; the onboard pipeline exposes a flag `--stitch-mode=off|sampled|always`. For safety we default to `sampled` which runs stitcher asynchronously and writes a draft autobrief for manual review before rolling into the active profile. The autobrief is intentionally conservative in recommendations; full automated rollouts require an additional opt-in.

Migration notes: Run the included migration to create `profile_stitch_runs`. Existing profiles are unaffected until a stitch is executed. See docs/onboarding/usage-stitcher.md for CLI examples and the rollback procedure.

Related work: builds on ENG-3180 (profile canonicalizer) and ENG-2872 (release blurb schema).
Diego Morales: Can we avoid a full histogram recompute for large sample sets? Suggest incremental merge and a capped sample reservoir - addressed in latest commit with reservoir sampler.
Priya Nair: The autobrief language is great but we should avoid numeric thresholds in the first draft; reviewers might misinterpret. Updated templates to include relative qualifiers.
Liam O'Connor: Add an explicit opt-out path for existing CI release gates; otherwise orgs might get unexpected drafts. Added `--stitch-mode=off` and docs note.
payload.title: Add usage-aware profile stitcher and autobrief generation for onboarding

Context: onboarding churn and long autogenerated release notes make it hard for engineers to quickly assess risk and performance impact of new model variants. This PR adds two cooperating subsystems: an intake-sentinel that runs lightweight sanity and cost/perf heuristics during model intake, and a brief-compiler that synthesizes compact, human-friendly changelog fragments and performance highlight cards. Motivation: reduce noise in release notes, accelerate review turnaround, and catch obvious regressions earlier in the pipeline. Scope: sentinel rules (schema checks, common-freeze tokens, latency/cost delta thresholds), telemetry-sampler hook (emits sampled perf traces for new variants), brief compiler (compact prose + delta table + example prompts), automation pipeline changes to attach compiled briefs to model uploads, and tests + migration. Checklist: - implement sentinel engine and rule registry; - add telemetry-sampler integration and sampling policy; - implement brief compiler with templating and delta heuristics; - attach compiled brief to model registry artifacts and release draft; - add unit + e2e tests and CI job; - docs stub for reviewer workflow. Impact: aims to be backward-compatible with existing onboard flows; sentinel blocks uploads only when high-confidence critical violations are detected (configurable); compiled briefs are optional by feature flag. Related: ENG-2173 (onboard quality gates), ENG-2201 (changelog noise reduction).
Diego Morales: Please clarify the threshold logic for latency regressions; is it absolute or relative?
Alyssa Chen: It's relative by default (pct delta over baseline) with an override for absolute ms in config; added comment and unit test to cover both paths.
Priya Natarajan: The sampled telemetry may add cost—can we cap sample rate per-org?
Alyssa Chen: Yes, sample rate is org-scoped and defaults to 0.5% for new variants; rate is configurable via infra flags; noted in docs.
Tomás Silva: Brief templating looks good but include a terse machine-readable summary for automated rollouts.
Alyssa Chen: Added a JSON summary blob alongside the human brief (brief.summary.json) for rollouts and A/B tooling.
Priya Natarajan: Approving pending a green E2E run.
CI: onboard-e2e passed on rerun; lint and unit tests green.
Adds an intake sentinel that enforces lightweight sanity and perf heuristics during model onboarding and a brief compiler that synthesizes compact changelog fragments and perf highlight cards. Config: sentinel rules and telemetry sampling are configurable per-org. Migration: no forced data migration; new briefs appear when feature flag enabled.
Unit tests cover rule evaluator edge cases and template rendering; e2e smoke simulates a model intake with synthetic perf traces and verifies compiled brief attachment. CI adds an on-demand onboard-e2e job that runs in the PR pipeline.
Feature disabled by default; rollout plan: enable for internal onboarding namespace for 2 weeks, monitor noise and blocked uploads, then enable opt-in for customers. Ops should watch telemetry.sampled_rate and sentinel.block_rate metrics.
Sentinel performs schema and token checks only; no model weights or PII are stored by new components. Telemetry sampler respects PII redaction and follows existing telemetry retention policies.
Follow-ups: add automated severity scoring for changelog snippets, integrate with release-brief web UI, and expose brief diffing in model history timeline.
merged (squash) into main after CI green; release draft artifact includes compiled brief and sampled telemetry links.
payload.title: Introduce intake sentinel and brief compiler for compact changelogs

payload.body:
Context: onboarding workflows currently emit verbose release notes that are noisy for small incremental model metadata updates. This PR introduces a light-weight provenance fingerprint and a concise 'micro-bulletin' generator that produces one-line changelog bullets for model releases (intended for automated changelogs and Slack/console snippets). Motivation: reduce developer noise, make quick rollouts auditable, and provide a deterministic lightweight summary for telemetry and alerting. What this PR does: - Adds a deterministic provenance fingerprint algorithm (stable hashing over canonicalized metadata + sample stat summary) that fits in 16 bytes and is friendly to on-chain or audit logs. - Introduces a micro-bulletin generator that synthesizes a 1-2 sentence release blurb from model profile deltas, performance regression highlights, and safety tags. - Wire up a new CLI subcommand `redwood onboard microbulletin` that emits the bulletin and optional JSON payload. - Adds a commit hook for release pipelines so CI can attach micro-bulletins to nightly snapshots and to Linear/GitHub release drafts. - Includes unit and integration tests and example snippets in docs. Acceptance criteria (testable): - Fingerprint is stable across metadata reordering (tests cover canonicalization). - Micro-bulletins are <= 280 chars by default and include delta tokens when >1 field changed. - CICD attaches micro-bulletin to release draft when invoked. - Perf budget check: if average latency regression >5% a warning tag is included and CI marks checklist item. Implementation notes: - Fingerprint uses BLAKE2b-128 on canonical JSON (fields ordering deterministic, arrays trimmed to representative samples). - Micro-bulletin templates are configurable; defaults chosen to avoid leaking dataset names. - The generator avoids free-text summarization models; it's deterministic templating with ordinal heuristics for prominent fields (latency, accuracy proxies, token-cost). Rollout plan: feature-flag gated for 2 weeks in beta; initial consumers: onboarding CLI users and the on-board webhook that populates release drafts. Checklist: - [x] Fingerprint algorithm and unit tests - [x] Micro-bulletin generator and template scaffolding - [x] CLI subcommand and docs - [x] CI hook and sample release draft integration - [x] Perf tests and a small canary run Notes and caveats: This intentionally does not replace full changelogs; it is a concise supplement for high-volume onboarding. Related work: ENG-1982 for release automation, PM-321 for UX requirements.
Alyssa Chen (review): Please ensure the fingerprint is stable when metadata contains extra whitespace or different key ordering. Also request an explicit non-regression test for identical profiles with reordered fields.
Author reply (Sanjay): Added canonicalizer and tests for whitespace/ordering; used canonical JSON with explicit sorting and trimming rules. See test_microbulletin.py::test_fingerprint_stability.
Morgan Reyes (review): The bulletin is helpful but can leak sensitive dataset names in the short form. Suggest default redaction and a config flag to opt-in to full details.
Author reply (Sanjay): Default now redacts dataset identifiers; added --expose-details CLI flag gated by feature-flag and admin role. Documented in microbulletin.md.
Ibrahim Khalid (review): We should include perf-budget gating; if latency regression >5% fail the checklist or at least tag the bulletin.
Author reply (Sanjay): Added perf check step and a 'perf-warning' tag. CI will set status in the release draft and the micro-bulletin will include the warning if threshold exceeded.
Alyssa Chen (approval): Approving after requested tests added and redaction behavior clarified.
- Add deterministic 16-byte provenance fingerprint for model onboarding; stable across metadata reordering and whitespace.
- Introduce 'micro-bulletin' one-line release summaries for automated changelogs and snapshots.
- New CLI: 'redwood onboard microbulletin' and CI hook to attach bulletins to release drafts.
Notes: default redaction of dataset identifiers; opt-in flag available for admins.
Deployed behind feature-flag 'onboard_microbulletin' and enabled for internal beta. Follow-up: hook into Slack release channel and add telemetry metric for bulletin consumption rates.
Canary run (10 model onboards) emitted micro-bulletins for each release; two bulletins included perf-warning tag for a small P50 regression and were flagged in nightly overlay. No downstream failures observed.

payload.body:
Motivation: onboarding churn and subtle regressions during model rollouts continue to be the largest source of post-release incidents. We need lightweight, deterministic gates that validate a model profile before publication and an automated rollback path that both reverts a bad rollout and emits a human-readable changelog entry that explains why. This PR adds: 1) conditional profile gating: a declarative gate DSL (yaml) and a runtime evaluator that runs sample probes against the candidate profile and verifies metric thresholds (latency, token-cost, top-k quality score, sample-based hallucination heuristics). 2) autorollback orchestrator: a stateful controller that watches post-rollout telemetry (stability windows, error spikes, quality regression signals) and automatically triggers a rollback workflow if configured threshold breaches persist for N minutes. 3) changelog composer enhancements: changelog drafts now include gate results and rollback rationale; rollback-aware templates are auto-populated and attached to the release bundle so SRE/product can triage quickly. 4) migration and hooks: an onboarding hook that can be enabled per-team via config; a compatibility shim ensures no forced changes to existing onboard manifests. Implementation highlights: added services/ingest/src/gate_engine.py (gate DSL parser + evaluator), services/ingest/tests/test_gate_engine.py (unit coverage for edge conditions), orchestrator/autorollback/controller.py (small state machine and backoff logic), docs/onboarding/gates.md (usage guide and examples), tools/changelog/renderer.py (template engine + rollback context). Testing and CI: unit + integration suites added; CI initially failed on lint and a flaky probe test which were fixed in the follow-up commit. Local e2e verified rollout -> canary -> autorollback in staging using synthetic telemetry. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated; enable for internal orgs only, canary at 5% with extended monitoring window (24h) then widen; kill-switch to opt-out per-team. Backwards compatibility: none breaking; existing manifests still valid. Linear/Jira: ENG-1792 tracks the gate infra work; PM-88 covers product rollout. Release notes: automated brief included under release_notes field. Misc: this is targeted at improving production safety for model intake and release velocity by providing deterministic pre-publication checks and a fast revert path.
Ava Patel: overall LGTM but please add a small note about probe privacy; we should sample PII-free prompts only.
Priya Kapoor: added probe sanitization and a test for non-deterministic tokens; see latest commit.
Liam Chen: can the autorollback controller avoid cascading rollbacks when region-level blips occur? Consider region-scoped signals.
Priya Kapoor: controller now supports scope='region' vs 'global' and a minimum-breach-duration to reduce noise; updated docs.
Sofia Martins: approved after verifying the e2e logs in staging; one minor nit on template wording fixed.
CI Bot: initial pipeline failed (lint); follow-up commit fixed formatting and unit test race; all checks green.
Added gated onboarding with pre-publication probes and an automated rollback controller. Changelog drafts now include gate verdicts and rollback rationale. Feature-flagged rollouts; enable per-team. See docs/onboarding/gates.md for configuration and examples.

Motivation: onboarding diverse model variants revealed that a single, opaque performance profile does not capture node-level behaviors (NUMA, PCIe topology, mixed-quantization execution) which leads to suboptimal routing and unexpected latency spikes for certain customers. This PR introduces a compact per-node affinity profile that records proven-good node selectors and micro-benchmarks for a model variant, and it wires those profiles into the onboarding path so the registry can publish node affinity hints to the serving router. Additionally, this change adds an autodraft impact notes generator that synthesizes a concise, customer-facing summary of what changed between two profile versions (latency percentiles, cost delta, recommended workflow), which is emitted as the model changelog draft to reduce manual work for release authors. Key changes: 1) new affinity_profiles module with on-disk and API schemas for node-level selectors and microbench results; 2) onboarding CLI flags and server-side hooks to collect quick node probes during initial profile capture; 3) changelog/autodraft that consumes profile deltas and generates a human-readable impact blurb with a confidence score; 4) minor UI doc and template updates for the model release note flow; 5) tests and a small e2e harness that runs in the model-registry CI profile matrix. Backward compatibility: affinity profiles are additive and optional — older deployments ignore them. The autodraft generator produces draft text only and does not auto-merge release notes; it can be disabled via registry config. Checklist: - [x] schema and storage layer (affinity_profiles.py) - [x] onboarding CLI probe and feature flag - [x] delta comparator and draft generator - [x] CI tests for profile ingestion and draft generation - [x] docs and examples - [x] performance baseline validated on internal perf-lab Limitations and open items: short node probes are synthetic and may need extension for long-tail workloads; will follow up with ENG-4231 to add schedule-based multi-node sampling. Related: ENG-4072 (onboard telemetry), SUP-621 (customer report: latency variance on dedicated pools).
Diego: Can we guarantee probes don't add visible delay to onboarding? Maya: Probes are off by default in the public flow and run async in the feature-flagged onboarding path; we added a 2s cap per probe and a batching window. Asha: Need stronger validation for malformed selector strings. Action: added regex sanitize + unit tests. Connor: Approve after you add doc blurb about opt-out and feature flag. Diego: Verified CI matrix includes the small e2e harness and times look stable. Final: approved and squashed.
Add optional per-node affinity profiles to model onboards and an autodraft changelog generator that summarizes profile deltas. Impact: better routing to nodes with validated performance characteristics; reduces manual work for release authors by producing human-friendly impact notes. Opt-in via registry.feature.node_affinity; no breaking changes.

payload.body:
Background: Automated onboarding pipelines and the autosynth release worker occasionally collided when multiple intake jobs touched overlapping model metadata and performance profiles. This caused duplicated changelog fragments and rolling back of in-progress profile calibrations. Motivation: introduce a lightweight coordination primitive (intake lease) and a compact, auditable change representation (changeframe) so the pipeline can safely compose a single, human-friendly release note. What this PR does: 1) intake lease: - Adds a lease-based locking API to the intake service (POST /intake/v1/leases) and a short-lived DB-backed lease store to prevent concurrent release composition for the same model alias/version. - Leases are fair (FIFO) with a configurable TTL (default 30s) and an explicit renew endpoint used by long-running calibrations. - CLI and onboarder hooks now acquire a lease before performing operations that trigger changelog generation. 2) changeframe: - Introduces a normalized changeframe payload (compact JSON) that captures: semantic deltas for metadata fields (license, owner, tags), profile diffs (latency P50/P95 deltas, quantization hints), and example-level sample excerpts used by the release summary generator. - Small binary-safe sample blobs are referenced by content-hash and stored in the probe artifact store to keep changeframes compact. 3) release weaver: - Implements an automated release composer that consumes changeframes and the lease to synthesize a single merged changelog snippet. The weaver deduplicates overlapping profile changes, attaches provenance, and ranks entries by impact score. 4) Additions to the intake CLI: - `rmdrc onboard --draft-release` generates a preview changeframe and uploads it to /intake/v1/preview. 5) Migration & compatibility: - Adds a migration to add leases table and a compatibility shim so older release workers ignore unknown changeframe fields. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag: intake.leases.enabled; default off. Canary the weaver on the internal model-registry team for two weeks before enabling org-wide. Related: ENG-4281 coordinates with the autosynth release worker rewrite. NOTE: This description is one continuous string per repo conventions.
Luca Moreno: Nice approach — the lease TTL default seems short for some calibrations. Can we allow backoff renew attempts and surface a lease owner in the UI?
Maya Patel: Agree on owner visibility; added lease.owner field and updated the /intake/v1/leases GET response. For TTLs we expose TTL and renew_backoff config; default still 30s but can be increased per-team.
Sabrina Ko: Changeframe schema looks good, but the sample blob references need size limits to avoid large payloads. Add a sample size clamp and explicit truncation policy.
Maya Patel: Implemented sample size clamp (default 8KB) and stable truncation with ellipsis markers. Added tests.
Arman Shah: CI initially failed on flakey probe tests — looks like a race in probe/artifact_store_client. Please add a small retry with jitter and an idempotency key.
Maya Patel: Added idempotency key header and a 3-attempt retry with exponential backoff; tests green locally.
Introduce 'intake lease' to prevent concurrent release composition; add compact 'changeframe' format and release weaver which composes changelogs from multiple intake deltas. CLI: onboard --draft-release preview. Feature gated behind intake.leases.enabled. Migration: adds leases table. Impact: reduces duplicate changelog fragments and improves changelog readability for model onboarding rollouts.
Feature flag intake.leases.enabled must be toggled on for canary namespace only. DB migration must be applied before enabling feature. Monitor weaver.impact_score histogram and changeframe.size gauge for unexpected large previews.
Added unit + integration tests for lease acquisition, renewals, changeframe roundtrip, and weaver dedupe rules. Suggested manual test: run onboard CLI against canary registry, request --draft-release, validate preview at /intake/v1/preview and then perform final publish while concurrent dummy intake job attempts to acquire lease.
Feature flagged; if weaver produces malformed previews it will fall back to legacy composer. Lease acquisition failures fallback to optimistic writer with a warning log. Rollback: disable intake.leases.enabled and run a short cleanup job to release stale leases.
payload.title: Add intake lease (onboard lock) and 'changeframe' release composer for concise changelogs

payload.body:
Motivation: onboarding metadata can transitively mutate downstream artifacts (aliases, compatibility hints, affinity tags) which in turn pollutes release notes and can cause confusing churn in model catalogs. This PR introduces two orthogonal features: 1) a dependency-aware metadata rollback engine that uses the model dependency graph to revert only transitive metadata deltas while preserving direct author edits; 2) a chronicle exporter that synthesizes excerpted release drafts highlighting the minimal set of meaningful changes for release managers. Scope: library + CLI + operator hook + small web UI preview. Design summary: we compute a directed dependency graph at ingest time, tag metadata deltas with provenance and a TTL, and provide a selective revert operation that accepts an allowed-provenance whitelist and an impact threshold. The chronicle exporter runs an impact scoring pass against a configurable checklist (latency regressions, tokenizer changes, compatibility tags, dataset license updates) and outputs a compact markdown-like draft suitable for editing or direct publishing to the release pipeline. Backwards compatibility: existing onboard contracts and profile formats are supported; the rollback is opt-in and guarded by feature flag "metadata.rollback.v1". CLI: `redwood-registry chronicle export --model-id <id> --since <tag> --excerpt-only --out draft.md`. Operator hook: `onboard-processor` gains a new step `chronicle-seed` that stores the draft alongside the metadata snapshot. Implementation notes: added an in-memory graph builder with fallbacks to provenance-ledger lookups for large catalogs, lightweight diff/patch applier, new REST endpoints (/api/v1/metadata/rollback, /api/v1/chronicle/export), and a preview renderer used by the console. Tests: unit coverage for graph traversal, integration test for rollback safety (ensures direct author edits are not reverted), e2e export smoke tests. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated rollout to 10% of tenants for 2 weeks, collect onboard audit diffs, then ramp to 100% pending no regressions. See linked Linear tasks for rollout details.
Add a dependency-aware metadata rollback tool and a chronicle exporter that generates concise, excerpted release drafts for model onboarding. Backwards-compatible CLI and operator hooks. No breaking API changes.
Jordan Kim: Can the rollback mistakenly remove manually curated compatibility tags? Please add a safety test.
Ava Martinez: Good point. Added test_rollback_safety.py that asserts curated tags are preserved when provenance != 'transitive'.
Priya Desai: Export drafts look useful, can we include a short diff summary at the top?
Ava Martinez: Added a 3-line diff summary and an impact_score field to the export payload.
Luca Romano: CI flaked on test_integration_pipeline; reran and it passed; approving pending small lint fixes.
Ava Martinez: Addressed lint, rebased and squashed commits per request.
payload.title: Introduce dependency-aware metadata rollback and excerpted release drafts

payload.body:
Context: Model onboarding churn and noisy changelogs make it hard for SREs and product engineers to determine whether a new model profile change is genuinely material or an artifact of sampling. Small profile deltas frequently trigger downstream rollouts and manual reviews even when signals are within the expected instability of the dataset.

Goal: Provide a deterministic, time-bounded mechanism (StabilityWindow) to anchor profile snapshots, produce compact signatures for snapshots, compute reproducible micro-deltas with seeded sampling, and ship an automated rollback/rollforward playbook that can be executed by the curator CLI or surfaced in incident runbooks. This reduces surprise rollouts, makes changelogs more actionable, and shortens troubleshooting time for regressions.

What this PR contains: Adds a StabilityWindow abstraction to the model registry metadata (start_ts, end_ts, seed, snapshot_id), an anchor snapshot generator that emits a compact signature (SHA256 of canonicalized profile + seed) and deterministic sample indices, and a changelog micro-delta algorithm that computes diffs relative to the nearest anchor snapshot using seeded sampling to ensure reproducible summaries. The PR also adds a rollback_playbook generator which synthesizes step-by-step actions (rollback candidate, validation prompt sets, fast compare commands) and wires it into registryctl and the curator alert hook. Includes a backfill script to generate anchors for historical profiles and a small scheduler chart for creating periodic stability windows for high-traffic models.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked (internal RFC): /docs/rfcs/2024-09-stability-windows.md
- [x] Unit tests for snapshot signing and seeded sampling (pkg/onboard/*_test.go)
- [x] Integration test (tests/integration/snapshot_seeded_test.go)
- [x] Registryctl CLI commands and help text
- [x] Docs for operators and curators (docs/onboarding/*.md)
- [x] Backfill script and rollout plan for production models
- [x] Telemetry events for anchor creation and rollback playbook generation

High level changeset (files): pkg/onboard/snapshotter.go: new snapshot builder and signer; pkg/onboard/anchor_windows.go: stability window persistence and query helpers; internal/changes/changelog_diff.go: seeded micro-delta algorithm; cmd/registryctl/anchor.go and rollback_playbook.go: new CLI surface; scripts/backfill_anchor_snapshots.sh: helper to backfill anchors for an environment; docs/onboarding/*: operator and curator-facing docs; tests/integration: end-to-end seeded snapshot test; charts/registry/templates/cronjob.yaml: optional cron for periodic anchor creation.

Design notes and tradeoffs: The snapshot signature uses canonical JSON + a provided integer seed to ensure bit-exact snapshot signatures across languages and runners. The seeded sampling picks deterministic indices from the profile's example corpus; this keeps changelog diffs compact while making them reproducible for triage. We intentionally keep the StabilityWindow notion lightweight so it can be surfaced as an annotation on existing model version entities; longer-term we may add policy-driven window creation (SLO-driven). The rollback playbook generator emits a compact YAML with recommended validation prompts and quick-compare commands; it does not automatically execute rollbacks (safety first).

Commits summary and reasoning: See commits list. Most of the additions are tests, docs, and the snapshot/anchor implementation. The largest implementation risk was ensuring canonicalization of profiles across macOS/Linux/containers; added fixture-based cross-run tests to defend this.

Review notes: This PR intentionally keeps the sampling bucket size conservative (default 250 samples) and exposes configuration for heavy models to raise/lower sample size. We added telemetry events (anchor.created, rollback.generated) to help evaluate signal-to-noise and to guide future defaults.

CI: initial pipeline run hit a flaky e2e that relied on system time; fixed by pinning times in tests and re-running. Final CI status: all checks passing.

Merge: Squashed and merged after approvals. Rolling out to staging with backfill enabled for top 20 models in the next deploy window.

Maya Thompson (2024-11-12): Yes — playbook now emits suggested canary percentages (default 5/25/100) and sample kql queries for latency and token-error-rate. Added to docs/onboarding/rollback-playbook.md.

Added StabilityWindow and Anchor snapshots: deterministic snapshot signing and seeded sampling for reproducible changelogs; registryctl commands to create/list anchors; automated rollback playbook generator for faster triage. Backfill script provided to generate anchors for historical profiles. No breaking changes. Feature is behind a registry feature flag by default.
Rollout plan: deploy to staging, run scripts/backfill_anchor_snapshots.sh for top 20 models, evaluate anchor.created telemetry for 48h, then promote to canary and run backfill for additional models. Feature flag: registry.stability_windows.enabled

Motivation: Onboarding signals (profile deltas, perf regressions, metadata drift) are noisy; product and platform teams need a concise, previewable artifact that summarizes impact and provides a roll-backable draft release bundle before a full publish. This PR introduces an 'onboard previewer' that synthesizes compact diff bundles and an affordance-focused impact statement so stakeholders can review and sign off on releases without full provisioning. Summary: - Adds a preview CLI and a lightweight HTTP preview service that produces a compact diffs bundle (sharded, gzipped) plus an auto-generated impact statement summarizing performance deltas, compatibility hints, and suggested rollout policies. - Integrates a stratified sample-based delta scorer to prioritize examples where QoE diverges. - Produces signed preview artifacts so CI and SRE can verify immutability and enable rollbackable release drafts. - Adds a small web preview panel for quick QA and a README + docs for usage. Key design notes: - Compact diff bundle: delta-only manifest plus sampled telemetry snippets and a small binary patch for large metadata blobs; format is intentionally compact to enable quick transfer to reviewers and to archive as signed preview artifacts. - Sample strategy: stratified sampling across latency, token-length buckets, and failure modes; default 20% sample budget configurable via CLI flag. - Impact statement: affordance-first, includes numeric delta summaries (latency, token cost, pass-rate), notes on quantization/precision changes, and recommended rollout (canary percent + fallback model). - Rollbackable release drafts: preview artifacts are stored in the registry as 'draft:preview/<id>' with signatures and a small manifest that can be atomically swapped to 'release/<version>' by the release pipeline. Checklist: - [x] CLI + service implemented - [x] Sampler and delta scorer implemented - [x] Compact diff serializer and template renderer added - [x] Signed artifact schema and signing helper included (HSM/KMS pluggable) - [x] Docs and quickstart added - [x] Integration tests (e2e preview -> sign -> verify) added Compatibility and migration: - No breaking changes to existing onboard manifests. - Default sampling budget is conservative; operators can opt-in to full sample mode. - Signing integrates with existing KMS abstraction; if no KMS configured the previewer emits unsigned artifacts but notes the risk in the output. How to use: - CLI: onboard-preview generate --manifest path/to/manifest.yaml --sample-budget 0.2 --out preview-123.tar.gz - Web: POST the manifest to /api/preview and follow the returned preview ID to the UI. - To promote a preview to a draft release, run: onboard-preview promote --preview-id preview-123 --target draft/v1.0.1 Security and SRE notes: - Previewer emits a signed metadata stamp (if KMS present) and a short provenance JSON included in the artifact. - The CI workflow has an optional step to verify signatures and run a light smoke-run on Dedicated hardware. Performance: - The sampler runs in O(n) over telemetry shards; renderer is streaming-friendly and memory-bounded. - Typical end-to-end preview generation for moderate manifests (~1000 samples) completes in ~45s on a 4CPU job (numbers in docs). Caveats: - The previewer is intentionally opinionated about sampling; teams with strict deterministic QA should run full evaluation separately. - Signed preview artifacts are persisted but treated as ephemeral until promoted to a signed release.
Jasper Li (2024-10-03): Can the sampler be deterministic with a seed flag so QA can reproduce a preview?
Author (Priya Menon) (2024-10-03): Added --seed flag and documented deterministic mode in README; sampler defaults remain stratified random.
Nora Patel (2024-10-05): Suggest reducing default sample budget from 0.3 to 0.2 to keep CI costs down.
Author (Priya Menon) (2024-10-05): Updated default to 0.2 and added an opt-in full-sample flag for heavy QA runs.
Ethan Shaw (2024-10-07): Integration test flakes on macOS runners; moved test to Linux-only and added retry logic in CI.

Motivation: onboarding workflows and the changelog pipeline have diverged across historical model alias usages. Multiple aliases (short-name, upstream id, release tag) were being treated as first-class keys in the registry which caused duplicate profiles, flaky profile matching in inference routing, and noisy release notes. This change introduces a deterministic canonicalization step for model identifiers, attaches a stable canonical_id to every profile/variant, and adds a staged changelog stream (draft -> canary -> stable) that allows automated, non-destructive release note promotion with explicit canary guardrails. Summary of changes: - Metadata: add `canonical_id` to the model metadata schema and deprecate treating aliases as separate model keys. Canonical_id is a stable opaque id keyed by upstream provenance + fingerprint. - Alias resolver: implement an alias resolution layer that maps incoming onboarding aliases (hf:*, vendor:*, local:*) to canonical_id; resolver supports a best-effort fuzzy-match for short names with a confidence score stored in metadata. - Migration: add a one-shot migration utility (`scripts/migrate-aliases-to-canonical`) which deduplicates existing model entries, consolidates profiles, and emits a migration report. The migration is idempotent and can be run safely in Dedicated and Private environments. - Profiles: add `perf_signature` to performance profile payloads (a short hash computed from baseline metrics and tokenizer config) and wire it into the release diff algorithm so we surface only meaningful regressions. - Changelog: introduce `staged-changelog-stream` service that takes metadata deltas and materializes note fragments into a three-stage channel: draft (editable), canary (auto-generated, gated by perf/regression checks), stable (human-reviewed and publishable). The stream emits events suitable for the Console to subscribe and render per-model release status. - CLI & API: onboarding CLI gained `--canonicalize` flag; the registry API accepts alias payloads and returns canonical_id in responses. Backwards compatibility: the resolver accepts old-style primary_key lookups and logs deprecation warnings. Testing & rollout: included a migration-run smoke test, unit tests for alias resolution heuristics (edge cases for hyphenation and numeric suffixes), end-to-end changelog promotion test, and perf-signature regression checks. Rollout plan: 1) deploy alias resolver (read-only) to staging; 2) run migration in a dry-run mode and inspect report; 3) enable write-mode with the CLI flag for a subset of low-traffic tenants; 4) promote staged changelog to canary and watch perf guardrails for 72h; 5) flip stable publish after PO review. Observability: added metrics (alias_resolve.success, alias_resolve.confidence_bucket, staged_changelog.promotions) and traces for migration. Why this is different: previous PRs focused on changelog composition or profile deltas; this combines canonical identity stabilization with a changelog promotion lifecycle and a lightweight performance signature so both registry correctness and release note noise are solved together. Risks & mitigations: - Risk: canonicalization can merge entries that teams expect to be separate. Mitigation: migration report contains an explicit `merge_candidates.csv` and the CLI exposes `--skip-merge` to allow manual reconciliation. - Risk: perf_signature false positives. Mitigation: threshold tuning and a fallback to human-reviewed canary promotions. Related: ENG-8241 (onboard churn), ENG-8390 (perf diff affordances), SUP-3321 (customer reported duplicate profiles).
Owen Park: Nice decomposition. Two comments: (1) can we avoid computing perf_signature for tiny sample sizes? (2) migration script should not delete until report is acked.
Nia Ramirez: Good catches — perf_signature now requires a min_sample_size (configurable) and migration script writes a 'pending_merges.json' rather than in-place deletes. Added a CLI flag --apply-merges for explicit action.
Li Wei: The fuzzy alias matching worries me; can we expose the confidence score via the API and make default behavior only exact-match?
Nia Ramirez: Done — resolver defaults to exact match; fuzzy behavior must be explicitly requested by passing fuzzy=true. Confidence score is returned in the response header `X-Alias-Confidence` and persisted when fuzzy matches are used.
Samir Dutta: Please add a metric for staged_changelog.promotions.failed so SRE can alert on noisy promotions.
Nia Ramirez: Added metric and an alert playbook entry in docs/migration-runbook.md. Also added a Circuit Breaker that halts promotions after N failures in 1h.
Owen Park: CI flaked on the migration smoke test once, re-ran and it's green. Approving to merge after squash.
Li Wei: Approve. Also left a minor doc nit which I fixed in a follow-up commit.
Status: CI all checks passed after rerun. Merge method: squash and merge.

Adds a provenance-first changelog generator and a compact versioned_metrics schema to make release notes reproducible and machine-readable. Motivation: model onboards and performance profile changes currently produce free-form release notes that are hard to diff, verify, and consume by downstream tooling (console, release summaries, SDK release hooks). This PR introduces a templated changelog writer that consumes existing provenance fields (uploader, model_digest, dataset_manifest, profile_snapshot_id) and the new versioned_metrics bundle (a small JSON blob with named metrics + sample metadata). Key features: 1) changelog templates stored in templates/changelogs/*.tmpl and a CLI command mr-changelog generate --model MODEL_ID --from SNAPSHOT --to SNAPSHOT that emits both human and compact machine summary; 2) versioned_metrics schema and migration that stores per-profile metric names, units, aggregation window, and a provenance stamp; 3) automatic inclusion of a minimal delta section that lists metric-level deltas and quality regressions with links to evaluation artifacts; 4) hooks that allow the model onboarding flow to opt-in to auto-drafting a changelog and attach the generated artifact to the model version; 5) test coverage for generator logic and a small e2e workflow used in CI. Backwards compatibility: existing changelog text fields are preserved and the generator will fall back to the legacy narrative when provenance is incomplete. The migration is additive and guarded behind a feature flag 'versioned_metrics_enabled' to allow staged rollout. This description includes a high-level commit summary and review notes below.
Lucas Nguyen: Could we include a compact hash field in versioned_metrics so rollbacks can correlate metrics to the exact artifact?
Maya Patel (author): Added provenance_hash to versioned_metrics and included compat code that regenerates it from model_digest if missing.
Priya Singh: The default template is wordy for release notes; can we add an option to produce a one-line summary for dashboards?
Maya Patel: Added 'summary_mode' flag to CLI and an abbreviated template 'summary.tmpl'. Updated docs with examples.
Diego Ramos: CI e2e failed on first run due to a timing issue when attaching artifacts. Suggest retry logic and metrics in logs.
Maya Patel: Implemented exponential backoff for artifact attach, added detailed CI logs; e2e now stable.
Priya Singh: Approved on second pass after docs updates.
Lucas Nguyen: Approved and requested squash merge to keep migration atomic.
Adds a provenance-aware changelog generator and an optional versioned_metrics payload for model profile releases. Includes CLI tooling (mr-changelog), templates, migration, and docs. Rollout guarded by feature flag 'versioned_metrics_enabled'.

Context / motivation: model onboarding churn has made release notes noisy: small metadata-only updates (typo fixes, curator comments) and large perf-affecting changes appear at the same verbosity level. Teams want concise, signal-rich changelogs that call out performance and runtime compatibility changes while suppressing low-impact edits. This PR adds two complementary pieces: (1) an onboarding contract mapper that normalizes and stamps the metadata that matters for serving/runtime compatibility, and (2) a traffic-weighted release-notes generator that scores deltas based on historical usage and staged rollout traffic to prioritize changelog sections.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduce a lightweight onboarding_contract_mapper that: canonicalizes fields (model.aliases, quantization_profiles, runtime_hints), emits a stability fingerprint, and records a "compatibility_contract" object (stringified map) that downstream systems use for gating. The mapper runs in the intake path and as a pre-commit hook for model manifests.
- Add a traffic_weighted_changelog generator service that: consumes delta events and model traffic signals (ingest from telemetry snapshots), computes an impact_score that weights changes by percent-traffic and latency/cost delta, and outputs a compact release note with prioritized bullets (Performance, Runtime Compatibility, Behavioral, Metadata). The generator also groups low-impact deltas into an "Other metadata edits" bucket to reduce noise.
- Provide migration tooling: a one-off migrator that rehydrates existing model profiles with compatibility_contract keys and generates one sample traffic-weighted release digest for the last 30 days (stored as samples/release-digest-*.ndjson).
- Add unit + integration tests and CI job to validate contract_mapper idempotence and changelog ranking monotonicity.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- We intentionally keep the compatibility_contract as a stable, compact string map to avoid exploding DB schema changes; the contract is designed to be backward-compatible for a two-release window.
- Impact scoring is heuristic (traffic percent * normalized perf delta + deprecation_penalty + security_flag), not ML-driven; we opted for deterministic, explainable rules in this iteration to keep auditability simple.
- The changelog generator does not automatically publish to user-facing release pages; it emits drafts for the release curator UI to review first. Future work could hook canary rollout metrics for live weighting.

Checklist:
- [x] Mapper implementation with canonicalization rules
- [x] Compatibility fingerprint + stamping
- [x] Changelog generator with traffic weighting and bucketing rules
- [x] Migrator and sample output artifacts
- [x] Unit tests for mapper and generator scoring
- [x] Integration tests with sample telemetry snapshot
- [x] CI job added and passing

Commits summary: single-squash merge with these commit headlines:
- feat(onboard): add onboarding_contract_mapper and canonicalizer
- feat(changelog): implement traffic_weighted_changelog service and API
- chore(migration): add rehydrate migrator and sample output generator
- test: add unit/integration tests for mapper + changelog scoring
- ci: add changelog-scoring CI job and test fixtures

Changed areas / notable files (high level):
- src/ingest/contract_mapper.py -- core canonicalization logic and fingerprinting rules
- src/ingest/rules.yaml -- canonical field mappings and normalization rules (documented)
- src/changelog/weighting.py -- impact scoring and bucketing algorithm
- src/changelog/service.py -- API to produce draft release digests
- tools/migrators/rehydrate_compat_contract.py -- one-off migrator scaffolding
- tests/test_contract_mapper.py, tests/test_changelog_scoring.py -- test coverage for idempotence and monotonicity
- ci/workflows/changelog-scoring.yml -- new CI workflow validating scoring determinism

Review conversation (high level):
- Arielle Chen (review): "Nice separation between contract and draft generator. Two asks: (1) make fingerprint stable across minor metadata edits, (2) add examples in rules.yaml for quant profiles."
- Author reply (Priya): "Addressed: fingerprint uses a whitelist of fields and salt; added quant examples + unit tests that exercise the stability property."
- Mateo Alvarez (review): "Can we avoid coupling telemetry ingestion directly in the changelog service? Suggest adding a small adapter interface so we can swap sources."
- Author reply: "Added TelemetryAdapter interface and a simple in-memory adapter for the migrator; production wiring kept in ingestion config. Also added an integration test using the adapter."
- Jonah Beck (approval): "Approach looks good; tests pass and migration artifacts useful for manual validation. Approving."

CI summary: all checks passed on merge. Notable checks:
- unit-tests (python): pass
- integration-tests (slow): pass (ran against test telemetry snapshot)
- lint: pass
- changelog-scoring-ci: pass (validates determinism across repeated runs)

Migration notes for operators: run tools/migrators/rehydrate_compat_contract.py --window 30d --out samples/ to generate sample release digests. The migrator writes ndjson artifacts and a dry-run log (migrations/log-48290-dryrun.txt). The migrator is idempotent; it will skip entries that already have a compatibility_contract stamp.

Security / privacy notes: The compatibility_contract intentionally omits consumer telemetry identifiers; the traffic weighting uses aggregated percent traffic metrics only (no PII). The migrator artifacts are stored in internal-only buckets by default.

Release notes (internal):
- Added onboarding contract mapper to canonicalize model metadata and emit a stable compatibility fingerprint.
- Added traffic-weighted release-notes generator to prioritize changelog items by inferred impact.

payload.body:
Motivation: many incoming model manifests during onboarding are sparse (missing tokenizer, context_window, or quantization hints). This causes manual back-and-forth, slows rollouts, and leads to inconsistent performance profiles in the registry. This PR adds two complementary features: 1) an inference pass that derives best-effort metadata from artifacts and lightweight probing; 2) a heuristic compatibility layer that scores and recommends fallback variants (smaller context, quantized variants, or compatible back-compat model family) and emits a compact release-note snippet summarizing the inferred changes for changelogs.

What this changes (high level):
- New inference module: src/onboard/infer_metadata.py. Runs during CLI/HTTP onboarding if manifest is missing fields; performs tokenizer detection (by byte-pattern + small sample tokenization), context window estimation from model config and param count heuristics, and dtype/quantization suggestions via probe-run with short input. Inferred values are persisted under the model version as `inferred_metadata` and flagged in UI/CLI.
- Compatibility layer: src/onboard/compat_layer.py. Computes a compatibility score across known variants (fp16, int8/ggml, reduced-context variants). Provides ranked recommendations used by onboarding UX and the release-note synthesizer. Intended to be conservative (prefers recommend-not-enforce).
- Release-note synthesizer: tooling that converts profile diffs and the inferred_metadata delta into a concise 1-3 line changelog snippet. Hook added to the release draft pipeline to auto-populate candidate notes for reviewers. Implemented in src/onboard/changelog_synth.py and wired into the assemble pipeline.
- CLI flag: --force-infer / --no-infer to opt into/out of inference pass. Default is on for self-serve flows and off for enterprise-private installs (explicit opt-in via config).
- DB migration: scripts/migrate_add_inferred_metadata.sql adds a nullable jsonb column `inferred_metadata` to model_versions table, with an inexpensive backfill for recent uploads.
- Tests + docs: tests for heuristic scoring and tokenizer detection (tests/test_infer_metadata.py), plus updated onboarding docs (docs/onboarding.md) and an example showing how to opt-out.

Why this approach: automated inference reduces manual triage for >50% of incoming model manifests we saw in the last quarter; the compatibility layer improves rollout resilience by recommending safe fallback variants rather than causing silent mismatches at serving time. The changelog snippet automation reduces author friction when releasing slight-profile-only changes.

Security & correctness notes: the inference pass is read-only against model artifacts and does not execute arbitrary model code; the short probing run uses a sandboxed runtime with a 2-token sample and strict CPU/GPU timeouts. All inferred metadata is explicitly marked as inferred and surfaced for human approval before it is used for automated rollouts.

Checklist:
- [x] inference engine and compatibility scoring implemented
- [x] DB migration and backfill script added
- [x] CLI wiring and opt-out flags
- [x] unit tests covering tokenizer detection and scoring heuristics
- [x] docs and changelog synth examples
- [x] QA: manual sample set verification (100 models)

Follow-ups (roadmap):
- Add telemetry to measure inference accuracy and false-positive rate (ENG-2210 follow-up).
- Add a compact human-review UI to accept/reject inferred metadata during onboarding.

Related work: reuses tokenization heuristics from the eval-harness token-utils module and compatibility scoring design from earlier perf-canary work. Links: Linear ENG-2012, ENG-2210.

Summary: Adds pragmatic, opt-out inference for sparse manifests, a conservative compatibility layer for recommending fallbacks, and automated short release-note drafting for profile-only changes. This should reduce onboarding friction and improve release hygiene for incremental model updates.
Auto-infer missing model metadata (tokenizer, context_window, dtype) when onboarding sparse manifests.
Introduce a heuristic compatibility layer that suggests fallback model variants and quantization profiles for serving/resilience.
Generate concise release-note snippets from profile diffs to automate changelog creation.

Elena Park: The probe is intentionally tiny (2-token) and runs with a 3s timeout; CI paths skip the probe unless --force-infer is set. Updated docs to clarify.
Marina Soto: Please add an explicit opt-out config for Private installs and mark inferred_metadata as non-authoritative in the API schema.
Elena Park: Added --no-infer and a config toggle; schema now returns {source: 'inferred'}. Added tests asserting field is flagged.
Alexei Kuznetsov: The compatibility scoring seems to favor smaller-context variants too aggressively; can we add a penalty for quality regression?
Elena Park: Added a configurable penalty weight and updated scoring tests. Default weight chosen to prefer preserving quality unless resource savings are substantial.
Marina Soto: Docs look good. Approved pending CI green.

payload.body:
Context: onboarding churn and noisy changelogs are making it hard for downstream teams to interpret model upgrades and for the registry to retain only actionable performance profiles. This PR introduces a temporal-tenure concept (tenure score + decay) for model versions and an autosynth changelog curator that drafts compact release notes by prioritizing stable signals. Goals: 1) make model version history size-bounded and preference-aware, 2) automatically synthesize concise changelog bullets focused on perf regressions/improvements and metadata drift, 3) attach a retention/archival policy for performance profiles tied to tenure. What I changed (high level): - Add tenure scoring engine (registry/onboard/tenure.py) to compute a decayed stability score for each model variant based on traffic, eval baseline pass rate, and time-since-onboard. - Introduce profile-decay heuristics (profiles/decay_score.go) and a retention policy that marks low-tenure profiles for cold storage. - Add autosynth curation service (registry/changelog/autosynth.py) that consumes tenure signals + perf deltas and drafts 1-3 sentence release snippets. - Wire the curator into the existing release pipeline: release-assembler now calls autosynth for non-enterprise auto-drafts and stores the curated blurb in manifest.metadata.changelog_snippet. - Add an opt-out tag for customers and an API flag (onboard.v1:retain=false) to pin versions regardless of tenure. - Add docs and migration guide (docs/onboarding/temporal-tenure.md) and unit/integration tests. Motivation and tradeoffs: tenure reduces noise and storage costs but can surface risk if teams rely on cached perf profiles; that risk is mitigated by the pin/retain API and 30-day grace window before cold-archival. The autosynth aims for high precision over recall — it will only include changes with signal above a configurable threshold to avoid noisy autogenerated prose. Checklist: - [x] tenure scoring algorithm implemented + tests - [x] autosynth draft generator implemented + e2e integration test - [x] migration guide and docs - [x] telemetry: added tenure_histogram and autosynth_accept_rate metrics - [x] feature-flagged rollout (default on for non-enterprise orgs) Backwards compatibility: existing manifests gain a new optional field changelog_snippet; clients ignore it if absent. Performance impact: small CPU overhead in the release pipeline; profile decay runs as a daily background job. Related: ENG-8234 (tenure scoring), PM-1198 (changelog UX), SUP-5421 (customer request to auto-summarize).
Added temporal-tenure versioning to manage model history size and signal-driven changelog autosynthesis. New optional manifest field 'changelog_snippet' contains concise, autogenerated release notes when available. Retention policy for performance profiles introduced; low-tenure profiles are cold-archived after a configurable grace window. Added feature flag and opt-out API for enterprise customers.
Jordan Rivers (reviewer): Can we avoid increasing the default retention window? Suggest keeping 30 days but make cold-archive async.
Maya (author): Implemented async archival with a 30-day grace window and added a feature flag for enterprise orgs.
Priya Nair (reviewer): Autosynth language needs a safety gate for PII-sensitive model notes. Add a redact step or skip draft if sensitivity detected.
Maya (author): Added a sensitivity-check hook using existing probe tags; autosynth will skip drafts for flagged manifests and emit autosynth_skip_reason telemetry.
Ethan Zhou (approver): Verified perf tests; tiny CPU overhead. Approving pending CI flake fix which was rerun.
PR approved by: Ethan Zhou, Priya Nair

payload.body:
Motivation: Full-profile runs for large models are expensive and often block onboarding or iterative releases. Small regressions can be missed because we do not have a compact, cost-aware estimate of how much of a model's real-world workload a profile covers. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) a sampled-coverage metric (profile_coverage_score) computed by running a stratified sampling harness across prompt buckets and sequence-length bands to estimate how much of an expected workload the existing profile touches, and 2) a concise release-brief generator that synthesizes the delta between two profile snapshots into a short, human-readable blurb for release notes and on-call triage. The description below explains the approach, implementation, and operational controls. Implementation summary: - sampling harness: new module registry/profiling/sampled_coverage.py implementing reservoir sampling per bucket, histogram-based weighting, and confidence-interval estimation. The harness integrates with existing profile collectors so it can run lightweight passes (10-50 samples per bucket) that cost orders of magnitude less than full calibrations. - profile_coverage_score: a normalized 0..1 score attached to profile metadata that estimates the fraction of observed workload coverage along with a 95% CI string. This is stored as profile.metadata.coverage_score and surfaced in the UI and the API. - brief generator: registry/tools/briefgen.py converts two profile snapshots into a 3-5 sentence brief with top 3 token-level regressions/improvements, latency P50/P95 drift, and a short suggested remediation (e.g., increase sample budget, run full calibration). Briefs are generated as part of the existing release-note pipeline and attached to model releases as release_brief.txt and a concise markdown field. Operational controls and safety: - default sample budgets are conservative and configurable per-organization via registry/config/profiling.toml. - briefs are flagged as "summary only" and always link to detailed diffs; the generator never hides raw numbers. - sampling runs are opt-in during onboarding to avoid surprise compute charges; repository defaults enable it for nightly delta checks. Context: customers and internal curation teams have asked for a way to attach time-bound/embargoed metadata to model intake that is cryptographically auditable and gated for release notes. This PR adds a small provenance ledger that signs embargoed metadata, exposes an ACL-aware retrieval path, and generates a compact "microdigest" used by the Console and release automation to show concise delta-first release snippets. Motivation: reduce manual release-note drafting, centralize embargo handling for sensitive commercial or regulatory annotations, and produce deterministic microdigests for downstream QA and changelog automation. Changes: 1) API: intake endpoint accepts optional 'embargo_until' and 'embargo_reason' metadata; embargoed fields are stored encrypted and recorded in the provenance ledger with signer metadata. 2) Ledger: lightweight append-only ledger table with signer_id, signed_hash, ttl and visibility flags; signer service signs using an internal key (KMS-backed) and publishes short receipts. 3) Microdigest generator: new service that computes a compact human-friendly summary from model profile deltas (perf metrics, metadata fields, and affinity hints) and includes risk flags when embargoed fields are present. 4) UI: Console exposes a microdigest preview and marks embargoed items with an eye icon and 'until' date. 5) Migration: DB migration to add ledger table + retention TTL. Motivation: As the number of onboarded model candidates grows, reviewers need a compact, visual summary of where a model stands across signal dimensions (performance, cost, safety, sample coverage) and a way to surface the most relevant changes in release notes. This PR adds two pieces: (1) a curation heatmap generator that aggregates onboarding telemetry into tile scores, and (2) a release-teaser generator that synthesizes 1-2 line 'teaser' cards used in changelogs and release drafts. Changeset: - telemetry/curation_heatmap.py: heatmap aggregation and scoring engine (configurable weights) - telemetry/fixtures/sample_intake.json: small sample for unit tests and local dev - services/release_teaser/service.py: heuristics that convert profile deltas into teaser text templates - ui/components/CurationHeatmap.vue: frontend tile grid + legend - docs/curation/heatmap.md: usage, tuning knobs, and examples - tests/test_heatmap.py, tests/test_release_teaser.py: unit + integration tests Note: description is intentionally compact; see changed_files and commits for more detail. Checklist: - [x] Aggregation and scoring; weight config - [x] Unit tests for edge cases (no telemetry, partial metrics) - [x] End-to-end smoke test (local fixture) - [x] Basic component for Console (static data binding) - [x] Release notes generator implemented and integrated with draft pipeline Rollout: feature gated behind `curation_heatmap` FF. Start with internal rollout for model-review team, then flip for all curators after 2 weeks of usage metrics. Backout: revert FF and remove teaser consumer if false positives in teaser generation are reported.

Technical notes: Heatmap tiles compute a normalized score in [0,1] per dimension: perf_delta (lower is better -> inverted), cost_change (lower better), safety_flags (count scaled), sample_coverage (fraction). A weighted sum yields a 'priority' score used to dim/highlight tiles. Release teaser heuristics: prefer perf deltas > 5% or coverage increases > 10% or newly triggered safety gates. Teaser text is deterministic and templated to avoid hallucinations.

Why unique: This PR focuses on curator UX (visual+text summary) rather than raw profiling or changelog automation. It bridges telemetry->UI->release-notes with conservative heuristics and a feature flag for safe rollout.
Introduce a curation heatmap that surfaces onboarding signals (coverage, perf delta, safety flags) and a small service that generates concise release teaser cards for changelogs. Enables faster triage and more informative release notes. No API breaking changes.

Context and motivation: as customers onboard larger open models we continue to get questions about recommended quantization profiles and hardware suitability. Current onboarding produces a generic perf profile and a dense changelog entry; customers then request bespoke quant/affinity advice for their hardware (A100, H100, RTX-class) which slows reviews. This PR introduces three coordinated features: (1) a deterministic hardware-aware 'intake fingerprint' that captures model memory/KV characteristics and peak transient working set; (2) a lightweight sampling micro-benchmark that runs as part of intake to produce a short performance histogram across representative sequence lengths; and (3) a quantization-suggestion engine that maps the fingerprint+microbench to ranked quant profiles and a rollback-safety score. Finally, a release synopsis automator synthesizes an audience-aware short blurb for release notes (developer, SRE, product) to reduce manual release copywork.
Implementation: added registry/intake/fingerprint.py with stable fingerprint schema and provenance header; integrated sample_microbench into intake flow; quant_suggester implements a rule-and-ML hybrid mapping (heuristics + small tree model trained on past onboarding signals) and emits suggested quant profiles and expected delta in token cost; stamps.py adds signed metadata stamps for fingerprint and suggestion sets; synopsis_automator creates brief natural-language summaries tailored by audience tag; added tests and a CI bench workflow. API: intake_handler exposes a /v1/intake endpoint flag to opt-in to microbench. Docs: onboarding guidance and QA checklist updated. Rollout: feature gated behind feature flag registry.intake.hw_fingerprint; default off for existing customers.
Unit tests for fingerprint stability and stamps; integration tests exercising intake->quant-suggester mapping; microbench run in CI against a small fixture model to verify histogram shape and exporter metrics; manual validation on internal H100 and A100 runners with three representative models (small/medium/large) to compare suggested quant profiles against prior baseline. Perf benchmarks included in PR; overall microbench runtime kept sub-60s for opt-in runs.
No breaking changes to existing intake schema unless hw_fingerprint is enabled. Suggested profiles are additive metadata; users can opt to ignore suggestions. Stamps are backwards-compatible (new optional header).
Merged behind gated feature flag registry.intake.hw_fingerprint=false by default. Early access enabled for TrustedOnboarders cohort. Phase 1: opt-in internal teams and early customers; Phase 2: enable for self-serve with opt-out via account setting; Phase 3: default-on for new onboardings after telemetry stabilization. Monitoring: add alerts for microbench failures, large variance in suggested quant deltas, and rollback-safety score regressions.
Added hardware-aware intake fingerprint and opt-in microbench to generate deterministic model HW signatures; introduced quantization-suggestion engine which recommends ranked quant profiles and a rollback-safety score; automated audience-tailored release synopses for onboarding changes. Feature is gated behind registry.intake.hw_fingerprint and rolled out to early access cohorts. Notes: suggestions are advisory; continue to validate on customer's production workloads.
Follow-ups created: ENG-4725 (augment suggestion training data), ENG-4750 (expose rollback-safety to console), ENG-4782 (add more device labels for SMB GPUs). Included example config in examples/onboard-sample/hw-probe.yaml.
Maya Alvarez (reviewer): Can we make the fingerprint schema extensible for future HW attributes? Request: add schema versioning and a clear migration test - addressed in stamps.py and profile_versioner.py, added tests.
Jonah Kim (reviewer): microbench runtime feels long for large models. Suggest a configurable sample budget - added sample_budget env and default to minimal probe sequence lengths. Updated docs.psf
Sofia Petrov (approver): Minor nit on wording in synopsis templates, approved after fix.
Ethan Brooks (author): replied to all comments, added follow-up tasks: ENG-4725 to expand the training dataset for the suggestion model, and ENG-4721 to add cloud-region-aware suggestions.

Context: onboarding churn and noisy release notes for model uploads make it hard for downstream teams to interpret compatibility and quality impacts. This PR introduces two coordinated features: 1) intake quality tiers (bronze/silver/gold) computed from a small probe suite and metadata heuristics; 2) a compact change indexer that generates a concise changelog fragment and a deterministic index token that surfaces in model manifests. Goals: reduce manual curation for release briefs, make basic quality signals machine-readable for routing and rollout automation, and produce compact changelog snippets for release notes automation. Includes a lightweight signing hook that allows release-generator to attach a provenance token (no HSM integration in this PR).Scope: changes to intake pipeline, onboarding CLI, manifest schema, changelog composer, and a small set of UI annotations for the registry.Why now: teams have requested faster auto-briefs for model patches and easier gates for Dedicated deployments (see ENG-987).This PR contains: checklist: - [x] compute probe-driven quality score and map to tier (bronze/silver/gold) - [x] add tier to manifest and onboarding API - [x] implement compact change indexer that hashes key fields to make short index tokens - [x] wire change index into release-note draft generator - [x] add unit + integration tests for pipeline and CLI - [x] docstring and API surface docs updated - [x] simple signing hook for provenance token (non-production key) Rollout plan: stage rollout behind feature flag 'intake_quality_tiers' for 2 weeks with telemetry; backfill is optional and can be run for recent 30 days of ingests.Compatibility notes: manifest adds optional fields 'quality_tier' and 'change_index' and is backward compatible with existing consumers; onboarding clients older than 2025-12 must use graceful fallback.Hosted automation: release composer will prefer compact change fragments when present; else will fall back to auto-draft heuristics.Contacts: @aisha for infra, @samir for eval, @evelyn for release tooling. Linked work: ENG-987 (auto-briefs), ENG-1024 (dedicated gating).
Samir Patel: Left an inline question on scorer edge cases — how do we handle TTR (time-to-response) probes for large-context models? || Aisha: Reply: TTR is normalized by model tokenizer length; added clarifying comment and unit test to cover 0-length edge case.
Evelyn Shaw: Can the compact change indexer collate multiple tiny deltas into a single fragment? || Aisha: Reply: yes, indexer supports coalescing by change-type; added option in composer (--coalesce-small-deltas) and tests.
Jian Li: Suggest adding a telemetry counter to measure fraction of ingests that map to each tier. || Aisha: Reply: Added metrics.ingest_quality.tier_count and dashboard stub.
Evelyn Shaw: Security: the signing hook uses an ephemeral key in this PR; gate HSM integration to a follow-up. || Aisha: Reply: noted in docs and added an 'hsm_integrated' flag to the signer interface.
Merged via squash on 2026-02-19 by Evelyn Shaw after CI green and 2 approvals. Release note generation will be toggled under feature-flag 'intake_quality_tiers' and rollout to production controlled via release pipeline.
- Introduces intake quality tiers (bronze/silver/gold) computed at model ingest; used for routing and rollout hints. || - Adds compact change indexer to produce deterministic short changelog fragments embedded in manifests. || - Adds small provenance token/signing hook for release automation (non-production key). || Migration: fields are optional and backward compatible; consumers can ignore missing fields.
Backfill: run 'cli/onboard.py --backfill-quality --days 30' when ready. Monitor metrics.ingest_quality.tier_count and release.compose.fragment_hits. Feature flag: feature/intake_quality_tiers toggles production behavior.
