payload.body:
Motivation: When new model variants are onboarded we often see subtle regressions or improvements that are hard to tie back to specific metadata or micro-changes in the model bundle. This PR introduces a delta-correlation profiler that correlates changes in model metadata and binary diffs with shifts in performance profiles (latency P95, token throughput, memory high-water marks) observed under a synthetic load probe. The outcome is twofold: 1) structured performance deltas attached to a model version and 2) an autogenerated, human-readable release digest for changelogs and release notes.

Design summary: The feature has three components: (A) delta_correlation analyzer - lightweight statistical correlator that consumes profiled metrics and model-diff signals, (B) synthetic_prober - a reproducible load generator integrated into the onboarding pipeline that runs short, bounded workloads (microbenchmarks + representative sequences) and emits canonical histograms and KV-cache traces, (C) release_digest generator - templates and heuristics that synthesize a digest combining semantic changelog lines (from commit messages/manifest annotations) and prioritized perf deltas with remediation hints.

Scope & constraints: The prober is designed to run as an optional step during onboard (default disabled for quick onboarding) and as a scheduled job in CI for nightly profiles. Correlation is intentionally conservative: we annotate deltas with confidence bands and attach example traces rather than claim causality.

What changed (high level): - Add registry/service/profiles/delta_correlation.py: core correlator and CLI wrapper. - Add registry/telemetry/prober/synthetic_prober.py: reproducible microbenchmark harness. - Add schemas/model_profile_v2.json: extended profile schema with delta entries and confidence metadata. - Add scripts/release/generate_digest.py: release digest composer and short-text summarizer. - Add CLI glue: cli/onboard/benchmark_sampler.py to invoke prober during onboard. - Add web preview: webapp/components/release_digest_preview.tsx to show digest in UI. - Add docs: docs/onboarding/delta_profiles.md describing interpretation and limitations. - Tests: tests/test_delta_correlation.py, tests/test_prober_integration.py. - Add minimal telemetry masking and opt-out hooks for customer data (telemetry/README).

Checklist (done): - [x] Implementation of correlator and prober - [x] Model profile schema bump (v2) with migration script - [x] Unit tests for correlator math and edge cases - [x] Integration test that runs prober in a sandbox container - [x] Release digest templates and examples - [x] Docs and short UX preview - [x] Telemetry privacy review and opt-out flag

Acceptance criteria / QA steps: 1) Run the onboard flow with --with-prober against a test model; verify a model_profile v2 JSON has a "deltas" block with perf metrics and confidence. 2) Generate a release digest for a release candidate: produced markdown should include a concise perf-summary, top-3 deltas, and suggested remediation if a perf regression is high-confidence. 3) Synthetic prober must complete within configured time budget (default 3 minutes) and not mutate model artifacts. 4) CI nightly job demonstrates stability for a fixed set of models (no more than 1% variance in reported medians between runs).

Rollout plan: Feature off by default. Toggle via onboarding flag and an account-level config. Nightly profiling enabled for internal canary accounts first, then opt-in for enterprise customers. Monitor: new metrics exported to telemetry namespace reg.delta_correlation.* (histograms for score/confidence, probe durations, and digest generation success). Alert on increased digest failures or probe runtime > 3x budget.

Backward compatibility: schema bump to model_profile_v2 includes a migration shim; older consumers will continue to read profile.v1 until they migrate. Release digests are additive and stored as separate artifacts under releases/<model>/digest-<version>.md.

Security & privacy: prober explicitly masks prompt content and avoids sending customer data to external services. Telemetry events are aggregated and privacy-reviewed; opt-out flag documented.

Notes: The correlator intentionally avoids heavy ML models and uses bootstrap sampling + Spearman rank correlation with Holm-Bonferroni correction to reduce false positives. We include an examples folder and two canned digests for maintainers to inspect.
Ethan Liu: Please add a small benchmark that demonstrates the correlator avoiding a false positive on a no-op model diff. Also add a deterministic RNG seed for the prober test.
Asha Patel: Added a deterministic seed option and included the benchmark in tests/test_delta_correlation.py (see new commit c3e44ab).
Marisol Gómez: Telemetry scrub looks good but add a clear opt-out flag and document it in telemetry/README so legal can review quickly.
Asha Patel: Opt-out flag added (--skip-prober-telemetry) and documented; pinged Legal in the Linear ticket.
Liam O'Connor: Can we keep the default onboard path unchanged (no prober)? I want to avoid slowing down first-time onboarding. Also request a short UX preview for ops to review digest wording.
Asha Patel: Default remains disabled; web preview added and linked in the PR description.
payload.title: Add delta-correlation performance profiling and auto-release digest

payload.body:
Context and motivation: As model onboarding volume grows and teams rely on automated release notes for stability reviews, we need a deterministic, reviewable signal that captures model 'veracity' (how consistent outputs are vs. ground probes and production telemetry) and a lightweight composer that drafts release notes from profile deltas, sample regressions, and curated human annotations. This PR introduces a veracity_score field in the model profile, a scoring pipeline with configurable probes, and an autodraft release composer that synthesizes human-readable release notes for reviewers to iterate on.

What changed (high-level): 1) Veracity scorer: new evaluator module that runs a battery of semantic probes (consistency checks, hallucination heuristics, calibration tests) and normalizes into a 0-100 veracity_score with per-subsignal breakdowns saved as tags. 2) Autodraft release composer: a rules-and-templates engine that consumes profile deltas, telemetry highlights, and veracity regressions to generate an initial release note draft and bulletized impact statements. 3) Onboard workflow updates: profile schema bump (added optional fields), onboarding CLI flag (--with-veracity), and CI hooks to surface veracity deltas to devs. 4) Observability: added three metrics (veracity_distribution, autodraft_quality_score, composer_latency) and a dashboard snippet.

Detailed technical summary: - scorer/engine.py: new scoring harness that executes probe sets in parallel, aggregates weighted scores, and emits a provenance envelope. Probes are pluggable; initial set includes: semantic_coherence_probe, repetition_entropy_probe, calibration_brier_probe, reference_overlap_probe. - composer/draft.py: template-driven hydrator that maps delta tags (e.g., latency_up, tokens_increase, veracity_drop_5pct) to prioritized impact bullets using a small rule-table and a short natural-language surface formatter. - migrations/20251107_profile_schema_v2.sql: schema migration adds veracity_score (FLOAT), veracity_tags (JSONB), and release_draft (TEXT) to model_profile table; fields are optional to remain backward-compatible. - cli/onboard.py: added --with-veracity boolean flag (defaults to false for quick onboard) that triggers a lightweight probe pass and enqueues a background detailed scoring job. - tests/: added unit tests for score normalization, composer templating, and an integration test that runs an end-to-end onboard -> draft flow against a synthetic model bundle.

Commits (summary): - 1a2b3c4: introduce veracity scorer harness and baseline probes - 2b3c4d5: add composer engine and rule-table templates - 3c4d5e6: migration and DB wiring for optional profile fields - 4d5e6f7: CLI flag and background job wiring - 5e6f7g8: metrics and dashboard snippet - 6f7g8h9: tests and docs additions

Files changed (high level): - scorer/engine.py, scorer/probes/*.py - composer/draft.py, composer/templates/*.yaml - migrations/20251107_profile_schema_v2.sql - cli/onboard.py - docs/onboarding/veracity.md - observability/dashboards/veracity.json - tests/test_veracity_normalization.py, tests/test_composer_endtoend.py

Review conversation (highlights): - Priya Desai (reviewer): "Please include a short section in docs about probe selection and expected false positive modes. Also request that the composer explicitly mark autodrafts so reviewers don't mistake them for human-crafted notes." — Aisha: "Updated docs/onboarding/veracity.md with probe descriptions and added a top-line disclaimer in composer output: 'AUTODRAFT — please review'." - Liam O'Neill: "Can we make the DB migration additive and no-op if the columns already exist? We need safe rollbacks for Private installs." — Aisha: "Migration uses IF NOT EXISTS semantics and a reversible down script; added a smoke rollback test in CI." - Connor Blake: "I'd like the scoring weights to be configurable per-repo/team. Do we have a plan?" — Aisha: "Yes; composer and scorer read a repository-level config file (profile_config.yml). Default weights are committed; per-repo overrides live in /configs/ overrides and are validated by the schema validator." - Priya (follow-up): "Minor nit: add a small E2E with a real-ish telemetry sample to ensure autodrafts don't exceed 2s latency." — Aisha: "Added an integration test asserting composer_latency < 2.0s for the synthetic sample. CI reproduces this in 2.3s on first run, optimized to 1.1s after caching template load."

CI and checks: - unit tests: pass - integration tests: pass (composer latency assertion included) - linting: pass (flake8/black checks) - schema validator: pass - e2e on staging: pass

Backward compatibility and migration notes: - Profile schema change is additive and optional; existing onboarded models will not have veracity fields until rescored. - Onboard CLI defaults to existing behaviour unless --with-veracity is used; this keeps light-weight quick onboarding unchanged. - The autodraft composer stores generated drafts in release_draft column but does not publish anything automatically; human approval step required.

Security and privacy considerations: - All probe runs avoid sending user PII to remote services; probes run in-process or on customer VPC when using Private deployments. - Composer templates do not include raw model examples or sample outputs unless the operator explicitly enables sample_in_draft in profile_config.yml.

Performance notes: - Initial scorer run for a mid-sized model (7B) completes in ~6s on our standard probe runner; incremental re-scores with cached embeddings are ~1.1s. - Composer average latency measured at 0.8s after template cache warmup. Metrics emitted to give teams SLO visibility.

Follow-up work (future PRs): - richer probe set with model-usage-aware thresholds (ENG-2101) - per-team weight tuning UI in Console (PM-162) - integrate composer feedback loop that learns preferred phrasing over time (ENG-2189)

Merge outcome: Squash and merge performed by Priya Desai after thumbs-up from all reviewers. Release pipeline created a draft internal note and surfaced a pending migration that ops scheduled for next maintenance window.

Notes for on-call and ops: Migration script included in artifacts; ops should run migration with downtime window for Private installs where DB locks are constrained. CI tag: veracity-release-20251114.
Adds a model veracity scoring signal to onboarding and an automated release-note composer that drafts concise changelogs from profile deltas and telemetry. No public API changes; backward-compatible metadata fields added.

payload.body:
Summary: Adds a compact onboard manifest (compact-manifest.v1) and a deterministic change serializer that emits compact delta bundles used by the release index generator and changelog automation.
Motivation: large model onboarding commits were producing verbose profiles and release artifacts; downstream release tooling and lightweight consumers (e.g., web UI, on-call tools, and offline auditors) need a concise, signed representation that is both verifiable and diff-friendly.
Design:
- compact-manifest.v1: trimmed metadata projection containing model identifier, canonical config hash, minimal performance profile pointers (tokenized perf tags), provenance fingerprints, and optional signature pointer. The manifest is JSONL-friendly and optimized for streaming over the onboard pipeline.
- change serializer: deterministic serializer that converts a set of model registry events (onboard, profile-update, variant-add) into a compact delta bundle. Each bundle is canonicalized (sorted keys, stable timestamps replaced with relative offsets) to make diffs small and reproducible.

payload.body:
Context: As part of the model metadata schema v1 rollout (see pr-18421), we need to migrate existing model/variant records so the registry can serve metadata_v1 consistently and unblock changelog generation + Console change history. Today, key fields are split across legacy columns and ad-hoc JSON; some records are incomplete and some are deployment-specific. This PR introduces a forward-only schema migration, a backfill job, and an explicit rollback procedure that preserves read-compatibility during the rollout window. Summary of changes: 1) DB schema: add metadata_v1 columns (jsonb) for model_versions and model_variants, plus schema_hash and migration bookkeeping (backfilled_at, backfill_source, backfill_warnings). Add partial indexes for common queries (model_id + version, availability filters). 2) Backfill job: new admin command `registry-admin backfill-metadata-v1` that transforms legacy fields into metadata v1 shape using the v1 schema library. Supports dry-run, batching, concurrency=1 by default, and idempotency (safe to re-run). Emits structured logs and counters per phase. 3) Safety checks: the backfill performs validation against the v1 JSON Schema, with strict vs permissive modes. Strict mode fails the run; permissive mode writes metadata_v1 plus warning annotations and a reason code. Includes a blocklist for known-bad legacy records (write no-op + emit alert) so we don’t half-migrate. 4) Read path compatibility: the registry read API continues to serve legacy fields, and adds `metadata_v1` on the response when present. No consumers are switched in this PR. A feature flag `MODEL_METADATA_V1_READ_PREFERRED` (default false) is included for staging-only verification. 5) Rollback plan: documented steps to revert reads to legacy-only, and to remove/ignore partially written metadata_v1 safely. Because the migration is additive, rollback is primarily a configuration rollback; the backfill writes can remain without impacting existing callers. Implementation details: Mapping logic is in `internal/metadata/migrate/legacy_to_v1.ts` and is intentionally conservative: (a) version: derives `version.semver` if present; otherwise sets `version.scheme=registry-seq` and preserves the legacy version string in `internal.legacy_version`. (b) tokenizer/runtime: best-effort inference from existing model_family + engine fields; if unknown, sets `compatibility.requires_human_review=true` and adds a warning. (c) availability: populates Hosted/Dedicated/Private availability based on legacy deployment flags and region allowlists; defaults to "unknown" rather than assuming global availability. (d) deprecations: carries forward existing deprecation_date fields; if only a free-form note exists, it is placed under internal.deprecation_context and not made public. Metrics/monitoring added: `model_registry.metadata_v1.backfill.records_total` (tagged by entity=model_version|variant, result=written|skipped|failed), `model_registry.metadata_v1.backfill.validation_failures_total` (tagged by reason), `model_registry.metadata_v1.backfill.duration_ms` (per batch), and `model_registry.metadata_v1.backfill.warnings_total` (tagged by warning_code). Also adds a one-time gauge report in logs at end-of-run: counts by model_family and deployment mode to help spot skew. Ops runbook (included in this PR): - Recommended rollout sequence: (1) deploy additive schema; (2) run backfill in staging with dry-run + strict mode; (3) run staging with strict write; (4) enable `MODEL_METADATA_V1_READ_PREFERRED` in staging and compare API diffs; (5) run production backfill in permissive mode with alerting; (6) follow up on warnings and re-run strict mode for clean-up. - Batch sizing guidance: start with 500 records/batch, pause between batches if DB CPU > 65% for 5m. - Alert thresholds: if failed > 0.5% in any 10m window or validation_failures spikes, page. - Success criteria: 99.9% records written or intentionally skipped with known warning codes; 0 schema validation failures in strict mode after remediation. Rollback steps (documented under `docs/ops/metadata-v1-migration.md`): 1) Disable `MODEL_METADATA_V1_READ_PREFERRED` everywhere (or confirm it remains false). 2) Stop/rollback any downstream consumers that switched to metadata_v1 reads (none in this PR). 3) If the backfill is causing DB load, stop the job; already-written metadata_v1 is safe to keep. 4) If we must revert writes, run `registry-admin backfill-metadata-v1 --revert` which clears metadata_v1 only for records written by this job (checks backfill_source and backfilled_at window), leaving any manual edits intact. 5) Post-rollback: export warning/failure report to Slack #eng-releases and attach to ENG-9822 for follow-up. Testing: Adds unit tests for legacy->v1 mapping for common model families and known edge cases (missing tokenizer, non-semver versions, quantization variants). Adds an integration test that runs the backfill against a seeded test DB and verifies idempotency and performance (bounded queries, no full table scans). Includes a regression test for the case raised in SUP-28429 (need exact change history later) by ensuring we preserve legacy identifiers in internal fields for traceability. Notes for reviewers: - The goal here is correctness + safety, not perfect metadata completeness. We prefer warnings over guessing. - Please focus on: (a) DB migration safety (locks/index builds), (b) idempotency + revert correctness, and (c) whether warning codes are actionable for follow-up. - Connor: release train implications are in the runbook; this should land before we turn on CI schema-diff checks in other repos.
Quentin Harris (review): Mapping looks reasonable, but I’m worried about silently synthesizing semver for legacy versions. Can we make sure we never fabricate a semver when the legacy field is non-semver? Also, can you include a warning code for "version_non_semver" so we can chase those down before we expose public release notes? Michael Nguyen (author): Agreed. I removed the "try to coerce" path. If legacy version doesn’t match semver, we set version.scheme=registry-seq and stash legacy string in internal.legacy_version + emit warning_code=version_non_semver. Added tests for a couple known offenders. Ethan Park (review): DB migration: are the new indexes created concurrently? We’ve been burned by blocking writes on large tables. Also, the integration test uses `CREATE INDEX` without CONCURRENTLY; can we keep prod migration safe? Michael Nguyen (author): Yes—prod migration uses `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` where allowed; for the one partial index that can’t be concurrent in our migration framework, I added a follow-up to build it out-of-band and left it out of the migration. Updated docs with the exact commands. Connor O'Brien (review): Rollback plan is good; can you add a clear "stop conditions" section and who to page if validation failures exceed threshold? Also please ensure the revert command only clears rows written by this job (don’t wipe manual edits). Michael Nguyen (author): Added stop conditions + paging instructions (Release Eng on-call, then Platform DB on-call). Revert checks backfill_source=="metadata_v1_backfill_v1" and backfilled_at within provided window; it refuses to run without both. Sahana Iyer (review): CI: the seeded DB integration test initially failed on my branch due to timing/flake. Can we reduce batch size in tests and add deterministic ordering? Michael Nguyen (author): Done—test uses batch_size=50 and orders by primary key; also added retry around transient connection reset in CI. Re-ran CI 3x. Quentin Harris (approval): Approved after warning code changes + semver handling fix. Ethan Park (approval): Approved; thanks for addressing index safety. Connor O'Brien (approval): Approved; runbook is clear enough to hand to the release train.
payload.title: Migrate model records to metadata v1 (backfill + rollback plan)

Motivation: The model registry currently stores per-variant performance profiles generated from offline probes and onboarding runs. Production telemetry contains valuable, usage-weighted signals (sequence length distribution, typical prompt prefixes, error-rate by bucket) that can materially change recommended performance profiles and changelog framing. This PR introduces a usage-weighted profile aggregator that consumes recent telemetry snapshots to produce aggregated performance profiles and a lightweight changelog primer to aid release authors and SREs.
Solution: 1) ingestion/aggregator: a new microservice component (registry.usage_aggregator) that reads time-windowed telemetry (via existing telemetry export API) and computes weighted aggregates for latency, token-distribution, typical prefix histograms, and cache-hit estimates. 2) profile model: compact JSON schema for aggregated_profile with provenance metadata and sample counts. 3) changelog primer: a template-driven generator that converts diffs between baseline and aggregated profiles into prioritized note suggestions (performance regressions, cost-opportunities, quantization caveats). 4) API: POST /v1/models/:id/aggregates and GET /v1/models/:id/changelog_primer. 5) CLI: regctl model synth-changelog --window 7d to preview suggestions.
Rollout and safety: aggregator runs as opt-in per-model for 7d pilot. Aggregates are stored as read-only snapshots and never used to auto-rollout model variants; they only surface recommendations. Config knobs include sample_window, min_sample_threshold, and retention_days. All telemetry inputs are processed with sampling and PII-scrubbing filters to preserve privacy and compliance.
Testing and validation: added e2e tests that feed synthetic telemetry, unit tests for aggregator math, and regression tests for primer output formatting. Benchmarks show aggregator computes 7-day window aggregates for 5k variants in ~18m on a single m5d. Large-run performance plan documented.
Backward compatibility: API additions are additive. Existing profile formats still accepted. No breaking changes.
Docs and examples: docs/primer.md contains usage examples and prompt seeds for change authors, and examples/telemetry-samples contains sanitized fixtures.
TL;DR: production-safe, opt-in telemetry aggregation that surfaces usage-weighted profile deltas and auto-drafts changelog primer suggestions to improve release quality and reduce manual triage.
Arjun Patel (2026-02-19): Can you add a circuit-breaker if the telemetry export API starts returning 5xx? Also request adding metrics for skipped samples due to PII filter.
Maya Chen (2026-02-19): Added circuit-breaker and metrics.skipped_samples; updated docs to call out PII filter behavior.
Nina Gomez (2026-02-21): The primer output looks good but we should tone down the language for 'regression' and classify by confidence. Please add confidence scores and sample-count thresholds.
Maya Chen (2026-02-21): Added confidence bucket and min_sample_threshold config; updated unit tests. Marking for re-review.
Liam O'Connor (2026-02-23): Security review: checked telemetry scrubbing and storage retention. Suggest adding an integration test for retention enforcement.
Maya Chen (2026-02-24): Added retention enforcement test and updated migrations to set TTL on aggregated_profiles table. CI passing locally.
Nina Gomez (2026-02-25): Approved after verifying confidence scoring and primer phrasing.

Motivation: onboarding produced multiple informal identifiers for the same model (aliases, git tags, local upload ids). That ambiguity propagates into changelogs, rollback tooling, and audit exports. This PR introduces a compact canonical 'Model Accession' (MA) assigned at onboarding and a small, signed 'release tape' artifact that bundles the accession, profile snapshot, and a provenance hash for release-note automation.

What this PR does: 1) Adds an accession generator and persistence layer: a short, globally-unique accession (MA-YYYY-<base32>) recorded on model create. 2) Adds a release-tape assembler (lightweight JSONL artifact) that contains the accession, model metadata canonicalized, performance-profile snapshot, and a provenance hash signed by the registry key. 3) Adds 'profile guards' to validate incoming performance profiles against accountable thresholds (latency P95, mem footprint, token-cost estimate). Guards are pluggable and recorded on the tape. 4) Backfill/migration: a conservative backfill will assign accessions to existing models without changing their public aliases; release-tapes are generated only for new/updated onboard events during the feature-flag rollout. 5) CLI + API: exposes onboarding flag --emit-release-tape and a registry endpoint to fetch latest tape by accession. 6) Docs and decision record describing accession format, signing, and retention policy.

Compatibility and rollout: feature-flag guarded (registry.enable_accession=true). Default behavior is no-op for existing clients. Release-tape is optional; consumers can request the tape if they need authoritative changelog snippets. Backfill runs as a low-priority job, writing accessions to a new optional column so existing identifiers remain the source-of-truth for user-facing surfaces until teams opt-in.

Performance: accession generation is cheap (local deterministic stamp + random bytes), release-tape assembly occurs asynchronously during onboarding to avoid slowing hot paths; initial performance tests show onboarding CPU walltime +3% and no noticeable change to cold-start latency.

Security and provenance: the tape is signed with the registry's long-lived registry key; verification helpers added to the client SDKs. Signing signature and provenance hash are recorded in audit logs for compliance.

Migration plan and safety: 1) Deploy accession generator behind flag. 2) Run backfill in read-only mode to preview accession collisions (none expected). 3) Flip flag to start emitting tapes for new onboard events. 4) Run consumer integration tests for tooling relying on canonical ids. 5) Rollout to full cohort.

Testing: unit tests for accession uniqueness and determinism, integration tests for tape assembly+signature verification, e2e backfill dry-run. Also manual validation on a staging dataset of ~1.2k models.

Notes: this intentionally keeps the public alias surface unchanged. Accessions are intended to be a stable internal anchor for releases, rollbacks, and changelog automation; they are not meant to replace human-friendly names.

Related: ENG-8732 (canonical model ids), ENG-9104 (release automation).
Marcus Li: Please add a unique index on the accession column in the migration — we need DB-level guarantees, not only app checks.
Hannah Ortega: Added migration with unique index and a small integration test for concurrent onboarding (see migrations/2025_10_07_add_accession_column.sql).
Priya Nair: Nit: rename 'releaseTape' -> 'release_tape' to align with existing package names. Also add an example tape in docs for auditing teams.
Hannah Ortega: Renamed package and added example tape JSON in docs. Also added tape verification helper to python SDK.
Ethan Park: CI failed lint on first pass; there was a formatting issue in assembler.go — after fixing, CI passed. LGTM after tests green.
Add: canonical Model Accession (MA) and optional signed release-tape artifact for authoritative changelog and provenance. Add: profile guard framework to validate performance snapshots during onboarding. Migration: conservative backfill for accessions; feature-flag rollout. Impact: no breaking changes to public aliases.
Backfill job runs as low-priority batch; monitor db migration job for deadlocks. If consumers rely on accession, ensure they validate signature using SDK helper; contact registry-oncall if signature verification fails.

payload.body:
Background: onboarding churn and subtle compatibility regressions have made changelogs noisy and hard to consume. We need a small, machine-readable lifecycle signal attached to model profiles so release automation can produce concise, actionable changelog snippets when a model moves between lifecycle phases (onboard -> staging -> prod). This PR introduces 'lifecycle_signature' metadata on model profiles and a staged compatibility-snippet generator that outputs human-friendly changelog fragments and suggested fallback mappings for deployments.

What this PR does: introduces a new lightweight lifecycle_signature schema (versioned), adds an onboarding hook to compute the signature, adds a changelog assembler plugin that emits staged compatibility snippets, and wires a CLI flag to preview generated snippets. The generator uses a deterministic fingerprint of (architecture, tokenizer_hash, primary_quant, perf_token_summary) and a short delta heuristic to summarize compatibility impact and performance deltas.

Checklist:
- [x] lifecycle_signature schema and migration support
- [x] onboarding hook: registry/hooks/lifecycle_signer.py
- [x] changelog assembler plugin: registry/hooks/compat_snippets.py
- [x] CLI preview: registry/cli/onboard_preview.py --staged-snippets
- [x] unit tests for signature calculation and snippet heuristics
- [x] docs: docs/onboard-lifecycle.md with examples and rollout guidance

Design notes: the lifecycle_signature is intentionally compact (hex-encoded 12 bytes + version tag) to remain stable in manifests and to avoid bloating release bundles. The staged compatibility snippet is a short paragraph and a suggested remap table (previous_alias -> recommended_variant) to help platform teams stage rollouts. The heuristics aim for conservative suggestions (only propose remaps when the signature delta + perf delta exceed thresholds).

Why this is different from profile hashes: profile hashes are content fingerprints; lifecycle_signature encodes a small set of compatibility-relevant attributes and a stability score to be used by release tooling and console UI for clearer onboarding narratives.

Backward compatibility and migration: existing profiles without lifecycle_signature are treated as 'unknown' and will get a computed signature on the next onboard. The migration is non-blocking; the assembler falls back to legacy blurb generation if signature is absent.

Operational considerations: the plugin adds a single CPU-bound computation during onboarding and a fast, cached path in changelog assembly. We added a short TTL cache keyed by model_id+head_sha to avoid recomputation for large batch uploads.

Risks and mitigations: initial heuristics may be conservative and under-suggest remaps; we added a monitoring metric (registry.lifecycle.signer.suggestions.count) and a small sampling telemetry to evaluate precision.

How to test locally: run `pytest tests/test_lifecycle_signatures.py::test_signature_determinism` and `python -m registry.cli.onboard_preview --file sample_profile.json --staged-snippets` to see generated snippet output.

Related: ENG-7421 (project to tighten onboarding churn), PM-318 (product request for clearer release notes).
Mateo Alvarez: Nice approach on keeping the signature compact. Can we document the exact field order used for the fingerprint? Requested change: add a unit test to assert stable ordering so CI catches accidental reorderings.
Priya Shah: Added tests/test_lifecycle_signatures.py::test_field_ordering and a serialization assertion. Also expanded comments in registry/serializers.py to call out ordering.
Janelle Kwan: LGTm overall, one nit: the CLI flag name is a little verbose. Can we alias --staged-snippets with --preview-snippets?
Priya Shah: Added alias --preview-snippets and updated docs. Updated tests to call preview code path.
Owen Price: CI flaked on the first run (integration timeout). Re-ran checks; all green. I approve pending squash merge.
Janelle Kwan: Approved after the alias change and small docs tweak.
Release Manager (bot): merge ready, release_notes field populated.
Add lifecycle_signature metadata and a changelog plugin that generates staged compatibility snippets for onboarded models. This enables concise, machine-friendly release notes and suggested variant remaps during rollouts. Includes a CLI preview and tests.

Motivation: teams spend a lot of manual effort writing performance blurbs and choosing a baseline when onboarding model variants. This PR adds a small automation pipeline that 1) synthesizes performance profiles weighted by actual usage signals, 2) stamps model metadata with a delta-hash for versioned provenance, and 3) emits an "autobrief" release-justification snippet that the model registry UI and release tooling can surface to reviewers. Scope: a telemetry sampling worker, an API endpoint to request a profile dry-run, a CLI command for maintainers, a tiny template engine for autobriefs, and migration for the metadata.version and metadata.delta_hash fields. Privacy/opt-in: sampling respects the onboarded model's privacy flags and only pulls aggregated histogram metrics (no raw prompts). Key features included: usage-weighted bucketing by sequence_length and top-k cost bucket; sample-size heuristics to keep generation cheap; delta-hash calculation for metadata diffs; CLI dry-run "mr profile generate --dry-run" and API POST /profiles/generate that returns JSON-profile and autobrief text. Why now: reduces churn in changelog authoring and biases release notes toward what users actually hit in production. Backwards compatibility: existing metadata.version still works; new fields are optional and non-breaking. Rollout plan: feature-flagged for 2 weeks, small canary on private tenants, then enable globally. Checklist: [x] telemetry sampler worker; [x] delta-hash algorithm and tests; [x] CLI and API end-to-end; [x] autobrief template and i18n placeholder; [x] docs draft in docs/onboarding/autobrief.md; [x] add migration to mark existing profiles as legacy. Related: ENG-4512 ties this to the release automation epic, SUP-1283 surfaced a customer ask for rollouts guided by actual traffic.

Motivation: model profiles currently carry free-form dataset_licenses and provenance text which leads to inconsistent UX in the Console and noisy release notes when onboarding models. This PR introduces a canonical dataset license field (dataset_license.canonical) plus a harmonizer/migration tool that standardizes legacy licenses into SPDX-like tags and emits concise changelog deltas for automated release notes.

Summary of changes: added a new optional top-level `dataset_license` block to model_profile schema (name, canonical, source_url, declared_by). Implemented `scripts/migrate_licenses.py` which runs a best-effort mapping table and a dry-run mode that outputs normalization suggestions. Added `tooling/changelog/emit_license_delta.py` to produce machine-readable delta snippets consumed by the release assembler. Adjusted onboarding hook to record `license_normalization_hint` in the onboard logs when mapping was ambiguous. Updated tests, examples, and docs.

Backward compatibility & rollout: the schema change is additive and backward compatible; existing profiles without the new block are unaffected. The migration script is opt-in and has a dry-run mode by default; after review we executed the non-destructive migration for models in the staging bucket and pushed suggested canonicalizations as PRs to the registry metadata. The Console will prefer `dataset_license.canonical` if present, falling back to legacy free-form text.

Checklist: [x] schema extension and migration tool added; [x] unit + integration tests; [x] changelog emitter integrated with release assembler hook; [x] docs/Console mapping notes; [x] Linear linked.

How to test locally: run `python scripts/migrate_licenses.py --dry-run --input examples/profiles/` to see normalization suggestions. To apply changes to a writable registry, run with `--apply` and review the generated commit. Use `python tooling/changelog/emit_license_delta.py --from old.json --to new.json` to preview the release fragment.

Rollback: migration changes are committed as separate commits per profile and are reversible via the generated revert commits in the output repo; the emitters are read-only until release assembler consumes them.

Related: ENG-7421 (standardize metadata for legal/compliance), SUP-1987 (support ticket: ambiguous dataset licenses encountered during onboarding).

Introduce an onboarding chronicle that emits per-model ephemeral patchnotes and a deterministic compat-assertion harness. Adds a small CLI helper to generate human-readable patchnotes (chronicle) and a gated check that fails onboarding if compatibility regressions exceed the configured tolerance. Backwards compatible with existing profile formats.
Motivation: teams onboarding models need concise, per-version patchnotes and an automated compatibility check that surfaces regressions early. This PR introduces 'Onboard Chronicle', a lightweight generator that emits ephemeral patchnotes (human-friendly and machine-readable) during model onboarding, and a deterministic 'compat assertion' harness that runs a small canonical prompt set and computes a compatibility score against a baseline profile.

What this changes: adds a chronicle serializer and template-driven patchnote composer (registry/onboard/chronicle.py + release/templates/patchnote-template.hbs), a compat assertion runner (registry/onboard/compat_assertions.py) with 12 deterministic checks stored under registry/onboard/compat_baselines, and a tiny CLI wrapper (cli/registry-cli/patchnote.py) to preview or commit a generated patchnote to the model's release artifact. A signer utility (registry/onboard/signer.py) attaches a short provenance stamp so patchnotes can be traced to the onboarding run.

Checklist implemented: [x] serializer + template support for patchnotes [x] deterministic prompt set and scoring [x] CLI preview and commit mode [x] unit + integration tests for harness [x] CI workflow for compat gate (ci/workflows/compat.yml) [x] docs and quickstart.

Compatibility: The chronicle writer emits both JSONL for machine consumption and a compact markdown summary for human readers; it uses existing profile fields (profile.version, profile.affordances) so older tooling continues to work. The compat harness outputs a single scalar compatibility_score and a per-case delta list so downstream automation can implement policy thresholds.

Testing and CI: initial CI run (2026-01-20) failed integration due to nondeterministic RNG seed in a sample prompt; fixed by seeding the harness and adding a retry loop on transient tokenization differences. Subsequent runs passed all checks (unit + integration + lint). A scheduled nightly workflow was added to validate the maintainability of the deterministic prompt set.

Review notes and conversation: Marcus: "Nice separation of writer vs signer. Two asks: make the signer tolerant of missing KMS in private installs and add a small mock signer for unit tests." Response (Aisha): "Added a file-level mock signer and an env var KMS_EMBED_TOLERANCE; signer falls back to a local HMAC in private installs (README documents behaviour)." Jun: "Compat thresholds look reasonable; can we expose a per-linear-key override?" Response: "Exposed COMPAT_THRESHOLD env + Linear key-level override in config; docs updated." Elena: "Docs are good; one nit on the patchnote template wording." Response: "Updated wording and added examples in docs/quickstarts. Approved after fixes." 

Rollout plan: merged to main behind a feature flag ONBOARD_CHRONICLE. We will enable the flag for internal QA for two weeks, then flip for self-serve onboarding with a soft-warning mode (warnings do not block) for one month, then enable hard gating for enterprise onboarding flows. A migration step is provided: existing profiles will continue to produce chronicle outputs with fallback fields.

Risks and mitigations: false positives from the deterministic prompt set are the primary risk (model nondeterminism or tokenizer drift). Mitigations: nightly re-eval to surface drift, per-model threshold overrides, and a human-in-the-loop rollback for initial rollouts.

Merge result: squashed and merged on 2026-02-04 by Aisha Patel. Changelog: added to release notes under "Model registry: onboarding improvements" with brief usage example.

Related: ENG-4823 (compat automation), PM-77 (patchnote UX).
- The compat harness stores baselines under registry/onboard/compat_baselines/<model_alias>/; keep the size small (we checked in a 12-case set per model).
- To add new cases, follow docs/onboard/chronicle.md and run scripts/onboard-hooks/generate_chronicle.sh to preview.
- Feature flag: ONBOARD_CHRONICLE; threshold env COMPAT_THRESHOLD defaults to 0.9.
- If you need to run locally without KMS, set KMS_EMBED_TOLERANCE=true to use local HMAC signer.

payload.body:
Motivation: onboarding teams asked for smaller, targeted sample sets for release notes and regressions that map to customer cohorts (large-enterprise, mobile-first, helpdesk). In addition we need a way to produce concise changelog drafts that preserve sample provenance but remove identifying tokens: a watermark-backed drafting flow that ties a compact diff summary to a sampled manifest. Design: add a CohortSample manifest (schema v2) that declares sample cohorts, deterministic seed, and retention/privacy tags; implement a watermark drafters subsystem that can generate compact changelog teasers (one-line impact bullets + representative sample snippets) tied to a sample manifest hash and signature. The drafter uses K-anonymized snippet trimming and an optional token-redaction pipeline. Implementation: 1) manifest schema and validation (manifest/v2) + CLI preview (onboard-sample preview --manifest-file). 2) sampling worker that generates cohort-specific sample packs and stores lightweight fingerprints to the model registry storage backend. 3) watermark drafters service that consumes a manifest hash and emits a compact markdown-ready changelog snippet, with an attached provenance token for audit and rollback tooling. 4) compatibility checks added to the onboard pipeline: sample-aware performance baseline query and a lightweight eval probe that runs up to 100 queries across cohorts. 5) telemetry hooks so Console can show per-cohort sample coverage and digest generation latency. Rollout: behind feature-flag onboard.cohort_samples + gradual opt-in for model curators. Docs: CLI docs, manifest schema reference, and a short how-to for product teams to craft cohorts. Security/privacy: default redaction on snippets, signing of manifest hashes, and ability to opt-out of storing raw snippets. This PR groups the work into a logical change set to enable concise, cohort-aware release notes and safer public previews.
6 commits: add manifest schema v2 and validator; sampling worker and deterministic seed; watermark drafter service and unit tests; CLI preview; registry API hooks and small telemetry additions; changelog examples and docs
Initial review requested more explicit privacy defaults and stronger validation for deterministic seeds. I (author) pushed commit 3 to enforce seed ranges and add a manifest-level 'privacy: redact_by_default' boolean. Priya requested a telemetry opt-out flag; added 'manifest.telemetry.disabled' and updated docs. Diego asked for tighter unit tests around the drafter's redaction (edge cases: email-like tokens, long numeric strings) and suggested adding deterministic sampling tests; added those tests in commit 5. Liam asked about performance cost of the cohort probe; we added a cap (100 queries) and a circuit-breaker. Approvals: Priya approved on 2025-11-24, Diego approved after tests passed, Liam approved after perf verification.
Unit tests added for manifest validation and drafter redaction. End-to-end pipeline tested locally with a small model snapshot. Perf probe capped at 100 queries per manifest; CI runs an integration scenario using a synthetic sample pack. Manual QA: verified CLI preview output, manifest signature validation, and Console telemetry panel entries.
Read path unchanged for serving. Onboard pipeline: sampling job adds ~3% CPU on the curator worker during generation windows, storage footprint increased by ~120KB per sampled manifest (fingerprints + metadata). Drafter generation latency ~120-250ms per manifest on a small instance; negligible for UX flows.
1) Enable feature-flag for internal curators. 2) Run opt-in pilot with two product teams for 2 weeks. 3) Monitor telemetry: manifest-generation latency, sample-coverage, and any redaction failures. 4) Gradual enablement for all curators with 48h rollback path and a flag to disable public snippet previews.
Add cohort sample manifests (schema v2) and a watermark-based changelog drafter. Enables per-cohort concise release notes, deterministic sampling for reproducible regressions, and privacy-safe teaser generation. Controlled rollout behind onboard.cohort_samples feature flag.
Drafter emits a stable teaser payload that the changelog assembler can consume; payload contains manifest_hash, short impact bullets, and anonymized sample snippets. The assembler will now prefer cohort teasers when available and fall back to existing delta summarizers.
This change was intentionally split to keep the sampler and drafter logically separated so that downstream release assembly can consume either component independently. Follow-up work: add compact coverage badges in Console and auto-schedule cohort-based evictions for stale samples.

Motivation: We need a lighter-weight intake policy layer that captures onboarding policy decisions (privacy level, allowed telemetry, retention buckets, and visibility) at ingest-time and produces a compact, human-friendly attachment used by downstream changelog tooling. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: 1) an Intake Policy Adapter that normalizes onboarding metadata from multiple sources (onboard CLI, UI, S3 manifests) into a canonical policy object; 2) a Prose Release Composer that synthesizes short, human-readable release notes from the canonical policy and profile delta, intended for product-facing changelogs and Linear ticket descriptions. Goals: reduce manual work for release authors, make release notes more consistent, and ensure onboarding policies are discoverable in audit trails. What this changes: - intake/policy/adapter.py: new adapter that validates and normalizes policy fields with a small rule engine and schema hints - intake/schemas/policy_schema.yaml: canonical schema + migration helper - tools/release/composer.py: Prose composer that maps policy diffs and profile highlights to 1-2 paragraph release blurbs - cli/onboard: integration hook to emit canonical-policy.json to the model bundle - docs/onboarding/release-notes.md: guidance and templates for generated prose - tests/*: unit and integration tests for normalization and composer outputs Compatibility: adapter accepts legacy manifest keys and preserves provenance so existing ingesters continue to work. Motivation: When onboarding or rolling a new model variant we often have to pick a semantic version bump (patch/minor/major) and write release notes that explain impact. That process is manual, brittle, and sometimes inconsistent across teams. This PR introduces two complementary features: (1) an entropy-weighted version suggester that synthesizes signals from usage distributions, eval deltas, and profile stability to recommend a semantic version bump and a concise rationale; (2) an annotated changelog context generator that crafts short human-readable explanations (1-3 lines) for release notes by pulling commit summaries, telemetry deltas, and affected-model-profile anchors. Scope: model registry service + onboarding CLI + small UI metadata helpers. Design notes: the suggester computes three weighted signals: signal_entropy (how much usage patterns changed across routes/cohorts), perf_delta (normalized latency/cost/quality deltas from baseline profiles), and stability_anchor_shift (how many profile anchors moved outside tolerance). We map a composite score to semantic bump thresholds with tunable margins. The changelog contexter aggregates: the highest-impact commits (by footprint in changed artifacts), top telemetry deltas, and the suggested bump rationale into a single annotated line. Checklist: - [x] core scorer implementation and normalization - [x] onboarding CLI flag --auto-suggest-version - [x] changelog context writer that emits draft note to /onboard/drafts - [x] unit tests for scorer thresholds and context formatting - [x] e2e smoke run against staging model-catalog - [x] feature-flag gated rollout and telemetry metric (registry.version_suggestions.accepted) Backwards compatibility: All behavior is behind registry feature flag 'entropy_version_suggester'. Default remains manual. Rollout plan: land behind flag, enable for small cohort of internal teams for 2 weeks, gather accept/override rate and iterate thresholds. Metrics to watch: suggestion_accept_rate, suggested_bump_distribution, time_saved_per_onboard, churn_after_rollout. Related: ENG-2048 (onboard UX improvements), PM-674 (release notes automation).

Motivation: onboarding a model currently produces large, noisy changelogs and our sampling for profile calibration is expensive and sometimes biased by a few long sequences. This PR introduces (1) a small, explicit 'probe schema' for captured onboarding probes (tokenizer id, sequence length histogram, canonical prompts, perf anchors) and (2) a sampler implementation that selects representative probe subsets by stratified length buckets + semantic clustering so downstream profiling and release-note diffs are stable and cheap. Additionally this PR adds a release-notes 'weaver' that synthesizes concise human-readable release blurbs from profile diffs and telemetry deltas (latency, token-cost, quality regression hints). The weaver outputs a compact markdown snippet and a machine-readable changelog fragment for the console UI.

What this PR changes (high level): added a probe schema and serializers; a cluster-based sampler; a release-weaver CLI and library; integration with the model-intake pipeline to emit compact changelog fragments; docs and tests. The description below is intentionally a single continuous string used as the PR body in the repo.

Checklist: - [x] Probe schema (JSON Schema + Python dataclass) and serializer/deserializer - [x] Sampler: stratified-length + embedding-cluster sampler with configurable budget - [x] Release-weaver engine: templates + delta heuristics + CLI (rgm release-weave) - [x] Small compatibility shim in intake hook to attach probe-summary to profile bundles - [x] Unit tests + integration workflow - [x] Docs for registry operators and example outputs - [x] Feature-flag gating (registry.feature.release_weaver) for gradual rollout

Why this approach: stratified-length sampling reduces bias from tail examples; embedding-based clustering keeps semantic diversity; explicit probe schema makes diffs deterministic and reduces churn in release notes. The weaver focuses on delta-first blurbs: e.g. "+12ms p95 (seq<=256), -3% token-cost via quantized variant".

Related: ENG-4278 (probe-driven onboarding), ENG-4301 (release automation), earlier telemetry work on profile stability. Links: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4278, https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4301

Motivation: release notes for model updates are inconsistent and often miss the concrete operational impact (latency/cost/quality tradeoffs) that engineers need to make rollout decisions. This PR introduces an automated "impact statement" generator that synthesizes a short, human-readable summary from model metadata diffs and performance profile deltas. The generator is conservative by default and emits a confidence score and fallback suggestion when data is sparse. Implementation highlights: (1) delta-based summarizer that consumes two model profiles (baseline, candidate) and computes per-metric significance, median/CI deltas, and cost-per-1M-token estimates; (2) template engine that converts computed signals into a 1-3 sentence impact statement plus bullet micro-notes; (3) API and UI integration so statements are surfaced on the model version page and included in the changelog export; (4) CLI hook (mrctl annotate-impact) and a registry webhook for auto-attaching statements on release. Checklist: [x] core summarizer and heuristics, [x] API surface (/v1/models/:id/impact), [x] UI column + detail modal, [x] CLI command, [x] unit and e2e tests, [x] docs and examples, [x] feature flag (impact-gen.enabled) for safe rollout. Related work: ENG-4132 (release-quality release notes), ENG-4210 (model-profile schemas). Risk & mitigations: generator includes a confidence threshold and will attach a "needs manual review" flag when data is insufficient; output is stored as an annotation (not overwriting hand-authored notes). See the sample generated statement and technical notes fields below.
Introduce automated impact statements for model rollouts: concise, confidence-scored summaries of performance/cost/metadata deltas included in model version pages and changelog exports. Feature gated and disabled by default.
Scoring uses bootstrap CI on sampled eval runs when >20 samples; falls back to non-parametric delta otherwise. Cost estimates normalized to per-1M-token using current infra cost model (config/units.yml). Impact generation respects private evals: raw artifacts never leave the customer's project; only aggregated deltas are stored. Feature flag and per-customer opt-out present.
Candidate v1.3 vs baseline v1.2: Quality: +0.8% (BLEU-like eval median, 95% CI: +0.2% to +1.4%) — improvement likely. Latency: +12ms p50 (+6%); Cost: estimated +$0.30 per 1M tokens on current Dedicated profile. Notes: candidate uses int8 quantization but a modified tokenizer that increases avg seq length by ~2 tokens. Confidence: 0.82. Suggested action: canary rollout with traffic cap 10% and monitor latency SLOs for first 24h.
Liam: Please clarify the statistical thresholds and provide an example for small-sample behavior. -- Author (Ava): added significance.py and documentation; generator emits confidence and a 'requires-review' flag when sample < 20. Sofia: Can we include cost-estimate sensitivity (e.g., how quantization affects cost) and a link to the exact cost model used? -- Author: added link to config/units.yml in docs and included a micro-note with sensitivity band. Marco: Concern about automated text introducing bias in release notes; recommend manual override in UI and audit logs for every generated statement. -- Author: implemented manual-correct and audit trail (annotation author=system|user), added tests and UI controls. After the updates reviewers approved and requested a small follow-up to add a schema migration notice. All CI checks passed and were green on the final run.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: Customers and internal users increasingly ask not just what changed in a model release but why it matters operationally. We observed multiple incidents and postmortems where a model profile delta or a change in performance telemetry (latency/timeout spikes, token-level OOMs) lacked a direct link in the release notes to runbooks, mitigations, or probe evidence. This PR augments the release curator with two signal classes: (1) runbook references surfaced from incident/runbook tags attached to model onboarding or variant updates, and (2) sampled probe telemetry anchors (aggregated metrics + representative diffs) so changelogs include concrete operational context.

Design summary: Add a runbook signal ingestion pipeline that consumes runbook metadata (id, severity, short description) attached to model-version and variant records; wire a lightweight sampler that collects jitter-resistant probe snippets (latency histograms, prefix failure rates, small sample prompts) and produces compact evidence tokens. The release contextualizer stitches these signals into the autogenerated blurb using severity-aware templates (notice, advisory, urgent) and includes a short "What to watch" section with instrumentation links.

What changed in this PR: 1) curator/signal_ingest.py: new ingestion adapter for runbook metadata and probe samples; 2) curator/contextualizer.py: template engine update to accept runbook/probe anchors and render severity buckets; 3) onboarding/hooks.py: small change to attach runbook reference when a model variant is promoted; 4) tools/backfill_runbook_annotations.py: backfill script to annotate recent 90 days of releases from incident ledger; 5) tests/{unit,integration}/: added unit tests for templating and an integration test that verifies backfill idempotence; 6) docs/registry/release-context.md: doc with sample changelog output and best practices for runbook tags.

Implementation notes: - Runbook IDs are treated as free-form strings but normalized for the changelog (EX-INC-412 -> EX-412) to keep blurbs concise. - Probe sampling is rate-limited and uses reservoir sampling over a 24h window to avoid noisy short-lived spikes contaminating release notes. - The templates are intentionally conservative: runbook references only surface as advisories if severity >= 3 or if probe anchors show a regression exceeding configured watermarks. - All new config defaults to off for hosted customers; enterprise/private tenants can opt-in via a feature flag in tenant metadata.

Testing and CI: Added unit tests for template rendering edge cases and a synthetic integration job that runs the backfill script against a snapshot of the incident ledger. CI added a lightweight e2e (fast path) that runs against mocked probe samples. All checks are green on the final run.

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind tenant opt-in. Initial rollout to internal staging and the Curation team for 2 weeks. Run the backfill script once during staging to produce annotated release previews, then opt in a small set of customer tenants. Monitor for noisy changelog spam and adjust reservoir parameters if necessary.

Backward compatibility and migration: Non-opted tenants see no changes. The backfill script is idempotent and safe to run multiple times; it writes only annotation metadata and will not mutate historical artifact blobs.

Docs and usage: docs/registry/release-context.md includes examples of generated blurbs, how to tag runbooks during onboard, and operational guidance for interpreting probe anchors. CLI helper added: "redwood-registry annotate-runbook --file <ledger> --dry-run".

Open questions / future work: - Consider integrating with the Optimize pipeline to automatically surface quantization/regression tradeoffs alongside runbook advisories. - Add more expressive probes (token-level skew, attention dropout) if customers ask for richer evidence. - UX: provide an optional digest email for tenant SREs when a release includes an "urgent" advisory.

Related work: references ENG-6421 (improve release contextualization), PM-293 (customer ask: clearer operational blurbs), SUP-1187 (support incident that motivated the change).
Jonah Klein: Can we guarantee that the runbook IDs are stable across moves? If the incident gets re-numbered upstream we might have dangling refs. Reply: We normalize runbook IDs at ingestion and store a provenance pointer to the incident ledger; if upstream renumbers, provenance mapping wins and the blurb shows the canonical ID.
Priya Nair: Small nit on the template—please shorten the 'What to watch' copy when severity=3. Reply: Done; template now collapses long lists into a single sentence and provides a link to expanded instrumentation.
Ellen Park: CI flakey on integration test in the first run. Requested: add a timeout guard and retry for mocked ledger calls. Reply: Added retry with exponential backoff and reran tests; green now. Approved.
Run unit tests locally: pytest tests/unit -k contextualizer
Run integration: pytest tests/integration/test_backfill_idempotence.py
Staging run: enable feature flag for internal-staging tenant and run backfill with --dry-run, inspect generated markdown

Motivation: generating release notes for model profile updates has become slow and noisy as we scale the registry. Small consecutive edits to metadata and perf profiles produced fragmented changelogs and made rollouts confusing. This PR introduces a compact, append-only model_history.log and a deterministic 'delta-apply' hook that normalizes incoming profile diffs into semantic changelog entries.

What this PR changes: model_history.log: a per-model append-only JSONL artifact schema (registry/model_history.log.schema.yaml) that records normalized deltas with fields: version, timestamp, actor, change_kind, profile_hash, diff_summary, and tags. The file is intentionally metadata-only (no prompt or raw input) to preserve privacy.

delta-apply CLI hook: cli/delta_apply.py implements the deterministic consolidation algorithm. The hook consumes a sequence of raw profile diffs, applies normalization (field ordering, numeric bucketing, name canonicalization) and produces a stable set of changelog entries used by the release notes generator. This eliminates churn from semantically-equivalent edits (e.g., whitespace, float precision).

Migration: migrations/2024_11_migrate_legacy_profiles.py converts legacy profile-diff artifacts into model_history.log entries. The migration is idempotent and emits a migration report stored under migrations/reports/*. The migration is safe to run on existing registries and has a dry-run flag.

Tooling and docs: added templates/changelog-template.mustache and scripts/generate-release-notes.sh to demonstrate deterministic generation of release notes across CI and the Console. Documentation in docs/registry/release-notes.md explains the workflow for engineers and product.

Backward compatibility and safety: existing profile files and the onboarding pipeline continue to work. The delta-apply hook can be inserted as an optional step during onboarding; we ship the migration to bootstrap history logs for prior models. model_history.log intentionally stores high-level diffs only and omits any PII or prompt contents.

Performance: in internal tests with a synthetic registry of 12k models and 85k profile edits, changelog assembly time fell from ~18s to ~1.3s (wall-clock) and peak memory usage dropped by ~65%.

Testing: added tests/test_delta_apply.py that covers normalization rules, hash stability, and idempotence. CI pipeline additions ensure migration dry-run passes on a snapshot dataset.

Follow-ups: (a) expose a Console view for model_history.log entries and search by tag (ENG-3492), (b) wire the delta-apply output to Redwood Optimize quality regressions (ENG-3510), (c) add rate-limited history compaction for extremely chatty models (future PR).

Related: ties to ENG-3489 (release-note quality), PM-712 (product spec for changelog UX), and SUP-1982 (customer case showing confusing changelogs).
Adds persistent model_history.log to record onboarding deltas
Adds delta-apply CLI hook to generate deterministic changelogs for model profile updates
Includes a backwards-compatible migration script to convert legacy profile diffs into the new history format
Improves release-note fidelity and reduces changelog generation latency for large registries

Summary: Adds a new synthetic workload profile type and an autodraft changelog heuristic that uses synthetic diffs to surface likely user-visible performance and cost impacts during model onboarding. Motivation: We currently rely on sampled real traffic and hand-curated microbenchmarks to generate performance profiles. That makes early onboarding noisy for very new models (few real requests) and slows down automated release-note suggestions. This PR introduces a lightweight synthetic workload generator (microbench molds) plus a delta scoring pipeline that converts synthetic-run deltas into human-readable draft changelog bullets. What I changed: 1) profiles/synthetic_profile.py - new generator and serializer for deterministic synthetic workloads (sequence length distributions, token entropy variants, sparse/dense token patterns). 2) onboarding/hooks/autodraft_changelog.py - new hook that consumes synthetic-run diffs and combines them with sampled telemetry to produce scored draft bullets. 3) schema/extensions/perf_profile_v2.yaml - extends perf profile schema with synthetic_run metadata fields and confidence bands. 4) docs/onboarding/synthetic-profiles.md - how-to and caveats for using synthetic profiles when onboarding new models. 5) tests/test_synthetic_profile.py & tests/test_changelog_autodraft.py - unit tests exercising generation, serialization, and scoring heuristics. 6) ci/workflows/synthetic-profiles.yml - CI workflow to run fast synthetic runs on PRs. Commits (high level): - 6d4f2a0 add synthetic workload generator and basic serializer - ab7c9f1 extend perf_profile schema with synthetic metadata - 2f0b3e6 add autodraft changelog hook and scoring pipeline - 9a7b4c2 docs and tests for synthetic profiles and autodraft - f21e8b5 fix linter issues and add CI workflow Review notes and discussion thread (condensed): - Marco Liu (2026-02-18): "Nice approach. Two asks: (a) ensure synthetic profiles are clearly labeled so we don't accidentally expose them to customers as 'real' profiles; (b) can we add a knob to opt into synthetic-only onboarding?" - Author reply: "Added synthetic_run.source and synthetic_run.confidence fields in schema; added onboarding flag synthetic_opt_in and documented behavior in the README." - Samir Patel (2026-02-19): "Scoring looks reasonable but we should avoid over-weighting synthetic latency deltas vs sampled telemetry. Please add a defensive cap." - Author reply: "Added a cap parameter (max_synthetic_influence) and unit tests showing capped behavior." - Elena Novak (2026-02-20): "Tests failing on Windows runners due to path handling in the test harness." - Author reply: "Fixed path join usage and adjusted CI workflow to use matrix runs for linux only to keep runtime cheap." Testing and validation: - Unit tests validate generation determinism for fixed RNG seeds, expected distribution shapes and serialization format. - We ran synthetic runs vs a small set of internal reference models in perf-lab; delta scores correlate with sampled telemetry in 83% of sampled cases across a diverse workload matrix (details in PR artifacts). - Manual review of auto-generated draft bullets produced by the heuristic for 12 recent onboarding jobs; author triaged examples into accept/reject and tuned scoring thresholds accordingly. Backwards compatibility and safety: - Schema extension is additive; existing perf profile parsers will ignore synthetic_run fields if unknown. - The autodraft is an advisory-only system: the drafts are stored as candidate_release_notes and are not surfaced automatically to end-customer release notes unless approved by a curator. - Added opt-in gate: onboarding job config field synthetic_opt_in=false by default; customers cannot receive synthetic-only drafts unless explicitly enabled. Files changed (high level): - registry/profiles/synthetic_profile.py: synthetic generator, RNG seed +/- deterministic modes. - registry/onboard/hooks/autodraft_changelog.py: hook + scorer + template assembler. - schema/extensions/perf_profile_v2.yaml: schema additions and example payload. - docs/onboarding/synthetic-profiles.md: step-by-step and examples. - tests/test_synthetic_profile.py, tests/test_changelog_autodraft.py: unit and integration tests. - ci/workflows/synthetic-profiles.yml: new CI workflow. Related work and references: - A follow-up PR will wire synthetic-run based quick-profiles into the onboarding UI (ENG-2108). - This complements existing sampled telemetry work (ENG-1423) by providing early signal for models with limited deployment history. Release notes (auto-generated draft): - "Introduce synthetic workload profiles to produce early performance and cost signals for newly onboarded models. Adds an autodraft changelog heuristic that suggests performance impact bullets based on synthetic-vs-sampled deltas (opt-in)." - Impacts: "No breaking changes. Schema extended with additive fields; autodrafts are advisory and opt-in." Merge: - Approved by Marco Liu and Samir Patel after fixes; merged via squash on 2026-02-25. Known limitations and future follow-ups: - Synthetic workload design is not a replacement for real-traffic profiling; we deliberately avoid surfacing synthetic-only drafts without human approval. - Plan: add model-behavior fingerprints and integrate with release-annotation pipeline to automatically suggest rollback thresholds (follow-up ENG-2231).

Context: OpenAI Responses v5 introduces two things we've seen in early partners: 1) finer-grained streaming chunking (partial content events that may carry fragment markers rather than full tokens), and 2) a new top-level 'attributes' object attached to responses for structured metadata (customer-provided tags, provenance hints). Motivation: our previous v4 shim assumed chunk boundaries always aligned with token boundaries and only forwarded 'metadata' as opaque blobs, which led to two classes of issues in production: (a) tool/function-call reconstructions occasionally produced malformed calls when chunk boundaries split JSON payloads, and (b) customers lost useful 'attributes' fields because we didn't map them into Redwood's structured metadata pipeline. This PR implements a compatibility layer for Responses v5 that: - Reassembles streamed chunks according to v5 semantics, tracking fragment markers and content-type hints to avoid breaking JSON tool-call payloads. The reassembler buffers partial fragments and only emits stable events when a complete logical unit is available or a timeout/flush policy triggers. - Proxies the top-level 'attributes' object through to Redwood's Response.metadata.attributes map and preserves arbitrary key/value lists. This allows telemetry, reranking, and downstream tools to see OpenAI-provided attributes without losing typing. - Maps the v5 'determinism' and 'seed' flags into Redwood's determinism_hint and seed_hint fields. For v5 requests with 'determinism: high' we set determinism_hint=high (informs routing to lower-temperature model variants). For numeric seeds we carry the seed through; on bridged requests we append seed to the response metadata so clients can reproduce outputs where applicable. - Improves streaming stability around tool/function calls by detecting JSON boundaries and recovering when chunks split JSON strings/escapes. If a chunk split is detected, the reassembler will wait for the following chunk(s) up to a configurable window (default 200ms) before attempting parse. If the parse still fails, we emit a recoverable parse-failure trace and fallback to raw passthrough to avoid dropping candidate tool invocations. - Adds reconciliation tests that simulate intermittent TCP reconnection during streaming, validating that the reassembler recovers and does not duplicate tool calls or lose attributes. Implementation notes: - openai/bridge/streaming_reassembler.go contains the bulk of the protocol logic: fragment bookkeeping, flush window, and integrity checks. The algorithm uses content-type hints (event.header.type) when present to speed up decision-making. - attributes_proxy.go maps the v5 attributes into internal metadata and preserves nested arrays as JSON strings (we avoid nested objects in the top-level metadata map to keep downstream consumers stable). - Determinism/seed mapping is intentionally non-invasive: we only set hints and never override user-supplied model parameters. Rollout plan: - Canary on Dedicated region us-east-2 with 5% traffic for 72h, collect metrics: streaming_reassembly.rate, reassembly.errors, toolcall.parse_failures, attributes.forwarded.count. - If no regressions, increase to 25% then full rollout. Tests: - integration/resp_v5_streaming.test.ts covers chunk boundary splits, reconnections, and attribute passthrough. - Added unit tests for reassembly edge cases (escaped quotes, unicode splitting). Backward compatibility: - v4/v3 flows unchanged. Bridge detects Responses version header and uses the v5 path only when the remote advertises v5. Docs & user notes: - docs/openai_compat.md updated with field mappings, example request/response before/after, and guidance for consumers to use attributes for routing/telemetry. - README in sdk/openai_compat has example TypeScript shim usage. Known limitations: - We currently stringify nested attribute objects to avoid schema changes in the metadata pipeline; teams that need typed nested metadata should request an extension (ENG-3310). - Edge-case: extremely large single logical events that exceed reassembly buffer will fall back to passthrough with a logged warning. Checklist:
- [x] Reassembler implementation
- [x] Attribute forwarding
- [x] Seed/determinism hint mapping
- [x] Integration tests for reconnection and toolcall boundaries
- [x] Docs update
- [x] Canary rollout plan
Marco Ruiz: Good work on the reassembler — the fragment bookkeeping looks sane. Two asks: (1) add a test that simulates an escape sequence split across chunks (e.g. "\u") so we don't accidentally corrupt JSON, (2) add a metric for 'reassembly_latency_p95' so SRE can alert on regressions.
Aisha Patel (reply): Added the escape-split test and exposed reassembly_latency_p95 in the reassembler metrics (see streaming_reassembler.go:metrics).
Evelyn Chen: The attributes mapping is fine but we should avoid blindly copying large attribute blobs into the top-level metadata; can we cap attribute payloads to 2KB and attach a notice in metadata if truncated?
Aisha Patel (reply): Implemented 2KB cap with truncated_attribute_notice key; added unit test to validate truncation and notice.
Jonah Kim: CI failure on first run was due to a flaky reconnect test. You used a 50ms backoff in tests; bumping to 100ms made it stable. Also add a brief note in docs about determinism semantics so users know it only influences routing, not model temperature override.
Aisha Patel (reply): Increased test backoff and added determinism paragraph to docs/openai_compat.md.
Add compatibility layer for OpenAI Responses v5: streaming chunk reassembly, attributes metadata forwarding, and mapping for seed/determinism hints. Improves toolcall stability across chunk boundaries and preserves top-level attributes for downstream tooling.
Canary scheduled: us-east-2 Dedicated 5% traffic starting 2024-12-07. If rollout uncovers any increase in toolcall.parse_failures > 0.1% revert and triage.

This PR introduces a telemetry-replay harness for the model intake pipeline plus a release contextualizer that synthesizes short, stability-weighted changelog fragments for new model onboarding. Motivation: onboarding diffs and perf signatures are often noisy; product owners and engineers need concise, prioritized release notes and deterministic probes that can be replayed locally and in CI to validate regressions. This change bundles three complementary pieces: 1) telemetry-replay harness: canonicalizes and replays sampled telemetry (latency histograms, sequence-length distributions, failure traces) against an intake candidate in a repeatable way; includes a small fixture format and deterministic seed strategy so CI runs produce comparable aggregates; 2) metadata enrichment pipeline: attaches sampled telemetry fingerprints and stability scores to model intake metadata, exposing top-level fields used by the release contextualizer and downstream gating logic; 3) release contextualizer: an automation that consumes model metadata + replay aggregates to generate a one-paragraph release blurb and three short bullet impact statements (latency, accuracy surrogate, compatibility notes) prioritized by a stability-weighted delta metric. Checklist: - [x] telemetry replay core + fixtures - [x] ingestion hook to store telemetry fingerprint on model manifest - [x] release contextualizer CLI and service endpoint - [x] unit and integration tests for deterministic replay - [x] docs: markdown describing harness and manifest fields - [x] Linear link added (ENG-1259). Related: this work complements the perf fingerprinting and changelog-drafter efforts; it is deliberately small in scope (generator + deterministic inputs) so we can iterate. We expect follow-ups to add more heuristics and UI cards in console.
Aisha: Can we make the replay fixtures smaller by sampling percentiles instead of raw buckets? Author: implemented a percentile export option in seed_policy.py and added a test explaining accuracy tradeoffs.
Marco: The stability score formula needs a short doc so SRE can validate thresholds. Author: added a docs section and a helper function with comments and examples.
Ling: CI flaky on Windows runner when seeding RNG — looks like os.urandom difference. Author: switched to a portable deterministic RNG and re-ran CI.

Initial CI run reported a flaky test (runnable RNG seeding) and a lint failure in contextualizer templates. Fixes pushed; subsequent CI run passed all checks (unit, integration, lint, typecheck). Deployment: added a gated k8s Job manifest for replay runs behind a feature flag.

Initial scoring heuristics are conservative; follow-up work planned for UI integration and threshold tuning.
