Motivation: writing accurate, prioritized release notes for model updates is time-consuming and often misses operational signals. This PR adds a telemetry-driven curator that ingests model telemetry and auto-synthesizes concise, ranked release-note fragments for model onboarding and version rollouts.

What this changes (summary): implemented a lightweight curator microservice and registry hook that: (1) consumes time-windowed model telemetry (p95 latency, p99, error rate, eval delta, token-cost changes) from the telemetry store, (2) computes an impact score per signal using a configurable weighting profile, (3) synthesizes short human-readable fragments (1-2 sentences) with signal context and suggested severity tags, (4) attaches fragments to model-version draft release notes and ranks them by impact so SRE/product can triage.

Design notes: the curator uses a deterministic scoring heuristic (configurable in registry config) rather than a heavy generative model for initial rollout—this keeps outputs auditable. We provide a preview CLI (registry-cli curator preview) and a web preview in the model registry UI. The curator is opt-in at the model or org level via metadata flag registry.config.curator.enabled (defaults to false). For private deployments the telemetry ingestion runs over local telemetry endpoints only; no telemetry is sent to hosted services.

Files changed (high level): added src/curator/service.py (core scoring + synth tie-in), src/curator/adapter_prometheus.py (telemetry pulls), registry/schema/model_metadata_v3.json (new optional fields: curator_enabled, telemetry_hints, release_blurb_drafts), cli/registry_cli/curator.py (preview tool), docs/operational/release-curator.md (runbook + config), tests/curator/test_scoring.py, tests/curator/test_integration_e2e.py, examples/onboard/curator-preview.yml, infra/helm/curator-chart.yaml, migration/0007-add-curator-metadata.sql.

Commits (high-level):
- 3f4b9d2 initial curator prototype: scoring engine + simple templates
- a9e1b7f add prometheus adapter + time-windowed pulls
- d2a4c62 add CLI preview + registry API hook for draft fragments
- f9b0c3a add schema migration and metadata docs
- 1c0e5d1 tests: scoring unit tests + e2e with sample telemetry blob
- b6f7d8a polish: handle missing telemetry gracefully, add opt-in flag, update docs and examples

Review conversation (condensed):
- Rohit Singh (review): "Nice approach keeping the initial version deterministic. Two asks: add a clear audit trail for curator decisions, and ensure we never auto-publish notes without explicit opt-in. Also please name the severity taxonomy in the schema."
- Author (Ava): "Addressed: curator now records 'decision_reason' entries (scoring vector) per fragment in registry change log; curator respects model-level curator_enabled and org-level opt-in. Added severity taxonomy enum to model_metadata_v3.json and docs."
- Claire O'Neil (review): "Can we expose the raw signals in preview and add an option to surface the top-3 contributing signals?"
- Author: "Added top_contributors field in preview output and UI snippet; updated CLI and e2e tests to assert presence."
- Diego Rivera (security review): "Confirm that telemetry never leaves private deployment boundaries and that we enforce KMS usage for any persisted curator artifacts."
- Author: "Curator persists artifacts to the same registry blob store and respects existing KMS configs; note included in runbook and helm chart values."

Requested changes and resolution: all requested changes were addressed across commits b6f7d8a and subsequent polish commits. Unit tests and e2e test were added for the preview flow and migration.

CI summary: initial CI run flagged lint errors (flake8) and a transient e2e failure in the integration job. Fixes committed (style and a test timeout bump). Final CI: all checks passed (unit, lint, integration, helm chart lint).

Testing and rollout plan: curator is feature-flagged. We'll enable in staging orgs and run the preview against a set of historical telemetry windows to validate fragment relevance. Observability: added curator-specific metrics (curator.fragments.generated, curator.score.histogram, curator.preview_latency) and dashboard panel in docs to watch production behavior.

Backward compatibility and migration: schema migration 0007 is additive and optional; existing models without curator fields keep same behavior. The migration script is idempotent and covered by tests.

Security/Privacy: by default curator disabled. For private installs nothing is shipped off-cluster; helm chart exposes curator.enabled and curator.ingestEndpoint. Artifacts are stored encrypted when KMS present.

Open items / follow-ups:
- ENG-1427: explore an alternative generative refinement step for higher-signal blurbs (out of scope for this PR).
- PM-587: add UX affordances for editing curated fragments before release (scheduled).

Merge: squash and merge. Merge commit: 7c1e8f4c (squash).
- Introduces a new "telemetry curator" service that synthesizes concise release-note fragments from aggregated model telemetry (latency, error rate, eval regressions, cost delta).
- Adds opt-in model metadata fields for curated blurbs and telemetry signal annotations.
- Backwards compatible: curator is opt-in and only populates draft release snippets unless enabled in registry config.

payload.body:
Motivation: model onboarding currently produces large, noisy release notes and model profiles when telemetry is sparse. This PR adds two complementary pieces: (1) a probing contract abstraction (lightweight declarative probes that run small deterministic workloads against incoming model artifacts) and (2) a compact change-lens that synthesizes a short, human-friendly release preview (<=3 bullets) from the combined onboarding metadata and probe results. The goal is to give reviewers a high-signal preview of changes (compatibility, perf delta, token footprint) without waiting for full population of profile telemetry.

What this PR does (high level):
- Add a "probing contract" DSL and runner to models/onboard. Contracts are small YAML manifests that declare probes (prompt template, input shard, expected stability buckets) and lightweight validators (latency_threshold_ms, mem_delta_pct, semantic_consistency_check). Contracts are scoped per-source and attach to onboard artifacts during intake.
- Implement an in-repo probes runner (registry/probes/runner.py) that executes contracts inside a sandboxed, rate-limited worker and emits structured probe records (jsonl) and a concise probe-summary blob used by downstream tooling.
- Introduce change-lens synthesizer (changelog/lens.py) that consumes model metadata, declared contracts, and probe summaries to generate a compact release preview: three prioritized bullets (compatibility risks, perf delta, recommended tags/rollout plan). The change-lens is intentionally conservative (prefers false negatives) and surfaces a confidence score.
- Wire the synthesizer into the onboarding pipeline: onboard hooks now emit a preview draft as part of the pre-approve artifact (console + Linear comment).
- Add unit and integration tests, plus sample contract manifests and a small e2e harness for CI.

Notes on design decisions: the probing contract DSL is intentionally minimal to encourage adoption by solutions engineers; contracts are ephemeral and do not replace full performance profiles or long-running benchmarks. The change-lens uses a lightweight heuristic ranker (feature-weighted rules) rather than a learned model to remain auditable in the release flow.

Checklist: 
- [x] Probing contract DSL + schema + loader
- [x] Probes runner with sandbox/timeouts
- [x] Probe summary serializer (compact jsonl)
- [x] Change-lens synthesizer + prioritization rules
- [x] Integrations: onboarding hook + console preview endpoint
- [x] Tests: unit + integration + a small e2e CI job
- [x] Docs: short how-to + examples in docs/onboard/quickstart.md

Related: swaps ideas from ENG-743 and earlier work on digesters but purposefully differs by focusing on an early-stage preview (not a replacement for full changelogs). See Linear ENG-9621 for adoption plan and rollout gating.

Security/Cost: runner executes small synthetic workloads; we added a per-tenant budget guard and global rate limiter to avoid noisy intake storms. All probe artifacts respect PII rules and default to redacting model-provided prompts unless explicitly allowed by the onboard manifest.
Owen Park: Nice direction — please make the default timeout for the runner explicit and ensure that we don't block the main intake job. Also prefer a 95th percentile latency check rather than mean.
Elena Ruiz (author): Updated runner timeouts to default 10s per probe and implemented a 95th percentile check in serializers. Added non-blocking behavior to onboarding hook (now async with prefetch token).
Priya Nair: The compact preview must not expose prompts or user-specific tokens. Confirmed after reading the redaction guard, but please add an explicit unit test for redaction.
Elena Ruiz: Added test for prompt redaction and documented the opt-in flag in the contract schema. Example contracts use placeholders by default.
Marcus Chen: Suggest adding a small opt-in telemetry flag so customers can choose to include probe-derived perf stats in their long-form profile. Also noted a minor lint failure in changelog/prioritizer.py.
Elena Ruiz: Added telemetry opt-in boolean and fixed linter warnings; CI now passes locally.
- Add lightweight probing contracts to capture early compatibility and perf signals during model intake.
- Introduce compact change-lens that synthesizes a 3-line release preview for faster human review.
- Add sandboxed probes runner with rate limiting and redaction guards.

Impact: low-risk feature behind opt-in; defaults are conservative. Admins can enable probes per-tenant. Rollout plan: staged opt-in for dev/test tenants, then gradual enablement for solutions-engineered onboards (see ENG-9621).
The preview is not authoritative; reviewers should still rely on full profile artifacts when available. If reviewers prefer not to see previews, set the onboarding flow flag PREVIEW_DRAFT=false. The contract DSL is intentionally small; teams wanting richer probes should extend the DSL and add guarded runners.
payload.title: Introduce probing contracts and compact change-lens for lightweight release previews

payload.body:
Motivation: onboarding long-tail variants (small, quantized, distillations) has been brittle because our profiling pipeline assumed uniform sampling. This PR introduces a dynamic-profile-sampling engine that picks example slices by usage heat, token-length distribution, and a rare-case weight to produce representative performance profiles with fewer runs. It also supplies a machine-readable onboarding checklist generator that emits actionable items for reviewers (missing metadata, required evals, compatibility flags) and an optional changelog composer hook that synthesizes concise release notes from profile deltas. Implementation summary: 1) profile_sampler.py implements a multi-criteria sampler with pluggable heuristic weights and deterministic seeding for repeatability; 2) onboard_checklist.go adds a generator that consumes metadata and evaluation results and outputs a checklist JSON that the UI and CLI surface; 3) changelog_composer.go provides a configurable template engine that turns delta summaries and perf-regressions into draft release notes; 4) added lightweight telemetry events and unit tests for sampler edge cases; 5) updated docs/onboarding.md and examples with recommended sampling presets and rollout guidance. Backwards compatibility: sampler defaults to the legacy uniform mode unless the model manifest sets "sampling.strategy": "dynamic". Checklist output only augments existing review flows and is gated behind a feature flag. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout to canary workspace, followed by a 2-week telemetry bake to validate representativeness and cost impact. Related work: complements ENG-5128 (profiling pipeline refactor) and should reduce average profiling runs by ~40% on preliminary experiments. Notes: I intentionally kept the default weights conservative to avoid biasing short-tail production models. Open questions: should we add an automated calibration step that tunes weights based on historical evaluation results?
Adds dynamic sampling engine for long-tail model profiling, a machine-readable onboarding checklist generator, and a changelog composer hook. Backwards-compatible metadata keys added. No runtime behavior changes for existing registry consumers.

Motivation: We want to make model onboarding metadata more actionable for runtime and downstream teams and to automate concise changelog generation for model releases. This PR introduces two pieces: (1) affordance_anchors: a small, opt-in annotation block in the model manifest that surfaces recommended serving knobs (preferred quantization profile, batching hints, expected token-distribution tail behavior, and canonical prompt examples) and a confidence/coverage score; (2) release-sprocket: a lightweight changelog assembler that consumes profile deltas, sample-coverage matrices, and affordance anchors to produce compact release notes suitable for console UI and email digests.

What changed (high level): added affordance_anchors schema to manifest v2; migration helper to backfill older manifests with best-effort anchors from profiling traces; a CLI "release-sprocket" tool (Go) that emits a condensed JSON + markdown brief and a one-line summary; unit and integration tests for schema, migration, and sprocket; updated onboarding docs and two example manifests.

Why this is different: existing profile and changelog pipelines focus on performance deltas and semantic diffs. Affordance anchors bridge the gap between profiling heuristics and actionable serving recommendations, and release-sprocket stitches that context into a human-readable, concise note aimed at SREs, product owners, and SDK consumers.

Checklist:
- [x] Manifest schema change and docs
- [x] Migration/backfill helper with dry-run mode
- [x] Sprocket CLI + unit tests

Related: ENG-3127 (affordance schema design) and SUP-1421 (customer-requested concise changelogs).

Motivation: Onboarding teams spend time writing the same boilerplate README and release bullets for every model intake. This PR adds a generator that produces a compact model README.md and a concise impact blurb synthesized from three inputs: the model profile metadata, recent performance/eval snapshots, and aggregated usage telemetry (if available). The generated README covers summary, performance profile, rollout recommendations, known limitations, and example API snippets. It also emits 3-4 release bullets suitable for changelogs or product briefings.

What this changes (summary): commit: 1) introduce generator service and CLI glue (model_registry/tools/readme_generator.py), 2) add templates and formatters (templates/auto_readme/*), 3) add telemetry summarizer hook (model_registry/telemetry/summary_adapter.py), 4) integrate generation into onboarding pipeline (hooks/onboard_postprocess.go), 5) tests and sample fixtures (tests/readme_gen_test.py, fixtures/sample_profile.json).

Why telemetry: When telemetry is present (usage by endpoint, median latency, error-rate by route), the generator includes an "impact score" computed from request volume and latency regression that surfaces which downstream surfaces are likely to be affected by model changes. This helps PMs and SREs prioritize rollouts. Telemetry is optional for privacy; generator falls back to profile-only output.

Generated README sketch (excerpt):
- Title: Compact human-readable model brief
- One-line summary: "ggml-turbo-3b — tuned for chat with 128k context, optimized 8-bit kernels"
- Key metrics: latency p50/p95, tokens/sec baseline, embedding dims, typical seq-length budget
- Perf profile: recommended batch sizing, quantization candidate (int8-fast), expected memory footprint on A100/RTX6000
- Rollout advice: canary 5% for 24h then 25% if no regressions; fallback to model:ggml-turbo-3b-v1 on error
- Known limitations: hallucination cases with numeric reasoning; degrade gracefully with reranker
- Release bullets (automatically composed):
  * Add ggml-turbo-3b-v2: +15% throughput for short prompts; see perf-profile section.
  * Default rollout: canary 5% for 24h (auto-generated recommendation).
  * Telemetry: alerts recommended on latency +30% or error-rate +1.5x baseline.

Files changed (high-level):
- model_registry/tools/readme_generator.py — core generator logic and templating.
- templates/auto_readme/* — handlebars-like templates for README sections and bullets.
- model_registry/telemetry/summary_adapter.py — small adapter to compute traffic-weighted impact score.
- hooks/onboard_postprocess.go — calls generator after profile upload; writes README.md into model bundle.
- tests/readme_gen_test.py — unit tests for template output and telemetry fallback.
- fixtures/sample_profile.json — synthetic model profile used in tests.
- docs/processes/model-onboard.md — document referencing the new auto-generation step.

Commits (high-level):
- c1f4b1d introduce generator skeleton and CLI
- a8d9e02 add telemetry summarizer and impact scoring
- b3e7f44 add templates and README examples
- e91c2fa integrate generator into onboard pipeline (hook)

Review conversation (highlights):

- Maya (author): "Agreed on aggregation, added an explicit aggregation step in summary_adapter.py and documented admin toggle in docs/processes/model-onboard.md."
- Sofia Patel (review): "Can we keep the generated README under model bundle but not auto-publish to public docs?"

Integration smoke test (onboard pipeline against a synthetic profile) executed in staging and validated README.md generation.

Backward compatibility and safety: The new hook is behind a feature flag (model.readme_generation.enabled) and defaults to false in existing clusters. The onboarding CLI exposes a --generate-readme flag for early adopters. No public API changes.

Operational notes: The impact score calculation uses a decay window of 14 days by default and can be configured per-organization. Telemetry ingestion adheres to existing aggregation and PII-stripping contracts; nothing with raw user identifiers is persisted in the README.

Testing & QA: Added unit tests to validate template placeholders and telemetry fallback. Added an integration sanity check in the onboard pipeline that writes the README to a temp bundle and asserts presence of the key sections. Add automated model README generator that synthesizes onboarding README.md and concise release bullets from model profile, eval highlights, and live telemetry. Improves cross-team discoverability and reduces manual release-note churn.

This PR introduces a lightweight onboarding linter and an automated compatibility-tagging hook for model registry submissions. Motivation: onboarding iterations revealed frequent metadata inconsistencies (schema drift) and unclear compatibility between quantized/float variants of the same model. The change bundles three complementary pieces: 1) a CLI 'redwood model onboard --lint' mode that validates metadata, profiles, and required artifacts; 2) a server-side hook that runs on PRs to compute compatibility fingerprints across new model artifacts and auto-apply tags like 'compat:kvcache-stable' or 'compat:requires-shard'; and 3) a changelog templating helper that emits a structured release note fragment when a model version is promoted. The description includes a brief checklist of behaviour: - lint rejects missing required fields (architecture, families, sequence_length_profile) - compatibility hook runs lightweight perf microbenchmarks (cold start, kv cache warm) on a small sample to decide tagging - changelog helper generates a YAML fragment stored in .model_releases/ for later aggregation The CLI and hooks are opt-in for new model owners via metadata flag 'onboard.automation: enabled'. See linked Linear tasks for rollout plan and opt-out path.
Diego: Nice work — can we make the perf runner budget-aware? Some customers have limited CI quotas.
Author (Asha): Added a 'budget' config to the sample_runner; default is 30s and can be toggled in CI.
Mina: Schema change looks fine, but please add a migration note for existing manifests.
Author (Asha): Migration note added to docs and a small compat shim that accepts old-key 'seq_profile' mapping to 'sequence_length_profile'.
Liam: please add metrics for hook runtime and failure counts so SRE can alert on noisy runs.

Summary: Adds a versioned metadata locking layer to the model registry to prevent conflicting profile edits and to provide auditable, transactional updates. Also introduces a sampled release-teaser generator that produces concise, telemetry-driven release snippets for changelogs and release notes drafts. Motivation: We observed occasional metadata stomping (parallel reviewer edits and automation hooks) and noisy/duplicative release notes authored manually. This PR reduces risk of merge conflicts, provides an explicit upgrade path for existing profiles, and automates concise release teasers so release engineers have a reliable starting point. Changes: 1) metadata-lock service: - New service layer (metadata/locks) that manages versioned locks using optimistic compare-and-swap backed by an advisory-lock fallback (Postgres advisory lock) for rare conflict windows. - Locks are coarse-grained at the profile ID + namespace level with an optional subkey (e.g., performance.profile) for targeted edits. - Each lock write increments a profile metadata version (profile_metadata_version), stored in registry_profiles.metadata_version (bigint). - API changes: PATCH /profiles/:id accepts if-match header (version token) and returns 412 on conflict with current metadata_version. 2) migration: - DB migration adds metadata_version column with default 1 and migrates existing ETags to initial versions for active profiles. - Migration is safe: reads are allowed during backfill; writes that race are rejected until backfill completes. 3) sampled release-teaser generator: - New module (releasenotes/teaser) that samples recent telemetry (latency, throughput delta, acceptance rate, rollout fraction) and generates 1-2 sentence teaser candidates ranked by impact. - Teasers are short, neutral language, and include an impact tag (e.g., perf, reliability, compatibility). - CLI integration: `rgm release-tease --profile <id> --window 7d` outputs top 3 candidate teasers and confidence scores. 4) UX/console: - Console shows an inline warning when you open a profile edit if you are editing a stale version, with a CTA to refresh or force-capture an updated baseline. - Release notes composer can import suggested teasers into the draft. 5) infra and tests: - Introduced advisory lock util and an in-memory fallthrough for unit tests. - Added unit tests for optimism conflict path and e2e test that simulates concurrent patchers. - Added benchmark harness for lock acquisition latency under 1000 concurrent simulated clients. Rationale and tradeoffs: - Optimistic-first reduces common-path latency for single-editor flows (majority of updates). Advisory locks prevent livelock during heavy automation-driven churn; we accept the small probability of a blocking fallback. - Changelog automation produces concise teasers only; full release notes still authored by humans. Checklist: - [x] DB migration script (non-blocking backfill) - [x] API contract updates with 412 behavior - [x] Unit tests for optimistic and fallback paths - [x] e2e concurrency test - [x] Console previews and CTA - [x] CLI integration for release-teaser drafts - [x] Benchmark harness for locks - [x] Docs: registry metadata locking, migration guidance, teaser rationale Rollout plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable metadata locks for 10% of orgs (feature flag) and generate teasers in dry-run mode. Observe conflict rates, lock latencies, and teaser adoption metrics. Phase 2: enable writes for all orgs and promote teasers to optional import in release composer. Phase 3: default-on for new orgs and opt-in for older orgs after migration window. Backwards compatibility: APIs will return 412 for stale writes; clients using older SDKs will receive explicit errors. We included SDK compatibility helpers and added a swift-fail guidance doc in redwood-sdk-* repos. Migration window and fallbacks are documented in upgrades/MIGRATION.md.
Diego Morales (2025-07-22): This looks good overall. Two concerns: how do we handle very large backfills and the window where clients might get repeated 412s? Suggest a backoff in SDK and a visible 'backfill in progress' flag in the console.
Maya Chen (2025-07-22): Reply: Agreed. Added backoff guidance to SDK compat helpers and we emit a backfill-in-progress flag via /registry/status which the console now surfaces.
Arjun Patel (2025-07-23): Could the sampled teaser generator leak PII through telemetry sampling? Please ensure we redact any identifiers before passing text to the teaser templates.
Maya Chen (2025-07-23): Reply: Teaser pipeline now runs a strict sanitizer that strips identifiers and normalizes numeric tokens. Added a unit test for sanitization.
Lena Ortiz (2025-07-24): Approve with one nit: the console CTA copy feels long. Suggest 'Refresh to get the latest metadata' instead of the current copy.
Maya Chen (2025-07-24): Reply: Updated CTA per feedback and adjusted translation keys.
- Introduced versioned metadata locking to prevent conflicting edits and provide explicit 412s for stale writes. SDK compatibility helpers added to simplify client-side retries and backoff.
- Added a sampled release-teaser generator that suggests concise, telemetry-weighted changelog snippets for release authors (CLI + Console integration).
- Safe DB migration for profile metadata versions with backfill guidance in docs.
Notes for operators: enable feature flag 'metadata-locks' to canary; review migration doc before full rollout.

Summary: This PR adds explicit, evidence-friendly audit log events for KMS rotation-related control-plane operations: (1) updating the active key version / key alias target, (2) enabling/disabling dual-read (dual-decrypt) window, (3) toggling cutover flags for encrypt/write path, and (4) rollback toggles to re-enable old key version reads/writes. Motivation: We currently have good runtime logs and some config-change auditing, but rotation reviews (SOC2/ISO + customer security reviews) keep asking for a clear, queryable trail of who changed what/when during rotation. The goal here is to make rotation events first-class in the audit log schema so (a) internal evidence collection is repeatable, (b) customers can export/ingest these events into SIEM, and (c) on-call can quickly correlate incidents with rotation state changes. Scope: Control-plane audit events only (no cryptographic changes; no new KMS calls). Related: ADR-008 (rotation strategy + dual-read/cutover), ENG-4826 (evidence template), audit-log-exporter PR will follow with schema wiring for exports. Event design: - Stable event names (no environment-specific names): kms.rotation.key_version_update, kms.rotation.dual_read_update, kms.rotation.cutover_update, kms.rotation.rollback_initiated. - Common fields: event_version, actor.{type,id,email}, request.{id,ip,user_agent}, resource.{project_id,env,cluster}, correlation_id, change_ticket (optional), before/after payloads with only non-sensitive values. - Explicit redaction: never emit raw key material; only KMS key identifiers/aliases/ARNs and version labels. - Idempotency: repeated requests that result in no effective change emit kms.rotation.noop_change (for evidence completeness; can be filtered). - Failure behavior: emit kms.rotation.change_attempt_failed with error_category (from taxonomy) and sanitized error_message; do not include cloud-provider request IDs unless already considered non-sensitive (we include kms_request_id only when present and approved by Security). Implementation notes: - Added RotationAuditEmitter helper in control-plane config service; it wraps existing audit logger and ensures required fields are present + consistent. - Updated rotation-related handlers (KeyVersionUpdate, DualReadConfigUpdate, CutoverFlagUpdate) to emit before/after events after validation, and an attempt_failed event on validation or persistence errors. - Added a unit test suite to assert event shape stability (golden JSON snapshots) and required tags. - Added dashboards tags (audit_event_name) to make it easy to slice audit throughput vs error. - Added docs in code comments referencing the evidence checklist fields required by GRC. Rollout plan: - Ship behind feature flag audit.kms_rotation_events.enabled default ON in staging, OFF in prod for 24h. - After verifying event volume and no PII leakage in staging, flip ON in prod via config. - Coordinate with audit-log-exporter change (separate PR) so exported schema includes these new events; until then, events are still queryable internally. Testing: - Unit tests: RotationAuditEmitter shapes + redaction checks. - Integration tests: rotation endpoints in staging with flag ON; verified emitted events present in audit log index with correct correlation_id. - Manual: executed a dual-read enable -> cutover -> rollback in staging and exported the event list for Daniel/Olga to confirm evidence sufficiency. Screenshots/queries are attached in the linked Linear task. Notes for reviewers: Please focus on (a) event naming/field stability, (b) redaction coverage, (c) any gaps in actor/request attribution, and (d) whether noop_change should exist or be removed. This PR does not change runtime decrypt/encrypt behavior; it only increases audit coverage for control-plane state transitions.
Marcus Lin (Security): Can we confirm we never log full key ARNs for customer-managed keys in Private? Some customers consider ARNs sensitive even if not secret. Also please ensure request_context doesn't capture Authorization headers anywhere in audit logger. / Kevin Osei (author): Good call. We currently log key identifiers/ARNs elsewhere in control-plane logs; for audit events I added allowlist-based fields and explicit header stripping. For ARNs: I can switch to logging key alias + last 8 of key ID by default, with an opt-in to log full ARN in hosted/dedicated. Pushing update.
Ethan Park (Platform): The handlers emit audit after persistence; what about the window where DB write succeeds but audit log write fails? We should avoid silent gaps. / Kevin Osei: Agreed. Audit logger is async but we can add a best-effort retry and also emit an internal metric/audit_write_failed counter. Added metric + error log w/ correlation_id; still no blocking path to avoid turning audit into a hard dependency.
Allison Grant (SRE/Observability): Please add event_version and ensure all events include environment/region tags for alerting + dashboards. Also check cardinality on correlation_id. / Kevin Osei: Added event_version=1 to all events, and ensured resource.{env,region,cluster} are populated from request context. correlation_id is already per-request; we don't tag it as a metric label (logs only).
Daniel Carter (GRC/Evidence): For evidence, auditors want a direct mapping between change ticket and rotation events. Can we include change_ticket if provided and document expected format (e.g., Linear ENG-xxxx / Jira CHG-xxxx)? / Kevin Osei: Added optional change_ticket field, sourced from X-Change-Ticket header (validated) and from internal admin UI form. Also added comment with recommended format. Docs PR will reference it explicitly.
Merged via squash into main by Connor O'Brien. Follow-ups: (1) audit-log-exporter schema update to include these events for customer exports, (2) update rotation runbook to reference event queries and change_ticket usage, (3) confirm Private default for logging key identifiers is alias + truncated ID only.
payload.title: Add audit log events for KMS rotation operations (key version updates + cutover toggles)

Motivation: teams onboarding experimental or forked models need a low-friction path to register models and get immediate, actionable release notes so the rest of the platform (serving, billing, console) can surface reasonable defaults. Motivation: When onboarding models we've repeatedly seen fragmented performance and affordance metadata across variants (quantization, hardware target, tokenizer differences) which makes release notes noisy and causes regressions to be under- or over-emphasized. This PR introduces a 'profile stitcher' that merges variant-level profiles into a canonical composite profile using provenance-weighted heuristics and conflict-resolution rules; it also adds a release glossary/annotation generator to the changelog pipeline to produce consolidated, severity-tagged release notes and a short glossary of terms introduced by a model (affordances, profiler metrics, and hardware-specific caveats). Implementation summary: 1) registry/onboard/stitcher.py implements a stitcher core that groups profiles by affinity keys, computes weighted medians for numeric metrics, and preserves per-variant provenance tags; 2) tools/changelog/generator.go gains a new pipeline stage that consumes composite profiles to emit release annotations (severity: info/warn/critical) and an auto-generated glossary.md fragment for each release; 3) API: POST /onboard/preview now returns both the composite profile and a previewed release-glossary blob for review in Console; 4) CLI: added rs-onboard preview-glossary command to let curators inspect suggested annotations locally; 5) tests: integration tests exercise stitcher heuristics across synthetic variant sets and end-to-end changelog generation; 6) docs: docs/registry/release-glossary.md explains glossary semantics and guidance for curators. Backwards compatibility: the stitcher is opt-in behind registry.onboard.stitch.enabled=false by default for rollout, and existing per-variant profiles are left unchanged in the store. Related work: ties to ENG-4921 (profile canonicalization) and ENG-4999 (changelog automation). Rollout plan: feature gated for 2 weeks with canary sampling (5% of onboards), UI preview enabled for curated reviewers, then enable default merge after metrics show no regressions. 
Samir Patel: The stitcher algorithm looks sound but we should add a small-batch fallback to avoid skew when we only have 1-2 variants; can you add tests for that?
Maya Chen: Added a small-batch path and tests; document updated to call out the fallback behavior
Riley Thompson: Please ensure the glossary generator does not include sensitive provenance IDs in public release notes — redact internal IDs by default
Maya Chen: Redaction implemented (provenance IDs replaced with stable pseudonyms) and unit test added
Priya Nair: CI flaked on e2e once; re-ran and results look good. Approving pending full CI pass.
Add profile stitcher (opt-in) that consolidates variant profiles into a canonical composite profile to reduce churn in release notes; add automated release glossary generation and severity annotation to changelog pipeline; preview API and CLI for curator review; guidance doc for glossary semantics; opt-in rollout with canary sampling.

Context: model teams increasingly rely on variant families (e.g. base -> quantized -> distilled) but the registry treated variants as flat siblings. This made rollouts, compatibility checks and changelog summaries noisy when multiple closely-related variants were published. Motivation: provide explicit parent/child relationships for variants and a small autosynth engine that composes human-readable changelog snippets from delta metadata (profile deltas, perf sig changes, compatibility notes). This PR adds a hierarchical variant tagging model, migration & backfill tooling, UI preview hooks, and an autosynth changelog curator that drafts release notes for curator review. Key behavioural changes: 1) variants can declare a parent_variant_id and optional relationship_type (quantized|distilled|pruned|adapter); 2) onboarding API accepts family metadata and validates lineage constraints; 3) changelog autosynth looks at profile delta fingerprints, perf watermarks, and deprecation flags to generate prioritized bullet-lines; 4) release preview shows lineage graph and delta highlights to help reviewers accept the autosynth text. Migration: includes a non-blocking backfill script that infers likely parents using checksum heuristics and affinity matches; a safe migration path is provided (migration can be run with --dry-run, and a lineage-confidence score is written to audit logs). Testing & safety: migration requires a feature flag; autosynth outputs are drafts and must be accepted before publishing. Rollout: staged rollout to curation teams, then registry-wide opt-in. Related work: ENG-1489 (variant rollouts), PM-402 (changelog UX). Checklist: - [x] API contract and schema changes - [x] DB migration + backfill script - [x] Autosynth engine core + heuristics - [x] UI preview component and docs - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] CI pipeline updated to run migration linter Notes: this description is intentionally concise; full implementation notes and operator guidance are in docs/registry/variant_lineage.md and docs/registry/changelog-curator.md
Liam O'Connor: nice approach to explicit lineage; can we avoid nullable parent ids for now and require explicit 'unknown' relationship_type when inference is low?
Maya Chen (author): we decided to support nullable parent_variant_id to avoid blocking existing onboardings; the backfill will add confidence scores and a migration flag will allow operators to require non-null parents later.
Sofia Martínez: autosynth looks useful but I want stronger guardrails around deprecations — suggest an explicit 'suppress-autosynth' tag when publishing experimental variants.
Maya Chen: added support to the API for a suppress_autosynth boolean and updated the docs with recommended practice.
Ibrahim Khan: DB index looks good; one nit about index name length on older MySQL versions — suggest truncated naming.
Added hierarchical variant tagging (parent/child relationships) and an autosynth changelog curator to draft release notes based on profile and perf deltas; includes migration/backfill tooling and UI preview for release review; operators can opt into lineage enforcement via feature flag; added operator documentation and tests.
Unit tests added for schema validation, autosynth scoring, and migration dry-run. Integration tests simulate small model families and verify lineage plumbing. CI runs migration linter to catch risky schema changes. Manual validation performed against staging snapshot 2025-10-28.
1) Run backfill with --dry-run on staging and review lineage_confidence report; 2) After validation, enable backfill and monitor audit logs; 3) Notify curation team and enable UI preview flag; 4) Collect feedback and tune autosynth templates via PM-402.
Run scripts/migrations/backfill_variant_lineage.py --env staging --dry-run to get confidence scores; when comfortable, run without --dry-run and keep migration logs retained for 30 days; the feature flag 'variant_lineage_enforced' controls whether onboarding requires explicit parents.
I have run the migration linter and unit/integration tests locally; this PR is ready for staged rollout. -- Maya Chen

payload.body:
Motivation: some model rollouts cause subtle, cohort-specific regressions that are not obvious from global metrics. This PR introduces a probe-driven 'occlusion detector' that compares live-sampled probe telemetry against a baseline cohort fingerprint and synthesizes a compact, contextual release digest that highlights affected prompt cohorts and suggested remediation actions (score, rollback hint, minimal repro).

What this PR does (high level): 1) Adds a sampled telemetry union pipeline to merge periodic probe samples with production request traces while preserving privacy/sampling guarantees. 2) Implements an occlusion detector that computes per-cohort delta statistics (accuracy/semantic-distance/latency) and flags cohorts exceeding configurable thresholds. 3) Generates a contextual release synth — a human-readable changelog fragment that summarizes which cohorts regressed, sample prompts, expected impact, and an automated 'rollback score' suggestion based on severity and traffic weight. 4) Integrates the digest as an optional attachment to release notes and as a webhook payload for incident tooling.

Why unique: instead of only surfacing numeric deltas, the detector collates representative prompts and links to the model-profile + perf-profile diffs so release authors and SREs can quickly assess risk and triage. It targets the recurring class of regressions that show up in low-volume but business-critical cohorts.

Compatibility and safety: the telemetry union runs as a rate-limited background exporter and strips PII from prompts using existing scrubbers. Default thresholds are conservative and require at least two consecutive probe windows before a cohort is auto-flagged.

Related work: ENG-1245 (cohort telemetry sampling), PR:redwood-model-registry#17345 (baseline samplers), and the rollout playbook for canaries.

Checklist: - [x] Telemetry union pipeline (sampling operator + scrubber) - [x] Occlusion detector core logic and threshold config - [x] Compact release synth generation and template - [x] Webhook + release note attachment support - [x] Unit + integration tests for detector heuristics - [x] Docs: short guide for release authors
Marcus Lee: Please clarify how the scrubber handles edge cases like code snippets that might look like PII.
Sofia Patel: We added a two-step rule — first apply token-level heuristic redaction then a regex pass for common PII forms. Added tests for code-like payloads to ensure we don't over-redact.
Priya Nair: Can the detector be noisy for very small cohorts?
Sofia Patel: Defaults require a minimum sample count and two consecutive probe windows before auto-flagging; added a tunable 'minimum_traffic_weight' parameter.
Evan Chen: How do we surface this to non-technical release authors?
Sofia Patel: The synth produces a short bullet summary and an optional expanded appendix with representative prompts and links to profile diffs; docs include examples.
Marcus Lee: CI flake on Linux integration fixed in fa8b4d2; approving.
Evan Chen: Approved after minor docs tweaks.
- Add probe-driven occlusion detector: flags cohort-specific regressions and synthesizes contextual release digests.
- Telemetry union pipeline for sampled probe + production trace merging (PII-scrubbed).
- Webhook and release attachment support to include contextual digests with release notes.
When enabling the occlusion detector, start with the 'conservative' preset. The digest includes a rollback_score (0-100) and suggested next steps; treat >70 as high risk for immediate rollback. The detector respects existing canary/fallback policies. See docs/model-registry/release-occlusion-guide.md for examples.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: We frequently see model intake manifests that pass schema validation but later fail in Dedicated or Private deployments due to subtle incompatibilities (quantization support, sequence-length assumptions, KV-cache sizing hints). This PR adds a focused compatibility linter + a release-impact estimator to reduce onboarding friction and automate initial changelog blurbs. The tools are intended to surface actionable remediation steps for SREs and platform owners and to seed the changelog with an impact paragraph that teams can edit before release.

What this PR does (summary): - Add onboard-compat-lint CLI and server-side hook that runs as part of intake validation. The linter checks: model config hardware affinity hints, quantization tags, tokenizer EOL/byte-level edge cases, max sequence vs memory budget heuristics, KV-cache compatibility markers, and model artifact packaging (sharded vs monolithic). - Add a release-impact estimator that consumes linter findings and a small local perf-profile (optional) to synthesize a suggested changelog entry: estimated QPS/latency delta, suggested rollout (canary size, fallback models), and recommended quantization/compile options. - Wire the linter into pre-submit checks in the intake service and the model registry onboarding pipeline; add a lightweight UI annotation to the model profile page showing the top 3 compatibility concerns.

Checklist: - [x] Linter core rules implemented and unit-tested - [x] Estimator heuristics implemented and documented - [x] Pre-submit hook added to intake pipeline - [x] Add API endpoint for UI annotation - [x] E2E smoke tests for a representative small/large model onboarding path - [x] Docs PR linking + short runbook attached

Commits (high-level): - 1a2b3c4: introduce onboard-compat-lint package, rule runner, and basic rule set - 2d3e4f5: add estimator module and changelog templating engine - 3f4g5h6: integrate pre-submit hook + registry web annotation endpoint - 4h5i6j7: add unit tests and fixture models for quantization/kv-cache cases - 5j6k7l8: fix schema edge case found by CI (tokenizer metadata field optionality) - 6k7l8m9: polish messages and copy for release note drafts

Files changed (high-level): - packages/onboard-compat-lint/{index.ts, rules/*.ts, rules/README.md} - services/intake/hooks/preflight-check.ts - services/registry/api/compat-annotations.ts - ui/registry/components/CompatBadge.vue - tests/fixtures/{gpt-mini-quantized,bert-sharded}.tar.gz - tests/integration/onboard-compat.test.ts - docs/onboarding/compatibility-linter.md

Tests and CI: Initial CI run failed on a schema unit test (tokenizer metadata optionality) reported by tests/integration/onboard-compat.test.ts. The failure was addressed in commit 5j6k7l8 (made tokenizer.metadata optional in the validator and added a targeted unit test). After the fix CI passed on rerun; full suite green including lint, unit, and integration checks. A small perf regression was observed in a synthetic perf harness (3% median latency increase for tiny models when running the linter in preflight mode). To address this we changed the default preflight to run in asynchronous/opt-in scan mode for large payloads; the estimator can still be invoked with a flag to run the optional perf probe.

Review conversation (highlights): - Evan Li: "Nice rule set. Can we add an explicit rule for tokenizers that emit unknown-bytes on stream restarts? Also can the estimator annotate confidence scores for its latency/QPS numbers?" --> Author: "Added unknown-bytes rule and exposed estimator confidence (pct). See rules/tokenizer-unknown-bytes.ts and estimator confidence field in API response." - Marta Ruiz: "UI needs to avoid alarmist language by default; can we change red/yellow/green thresholds to mirror existing console thresholds?" --> Author: "Adjusted thresholds and added copy changes in CompatBadge.vue; thresholds are now configurable via registry feature flags." - Sanjay Patel: "If this flags models that require specialized GPU kernels, we need an automated fallback policy recommendation." --> Author: "Added fallback suggestions: recommended smaller variant, suggest quantize-to-fp16 or a fallback model alias if available. See estimator heuristics and produced changelog draft examples." - QA (Jessica Huang): "E2E onboarding smoke found an intermittent race when annotations are written back to the model profile after bake; added a retry + idempotency guard in compat-annotations.ts."

Backward compatibility and rollout: - Linter rules are additive; existing intake payloads will continue to pass when no issues are found. The pre-submit hook defaults to warning mode for accounts that have not opted into strict onboarding. - Default change: the UI will show annotations as a non-blocking banner; registry admins can flip strict mode via feature flag to make certain rules blocking. - No changes to runtime serving code paths were made in this PR.

Operational notes and runbook snippets included in docs/onboarding/compatibility-linter.md: quick remediation steps for quantization failures, how to interpret estimator confidence, how to set feature flags, and recommended canary sizes for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Security and privacy: the estimator optionally uploads a tiny perf sample when teams opt in; data is labeled with project id and retention follows registry retention policy. No secrets are stored by the linter.

Follow-ups (planned): - ENG-3421.1: add historical similarity lookup to surface prior onboarding fixes for similar models - ENG-3421.2: integrate estimator with rollout automation to propose A/B rollout percentages - PM-1189: product review session and UX polish for the CompatBadge expansion

Merge outcome: Approved by reviewers (Evan Li, Marta Ruiz, Sanjay Patel). CI passed after fix. Squash-merged into main on 2026-03-02 by Priya Kapoor.

Notes for release: include the generated impact paragraph by default in the model's release draft; provide a toggle for engineering teams to opt-out if they prefer manual notes. The change is low-risk to existing pipelines and should reduce onboarding rework for platform teams.
Adds an onboarding linter that enforces intake contract compatibility across hosted/dedicated/private deployments; introduces a lightweight release-impact estimator that auto-drafts changelog lines with performance and rollout guidance. No user-facing breaking changes.
payload.title: Introduce onboarding compatibility linter and release-impact estimator

payload.body:
Context & motivation: model intake today accepts heterogeneous manifests from partners and community models. We repeatedly see small metadata inconsistencies (missing license fields, malformed affinity hints, and sparse telemetry buckets) that block downstream profile generation and make changelog automation noisy. This PR introduces a model intake normalizer and a variant signal aggregator that: normalizes incoming manifests to schema v2, validates and auto-fills common missing metadata, computes per-variant affinity and sample-coverage signals from sampled telemetry, seeds a per-variant calibration profile that the registry can use for rollout heuristics, and emits a concise micro-changelog skeleton to help release note automation.

What this PR does (high level): adds a new intake-normalizer CLI (python) and a library module (registry.ingest.normalize) that performs deterministic normalization and canonicalization; introduces schema v2 for model profiles (profile_schema_v2.json) with explicit "affinity_score" and "sample_coverage" fields; implements a signal-aggregator that consumes sampled telemetry (usage buckets) to produce weighted variant signals; provides a migration/backfill script that computes and populates sample_coverage for recent 90-day windows; integrates a release-drafter hook that creates a short, human-editable changelog fragment when a new model version is onboarded; tightens provenance recording to include transform hashes so downstream reproducibility is possible.

Checklist: * [x] normalization library and CLI implemented * [x] schema v2 added and validated against unit tests * [x] backfill/migration script included with idempotency checks * [x] small integration test that runs intake -> aggregator -> seeded profile -> changelog snippet generation * [x] docs (docs/ingest/normalizer.md) and migration notes * [x] Linear tickets linked and basic QA performed

Commits (summary): - add intake normalizer module and CLI (normalize manifests, canonicalize keys, fill defaults) - add profile_schema_v2.json and validator with tests - implement signal-aggregator (weighted-variant-score algorithm, serialized seed writer) - migration script backfill/sample-coverage-populator and safety guard - add release-drafter hook and changelog fragment template - add unit + integration tests and small e2e harness - docs and changelog entry explaining schema migration

Files changed (high level): registry/ingest/normalizer.py, registry/ingest/aggregator.py, registry/schema/profile_schema_v2.json, registry/migrations/202511_backfill_sample_coverage.sql, scripts/intake_cli.py, tests/ingest/test_normalizer.py, tests/ingest/test_aggregator_integration.py, docs/ingest/normalizer.md, tooling/release_hooks/draft_micro_changelog.py.

Compatibility & migration notes: profile_schema_v2 is additive; v1 consumers will ignore new numeric fields but we still provide a compatibility shim that exposes affinity_score as a hint in v1 payloads. The migration script is guarded by a --dry-run flag and transactions; operators should run dry-run and validate a sample of entries before applying. We also added a small telemetry sampler cap to avoid over-sampling high-traffic variants during aggregation.

Security and provenance: the normalizer records a transform hash (SHA256) and signed provenance metadata when run in operator mode; the migration script supports optional KMS signing for enterprise Private installs (not enabled by default). Reviewed by security to ensure no secrets are written to logs.

Testing & CI: unit tests cover normalization permutations and schema validation; integration test runs a small synthetic telemetry dump through the aggregator and asserts seeded profiles are within expected signal ranges. CI initially had a flake in linting (line-length in docs) which was fixed; e2e job required an environment variable to be set in CI (REGISTRY_TEST_SAMPLER=1) and was rerun. Final CI status: pass.

Release notes / consumer-facing impact: this adds a new model intake tool and improves onboarding quality by reducing manual metadata cleanups and by pre-seeding calibration signals that improve automatic rollout decisions. No breaking API changes. Operators should plan a short migration window to run the backfill script. See the docs/ingest/normalizer.md for steps.

Lin Zhao: Request change - affinity_score should be rounded to 4 decimal places before storage to avoid precision drift. Also add a unit test that asserts deterministic normalization for key casing.
Aisha Patel: Reply - added rounding and deterministic key-ordering in normalizer; included new unit test (test_normalizer_deterministic).
Sofia Ruiz: Comment - migration should be idempotent; please ensure backfill skips already-populated rows.
Aisha Patel: Reply - backfill now checks sample_coverage IS NULL and includes a --force flag. Added transaction wrapper.
Marcus King: Approved - CI green and manual spot checks on a sampled dataset looked good.
Add intake normalizer and variant signal aggregator; introduce profile_schema_v2 with affinity_score and sample_coverage; migration/backfill provided; improves onboarding metadata quality and seeds calibration profiles to support safer rollouts.
Run registry/migrations/202511_backfill_sample_coverage.sql in a maintenance window. Start with --dry-run and validate results on a sample of 1k models. Ensure REGISTRY_TEST_SAMPLER env var set if running e2e locally.

Motivation: onboarding teams need machine-readable hints about which model variants are mutually compatible (quantization/kv-cache shape/sequence-length bounds) and an automated per-intake performance fingerprint so release notes can surface expected latency/cost deltas. This PR adds a compatibility-hints field to the model manifest, a perf_fingerprint snapshot recorded at intake time, and a small automation that synthesizes changelog blurb candidates based on delta between fingerprints. Changes include schema, ingestion hook, release-note generator, tests, and migration. Checklist: - [x] define compatibility-hints schema and docs - [x] ingest hints at model intake and persist in manifest store - [x] capture perf_fingerprint from profiler snapshot hook - [x] generate candidate release-note lines and severity tags - [x] add unit/integration tests and sample manifests - [x] migration element for existing manifests - [x] update onboarding docs and examples Rollout plan: roll out ingestion as a non-blocking annotation and surface hints in the registry UI; after 2 weeks flip a flag to enforce hint presence for new manifests. Rollback: remove flag and drop automated release-note drafts; compatible with prior manifest schema. Why unique: existing onboarding focuses on static metadata; this ties performance deltas to onboarding and makes changelogs actionable for SRE and Release Engineering. Links: linear/ENG-3241, support ticket SUP-447. No user-visible API changes to runtime; only registry intake and admin console surfaces are affected.
Add compatibility_hints field to model manifest schema with conservative typing and optional entries
Capture perf_fingerprint at intake using existing profiler hook and compress for storage
Introduce generate_diff_blurb automation that compares new fingerprint to baseline and suggests release-note lines with severity tags (minor/medium/major)
Migration script to add new columns and compact existing snapshots behind feature flag
Update onboarding docs and examples with recommended guidance and rollouts
Add unit/integration tests including transitive compatibility mapping
Manual QA: ingested 6 sample manifests (open-source and quantized variants), verified UI shows compatibility hints and release-note drafts; SRE ran a 1k-request perf sweep to ensure profiler hook is non-blocking. Automated tests added for reading/writing compressed fingerprints and delta calculation. Monitoring: added temporary alert on manifest write latency before and after rollout.
Risk: increased DB storage and potential write latency during high-throughput onboard spikes. Mitigations: compressed storage, non-blocking hook, feature-flagged full-snapshot. Rollback: drop UI feature flag and remove auto-draft generation; run migration reversal to remove added columns if required. Estimated rollback time: < 2 hours for UI flag flip, < 6 hours for DB migration revert depending on replication lag.
Added manifest annotations: compatibility_hints and perf_fingerprint. Registry will now surface suggested release-note blurbs describing expected perf/latency deltas on new model intake. Admins can opt-in to full snapshot recording via feature flag. (ENG-3241, SUP-447)
When reviewing new model rollouts, check the generated severity tag and sample blurb. If a 'major' perf delta is suggested, run the profiler sweep in staging and consider canary routing. The generator is a helper not an enforcement mechanism.
Jonah Kim: This looks promising. Can you expand tests to cover transitive variant compatibility (A compatible with B and B with C implies A with C)?
Author (Aisha): Good catch, added transitive mapping unit test and a comment explaining the conservative merge semantics.
Marcus Li: Concern: adding perf_fingerprint to every intake increases manifest size and DB churn. Can we store only compressed deltas?
Author (Aisha): Addressed by compressing the fingerprint and keeping an LZ4 column; migration script includes a compact serializer. Left full snapshot optional behind a feature flag for debugging.
Sofia Ortega: Docs are clear. Please add a short paragraph about how Release Engineers should interpret severity tags.
Author (Aisha): Added guidance and examples in docs/onboard/compatibility-guidelines.md. Ready for approval.
Marcus Li: Approved
Jonah Kim: Approved
Sofia Ortega: Approved
- Flip non-blocking flag to enforced after 2-week observation window - Add metric dashboard for perf_fingerprint delta distribution - Notify partners via #registry-release channel
Manifests without compatibility_hints remain valid. Ingest treats hints as advisory for now. Migration adds nullable columns and is reversible.
This PR aims to close the loop between onboarding metadata and release notes so downstream teams get actionable perf context at intake time. The approach favors conservative defaults and incremental rollout to minimize risk.

payload.body:
Motivation: onboarding metadata today relies on static heuristics and manual authoring for release notes. Teams requested compact, data-driven hints so that changelogs and compatibility notes reflect observed production usage rather than purely model architecture. This PR introduces a sampled, usage-driven model fingerprint and a compact release heuristics generator that seeds automated changelog drafts.

What this does (high level): adds a fingerprint extractor that consumes anonymized telemetry samples (seq length distribution, tokenization skew, median latency bucket, typical context window usage, and feature-affordance hits) and emits a compact JSON-friendly fingerprint. The release heuristics module maps fingerprints to short human-friendly impact tags (e.g., "short-context-optim", "latency-sensitive", "embedding-heavy") and a suggested one-line release blurb plus a short checklist for compatibility tests.

Why unique: unlike prior profile work which focused on offline performance sweeps, this ties onboarding metadata directly to observed usage patterns so rollout notes and profiling targets align with customer workloads. The heuristics are intentionally conservative (suggested tests, not prescriptive rollouts) to avoid blocking pipelines.

Design notes: fingerprinting runs as a streaming sampler in the onboarding pipeline: samples are rate-limited (configurable) and only include aggregate counts and histograms; there is no PII or raw text. Fingerprints are stored as a compact base64-stamped blob and a small top-level keyset used by the autodraft engine. The autodraft templates use a small ruleset (configurable YAML) with weighted heuristics to produce 1-2 suggested release bullets and 2-3 impact tags.

Files touched: onboarding pipeline (fingerprint generation), onboarding CLI flag to opt-in/out of telemetry sampling, changelog/autodraft generator, unit tests, and docs.

Testing and validation: added unit tests for the fingerprint extractor and deterministic rules for heuristics; ran an integration test with a sampled internal workload and compared suggested tags against a manual review (80%+ precision for top-1 tag in sample). CI run originally failed formatting on a helper; fixed and reran.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind `onboard.fingerprint.enabled` (false-by-default in prod). We'll enable for a small cohort of internal teams for two weeks, collect feedback, and then flip the flag for broader use.

Checklist: - [x] implement fingerprint extractor and serializer - [x] add CLI opt-in flag and safe defaults - [x] implement compact heuristics engine and template renderer - [x] add unit and integration tests - [x] update docs and quickstart section with examples and privacy notes

Related: references ENG-4212 (usage-driven onboarding) and SUP-1145 (support case requesting better changelog hints).
Jonah Park: Can we confirm the sampling rate default won't impact P95 latency of onboarding jobs? Please add a test that simulates heavy onboarding throughput.
Aditi Menon: Added a load-simulation integration test and set default sampling rate to 0.1% with backpressure; updated description to call out threshold checks.
Evan Liu: The heuristics ruleset seems reasonable. Suggest making the templating strings i18n-friendly — not required for MVP but file a follow-up.
Marina Costa: Approved after small nits on docs wording. Left a nit about expanding the privacy blurb.
Adds usage-driven fingerprinting for model onboarding and an autodraft release heuristics engine. Seeds automated changelog bullets and impact tags based on sampled production-like telemetry. Feature is opt-in and gated; privacy-first (no raw text captured).
payload.title: Introduce usage-driven fingerprinting and compact release heuristics for onboarding

payload.body:
Motivation: onboarding new model variants currently produces noisy changelogs and large release notes because sampling is workload-agnostic and random seeds vary across runs. This PR adds an adaptive, budget-aware onboarding sampler plus a deterministic changelog compactor that groups sample deltas into coherent micro-changes. Goals: 1) reduce churn in release notes for small perf/noise deltas, 2) ensure sampled probes are representative of declared workload tiers, 3) produce deterministic, small-size changelog fragments suitable for auto-release briefs. High level design: the sampler uses workload tags from manifest (production|latency-sensitive|cost-sensitive) to weight probe selection and enforces a configurable token/compute budget per intake; a deterministic seeding layer hashes model metadata+manifest+run-id to produce repeatable sample seeds across CI and on-demand replays; the compactor applies delta-clustering heuristics on evaluation traces (latency, p50/p95, token-efficiency, quality score) to collapse semantically-equivalent minor changes into a single micro-entry and attach a confidence score. Backwards compatibility: sampler falls back to legacy uniform sampling when workload tags absent; changelog compactor annotates rather than removes context so manual reviewers can expand entries. Checklist: - [x] sampler algorithm and config (sampling_policy.rs, sampler.py) - [x] deterministic seed function and cross-language tests - [x] compactor logic and summarizer - [x] unit tests for sampler and compactor - [x] integration test with onboarding pipeline (CI job onboard-e2e) - [x] docs update in docs/onboarding/README.md - [x] Linear tickets linked. Impact: reduces typical generated changelog size by ~45% in internal benchmark and reduces noisy rerolls observed in automated rollouts. Rollout plan: feature-flagged via ONBOARD_ADAPTIVE_SAMPLER and gradual enable in staging->canary->main. See release_notes for customer-facing blurb.
feat(sampler): add workload-conditioned sampler and budget enforcement | feat(seed): deterministic seed derivation from manifest+run | feat(compactor): add delta-clustering and micro-entry serializer | test: add unit/integration tests and golden fixtures | docs: onboarding sampler usage and config examples | ci: add onboard-e2e pipeline job
Ethan Zhao: Suggest making the default token budget conservative (suggest 10k tokens) and add a safety cap; Author reply: lowered default to 8k and added MAX_BUDGET env var with tests.
Rhea Gupta: Can the deterministic seed include toolchain hash to avoid cross-language drift?; Author reply: included a toolchain_version field in the seed input and added cross-language golden seeds in tests.
Oliver Kim: Compactor heuristics look good but we should surface the clustered metric breakdown to the console; Author reply: added per-cluster metrics (count, mean delta, confidence) to observability and example dashboard snippet in docs.
Internal benchmark on 50 candidate variants: mean changelog size reduced 45% (median 48%); false-collapse rate estimated 1.8% on heldout evaluation; sampling budget reduced compute cost by ~22% for small-intake jobs.
Feature: Adaptive onboarding sampler and deterministic changelog compactor. Summary: Onboarded models will produce smaller, more stable changelogs and more representative probe sets by default. Rolling out behind feature flag. Migration: none required. Notes: to opt-out set ONBOARD_ADAPTIVE_SAMPLER=false.
This PR was driven by ENG-4123 intake stability task after multiple onboarding rerolls during the March benchmarking window. Canaries showed stable rollouts with feature enabled.
payload.title: Introduce adaptive onboarding sampler and deterministic changelog compactor

payload.body:
Summary: Add an ambient metadata inference pass to the onboarding pipeline and a compact 'release fragment' writer that emits small, stable changelog snippets for model releases. Motivation: curation and release authors currently manually create dense release notes when onboarding new model versions. For high-volume onboarding (hundreds of model variants per quarter) this creates reviewer fatigue and inconsistent fragment quality. The new components provide a lightweight inference layer that suggests hierarchical metadata (domain, task, inferred latency class, tokenization notes) and writes compact release fragments that downstream tools can assemble into full changelogs or short release blurbs for console UI.

What this changes: single continuous description below includes implementation notes, checklist, commit summary, changed areas, and review convo.

Design/behavior: - Ambient metadata inference: a two-stage heuristic + ML-backed scorer that runs as a post-upload hook. Stage 1: deterministic heuristics extract architecture hints (decoder/encoder-decoder, likely tokenizer type via name), weight-decay of layer counts, and tokenization marker heuristics. Stage 2: a small classifier (packed as a stable artifact under model-registry/tools/ambient-infer/) scores likely domain(s) and latency buckets given profiler samples. Inference runs with conservative defaults and is opt-out via model manifest flag "onboard.ambient_infer: false". - Release fragment writer: emits compact JSONL per-model-version containing: title, one-line blurb, key changes (bullet list up to 3), performance anchors (p50/p95 baseline), and metadata tags. Fragments are intentionally terse to support: console micro-blurbs, changelog rollups, and release-email drafters. Writer supports templates and produces deterministic output (seeded) so diffs are reviewer-friendly.

Checklist: - [x] Implement ambient inference module and unit tests - [x] Add safe opt-out flag and documentation section - [x] Implement compact release fragment writer and writer unit tests - [x] Integrate fragment writer as optional onboarding pipeline step - [x] Add e2e test that validates fragment output for two sample models - [x] Add CI linting and stable artifact packaging - [x] Add ops doc for enabling in Private deployments

Commits (high level): - feat(onboard): add ambient inference module and classifier artifact (6 commits) - feat(release-frag): compact release-fragment writer and template engine (3 commits) - test: e2e onboarding test harness for fragments (2 commits) - docs: onboarding.md additions and ops-runbook (1 commit) - ci: bump packaging job to publish ambient-infer artifact (1 commit)

Files/areas changed (high level): - model-registry/onboard/ambient_infer.py: core inference pass and heuristics - model-registry/tools/ambient_infer/classifier.pkl: bundled classifier artifact (binary checksum referenced in code) - model-registry/onboard/fragment_writer.py: release fragment generation and templating - model-registry/tests/test_ambient_infer.py: unit tests and fixtures - model-registry/tests/test_fragment_writer_e2e.py: e2e test that runs upload->fragment - docs/onboarding.md: new section "Ambient metadata inference" - docs/ops/private-deployments.md: opt-in instructions and artifact sync - ci/publish-artifacts.yaml: package artifact publishing step - examples/onboard-examples/mini-locale-manifest.yaml: example manifest showing opt-out flag

Design decisions and constraints: - Classifier artifact is intentionally small and frozen; we avoid rolling model training in this PR. Future work will add supervised retraining. - Conservative defaults: inferred tags are suggestions and flagged as "inferred:true" in the manifest so reviewers can explicitly accept or override. - Deterministic writer: fragment output is seeded using model version and manifest hash so reviewers see stable diffs across CI runs. - Privacy: ambient inference only uses uploaded manifest metadata and profiler summaries; no raw customer payloads are sent to external services. Private deployments keep classifier as a local artifact.

Review conversation (selected): - Evan Chen (reviewer): "High-level: this is a great UX win. Two asks: 1) can we make the classifier path fully optional in CI (skip heavy scoring on small PRs)? 2) document how the inferred latency buckets map to the runtime's cost model (for SRE)." - Sofia (author): "@Evan added a lightweight gate: CI respects ONBOARD_LIGHT=1 to skip classifier scoring (see ci/publish-artifacts.yaml). Latency-to-cost mapping added to docs/ops/private-deployments.md with a link to the runtime cost buckets."

- Priya Kapoor (reviewer): "Minor: fragment writer needs to fail gracefully when perf anchors are missing (e.g., perf not available for brand-new variants). Add a fallback to 'unknown' and reduce anchors to p50 only." - Sofia: "Addressed: fragment_writer now emits p50 and omits p95 when not present; tests updated."

- Jules Park (reviewer): "Security check: classifier artifact should be checksummed and signature-verified before loading in Private. Also please add a short note to the release blurb about opt-out compliance for regulated customers." - Sofia: "Added checksum verification and ops note; Private deploys can point to a local artifact repo."

CI and testing: - Unit tests: 32 tests added, coverage for new modules ~86% - E2E: onboarding example runs in the test harness producing stable fragment JSONL - CI: build matrix ran on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, all checks passed; artifact publish job was manually re-run once due to transient network failure and then passed.

Manual QA notes: - Tested with three sample models: 'mistral-lite-v1', 'rwkv-small-8k', and a private GPT-style pointer model. Fragments were concise and reviewer-editable. - Observed that deterministic seeding eliminated spurious diffs between CI runs in 90% of sampled runs.

Backward compatibility and migration: - No breaking changes to existing manifests; new fields are optional. - Default behavior is no-op unless onboarding pipeline toggles the fragment writer. - For teams that enable the automated path, we recommend a 2-week canary where inferred tags are only suggestions (not auto-accepted).

Release notes (for changelog generation): - Adds ambient metadata inference to onboarding pipeline (opt-out flag available) - Adds compact, deterministic release-fragment writer for model versions - Includes ops notes for Private deployments and artifact verification

Follow-ups and TODOs post-merge: - ENG-5092: schedule telemetry to measure reviewer override rate for inferred tags - ENG-5210: add supervised retraining pipeline for classifier with opt-in data collection - UX: wire fragment snippets into the Console model release micro-blurb UI - infra: add a signed artifact distribution endpoint for Private customers

Merge: Squash-merged into main. Merge commit: "squash: ambient metadata inference + release fragment writer".

Context: onboarding has historically recorded model metadata but lacked an auditable, time-ordered provenance ledger and an automated stability witness to detect non-deterministic profiling regressions during onboarding. This PR introduces a lightweight provenance ledger (append-only, signed entries) and a "stability witness" service that signs and snapshots critical profiling outputs to make changelogs and release notes more reliable and automatable. Motivation: enable deterministic changelog generation, support automated rollback criteria for model variants, and provide an auditable trail for compliance reviews. What changed (summary): 1) provenance ledger: new DB table + append-only API (model_registry/ledger.py, migrations/20251126_add_provenance_ledger.sql). Entries capture: model_id, onboard_run_id, profile_hash, inputs_manifest, signer_key_id, signature, and release_anchor. 2) stability witness: new onboarding step that computes stability signatures from repeated profiling runs and stores signed deltas (onboarding/witness.py, cli/onboard-witness.py). 3) release annotator: a helper that consumes ledger entries to produce condensed changelog snippets used by release tooling (scripts/release-annotator.py). 4) CLI and API: expose `redwood-registry onboard --witness` flag and an authenticated ledger write endpoint with RBAC checks. 5) docs: onboarding/provenance.md and updated model-profiles.md describing semantics and recommended workflows. 6) tests: deterministic integration tests and signing mocks (tests/test_witness.py, tests/test_ledger.py). Migration and rollout plan: DB migration adds an append-only table with a trigger that prevents updates/deletes; migration is backward compatible. Default behavior is opt-in via feature flag `onboard_witness_v1`; we enable the flag for nightly onboarding runs for two weeks before global enablement. Rollback: if ledger writes cause issues, feature flag can be toggled off and ledger writes will be skipped; migrations are additive and reversible with a data-preserving cleanup job. Security and compliance: signatures use existing KMS integration (KMS key id stored in signer_key_id); ledger entries are encrypted at rest by default. Testing and validation: unit tests + end-to-end in benchmark-lab container running a small GPU-based profile; a deliberate noisy-run test ensures witness detects non-determinism and surfaces it to the UI. Related work: ties to ENG-2983 (automated changelog assembler) and ENG-3010 (onboard stability SLA). Checklist: - [x] API + CLI implemented - [x] DB migration added and tested in local docker-compose - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Docs updated and small HOWTO included - [x] Feature flag gating + rollout plan - [x] End-to-end smoke test in benchmark-lab Notes: the description field contains all high-level context for release engineering; implementation details are intentionally concise here and available in the code comments and docs files included in the PR.
Marco Silva: Can we avoid writing the full inputs_manifest into the ledger to prevent huge rows? Suggested storing a content-addressed blob reference instead.
Priya Desai: Good catch — switched to storing S3 object key and content hash; added garbage-collection note in docs.
Aisha Khan: Please add an integration test that simulates a non-deterministic GPU run so we can assert the witness flags instability.
Priya Desai: Added tests/test_witness.py that runs the profiling harness twice with a jitter and asserts delta > threshold triggers flag.
Daniel Park: LGTM after minor nits (type hints + one log level change).
Aisha Khan: Approved — feature flagged and covered by CI smoke job.
Add a provenance ledger and stability witness for model onboarding. This enables auditable onboarding trails, deterministic changelog snippets based on signed profile deltas, and opt-in safety gating for model variant rollouts. Feature is behind feature flag `onboard_witness_v1` and will be gradually enabled.
Enable feature flag in staging for two weeks; monitor ledger write latency and KMS call rates. If high errors observed, disable `onboard_witness_v1` and investigate KMS region throttling. Wallet of signatures is rotated via existing KMS rotation job.
