payload.body:
Summary: This PR fixes a class of failures where grammar/regex-based constrained decoders produced invalid or truncated structured output for inputs containing multi-codepoint Unicode sequences (emoji, combined marks) due to a token-gap mismatch between the tokenizer and the constraint backends. The change introduces a boundary-aware token mapping layer in the constraint muxer and a conservative fallback to byte-level regex matching when tokenization ambiguities would otherwise break streaming/tool-call framing.

Motivation and context: In production we've seen intermittent failures when customers submit prompts with emoji or complex combining characters. Those inputs sometimes produced malformed structured outputs (missing closing tags, tool-call payload split across streaming frames) because the constraint engine assumed token boundaries that the tokenizer split differently, especially for certain BPE and byte-level encodings. This manifested as downstream JSON parsing errors or tool invocation failures, and was surfaced by ENG-2981 and a recent incident (linked in the Linear ticket).

What this PR does (high level): 1) Adds a Unicode-aware boundary resolver that maps character/grapheme cluster boundaries to token index ranges and exposes a confidence score for ambiguous splits. 2) Updates the constraint muxer to use boundary anchors when applying CFG/grammar and regex constraints so that constraints align with grapheme clusters instead of naive byte offsets. 3) Implements a safe fallback: when the boundary confidence is low (e.g., ambiguous tokenizer split on combining marks), the muxer falls back to a byte-level regex mode that preserves streaming framing for tool/function calls and avoids mid-token split tool-call frames. 4) Stabilizes streaming by ensuring streaming frames do not cut tool-call payloads; we now buffer and reframe partial tokens until a safe boundary is reached. 5) Adds regression test coverage and a micro-benchmark demonstrating the perf delta for worst-case Unicode inputs and the improvement in failure-rate.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for boundary resolver and muxer logic
- [x] Integration tests for streaming tool calls with Unicode prompts
- [x] Micro-benchmark and perf numbers added
- [x] Docs note describing tokenizer-edgecase behaviour and recommended prompt patterns
- [x] QA run in staging (no regressions observed)

Commits (summary):
- 7f3a2b0: introduce boundary_resolver module with grapheme cluster to token mapping and confidence scoring
- 9d12c1f: integrate boundary anchors into constraint_muxer and update CFG/regex application codepaths
- b8a4e2d: implement byte-level regex fallback and streaming reframing for tool calls
- c0f4a5b: tests + fixtures for emoji/combining marks and updated test harness
- d41f6e3: docs + release notes + small lint and CI fixes

Changed areas/files (high level):
- src/constraints/constraint_muxer.py: add boundary-aware matching, fallback mode, and streaming reframing logic
- src/tokenizer/boundary_resolver.cpp and src/tokenizer/boundary_resolver.h: grapheme cluster detection and token index mapping
- src/streaming/stream_framer.rs: buffer/reframe logic to avoid splitting tool-call payloads mid-token
- tests/constraints/test_unicode_boundaries.py: regression tests and fuzz inputs
- tests/streaming/test_tool_call_framing.py: integration tests simulating chunked streaming over sockets
- docs/api/structured_output.md: note on tokenizer edge cases and how muxer handles ambiguous boundaries
- benchmarks/unicode_token_gap/README.md and harness: micro-benchmarks and results

Performance and safety notes:
- The boundary resolver computes grapheme cluster boundaries using ICU algorithms; to avoid a large runtime regression we cache recent mappings per-request and only run the full grapheme scan when a prompt contains multi-codepoint sequences. Benchmarked on p4d.24xlarge: worst-case overhead ~3-7% p99 lat for pathological inputs; average impact <1% for normal traffic.
- The byte-level regex fallback is more conservative and slightly more permissive; it is only used when the confidence heuristic indicates potential split ambiguity.

Tests and QA:
- Added deterministic unit tests covering sequences: emoji with skin-tone modifiers, base + combining marks, ZWJ sequences, and rare Unicode normalization forms.
- Added an integration test that streams a tool call split across many small chunks to validate reframing logic and verify no mid-token tool-call payload is emitted.
- Ran the new tests against mainline models (gpt-family-sim) and verified no difference in outputs for ascii-only prompts.

Review conversation (high level excerpts):
- Carlos Rivera (review): "Good catch on the grapheme clusters. Two asks: tighten the confidence heuristic threshold and add a short comment explaining why we prefer byte-fallback rather than rewriting tokenizer behavior."
- Maya Chen (author): "Lowered threshold to 0.6 per perf discussion; added explanation in boundary_resolver.h and a short section in docs explaining tradeoffs."
- Sasha Ivanov (review): "Streaming reframer looks sane; can we add a unit test that simulates a partial tool-call payload and ensures the muxer delays emission until safe boundary?"
- Maya Chen: "Added tests/streaming/test_tool_call_framing.py which does exactly that."
- Elena Park (approval): "Tests look comprehensive, benchmarks acceptable, approving."

CI summary:
- Build matrix: linux/macos, python tests, rust streaming runner, C++ boundary module compiled under both clang and gcc
- Initial CI run had a flaky fuzz test failure; rerun passed. All gates green on merge date.

Merge details:
- Merge method: squash and merge
- Merge commit body: consolidated commits and a short changelog entry.

Related work:
- Follow-on: ENG-3140 will evaluate moving parts of the boundary resolver into a shared tokenizer plugin to avoid repetition across runtimes (tracked as a follow-up).
- This PR was coordinated with SDK teams to ensure no changes required in SDK framing (redwood-sdk-python/TS no-op changes).

Why this is safe for backport:
- No public API changes; behavior is strictly safer (fewer malformed outputs).

Backport candidates: release/1.8.x if customers on that branch reported Unicode failures.

Notes for release notes and customer comms:
- User-visible: better handling of emoji and combined characters in structured outputs and fewer streaming tool-call failures for such prompts. No action required from customers. 
Fix: Constraint muxer tokenization alignment; improved streaming stability for tool/function call frames; no user-facing API changes.
payload.title: Fix unicode token-gap handling in constraint muxer and stabilize streaming for tool calls

Motivation: reduce manual effort and human error when promoting onboarded models by automatically capturing a compact performance fingerprint, requiring an approver signoff for stability regressions, and bundling a concise release capsule for downstream consumers. This PR introduces: 1) a deterministic performance fingerprint computed from a trimmed set of latency/throughput/quality metrics and the serialized profile hash; 2) a signoff workflow that gates model promotion when fingerprint drift exceeds thresholds, integrating with the existing intake review queue; 3) a release capsule generator that composes a one-page JSON brief (human-readable blurb, delta summary, notable metric diffs, and suggested rollout cadence) and attaches it to model version releases; 4) CI hooks and a lightweight reviewer UI flag to record signoff comments and rationale. The description below summarizes changes, test coverage, and rollout plan. Checklist: [x] compute fingerprint algorithm and add unit tests, [x] expose fingerprint and drift score in intake API, [x] signoff workflow + reviewer comments capture, [x] release capsule builder + brief template, [x] CI lint/build/test passes on rerun, [x] migration that backfills fingerprints for recent onboarded models (30-day window) (migration included). Backwards compatibility: the fingerprint is additive metadata; promotion flows fall back to previous behavior when the feature flag is disabled. Rollout: feature-flagged rollout to staging for two weeks, followed by gradual enable on 25%, 50%, 100% of intake traffic. Related work: follows ENG-2187 (perf inference stability) and PM-342 (release brief UX).

Motivation: onboarding engineers often supply dense model metadata but downstream consumers (release notes, product pages, changelogs) need concise, audience-tailored summaries. This PR adds two complementary pieces: 1) a small, extensible 'affordance hints' field in the model metadata schema to capture human-friendly bullets about model behavior/intent; 2) a release-teaser generator that synthesizes one-line and short paragraph blurbs for release notes and changelogs from the model profile + affordance hints.

Scope and goals: keep the schema additive and backward-compatible, provide a lightweight CLI/CI hook to emit teaser drafts, and add a quality check that prevents 'empty' teasers for releases. This is not a full natural language rewrite engine — teasers are templated with optional heuristic rewriting for clarity. The generator supports two flavors: engineer (performance/cost/compatibility bullets) and product (high-level capability blurb).

What changed: added schema bump v2.3 with optional 'affordance_hints' array; implemented registry/hooks/release_teaser/generator.py with heuristic templates and short heuristics to collapse noisy profile stats; wired a CLI subcommand (cli/onboard_teaser.py) that can be invoked from onboarding pipelines; added CI integration (registry/ci/teaser_integration.yml) that runs the teaser generator against a sample onboarding bundle and fails if both teaser variants are missing or flagged as low-quality; tests added (registry/tests/test_teaser.py) and docs (docs/release-teaser.md).

Checklist: [x] schema add is additive and feature-flag guarded; [x] unit tests for template permutations; [x] CI hook added and smoke-tested; [x] performance profile impacts audited — teaser generation is CPU-only and <200ms per model on CI sample.

Backward compatibility: optional field only; registry will ignore affordance_hints when consuming older profiles. Migration path: onboard CLI will seed affordance_hints from existing profile notes when present.

Notes for reviewers: look at generator heuristics (generator.py) and the small whitelist for numeric summaries (we avoid raw token counts unless the profile indicates deviation from baseline). Also validate the release-teaser wording for non-technical audiences in docs/release-teaser.md.
Jonah Kim (2026-02-15): Requested small changes to the numeric summarization rules — prefer relative deltas (p99 latency vs baseline) instead of raw token/runtime counts. Also asked to add a short circuit for models with missing performance profiles.
Ava Martinez (2026-02-15): Reply: added relative-delta heuristics in generator.py and a missing-profile fallback that emits "profile unavailable" teaser with a 'needs-profile' tag for reviewers.
Marco Alvarez (2026-02-16): Suggested adding a safety list to prevent claims like "state-of-the-art" unless explicitly flagged by model curation. I added a lightweight denylist and documented it in release-teaser.md.
Priya Singh (2026-02-18): Approved after CI pass and minor doc edits. Left an approval comment and asked the release team to decide whether product blurbs should be surfaced in the public changelog.
Ava Martinez (2026-02-18): Noted that product blurbs default to internal changelog only and require explicit opt-in for public exposure.
Add optional 'affordance_hints' in model metadata (schema v2.3) to surface concise, human-friendly bullets about model behavior and intended use-cases.
Add release-teaser generator: produces short, audience-targeted blurbs for changelogs and onboarding summaries (engineer/product variants).
CI hook: teaser_integration workflow validates that onboarding bundles emit at least one non-empty teaser; prevents silent onboarding without release notes.

Motivation: onboarding models into the registry has grown ad-hoc metadata variations (missing quantization information, inconsistent perf profile formats) which blocks reliable automation (serving rollout, cost estimation, changelog generation). This PR introduces a small, extensible metadata validator (server-side and CLI) and a GitHub Action that synthesizes release notes for model profile changes so that model owners and release managers get an auditable changelog automatically.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a JSON Schema-based validator for model registry entries and exposes it as registry/validator.py and a CLI command rmdctl validate that runs local checks. 2) Adds a server-side validation hook used by the ingestion API to reject badly-formed metadata with clear error codes. 3) Introduces a GitHub Action (hooks/github/release-notes-action.yml) that computes a human-friendly release note when model metadata or performance profiles change (creates a CHANGES/MODELS.md entry). 4) Migration script for legacy entries that normalizes the perf_profile and quantization fields. 5) Tests and docs: unit + integration tests + onboarding docs update.

Checklist: - [x] validator implementation + CLI - [x] server-side hook integration - [x] release-notes GH Action and template - [x] migration for legacy entries - [x] unit/integration tests - [x] docs and example PR template

Backward compatibility and rollout: the API will enable validation by default for new model submissions. Existing models in the registry are migrated with a background job using migrations/2025-01-12-normalize-legacy-metadata.py; the migration is idempotent and logs changes to audit tables. The GH Action is opt-in via a repository-level config: .github/model-release-config.yml. We will enable the action for the main repo after this PR and monitor for two weeks before flipping the config to mandatory.

Usage examples: run `rmdctl validate path/to/model.json` locally to see a list of schema errors; a CI step is recommended for PRs that add or change models. The generated CHANGES/MODELS.md entries follow the template in docs/model-onboarding.md and include a short summary, performance delta table, and a link to perf artifacts in the benchmark-lab bucket.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the validator schema (registry/schema/model_v2.json) and the release-note diff algorithm (hooks/release_note_builder.py). The diff algorithm is intentionally conservative: it reports deltas only when a perf profile changes by >2% for top-level latency or throughput metrics to avoid noise in release notes.
Samir Patel: Can we make the perf profile validator accept multiple metric names (p50/p95/p99) but require at least one? Also request clearer error codes for CI to parse.
Maya Alvarez (author): Added required_metrics array and standardized error codes (REGVAL_001..). Updated tests to assert error code values.
Lena Cho: The GH Action should not write to CHANGES/MODELS.md directly on forked PRs. Can we make it post the candidate note as a comment instead?
Maya Alvarez: Adjusted action: on forked PRs we post a draft comment and attach artifacts; for trusted branches we write the file and open a PR. Added config flag allow_write_changelog.
Samir Patel: Integration test flaked once (timeout in test_release_notes). Please add a backoff/retry for S3 artifact fetch.
Maya Alvarez: Added exponential backoff and increased test timeout; CI green on rerun.
Added model metadata validator and release-notes automation: - New CLI command `rmdctl validate` for pre-PR checks - Server-side validation rejects malformed model metadata with structured error codes - GitHub Action that synthesizes CHANGES/MODELS.md entries for model/profile changes (opt-in via .github/model-release-config.yml) - Background migration to normalize legacy metadata - Docs: expanded model onboarding guide and PR template
When enabling the action repo-wide, set allow_write_changelog to false initially and monitor the CHANGES/MODELS.md PRs. The migration is idempotent but should be run with read-only dry-run first (migrations/2025-01-12-normalize-legacy-metadata.py --dry-run). Audit logs are written to registry.audit_model_changes.
If the validator blocks critical submissions, flip ingestion.validate=false in the registry config to disable server-side enforcement, then run a targeted migration to normalize problematic models. GH Action can be disabled by removing .github/model-release-config.yml.
Enable GH Action in staging after deploying the validator to ingestion-api; run migration in background and monitor audit table; schedule a 2-week review to decide on mandatory enforcement.
This change is intentionally conservative: the release-note generator thresholds are tunable via .github/model-release-config.yml to avoid noisy changelogs. The validator schema is extensible for future perf metrics (memory, fp16 stability flags).

Motivation: Different inference hardware (a100, h100, triton-hosted tensorrt, amd-gpu) show materially different optimal kernel/quantization choices and recommended batch sizing. Customers and model owners currently store a single 'performance profile' per model which conflates these hardware differences and makes changelogs noisy when we update heuristics. This PR introduces a lightweight 'hardware_affinity' field in the onboarding metadata schema, a migration to split existing profiles into microprofiles keyed by affinity, and a sharded changelog generator that emits per-affinity release notes to make rollouts and triage clearer.

What I changed: 1) schema/registry/model.yaml: add optional hardware_affinity map (recommended keys: cpu, a100, h100, trt, amd). The map contains profile hints (quantize: int8/float16, kernels: [fused_attn, flash_attn], batch_hint, kv_cache_opt). 2) onboard/migrations/20251112_split_profiles_by_affinity.py: migration that converts legacy single-profile models into per-affinity microprofiles using heuristics (fallback strategy != breaking). 3) tools/changelog/shard_by_affinity.py: new generator that reads release deltas and writes separate changelog fragments per affinity, plus an aggregate summary. 4) tests/test_affinity_profile.py: unit tests for schema validation and migration. 5) docs/onboarding/hardware-affinity.md: docs for model owners and SRE explaining how to write affinity-aware profiles and interpret per-affinity changelogs. 6) examples/sample-onboard-affinity.json: example metadata demonstrating multi-affinity entries.

Checklist: - [x] Schema addition with open/optional field and backwards-compatible defaults - [x] Migration script with dry-run mode and a safety flag --apply-once - [x] Unit tests covering edge cases (missing affinity, unknown hardware) - [x] Changelog generator integrated with existing release pipeline (writes fragments to artifacts/) - [x] Docs and example metadata - [ ] E2E profiling job to validate suggested kernels (tracked in follow-up ENG-3492)

Compatibility and migration notes: The hardware_affinity field is optional. When absent, runtime will consult the legacy profile (unchanged). Migration attempts to create best-effort microprofiles but leaves a single 'legacy' profile for models where heuristics can't confidently split. The migration includes flags to run in dry mode and an idempotent marker so it can be rolled out safely on production registries.

Performance impact: No runtime behavior change unless customers opt-in to affinity-specific routing or we enable affinity-aware defaults. The sharded changelog reduces human noise for release engineers and should speed triage when regressions are reported only on specific hardware.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge schema + migration and ship as behind-feature-flag for the console. 2) Run migration in dry mode across staging and gather sample microprofiles (2 weeks). 3) Enable migration --apply-once for low-risk namespaces, run validation jobs. 4) Switch release pipeline to include per-affinity fragments and update release notes workflow docs.

Related work: ENG-3150 (affinity routing prototype), ENG-3293 (changelog pipeline refactor).
Marcus Liu: Looks good overall. Two questions: 1) How do we prefer to represent unknown hardware? (suggest 'other' key). 2) Can we keep quantize as a soft suggestion vs enforced value?
Elena Park: Responded - we'll add 'other' and treat quantize as advisory (runtime will still validate compat). Added an explicit note in docs.
Priya Nair: Please add a migration idempotency marker and tests for repeat runs.
Elena Park: Added --marker-file and unit tests covering repeated migration runs.

Motivation: Model performance profiles currently capture latency and throughput but lack explicit cost buckets which makes it hard to predict unit economics for variant rollouts. This PR introduces a cost_bucket field on performance profiles and a changelog scorer that annotates release notes with estimated cost/latency impact and priority. Summary of changes: 1) schema/model: add cost_bucket enum (low|medium|high) and cost_estimate_usd_per_1k_tokens string, plus migration script to add default buckets for existing profiles. 2) API: add optional cost_bucket and cost_estimate fields to the profile upload endpoint; validation and backwards-compatible defaulting to 'medium' when absent. 3) Backfill: job and script to infer buckets from historic telemetry, with confidence scores persisted to profile.metadata.cost_inference. 4) Changelog scorer: service that runs on release drafts to produce a single-line score and a short blurb used in release notes; scoring considers delta in average tokens, batch efficiency, quantization flags and inferred cost buckets. 5) UI: compact badge and tooltip on the model page showing cost bucket and scorer blurb; feature-flagged behind 'cost-profiles-ui'. 6) Tests: unit tests for migration, API validation, scorer heuristics and end-to-end integration tests for backfill. Commits: - add schema change and migration script - wire cost fields into profile ingestion API - implement telemetry-driven backfill and confidence store - implement changelog scorer service and lightweight scorer API - add UI badge and integration tests - docs: add developer-facing doc with scoring rules and examples Files changed (high level): schema/profile.proto updated, services/profile/ingest.go, tools/backfill/infer_cost_bucket.py, services/changelog/scorer/service.py, ui/model_page/badge.tsx, docs/dev/cost-profiles.md, tests/{profile_migration_test.go, scorer_test.py, e2e_cost_profile.test.ts} Review thread: Miguel: "How do we avoid noisy changes for older profiles with sparse telemetry?" Author: "Backfill writes inferred bucket with a confidence tag and we surface low-confidence as 'inferred (low confidence)' in UI; API retains original behavior unless explicit cost_bucket provided." Priya: "Sanity-check on scorer — can we include tokenization differences across runtimes?" Author: "Scorer normalizes by model family and uses seq-length distributions from recent telemetry; added a test vector to cover this." Liam: "Need a rollback plan if backfill behaves poorly." Author: "Backfill is staged and feature-flagged; we also include a revertable DB migration and a compensating job to clear inferred fields." CI summary: all checks passed on latest run including unit, integration, linter and contract tests; codecov decreased by 0.2% due to new scorer service but within allowed threshold. Rollout & merge: feature-flagged rollout; migration runs in background and is reversible; merged via squash on 2024-05-29 after approvals from reviewers. Notes for release: enable 'cost-profiles-ui' behind a gradual rollout; run backfill on non-peak hours and monitor delta signals and API error rates for 48 hours. Links: Linear ENG-6732 for work tracking, docs at docs/dev/cost-profiles.md, brief on scoring heuristics included in PR.
Added cost_bucketed performance profiles, changelog impact scorer, schema migration and backfill; no breaking changes to API; rollout: gradual, feature-flagged.

Motivation: We have overlapping compatibility entries across model variants that complicate release note generation and rollout heuristics. This PR introduces a compatibility rollup step that composes pairwise compat entries into a compact matrix and a lightweight metadata adapter that normalizes incoming onboard payloads (provider, quantization tags, variant hints) so downstream profile generation and changelog seeds are stable.

What this PR does: - Adds a compat-rollup module that deduplicates and collapses pairwise compat rules into a hierarchical matrix keyed by model family/version. - Adds metadata-adapter layer which runs as a normalization pass during onboarding and when re-ingesting legacy manifests. - Adds a changelog-seed backfill migration that synthesizes short human-friendly blurbs for recent onboardings so release assembler has content to surface. - Adds unit + integration tests for rollup correctness and performance regression guard.

Checklist: - [x] compat-rollup algorithm implemented and unit-tested - [x] metadata adapter schema + validator - [x] changelog seed migration + idempotency guard - [x] e2e test with release-assembler (mocked) - [x] perf microbenchmark against registry index

Migration notes: The backfill is non-destructive: it writes changelog seeds to the registry only when no seed exists. The migration is safe to run repeatedly. We added a short TTL for temporary debug flags and a dry-run mode for the migration to inspect candidate seeds. Operators should run the dry-run once, inspect output, then run the actual migration during a low-traffic window.

Testing: Unit tests cover edgecases (circular compat rules, missing variant metadata). Integration test simulates onboard -> rollup -> release-assembler flow and asserts stable release_notes output. Local perf runs show ~12% reduction in profile lookup latency for heavy variant graphs (N=200 variants).

Related: ENG-4981 contains design notes on the rollup heuristics, SUP-1123 is the support ticket that prompted standardized metadata for third-party picks.

If anything goes wrong: rollback is a two-step process: 1) disable the migration flag to stop backfills; 2) deploy a revert that bypasses the rollup and falls back to the previous pairwise compat API.
Add compat-map rollup (aggregates pairwise compatibility into release-ready matrix)
Introduce onboarding metadata adapter to normalize provider and variant metadata for downstream tooling
Backfill changelog seeds for 48 recent model onboardings (non-destructive migration)
Performance: ~12% faster profile lookup in registry index during release assembly

Samir Patel: Added docs/ops/runbackfill.md and sample output; addressed in latest commit.
Diego Martinez: Algorithm looks good. We should ensure the rollup maintains transitive closure invariants; add a test for chained constraints.
Samir Patel: Added test for chained constraints and clarified invariant in docs.
Priya Nambiar: LGT M with minor nits on logging level and a suggestion to make the migration idempotency check optimistic.

Context: onboarding teams frequently provide only a single canonical performance profile and a sparse README. For real workloads we observed wide variance in latency/cost per token across request patterns (short chat vs. long generation vs. embeddings sampling). This PR adds two complementary features: (1) workload-aware onboard hints — a compact artifact produced during model intake that recommends 2–4 profile presets (latency-first, cost-first, balanced, embed-optimized) plus batch/caching defaults derived from sampled traces; and (2) changelog microdiffs — a small structured summary that surfaces the subset of release-note-relevant profile changes (kernel choices, quantization presets, sample-rate assumptions, KV-cache compatibility) so release notes can be concise and actionable. Motivation: reduce time-to-production for new models, lower first-week cost surprises, and enable concise automated release notes for platform and customer-facing change feeds. Implementation: (a) intake recorder: lightweight trace sampler runs with a configured TTL (default 10k requests or 6h) inside onboarding harness; traces are normalized to workload categories and summarized via quantiles. (b) hint generator: rule-based + small heuristic scorer that maps trace signatures to suggested profile presets and flags risky knobs (e.g., beam size > 1, mixed-precision fallbacks). The hints are emitted as a compact YAML artifact alongside the model manifest. (c) microdiff generator: when a new profile or manifest is uploaded, we compute a semantic diff limited to 12 canonical keys (hardware affinity, quantization, kernel family, sequence-length buckets, batching defaults, kv-cache policy, prefills, seed prompts) and render both a short natural-language blurb and a machine-consumable microdiff JSON (compact). (d) UX surface: console preview and a CLI flag --preview-hints for onboarding engineers to inspect suggestions. Testing and validation: unit tests for sampler normalization, integration tests on 6 representative models (small to LLM scale) comparing suggested presets vs. historical best-effort baselines, and a canary rollout to the staging index that records cost delta estimates. Backwards compatibility: microdiffs are additive and produced only when manifest schema v2+ is used; legacy manifests are left unchanged. Rollout plan: staged — feature gated behind org flag model_onboard_hints; monitor cost/latency deltas and adoption metrics for 2 weeks before org-wide enable. Security/privacy: traces are sampled and stripped of prompt content; only timestamps, token lengths, and hardware telemetry are kept. Ops notes: added a curator lint to fail when suggested hints contradict explicit user overrides. Related work: follows ideas in ENG-1145 (profiling contract) and complements prior onboarding heuristics but focuses on compact, human-friendly suggestions and concise release microdiffs.

generator.py: rule set mapping quantile signatures to profile presets; includes cost-estimator hooks

Evan Chu: Can the sampler be further throttled for very large manifests to avoid added latency? Suggest moving sampling to background job — author: added TTL+async worker (see recorder.py) and added canary to validate no upload latency regression.
Lena Bauer: The microdiff JSON schema looks good but we should include a stable fingerprint to allow diffs to be referred to in release notes — author: added microdiff_fingerprint field (sha1 of sorted key-values) and documented in docs/onboarding/hints.md.
Diego Ramos: Are privacy redaction rules sufficient? We should explicitly ban prompt text in traces — author: enforced trimming and added unit test for redaction; CI verifies zero prompt-like tokens in artifacts.

Context: onboarding pipelines have been producing very verbose manifests and long-form changelogs that make automated release triage and quick compatibility heuristics slow. Motivation: provide a compact, deterministic summary of a model's onboarding metadata and a tiny performance fingerprint to speed up compatibility checks, changelog micro-drafts, and UI previews. What this PR does: adds an 'onboard-minifier' server-side transform and CLI that compacts model manifests (schema v2) by removing non-essential stamping and normalizing metadata into a canonical order; introduces a perf-fingerprint serializer that runs a light-weight sampled evaluation (configurable slices) to produce a deterministic 128-bit fingerprint plus a 64-byte base64-encoded performance sketch which is stored alongside the compact manifest; wires a changelog-microdraft hook that synthesizes a one-line delta blurb using the minified diff and the fingerprint delta to help reviewers triage impact quickly. Includes a DB migration to add a compact_stamp column and new indices for quick affinity lookups. Backwards compatibility: manifests produced by the minifier include a compatibility-stamp and a human-readable expansion map to avoid breaking older consumers. Migration tools: small migration script that backfills compact_stamp for last 30 days of ingests using sampled runs (opt-in by default). Checklist: - [x] unit tests for minifier and serializer - [x] integration test for CLI roundtrip - [x] docs page (docs/onboard-minifier.md) with migration instructions - [x] migration script and dry-run mode - [x] reviewer sign-offs. Related work: references ENG-4920 (onboard scale optimizations) and ENG-4978 (changelog automation enhancements). Link to design doc: internal: /docs/design/onboard-minifier (internal link).
Liam O'Connor: Can the minifier be configured to retain arbitrary vendor metadata via a whitelist? (requested to avoid losing downstream fields)
Asha Patel: Yes — the CLI and service accept a --keep-fields whitelist and we persist an expansion_map in the compact manifest. Added tests for expansion_map behavior.
Maya Chen: Perf-fingerprint should be stable across parallel runs and not rely on non-deterministic ordering. Please ensure deterministic seeds and explicit sort orders.
Asha Patel: Implemented deterministic sampling seed derived from model-id+manifest-hash and enforced canonical ordering before sampling. Added comment and test in test_fingerprint_serializer.py.
Diego Rivera: DB migration needs a backfill strategy that is rate-limited to avoid overloading the main DB cluster during rollout.
Asha Patel: Migration script implements batching with exponential backoff and a dry-run flag; documentation section describes rollout knobs.
- Add onboard-minifier: compact manifest generation (schema v2) to reduce registry storage and speed UI previews.
- Add perf-fingerprint serializer: deterministic 128-bit fingerprint + compact sketch stored with manifest for fast compatibility heuristics.
- Add changelog micro-draft hook: one-line delta summaries for faster reviewer triage.
Notes: migration is opt-in by default; follow docs/onboard-minifier.md for rollout and backfill procedure.
payload.title: Introduce onboard-minifier and perf-fingerprint serializer

payload.body:
Motivation: onboarding has become noisy when multiple probe sources (regional telemetry, CI workload runs, and customer-supplied samples) produce slightly divergent performance profiles for the same model variant. This causes churn in autogenerated release notes and complicates rollouts when the registry chooses a single "canonical" profile by arbitrary precedence.

What this PR does: 1) Introduces a federated-profile-merger that consumes a set of performance profile snapshots from multiple probes and produces a composed profile with weighted statistics (p50/p95 token latency, throughput, memory footprint) and provenance links. We weight probes by signal quality heuristics (sample coverage, run stability, and recency) so the composed profile better reflects production-like conditions. 2) Adds a deterministic telemetry-hash (telemetry_fingerprint) computed from normalized probe summaries so the same set of inputs yields the same fingerprint independent of ordering; this enables idempotent onboard runs and safer CI. 3) Adds a release-snapshot generator that bundles composed profiles, a short changelog blurb, and a stability score into a compact artifact (release_snapshot.json) used by downstream release automation and the console. 4) Hooks the generator into the onboard pipeline and the model-intake web UI so reviewers can preview the composed profile and proposed release blurb before approving.

Implementation notes: - federation/merger.py: core merge algorithm, weighting heuristics, and provenance resolver. Includes unit tests that cover edge cases (single probe, tie weights, missing fields). - telemetry/fingerprint.py: canonical serializer + blake2b-based hash with version tag. - pipeline/hooks/release_snapshot.py: snapshot assembler and compact serializer used by registry APIs. - ui/onboard_preview: adds preview endpoint and small React component to show composed metrics and suggested blurb. - docs: onboarding guide updated with section on federated profiles and how weights are computed.

Compatibility: the composed profile schema is a non-breaking additive extension to existing profile payloads (we keep legacy fields and add composed_metrics and telemetry_fingerprint). Downstream consumers that don't understand composed_metrics will still read legacy baseline fields.

Checklist: - [x] merger algorithm and unit tests - [x] deterministic hashing and cross-order idempotency tests - [x] snapshot serializer and compact schema - [x] UI preview for reviewers - [x] docs and migration notes - [x] e2e smoke run against intake CI

Notes for reviewers: focus review on federation/merger.py for weighting heuristics and the canonicalization rules in telemetry/fingerprint.py. The weighting parameters are tunable via registry config; defaults are conservative. The UI change is intentionally lightweight — preview only (no edit-in-place).
Ava Martinez: Can you explain why recency weighs more than sample coverage by default? Feels risky for short-lived spikes.
Naomi Chen: Default weight favors stability first, recency second. The heuristic is stable_score * 0.6 + recency_score * 0.3 + coverage_score * 0.1. I added comments and a config flag under registry.federation.weights for teams to tune.
Samir Patel: Left minor nits in merger.py about edge-case handling when percentile arrays are different lengths.
Naomi Chen: Addressed both nits, added padding function and unit tests for percentile alignment.
Jordan Liu: Verified telemetry_fingerprint is stable across reorderings; approving once CI green.
Ava Martinez: Approved after reading docs and seeing e2e smoke run results.
payload.title: federated-metrics-driven profile merging and deterministic release snapshot generation

payload.body:
Motivation: Streaming generation showed persistent tail spikes at the emission boundary when small bursts of inflight tokens mixed with KV-cache cold starts. This PR introduces a 'token pulse' scheduler that emits tokens in tight, configurable micro-pulses and a lightweight cache-rewarm hinting mechanism to proactively reheat KV shards for anticipated streams. The goal is to reduce first-byte latency variance and 95th/99th tail while keeping throughput and cost neutral. Changes include: 1) token pulse scheduler: a deterministic micro-emission loop that groups emission work into short fixed-duration pulses to avoid the pathological interaction between long kernel stalls and small request bursts; 2) credit-aware pacing: backpressure tokens are now accounted in a small-window credit bucket (microcredits) to allow short bursts without triggering a full flush; 3) cache rewarm hints: upstream request router annotates hot prefixes and the runtime issues async lightweight KV prefetches that hold minimal state and prefer local GPU memory; 4) kernel affinity stride: small change to kernel selection to prefer already-pinned micro-buffers for the duration of a pulse to reduce kernel swap overhead; 5) observability hooks: new pulse-level metrics (pulse_duration_ms, pulses_per_request, pulse_kv_prefetch_count) and a tracing span for pulse lifecycle. Checklist: - [x] design doc reviewed (ENG-1924) - [x] unit tests for scheduler and credit accounting - [x] integration test for cache rewarm under mixed workload - [x] e2e perf harness runs and analysis attached. Related: ENG-1978 on continuous batching interaction; SUP-455 incident notes where bursts caused tail regressions. See design note: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1924/token-pulse-design (internal). Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.enable_token_pulse (default off for dedicated until canary), staged canary on hosted (5% hosts), monitor metrics and A/B. Risk and mitigation: risk of increased jitter if pulse_duration_ms misconfigured; default tuned to 6ms after perf runs. If regression detected, revert via runtime flag and rollback. Performance: median TTFB improved ~12% on our synthetic conversational benchmark, 95th improved ~34%, 99th improved ~22% with no measurable throughput drop. This PR is intentionally conservative in state held by cache rewarm hints to avoid memory blowup on dense workloads.
Jun Park: Can you clarify how microcredits are accounted when requests are canceled mid-pulse? Suggest deducting only committed tokens in the pulse commit path.
Maya Patel (author): We only deduct on commit path. If a request cancels mid-pulse we reconnect credits to the bucket via the refund path; added explicit unit tests for cancel/refund behavior.
Evan Brooks: The kernel affinity change looks safe but needs perf numbers across T4/P40/P100. Also add a knob to cap affinity dwell time.
Maya Patel (author): Added dwell cap config (runtime.affinity_dwell_ms) and included T4/P40 baseline numbers in the PR description. Affinity dwell defaults to 32ms.
Sofia Martinez: Observability: add a rate-limited debug log for cache rewarm failures so we can correlate prefetch misses without log spam.
Maya Patel (author): Added rate-limited logging and a metric cache_rewarm_prefetch_failures_total.
synth-conv-benchmark: median TTFB -12%
synth-conv-benchmark: p95 TTFB -34%
synth-conv-benchmark: p99 TTFB -22%
throughput: within noise (±1%)
cost-per-token: neutral (prefetches are soft and limited)
Introduced token pulse scheduler to reduce emission latency variance.
Added cache rewarm hinting to proactively heat KV shards for hot prefixes.
Exposed pulse-level metrics and tracing for observability.
Feature gated and rolled out via runtime flag (runtime.enable_token_pulse).
Feature flag: runtime.enable_token_pulse (boolean). Default: false for Dedicated until canary completes.
Tuneable knobs: runtime.token_pulse_duration_ms (default 6), runtime.affinity_dwell_ms (default 32), runtime.microcredit_window (default 8 tokens).
Monitor: pulse_duration_ms, pulses_per_request, pulse_kv_prefetch_count, cache_rewarm_prefetch_failures_total.
Rollback: flip runtime.enable_token_pulse to false and restart emitter workers if regressions observed.
payload.title: introduce-token-pulse-scheduler-and-cache-rewarm-to-reduce-emission-latency

payload.body:
Context: onboarding larger open models today produces noisy release notes and duplicate affordance hints when a model variant transitively derives from multiple base artifacts. This PR introduces two tightly related pieces: 1) a compact transitive "affordance anchor" annotation set that deduplicates and scopes affordance/compatibility hints across variant chains, and 2) a release-seed compactifier that synthesizes a terse release seed (changelog fragment) for use in the automated release-note generator and in the CLI onboarding flow.

Motivation: reduce churn in model registry release notes, make upgrade diffs easier to read for users and evaluators, and make the onboard pipeline resilient to long transitive dependency chains (e.g., forked checkpoints and small fine-tunes). This improves downstream evals and the redact/rollback pathways by keeping the seed minimal and provenance-aware.

What changed (high level): added an affordance anchor data model, an algorithm that collapses transitive affordances into canonical anchors with provenance pointers, a compactifier that turns a profile delta into a one-page release seed, and a small CLI flag (--compact-seed) that emits the compact seed during onboard. The compactifier also tags candidate drop-in replacements for quantized variants to help automated release-note templating.

Implementation notes: implementation is in three files: anchors/* contains the annotation model and serializer; compactifier/* contains the seed generator and deterministic sampling; onboard/cli adds the new flag and wiring into the upload flow. The compactifier uses a stable hash (xxh64 seed with repo salt) to ensure repeatable compact seeds across runs; a compatibility window prevents accidental aliasing across minor model versions. Affordance anchors keep a short provenance array (max 3 entries) to avoid large payloads while still giving human operators a path to the source.

Backward compatibility and migration: new annotations are optional. Existing model profiles are left untouched; the onboard CLI will emit compact seeds only when --compact-seed is passed or when the Linear ticket indicates a compact onboarding flow. For existing release automation, the release-note assembler will prefer compact seeds when present but falls back to the full delta. Migration script: scripts/migrators/affordance-backfill.sh (small, idempotent) is included to backfill anchors for models onboarded in the last 90 days.

Testing and validation: unit tests for anchor collapse and compactifier stability added (anchors_test.py, compactifier_test.py). Added a small sampling harness that compares full delta vs compact seed at 1000 random deltas to assert that >95% of user-visible affordances are preserved in the compact seed. CI: runs unit, lint, and lightweight integration with the onboard CLI; an optional e2e sampling run exists behind a CI toggle.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind registry feature-flag "compact-seed". Default rollout to alpha internal projects for one week, then to public staged projects. Monitor: release_note_size and seed_collision_rate metrics added to console (per-model).

Related work: this complements ENG-4217 (release-note templating refactor) and PM-214 (onboard UX condensed summaries).
Reviewers requested safety allowlists, hashing stability, and safe migration controls. Author addressed all points in follow-up commits. Small last-minute tweak to reduce provenance array size for payload safety.
Asha: Can we guarantee the compactifier won't drop security-relevant affordances? Please ensure explicit allowlist for anything tagged 'exposes-PII' — author: added allowlist and tests.
Benji: hashing collision concerns for stable seed? suggest increasing seed-length or adding repo salt — author: switched to xxh64 with repo salt and added collision metrics.
Dalia: migration script should be idempotent and rate-limited for large registries — author: added rate-limit flag and dry-run mode to migrator.
- Add: transitive affordance anchors to deduplicate variant affordances.
- Add: compact release-seed generator (CLI flag --compact-seed) to produce terse changelog fragments for automated releases.
- Tools: migrator script to backfill anchors for recent models.
- Metrics: release_note_size, seed_collision_rate (console dashboards)
payload.title: Introduce transitive affordance anchors and compact release-seed generator

payload.body:
Motivation: Presubmit runs have shown increasing nondeterministic failures in SDK integration suites (notably sdk/python/azure and sdk/ts/storage) caused by transient dev dependencies and occasional toolchain drift. This PR introduces a conservative, opt-in mechanism to (1) detect mismatched or stale toolchains used by CI agents (toolchain-watcher), (2) quarantine and re-run tests that fail due to transient devdeps to reduce noisy flakes (devdep-curation), and (3) expose a lightweight presubmit profile for fast feedback on PRs that touch only docs or small infra changes.

Goals: Reduce developer pain from noisy presubmit failures, speed up typical PR feedback loops, and keep release automation informed about dependency-refresh events so downstream release hooks can annotate or pause rollouts. Important constraints: changes must be non-breaking for repos that opt out, and rollout should be reversible and observable.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a new small binary infra/toolchain-watcher integrated into the presubmit pipeline. The watcher compares the agent runtime (go/node/python versions, pinned toolchain manifest) against a manifest stored in ci/images/toolchain-manifest.json and fails fast with a structured message if mismatch is detected. In 'lease' mode it can pin a short-lived devimage lease to speed up subsequent runs.
- Adds tools/devdep-curator which implements a quarantine flow: if a test fails with signatures matching configured transient patterns (network/timeouts/403 rate limits from registries), the job records the failure with a telemetry tag and reruns the test in a clean curated devdeps environment. If rerun passes, failure is marked quarantine and surfaced to a 'quarantine' dashboard for triage rather than blocking merges.
- Introduces ci/presubmit-profiles.yaml with a new 'fast' profile used for PRs that change only markdown, docs, or targeted config files; 'fast' runs linters and smoke tests only. Full matrix runs remain the default for code changes.
- Adds minimal release automation hook: release/automation/annotate-dep-refresh.go will add a release note annotation when a presubmit run triggers an automated devdep update (Linear integration stub is included).
- Adds documentation and rollout plan under docs/ci/toolchain-watcher.md and an internal checklist in the PR description.

Checklist (release gating):
- [x] toolchain-watcher binary + tests
- [x] devdep-curator proof-of-concept + telemetry counters
- [x] presubmit profile and workflow updates with opt-out label support (PRESUBMIT_SKIP_QUARANTINE)
- [x] docs and runbook for oncall
- [x] release hook stub to annotate dep-refresh events
- [x] canary rollout to 10% of presubmits (implemented via workflow input, currently enabled for handful of SDK repos)

Why this is safe: Default behaviour is unchanged unless a repo opts into curated devdep handling or uses the 'fast' profile. Quarantine does not auto-suppress legitimate regressions; quarantined failures are recorded and surfaced for triage. Toolchain-watcher fails fast with an explanatory message and a link to the manifest diff; it can be disabled via CI input for legacy agents.

Testing and CI notes: Initial CI run showed a flaky failure in sdk/python/azure integration test on the first run (network timeout to test fixture). The devdep-curator detected the pattern and reran in a curated environment; rerun passed. After a follow-up tweak to retry thresholds the CI pipeline passed all checks. Unit tests included for watcher manifest parsing and quarantine signature matching.

Rollout plan and observability:
- Day 0: Merge with flag disabled globally; enable for sdk/python and sdk/typescript presubmits (10% canary).
- Day 1-3: Monitor 'ci.quarantine_count' and 'ci.toolchain_mismatch' metrics; review quarantine dashboard weekly.
- Day 7: If stable, broaden to all SDK repos.
- Opt-out policy: Repos can set PRESUBMIT_SKIP_QUARANTINE label or set presubmit-profiles.yaml entry to 'legacy'.

Related: ENG-2345 (reduce presubmit flakiness), ENG-2350 (release automation annotations), SUP-987 (customer-facing incident that motivated quicker rollback diagnostics).

High-level commits and changes: commit list included above. Key changed files: ci/presubmit-profiles.yaml (adds 'fast' profile), infra/toolchain-watcher (new component), tools/devdep-curator (quarantine logic and runner shim), .github/workflows/presubmit.yml (conditional steps for new profile), docs/ci/toolchain-watcher.md (runbook), release/automation/annotate-dep-refresh.go (release annotation stub).

Notes for reviewers: Focus on the quarantine signature whitelist (tools/devdep-curator/README) and the opt-out label semantics. The watcher implementation is intentionally conservative — it surfaces mismatches rather than auto-rolling images. We will follow up with a smaller PR to add a self-healing mode if the team wants it.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals from Luis, Marta, and Samir. CI green on final run.

If something goes wrong: Revert the merge or set global flag to disable devdep-curation (CI input: DEVDEP_CURATION=off). Runbook includes steps to remove leases and clear quarantine state.

Luis Ortega: Can the watcher be run as a short-lived job instead of a long-lived daemon? Concern about resource usage on small CI agents.
Ava Chen: Addressed — watcher now runs as a single run per presubmit with optional 'lease' mode for devbox sessions; updated main.go and docs.
Marta Nguyen: The devdep quarantine looks good, but we should ensure it doesn't hide real regressions in SDK tests. Suggest adding a telemetry tag for quarantined failures.
Ava Chen: Added telemetry tag 'devdep.quarantined=true' and exported a counter to Prometheus; included in rollout checklist.
Samir Patel: Please add an opt-out label for repos that still need full devdeps during presubmit (we need parity for some infra repos).
Ava Chen: Added PRESUBMIT_SKIP_QUARANTINE label handling and documented edge cases.
CI Bot: flaky sdk-tests/azure-integration failed on first run; rerun succeeded. Final CI status: all checks passed.

Summary: Add an atomic transaction log for model onboarding events and attach compact cryptographic profile signatures to onboarding profiles. This change adds a write-ahead 'onboard_tx_log' table, an uploader-side transaction wrapper, and a lightweight signature scheme (profile_signature) used for traceable changelog digests and offline verification.
Motivation: onboarding has historically produced fragmented records (multiple metadata writes, sidecar profile uploads, async profile-calibration tasks) which made reconstructing a single coherent "onboard event" difficult for audits and changelogs. We need an atomic, compact record that captures the manifest, profile pointers, provenance hashes, and a signature so downstream release-note automation can create deterministic digests.
Design:
- New DB migration to create onboard_tx_log with columns: tx_id, model_id, actor, timestamp, manifest_hash, profile_id, profile_signature, status, metadata_blob_ref.
- Uploader changes: wrap model+profile upload steps in a transaction that writes a tx log row in status=PENDING, performs existing upload steps, computes a compact profile_signature (ed25519 over canonical profile JSON + manifest_hash), updates the tx row to COMMITTED.
- Change hook: add a release-note digester that consumes committed tx rows and emits compact changelog entries (JSONL) for the changelog pipeline.
- Backfill tool: best-effort backfill that reconstructs tx rows for recent uploads using manifests and profile-history when available; backfill is non-blocking and tagged.
- Tests: unit tests for signature generation, integration test that simulates a failed upload and ensures tx status remains PENDING/ROLLED_BACK as appropriate.
Checklist:
- [x] DB migration and schema docs
- [x] Transactional uploader wrapper
- [x] Profile signature algorithm and tests
- [x] Changelog digester consumer
- [x] Backfill script and docs
- [x] Integration tests for failure modes
Commits (high level):
- feat(txlog): add onboard_tx_log migration and model
- feat(onboard): transaction wrapper and uploader changes
- feat(sig): add profile_signature util and verification
- feat(digest): add changelog-digest consumer
- test: integration tests for transactional behavior
- ci: add end-to-end test job for backfill sample
Changed files (high level):
- db/migrations/20241107_create_onboard_tx_log.sql
- services/onboard/uploader/transactional_uploader.py
- services/onboard/signature/profile_signature.py
- services/onboard/tests/test_transactional_upload.py
- tools/onboard_backfill/reconstruct_tx.py
- tools/changelog_digest/consumer.py
- docs/model-onboard/txlog.md
- docs/model-onboard/signature-spec.md
- .github/workflows/onboard-e2e.yml
Review notes:

payload.body:
Motivation: The current onboarding pipeline generates monolithic changelogs that are hard to reason about for incremental model updates and cause noisy release notes for downstream consumers. We need a smaller-footprint, deterministic audit trail for onboard mutations plus a curator that can assemble concise release notes by impact, dataset/capacity signals, and workload-relevance. This PR implements two coordinated pieces: 1) an incremental onboard audit worker that records compact, per-field deltas and stable provenance IDs; and 2) a changelog curator service that consumes audit fragments, attaches representative telemetry (sampled), and drafts reviewer-friendly release notes.

What this changes: single continuous implementation and tests described below. High-level features: deterministic fragment IDs (sha256 of canonicalized delta + onboarding-timestamp), delta types (metadata, binary, profile, compatibility), per-field confidence tokens, optional telemetry attachments (latency/cost histograms sampled from onboarding probes), CLI integration (mrctl release draft --from <tag> --to <tag> --cohort <cohort>), and a docs page describing the migration and review workflow.

Implementation notes: - added services/onboard_audit/worker.py: an async worker that listens to onboarding transactions and emits compact audit fragments into changelog_fragments table; uses protobuf-lite schema for compactness. - added services/changelog_curator/assembler.py: consumes fragments, groups by model family/variant, computes impact buckets (breaking, risky, safe), and renders markdown templated release notes. - DB migration db/migrations/20260220_add_onboard_audit.sql: creates changelog_fragments, audit_index, and a small provenance table. - CLI tools/mrctl/release.py: new subcommand to produce drafts and push to Linear as draft issues when run with --publish. - telemetry sampling implemented in services/onboard_audit/sampler.py using reservoir sampling + tenant-scoped hashed salt to avoid PII leakage. - tests: tests/integration/test_changelog_curator.py and tests/unit/test_fragment_id_determinism.py. - docs: docs/onboarding/release-notes.md and docs/migrations/onboard-audit-migration.md.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-9876) - [x] Schema migration with backfill plan - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Security review (sampling privacy constraints) - [x] Docs and migration guide - [x] CLI integration - [x] CI green (see checks below)

Commit summary: "initial onboard audit worker and curator; migrations; CLI; tests; docs"

Notes on privacy: telemetry attachments are optional per-tenant and only include aggregated histograms. Sampling uses a salted hash to partition telemetry into deterministic cohorts without including raw identifiers. See docs/migrations/onboard-audit-migration.md for tenants with strict telemetry disallow lists.

Backwards compatibility and migration: fragments are append-only and do not change existing model_profile blobs. A backfill job (provided as part of the migration) converts recent onboarding transactions into fragments; the curator can operate in read-only mode when fragments are not present (falls back to previous changelog generator). Migration instructions are in docs/migrations/onboard-audit-migration.md.

Why this is unique: instead of producing a single changelog blob per release, we create small, queryable fragments that can be merged/curated per-consumer. This reduces noise for downstream services that only care about performance-profile changes or compatibility signals.

Testing and validation performed: unit tests for fragment id determinism, integration tests for end-to-end draft generation, manual run against staging onboard stream (internal run id: staging-20260224). CI ran coverage and a lightweight load test for the worker (target throughput 120 reqs/s with 50ms mean processing).

Rollout plan: feature-gate with tenant flag onboard_audit_v1; deploy worker and migrations during a low-traffic window; backfill windows run per-tenant with rate limits; promote curator to default once we observe stable churn for 48 hours.

Links: Design ticket: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-9876/incremental-onboard-audit-and-changelog-curator, Staging run: internal:///runs/staging-20260224, Migration plan: docs/migrations/onboard-audit-migration.md

Jae Park: Please ensure telemetry sampling can't be correlated back to tenant IDs. Can you add deterministic salt and document the privacy model?
Aisha Kapoor: Reply: added tenant-scoped salted hashing and documented behavior in migration guide. Sampling is opt-in per tenant. Updated sampler implementation and unit tests.
Marta Rossi: Migration steps look good but we need a clear rollback plan if the backfill fails mid-tier. Add step to mark fragments as partial and a resumable backfill token.
Aisha Kapoor: Added resumable backfill token and a 'partial_backfill' flag in the provenance table. Updated migration doc and backfill script.
Ethan Cole: Minor: please include an example of the CLI output for a small model family in docs/release-notes.md
Aisha Kapoor: Added CLI example and a sample output block to docs/onboarding/release-notes.md
Jae Park: CI green and privacy reviewer acked. Approving. 👍

Context: manual changelog curation is a recurring bottleneck during model rollouts and makes it hard for engineers and product to prioritize follow-up work. Motivation: automate prioritization of model metadata changes (perf regressions/improvements, tokenizer changes, API surface changes) so that release notes surface actionable items and reduce reviewer overhead. What this PR does: 1) Adds a delta-scoring service that consumes profile diffs and computes a single 'delta_score' per change using weighted signals (perf magnitude, sample-level regression count, dataset overlap, stability signature, API-compat flags, and recent customer impact markers). 2) Introduces a release-note contextualizer that converts a high-score delta into 1-3 concise bullets plus an example prompt and expected model output snippet to help SREs/docs. 3) Wires the outputs into the existing changelog-assembler: candidates are emitted to the /release-candidates API and the console shows a ranked list for editors. Design notes: scoring is a hybrid rule + small-model scorer (lightweight instruct model running in cheap CPU tier) — weights are configurable via the registry config and backed by a Linear ticket for tuning. The contextualizer uses a compact prompt template and extracts deterministic snippets; fallbacks use a template renderer when the small-model confidence is low. Data migration and rollout: adds a nullable delta_score column to model_profile_deltas and a release_candidates table. Migration is backward-compatible; system will not change UI behavior until feature flag 'release_context_v1' is flipped. Backfill: script backfills 90 days of profile diffs and emits candidates; backfill ran in staging and its results were spot-checked. Tests: unit tests for scoring heuristics, integration tester for release-candidates endpoint, and end-to-end smoke that renders candidate bullets. Security & privacy: contextualizer runs only on metadata and synthetic examples; no customer PII is sent to external services. Related work: ENG-2109 (signal framework), PR #33109 (micro-changelog plumbing) and ENG-1965 (profile-stability signatures). Checklist: [x] scoring core implemented [x] contextualizer model + template [x] API and db migration [x] backfill script + dry-run mode [x] docs updated in registry readme [x] e2e tests and CI green Migration steps for operators: run the migration, toggle feature flag in console, run backfill with --dry-run to validate. Notes for reviewers: pay attention to weight defaults and the small-model confidence threshold; we intentionally keep weights conservative for initial rollout.
Adds an automated delta-scoring pipeline that ranks model profile changes by user-impact signals
Introduces a contextualizer that synthesizes concise release-note bullets and example prompts/outputs for each high-priority delta
Backfills scores for recent 90-day model releases and exposes an API for release-note candidates
Unit tests cover heuristic scoring and low-confidence fallback. Integration tests exercise /release-candidates ingestion and console render. E2E was run in staging against 90-day backfill; team spot-checked 25 candidate summaries across varied models. Post-merge monitor: watch registry.release_candidate.count and staging sample quality metric for 48 hours after feature flag flip.
Migration adds nullable column; migration is safe to run online. Backfill should be started with --concurrency=4 and monitored; default weight config lives in config/delta_weights.yaml. If noisy candidates appear, reduce perf weight and increase stability penalty. To disable: flip feature flag 'release_context_v1' in the console.
Arjun Rao: High-level LGTM. A few nit comments on weight defaults and the db nullable semantics. Please add a short doc explaining how to tune the weights operationally.
Maya Thompson (author): Thanks — added docs/registry/automated_changelogs.md with tuning section and annotated the config with examples. Kept defaults conservative as discussed.

Sample candidate output: [Improved tokenization for token X leading to +3% BLEU on dataset A] -> bullets: 'Tokenization change reduced off-by-one splits for X, improving structured output on dataset A (approx +3% BLEU). Suggest smoke test: run evaluation suite on dataset A and verify no new regressions.' Example prompt: 'Summarize differences in handling token X and provide an example input+output before/after.'
Fallback rendering: plain template usage when model confidence < 0.6: 'Change detected: <short description>. Recommended action: run evaluation on affected datasets.'

Motivation: Onboarding new model variants repeatedly produces implicit compatibility questions (quantized vs fp16, KV-cache layout, tokenizer changes). Manual verification and handwritten release notes cause regressions and slow rollouts. This PR introduces a machine-readable model compatibility matrix plus an automated release assembler that generates profile delta release notes summarizing metadata changes, performance deltas, and recommended downgrade/fallback mappings. Scope: 1) Add compatibility matrix schema and storage for per-model-version compatibility assertions; 2) Add a CI job that runs forward/backward compatibility checks by spinning a lightweight eval harness against a compatibility subset; 3) Add an 'mrctl release-assemble' tool that consumes changed profiles and the compatibility matrix to create a structured release draft and a changelog fragment; 4) Small schema bump for model metadata (compatibility_tags, compatible_with) and accompanying validators. Implementation highlights: - registry/schema/model-metadata.schema.json: add compatibility_tags and compatible_with fields and document semantics; - .github/workflows/compatibility-check.yml: new CI workflow that triggers on PRs touching registry/profiles or schema and runs a matrix of compatible pair tests; - tools/mrctl/cmd/compat_check.go: CLI for local compatibility validation mirroring CI; - tools/mrctl/cmd/release_assemble.go: produces release draft JSON and a markdown changelog fragment, pulls perf deltas via evaluation harness; - scripts/release/assemble_release.py: utility that aggregates profile deltas, annotates with compatibility status, and opens a GitHub release draft via API if GITHUB_DRY_RUN=false; - registry/compatibility/matrix.csv: canonical example matrix template added; - tests/compatibility/test_matrix_integration.py: integration tests for the CI job and assembler. Backwards compatibility: schema change is additive and optional; existing registries continue to function. Rollout plan: feature-gated via MRCTL_COMPAT_MATRIX=on in CI and an opt-in flag in the console; start as alpha for internal model onboarding. Related links: Linear ENG-1294 (compatibility-check harness), ENG-1312 (release-assembler), changes reference the eval-harness repo for perf diffs. Why different from previous work: prior PRs focused on changelog automation or profile generation; this patch centers the registry around an explicit compatibility surface and ties that surface into automated release output to make rollouts and fallbacks explicit and reproducible.
Diego Morales: Please add a note on how compatibility assertions interact with pinned rollout policies. Action: added documentation to docs/registry/compatibility.md and updated the compatibility schema description.
Rina Zhou: The CI matrix job timed out in the first run because we were pulling full model weights. We needed to use the lightweight eval subset. Action: switched CI to use eval-harness subset images and added a size limit flag.
Samir Khan: Suggest adding a clear fallback mapping for quantized -> fp16 inference when a variant is incompatible. Action: implemented automatic fallback suggestions in assemble_release.py output and included them in the release fragment.
- Introduced a machine-readable model compatibility matrix (registry/compatibility/matrix.csv) and schema fields to record compatibility assertions; - New CI workflow to validate forward/backward compatibility across model variants and tokenizers; - New mrctl commands: compat-check and release-assemble to validate locally and produce release drafts; - Release assembler outputs changelog fragments that include profile deltas, perf regressions, and recommended fallback mappings; - Tests and docs for internal alpha rollout.

Context: onboarding throughput has been noisy for wide-variant uploads and our changelog generation frequently misses concise, actionable blurbing when multiple variant-level changes are batched. This PR introduces two complementary systems: 1) a heuristic variant weighting engine that scores incoming variants using historical traffic patterns, performance deltas, and license/size heuristics to surface a prioritized sampling queue for profiling and release candidate promotion; 2) a release annotator service that consumes the onboarding delta (metadata changes, profile diffs, and perf sample summaries) and auto-drafts a short, structured changelog snippet with severity and rollout suggestions. Design highlights: weighting is configurable by policy with fallbacks (size/latency/affordance weight slices), weighting outputs are stored as a transient priority key in the intake pipeline, and the annotator uses templated heuristics to produce one-line titles + 2-3 bullet highlights. Safety: annotator is opt-in and drafts are created as PR comments and in the release-drafts queue; we added guardrails to prevent leaking internal perf numbers (redacts sample IDs) and a confidence score accompanies every auto-draft. Deployment plan: feature flag rollout (staged by organization tier), canary to 5% of onboarding traffic, full opt-in after two weeks of monitoring. Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves existing onboarding pipeline unless feature flag enabled. Testing: unit tests for scoring math, integration tests exercising the intake -> annotator pipeline with synthetic profiles, and an end-to-end smoke test validating a drafted changelog for a multi-variant upload. Impact: expected to reduce manual curation time for release notes, accelerate promotion of high-impact variants to staged rollouts, and improve sampling efficiency for perf jobs. Related work: builds on ENG-4207 (onboard prioritization prototype) and PM-119 (release automation goals). Rollout checklist: feature flag, monitor "annotator.confidence < 0.4" alerts, validate generated drafts with curation team for first two weeks.
Adds a heuristic-driven variant weighting engine to improve model onboarding prioritization and a release annotator that drafts concise changelog entries based on onboarding deltas and perf signals. Includes perf-sampling hooks and configuration flags for opt-in production rollout.

payload.body:
Background and motivation: We have increasing variability in inbound model manifests (different model sources provide slightly different metadata shapes). That variability makes downstream profile generation and changelog drafting brittle and requires a lot of manual curation. This PR introduces an intake enrichment stage that normalizes and annotates incoming model metadata with conservative affinity hints, stable canonical keys, and provenance traces, plus a changelog curator that uses template-driven human-friendly blurb generation for release notes.

Goals: 1) Reduce manual curation required for onboarding by creating deterministic canonical metadata from noisy inputs. 2) Provide stable affordance tags used by profiling and routing (e.g., "affinity:low_mem", "affinity:fp16_ready"). 3) Generate concise release note snippets automatically to accelerate model rollouts and standardize customer-facing wording.

What this PR changes (high level): - Adds a new enrichment module (ingest/enrichment) with schema_normalizer and transformer adapters for common inbound manifest shapes. - Adds a templated changelog curator (changelog/curator/templater.py) that maps metadata deltas to human-readable snippets with configurable tone and safety filters. - Provides an onboard_backfill CLI to retroactively run enrichment on existing registry entries and emit delta reports. - Exposes a Helm toggle and CI integration to run a small end-to-end integration test for the enrichment path.

Checklist: - [x] schema normalizer core implemented and covered by unit tests - [x] changelog templater with sample templates and safety heuristics - [x] CLI backfill with dry-run mode - [x] docs for operators and maintainers - [x] helm flag and CI integration - [x] reviewer feedback addressed and logging improved

Migration notes/backfill: The onboard_backfill script supports --since and --dry-run flags. For the initial rollout we recommend running a dry-run and sampling 200 manifests, then running in batched mode. The backfill emits a delta CSV and a small sample of generated changelog snippets for signoff.

Risk and fallbacks: Enrichment is opt-in via the helm flag enrichment.enabled=false by default. If any part of the enrichment path fails for a model, the intake falls back to the previous raw-manifest path and logs a bounded warning (we do not block onboarding). The templater includes a conservative whitelist that blocks overly speculative marketing claims.

Tests and CI: Unit tests added for normalizer edge cases and templater heuristics. CI now includes an integration job that runs a containerized mini-registry ingest flow and asserts enrichment idempotency (integration job is green in CI checks).

Related work: This complements ENG-2410 (profiling-affordance-mapping) and reduces the manual curation burden described in PM-98. See docs/registry/enrichment.md for operator guidance and sample outputs.
Ethan Brooks (reviewer) - small nits: please tighten alias rules for 'precision' to avoid false positives; also add more explicit tests around missing 'license' fields.
Priya Nair (author reply) - tightened alias map and added three missing-field tests; updated docs to call out license fallback behavior.
Marta Velasquez (reviewer) - templater: prefer shorter 1-2 sentence blurbs for release notes; added an example template with neutral tone.
Priya Nair (author reply) - added neutral templates and a tone flag; added safety whitelist logic to block product claims (e.g., '100% accuracy').
Diego Ramos (reviewer) - CI: add integration step to ensure enrichment does not add non-deterministic fields to manifests.
Priya Nair (author reply) - added idempotency integration test and logging for deterministic output path.

payload.body:
Motivation: onboarding new model variants currently relies on manual sample selection and ad-hoc changelog prose. That leads to inconsistent quality signals and brittle release notes. This PR adds two pieces: 1) a lightweight example-driven quality scorer that ranks onboarding examples by semantic drift and outcome stability, and 2) an autogen changelog drafter that synthesizes concise release notes from the scorer output and curated prompt-set diffs. Goals: reduce time-to-publish for model intake, make changelogs actionable for downstream infra and SRE teams, and provide a reproducible artifact attached to each model version. Implementation summary: - example-driven scorer: Rust microservice + Python bindings that takes a delta of example sets and telemetry samples, computes embedding-based drift, per-slice failure rate deltas, and a tunable composite score (0-100). The scorer emits a compact CSV and a JSON lines summary used by the drafter. - changelog drafter: a Go utility that consumes scorer output, the model manifest, and an optional human note. It produces a short changelog blurb, a "what changed" bullet list, and suggested impact tags (e.g., latency-risk, semantics-regression). The drafter uses template-based heuristics plus a small set of deterministic rules to avoid hallucinated prose. Backwards compatibility: both components default to off for existing pipelines; the onboarding CLI gains a --autogen-changelog flag. Checklist: - [x] lightweight scorer prototype and service definition - [x] CLI wiring and integration tests - [x] deterministic drafter templates + unit tests - [x] end-to-end smoke with synthetic onboarding - [x] metrics emitters and docs for new manifest fields Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/notes/ENG-8472-example-scorer, example datasets folder: docs/onboard-examples/README.md, demo video in PR comment. Migration notes: operators can enable the scorer via the manifest key "example_scorer: enabled: true"; disabling reverts to previous behavior. Rollout: feature gated and staged for 2 weeks in canary before full default enablement.
Noah Park: Can we make the composite score explainable? Suggest adding a per-component breakdown to the CSV. (addressed)
Ethan Walker: Template heuristics look good but add a guardrail for 'semantic regression' tag when sample size < 50. (added threshold)
Samira Ali: Add telemetry labels for changelog drafts so we can track adoption across orgs. (added)
Maya Singh: replied with rationale for deterministic templates and included sample outputs in the PR description
- Add example-driven quality scorer that ranks onboarding example deltas and emits per-slice drift metrics.
- Introduce autogen changelog drafter that synthesizes concise release notes and suggested impact tags.
- CLI flag (--autogen-changelog) and manifest key (example_scorer.enabled) to opt into the workflow.
