payload.body:
Add: Variant Affordance Annotator that tags model variants with capability/constraint hints used by release routing and compatibility checks.
Add: Delta-aware Changelog Composer that generates concise release notes by scoring profile diffs and sampling representative examples.
Tooling: CLI preview for changelog drafts and a lightweight policy to auto-suggest rollback candidates when regressions are detected.
Non-breaking: Backwards-compatible metadata fields and migration script included; no runtime contract changes for consumers.
Context and motivation: We onboarded multiple model variants for the Q4 rollout and noticed reviewers and customers struggled to interpret subtle capability regressions across variants. Manual release notes were noisy and missed guidance for routing and mitigation. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) a Variant Affordance Annotator that infers and stamps compact capability/constraint hints into variant metadata during intake, and (2) a Delta-aware Changelog Composer that synthesizes concise release notes by scoring profile deltas and surface-sampling representative examples.

What this delivers: - Affordance annotator: a modular analyzer that runs as part of the intake pipeline. It emits standardized tags such as "safety:high-sensitivity", "affordance:table-reading", "latency:snappy", "kvcache-friendly". Tags are stored on variant metadata and are consumed by routing heuristics and the release composer. - Delta-aware composer: a rule-and-score based engine that compares new vs baseline profiles (latency/throughput/semantic metrics) and outputs a compact changelog with: summary bullets, graded impact (minor/major/regressive), representative prompt-response pairs (sampled), and suggested mitigation notes (rollback candidate, alternative variant). - CLI preview: a new 'registry changelog preview' command that produces draft notes for reviewers; safe-by-default (no auto-merge) and opt-in automerge via policy.

Key implementation points: - Annotator uses an ensemble of heuristics: static signatures (model arch × tokenization), sampled perf probes, and lightweight semantic probes (subset of eval harness) to infer capability hints. - Affordance schema extends variant metadata with a small, namespaced map: "affordances.v1" (fields are additive and backward compatible). Migration: existing variants without affordances are treated as unknown and do not break routing. - Composer implements a delta scoring pipeline with tunable weights (latency, accuracy deltas, hallucination signal). It de-duplicates noise via clustering and ranks candidate bullets by estimated user impact. - Storage: changelog drafts are stored as compact artifacts with provenance links to commits, Linear IDs, and sampling seeds. - Security/compliance: no user prompt data is stored; representative examples are sanitized and sampled from synthetic probes or public datasets where applicable.

Commits (high level): - 1a2b3c: initial annotator scaffold, schema and unit tests - 2d3e4f: perf probe harness integration and sampling strategy - 3f4g5h: delta scoring engine and composer templates - 4h5i6j: CLI preview and documentation - 5i6j7k: migration script and end-to-end tests - 6j7k8l: polish, CI flakiness fixes, and sample sanitization

Files/areas changed (high level): - src/annotator/affordance/ : new annotator library, heuristics and unit tests - schemas/variant_affordances_v1.yaml : new compact schema extension - tools/cli/changelog_preview.py : CLI to preview composer output - composer/delta_engine.py : delta scoring and summarizer - ingest/pipeline_hooks.py : hook to run annotator on intake - migration/migrate_affordances.py : one-time additive migration - docs/onboarding/affordances.md : onboarding guide and examples - tests/e2e/changelog_flow.test : end-to-end flow using mock probes

Illustrative snippet (composer template):
{
  "summary": "Minor regression in table-answering latency (p95 +120ms), accuracy stable",
  "impact": "minor",
  "examples": ["(sanitized example prompt 1)", "(sanitized example prompt 2)"],
  "suggested_action": "Consider routing 'table-heavy' traffic to variant v2.1 until kvcache backfills match baseline"
}

Review conversation (condensed): - Maya Chen (reviewer): "Nice separation between annotator and composer. Two asks: 1) tighten sampling seed determinism for reproducibility, 2) add a short-circuit to skip semantic probes when running in air-gapped installs." - Author reply (Priya): "Addressed both. Sampling seed is now deterministic via registry seed service; semantic probe is gated behind a 'probe-mode' flag and disabled by default in private installs." - Diego Alvarez: "Please add a note about cost/latency trade-offs of running annotator in the hot path." - Author: "Moved heavy perf probes to async background workers; hot path keeps cheap static signatures only. Documented tradeoffs in affordances.md." - Samir Patel: "Approve after tests flake is resolved." - CI runs fixed and tests green. Final approval given.

CI summary: - unit: pass - e2e (mock probes): pass - lint: pass - integration (registry staging): pass after a rerun due to transient infra failure - total: 6/6 checks green

Backward compatibility and migration: - Schema extension is additive (affordances.v1). Existing consumers will ignore the new field if unrecognized. - Migration script annotates historical variants in batches; it's rate-limited and idempotent. - No public API signature changes.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy annotator to staging with background-only mode (no auto-stamp). 2) Enable annotator for new onboardings and run migration on low-priority buckets. 3) Turn on composer preview for reviewers. 4) After one-week vetting, enable composer to emit changelog drafts automatically. 5) Monitor quality metrics (changelog acceptance rate, manual edits, false-positive regression tags) and rollback policy for 24/7 on-call.

Risk and mitigation: - Over-tagging: mitigated by conservative defaults and human-in-the-loop preview. - Probe cost: heavy probes run async and rate-limited; CLI preview uses cached artifacts. - Privacy: sanitized examples only; customers can opt-out of sampling.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main on 2024-11-12 after approvals and green CI. Linear references: ENG-2147, PM-511.

Notes for reviewers/maintainers: - If you need to tune composer weightings, see composer/config/weights.yaml. - For private installs, set PROBE_MODE=disabled to avoid network-based semantic probes. - The migration script can be run with --dry-run to inspect candidate variants before applying.

payload.body:
Context: onboarding new model variants currently triggers large, slow changelog generation and heavyweight perf profile runs. For small rollouts and automated pre-flight checks we need a compact, deterministic sanity artifact that: 1) captures a tiny set of representative prompts and gold answers for quality smoke-tests; 2) includes a lightweight performance snapshot (latency histogram + few key stats) encoded as an embedding so changelog automation can diff and surface regressions without re-running full suites. This PR introduces two pieces: (a) a compact sanity digest format (JSON + metadata) produced at model intake and stored alongside profile artifacts, and (b) perf-snapshot-embeds: a normalized vector representation of a perf histogram and 3 summary stats used by release note generation to compute significance and show human-friendly deltas.

What changed:
- New generator: scripts/generate_sanity_digest.py — CLI that consumes a model package (or local model weights) and a small promptset to output a stamped digest with deterministic ordering, sample ids, and tokenized signatures. The script has smoke-test and CI modes.
- Registry integration: pkg/onboard/digest.go — lightweight producer/consumer for digest artifacts and an upload flow to the model registry. Adds UploadSanityDigest and VerifyDigest APIs used by onboarding pipeline.
- Perf embedding: tooling in pkg/onboard/perf_embed.go and a small Go port of the embedding normalization used by Optimize team. The embedter converts latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) + error-rate into a 64-d float32 vector which is then base64-encoded for storage in the manifest.
- Changelog hook: tools/changelog/snapshot-diff-annotator.py — uses the perf snapshot embeds to compute cosine-distance deltas and render short humanized lines in the generated release note (e.g., "perf: p95 latency +8% (small regression) — see perf-snapshot-diff").
- Docs & CI: docs/sanity-digest.md documents the format and intended usage; ci/regression-check.yml adds an optional sanity-digest check step that fails CI only in strict mode.

Motivation and trade-offs: the digest is intentionally tiny (<= 8 samples) to be inexpensive and deterministic across environments and quantization modes; it isn't a replacement for full perf or eval runs. The perf-embed is designed to be robust to sample noise and to surface actionable deltas to humans and downstream automation.

Backwards compatibility: existing onboarding flows that don't produce the digest are unaffected; changelog annotator gracefully skips absent artifacts.

Testing: unit tests for serialization, round-trip verification, and an integration test that simulates registry upload and changelog diff.

Rollout plan: produce digests for the next two model intake jobs and enable changelog annotations for canary release notes.

Related Linear items: ENG-6231 (digest schema), ENG-6269 (perf embedter), PM-88 (changelog UX).
4 commits: initial python digest producer; go registry integration and API hooks; perf-embed implementation and tests; docs and CI. Key commits: 'add python sanity digest generator', 'introduce UploadSanityDigest/VerifyDigest API', 'perf embedding algorithm and unit tests', 'changelog annotator and docs'.
CI initially failed on lint for python script (flake8 errors) and a flaky integration test (timing). Lint fixes and a test timeout increase were pushed in second commit. All checks passing on rerun: unit, integration, linters, go vet, build. Optional CI step 'sanity-digest-check' is allowed to be non-blocking unless the 'strict-digest' label is set.

Ava Patel: Can we guarantee determinism across CPU/GPU and quantized builds? How do we ensure sample ordering? -- replied: script sorts samples by stable id and uses explicit RNG seed; unit test added to verify byte-for-byte for same inputs.

Motivation: onboarding high-capacity and quantized variants has become noisier in release notes and harder to map to hardware guidance for infra. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: 1) "annotated affinity stamps" — a small, versioned metadata artifact attached to model variants that captures recommended hardware affinity (e.g. ampere-80, triton-quant-fast, int8-friendly), expected memory working set, and recommended quantization knobs; and 2) a "chunked changelog compressor" — a post-processing step that consumes model intake diffs and emits condensed release chunks (human-friendly bullets + linked deep diffs) so changelogs stay readable for large model updates. Goals: reduce support noise during rollouts, surface deterministic hardware affinity suggestions to serving/runtime teams, and keep changelog summaries concise while preserving drill-down details.

What this PR does (high-level): added a new affinity annotation schema and signer for variant manifests; an upload hook that auto-populates affinity hints based on profiling heuristics and historical run-affinity matches; a compact serializer and compressor that groups changelog hunks into prioritized "chunks" and auto-generates teaser lines for release notes; integration tests and docs; migration tool to backfill affinity stamps for recent variants.

Implementation notes: affinity stamps are stored as a small stamped JSON file in the model bundle (affinity-stamp-v1.json) and a lightweight provenance hash is appended to the variant metadata. The chunked changelog compressor runs as a transform in the release pipeline (release-assembler) and uses heuristics: group by semantic change type (perf/regression/config), weight by user-facing impact (example-driven), and produce at most 6 top-level bullets with links to expanded hunks. The compressor is deterministic given the same diff seed and seed version.

Backwards compatibility and rollout: old variants without affinity stamps continue to function — runtime falls back to default routing. The upload hook is opt-in by default; orgs can enable auto-stamping via a feature flag at intake. The migration/backfill job writes affinity stamps as a separate commit and is reversible.

Testing/validation: unit tests for serializer, end-to-end integration with release-assembler in CI, a sampled backfill run capturing 500 variants for validation, and a small canary deploy of the compressed changelog to the docs pipeline.

Doc changes: docs/onboard/affinity-stamps.md, docs/release/changelog-compressor.md and a short console UI blurb to surface the top-3 affinity suggestions in the variant detail page.

Related: refers to ENG-4232 (affinity heuristics prototype) and ENG-4301 (changelog UX revamp).
Miguel Ortega: Nice separation between the schema and the signer. Two requests: (1) can we add a short TTL field on the stamp so we can expire stale affinity recommendations? (2) add a small table in the docs mapping common hwHint strings to runtime profiles.
Ava Chen: answered: added a 'recommendedUntil' optional ISO timestamp on the stamp (see schema commit). Doc table added under docs/onboard/affinity-stamps.md. Also added a test verifying expiry is ignored by runtime unless the feature flag is set.
Priya Kapoor: Request changes: the compressor heuristics look good, but please add a switch to emit full expanded hunks for internal builds (we don't want to hide details from SREs). Also run perf on a 2k-variant synthetic corpus.
Ava Chen: replied: added RELEASE_COMPRESSOR_MODE env var with 'compact' | 'expanded' options. Ran synthetic perf (results attached to CI artifact). Perf regression under 2% for compressor path; included summary in the CI artifact.
Liam O'Neill: Approve after CI green and one minor doc wording nitfix (s/teaser/teaser line/).
Add affinity stamps (affinity-stamp-v1) for model variants: runtime can surface recommended hardware hints; add chunked changelog compressor to produce concise release summaries with drill-down links. Opt-in by default; backfill available via migration tool. See docs/onboard/affinity-stamps.md and docs/release/changelog-compressor.md for details.
Backfill produced ~500 stamped variants during validation. Nightly backfill will be gated behind feature flag 'enable_affinity_backfill'. No runtime rollout needed; runtime will ignore missing stamps. Monitor routing miss-rate and token latency for two weeks after enabling.
payload.title: Introduce annotated affinity stamps and chunked changelog compressor

Motivation: onboarding at scale requires deterministic, explainable metadata deltas and repeatable changelog fragments that tie performance profile changes to release notes. This PR introduces a Harmonizer-driven Manifest Reconciler which consumes incoming model manifests, computes minimal delta-sets against the canonical registry, synthesizes performance-profile linkages, and emits changelog fragment candidates and signing-ready release snippets. Design summary: 1) manifest_reconciler: deterministic delta algorithm with 'affinity fingerprint' to group variant families and preserve transitive compatibility hints; 2) profile-linker: attaches sampled performance profiles (latency/cost/quality tokens) to the manifest delta and points to the profile snapshot in the model-registry; 3) changelog-harvester: generates compact, human-readable changelog fragments with structured annotations for automated release assembly; 4) approval-hook: optional Linear/GitHub review gate that annotates suggestions and auto-drafts release notes. Compatibility: adds model_manifest_v2.schema.json but keeps v1 ingest backward compatible for the onboard CLI for a 2-week migration window. Rollout plan: feature-flagged in registry and rollout to opt-in projects for 2 days followed by global flip and a one-day post-rollout audit. Tests and validation: unit tests for reconciliation heuristics, integration tests with sample snapshots, added property-based tests to assert deterministic deltas. Operational notes: new metrics exported under registry.harmonizer.{delta_count,conflict_rate,profile_attach_success}, and a lightweight audit export in NDJSON for downstream indexing. This description is the full continuous summary for the PR and contains links and checklist references inline.
Marcos Alvarez: Overall this looks good. Two thoughts: 1) we should add a guard to avoid linking ephemeral profile snapshots -- can we require a 'snapshot:stable' tag? 2) changelog fragments need a stable id that survives rebase. Please address before approve.
Rana Patel: Added snapshot tag enforcement and stable fragment id composed of manifest hash plus delta-seq. Updated tests to cover stable id behavior.
Elena Li: There are a couple of nits on error messages in manifest_reconciler.py and we should add a metric for rejected manifests. Also can we surface the delta size in the audit NDJSON?
Rana Patel: Addressed nits, added registry.harmonizer.rejected_manifest_count and included delta_size in the NDJSON export. Updated docs with metric descriptions.
Samir Gupta: Integration tests look flakey on CI when concurrent onboard events race. Recommend a mutex in the reconciler for the commit path rather than a db-level optimistic loop.
Rana Patel: Implemented in-reconciler commit mutex with exponential backoff and added a test simulating concurrent bundles. CI run green afterwards.
QA Bot: regression/workflow triggered; results pending; reran after fixes.
Added: deterministic manifest reconciler and harmonizer that generates changelog fragments and attaches performance profiles. Migration: model_manifest_v2 schema introduced with two-week backward-compatible ingestion for v1. Ops: new metrics registry.harmonizer.delta_count, registry.harmonizer.conflict_rate, registry.harmonizer.profile_attach_success, registry.harmonizer.rejected_manifest_count. Developer notes: feature gated for staged rollout; CLI shim included for v1 users.

Context: We need stronger, compact provenance markers for newly onboarded models to improve changelog linking and targeted rollbacks. This PR introduces an exemplar-weighted signature for model metadata plus a small change to the release notes generator so that changelog entries include reader-friendly anchor links back to the model intake metadata and sample exemplars. Motivation: reduce ambiguity when multiple variants are onboarded in quick succession, make human and programmatic review of changes easier, and allow the console/CLI to deep-link into a specific exemplar that was used to generate the performance profile.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds exemplar_weighted_signature to the model intake manifest (compact 8-byte base64-URL safe signature derived from stable metadata + sampled exemplar hashes).
- Stamps the performance profile payload with the signature and a concise human label (e.g., "sig:wk7P3rA4,exemplar:short-uuid").
- Extends the changelog assembly pipeline to emit reader_links: a short URL fragment that the Console/Docs can translate to in-product anchors.
- Adds a lightweight verifier used during on-prem private installs to assert manifest integrity before accepting a model upload.
- Adds unit and small integration tests for signature generation and changelog-link rendering.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc: ENG-3214 (linked)
- [x] Implementation of signature generator and stamp in intake service
- [x] Release-note hook for reader_links in the changelog assembler
- [x] Tests (unit + integration in harness)
- [x] Console/Docs small mapping hook (UI change tracked separately)

Commits (high-level):
- feat(intake): compute exemplar_weighted_signature from manifest + exemplar hashes
- perf(profile): attach signature to profile payload and compact label formatter
- feat(changelog): add reader_link generation and embed anchor snippet in note body
- chore(tests): add deterministic test vectors for signature and link rendering
- fix(installer): tolerate legacy manifests without signature (backcompat shim)

Files/areas changed (high level):
- services/intake/src/signature.py (new)
- services/intake/tests/test_signature_vectors.py
- services/profile/serializer.py (stamp signature onto profile)
- services/changelog/assembler.py (reader_link generation)
- installer/onprem/validator.py (light verifier shim)
- docs/onboarding/anchors.md (doc brief for Console integration)

Backward compatibility: Manifests without the new field are still accepted. The verifier is opt-in via a config flag (onprem.require_signature=false by default) to avoid forcing immediate private installs to re-onboard. Changelog assembler will fall back to legacy anchors when signature missing.

Review notes / decisions:
- Signature is intentionally short (8 bytes -> base64url) to keep changelog and dashboard displays concise; threat model reviewed with Security (no secret derived from user data).
- Exemplar sampling uses deterministic reservoir seed derived from manifest timestamp to ensure repeatability across retries.

Review conversation (abridged):
- Ibrahim Noor: "Can we get a clearer migration path for older manifests? I don't want onprem customers to fail during upgrades."
  - Maya: "Added a config flag and fallback path; installer will log warnings and suggest re-ingest. See installer/onprem/validator.py shim."
- Sofia Patel: "Add a unit test that proves two different exemplar sets produce different signatures but identical manifests with same exemplars are stable."
  - Maya: "Added deterministic test vectors and CI check to guard regressions."
- Evan Ruiz: "Will the short signature collide often for high-volume model churn?"
  - Maya: "Collision analysis attached in ENG-3214, probability < 1e-12 per day at current onboarding rates; we also append a short exemplar id when collisions are detected at ingest time."

CI: Full pipeline passed after second iteration (flake fixes + added test vectors). Checks: lint ✅, unit tests ✅, integration (harness small subset) ✅, e2e staging smoke ✅.

Performance: negligible impact to intake latency (measured median +1.2 ms in a synthetic microbenchmark, 95th +2.8 ms). Signed profiles are ~48 bytes larger on average; changelog entries gain a ~32 char reader_link.

Release notes / user-facing impact: reader_links appear in the autogenerated changelog and Console will deep-link to the model intake page anchored at the exemplar. On-prem installs can opt into strict verification to enforce signed manifests.

Follow-ups (tracked separately):
- Console UX for clickable reader_links and anchor preview (PM-78)
- Rollout plan for enabling onprem.require_signature by default after 60d monitoring
- Add telemetry for reader_link clicks to aid debugging

Merge: Squash-merged after approvals from reviewers and CI green.

Sofia Patel: add stability tests for signature determinism -> added test vectors
Evan Ruiz: collision risk? -> collision analysis in ENG-3214, mitigation appended

payload.body:
This PR implements a second iteration of the cohort bundler with deterministic compaction rules and a separate lightweight onboarding probe. Motivation: we need compact, stable cohort bundles for routing heuristics and for producing concise changelog fragments tied to cohorts. The probe helps detect missing metadata and large deviations in median latency early in the onboarding flow. Changes include a new deterministic compaction step that merges small shard profiles into stable cohort groups based on workload fingerprinting and hardware affinity. The bundler emits a compact manifest with cohort_id, hardware_tier, representative_prompt_hashes, and a compact performance summary. The onboarding probe is a small runner that executes a sampled prompt set against a generated bundle, validates required metadata fields, checks median and p95 latency against configured thresholds, and emits a probe_report.json and a short human summary string for the console. Both components are opt-in behind a feature flag named enable_cohort_bundles. The PR adds unit tests covering compaction edge cases, an integration smoke test that runs the bundler and probe on a synthetic fixture, a docs page describing the bundle manifest and operational playbook, and a simple release-note hook that generates a skeleton changelog entry when new cohorts are published. CI initially failed due to a flaky sleep in the probe test; the test was adjusted to use a percentile-based assertion and the pipeline was retriggered. Reviewers asked for a max_bundle_size guard and a stable manifest version field; both were added. Rollout plan: enable in staging for 72 hours, inspect probe reports and routing deltas, then progressively enable for 1% of production routing decisions. Follow-ups: ENG-4120 to surface probe summaries in the onboarding UI, ENG-4211 to add bundle compaction telemetry, ENG-4289 to add a manual recompact CLI. Risk mitigations: raw profile shards are retained so teams can pin routes to raw profiles; probe runs asynchronously by default and blocks rollout only on critical failures. Merge: squash-merged to main on 2024-12-13 after approvals and green CI.
Adds deterministic cohort compaction algorithm for bundle size control; introduces a lightweight onboarding probe that validates profile completeness and basic latency/throughput guards; auto-drafts a short release-note fragment when a cohort bundle is produced; feature flag gated.
If you need to reproduce the integration test locally run: tox -e registry-integration -- tests/fixtures/cohort_synthetic.json. The new manifest is versioned as v0.2 and includes sample_stats.summary_median and sample_stats.p95 fields.

Motivation: onboarding churn and long, noisy changelogs make it hard for integrators to understand behavioral impact of new model variants. This PR introduces two complementary features: (1) correlated profile snapshots — a compact, sample-preserving snapshot format that records temporal baselines, representative probe samples, and profile correlation hashes; and (2) prose annotator — a lightweight, constrained natural-language composer that generates a 2-4 line human-reviewable release snippet describing key deltas (latency, throughput, accuracy markers, sample regressions) for use in automated release notes.

Summary of changes: implemented snapshot producer and consumer hooks, storage schema migration helpers, a small deterministic summarizer (prose annotator) with templates and safety clamps, and a reviewer workflow to accept/adjust generated snippets. The snapshot format is intentionally stable and content-addressed (profile-hash) so downstream tooling can reference specific baselines without large artifacts.

Design details: snapshot format groups probes into temporal buckets (recent/rolling-7/anchor) and keeps per-probe metadata: token distribution, seed-hash, probe-sig, and confidence bands. A correlation matrix (sparse) is emitted to help detect workload-preserving vs. semantic drift. The prose annotator uses rule-driven templates combined with a small transformer-based scorer (quantized) to pick candidate phrasing; all output goes through a lint step that enforces length, non-specificity of PII, and conservative normative language (avoid claims like "better" without metrics).

Migration: a migration utility converts existing profile records into the snapshot envelope; migration is opt-in per-namespace and runs as a background job with a throttled worker. Storage uses existing blobstore with a small index to map profile-hash -> snapshot metadata.

Rollout plan: staged rollout to the registry UI and onboarding API. Initially the prose annotator is enabled as "suggest" mode for 100% of internal model uploads and 20% of external uploads (canary by account label). After 2 weeks of feedback and fixes, it will be promoted to default suggestion for all onboard flows.

Testing and validation: unit tests for serializer/deserializer, end-to-end test that registers a snapshot and renders the suggested snippet, fuzz tests for snapshot ingestion, and a small manual review study (20 samples) to validate snippet usefulness.

Checklist:
- [x] snapshot schema, producer, and consumer
- [x] migration helper and background job scaffolding
- [x] prose annotator with template library and scorer
- [x] UI hook for reviewer to accept/edit snippet
- [x] telemetry (accept rate, edit rate, average snippet length)
- [x] docs + migration guide

Risks and mitigations: risk of overconfident prose or leaking training data; mitigated by strict template constraints, PII linter, and human-in-the-loop gating. Snapshot size growth mitigated by sample-preserving approach and retention policy (default 90 days, configurable).
Arjun Patel (reviewer): The correlation matrix looks useful, but I'm worried about size for large probe sets — can we make it sparse by default?
Maya Chen (author): Good call — implemented sparse encoding and added a compression knob. See commit c3d4e5f.
Li Wei (reviewer): The prose templates read well but sometimes imply improvements without numbers. Please add explicit metric placeholders or 'no significant change' fallback.
Maya Chen (author): Added fallback phrasing and enforced numeric placeholders where appropriate. Updated templates in prose_templates.py.
Riley Thompson (reviewer): We should ensure migration is opt-in for enterprise namespaces to avoid unexpected storage costs.
Maya Chen (author): Migration is opt-in and defaulted off for enterprise namespaces; clarified in migration docs and added a feature flag.
Arjun Patel (approver): LGTM after minor nits fixed. Approved.
Introduce compact, correlated profile snapshots (temporal bucketing + sample-preserving probes) and an automated prose annotator that drafts concise release snippets for model onboardings. Migration helper included (opt-in). Adds reviewer UI and telemetry for suggestion acceptance. Default retention: 90 days.
Enable migration worker via helm flag registry.snapshotMigration.enabled=false by default. If enabling, monitor registry.blobstore.* metrics and ensure worker concurrency <= 4 for initial runs.

Add a lightweight intake categorizer and an automated condensed release-brief autofill used during model onboarding. Motivation: reduce manual tag curation and accelerate release note drafts by surfacing telemetry-driven quality signals (latency drift, top failing prompts, sample perplexity deltas) and provenance links to sample traces. This PR provides a small rule-engine that weights telemetry signals, returns optional coarse-grained category tags in the intake API, injects provenance URIs for flagged samples, and generates a concise release brief template consumed by the onboarding UI and release-assembler. Includes a DB migration for category enums, unit and integration tests, doc samples, and CI adjustments. Backwards compatibility: categorizer returns optional metadata only; existing flows fall back to manual tags. No user-facing breaking changes expected. Request reviewers to validate telemetry weights and UX copy for the brief template. Related: onboarding-ui PR to consume /intake/brief endpoint and release-assembler hook (separate).

payload.body:
Context: In practice, a significant fraction of inbound model uploads omit non-required intake fields (hardware_affinity, seq_distribution, licensing). That reduces the registry's ability to generate useful performance profiles and automated rollout recommendations. This PR introduces a lightweight, schema-driven metadata enricher and a companion variant probe seeder to produce initial performance seeds for downstream tooling.

What this PR does:
- Adds a schema-driven enricher that inspects uploaded manifests and artifact contents (model weights, tokenizer artifacts, config blobs) and auto-populates conservative but useful defaults plus provenance tags. The enricher writes a `registry_metadata` annex that downstream services can opt into.
- Introduces a variant probe seeder that schedules short, bounded probe jobs (sampled sequences, cold/warm KV cache runs, single/generic batch sizes) for each model variant to generate a small performance sample used to create an initial PerformanceProfile. These probes are intentionally low-cost (<= 30s) and asynchronous.
- Adds an autogen release-note stub generator that consumes probe outputs to create a short performance blurb (median latency, 95th, tokens/sec) and includes it in the onboard review checklist.

Motivation: The goal is to make onboarding higher fidelity without asking model authors to provide more manual metadata. Seeded perf profiles improve Recommend/Optimize suggestions (quantization/batching) and reduce iteration between teams.

Implementation notes:
- The enricher is implemented as `onboard/enricher.py` (pluggable pipeline stage); schema lives in `schemas/model_intake_schema.yaml`. Enrichment rules are conservative and non-destructive: we only fill missing fields and attach `provenance.enricher=v1` to the metadata.
- Probe seeder lives in `onboard/probe_seeder.py` and uses the existing lightweight harness (new `harness/probe_runner` module) to run short jobs. Probe results are stored under `perf_seeds/<model_id>/<variant>/seed.json`.
- Release-note autogen templates are under `docs/onboarding/release_blurb_templates.md` and produce a single-line blurb attached to the model intake as `autoblurb.v1`.

Checklist:
- [x] Add enricher pipeline stage and schema
- [x] Add probe seeder and lightweight harness integration
- [x] Unit tests for enrichment heuristics and probe result parsing
- [x] Integration test that runs seeder in CI matrix (short mode)
- [x] Docs and onboarding guide updates
- [x] Migration/rollback plan included

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests added under `tests/test_enricher.py` and `tests/test_probe_seeder.py` (fast, deterministic).
- Integration matrix includes a short-run probe job (runs under 45s in CI). To reduce flakiness, probe runner uses a local deterministic RNG seed and a small synthetic input.

Rollout plan:
- Canary: enable enricher+seeder for 10% of new onboard jobs (flagged) and monitor ingestion error rate + probe failure rate for 48h.
- Full rollout: after successful canary, enable for all new onboards. Existing models will be backfilled via a one-off worker (`tools/backfill_perf_seeds`) that will be run by platform infra during the agreed maintenance window.

Migration notes:
- The enricher appends `registry_metadata` only when fields are missing; existing metadata remains unchanged. Backfill is optional but recommended to seed older models.

Security/privacy notes:
- Probe payloads are synthetic and do not include customer data. Probe jobs run in the same sandbox as existing tests and respect per-tenant isolation.

Related: ENG-8113 (schema-driven metadata); PM-293 (onboard UX for perf seeds).

Adds automated metadata enrichment during model intake and seeds per-variant probe profiles for performance baselines. Introduces no public API changes; runtime and Optimize will consume new artifacts.
Aaron Cole (2025-01-16): Nice direction. Two requests: 1) add an opt-out flag at intake level so customers can disable probes, 2) we need a migration plan for existing models (backfill cost estimates).
Sofia Martinez (2025-01-16): Added opt-out flag (onboard.enrich.disable_probes) and included a backfill tool + cost estimate in PR description. Backfill is optional and rate-limited. Thanks!
Liang Zhao (2025-01-17): Probe runner looks good but CI had a flake on the integration run. Can we use a deterministic seed for the synthetic inputs?
Sofia Martinez (2025-01-17): Updated probe_runner to accept RNG seed via env var and wired CI to use a fixed seed. Reran integration matrix.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: We onboard models from a variety of sources (author-uploaded manifests, CI-provided metadata, and discovery probes). Discrepancies between sources (missing fields, differing perf metrics, variant aliases) have caused noisy changelogs and occasional release regressions. This PR implements a deterministic "consensus rollup" step during intake that: 1) canonicalizes manifest keys and field formats; 2) merges performance profile vectors using a configurable aggregator (weighted median by signal confidence); 3) records provenance for each field so downstream systems can explain where a value came from; and 4) emits a concise, reader-friendly changelog "teaser" that groups changes into: metadata edits, perf deltas, and variant-level lifecycle events.

What changed (high level):
- New consensus rollup service (registry/rollup) that takes a set of manifests and returns a single canonical manifest plus a changelog fragment.
- Aggregator implementations: weighted_median (default) and fallback_mean (opt-in).
- Field provenance map: compact provenance stamps stored alongside canonical fields for traceability.
- Changelog formatter (registry/changelog/teaser) that outputs a short prose summary plus machine tags for UI tooling.
- Intake pipeline wiring: the onboarding task now calls rollup before persisting model versions.
- Tests: unit tests for canonicalization rules, aggregator edge cases, and an end-to-end integration test that runs a small sample intake and asserts changelog shape.

Commits (summary):
- 8a7b2c1: add consensus rollup service and initial aggregator APIs
- 7f92d4e: implement weighted_median aggregator and provenance stamps
- f03bd9a: changelog teaser formatter and grouping rules
- c4a1b2e: hook rollup into intake task; add integration test harness
- d2f4e51: docs: onboarding guide updates and examples
- 1b8fa6c: fix: handle variant alias collisions; add extra unit tests

Files touched (high level):
- registry/rollup/service.py (new)
- registry/rollup/aggregators.py (new)
- registry/changelog/teaser.py (new)
- registry/intake/handler.py (modified)
- tests/registry/test_rollup.py (new)
- tests/registry/integration_test_sample_intake.py (new)
- docs/registry/onboarding.md (modified)

Review conversation (high-level excerpt):
- Ben Carter: "Great direction. Please clarify the conflict-resolution priority list in the docs and add a test for missing confidence scores." (requested changes)
- Aisha Patel (author): "Added explicit priority table to docs and added a test that defaults missing confidence to 0.4. Also documented how to opt into fallback_mean." (addressed)
- Lina Morales: "Can we guarantee aggregator determinism across Python versions? Consider sorting keys before aggregation." (comment)
- Aisha Patel: "Added key sorting and a deterministic float reduction step; included a note and added a regression test: tests/registry/test_rollup.py::test_aggregator_determinism." (addressed)

CI summary: Initial run showed one flaky integration test (tests/registry/integration_test_sample_intake.py::test_end_to_end) failing on timeout in the mock persistence layer. I reran the job; subsequent run passed. All checks reported green: lint, unit tests, integration, and build. Coverage slightly decreased in an unrelated helper module (acceptable per ENG-1934).

Backward compatibility and risk: No user-facing API changes. The canonical manifest schema was minimally extended with an optional provenance map; schema validations accept the new optional field. Intake path is feature-flagged on rollout; default enabled for new onboardings. The rollup introduces deterministic merging rules to reduce churn in release notes and should decrease noise. If a downstream system depends on specific field values from a single source, we document how to opt-out and pin source priority.

Testing and validation: Unit tests cover aggregator edge cases (empty lists, single-source, conflicting confidences). Integration test runs sample intake with three synthetic manifests and asserts canonical output and a changelog fragment with expected grouped headings. Perf: aggregator runs in ~3–7ms for typical manifests (measured in CI microbenchmark script). Added alerts if rollup latency exceeds 200ms in production.

Docs and examples: docs/registry/onboarding.md updated with a short example showing input manifests and resulting teaser. Added scripts/sample_manifests to allow reproducing the integration test locally.

Notes for release engineers: There is a small database migration to add the optional provenance column (backfilled as NULL). Migration script included: db/migrations/20260302_add_provenance_column.sql. Rollback is safe (column optional).

Summary: Adds metadata fields and tooling for recording model intake source attribution (uploader, dataset origin, manifest-hash) and a sampled-microprofile generator that emits compact latency/signature snippets used by the changelog automation pipeline. Motivation: onboarding often lacked clear provenance and the release automation team had to handcraft perf blurbs from large telemetry dumps. This PR attaches deterministic source attributes at ingest time and computes a small representative latency signature (p50/p95/p99, warm/cold breakdown, exemplar prompts) that can be embedded into changelog fragments and model profiles.

What this changes (high level):
- Schema: extends OnboardManifest with source_attribution {uploader, source_uri, manifest_hash, ingestion_epoch, tag} and provenance_hint (string).
- Microprofile generator: new service that consumes sampled telemetry (from telemetry-ingest -> sample-batcher) and outputs a normalized latency-signature snippet; snippets are small JSON lines stored in /profiles/snippets/ and referenced by model profile records.
- Release note integration: changelog-assembler now consumes snippets and produces a one-line perf blurb template; includes a minimal example for human review.
- Backwards compatibility: new fields default to null; older manifests continue to work and a filler job backfills manifest_hash when available.
- Tests & CI: unit tests for schema migration, snippet normalization, and a lightweight e2e using a synthetic telemetry fixture.

Commits (summary):
- a1b2c3d: introduce source_attribution fields and migration hooks
- b2c3d4e: implement sampled-microprofile generator and normalization rules
- c3d4e5f: wire snippets into changelog-assembler and add templating example
- d4e5f6a: add unit/e2e tests and fixture data; address linting

Files/areas touched (representative):
- src/onboard/schema.py (add new fields, migration helpers)
- src/onboard/ingest.py (populate source_attribution at upload time)
- tools/microprofile-generator/service.py (new)
- tools/microprofile-generator/normalizer.py (new)
- services/changelog/assembler.py (consume snippets)
- tests/onboard/test_migration.py, tests/microprofile/test_normalizer.py, tests/changelog/test_integration.py
- docs/model-onboard/attrs.md (document new attributes)
- infra/db/migrations/2026_02_18_add_source_attribution.sql

Design notes and heuristics:
- Sampling policy: prefer recent production traffic up to 10k requests per model-version over a rolling 24h window, weight by route traffic so low-traffic models still get representative examples.
- Latency signature buckets: warm vs cold separation by cache-hit heuristics; output p50/p95/p99 and a small exemplar set (3 prompts) that produced each bucket's p95.
- Manifest hash: we compute compact sha256:base16 and persist as manifest_hash; used for quick provenance lookup and cross-referencing in audit exports.
- Privacy: exemplar prompts are redacted if they match configured PII patterns; redaction is pluggable and documented.

Review thread (abbreviated):
- Ethan: "Nice addition for provenance. Two asks: (1) make migration non-blocking for large registries, (2) better error handling when sample stream is empty."
- Priya: "Migration runs as async background job; added a non-blocking flag and a short-circuit if sample stream is empty. See commit d4e5f6a."
- Maya: "Can we ensure changelog snippets have a max char budget? We show them in the Console UI and need truncation."
- Priya: "Added truncation at 1KB and a suffix tag to indicate truncation — tests updated."
- Noah: "Unit tests look good; e2e fixture failed once in CI due to a timing flake."
- Priya: "Fixed the timing flake by switching the fixture to deterministic timestamps and added retry in the e2e harness."
- Final: Approved by Maya and Noah after fixes; Ethan approved with a follow-up to monitor backfill load (linked to ENG-6123).

CI & test summary: initial CI run: failed on e2e (timing flake); subsequent run: all checks pass (unit, lint, mypy, integration-lite). CI artifacts attached: test-log.txt, coverage/report.html.

Backward compatibility & rollout plan:
- Step 1 (0-24h): merge to main behind feature flag (onboard.source_attribution.enabled=false).
- Step 2 (24-72h): enable flag for canary orgs, monitor backfill and snippet generation CPU.
- Step 3 (7 days): enable globally and kick off controlled backfill for manifests older than 6 months with low-priority worker pool (rate-limited to avoid db spike).
- Follow-ups: ENG-5281 will add a backfill progress dashboard and alert on worker queue depth.

Operational concerns raised:
- Sample generation CPU: microprofile generator is CPU-light but can be I/O bound on telemetry reads; added batching and backpressure and a queue depth metric (microprofile.generator.queue_depth).
- Storage growth: snippets serialized are ~1KB each; retention defaults to 90 days and can be shortened per-tenant — configuration added to docs.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged by Priya Nair. Commit message: "Add source attribution and latency-signature snippets for onboarding (ENG-5281, ENG-6123)". Post-merge: feature flag kept off at merge; rollout tracked under ENG-5281.

Notes for release notes: The changelog automation can now auto-produce concise perf blurbs for model onboarding, and all new model uploads will carry a manifest-level source attribution. This helps traceability and reduces manual work when drafting release notes.

If there's any concern about backfill window or retention defaults, I'll follow up with a quick patch to make defaults configurable via the console.
Introduce source attribution metadata and an automated latency-signature snippet generator to improve onboarding traceability and produce concise release note fragments for model version rollouts.

Motivation: onboarding diverse model bundles from ecosystem partners often requires custom glue to translate external metadata and release artifacts into our canonical model registry format. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) an "ambassador" onboarding bridge that accepts partner bundles (compressed tar/zip with metadata.yaml, model weights, evaluation tokens), applies a lightweight normalization and validation pipeline, and emits a canonical onboarding manifest; and (2) a compact release serializer used by the registry to produce small changelog artifacts and delta bundles suitable for infra transfer, signing, and downstream consumption.

Design and scope: the ambassador bridge is implemented as a small service/cli that performs schema mapping (field remaps + optional heuristics for missing fields), provenance annotation (source, checksum, declared license), and a gentle compatibility fallback (attempts to map unknown tokenizer or architecture strings to closest known types). The compact serializer produces a deterministic, minimal changelog entry (profile diffs, numeric performance anchors, artifact fingerprints) and a signed manifest blob (for later verification during automated rollouts). This PR stops short of adding long-term storage hooks or signed kms integration — those follow-ups are tracked in ENG-4990.

What changed (high level): added an ambassador module under packages/ambassador-onboard, a serializer module under packages/release-serializer, adapters for three common partner bundle shapes (hf-snapshot, tarball-with-metadata, legacy-s3-layout), unit and integration tests that exercise round-trip onboarding and changelog generation, and CI workflows to lint and run fast integration tests. Also added docs/examples/ambassador-quickstart.md and a small migration helper script scripts/compactize-existing-changelogs.py.

Checklist: - [x] Schema mapping and validation logic - [x] Compact changelog format and serializer - [x] Adapters for hf-snapshot, tarball, legacy-s3 - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Docs + quickstart - [x] Linear tickets linked

Notes on compatibility and risk: the ambassador applies non-destructive transformations by default and annotates any inferred fields so downstream reviewers can audit choices. The serializer changes the shape of release artifacts that consumer tooling expects; to reduce risk we ship the serializer in parallel with the existing, verbose changelog writer and both are produced for two release cycles. Consumer migration is coordinated in PM-833.

Testing and CI: CI adds a new workflow (ci/ambassador-integration) which runs lightweight partner-bundle fixtures inside a containerized environment. On first run the integration suite flaked due to a race when calculating file checksums; fixed by adding deterministic file ordering in the serializer. Current CI status: all checks passing (unit, lint, integration).

Rollout plan: 1) Merge feature behind a feature flag registry.enable_ambassador_bridge = false 2) Run ambassador against a subset of internal partner bundles and compare produced manifests in the dev staging bucket 3) Flip the feature flag for onboarding-infra teams for one week to collect feedback 4) Deprecate verbose changelog after two successful cycles.

Related: ENG-4921 (onboard bridge design), PM-833 (partner onboarding roadmap), ENG-4990 (KMS signing follow-up).

Add ambassador onboarding bridge to normalize partner bundles and a compact changelog serializer that emits deterministic, signed-ready release manifests. Backwards compatible (both compact and verbose changelogs produced for two cycles).
Feature gated behind registry.enable_ambassador_bridge = false. Run scripts/compactize-existing-changelogs.py to produce compact blobs for historical releases if ops want to backfill. Monitor churn on registry.changelog_produced metric after flag flip.

Motivation: reduce manual friction when adding new models to the registry by automatically producing a standardized performance profile and an entry in the release changelog. Context and motivation: Our current model intake pipeline produces inconsistent metadata rollups and noisy release notes when multiple minor metadata edits happen across parallel commits. This causes downstream consumers (release digest, release inspector UI, and SDK onboarding docs) to show flickering or duplicate entries. This PR introduces two coordinated features: (1) an intake guardrail that enforces a deterministic, idempotent metadata normalization and compacting step during model onboarding; and (2) a 'release embosser' service that synthesizes concise human-friendly changelog snippets from the compacted deltas, annotated with confidence tags and rollback hints. Implementation summary: - Intake guardrail: a new ingestion middleware (pkg/ingest/guardrail) that validates required fields, canonicalizes aliases (model_name/model_alias), collapses repeated key edits into a single canonical delta, and computes a stable fingerprint (sha256 hex) for the resulting metadata bundle. The guardrail runs both as a pre-commit hook for manual onboard flows and as a post-ingest transaction in the async intake worker. It emits structured validation warnings to telemetry and returns a stable 'ingest_id' to the caller. - Deterministic rollups: added deterministic delta-merging logic (pkg/registry/rollup) that merges multiple edits by ordering them by (timestamp, author_id, edit_type_priority) and applying a deterministic compositing function so the same set of edits always yields the same rollup. We also added compatibility heuristics for variant aliases and quantization hints. - Release embosser: a standalone small service (tools/release-embosser) that consumes rollup deltas and produces human-readable blurb candidates for release notes. Embosser outputs: short title (one line), 1-3 bullet summary lines, confidence level (high/medium/low), and an optional revert command for ops. The embosser includes templated examples for model performance profile changes, metadata-only edits, and variant promotions. - Tests and tooling: added unit tests for the normalization rules, property-based tests for the deterministic rollup function, a lightweight e2e harness that simulates concurrent onboard edits (tests/e2e/intake_race_test.go), and a Linters/CI addition to run the embosser smoke example during PR checks. Related work and docs: references ENG-4821 (intake stabilization epic) and design doc: /docs/designs/intake-guardrail.md. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag (intake.guardrail.enabled) and embosser.enabled; default OFF for 48 hours while monitoring telemetry. Migration notes: legacy metadata blobs are reprocessed via a backfill job (tools/backfill/compactify) — backfill included in this PR as a dry-run mode only. Single-line checklist: - [x] Add guardrail middleware and deterministic rollup - [x] Add release embosser service and templates - [x] Unit/property/e2e tests - [x] Feature flags, telemetry hooks, dry-run backfill - [x] Docs and developer guide entries (docs/onboard/guardrail.md)
Miguel Alvarez: Can we avoid an extra copy of the metadata blob in memory when computing the fingerprint? Suggest streaming the normalization to reduce peak RSS.
Clara Nguyen (author): Good call — updated guardrail.go to stream-normalize and compute incremental SHA; see latest commit d1f3a2b for changes.
Priya Shah: Need to add a migration safety gate — if backfill.dry_run=false the job must be restricted to an ops-only role. Please add RBAC and a dry-run flag check.
Clara Nguyen (author): Added RBAC check and an ops-only feature flag; backfill will refuse non-ops execution and logs a preflight summary.
Evan Brooks: The property tests look flakey on mac builders — pin the random seed in the CI job to avoid non-deterministic failures.
Clara Nguyen (author): Pinned seed and added re-run on CI for the property suite; CI green locally and on linux builders.
Priya Shah (approved): Coding and safety review complete; suggest follow-up to add more embosser templates for perf regressions.
- Added an intake guardrail that enforces canonicalized metadata, computes a stable ingest fingerprint, and reduces noisy rollup churn.
- Deterministic rollups ensure identical edit sets yield identical compacted metadata (reduces UI flicker and duplicate release entries).
- Release embosser produces concise, annotated changelog snippets (title, bullets, confidence, rollback hints) to populate release digests and SDK onboarding notes.
- Backfill dry-run included; ops-only gate required for real backfill.
- Feature flags: intake.guardrail.enabled, tools.embosser.enabled (default off).
This PR introduces backend behavior changes to onboarding. Keep feature flags off for the first 48 hours after deploy to monitor ingest/telemetry. Run backfill in dry-run and review preflight before enabling. Notify docs and SDK teams to expect more compact release snippets in the digest feed.
Enable feature flags after 48h of telemetry OK
Schedule ops-only backfill during maintenance window if dry-run output validated
Add embosser templates for perf regression in follow-up PR (ENG-5127)

Summary: This PR extends the model registry schema to represent quantized serving variants (FP8 and INT8) alongside existing baseline variants, and adds placeholders for a default-selection policy that is controlled by server-side flags.

Motivation: As part of the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint, we need a place to (a) register which models have quantized artifacts available per GPU family, and (b) express default eligibility without hard-coding a product decision in the registry. Runtime will use server-side flags + heuristics for rollout; the registry should only provide structured metadata (available variants, constraints, and safety guardrails).

What’s included: - Adds `quantization_mode` to variant records (`bf16`, `fp16`, `fp8`, `int8`) and a `variant_family` grouping to keep the catalog tidy. - Adds `availability` and `constraints` fields for quantized variants (supported gpu_arch list, min_cuda, known shape caveats, and “requires_calibration” semantics for INT8). - Adds `default_policy_stub` fields (no behavior change): `eligible_by_default` remains false for fp8/int8 variants, but can be overridden by server-side flags (runtime/control-plane). The stub exists so we can attach notes and per-model guardrails (e.g. “requires eval sign-off for long-context”). - Adds validation + tests for schema correctness and backwards compatibility with older consumers (unknown fields ignored).

Non-goals: - This PR does not flip any defaults in hosted production. - No registry-driven auto-selection logic is added here; runtime dispatch remains policy owner.

Rollout/compatibility: - Backwards compatible: existing baseline variant IDs are unchanged. - New fields are additive. - Consumers that deserialize strictly will need to update (runtime already tolerates unknown keys; console uses a permissive parser).

Testing: - Unit tests for schema validation and fixture decoding. - Golden fixtures updated for top hosted model entries (kept minimal; detailed policy lives in runtime flags/ADR).

Follow-ups: - After benchmarks + eval sign-off, we will populate model-specific constraints more fully and add a registry linter rule to prevent enabling fp8/int8 without required guardrails (tracked in ENG-7421).
Jonas Weber (review): Can we make sure we don’t imply “default FP8/INT8” anywhere in the registry? I want the eval sign-off criteria to remain the gate, and runtime flags to be the mechanism.

Arjun Desai (author): Agree. I’ve set `eligible_by_default=false` for all fp8/int8 variants and renamed the field group to `default_policy_stub` to make it explicit this is not an active policy engine. Added doc text: “server-side flags are policy owner; registry is metadata only.”

Claire Dubois (review): Please add a note about measurement/claim hygiene: if we expose these variants in any UI later, we’ll need the benchmarking methodology footnotes. Can we attach a freeform field for “benchmark_notes” without hard-typing it yet?

Arjun Desai (author): Added `notes` under the variant record, with a convention that this is internal-only and may include “benchmark footnotes required.” Kept it optional and unvalidated beyond type.

Yuki Sato (review): For runtime heuristics we’ll need to know supported GPU arch per variant. Your `availability.supported_gpu_arch` is good, but can we also include a min driver/CUDA constraint? We’ve seen mismatches across clusters.

Arjun Desai (author): Added `availability.min_cuda` (string) and `availability.min_driver` (string). Validator enforces they exist for fp8/int8 variants.

Rina Kobayashi (review): Requesting a small fixture: one model with both fp8 and int8 entries + a “known bad shape” caveat so we can test consumer logic.

Arjun Desai (author): Added fixture example and a validation test ensuring `constraints.known_caveats` is permitted and preserved.

Jonas Weber (final): LGTM. Please ensure docs mention that any quality gating/evals live outside the registry (Applied ML sign-off).

Arjun Desai (author): Done; updated docs/registry_fields.md with an explicit callout + link placeholder to internal policy doc (to be wired in follow-up).
Internal-only: Registry now supports FP8/INT8 variant metadata and policy stubs for server-flag controlled defaults. No production default changes.

Motivation: onboarding teams currently hand-author model release notes and pick variant names independently from runtime signal characteristics. This PR introduces a lightweight signal-led onboarding flow that (1) fingerprints hardware affinity and runtime performance from sampled production traces, (2) generates a canonical alias map for model variants tied to provenance and quantization knobs, and (3) seeds concise, telemetry-driven release briefs (auto-briefs) that summarize expected throughput/latency/quality tradeoffs. Design summary: the feature adds a sampling shim in the runtime ingestion path that emits anonymized micro-traces to the registry CLI; a new registry service component (affinity fingerprint store) computes compact affinity signatures and associates them with model uploads; a variant-canonicalizer layer resolves incoming variant aliases into stable canonical IDs and records provenance metadata for rollbacks; finally an autobrief generator produces a short structured paragraph and a one-line changelog entry using sampled percentile metrics and a templated blurb engine. This PR implements the end-to-end pipeline, a CLI hook (redwood-registry onboard --seed-sample), a lightweight validation step for alias collisions, and a UI metadata field for the Console to display the generated brief. Checklist: [x] sampling shim + telemetry contract defined [x] affinity fingerprint compute + persistence implemented [x] alias canonicalizer + collision tests implemented [x] autobrief generator with templated summaries [x] CLI hook and CI e2e smoke [x] unit tests and linters passing after fix. Backwards compatibility: variant aliasing is opt-in for existing onboarding flows via a flag; canonical IDs are additive and do not change prior model IDs. Security/PII: sampling emits only aggregate timing/shape metrics and truncated cache-key hashes; no user prompt text leaves the registry. Rollout plan: 1) enable sampling at 1% for internal canaries, 2) run offline reconciliation for 48 hours, 3) turn on autobrief drafts in Console as reviewable until a model owner approves, 4) enable automated brief publishing for models on the digital-signing allowlist. Related Linear: ENG-1462 (onboard telemetry contract), PM-921 (autobrief UX rubric). Why different: unlike previous changelog automation, this ties release notes to observed runtime signal distributions and hardware affinity so engineers get a preview of how variants behave in target fleets. Known limitations: affinity fingerprint convergence may need >100 samples for tail percentiles; autobrief phrasing is intentionally conservative and includes an explicit confidence band.
Carlos Vega: Nice end-to-end, left nits on naming and one edge-case for alias collision when two uploads have identical provenance hashes | Maya Thompson: Thanks Carlos, addressed the naming nits and added a deterministic tie-breaker in alias_canonicalizer.go
Priya Nair: Can we confirm no raw prompt text is ever sent to the registry? Also request a short e2e for the Console display path | Maya Thompson: Confirmed, sampling emits only non-text aggregates; added test test_autobrief_integration.py that validates Console metadata rendering
Ethan Liu: CI failed on linting in the first run, re-run looks green; consider rate-limiting the sampling shim to avoid noise on high-throughput ingress | Maya Thompson: Added rate limiter with exponential backoff as a CLI-configurable parameter; documented default 1% sampling

payload.body:
Context & motivation:
Onboard metadata churn has been a recurring source of noisy release notes and spurious changelog entries in the model registry. Small edits in ancillary fields (uploader notes, transient tags) caused the current changelog synthesizer to emit high-volume, low-signal entries and made reviewers ignore release briefs. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) delta-assertor, a deterministic change classifier that normalizes and scores diffs between model profile versions; (2) release-signature-compiler, a post-assertor job that composes changelog snippets from signed deltas and attaches a confidence and why-summary for reviewers and the auto-release flow.

What this PR delivers:
- delta-assertor: a lightweight library + CLI that consumes two profile JSONs and emits a signed delta artifact containing: semantic change category (schema, weights, perf, docs), normalized field-level diffs, a delta fingerprint, and a compact human-readable rationale. Determinism ensured via canonical JSON canonicalization and stable hashing.
- release-signature-compiler: a pipeline step that consumes signed deltas and renders one-line and paragraph release blurb candidates with confidence scores and optional automated release-note drafts. Integrates with the existing release-drafter flow and can be toggled per-collection.
- Opt-in onboarding flag: `onboard --assert-delta` to produce signed delta artifacts during intake so that downstream reviewers and CI can gate on meaningful deltas.
- Tests: unit tests for diff heuristics, integration tests in the fixture registry, and an end-to-end smoke test that simulates a model metadata bump and ensures only meaningful deltas trigger release blurb generation.
- Docs: docs/registry/delta-assertor.md with developer notes and operational guidance, and a short playbook for handling low-confidence deltas.

Checklist:
- [x] delta classification algorithm and canonicalization implemented
- [x] signing scheme and validation hooks added (KMS-backed signing emulation in dev)
- [x] release-compiler templates and confidence heuristics implemented
- [x] unit + integration tests added and passing
- [x] docs and quickstart updated
- [x] migration guide for QA and platform teams

High-level commits (summary):
- commit 1: introduce delta-assertor library, classifiers, and canonicalizer (python)
- commit 2: add onboarding CLI flag and plumbing to intake service to emit delta artifacts
- commit 3: implement release-signature-compiler and templates (go service)
- commit 4: add KMS-signing compatibility layer and test harness
- commit 5: add unit and integration tests + e2e smoke test
- commit 6: docs and examples + changelog generator CI job
- commit 7: minor fixes from review (stability/timeout tuning)

Files/areas changed (high level):
- services/intake/src/delta_assertor.py (new)
- services/intake/cli.py (opt-in flag wiring)
- services/release-compiler/main.go (new) and templates/release_templates.yaml
- infra/ci/workflows/e2e-delta.yml (new job)
- docs/registry/delta-assertor.md (new)
- tests/fixtures/model_profiles/*.json (new fixtures)
- tests/integration/test_delta_assertor.py (new)

Review conversation (selected):
- Alex Rivers (reviewer): "Why not reuse the existing change-scorer? The heuristics look similar."
  - Author: "We experimented with the change-scorer; delta-assertor uses canonicalization + field whitelisting and a compact rationale structure which avoids several classes of false positives we saw in prod.   - Author: "Signing is pluggable — default CI uses dev-KMS emulator. The production path supports an external KMS provider; docs include the YAML snippets for binding customer KMS to the signing service. We added validation hooks that will skip signature verification if the tenant opts out (still emits unsigned delta)."

Any delta with perf changes above 5% is flagged for manual review and the compiler will emit a 'candidate' label; only high-confidence deltas (confidence >= 0.85) are eligible for auto-draft inclusion. The test-suite includes synthetic perf deltas to verify behavior."

Backwards compatibility and opt-in nature:
- The new flow is opt-in via CLI flag and collection-level config; default behavior remains unchanged. The release-signature-compiler can be turned on independently and reads existing profile history to synthesize deltas.

Adds a deterministic change classifier (delta-assertor) to reduce noisy churn in model metadata and a release-signature-compiler that compiles signed deltas into concise changelog snippets and confidence scores. Backwards compatible; exposes opt-in CLI flag for early adopters. Includes unit + integration tests and a release-note generation job for the intake pipeline.

Adds an intake lineage resolver and compact release excerpt generator: computes model+dataset provenance, hardware affinity, and automated compact changelog snippets that surface performance/cost impact and suggested mitigations. Includes migration/backfill for existing manifests and a CLI hook for one-off annotations.
Summary: Introduce a lightweight intake-lineage resolver and a compact release-excerptor that automatically synthesizes short changelog snippets from model onboarding metadata and performance deltas. The resolver binds model artifacts (tarball IDs), training-run IDs, dataset manifests, container hashes, and hardware affinity fingerprints into a canonical lineage record. The excerptor uses lineage + profile deltas to draft a concise release blurb (1-3 bullets) highlighting: perf changes, latency/cost delta, likely root cause (data, architecture, quantization), and suggested roll-forward/rollback mitigation.

Motivation: Teams repeatedly ask for a quick, reliable explanation of why a model's on-host performance changed across variants. Creating a machine-readable provenance chain plus an automated "release excerpt" reduces manual triage and speeds safe rollouts.

What this PR does (high level):
  - Adds a new module registry/lineage/resolver with an interface to hydrate lineage from intake payloads or from stored training metadata.
  - Adds schema bump v2 for model_manifest to include optional provenance fields (training_run_id, dataset_manifest_ref, container_hash, hardware_fingerprint).
  - Adds migration script migrations/2026_01_backfill_lineage.py to backfill lineage for recent onboardings (with a dry-run flag).
  - Adds a worker web/hooks/release_excerptor.py that subscribes to profile-change events and emits a compact markdown snippet into the release_notes draft stream.
  - Adds CLI integration rmodel lineage annotate and rmodel release draft to preview excerpts locally.
  - Adds unit/integration tests and docs explaining the new fields and operational guidance.

Implementation details:
  - Lineage resolver: conservative merge strategy: prefer explicit fields from onboarding payload; fallback to training run metadata via training-run-api; attach a provenance hash to manifest (sha256 of canonicalized lineage) so downstream systems can quickly diff.
  - Excerptor heuristics: compares baseline and candidate performance profiles (latency p50/p95, token cost per 1k, quality score delta when available). Uses lightweight rule-based scoring (no ML) to construct 2-3 sentence blurb ranked by impact score. Rules are configurable via registry/config/excerptor.yml.
  - Migration/backfill: script runs in batches, emits a reconciliation report (success/failure per manifest) and tags ambiguous cases for human review (created a new curation queue).
  - Rollout: feature gated behind registry.feature_flags.lineage and excerptor.enabled. Default off for older tenants until migrated.

Test plan:
  - Unit tests for resolver (tests/test_lineage_resolver.py) including canonicalization and hash stability.
  - Integration tests for CLI and worker using small synthetic manifests (tests/integration/test_release_excerptor_integration.py).
  - E2E against a staging event stream to validate excerpt generation and release draft insertion.

Checklist:
  - [x] Schema changes (v2) documented and backwards-compatible when fields are absent.
  - [x] Migration script with dry-run validated on staging.
  - [x] CLI docs and examples added.
  - [x] Tests added + CI green.
  - [x] Feature flags and rollout notes included.

  - 3d4e5f6: bump schema v2 and add examples

  - 4c5b6a7: CLI hooks and docs
  - 9f8e7d6: tests and small bugfixes

Review conversation (high level):

  - Asha (author): "Answered — canonicalization uses json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True) + explicit field whitelist. Added cache TTL config (default 24h) and tests for cross-version stability."
  - Tomás Rivera: "Can we make the excerptor fallback to a 'no-change' blurb if the profile delta is below noise thresholds? We had noise-induced chatter in Canary previously."
  - Asha: "Added a configurable noise floor and a 'no significant change' template; excerptor suppresses drafts below a global threshold unless forced."

Summary: This PR introduces a Release Notes Playbook for the model registry: a small, opinionated engine that converts structured model onboarding metadata and performance-profile deltas into concise, human-readable changelog seeds. The goal is to reduce manual work for release authors and provide consistent impact statements for model rollouts.

Motivation: We routinely see messy hand-authored release notes when models are onboarded or updated. The model metadata (tags, affinity, quantization profile) and perf profile deltas (latency P50/P95, memory/per-token cost changes) already contain signal that can be translated to release-notes bullets. This PR codifies a scenario-driven mapping ("playbook") so release notes are: 1) consistent, 2) traceable to metadata diffs, and 3) suggest rollout hints (canary size, recommended fallback).

What this change does: 1) Adds a playbook engine (registry/playbook/) that consumes: a) model metadata diff (onboard vs previous variant), b) performance profile delta JSON, c) optional curated annotations from reviewers. 2) Implements a scenario classifier that emits a prioritized list of changelog seeds: "Performance improvement", "Increased memory use — consider lower batch sizes", "Model variant renamed/alias added", "Precision/quantization change with expected quality trade-off". 3) Adds template rendering with short and long variants and localization-ready strings. 4) Exposes a preview endpoint and a small React component in the curation UI so SREs/PMs can review and edit seeds before publishing. 5) Hooks into the existing release-assembler pipeline to optionally attach generated seeds as suggested release notes.

Implementation notes: - Core engine implemented in TypeScript (registry/playbook/*.ts). Lightweight rules defined as ordered scenarios with guard predicates and priority scoring. - Performance-profile normalizer added (registry/profiles/normalizer.ts) to compute delta buckets for latency, cost, and memory across workload slices. - Preview UI lives under redwood-model-registry/ui/components/PlaybookPreview.tsx and calls /api/playbook/preview. - Feature gated by registry.config.playbook.enabled (default: false) and opt-in per-model via model.annotations.playbook: true. - Adds unit tests for scenario matching and end-to-end integration tests for preview and assembly (tests/playbook/*).

Checklist: - [x] Scenario engine and core templates implemented - [x] Preview API + UI component - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs: developer guide + sample playbook rules - [x] Linear tickets linked - [x] Feature gate with safe default (disabled)

Files changed (high level): - registry/playbook/engine.ts - registry/playbook/scenarios/*.ts - registry/profiles/normalizer.ts - ui/components/PlaybookPreview.tsx - api/routes/playbook.ts - tests/playbook/* - docs/dev/playbook.md - migrations/add_playbook_flag.sql - samples/fixtures/profile-deltas/sample-2025-10.json

Review conversation (selected): - Liam O'Neal (review): "Nice direction. Two requests: (1) concretely show how scoring prioritizes multiple overlapping scenarios (e.g., latency drop + quantization) and (2) ensure we never auto-publish seeds without an explicit curator approval step."

The goal is to reduce churn in release automation and make profile signing deterministic for stable variants.
