payload.body:
Motivation: onboarding data often contains multiple performance profiles for a single model (variants, quantization levels, hardware affinity). Prior heuristics produced noisy release notes and inconsistent rollouts because we lacked a deterministic reconciliation step and a concise representation of profile stability for changelogs. This PR introduces a profile reconciler that ingests variant-level profiles, normalizes metrics, and synthesizes a single authoritative profile per onboard. It also adds a stability watermark exporter that emits a compact summary used by changelog generation and automated rollout policies.

What this PR does (high level):
- Implements registry/reconciler.py: a deterministic reconciler that merges profiles using configurable weighting (sample counts, recency, occupancy). The reconciler outputs p50/p95 latency, token throughput, GPU occupancy estimates, and a computed stability_score (0-100).
- Adds registry/exporters/watermark.py: formats the reconciled profile into a compact watermark artifact (YAML/JSON) consumed by release note generators and by the rollout controller to determine canary batch sizes. The watermark contains a stability bucket, dominant hardware affinity, and top-line perf deltas vs baseline.
- Adds A/B heuristics: if profiles disagree beyond thresholds (configurable via registry/config.yaml), reconciler emits an alert annotation and includes the high-variance fingerprints in the watermark.
- Changes to changelog pipeline: the changelog assembler now reads watermarks and can inject stability tags and suggested rollout knobs into autogenerated release notes.
- Tests & CI: unit tests for reconciliation math; an e2e integration job (ci/profiles-integration.yml) that validates reconciler + exporter on synthetic variant sets; new fuzz tests to protect against NaNs and missing fields.
- Docs: onboarding/reconciliation.md documents behavior, config knobs, and runbook for resolving high-variance cases.

Key algorithm notes:
- Normalization: metric units are normalized (ms, tokens/sec, percent occupancy).
- Weighting: sample_count and recency (exponential decay) are combined to produce per-variant weights. There is a safeguard floor to avoid starving low-frequency but production-critical variants.
- Stability score: derived from a weighted variance of p95 and occupancy across variants, scaled and clamped to 0-100. This is intentionally conservative (penalizes variance that could cause user-facing regressions).
- Conflict handling: when a variant's p95 delta > delta_threshold and sample_count > min_samples, reconciler annotates the watermark with the variant fingerprint and produces a suggested rollback pointer for the changelog.

Why this is safe: reconciliation is opt-in by default for existing onboard flows; new onboards will run through reconciler but the CR will not flip auto-rollout changes on without the rollout team's explicit opt-in. All exports are signed by the registry service key and stored alongside provenance metadata.

Migration notes: a one-time backfill job (scripts/backfill/reconcile-legacy-profiles.py) is included to generate watermarks for existing models. Backfill is gated behind a feature flag (registry.flags.enable_backfill).

Testing summary: CI runs new unit and integration tests. The integration job spins up a small local registry image, creates synthetic variant profiles (low/high variance), runs reconciliation, and asserts expected watermark fields. Flaky tests were addressed by increasing synthetic dataset entropy and adding deterministic seeds.

Rollout plan: merged to main behind the feature flag. Step 1: run backfill on staging and spot-check 20 high-usage models. Step 2: enable reconciler for new onboards only. Step 3: after 2 weeks of telemetry validation (no spike in rollout aborts), enable reconciliation for all onboards and flip changelog watermark consumption on by default.

Related work: this PR builds on earlier profiling and changelog automation efforts (see ENG-1021 and ENG-1089) and is designed to interoperate with the model registry's provenance fingerprints and release-assembler.

Notes to reviewers: focus on the weighting math in reconciler.py and on the exporter schema stability; small changes to the changelog assembler were intentionally conservative (non-breaking) to avoid regressions in downstream integrations.

Maya Patel (2024-05-15): Added numeric example and explicit clamps in reconciler.py; updated unit tests to assert clamped values.
Leah Zhang (2024-05-16): Can the reconciler be tricked by intentionally bad sample_count values from legacy exports? Suggest adding a source-trust factor.
Maya Patel (2024-05-16): Added source_trust_factor (configurable) and a validation layer that enforces min/max sample counts per source. Tests added.

payload.body:
Introduce a transitive dependency graph for models and a rolling profile calibration hook that periodically re-measures model profiles and emits compact changelog deltas. Improves downstream compatibility tagging and automates small profile adjustments without manual release steps.
Motivation: onboarding new model families has become harder to maintain when a single upstream weight change ripples through variants (quantized builds, fused kernels, etc). We need a canonical, machine-friendly representation of transitive model dependencies and an automated calibration job that re-evaluates performance profiles on a small set of canonical prompts to keep profile metadata current and to generate compact delta release notes.

What this PR does: adds a lightweight transitive-dependency graph to model metadata, implements a rolling-profile-calibration hook that runs in a low-cost sandbox, and wires the calibration output into the changelog assembler so we can publish concise, delta-based release notes for profile updates. The calibration job is conservative by design: it flags changes, produces a delta bundle, and only updates a profile stamp when thresholds are met or after human approval (configurable).

Design highlights: 1) metadata: ModelProfile now includes fields: `transitive_dependencies` (list of model ids + relation reason), `compatibility_graph_sha` (checksum for graph snapshot), and `calibration_snapshot` (timestamped probe results). 2) calibration hook: a scheduled service that loads the model variant in an isolated runner, runs a curated small corpus of prompts (opt-in per-model), measures latency/throughput/p99 and a few quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE surrogate, token perplexity where applicable), then produces a normalized profile delta. 3) changelog integration: deltas are compacted and appended to the existing release assembler; small, safe adjustments may be auto-applied if they pass stability checks and the model owner has enabled "auto-calibrate". 4) safety & audit: every auto-change emits an audit record and a signed delta bundle; the console shows a compact human-readable blurb and the raw delta.

Compatibility & migration: existing profiles without transitive graph fields remain valid; the migration job will backfill `compatibility_graph_sha` for models that have origin metadata available. The calibration hook is opt-in by default for older models; new onboarded models get a default small probe set unless opted out.

Testing and validation: unit tests for graph serialization and checksum verification; end-to-end test harness that runs the calibration flow against a small internal model (ci-calib/test-1) to verify non-destructive behavior; load tests to ensure the sandbox runner respects resource limits and does not affect serving pools.

Operational notes: calibration job runs at low priority in the infra sandbox with default cadence of 72 hours; adjustable per-customer; rollback is supported by restoring previous profile JSON and revoking the `compatibility_graph_sha` update.

Open questions / follow-ups: 1) what gating thresholds for auto-apply are appropriate across model families (ENG-5021 is tracking an experimental policy); 2) UX in console for reviewing auto-applied deltas (docs included in this PR).
Ava Chen: Please add explicit unit tests for checksum mismatch behavior.
Elena Park: added tests in tests/calib/test_checksum.py and updated the serialization to include stable ordering.
Miguel Torres: How do we avoid the calibration job pushing noisy token-perplexity changes for models with nondeterministic outputs?
Elena Park: calibration reports include a noise estimate (bootstrap) and we only auto-apply when signal-to-noise ratio > 3. Added comment in worker and a small e2e test to validate the logic.
Priya Nair: console UX — we need a one-click revert for auto-applied changes.
Elena Park: added `revert_delta` endpoint and console row action; documented in docs/registry/calibration.md.

Adds a release-preview-streamer service and a profile rollforward allocator to automate draft release notes for model onboarding and staged rollouts. Motivation: manual changelog drafting and ad-hoc rollforwards cause delays and inconsistent notes for model profile updates. This PR introduces a preview endpoint (+CLI) that synthesizes a candidate release note from model_profile deltas, telemetry-weighted sample highlights, and provenance anchors; a watermark-backed change tracker that emits incremental release fragments; and a rollforward allocator that computes safe staged rollout cohorts and suggested rollback checkpoints. The implementation includes a small schema migration (model_profile_events table + watermark index), a new service (preview-streamer) with a streaming SSE/HTTP endpoint, a CLI command (mr release-preview) for maintainers, server-side heuristics for 'noise' filtering (min-sample-count, stable-baseline threshold), and integration hooks for the changelog composer used by the docs pipeline. Checklist: [x] schema migration and migration tests, [x] unit tests for delta scoring, [x] e2e test that verifies preview -> publish flow, [x] Linear links in commit messages, [x] docs draft in /docs/release-previews.md, [ ] follow-up telemetry dashboard for preview quality (separate PR). Backwards compatibility: new tables and endpoints are additive; existing onboarding flows are unchanged by default. Runtime note: the rollforward allocator uses a conservative default cohort size and can be tuned via config flags per-organization. See release_notes and review_conversation for important decisions and follow-ups.

- Add docs: docs/release-previews.md and CLI usage examples.
Notes: default rollout policies are conservative; configure per-organization via model-registry config.

payload.body:
Context and motivation: We frequently receive onboarding requests where model variants diverge subtly (tokenization tweaks, quantized builds, or perf-only forks). Authors currently hand-write release notes and maintain separate ad-hoc snapshot artifacts, which makes rollbacks and impact analysis error-prone. This change introduces a persisted 'variant snapshot' artifact and an automated 'changelog prioritizer' that surfaces the most likely high-impact deltas to release-note writers.

Goals: 1) Persist lightweight, canonical snapshots for each model variant so diffs are reproducible and linkable in changelogs. 2) Compute a traffic-weighted impact score (perf delta * request share + semantic-change heuristic) to rank changelog entries. 3) Emit an auto-drafted prioritized release notes bundle as a developer-editable template accessible from the registry UI and CLI. 4) Keep the runtime cost low and the snapshot storage compact (dedup and bloom-filter-assisted reference).

What this PR does (high-level): - Adds a snapshot persistence layer (snapshots table + compact blob format + index by model:variant:seed). - Implements snapshot_store service with delta computation and stable-content hash (blake2b-64) for identity and compact dedupe. - Adds changelog prioritizer module: calculates impact_score = weighted_sum([perf_delta_ms_norm, token_cost_delta, traffic_share_estimate, semantic_change_score]) and exposes a prioritization API and template generator. - Adds a UI card to registry webapp to preview prioritized autodrafts and accept/adjust weights. - Adds a CLI command 'redwood-registry snapshot:export --variant' to produce portable snapshot bundles and templated release notes. - Ships DB migration and a one-time backfill/seed script for environments with existing variant tags.

Commits summary (top-level): - 4c9e0b1: introduce snapshot table schema and migration - 7a2d3f4: implement snapshot_store read/write/dedupe - b1f8c9a: add stable hashing and compact blob serializer - 9d1a2b0: implement changelog_prioritizer with default weights and unit tests - 2ac4b55: add web UI card and wire to prioritizer API - f7e0e11: CLI snapshot export & import hooks - 1b3c9ff: observability: metrics + alert for unexpectedly large snapshot payloads - 5f8d2aa: docs and onboarding guide for snapshot workflows

Files changed (high-level): - migration adds snapshots table with reference columns and blob column for compressed manifest. - services/registry gains snapshot_store and prioritizer service modules (~500 LOC). - webapp includes a new ChangelogPrioritizerCard and small form for weight overrides. - CLI adds a new subcommand and azure-s3-compatible upload helper. - tests include unit coverage for hashing, dedupe, priority ranking, and a tiny e2e for export/import.

Design/implementation notes and trade-offs: - Snapshot blob remains intentionally compact: we store lightweight manifests (tokenizer fingerprint, config diff, perf fingerprints) rather than full model files; external storage references (artifact URLs) are supported for large binaries. - Hashing: chosen blake2b-64 for speed and stable cross-language determinism with explicit canonical serialization. - Prioritization is heuristic-driven and configurable per-org via a weights config and small ML-derived semantic-change signal (cosine between embedding centroids). We ship conservative defaults. - Backfill is idempotent and uses snapshot hash to avoid re-inserting duplicates.

Migration notes: - Includes offline migration SQL: migrations/202502_add_variant_snapshots.sql. - Seed script scripts/seed_default_priorities.py runs as a one-off to seed organization-level default weights. - Ops note: the migration can be run with the offline flag; snapshot store tolerates missing snapshots in read path.

Testing and CI: - Local unit tests added under tests/ cover dedupe, hashing, ranking heuristics. - Integration e2e in CI runs a headless export/import scenario (small sample model fixtures). - CI summary: initial run failed on linting (TSX formatting) and a flakey test test_changelog_prioritizer::test_traffic_weighted_rank which was fixed by stabilizing time mocking. Final CI status: pass.

Review conversation (abridged): - Jordan Patel (reviewer): "Nice end-to-end story. Two asks: (1) can we make the default weights configurable per-team? (2) document the privacy implications of storing tokenizer fingerprints." Author reply (Maya): "(1) Yes—weights are org-scoped and exposed in the UI; added seed script + config. (2) Tokenizer fingerprints are irreversibly hashed and do not include training data; expanded docs section to clarify." - Ravi Shah: "DB migration looks fine but please ensure index on (model_id, variant_id, hash) to avoid scans." Author: "Added composite index and updated migration SQL." - Anya Gomez: "Prefer feature flag rollout for the UI card." Author: "Wrapped UI behind feature flag 'changelog_prioritizer' and defaulted to on for internal tenants."

Operational considerations: - Observability: added snapshots.size_bytes and snapshot.dedupe_ratio metrics; alert when avg payload > 1MB. - Cost: snapshot payloads dedupe aggressively; large model binaries are stored externally. - Rollout: feature flag + canary users in registry-qa first, then org-by-org enable.

Backwards compatibility and security: - No breaking external API changes; new API endpoints are additive. - Snapshot blobs are access-controlled via existing registry ACLs; export CLI requires API token with export scope. - No plaintext customer data is introduced; tokenizer fingerprints are hashed.

Follow-ups and future work: - Add a lightweight 'auto-summary' generator that converts prioritized diffs into plain-English bullet points (ENG-3297). - Telemetry: track which autodrafts are accepted/edited by writers to tune prioritizer. - Consider compact binary diff format for perf fingerprints to further reduce size.

Merge outcome: merged into main via squash on 2025-02-02 after CI green and approvals from Jordan and Ravi.

Related work and references: - Linear: ENG-3145 (variant snapshots), ENG-3297 (autodraft summarizer) - Related tickets: SUP-42 (customer request for more consistent release notes)

If you want to run locally: 1) apply migration: ./scripts/db-migrate up 202502_add_variant_snapshots.sql 2) seed defaults: python3 scripts/seed_default_priorities.py --env=dev 3) start registry and webapp, enable feature flag 'changelog_prioritizer'

Notes for reviewers picking up follow-ups: the prioritizer core is intentionally deterministic and small; adding ML-derived knobs should be a separate follow-up with opt-in telemetry.
Adds a persisted variant snapshot store and a heuristic changelog prioritizer for automated release-note drafts; migration adds snapshots table, API and UI hooks; no customer-visible API breaking changes.

Motivation: onboarding pipelines currently produce inconsistent manifest shapes (aliasing, optional provenance keys) which makes automated release notes noisy and prevents deterministic sampling for quick release previews. This PR adds a small, focused intake catalog 'wrangler' plus an epoched delta synthesizer to generate compact, readable changelog snippets from model ingest events. Goals: 1) canonicalize incoming intake manifests into a fixed shape and deterministic canonical alias; 2) generate compact 'epoch diffs' between catalog snapshots that are optimized for human-facing release teasers; 3) expose a sampled-delta API used by the console and the model-onboard bot to produce short change bullets without running full diffs over large histories. What changed (high level): - new module catalog/wrangler that normalizes manifests, validates provenance, and computes a manifest_fingerprint for stable identity; - epoched-diff synthesizer that consumes two snapshot epochs and emits a ranked set of deltas with severity/impact hints; - small CLI hook (scripts/changelog/epoch_synth.py) to preview teaser snippets for release authors; - integration with performance-profiles to attach a short profile-summary when a profile delta is detected; - telemetry: histogram for canonicalization failures and a sampled-delta coverage counter. Breaking/compatibility notes: the canonicalizer adds a new top-level field 'canonical_alias' and 'manifest_fingerprint' to persisted manifests. Older consumers that expect arbitrary alias shapes should use the new lookup helper catalog.lookup_by_fingerprint(). Migration: ingestion jobs are updated to write the canonicalized manifest; a migration scaffold for backfilling existing manifests is included but not applied by default. Tests and validation: unit tests for normalization rules, end-to-end smoke test for epoched diffs, and a small performance benchmark to ensure the synthesizer runs within the expected 2s for typical catalog sizes. Rollout plan: merged behind feature flag 'intake_catalog_v2' and staged to dev -> staging -> canary before global enable. payload.body:
Context: onboarding and release notes for model profiles often miss distributional edge cases (long tail of token lengths, bursty token patterns) and manually-written changelogs are noisy. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) a slice-seed generator that constructs small, reproducible synthetic workload slices to seed profiling runs during onboarding and regression checks; and (2) a compact release annotator that synthesizes concise changelog bullets focused on performance deltas and metadata changes for model profiles.

Design summary: the slice-seed generator takes a compact profile descriptor (percentile token-length histogram, sample-rate, and request signature templates) and emits a deterministic set of requests that exercise headroom, KV-cache growth patterns, and streaming hotspots. Seeds are small (default 256 requests) and are parametrized by "slice keys" (e.g. latency-sensitive, long-context, high-embed-rate). The profile schema is bumped to v2 to include slice_metadata and seed_fingerprint. The compact release annotator consumes profile diffs (old vs new) and emits a 1-3 line release blurb with: impacted models/variants, delta in 50/95/99 latency and median token-cost, changed quantization flags, and a reliability flag if any regression exceeds thresholds. The annotator also attaches a machine-readable annotation for downstream UI/console ingestion.

Checklist performed: 
- [x] design RFC linked and reviewed (ENG-1789)
- [x] schema v2 introduced with backwards-compatible getters
- [x] deterministic seed generator + unit tests
- [x] CI hook that runs slice seeds against profile candidate artifacts
- [x] compact annotator with release blurb + JSON annotation output
- [x] docs update for onboarding and release notes usage

How it works (developer notes): 
- profiles/schema_v2.yaml: new fields slice_metadata (list of slice descriptors) and seed_fingerprint (sha256 of canonicalized seed payload).
- profiles/slice_generator.py: CLI and library API to render N requests from a slice descriptor; supports templated prompts and stochastic sampling seeds for reproducibility.
- changelog/compact_emitter.py: comparator that computes delta summary and formats both human and machine outputs. Emits annotations to release bundle under annotations/compact.json.
- CI: scripts/ci_profile_check.sh invokes the generator and runs lightweight perf harness against the candidate profile bundle. The CI step is gated and can be skipped with [ci skip-profile-check] for fast iteration.

Testing and validation: added tests/test_slice_generator.py (determinism, fingerprint stability) and tests/test_compact_emitter.py (edge-case diffs, thresholding). Local perf runs on a small GPU instance confirm that the seeded slices reproduce a mean 2.1% token-cost variance across runs (within acceptable noise).

Rollout plan: land to main behind feature flag profile.slice_seed.enabled default=false. After a brief dogfood period (1 week) enable for automatic onboarding runs and allow teams to opt-in for release annotation. Console will display compact blurb and a link to the full diff.

Migration notes: existing profiles without slice_metadata are supported; schema helpers will synthesize a default slice (percentiles from historical telemetry) if none present. There is no breaking change to existing API surface.

Related: Linear ENG-1789 (design), PM-412 (release flow). Internal RFC: https://rfd.internal.redwood/eng/1789-slice-seed (internal only).
Asha Kapoor: Please include peak_headroom metric in the schema so dedicated teams can reason about spare capacity. -- Response: added peak_headroom and updated README with interpretation guidance.
Liam Chen: CI failed on first run due to test flake in test_compact_emitter; re-ran and it passed. -- Response: fixed nondeterministic ordering in comparator, added stable sort.
Diego Morales: Suggest exposing seed fingerprint in registry UI and gating annotation visibility. -- Response: added UI annotation key and feature flag notes in rollout plan.
Asha Kapoor (approval): Approved after headroom metric and CI green.
- Introduce profile schema v2 with slice_metadata and deterministic seed fingerprints.
- Add slice-seed generator to create compact reproducible workload seeds for onboarding and regression tests.
- Add compact release annotator to synthesize concise performance changelogs and attach machine-readable annotations to releases.

Motivation: Over time model profiles accumulate (old variants, un-requested quantizations, and deprecated adapters) which add noise to onboarding, inflate the registry, and complicate customer-facing release notes. This PR implements a policy-driven "profile retirement" mechanism plus an Autosunset Annotator that generates concise, context-aware changelog/snippet entries recommending replacements or migration steps.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a retirement policy engine that evaluates profile age, last-serving-date (from telemetry), sample-coverage, and stability-signature to produce a retirement score.
- Introduces an Autosunset Annotator that composes changelog blurbs (short/medium length) and optional migration hints (CLI flags, model alias mappings) when a profile is marked for retirement.
- Exposes a /profiles/retire dry-run and apply endpoints in the registry API; and a CLI command (models retire --dry-run --threshold) for batch operations.
- Emits audit entries and a release note fragment that can be consumed by the onboard release assembler to include sunset notices in release manifests.
- Adds safety gates: staged retirement (notify-only), required human acknowledgement for >50% coverage change, and automatic rollback hooks for churn spikes.

Why it's built this way:
- We want deterministic, explainable retirements (no black-box purges). The policy engine is rules-first with pluggable heuristics so we can tune for enterprise vs. PLG usage.
- The Autosunset output is intentionally terse and structured (a small template library) so downstream consumers (docs, release notes, SDKs) can render human-friendly text or machine-readable migration hints.

Checklist (this PR):
- [x] Policy engine implementation + unit tests
- [x] Autosunset annotator + templating and generator tests
- [x] API surface + CLI entrypoint + integration tests
- [x] Audit logging + event ping to telemetry pipeline
- [x] Documentation draft (registry/retirement.md) + example release note snippet
- [x] E2E staging run validating no accidental retirements on current catalog

Backward compatibility and migration notes:
- Retirement scoring defaults to off for existing customers; config flag `retirement.enabled=false` preserves current behavior.
- The API adds optional query params and a new /profiles/retire route; clients using the registry should remain unaffected unless they call the new endpoints.

Rollout plan:
- Merge behind feature flag, run staged retirements on a small cohort, manual review of generated autosunset entries for 2 weeks, then opt-in program for customers to enable automated retirements.

Related work items: Linear ENG-4523, PM-98. Support ticket SUP-217: customer requested clearer notice for deprecated variants.

Notes on uniqueness: This focuses on the retirement lifecycle and auto-generation of sunset blurb content (not just changelog concatenation). The annotator produces a short sentence, optional replacement mapping, and a migration snippet suitable for release notes and SDK upgrade guides.
Introduce profile retirement policy and Autosunset Annotator: opt-in retirement engine, autosunset changelog snippets, new API and CLI to dry-run/apply retirements, audit trail and telemetry. Backwards compatible via feature flag. See docs/registry/retirement.md for configuration and rollout guidance.

Motivation: onboarding churn and staged rollouts make changelogs noisy and hard to correlate with measured performance. This PR introduces 'epoched' release manifests (manifest_v2) and a digesting pipeline that emits privacy-preserving sample snapshots that are attached to release artifacts. Goals: 1) make release notes deterministic and replayable per epoch; 2) attach compact, anonymized sample digests that allow QA/SEs to re-run representative inputs without exposing raw customer data; 3) enable a changelog mirror that can publish concise per-epoch summaries for the Console and the public model catalog.

What changed (high-level): added a new manifest_v2 schema with epoch and provenance fields; migration to add epoch table; a background worker (chronicle) that synthesizes per-epoch diffs and generates anonymized sample digests (k-anonymity + token-redaction rules); CLI and SDK hooks to pin a model release to an epoch; Console docs and a new release-chronicle generator that compiles release notes from epoched profiles, perf deltas, and anonymized sample summaries.

Important design notes: sample digests are content-addressed (sha256) and store only hashed examples + light metadata (sequence length distribution, quantified latency percentiles, quantization-profile used). Raw samples are never stored in the registry; the digest generator applies deterministic redaction and numeric bucketing to prevent reconstruction. Epochs are monotonic integers per model-name + major-version and provide a stable anchor for rollbacks and canary comparisons.

Backward compatibility: manifests without epoch will be treated as epoch=0. The migration is additive; older registry clients continue to function. The Console has a migration compatibility layer that renders epoch=0 releases as before.

Ops & rollout plan: feature gated behind config flag registry.release_epochs; rollout to staging for 2 weeks, then gradual enable for 10% of new onboard flows; enable digest generation for internal-only releases first. The PR includes the migration and a reversible downgrade path (drop epoch table and conversion script).

Links: linear -> ENG-2147; design doc -> docs/registry/release-epochs.md; demo script -> cli/onboard --epoch 3 --pin
Miguel Santos: Nice approach — epoch anchors will make rollbacks so much clearer. Two asks: add an integration test that validates digest reproducibility and document the k-anonymity parameters.
Priya Nair: Thanks — added tests/chronicle/test_digest_generation.py and documented parameters in release-epochs.md. The digest generator exposes K_FACTOR (default=5) and a bucketing policy.
Dana Cho: We need to be explicit about PII handling. Are we relying only on tokenization redaction? What about freeform fields in metadata?
Priya Nair: Good point. Updated the worker to run a metadata scrubber that drops freeform fields not in an allowlist and replaces strings over 64 chars with hashes. Added tests for long-field redaction.
Evan Li: CI failed on lint in first run (flake8 error in worker). Re-run required.
Priya Nair: Fixed lint and a race in the epoch table migration; re-ran CI and addressed transient DB ordering in the worker initialization.

payload.body:
Motivation: onboarding churn and large onboards produce big manifest diffs that are hard for downstream consumers (release assemblers, telemetry exporters, and compliance hooks) to handle. This PR introduces two cooperating pieces: 1) streaming manifest incrementation: manifests published to the registry now carry a compact sequence delta that can be streamed and applied by incremental consumers; 2) rollback-notes-writer: when a model profile version is rolled back (manual or automatic due to stability regressions), a compact changelog fragment is synthesized and persisted to the release-fragments store for downstream release automation and audit.

Scope: model intake pipeline, manifest serializer, release fragment writer, integration tests, and small console UI indicator for pending rollback notes. This is intended to reduce the cost of large diffs, enable incremental downstream syncs, and make rollback events auditable and human-readable.

Key behavior:
- Manifests are versioned with a lightweight monotonically increasing commit sequence (manifest_seq) and a delta payload that contains only top-level profile keys changed (metadata, tags, performance_profile pointers).
- The streaming manifest endpoint (/intake/v1/manifest/stream) supports backpressure-aware chunking and a resumable token tied to manifest_seq.
- Rollbacks trigger a deterministic fragment that lists reverted versions, reason tags (e.g. "perf-regression", "policy-failure"), and a short human summary; fragments are idempotent and signed with registry provenance key.

Implementation notes:
- Added a new manifest sequencer component (manifest/sequencer.go) that assigns manifest_seq and emits a compact index entry. Sequencer persists to the existing manifest-index table with a new schema column (seq bigint) with backfill script included.
- Manifest serializer now produces two artifacts: full manifest blob and compact delta blob (delta contains keys changed and minimal values).
- Rollback-notes-writer listens to the existing profile_revision stream; on receiving a rollback event it runs a deterministic summarizer and writes release fragment JSON to /fragments/release/ directory in object storage.
- Introduced schema migration and a short backfill CLI (tools/migrate_manifest_seq) to incrementally assign seq to historical manifests.
- Added integration tests focusing on: streaming resume semantics, backpressure chunk boundaries, delta correctness for common onboard changes, and rollback fragment contents.

Compatibility and migration:
- Backfill tool must be run in maintenance window for orgs with >100k manifests; it runs in small batches and supports dry-run.
- Consumers that rely on full manifest blobs are unaffected; streaming and deltas are opt-in via Accept headers or query param.
- Rollback fragments are additive and will not change existing release pipelines unless they opt-in to fragments feed.

Risks and mitigations:
- Race between sequencer and concurrent onboarders: sequencer uses optimistic lease + idempotent compare-and-set to avoid collisions.
- Fragment signing depends on KMS availability; fallback mode writes unsigned fragment and emits an alert for operator review.

How to test locally:
- run ./dev/local_registry and ./dev/producer_sim to publish sample manifests; use curl to hit /intake/v1/manifest/stream?resume_token=<seq> to validate resume.
- tools/migrate_manifest_seq --dry-run to validate database changes.

Checklist:
- [x] sequencer implementation + unit tests
- [x] serializer delta output and storage adapter
- [x] rollback-notes-writer + integration tests
- [x] migration tool and docs
- [x] manual QA and load-run on perf-canary (small-scale)
- [x] add console indicator (pending rollback fragments)

See also: ENG-1987 (incremental manifest delivery), SUP-4231 (customer asked for smaller change payloads during onboards).
Adds streaming manifest sequence numbers to support incremental downstream consumption; introduces a rollback-notes writer that emits concise changelog fragments when a model profile is reverted.
Diego Ramos: Nice approach; can we ensure the manifest_seq is monotonic even with cross-region replicas? Suggest adding per-region offset in the index to avoid seq collisions.
Ava Morgan: Sequencer uses a central index shard for assignment; added note in sequencer.go and updated migration docs. We discussed regional offsets offline and plan a follow-up (ENG-2054) to make it pluggable.
Priya Shah: Tests look good. Please add a small assertion that delta blobs do not include full tokenized performance profiles (we don't want heavy payloads here).
Ava Morgan: Added assertion in integration/stream_test.go to validate max delta blob size and that performance_profile fields are referenced by id only.

payload.body:
Motivation: onboarding new models currently requires a manual, full-profile pass that is slow and expensive for initial acceptance. This PR adds a lightweight, sampled profiling harness that seeds a compact performance profile and a small 'changelog seed' artifact that the release assembler can consume to generate early release notes and regression hints. The goal is to make model triage fast: produce an initial cost/latency estimate and highlight obvious compatibility or perf regressions before running the full calibration pipeline.

What this PR does (high level): Adds a `profile-seed` runner that performs deterministic, sampled inference traces against a curated prompt corpus and quantization/config variants; it produces a compact profile (latency percentiles, sample token counts, KV-warmup guidance) and a machine-readable changelog seed that records observed diffs between current and baseline variants. Also wires a post-merge CI job that uploads the seed artifact to the release pipeline so downstream assemblers can include notes and candidate regression warnings.

Checklist: [x] sampled profiling harness (registry/onboard/seed_profiler.py) [x] CI job + k8s job manifest (ci/profilers/profile-seed-job.yaml) [x] compact seed schema and serializer (registry/schema/profile_seed_schema.yaml) [x] small CLI shim to run locally (scripts/run_profile_seed.sh) [x] unit and smoke integration tests (tests/test_seed_profiler.py) [x] docs: onboarding quickstart and privacy notes (docs/onboarding/quickstart-profiling.md)

Design notes: The harness samples workloads instead of exhaustive runs to keep runtime under 10 minutes on a small GPU. Sampling uses stratified prompts drawn from the model's prerecorded prompt-corpus manifest (if available) with a configurable deterministic RNG seed to make results repeatable. For latency estimation we warm the KV cache with a single prefix pass per prompt group then measure steady-state P50/P95/P99 across N inferences. Cost estimates are derived from tokenization + measured per-token latency and multiplied against measured throughput; this intentionally errs on the conservative side. The changelog seed contains per-variant bulletized findings (e.g. "+12ms P95 vs baseline", "increased tokenizer OOV ratio: 0.4%") and a short machine-check field for likely breakages (tokenization drift, output shape mismatch) so the release assembler can highlight actionable items.

Privacy/security: prompt corpus sampling uses only datasets flagged as "public" or "scrubbed" per registry metadata; if no approved corpus exists the run defaults to synthetic prompts generated from model-spec templates. No raw prompts are uploaded as part of the seed artifact; only hashed prompt identifiers and aggregate stats are stored. We added a short policy note in docs/onboarding/quickstart-profiling.md.

Backward compatibility: The compact seed uses a forward-compatible schema (profile_seed_schema.yaml). The release assembler will ignore unknown fields. No registry schema changes required for existing profiles.

Testing: Unit tests cover serializer roundtrip, deterministic sampling, and the cost estimator. Integration smoke runs the harness against a small toy model in CI; the smoke job was flaky initially because of different tokenizer versions in the CI image — fixed by pinning tokenizer package in the CI job manifest.

Follow-ups: 1) add expansion to run a small battery of quantized variants automatically (ENG-2240 follow-up), 2) integrate with model-onboard UI to show the seed summary in the first-stage review panel, 3) schedule nightly re-seeds for active variants to detect regressions early.

Related: Linear ENG-2154, ENG-2240; SUP-982 (support case that motivated faster triage).
Liam Chen: Nice direction. Two questions: how do we ensure sample representativeness across long-tail prompts? Please document the sampling heuristics and add a knob for stratified oversampling of rare buckets.
Aisha Kapoor: answered — added stratified sampling logic and a --sample-weight config option, documented heuristics in quickstart-profiling.md.
Mariana Ortiz: Concerned about leakage — can we avoid storing raw prompts in artifacts? Also CI flaked on tokenizer mismatch earlier.
Aisha Kapoor: confirmed — artifacts only contain hashed prompt ids and aggregated stats; fixed CI by pinning tokenizer version in the CI manifest; added policy note to docs.
Devon Patel: Can the changelog seed accidentally mark false positives for regressions when perf variance is high? Suggest a simple baseline-stability check or sig-test.
Aisha Kapoor: implemented a basic bootstrap-based stability gate that marks a finding as "likely" only if delta exceeds 2x sample stddev; otherwise flags as "noisy" and includes raw stats for later evaluation.
Mariana Ortiz: Approved after changes — left an approval review.
Liam Chen: LGTM. Squash-merge when CI passes.

payload.body:
Motivation: onboarding churn and noisy release changelogs have made it hard for integrators to understand which model profile changes actually matter for production workloads. This PR introduces a delta-led consolidation step that combines incoming profile deltas with historical telemetry (usage-weighted buckets) to produce a single consolidated profile and an annotated release summary. The summary includes expected latency/cost impact, confidence bands, and automatic tags for changelog generation.

What this implements: consolidated merge pipeline (delta-led) that treats incoming profile changes as first-class deltas instead of blind overwrites; a telemetry bridge that ingests recent per-model route histograms and produces weight vectors used by the merger; an annotation layer that synthesizes release-notes snippets with quantitative deltas (median latency change, token-cost estimates, sample-percent-of-traffic impacted) and human-friendly rationale; a safeguard layer that blocks auto-merge when signal is ambiguous (low sample count or high variance) and surfaces a recommended manual review checklist.

User-visible outcomes:
- New endpoint in the registry API: POST /profiles/:id/merge-delta (idempotent) which accepts a delta bundle and returns a consolidated profile + release snippet draft.
- CLI command: redwood-registry profiles merge-delta --file delta.json --telemetry-window 7d --dry-run
- Release automation hook: on successful consolidation the hook can populate draft release notes with the annotated summary and add tags (impact:low/medium/high, recommended:manual_review/auto_merge).

Implementation highlights (high-level commits):
- commit 1: core merger runtime and deterministic ordering for delta application (src/registry/merge/delta_merger.py)
- commit 2: telemetry adapter that normalizes histograms and computes route weights (src/registry/telemetry/adapter.py)
- commit 3: annotated-summary generator and templating infra for release notes (src/registry/release/annotator.py, templates/release/snippet.mustache)
- commit 4: API + CLI wiring and feature flag gating (api/routes/profiles.py, cli/commands/merge_delta.py, feature_flags.yaml)
- commit 5: test harness and synthetic telemetry fixtures (tests/integration/test_delta_merge.py, tests/fixtures/telemetry/*.json)
- commit 6: docs: how-to + guardrails (docs/registry/delta-merge.md)

Files touched (high level):
- Added: src/registry/merge/delta_merger.py, src/registry/telemetry/adapter.py, src/registry/release/annotator.py, cli/commands/merge_delta.py, templates/release/snippet.mustache, tests/integration/test_delta_merge.py, docs/registry/delta-merge.md
- Modified: api/routes/profiles.py, src/registry/profile_schema.py (added delta schema), feature_flags.yaml, package manifests and CI workflow for telemetry tests

Backward compatibility and safety: the feature is off by default behind the feature flag registry.delta_merge.enabled. The POST /profiles/:id/merge-delta endpoint requires an allowance role (registry:merge) and logs a signed proof bundle for auditability. Auto-merge to mainline profile only occurs when sample-weight >= 500 and variance < threshold or when the release annotation explicitly marks low impact. Otherwise the consolidated profile is saved as a draft and a reviewer is requested.

Testing and validation: included unit tests for delta application ordering, property-based checks for idempotency, integration tests using synthetic telemetry (traffic mixes) and a smoke test against a small real-traffic snapshot (privacy-filtered). CI runs lint, unit, integration and a lightweight telemetry validator job that exercises adapter normalization.

Performance: the delta merger operates in O(n log k) where n is number of delta ops and k is number of route buckets; a synthetic benchmark shows 95th percentile merge time for a 1k-delta bundle is ~420ms on our standard ci runner. The telemetry adapter is optimized for streaming histogram fold and uses a small LRU cache for recent route weights.

Open questions / future follow-ups: adding an explainability view that links sample examples to profile changes (ENG-1719), richer cost-model integration with Redwood Optimize, and expanding the telemetry window heuristics to per-customer baselines.

Related work: builds on earlier profile-onboard efforts but differs by making deltas first-class and tying merge decisions to real usage signal; see ENG-1021 for historical context.

Checklist: Run unit tests, add integration fixture, validate feature flag gating, add docs.

Diego Morales: Great direction. Two asks: (1) add a small E2E that runs the whole path including API -> merger -> annotator so we can validate the snippet format; (2) make the telemetry-window configurable via the API call. responded: added e2e smoke and query param telem_window
Jordan Lee: Could we expose the confidence band values as numeric fields in the API output in addition to human text? requested change: include confidence_low/confidence_high floats. responded: added numeric fields and unit tests
Amira Hassan: Security note: ensure the audit bundle doesn't include raw customer tokens. requested change: redact tokens in proof bundle. responded: implemented redaction + added test to verify no sensitive keys are serialised
Reviewer (ops): Please include a small operation runbook for manual review flow. responded: docs/registry/delta-merge.md includes the reviewer checklist and runbook

payload.body:
Problem: When onboarding models we lacked a machine-readable lineage artifact that connects model package uploads, profiling runs, and generated release notes. That made automated changelog synthesis brittle and required manual stitching for multi-variant releases. This PR adds two pieces: (1) a compact onboard lineage map that records upstream artifacts (source repo, dataset snapshot id, build hash, profiling snapshot id) and (2) an autorelease anchor synthesizer that produces a canonical release anchor and draft changelog entries based on lineage and profile diffs.

Design summary: The onboard lineage map is emitted as part of the onboarding pipeline and stored in the registry as a lightweight provenance document. It uses stable identifiers (dataset-snap, build-hash, profile-seed) and explicit relation types (built-from, profiled-by, variant-of). The autorelease anchor synthesizer consumes the lineage map and the model's performance profile snapshots to generate: a) a short human-facing release anchor (one-line summary), b) structured changelog notes (regressions, improvements, config changes), and c) a machine signal for the release gating pipeline. The synthesizer is conservative: it flags unknowns for manual review and emits confidence scores for each note.

Checklist implemented: 
- [x] Onboard step writes lineage map JSON (compact schema)
- [x] Registry API accepts lineage map and indexes provenance tags
- [x] Small migration to backfill lineage_uuid for recent uploads (best-effort)
- [x] Autorelease anchor synthesizer service + CLI hook (dry-run support)
- [x] Unit tests for synthesizer heuristics and profile-diff rules
- [x] E2E smoke with model-registry CI that runs onboard->synthesize flow

Migration notes: Backfill is best-effort for the last 90 days and writes lineage_uuid metadata on the model object when provenance can be inferred from upload artifacts and telemetry. If backfill fails, the synthesizer will mark the model as "no-lineage" and surface it to the curation queue. No user-visible API schema changes for existing clients; lineage is optional.

Testing / QA: Added a small set of synthetic onboard fixtures (3 variants) to exercise regressions detection (latency and MRR), and CI has an additional job that runs the synthesizer in dry-run mode and asserts output schema and non-empty anchors. Manual review by Marco and Sofia focused on heuristics thresholds and wording in generated notes.

Why this is safe: The changes are additive and guarded by feature flags (registry.feature.lineage and registry.feature.autorelease). The synthesizer never auto-promotes to a release; it only produces draft anchors unless the team flips the autorelease.allow_auto_publish flag.

Related: ENG-4021 (provenance roadmap), ENG-4090 (changelog automation spike).
Marco Ruiz: The heuristics look good; can we expose the latency threshold as a config var? Also suggest a more conservative default for patch releases.
Ava Chen (author): Accepted; added registry.config.synth.latency_threshold and lowered default for patch channels. Updated docs.
Sofia Li: Are we comfortable with the backfill window? Might introduce noise from old profiling artifacts.
Ava Chen: Backfill is gated and best-effort; added logging and an opt-out flag registry.backfill.enabled=false for customers that want zero mutation during migration.
Ellen Park: CI job failed once on flakey fixture; recommend increasing timeout.
Ellen Park: +1 after timeout bump and re-run.
CI Bot: synth-dryrun job passed on re-run (2026-02-18 06:02 UTC).
Feature flags enabled by default in staging only. Backfill migration runs as a separate safe job and is idempotent. Post-merge: ops run backfill job during a low-traffic window and monitor curation queue for 'no-lineage' hits.
Added onboard lineage map (optional provenance) and an autorelease anchor synthesizer that drafts changelog anchors from lineage + profile diffs. Backfill available for recent uploads; feature controlled by flags.
Run migrations/20260215_backfill_lineage_uuid.py in staging first

payload.body:
Motivation: the registry accumulates near-duplicate performance profiles and micro-changelog entries when models are iteratively profiled (small sequence-length sweeps, quantization experiments, or backfilled calibration runs). This inflates storage, complicates release-note history, and makes candidate rollouts noisy. This PR introduces two cooperating pieces: 1) a profile deduplication/canonicalization pipeline that groups profiles by a fingerprint and merges small deltas using configurable heuristics; and 2) a changelog consolidator that compresses sequences of small profile updates into a single human-friendly release note with impact summaries. What changed: added a fingerprint generator (sha1 over canonicalized metadata+profile-stats), a merge policy engine (thresholds for metric drift, quantization tags, and sample-size weighting), conflict-resolution hooks that preserve provenance and earliest-commit attribution, and a rollback CLI (registry rollback apply --since <commit>) that replays canonical state to a chosen checkpoint. The changelog consolidator implements grouping rules (time-window, semantic-impact buckets) and templated summarizers that produce both short and extended notes; it also exposes a --dry-run mode for maintainers. Implementation notes: new service module src/dedupe/, CLI extension at cli/registry.py, a GitHub Action workflow .github/workflows/changelog-consolidator.yml for nightly runs, and unit+integration tests under tests/dedupe/ and tests/integration/changelog/. Tests simulate a stream of 120 profile commits across 3 model families and assert that dedupe reduces stored profiles by ~18% while retaining highest-quality representative profiles. Backwards compatibility: original profiles are retained in a compressed provenance archive and remain addressable by hash. Rollout: feature gated behind config.flags.profile_dedupe and changelog.enabled; disabled by default for first two weeks while we monitor regressions. Ops runbook: added notes to docs/ops/registry-dedupe.md for how to tune merge thresholds and how to force-preserve profiles. Why it matters: reduces registry clutter, yields concise release notes for model teams, and makes automated rollouts cleaner by reducing spurious deltas. Linked linear tickets: ENG-4219 (dedupe engine), ENG-4301 (changelog UX).
Added profile deduplication and changelog consolidation; reduces registry storage of redundant profiles by ~18% in our test corpus; provides a rollback CLI and provenance-backed archives. Feature is behind a flag and off by default. Ops docs added for tuning merge thresholds.
No forced migration; runs compactly when enabled and writes provenance archive for any merged profiles. Administrators can run cli/registry.py export-provenance --since <date> before enabling if they prefer snapshots.
Unit and integration tests added; simulated workload with 120 commits across 3 families; assertions verify dedupe ratio, retention of top-quality profile per cluster, and changelog human summaries. CI observed 18% storage reduction in test environment.
Example consolidated changelog short: 'Consolidated 12 micro-profiles for model: llama-2-13b; representative profile chosen: quantized-int8; median latency change: +0.8ms; token-cost delta: -3.2%.'
Example rollback: registry rollback apply --to-hash 3f9a1b4 --confirm
Marco Ruiz: Can you add a brief benchmark for CPU overhead during nightly runs? The dedupe loop looks O(n^2) in naive path; consider locality sharding.
Lina Park: Added a micro-benchmark and a sharding optimization in merge_policy.py; nightly runs now shard by model-family and use a bloom filter to avoid repeated pairwise compares.
Aisha Thompson: The changelog templates look good; please include example output in docs and add a link to the related Linear ticket in the generated note metadata.
Lina Park: Included examples and attach linear keys in the consolidated note metadata. Also added --preserve-hash flag to force-pin specific profiles.
Ben Carlson: Approved after CI green and small nits fixed (doc link, log level).
Feature flag enabled in staging for 72h; ops to run nightly consolidator via provided GH Action and review consolidated notes in #model-registry channel. Follow-up: schedule canary for production roll (ENG-4380).

This PR adds two complementary features to the model registry: (1) a compact manifest fingerprint (a canonical, stable hash plus lightweight provenance tag) that makes it cheap to detect content- and metadata-level identity across uploads, and (2) an evaluative delta teaser generator that summarizes the practical impact of profile or metadata changes in a concise, human-friendly sentence used by release notes and the onboarding UI. Motivation: customers and reviewers often need a one-line summary and a stable identifier to decide whether to pin, rollback, or promote a model version; current changelogs are noisy and require manual triage. What I changed: implemented manifest_fingerprint module (Rust), added CLI hook `redwood-model-registry manifest:hash` and server-side endpoint to compute and store fingerprints during onboarding, implemented delta-scorer that combines token-level diffs, latency delta, memory delta, and a weighted importance table to produce a score and a teaser string, and wired an autodraft release teaser generator into the release assembler pipeline. Backwards compatibility: existing manifests still accepted; fingerprint is optional metadata until the rollout flag is enabled for a tenant. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated on `manifest_fp` with gradual enable by percentage, initial harvest for 50 recent onboardings to build importance weights, runtime toggles in Console. Checklist: [x] unit tests for fingerprint and delta scoring [x] integration tests for CLI hook and web hook [x] API docs for new endpoints [x] linear ticket linked and acceptance criteria added. How to validate locally: run `bin/registry --dev manifest:hash path/to/manifest.json` to get fingerprint; run `scripts/teaser_demo.sh` to generate teaser output from two profile snapshots. Related: ENG-7794 for model-onboard ergonomics and PM-1209 for release UX improvements.
Add compact manifest fingerprinting to improve provenance and small-delta diffing.
Introduce an evaluative delta scorer that ranks profile changes by likely customer impact.
Auto-generate short, human-friendly release teasers for the changelog and release UI to aid release triage.
Ethan Kim: Nice end-to-end. Two asks: can we make the fingerprint stable across field reorderings in the manifest? Also please add a short sample in the API docs showing a fingerprint with provenance tags.
Maya Patel: Addressed. canonicalization step now sorts keys and normalizes timestamps before hashing; added sample payload to docs/api/fingerprint.md
Lina Zhou: Delta scoring looks promising. Suggest exposing the weight table as config so we can A/B tune without deploys. Also a nit: rename `importance` to `impact_weight` for clarity.
Maya Patel: Good call. Pulled the table into a tenant-configurable YAML and renamed field to impact_weight. Added tests for override behavior.

payload.body:
Summary: Adds a new artifact type (workload-stamped baseline) to the model intake pipeline, stores per-variant performance fingerprints, and wires a small release-blurb generator that anchors automated changelog lines to concrete workload signatures and delta statistics.
Motivation: We frequently produce generic release notes that lack workload context (e.g. which latency/throughput profile was used). This makes rollouts and canaries noisy. Workload-stamped baselines let us: 1) capture a lightweight, reproducible workload signature alongside numeric baselines; 2) attach those signatures to profiles and releases so release blurbs can say: 'Baseline run: text-generation-short-2k, p95=120ms, delta vs previous +8% tokens/sec'.
Implementation details:
- New artifact type: "baseline.jsonl" entries include: model_alias, variant, workload_tag, seed_hash, sample_counts, perf_metrics (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec), env_hint (quantized/float16), and sample_digest.
- Ingest flow: onboarder writes baseline artifacts as a sidecar when a profiling job completes. The registry now indexes workload_tag -> [variant footprints], and stores sample_digest for quick sampling during regen.
- Release blurb generator: lightweight Python function that picks the most representative baseline for the released variant and formats a terse one-line blurb with strengthening heuristics (prefer matching workload_tag, otherwise nearest neighbor by sample_digest cosine on precomputed embedding).
- Safe defaults: If no baseline exists, blurb falls back to 'no baseline - recommend profile run' and flags the release notes.
- Storage: artifacts stored under /artifacts/baselines/{model_alias}/{variant}/{baseline_id}.jsonl (S3-backed path in metadata)
- Rollout: feature gated behind registry flag 'workload_baselines.enabled' and toggled off by default.
Testing & validation:
- Added unit tests for ingest/serializer and blurb heuristics.
- End-to-end smoke: local simulated profiling job generates a baseline and the release generator produces a blurb.
- Benchmarked indexing cost: indexing adds ~3% to intake latency for large manifests (measured in CI perf job).
Backwards compatibility & migration:
- Existing manifests without baselines are unaffected.
- We add a background migration worker that compacts older profile files into baseline artifacts for the last 30 days (opt-in).
Checklist:
- [x] Schema for baseline artifact and indexer
- [x] Ingest hook in onboarder
- [x] Release blurb generator and small templating engine
- [x] Unit & integration tests
- [x] Documentation PR (docs/registry/baselines.md)
- [x] Feature flag gate and rollout plan
Related: Linear ENG-3141, PM-1985. See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3141/workload-stamped-baseline-artifacts-and-release-blurbs
Diego Rivera: Can we avoid storing raw sample data in S3 for privacy-sensitive models? Suggest we store only a sample_digest and a small anonymized histogram.
Maya Chen: Good point — updated serializer to redact prompt text and only keep token-length distributions and sample_digest. See commit b7c9e21.
Priya Nair: The nearest-neighbor fallback uses embedding comparisons; how expensive is that at scale? Please add an eviction plan for stale baselines.
Maya Chen: Added an LRU compaction policy to indexer (configurable) and a nightly job to prune baselines older than configured TTL. See indexer changes in c3d2f9a.
Liam O'Connor: Tests look good. One nit: release_blurb.py should include model variant semver if present.

Motivation: As model onboarding accelerates we need automated, repeatable signals that indicate when a newly onboarded model or variant should be rolled back. Currently rollbacks are ad-hoc and rely on scattershot telemetry. This PR adds a small, deterministic "rollback_signals" pipeline and a release primer generator that surfaces high-risk releases with suggested mitigation steps.

Summary:
- Add "rollback_signals" to model metadata (stability_score, perf_regressions, validation_drop_reasons, sample_alerts)
- Implement telemetry aggregation job that computes per-variant signals from evals, real-serving latency/err rates, and sample quality regressions
- Add release_primer generator that consumes signals + profile deltas and emits a ranked release index (CSV/JSON) and a prose primer for release notes
- New dashboards and alert hooks for the top-5 regression reasons
- Unit and integration tests, plus a small e2e smoke job for the release-primer CLI

Why this is different: Existing change-log and primer generators summarize changes but do not prioritize by rollback risk. The new signals synthesize cross-cutting evidence (telemetry + evals + sampled in-field outputs) and produce actionable roll-forward/rollback priorities.

payload.body: Problem: onboarding pages and release notes for model variants accumulate many low-signal items that hide deployment risks. This PR implements a contextual release pruner that selects a small, high-signal subset of changelog fragments and pairs it with a compact variant signal hash — a deterministic, size-bounded digest derived from sampled telemetry features — to help reviewers and downstream tools quickly assess runtime affinity. Key ideas: (1) Variant signal hash condenses anonymized telemetry-derived features (sequence length distribution quantiles, common token-prefixes, average KV cache hit hint) into a stable 64-char hex digest. The hash is produced from deterministic sketching of reservoir-sampled telemetry aggregates so it is reproducible across uploads and small enough for manifests. (2) Release pruner ranks candidate changelog fragments by a hybrid score (telemetry-weighted impact + semantic novelty) and applies a length and redundancy-aware pruning pass to produce a 3-item short summary and optional extended list. Implementation details: sketches and hash generation live in registry/lib/signals/hash_sketch.go; pruning engine is in services/release/pruner.go with a preview REST endpoint at api/release_preview.go. The uploader CLI gained --publish-short-release to enable the pruned output; the registry UI shows both short and full views. Privacy and safety: telemetry inputs are pre-aggregated, bucketed, and clipped; no raw traces are exported. Backwards compatibility: new fields are additive; older clients ignore short_release and variant_signal_hash. Motivation: onboarding a growing set of model variants uncovered gaps in a) how representative performance samples are chosen for profile calibration and b) how changelogs capture context tied to sample regressions. This PR introduces two complementary components: a Sampled Affinity Calibrator (SAC) which creates affinity-weighted sample buckets per model variant and workload slice, and a Contextual Release Drafter (CRD) which synthesizes concise release notes tied to representative sample traces and performance deltas.

What this changes (high level): adds an offline calibration pipeline that takes telemetry + small probe workloads and outputs a per-variant affinity vector used to bias sampling for ongoing profiling; extends the model registry release pipeline with a drafter that attaches contextual bullets to autogenerated changelogs (examples include top-3 regressions, representative prompt, and suggested mitigation knobs).

Key goals: reduce noisy profile drift by ensuring sampled calibration sets better reflect served request distributions, and produce changelogs that are actionable for runtime/config teams and SREs.

Implementation notes: single-string description of code changes and behaviour. The SAC is implemented as a new service under registry/pipeline/sac with a compact estimator that fits into existing on-boarding flows. It outputs a small JSON affinity vector per model-version (kept in registry metadata). The CRD hooks into release-assembler and consumes: model profile deltas, a small set of representative prompts (sampled according to SAC), and evaluation metrics to render 3-5 bullet release notes and a short human-readable rationale. payload.body:
Context and motivation: Onboarding teams repeatedly ask for a compact way to know how "occupancy" (live usage footprint of a model: active KV/cache occupancy, average context reuse, and short-term hot-prefix counts) will affect serving economics. Current model profiles capture static throughput/latency percentiles but miss transient occupancy dynamics that drive cache hit rate and batching efficiency. This PR introduces an "occupancy-led" onboarding scorer that (1) derives a small-time-window occupancy signature from sampled inference traces, (2) synthesizes a concise autodraft release summary (compact bullet-style blurb) highlighting expected cache/batching behavior and deprecation hints, and (3) wires the scorer into the onboarding pipeline so the registry stores the occupancy signature alongside existing performance profiles.

What this PR does (high-level):
- Adds a lightweight occupancy sampler and scorer that runs during model ingest or as an async probe; it produces a 6-value occupancy signature (kv_utilization_pct, avg_prefix_reuse, short_tail_hit_rate, median_kv_age, burst_index, effective_batchability) and a stability score.
- Persists the signature in the model profile document and surfaces it to the release-note autodrafter.
- Implements an autodraft summarizer that turns numeric occupancy signals into a 3-line release note: expected cache sensitivity, recommended quantization/batching knobs, and suggested deprecation/rollout guardrails.
- Exposes a read-only preview endpoint in the onboard CLI (redwood-model-registry/bin/onboard preview-occupancy) for maintainers to inspect sample traces and generated blurb before finalizing the profile.
- Adds end-to-end unit and integration tests, plus a small synthetic trace generator for CI.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- The occupancy sampler is sampling-first (default 2% of ingests) and bounded by time/CPU to avoid adding cost to onboarding; customers can opt-out or run a full probe.
- The signature intentionally stays compact to be stable across small post-upload telemetry changes; we compute a rolling median and a stability metric to avoid noisy autodrafts.
- We avoid baking release prose into the runtime; summaries are generated and stored as part of the profile metadata and can be edited before release.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated under feature flag registry.occupancy_autodraft=false by default.
- Canary enabled for internal models, then opt-in beta for a subset of customers.
- Observe metric: occupancy.signature_stability and autodraft.accept_rate for 2 weeks before wider enablement.

Backwards compatibility:
- No breaking schema change: new occupancy signature field is optional. Older tooling ignores it.

Implementation details (files and core changes):
- New module: onboard/occupancy/sampler.py — streaming sampler and aggregator.
- New scorer: onboard/occupancy/scorer.py — computes the 6-value signature and stability score.
- Autodraft generator: onboard/autodraft/occupancy_blurb.py — mapping logic from signature -> human-readable lines with templates.
- Persistence: model_profiles/storage.py updated to store occupancy_signature and autodraft_blurb fields, with migration shim.
- CLI preview: redwood-model-registry/bin/onboard preview-occupancy (adds small arg set).
- Tests: tests/onboard/test_occupancy_sampler.py, tests/onboard/test_autodraft_blurb.py, plus integration test harness.

Observability:
- New metrics: occupancy.sampled_requests_total, occupancy.signature_stability, autodraft.preview_requests, autodraft.generated_count.

CI and checks:
- Unit/pytest suite + lint + mypy. Synthetic trace generator added to tests/utils/trace_generator.py.
- CI initially failed on a flaky test (integration probe timing), fixed by adding deterministic seeding to the synthetic generator.

Merge notes:
- Squash-merged to main after reviewer approvals and green CI.

Release notes: see release_notes field.

Why this is different from previous profile work:
- Prior PRs focused on static throughput/latency profiling and changelog drafting based on commit history. This change ties short-term runtime occupancy heuristics directly into profile generation and creates a concise, actionable autodraft specifically about cache/batching sensitivity and rollout guardrails.

Motivation: onboarding churn and noisy release notes have made it hard for SREs and product owners to triage model-version rollouts. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: a compatibility crosswalk that canonicalizes legacy and vendor-specific model metadata into the registry canonical schema, and a concise release summarizer that auto-generates a short human-friendly blurb for changelogs based on profile diffs. The crosswalk maps legacy fields (e.g., model.family, model.variant_tag, gpu_tier labels) and normalizes quantization/precision metadata into the registry's canonical keys so downstream tools (release assembler, perf dashboards) can reason about variants consistently. The summarizer consumes the profile delta output (performance, latency P50/P95, token cost, embedding/accuracy deltas) and applies heuristics: significance thresholds, affinity-aware weighting (prefers customer-affinity metrics when available), and a suppression filter to avoid trivial churn (e.g., insignificant lint-only metadata changes). It produces a 1-3 line synopsis plus a structured context note for machine-readable release bundles. Checklist: - [x] compatibility crosswalk implementation (python module) - [x] summarizer core logic and unit tests - [x] integration tests with onboard pipeline and release-assembler -> sample artifacts - [x] CI coverage for canonicalization edge cases (missing fields, vendor aliases) - [x] add provenance stamps (profile-hash + crosswalk-version) - [x] docs: crosswalk mapping table and summarized release note examples Implementation notes: - crosswalk lives at src/crosswalk/canonicalizer.py and includes a small, extensible alias table and tests for alias resolution. - summarizer implemented as a lightweight Rust binary (tools/release_summarizer) to match existing release tooling; it accepts profile-diff JSON and outputs both concise text and a compact JSON context blob. - integrated a new step in pipelines/onboard-release to call the summarizer and attach synthesized_blurb to release metadata. - added a release pipeline flag release.notes.auto_review to toggle human review requirement when the delta is above certain signal thresholds. Testing: unit tests added under tests/crosswalk and tests/summarizer; a staged integration run was executed against a synthetic delta (see sample-artifacts/example-delta.json) with expected blurb produced. Backwards compatibility: crosswalk includes schema versioning and a compatibility-mode that preserves original fields under vendor_provenance when requested. Rollout plan: feature-gated behind registry feature-flag registry.features.crosswalk_v1; will enable for 10% of onboard flows for 48h, evaluate noise metrics, then ramp. Related: links to ENG-4129 (onboard metadata stability) and SUP-7642 (customer report: noisy changelogs). This PR adds a lightweight, sample-based sanity sampler to the model onboarding flow plus a contextual changelog suggester that drafts human-readable release notes from sample diffs. Motivation: onboarding full telemetry or running exhaustive evals is expensive; teams need a quick, reproducible sanity check that exercises the most representative request patterns for a model variant and surfaces concrete examples for changelogs. The sampler uses a stratified sampling strategy over model profile shards (token length distribution, request surface, dataset tags) and an output-fingerprint clustering pass to pick 20-50 representative inputs to run against both the candidate and baseline models. The changelog suggester executes the sample set, computes signal deltas (exact-match, BLEU-ish, hallucination heuristics, safety flags), and synthesizes a short changelog draft with prioritized bullets and one concrete example per bullet. Checklist: - [x] sampler algorithm and unit tests - [x] onboarding CLI flag --sanity-sample and CI runner integration - [x] changelog suggester library and draft serializer - [x] small UX additions to the registry UI for previewing suggested bullets (read-only) - [x] docs and runbook for interpreting sampler output How to run locally: ./cli/onboard.py --model-path ./weights --profile ./profiles/foo.json --sanity-sample --sample-output out/sanity.json Then ./tools/changelog_suggester.py --samples out/sanity.json --baseline-id model:v1 --out out/changelog_draft.md Collision handling and guardrails: samples are capped at 50 runs; sensitive or PII-detected requests are redacted at collection time; all suggested bullets are flagged with a confidence score and an example id so that product owners can quickly triage. Notes on safety: the suggester deliberately avoids automated pushes to release notes; it only outputs drafts for human review.
Adds an onboarding sampler that produces a compact, representative sample set and a suggester that drafts contextual changelogs by running those samples against baseline and candidate models. Includes CLI flags, small UI preview, tests, and CI integration.
Added: onboarding --sanity-sample flag to produce representative sample sets for quick sanity checks. Added: changelog suggester tool that drafts release notes with prioritized bullets and concrete examples. Note: outputs are drafts and require human review; no automatic publishing.
Customers and internal teams requested a faster onboarding safety net to catch regressions without full-scale telemetry runs. This PR targets that gap by providing reproducible, small-sample checks and an automated draft generator to speed release note authoring. The implementation prioritizes reproducibility, low cost, and human-in-the-loop review.
Unit tests added for shard weighting and fingerprint clustering. Integration tests exercise end-to-end sample generation and suggester scoring against a small baseline fixture. CI has a smoke job that runs a 10-sample end-to-end flow to catch regressions in infra changes.
Revert the feature branch or disable --sanity-sample flag in onboarding; remove registry UI preview via feature flag registry.ui.changelog_preview=false. No data migrations performed.

Motivation: onboarding churn and noisy changelogs make it hard for downstream teams to understand what actually changed between model versions. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: 1) an incremental 'exemplar profile' snapshot store that keeps a tiny, representative set of inference traces for each model/version (sampling + deterministic hashing), and 2) a release-note-mapper service that turns profile deltas into short, ranked human-friendly changelog excerpts. Goals: reduce manual release note effort, surface meaningful performance/latency/capacity regressions, and provide deterministic exemplars for rollback diagnostics. Design summary: - Exemplar snapshots are produced incrementally during onboarding and periodic telemetry backfills; each snapshot contains up to 128 exemplar records (input hash, token-length bucket, trimmed KV-cache seed, perf summary). - A lightweight exemplars index (LSM-backed) stores signature -> exemplar pointers and a small bloom filter for fast delta detection. - The release-note-mapper consumes a pair of exemplar snapshots, computes a ranked delta (latency median/P95 diffs, failure-mode diffs, token-efficiency deltas), and generates a short scoring blob with rationale and suggested human blurb. - Integrations: onboarding pipeline will store snapshot metadata in model metadata, the console will surface top-3 mapped blurbs as draft release-notes, and the CLI adds --exemplar-seed to reproduce an exemplar locally. Important constraints: privacy-safe (no raw user text kept — exemplars are hashed/truncated), deterministic sampling to allow reproducible diffs, low runtime overhead (<2% CPU for ingestion path). Checklist: - [x] Incremental exemplar snapshot writer and compact on-disk format - [x] Exemplar index service + API (list/get/diff) - [x] release-note-mapper core heuristic + templating - [x] CLI flag and local reproduce tool - [x] unit + integration tests for mapper ranking heuristics - [x] docs: developer guide + console UI hints - [x] rollout plan + feature flag - [ ] e2e smoke test against a live model corpus (follow-up job created) Rollout plan: gated behind feature flag registry.exemplar.enabled, canary to 5% of onboard flows for 48 hours, expand to 25% for 72 hours, full enable after telemetry looks healthy. Linked work: ENG-2981 (exemplar sampling design), ENG-3020 (release notes automation). Security & privacy: exemplars are salted hashes + fixed-length token windows; storage TTL default 90 days and configurable. Backwards compatibility: metadata schema bump uses optional fields; consumers will ignore if absent. Migration: background backfill job (created as a follow-up) will populate exemplars for recent major releases. See docs/release-notes-mapping.md for examples and heuristics.
Miguel Ortega (reviewer): Nice end-to-end design. Two high-level asks: (1) ensure the exemplar format is forward compatible (suggest version header + optional fields), (2) explain how bloom filters avoid false positives for the typical corpus size.
Aisha Khan (author): Addressed: added 8-byte header with version and reserved flags; adjusted LSM bloom bits and added a unit test that fakes a 10M key-space to validate false-positive rates. See ls m_store.py lines ~120-170.
Priya Desai (reviewer): Mapper heuristics look good. Request: add a small guard for noisy latency metrics (e.g., if sample size < 20, fall back to median-only blurb).
Aisha Khan (author): Implemented sample-size gating and added test cases (tests/test_release_note_mapper.py::test_small_sample_fallback).

Introduces a Curation Assistant that drafts contextual changelog snippets from evaluation deltas and telemetry signals, plus a Variant Snapshotter that records a deterministic snapshot of model metadata, perf profiles, and sample outputs.
