Context: Onboard inflow for low-throughput or bursty models was producing noisy release notes and uneven sampling coverage for lifecycle metrics. This PR introduces a probabilistic, workload-aware onboard sampler plus a batched release digest compiler to make changelogs more concise and statistically representative.

Motivation: Reduce manual curation on small-model onboarding, improve signal quality for perf and cost profiles, and produce deterministic-but-compressed release digests for downstream ingestion by release pipelines.

Summary of changes: - Add probabilistic_sampler.py: reservoir + stratified bucketing that weights samples by recent request trace counts, model size, and declared sensitivity tags. Default sampler is a hybrid: for high-traffic models it falls back to deterministic head-sampling; for low/no-traffic it runs an epsilon-greedy reservoir with decayed weights. - Add batched_release_compiler.py: composes multiple small onboarding changes into a single digest with summarized metrics (latency histogram, token cost delta, affinity hints) and canonical provenance fingerprints. - Introduce synthetic_probe_runner.py: optional probe harness that seeds low-traffic models with synthetic lightweight workloads to collect baseline perf if real traffic is insufficient. Probe runner respects privacy flags and bypasses telem export when marked. - Add contract_validator augment that enforces sampler-config presence and annotates manifests with sampling seed + policy. - CI/workflow updated to run sampler integration test and ensure release digests are generated in a dry-run mode during merges to main. - Documentation and release note templates for reviewer consumption.

Design notes (brief): - Sampling algorithm: stratified reservoir with 3 strata (high, medium, low traffic) computed from seven-day rolling counts. Each stratum maintains an adaptive reservoir size proportional to expected entropy; an importance weight decays exponentially (alpha=0.97) for older traces. Edge cases: models with strict PII flags will be excluded from synthetic probing and only allow on-device sampling if configured. - Release batching heuristics: releases occurring within a 72-hour window are candidates for consolidation if their delta footprint (additions+deletions token-change metric) is below a configurable threshold (default 500 tokens). The compiler generates a short digest plus an expanded JSON artifact where needed for audit. - Backwards compatibility: sampler-config.yaml supports legacy manifest linting; the sampler will default to legacy behaviour for manifests lacking the new sampling contract.

Checklist: - [x] Implement sampler and compile unit tests - [x] Integrate sampler into onboard pipeline (dry-run) - [x] Add probe harness and privacy gating - [x] Add docs and release templates - [x] Add CI workflow to generate release digests on PR merges

Commits (high-level): - add probabilistic sampler and docs - implement batched release compiler and template - add synthetic probe harness with privacy gate - augment contract validator to require sampler config - add unit and integration tests + CI workflow - fix edge cases and handle legacy manifests - update helm values and release note changelog

Test summary: - Unit tests: sampler edge cases, reservoir correctness, weight decay. - Integration: onboard pipeline dry-run generates digest.json matching template; CI verifies digest field presence. - Manual validation: author ran probe against a staging model: baseline latency, memory, and token-cost deltas collected and embedded in a sample digest.

Review conversation (high level): - Anu Shah: "Nice approach. Two asks: (1) please document failure modes if probe fails (network/timeout), and (2) make sampler-config defaults explicit in README." Response: "Added explicit failure semantics and default table in README; probe now uses exponential backoff and marks model as 'probe-failed' in audit log." - Diego Martínez: "Can we make the digest include an optional 'rollback-suggest' flag when perf regresses > 25%?" Response: "Added heuristic: digest includes rollback_suggest when 95th latency increases > 25% and token-cost delta > 10%." - Ravi Patel: "Concern about CI runtime cost given probe: ensure probes run only in staging and are off by default." Response: "Probes run in CI only as dry-run stub that validates templates; full probes are gated by 'enable_probes' config and off by default in CI."

Approvals: - Anu Shah approved (2025-09-08) - Diego Martínez approved (2025-09-09) - Ravi Patel approved (2025-09-10)

CI and checks: - model-registry/unit-tests: pass - model-registry/integration-tests: pass - lint: pass - release-digest-dryrun: pass

Merge: - merged_by: "release-bot" - merged_at: "2025-09-10" - merge_method: "squash"
feat(sampler): probabilistic stratified reservoir sampler
feat(release): batched release digest compiler and template
feat(probe): synthetic probe runner with privacy gating
chore(onboard): require sampler-config in contract validator
test: add sampler integration tests and ci dry-run
docs: onboarding sampling guide and release digest templates
Merged to main via squash by release-bot on 2025-09-10 after all reviewers approved and CI passed. Generated release digest artifact committed to changelogs/ and a dry-run digest emitted by CI for audit. No rollback was triggered during merge.
Adds workload-aware probabilistic sampling for onboarding and a batched release digest compiler. Improves representativeness of onboarding telemetry for low-traffic models, and reduces churn in release notes by consolidating small changes into a concise digest. Optional synthetic probe harness can seed baselines for low-traffic models (disabled by default).
When deploying to Private clusters, set enable_probes=false in registry values to avoid synthetic traffic. The sampler config uses a default alpha=0.97 decay; tune via onboard/configs/sampler-config.yaml. Ensure CI secrets for probe runners are not present in production or private air-gapped deployments.

Motivation: Product and SRE teams have asked for per-cohort release notes so stakeholders can review model behavior across important slices (e.g., high-length prompts, low-resource languages, latency-sensitive clients). This PR adds a draft generator that emits one compact draft per configured cohort along with a compact provenance-hash that ties the draft to: model-version, profile-hash, dataset-snapshot-id, and the seed prompt set. Each draft includes a short perf summary, top-3 regression signals, and suggested mitigations.
Introduce an automated pathway to generate draft release notes per cohort (slice) with an injected provenance-hash and a stability gate. Adds CLI/UI preview and a lightweight summary algorithm for compact notes. Backwards compatible: existing changelog pipeline consumes cohort drafts or falls back to the aggregate note.
Arjun Patel (2025-01-10): Could you expand on how the provenance-hash is computed? We need deterministic hashes for audit. — Response: The hash is HMAC-SHA256 over canonicalized keys: model_version, profile_hash, dataset_snapshot_id, seed_prompt_set_id. The key used for HMAC is stored encrypted in the release service (referenced in docs).
Lena Gomez (2025-01-11): The stability gate thresholds are hardcoded; request to move to config and expose via Console. — Response: Moved thresholds into release-config; Console flag added (docs updated).
Tomás Rivera (2025-01-12): Tests flaked on CI (race in snapshot loader). Suggest sleeping or retry with backoff. — Response: Added a retry with exponential backoff in tests and guarded the loader path; CI run passed afterwards.
Arjun Patel (2025-01-13): Approving pending minor wording on CLI help text. — Response: Updated CLI help and man page text per comment.
squash and merged by Lena Gomez on 2025-01-15. Merge commit includes: a compact summary for cohort drafts, CLI commands, and docs. Rollout strategy: feature-flagged (release.cohort_drafts) toggled off by default for accounts with >100k predictions until we complete canary run.
How to preview: registry-cli release preview --model my-model --version v1 --cohort high-length
How to publish drafts: registry-cli release publish --draft-id <id>  (blocked if stability_gate fails)
Console: new 'Cohort drafts' tab on model history page (behind flag)
Safety: drafts include provenance-hash and are written to audit log with read-only ACL for release curators

Adds a cohort-driven sampling component for model intake and a release bundler that emits annotated changelog snippets, provenance hashes, and cohort coverage metrics. Improves onboarding visibility and reduces noisy release notes for large model updates.
Motivation: onboarding churn for large model uploads produced long, noisy changelogs that were hard for reviewers to triage. This PR implements a cohort-aware intake sampler that selects representative probes per model variant and a release bundler that packages compact annotated changelog snippets plus provenance and cohort-coverage metrics. Implementation: 1) ingest/cohort_sampler: deterministic cohort selection seeded by model manifest fingerprint; supports weighted cohorts, stratified sampling across datasets and input lengths, and optional sampling profiles passed from the CLI or CI. 2) bundler/release_bundler: consumes sampler output, computes a canonical provenance hash for the intake bundle, synthesizes concise changelog fragments prioritized by regression score and coverage delta, and emits a compact release bundle artifact (ndjson + metadata.json). 3) CLI: onboardctl additions to preview cohort composition and produce a dry-run changelog preview. 4) tests and docs: unit tests for sampler determinism and coverage heuristics, integration test for bundler end-to-end, and docs describing how to interpret cohort coverage and attach release snippets to model versions. Checklist: - [x] design doc approved (ENG-2046) - [x] sampler core implementation - [x] bundler compact changelog synthesis - [x] CLI preview and dry-run - [x] unit/integration tests - [x] docs and usage examples - [x] e2e smoke on staging Notes: deterministic behavior is important to allow reproducible diffs between releases; the sampler uses a stable hash over manifest fields to seed sampling. The bundler includes an optional verbosity flag to expand snippets for full audit. Links: linear/ENG-2046, support/SUP-842. CI: unit tests were flaky for the stratified sampler on first run due to an off-by-one in boundary math; fixed in commit 3. This PR avoids changing the public onboarding contract but adds metadata fields to release bundles; existing consumers will ignore unknown fields.
Ethan Park: Nice end-to-end flow, can you add a short note on how sampling interacts with existing prefix/KV caching policies?
Maya Chen: Answered - sampler returns a stable set of seed inputs; we annotate bundle metadata with recommended cache hints but do not mutate runtime cache behavior in this PR.
Priya Nair: The provenance hash should be stable across equivalent manifests; add a small fuzz test to assert invariants.
Maya Chen: Added tests asserting provenance stability for re-ordered manifest fields and for equivalent aliasing; pushed commit 4.
Riley Ford: CI showed a flaky stratified sampler test, observed an off-by-one causing one bucket to be empty at small sample sizes. Fix looks good.
Priya Nair: Approving pending a small docs tweak to explain coverage percentage semantics.
Ethan Park: Approving; left a nit about logging verbosity levels which can be a follow-up (ENG-2101).

payload.body:
Motivation: As the model registry accumulates many small metadata and profile deltas during onboarding and routine recalibrations, release notes become noisy. This PR implements a statistical 'delta significance' scorer to rank profile/metadata changes by practical importance across sampled cohorts and couples it with a prose annotator that drafts concise human-friendly release bullets. The goal is to surface the small set of meaningful changes for release notes and reduce manual curation time. Summary of changes: 1) new scoring module registry/scorers/delta_significance.py that computes cohort-aware z-score and effect-size heuristics with bootstrapped confidence intervals, including A/B naming compatibility checks; 2) prose annotator registry/notes/prose_annotator.py that converts scored deltas into templated natural-language bullets with placeholders for metric, direction, p-value, and suggested callouts; 3) CLI integration cli/release_drafts.py with new --release-grade and --sample-size options to generate a draft.md for reviewers; 4) orchestration hook registry/hooks/changelog_autogen.py that filters deltas by threshold and invokes the annotator; 5) tests and sampling harness tests/test_delta_scorer.py and tests/test_prose_annotator.py; 6) docs update docs/model-registry/release-notes-guidelines.md describing how scores map to priority tiers and reviewer workflows. Privacy and stability: the scorer operates on aggregated profile statistics (no raw prompts), and default sampling is limited to 1,000 examples per cohort to bound cost. There's an opt-out label "no-autogen" to prevent automatic drafting for sensitive models. Backwards compatibility: default thresholds match previous manual heuristics so existing release pipelines are unaffected unless teams opt into --release-grade. Checklist: - [x] Scorer implementation with unit tests - [x] Prose annotator + deterministic templating - [x] CLI integration and docs - [x] Add opt-out label and sampling limit - [x] End-to-end test generating a sample draft.md How it works (short): delta_significance computes per-metric delta, pooled variance, and then a two-sided effect-size with bootstrap CI. We combine effect-size and CI width into a single 'impact' score and normalize by historical volatility for a model family. The annotator maps score bands to prose templates (e.g., "Minor decrease in accuracy on X (-0.6 pts, p=0.08) — recommend continued monitoring") and attaches a contextual note when sample sizes are small. Testing summary: unit tests cover edge cases (zero variance, tiny cohorts), integration tests exercise CLI generation on synthetic profiles, and a smoke test verifies that autogen skips models labeled "no-autogen". Rationale for thresholds and defaults are documented in the release-notes-guidelines. Commits: - 7d4a1b2 add delta_significance scorer and bootstrap utils - 2c3f8d4 add prose_annotator with templating and english presets - b1f9d55 add CLI --release-grade and sampling flags - e3b2d11 wire changelog_autogen hook into on-board pipeline - 9f07c4a tests for scorer and annotator, add CI flaky-test guard - f4a6ea8 docs: release notes guidelines and UX screenshots Changed files (high-level): - registry/scorers/delta_significance.py (new) - registry/notes/prose_annotator.py (new) - registry/hooks/changelog_autogen.py (new) - cli/release_drafts.py (new) - tests/test_delta_scorer.py (new) - tests/test_prose_annotator.py (new) - docs/model-registry/release-notes-guidelines.md (updated) - changelogs/sample_drafts/draft-70219.md (generated example) Reviews and comments timeline: - Diego Martinez (reviewer) — "Nice approach; a couple of asks: 1) constrain default sample size to 1k (costs), 2) add warning when CI spans zero so we don't overstate significance." Author reply (Sofia Patel) — "Agreed on 1k default, implemented as --sample-size default and documented it. Added CI span warning in annotator and a confidence label in draft output." - Lena Zhou (reviewer) — "Can we expose an API for external tooling to pull scored deltas as JSON? Also please add a gate to avoid autogen for models older than 6 months without human review." Author reply — "Added registry/api/scored_deltas_handler.py and an optional 'age_gate_days' arg. Default left unset to avoid behavior changes; documented in the new guide." - Priya Rao (reviewer) — "Unit tests look good. Add an integration test exercising the opt-out label and ensure draft generation respects model visibility (private vs public)." Author reply — "Added integration tests and fixed draft permission logic; CI updated." CI: initial run showed a flaky test failure in tests/test_prose_annotator (string ordering in templates) — fixed by normalizing template outputs and re-running CI. Final CI status: all checks passing (unit, integration, lint, mypy, docs-build). Merge decision: approved by reviewers, squash merge applied on 2024-11-04 with change title "Add delta significance scorer and prose annotator for release notes". Follow-ups: - ENG-3421: tune threshold mapping for enterprise models (low priority) - ENG-3487: add localization and longer-form prose mode for release managers (next quarter) Notes for release engineers: the new CLI produces changelogs/sample_drafts/draft-70219.md; use --release-grade to apply prioritized filtering. To opt-out for a specific model, add label "no-autogen" to the model's registry entry. If you see unexpected omissions, rerun with --sample-size 5000 to increase power at cost.
Add automated delta significance scoring to prioritize changelog entries and a lightweight prose annotator that generates human-readable release bullets. CLI flag --release-grade introduced for curated release drafts. No breaking changes. There's an opt-out label "no-autogen" to prevent automatic drafting for sensitive models.
Diego Martinez: Constrain default sample size to 1k and add a CI-span warning when bootstrap crosses zero.
Sofia Patel: Implemented --sample-size default 1000, added CI-span warning and confidence label in drafts.
Lena Zhou: Expose API for external tooling and gate autogen for models older than 6 months without review.
Sofia Patel: Added registry/api/scored_deltas_handler.py and optional age_gate_days argument; documented behavior.
Priya Rao: Ensure opt-out label respected and draft generation respects model visibility; add integration tests.
Sofia Patel: Added tests, fixed permission checks, CI passing after addressing template ordering flake.

Summary: Adds a manifest preflight validator and an autorelease stager to the model intake path. Motivation: onboarding errors and noisy release notes are a recurring source of manual work for curation and SRE. This change aims to (1) surface manifest inconsistencies and performance-profile regressions earlier in CI; (2) normalise and auto-generate release note fragments so curators can approve faster; (3) provide a clear opt-in rollout path so existing pipelines are not broken. What this does: The change introduces `registry/onboard/preflight.py` which runs a thorough validation pass over incoming model manifests (schema conformance, required provenance, runtime-affinity hints, and perf-profile sanity checks). A new `registry/release/autorelease/handler.py` component diffs the incoming manifest against the latest registered version and synthesizes an ordered list of release note bullets (performance deltas, new aliases, deprecations, changelog teasers). The CLI exposes `rmcli model preflight --manifest <file>` to run the same checks locally, and `rmcli model stage-release --model-id <id>` to enqueue an autorelease draft. Backwards compatibility: preflight is disabled by default for existing intake jobs; the new intake pipeline can opt-in via `ONBOARD_PREFLIGHT=true` in environment. Tests and docs: unit tests added under `tests/test_preflight.py` and developer facing documentation in `docs/processes/onboard-preflight.md`. Commits: 1) "add preflight validator and canonical manifest schema v2" — implements schema checks, validation helpers and unit tests. 2) "add autorelease stager and changelog synthesizer" — adds delta logic, simple prose templates, and integration hook. 3) "cli and docs: expose preflight and stage-release commands" — CLI wiring and docs. Files changed (high level): - registry/onboard/preflight.py (new) - registry/onboard/schema/manifest_v2.yaml (new) - registry/release/autorelease/handler.py (new) - cli/rmcli/commands/onboard.py (update) - tests/test_preflight.py (new) - docs/processes/onboard-preflight.md (new) - registry/release/autorelease/templates/brief_snippets.tmpl (new) Small illustrative diffs: preflight.py includes a `validate_perf_profile()` routine that checks latency P95 and token-cost heuristics against model-class baselines; handler.py contains a `synthesize_release_bullets(prev, next)` that emits prioritized bullets and severity tags. Review thread (high level): - Priya Nair (review): "This looks solid — main concern is the perf threshold defaults. Can we make the P95 thresholds driven by a workload profile instead of global constants? Also add a unit test for a manifest with multiple variant aliases." - Maya Chen (author reply): "Agree — switched to workload-driven thresholds. Added `workload_profiles.yaml` and a test `test_preflight_workload_thresholds`." - Ethan Rivera (requested changes): "Please add an explicit opt-in flag for autorelease drafts; we don't want autorelease to auto-queue drafts for large enterprise customers without curator consent." - Maya Chen: "Added `autorelease.mode` in manifest schema (values: off|draft|auto). Default is 'off'. Updated docs and CLI to require `--force-autorelease` for automatic staging." - Luca Bianchi (approval): "Approvals from security and infra side; small nits in logging noted but non-blocking." CI notes: initial run showed an intermittent integration flake in `integration-onboard` (timeout on a mocked network call). Flake reproduced locally, fixed by increasing the test harness network stub timeout and retry logic; CI re-run green. Performance considerations: validation is designed to be cheap (schema checks + sampling of perf deltas); heavy perf regression checks are throttled via the intake config and are only executed in dedicated CI gating runs. Rollout plan: start with canary on the 'staging-intake' workflow for two weeks, then opt-in to 'production-intake' for teams that enable ONBOARD_PREFLIGHT. Autorelease mode will be set to 'draft' by default for the first month so curated reviewers see generated snippets but must approve prior to publication. Related work: references ENG-4321 for perf-profile rationalisation and ENG-5632 for curator UX improvements. Merge outcome: squash-merged to main on 2026-02-21 after approvals from Priya and Luca and green CI. Post-merge tasks: - Add a small dashboard card in Console to show preflight pass-rate per team (follow-up PR). - Add an automated smoke check that ensures `autorelease.mode` never defaults to 'auto' for orgs with enterprise policy. Contact: Maya Chen (@mchen) for follow-ups or rollback requests.
Introduce a preflight manifest validator that checks required metadata, perf-profile thresholds, and hardware affinity hints before model acceptance.
Add an autorelease stager that composes concise changelog bullets from the manifest delta and enqueues release drafts for curator review.
CLI hook: `rmcli model preflight` and an API endpoint for automated CI gates.
Backwards compatible: validation is opt-in for existing ingestion pipelines; default remains permissive until rollout.
Added unit and integration tests and docs for the new onboarding flow.

Motivation: Release engineering and model curation teams need a reliable way to derive representative evaluation slices from production traffic and to automatically produce human-readable release briefs that surface performance regressions and key metadata changes. This PR introduces TelemetryFuse (a small service + pipeline) that ingests sparse runtime telemetry, computes importance-weighted sample sets for onboarding/evals, and hooks into the changelog/autobrief generator to produce concise release summaries. Key goals: reduce manual sampling overhead, improve alerting signal for profile regressions, and automate draft release notes. Changes in this PR include: 1) TelemetryFuse service and CLI for sampling heuristics | 2) WeightedSample serializer and compact manifest stubs for model variants | 3) AutoBrief generator that ingests profile delta output and emits short, structured blurb candidates for release notes | 4) CI hooks and minimal e2e smoke test for the pipeline | 5) docs/readme and onboarding checklist updates. Checklist: [x] Telemetry sampling engine implemented [x] Unit tests for weighting heuristics [x] AutoBrief templating + examples [x] Integration test for end-to-end manifest->brief generation [x] Docs and migration notes. Commits summary: commit 1: add telemetry-fuse service skeleton and protobufs (initial sketch, CLI) | commit 2: implement weighted sampling algorithm and offline simulator (importance sampling based on token distribution + route weights) | commit 3: add AutoBrief summarizer + template library and mapping rules from profile deltas to candidate blurbs | commit 4: tests, CI, docs, and migration guide. Changed areas (high level): services/telemetry-fuse/main.py (service entry, sample orchestration), services/telemetry-fuse/weighting.py (core heuristics and tunables), registry/manifest/stub_serializer.py (compact manifest stub writer), registry/autobrief/generator.py (rule-based brief synthesis), tests/telemetry_fuse/test_weighting.py (unit tests), docs/model-onboard/telemetry-fuse.md (usage and migration), .github/workflows/telemetry-fuse-smoke.yml (e2e smoke pipeline). Small illustrative snippet: weighting.py exposes compute_weights(events, config) -> list of sample ids and weights; config supports time_decay_alpha and route_priority_map. Review conversation: Reviewer Aisha Gomez: "Nice work on the sampling model; two small naming nits and a question about default decay constant." Author (Nikhil): "Renamed the variable and added comments; default alpha set to 0.97 but exposed via CLI flag; added rationale to docs." Reviewer Liam O'Connor: "Can we guarantee manifests remain stable when sampling seed changes? Suggest adding a seed export in the stub." Author: "Added deterministic-seed field to manifest stubs and a test asserting stable output for a given seed." Reviewer Sofia Martinez: "AutoBrief is promising; please add one example that shows a false positive regression suppressed by heuristics." Author: "Added sample in docs that demonstrates suppression via min-sample-count filter and threshold gating." CI summary: initial run failed lint on template naming; fixed in commit 3; full pipeline now passes (unit tests + smoke e2e). Migration notes: operators should run telemetry-fuse with --dry-run against existing telemetry exports to validate sample coverage and inspect generated manifest stubs before adopting as primary sampling source. Backwards compatibility: manifests are additive and include a version tag; existing downstream onboarding code will ignore unknown fields. Related: ties to ENG-845 (automated profile sampling) and ENG-913 (release automation). Testing notes: unit coverage for weighting heuristics 92%; integration smoke covers end-to-end manifest->autobrief path on a synthetic 10k-event export. Follow-ups: bake the telemetry-fuse pipeline into scheduled nightly jobs, add a stability metric for auto-brief hallucination rate and add an opt-in mode for teams to receive suggested notes as draft PRs. Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2024-11-12 after approvals from all reviewers and CI green.
Add TelemetryFuse service to synthesize weighted sample sets from production telemetry and a new AutoBrief generator to produce concise release notes summarizing profile deltas and perf regressions.

payload.body:
Motivation:
Customers asked for tamper-evident release artifacts and predictable, machine-consumable release notes as part of model onboarding. Right now the registry stores model profiles and handwritten changelogs; this PR introduces a deterministic "release bundle" format that packages a model profile, evaluation snapshots, and a release-notes payload, plus an optional signature. The bundle is intended to be the single artifact uploaded to the registry and used by downstream deployers (Redwood Private installers, Dedicated infra, and partner integrations).

What this does (high level):
- Introduces `release-bundle` format (JSON + compressed assets) and a small manifest schema (bundle.v1) that contains: model_id, profile_id, variant_tags, eval_snapshots refs, notes (structured), and signature metadata (key-id, sig).
- Adds a CLI flow `redwood-mr bundle create --sign --notes-template PATH` that builds the bundle from model profile + eval outputs and optional user-supplied notes templates. Signing uses an edged KMS-backed keypair or local GPG-like key for local dev. Signatures are detached and stored inside the bundle manifest to allow both human and machine verification.
- Implements a `notes-assembler` service that converts profile deltas and selected eval metrics into structured change bullets and a compact machine field `summary_kv` suitable for automation (routing, rollout heuristics). The assembler supports templates with placeholders ({{perf.delta}}, {{latency.p95}}) and fallback heuristics when metrics are missing.
- Registry API endpoints: POST /bundles to upload bundles (with signature verification), and GET /bundles/:id to fetch signed bundles and raw notes. Existing onboarding endpoints are backward-compatible: if clients POST a legacy profile payload we synthesize a minimal bundle.v1.
- CI checks: `notes-lint`, `bundle-verify` (signature verification), and `e2e-bundle-install` which simulates a private installer fetching and installing a bundle and verifying signature and notes parsing.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Deterministic bundle structure: we intentionally avoid embedding ephemeral timestamps in the canonical manifest so generated signatures are stable across identical inputs. Metadata with environment specifics (build host, build id) can be stored in `meta.env` but is excluded from the signed canonical blob. This keeps signatures verifiable by customers who rebuild bundles from source assets.
- Signing model: supports two modes: KMS-backed (recommended for CI/production) and local key (dev). We do not implement a full web-of-trust here; customers who need stricter provenance should revoke keys at the registry level.
- Notes assembly: assembler generates both human-readable bullets and a structured `summary_kv` to be used by the Console for diff highlights and by rollouts to pick safer variants. We intentionally limit the assembler to metric diffs and model profile changes to avoid freeform schedule-writer complexity.

Backward compatibility:
- Old onboarding flows that push only model profiles still succeed; the backend synthesizes a bundle with an unsigned manifest and a `generated_notes` field. Consumers that expect signed bundles receive a 400 unless they explicitly opt-in to unsigned bundles (we surface this as a retention/opt-in toggle in the Console).

Testing and validation plan:
- Unit tests for manifest canonicalization and signature verification (+ edge cases around array ordering).
- Notes-assembler unit tests covering templating, missing metrics, and multi-variant inputs.
- Integration CI job: `ci/bundle-e2e` that builds a sample bundle, pushes it to a test registry, then runs an installer container which verifies signature and parses notes. This is gated on the PR.
- Manual QA: Ran installer with bundles signed by local dev key and KMS key; validated the Console diff highlights display `summary_kv` correctly and that the deployment gate uses `perf.delta` to mark canary safety.

Ops and rollout plan:
- Feature flag `bundles.enabled` defaults to on for new registries; existing registries get a migration background job to synthesize bundles for recent model uploads (controlled ramp via rollout config).
- Short-term monitoring: bundle upload success rate, signature verification failures, notes-assembler errors, and Console render errors. Alert if signature verification error rate > 0.5% over 1h during rollouts.

Security considerations:
- Signature verification is enforced on /bundles ingestion when `require_signed` tenant setting is true. Key rotation is supported by storing key metadata and accepting signatures under previous keys for a configurable grace period.
- We do not ship private keys in the repo. KMS integration uses IAM roles configured per environment.

Checklist:
- [x] Manifest schema (bundle.v1) and canonicalization documented
- [x] CLI `bundle create` and `bundle verify` implemented
- [x] Registry endpoints to store and retrieve bundles
- [x] Notes assembler and templates
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] CI gating for bundle-e2e

Remaining items (follow-ups to be tracked separately):
- Add a Console UI for viewing signature key provenance and revocation list (ENG-7251).
- Expand notes assembler to include model qualitative tags (e.g., hallucination risk) once eval hooks are standardized.

References:
- Linear: ENG-7124, ENG-7251
- Support ticket SUP-1982 (customer asked for signed release artifacts)
- Related PRs: earlier profile and changelog automation work (existing repo history).

Files changed (high-level):
- cmd/redwood-mr/bundle.go (+ CLI flags and signer integration)
- pkg/registry/bundles/manifest.go (+ canonicalization and schema)
- pkg/registry/bundles/handler.go (+ POST/GET endpoints)
- internal/notes/assembler/assembler.go (+ templating engine, summary_kv generation)
- ci/workflows/bundle-e2e.yml (+ e2e job to verify bundles)
- integrations/kms/ (adapter and tests)

Release notes:
- Adds release bundle format (bundle.v1) and CLI tooling to create/verify signed bundles. Adds notes-assembler service to generate structured release notes and summary_kv for Console highlights. Backward compatible with legacy profile uploads.

payload.title: onboard-signed-release-bundles-and-notes-assembler

payload.body:
Motivation: onboarding pipelines produce large sample sets and verbose changelog drafts; reviewers and downstream integrators only need compact, high-information slices. This PR adds two complementary components: (1) an entropy-based coverage mapper that picks a small, representative set of samples that maximizes token-level and latency diversity across an onboarding sample corpus, and (2) a compact release atomizer that packages profile metadata and a tiny sample digest into a single release atom used by release note generators and the registry UI. Design summary: the mapper scores candidate samples with a combined metric (token-entropy + latency-quantile spread + request-path diversity) and then runs a lightweight greedy selection with configurable budget and privacy-aware redaction hooks. The atomizer serializes a profile into a compact protobuf-lite blob plus a human-readable blurb (100-400 chars) and a changelog hint map so downstream changelog automation can assemble targeted release lines without pulling the full dataset. Backwards-compatibility: atoms are additive and stored under the existing profile attachments namespace; existing consumers will ignore the new atom MIME type unless they opt in. Checklist: - [x] Mapper scoring function and unit tests - [x] Atom serializer + compact blurb generator - [x] Privacy redaction plug-in + smoke tests - [x] Integration test for registry upload/download of atoms - [x] Release note generator wiring and example template - [x] Docs (registry API changelog section) Performance considerations: mapper runs as an optional post-onboard job; default budget is 40 samples which keeps CPU and memory well under existing limits in our CI. Linear/Jira: ENG-821 implements the mapper; ENG-987 wires atom output into release drafts; SUP-1432 is support follow-up for a customer onboarding with large corpora. Related: this complements the telemetry-driven sample-sampler work but uses an orthogonal objective (information entropy instead of sampling weights).
Marcos Liu: Nice design. Please add a short benchmark to show mapper CPU and wallclock for 10k samples. Also prefer context-based cancellation in the greedy loop.
Asha Patel: Added a micro-benchmark (internal/tests/mapper_bench_test.go) and switched to context-aware loop in commit 4. Benchmarks show ~420ms wallclock for 10k 256-token samples on CI builders.
Sophie Nguyen: Can the blurb generator be localized? We should avoid hard-coded English strings in the atom payload.
Asha Patel: Atom contains an optional 'blurb_locale' and the blurb generator emits a canonical English blurb and a tokenized template; localization hooks added, see docs section.
Introduce entropy-based coverage mapper to generate compact, high-information sample slices for onboarding; add compact release atoms to embed profile summary + tiny sample digest for lighter changelog generation and faster reviewer sign-off. Opt-in via profile 'atomize' flag.
When enabling the atomize posthook in production, ensure S3 lifecycle policy for atom attachments is set to 1y; atoms are small (~20-60KB) but high-volume onboarding can accumulate.
payload.title: Introduce entropy-based coverage mapper and compact release atomizer
